project_name: Child Protection Prevention and Response Services for Children Affected by Conflict in Iraq
project_objective:
Overall Objectives:  To improve access to Child Protection prevention and response services for at-risk children and caregivers affected by the conflict between the Government of Iraq and ISIL, including the specific protection needs of adolescents. 

The situation in Iraq is one characterized by the existence of both chronic and acute protection concerns due to the protracted and immediate nature of the conflict.  Through multiple modalities, this project aims to address the multiple needs of at-risk Iraqi children affected by conflict, including adolescents, whether they are displaced, returned to places of origin, or living in areas recently retaken by the government or in host communities. UNICEF is the provider of last resort for child protection and is the lead agency for coordination at the national and subnational levels and seeks funding through this project to fulfil its mandate.

Specific Objectives:
1. Provide immediate, emergency child protection response services to the most at-risk children and families, including adolescents, particularly those who have been newly displaced, those residing in communities that have recently been retaken from ISIL, and those who are newly returned to their places of origin.

2. Provide and support specialized, community based child protection prevention and response services to children and families, including adolescents, who have experienced, witnessed or been forced to participate in violence, exploitation, or abuse.

3. Support sustainable, systems and community-based child protection prevention and response services that are holistic, gender-sensitive, age-appropriate, and enhance social cohesion.

project_name: Strengthening equitable access to quality learning for school-age children in Syria
project_objective:
In line with the No Lost Generation (NLG) initiative, UNICEF aims to expand equitable access to quality learning and skills development for the most disadvantaged children, adolescents and youth (Adolescents are defined as 10 19 years, Youth are defined as 15 24 years), in particular those who are displaced and out of school. Based on the latest education sector analysis, UNICEF will maintain the following three priority areas:  
a) Scaling up equitable access to education
b) Enhancing the quality of education services
c) Strengthening education systems
Vulnerable children, adolescents and youth often face multiple complex barriers to formal schooling. It is therefore critical to strengthen a knowledge/evidence base and address education barriers at upstream and downstream levels. UNICEF remains committed to the No Lost Generation Initiative, where UNICEF increases cross sectorial synergies with Child Protection, Adolescent Development and Participation (ADAP), Communication for Development (C4D), and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). 
For greater equity and impartiality, UNICEF will advocate for wider humanitarian access and try to reach the most marginalized in government controlled, opposition controlled, hard to reach and besieged areas. UNICEF will also reinforce cross border coordination with Damascus, Amman and Gaziantep hubs in a Whole of Syria approach.  
In addition, UNICEF will attempt to bridge the gap between immediate humanitarian action and long term sustainable development. UNICEF will strengthen partnerships with local authorities, NGOs, communities, schools and youth volunteers in view of resilience building and early recovery. To enhance inter agency collaboration, UNICEF will coordinate with other UN agencies to leverage resources in the selected communities and schools. UNICEF will lead the ESWG in Syria, Amman and Gaziantep for timely information sharing, contextually relevant, collective and effective education response.

project_name: Integrated WASH response for 61690 (12338men, 15422women, 18507 girls and 15423 boys) drought affected and conflict displaced populations in Banadir, Sool, Nugaal, Bari, Gedo and Lower shabelle regionsions
project_objective:
The project aims to reduce the vulnerability of 61690 (12338men, 15422women, 18507 girls and 15423 boys) through increased and sustained access to safe water and adoption of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices. 
Based on Inter-agency assessments by OCHA in September 2016 where Norwegian Church Aid -NCA participated, community members (men and Women) were consulted during needs identification in select locations. The impact of the drought and the adverse effects it has had on people remains alarming as coping mechanisms are further weakened. The need for water remains high on the list of priorities as a life saving measure for both people and animals. 
To enhance provision of WASH services, Specific objectives of this project will include;
•	Increase access to safe sustainable water supply in target locations at both household and institutional level while promoting water treatment and household level
•	Improving nutritional levels for children and households through hygiene awareness campaigns and promotion of hand-washing with soap/ash to ensure reduced exposure to disease outbreaks. 
•	Capacity enhancement for men and women to increase ownership and enhance sustainability of water supply systems through training on operation and maintenance
•	Promote construction of culturally sensitive gender segregated latrines at household and institutional levels towards achievement of open defecation free communities
•	Ensure 50% women representation in decision making structures like the water committee and there inclusion in planning to enhance their safety and security.
•	Encourage protective healthy behavioral practices amongst the affected population.
•	Provide access to safe water, hygiene and sanitation for people in emergency need

project_name: Protracted Relief and Recovery Operations (PRRO) - Ukraine 200953: “Assistance for food insecure and vulnerable populations affected by conflict and loss of livelihoods in eastern Ukraine”.
project_objective:
After two years of conflict, the security situation in eastern Ukraine remains fragile. The consequences of conflict and political stalemate are felt by individuals and communities throughout Ukraine. An estimated 1.1 million people are in need of food assistance, with many resorting to negative coping mechanisms. The Government continues to face massive challenges, including a deepening economic crisis and the urgent need for social and fiscal reform. Without medium- to long-term interventions, more people will require humanitarian assistance in the months and years to come.

The proposed protracted relief and recovery operation (PRRO) builds on the activities and lessons learned from emergency operation 200765. It is informed by assessments, evaluations and participatory consultations, which have led to a refinement of the program strategy and the choice of transfer modalities. WFP will address the food needs of the most vulnerable people in eastern Ukraine while gradually supporting early recovery. 

The operation is aligned with WFP’s Strategic Plan (2017–2021) and gender and protection policies and guidelines. It is guided by Sustainable Development Goals 2 and 17, fostering partnerships and national plans and strategies to achieve zero hunger.
The operation is in line with the United Nations Development Assistance Framework; contributes to the Government’s Single and Comprehensive Strategy and Action Plan for Agriculture and Rural Development in Ukraine for 2015–2020 by enhancing food security and monitoring systems; and is aligned with national social protection schemes. It also builds on the priorities of the humanitarian response plan and national recovery plans.

Under planned PRRO, over the period January-December 2017, WFP will provide food assistance to 220,000 food insecure people in conflict-affected eastern Ukraine through a combination of food in kind and cash based transfers.

project_name: Lifesaving Emergency Nutrition Services Scaled-up to Reach Unnerved Payams in Fangak and Nyirol Counties South Sudan
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to save lives of under 5 children and PLW suffering severe acute malnutrition and related medical complications in payams not being adequately served in Fangak and Nyirol counties. The overall objective will be achieved by:
1.	Delivering quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk at least 75% of SAM and 60% of MAM in girls and boys 6-59 months and 60% of PLW.
2.	Increasing access to integrated programs preventing under-nutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk children 6 – 23 months including through IYCF for 60% PLW. 
3.	Ensuring enhanced needs analysis of nutrition situation and robust monitoring and coordination of emergency nutrition responses. 
4.	Increasing access to safe and integrated nutrition, health and WASH responses in counties with critical levels of acute malnutrition.

The project will scale-up and expand nutrition service delivery from 6 OTP centers at existing health facilities in 3 payams in Fangak County (Manajang, Paguir and Mareang) and 2 payams in Nyirol County (Chuil and Pultruk). Through a strong outreach approach, the project will ensure that the most vulnerable single parent and women headed HHs of unreached IDPs and affected host community populations have access to high quality emergency nutrition services.  Effective programs of malnutrition prevention will include IYCF along with WASH messages to prevent AWD, and include vitamin A supplementation and deworming. CMA recognizes that insecurity creates a situation of vulnerability for PLW and children under five years. Through community mobilization, awareness raising and advocacy, the project will help communities implement appropriate protection practices to reduce risk of GBV and enable women (IDP and host community) and children to have unimpeded access to nutrition services.

project_name: Integrated Protection and PSS Response in Ninewa
project_objective:
HAI proposes a 6-month project, complementing an existing child protection project in Ninewa funded by UNICEF, to address the protection needs of IDPs, new returnees, and host community individuals from Mosul. This project will provide psychosocial support (PSS) and legal assistance through mobile services in newly retaken, and difficult to access areas in Ninewa (Hamam Ali and Al Shura Districts, Al Karama and Al Zahrai neighborhoods within Mosul). This project fills in gaps in protection services identified by the protection cluster, protection partners, and HAI during the current child protection project, including specialized PSS for survivors of trauma and specialized legal assistance for IDPs and returnees, women, girls, men, boys, and people with disabilities who have survived GBV, arrest, detention, or recruitment. HAI will respond to the protection cluster’s 1st and 2nd line response, addressing protection objective 1: providing immediate protection support to highly at risk populations, including people in difficult to reach and unstable environments and objective 2: providing specialized support to populations suffering from abuse and violence and facilitate community based support for families and people affected by the conflict. 
HAI’s 1st line response includes providing protection support to highly at risk people inside Mosul including PFA and emergency case management and ensuring passage to protected safe spaces. 2nd line response activities will include the provision of mental health and PSS, emergency legal aid in lower risk areas of Ninewa. HAI will address the critical needs of IDPs settling outside of camps. HAI mobile teams will have greater access to vulnerable populations by working through local partner NCSON, which works in and around the Mosul area. HAI has over 10 years of results based protection programming and has built close relationships with government stakeholders & local implementing partners focused on IDP protection.

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) for conflict-affected populations in Iraq
project_objective:
The Cash Consortium of Iraq (CCI)’s overall goal is to enhance the impact of MPCA through a harmonized approach, coordination between CCI partners, and maximized reach. 

To achieve this goal, the CCI has harmonized targeting, monitoring, accountability and delivery mechanisms, enabling an efficient, coordinated and well-targeted response that reaches the most vulnerable families across Iraq. CCI partners will directly implement the proposed program, building on CCI partners’ experience and learning of MPCA implementation, combined with referrals, in Iraq and the region.  The referral pathways are also a foundational element of the CCI structure, drawing upon all the protection expertise on offer and utilizing the Consortium model to efficiently refer beneficiaries between CCI partners and other agencies. This synchronized approach translates into greater value for money, efficiency and effectiveness in program implementation.

Under the first line response, the objective is to meet the emergency needs of newly displaced households (including returnees) and under the second line response, the objective is to enable highly vulnerable households (including IDPs, returnees, host community households and the protracted displaced) to meet their critical basic needs. The CCI’s full cluster response will aim to connect MPCA beneficiaries with the government social safety nets using established referral pathways. Legal support will be provided to vulnerable households to help them obtain official identification and, thus, access to government social safety nets. 

Taking a Do No Harm approach, the program will extend its reach to all vulnerable households for un-served/underserved populations, in poverty pockets and in locations where social tensions are on the rise. The program will take a whole-of-Iraq approach in locations where markets are functioning and there is high need. All CCI programming will be characterized by flexibility to respond based on needs.

The Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre
project_objective:
The Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre (IIC) is an inter agency accountability mechanism that allows aid beneficiaries to access information on existing and planned humanitarian assistance and convey feedback on and complaints about the humanitarian response in Iraq. 

The objective of this project is to ensure that feedback from callers identifies gaps in assistance, permits ongoing information exchange, influences how information is shared, and shapes how humanitarian assistance is organised and delivered. 

Accountability to Affected People (taking account, giving account and being held to account) lies at the heart of the IIC.

The Iraq IIC's primary objective is to promote two-way communication between affected populations and humanitarian actors to:
i. Empower communities through the provision of accessible and timely information on how to access services and resources required to improve their situation
ii. Help ensure efficient and effective coordination of UN agencies, funds, and programmes operating in Iraq by collecting and circulating information about the urgent needs and priorities of affected populations
iii. Support an environment of transparency and accountability by: (a) Establishing an easy-to-access and safe mechanism through which affected populations can lodge feedback, complaints, and access information on service provision; and (b) Channelling feedback and complaints to humanitarian actors to influence humanitarian programming and shape quality advocacy

•	Identification and response to individual child protection concerns through specialized services 
•	Identification, documentation, tracing and family reunification of unaccompanied and separated children with alternative care arrangements

The main objective is access to life saving WASH services for 64,000 (39,600 female and 32,400 male), people affected by recent conflict and/or natural recurring disasters in Southern Kordofan, Western and Southern Darfur, and Red Sea, including local populations, IDP's and returnees, with a special emphasis in targeting vulnerable populations such as women, children, and the elderly. The inclusion of large percentages of women in the intervention is a key objective that will not only save more lives, but to improve the quality of services to alleviate suffering for the present situation, add valuable input in the plan to help mitigate negative impacts of future life threatening occurrences and affect true inclusive sustainability for communities.

In order to reach this objective IAS will utilize an Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) approach. IAS has developed a practical field manual on IWRM that serves as guide in the implementation of its WASH programs. Practical examples include: Following hydro geological studies and community consultation, the most sustainable method for water provision will be selected. Drilling of new boreholes equipped with hand pumps are good options in most of the states’ rural areas. In areas with high demand and adequate water supply; solar powered water yards and mini water yards are a good option.  In the areas with rare to limited availability of ground water the best option might be solutions related to the heavy rainfall. 

IAS application of the IWRM approach also means that it remains flexible in the planning and execution of activities in line with best practices and in accordance with the needs identified by the communities for the WASH sector and includes mitigation planning for potential environmental issues impacted by the intervention. For more environmental, gender and other considerations, see below under 'activities and outputs'.

Objective

Since the beginning of the response, Save the Children has reached children in Donestsk GCA aand Luhansk GCA. SCI has gained funding for MPG activities from Dorcas (Netherlands MFA) and DFID in the SC Ukraine funding pipeline. The total beneficiary reached 3660 households benefitting 12024 individuals. 

SCI has implemented the MPG through bank system and national post services systems which was proven successful as conflict-affected people has the option to access money particularly those who are hard to reach.

Learnings and best practices in implementing MPG:
a.	Cross-checking of potential beneficiaries to other actors to prevent overlap.
b.	Integrated approach where protection awareness is being conducted during community mobilization, referrals from SC Education and Child Protection team
c.	Diversification of cash channel services facilitates better access and effective programming
d.	Monitoring of cash utilization prior to second tranche is a good practice to assess expenditures
e.	Based on monitoring data, MPG activities are successful as it responds to different needs (e.g. shelter, health, education, food)

Our experiences and lessons learnt will positively contribute to the successful project delivery for the next implementation phase.

SCI will be targeting:
•	80% - areas of high concern: contact line of Lugansk GCA region (Horskoe, Zolotoe, Toshkivka and Kamushevaha), contact line of Donetsk GCA  (Volnovaha, Avdeevka, Toretsk, Krasnogorovka, Mariinka etc) and contact line of Donetsk NGCA (Donetsk, Gorlivka, Yasinovata)

SCI successfully implemented Shelter light repair last winter (Dec 2015–Jan 2016) in 4 areas of GCA Donetsk contact line(Svetlodarsk, Mironovskoe, Luganskoe and Avdeevka) reaching 661 HH. The combined approach used was of providing materials and labour.This year SCI is focused at rehabilitating schools & community centers in contact line of Lugansk and Donetsk, with total amount of 21 places: 18 (1 kindergarten, 1 music school, 2 child friendly spaces, 1 youth friendly space, 2 community centers, 11 schools in Avdeevka, Torezk, Bahmut, Mironovskoe, Kramatorsk, Orlovka,Stanirza Luganskoe, Valujskoe, etc) in GCA and 3 places (kindergarten, school & lyceum, Donetsk, Gorlivka) in NGCA.SCI is funded by OFDA in rehabilitating schools in 11 oblasts. All hard components are implemented & monitored by professional engineers.
SCI has implemented winterization cash grants (1685 HH)  & shelter cash assistance (rentutilities) (1575 HH) through bank system & the national post services systems which has proven successful as beneficiaries has the option to access money particularly those in isolated/hard to reach areas. project_name: Communication with Communities activities to support information-based decision-making by affected populations and humanitarian responders in PoCs sites
project_objective:
This project seeks to support the Camp Coordination and Camp Management Cluster (CCCM) cluster by addressing communities’ need for better access to information and enabling communities to have a stronger voice and better accountability in the humanitarian response. By building on Internews work, best practice and lessons learnt from last year’s humanitarian response in South Sudan, the project’s support for humanitarian agencies across all clusters and sectors will lead to stronger Communications With Communities (CWC) and Accountability Strategies (AAP). 

The project aims to ensure that the most vulnerable communities (particularly women, children, elderly and socially excluded) affected by the conflict, have better access to reliable, accurate, timely and effective information so that they can: make informed decisions about their own lives; have a stronger voice to demand accountability to services delivered by humanitarian actors (through multiple channels of communication to deliver feedback); and are more engaged in the decision making process about the humanitarian response and service delivery.

Capturing and sharing best practice in CWC by partner organizations, and demonstrating how multiple tools and channels can be used to understand and respond better will be a strong focus. Even in the absence of an audio service, tools like the planned development of the Talk Talk Tent – a community space designed to facilitate and capture Conversations With Communities can be used to assess what is ‘trending’ in the sites – and then used by agencies to improve the impact of their work and respond with relevant information. 

This project also aims to ensure humanitarian agencies and actors have the ‘mind-set’, strategies, tools, skills and capacity to engage, listen, and respond to community driven information needs, in order to deliver more targeted and more effective services and activities that are influenced, and indeed led by communities changing needs.

project_name: Provision of community based protection to displaced and affected communities in Ukraine
project_objective:
The overall aim of the protect is to improve the protective environment for those affected, and to improve access to and quality of protection services. Delivery priority will be to populations at the line of contact and in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.  

Objectives include:   

1) Promote the Centrality of Protection in the on-going humanitarian response and support the transition to early recovery in the development response. 
2) Provision of quality protection services, including legal and other referral pathways
3) Increase capacity of government, and support community capacity to deliver quality protection services.
4) Enhance community capacity and networks to prevent gender-based violence. 
5) Engage in information sharing and solutions oriented rights based advocacy, with government, communities and other relevant stakeholders.
7) Increase protection mainstreaming to enhance the overall humanitarian response.
8) Continue protection by presence as well as systematic monitoring to support joint analysis and response.
9) Support Communty-based protection networks to empower communities and foster resilience

Specific protection activities will target the most vulnerable, predominantly in host communities: including older persons without caretakers, children, women at risk especially when head of household, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk as a result of the conflict.  Tailored assistance will be provided, including through cash.  The community based approach will seek to strengthen referral networks, improve access to services, increase awareness on basic rights and reduce discrimination.  Priority delivery will be in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.

This project will improve access to well-coordinated child protection services and psychosocial support activities for 5000 unaccompanied and separated girls and boys impacted by the conflict, children at risk and survivors to reduce  their exposure    to  violence, exploitation, stigmatization, neglect and abuse. The project will create a referral network of community stakeholders, dedicated community contacts and trained women and men social workers on child protection with focus on SGBV and PSS, within 100 communities in most affected areas.  

There will be team monitoring and response to reported grave violations of children’s rights with gender-sensitive approach and a focus on reintegration of children (girls and boys) associated with armed groups. Unaccompanied and separated children, orphans and other children with protection concerns, especially SGBV, will be prioritized for referral. Children will be assessed and receive holistic support including emergency basic needs support where necessary (e.g. when first entering and identified in IDP camps), with sensitivity on gender issue and then given PSS.  The team will trace the family or an alternative caregiver where possible using community networks, and priority will be given to tracing and reunifying UASC girls and boys with their family/ another foster family. The child will be supported to access emergency education where possible, as well as given access to child friendly clubs with appropriate gender-sensitive facilitation.

1. Facilitate safe access to emergency WASH services to vulnerable populations

3. Support extension of sustainable and equitable water distributions, including facilitating hand over to relevant government authorities

NRC will employ a phased response and in each of the stages the aim will include the following;

1.Target population have safe, sustained and equitable access to  clean water for drinking, cooking and other domestic uses
2.Target Populations  have access to  improve, gender sensitive and dignified sanitation facilities with a clean environment free of human defecation and solid waste
3.Target population understands the risks and relationship between hygiene and health and take measures to adopt preventative measures accordingly 
4.Target population have access to supplies and materials that support positive coping mechanisms and promote good hygiene behavior

The objectives will span across all the areas where NRC will carry out its interventions in Iraq in 2017.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving emergency WASH support to the IDPs and destitute vulnerable host communities’ in South Darfur, South Kordofan and Blue Nile States to meet their immediate daily WASH needs in sustained manner
project_objective:
This proposed project is an integrated approach that builds on MC’s ongoing WASH and FSL programming in the target areas, and is part of coordinated and integrated response to the lifesaving needs of an estimated 100,500 extremely vulnerable conflict-affected displaced population, host communities and returnees in Jabal Marra, El Salam and Bielel localities in South Darfur; Diling, Reif Ashargi and Abbassiya localities in South Kordofan; and El Roseires and Al Kurmuk localities of Blue Nile States.
The objective of the project is to support these communities to meet their daily immediate lifesaving WASH needs as per SPHERE and WASH sector standards. Therefore, the project aims to provide these affected populations sustained access to these basic lifesaving WASH services through the community based operation and management (CBOM) based on the cost recovery and user fee systems managed by the community-based WASH committees in a self-sustained manner in order to enhance their resilience.
This objective will be achieved through reducing the recurrent running costs for the provision of:
•	Clean and quality water supply through solar powered water systems, community operated and managed hand pumps and protected shallow wells;
•	Sanitation facilities using CLTS;
•	Hygiene promotion through CHAST and PHAST
The proposed intervention follows the strategic positioning guiding the 2017 Sudan Multiyear Humanitarian Strategy. In particular, the outcome 1 and 2 and their respective outputs are emphasized throughout and all the interventions aimed at saving lives and reducing needs and vulnerabilities by the service delivery of WASH services managed by the community based WASH committees through CBOM based on the cost recovery and user fee system.
This intervention is shaped by the continuous process of ensuring Accountability to Affected populations is respected and due consideration is also paid to gender equality, particularly considering the role of women in WASH.

188 communities are prioritized for empowerment and rehabilitation based on their vulnerability to FT, initially assessed using the OCHA VPP, supplemented with in-depth assessments taking into consideration the specific needs of women, men, children, elderly, and people with disability. Emergency and legal aid activities will be implemented across the West Bank based on needs and referrals.
 
Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Framework and coordinates with other actors meeting humanitarian needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers and ICCG coordination of response to demolitions. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSS, legal responses, settler violence interventions and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs. The Project is built on an integrated protection approach envisaged to contribute to HRP objectives: 1. The rights of Palestinians under occupation are protected in accordance with IHL/IHRL; 2. Ensure acutely-vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank have access to essential services; 3. Strengthen the ability of acutely-vulnerable Palestinian HH to cope with protracted threats & shocks. The Project further contributes to Shelter Cluster objectives (1. Shelter repair & upgrading; 2. Emergency & transitional shelter response; 3. Contingency planning & preparedness measures) and crosscutting themes (Accountability to affected populations;Protection; Gender).

project_name: Providing food security in the most vulnerable, conflict affected and hard to reach areas of the Eastern Ukraine, through daily home delivery of high caloric ready hot food to isolated, home-bound, immobile seniors and provision of  ready meals to highly vulnerable mobile seniors at the Canteens.
project_objective:
Supreme objective of the given proposal is ensuring access to high caloric, ready food intake to the exceptionally vulnerable, elderly men and women of the Eastern Ukraine, those who are unable to prepare food for themselves due to age and health related conditions.
Humanitarian agencies mostly distribute food baskets. What is vastly overlooked is the program ensuring proper food intake for persons who are unable to prepare their own meals especially home-bound (often bed-bound), single, isolated seniors residing in in the most vulnerable conflict affected and hard to reach areas of the Eastern Ukraine. 
The proposed project will ensure daily provision of the ready, high caloric food intake to the elderly beneficiaries:  1000 home-bound beneficiaries will be delivered  high caloric ready food once a day (7 times a week - via mobile groups) and 1000 canteen beneficiaries will be served hot food once a day (5 times a week) for the duration of at least 8 months.

project_name: Community Based Gender Based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response Services for Women and Girls Affected by Conflict in Iraq
project_objective:
Overall Objectives:  To improve access to GBV prevention and response services for women and girls affected by the conflict between the Government of Iraq and ISIL. 

The chronic and acute GBV concerns due to the protracted and immediate nature of the Iraq conflict requires both systems-based interventions to allow for sustainable GBV service delivery, especially age-appropriate case management services and services to address long-standing culturally-based GBV, while the onset of new acute crises and displacements requires a flexible and immediate response through emergency mobile teams that can respond quickly and effectively to emerging needs of GBV survivors, women and girls.  Through multiple modalities, this project will provide GBV prevention and response services to those who have been affected by conflict, whether they are displaced, returned to places of origin, or living in areas recently retaken by the government or in host communities.  

Specific Objectives:

1. Provide immediate, emergency GBV response services to survivors of GBV, particularly women and girls, who have been newly displaced, those residing in communities that have recently been retaken from ISIL, and those who are newly returned to their places of origin.
2. Provide and support age-appropriate, survivor centered, community-based psychosocial support services and case management services.
3. Support sustainable, systems and community-based GBV awareness raising programmes to affect behavioural change.

project_name: Emergency upgrade and repair of vulnerable households’ substandard shelters in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The aim of this project is to assist acutely vulnerable households living in substandard shelter to access adequate and safe shelters in the Gaza Strip and strengthen their capacity to cope with future shocks through a community based approach

The project will establish a shelter self-repair / upgrade mechanism through provision of conditional cash. In addition, close engagement with communities through Community Protection and Preparedness Committees (CPPC) will enable beneficiaries to increase their Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) in shelter reparation, protection and preparedness to future shocks.

The project has been designed to take into account the specific needs of men and women, as well of vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly, persons with disability (PWDs) and the chronically ill. Through fully fledged community engagement and accountability tools, they will be able to express their views and concerns from the project onset to ensure assistance is tailored to their needs, and will then receive increased support throughout project implementation. 

In order to maximize beneficiaries involvement, ACTED and MA’AN will capitalize on the expertise gained during former project by involving CPPCs throughout the project implementation, by giving them a crucial role in beneficiary selection, project monitoring, community outreach and project evaluation. Eventually, accountability to beneficiaries will be ensured by a fully-fledged Complaint Response Mechanism, in line with ACTED standard procedures across all its interventions.

This action is in line with the result 1 of the Shelter Cluster 2016 HRP  “Ensure access for women, girls, boys and elderly men to a basic level of adequate shelter” aiming at achieving the strategic objective 2 “Ensure acutely vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank have access to essential services”

project_name: PEMAPA Burundi  (Protéger les Enfants contre la Malnutrition Aiguë c’est  Préparer leur meilleur  Avenir).
project_objective:
L'ONG World Vision est présente au Burundi depuis 1995 et mets en œuvre des activités de nutrition et de sécurité alimentaires dans certaines communes des deux  provinces visée par ce projet (Rutana et Karusi). World Vision cultive une approche de renforcement des capacités des autorités locales et de la population pour une meilleure résilience au choc dans les moments difficiles. L'expérience a montré que le dépistage communautaire et la référence des enfants malnutris accomplis par les acteurs-clé communautaires volontaires au niveau provincial ne sont pas réalisés régulièrement par manque de capacités techniques de ces acteurs et des supervisions insuffisantes de la part des autorités sanitaires. La promotion des pratiques familiales-clés dans ces provinces souffre aussi d'un manque de suivi et d'appui technique réduisant les chances de prévenir la malnutrition aiguë. Le taux de malnutrition aigue modern et severe sont respectivement   a karusi 6.2 % et 3.3% et a Rutana 6.4% et 1%.
Ainsi, World Vision contribuera à la réalisation de trois  objectifs stratégiques du secteur nutrition qui visent à:
. OS1 : Mettre en place un système de surveillance nutritionnelle pour l’identification des provinces a risque élevé de malnutrition et le suivi nutritionnel des enfants 6-59 mois filles et garçons  des ménages les plus pauvres des 2 provinces les plus affectées par la malnutrition aigue
OS2 : En 2017 assurer l’accès aux soins de prise en charge de qualité  a 146751enfants 6-59 mois filles et 27331 garçons malnutris aigus des 2 provinces les plus touchées 
OS3 : En 2017, prévenir la malnutrition chez 13000 enfants 6-23 mois filles et garçons et 11135 femmes bénéficieront de  la supplémentation alimentaire et la promotion des pratiques optimales d’alimentation  dans les provinces a risque élevée de malnutrition

project_name: Provision of healthcare services for conflict affected populations in Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine.
project_objective:
The objective of the project  is to improve primary health and preventative care for populations in Luhansk Oblast, encompassing Health Cluster 2017 Objectives 1 and 3 as well as HRP 2017 Specific Objectives 2 and 3. The project is based on two results, one focusing on the access to primary health care (PHC) and medical supply, the other one on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support services for conflict-affected population located in the areas of high concern. This approach intends to address the main health-related issues identified by MdM in Ukraine since August 2015: limited access to PHC services due to the protracted crisis (especially for chronic conditions), limited access to drugs due to geographic and economic constraints, ongoing mental health and psychosocial needs due to protracted crisis and limited access to care (including gender based violence (GBV) survivors).
Through its integrated approach based on comprehensive services delivered by mobile units and strengthening of the local health system, MdM is targeting specific gender and age vulnerable groups, such as the elderly, people with chronic diseases, children and women in need of family planning.
MdM medical activities are gender-responsive, in particular through:
1. The inclusion of sexual and reproductive health (SRH)/GBV response services into its PHC package. MdM provides SRH services in all PHC facilities supported. MdM recognizes SRH services as an entry point to the prevention, identification and treatment and care of gender-based violence.
2. Advocacy around respect for the right of these populations to access appropriate health services.
Special attention is also given to disabled people and the elderly, as special awareness raising activities and trainings are focused on chronic diseases. Finally, MdM supports a community-based approach through awareness raising sessions on mental health (MH) issues at community level fostering resilience and improved community mental health.

project_name: Providing Leadership and Life Skills for Adolescents and Youth
project_objective:
Mercy Corps’ vision is to reduce the vulnerability of crisis-affected adolescents through the development of positive social networks, safe spaces and increased community engagement. Throughout the life of the program, the program will directly reach youth through drop-in sessions that provide recreational and creative outlets for expression; youth will access psychosocial support through intensive sessions delivering life skills and resilience courses, and youth will gain access to community resources through field trips and information sessions. Volunteer coaches and youth leaders will be trained as mentors and facilitators, while parents and caregivers will receive training and tools to address child protection issues and make use of referral services. Community members will be reached through youth-led awareness campaigns and social cohesion programs.
Mercy Corps’ portfolio of youth programming is critical to improving the wellbeing of youth in Iraqi society and focuses on reaching Iraqi IDPs, Syrian refugees and vulnerable host community members. Mercy Corps is expanding programming to include AFSs in Baghdad and Salah al Din governorates, in addition to centers in Erbil. Mercy Corps works with the most vulnerable, conflict-affected adolescents in the targeted communities, identifying and engaging them through a variety of tools, including specific outreach to adolescent girls. This proactive engagement of youth from a variety of backgrounds and experiences ensures greater interaction between the diversity of identities, resulting in decreased social tension and increased cohesion. Through participation in psychosocial, life skills, short-term goal setting and recreational activities, as well as youth-led social cohesion programs, adolescent girls and boys will develop leadership and decision-making skills while gaining greater confidence, self-esteem, self-efficacy and trust in those around them.

project_name: Resilience Building through Income Generation for Conflict-Affected Households in Iraq
project_objective:
To sustainably reduce the recurrent needs of vulnerable conflict-affected households in Iraq through introducing viable income generation opportunities.

The livelihoods project is part of a larger program implemented by the Cash Consortium of Iraq (CCI) addressing critical needs of newly displaced households and returnees, and extremely vulnerable host and protracted displaced households through multi-purpose cash assistance. Based on an evolved understanding of the crisis in Iraq, the program has incorporated viable income generating interventions and skills building into the program to provide vulnerable households with the means to support their household needs beyond the immediate cash assistance. This two pronged intervention will help sustainably address recurrent needs of a growing population-of-concern through meeting their immediate needs and providing livelihood opportunities for recovery, with a particular focus on women and youth for income generating activities. In 2017, the pilot in Diyala would be continued and the approach scaled up to new areas.

project_name: Strengthening the resilience of vulnerable households affected by the Boko Haram insurgency in the Far North of Cameroon by improving their food and nutrition security
project_objective:
The main objective of the project is to restore and strengthen food security in order to improve the resilience of vulnerable households in the Far North region of Cameroon

The project seeks to improve the targeted populations’ food security through the production of maize, sorghum and cowpea. Cowpea has high protein content (16 percent) and is rich in iron, vitamin B6 and magnesium, making it good for malnourished children. The cowpea which will be produced within the framework of the present project will help in reducing malnutrition in the localities targeted by this assistance.

The specific objectives are to:
-	ensure the production and dissemination of reliable food security and nutrition data at household and community levels for better early warning in the Far North region within the framework of the Food Security Thematic Group; and 
-	assist 5 000 farmer households comprising 2 500 IDP households and 2 500 host community households, mainly in the divisions of Mayo Tsanaga, Logone and Chari in the Far North region through the provision of improved seeds and fertilizers for the upcoming raining season 2016. Each household will receive 5 kg of improved maize seeds, 6 kg of improved sorghum seeds plus 6 kg of improved cowpea seeds. These seeds will enable the beneficiary household to cultivate 0.25 ha of maize, 0.25 ha of sorghum and 0.25 ha of cowpea (for a total 0.75 ha per beneficiary household). In addition, each beneficiary household will receive 25 kg of NPK fertilizer and 25 kg of urea for the cereal crop. During beneficiary selection, only households which possess land will be considered.

This project will contribute to increase the production of bread in northern rural Idleb and to improve the resilience of the local community, as both IDPs and Host Communities will be targeted. This project is made up of three interlinked components: support to an existing bakery, set up of a new mobile bakery and a baseline study to assess potential for local wheat production.
The project will contribute, either fully or partially, to 3 out of the 4 sector objectives set by the HRP 2017: the 1st the 2nd and the 3rd. By supporting the existing bakery and setting up a new mobile one, we will contribute to “improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people by emergency life-saving and regular life sustaining food assistance”, with special regard to the IDPs. The baseline study, on the other hand, will allow us - although in perspective –  to “support the life-saving livelihoods of affected households by increasing agricultural production, protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities”, as well as to “improve the capacity to deliver essential services for improved linkages with value chain through the rehabilitation/ building of productive infrastructure as well as supporting services […]”. Increasing the current production of bread and paving the way to the establishment of a local, small scale supply chain will help “restore and strengthen productive assets and create livelihood opportunities for the targeted populations, thus contributing to the overall food production and availability in Syria” (HRP 2017).

project_name: Emploi, résilience et cohésion sociale dans la bande sahélienne et la zone du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Lac Tchad en renforçant le développement local durable et en accroissant les opportunités économiques. L’intervention sera mise en place dans le cadre d’un consortium composé d’Oxfam, ACF et Care International et porté par Oxfam, en collaboration avec les partenaires locaux Chora, ARDEK et AIDER. Le projet a été élaboré en étroite collaboration avec ces trois ONG, en consultation avec l’Union Européenne, et en comptant sur une implication forte des autorités locales et des communautés ciblées (ateliers avec les autorités, échanges avec les groupements de jeunes /femmes). 

L'action proposée cible les régions du Bahr el Gazal (Oxfam), du Kanem (ACF) et du Lac (CARE), trois zones fortement affectées par le changement climatique. Différentes crises (Lybie, Boko Haram) menacent la sécurité et entrainent des mouvements de population dans ces régions, menaçant la stabilité sociale dans la zone. Le projet repose sur l’hypothèse que la redynamisation de l’économie locale  couplée à des investissements dans les secteurs de la sécurité alimentaire/nutritionnelle et de la gouvernance locale, peuvent offrir de nouvelles opportunités économiques et des rôles positifs aux ménages vulnérables. L’expérience des 3 ONG au Tchad permet de proposer une approche efficace ayant pour but de sortir durablement les populations vulnérables du “cercle vicieux” de la pauvreté. 
OS1.R1. Les femmes et jeunes ont un meilleur accès aux opportunités d’emplois et diversifient leur source de revenu, via l’appui aux filières agro-sylvo-pastorales créatrices d’emploi et à l’auto-emploi.
OS2. R1. La sécurité alimentaire des ménages est améliorée via le renforcement de leurs moyens d’existence agro-pastoraux ou l’accès à la protection sociale. 
OS2.R2. L´environnement sanitaire des populations vulnérables est amélioré.
OS3.R1. Les capacités des structures publiques de développement et des OSC au niveau local sont renforcées afin de mener des actions de développement socio-économiques durables.

project_objective:
L´action proposée vise à réduire l’impact du conflit Boko Haram et de la crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle sur les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons déplacées et hôtes les plus vulnérables en rétablissant leur dignité. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une stratégie d´intervention intégrée dans les secteurs WASH/moyens d´existence et sécurité alimentaire(MESA)/Protection.
Pour répondre aux besoins urgents des populations les plus vulnérables engendrés par cette crise dans le bassin du lac Tchad, Oxfam mène des actions d´urgence dans la cuvette Nord du Lac Tchad depuis juin 2016 (phase 1 de 8 mois, de juin 2016 à janvier 2017). Dans un contexte de mouvements de population encore importants, la réponse proposé vise à assurer une couverture des besoins de base des personnes déplacées et hôtes les plus vulnérables de la région, ainsi qu’à mettre en œuvre des activités de relèvement/LRRD, tout en garantissant et pérennisant les acquis de la première phase. L´action correspond donc à la seconde phase de réponse qu’Oxfam souhaite mettre en œuvre dans la zone à partir de mi janvier 2017 - (phase 2 de 11 mois, de janvier à décembre 2017).
Plus précisément, l´action ciblera environ 9 460 ménages, soit 47 300 personnes dans les départements de Fouli (sous-préfecture de Daboua) et de Kaya (préfecture de Bagasola) – environ 27 sites/villages (département de Fouli) et quartiers/sites dans/autour de la ville de Bagasola

project_name: W. Increasing access to education for out of school children through the Self Learning Program – Education Above All/ Educate A Child (EAA/EAC) - UNICEF partnership
project_objective:
The proposed project, as part of EAA/EAC- UNICEF partnership which is a flagship EAA/EAC and UNICEF partnership “QUEST Education”, is a contextually relevant approach to reach Out of School Children (OOSC) who are internally displaced and living in accessible, hard-to-reach and besieged areas with limited or no access to schooling due to active conflict or insecurity. The goal of the SLP and its complementary activities (i.e. psychosocial support, school learning supplies, teacher training and rehabilitation/construction/operations of learning spaces) is to deliver a comprehensive self-study course with a curriculum and an environment that is conducive to learning within a conflict situation so OOSC who have missed out on regular schooling opportunities continue their learning and can ultimately return to a formal educational setting. Also, as the SLP is looking to scale-up, a secondary goal is to refine and enhance the program itself and look for ways to scale it up in Syria and potentially in the neighbouring countries hosting Syrian refugee children.

Proposed objectives:
1)	Increase access to education for 32,000 out-of-school children through the SLP
a.	Increase access to protective learning spaces and learning materials where required (includes construction/rehabilitation of learning spaces and provision of prefabricated rooms)
b.	Expand access to psychosocial support and recreational activities
c.	Training for teachers and resource persons for the SLP
2)	Strengthen the SLP program components, such as quality standards, learning measurements and M&E for the program, and explore ways to sustain and scale this to other Syrian OOSC, including in the neighbouring refugee host countries

project_name: Protection of Refugee Children in Minawao camp and Vulnerable Children in host Community around
project_objective:
Since May 2013, attacks by the Nigerian based militant group Boko Haram have intensified along the Cameron’s northwest border resulting in the looting of villages, killing of innocent civilians as well as mass kidnappings, including of children. The massive human rights violations and escalation of violence caused continuous influx of refugees resettled in Minawao (Far North Region – Cameroon). As of October , UNHCR has registered and resettled almost 60,000 refugees in Minawao camp. 36,000 are children (61% of the total number of refugees) in need of psychosocial support and at risk of violence, exploitation, abuses and neglect. Minawao camp is settled near villages of Gawar, Gadala, Zamai, and minawao villages itself, where vulnerables children are in need of Protection

The projects aim to provide essential child protection services to refugee children as well as those from the host communities around Minawao Camp with a specific focus on facilitating access to services offering support to women and children affected by family separation, psychosocial distress. The response includes providing psychosocial support to children and adolescent (boys and girls) through child friendly spaces, youth clubs, and support to unaccompanied and separated children in terms of psychosocial support, family tracing, identification and monitoring of foster families and support as needed.

In the long term, the aim is that the community will have the capacity to ensure child protection mechanisms and activities for the children of their community.

Providing child protection assistance to vulnerable, conflict-affected IDP and host populations in recently liberated areas of Ninewa
project_objective: In response to the ongoing humanitarian crisis in northern Iraq, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) will provide access to specialized services and psychosocial support for conflict affected children, and strengthen the capacity of children, their families, the community, and other CP actors to prevent and respond to child protection concerns. By combining a static space and a mobile child protection team, the IRC will ensure children are safe in their homes and wider communities, and that they receive support when they experience harm via community-based and individualized child protection programming. This multi-faceted approach will ensure the immediate care and protection of children, while also enabling long term stability and development for children, bolstering their resilience, and increasing their safety. The IRC team will be comprised of one Senior CP Officer who will supervise and support three caseworkers and one child protection officer. The team will be based out of IRC’s Dohuk office, but will operate its static space in an urban area of Ninewa, with the mobile team deploying to underserviced urban areas in coordination with other humanitarian CP actors. The team will conduct activities from its static space to provide children with the tools to focus, regulate their emotions, interact well with others and cope with stress and challenges in support of mitigating the affect that crisis and conflict have on children’s feelings of safety, well-being and ability to learn. The IRC’s CP caseworkers will be supported to respond to individual child protection cases using a case management approach for children who are identified as needing specialized support. With the child’s informed consent, caseworkers will assess the child and the child’s protective environment, develop a case plan to respond to child protection issues with the child and the child’s family where appropriate, and implement the plan with the child until the case is closed.

project_name: Nationwide cholera prevention and response
project_objective:
Contribute to reduce the cholera related morbidity and the mortality of the population of Haiti in 2017 with the objective to reach the annual incidence rate of 0.1% by December 2018as per the Medium-Term Phase of the Elimination Plan. The project will contribute to the three pillars of the Plan as follow:
1. Coordination and support to decision-making (surveillance)
2. Access to preventive healthcare (OCV social mobilization, OCV household water component, Emergency health care departmental funds)
3. Cutting the transmission in communities (alert-response strategy, emergency water chlorination, quick repairs of water systems at risk)
Sub-Objectives:
1) improve the alert and response coordination at national and departmental 
2) improve early detection and ensure consistent monitoring of the disease trends
3) prevent and control transmission of cholera among affected and at risk populations through rapid response and the implementation of the Oral Cholera Vaccination campaign in the Centre department  
4) reduce the vulnerability to cholera in the most exposed areas

Coordination activities will be ensured by UNICEF staff. Response activities will be carried out through UNICEF long-term NGO partners implementing the response strategy since early 2014. OCV social mobilization will be ensured by supporting MSPP department  directorates and household chlorination strategies will be implemented by NGOs partners in the Centre.

The focus of the project will be equally on women and male headed IDP households with priority to be given to families with the lowest income levels and the highest number of children under the age of 13. 

The pilot has the other main objective to provide the Municipalities of Hargeisa and Mogadishu with adequate technical expertise, capacity building and financial support to establish a municipal rental housing system  to provide durable and sustainable shelter solutions and secure land tenure to protracted urban IDPs. The objective is to create the basis on which future reinvestment capital can be generated for continuation of durable rental housing provision to other displaced populations in Hargeisa and Mogadishu. The project goal is to provide the local governments with the initial support to initiate a government owned, sustainable and self-financing approach to provide durable shelter solutions to protracted urban IDP populations.

project_name: Advancing the Future of Iraq’s Displaced Youth II
project_objective:
Goal: Enable conflict-affected youth to access education in partnership with the public sector and civil society.
• Objective 1: Increased ability of displaced, returnee and vulnerable host community youth, especially girls and young women, to enroll in education. 
Mercy Corps will work with vulnerable out-of-school  youth ages 10-20, with a particular focus  on girls not receiving government sponsored education. Youth will receive access to counselor, mediator and other services, enabling their return to education. The program prioritizes girls because they tend to be out of school at higher rates and face greater barriers to re-entry. To ensure comprehensive support, Mercy Corps will provide psychosocial training to counselors and mediators.
• Objective 2: Community and local, provincial and national government take action to improve access to education. 
Mercy Corps will establish and support Community Education Action Groups (CEAGs), district level Task Forces and a national Policy Advocacy Group to address barriers to education. An awareness campaign will raise community awareness of the importance of education and the rights and options of out-of-school youth to access government education programs.
• Objective 3: Improved quality and increased accessibility of supplemental education programs to support access to education.
In partnership with the Ministry of Education, Mercy Corps will activate MoE-licensed accelerated learning centers where youth aged 10-18 can complete primary education and obtain certification. MC will also provide preparatory courses to youth aged 12-20 to enable them to complete their secondary education and take final examinations.
• Objective 4: Preposition temporary learning spaces and emergency education response materials and train education professionals to provide support to vulnerable adolescents and youth.

project_name: Conflict affected families in Iraq have improved access to essential non-food items.
project_objective:
Conflict affected families in Iraq, including newly displaced IDPs, protractedly displaced IDPs, returnees, and host communities, have improved access to essential non-food items.
IDPs fleeing from the Mosul offensive are highly mobile and, as a consequence, are unable to carry many of their possessions. This results in a diversity of unmet needs, further compounded by their continued mobility. In order to meet immediate needs, Mercy Corps employs light NFI kits that provide vulnerable families with the resources to reach their destination with dignity. NFI distributions also remain an option in final settlements where there is limited or insecure access to local markets. In these situations, the standard NFI kits, more comprehensive than the light kits and in line with cluster and SPHERE standards, will be utilized, when multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) is not feasible, to provide longer-term responses.

project_name: Conflict affected families in Iraq are provided lifesaving WASH services in line with scale and speed of displacement from Mosul, and have improved access to appropriate facilities and hygiene practices.
project_objective:
Conflict affected families in Iraq are provided lifesaving WASH services in line with scale and speed of displacement from Mosul, and have improved access to appropriate facilities and hygiene practices.
The first line emergency WASH intervention will enable access to safe water for IDPs through water trucking, water treatment, and installation of water tanks (including water disinfection and testing at water source and distribution points), in addition to provision of bottled water. Sanitation will be addressed through provision of emergency latrines, garbage bins, and waste disposal services. Hygiene will be addressed through delivery of key hygiene messages and provision of emergency showers, and for the IDPs receiving NFI kits, they will receive soap/buckets/jerry cans. In geographic areas with greater stability (Anbar, Baghdad, parts of Salah al-Din), Mercy Corps will additionally provide WASH support to community households, returnees, and schools. This includes repairing and installing adequate water and sanitation facilities for IDP students and highly vulnerable households, combined with provision of hygiene promotion training for students to support these initiatives.

(b) Provision of medical and psycho-social  assistance to GBV victims among IDPs, Refugees, Returning and other targeted populations in humanitarian crisis
(c) Capacity building through training of  health staff on Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for them to be able to provide emergency reproductive health services among IDPs, returnees, other target populations in humanitarian crisis and the host communities, training doctors on emergency obstetric and neonatal care (EmONC), safe delivery and family planning in order  to respond to complications during pregnancy, training health staff on family planning and training midwives on safe delivery; and training midwives on Maternal nutrition
(d) Conducting integrated community outreach targeting nomadic and hard to reach populations
(e) Nutrition Screening of pregnant women
(e) Provision of Emergency Reproductive Health supplies to facilities providing emergency reproductive health services
(f) Provision of iron and folic acid 
(g) Providing support to develop and emergency operations plan for emergency reproductive health.

project_name: Shelter Upgrades for Sub-Standard Housing in Gaza
project_objective:
CRS proposes a shelter project to upgrade 300 sub-standard housing units for acutely vulnerable households, with a focus on winterization and protection.  This intervention is in direct alignment with the second strategic objective of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) to “Ensure acutely-vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank have access to essential services, focusing on shelter,” Shelter Cluster Activity 1 that underscores: “Protection of acutely-vulnerable groups through repair and upgrading of substandard or damaged shelters,” and finally Shelter Cluster Activity 2.3 that promotes an “Emergency NFI or shelter response to flooding, winter or summer weather.” 

The project ensures the full participation of the most vulnerable groups, namely female heads of households, elderly and disabled persons through an innovative approach of accompaniment. Each household will be paired with a technical advisor from CRS’ on-going cash-for-internship program who will serve as a facilitator to help families develop upgrade plans reflective of all household members. The technical advisors will be trained in protection, gender principles and winterization techniques. They will also receive guidance from CRS on participatory methods for working with families. Technical advisors will accompany all beneficiaries throughout the project term.

Building upon on-going shelter work in the Khan Younis governorate, CRS will expand into Middle Area and Rafah, targeting a minimum of 50 female heads of households and prioritizing assistance to elderly and disabled persons.
Through this approach of accompaniment, beneficiaries—especially the most vulnerable—will be fully equipped to actively participate and benefit from the project.

project_name: Strengthening community-based protection mechanisms for South Sudanese Refugees in WNS
project_objective:
The project aims at reducing the vulnerability of South Sudanese Refugees (SSR) and host community members to protection risks related to firewood collection and food insecurity linked to the adoption of negative coping strategies among which the monetization of food for fuel. In order to do this, the project will focus on improving community-based self-protection and referral mechanisms, promoting the use of Fuel Efficient Stoves which reduces the consumption of cooking fuel and providing charcoal vouchers for most vulnerable new arrivals reducing their need for buying and/or collecting cooking fuel.
The project objective is in line with the MYHRP Outcome 2 "" Displaced populations refugees, returnees and host communities meet their basic needs and/or access basic services while increasing their self-reliance"" particularly Outputs 2.1 "" Assistance provided to affected communities through vulnerability-based targeting"" and 2.2 "" People in need continue to have sustainable access to quality basic services"".
The project objective and results are aligned with the 2017 RCF Sector Strategy which emphasizes the need to integrate of Safe Access to Fuel and Energy (SAFE) strategies in the refugee response interventions. Indeed, according to the Sector Strategy “access to energy remains a cross-cutting issue affecting the protection, health, education and ability of refugees to engage in other productive tasks. Many refugees lack access to clean and sustainable energy for cooking and lighting and refugee households have been reported to exchange food for fuel.”

project_objective: This project aims to provide life saving WASH assistance to mitigate the suffering of populations affected by natural or man made disasters and reflects all 3 outcomes of the Multi Year Humanitarian Response Plan strategy. Under Outcome 1 IOM will provide life saving assistance to people newly displaced by conflict or natural disasters in an effort to recreate pre emergency conditions using early recovery approaches to improve the overall access to WASH services, connecting the need for short term emergency interventions with long term solutions and applying development principles by working directly with local communities to facilitate ownership and accountability. The objective is to not only focus on WASH emergency interventions but gradually contribute to socio economic inclusion of forcibly displaced populations and returnees by directly increasing access to basic services for the displaced and host communities and indirectly increasing employment opportunities. Under Outcome 2 IOM seeks to improve and sustain access to safe water in target communities especially in Blue Nile, Durdeb, Abyei, North Darfur and South Darfur as these communities primarily rely on agriculture and livestock, therefore water is critical to their livelihoods. Under Outcome 3 improving and sustaining access to safe water and sanitation facilities and hygiene messages will address malnutrition related risks and increase community resilience to disease outbreaks. IOM will consider emergency water provision, access to proper sanitation facilities and hygiene campaigns; coupled with the establishment and rehabilitation of water points. This will include environmental impact mitigation such as the provision of solar technology to power water points and monitoring ground water to moderate depletion levels. Exit strategies will be developed to alleviate aid dependency in protracted emergencies by strengthening self reliance and facilitating community solutions in a more holistic approach

project_name: Emergency Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Yemen - Food Security and Livelihoods Component
project_objective:
To restore livestock-based productive assets of conflict-affected households.

Restoration of livestock-based productive assets for at-risk populations affected by the conflict is a key objective of the ongoing humanitarian response and is directly aligned with the strategic objectives of the 2017 Yemen Humanitarian Response plan (i.e. ensuring that humanitarian action supports resilience and sustainable recovery). IMC, in its integrated approach to the emergency response in Taiz Governorate, proposes to continue ongoing livestock support interventions to include: voucher-based restocking support to conflict-affected households in Mawyah and Dimnat Khadir Districts; improved access to livestock feed; training and equipping community animal health workers; and conducting mass vaccination and deworming campaigns for sheep and goats in Maqbanah District. The livelihoods restoration component will be integrated with ongoing CMAM activities in Dimnat Khadir and Mawyah Districts, while emergency vaccination and deworming interventions will target the catchment population in Maqbanah District. The intervention is expected to contribute towards shortening the relief phase for CMAM beneficiaries and strengthening IMC’s overall emergency response in the targeted program areas. This type of household support is critical to maintain as a number of other partners are focused purely on emergency food commodity and/or food voucher distributions, while IMC has engaged in emergency food voucher distributions under other funding in Taiz, it is also critical that such medium-duration assistance be maintained to ensure that households have basic resources to improve their nutritional and food security status, as well as livelihoods options in the somewhat longer term

project_objective:
• Better Learning Project (BLP) is a school based intervention combining psycho social and educational approaches. The first stage of the program (BLP 1) is carried out by teachers and targets students by stimulating their resilience and natural recovery process. They are provided with explanations of what normal reactions after crisis are, and taught relaxation methods to enhance their normal coping resources while the second phase (BLP 2) targets children with chronic problems that severely affect their school functioning, including behavioral problems, bed wetting, and sleep disturbances such as nightmares, depression and concentration problems. 
•Provision of capacitation grants to allow target schools to meet the gap in educational materials;
•Rehabilitation of MoEHE schools to provide physical and climate protection and access to adequate WASH facilities 

The proposed project is in line with the SRPs of the Education and Wash Cluster. In education the project relates to SO1 ‘Safe access to school, quality learning spaces and/or essential educational services’ and SO2’ School based psycho social support’. In WASH it relates to SO2 ‘ensure basic WASH services for conflict affected or vulnerable populations’. The psycho social and physical environment strongly affect the learning environment of students and impact the way they learn including their well being, belonging, personal safety, privacy, protection and dignity. Schools which remain with damages from the war are a physical reminder of trauma’s and nightmares for children.

project_objective:
This project aims to achieve objective 2 and 3 within the 2017 WASH Cluster Response by expanding coverage of water and sanitation services and hygiene practices in at risk communities and supporting the extension of sustainable, equitable water and sanitation services and facilitate the handover of operations and maintenance to communities and national actors. 

Specifically, this project will target SO 1 (WASH support to returnees and protracted IDPs/HCs) and SO 3 (durable, inclusive, equitable services, for IDPs/HCs). With the rehabilitation of the 8 water treatment plants within Tikrit area, Salah Al Din province, our aim is to provide WASH assistance to over 50,000 IDPs, returnee and host community beneficiaries by expanding services to people with acute vulnerabilities and restoring and extending water systems and connecting users to existing facilities and public networks in Salah Al Din.

In Al Anbar, this project will target SO 1 (WASH support to returnees and protracted IDPs/HCs) and SO 3 (durable, inclusive, equitable services, for IDPs/HCs). With the rehabilitation of the 11 water treatment plants, water networks and 2 sewage treatment plants within Ammeriya Al Fallujah and Fallujah, Al Anbar, our aim is to provide WASH assistance to over 350,000 returnee and host community beneficiaries by expanding services to people with acute vulnerabilities and restoring and extending water systems, connecting users to existing facilities and public networks.

Objectives within Salah Al Din and Al Anbar will target 50% FULL Cluster response and 50% 2nd Line response. Our project does not cover the full WASH package as other actors in the geographical areas are covering the 1st Line needs of the beneficiaries. We are providing 2nd Line and Full cluster responses to improve the sustainability of the required WASH upgrades and increase the exit strategy methodology.

The proposed objective is reached through mentoring programs, awareness raising activities to sensitize the community on the importance of parental participation; strengthen capacity of SMCs through training in the development of school growth plans & budgeting. Emphasis will be given to increase girl’s enrolment/retention rates; including life-saving messages in peace education, WASH, child protection, girls’ education, GBV, early marriage, HIV/AIDS in school.

project_name: Protecting the Rights of Palestinian Minors Detained by Israel in the West Bank
project_objective:
This project will expose the procedures used by the military in the arrest and interrogation of minors in the West Bank and lead to the preservation of the minors’ rights by requiring the military to detain them per the Israel Youth Law instead of the military law currently in force.  The action will promote accountability for violence and the violation of rights of Palestinians under occupation, particularly the young, helping to address a key Protection Cluster objective.

It will require detention of minors be according to the Israel Youth Law, by invitation and prior notification, during daylight hours only, and with full presence of a parent or guardian or attorney at all stages of detention, including interrogation only by a trained youth interrogator. While the Covenant on the Rights of the Child, signed and ratified by Israel, is the basic tool for protection, the Israel Youth Law incorporates many of its elements and expands them to specify how these rights are to be guaranteed.

The vast majority of Palestinian minors detained by Israel in the West Bank are males, but their arrest and mistreatment affects all of their family members of whom an average of 50 percent are women and girls.  By exposing the treatment of their detained sons and siblings and pressing for change, the action will relieve suffering and provide recourse to address wrongs to all family members.

Results statement: 70-80 minors detained by Israel in the West Bank in 2016-17 and their 400 family members will see Israel’s unlawful and harmful practices during arrest, interrogation and detention of minors exposed and challenged in the Israeli judicial system. Through the project’s legal challenges and detailed, factual reporting, Israel will be pressured to change its illegal practices and respect its commitments to protect the Palestinian population under occupation, especially its most vulnerable members, children and their families who undergo the trauma of arrest and detention.

Through the proposed program, MC (MC) will address the poor housing conditions currently affecting the quality of life of vulnerable families and forcing them to live horrible conditions. project_name: Accountability for victims of Israeli 2014 Operation Protective Edge and Accountability of victims of Israeli violations of IHL and IHRL in Access Restricted Areas
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is seeking for accountability by resuming the legal interventions, already instituted, on behalf of victims of Israeli attacks occurred in the context of the Israeli Operation Protective Edge that took place in the summer of 2014. 

The second objective relates to Accountability for victims of violations occurred in the  eastern ground and western maritime Access Restricted Areas of the Gaza Strip 

Those objectives are directly linked to Humanitarian Response Plan Country Level Strategic Objective 1: The rights of Palestinians under occupation are protected in accordance with International Humanitarian Law, IHL, and International Human Rights Law, IHRL, and linked to strategic result statement 1 of the Protection Cluster: 1. Increased respect for International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights Law and Accountability for Violations 

Background:

During and after the Operation, the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights, PCHR, has documented hundreds of Israeli violations to the Israeli obligations underlined pursuant to the IHL and IHRL applicable at armed conflicts. Basically, the violations are pertinent to violations of basic principles under IHL, such as distinction, proportionality, and precautionary principles. 

Regarding the second object stated above, PCHR seeks fund to continue documenting Israeli violations of IHL and IHRL in the Access Restricted Areas. The Access Restricted Areas, or the No Go Zone, includes the agricultural plots near the fence separating the Gaza Strip and Israel. The farmers at those areas are systematically attacked by the Israeli forces. In addition, the  Access Restricted Areas includes the maritime area, as fishermen are allowed to access only 6 nautical miles off the Gaza shore, and even within the 6 nautical miles, the Israeli gunboats attack fishermen and confiscate  their fishing boats.
