WAC is a human right organization and a partner for Human Rights & IHL Secretariat, has received  core funding and built sound experience in applying IHL and IHRL in protecting and empowering vulnerable women and girls and monitoring and documenting violations of women's rights.

The affected population includes IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host communities. The project is line with the three FSL Sector Strategic Objective 1, 2 and 3;  it is in line with the Multi Year Humanitarian strategy (2017 2019) Outcome 1: Populations affected by natural or man made disasters receive timely assistance during and in the aftermath of a shock; and Outcome 2 which aims to increase resilience and risk management capacities at community and policy levels; and will contribute to Outcome 3: Vulnerable residents in targeted areas have improved nutrition status and increased resilience. project_name: Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM): Tracking, Registration and Verification of IDPs, Returnees, and Other Affected Populations in Sudan.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to improve the efficacy and accuracy of targeted humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations (focusing on new and protracted IDPs, returnees and refugees) by providing humanitarian partners with accurate and timely information (number of affected population, vulnerability status, demographic data, place of origin, place of displacement). 

The Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) is IOM’s primary set of tools used to track and monitor displacement and population mobility. It is designed to regularly and systematically capture, process and disseminate information to enable a better understanding of movements and evolving needs of populations on the move, and to provide the information needed by humanitarian partners to adequately address the life saving and protection needs of mobile populations. Detailed information will be provided on the availability and gaps of basic services within settlements, and will alert relevant responsible parties on where the most acute needs are. Information on population movement will also be provided through the early warning system that will be established through this project. 

This project contributes to the Multi Year Humanitarian Response Plan Outcome 1: “Populations affected by natural or man made disasters receive timely assistance during and in the aftermath of the shock.”

(2)	Ensure effective protection of refugees, asylum seekers, refugee returnees and those with undetermined nationality status, with particular attention to vulnerable groups including children, youth, women at risk, survivor/victims of trafficking and kidnap;

project_name: Provision of first-line assistance to newly displaced populations and remainees in Mosul and surrounding areas (Ninewa governorate).
project_objective:
The overall objective is to ensure that vulnerable populations affected by Mosul Operations and the violence in Northern Iraq receive immediate, efficient and life-saving humanitarian assistance.

In line with the objective 1 of the Shelter and NFI cluster “Provide safe, appropriate emergency shelter and distribute critical life-saving non-fond items to vulnerable populations in priority locations”, FRC wishes to scale-up the immediate response to identified humanitarian needs, gaps and constraints linked with the current military operations to retake Mosul and continued violence across Ninewa governorate. Lots of conflict-affected populations fleeing ISIS controlled-territories or trapped in the areas of combat remain neglected or un-served due to the volatility of the situation and the difficulty to access the violence prone areas (Mosul and surrounding areas). This analysis led the IRCS and FRC to design a project aiming at filing these gaps, addressing the basic needs of the newly IDPs and remainees (2500 HHs) by pre-positioning and distributing standardized, seasonally-appropriate non-food item kits in priority locations, through a Rapid response mechanism (72h). 
This action will be the opportunity to strengthen the operational capacity of IRCS to provide an emergency response to large scale disasters. The response must also be planned with a high degree of flexibility and the project locations may have to be revised to take into account sudden or unforeseen population movements of the IDPs.

Direct beneficiaries will be IDPs and remainees who are temporarily left aside from the coordinated humanitarian assistance system. The project aims at providing NFI assistance to an estimated 2,500 households, particularly women, children, the elderly and the poorest of the poor families. Assistance will help newly-displaced and accessible persons as well as existing vulnerable population in hard-to-reach areas to meet their immediate needs.

project_name: Information Management and Capacity Strengthening Centre for Humanitarian Partners in Iraq
project_objective:
Having a national information management (IM) capacity to effectively respond to the humanitarian crisis in Iraq remains a challenge for the coordination mechanism.  Having timely, relevant, and accurate information and IM tools to enable decision makers to effectively, appropriately plan prioritized responses is an ongoing need. 
The on-going record high rate of security and explosive  incidents  has further deteriorated the situation in the country which is a major challenge for the government and humanitarian actors resulting in increased levels of mobility impairment amongst  people in need and actors responding to the humanitarian crisis.

iMMAP aims to leverage its extensive experience in emergency and development work in Iraq through it national capacity to address this need.   

iMMAP will be working to:

-Strengthen governmental information management capacity for humanitarian coordination. 
-Enhance national capacity for humanitarian information management within the clusters. 
-Enhance the information management capacity of key partners involved in the coordination mechanism
-Provide information on security risks for the whole of Iraq, publish analytical biweekly and facilitating threat warnings and the SMS alert system.  This is an expansion of the current dedicated Mosul Risk Mitigation Information Management Center where iMMAP rapidly assesses the level of explosive contamination and security situation to set up informed safety, security and risk management systems in new contexts and rapid onset emergency response situations to humanitarian actors  in the Mosul response.


The following cluster objective is addressed through this project:

“Facilitate access, coordinate common needs assessments and analysis, provide guidance on targeting, delivery mechanisms and impact monitoring, mobilize resources to cover critical gaps and produce standardized information products”.

X Emergency WASH intervention to conflict affected population in Hassakeh, Aleppo and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
The Syrian Arab Republic is now in its sixth year of civil crisis and a political solution remains elusive. Human rights violations and abuses continue to occur in the context of widespread insecurity and in disregard of international law, international humanitarian law, and human rights law. Over 220,000 people have been killed, about half of them civilians, although the Syrian Arab Republic Observatory for Human Rights reckons that this figure may be much higher. Over one million injured. Under normal circumstances, and using the country’s pre-crisis population growth rate, Syrian Arab Republic’s population by 2015 would have been expected to exceed 23 million; however, with out-migration and conflict-related deaths over the last four years this figure is now thought to be about 18.2 million. 
Syria’s water crisis has deepened along with the conflict; water availability is about half what it was before the crisis began in 2011. Ongoing violence and heavy clashes have caused severe damage to pipelines and other water infrastructure, and municipal workers are often unable to carry out the necessary repairs. Frequent power cuts make it hard for technicians and engineers to pump water to civilians. Some areas receive only one hour of electricity a day and cuts lasting up to four days are reported. 
People living in areas where the piped infrastructure is dysfunctional suffer from reduced quality, inferior quantity and uncertain availability - some 69 % of the entire population. Private tankers or other potentially risky sources are the main form of supply, leaving consumers at greater risk of water-borne diseases and vulnerable to high prices and price fluctuation. The most affected groups are (a) the most vulnerable IDPs living in unfinished buildings and informal settlements where WASH services are often far below minimum standard, (b) the people living in besieged and HTR areas and (c) the socio-economically disadvantaged families

project_name: Community–based Nutrition Integrated Programme (CNIP)
project_objective:
Project goal: To improve the nutrition status of children under five and women of reproductive age in Kass IDP camps, host communities, and nearby rural communities in South Darfur.

Objective 1: Women and men empowered and engaged to promote proper family nutrition.
Key to this project is improving community awareness and public education about reducing risks to food insecurity, malnutrition and related health risks and sustainable household livelihoods. By engaging the community at large along with community leaders, parents, mothers, fathers, youth and partner institutions, the project seeks lasting interventions to build the resilience of the affected community.  Local input can help shape project plans, ensure response to local needs, and build support for challenges surrounding malnutrition and its underlying causes. Conducting a community consultation process will facilitate relationships with community stakeholders and leaders and leverage existing community assets and practices, and identify potential threats (i.e. individuals or structures concerned about planned project activities).  Building community organization capacity, enhancing social cohesion, and building social assets (formal and informal local institutions) is the focus for this project. 

Objective 2: Facilities capacities strengthened to enable quick recovery of malnourished people.
To ensure continuity of service delivery for the communities in need, strengthening the technical and material capacity of health institutions is critical.  A participatory assessment will be conducted and a plan will be made to identify the role of each partner to address the gaps within the facilities around the project areas. Identified support includes: provision of medical supplies, drugs, maintenance of rooms, training and incentives. The project assumes that if key needs of the facilities are fulfilled, user communities will get easy access to services, improving the cure and rehabilitation rate.

The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the stability and the security of the targeted local communities through livelihood support for IDPs, prevent radicalisation and reinforcement of local public services by supporting local governments and community-based structures. The project will allow the beneficiaries to manage and coordinate a process to build resilience of conflict affected communities. It will also empower affected populations including young women and men, to become drivers of economic recovery, innovation and economic development. Consequently, this project will contribute to peaceful coexistence among IDPs, returnees, refugees and host/local communities.

There are three outcomes expected:
Outcome 1: Vulnerable groups are resilient to the socio economic consequences of the crisis (especially youth and women among IDPs, host/local communities and returnees)

project_name: Integrated emergency assistance to Palestinian refugees from Syria, Libya, Yemen and Iraq in the Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
The project will aim at providing life-saving emergency assistance to displaced Palestinian refugees who fled from conflict zones in Syria, Libya, Iraq and Yemen back into the Gaza Strip. The proposed intervention will support them through Transitional Shelter Cash Assistance and direct access to food through vouchers, while also building the capacity of their representatives to provide basic protection services.

Considering the extreme vulnerability identified among some targeted beneficiaries, the project will have lifesaving impact. The proposed assistance is time critical, in so far as the assessments conducted reveal that the coping capacities of targeted populations is exhausted, and that any further deterioration of their vulnerability could have lethal consequences. project_name: Start Up of Agricultural Activities in support of Women Heads of HHs in Rural Idleb
project_objective:
Contribute to increase the food security of the local and displaced population in the North of Syria, by stimulating their resilience and social cohesion through agricultural activities of self-reliance and income generation. 
540 female heads of households engage in agricultural activities of self-reliance and income generation, thus improving their food security condition and preventing the adoption of negative and irreversible coping strategies.
Through this proposal we want to contribute to the providing of a type of support to the beneficiaries that is focused on maintaining and/or returning to sustainable livelihood activities, in order to allow them to transition to a progressive detachment from humanitarian aid. project_objective:
L´action proposée vise à réduire l’impact du conflit Boko Haram et de la crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle sur les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons déplacées et hôtes les plus vulnérables en rétablissant leur dignité. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une stratégie d´intervention intégrée dans les secteurs WASH/moyens d´existence et sécurité alimentaire(MESA)/Protection.
Pour répondre aux besoins urgents des populations les plus vulnérables engendrés par cette crise dans le bassin du lac Tchad, Oxfam mène des actions d´urgence dans la cuvette Nord du Lac Tchad depuis juin 2016 (phase 1 de 8 mois, de juin 2016 à janvier 2017). Dans un contexte de mouvements de population encore importants, la réponse proposé vise à assurer une couverture des besoins de base des personnes déplacées et hôtes les plus vulnérables de la région, ainsi qu’à mettre en œuvre des activités de relèvement/LRRD, tout en garantissant et pérennisant les acquis de la première phase. L´action correspond donc à la seconde phase de réponse qu’Oxfam souhaite mettre en œuvre dans la zone à partir de mi janvier 2017 - (phase 2 de 11 mois, de janvier à décembre 2017).
Plus précisément, l´action ciblera environ 9 460 ménages, soit 47 300 personnes dans les départements de Fouli (sous-préfecture de Daboua) et de Kaya (préfecture de Bagasola) – environ 27 sites/villages (département de Fouli) et quartiers/sites dans/autour de la ville de Bagasola

project_name: Early Recovery Assistance to IDPs, Returnees & Host Communitiesin the Central African Republic
project_objective:
The proposed project Early Recovery Assistance for displaced persons, returnees and host communities in the Central African Republic (CAR) aims at assisting sustainable (re)integration and return of the displaced populations to their areas of choice. It also aims at augmenting the resilience capacities of host communities in settlements where internally displaced people (IDPs) are, de facto, integrated after prolonged periods of displacement.

Through an integrated settlement approach (e.g. Peace Villages developed by IOM in the North of CAR, Kabo, Moyenne Sido), the project aims at assisting populations to rebuild resilience by supporting the creating of income generating activities and infrastructure rehabilitation, creating conditions conducive to sustainable return and integration and peaceful coexistence. 

The objective of the here proposed project is to support the newly elected Government of CAR in ensuring the continuity of humanitarian interventions, while laying the foundations for an effective and sustainable transition to recovery and development and most importantly to adequately implement the Kampala convention for durable solutions for displaced population. IOM has been and will continue working alongside existing humanitarian mechanisms in order to assist in reducing and preventing the impacts of, and recovering from, the longer-term consequences of crises, in particular its effect on human mobility and displacement and in ensuring conditions are conducive to meeting the complex needs of a sustainable return and reintegration. To this end, IOM is participating actively in the durable solutions group as well as the return working groups in the different geographic zones.

project_name: Preventing violence and increasing the protection of civilians in South Sudan
project_objective:
NP's overall objective is: To effectively respond, prevent and reduce protection concerns of conflict affected communities in South Sudan.

This objective will contribute to HRP Objective 1: Immediate lifesaving assistance provided to address the urgent protection needs of the most vulnerable (including vulnerable women, unaccompanied children, elderly, disabled and survivors of sexual violence in conflict), Objective 2:  Enhanced prevention programming to mitigate risks from the consequences of conflict or displacement and Objective 4: Enhanced protection assessment and monitoring to inform protection and the overall humanitarian response. 

The activities are designed to increase the safety and security of civilians and saving lives of civilians affected by violent conflict through risk mitigation, deterrence, protection through presence, strengthening local protection mechanisms, community based psychosocial support and protection mainstreaming. Project activities are implemented in both static locations, as well as through mobile response missions that allow protection officers to respond to the most urgent needs throughout the country. Specific and unique needs of women, men, boys and girls are incorporated into all interventions.

project_name: Provision of general food assistance in the form of regular in-kind monthly food rations and ready-to-eat rations in the initial phase of displacement.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project: saving lives, sustaining lives and protecting livelihoods through the provision of emergency and regular food assistance to the most vulnerable families affected by the crisis. This contributes to SO1.
Based on the Food and Agriculture Sector 2018 sector strategy, approximately 6.5 million people are facing acute food insecurity with an additional 4 million at risk of falling into a situation of being food insecure. IDPs and people in besieged and Hard to Reach areas in addition to female headed households are between the most vulnerable groups that need food assistance to meet their minimum consumption needs. Women are increasingly becoming family breadwinners, heading more than third of the households.  Assistance to vulnerable groups with focus on female headed household will be prioritized. In addition, if the situation changed allowing a significant number of returnees among the IDPs and refugees, WFP will consider this group in the emergency general food assistance. WFP will consider various modalities as appropriate: including in-kind food assistance (Main modality for GFD) as well as cash based transfer (CBT). 
Emergency general food assistance is one of the four main activities/projects of WFP in 2018.  It will be complemented by i) nutrition project, targeting women and children to prevent and respond to undernutrition, ii) livelihood project to re build livelihood and resilience, and iii) school meals project, targeting pupils to support their learning. 

The emergency general food assistance project is aligned with the objectives 1 and 4 of the Food Security Cluster:
1. Improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people by emergency life saving and regular life sustaining food assistance
4: Strengthen the effectiveness and quality of the WoS response based on evidence, capacity building and strong coordination within the Food Security and Agriculture Sector and cross sectors.

project_name: Improving short-term and long-term food availability and livelihoods access in Western Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile and Lakes states through investment in food production assets, and utilization and strengthening of local capacities.
project_objective:
To provide immediate food assistance to insecure individuals in Greater Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile and Lakes states, while working with communities to invest in long term food security interventions.
To provide immediate food assistance, ACTED plans to make unconditional cash transfers, conditional cash transfers , and restricted cash vouchers. Conditional cash transfers will not only improve purchasing power of beneficiaries, but will also contribute to creation, construction and rehabilitation of key livelihood assets such as water catchments and dykes to manage floods. Restricted cash will focus on purchase of livelihood inputs and assets such as seeds and tools to enable beneficiaries invest on their lands thereby increasing amount of land planted, and addressing the challenge of seeds scarcity. 
Long term investment on productive assets will also be achieved through resilience programming. ACTED will adopt the APFS model to encourage transfer of knowledge and skills in modern farming techniques, encourage community engagement through participatory risk assessments, toward participatory planning and joint ownership of resources. Such an investment will be pegged on utilization of local capacities and knowledge, which will then be reinforced through interactive sessions toward realizing improved livelihoods, reduced gender inequality, inclusive economic and social growth, and overall transformation of communities.

project_objective:
General objective: Contribute to a comprehensive Protection system of vulnerable communities in the North-West Bank 
Specific Objectives: 
1. Mitigate the impacts of conflict related violations (Settlers violence, demolitions, excessive use of force by ISF, displacement)  on the mental health and psychosocial (here after called MHPSS) wellbeing of Palestinian communities living in North West Bank including the North Jordan Valley
2. Strengthen the resilience and positive coping mechanisms of Palestinian communities living in North West Bank including the North Jordan Valley
3. Third States Parties, notably France & EU Members are deeply mobilized and take systematic and concrete measures toward the occupation practices which negatively impact the protection of Palestinians and their effective access to services in the WB 
Within this action, MDM will contribute to the Protection Cluster Objectives 1 and 2, both relating to the Strategic objective 1 of the HRP: The rights of Palestinians living under occupation, including those living under the blockade and other restrictions, are protected, respected and promoted in accordance with IHL and IHRL .
In relation with the Objective 2, MDM intervention focuses in the provision of MH and Psychosocial services. MDM implement Emergency MHPSS support as well as resilience-based interventions (to improve positive coping mechanisms) and case management in the communities of the North-West Bank most exposed to Settlers violence, demolitions, ISF violations and possible forcible transfer.
MDM advocacy efforts will also contribute to the Objective 1 of the Protection cluster “Increase Respect of IHL & HRL”. The Advocacy contribution of MDM will be through field briefings to diplomats and international media, production of periodic reports and factsheets to reflect the impact of the violations in the MHPSS of the Palestinian communities, in addition to a lobby tours in Paris and Brussels addressing the same topics.

project_name: Most crisis-impacted communities provided access to livelihoods and basic services (PHASE 1 in a multi-year 320 Million $ project targeting 300 communities)
project_objective:
In line with the HRP cross-cutting resilience objective and the ERL Sector strategy, the project aims at providing comprehensive support through Early Recovery and Resilience-building in 150 communities impacted by the crisis. 
Communities, particularly those most dramatically affected – and/or soon to be under stress when/if IDPs and refugees start to return -  need assistance in re-establishing their resilience to address these shocks, and their needs on depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The project, submitted and managed by UNDP as the Sector Lead Agency, also provides an opportunity to associate multiple sector partners in implementation, thereby strengthening coordinated strategy formulation and programme delivery.
The essence of the programme is to provide Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain control over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian aid. Prioritized locations are selected based on a needs assessment conducted on more than 5,000 Syrian communities, using the following set of criteria:
1) Hard to Reach Areas
2) De-escalation zones
3) Areas of major IDPs and possible refugees return
4) Presence of IDPs
5) Community Scores in the 2017 ERL Sector Severity Analysis
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions, and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors eager to support this initiative will be able to indicate certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their choice, within the 200 prioritized communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives, targeting:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5. Social protections
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing civic engagement opportunities/capacities

For population monitoring, PMI developed a baseline of stock figures for IDPs, residents, and total population in 108 villages in Dar’a and Quneitra in September 2017. The overall objective of this project is to protect food production capacities and income sources in locations that are most at risk due to the increasing electricity deficit in the Gaza Strip. The rationale of this project is to target areas most impacted by the increasing electricity deficit in order to protect current levels of food and agricultural production, livelihoods and food security by providing vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip with a consistent, clean and renewable source of energy to guarantee sufficient electricity for essential food production.

This intervention responds to the first need under the Agri-Livelihood section in the Food Security Sector Response Plan, which indicates the need for interventions that prioritize the shortage of power and supply of electricity in the Gaza Strip. The intervention falls under Strategic Objective 3 of the HRP 2018-2022 as it invests in solar energy sources to ensure that targeted farmers have a consistent electricity supply as and when required in order to cope with the protracted crisis.

As an emergency intervention, this project aims to minimize damages and losses to domestic crop production in the current season and to enable normal levels of cultivation in subsequent seasons. Thus, this project is designed as a multi-year project with similar activities recurring every year. In doing so, this project will protect agriculture-based livelihoods, food security and domestic food production that are at risk given the latest electricity reduction and will enable normal levels of cultivation if or when electricity supply to the Gaza Strip is further reduced.

project_name: Emergency Livestock Support Project (ELSP) in Gedo-Somalia
project_objective:
To protect and restore livelihoods of 10,220 households comprising of vulnerable pastoral, agro-pastoral,-- women, men, girls and boys by supporting the core breeding stock through emergency livestock treatments, feed distribution and fodder production, conservation and utilization in Gedo Region of Somalia in 2018. 

The proposed project objective is in line with the FSC objectives (2) and (3) that contributes towards protecting and restoring livelihoods (related to food and income) and building resilience against current and future shocks respectively,  and  the four HRP strategic objectives of providing (life-saving, nutrition, protection and resilience). Milking animals and small stock (that are managed by women) don’t migrate, thus posing a threat on sustaining them during drought. Other challenges facing (agro) pastoralists in Gedo on Animal health component are: unavailability, inaccessibility and affordability of quality veterinary pharmaceuticals as well as inadequate veterinary services. VSF-Suisse plans to conduct emergency livestock treatments targeting the core breeding stock and milking animals. This intervention has the potential to provide positive impact on protecting and re-building livestock assets at all stages of the drought cycle through preventing death in the herd and strengthening livestock resistance to drought. Practical Action (2009) in the Livestock Emergency Guidelines and Standards (LEGS) on a study conducted in Northern Kenya and Eastern Ethiopia; indicated that it was between 3 – 6 times more expensive to restock a core breeding stock following a drought than to keep the animal alive through feeding. This justifies our feed distribution and fodder production intervention that will enhance survival rate of the key breeding stock as a foundation stock to rebuild (agro)pastoralists herds. Fodder production will also increase access to feeds, animal productivity (especially milk), income and be an exit strategy for emergency feeding.

project_name: Emergency response to vulnerable households affected by natural hazards in Area C
project_objective:
The aim of this project is to provide immediate humanitarian assistance to vulnerable households whose residential shelter was damaged as a result of natural disasters, and to prevent further displacement. This action will focus on damages resulting from weather conditions such as floods and storms. In particular, the assistance will target Area C, home to vulnerable Bedouin and herder communities. Although the action will place a strong focus on response speed, a specific attention will be paid to beneficiaries’ involvement and to adapting the response to the specific needs of different vulnerable groups.in particular women.

This Action will contribute to the result 3 of the 2017 Humanitarian Response Plan defined by the Shelter Cluster “Mitigate the risk and immediate effect of displacement due to natural disasters or conflict through preparedness and appropriate emergency shelter interventions” aiming at accomplishing the country level strategic objective 3: The project contributes the Country Strategic Objective 3 “the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”.

The action will provide time critical assistance within 72 hours to the most affected HH, providing them with lifesaving assets. It will thus contribute to prevent the displacement of vulnerable Bedouin and herder communities, enabling other actors to further assist them after the initial relief response.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Preparedness Safety & Risk Education in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Project Objective: Civilians living in high risk conflict-affected communities in the Gaza Strip are better prepared to protect themselves in case of armed conflict and are empowered with the knowledge they need to mitigate risks associated with explosive weapons.

The proposed interventions supplement the NPA Palestine Country Strategy 2016-2019 in Gaza and are aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 2: “Prevent and mitigate the effects of the Occupation and conflict related violence.” Project activities are also specifically aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 2 of the HRP, “Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence,” and will contribute to this objective through the provision of emergency preparedness risk education (EPRE) and Explosive Remnant of War (ERW) risk education for civilian residents (adults and children) of the Gaza Strip.

The proposed interventions are part of a multi-year programme. Over a three-year period, the programme will be implemented using the same activities, but for new beneficiaries and new communities which will be prioritized later based on Ministry of Education planning and in consultation with Protection Cluster, the Mine Action Working Group, and NPA’s local partners.

project_objective:
Principal objective - To reduce the vulnerability of the conflict-affected elderly people of Donetska Oblast.
Specific objective - To ensure dignified living conditions for the conflict-affected elderly people of Donetska Oblast by strengthening their food security.

The core objective of the given proposal is to ensure access to caloric, ready food intake for the exceptionally vulnerable, elderly population of Donetska Oblast, especially those who are unable to prepare food for themselves due to age and health related conditions. The majority of them are elderly women who are the most vulnerable and are in urgent need of the food assistance. 

Additional objective: To provide protection and psycho-social services for the conflict-affected people to strengthen social support systems.
The conflict  in Donbas is further breaking communities and families apart. Many of elderly people live alone and have no relatives/friends near them. The majority of elderly population is comprised of elderly women, often widows, whose children and grandchildren have died or left the region. As it is planned, specially trained Protection Officers will provide counseling to the beneficiaries and offer some socialization for those who are severely isolated in order to mitigate the symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression among most vulnerable elderly people.

The overall goal of WHO emergency response strategy is to reduce morbidity and mortality among Rohingya Refugee population and host community in Cox’s Bazar. Where possible, emergency response will build on existing health infrastructure, network of partners, community resources and structures. The response will integrate resilience building components to foster sustainable solutions to the Rohingya Refugee crisis and affected host community.
WHO will support the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Bangladesh, the Civil Surgeon’s Office, Cox’s Bazar, Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner’s Office (RRRC), and work in conjunction with sector partners, in particular those in the health, WASH and nutrition clusters. The activities prioritized by WHO under this project are also based on the Humanitarian Needs.
The health sector, co-led by WHO, is working in a coordinated approach within the scope of the Inter-Sectoral Coordination Group (ISCG). WHO’s response strategy is aligned with the overall Health Sector Strategy as articulated in the Joint Response Plan 2018.
WHO will continue to prioritize the focus on life-saving health related needs. The plan will involve:
• Strengthening of routine immunization services 
• Standardization of case management protocols
• Infection prevention and control • Disease early warning 
• Outbreak response
• Coordinating with partners on integration of in-patient SAM support at PHC level 
• Community and health facility based surveillance  
• Standardization of data gathering • Information management.

project_name: Strengthening community resilience to provide equitable access to a quality education for school-age refugee boys and girls (3-17 years old) affected by the CAR and Sudan crises
project_objective: The project aims to strengthen the resilience of communities affected by crisis to provide equitable access to a quality education for school-age refugee boys and girls (3 – 17 years old) from the Central African Republic (CAR) and Sudan in the south and east of Chad. The overall intervention will be closely coordinated with other relevant sectors such as WASH, Health, Nutrition and Child Protection to ensure enhanced intersectoral actions and make a greater impact on children and communities affected by crisis.

Ce projet vise à mettre en place des stratégies de prévention et de réduction des risques liées à la vulnérabilité des enfants affectés par la crise centrafricaine. Ces interventions incluent l’analyse de la situation et des différents risques de protection, la mise en place d’un environnement protecteur à travers des garanties de droits fondamentaux et la facilitation de la cohésion sociale entre les populations hôtes et les retournés.
Les activites de protection de l'enfant etant deja mis en oeuvre depuis le debut de la crise et les deplacements des populations,des consultations avec les membres des communautes et des autorites traditionnelles et gouvernementales pour l'evaluation des projets et activites precedentes et celle a venir. Pour etre en ligne avec les principes des droits de l'Enfant, la participation des enfants sera primordiale tant dans la conception, la mise en oeuvre des activites et a la fin. 
Les mecanismes de protection a base communautaire sont les meilleurs outils  pour assurer l'integration de la protection transversale car elles sont non seulement de par leurs composiitons constituees des membres de  communautes des deux sexes ainsi que des representants d'enfants. Lors de leurs rencontres et suivi de la protection des enfants au sein des communautes, le dialogue communautaire est privilegiee.

project_name: Renforcement des moyens d'existence des communautés et des ménages vulnérables  affectées par différentes crises dans les régions du sud du Tchad
project_objective:
La FAO présente une expertise avérée dans le domaine agricole et possède les avantages de l'expérience acquise les années antérieures dans la mise en œuvre des projets d'assistance aux ménages victimes des chocs ou des crises alimentaires au Tchad et dans la sous région.Les partenaires institutionnels du projet sont le Ministère de l’Agriculture et de l’Environnement au niveau central et les services techniques déconcentrés du Ministère. D’autres Ministères (Santé, Elevage, Micro-finance) ainsi que leurs services déconcentrés seront également sollicités. Les ONG intervenants dans les sites de retournés, les autorités administratives, traditionnelles seront également impliquées dans le projet.

Considérant le niveau élevé de malnutrition des enfants et du rôle important des femmes dans l’économie familiale, les principaux bénéficiaires directs des actions du projet sont les femmes, en particulier les plus démunies qui, marquées par leur vulnérabilité due à plusieurs facteurs, ont des revenus faibles et des difficultés économiques importantes. Il s’agit des femmes chefs de familles, les femmes pauvres avec des enfants mineurs, les femmes seules ou âgées  vulnérables mais capables de mener des AGR.

Ce projet ciblera les groupes féminins dans les zones d’installation des retournés  dont certains ont déjà commencé à s’organiser et réaliser des activités génératrices des revenus, l’éducation nutritionnelle dans les cadres des  projets précédents.  Les principales activités génératrices de revenus pratiquées sont les petits commerces des produits alimentaires. Les femmes seront mises en avant dans tpout le processus.

project_name: Projet d’urgence de sécurité alimentaire et de protection des moyens d’existence des populations retournées affectées par la crise centrafricaine au Salamat et au Sud du Tchad.
project_objective:
Malgré l’élection d’un nouveau président, la situation sécuritaire reste toujours instable en RCA, entrainant des violences et des mouvements de populations vers les pays voisins dont le Tchad. Cela se traduit par l’arrivée continue de réfugiés et de retournés qui sont dans des situations alimentaires et nutritionnelles difficiles, ayant fui juste pour sauver leur vie sans aucun autre moyen de survie. 

Les dernières enquêtes montrent que les retournés vivent dans des situations très difficile et ne comptent que sur l’assistance humanitaire dont l’assistance alimentaire constitue une priorité. Le présent projet vise à leur apporter une assistance alimentaire sous forme de transferts monétaires qui renforcera leur sécurité alimentaire, tout en apportant un appui au marché local a travers une injection de cash. Cette forme d’assistance leur permettra de subvenir à leur besoin alimentaire à travers le marché local et respectera mieux encore leur dignité et leurs préférences alimentaires.

project_name: Treatement of malnutrition (crisis response - treatment)
project_objective: The nutritional condition of refugees differs significantly by geographical region and place of origin, with particular concern for the north-eastern camps of Sudanese refugees. Between 2008 and 2015, a significant improvement has been noted in the nutritional situation, with a decrease of global acute malnutrition in Sudanese camps from 12.3 percent to 7.4 percent . Results from the 2016 assessment show a tendency toward an increase in global acute malnutrition levels, though prevalence remain under 10 percent in all but 5 camps. Moreover, anemia rates for children 6-59 months and for pregnant and lactating women remain sources of concern, as does chronic malnutrition, with over 40 percent of the children 6-59 months in camps being affected.WFP will implement the program for the management of moderate acute malnutrition in the Sahelian belt in collaboration with DNTA. the community outreach component will be scaled up to improve coverage and will target both women and girls as well as men. For that, WFP will ensure that the distribution sites are close to the villages and that there is a water point and shed for the beneficiaries. The complaint management committee will consider the type of transparency in their work. A monitoring and evaluation schedule will inform both the quality of the program and the level of satisfaction of the beneficiaries

project_name: Strengthening Lifesaving, Comprehensive, and Multi Sectoral Prevention and Response to Gender Based Violence in Sudan (Darfur states, Blue Nile, South Kordofan)
project_objective:
NFPA formulated this project as part of the Sudan 2018 HRP under the Multiyear Humanitarian Strategy (MHS) 2017 to 2019. Its overall objective is to address Gender Based Violence prevention and response needs of vulnerable people newly displaced or affected by disaster ensuring that GBV prevention and risk mitigation measures are in place, and receive timely protection assistance to prevent serious risks to their safety and dignity. The project focus on the 7 states in Sudan (5 Darfur states, South Kordofan, and Blue Nile). 

UNFPA's protection interventions will contribute to 2 of the 3 outcomes of the 2017 – 2019 Multi Year Humanitarian Strategy and 2 of the 3 HRP Protection Strategic Objectives formulated for 2018: 

(1) MYHRS Outcome 1 (timely assistance during and in the aftermath of a shock)     2018 HRP Protection Strategic Objective 1 ""the Protection Sector and its subsectors (child protection, gender-based violence (GBV) and mine action) will ensure that vulnerable people newly displaced or affected by disaster receive timely protection assistance to prevent serious risks to their safety and dignity""

(2) Outcome 2: (Populations in areas affected by natural or man-made disaster receive timely assistance during and in the aftermath of a shock),     2018 HRP Protection Strategic Objective 2 “the sector will ensure that communities have the capacity to protect their members and that social services are accessible in protracted displacement.""

-	Set-up vaccination centre integrated within Sarmada PHC, especially to children under 5t. Nurses and lab technician will be hired for this centre.

The overall aim of the project is to increase enrolment and retention rates within IDPs and host community children through reduced hunger and malnutrition in Jonglei State, as well facilitate the return to school for children & youths who dropped out as a result of hunger, forced child labor or recruitment into armed groups. Since 2014, FCA has been covering standard EiE activities such as teacher trainings, community awareness campaigns on back to learning, PTA/SMS formation & strengthening, construction of semi-permanent schools & TLS, protection activities, ECD, ALP and paying teacher incentives. The proposed school feeding project will integrate nutrition education, WASH in schools and disease prevention.   
Objective 1: Reduced hunger and malnutrition in 12 schools for 5835 conflict-affected and host community children in Jonglei State.
The proposed objective is reached through provision of on-site school meals, construction of basic school kitchens/stores, and hygiene training for safe handling, preparation, cooking and storage of food. This objective will increase school attendance by lowering the opportunity cost of attending school, and lead to more time spent in school, and towards learning. 
Objective 2: Enhanced awareness on nutrition education and WASH for school governing bodies (SGB), teachers and children. 
The proposed objective is reached through establishment of nutrition clubs to popularize availability, diversity and accessibility & benefits of food values; and capacity support to SMCs/PTAs and youth on nutrition and food security advocacy at community level.  School hygiene clubs & WASH facilities will be established to support messaging on safe use of latrines. This objective will lead to better health and resistance to infectious diseases & illnesses that would keep children from attending school. Better nutrition indirectly improves educational achievement by increasing school attendance.

project_name: Renforcement de la sécurité nutritionnelle dans les districts sanitaires de Mao et Mondo -Région du Kanem
project_objective:
L’intervention proposée  a pour objectif général de contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et mortalité par une amélioration de la sécurité nutritionnelle des populations du Kanem . Spécifiquement le projet  va renforcer la prévention et la prise en charge de la malnutrition et l'accès aux soins de santé primaires des enfants de moins de 5 ans, des femmes enceintes et allaitantes.
Elle couvrira les deux districts sanitaires de Mondo et Mao  et la stratégie d'intervention sera déclinée selon les axes prioritaires suivants :
1. Assurer un accès aux soins médico-nutritionnels gratuits et de qualité pour les enfants < 5ans en renforçant la détection précoce et le référencement des enfants MAS avec la mise à l'échelle de l'approche (Maman PB) et en renforçant les actions en lien avec l'approche des 1000 jours,
2. Renforcer la qualité de la santé maternelle de prise en charge des FEFA à travers un paquet intégré d'actions préventives et curatives de ces dernières et continuer à travers la sensibilisation notamment la promotion de l'accouchement en milieu institutionnel;
3.Mettre en place un paquet minimum Wash in Nut dans les centres santé.

A travers ce projet, ACF intégrera la dimension genre à chaque étape de son programme, pour les bénéficiaires directs, indirects et équipes ACF, afin de répondre de façon adaptée aux besoins de l’ensemble de la population. Les données seront analysées par genre et par catégorie d’âge. Les bénéficiaires  de ce projet sont en majorité des enfants <5 ans, qui sont les plus vulnérables et leurs accompagnantes, les femmes enceintes et allaitantes .
Le projet prévoit l’implication des autorités sanitaires et de la communauté affectée et plus particulièrement les femmes, lors de la conception / la planification des actions/ la mise en œuvre et le suivi/l’évaluation du projet.

project_name: W - Strengthening equitable access to quality learning and skills development for the most margianlised children, adolescents and youth, with a particular focus on displaced and out-of-school children.
project_objective:
Championing the No Lost Generation (NLG) initiative, UNICEF aims to advance equitable access to quality learning for the most disadvantaged children, adolescents and youth in Syria. UNICEF’s priority areas are as follows:  

a) Scaling up equitable access to education
b) Enhancing the quality of education services
c) Strengthening education systems

For equity and impartiality, UNICEF will advocate for greater humanitarian access and seek to reach the most marginalized children. Priority vulnerable groups will entail those who are displaced and out of school and who are in the communities that host them. Geographical priority will be given to areas with high severity, including newly accessible, militarily encircled, besieged and hard-to-reach areas. UNICEF will reinforce coordination within Damascus, Amman and Gaziantep hubs in a Whole of Syria approach.  

As these vulnerable groups face multiple barriers to schooling, it is critical to strengthen a knowledge/evidence base and address their barriers in a cross-sectorial way. UNICEF will increase synergies with Social/Child Protection, Adolescent Development and Participation (ADAP), Communication for Development (C4D), and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). 

UNICEF will respond to immediate humanitarian needs as investments for the future.. It will strengthen partnership with authorities, NGOs, communities and schools in view of resilience building and early recovery. Furthermore, UNICEF will coordinate with other UN agencies to leverage resources in jointly selected communities and schools. UNICEF leads the education sector coordination in all the WoS hubs including the sub-hubs of  Aleppo, Homs, Tartous, Hassakeh, Idleb, Hama, Raqqa, Dar’a, Quneitra and Deir ez Zor. The coordination mechanism is envisaged to facilitate the institutional capacity development at all levels and improve information management for contextually relevant and inclusive education interventions.

project_name: X - Support debris removal and vocational trainings in Syria
project_objective:
Objective: 
Enable local authorities in Homs and Aleppo to accelerate recovery efforts in damaged areas and improve capacity of municipal authorities to remove debris by providing access and training on heavy equipment / earth-moving machinery, creating jobs and economic opportunities in the sector.

Project in brief:
The aim of the project is to support local municipalities in Homs and Aleppo to clean-up areas and to allow for early recovery.

By clearing damaged sites, this project will create conditions on the ground, which will restore critical infrastructure, economic activity and livelihoods.  This project will build and enhance the capacities of municipal authorities to safely remove, recycle and reuse rubble that is present in damaged affected areas (particularly into industrial zones and areas with high destiny of productive sectors activity). The project will provide the necessary machinery and training that will enable local authorities to safely remove and reclaim damaged debris. The reclaimed debris can be used as a sub-base for further reconstruction (i.e. backfilling, road improvements, etc.). The equipment and training needs will be determined based on an assessment of the project areas. Machinery needs may include: hydraulic excavators, haulers, crushing and cutting attachments, mobile crushers, tooling and training aids (i.e. operator simulators). The training objectives will build-on UNIDO’s past experience working with Komatsu Ltd. to develop courses for the operation and maintenance of heavy equipment. The existing training material includes the operation of machinery, safety and general maintenance. The project will operate in all areas that will allow for safe operation of the equipment.

This project is in-line with the 2018 HRP Early Recovery and livelihoods sector strategy.

project_name: Appui aux retournés tchadiens de RCA dans le Sud du pays par la fourniture de solutions durables en termes d'abris et d'opportunités économiques
project_objective:
Par sa situation géographique, le Sud accueille de nombreux retournés tchadiens de RCA (essentiellement des femmes et des enfants) fuyant le conflit dans le pays, notamment après la crise de fin 2013. Cependant, ces retournés font face à de fortes difficultés d’intégration causés par des problèmes de protection et un accès limité aux services de base. 
Cette situation a été aggravée à la suite des inondations qu’a connu le Sud cette année et qui ont détruit une partie des moyens de subsistance des populations de la zone. Cette pression supplémentaire sur une économie pauvre et sous-développée a accru les difficultés des communautés hôtes et donc des retournés.
Pour répondre aux besoins constatés, l'intervention d'ACTED s'inscrit dans le cadre des solutions durables à travers la mise en place d'activités de soutien au logement et de soutien économique pour permettre une amélioration des conditions de vie des retournés dans la zone et leur intégration dans la population tchadienne.

project_name: Sustaining and Expanding Lifesaving Emergency Nutrition Services Scaled-up to Reach Under-served Payams in Fangak and Nyirol Counties South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will save lives of children 6-59 months and PLW suffering from SAM and MAM with focus on under-served payams in Fangak and Nyirol counties. This objective will be achieved by:
1. Delivering timely quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk targeting 80% of SAM and 62% of MAM in girls and boys 6-59 months and 53% of PLW.
2. Increasing access to MIYCN program preventing under-nutrition among the most vulnerable and at risk, reaching at least 60% of PLW in need in high burden areas.
3. Enhancing nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and utilization of early warning information for timely coordinated response decision making.
4. Increasing access to integrated Nutrition and Health services, and access to WASH, FSL, Education and Protection activities in counties with critical levels of global acute malnutrition (GAM =22%) and/or in IPC 4.

The project will scale-up services from 4 to 10 OTP/TSFP sites in 4 payams in Fangak (Manajang, Paguir, New Fangak and Mareang) and 3 payams in Nyirol (Chuil, Pultruk and Pading) all currently accessible. Main response strategies will be (1) carry-out case-finding outreaches and referrals (including malaria test) from static OTPs to unreached PHCUs where IDPs are integrated with host community for referral to OTPs, (2) dispatch mobile teams by boat/charters to locations beyond the reach of on-ground case-finding outreaches and referrals, and (3) to fully integrate nutrition and health services, and partially integrate WASH, FSL Education and Protection activities. MIYCN will reach PLW and care-givers of children U23 months. At OTP sites, health services will deliver SAM with medical complications, malaria treatment, Vit A and deworming. Insecurity creates risks for PLW and U5s. Through project mobilization and awareness support, communities will implement appropriate protection practices to reduce risk of GBV children and PLW.

project_name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

project_name: Appui d’urgence durant la soudure et renforcement de la résilience pour les populations affectées par les crises alimentaires et nutritionnelles dans la Bande Sahélienne au Tchad
project_objective:
Les analyses nationales conduites en 2017 révèlent que le Tchad souffre d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle et de faibles moyens de subsistance, en particulier dans certaines régions. Parmi elles, figurent la région du Lac Tchad et celle du Batha. Les besoins humanitaires de ces zones s'expliquent par l'activité des groupes armés, les déplacements de population, les restrictions de mouvement, les tensions intercommunautaires, les épidémies et les désastres naturels et climatiques.
Une intervention d'ACTED se justifie dès lors dans ces deux régions, particulièrement dans le département du Wayi (région du Lac) et dans les départements du Batha Est et du Batha-Ouest; d'une part parce que les besoins sont criants et d'autre part, pour assurer un suivi et un renforcement des activités mises en place par ACTED dans le cadre du HIP 2017 financé par ECHO. Ainsi, ACTED soutiendra 10 000 ménages, soit 70 000 personnes (7 personnes par ménage), classés comme étant très pauvres par les résultats des outcomes analyses (HEA), et ayant en leur sein des enfants de moins de 5 ans et des femmes enceintes et allaitantes (FEFA).
L'intervention d'ACTED se déroulera dans un premier temps sous forme d'une aide d'urgence à travers des transferts monétaires saisonniers conditionnés à une participation à des sessions de sensibilisation au profit de 10 000 ménages durant la période de soudure, leur permettant de couvrir leurs besoins alimentaires de base. Ces distributions seront combinées à des distributions de compléments alimentaires (CSB +/++) en faveur des enfants de 6 à 23 mois et des FEFA pour prévenir les risques de malnutrition.
Par ailleurs, ACTED renforcera la résilience des populations à travers des activités agricoles (maraichage) et d’élevage et poursuivra son appui aux structures du Système d'Alerte Précoce et Réponse d’Urgence (SCAP-RU) dans les départements ciblés.

project_name: Prévention de la malnutrition aigue pour les  populations déplacées internes du Lac Tchad.
project_objective:
The Lake Region of Chad is situated on the shores of Lake Chad and borders Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon. This region is one of the most vulnerable within Chad due to accessibility challenges, the lack of basic social services and the high frequency of natural and environmental hazards, which include floods and droughts.
Chronic food insecurity, poor access to quality health care, low vaccination coverage, inadequate nutrition education and practices on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and chronic poverty are factors fueling high malnutrition rates in the Lake Region. These factors are exacerbated by the level of insecurity as the result of violence instigated by Boko Haram militants in the area, which has resulted in the widespread disruption of community structures and massive population displacements.
Several assessments and studies were carried out in the three health districts, and although some show improvements in health and nutrition indicators, there are still many factors that impede improved health and nutrition outcomes. The national SMART survey conducted in September 2016 indicted the prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) as 18.1% and the SAM prevalence as 3.4% in the Lake Region. 
WFP will implement the program for the management of moderate acute malnutrition in the Sahelian belt in collaboration with DRS and DNTA. the community outreach component will be scaled up to improve coverage and will target both women and girls as well as men. For that, WFP will ensure that the distribution sites are close to the villages and that there is a water point and shed for the beneficiaries. The complaint management committee will consider the type of transparency in their work. A monitoring and evaluation schedule will inform both the quality of the program and the level of satisfaction of the beneficiaries.

EAA/EAC and UNICEF partnership “QUEST Education”, is a contextually relevant
approach to reach Out of School Children (OOSC) who are internally displaced and
living in accessible, hard-to-reach and besieged areas with limited or no access to
schooling due to active conflict or insecurity. The goal of the SLP and its
complementary activities (i.e. psychosocial support, school learning supplies,
teacher training and rehabilitation/construction/operations of learning spaces) is to
deliver a comprehensive self-study course with a curriculum and an environment
that is conducive to learning within a conflict situation so OOSC who have missed
out on regular schooling opportunities continue their learning and can ultimately
return to a formal educational setting. Also, as the SLP is looking to scale-up, a
secondary goal is to refine and enhance the program itself and look for ways to
scale it up in Syria and potentially in the neighbouring countries hosting Syrian
refugee children.
Proposed objectives:
1) Increase access to education for 32,000 out-of-school children through the SLP
a. Increase access to protective learning spaces and learning materials where
required (includes construction/rehabilitation of learning spaces and provision of
prefabricated rooms)
b. Expand access to psychosocial support and recreational activities
c. Training for teachers and resource persons for the SLP
2) Strengthen the SLP program components, such as quality standards, learning
measurements and M&E for the program, and explore ways to sustain and scale
this to other Syrian OOSC, including in the neighbouring refugee host countries

project_name: Projet d’assistance alimentaire d’urgence aux populations déplacées internes, retournées et refugiées du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Dans la région du Lac, l’insécurité est toujours d’actualité due aux attaques de Boko Haram est toujours d’actualité et entraine des mouvements continus de population. En avril et mai dernier, environ 2 350 nouveaux IDPs ont été enregistrés dans 4 nouveaux sites (Kiskawadine, Kabia, Blegue and Kadjerba), augmentant ainsi le nombre de personnes en besoin d’assistance humanitaire dans la région. Cet état des faits vient renforcer, si besoin en est, la nécessité d’une assistance alimentaire à ces populations vulnérables dont le nombre ne cesse de croitre. Les résultats de l’ENSA d’October 2016 indiquent une nette détérioration de la sécurité alimentaire dans la région par rapport à 2015. Le taux d’insécurité alimentaire a augmenté de  14.72 à 21.7 pourcent au Lac (37.8 pourcent pour les IDPs). Le dernier ENSA dont la collecte des données a eu lieu en ocobre permettra d’avoir des données plus actualisées.

Par ailleurs, les pressions de tout ordre exercée par la présence des IDPs et Réfugiés sur les communuatés hôtes n’ayant pas un accès approprié aux services sociaux de base contribuent à accroitre la situation de vulnérabilité dans la région.

project_name: Providing Comprehensive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Assistance to Affected Populations in Darfur, Blue Nile, Kordofan States and East Sudan.
project_objective: This project aims to provide life saving WASH assistance to mitigate the suffering of populations affected by natural or man made disasters and reflects all 3 outcomes of the Multi Year Humanitarian Response Plan strategy. Under Outcome 1 IOM will provide life saving assistance to people newly displaced by conflict or natural disasters in an effort to recreate pre emergency conditions using early recovery approaches to improve the overall access to WASH services, connecting the need for short term emergency interventions with long term solutions and applying development principles by working directly with local communities to facilitate ownership and accountability. The objective is to not only focus on WASH emergency interventions but gradually contribute to socio economic inclusion of forcibly displaced populations and returnees by directly increasing access to basic services for the displaced and host communities and indirectly increasing employment opportunities. Under Outcome 2 IOM seeks to improve and sustain access to safe water in target communities especially in Blue Nile, Durdeb, Abyei, North Darfur and South Darfur as these communities primarily rely on agriculture and livestock, therefore water is critical to their livelihoods. Under Outcome 3 improving and sustaining access to safe water and sanitation facilities and hygiene messages will address malnutrition related risks and increase community resilience to disease outbreaks. IOM will consider emergency water provision, access to proper sanitation facilities and hygiene campaigns; coupled with the establishment and rehabilitation of water points. This will include environmental impact mitigation such as the provision of solar technology to power water points and monitoring ground water to moderate depletion levels. Exit strategies will be developed to alleviate aid dependency in protracted emergencies by strengthening self-reliance and facilitating community solutions in a more holistic approach.

project_name: Reducing food insecurity, restoring livelihood and building resilience for the vulnerable households and communities in Blue Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan (including Abyei north), Kassala, Gedaref and Red Sea States.
project_objective: The main objective of this project is to reduce food and nutrition insecurity, restore livelihood and build resilience of the affected population/communities in the protracted crisis areas of in Blue Nile, White Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan (including Abyei north), Kassala, Gedaref and Red Sea states by safeguarding their assets and strengthening their productive capacity. The affected population includes IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host communities. The project is in line with the three FSL Sector Strategic Objective 1, 2 and 3; and in line with the Multi Year Humanitarian strategy (2017 2019) Outcome 1, 2 and 3. The multi year strategy will allow FAO to provide immediate lifesaving assistance whenever the need arises and at the same time engage strategically to address the drivers of vulnerabilities and underlying structural issues across the targeted states. In particular, the project will focus on increasing the access to productive assets, inputs and services to enable the beneficiaries to improve food and nutrition security status and sustain their livelihoods. It will also enhance the income generation capacities of particularly disadvantaged population groups, such as women headed households and support them with diversified livelihood means and skills. The project will ensure a balanced dietary intake to avoid any type of malnutrition, including micronutrient deficiency.

project_name: Improving access to life-saving medical healthcare and protection for vulnerable groups in Western and Southern Libya
project_objective:
Overall in Libya, an estimated 1.1 million Libyan and non-Libyan individuals are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance according to the Humanitarian Needs Overview 2018 (HNO).  In particular, 1,056,000 individuals are reported to be in need of health assistance including 380,000 non-displaced Libyans, 190,000 returnees, 308,500 mixed migrants and 177,500 internally displaced persons (IDPs). In addition, a total of 1,047,500 individuals are reported to be in need of protection assistance including 334,000 non-displaced Libyans, 187,500 returnees, 400,445 mixed migrants and 125,500 IDPs. 
Based on the needs above, the IRC plans to develop a programme which will provide vulnerable Libyans and non Libyans with quality primary health care and protection services through the provision of free preventive and curative outpatient medical consultations and set up of comprehensive referral pathways, while strengthening their resilience from the effects of violence through structured and sustained mental health and psycho-social support (MHPSS) services. IRC also plans to contribute to the strengthening of primary healthcare, reproductive healthcare and address the mental health gap through rehabilitations, health information system building, capacity building of healthcare workers, and donations of medical supplies. 
The IRC's overall mission is to to deliver humanitarian assistance and reduce the suffering of conflict-affected communities, IDPs, migrants and refugees in Libya and providing lifesaving services to target populations in identified areas. the IRC will seek to contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality among target populations with a focus on vulnerable people including women and children.

project_name:
Appui intégré et inclusif à l'éducation et à la protection des enfants et personnes à besoins spécifiques
affectés par la crise du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Le consortium constitué par COOPI et HI va intervenir dans 19 villages et sites de la sous-préfecture de Bol pour renforcer son apport pour l'amélioration de l'accès à l'éducation et de la qualité de l'éducation, de la protection grâce aux services inclusifs d'éducation et de protection. Comme reflété dans la stratégie à 4 ans détaillée en Annexe 5, les principes d'intégration, d'efficacité et d'efficience et le principe de responsabilité guideront l'action dans sa toute mise en oeuvre. Le consortium mènera des
activités d'éducation formelle et non formelle au sein de structures éducatives existantes ou nouvelles créées par le projet. L'action tend à offrir un environnement protecteur et renforcer les méchanismes d'identification, référencement et assistance des enfants souffrant des problèmes de protection, réduire le risque d'exposition à de différents problèmes de protection,garantir la protection des personnes , en particulier pour les des enfants et des adolescents, face aux risques de violences (y compris SVBG, risques d'enrôlements et abus) en garantissant des espaces éducatifs sécurisés . Ces espaces d'apprentissage permettront parallèlement d'offrir aux enfants et aux jeunes un soutien psychosocial d'apprentissage permettront parallèlement d'offrir aux enfants et aux jeunes un soutien psychosocial lorsqu'ils en auront besoin . Un soutien psychosocial individuel et familial va permettre aux enfants de s'exprimer en réduisant leur tension émotionnelle et aux familles de renforcer le support aux enfants..
En plus, ça leur donne une occasion de réflexion, clarification, réassurance et de nouvelle stratégie d'ajustement bien adaptées à leurs vécus traumatique. Le but ici est d'amener ces enfants à se socialiser avec les autres enfants et à partager leurs soucis avec leurs parents la resocialisation avec les paires et l'appui émotionnel de la famille ayant une importance clé dans le parcours de soin des enfants.
Le projet cherchera à garantir un accès inclusif transverse à toutes les personnes vulnérables, y compris les personnes handicapées et à besoins spécifiques dans toutes les activités mises en oeuvre  par le projet, dans le respect des 4 piliers fondamentaux de la Protection transversale. L'inclusion sera garantie et renforcée à travers la mise en place d'une Cellule Technique Inclusion (CTI) de HI constituée de la coordinatrice Handicap et inclusion à la mission à Ndjamena et du chef de projet
éducation inclusive et des 4 chargés d'inclusion. Cette CTI permettra d'agir de façon intégrée sur les  aspects de prise en charge, d'accessibilité, de sensibilisation et de plaidoyer dans le but de garantir une égalité d'accès à l'éducation et d'assurer la prise en compte des personnes à besoins spécifiques. Cette approche inclusive permettra d'intervenir sur la protection des enfants les plus vulnérables de façon transversale.
Enfin, l'ensemble des activités sera mis en oeuvre à travers une approche à base communautaire, pour une réponse plus efficace, efficiente, culturellement acceptable et adaptée aux besoins des populations cibles.

project_name: Integrated Protection, Legal and PSS Response for IDPs/Returnees in Mosul, Ninewa
project_objective:
This project is intended as an extension of the current project programming funded through the IHPF.  The project  will address the needs identified by UNHCR, HAI and the protection cluster to provide more effective PSS and legal services, in cooperation with local authorities, to vulnerable populations in Hamam Al-Alil,  Shoura, Qayyarah, and neighborhoods in Mosul. HAI will continue to provide services through mobile teams to maintain flexibility in reaching IDPs in hard to reach areas in the targeted locations (with a focus on out of camp) as well as respond to changing needs on the ground. project_name: Improving the well-being and strengthening the resilience of extremely vulnerable displaced children and their families affected by the humanitarian crisis in Borno State through psychosocial support, protection services, community-based awareness raising activities and through strengthening the technical and project management capacity of local CP organization.
project_objective:
The project aims to improve the well being of conflict affected children and caregivers while strengthening child protection services and increasing awareness at community level to reduce child protection risks. An integrated protection response will aim at delivering individual protection assistance to children identified being extremely vulnerable and/or victims of violence. Provision of case management system and individual follow up will ensure needs tailored assistance to the most vulnerable children, with a special focus on unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), children formerly associated with armed forces and armed groups, children from elderly, single parent headed households, children victims of GBV and children exploited in sexual transactions as assessment’s findings show. 
For UASC, community based alternative care arrangements will be established to ensure adequate care and protection to vulnerable children. Existing foster care practices will be reinforced promoting other forms of community based child care. The objective is to make sure that the community is mobilized and actively participates in the protection priorities. Awareness raising will be done to spread information on child protection, child’s rearing and identification of children victims of violence as identified as significantly lacking at the moment. Community key actors such as religious and community leaders, community volunteers, teachers, health workers will receive training and continued coaching and mentoring to be able to act as agent of change to reach greater number of community members. Similarly, sessions on positive parenting and child care will be organized to improve caregiver’s understanding on child’s development and needs. The community-based approach aims at building on existing capacities and resources with a bottom-up approach that will promote community’s knowledge and foster its meaningful engagement into improved child protection system and practice

project_name: Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre
project_objective:
The Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre (IIC) is an inter agency-accountability mechanism that allows affected populations to access information on existing and planned humanitarian assistance and convey feedback on and complaints about the humanitarian response in Iraq. 

The objective of this project is to ensure that feedback from callers identifies gaps in assistance, permits ongoing information exchange, influences how information is shared, and shapes how humanitarian assistance is organised and delivered. 

Accountability to Affected People (taking account, giving account and being held to account) lies at the heart of the Iraq IIC.

The Iraq IIC's primary objective is to promote two-way communication between affected populations and humanitarian actors to:
i. Empower communities through the provision of accessible and timely information on how to access services and resources required to improve their situation;
ii. Help ensure efficient and effective coordination of UN agencies, funds, and programmes operating in Iraq by collecting and circulating information about the urgent needs and priorities of affected populations; and,
iii. Support an environment of transparency and accountability by: (a) Establishing an easy to access and safe mechanism through which affected populations can lodge feedback, complaints, and access information on service provision; and (b) Channelling feedback and complaints to humanitarian actors to influence humanitarian programming and shape quality advocacy.
