project_name: Humanitarian Support to Protect Palestinians in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) from Forcible Transfer.
project_objective: This Project contributes to the protection of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, from forcible transfer (FT) through a protection-centered approach to humanitarian responses incorporating: emergency support (cash/in-kind); provision of material assistance and essential services; legal aid; advocacy; and community empowerment.  188 communities will be specifically targeted each year for medium-term resilience-building support based on their vulnerability to FT, initially assessed using the OCHA VPP, supplemented with in-depth protection assessments taking into consideration the specific needs of women, men, children, elderly, and people with disability. Emergency and legal aid activities will be implemented across the whole West Bank, based on needs and referrals. Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Policy Framework and coordinates with other actors meeting humanitarian needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers and ICCG coordination of response to demolitions. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSS, legal responses, settler violence interventions and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs. The Project is built on an integrated protection approach envisaged to contribute to all HRP objectives: S1:  The rights of Palestinians living under occupation are protected, respected and promoted; S2:   The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services; S3:   The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. The Project further contributes to the three Shelter Cluster objectives (1. Support to the displaced; 2. Support to vulnerable households; 3. Increased response capacity).

NRC has several accountability mechanisms in place to ensure that affected communities are well informed and aware of modes for approaching NRC with feedback. NRC has its own Accountability Framework facilitate transparent communication directly with the organization and affected population can provide feedback through dedicated complaint and feedback hotline numbers, email, staff field visits, complaint and suggestion boxes. project_name: Provision of an integrated package of life-saving interventions and protection to South Sudanese Refugees children in Sudan
project_objective:
The overall objective of UNICEF is to support the South Sudanese refugee, especially women and children, mainly in out-of-camp settings in eight targeted states. Integrated package of lifesaving interventions and protection will be provided through child protection, education, health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions. 

Child protection
Child protection interventions will enhance the lifesaving intervention of children through psychosocial support service as well as the family tracing and reunification (FTR) efforts for unaccompanied and separated refugee child.

Education
UNICEF focus on restoring access to quality education for 49,080 school aged South Sudanese refugees and host community children (50 per cent girls) in the targeted states and localities.

Health and Nutrition
The objective of health intervention is to improve the health status of refugees through supporting provision of life-saving health interventions with a special focus on children under 15 years and women. The proposed health interventions include provision of an integrated primary health care package such as immunization and integrated management of childhood illnesses, Antenatal care through fixed, mobile and outreach services as well as supporting provision of community based health interventions. 

Also, UNICEF will support to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with acute malnutrition among highly vulnerable refugee population and host communities.

WASH
UNICEF will support South Sudan refugees and hosting community members with lifesaving WASH service including water trucking, rehabilitation of the non-functional water source and constructing planned water supply distribution systems. Hygiene and sanitation promotion will focus on the safe use of latrines, handwashing at critical time and personal hygiene and constriction of emergency latrines.

project_objective:
Les objectifs sont les suivants : 
- Le renforcement de la protection contre les conséquences des conflits armés
- L’amélioration de l’accès à l’assistance et aux voies de recours juridiques 
- Le renforcement des services pour les personnes à besoins spécifiques
- L’augmentation de l’accès aux documents d’identité et d’état civil
- La mise à jour ou le renforcement d’une stratégie globale de solutions durables
- Le renforcement de la coordination et des partenariats

En 2018, le HCR continuera à fournir la protection et l’assistance humanitaire dans le cadre d’une réponse coordonnée en faveur des déplacés internes, des personnes vulnérables parmi les communautés d’accueil et des retournés, en collaboration avec le Gouvernement du Cameroun, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG internationales et locales ainsi qu’avec d’autres parties prenantes.  Le projet vise à améliorer la situation des déplacés et communautés d’accueil en matière de protection, en renforçant le monitoring de protection et le référencement et en développant un fort plaidoyer sur des questions de protection.  Le projet vise également à identifier, orienter et assister des individus ayant besoin d’une assistance ou de conseils juridiques ainsi qu’à renforcer les capacités d’une large gamme d’intervenant en développant la formation et la sensibilisation sur les thématiques de protection.  Enfin le projet sera mis en œuvre en prenant en compte la diversité des communautés à travers une approche AGD

project_name: Y: Food security and livelihood assistance for vulnerable families in Syria.
project_objective:
The following are three main project objectives:
1. Improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people by emergency lifesaving and regular life sustaining food assistance. 
2. Support the lifesaving livelihoods of affected households by increasing agricultural production, protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities.
3. Improve the capacity to deliver essential services for improved linkages with value chain through the rehabilitation/ building of productive infrastructure as well as supporting services.

To achieve the stated objectives, project will focus on the gender, youth and protection mainstreaming. The following will be ensured:
Access to food security programmes will be monitored by collecting disaggregated data by age, gender, and location or specific community.
If some individuals for example, older persons or persons with disabilities, cannot access the services special arrangements will be made to bring food or cash to them.
Activities will promote and help protect and the rights of people who have historically been marginalised or discriminated against, such as certain castes, tribes or women and girls.
Men, women, boys, girls, the elderly, and persons with disabilities will be consulted to understand their needs and preferences for location, design, and methodology of assistance.
A complaints feedback mechanism will be established with a view to improving programming, assisting in understanding beneficiary and community perceptions, promoting beneficiary empowerment and assisting in the early detection of problems such as targeting, misconduct including sexual exploitation and abuse, food diversion and fraud.

project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen a rights-based protection response for IDPs, IDP returnees and host communities, in particular those most vulnerable; through stronger advocacy, timely life-saving activities, streamlining prevention-oriented initiatives and evidence-based planning, with a focus in expanding outreach and developing the capacity of affected communities to cope, recover, contribute to and achieve solutions.
With a renewed UNHCR strategy for the IDP situation, the 2018 programme is designed to ensure the operation is fit-for-purpose, aiming for increased operational presence (static or mobile); efficiency in performance; as well as improved response and delivery, both in quality and speed. UNHCR has expanded its field protection unit to ensure systematic mobile protection monitoring and a strong presence in integrated missions, rapid assessments and RRM interventions. While response and monitoring will continue to cover POC and collective sites; coverage will also be expanded to 163 identified priority locations, including remote or hard-to-reach areas, in full support to the Protection Cluster Strategy.
Resources and advocacy will have a primary focus on solutions, either durable or transitional (where the former is not yet possible), including activities planned to rapidly assess needs, risks, intentions, feasibility of returns, relocations or integration; family reunification, absorption capacity of host communities; while also strengthening community-based structures, HLP initiatives, promotion of livelihoods and peaceful coexistence.
Improving coordination and quality of assessments and monitoring will be a key component; using innovative technology for accurate, up-to-date, quicker data collection, analysis and sharing, which will improve the relevance of information products, leading to a more fitting risk-mitigation approach, reduced first-time response time; while underpinning protection mainstreaming across other operational interventions.

project_name: Treatment of moderate acute malnutrition (Sahel)
project_objective:
In the Sahel, levels of acute malnutrition in Chad remain high, 13.9 percent in July - August 2017. The MAG presents a lot of disparities depending on the region. In twelve (12) out of twenty-three (23) regions, the MAG exceeds the critical threshold of 15% set by WHO.it is Ennedi Est (30,0%), d’Ennedi Ouest (27,3%), du Salamat (23,0%), du Batha (22,1%), du Barh El Ghazel (21,3%), du Wadi Fira (20,5%), du Kanem (19,2%), du Lac (18,1%), du Borkou (17,7%), du Sila (17,1%) et d’Hadjer Lamis (16,3%) et Ndjamena (16,3%).Rates of chronic malnutrition are also high (32.4 percent).Overall, at the national level, the nutritional status of children shows a deterioration compared to last year. Disaggregation by sex also shows that boys are more affected by MAG (15.4%) than girls (12.4%) with a significant difference The high prevalence of malnutrition is strongly correlated with food insecurity, poverty, inappropriate nutrition practices, insufficient access to and use of basic health services, and poor living conditions. The Cost of Hunger in Africa study, carried out by the Government of Chad with support from WFP and in collaboration with the African Union, concluded that 43 percent of child mortality is related to malnutrition. 

WFP will implement the program for the management of moderate acute malnutrition in the Sahelian belt in collaboration with DRS and DNTA. the community outreach component will be scaled up to improve coverage and will target both women and girls as well as men. For that, WFP will ensure that the distribution sites are close to the villages and that there is a water point and shed for the beneficiaries. The complaint management committee will consider the type of transparency in their work. A monitoring and evaluation schedule will inform both the quality of the program and the level of satisfaction of the beneficiaries.

Overall Objectives:  To improve access to quality life-saving GBV prevention and response services for women and girls who are survivors or at risk of GBV, through age appropriate and survivor centered approaches. 

Pervasive GBV abuses against women and girls, in particular sexual violence, family violence, sexual exploitation, forced and child marriage persist.  Fears of harassment, reprisal and stigmatization, including honour killing, remain real barriers to seeking services, justice and protection for GBV survivors. The consequences of GBV require a sustained and multi-sector responses, including specialized case management services and prevention and risk mitigation strategies to ensure the safety and dignity of women and girls and reduce risks of GBV. 

This project aims to address the broad and critical needs of conflict-affected women and girls survivors or at risk of GBV and strengthen the protective environment through case management, psychosocial support and community-based prevention programmes and activities.

Specific Objectives:
1.	Provide GBV prevention and response services for highly vulnerable women and children, including community-based mitigation of GBV, in camps, non-camps settings and for those newly returning to their places of origin, to ensure their rights, safety and dignity.
2.	Provide specialized GBV case management and PSS services and protection assistance for survivors and women and girls who are at risk of GBV, including returnees, stayees, IDPs, host community and those living in mixed population areas of return.
3.	Provide emergency GBV response and protection assistance to newly displaced women and girls.
4.	Provide critical services and assistance to vulnerable women and children in areas of return to access government provided social assistance and support systems.

project_name: Humanitarian WASH support to vulnerable population in the southern areas of the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
This proposal is within the objectives and the framework of the OPTI country HRP strategy under the objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

Further, this project is also aligned with the WASH Sector HRP objectives as follows:

•	Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable access to safe and sufficient WASH services in accordance with dignity of the unserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank                          

•	Strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacity to the unserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank to reduce threats and to cope with emergencies and shocks

The specific objectives include:
a)	Enhancing resilience through improvement of sanitation and sewage networks to reduce rain water and sewage flooding risks
b)	Improving communities’ awareness and comprehension of hygiene awareness standards, especially for women, in order to improve best WASH practices among household members.  

The objectives are referring to needs identified by the HNO and Oxfam conducted assessments.

2.	To strengthen the disease surveillance, outbreak control and response capacity of conflict-affected population at both sides of the contact line of Donetska oblast through development of Early Warning System and promotion of health and hygiene education (will help address Health Cluster Objective 2 - Reduced public health risk through strengthened early-warning and prevention and improved health/risk communication).

project_name: Emergency Assistance and Protection to Conflict-Affected Older People in Government Controlled Areas of Donetsk Oblast
project_objective:
The project goal is to deliver appropriate protection services to conflict affected vulnerable older people in Donetsk GCA and advocate for inclusion and access to services and support from government and local/international organisations.

The proposed action recognizes the need to ensure that ongoing protection based services are delivered to conflicted affected older people. This necessitates HAI to shift operational focus to enabling local community action and participation. HAI Ukraine has already established pre-cursers to increasing community participation through previously established Community Safe Space Centres (CSS). This project will increase community resilience and coping strategies. In order to achieve this, the action will purse to objectives: 

Objective 1: Establishment of 7 Initiative Groups in conflicted affected communities in the grey-zone in Donetsk Oblast by December 2018.  

The Initiative Groups will begin to take over direct responsibility in delivery of key services provided through the Community Safe Space Centres currently supported by HAI Ukraine.

Objective 2: Established “Initiative Groups” are able to support and deliver a range of essential and priority protection based services to conflicted affected vulnerable older people.  

Range and types of services will be set/defined by each Initiative Groups, through community consultation/assessments. Activities could include handicrafts, choirs/group events, health/wellbeing activities, rights information, outreach support visits to vulnerable immobile older people (through creating/supporting Peer to Peer Support Groups (P2P)).  Such activities will improve psychosocial wellbeing, reduce isolation and rebuild disrupted community networks/connections.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving emergency food security and livelihood support to the IDPs and destitute vulnerable host communities’ in West and South Kordofan, and Blue Nile States (PSC sharing consortium)
project_objective:
This proposed project builds on MC's ongoing FSL programming under the consortium arrangement in the target areas, specifically the current SHF funded consortium project, and aims to mitigate the imminent deterioration of food security and nutrition conditions among IDPs and vulnerable host communities and to protect livelihood assets of an estimated 99,000 direct beneficiaries in Abu Kershola, El Qoz and Dellami localities in South Kordofan State; Al Khowey, El Nehoud and Ghubaysh localities in West Kordofan State; Bau, El Kurmuk and El Roseires localities of Blue Nile State. 

The objective of this intervention is to provide the lifesaving assistance to the targeted affected populations through community-based participatory informed approaches with an early recovery methodology so as to reduce their needs and vulnerabilities, increase ownership, enhance their resilience which should also result in some form of sustainability and lay a foundation for follow-up through longer-term approaches.

This will be achieved through providing these affected target communities with needed agriculture inputs (seeds and tools) and infield sessions on best agronomy practices to restore their agriculture-based livelihoods; introducing cash based (through vouchers) approach in livestock vaccination and treatment to gear toward restoring livelihoods and assets lost during the displacements. 

The proposed intervention follows the strategic positioning guiding the Sudan MYHS 2017-19. In particular, the outcome 1 and 3 of MYHS are emphasized throughout the project and all the interventions aimed at saving lives and reducing needs and vulnerabilities by directly increasing production and access to crops contributing to enhanced nutritional status and indirectly strengthening livestock and non-livestock based livelihoods to achieve the same objective. This intervention is shaped by the continuous process of ensuring Accountability to Affected populations and gender equality.

project_name: Provision of WASH and nutrition support to IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities’ in South Darfur and South Kordofan states, to meet their urgent and continuing needs through sustainable methods and solutions
project_objective:
The proposed project builds on Mercy Corps Scotland’s (MC) WASH and FSL programming. MC is currently operational in the following states: 1) In South Darfur: Nyala, IDP camps in El Serif, Dereige, Sakaly; Derbait, East Jebel Marra locality; Almlam, Alwehda locality and Marla, Bielel locality; and 2) in South Kordofan: Kadugli locality (Murta, Kulba, Tillow, As-Samma); Abukershola locality (Khur Al Tina, Umbaraka, Hilat Hussein, Elbobaya, Mabsoot, Elfait, Fajoj, Hilat Gadim, Elrosairis, Hajr Sineina, Ambeer, and Rashad), and Rashad locality (Tag Malla and Rashad central). The project is part of a coordinated and integrated response to address the needs of an estimated 159,530 extremely vulnerable populations in East Jebel Marra locality (Liba, Jawa and Kidneer villages) in South Darfur; and Diling, Reif Ashargi and Abbassiya localities in South Kordofan.

The objective of the project is to support these communities to meet their daily immediate lifesaving WASH needs as per SPHERE and WASH sector standards, build capacity to ensure sustainability for the long-term, build community resilience, and ensure integrated nutrition programming. The project aims to provide affected populations sustained access to WASH services through community based operation and management (CBOM) techniques, using a tried and tested cost recovery and user fee systems managed by community-based WASH committees, and social and behavior change (SBC) methodology to improve nutrition in targeted populations. MC’s efforts will strengthen local systems, improve access to nutrition and water and sanitation services, and promote key behaviors and practices that improve the health and well-being of individuals and communities. MC underscores the importance of integrated programming to achieve this including supporting efforts to address acute malnutrition in countries affected by chronic and acute emergencies and support WASH interventions.

project_name: Protection Response to IDP communities and IDP returnees in Iraq
project_objective:
This project aims to support vulnerable displaced families living in camps and sub-standard accommodation, and highly vulnerable people inadequately covered under the social protection network by providing them with legal counselling and legal representation services in line with all 4 Cluster Objectives of the HRP 2018. It aims to provide vulnerable families who are willing to return home but are unable to do so, the relevant information for them to take an informed decision on their return. It also aims to support people brutalized by violence, especially men and boys, as well as people with disability and their caregivers, to cope and recover through the provision of psychosocial support (PSS) activities.
In response to the ongoing humanitarian crisis in large parts of Iraq, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) will provide assistance to vulnerable conflict-affected populations through an integrated protection response program, targeting specifically IDPs and returnees in Ninewa, Anbar, Kirkuk, Baghdad and Salah al Din. This intervention will consist of protection monitoring, legal assistance (civil documentation, HLPs) and PSS for men and boys. More specifically, the project will focus on legal assistance for IDPs and returnees, through legal counselling, legal representation for civil documentation, Housing Land and Property, and GBV survivors. The legal program also includes representation for detention cases. The IRC will also ensure provision of PSS directly targeting adult men and adolescent boys to assist them to survive, recover and manage the effects of their trauma, as it impacts themselves, their families and community members. As part of the detention legal assistance, the IRC protection team will follow-up on the detainees released from detention centers through case management, linking the ex-detainees and their families to torture case management, psychosocial support, cash assistance, health provision, and any other relevant services.

project_name: Emergency upgrade and repair of vulnerable households’ substandard shelters in the Gaza Strip

The action will provide emergency assistance to acutely vulnerable households living in substandard shelters in the Gaza Strip by ensuring they access adequate and safe shelters and strengthening their capacity to cope with future shocks through a community-based approach. 
The project contributes the Country Strategic Objective 2 “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.” For beneficiaries for whom a full upgrade is not possible, the action will provide emergency winterization and transitional support, this contributing to the Country Strategic Objective 3 “the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”.

The project design endorses all of the Shelter Cluster recommendations, in particular by providing a tailored combination of modalities to maximize impact on beneficiaries while fostering ownership and resilience through a demanding community based self-implementation approach. Through its upgrade component, the action will contribute to the Shelter Cluster objective 1 “Support to displaced populations to mitigate immediate harm and ensure adequate and safe temporary shelter solutions.” Likewise, the transitional assistance / winterization component will contribute the Shelter cluster objective 2 “Support to vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns.”

project_objective:
Strengthening the effectiveness and capacity of the humanitarian leadership and humanitarian sectors and partners to implement a robust humanitarian response based on international human rights law and international humanitarian law (IHL/IHRL).

The proposal aims at strengthening the protection of rights under IHL/IHRL across the humanitarian response to the Syria crisis, including by contributing to the 2018 HRP Strategic Objective 2 and Objective 1 of the HRP Protection Sector Strategic logframe: “The protection of population affected by the crisis is improved through community-based and individually targeted protection interventions and through advocacy with duty bearers”.

This will be done by supporting analysis and mitigation of protection risks, promoting accountability of duty bearers and enhancing protection mainstreaming by all sectors, including by ensuring that the needs of particularly vulnerable groups, such as women and girls are addressed through incorporation of human rights analysis. 

A central element of the project is also to support a consistent, effective and robust implementation of the SSG Protection strategy adopted in 2017 through direct substantive support to the humanitarian leadership throughout the Whole of Syria response.

project_name: Gestion concertée et durable des ressources pastorales pour une résilience aux changements climatiques des populations vulnérables de la région du Guéra et du Département de Fitri (PASTOR CENTRE)
project_objective:
L'action a été élaborée sur la base des données collectées durant la mission terrain et les consultations participatives menées par Oxfam et ses partenaires (ATVP et Nagdaro) dans la région du Guéra et le Département de Fitri. Multiples parties prenantes ont également été associées à la collecte des données de l'action en août 2017, dont les autorités politico-administratives (Préfet, sous-préfet) et traditionnelles (Khalifa, chefs des cantons et notables), les services techniques déconcentrés de l’Etat (Elevage, ANADR, Santé, Education) ainsi que des groupements de pasteurs et agro-pasteurs. 
Objectifs
L'action a pour objectif global de contribuer à la résilience climatique et la réduction de la pauvreté des populations des zones pastorales et agro-pastorales de la région du Guéra et du département de Fitri à travers la promotion de l’exploitation concertée et durable des ressources naturelles. L’objectif spécifique consiste à sécuriser durablement la gestion et l’exploitation des ressources agro-pastorales et l’accès aux services sociaux de base des ménages pasteurs, agro-pasteurs et agriculteurs de la région du Guera et le Département de Fitri.
Parties prenantes
Les Autorités locales et traditionnelles (préfets, sous-préfets, chefs traditionnels), les Services techniques déconcentrés de l’Etat (Elevage, ANADR, Santé, Education) consultées, ont montré leur intérêt pour l’action. Les pasteurs et agro-pasteurs, regroupés en Fédération et Unions avec une représentation des femmes, considèrent les objectifs du projet en cohérence avec le contexte de leur zone et, s’alignent sur la recherche de solutions aux problèmes prioritaires de la zone du centre. Les Comités locaux de prévention et de gestion des conflits, constitués majoritairement des chefs traditionnels, des représentants des pasteurs et des agro-pasteurs consultés dans le Guéra et le Fitri, ont jugé l’action pertinente. project_name: Human rights in humanitarian action – deployment of monitors to Luhansk and Donetsk regions
project_objective:
As per the Centrality of Protection in Humanitarian Action statement by the IASC Principals of 17 December 2013 protection in a humanitarian setting entails upholding human rights and respect for international humanitarian law (IHL). 

1  The project “Human rights in humanitarian action” seeks to increase the presence of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine in the conflict affected areas, including along the contact line, both in the areas controlled by armed groups and areas controlled by the Government of Ukraine, and to establish a stable and continuous monitoring mission with geographical coverage throughout the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, including the ability to cover the grey zones.

2  An important aspect is to ensure that analysis stemming out of the human rights monitoring is utilized by key humanitarian actors, and thus contribute to shape their humanitarian response to the protection needs of the conflict affected population. A human rights approach including gender analysis to the humanitarian response is vital where the population is suffering due to lack of protection and failure of accountability mechanisms. 

3  The project also aims at providing direct support to victims and their families, and strengthening the protection of the conflict affected population as the physical presence of human rights monitors in conflict affected areas may deter further human rights violations and serve in itself as a protection mechanism. By engaging directly with victims and witnesses of human rights violations, this will allow to refer victims to life saving humanitarian services, promote an environment that is conducive to the promotion and respect for human rights and contribute to protect the humanitarian space.

project_name: RÉPONSE INTÉGRÉE EHA, MESA & PROTECTION POUR couvrir les besoins essentiels et protéger les moyens d’existence DES POPULATIONs déplacées et hôtes AFFECTÉES PAR LA CRISE DE Boko Haram dans la région du Lac
project_objective:
L´action proposée vise à réduire l’impact du déplacement des femmes, hommes, filles et garçons lié au conflit Boko Haram , à la restriction d’accès aux zones de production ( les populations dépendent à 80% de l'agriculture et de l'élevage)suite à l’instauration de l’état d’urgence, et à la vulnérabilité structurelle.
Depuis son arrivée sur le Lac en juin 2016 suite à la sollicitation du gouvernement Tchadien, Oxfam a déjà mis en œuvre des activités multisectorielles notamment dans le secteur de la sécurité alimentaire, de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, de la Protection et du plaidoyer humanitaire. L’objectif visait dans un premier temps à répondre aux besoins immédiats (sauver des vies) et ensuite tout en garantissant les acquis de la phase d’urgence, progressivement introduire des activités de relèvement précoce(LRRD). Ainsi 42.800 personnes ont été assistées lors de la première phase de l’intervention (juin 2016 à janvier 2017) et 43.300 personnes lors de la seconde phase (mars 2017-février 2018).
La persistance des mouvements de population (insécurité, faible accès aux facteurs de production) ont conduit Oxfam à continuer son assistance dans le Lac à travers le renforcement des capacités endogènes des communautés déjà assistées lors des phases précédentes, mais aussi de pouvoir répondre à des contingences éventuelles dans toutes la région du lac quand la situation sécuritaire le permet.

Les populations de la Région du Lac Tchad sont sévèrement affectées par la crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle aggravée par la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire liée à la présence du groupe Boko Haram (BH) depuis les dernières années. Les raids du groupe BH, la forte militarisation de la zone (l’état d’urgence est toujours en vigueur jusqu´à ce jour), bien que la dernière attaque des BH dans le Lac cote Tchad remonte en mars 2017 , le retrait des militaires de la FMM  des pays voisins (Niger, Nigeria) a suscité un regain  du climat de peur au sein des populations surtout nomade (Niger-Nguiguimi). A cet effet une tendance de déplacement du nomade (arabe et peul) du Niger vers le Tchad prend de plus en plus de l’ampleur. (Environs 4700 personnes au mois d’aout)    ainsi que des déplacements encore réguliers inter sites. Au Tchad, à ce jour, la crise affecte environ 299.000 personnes dont environs 191.000 communautés hôtes.  106.045 déplacés enregistré depuis mai 2015 dont 90.911 déplacés internes, 14.819 retournés Tchadiens, 324 personnes ressortissant des pays tires . 12.759 déplacés  sont estimés pas encore enregistrés et 8 368 réfugiés dont 6 056 dans le camp de Dar-es-Salam depuis janvier 2015 . 

Cette crise est venue aggraver des conditions de vie déjà précaires d’une grande majorité des populations de cette région caractérisée par un manque d´accès aux services de base (un médecin pour 140 000 habitants) et à l’eau, par l´insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition (12,2 %MAG (seuil urgence 15%) 2,1 MAS (seuil d’urgence 2), faible accès à des infrastructures sanitaires adéquate. Par ailleurs, la stratégie initiale qui consistait à vider les iles du lac pour traquer les combattants a atteint ses limites car elle affecte non seulement les moyens de production mais déstructure aussi les sociétés en menaçant leur mode de vie basé sur les activités lacustres (agriculture, élevage et pêche) fragilisant leurs moyens d’existence. Sur le plan de la protection, 340  incidents de protection ont été recensés en 2016 et concerne les personnes déplacées (91.47%) et les populations hôtes (8.52%). Ces incidents sont liés aux violations du droit à la propriété ; du droit à la vie et à l’intégrité physique ; du droit à la liberté et aux violences sexuelles.

project_name: Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) for Conflict-Affected People in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective: The objective of the project is to contribute to protection and promotion of rights and durable solutions for people affected by the conflict in eastern Ukraine. Within this goal, the specific objectives are to: (1) ensure that a greater number of the most vulnerable conflict-affected people in hard-to-reach areas have access to basic rights and humanitarian assistance, reduce their vulnerability and build resilience; (2) provide IDP with equal access to, and enjoyment of right to adequate standard of living without discrimination, including shelter, livelihoods and employment, effective and accessible mechanisms to restore housing, land and property rights, access to personal and other documentation and freedom of movement, and to push forward adoption of durable solutions policy and practice in line with international standards; and (3) strengthen the respect for human rights and contribute to transitional justice and the rule of law processes. ICLA activities will enable beneficiaries, regardless of their nationality, geographic area of origin or political opinion to access relevant mechanisms to prevent displacement, claim and exercise their rights and entitlements and reach durable solutions. ICLA will seek to address the specific needs and vulnerabilities of women, men, girls and boys with adapted programming and focus on reaching the most vulnerable, notably women/single headed households, specifically with a large number of children, elderly (particularly living alone), people with disabilities or limited mobility, extremely poor and low or no-income families. The project will take into account gender and age to adapt programming and ensure equal opportunities to participate for women and men, girls and boys and prioritize those groups more at risk because of their age, gender, geographic location or disability.

Le programme 3A est basé sur des principes de base que sont : une assistance alimentaire conditionnelle basée sur les besoins nutritionnels et préférences alimentaires des ménages et différents groupes cibles, la saisonnalité, prise en compte de la vulnérabilité à l’insécurité alimentaire/nutritionnelle des ménages bénéficiaires, utilisation de la haute intensité de main d’œuvre (HIMO), normes standards de travail flexibles, de  l’intégration de l’aspect genre, de la protection et du partenariat.

project_name: Improved Access to Specialized Services for the Most Vulnerable Persons Affected by the Libyan Crisis
project_objective:
The project aims at improving access to services for the most vulnerable persons affected by the crisis; in many cases this includes persons with disabilities and persons with injuries. All persons with disabilities in Libya continue to have insufficient access to essential services, regardless of the cause of the impairment, with the situation of survivors of explosive hazards and other persons injured in conflict remaining critical. Victim assistance is a powerful door way to address issues of vulnerability and disability, particularly in a context where other actors who should address these needs are weak or under resourced, and when casualty rates from accidents from conventional and improvised weapons are rising. 

Handicap International’s project therefore follows an integrated approach including victim assistance aiming at improving the access to services for the most vulnerable persons affected by the crisis regardless of the cause of disability; including victims of explosive hazards and other persons with disabilities or injuries. The dual imperatives of the integrated approach are to:
(a) ensure that, as long as specific victim assistance efforts are implemented, they act as a catalyst to the inclusion of women, men, girls and boys with disabilities and other vulnerable groups; and
(b) ensure that broader efforts actually do reach the survivors and indirect victims amongst the beneficiaries.

HI’s comprehensive approach to rehabilitation aims to ensure a holistic improvement of beneficiaries’ capacities, physically and functionally as well as psychologically. Each beneficiary is individually assessed for the definition of their individual treatment plan; implemented either directly through HI Outreach teams, consisting of Physiotherapists and Psychosocial Workers, or through external referrals to other services, either public or via alternative aid programs. 

The project activities will aim at improving and facilitating the ability to access essential services for persons with disabilities or injuries through direct provision of services, including physical therapy, psychosocial support, provision and fitting of assistive devices and mobility equipment, and referral to external specialized services as required. Information on functioning services for referral covering a variety of needs for beneficiaries will be readily available through updated mapping of services and an active referral mechanism.

project_name: WASH Support to Vulnerable Gaza Population in Fragile Unserved and Under-Served Communities
project_objective:
This proposal is within the objectives and the framework the OPTI country HRP strategy under the strategic Objective 2:  The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

Further, this project is also aligned with the WASH Sector HRP objectives as follows:

•	Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable access to safe and sufficient WASH services in accordance with dignity of the unserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank                          

•	Strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacity to the unserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank to reduce threats and to cope with emergencies and shocks

The specific objectives include:
To provide an appropriate, integrated WASH response for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in fragile and critically under-served communities by ensuring access to clean drinking water especially for pupils in schools

To support the capacity building of communities and vendors in maintaining safe drinking water, and promoting hygiene awareness, specifically for women, to minimize the water crisis in the Gaza strip. 
The objective refers to needs identified in the HNO and Oxfam’s recent assessments.

project_name: Promoting a Child Safe Environment in the Gaza Strip through Enhancing Child Protection Response Mechanisms
project_objective:
Objective:
Strengthening an inclusive child protection response and prevention against all forms of violence, child abuse, exploitation, as well as access to legal protection. 

The project is in line with the strategic objectives of the protection cluster that aim at enhancing protection mechanisms, thus contributing towards the respect of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights Law, resulting in mitigating the risk of violence in the society. 
On multi-year approach, the project will contribute towards enhancing the children and children with disabilities (CwDs) resilience through empowering them to be self-protective, claiming their rights through boosting their participation in the community, and strengthening their equal and inclusive accessibility to services and comprehensive referral systems. The capacity building of teachers and services providers on child protection and psychosocial interventions will guarantee the quality of services provided to children, thus improving the well-being of children. The community members will be sensitized on child protection mechanisms and concerns; therefore, this will contribute to better understanding the needs and rights of children with and without disabilities.  
The project will contribute towards building a protective environment for children with and without disabilities that will prevent and respond to violence, abuse and exploitation through strengthening the capacity to fulfil children’s right to protection; promoting the establishment and enforcement of adequate legislation; addressing harmful attitudes, customs and practices; encouraging open discussion on child protection issues that include media and civil society partners; developing children’s life skills, knowledge and participation; raising awareness of families and communities; providing essential services for prevention, recovery and reintegration.

project_name: Integrated child protection and psychosocial support for 20,000 children and strengthening the resilience of 3,000 caregivers  in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states
project_objective:
Street Child will ensure that at least 20.000 girls and boys who have experienced distress in targeted areas of Borno Adamawa and Yobe states have access to a well-coordinated child protection services and psychosocial support activities. The programme will be integrated into our planned EIE activities, utilizing temporary learning spaces and rehabilitated classrooms as safe spaces for children.
With CP activities already planned and funded for 2018 in MMC, Jere, Dikwa, Mobbar and Biu LGAs in Borno, Mubi South and Michiga in Adamawa and Gujba LGA in Yobe, we intend to deepen our presence in these conflict-affected communities. We also intend to expand, given the funding opportunity and relative security stability, to Konduga, Mafa and Damboa LGAs in Borno, and to Madagali in Adamawa.
Street Child is seeking to develop a community CP network that responds to the needs of crisis-affected children, including unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) and children associated with armed groups (CAAFAG). We will establish and/or strengthen community based child protection committees (CBCPCs) in a minimum of 100 communities, supported by an established network of 200 trained in-school PSS facilitators, and 400 PSS facilitators in communities to identify cases, conduct basic PSS and refer cases to social workers where necessary.
Our objective is to establish an effective and coordinated case management mechanism for vulnerable children, and train a team of community social workers to manage cases. They will have resources for these children, including emergency aid kits and conduct family tracing and reunification (FTR) where possible to receive the appropriate integrated response. Street Child also has the objective to build resilience within particularly vulnerable households, to ensure all children at risk live in a safer, more secure environment. Street Child will work to strengthen the livelihoods of at least 500 households and caregivers in targeted LGAs.

project_name: Right To Learn: Supporting Children To Access Education in North East Nigeria
project_objective:
Street Child will ensure that 40.000 children who are out of school in targeted areas of Borno Adamawa and Yobe states have access to formal and non-formal education.
With EiE activities already planned and funded by UNICEF for 2017/18 in MMC, Jere, Dikwa, Mobbar and Biu LGAs in Borno, Mubi South and Michiga in Adamawa, Gujba and Gulani LGAs in Yobe, we intend to deepen our presence in these conflict-affected communities and to expand, given the funding opportunity and relative security stability, to Konduga, Mafa and Damboa LGAs in Borno, and to Madagali in Adamawa.
By creating/rehabilitating 450 classrooms for formal and non-formal Education in conflict-affected communities where displaced people are hosted or in accessible communities where they are returning, and by providing school materials to teachers and children Street Child aims to ensure that at least 40.000 children in these communities do not get left behind in education. Training teachers and communities in PSS, prevention of SGBV, Disaster Reduction and peace-building contributes to children’s safety and well-being.
Street Child is seeking to develop a community EiE network that responds to the education needs of crisis-affected children by establishing and strengthening School Based Management Committees in every formal and non-formal centre supported.
The EiE intervention for Street Child is considered as an integrated approach that includes Child Protection activities in every communities for the most vulnerable and at risk to ensure safe, meaningful and sustainable solutions.
Street Child promotes localisation of the humanitarian response through partnerships. The engagement of local actors is relevant especially considering long term benefits of the response to bridge with the development strategy when the humanitarian actors will start to leave.
We implement partnering with 7 different community-based organizations and national NGOs to build on their extensive experience and knowledge

project_name: Delivery of protection support to IDPs through community mobilization and empowerment in Juba and Yei, Central Equatoria States
project_objective:
The overall aim of the proposed project is to enhance protection of the most vulnerable persons, with focus on persons with specific needs or PSNs (persons with disabilities (PwDs) and other persons in disabling situations such as children/adolescents at risk of illegal trafficking and child labour, unaccompanied or separated children, women at risk of SGBV, single parents, pregnant or lactating women, persons with serious medical conditions, elderly people) by enabling access to psychosocial and rehabilitation support and access to other humanitarian response in South Sudan conflict-affected communities both in Juba and Yei States. HI’s previous and ongoing engagement from 2016 are covering standard general protection activities such as providing tailor-made comprehensive psychosocial and rehabilitation support services for persons with specific needs to strengthen existing coping mechanisms; improving access to basic and specific services; supporting humanitarian actors and communities in gaining awareness on the needs of persons with specific needs and in responding to them in an inclusive manner; and enhancing independence and self-reliance of persons with specific needs through livelihood programming.
In line with Cluster Objectives 1, 2 and 4 HI will:
Reduce vulnerability of PSNs in Juba and Yei states targeting 7000 PSNs in Juba and 5000 PSNs in Yei. The proposed objective is reached through provision of rehabilitation and psychosocial sessions with referral services with components of emergency relief assistance such as distribution of hygiene kits and emergency medical support.

project_name: Provision of basic needs and services for the most vulnerable population groups
project_objective:
The majority of the IDPs in Libya are staying in urban environments with host community families, in rented accommodation or collective shelters. Urban IDPs, who are less visible than those living in camps or rural settings, are often denied basic human rights, live in squalor and lack physical security and freedom of movement. Protracted displacement remain one of the high concerns. Despite several local reconciliation efforts and agreements which included measures to encourage their return, the majority of protracted IDPs are unable to return back to their areas of origin in fear of retaliation, physical safety for them and their families, lack of basic services in areas of return.
The Humanitarian Needs Overview clearly outlined that IDPs lacks proper access to basic services.
For the newly displaced IDPs, UNHCR continues to provide direct humanitarian emergency assistance in the form of in-kind assistance (Non-food items).
The housing situation in return areas is precarious due to a lack of building materials or funds to purchase materials to establish and/or rehabilitate the destroyed or abandoned homes. For the protracted IDPs and non-displaced, for the newly returned, UNHC will provide direct humanitarian assistance, in the form of a combination of in-kind and cash-based assistance wherever feasible and appropriate. This assistance will take the form of in-kind assistance (shelter material kits) combined with tailored family tailored kits and/or combined also with in-kind assistance (one-off or multiple, unrestricted cash grants).
The Libyan authorities have not yet found a permanent solution for the internally displaced populations and returns are sometimes conditioned by payment of compensation. The problems commonly experienced by returning IDPs include access to their property, reestablishment of livelihoods, rehabilitation of a damaged house/apartment and in some cases reconciliation between those who were displaced and those who were not. Protection, as well as Shelter and NFI interventions will be harmonized and closely coordinated with other sectors, particularlyProtection and WASH in order to ensure a multi-sectoral, comprehensive and holistic approach. For example, shelter interventions in collective spaces can include improvement of WASH facilities.
Also community-based approach will be developed through livelihood initiatives, community support projects that take many forms in various sectors, including short-term employment opportunities through infrastructure rehabilitation, service activities; business stimulation through local contracting and procurement; vocational training; market analysis.

project_name: Supporting Early Recovery through Cash Transfer and Livelihoood Opportunities
project_objective:
The project is designed to improve access to food for IDPs and vulnerable host communities in one LGA (Madagali) of Adamawa state through both unconditional cash and cash for work (CFW) programs. Intended target wards of the program include Madagali, Gulak, Shuwa, and Kirchiga. The project will reach 15,750 individuals (approximately 3,150 HHs). in areas with functional market systems providing consistent availability of food commodities.

Cash distributions, both unconditional and CFW, are best suited to meeting the food security objectives of the proposed response especially when it comes to diversification of diet and beneficiary targeting.  Cash transfers allow beneficiaries to make their own choices, yet experience shows that extremely food insecure households typically elect to spend a significant proportion of the cash on food, investing particular attention in nutritionally sound decisions especially when this aspect is reinforced in awareness sessions. 

CFW in particular, in addition to promoting stakeholder ownership, owing to the type of works that will be selected, fit in with the broader strategy of reinforcing existing actors’ initiatives in the target area.  The same is true of DRC’s support to Community Health Clubs.
	
Specific social dimensions, namely; ensuring that women and youth have equal opportunity to be a part of the response, will also be taken into account as described above through the use of DRC’s targeting criteria.  Special emphasis is placed on female heads of households and households with children under five, as well as elderly or disabled individuals.

c) To build community resilience’s to withstand the effects of the current and future shocks
CARE Somalia Humanitarian response plan of 2018 seeks to foster an   integrated multi-sectoral   strategy that will largely be based on linking   emergency response to recovery and resilience building initiatives.  By adopting this approach, CARE will have the leverage to address both the immediate and long-term needs of the drought and conflict affected vulnerable households of Somalia in line with its Country office strategy plans as well as that of the Somalia national development plan of 2016-2020. Beside the approach helps to reduce target communities’ vulnerability to similar risks in future by stimulating transformational change that will build the community resilience’s to future shocks and stresses. in addition, the approach will fully align CARE’s response with the wider Somalia Humanitarian Strategy which prioritizes humanitarian responses under three key objectives: 1) providing life-saving and life-sustaining assistance 2) restoring and strengthening livelihoods and basic service delivery to build resilience and 3) strengthening the protection of vulnerable people and catalyzing durable solutions.
CARE Somalia have strategic Gender action plan which it integrates in all its Emergency response projects to ensure its interventions prioritizes to benefit women, girls and boys who are often the most disadvantaged groups in every disaster. Through this plan, CARE will ensure that over 70% of the beneficiaries under this intervention will be women and children.

project_name: Emergency vaccination and treatment of livestock of the most vulnerable returnee and non-displaced households to control and reduce the spread of zoonotic  diseases
project_objective:
Given the current security situation in Libya that has greatly affected animal health due to lack of vaccines, drugs and veterinary services, the spread zoonotic diseases is expected to increase.  Transboundary Animal Diseases (TADs) are one of the biggest obstacles to livestock production and development in Libya.  This is in addition to existing production systems which are characterized by an extensive farming system-mainly nomadism.

The most important endemic TADs are Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) in cattle and sheep and goats, Bluetongue, peste des petits ruminants (PPR), Bovine brucellosis, Brucellosis in sheep and goats and Rabies (dogs). For the poultry sector, the Newcastle disease is one of the most important. Several other diseases such as contagious respiratory bronchitis (IB), inflammation of the larynx and trachea gastro ILT, chronic respiratory disease, Salmonella, and E. coli are notified.  These diseases are a big threat to food security, nutrition, livelihoods and internal or international trade. 

In order to control and reduce the spread of zoonotic diseases, FAO plans to provide support to 3000 most vulnerable returnees and non-displaced households through vaccination and treatment of livestock.   This will safeguard and protect the livestock which is one of the main food and income sources of the affected population.   The protection is to ensure that the most vulnerable segment of the affected communities, especially pregnant or lactating women, those with children under 5 years of age get access or continue to access animal products (milk products and meat) for a healthy growth and life.

The project will be implemented within the framework of the Libya Humanitarian Response Plan in collaboration and partnership with Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Marine (MoA) and NGO partners on the ground.

project_name: Protective environment for most vulnerable women and children in Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The project interventions are designed to: 
•	Increase psychosocial wellbeing of most vulnerable women and children in vulnerable communities. 
•	Legally empower most vulnerable women and children in vulnerable communities and improve their access to justice.  
•	Increase quality of services provided to most vulnerable women and children through capacity building approach for service providers.   
•	Improve policies and procedures related to GBV, children and women protection. 
As the project is targeting most vulnerable groups of women and children, the project team will work with the spirit of the following principles: prioritizing safety and dignity of targeted communities, including do no harm; enabling equal and impartial access to services including targeting of vulnerable groups and people with specific needs; supporting self protection and assist people claim their rights. 
The project is in line with the objective 3 of 2018 2020 HRP for oPt  which is supporting the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis.
The project is designed for a period of 3 years, some of the activities including provision of psychosocial and legal services to women and children will continue in the next years but in new target areas, but the advocacy campaigns will include new activities to build on the results achieved in the first year, e.g. more efforts will be done towards applying severe punishments on perpetrators committed crimes of children sexual abuse . The 3 years project seeks to achieve long term changes on quality and accessibility to services provided to vulnerable groups, and developing constructive and responsive environment that deals with threats and risks face vulnerable groups. The main long term outputs are improvement in vulnerable groups access to quality services, building capacities of service providers, enhancing referral pathways and coordination between organizations concerned in women and children protection.

project_name: Community based Psychosocial Support and reintegration of children affected by armed conflict
project_objective: Children have been among the most negatively impacted by the ongoing conflict, as they comprise around 40 percent of the Libyan population. Children have been the victims of human trafficking; forced recruitment by armed groups, particularly in the southern region; abduction and torture by armed groups and in migrant detention facilities; and of collateral damage from airstrikes and other targeted attacks. The psycho-social impact on children has been devastating and is further aggravated by the continuous exposure to violence and by their experience of forced displacement. Underage recruitment into armed groups and fighting forces is a key concern, especially among the radical groups including IS. There is lack of social, and in some cases economic, opportunities for adolescents/youth to engage positively among themselves, and to make a meaningful and positive contribution to their families and communities. Additionally, there is the lack of supportive child protection and family welfare services within communities, including more focused specialized services for vulnerable children affected by armed conflict. Also, the presence and control of militias within communities in which children live, increases risk of association with armed groups, including the radical ones. Recruitment and use of children violates their rights and causes them physical, developmental, emotional, mental, and spiritual harm. At a most basic level, children are at risk of death and injury. UNICEF foresees a niche in the release and re-integration of children associated with armed groups as an entry point for strengthening capacity to deliver child protection services and policy advocacy on child rights. A more significant investment in the Children Affected by Armed Conflict (CAAC) monitoring work will support this as well as the scale up of programmes and conduct further assessment on recruitment of children with armed groups. The project will coordinated with similar projects augmented by other sector partners like IOM, UNFPA. An agreement will be reached on the locations of beneficiaries and delivery mechanism to avoid duplication and services.

This will help the children to continue education either through formal or non-formal education setting. This also to help the students to focus on their education to safeguard them not to involve any unwanted social activities as well as for their psychological wellbeing.

Provision of educational support to the most vulnerable students due to the protracted conflict is another target for the Sector under this project. The educational support includes provision of remedial education for those who are at risk of dropping out and low performing students, due to the humanitarian crisis, to help them achieve and stay in the education system, and catch up classes for children out-of-school, due to the humanitarian crisis, to support them to go back to school/education system. In addition, recreational activities will be provided to help the children to create a sense of stability and normalcy which plays an important role in children’s psychosocial well-being and development. While implementing all these activities, education in emergencies and recreational supplies will be provided to this same target students.

project_name: HURRICANE MATTHEW SHELTER RECOVERY PROGRAM
project_objective:
The PADF proposes its proven Build Back Better, Safer and Greener (B3SG) participatory, owner-driven, results-oriented, and sustainability-focused approaches to address the housing post-disaster needs of communities of Cavaillon (South), and Miragoane, Plaisance du Sud, Baraderes, Petit Trou de Nippes, and Anse-a-Veau (Nippes).

The B3SG project objectives are to: 1) assist local residents to rebuild destroyed or to rehabilitate damaged housing stock, in full compliance with Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) best practices, the recent guidelines on shelters response: “Core-House et cadre conceptuel relèvement post-Matthew dans le secteur logement”, and DINEPA sanitation guidelines; 2) improve households’ sanitation and hygiene conditions and behavior; and 3) improve economic recovery through job creation, training youth to participate in housing rehabilitation and construction activities, and supporting local entrepreneurs in the homebuilding trade. 

B3SG supports the MPCE Strategic Objective #1 of the “Relèvement Rapide et Moyens de Subsistance (RRMS)”  initiative. It promotes the MTPTC standards, and extends efforts by the MAST, MSPP, and DINEPA in the target communes. The DRR elements fall within HFA  Priority Action #4 (Reduce the underlying risk factors), and with SFDRR’s Priority #1 (Understanding disaster risk), #2 (Strengthening disaster risk governance to manage disaster risk) and #3 (Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience). 

B3SG is also well-aligned with 1) the Haitian major development projects defined in the Strategic Plan for the Development of Haiti (PDSH), and the Three-Year Investment Program (PTI) 2017-2019; 2) the National Policy of housing and habitat; 3) the PDNA taking into account the environmental, social, economic, and governance pillars; 4) the recent guidelines on shelter response: core-house and recovery conceptual framework in the shelter sector; and 5) the strategic objectives of the shelter group.

project_name: Enhance the resilience of vulnerable Farmers in Gaza strip
project_objective:
Project Specific Objectives:
• 	Support the productive capacity of farmers by providing access to water through functioning water systems (irrigation, collection ponds, carrier lines)
• 	Recover and sustain the livelihoods of farmers by providing cash for work activities
The project will address Country Strategic Objective 3  and will be implemented in partnership with UAWC that have a strong presence and history of intervention in the OPTI including the Gaza Strip. Oxfam’s partnership approach is holistic and
rights-based. The project is planned to be implemented for a period of three years to achieve complementary and transitional activities aiming to enhance the productive capacities of farmers at all levels to sustain food security of farmers and bring their resilience a step forward. Phase one of the project includes activities in Gaza Strip targeting Khanyounis, Middle Area and Northern Gaza Governorates. Activities will include land rehabilitation, planting of field crops and intercropping vegetables, water collecting ponds and carrier lines which will be established in the first year, reaching an estimate of 1120 farmers. Noting that carries lines will be fed from existing wells based on the consultation that UAWC and OXFAM did with MoA. Moreover, the project aims to address aspects of gender injustices between men and women in
the agricultural sector. It will also address safe agricultural practices and enable farmers to follow proper adaptation options. The project follows Oxfam’s resilience framework; therefore, it ultimately aims to increase their absorptive and adaptive capacities.
The project is in line with FSS’s specific objective 1 which aims to enhance the productive capacity of farmers by improving their livelihoods and enhancing their access to water for agricultural purposes which improves the general food security situation and has a positive impact on their overall nutrition and health status.

The overall obj. of this project is to contribute to sustainable farming practices, increase the income of men and women small-scale olive farmers in the targeted areas. The project will operate at two levels: one, at the sub-sector and community level, to facilitate the overall access to the agricultural land, and two, at the farm level to address the opportunities and constraints in the targeted areas and in the olive trees mainly. These two inter-connected layers will be approached from the small producers’ perspective, with clear benefits to women farmers. The specific outcomes are: 
Outcome 1: Improved and more productive small farming system, with more access agricultural land. The project will contribute to the country S.O. and to the FFS objective by increasing Palestinian resilience to the Israeli occupation practices as well as to natural crises, mainly to the following objective:
Strategic Objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.The project will enhance farmers’ accessibility to their agricultural lands where occupying power did not provide this basic need.
The targeted farmers are highly vulnerable and lack access to basic services, including access to land, market, agricultural extension, and finance. This has prevented people living in this areas like others. Thus, AAA will facilitate these essential services, to ensure threats to life, food security, and income are minimized.More precisely, this will contribute to:
 1- Support farmers’ resilience in the targeted locations against the climatic changes and the occupation practices on their land's productivity.2- Improve farmers' livelihood sources in the targeted villages.3- Prevent farms and trees from wild pigs.

project_name: Respondng to and Prevention of GBV incidences affecting children and adolescents impacted by the prolonged conflict in Borno State
project_objective:
The project aims to
1. Provide quality care and case management services to children and adolescent victims and survivors of  gender-based violence in 4 LGAs Ngala, Bama (Banki), Gwoza (Pulka), Kala Balge (Rann) of Borno State 
2. Establish 4 adolescent centers in 4 locations, one of which CHAD will use to pilot an ICT-based psychological first aid (PFA) counseling session in one location (Banki) for victims and survivors of GBV that will entail deploying online technology in the form of an app to connect identified adolescent victims of GBV with an online relief community around the world to share their experiences and engage in safe and meaningful interactions that will help them recover their psychological well being. This effort is expected to improve the resilience and well being of the survivors.  
3. Establish Gender Based Violence Committee (GBVC) in 4 LGAs to organize community activism and awareness campaigns against GBV
4. Provide life skill education and livelihood opportunities to female adolescents as a strategy to strengthen protection around identified victims of GBV and those extremely vulnerable to GBV incidences both in IDP camps and host communities. Life skill sessions could be leveraged on to identify children or adolescents at risk of GBV and refer to appropriate response and prevention service
5. Build the capacity of GBV personnel from CHAD and other sectors using a mentoring approach in order to provide quality care for GBV victims and promote GBV mainstreaming 

It is expected that these objectives contribute to the GBV sub-sector:

project_name: Protecting the human rights of Palestinians in the oPt: Monitoring, Documentation and Advocacy
project_objective:
This project aims to protect Palestinians living under occupation in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and Gaza, through monitoring, documenting and advocacy to end violations of human rights and International Humanitarian Law (IHL) inherent to Israel's occupation, and promote accountability for these violations. The project focuses primarily on two broad issues: First, the imminent threat of demolitions and forcible transfer of communities in Area C and East Jerusalem and the heightened risk to these communities posed by the extreme political reality in Israel and the absence of an international response. Second, the lack of accountability for the killing and injury of Palestinians, including children, by the Israeli security forces throughout the oPt.
The project is based on direct engagement with local Palestinian communities on the grassroots level, the employment of skilled Palestinian field researchers, and cooperation with local and international actors. It also utilizes B'Tselem's unique ability to reach wide and diverse audiences with timely, accurate information and powerful video evidence.
Specific objectives:
Objective 1   Information:
To collect accurate, reliable and timely information that will inform public and policy discourse on violations of human rights and IHL in the oPt.
Objective 2   Awareness:
To raise awareness amongst the Israeli, Palestinian and international public and decision makers of the injustices and human rights violations perpetrated under the prolonged occupation, and to erode the occupation’s guise of legality and temporariness.
Objective 3   International pressure:
To advocate for greater international pressure on Israel by foreign governments and civil society to respect human rights and IHL in the oPt

project_objective: Les conditions d’hygiène et d’assainissement ainsi que l'accès à l'eau potable des populations affectées par le contlit du bassin du Lac Tchad sont améliorés

project_name: Amélioration des conditions d'assainissement, d'accès à l'eau et des pratiques d'hygiènes des communautés du département du Wayi, en particuler les sous-préfectures de Doum Doum et Kouloudia, et du canton de Kangallom
project_objective:
La faible présence d'acteurs humanitaires dans le département du Wayi plonge les habitants de cette zone du Lac dans des conditions de vie précaires, surtout pour leur accès à l'eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène, comme rapportés par les autorités locales de Ngouri. Ces priorités s'inscrivent également dans le Plan d’Action National de Renforcement des Capacités pour la Réduction des Risques de Catastrophes, la Préparation et la Réponse aux Urgences 2015-2020 au Tchad.
Le projet propose ainsi d’améliorer l’accès à l’eau ainsi que les conditions d’hygiène et d’assainissement des populations du département du Wayi et du canton de Kangallom dans la région du Lac. Pour cela, ACTED propose de construire ou réhabiliter des points d’eau existants et controler la qualité de l’eau dans les puits et lieux de stockage existants. Pour s’assurer de l’entretien durable de ceux-ci, ACTED réactivera ou mettra en place des comités de gestion des points d’eau qui seront formés et équipés pour maintenant le puit en état de fonctionnement. Enfin, des campagnes de sensibilisation sur la gestion de l’eau à domicile seront menées pour garantir un bon usage de l’eau de consommation. 
Pour améliorer l’hygiène et l’assainissement, ACTED mènera des sensibilisations aux bonnes pratiques d’assainissement et d’hygiène. L’approche Assainissement Total Pilote par la Communauté (ATPC) sera également promu au sein de la population pour encourager la construction de latrines et ainsi réduire la pratique de la défécation à l’air libre.
Des activités EHA dans les centres de santé (WASH in Nutrition) et dans les écoles (WASH in School) telles que les distributions de kits, la sensibilisation et la construction d'infrastructures EHA permettront également une amélioration globale des conditions sanitaires des communautés visées.

project_name: Education Support for Conflict-Affected Iraqis
project_objective:
This CRS project is designed to address the following education cluster objectives for the year 2018:
• Increase access to inclusive, protective and quality education – formal and non-formal – for conflict affected children, adolescents and youth. 
• Improve the quality of formal and non-formal education for conflict affected children, adolescents and youth through strengthening the capacity of teachers, provision of appropriate teaching and learning materials.   

The project will target 9708 conflict-affected students (primary and secondary) with improved physical infrastructure, social and emotional learning, and strengthened caregiver engagement. Drawing from global best practice, the intervention is integrated within the existing formal school system and targets Dohuk, Ninewa and Kirkuk, the governorates with the highest concentrations of out-of-camp IDPs in Iraq. 

The proposed intervention is designed with strong consideration of protection concerns, as well as the unique needs of girls and boys, persons with disabilities, and diverse groups. In order to foster social cohesion, the project will include host community children living in the same geographic areas; however, given that schools in targeted communities have limited numbers of host community students, CRS estimates that the percentage of host community beneficiaries will be 15%.

project_name: Wrap-around Mental Health, Psychosocial, and Other Support Services for Survivors of GBV in North Iraq
project_objective: The overall objective of the project is to prevent and respond to GBV in its various forms with a focus on sexual harassment, rape, sexual slavery, intimate partner violence, survival sex, sexual exploitation, polygamy, and early/ forced marriages. Activities will primarily target vulnerable women and girls that have been displaced by conflict and/or are returnees to the Ninewa Plain and Duhok governorate in North Iraq. Sites will include camps and temporary formal and informal settlements, and services will be provided in “safe spaces”. In order to reach survivors in remote and isolated areas, mobile outreach teams will also be utilized. All interventions and activities will be designed according to cluster objectives and will be life-saving as they will address and reduce the debilitating and dangerous consequences of GBV. Interventions will be comprehensive, holistic, and tailored to match the individual needs of survivors. Services offered will include psychological first aid, psychosocial support, mental health care, psychotherapy, counselling, and psychiatric medication support. When possible, interventions will also incorporate local spiritual beliefs and traditional healing practices that promote recovery. The project will also support reintegration of survivors into their families and communities by raising awareness about GBV, organizing support groups, working directly with families, and engaging with religious and other community leaders. In addition, the project will strengthen the technical capacity of staff that are providing services including mental health and psychosocial support, case management, and clinical management of rape (CMR). Norwegian Church Aid will provide overall management of the project throughout its lifecycle. However, in order to raise local capacity and ensure sustainability, most activities will be implemented by local partners.

project_name: Improve the access to food services to the refugees populations affected by the conflict in the Far North of region of Cameroon.
project_objective: In addition to the security context, the far North region of Cameroon suffers frequent droughts, floods and epidemics that usually strike the Sahel countries.  The combination of conflict and disasters together with chronic poverty have caused the gradual deterioration of the population’s livelihoods. Moreover, the fear of infiltration of Boko Haram fighters to outsource basic supplies from areas close to the Nigerian border has prompted local authorities to restrict the amount of goods to the areas which has limited the ability of the refugees and host communities to access sufficient food.
