project_name: LEBANON - United Nations Children's Fund
JORDAN - United Nations Children's Fund
Emergency WASH Response and Building Resilience for Conflict affected Women, Men, Boys and girls in Syria
project_objective:
Building on experience of project interventions in Syria since 2013, Oxfam is planning to respond in the most vulnerable districts/sub-districts with high severity in Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Homs, Hama, Dar’a and Idleb based on the severity of WASH needs 

The sub-districts that will be targeted by this project have all been heavily affected by conflict and are in need of additional WASH support, based on a rapid Oxfam assessment in some of the selected villages, consultations with Syrian and international NGOs, and reliable secondary data, including the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2019. The project is designed to meet specific life-saving needs around water sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and is aligned to HRP 2019 for Syria. The project focuses on WASH response with gender mainstreamed, and with a well-defined response strategy suitable to access situation and security challenges; this includes implementation through reliable and experienced site engineers, public health promotion volunteers and focal points, carefully screened private contractors, and coordination with other actors. The total estimated populated, as per UN-OCHA datasets in these sub-districts, is over 1,752,742 people.  This estimation has to be taken as a rough guide, given that many people have been displaced, with many IDP and returnee fluctuations within Governorates and Districts across Syria.

Target locations have been proposed according to severity of humanitarian needs and number of population in need. They may be altered depending on the evolution of the context on the ground, access and people's movement. 
The project aims to support life-saving WASH interventions as well as activities that focus on the maintenance and/or the light rehabilitation of existing WASH systems: a) improve the target communities' access to safe water facilities, b) appropriate capacity to maintain key health and hygiene practices; c) access to safe sanitation facilities and services and; d) WASH emergency response including the provision of WASH materials, equipment and services i.e. water taks, O&M water trucking and emergency WASH facilities 
Oxfam planned interventions will be inline with: SO1 that captures sector efforts to restore or keep Water and Sanitation infrastructure at the minimum level of operation and SO2 which describes life-saving WASH interventions such as emergency provision of water, sanitation and solid waste facilities and services as well as WASH NFI distributions. 
In the terms of the interventions above, Oxfam will target all age groups for water and sanitation interventions. For the hygiene interventions, these will be targeted women and a focus on children as a proportion of the activities will be conducted at school level.
The specific locations for activities in these sub-districts are still to be declared.  Specific WASH interventions will be assessed by Oxfam WASH teams, including full costings, and will be discussed with LWE officials, local authorities, and WASH Sector actors to ensure complementarity of interventions versus work of other actors in targeted areas.  As final interventions will require approval of both the MoWR and MoE, Oxfam will convene a project steering committee which will include both Oxfam management staff and Government representatives at Damascus level, who will discuss and agree selection of possible activities and operational challenges

project_name: Global Rehabilitation and mental health-psychosocial support services for conflict affected populations and support to health structures in Syria
project_objective:
The health intervention will focus on the injured pathway, as part of its victim assistance approach, i.e. will support the health partners and structures and manage its health teams for the provision of various services. 
The NGO, its implementing partners and the health facilities supported will comprehensively address the urgent needs of persons with functional limitations through a combination of physical rehabilitation (including provision of assistive devices and education sessions for caregivers), P&O and PSS services within the global rehabilitation framework, and MHPSS. These services will aim to foster the beneficiary's recovery of functional independence and acceptance of his new condition to regain a certain level of confidence, autonomy and wellbeing. Interventions will be delivered through stand-alone, complementary and integrated services. Further to supporting beneficiaries with functional limitations, the Action will target caregivers for a holistic service delivery to alleviate and help them cope with stress, fatigue and other psychosocial impacts and vulnerabilities related to their new caregiving responsibility. In NES, the Organization will consolidate and strengthen its support to health facilities including referral hospitals so as to set up sustainable rehab and prosthetics services while reaching out to remote and underserved communities as part of its first-line emergency response in the three governorates. In GoS-controlled areas, the INGO will focus at developing rehab and MHPSS services in areas where services are not present or functioning, through the support and capacity-building to local partners.
The MHPSS component, offered to assessed-persons suffering from psychosocial disabilities, will be built on the innovative pilot activity conducted during the 2018/2019 Action. In parallel, the Organization will develop capacity development plans for its health partners and the health facilities supported to build their independence through technical and organizational long-term support. the Organization will also seek to foster operational coordination between humanitarian actors at hub and WoS levels so as to improve the quality of interventions.

i) physical and functional rehabilitation (including physical and functional rehabilitation sessions, provision of assistive devices, education sessions for caregivers), 
ii) P&O services (sessions and provision of P&O items),
iii) PSS sessions to people with functional limitations and their caregivers
iv) MHPSS services (psychological first aid, psychoeducation, individual session therapy or MHPSS group sessions).

project_name: WASH life saving assistance and building resilience for conflict affected population in Syria
project_objective:
WASH services are critical to the survival of displaced people and returnees, fundamental to the recovery of their dignity as human beings and a basic point for their acceptance by host communities. 
In 2019 AAH will prioritize activities that directly support life-saving WASH interventions as well as activities that focus on the maintenance and/or the light rehabilitations of existing WASH systems. Both aspects of the sector strategy are life-saving and life-sustaining and can help reduce recourse to harmful coping strategies that risk exacerbating existing needs. 
In line with this sector strategic objectives, AAH offers a mix of delivery modalities ranging from water trucking, coupled with the installation of water tanks and the distribution of jerry cans, and more permanent options such as rehabilitating wells or boreholes or extension of the existing infrastructure. 
Sanitation systems will be improved through the maintenance and rehabilitation of sewage. The connection of sewerage to the public network has been identified as a key intervention by beneficiaries (including women and people with a disability) to eliminate exposure to faecal contamination and to remove the physical danger of open pits. WASH team will design the system to minimize the risk of leaks and breaks. Once the sewerage systems will be repaired and functional, the local municipality will be responsible for continuing the operation and maintenance. 

In terms of hygiene women, men, girls and boys will receive emergency gendered hygiene kits, potentially during the first days of displacement. These kits have an important role to play in preventing disease outbreaks and to carry out everyday requirements. Some items are lifesaving, such as soap for maintaining hygiene. Other items may simply contribute to people’s sense of dignity in difficult circumstances e.g. underwear, razors and toothbrushes. Distributions will be done mostly through SARC.
AAH will integrate protection and gender-sensitive approaches to ensure the infrastructure are safe for women and girls, boys and men at the point of delivery using artificial light, safe routes and segregation by sex. It will also take in consideration general public safety and environmental issues to ensure that there are no irreversible impacts in public health or ecological footprint.

project_name: Ensure protection and assistance for refugees in Sudan
project_objective:
The programme addresses the basic needs of all non-South Sudanese refugees and asylum seekers, including refugees from Eritrea, Ethiopia, Syria, Yemen, Chad, Somalia, CAR and others. This includes ongoing voluntary repatriation of Chadian refugees in West Darfur.
Voluntary return is not a viable option for most refugees in Sudan, and resettlement options remain limited. For this reason, the refugee response integrates asset-building and livelihoods, to strengthen self-reliance and ensure refugees may lead dignified lives while in Sudan. Mainstreaming of protection assistance, including direct support to SGBV survivors, will be prioritized. In eastern Sudan, the response will continue to bolster reception and protection services for new arrivals, including prepared meals and health and nutrition screenings. It will maintain basic assistance for the most vulnerable refugees in camps across Kassala and Gedaref, including food assistance through cash based transfers (CBT) for both asylum seekers and newly recognized refugees. Protection assistance will emphasize UASC identification, family tracing and reunification and psychosocial support services, as well as improved referral pathways for direct GBV support to survivors. The response also prioritizes longer-term solutions, with a strong role for protection through self-reliance initiatives to address the unique needs of protracted caseloads. The response will include specific protection assistance for refugees transiting through Sudan, as well as for victims of trafficking. Targeted outreach to asylum seekers on onward movement risks will be pursued and integrated within livelihoods programming to support a more favourable protection environment.
The response also addresses the needs of refugees living in urban areas, especially in Khartoum, with a focus on livelihoods programming to support self-reliance, such as vocational training opportunities, CBT, micro-financing and livelihood asset protection, with efforts to create partnerships with the private sector and development actors. To safeguard basic needs support will also be expanded to ensure refugees can access national education and health systems, as well as to strengthen community-based protection networks and improve referral pathways for GBV prevention, treatment.

project_name: 2019 UNICEF PROJECT MODULES: INTEGRATED NUTRITION RESPONSE TO THE HUMANITARIAN CRISIS IN NORTH EAST NIGERIA
project_objective:
The food security and the nutrition situation remains fluid and fragile across the north-east. An estimated 1,600,367, 870,162 and 515,005 people in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states respectively were in a crisis and emergency food insecurity situation throughout the months of June to August 2018 (March 2018 Cadre Haromonisé). Malnutrition is worse among certain population groups, for example IDPs who are arriving in ‘reception sites’ from inaccessible areas. 
In 2019 the nutrition response aims at strengthening access to quality integrated nutrition services for the most vulnerable malnourished children and women in North-East Nigeria though strengthening of existing government health system, deployment of mobile nutrition outreach teams in hard-to-reach areas and ensuring coordinated and convergence approach. It will facilitate access to life-saving nutrition services through early detection and referral of malnourished children to nutrition service centres for appropriate nutrition services as well as strengthen government system and empower communities for better resilience. 
In alignment with the sector response, UNICEF interventions will consider acute, moderate and chronic needs to reach 1,187,924 beneficiaries made up of 729,713 children and 458,211 women. An amount of $27,225,083 is required for the response.

Objective
•	Enhance access to quality nutrition services for prevention and treatment of malnutrition among children, pregnant and lactating women.
•	Strengthen capacity of nutrition service providers and community volunteers for timely identification, referral and follow up of malnourished cases and provision of appropriate nutrition services.
•	Enhance routine monitoring of the nutrition situation through regular assessment and analysis of data. 
•	Strengthen coordination within the nutrition partners and other sectors to address the gaps and avoid duplication.

project_name: Food Production for Vulnerable Households
project_objective: Through the support of village farming schools and the creation of kitchen gardens for women, the project aims at establishing sustainable agricultural production and improving the livelihood situation of the most vulnerable rural populations. This shall be achieved with the distribution of seeds and tools and the teaching of improved cultivation techniques, sustainable agricultural practices and through cooking demonstrations about how to prepare and process nutritious foods. Around 500 women will receive support through kitchen gardens and 500 farmers will be assisted through agricultural field schools. In total, around 1,000 households will benefit from the project.

project_name: Projet d'Assistance Multisectorielle d'Urgence pour les NOuveaux Réfugiés centrafricains et des Communautés Hôtes de Goré et de Moissala (PAMUNOR )
project_objective:
La présente action vise les réfugiés des sites de Bekan (Goré), de Silambi, Dilingala et de Gon
(Moissala) et des villages hôtes, avec pour objectif de contribuer à la restauration des moyens
d'existence et le renforcement de la coexistence pacifique/lutte contre les Violences Basées sur le
Genre (VGB/GBV). Elle passera par l'amélioration de leur niveau socio-économique à travers le
développement des activités économiques à savoir l'agriculture et les activités génératrices de revenus.
Cependant, vu qu'aucune intégration ne peut être possible dans un contexte où règne l'insécurité,
l'action mettra l'accent sur le renforcement de la cohésion sociale à travers la mise en
place/redynamisation/renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de prévention et de gestion des
conflits ainsi que ceux relatifs aux violences basées sur le genre. Par ailleurs, pour tenir compte de la
spécificité des personnes à besoins spécifiques (PBS) dont les personnes âgées, les personnes ayant
une déficience qui vivent dans les conditions très précaires, des abris en semi-durs seront construits.
Les campagnes d'information et de sensibilisation en fonction des activités seront menées pour une
meilleure compréhension, connaissance et appropriation de l'action. Les autorités locales seront
impliquées dans les différentes phases de l'action. Les activités proposées s'intègrent dans la Stratégie
globale de réponse à la nouvelle crise centrafricaine élaborée par les acteurs humanitaires.

project_name: Enhance the collection and provision of evidence-based information on migration and displacement inside Libya
project_objective: The project aims to enhance IOM’s ongoing efforts to support the humanitarian community by providing a common operating picture concerning the movement of populations in Libya, allowing humanitarian actors to provide timely assistance to those in need. This includes monitoring migratory trends, tracking migration dynamics, capturing data on migrant demographics, profiles and vulnerabilities, monitoring displacements, profiling detention centres  , and building capacities of national authorities on information collection and database management. The data and results produced by DTM help to implement evidence-based humanitarian assistance, advocacy and identify locations in need for further in-depth sectoral assessments.

project_name: Strengthening the Children and Adolescent Protection Mechanisms for Vulnerable Rohingya Refugees and Host Community in Cox Bazar
project_objective:
The main objective of this Project is to strengthen the protective mechanisms of vulnerable children and Adolescent in refugee camps and in the host community. The project targets 299,770 persons through strengthened community-based mechanisms, provision of psycho-social support, specialized case management and through integrating and mainstreaming child protection and gender in other sectors. The project will strengthen referral mechanisms and will empower children, adolescents and communities by promoting their active participation. Peaceful co-existence with host community will also be strengthened.  The partnership with the Department of Social Services (DSS) will help to promote social coexistence through sports, peace-building, meetings, and coordination.
In the camps, UNICEF will target 60,646 girls, 56,700 boys, 47,905 adult males and 51,223 females.  In the host community, UNICEF will target 3,296 refugees (824 girls, 824 boys, 824 men and 824 women).  UNICEF will also target 80,000 vulnerable Bangladeshi in the host community. The project will be delivered through partnership with 4 local organizations, 8 international organizations and in partnership with the Department of Social Services.

project_name: Enhancing coordination to support Early Recovery and Livelihood response.
project_objective:
Opportunities and Needs are increasing for enhanced Early Recovery action on the ground. This requires additional efforts to strengthen coordination at the national as well as sub-national levels by allocating human resources to support the growing membership of the Early Recovery Sector to undertake comprehensive Early Recovery planning and to ensure effective coordination in the collective response of sector partners.
Furthermore, in view of the broad range of Early Recovery interventions, cutting across several line ministries and the sectors they represent, it is essential to continue supporting the work of focal points within the administration, at the appropriate decision making and operational level to ensure continuous information exchange on needs assessed, priorities and to fast track clearances required for implementation.
The ERL sector has established this sector coordination and interface capacity in the five governorates where currently the UN hubs are present.  Additionally, coordination for cross-border ERL activities has been in place at the Whole of Syria level.  The coordination at the field level proved to be essential to bring the ERL partners under one umbrella to enhance early recovery actions on the ground not only to avoid overlapping and gaps, but equally to attain synergies in interventions.

project_name: JORDAN - Danish Refugee Council
Integrated Emergency WASH, Food Security and Education Services in Blue Nile and Central Darfur States
project_objective:
This proposed project aims to sustain, expand the provision of improved WASH, food security and livelihood, and Education services to conflict affected IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in Blue Nile State (Al Kurmuk, Damazine, Rosaries and Geissan localities) and Central Darfur State (Nertiti and Golo in Central and West Jabal Marra localities). The project will address the WASH, FSL and Education needs of 47,190 in Blue Nile state in addition to WASH and Education needs of 76130 persons in Central Darfur state. 
In Blue Nile State, this project will: - enhance  and sustain access to improved drinking water  and basic safe sanitation through drilling and installation of new HPs; rehabilitation of nonfunctional HPs; training of HP mechanics and provision of hand pump maintenance tool sets. The WASH activities will reduce overcrowding at host community water sources that are partially utilized by IDPs – i.e. the intervention will contribute to improved social cohesion between the IDPs and host communities. Aiming at enhancing access to safe basic sanitation facilities for the IDPs, especially those will be affected by AWD, the project interventions will include  construction of school latrines; building the capacity of communities through training of WASH committees on water resources management; establishment and support of sanitation clubs; conduct of sanitation awareness campaigns; provision of hand washing facilities; training on CHAST approaches; and water quality monitoring and testing. Hygiene promoters training will be key  part of the project to  facilitate safe knowledge and practices transfers to end beneficiaries towards sustainable behavior change and adoption of good hygiene practices. To preserve the natural environment, the project contains solid waste management, vector control, and environmental friendly technologies will be adopted.  - In FSL sector The project will provide varied interventions to support livelihoods of vulnerable displaced and host communities that have suffered widespread conflict and violence. The proposed project will achieve this through provision of emergency agricultural inputs and services which include distribution of food crops and vegetable seeds, tools and extension service; provide emergency livelihoods training and start up kits, free animal vaccination as part of emergency livestock inputs and veterinary services that will be provided to the IDPs, formation and support of women farmer associations, and natural resources conservation and management. 
- In Education sector, the project intends to increase and sustain access to education in emergencies for IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Damazine, Rosaries, Rosaries, Kurmuk and Geissan localities. IRW will provide access to safe learning spaces for 5,303 boys and girls through construction of 8 semi-permanent classrooms and rehabilitation of 8 classrooms. In Central Darfur State, , the project will
-	enhance and sustain access to improved drinking water and basic safe sanitation facilities. WASH services will cover nearly 45000 conflict affected IDPs, returnees and host communities, 
-	In Education sector, the project will focus on the construction and rehabilitation of both girls and boys government schools, aiming at creating a child and education friendly environment with maximum enrollment and minimum drop outs. Quality of education will be enhanced through teacher trainings and provision of reaching aids e.g. quality furniture for teachers and schools, learning and recreation kits and improved water and sanitation services.

project_name: Improving Health  and Nutrition of SSR and Host community in El Mairam
project_objective:
The proposed project is intended to contribute to improving the health status and nutritional wellbeing of refugees through provision of basic health and nutritional services in five PHC centers across the Locality of El Mairam. The project will target 12,000 individuals (5760 male and 6240 female including 2100 under 5 year-old children) from South Sudan refugees and host community in El Mairam Locality of West Kordofan state. 
There is only one functioning health center in El Mairam town serving both the refugees and host community 12,000 with very limited capacity in terms of facilities, equipment and staff. There are other four health centers in the admin units (El Heraika, El Odam, Umm Deries and Umm Senainaiya), not functioning and without even health or nutrition staff. The buildings are well constructed, need some repairs, equipment and furniture and then support with trained staff to deliver the services. 
The proposed intervention will aim to rehabilitate the existing centers, provide essential equipment, furniture and train local staff as well as provide support for operation cost and incentives for staff to ensure continuity of services. The project will deliver RH comprehensive package, case management and vaccination services as well as awareness to refugees and host community to increase knowledge on health interventions. It will also provide support to PLW, children and mother groups for supplementary feeding, MUAC and IYCF programme.

project_name: Multi-purpose cash-based support of food security and resilience in Upper Nile, Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective: With the aim of saving lives, the project will center on providing multi-purpose cash-based support to the most vulnerable households to meet immediate food and basic needs with dignity. The multi-purpose cash-based support is combined with support to local markets, distribution of productive assets (fishing gear) and training support to producer and market groups. Combined, these activities are expected to protect productive livelihoods assets, lower the use of irreversible and damaging coping strategies, and reducing the increasing aid-dependency, increasing overall resilience to shocks.

project_name: Protecting Civilians through Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in Syria has been compounded by the scale and scope of diverse explosive hazards, lingering long after hostilities have ceased. 10.2 million men, women, boys, and girls now live in communities reporting explosive contamination. 

The overall aim of UNMAS project “Protecting Civilians through Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria” is to reduce the impact of explosive hazards on the civilian population and humanitarian workers in Syria through effective sector coordination and the implementation of humanitarian mine action activities from both the cross-border hubs, in line with UNSCR 2449, and from Damascus. UNMAS has been operational, in cross border hubs of the Syria Response since 2016 and in October 2018, UNMAS opened its office in Damascus to directly carry out humanitarian mine action in Syria. UNMAS leads the Mine Action Sub-Cluster (MASC), with a view to enhancing coordination and therefore operational effectiveness, including better integration of humanitarian mine action into the wider humanitarian response.

Under this project, in accordance with this humanitarian response plan, UNMAS will lead, manage and coordinate humanitarian mine action activities: risk education, victim assistance and clearance as defined by International Mine Action Standards (IMAS). In strict respect of humanitarian principles UNMAS activities are driven by the needs of vulnerable population groups. The delivery of risk education, tailored to age, gender, localized threats and activity patterns of different at-risk groups, is a critical, life-saving activity for raising the awareness of civilians and humanitarian personnel about the dangers posed by explosive hazards. As the Syrian crisis has been characterized by large-scale conflict and displacement, survey, data collection, and mapping are critical to informing on localized threats, humanitarian programming, and needs-based prioritization, as well as the expansion of clearance to remove the contamination threats facing civilians, particularly in high-priority areas. Furthermore, UNMAS will support the expansion of victim assistance and provision of specialized services for persons with disabilities, in particular survivors of explosive hazards and their families.

UNMAS activities will also promote and support the understanding and use of humanitarian mine action technical standards and guidelines, in coordination with the Government of Syria, to enhance safety and effectiveness.

project_name: Protection from eviction through integrated HLP interventions in Somalia
project_objective:
Characterized by entrenched intertwining complexities and having far-reaching consequences on general protection and recovery efforts, i.e. durable solutions initiatives, evictions remain unarguably one of the most pressing protection challenges in Somalia. As a country that is still recovering from the legacy of prolonged state collapse, and grappling with persistent insecurity and cyclic natural disasters, evictions further exacerbate the protection vulnerabilities of displaced communities. Albeit important strides are being made, the scale, scope and prevalence of the problem have proportionally outmatched ongoing eviction response initiatives, thus necessitating a more robust, integrated and coordinated program response. It is within this broader strategic framework that the current project, which seeks to facilitate enhanced protection of displaced communities from evictions, has been conceptualized. Project services and customized assistance packages will benefit 71,400 individuals in 21 districts across 15 regions. In terms of delivery modalities and outputs, the overarching objectives of the project will be achieved through a combination of complementarily reinforcing set of actions that are framed around the following eight core pillars. 

1. Strengthening ongoing eviction monitoring systems to enhance analysis, data availability and usability. 2. Scaling up and consolidating eviction risk mapping to inform advocacy and response. 3. Supporting proactive engagements to negotiate improved tenure arrangements and/or facilitating dignified relocations for populations of concern. 4. Mitigating protection risks exacerbated by evictions by providing different forms of tenure security support to displaced populations, including facilitating issuance of documentations at both household and group levels. Documentation will also seek to reduce risks to HLP assets on which local livelihood initiatives are dependent. 5. Supporting extremely vulnerable victims of evictions cope with post-eviction stress (PES) through the provision of multi-sectoral cash assistance, specialized counselling and legal assistance services. 6. Mobilizing and supporting government’s effort to address evictions, including robust engagement with landlords, gatekeepers and community leaders. 7. Facilitating access to information designed to assist IDPs access services, navigate complex procedures, and utilize existing remedies in areas of displacement to enhance their protection. 8. Strengthen coordination as well as the functional and operational capacity of the HLP sub cluster.

project_name: Strengthening the protection environment and supporting psychosocial needs in affected communities in Iraq
project_objective:
IOM will continue to offer holistic support predominantly to internally displaced persons (IDPs) including individuals, families and other vulnerable people in camps and return areas in Ninewa and Dohuk Governorates, Kirkuk and Diyala, particularly those returning to their original communities or integrating in the communities of displacement. IOM is planning a wide variety of protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) activities to support vulnerable populations, at all layers of intervention under the Health and Protection Clusters. IOM will provide activities in line with the Protection Cluster objectives 1 -Provide specialized protection assistance, and community-based support, to conflict-affected individuals, thereby enabling them to secure their rights, access humanitarian assistance and public services, and overcome barriers to achievement of durable solutions; 2 -Support and advocate with authorities, humanitarian and recovery actors to address protection issues in accordance with protection norms and applicable legal standards, thereby contributing to a favorable protection environment; and 3 - Improve response timeliness through preparedness: to prevent further degradation of humanitarian needs. 
Focused-non-specialized and community-based activities will help beneficiaries to feel safer and calmer, reactivate or strengthen their social networks, and regain hope in the future.  This includes case management, emotional supportive sessions, social gatherings, skills training, educational activities and guided group discussions. Vulnerable populations will gain tools to cope with displacement and be more resilient, being active members of their recovery. Services will be offered though static community centers and mobile teams, including outreach visits in both modalities. Referrals will be done to specialized services. Services will be carried out in line with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) and global cluster guidelines and in coordination with the Clusters. MHPSS activities will be implemented through Psychosocial Staff based at the centers, with the support of community based Focal Points and volunteers. The project will engage qualified IOM national staff, including psychologists, social workers and educators, some of them belonging to the minorities. They would be directly supervised by international psychologist, psychiatrist and peaceful co-existence experts.  Activities related to peaceful co-existence, including awareness and community-based activities, will primarily focus on supporting IDPs in areas of displacement.
For sustainability and preparedness, capacity building for humanitarian and development partners and government staff will be provided to enhance their capacity to provide MHPSS services, and IASC guidelines. Capacity building is provided though classroom base training, coaching and supervision. To improve timeliness and response, there will be a focus on improving referral pathways, access to hotlines and a big emphasis on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), through internal and external trainings, awareness raising and speaking directly to beneficiaries. IOM interventions are designed to support the coping mechanisms and resilience of affected communities. 
Specify governorates and districts for GBV
IOM protection is currently conducting protection scoping missions to determine gaps in GBV programming. As part of this process, IOM will work closely with the GBV and protection clusters, and other I/NGOs and local stakeholders. Possibilities include IOM Mosul or Falluja Community Resource Centers (CRCs) (note these are different to the IOM Community Centres); Sinjar; and scaling up of the Dohuk response. Currently GBV programming is in Ninewa: Haj Ali IDP camp and Dohuk: city and Sharya IDP camp. GBV awareness raising activities take place throughout Iraq, mainly in Erbil, Dohuk, Sulaymania and Baghdad, in and out of camps.

project_name: JORDAN - Action Contre la Faim
LEBANON - Norwegian Refugee Council
Integrated protection, monitoring and response assistance to conflict affected populations in Libya
project_objective:
Since the outbreak of conflict in 2011, Libya continues to suffer from the impact of a protracted political crisis and civil conflict, which affected an estimated 1.5 million people in 2018 (Libya 2019 HNO (draft)). In response, DRC proposes to provide a comprehensive package of support, which includes protection, cash assistance and quick impact projects (QIPs) to build a more favourable protection environment for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees, at both the individual and community level in western Libya (greater Tripoli, Zawiya, Sabratha, and Al Gabal al Gharbi), where DRC has ongoing projects in 2018. The protection activities will have a strengthened protection monitoring and referral mechanism at its core with the aim of a more informed response and advocacy initiatives. This will be complemented with specialized protection service provision targeted at the most vulnerable groups of women, girls and boys. In line with its aim to be a comprehensive programmatic approach, activities have been proposed to reach those affected at each stage of prevention, assessment and response, and therefore will reference objectives 1, 2 and 3 of the HRP protection objectives. 

Note: this proposal describes a single programme of three (separately funded) projects.

project_name: Emergency Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The project “Emergency Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Eastern Ukraine” (February 14, 2018 - June 13, 2019) aimed at addressing the most urgent food needs of the conflict affected, food insecure populations residing in the government-controlled areas of Luhansk and Donetsk Oblasts, particularly in communities within 5 km of the Line of Contact. Since markets are operational (see e.g. ACTED-led Market Monitoring Reports), the main project modality was cash assistance (unconditional grants to cover basic food needs). However, bed-bound beneficiaries and beneficiaries with limited mobility, who were unable to shop on their own, are provided with in-kind assistance. Until 13 June 2019, the project was implemented by ASB in consortium with ACTED and SSU and was funded by the Federal Foreign Office of the Federal Republic of Germany. 
The follow-up project “Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine” (14 June 2019-13 June 2021), funded by the Federal Foreign Office of the Federal Republic of Germany, will be implemented by ASB Country Office Ukraine (food, hygiene and winterization components) and Samaritan Union of Ukraine (psychosocial support component).

project_name: Renforcer l’accès des communautés, et particulièrement des individus les plus vulnérables, aux services de protection dans les cercles de Koro, Bankass et Douentza
project_objective:
Ce projet mis en oeuvre par l'équipe de protection de DRC vise à assurer une assistance immédiate aux victimes de violations de droits humains, aux survivantes VBG et aux enfants victimes d’abus dans les cercles de Koro et Douentza, et à faciliter le renforcement d'un environnement protecteur dans les communautés affectées par la crise sécuritaire au centre du pays. Ce projet vise à la fois à renforcer la protection à base communautaire, par le biais de renforcement des comités locaux de protection communautaire en identification, référencement et prise en charge immédiate des victimes de violations, mais également à consolider les capacités des acteurs institutionnels à répondre aux incidents de protection de manière immédiate, continue, et durable. Le projet engage notamment la Commission Justice, Vérité et Réconciliation, ainsi que les centres de santé de référence, les mairies, les directions régionales de la promotion de l'enfant et des familles, et autres acteurs locaux. Le projet inclut notamment des activités d’identification, de prévention et de réponse aux besoins de protection au niveau individuel et communautaire, à travers l’apport direct de services psychosociaux et de premiers secours psychologiques, le référencement, un appui individuel spécifique à des structures appropriées, le soutien à deux centres communautaires permettant la mise en place d'espaces sûrs pour les victimes de violations de droits et les survivant(e)s de VBG. Ce projet inclut également une forte composante de monitoring de protection, avec le déploiement d'une équipe mobile de moniteurs à travers les localités d'intervention (et en coordination avec les partenaires déployant du monitoring de protection dans la région). La participation active de l'équipe de projet aux groupes de travail régionaux et nationaux permettra également de développer un solide plaidoyer en faveur du renforcement de la protection au centre du Mali, en collaboration avec les partenaires engagés dans la réponse de protection. 

L’action de ce projet aura un impact direct à niveau local et régional, avec d’une part, le renforcement des capacités des collectivités et des communautés elles-mêmes, et de l’autre, l’amélioration de la coordination et du partage d’informations au niveau régional entre tous les acteurs du Sous-Cluster Protection de Mopti et les autres parties prenantes. Au niveau national, les produits seront partagés au Cluster Protection de Bamako et contribueront à l’analyse du contexte protection dans les zones ciblées pour un plus large plaidoyer avec les autorités étatiques et les autres parties prenantes.

Le projet travaillera directement avec 11 comités locaux de protection communautaires, composés de 12 membres chacun (132 au total). Dans chaque localité cible, 2 points focaux Psychosocial (PSS) et 2 points focaux Protection de l'Enfance (PE) seront accompagnés et formés pour l'identification, la prise en charge et l'orientation des victimes de violations de droits, en collaboration avec les comités locaux. Ils organiseront également des séances de groupes pour renforcer la prise en charge communautaire et mieux identifier les besoins en suivi individuel avec les victimes de violations, les survivant(e)s VBG et les autres personnes en besoin. Les enseignants et personnels des écoles et des centres communautaires seront également formés en premiers secours psychologiques, PSS, et orientation des victimes. Enfin, 140 membres des groupements locaux et notamment les associations de femmes seront accompagnés à mener des activités renforçant l'environnement protecteur dans les localités de Douentza et Koro les plus affectées par les incidents de protection. 
Le projet atteindra au moins 3,000 membres des communautés ciblées (132 membres des comités, 44 points focaux, 55 personnels des écoles, 144 membres des groupements, 150 survivant(e)s VBG, 200 enfants victimes d'abus, au moins 2,000 personnes au sein des communautés).

project_name: MA - Accelerated clearance of priority minefields/cluster strikes preventing resettlement and expansion of communities in Central, Eastern Equatoria and Jonglei
project_objective:
EDITS:
(1) References to non-HRP teams/activities have been removed. 
(2) Target of 34 HAs surveyed and cleared (CL11/CO1, indicator 1.5) has been added. Explanation added to activities.
(3) MRE beneficiary sex and age disaggregated data added and total corrected: the revised grand total is: 7,734 including: men 938; women 964; boys 2814; girls 3552. This figure includes NGO staff. Further breakdown by activity with SADD added to activities.

PURPOSE:
To clear priority Minefields, cluster strikes and ERW to enable towns to expand to accommodate returnees building resilience by releasing land for agriculture  and housing 

TARGET:
The MTT will release 1,420,000m2 (142 Ha) of high priority minefields and cluster strikes and all spot tasks in Torit/Canal/Fangak. This should equate to 34 hazardous areas surveyed and cleared. 

MAG’s CL team will:
1. Build local capacity by training 206 NNGO staff (M:131, W:75) (MRE).
2. Provide MRE for 7,200 residents through community sessions. (M:600, W:768, B:2280, G:3552)
3. Train 175 Community Focal Points (W:105, M:70), empowering women decision makers to participate in   
    prioritisation of MRE & the collection of data to aid prioritisation for clearance tasking.
4. MRE for 328 INGO staff (W:121, M:207).

SUMMARY: 
MAG will deploy a multi-task team (MTT 1) to Torit, Eastern Equatoria, and Fangak/Canal, Jonglei to clear high-impact minefields and cluster munition strikes. The team will be supported by a MineWolf on minefields during the dry season and switch to cluster strikes with the support of a Bozena with a mulching head during the wet season. MAG is the only NGO using ground preparation MineWolf 370 and Bozena 3 machines in South Sudan. As such MAG delivers clearance faster and more cost effectively than manual teams. Increased clearance is needed to provide land for housing and agriculture as displaced people and refugees return to their villages. The ability to settle and farm increases the resilience of these communities and reduces reliance on other forms of aid. With access to mechanical assets to support clearance, MAG is in a position to begin to return large areas of contaminated land back to these communities in Tier 1 locations.

MAG community liaison team will support the MTT providing risk education to local communities and INGO staff. The team will also train Community Focal Points (CFPs) to provide risk education to their communities and aid prioritization of clearance tasking, as well as build the capacity of national NGOs to undertake mine risk education activities. The community liaison element of the project is expected to increase national ownership of risk education and improve the sustainability of life-saving messaging in vulnerable communities.

Inputs
MTT 1 is made up of 27 people: 1 Technical Field Manager; 2 mechanical operators; 13 deminers; 3 Community Liaison staff; 6 drivers; 2 medics and 2 cooks. Teams live in tents in communities, and remain highly mobile, moving between tasks as needed.  The team uses a MineWolf 370 in the dry season and a Bozena 3 fitted with a ‘mulching head’ on cluster strikes during the wet season that speeds the removal of vegetation to improve clearance efficiency.

The Bozena machines increase Cluster clearance outputs to 7 Ha (70,000m2), while the Minewolf clears 10 Ha (100,000m2) of minefield per month in the dry season. 

LOCATION:
Torit, Eastern Equatoria
Using HRP funding, MAG would move MTT1 & the MineWolf 370 in January 2019 to prioritised minefields in Torit. The MineWolf will support the team throughout the dry season. In the wet season the team will move to clear cluster strikes with the Bozena. 100% of spot tasks reported in Torit will be destroyed as part of the workplan.

Canal/Fangak, Jonglei
If agreed as a priority, in Sep 2019, MAG could send the MineWolf to Fangak and Canal, to resurvey & clear the minefields there. MTT1 would fly to Northern Jonglei as soon as the land is dry enough for operations.

project_name: Provision of  Integrated lifesaving Nutrition, Education, Protection and WASH Assistance to vulnerable Internally Displaced, Returnee and Resident boys, girls, women and men in Sudan
project_objective:
Under Sudan’s MYHS 2017-2019 and HRP 2019, UNICEF will endeavor to support the most vulnerable and marginalized particularly, women and children. 

UNICEF positions itself to work in the deprived communities with the highest level of vulnerability aiming to address the underlying immediate and long-term causes. Based on the comparative advantage of UNICEF’s programming and hands-on experience of 60 years in Sudan, it is evident that a meaningful impact and results only be attained by adopting inter-sectoral approaches given they are fully integrated. 

UNICEF aims to deliver an integrated package for children by adopting a “whole child” approach wherein, the UNICEF led sectors would work together by identifying the geographic convergence, improving programmatic complementary under a common result framework thus, realizing rights of the most vulnerable children in the areas of health, education, WASH and protection. 

This will allow UNICEF to enhance sustainability within the projects and build resilience of the affected population and thus, bridging the humanitarian and development. 

In the spirit of partnership and the new way of working, UNICEF submits an inter-sectoral proposal – a progressive step in the direction of achieving integration.

project_name: Ensuring girls and boys aged 3-18 years (40% girls) affected by conflict have equitable and inclusive access to quality learning opportunities in safe and protective environments in South Sudan (Front-line)
project_objective:
The project is planned to respond emergency education services of  IDP and host community children in 10 former States of South Sudan. The main goal of the project is to increase access to safe and protective learning environments for conflict affected children, adolescents/ youth. 
The project has two components; front-line and pipeline. Under Front-Line UNICEF will support 729,000 (Boys-419,175; Girls – 309,825) children to access education services in the 10 former states of South Sudan. This includes setting up temporary learning spaces (TLS), rehabilitation of WASH facilities. This component will further focus on training 5,500 teachers and 8,500 PTA/SMCs to improve school management and quality of education is South Sudan. 
UNICEF will strengthen the provision of child protection services to children in and out of school through school and community based initiatives. The involvement of adolescents and youth in community based activities to prevent and respond appropriately to GBV and create awareness within the community. GBV issues will be addressed in schools through the sensitization of teachers and by linking them to an established referral system. In addition, in collaboration with the MoGEI, a teachers’ Code of Conduct will be implemented to mitigate the risks of GBV and, more specifically, prevent sexual exploitation and abuse.

project_name: Emergency Health Intervention through Mobile Clinic and support to PHCCs/Us for urban IDPs and Host Community in Juba
project_objective:
The project aims to provide basic health services to the IDP population of the “informal” camps of Juba through a mobile clinic and a network of PHCCs/Us, also conducting screening on STD, Measles, Cholera, Meningitis, visual apparatus diseases. The project will support PHCCs/Us in collaboration with the MoH Jubek State through supply of drugs, consumables and micronutrients with a particular focus on Malaria prevention and treatment and on pharmacological management of cases of epilepsy.
In the framework of the project there is the direct management of 1 PHCC and 2 PHCUs in town (which are the main health referral structures for the Urban IDP Camps), the support to other 2 governmental PHCCs through capacity building of the staff and drugs and supplies delivery, the management of ante natal and post natal care units in two dispensaries. Particular attention is put on prevention of diseases in new born children leading to disabilities.
A support to the Health County Department in the large scale vaccination campaign is also included, as well as hygiene promotion through events and distribution of soap and chlorine.
A specific activity regards nutritional support, in the direct managed PHCC, for children with MAM and referral of SAM cases, as well as support to PLW through the distribution of vitaminized milk.

All the activities are carried on with a particular attention on gender, focusing on the role of women at different levels. Furthermore an important component of the action is the attention on disability, particularly to children with disabilities, ensuring access to health services and rehabilitation, directly dealing with particular cases such as epilepsy, cleft lip and palate, spina bifida, hydrocele, osteomyelitis, cerebral palsy.

project_name: Provision of Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) among children under 5 and PLW at PHCU level and through outreach activities integrating health and nutrition services, in Aweil North, Northern Bahr el Ghazal.
project_objective:
PUI has been implementing projects in South Sudan, in Aweil North since April 2015, through an integrated approach, combining Health, Nutrition, FSL and basic WASH interventions. In 2018, PUI has provided Community Management of Acute Malnutrition services in 15 nutrition sites, in Aweil North – including two in the disputed 14-mile are a – with funding from WFP, UNICEF, GIZ and ECHO. With the expansion of its programs since 2015, PUI has reached more beneficiaries and ensures early identification of malnutrition through outreach activities. The ratio SAM:MAM has indeed changed, with a fewer SAM cases. In 2016, the percentage of new SAM cases was 50%, while in 2018 the percentage of SAM cases decreased to 34%. Moreover, the number of children admitted in the stabilization Center has dropped dramatically. In 2016, the average number of admissions in the Stabilization Center was 26 per month, even reaching 39 admissions per month in the peak of the lean season. In 2018, the average number of admissions is 12 per month, with no peak in the lean season. The lower number of admissions in the Stabilization Center and the lower percentage of children with SAM in OTP can be associated with an increased access to OTP and TSFP and early identification of malnutrition through outreach activities. According to the latest reports, there are 5,576 SAM children, 17,004 MAM children and 23,813 MAM PLW in Aweil North expected in 2019. 

Although Aweil North -and Northern Bahr el Ghazal in general- is a stable area, malnutrition remains a major public health issue, which requires continuing activities there. In 2018, PUI aims to implement a complete CMAM program, targeting and treating children under 5 years old and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) for Severe and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (SAM and MAM respectively), through OTP, TSFP and BSFP services – the latter in all of Aweil North while the two others will be in PUI’s 15 nutrition sites. Vulnerable populations will be screened (active and passive screenings) for malnutrition by PUI’s staff, including the Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) who will be trained to screen, trace, refer and sensitize community members. Children under 5, will also be screened and treated for malaria. In the meantime, CNVs, Nutrition Health Workers and members of the Mother to Mother Support Groups will be trained to disseminate individual key messages for mothers and caretakers on Maternal, Infant and Young Child Feeding (MIYCN). To complete these activities, PUI hopes to start Conditional General Food Distribution in PUI’s catchment area for its FSL activities and foster community’s participation and engagement, to lower dependence on the nutrition program and encourage resilience and communities’ future self-reliance. With the same goal in mind, PUI will also establish Project Monitoring Committees and train community members on project monitoring. Finally, to counteract the paucity of reliable secondary health and nutrition data in several parts of South Sudan, PUI plans to conduct SMART surveys, in coordination with the Nutrition Information Working Group. In line with the cluster’s strategic objective for the HRP 2019, PUI wishes “to enhance the nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and nutrition information” and thus contribute to the generation of consistent and reliable public health data. 

The purpose of the project is thus to provide quality Community Management of Acute Malnutrition and prevent as much as possible malnutrition through health promotion and early identification of populations at risk. PUI will foster community participation and will aim to reinforce the community’s engagement and ownership of the services, to ensure a healthy lifestyle and productive community. 

The services will target:
Children under 5:  22,470 (11,460 Females; 11,010 Males)
Pregnant and lactating women: 9,421
Total: 31,891

project_name: Appui au renforcement de la résilience des moyens d'existence des ménages agricoles et des éleveurs affectés  par les changements climatiques dans la bande sahélienne du Tchad
project_objective:
L’opération de ce projet consistera à cibler et appuyer les groupes des personnes surtout les groupes des femmes dans les provinces situées dans la bande sahélienne, notamment le Batha, le Guéra, Le Bahr El Gazal, et le Hadjar Lamis dont certains ont déjà commencé à s’organiser et réaliser des activités de production agricole ou des activités génératrices des revenus, l’éducation nutritionnelle dans les cadres des projets précédents. Les principales activités sont celles relatives à la production agricole, l’élevage des petits ruminants et les petits commerces des produits alimentaires. Les femmes seront mises en avant dans tout le processus.
En effet, les populations directement affectées par les épisodes de changement climatique, notamment les mauvaises répartitions des pluies des campagnes agropastorales 2016/2017 et 2017/2018, se situant majoritairement dans les provinces susmentionnées de la bande sahélienne, nécessitent un appui conséquent. Les aléas climatiques affectent principalement les moyens d'existences des agriculteurs et des éleveurs. Ces populations ont subi des dommages importants, certains ont perdu une partie voire la totalité de leurs sources de revenus. Les femmes sont particulièrement affectées. Ces dernières qui représentent 40% de la population active du Tchad, sont pour la plupart de petites productrices, main d’œuvre pour les récoltes et/ou commerçantes de denrées agricoles, ce qui les rend de fait particulièrement vulnérables en cas de choc lié à la mauvaise production. Cette situation va avoir des effets collatéraux sur la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle aussi bien pour la population humaine qu'animale. Ainsi, un appui aux ménages pour renforcer leur capacité de résilience afin de faire face à ces chocs est souhaité.
En matière de protection transversale, toutes les actions seront axées sur les quatre éléments clés dans la mise en œuvre de ce présent projet. Surtout dans sa politique relative à la redevabilité, la FAO mettra en facteur les équipes de plaintes qui pourront remonter toutes les actions susceptibles de nuire à la bonne la dignité des bénéficiaires à travers cette opération. Dans le cadre de ce projet, plus de la moitié des bénéficiaires seront choisis par les femmes chefs de ménages vulnérables, les ménages ayant des enfants et des vieilles personnes. Ceci permettra de mieux protéger toutes ces couches qui sont souvent très vulnérables par rapport aux chocs et aux catastrophes.

project_name: Population has optimal access to education and other learning opportunities
project_objective:
Over the past year the education sector supported over 160,552 refugee children to access education. A total of 35% (55,744) of children are enrolled in the Learning Competency Framework and Approach (LCFA) Level I (children aged 3-5 years), and 64% (102,753) in Level II (6-14 years). Furthermore, the sector developed intermediary materials for Level I and Level II, recruited over 3,208 teachers, provided foundation teaching and learning as well as constructed 2,077 learning spaces. As part of the overall response, UNHCR and partners directly guaranteed access to over 40,820 learners (20,745 girls and 20,075 boys). The interventions included the construction of 344 learning spaces in 16  camps, recruitment, training, and deployment of 842 (424 male and 418 female) teachers. Development, production and distribution of teaching and learning materials as well as mobilizing and working with over 673 School Management Committee Members to facilitate and ensure community engagement and involvement in education services delivery. Furthermore, UNHCR supported Disaster Risk Management (DRR) activities in schools by training teachers, forming school-based DRR committees, and disseminating critical messages among parents, teachers, and students. Additionally, in collaboration with partners UNHCR established six Community Technology Access (CTA) centers in six different high schools, college and social institution targeting 3,660 host community children and youth.  
It is noteworthy that in Bangladesh since the 1990s, UNHCR and partners made significant progress in advocating for the use of the national curriculum which has been taught in schools in the registered camps since 2007 and access was extended to secondary levels in recent years, with classes up to grade 8 by 2016. Certification was however still not provided, and children do not sit for exams. Nonetheless, the system provides structured teaching and learning using materials vetted and approved by the National Curriculum and Text Book Board (NCTB) with predictable progression essential for academic stimulation.
As part of JRP 2019, UNHCR will expand its education interventions in collaboration with partners in 2019. Through the sector UNHCR seeks to strengthen and expand equitable quality lifelong learning opportunities aligned with the education sector standards, Ministry of Primary and Mass Education (MoPME) as well as Ministry of Education (MoE) standards. Moreover, UNHCR will seek to expand its intervention through the maintenance of 464 existing education facilities (344 classrooms and 120 home based learning center), constructing 242 classrooms with adequate Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) facilities, establish 418 home base learning facilities, recruit 958 teachers and facilitators, train 1800 teachers and establish 280 community education committees. Further effort shall take a series of project targeted at adolescents and youth through Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC), engaging peer and volunteer in youth clubs in non-formal education programming and addressing lack of skills training opportunities. Emphasis will be given to enhance school community governance and participation mechanisms, including risk reduction activities; integrate school community-based participatory planning and community awareness. Additionally, host community children also will be benefited through classrooms renovation in host community schools and continuing Community Technology Access (CTA) services.

project_name: Emergency and Relief Intervention - Nutrition Activities in South Sudan by Medair
project_objective:
Medair has worked in South Sudan since 1992. Currently its operations consist of the static projects in Renk (former Upper Nile State), Aweil Centre (former Northern Bahr el Ghazal State) and Leer and Mayendit (former Unity State) with the main objective of decreasing preventable morbidity and mortality due to acute malnutrition by treating children and PLWs with GAM and underlying illnesses, building local nutritional treatment and prevention capacity, and increasing preventative infant and young child feeding practices. In all the sites, Medair’s main activity will be implementing the management of acute malnutrition, according to the national CMAM guidelines, targeting the vulnerable 5 and pregnant and lactating women. This will include facility and community level promotion of IYCF-E in line with national MIYCN guidelines as well as training, capacity building and regular supportive supervision at supported Medair sites.  In total, the target for 2019 will be of 6,602 SAM new admissions, 17,374 MAM new admissions and 9,529 PLWs.

In Renk, Medair remains the only long-term nutrition partner and one of the only health actors to respond to the nutritional emergency. In May 2018, Medair conducted a SMART survey in Renk County that revealed GAM and SAM rates above the emergency threshold, with the critical level of 22.8% and 6.0% among IDPs and 26.9% and 6.4% among the host community, respectively. 

Medair performed a SMART survey in Leer County in April 2018 showing a GAM rate of 12.2% (SAM 3.0%). Soon after the completion of the survey, violence erupted in southern Unity resulting in displacement of the population and interruption of the services. A mass MUAC screening in July 2018 (during the OCV mass vaccination campaign) revealed a ‘proxy GAM’ of 19%, corresponding to very critical levels of acute malnutrition (IPC 5 for Acute Malnutrition). The subsequent FSNMS round 23 (done in early August 2018) showed a GAM (by WFH) of 13.7% (however, it has to be noted that the exercise captured children from 0-59 months and not the classic category of 6-59 months as in the standard SMART survey)

In Aweil Centre, the results from the SMART survey of July 2018 revealed the prevalence of a GAM rate of 6.3% (including a SAM prevalence of 1.3%), which is much lower than the GAM rate of 23.3% measured by the SMART survey of July 2017. 

The IPC classification of September 2018 indicates that Aweil Centre is IPC 3 (Serious) and would likely deteriorate at least one IPC Phase without continued humanitarian assistance. 

In all of these project sites, Medair will ensure the  minimum WASH package of safe water and latrine access, including waste management is present and functional. Systematic malaria RDT is conducted on admission for SAM children, and treatment of malnourished children suffering from malaria will be implemented. Moreover, treatment of co-existing illness and measles vaccination will be ensured. Where possible, linkage with FSL partner will be encouraged, while child friendly spaces and early child development activities will be fostered in order to allow the full neuro-cognitive development of the child and promote the importance of mother-child relationship.


The Emergency Response Team (ERT) responds to nutrition emergencies in South Sudan.
About 64% of the 33 SMART surveys conducted between January and August 2018, reported critical nutrition situations with GAM prevalence of 15% and above - the WHO emergency threshold. Moreover, according to the Nutrition Information Working Group (NIWG) of South Sudan, about 76% of the 21 repeated SMART surveys conducted in same period and in the same locations in 2017 and 2018 confirmed the critical levels of acute malnutrition.

The 2018 FSNMS SMART survey results (Round 23 performed in August 2018) depicted a concerning nutrition situation in most parts of the country: about 61% of the 46 counties reported serious or critical levels of acute malnutrition.
