project_name: Increased access to physical rehabilitation and psychosocial support services for conflict affected vulnerable communities in Iraq
project_objective:
The specific objective of the project is to improve access to specific services for the most vulnerable people in Ninewa, Kirkuk, Anbar, Diyala and Baghdad Governorates.

In direct relation with the priority needs identified, the project will provide both an immediate and long term response. This will be delivered through a package that focuses on the availability, accessibility and quality of health care services through direct service provision and capacity building with a view of addressing the short term and long term needs for Iraq. The project will target IDPs, returnees and host communities identified as being vulnerable within this context including persons with disabilities, children, and youth.

Specifically, Handicap International (HI) plans to:
	address the lack of availability of health services through the provision of physical and functional rehabilitation services for IDPs, Returnees and host communities combined with PSS services for the respective patients and their relatives. 
	address the lack of accessibility to health services through promoting existing services to mitigate the barriers of non-information; support the local health services to be able to address the specific needs of vulnerable populations; provide cash assistance for high cost of transport for IDPs, returnees and host communities; support existing health structures in the accessibility for people with a physical impairment to their services.
	work to Improve the quality of existing functional and physical rehabilitation services for IDPs, returnees and host communities with a focus on training of staff in health centers;

The modalities for the intervention will depend on the nature of the activity and the level of access (including security considerations). Furthermore the intervention will follow a comprehensive approach as it will benefit from other HI interventions to ensure multiple yet integrated activities (including risk education, MHPSS, physical rehabilitation, and inclusive access to service) in order to maximize the intervention for beneficiaries. Finally, inclusion mainstreaming will be applied throughout the intervention with a specific focus on Gender, Age and Disability.

project_name: Provision of quality lifesaving emergency CMAM and MIYCN services to children under five and PLW among conflict affected communities (IDPs and host communities) in the republic of  South Sudan
project_objective:
WHO in its 2018 country cooperative strategy stated that South Sudan has some of the worst health outcome indicators globally: maternal mortality ratio stands at 789 per 100,000 live births, whereas neonatal and under-five mortality rates are 39.3 and 99.2, per 1000 live births respectively (2014). The immunization coverage in South Sudan is also low and outbreak such as measles are common. Access to clean drinking water is very limited and open defection is a common practice. Household and community hygiene and sanitation levels are extremely poor throughout the country. All these are drivers that increase cases of acute malnutrition in children under five and PLWs. 
The Greater Equatorial region has been severely affected by insecurity and the economic crisis, which have disrupted agriculture-based livelihoods –and for a traditionally surplus-producing area, this has been hard-hitting. Farmers were not able to safely access their fields to plant, fishers unable to venture out to fishing grounds and traders limited by hyperinflation, lack of hard currency, insecurity and access. More than 1 million people from Greater Equatorial have fled to Uganda, citing insecurity and hunger as the main reasons for fleeing. Displacement has left many farmers without access to the tools and inputs needed to restart their livelihood activities when they return to their lands or settle with host communities.
 Greater Bahr el-Ghazal, a region traditionally dependent on markets, has been heavily impacted by disrupted trade routes and diminished purchasing power of the local currency. As a result of these factors, as well as inter-communal conflict, massive displacement and climate extremes that have affected production, the region faces record levels of food insecurity, with the largest number of food insecure people. In the Greater Upper Nile, recurrent fighting has caused massive displacement, impacting livelihoods and disrupting humanitarian access. The conflict has also affected livestock migratory routes, resulting in an increase of livestock disease incidents and compounded by weakened capacity to respond. This situation has also affected the nutrition situation of family, household, especially children and women. 


The overall situation of acute malnutrition has slightly improved this year compared to the same period last year with no counties reporting extreme critical levels (GAM above 30%) of acute of malnutrition in 2018. But the level of acute malnutrition is still high and this can be attributed to severe food insecurity, poor access to health and nutrition services, high morbidity, extremely poor diets and poor sanitation and hygiene. Levels of acute malnutrition are expected to improve marginally between October and December 2018 due to the seasonal availability of local production, increased availability of fish and milk, and relatively better access to markets and key services. However, levels of acute malnutrition are expected to deteriorate in the first quarter of 2019 with an early onset of the lean season as most households are expected to deplete food stocks from their own production. In 2018, World Vision South Sudan conducted a SMART survey. The findings showed a Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM)  rate in Gogrial East County of 18.0% (14.0-22.8 95% CI), while severe and acute malnutrition (SAM) prevalence was found to be 2.8% (1.7- 4.7 95% CI). In Tonj North, the GAM rate for the County was 11.6% (9.0 – 14.9 95% C.I.), and the severe acute malnutrition (SAM) rate was 3.1% (1.8 – 5.3 95% C.I.).). In this assessment, no cases of edema were observed. The findings indicate a serious level (GAM 10.0-14.9%) phase of malnutrition according to WHO classification. Although there is a decrease in GAM and SAM rates compared to July 2017 results {14.7% (95%CI: 12.5-17.3), July 2017}, the deterioration is not statistically significant, and the levels indicate a sustained serious nutrition situation compared to July 2017. There was no SMART data for certain counties in 2018 due lack of funding. It is important to note that in 2017 the GAM rate in Upper Nile, Western Equatorial and Juba were respectively as follows: Juba (14.6%), 5.1% (Ezo, Nagero, Nzara, Yambio, Tambura), 21.8% ( Fashoda, Manyo, Panykang, Melut and Baliet), 22% ( Gogrial East), 22.8% ( Gorgrial West),  14.7% (Tonj North), and 35.9% ( Twic county).  Western Equatorial has experienced armed conflict this year, since May which has led to increase internal displacement.  In 2019, WVSS intends to continue providing emergency nutrition interventions in Upper Nile, Warrap, Western Equatorial, and Central Equatorial states. WVSS will be targeting 1,938 SAM children and 4,776 MAM children.

project_name: Prevention of malnutrition and reducing morbidity through addressing chronic and acute Water, Hygiene and Sanitation needs of vulnerable and affected populations of Lakes and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective:
This project will aim at increasing timely and equitable access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services to 73,400 (women, men, girls, and boys) emergency-affected populations in Eastern Lakes State and the Eastern Equatoria States. HELP-eV has been responding to the ongoing humanitarian crisis since the onset of the conflict in the country both in conflicted-affected states and noncrisis states. The project objectives are; 
-	Ensure provision to affected populations with safe, equitable, and sustainable access to sufficient quantity of water for drinking, cooking, and personal and domestic hygiene (15 L/p/day). 
-	Ensure that the targeted populations have access to safe, sanitary, and hygienic living environment through the provision of sanitation services that are secure, sanitary, user-friendly and gender-appropriate. 
-	Ensure that affected populations have reduced risk of WASH¬ related diseases, or negative impacts on nutritional status, through access to improved hygienic practices, hygiene promotion and delivery of hygiene products and services on a sustainable and equitable basis. 
HELP-eV will support WASH Cluster response in locations of critical malnutrition in Eastern Lakes and the Eastern Equatoria States by ensuring the provision of a minimum standard of improved basic WASH services in the areas. The activities include; comprehensive rehabilitation of hand pumps, distribution of WASH NFIs, Improving latrines, and hygiene promotion campaigns both at institutional and community levels HELP-eV will ensure that WASH services, specifically in regards to latrine construction, incorporate the minimum safety and privacy considerations with use of the WASH Cluster Latrine Checklist, developed with the GBV Sub¬Cluster. HELP-eV will work with WASH Cluster and NFI/ES, Logs and other clusters to ensure adequate supplies are strategically pre¬positioned in the field to respond to new displacement and potential disease outbreaks through the 2019 rainy season. HELP-eV will maintain its active participation in the WASH Cluster meetings both at the state and National levels where ideas and project updates are shared, and monthly WASH reports are submitted. HELP-eV will encourage the active participation of the local community including women and children in the implementation of the proposed project. Through Consultation of local authorities at all levels, women, men, boys, and girls in the selection of the project areas within the States based on the identified needs. Hygiene promoters including hand pump technicians will include both host community, returnees and IDPs men, women, boys and girls in the targeted project sites in the county. The local authorities, host community, and IDPs men, women, girls and boys will be involved in the design of the community and institutional sanitation facilities putting into consideration the need for privacy for females for the case of latrines and bathrooms construction. This project is expected to complement current Help-eV WASH activities in the locations and will integrate with our Nutrition and FSL activities.

project_name: Peru - International Organization for Migration
Emergency food assistance and small-scale food security support to vulnerable households in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims at improving the food security of vulnerable Syrian households, in both the short and the medium-long term. 

In the short-term, ACTED will reduce the food security of conflict-affected communities through the provision of rapid and flexible food assistance. This will include the following 3 modalities:  1) RTERS for vulnerable beneficiaries who do not have access to cooking facilities; 2) Food rations for households living in areas where markets are inaccessible or food is unavailable; 3) Food vouchers for families with access to functioning markets.

In the medium and long-term, ACTED food security assistance will be underpinned by the rationale of giving vulnerable households the resources and skills to obtain a self-sufficient food production. In order to achieve this, ACTED will provide targeted support to households, depending on their needs and size of land. The type of support ACTED will provide to vulnerable households will include: 1) kitchen garden kits and training; 2) polytunnel kits and training; 3) poultry kits. Overall, this project will benefit approximately 72,900 individuals. 

ACTED is coordinating with Food Security cluster members and other NGOs supporting the food security and agricultural sector to ensure that there is no duplication of assistance planned in 2019. 

While implementing its food security programming, ACTED always respects the nutrition standards of the Food Security cluster. Additionally, while targeting different locations for its programming under Food Security, ACTED also ensures that its interventions are complementary to projects under other sectors to comprehensively respond to needs in the target area. Indeed, for instance, in emergency context and whenever relevant ACTED will complement emergency food distribution with NFI distribution. In turn, ACTED often implements agricultural early-recovery activities such as the rehabilitation of agricultural assets or irrigation canals used for agricultural purposes to support further the agricultural production and availability of food products on the market.

The activities and targets proposed for this intervention reflect the current activities and targets for which ACTED has secured funding for 2019.

project_name: Brazil - International Organization for Migration
Brazil - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women
Early recovery support to conflict-affected communities in Northwest Syria
project_objective: The proposed project aims at restoring rural and urban livelihoods for conflict-affected communities in Idleb governorate, Northwest Syria. This will be achieved through a combination of different interventions at the individual and community-level. In rural areas, at the individual level, crop farmers will be provided with a voucher to redeem seeds, fertilizers and tools and training on climate-smart agriculture and best practices, while breeders’ farmers will be provided with vouchers to redeem fodder for their livestock. ACTED will provide as well cash grants and training to small and medium size agricultural entrepreneurs to enable them to start their own business. At the community level, ACTED will rehabilitate communal productive assets, including bakeries, mills, silos, but also rehabilitate and perform canal drainage and cleaning. These interventions will benefit both farmers (who will have increased access to water for irrigation through canal rehabilitation) and also communities (who will be able to access good quality bread through bakeries rehabilitation, for instance). In urban areas, instead, ACTED will support existing and new small-scale businesses with cash grants and training, enabling them to restore and expand their business. Finally, ACTED will provide vocational and educational training classes to men and women through an Educational Vocational Training Centre (TVET), in order to provide them with a wide range of skills to increase their employability. This project is estimated to benefit 6,420 individuals.

project_name: Provision of emergency child protection, child and youth centered resilience building in conflict affected States of Jonglei and Western Bahr El Ghazal.
project_objective:
The project provides support to the most vulnerable, conflict-affected girls, boys and women in South Sudan who are exposed to child protection risks in targeted areas of Raga, Wau, Uror, and Pochalla counties of Western Barl El Ghazal State and Jonglei State respectively. 

To address the needs the project will provide frontline services to most affected populations through; the provision of comprehensive case management, provision of family tracing and reunification, provision of psychosocial support services (PSS), conduct child protection assessments and monitoring using the existing and recommended tools (monitoring of grave child rights violations through the monitoring and reporting mechanism (MRM)), establishing and supporting of referral mechanisms, conduct Mine Risk Education (MRE), conduct awareness-raising & prevention messaging and Peacebuilding and peaceful coexistence activities.

To avoid overlapping and duplication of activities in the targeted locations Hold the Child will work closely with other child protection partners in mapping the areas with the close supervision and support from the Child Protection Sub-Cluster at the National level and the Child Protection Working Groups at the State level. As this will enable Hold the Child and other Child partners to have specific areas of interventions as agreed.

project_name: GBV – Prevention and response to sexual and gender based violence in conflict and displacement affected locations in South Sudan.
project_objective:
In line with the Humanitarian Needs Overview for 2019, and the planning for the Humanitarian Response Plan for 2019, DRC plans to implement Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) prevention and response activities in hard-to-reach conflict areas in South Sudan, through static and mobile responses. DRC strives to contribute to the two Protection cluster strategic objectives: 
-	Provide immediate lifesaving assistance to address priority protection needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach areas
-	Prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience
DRC will provide SGBV response activities for identified cases, including case management and psychosocial support (PSS). The SGBV response element will follow a survivor-centered approach, following the Inter Agency Standing Committee (IASC) GBV guidelines, and ensuring DRC staff are well trained and qualified to handle sensitive and confidential cases. The prevention activities will focus on promoting community engagement and ownership in addressing sexual and gender-based violence, while ensuring communities are aware of GBV services available. Awareness raising sessions, community activists’ trainings, mass awareness campaigns and information campaigns will be organised to ensure GBV messaging is consistent and effective, as well as community-led. DRC uses the SASA! methodology, developed by Raising Voices, which aims to address one of the root causes of GBV and HIV, the power imbalance between men and women, through community mobilisation and activism. DRC will also engage in advocacy with the GBV sub-cluster at the state-levels, and with the relevant authorities, such as the minister of gender, to ensure buy-in and support from the main and relevant stakeholders. These activities will be linked with the food security and livelihood activities, which will focus on women empowerment and resilience, while engaging with men on improving gender equality.

DRC has static presence in Unity State, operating from Bentiu, and in Upper Nile, operating both in Maban and in Malakal, Aburoc and several locations on the West bank of the Nile. In addition, DRC operates three mobile protection teams, which conduct integrated protection analyses, identifying SGBV risks and issues in hard-to-reach areas and among populations affected by conflict and displacement (targeted locations identfiied by GBV sub-cluster). In Upper Nile and Unity States, the GBV program will focus on increasing access to services for survivors and setting up safe spaces for women, where they can discuss their concerns, and alleviate stress and trauma through PSS activities. In all target locations, beneficiaries engaging in awareness raising and activism will be selected based on their motivation to support to behavioral change in the power relations between men and women, while survivors will not be sought out but supported based on need and referrals. Through the intervention, DRC intends to ensure women and men are equally sensitised on the issues concerning gender based violence and gender inequality, while providing life-saving assistance to survivors, encouraging help-seeking behavior, and support to vulnerable men and women. Overall, DRC aim to reach approximately 96,500 vulnerable conflict and displacement-affected individuals from host communities, IDPs and refugee communities in South Sudan.

project_name: Mine Action Intervention in Ninewa and Anbar
project_objective:
Civilians in the accessible liberated areas in Ninewa and Anbar are faced with a difficult humanitarian situation. Large-scale destruction, explosive device contamination, and lack of basic services, all poses a threat to the population. Most of the liberated areas are contaminated with explosive ordnances, including unexploded ordnance, as a result of the conflict. In addition, IEDs are intentionally placed by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) in and around schools, health centres, public- and residential buildings, as well as along main routes and roads. 
NPA’s mine action intervention in areas contaminated with improvised landmines and IEDs comprises of survey, clearance, and risk education activities with special competence in working in areas contaminated by improvised landmines and IEDs. NTS activities are aimed at collecting and processing information on areas contaminated with improvised landmines and IEDs, and threat impact assessment among highly at-risk populations. NPA provides risk education integrated with NTS, aiming to reduce the vulnerabilities of highly at-risk groups of girls, boys, women and men. Technical survey and mine clearance of highly prioritised areas contaminated by improvised landmines and booby-traps, will improve community safety, allow livelihoods to be built again, homes to be renovated and following detailed surveys of the task areas coupled with strong community liaison, it will give the returning population the confidence to use the cleared land and transit safe access routes. For technical survey and clearance operations, NPA will primarily deploy manual clearance and technical survey teams with special competence in working in areas contaminated by improvised landmines. NPA's manual teams will be supported by a mechanical team that will increase safety and efficiency of operations through safe disruption of improvised mines and booby-traps, creating rapid access to suspect areas, assisting in rubble removal in high priority house/compound clearance tasks, and verification of suspected hazardous areas.
Long Term Objective: To facilitate the safe return of refugees and IDPs and enable the local population to safely resume normal activities, free from the threat of mines, cluster munitions, and other explosive weapons, and significantly contribute to Iraq government in fulfillment its obligations as state-party to the MBT and CCM.
The immediate Project objective 1: Survey and clear priority hazardous areas (in NPA’s area of operations), releasing land of improvised landmines and explosive devices, allowing access and return.
The immediate Project objective 2: Reduced vulnerability of the population living in the affected communities by improving their knowledge and promoting safe behavior in explosive contaminated areas.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts
project_objective:
HALO will conduct risk education, survey and clearance operations in eastern Ukraine, to respond to the needs of mine-affected communities across Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, focusing on high-priority areas within the 15km buffer-zone from the line of contact. HALO will also provide training and capacity building sessions for the key mine action stakeholders including the newly established mine action authorities in order to contribute to an effective and efficient mine action sector. Risk education sessions are a preventive measure that will inform on the threat related to mines and other explosive items and decrease the probability of accidents. Survey work will establish the extent and nature of mine contamination in the region, while clearance will permanently remove these threats, improving the physical safety and livelihoods opportunities of those affected. HALO aims to clear two million square metres of land contaminated with explosive hazards during 2019.

HALO began landmine clearance in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts in April 2016, and is the largest humanitarian demining organisation working in the region. Since the start of operations, HALO has cleared over 3 million square meters of land, with 81,389 people benefitting so far from completed or ongoing tasks. Current capacity comprises 360 staff in 22 clearance teams, 1 mechanical clearance team, 2 technical survey teams and 3 non-technical survey teams. 
In 2019, HALO aims to continue risk education, survey and clearance operations in government controlled areas of eastern Ukraine including along the contact line, and is investigating the possibility of starting work in non-government controlled territory.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Food Security and CASH Based Intervention in South Kordofan and Blue Nile States, Sudan
project_objective:
VSFG intends to improve access to food security and nutritional status of conflict affected communities, IDPS and returnees in newly accessible areas of Blue Nile and South Kordofan States - in total 122,500 people - through: 
-Provision of agricultural support in the form of assorted vegetable and pulses seeds and extension training on good agricultural practices. 
-Establishment and rehabilitation of slaughter slabs, provision of inputs and training.
-Voucher-based treatment program: VSF Germany will use voucher based animal health service delivery system as a strategy to create access to veterinary services for 3,000 vulnerable HH in the project area - a subset of the above mentioned 20,000 HH. This modality is chosen to address targeting vulnerable HHs through distribution of voucher only for selected benefiting HHs, it also involves livestock owners and gives them a choice in the treatment of their animals, this modality is also used as a strong monitoring mechanism to trance the number of animals treated and activity of CAHWs. Targeted vulnerable families will be selected by an emergency animal health intervention committee made up of community leaders/representatives, local authorities and beneficiary community. The selected HHs will then be given vouchers worth up to 8 USD per household in order to contract the services of their respective CAHWs and to pay for the services obtained if any of their animals falls sick from common livestock diseases and also to receive treatment with de-wormers and acaricides to strengthen the health of their core stock. The livestock owner has a choice according to his/her needs and this guarantees the owner makes a choice and no CAHW can decide on his own what drugs will be given to the farmer, and no influential person can divert the use of veterinary drugs for his benefit. The voucher guarantees that the family identified as a beneficiary has the purchasing power with the voucher. And the CAHW needs the voucher to account for the received drugs 
- Provision and capacity building on fuel efficient stoves (FES) and Safe Access to Firewood and Alternative Energy (SAFE)
- Protecting key livestock assets which contribute to the food security and income generation of households through provision of veterinary services, restocking and supplementary animal feed.
-Breeding goats Restocking programs: This activity will be undertaken to support targeted beneficiaries to rebuild their assets and contribute to the food security of targeted HHs. In this project a total of 1,200 dairy goats will be procured from the local market through contracting existing community based income generation groups, then they will be distributed to 300 households in the four intervention localities. Beneficiaries will be targeted with particular emphasis on female-headed household, household with malnourished children and households who have lost their livestock.
- Increasing household income through supporting women groups in food processing (fish processing, cheese making and ago-food preservation, techniques etc.) and cash transfer programing in order to cover immediate needs such as food and other basic services.
-Cash transfer modality is chosen to assist extremely vulnerable HHs to access their basic needs including food and other commodities and services. This modality is flexible, it also empowers beneficiaries to make their own choices, preferences and to prioritize.Unconditional multipurpose cash transfer to vulnerable HHs to enable them to procure particularly food items while giving them choice and flexibility to spend some of the cash on NFIs, health or education; depending on their more pressing needs. Only heads of selected vulnerable households will be registered in beneficiaries’ registry indicating name, village and contact of beneficiary. There are a key criteria for targeting unconditional cash transfer beneficiaries. Markets are assessed and the amount of transfer determined accordingly.

project_name: Emergency Food and Livelihood support to the most vulnerable, men, women, boys and girls affected by protracted conflict, economic, seasonal and climatic shocks, in the former states of Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria, Warrap, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Upper Nile and Unity states in South Sudan.
project_objective:
This project aims to provide emergency food and livelihood support to close to 210,000 vulnerable households (1,260,000 individuals) in Western and Central Equatoria, Warrap, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Upper Nile, and Unity states of South Sudan. The project will adopt a mixed intervention approaches including but not limited to Cash transfers, Livestock support, distribution of farm inputs, knowledge transfer, and cash programming among others. 
The project will be implemented in synergy with other sectors within World Vision such as Nutrition, NFI, WASH, Health, and Protection. Needs identified by this project will be referred to the relevant sector for action and support.

project_name: GBV: Emergency GBV Prevention, Mitigation & Response in Conflict Affected & High Risk Areas
project_objective:
This project seeks to provide life-saving GBV prevention, mitigation and response in alignment with the HRP Strategic Objectives 2 & 3, Protection Cluster Strategic Objectives 1 & 2, and the priority actions identified by the GBV Sub Cluster. 
The project prioritized Tier 1 locations Yambio and Nasir/Luakpiny, as well as Tier 3 locations Tonj East, Twic, Tambura, Ezo, Nagero, Ibba (prioritizing Tier 1 locations but recognizing the absence of resourced GBV response services in Tier 3 locations for 2019 and World Vision’s operational presence with capacity to respond in the emergence as a hotspot). 
The project will target a total of 675,000 individuals (W: 227,500; G: 227,500(Adolescent: 150,000); M: 110,000; B: 110,000 (Adolescent: 90,000)), recognizing a specific emphasis on strengthening life-saving assistance meeting the unique and unmet needs of child survivors, specifically adolescent girls, and engaging male/female youth and adolescents in GBV prevention.
The project will include the following key interventions in all locations, based on specific assessed need, disaggregated by sex and age: GBV case management; provision of PSS; safe referrals (medial, legal, livelihood, other); provision of legal advice to survivors; GBV information management; engagement of and advocacy to police and justice actors (formal and traditional) to strengthen access to justice; monitoring of GBV risks for prevention/mitigation through safety audit & safety perception mapping; community engagement interventions to prevent and respond to GBV such as establishment of Women & Girl Safe Spaces & comprehensive programming per the WGSS South Sudan Guidelines; establishment/strengthening of community based protection/GBV structures and systems including women’s groups; community based advocacy and awareness raising, especially engaging male/female youth as change agents in adoption of positive masculinities, respect for women and girls’ equal rights, ending of social acceptance of violence (especially sexual/physical violence) and positive attitudes/behaviours that promote the end of GBV. 
The project reflects the feedback of beneficiary consultations and includes accountability mechanisms, and considers the unique needs and adapts its design based on gender and age considerations/vulnerabilities (Code 4). The project approach seeks to place communities at the centre of interventions and contribute to localization through capacity building in all community-based initiatives (i.e. strengthening community protection committees in monitoring, reporting, referral). The project design prioritizes a Do No Harm approach with an explicit intention to address protection issues experienced by women, girls, boys and men, specifically GBV, recognizing that respect for human rights and increasing gender equality are enablers of the South Sudan humanitarian response strategy.

project_name: Provision of life-saving and sustainable Shelter and Non Food Items to vulnerable people in South Sudan.
project_objective: World Vision proposes an Emergency Shelter and Non Food Items (ES/NFI) intervention that seeks to respond to the needs of 40,000 very vulnerable newly internally displaced persons as a result of armed conflicts and the expected returnees in various locations. The primary objective of the response is to protect and save lives of the internally displaced persons and returnees. The project will seek to help these vulnerable individuals with coping mechanisms that are combination of in-kind distribution, cash transfers and the use of locally available resources to better their lives. Where possible, the use of locally available materials will be encouraged as these materials are considered to be more sustainable than the in kind distribution, they will be done alongside the cash interventions in selected locations. With the Signing of the peace deal by the warring parties, it is expected that the country might expect a lot more of returnees than new displacements. Most of these are expected to return to their previous homes with limited materials and therefore would need support to ensure that they become self-sustaining and building of their livelihoods. Therefore, the 2019 project will seek to respond to the needs of these vulnerable IDPs and returnees with the view of making their shelter needs and livelihoods more self-sustaining than depending on continuous donor support. This however would only be possible if these locations of response experience sustainable peace. The response will be done within the prioritized locations and any other locations that might experience new displacements or returnees during the project period. The organization seeks to achieve this through the utilization of its frontline mobile team and the experienced static staff in its various operational areas within the country. WVSS will continue to be part of the responses that are multi-cluster and multi- agency. This will ensure that the needs of the affected populations are served in a more holistic and shortest possible response time.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Nutrition Services for Malnourished Children under Five Years and pregnant and lactating women in Greater Bagari, Wau Western Bahr el Ghazal
project_objective:
The goal of this intervention is to provide quality lifesaving CMAM interventions to children 6-59 months and Pregnant and Lactating Women in 14 Bomas of Greater Bagari (Baggari, Bazia and Besselia).
 
Through this project, Johanniter will screen over 90% of children under five years 9,564 (4,878 girls and boys 4,686) and also over 90% of pregnant and lactating women 1,910 for malnutrition in the 14 Bomas of Bagari and Besselia areas. Additionally a total of 4,027 women and 425 men will directly be reached through MIYCN messaging and counselling at community level. The project will reach at least 80% of SAM and MAM in girls and boys 6-59 months; 80% of PLW. The estimated number of SAM cases is 628, MAM in children under five years 1,913 and MAM in PLW 523.   Indirect beneficiaries of this project will include 790 males who are caretakers of children under five, County health department staff, health workers and Community nutrition volunteers.

The project will be a continuation of the current emergency nutrition response in Bagari, Bazia and Besselia by Johanniter under the SSHF 2018. The project will be complemented by on-going UNICEF and WFP projects in Wau and Jur River, and a GBV project privately funded under Johanniter which will support with protection services.

In an effort to address the prevailing humanitarian situation in the Baggari, Bazia and Besselia area, Johanniter is requesting SSHF funds to continue the current emergency nutrition intervention which has already seen nutrition centers established, staff trained, increased outreach activities, formation of mother to mother groups, reporting and referral system set up. This will also complement the on-going UNICEF and WFP projects to provide integrated nutrition services to the affected and vulnerable populations. At the moment, Johanniter is final stages of development of the PCA with UNICEF and FLA with WFP to cover the OTPs and TSFP activities in Baggari for the period of 2019. 

The 250,000 USD that is being requested for will ensure that there are no gaps or interruption in services to the population that has been greatly affected by prolonged insecurity, limited access to basic services and displaced.  Under this funding, Johanniter will scale up outreach activities, train health workers on CMAM and MIYCN, recruit more nutrition staff to meet the minimum standards in the nutrition sites, integrate WASH interventions particularly messaging and WASH supplies at facilities so as to reduce on WASH related diseases, setup feedback mechanisms at the facilities, referral system for both complicated medical cases and GBV cases.

project_name: Provision of emergency and integrated water and sanitation and hygiene promotion services to conflict affected and vulnerable populations  in the former  Warrap, Upper Nile, Northern Bhar El Ghazal, Upper Nile, and Western Equatorial States in the republic of South Sudan
project_objective:
According to the UNICEF-WHO 2017 Joint Monitoring Programme, over 61 percent of the population of South Sudan practiced open defecation and the few existing sanitation facilities are mostly in disrepair. High open defecation rates are exacerbated by the internal displacement of over 1.94 million people since December 2013. The worsening economic crisis has negatively affected the cost of delivering WASH services. Institutional capacity is fragmented and communities that are unable to afford clean water have reverted back to using contaminated water sources. The shortage of fuel has increased the cost for hiring water trucks and this service is vital in areas such as Protection of Civilians (PoC) sites and refugee camps.
WASH infrastructure has been deliberately targeted by armed actors during the conflict, leaving most of the water infrastructure in conflict-affected areas destroyed. Internal displacement puts a strain on existing water sources and increases WASH needs. The deteriorating economic situation has made it difficult for the population to afford safe water, as in most locations, the price per liter has doubled while outside Juba the price has tripled compared to late 2016. With congested populations, both in crowded PoC sites and urban areas, water-borne diseases spread rapidly. The ongoing cholera outbreak, which has spread to new areas, is both a consequence and a cause of unmet WASH needs. High malnutrition rates are also linked to poor WASH conditions, as exemplified in the diarrhea-malnutrition cycle prevalent in vulnerable populations.
Recent surveys show that more than 30 percent of people in South Sudan do not have access to safe water supplies; only 13 percent have access to adequate sanitation facilities, making this one of the lowest service coverage statistics in the world. Only 45 percent of South Sudan’s 3,349 basic primary schools have access to safe water and a mere 17 percent have adequate sanitary latrines for both girls and boys. South Sudan remains host to 98 percent of the world’s remaining Guinea worm cases, despite a reduction in caseload from more than 20,500 in 2006 to below 1,000 in 2011. Concerted efforts are being spearheaded by UNICEF to achieve eradication of this debilitating diseases by providing safe and clean water to affected communities. The overall situation of acute malnutrition has slightly improved this year as compared to the same period last year with no counties reporting extreme critical levels (GAM above 30%) of acute of malnutrition in 2018.  
In 2018, World Vision International South Sudan was able to provide clean and safe drinking water to 217,770 people who received at least the minimum 20 liters of safe drinking water per person every day through surface water treatment systems (water treatment plants and Small scale water treatment system) and ground water (boreholes).  WVSS also constructed 4,239 shared household latrines and reached 193,110 people with hygiene promotion messages. In schools and health facilities, WVSS continues to provide WASH interventions. These activities were implemented in Central Equatorial, Western Equatorial, Unity, Upper Nile, Northern Bhar El Ghazal and Warrap states.  

 In 2019, WVSS intends to continue providing emergencies WASH interventions to the same states mentioned above for the following reasons :
1. The increased movement of the IDPs due to multiple armed conflicts is putting a strain on existed WASH resources for both the IDPs and host communities. Thus, there is a need to construct additional WASH facilities and rehabilitated existing facilities. 
2. The drought has left communities with very limited options for WASH facilities support, particularly water supply. There is a needs for adequate and sustainable water sources and supply systems to ensure that communities have enough support to overcome environmental risks and challenges, as well as build their resilience to respond to future challenges.

project_name: Support to vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and host families in North East Nigeria to Improve agricultural production, availability and access to nutritious food
project_objective: The project aims at addressing food, income and nutrition insecurity by Support nutritious food production during the rainy and dry season farming through the provision of mixed emergency agricultural inputs to support the most food insecure and vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in the states of Adamawa, Borno and Yobe. This will go hand in  hand in hand with training on Good Agricultural Practices, nutrition and gender sensitive agriculture. FAO aims to increase the participation of women in these small scale production activities, especially through distribution of small ruminants and poultry, and women savings groups. In addition, FAO will also provide poultry inputs (chickens, housing, feed). These interventions will be aiming to rebuild the productive capacities of vulnerable women, who have lost large parts of their livestock/poultry assets due to the conflict.  The project will target 190,000 households (approximately 1,330,000 individuals) with crop farming and livestock related support. The project will further target 20,000 households (approximately 140,000 individuals) address limited access to energy. Multiple challenges related to energy access directly result in food insecurity and malnutrition (e.g. insufficient fuel to cook food), deforestation (e.g. unsustainable cutting of wood resources for fuel), protection risks (e.g. harassment, assault, rape of women when collecting woodfuel) and health risks (smoke inhalation, respiratory illnesses). FAO will promote use of fuel-efficient cookstoves and support to sustainable management of woodfuel resources (tree nurseries, communal woodlots and agroforestry)

project_name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018-2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

project_name: Appui au district sanitaire d'Ansongo pour l’amélioration des soins de santé essentiels dans la communauté
project_objective:
Afin de contribuer à l’amélioration des indicateurs de santé, le Mali a décidé d’améliorer son approche de santé communautaire par la mise en place d’Agents de Santé Communautaire (ASC) dans les régions du Sud et du Centre. 
Les interventions de ces ASC ont contribué à augmenter la couverture et l’accès aux services curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels au sein de la communauté et dans les ménages.

C’est dans ce cadre que s’inscrit le présent projet qui vise à renforcer les capacités du système sanitaire de la zone d'intervention dans la prise en charge communautaire des maladies de la femme enceinte et de l'enfant afin de réduire la morbi mortalité élevée au sein de ces groupes vulnérables. Il cible le district sanitaire de Ansongo dans la région de Gao située au Nord du Mali.
Les 3 principaux résultats attendus du projet sont :
- Les enfants de moins de 5 ans et les femmes enceintes ont accès à des soins de santé essentiels gratuits de qualité dans la communauté
- Les enfants de moins de 5 ans bénéficient d’une prise en charge médico-nutritionnelle gratuite et de qualité dans la communauté 
-Les communautés sont sensibilisées et la gouvernance communautaire est renforcée pour une meilleure appropriation des problèmes de santé
Ainsi, le projet intervient essentiellement au niveau communautaire et s'inscrit dans une logique temporelle à 3 niveaux :
-A court terme pour répondre aux besoins sanitaires de base en améliorant l'accès aux soins des populations les plus vulnérables ;
-A moyen-terme à travers l'amélioration durable de la qualité des services de santé et le renforcement du plateau technique (personnel et matériel) ;
-A long-terme à travers le renforcement de la gouvernance locale et l'amélioration de la gestion des centres de santé communautaire.

project_name: RESTORING COMPREHENSIVE HEALTHCARE SERVICE DELIVERY IN PRIORITY COMMUNITIES AND STRENTGHENING THE HEALTH TRAINING INSTITUTIONS IN BORNO, YOBE AND ADAMAWA
project_objective:
The Health systems and indices in the Northeastern Nigeria has been severely devastated by the years of violent conflict that left devastations on the health infrastructure, looting of equipment and massive displacement of health workforce. The risk of disease outbreak has more particularly increased in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe, affecting 14 million people with 1.4 million Internally Displaced People (IDP) and 5.2 million people in need are taking shelter in overcrowded and unsanitary camps and dwellings with limited or no access to clean water and adequate sanitation. The ongoing conflict and continued displacement has a serious impact particularly on the most vulnerable population including women, unaccompanied/ separated children, adolescent boys, pregnant/ lactating women and abductees. Since the declaration of humanitarian Emergency in the Northeast states, health service delivery has focused majorly on the delivery of rapid emergency lifesaving healthcare services through the temporary health structures and mobile teams. The result is that most of the health infrastructures still remains in dire need of rehabilitation and full restoration of health services with outbreaks of cholera and other epidemic disease increasing due to lack of infection prevention and control structures, effective waste management, water as well as sanitation facilities . The Health systems availability monitoring systems (HeRAMS) estimates that only a marginal improvement in functionality of the health infrastructure has been achieved between 2016 and 2018 across the 3 states especially in Borno state.  
This project aims to restore comprehensive healthcare service delivery to the most vulnerable displaced population and returnees including women and children in the North east states of Borno, Yobe and Adamawa.  The program will focus on revitalization of sustainable basic service delivery in the areas of health, the full rehabilitation and equipping of health facilities would be carried out based on the minimum standards provided by the National Primary Healthcare Development Agency (NDPCDA) and adopted by the state ministries of Health with the concept of building back better.  Health training institutions would also be strengthened to produce quality health workers who would be engaged and deployed to the rehabilitated health facilities through provision of equipment to the school practical demonstration rooms, classroom furniture, library equipment, office equipment and other teaching aids.
This project will support the following: 
•	Rehabilitation of health facilities as per the Nigerian MoH norms and standards, and best practice recommended by WHO ( 8 primary health centres in Borno, and 4 primary health centres each for  Adamawa  and Yobe states )
•	Procurement and distribution of medical equipment and (limited and time-bound) supplies for 16 rehabilitated health care centres.
•	Establishment of standard waste management systems for infection prevention in 40 primary healthcare facilities in Borno Yobe and Adamawa
•	Provision of equipment and teaching aids for the 6 departments of college of health technology
•	Assessment of Workload indicator of Staff Needs
•	Support the HDN sensitization Meeting with stakeholders and partners at the national level
•	Set up a technical working group on HDN in the health sector in the three states on the North East Nigeria
•	Support the HDN coordination  meetings at the LGAs in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states

project_name: Installation of solar panels to private desalination plants to increase the access to sustainable, adequate and safe drinking water for vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
This action is an immediate response to ensure that girls, boys, women, men, elderly with and without disabilities have sufficient means to respond to their WASH related needs. Specifically, the action aims at improving access to drinking water supply by installing solar panel systems for 13 private desalination plants (PDPs), In Gaza Strip (GS), drinking water is largely supplied by PDPs, which provide more than 4 MCM/year to Gaza households, representing 95% of the water used for drinking and 67% of the water used for cooking. The action directly contributes to the 2019 oPt Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) Strategic Objective 1: “The rights of Palestinians living under occupation, including those living under the blockade and other restrictions, are protected, respected and promoted in accordance with International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL), while duty-bearers are increasingly held to account”; and Strategic Objective 2: “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic service and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”. Specifically, this action directly contributes to the WASH Cluster Strategic Objective 1, by ensuring equitable access to drinking water services to the most vulnerable people in GS; and WASH Cluster Objective 2: “Strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacity to the un-served, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank, to reduce threats and to cope with emergencies and shocks” through provision of alternative energy sources (solar) including alternative solutions to water access, and support critical PDPs located in the un-served, underserved and most vulnerable communities in the GS. 
The action aims to achieve the above objectives through the installation of solar panel systems for 13 PDPs which are committed to work during emergency, and willing to contribute on 20% of the total amount of the solar panel systems. The action also envisages a capacity building programme on operation and maintenance of desalination plants and solar panels systems and water quality and safety of water trucking. This action’s purpose is to maintain minimum operations of private water desalination plants in the GS, which will lead to guarantee drinking water access in communities who live in deteriorated public health conditions and to enhance the drinking water safety and quality. The provision of alternative source of energy to the 13 selected plants is the result of a the 2018 GVC study titled “Drinking Water Distribution Mapping During Crises in the Gaza Strip, with Desalination Plants of Private Vendors”, endorsed by the WASH cluster and PWA, The study analysed the capacity and the cost of drinking water production in the GS during large and medium scale crisis. The analysis, which targeted 96 PDPs in the GS to be used in case of emergency, has led to the selection of 21 PDPs as the most suitable to respond. Further, the study recommended to improve and upgrade the selected private desalinations plants in terms of potable water quality and safety and to conduct practical technical trainings to improve staff technical capacity and management during crises for the selected plants. 
The activities will be coordinated with the Palestinian Water Authority (PWA), WASH cluster, and the relevant working groups (e.g. Renewable and Sustainable Solar Energy Coordination Task Force, WASH Monitoring Working Group (WMWG), Water Quality Working Group (WQWG)).
The 13 PDPs are located in Beit Hanoun (2), Bet Lahia (1), Jabalia (1), Gaza (Al Shejaiya) (2), Beach Camp (2), Al Nussirat Camp (1), Khan Yunis Camp (2), Al Mawasi (Khan Yunis) (1) and Rafah (1). 
It is expected that this action will directly benefit 216,000 people (57,161 girls, 59,706 boys, 49,086 women, 50,047 men), 67% out of them are refugees and IDPs, while it will indirectly target 360,000 individuals (95,628 girls, 99,509 boys, 81,810 women, 83,412 men) during emergencies.
Coordination with UNRWA infrastructure & camp improvement programme was ensured to avoid overlapping and ensure complementary to the services provided by the Agency

project_name: NIGER INTERIM COUNTRY STRATEGIC PLAN
project_objective: 'The percentage of Malian refugees not recurring to negative coping mechanisms was 93 percent in 2017. Although this is a positive result if compared to national figures, for assistance provided within the Malian refugee camps and residence zone, an open residence area where beneficiaries are free to leave and return for distributions, it represents a deterioration compared to results of the same period in 2016 when 96 percent did not recur to negative coping mechanisms.As in the rest of the country, the dietary diversity score (DDS) for Malian refugees deteriorated in 2017 compared to 2016: an average of 3.7 food groups on 8 were consumed by beneficiaries in the seven days preceding the survey. The percentage of Malian refugee households with a poor food consumption score (FCS) has also increased, going from 7 percent in 2016 to 26 percent in 2017. The Malian refugee community is mostly pastoral. The fodder deficit of 2017 had an impact on beneficiaries in the Tahoua and Tillabéri regions, including the mostly pastoral Malian refugee community. To find areas to bring their animals to pasture, many refugees residing in the Intikane residence zone were forced to go to further distances to find green areas for pasture. This meant that they may miss their monthly distribution with negative effects on their nutrient intake. Negative results were found mostly in the Mangaizé refugee camp, where food voucher distributions were carried out, and beneficiaries tended to choose cereals over pulses and other food groups, resulting in a negative impact on the FCS and DDS. Solutions to promote better diet diversity and food consumption will be key in 2018

project_name: Emergency and post-emergency response to specific protection needs of conflict-affected populations inside Syria
project_objective:
In order to mitigate the protection-related risks associated with the high level of land contamination by CW, CM and IEDs in Syria, the Organization will implement its integrated two-tiered Humanitarian Mine Action programme: 

1/ Risk prevention and local capacity building
the INGO will provide RE for most at-risk populations living and working in highly contaminated areas in Syria. the Organization's strategy is based on a composite intervention methodology, allowing the activity to remain flexible to changes in context and needs. Thus, based on context, access and needs analysis, the RE will be conducted either through direct RE sessions at households’ level or through public information. Direct RE sessions will allow the INGO to reach the most isolated people and to adapt the content and approach of the sessions to the target audience. Public information will raise awareness at a global scale and will be carried out under different modalities, decided according to the context and the resources available locally.

In addition, safety briefing will be proposed to humanitarian workers to spread RE knowledge within the humanitarian community and thus to promote safe behaviours and minimize the risk of accidents.

Also, ToT will be proposed to key members of communities (teachers, community leaders and EO survivors) so they become focal points and empowered to dispense safety messages to reduce their peers' vulnerabilities This activity aims to strengthen the skills of key local actors in order to ensure the appropriation of the messages disseminated and thus the sustainability of the activity.

Finally, the Organization will produce and externally disseminate evidence-based advocacy factsheets so as to mobilize and persuade local, national, regional and international stakeholders and denounce key humanitarian and protection issues for populations and humanitarian actors in Syria.

2/Clearance 
The INGO will work towards the identification, marking and the safe disposal of explosive ordnances when safe to remove the immediate threat.
Through this Action, the Organization will also implement clearance activities in Raqqa Governorate, while maintaining the possibility of deploying Clearance teams to Deir Ezzor if the context allows. In this perspective, NTS activities will only be carried out in Deir Ezzor if demining in the area is confirmed so that it does not raise expectations and places people at greater risk. 

3/ Victim Assistance
The organization will provide physical rehabilitation, prosthetics and orthotics as well as MHPSS services to EHA survivors and as well as other People with Injuries or Disabilities living in contaminated areas; the organization will also support access to other services through referrals.

project_name: GBV - Integrated Community-Based Protection Services for Conflict-Affected Populations, especially GBV survivors and their communities, in Central Equatoria, Western Equatoria, and Upper Nile States (GBV sub-cluster).
project_objective:
The Project’s ultimate goal is to ensure that the displaced and host communities affected by the recent hostilities and subsequent displacement and trauma in Urban Juba, Lainya, Yei, Kajo Keji, Maridi, and Maiwut, including child survivors of GBV, 1) have access to, and receive comprehensive, gender-sensitive, survivor-centered, life-saving psychosocial, case management and referral services; 2) rebuild social cohesion and community-based support mechanisms; and 3) are prevented from further harm. To reach this ultimate goal, the project will seek the following outcome: Enhanced life-saving and survivor-centered prevention and response protection services of quality available to/and visible to vulnerable communities affected by the recent conflict, with a particular focus on GBV survivors. 

In addition, the project will work with communities to (re) build community-based prevention mechanisms and ensure a safer environment for all, especially girls, boys, women, the elderly, and people with disability – who were particularly affected by the shocks of conflict, displacement and crisis. Thus, the project will ensure that communities are capable and prepared to address threats and vulnerabilities, while maximizing existing positive coping mechanisms, in accordance with the Protection Cluster’s second strategic objective to prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience.

One key aspect of IsraAID’s mandate is to accompany national/local actors in their efforts to design, implement and evaluate their own programs to ensure local ownership and sustainability. IsraAID identifies local actors to design and implement Protection/GBV programs. IsraAID’s role is to provide continuing technical support and on-going training and mentoring to ensure that service providers in each of its partner institutions have the skills and tools needed to deliver services of quality. In order to ensure that IsraAID’s programs have a long-term impact, the organization involves and trains local partners from the need assessment to the evaluation phase (including national CBOs and service providers). Throughout its programs, IsraAID places a particular emphasis on IASC Accountability for Affected Populations Principles (AAP). It continuously trains its own staff as well as national partners on those principles and how to incorporate them into activities.

In 2019 IsraAID will engage with new partners during 2019, including, Nile Initiative Development Organization (NIDO) in Maiwut/ Upper Nile State, Facilitating Action for Community Empowerment (FACE) in Maridi, and TITI Foundation in Juba. IsraAID will also continue to work with our existing partners, including Street  Children Aid (SCA) in Kajo Keji, South Sudan Health Association (SSUHA) in Lainya and Voice for Change (VfC) in Yei.

project_name: Provision of and support to healthcare services with a specific focus on Sexual and Reproductive Health, Mental Health and Psychosocial support and GBV prevention for conflict affected population in Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast, Eastern Ukraine (GCA and NGCA)
project_objective: The proposed intervention aims to continue answering to the most urgent humanitarian needs along the contact line while looking for medium to long term solutions to ensure an improved access to quality health services for the most vulnerable people affected by the protracted crisis in Eastern Ukraine (Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast). The project will particularly target vulnerable women and girls affected by on-going conflict by ensuring access to Sexual and Reproductive Health services and access to GBV prevention and response services. The project will also contribute to address the high level of mental health problems among internally displaced persons and host populations in conflict affected areas. In order to achieve this objective, MdM will target the most vulnerable communities and categories of people affected by the conflict (such as women and girls, elders, people exposed to conflict-related stressors): - The mobile unit approach in remote locations of Luhansk and Donetsk oblast close to the line of contact will ensure access to PHC, treatment and referral to specialized care. The mobile unit will promote a comprehensive approach by providing PHC, MHPSS and SRH services and will be integrated within the existing health facilities (feldshers’points). - The local health system will also be supported through targeted donations of supplies and equipment and health staff will be trained (with a specific focus on SRH including Family Planning and MHPSS) to face current lack of capacity building opportunities in conflict-affected Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast. The training plan will be developed in line with the ongoing Health System Reform and by creating synergies with public training institutes and/or hospitals. - Building up on MdM experience in the area MdM will build a new project aiming to strengthen local authorities’ and local NGOs capacities to provide a comprehensive package of services to survivors of Gender-Based Violence including the most vulnerable population, and by raising awareness on health and mental health consequences of GBV, promoting the development of a sustainable referral pathway. - MdM mental health and psychosocial intervention based on evidence-based methodology will be expanded and disseminated to support the needs of persons who deal with psychological problems such as: stress, fear, feelings of helplessness, as well as practical readjustment challenges related to conflicts within families, issues with communities and livelihood difficulties. MdM advocacy efforts will also continue to ensure the integration of MHPSS into PHC in the framework of the current Health Reform. In NGCA, in so-called Luhansk People Republic, where MdM has been registered since October 2017, MdM will continue to support PHC facilities close to the contact line, which have been particularly affected by the conflict. MdM will pursue with donations of life-saving medical equipment to Emergency departments of hospitals with focus on Children’s health and Sexual and Reproductive Health. Besides, MdM will seek to extend its activities in NGCA.

project_name: Strengthening humanitarian coordination,  advocacy and efficient humanitarian assistance in Mali
Improving Access of Vulnerable People to Infectious Disease Management Services
project_objective:
The primary goal of this project is to reduce preventable morbidity, mortality and disability as a result of infectious diseases through supporting existing health facilities in the geographical targets. The project founds an improved access of vulnerable people including migrants, displaced families, returnees and people with special needs to an integrated health care services at primary and secondary facilities with the focus on infectious disease management.
Under this project, WHO will strengthen the technical and operational capacities of the primary and secondary health facilities by providing health service providers with effective disease diagnosis and case management training opportunities. Equally the targeted health facilities will be supported with medical equipment and essential drugs for the timely provision of preventive and curative services to all communities.
