project_name: Emergency Health Services and core-pipeline support to the populations affected by the Humanitarian Crisis in South Sudan
project_objective:
There can be no health services without medicines and medical supplies. This project will target all the ten operational hubs states, focusing more in areas which bear the highest burden of IDPs, and other vulnerable segments; children and women of childbearing age, who account for 25% of the population). Preparedness and prevention activities on EVD will also be given high priority in EVD high risk counties. WHO will cover all the Health Cluster priority locations with emphasis on the earmarked for integrated approach with three other Clusters.

The core pipeline will enable the procurement and prepositioning of  inter-agency emergency health kits to support health cluster partners providing life-saving humanitarian response in deep field areas. These will VHF kits, IEHK, DDK, Nutrition Kits, Basic Unit IEHK, Major and Minor Surgical Kits, Malaria Kits including antimalarial drugs and malaria RDTs, and Trauma & Surgical Kits), basic medical equipment & supplies for life saving surgery & comprehensive EmNOC in selected health facilities, state & county hospitals

The existing disease surveillance system [IDSR and EWARN] will be strengthened. The project will support the verification of health alerts and events, outbreak preparedness and response. Supportive supervision will also be provided to enhance surveillance capacities at state, county, and health facilities & rapid health assessments in acute & protracted emergencies, and operationalize a national Public Health Emergency Operations Center at national level.  Medical mobile teams to will deployed to provide rapid response in areas with limited or no humanitarian partners in a timely manner, and provide lifesaving health services to displaced populations, hence reducing avoidable morbidity and mortality


WHO will target to reach a minimum 377,049 beneficiaries and a maximum of 565,573 beneficiaries. It is expected that these supplies will complement the regular streams of the MoH and bilateral funding to partners.

project_name: Prevention and Management of Acute Malnutrition in Vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities in Ayod County, Jonglei State.
project_objective:
September 2018 IPC findings estimate 6 million people to be facing Crisis and Emergency (IPC phases 3 and 4) acute food insecurity, out of which 4.3 million of people are facing Emergency (IPC phase 4) acute food insecurity in South Sudan. Humanitarian situation in Ayod county of Jonglei remains critical due to repeated devastation and displacement. Population displacement is rampant with people moving to areas perceived safer. With most of the population having lost their livelihood and with missed planting seasons consecutively for three seasons, coupled with insecurity, the host community and IDPs have been left food insecure and the malnutrition levels alarming. Previous nutrition response has been stretched by influx of IDP’s and host community. Most families are without employment; most population heavily reliant on humanitarian assistance. (WFP 2018).

CMD will be implementing minimum package of Integrating Out Patient Therapeutic Program (OTP) within existing health facilities by providing routine treatment using simple medical protocol to SAM without medical complications. In addition, CMD will integrate Health, WASH and FSL into Nutrition targeting the 15 OTP sites and 4 SC’s within Northern and Southern Ayod this includes Pagil, Menime, Normanyang, Kandak, Mogok, Jiech, Gorwai, Padek, Kuachdeng, Haat, Kharmun, Mhaar, Nyawit ,Ayod town  and Wan-Machar where CMD has existing health facilities while SC will be situated in Pagil, Mogok, Jiech and Padek to treat 491 SAM children with medical complications. CMD will leverage on its ongoing responses on thematic areas of WASH, Health and Education. CMD currently runs WASH interventions in Ayod mainly through the provision of WASH services at nutrition OTPs and SCs run by CMD. 
CMD proposes to continue delivering nutrition services in Ayod County- Kandak, Menime, Pagil, and Normanyang and scale up activities in Mogok and Padek in collaboration with MoH, partners and local authorities through supporting initiatives for the decentralization of OTP and SC sites, increasing awareness through community mobilization on: IYCF Practices for prevention of Malnutrition, socio-mobilization for vitamin A supplementation and advocacy for the proper use of LLITN. With UNICEF and WFP collaboration, they will enable CMD provide targeted emergency nutrition supplies and services to a SAM caseload of up to 2,454 (Including 491 children with complicated severe acute cases) in need (< 5 years both boys and girls) and MAM caseload of up to 6,466(<5 years) and PLW’s caseload of 4,978. CMD will train Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) and Mother-to-Mother support groups from host community to acquire skills and knowledge on Integrated Management of SAM and Maternal Infant and young child feeding practices so as to provide quality nutrition services. Health staff and Nutrition staffs will be capacitated for integration of SAM and MAM management into health programmes especially on malaria screening and referral of severe cases to OTP and Stabilization centres.

project_name: Réponse à l’urgence nutritionnelle dans la région du Bahr El Gazal Sud et Ouest
project_objective:
L'intervention proposée vise la réduction de la mortalité des enfants de moins de 5 ans dans la région du Barh El Gazal Sud à travers l’amélioration du statut nutritionnel des enfants de moins de 5 ans et des femmes enceintes et allaitantes par les activités spécifiques et sensibles à la nutrition avec la mise en place d’un paquet d’activités préventives à travers la stratégie de 1000 jours. De façon plus spécifique, elle contribuera à l’amélioration de la couverture et de l’accès à une prise en charge préventive et curative gratuite et de qualité des principes pathologies de l’enfant  dont la malnutrition aigüe sévère en ambulatoire et en hospitalisation ; le renforcement du dépistage et du référencement des enfants malnutris aigus par l’approche PB- œdème mère ; de l’amélioration de la demande, du recours et de la disponibilité des soins néonataux et obstétricaux d’urgence dans la zone ciblée par le projet ; le renforcement de la résilience des structures de santé à travers l’approche SURGE ; la promotion des pratiques familiales essentielles à travers des stratégies de communication prenant en compte les spécificités socio-culturelles de la zone et le renforcement du paquet minimum Wash  dans les centres de santé. L’intervention couvrira 28 aires de santé dans les districts sanitaires de Moussoro , Michemiré et Chaddra .
La dimension genre sera intégrée à chaque étape du projet, pour les bénéficiaires directs, indirects à travers une approche participative, afin de répondre de façon adaptée aux besoins de l’ensemble de la population. Les données seront analysées par genre et par catégorie d’âge. Les bénéficiaires de ce projet sont en majorité des enfants <5 ans et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes. Le projet prévoit l’implication des autorités sanitaires et de la communauté affectée, aussi bien les femmes que les hommes, lors de la conception, la planification des actions, la mise en œuvre et le suivi et l’évaluation du projet.

project_name: Pro-Resilience Food Security & Livelihood Restoration for vulnerable men, women, boys and girls affected by the protracted conflict and economic shocks in Rubkona and Panyijiar Counties of  Unity State, South Sudan
project_objective:
Based on the September 2018 IPC analysis, it is expected that 6.1 million1 people in South Sudan (59% of the total population) face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity at the peak of the lean season (July – August), of whom 47,000 are in Catastrophe (IPC phase 5) and 1.7 million in Emergency (IPC Phase 4). Unity state where the project falls has 71.3% or 214,000 people in emergency or catastrophic phases of the IPC classification and a further 395,000 in phase 3. This project is therefore developed to address the food insecurity issues. 
 Mercy Corps aims to contribute to building the resilience of the crisis affected populations through support to  beneficiaries to improve their livelihoods performance  . The project will also contribute to sustainable, equitable production, income and employment for the vulnerable through market-led production.
Mercy Corps appreciates that emergencies affects people differently. In South Sudan women, children and elderly are the worst affected with the conflict and economic shocks. As such in terms of targeting or selection, women, child headed households, elderly, PWD and the chronically ill will be highly preferred during the process. All activities including targeting, post distribution monitoring, evaluations will engage women separately to ensure adequate contribution to issues affecting them. All reports will be presented with information dis aggregated by gender. The project will target a total of 10,830 households that comprises approximately 65,000 individual beneficiaries.
The proposed project will contribute to the Food Security and Livelihoods cluster objectives 1 and 2 namely:
-	Cluster Objective 1:  Unconditional food assistance: Provide emergency regular life sustaining and life-saving food assistance to prevent famine, improve food consumption, improve dietary diversity and improve coping strategies for the most vulnerable population
-	Cluster Objective 2: Food production for the most vulnerable households: Increase vulnerable household food production to protect the erosion of livelihoods through agricultural seeds and fishing inputs.

Cash for work grants to most vulnerable households with labour ability will avail temporary income for vulnerable households to meet their immediate food requirement while community common resource properties like dykes are rehabilitated to combat flood events.
 Cash programming will be complemented by vegetable farming and staple crops inputs as a means to diversify their diets. Programme design is based upon market survey and vulnerability assessment and the FSNM  September 2018 report  high quality risk analysis with assessment of multiple types of shocks and stresses people face.
Livelihood promotion: 
-	Support vulnerable households towards short-cycle vegetable food production systems for home consumption and sale of surplus by distributing livelihoods assets e.g. vegetable seeds and tools, pro-resilience livelihood  business startup grants aimed at diversifying livelihood options. 
-	Where possible, livelihood activities are supported to improve household income aimed at immediate improved household purchasing power of diversified food of choice and working capital of other livelihood options. 
-	Communities are supported in preferred livelihood supply chain management and livelihood value chain development aimed at strengthening their resilience to the causes and effects of the common disasters. 
Through this project, Mercy Corps is planning to target the most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls in Rukona and Panyijiar for IGAs through  distribution of livelihood inputs to support  beneficiaries during the dry season hunger gap, which will be from February – April 2019 (three months earlier than normal). The 
 business start-up grants will be complemented by low input vegetable gardening  and staple crop production(from March to May) as a means to promote household self-reliance and immediate food provision through own food production for both home consumption and sale of surplus.

project_name: Improved Water Supply for returnees, through 5 well rehabilitation and 2 sewage networks rehabilitation in rural Damascus (Sbeinah).
project_objective: The purpose of this project is to provide the most vulnerable people-returnees in targeted locations of Rural Damascus (Sbeineh) with quality, reliable access to water through the revitalization and rehabilitation of WASH facilities.  As a result of the continuous conflict in the area, water and sewage mainlines have been neglected, damaged, or destroyed, causing a substantial hazard to the health and well-being of beneficiaries as well as a risk to the environment. Therefore, HELP will undertake a series of focused activities aimed at improving the sewage networks and the rehabilitation and maintenance of 5 wells in selected locations that have been identified as the most underserved and vulnerable by the Allocation Strategy Paper.

project_name: Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance for Protecting Legal Identity, and Housing, Land and Property
project_objective: In 2019, NRC’s overall objective in Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) programming is that Iraqis affected by displacement are able to claim and exercise their rights vital for achieving durable solutions. To achieve this, NRC has two primary objectives: that target groups 1) claim and exercise HLP rights; and 2) possess legal identity, including civil documentation. These objectives will be achieved through a multiplicity of ICLA activities, including the delivery of information sessions, provision of legal assistance, advocacy and training on issues such as Housing, Land and Property (HLP) and Conflict Dispute Resolution (CDR). NRC's ICLA interventions are consistently coordinated and integrated with other sectors and departments, including Camp Management, Education and Shelter.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Recovery of Livelihoods for the Most Vulnerable IDPs and Conflict affected households.
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in eastern Ukraine is now at its fifth year with no end in sight yet. So far it has caused the displacement of 2.6 million persons and 35,081 casualties, of which 10,303 people killed , and a considerable destruction of infrastructure. The Line of Contact (LoC) separates now the government controlled areas (GCA) and non-government controlled areas (NGCA) of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts. The Government of Ukraine (GoU) has registered 1.5 million Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), of which 800,000 are estimated to be permanently living in GCA. Over 1.9 million Ukrainians are living within 20 km zone along the LoC on both sides, and they are among the most vulnerable affected by the conflict.
Due to the protracted conflict food insecurity and disrupted livelihoods remain to be the main issues affecting hundreds of thousands of IDP and local population in eastern Ukraine. Over 2019-2020 period NRC will continue its comprehensive support to the most vulnerable conflict-affected population in GCA to enable  their (1) access to food, (2) restoration of productive assets, and (3) employment and income generation opportunities.

project_name: Humanitarian Coordination and Advocacy in Nigeria
project_objective: In 2019, OCHA will continue to focus on the humanitarian crisis in the north east of the country, with the centre of the operational response in Maiduguri, while maintaining a commitment to support the HC, humanitarian partners and the Government in Abuja, including for emergency response and preparedness  as dictated by events and circumstances

project_name: Reduce the threat of ERW, mines, and IEDs for at risk communities
project_objective:
The specific objective of the project is to reduce the impact of explosive hazards for conflict-affected populations through Risk Education and land release in Suleymaniya, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Baghdad, Anbar and Diyala Governorates. Specifically, both risk education and land release activities will take place in Kirkuk, Suleymaniya, Diyala and Ninewa. Risk education activities will also take place in Baghdad and Anbar.

In direct relation with the priority needs identified, the project will provide an immediate humanitarian response and contribute to recovery efforts through integrated and comprehensive humanitarian mine action. The project will target IDPs, returnees and host communities living in and around contaminated areas in Iraq. The total target beneficiaries for this project are 137,500 including 120,000 for Risk Education activities and 17,500 for clearance and survey activities.

The project activities related to clearance and survey will be executed by direct implementation by Handicap International (HI). The Risk Education activities will be implemented both directly by HI and in partnership with Iraqi Health and Social Care Organization (IHSCO). The intervention will work in close collaboration with the National Mine Action authorities; Directorate of Mine Action (DMA) and the Iraqi Kurdistan Mine Action Agency (IKMAA)

Specifically, HI will work to facilitate safe return of populations and access to land by reducing the immediate threat posed by Explosive ordnance and increase awareness of the population in the target areas on the risks and threats posed by Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) and Explosive Remnants of War (ERW).
	
In addition to the above, HI will contribute to national level advocacy, targeting the Government of Iraq and the international community. HI is indeed promoting a blended approach to Mine Action (MA) and is advocating for stakeholders to consider a fresh, community-based and cost-effective approach to the ongoing MA in the country.

Furthermore the intervention will follow a comprehensive approach as it will benefit from other HI interventions to ensure multiple yet integrated activities (including risk education, MHPSS, physical rehabilitation, and inclusive access to service) in order to maximize the intervention for beneficiaries. 

The majority of the project is allocated to clearance and mine action which requires specific materials and human resources accordingly resulting in a higher budget required.

project_name: Ukraine Humanitarian Response Plan 2019 -2020 : Project Proposal
project_objective: The project will contribute to protection and promotion of rights and durable solutions for people affected by the conflict in eastern Ukraine, in close coordination NRC Ukraine’s LFS and S&S programs. Within this goal, ICLA’s specific objectives are to: (1) ensure that a greater number of the most vulnerable conflict affected people in hard to reach areas have access to basic rights and humanitarian assistance, reduce their vulnerability and build resilience; (2) Support economic and social well-being as durable solutions by providing IDP with equal access to, and enjoyment of their right to an adequate standard of living without discrimination, including shelter, livelihoods and employment, effective and accessible mechanisms to restore housing, land and property rights, access to personal and other documentation and freedom of movement (3) build the capacity of government and civil society legal service providers to adopt the maximum feasible case load for IDPs and other such conflict-affected populations in need of assistance (4) support advocacy in pursuing the adoption of policies and practice which promote durable solutions in line with international standards. ICLA will endeavour to reach the most vulnerable within the above target groups, notably women/single headed households, especially with a large number of children, elderly (particularly living alone), people with disabilities or limited mobility, extremely poor and no-income families, people of pre-retirement age, people living in rural or remote areas. This will include persons from GCA and NGCA where possible.

project_name: Stabilisation of Livelihoods and Strengthening of the Resilience of Smallholder farming families in Northern Bahr el Ghazal
project_objective:
The project will contribute to improve food and nutrition security of vulnerable households through provision of seeds, tools and agriculture trainings on staple crops and vegetables. Targeted households are supported to increase their income through various activities, such as temporary employment in Cash for Asset activities during lean season, but even more so by training them on income generating activities for additional income as well as organising themselves in VSLAs which allow them to access funds in times of need. Supporting improved post-harvest management, especially improved storage facilities, will also help to make households more resilient to inflationary price developments. 
Furthermore, the communities are supported and train to identify the risks of possible external environment impacts and to respond to mitigate such risks with the construction of dykes and drainage channels for flood protection or irrigation ponds. These measures will help to limit the impact of droughts and floods and thus help to reduce harvest losses and damages to basic infrastructure. 
In addition, the capacities of both individuals among the target group as well as of the local state actors are developed through trainings and skills-development and local structures are strengthened which will ensure that developed infrastructure will be managed and maintained. Social infrastructure in the communities will be rehabilitated through construction of feeder roads, but also construction of one school building. 
The direct beneficiaries will be 6,000 vulnerable semi-pastoral rural households in two counties in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil West and North), i.e. around 40,000 individuals. The indirect target group is the entire population of the 12 payams, approx. 246,500 people. Wherever possible, the project will target the most vulnerable, high risk groups, especially women and women-headed households, IDPs and recently returned households, as well as children and old and chronically ill people, as these groups are most at risk for food insecurity and malnutrition and are often marginalised in their communities. The project aims to target approx. 21,600 women and 18,400 men.

project_name: Improved sanitation and enhanced knowledge on hygiene in schools and communities in the Greater Equatoria Region and Northern Bahr el Ghazal
project_objective: The project will focus on hygiene education on household level in rural and semi-rural communities as well as implementing child-friendly hygiene trainings in schools. Both will be combined with rehabilitation of existing WASH infrastructures at individual level as well as in schools. Welthungerhilfe plans to implement simultanously a FSL programme to ensure improved WASH facilities and hygiene behavior changes are strongly interlinked with agriculture activities as improved, diversified crop production and improved food use to contribute to strengthening nutrition security in a wholistic approach. Welthungerhilfe also plans to pilot menstrual hygiene promotion activities in its areas of intervention to contribute to women's and girl's equality and not longer being stigmatized during their menstruation cycle. In total up to 20 schools will be targeted in Torit and Yambio for improved WASH facilities and child-friendly hygiene trainings. In NBeG 12 primary schools will be targeted for rehabilitation of latrines in schools, serving approx. 12,000 school children and provide trainings on improved hygiene practices to 1,200 children and teacher. In NBeG in total 600 rural households, i.e. 4,200 individuals will be trained on improved hygiene,  practices and will benefit from 12 rehabilitated drinking water boreholes. In Torit another 800 households will be targeted for hygiene trainings through a network of volunteer hygiene promoters. In each target school a WASH club will be strengthened or newly established where school children will be trained using the CHAST-approach on improved hygiene practices, they will be supported in organizing particular WASH-days (handwashing day, etc.) where they will be supported to do mass-campaigns and hygiene messaging for other school children.

project_name: Holistic Protection Monitoring and Service provision across Northern Ninewa and Duhok Governorates
project_objective:
Ninewa is the main originating Governorate of IDPs in Iraq and currently also hosts the majority of the returnees (1,550,000 IOM November 2018) whereas Dohuk Governorate host the majority of the IDPs in the Kurdish Region of Iraq (350,000 IOM November 2018). Both returnees as well as IDPs and remainees face significant protection issues. Dorcas has been executing 68 FGDs in 2018 including 940 male & female respondents in Ninewa along with 725 HH assessments to identify most prominent protection issues and their root causes. Most frequent mentioned issue that acerbates HH’s vulnerability is absence, loss or barred civil documentation like ID cards, passports, PDS cards and birth-, marriage- and death certificates, obstructing HH’s access to basic services like healthcare, education, social support, disability allowances, etc. Second pertaining protection issue is incidents of recruitment into government-affiliated armed groups reported in parts of Ninewa;  groups who control the areas make returns conditional on the commitment of families to enlist one or more male family members (UNHCR Protection Update – July 2018). Thirdly, for many (Sunni/Shia) IDPs from Tel Afar, Sinjar, Mosul & Hamdaniya, returns to their AoO are considered as unsafe due to perceived extremist affiliation and associated risk of (unjustified) detention (UNHCR Protection Update – July 2018). Remainees in Ninewa face similar protection issues. Fourthly, risks of secondary displacement are rampant due to lack of available services in AoO, lack of livelihood options and perceived lack of safety, which is particularly troubling in Sinjar, Tel Afar and Tilkaif (REACH ROAR, April-May 2018; IOM Return Index October 2018). Fifthly, in Sumel and Zakho, between 31.3% and 45.5% of the IDP population faces HLP issues (UNHCR Protection Update – July 2018). Similarly identified issues are common in Sinjar and Wana where 324 returned HH reported lack of documentation to proof ownership over their housing and land. Not only does this obstruct people from re-settling in their AoO, it also disables them to take up (agricultural based) livelihoods which subsequently affect each sphere of family and economic life. Sixthly, the armed conflict and associated atrocities such as witnessing violence, disappearance of family members, forced displacement, (S)GBV and (fear of) imprisonment have been identified as having severe potential negative mental health impacts (Ibrahim et al., 2018). 
Based on each partner’s years of technical expertise, (Dorcas in general protection and legal support, Harikar in (S)GBV protection) Partners propose the implementation of a holistic protection package covering in total 32,400 IDP-, Returnee- and Remainee populations in Northern Ninewa (Sinjar, Tel Afar, Telkaif) and Dohuk Governorate (Zakho & Sumel). 
This will be done through a combined mobile and static approach providing the following services through 6 centers: protection monitoring and HH-level assessments, awareness raising and community mobilization to tackle protection issues, provision of legal counselling and legal assistance by lawyers (related to HLP, Documentation, Detention), case management, provision of SGBV services (and Child Protection services through coooperating with WarChild), provision of structures PSS and ensuring adequate referral pathways for protection cases. Specific attention will be paid to the plight of women, girls and boys who are assessed to be extra vulnerable when there is a breach in the protective atmosphere (i.e. armed forces recruitment, (S)GBV, etc.).

project_name: TURKEY - United Nations Population Fund
Increase food production and strengthen coping strategies of vulnerable households in Aweil North and Twic.
project_objective:
Première Urgence Internationale develops an integrated approach, combining health, nutrition, and FSL services to effectively tackle the needs of the populations: this allows to respond to urgent needs and to foster recovery and improve the resilience of the communities, for a more sustainable program. 

PUI will provide livelihood support to 35,000 food insecure households in Aweil North (Northern Bahr el Ghazal) and Twic (Warrap State). The vegetable and fishing intervention planned will help increase food production, improving dietary diversity and coping strategies for the most vulnerable populations. 

The project will revolve around 3 key pillars. 
The targeted households will receive vegetable and fishing kits, with seeds, tools (ie, hoes) and fishing equipment (ie, twines, hooks) to improve production means and thus reinforce the accessibility, availability and diversity of food at household and local market levels. The project targets 16,000 households in Aweil North, where PUI already supports 15 nutrition sites and has implemented a FAO funded Emergency Response Livelihoods Project (ERLP) as an integrated approach to complement its nutrition and health programs –meaning that households with pregnant and lactating women and children under 5 suffering from malnutrition will be prioritized. In Twic, 16,000 households will also be targeted and receive kits, as PUI will take over and expand activities started under the previous FAO ERLP in the area by other FAO-funded partners. 

PUI also proposes to implement Conditional General Distribution for 3,000 households, providing food to vulnerable people in Aweil North in exchange for their involvement in an activity chosen by the community. The chosen activity will create an added value for the household or the community at large, while reinforcing ownership. PUI will indeed discuss their needs with each community through its Program Management Committees and other possible focused group discussions. 

Farmer and fishing groups will be established to manage demonstration plots, provide a forum for PUI trainings and ensure peer-to-peer experiential learning: 1,067 households in Aweil North and 533 households in Twic will be part of farmer groups and fishing groups. The groups will collectively fence the group gardens, prepare the land and make conventional seed beds. PUI will provide pilot pond fishing farming trainings in some of the Payams with more persistent and localized swamps as well. Households will be trained on conservation agriculture techniques, including post-harvest and handling techniques to enhance conservation and preservation of the vegetables. They will also learn about Integrated Pest and Disease Management (IPDM), using local resources as a way to build resilience within the communities. Fishing groups will furthermore benefit from trainings on good, safe and hygienic fishing practices, including learning about fish preservation with smoke kilns and salting techniques and will be trained on fishing-net making. 

Through the vegetable gardens, the availability of food for consumption and the dietary diversity will be increased, while the training in conservation agriculture, good agricultural and fishing practices will improve coping strategies. Through garden groups’ establishment and trainings in conservation agriculture, food processing and preservation, rural livelihoods will be protected, safeguarded and stabilized all while improving food availability and reducing the food gap. As PUI links beneficiaries in the nutrition program to the FSL program, PUI aims to shift interventions, lowering dependence on the nutrition program and focus more on fostering resilience and communities’ future self-reliance.

project_name: World Council of Churches/ Ecumenical Accompaniment Programme in Palestine and Israel (EAPPI)
project_objective:
The Ecumenical Accompaniment Programme in Palestine and Israel is an international, ecumenical programme that recruits and dispatches observers (known as Ecumenical Accompaniers - EAs) to several Palestinian towns and villages to monitor the interaction between the Palestinian inhabitants and the Israeli military. The presence of EAs is intended to offer protection and to moderate friction. Abuses of authority are monitored and reported and EAs speak publicly of their experiences. Accompaniers have four stated tasks: to offer protection through nonviolent presence; to monitor and report violations of human rights and international humanitarian law; to support Israeli and Palestinian peace activists; to undertake advocacy work including public speaking.
EAPPI also seeks to cross fertilize through networking with host churches as well as Israeli, Palestinian and international partners at local and international level. EAPPI mission is to witness life under occupation, engage with local Palestinians and Israelis pursuing a just peace, to change the international community’s awareness and involvement in the conflict, urging them to act against injustice in the region

project_name: Provision of emergency health services to internally displaced persons and vulnerable host communities in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective:
Multiply displaced communities face significant health challenges in parts of Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria, which prior to the conflict had limited or no access to health care services. The project seeks to provide access to essential lifesaving health care services to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality in the counties of Ayod,Uror (Jonglei);  Longechuk, Ulang (Upper Nile State) and Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East (Eastern Equatoria State)

CMD aims at fostering improved access, prevent, detect and respond to epidemic prone diseases, improve resilience among vulnerable populations and deliver an integrated response cutting across health, WASH, Nutrition, food security and protection. The project will implement and expand essential primary health care emergency clinical packages targeting the most vulnerable, carry out preventive health measures through immunisation targeting children, PLWs and <5s. Working alongside health cluster leads; CMD will implement outbreak investigation and response in the targeted locations while mainstreaming accountability to affected populations. 
An expanded program will include HIV/AIDS/TB care and reproductive health (RH) services including SGBV. CMD will implement integrated response for severe acute malnutrition with medical complications especially in locations with high cases of malnutrition as well as implement integrated response for epidemic prone communicable diseases including diarrheal, vector, Viral Hemorrhagic diseases with WASH/Nut/FSL. Emergency health protection for people with disabilities will be provided across all project locations. 
In the locations of Kapoeta South, East and Ulang, CMD will carry out referrals for Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CeMONC), minor trauma and surgery, and work with development health partners to scale up integrated response to SAM with medical complications. 

The project will directly benefit 15,000 people (51% female, 48% IDPs, 45% vulnerable host communities, 7% returnees and other groups in the locations of Ayod, Uror (Jonglei);  Longechuk, Ulang (Upper Nile State) and Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East (Eastern Equatoria State)

project_name: JORDAN - International Organization for Migration
Lean Season Food Assistance to the most food insecure people in rural areas
project_objective:
Under this Flash Appeal, Food Security sector partners plan to address the most urgent food security needs of people in rural areas across the country, who are adversely affected by multiple crises, including last year’s poor harvest for many small-holder farmers, economic shocks and recent cholera and typhoid outbreaks. Building on the funding already received to reach an estimated 900,000 people as of January 2019 and the Government’s Food Deficit Mitigation Strategy, partners aim to expand the geographic coverage of assistance to reach an additional 700,000 people in food insecure rural communities through primarily cash-based assistance. Focus will be on the low-lying areas relying on rainfed agriculture disproportionately affected by last year’s erratic rain. Market-based interventions are viable despite the current economic stress, as essential food commodities remain available on rural as well as urban markets, according to the national market assessment conducted by WFP and partners in November 2018. 

The IPC analysis conducted in January 2019 projects that nearly 3.8 million people in rural areas are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance, including 2.9 million who are severely food insecure (IPC phase 3 or 4) and a further 900,000 people who are currently receiving humanitarian assistance, without which they would be in IPC phase 3 or above.

In the face of the high prevalence of food insecurity (IPC phase 4 and 3), and the high probability of another El Niño phenomena in 2019 (90% likelihood according to the most recent SARCOF analysis), partners will provide a specialised food ration in the form of CSB++ specifically targeting children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women to increase the nutritional value of the food basket provided as part of the general household ration/cash. 

Based on the findings of the national market assessment conducted by partners in November, partners will select the most appropriate transfer modality for each district (cash or in-kind). According to the latest price information, partners aim to cover approximately 80% of the targeted individuals’ daily food energy needs (based on a 2100 kcal diet) to supplement other available food sources, thus enabling households to meet their basic food and nutrition needs. 
 
In view of the high probability of another El Nino, food assistance at this juncture can be considered as an early action to prevent further deterioration of food insecurity amongst particularly households already in IPC 3 (Crises) and 4 (Emergency).

project_name: Improvement of WASH conditions in Volnovaskyi, Nikolskyi, Marinskyi, Mangushskiy, Yasynuvatskyi, Velykonovosilkivskyi rayons in Donetsk region
project_objective:
Through this project, ADRA aims to improve access of population affected by the conflict in Eastern Ukraine to essential services as well as critical civilian structures by repairing infrastructure.  This will be achieved by increasing their access to clean water through delivery of water chemicals and water trucking/bottled water, testing water quality and distribution of sanitary water storage vessels. this will be combined with sustainable emergency repairs of pipes, tanks, as well as the supply of essential material, equipment and pumps of decentralized water supply systems and in schools and health facilities. The project will also address waste management problems by emptying septic tanks as well as distribution of essential hygiene items with hygiene promotion
The project will be implemented in GCA Donetsk Oblast with main focus on settlements near the contact line (0-5 km), and will be targeting vulnerable groups with focus on elderly people, persons with disabilities or injury, persons with chronic illness, and women & girls.
The project proposal is prepared based on Humanitarian Response Plan 2019 (HRP). The project will contribute to the implementation of HRP Strategic Objective 2 (SO2): Provide emergency assistance and ensure non-discriminatory access to quality essential services for populations in need. The project will also contribute to the WASH Cluster Objectives 1 and 2: WASH Objective 1. Ensure immediate and sustainable access to sufficient safe water, and minimal levels of sanitation provision, for conflict affected people. WASH Objective 2. Provision of critical WASH-related supplies and information for the prevention of water- and sanitation-related diseases.

project_name: Building Refugee Resilience in White Nile & Khartoum
project_objective:
In 2019, ADRA will continue to support protection for the SSR by strengthening community based self-protection structures such as Inter Communal Dialogue Groups (ICDGs), Women’s Groups (WGs) and forming Youth Groups. This action will strengthen accountability towards decision makers and other actors. The aim is to institutionalize the groups to be part of the former camp governance system. This action will build the capacity of the SSR and host community (HC) to improve social protection systems and increase the groups’ awareness of and linkage to referral mechanisms.
This action will reduce protection risks associated with negative coping mechanisms by implementing cash for work and distributing charcoal vouchers. More specifically, these cash based interventions will reduce exposure to GBV during firewood collection, supported by production and distribution of Fuel Efficient Stoves (FES).
Particular attention will be given to trainings on stove usage and environmental issues and cash for work will include targeted reforestation as well as FES production, thereby strengthening the linkage between activities, aligning interests of SSR and HC and creating space for the SSR and HC to jointly address protection issues.
In Khartoum the project aims at supporting refugee children enrollment, as well as female targeted literacy programs. The programs will be conducted hand in hand with protection and community engagement programs in the same area.

project_name: Provision of shelter assistance to internally displaced and conflicted affected communities in Ukraine
project_objective: There is ongoing armed conflict in Ukraine, and daily violations of the ceasefire agreement. Examples of these localized flare-ups include the fighting in Avdiivka in late January 2017 and the shelling of Novoluhanskoe in December 2017. These ceasefire violations have a serious impact on civilians’ lives and property. They damage or destroy housing and infrastructure, necessitating an emergency response in terms of shelter and basic needs, especially for most vulnerable and persons with specific needs. To provide displaced and conflict-affected persons with specific needs in a timely manner UNHCR will preposition emergency NFI kits to be distributed to families at risk of displacement or newly displaced, as part of emergency response. In GCA, the emergency response is generally led by local authorities, and UNHCR’s contribution will complement their efforts. Some 1,250 kits composed of basic and domestic items will be prepositioned closed to the line of contact for households living in or returning to individual or multi-story buildings damaged during the conflict and/or newly displaced or evacuated UNHCR’s emergency response will be coordinated closely with local authorities and complementary to their efforts to respond. Winterization activities are not in UNHCR’s prioritized plan, but could be implemented if there are critical needs and pending availability of donor funds as a part of the comprehensive plan. Should funds be available, UNHCR would provide cash assistance (in GCA) or coal (in NGCA) to households who live along the contact line and have no access to the supply of fuel for heating

project_name: Life-saving assistance for the most vulnerable and at-risk children in Koch and Aweil Center
project_objective: The project targets to reach 27,000 most vulnerable children and at-risk children in Koch and Aweil Center in former Unity and former Northern Bahr el Ghazal States. The project aims to provide critical child protection services for children at high risk and to prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience. IRC proposes interventions that improve the social-emotional well-being of children using a combination of center-based, school-based and community-based approaches utilizing UNICEF’s PSS manuals and IRC’s Social and Emotional Learning manuals. This will be coupled with case management services for vulnerable children including family tracing and reunification (FTR) services for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). The project shall also build the capacity of IRC child protection workers, protection workers, government officers, and community-based child protection structures in CPiE in order to promote longer-term and sustainable change.

project_objective: L’objectif global est d’apporter un soutien à la coordination effective des activités d’urgence et de réhabilitation agricole et de promouvoir une meilleure prise en compte des besoins des groupes spécifiquement vulnérables. project_name: Emergency Assistance for drought affected small holder farmers
project_objective: Provide agricultural inputs (crop and livestock) to restore the productive capacity of drought affected small holder farmers; Enhance the provision of water for agricultural production and human consumption; Enhance early warning information systems; and  sector coordination

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan
project_objective: Women, men and children in conflict and disaster affected communities are able to meet their basic household needs and protect their livelihoods, despite shocks and uncertainties. This will be achieved through a combination of emergency, recovery and resilience projects. The aim of emergency projects will be to provide lifesaving unconditional cash and voucher transfers to prevent famine, improve food consumption, improve nutrient intake and dietary diversity. Targeted groups will include recently displaced populations, host communities, households in locations under IPC 4 and 5 in areas where markets are functional. Relief and resilience projects will aim to increase household food production promote and protect rural and urban livelihoods, through public works, training and provision of agricultural inputs through support to market systems. Target groups will include IDPs, returnees, host communities in locations under IPC 3 and 4.  Emergency, recovery and resilience projects will all contribute towards improving coping strategies of vulnerable households and reduce their reliance on general food and in-kind distributions. Women and youth will be prioritized as most the vulnerable groups.

project_name: Emergency Education Response for crisis affected children and youth in South Sudan
project_objective:
The conflict in South Sudan continues to have negative impact on access to quality education for children and youth. As the conflict continued into 2018, the displacement, attacks on school, as well as hunger and economic crisis, continued to deprive children of education opportunities. An estimated 2.2 million children are not attending school in South Sudan . The purpose of the project is to ensure conflict-affected children and youths in South Sudan continuously access lifesaving and quality learning opportunities that are relevant to their psychosocial, emotional and cognitive development in a safe, inclusive and protected environment.

NRC will work to ensure that conflict-affected children and youth in conflict affected areas of Jonglei, Unity, Eastern Equatoria, Central Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, have access to life saving education, have strengthened resilience to current and future crises, and can contribute to the peaceful socio-economic development of South Sudan. The project will focus on ensuring access to safe and protective education for IDPs and returnees, strengthening and improving quality in the delivery of the Education for vulnerable children and Youth. This will be achieved through three strategic response areas: 1) support to formal basic education in static operations; 2) first phase response through the mobile education Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). And 3) Alternative Education Programme (AEP) for children and youth who have missed out on education due to conflict. The project will coordinate with the Education Cluster and MoGEI to support examination registration for Primary 8 (P8) students in POCs; implement school feeding programmes in areas without general food distribution. It will also construct or rehabilitate learning spaces, existing classrooms, gender-segregated latrines, and water points and storage tanks. It will enhance teacher professional development to improve the quality of teaching and learning and enhance teachers’ use of child-centred, inclusive teaching methods and positive discipline, improve their subject knowledge, and develop teachers’ skills in formative assessment and classroom management. 

The project will respond to the education needs of children in the most emergency-affected and hard-to-reach locations in South Sudan as part of a wider multi-sectoral rapid response mission. This includes conducting needs assessments within two weeks of a rapid onset emergency, and being able to initiate an emergency response within the subsequent twenty days. NRC’s Rapid Response Team (RRT) will work in coordination with the Education Cluster and the Inter-Cluster Working Group to respond in hard-to-reach locations, which are less visible but have significant needs but insufficient education actors. The RRT will target conflict-prone areas of the Greater Equatoria region, and position itself for responses in former Unity and Jonglei states, where access and security protocols can be met. The project will be delivered in an integrated manner to ensure safety and protection of girls in schools through the provision of dignity kits to girls, segregated WASH facilities for boys and girls, clean school environment, sensitisation of school communities on protection, child safeguarding, teachers’ professional code of conduct, as well as referral pathways for reporting cases of abuse.

•	11,957 boys, and 11,489 girls) are children and youth aged 6-18 years
•	1,750 are adults (1,135 men; 615 women) including teachers, PTA and other education personnel, Ministry of Education officials at state, county and payam levels 
•	
•	10,078 IDPs
•	12,598 Host communities
•	2,519 Retunees

project_name: Sustaining Lifesaving Primary Health Care Services and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support for Vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and affected Host Communities in South Sudan
Emergency WASH for the IDPs, host communities, returnees, GBV affected, risk of famine and outbreak affected population in South Sudan
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services for conflict affected people, vulnerable host communities and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. Over all the project will reach to about a population of 800,000 with WASH services and facilities. 

This emergency WASH project will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, frontline emergency WASH response, strengthening partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination as well information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere Standards. 

The project will focus on addressing the following:  

-	Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country 
-	Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees
-	WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
-	WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.) 
-	While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related GBV.

The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs and CBOs in areas highly affected by the conflict to ensure basic services are provided and long-term capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_name: Protection and legal assistance for persons in hard to reach and conflict-affected areas in South Sudan
project_objective:
The proposed project is a graduated approach to support the protection of displaced and conflict-affected populations through static, mobile, and emergency responses. 
The project will offer the following services:
•	Protection context assessments in all locations and, where possible, community-based protection monitoring, in which community focal points will be trained to report on protection needs and risks. NRC will prioritise working with women, youth, and vulnerable persons as monitoring focal points. Protection incidents will be documented and analysed to understand trends and evolution in the protection context, and results disseminated to communities and relevant stakeholders.
•	Provision of individual protection assistance (IPA), to persons with urgent protection needs. This will include providing a tailored intervention to an individual or small group of individuals. It will t include facilitated referral, material assistance, or unconditional cash transfer.
•	Support the creation of community-driven protection (CDP) mechanisms in hard to reach, underserved areas. NRC teams will work with communities to establish a series of local committees, including marginalized groups, through careful selection of representatives to ensure effectiveness and inclusiveness. 
•	Facilitate improved access to legal identity documentation for displacement affected persons who cannot access basic rights and services, especially school-aged children who have challenges applying for state exams. NRC will provide both awareness raising sessions to at-risk populations and individualized assistance in accessing national identity documentation. 
•	Housing Land and Property (HRP) rights. The HLP activities will include: 1) organizing dialogue between government and women leaders, host community’s leaders and for land allocation for persons returning from camps (if needed) to discuss HLP rights for returnees. 2) HLP rights trainings targeting chiefs, youth groups, older people, opinion leaders, customary authorities, local government authorities to enable fair allocation of land to returnees 3) Free legal counselling to those in need of it.
INTEGRATION: The project will be implemented in an integrated way so that IDPs and returnees don’t only receive protection support but also a source of Food, WASH and Shelter through other NRC projects in the planned locations as well as referrals to other agencies. This process will start with multi-sectoral assessments, joint trainings and deployment of integrated teams to respond. NRC is already using this approach of protection mainstreaming and integration in Education where NRC works with school management committees on prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) of children.
COORDINATION: The project will be implemented in coordination with other players in the sector especially UNHCR, IOM for information sharing and use of the cluster core pipeline supplies as well as other Shelter cluster members for joint assessments and response when appropriate. The project will also be coordinated with the Protection cluster especially in prioritization of locations and needs assessment.
GENDER: In both CDR, HLP and other components of the project, the implementation will be preceded by the Gender and vulnerability analysis so as to best understand the needs of boys, girls, women and men as well as the social structures and resources to advance inclusion of all categories of people including the elderly and PWDs.
RISKS: The risks associated with HLP work are lack of acceptance of the IDPs and returnees by the Host communities as well as politicizing the land allocation to returnees. NRC will not be directly involved in land allocation discussions and all the activities will be done in a transparent and participatory manner with all stakeholders. The project will limit its scope to training, advocacy and facilitating dialogue and acquiring legal documents.

project_name: Support to the Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit (FSNAU) for Somalia
project_objective:
The fragile food security and nutrition situation in Somalia requires close monitoring in order to ensure timely interventions by all stakeholders. Without this crucial information generated by FSNAU, response agencies would lack the evidence to effectively design the appropriate food security, nutrition and livelihoods interventions; the government would not be able to advocate for resources and coordinate responses; and resource partners would lack the evidence to make informed decisions to fund the interventions.  

The project objective is to support emergency and longer-term policy and programme interventions through the provision of timely information and analysis on the current and emerging food, nutrition, and livelihood security situation in Somalia.
