project_name: Deliver integrated, quality, live-saving inpatient nutrition services for SAM/MC, and surveillance, for the most vulnerable.
project_objective:
WHO proposes to reduce the health impact of the nutrition crisis through integrated health/nutrition/ protection/WASH/education interventions and nutrition surveillance, focusing on quality live-saving services, in areas with high burden of acute malnutrition, in South Sudan. In the effort to close child survival gaps, the project directly targets 15,000 SAM/MC children (58% of the SAM/MC annual caseload), their caretakers, and at least 100 health/nutrition staff working in stabilization centres and 50 staff in nutrition surveillance sites, in areas with high burden of acute malnutrition, food insecurity and morbidity. WHO will employ a two-pronged approach: 
1)	SAM/MC PACKAGE: 
a)	Implement a capacity building program designed by WHO to improve the quality of inpatient management of SAM/MC. Trainings to be conducted at the ToT and facility levels, combined with MIYCN component.
b)	Distribution of essential medical supplies (SAM kit), specifically designed by WHO to attend medical complications associated with SAM, to be used in stabilization centres.
c)	WASH services, which include distribution of equipment (life-straw) to mitigate the risk of infections in stabilization centres and WASH training.
d)	Conduct standardized trainings on MHPSS for health and nutrition staff working in stabilization centres and outpatient nutrition programs.
e)	Distribution of Early Childhood Development kits (procured in collaboration with UNICEF Education Division and Supply Division) and train SC staff on techniques on child stimulation, play with children, supervise play sessions, and make toy , and counselling caretakers on techniques to continue care, play and stimulation ant home.
f)	Regular on-site supportive supervision missions to reinforce the quality of live-saving services provided, focusing on on-the-job mentorship on clinical management based on the ITP guidelines

2)	INFORMATION PACKAGE: strengthening early detection of acute malnutrition in health facilities through expanded MUAC screening and surveillance, to early detect and timely refer patients at an earlier stage of acute malnutrition. Through MUAC surveillance WHO is targeting to screen at least 50,000 children under five, and train at least 50 health staff. WHO will:
a)	 establish additional MUAC sentinel sites at the health facility level 
b)	strengthen the reporting capacity of existing sites, to rapidly detect hot spots, encourage timely case referral
c)	disseminate weekly analysis to alert partners and trigger rapid response
d)	The health and nutrition staff will be supported remotely and through field mentorship and regular supportive supervision missions.

WHO’s mandate focuses on improving inpatient management of severe acute malnutrition and establishing nutrition surveillance. Since the beginning of the humanitarian crisis in 2013, WHO in South Sudan has put intensified efforts and operations, catalysed technical and financial resources to support improved inpatient therapeutic programs (ITP) for SAM/MC, as well as rolling out facility-based nutrition surveillance. Through this project, WHO will ensure that quality lifesaving medical treatments are provided for SAM/MC children so to prevent unnecessary deaths and ensuring quality across the continuum of care. Capacity building of medical doctors, nurses and other health workers responsible for case management of severely malnourished children is essential to achieve reductions in mortality. Supplies will provide a stop gap measure and ensure sustainability of treatments. WASH services will be extended to stabilization centres in priority locations. Nutrition surveillance sentinel sites will be established in high food insecure areas with alarming GAM rates. The existing sentinel sites will be closely supervised and supported to improve efficiency, case referral and reporting performance. WHO plays a unique role in emergency nutrition, provides technical support, builds sustainable institutional capacity, monitors the health situation and trends. Therefore the added value of this project is critical and very distinctive within the CMAM.

project_name: Improved access to safe water and vector control activities for the vulnerable, nutritionally affected and underserved population in Sudan
project_objective:
The WHO project aim is to decrease the avoidable mortality and morbidity related to water, vectors, and hospital acquired infections among 1,937,500 affected population in Blue Nile, Central Darfur, East Darfur, Gadaref, Kassala, North Darfur, Red Sea, South Darfur, South Kordofan, and West Darfur.


WHO will also support the MoH and partners to implement integrated vector management campaigns in response to acute events (such as outbreaks of vector borne diseases) and for the mitigation of the imminent health threats created by floods, and displacement. 

To decease avoidable mortality and morbidity it is essential to reduce the burden of vector and also water related disease below the epidemic threshold among targeted IDPs and vulnerable communities in Blue Nile, Central Darfur, East Darfur, Gadaref, Kassala, North Darfur, Red Sea, South Darfur, South Kordofan and West Darfur. This will be achieved through a comprehensive package of water safety activities: water quality monitoring and surveillance in targeted high risk locations; community based integrated prevention and control of water and vector borne diseases, and biomedical hazard control at health facility level. 

The water quality activities will be implemented by the MOH and WASH partners at state and national level with sustained support from WHO, complementing the UNICEF WASH intervention. This year, the focus will be at locality level, to promote efficiency by reducing the cost of sample transport from field to states capital cities and enabling the local authorities to conduct regular water sampling and testing in prioritized high risk locations. The main activities related to this component includes training of environmental officers/workers (MOH and WES), community volunteers and hygiene promoters on water testing using portable kits; sanitary inspection of water sources; proper water sources maintenance and house-hold chlorination, treatment and storage. The results of the regular monitoring of water sources quality and sanitary conditions will allow timely identification of health threats and implementation of corrective measures through sharing with all relevant partners. Close information sharing and consultations with Health sector will facilitate the early warning on  identified public health alerts related to water and vector transmission and joint planning of control measures. 

WHO comprehensive package of vector control activities includes; training of the  environmental health officers, CHW workers from MOH/WES in the selected 16 localities/locations on the integrated vector management and entomological surveillance, printing of the IEC material on the common vector, technical and logistic support to vector control campaigns and vector surveillance mission. The implementation will take into account the specific demographics of the IDP camps in targeted states with high population density, and also be directed by health information data on prevalence and trends of the diseases.

project_name: Emergency provision of agriculture-based livelihoods and resilience building support to vulnerable farming and pastoral communities in Darfur
project_objective:
The project will provide emergency agriculture and livestock-based livelihoods interventions and resilience building support for vulnerable farming and pastoral IDPs, returnees, refugees and hosting communities in South, North, West, East, and Central Darfur states.  Vulnerability of the target populations stems from the protracted crisis, the ongoing economic hardships at the macro and micro-levels and recent poor harvest because of localized droughts and pest infestations. This situation has led to high rates of acute and chronic food insecurity and malnutrition. FAO prioritized in a participatory manner 28 localities in the five states of Darfur based on the high degree of vulnerability to food insecurity and malnutrition.
This project will target 741,300 people among the most vulnerable communities including 185,325 returnees, 222,390 IDPs, 259,455 residents and 74,130 South Sudanese refugees. The focus will be on benefiting 226,850 women, 151,200 girls (less than 18 year of age), 217, 950 men and 145,300 boys(less than 18 year of age) from the proposed interventions based on their basic and specific needs taking into account the factors of age and gender. The project will target about 59,305 elderly people among the adult population including persons with disabilities.
The project will follow the FSL Sector Strategy that follows the Multi-year Humanitarian Strategy adopted by the Humanitarian Country Team in Sudan for the period 2017-2020. The FSL Sector Strategy entails providing livelihoods-saving interventions and addressing the root causes of food insecurity and malnutrition to tackle all aspects of food security, including physical and economic access, availability and utilization of food and the stability of food systems through complimentary emergency life-saving and resilience building  through agricultural and livestock-based livelihood interventions and income generating activities.
The project objectives are aligned with the FSL Sector objectives 1, which includes addressing immediate lifesaving humanitarian needs through emergency agricultural assistance including crop, livestock and veterinary inputs and extension services targeting 300,000 people.  This will include as well building the capacity of governmental institutions and sector partners to improve preparedness and response for new emergencies. Under FSL Sector objective 2, the sector aims to restore and improve food and nutrition security and enhance self-reliance of the most vulnerable communities to cope with current and future shocks and stresses. Agricultural production will be improved through provision of climate-smart crop production, livestock and veterinary inputs and support to services. Similarly, small scale farmers will be targeted for reduced food losses and strengthened post-harvest techniques through improved food and crop storage and processing facilities. On and off farm livelihood assistance will be diversified and managed and coordinated to respond to food chain threats including animal and plant pests and diseases;  In addition, communities will be involved in building, restoring and maintaining productive assets through cash and/or food for assets schemes.  About 387,000 people will be targeted under Sector objective 2. Under Sector objective 3, the sector will strengthen nutrition, water and energy sensitive agricultural, livestock and natural resources management- based livelihoods inputs, kits, and capacity building, and increased resilience of 54,300 vulnerable people.

Protection of people, specifically women and girls, against GBV; accountability to affected populations and environmental concerns will be mainstreamed into the proposed activities to reduce risk to GBV, respond to the needs of the target population, promote climate change adaptation measures and ensure implementation of environment-friendly interventions.

project_name: Renforcement des moyens d'existence pour accroitre la sécurité alimentaire des communautés agro pastorales dans les villages d'accueil  à l'Est du Tchad
project_objective:
L’Est du Tchad (Ennedi Est, Ouaddai, Sila et Wadi Fira) est affecté par une crise multidimensionnelle où l’insécurité alimentaire, la malnutrition et la présence prolongée de réfugiés soudanais s’ajoutent à un contexte de faible développement et d’accès limité aux ressources pour la sécurité alimentaire,
En 2017, la saison des pluies a été marquée dans certaines provinces par des pauses pluviométriques assez longues et une fin prématurée par endroit, entraînant une baisse de la production céréalière nationale de 2,1% par rapport à la moyenne quinquennale et de 5,1% par rapport à 2016. Les plus fortes baisses de production ont été enregistrées dans plusieurs provinces du Sahel mais aussi dans la bande Est où on a noté dans le Wadi Fira une baisse de 39%.  Des déficits fourragers et l’assèchement rapide des marres semi-permanentes ont de leur côté entrainé un mouvement précoce du bétail des régions du Sahel vers la zone soudanienne. En 2018, ces problèmes ont occasionné une détérioration de la situation nutritionnelle qui se révèle très préoccupante dans plusieurs provinces de l'Est et aussi à N’djaména. Le taux de malnutrition aigüe globale est de 13,9% en 2017, soit deux points de plus qu’en 2016. La malnutrition aigüe sévère est à 3,9%, un taux supérieur au seuil d’urgence de 2% et à celui de 2016 de 2,6%. La mise en œuvre d’une réponse d’urgence à la malnutrition aigüe est prioritaire dans 15 provinces dont le Ouaddaï, le Sila et Wadi Fira et aussi dans la bande sahélienne et N’djaména, y compris dans les camps de réfugiés, les sites de retournés et les déplacés de l'Est où le taux de MAG et/ou de MAS est souvent supérieur ou égal au seuil d’urgence (MAG = 15% et MAS = 2%).
En 2018, la situation n’est guère reluisante. La malnutrition est : Sila (MAG : 17,9%, MAM : 12,4%, MAS : 5,5%), Ouaddaï (MAG : 17,8%, MAM : 12,7 %et MAS : 5,1%) et Wadi Fira (MAG : 20,3%, MAM : 15,9%, MAS : 4,4%). Cette situation est réellement préoccupante.
Selon l’analyse EFSA de mai 2018, ces détériorations de l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle ont déjà commencé à impacter la situation nutritionnelle des enfants de moins de 5 ans, et il faut s’attendre à des dégradations plus importantes pendant le pic de la soudure du fait de l’augmentation de l’insécurité alimentaire et d’autres facteurs socioculturels structurels.
En tenant compte du niveau élevé de malnutrition des enfants et du rôle important des femmes dans l’économie familiale, les principaux bénéficiaires directs des actions du projet seront les femmes, en particulier les plus démunies qui, marquées par leur vulnérabilité due à plusieurs facteurs, ont des revenus faibles et des difficultés économiques importantes. Il s’agit des femmes chefs de familles, les femmes pauvres avec des enfants mineurs, les femmes seules ou âgées vulnérables mais capables de mener activités de production et des AGR.
En matière de protection transversale, toutes les actions seront axées sur les quatre éléments clés dans la mise en œuvre de ce présent projet. Surtout dans sa politique relative à la redevabilité, la FAO mettra en facteur les équipes de plaintes qui pourront remonter toutes les actions susceptibles de nuire à la bonne la dignité des bénéficiaires à travers cette opération. Dans le cadre de ce projet, plus de la moitié des bénéficiaires seront choisis par les femmes chefs de ménages vulnérables, les ménages ayant des enfants et des vieilles personnes. Ceci permettra de mieux protéger toutes ces couches qui sont souvent très vulnérables par rapport aux chocs et aux catastrophes.

project_name: ""Integrated Community and facility based nutrition emergency response in Chad Sahel Belt""
project_objective: In Chad, the humanitarian situation is characterized by recurrent emergencies: flooding, droughts, diseases outbreaks, food insecurity, influx of refugees from neighbouring countries and a protracted conflict in the Lake Chad Basin area. Chad ranked 186 out of 189 on the 2018 Human Development Index. Poor governance, poverty, low status of women, insufficient funding of basic social services remain barriers in improving children’s and women’s lives and constrain the development of the country. The nutrition SMART suvey carried out in Agust 2018 revealed that acute malnutrition remains a public health concern in many regions. It was found that 12 regions namly (Kanem (25%), Ennedi Ouest (22.8%), Wadi Fira (20.3%), Borkou (19.4%), Bahr El Ghazel (18.7%), Hadjer Lamis (18%), Sila (17.9%), Ouaddai (17.8%), Batha (17.1%), Ennedi Est (17.7%), Guera (17.6%) and Salamat (15.9%) exceed the emergency threshold as defined by WHO. These regions bear more than 80% of the national burden. This situation is exacerbated by an influx of refugees and returnees from Sudan, Central African Republic and Nigeria. Based on the caseload estimates of 2019, it is expected that over 349,660 children will suffer from severe acute malnutrition and will need care within 750 health facilities. The nutrition cluster target is to treat over 300,440 children within the 684 supported health facilities. In order to respond to the needs of children under 5 , it will be essential to secure the Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) pipeline and essential medicines in order to provide the most needed treatment in the target regions. UNICEF’s intervention is lifesaving and will directly contribute towards the achievement of the objective 2 of the Sustainable Development Goals through the following outcomes: (i) Scaled up treatment of severe acute malnutrition in the most affected regions; (ii) Capacity building of frontline health staff on SAM management, and (iii) Promotion of improved infant and young child feeding (IYCF) knowledge and practice of caregivers in the targeted communities. On top of accessibility, the project will focus on gender balance and equity in service delivery.

project_name: Support for mother/accompanying couples of severe acute malnourished children through WASH in Nut activities
project_objective:
Les crises nutritionnelles récurrentes qui continuent à frapper le Tchad touchent notamment les enfants de moins de 5 ans où les taux de malnutrition aigüe globale dépassent généralement le seuil d’urgence de 15%. En aout 2018 (SMART 2018), 12 régions (soit une région sur deux) présentent des prévalences supérieures au seuil d’urgence (15%) selon la classification de l’OMS.
Selon cette même SMART sur le plan national, 27,6%, 40,2% et 28,1% des enfants de 0-59 mois ont souffert respectivement de diarrhées, de fièvre et des infections respiratoires aigue au cours des deux semaines ayant précédé l’enquête, ces taux de morbidité élevés qui sont attribués en grande partie aux mauvaises conditions d’accès aux services d’eau potable d’hygiène et d’assainissement qui sont faibles dans le pays, selon le Programme Conjoint de l’Unicef et l’OMS pour le suivi des indicateurs WASH (JMP) de 2017, 43% des ménages ont accès à un service de base d’eau potable (disparité urbain/rural) et près de 68% de la population pratique encore la défécation à l’air libre et seule 10% de la population a accès à un assainissement de base et seulement 24 % de la population ont accès à des services pour se laver les mains avec de l’eau et du savon.
Afin de répondre aux besoins des enfants (filles et garçons) de moins de 5 ans souffrants de la malnutrition aigue sévère (MAS) en 2019, conformément à la stratégie nationale WASH In Nut de 2017, l’Unicef accompagnera la Prise en Charge Intégrée de la Malnutrition Aigüe (PCIMA) par des activités WASH in Nut dans les zones prioritaires. 
Les objectifs de la réponse multisectorielle s’alignent parfaitement avec ceux du développement durable notamment les objectifs 2 et 7. Cette réponse vise à sauver les enfants MAS et à améliorer leurs environnements ainsi que la résilience de leurs communautés et consiste à :
1- Améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable dans les centre de prise en charge de la MAS (UNT/UNA)
2- Améliorer l’accès aux services d’assainissement au niveau des centres 
3- Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène au tour de l’enfant du domicile au centre de prise en charge et au niveau communautaire  
La stratégie de réponse prendra en considération les aspects liées à l’égalité des sexes à la protection et à l’équité un rôle important sera attribué aux bénéficiaires dans toutes les étapes de la réponse.
Le projet s’intègre parfaitement avec la réponse nutritionnelle notamment le programme PCIMA et permet de construire des ponts solides entre l’urgence et le développement en renforçant aussi la résilience des communautés.

project_name: Education-in-Emergencies Response 2019-2020
project_objective:
UNICEF will continue to facilitate access to safe learning environment where children can access quality education in areas near the contact line in both GCA and NGCA. Specifically, UNICEF will continue to undertake urgent rehabilitation of education institutions as well as provide education supplies, including Early Child Development (ECD) and educational kits. 

In order to increase the protective nature of schools in increasing resilience of children, UNICEF will expand to provide capacity building trainings to a total of 740 teachers, community workers and NGO representatives on the delivery of Life Skills Education to 10,500 children within 347 schools on both sides of the contact line.   

Supporting efforts of schools and local authorities to develop policies, interventions and activities which effectively mitigate the impact of the conflict on children, UNICEF will provide trainings on Conflict Sensitive Education (CSE) to a total of 800 education professionals and local authority representatives in areas near the contact line (GCA).

UNICEF will also continue the development of different distance learning modalities to ensure uninterrupted access to all levels of education for children in NGCA as well as in areas near the contact line in GCA

project_name: UNICEF Maternal and Child Health Emergency Response 2019
project_objective: UNICEF proposes to enhance access of the conflict-affected population in eastern Ukraine to quality maternal and child health services by strengthening capacity of health workers, increasing awareness of Infant and Young Child feeding practices and immunisation, supporting rehabilitation of health facilities essentially through the procurement of supplies and equipment, and provision of supportive services for people living with HIV, children and adolescents, and where possible improvement of water and sanitation facilities.

project_name: Provision of Protective Services to Children and Caregivers Affected by the Conflict
project_objective: Ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine continues to weaken child protection systems creating new risks for affected boys, girls and their caregivers. To respond to the urgent needs, UNICEF is planning to strengthen child protection systems (C01) and to provide direct services to affected children and their families (CO2). Specifically, UNICEF will continue to provide psycho-social and protective services to children and their caregivers (including to survivors of gender-based violence, to children affected by violence and to children affected by mines and unexploded ordinance) (P02), invest in activities aimed at prevention (violence, mine-risk education) (P01) and ensure capacity building to community professionals working with children (P02). In addition, UNICEF will carry out activities directed at improving parenting skills among caregivers to improve and strengthen relationships between caregivers and their children. Taken together, these activities are aimed to strengthen local response systems, including availability of specialized services, as well as to ensure direct service provision where needed services are not available.

project_name: UNICEF Humanitarian WASH response in Eastern Ukraine 2019-2020
project_objective:
UNICEF intends to support the Coordination in the WASH sector, essential to strategize and optimize the intervention of all actors in WASH.
After reviewing different assessments, keeping in view the situations in East, needs, capacity and comparative advantage, UNICEF is planning to respond the needs of 1.77 million individuals in the two conflict affected areas of Donetska and Luhanska oblasts (GCA and NGCA), with provision of safe drinking water, improving access to safe sanitation and hygiene supplies, dissemination of critical water and hygiene related messages on communities located on both side of contact line in Donetsk and Luhansk, in Eastern Ukraine. This will be implemented through the water utility companies (centralized network of primary and secondary water suppliers) and decentralized structures. A particular focus will be made on WASH in social institutions (education/health facilities).
The different activities take into account the gender, age and disabilities specificities and promote equality, especially on gender. People reached with more than one activity are only considered once to avoid duplication in counting beneficiaries.

project_name: Improving the Protection Environment for IDPs, Returnees, and Host Communities in Iraq
project_objective: Despite the Iraqi Security Forces retaking Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIS) by December 2017, Iraqis affected by the conflict remain vulnerable and exposed to numerous protection threats. As the humanitarian response transitions from emergency to early recovery, the protection response enters a critical phase. Displaced and conflict affected people face barriers accessing rights and the discrimination faced by families of individuals with alleged or perceived links to ISIS is increasing. The ability for displaced people to find their own durable solutions and harness their own resilience mechanisms is curtailed. In this climate, the IRC will implement a project that is targeted at breaking down some of these structural barriers by conducting multi-pronged protection interventions aimed at supporting vulnerable people and harnessing community based modalities. This project will focus on the provision of legal assistance to vulnerable people, particularly women and children, protection monitoring, awareness sessions, advocacy, capacity building authorities and community leaders, engaging with Community Representation Groups and providing psychosocial support.

project_name: Integrated Health and Nutrtion Support for conflict affected and vulnerable population in Central,West and South Darfur
project_objective:
International Medical Corps (IMC) is proposing the implementation of an integrated health and nutrition project in targeted health facilities in  Central and West Jabal Mara Localities of Central Darfur and in Biliel locality of South Darfur serving an estimated catchment population of 450,000 affected by conflict and disaster, including internally displaced persons and host populations. International Medical Corps will provide support to health facilities, the health facilities will provide the following primary health and reproductive health services: outpatient consultations, EPI, disease surveillance, reproductive health services (antenatal care (ANC), postnatal care (PNC), family planning and delivery care) and integrated management of childhood illnesses (IMCI). Health education will also be a component of the project. This project will support referrals of patients to the next level of health care. Furthermore, IMC will continue to strengthen basic obstetric services in targeted clinics, as these are the only options for women that require reproductive health services in the camps. IMC will provide support Ministry of Health in epidemic disease surveillance, outbreak response and immunization campaigns. During this proposed project, IMC is also planning to conduct minor rehabilitation on targeted clinics to ensure quality, patient safety, infection prevention and continuity of services. IMC also intends to continue to provide short-term and on the job training to health facility staff. Drugs and medical supplies will also be procured and delivered to the clinics.International Medical Corps’ integrated nutrition intervention will focus on CMAM. The components of CMAM include community outreach and active case finding, defaulter tracing, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) screening of children aged 6-59 months, and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW).  Children aged 6-59 months will be screened for malnutrition at the health facility. Nutrition workers/CHWs will collaborate with PHC staff to ensure coordination of care and referrals to health services and/or nutrition services. By fully integrating the nutrition treatment into the primary healthcare response, International Medical Corps provides a comprehensive package of services to beneficiaries.  

This project will treat children aged 6-59 months and PLWs with MAM at 16 SFP sites.  Children with MAM will be enrolled and receive a medical and nutritional check-up, 

In addition to the activities proposed above, International Medical Corps will provide life-saving services to eligible pregnant and lactating women (PLW) and children (6-59 months of age) with moderate acute malnutrition through SFPs programs at health facilities. The health facilities will also provide treatment for children (6-59 months) with severe acute malnutrition (SAM). All targeted health facilities will have OTPs and SFPs. Those cases with severe acute malnutrition and medical complication will be referred to stabilization centers. International Medical Corps will support also  SCs at targeted locations. Nutrition education and counseling will be provided for caretakers of children under-two years of age as a component of infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices. Selected training will be provided for health facility staff on CMAM, IYCF and Monitoring and reporting. Community screenings, defaulter tracing and necessary follow-up will also be part of the intervention. International Medical Corps has the required operational structure and technical capacity to deliver, implement and monitor this project in Central Darfur and South Darfur State. International Medical Corps will also coordinates with communities, agencies and government authorities to enhance the performance of this project. This project expects to reach a total of 450,000 direct beneficiaries. These beneficiaries include women, men, girls and boys who are eligible for medical and nutrition services.

project_name: Emergency shelter/NFI and Recovery response for affected populations by natural disaster /or climate change, including internally displaced persons (IDP's)
project_objective:
This project aims to address the current gaps and emergency shelter/NFI needs identified by the Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) of IOM-DTM Unit, and reinforce the recovery mechanism in-country through a Disaster Risk Reduction approach, by: 

a) Reinforcing the capacity of national and local authorities on DRR response
b) Creation of an early warning system and strengthening the rapid assessment capacity following natural disasters, including monitoring of IDPs
c) Building a recovery response to natural disaster through the distribution of livelihood assistance
d) Implementing Quick Impact Projects (QIPs) through cash-based intervention and social cohesion activities
e) Providing emergency shelters and NFI response to populations affected by natural disasters, including cash-based intervention to support during construction process
f) Providing transitional shelters and shelter repair kits to the most vulnerable households affected by natural disasters, including cash-based intervention to support the construction process
g) Cash-based intervention for the construction of improved kitchens 
h) Reinforce Emergency Communication with Community mechanism in country, specifically the Hotline -109 

In addition, this project will reinforce the IOM’s Emergency Event Tracking system (EET) for rapid assessment following natural disasters and other displacement events, including the development of an emergency response team dedicated to assessing life-saving shelter needs of returnees. 

The project, and, specifically, the Emergency Event Tracking (EET) will covering the 18 provinces of Burundi, namely Makamba, Rumonge, Bubanza, Cibitoke, Kayanza, Ngozi, Ruyigi, Rutana, Gitega, Bururi, Mwaro, Murumvya, Karusi, Cankuzo, Muyinga, Kayanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural.

project_name: 'provision of education in emergency services to conflict affected boys and girls in North East Nigeria
project_objective:
Plan International requests funding of 4,000,000 USD for a 12 months’ period to implement Education in Emergencies (EiE) activities to reach 60000 children (45% boys and 55% girls). The requested fund will be used to create equitable access to education for conflict-affected children. The funding will also improve the quality of learning while providing a protective learning environment for children under the do no harm policy and focus on targeting new arrivals in the local government areas of Gwoza, Kaga, Pulkha, Dikwa, Konduga and Mongunu all in Borno state North East Nigeria.
To achieve the above project objectives, and based on needs identified, Plan international I will establish, and refurbishment temporary learning spaces, do awareness raising and community mobilization to create access while to achieve improved quality, the action foresees training of teachers, provision of teacher materials, in-service and mentorship sessions. The action will build on the exist School Based Management Committees, train learners on life skills, establish and clearly mark gender segregated latrines, incorporate safe schools approach and other interventions in a bid to provide a protective learning environment.
The action will further seek to use the TaRL like approach that Plan International is currently using in providing education services to the children in MMC and Jere LGAs that has proved effectiveness in improving learning outcomes in literacy and numeracy.
The proposed action will target children aged 3-6 both boys and girls to benefit from early childhood development (ECD) and children aged 6-17 to benefit from formal education and non-formal education(ALP). Both in and out of school children belonging to the host and IDP communities will be targeted through the project with an aim of increasing enrollment, retention as well as increasing school attendance.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition assistance for vulnerable IDP and Host communities
project_objective: This project aims to contribute to reduction of infant morbidity and mortality through improved access to screening, treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition; as well as availing preventive micronutrient supplementation among some of the most vulnerable communities and regions in South Central Somalia.

project_name: Education and PSS for Vulnerable Children and Adolescents in Tripoli and Benghazi
project_objective: NRC will provide and improve access to protective, quality education in Tripoli and Benghazi, reaching approximately 5800 vulnerable and out-of-school children and adolescents (Libyan and non-Libyan) with non-formal education classes and PSS, improvements to the school environment, material distribution and will train and support 318 non-formal and formal teachers.

project_name: Assistance médicale aux populations affectées par les conflits armés dans la commune Gossi, district de Gourma Rhaous (Région de Tombouctou)
project_objective:
Ce projet de clinique mobile vient en un appui des interventions actuelles d’International Medical Corps dans la région de Tombouctou, Nord du Mali. Son objectif global est de fournir des services de stratégies avancées aux personnes touchées par le conflit armé et inter-communautaires dans la commune de Gossi, district sanitaire de Gourma Rhaous. Il contribuera à la réduction de la mortalité et de la morbidité liées à la crise humanitaire dans la commune de Gossi au Mali et accroître notre capacité de réponse aux urgences, aux épidémies et aux catastrophes naturelles.
IMC afin de s'assurer d'une appropriation des bénéficiaires par le projet,  mettra en place des mécanismes de redevabilité en début de projet avec l'organisation de réunions communautaires dans les zones touchés. Ces réunions auront pour objectifs d'identifier avec les communautés les canaux à utiliser pour la redevabilité. IMC veillera dans la mise de ce projet à intégrer les aspects liés au genre dans toutes les phases de la mise en œuvre de ce projet ; au moins 40% du personnel recruté sera des femmes.  Le suivi évaluation de nos programmes intégrera la ségrégation des données par genre et par âge pour mieux identifier les besoins des couches les plus vulnérables.

project_name: Protection case identification referral and assistance in the East and South of Libya
project_objective: The objective of the proposed actions is to respond comprehensively to the protection risks that vulnerable populations face in the East and South of Libya. The proposed action will focus on identifying and addressing the needs of vulnerable communities namely, IDP, Returnee and host communities. The geographic scope of intervention for the proposed action will largely focus on the East (with Benghazi, Ejdabiya and Derna being the focus) and in the South (with a focus on Sebha, Ghat and Ubari).

project_name: Supporting the National Plan for the Elimination of Cholera in Haiti, through the strengthening of disease surveillance, clinical management, alert and response and vaccination
project_objective: The main objective of this project is to reduce the number of cholera cases in 2019 by reinforcing coordination, epidemiological and community surveillance; improving laboratory capacities; improving cholera case management and infection prevention and control at institutional level; and through the use of reactive vaccination to reduce the risk of transmission. All these activities in support of the Ministry of Public Health and Population’s National Plan for the Elimination of Cholera 2019-2022.

project_name: Integrated psychosocial support and child protection services for the most affected boys and girls in Gaza, especially those impacted by  ‘the Great March of Return’
project_objective:
This project is in line with and contributes to the Protection Cluster Objective Two, which calls for putting in place protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence. This project will support the delivery of quality, integrated child protection and psychosocial support services to the most vulnerable boys and girls aged 4-18 in Gaza, especially those associated with injuries during the ‘Great March of Return’ protests. The crisis has demonstrated the almost absence of available child protection services to address critical needs.  The project will ensure that 11 Family Centers and 30 outreach sites in Gaza, are fully operational, responding to the pressing mental health and psychosocial, as well as child protection needs, of affected children. Service delivery will be targeted to the most affected locations and the most vulnerable children through a coordinated continuum of services in Gaza. Each Family Center will be connected to a community based child protection committee who informs the family center of community needs and acts as a focal point for identifying vulnerable children for referral. Family Centers will operate through established Community based organizations (CBOs) and mobile units, and will assess/screen and refer children for further services through:  
1) a case management approach for the worst affected; 
2) referral of complex child protection cases to child protection services (Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)); and 
3) referral of children with further psychosocial support needs to focused and specialized psychosocial support. 
Services will also strengthen outreach capacities to detect and link up children in need with service providers, whilst providing mental health psychosocial support (MHPSS) support through the family centres.

project_name: Most vulnerable schools and students, boys and girls, in Gaza provided with emergency supplies to continue learning
project_objective:
The project responds to Cluster Objective 1: Increase equitable and safe access to inclusive quality educational services for vulnerable children. It will enable 100 (out of 409) vulnerable schools in Gaza to continue functioning through the provision of necessary teaching and learning materials.  The schools will be selected based on the vulnerability mapping conducted by the Islamic Relief, UK, 2017  

The project will also support over 33,000 (50% girls) poorest students ages 6-17  who may be at risk of dropout due to poverty, to continue in their education by providing basic, urgent supplies including school bags, school uniforms, warm clothes, and shoes. The students will be provided with these materials via the e-voucher system designed with the World Food Programme (WFP) to avoid stigmatizing children and families and allowing the option to select their own supplies.

project_name: Household WASH services for the most vulnerable families in Gaza
project_objective: The project is an immediate response to ensure vulnerable women, children and men to have sufficient storage capacity of domestic and drinking water whenever it becomes available and have better access to safe water and safe sanitation facilities and public services through the rehabilitation, construction and upgrade of existing wastewater infrastructure and practice proper daily hygiene through increased advocacy and awareness raising.

project_name: Lifesaving healthcare services in South Central Somalia
project_objective:
This project aims to ensuring that there is increased equitable access to health services at health facility, at community level and through integrated outreach activities conducted by mobile teams among IDP and Host (rural and urban) populations in South Central Somalia. The project design takes on a targeted approach with a focus on:
1. Control of communicable childhood illnesses (diarrhea, acute respiratory illnesses malaria and measles).
2. Integrated management of common childhood illnesses (Eye, ear, skin, worm infections, anaemia and chronic childhood diseases)
3. Expand access to EPI, contributing to control of vaccine preventable diseases
4. Expanded access to reproductive healthcare services for women of reproductive age.
4. Community Disease surveillance and response - An emergency Rapid response component is built in to allow quick scale up of lifesaving health services ( eg through CTCs/ORT corners/mobile ORT and isolation wards) during rapid onset emergencies.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services in Sudan
project_objective: According to the 2019 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), more than 4 million people are in need of food security in Sudan. The key driver of humanitarian needs in Sudan is conflict which has led to displacement of both IDPs and refugees. The impact of conflict is new and protracted displacement, and access  to basic services. It also disrupts the livelihoods and food security of people in need. In 2019, UNHCR estimates 1.2 million refugees and asylum seekers will be living in Sudan and in need of humanitarian assistance. Disease outbreaks, AWD  in particular, and floods also cause humanitarian needs. Acute malnutrition in children under the age of 5 is above emergency thresholds. Access to formerly inaccessible areas in Jebel Marra (Central Darfur), South Kordofan and Blue Nile remains key. Effective and timely delivery of humanitarian assistance will require a coordinated response that brings together all relevant humanitarian stakeholders to agree on needs and priorities based on coordinated inter agency assessments, access, and the  vulnerability of the affected populations. To meet the needs of these populations, the HNO identified priority needs around the three outcomes of the MYHS: saving lives when new needs arise either due to natural or manmade disasters, responding to protracted displacement and addressing malnutrition and resilience.

project_name: Emergency livelihoods assistance for Returnees and host communities in Diyala, Kirkuk, and Salah al-Din
project_objective: IOM aims to increase economic opportunities for displaced and conflict affected populations (Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities). IOM will target governorates with high levels of continuing displacement, emphasizing Diyala, Kirkuk, and Salah al-Din. IOM will provide emergency livelihood services to the most severely affected IDPs living in camps and informal settlements to set the foundations for eventual, voluntary return and to strengthen individual and community resilience.

project_name: Strengthening access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene practices in rural, urban and peri-urban setting of Chimanimani, Chipinge, Buhera, Harare, Epworth, Binga, Kariba, Gokwe North, Gokwe South, Kwekwe and Mt Darwin districts.
project_objective: . Improve access to sufficient water of appropriate quality and quantity to vulnerable communities to fulfil basic needs,                                                                                                                                                                                 . Increase awareness of safe hygiene and sanitation practices, with a focus on participatory health and hygiene education (PHHE) using the school health club and community health club approach,                              . Provide access to critical WASH related Non-food items (NFIs), with a focus on schools to enable continuation of learning and the most vulnerable families in the targeted areas.

project_name: Addressing the needs of Limb Reconstruction patients
project_objective:
Relates to Strategic objective #2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL, and to health cluster objective #1: Ensure the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of essential lifesaving health services to the most vulnerable communities in Gaza and West Bank/EJ, including through health system strengthening, preparedness and community resilience building.

This project will aim to address the urgent needs of Limb Reconstruction patients in Gaza, especially those who suffered from traumatic LR injuries since the start of the Great Return Marches (GRM) events. This category has been neglected by organisations and left for the under-resourced MoH to deal with as these cases require years of treatment and are financially overwhelming. Plus, the skills' set available in Gaza are not able to meet such great demands.

MAP has been active since 2014 establishing the first dedicated LR unit in Palestine, however, this project is designed to meet the urgent needs of the very recent and late-complex limb injuries of the Great Return Marches (GRM) as these far exceed any local capacity that exists in Gaza.

project_name: Provision of life saving drugs and disposables to respond to the emergency medical needs in Gaza
project_objective: As a result of the Great Return March events, the burden on the already overstretched health system has increased to unbearable level leaving it on the verge of collapse where more than 10,000 of injuries needed hospitalization and non-trauma patients suffer from interrupted treatment and health care. However, few organizations like MAP were able to respond immediately, and the level of needs far more exceeds the provided response. Health Cluster indicated that the total funding required for interventions from 30 March until the end of 2018 is US$43.8 million, of which $22.7 million has been contributed to date, leaving a shortfall of $21.1 million. Therefore, MOH has been calling for immediate response from the health organizations working inside Gaza to assist with the provision of urgently needed drugs and disposables in order to be able to save the life of Palestinian patients in Gaza. MAP is planning to purchase a list of essential drugs and disposables to be delivered to Central Drug Stores to ensure the access of trauma and non-trauma patients to the treatment and medical care they need.

project_name: Ecuador - World Food Programme
Peru - Save the Children
Peru - World Vision
Protection of girls and boys in conflict areas in Sudan through quality preventative and remedial interventions
project_objective:
This project is planned to  target conflict affected girls and boys and their families in North and Central Darfur; who have fled from the outbreak of violence in the Jebel Marra (JM) area which started in Jan 2016. The JM areas lies in the center of the Darfur region, bordering the state divisions of Central, South and North Darfur. The region is mainly inhabited by the Fur tribe and has, since 2003, been the primary stronghold of the Sudan Liberation Army (SLA), a Fur-dominated group. It is  the only place in Darfur where an armed opposition group maintains prolonged control over territory and the only area in Darfur to which humanitarian organisations have had no access since 2011.
This will be done through the delivery of quality preventative and remedial interventions to improve response to emergency humanitarian child protection needs in communities affected by conflict. Save the Children (SC) will ensure the provision of timely and rights based child protection services to the most deprived and marginalized girls and boys. These services will include psychosocial support, prevention and response to the needs of child victims of Sexual and Gender Based violence (SGBV), family Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) for the Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC), as well as assistance to child victims of landmines.
To prevent and mitigate child protection risks in communities affected by conflict,; SC will strengthen community based child protection mechanisms in their capacity to prevent and raise awareness around key child protection risks, such as family separation, gender based violence, psychosocial distress, children’s association with armed forces or groups and landmines. SC will invest in capacity building of CP Sub-sector members including the National Council on for Child Welfare and other SC humanitarian partners to ensure the quality of child protection interventions.
In order to reinforce the resilience of communities and strengthen capacity of child protection institutions,; SC will support community based child protection mechanisms and civil society organisations to disseminate information on relevant services and contribute to advocacy and the referral of child protection cases. As part of SGBV (Sexual and Gender Based Violence) eradication programming, SC will engage with men and boys in gender focused prevention work, addressing root causes and changing social norms around gender relations and masculinity.
Gender power relations restricting women's and girls’ possibilities to participate were analyzed in programme activities as domestic workloads, social norms and/or threats of sexual violence restrict their mobility. Accordingly, gender sensitive measures will be adopted to mitigate these programmatic risks including adapting schedules and meeting venues to ensure equitable participation, using single sex discussion groups at the CFS, promoting a girl-friendly space once a week to ensure that adolescent girls are able to participate, adapting case management to the different types of violence faced by boys and girls. It will also include using quotas to ensure equitable participation in the child clubs and CBCPN.
To mainstream gender in this project, the IASC Guidelines for integrating Gender-based Violence interventions in Humanitarian Settings were adopted as follows: there will be a reference document for ensuring quality in planning and coordination and staff will be trained on the guidelines. A SGBV screening of any alternative care facilities to be used for UASC will also be included as a first measure. The project activities were trailered to cater for the needs of girls and boys between the age 5 and 17 years old, after conducting a thorough analysis to the power relation, gender dynamics and accessibility in the selected communities. Children and communities should be consulted to identify the appropriate locations for the construction of the CFSs.

project_name: Complimentary Education in Emergencies support through school meal programs integrated with WASH in Greater Pibor Administrative Area GPAA, South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of the project is to increase enrolment and retention in selected schools through reduced hunger and malnutrition in Greater Pibor Administrative Area GPAA, and facilitate the return to school for children & youth who dropped out because of hunger, forced child labor or recruitment into armed groups. Since 2014, FCA has implemented standard EiE activities such as construction of semi-permanent and temporary learning spaces, teacher capacity building through training, awareness raising activities, PTA/SMS formation & strengthening. In addition, FCA integrates protection and WASH in EiE programs and supports ALP and ECD centres. The proposed school feeding project will integrate nutrition education, WASH in schools and disease prevention.   
Objective 1: Reduced hunger and malnutrition for 2,895 children in eight (8) schools in GPAA.
The proposed objective is reached through provision of on-site school meals, construction of basic school kitchens/stores, and hygiene training for safe handling, preparation, cooking and storage of food. This objective will increase school attendance by lowering the opportunity cost of attending school, and lead to more time spent in school, and towards learning. Schools targeted Pibor, Lekuangole and Gumuruk include Lurnyang, Manyiran, Tangajon, Kavachoch, St. Clement, Gei and Agoy primary school.  
Objective 2: Enhanced awareness on nutrition education and WASH for school governing bodies (SGB), teachers and children. 
The proposed objective is reached through establishment of nutrition clubs to popularize availability, diversity and accessibility & benefits of food values; and capacity support to SMCs/PTAs and youth in nutrition and food security advocacy at community level.  FCA will establish school hygiene clubs & WASH facilities to support messaging on safe use of latrines. This objective will lead to better health and resistance to infectious diseases & illnesses that would keep children from attending school. Better nutrition indirectly improves educational achievement by increasing school attendance.

project_name: JORDAN - ACT Alliance / Finn Church Aid
Protect the basic livelihoods of communities and people acutely affected by protracted crisis to cope with the threats and shocks through cash programming
project_objective: Overall objective of this intervention is to improve food security status for conflict-affected population in the Gaza Strip. The intervention aims at enhancing economic access to food and livelihoods for vulnerable households of young graduates and unskilled laborers by increasing their income as well as improving their skills and quali cations which will increase their independence and recognition within the community. Young graduates and their families will be targeted through creating temporal employment opportunities in civil society organizations (CBOs) and the private sector through a cash for work (CfW) modality. The project target population is 400 young graduates and unskilled laborers from food insecure households taking into consideration targeting female graduates with at least 55% of the targeted graduates and female headed households as the most priority The project aims to create 50,000 paid working days through temporary employment opportunities for target beneficiaries.

project_name: Provision of critical support to health care system.
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to contribute in reduction in morbidity and mortality among the conflict affected IDPs and host communities in the targeted areas of Idleb, Aleppo, Hama and Latakia (administratively supported) in North-western Syria. A total of 346,873 Individuals (men, women, boys and girls) will receive health care through 46 facilities. The project will start on 1st March 2019 and will end on 28th February 2020. The main project components include:

•	Drugs, disposables, dialysis kits provision to 40 PHC, 4 Mobile Emergency unit (MEU) and 2 dialysis centres. 
•	Stipend support to 146 health workers and running cost to 11 facilities (5 PHC, 4 MEU and 2 dialysis centres). 
•	Capacity building (trainings) for 150 health workers and facility management on GBV, protection, inclusion and data management. 

The proposed project will provide support to those people most in need of life-saving and life-sustaining assistance. Specifically, the project will prioritize assistance to people with acute and immediate humanitarian health needs, many of whom have suffered trauma injuries or otherwise lack access to basic life-saving medical-care for both acute and chronic conditions (such as renal failures) that renders them particularly at-risk.

project_name: JORDAN - IRJ
Protection of Palestine Refugees Affected by the Occupation and Forced Displacement in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem).
project_objective:
Objective 1: Increased respect for International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL) and accountability for violations. The project is contributing to the UNRWA strategic objective 2: Palestine refugees maintain access to critical services and are protected from the effects of conflict and violence

project_name: Water, Hygiene and Sanitation (WASH) requirements for Norwegian Refugee Council
Life-saving integrated food security and livelihoods support for Somaliland and Puntland communities
project_objective:
The project is responding to humanitarian needs of drought affected community in target locations of Puntland and Somaliland through cash injection to address the immediate food needs of the people. Cash transfer programming will be used to reach households that are in IPC 3 and above. While focusing on life-saving interventions, the project will also support recovery and resilience building of the people where possible. 

Improving food availability through support to agricultural production in Awdal, and introducing it in Sool and Sanag regions of Somalia is seen as an entry point to diversify pastoral livelihoods of those two regions. This plan involves also supporting communities’ recovery and livelihoods diversification interventions through livestock support with vaccination and treatment and Improving Agricultural Production/Food Security. 

Livestock production was severely affected by the drought leading to substantially reduced herds; which is the country’s prime investment especially in rural communities. The mains reasons leading to the death were water shortages and lack of pasture.  In view of this situation the project will explore fodder production combined with campaigns on livestock vaccination and treatment. These include promotion of carrying capacity for sustained production. These actions will be coupled with Cash for Work activities which will be used for communal asset development linked to crop and animal husbandry. 

In improving agricultural production/ food security, the project will use conservational agriculture model as a climate smart agriculture technology to facilitate regeneration of agricultural production among agro-pastoral households. The beneficiaries will be given seed to improve seed security for the coming farming season. Farmers will be trained in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture on agricultural techniques to obtain optimal yields from their fields. Upon harvesting farmers will be able to reserve part of the harvest as seed for next season. 

In times of shock and more critical food insecurity, Oxfam will utilize multi-purpose cash transfers to meet the immediate emergency needs of at risk communities. More structurally, Oxfam will help to setup mobile early warning on dissemination of national early warning info to communities to enhance preparedness measures.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Vulnerable Populations in Pibor County, Jonglei State, South Sudan.
project_objective:
Under the proposed project, farming inputs and training on better agricultural methods for staple crops and vegetable production will be provided to 5000 vulnerable households (30,000 people). Within this number, 300 female headed households (1,800 people) will be assisted with a cash intervention in addition to the kit mentioned above by virtue of their high CSI scores. At the same time, 1000 fisher folk households (6,000 people) will receive training on better fishing methods and also receive a fishing kit. In total, 6000 households (36,000 people) will be targeted.
The intervention strategy will be based on the livelihood activities of target beneficiaries and aligned to the seasonal calendar. The response plan aims at ensuring that at any given time, household needs are covered. Lean periods and planting seasons should be well covered to discourage consumption of crop seeds or engaging in negative coping practices in order to fulfill household needs.
Livelihood activities and support through this project will be coordinated with the food security cluster at county, state and national level to avoid duplication. Targeting of beneficiaries for this activity will be done based on the Food Consumption Score (FCS) as well as Coping Strategy Index (CSI).
In addition to rebuilding of livelihood assets, proposed activities are intended to have a multiplier effect on improving household dietary intake and livelihood coping capacity. In the short run, income from any of the proposed activities can be used to acquire inputs for other activities in addition to providing for basic household needs.  This will in turn contribute to strengthening the resilience of the target population.
From a protection point of view, in order to combat negative coping strategies, this action proposes to use livelihood activities to attain education and protection objectives. As an entry point, targeting of beneficiaries will be based on the Food Consumption Score (FCS). However, to ensure that households most a risk of resulting to negative coping mechanisms are included in the intervention, the Coping Strategy Index will also be used simultaneously. WFP and cluster approved tools will be used for these analyses.

project_name: Emergency agricultural livelihood support in hard-to-reach areas along the „contact line‟ of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts
