project_name: Projet de prévention de la malnutrition et traitement de la MAM au Lac
project_objective:
La région des lac est située sur les rives du lac Tchad et borde le Niger, le Nigéria et le Cameroun. Cette région est l'une des plus vulnérables au Tchad en raison de problèmes d'accessibilité, du manque de services sociaux de base et de la fréquence élevée de risques naturels et environnementaux, notamment d'inondations et de sécheresses.
L'insécurité alimentaire chronique, l'accès limité à des soins de santé de qualité, la faible couverture vaccinale, l'éducation et les pratiques nutritionnelles inadéquates en matière d'alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant (ANJE) et la pauvreté chronique sont des facteurs qui alimentent les taux de malnutrition élevés dans la région des lacs. Ces facteurs sont exacerbés par le niveau d'insécurité résultant des actes de violence perpétrés par les militants de Boko Haram dans la région, ce qui a entraîné une perturbation généralisée des structures communautaires et des déplacements massifs de population.
Plusieurs évaluations et études ont été réalisées dans les trois districts sanitaires où IMC met en œuvre des activités. Bien que certaines montrent des améliorations des indicateurs de santé et de nutrition, de nombreux facteurs entravent l'amélioration des résultats en matière de santé et de nutrition. L'enquête nationale SMART menée en septembre 2018 a mis en évidence une prévalence de la malnutrition aiguë globale de 10,5% et la prévalence de la MAS de 1,8% dans la région du lac.

project_name: Projet de prévention de la malnutrition et traitement de la MAM dans les camps de réfugiés
project_objective:
a malnutrition aiguë demeure un problème de santé publique majeur au Tchad avec une prévalence de malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG) estimée à 13,5%, très proche du seuil critique fixé par l’OMS et, avec une prévalence de la malnutrition aiguë sévère (MAS) estimée à 4,0%. On note de fortes disparités régionales avec douze (15) régions sur les vingt-trois (23) que compte le pays, ayant une prévalence de la MAG dépassant le seuil critique de 15% fixé par l’OMS et ou MAS au dela des seuils d'urgence. Dans les camps de refugies, les 6 camps du nord ont des prévalences au dela des seuils d'urgence de l'OMS. Le PAM a prévu de fournir des services de nutrition pour preventir la malnutrition chez les enfants et les femmes vivant au niveau des 6 camps de refuciés où la prevalence de la malnutrition dépasse le seuil d'urgence.  La provision de suppléments nutritionnels permettra d'améliorer les apports nutritionnels des groupes vulnérables. Un important vollet de sensibilisation sera associés à la distributrition des suppléments nutritionnels en vue d'améliorer les pratiques alimentaires chez les communautés ciblées.

Le traitement de la malnutrition aiguë s’inscrit dans le cadre global de la prise en charge intégrée de la malnutrition aiguë qui comporte d’autre composantes telles que la mobilisation communautaire pour l’identification et le suivi des cas de malnutrition et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère en ambulatoire et en hospitalisation.

project_name: JORDAN - United Nations Population Fund

project_name: Provision of GBV services to IDPs, Returnees and Host Community across Iraq
project_objective: Various forms of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) continues to be perpetrated against women and girls, in particular in the current protracted humanitarian environment, with a particular exacerbated focus on displaced women and girls and returnees. In seeking access to safe areas, women and girls are at heightened risk of sexual harassment, abuse and exploitation. Similar violations are perpetrated in camp settings, particularly where armed actors are present, and in temporary settlements which fail to provide a sufficient protective environment. In displacement, many women and girls experience high rates of physical, sexual and mental abuse, and denial of resources and opportunities. Negative coping strategies such as early marriage and survival sex have become more commonplace. The provision of GBV prevention and response activities is critical at all stages of the displacement cycle, as service gaps pose grave risks to the safety and dignity of women and girls. With the continuous movements of displaced people and returnees during 2018, it goes without saying that women and girls still face vulnerabilities related to their access to minimum services and the additional GBV risks. When the return movement is accelerated, it is important to ensure proper follow-up of open GBV cases in the return areas and to support establishing a proper protection environment for women and girls. This necessitates strengthening of existing GBV services as well as establishment of new GBV services in retaken/return areas where IDPs and vulnerable groups are concentrated. Through this project, UNFPA and its Implementing Partners will provide holistic prevention and response to women and girls, in particular survivors of GBV. By involving the whole community including men and boys, UNFPA adopts an inclusive approach that will lead to long-term changes for IDPs, Returnees and Host community members. Interventions will be in continuity of the ones in 2018, in particular in hot areas as designed through the HRP process.

project_name: Emergency response, recovery of livelihood assets to protect and strengthen Resilience of vulnerable populations in Somalia
project_objective: The project focuses on the delivery of basic lifesaving and protection/restoration of livelihoods of the target population as well as community resilience building activities in Gedo Bay and Togdeer regions with a special focus on all locations with high prevalence of malnutrition (GAM/SAM), including IDP camps and host communities that are in IPC 3 & 4. This will be done through unconditional cash and fresh food vouchers transfer to improve immediate access to food and reduce risk of malnutrition among vulnerable girls, pregnant and lactating women, boys and men as well as the provision of livelihood specific and seasonally appropriate inputs to protect/restore livelihoods and strengthen their resilience to current and future shocks.

project_name: Integrated Education in Emergencies response for  IDP children, learners with disability and vulnerable host community out of school children in Baidoa,Dinsor, and Wajid districts in Bay and Bakool Regions -South Central Somalia
project_objective: This project aims at providing access to education for marginalized children from IDP communities, children with disability and vulnerable host community children who face challenges in accessing school. Through sustained education campaigns  that will also advocate for girls and children with disability ,  out of school children will be identified and enrolled in school. With the proposed infrastructure support that includes rehabilitation and equipment of classrooms, construction of gender segregated WASH facilities and hygiene campaigns, supply of learning kits and school materials, provision of school feeding and clean water to IDP learners, the project purposes to remove key costly barriers to education for these marginalized children,to provide a conducive learning environment that enables them to attend and progress in school. Girls will be specifically targeted with menstrual hygiene education as part of lifeskills and provided with dignity kits to mitigate any absenteeism  due to their periods.As part of durable solutions and resilience building, the IDP schools will linked to public schools for transition of learners,and to promote integration of IDP learners into the national education system. Using an integrated child sensitive and gender responsive approach that puts child protection and psycho social support at the center of  activities, the project aims to build the resilience of the learners by providing them with key lifeskills information for their personnel well being and social interaction. Further, the project goes beyond access to also incorporate quality components that ensure meaningful and positive learning outcomes out of the learning process. Teachers will be trained on basic pedagogy skills, learner testing and participatory classroom instruction for effective learning,and the teachers code of conduct enforced in all target schools. The teachers  will also be closely supervised and mentored to improve their practice, and also assisted to establish structured student testing, based on the national curriculum timelines to inform students learning. The CEC's  will be trained on their roles and responsibilities, including child protection principles and standards in emergencies, because of changes in the membership that could have arisen in the last year (2017)while follow up support will be given to the CEC's in the target schools in Wajid, as they have already been trained. The MoE and respective district education stakeholders will also be trained on disaster risk management and response and education coordination during emergency aimed at ensuring effective and coordinated education response that minimizes disruption to learning during crises. Schools will  also establish children support centers and clear referral pathways for learners facing protection issues.  INTERSOS and the Ministry of Education in the respective district will conduct joint school monitoring to determine the quality of the teaching and learning process and provide feedback to the teachers and CEC's on areas of improvement. The project will also use its internal monitoring structures to track the quality and progress of activity implementation, ,as well as using the cluster based monthly 4W matrix. School structures and the ministry of education will also be mobilized to sustain the schools upon project phase out.

project_name: Enhancing youth resilience focusing on female heading households through supporting entrepreneurship and civic engagement initiatives

project_name: Provision of comprehensive and lifesaving Reproductive Health services
project_objective:
The interventions planned with this project will ensure timely access to essential live saving and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services to Rohingya refugees and a host community in ukhiya and Teknaf Sub districts of Cox’s bazar district. The project aims at addressing the priority sexual and reproductive Health include ensuring the minimum initial service package (MISP) for reproductive health in crisis, and now expanding to comprehensive SRH for the affected population. Although some partners are providing the minimum initial service package of sexual and reproductive health, access to essential comprehensive reproductive, maternal and new-born health services remain a major concern. 
Safe access to 24-hour rapid transfer of all life-threatening emergencies is in need of expansion. This is of particular concern with obstetric and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) conditions of women and adolescent girls to prevent maternal and gender-based violence morbidity and mortality the project will support the emergency referral hubs. The project will also ensure 24/7 lifesaving services (EmONC and support CEmONC services in selected referral facilities) and strengthen referral pathways as well as maintaining continues supply of life saving SRH commodities including family planning services. 
Based on available data an estimated less than 32% of deliveries among the refugees occurred in facilities which may reflect a combination of both demand and access issues. So the project will employ several approaches to increase service uptake which includes:
•	Strengthening community based SRH services and behavioural change approaches by ensuring that quality SRH information and services are available near the communities.
•	Scale up quality midwifery led care across the camps by providing mentorship support to the service providers. 
•	Attract women to deliver in health facilities using evidence based financial and non-financial incentives, which the project will cover
•	Address issues such as obstetric fistulas and the comprehensive SRH services 
The project will also address SRH needs for high-risk and special need populations (e.g. sex workers, Adolescent Sexual Reproductive Health and disabled) which are currently yet to be addressed systematically and need to be integrated into the overall reproductive health care response. 
The project will also ensure SRH and GBV services are provided in an integrated manner. 
Due to the temporary nature of facility infrastructure which poses a challenge to longer-term continuity of services, as the infrastructures degrades the project will reinforce, repair, and maintain vital sexual and reproductive health structures. 
Continued support to the SRH Sub Sector coordination to provide high quality technical assistance to ensure comprehensive SRH information and services are of international standards and on par with nationals.
The project will directly target 406,108 population including women of reproductive age, men,boys and girls and high risk and special need (Key) populations.

project_name: Lifesaving support to the Conflict and Floods affected IDPs in Marka, Wanla Weyn and Qoryooley of Lower Shabelle through in kind distribution of Shelter and NFI's Kits.

project_name: Education Program for Vulnerable School Aged Children (Boys & Girls) in Banadir and Lower Shabelle regions of Somalia
project_objective:
Severity of drought and flood disasters and prolonged conflicts have worsened the living conditions of the populations, particularly internally displaced persons (IDPs) and impoverished households in Banadir and Lower Shabelle regions of Somalia. Most of the children in IDP settlements in these regions are currently out of school. There are challenges including funding gaps and insufficient humanitarian responses in these areas. The learning resources are in short supply and number of teachers left teaching work because of a lack of salaries or incentives. Some displacement settlements have no schools, and/or if there is one, it is a private school that charges tuition fees on children, that IDP households and low income families cannot afford. Instead, many parents tend to send their children (girls and boys) to the market and streets to do hazardous jobs such as collecting Khat endings (garabo), cleaning houses and washing clothes for other families to contribute to earning a sustainable living for their poor families.
The proposed program complements Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan 2019. It is intended to contribute to the Education Cluster Strategic Objectives. This project will focus on four main components with the purpose of improving access to protective and life-saving quality education for 3,000 school children (1,400 girls and 1,600 boys) in Banadir (Daynile and Kaxda Districts) and Lower Shabelle (Afgoye and Wanlweyn Districts) regions of Somalia. The first component will concentrate on increasing the number of the marginalized, out of school children (boys and girls) enrolled and retained in constructed/rehabilitated schools with gender responsive latrines and safe drinking water taps. The second component will put emphasis on the establishment or the renovation of primary schools with appropriate gender responsive sanitation facilities for out of school children (1,400 girls and 1,600 boys). The third component will be aimed at providing life-saving school feeding rations, supplies and learning materials to 3,000 school children (1,400 girls and 1,600 boys). And the fourth component will intend to develop teachers’ professional competence and CECs capacity to improve the quality of teaching and learning in the schools, to increase awareness on protection of children’s rights and also to promote school management and supervision skills for 95 teachers (30 female and 65 male) and for 75 persons of community education committees (45 female and 30 male) at primary schools in the target districts.

project_name: Provision of emergency reproductive, maternal, new born and child health services to crisis affected populations in Somalia
project_objective: The project is to provide life-saving emergency healthcare to an estimated 70,000 crises affected beneficiaries in Bay, Bakool and Hiraan regions. This action will deliver comprehensive reproductive health care to women of reproductive age among the target beneficiaries and promotion of health seeking behaviour including adoption of preventive practices through campaigns, health and hygiene education sessions. Emphasis will be on maternal, neonatal and child health including emergency immunization to the host communities and Internally Displaced People (IDPs). This action will focus on provision of both preventive and curative health services at primary level integrated with nutrition and WASH activities to provide holistic and integrated support. Through deployment of trained health workers including midwives and community health workers in facilities and mobile teams, essential primary care services including treatment of common childhood illnesses, as well as emergency obstetric and neonatal care for pregnant and lactating women will be provided. HIDIG an actor in the target regions will leverage on existing support & activities to ensure the gains made in the post-drought response are not rolled back. Building the capacity of health workers through training on Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmONC) will be done to equip health workers with the required skills to deliver quality health care services to the affected population. The project with the technical guidance of WHO and the Health Cluster will also integrate surveillance and emergency preparedness in the program so that enough steps are taken in ensuring prompt response. The project will also contribute to strengthening early warning disease surveillance through weekly submission of eDEW reports from all the functional supported health facilities. Referral system for patients seeking secondary healthcare services to Baidoa and Beletweyne regional referral hospitals will be strengthened focusing on pregnant women requiring emergency services, and GBV cases referred to secondary care immediately.

project_name: Provision of emergency and sustainable life- saving WASH assistance to the vulnerable drought and AWD affected IDPs and host communities in Nugal and Mudug regions of - Somalia.
project_objective:
The proposed project is complementary to ongoing KAALO WASH project  in Nugaal  region in Puntland and to response the existing WASH gaps to drought affected people in Puntland, KAALO proposes to provide WASH interventions and resilience strengthening to the target groups men, women and children and institutional facilities during this critical period of water shortage and Acute Water Diarrhea (AWD) risks in providing safe water through water voucher, constructing/rehabilitating WASH infrastructures for sustained access. Hygiene awareness, training on management & maintenance and Disaster Risk Reduction targeting  affected people with equal access to boys, girls, men and women., 
The committee need further training on  hygiene and sanitation as well as distribution of sanitation tools. Sensitization within members of WASH committees are needed, community education activities on hygiene and proper use of latrines etc. need more emphasis, KAALO intends to complement this with  the ongoing WASH project to cover all the existing gaps in the  targeted areas. The project will be implemented six villages in Nugaal and Mudug region covering eyl, Garowe,  burtinle and Galkacyo districts.
Accountability : KAALO will develop elaborate beneficiary complain and feedback tool. Project beneficiaries and stakeholders will be given 1 day workshop on how to use the complaint /feedback system to enhance transparency and accountability. Community ownership of the project will be done through formation of structures such as Beneficiary Representatives, WASH Committees, and CHPs (consisting of women and men). 
implementation  plan : KAALO will recruit experienced WASH project staff that will ensure effective community participatory approach in project planning, implementation & management. The WASH Manager will be responsible overall the project implementation while the WASH Engineer will be responsible for the design of the rehabilitation/construction works and ensure the quality of the work is standardized. 
Disaster risk reduction : This project objective is to improve WASH sectors resilience to emergencies and disasters while also covering the urgent needs of affected people. The project will invest on improving WASH infrastructure through rehabilitation/ construction of strategic priority boreholes and increase the capacity of WASH committee and staff on disaster risk reduction.

project_name: WoS: Strengthening and provision of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for conflict-affected populations in Syria.
project_objective:
Through this intervention, UNFPA will continue to execute its goals for the reduction of maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality as well as the provision of medical assistance and care to survivors of GBV. This will be achieved by ensuring (a) the availability, access to and utilization of integrated quality SRH services and information for women, men, girls and boys; (b) building the capacity of health workers and community health workers; (c) reactivate and activate services in areas where no SRH services are in place; (d) ensure availability of essential equipment’s, medicines and supplies for delivery of SRH services and family planning.

UNFPA will take a Whole of Syria (WoS) approach with implementation taking place from Damascus as well as cross-border services from Turkey and Iraq, thereby achieving a country-wide response. All 13 Syrian governorates will be targeted (Hama, Al-Hassakeh, Aleppo, Quneitra , Rural Damascus, Dar'a, Raqqa, Sweidaa, Damascus, Homs, Latakia, Quneitra and Deir-Ez-Zor) with the possibility to shift modality of response across implementing hubs, when needed. Vulnerable population groups in need to be targeted will include: Women and girls of reproductive age, Internally Displaced Population (IDP), host communities and returnees, adolescents as well as people living with disability (PwD).

The following key objectives will be pursed:
(1)	Increasing access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable health services for those most vulnerable and in need: 
•	Increasing access to primary health care through the provision of essential primary health services to cover the health care needs of vulnerable populations, including Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH).
•	Improving access to secondary and tertiary health care for high risk pregnancy, emergency obstetric and newborn care (EmONC) cases, and acute cases which cannot access treatment in the area in which they reside, particularly rural areas.
•	Strengthening and consolidating medical supply chains, ensuring availability of safe and quality medicines for essential primary health care, obstetric care, infectious diseases including HIV to prevent transmission from mother to child and family planning methods. Pre-positioning of emergency supply stocks at warehouse and health facility level in line with contingency scenarios for reduced access and increased level of hostilities requiring RH kits.
•	Supporting essential repairs, rehabilitation and equipping of health facilities providing public and specialized health services, in particular in areas of most acute need where the resumption of basic health care services will have the greatest life-saving impact, as well as facilities that receive referrals from areas of acute need.

(2)	Strengthening health sector coordination and health information systems, with an emphasis on enhancing protection and increasing access to health services and continue  coordination within and across hubs, including thorough joint contingency and preparedness planning for changes in context.

(3)	Engage in activities that support continuity of care, strengthening of community resilience, and response to IDP movements and shifts in control; in addition to ensure proper community and beneficiaries participation during designing, planning and implementation of SRH activities all over the country.

UNFPA will continue to monitor the implementation of these activities based on the five principles of accountability to affected populations as well as UNFPA’s global results-based monitoring framework. This will ultimately help to ensure quality, compliance and the identification of gaps and achievements, for lessons learned as well as corresponding corrective actions to be taken.

project_name: Improved Resilience Through WASH in Blue Nile and West Darfur (IRWA)
project_objective: ADRA proposes to work with IDPs and host communities in the following localities: ElKurmuk, Al-Geissan, Bao in White Nile and West Darfur a ADRA’s approach is to compliment the local partners’ food assistance programs through interventions focused in WASH. Intervention 1: WASH remains the most critical area of need for this program. The focus of this intervention will be the prevention of waterborne disease, thus leading to the protection of health. The project will continue to support the Phase 1 villages in Phase 2 by increasing access to safe water sources by simultaneously rehabilitating and treating the existing water sources to improve water quality, making it safe for human consumption. The project will also continue to promote good hygiene and sanitation practices to reduce transmission of waterborne and fecal-oral diseases. It is imperative that disaster-affected people have necessary information, knowledge and understanding to prevent water- and sanitation-related diseases .

project_name: Assistance and Recovery to Affected Population in Darfur, Kordofan and Kassala
project_objective:
Purpose: Provide safe and clean water, adequate sanitation facilities; ensure access to quality primary health care facilities; preventive and curative nutritional interventions and income earning opportunities. 
The project will work in an integrated manner to address the WASH, health, nutrition and FSL needs of the affected community to save lives and reduce unnecessary human suffering through reduced morbidity and mortality and life free from violence. 
CIS with its national NGO partners and sectoral ministries will support disaster affected and vulnerable people in the targeted areas of East Darfur, South Darfur, Kassala, South and West Kordofan. The aim of integrated sectors is to contribute to the immediate life-saving needs for adequate and safe services and reduction of morbidity and mortality among IDPs, returnees and affected host communities of women, girls, men and boys. This will be done through improving water and sanitation services, linking to health and nutrition facilities for synergistic impact through mobilizing communities for individual and common efforts. 
WASH activities will mainly focus ensure adequate and safe water supply, provision of acceptable sanitation facilities through rehabilitation and construction of facilities as decided by the community and sector partners. The WASH activities will be integrated to nutritional prevention and curative actions and community based health response mechanisms. Health activities will include delivery of basic health packages of primary health care services, medical supplies, expand and maintain disease surveillance, reproductive health and emergency obstetrics. Nutritional interventions will include the full package of CMAM and IYCF services in 20 CMAM sites for provision of CMAM and SAM services. FSL interventions will include support to targeted families that experience malnutrition, food insecurity and have special needs and also capability to engage in income earning opportunities to enable families’ resilience.  Agricultural and livestock based and off farm income generating activities are planned by the project.

project_name: Increasing access of vulnerable women to safe and secure shelters through shelter rehabilitation and winterization assistance
project_objective:
The proposed action falls under the 2018-2020 HRP strategic objective 2 “the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”. Specifically, the project will support and enhance the coping capacity of vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns.

The action will provide emergency assistance to acutely vulnerable households living in substandard shelters in Middle Area governorate (Gaza Strip). The action ensures their access to adequate and safe shelters and strengthens their capacity to cope with future shocks through a community-based approach.  In total, 700 households (3,920 beneficiaries at households’ level) will be assisted, through the urgent rehabilitation of 200 shelters and the provision of 500 emergency winter kits to beneficiaries for whom a full upgrade is not possible, thus contributing to the Country Strategic Objective 3 “the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”.

The project design endorses all of the Shelter Cluster recommendations, in particular by providing a tailored combination of modalities to maximize impact on beneficiaries while fostering ownership and resilience through a demanding community based self-implementation approach. 

Eventually, the project will be developed based on ACTED and MAAN (partner) experience in emergency shelter rehabilitation in Gaza since 2016. The project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA), with a specific focus on women and vulnerable groups, and a strong Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) component. In particular, beneficiaries will be heavily involved in the action through community-based empowered committees, and a comprehensive Complaint Response Mechanism will be deployed. Gender principles will be mainstreamed during the action and Committees will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases with a particular focus given to women and children issues such as related to GBV. An ACTED protection officer will be a focal point of the committees in order to receive and follow-up on cases.

project_name: Documentation and protection of victims of IHL/IHRL violations and securing access to medical care outside Gaza
project_objective: Monitoring and documentation of IHL/IHRL violations in ARA, providing casualties with legal counseling and interventions, and securing travel permits to patients refereed to treatment facilities outside Gaza.

project_name: Provision of life-saving WASH interventions to drought, floods and conflict-affected host communities, IDPs and returnees in South Central Somalia.
project_objective: This project aims at providing access to temporary and sustained water supply, safe sanitary facilities and increased awareness on safe hygiene practices to IDPs, host communities and returnees affected by drought, floods and conflict in Middle Shabelle, Hiraan, Kismayo, Baidoa and IDP settlements in Banadir. Water vouchers will be provided to 20,500 people and 23 strategic water points will be constructed/rehabilitated. The water sources will be located 30m away from latrines to avoid contamination. Dewatering of 30 wells and application of shock chlorination will be done in flood-affected areas.  To strengthen community ownership and ensure sustainability of WASH assets 50 water management committee members (50% women) will be trained on operation and maintenance. The project staff and WASH committee members will also be trained on DRR and protection mainstreaming. 97 gender-sensitive latrines with hand-washing facilities, raised to avoid flooding and fitted with locks from the inside to curb GBV will be constructed in IDP camps, schools and health/nutrition centers. CLTS approach will be introduced where no latrines will be constructed. Community members particularly women and girls will be consulted in the siting and design of WASH facilities.  5000 hygiene kits will be distributed to targeted high-risk families i.e. families with malnourished children and affected by AWD. 600 hygiene promoters will be trained in the PHAST method and will carry out community hygiene campaigns. WOCCA will continuously monitor the Shabelle river and disseminate early warning and hygiene messages through radio and SMS when floods are imminent. Sensitization meetings will be held at the inception of the project with all project stakeholders including groups at risk of exclusion to inform them about the project objectives, scope, beneficiary selection criteria, and beneficiary entitlement and roles. Accountability to the affected population will be enhanced through the provision of a feedback hotline to beneficiaries where they can provide feedback and complaints. To ensure quality in the project outputs the project staff will continuously monitor and report on project indicators. WOCCA will also share GPS coordinates of all WASH structures and monthly project reports with the WASH cluster and donor. Signing off and handing over of WASH structures to beneficiaries upon completion will be done through community elders, government officials and religious leaders. WOCCA will also adhere to the principles of ""Do no harm"" through not creating any partial, nepotism, conflict-oriented and sensitive issues within the project beneficiaries.

project_name: WASH assistance for herders and farmers in Area C and vulnerable families in Hebron city’s H2 area, West Bank
project_objective:
The proposed project will target the most vulnerable families in Area C and in Hebron’s H2 area. These groups suffer from no, or limited, access to water and sanitation services due to Israeli restrictions on construction and development in the area. This makes them particularly vulnerable to the threat of forced displacement. The target communities are farming and herding families dependant on livestock and agricultural activities to maintain their livelihoods and, as such, heavily reliant on water availability, quality and affordability. Lack of water has forced families to adopt negative coping mechanisms such as reducing their consumption to an average of less than 30 l/d/c (Area C Water Master Plan 2017) depending on unsafe water resources or reducing their expenditure on basic needs such as health and education to afford the high cost of water.

(1) By constructing and rehabilitating water networks, filling points and household cisterns, the proposed project will decrease the target communities’ dependency on trucked water as well as deter them from sourcing unsafe water. 

(2) The project will also improve the communities’ access to sanitation facilities through the construction and provision of household WASH facilities such as latrines and plastic tanks. Families often disregard these facilities and prioritise other basic needs such as food and water. This negative copying mechanism has left many households in poor health, hygiene, privacy and dignity conditions. 

(3) Thus, to complement these activities, AAH will also carry out training and awareness workshops on subjects ranging from hygiene promotion to water saving techniques and cistern management.

Ultimately, by mitigating the effects of the Israeli occupation on water access and thus improving the target communities’ livelihood prospects, the proposed project will reduce their exposure to forced displacement and provide them with the means to show resilience in the face of these challenges. The proposed intervention ensures protection mainstreaming as it is guided by protection principles and considers safety and dignity, meaningful access, accountability as well as participation and empowerment.

project_name: Provision of Specialized Mental Health and Free Telephone Counseling (HL) Services to Women, Men, Boys and Girls Affected by Violence in the Great March of Return at Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The project of "" Provision of Specialized Mental Health and Free Telephone Counseling (HL) Services to Women, Men, Boys and Girls Affected by Violence in the Great March of Return at Gaza Strip"" aims at contributing to alleviate the effects of the Israeli occupation practices through delivery of quality specialized mental health services to the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys who are affected in the context of the Great March of Return (GMR) and living in the most affected and marginalized socio-economically vulnerable and under-served communities. The project has three main interventions as follows:
A1)	Provision of specialized mental health services for 400 children (boys and girls) and 600 adults/parents (women and men) who have displayed symptoms of severe psychosocial distress. By using the existing referral system, those cases will be detected and referred by the case managers and psychosocial support staff working in family centers and Child Protection and MHPSS networks. Additionally, other cases will be detected through structured activities implemented through other venues such as GCMHP’s community centers and their field teams. The clinical services will be provided by specialized multi-disciplinary team including psychiatrists, psychologists, psychiatric nurses, social workers, and rehabilitation specialists at GCMHP three community centers located in Gaza city, Deir El Balah and Khanyounis. Therapy plans include psychotherapy, play therapy, medication, family counseling and home visits. GCMHP has procedures that offer practical guidance and assistance in taking protection issues seriously in the workplace, and to make staff aware of their roles and responsibilities while interacting directly with women and children. 
A 2) Provision of free telephone counseling (Hot Line) service for 400 persons including children (girls and boys) and adults/parents (women and men) who couldn’t reach mental health centres due to economic or social barriers. Through this service, the telephone counselors will provide psycho education, individual and family counseling, and also detect and refer children and adults with severe symptoms to GCMHP community centres to receive specialized mental health services including medications if necessary. This service helps overcome stigma attached to mental health problems. This service provides another differentiated aspect, where some cases will be detected and referred to legal and protection services provided by other service providers in Gaza Strip. GCMHP through its awareness raising activities including (public meetings, radio spots and programs, street billboards, publications, etc,) enhances access of the target group to this service.
A3) Provide training courses to 50 child protection workers (50% women) who are working in the field of child protection and MHPSS sector. The training topics will address the most common disorders among children and adults, and detection and referral skills. 
A4) Produce one fact sheet, including gender and age-disaggregated data, to document trends/patterns of psychological disorders among those assisted to be shared with all stakeholders to help improve the prevention and protection response and for joint coordinated advocacy messages and actions.

project_name: Ogossagou Cash Emergency Response
project_objective:
This emergency response project will provide cash assistance to 374 households of the communities of Ogossagou Peulh, Ogossagou Dogon, Guiwagou and Wélingara for a three month period to enable surviving households of the Ogossagou massacre and surrounding affected communities to cover their basic needs and survive the onset of rainy season. The massacre of Ogossagou took place on 23 March 2019, and saw 161 people killed, 410 houses burnt, 80 granaries destroyed and large amounts of village livestock carried away. 374 households (2,244 people) were seriously affected including IDPs, returnees, village, neighbor and host communities) and are living in dire conditions. Needs include immediate need for shelter and NFIs, health and nutrition, food security, rebuilding of livelihoods, protection, and education. The project will allow the most affected households cover their basic needs while waiting for specialized agencies to intervene, subject to a detailed needs assessment and available funding. 
The project will also benefit 186 female-headed households, and in some cases households of up to 14 people due to the skewed demographics and victims of the massacre. The immediate survivors and surrounding population are in an extremely vulnerable situation, subject to worsening security conditions, ongoing exodus of people in need not able to access relief as well as complete obliteration of livelihood means and income-generating activities.

project_name: Protect the Health and Safety of IDPs and Hardship Cases through Emergency Shelter Responses
project_objective:
The project addresses critical protection concerns of 271 families including IDPs families and other families who are at risk of displacement due to not being in a position to afford their rent. Severe socioeconomic vulnerabilities associated with poor access to safe and adequate shelter had resulted in a critical humanitarian situation for 353 women (18-59), 322 men (18-59), 417 girls (under 18), 408 boys (under 18), and 14 elderlies (above 59)). The project target includes 29 women headed households, 16 disabled headed households, and 8 elderly headed households.

This action is in line with the assigned objectives of the Shelter Cluster; objective 1: “Displaced populations are provided support that mitigates immediate harm and ensures adequate and safe temporary shelter solutions”, and objective 2: “Vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns are supported to meet basic needs and enhance their coping capacity”.

The project aims at:
1.	Providing for the protection of vulnerable internally displaced families who are living in inadequate shelters through the provision of safe temporary shelter solutions, and adequate NFIs.
2.	Providing for the protection of hardship cases, who are at risk of losing tenancy due to not being in a position to afford their rent, through provision of temporary shelter assistance, and adequate NFIs.
The Interventions include:
1.	Provision of temporary shelter assistance to IDPs from previous conflicts and rely on the TSCA to pay the rental accommodation. (Target: 165 families of IDPs including 196 women (18-59), 192 men (18-59), 244 girls (under 18), 239 boys (under 18), 10 elderlies (above 59)).
2.	Provision of shelter assistance to households at risk of displacements due to economic deterioration and salary cuts. (Target: 106 families including 157 women (18-59), 130 men (18-59), 173 girls (under 18), 169 boys (under 18), and 4 elderlies (above 59)).
3.	To support the targeted families to be more prepared for the winter weather conditions through the distribution of winterized NFI kits. (Target: 271 families, including 353 women (18-59), 322 men (18-59), 417 girls (under 18), 408 boys (under 18), and 14 elderlies (above 59)).

project_name: Accountability for the victims of IHL and IHRL violations during the great march of return in the ARA.
project_objective:
The main objectives of this project is seeking accountability by providing legal interventions on behalf of victims of Israeli attacks occurred in the context of the great march of return that is taking place  in the access restricted areas and also to strengthen monitoring, verification and documentation of the possible IHR/IHRL violations including attacks on health staff and other protected and/or vulnerable groups in the Gaza borders in addition to enhance access to medical care for the victims outside Gaza and in the special context of peaceful demonstrations in the Gaza Borders.
Those objectives are directly linked to Humanitarian Response Plan Country Level Strategic Objective 1: The rights of Palestinians under occupation are protected in accordance with International Humanitarian Law, IHL, and International Human Rights Law, IHRL, and linked to strategic result statement 1 of the Protection Cluster: 1. Increased respect for International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights Law and Accountability for Violations 
The project will be implemented by the Palestinian Center for Human Rights –PCHR, and it will last for 12 months starting from 1st January, 2019.
The activities of the project will vary between legal aid for the victims of IHR/IHRL violations in ARA, Monitoring and documentation, reporting of the violations in the border areas and also providing legal aid to address the freedom of movement restrictions impeding injuries and patients from receiving treatment outside Gaza.

project_name: Responding to Protection Needs of Vulnerable Children in the Gaza Strip through Child Protection Case Management System
project_objective: Since March 2018, the Gaza Strip has been witnessing a progressive deterioration of the political, social and security environments. This situation has been contributing towards volatility in the security context, as well as for a rise of the instability levels in Gaza. Furthermore, since 30 March 2018, it was observed that there was a significant increase in the number of demonstrations under what is called the ""Great March of Return"". Since March 2018, demonstrations are taking place at several border areas, East of Gaza Strip on daily/weekly basis. The participation of children in the demonstrations exposes children to different kinds of risk, including the risk of being injured or even killed. According to the OCHA (As of Oct. 2018), 38 children (36 boys and 2 girls) were killed and 4250 were injured by Israeli occupation fire since the beginning of the Great March of Return, along Gaza's borders. Recently (Oct 2018), OCHA has identified providing mental health and psychosocial support to children affected by violence in the context of the Great March of Return as well as those whose parents or close family members are directly affected as a key humanitarian response. Along with providing child protection services for children who have protection concerns, Tdh has been providing child protection services to injured children during the Great March of Return. So far, about 100 of injured children (99% boys) have benefited from child protection case management and more than 120 children (99% boys) benefited from structured PSS. This project is a continuation of Tdh intervention targeting injured children and their families across the Gaza Strip and children who have protection concerns. The project aims to target 8900 beneficiaries, including 900 children.  The proposed activities will include responsive, remedial, and environment-building child protection activities to 250 recently injured children and 400 children (200 boys and 200 girls) who have recently lost parents or close family members, and 250 children who have protection concerns. The main child protection activities will include, but not limited to, structured psychosocial support, psychological first aid, protection case management, individual and group counseling sessions, and referral to specialized health and mental health services as needed. Additionally, under this Action, awareness sessions on how to deal with traumatized children- victims of the current situation will be conducted targeting 8000 members, including families who have injured cases and schools' staff, and staff of CBOs dealing with injured cases.  In coordination with the line ministries, the implementing partners and FSS, this project will also provide cash assistance support for 200 families of injured children that face additional concerns to support them in the care of children. The targeted beneficiaries, including children and adults from different age groups, including seniors were involved in the design of the project, including the proposed activities. Additionally, both men and women from different targeted localities were involved in the project through identifying the needs and activities. During the implementation, beneficiaries will be involved in monitoring the project activities.  The activities of the project are tailored according specific needs of children, taking into accounts their gender and their age groups.

project_name: Emergency Response Teams
project_objective:
PCDCR seeks to respond to emergency protection, and psychosocial needs of GMR injured individuals and their families in Gaza, Khanyounis and North Governorates and to reintegrate them in their community. When designing the project, PCDCR conducted several discussions with CP and MHPWG. It will continue coordination with CPWG, and other current service providers through the implementation of the project to avoid overlapping and duplication in the interventions or targeted beneficiaries.    
PCDCR will form three emergency response teams-ERTs; each consists of two counselors and a case manager. The ERTs will be ready to respond to protection, and psychosocial needs of GMR injured individuals (adults and children) and their families. The teams will conduct 1500 assessment home visits for GMR injured individuals aiming to assess their different needs. Then, the teams will conduct regular home visits along the project period to respond to the identified needs of each patient of 1500 injured individuals. The teams will provide different psychosocial and protection services as follows. Structured psychosocial support services will be provided for 1500 injured individuals and 1500 of their families including: 1) psychosocial first aid sessions for 450 injured children and their families (420 boys, 30 girls); 2) psychosocial group counseling for 225 injured children (210 boys, 15 girls) and 675 injured adults (625 males, 50 females); 3) individual counseling for 150 injured children (140 boys, 10 girls) and 450 injured adults (420 males, 30 females); 4) group therapy sessions for 37 injured male adults and 8 injured boys with disabilities; 5) stress management sessions for 225 women (mothers and wives of injured individuals); and 6) reintegration of injured individuals within their families and community through 100 groups awareness sessions for 1500 families (200 men, 1300 women). Additionally, to respond to multi sectorial needs of injured individuals including homes’ adaptation and shelter needs, case management and referral services will be provided for 30 injured children (27 boys, 3 girls) and 90 injured adults (83 males, 7 females). 

PCDCR is committed to the five levels of citizen participation and engagement in the different stages of the project management cycle. When identifying the targeted communities, PCDCR took in consideration the statistics of MOH about injured individuals and their families and coordinated with protection cluster to avoid overlapping with other service providers. Through assessing the needs and priorities of the targeted groups (injured individuals and families of people killed or injured), PCDCR applied the first and second levels of citizen participation “to inform” and “to consult” through conducting interviews and focus groups with injured individuals. Also, PCDCR applied the third level “to involve” through enabling the target groups and other CBOs in the targeted communities to participate in the design of the project activities and interventions based on their identified needs. Additionally, PCDCR will apply the fourth and fifth levels of ""to collaborate, and to empower"" in the implementation of the project through forming 3 local follow up and support committees from 30 community members including women, men, youth and elderly people. These committees will participate effectively in implementing and following up the project activities, and they will have influential role in monitoring and evaluating the activities. They will share their feedback, comments and opinions with the project staff and partner CBOs to improve the quality of the project. 
To enhance accountability, PCDCR will conduct two meetings with beneficiaries in the targeted communities to enable them provide their feedback and comments about PCDCR performance and staff behavior in the project. PCDCR will consider the beneficiaries’ feedback in the remaining activities and interventions of the project. Moreover, PCDCR will develop a complaints mechanism (via complaints Box) inside the partner CBOs for beneficiaries and (via PCDCR website) to let beneficiaries share their feedback, comments and opinions about the services provided and the behavior of the staff with PCDCR and project management.

project_name: Protection of Women Survivors of violence in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The project aims at improving the protection and reintegration of women survivors of violence, refugee
women and girls(RWG) female heads of households, and women and girls with disabilities(WGD) into society through improved access to essential multisectoral  services Including psychosocial support, legal support, referral  and GBV case management  in alignment with international Human Rights standards.
The project geographical area will focus on Gaza Governorate particularly the refugee camps, east part of Gaza and North Gaza. The project will be implemented directly by CWLRCP. The project will work to achieve the key result: R1: Improved access of vulnerable women and girls to  essential multisectoral services including GBV prevention and response (  The project will target 300 women of them 160 middle age,125 youth, 15 elderly age  (from vulnerable background with severe poverty and social marginalization, Women survivors of violence (Hayat and CWLRCP beneficiaries)and Households' women victims of violence.)by providing multi sectorial services ( psychosocial support, legal assistance, sheltering services and economic
support ),raising awareness sessions will be provided for communities ( 1000 women and 250 men)on GBV, GBV prevention, and on the importance of seeking the protection services ,The Hayat centre will provide child visitation services for at least 20 families (divorced couples) and their children which entails biweekly visits to the centre to enable the parent
(can be the mother or the father) who does not have custody over the children to see them in a supportive child-friendly environment. The visitation services are coupled with counseling for parents on how to deal with the children to minimize the impact of divorce on the wellbeing and psychosocial status of the children. It also avails regular support
(mainly psychosocial and legal) by the social workers and lawyers to the divorced
spouses and their children.

project_name: Ensuring lifesaving health services for trauma cases.
project_objective:
The idea of the project came as a response to the deteriorated humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip especially in the health sector, in connection with the continuation of the Great Return of Marches event.
The project will target the trauma cases from the women, men, girls, boys, elderly and people with disabilities, who are at high risk of morbidity and mortality.
This intervention will support UHWC to expand the provision of emergency health services to trauma cases through the following trauma pathway that includes: (i) deploying UHWC volunteers at MoH (TSP), (ii) transportation of patients from TSPs to Al Awda Hospital, (iii) Provision of hospital care including emergency services, surgical operations and hospitalization, (iv) post-injury wound care such as dressing will be provided to trauma cases even in the hospital or at home to cases who are facing difficulties to access the hospital, (v) providing physiotherapy services even at hospital or at home, (vi) providing psychological support.

From 30/3/2018 to 8/10/2018, Al-Awda Hospital provided emergency services to 941 trauma cases (162 out of them underwent surgical operations) with support from Humanitarian Fund that will be ended on 12/11/2018. This intervention is an extension of the previous project and it will support the treatment of 2,000 trauma cases during 2019 and will enable Al Awda hospital to provide new life-saving services for the injured in general and patients with limbs and vascular injury in particular.

Thus, this project will enable Al-Awda Hospital to perform new trauma health services that weren’t previously provided, and this includes:
-	Conducting vascular surgical operations to trauma cases, by contracting a consultant specialized in vascular surgery. These cases were previously referred to MoH hospitals, which are already overloaded. Since 30/3/2018, 120 vascular injured has been referred by Al Awda Hospital to MoH Hospitals. Here lies the importance of this project that it will reduce the number of cases referred to the MoH through conducting 200 vascular operations to trauma cases at Al Awda Hospital.
-	Moreover, this project will enable Al awda Hospital to provide physiotherapy services even at hospital or at home to patients who couldn’t reach the hospital.
-	Psychological support will also be provided to the patients and their families inside and outside the hospital in order to provide comprehensive health services.

It is estimated that 2000 cases will benefit from theses services (7 % female and 17% children).  All the project cases will be documented and desegregated by gender and age according to the unified models, and information will be shared with MoH and health cluster.
In order to ensure the continuation of the provision of the lifesaving health services to the trauma cases through Al Awda Hospital; essential lists of medication, medical disposable, lab reagents in addition to fuel should be guaranteed. 
All the above mentioned services will be provided to the affected people in a safety and dignity manner, and without any discrimination.  Gender and age needs have been taken into consideration, besides all data will be disaggregated by gender and age group.
Protection mainstreaming will be taken into consideration, as the services will be available to all beneficiaries who needs them, trauma services will be provided totally free of charge.  Female and paediatric staff will be available as a response to gender and age needs, privacy and confidentiality will be respected.
In order to enhance preparedness and to better deal with causalities, 10 of UHWC health workers (60% female) will received training in management of emergency cases and lifesaving interventions.  
Community engagement and accountability will be ensured through active participation of the affected population in all the project stages through focus groups, sharing information, measuring patients’ satisfaction and receiving feedback through accountability sessions.

project_name: Protection of Vulnerable Women and Girls Survivors of GBV in the Gaza Strip Through Coordinated and Multisectoral Responses
project_objective: The project objective is “Improved protection and respect of rights of acutely vulnerable women 18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years survivors of GBV and increased access to essential services based on IHL and IHRL.” WAC partners with RCS4GS and WEFAQ to make incremental changes in situation of women and girls, targeted community and duty bearers as reflected in project outcomes:1. Vulnerable women >18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years manifested well-being, knowledge and confidence, good health status, economic self-reliance, legal enablement and protection; 2. Targeted communities actively engaged in GBV prevention and protection; and 3. Duty bearers are accountable to vulnerable women >18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years and CBOs and increasingly act to protect them and reduce incidence and impact of human rights violations against them. The project targets 16814 direct beneficiaries (9389 women and 2010 men>18-59 and>59 years, 4275 girls and 1140 boys<18 years) identified based on defining vulnerability and acutely vulnerable groups according to their location, status, gender, protection risks and needs severity. Beneficiaries are selected from most affected locations in North (east/west Jabalia camp, Jabalia, Beit Lahia, Beit Hanoun, Ezbet Beit Hanoun) handled by RCS4GS; Gaza (Gaza City: Shijaia and Zaitoon, Juhor adDik) and Deir ALBalah (Bureij camp, An Nuseirat camp, Mussadar, Deir Al Balah) handled by WAC; and Khan Younis (Bani Suhaila, Fukhari, Qarara, Abasan AlKabira) and Rafah (Shuket Elsoofi, Rafah camp, Rafah, Mawasi) handled by WEFAQ. The project links to HRP (2018-2020) Strategic Objective 1” The rights of Palestinians living under occupation, including those living under blockade and other restrictions, are protected, respected and promoted in accordance with IHL and IHRL, while duty bearers are increasingly held to account,” and Protection Cluster Objective 2 ""Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of occupation and conflict related violence"", and standard activities/ indicators. Partners introduce an effective partnership model that consolidate their human capital to implement responsive, remedial and environment-building activities to address urgent needs of women/girls reflected in HNO/ HRP 2019 and achieve project objective/outcomes. Activities  include group psychological support for 960 women and 480 girls; recreational days for 960 women and 480 girls; individual psychological counseling to 120 women and 60 girls; referral of traumatized 42 women and 18 girls; psycho-therapy for 150 couples; group legal counselling to 960 women and 480 girls; individual legal counseling to 120 women and 30 girls; legal representation to 120 women and 30 girls; emergency hotline; emergency health care for 480 women and 240 girls; cancer diagnostic and treatment services for 90 women survivors of cancer; dignity kits for 225 women and 75 girls; training and grants to 21 women; awareness for 960 women, 960 men, 480 girls and 480 boys; training of 25 women and 25 men of GBV service providers; training of 25 women25 men from humanitarian actors; periodical monitoring and coordination with GBV humanitarian key actors; and 3 advocacy initiatives. This project is first phase of 2-year program in line with HRP multiyear strategy and “do no harm” principle. The second phase will be designed based on documenting/systematizing good practices/lessons learned from community engagement (CwC, AAP) like 9 community meetings, 18 FGDs, complaints mechanism, 3 radio ads, 9900 brochures, 3 fact sheets, 9 press releases and pre/post evaluation. Partners follow 4W (Who does What Where When) activity tracking matrix to coordinate with organizations executing activities in project locations in a way that ensures humanitarian needs are met, complementarity with ongoing projects, resilience of beneficiaries, participatory monitoring GENDER and AGE differences, environmentally neutral, protection mainstreaming, security and full access to project.

project_name: Community based protection for children affected by conflict and other emergencies
project_objective:
Children in Somalia live in a complex environment with scant protection mechanisms. Recruitment or use of children by armed groups, the Somalia National Army (SNA) and allied militias, and others – places children at great risk. In some areas families feel obliged to send their children to serve in clan militias. Impunity is widespread resulting in grave child rights violations including the arbitrary arrest and detention of children.
Population displacement due to chronic conflict, droughts and famines has resulted in the separation of children from their families, which exposes them to exploitation, violence and abuse children of IDPs and minorities are particularly vulnerable.
Years of armed conflict in Somalia has resulted in widespread contamination of explosive remnants of war (ERW) and landmines, the proliferation of small arms and light weapons and a steady rise in the use of improvised explosive devices (IEDs).
UNCEF will respond to the above needs in the following ways:
•	Provision of psychosocial support services through open spaces reaching 120,000 (50,000 boys & 50,000 girls) children and (5000 men and 15000 women) caregivers
•	Provide community-based reintegration for 3,000 children formerly associated with armed forces/groups (1,700 boys & 400 girls) and other vulnerable children (600 boys & 300 girls)
•	Tracing and reunify unaccompanied and separated children with their families (Boys: 6500 & Girls: 3,500)
•	Raise awareness on the threats posed by unexploded remnants of war reaching 45,000 people (17,500 boys; 17,500 girls, 5,000 women & 5,000 men)
•	Raise awareness on main CP concerns on child labour, child marriage and prevention of family separation reaching 250,000 people (102,500 boys, 102,500 girls, 25,000 men, women 20,000)

project_name: Provision of emergency safety net cash assistance to address root causes of severe acute malnutrition
project_objective: UNICEF proposes admissions into severe acute malnutrition therapeutic treatment as an entry point to target beneficiaries for emergency safety net cash assistance. This design aims at channeling assistance to the most vulnerable families using severe acute malnutrition (SAM) as a proxy for extreme vulnerability; and thus to prevent children from relapsing into acute malnutrition by addressing the multifaceted causes of malnutrition (including extreme poverty, lack of access to basic services, disease outbreaks, poor hygiene) and aiming to enhance impact of nutrition therapeutic interventions. Cash assistance could also help reduce related negative coping mechanisms such as sharing nutrition therapeutic commodities at household level. The program will also aim to build on current cash plus interventions including positive messaging to change behaviours and social norms that may be contributing to vulnerability, extend community engagement, accountability and feedback systems, integration of WASH services through hygiene kit distributions at discharge from SAM treatment centres, strong referral mechanisms to health program and deployment of a robust research and monitoring element to expand context speci􀂡c evidence base on cash as a modality to support nutritional outcomes. Geographical targeting will start with the areas where UNICEF is already providing cash assistance in Bay and Bakool and aims to be extended to rural areas in those districts, which may encourage return in safe areas and initial contributions to rebuilding livelihoods and resilience to shocks and crises. Additionally, UNICEF aims at piloting this approach in Gedo and Banadir where a resilience programme in partnership with WFP, and funded by the German cooperation, is being implemented. The selected household upon diagnosis of SAM, the mother or the regular care giver will be enrolled to the UNICEF supported therapeutic feeding centres. Upon admissions mother or the regular care giver will received monthly cash assistance. The beneficiaries will be register in SCOPE allowing them to track beneficiary across the different type of assistance received. This would also enhance coordination efforts with other partner to avoid duplication of assistance being received (medical treatment vs cash transfers).

project_name: Increasing access to inclusive quality basic education for the most vulnerable children and adolescent (girls and boys), with a special focus on IDPs and those in conflict-affected areas in Somalia.
project_objective: The proposed project will increase access to education for the most vulnerable children and adolescents (female and male), including IDPs and other  emergency-affected,   while also supporting those already enrolled to continue learning in a safe and protective space.  The lack of educational opportunities coupled with an uncertain environment due to displacement leave many children in psychosocial distress and vulnerable to further violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation.  UNICEF will deliver a comprehensive Education in Emergencies package of evidenced effective interventions, inclusive of social mobilisation, enrolment campaigns, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive WASH, lifesaving and lifeskills development, essential education supplies, and teacher training aimed to achieve the highest positive education results for girls and boys, and for women and men to better improve emergency education service delivery. Without child-friendly education, protection, safe water, and psychosocial support, these children and adolescents are at risk of losing hope, of accepting violence as the norm, and replicating it - undermining their own future, the future of Somalia, and the stability of the region.

project_name: Immediate life-saving food distributions to populations affected by Tropical Cyclone Kenneth and floods.
project_objective:
Provide 3-month life-saving food assistance to displaced people in Accomodation Centres and in affected communities, including in hard to reach areas (using boats and iar transport).
Coordinate food assistance interventions, FSL assessments and monitoring activities.

project_name: Provide Life saving Emergency Health Response to Kenneth cyclone affected population till end of May 2020
project_objective: 1. Strengthen and sustain the capacity of the provincial,  district, health facility and community to promptly detect, confirm and promptly respond to disease outbreaks. 2. Ensure continuity of basic life saving health services in the affected districts, resetlement areas, hard to reach areas and insecure areas feeling critical gaps that can not be addressed by the recovery program in the short term. 3. Strengthen the coordination and leadership in the health sector; 3. Procure and preposition essential medicines and medical and laboratroty supplies such as Interagency Emergency Health Kit (IEHK), Interagency Diarrhoeal Disease Kits (IDDK; revised Cholera Kit (RCK), Reproductive Health Kit (RHK), Non-communicable diseases kit (NCDK) SAM kits etc.

project_name: Vulnerable women and girls are protected against violence in cyclone Kenneth affected areas of northern Mozambique
project_objective:
To strengthen the capacity of women and girls affected by cyclone Kenneth, including the most vulnerable, such as women headed households, people with disabilities and chronic diseases, as well as boys and young men survivors of GBV, to demand for and access to quality SRHR services and GBV prevention, mitigation and response services, and to empower them to be resilient and exercise their agency, from emergency into early recovery phases in targeted districts. The project aims to target 125 000 beneficiaries by:
1.	Establishing and implementing 4 Women and Girls friendly spaces to sensitize on GBV and promote life skills activities; disseminate codes of conduct and existing case management and referral mechanisms to other services for survivors seeking assistance; Including psychosocial support, to save the lives of GBV survivors, and their immediate access to referral and assistance mechanisms
2.	Distribution of 3,000 dignity kits to ensure early recovery, protection and dignity for women and girls survivors of GBV.
3.	Support the national GBV multisectoral approach for prevention and response- social action, health, legal aid, police, ensuring that Psychosocial support, medical care, legal and judicial support are survivor-centered:
•	GBV case management and psychosocial training for government social workers
•	GBV training for community-based volunteers
•	Establish a platform in the local community for behavior change communication to increase knowledge and understanding of GBV prevention to promote positive behavior change that can prevent GBV in an emergency.
•	Strengthening platforms for GBV Awareness raising in disaster-affected communities for positive social behavior change

project_name: Lifesaving support for restoration of PHC services, including immunization and disease prevention and control (cholear/malaria) in response to Tropical Cyclone Kenneth
project_objective: To prevent an increase in excess mortality by increase in infectious disease and decreased access to basic services.

project_name: Provision of quality multisector humanitarian Health, Nutrition & WASH services for IDPs, Returnees and host communities in targeted areas In Sudan
project_objective: The proposed Activities targeting children under 5 and pregnant lactating women and communities. Health intervention will include PHC services (treatment of childhood illness, antenatal care, assisted deliveries, vaccination, provision of essential drugs and supplies, emergency preparedness and response in addition to building capacity of health staff in service delivery and monitoring implementations. Nutrition includes treatment of Acute Malnutrition and preventive services of IYCF, provision of nutrition supplies, training of volunteers, case identification and follow up, strengthen the community awareness of causes, danger signs and treatment of acute malnutrition, promoting positive health and nutrition behavior change. Under WASH, will rehabilitate facility latrines, water sources, provide cleaning materials and conduct home visits for hygiene promotion, provide water dispensers and hand washing facilities at health facilities in addition to improving medical waste management and infection prevention. SC integrated services delivery based on need and is inclusive and non-discriminatory. SC will ensure assistance is available to those who are most. The services provided will be respectful of cultural and religious backgrounds and will consider environment aspects. Whenever possible, health staff composition will reflect the gender, ethnic, and linguistic balance of the beneficiary population. Enforced policies prevent and respond to any breach of SC's Child Safeguarding Policy

project_name: Food distribution to vulnerable households in the Buffer Zone of Gorongosa National Park
project_objective: Provide access to food to vulnerable households severely affected by the flooding caused by cyclone IDAI

project_name: Integrated Primary Health Care and Nutrition services in conflict-affected and under-served areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan
project_objective: GOAL will support the provision of comprenhensive health & nutrition services in 24 health facilities across South Kordofan and 17 clinics in North Darfur, in areas with high numbers of conflict-affected households (including long-term IDPs, vulnerable host communities, and some returnees. GOAL has identified areas where we have implemented in 2018 and still need support (6 health facilities in Dilling locality and 3 in Delami locality), as well as new areas with no partners currently working that are in high need of support (3 health centres and 1 Stabilization Center in Talodi; 4 health facilities in Rashad locality; 3 health facilities in Habila locality, and 5 health facilities in Abu Karshola locality). Services include Reproductive Health, EPI, early warning and outbreak response, support and training for health staff, clinic running costs, provision of drugs, medical supplies and equipment, and support for the Locality Health Department, including the Health Information System. GOAL also provides community health through Care Groups, community health promotion, defaulter tracing for RH and OTP services, and the Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP) approach to prevent and treat Moderate Acute Malnutrition. Prioritization of new areas includes areas covered in GOAL's December 2018 needs assessment in Talodi, Rashad, and Habila localities, as well as provision of comprehensive support to Abu Karshola as part of a consortium in SHF 3rd allocation. GOAL will ensure comprehensive care in supported facilities, and GOAL will continue to closely coordinate through the Ministry of Health and the Health and Nutrition Sectors in Kadugli and Khartoum, and will also engage in ongoing coordination  with other partners in each locality to ensure no overlap.

project_name: Promotion de la santé mentale et du bien-être psychosocial de la population de déplacés dans la Province du Lac Tchad
project_objective: Le projet vise à promouvoir la santé mentale et le bien-être psychosocial de la population de déplacés touchée par la crise de Boko Haram dans la Province du Lac Tchad. L’intervention de COOPI apporte un soutien à tous les niveaux de la pyramide «Orientation santé mentale et soutien psychosocial dans les situations d’urgence» (IASC) dans les départements de Mamdi, Kaya et Fouli de la Province du Lac Tchad.

project_name: Sustain and expand life-saving basic WASH services for the vulnerable drought, flood, AWD and conflict affected and displaced populations in Somalia
project_objective:
Save the Children intends to sustain and expand the provision of basic WASH services to drought, flood, AWD and conflict affected populations in target regions in Somalia through the provision of water, sanitation and hygiene services in communities, schools and health/nutrition facilities. The proposed project is also designed to ensure equitable access to WASH services considering people with disabilities and elders, safety of children as well as dignity and privacy for women and girls. Coordination will be maintained with nutrition and WASH clusters at national and state levels, in addition to coordination with key actors in target areas. The project will contribute to the recovery and resilience of the target community and health systems ensuring participation of beneficiaries in the project cycle. The project will address gender issues and collect sex and age disaggregated data which will be analysed to identify gaps, provide gender sensitive interventions and ensure participation and empowerment of women. The accountability to affected populations will be ensured by involving communities, information sharing and engaging them in the complaints and feedback system. Protection of beneficiaries will be ensured during access and utilization of services reducing further risks. The interventions also fit under the sector specific objective to sustain and expand WASH services for IDPs and the affected population.
The proposed project activities will include construction of strategic water sources, pipeline extensions and distribution systems, provision of operation and maintenance tools, construction/rehabilitation of sanitation facilities in the target villages, IDPs, schools and health/nutrition facilities, trainings and dissemination of hygiene best practice through IECs with and distribution of hygiene kits.

project_name: Improved Access to Quality Education for Displacement-Affected Children in Somalia through an Integrated Response
project_objective: The proposed intervention will improve access to quality education, increase access to critical WASH inputs and enhance child protection mechanisms in schools for 16,200 (8,910 boys and 7,290 girls) displacement-affected children and their surrounding communities in Somalia. Support to schools with large IDP communities in the catchment areas will be a specific focus.
