Education specific activities will include the provision of education supplies, emergency take-away food rations for students to meet their food and energy needs, emergency teacher incentives to motivate teachers to stay in the schools, and sanitary kits for adolescent girls to encourage their regular attendance at school. Specific WASH activities will include increasing schools’ water storage capacity through the provision of PVC storage tanks, the construction and rehabilitation of latrines, and improving hygiene practices among children through engagement with community hygiene promoters (CHPs). As CHPs will interact closely with students during hygiene promotion sessions and recreational activities, RI will train this cadre on hygiene promotion, psychosocial support (PSS), and child protection and safeguarding. RI will work with the Child Protection Clusters/ Working Groups in each area to ensure up-to-date service mapping is available. Mapping will then be utilized to guide any child protection referrals necessary in the project. RI will conduct a child protection school-level assessment to identify the particular child protection issues faced by girls and boys in schools.  Results will be analyzed and action plans developed to strengthen school level child protection systems.  Plans will include actions such as the training of child protection focal persons at each school, and awareness raising and training of community education committees (CEC) on child protection. RI, through CECs and other community volunteers, will deliver messages to schools and communities on key protection concerns affecting the community based on the findings of the child protection assessment. These messages will target prevention as well as the response in the event protection concerns arise. RI will also continue to engage with relevant government ministries. Relief International (RI) will provide training to CECs on their roles and responsibilities, food and water management, disaster risk reduction (DRR), civic skills, proposal development, and child protection in the respective schools. To ensure water availability in targeted schools, RI will provide cash grants to CECs. In return, CECs will contribute in-kind or cash to procure safe water and manage its distribution to students. Further, the CECs will be trained on DRR to build their capacity and improve school preparedness against future disasters. Child- and gender-friendly latrines in the targeted schools will be rehabilitated or, where necessary, constructed to minimize disruptions in learning for girls and boys. RI will coordinate a back-to-school campaign with CECs and religious leaders to encourage school enrollment with an emphasis on children affected by displacement. RI, in collaboration with the appropriate ministries, will assess the existing child protection mechanisms at the start of the project, and, as determined from the assessment results, targeted schools will develop appropriate action plans to address areas of concern. To measure the effectiveness of the child protections systems implemented and capture lessons learned, RI will conduct an endline assessment. Through engagement with ministry officials and CECs, RI will leverage the agencies' apparatus and community assets to raise awareness among children on child protection and the established referral mechanisms which will serve to strengthen child protection in schools and the larger communities.

project_name: Shelter response to displacement effected population including IDPs, refugee returnees and vulnerable host communities across Somalia
project_objective:
The project will focus on improving the physical protection and dignity of IDPs, refugee returnees and poor host communities across Somalia through the provision of locally purchased Non Food Items (NFIs) and Emergency Shelter Kits (ESKs) through cash/voucher/in-kind modalities, construction of Semi-permanent and Permanent Shelters through community driven or owner driven approaches, settlement (re)planning training to reduce congestion and overcrowding, conducting Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for Shelters and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs & ESKs and participation in infrastructure mapping exercises led by Shelter cluster or any other partner.  

For the beneficiaries’ selection and registration, NRC will use an electronic mobile data collection tool called Kobo tool box, which provides an accurate and real time data. The data received through Kobo is easily manageable and transferable. 20% to 30% Poor host community members will also be selected to ensure 'DO NO HARM' principle ensuring other humanitarian principles including humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. For the provision of NFIs, each HH will be provided with a cash of $100 as per cluster agreed standard NFI kit while for the provision of ESKs, each HH will be provided with a cash of $145 (70% or $101 as first installment and remaining 30% or $44 as second installment) as per cluster approved ESK design. NRC will acquire the services of local telecom companies (viz. Hurmuud telecom in South and Central Somalia and Somtel & Golis in Puntland and Somaliland) for the cash transfers. NRC will provide a complete list of selected beneficiaries to respective telecom companies for their cross checking purposes. This list will include all details of selected beneficiaries including their telephone numbers and token numbers. After reviewing and cross checking, respective telecom company will transfer specified amount of money to selected beneficiaries through mobile transfer facility. 

Beneficiaries will be selected through predetermined beneficiary selection criteria prioritizing the Extremely Vulnerable Individuals (EVIs) including female and single headed HHs, orphans, chronically ill, aged and child headed households. Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age and diversity dis-segregated data. NRC will target total 130,000 individuals (50% females) consisting of 45,000 in South Central, 45,000 in Jubbaland, 30,000 in Puntland and 10,000 in Somaliland through different Shelter interventions throughout the year 2019.

NRC staff will ensure that the provided cash has been utilized for intended purpose by coordinating with the beneficiaries themselves and conduct follow ups with the support of the community leaders, local authorities and the relevant clusters. A Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs and ESKs and Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for semi-permanent and permanent Shelters will be conducted to analyse outcomes, the beneficiaries’ level of satisfaction and draw lessons learnt for future programming.

project_name: Education in Emergencies for children and youth affected by crisis in Somalia
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to provide quality and inclusive basic education to conflict/crisis affected children in Somalia. Focus will be made on improving the enrollment and retention of affected children through the provision of quality and inclusive basic education and this includes having access to a  safe and protective learning environment. Conflict / crisis affected children are often subject to drop and remain out school as they face difficulty to rejoining school because livelihood becoming a pressing priority.  The project will adopt an integrated approach to promoting safe, inclusive and quality learning opportunities for affected children.  This includes the construction of temporary learning spaces, as well as semi-permanent and permanent classrooms rehabilitation/construction. The project will also support children with the provision of lifesaving school meals, and the construction/rehabilitation of WASH facilities in school. This includes, the rehabilitation of water storage facilities, construction of water tanks, drinking water supply, gender segregated latrines and hygiene and water service promotions. Moreover, for improving the quality of education, the project will provide pedagogical Skills training, DRR and psychosocial support to teachers, including provision of incentive for teachers. The project will support  a total of 39000 (50% are girls) crisis-affected children with scholastic materials and uniforms CECs, head teachers in school’s management, community members and key staff within the ministries of Education in Somalia will have their capacity built in  in planning and responding to education in emergencies, as well as resilience building of communities.
Beneficiaries will be selected through participatory and predetermined selection criteria prioritizing the most affected and needy people. Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys and girls during the design of activities. Fifty percent of the total beneficiaries will be female. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age and diversity dis-segregated data. 
NRC will ensure adequate participation of the project by the target communities. Besides, Monitoring, evaluation and reporting plans and tools will be developed. Information will be collected on regular basis using Koobo toolbox and analyzed so that achievement is measured and changes made when necessary.

project_name: Increased access to quality education and support services for the welbeing of boys and girls with a focus on IDPs and host communities in Mudug and Galgaduud.
project_objective:
The proposed 12-month intervention will improve access to quality education, increase access to critical WASH inputs and enhance child protection mechanisms in 18 schools for conflict-affected IDP’s and host community learners in Mudug and Galgaduud regions of Galmudug State of Somalia. Education specific activities will include the provision of education supplies, emergency take-away food rations for students to meet their food and energy needs, emergency teacher incentives to motivate teachers to stay in the schools, and sanitary kits for adolescent girls to encourage their regular attendance at school. Specific WASH activities will include increasing schools’ water storage capacity through the provision of PVC storage tanks, the construction and rehabilitation of latrines, and improving hygiene practices among children through engagement with community hygiene promoters (CHPs). As CHPs will interact closely with students during hygiene promotion sessions and recreational activities, CISP will train this cadre on hygiene promotion, psychosocial support (PSS), and child protection and safeguarding. Specific Protection activities will include the mapping and sharing of existing child protection service providers and their respective services to school administrators and communities, strengthening child protection systems in schools, including the recruitment and training of child protection focal persons at each school, and awareness raising and training of community education committees (CEC) on child protection. CISP will also continue to engage with Ministry of Education Culture and Higher Education (MoECHE)
CISP will provide training to CECs on their roles and responsibilities, food and water management, disaster risk reduction (DRR), civic skills, proposal development, and child protection in the respective schools. To ensure water availability in targeted schools, CISP will provide cash grants to CECs. In return, CECs will contribute in-kind or cash to procure safe water and manage its distribution to students. Further, the CECs will be trained on DRR to build their capacity and improve school preparedness against future disasters. Disability and gender-friendly latrines in the targeted schools will be rehabilitated or, where necessary, constructed to minimize disruptions in learning for girls and boys. CISP will coordinate a enrolment drives through MoE and with CECs and religious leaders to encourage school enrolment with an emphasis on children affected by displacement. CISP education department will utilize the existing synergies with CISP protection department to will assess the existing child protection mechanisms at the start of the project, and, as determined from the assessment results, targeted schools will develop appropriate action plans to address areas of concern. To measure the effectiveness of the child protections systems implemented and capture lessons learned, CISP will conduct an end line assessment. Through the CISP protection department engagement with CEC’s and the regional Gender Focal Points (GFP’s) of MoECHE, CISP will leverage the agency's apparatus and community assets to raise awareness among children on child protection and the established mechanisms which will serve to strengthen child protection in schools.

project_name: Strengthening community protection mechanisms through a comprehensive, prevention strategies and timely response in Banaadir and Galmudug Regions.
project_objective:
Based on the analysis of the current situation in Banaadir and Galmudug region, CISP intends to extend its protection programme to contribute towards enhancing protection, increasing safety and promoting dignity of conflict-affected women, men, girls and boys in target locations. These areas are currently concerned by prolonged drought, displacement and voluntary return movements and, with the intensification of the military operations around AS control areas, it is expected that a high number of newly displaced people and/or newly accessible people will be imminently in need of critical assistance.

The overarching objective is to contribute towards enhancing the first-line and second-line overall child protection and GBV response capacity, through the deployment of specialized mobile teams composed of Social Worker, Case Manager, Health Worker and IDTR Officers, for increased identification and service delivery. 
The intervention will target: extremely vulnerable men, women, girls and boys and those at high risk of being exposed to violence and abuse at large. The most vulnerable cases will be provided with the needed support through case management and the provision of specialized services. Beneficiaries in need of individual assistance will be identified through the work of technical trained staff (namely case workers and social workers) in conjunction with expertise in CP and GBV capitalized by CISP. Beneficiaries and most vulnerable households will also be identified with the support of community leaders and key informants. Special attention will also be given to individuals with specific needs, especially persons with disabilities, as they might be more at risk of being exposed to violence and abuse. 

Children meeting the following vulnerability criteria will be targeted: unaccompanied and separated children; children showing signs of severe trauma, children requiring immediate, lifesaving services (e.g. emergency healthcare, provision of shelter etc.); children who have survived grave violations (sexual violence, child recruitment, abduction or maiming); disabled children, child survivors of GBV (physical, sexual and psychological). These children are extremely vulnerable, since without immediate intervention and support, they may be at risk exploitation and abuse that endangers their life and long-term wellbeing.

project_name: Integrated Nutrition Program aimed at reducing morbidity and Mortality related to malnutrition and build resilient communities through Facility and strong community based approach in Kismayo of lower Juba, Dharkenley in Banadir and Hobyo  and  Jariban in Mudug region in  Somalia.
project_objective:
Proposed project areas cover some of the most needy with vulnerable host communities and IDPs. Kismayo and kahda have  some of the most vulnerable and protracted IDP in Mogadishu, most facing multiple displacement. Most households have limited access to health services and poor WASH status exacerbating disease and malnutrition. GAM rate is above emergency threshold (FSNAU,2018). Birth assisted by skilled attendant is still low with few projects offering focused antenatal care thus  presenting missed opportunity to strengthen IYCF at an early stage. 
Hobyo and Jariban nutrition situation is critical for respective districts with aggravating factors. The areas were greatly ravaged by 2017 drought with animals dying,scarcity of  water,  very limited access to toilets leading to increased AWD /Cholera cases,low vaccination coverage,limited access to health services and a critical Food security situation.  The situation expected to deteriorate for all areas if nothing is done especially if rains fail again.
SAF UK will therefore focus on life saving, Resilience building, protection activities in hard to reach areas and most vulnerable populations e.g children under 5(Boys and girls), women, elderly,HIV/TB patients, IDP and remote rural population. Activities that support full recovery from effects of drought and resilience building for affected population will remain a primary focus. 
This will be done through prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition with a strong community component that will promote community participation and Information sharing, to improve access to those in need and provide a platform for surveillance. SAF UK has developed strong links with communities and  conducts biannual community conversations with affected population including them in programming in all stages of the program cycle. The organization has developed community structures that ensure services are devolved to clusters of 15 households especially IDP, in line with organizations community strategy and Accountability to affected population (AAP) Framework.
 Programs will integrate with health, WASH and food security and livelihood activities.This will include integration with basic health and maternal services, including Expanded program for immunization (EPI), BSFP, hygiene promotion including hygiene kits.The project will also seek to improve health seeking behavior though community mobilization.
Significant others to the target beneficiaries, especially Men and grandmothers, will be targeted for health promotion. Peer support groups will also be formed to promote peer learning. Involvement in multi  cluster coordination, including attending coordination meetings and related activities will be high on our priority. 
 The project will employ and train  staff (Men and women) and include community workers(Men and women) through a transparent process.

project_name: Education Proposal For Sustainable Delivery Of Equitable, Quality And Protective EiE For School Age Children In South West State.
project_objective: The project targets Baidoa districts affected by crisis in South west State. READO in response to conflict and environmental related crisis and other emergencies affecting the larger Somalia has proposed this project to mainly keep 2004 learners and 61 teachers and 30 CECs at school while looking at multisectoral approach in solving the case of high school dropout rate following the 2017 drought, Floods and conflict. Flood Response Plan by OCHA, May 2018 has indicated that most schools in flood prone areas has been affected and destroyed thus the schools will need temporary learning spaces and rehabilitations. Through provision of water, food, trainings on resource management, systems strengthening and supply of teaching and learning materials, READO will manage to address Education with reference to Education cluster HNO2018, Food Security and Protection concerns like equity, impartiality, accountability, and safety in and around schools, through the schools as the entry point to aid provision. This is hoped to reach some 2098 (1203 boys, 801 girls, 60 men and 34 women) through a period of 12 months with the assumption that the region will remain stable.

project_name: Improved access to essential and emergency health services to host communities and displaced populations in Puntland, Somaliland and South Central Regions of Somalia.
project_objective: The proposed action will be implemented through the already existing Government-MOH systems to enhance sustainability through the strengthening of the health system to offer quality health services to the target populations; IDPs and host community during humanitarian crisis. The action will aim to enhance sustainability through strengthening of the health system to offer quality health services to the target populations. Target locations are Baki and Lughaya districts of Awdal region, Burco and Odweyne districts of Togdheer region both in Somaliland, Garoowe, Burtinle and Eyl districts of Nugaal region in Puntland and Baydhaba, Qansax Dheere and Buur Hakaba districts of Bay region in South Central Somalia. The interventions seek to increase access, utilization and coverage of essential maternal, new-born and child health services through strengthened health system for better service delivery through; capacity building to the health care workers on safe motherhood, BEmONC and CEmONC, EPI and cold-chain management, integrated disease surveillance and response (IDSR) and mass casualty management in order to improve their capacity to deliver quality health services; provision of essential medicines including vaccines thus avoiding stock outs and ensure availability and accessibility of supplies; strengthening emergency obstetric and new-born care through adequate staffing to provide both BEmONC and CEmONC services 24/7; scale up of immunization services both routine immunization and campaigns during disease outbreaks. Through this action also, mitigation of impact and response to shocks to the affected populations as a result of conflict and public health emergencies will be enhanced through supporting the MoH prepare emergency response plans (ERPs) at regional health authorities level and have rapid response teams (RRTs), who are trained and can promptly investigate rumors, confirm outbreaks, notify WHO and MoH, mount an aggressive response, and report promptly. Referral health facilities will be selected strategically and equipped to enable management of mass casualties during catastrophe and staff trained on mass casualty management. It is envisaged that through this interventions, target populations will have improved access to quality healthcare services during humanitarian crisis and therefore reduce excess mortality.

project_name: Life-saving, recovery and resilience project for vulnerable populations in Galmudug, Banadir and Lower Shabelle.
project_objective:
An estimated 1.5 million people in Somalia are expected to be in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) 1 or worse through December going into 2019, according to findings from the post-Gu seasonal assessment conducted in June and July 2018. Forecast average to above-average Deyr (October-December 2018) rains, expected average to above-average off-season harvests, and favorable market conditions are expected to further improve food security conditions through December 2018. However, acute food insecurity remains prevalent among pastoral populations who lost most of their livestock and became destitute during the 2017 drought and Cyclone Sagar; riverine populations affected by flooding in April and May 2018; and others experiencing large-scale, protracted displacement due to conflict and natural hazards. 
The forecasted El Nino phenomena and associated abnormal rainfall in last quarter of 2018 is expected contribute to an increase in production while at the same time risks of shocks, including loss of production are real. Indeed, the expected above normal rains may cause the deterioration of the situation of IDPs who are already in a precarious situation. Under these circumstances Somali household’s recent food security improvements risk deterioration if the humanitarian assistance is not sustained particularly among vulnerable population groups. Assistance should be sustained including livelihood support to make lasting improvements to the Somalis food security situation.
In Galmudug, an inter-agency assessment report established that an estimated 28,000 people were displaced from Xarardheere district between 16 April and the third week of July 2018. Of these, 26,000 were in the assessed areas of Cadaado and Hobyo districts, whilst another 2,000 people had reportedly settled in the villages in Hobyo district. Amongst the IDPs there were 430 unaccompanied and separated children. Alarming levels of food insecurity were observed among new IDPs, with respondents reporting consuming only one meal per day.
An estimated 6,966 people (around 1,061 HHs) have fled their homes in lower and middle Shabella, Bakol and Bay regions in search of safety and security due to natural disasters, armed conflict and escalating violence since mid-2011 and settled in five IDP camps in Banadir. An assessment by Human Appeal in Banadir in September established that  IDP groups most susceptible to food shortages were reported to be the newly arrived IDPs. Child-headed and female-headed households, as well as households headed by older persons, also face major constraints in accessing food due to high prices of food commodities if they are available. People with low mobility or those in remote locations far from the main street of KM 13 had no access to humanitarian assistance since they arrived in the assessed locations.
CPD proposes to intervene by providing immediate access to food to the vulnerable communities and IDP’s through unconditional cash transfers and conditional cash (through cash for work in water structures rehabilitation. The water structures will be used by the community to enhance their resilience towards drought and conserve the environment they live in. CPD will also strive to restore livelihoods of the communities by providing farm and agricultural inputs and support like seeds, tools and training.

project_name: Strengthening and sustaining protection services through prevention and response to gender-based violence (GBV), and mitigation of child protection in emergency (CPiE) or risks for the displaced communities of Middle Shebelle, Lower Shebelle,Lower Jubba, Banaadir, Bay and Bakool regions of Somalia.
project_objective: The project seeks to strengthen and scale up lifesaving protection services in the targeted location to prevent and respond to protection risks/concerns experienced by women, men and children especially in Internally Displaced Peoples camps but also in the host populations. The key focus will be sustaining and scaling up prevention and response to separation of children from their families and gender based violence survivors. The project will conduct regular analysis of the situation of children regarding causes and patterns of separation and respond accordingly through prevention and strengthening of appropriate protection systems and services, build capacity of protection service providers and stakeholders. This project also strengthens service mapping to facilitate appropriate referrals and coordination and linkage in service delivery to ensure quality comprehensive services to unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) children at risk of being recruited by armed forces or armed groups (CAAFAG) and gender based violence (GBV) survivors.

project_name: Bridging Essential Health Service Gaps Among Conflict-affected Populations in Adamawa, Borno, and Yobe States of North-east Nigeria
project_objective: The context in Borno and Yobe states of large number of displaced persons particularly in camps on a background of weakened health systems increases the risk of spread of communicable diseases. For instance, in 2017, there was a large outbreak of cholera which affected more than 5,000 persons with 61 associated deaths mostly among internally displaced persons. Furthermore, as new areas are recaptured from non-state armed groups (NSAGs), many persons who were trapped in such areas return to many high risk areas for disease spread with low immunity to vaccine-preventable diseases as they have not received any vaccination in years. These, among other factors, predispose a large number of vulnerable persons to easily contract diseases in epidemic proportions. In order to ensure that mortality and morbidity from outbreaks are minimized, early warning systems are required to be set up to effectively detect and respond to any alerts of epidemic-prone diseases. The project, ‘Bridging Essential Health Service Gaps Among conflict-affected populations in Adamawa, Borno, and Yobe States of North-east Nigeria is three-year project aimed at improving access to basic life-saving integrated health services in Adamawa, Borno, and Yobe States. The project will work through Hard-to-Reach mobile medical teams, Community-oriented resource persons, and mental health focal points to reach 585,000 people in IDP camps and host communities in the project states. These include men, women, girls, and boys. Overall, the project will ensure continued provision of essential health services to conflict-affected people through deployment of H2R MHTs and implementation of iCCM while maintaining the specialized mental health care at the PHCs of Borno state.

project_name: Provision of health interventions  covering primary, secondary and tertiary prevention including maternal and child health and  AWD/ cholera response in Kismayo, Kahda and Hobyo districts of south central Somalia.
project_objective:
In Somalia a huge percentage of the population still relies on humanitarian health
assistance with the number increasing. 41% of Somalia’s population need life saving
humanitarian assistance (OCHA ). Approximately 3.3 million women, girls, boys and men
need access to emergency health care.Neonatal, infant and child mortality remain high
with communicable diseases as leading causes. AWD/cholera is prevalent enhanced by
poor WASH. High maternal mortality rate remains contributed by limited antenatal care
(1/4 of women), the low proportion of births attended by skilled medical personnel (1/3)
and the inadequate facilities for emergency maternal care. Insecurity, poor health seeking
practices, lack of functioning referral systems, limited access to health services and
underlying malnutrition pose major challenges for control and prevention of disease
outbreaks.The in􀂢ux of IDPs continues to increase their vulnerably and reduces access to
health services decreasing their resilience as majority prefer urban centers.
SAF UK intends to provide lifesaving assistance and strengthen community level resilience. The organization will intervene by providing basic and emergency health services through 5 camp based and 4 mobile clinics in IDP camps in kismayo and Kahda, and OPD in all areas. The organization also seeks to establish a CTC in rural areas of Hobyo and Jariban where AWD cases are on the increase and maintain the one in Dalxiska Kismayo.The organization will also step up EPI in all areas, through health facilities and mobile teams. We also intend to improve birth assisted by skilled birth attendants through our MCH facilities and enhance ANC and PNC integrating with EPI and Nutrition services. Strong social mobilization for use of health services will continue.We will also focus of improving capacity of both health and community based staff (Men and women)in provision of quality services.

project_name: Prevention and Treatment of Malnutrition for children aged 6-59 months and PLWs in South Galkayo and Hobyo Districts, Mudug region Somalia
project_objective: The project aims at providing life-saving nutrition services for targeted 3960 children (1980 boys and 1980 girls) aged between 6-59 months and 1961 Pregnant Lactating Women (PLWs) that are severely acute and moderately malnourished by providing an integrated nutrition package based on Somali IMAM  standards with strong community support through capacity building of nutrition staff, Community Health Workers and Community Nutrition volunteers on case detection through MUAC measurements and weight-height measures to mitigate against sustained and escalating malnutrition caseloads in South Galkayo and Hobyo Districts. This will be achieved through:  Screening and treatment of severely acute and moderate  malnourished boys and girls aged between 6-59 months and PLWs by OTP/SFP program, Prevention and management of common diseases (anemia, diarrhea, malaria etc) by provision of Vitamin A supplementation, deworming, multiple  micro nutrients, supplements, iron/folate supplements and dissemination of hygiene promotion messages and practices to the targeted 3960 children (1980 boys and 1980 girls) aged between 6-59 months and 1961 Pregnant Lactating Women (PLWs), provision of lipid based nutrient supplements to boys and girls aged 6-59 months through health facility and mobile teams alongside food distribution and advocacy for promotion of dietary diversification.

project_name: Provision of psychosocial support; activation of protection mechanisms to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect against children; and support access to birth registration.

project_name: Provision of WASH assistance to vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
The purpose of the WASH intervention is to deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services to most vulnerable people and support to water, sanitation and sewage systems to ensure continuous services for affected people in Syria. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable populations throughout Syria through the delivery of a multi-faceted WASH response.  The different components of NRC’s WASH project are intended to contribute to HRP WASH Sector Objectives 1 and 2.
NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and hybrid modalities. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality
Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable conflict and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities, IDP and refugee returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the conflict. All interventions will seek to prioritize the most vulnerable households. Where appropriate, multi-sectoral vulnerability scoring techniques will be used that integrate vulnerability indicators

This project includes: This 
-	Emergency response through the provision of one-off support as part of an integrated, multi-sector response in accordance with the Emergency Preparedness and Response Plans (EPRPs). Comprises of three Result Areas: Temporary WASH services, Household assets (Hygiene NFIs) and support to Education in Emergencies (WASH Services for Temporary Learning Spaces).
-	The provision of medium-term shelter support at household and settlement-level to populations living in and out-of-camps. Comprises of two Result Areas: Community Infrastructure and Services in Camps, and Household assets (Hygiene vouchers)
-	The provision of longer-term assistance at household and settlement-level in urban and peri-urban out-of-camp areas. Comprises of three Result Areas: Community Infrastructure and Services, Housing Rehabilitation for WASH facilities, and school rehabilitation (WASH Facilities) (see NRC’s Education project submission).

project_name: Assistance alimentaire  à 2000 ménages victimes des attaques de Boko Haram dans les départements de Bosso, Diffa, Mainé Soroa et N'guigmi, région de Diffa
project_objective: La région de Diffa fait face depuis 2014 à des conflits multiformes liés à la présence de Boko Haram occasionnant ainsi une crise humanitaire sans précédente avec des mouvements importants des populations provenant du Nigeria voisin et des déplacés internes et retournés. Cette crise a fait plus de 205000 PDI et refugiées. les départements de Bosso, Diffa, Mainé Soroa et Nguigmi sont tous touchés par ce phénomène. Dans chaque département cible, environ 500 ménages extrêmement vulnérables seront ciblés (enfants abandonnés et femmes victimes des abus).

project_name: Linking Emergency Assistance and Response in Northeast Syria (LEARN)
project_objective:
Solidarités International (SI), will support equitable and safe access to essential basic services including WASH, and Shelter, for the most vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Northeast Syria (NES.). The program strategy is grounded in needs assessments, contextual analysis and scenario planning. In the areas of intervention, HNO shows 1.2m are facing acute WASH needs, 1.5m acute Health needs, 590,511 acute Shelter needs and 1m acute NFI needs, which negatively impacted their health and well-being. In the past 12 months, of the 1.2m displaced, 241,329 (19.6%) was reported to be from DEZ governorate, due to recent clashes between Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and Syrian Arab Army (SAA).  Displacement from the Ar Raqqa offensive has exceeded 400,000 people in the last year alone. These trends are likely to continue with IDP flows entering Ar Raqqa, DEZ, Al Hasakah, and Aleppo governorates. Based on acute inter-sectoral needs, the Governorates of DEZ, AR-Raqqa, Al-Hassakeh and Aleppo have been prioritized for the intervention. 

LEARN will provide an integrated and harmonized multi-sectoral package of comprehensive essential services for vulnerable conflict –affected populations, drawing on demonstrable technical capacity in Heath, Shelter, WASH and protection. To ensure effective delivery of the program, LEARN will operate under a field-based coordination unit. LEARN will capitalize on its comparative advantage of having efficient, flexible and nimble systems that can adapt to the rapidly changing context and needs. It will draw on widespread and established operational capacity, presence, and community networks. The Consortium will prioritize the specific needs of highly vulnerable households, such as those headed by females as well as elderly, children and people with disabilities. The Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) will provide timely assistance to meet new humanitarian needs across the whole of NES, under an integrated model and joint framework. This mechanism will see LEARN initiate coordinated, rapid response to sudden onset displacement and other humanitarian crises such as health epidemics within 24-48 hours. Rapid Need Assessments (RNAs) will be conducted concurrently with initial life-saving activities, followed by delivery of a comprehensive package of emergency services. The intervention will strengthen the skills and knowledge of communities and aim at building resilience and the ability to cope with, respond to and recover from future shocks and stresses. LEARN will utilize a joint, integrated data management and M&E system, drawing on extensive expertise and strong Complaints Response Mechanisms (CRM) capacity. LEARN Consortium will focus on ensuring monitoring data, learning and beneficiary feedback is integrated into the program cycle. LEARN will continue to proactively take a leading role in relevant cluster and working groups, thus further broadening the coordinated and coherent approach across the consortium partners into the wider humanitarian community. LEARN’s value is significantly greater than its constituent partners, promoting synergies to maximize coherent and holistic responses in areas of greatest need. LEARN management and governance structure is based on robust processes and controls, which will guide operations, as well as swift and effective decision-making, risk management, communication, grant management and compliance. This will ensure accountability and effective management.

project_name: Providing life saving and life sustaining health assistance in NES - Phase 3
project_objective:
North East Syria (NES) continues to experience conflict and displacement, whilst access to health care for the population remains a serious concern, particularly in hard to reach and recently retaken areas of Hasakeh, Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor (DeZ). Un Ponte Per (UPP) with its local partner contribute to improving access to health care for war affected persons.
Through this action, in continuation with previous project phases (Jun. 2017-Jan.'19), partners aim to ameliorate health conditions for the population in the humanitarian response. Through community based approaches it will provide prevention outreach in health&protection for supporting local resilience. Protection mainstreaming will be ensured to address barriers for vulnerable groups. It will provide health services to all free of charge, with specialized services to women and children. Public health system is supported with improved hospitals emergency capacity, ambulance system and referral pathways.
UPP and its partner provide timely and quality access to life-saving treatment and life-sustaining primary health care for war affected persons, where few providers can reach. This action will provide continuity of services to the Emergency Primary Care Center (EPCC) opened under phase I in west Raqqa city, including trauma care due to explosive remnants of war (ERW) to returnees in need, while the city is being rebuilt. In conflict ridden DeZ, action will respond to needs of IDPs in camps and undeserved areas through an ambulance-mobile clinic network (25 ambulances), the continuation of EPCC service in Areesha and set up a basic EPCC in Abu Khashab camp, where needs identified are high.
The expected result is to provide access to care reaching 96.000 beneficiaries over 12 months including IDPs, returnees, refugees, local population. It also expects to train 200 local staff operating in emergency. In such a volatile context the project provides the capacity to quickly adapt to emerging health needs in other NES locations.

project_name: Responding and Rebuilding: Shelter interventions within the Syrian Arab Republic

project_name: Meeting the Protection Needs of Vulnerable Children in Barawe, Kurtunwarey, Marka and Qoryoley through Community-Based Child Protection and Comprehensive Advocacy
project_objective:
The proposed interventions are centrally located within the 2019 Protection Cluster Objectives 2 and 3. Responses to address the recent conflict, displacement, floods, and violence in Lower Shabelle districts are current priorities within the cluster. New Ways will respond to the needs of vulnerable populations including boys and girls from affected communities, IDPs and host communities in hard-to-reach areas in the region. 

The project will conduct regular analysis of the situation of children about causes and consequences of child rights abuse and respond accordingly through prevention and establishment of proper protection system and services. The project is designed to empower the target communities to meet the challenges they face in the prevention and protection of children from violence and all forms of abuse. This project will map the existing services for appropriate referrals and coordination to ensure immediate response to the children with disabilities, neglected children, unaccompanied, and separated children at risk. 
This project reinforces the protection element of providing assistance based on need and without discrimination and ensures children from vulnerable communities are not neglected or deprived from humanitarian assistance.
Close cooperation with other IP, local authorities, elders, and all relevant stakeholders will be also established and maintained along the project implementation. The intervention will target both urban and rural population to sensitise protection issues and negative cultural beliefs.

The project will focus on activities that meet the growing identified and perceived needs of children as outlined in the need, mainly focusing on improving the quality of response and prevention services as well as establishment of community-based child protection mechanism with meaningful child participation through capacity building and coaching of protection service providers, community members; women, youth, children, elders, social workers, caregivers and school teachers. 

In order to reach more children with better protection from all kinds of violence and abuse, the project aims to build and strengthen child protection structures at community and district level, with the meaningful participation of children as a key component. On monthly basis, the project will bring together authorities, parents and children in a workshop to discuss violence against children and the other protection issues and their effects to their children and their communities, and encourage them to work together to stop all forms of child rights abuse and to protect their children to the best they can. Children are themselves actively engaged in identifying the risks and protection issues as well as proposing protection measures.

The project main objective is to establish and support community-based child protection method in the region and to improve quality of child protection response and access of services for children at risk of or experiencing abuse, abandonment, separation, neglect or exploitation. 

The intervention starts with an extensive protection TOT training for 8 child protection advocates 4 male and 4 female. The CPAs will organize and facilitate all planned training events for the protection teams, community volunteers, children, duty bearers, elders and other stakeholders. Two protection teams will be deployed in each of the districts that will mobilise, support and form community protection committees. Organising and forming 16 effective child protection committees at IDP settlements in the target districts, which will be provided with capacity building opportunities and will be supported to design and implement an initiative that addresses their needs within their community. Organising 48 awareness sessions for the target communities. Empowering stakeholders including children and equipping them with the necessary skills of preventing, detecting, documenting, managing and responding to the protection issues. Organising 4 Group-based psychosocial support and life skills sessions for children. Training 80 community members, duty bearers and volunteers on child protection issues, empowering them identifying and supporting children with special psychosocial and child protection needs. Training 40 health-service providers on child protection and referral, enabling them to detect, document and refer protection cases and report protection-related cases. Conducting psychosocial support intervention training for parents, on how to support children in high stress and emergency situations, including displacement due to natural disaster and protracted conflicts in the region. Organising four Positive discipline training to school counsellors and community people to reduce harsh disciplining practices and identification and referral of distressed or maltreated children who need extra care to appropriate services through comprehensive case management service.
Conducting 4-stress management support and ‘positive parenting’ workshops to caregivers, community leaders and influencers to reduce harsh parenting practices and family conflict, and increase knowledge of social norms and harmful practices. Meanwhile 880 boys and girls including children with disabilities are planned to participate in the structured community-based psychosocial support activities. More 6800 individuals of will be targeted with rights-based public outreach and awareness raising activities to raise their levels of awareness.    In addition to that 20 children with physical disability will be reached with protection-oriented direct assistance and construction of disabilities access in New Ways’ managing health centres in the four target districts.

The project strategy prioritizes 4 areas of work:
- Engaging communities carefully particularly traditional elders, women, youth, boys and girls by giving considerations of how different community groups and interests can be included and addressed while recognising of that communities are not homogenous, and neither are the interests of their subgroups. 
- Contributing enhancement of the quality and access of child protection services through strong coordination with other on-going humanitarian/emergency projects in the region including New Ways’ projects, realising that protection is placed as mainstreaming in all projects.
- Increasing protection knowledge and information to the decision makers, women, youth and children.
- Understanding how and why violence occurs and to equip communities with tools to stop the violent behaviour before it starts, emphasis will be also placed on traditional custom law  ‘XEER’ to respond to the children’s rights.

The project targets vulnerable children according to the humanitarian operations in Somalia defined vulnerability categories through direct support, empowerment, referral and advocacy. Among them are:
•	Children from minority groups and IDPs.
•	Unaccompanied boys and girls living alone (no foster family).
•	Children from large family and Child headed household.
•	Children with severe medical condition.
•	Children from single female heads of households, especially those with multiple dependants.
•	Children with a physical disability from birth, or resulting from illness, infection, injury, or trauma.

project_name: Provision of life-saving basic education  for vulnerable children in Banadir, lower and middle Shabelle regions.
project_objective: The project will increase access to safe learning spaces for for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and poor hosting children and adolescent youths of male and female of emergency-affected population in Daynile, Kaxda, Afgoye, Walanweine and Jowhar districts of Banadir, Lower and Middle Shabelle regions. project_name: Distributing food rations and bread for Vulnerable people in northwest Syria
project_objective:

This project has a two-fold objective, as follows:
