project_name: Emergency Live-saving Support to the drought and conflict affected IDPs and host communities in Sool, Sanaag, Togdheer and Bari regions of Somalia
project_objective:
Provide life saving and life sustaining integrated interventions food and Livelihood
interventions to the drought and conflict affected vulnerable women .girls boys, and
men in Sool, Sanaag, Togdheer and Bari regions of Somalia. the project will target IDPS and poor host communities Households

project_name: Food Assistance and livelihood support for crisis affected rural populations and IDPs in Galgaduud and Gedo regions.
project_objective: SADO’s proposed response is designed in alignment with the Food Security priorities and objectives focusing on livelihood support and food assistance using food vouchers targeting support to both urban centers of displaced persons and preventing displacement in rural areas in Galgaduud and Gedo region. SADO will provide extremely vulnerable HHs with unconditional food vouchers to redeem the food items from food vendors in functioning markets. SADO will build on its successful experience implementing similar SHF funded project in Gedo and Galgaduud regions in Somalia. Each selected household will receive monthly food voucher equivalent to 100% MEB for 3 months. The MEB is based on Cash Working Group (CWG) recommendations. The targeted beneficiaries are the weakest and most vulnerable families that are not able to meet the MEB or are not able to meet the minimum living threshold of 2100Kcal per person per day. As well, appropriate farm inputs (seed and farm tools and equipment) will be provided to riverine farmers recently affected by floods in Gedo to restore and protect their livelihoods.  For households who are food insecure but can participate in labour work, the project will engage them in CFW activities of rehabilitating community assets. SADO’s response will help stabilize crisis affected communities and prevent populations from migrating to urban centres in search of food and other services.

project_name: Livelihoods Development For Food Security Project in South Central and Banadir
project_objective: The proposed project will ensure protection and restoration of livelihoods associated through agriculture, livestock and income generating  activities. This will be achieved through provision of seasonally appropriate agricultural inputs, emergency livestock assistance, livelihood diversification, improved post-harvest practices and response to food chain threats. This is aimed at reducing overreliance on livestock products and reduction in livestock morbidity rate. Additionally, NAPAD will ensure women participation in community development and decision making by encouraging women participation in disaster response by empowering women and the youth through vocational education and providing an enabling environment for self-employment opportunities.

project_name: Provision of Quality and Protective Education Opportunities for Children in Northern Syria
project_objective:
In this project, Ataa is planning to target children who are in Aleppo and Idleb governorates as follows:
•	Aleppo governorate, Afrin sub-district. 
•	Aleppo governorate, Jandairis sub-district. 
•	Aleppo governorate, Atareb sub-district.
•	Aleppo governorate, Jebel Saman sub-district.
•	Aleppo governorate, Zarbah sub-district
•	Idleb governorate, Dana sub-district.
•	Idleb governorate, Ehsem sub-district.
•	Idleb governorate, Ariha sub-district.
•	Idleb governorate, Saraqab sub-district.
•	Idleb governorate, Teftnaz sub-district
The schools located in Aleppo governorate are 12 (11 in villages and 1 in camp) whereas there are 11 schools located in Idleb governorate, 2 of them are in camps while the other 9 schools are in villages. The above-mentioned communities were chosen and prioritized based on 1) its high severity on HNO severity scale, 2) the concentration of IDPs, and 3) its accessibility for Ataa.
The targeted areas in this project are economically poor suffering from high rates of severe illiteracy and dropout especially among children of basic education. The poor state of education in the targeted areas is mainly because families not sending their children to schools because they cannot afford to, damage to schools that need rehabilitation and lack of education personnel because most of the qualified teachers work in other positions. Many children are also in a state of psychological distress as a result of frequent displacement, harsh circumstances, and difficult living conditions. Therefore, providing education opportunities have become a requirement that children would like to accomplish. So, there is an urgent action to address the devastating impact of conflict on children in particular which is the main goal of this project.
In this project, Ataa will address the problems identified above, in line with the WoS goals of increasing access to education for crisis-affected children and improving the quality of formal and non-formal education within a protective environment, through the support of these schools in Idleb and Aleppo governorates ( the locations which will be provided with formal and non-formal education explained in the implementation of activities chapter). Ataa will address the most critical needs such as the rehabilitation of damaged learning spaces, including WASH facilities in line with INEE/Sphere standards; support delivering of increased pre and in-service teacher training support in key areas of Basic Teacher Training, inclusion, wellbeing, classroom management, psychosocial support, child protection, child safeguarding & referral systems.
The education in the targeted schools will be (formal and non-formal education) includes the basic and secondary education level, from the first till the twelfth grades which are through teaching the SIG curriculum as well as providing remedial, catch up classes, basic literacy and numeracy and SLP.
The project will provide education opportunities for 10715 children (Female; 5429, Male; 5286) and 537 educational personnel includes headteachers, teachers, cleaners and guards (Female; 285, Male; 251), the percentage of students (51% females and 49% males), the percentage of staff (47% females and 53% males).
Ataa will conduct FGDs with targeted communities to inform them about the goal, outcome, and, activities of the project. Brochures and banners will be used to share information with the communities. Ataa will set a community – based mechanism to make sure that community members can submit their complaints and feedback. feedback tracker will be prepared on monthly basis.
The project will support parents in their children's education and increase the awareness of targeted communities in relation to children education issue. The project also will ease the burden on other schools that can’t accommodate children in safe and quality conditions. Moreover, it will help the host communities to improve their resilience and their capacities.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency Health, Nutrition, Food Security, Shelter and WASH services to populations living in the different states of Federal Republic of Somalia.
project_objective: In this project, QRCS will improve the access and utilization of Emergency integrated health/WASH and Nutrition services for women and children living in the most affected areas in all the states of Somalia using both static and outreach facilities. The static health centres will be strengthen by adding WASH and Nutrition Services, provision of medical and nutrition supplies and the improvement staff capacity. Remote villages will be reached through mobile clinics; community mobilizers and CHWs will be recruited and trained. Among the activities that QRCS will be providing include: Immunization to under 5 children and Women of child bearing age (WCBA); Provision of antenatal and post-natal care to pregnant and lactating mothers, Treatment and control of communicable diseases targeting; Provision of basic lifesaving medical services to sick patients; Treatment of uncomplicated malnourished cases i.e SAM. Identify and refer patients with severe medical cases that requires admission at secondary health facilities after providing first aid services; Referral of complicated malnourished children; Promote the adoption of good hygiene and sanitation practices to the affected communities; Breast feeding promotion and support of infant and young child feeding; Identify and assist in the train of community volunteers on health promotion and education; MUAC screening and identification of malnourished children; Organize community sensitization and mobilization sessions at facility and outreach level of the affected areas; Distribute standard IEC materials for social mobilization; Support distribution of hygiene kits; provision of adapted sanitation infrastructures and related hygiene promotion; MUAC screening for all children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW); Treatment of SAM cases without medical complications; Referral of SAM cases with medical complications and failed appetite test. Under this project, QRCS will scale up its intervention through two fixed integrated health and Nutrition facilities and mobile outreach services targeting 81338 drought affected people IDPs and Host communities. the health services to be offered include outpatient treatment, management of common child illness like Pneumonia, diarrhea, ear infections, fever, provision of immunization services, antenatal care services as well as skilled deliveries .Through this project, the capacity of 45 staff will be improved through training while the 60 community members will also access health education and awareness session on services utilization and communicable disease prevention and treatment

project_name: Community development in site management and coordination of  settlements  in Adado and Dhusamareeb districts
project_objective: The purpose of the project is to enhance the coordination and management of IDP camps in Adado and Dhusamareeb district. This project will target 20,000 beneficiaries (10,000 Adado and 10,000 Dhusamareeb). Most of the IDP camps are manned by gate keepers. The relationship to and with the IDP community is similarly diverse but in the long absence of the Government providing IDPs with assistance and protection, informal managers have often become the primary go to person and provider of support and, to a certain extent, protection, in particular since communities of IDPs are often marginalized and discriminated against because they belong to minorities or are separated from the protection of their clans. Aid diversion has been allegedly high in informal settlements, but the extent of it remains unclear. SSWC intends to establish new community structures and strengthen the existing structures in collaboration with the local authorities in Adado and Dhusamareeb districts. SSWC will focus on creating coordination structures and mechanisms that help the beneficiaries’ access different services in their settlements. Communication channels will be enhanced to foster information sharing in the camps with other service providers in the targeted areas. The project will develop service mapping mechanisms to address the population movements, trends of new arrivals, exiting individuals and returnees in the IDP camps. This will be enhanced by engaging focal points in the camps, the focal points will conduct service mapping and record all the essential needs/gaps in the camps.

project_name: Provision of an improved coordination and self management of IDP camps for newly displaced and protracted internally IDPs in Banadir, Lower Shebelle and Gedo Regions
project_objective: NoFYL will implement emergency sites improvement projects to minimise risks of exclusion and high incidence of protection violations in IDP sites, as well achieving durable solutions. NoFYL will also conduct settlement planning training for settlement leaders; create coordination structures and SOPs for emergency displacements; conduct capacity building trainings for government’s actors and relevant stakeholders; establish/reinforce community mechanisms for communication channels among others. Gender and protection will be mainstreamed in all program activities. Lastly, NoFYL will develop systems to strengthen community self-management to promote durable solutions for displaced people in sites.

project_name: Promote equitable access to services and durable solutions for the Internally Displaced People in Somalia
project_objective: The proposed intervention targets the Internally Displaced People (IDPs) in Benadir, Bay, Bakool, Hiran, Galgadud, Gedo, Middle and Lower Shabelle regions of Somalia who face deplorable living conditions in overcrowded settlements. By delivering a number of interrelated activities to enhance information gathering at site level, stakeholder coordination, camp management, settlement planning and structure, the project will significantly enhance the living conditions of the IDPs and foster durable solutions to their plight.

project_name: Improve access to life-saving unconditional cash transfer and livelihood support to crisis and emergency affected communities through facilitating recovery and resilience to the affected women,men,boys and girls  households in Galgadud and L.Shabele (Afgooye) regions Somalia
project_objective: The project entails to provide immediate access to equitable livelihood assistance to the most vulnerable population in  needs in Galgadud and lower shabelle regions  through provision of unconditional and conditional cash for work to enable restore the lost community asset and ensure community resilience enhancement through this project will be able to provide community capacity building more specifically these in agropastral livelihood or farmers by providing both the inputs and tools to carry out their farming with ease and as well improve their livelihood needs.

project_name: Emergency Interventions, Recovery Solutions: Responding to WASH needs within the Syrian Arab Republic
Food Security in Northern Syria 2019
project_objective:
The project is to fill the gaps in the FSL sector through Improving the food security status of assessed food insecure people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance which planned to be achieved by emergency response to crisis affected vulnerable people with short term food assistance through appropriate modalities, and the provision of flour or bread directly to households or to bakeries, also, it aims to support self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives in the north of Syria through distribution of agricultural inputs, such as seeds, fertilizer, pesticide and equipment; and related training, and support to asset building and asset protection (small livestock and animal feed distribution) including winterization activities; and related training.
We aim to :
Distribute 5,000 food basket monthly for 5,000 HH in need.
Distribute bread for 4,000 HH (200 MT of flour)
Support farmers agricultural Inputs and trainings ( 1850 HH  with wheat seeds , and 600 HH with vegetable seeds)
Targeting of 800 HH by distribute livestock and animal feed.

project_name: Logistics Cluster activities in support of the humanitarian community in South Sudan
project_objective: The Logistics Cluster as a service based cluster and provider of last resort aims to facilitate the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance to the vulnerable population through its logistics coordination support, information management and provision of common services to the humanitarian community in South Sudan

project_name: Provide lifesaving emergency response and life sustaining food assistance
project_objective:
Provide lifesaving emergency response and life-sustaining food assistance for improved food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategy.

Violet aims through this project to provide life-saving assistance through implementing the following activities:
1. RTE distribution for the newly IDPs 
2. MPGs distribution for the newly IDPs 
3. one-off Food baskets distribution for the newly IDPs 
4. Regular distribution of food baskets for 1818 HHs living in Idleb city for four rounds

project_name: Protection and assistance of refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, IDP returnees and host communities
project_objective:
The project will cover Protection and assistance with the overall aim of strengthening the protection of refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced persons as well as host communities affected by the current situation in Libya through life-saving and essential services. 
With regards to refugees and asylum seekers, UNHCR will continue providing urgent life-saving assistance upon disembarkation and in detention centres, advocating for release from and alternatives to detention of refugees and asylum-seekers intercepted or rescued on land or at sea by the authorities and undertaking registration and providing basic aid and information through community centres, outreach partners and hotlines. UNHCR will focus on identifying solutions for refugees and promoting alternatives to the use of smugglers, raising awareness on the dangers along the migration routes and within Libya and strengthening communication to get the messaging out to the right platforms, enhancing inter-state cooperation and government capacities to provide protection and strengthening partnerships to address the problems and deliver much needed responsive services to those affected. UNHCR will also engage in developing mechanisms to protect the most vulnerable persons with specific needs, including survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, victims of trafficking and UASC, or persons of concern to UNHCR in detention and urban settings in Libya. 
UNHCR will expand the programme for IDP protection and assistance through a more enhanced Protection monitoring/assessment, coordination and/or provision of assistance but as well reinforcing assistance to host communities and Libyan civilians in need including individual and community based assistance. The support to IDPs and host communities will impact positively in this context where all communities are in need due to the country current situation. UNHCR will focus on advocacy and outreach to communities, including through information sharing mechanisms to reach IDPs and host communities and support response initiatives of the Libyan authorities. UNHCR’s key priorities in the IDP response is to identify and report critical protection risks, violations of human rights and international humanitarian law. Key activities will include protection monitoring, field missions and strengthened communications with communities. UNHCR will also focus on responding to such risks and violations through various means including establishing proper and confidential referral mechanisms to address immediate needs. As a means to support/enhance the recovery program in conflict-affected areas as well as areas burdening population movements, small-scale projects referred to as QIPs or community-based projects will be supported to create social cohesion between IDPs, returnees, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and host communities in coordination or consultation with host communities and local authorities according to priorities; create rapid conditions for durable solutions towards and return/recovery, and lead to improvement of the protection situation of the people of concern.

project_name: WASH emergency response for people affected by Cyclone Kenneth
project_objective:
UNICEF will target affected households in Cabo Delgado and Nampula Provinces to restore access to WASH services and facilities through a holistic package of interventions that include the following activities:
• Effective WASH sector coordination for emergency response
• Restoration of water supply services from centralized systems focusing on small town water supply systems
• Water supply to accommodation centres / transit camps / resettlement areas 
• Distribution of point-of-use water treatment materials / products, including training and monitoring on proper use at household level.
• Rehabilitation and disinfection of existing water points affected by cyclone / flooding and re-establishment / support for water committees.
• Construction of new water sources for most vulnerable communities / resettlement areas.
• Installation and management of temporary sanitation and bathing facilities in accommodation centres / transit camps and / or institutions.
• Solid waste management (including collection, removal, disposal and drainage) in accommodation centres / transit camps or institutions and other centralized locations with high risk of disease spread.
• Promotion activities for self-construction of household latrines and garbage pits in long-term resettlement and returning areas 
• Dissemination of WASH related messages through mass communication media.
• Community and household level hygiene promotion activities in accommodation centres, return communities, and related institutions.
• Procurement and distribution of WASH related non-food items, with focus on most vulnerable families / households.

project_name: Shelter and Non-Food Items requirements for Relief International
Enhance access to secondary health care and referral services
project_objective: The project is aiming to provide life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian health assistance to affected people, Improve access to secondary health care through supporting health referrals services via the national NGOs in the following governorates: Rural Damascus, Hama , Dara, Homs, NES, Aleppo, Damascus, and other locations in HTR  and areas with severity of scale > 3 . In addition, the project will participate in improving the capacity of secondary and tertiary hospitals to respond to the health needs of about 2,200,000 populations in needed for secondary health care. From the cross-border approach, WHO Gaziantep hub strengthens the access to secondary health care through technical expertise and capacity building, operational support, basic rehabilitation, and by providing equipment, medicines and medical supplies through the cross border supply chain.

project_name: Increased access to food through provision of conditional and unconditional cash transfers, provision of agricultural inputs, solar powered pump and drip irrigation equipment for small scale farmers, in south central regions
project_objective: This programme is designed to improve the immediate food needs for the people affected by floods, drought, conflict and diseases, that are in the acute food insecurity category in South Central Somalia regions. The purpose is supporting them to protect their livelihoods, enable local food production and adoption of resilient strategies to mitigate against the recurrent shocks. The project conception is that the beneficiary targeted will be determined based on the needs, which shall majorly be determined by IPC levels, and mostly IDPs, with host community. The interventions will focus on emergency response for 2000 dis-aggregated acutely affected households, and these will benefit from unconditional cash transfer, with the amount of distribution being MEB-based per region of target. Transitional interventions will also be implemented targeting communities that need to restore their lost livelihoods through building of assets while participating in conditional and restricted cash transfers. These include agriculture input to 200 farmers through introduction to new affordable solar powered drip irrigation system for non-riverine small-scale farmers, fodder production by the destitute agro-pastoralists, animal health support targeting 6,000 pastoralists and provision of productive assets and enterprise development and skills enhancement for 200 youth. ZZF will mainstream protection in its programming ensuring that only deserving cases are selected to gain in the project. In addition, gender will be a major consideration through determination of intervention participants. A PDM will be conducted for all distribution activities to measure effectiveness of the project.

project_name: Reinforcing surveillance systems for the early detection, prevention and control of potential epidemic prone diseases and outbreak response in Syria
Improving access to Primary Health Care (PHC) services
project_objective: The project aims to improve and sustain delivery of standard basic Primary health care services addressing chronic diseases, elderly Health, reproductive health including services for adolescents, child and maternal health, oral health & laboratory services at PHC level to improve health status of the affected populations across Syria.

project_name: Strengthening health information systems for evidence-based emergency response and resilience
project_objective: The aim of the project is to strengthen health information systems for emergency response and resilience across the country. The information generated from the health information systems provides up-to-date information on functionality of facilities, availability of services, and accessibility of beneficiaries. All health partners are/would report including those operating public, NGO, private health facilities in addition to cross-border partners.

project_name: TURKEY - World Health Organization
Improved safe access to inclusive and quality education for most vulnerable children and teachers in the Gaza strip
project_objective: The project will support 8,000 vulnerable and underserved children and 350 teachers through the provision of emergency education supplies and school-based psychosocial support. It will also provide remedial education to vulnerable school-aged children including training of teachers on the home-based learning methodology. Furthermore, it will support conflict-affected students with disability with assistive devices to ensure their equal access to inclusive quality learning opportunities.

project_name: Provision of integrated emergency preventive and curative nutrition support project to drought and cyclone affected communities in Somaliland
project_objective:
ANPPACNSOM is currently responding to the emergency nutrition situation in parts of Waqooyi-Galbeed region with SHF and UNICEF funding providing services in 9 health centers, 1 SC and 4 mobile OTP. ANPPCANSOM seeks to expand and scale up its nutrition support to areas with dire needs. This approach, which is in line with the Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan, will be primarily aimed at providing lifesaving nutrition interventions. 

ANPPCANSOM drought response plan will scale up treatment of severe acute malnutrition and moderate acute malnutrition by increasing the number of static and mobile outreach clinics from 9 to 23 subsequently reaching an estimated 2450 children affected by SAM and 1260 children with MAM while maintaining treatment outcomes consistent with Sphere standards. 

ANPPCANSOM will build on and sustain the delivery of a holistic basic nutrition services package (BNSP) in priority to internally displaced people and their host communities and other socially marginalized groups in pastoral and hard to reach areas while ensuring the inclusion of treatment, promotion and prevention components in this project.

ANPPCANSOM will use the combined protocol for the management of acute malnutrition in close consultation and coordination with Somali Nutrition Cluster, Somaliland Nutrition Working Group and other nutrition partners including MOH, UNICEF and WFP. Meanwhile, ANPPCANSOM proposed OTP sites (fixed and mobile) will provide a platform for the delivery of integrated services while ensuring full community participation in service delivery.

project_name: Prevent risk associated with acute malnutrition among boys, girls and PLWs in Elwak, and Baardhere districts of Gedo region Somalia
project_objective: This project is an integrated response around Nutrition. It is intended to mitigate the physical and protection consequences of drought on populations and communities directly affected in Elwak, and Baardhere of Gedo region, The main objective of this project is to provide integrated life-saving emergency Nutrition services to 19,700 drought affected direct beneficiaries and intends to achieve the following, capacity building of nutrition staff on IMAM/IYCF services, infant young child feeding best practices (IYCF), as well as conduct caregivers infant and young child feeding practices, IYCF promotion session for better information dissemination to the caregivers in the project area. Referral of malnourished children with complicated cases will be done to the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) centers managed by HARD and other actors in the program areas thus providing more holistic opportunity to the target beneficiaries HARD will closely coordinate with Local MOH as well as Federal level MOH and social mobilizers, elders all involved in activities on mobilizing communities. To support increase access to basic nutrition services in the area

project_name: Emergency shelter and NFI for the most vulnerable  returnees and IDPS  and Host communities affected by drought and conflict in Darkenley, Daynille and Afgooye corridor
project_objective:
This project is aimed at  improving the lives of 22092 (3682HH) newly displaced individuals (10604 women, 7070 men, 2651 girls and 1767 boys) living in precarious crowded settlements, without sufficient access to basic services, with poor shelter conditions that raise protection and health concerns.  This will be achieved through provision of emergency kits and NFIs to the most vulnerable IDPs in Nimcaturabi and salama2 camps in Daynille, Boqolson and Macin Alle camps in dharkinley and Balsar and maslah camps in Afgoye.
The target population (women, girls, men, boys, the elderly and people with disabilities) living in the IDP camps reside in small makeshift structures made of rugs, recycled cloth and card boards. These structures are insufficient in so far as providing the basic physical protection, privacy, dignity, or protection from extreme climatic conditions
Included will be returnees and IDPs living in deplorable conditions and in need of emergency shelters and NFIs.  The most vulnerable  men, women, boys ,girls and  the elderly  will be prioritized during the beneficiary selection process. Save Somali Women and Children will Introduce special arrangements for persons who have difficulty accessing the distribution point or unable to carry the kits. Save Somali Women and Children will directly implement  the activities.

project_name: SAUVER DES VIES DANS LE DISTRICT SANITAIRE DE YOUWAROU ,  REGION DE MOPTI
project_objective: Le projet contribuera  en général à améliorer la santé de la population .en particulier  les enfants de moins de 5 ans , les femmes enceintes et allaitantes   affectés par la crise sécuritaire   grâce à l’accès aux services de santé  de qualité dans le district sanitaire de YOUWAROU.

project_name: Emergency assistance to conflict-affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon: Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
project_objective:
Maintain and strengthen the system of data collection in the Far North region of
Cameroon through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the
coordination of humanitarian activities. The DTM aims to provide reliable and up to
date information on the numbers of displaced populations, displacement trends and
reasons for displacement to better assist and inform the governmental and
humanitarian response. The assessed groups consist of internally displaced
persons, unregistered refugees and returnees. The data will be disaggregated by
age and sex. The DTM has the potential to be expanded and/or modified to take
into account changes in the regional context.

project_name: Improved Educational Opportunities and Psychosocial well-being of Conflict-Affected Children in Syria
project_objective:
The conflict in Syria is entering its ninth year and is ranked a Level 3 crisis, resulting in 13 million people in need of humanitarian assistance. In Dara’a governorate, where the uprising originally started in 2011, up to 300 000 children are in need of assistance in education and psychosocial support. Education services are especially poor in communities to which inhabitants are returning to after a period of displacement.

The operational strategy of Fida will focus on providing safe learning spaces and psychosocial support for primary school aged children. The aim is to target two sub-districts of Kherbet Ghazaleh and Dara’a Al-Balad in southern Syria. Twelve schools will be rehabilitated, including classrooms and latrines. 5250 school children will receive school supplies. Out-of-school children and academically challenged students, including children with disabilities, will receive catch-up and remedial education during the summer to enable them to take part in the new school year. 

Teachers report that they feel ill-equipped to provide psychosocial support to students who have lived through the crisis and are often traumatized. Therefore, 100 teachers will be trained to provide psychosocial support for their students and to identify specific traumas. 800 children will improve their resilience in crisis through attending a summer school with activities that support their educational and psychosocial well-being. 400 parents of children will receive PSS group support to enhance their ability to provide PSS support for their children.

project_name: Projet de réponse d'urgence pour les populations vulnérables du département de N'Guigmi, affectées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad
project_objective: La réponse proposée dans le cadre de ce projet entend contribuer à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations les plus vulnérables, et notamment de réduire la morbidité et mortalité maternelle, néonatale et infantile chez les populations affectées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad, dans le département de N'Guigmi (région de Diffa) au Niger.

project_name: Humanitarian assistance for communities and IDPs affected by the civil war in the provinces of Aleppo and Idlib in Syria
project_objective: Providing life-saving assistance and improving living conditions of IDPs and host communities through the distribution of food and non-food items, provision of WASH supply, repair of informal settlements/houses for IDPs and solid waste disposal in the provinces Idlib and Aleppo in Syria.

project_name: LEBANON - Action Contre la Faim
Respuesta en seguridad nutricional integrada de emergencia a la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis alimentaria y nutricional en Venezuela.
project_objective:
Este proyecto contribuye a mejorar la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional y la resiliencia de individuos y familias vulnerables con enfoque multisectorial que comprende actividades relacionada a seguridad alimentaria, nutrición y agua, saneamiento e higiene básica.
La implementación se hará con el apoyo de dos organizaciones socias nacionales que están presentes en colegios (FUDEP) y centros comunitarios y vicarías (CESAP).
A nivel individual, se plantea la distribución de alimentos en escuelas y centros comunitarios/vicarías. En las escuelas, la distribución se complementará con el provisto por el gobierno, apuntando a asegurar el 50% de los requerimientos diarios de energía y proteínas. Las distribuciones de alimentos también se organizarán en cocinas comunitarias de vicarías. Las “madres procesadoras” participarán de capacitaciones en aspectos de planificación de menús y buenas prácticas de manejo de alimentos. Con un componente de nutrición, se detectará, brindará tratamiento y monitoreará los casos de desnutrición y en riesgo nutricional en niños/as y mujeres embarazadas/lactantes. Los/as niños/as identificados en desnutrición aguda, moderada o severa sin complicaciones entrarán en un programa de tratamiento y seguimiento semanal hasta su recuperación, por un equipo de personal médico (pediatras y nutricionistas) capacitado; los casos con complicaciones médicas serán referidos a hospitales locales, mientras que las mujeres lactantes y embarazadas en riesgo nutricional recibirán tratamiento mediante distribución de supercereales. Este componente también brindará asistencia a niños y niñas con riesgo de desnutrición aguda con un enfoque preventivo y basado en la comunidad usando un suplemento nutricional. 
Se mejorará el acceso a condiciones de higiene adecuadas y agua potable segura en escuelas y centros comunitarios/vicarías. Se distribuirán productos de higiene para sus instalaciones, y donde sea necesario se realizará rehabilitación de baños y de puntos de agua. Se instalarán sistemas de producción de cloro in-situ para tratamiento del agua para consumo e higiene, junto con la formación de puntos focales y la entrega de kits de mantenimiento y monitoreo de calidad. Se capacitará a docentes y referentes con respecto a buenas prácticas de higiene, los cuales realizarán sesiones de promoción de higiene con niños/as y madres. Se realizará la entrega de kits de higiene básica para hogares que se benefician de los comedores escolares y vicarías.
A nivel comunitario, se mejorará el acceso a agua de calidad y cantidad adecuada a través de rehabilitación de fuentes de agua y se distribuirán materiales para el tratamiento de agua domiciliario, se reactivarán y apoyarán las mesas de agua y se llevarán a cabo campañas de buenos hábitos de higiene. En relación a nutrición se implementarán acciones preventivas para reducción de deficiencias nutricionales mediante desparasitación dirigidas a niños/as menores de 5 años y suplementación con micronutrientes en polvo; las mujeres embarazadas recibirán suplementación con ácido fólico y hierro.
A nivel familiar, se brindará apoyo a 400 familias de niños/as y mujeres embarazadas/lactantes identificadas en riesgo nutricional a través de un pilotaje de transferencia monetaria para familias asentadas en contexto urbano (a través de dinero/cupones con un valor monetario que permita cubrir necesidades alimentarias por un periodo de 6 meses) y la distribución de insumos productivos para familias rurales (junto con entrega de alimentos durante 4 meses mientras activan y mejoran dieta con producción propia). 100 de estas familias participarán en un proyecto piloto desde el enfoque BabyWASH: se asegurará la higiene básica del hogar y personal por un periodo de 6 meses. En estos hogares y los 5 más vulnerables de su comunidad se llevarán a cabo mejoras en la infraestructura y capacitación con el fin alcanzar hábitos y entornos de cuidado adecuados desde el enfoque de la ventana de los 1,000 días.

project_name: Improved Food Security, Livelihoods, and Protection Outcomes in Jebel Mara
project_objective: This project will address the food security and livelihoods needs vulnerable households in the Jebel Mara area of Central Darfur through improving agricultural and livestock production and providing vocational training and start-up materials for youth. project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle aux populations vulnérabilisées par la crise au Nord du Mali, dans la région de Tombouctou
project_objective:
L’intervention d’ALIMA et de son partenaire malien AMCP en 2019 vise à contribuer à la réduction de la
morbidité et mortalité des populations affectées par la crise dans le nord dans la région de Tombouctou
(DS de Goundam). Dans le DS visé par ALIMA/AMCP, l’action vise plus spécifiquement à améliorer
l’accès et l’utilisation des soins médico-nutritionnels gratuits et de qualité pour les populations affectées
par la crise sécuritaire et ses conséquences socio-économiques dans les zones précitées, et plus
spécifiquement pour les femmes enceintes et allaitantes et les enfants de moins de 5 ans, qui
représentent les plus vulnérables dans ces zones. Dans la région de Tombouctou, l’intervention
d’ALIMA/AMCP se focalisera sur la santé et la nutrition. Au total, ce sont 26 CSCom et 1 CSRef qui
seront appuyés lors de l’intervention. ALIMA/AMCP renforcera aussi les activités curatives pour les
populations qui n’ont pas accès aux soins primaires, à travers une clinique mobile dans le DS de
Goundam notamment pour les populations dont l’accès aux centres de santé est limité par la distance
géographique (populations situées au-delà de 15km des CSCom) et les populations de déplacés
internes après évaluations des besoins.
Le volet communautaire sera également renforcé, en incluant une campagne de formation PB mères
pour les femmes en âge de procréer. Enfin, ALIMA/AMCP apportera une contribution à la veille
sanitaire et humanitaire et éventuellement participer à la réponse aux situations d’urgences à travers le
mécanisme RRM.

project_name: Projet d’assistance en soins de santé  aux personne vulnérables affecte par la crise du bassin du lac Tchad ( refugiés,retounés ainsi que les déplaces interne)
project_objective:
Depuis 2009, l’insécurité liée à l’insurrection du groupe Boko Haram et à sa répression s’est diffusée depuis le cœur du Borno nigérian vers tout le nord-est du pays puis vers les zones frontalières des pays voisins, Cameroun, Niger et Tchad. La crise a affecté progressivement toute la région du lac Tchad, un des grands espaces transfrontaliers de l’Afrique sahélienne, à la charnière de l’Afrique des savanes et du désert, de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et de l’Afrique centrale et orientale.
En septembre 2018, OCHA estimait à 139 000 le nombre de personnes qui ont quitté les îles du Lac Tchad pour trouver refuge sur la terre ferme, laissant derrière elles leurs biens et leurs moyens de subsistance. Ces populations se réfugient souvent dans des camps de fortune, ou trouvent refuge auprès de villages d’accueil, plus de 120 villages ou sites ont accueilli des personnes déplacées. Les besoins humanitaires de ces populations restent considérables, tandis que les populations locales, déjà très vulnérables, subissent une pression supplémentaire du fait de leur arrivée.
Cela a des graves conséquences dans la région du Lac au Tchad où la conjonction de ce conflit armé associé à une crise écologique ont poussé au bord de la famine près de 8 millions de personnes.
Cette situation a aggravé les indicateurs d’un système de santé qui étaient déjà faible. Les centres de santé manquent d’équipement, de médicaments et personnel qualifié pour fournir des services médicaux suffisants de qualité.

project_name: 2019 Humanitarian WASH in NE Nigeria: sustaining services and reaching newly displaced population
project_objective:
The project will sustain water supply, sanitation and hygiene services being provided in response to protracted displacement, loss of dignity and human suffering of population affected by armed conflict in north-east Nigeria and expand services to reach newly displaced persons from hard to reach areas and populations living in areas affected by recurrent incidents of disease outbreaks such as cholera, acute watery diarrhoea, hepatitis E and other emergency disasters.  The response will be integrated with protection, health,  nutrition and education in emergency response projects supported by UNICEF and other humanitarian agencies. The purpose of the project is to provide immediate life saving WASH services in hard to reach areas, sustain and improve services for populations living in areas of protracted emergencies and support evolving links between emergency programming and early recovery and development in areas of return.  The following interventions and targets are planned:
i) 65,000 people (new arrivals or people living in hot spot areas of disease outbreak) access temporary services for safe water supply (15 lppd for 60 days) 
ii) 136,000 people newly affected by conflict access safe water   
iii) 1,550,000 people affected by conflict and living in IDP camps and host communities access risk-informed hygiene promotion and behaviour change messages 
iv) 75 institution (health/nutrition centre, public places, Learning spaces, CFS) provided water supply source or connection, serving population affected by conflict or disease outbreaks
v) 75 Institutional latrines (2-drop hole VIP latrine with hand washing facilities) provided in areas of return and host communities; or in IDP camps 
vi) 5,000 households affected by conflict receive cash transfers for WASH commodities and supplies
vii) 400,000 people affected by conflict gain new access to improved sanitation in IDP camps
viii) 480,000 people affected by conflict or disease outbreaks receive initial WASH response kits or replenishment kits.
ix) 200,000 women of child bearing age receive reusable sanitary kits distributed (pack of 6 per person)
x)  77,500 Households with SAM affected children receive a SAM NFI package
vi) 4,000 latrines per months are desludged to sustain use of improved latrines in IDP camps; 16,000 cu m of sludge removed per month, benefitting 500,000 internally displaced persons.

project_name: Reduced threat of ERW and improved support to ERW survivors in north-west Syria.
project_objective:
HALO with its implementing partners will deliver a comprehensive approach to Mine Action in NW Syria, involving Contamination Impact Survey (CIS), an enhanced version of CIS (ECIS), Risk Education (RE), Victim Data Collection (VDC) and Victim Assistance (VA).  Note: the key difference between ECIS and CIS is the identification, marking and reporting of ERW items. HALO will also seek to extend the scope of its activities to Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Disposal. 

To better understand the threat that ERW poses, HALO will conduct systematic CIS in 111 communities and ECIS in 692 communities across Idleb and Aleppo governorates. Under this activity, teams will visit communities, with the overall goal to identify, mark and report ERW contamination and to record its impact on the community. Data will be used to identify areas of highest priority for RE, create contamination maps, and provide essential information for future ERW clearance. The scale of this activity is unprecedented but is required to inform current and future ERW disposal/clearance, as well as immediately improving the awareness and safety of affected communities. ECIS activities will be coordinated from HALO’s operation room in Jordan, staffed by technical personnel. If the relevant authorizations are granted from the Turkish government, HALO will also establish ERW survey and disposal teams trained to complete surface-located ERW tasks (excluding IEDs) via a 6-week course derived from International Mine Action Standards (IMAS). They will be deployed under the direct control of HALO’s operations room in Jordan. At a later stage in 2019, they will complete advanced training relevant to the detection and disposal of sub-surface ERW (excluding IEDs). Extension to IED disposal requires a separate 4-week course. All disposal activities will be conducted via the use of thermite torches (T-Jets). No high explosives will be used. HALO’s ERW survey and disposal objectives for NW Syria are based on its experience in southern Syria in 2018.     

HALO will provide RE to 108,472 beneficiaries in 2019 (18,364 men, 17,692 women, 38,248 boys and 34,168 girls). A particular focus will be placed on those who are most at risk of accident (including children, young men and IDPs). Two new RE ‘Training of Trainer’ (ToT) Trainers will build on the work already underway by HALO’s existing RE ToT Trainer in NW Syria. Together, they will support NGOs currently delivering RE to vulnerable communities and IDPs, as well as NGOs willing to deliver RE along with other activities; improving the relevance, integration and reach of RE messaging across all relevant sectors. 

HALO will also collect information about ERW accidents and victims (survivors) through VDC which will be used to develop a better understanding of how and why accidents are occurring, enabling HALO, and other actors, to better tailor RE and VA activities.

In 2019, HALO and one of its implementing partners will implement a new VA initiative, where approx. 200 survivors of ERW accidents will benefit from initial basic health screening, referrals to reputable service providers and a one-off distribution of basic medical and hygiene items. The project will also support survivors (approx. 1,200) through the establishment of a rehabilitation centre and 2 x mobile outreach teams, providing physiotherapy, mental health and psycho-social support (MHPSS), peer support counselling, and referrals to a prosthetics centre. A social protection scheme providing ‘in-kind’ support to selected survivors will also be implemented. Additionally, in order to promote workplace inclusion, 5 survivors will be recruited, trained and employed by HALO’s partner.

project_name: Enhancing and improving Water and Sanitation Needs of Men, Women and Children in disaster prone areas in Somalia
project_objective:
Although last years Somalia hosted severe droughts that resulted in wide displacement across the country, the very recent Gu rains presented a hope for the affected communities though pastoral communities haven’t yet well recovered. Since Somalia doesn’t utilize rain water by harvesting means including durable dams, efficient subtraction of underground water, yet water scarcity persists in large parts of the country. Deteriorating Sanitation conditions of displaced people signals the importance of a collective efforts to end open defecation and maintain existing latrines through comprehensive hygiene and sanitation promotion. The ongoing conflicts continue to reduce the resilience of communities, trigger displacement and impede civilians’ access to basic services and humanitarians’ access to those in need. Resilience of pastoral communes is getting weaker as well as agricultural communities due to lack of comprehensive support that enables them to move forward. Communities used to have permanent water sources in riverine areas started to appeal for water as water table gets down and hence causing water sources to dry and thereby engage in unhygienic way of water collection that increase the likelihood of AWD outbreaks as happened during the last years in major and minor cities along Shabelle river.  

However, Zamzam Foundation has embarked on a strategy that contributes to the wellbeing of affected communities who are in need especially the most vulnerable people, IDPs and people at risk of AWD/ cholera, acute malnourished children, people living in affected areas and children attending school through provision of sufficient and clean water and provision of healthy sanitation facilities and by Engaging communities to build their own latrines through the CLTS approach, and raising and promotion of communities' awareness to hazards of misuse of the sanitation facilities and negligence of good hygiene practices to deter and prevent diseases through targeted and comprehensive hygiene promotion activities. However, Project activities will be implemented in close coordination with other clusters (shelter, nutrition, health and education) to respond to life-saving emergencies.

project_name: Shelter and NFI response in North - East Nigeria.
project_objective:
Since the beginning of 2015, the North-East of Nigeria has witnessed an increase in violence perpetrated by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG), causing a major humanitarian crisis. The intensification of attacks has resulted in prolonged insecurity, exacerbating the plight of vulnerable civilians and triggering waves of forced displacement as well as violation of human rights resulting into different forms of Gender Based Violence (GBV). More than 1.9 million individuals have been displaced due to the conflict and displacement continues to be a significant factor in 2018, with the highest number of displacements and returns occurring in Adamawa, Borno, and Yobe States(IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Round 24). Despite the fact that some displaced individuals have started to return home after relative security has been restored and more areas are now accessible to humanitarian actors, the situation on the ground remains dire and several remain in inaccessible areas. The Displacement Management and Shelter/(Non-Food Item(NFI) Sector has recorded that over 40 camps out of the 148 camps in Borno state are over-congested, i.e. 1,000 individuals above camp capacity – the most congested camp has 36,000 individuals above camp capacity (Muna Garage).
To support displaced individuals and new arrivals under these contextual dynamics, IOM  through this project will contribute to ensuring an adequate humanitarian rapid response to needs. This will include the continuation and scaling-up of shelter and NFI support for people in camp and camp-like settings (including for new arrivals), through the establishment of transit and emergency shelters, the distribution of emergency shelter kits and NFI kits, as well as care, maintenance and upgrading of existing shelters, in accordance with Sector standards. 
To compliment ongoing emergency shelter response activities, this project further proposes to enhance recovery support, particularly as it pertains to supporting the more than 1.5 million individuals who have returned to their areas of origin in the three states. With the principal aim of promoting safe, dignified and voluntary returns and preventing situations of secondary displacement, IOM will support the rehabilitation of community infrastructure (including markets, hospitals, schools, etc.), shelter solutions for returnees and host communities (shelter repair kits, transitional shelters).
Clear-cut focus will be given to mainstreaming GBV into shelter and settlement response activities during site planning and distribution of shelter and NFI related kits. Designs of shelter solutions will also take into account privacy, security and comfort of beneficiaries. IOM plans to guarantee the participation of Women, Men, Girls and Boys as equals to ensure that the special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and different age group, and specifically address women's and girls' specific needs, especially in terms of protection and access concerns. To illustrate, (1) the content of NFI kits will be tailored in accordance to the needs of women as well as men; (2) site plans will be developed to mitigate the risk of GBV. All activities related to this project will equally benefit women and men, girls and boys and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. In regard to assessment, monitoring and evaluation of gender specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels with them where possible, and all activities will be centered on Do No Harm principles.

project_name: Improved WASH services to the conflict affected population in North-East Nigeria.
project_objective:
Nigeria’s North-East continues to experience intricate and multi-faceted humanitarian crisis in the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector, as a result of the ongoing protracted conflict, unpredictable and continuous large-scale population displacements, recurrent large-scale cholera epidemics and seasonal flooding and fierce storms and winds. 3.4 million people need support to access safe water and basic sanitation facilities across the three most affected states (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states). The main drivers of vulnerabilities related to WASH are closely linked to the conflict, including recurrent, unpredictable and continuous population displacements. They are also a result of pre-existing low levels of WASH services.
With the protracted displacement crisis WASH solutions are needed, particularly in 43 LGAs across Borno and Adamawa states. With congested populations in displacement sites, especially in 15 LGAs and wards in Borno State, water-borne diseases spread rapidly. Spiraling cholera outbreaks have taken hold each year. In 2018, the cholera outbreak has affected 18 LGAs with a total of 4,250 cases . In addition, 1.5 million people in the affected LGAs , including IDPs and host communities, are considered at risk and require cholera prevention interventions.  
Flooding, fierce winds and sand storms have resulted into substantial damages of WASH infrastructures. In 2018, at least 20 per cent and 28 per cent of IDPs living in camps in Borno and Adamawa states respectively have been seriously affected as a sizeable number of latrines, showers, handwashing points, and solar panels got partially or totally destroyed, affecting access to WASH facilities and services. These conditions contribute to a more insecure environment for the population, further comprising their safety and dignity, and exacerbating risks of exposure and vulnerabilities to GBV. New arrivals from hard-to-reach areas, especially women and children, are particularly at risk and need urgent WASH support. They include at least 100,000 children under five and 30,000 pregnant and lactating women across nine LGAs in Borno State and two LGAs in Yobe State. 

3.4 million people urgently need sustained, equitable and safe access of appropriate WASH services. This includes 1.1 million IDPs, 664,860 individuals in host communities, 867,233 returnees and 818,170 people in hard-to-reach areas.  New arrivals from hard-to-reach areas as well as host communities and displacement sites receiving those people need to be prioritized, especially in already congested sites. With the rainy season (during the months of April-September)  exacerbating issues regarding road access to certain LGAs, especially in Borno State, the delivery of humanitarian supplies and material is rendered impossible, leaving people in those locations without access to safe water and sanitation facilities. 

In response to the needs identified and in contribution to strategic Sector objective 1, 2 and 3 of the WASH sector, IOM will scale-up its provision of WASH services targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host community in camp and camp-like settings. 
To this end, IOM will (A) Ensure safe access to safe water facilities and services through the drilling, installation, maintenance and rehabilitation of boreholes; (B) Ensure safe access to sanitation facilities (latrines, showers, handwashing stations) through the operation and maintenance of existing facilities and the construction of additional gender segregated facilities; (C) Promote improved sanitation outcomes and practices in targeted settings through increased capacity of established community based committees. (D) Ensure environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in operation area through establishment of WASH Committee including- male and female community members, procurement and distribution of tools and equipment; (E) Distribution of WASH non-food items (NFI); (F) Capacity building and partnership with WASH partners and stakeholders  
The IOM WASH project will be implemented in three States of North East Nigeria; Borno (20 LGAs), Adamawa (6 LGAs) and Yobe State (4 LGAs), targeting 210,000 individuals. 
IOM ensures that all WASH activities take into consideration the gender-specific needs of project beneficiaries. Through this project, IOM plans to guarantee the participation of female, girls, boys and males as equals to ensure that the special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and age group, and specifically address women and girls’ specific needs, such as Menstrual hygiene management (MHM).. All activities related to this project will equally benefit women and men, girls and boys and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. In regards to assessment, monitoring and evaluation of gender specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels with them where possible. IOM will ensure that Do No Harm principles are adhered to throughout WASH interventions, particularly when it comes to WASH activities pertaining to latrine and water point locations and construction. The IOM WASH Team consist of both male and female staff members, which is an important component to ensure that both males and females are consulted and reached through IOM’s interventions. It also enables better monitoring of the true impact of interventions as it will ensure that women’s and girl’s voices are taking into consideration/promoted.

Despite the fact that some displaced individuals have started to return home after relative security has been restored and more areas are now accessible to humanitarian actors, the situation on the ground remains dire and several remain in inaccessible areas.

project_name: Rehabilitating and Expanding MNCH Services in Returnee and Host Communities in BAY
project_objective:
Prior to the insurgency, the Northeast had some of the worst MNCH indices in the country. PHC systems have collapsed as a result of the armed conflict and MNCH services have been slower in response and recovery than other PHC services.
This project aims to rehabilitate BEmONC and expand CEmONC in health facilities in returnee and host communities. Using a double pronged strategy, rehabilitation and expansion will be done to a level in congruence with emergency needs and minimum standard expected of the level of care the facilities offers in the PHC system i.e. PHC post, clinic or center. Children under five (especially neonates & infants) and women of child bearing age (especially pregnant women & new mothers) will be reached through demand creation activities, fixed and outreach service delivery mechanisms.

project_name: Shelter and NFI response to the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations in northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Through this project, NRC aims to provide immediate and reliable response to unmet need in the Northeast Nigeria including Dikwa, Munguno, Ngazai and Mobbar LGA and other newly accessible areas. 
In accordance with the NRC’s operational location and its program response strategy, NRC will implement shelter and NFI provision to enable targeted households to access timely the improved better living and protective living condition. The NRC shelter response will also include emergency shelter package, which will consist by providing the emergency shelter and NFI kits while the most and adapted robust shelter response will be designed. The NRC response strategy will also include technical training to enable local carpenter to build and maintain better the provided shelter and the provision of habitability measure training and awareness for the improvement and maintaining the healthier living environment. 
Following the NRC community base approach, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the traditional leaders, the affected group representation and other stockholders (on ground humanitarian actors including the CCCM agency) to establish the Beneficiary Selection Committee (BSC) through which NRC will emphasize about the project objectives and beneficiary selection criteria. In order to strengthen the project impact, NRC will coordinate the response with other partners through the shelter sector in providing rapid and timely delivery and avoid gaps and duplication of efforts

project_objective: The intervention aims to provide a wide-ranging support from emergency to regular food assistance as well as household and community based agricultural, livestock and livelihoods assistance. The project aims to target populations who are both foods insecure as well as at risk of food insecurity through multiple activities but mutually reinforcing activities to ensure that all four pillars of food security related to access, availability, utilization and stability of food are adequately addressed through lifesaving, life-sustaining, appropriate resilience, and early recovery interventions.

project_name: Provision of inclusive & quality education in safe Educational environment for girls and boys (aged between 5 – 17 years) .
project_objective:
The project aims to support the Education opportunities in north of Syria for the most vulnerable Syrian children (girls and boys, considering; physically disabled children, adolescents and upper-age girls ). QC will provide complementary Education services to improve the educational infrastructure that increase physical access to schools for all children. Also, the project is designed to enhance the quality of Education through building capacity of teachers and schools’ admin staff and support their monthly stipends as well as schools running costs in addition to distribute teaching and learning materials, stationery and school bags to both children and teachers (girls, boys, females, males). 
Finally, and in regard to system strengthening, the project will respond to the gap of school textbooks by printing and distributing educational curriculum in place, considering the sensitivities of the Syrian crisis.
QC intervention is planned to cover all the Education objectives after 8 years of the Syrian crisis that imposes education as urgent priority to prevent a lost generation.

project_name: Imparting Vocational Training and Technical Skills for 2340 young women and men in North Syria
project_objective: The project comprises on a broad-based market assessment of the trades and skills which are in sever need in the north of Syria after the long years of conflict, delivering technical and vocational training for young women and men, offering support to establish and run small shops and home-based businesses and linking young entrepreneurs with potential markets. Potential entrepreneurs will be selected through detailed assessment. After completion of the training, QC will execute a small grant scheme including provision of vocational kits. This will enable the trainees to start their income generating ventures. QC will thoroughly monitor the business and job efficiency status of the participants in order to ensure project effectiveness.

project_name: Enhance Resilience through Rehabilitation of WASH Infrastructure in Idleb & Aleppo Governorates
project_objective:
QC will conduct an identification/ assessment of existing water sources through a systematic assessment/ mapping, including the functionality status, major issues (if not functional) and estimated number of populations benefitting from the water source in the targeted areas. Based on the results of the assessment, ,the project will provide safe water fitted by submersible pumps, for communities that do not have access to water stations. QC will choose to repair/reconstruct water sources over constructing new water facilities.
In order to monitor the effectiveness of this result, reports will be maintained by assistant engineers, tracking the number of IDPs/host communities who have access to safe drinking water, and the percentage of beneficiaries who have access to functional water sources. In addition to this, water quality tests will be conducted and the number of main stations and sub stations which are functional will also be monitored.

Fuel will be required for running the generators, which operate the pumps, powering the movement of water to cities, from the water stations. Engine oil, oil and diesel filters are necessary for the ongoing maintenance of these generators. The electrical panelboards are the electrical circuitry running the water station, which control the operation of the generators.

Water will be treated with chlorine, to ensure the safe consumption by beneficiaries. Additionally, dosing chlorine pumps provide the correct amount of chlorine treatment, just outside of the water well, in order to ensure that water is appropriate for human consumption. Water testing will be completed on a daily, weekly and monthly basis, in order to ensure water quality. Water samples will be taken at random locations throughout the entire water network and tested for Free Residual Chlorine (FRC) and microbiological presence, ensuring that the water is pathogen free.
QC will meet with the local council and local water authority to explain how the repair and rehabilitation of the systems will be conducted, and organize trainings for them in order to continue the water pumping after the project is completed through the collection system, which secures the sustainability of the service.

For those HHs that aren’t able to connect to the city water network, metal tanks and safe and clean water tankers will be distributed to them.
The sewage systems in the most urban areas/district capitals in northern Syria, discharge to a network of sewage ponds that provide secondary treatment for sewage. In assessments carried out by QC’s team, it was found that some of the sewage systems are provided with pumps and power supply for pumping the wastewater, through the piped network to the ponds. Some of these ponds are situated alongside an existing natural water system. As long as households have access to a sufficient and reliable water supply as well as support to the pumping system, wastewater will move through the network consistently. However, there are blockages and leakages in the sewage system, as with any network. Thus, QC will support the target communities with resources to repair blockages and leaks, so the system is in good working order.
The project team will conduct hygiene promotion sessions through a hygiene promotion team to promote diseases prevention mechanisms, focusing on the most vulnerable groups, such as children < 5 years, lactating mothers and pregnant women, the elderly and households with critically ill family members, and then hygiene kits will be distributed to the targeted groups.

project_objective: This project will target IDPs and returnees in three affected states, Yobe, Adamawa and Borno with provision of emergency shelters, Non-food Items (NFIs), transitional and shelter repair kits as protection live-saving assistance aligned with Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM Sector strategic objectives for the HRP 2019. In 2018 UNHCR continued to effectively respond to shelter needs with a total of 5,231 households, 26,155 individuals in formal and informal camps, host communities and newly accessible areas. As the number of returns and displacement increases due to military operations, there is need to provide shelter related assistance for returnees who are residing in their plots and as well as for host families whose resources have been overstretched. Subsequently acknowledging that the humanitarian situation is likely to further deteriorate; there is need to provide shelters and NFIs for life-saving emergency assistance to promote the protection, safety and dignity of affected Persons of Concern (PoCs). Despite the achievements in the past, the continuous needs for IDPs, though shaped by very different dynamics, revealed that quite a significant majority of people are living in congested camps. The recently concluded shelter needs assessment carried out in September 2018 by Shelter/ NFI and CCCM Sector actors indicated that a total of 265,332 HHs are in need of shelter assistance with 82,144 HHs in camps while as 183, 188 HHs in host communities. In 2019, UNHCR shall build upon progress being made in 2018 and proposes to respond to unmet needs of IDPs in Adamawa (Fufore, Hong, Yola North, Yola South, Mubi North, Mubi South, Madagali, Michika, and Numan), Borno (Bama, Banki Damasak, Damboa, Dikwa, Jere, Kaga, Konduga, Gwoza, Pulka, Maiduguri, Mobbar, Monguno, and Ngala) and Yobe (Damaturu Geidam, Gujba, and Potiskum) States through provision of; - 1. 10,000 Emergency shelters 2. 35,000 NFIs to IDPs in both formal and informal camps 3. 5,000 Shelter repair kits to returnees with provision of conditional CASH component of NGN 30,000 Naira adequate to cover for the cost labour and molding of mud bricks among other unforeseen needs. 4. 3,000 Transitional shelters to IDPs and returnees within host communities. All the shelters are designed to cater for Women, Men, Girls and boys, persons with specific needs and partitioned to mitigate SGBV cases. The selection of beneficiaries will be based on needs assessment and vulnerability screening in the locations at the time of implementation. Identification and verification of beneficiaries are guided by UNHCR’s Protection principles, and endorsed by community leaders, NEMA, and SEMA officials at LGA areas. UNHCR will advocate for the development of a transparent process of beneficiary selection and the prioritization of needs of vulnerable groups. The project targets the IDPs and Returnees households suffering from protracted displacement and returning home. UNHCR will work to ensure that potential beneficiaries are aware of their responsibilities during the project and of options available to them. It is important to recognize that not everyone can manage the construction/ repair of their own house and that their time might be better used to generate income. The families’ decision to participate in this programme will be achieved through sensitization meetings, detailed assessments, participatory planning and prioritizing the provision of technical training and capacity building. A community-based feedback mechanism through regular mass meetings and focus group discussions will be established to enable IDPs and Returnees to express their opinions on issues affecting their assistance need. The discussions will also provide beneficiaries the opportunity to understand the shelter selection and allocation process.

The project has been designed to meet the affected population’s most urgent needs in a sustainable way that empowers local communities and service providers by working through existing structures where available, adhering to Nigerian guidelines and protocols, and empowering community stakeholders and other project’s beneficiaries in direct service delivery. Focusing on the particular needs of women and children, elderly and disabled people, INTERSOS will target communities where service providers are currently unavailable or unable to cope with the overwhelming needs of returnees, IDPs and host community.

In the project focus areas, INTERSOS will scale up its interventions with the provision of 750 emergency shelters kits and will strengthen the reception center management in Monguno and Ngala. INTERSOS will strive to fulfill the basic humanitarian needs of the ultra-vulnerable communities through the provision of adequate temporary housing solutions and reception center facilities. With the assistance of other services providers, the project will enhance the different referral pathways and the referral mechanism.

project_name: Providing first line gender-based violence response and prevention services to new arrivals/returnees and other vulnerable populations in Konduga LGA of Borno State
project_objective:
Jireh Doo Foundation (JDF) operating as a single entity is through this project aiming to provide first line response GBV and protection services to new arrivals/returnees in Amarua, Tungushe B communities of Konduga Local Government Area. The project will seek to ensure that new arrivals are promptly provided with the needed protection services on arrivals to include psychosocial support services, referral, case management and the provision of critical dignity/NFI kits to women and girls. Two mobile teams made up of nurses and case workers, in addition to providing services to new arrivals/returnees in the communities, the mobile teams will also help bridge the gaps in services in surrounding areas where new arrivals or other vulnerable women and girl’s population have difficulty accessing the women and girls’ safe spaces. A significant number of new arrivals arrive communities without the knowledge of existing services or how to access these services. The mobile teams will also be trained to be able to conduct gender-sensitive hygiene promotion targeting women and girls. Tungshe have had recent cholera outbreaks. 

Services provided on the project will be geared towards reducing the severe distress, hardship occasioned by the displacement of vulnerable persons. JDF will pay particular attention to new arrivals as they arrive the communities and will seek ways of working with security forces in the screening and processing of new arrivals into the communities at the point of arrival to ensure that protection concerns are quickly identified and addressed. 

The selected LGA, Konduga stands as a priority LGA under this location and JDF already has presence in implementing GBV and other protection activities in the communities and has very good pre-existing relationships with stakeholders that facilitate work in the communities. JDF will continue to nurture with zeal and dedication these relationships for the success of this project 

A key component of the project will be the establishment of two women and girls’ safe spaces (WGSS) in Tungushe and Gomari communities of Konduga LGA which will further expand current community services. Through these safe spaces, women and girls will be provided with life-saving services such as psychosocial support, group therapy, group and individual counseling, psychological first aid and case management services to new arrivals. 

A small livelihoods component of the project will identify 60 women and older adolescent girls to provide specialized training and grants and monitoring by case managers. 200 women and girls will be also trained and formed into groups for Village Savings and Loans as a livelihood and resilience building interventions 

Additionally, the project will include a community engagement and awareness-raising component, targeting a total of400 men, women, boys, and girls in the communities of interest. This approach aims to remove negative attitudes and practices that lead to stigmatization of GBV survivors, which serves to remove barriers to reintegration of survivors over time. This component of the project will also enable community-based referral pathways for individuals who experience violence. 

Jireh Doo Foundation is keen on the principle of leaving no one behind and ensuring that unreached populations are reached. JDF will pay particular attention to ensure that project activities, infrastructures to be constructed such as women and girls’ safe spaces take into cognizance the needs of people with disabilities. 

In total, the project will reach 3000 beneficiaries, split equally between host and IDP communities
