project_name: Integrated Prevention of and Response to GBV and Child Protection Concerns in Jubaland State
project_objective:
Recurrent emergencies have highlighted the need for community-based response and prevention of Gender Based Violence and Child Protection Issues and to sustain strengthening the capacities of community structures resourceful towards improved protection environment for women, girls, boys and men.
The project aims to sustain gains made by SEDHURO Child Protection and GBV  programs in the promotion of rights, care and protection of children in Gedo and Lower Jubba regions of Jubbaland State through a multi-sectorial resilience programming encompassing Social Norms, GBV, FGM, IDTR and strengthening community child protection structures. The project enhances local knowledge by promoting dialogue on social norms issues including harmful traditional practices, women and children’s rights which are enshrined in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and Somali constitution. 
The program places family at the center of child protection and hence unaccompanied and separated children will be provided with services aimed at reunifying them with their parents or customary caregivers as quickly as possible and as informed by the “best interest of the child”.
The project will incorporate a plan for capacity building notably strengthening community-level capacity to prevent/mitigate family separation, GBV and Harmful practices.
The project will build synergy with other protection programs and cross-sector partners to ensure children, including unaccompanied and separated, will have their lives protected and for them to grow and develop healthily, including with access to the resources necessary to achieve their maximum potential. Holistic and comprehensive support to children’s welfare will therefore be pursued through establishing referral pathways, establishing/reactivating coordination platforms and creating a space for community contribution. Among other partners, SEDHURO will coordinate ICRC, Intersos, HILWA, CEDA and WRRS who may be working in UASC’s “next destination” to ensure cross-regions reunification is possible. The project will benefit from community structures including CPC, religious leaders and women groups. SEDHURO is running CFS in Dollow, Luq, Bardera and Kismayo in partnership with UNICEF and SHF. SEDHURO has also established one-stop GBV centre in Gulwade IDP camps in Kismayo. This project will build on and sustain those activities. 
The project aims to achieve the following:
1.0 Address acute protection needs of women, men, girls and boys, stemming from violence, including GBV, as well as coercion, and abuse in Gedo and Lower Juba. 
1.1 Enhance the protection of unaccompanied and separated children affected by emergencies including conflict and natural disaster in Gedo and Lower Juba, through strengthening and harmonising case management of UASC. 
1.1.1 SEDHURO will carry out identification urgently as part of a coordinated and strategic programme response. Inform staff in all sectors, local authorities, community-based organizations including CPCs and CPAs, community and religious leaders, and camp managers of the need to identify UASC and refer them to SEDHURO for assistance. SEDHURO will identify 600 separated and unaccompanied children through out the project period. 
1.1.2. SEDHURO will reunify 500 UASC with their families ensuring the child’s genuine participation, organizing transportation, and ensuring formal handover of the child to the responsible family member. Further post-reunification follow-up will be conducted to ensure the child has successfully reintegrated into his/her family. If the child has additional protection concerns, SEDHURO will refer the child to appropriate service provider. If tracing is positive, SEDHURO will verify all family relationships and both the child’s and family’s willingness to be reunited.
1.1.3 SEDHURO will involve already well-trained foster mothers to provide family care to UASC considering the best interest of the child. Children will only placed there as a last resort i.e. when immediate reunification is not possible, and when placed under foster care, SEDHURO will plan ways to keep children safe, and facilitate their return to, or contact with, their families. Through the project period, SEDHURO will provide 100 UASC with family-based care. 
1.1.3 SEDHURO will provide training to 300 social workers, HW, Case workers drawn from community members (50% female) in knowledge/ skills related to separation, family tracing and reunification and case management, communication skills, ability to complete forms to a high standard, familiarity with data confidentiality requirements, and training and competency in working with and interviewing children.
2.0 Improve access to GBV service delivery for Girls, boys, women and men subjected to GBV in Gedo and Lower Juba
2.1 Provide PSS to 1000 GBV survivors. The PSS workers will support survivors to overcome trauma and assume positive roles in their communities. Provide age-sensitive dignity kits to 300 GBV survivors and at-risk individuals. The project will provide transportation assistance and logistical support for 300 GBV survivors from hard-to-reach areas to service centers. Provide emergency and life-saving medical care and support including PEP treatment administered within 72 hours after rape for 200 survivors.
2.3 Establish two alternative interim-care centers in Dollow and Kismayo providing full board for a total of 80 at risk/GBV survivors 
2.4 Provide legal aid services for 50 GBV survivors. The project will coordinate with Jubaland line ministries, JRA, and community groups.
2.5 Train 150 districts authorities, village, religious and IDP leaders in principles of child protection, human rights and GBV as well as on the role of community towards prevention of child protection (sphere standards)
2.6 SEDHURO will carry out massive awareness campaigns through outreach activities, broadcast over local FM stations, dialogue sessions reaching out 120,00 community members on prevention of GBV and family separation. 
2.7 provide structured PSS through CFS in six districts in Gedo and Lower Juba. The project, instead of reinventing the wheel, will build on existing CFS established by SEDHURO in previous/on-going programs. SEDHURO is running four CFSs in Kismayo, Dollow, Luq and Bardera supported by SHF and UNICEF. To avoid disruption of normal learning sessions, as children naturally prefer sports over being confined in class rooms, SEDHURO will coordinate with educators to ensure Child Friendly Space should only be facilitated during break times or after school hours to avoid disruption of normal learning sessions at schools . CFS can continue all-day long during weekends. SEDHURO will also carry out outdoor recreational facilities to ensure active engagement with excluded children. SEDHURO will provide capacity building to CFS facilitators and provide adequate supervision related to life skills and psychosocial support. SEDHURO will further use CFS to link to other services for community. For example, when caregivers gather in and near the CFS, SEDHURO will raise awareness on services available, identification of child protection concerns, referral pathways for services as well prevention strategies.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Malnutrition of Children Aged 6 - 59 Months in the Eastern Regions (70,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective:
The eastern regions in Cameroon continue to face a complex and unprecedented humanitarian crisis with growing insecurity in the Lake Chad Basin region, the conflict in the Central African Republic (CAR) and the significant deterioration of food security and nutrition situation. 
The main goal of WFP nutrition programme in the Eastern Regions is to contribute to reduction of under-nutrition and associated levels of mortality by 2020. WFP through the implementation of the nutrition programme under its Country Strategic Plan(CSP) will facilitate access to appropriate nutritious foods for vulnerable groups to prevent or treat malnutrition and thus makes a crucial contribution to saving lives and strengthening physical resilience to shocks in affected communities.
Therefore, as a nutrition intervention in the Eastern regions, WFP will prioritize integrated approaches for prevention and treatment of acute and chronic malnutrition targeting 62,400 children aged 6–23 months through the blanket supplementary feeding programme (BSFP) in targeted health districts and 7,600 moderate acute malnutrition(MAM) children aged 24–59 months in food-insecure areas with high malnutrition rates for 12 months in 2019.

project_name: Food by Prescription for Malnourished ART Patients in the Eastern Regions (2,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: Cameroon is the second most affected country in the West and Central African Region by HIV/AIDS. Since the malnutrition is a major reason for discontinuing Anti-Retroviral Treatment (ART), nutrition and food support should be integrated into HIV programmes. Research shows that severely malnourished individuals are six times more likely to die in the first three months of infection than those with normal nutrition status. Malnourished people living with HIV and on ART need, accordingly, food supplements through food by prescription(FbP) to improve their nutrition status and adherence to treatment under the WFP/UNAIDS joint programme. WFP will provide food assistance to total 2,000 malnourished people living with HIV under ART treatment with nutrition support and counselling under the Food by Prescription (FbP) programme in the East and Adamaoua regions for 12 months in 2019. A nutritious ration composed of 25g vegetable oil and 250g of super cereal per person/day will be provided to these ART clients to maintain their food security and nutrition status.

project_name: Early Recovery Support for the Host Population and the Refugees in the Eastern Regions (36,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: The East and Adamawa regions in Cameroon continue to face a complex and unprecedented humanitarian crisis with growing insecurity in the Lake Chad Basin region, the conflict in the Central African Republic (CAR) and the significant deterioration of food security and nutrition situation. The resurgence of violence in CAR has continued to drive vulnerable households towards the eastern regions of Cameroon, which are host to the largest number of CAR refugees (total 264,578 refugees, UNHCR, September 2018). This influx is exerting significant pressure on natural resources and basic social services in host areas, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities. Therefore, WFP will target total 36,000 beneficiaries including the refugees living in the host communities to engage in community asset creation activities for the early recovery from March to August 2019. Early recovery activities will use food assistance for assets (FFA) to mitigate community stresses so those who engage in this activity will be equal participants, decision-makers and beneficiaries in food(25,000 beneficiaries) and cash-based support(11,000 beneficiaries) to promote early recovery of local communities as well as reconciliation and social cohesion between host and displaced communities.

project_name: Immediate Food Assistance for Internally Displaced Persons(IDPs) in the Far North (40,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: In the Far North region, the Boko Haram insurgency in Nigeria has displaced 100,504 Nigerian refugees in Cameroon as of October 2018, and 98,590 of them live in the Far North region (UNHCR, October 2018). Boko Haram attacks have also resulted in 227,581 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (UNHCR, October 2018), who are struggling to survive in strenuous conditions in villages or small towns in the area. The region is predominantly arid and regularly hit by drought and seasonal floods. Access to basic services is also more limited than in other regions of the country. The arrival of IDPs in food-insecure areas has severely affected host communities as well. This has put enormous pressure on already scarce community resources and the local economy by reducing farm productivity and access to land and food markets. Boko Haram attacks have disrupted the economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in the Far North region, causing a depletion of livelihoods and household assets. As a consequence, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food insecurity have been aggravated. IDPs have fleed from the bordering regions where the Boko Haram attacks have occurred but the vulnerable IDP households live without means or assets to support themselves. To address the urgent food needs of the most vulnerable IDPs, WFP plans to provide immediate food assistance with full ration to the most vulnerable 40,000 IDPs in the Far North for 12 months in 2019. 25,000 beneficiaries will be supported with the in-kind food assistance and the rest 15,000 with Cash-Based Transfer(CBT).

This has put enormous pressure on already scarce community resources and the local economy by reducing farm productivity and access to land and food markets. Boko Haram attacks have disrupted the economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in the Far North region, causing a depletion of livelihoods and household assets. As a consequence, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food insecurity have been aggravated. Currently in the region, Nigerian refugees reside in the Miniwao Refugee Camp and they have limited means or livelihood activities to support themselves. To address the urgent food needs, WFP plans to provide immediate food assistance with full ration to the most vulnerable 55,000 Nigerian refugees for 12 months in 2019.

project_name: Immediate Food Assistance to CAR Refugees in the Eastern Regions (100,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: The East and Adamawa regions in Cameroon continue to face a complex and unprecedented humanitarian crisis with growing insecurity in the Lake Chad Basin region, the conflict in the Central African Republic (CAR) and the significant deterioration of food security and nutrition situation. The resurgence of violence in CAR has continued to drive vulnerable households towards the eastern regions of Cameroon, which are host to the largest number of CAR refugees (total 264,578 refugees, UNHCR, September 2018). This influx is exerting significant pressure on natural resources and basic social services in host areas, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities. In 2019, WFP plans to assist 100,000 CAR refugees with a full ration of food basket for 12 months. Newly arrived refugees could also be taken into account when updating the list. While getting ready to review the  strategy for profiling and targeting of refugees, following the Joint Assessment Mission(JAM) scheduled for January 2019, WFP will tentatively plan to provide food assistance to approximately 100,000 extremely vulnerable Central African refugees in the East, Adamawa and North Regions, including 48,800 refugees through Cash-Based Transfer (CBT).

project_name: Integrated Multi-AoR protection services for high at risk groups in Jebel Saman, Aleppo
project_objective:
The intervention is part of a project aiming at securing the basic needs and providing integrated community-based protection activities in Jabal Badro/Ard Hamra and Karm Jazmati . In these two areas, Caritas Germany (CG) seeks to provide integrated community-based protection services, implementing through its partner organization Caritas Syria (CS), to high at risk groups such as women, adolescent girls, children and elderly. In Jabal Badro/Ard Hamra, Caritas Syria has been implementing Basic Assistance activities since the beginning of 2017. CS has also been distributing relief items for SARC, UNHCR and WFP in the area. In 2018, Caritas Syria established a community center in Jabal Badro/Ard Hamra, implementing informal education activities for school-age children as well as PSS for women, children and elderly. The concept of first establishing a relationship of trust with the local community through distributing relief items before opening up a community center has proven successful and shall be replicated in Karm Jazmati. Karm Jazmati will be a new project area for Caritas Syria. After consulting with regional coordination sectors UNOCHA, UNHCR, WFP as well as with organisations operating in neighbouring areas, Karm Jazmati has been identified as in high need for protection activites and therefore selected as second area of implementation under the proposed project. 

The intervention aims at reducing the protection risks for at high risk groups through a community-based approach. The intervention will respond to the protection needs of vulnerable women, adolescent girls, children and elderly in Jabal Badro/Ard Hamra and Karm Jazmati. The intervention will respond to protection needs in Jabal Badro/Ard Hamra and Karm Jazmati with four pillars of activities: non-specialized PSS and awareness sessions for women, children and elderly; literacy courses for adolescent girls and women as protection measures against GBV risks; informal education for school-aged children aiming at reducing risk of child protection risk factors as well as a capacity building component aiming at strengthening the responding capacity of Caritas Syria staff on a national level.

project_name: Provision emergency shelter materials and core relief items for South Sudanese Refugees in Bilel, Buram, A Salam and Al Radoum localities in South Darfur state.
project_objective:
Sudan hosts the largest population of South Sudanese refugees in the region, with more than 850,000 individuals reported across the country as of December 2018. Among these, nearly 385,000 fled to Sudan since the outbreak of conflict in South Sudan in 2013 and have been registered or recorded at reception areas by UNHCR and the Government’s Commissioner of Refugees (COR). An additional estimated 467,000 South Sudanese have been recorded by various government and UN sources, most of whom were living in Sudan prior to the conflict in South Sudan and are recognized by the Government as refugees because they cannot safely return home. These individuals are yet to be officially registered by UNHCR and COR. Overall, the Government of Sudan estimates there are up to 1.3 million South Sudanese refugees in Sudan; however, additional estimates require further verification. 

The proposed project will reach 5,745 households (18,565 people) in Al Radom, Buram, A Salam and Bilel localities in South Darfur state, through NCA’s Emergency Response & Preparedness Unit (EPRU). The main activities proposed include: assessments, verifications, and distribution of emergency shelter material and distribution Core Relief Items. Joint coordination with UNHCR and other actors in Khartoum and the field will be done to ensure that the new arrivals receive emergency shelter and core relief items timely and in the appropriate quantities and quality. The NCA Darfur Programme (DP) emphasizes active participation of the target communities through their respective representatives and the relevant community structures to ensure that materials and services provided adequately meet the needs of the affected communities. The proposed project will focus on ensuring that boys, girls, men and women have equal opportunities to highlight their specific needs through appropriate consultations in focus group discussions (FGDs) during assessments and verification.

project_name: Columbia - Caritas Switzerland
Emergency protection support to Rohingya refugees outside of camps and host communities
project_objective:
The proposed intervention will support community-based protection activities in the camps adjacent to the host community and support joint initiatives towards social cohesion between the two communities. In addition, the analysis from protection monitoring will be used to tailor community-based protection responses to the needs of specific groups, such as supporting women and girls in accessing services or peer support groups for elderly and persons with disabilities. Formation of community groups will also take into account identified gaps in community participation to foster social inclusion for less empowered groups, such as adolescent boys and girls, youth, and women. Beneficiaries under this project will be targeted using an AGD approach and target estimation was calculated based on this year experience and available data/assessments. HC intervention will seek to engage with the relevant ministries and government service providers (particularly DSS/MoWCA) to support exchanges on good practices, joint consultations and capacity-building at the field-level (particularly on referrals and improving access to services). 
Complaints and Feedback Response Mechanism (currently rolled out in camps by DRC SMS) will be also available in host communities through community centres; and consultation and feedback mechanisms are incorporated into the methodology of all DRC protection activities. DNH principle is at the core of all DRC Protection approaches, is reflected in activity SOPs and tools (incl. selection/targeting approach, risk analysis, etc.). Social cohesion work will be based on careful analysis of communities’ dynamics and community-led process to identify opportunities for joint initiatives which would contribute to improved relationships. All DRC staff are required to sign a Code of Conduct with specific PSEA provisions, and CoC trainings are provided to all joining staff and volunteers; DRC has a robust CoC response mechanism, with Protection staff as PSEA focal point, and links to CFRM and protection referral. 
DRC is an active member of PWG and PWG TF (as well as CPSS, GBVSS and CXB PSEA Network) and will coordinate within these fora to ensure that protection activities are complementary and holistic in the humanitarian response.

project_name: JORDAN - International Medical Corps
Provision of equitable quality lifesaving and essential health services for Rohingya refugees and host communities children and women in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
Since 25 August 2017, extreme violence in Rakhine State, Myanmar, has driven an estimated 730,000 refugees across the border into Cox's Bazar. The majority of the population are children (55 per cent) and women (52 per cent) They live in the overcrowded settlement in Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazila and in the poor condition,  prone to infectious disease outbreak (due to low immunity and poor health and nutritional status). 
UNICEF proposes the project “Provision of equitable quality lifesaving and essential health services for Rohingya refugees and host communities’ children and women in Cox's Bazar” providing services to Rohingya Refugees and Host population. UNICEF project will serve 167,103 beneficiaries through this project. UNICEF will implement this project in partnership with Cox's Bazar Civil Surgeon, DD Family Planning, Partners in Health and Development (PHD), Relief International (RI), Research, Training, Management International (RTMI), Food for the Hungry/Medical Team International (FH/MTI), icddr,b. UNICEF will need 15, 608,320 USD in order to implement this project. 
UNICEF’s project activities are in line with health sector’s following four objectives:
Objective #1 Improve equitable access to and utilization of quality lifesaving and comprehensive primary and secondary health services for crisis-affected populations with special focus on sexual reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health; mental health and psycho-social support; and non-communicable diseases.
Objective #3 Encourage healthy living, improve health seeking behavior and utilization of essential service package among refugees and host populations through community engagement, with special attention to gender considerations and vulnerable groups.
Objective #4 Strengthen health sector coordination and information management with a focus on rational and accountable health service delivery systems, including monitoring of minimum standards and the quality of the services provided.

project_name: Comprehensive child protection assistance to children in Rohingya refugee camps
project_objective: This project will contribute to comprehensive child protection assistance to children in Rohingya refugee camps 2E, 2W, 6 and 7, building on DRC CP intervention in these camps during 2018, and focusing on strengthening community-based child protection networks/systems, mobile and static PSS services, holistic case management and awareness-raising and outreach activities, incorporating social cohesion and DRR elements, and reaching a total of 30,572 beneficiaries.

project_name: GBV prevention and quality services for GBV survivors in refugee camps and host communities
project_objective: This project will provide GBV prevention and quality services for GBV survivors in a refugee camp and neighbouring host community, addressing existing gaps in assistance and contributing to strengthening social cohesion, focusing on establishing safe spaces for women and girls,  peer support and awareness-raising activities to enhance capacity, social empowerment and safety; case management, individual protection assistance and referral; psychosocial support and participatory prevention with a total reach of 4,013 beneficiaries.

project_name: Education in Emergencies' Intervention in Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria and Upper Nile States
project_objective:
Education remains a challenge in Greater Upper Nile as a result of multiple displacements, food insecurity, lack of infrastructure and human resource coupled with negative community attitude towards education. 
The project aims at providing equitable and uninterrupted access to safe, protective and inclusive learning, improving cognitive skills and coping abilities of male and female children, adolescents and school aged youths through education in emergency ECD, basic education, youth education and ALP, and ensuring girls and boys are protected through increased access to psychosocial support, life skills and referral pathways. 
Schools will be used as platforms to provide other services such as nutritional support, WASH interventions, health services and as a protection safety net. 
The project thus contributes to the return of children to school in a school environment that favours their instruction and protection; and offers an alternative to early marriage, and widens economic opportunities for youth beyond the traditional agriculturalist/pastoralist activities which aren’t sufficient to sustain the existing population. This is an effective and cost-effective sustainable intervention that CMD is pursuing to close equity gaps by preserving over 30,000 children and youths in schools. Furthermore, CMD intends to wage an advocacy crusade alongside skills development for out-of-school adolescents by pressing for recognition of youth as pivotal in achieving sustainable livelihood profiles across Jonglei, Upper Nile States and, indeed, South Sudan at large. 
CMD’s solid experience in undertaking large-scale interventions and its unparalleled country-level knowledge and relationships at the grassroots will guide this endeavour.

project_name: Strengthen CCCM activities in Wau collective sites, camp like settings and out of camps to improve delivery of humanitarian services and protection of IDPs through efficient and effective multi-sectoral response in Wau.
project_objective: Wau collective sites have been served by camp management agencies since June 2016 following the outbreak of violent clashes which have been intermittently occurring since. Between ongoing violence and the recent initiative of moving individuals from the PoC to Wau town, there are currently 11,574 individuals residing in collective centres. In 2019, AFOD will continue to provide extensive camp management support in Wau’s five collective centres to meet the needs of the population in the way of: communicating with communities; site maintenance; partner coordination; information management and advocacy. As one of the few national NGOs in the CCCM sector in South Sudan, AFOD is in a particularly unique position and has a clear added value in ensuring strong community engagement and a sustainable impact in meeting the needs of those most affected by displacement in the country. The population of Wau and surrounding areas have been particularly affected by outbreaks of violence since early in the year resulting in significant influxes into collective sites. In 2019, AFOD expects to grow technical capacities and work toward gradual expansion of work in the collective centres whether they be existing or new.

project_name: Lifesaving Shelter and NFI response to vulnerable populations in Yirol East and Yirol West
project_objective:
This proposed project will address short to mid-term emergency shelter and non-food items needs of conflict affected vulnerable populations both displaced and in secondary displacement. The project will target 2000 HHs or 12,000 individuals both IDPs and host communities, disaggregated as follows (Men 2,403, Women 3,531, Boys 2,863 and Girls 3,203) for emergency shelter and NFIs activities response in Lakes (Yirol East & Yirol West) most vulnerable populations in need (after an assessment). The target population comprises of displaced persons in need of shelter and NFI for their sustenance. Yirol East and Yirol West have also been categorised under Catastrophe IPC 5, making the communities here more susceptible to famine. This is worse especially for newly displaced and vulnerable populations in secondary displacement. The project will aim to meet the needs of the vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host community who become vulnerable as a result of conflict and continuous displacement as a result of conflict, food insecurity or due to economic deterioration. 

Though there are 28574 vulnerable displaced persons (4618 HHs) in Yirol, CCOSS has previously through funding from RRF responded to 3000 HHs. There still exists a bigger gap of 1618 HHs that requires S/NFIs response (Men: 2047, Women: 2741, Boys: 2397, Girl: 2523 and total 9,708 individuals). In line with Do¬-No--Harm principle which is also supported by the cluster’s position, CCOSS will also include host community, (local populations) as beneficiaries, whenever applicable, as they are also sharing burden of displacement by giving their already meagre resources to their displaced relatives. The breakdown for host communities includes the following 383 HHs – 2,292 individuals disaggregated as follows (Men 356, Women 790, Boys 466 & Girls 680). 

Prior to project implementation, CCOSS will conduct, focus group discussions (FGD) with women, men, boys and girls at targeted community settlements will be conducted to get feedback on design, implementation, ensuring safety and mitigation of Protection / GBV risks, especially for females. An assessment and verification exercise will be conducted to establish the exact emergency shelter and lifesavings non-food items needs requirements of the targeted population. This will be followed by registration of the targeted beneficiaries and subsequent distribution of S/NFIs. However it should be noted that the composition of the people in need may fluctuate according to the changing security situation. CCOSS will do its best to adjust actions in the most possible way, striving to adhere to SPHERE standards for the populations in needs for the duration of the project period. CCOSS will also ensure that there is proper coordination especially in locations where there is more than one implementing partner. County cluster meetings will be held weekly to ensure proper coordination, to avoid double counting and as well reduce duplication of efforts. CCOSS is a key member of other clusters working within the same locality. CCOSS will therefore ensure that there is synergy between S/NFIs Cluster, WASH and Food Security. This is particularly to ensure there is no duplication for WASH NFIs and S/NFIs being distributed, but also ensure the FSL compliments the work of the other clusters. For instance, during the first distribution, the IDPs sold some of the plastic sheets for food in market. CCOSS responded by requesting WFP to scale up its operations in the area. 

General Operation & other Direct costs include costs associated with providing direct management & other support functions at the Main office in Juba. This includes management staff salaries, communication, stationary, rents etc. The Indirect project costs include bank charges, staff recruitment & servicing costs, auditing and consultancy costs.

project_name: Saving live by providing timely and appropriate access to safe and adequate water, dignified Sanitation, and enhancing safe hygiene practices for crisis affected communities through integrated WASH interventions, reinforcing protection and enhancing resilience through building capacities of communities to prepare for and cope with recurrent shocks and sustain livelihoods.
project_objective:
In this project, CMC aims to provide timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water as well as improving knowledge of most vulnerable population on hygiene to reduce morbidity and mortality resulting from WASH-related diseases and malnutrition.
CMC will implement integrated lifesaving WASH and nutrition activities mainstreaming protection, accountability to affected population and strengthening the capacity of affected community on copping mechanism and resilience through training of different groups of people in the community such as pump mechanics, Water management committee, women groups, community leaders among others The project will target communities affected with conflict and natural disasters with limited access to safe water supply, unsafe hygiene and sanitation practices and food insecurity with support to institutions like nutrition/health centers and schools with WASH facilities and hygiene promotion.
Under this project, CMC will implement life-saving WASH activities targeting 15000 Direct Beneficiaries and 10000 indirect beneficiaries suffering from inadequate access to safe drinking water and poor hygiene conditions. CMC intends to target vulnerable and crisis affected population with a structured, effective preparedness and response programme aimed at improving access to safe water, enhancing community awareness on safe hygiene and sanitation practices in order to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. 
CMC will coordinate with nutrition, education and FSL partners to reduce malnutrition level through supporting nutrition centers and schools with WASH facilities and enhancing knowledge of mothers who are the primary care givers on safe hygiene and sanitation practices especially in areas of new displacement. This will contribute to the reduction of risk of WASH related diseases including malnutrition hence making health, nutrition and education centers safe for users. 
To enhance sustainability and resilience, CMC will implement capacity building of the community to prepare for and cope with current shocks and sustain livelihoods, linkages with development action to support resilience
Protection and accountability to affected people will be at the central point in this project, putting communities at the centre of the response. CMC will ensure that services delivered are gender-sensitive and will consider the needs of older people, children (boys and girls) and people living with disabilities. Where necessary cash programming will be incorporated through voucher for WASH NFIs like soap provided to health/nutrition centers at risk of contamination and malnutrition. Key hygiene and nutrition messaging at these institutions will be accompanied.
Before response, initial needs assessments (either IRNA or CMC’s own assessment) will be carried out in consultation with the national WASH cluster and WASH states focal persons for the targeted locations. Activities will include will include safe water supply through water point construction repair and rehabilitation, provision of sanitation facilities at institution levels especially health/nutrition centers and schools, hygiene promotion focusing on key messages  (hand washing, safe water chain and safe excreta disposal) Hygiene and sanitation campaigns in communities and institutions, capacity-building of community through trainings (pump mechanics, water user committees, community hygiene promoters, school's hygiene clubs), and distribution of WASH NFIs and Menstrual hygiene Management Materials to women and girls of reproductive age. 
To ensure accountability to affected population, indicators will be put in place to track cooperation with communities by attending to complaints and carrying out feedback sessions with the community to address GBV threats in WASH, and ensuring services provided meet the needs of the beneficiaries. Post intervention monitoring will be conducted to measure the appropriateness, coverage and effectiveness. Clear WASH NFI beneficiary selection criteria will be put in place and clearly presented to the community before and during distribution.
The continuing deteriorating access to humanitarian support services for the Internally Displaced People and Returnees contributed negatively to the affected population with serious traumatic life experiences in the sites of displacement and return, through lessons learnt by other partners in current and most recent projects, (CMC) has acknowledged the rapid increasing cases of protection and Sexual Gender Based Violence which stand as a prove that protection and Sexual Gender Based Violence is a cross cutting thematic issue that need to be addressed across all projects and this project will contribute in addressing the gaps through inter-sector response.

project_name: Improving emergency Shelter and Non-food items response to newly IDPs  in Fangak, Ayod and Uror county of Jonglei State
project_objective: As a result of the continues crashes between Government forces and Opposition forces in Wau payam of Ayod county, Yuai of Uror County and sequence influx of IDPs from Unity State to Fangak County of Jonglei State. This positioned Jonglei State often as more vulnerable due to its exposure both to natural and man-man disaster like flood and displacements from nearby states, tribal attacks and intensity of conflict between warring parties.  This state has been always experiencing a massive displacement of people, killing of children, women, elderly and loss of livestock and property, including burning of houses. An estimated 51,000 individuals from Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) households are quarterly displaced 24,000 individuals Returnees from Bor PoC, Malakal PoC, UN House PoC, Ethiopia  and Sudan making a total of 75,000 individuals, who were both displaced and returnees. These IDPs and returnees currently settled in Old Fangak, new Fangak, Juaibor, Paguir, Keew, Toch, Mareang, Nyadin and Diel villages of Fangak County, Other settled in Guwai, Nor Manyang, Jiech, Pagil, Wiechdeng, Wichdieng, Mugok, Riang, Guduk, Bilgak and Thanyni  villages of Ayod county. Many more settled in Motot, Peiri, Pulchol, Karam, Pathai, Wechjal, Wechwal, Walgak and Motdit villages of Uror County of Jonglei State. However, several joint assessment were conducted from 20th June 2018 to 20th October 2018, IDPs reported lack of essential NFIs service. Other IDPs reported health related issues, especially diarrhea, vomiting, skin diseases, and fever, especially amongst children.  IDPs also sleep on Kangas and shawls, with about ten or more individuals sharing with the host community. Many children who were attending school are now out of school in the locations where IDPs have settled. Children are also at risk of neglect, child labour, gender based violence (GBV), recruitment into armed groups, forced marriage (for girls) and family separation especially after going through the violence when fighting broke out. There is no markets in the villages where IDPs are currently located. In regard to the above needs, there is urgent need for an emergency humanitarian response to 30,000 individuals from the displaced communities in shelter and Non-food Items. This project therefore aims at providing an Integrated Emergency response for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) through Non-Food Items (NFIs) in Fangak, Ayod and Uror county of Jonglei State. This project will not only target the IDPs in Old Fangak, new Fangak, Juaibor, Paguir, Keew, Toch, Mareang, Nyadin and Diel villages of Fangak County and Gowai, Nor Manyang, Jiech, Pagil, Wiechdeng, Wichdieng, Mugok, Riang, Guduk, Bilgak and Thanyni  villages of Ayod county. Motot, Peiri, Pulchol, Karam, Pathai, Wechjal, Wechwal, Walgak and Motdit villages of Uror County. ADA will expand it operation into more “hard to reach location” in greater Jonglei this may include Haat, Menime of Ayod county,Pigi, Canal, Korfulus of Fangak county and more locations in greater Akobo county of Jonglei State.The project would aims at responding to the current emergency situation in hard to reach areas of Fangak, Ayod and Uror county of Jonglei state.

project_name: Building resilience and increasing own production through livelihood support and livestock intervention in  Maiwut, Longechuk and Nassir of Upper Nile State and Mayendit of Unity State.
project_objective:
This project is designed to effectively contribute to the building of resilience and increasing own production through livelihood support and livestock intervention in Maiwut, Longechuk and Nassir of Upper Nile State and Mayendit of Unity State. It is a twelve month project targeting 12000 HH of vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host communities. AHC intends to make use of the window of opportunity for the targeted population who missed out the cropping season either due to conflict, or lack of access to humanitarian assistance. Those who planted also suffered from dry spells and FAW attack thus less harvest. It is in line with the FSL allocation both in terms of the Priority, Geographical coverage, and the seasonality of the proposed activities; crop, vegetable, and fishing production, training and livestock treatment and vaccination. This project corresponds to strategic objective 3 as well as cluster objectives 2 and 4.
A total of 72000 vulnerable individuals will be targeted and selected from the targeted areas. These will include 21600 men, 36000 women, 8000 boys and 6400 girls selected from the 36,000 IDP, 14400returnees  and 21600 host population. The targeting will be done with gender consideration as well as the invaluable incorporation of Accountability to affected population and mainstreaming of protection issues. The Do No Harm principle will be adhered to as we endeavour to give priority to the community to have a say over their own situation. 
AHC is committed mitigate any risks associated with this project bearing in mind the added advantage we have as a local NGO based in the target project sites with extensive integration with the community. The presence and good rapport we have with the community is an added advantage to the success of this project.
FAO will be the core pipeline and technical backstop partner. The requested funding from SSHF is going to be used to provide front line services. A transparent direct distribution system based on the FAO guidelines will be used to implement this project. There is a huge influx of returnees and the number of the IDPs and most vulnerable host community members is also high.

project_name: GBV emergency lifesaving assistance to the most vulnerable populations of IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in LEER, MAYENDIT AND KOCH COUNTIES
project_objective:
This project targets directly a total of 9,700 beneficiaries broken down as follows (4,000 women, 3,200 girls, 1,500 men and 1,000 boys) in the three counties of Leer, Mayendit and Koch. Coalition for Humanity (CH) will provide assistance to women and girls affected by sexual and gender based violence in the target areas through conducting of a rapid diagnostic assessment of the GBV context to inform an appropriate response. We anticipate this response to include development of Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS), provision of GBV case management and psychosocial services to affected persons.  Coalition for Humanity (CH) will also provide safe refers for cases for several reasons including WASH provision, livelihood support among others. 
In collaboration with our Conflict transformation project by GIZ, CH will enhance participation of women and girls in peace-building and peaceful co-existence through capacity building of local women's groups/women's organisations and women leaders on mediation and peaceful resolution of conflicts. This hopefully will contribute towards long term prevention of conditions that give rise to increased GBV in the target area. 
In order to ensure that long term solutions towards combating GBV are achieved, CH will work with government and partners to strengthen implementation of institutional policies, standards, and practices that drive action and accountability on GBV and gender equality in humanitarian service delivery as linked to our commitment to Call to Action on GBV in emergency. This is besides identifying opportunities within the local culture to reduce or if possible altogether eliminate local drivers of gender based violence.

project_name: Distribution of lifesaving non-food items and shelter materials for most vulnerable conflict and other disaster affected populations
project_objective:
The DRC mobile response team aims to support the most vulnerable and underserved populations in Upper Nile and other hard to reach communities in other parts of the country affected by conflict through the provision of multi-sector survival kit, non-food items, and emergency shelter support. All responses are led by a protection centred need assessments that will determine the exact nature of the response. Through this project, DRC will fund a mobile team based in Malakal and Juba with rapid response capability to cover various areas of the Upper Nile State and hard to reach locations prioritized by the cluster and SNFI state focal points. The Juba-based mobile team will quickly deploy to locations of Upper Nile and other prioritized hard to reach locations where land access is limited for the Malakal based mobile team in Upper Nile and rest of the country, respectively. By having mobile teams in Malakal and Juba, DRC will be best placed to support new displacements and spontaneous returns across the Upper Nile and other hard to reach locations throughout South Sudan. Additionally, DRC will continue to have a static presence in Malakal PoC, providing robust emergency shelters and NFI distributions. Reconfiguration of PoC will take place in early 2019, requiring shelter construction for Sector 3 of the PoC and shelter upgrades for approximately 75% of Sectors 1 and 2.

Furthermore, following a thorough market analysis, the static Malakal team will pilot an outreach Cash for Shelter program in the west bank of Malakal and Fashoda County in areas where local resources and markets are functioning.

All S/NFI materials (with the exception of the Cash for Shelter activity) will be provided by the cluster pipeline and will not be budgeted under the project. These items will include survival kit, NFI kits, and emergency shelter items distributed by the cluster. The beneficiary calculation for the mobile emergency response teams is in line with the USD $13 per beneficiary targeted by the cluster, including household members (i.e. one S/NFI kit directly benefitting all members of a household), while Cash for Shelter is $25. The response missions will be followed by a rapid monitoring exercise during the response mission in hard to reach locations where access is limited to redeploy team for evaluation and post-distribution monitoring in locations that are easily accessible to the redeployment of a team. The PDM and the rapid monitoring exercise will highlight any risks by the S/NFI intervention as well as lessons for considerations for future responses. Beneficiaries will be able to provide their opinions on how DRC and cluster interventions can be improved and they will be given the opportunity to make a complaint. A formal feedback mechanism will be fed through DRC’s hotline whereby complaints or queries may be logged and responded to remotely.

project_name: Mine Action - Roving mine action capacity supporting a protective environment for conflict affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
Summary of revisions:
•	Number of teams (both MTT and MRE) reduced from 8 to 5
•	Target: total number of HA surveyed and cleared reduced from 2000 to 1250
•	Target: total number of MRE beneficiaries reduced from 139,200 to 90,000
•	Breakdown of MRE beneficiaries provided. This is provided in the 'Activites’ section, as the system does not allow for disaggregation in the ‘Clusters’ section. DDG will provide further disaggreation at the county level upon request.
•	HRP Strategic objective 1 removed and objective 3 added.
•	Changes made to project locations. The following locations were removed: Koch, Mayendit, Panyjar, Abienhom, Panyikang, Luakpiny/Nasir. The following locations were added: Raja (Tier 3), Wau (Tier 2), Mvolo (Tier 3).

DDG will deploy 5 highly mobile Multi Task Teams (MTTs), together with 5 embedded Risk Education (RE) teams to respond to urgent threats to physical safety, dignity, freedom of movement and access to humanitarian assistance within communities. The objectives of the project are to:

1. Provide immediate lifesaving assistance to address the urgent protection needs of the most vulnerable (including women, children, elderly, disabled and survivors of sexual violence in conflict) in hard-to-reach areas.
2. Enhance prevention and preparedness programming to mitigate risks and strengthen resilience
3. Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other affected populations 

Tasks which will support the humanitarian response in the country will be prioritised through the following key activities:

• Non-technical survey (NTS) and technical survey (TS) – to target and prioritise clearance according to humanitarian need, survey will be conducted using a mixture of key informant interviews and household questionnaires held with the local population and authorities. NTS will determine the likely locations and density of ERW contamination in target locations, whilst assessing the impact of these hazards on vulnerable populations in any given location. TS (using detectors) will be used upon discovery of an area with a high concentration of explosive hazards.
• Explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) and battle area clearance (BAC) – once NTS has determined the nature of the threat, technical capacities within the teams will be deployed to remove and destroy identified hazards.
• MRE – all teams will contain a capacity to deliver risk messaging raising awareness about how to recognise dangerous items, as well as associated safe practices that should be followed, and high risk behaviour that should be avoided in relation to mines and explosive remnants of war.

The activities outlined in this document will primarily target 90,000 IDPs and host community members living across Upper Nile, Unity and Western Equatoria States, including in hard-to-reach locations where mine/ERW contamination remains substantial. DDG will target these populations with RE, improving their knowledge of the explosive hazards they can encounter, and at the same time collect evidence for clearance tasks. RE will be delivered based on analysis of specific needs of women, men, boys and girls. A total of 17,325 women, 14,175 men, 32,175 girls and 26,325 boys will be targeted by this intervention. Furthermore DDG will, through Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), will identify the major service delivery points which will be a primary target for clearance responses.

This project has broadly been designed to directly benefit the 2019 multisector response in South Sudan. The intervention will be delivered as a protection mainstreaming effort, designed to target survey, clearance and RE towards areas to which population movements are expected, as well as ensuring beneficiaries are able to safely access water points, schools, health facilities and other socio-economic assets being supported / rehabilitated by agencies on the ground. In doing so, DDG will ensure that beneficiaries of other partners are not at undue risk when accessing services.

project_name: Provision of Camp Coordination and Camp Management services for displaced populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
Years of violent conflict have left millions of South Sudanese facing one of the world’s most devastating, complex and deep-rooted humanitarian crises in recent history. The compounding effect of repeated waves of violence and an increasingly fast economic decline have pushed the number of people uprooted since the start of the conflict to 4 million, with roughly 1.4 million estimated to be internally displaced. In response to the growing and shifting needs in South Sudan, ACTED proposes to extend the scope of its current response through rapid interventions to reach some of the 84% of internally displaced people (IDPs) living in precarious conditions outside of the Protection of Civilian (PoC) sites. ACTED will build on its experience in Camp Coordination and Camp Management in PoCs and camp-like settings across the country, to launch a CCCM Mobile Team able to respond to sudden IDP emergencies and crises. In a context where prioritisation is becoming ever more complex and there is a disjunct between data and response, ACTED will ensure that this response is coordinated, and that sustainability is built within through a grassroots approach focusing on community capacity building and self-management. ACTED will also continue its historic commitment to the residents of Bor and Juba PoCs by continuing to provide Camp Management and Camp Coordination (CCCM) services geared towards the improvement of living conditions of more than 34,000 residents. Services will include amongst others day-to-day coordination and service delivery monitoring and site maintenance activities. A special focus will be put on improving communication and community engagement and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP). A core component of the approach proposed will be to strengthen the community governance structures and capacity for self-management. The unique nature of the PoCs – this “72-hour solution” to a 5-year situation – has generated increased frustration amongst its residents. As Camp Manager, ACTED strongly believes that it is our responsibility to ensure that our response is guided by fundamental humanitarian principles as well as ensuring the right to life with dignity which include considerations beyond basic survival. ACTED therefore proposes to provide recreational spaces for people to carry out sports and craft activities, where they will also be able to organise group discussions on themes chosen on a weekly/monthly basis (e.g. protection-related topics, GBV, etc.). 
As the scale and geographic spread of the humanitarian crisis increases, it also becomes more important than ever to have a realistic, regular and predictable country-wide needs monitoring mechanism and strong coordination structures to trigger cost-efficient ad needs-based interventions. Secondly, in hosting the Camp Management and Camp Coordination (CCCM) cluster co-lead, ACTED endeavours to ensure a strong contribution in working toward a coordinated response and advocacy at the highest levels of the humanitarian architecture to ensure that the voice of displaced people is represented and heard.

project_name: GBV: Strengthening life-saving GBV Respose for Vulnerable populations in Ulang, Kaji  Kejo and Kapoeta East Counties in Upper Nile, Central and Eastern Equatoria States in South Sudan
project_objective: This project aims at building on and deepening ARC's on-going GBV response and prevention interventions in Ulang, Kajo Keji and Kapoeta East Counties.  The activities are centered on Women and Girl's Friendly Space (WGFS) programming through complementary funding from other ARC funding sources including South Sudan Humanitarian fund (SSHF) in Kapoeta East County and OFDA in Ulang and Kajo Keji Counties respectively. ARC is running six (6) WGFSs-four in Ulang and one in each County in Kapoeta East and Kajo Keji Counties and plans to use HRP funding mechanism to add one more WGFS in each locations of Kapoeta East and Kajo Keji.

project_name: Nutrition Interventions for Disaster affected populations in Former Unity and Former Eastern Lakes States.
project_objective: Integrated emergency nutrition interventions for children under the age of 5, pregnant and lactating women in the former Unity and the former Eastern Equatoria states. The project will support CMAM sites through strengthening community outreach and referrals, and access affected communities to maternal infant and young child nutrition programs. The intervention includes a cash component where mothers with malnourished children will be provided with cash to facilitate movement, especially those that stay far away from treatment facilities. The project will also work with communities to prevent under-nutrition.  CARE will strengthen nutrition situation assessments, reporting and accountability mechanisms within the areas of operation including monitoring and evaluation.

project_name: Provision of WASH Services to vulnerable populations in Cox's Bazar District
project_objective: Provision of lifesaving water, sanitation and hygiene interventions for 250,000 refugees and 350,000 people in affected host communities.

project_name: Delivering holistic GBV prevention, response & risk mitigation services to conflict affected women, girls, boys and men in Jonglei, Unity, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States.
project_objective: CARE seeks to implement GBV prevention, response and risk mitigation activities by providing quality and timely age appropriate case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors in Koch, Uror, Maiwut, Abiemnom, Pibor, Torit, Lafon, Ikotos in Jonglei, Unity, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States.  This project is designed to improve responses to cases of GBV, enhance the ability of survivors to recover from GBV, and make progress towards changing the social norms that perpetuate GBV, with the intent of fully mitigating the effects of GBV and preventing future cases. It will provide GBV response services and address critical gaps in information and knowledge among women and girls on GBV response, which limit access to services and heighten GBV risk. CARE will encourage health-seeking behaviours among GBV survivors, facilitating referrals, and creating supportive structures to prevent GBV. CARE will work in collaboration with local partners and will establish and operationalize women and girls’ safe spaces and provide periodic individual and group psycho social support for women and girls. This will include dialogue sessions, psychosocial support through group counselling sessions, skills building, production of reusable sanitary pads using locally available materials, alternative fuel strategies through production of fuel efficient stoves, information sessions on pertinent issues to women girls on access to available services, sexual and reproductive health issues on safe deliveries, family planning and post abortion care, personal hygiene, menstrual hygiene management, decision making and peer to peer support. This project will support the healing process of GBV survivors by providing community based case management and psychosocial support services and engage men and boys in community dialogues and awareness raising sessions on GBV, its effect and consequences and their roles in prevention. Protection interventions will be integrated within CARE’s health, nutrition and FSL programmes to compliment holistic assistance to communities through static and mobile services. CARE has experienced increased uptake of protection services through mobile services as people felt comfortable to seek help close to their homes. CARE will ensure commitment to diversity and gender equity as CARE’s core business is premised on women and girls’ empowerment and therefore will strive to periodically carry out gender and protection analysis including assessments of vulnerabilities related to age, sex and diversity, and will give  priority   to vulnerable population. CARE will ensure protection from sexual exploitation and abuse for beneficiaries through awareness and training to CARE’s staff, partners, volunteers, vendors, contractors and awareness to ensure beneficiaries are aware of PSEA and reporting mechanisms. As part of CARE’s conviction for effective humanitarian programmes, addressing the humanitarian needs of women and girls remains an integral part of any response in South Sudan.  In many instances, women play multiple roles in relief and recovery activities, as participants, organizers and leaders. CARE takes a deliberate focus on women by recognizing that disaster and conflict increase women’s vulnerability to poverty, violence and other human rights violations. To this end, CARE will work with women’s rights organizations to build their capacity to take leadership of, participate and be represented in humanitarian coordination. The project will ensure that women are engaged and supported to become first responders within their communities.  CARE will work to advance women’s rights, voices and leadership through increasing their knowledge and their participation in humanitarian coordination. This will contribute to women’s protection and  empowerment and will transform women’s position in emergency response and resilience, while helping to address the core issues that affect communities in emergencies.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality in the Counties of Fashoda, Manyo, Raja, Budi and Torit.
project_objective:
Following the recent revitalization of peace, much more efforts is still needed to rebuild and restructure the health system in South Sudan after the civil conflict. High number of IDPs are still in the different exiting POC sites and also greater number of returners are expected to resettle in the different Counties accross the Country. 
Cordaid intend to provide lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality in both primary health care units and hospitals to bridge the unmet health gaps that was compounded by the long period of conflict in the Country. The project will target the IDPs, returnees and the host population in the Counties of Fashoda, Manyo, Raja, Budi and Torit. A total of 5,495 male population and 4,505 female population is expected to be reached with essential health care services in 5 Counties by the year 2019.
In Fashoda and Manyo Counties, the project will be implemented in 2 PHCUs and 2 PHCCs while in Raja, Budi and Torit, the project will be implemented in Raja hospital, Chukudum and Torit hospital. Cordaid has existing health grand in all the location of intend but due to increasing need and demand for health services, the supplementary support under this grand will health to close the gap and focus will be directed towards Improving access and scale-up responsiveness to integrated essential healthcare needs of the vulnerable populations focusing on major causes of morbidity and mortality, Prevent, detect and respond to epidemic prone disease outbreaks and Increase access to essential clinical health services among vulnerable populations targeting SGBV, NCDs, SAM with Medical Complication which will not be fully covered the existing funds.

project_name: Provision of safe water, sanitation and hygiene promotion to conflict or crisis-affected vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons and host communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
This project will be targeting a total number of 5000 households approximately 30,000 individuals which include IDP 9,000 individuals, Returnees and host communities 21,000 individuals. Out of these population, 24,000 beneficiaries will be supported with access to safe drinking and domestic use water, 6000 will be supported with sanitation infrastructures (latrines) in schools, health facilities and community gathering places and all of them will also be covered by hygiene promotional activities.

Cordaid has pre-positioned one drilling pad machine at Bentiu, one manual village drilling machine stationed and one SWAT system at Upper Nile. Cordaid has successfully installed the SWAT system in Panam (Canal/Pigi) and it is fully operational. These equipment, together with our 3 field offices in Wau, Bentiu and Malakal, enable us to respond in a timely manner during emergencies (e.g. new IDP movement), and to support more durable solutions in recovery process (e.g. for returnees).

project_name: Water, Hygiene and Sanitation emergency intervention to alleviate severely affected communities
project_objective: The action will be an integrated WASH and Nutrition program where WASH integrated interventions starting from SAM/MAM admission at OTP/SC will be targeted “mother/caretaker – malnourished children” until the household level aiming to break the vicious circle of diarrhea diseases/nematodes with malnutrition, addressing also small stock open defecation affecting the young children. Emergency hygiene and sanitation programming will be done alongside nutrition treatment and prevention targeting vulnerable populations affected by conflicts at health/nutrition sites and in the community. Community volunteers such as hygiene promoters, hand pump mechanics and MIYCN support groups will be engaged in coordination with government structures while local leaders will be engaged in consultative meetings and encouraged to actively support programming.

project_name: Communicating with communities with a provision of key life saving information and messages through community engagement, social mobilization and strengthened community accountability systems and mechanims.
project_objective:
Empowering Rohingya refugees and host communities to provide feedback is key to enable a relevant, conflict-sensitive and localised response. Using established feedback systems supplemented with additional feedback through targeted outreach and engagement, such as perception surveys and focus group discussions, will help provide data that can be consolidated and can support sectors’ in decision-making. UNICEF through its project interventions will ensure community engagement , participation and a paradigm shift from messaging to dialogue, by engaging key community stakeholders and wider communities. Some of the key activities: i) TRAINING & CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT: Identify, engage and train community volunteers and staff of partner organanizations on IPC and CwC techniques and methods.

ii) AWARENESS GENERATION & BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: Raise awareness to targeted population (children, women, men) on key behavioral and social change messages on health, nutrition, education, hygiene, sanitation, and protection through door to door visits, community consultations & community dialogue for sustained behaviour change.

iii) RADIO & LOCAL MEDIA PROGRAMMING & BROADCASTING: Develop age-appropriate and culture sensitive  local media programme i.e IPT show, folk song and Tarara shows, development of public service announcements, partnership with the ministry of information/Bangladesh Betar, BBC Media Action & community Radio Naf. 

iv) SOCIAL MOBILISATION & COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT: Identify community leaders including children and adolescents who have the potential to influence their immediate community; conduct training/ orientation with local community leaders e.g., maji, imams, women leaders, children and adolescent on key Community engagement approaches and messages; and engage local community leaders in designing, development, and implementation of Community engagment activities. To mobilise communities on DRR, enviornment and social cohesion through Inter personal sessions and wider community consultaions. Development of gender sensitive materails and ensuring sex disaggretated data is collated and synthesised through online platforms.

v) COMMUNITY ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISM: Train staff/volunteers managing IFCs especially in handling feedback and complaints; 
UNICEF will: continue to collect disaggregate data by sex, age and disability; ensure gender balanced teams (staff and volunteers); use mechanisms and create opportunities to engage community members and ensure equal access of women, girls, boys and men in the design, implementation and evaluation of  integrated programs.   Accountability will remain a key UNICEF priority in the years to come as well. UNICEF partners to collect feedback, grievances or complaints and respond to them with effective and timely data sharing and evidence generation with other agencies/sectors.  UNICEF will be covering a total population of 825,000 people through different community engagement approaches. Working in line with the CwC vision and objectives , UNICEF will ensure Human rights based interventions across the target groups.

project_name: Increasing access to lifesaving emergency healthcare services to vulnerable populations in Fangak and Nyirol focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality.
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to increase access to lifesaving emergency healthcare services to vulnerable populations in Fangak and Nyirol. This project seeks to scale up the provision of Lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality. According to HC bulletin (July 2018), a total of 7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Out of this, it is estimated that 4,058,392 women, men and children will need humanitarian healthcare services in 2019. People in need are 82,791 in Fangak and 91,861 in Nyirol, including 26,200 IDPs in Fangak and 53,590 in Nyirol integrated into host communities. Cluster targets are 46,363 in Fangak and 51,442 in Nyirol (Cluster PIN 25 Oct 18). The payams in greatest need are Manajang, Paguir in Fangak and Waat, Pultruk and Pading in Nyirol. 

This objective will be achieved by: 1). Increasing access to essential PHC and an integrated multi-sector assistance and services which address life threatening diseases as well as the medical complications associated with malnutrition, WASH and SGBV 2). Strengthening protection of and increasing access to specialized and integrated services for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys 3. Scaling up support to the most vulnerable as well as at-risk communities to sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks including promotion of emergency health protection for people with disabilities and 4). Improving prompt and quick response to outbreaks such as to cholera, kala-azar and other highly infectious diseases

To offer quality services, the project will prioritize capacity building of health and nutrition actors on standard procedures for screening and referral of SAM children with medical complications as well as Malaria RDT training. In the spirit of integration, the project will promote water quality testing and Monitoring in health facilities to mitigate disease spread and implement the integration of Health education messages across sectors on risk communication. Further, the project will promote collaboration with protection on Mapping of SGBV services and referrals.

This project is aligned to both the HRP as well as the health cluster strategic objectives and deliver services through PHCC, PHCU and mobile modalities. Activities will revolve around screening/detection for both health and nutrition problems, management of common illnesses, referral, prevention and surveillance/ EWARN reporting. It is envisaged that a successful implementation of these activities would significantly result in the overall improvement of access and scaling-up of responsiveness in the two counties as well as prevention, detection and response to epidemic prone diseases. Project activities will also achieve the dividends of an integrated response involving key sectors such as health, Wash, Nutrition, food security and protection.

For purposes of Gender and Protection Mainstreaming, the project will applying IASC guidance, measures to identify specific needs by: 1. involving the at-risk group women in project planning, implementation and monitoring 2. Implementing strategies that increase the safety, availability and accessibility of health and nutrition services for women, girls, boys and other at-risk groups especially pregnant adolescent girls and work with them to plan schedules that are convenient and safe for at-risk women, girls and boys 3. Implementing proactive strategies to meet the protection needs of most-at-risk groups accessing nutrition services 4.Designating a facility-based safety focal person to conduct safety audits and ensure staff know the referral pathway for victims of SGBV 5. Providing health education and gender awareness training to men and women on SGBV risk and the need for protection to secure that the most-at-risk groups have unimpeded access to health services.

project_name: Emergency WASH support to IDPs and Vulnerable host communities in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States.
project_objective:
Provision of adequate WASH services is key to achieving sustainable solutions to communities in emergency. CMD, a national NGO working in the locations of Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria envisages a response aimed at reaching internally displaced persons and vulnerable host communities with water, sanitation and hygiene services. Spanning a period of 12 months, the project targets the locations of Ayod, Duk, Nyirol, Uror and Twic East (Jonglei), Ulang, Maiwut and Longechuk (Upper Nile) and Kapoeta South, Kapoeta North, Kapoeta East and Budi (Eastern Equatoria) with WASH temporary and sustainable services, to address the vital needs, public health and protection issues. 
 
The response aims at mitigating WASH related GBV by providing gender appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities and tackling issues surrounding gender, safety and WASH.  Persistence of food insecurity, signalled by high GAM rates, with <5s and PLW mainly affected will be mitigated by the provision of WASH in Nutrition services, through targeted WASH minimum packages at OTP/SC mainly for mother/caretaker – malnourished children. 
Water related disease outbreaks have been traced to health facilities and community infrastructures/settings without adequate WASH facilities. A WASH in health outbreak control response is planned especially in disease prone counties. 

The project targets a total of 98,000 people; 44,100 of these in Jonglei (45%); (Ayod – 14,700; Duk – 2,940; Nyirol – 11,760; Uror - 10,780; Twic East – 3,920.); 24,500 in Upper Nile (25%); (Ulang – 9,800; Maiwut – 6,860; Longechuk – 7,840) and 29,400 in Eastern Equatoria (30%); (Kapoeta North – 5,880; Kapoeta East – 7,840; Kapoeta South – 11,760 and Budi – 3,920). 52% of those targeted are females, 31% of them girls. IDPs consist of 52% of those targeted.

project_name: Enhancing emergency and integrated lifesaving primary health care services among the vulnerable communities of Pochalla, Uror, Koch,Mayom and Pibor Counties (Jonglei and Unity State).
project_objective: Improve access and scale-up responsiveness to essential healthcare needs of the vulnerable populations by focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality through the existing 8 Health Facilities in Pochalla (7 PHCUs, and 1 Upgraded PHCC+ in Pochalla (Pochalla, Alari, Ajwongbai, Otali, Ajwara, Ojangbai,Obudi and Okadi),  Uror (Yuai, Pathai, Payai, Wei-kol, Patuet and Thiam) Koch ( Koch PHCC , Bow PHCC and Bieh PHCU) Pibor (Verteth, Thanajon, ) Mayom (Kueryei, Mankien, Mayom town and Bieh) .To Prevent, detect and respond to epidemic prone disease outbreaks and promote WASH in health facilities in conflict affected and vulnerable populations.

project_name: Nutrition Emergency assistance for IDPs, Host and Returnees in Fangak County , Jonglei state .
project_objective: In line with Nutrition clusters 2019 HRP response plan, CAO proposes life-saving treatment services targeting children less than five years, pregnant and lactating women as the most vulnerable groups to acute malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs. Prevention activities will also be incorporated in the response to reduce incidence of acute malnutrition and promote good health. An integrated response will be considered with other sectors e.g GBV and Child Protection which CAO is a strong and active member to address the drivers of malnutrition; food insecurity, sub-optional child care and feeding practices, morbidity, lack of safe water and sanitation, internal displacements. The response has prioritized uncovered hard to reach locations in conflict prone areas where population especially target group experience high rates of acute malnutrition. The proposed Nutrition in emergency project for the year 2019 will reach out to 14500 beneficiaries through both static and mobile approaches, working to ensure value for money with the 100,000usd fund support if granted. CAO has existing CP, GBV and Health projects already running with support from SSHF , UNICEF & IOM . All activities throughout the project will be shared with stakeholders and beneficiaries through an existing mechanism for transparency. As required CAO will ensure accountability of resources as well as proper Monitoring and evaluation of activities and reports in Fangak County is well implemented .

project_name: CP-Provision of Emergency CP Services and interventions Through Case Management and Supporting Community Base Child Protection Mechanism In Uror, Fangak And Canal/Pigi-Jonglei State.
project_objective: This project will be targeting 50,000 IDP, host communities and people returnee from Uror, Fangak & Pigi in Jonglei state with significant impact aiming at improving continuation support at helping children and young people affected by armed conflict.
