With provision of comprehensive Case Management and  FTR, process, organize structural and semi-structural and strengthening access to community led Child Friendly Spaces, Psycho-social Support, developing healthy and safe coping mechanisms to reduce the risk of children and adolescents resulting in recruitment by armed groups/forces, becoming street working children, or being left without care takers in hard-to-reach of Uror, Fangak and Pigi counties as prioritized areas, improve protection of conflict affected males, females under the age of 18 years and internally displaced children, especially separated and unaccompanied children are better protected through: 1) comprehensive case management system and provision of dignity kits and life-saving material assistance; 2) building the capacity of the community-based Child Protection network on mechanisms and approach; 3) improve Referral system for GBV and CP cases; 4) provide alternative care support to children without care givers, conduct Family Tracing and Reunification; 5) CP mainstreaming into Education, WASH, Health, and FSL and conducting awareness raising to prevent and respond to child protection issues.

project_name: WASH.Provision of Emergency WASH with Integrated GBV Prevention and Health Services for Disaster Affected Population in Nasir (Upper Nile State) and Pigi (Jonglei State), South Sudan
project_objective:
The project is targeting 25,477 individuals of 4,246 households including vulnerable children, women, and men from IDPs and host communities in Nasir County (Upper Nile State) and Pigi’ County (Jonglei State) who are living with chronic emergency WASH needs and impending cholera outbreaks. The planned WASH activities will as well support cholera prevention and management interventions by creating synergies through preventing WASH related diseases aimed at reducing morbidity and mortality rates through provision of clean, safe and adequate water, dignified sanitation services, Cholera kits as well as hygiene promotion messaging among the affected population in Nasir and Pigi Counties. This project targets IDPs, returnees and host communities.

The project activities and targets will include; refresher training of 50 hygiene promoters (30 females and 20 males) and 18 hygiene campaigns across the two Counties and benefiting 3,000 men, 3,400 women, 10,590 boys and 8,487 girls through participatory hygiene promotion, training of 30 water management committee members benefiting 150 people (100 females and 50 males), distribution of WASH NFIs benefiting 4,246hh or 25,477 people (3,000 men, 3,400 women, 10,590 boys, and 8,487 girls) and distribution of menstrual hygiene products benefiting 3,566 girls and women (30% of female population). The project will further promote sanitation through construction or installation of 45 emergency latrine structures with 4 stances each (amounting to 180 stances) aimed at promoting proper human excreta disposal in public places at Boma level. The project intends to benefit 25,477 people, majority of whom are women and children.

This project comes at a time when Nasir and Pigi counties have received high influx of IDPs due to displacements resulting from the recurring conflicts in other parts of Jonglei State and mostly from Akobo, Nyirol and others as returnees from other Counties hosting them as IDPs. The situation in the IDP sites has negatively impacted on the already limited basic WASH services that are shared with the host communities in the target areas. Therefore, this project will address the needs of the most vulnerable women, men, boys and girls affected by the conflict and lacking sufficient basic WASH services.
Among others, the deliverable for the project will include:
• Vulnerable and affected populations have access to safe and sufficient water (based on Sphere standards), provided through the active involvement of local communities.
• Vulnerable and affected populations have knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases.
• Vulnerable and affected populations enabled to access adequate, safe, secure, and dignified and gender segregated sanitation services (based on Sphere standards) 
• Availability of trained hygiene promoters, volunteers and local community on good WASH practices.

project_name: Integrated program to support the most vulnerable and food insecure households in Uror, Nyirol, Canal/Pigi, Lafon and Kapeta East Counties in Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria States through provision livelihood kits, food and resilient building initiatives.
project_objective:
The signing of the Revitalised Peace agreement and the recent cerebration in Juba on 31st October 2018 with both parties showing commitments to its implementation and an international community that is sceptical, CAFAD proposes an integrated program with aspects of emergency humanitarian assistance and resilience in 2019 that is in line with FSL cluster objectives 2, 3 and 4 (FSL HRP 2019 plans)

The emergency aspect is to support the most vulnerable 20,000 women, girls men and boys classified in IPC 4 and 3 in the Uror, Nyirol, Canal/Pigi and Lafon Counties with emergency food and livelihood support; fishing kits and 3 variety of fast maturing vegetable seeds. Emergency food production activities will be carried out to support main season agricultural inputs; seeds and tool distribution and fishing kits.
During distribution, CAFAD shall provide technical information and guidance to the beneficiaries on best use of agriculture and fishing kits being distributed. This will cover handling of inputs provided with support of visual aids and captions with instructions. Good agronomic practices, seed production and preservation techniques, post-harvest processing and store management, family nutrition with special emphasis on food preparation, processing & utilization will be covered in the trainings.
Under this also livestock treatment and vaccinations will be pursued in cases of diseases outbreaks and for preventative measures for high risk diseases such as FMD, RVF. Vaccinations will target 150,500 animals; 65,000 Shoats, 2500 Poultry, 85,000 Cattle and 250 dogs. A total 55,000 animals will be treated against worm infestation, ectoparasite, pneumonia in calves etc. 20 Community animal health workers in each County will undergo refresher training on livestock disease management and vaccination.
CAFAD will also give support to seed fairs using locally sourced seeds in Kapoeta East and Lafon Counties. Voucher system will be employed for seeds procurement. Accountability with complaint and feedback mechanisms will ensure inclusion of vulnerable target groups.
In order to reduce the overreliance on food aid and the dwindling donor resources, CAFAD also proposes transitional emergency food assistance. This will target vulnerable 5,000 HH in Uror, Nyirol, Lafon and Kapoeta East classified in IPC 3 and some in IPC4 with potential for sustainable livelihoods with food for assets activities. Beneficiaries will be monitored through created template that will capturing completed outputs against set targets for FFA activities. As part of enhancing human capitals, CAFAD shall conduct integrated trainings for beneficiaries on best farming practices, agribusiness and food nutritional value during the entire period of assets creation.
This aims at strengthening food security and capacity of local communities in target counties to manage risks through investment in livelihood asset. This will be complemented by sensitization and awareness as well as strengthening institutional capacities of local systems in order to provide adequate response in time of such disasters or shocks. 
Women needs, rights and voice will be taken into consideration in all the interventions and ensure integration, inclusion of youths in peace building.

Activities to support value chain addition like milk and fish preservation, trainings on farm production will be pursued

project_name: GBV: Increasing access to services by GBV survivors in Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria and Upper Nile States
project_objective: This project is targeting conflict affected host community, returnees and IDPS   living in Yei , Morobo, Kapoeta North and Renk counties  who are at high risk of gender based violence,death, injury and life threatening diseases like HIV/Aids, STIs and reproductive health related illnesses aggravated due to violence. The primary purpose of the project is to prevent protection risks and to provide timely response services to men, women, boys and girls affected by conflict .The target population is 12200 individuals broken down as 1000 boys and 4000 girls, 6200 women 1000 men. The project will be implemented in a period of 12 months and is costed at a budget of $ 440,000 .CIDO will implement this project directly in the target locations  in collaboration with the target population, the local administration ,line ministry  and partners on ground to achieve maximum project results. The project activities are designed to prevent and respond to GBV. This are; Case management / Individual PSS, community Outreach and safe referrals. GBV risk mitigation, Operations of WGFS, engagement of women , youth and adolescent girls and boys in GBV programming. The project dedicates 30% of the budget to cash based interventions. It is expected that by the end of the project period, lives of vulnerable women and girls will be saved, they will have increased access to services and positive life skills and positive coping mechanisms entrenched in them. It is anticipated that boys and men will be better informed on GBV prevention mechanisms in emergencies and will make meaningful contribution to the population needs of safe and, dignified lives.

project_name: EMERGENCY FOOD SECURITY AND  LIVELIHOOD RESPONSE PROGRAM TO  10000  VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS (60000 PEOPLE)   IN  HIGH FOOD INSECURE AREAS IN WESTERN BAHR EL GHAZAL STATE OF WAU (GREATER BAGGARI )  AND RAJA COUNTIES.SOUTH SUDAN
project_objective:
South Sudan is still facing alarming Humanitarian situation .Recent September, 2018 reported that  it is expected that 6.1 million1 people (59% of the total population2) faced Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity3 at the peak of the lean season (July – August), of whom 47,000 were in Catastrophe (IPC phase 5) and 1.7 million were in Emergency (IPC Phase 4). 

According to  same report the food security situation in the Western Bahr-El Ghazal State is deteriorating  in Septemeber 2018 compared to the same time last year (Wau urban in phase 4, Greater Bagari in phase 4, Raga in phase 4 and Jur River in phase 3).The main driving factors includes Insecurity, looting of livelihood assets, poor access to food due torestricted movement to productive farmland,limited access to natural food sources, Seasonally poor feeder road conditions causing low market supply andirregular salary payment to the civil servants. However, with presence of Raga and Greater Bagari in phase 4 and few population amount to 5% IPC phase classification are catastrophe phase. The key message of the IPC report further indicates that between Based on the September 2018 IPC analysis, the overall IPC phase is projected between January to March 2019 to be in( phase 3 in Wau Urban, phase 4 in Greater Bagari, phase 2 in Jur river and phase 3 in Raga County respectively). The main driving factors includes Reduction in purchasing power,decreased projection in humanitarian assistance, Possible returnees – affecting market by increasing local demand, depleting households stock level livestock disease prevalence, limited health facilities and  services, limited clean and protected water sources, increase number of returnees, Cattle movement far away from homestead.
Raja and Greater Bagri have limited access to Humanitarian assistance- area faced with persistent fighting.In 2017, interagency assessment conducted in greater Baggari, wau County (Nutrition report 23rd to 26th August, 2017, acute malnutrition prevalence remains at castratophic in Mboro (SAM 16.7%, MAM  21.3%, GAM  38.1%). Famine in Greater Baggari area in Wau is eminent with the nutritional trend. With huge humanitarian response, the nutrition situation improved. However with the recent blockade to these areas for Humanitarian services, the area is expected to face significant food insecurity. Similarly inn 2017, the South Sudan crop watch update (september 2017)  reported that the cropping season is characterized by heavy infestation of crop weeds, diseases and insect pests, including Striga (parasitic weed on sorghum and maize) in most areas and presence of relatively new pests particularly Fall Armyworm (FAW) in some areas. Common diseases were sorghum smut and groundnut leaf spot. Similar field reports from COER shares the same issue 
Nearly 50,000 people are expected to be highly food insecured. Food insecurity is affecting all categories of people  but the most vulnerable people at risk are women and youths. Women in addition to the food insecurity that they are faced are also at high protection risk of been raped, kidnapped or kill as they fend their livelihoods. Youths are at risk of been conscripted into the fighting forces. This is also another trend happening because of lack of access to food. 
Despite these challenges faced in South Sudan, there is need for a proactive Food Security livelihood intervention in the short run  and need for resilience based activities in the long term so that communities will cover from the shocks.. Central to addressing this food need is consideration of accountability to affected population, centrality of protection in Humanitarian action and multisectoral programming especially coordinating with other clusters

project_name: Title: EMERGENCY FOOD SECURITY LIVELIHOOD  WITH RESILIENCE  LIGHT INTERVENTIONS TO  10000  VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS  IN  HIGH FOOD INSECURE AREAS IN WAU (WESTERN BAHR EL GHAZAL), NYRIOL ( JONGLEI) AND MAYENDIT ( UNITY ) STATE  SOUTH SUDAN
project_objective:
Cisda is proposing an Emergency and Resilience light support interventions in three major hot spots food insecure States in Unity, Jonglei and Western Bahr- El Ghazal . The proposed project runs from January 2019 to December, 2019 . 
The key objective of the project  are to increase Vulnerable household access to food through support to increase food production  and to reduce the level of vulnerability amongst malnourished children through access to nutrition vouchers and production of high nutritious vegetables. The project is  line with HRP strategic objective 2 ( SO2) and is in support of FSL cluster objective 2 and  FSL cluster objective 4

The project will target mainly IDPs and Vulnerable host population in these areas. A total of 50,000 people will be targeted. The program will be delivered through direct distributions of inputs, voucher assistance support to vulnerable households, training in improved vegetable production  and vaccination of livestocks. These activities are mainly agricultural and livestock related and they are 
Women , children, girls that are at  high protection risks will be targeted throughout the implementation of the project . Additionally the project has major consideration for the accountability to affected population, thus a very strong AAP committee will be established.

CISDA has over three years  strong experience in implementing similar Emergency food security and livelihood projects in the same geographical context. The project thus will leverage on the experiences gained during the past implementation inorder to adequately address the food insecurity problem.

The project will integrate or work closely with both the protection cluster and the nutrition cluster. With protection cluster, the project will support beneficiaries identified by the protection partner that are high protection risk. they will be mapped out and supported during implementation. With the nutrition project, the project will set up demonstration sites at OTP centres and train households with malnourished children. These households will  also be supported with high nutritous vegetables which they will produce to address the nutritional needs of their malnourished children.

project_name: Provision of emergency WASH Support interventions targeting most vulnerable Internally Displaced Populations and Host Communities in Jonglei, Eastern and Western Equatoria States
project_objective:
Despite recent revitalized peace deal signing by the different factions,  the country has continued to witness increasing ceasefire violations especially in the Equatorias and bureaucratic impediments, further undermining efforts to create the previous status quo. Subsequently, 5.7 million people will not have access to adequate water, sanitation and hygiene in 2019 and at least 5.2 million people are estimated to be facing extreme levels of food insecurity in the beginning of 2019 with significant populations projected to face alarming food consumption gaps, asset depletion and malnutrition rates in the Equatorias, Jonglei among others regions (IPC September, 2018). 

Proposed actions will target beneficiaries primarily made up 2,500 households (15,000 beneficiaries) in Jonglei, Eastern and Western Equatoria States. These will be a total of 5000 girls, 5000 boys, 2500 men and 2500 women - these include elderly and people with special needs amongst the most vulnerable emergency affected IDPs and host communities affected by the ongoing conflict. The action will respond to prioritized locations taking into account cost effective measures of prepositioning supplies through WASH Cluster/IOM pipeline. 

Community Aid for Relief and Development (CARD) proposes to implement activities which are aimed at improving access to safe water supply,  improving safe and gender appropriate  sanitation facilities , hygiene promotion, support children admitted for SAM treatment discharged with WASH/Hygiene kit from functional OTP/SC , provision of access to safe drinking water, provision of functional handwashing facilities by soap and provision of WASH minimum package of activities to mitigate WASH-related diseases including Ebola Virus Disease hotspots in the Equatorias. 

CARD will in addition regularly review and adapt ways of working with affected populations and increase levels of transparency and participation of affected boys, girls, women and men. CARD will also mainstream cross cutting measures as gender equality and women and youth empowerment,
protection, environmental conservation, HIV/AIDS, accountability to affected populations and youth involvement including taking into account Gender Based Violence and sexual exploitation and mitigating risks associated with crowding and long distances during implementation.

project_name: Provision of integrated emergency GBV response and strengthening communities to prevent and mitigate vulnerabilities of women and girls at risk of GBV in Unity, Upper Nile, Lakes and Warrap States.
project_objective:
The planned CHADO integrated GBV strategy for 2019 will focus both but more on emergency GBV response including at a lesser components of transition and recovery GBV programming. The emergency response activities which comprises of provision of comprehensive case management targeting 1250 women and girls including those living with disabilities, provision of psychosocial support (PSS) through specialized counselling, group counselling and inter-generational meetings (TEA-TALKs) where older women interact with younger and girls to discuss issues regarding domestic roles to prevent domestic violence and early child marriages. The PSS activities will target 4,000 women and girls. The provision of Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) to most vulnerable women and girls including PwD’s will on be on case-by-case basis to help the most vulnerable person’s with life-saving assistance such to reduce the impact of hunger, lack of access to services, NFI’s, and those at risk stigma due to culture and traditions. The assistance will also include where appropriate, provide access to justice. Individual Protection Assistance will target 600 women and girls. As part of the life-saving activities CHADO will use the theory of “Information/communication Saves Life’s” provide of safe referrals, including information dissemination on available services through findings of 11 safety audits in the targeted Counties and the subsequent dissemination of key safety messages including advocacy to local authorities where appropriate.
The recovery and transition centered activities will basically focus on provision of support programming through establishment of 15 Women and Girls Friendly spaces, strengthening 15 community-based protection monitoring committee’s with 15 members each totaling 225 persons (65% women and girls) in each location, provide protection awareness campaigns and GBV prevention messaging targeting 15,000 men, women, boys and girls. The women support component will focus on provision protective socio-economic support to vulnerable women and girls through trainings on Village Savings and Loans Association which is Small Scale Micro-finance Enterprise (SSME). The training will also include commodity retailing and Vegetable Farming as business. They will either be provided with Conditional Cash Transfers (CCT) in VSLA groups or vegetable seeds for commercial purpose. The targeted women for protective socio-economic support are 2,200 women and the girls will be only those above the age of 18. A clear vulnerability criterion will set and the final list of beneficiaries in each location will be jointly validated with stakeholders such as RRC, local authorities and local community leaders. The use of Fuel Efficient Stoves (FES) from CHADO experience in Koch County has proven that the use of FES for cooking is an excellent GBV mitigating strategy as it limits by half the risk of GBV faced by women and girls including domestic violence. It also reduces by half the frequency of fetching firewood and reduces health risk children and women to indoor respiratory tract diseases. Therefore CHADO will facilitate trainings on moulding and use of Fuel Efficient Stoves targeting 1200 women and girls. Another mitigation strategy is the mentoring of boys and youths, including adolescent girls and young women on Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) programming  (mentoring youth as agents of change on risks mitigation against GBV) will target 2500 adolescent boys and girls, male and female youths in the targeted locations. The need for sustainable peace in all communities in South Sudan is of high importance therefore CHADO will engage all targeted communities in peacebuilding and peaceful co-existence to strengthen inter- and intra-clan/community peaceful coexistence o ensure durable humanitarian access and programming. The targeted population for peacebuilding and peaceful co-existence 1,100 community leaders and other community gate keepers.

project_name: Emergency Food Security and Livelihoods Response for Conflict-Affected Populations in Leer, Mayendit, Koch and Panyijiar Counties of Central Unity State.
project_objective:
The project will target 8,000 vulnerable IDPS, Returnees and Host communities in Koch, Leer, Mayendit and Panyijiar Counties with support to help rebuild the ability of communities to produce their own food and thereby safeguard their livelihoods. It is envisaged that for the project to achieve its overall goals,CH shall integrate and mainstream across the various activities elements of  GBV, general protection,conflict transformation and WASH to have holistic results.Where necessary, CH will work in close collaboration with other partners where we do not have experience and expertise in achieving the overall goal of mainstreaming and integration to maximise on resources as well as benefits.The project is expected to address urgent short and medium term support to most vulnerable members of the communities in concentrated IDPS sites such as in islands and other hard to reach areas as well as providing basic support for them as some start to return slowly to their homes. 
CH will provide agricultural inputs for vegetables and crop seed to the returning farmers. Given the potentially devastating risk of fall armyworm infestation, CH will support development an Early Warning System (EWS) to ensure farmers are able to prepare and deal with this risk appropriately. Alongside this, CH will also provide transitional livelihood kits in the form of fishing rods, fast maturing vegetable crop seeds, and other agricultural inputs to enable them farmers cultivate food for their families and some for sale to the market. 
In order to ensure livestock diseases are managed effectively, CH will support livestock vaccination against disease prevention and treatment especially targeting Zoonotic diseases as Rift Valley Fever, Anthrax, Haemorrhagic septicaemia (HS), black quarter which are common in these areas. CH will also strengthen the provision of extension support to enable farmers adopt best practice in agricultural production and livestock management in order to increase their productivity. This with other tactics involve working with the farmer field schools to train farmers in each of the payams ensuring that they can optimise their farms under cultivation.

project_name: To promote resilience through Food Security and Livelihoods intervention in North Waziristan and Orakzai tribal district
project_objective:
Through this project, Muslim Aid aims to support most vulnerable communities in North Waziristan and Orakzai tribal districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. These communities are in a transition phase where they have been affected by crises when government of Pakistan carried an operation against terrorists. 
Through this project Muslim Aid intends to contribute in the FATA Transition plan through outcome # 1 Livelihood and Economic growth and outcome.  Strengthening the humanitarian-development nexus in service of economic growth and livelihoods in the Tribal districts will not only improve the lives of the most vulnerable, but the reductions in risk and vulnerability will be essential to ensuring that development progress is accessible to all, including those affected by crises. Putting the new way of working into practice will enable the immediate rehabilitation and restoration of community livelihoods, coupled with long-term initiatives that make these livelihoods sustainable over time, endow Tribal Districts’ populace with the skills needed to thrive in the labour market, and spur business development across the region. These aims are vital for ensuring that FATA/Tribal districts have a skilled, secure and healthy workforce capable of achieving economic growth targets and coping with potential future crises.
Given the fact there has been temporary displacement took place over the past years, Muslim Aid has incorporated the length of displacement in its program design. This program will priorities female beneficiaries of the current returnees, some only 45% registered returnees are women, which reflect the cultural and administrative hurdles that limit their ability to get registered and access assistance. Given the fact that returnees have different skills set, this program will customize services provided by Muslim Aid to the individual needs of returnees, skills they possess and the suitability of livelihoods opportunities in each area. Through local CBO's and Community Committees, MA will identify on-farm and off farm rehabilitation projects; environmental improvement projects; initiatives to restore abandoned agricultural land, irrigation systems and new command areas; flood protection and soil erosion control measures, and new infrastructure requirements, including improved market linkages. Implement these through cash for work / In-kinds modalities, ensuring screening for natural resource impacts.  Provide agricultural and livestock inputs to restore livelihood capacity at the household and community levels.

project_name: Emergency Child Protection Services for Vulnerable Children and Caregivers in Awerial and Yirol East (Lakes) and Nagero and Tambura (Western Equatoria)
project_objective:
It is estimated that 6,023,576 South Sudanese women, men, boys and girls face multiple protection threats and vulnerabilities resulting from active conflicts, displacement, and breakdown of community protection systems and structures exacerbated by economic decline, lack of basic services and disease burden (Protection Cluster HRP 2019 Strategy). 192,574 of the people in need of protection assistance are from Western Equatoria (Nagero and Tambura) and Lakes (Awerial and Yirol East). While 65% of these are IDPs, 61% of the affected people are children. Crises affected children are exposed to serious threats and risks including separation from families, psychosocial distress, armed recruitment and sexual and physical violence. Without appropriate care and family-based support, affected children are forced to process their conflict experience alone, which may prevent them from being able to fully engage in daily activities such as playing, learning, or basic social interaction. Of the children in need, 16000 children and their caregivers (7000 girls, 6500 boys,  1500 women and 1000 men) will be targeted for integrated life-saving child protection in emergency services in Nagero, Tambura, Awerial and Yirol East in 2019.

Nagero experienced fighting in April 2018 and populations have been displaced to Tambura. Mingkaman IDP camp in Awerial hosts the largest caseload of IDP in the country. Military forces clashed with civilians in Rumbek causing a protection crisis in Yirol East in May 2018. In all these contexts, children have been severely affected and the poor child protection indicators include high caseload of separated and unaccompanied children (UASC), lack of psychosocial, recreational and learning opportunities for affected children, precarious incidents of sexual and physical violence against (SGBV) children and adolescents, use of children by armed forces and armed groups (CAAFAG), and increase in child marriages and child exploitation.
 
To ensure that boys and girls of high protection risks receive critical child protection services, CINA will provide comprehensive case management including for separated and unaccompanied children, children associated with armed forces/groups, child survivors of SGBV, severe psychosocial distress and children in conflict with law. CINA will support caregivers and caseworkers to provide the critical protection care and structured psychosocial support services through emergency CFS, PSS in the community and in schools through support to teachers/PTAs, CP helpdesks and life skills and resilience services for adolescents. In order to increase access to, and strengthen resilience to well-coordinated age and gender-sensitive child protection and preventive services, CINA will conduct child protection risk awareness sessions, CP campaigns and provide support to child protection structures and adolescent peer to peer groups to prevent and respond to violence against children. 
To ensure centrality of protection, this project will address risks facing UASC, OVC, CAAFAG, child headed households, adolescent girls, and children living with disabilities, etc. through strengthened community safety audits, community protection mechanisms, etc. CINA’s staff will sign and adhere to code of conduct and CP policy to ensure safety, dignity and avoid causing harm. The team will conduct community and caregivers’ consultations on sites for CFS, etc and conduct monthly beneficiary feedback mechanisms on quality of CP services delivered by CINA as a means for Accountability to Affected Populations. Adolescents and children with disabilities will be particularly empowered with self-protection and life skills and involved to ensure meaningful participation for all children. CINA is currently implementing CP activities in Tambura and Awerial. To avoid overlapping in Tambura, CINA has agreed with WV for CINA to focus its CP activities in Nagero, Mapoi and Jerusalem areas in Tambura town.

project_name: Coordinated support to the NGO Forum members to improve and save lives
project_objective: In recent years, especially since the passing of the NGO Act 2016 and the proliferation of State and National-level operational requirements, NGOs have become increasingly the target of requests for fees, authorisations or taxes in relation to their operations, staff and equipment. These processes/ activities by authorities can sometimes provide assistance and facilitation to operations, however there are many more requests which detract from humanitarian activities and can lead to difficulties aid workers when compliance is not forthcoming. The NGO Forum is a membership body of over NGOs provides a unique platform to collaborate and share information among humanitarian actors working in South Sudan. The NGO Forum also serves the purpose of reinforcing capacity of National NGOs for improved and effective delivery of humanitarian services, sharing information and best practices, internal networking of NGOs for collective voices and joint representation to create an enabling environment for the INGOs and NNGOs in South Sudan. The NGO Forum project aims to effectively support the NGO community in South Sudan through information sharing on the security situation, trends and risks, representing member organisations at various fora, take the lead on advocacy and to create an enabling environment, and to coordinate with other actors such as the Government, UNOCHA and UNMISS. Therefore, this project will provide support to 214 national and 116 international NGOs who are the members of NGO Forum that supports its members to effectively respond to the humanitarian and development needs in South Sudan. All member organisations provide assistance to the South Sudanese people regardless of ethnic background, political affiliation, or religious belief.

project_name: Provision of life-saving shelter and non-food items to IDPs and affected populations in Rubkona, Guit and Koch Counties, Unity and Juba PoC and surrounding areas and Yei and surrounding areas, Central Equatoria, South Sudan 2019
project_objective:
Concern’s SNFI response will provide time-critical and life-saving assistance to populations facing greatest needs due to displacement through i) improved access to safe, appropriate emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to newly displaced or vulnerable populations in secondary displacement and ii) improved living conditions of highly vulnerable IDPs in protracted displacement, returnees and host communities unable to meet their S/NFI needs. The response will be targeted based on population needs and context. Concern has been providing SNFI assistance to conflict affected populations since the conflict began in December 2013 in Juba and Bentiu PoCs. This response will continue to support to populations in Juba and Bentiu PoCs with repair and replacement materials, construction of shelters in case of influx, as the main SNFI partner and with strong relations with the CHCs allowing for collaboration in planning and designing shelters. Concern was one of the first organisations to respond outside of Bentiu as part of BBR in 2016. As part of the BBR, Concern SNFI team will continue providing assistance to hard to reach and underserved populations in Rubkona, Guit and Koch Counties through mobile response. Also, IDPs have resettled in Bentiu and Rubkona towns due to congestion in Bentiu PoC and from more insecure locations in Unity. As Bentiu and Rubkona towns were destroyed during the conflict, rehousing opportunities remain low and SNFI needs are high. Concern’s market assessments in Bentiu and Rubkona have found that suppliers can meet some demands for shelter materials but as the markets are still recovering other materials will be provided in-kind. Concern piloted CBIs in Bentiu and Rubkona towns and will continue this approach in 2019. Concern will also implement a SNFI response in Juba to support IDPs resettling from Juba PoC and in Yei, with a combination of in-kind material and cash-based intervention, building on Concern’s experience in BBR to quickly set up SNFI operations in new locations. Concern aims to focus more on cash-based interventions in locations were security is more stable with functioning and accessible markets. This will give beneficiaries more flexibility in meeting needs and also contribute to market recovery. Concern mobile teams based in Juba and Bentiu hubs will be implementing the mobile responses. Concern will consult with beneficiaries to prior to distributions to ensure that shelter and NFI materials are as per social and cultural norms.
 
The targeted beneficiaries will be 14,092 households (47,988 individuals, 47,388 women and girls, 42,065 men and boys) in Bentiu PoC; 13,257 households (32,133 individuals15,540 women and girls, 16,573 men and boys) in need of reinforcement of shelters and new arrivals. 17,500 newly displaced and protracted IDPs in Juba and Yei Counties in Central Equatoria and Rubkona, Guit and Koch Counties in Unity will be targeted for access to shelter and NFIs. To ensure adherence to Do No Harm and to reduce community tensions, the most vulnerable host community or returnee populations will also be selected as vulnerability is not exclusive to IDPs. Beneficiaries will be selected based on strict criteria identified with communities to ensure needs are properly identified. The most vulnerable will be prioritised including PLW, households with the largest number of under 5 children, child-headed households, disabled, elderly, widows, orphans, and vulnerable female-headed households. 

Concern as the Unity State SNFI Cluster focal point and Juba PoC site focal point is in a position coordinate with other partners including sharing assessment information, identifying gaps in Unity and Central Equatoria to ensure coverage of needs as well as coordinating with the national SNFI Cluster. Despite a revitalised peace agreement, security remains unpredictable along with displacement, thus coordination with partners is essential to improve efficiency of responses.

project_name: Camp Coordination and Camp Management for Malakal PoC and mobile CCCM for South Sudan
project_objective:
Under DRC’s CCCM programme, the following major interventions will be implemented:
-	Camp management of the Malakal Protection of Civilian (PoC) site, including ongoing management, service coordination, monitoring and community engagement.
-	Mobile site management and site coordination for camps, collective centres and camp like settings in Unity State as part of the ‘Beyond Bentiu Response’, including service mapping, rapid assessments and monitoring, community engagement and community governance support.
-	Mobile site management and site coordination for Fashoda, Malakal, Baliet and Canal counties including service mapping, rapid assessments and monitoring, community engagement and community governance support.
-	National mobile emergency site management support in camps and camp like settings through emergency deployable CCCM teams.

project_name: Emergency Integrated Health & Nutrition Project (EIH&NP) In Equatoria region-South Sudan

SO1: Save lives by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys
SO2: Protect vulnerable women, men, girls and boys through provision of specialized and integrated services. The project will be implemented in compliant to the Health cluster strategy 2019; Provide Lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality.

project_name: HLP Awareness and restitution of property Rights in Yambio and Rumbeki
project_objective:
This project aims to implement  Housing, Land and Property  Rights’ project in
Yambio County in Western Equatoria state and Rumbeki County in Lakes state
This project covers the following protection cluster strategic objectives
The 3 S.O. for the Protection Cluster are:
1.   S.O.1: Provide immediate lifesaving assistance to address priority protection needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach areas
2. S.O.2: Prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience
3.      S.O.3: Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other affected populations
 The project proposal  has five activities:-
1.1.	 Provision of age and sex  appropriate legal awareness, assistance and counseling  to 560 beneficiaries on housing  land and property rights. This activity intends to hire services of legal experts to create awareness, provide legal assistance and legal counseling to men, women , boys and girls whose rights are under threat. 
1.2.	1.2. Provision of quality community awareness on fundamental rights relating to housing, land and property  targeting 9,520 beneficiaries 
1.3. Formation,  training  and support of  15 housing, land and property Right protection  committees to link communities  with survey departments, land commissions, local government authorities and community land committee  to advocate for respect of land rights, inclusion of women in land management and guarantee community rights to compensation when government discuss contract. The committees will consist of 14 members (at least 6 female and male members) will be formed in following places in Yambio county:- Li Rangu, Bangasu, Saura, Gangura, Hai Masia, Remenze, Timbiro, Hai Aworo, Hai Sujunu and Mumbai all in Yambio and Amongping, Jiir, Maleki, Matangai and Mayom in Rumbeki. .  This activity will benefit 3,640 individuals.
1.4. Conduct 12 Protection assessments and continuous monitoring in Yambio and Rumbeki. The activity is meant collect and analyze data related housing, land and property rights.
 1.5. Provision of individual Protection Assistance( NFI) to individuals and or families   whose  land and property rights have been abused . This activity targets  280 beneficiaries.



This project plan targets in total fourteen thousands  beneficiaries (men 3,500=25%,  women 4,760= 34%, boys  2,520= 18% and girls 3,220 =23%). The project is developed following grassroots consultations in  different payams of Yambio. The total Project cost will be USD 400,000. The project has established mechanisms aimed at enhancing accountability to affected populations through provision of information about assistance, protection from sexual exploitation and abuses, continuous consultation with affected population beyond community leaders, Feedbacks and complain mechanisms and community engagement monitoring and evaluation are put in place. To ensure the centrality of protection in humanitarian actions, this project is based on protection risk analysis that considered specific needs of different groups. It also seeks to Identify and address barrier to access that different population could face. These project activities are made in a way that promotes gender equality and addresses protection threats such as violence, coercion, exploitation etc. The project tools are tailored to specifically measure beneficiaries’: accesses, safety and dignity.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Food Relief and Livelihoods Resilience programmes for the vulnerable people in South Sudan (Bor South, Pibor, Aweil East, Aweil West and Magwi County).
project_objective:
According to Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), an estimated 5,749,000 South Sudanese women, men and children will not have sufficient access to food and livelihoods in 2019. GBI seeks to deliver a 12 months emergency Food Security and Livelihoods activities to critically vulnerable Households through Provision of Emergency Food Relief and Livelihoods Resilience programmes for the vulnerable people in South Sudan (Bor South, Pibor, Aweil East and Magwi Counties).

In line with the FSL cluster strategy and the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), GBI is proposing to scale up response in these locations through distribution of dry season kits (vegetable and fishing kits), livestock vaccination and training of CAHWs, cash transfers, assets creation and unconditional food) supporting existing partners responding or planning a response. 

The overall objective of this project is to improve the food security and livelihood status of vulnerable households (IDPs, returnees and host) in Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria and Northern Bahr El Ghazal states. This project is designed to reduce vulnerabilities and risk associated with the current food insecurity and poor economic conditions as a result of conflict, seasonal variability and displacement. A total of 10,000 beneficiaries comprising (returnees, IDPs and host) will be targeted directly with lifesaving livelihoods and food security interventions. The project will require $500,000 to provide the intended services and activities throughout the intervention period.

project_name: ENHANCE ACCESS TO  NUTRITIONAL SERVICES IN BALIET AND PANYIKANG COUNTIES IN SOUTH SUDAN.
project_objective:
The nutrition situation in South Sudan remains critical as food insecurity is expected to worsen. Currently the Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) levels in South Sudan are at 23% which is above 15% threshold of an emergency (UNICEF 2018).
 In Upper Nile GAM, SAM and MAM rates are even more higher reported at 21.8%, 5.8% and 16% respectively, The FSNMS ( Food Security and Malnutrition system Rates) shows increasing levels of malnutrition in the Upper Nile States and Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) 2018 classifies region to be in the Emergency level, grading  malnutrition at critical levels. Its estimated that 1 in every 4 persons are food insecure. (IPC May-July 2018).
Contributing factors include limited food availability due to reduced planting and harvesting, insecurity, economic crisis and limited humanitarian access. The high cost of living combined with high levels of inflation has continuously suffocated livelihoods in families and children are hit hardest by this catastrophic situation change. 
The Objective of this project is to:
•	Deliver quality life-saving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at-risk under-five children, pregnant and lactating women
•	Increased access to maternal infant and young child nutrition programs preventing under-nutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk.
•	Enhanced nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information for early warning timely coordinated response decision making.
The modalities to achieve the above objectives will be delivered through:
•	In patient management of SAM with Complications, Out Patient therapeutic program, and Targeted supplementary feeding programme. 
The project targets a total of 3,436 direct beneficiaries: 721 SAM, 21618 MAM (among Children aged 6 to 59 months) and 97 MAM (among Pregnant and Lactating Mothers)
The major activities will be:
•	Treatment of SAM and MAM among children aged 6-59months and Pregnant and Lactating mothers, 
•	Routine nutritional screening at facility entry points and community. 
•	Establishment of one stabilization centre at Baliet PHCC, 12 OTP and TSFP service sites at all the 12 functional health facilities of Baliet and panyikang. 
•	Training of Service on IMAM, CMAM and MIYCN. 
•	Establishment of 12 Mother support groups and conduct Individual and group IYCF counselling
•	Conducting community outreaches and engagement meetings.
•	Conducting Smart survey to access nutritional status of the population.
This proposed nutrition project will be integrated in to the already existing health programmes provided being provided in this location with support from World Bank. The integration will better address the nutritional needs of children and P&LW.  
HLSS will implement this project in collaboration with other stakeholders such as the county health department and other clusters to ensure a holistic approach in service provision.

project_name: Increasing access to Lifesaving emergency healthcare services to vulnerable populations in Panyikang County (Upper Nile State)Canal/Pigi and New Fangak Jonglei State focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality.
project_objective: The main objective of this project is to increase access to lifesaving emergency healthcare services to vulnerable populations in New Fangak,Panyikang County Upper Nile State,Pigi/Canal County Jonglei State This project seeks to scale up the provision of Lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality. According to HC bulletin (July 2018), a total of 6 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Out of this, it is estimated that 8,058,392 women, men and children will need humanitarian healthcare services in 2019. People in need are 12,791 in Panyikang 25395 people in need including IDPs 12028 and in Canal/Pigi, including 12527 IDPs in Fangak and 53,590 integrated into host communities. Cluster targets are 46,363 in Fangak and (Cluster PIN 25 Oct 18). The Payams in greatest need are Mankulaual, Keew Door in new Fangak and This objective will be achieved by: 1). Increasing access to essential PHC and an integrated multi-sector assistance and services which address life threatening diseases as well as the medical complications associated with malnutrition, WASH and SGBV 2). Strengthening protection of and increasing access to specialized and integrated services for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys 3. Scaling up support to the most vulnerable as well as at-risk communities to sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks including promotion of emergency health protection for people with disabilities and 4). Improving prompt and quick response to outbreaks such as to cholera, kala-azar and other highly infectious diseases to offer quality services, the project will prioritize capacity building of health and nutrition actors on standard procedures for screening and referral of SAM children with medical complications as well as Malaria RDT training. In the spirit of integration, the project will promote water quality testing and Monitoring in health facilities to mitigate disease spread and implement the integration of Health education messages across sectors on risk communication. Further, the project will promote collaboration with protection on Mapping of SGBV services and referrals. This project is aligned to both the HRP as well as the health cluster strategic objectives and deliver services through PHCC, PHCU and mobile modalities. Activities will revolve around screening/detection for both health and nutrition problems, management of common illnesses, referral, prevention and surveillance/ EWARN reporting. It is envisaged that a successful implementation of these activities would significantly result in the overall improvement of access and scaling-up of responsiveness in the two counties as well as prevention, detection and response to epidemic prone diseases. Project activities will also achieve the dividends of an integrated response involving key sectors such as health, Wash, Nutrition, food security and protection. For purposes of Gender and Protection Mainstreaming, the project will be applying IASC guidance, measures to identify specific needs by: 1. involving the at-risk group women in project planning, implementation and monitoring 2. Implementing strategies that increase the safety, availability and accessibility of health and nutrition services for women, girls, boys and other at-risk groups especially pregnant adolescent girls and work with them to plan schedules that are convenient and safe for at-risk women, girls

project_name: Provision of equitable access to quality emergency lifesaving Nutrition services to boys, girls and women in Fangak, Duk and Bor South Islands
project_objective:
This project will support the delivery of preventative and therapeutic nutrition services for 6,391 boys and 5,899 girls 3,550 PLWs in Old fangak, Wangchot, Chotbora, Nyatuat, Dhonor, Tock, Wanglel (Fangak); Amiel, Pajut, Dongchak and Pagaak (Duk); Mayen, Pajariei, Wutliet (Islands of Bor South) during 2019. project_name: Provision of primary health care services for vulnerable children and women in Syria
project_objective:
Under the overall framework of support to basic primary care services, this project aims to provide pediatric and maternal health consultations for children and women in the high-risk areas and IDP camps inside Syria through fixed health points and medical mobile teams run by NGOs, Implementing Partners (IPs) and government health directorates, and provide them with the essential health supplies (emergency health kits, midwifery kits, paediatric kits, diarrhea kits, first aid kits, medicines and equipment) to treat the common maternal and childhood diseases and prevent deaths among the vulnerable children and women. It will also focus on raising awareness among vulnerable mothers and care-givers on prevention of maternal new-born and child diseases, the importance of timely and complete vaccinations, hygiene promotion, danger signs for ill child and ill new-born, high-risk pregnancies and the importance of antenatal care and facility delivery.
The project will support routine immunization program for children under the age of one year, and supplementary immunization activities for children under the age of five years.
The project will also provide capacity building for health staff and community volunteers to ensure quality service and compensate for the heavy loss of health workers during the 8 years of the conflict.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Nutrition Interventions for Vulnerable Populations in Aweil South, Aweil East, Panyijiar, and Rumbek East Counties
project_objective:
The IRC has 25 years of experience working in South Sudan which uniquely positions IRC to continue to provide assistance in established field sites.  IRC has field offices located in Aweil East, Aweil South, Panyijar, Rumbek and Pamir and has longstanding relationships with the government, local authorities and communities in these geographic areas. Furthermore, IRC provides health and nutrition programming in each of these states, offering a foundation upon which to build strengthened nutrition service
This project will address life-saving humanitarian needs in Aweil East and Aweil South Counties, which are some of the counties with chronically high GAM rates of above 20%. SMART surveys conducted in Aweil East and Aweil South in June and August 2018, respectively, reported high prevalence of malnutrition in the two counties. The survey findings indicated that the nutritional status in Aweil East was very critical by GAM prevalence WHZ 21.2% %, which would require integrated strategies to control the situation. In Aweil South, the GAM rates were reported at 16.3 %. In Aweil East, the survey indicated high prevalence of acute malnutrition among children in the youngest age groups 6 -23 months with GAM 27.1% as compared to children aged 24-59 months with GAM of 16.4%.   In Panyijiar County, GAM levels have consistently been above 15% with insecurity and influx of IDPs from Leer and Mayendit counties as aggravating factors.  In Rumbek East, the coverage of the community management of malnutrition (CMAM) program is quite low and requires scale up of nutrition interventions to address needs. According to the FSNMS round 20 (at state level), in Lakes State, the prevalence of MAM and SAM in children under five years of age at 21.7% and 5.9 % respectively. The FSNMS also estimated the prevalence of PLW with MAM as 31.4% in Rumbek East. Aweil East is one of the counties with a high GAM rate and IPC of level 4 on the Nutrition Cluster strategy paper severity ranking matrix. The project will be integrated the health, child protection, WASH and food security sectors supported by UNICEF, WFP, OFDA and HPF in the counties.

The main components of this project are: 

1)	Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) among children under five years of age

2)	Management of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five years of age 

3)	Management of malnutrition among Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW)

4)	Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergency (IYCFE)

Treatment will directly target children under 5 years of age (without discrimination between boys and girls) and PLWs. The project will ensure inter-sectoral collaboration with the health sector for provision of stabilization kits for SAM with medical complications. Nutrition Cluster partners will provide malaria screening and referral/treatment for SAM and MAM cases. The WASH Cluster will support partners in the county to ensure the provision of clean and safe water for OTP/TSFP services, including appetite tests, hand washing, and appropriate ablution facilities. FSL Cluster partners in the county shall conduct general food distribution sessions that target households with SAM and MAM beneficiaries. Throughout the project cycle, community outreach and mobilization will be conducted to ensure early detection and improved coverage of the nutrition services in the targeted areas by the mobile and outreach teams. This project will target 25% of the nutrition cluster caseload as follows: 
􀀀 Aweil East SAM 3,868, MAM 7,146, MIYCN 3,599 
􀀀 Aweil South SAM 1,283, MAM 2,567, MIYCN individual counselling 3,483
 􀀀 Panyijiar SAM 1,511, MAM 3,666, MICN individual counselling 3,643 and 
􀀀 Rumbek East SAM 6,906, MAM 10,831, MIYCN individual counselling 871.

project_name: Emergency WASH Support to Crises-Affected IDPs, Vulnerable Host Communities and Returnees in Jonglei, Northern Barh el Ghazal, Eastern Equatoria and Western Equatoria States in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Severe WASH needs have been identified in the locations of Northern Bahr El Ghazel, Jonglei, Eastern and Western Equatoria as a result of multiple displacements, insecurity, economic hardships, food insecurity, malnutrition and disease outbreaks. Despite several efforts to alleviate suffering caused by the aforementioned triggers, challenges in meeting up to acceptable standards have been encountered which span across several thematic areas of WASH, Health, Nutrition, Protection and Food Security. Provision of adequate WASH services is key to achieving sustainable solutions to communities in emergency. 

HUMANITARIAN AID FOR CHANGE AND TRANSFORMATION (HACT) works in the locations of Aweil North, Aweil West, Pibor, Budi, Lafon and Yambio providing an integrated multi – sectoral response to mainly IDPs and vulnerable host communities.  HACT has presence and field offices in Yambio implementing an Access to Justice project, Lafon implementing SSHF WASH project, Aweil implementing a UNICEF Education project and Pibor through support from RRF. 

HACT will provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees, through temporary and sustainable solutions to address the vital needs, public health and protection issues through community approaches. The response aims at mitigating WASH related GBV by providing gender appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities and tackling issues surrounding gender, safety and WASH including provision of dignity, hygiene and non-food item kits. 
As a result of high GAM rates in the areas targeted, WASH integrated interventions starting from SAM/MAM admission at OTP/SC are planned to provide WASH in nutrition for famine prevention minimum package of interventions. 

Since the locations targeted are disease prone, a WASH in health response is planned for outbreak preparedness, response and risk reduction. The project seeks to provide a timely WASH minimum package of interventions on an adhoc basis. This will include setup of WASH  services, training of health workers and other stakeholders as conveyors of appropriate hygiene practices. 

A total of 40,000 people are targeted through this 12 month project, more than 53% of those targeted female in the counties of Aweil North and West, Pibor, Budi, Lafon and Yambio. 38% of the beneficiairies are IDPs, 60% vulnerable host communities, 2% of these returnees.

project_name: Provision of shelter and non-food items to conflict affected persons in Jonglei, Central Equatoria and Lakes in South Sudan
project_objective:
With the signing of the revitalized peace agreement in September 2018 and the celebration of Peace in the capital of South Sudan in October 2018, many South Sudanese are hopeful that this peace will hold and several others who have been displaced by the conflict are expected to return. However it was acknowledged by the president that there will still be pockets of individuals/groups who may continue armed conflict of whom the government reported, will reach out to include in the peace implementation. These groups may cause more displacements in those areas.

Though calm is expected to return to most parts of South Sudan, the devastating effects of the 5 year conflict will still linger. Homes, property and livelihoods destroyed, lives lost, people displaced. The impact of the conflict has resulted in country-wide economic and humanitarian crisis which has exacerbated living conditions of those most affected. There is prevalence of deaths due to hunger and curable/preventable diseases, increased crimes and insecurity (looting, stealing, robbing, road ambushes), cattle stealing and raiding has become more frequent because of increased poverty resulting in deaths and displacements. Protection risks and negative copying mechanisms are rising; prostitution and survival sex, early girl-child marriages, bride price increment that results into increased promiscuity among girls and young men, exposure to STDs and sexual and gender-based violence, exploitation and abuse. 

South Sudan IPC Analysis released September 2018 puts areas Jonglei and Lakes at crisis or emergency level (Phase 3-4) just one level below famine with prediction that it will get worse especially in Pibor, Twic East and Awerial between January and March 2019. Whenever there is high food insecurity as predicted by IPC, in order to survive, conflicted affect persons will sell their belongings to cope with food shortage. People selling their belonging have been seen in these areas thus greatly increasing shelter and NFI needs.
 
HDC plans to action S/NFI Cluster strategies and objectives (improve access to safe, appropriate emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to newly displaced or vulnerable populations in secondary displacement, improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable IDPs in protracted displacement, returnees and host communities unable to meet their S/NFI needs and support most vulnerable returnees, host communities and IDPs in secondary displacement rebuild lives through coordinated, integrated and targeted shelter and NFIs solutions.) by; providing access to emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to most vulnerable persons in the newly and secondary internally displaced populations in Pibor and Uror; upgrade shelters and replenish essential NFIs and emergency shelters for Protracted IDPs, returnees, HC and people in secondary displacement in Awerial, Bor, Twic East, Duk and Juba; monitor quality of service provided and mainstream protection (especially GBV), HLP and conflict sensitivity approaches in all stages of response.

These objectives can be achieved since HDC is a well established National NGO static in 8 out of 10 former states with current and previous S/NFI projects in Pibor, Bor, Duk and Uror and livelihood and/or protection projects in those other target locations for HDC in 2019. HDC is currently a sub-national co-coordinator for Protection Cluster in Jonglei and focal point for S/NFI Cluster in Awerial – Minkaman. Coordination is key in any response especially in S/NFI and HDC values this and continues to seek for ways and opportunities to improve.
Over the years we have worked well with various international and national NGOs like INTERSOS, NRC, PAH, NCA, SSRC, Concern Worldwide, World Concern, Medair, ADA, TOCH in S/NFI interventions and are now well acquainted with cluster strategies and methodologies of response. As outcome of this, we have been part of the tasks teams to review cluster tools to incorporate protection and AAP aspects a thing that has subsequently built on and strengthened our capacity to deliver S/NFI projects.
HDC’s wide coverage and strong staff helps cushion certain risks – financial, human resource, logistics, etc that can easily derail normal functioning of an organisation to effectively and efficiently deliver to the communities they serve.

In Uror, HDC is exploring an initiative to build on unity and peaceful co-existence by working with its fellow NNGOs. Our believe is that when these conflict affected communities see national staffs working together despite their different ethnities, it will influence them to embrace unity and build peaceful co-existence.

project_name: Emergency food security livelihood and resilience light support to 12000 Food insecure households in  Gogrial West and Twic Counties in Warrap State
project_objective:
The project is an Emergency Food security support intervention with promotion of resilience light activities. The implementation period is  one year  running from January 2019 to December, 2019 . The key objective of the project The key objective is to increase people’s access to food and availability of food through support to food production. the project is  line with HRP strategic objective 2 ( SO2) and is in support of FSL cluster objective 2 and  FSL cluster objective 4
The main programmatic approach is through direct distribution of inputs, input trade fairs , training  and  working with accountability to affected committee. The activities are in line with the indicative activities under the Food security cluster The activities  falls within the seasonal calendar and within the livelihood zones of warrap state 
The targeted households are mainly vulnerable households in host and IDP areas50,000 vulnerable households will be supported . The main target location is in Gogrial West and Twic Counties in warrapstate which falls mainly in Phase 3 and 4 of the  food security classification phase. Centre to the project implementation is the consideration given to address protection concern and to involve and be accountable to the affected community. The needs of Women, boys and children are focused. these needs will be established in close collaboration with the protection cluster. Another sphere of integration is with the nutrition cluster wherein the caretaker or mothers of malnourished children will be trained and supported with high nutritious  vegetable seeds for production. The project will also participate in joint assessment missions and response with both the nutrition and protection cluster.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Health Service project in Fashoda and Magwi County.
project_objective:
Impact Health Organization (IHO) proposes the Provision of Emergency Health Care Service project to be implemented in Magwi and Fashod County in the year 2019. This project will deliver a package of Integrated Health services activities in an effort to ensure continued access to minimum, and responsive integrated essential healthcare service that meet the needs of the vulnerable populations (IDPs, host community and returnees) in Magwi County, Eastern Equatoria and Fashoda County Upper Nile state by focusing on major causes of morbidity and mortality. 
IHO  conducted a needs assessment in both Fashoda October 2018 and Magwi County June and October 2018, and concluded that the health systems in the two locations were not only challenged with limited access to human resource medicine and other supplies but also limited access to blood transfusion services, obstetric care service, mental health services but also limited access to WASH services but the referral system is hampered by poor roads. The community has limited access to health education, Immunization coverage is still low. The leading causes of morbidity include Malaria, Pneumonia, Watery Diarrhoea among children, HIV/AIDS and Tuberculosis.  The IPC analysis September 2018-March 2019 classified Magwi County malnutrition level in crisis stage IPC 3 classification and the Smart Survey conducted in Magwi County in 2017 reported the GAM rate at 15.2% slightly above WHO emergency threshold of 15%, a serious indication that malnutrition rates might increase in the near future.  
 In this project, IHO will provide lifesaving quality health service to 10000 Individuals (5040 Male and 4960 Female) of 21% whom shall be children under five years and 47% under 15 years of age  part of health cluster target in the Magwi and Fashoda Counties by undertaking 1 mobile team, 1 PHCU and 1 PHCC and for fashoda County.   IHO will work closely with communities to identify the problem affecting them and the community will greatly participate development and implementation of activities and community shall provide feedback on the progress of the interventions. The project will build capacities of the communities through trainings and awareness campaigns designed to halt the spread of communicable disease.  IHO will address unique health needs of women and girls, particularly respond to GBV, including clinical management of rape. Finally, IHO will work closely with WHO, health cluster and MoH in ensuring provision of timely live saving health care services.

The project will build capacities of the communities through trainings and awareness campaigns designed to halt the spread of communicable disease.
