project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency WASH Service in Torit County and Fashoda County.
project_objective:
Impact Health Organization (IHO) proposes the Provision of Integrated Emergency WASH Service project to be implemented in Torit County. The project will deliver a package of integrated WASH services (WASH-NUT, WASH-Protection and WASH Health) to meet the needs of the vulnerable populations (IDPs, host community and returnees) in Torit County, Eastern Equatoria and Fashod County, Upper Nile state. 
Impact Health Organization (IHO) needs assessment conducted in Torit County, and Fashoda in October 2018 howed that Most Households had no access to latrines, drink and use water from the river with limited treatment, limited access to water collection containers and as well as limited hygiene awareness. In both locations WASH infrastructure at the nutrition centers, health centres, schools and at the community-level were limited hence there is a need for an urgent response
The IPC analysis September 2018-March 2019 classified malnutrition level in Torit County at IPC 2 classification (Stressed) for Fashoda IPC 4 emergency Phase and the smart survey conducted in 2018 reported GAM rate for Torit County at 12.2% and Fashoda 16.1%.  This project will integrate health, nutrition and education WASH related interventions into the response. The project will target communities with poor access to safe water supply, unsafe sanitation and hygiene practices, areas with poor sanitation coverage and support health, education and nutrition centers with rehabilitation of WASH facilities. 
In this project, IHO will provide lifesaving quality WASH service to 25000 host community, IDP and returnees in Torit County 49% Male (12250) and 51% female (12750 Female) of which 15% shall be children below 18 years and 75% adults 18-59 years and 10% elderly 59 and above years. In Fashoda County IHO will reach 21312 Individuals (10741 Male and 10571 Female of which 15% shall be children below 18 years and 75% adults 18-59 years and 10% elderly 59 and above years. This Integral package of activities will decrease the prevalence of diseases and malnutrition and increase protection of especially women and girls. In the process of implementation, IHO will work closely with communities to identify the problem affecting them and the community will greatly participate in the development and implementation of activities and provide feedback on the progress of the interventions. The project will build capacities of the communities through trainings and awareness campaigns designed to halt the spread of WASH related disease.  IHO will address unique WASH needs of women and girls, particularly respond to GB. Finally, IHO will work closely with WHO, WASH, health, Nutrition, Protection clusters and relevant government ministries in ensuring provision of timely live saving WASH services.

project_name: Restoration of basic WASH services to ensure equitable and sustainable access to Water and Sanitation in Syria.
project_objective: Sustainable water and sanitation systems are maintained and/or restored to improve public health and sustain livelihoods. The project aims to increase the resilience of the Syrian population by building the resilience of WASH services and the mitigation the further degradation of WASH basic services in the most vulnerable communities.

project_name: Increasing access and strengthening capacities of PHC to provide emergency lifesaving health care services in Juba, Malakal and Wau PoCs locations through the provision of (2 mobile unit in Nyal, 1 PHCU, 3 PHCC (Integrated and/or Outbreak response). Emergency health support for IDPs  and host communities
project_objective:
International Medical Corps (IMC) is a US-registered independent affiliate organization of International Medical Corps UK (IMC UK), with which IMC UK shares the same name and charitable objectives and mission. IMC UK and IMC work together to deliver assistance programs in an accountable and effective manner in pursuit of their commonly-held charitable objectives. IMC UK will engage IMC to implement its Programmes in the field, with IMC UK oversight, according to the terms and conditions of any agreement that results from this proposal and the terms of the parties’ administrative service agreement. IMC maintains a branch office in Croatia, IMC Split that provides administrative and operational support to IMC UK and to the programmes on the ground, including but not limited to financial management, procurement management/international procurements, and logistics.
International Medical Corps proposed response plan will support delivery of integrated primary health care services backed by outreach activities for provision of services to vulnerable segments in hard to reach areas which aims at directly serving IDPs and conflict affected populations with health, , mobile medical teams, mental health and a contingent medical supplies system for emergencies. 
Through the proposed 2019 response plan , IMC will implement Integrated Health Care services, including primary health care, comprehensive reproductive health service, mental health services, EPI  and secondary health care are strengthened and available to vulnerable populations, referral system is reinforced and rape survivors have access to CMR and psychological first aid and that epidemic-prone diseases are detected on time and responded to immediately in Juba PoC, Wau PoC ,Malakal  PoC and  their catchment areas while in Nyal  IMC will provide mobile clinic services. 
The primary objective of the proposed project is to improve access to basic curative and preventive health care services to internally-displaced and resident populations in the post-conflict area.
In the area of intervention International Medical Corps will reach out to 140,441 people, of which 70,782 male and 69,619 female. 29,493Children under 5 years will be reached by the project.

project_name: Integrated lifesaving nutrition assistance to conflict, most affected and vulnerable populations in IDPs and Host Communities in Malakal PoC , Malakal town, Juba PoC  and Nyal Panyijar County in South Sudan.
project_objective:
International Medical Corps aims to provide integrated lifesaving nutrition responses to conflict affected resident and displaced populations in four locations: Juba PoC; Malakal town, Malakal PoC and Nyal Panyijar County. The protracted crisis and continuous critical malnutrition situation in the selected areas requires extended services to meet the current need and prevent the incidence of the cases in future. According to the assessments conducted in the proposed areas, the undernutrition situation is classified as critical with the prevalence of GAM rates 18.5% and 19.6% for Malakal PoC and Panijiyar respectively. The presence of underlining causes of malnutrition inflates the prevalence and deteriorate the nutritional status of the targeted population.
   
IMC will respond to the reduction of mortality, morbidity and impact of poor growth development, by treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among children (boys and girls) aged 0-59 month pregnant and lactating women with acute malnutrition through management of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), at OTP/TSFP nutrition facilities and provision of support to maternal infant young child nutrition (MIYCN) focusing more on the first 1000 days, of a child life and the mother as well through increasing awareness, encouraging adoption of optimal Maternal, Infant and Young Child feeding and hygiene practices among caregivers and household members. Mother support groups will be supported to reach caregivers/mothers. 

IMC with already established Nutrition surveillance team, will undertake nutrition assessments that provide robust information on the nutrition situation of a given population, this information will be key in responding effectively to nutrition needs in the project area, as well the team will work closely with the nutrition cluster Information working group to identify key priority areas with no or limited surveillance information to conduct appropriate assessment. Capacity building of the nutrition team, MoH staff, to equip them to respond to nutrition emergency on timely management of SAM and MAM cases. 

Through the proposed humanitarian response plan, IMC will reach 14,664 children under five for the treatment of SAM and MAM prevalence and 4036 PLW beneficiaries with acute malnutrition by provision of supplementary foods and creating awareness on preventing measures. PLW will form support groups and will support in raising awareness through MIYCN key messages, and sessions on nutrition package. The project will provide lifesaving nutrition services focusing on the most vulnerable, especially PLW and children under five. Similarly, following the CMAM guideline IMC will identify and target the older people (>60 years) for the TSFP program and provide the supplements according to the protocol under WFP FLA. All the elderly vulnerable beneficiaries will be provided by fortified blended food (FBF) also locally known as CSB++.

IMC will engage the affected population to participate fully in the project design and implementation to ensure acceptance, quality services and accountability, through formation of Quality, Accountability of Affected population committees in each site in Juba PoC; Malakal town, Malakal PoC and Nyal Panyijar County. Community consultative sessions will be organized on a quarterly basis by field nutrition managers, site managers and field M&E officers, to receive feedback and draw an action plan on areas to improve program implementation.
IMC has already started the process of 2019 Field level agreement with WFP for TSFP supplies in managing moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) cases and PCA with UNICEF to support severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases covering in Juba PoC; Malakal town, Malakal PoC and Nyal Panyijar County

project_name: Food Security Assistance for IDPs in Borno State
project_objective:
In order to address severe food insecurity experienced in Kukawa and Mobbar LGAs, ACTED is proposing a food security intervention to provision 4,000 households with critical food security and livelihoods assistance. ACTED will implement a flexible approach through the use of cash vouchers and income generating activities with a focus on agriculture in order to provide emergency access to income to ascertain food security for the most vulnerable population groups in Kukawa and Mobbar LGAs, with specific emphasis on providing food assistance to women-headed households in hard to reach areas by pushing out from LGA capitals, contingent on the evolving security context in these LGAs. 

Assistance will be provided to IDPs and host communities in order to relieve pressure that large-scale displacement has placed on local food resources. Program activities will specifically focus on targeting women-headed households, and child-headed households, and will work in collaboration with REACH to utilise conclusions drawn from the Hard To Reach Assessments conducted in Kukawa and Mobbar LGAs to identify new areas of intervention, as well as liaise closely with protection partners to receive referrals for program enrolment of beneficiaries. 

ACTED will work to identify local vendors Cash vouchers will be facilitated through the use of the red rose platform, and through identification of local vendors able to partake in the program. Additionally, ACTED will implement an IGA component by provisioning one-off agriculture inputs in the rainy season, specifically targeting women-headed households with access to land, in order to build resilience of displaced and conflict-affected communities. Protection mainstreaming is a core component of program design, with specific emphasis on inclusion of vulnerable population groups as primary target beneficiaries, and as such fifteen percent of the overall budget will be dedicated to delivery of protection mainstreaming integrated activities.

Key protection principles that underpin humanitarian interventions have informed the design of the project, and will be actively present as a core component of implementation. ACTED will ensure that activities conducted prioritize the wellbeing, safety and dignity of beneficiaries at all times. Activities will avoid incurring any harm, will ensure meaningful access to food security assistance, and will collaborate with stakeholders to identify the most vulnerable beneficiaries for enrolment.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and NFI assistance to IDPs in Borno State
project_objective:
ACTED is proposing a nine-month intervention that supports women, girls, boys, and men meet their basic shelter and NFI needs; therefore, promoting improved resilience and urgent assistance in areas facing limited livelihood opportunities and suffering from public and private infrastructure destruction. This intervention will target Jere, Monguno, and Kukawa LGAs. 

The proposed project suggests to procure 1,500 emergency shelters and 1,500 NFI kits for distribution to new arrivals in target areas, which expect to receive a new influx of displaced families due to the ongoing military offensives. 800 ESKs and 800 NFIs will be procured, prepositioned, and distributed by ACTED’s Shelter Team to new arrivals; while 700 ESKs and 700 NFI Kits will be prepositioned between Maiduguri and Monguno Logistics Sector Warehouses to contribute to the Shelter/NFI Sector pipeline. The prepositioned humanitarian items will be available for Sector partners for distribution, enabling rapid response to new onset of needs. 

Both items are expected to be provided to new arrivals based on needs and vulnerability criteria, specifically targeting newly arrived families that have been unable to receive assistance from any other implementing partner, women- and child-headed households, the elders, persons with disabilities, etc. The intervention will target 15,000 individuals (assuming five members per household). Through the response, ACTED expects to promote the safety and dignity of families affected by the conflict.

project_name: Common Transport Services for Humanitarian Partners in South Sudan
project_objective:
The Common Transport Services (CTS) is a free-for-user service that transports key humanitarian supplies on behalf of humanitarian actors. CTS serves as a critical link in the supply chain, enabling products and materials that arrive from regional and international suppliers to rapidly move onwards to partners located deep in the field. IOM CTS has significantly progressed from a baseline of 2,000 metric tons (MTs) of humanitarian cargo delivered in 2011, to around a total of 19,827 metric tonnes transported in 2017 with forecast of reaching 20,000 MT during 2018. IOM works with more than 80 unique agencies in key operational locations in Jonglei, Unity and Greater Upper Nile Region and Humanitarian Logistics Hubs (Malakal, Melut, Bentiu) and Rumbek, Bor, Juba and Wau. IOM will maintain heavy vehicles and transport cargo from the main ports of dispatch via air, road and river and will continue warehouse management in key operational locations. 

Through the effective management of the CTS IOM aims to support organizations preparedness measures to mitigate risk associated with increased insecurity, looting/theft of humanitarian supplies, critical access impediments to very vulnerable people and reduce expensive air and road transport costs and ultimately support the timely response to the needs of the affected populations.

project_name: Integrated Food Security and Livelihoods Protection Project
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to enhance protection, recovery and resumption of agricultural and livelihoods activities of the most vulnerable and food insecure (classified as IPC 3 and 4) households in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG) State of South Sudan.  

The IRC will provide immediate and short term livelihood protection support in the beginning of 2019 lean season to the most severely food insecure and vulnerable households in NBeG. To enhance recovery and resilience, interventions will include mainstream support to at-risk households focused on improving crop, livestock and fisheries production and bolstering resilience towards recurrent shocks. Cash based activities will be used to build household and community productive assets while promoting job and income opportunities for vulnerable households.  

This objective will be achieved through the following main activities:
(a)	Community and local leaders engagement and consultation to prioritize needs and identify most vulnerable households  
(b)	Distribution of agricultural inputs (seeds and tools) in the form of kits and through seed fairs to farmers. In kind inputs to be accessed through the Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO). Input trade fairs will also be utilized to enhance  restocking of livestock assets – mainly small ruminants (sheep and goats) and backyard poultry targeting most vulnerable households including female headed households, widows and widowers, the elderly and households with malnourished mothers and children ;  
(c)	Conditional cash transfers for asset development (public works) will be distributed to develop community viable assets as well as provide job and income opportunities for households in IPC phase 3 and 4 food insecurity situations. IRC will engage the community to prioritize economically viable assets for rehabilitation and or establishment through conditional cash transfer activities. Cash vouchers will be provided to households who have completed tasks during assets establishment and they will use vouchers to access prioritized services including food and seeds during seed fairs.
(d)	Training of extension agents (CAHWs, AEA), crop growers, pastoralists and fisher folks on sustainable production skills and provision of extension services around the package of production inputs and post-harvest handling technologies supported by the project. Furthermore, the project will promote value addition and marketing through improved post-harvest handling, food storage techniques and facilities at household and community level – including household granaries, fish processing, food storage bins and local market structures to be established through cash based interventions. 
(e)	The Project will promote resilience building through inclusive livelihoods diversification by providing support to women-led VSLAs, income-generating activities, business and life skills trainings and start-up capital provision to youth out of school. 

During planning and implementation of project activities, IRC will mainstream gender equity and promote gender inclusiveness, allowing for the most vulnerable and disadvantaged women and girls to access and participate in project activities for household benefits. Participatory monitoring and evaluation of the project will be enhanced through community and local leaders’ consultation at project launch, participatory beneficiary identification and selection (PBIS) including agreeing on affirmative action to register at least 60% female beneficiaries under the project. IRC and the community will set up a project feedback and complaint mechanism consisting of an inclusive feedback and complaint committee (equal men and women representatives) to promote equal opportunities for beneficiaries to voice their interests and feedback. In promotion of complementary programming with other projects and partners, IRC will exercise robust coordination with nutrition, protection and health projects including providing support to referred vulnerable persons affected by chronic food insecurity and malnutrition. 

Through this intervention, IRC will support a total of 12,000 (6,000 Women, 3,820 Men, 1,200 Girls, 980 Boys) beneficiaries.  By program type: 12,000 through input trade fairs, 2,200 through communal works and cash vouchers, 600 through farmer field schools, 1,000 restocking and pastoral field school, 270 through seed groups , 60 through fisheries support and 2,180 through livelihoods diversification and restoration.

project_name: GBV prevention and response through life-saving services for women and girls affected by conflict in Koch, Ganyiel, and Nyal, Unity State
project_objective:
The project will provide lifesaving GBV services and prevention of GBV in Nyal, Koch, and Ganyiel targeting 47, 107 (30, 255F, 16,852M) IDPs and host community. In Nyal and Ganyiel, the proposed project will target 38, 225 (16,288 women and 13,937 male) members of the crisis affected population. IRC will promote access to lifesaving services through comprehensive case management, referrals, and individual and group psychosocial support services in women and girls’ friendly spaces (WGFS). IRC will utilize two existing women and girls’ friendly spaces in Nyal and establish three women and girls friendly spaces in Ganyiel for the provision of psychosocial support services, skills building activities, recreational and life skills activities for adolescent girls, group information sessions, and provision of social cohesion and support networks for women and girls. To promote resilience and enhance psycho-social support, women will be consulted and supported with, unconditional cash assistance to improve access to food and basic needs including hygiene and sanitary items and reduce vulnerability for female and child headed households, elderly, women with disability and those that who are chronically ill. The cash will enhance household purchasing power and economic capacities of beneficiaries to access food commodities of their choice and basic needs from the local market. Discussions will be held on power dynamics to mitigate risk factors that may come with cash based support to women for petty business.  

In Koch County, Unity State, the proposed project will support 8,882 (5,967 female and 2,915 male) direct conflict affected beneficiaries through the provision of case management and psychosocial support services in an adequate and timely manner through the daily operation of the women and girls’ friendly spaces and through mobile services to Ngony, Patit and Bieh. IRC’s trained GBV Response Officers and Caseworkers will be based in the women and girls’ friendly spaces located in Pachol, Koat, Bargok and Mirmir as well as in Buaw with regular travel to support mobile outreach services in Ngony, Patit and Bieh, and link up with the health partners and other service providers for provision of clinical management of rape services. The IRC will work to mitigate and respond to the needs of women, girls, men and boys affected by conflict by reducing GBV risks through frequent joint community-based safety audit assessments, address risks identified, and strengthen community based support mechanisms, creation of safe and meaningful access to relevant services, and advocacy with other humanitarian actors on GBV mainstreaming. The IRC will also provide material support such as dignity kits and survival kits to the most vulnerable women and girls in Koch and Nyal. 
Within the women and girls’ safe spaces, specialized, age-appropriate, group-based support is available to women and girls who fear to come forward to access available GBV services. Women will also be supported with cash for petty business to promote resilience and psychosocial support.

To mitigate barriers such as fear, stigma, and a lack of information on health consequences of sexual violence, which prevent GBV survivors from seeking help, the IRC will implement both basic and more tailored psychosocial support interventions including GBV information sessions, as well as specialized group psychosocial support sessions with a focus on supporting survivors’ healing process from traumatic events. These structured sessions are designed to provide emotional support to survivors, and equip women and girls with improved coping mechanisms, self-esteem, resilience and social support networks. The IRC will also provide tailored psychosocial support activities for adolescent girls to mitigate their vulnerability to multiple forms of GBV, and offer support systems and access to information. This will be pivotal in reducing women and girls’ isolation, and boosting their self-confidence.

project_name: WOS: Improve equitable access to integrated lifesaving, preventive and curative nutrition services for under-5 girls and boys, and pregnant and lactating women in Syria.
project_objective: Under the overall framework of support to nutrition services, this project aims to provide nutrition services for children and pregnant lactating women in the high-risk areas and IDP camps inside Syria through fixed and medical mobile teams run by local NGOs, Implementing Partners (IPs) and government health directorates, and provide them with the essential lifesaving nutrition supplies to treat and prevent malnutrition and prevent deaths among vulnerable children. It will also focus on raising awareness among vulnerable mothers and care-givers on prevention of malnutrition, breast feeding and Infant Young Child Feeding. The project will also provide capacity building for health staff and community volunteers to ensure quality service and compensate for the heavy loss of health workers during the 8 years of the conflict.

project_name: Strengthening community engagement using an integrated approach in South Sudan
project_objective:
A core component of Camp Management roles and responsibilities is to engage with displaced populations to: 
a)	ensure access to assistance, protection and services in camps and camp-like settings. 
b)	Inform, consult, mobilize and support community structures in a location, such as camp leadership or women’s groups, to address barriers to participation, particularly for underrepresented groups, so they can participate in camp activities and decision-making processes at every stage of the camp lifecycle. 

However, throughout 2018 there has been a rise in the occurrences of protests in camps – sometimes exacerbated by miscommunication with humanitarian responders.  At the same time an overreliance on camp leadership for engagement does not consider their actual representative value.

Instead for effective implementation of project to take place we need to develop a comprehensive understanding and engagement of: 
•	Relations between leadership and community 
•	Existing/organic and imposed/inorganic leadership structures 
•	Who the local social influencers or decision makers are 
•	The Information flows within and between settlements
It is widely recognised that it is vital for recipients of humanitarian assistance to feel that they have a voice and agency in determining the assistance that is needed. In addition, it is also recognized that with strong community engagement strategies, recipients of humanitarian assistance can provide relevant and timely feedback to improve the humanitarian response. However, it is also highly likely that protest instigated by a minority of the population can hinder an effective humanitarian response and that a feasible mitigation strategy is to effectively and efficiently engage the community-at-large in conversation and feedback about their felt needs.

Therefore, to overcome disputes and engagement challenges that are sure to arise in the humanitarian context in South Sudan, this proposal presents a comprehensive package of innovative Community Communications and Engagement (CCE) activities, led by the development of both a physical and virtual (radio-led) town hall meeting system involving host and IDP communities with humanitarian agency representatives. This will ensure a coordinated engagement strategy with all parties, that provides full accountability to all affected populations and mitigates risk of conflict between the two groups. 

This project will build upon Internews’ expertise in CCE and Communication with Communities (CwC), particularly the pre-existing networks of listening groups, focus groups and broadcasting systems (both BBTT and radio), in addition to, a systematic and formalized town hall meeting system. This will be implemented in Malakal, Juba, Wau and Bentiu and their surrounding collective sites, and once implemented they  will provide clear avenues for all  humanitarians in these locations to further engage and communicate with the communities they serve.

project_name: CHILD PROTECTION - WOS - Strengthening child protection services and responses including risk education and GBV for girls and boys most at risk of violence, exploitation and abuse
project_objective:
Preventing &responding to child protection(CP) is lifesaving and continues to be an essential component of the humanitarian response in Syria.As the largest CP agency in Syria, UNICEF has technical&operational capacity, global expertise &responsibilities to lead on the delivery of quality, innovative&scalable programming efforts.UNICEF’s CP programming is critical not only as a standalone intervention, but also as an essential part of UNICEF’s health,education,nutrition,WASH,Adolescent Development &Participation &other programming efforts.
This project aims to contribute to the reinforcement of CP systems by expanding the availability &quality CP services for girls&boys in targeted locations.In line with the strategic priorities of the 2019 CPAoR Humanitarian Response Plan(HRP)&the No Lost Generation initiative, UNICEF will focus on 3intervention areas:1)improving the quality of community-based CP interventions;2)expanding the reach &improving the quality of specialized CP services for children most at-risk &survivors of violence, exploitation&abuse; and3)strengthening the CP workforce.Advocacy&evidence generation will underpin these intervention areas as a strategy to achieve results for children.
CP:UNICEF&partners will continue to support community-based CP interventions such awareness raising on critical CP risks,including risk education.Parenting programmes,structured &sustained PSS interventions will be scaled up to reduce vulnerabilities of children&strengthen individual resilience,as well as support the identification of children in need of additional support.UNICEF will build on the investment of previous years in case management systems to expand access to specialized services, including FTR,for children in need &children living with disabilities.Centre-based,mobile teams & CP networks will serve as delivery mechanisms for reaching girls&boys.Additional focus will be directed to multi-sectorial collaboration to jointly address CP concerns, as well to build the CP workforce. 
GBV:Contribute to expanding the mainstreaming of GBV responses in other thematic areas &the response through case management&referrals for women,girls&boys in targeted locations.UNICEF’s GBV programming is critical not only as a standalone intervention,but also as mainstreaming into other essential part of UNICEF’s response including CP,health,education&other programming efforts.In line with the GBVAoR HRP results framework,UNICEF will adopt a holistic approach to: i) assist &support survivors to address the consequences of GBV through case management &referrals; ii) mitigate the risks of GBV &build safer environments for women,girls &boys and; iii) implement preventive measures to tackle the underlying causes of GBV.A core package of interventions will build a minimum response within UNICEF’s existing CP interventions, &serve as a strategic entry point to promote further GBV-specific programming.PSEA,as a core corporate responsibility, to reduce the risk of sexual exploitation&abuse of people of concern; therefore, UNICEF will work on building the capacity of partners&humanitarian actors to address&prevent SEA. 
Risk education:is lifesaving&continues to be an essential component of the humanitarian response in Syria.UNICEF’s RE programming is critical not only as a standalone intervention but also as mainstreaming into UNICEF’s&programming efforts.Project aims to contribute to expanding the availability&quality of RE for girls,boys,women&men in targeted locations.In line with the Mine Action AoR HRP results framework,UNICEF will provide RE through,humanitarian risk education actors &public service providers, including education,health,religious leaders&Media personnel.UNICEF will strengthen the capacity of risk education providers&members of the RE working group,created in 2018 &chaired by UNICEF,with the participation of UNMAS,NGOs,INGOs&governmental partners;as an overarching platform of coordination on RE in Syria for all active members in RE

project_name: Distribution of emergency shelter and Non-Food Items for populations in need of assistance and protection in South Sudan.
project_objective:
INTERSOS will provide lifesaving shelter and NFIs in response to specific needs of 40,000 IDPs and conflict affected populations assessed and verified to be in need. Deep field locations with recent displacements having populations in dire need will be the priority of INTERSOS in the distribution of life saving ES/NFI commodities. IDPs, returnees and conflict affected populations assessed and verified as most in need will be targeted in the counties of Nyirol, Pibor and Uror (Jonglei state), Tambura, Ezo, and Nzara, (Western Equatoria State), Leer, Koch, (Unity State) with mobile front line services. 
INTERSOS will provide support to 10000 beneficiaries (protracted IDPs, vulnerable HC and returnees) in the counties of Bor South and Magwi through static response and CTP interventions. INTERSOS has gained significant experience in CTP interventions in South Sudan, piloting and implementing CTP programs in Torit, Magwi and Kapoeta South where a combined 1400 Households and more than 8,600 individuals have been served, and is currently implementing CTP activities through voucher and unconditional cash transfer in Magwi and Torit counties for a total of 1965 HHs. 

INTERSOS will consider the specific needs, concerns and priorities of women and girls, men and boys of different age and with specific needs such as people with disability, pregnant and lactating women and other vulnerabilities so incorporating protection principles during project implementation. 

As a short-term intervention, the impact on the population and the contextual dynamics is sensitive and delicate balances are at play, for this reason the team will ensure that all accountability processes to the affected population are carefully followed. The intervention must be clearly defined and protection concerns taken into consideration so that distribution respects community dynamics, does no harm and is done in a dignified meaningful way. Contextual feedback mechanisms will be established in line with the distribution method and the location dynamics. Beneficiaries will be identified using approved South Sudan SNFIs cluster criteria of selection. In addition, INTERSOS will endeavor to give priority to child headed household, women, persons with disability, the elderly and other vulnerable people in the community who will benefit from Emergency Shelter and NFI distribution. Currently, the counties of Nyirol, Pibor, Uror, Leer, Koch, Tambura, Ezo, Nzaraa and Bor South need emergency shelter and NFIs assistance due to dire needs, where their fulfilment is crucial in saving lives; Magwi and Bor south are also in need of Emergency Shelter and NFIs assistance here the proposed project intends to deliver this assistance through CTP. 
In Bor south INTERSOS will work closely with Protection and GBV partners.

This CTP intervention will enable most vulnerable groups such as unaccompanied elders, persons with disabilities, pregnant and lactating women and child headed families to receive Shelter/NFIs support as per their needs to restore their dignity and improve living standards. Project team will also comprise of Cash Transfer officer who will lead implementation and monitoring of cash Transfer programming activities in the proposed locations. INTERSOS proposes to use a mix of vouchers and unconditional cash transfer in order to meet the varying needs of the beneficiaries.

INTERSOS' CBI officer will be responsible for CTP interventions in Magwi and Bor South. and he may conduct, in coordination with the Cash Working Group and other partners market assessment in other location to explore the feasibility of CTP S/NFIs interventions.

project_name: Preventing and Responding to GBV in Jonglei and Unity States
project_objective:
Prevailing social norms, gender roles, national conflict, a highly militarized environment, and the frequent cattle raiding and revenge killings among the different clans and tribes exacerbate the risk of GBV in South Sudan. Protection concerns such as generalized violence and insecurity, access to food, water and firewood, expose women to a high risk of GBV. There is, therefore, an urgent need to enhance GBV prevention efforts with additional strategies to mitigate risks, such as fuel strategies and protective accompaniments. Furthermore, lack of recognition of GBV as violation of fundamental human rights continues a culture of impunity throughout the country. Therefore, nowtihstanding the advancing of the peace process, it is important to continue to raise awareness, reduce prevalent stigmas in the communities and increase identification and documentation of GBV cases as well as providing survivors access to psychosocial support and other services for their recovery and healing. INTERSOS GBV interventions therefore aim to strengthen prevention and response to GBV. INTERSOS will provide women and girls a safe and confidential environment in Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) where they will access psychosocial support services in form of peer-to-peer support, individual case management and recreational activities. All activities will focus on overcoming trauma and psychosocial distress by strengthening their individual coping mechanism, resilience and social network. Cases will be identified through the Protection Monitoring Officers, community based protection networks and Community Mobilizers and will be referred to trained and skilled GBV Caseworkers. Furthermore, INTERSOS will continue to support the economic empowerment of women through income generating activities that support their livelihood. A selected group of women that is interested in starting their own business will attend regular business skills training and be assisted in developing a business plan.

In order to confront social norms that drive GBV, INTERSOS will specifically focus on engaging men through its programming to become change agents for shifting gender roles. The discussion around gender and social norms will be facilitated in regular workshops, including influential community leaders to reflect on masculinity and the reasons behind their violence towards women, gender, sexuality, and substance abuse. In addition, INTERSOS will conduct awareness campaigns addressing specific problems affecting girls such as early and forced marriage and the low inclusion of girls in school. There will be specific awareness campaigns in primary and secondary schools for the promotion of girls’ enrolment and to reduce the drop out from schools. 

INTERSOS has played an important role in strengthening coordination among humanitarian actors present in in its areas. INTERSOS in Bor will lead the GBV Sub Cluster and is strengthening coordination with the GBV Working Group in Akobo, as well as coordinating with the Protection Working Group in Lankien, which is led by INTERSOS. In 2019, INTERSOS will also take over leadership of the GBV subcluster in Jonglei State. The coordination is deemed fundamental to elaborate a common strategy for the GBV sector, including partners’ joint activities and to prevent duplication or overlapping. INTERSOS GBV interventions will be aligned with the GBV Sub-cluster Strategy. To effectively respond to GBV, INTERSOS will collaborate with strategic partners to contribute to the provision of the basic package of multi-sectoral GBV services at community level and build capacity of service providers and communities to deliver quality GBV services in line with best practices and minimum standards for humanitarian settings. INTERSOS will strengthen GBV prevention and risk mitigation across its interventions through mainstreaming GBV in Education, WASH and Health sectors.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving child protection services to vulnerable, conflict-affected children in Jonglei and Unity State
project_objective:
Due to dire needs identified throughout its previous Child Protection and Education activities implemented in 2018, and in line with the desire to implement life-saving activities, enhance protection and strengthen coping capacities with an eye to support the latter, this proposal aims to work in hard-to-reach areas where INTERSOS has identified compounded risks and observed the impact of protracted periods of under-servicing, denoting the priority of this intervention. More specifically, INTERSOS proposes a response that is static in 5 locations: 3 locations in Ayod (Jiech, Mogok, Karmoun), Mayom (Mayom) and Leer (Mayendit) with regular field-based roving activities to other hard-to-reach areas. 

INTERSOS aims to provide child protection to vulnerable, conflict-affected children through a holistic approach consisting of various activities which strengthen each other. The primary activity proposed intends to directly address life-saving needs of children through structured and comprehensive case management, coupled with PSS provision (including PFA) and FTR services for girls and boys with protection needs (UASC, CAAFAG and GBV survivors), orphans and children with other specific needs identified including children with disability. As an additional channel for the identification of protection needs as well as a space to provide PSS activities, malnutrition screenings and referrals for children, a CFS with daily activities in each location has proven to be successful. The intervention will also be characterized by a focus on community engagement activities, awareness-raising and risk mitigation achieved through a strong system of ToT whereby INTERSOS will provide training and engage community members in specific techniques for contextualized approaches to strengthen the protective environment for children. INTERSOS will also strengthen caregivers’ coping mechanisms and resilience through thematic workshops as per the needs identified in each micro-community, this is vital to maintain since children directly suffer as a consequence of distress experienced by their parents. Customary negative discipline measures can contribute to further enhancing the sense of insecurity already perceived due to the tension in the surrounded context. To ensure the protection of children throughout the referral pathway, INTERSOS also aims to provide support and training to non-CP actors in the areas of intervention

As a holistic protection intervention, the project will directly support 6,450 (1,950 adults and 4,500 children) in Ayod County, 2,150 (650 adults and 1,500 children) in Mayendit and 2,150 (650 adults and 1,500 children) in Mayom, and approximately 5,000 indirect beneficiaries in each location. While approximately 70% of the direct beneficiaries are part of the IDP community, an estimated 30% of the host community can be considered as directly targeted too. The objective of this intervention is to provide at least 1,000 children with comprehensive case management support (CP and GBV). As stated before, the past has shown that the CFS is an important part of the integrated approach of this project. Therefore, INTERSOS child protection interventions aim to reach at least 7,500 children through CBCPSS activities, through accesses to a total of 5 CFS and others. Other direct beneficiaries include all the community members targeted in relation to extending child protection by training adult caregivers and other community members on child protection, child rights, parenting skills and positive discipline methods.  More specifically, numbers estimated for direct intervention include 250 adults through the participation in workshops and regular meetings, as part of the CBCPNs, 100 foster caregivers targeted to attend specific training on parenting skills and positive discipline methods. Furthermore, awareness raising activities seek to target at least 5,000 individuals across the population at large between host and hosted community.

project_name: Equitable Basic healthcare Services to Conflict Affected People in Baggari and Bazia- Wau, South Sudan
project_objective:
South Sudan health indicators are among the worst in the world, high disease burden and < 5 Mortality at 93/1000 live births and maternal mortality ratio is at 789/100,000 births, a young girl in South Sudan is three times more likely to die in childbirth than to finish primary school (according to South Sudan national human development index 2016). Following the renewed conflict in 2016 and the resultant economic downward spiral, violent behaviour towards civilians, particularly against the women and children increased, with most of the population been affected and the gender implications has been dire. Roles have changed due to absence of men; women and children have taken up the role of breadwinner in the family by moving in search of food, firewood, and petty jobs, these somehow has exposed them to exploitation and sexual violence. Additionally, school attendance has been affected as most children are forced out of school to support their parents and HMIS includes girls engaging in transactional sex that exposes them to negative reproductive health consequences.
Together, the level of humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains precarious as communities are still continuously being forced out of their respective areas due to active conflict between the warring factions. In June 2018, thousands were forced to flee their homes after fighting broke in different locations in greater Baggari-Wau County, mainly women, children and elderly . During the fighting the existing functional health facilities supported by partners including Islamic Relief in (Wadalel, Ngodakala, Ngoku, Ngisa and Mboro) were either vandalized and/or properties and supplies looted. For the last 5 years active conflict in Wau resulted into health facilities destruction, attacks on civilians, and few functional health facilities face challenges of delivering the complete basic package of health-care services because of pipeline breakage of drug supplies and shortages of skilled health personnel. It has been challenging for humanitarian organizations to access the areas because of denial or uncertain security situation in greater Baggari in to provide services, however the need to provide basic health services is high to the population including children <5 who are susceptible to Vaccine preventable diseases (VPD), malaria endemicity, acute malnutrition, war related injuries, and disease outbreaks risk within the county.
On that backdrop, Islamic Relief South Sudan (IRSS) intends to continue to provide lifesaving humanitarian health assistance to approximately 12,855 (50.4% Male and 49.6% Female) individuals, with focus on women, children and elderly as the most vulnerable population in Wau (Baggari and Bazia). The interventions will respond to the immediate needs and contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality in the conflict affected host communities and IDPs in greater Baggari and Bazia of Wau County, Western Bhar El Gazhal. 
Guided by MOH and WHO relevant health guidelines with presence of technical capacity; through qualified health team, Islamic Relief South Sudan will implement the project at which very person will be entitled to the highest attainable level of medical services regardless of age, gender, religion and social diversity.
The Purpose of Interventions is life saving and contribution to reduction to mortality and morbidity in the area of operations through;
1. Implementing essential primary healthcare emergency clinical packages targeting the most vulnerable displaced population in Baggari and Bazia (Wau)
2. Immunize the most vulnerable displaced groups (Children U5, PLW)
3. Implement outbreak investigation and response.
4. Procurement of emergency health pipeline
5. Mainstream Accountability to Affected People.

project_name: Integrated response to life threatening malnutrition for Conflict affected populations in Duk County, Jonglei state, South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of the project is to save lives and alleviate suffering through safe access to services and resources with dignity by targeting delivering quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition to children of 0-59 months of age with SAM and MAM respectively including PLW with MAM in Duk County.
The county underwent through spreading conflict coupled with increase in severe food insecure households, high prevalence of morbidity and outbreak AWD related diseases; deterioration of economy and inflation that has contributed to worsening of nutrition situation in both IDPS and host communities in Duk County. This situation has resulted into GAM at 25.3 %, MAM at 23.4% and SAM at 6 % which are above the WHO threshold for emergency intervention (ACF SS report 2018).
Therefore, treatment of SAM for children below five years and MAM for children below five years as well as PLW continues to be one of key need for saving lives of most at risk in Duk County.  
The target groups for this project will be 22,830(Boys= 11,643 & Girls=11,187) children of 6-59 month of age and 3,997 PLW in Duk County.
This project intends to reach the target numbers of 1,583(M=798, F=785) SAM and 14,828(M=7,600, F=7,228) MAM cases for children of 6-59 month of age respectively as well as 3,997 MAM cases for PLW. 
The proposed project objectives will be 1) To deliver timely   quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk, reaching at least 85% of SAM and 76% of MAM in girls and boys 6 59 months; 62% of PLW and 60% of elderly in need in Duk County; 2) To increased access to Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition  programs preventing under nutrition among the most vulnerable and at risk, reaching at least 88% of PLW in need in Duk County; 3)To increased access to integrated Nutrition, Health, WASH and FSL activities in Duk County with critical levels of global acute malnutrition (GAM 25.3%).
The proposed activities will be: Treatment of SAM and MAM among under-five children (Target SAM 1,583(M=798, F=785) and (Target MAM 14,828(M=7600, F=7228)); Treatment of MAM among PLW (Target PLW MAM 14,828(M=7600, F=7228)); Training community health workers on creating and facilitating MIYCN education, information sessions, and mother support groups (Target 40 M=20 & F=20); Train health and nutrition care providers on management of acute malnutrition (Target 40 M=20 & F=20); Screening/testing and treatment of malaria and other illness (URTI, UTI) in OTPs among children with Severe acute malnutrition (Target 14,828(M=7600, F=7228); Treatment of children with vitamin A deficiency and infested with worms and participate NIDs (Target 23,000 M=11,600, F= 11,400); Provide WASH -NFIs supplies (soap, jerry cans) to the nutrition sites ( Target 1,583(M=798, F=785)); Establish kitchen garden at nutrition sites for demonstration (Target 7 sites); Linking with targeted distribution for livelihoods and GFD responses for malnourished children based on criteria for targeting including CMAM exits; Establish a community complains and feedback mechanism in the nutrition facilities by placing a suggestion boxes in the 7 OTP/TSFP sites; Raise awareness and provide information to beneficiaries on their rights and entitlement in the 7 OTP/TSFP sites

project_name: Shelter and NFI assistance for IDPs in Greater Equatoria.
project_objective:
This project will respond to the need of the most vulnerable 40,000 individuals (9,600 men, 14,400 women, 6,400 boys and 9,600 girls) in Greater Equatoria, targeting with static response Mundri E/W and Tambura counties (WES) and with mobile response Lainya (CES) and Magwi county (EES). The project targets the most vulnerable IDPs (60%), returnees (30%), and host population (10%), particularly focusing on people with protection concerns and acute needs.
LCED will contribute to save lives by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys (SO1) and protect vulnerable women, men, girls and boys through provision of specialized and integrated services (SO2). This will be done through in-kind distributions of S/NFIs, including replacement of S/NFIs which have outlived their life span, to the most vulnerable households, including pregnant and lactating women (PLW), elderly and disabled persons, and children under 5. In some remote areas shelter framing material is available but not accessible to the beneficiaries (women, elderly), who experience protection concerns on the road, including harassment and looting, and it is not possible to implement a CBI due to lack of functioning markets. In such areas LCED will procure shelter framing material locally for estimated 15% of beneficiaries. Local material is preferred to pipeline items due to higher quality and lower cost of local supplies and transportation, and the possibility of revitalizing the local market.
LCED will continue and strengthen collaboration with other S/NFI, WASH and Protection cluster partners. As SiFP for Greater Mundri for the S/NFI cluster and DFC focal point for UNOCHA, LCED will engage new S/NFI partners with static presence in the area, offering capacity building and conducting joint interventions in order to improve the S/NFI response in the area. At the same time, LCED will strengthen the collaboration with SFPs in CES, WES and EES, in order to improve humanitarian coordination and avoid duplications in Tambura, Lainya and Magwi counties. Since 2014, LCED collaborated with WVI, Medair, IOM and Titi Foundation for static and mobile response in Mundri E/W, Mvolo, Tambura (WES), and Lainya, Wonduruba and Kajo-Keji (CES). As former member of the SAG, LCED is well positioned to lead humanitarian interventions applying the cluster methodology. 
Additionally, LCED will continue incorporating protection in its activities, involving partners such as NP, through community sensitization on GBV, incorporation of risk mitigation measures, and referrals. LCED will also participate in multi-cluster needs assessments, leading them in Greater Mundri, and refer needs and gaps to the ICWG for mobilization of specific clusters. Finally, LCED plans to integrate the S/NFI activities with FSL and WASH, as member of these three clusters. Distribution of S/NFI and WASH NFIs to vulnerable displaced population will be integrated, and vulnerable communities will be targeted with rehabilitation of assets (water points and latrines) and construction of emergency shelters. 
CBIs will combine S/NFI and FSL, in order to revive the local market economy for both food and non-food items, considering the risk of people reselling the NFIs in order to buy food. LCED will contribute to support at-risk communities to promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks (SO3) targeting 15% of beneficiaries with restricted, unconditional cash vouchers. This will be implemented only in areas where the population has access to the market but no purchasing power. A market assessment was conducted in Mundri W/E counties (Oct‘18) and the results were shared with the S/NFI cluster. After defining the ES/NFI package for the targeted beneficiaries, according to their needs, LCED will engage suppliers in the targeted locations to set the price of the items, according to actual prices in the market.

project_name: WASH assistance for IDPs, returnees and host community in Greater Equatoria
project_objective:
This project will respond to the need of the most vulnerable displaced 20,000 individuals in Eastern and Western Equatoria State, targeting with static response Mundri East and West counties (WES) and with mobile response Tambura (WES), and Magwi county (EES), over the period of one year. The disaggregated numbers of estimated beneficiaries are: 4,500 men, 6,900 women, 4,100 boys and 4,500 girls. The project targets the most vulnerable IDPs (60%, both newly displaced and protracted IDPs), returnees (30%), and host population (10%), particularly focusing on people with protection concerns and with most acute needs, in order to alleviate their sufferings and foster protection through access to safe water, and improvement of hygiene and sanitation.
The project activities will include direct distribution of WASH kits (each containing 120 aqua tabs/PUR, 3 bars of soap, 1 filter cloth and 2 buckets) to the most vulnerable households, including pregnant and lactating women (PLW), elderly and disabled persons, and children under 5. Also, it includes distribution of MHM kits to women and girls of reproductive age. 
The LCED team will identify distribution locations through in-depth assessment, and Relief
Distribution Committees (RDCs) will be established at each distribution site, to facilitate the identification of the most vulnerable households and their needs, through community participation. This activity will also imply training of the beneficiaries on household water treatment, which will be conducted house-to-house by trained community hygiene promoters. The project activities will also include Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with women and girls in order to identify collective water points with secure location and access. At the same time, Water Management Committees (WMCs) will be established and trained in each area, which will be responsible for the maintenance of water points identified.
Another project activity will be the rehabilitation/improvement of existing sanitation facilities, in order to make them secure, protected and gender-appropriate (gender-segregated latrines with provision of locks and doors). This will include other FGDs, 50% with women and 50% with men. These activities will be paired with community sensitization on the use and maintenance of safe water sources and appropriate sanitation facilities, and on the use of correct hygiene and sanitation practices, e.g. the need of washing hands at critical moments, food preservation and proper storage of water safe for drinking, and discourage defecation, especially near open water sources. Community sessions of hygiene promotion will be conducted in common spaces in various locations, accessible by all categories of marginalized persons, by trained hygiene promoters in the course of one year.
Finally, a CBI will be implemented, targeting 10% of the total project beneficiaries. LCED will implement two types of CBI: a cash-for-work program, in which beneficiaries will receive restricted, conditional cash vouchers in exchange for their work in the construction of new temporary latrines (LCED will provide the tools, material and technical supervision) and a CBI targeting  vulnerable women, elderly and disabled persons who are not in cannot be targeted in the cash-for-work interventions, with restricted, unconditional cash vouchers for the purchase of essential WASH NFI. This approach will contribute to the resilience and supporting local market economy.

project_name: Providing Emergency Nutrition interventions for Conflict affected people in Wau, Tonj North and Kapoeta East
project_objective:
The level of humanitarian emergencies in South Sudan is still high as communities are still witnessing conflict and drought. In Mid -June 2018, thousands have been forced to flee out of their homes after fighting broke in different location in Wau County, The displaced people were mainly women, children and elderly who had arrived from Great Baggari in Wau to Agok, Hai Masna about 8km from Wau town.  The nutrition situation still remains dire, with many counties Greater Bahr el Ghazal, and Eastern Equatoria expected to experience a critical or very critical status during the lean season, based  per the IPC acute nutrition analysis. Furthermore, humanitarian access remains a major challenge in implementing life-saving interventions. Islamic relief World Wide (IRW) South Sudan Operation, has been part of Humanitarian response in Wau (Bazia and Baggari), Tonj North and Kapoeta East. During the 2018 interventions in health and nutrition IRW have witness the humanitarian gaps and needs to Vulnerable population in Wau (Bazia, Baggari County) and Eastern Equatoria Kapoeta East, that still needs to be intervened.
In Kapoeta East, Narus Payam, Lopua Boma, IR managed to construct a PHCU, and Established OTP and TSFP with WASH facilities that supported, 8,000 Individuals from 16km walk to access basic health and nutrition service. IR is willing to maintain the facility and establish 2 OTP sites (Lochua and Lomuta) given the population in this areas are still Vulnerable moreover the latest SMART survey done in June 2018, GAM – WHZ Score level of serious (10.4%) and initial trend of Critical and emergency (IPC 4 and 5).

project_name: Provision of timely equitable access to WASH services for conflict and drought affected people in Yei , Kapoeta east , Tonj east and Terekeka counties.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the proposed project is to provide timely, equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services to 48,500 people affected by conflict and drought in Yei, Terekeka, Kapoeta east and Tonj east counties. The project is expected to provide Water, sanitation and hygiene temporal and sustainable services that will address the vital needs and public health and protection issues using AAP community approach to the targeted vulnerable women, children, men, elderly and disabled people affected by drought and conflict. The intervention will further enhance community resilience by addressing the main drivers of vulnerability in the targeted areas of Yei, Kapoeta east, Terekeka and Tonj east. 
The project will seek to improve and increase timely access to equitable safe water and sanitation and hygiene services through construction of new water points (boreholes ) , rehabilitation of existing water and sanitation facilities in both the community and health facility set ups . 17 new boreholes are expected to be drilled, 50 existing but defunct boreholes are expected to be rehabilitated and restore clean water supply to the targeted communities. The project is expected to target the most vulnerable households with  WASH NFIs  these include water storage and collection containers , washing basins , washing soaps   to  3,000 Households, while 3,000 girls of adolescent age and women of child bearing age  will benefit from women menstrual management kits , this is to improve the health and protect the dignity of women . 
The project is expected to enhance behavioral change towards better hygiene practices, different groups will be targeted with hygiene specific message, schools, nutrition and health centers will be targeted to increase their knowledge on hygiene.  The project is expected to build resilience of the affected people, selected members from the community will be trained as members of water management committee with 40% women represented, and capacity of selected members of the affected people will be enhanced to carry out hygiene promotion activities and campaigns in the targeted areas. The project is expected to build and strengthen the capacity of local community members as village hand pump mechanics with specific roles of repairing and maintaining the community water supply systems in Yei, Kapoeta east, Tonj east and Terekeka. 
The intervention is expected to reinforce protection of the various groups affected by the conflict during service delivery by so doing, IRSS will conduct protection risk analysis and the intervention will be based on understanding the local context in terms of socio-cultural dynamics to mitigate all risks to various groups (women , girls, and children) of the affected group.  Awareness on GBV and sexual exploitation will be conducted to raise awareness and inform the affected community of all forms of GBV and sexual exploitation practices and action that might affect the people and be able to mitigate.
The project will ultimately contribute to saving, improvement, protection and recognition of dignity of the affected people and ultimately reduce their vulnerability and enhance their resilience.

This project will provide support to host communities in underserved areas affected by the recent violence in Duk County. project_name: Improved access to safe water, and improved sanitation and hygiene practices for vulnerable populations in Renk, Leer, Aweil and any other location across South Sudan
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to contribute to the reduction in morbidity and mortality resulting from waterborne diseases, by increasing access to safe water, sanitation and better hygiene practices among displaced populations, vulnerable communities, and host communities in South Sudan.
1. WASH in Nutrition: This project will support efforts to combat malnutrition (for SAM and MAM cases), aiming at providing beneficiaries of therapeutic nutrition with means to purify their drinking water, improve their basic hygiene and equip the caregivers to be able to offer/implement safe hygiene practices. Follow-ups with families to monitor correct use of the PoUWT items and hygiene kits will also be done. Medair plans to support nutrition centres with safe drinking water, latrine(s), hand washing stations and waste disposal facilities. The project will be implemented in Renk, Aweil, Leer and in any emergency response location that Medair will be involved in.
2. WASH in Nutrition and Health Centres: The proposed environmental health activities for this project will focus on providing Medair-supported health and nutrition facilities with appropriate waste management which may include a placenta pit, an organic waste pit, a sharps pit, an incinerator/ burn pit and destruction of the returned therapeutic food wrappers. Medair intends that all facility sites are supported with the minimum WASH package of safe water and latrine access, including waste management. For mobile clinic sites, safe water will be transported with the Medair teams and the waste taken to a centralized waste management site by the Medair teams, if necessary. Training on appropriate chlorination of water supply for use in the health and nutrition facilities will be provided with monitoring records compiled by clinic staff and reviewed by WASH technical staff to ensure safe water quality.
3. Acute Watery Diarrhoeal diseases prevention and response: With cholera, HEV, EVD and typhoid still presenting a high risk in South Sudan, Medair will seek to actively implement activities aimed at preventing such outbreaks including providing timely WASH minimum packages during interventions on a needs basis, adapted to the specificities of the outbreaks, at institutional level (health facilities) as well as for the wider community. The location of these activities will be decided after assessments by the emergency response team and after coordination with the WASH cluster and other relevant clusters.
4. WASH interventions in communities: This type of interventions is planned for static project sites, which have host and IDP populations. The main aim will be to provide water, sanitation and hygiene services that meet or exceed the Sphere Standards. These types of interventions will include water supply through various abstraction, purification and storage technologies, hygiene interventions aimed at promoting hand washing at critical times, increased knowledge on safe hygiene practices, and supporting latrine construction at HH level. This type of intervention is planned for Aweil, Leer, Renk, and to some extent, to some emergency response sites.
5. Emergency preparedness and response: In line with the proposed WASH Cluster Emergency Preparedness and Response Mobile Teams Strategy, Medair’s Emergency Response Team has capacity to respond to rapid or slow onset disasters anywhere in South Sudan, within set timelines. Medair’s ERT will continue to respond to disasters and align with the proposed WASH Cluster Strategic Objectives to provide timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water to vulnerable and affected populations, increase knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices among vulnerable and affected populations, to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases and to enable vulnerable and affected populations to practice safe, sanitary and hygienic living, through secure, dignified and gender appropriate sanitation services.
