project_name: Improvement of Health Access  for the population of Bor South and Pibor Counties, Jonglei State, South Sudan
project_objective:
South Sudan enters in its 5th year of conflict, the humanitarian crisis that suffers the country continues intensifying and expanding: violence is increasing and the economic decline threaten health, security and subsistence of the population. The conflict has had a major impact in the health system of Jonglei State, affecting the wellbeing of the population, both host and IDP population live together and mixed in the community and therefore both of them will benefit equally of the project.
South Sudan has a fertility rate of more than 4 births per woman, and 90 percent of women give birth without the assistance of a skilled professional. In 2013, the average neonatal mortality rate was 39 per 1,000 while the infant mortality rate was 64.1 per 1,000 live births . Much of women and girls give birth at home. Inadequate child spacing, poor feeding habits and the lack of food affect the general health of the community; this situation is similar in Jonglei State
In South Sudan, only 22% of the country’s healthcare facilities are operational and the absence of services contributes to morbidity and mortality. The ongoing conflict and insecurity limit access to medical assistance and hamper the timely treatment and control of disease. Women, who are in a subordinate position, are particularly affected. The conflict has exposed the Jonglei State population to multiple protection risks at home and within communities. Women and girls can be kidnapped, injured and/or killed, or become victims of gender-based violence (GBV) including sexual violence; men and boys are at risk of being recruited by armed groups, detained and even killed.
Doctors of the World-Médecins du Monde (MdM), in close partnership with the Ministry of Health (MoH), has been supporting the Bor State Hospital (reference facility for the whole Jonglei State) since November 2017, reinforcing maternity and paediatric services. Yet it remains short-staffed, in need of technical support and capacity strengthening as well as medical supplies. The regular needs assessments carried out by MdM outline the need to strengthen sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services as well as children health services in terms of capacity building, resources, coordination and supervision. 
MdM is the main health organization in Bor South and the only one present at the state hospital, this means that the organization has direct access to a vulnerable population, victims of gender-based violence and abuse, and that it can easily establish a coordination system with other organizations related to protection and violence issues, as well as offer clinical management of situations of gender violence, always including the MHPSS component.

project_name: Access to basic, inclusive and protective lifesaving quality education with Integrated Emergency School Feeding Program and Multi-Sector Linkages services provided to crisis affected children and youths (3-18) in South Sudan.
project_objective: The increased access to basic quality education with Integrated Emergency School Feeding Programme response programme will focus in Uror, Nyirol, Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor and Twic Counties, South Sudan.  The programme will seek to improve the access to quality education amongst the crisis affected children and youths as an effort to promote sustainable quality education with incentivised enrolment and attendance to learning, reduce risks of cognitive underdevelopment and malnutrition, and provide access to safe and protective learning environments. The project will targets a total of 24,400 total beneficiaries desegregated into 16,400 children and youths (10,000 B & 6,000 G), 200 teachers (120 M, & 80 W), 200 PTAs/SMCs (120 M, & 80 W); the response aims at provision of scholastic materials, establishment and renovation of TLSs, capacity building of teachers & PTAs/SMCs, providing school feeding, restoring and providing safe and protective education among boys and girls while integrating with already existing projects in intra-sectors (especially Health, Nutrition, FSL, WASH, and Protection). The project equally hopes to enhance psychosocial development of learners besides improving hygiene and sanitation. The project will use its existing M&E system to monitor report, feedback, document, and share evident lessons. The project is also designed to ensure maximum impact is achieved through the proposed interventions besides ensuring accountability to the affected population.

project_name: GBV prevention and response to conflict affected populations in Leer, Uror, Nasir and Akobo Counties of Unity, Jonglei and Upper Nile States.
project_objective: Nile Hope seeks to implement GBV prevention and response and  by providing quality and timely appropriate case management and psycho social support to GBV survivors in in Uror, Leer, Akobo and Nasir Counties of Jongle, Uppernile and unity States. This project is designed to improve responses to cases of GBV, enhance the ability of survivors to recover from GBV, and make progress towards changing the social norms that perpetuate GBV, with the intent of fully mitigating the effects of GBV and preventing future cases. It will provide GBV response services and address critical gaps in information and knowledge among women and girls on GBV response, which limit access to services. The project will focus on provision of Psycho social support for women and girls through cases management in women and girls friendly spaces. This will be in line with minimum standards on case management. Access for services for survivors will be promoted through community wide campaigns on availability of services. Women will also be provided with some little cash for income generating activities to support their healing process and resilience. GBV risk mitigation will also be conducted through joint safety audits with different clusters to identity risky areas for women for redress. Therefore, the entire project will address the GBV issues affecting both Women and girls in the Communities. Through this project Nile Hope will target a total population of 10968( 6268 Women, 1200 Men, 1500Boys and 2000Girls) direct beneficiaries ion the all the project locations that is Leer, Akobo. Uror and Nasir of Jonglei, Unity and Uppernile states.

project_name: Provision of timely life saving WASH to the most vulnerable communities affected by conflict, disease outbreak, in areas of high malnutrition through integrated response, reinforced protection and community capacity building to increase coping mechanism.
project_objective:
Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) will conduct life-saving WASH activities aimed at meeting the emergency critical needs of vulnerable people in South Sudan affected by conflict, natural disasters, disease outbreaks, and areas of high malnutrition rates. PAH is delivering relevant, effective and needs-based WASH interventions across South Sudan through mobile Emergency Preparedness and Response (EP&R) teams, static presence in cooperation with static partners and coordination with the WASH Cluster.

This project aims at providing timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water to vulnerable and affected populations, increase knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases targeting IDP’s, host and the returnees. Interventions will include safe water provision through water point construction and rehabilitation (hand pumps, SWAT systems, water trucking, or provision of household water filters, depending on the needs); provision or rehabilitation of sanitation infrastructure (latrines, hand washing facilities and solid waste management); hygiene promotion (hand washing campaigns in communities and institutions, safe water chain and jerrycan cleaning campaigns); capacity-building of community institutions (pump mechanics, water user committees, community hygiene promoters, school's hygiene clubs), and distribution of WASH NFIs (soap, hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene kit, water containers, water purification filters, PUR or others).
Total targeted group is 250,000 beneficiaries. The project will target communities with poor access to safe water supply, unsafe sanitation and hygiene practices, poor sanitation coverage and support nutrition, health and education centers with WASH facilities (i.e. GAM rates of more than 27%).

The intervention will include detailed multisector needs assessment to identify the needs, affected gender, age and diversity groups, the vulnerabilities of the targeted community and coping strategies employed by the affected population. Based on the assessment report multisector interventions will be designed accordingly with PAH capacity (sectors of S/NFI, Protection, FSL), or with the support of the clusters coordination, response with other partners will be planned. The main priority is to provide emergency WASH necessary to reduce morbidity and mortality caused by WASH related diseases and limited access to water integrated with other sectors for holistic response.  

PAH will use the Emergency Response Teams (ERT) and the static project to reach crisis affected vulnerable communities in difficult to reach locations as soon as areas become accessible. During this action, the assessment team will be deployed within 8 days of the clearance to respond by the EP&R partners and the WASH Cluster. The team can deploy to at least three locations at the same time with a team of WASH Technicians and Hygiene and Sanitation Officers. 

Centralizing protection to promote principled access to basic services for the displaced and other vulnerable groups at risk, accountability to affected people and strengthening the application of cash – based programing will be part of the employed approach. PAH will implement capacity building of the community to reinforce coping mechanism to manage current shocks and sustain livelihoods, strengthen linkages with development action to support resilience. 

PAH will focus on integrating activities with other sectors as Health, Nutrition, Education, FSL and Protection through support with WASH facilities like soap, hand washing facilities, improvement of waste management facilities, access to latrines and capacity building of community health, nutrition workers on WASH related disease preventive measures among others.

project_name: Enhanced access to inclusive, quality and protective education in Unity State and Western Equatoria State South Sudan
project_objective: The project seeks to enhance access to quality, inclusive education in Western Equatoria and Unity States targeting conflict affected adolescents, children and youth aged between 3 and 18 years.   Teachers, Community members representing PTAs and local education officials will also benefit from the project as primary project participants.   Mercy Corps with Unicef funding is a currently implementing EiE project in the two States covering 92 schools (25 in WES & 67 in Unity State)  While complementing already on-going activities, the new project to be implemented during 2019 school year (February - December 2019) will increase the number of supported schools to 123 (49 in WES and 74 in Unity State).  At least 24 additional schools to be supported by Mercy Corps will be from Mundri West, an area that is not covered under the current Unicef education PCA. However, Mercy Corps is already implementing an OFDA funded WASH program in Mundri West and has already established contact with local officials.  By taking the new education project to Mundri West Mercy Corps does not only respond to local needs but the organisation also remains compliant within its strategy addressing community needs holistically through integrated programming.  As part of WASH project, in August 2018, Mercy Corps distributed hygiene kits to schools.  In Unity State Panyijiar County  which is classified as an IPC 4  area, the project will implement school feeding activities in 10 schools including minor repairs of school kitchens and storage facilities.  In Mundri West, where insecurity has resulted in the destruction of school infrastructure, the project will repair (10) and establish (10) TLS as well as construction of (10) gender sensitive school sanitary facilities.   Moreover, in both States, Mercy Corps will jointly facilitate psychosocial support for teachers and community members while providing essential teaching-learning and recreational materials to enable conflicted affected children to access quality education. The project will target children aged between 3 and 18 from IDPs, returnees and host communities.  Teachers and PTAs will also be linked to child protection and GBV services to enable them to provide requisite support to children traumatized by conflict.

project_name: Empowering and strengthening the resilience of adolescent boys and girls in Koch County, Unity State
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in South Sudan continues: 4.43 million people are displaced, including 1.96 million IDPs (OCHA Humanitarian Snapshot Sept.’18), with up to 85% estimated to be women and children (HNO 2018). This is exacerbated by continued economic decline, with inflation up to 183% year on year, as well as severe food insecurity over already more than 5 consecutive years. 

In this context, in line with South Sudan’s HRP objectives and, more specifically, the objectives as they are outlined by the Protection Cluster and Child Protection Cluster for South Sudan for 2019, Mercy Corps proposes an intervention that aims to provide life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable population to address their protection needs, as well as to prevent, mitigate and respond to their protection risks and strengthen their resilience. 

More specifically, Mercy Corps proposes a 11-months project that aims to empower and strengthen the resilience of the most vulnerable adolescent boys and girls – which will include supporting the socio-economic reintegration of CAAFAG (Children associated with armed groups and armed forces) and GBV (Gender-based violence) risk mitigation/prevention activities – in Koch County, Unity State. This will be achieved through psychosocial support, economic skills building, community engagement and GBV risk mitigation/prevention activities. In particular, the intervention will address factors associated with voluntary and forced participation of children and adolescents in armed forces and armed groups, especially the social alienation of this age group and the lack of livelihood and educational opportunities. The ultimate aim is that adolescent boys and girls will safely transition to adulthood, be a full member of the society and have lasting positive multiplier effects on their families, communities and social and economic structures. 

Project activities will be based on four components:  
1.	Providing quality and age- and gender-appropriate psychosocial support (PSS) and skills building activities to adolescent boys and girls in safe spaces
2.	Strengthening the skills of adolescent boys and girls to seek healthy economic and livelihood opportunities
3.	Enhancing awareness and understanding amongst parents/caregivers, gatekeepers and community members to facilitate an integrating, enabling, peaceful and protective environment for adolescents
4.	Enhancing the safety and well-being of vulnerable adolescent girls through GBV risk mitigation and prevention 

Through this, the project aims to target a total of 17,035 people (5,630 boys, 5,455 girls, 2,975 women,  2,975 men).

project_name: Protection monitroing,risk prevention,mitigation,protection assessment to identify the needs at the community level and strengthen their local capacity in Leah,Bieh,Mirmir,Nyoat,Tay,Buok,Dongol in Mayendit,Leer and Koch counties.
project_objective:
Fighting and Recycling of violence in southern unity has caused severe mental distress to internally displaced persons and host community in the proposed project locations leaving children and women vulnerable to sexual abuses and psychological distress, livelihoods disrupted, separation of children, child recruitment and households looted.
Despite efforts made by the warring parties to silencing the guns, however, human right violations are still being perpetrated by the same parties and most of violation and abuses went unreported especially in the hard-to-reach areas. The aims of this project are to prevent and mitigate protection risks by working together with community-based
protection mechanism and protection monitoring in hard to reach areas targeting 3500 girls, 3000 boys, 5000 women, and 3200 men.
 Gender-based violence (GBV) remains under-reported due to barriers to reporting. Through MHA ongoing protection monitoring
project in Dablual and Tochriak, 12  GBV related incidence including the death of two underage girls were recorded. That indicates that the level of GBV is high amongst the community in southern Unity especially in hard-to-reach areas. women and girls being exposed to rape forced marriages and other forms of GBV due to the fact that displacement makes women and girls particularly vulnerable to exploitation and abuse due to their social and economic status. Women have been reported exposure to the sexual assault between several locations, Mayendit-Mirnyal and between Leah-Biehpadeah when it comes to accessing services and assistance. They face similar risks when
walking long distances to collect water and firewood. According to the report and individual/group focus discussion during MHA Assessment to Leah as mentioned above, MHA wanted women and girls to have safe spaces for sharing their experiences and accessing support, link them with services providers and dissemination of life-saving
messages through awareness raising/community mobilization. MHA as protection partner implementing protection monitoring project under HRP 2018, we have conducted an assessment between19-21 of Sept 2018 in Leah and surrounding villages and interviewed a good number boys, girls, and women who expressed their basic needs and protection as well. Based on the discussion and observation, It was clear that more efforts are needed to ensure that most vulnerable and persons with specific need must be reached wherever they are. People from Leah had to walk a distance of 3 hrs either to Padeah or to Bieh in order to access humanitarian assistance. Following were discussed to have been the major challenges.
 1. Most vulnerable IDPs and host community have very little chance or no chance at all to express their need if they are not reached by humanitarian agencies in the hard-to-reach villages/Island, this is due to accessibility issue where they are not able to reach the services and humanitarian assistance.
 2.
Protection monitoring and assessment to identify the basic need and protection related concern amongst IDPs is lacking. 
3. Awareness raising to sensitize the community on harmful practices, negative coping mechanism, their rights, their responsibilities within the community, where they should access services and humanitarian assistance is lacking due limited partners accessing hard-to-reach locations due to insecurity and the distances.
4. There is also a need to strengthen the community based-protection networks because communities are the primary support mechanism for women, men, girls, and boys affected by the conflict. Through our ongoing protection monitoring project, MHA is working with the community-based protection networks in Dablual and Tochriak building on existing community structures and networks because they are also best placed for identifying vulnerable children, GBV survivors and can greatly reduce the risk of exploitation, violence, and abuse of children.

project_name: Provision of Mine Risk Education (MRE) to affected communities and internally displaced persons (IDPs), school children, women and men Manyo (Upper Nile State) and in Canal/Pigi, Twic East Counties in Jonglei State
project_objective:
In the current emergency situation, MTT to provide continuous risk education, community liaison and data gathering to affected populations on existing explosive remnants of war (ERW) threats in order to protect civilians and humanitarian actors.
The teams will focus on the two main approaches to reach people with key MRE messages in all areas of operation, namely: primary and secondary approaches. Primary approaches will be used for groups identified as the most-at-risk in the community and these groups will benefit through direct presentations and other important activities that will benefit the population. The activities aim to promote safe behaviour to populations living in or close to contaminated areas or other suspected hazardous areas. Secondary approaches will involve the most influential stakeholders, regarded as very close to their population, who act as agencies of change in their community. These are mainly religious leaders, teachers, group leaders or representatives. They will be provided with MRE information to reach out to other members of the population who are unable to be reached directly by MTT teams. 
In addition, this project will seek to increase the capacity of the target community to identify and report any suspected hazardous areas. This information will be shared directly with the NMAA and UNMAS. MTT also will coordinate with other sector as WASH, Nutrition, Child Protection and Health in schools alongside key life-saving messaging on food crisis/ rationing. It seeks to reach a majority of the population with key MRE information.

project_name: Enhance Food Security and Livelihoods Support for conflict affected households in Akobo,Fangak, Maiwut,Nassir and Leer of Jonglei, Upper Nile, and Unity States
project_objective:
The project will reach the most vulnerable 270,000 people (97,200 girls, 64,800 women, 48,600 boys and 59,400 men) which corresponds to 45,000 HH in Nassir 9500HH, Maiwut 8500HH, Akobo 7500HH, Leer 10,000HH and Fangak 9500HH. We shall contribute to FSL cluster objective 2 and 4 by providing production inputs (crop kits, fast growing vegetable kits and fishing kits). This will improve food production and provision of fishing kits will contribute to better nutrition at the HH level and in other cases improve HH income due to the sale of excess fish, this will take place from January 2019 to December 2019. We shall also provide unconditional cash assistance in line with FSL cluster objective 1 lifesaving food assistance, this response plan is aimed at an effort to prevent an even more severe food shortage as well as strengthening the coping capacities of the vulnerable host community and IDPs. Nile Hope shall liaise with FAO to get in kind support for the crop fishing and vegetable kits for the emergency responses but will procure for the other ongoing development projects
The production inputs will be given to 39,000 HH (23,400 Female HH and 15,600 Male HH)  7500 in Akobo,10,000 HH in Leer,7500HH in Fangak,6500 HH in Maiwut and 9500 HH in Nassir ,which corresponds to 234,000 beneficiaries vulnerable Host Communities 60% and IDPs 40% and unconditional cash assistance to 6000 HH (2000 HH in Maiwut,2000HH in Nassir and 2000HH in Fangak) which corresponds to 36000 beneficiaries. Special focus will be given to people with disability to make sure they are not left out. Capacity building training will be conducted on improved crop, vegetable and fishing practices and continuous practical sessions in the farms to selected recipient beneficiaries at the Payam level as TOTs to the rest of the Community for sustainability purposes targeting 10,000 people (6000 women and 4000 men). The overall project objective is improved food security and livelihoods at house hold level for the vulnerable population at risk of hunger and malnutrition

project_name: Provision of Integrated emergency and life-saving health services to vulnerable community in hard to reach and insecure areas of six counties of Jonglei, Unity and Uppernile states, South Sudan
project_objective:
This project aims to increase access to emergency essential primary health care services through an integrated service delivery package using both the developmental and emergency service with a focus on the major causes of Morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable community (Mothers and under-five children).  This project will support three mobile clinics, five PHCUs and three PHCCs while one county Hospital will also be supported to enhance integrated service provision in AKobo County. Through this project a total of 70,000 (23990 Men, 23610 Women, 11290 Boys and 11110 Girls) people will be reached with Preventive Promotive and curative health care services, of this 33,600 (48%) are IDPs, 28,000 (40%) are Host community while the rest 8,400 (12%) are Other sections of community. Nile Hope will also provide OPD consultation to 34,618 clients in the course of the project duration, we are also anticipating to reach to a total of 267 (15%) mothers with skilled delivery. To ensure enhanced service on Mental Health and Psycho social support we anticipate to support four PHCCs/ One PHCC in all the four counties Uror, Pigi, Akobo and Maiwut. The PHCCs are to be a center of provision of integrated Health Nutrition and WASH services including MHPSS and CMR service to Rape survivors. Hence a total of 114 under five children with SAM with medical complication will be treated in the targeted PHCCs, A total of 135 beneficiaries will be reached with CMR service. In addition a total of 1,154 beneficiaries with PTSD will received Mental health support and counseling. This funding will also ensure access to Immunization of 14,722 with measles and 16,322 children will be reached with EPI. 
A total of 11,66 house holds will be reached with Health education and awareness creating sessions to enhance community level surveillance, Disease prevention and early health care seeking behaviours hence enhancing resilience among crisis affected populations. Nile Hope believes that an enhanced coordination between humanitarian and development approaches is essential. As a result the development support has increasingly been forced to move away from the ambitions of building sustainable health structures and come to focus more on service delivery and resilience oriented activities, In that way, the gap between humanitarian and development interventions has shrunk. Nile Hope will work on enhancing and synergizing the emergency humanitarian response to focus on lifesaving activities while striving at building more durable solutions from the start. With the urgent life-saving needs that exist in South Sudan at present this is a considerable challenge which requires a joint effort of intertwining and synergizing both the development and humanitarian responses together. The laboratory capacity of eight PHCC/Us and One county Hospital will also be strengthened to be able to diagnosis of malaria,  TB, HIV/AIDS, Kala-Azar both in Pigi and Akobo/Wechjal PHCC.

project_name: Provision of Integrated emergency and life-saving nutrition services to under 5 children, pregnant and lactating women and girls and other vulnerable groups in insecure and hard to reach communities in five counties in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Unity State, South Sudan
project_objective: Through this project, Nile Hope will be able to continue providing nutrition interventions in Pigi, Leer, Akobo, Nassir and Fangak counties. The project will seek to screen 87,525 children below five years and 47,776 PLWs and reach 10,090 children with SAM treatment services, 15,223 under fives with MAM treatment, 5,624 PLW with treatment for acute malnutrition, 48,827 caregivers and pregnant women with MIYCN messaging and counseling. The project will provide SAM management to children between 6-59 months, MAM management to under five children as well as to pregnant and lactating women as well as MIYCN and a strong component of community mobilization and sensitization. In order to offer the said services, there will be a strong component of surveillance through continuous program monitoring that will also include SMART surveys/Mass MUAC screening/KAP surveys. Routine community mobilization and sensitization, active case finding, referrals and follow ups at the household level will be done to strengthen all the components. There will also be a strong linkage with health facilities and other existing programs particularly livelihood programs, WASH and GBV/child protection. The project will rely fully on log cluster to deliver supplies to the project locations. There is are existing agreements with WFP for supply support in managing MAM cases and with UNICEF to support SAM cases in both Pigi/Canal and Leer counties. Both WFP and UNICEF agreements support Nile Hope with supplies. WFP also supports some CNVs. There will be static sites offering integrated management of SAM and MAM in both locations. Community mobilization strategy and basic monitoring and evaluation paying attention to data collection, reporting and supply chain management.

project_name: Improving health standards among 15,900 host community members, returnees and displaced persons who are at risk of getting WASH related diseases in Juba and Terekeka Counties
project_objective:
Juba and Terekeka Counties of South Sudan has consistently remained below sphere minimum standards in terms of WASH infrastructure and services due to the conflicts and economic crises. Having access to safe water and basic sanitation and adopting good hygiene practices has remained extremely below the recommended standards. Improving access to safe drinking water, appropriate sanitation and proper hygiene practices plays a critical role in preventing water related diseases often associated with conflicts.

This project will focus on improving quality of life among 15,900 female and male individuals who are directly affected by conflict and having very limited access to basic WASH services; which exposes them to the risk of outbreak of WASH related diseases in Juba and Terekeka Counties. The project will target beneficiaries at health facilities, schools, market places and households for improvement of WASH services and fixing gaps for mitigation of WASH related diseases. Water supply, sanitation and hygiene services will be provided for timely access at locations where community members remain vulnerable at sites of high risks identified during joint assessment with Payam authorities.
11,000 individuals will benefit from regained access to clean water supply through rehabilitation of communal water collection points. 3 communal latrines will be rehabilitated and handwashing facilities with shops will be provided for 13 primary schools and 4 health units. Also 4000 community members will have access to 8 newly constructed water collection points.

For effectiveness of the WASH services, provision of basic WASH facilities will be accompanied by capacity building through training of 20 health care workers as hygiene focal persons. 13 school hygiene clubs will be formed and pupils trained including 26 female and male teachers to support hygiene promotion sessions in schools. 30 community hygiene promoters will be trained and enormous participatory hygiene and sanitation promotion sessions, water quality monitoring, disinfection and chlorination will be conducted at times of needs. Training will be given for 208 female and male Water User Committees at the rehabilitated and newly constructed water points to support efficient use and maintenance.

During the project cycle, NSDO field team will coordinate with key partners on ground who are providing WASH, health, nutrition and protection services at other sites in same Counties Regular joint activity monitoring sessions will be conducted and will involve County Department of Water and Sanitation and Public Health and Environment and partners.
NSDO will also prioritize daily and weekly reporting and information sharing.

Protection mainstreaming will consider design improvements to accommodate the disabled, small boys and girls, and considering privacy, dignity and protection. Hand washing facilities will be fixed and soaps provided to promote the habit of hand washing at critical times among school pupils. Menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits will be provided for girls of reproductive age accompanied with Menstrual Hygiene Management sessions so that girls will not miss classes during their periods.

project_name: Early recovery livelihood assistance to IDPs / Vulnerable host community
project_objective:
This project is designed to link food assistance to early recovery livelihoods activities and compliments NPA’s emergency projects and the NPA Rural development projects in Awerial, Yirol East and West. NPA plans to provide an appropriate package of emergency and early recovery assistance by distributing livelihoods inputs to vulnerable farmers in Awerial , Yirol East and West. This project is integrated with NPA rural development project as the first phase of assistance as project participants wait for the long term sustainable assistance under the rural development programme.

South Sudan has numerous challenges as a result of the protracted crises. In response, NPA is now planning and implementing more sustainable projects, which link emergency food security interventions with early recovery and livelihood activities. In this project NPA is proposing to distribute fishing kits to 2500 households (HHs) with vegetable kits and tools , 2500  H/H with fishing kits  and  crop seeds to 3 000 HHS. This would follow by training 1500 farmers on crop and vegetables will also receive training on improved agronomic practices and 500 farmers will be trained on fish preservation marketing and group dynamics. The trained farmers will be expected to pass on their knowledge to other vegetable farmers and fishermen. The farmers will undergo training on vegetable production, crop production and this knowledge will be of importance in building the community resilience to future shocks. These activities are aimed at improving production of vegetables hence contributing towards reducing malnutrition rates. The vegetables, crops and fish will go a long way in restoring the nutritional status of the affected population, through increased food consumption and widened dietary diversity options. 

Beneficiaries of this project are household members who are extremely food insecure individuals (i.e. population in IPC 4 and 5) spread across 3 project locations.  NPA will follow a community-based approach, whereby the community take up the role in the selection of eligible households particularly returnee and internally displaced households, while also including vulnerable members of host communities. A vulnerability selection criteria will be developed where communities also participate in discussing and endorsing the beneficiary selection criteria. The beneficiary selection criteria will also be comprised of both status and proxy indicators, such as: i) Displacement status and duration, ii) Vulnerability status (female, child, disabled/chronically ill headed households, and large households), iii) Economic situation (income, debt and living conditions). Other issues are households with malnourished children under 5 years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW). 
Beneficiaries will therefore be the prime movers of the implementation process through their continuous engagement in the project. During periodic community meetings and Post Distribution Monitoring assessments NPA will ensure that the voices and concerns of all groups are captured. In addition, beneficiaries will actively participate in project implementation through mechanisms such as Food Management Committees. Targeting criteria will also be verified and refined through active participation of the beneficiaries. Further, to promote accountability, NPA will continue using the community based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide platforms for beneficiaries' active involvement in the project and avenues to voice any issues or concerns.

project_name: Emergency Shelter/NFIs Assistance to IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities of South Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to provide Survival Kits /Emergency shelter/Non Food items to the most vulnerable
persons newly displaced/host communities and returnees. The project will focus on the life saving shelter/NFIs needs as identified through assessment to protect the affected displaced people from harsh weather conditions and protection risks targeting all states of South Sudan through mobile response as per need as well as using its static teams based in Wau, Bor, Akobo, twic and Duk. However major focus areas will be Jonglei, Unity, Northern Bahrul Ghazal, Westerna nd Eastern Equatoria states. Cash programming will also be considered in areas where markets are functional and shelter/NFI items are available and accessible to the community.  
When blanket targeting is not the applicable, the action will target mainly lactating and pregnant women,
households with malnourished children, and households with members who have certain health
complications. Besides unaccompanied children, unaccompanied elderly and persons with no
community linkages will also be targeted.
The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in
line with humanitarian priorities for 2019 HRP's SO 1 and SO2. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 14 days for full-fledged delivery of NFIs
and emergency shelters and other activities per location.

The project will also support returnees in settlement as a part of their local integration or returns to their areas of origin. This will be done in an integrated way with other projects being implemented by NRC so that the returnees dont only receive shelter support but also a source of Food security and Livelihood through the food security projects in the planned locations. Additionally provision for education in emergencies and Legal Counseling  will be made for the returnees.

Approach:
Under the Cash Programme mainly the focus will be on construction of Shelters for returnees with active involvement of communities. Geographic preference will be in WAU, Bor and Yei areas where there are many returnees and markets are functional. Around $400,000 is estimated for the cash programme mentioned under the Supplies cost. The Cash programme will target 10,000 people covered by shelter and NFIs.    

Integration: The shelter interventions will be implemented as part of the integrated Emergency Preparedness and Response (EP&R) where implementation is based on the multi-sector assessments and team involving WASH, Shelter, Food security and emergency Education with protection as a cross cutting theme. In some of the locations, the shelter projects link up with other ECHO and WFP funded emergency projects to ensure the beneficiaries receive a comprehensive response package.

The project will be implemented in coordination with other players in the sector especially IOM for information sharing and use of the cluster core pipeline supplies as well as other Shelter cluster members for joint assessments and response when appropriate. The project will also be coordinated with the Shelter cluster especially in prioritization of locations and needs assessment.

project_name: Provision of essential integrated primary healthcare emergency clinical Packages to most vulnerable displaced populations, host communities and returnees in Greater Kapoeta (East, North & South) Counties.
project_objective:
This project will be implemented in Greater Kapoeta Counties (East, North and South) to provides essential primary healthcare emergency clinical packages to the most vulnerable displaced populations, Host communities and Returnees targeting 10,751 (1,531 males, 1,428 females, 299 children under 5 years and 330 children under 15 years in Kapoeta East, 1,528 males, 1,427 females, 299 children under 5 years and 329 children under 15 years in Kapoeta North, 1,528 males, 1,426 females, 298 children under 5years and 328 children under 15 years in Kapoeta South) provision of Medical consultation and treatment for common childhood illnesses, maternal health and other medical condition (ANC, delivery & Post-natal care), Preventive intervention; Health Education on integrated health (WASH, Nutrition GBV etc); - psychosocial counseling, expanded program on immunization and the project will support active surveillance for epidemic prone diseases such as malaria, cholera, measles and meningitis throughout implementation periods, referrals for Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CeMONC), minor trauma and surgery, scale up TB/HIV/AIDS/Disability care, Scale up integrated response to SAM with medical complications and Procurement 12% of emergency health pipeline to bridge in gaps for medical supplies and other essential equipments’ through provision of mobile clinical packages in 4 hard to reach areas, support 3 Primary Health Care units (PHCUs) and 2 Primary Health care centers (PHCCs).
Organization for Peoples’ Empowerment & Needs (OPEN) Implemented SSHF round one with support from Health cluster in Kapoeta East and SSHF round two allocation is currently ongoing in Kapoeta South to complement efforts toward to lifesaving given few functional health facilities in the Counties and the proposed activities will bridge the huge health needs and contributes to HRP 2019 strategic Objective 1 of  save lives by providing timely and integrated multisector assistance and services to reduced acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys.

project_name: TURKEY - United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
Provision of Shelter and Non Food Items to vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and Host Community families in Iraq
project_objective:
The proposal presents the UNHCR concept note on the Provision of Shelter and Non Food Items to vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and Host Community families in Iraq. The proposal considers the humanitarian needs in shelter and NFI recently assessed in the country by the IOM-DTM and MCNA VI. It is also built on the UNHCR operation plan for 2019 and the SNFI cluster HRP target for 2019 (347,750 for shelter; 513,900 for NFIs). The UNHCR intervention will be strongly based on vulnerability considerations to make sure that the Vulnerable IDPs living in camps and the highly vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host community members living outside camps will receive due priority attention. 
The concrete activities outlined under the proposal relate to the provision of emergency and transitional shelters, maintenance of camp infrastructures, provision of cash for shelter to repair damaged shelters (WDS) and distributions of NFIs to vulnerable families. UNHCR will continue to use its strong assessment and monitoring tools to guaranty full accountability to beneficiaries up to the humanitarian recommended standards. UNHCR will work with strategic partners including the Government institutions (MoDM, JCCs, etc.) to ensure a smooth handover and nationalization of the IDP/Returnee assistance as the emergency gets protracted.

project_name: Prevention and response to Sexual and Gender-Based Violence strengthened for IDP and returnee women, men, girls and boys
project_objective: In 2019 and beyond, UNHCR’s SGBV programmes in Iraq will focus on strengthening the capacity of national institutions, creating conditions conducive to disclosure, ensuring lifesaving services for survivors, and promoting innovative approaches to change social and cultural norms that justify or tolerate violence against women and girls. UNHCR will support capacity building of UNHCR staff, partners, law enforcement bodies and government officials to identify, refer and effectively support survivors to reintegrate back into their communities. UNHCR will mainstream SGBV into other sectoral response (NFI, Shelter and camp management) and community-based SGBV mechanisms to ensure that communities gradually assume responsibility for psychosocial support programmes and case management of non-complex cases. Engagement with local organisations and civil society networks, including human rights defenders, will be key in ensuring access to prevention and response services in areas of return. The existing capacity building project for the Directorate for Combating Violence against Women (DCVAW) will be upscaled to ensure provision of comprehensive SGBV prevention and response services in Erbil, Dohuk and Sulaimaniyah, Mosul and Ninewa. UNHCR will reinforce and sustain existing partnerships and collaborations with UNFPA, UNWOMEN, UNDP and other protection partners within the framework of the GBV Sub Cluster and other coordination mechanisms including GBV TF, TF on Child Marriage, TF on Survival Sex, RTAP, MARA, and through its co-leadership of the GBVIMS to ensure prioritisation of interventions addressing the protection needs of women and girls, especially those subjected to ISIL related sexual violence.

project_name: Supporting legal and physical protection of IDPs and returnees and supporting sustainable solutions
project_objective: UNHCR’s protection programme for IDPs and IDP returnees will focus on ensuring access to legal and physical protection for IDPs and returnees, with a strong focus on supporting the national authorities to identify and implement sustainable solutions for Iraq’s forcibly displaced population. UNHCR’s rights-based approach to programming will have a strong focus on non-discrimination and ensuring that all Iraqis have access to rights in line with international and national standards. The anticipated transition from humanitarian to development programming in Iraq will focus on advocacy for increased integration and self-reliance through longer-term livelihoods and access to employment, inclusion in national systems (including the national protection and social welfare systems) and other forms of durable solutions for IDPs and IDP returnees. UNHCR will reinforce coordination mechanisms among protection partners, advocate for increased funding for protection and rule of law interventions (particularly with regard to strengthening of national systems and national actors), and continue to focus on mainstreaming protection (including child protection and SGBV) in the humanitarian and development responses. Capacity building on protection, including CP and SGBV and PSEA and community-based complaints mechanisms, will be a key component of UNHCR’s strategy to strengthen national protection systems and national actors, and to strengthen the protection component of other sector assistance programmes. UNHCR will continue to work to reduce protection risks through protection monitoring, resulting in referrals to targeted services and protection interventions and through evidence-based protection advocacy. Legal counselling, assistance, and representation on civil documentation, detention and advocacy for cases of forced returns and forced evictions will be prioritized as will strengthened case management and referrals to specialized services for children at risk and survivors of SGBV. UNHCR will also support feedback and two-way communication mechanisms with IDPs and returnees, including community-based complaints mechanisms and confidential and safe complaints mechanisms for SEA. UNHCR will also continue to support communication with communities (CwC) activities, in particular to support IDPs to make an informed decision regarding solutions to their displacement. UNHCR will work with strategic partners including the Government institutions at Baghdad and KRI level (MoDM, CoMSec, MoI/Civil Affairs Directorate, JCMC/NOC, MoLSA, DCVAW) to ensure a smooth handover and nationalization of IDP/Returnee protection and assistance, and ensuring that national authorities assume their responsibilities for protection

project_name: Projet d'appui aux populations vulnérables à l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle dans le Fitri et Batha-Ouest
project_objective:
Selon le cluster Sécurité Alimentaire et le Cadre Harmonisé 2019 (qui le classe en phase 2 ""sous-pression"" pour la période de soudure 2019), la région du Batha va à nouveau connaitre, en 2019, des taux de Malnutrition Aigüe Sévère et de Malnutrition Aigüe Globale dépassant le seuil d'urgence de l'OMS. Les données provisoires font en effet ressortir un taux de MAG de 17.1% (au delà du seuil d'urgence OMS de 15%) et un taux de MAS de 4% (au delà du seuil d'urgence). En outre, le Fitri et le Batha-Ouest sont deux des 11 départements (à l'échelle du pays) pour lesquels des stratégies de crise et d'urgence ont été observées chez certains ménages. Ces départements connaissent également une consommation alimentaire relativement faible. Ces nombreux indicateurs témoignent de la persistance d'une insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle grave.
Afin d'atténuer l'insécurité alimentaire et prévenir la malnutrition dans la zone, l'action proposée développera 2 axes d'intervention :
i) SI continuera à mettre en oeuvre des actions de prévention de la malnutrition chez les enfants de 6-59 mois et les Femmes Enceintes ou Allaitantes (FEFA) issues des ménages Très Pauvres à travers : le dépistage et le référencement aux centres de santé des personnes en situation de MAS; la distribution de cash inconditionnel permettant la couverture des besoins alimentaires pendant les trois mois de soudure aux ménages ayant en leur sein des enfants de moins de cinq ans; et la distribution de compléments alimentaires aux enfants de 6-23 mois et aux FEFA. Enfin, le Moringa, aux nombreuses vertus nutritionnelles, sera introduit et vulgarisé au sein de la communauté.
ii) SI participera également à l'amélioration des capacités de résilience face aux aléas climatiques de ces mêmes ménages, qui verront la possibilité de diversifier et augmenter leurs revenus, à travers un appui en intrants agropastoraux, des formations agro-pastorales pour les ménages bénéficiaires et un soutien et renforcement des organisations paysannes (AVEC et groupements maraichers), ainsi que des comités locaux d'action (CLA) et comités villageois de développement (CVD).
Tout au long du projet, une attitude particulière sera portée sur les questions de protection transversale (avec des formations et messages clés et la mise à disposition de mécanismes de gestion des plaintes) ainsi qu'au genre, puisque certaines activités sont spécifiquement dédiées aux femmes (comme l'appui aux groupements et AVEC).

project_name: Improving The Protection of Civilians Affected By Crisis in South Sudan
project_objective:
The current humanitarian and protection crisis in South Sudan requires an integrated, multidisciplinary strategic response and support to the widened and deepened humanitarian and protection needs. The main objective of this Oxfam GB project in South Sudan is to improve the protective environment and protection of civilians in South Sudan. To contribute towards that, Oxfam GB will apply a static and mobile modality to respond with protection programming. Static programming will link humanitarian and development/resilience programming through strengthening community based protection mechanisms whilst sustainable linking local actors and national actors on issue affecting women, men, girls and boys. 
Mobile response will contribute towards serving the hard to reach areas through its protection mainstreamed and integrated rapid response missions. This broad objective contributes to the HCT, Protection Cluster, HRP and HRP Protection Strategic Objectives as well as Oxfam Country Protection Strategic intervention for 2019 and for emergency preparedness and response protection strategy. Specifically, the following activities will be undertaken to achieve the main objective of this project: Protection assessments and protection advocacy; information dissemination, awareness raising, and campaigns on protection messaging, rights, entitlements and protection from sexual exploitation; individual protection assistance in-cash and in-kind; service mapping and referrals; strengthening community based protection; supporting safe programming (protection mainstreaming) and supporting local peace and security for women, youths and communities. 
Oxfam executes its protection programming through protection mainstreaming, protection integration and standalone protection initiatives. Protection integration into Food Security and Livelihood, WASH and Education programs will be framed on an overarching protection analysis and on sector specific risk analysis thereby ensuring that protection risks and potential violations are taken into consideration and addressed effectively. Specific protection objectives will be embedded to execute protection integrated multi-sectoral (EFSVL, WASH, Education) projects/programs- that will outcome to promote safe and meaningful access to services, build community resilience and curb the risks of exclusions and violence.

The project targets approximately 150 000 ( 61 620 women, 56 880 men, 18 270 girls and 15 120 boys,). Targetted geographical areas are tier one, two, and three through mobile (RRMs, EP&R, mobile response) and static programming. Specifically, the areas include: Pibor, Nyirol, Uror, Akobo, Ayod, Mvolo, Mundri, Yirol, Juba, Maridi, Kapoeta, Wau, Yambio, Kajo Keji, Rumbek, Cuiebet, Torit, Malakal. That is basically in Jonglei State, Central Equaotoria, Western Equatoria, Eastern Equotoria, Western Barh el Garzal and Upper Nile State. In order to support quality programming in other sectors, this project will support ‘safe programming’ (protection mainstreaming) through the risk reduction approach, conflict sensitivity approaches, as well promoting inclusive local peace and security for women, youths, and communities. At the same time, the project will strengthen gender mainstreaming and gender justice through transformative gender approaches in community based protection structures, and promoting women participaction and in leadership. A strong influencing strategy of this project will be guided by centrality of protection, protection of civilians, accountability to affected populations, promotion of gender justice, community accountability and Prevention from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). Collaborative interaction with the protection cluster will be done towards supporting and strengthening deep field cluster coordination in order to enhance coordination, complimentary, local humanitarian leadership, and maximising resource utilisation through shared responsibilities.

project_name: Provision of Water, Sanitation & hygiene to the most vulnerable & conflict affected population through static programme and EP&R"" in Boma state,Western Bahr El Ghazal, Western Equatoria, Nyirol and Akobo
project_objective:
The intervention will focus on IDPs, Returnees and Host Community (conflict, malnutrition and disease affected). Emphasis on female headed households, PLWHIV/AIDS, elderly and disabled.

The needs of the population in terms of WASH is directly related to the number of IDPs in the community, which always puts a strain on existing services and water sources. The cluster has taken into account high GAM rates that make populations more prone to diseases, and areas with a history of cholera outbreaks. Overall, this relates to poor WASH infrastructure and bad hygiene practices. 
In conflict-affected areas, water and sanitation infrastructures in IDP camps are often overstretched by the arrival of new IDPs or need to be upgraded/ maintained due to the protracted situation. Significant refugee influxes in areas that are already underserved in terms of access to water and sanitation facilities are creating additional health risks whilst emergency response struggles to meet sectoral standards in time. Self-reliance should be fostered and enhanced in all projects. The increasing demand for natural resources in densely populated areas, coupled with climate change, continues to challenge sustainability of water resources and their exploitation.

Oxfam 2019 WASH response will target 120,000 most vulnerable people of which 25,000 IDPs, 15,000 Returnees and 80,000 Host communities affected by crisis, food insecurity (high GAM rates) and disease outbreaks, with a strong focus on the most vulnerable members of the community.

project_name: Provision of quality prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five years and PLWs  in Rumbek Center (Lakes state) and Pibor (Jonglie) counties
project_objective:
The purpose of this project is to prevent and manage acute malnutrition in children under five years and pregnant and lactating mothers through implementation of community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and maternal infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN) activities in Rumbek Center and Pibor counties.  This project will focus on the management of children with moderate and severe acute malnutrition and pregnant and lactating mothers with acute malnutrition and will be implemented using the national CMAM guideline. Children of SAM with medical complication will be referred to nearby stabilization center (SC). To ensure quality and good coverage of the program, CNVs and MtMSG will do continuous screening, referral and follow up cases at community level. Furthermore, preventive activities will be conducted at nutrition sites and at community level and areas of focus will be awareness creation on maternal infant and young child feeding, identification and prevention of malnutrition, sanitation and hygiene, cooking demonstration and kitchen gardening. As part of treatment protocol, all children (if there is enough supply) with SAM will be screened and treated for malaria according to the national protocol. Furthermore, preventive kits (jerry cans, Mosquito nets, soaps) shall be provided to mothers /care takers of children under treatment for in OTP/TSFP sites as these children are at higher risk of getting infected and also a way to promote personal hygiene. 

All children who will be discharged cured from OTPs will be enrolled to TSFP programs for full nutritional recovery. When there is de-worming and vitamin A supplementation campaign, this project will support to ensure children under five in the county get it in collaboration with SMOH/CHD and the health partner in the county. Furthermore, children who may deteriorate while in TSFP programme will be enrolled to the OTP programme. PI will implement OTP and TSFP programme together in Rumbek Center but only TSFP programme in Pibor county. In addition to the above mentioned interventions, PI will implement BSFP in five sites of Pibor county.
Currently, PI is implementing OTP programme in seven OTP sites (2 OTPs in Kapoeta East, and 2 OTPs in Rumbek East, 3 OTPs in Cueibet) and 23 TSFPs (13 TSFPs in Rumbek East, 5 TSFPs in Rumbek Center, 4 TSFPs in Awerial and 8 TSFPs in Pibor, 1 TSFP in Wulu county) and 5 BSFP sites (all in in Pibor but ended in August).

project_name: Provision of quality lifesaving integrated management of life threatening acute malnutrition for vulnerable and conflict affected populations of  Ayod and Pibor counties, Jonglei state, South Sudan
project_objective:
RMF has a stong presence in Pibor and Ayod counties of Jongolei state implementing an integrated nutrition program in areas.  
The conflict-related displacement of over 200,000 people from northern, central, and eastern former Jonglei has severely disrupted livelihoods and access to social services, thus severely undermining food security in the State. The situation was exacerbated further by last year’s poor harvests as well as the economic crisis that has eroded households’ purchasing power. 

For the past two months the security situation has worsened in and around Boma areas due to increased increased inter tribal clashes between the Murle and Jie tribes leading to mass displacements and restricted movement. 
Displacement in the area led to disruption of nutrition and health services which made it impossible to implement a coordinated and integrated programming in the areas. 
Furthermore with the onset of the raining seasons the population is always expected to be highly vulnerable to malaria and other related illnesses which could in turn worsen the nutrition situation for under five children as well as PLWs. 
A recent SMART survey conducted by IMC had Pibor GAM rates at 20.7% and SAM rates of 5% well above the W.H.O recommended threshold .This has placed Pibor County at IPC phase 4 classifications and at risk of humanitarian catastrophe. 
RMF will work in close collaboration with WASH,health and FSL partners in order to implement minimum package currently recommended as an intervention package for partners working in Pibor and Ayod counties
This intervention will lead to improved management of SAM cases in both under 5 and PLWs .Over all 4490 children 6-59 months are expected to be treated for  SAM while while 6313 children 6-59 months  are expected to treated for MAM.7616 PLWs will be treated for MAM.The intervention is also expected to champion preventive aspect of the nutrition program through an elaborate MYCN activities .Our presence on the ground will allow us to work together with other stake holders to continue to monitor, analyze and share the nutrition situation on a regular basis.

project_name: Provision of ES/NFI support and resilience building to IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable Host community in Upper Nile State
project_objective: The purpose of this project is to provide timely and critical lifesaving ES/NFIs as well as building resilience through cash based programming to 35,000 (20,000 females and 15,000 Males) conflict affected IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable host communities in Upper Nile State. The target population are based in Upper Nile counties that has experience a cycle of violence that has made it difficult to access for a long time. The same conflict has displaced many of the target population to either neigbouring settlement areas, POCs or neighbouring countries and are now returning to settle back in their original homes and are in need of immediate ES/NFI support and or resilience support. The host communities in these areas are getting it hard to cope with the number of returnees who are in need of their support and care with the little resources that they have. SSUDA proposes to intervene in three areas or objectives: save lives by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys; Protect vulnerable women, men, girls and boys through provision of specialized and integrated services; and support at-risk communities to promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks. This will be done through: providing access to life saving NFIs, providing access to emergency shelter using in-kind support as well as cash based program. SSUDA will focus largely on increasing cash based projects based on cash feasibility assessment report that is to be done in Upper Nile this year 2018 that will indicate which counties has active markets and advise on cash modalities to be used. Apart from this, SSUDA will mean-stream protection including GBV and HLP, consultations with the affected populations, working closely with other clusters, and other SSUDA implemented projects, monitoring of activities, and provision of skills, as well as providing messages of protection and health. SSUDA has experience in working in Upper Nile State and is implementing other projects such as education, communication for development, child protection, food security among others in the region that will help in providing not only synergy to this project but also information and critical understanding of the context and dynamics of the counties, knowledge of the local leadership and prospected beneficiaries, such as a 3-year EU funded Pro-Act resilience project for food security, livelihoods and WASH in Fashoda, Malakal, and Manyo, Education project in Panyikang and Manyo, Communication for Development (C4D) project in Ulang, Nasir, Panyikang, Longochuk, and Maiwut, and Child Protection in Ulang both supported by UNICEF. SSUDA is the ES/NFI state co-focal point in Upper Nile with an office in Malakal, and therefore about 6% of the project costs will go into overhead costs of SSUDA to improve its presence in the State and region.

project_name: Emergency WASH Provision Among Most Vulnerable Displaced and Host Populations in Jonglei and Central Equatoria States
project_objective:
Recent Inter-agency assessments in Jonglei and Central Equatoria indicate deficient key water supply infrastructure due to both the lack of maintenance and damage sustained during the active months of conflict, compounded by recent mass flooding in Pibor which disrupted livelihoods and displaced of over 14,348 households. Open defecation is widespread and risks exposure to water borne diseases; both communities reported an increase in cases of diarrhea and Acute Watery Diarrhoea. Untreated water from River Kengen, Kubal and Lothila including makeshift ponds has been attributed as the main cause; however, poor sanitation coverage including schools and lack of hand washing facilities, poor knowledge and practices on personal and environmental further fuel the situation.

Stop Poverty Communal Initiative (SPOCI), a national NGO, proposes to provide timely equitable access to safe  water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees; mitigate WASH-related GBV; WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention minimum package of interventions; and WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level. The project will target 15,000 beneficiaries comprised of 5000 girls, 5000 boys, 2500 men and 2500 women in Jonglei and Central Equatoria States. These will include elderly persons, pregnant and lactating women, people with disabilities drawn from the most vulnerable households. Among these will be beneficiaries at risk of gender based violence and sexual abuse, communities with poor access to nutrition and health, SAM/ MAM children or Ebola Virus Disease high risk zones in Central Equatoria. Inter-cluster synergies will be explored in targeted by close working with partners in nutrition, health, FSL, Protection.

Activities will focus on improving access to access to safe water supply, improved, secured and gender appropriate  sanitation facilities , hygiene promotion messages, support children admitted for SAM treatment discharged with WASH/Hygiene kit from functional OTP/SC , provision of access to safe drinking/chlorinated water , provision of functional handwashing facilities by soap or 0.05% chlorine running water and populations are  provided with a WASH minimum package of activities to mitigate WASH-related diseases. 

SPOCI has been operational in proposed areas for many years and currently implementing SSHF and UNICEF funded WASH actions. SPOCI is a member of State level Cholera Preparedness Task
Force, National NGOs Steering Committee, member of the ICWG and WASH Cluster Accountability to
Affected Populations Technical Working Group. In addition, SPOCI has for the past two years supported over 30,000 vulnerable populations with WASH/Education interventions through UNICEF among other partners support in Pibor. Through these, the organization has fostered strong linkages with communities, state/county line ministries of water and irrigation. This is in addition to strong and competent team including staff redeployment to scale up interventions based on needs.
Activities will ensure delivering a WASH integrated package. These will be further integrated with other Health-related priorities, acknowledging that poor WASH services are a key driver to poor health, and ultimately resulting in high malnutrition. This is in addition to regular assessments to mitigate GBV risks including sexual exploitation and abuse.
