project_name: Provision of Emergency Shelter & life-saving NFIs to vulnerable communities in Ulang & Nasir Counties, Upper Nile State
project_objective:
Nasir and Ulang counties in Upper Nile state are among the most affected by the war since 2013. Continuous clashes by warring parties in the area, and in Jonglei have led the two counties to play temporary home to a huge population of displaced persons. Their geographical place of being the route to Ethiopia camps make them the vulnerable counties in this war. Recent displacement from fighting in Nasir and subsequent displacement from fighting by warrying parties in Uror and Nyirol Counties, Jonglei state has further worsened the situation of IDPs in these areas. 

An IRNI assessment, conducted in May 2018 in Ulang and Nasir, by humanitarian teams that included TADO/SSUDA/IOM and other non-NFI partners exposed a huge need in the population assessed. The needs found among the population included: a)Lack of shelter for newly arrived returnees and IDPs b) Dilapidated shelter for IDPs, Returnees and host community C) Lack of blankets e) Lack of mosquito nets f) Lack of Water cans/pots to fetch water g) Lack of cooking utensils and h) Lack of dignity kits. An intervention conducted by SSUDA/IOM and TADO was effective in mitigating the immediate situation then but there is still a huge unmet need. The signing of the latest peace agreement in August 2018, has brought about hope among refugees and IDPs. This is likely to lead to an upsurge in population in the two counties in form of returnees. 
 
With these real needs, this project would support provision of and rehabilitation of emergency shelter and life-saving Non-Food-Items (NFIs) to vulnerable populations in Ulang & Nasir Counties in Upper Nile State. The core of this intervention is to improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable IDPs in protracted displacement, returnees and host communities unable to meet their S/NFI needs. The project also responds to urgent, demonstrated needs among the target 6000 beneficiaries. The intervention will involve continuous assessment and monitoring of the situation and will adopt an integrated approach, informed by and collaborating with other clusters’ interventions. This will improve protection for displaced persons as their access to emergency shelter protects them from harsh weather conditions and other protection risks. Further, the intervention supports communities in a dignified, integrated and coordinated manner by using local materials to support livelihoods through skills training, using skilled and unskilled labor. TADO will work closely with SSUDA the state focal point organization on S/NFIs.

TADO will pursue the following cluster objectives: 
1) Improve access to safe, appropriate emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to newly displaced or vulnerable populations in secondary displacement, and
2) Improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable IDPs in protracted displacement, returnees and host communities unable to meet their S/NFI needs.

The project will employ the following strategies/activities in order to contribute to the foregoing objectives:
a) Provide   access to emergency shelter (in-kind)
Target IDPs and returnees that have either newly arrived or missed out completely on past interventions 
b) Provide access to life-saving NFIs (in-kind)
Beneficiaries will be identified and mapped, priority to pregnant and lactating mothers, the elderly and the disabled. Households with young children or child-led households and unaccompanied minors will be prioritized.
c) Shelter upgrades (in kind) 
TADO in collaboration with local project implementation committees will identify beneficiaries whose shelters are dilapidated and/or inadequate due to emerging needs and prioritize upgrades to ensure that they continue being protected from harsh weather and other protection risks.
d) Replenish essentials NFI and emergency shelter
Beneficiaries whose NFI supplies are depleted or otherwise missing will be targeted for replenishment to ensure that they have access to a life of dignity and protection.
e) Engage the community in a way that stimulates active participation
Programming will continuously seek to engage beneficiaries and other stakeholders in order to build resilience to recurrent shocks. Beneficiaries will be given skills to enable them to cope and help each other and promote peaceful co-existence.
f) Mainstream HLP and conflict sensitive approaches throughout all stages of S/NFI response
TADO will ensure that HLP and peacebuilding messages are integrated into the interventions. Participants will be given capacity through training and dialogue meetings to take an active role on the matters that affect them
g) Mainstream GBV throughout all stages of S/NFI response
Beneficiaries will be aided and given training and to ensure that they participate in the protection process. Community-led initiatives will be encouraged and supported so that the beneficiaries can embrace gender equality and put in place mitigation measures against GBV.

TADO has over 5 years of hands-on programming experience in the Upper Nile State in the field of Education in Emergency and Peacebuilding. The organization has an intimate knowledge and understanding of the needs of the region and has thus far established excellent working relationships with the local community and the county government authorities. With a field office in Ulang, TADO is a formidable partner in the region with a vast network and infrastructure to support project implementation. TADO has 7 national staffs including S/NFI team leader and focal point based in Ulang field office with a good understanding of S/NFIs implementation and well experienced and always involved during the S/NFIs needs assessment in collaboration with ROSS and other partners in the field.
The unstable security context of Upper Nile State necessitates flexible responses; and in Ulang and Nasir counties, TADO has adapted to deliver quick implementation projects to continue to provide lifesaving interventions while limiting the time staff spends away from a permanent field base. The targeted counties continue to face high levels of displacement and intermittent conflict, with limited access to key services and infrastructure. Simultaneously, skyrocketing inflation has negatively influenced the ability of households to purchase basic goods.

project_name: Prevention and Treatment of Acute Malnutrition in Greater Upper Nile
project_objective:
Through the proposed project, RI will provide timely and quality treatment of acute malnutrition to children 6 to 59 months and Pregnant Lactating Women (PLW) reaching at least 85% of SAM with the expectation of 10% of which will be referred and managed at the stabilization center (SC) for medical complications, 80% of MAM children 6-59 months and 55% of PLWs. Additionally, RI will provide  nutrition preventive services through early screening at the community level and referrals, increasing access to MIYCN services, deworming and Vitamin A supplementation as well as improving the access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH and FSL services. 
Blanket supplementary feeding programme (BSFP) for children 6 to 59 months, PLW and people living with HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis patient will be implemented. 
RI will strengthen nutrition surveillance mechanisms through accurate and timely reporting, monitoring and analysis of data for early and objective decision making.

project_name: Livelihood support and livestock intervention to reduce dependency on food and agricultural input support in Upper Nile, Jonglei and Central Equatorial States: Panyikang, Baliet, Fashoda,Manyo, Canal Pigi, Juba, Lainya and Morobo Counties.
project_objective:
In line with strategic objective 3, SO3: Support at-risk communities to promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks and  cluster objectives 2 and 4 : CLO2 food production for the most vulnerable households: Increase vulnerable household food production to protect the erosion of livelihoods through y agricultural seeds and fishing inputs, CLO 4: Dependency reduction on food and agricultural input support: Prevent and reverse the erosion of vulnerable rural & urban households and community assets through livelihood & conditional cash based support for more sustainable livelihoods; RuCAPD seeks to help the populations in Panyikang , Manyo, Fashoda, Baliet in Upper Nile state, Juba, Lainya and Morobo in Central Equatorial as well as Canal Pigi in Jonglei state move  through recovery and resilience toward development through own food production livelihood support and livestock health services. This project is designed to effectively contribute to the protection and rehabilitation of livelihoods of the most vulnerable and affected population in Fashoda County, Upper Nile State. The project is a 12 month project targeting 20,000 HH equal to 120,000 vulnerable individuals IDPs -52,800, returnees 45,000, and host community 22,200; of whom 37800 are Men, 58200 are women, 12000 are boys and 12000 are girls. The targeting will be done with gender lens and consideration of incorporation of Accountability to affected population. We expect to train a total of 300 HH on different agronomy practices as well as 140 Community Animal Health Workers (CAWHs) for the livestock aspect of the project. Vouchers will be used in the seed fair project sites. The beneficiaries will use them to get the seeds they want and the traders will then redeem them for cash. The program implementation will ensure that Do No Harm principle is adhered to as transparency and accountability to the affected population is placed right at the center of beneficiary targeting and provision of support. RuCAPD extensive presence and history in Upper Nile, Central Equatorial and Jonglei coupled with an in-depth understanding of the community conflict dynamics and context tailored approaches to specific communities will help identify, analyze and manage risks as well as reduce any potential negative impacts of the project and any protection issues.
The project will receive pipeline supplies from FAO whilst the requested funding from SSHF will be used to provide front line services. The project will use direct distribution to the targeted groups through a transparent process of identification and distribution. In case of security hitches, RUCAPD has extensive network of how to reach the targeted beneficiaries.

project_name: Provision of emergency lifesaving mobile health care services, to IDPs and host communities in Pibor and Pochalla counties in Jonglei State
project_objective:
The proposed project intends to contribute to the reduction of excess morbidity and mortality caused by common communicable diseases and injuries sustained from violent conflicts through ensuring access to quality essential Lifesaving mobile emergency health care services to women, men, girls and boys, and gender based violence services in conflict affected population and host community (Marrow, Labarab, Kessingor, Dourein and Thangojon) in Pibor county and the needy People( Otallo1 and 2, Daktek, Chaam, Nyium,Ajwara, and Omila Payams) in Pochalla County. RHS found that the primary heath facilities in the both proposed Counties  have been reaching only the nearby population, just like at Gumuruk PHCU, Lekwangole PHCU, Jebel Boma PHCC, Pibor PHCC, and Pochalla PHCC, leaving other population without essential lifesaving primary health care services, unprotected against bad practices, sexual exploitation and abuses and more vulnerable and exposed to increased morbidity and mortality. This has been augmented by vulnerability of the communities due to the common infections  and long distances to reach Pibor, Pochalla, Gumurk, Lekwangole and Jebel Boma and some go beyond walking for several days to Dimma Refugee camp in Ethiopia to access medical services.  
RHS plans to open 1 static PHCU at Thangajon in Pibor County and establish 2 mobile clinics; 1 in Pibor County(Maruwo) to reach IDPs and host communities in Maruwo, Labarab and Kessingor areas. To save lives by providing timely and integrated assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in those places, and 1 mobile clinic to be in Pochalla North for the needy people of  Otallo 1&2, Daktek Chaam, Omila, Ajwara and Nyium. The 2 mobile clinics will do integrated services of curative consultations, ANC, Vaccination of children under 5 years of age screening and treatment of MAM and transfer of SAM cases to the nearest PHCC, disease surveillance and health promotion and education.
The RHS will also train the key project workers in both at the static PHCU  and at the 2 mobile clinics in preparedness and response to epidemic prone disease outbreaks with the focus on cholera, Measles, Ebola & Rift Valley Fever. as well as Malaria, meningitis, and Hepatitis E.
Inline with the health cluster objective 1 Save lives by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys, RHS intends to ensure adequate provision of essential and emergency healthcare services , including addressing the major causes of Morbidity and mortality among children under 5 (Malaria, diarrhea and Pneumonia), basic emergency obstetric and Neonatal care, (BEMONC) services, SGBV services, Clinical Management of Rape Cases (CMR) services to women and girls in Pibor and Pochalla Counties, Jongolei State, South Sudan. This will be further achieved through the continuity of curative consultations care services at Pibor and Pochalla. Other activities will include not limited to conducting clean, safe and hygienic deliveries by skilled birth attendants, minor surgeries, BEMONC including blood transfusion services, ANC to pregnant mothers including provision of HIV services, IPT, LLITNs and micro nutrient supplementation, growth monitoring and nutrition assessment to under 5 Males and Females, provision of screening and supporting treatment for MAM/SAM.
This project is designed to directly benefit a total of 10,000 individuals over the entire period segregated by age and gender.

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving WASH services to Cholera prone outbreak areas/communities and returnees communities in Ikotos County, Torit State and Awerial County, Eastern Lakes State in South Sudan
project_objective: The project aims to reduce the mortality and morbidity rate caused by high incidences of water borne diseases outbreak specifically cholera in the Prone and vulnerable communities in Awerial County and Ikotos County through provision of lifesaving safe water supply (new boreholes drilling, repairs and rehabilitations), increased household rural water treatment using Pur/Aquatabs, hygiene promotion sensitization at household and institutional levels, improved safe sanitation practices awareness, and breaking the cholera transmission routes between victims and caretakers/community members by 'contact tracing', disinfection, sensitization, WASH NFIs support and monitoring the gradual progress in hygiene and safe sanitation practices.

project_objective:

•	Resultat 3 : L’accès égal à la gestion et au contrôle des ressources au sein du ménage sont promus.

project_name: MRE: Improved the Protection of Vulnerable communities through provision of Mine Risk Education & Non-Technical Survey in Akobo, Nyirol, Uror (Jonglei) Mundri East & West (Western Equatoria) Yei, Lainya & Morobo (Central Equatoria) States
project_objective:
Due to decades of military battles around Jonglei, Central Equatoria & Western Equatorial States, it is anticipated that high contamination from explosive hazards is lingering around the areas and post a threat to the local communities, IDPS and returnees. The Project is to improve the ability of those IDPs, returnees and other community members, in particular children, to protect themselves from the risks they face in areas that have encountered previous fighting. This project falls under the cluster objective 1 & 2 and this will be achieved through the deployment of trained and accredited 8xMobile MRE/CL response teams (24xMRE/NTS Officers and 8xMRE/CL Team Leaders) and SLI-SS Technical MRE personnel. Each team will be deployed to different location such as Akobo, Nyirol, Uror (Jonglei), Mundri East and West (Western Equatoria), Yei, Lainya & Morobo (Central Equatoria) Through the use of both Trainer and Mobile RE Response SLI-SS intent to ensure that the project will:
 Provide Men, women and children in the areas affected by violence with an understanding of the danger of ERW and Mines, how to reduce it. 
 Aim at improving school-based MRE targeting school children and teachers using the MRE School guide and different approach to ensure sustainable approach and this is to increase the sharing and adoption of safety messages. 
 Ensure Community focal persons trained as well to ensure mines/ERW reporting and briefing of any new comer to the community they are made aware of the dangers of mines/ERW.
 Ensure that materials and equipment are made available to deliver RE Messages.
The implementation of the project will be In coordination with the National Mine Action Authority, UNMAS and Protection cluster, as the team will be expecting hazardous areas been reported during community liaison and RE presentation, this will be compiled reported through the IMSMA forms to UNMAS

project_name: Supporting Access to Family Planning and Post-abortion CARE (SAFPAC)
project_objective:
CARE Nigeria has been implementing the SAFPAC III project from early January 2018 in Borno and Yobe States, followsing a similar model to Chad, DRC and Mali SAFPAC projects. Health facility, community, and provider attitude assessments were followed by trainings for service providers and clinicians in key SRH clinical competencies and training for community facilitators on engagement and reflective dialogue to overcome social norms and barriers that inhibit women and girls’ access to family planning and post-abortion care. Routine clinical skills assessment, supportive supervision of providers and community facilitators, and improved stock management and supply chain are all considered in the model. Given the shortage of the functional health facilities in Borno and Yobe State, CARE Nigeria has been working to address key MISP objectives in its approach, including clinical management of sexual and gender-based violence.  Through this initiative, CARE is supporting 20 Health Facilities in Borno State, and planned to reach 4,800 new family planning users by December 2018 (with 60% using a LARC method), and 280 PAC users. From February, 2018 to June, 2018, CARE has reached a total of 1157 New Family Planning Users (24% of target); 113 LARC users (4.6% of target); 6 PAC Users with 2 PAC Users leaving with a FP method.
SAFPAC IV
CARE Nigeria will position SAFPAC phase III to scale-up for Phase IV with an additional 10 Health Facilities and expanding FP/PAC services to the second worst crisis-affected state in the Northeast - Yobe. Following the same strategy for SAFPAC phase IV, CARE will support a total of 30 Health Facilities (25 in Borno State and 5 in Yobe state), with the aim to reach 22,000 new family planning users by December 2021; 11000 (50%) targeted for LARC method and 1,290 PAC users.

project_name: Integrated GBV prevention and response in Borno State, North-East Nigeria.
project_objective:
The Action aims to strengthen prevention of and response to gender-based violence (GBV) for 7,832
displaced vulnerable women, men, girls, and boys and vulnerable host commmunity members through
coordinated, principled humanitarian support in Bama town and Ngala LGA in Borno State, Nigeria. As
well as the 7,832 IDPs and vulnerable host community members, the Action will reach 62 CARE and
other humanitarian staff, religious leaders, police, security forces, community leaders, and volunteers
engaged in addressing GBV in the areas of intervention.

project_name: All children and youth have  access to inclusive, safe and quality basic education among vulnerable  communities (IDP & returnees) in Jonglei (Nyirol, Uror & Akobo), lakes (Rumbek Centre & Rumbek East), Upper Nile (Maban), EE and CES (Juba)
project_objective: The proposed interventions aim to ensure that children and youth (boys and girls) have access to quality education and those already in schools are retained including children and youth with disabilities in line with INEE Minimum Standards for Education based on HRP priorities for 2019 and SCP CSP 2019. SCI targets to enroll 46,790 (25,818 boys; 13,902 girls) primary school age leaners in 75 primary schools Jonglei (Nyirol 15; 10 Uror 10 Akobo west; 10 Bor South); Upper Nile (10 Maban) and Lakes (10 Rumbek Centre; 10 Rumbek East). The programme will further target 2,500 (1,625 boys; 875 females) youth will life skills and business skills in 18 drop-in centres and 2,500 (1,625 boys; 875 females) young children in 60 ECD centres in all five locations including CES (Juba) and EE. SCI will focus to deliver life-saving education interventions and learning opportunities through the provision of safe learning spaces, education supplies, psychosocial supports (PSS), capacity building and back to learning school campaign including provision of school meals and take home ration for adolescent girls. SCI will link these interventions with other existing grants (NORAD, UNICEF and DANIDA) grants. SCI is commit to reaching vulnerable children by adopting flexible or alternative modality of delivering education. SCI will undertake multi sectoral and crosscutting components such us gender, protection, disability, child participation and accountability in their activities. Strong advocacy will be carried out to ensure prioritization and protection of education throughout the crisis. Monitoring will be done joint with the Child Protection cluster as a way of mapping and updating education facilities used as shelter by IPDs and/or attacked.

project_name: Emergency Response for Crisis-Affected Persons in BAY States, Nigeria
project_objective:
Provision of health care services was greatly affected by the crisis in north east and posed a huge burden on Women and children. Most of the health facilities in the rural areas were damaged and are non-functional. Women and children are the most affected in a crisis specifically those arriving from the inaccessible areas are extremely vulnerable as they have not accessed humanitarian services prior to their arrival at the reception sites.  The leading causes of morbidity and mortality linked to malnutrition has been heavily linked with diseases outbreaks such as the acute watery diarrhoea and malaria. Female headed households as well as separated and unaccompanied children face an uphill task of accessing adequate services and are exposed to sexual exploitation and abuse as well as gender based violence. Communities that have settled in the host with limited restoration of livelihood as they cannot access their fields for cultivations and are not actively engaged with economic activities, their children face the risks of repeated episodes of acute malnutrition.
Nutrition intervention targets 4M women and children in BAY states, of which 3M are children below the age of 5 and 1M are women of reproductive age with infants below 2 years.  Majority of those in need are in the host communities 2.6M while approximately 0.6M are IDPS and 0.5M returnees while 0.2M still not accessed by humanitarian workers. The prevalence of acute malnutrition in the north east is further heightened by inadequate health services coverage, poor child care practices, inadequate hygiene and sanitation conditions and food insecurity. 
Population arriving from the inaccessible areas have particularity high prevalence of acute malnutrition, a SMART survey conducted in Bama in August 2018 indicated a very high prevalence of GAM among the new arrival compared to those that have been in the camp GAM by WHZ – 37.5% (reception site) while 7.8% (rest of camp) . Similar situation is observed in all the 9 reception sites in Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Kalabarge, Kukawa, Mobbar and Ngala, through the screening of new arrivals. Population in host communities continue to grapple with serious nutrition situation, routine monitoring of the prevalence of acute malnutrition though the nutrition and food security surveillance Findings indicate that Borno State has a GAM rate of 9.1 per cent and a SAM rate of 0.8 percent; Adamawa State has a GAM rate of 8.2 per cent and a SAM rate of 0.4 per cent, Yobe State has a GAM rate of 12.1 per cent and a SAM rate of 2.1 per cent. North Adamawa has reported increase in GAM prevalence from 9.2 per cent reported in November to 10.1 per cent in April 2018. Yobe reported improved GAM rate in South and Northern parts while central Borno reported increased GAM from 11.6 per cent in Nov 2017 to 14.1 per cent in April (NBS, UNICEF Nutrition and Food security surveillance round 5 April 2018) .The health system is still contending with extensive damage and inadequate human resources as well as insufficient medical supplies to cater for the needs of the displaced population as well as those in the host communities to date the health system functionality is below 50%
Population movement within the northeast has been a key phenomenal with the majority arriving from the inaccessible areas has increased the burden on the existing nutrition services as this movements are associated with extreme needs as those IDPS arriving from these areas have not accessed humanitarian services. Movement have also been realized for those intending to move back to their LGA of origin to explore livelihood activities have also been reported.  This movements have been sporadic and have continued to put pressure on existing humanitarian services mostly affected including the nutrition sector as services providing SAM with medical complication have been inadequate. 
Acute malnutrition is often an outcome of poor food security, Health and poor child feeding and caring practices as well as other humanitarian services with chronic malnutrition thus the importance of involving multiple sectors in addressing malnutrition. The causes of malnutrition are complex and interconnected hence requiring intersectoral collaboration and integration with health agriculture social protection among others. An IRC Semi-Quantitative Evaluation of Access and Coverage survey (SQUEC) survey conducted by IRC between 5th to 23rd of March 2018 in 10 communities in MMC and Jere  estimated single coverage at 47.7 percent of existing needs (95 percent confidence interval between 38.7 and 56.9 percent coverage). This coverage is below the 70 percent Sphere minimum standard for urban settings
IRC has been present in North east as health and Nutrition actor since 2012 and an active member and co-lead in both sectors in the 3 north east states, As for nutrition programming IRC is currently supporting 22 OTP clinics and 1 stabilization centre in Adamawa state,22 mobile clinics in Borno state comprising of :12 mobile clinics in MMC and Jere,4 mobile clinics in Konduga, 4mobile clinics  in Monguno,10 health facility OTP in Askira Uba and also run the largest in-patient stabilization centres in Borno state(64 bed stabilization centres in MMC and Jere,10 bed capacity in Askira Uba. In addition IRC also Run 22 bed capacity stabilization centre in Gujba LGA and 12 OTP clinics in Yobe state. Each of the facilities are run by dedicated MOH and IRC staffs. IRC has expert medical Doctor who oversees all the SC’s and train SC staffs on clinical care for SAM children. The IRC expert Doctor also conducts and support WHO/UNICEF and other partners in training of staffs.In addition IRC has technical health and nutrition advisers who oversee the Quality of the CMAM and health programs. Nutrition Technical adviser visit the country after every 6 months and conduct Quality assessment and reviews the performance of the CMAM and IYCF activities

project_name: Emergency Response for Crisis-Affected persons in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa state, Nigeria
project_objective:
The Overall goal for this project is to improve the health and well being of approximately 110,000 internally displaced persons. 

The purpose of this project is protect people from water, sanitation and hygiene related diseases through provision of access to safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states. 

The IRC will work to improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene; through the construction and rehabilitation of water points, construction and rehabilitation of sanitation facilities, supply of WASH NFI's to vulnerable households and through hygiene messaging at IDP camps, host and returnee communities as well as in health centers, nutrition centers and schools. Working in health and nutrition centers will help improve the service delivery as well as provide a platform for sharing key hygiene messages to the patients and their care givers. Also households with severely malnourished children will be targeted for hygiene and water storage kits, which will be followed up with hygiene messaging in their homesteads.  

The IRC through the WASH sector, will also work closely with other partners to continue promoting menstrual hygiene management (MHM) in IDP camps as well as continue coordinating during emergency response such as cholera outbreaks.
  
In Yobe and Adamawa state, the IRC will focus it's WASH activities in schools, health and nutrition centers and also adopt long term recovery and development strategy in host communities. The IRC will build on current experience of establishing, training and working closely with community structures which include WASH Committees, School WASH clubs and Community health clubs to promote community ownership of installed water and sanitation projects. 

The IRC will continue to coordinate its activities with the WASH sector and work closely with the local and state level Ministry of water, Ministry of health and Ministry of education during the assessments, implementation and monitoring of its WASH projects.

project_name: Livelihood based Emeregncy Responses to conflict affected communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The main objective of the proposed action is to save lives, improve food and incomes security of households’ and increase their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks. 
The key interventions proposed through this action are cash/voucher assistances and market based agricultural inputs provisions and productions. The livelihoods support will help target beneficiaries in meeting lifesaving and immediate food needs and also contributing to agriculture productions and livelihoods diversifications and building disaster management capacity of vulnerable communities. The improved agricultural productions can increase the availability and affordability of nutritious food and hence improve dietary diversity to women and children. Combinations of food security and livelihoods support will help the target households to improve their food and nutrition status, build resilience and reduce vulnerability to malnutrition and other shocks. 
The proposed action will be implemented for 12 months in four States of South Sudan, specifically Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil East), Jonglei (Akobo, Bor South, Nyirol), Warrap ( Abyei Area) and Eastern Equatoria (Torit and Kapoeta North) targeting a total of 60,000 people.

project_name: Integrated Emergency nutrition response in Former Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria and Warrap States, South Sudan
project_objective:
This project will complement the nutrition cluster response objectives through implementation of emergency nutrition program mainly using four main intervention strategies: 1. Increase accessibility and Provision of quality nutrition treatment services, 2. Capacity building of the response team including CHD nutrition service providers. 3. Promote Protect and support of safe and appropriate feeding for infants and young children affected by the crises or emergency
4. Increased access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH, FSL and protection interventions/responses in all nine counties (Akobo, Bor, Nyirol, Magwi, Torit, Lopa Lafon, KN, KE and Abyei) in 96 Payams across the nine counties (the list of Payams is attached herein). The overall objectives of the project is to contributes to reduction of morbidity and mortality of under five children and PLW due to acute malnutrition in former Jonglei, EES and Warrap state through provision of timely and quality management of acute malnutrition, promotion of maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN) and integration of nutrition response with different sectors that includes WASH, Health FSL and protection.
The project will reach a total of 55,526 (12,404 U-5 SAM, 27,303 U-5 MAM, 15,819 MAM PLW)  acute malnourished  beneficiaries through management of acute malnutrition and MIYCN interventions which includes hygiene and sanitation promotion .The response will be focusing to achieve the following three results R.1. Children and PLW screed end detected and referred to appropriate nutrition centres. This will be done through active case finding using CNV/HHP, provision of acute managements of nutrition service trough 96 OTP and 94 TSFP static sites supplemented by RRM and mobile team to the area where service is not accessible.

project_name: Provision of Comprehensive quality Child Protection services for Un accompanied, Separated and other at risk children in South Sudan
project_objective: Strengthening Child Protection systems and provision of quality services through comprehensive case management, strengthening resilience of vulnerable conflict affected children in Akobo, Nyirol, Uror, Kapoeta East, Rumbek center, Kapoeta South, Kapoeta North, Torit, Lafon locations by December 2019.

project_name: To Support and Improve Health service delivery status  to IDPs and  vulnerable Communities of Bor, Twice East and Duk counties of Greater Jonglei.
project_objective: This Project seek to meet the emergency and Primary health care needs of vulnerable and Internally displaced population in three counties of greater Jonglei state, with focus on post conflict movements in Bor, Twic East and Duk counties. We seek meet significant gaps in affected areas targeting  29,434 beneficiaries in Bor, Twice and Duk Counties. Our focus will be on lives lifesaving, which translate to health, water & sanitation and food security. We will improve the health status of the IDPs through provision of effective and Equitable basic health services and emergency health care to support the ongoing and already affected primary health care services through mobile clinics and Establishing Primary Health Care package in form of Mobile, PHCU and PHCCs, Supporting the most vulnerable group of rural communities to have access to improved health services, Infrastructure and disease prevention and control. The Primary health care package & the emergency services include Ante-Natal care (ANC) maternal &Child health, Reproductive health. Expanded program on Immunization and curatives services in One hand, while the emergency component will focus on the disability, trauma, referral and GBV screening and management. The Psycho-social needs with Infrastructure rehabilitation components to improve and reopen the previously affected facilities in line with the security improvement.

project_name: Provision of integrated WASH priority needs of IDPs, host community and returnees in Central Equatoria, Jongolei and Unity.
project_objective: SPEDP proposes a 12 months project aiming at providing an equitable access to safe WASH services for internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities and returnees. It will integrate WASH in nutrition, health and GBV mitigation initiatives. The humanitarian situation in South Sudan still remains dire despite significant efforts made on the provision of humanitarian assistance since the conflict broke out on 15th December 2013. Several surveys and needs assessments conducted by partners and UN Agencies highlighted on the significant needs in WASH, nutrition, health and protection. This project targets 84,750 vulnerable people (18028men, 21167 women, 21318 boys and 26057girls) among IDPs, returnees and host communities in Central Equatoria, Jongolei and Unity with minimum WASH packages. The activities will focus on drilling, protection and rehabilitation of water points; construction and rehabilitation of institutional sanitation facilities; installation of hand washing facilities to promote hand washing; promotion of hygiene education through door to door visits, participatory hygiene sessions in public places and school children for effective behavioural change; distribution of hygiene kits to mothers and caretakers of children admitted for severe and moderate acute malnutrition (SAM/MAM) treatment at outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP)/SC. Menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits will be provided to adolescent girls and women of child bearing age accompanied with menstrual hygiene management sessions so that girls will not miss attending classes during their periods. All the WASH temporary and sustainable services will address the vital needs, public health and protection issues through anaccountability to affected populations (AAP) community approach to target the acute vulnerabilities based on inter/cross-sectoral evaluations and analyses. This project will focus on the various needs of men, women, boys and girls identified through focus group discussions (FGDs) with all the sex and age groups, people with disabilities and pregnant lactating mothers incorporating gender dynamics and specific needs of different groups into needs assessment and response recommendations. Throughout the project life cycle, SPEDP team will coordinate with the authorities, community and the key partners on ground who are implementing WASH, nutrition, health, and protection for integration of activities in order to avoid project overlap and duplication.
