project_name: Strengthening community resilience against GBV in Juba.
project_objective:
This project will be based in Juba and will benefit an estimated 25,000 people from both the internally displaced persons and the host communities comprising 10,000 women, 5,000 men, 5,000 girls and 5,000 boys. This project is expected to cost 350,000 USD. After the August 2018 displacement of IDPs from POC 3 in Juba, UNOCHA reported that over 7,000 IDPs displaced to Jonduru in Juba were adult women, adolescent girls, children and youth. And an estimated 18,000 inhabits the host communities.
An assessment conducted by STEWARDWOMEN in August 2018 highlighted the urgent need for livelihood support and GBV prevention and response services for IDP women and girls against incidences of sexual violence, primarily by armed actors. As such, a holistic GBV prevention/response is urgently needed, specifically for women, adolescent girls and female youths.
The project will provide life-saving GBV prevention and response and risk mitigation activities through the extension of existing protection interventions in Juba to ensure a holistic approach to addressing community GBV concerns for women, girls, boys and men through: (1) establishment of a static Women & Girl Friendly Space; (2) provision of integrated GBV prevention and response services; (3) provision of GBV case management services including focused PSS for survivors of GBV; (4) conducting legal awareness, assistance and counselling and provision of legal aid clinic assistance in Juba; (5) dissemination and support to the already existing referral pathway for Juba urban; (6) conducting protection awareness and GBV prevention through neighbourhood assemblies; (7) provision of IGA and livelihood support for persons of concern; (8) conducting prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience and; (9) provision of in-kind support to women, girls and youth to strengthen their resilience during displacement. 
We will ensure that all our activities take a “Do No Harm and conflict sensitive approach”. IDPs and local host communities will be targeted, as well as all other survivors and all those at risk of GBV.
STEWARDWOMEN is a women organisation and the only partner implementing a victim support group (UNDP) and FSL (NPA) interventions in Jondoru, Juba- Central Equatoria State (CES).
STEWARDWOMEN has a protection and economic empowerment team in place in Juba, as well as other protection interventions, and can meet the urgent and specific lifesaving and GBV prevention and response and risk mitigation needs of this project. 
In September 2018, STEWARDWOMEN held a meeting with IsraAid on the possibility of life-saving GBV prevention and response and risk mitigation intervention in Jonduru. This was followed by a community consultative meeting held with Jonduru community on the 7th September 2018.

project_name: Integrated Response to Life Threatening Malnutrition in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla counties, Jonglei State, South Sudan-2019
project_objective:
Hunger and malnutrition have increased persistently in South Sudan, with nearly 1.1 million children under age 5 estimated to be acutely malnourished and in need of life-saving services (HNO, Nov. 2017).  Admissions to Tearfund Feeding Centres continue to rise even in the post-harvest season when typically malnutrition rates dip as the dry season brings improved access for nutrition and health services as well as humanitarian assistance, and a reduction in morbidity and outbreaks of disease. With the rapid depletion of food stocks and subsequent early onset of the lean season the nutrition situation is expected to deteriorate with persistent food insecurity, outbreaks of diarrhea and other illnesses, poor Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and high morbidity, exacerbated by limited access to services during the seasonal rains. The GAM rate in Uror is currently 16.0 while the GAM rate in Twic East is 24.3 and in Pochalla it is  15.8- all above the WHO Emergency Threshold. 
The high levels of food insecurity seen among children under 5 in the targeted areas can be partially attributed to the scarcity of food and the consequent lack of variety in diet. This is further compounded by the lack of knowledge of minimum dietary diversity required.  Tearfund’s MIYCN component aims to address this issue through mothers groups both within the community and at the feeding centres. Furthermore, Tearfund’s wider nutrition programme contains a kitchen gardening component, in which the IYCF information in complemented by increasing access to more diverse food items. 
 Tearfund  will continue  implementation of a nutrition program in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla counties. Tearfund is currently responding to the crisis in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla, supporting 22 nutrition centers in total. This project will continue to address high rates of GAM through the provision of Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP) services, thus alleviating malnutrition and reducing susceptibility to other health issues, including water-borne diseases. As children under 5 and pregnant and lactating women and girls are the most vulnerable to MAM and SAM, these individuals will be the primary target group  for this intervention. A total of 3580 children under 5 will be targeted for treatment of SAM (100 Pochalla, 808 Twic East, 2671 Uror). A further 14963 children will be targeted for treatment of MAM (6817 Pochalla, 1406 Twic East, 6740 Uror).  As part of the MAM and IYCF component, a total of 9266 PLWs will be targeted (226 Pochalla, 3262 Twic East, 5777 Uror). 

Tearfund is the sole organization supporting nutrition interventions in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla, therefore without this response, GAM rates would inevitably rise and morbidity and mortality would increase.

project_name: Integrated WASH Response in Northern Bar el Ghazal and Jonglei States, South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed Project will be implemented in Uror and Twic East counties of Jonglei state and Aweil East and Centre of Northern Bar el Ghazal state. There are currently 67,344 IDPs in Northern Bahr el Ghazal NBeG), primarily because it provides a safe haven for those fleeing conflict in neighboring states ,while 50% of communities in Uror are hosting IDPs .  Uror and Twic East are predicted to remain at Crisis and Emergency levels (IPC 3 and 4) in January –March 2019, and would be likely one phase worse without humanitarian intervention.  Aweil East county is predicted to slip into Emergency levels (IPC 4) in the January –March 2019 period. Poor food security in all locations, coupled with poor WASH practices, is leading to high rates of global acute malnutrition, over WHO’s critical level of 15%.  The strong relationship between poor WASH infrastructure and practices, food insecurity and malnutrition is perpetuating high SAM and MAM rates. Use of unsafe drinking water and poor hygiene and sanitation practices are contributing to the high incidence of diarrhea and water-borne diseases in vulnerable communities, sustaining the malnutrition-diarrhea cycle and reducing the nutrient uptake in infants and young children. Tearfund will (1) Improve water supply infrastructure to increase access to safe drinking water and (2) Facilitate hygiene promotion throughout the targeted communities to encourage behavior change relating to hygiene and sanitation practices. The proposed action will enable Tearfund to continue providing critical services to the most vulnerable members in, including IDPs and host communities. Tearfund has a static presence throughout Jonglei and Northern Bar El Ghazal, with bases in Aweil East and Centre, Uror, Pochalla and Twic East and a sub-base in Yuai. The  proposed project is part of Tearfund’s wider programme, which integrates WASH, Nutrition and Food Security.

project_name: Provision and management  of core nutrition supplies  for timely emergency preparedness and response in South Sudan
project_objective: The findings of county level nutrition assessments conducted in 2018 reveal that 68 per cent of the 32 SMART surveys had global acute malnutrition (GAM) prevalence above the emergency threshold of 15 per cent. This signals a critical nutrition situation in South Sudan in 2019 which will require scale up in nutrition interventions by UNICEF and implementing partners. The purpose of this nutrition project is to support preventive and lifesaving nutrition interventions through treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM), provision of maternal infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN), capacity building and robust information systems in all the ten states of South Sudan including use of integrated rapid response mechanism (IRRM) modality to deliver nutrition services in the hardest to reach locations. UNICEF will also work closely with other sectors to deliver integrated nutrition sensitive interventions through an array of cross-sectoral linkages with education, health, water and sanitation, child protection interventions to contribute to reduction in stunting and acute malnutrition. In response to the humanitarian needs in South Sudan, UNICEF together with implementing partners plan to reach 984,701 pregnant women and caregivers of children below the age of 24 months and 220,680 children with SAM. The total cost of delivering UNICEF front line project is estimated to be USD 33,283,200 for a duration of twelve months.

project_name: Ensure livesaving emergency healthcare services that reduces major causes of morbidity and mortalities
project_objective:
Republic of South Sudan continued to be affected by complex emergencies resulting from prolonged conflict, broken health system, emergence of communicable diseases and climate change affecting livelihoods of the citizens. The signing of the Revitalised ARCISS on September 12 2018 is hoped to pave ways to provision of basic emergency services including healthcare services to the IDPs, host community and returnees who are in dire needs to access live saving emergency health services. This Project aim to address the major causes of morbidity and mortality through ensuring lifesaving emergency healthcare meeting 2019 HRP and health cluster objectives through mobile outreaches, RRM, and facility-based services deliveries. THESO has resolved to continue providing live saving emergency healthcare with dignity to IDPs, returnees and host community in 2019 following the humanitarian code of conducts across the country despite the documented high number of attacked on healthcare and extensive looting and damage of health infrastructure. 
Assessments made by The Health Support Organisation (THESO) and corroborated by other humanitarian agency reports  (UNICEF, IOM, and WHO) indicated that there is a big gap at reaching the IDPs, returnees and host communities both under government and opposition control areas in Panyikang, Mundri West, Twic East and Uror counties. Insufficient access to health, water, and sanitation services combined with gaps in livelihoods and food security brought major contributing factors towards the high prevalence rate of malnutrition in the area  and malnutrition associated illness (e.g. ARI, Measles, Diarrhoea and Malaria). The weekly IDSR reports and monthly HMIS reports shows increase in prevalence of endemic and communicable disease such as malaria, measles, and Hepatitis E in various location such as Mayom, Rubkona, Yirol East, Fangak, Aweil. (WHO). There is doubt in having sustainable funding for health facilities in Twic East and Panyikang counties in 2019, and will not cover all health facilities if funded RRHP 2018). Moreover, presence of increased number of returnees and Internally Displaced Peoples (IDPs) from North Sudan, Ethiopia, and Uganda to Panyikang, Mundri West, Uror and Twic East Counties can contribute for occurrence of emerging and re-emerging diseases due to breakdown in immunisation services and weak diseases prevention and promotion services.
The effect of South Sudanese poor health situation increasingly contributed for recurrent occurrence of morbidity, mortality and sufferings among vulnerable people in under 5 children and pregnant and lactating mothers continue to be unacceptably high. A high proportion of childhood mortality is rooted in malnutrition which is the underlying cause of death for neonatal, pneumonia, malaria, diarrhoea, and measles related cases. South Sudan is acknowledged to have some of the worst health indicators in the world.  The under-five  mortality rate is 135 per 1,000 live births, whilst maternal mortality ratio is the highest in the world at 2,054 per 100,000 live births (SSHS 2006).

THESO in South Sudan, in collaboration with the Government structures at State and County level, are responding to these primary health care activities through delivery of static and mobile health service to identified returnees, host community and internally displaced persons.  In recent years, THESO has been at the forefront of the development and implementation of live saving emergency primary health care  through static, mobile outreaches and rapid response mechanism approaches  in Twic East, Nyirol, Uror, Bor South, Ikotos, Magwi, Morobo, Kajo Keji, Lainya, Tonj North, Gogrial East, Abyei, Guit, Koch and Pariang Counties; these programmes strategic approaches will be used to provide live saving emergency healthcare services to the IDPs, returnees and host communities in dire needs of humanitarian assistance in Panyikang, Mundri West, Uror and Twic East Counties.

project_name: Emmergency Life saving health services to IDPS, Host communities & Returnees in Kajo-Keji, Yei, Morabo and Magwi counties
project_objective:
This project is expected to mobilize 984,129 United States dollars to provide emergency lifesaving health services for 16,393 IDPs, Host communities & returnees in Kajo-Keji, Yei, Morobo and Magwi counties over a period of 1 year. The locations targeted are mapped as Ebola risk counties due to the outbreak of Ebola in Neighboring Congo. These areas are still experiencing active fighting despite the peace agreement. As a result of the conflict, a total of 85, 621 people are displaced; 66,326 in Yei, 6925 in Morobo, 5855 in Kajo-Keji and 7145 in Magwi (Health cluster, PIN 2019). While environmental conditions are ripe for vector growth and disease transmission, there are inadequate health services due to lack of trained health personnel, functional health facilities and increased attacks on health care increasing the potential for disease outbreaks.
The proposed intervention is expected to provide lifesaving health care to the IDPS and host community by implementing essential primary healthcare emergency clinical packages targeting the most vulnerable displaced populations (PHCU, PHCC& Mobile teams), immunizing the most vulnerable displaced groups (Children U5,PLW), Implementing outbreak investigation and response (IDSR) and  Mainstreaming Accountability to Affected People. Five thousand four hundred and thirty four (5434) IDPS & Host community in Yei, 3,809 in Morobo, 3220 in Kajo-Keji and 3930 IDPs, Host communities & Returnees in Magwi will be targeted.

project_name: Provision of timely live saving WASH services to the most vulnerable communities affected by conflict to Reduce water bone diseases that leads to public hazards cholera and severe acute malnutrition
project_objective:
The Rescue Mission (TERM) will conduct life-saving WASH activities aimed at meeting the critical WASH needs of vulnerable people in South Sudan affected by conflict, natural disasters, disease outbreaks, and areas of high malnutrition rates. 
This project aims at providing timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water to vulnerable and IDPs, and conflict affected populations, cholera hotspots and mitigating GBV resulting from inadequate WASH services increase knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases targeting IDP’s, host and the returnees. Interventions will include safe water provision through water point rehabilitation (hand pumps, Water yards water quality monitoring and treatment of contaminated water source, provision of household water filters, depending on the needs); provision or rehabilitation of sanitation infrastructure (latrines, hand washing facilities and solid waste management); hygiene promotion (hand washing campaigns in communities and institutions, safe water chain and jerrycan cleaning campaigns); capacity-building of community institutions (pump mechanics, water user committees, community hygiene promoters, school's hygiene clubs), and distribution of WASH NFIs (soap, hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene kit, water containers, water purification filters, PUR or others).
Total targeted group is 30,000 beneficiaries. The project will target communities with poor access to safe water supply, unsafe sanitation and hygiene practices, poor sanitation coverage and support nutrition, health and education centers with WASH facilities (i.e. GAM rates of more than 27%).

The intervention will include detailed needs assessment to identify the needs, affected gender, age and diversity groups, the vulnerabilities of the targeted community and coping strategies employed by the affected population. Based on the assessment report, interventions will be designed accordingly with TERM capacity, response with other partners will be planned. The main priority is to provide timely WASH response necessary to reduce morbidity and mortality caused by WASH related diseases and limited access to water.  

TERM will focus on supporting other sectors as Health, Nutrition, Education with WASH facilities like soap, hand washing facilities, improvement of waste management facilities, access to latrines and capacity building of community health, nutrition workers on WASH related disease preventive measures among others. 
Centralizing protection to promote principled access to basic services for the displaced and other vulnerable groups at risk, accountability to affected people and addressing and mitigating GBV risk resulting from WASH related needs . TERM will implement capacity building of the community to reinforce coping mechanism to manage current shocks and sustain livelihoods, strengthen linkages with development action to support resilience.

project_name: Providing Emergency Life-saving ES/NFIs for Conflict Affected Vulnerable  populations in Kajo-Keji, Lainya and Yei, in CES and Magwi and Lafon in EES of South Sudan
project_objective:
This project aims at providing lifesaving shelter and NFI items to the most vulnerable newly displaced IDPS, refugees, returnees and host communities in Kajo Keji, Yei, Lainya, of central equatoria state and Magwi and Lafon counties of Eastern equatoria state. These populations that consists of the IDPS and host communities have been experiencing a confluence of consistent clashes between warring parties in the country especially the most recent which was between September and October 2018 in yei and Lainya which had spill overs into kajokeji leading to displacements into the korijo idp settlements in liwolo payam in western kajokeji. the recent idps who fled the crises from mukaya,Lainya and some parts of yei and sokare in liwolo payam  were forced to settle in korijo which is the newest idp settlement in kajokeji. This report was verified through an Irna conducted on the 18/10/2018 by Titi foundation teams and partners operating in kajokeji. Given that this areas where titi foundation operates as a static partner in, are also close to the border of Uganda, Kenya and DR.Congo we have experienced an inflow of mainly returnees and some refugees into areas like kajokeji through the moyo and mijale points, magwi  and Lafon through lobone from Uganda and yei where the returnees are hailing from Uganda and DR.Congo escaping the harsh conditions in the  various refugee camps in search for  better living conditions in south sudan.  These locations have not just been experiencing the effects of war alone but also in the 2018 september –october IPC released results we have seen that areas like kajokeji have been classified in phase 4 and the other locations between phase 3-4 which depicts emergency situation and depicting the high need for an intervention in various sectors including shelter/nfi.These areas have also been unique in that politically they are controlled by both IG and IO parties especially locations like kajokeji, Lainya and partially yei  in central equatoria which has also to a greater extent escalated the suffering of the populations in this areas.
Its in this regard and background therefore that Titi foundation has identified through information gathered from sources like iom DTM,REACH SURVEYS and the recently just concluded IRNA as of 18/10/2018  that the population in some locations like Korijo in kajokeji is hosting a total population of 40294 newly displaced idps and hence the huge Shelter and NFI needs for vulnerable populations in these locations (according to the October/18/2018 IRNA report). With Titi foundation as the only shelter/nfi partner that has demonstrated the ability and competence to deliver s/nfi assistance to the most vulnerable populations in this hard to reach areas like kajokeji where we just recently concluded some assistance to nearly 766 households. Titi also has an advanatage over other partners in that we have existing agreements with URA(Uganda revenue authority) to use Uganda routes to deliver services to border areas like kajokeji, morobo, and magwi through its territories during our project implementation process and hence curbing the problem related to access.
Titi foundation in its planned intervention will distribute inkind s/nfi items like blankets, plastic sheet mosquito nets, kitchen sets, sleeping mats to beneficiaries which will improve both their living conditions and access to emergency shelter which will protect the displaced persons from harsh weather conditions and protection risks, support the communities in an integrated and dignied manner by using locally available materials to support livelihoods through skills training. The shelter and NFI items that will be distributed to beneficiaries will also contribute to improvement of their health, enhance protection and better hygiene through a multi-sectoral survival kit distribution. The purpose of the project is also to engage the community in a way that stimulates active participation hence increasing their ability to respond to new shocks and build on existing skills. The project will also ensure quality monitoring services which will foster fast life saving response to the right beneficiaries, enhance the ability to use S/NFIs for supporting results based health, protection, livelihood, and hygiene needs, and really to improve understanding of trends in order to reduce overlap and reach the truly vulnerable populations who can’t help themselves. 
Titi foundation which already has office spaces and implementing  ongoing projects like FSL, GBV and protection activities in all this locations will mainstream its activities like the ongoing fuel efficient stoves and briquettes program which is aimed at mitigating gender based violence will be mainstreamed to our planned s/nfi interventions to ensure that the beneficiaries will also be trained along the (FES) project to reduce on the possibility of gender based violence that they could face. Titi will also blend ongoing projects like child protection especially to our s/nfi beneficiary category such as child headed households and people living with disabilities to acquire psychosocial support (pss) by involving our specialized staffs from the various sectors to assist our s/nfi beneficiaries acquire our extra services.
Titi Foundation will target 25000 (5500 household) most affected vulnerable people with distribution of s/nfi kits, upgrading or repairing of substandard shelters and will explore the targeted beneficiaries on relevant and environmentally friendly emergency shelter materials to reduce costs of construction and improve shelter conditions based on content.

project_name: Provision of Emergency integrated mobile health interventions to vulnerable and affected populations in Magwi and Nasir Counties
project_objective:
South Sudan has been in political conflict since December 2013. This conflict has seen immerse suffering to the people of South Sudan and great humanitarian crisis. There has been mass displacement of populations and according to UNHCR there are over 3.1 million people who have sought refuge to the neighboring countries.
This crisis has greatly hit the health sector and affected service delivery to the people of South Sudan. Magwi County has been largely affected by the crisis especially after the June 2016 fighting which spread rapidly to areas that were relatively calm. Mass displacement of the populations and destruction of infrastructure was witnessed. 
The signing of the peace agreement between the warring parties on 12th June 2018 in Addis Ababa Ethiopia has seen relative calm return in the country and has also seen influx of returnees from the neighboring countries and from the IDP camps.
This therefore calls for integrated humanitarian response in the county. There is risk of disease outbreaks since the county is a bordering Uganda and the movement of populations to and from the county increases the risk of outbreaks. In February 2018, a suspected meningitis outbreak was reported in Torit County, which borders Magwi County, and it claimed lives of 15 people and affected around 34 others (WHO meningitis Sit rep, 2018 March). It is therefore prudent to have integrated health interventions in the county to avert such outbreaks.
Due to the ongoing Ebola Virus outbreak in democratic republic of Congo, Magwi County remains a very high risk County and therefore needs more attention and high community sensitization to evert possible Ebola outbreak in the county.
Nasir County in Upper Nile State has also been greatly affected by the humanitarian crisis which hit the county since 2018. Immunization services have not been offered in this county for the last 5 years according to the county health Department. This has been partly due to the unavailability of cold chain facilities and closure of health facilities who could offer essential healthcare and routine immunization services.
This being a border county also, there is increased chances of disease outbreak and therefore increasing the infant mortality and morbidity rates.
This project therefore wishes to address the health challenges in these two counties by supporting primary health care units and having two mobile health clinics in each county to offer integrated health services to the vulnerable and affected populations. 
The projects also wishes to improve response to outbreaks by timely reporting and investigating suspected disease outbreaks within 48 hours in order to avert possible spread of outbreak prone diseases. 
The project will also integrate WASH messages to the communities in order to avert diseases related to poor sanitation conditions like cholera and acute watery diarrhea.
Screening of cases of malnutrition and referring them to the OTP and stabilization centers will be done in order to help reduce cases of malnutrition in the counties and also help reduce mortality and morbidity rates caused by acute malnutrition.
IDSR and EWARS reports will be sent on time to the Ministry of Health and the health cluster to help them plan well for health services in the county monitor disease trends and help respond to possible disease outbreaks.
All funds received will be reported to the financial tracking system in order to inform the cluster of the funding gaps for proper resource mobilization in order to improve health service delivery.

project_name: Livelihood Support to Conflict Affected Communities in Greater Upper Nile and Western Equatoria
project_objective: The project involves provision of training, mentoring and livelihood kits to conflict, drought and flood affected communities  in Greater Upper Nile (Pigi Canal, Old Fangak, Ulang) and Western Equatoria ( Mundri East, Mundri West and Mvolo). The support will target 10000 returnees, internally displaced persons and vulnerable host households ( 60000 individuals) in Western Equatoria ( 4000 households) and 6000 households in Greater Upper Nile. The intervention is designed to bridge the trajectory from relief to early recovery through revitalization of existing and establishment of new agriculture activities. Supported with training on agriculture and protection, the project seeks to strengthen beneficiaries' resilience to cope with natural ( droughts, floods) and man made disasters (conflict) thereby, reducing their exposure to risk and negative coping strategies.  Project activities have been designed to mitigate risks to beneficiaries by ensuring that input distribution is done on time and at various distribution sites. The project will seek to integrate livelihood and education through promotion of the establishment of school based vegetable gardens.

project_name: Integrated WASH response to returnees, IDPs and host communities in Unity State and Mundri of Western Equatoria South Sudan
project_objective:
Mercy Corps proposes to implement a 12-months project to carry on and build up current lifesaving water, sanitation and hygiene services for returnees, host and IDPs communities in Unity State and Western Equatoria.  The program aims to reach a total of 120,829 individuals in Unity (70,829) and Mundri East (50,000). 
The goal of the program will be to ensure access to clean water, access to sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion (including NFI distribution) and enhancements to environmental health conditions. The intensified package will implement comprehensive hygiene behavior-change components, robust integration with health and nutrition interventions, and fully streamlined gender and protection needs as identified via implementation of current OFDA  and UNICEF funding and protection partners.
The main components of the program will be:
Provision of adequate safe clean water supply to households and community structures through ensuring access to water infrastructures that include rehabilitation of broken/damaged boreholes and drilling of new boreholes with rigorous water quality testing.
Provision of dignified sanitation infrastructure using community participation strategy to host communities and returnees and construction of semi-permanent structures for IDPs will be implored with tailored designs for people with disabilities/older adults and children.  
Extended, all-inclusive hygiene promotion with a focus on behaviour change interventions and menstrual hygiene and NFI distributions that address acute basic needs and facilitate individual ownership of personal and community health and well-being.
Health, nutrition, food security, and WASH integration to mitigate WASH-related illness and morbidity and malnutrition rates via referral tracking systems and integrated outbreak response planning. Coordination with Health, Nutrition and Protection clusters to ensure an integrated timely response to any need. Mainstreaming of Menstruation Hygiene Management among school going children with an aim to increase school enrolment among girls.

project_name: Increase access to primary health care services focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality for vulnerable populations in Unity and Jonglei States (Bentiu PoC and Fangak county)
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to increase access to primary health care service by supporting existing health facilities raising their capacities of management, human resources, infrastructure, materials and medical equipment. WRSS will continue to provide support to health facilities in Fangak County and in Sector 2 of Bentiu PoC camp. WRSS supports the involvement of communities, prioritize community outreach and discussions in the aim to design and implement more strong and sustainable health programs.

While focusing on primary health care package, there will be a strong need to integrate relevant crosscutting interventions such SGBV, gender and other protection mainstreams. WRSS will support community education and promotion activities by increasing awareness on infectious and preventable diseases. Community services are led through a strong network of volunteers and home health promoters who organize frequent home visits and who disseminate preventive messages.  By implementing IMCI programs, WRSS prioritizes the health of the children under five. To implement EPI programs and to link with vaccine supplying Core pipelines will be a key component to ensure children are immunized. Maternal and Child health care programming is a key component to ensure safe, comprehensive and integrated reproductive health and to ensure women receive adequate and high quality obstetric and neonatal care.

The provision of essential drugs and medical supplies will play a major role to support the recon structuring health system, and the integration of WASH activities and the implementation of waste management mechanisms will also be prioritized for this project. Trainings sessions will be organized for health officials to slowly build up more accountable and sustainable systems and WRSS will also train health professionals and will organize supervisions to ensure health services are adequately provided. There is a strong need to scale up activities and to include the care for NCDs and to ensure HIV/AIDS-TB patient receive adequate services and are fully supported. (Psychosocial, nutrition...). All these activities will be implemented following actual national protocols, guidelines and strategies and WRSS will maintain strong referral mechanisms in all its programs.

project_name: Scaling up  Integrated Nutrition services to conflict most affected  and vulnerable population of children age 6-59 months ,pregnant and lactating women (PLW) in Mayendit,Panyjiar and Leer counties in Unity state
project_objective:
Malnutrition situation in Unity state in Mayendit, Leer and panyijar continues to be a major concern showing localized pockets of humanitarian needs which are being attributed to severe food insecurity , poor access to health nutrition services ,extremely poor diets and poor sanitation and hygiene. According to the September 2018 – March 2019 IPC project analysis   its places Mayendit and leer at phase 5 with GAM (WHZ) 15.0- 29.9 while panyijar is at phase 4 with nutrition cluster fortnight monitoring showing panyijal among the counties with GAM 16.2,MAM 18.9 and prevalence of 35.2 to PLW. Thus in this project  UNIDOR seek to  continue in providing live saving support to the conflict affected and most vulnerable population,Targeting children age 6- 59 months, Pregnant and lactating mothers and people with disabilities through the provision of integrated nutrition services to the needy population.The project will provide treatment and rehabilitation to children suffering from severe acute malnutrition( SAM) 1198 in leer, 3496 in panyijar and 4496 in mayendit and moderate acute malnutrition(MAM) Leer 2862,5008 panyijar and 6440 mayendit and treatment of 230 girls and 220 boys severely malnourished children with medical complication in the 2 SC in mayendit and treatment of 8000 PLW in the respective counties  and will also provide linkages and referral within the programs like Health,WASH ,Protection/GBV and FSL through referrals and provision of key interventions with the programs i.e OTP,TSFP and SC.UNIDOR will ensure  that there is integration of Early childhood Development at every OTP/TSFP facilities so as to ensure there are friendly spaces for stimulation for the U5 children .  
there will be a strong component of surveillance through continuous program monitoring that will also include SMART surveys and Mass MUAC screening. Routine community mobilization and sensitization, active case finding, referrals and follow ups at the household level will be done to strengthen all the components with key nutrition practices ,hygiene and promotion and the MIYCN practices.
The main objective of this project is to ensure: 1,Timely,quality and quantity lifesaving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at risk children boys and girls under five years of age and pregnant and lactating mothers by reaching at least 80% of SAM, 62% of MAM and 53 % of PLW in Mayendit, Panyijar and Leer counties.2, Increased integration of Nutrition with Health, WASH, GBV and FSL activities in mayendit , panyijar and leer in line with the cluster objective 3, Increased access to Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition preventing under nutrition to the vulnerable and at risk in mayendit , panyijar and leer counties4, continuous nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and utilization of early warning information for timely coordination response and decision making and ensure we report to the cluster and taking part in assessments and surveys 
UNIDOR will continue with nutrition activities for instance community nutrition assessment through community screening, treatment of MAM and SAM U5 children ,Reaching mothers with MIYCN messages , conducting CMAM training to health workers , screening and testing for malaria for U5 children ,RDT trainings to the health workers, de-worming of children 12-59 months twice a year, Vitamin A supplementation to children 6-59 years twice a year and Intergration of Early Child Development with Nutrition services

project_name: Provision of critical child protection services to 30,000 conflicted affected populations in Leer,Mayendit and Koch Counties.
project_objective:
In response to the growing humanitarian crisis in South Sudan, UNIDOR is proposing to enhance the provision of critical child protection services to 30,000 vulnerable populations in Unity State, covering Koch, Leer and Mayendit. These areas were selected based on the needs assessment that revealed that the needs were severe and the fact that UNIDOR already has running projects in the areas. 

The proposed one year’ emergency intervention is designed to :i) support extremely vulnerable, children including unaccompanied and separated children through individual case management ii) identify and register unaccompanied and separated children and ensuring that they are reunified with their parents/caregivers ii)provide psycho social support to conflict distressed children through structured gender disaggregated games and activities at child friendly spaces, community based and school based PSS. iii)Raising awareness on child protection risks on landmines and ERWs in schools and communities and iv) integrating child protection monitoring and mainstreaming into the protection intervention to improve the overall context analysis to respond to the identified needs and enhancing the understanding and analysis among humanitarian actors on the child protection context and needs. 

UNIDOR will also integrate child protection into the already existing UNIDO Nutrition, WASH, FSL and Health programs in Leer, Mayendit and Koch counties. The already existing Community Based Child Protection Networks (CBCPN) will be trained to provide a platform for the identification of and response to child protection concerns, the development of community-based mitigation plan, prevention of separation messaging on FTR, forced recruitment , early marriage and child protection surveillance mechanism.  CBCPN will also identify and refer vulnerable children in need of individual support. UNIDOR will also operate three safe healing and learning spaces for children that facilitate their recovery, restore a sense of normalcy, and promote their cognitive, physical, social and emotional development and provide parenting support.

Youth engagement to provide peer support, recreational activities and referrals to FSL programming will also serve as an entry point to develop future interventions with Children Associated with Armed Groups and Armed Forces. An ongoing monitoring and reporting of grave violations and collaboration with local authorities will be needed to prevent children from being recruited into the armed forces and armed groups.
.
Through the child protection program, UNIDOR intends to work with the Nutrition program and teams to identify unaccompanied and separated children including children living within vulnerable families that affect their care and nutritional well being and refer them for Nutrition screening and support. UNIDOR Nutrition team will then provide support the identified children to ensure continuity of care and support at home within the family setting. The CP team will provide follow up support to malnourished children receiving support within the family environment. Complementary funding supports over 150 caregivers in providing appropriate, positive care for children. This project will also support population within the communities, host and IDPs with awareness messages and other community level support services such as WASH, Health and food through static and community outreach.
UNIDOR is the only agency providing child protection services in Leer,Mayendit and Koch,hence there is no likelihood or possibility of duplication of services.

project_name: Addressing acute Water, Sanitation and Hygiene needs of conflict affected communities through an integrated intervention in Nutrition and GBV streamlining in Leer, Koch, Panyijiar and Mayendit North Counties in Unity State
project_objective: The WASH situation in Leer, Koch, Panyinjiar and Mayendit Counties are really demanding due to the impact of clashes and war experienced in some parts of the region in the past. Most of the existing WASH infrastructure were destroyed and now the hosts, returnees and the IDPs in these locations are in dire need of WASH services. The WASH project will address acute water shortages by rehabilitating water points and developing protected hand dug wells so that the population will access safe and adequate amount of water for drinking and other domestic uses. The rehabilitation, construction and repairs will be done after a GBV risk analysis have been conducted in the focus groups discussion with women and girls, conducted by female staff on the safety and best location to access safe equitable and sustainable water source and thus reducing cases of GBV and risk of sexual exploitation of women and girls since they are the primary beneficiary. The OTP/TSFP nutrition sites and PHCC/PHCU health facilities will be prioritized so that the children with SAM/MAM cases will not be left behind as part of the integration. The project will also ensure the vulnerable communities of Leer, Koch, Panyijiar and Mayendit Counties access improved sanitation services through rehabilitation of latrines in the safe agreed locations after discussions and consultations in the FGDs and the latrines will have locks to enhance privacy, dignity and security and hence reducing the risk of exploitation, such as sexual exploitation and abuse. The communities will also be taught by WASH staffs and Nutrition/Health staffs (trained on WASH minimum package) on how to improve hygiene situation through hygiene creation awareness campaigns with emphasis on hand-washing with soap at critical times, safe disposal of human wastes,  treatment and storage of drinking water to prevent occurrence and transmission of Cholera and other water borne diseases.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency Lifesaving Healthcare Services for Most Vulnerable populations of Jonglei State
project_objective:
According to the South Sudan health cluster report (2019 HNO released in October 2018), it is estimated that 4,058,392 South Sudanese women, men and children will need humanitarian healthcare services in 2019 and of which 829,949 in Jonglei State accounting to 20.4% and number estimated for Pibor and Twic East counties stand at 70,489 and 54,521 respectively. Due to high disease burden resulting from endemic, epidemic, pandemic and neglected diseases the population targeted for 2019 humanitarian healthcare services is 2,272,700 and of which 464,435 (20.4%) is for Jonglei and 39,474 and 30,532 for Pibor and Twic East Counties respectively. The health needs for Jonglei is as huge as the state has suffered a significant destruction and displacement during the armed conflict between Juba government and opposition forces in the past five years.
The Rapid Results Health Project (RRHP) with financial support from World Bank for Jonglei and Upper Nile is facing significant financial gaps, 211 out of 318 facilities are now being supported and no real surety for continuity in 2019 (RRHP 2018). From the September 28, 2018 released IPC result by South Sudan Bureau of Statistics, 65.2% of Jonglei will be IPC phase 3, 4 and 5 in January to March 2019 and Pibor and Twic East Counties in IPC phase 4.
United Networks for Health response focuses mainly in Pibor and Twic East Counties of Jonglei State. These counties are hard to reach, very vast, prone to floods and displacement due to inter-clan and tribal conflicts. Twick East is now managed by the County Health Department that has limited capacity, no health partner and most services are concentrated at county headquarter with no adequate lifesaving health services for the vulnerable populations in dire needs. Former Pibor County is so vast with poor transport networks and difficult to access during rainy season. Most of the vulnerable population live in the rural (very hard to reach) areas with no access to lifesaving healthcare services, EPI coverage is limited only in Pibor headquarter and Boma health facility. UNH has a strong networks in Pibor and Twic East and will work together with the County Health Departments, health partners on the ground and other clusters (nutrition, protection and food security) to ensure synergies. UNH will scale up response and increase access through establishing 2 mobile clinics (1 in Pibor and 1 in Twic East), strengthening and supporting 2 primary health care centers (1 in Pibor and 1 in Twic East), 1 primary health care unit in Pibor. The response will targets the IDPs and vulnerable host communities; women/men and girls/boys of all age groups without discrimination in the two counties; 10,000 beneficiaries (5,645 in Pibor and 4,355 in Twic East) will receive healthcare services of which 2,560 IDPs and 7,440 vulnerable host communities. Generally the whole community in the catchment areas will benefit from the response directly and indirectly.

project_name: Increasing access and strengthening capacities of PHC to provide emergency lifesaving health care services in Leer, Mayendit, Koch and Panyijar counties through the provision of 7 mobile units, 6 PHCUs, 2 RRMs and 2 PHCCs for Integrated response.
project_objective:
This project is aiming at increasing access and strengthening capacity of PHC to provide emergency lifesaving health care in Leer, Mayendit, Koch and Panyijiar Counties through the provision of mobile response, PHCUs, RRMs and PHCCs with integrated responses. After the cessation of the most deadly attack to Mayendit north and Leer County between April to July 2018, the security situation has been relatively calmed in southern unity, however due to the massive displacement caused by April fighting, the local community lost more times in preparing and planting their farms, hence there was poor or no harvest in 2018, and for this reason, southern unity is expected to face a serious starvation which will lead to malnutrition increasing chances of morbidity and mortality rates in 2019. This project proposal will be targeting beneficiaries of 20, 627 individuals in Leer, 20,627 in Mayendit, 5,157 in Koch and 5,156 in Panyijiar counties. 
This project will benefit all gender groups including, 28,599 men, 30,982 women, 33,564 girls and 30,982 boys across all the project catchment Counties. 
Predictions from IPC findings show that 8 counties which include Leer and Mayendit may go into catastrophic levels which might further trigger diseases.
A SMART Survey conducted by UNIDO in Nov 2017 reported GAM rate at 17.9% and SAM at 3.5% in Mayendit county, while in a reference made to SCF SMART Survey conduct in April 2017 shows a prevalence of malnutrition rates among children in Leer county is high – estimated GAM prevalence of 20.1% (15.6-25.5 95% C.I.) and SAM of prevalence of 5.0% (3.2- 7.7 95% C.I.) based on weight-for-height/WFH z-score; this is alarming and classified as ‘Critical’. IDSR report of week 30 in Aug 2018 indicated a proportional morbidity at 67.9% for malaria, AWD, 9.3% and ARI with 8.8% while the same diseases are also leading in mortality rate, malaria with 55.6%, AWD 14.0% and ARI with 12.8% across the Country. UNIDO report on EWARS in the IDP site at Leer TPA has always shown a 100% in health cluster weekly IDSR report. The routine EPI services in Koch, Nyal and Leer TPA is progressing well with Penta3 coverage of  84 in Koch PHCC. Although due to insecurity, the entire County of Mayendit, most payams in Leer and Koch County are not benefiting yet from both routine and outreach EPI services. The provision of this primary health care service shall include OPD curative consultation in 7 mobile sites, 6 PHCUs, 2 RRMs and 2 PHCCs with integrated responses. The Seven mobile sites are Meer island, Tuochriak island, Tuochnhialchang island (in Leer County) Dhorleak and Dongol island (in Mayndit County), Gany and Gony (in Koch County) while the static sites are Bow, Dindin and Pillieny, (in Leer County) Pabuong and Dablual, (in Mayendit County) Duong and Majak (in greater Nyal of Panyijiar County). The project will support one stabilization center at Mayendit PHCC to treat SAM cases with medical complications. We will also support the psycho social and basic mental health services through updating/on-job training targeting nurses, midwives and clinicians on clinical management of sexual violence using SGBV treatment protocol and to offer the first aid such as protection and care for the survivors.

project_name: Support Humanitarian Services by Promoting Public Recognition and Local Feedback Mechanism in Nasir and Pochalla County, 2019.
project_objective: In light of the context, there is need to relook at the issue of revenge killing from a critical perspective through a comprehensive assessment and inform a conceptual framework on how to use CwC approaches to strengthen community recognition of humanitarian work, and commitment to upholding the safety and security of aid workers, including by providing a feedback mechanism platform that is relevant, feasible and sustainable for both humanitarian actors and the local community. This will enable the community to voice their opinions, as well as to better appreciate and understand the impact of revenge killings on humanitarian action, thereby promoting mutual respect between the community and aid workers and helping to increase partners’ confidence and a safe environment for the provision of humanitarian services. A total of 30,000 beneficiaries mostly from host communities & local leaders will be targeted of which (14,700 Male & 15,300 female) as beneficiaries.

project_name: Providing critical lifesaving assistance & strengthening copying mechanisms for vulnerable communities in Nasir, Longechuk and Ulang Counties in 2019
project_objective:
The proposed twelve (12) months project will be implemented in Upper Nile state targeting 15,000 HHs (5,000 Beneficiaries per each County) of Longechuk, Ulang and Nasir which is in crisis due to insecurity, yearly flooding, drought and where the farming practices among the predominantly peasantry community are very poor culminating in to problems of food insecurity, poverty and environmental degradation. 
UNKEA intends to support the affected communities of Three Counties (IDPs, returnees, Hosts, Disabled, HIV/AIDS Patients, gender based violence (GBV) survivals, women headed households) with agriculture inputs (seeds and fishing kits and implementing technical guidance training to vulnerable communities including Beneficiary selection, registration and Verification. 
UNKEA through the donor support will distribute livelihood inputs to 15,000 beneficiaries including boys and girls of 15 to 18 years who will be provided with agriculture inputs (seeds & Tools and fishing kits) support in the project area.
UNKEA will carry out the following activities; mobilization and sensitization of community through dialogue in the project area to create awareness of what project activities to be implemented, time frame and importance of the project to the community, identification and registration of beneficiaries, securing the agricultural inputs from the pipe line (FAO) and delivery to the distribution points, distribution of agriculture inputs to ensure access to agriculture inputs by the most vulnerable groups as a start-up package for increased crop production, Technical guidance/training on use of recession irrigation in vegetable production during dry season, technical guidance on agronomic practices including sustainable agricultural land use practices, environmental awareness, HIV/AIDS advocacy and mainstreaming including gender based violence (GBV), activities. 
The community where this project will be implemented will be identified through consulting the local authorities and other stake holders on ground on the most vulnerable groups (IDPS, Women headed Household, child headed household, disabled, gender based violence (GBV) survivals and chronically sick) who will be prioritized in the selection.

2 Environmental awareness sessions held to 1500 women and 1000 men in all project locations. 12500 women and 750 men technically guided on sustainable agronomic practices in crop production and have planted their seeds.

project_name: Community emergency nutrition services to IDPs, Returnees, and host population in Nasir and Ulang counties, Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
Socioeconomic situations in both Ulang and Nasir have remained dire since 2013, with various escalations of security situations last in March 2018 which resulted in population displacements. With return of calm and continued clashes in other counties, Ulang and Nasir have hosted over 40,000 IDPs. This situation is worsened by natural disasters such as flooding, drought and diseases, leading to increase in suffering and displacements of the already vulnerable populations. This is demonstrated in the high GAM rates for both counties i.e. 21.8% and 20.1% for Ulang and Nasir respectively.
UNKEA operates only 28 OTP sites (14 per county) and 2 SC in Nasir to serve a population of 288,704 and 95,880 in Nasir and Ulang respectively. This is inadequate and UNKEA intends to increase to 34 OTP sites. OTP sites do not provide much needed WASH and FSL services that would improve the well-being of children and women. 
UNKEA will scale up service provision by providing the most critical interventions such as Treatment of SAM among children 6 – 59 months (2,540 targeted); Treatment of MAM among children 6 – 59 months (6,994 targeted); Treatment of 2,546 PLWs with MAM; Training 34 health and nutrition workers on CMAM; Training 34 Nutrition and Health workers on IYCF/MIYCN counselling; Conduct individual IYCF/MIYCN counselling for PLWs and caregivers of children 0 - <23 months; Provide Nutrition education session to IYCF/MIYCN support groups in the community; Monitor availability of nutrition supplies at nutrition sites; Establish demonstration gardens at all nutrition sites for on-site dietary diversity demonstration; Screening/testing and treatment of all SAM children in the OTP sites for Malaria; Conduct safety assessment at nutrition sites to identify and address women and children’s protection and safety needs including GBV referral path ways; Provide WASH kits to children with SAM in all OTP sites; Establish child/mother friendly spaces in all (34) OTP/TSFP sites; and Provide ECD kits for all OTP sites to enhance mental and physical development of children in the programme. 
The project will be implemented with consideration of best practices and key interventions for gender/protection mainstreaming, and in total consideration of community participation. 
All activities will be reported as per the timelines of the Nutrition cluster using existing NIS system i.e. bi-weekly, monthly and quarterly as needed. Data collection tools, monitoring tools, and reporting tools of the cluster shall be used. 
Total estimated budget to cover the 2 counties is $800,000 (Eight Hundred Thousand US dollars).

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods of Vulnerable  Agro-pastoralists Communities in former Unity, Jonglei and Northern Bahr el Ghazal States, South Sudan
project_objective:
Despite the recently signed revitalized peace agreement in late 2018 and the promise of better times to come, a lethal combination of prolonged dry spells, floods, conflict, poor access to inputs, low productivity, pests such Fall Army Worm invasion, livestock diseases and subsequent high mortalities, poor infrastructure, dysfunctional markets, poor terms of trade and poor trade flows, declining economic opportunities and rising inflation have pushed food insecurity situation in South Sudan to the highest levels since 2010, with at least 5.2 million people projected to be extremely food insecure in the first quarter of 2019 (IPC, September 2018 Update; FEWSNET-SS Food Security Outlook,  2018). 

Throughout the crisis, many vulnerable host and displaced families, especially women, widowed women, child headed households, the elderly, boys and girls and children solely depend on agriculture (crop and livestock production) and fishing among other coping strategies. Fishing resources (projected to deliver immediate/short term benefits) and vegetable production (medium term benefits) are projected to still play a very key role in securing household food and nutrition security in 2019 especially among children (boys and girls) under 5 years and pregnant women (FSL Cluster Strategy, 2018). In locations with IPC 4 and 5, VSF Suisse will deploy limited unconditional cash grants to selected worst off households, to enable them access essential foods from the market, which should result into improved food and nutrition outcomes of the Households within a short period and inject cash in the nascent markets. Cash-based transfer interventions will be guided by information gathered from its own assessment and emergency market assessments (EMMA) conducted by other partners. The cash transfer value will be based on the prevailing cost of food basket (linked to the calories required per person per Household in a day). 
Many displaced families, especially women, the elderly, boys and girls and children camped with livestock in the safe havens for easy access to livestock and fisheries derived food (meat, milk and fish) (FAO Conflict and Livestock in South Sudan, February 2016).

VSF Suisse proposes to target 30,000 beneficiaries (men, women, girls and boys – includes elderly and people with special needs) with a multi-sectoral approach to promote food and crop production, reduction in post-harvest losses and safe guarding animal health, restoration and support of fishing activities, focus on restoring and strengthening livelihoods (IPC 4 and IPC 3) alongside more multi sector integrated actions (e.g.  WASH, Nutrition & Health), advocacy for women’s needs, voice and rights, capacity building and skills transfers, livestock vaccinations and treatments, cash transfers where possible to empower beneficiaries and increase efficiency and informed assistance through robust assessment and post distribution monitoring. 
Through inter-cluster synergies, quality programming, cost efficiency in addition to mainstreaming cross-cutting programmatic approaches that include application of Accountability to Affected Populations principles, protection including Gender Based Violence/ Sexual exploitation mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conflict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention, environmental conservation and sustainability.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood support to vulnerable and multiple crises affected households in Yirol East,Yirol West counties Lakes state and Mvolo county Western Equitoria State of South Sudan.
project_objective:
Please provide a short summary of the intervention, describing its purpose and target. – Limit 4000 characters
WAV proposed project aims to support IDP and host family farmers, fishermen and vulnerable communities in Yirol East/ West of Lakes state and Mvolo counties of Western Equitoria state to increase their livelihood self sufficiency. WAV needs assessments, as well as Post Distribution Monitoring from ongoing programs, have identified significant unmet need for both IDPs and host families who have lost productive crop agriculture or fishing assets due to ongoing conflict or displacement, and as a result have reduced purchasing power and incomes that hinder food security. It is critical to support these households to begin to restore lost crop agriculture or fishing livelihoods, thus enabling them to have increased food availability through personal production, as well as a small income for increased food access. WAV plans to target 1,400 households (HH) through the proposed interventions. The target for seeds and tools distribution is 800 HHs, including 560 female headed HHs and 240 male headed HHs. Furthermore, WAV plans to distribute fishing kits to 600 HHs, including 60 female headed HHs and 540 male headed HHs. These activities will be implemented in the 3 counties. The project will distribute fishing kits and then train fishermen on the usage of the new fishing equipment. Early distribution of fishing kits will support fishermen to take advantage of the fishing season. Similarly the project will distribute vegetable seeds and tools to beneficiaries (farmers) during early February for plantation in the same month. In addition, the project will do post planting monitoring and provide periodic technical advice and follow up as necessary. During April and May, WAV will distribute staple crop sees and tools to farmers. . The beneficiaries of staple crops and tools will take advantage of planting season and will do the planting between May and ­June, 2019. The majority of IDPs in Yirol East/West traditionally from Rumbek East and unity men take care of the livestock and area also involved in the fishery business, while women do most of the agriculture work. Due to these cultural and traditional approaches, the majority of agriculture beneficiaries will be female headed HHs.

project_name: Providing Education in Emergencies & School Meals for Affected Vulnerable Boys and Girls in Koch, Guit (Unity State) and Fangak (Jonglei State) and Western Equatoria State (Ibba, Mvolo)
project_objective:
Continued fighting and insecurity has resulted in displacement, livelihood disruption, dire food insecurity, and malnutrition, contributing to high dropout rates in education. Children and youth have been made increasingly vulnerable as they have discontinued their academic activities to search for food and safety, with increased exposure to protection risk such as sexual violence, child labor, early marriage, and recruitment into armed groups.

The project will implement an integral education intervention with key activities to address the unique needs of those affected by the conflict, such as emergency school meals and life-skills messages and referrals of GBVs survivors for both girls and women. The project will target 15,842 beneficiaries (Male 9,550 female 6,292) of whom 8,750 children (Male 4,850 female 3,900) will directly benefit from the school meals during the project period.  A total of 10 Temporary Learning Spaces (TLSs) will be established or rehabilitated with environmentally friendly materials, along with 10 gender-segregated latrines and WASH facilities. Teaching and recreational supplies will be distributed and psycho-social support will be provided. Teachers will be trained in using the Skills for Life Kit. 

IDPs and host communities will receive orientation in peacebuilding and trauma healing activities, how to share limited resources, child protection, and GBV prevention and response in emergencies. Schools and communities will be sensitized concern sanitation, the prevention of disease transmission, and HIV/AIDS. Campaigns for supporting girls’ enrollment will be organized for IDPs and host communities. All schools will be supported to become safe and inclusive spaces where children, parents, and the community can receive improved psychological awareness for other possible crises.

project_name: Emergency Food Security and Livelihood Support to Vulnerable populations in Koch County, Unity State and Fangak County, Jonglei State
project_objective: This Emergency Food Security and Livelihood Support to Vulnerable populations in Koch County, Unity State and Fangak County, Jonglei State. The project duration will be one year from January to December 2019. The project will serve 30,000 Households, 18,500 in Koch County and 11,500 in Fangak County. The project will adopt a year round programming with main season activities involving crop production and some fishing activities while dry season activities will involve vegetable production and fishing activities. The project will have three main components, livelihood kits support, training and conditional cash transfer. A conditional cash transfer modality is included to provide access to cash for food and other household needs with the main focus being creation/rehabilitation of communal assets. Collaboration and integration will be key tenets of this project. Working in collaboration with other stakeholders will reduce duplication. Integration with other sectors including nutrition, WASH and protection is meant to ensure greater impact at household level. The project also aims at ensuring gender parity by according both men and women an equal opportunity to participate in project activities. Right from inception, community involvement will be pivotal to project implementation to ensure transparency, accountability but also project sustainability through localization.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition Intervention in Unity and Jonglei States (Koch County, Bentiu PoC and Fangak County)
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to reduce the morbidity and mortality of young children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) due to malnutrition by increasing access to Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) services and nutrition education (MIYCN/IYCF-E). 
The onsite nutrition education to mothers and caregivers on use of treatment nutrition supplies and promoting dietary practices will equip them with knowledge and skills to prevent malnutrition and make healthy food choices within their context. 
Currently WRSS has oversight of 11 nutrition sites in Koch County, 2 sites in Bentiu PoC and 6 nutrition sites in Fangak County. This project seeks to support outpatient therapeutic feeding program (U5-OTP), Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP – U5 MAM and PLW) and Mother, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) programming in these 19 sites by including community outreach and mobile interventions. The project will also increase the capacity of OTP/TSFP sites through improved infrastructure and maintain the number of Stabilization Centers in Koch and Fangak Counties.

Program integration shall be ensured by establishing kitchen gardening in selected nutrition sites, PLWs beneficiaries linked to receive vegetable kits where possible and they will also benefit from cooking demonstrations. Proper sanitation facilities (latrines), safe drinking water, handwashing stations and ECDE materials shall be mainstreamed across nutrition sites. SAM children will be tested for malaria and other illness (URTI, UTI) and referred/linked to adjacent PHCC/Us for comprehensive treatment. The program shall be sensitive to the needs and safety of women, boys and girls by creating a friendly and sanitary atmosphere. 

WRSS will apply an adaptive strategy for accessing and serving the affected populations ranging from static sites to local outreaches to accompanying RRMs and ensuring supervised services continue thereafter. As possible and necessary, nutrition centers damaged during the conflict will be rehabilitated so that services can be normalized.

L'accès aux soins de santé primaire (curatifs, préventifs et promotionnels) de qualité des groupes  vulnerables (FEFA, enfants de moins de 5 ans) est amélioré  dans les Provinces du Ouaddaï et Wadi Fira
project_objective: La situation sanitaire est caractérisée par la récurrence des maladies à potentiel épidémique, telles que l’hépatite E, le choléra, la rougeole, la méningite. Les maladies endémiques, tel que le paludisme, ont parfois tendance à dépasser le seuil normal. Ceci pourrait être attribué à la faiblesse du système sanitaire, les mauvaises pratiques d’hygiène, la faible couverture vaccinale. Depuis le début de l’année à septembre 2018, le Tchad a notifié 2887 cas suspects de rougeole avec 79 décès (soit une létalité de 2,8%) dans 33 districts sanitaires de régions du centre et du nord sur les 117 districts que compte le pays. Le Tchad reste exposé au choléra, particulièrement dans ses zones endémiques à l’Est et dans les régions du Sud suite à la continuité du Tchad avec le Nigeria, le Cameroun et le Niger qui sont actuellement en épidémie de choléra. En 2017, l’épidémie de choléra avait affecté 1253 personnes parmi lesquelles 81 décès dans les régions du Sila et du Salamat; entre 2016 et 2017, 1 859 cas d’hépatite E occasionnant 22 décès ( soit une létalité de 1,1%) avaient été notifiés dans la région du Salamat. Ce projet vise à soutenir le gouvernement dans la lutte contre les maladies transmissibles et non transmissibles afin de rehausser les indicateurs sanitaires du pays dans les provinces du Ouaddaï et Wadi Fira. Des rencontres périodiques et un système de suivi évaluation (rapportage) sera mis en place pour la redevabilité du projet.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action Operations in Sudan
project_objective: This project will reduce risks posed by explosive hazards, enabling the affected population to safely access productive land, natural resources and basic services. Additionally, the project aims to provide assistance to landmine/ERW survivors for socioeconomic reintegration. 30 known hazardous areas will be surveyed and cleared, securing access to 5,000,000 square meters of priority land for safe movement of refugees and IDPs and/or productive use by the local populations. 240,000 vulnerable populations will learn how to adopt safe behaviors in landmine contaminated areas. 190 landmine/ERW survivors and other persons with disabilities (PWD) will be empowered by gaining physical mobility and means for livelihood. Through this project, the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) will support the Government of Sudan to meet its commitment to the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention (APMBC) by strengthening the institutional capacity of the National Mine Action Center (NMAC). In this endeavor, the project will continue to build the national capacity in mine action by providing training to national partners including NMAC and non-governmental organization (NGO) staff members.

project_name: Reducing food insecurity,  and building resilience for the vulnerable households and communities in Blue Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan (including Abyei north), Kassala and Red Sea States.
project_objective: The main objective of this project is to reduce food and nutrition insecurity, restore livelihood and build resilience of the affected population/communities in the protracted crisis areas in Blue Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan (including Abyei north), Kassala, and Red Sea states by safeguarding their livelihood’s assets and strengthening their productive capacity. The affected population includes IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host communities. The project is in line with the three FSL Sector Strategic Outcomes 1, 2 and 3; and in line with the Multi Year Humanitarian strategy (2017 2019) Outcome 1, 2 and 3. The multi-year strategy will allow FAO to provide immediate lifesaving assistance whenever the need arises and at the same time engage strategically to address the drivers of vulnerabilities and underlying structural issues across the targeted states. In particular, the project will focus on increasing the access to productive assets, inputs and services to enable the beneficiaries to improve food and nutrition security status and sustain their livelihoods. It will also enhance the income generation capacities of particularly disadvantaged population groups, such as women headed households and support them with diversified livelihood means and skills. The project will ensure a balanced dietary intake to avoid any type of malnutrition, including micronutrient deficiency. The project will also contribute to environmental protection and conservation through interventions on establishment/rehabilitation of tree’s nurseries for production and distribution of multipurpose trees’ seedlings as well as training of the targeted communities’ members (especially women) on production and use of Fuel Efficient Stoves (FES).

project_objective: This project will focus on GBV response in humanitarian contexts. The main focus will be on service provision in line with SOPs and GBV guiding principles. The program will offer immediate lifesaving services to survivors of GBV including comprehensive case management, facilitating access to clinical care for sexual assault survivors, dissemination of key messages on GBV, referrals and capacity building of relevant actors to ensure services are quality and responsive to the protection needs of women and girls. The project will seek to enhance access to GBV services. IRC will provide PSS services at the safe spaces where women and girls (including survivors of GBV) will get psychosocial and economic skills including counselling services, skills building, listening sessions and build social networks. The safe spaces will be a hub for women and girls to build agency and those that are survivors to learn strategies on how to protect themselves as well help them get reintegrated in the community as they undergo the healing process. Some of the stakeholders include the local administration, the police, and women leadership at community level, community and religious leaders and will establish protection networks for women and girls.
