In 2019, the humanitarian community in Iraq is prioritizing the centrality of protection by responding to protection needs of affected people as well as increasing access to basic services for the most vulnerable populations. 

To contribute to this objective, UNICEF intends to support 180,000 internally displaced and conflict affected children, through the provision of winter clothes, in order to protect the most vulnerable children from the harsh winter elements. 

UNICEF’s winter response programme falls within UNICEF’s mandate to protect vulnerable children from risks and to guard their safety and well-being and their rights to grow in an environment in which they are enabled to reach their full potential in life. The provision of life sustaining and saving winter supplies to children ensure adequate protection to cope with extreme weathers and proves to be a lifesaving response for children living in precarious situations.

project_name: Regional - International Labour Organization
Peru - International Labour Organization
Ecuador - International Labour Organization
Capacity Building and Strengthening of Government Counterparts for the Handover of RRM
project_objective:
In 2019, the humanitarian community in Iraq is prioritizing contingency planning for any new phase of humanitarian response that may emerge. The UN Humanitarian Country Team (UNHCT) has agreed an overarching strategic objective in relation to improving humanitarian response timeliness and capacity through preparedness-related interventions. To contribute to this objective, the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) Consortium intends to enhance capacity of existing government structures and local authorities including the Joint Coordination and Monitoring Cell (JCMC), the Joint Consultative Committee (JCC), the Board of Relief and Humanitarian Affairs (BRHA) in Dahuk, the Erbil Refugee Committee (ERC), the Ministry of Migration and Displacement (MoMD), and Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) and its relevant Departments to enable these to better cope with future emergencies, including taking over the responsibility for and operation of the RRM. 

To facilitate this, the Consortium intends to conduct a feasibility study, including a risk analysis and capacity assessment, which will ascertain the feasibility of handover, identify relevant counterpart/s and guide the overall transition. The study will identify government capacity gaps in the areas of contingency planning, emergency preparedness and response, operational planning, supply chain management, prepositioning and logistics, monitoring, information management, and reporting. The assessment will provide a baseline for the capacity development actions, led by the RRM Consortium, to facilitate successful handover to the Government.

project_name: Cash for Education

The project will support 15,000 extremely vulnerable children (as defined through specific and coordinated vulnerability assessments at household level), approximately an equal number of boys and girls. Indirect beneficiaries include the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) and its Directorates who will benefit from the cash transfer, which will include elements of institutional and technical capacity development. 

The project intends to build on and enhance existing cross-referral mechanisms with Government-led social and child protection systems for affected children or caregivers who may require case management support. This element of the project will be undertaken in collaboration with UNICEF Child Protection programme.
Expected results include: Increasing school enrolment and retention of out of school children and children at risk of drop-out; decreases in negative coping strategies such as child labour and taking children out of school; Government systems strengthening by establishing cross referrals and social care service provision.

project_name: Improving the livelihoods and resilience of communities through creation of community assets
project_objective:
The insurgency in Nigeria continues to affect the population living in the North-East. According to the Needs Overview by the Early Recovery & Livelihoods sector(August 2018) an estimated 5.5 million people, in the most affected states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe, are in acute need of early recovery assistance.

ER&L sector need overview reveals 5.5 million people in need, 1 million are IDPs in host communities, 1.5 million IDP returnees, and 2.9 million people in host communities . Several LGAs have been prioritised based on the levels of damages and service delivery burden associated with high numbers of returnees and IDPs in host communities: Damboa, Konduga, Monguno (Borno State); Madagali, Mubi North, Hong (Adamawa State); and Gujba, Potiskum and Fika (Yobe State).

The XXIV round of the Displacement Tracking Matrix (IOM - August 2018), estimated the number of IDPs and Returnees to be 3,506,841 (1,926,748 IDPS and 1,580,093 Returnees), 94% of whom have been displaced due to the Boko Haram insurgency in the North East. Out of the total number of displaced people, 137,588 IDPs and 165,771 Returnees are currently in Yobe State. 
Ongoing crisis has worsen the situation including disruption of market supplies and livelihoods, and significantly limiting the populations having access to livelihoods. IOM estimates that 60% of the IDPs reside with host communities.
According to FEWSNET ’s Market Monitoring Bulletin of May 2018, prices in NE Nigeria are generally higher than other regions as result of insecurity and are expected to remain above average until the revival of main harvest, moreover, populations depend heavily on market purchase, currently since significant improvement in security in Yobe state, many markets are functional with enough supplies. The persisting conflict continues to substantially impact households’ livelihoods in the NE Nigeria. Despite the main seasons harvest coming soon, due to restricted access to land for most households in the NE, harvest will be substantially below average for most of the households. As situation in Yobe state is stabilizing, COOPI proposes livelihood activities in Yusufari,Geidam, Potiskum, Fika and Gulani LGAs. The project will target 5,865 households (approximatively 24,173 beneficiaries) in the project. Beneficiaries will be supported in order to foster the transition from emergency to resilience as COOPI is committed to apply the humanitarian-development nexus approach and ensure coherence between the actors. COOPI intends to protect and rehabilitate livelihoods of most vulnerable groups, pre-identified through COOPI’s ongoing food assistance and CBT activities funded by other donors, through technical trainings on adapted livelihood practices where possible in coordination and complementarity with ongoing line ministries and sector. 

COOPI, in order to ensure sustainable and longer term impact and contribute to Yobe state government’s early recovery strategy (YOSERA) will consider beneficiaries from its food assistance programs to be trained and supported for livelihood assistance as transition. COOPI is suitably placed (technically and operationally) to implement livelihoods support projects in Yobe state due to current presence, access, and ongoing partnership with WFP. COOPI forecast strong potential for humanitarian development nexus through its presence in Yobe and particularly in proposed LGA. COOPI has already developed liaison and MOUs with state government’s line departments as well as providing capacity building opportunities to government institutes. COOPI will also consider the livelihood action to be linked with other sectors which are planned to be executed as multiyear response mainly to ensure transition from emergency to recovery and rehabilitation including conflict management. COOPI will consider to work through local NGOs. Implementation of current activities in the area have revealed a deterioration in livelihoods sources primarily due to frequent conflicts and inherent hardships in the state as well as climactic conditions and increased market demands. COOPI, following Early Recovery and Livelihood sector's objectives, intends to protect and rehabilitate livelihoods of most vulnerable groups, identified through technical trainings on adapted practices and formation and training of livelihood beneficiaries focusing on women groups who are already engaged with various small enterprises. COOPI will ensure that composition of sectors is defined based on COOPI Community Based Participatory Planning sessions and standard as well as aligned and coordinated with the Early Recovery and Livelihoods working groups. COOPI is implementing protection project in proposed LGAs, will ensure all the livelihood action is linked to protection support to the beneficiaries, particularly women and children.
Monitoring and reporting 
COOPI is committed to monitor and report the proposed project as per ER&L sector monitoring framework and guideline and will ensure that results and indicators are achieved within the designated time frame.  Programme Coordinator based as well as the Country Admin will ensure a constant and close monitoring of activities from program and administrative/financial point of view, while Child Protection team will support Protection Mainstreaming of livelihood response and also provide advice to ensure that all protection activities are responding to COOPI and global protection standard. Logistic Coordinator will also support Project Manager to ensure all procurement will be in line with donors and COOPI’s regulation and requirements.
COOPI’s monitoring system will involve all program staff and beneficiaries aiming at: a) assess impact of activities on the lives of beneficiaries, through interviews, focus group discussions, surveys, market surveys and observations; b) assess actual program achievements against its planned objectives and indicators; c) identify strengths and weaknesses of individual program activities; d) make changes to programming as needed to increase the quality of services; and e) advocate for unmet needs and gaps. The project M&E system will include: Monthly outputs and outcomes tracking against defined indicators as well as 5Ws. Project Manager will submit with timely updates as dynamic way of sharing challenges and progress. PM will also keep relevant donors and sector update on regular basis for any project related issues as required. COOPI will submit interim report as per guidelines as well as final report within timeframe of the project completion as per agreement.

• Promotion activities for self-construction of household latrines and garbage pits in long-term resettlement and returning areas (including the provision of sanitation supplies for most vulnerable households).
• Dissemination of WASH related messages through mass communication media.
• Community and household level hygiene promotion activities in accommodation centres, return communities, and related institutions.
• Procurement and distribution of WASH related non-food items, with focus in most vulnerable families / households.

project_name: Columbia - Red Cross Colombia
Support the Libya INGO Forum to enhance INGO ability to effectively operate in Libya through improved coordination
project_objective: The Libya INGO Forum exists to serve the needs of its members and to promote the voice of international NGOs in the Libya humanitarian response. Under this project, the Forum will build upon its current work to improve operational coordination and facilitate the sharing of best practices among INGOs operating in Libya, lead collective advocacy effort towards the Libyan authorities, donors, governments and UN agencies, as well as represent the best interest of the NGOs in the coordination fora.  The Forum will provide support to its membership (currently composed of 15 INGOs operating in Libya), and to humanitarian organisations seeking to start operations in Libya.

project_name: Unconditional Gender-sensitive multipurpose Cash assistance to 2600 vulnerable households  across Libya
project_objective: The purpose of this project is to address the life-saving needs of 2600 highly vulnerable conflict-affected IDP, returnee, and host community households, in the Western (1100HHS), Eastern (1100HHS), and Southern (400 HHS) regions of Libya, and improve their access to essential goods and services of their choice at their own discretion and with dignity, but also to enable them to diversify their expenditures and ensure their protection needs. This would be through the delivery of three installments (580 LYD each) unconditional multi-purpose cash-based assistance and through the provision of one-off multi-purpose cash assistance for the emergency response in Tripoli.

project_name: Improving educational environments for the crisis-affected school-aged children of internally displaced (ID), non-displaced, and returnee families, across East, West and South regions of Libya.
project_objective: This project aims at improving and creating better educational environments, via the rehabilitation of the war-torn infrastructure, for the crisis-affected school-aged children of IDP, non-displaced, and returnee families, across Cyrenaica, Tripolitania, and Fezzan regions and enhance their well-being and personal development, via the provision of child protection services and referral to adequate psychosocial support.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood Improvement Project for Drought and Conflict -Affected Population in South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of this intervention is to save lives, reduce severe food insecurity and stabilize the condition of vulnerable groups including the elderly, IDPs, persons with disabilities, child-headed households, women and children in South Sudan. The interventions will further enhance community resilience by addressing the main drivers of vulnerability in the targeted areas of Kapoeta East, Tonj North, Tonj East and Terekeka. The project will seek to enhance both food security and livelihoods of vulnerable people by improving livestock production and access to animal health care services, improving access to agricultural production units & extension services and supporting communities to develop alternative income sources / livelihoods diversification by providing financial services through Group Savings and Loan Associations (GSLAs).  Cross-cutting themes will be to promote gender equity and increased women’s participation in building resilience, peace building and conflict reduction, disaster risk reduction and sustainable natural resource management. The geographical focus of the project is Kapoeta East County (Kauto 5,064 HH; Jie-900 HH, Mogos-3,650 HH, Lotimor-1,550 HH;  and Nating'a-990 HH;  payams);  Tonj North County (Alabek-2,400 HH, Akop-2,100 HH, Rualbet- 1,900  and Marialou 1,600 payams), Tonj East (Kacuat-2,080 HH, Paweng-2,150 HH Malualchum 2, 200-HH payams) and Terekeka County (Terekeka-2,400 HH, Muni-1,800 HH, Reggo-1,750 and Nyori-1,900 payams). Proposed interventions are aligned to FSL HRP Cluster objectives as shown below:  
•	Under unconditional food assistance, IRSS proposes to provide emergency regular life sustaining and life-saving food assistance to prevent famine, improve food consumption, improve dietary diversity and improve coping strategies for the most vulnerable population. This will target the most vulnerable households including IDPs 
•	Regarding food production for the most vulnerable households, the proposed interventions will seek to increase food production by vulnerable household in order to protect the erosion of livelihoods through improved agronomic practices i.e. use of ox plough animal traction, agricultural seeds and other faming inputs. 
•	Under the transitional emergency food assistance, IRSS proposes to provide emergency targeted life sustaining food assistance to strengthen households and community coping capacities by building productive assets and reduce reliance on general food distribution transfers. Food for Asset modality will be used to enable communities produce their own food in the long-term.  
•	In order to reduce dependency on food and agricultural input support, IRSS will through livelihood & conditional cash based support for more sustainable livelihoods seek to prevent and reverse the erosion of vulnerable rural & urban households and community assets. 
The proposed interventions will therefore be aimed at providing a link between rapid humanitarian response on one hand and building community resilience on the other. This will in turn contribute to reduce community vulnerability and build their capacity to bounce back in the face of livelihood shocks resulting from drought,conflict and others.

project_name: Emercency Support to Recover Livelihoods of People Affected by the Cyclon Kenneth
project_objective: Provide urgent assistance to 220,000 most vulnerable people (44,000 households) affected by the cyclone through the restoration of the livelihoods.

project_name: LEBANON - Syrian American Medical Society Foundation

LEBANON - Restart Center for Rehabilitation of Victims of Violence and Torture
Maintenance and Establishment of Humanitarian Hubs in North-East Nigeria
project_objective: IOM operates a main hub in Maiduguri (Red Roof) and a total of additional seven7 field hubs in Gwoza, Bama, Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, Banki and Damasak in deep -field locations.  Humanitarian hubs are providing humanitarian partners in Maiduguri and various deep field locations with safe and secure accommodation, office spaces,  and support services enabling access of partners and delivery of services to the affected .population. The humanitarian base camp in Maiduguri currently accommodates 167 people at a time, and each of the seven deep field accommodates 15 people at a time. Under the proposed project, IOM will aim to support the maintenance of seven humanitarian hubs and one1 humanitarian base camp. IOM will also complete the establishment of the humanitarian hub in Rann, and initiate the establishment of two new humanitarian hubs in deep field locations (as directed by the Humanitarian Hub Task Force). Tented structures in Damasak, Banki and Monguno will also be upgraded to concrete structures, and the capacity of the humanitarian hub in Banki will be increased to 100 beds.

project_name: Emergency response for most at risk displaced and host population with a focus on elderly, people with injuries, chronic illness, physical disabilities and/or psychological distress and their family members affected by the crisis in Somalia.
project_objective:
Conflict-affected populations are of particular concern, including those in hard-to-reach areas and displaced and marginalized (elderly, people with injuries, chronic illness, widows, divorce, pregnant and lactating women, malnutrition children,  physical disabilities and/or psychological distress, polygamous wife, minority clans and their families) populations. IDPs, particularly those settling on the private land, are at constant risk of forced eviction. Protection issues include pervasive eviction and gender-based violence (GBV); child recruitment and early marriage. 

Over 204,000 people were forcibly removed from their homes this year, nearly double the same period last year, with many people made homeless multiple times . Forced evictions in Somalia are predominantly an urban phenomenon and are typically carried out with no notice. In their search for shelter, evicted IDPs have been forced to relocate to overcrowded settlements or became homeless.  Evicted IDPs are at risk of being recruited into armed groups. 

Inadequate data disaggregation on PSNs, has contributed to limited awareness of disability issues among policy makers, planners, community leaders, services providers and the general public. The lack of information poses a threat to the design and implementation of policies and programs needed to support resilience and development as well as humanitarian assistance in the event of shocks for PSNs. 
a)	Comprehensive identification, registration and referral of PSNs 
b)	Enhance capacity of community members to sustain self-protection through awareness on existing community-based protection mechanisms, awareness on conflict resolution/mediation and peaceful co-existence messaging through focus group discussions and sensitization campaigns.
c)	Response to Gender-based Violence
d)	Service providers have increased their knowledge and show positive attitudes towards the inclusion of most vulnerable, including people with disabilities and better consider them within strategic planning and operations

project_name: To Improve access to equitable quality education in the merged Tribal districts
project_objective:
Between 2017 and 2018, some 60,121 families have returned to areas of origin in five tribal districts of KP . This translates into a population of 162,326 children in age-bracket of 3-18. The erstwhile FATA EMIS report for 2016-17 shows that more than one million (1,038,933) children in the age group of 04-14 are out of school in the tribal areas. The overall drop-out rate in Government Primary Schools over a cycle of 6 years is 76% (74% Boys, 80% Girls). Per the FATA Vulnerability Assessment (August-September 2017), half of the respondents expressed dissatisfaction with the quality of education due to lack of basic facilities, lack of teachers, teaching materials and damage to school infrastructure. In terms of damaged infrastructure, the RRU data shows that 943 educational institutions were partially and fully damaged in five tribal districts. 

Under the project, UNICEF will support the returnee children to resume education in a safe and protective environment by addressing the unmet needs in education for some 80,000 school going children in all merged districts of erstwhile FATA, preferably in the newly returned areas of Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North and South Waziristan. The children in return areas need access to safe, inclusive, and quality education to reduce the risk of exploitation, establishing a routine and normalcy through psycho-social support, providing a child friendly environment and equipping them with life skills. The available data indicates that need to increase girls’ access to education institutions in the merged districts. To increase the girls’ access, it is pivotal to ensure female teachers’ attendance, quality of education, availability of supplies and engagement of community especially women in TIJs/School Management Committees.   UNICEF will provide prefabricated school buildings, develop the capacity of Education staff, provide school supplies, strengthen TIJs/School Management Committees, and support Alternate Learning Program.

project_name: Strengthening the child protection preventive and responsive mechanisms and services for children in the areas of return
project_objective:
The objective of the project is that the Children displaced due to the emergency situations and who have returned in  to the five merged districts North and South Waziristan, Khyber, Orakzai and Kurram Agencies) of KP benefit from the  child protection services that are in line with the UNICEF’s Child Protection  Core Commitments in emergency.   

The target beneficiaries of the project include: 
Children (4-17 years): 	74,004 (35,522 girls and 38,482 boys)
Adults (18 – 59yrs): 	13,761
Total Beneficiaries: 		87,765

UNICEF has been the only agency who has been providing Child Protection services to the children in the merged districts. During 2018 UNICEF supported the Social Welfare Department erstwhile FATA in the provision of protection services through the child protection Vans intervention in two merged districts namely; Khyber and North Waziristan. The interventions designed to focus on strengthening, at the community-level, children’s self-protective behavior, as well as contributing to enhanced knowledge and skills among families, gatekeepers and community members in support of preventing the abuse of children. Additionally, practical skills and knowledge was imparted to the children of various age cohorts and their families / care-givers through the medium of an existing training tool entitled – ‘Sticks and Stones’. In this way, the active participation of children in their own protection was encouraged.
During 2018, a total of 32,562 beneficiaries in the targeted 23 villages were reached and were involved in various activities related to self-protection including MRE, and Birth registration 
The vulnerability Assessment conducted in 2017 indicated that women and children are highly vulnerable to mine risks when collecting firewood, fetching water and grazing livestock, the outreach of mine risk education to women remains far lower (8%) than to men (24%). Considerably fewer women (5%) than men (14%) have access to mobile phones and thus rely more on word-of-mouth for information. There has been a continuous increase in the cases related to Mine risk.  The children are also facing many psychosocial issue, as they have lost their family members and friends, and even the conditions of their houses in the areas of the return adds on to their stress. 
Multi-Cluster Indicator Survey (MICS) is another data source that suggests that rates of birth registration are is very low at below 1% in Merged districts of KP. UNICEF has been assisting the government in strengthening the formal system and associated mechanisms and processes for the registration of child births. 
The project has two major outputs which are as under:
Output 1: Government and informal community based structures have improved capacities, i.e. knowledge, and material and financial resources to provide psychosocial support to returnee children affected by displacement.
Output # 2: 
74,004 children and 13,761 number of parents and community members understand the risks pose by land mines and UXO and know how to prevent these risks and parents understand the importance of registering the birth of their children and act accordingly

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services for drought, Idai, and Kenneth responses in Mozambique
project_objective: More effective and principled humanitarian action that meets the needs of people affected by drought, insecurity, and cyclones Idai and Kenneth.

project_name: Fortalecimiento del sistema de salud en 6 Estados de Venezuela
Asistencia directa y protección a personas vulnerables en Venezuela
project_objective:
Finalidades del proyecto: 
1.	Asistencia a población pendular y en tránsito hacia Colombia. 
2.	Lucha contra la trata
    
1.	Asistencia integral a personas cruzando la frontera a Colombia

Aproximadamente 2,200 personas transitan diariamente por trochas en Santa Maria de Guarna, Caigua-el cubo y Machiques (350), San Antonio del Táchira y Ureña (1500) y Mantecal (300) en condiciones precarias de salud y escasos recursos para cubrir agua, alimentos y alojamiento.  
En las zonas mencionadas transitan miles de personas en movimiento pendular entre fronteras o migrando hacia otros países en situación de alta vulnerabilidad y sin acceso a servicios básicos.

1.1 Fortalecimiento de 6 centros de tránsito

•	Rehabilitación de espacios-albergue con equipamiento básico incluyendo cocina, dormitorios, baños y duchas, considerando riesgos VBG.
•	Provisión de alimentación básica, enseres, kits higiene.
•	Orientación sobre migración segura y prevención de la trata.

1.2 Servicios básicos de salud

•	Valoración médica y psicológica, provisión de medicamentos de atención básica.


2.	 Lucha contra la trata de personas

El flujo migratorio en Venezuela activa redes de tráfico y trata de personas, con un riesgo mayor en mujeres, jóvenes en edad de empleo, NNA. Mediante un enfoque de abajo hacia arriba y descentralizado, la OIM diseñará e implementará una estrategia para combatir la trata:

A. Prevención de la trata de personas.
 • Evaluación rápida sobre trata, identificando comunidades con mayor incidencia, tipos de trata y sectores, perfil de víctimas y personas en riesgo.
• Diseño e implementación de estrategia de comunicación.
• Diseño e implementación de estrategia de prevención trabajando con agentes y líderes comunitarios.

B. Atención y asistencia de las víctimas de trata.
• Apoyar al Gobierno con el diseño y desarrollo de directrices nacionales sobre víctimas de trata. 
• Identificación, referencia, asistencia a víctimas y personas en riesgo.
• Fortalecimiento a proveedores de servicios públicos y privados locales.
• Servicios integrales y coordinados a víctimas y personas en riesgo.
• Fortalecimiento de la coordinación interinstitucional para la remisión y contra remisión de víctimas.
• Apoyo a las víctimas de trata identificadas a través de alojamiento temporal o transicional.

project_name: Food security requirements for Deutsche Welthungerhilfe
project_objective: WHH is supporting sophisticated vegetable, legume and grass seed facilities to produce high-quality and quantity vegetables mainly for child institutions, a project which also incorporates nutrition-awareness campaigning. A notable and separate component of the projects are focused on nutrition-sensitive and climate-resilient agriculture production systems, combined with improved livestock production facilities. A parallel concentration on sloping land users’ groups helps these households to better maintain and secure their livelihoods through improved nursery management, reforestation, agroforestry, and crop production initiatives, and enhances their food security via on-site food processing systems.

project_name: Health response for people fleeing Myanmar in Ukhiya and Teknaf, Cox`s Bazar
project_objective: The project will ensure equitable, comprehensive and essential primary health care services. The project will provide direct clinical service inclusive of basic primary healthcare, reproductive health, and referral services. Clinicians at supported health facilities will be trained on child protection basic concepts, child safeguarding, child rights, confidentiality and on how to be child/adolescent-friendly providers. The scope of services will include preventative and curative services aligned with the essential package of primary health care services for Cox’s Bazar as agreed with the ISCG health sector working group.

project_name: Rohingya Response Protection Program
project_objective:
Oxfam began responding to the Rohingya response program in September 2017 to provide essential WASH, emergency food security, and protection assistance. Oxfam has established field offices in Cox Bazaar in Teknaf, with a field office to open in Uhkia in the beginning of 2019. Protection is central to Oxfam’s response strategy. The protection program is established in Uhkia and Teknaf areas, and protection teams are working in host community areas as well as in refugee camps. 
The project aims to respond to protection risks identified in refugee camps and host communities by addressing critical living conditions, strengthening the protection environment, and preparing for durable solutions. 
Gender is the heart of Oxfam’s response, and the protection program has a focus on women and girls, recognising their specific protection needs and challenges.
Underlying the entire Oxfam response is the commitment to safe programming; taking proactive measures to ensure the response does not cause inadvertent harm, is conflict sensitive, and reduces the risk of GBV.
The project continues the 2018 program with an expansion in the current areas of working to cover more beneficiaries. The protection program aims to reach 27,000 households, 4000 of which are from the host community. 
The project will include supporting community protection structures, capacity building with key stakeholders, and facilitating access to services. There will also be a focus on protection monitoring to provide the protection sector with analysis of protection gaps and trends, as well as to guide protection programming. The project will work in cooperation with the sector through the Protection Working Group. 
Oxfam’s protection baseline survey demonstrates that community protection needs include NFI items. To provide a comprehensive protection package, as well as soft activities the project includes an NFI component including solar street lights to address safety issues, particularly for women and girls, in camps and in host community.

project_name: Life-saving WASH Emergency Response to  Cyclone Idai Affected people  in Chimanimani, Chipinge and Buhera districts of Manicaland Province
project_objective: To restore access to basic WASH services to people  affected by cyclone Idai  in Chimanimani, Chipinge and  Buhera districts

project_name: Promoting civil documentation and HLP rights of displacement affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon.
project_objective: This project aims to promote the HLP rights of internally displaced people and affected communities and prevent HLP related conflicts in displacement and return areas. The displaced population faces various kinds of HLP related issues such as lack of land for agriculture, forced eviction from housing and land, secondary occupation in return areas, etc. Women are more vulnerable and face more HLP issues as according to the customary law in the region, women do not inherit land. While their gender roles expect them to bring food home form farming, their access to secure land is very limited. Even though, they had money to buy a piece of land, they will need authorisation from their husband or family related male. Women widows are evicted form land inherit after marriage and have to struggle to meet their basic needs. This project will pay specific attention to the most vulnerable such as women, the elderly and other marginalised groups.

project_name: Improving access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and hygiene practices for returnees, IDPs and host communities in the Far North region of Cameroon   ""
Improving living conditions, access to physical safety to promote dignity and protection of returnees, displaced people and vulnerable host communities in the Far North Region of Cameroon
project_objective: This project aims to provide returnees, internally displaced people and vulnerable hosts communities with  adequate shelter solutions. It will target 50% men and 50% women. Women will be considered as head of household in order to include those in polygamous family.

project_name: Social inclusion in areas most affected by the Lake Chad crisis in Far North Cameroon.
project_objective:
This project aims to improve access for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities to social services namely quality primary education for boys and girls, vocational training and economic integration for youth and young women through improved governance of councils and local institutions in areas affected by the Lake Chad crisis in the Far North region.
The project is a community-driven, integrated cross-border programme across three priority sectors: ICLA, which includes access to civil and identity documentation, HLP rights, and Collaborative Dispute Resolution (CDR); livelihoods and food security (LFS); and education. 
Livelihoods and Education components will complement ICLA component in order to ensure protection to the most vulnerable individuals and own their right.

project_name: Life-saving emergency assistance to displaced populations in the South West and North West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
The project aims to reduce the exposure of displacement affected population to WASH related illnesses through improved access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and strengthened hygiene practices. NRC will strive to reach the most affected and in need in rural areas including bushes security permitting. Specific attention will be paid to women and girls are the crisis has forced them to lose their female dignity due to lack of dignity material, using leave and other plants related material as indicated by women in a gender analysis recently conducted by NRC in the Fako division.
To achieve this objective, the following activities will be implemented in partnership with local NGOs that have better access to communities:
1.	Assessments on the water points conditions
2.	Formation and training of hygiene promoter groups of water user’s committees
3.	Capacity building of WASH actors and partners in emergency WASH and related issues
4.	Promotion of safe hygiene and sanitation practices among IDPs and vulnerable host communities
5.	Distribution of Wash Kits
6.	Distribution of menstrual hygiene kits to vulnerable women and girls of childbearing age coupled to sensitisation on menstrual hygiene management.

project_name: Improving the Access to Domestic water for Vulnerable Community in area C in Zatara and Beit Tamir in Bethlehem Governorate
project_objective:
This proposal comes within the under of WASH Sector according to the following WASH cluster HRP objectives:

Objectives: Ensure acutely vulnerable Palestinians in area C in Zatara  second phase and Bait Ta’amar in Bethlehem has access to essential services by improving access to WASH services by providing an appropriate domestic water services response for vulnerable women, men, girls, and boys in fragile, and critically underserved communities by ensuring resilience and access to clean drinking water in  Zatara and beit Tamir in east Bethlehem Governorate.

Country Strategic Objectives: S.O.2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

WASH Cluster Objective 1: Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable access to safe and sufficient WASH services in accordance with dignity of the unserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank                  
     	
Sector Activity: Provision of domestic water services.
It is about an extension of an 8-inch carrier water line, 3900 meters from the point of Janata water, to the beginning of Za'tara municipality, serving six residential communities (Zatara, Ras Al-Wad, Beit Tamir, Jib Al-Theb, Al Aranda, Al aqban). the old line was installed before more than 50 years and suffers a loss of up to 45%, and this project is a complementary of the project to rehabilitate internal lines in Zatara.

project_name: JORDAN - INTERSOS Humanitarian Aid Organization
Accessible clean and potable water and improved hygiene practices in vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective: The intervention will respond to the shortage of household water supply in 6 communities in the Gaza strip through: 1) equipping three municipal wells with Photovoltaics (PV) solar energy units to improve pumping water in Al Moghraqa and Wadi Gaza in Gaza and Heker Aljam’ neighborhood in Dier Al Balah, and 2) improve water storage capacity for poor households in Bani sohailah, Al qarara / Khanyounes and Al Bayuk / Rafah.

project_name: Strengthening Integrated Primary Health Care Service Delivery To Vulnerable Populations in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States
project_objective:
This project is aimed at strengthening integrated primary health care services delivery in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States. These states bordering Niger, Cameroon and Chad are expected to receive many returnees from hard to reach locations within Borno, Chad and Cameroun and host over 1 million IDPs. Over the last several months and with increasing activity of the military, these locations, especially in Borno state, are also overburdened by an increasing congestion within the limited available IDP camps.
UNICEF, in partnership with the primary health care agencies, plans to reach these groups through provision of an integrated package of health services to children under five years old, women and their families through IDP camp clinics and health facilities in host communities.
UNICEF will work with other partners to support the Government to provide rapid response activities desperately needed in locations with high humanitarian needs. We will also work in the 16 (13 Borno and 3 Yobe) LGAs with ongoing protracted crises while supporting HSS work in the rest of the stable LGAs. We will focus on how to reach people in need including returnees, we will support states to implement interventions that will enable transition from emergency phase to development in some LGAs, partner with INGOs that are present on the ground and provide strategic TA in building capacity for resilience at the community level. We will review our supplies and focus on the critical component. We hope to leverage resources through convergence with other sectors at the state, LGAs and community levels.
In all we have the following objectives 
•	Meet the immediate health needs of conflict-affected populations; 
•	Restore essential health services; 
•	Rehabilitate the health system; and
•	Transit into government led/operated health systems strengthening program

project_name: Provision of integrated and lifesaving Primary Health Care (PHC) services for conflict affected and vulnerable populations in Melut, Upper Nile State (UNS)
project_objective: GOAL’s primary objective for 2019 is to provide quality and essential healthcare services, scale up responsiveness to needs of targeted vulnerable populations in Melut County, Upper Nile, through a network of 3 primary health care facilities (Dethoma and Koradar IDP clinics and 1 mobile clinic- Malek) by delivering the basic PHCC, PHCU and mobile health care packages. GOAL will target 20,329 internally displaced persons (IDPs), with a focus on children under 5 years (target 4274 children) and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs – target 1,628  PLWs).

project_name: Supporting Healthcare Services in Bab Al Hawa Hospital
project_objective:
The project aims to support healthcare services in Bab Al Hawa Hospital by providing financial support along with providing all medicines and medical consumables needed, to provide people in need with all required services, this includes local communities and IDPs, women, children and elderly people.
Bab Al Hawa Hospital is considered the biggest specialized hospital in NW of Syria, and it’s now considered the main referral health facility for all primary health facilities in NW of Syria.
The services provided at the hospital includes but not limited to: Emergency unit, Renal Dialysis unit, Scanning and Imagining unit, GI Endoscopy unit, Laboratory and Blood Bank, Neonatal unit, Neurology unit, Cardiology unit, Ophthalmology unit, and Outpatients Clinics, and Specialized Operations unit which includes General Surgery, ENT Surgery, Neurology Surgery, Orthopaedic Surgery, Thoracic Surgery, Maxillofacial Surgery, Urology Surgery and Pediatric Surgery, which will be all supported by this project.
The hospital facilitates the services provision for women by preparing a specialized reception utilities and isolated room for privacy, in addition to the availability of women in the hospital staff.
In addition, the hospital is the authorized referral point to Turkey for the most complex cases.

project_name: Fortalecimiento del sistema de protección para brindar servicios de prevención, atención y respuesta a las necesidades de mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes en el contexto de la crisis venezolana.
project_objective:
UNICEF promoverá el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de las instancias de Protección de la niñez y adolescencia del Estado y de la sociedad civil para expandir y mejorar la calidad, oferta y acceso a los servicios para las niñas, niños y adolescentes identificados en el análisis de necesidades (Humanitarian Needs Overview) más vulnerables, tales como: niños separados y no acompañados, sobrevivientes de violencia, incluida la violencia sexual y la violencia basada en género, vinculados o en riesgo de ser involucrados en grupos armados, niños en las peores formas de trabajo infantil y explotación laboral incluido en actividades ilícitas (trabajo en las minas y el contrabando de gasolina), desplazados internos, privados de libertad. Estas acciones estarán focalizadas en: 

•	Ampliación y consolidación de  servicios especializados de protección  para responder y atender a las necesidades específicas de niñas, niños y adolescentes  víctimas o que están en riesgo de abuso, violencia, explotación y negligencia en el marco de la actual crisis, haciendo énfasis en la calidad de los servicios y al manejo de los casos según los estándares internacionales (Normas Mínimas de Protección de la Infancia en la Acción Humanitaria) y legislación nacional (Ley Orgánica de Protección al Niño, Niña y Adolescente).
•	UNICEF trabajara para mejorar las capacidades y la resiliencia de las comunidades y de las familias, en prevenir, identificar y remitir a los servicios correspondientes casos de vulneración de derechos de protección y para aumentar el bienestar psicosocial de la niñez y adolescencia.

En conjunto con sus socios serán desarrolladas e implementadas intervenciones a nivel comunitario como actividades de sensibilización y estrategias de comunicación con comunidades, espacios comunitarios y educativos, para prevenir la separación familiar, la trata y el reclutamiento, promoción de la crianza positiva, fortalecimiento de las redes y entornos comunitarios seguros, actividades estructuradas y continuas de apoyo psicosocial, incluyendo programas de empoderamiento y construcción de resiliencia y actividades recreativas.
La intervención a nivel comunitario tiene como objetivo reducir las vulnerabilidades que enfrenta la niñez y la adolescencia en Venezuela, fortaleciendo la resiliencia individual y comunitaria, aumentando la comprensión de los riesgos de protección y mitigando las secuelas de las vulneraciones de derechos cuando ocurran.
El alcance de este objetivo se logrará mapeando, involucrando y apoyando a las instancias de protección existentes desde el comienzo de la respuesta humanitaria. El involucramiento y el trabajo conjunto con la población afectada permitirá reducir las vulnerabilidades de los niños, niñas y adolescentes construyendo entornos protectores sostenibles a nivel familiar y comunitario.

•	UNICEF está comprometido en liderar el Area de Responsabilidad  de niños, niñas y adolescentes y en fomentar la colección y análisis de información relevante para la protección de la infancia y adolescencia en el país, mapeando los actores y servicios existentes para mejorar la coordinación de la respuesta humanitaria y promoviendo diagnósticos, análisis e informes técnicos de la situación de los niños, niñas y adolescentes en las zonas priorizadas por el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria, llegando a más niños, niñas y adolescentes posibles con servicios y rutas de atención y referencia de casos de calidad.

project_name: LEBANON - Heartland Alliance International
Informing humanitarian planning and response to the needs of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Somalia through baseline assessments and population-based surveys
project_objective: Maintain and strengthen the system of data collection in the Somalia through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the coordination of humanitarian activities. The DTM aims to provide reliable and up to date information on the number of displaced populations, their location, profile, displacement trends, reasons for displacement, and needs disaggregated by age and sex to better assist and inform the governmental and humanitarian response. The DTM has the potential to be expanded and/or modified to take into account changes in the national context and need to inform durable solutions.

project_name: Provision of Life-Saving Shelter and Life-Sustaining NFI Services to Vulnerable Populations in Somalia
project_objective: Through this project proposal IOM will provide humanitarian Shelter/NFI Assistance to 372,000 newly displaced and protracted IDPs and host community. The geographical areas of intervention will be Lower Jubba, Gedo, Bay and Benadir regions for static interventions. The pipeline prepositioned emergency light kits will be distributed countrywide wherever the needs arise and are endorsed by the cluster. The target is to have 70% of the beneficiaries stated in the proposal reached out through cash-based interventions, whenever this is feasible and appropriate. IOM will contribute to the delivery and piloting of cash-for-rent scheme in the Municipality of Mogadishu for 2,000 households with a clear exit strategy that relies on the financial stabilization of IDPs through the access to livelihood opportunities. The quality programming of this response will revolve around a solid approach to accountability to affected population by promoting community participation in programme implementation and accountability to inform analysis and future response.

project_name: Shelter and NFIs provided by UNHCR
project_objective: Construction of new permanent Shelters and infrastructure established, improved and maintained to support reintegration of returnees, IDPs and host communities. Provision of core relief items to approximately 35,000 households, either in kind or cash. In addition, UNHCR will support approximately 25,000 women and girls of reproductive age with sanitary kits.

project_name: Improving provision of services and protection responses through strengthened camp coordination and camp management
project_objective: Providing streamlined life-saving, humanitarian multi-sectoral assistance and strengthening the basic infrastructure support in IDP sites and ensure equitable access to services and assistance of all persons in need, with a clear focus on moving toward attaining durable solutions with full participation of the displaced and host communities

project_name: Enhancing access for GBV survivors to quality, timely and confidential services Somalia
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to enhance access for services for GBV survivors through improving capacity of service providers, strengthening of referral pathways and provision of material and livelihood opportunities for women and girls. 

The specific objectives of this project are:
a.	Facilitate access to comprehensive multi sectoral GBV services (medical, legal, psychosocial) for 6000 women and girls 
b.	Enhance the capacity/and mobilize 200 PSS counsellors; 150 health workers to provide timely, quality and confidential PSS and rape treatment 
c.	Promote mobilization of women and girls to access services through the establishment of 15 safe spaces for women and girls (WGSS) to reach 3000 women and girls
d.	Strengthen referral pathways for dissemination and access to services reach 2000 women, girls, boys and men.
e.	Provide 2,000 dignity kits and 36 post rape kits dignity protection for women and girls and treatment of rape
f.	Support 200 women and girls’ survivors of GBV with skills and grants for livelihood

project_name: Improve access to adequate, safe and dignified water & sanitation facilities and improve hygiene practices among children and their families of displace rohingya population to reduce associate public health risks
project_objective: The project support on improvement of existing WASH facilities and installation of new facilities on requirement to provide safe, adequate and dignified WASH services to Refugee in the camps. All available WASH facilities especially the latrines and bathing units, in targeted camps/area, will be improved and rehabilitated meeting emergency WASH standards. It is aim to provide water supply access with installation of bore hole as per need including pumping and distribution network on selected area. Likewise, decentralize Fecal Sludge Management (FSM) unit will be constructed and regular desludge will be carried for sustainable management of sludge generated. The activities will be implemented in coordination with the community; WASH committee will be formed and capacitate to able to construct, operate and maintain the facilities. Hygiene promotion activities will be intensified with better access to hygiene product to improve the hygiene practice contributing towards the behavior change and to increase health assistance seeking behavior. Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) session will be target to women and adolescent girls and community base solid waste collection and management activity will initiate with this project.  Access pathway, lighting system at WASH facilities will be ensure by project to increase access, dignity and protection.

project_name: Primary, Maternal and Child Health Care for FDMN and host communities, Cox's Bazar
project_objective: The aim of this project is to improve the general health status and health awareness of FDMNs (Forcebly Displaced Myanmar Nationals) and bangladeshi host communities, including maternal and child health. Activities will include providing primary health care support through established health post, improving knowledge amount FDMNs in relation to personal hygiene, family planning and nutrition, and to improve nutritional needs of pregnant mothers and malnourished children through advice on nutrition and assistant on nutritional suppliment.

project_name: Alternative learning opportunities and support for Rohingya refugee and host community children and young people in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
Our Education in Emergencies (EiE) Programme's ambition is to increase equitable access to culturally and age appropriate care, learning and development through early childhood education and parenting. Plan International also aims to provide primary education to children aged 3-14 and work with out-of-school and drop out children (boys and girls) to increase their access to safe protective and inclusive educational opportunities. We also work towards building and strengthening the capacity of teachers and other education personnel for improved quality education for all children.

Plan International Bangladesh is implementing a one-year education in emergency response in support of the Rohingya refugees’ education program through compendium of community-based and mobile approaches in reaching the target beneficiaries in Cox’s Bazar refugee camps. 
Plan International will continue to implement EiE activities based on ambitious and locally contextualized innovative approaches that have been able to witness increased enrolment of children into learning centres. To date, 13,520 refugee and host community children of age 3-17 years as well as 500 Youth and Adolescent targeted for support. 50% of the beneficiaries reached are female. This coming year we plan to expand our programming to provide increased access and opportunity for children in the highest-need camps and surrounding host community. 

Our innovative approaches are a combination of home-based and community-based learning centers. We will rollout three models for basic education (ages 7-14) and a model of home-based pre-primary (ages 3-6). These have been successfully piloted during the 2018 year and as part of the previous 2018 Joint Response Plan and will build on this success and lessons learnt to provide better access and better quality education to a target of 31836 refugee and host community children and adolescents. 

Each learning center is clustered into learning communities which have a focal point and an Alternative Learning School Management Committee to help oversee, monitor and provide feedback on the learning centers and the project at large.

project_name: Improved Prevention and Response to Gender Based Violence in two camps in Ukhia,Cox Bazar District.
project_objective: The project will provide improved access to quality survivor centered services responding to individual needs, prevention and mitigating of GBV risks, and empowerment of women, girls and survivors of GBV. Beneficiary number 29899.

project_name: Improving Access to Basic Safe Water Supply, Sanitation and hygiene practices in UN-House POCs-Juba and Bor Host Communities in Central Equotoria and Jonglei States.
project_objective:

*To sustain and improve water supply for IDPs and targeted Juba and Bor host communities through drilling (14) and rehabilitation (14) of hand pumps, Installation of solar power water scheme(0ne in Juba and 0ne in bor) and repairs of water points in POCs (20) and Mahad IDP camp (5).
* Hygiene promotion activities in Juba and Bor Host Communities through training of 32 Community Hygiene Promotors in both Juba and Bor to disseminate  Hygiene messages to the beneficiaries.
*Formation and Training of School Health Club members in 2 selected schools in Juba and 2 selected schools in Bor

project_name: LEBANON - Japan Campaign for children of Palestine
IRAQ - Peace Winds Japan
Emergency Water and Sanitation Service Provision for Conflict Affected Population in the Lake region
project_objective: The project will contribute to improve health and living conditions of the returnees, IDPs and host communities through a provision of safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion in the regions affected by the Boko Haram in Lake region. Women and under five children represent more than half of this population

project_name: Integrated child protection interventions in the nutrition emergency response in Chad Sahel Belt and Lake Chad Region
project_objective:
Les crises nutritionnelles récurrentes qui continuent à frapper le Tchad touchent notamment les enfants de moins de 5 ans où les taux de malnutrition aigüe globale dépassent généralement le seuil d’urgence de 15%. En aout 2018 (SMART 2018), 12 régions (soit une région sur deux) présentent des prévalences supérieures au seuil d’urgence (15%) selon la classification de l’OMS. 
En conformité avec le Protocol de prise en charge national, la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigüe doit aussi comprendre un volet de réhabilitation émotionnelle et de stimulation psychosociale. La strategie du SCPE souligne egalement l’importance d’une prise en charge psychosociale des enfants et partent(s) affectes. Afin de répondre aux besoins des enfants (filles et garçons) de moins de 5 ans souffrants de la malnutrition aigue sévère (MAS) avec complications en 2019, l’Unicef accompagnera la Prise en Charge Intégrée de la Malnutrition Aigüe (PCIMA) avec complications par une stimulation émotionnelle des enfants affectes et la personne  accompagnante. 
La stratégie de réponse prendra en considération les aspects liées à l’égalité des sexes, à la protection et à l’équité et un rôle important sera attribué aux bénéficiaires dans toutes les étapes de la réponse.
Le projet s’intègre parfaitement avec la réponse nutritionnelle notamment le programme PCIMA et permet de construire des ponts solides entre l’urgence et le développement en renforçant aussi la résilience des communautés.

project_name: Appui à une éducation inclusive de qualité aux filles et garçons (âgées de 3 - 17 ans) réfugiés de l'Est du Tchad
project_objective: Cet appui se traduit concretement par le renforcement de capacité des enseignants, des associations des parents d'élèves, des mères d'élèves par quelques formations proposées pour ces differentes entites pré-citées. En outre il est aussi judicieux que les bénéficiaires et les formateurs diposent une certaine quantité de matériel pour que l'apprentissage puisse se derouler sans faille ( kits scolaires, kits de dignite, matériels didactiques, manuels scolaires). Il est primordial que l'appui en éducation prenne en compte la petite enfance notamment le prescolaire ceci contribue énormément pour la suite du curcus de l'enfant en terme d'évolution ( habilité a écrire, transmissions de connaissance chez l'enfant de 3 a 5ans). C'est pourquoi quelques activités proposées par rapport aux prescolaires (matériels,formations des monitrices et autres etc...).

project_name: Strengthening Resilience through Child-Centred Programming
project_objective: The project is built upon the Ecological Model of Child Development with the intention to strengthen various levels to support to the most vulnerable children, including adolescent boys, adolescent and frequently home-bound girls and children with disabilities. The project seeks to promote social-cohesion through opening services to both host and refugee communities in an effort to integrate children and caregivers in specific activities. The project will bring new focus to meeting the needs of marginalized groups; reaching the most vulnerable children and families through integrated mobile teams; developthe capacity of local community structures and promotes self-reliance at the individual and household level, while integrating host community programming that combines both target groups with the aim of generating better understanding.
