project_objective: WASH interventions to rapidly meet the immediate basic needs of the most vulnerable and facilitate transition to a more sustained humanitarian response.

project_name: Ecuador - Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society
Ecuador - Dialogo Diverso
Ecuador - World Vision
Mejora de las prácticas de higiene y del acceso de la población vulnerable a servicios básicos y resilientes de agua, higiene y saneamiento
project_objective:
El análisis de necesidades del sector ha destacado que el acceso a agua, saneamiento e higiene en las comunidades ha sido afectado de forma crítica, tanto en términos de cobertura, de calidad, de continuidad como en cuanto al acceso de las personas a productos básicos de higiene. En el contexto actual, es necesario implementar acciones de gran escala para la recuperación de los sistemas existentes de previo a la crisis, y aumentar la percepción de riesgo de las comunidades, que deben adaptar sus prácticas a una situación con mayor riesgo de enfermedades de origen hídrico.  

Con el proyecto, se trabajará en dos líneas:
-Recuperar los servicios de abastecimiento de agua potable y sistemas de saneamiento en las comunidades, tanto a nivel urbano, peri-urbano como rural, en colaboración con las instituciones encargadas del servicio (hidroven, municipalidades, etc.). 
-Empoderar a las comunidades en la adopción de prácticas básicas de higiene y de tratamiento y conservación del agua en el hogar, a través de la implementación de una estrategia de comunicación para el desarrollo y de la mejora del acceso a productos básicos para un impacto inmediato y como facilitadores del cambio sostenible de comportamiento. 

Con el proyecto, se abordarán causas inmediatas y estructurales para mejorar los sistemas de abastecimiento de agua potable y los servicios de saneamiento. Inicialmente, se priorizarán acciones de impacto inmediato, tales como:
-Diagnóstico de las instalaciones estratégicas e identificación de las acciones prioritarias. 
-Rehabilitación de fuentes existentes de agua subterránea para abastecer a hospitales y camiones-cisternas; incluyendo la instalación de puntos de cloración (cloro residual). 
-Rehabilitación y fortalecimiento de fuentes superficiales existentes para distribución de agua (cloradores, plantas móviles de tratamiento de agua, etc.); de donde se abastecen camiones-cisternas y puntos estratégicos de la red de agua. 
-Refuerzo de la distribución de agua a través de camiones cisterna, a través de la reparación de los camiones existentes o del aumento de la flota (alquiler) para distribución de agua en puntos estratégicos en caso de contingencia (como fallos eléctricos). 
-Apoyo para control y monitoreo de la calidad del agua en puntos estratégicos (cloración en línea/equipos móviles de medición).
-Distribución de tabletas purificadoras y promoción de buenas prácticas en tomas de agua informales.
-Instalación de generadores eléctricos en puntos estratégicos para asegurar el bombeo de agua en contingencias eléctricas. 

Además del trabajo para la recuperación de los servicios públicos, se trabajará en la línea de agua, saneamiento e higiene con la población vulnerable. En este sentido, se priorizarán las siguientes actividades: 
-Elaboración e implementación de la Estrategia de Comunicación para el Desarrollo para la promoción de las prácticas clave de higiene y de tratamiento y conservación del agua a domicilio en poblaciones vulnerables, incluyendo una primera fase de incremento de la percepción de riesgo, necesaria para comprender el contexto actual y lo importante de la adoptación de prácticas adecuadas. 
-Promoción de prácticas de adecuadas vinculadas al control de vectores, como la eliminación de criadores de mosquitos en el hogar, la utilización de mosquiteros por parte de la población vulnerable (como mujeres gestantes, etc.), y acciones de movilización social. 
-Promoción de prácticas adecuadas de saneamiento e higiene en el hogar


En la actualidad, según los datos disponibles indican que el acceso a servicios básicos (según términos ODS) está comprometido, con alrededor un estimado de 9,000,000 de personas vulnerables que no tienen acceso a agua todos los días; de los cuales 4,300,000 no reciben agua por lo menos una vez por semana

project_name: LEBANON - Relief International
LEBANON - Terre des Hommes - Italy
Regional - International Organization for Migration
WASH Support for displaced and conflict affected communities in Baggari Corridor and Jur River County
project_objective: This intervention is meant to provide access to safe water and improved sanitation support to conflict affected and Internally displaced and vulnerable host communities affected in Jur River and Bagarri Corridor of Wau County

project_name: Provision of life saving WASH assistance and improvement of health standards for displacement affected communities in Middle Shabelle, Bay and Bakool regions of Somalia
project_objective:
This Action aims at implementing lifesaving responses for the displacement affected communities. The project aims to increase access to safe water and improve sanitation and hygiene in an effort to reduce the transmission of AWD/cholera and water borne diseases for the host community, IDPs and returnees in the regions of Middle Shabelle, Bay and Bakool. The current WASH gaps cited in thethree regions are: depletion of water source, lack of improved sanitation, high water prices, inadequate quantity and quality of water due to recurrent drought across the country and influx of IDPs which increase the demand for WASH facilities. INTERSOS intends to intervene to ensure rapid and sustained WASH services at key health and nutrition centers as well as in any strategic basic services' provision facility in areas highly affected by displacement. For this reason, schools will be targeted to both retain and reintegrate children in schools in a safely and dignified manner, with a focus in providing wash services for girls (i.e. sanitary pads) to ultimately improve hygiene standards and access to education. During the intervention, Water Committees, composed equally by women and men to represent equally the community, will be trained to manage wash facilities and scale up hygiene promotion to prevent potential AWD/Cholera outbreak, thus to build resilience and promotion of preparedness and disaster risk reduction mechanisms. 
INTERSOS is committed to ensuring that its programs are gender sensitive and achieve the Gender Marker scale. Women and girls have been adversely affected by the conflict, mainly due to breakdown in community protection mechanisms. Therefore, particular attention will be given to Lactating, pregnant women and children (0-5 years old) visiting Nutrition Centers, who will be provided with Hygiene Kits. Menstrual hygiene products and specific targeted items will be included as part of the hygiene kits.
To guarantee communities' engagement, consultation in all planning and implementation phases of the project will be constant. In addition, water distribution points and sanitation facilities will be established in areas that are safe and appropriate for women to access and will be designed considering people with disability in the community. INTERSOS will use its established female community network to divulgate hygiene promotion messages. A feedback and complaints mechanism will be put in place and beneficiaries provided with a hotline number in order to ensure accountability towards the affected population.

project_name: Provision of Basic and Life Saving Primary Health Care service for conflict and drought affected vulnerable populations/IDPs in Benadir and Lower Shabelle Region
project_objective:
The project intends to ensure access to basic primary and life-saving health care services for 43,200 Vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities including 12,500 Girls, 12,500 Boys, 14,200 Women and 4000 
affected in Daynile, Bondhere, Dharkenley District IDPs/drought affected In Mogadishu and Afgooye Corridor for Health centers of Lower Shabelle region. SOYDA through this project will provide life-saving medical consultations and drugs to the health facility, establish referral mechanisms between SOYDA facilities and secondary healthcare providers in Banadir region, improve the coverage of measles vaccinations and Vitamin A; and support safe motherhood and reproductive health while also ensuring readiness to prevent and respond to outbreaks such as malaria, measles or Acute Watery Diarrhea AWD/Cholera and promote health update through health education and beneficiary sensitization as well as linking this with the nutrition program in order to enable provide a holistic services within the organization target site.

project_name: Provision of Live Saving Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition among vulnerable affected IDPs and Host Communities of Under Five Children, Pregnant and Lactating Women in Benadir and South West -Lower Shabelle Region
project_objective: The proposed project aims at providing integrated Nutrition treatment and prevention services for drought affected under five boys, girls and caregivers in Daynile, Kahda, Dharkenley of Benadir region and Afgoye corridor of Lower Shabelle region. It will contribute to reduction of nutrition related morbidity and mortality rates. SOYDA intervention will target pregnant and lactating mothers together with children aged below 5 years among the host communities, IDPs and returnees. Active case finding for malnourished cases will be done through mass screening of children aged below 5 years and pregnant and lactating mothers for rapid identification of malnourished cases. Moderate acutely malnourished children and pregnant and lactating mothers will be referred for enrolment in the SFP programs run by other actors in Benadir and Lower Shabelle Region The project will support a network of 11 fixed Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP and 8 mobile sites fully equipped with OTP commodities including Ready To Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF), essential medicines for treatment of communicable diseases, vaccines, trained OTP nurses, vaccinators and hygiene promoters. The trained OTP nurses will treat severe acutely malnourished children in the static and mobile OTPs according to IMAM protocol. Mass screening will be done by trained health workers deployed in the 8 mobile clinics and trained 30 CHWs each assigned at least one village in the areas covered by the project. Immunization status of all children screened will be checked by both static and mobile OTP staff and children who are eligible for vaccination and do not have updated immunization status will be immunized by the vaccinators and assistant vaccinators in the mobile OTPs. Severe acutely malnourished children with medical complications will be referred by the mobile clinics and the CHWs to the stabilization Centre in Afgooye and Benadir hospital for nutrition rehabilitation. Hygiene promoters will during the activities of the mobile clinics disseminate hygiene promotion messages to the communities to prevent outbreak and spread of communicable diseases like AWD/cholera and measles. During the same time, mothers will be counseled individually and in groups by trained health workers and Community Health Workers (CHWs) on appropriate maternal infant and young child feeding as part of efforts to prevent malnutrition. The project will also provide micronutrient support by distributing multiple micronutrients (MNPs) and Vitamin A supplements through the static and mobile clinics. Staff dedicated to the static and mobile OTPs will be subjected to proper trainings on infant and young child feeding, integrated management of acute malnutrition and nutrition, health and hygiene promotion. Efforts will also be made to link households with children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) conditions and suspected cholera cases to WASH interventions and food security/ livelihood programs. There will be regular coordination meetings at the field level between WASH, Health and Nutrition clusters to foster synergy, avoid duplication of efforts/ resources and share information on response efforts. SOYDA will keep the nutrition cluster, Ministry of Health and UNOCHA regularly informed on progress of activities through sharing of progress reports and also share any challenges encountered for rapid assistance.

project_name: Life saving assistance to crisis affected populations of Somalia through improving their access to food and promoting livelihood opportunities
project_objective: The Project is aimed at life-saving humanitarian response by reducing household food consumption gaps in drought- and flood- affected districts of Somalia with life-saving multi-purpose cash. Additionally, ACTED will ensure provision of livelihood-specific and seasonally appropriate inputs for both rural and urban populations, including through formation of Agro Pastoral Field Schools, livestock restocking and support to community animal health workers, as well as cash grants to support Village Savings and Loan Associations. ACTED will also promote restoration of community productive assets and disaster preparedness. This intervention will result in improved household income, assets and community resilience and risk mitigation capacity.

project_name: Provision of emergency and sustainable safe water, sanitation and hygiene to drought/AWD and flood affected communities in South Central Somalia
project_objective:
The project will provide immediate access to safe drinking water to 15,000 vulnerable population boys,girls,women and men affected by the drought and other natural disaster, HIDIG intends to rehabilitates 15 shallow wells benefiting 15,000 men, women and children  to enable enhanced the  community access to safe drinking water. The project will also provide the target beneficiaries with hygiene kits as well as provide hygiene promotion to ensure community is aware of the water born risk as well as sanitation and other vector born disease. Through this HIDIG will ensure to establish 19 water management committee at IDPs and rehabilitate 19 water sources to enable ease the water related protection risk among the community in the target location.
HIDIG will construct both IDPs latrines as well as health facilities and schools to ensure proper sanitation in the target areas. Through this project HIDIG will ensure the project is coordinated across other  sector as well as regional leadership to enable have  better and well managed program

project_name: Provision of  quality and timely protection services in Afgoye corridor
project_objective:
The intent of the project is to fill the existing critical gaps in protection targeting  14,000 beneficiaries in Afgoye corridor particularly Kahda district. The purpose of the intervention is to reduce the incidents of SGBV and providing child protection services in the community living in Kahda. The project is intended to respond, have positive impact in reducing SGBV and improving the life of children and help the community to have behaviour change towards GBV.
Most of the peeople who are violated particularly in the IDP camps  are women, they have limited information and their rights are violated to the extreme therefore the project will enlighten the GBV survivors on our centres to seek protection services.

The other vital purpose of the project is to respond to GBV incidents by providing quality survivors centred services. The protection activities include counselling, medical support, referral, awareness and sensitization and legal services to overcome trauma and depression. The child protection services will include establishment of Child friendly spaces, identification, documentation and reunification of children with their families.

Material supplies for GBV survivors and children will be provided. This include dignity kits,  solar lamps, child playing materials and children clothing.

project_name: Provision of Integrated approach to preventing and responding to child rights violations and gender based violence (GBV) for the displaced persons and most vulnerable host communities in Benadir and Lower Shabelle Region
project_objective:
This project seeks to sustain and scale up lifesaving GBV prevention and response services in the IDPs in Mogadishu and  along Afgooye corridor to prevent and respond to protection risks/concerns experienced by women, men and children affected by droughts especially in Internally Displaced Peoples camps but also in the host populations. Gender based violence survivors through integrated cluster approach. The proposed integrated child protection and gender based violence interventions will address the most urgent and critical protection issues in Dharkenley, Daynile, Kahda district of Mogadishu and Afgooye corridor, Lower Shabelle region focusing primarily on the internally displaced population. SOYDA will ensure to intervene on timely, effective and holistic manner to the protection needs of mainly children and women of the displaced communities in our target areas. The project will address both child right violations and gender based violation through existing inter- agency referral mechanism. SOYDA runs community health services in 10 different locations in Dharkenley, Daynile, Kahda district of Mogadishu and Afgooye corridor, Lower Shabelle region; This project will be integrated in the existing health projects so that we strengthen both protection and health service provision. Mobile CPIE and SGBV activities will be undertaken in response to any new displacement and needs including when there is new displacement or influx. SOYDA has strong and solid outreach protection and health programming and this project will fit into that modality of programming. The project will significantly strengthen and significantly scale –up the on- going case management response services in targeted communities. The key focus will be to scale up prevention and response to separation of children from their families through family tracing and reunification activities and gender based violence survivors. Mainstreaming child protection to other service providers to ensure compassionate, confidential, and competent action for children in emergencies. The project will invest in building the capacity of the both protection and health sectors staff on provision of psychological first aid to the highly psychological distress community members as part of the first line emergency response. The project aims to provide immediate life-saving assistance to vulnerable populations. Beneficiaries will receive comprehensive case management and psycho-social support (PSS), including emergency care, referral to SOYDA medical teams trained in clinical management of rape (CMR), access tailored material assistance, basic emotional support, and follow up on the services. Capacity building of duty bares including formal and informal authorities to strengthen and improve identification. Mainstreaming child protection to other service providers to ensure compassionate, confidential, and competent action for children in emergencies.
SOYDA will closely working with all coordination structures such as Federal Government and States line ministries,  protection cluster AORs and working groups in Mogadishu and  Baido.

project_name: Prevention and treatment of acute Malnourished Boys, Girls, pregnant and lactating women through Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) with stabilization center services to avert nutrition related morbidity and mortality in middle shabelle region
project_objective: The project seeks to provide emergency and lifesaving nutrition services to vulnerable drought-affected populations living in Balcad district of Middle Shabelle.  The intervention will target pregnant and lactating women (PLW) together with children under the age of 5 years among host communities, IDPs and returnees in Balcad district where we are the primary rationalized partner, Wocca will operate one fixed outpatient therapeutic center and 3 mobile out- patient therapeutic programme teams targeting six drought-affected villages/settlements in Balcad district. The static facility will be established in Muki-dheere settlement with the highest population among the targeted locations while the three outreach teams will serve 5 locations namely; Kurshaale, Mareerey, Bulo sheikh, Bananey and Bulo Doonka villages. WOCCA will engage UNICEF, who will support the project by facilitating training of the project staff ,community health workers and hygiene promoters on nutrition screening, case identification and Integrated management of acute malnutrition(IMAM).The trained staff shall be deployed to the targeted villages, mobile and static OTPs where they will screen children under 5 and PLWs. Children under 5 with SAM conditions and no medical complications will be enrolled to the static and mobile OTPs for treatment while the cases with medical complications will be referred by the mobile clinics and CHWs to the SC in Waberi star village managed by WOCCA for nutrition rehabilitation. Children under 5 and PLWs with MAM conditions will be referred to TSFP center managed by SHARDO. The project will also provide micronutrient support by distributing multiple micronutrients (MNPs) and Vitamin A supplements to pregnant and lactating women and children under the age of 5years through the static and mobile facilities.UNICEF has been supporting WOCCA with nutrition supplies and technical guidance on previous nutrition projects within the targeted locations and currently supporting our SHF funded project running in Daynille and Kaxda camps. Therefore, for this project WOCCA will also engage with UNICEF to provide nutrition supplies and technical support for management of SAM cases .

project_name: Provision of improved access to Emergency and lifesaving health care services to vulnerable boys, girls, men and women from host communities, internally displaced population and returnees through a fixed health facility in Balcad District, Middle Shabelle region.
project_objective: This project will deliver lifesaving emergency health services including maternal, neonatal and child health through a fixed health facility targeting seven settlements in Balcad district Middle Shebelle namely Waberi star, Qalimow, Hawo tako, Ceel Gelow, Farax gololey, Horseed and Halgan with a total population of 87438 persons. The health facility will be equipped with essential medicines and equipment and trained staff to provide quality services. Emphasis will be laid on Maternal and Child Health, including Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEmONC) and Expanded Programme on Immunization, EPI, to beneficiary communities. This action will focus on provision of both preventive and curative health services at primary level integrated with nutrition, WASH and protection components. Attention will be paid on application of treatment guidelines as per Essential package of Health Services, EPHS at the Primary healthcare, PHC. Building the capacity of health workers through training on integrated Management of childhood illness (IMCI) and infection control, Antenatal care,ANC and BEmONC will be done to equip health workers with pertinent skills to deliver quality health care services to the affected population. 7 staff, 1 for each of the targeted settlements, will be trained on emergency/cholera preparedness and response to equip them with skills and knowledge to be able to effectively respond to epidemic outbreaks. This project will deliver comprehensive reproductive health care to women of reproductive age among the target beneficiaries and promotion of health seeking behavior including adoption of preventive practices through campaigns, health and hygiene education sessions. Health and hygiene promotion will mostly be done by 12 trained CHWS, 2 from each of the targeted settlements. The project will also contribute to strengthening early warning disease surveillance through weekly submission of CSR reports from the health facility. Referral system for patients seeking secondary healthcare services will be facilitated to the recognized referral hospitals on pregnant women requiring more specialized emergency services, victims of armed conflicts, casualties from accidents, trauma cases among others. The project will also refer GBV victims to the wocca health facilities or any of the above mentioned facilities for comprehensive care and psycho-social support. This project will complement a Wocca run nutrition project, funded by SHF and UNICEF but now in final stages of being fully funded by UNICEF, Children with severe acute malnutrition will also be referred to nutrition centers for nutrition care and rehabilitation. Finally, Wocca will coordinate with Health, WASH, and Nutrition clusters to coordinate response activities for maximum impact to beneficiaries.

project_name: Traitement de la malnutrition aigue dans les zones affectees par la secheresse
Bureaucratic Impediments Liaison Unit (BLU)
project_objective:
A clear and practicable regulatory environment is a critical prerequisite for access and a principled humanitarian response.  NGOs have regularly cited to NCCI that bureaucratic lack of clarity, inconsistencies, frequent changes and overlapping jurisdictions to be among the greatest challenges facing NGOs Iraq.  This results in reduced access, visa & registration challenges, delays and additional costs for NGOs in Iraq.  community needs centralized regulatory guidance and support to help advocate for a positive and clarified regulatory environment.  

NCCI will continue the critical work of a bureaucratic liaison unit (BLU) prioritizing NGO oriented solutions to bureaucratic impediments.  BLU will work closely with government authorities and other external actors to understand new and changing regulatory policies and practices, and to communicate those to the NGO community. The BLU will work with NGOs to report and analyse the challenges being faced by NGOs and to clearly communicate those back to relevant government stakeholders.  The BLU’s integration of NCCI Advocacy, knowledge management and coordination capacity help the NGO community in Iraq assure access and effectiveness through positive collaboration with government stakeholders.

project_name: LEBANON - Himaya Daee Aataa Association
Emergency Livestock Response through Vaccination and Treatment in Bor South County of Jonglei State
project_objective: As the crisis in South Sudan entered its 5th consecutive year in 2018, 5.3 million people, (42% of the population) are in need of life-saving food assistance, an increase of 40% over 2017 of people facing severe food insecurity soon after crop harvest. East Coast Fever (ECF) disease has claimed more than 20,000 heads of cattle in the Jonglei state and its neighboring States (Lakes, Warrap and Equatorias) in the past 5 years. Losses caused by the disease are due to high mortality rates are estimated to be at USD 134,325 annually .  Survival among the predominantly pastoral communities (displaced and host) has been buoyed up by food aid which is presently contributing up to 30% of food consumed at household level, and increased utilization and liquidation of livestock products and livestock assets among livestock owning households. Livestock derived food is making up to 60% for host groups and 81% for IDPs (up from about 42% in 2013) of the food basket in 2017/18. The pressure on livestock keepers to exchange their animals for food for survival has spurred a rebound of livestock markets in Western Jonglei (covering Uror, Nyiror, Duk, Twic East and Bor South). However, the concentration of livestock in confined spaces has significantly enhanced the spread of communicable diseases among livestock, resulting in losses of up to 35% in areas without services. The objective of the action is to improve or sustain access to animal source food and related income for crisis affected individuals at risk of malnutrition particularly children and women. This is aimed at impacting on health and nutrition of the affected pastoralists, thereby saving lives that may be lost through attributed excess morbidity. The project will target 7000 households in Bor South County, comprised of IDP, host and returnee groups with support to local institutions and mechanisms for delivery of Animal health and public health services. VSF Germany will employ two livestock protection interventions – vaccination and treatment using the Community based Animal Health Service approach. These exercises are carried out in accordance to the annual dry season vaccination plan issued by the Ministry of Animal Resources and Fisheries (MARF) & FAO which is based on region specific disease seasonal calendar. The exercises will involve mass vaccination of 100,000 heads of livestock and about 25,000 cases of treatment against East Coast Fever disease. VSF Germany will use its disease surveillance and response systems.  Cattle camp chiefs communicate herd disease situations systematically to their Community based Animal Health Workers (CAHWs). This is then reported to Animal Health Auxiliaries, to Stock Persons and to Veterinarians who carry out preliminary investigations and where necessary make outbreak reports to VSF and MARF. MARF with support of VSF and FAO carries out confirmation investigations and defines immediate and longer term intervention plans.

project_name: Building Resilience and Food Security in South Sudan
project_objective: This project will be implemented in Bor, Twic East, Duk, Pibor and Uror counties in Jonglei state. The 2019 project includes different interventions including support to farming, livestock and fisheries producer groups with a range of livelihoods interventions including but not limited to training, inputs like vegetable kits, staple crops’ kits and tools. The project will provide 9,421 MT of target unconditional food and conditional food assistance. The project will also establish and strengthen community structures like the disaster risk reduction committees to be able to plan and respond to disasters. They will then implement various small projects of their choice through food for assets.

project_name: Proyecto de fortalecimiento de medios de vida de familias vulnerables y sus comunidades en los Estados Dto. Capital, Miranda, Zulia, Carabobo y Sucre
project_objective:
La crisis que afecta a Venezuela desde hace algunos años tiene las características de una situación de instalación lenta:  
•	Aumento de la precariedad de los hogares en situación de vulnerabilidad. 
•	Desgaste de los medios de vida y los capitales familiares.
•	Dificultades para la eficacia de respuestas asistenciales por el colapso de servicios básicos.   
Es necesario apoyar a los hogares en el fortalecimiento y diversificación de sus medios de vida para mitigar el efecto de la crisis sobre su seguridad alimentaria, a la vez que se apoyen actividades asistenciales y de bienestar comunitarias. Se quiere iniciar un proyecto que permita hacer en simultáneo intervenciones tipo redes de protección social (social safety nets) y asistencia inmediata. 
El proyecto se orientará a: 
•	Comprender mejor los medios de vida familiar en las zonas vulnerables de los Estados priorizados.
•	Apoyar a los hogares en el fortalecimiento de los medios de vida familiar o diversificar los existentes con rendimiento asistencial a la comunidad.
•	Mejorar la integración entre las actividades de asistencia nutricional en servicios de salud, con las de resiliencia de medios de vida a nivel familiar. Esto se hará facilitando la operatividad de la referencia y contrareferencia entre puestos de salud y unidades parroquiales en las que Caritas da asistencia ambulatoria a niños con desnutrición aguda sin complicaciones.
Se espera realizar actividades de formación en oficios, asignación de subvenciones comunitarias (cash grants) y transferencias monetarias familiares (vouchers) para la, reparación, mantenimiento y funcionamiento efectivo de infraestructuras comunitarias y mejoramiento del acceso a los servicios de salud (instalaciones sanitarias de escuelas y dispensarios, reparación de flota de transporte colectivo). Se intentaría, con predilección, apoyar una o varias de estas iniciativas (a discutirse con la comunidad):
	Capacitación en oficios básicos y relevantes para la rehabilitación de servicios e infraestructuras.
	Activación de una ruta de transportes de bajo coste que permita un medio de vida para las personas que se integren, a la vez que sirva de transporte hacia servicios esenciales (hospitales, escuelas, mercados).
	Subvenciones a juntas parroquiales para la contratación y provisionamiento de cuadrillas de vecinos para la recolección de desechos y mantenimiento de zonas limpias.
	Facilitar la vinculación de pequeños productores de áreas periurbanas a mercados urbanos y lugares en los que pueda asignar sus mercancías (ferias alimentarias, mercados campesinos, comedores).
El proyecto se realizará en parroquias en las que Caritas tiene en curso proyectos de protección nutricional y estrechos vínculos con servicios comunitarios (Miranda, Carabobo, Zulia, Sucre y Distrito Capital).

project_name: JORDAN - World Relief Deutschland e.V.
JORDAN - Save the Children
Columbia - United Nations Food and Agricultural Organization

Increase Access to Basic Education in emergency and crises affected areas for the vulnerable children and IDPs in Merka, Qoryooley, Wanlaweyn, Awdhegle and Kurtunwarey districts, Lower Shabelle region.
project_objective:
The main purpose of this project is to access primary schools in Lower Shabelle region particularly Merka, Qoryooley, Kurtunwarey, Wanlaweyn and Awdhegle districts, the objective is to enable vulnerable schools aged children and youth with immediate access of learning opportunities, support learners retention, improvement of learning environment and strengthening and improvement of quality of effective service delivery. In addition more focus will be paid on system strengthening to ensure sustainability and enhancing education capacity particularly with a focus on strengthening education in emergencies preparedness, response planning of the education system, AYUUB will get advantage on the new liberated areas and provide free access to primary schools, through this AYUUB will collaborate with the Ministry of Education of South West State.
The community is the primary source, the owners of the schools, they will co-lead the implementation of the program, the CECs will be trained on the management of the schools, water management and school feeding administration.
Special care and priority will be given the  vulnerable and marginalized girls and boys for the internally displaced persons and food insecure communities in Merka, Qoryooley, Kurtunwarey, Wanlaweyn and Awdhegle districts in Lower Shabelle region.
AYUUB will target 3,500 persons (1600 fem) 80 teachers(30 fem), 120 CEC members (60 female) by providing incentives & quality trainings to teachers & CECs, provide emergency incentives for teachers, establish new TLS & ensure learners have access to learning materials & provide safe drinking water as well as school feeding in Merka, Qoryooley, Kurtunwarey, Awdhegle & Wanlaweyn districts.
AYUUB, being also the Education leading cluster in the region will work closely with the line ministries and Education cluster for a coordinated integrated response approach,  AYUUB will continue to work closely with WASH, protection, Food Security and Nutrition to expand the provision of services to children in schools. This will ensure and  improve the teaching quality and retention of learners.

project_name: Improving food security and resilience for the conflict and drought affected communities in Lower Shabelle region.
project_objective:
The project will support the immediate recovery of drought affected people in Lower Shabelle region through provision of cash and food assistance and restoration of livelihood opportunities, while helping vulnerable people and building resilience through sustainable intervention. The project also connects to cover the need to enhance the productive capacities and coping mechanisms of displaced populations, in a way that promotes social cohesion and mitigates tensions. The project will struggle to build the capacities of community structures to be able to respond to disaster early warnings and all these will be tended towards improving food security and building community resilience while fostering disaster risk reduction. The primary focus will be to increase and diversify sources of incomes among targeted communities in with focus on sustainable sources. The project will Endeavour to build capacities of community to be able to cope with the changing times devised by Climate change; these would be realized through trainings and cash for work in the form of rehabilitation of community infrastructures. The aim of the project will be to alleviate chronic poverty and reverse vulnerability to drought shocks thus promoting self reliance in economics, social and cultural needs of project area populations as well as enable them live in harmony with their neighbors. Cash Programming will be conditional in nature and will be done in form of Cash for work; identified beneficiaries will participate in the rehabilitation of community infrastructure, and earn the cash needed to purchase food and other basic items and services.  Community Capacity Building is intended to ensure that communities have the skills and knowledge needed to plan for and cope with future livelihood shocks.

One of the primary objectives of the project is to build and fully equip the Communities which will be durable solution and will promote self sufficient, the Community will run directly and look after the implementation of each project, AYUUB will seek collaboration with the ministry lines  both Federal and state level and focus will be paid on system strengthening to ensure sustainability and enhancing  capacity particularly with focus on strengthening and self sufficient in emergencies preparedness, response planning of the  This strategy will support the Ministry of Agriculture  in Emergencies and engagement of community to realize effective response and fundraising upon the termination of the project. In addition the response will continue to invest in community mobilization of the local people and local authority as an integral part of broader programme. There are some good news from the Somali president who visited recently Merka district, the president ordered some of the Ministry lines to visit Merka and start lifesaving and development programs.

project_name: Stabilizing the learning environment for Palestine refugee children
project_objective: It is estimated that 80 per cent of the 278,938 students (male 143,973 and female 134,965) registered at UNRWA schools in the 2018/2019 school year in Gaza require assistance in overcoming a variety of challenges, including poverty, additional learning needs, access restrictions and electricity shortages at home. Recurrent hostilities and the blockade continue to have a deleterious impact on the learning environment for Palestine refugee children in Gaza, who are accommodated in 274 schools, 70 per cent of which operate on a double-shift basis. In response, the Agency-wide Education in Emergencies (EiE) approach provides inclusive, equitable, quality and safe education to Palestine refugee children and youth in times of emergencies. In addition to implementing the EiE approach across all Agency schools in Gaza, UNRWA will: (i) through the recruitment and training of additional support teachers and the provision of remedial materials, assist selected students in grades 3 and 4 who are struggling to meet minimum academic standards in Arabic and mathematics; and (ii) ensure that  80 percent of children have access to basic school and learning materials through the distribution of back-to-school and recreational kits and stationery. In line with  cluster logical frame work and plan, this intervention will target 15,558 students for remedial education assisted by 230  support teachers.

project_name: Strengthening FSL Sector Coordination at National and State Levels in Sudan
project_objective: The Food Security and Livelihoods Sector aims at improving the food and nutrition security situation of the most vulnerable refugees, returnees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and host communities in Sudan. The sector’s overall objectives are to respond in a timely manner to the immediate lifesaving humanitarian needs; improve and restore the livelihoods and self-reliance and promote nutrition sensitive interventions of the affected population. This FSL Sector Coordination project will 1) support timely, reliable and continuous data flow on food security and livelihoods related issues, where assessment findings are produced and disseminated; 2) provide overall strategic guidance to the sector members and all humanitarian actors; 3) support sector partners in capacity building initiatives and training opportunities on food and nutrition security related topics (example: food security concepts and indicators, Integrated Phase Classifications – IPC, monitoring and evaluation of FSL activities, agricultural and livestock technical standards, emergency preparedness, disaster risk reduction, etc.) to insure adoption of international standards and guidelines; 4) promote sector activities and support resource mobilization; 5) monitor partners’ interventions to minimize potential overlaps, ensure complementarity and address gaps; 6) ensure inter-sectoral coordination for a multi-dimensional response and mainstream protection, gender, and environment. This project will target about 20 agencies and 250 people who are members in the FSL sector with interventions that aim at building their capacity on food and nutrition security related topics including assessments, monitoring and evaluation, disaster risk reduction and emergency preparedness.

project_name: LEBANON - War Child Holland
Dignified living conditions and equitable access to services and assistance for IDPs living in sites and settlements, through enhanced coordination and with strengthened community participation
project_objective:
Through this project, DRC aims at creating an environment that facilitates the delivery services to affected populations and ensure that all displaced persons are enabled to participate meaningfully in the governance and management of the sites, as well as facilitate the engagement of site residents in care and maintenance activities aimed at improving accessibility, reducing hazards and protection and health risks. 
This will be done through establishment and strengthening of inclusive community governance structures and thematic committees at each site level, the engagement of these structures in CCCM coordination mechanisms alongside humanitarian partners active in the respective sites and representatives of relevant government and local authorities, as well as through continued support for capacity building, mainly through the delivery of trainings adapted to each type of participation (thematic IDP committee members, site governance members, local authority representatives). 
In addition to the strengthening of coordination and information sharing between all stakeholders, the project aims to support community led site maintenance activities to ensure upkeep of sites (through cash for work, establishment of site maintenance committees, distribution of tools) and implementation of emergency sites improvement projects (small infrastructure upgrades) that would minimize protection risks and ensure safety in sites (flood mitigation measures, installation of fire points, construction of foot bridges and walkways for improved accessibility, etc.). These specific interventions will be agreed upon in consultation with community representatives in each site. 
Furthermore, the project will enhance community communication and feedback mechanisms through construction of community information centers, employing community outreach mobile teams, establishing feasible and context-based feedback mechanisms and conducting awareness campaigns. 
To support opportunities for displaced people to achieve durable solutions, the project will contribute through community based initiatives that can promote community cohesion and recovery and as well as support communities in IDP sites towards self-reliance in locations where prospects of obtaining land rights is achievable. The project aims to reach over 150,000 drought and conflict displaced women, boys, men and girls.

project_name: Primary Health Care Services for the returned population at North Waziristan Tribal District - KP
project_objective:
The proposed project will fill the gaps in the delivery of essential lifesaving Primary Health Care (PHC) services to the vulnerable returned population of North Waziristan Tribal District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. For this purpose, EHSAR will target 4 government Health facilities (BHU level) in the targeted District of North Waziristan Tribal District. EHSAR will make transitional arrangements at existing 4 non-functional Government’s Health facilities. The services will include consultations and treatment of infectious diseases, management of acute and chronic health disorders, psychosocial support to mentally handicapped persons, MHCH services, support the government in routine immunization and vaccination, routine investigation through Laboratories, provision of lifesaving drug and other supplements and referrals of complicated cases to tertiary health facilities. EHSAR will supplement these services with health education and Hygiene Promotion activities.
Moreover, the targeted Health facilities will be renovated through minor repair, supplemented by solarization of the targeted health facilities, to ensure the smooth and facilitated operations of the health services. 
It is estimated that a total of 69,250 individuals will be benefited from this intervention in the proposed 9 months.

project_name: Humanitarian WASH Assistance for conflicted affected returnee population in Central Kurram
project_objective:
This Humanitarian WASH assistance project is designed in light of supporting return population in merged tribal district Kurram, enabling them to meet their immediate humanitarian WASH needs and hence protecting them from WASH related risks. 
It is likely that the provision of improved water, sanitation and hygiene facilities along with increased knowledge and capacity building of target population would reduce their vulnerability and would meet their humanitarian WASH needs to  great extent.
In this regards adequate access to safe & clean drinking water facilities would cater through rehabilitation/construction of 2 gravity water supply schemes, along with provision of 80 water storage tanks for HHs lacking safe storage means. In parallel, water safety plan would be developed and operation and maintenance training and tools will be provided for ensuring sustainability, community participation and ownership aspect.

For addressing immediate humanitarian sanitation needs, households/ compound sanitation facilities to extremely vulnerable households would be provided through community participation i.e mobilization for skilled and unskilled labour provision of locally available materials for latrine construction , that are culturally appropriate, secure, user friendly with focus on gender mainstreaming at community and institutional level. Humanitarian assistance would be provided through construction/rehabilitation of 190 low cost latrines at HHs level on component sharing approach focusing on PWDs, women/widow headed HHs, elderly, child headed, extended family size with low income for reducing open defecation along with the provision of twinset latrine and hand washing facility at one school level. 
In parallel MH would adopt Participatory, Hygiene Sanitation Transformation Training (PHAST) approach and would conduct hygiene awareness raising sessions in targeted area with the aim to improving their hygiene practices, to promote positive hygiene behaviors and increased understanding of key health WASH related risks to prevent most common waterborne diseases  and poor sanitation related risks in targeted villages of Zaimusht tribe in Central Kurram. Through participatory hygiene awareness raising the targeted community including men, women, girls & children would be sensitized keeping in due consideration the socio-cultural dynamics. This would be achieved through conducting 30 Hygiene sessions (20 women focused sessions for 500 women and adolescent girls @25 participants each session & 09 sessions targeting 225 men and 1 session targeting 01 government primary schools @25 participants each session. Alongside, 10 PHAST sessions would be conducted in 10 villages (1 session per village @20 participants/ session). In addition, 100 schools diaries with printed hygiene messages, 1000 IEC material & 950 hygiene kits would be distributed in areas of intervention.

Overall 6422 beneficiaries i.e. 5138 beneficiaries for water, 3853 for sanitation & 6422 through health & hygiene improved measures would be reached@ of 27% women, 26% men, 24% Girls and 23% Boys. The project would contribute to Gender Mainstreaming through producing an impact working on Gender Marker Code 2 (a) with equal and increased participation of women with men as decision makers, acting as a way in improving & maintaining female dignity. For this purpose separate men and women village WASH committees would be established for equal representation at all stages of project cycle.

A comprehensive M& E work Frame would be developed and practice for quality assurance at field level, whereas regional and country office random visits would be a value added to quality assurance in terms of monitoring and advising on the management of triple constraints of project.
Throughout the project life cycle closed coordination with line departments including F/PDMA, civil/ military administration, community elders and other relevant stakeholders would be maintained.

project_objective: Disaster risk reduction in schools

project_name: Restoring access to safe clean and sufficient water and improving hygiene practices in 4 districts of Manicaland Province (Mutare, Makoni , Mutasa and Buhera)
project_objective: The project intends to restore access to safe, clean and sufficient water and improve hygiene practices in 3 districts of Manicaland. The project will raise awareness on health and hygiene among the communities including religious groups in the target districts.There is need to stop the advance of water borne diseases in the province to save the lives of children, women and other vulnerable groups of the selected communities.

project_name: Renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages très pauvres et vulnérables aux risques de protection dans la Région de Tombouctou.
project_objective: Le projet sera basé sur deux composantes : l'assistance monétaire pour couvrir les besoins alimentaires et de première nécessité et répondre aux besoins de 1220 ménages les plus vulnérables lors de la soudure 2019, et l’intégration d’une expertise de protection transversale.

project_name: Health Program for Conflict Affected Population in Northern Syria 2019
project_objective:
Shafak's health program aims to contribute in the provision of access to life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian health services for people in need and conflict affected population in northern Syria. The proposed intervention will prioritize internally displaced people and other vulnerable populations especially (Women ,children and disabilities) in the targeted areas. The intervention will be implemented through:
1. Delivery of services per essential primary health care (PHC) Package that includes; Child health, including EPI, reproductive health, prevention and control of communicable diseases, prevention and treatment of non-communicable diseases, provision of essential medicines and medical supplies and equipment by supporting 3   primary health care facilities center in rural Aleppo.

2. The provision of emergency obstetric and newborn care (EMONC) services and management of SRH-related diseases to the specialized hospital for women and children which provide maternal and child health services to most vulnerable people in the rural of Idlib, Marretmasrin. 

3. Provision of health services through Mobile clinic for reaching communities that have a problem of access to primary health-care services in the rural of Aleppo. 
4- Supporting 2 dialysis centers 1 in Idlib and 1 in Aleppo governorate with running costs and dialysis kits. In addition to conduct capacity building and training for the medical staff of the two centers.
5- Distribution of needed dialysis kits, medications and consumables adequate for a lot of months by coordination with WHO,health directorate and the health clusters. 

By achieving the above components, Shafak aims to contribute in enhancing the health status in the targeted areas.

project_name: Water Assistance for Returnees and Host Population in Telkaif, Ninewa
project_objective:
NCA plans a project to rehabilitate and improve of the water supply networks in nine towns/villages located in Telkaif district, in the north-west of Ninewa governorate, about 30 kilometres from Mosul namely Telkaif, Tallskuf, Rashidiyah, Qawsiat, Bawizah, Sada, Tall Yabis, Najmok and Derke . Telkaif district is part of the so-called Nineveh plain, historically the homeland of most of Iraq’s minority groups, such as Christians (Assyrians and Chaldeans), Yezidis, Turkmen, Sunni Arabs and Shabaks (Shia Kurds) and is known for many archaeological sites e.g. Lalesh, the holy site for Yazidis. 
NCA aims to ensure sustainable access to adequate and safe drinking water, as well as enabling people to protect their health and prevent spread of waterborne diseases through hygiene promotion interventions, especially targeting at-risk groups like returnees. In this sense, the project is compatible with the priorities of the UN and of the Government of Iraq. Specifically, this project aims to ensure sustainable supply of drinking water to 9 towns/villages in Telkaif district, through the rehabilitation and improvement of sustainable and permanent water distribution networks. With much of the water distribution systems in disrepair in these places, the connection with Telkaif will not serve any benefit to local communities unless a complete overhaul of existing network is undertaken in the target areas.

project_name: Conflict Preparedness and Protection Safety & Risk Education in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Project Objective: Civilians living in high risk conflict-affected communities in the Gaza Strip are better prepared to protect themselves in case of armed conflict and are empowered with the knowledge they need to mitigate risks associated with explosive weapons.

The proposed interventions supplement the NPA Palestine Country Strategy 2016-2019 in Gaza and are aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 2: “Prevent and mitigate the effects of the Occupation and conflict related violence.” Project activities are also specifically aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 2 of the HRP, “Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence,” and will contribute to this objective through the provision of Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP) and Explosive Remnant of War (ERW) risk education for civilian residents (adults and children) of the Gaza Strip.

The proposed interventions are planned to take place in 2019, representing the second year of NPA's CPP implementation for 2018-2020. Over three-year programme period, the programme will be implemented using the same methodologies; training adults and children, but for new beneficiaries and new communities which will be prioritized based on Ministry of Education planning and in consultation with Protection Cluster and the Mine Action Working Group.

project_name: Emergency Lifesaving Support to Improve Shelter and NFIs for vulnerable protracted displacement affected IDPs, and Returnees in Duk and Uror Counties, Jonglei State, South Sudan
project_objective:
LWFs Shelter  and NFI project is targeting protracted conflict and displacement  affected most vulnerable IDPs, and Returnees who have been displaced due to a protracted crisis over the past one year or more years , compounded by inter-clan, inter-tribal violence and cattle raiding. LWF planned to reach 1700 HHs ( about 10,200 people) from IDPs, and Returnees communities in Duk and Uror counties through provision of emergency Shelter and  NFI kit for life saving. 

The beneficiaries’ selection can be done through community participation and lead of community based Cash Committees (CDCS). The process involves identification, registration and verification of beneficiaries. To ensure complains are responded timely and properly there will be complain response committees at each payam and county level.

The project will address the shelter building through conditional cash modality to build Tukuls and restricted cash transfer modality for fulfilling HHs Emergency NFI Needs. The shelter component will be addressed through conditional cash transfers to beneficiary HHs  in one round, the cash  transfer can be made after single HHs prepared construction site ( clearing the ground and laying foundation ) and the continuous monitoring will be done on  building of Tukul. The NFI component can be addressed through vouchers, by having agreement with local venders to supply identified items (restricted cash) and the beneficiaries can collected the items from venders. 

After each cash distribution, there will be Post Cash Distribution Monitoring (PDM) that can inform future action and help to take corrective measures on ongoing program too.

project_name: Save lives and build resilience of protected crisis affected communities (IDPs, Returnees and Host communities) in Duk, Uror and Twic East Counties of Jonglei State, South Sudan
project_objective:
LWFs Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) project is targeting protracted conflict and displacement  affected most vulnerable IDPs, and Returnees who have been displaced due to a protracted crisis over the past one year or more years , compounded by inter-clan, inter-tribal violence and cattle raiding. LWF planned to reach 8000 HHs(of which 79% is female)  from IDPs, and Returnees communities in Duk, Uror and Twic East counties through increasing food consumption (using cash modalities) and enhancing agricultural production capacities. The agricultural capacities of targets beneficiaries will be enhanced through building skill on farm practices (on farm and off farm management) and Supporting by agricultural inputs.  

The beneficiaries’ selection can be done through community participation and lead of community based Cash Committees (CDCS). The process involves identification, registration and verification of beneficiaries. To ensure complains are responded timely and properly there will be complain response committees at each payam and county level.

The project will address the lifesaving food consumption through unconditional cash modality. In addition the farmers supporting through farm field schools, seeds fairs and direct seeds and tools delivery. The farmers will get intensive season long training on agricultural practices and skills to ensure that the targets will be resilient and bounce back future shocks (absorb the shocks). 

LWF will integrate all its projects (WASH, Food security, alternatives livelihoods, shelter/NFI, Education) in the operation to maximize the lifesaving, to minimize further deterioration of livelihoods and building resilience.
The project will be implemented in coordination with stakeholders and partners working in the operation areas in food security and livelihoods, Education, WASH, Shelter, NFI and health). The coordination can help to find solution for common challenges, learn from each other, and avoid duplication efforts and maximise outcomes and impacts.

project_name: Atención nutricional de niños y niñas menores de 5 años, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia en 10 estados priorizados.
project_objective:
La atención nutricional propuesta por Unicef está dirigida a niños y niñas menores de 5 años, madres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia - MEL, ubicados en zonas de alta vulnerabilidad en los estados de Zulia, Delta Amacuro, Amazonas, Bolívar, Táchira, Apura, Miranda, Sucre, Distrito Capital y Delta Amacuro, - priorizados por el HRP. La atención nutricional incluye las siguientes acciones, a saber:
1.Prevención de la desnutrición aguda y otras formas de desnutrición. Las acciones preventivas se enfocarán en las siguientes intervenciones: a.Tamizaje del estado nutricional - a 500,000 niños, niñas menores de 5 años, y 110,000 MEL; b. Tamizaje para la determinación de anemia a 50,000 niños menores de 2 años y 22,000 MEL; c. Desparasitación a 1,150,000 niños y niñas de 2 a 14 años y 25,000 embarazadas en 2T y 3T de gestación, d. Suplementación con micronutrientes a 400,000 niños y niñas de 6 a 59 meses y 110,000 MEL; e. Prevención de la desnutrición aguda en 75,000 niños y niñas con riesgo de desnutrición aguda; f.	Consejería en alimentación del lactante y el niño pequeño a 100,000 familias de niños y niñas de 0 a 23 meses de edad; g. Promoción de prácticas clave en salud, higiene y nutrición en 700,000 familias de las zonas priorizadas.
2.Tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda y deficiencias de micronutrientes. La atención se realizará con los servicios de salud ambulatorios y hospitalarios adscritos a las autoridades únicas de salud y MPPS, respectivamente. Incluye el a. Tratamiento ambulatorio a 12,000 niños y niñas con desnutrición aguda moderada y severa sin complicaciones. b.	Tratamiento intrahospitalario 3,000 niños y niñas con desnutrición aguda moderada y severa con complicaciones y apoyo en la transición al manejo ambulatorio. c.	Tratamiento de la anemia nutricional en 60,000 niños, niñas menores de 5 años y 11,000 MEL.
3. Fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales en salud como parte del mejoramiento de la calidad de la identificación, atención y seguimiento de la atención nutricional a nivel ambulatorio e intrahospitalario de los niños, niñas menores de 5 años y MEL. Incluye a.	Realización de 3 Entrenamientos de entrenadores en nutrición en emergencias a socios implementadores de Unicef. b. Capacitaciones y jornadas de trabajo en atención nutricional y manejo integrado de la desnutrición aguda dirigido a 4,000 trabajadores de la salud a nivel Estadal. c.	Apoyo a 1,000 centros ambulatorios en el fortalecimiento de capacidades en clasificación antropométrica y atención nutricional con calidad y oportunidad. d. Fortalecimiento del monitoreo y reporte del estado nutricional de los niños, niñas y MEL. e. Apoyo técnico al MPPS, INN, y tres autoridades estadales de salud, 3 centros hospitalarios en Promoción, Protección y Apoyo en Lactancia Materna - Programa Madre canguro.
4.Generación de conocimiento en temas de atención nutricional. Incluye a.Realización de una línea de base sobre situación nutricional de niños y niñas menores de 2 años y MEL. b. Apoyo en la realización de por lo menos 2 encuestas SMART en los estados priorizados. c.Asistencia técnica al gobierno nacional en la actualización del protocolo nacional de manejo de la desnutrición aguda y definición del protocolo de manejo de las deficiencias de micronutrientes. Actualmente Unicef está en 8 estados atendiendo a aproximadamente 140,000 niños y niñas con fondos de ECHO y otros donantes hasta diciembre de 2019 por 1.8M USD. No obstante, se requiere incrementar la capacidad operativa para garantizar atención nutricional a 610,000 niños, niñas. En total se espera que en total, Unicef pueda atender a 750,000 niños y niñas menores de 5 años y MEL entre Junio de 2019 y Mayo de 2020.

project_name: Provision of emergency education services to Palestine refugee school children in Syria
project_objective:
In 2019, UNRWA will continue to provide formal and non-formal education services to up to 51,000 Palestine refugee children (an increase from 48,100 enrolled in 2018) in 103 schools located in Damascus, Rif Damascus, Aleppo, Hama, Homs, Latakia and Dera’a. A majority of schools still operate on a double shift basis. UNRWA will employ approximately 1,700 teachers including daily paid teachers to cover possible gaps created by the conflict. 

The Agency will also continue its Education in Emergencies (EiE) interventions, including the provision of Summer Learning activities; the engagement of parents through awareness raising sessions on violence / Gender Based Violence (GBV), explosive remnants of war (ERWs), and career guidance for their children; the strengthening of the identification and management of Psychosocial Support (PSS) cases in schools; and continued capacity-building for education staff. Students in all UNRWA schools will benefit from group and individual psychosocial support counselling sessions guided by professional counsellors throughout the academic year, providing them with the necessary skills to cope with the anxiety and stress generated by the trauma of conflict. 
  
School principals and teachers in UNRWA schools will receive training on safety and security topics with the aim of enhancing preparedness and response to security threats in schools, particularly those located in areas affected by conflict. Training topics will include evacuation procedures; dealing with ERWs; and tips on fire safety, in addition to live drills. Similar training sessions will also be provided to students, offering them basic survival skills and raising their awareness of security risks.

UNRWA will also focus its intervention on the resumption of educational services in newly accessible areas including in Yalda/Yarmouk, Sbeineh and Khan Eshieh camps in Damascus and Rural Damascus and in the South (Dera’a) provided that safe access is granted. Major construction, maintenance and rehabilitation works will be undertaken on UNRWA installations, with special focus on camps that witnessed major destruction, depending on the availability of funding, safety and security conditions, and access.

project_name: Incrementar la producción agropecuaria y la SAN con enfoque de resiliencia en comunidades vulnerables y fortalecer el Sector de Seguridad Alimentaria.
project_objective:
Esta propuesta contiene dos elementos, refuerzo de la resiliencia y refuerzo de la Coordinación del Sector de Seguridad Alimentaria.
El refuerzo de la resiliencia se busca incrementar aumentando la capacidad productiva de alimentos y formulación de un plan de mejora y recuperación productiva del campo para la producción sostenible de alimentos, en comunidades vulnerables, a través del impulso productivo agrícola (especies vegetales y especies menores) en 3.600 familias de 6 estados del país.
Con esta iniciativa se pretende atender la producción de cereales en el estado Portuguesa (específicamente maíz), a través de la distribución de insumos agrícolas, ya que la temporada de lluvias inició y es la apropiada para la siembra. Esto aspira atender la necesidad de los productores que históricamente han sembrado y actualmente no han podido hacerlo por falta de insumos. Es importante destacar que el consumo de maíz en la población venezolana es esencial, pues es utilizado para consumo humano y para alimentación de especies pecuarias. La producción aumentada en esta zona será dirigida a los estados priorizados a través de organizaciones que estén haciendo labores en ellos.
En el estado Carabobo, los cítricos están siendo afectados por una bacteria que arrasó con las hectáreas sembradas, ocasionando muy baja oferta y altísimos precios. La producción de cítricos en Venezuela está destinada fundamentalmente al mercado nacional. Se producen, en orden decreciente naranjas, mandarinas, limones y grapefruit; siendo la naranja, la principal fruta procesada en Venezuela, ya que más del 35% de su producción se industrializa. Las principales industrias procesadoras se hallan próximas a las zonas de producción, en el centro y occidente del país.
Reactivar la producción de “casabe” en el estado Sucre, mediante el fortalecimiento productivo de la yuca y dotación de insumos herramientas y utensilios para el procesamiento de la yuca agria.  En Nurucual, el principal sistema de producción agrícola es yuca-casabe. La yuca agria se procesa en casaberas y rallanzas artesanales administradas por una familia individual o por familias emparentadas entre sí. Existen 3 variedades de yuca agria que se cultiva en la zona, las cuales producen más de 5 Kg de raíces/planta. Es necesario fortalecer las casaberas, las cuales son estructuras abiertas construidas con madera, techo a dos aguas, elaborado con láminas de hierro galvanizado, piso de tierra.
Además, en los estados Táchira, Apure y Delta Amacuro; estados con alto potencial agrícola, se va a promover el fomento y desarrollo de agricultura familiar que incluya la producción de especies vegetales y especies menores.
El Sector de Seguridad Alimentaria en Venezuela:
La FAO y el PMA son los organismos principales del Grupo de Seguridad Alimentaria a nivel mundial. En el caso de Venezuela, donde el PMA aún no está presente, la FAO es la líder del Sector Seguridad Alimentaria.
Los socios del Sector son organizaciones internacionales y nacionales que trabajan en el país con programas para mejorar la seguridad alimentaria, los medios de vida y la resiliencia, desde el socorro inmediato de las personas necesitadas hasta el aumento y la seguridad de la producción de alimentos a más largo plazo. El objetivo del Sector es de asegurar una coordinación adecuada de las Intervenciones de Seguridad Alimentaria en el país, evitar solapamientos y reducir las brechas, así como fortalecer la capacidad local para mejorar la disponibilidad, el acceso y la utilización adecuada de los alimentos y los medios de subsistencia.
El trabajo del Sector empezó en 29 de abril de 2019. Se preparó el Marco Lógico y el Narrativo del Sector, así como la recepción de los proyectos para componer el Plan de Respuesta (HRP) de OCHA.
El Sector contará con el apoyo de un Coordinador Internacional, un Oficial de Gestión de la Información y un Coordinador Regional (nacionales) para Zulia, Tachira y Apure.
