project_name: Food assistance to conflict-affected populations and most vulnerable groups across Northern Syria
project_objective:
PIN will target the most vulnerable individuals/HH notably IDPs, the most vulnerable among hosting populations, people in-hard-to-reach areas, people with chronic illness, people with disabilities and people facing extreme socio-economic hardship- all possibly facing further various level of protection risks and vulnerabilities which can lead them to resort to harmful coping strategies.  This is achieved through protection-sensitive programme design, targeting, and implementation, to ensure an inclusive approach to programming; notably intended to reach female-headed houses, which are often isolated. Food assistance in its various modalities are in themselves protection mechanisms, supporting vulnerable households to meet urgent needs and preventing the resort to negative coping strategies. Women are routinely identified as heads of households for the purposes of receiving assistance, to promote their participation in decision-making regarding utilization of assistance given.

PIN will monitor the conflict and population movement to be able to assist newly displaced persons in the timeliest manner with appropriate response both across North East and North West Syria. A specific attention will be pay to IDPs as being 6.1 million in-country presently living in camps, host communities, last resort and makeshift settlements, resulting from both newly or protracted displacement.

The activities fall both into emergency and life-sustaining response to address food and basic needs of target beneficiaries. Ready to Eat Rations (RTERs) distributed within 96 hours of displacement is complement by Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to cover full monthly Survival Monthly Expenditure Basket (SMEB) up to 6 weeks.
The second component is regular monthly food assistance as a regard of life-sustaining strategy. PIN aims to provide for up to 9-month consecutive food assistance when possible. These activities will cover up to 78/80% of the monthly SMEB, the remaining is aimed to be provided by beneficiaries themselves through their own means. Yet particular attention should be brought in situation where assistance is the sole source of income of target HH as PIN monitoring activities as underlined, for them to be kept them away from harmful coping strategies. 
In the first days of displacement, rapid assessments are carried out by PIN and in coordination and consultation with other response actors, local councils, and/or camp management committees, as applicable and in line with internal SOPs and SPHERE standards.

Likewise, this emergency response is complemented by early recovery assistance covering WASH, Livelihoods, Education in host communities receiving IDPs, in order to maximise ‘do no harm’ considerations and ensure that vulnerable host populations also receive appropriate assistance. When possible beneficiaries will be directed from emergency to regular food assistance and early recovery.
Constant M&E monitoring act as activities backbone through beneficiary selection and verification, need assessment, market monitoring, post-implementation (such as distribution) monitoring, routine monitoring, Complaint and Response Mechanism (CRM).
It should be noted that activities are designed to be in line with the relevant coordination system such as Sphere standards and meet FSL cluster recommendations (length of assistance, contents of kits, value of cash/vouchers etc.).
Lastly, all activities will be carried out in coordination with local councils (LC), ensuring to share information on needs and response gaps at the village level as well as involved in beneficiary selection process; local associations, and IDP representatives at village level will be considered, if any.

project_name: Protecting vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons, Returnees, and Host Communities in Mali through identification of specific vulnerabilities, basic needs, and provision of psychosocial assistance and referrals.
project_objective:
This project will assist internally displaced persons, returnees, and host communities in addressing their psychosocial needs. It will do so by targeting communities affected by the internal and communal conflicts and identifying victims of conflict-related incidents. 
In coordination with members and leaders of the target communities, outreach teams will be established and trained in identifying vulnerable cases, provide immediate protection assistance and refer vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and repatriates to specialized institutions. 
Direct assistance, as per beneficiaries’ needs will be provided. This will include but not limited to income generating activities that will contribute to the resilience of households. 
According to the protection cluster, about 5,800,000 persons are affected of which 755,355 are in need of assistance and 509,345 are targeted for assistance. Under this project, 25,000 persons needing psychosocial assistance will be considered. They will comprise of women and men including young girls and boys.
The project will be carried out in the regions of Gao, Mopti, Tombouctou, and Kayes over a period of twelve (12) months.

project_name: Appui à la restauration immédiate et au renforcement des moyens d’existence des ménages agricoles vulnérables affectés la crise sociopolitique et les changements climatiques au Nord et au Centre du Mali
project_objective: L’objectif global est de restaurer et renforcer les capacités productives de 45 000 ménages (270 000 personnes) victimes, dont les femmes vulnérables chefs de ménage, du conflit et des inondations et leur permettre de vivre dignement de l’Agriculture pour la couverture de leurs besoins de base

project_name: Projet de réponse et  d'atténuation des risques aux violences basées sur le genre dans les régions du Nord et du Centre affectées par les conflits au Mali
project_objective:
La Violence Basée sur le Genre constitue l’un des déﬁs majeurs de protection auxquels le Mali est confronté. Toutes les statistiques convergent vers une exacerbation des violences sur toute l’étendue du territoire avec un accent particulier pour les régions du nord et du centre. Durante toute l’année 2018 les régions du nord et plus particulièrement celles du centre ont été le théâtre d’affrontements intercommunautaires qui fortement fragilisé la situation des femmes et des ﬁlles. Plusieurs types de Violences Basées sur le genre sévissent dans ces régions. On peut citer entre autres la violence conjugale ; le viol, l’agression sexuelle, le mariage des enfants, les mutilations génitales féminines, la traite des êtres humains, la violence physique et psychologique et le déni des ressources/d’opportunités. Ces Violences Basées sur le Genre sont perpétrées à une fréquence assez inquiétante provoquant ainsi un traumatisme chez les personnes survivantes et affectant par la même occasion la résilience de la société. 
Selon les statistiques, au Mali 33240 femmes et ﬁlles sont à risque de Violences Basées sur le Genre dans les régions du nord et du centre. Une analyse auprès des structures sanitaires du nord et du centre révèle que près de 35 % de ces structures ne disposent pas de kit post Viol notamment à Kidal, Mopti, Koro, Menaka et Asongo. Egalement 100% des structures sanitaires disposant des kits post viol seront en ruptures de stock à la date du 1er janvier 2019 s’il n’y a pas d’approvisionnement à temps. Sur 1 742 cas de VBG rapportés par le GBVIMS en 2018, on note que 17% n’ont pu accéder à l’assistance médicale, 72% et 88% des personnes survivantes, respectivement dans le besoin d’hébergement en lieu sûr et de réinsertion socio-économique et scolaire n’ont pas pu être assistés à cause de l’indisponibilité de ces services. 
L’analyse de la carte de sévérité du Sous Cluster VBG révèle un besoin critique des services dans les cercles de Tinassoko, Koro, Tenenkou, Youwarou, Bankass, Kidal, Goundam, Gourma Rharouss, Ménaka, Gao et Mopti.  
Le projet s’attèlera à mettre en œuvre les différents plans d’action des clusters prioritaires pour la prévention et l’atténuation des risques de VBG. Ainsi pour l’année 2019, les interventions humanitaires viseront prioritairement à renforcer l’accès aux services de prise en charge holistique (santé, psychosocial, sécurité, accès à la justice, réinsertion socio-économique et scolaire, provision en kits de dignité) dans les régions du centre et du nord affectées par les conﬂits, plus particulièrement les communes de : Koro, Tenenkou, Youwarou , Bankass, Kidal, Goundam, Gourma Rharouss, Ménaka, Gao, Mopti. L’accent sera mis particulièrement sur le renforcement des services de prise en charge des VBGs à travers le renforcement du guichet unique ou One Stop Center. Les mécanismes communautaires de prévention et d’alerte précoce seront également renforcés ainsi que la dissémination du système de référencement. 
Pour assurer l’intégration de la prévention des risques de VBG dans le plan d’action des autres clusters, le projet assurera  la prise en charge holistique des cas de VBG à travers les structures de santé qui seront dotées de kits post viol/SR. L’accent sera également mis sur les évaluations multisectorielles lors des incidents humanitaires tels que les mouvements de population ou les inondations ce qui permettra la prise en compte des aspects genre dans ces différentes évaluations. Afin d’assurer une réductions des risques de VBG dans tous les domaines  le projet veillera également à l’intégration de la dimension genre dans les activités des autres clusters prioritaires, telle que la prise en compte des femmes et filles lors des distributions alimentaires, le renforcement de la sécurité des femmes et filles à travers les comités d’alerte précoce et de même que les comités de gestion des points d’eaux.

project_name: Saving lives by improving WASH service delivery for disaster affected communities in Somalia
project_objective: The Humanitarian Response Plan identified WASH red sport districts which are at high risk to disease outbreak, water scarcity, high latrine safety index owing to high mobility associated with disaster. WV Somalia will target 3 regions and having worked in Lughaya, Zeylac, Burtinle, Garoowe Dollow and Luuq districts would like to build on its foot prints with regards to WASH service delivery. WASH programming will be undertaken at community, school and health levels. The program aims to achieve two results/outcomes, that is, firstly increased access to sustainable and safe water supply for poor, vulnerable communities, children in school and in health facilities and secondly target population has access to reliable and sustainable environmental sanitation.  WV has the commitment to supporting capacity-building efforts for local people and government line ministries. World Vision currently works with the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources and the Ministry of Health in the implementation of its WASH activities in South West State. This deliberate effort at partnering provides a platform for capacity building for the Ministry personnel, and at the same time strengthens collaboration and ensures World Vision strategy is in sync with the mandate and strategy of the local government. WV is mindful of local custom and culture. It is also committed to participatory and sustainable development and to providing assistance impartially. WV acknowledge their accountabilities to those whom they assist and those who provide support to their work and also committed to ensuring that it does not expose intended beneficiaries, including children, to any form of discrimination, abuse or exploitation. Inorder to ensure sustainable delivery, WV seek to encourage participation in decision making processes and skills training so as to ensure that the beneficiaries will act as an active component in the implementation of the program. The WASH program has been deliberate in ensuring its facilities are inclusive and can be used by people with physical disabilities. One of the key areas has been ensuring that latrines are accessible to wheel chair bound persons by incorporating ramps as standard at doorways and having wide fully opening doors. For public sanitation facilities, ramps and rails have also been installed as standard for the sanitation facilities. Sector integration will also be fostered. The WASH program will work closely with the Education and Protection and Health and Nutrition sectors. The WASH programme in Health Facilities will focus on ensuring all consultations and admissions including children under the age of 5 have access to clean water and sanitation within the target locations. At each of the health facilities World Vision will provide an elaborate water and sanitation management programme which will include incinerators, autoclaves, clean water, and institutional latrines for proper infection prevention and control practices. The schools will be connected to the main water supply and receive occasional water trucking at times when the main water supply is erratic. Children will also be provided with WASH NFIs, including MHM kits that will be given to adolescent girls at the schools to help reduce on the number of girls who drop out of school during their menstrual cycle.DRR will include developing capacity of local government to understand, own and trigger demand for WASH through advocacy to take policy decisions  to develop political will that enable a WASH resilience building environment.

project_name: Providing humanitarian WASH assistance and improving basic WASH infrastructure and living condition of IDP sites in northwest Syria.
project_objective:
This project aims to support the WASH response and the immediate needs of most vulnerable displaced populations in the northwest of Syria by providing emergency WASH assistance in camps and improving the basic WASH infrastructure and WASH conditions in IDP sites in northwest Syria through: 

i)	Improving access to drinking water by rehabilitating 13 water systems and installing connections to IDP camps.
ii)	Rehabilitation and construction of 21 drainage systems in informal IDP sites.
iii)	Provision and distribution of 12,000 WASH NFI kits.
iv)	Provision of temporary water supply to newly displaced and/or highly vulnerable populations living in 34 IDP camps.
v)	Provision and construction of 70 communal latrine units in IDP sites.

The project will contribute to the two objectives of the WASH cluster which are:
•	Support to water, sanitation/sewage and solid waste management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria
•	Deliver humanitarian WASH supplies, services and improve hygienic behaviour and practices of most vulnerable people

Overall, the project aims to support 155,144 beneficiaries with humanitarian WASH assistance and improvements to basic WASH infrastructure in informal IDP sites in NW Syria. Project locations are Harim, Dana, Ma’arat An Nu’man and Azaz.

project_name: IRAQ - International Organization for Migration
Whole of Syria PSEA Programme
project_objective:
The Whole of Syria Inter-Agency Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) project, housed at IOM, works to support the entire Syrian humanitarian response in coordinating one common voice and joint, coherent, implementation on PSEA. This project will contribute to the protection of civilians, reduction of suffering and building resilience by improving the overall effectiveness of the Syria Response through continued support to inter-agency PSEA Networks in all hubs; training and awareness raising amongst humanitarian workers and decision-makers on PSEA and SEA investigations; and the continued rollout of inter-agency community-based complaints mechanisms which will allow beneficiaries to safely and confidentially report SEA.

The project contributes to:
1)	Strategic Objective 2: Enhance protection (particularly by enhancing ‘quality, principled’ assistance)
2)	Strategic Objective 3: Increase resilience and access to services (especially as evidence from HNO2018 shows that sexual exploitation is a critical barrier for certain segments of the affected population in accessing aid and services.)

project_name: Supporting Community Revitalization & Resilience through Early Recovery and Livelihood interventions in North West of Syria
project_objective: Contribute to Community Revitalization and Resilience through supporting Local Economic Recovery, Improving Access to Basic/ Social Services and Promoting Community Cohesion. This comes in line with both Early Recovery and Livelihood Sector and Food Security and Livelihood Cluster 2019 objectives.

project_name: Improving WASH and Meeting Basic Needs in the South West Region for Conflict-Affected Communities In Cameroon
project_objective: This project aims to improve WASH and meeting Basic Needs in the South West Region for Conflict-Affected Communities in Cameroon. To achieve this objective, the project proposes to rehabilitated 20 water points to improve access to water for displaced and host communities of the Fako and Meme divisions in the South West of Cameroon. In order to limit open defecation and prevent waterborne diseases, the IRC will built 100 emergency latrines, 100 emergency showers and 100 family latrines. 500 WASH kits and 500 NFI kits will be distributed to the most vulnerable households. The IRC will engage 80 community health workers (CHWs) in this project to ensure community participation and dissemination of messages on good hygiene practices in topics such as: key hand washing moments, water treatment at home, food hygiene, latrine use and maintenance, prevention of waterborne diseases, and environmental hygiene. The IRC will also train members of water management committees (WMCs) to ensure the sustainability of water points. In total, 40,300 individuals will be benefit from the WASH project including 32,240 IDPs and 8060 hosts.

project_name: Reducing Protection Risks and Meeting Basic Needs of Conflict-Affected Communities in the Far North Region, Cameroon
project_objective:
Since 2014, Cameroon’s Far North region has been the scene of a brutal war in which civilians have done most of the suffering and dying. Boko Haram attacks and harsh wartime measures taken by local authorities have devastated the local economy, restricted basic services, and thrown both refugees and host communities into a climate of destitution and fear. Over 330,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) have been driven from their homes, and a total of 2.1 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.  
In the ongoing conflict, civilians remain vulnerable to insecurity and serious violations of their human rights. Women and girls are the group most exposed to violence, including gender-based violence (GBV), and to serious human rights violations.  They continue to be at risk of rape, sexual and physical abuse, early and forced marriage, emotional abuse, and lack of resources and opportunities.There were 1,649 reported cases of GBV in the Far North in 2017, and it is likely that many more cases went unreported.   Gender inequality severely limits opportunities for women and girls, as cultural practices favour men’s and boys’ economic and educational advancement. Services for GBV survivors are limited, and survivors often lack access to appropriate assistance. 
Vulnerable individuals face a number of threats to their safety and dignity. Protection monitoring conducted by IRC in July 2018 showed that more than 20 villages in Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga departments, near the border with Nigeria, have many displaced persons and asylum seekers from Nigeria, but lack adequate access to humanitarian assistance due to insecurity. 
Affected populations in the Far North continue to bear the economic burden of this conflict. Most of the displaced lost their means of livelihood and almost all of their material possessions during their flight. Host communities have seen the local economy shattered by conflict and restrictive wartime measures. These factors have compounded the chronic poverty of the Far North. Three-quarters (74.3%) of Far Northerners live below the national poverty line, double the national average (37.5%).  In the border areas most affected by the Boko Haram crisis, the poverty rate exceeds 80%.   A baseline survey conducted by IRC in July 2018 in Mayo Sava shows that 75% of households surveyed reported resorting to negative coping strategies to meet their basic needs, potentially threatening their safety, health, and resilience to future shocks. For women, girls and vulnerable individuals, economic deprivation further exacerbates protection risks, potentially exposing them to sexual exploitation and other forms of harm

project_name: Promouvoir la sécurité et l'accès aux moyens de subsistance pour les jeunes filles et garçons affectés par la crise dans l’Extrême Nord Cameroun.
project_objective:
Cameroun (18,2%) - Les trois quarts de la population camerounaise vivant dans l’extrême nord vivent au-dessous du seuil de pauvreté national. La région est sous-développée de manière chronique, exposée aux inondations et à la sécheresse, et est isolée géographiquement. La fragile économie de l'extrême nord du Cameroun, qui repose largement sur le commerce transfrontalier, a été ébranlée par les fermetures de frontières avec le Nigéria et les restrictions au trafic et au commerce mises en place par les autorités locales comme mesures de sécurité à la suite du conflit brutal lié aux actes terroristes de la secte terroriste Boko Haram. Les gens sont touchés par le conflit et nombre d'entre eux sont incapables de subvenir à leurs besoins fondamentaux. Selon la matrice de suivi des déplacements (DTM 14, juin 2018) publiée par l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIMO), dans l'extrême extrême nord du Cameroun, le nombre de personnes déplacées est estimé à 359 222 personnes: 227 581 personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays (PDI), 39 403 réfugiés hors camp et 92 238 rapatriés. Une grande partie des personnes déplacées dans le Grand Nord ont perdu leurs moyens de subsistance.
Pour ces personnes déplacées ainsi qu’une grande partie de la communauté d’accueil, la question de l’emploi se pose avec un besoin pressant. Les activités proposées font partie des résultats 2 et 3 décrits ci-dessus. Les jeunes de l’arrondissement de Mora dans le département de Mayo Sava bénéficieront des multiples services fournis par le projet, y compris une formation aux compétences en entrepreneuriat dispensée par les centres de formation de Mora. Entreprises existantes. Des séances de sensibilisation de la communauté seront organisées pour veiller à ce que les communautés touchées (déplacées et hôtes) soient informées de la présence de l’IRC dans leur région et faciliteront le transfert d’informations entre le personnel d’IRC et les bénéficiaires potentiels des actions proposées. Ces séances consolideront également la cohésion sociale, l’implication des communautés et leur participation à la mise en œuvre du projet. Cela inclut également de faciliter le placement des clients chez des entrepreneurs existants pour le programme de mentorat et pour un emploi dans la mesure du possible.
•	Résultat attendu 1: les jeunes participants acquièrent des compétences pertinentes pour le marché et sont préparés à l'emploi ou au travail indépendant.
•	Résultat attendu 2: les entreprises locales et les nouvelles entreprises appartenant à des jeunes sont encouragées à démarrer et à se développer.
•	Résultat attendu 3: Les leaders de la communauté locale et les acteurs urbains collaborent et travaillent en partenariat pour aider les jeunes à s'engager sur les marchés du travail locaux.

project_name: Integrated Response for Conflicted Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) II
project_objective:
This project will seek to build on gains made through programming in 2015–2018, meeting the needs of approximately 115,813 conflict and famine-affected individuals in South Sudan through an integrated Nutrition, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response.  Under FSL programming, Agricultural Training Groups (ATGs) will be formed, seeds and tools will be distributed to beneficiaries, tree nurseries will be established, and fishing kits with training on best practices will be provided to improve future food security. 

The areas of South Sudan targeted for this project include: Mayendit, Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG), Abiemnhom and Mayom Counties.  According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), it is expected that between June and September of 2018, Mayendit, Abiemnhom and Mayom Counties will reach Crisis levels (Phase 3) for acute food insecurity; NBeG is expected to reach Emergency levels (Phase 4) classification.   In addition to their levels of food insecurity, each area has been identified due to a lack of access to clean water, high rates of malnutrition, or overall poor health and hygiene practices.  According to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET), insecurity in South Sudan has negatively impacted markets by disrupting staple crop production and access, and increasing prices.

project_name: Integrated Response for Conflicted Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) II
project_objective:
This project will seek to build on gains made through programming in 2015–2018, meeting the needs of approximately 115,813 conflict and famine-affected individuals in South Sudan through an integrated Nutrition, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response. To increase adequate access to clean water, hand pumps will be rehabilitated, a manual drill will be utilized to drill additional wells, existing water points will be upgraded to solar, water-management committees will be formed and hand pump mechanics will be trained.  With regard to efforts to improve health and hygiene practices, communal and HH latrines, and gender segregated bathing shelters will be constructed, and trainings will be conducted on better health and hygiene practices.

The areas of South Sudan targeted for this WASH project include: Mayendit, Abiemnhom and Mayom Counties. In addition to their levels of food insecurity, each area has been identified due to a lack of access to clean water, high rates of malnutrition, or overall poor health and hygiene practices.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de los servicios hospitalarios en estados priorizados de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela
project_objective:
El presente proyecto se vincula con el objetivo estratégico, de proteger la supervivencia de las personas mas vulnerables mejorando su acceso en cantidad, calidad, continuidad y de cobertura territorial a los bienes y servicios esenciales bajo un enfoque de derechos.

La atención de necesidades se base en la información obtenida a través de la aplicación del Índice de Seguridad Hospitalaria (ISH) donde se evidencia la importancia de reforzar la atención de pacientes en las áreas criticas como emergencias, sala de partos, sala de operaciones, cuidados intensivos, esterilización, morgue, laboratorio y diagnóstico por imágenes dando continuidad a los sistemas y líneas vitales como agua, energía, gases medicinales, comunicaciones, alimentación, climatización, información y otros.

La intervención esta orientada a asegurar la capacidad operativa y continuidad de la respuesta de los servicios críticos de los hospitales seleccionados en el marco de la iniciativa de hospitales seguros frente a desastres buscando la articulación con la atención que se brinda a través de las clínicas populares y en los establecimientos bajo el ámbito de los ASICs que estén cercanos a los hospitales priorizados.

Se incluyen actividades para asegurar la operación y respuesta de los servicios mediante la dotación sostenida de medicamentos e insumos médicos, el mantenimiento preventivo y recuperativo de los sistemas de climatización, gases medicinales, ascensores y otros sistemas; así como el entrenamiento del personal de salud en la gestión de emergencias, triaje, atención de emergencias y la elaboración de procedimientos y protocolos de atención, y para la referencia y contrareferencia de pacientes.

project_name: Strengthening Lifesaving, Comprehensive, and Multi Sectoral Prevention and Response to Gender Based Violence in Sudan (Darfur states, Blue Nile, South Kordofan and Abyei area)
project_objective:
UNFPA's GBV interventions will contribute to outcome 1 and outcome 2 of the 2017 – 2019 Sudan Multi Year Humanitarian Strategy and contribute to saving lives and reducing the social and economic impact of humanitarian emergencies through addressing the needs of population affected by emergency situation in Darfur, South Kordofan, Blue Nile and Abyei area, the intervention include GBV service provision focus in the  high-need areas, the newly accessible areas and new displacements within the recent two years. 
The project will support existing and new establishment of women centers in  targeted localities through implement activities package include;  environmentally friendly rehabilitation/ construction of the centers and provision of GBV services within these centers such as; awareness raising on GBV related issues and information, life skills training, and  psycho-social support include individual and group counseling. 
The women centers will also serve as safe space for  gathering and an entry point for 60,000 women and girls to discuss a range of issues of concern  and to receive information on protection and GBV related issues. 
The project will ensure access of GBV survivors to health services and psychosocial support and counseling through provision of individual and collective GBV services  targeted 15,000 girls, boys, women and men.  Support community protection networks  will provide the linkages between the community and GBV services and facilitate referral of GBV survivors to access medical treatment and PSS support .
In addition, capacity building for 1000 front line respondents – service providers and community members on CMR, psycho social support, referral pathway, legal aid, national and international legal frameworks and protection policies supporting GBV survivors.  
 The community level consultations will also create a sense of ownership and agency of the population over issues that affect their lives.
Support existing national and sub national level coordination mechanisms at national and in  4 Darfur states lead by UNFPA to advocate for and respond to GBV concerns, in addition to UNFPA participation in joint needs assessment missions to provide timely response and interventions. 
UNFPA will Procure and distribute 35,000 personal hygiene kits and sanitary supplies to the new arrivals and most vulnerable women and girls of reproductive age including IDPs, GBV survivors, and females heading households.
Total of  30,000 individual will benefit from community protection networks outreach activities  and information .

project_name: IRAQ - United Nations Population Fund
Emergency assistance and implementation of livelihood restoration and resiliency interventions to food insecure communities in conflict affected counties of Twic County in Warrap State
project_objective: GOAL’s primary objective for 2019 is to provide urgent and lifesaving assistance to 60,000HH (360,000 beneficiaries) through the distribution of emergency livelihood kits, seeds, and tools, support of market functionality interventions, training and capacity building to support resiliency, and diversification and restoration of livelihoods for vulnerable households across IPC 3 and 4 phases of food insecurity.

project_name: EMERGENCY PROTECTION OF IDPs IN JUBA, MAYENDIT, YAMBIO AND TAMBURA COUNTIES
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in South Sudan with accompanying mass displacement continues to place a high toll on IDPs in POCs, IDP camps and on affected host communities. OCHA estimates that 6.1 million people or 47% of the estimated population of the country in 2018 are affected. The protection cluster estimates that of the 6.1 million, 2,825,242 people are in need of protection services, 56.4% being women, 61% children and 2% elderly. HI estimates Persons with disabilities including mental health issues affected by conflict and displacement to be in the range 5-7% of the whole caseload. 
In 2019, HI will target 33,200 persons (19,700 females and 13,500 male (from about 5,533HH) in Juba county in Central State, Mayendit county in greater Unity state and Yambio & Tambura counties in Western Equatoria state for general protection and GBV (Gender Based Violence) services. At least 23,200 beneficiaries will benefit from general protection services and 10,000 from GBV services. Four key interventions will be implemented: psychosocial support with disabilities rehabilitation; life skills and IGA training and support for survivors of GBV; dispute resolution/peacebuilding among communities affected by conflict; and comprehensive case management for GBV survivors. All actions will mainstream protection awareness raising and GBV prevention messaging. In view of the new peace agreement initiatives, there are high hopes of reconciliation and peace process, HI anticipates to engage the communities  in IDP camps and those in the host communities in peace-building and conflict mitigation to promote peaceful coexistence among communities in target locations. The prospects of peace come with an increased likelihood of returnees. HI will therefore preposition to be able to provide services to refugees and IDPs returning to their homes or being re-integrated in communities. Displacement impacts more seriously on persons with disabilities, and HI will single them out to ensure they have equal access to humanitarian services. The challenge of idle youth including those with disabilities  in camps is overarching; idle youth are a ticking bomb, and HI will aim to harness their energy by organizing them in groups, training them in IGA and vocational skills and linking them to procurement opportunities within HI and other agencies for them to compete for supply of basic products and materials such as T-shirts, scarfs, banners and simple assistive devices (walking sticks and canes, reusable sanitary pads, tricycles, crutches, etc).  

Activities will target IDPs in POCs and IDP camps or informal settlements, members of host communities in villages and returnees. These actions contribute towards realization of South Sudan HRP 2019 objectives 1, 2 and 3, and Protection Cluster objectives 1, 2, 3 of 2019. The interventions target children in POCs, IDP camps, schools and in host communities, in a static environment, but with flexibility to relocate as per population movements.. 
        These actions will be undertaken in or around locations where HI already has a static presence. Where access constraints are low to medium, HI will implement activities directly, where constraints are high, HI will work through Local NGOs (including Disabled Peoples Organizations), employing staff locally and equipping them with desired training. HI currently has field offices in all the targeted states, or will have established bases by first quarter of 2019 using existing funding on MHPSS and disability rehabilitation programs. Where possible, HI will conduct a targeting assessment in collaboration with other humanitarian actors, local authorities and interest groups to avoid duplication and overlapping of resources and services.  HI’s intervention in the 4 counties is estimated to cost USD 1,000,000 (USD 30.12 per capita, over a period of 12 months), with USD 700,000 towards general protection actions and USD 300,000 towards SGBV activities.

project_name: Supporting evidence-based response prioritization
project_objective: In the context of a large-scale humanitarian crisis in South Sudan, with severe needs and limited funding, effective aid prioritization becomes an urgent priority. To help fill critical information gaps, REACH will deliver common services for the humanitarian response in South Sudan, providing information and analysis through the Area of Knowledge (AoK) and Port and Road Monitoring (PRM); multi-sector rapid assessments and ensuring that information is accessible and relevant to decision makers by feeding findings into the humanitarian coordination structure through REACH's role as co-chair of the Needs Analysis Working Group

project_name: Access to Education in a safe and quality learning environment for children affected by the armed conflict
project_objective:
The conflict in the North East Nigeria which started some nine years ago had left an estimated 1.8 million people displaced in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe and around 40 percent (0.8 million) of that population is comprised of school aged children between the ages 3-17 years displaced across the three states. While the number of displaced persons and returnees increased compared to the previous year, the total number of children and education personnel in need decreased from 2.9 million for 2018 to 2.2 million for 2019 based on education sector estimates (EiEWG HNO, 2019).  
It is also clear that because of the displacement and destruction caused by the armed conflict, North East has the highest number of out of school children, and high pupil to qualified teacher ratios which standards at 152: 1. Additional 59,074 teachers are needed to reach the required pupil teacher ratio of 40:1. Schools have been destroyed and the few that are existing are grossly congested making it hard for children to learning and this combined with other factors explains the low literacy levels. Parents, children and teachers have been traumatised and in great need of psychosocial support and Social and emotional learning. If these issues are not addressed, they will further fuel conflict in the region.
The goal of Save the Children’s project is to increase Access to Education in a safe and quality learning environment for children affected by the armed conflict.   Save the Children will work with implementing partners such as Gender Equality, Peace and Development Center (GEPaDC), Federation opf Moslem Women Association (FOMWAN) and Ekklesiyar Yaúw A Nigeria (EYN) projects to reach 50,000 school age children (5-13): 
The project will particularly target 50,000 (26,400 girls and 23,600 boys) in selected Local Government Areas of Maiduguri, Jere, Konduga, Mafa, Biu and Damboa in Borno and Damaturu, Gujba, Potiskum and Fune of Yobe. This figure will comprise of IDPs: 25,000; Returnees & Hots Communities: 24,000; Teachers: 900; School/ Centre Based Management Committees: 80; State Quality Assurance Department: 15 and Colleges of Education: 5.

project_name: Immediate Food Assistance to the Returenees in the Far North (10,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: In the Far North region, the Boko Haram insurgency in Nigeria has displaced 100,504 Nigerian refugees in Cameroon as of October 2018, and 98,590 of them live in the Far North region (UNHCR, October 2018). Boko Haram attacks have also resulted in 227,581 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (UNHCR, October 2018), who are struggling to survive in strenuous conditions in villages or small towns in the area. The region is predominantly arid and regularly hit by drought and seasonal floods. Access to basic services is also more limited than in other regions of the country. The arrival of IDPs in food-insecure areas has severely affected host communities as well. This has put enormous pressure on already scarce community resources and the local economy by reducing farm productivity and access to land and food markets. Boko Haram attacks have disrupted the economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in the Far North region, causing a depletion of livelihoods and household assets. As a consequence, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food insecurity have been aggravated. Among the moderately vulnerable IDPs, many of whom have returned to their home villages (IOM, Displacement Tracking Matrix #14), 10,000 will be assisted throughout the year through Multi-Purpose Cash-based Transfers(MCBT) to cover basic needs that can be met by local market and available services.

project_name: Explosive Hazard Management in Somalia
project_objective: The project will enhance the capabilities of the FGS and Federal Member States to promote human security among local communities. Activities support the Comprehensive Approach to Security, the Transition Plan from AMISOM to Somali Security Forces, Community Recovery and Extension of State Authority and Accountability, as well as wider efforts towards preventing violent extremism. Principle activities include: (i) Conduct clearance and risk education and victim assistance in areas contaminated with landmines and other explosive hazards, that pose a threat to local communities and hamper the delivery of humanitarian aid; (ii) Support SEMA’s capacity to coordinate and manage humanitarian mine action activities, and; (iii) Further enhance the explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) capabilities of national mine action organisations including the Somali Police Forces.

project_name: MA--Removal and Disposal of ERW and Provision of RE to Enhance Safety and Security for At-Risk Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
UNMAS will field four Quick Response Teams, with embedded MRE/Community Liaison Teams (CLTs)—to provide explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) spot tasks, survey and clearance of land areas (calculated in sq. meters), technical and non-technical survey, as well conduct MRE and CL.  The 40,000 MRE will cover 12,000 boys, 12,000 girls, 8,000 women, and 8,000 men.  During the sessions, further information is gathered by the MRE/CLTs on suspicious hazards which is shared with the operations team members for survey, marking, and clearance.  MRE alerts communities how to identify, avoid and report explosive hazards they may encounter to reduce their threat of injury or death.   Additionally, the teams will survey and clear 600,000 sq meters. 

Deployment of mobile clearance capacity to respond in urgent and prioritized locations throughout South Sudan to provide survey and clearance of explosive hazards as well as provide risk education to women, men, boys, and girls to mitigate the threat of injury or death from explosive hazards.

project_name: Reducing Food Insecurity of the Most Vulnerable Conflict-Affected Populations in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective: The project will address the high levels of food insecurity which persist in locations close to the contact line (0-5km), incl. those that are hard to reach. Specifically, the project will look to micro-target and assist the most vulnerable amongst those affected by the conflict, including the elderly, women heads of households, and people with disabilities/limited mobility.

project_name: Peru - Plan International
Nutrition response (prevention and management of severe acute malnutrition) in Cameroon in North West and South West regions
project_objective: The project aimed at reinforce the assessment of the nutrition situation among the most vulnerable population in the SW and NW regions, and to implement treatment of severe acute malnutrition alongside with promotion of Infant and Young Child Feeding practices.

project_name: Provision of life-saving healthcare services to Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
In 2019, UNRWA will continue to sustain the delivery of quality primary health services through 17 Health Clinics offering the full range of Agency primary medical services, five Health Points (HPs) operating in areas of displacement of Palestine refugees and two mobile health clinics which are able to deploy according to needs. UNRWA health facilities provide a range of primary medical services, including out-patient consultations, vaccinations, growth monitoring, provision of medicine, gynecology consultations, laboratory services, non-communicable disease care, maternal and child health care and dental services. 

Furthermore, the Agency will continue to provide support to Palestine refugees seeking secondary and tertiary healthcare through a system of referrals to public hospitals. UNRWA subsidizes the costs of treatment of referred patients by 75-95 per cent, depending on the socio-economic status of the patient. UNRWA will continue to ensure that patients have adequate access to essential medical supplies and drugs. The Agency will also strive to maintain contingency stocks of medical supplies and drugs to address any emerging situation.

UNRWA will endeavor to resume healthcare services in newly accessible areas and to rehabilitate and maintain damaged facilities. The re-institution of the Agency health personnel in areas of spontaneous return will also be a priority. Those areas will include the South of Syria (Dera’a camp, Muzeirib, Jillin), southern Damascus area where accessible (Yarmouk/Yalda), and Ein El-Tal camp in Aleppo, as well as other gathering areas of Palestine refugees depending on access and based on needs. This component is largely responsible for the increase in the budget requested by UNRWA under the Health sector in HRP 2019. If conditions allow (access, safety and security, rehabilitation of basic infrastructure by authorities, sufficient funding ), the rehabilitation/reconstruction of health clinics in Dera’a camp, Yarmouk camp,  Ein El-Tal among other locations will require additional financial resources this year in comparison to 2018.

project_name: Provision of Education in Emergencies services for critically affected displaced children in the Rohingya Response
project_objective: SC's EiE Response will provide safe, protective, inclusive and age appropriate learning for 14,729 children aged 3-18 years (58% girls and 42% boys) and ensure refugee and host community children have optimal access to education. In 2019, SC will further consolidate its existing EiE presence in 15 camps across Ukhia and Teknaf. This programming is strategically integrated within SC’s larger humanitarian response in order to provide children with access to essential services. Teachers will be trained to identify and refer children to SC's wider child protection, psychosocial support, health, and nutrition response activities. SC will be mainstreaming wider inclusion practices across all sectors on issues related to Gender Based Violence and Disability. Activities will lead to improved gender equitable, gender sensitive, GBV preventative, GBV responsive, and disability sensitive programming. This included conducting an intra-agency assessment looking at inclusion needs in SC’s shelter, health and education programmes. To ensure gender equity, SC’s response will include targeting adolescent girls as they face a distinct set of barriers in accessing education.  SC is also committed to ensuring that at least 50% of teachers are female and that 50% of teachers are from the Rohingya population. To mitigate the risk of reinforcing existing inequalities between women, men, girls and boys, or the risk of creating new gender inequalities, the initiative will seek to engage female and male stakeholders in a gender-responsive and culturally sensitive manner and ensure alignment with SC’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Do No Harm principle.

project_name: Cash for Shelter in Tal Afar
project_objective:
ZOA and CNSF will partner to implement a Cash for Shelter project to rehabilitate 230
homes in Al Wahadena neighbourhood of Tel Afar as decided through mutual agreement and coordination with the communities and other actors in the region. In addition, ZOA and CNSF will upgrade and repair 4 collective centres. The objective is to support highly vulnerable households in Tal Afar to achieve transitional shelter solutions through activities which supports the dignity and empowerment of the
beneficiaries.

Tal Afar was selected as the target location for this project following a needs assessment
and based on our previous projects and good relationships with the communities in Tal
Afar. This project will target highly vulnerable families inhabiting homes with “major”
damage (category 2) as outlined by the Shelter Cluster and requiring interventions of
$1500 USD in line HRP 2019 Shelter Strategic Objective 2, “Assist highly vulnerable people
out of camp transitioning to durable solutions through the provision of adequate shelter
and non-food items in priority areas of displacement and return.”

The outcomes of this project include:
1) Highly vulnerable families have access to durable transitional shelter solutions.
2) Highly vulnerable families are empowered

Methodology:
Households will be assessed using the Shelter Cluster War Damage Assessment
guidelines to categorize the damage level of each household and the CWG Vulnerability
Assessment tool which uses socio-economic factors to identify the most vulnerable. Once
the target households have been selected a Scope of Works and BOQ will be established
and approved by each household and Project Engineers.

Previously, ZOA repaired collective centres in Mosul. Based on this experience, ZOAs M&E team will assess collective centres in Tel Afar and ensure the best use of funds by selecting the collective centres where the living conditions are poor and where the most vulnerable people reside, in order to improve the living of those forced to remain displaced there. 

Each household selected for the shelter rehabilitation part of this project will be eligible for a conditional Cash Transfer to support the repair works to be done on their houses. This will be available in two forms for the household to choose the most suitable:

1) Direct cash – using the Hawala system (or other method based on community
consultation). Conditional cash will be provided to the households who choose to
undertake the repair work themselves if they have the required skills. A work plan will be
created with targets for the household to meet to receive the installments of the transfer.
The transfer value will correspond with the Minimum Expenditure Basket amount as set
for the region.

2) Vouchers – If families do not have the skills to make the repairs themselves then they
can access restricted cash vouchers to be used at pre-approved and vetted local
contractors who have agreed to a Scope of Works Agreement to complete the work at set
rates.

ZOA will be responsible for all monitoring during this project, also to do a quality control of the local partner CNSF. All work undertaken by the households or the contractors will be monitored and signed off by the Project Engineers. The Engineers will also provide mentoring, guidance and support to the families. The cash component will empower families to rebuild their homes or to support the local economy by linking local contractors with local needs.   Through our experience in the region and understanding that the average home consists of 7 individuals we anticipate that 1610 individuals will receive durable shelter solutions in line with the Shelter Cluster guidelines while supporting the local economy. This response was originally designed for Tal Afar but can be rolled out in multiple locations following a market assessment and needs assessment.

project_name: ""Provide specialized CP services for at risk children in KRI and in Central and South Iraq""
project_objective: The project aims to provide child protection specialized services to 12,000 children (from 4 to 17 years old) exacerbated by prolonged displacement and/or lack of livelihood opportunities living in camps and no camps settings in Erbil, Ninewa and Anbar governorates. This includes also children at risk due to perceived affiliation, possible exploitation and abuse, impossibility to access civil documents and/or basic public services.  On this regard a particular attention will be given to youths and adolescents through specific PSS and life skills activities. The child protection services offered mainly consist in case management and structured PSS activities. At the same time through this project TdH Italy wants to build the capacity of local actors (government and local NGOs) as well as strengthen child protection community based mechanisms. Parents, youths and community key leaders will be involved in the process through information dissemination, training, mentoring and community based activities. Finally the proposed activities are strongly linked and integrated with education activities. 6,000 children living in camps and no cams setting in the same areas are supported to access quality education services through non formal education activities (remedial classes, catch up classes and tutoring). Quality and inclusive education will be also reinforced through ad hoc training for formal school teachers on child protection, PSS, inclusive approach and positive discipline.

project_name: Reducing and Mitigating Sexual and Gender-based violence in Conflict-affected areas of Anbar governorates, Iraq
project_objective:
The project will contribute to filling in a gap of services in the protection sector particularly SGBV. This will be achieved through multi-sectoral SGBV prevention and response programming in four key areas of intervention (health, psycho-social services, protection and livelihood). The project will directly contribute to lessening the impacts of the challenges identified in Section A. The project will also explore working with local faith leaders to promote awareness on SGBV and battle social norms that harm survivors and further stigmatizes them.  
The project is designed to contribute to the goals and objectives as set by the Iraqi Government and Humanitarian community in Humanitarian Response Plan 2018.  The project is also in line with the IRW’s commitment to gender equality, women’s rights, and supporting the basic needs of the hardest hit by conflict by addressing gender rights to protection and their equal access to SGBV resources (including physical and mental health) from a rights-based approach.   
The project has three main components including i)Sexual and reproductive health, ii) gender empowerment and iii) community outreach and sensitization.  
 
 
i) Sexual and Reproductive health  aims to:  
• Increase the coverage and referral systems of basic and comprehensive emergency obstetric and neonatal care services.  
• Increase the coverage of family planning services for populations affected by the emergency. 
• Awareness raising on sexual and reproductive health.  
 
ii) Gender empowerment will be strengthened through a multi-sectoral response to gender-based violence (health, psychosocial and livelihoods) aiming to: 
• Develop skills of health service providers and social workers on GBV prevention and response through a multi-sectoral training package 
• Institutionalize community-based service mapping and effective referral systems for GBV 
• Support the provision of quality psycho-social services, life skills training, provision of dignity kits  and referrals in Women and girls space centres 
• Integrate GBV prevention and response into RH services through training of RH providers in caring for GBV survivors including CMR 
• Distribute Dignity Kits as an entry point for awareness raising on GBV services 
 iii) The third component will increase public awareness of the detrimental impacts of gender-based violence on families and communities, including child and forced marriage, domestic violence, honour killings and temporary marriages.  
• Community centres will be established 
• Community outreach through awareness campaigns will be conducted targeting boys, girls, women and men. 

In December 2017 the Iraqi government has announced that the Iraqi land is completely liberated from ISIS. Hence the government started encouraging the IDPs who are living in IDP camps to go back to their origins in Anbar, Mosul, SalahEl Den, and Kirkuk governorates. The government started encouraging IDPs to go back to their origin in a very quick manner. This immature return has caused second and third state of displacement. As a result of the engorgement of the return of IDPs to their origin, the IDPs camps in Baghdad, Anbar, and some camps in Kirkuk have been closed and families were evicted from camps. Most of the IDPs who could not go back to their origin have resided in out-of-camp areas in Baghdad and Anbar. 
Due to the above mentioned changes in the context of Iraq, Islamic Relief Iraq will adjust the response plan of this project and focus on out-of-camps areas in Anbar governorate.  This project will establish a total of 10 women space centres (5 in Ramadi and 5 in Falluja) in off-camp areas, the established women centers will be operated by social workers who will deliver protection and PSS sessions, in addition rto Case Management Officer who will be responsible for case management, address service mapping, and develop referral pathway for survivors among girls and women.

project_name: Agriculture Support and Livelihood Assistance to the extreme vulnerable returnees and local communities in West Anbar, in Iraq
project_objective:
This project aims to promote food security and livelihood assistance through the support of farmers and animal husbandry among the extreme vulnerable returnees and local communities in west Anbar governorates of Iraq. The overall objective of this project is to contribute to decrease the vulnerability of the targeted returnees and local communities through the support of farmers, youth among males and females and women in the proposed targeted areas. 1000 HHs will be economically supported through livelihood intervention in the sectors of agriculture and livestock, 500 HHs will be supported through distribution of seeds, fertilizers, and fuel for agriculture farmers and 250 HHs will be supported with livestock inputs (2 female sheep and 1 Male sheep per family) and fodders for animal breeders.The project will mainly contribute to ensure that food security is promoted through the improvement of agriculture productions as well as improve income generation for the targeted families and promote the stability of living of these families in theri origins after a prolonged displacement as a result of conflict and the rapid return to their homes. This project will also ensure the alleviation of suffering of the targeted beneficiaries through the provision of qualitative assistance to the targeted families which will enable them to secure income that will help in supporting their family members and children to provide them with nutritional values and improve daily food intake of the family members and children. 
The project will also form community committees among men and women in the targeted area to act as a link between the project and targeted beneficiaries, represent the beneficiaries, and be part of the service delivery monitoring process. The formed committees will be part of the rapid assessment to identify the most vulnerable beneficiaries among the returnees and local communities. The project also aims at introducing cash flow into the targeted communities through the rehabilitation of agriculture schemes through Cash for Work, Cash for work will be carried out by engaging unskilled and skilled labourers to rehabilitate and clear access roads, irrigation channels, bunds and irrigation structures. The cash for work will be implemented during the project life cycle. However, it will provide employment opportunities among skilled and unskilled local labours for as the proposed infrastructure is designed to be labour intended collective activity. The objective of CfW activity is to reintroduce cash flows into beneficiary communities, revitalize local markets and restore basic economic functions. The availability of short-term employment helps prevent the selling of fundamental assets such as livestock, equipment, land or even household furniture. Also, this will reduce the chances of indulgence in crime or security incidents.
IRW has a strong presence in the proposed targeted areas. IRW will coordinate with FSC, WFP, relevant UN agencies, Department of Agriculture, local authorities, Area Leaders (Mokhtar), and relevant working actors (I/NNGO). IRW has formed community committees among the targeted community member to who represent their areas and speak up for the beneficiaries needs and entitlement. The project team will coordinate with the working I/NNGOs about the project intervention to reduce the gap, avoid duplication and overlapping, and ensure all actors in the targeted areas are aware about the implemented intervention. In addition, Information sharing will be done on monthly basis through the cluster.

project_name: Improve shelter conditions of most vulnerable returnee families in Heet District in Anbar Governorate, Iraq.
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to support most vulnerable families in the Governorate of Anbar, particularly in Heet District. CCR and its partner AL MAHABA WES-SALAM (Al Mahaba) will identify and prioritize the most vulnerable families in Heet district whose houses were damaged in different levels due to the military operations. Beneficiaries will be selected based on a social and economic vulnerability assessment (recommended by the Cash Working Groups in Iraq) and the damage categories of their shelters (Based on Iraq Shelter Cluster’s Guidelines).

Partners will rehabilitate 100 damaged shelters in Heet District. Targeted houses will fall under category 2 (and 3 based on the technical assessment) of war damaged shelters. Shelter rehabilitation activities will be implemented through framework agreements with local suppliers and locally hired skilled labours. Partners will verify the local market capacity through market assessment prior to start rehabilitation. 

Partners will select 330 vulnerable families whose damaged shelter fall under damage category 1 who will be eligible to receive Sealing Off Kits (SOKs). SOKs will be designed based on the findings a community-level assessment at the beginning of the project where technical engineers will evaluate the most critical shelter repair needs and advice on selecting the components of the kits. Distribution of SOKs will follow the method of house to house/ family distribution given that selected families lack resources and capacity to manage transporting kits from central locations. Partners will ensure that targeted families will receive training on the best usage of the SOKs and distribute manuals along with the kits.

Activities aim to improve safety and privacy elements in families’ shelters which are critical to adequate shelter conditions for women, men, girls and boys. Furthermore, the proposed project will contribute to improve the substandard shelters by protecting from climate and foster healthier conditions.

CCR will coordinate with the Community Resource Centers in Anbar Governorate and HLP actors to address the needs of HLP intervention of targeted families. CCR will ensure that no harm is associated with its intervention on vulnerable families especially related to governmental compensation and lands properties and rights issues.

project_name: Protection assistance for Crisis-Affected People in Syria
project_objective: DRC's Protection intervention in Syria during 2019 will deliver child protection, social services, and legal assistance in Damascus, Rural Damascus, Dar'a, Homs, Hama, Aleppo, and Deir-ez-Zor.

project_name: Fortalecimiento comunitario y asistencia humanitaria a personas con necesidades específicas en comunidades priorizadas de Venezuela.
project_objective:
En el marco del Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria, y dando continuidad a su trabajo de protección con enfoque comunitario, el ACNUR pretende ampliar sus intervenciones comunitarias en los siguientes sectores de protección; alojamiento, energía y enseres; educación; seguridad alimentaria; salud y agua y saneamiento, siendo el enfoque de protección el eje central de todas las intervenciones.
Protección: se trabajara con las estructuras comunitarias en derechos y rutas de atención, asistencia humanitaria individual, dotaciones y apoyo a infraestructuras comunitarias. También asegurará la respuesta multisectorial a nivel comunitario a través de intervenciones en materia de educación, agua y saneamiento y alojamiento, como estrategia de prevención y protección al desplazamiento. De igual forma ampliará las redes de protección para proporcionar información, asesoría y asistencia humanitaria a personas en tránsito, personas en riesgo de apatridia, y desplazados internos. 
En coordinación con el sector de protección y el Área de Responsabilidad para la Violencia de Género, promoverá espacios seguros y las rutas de atención para sobrevivientes de violencia de género y realizará la gestión de los casos.
Asimismo, en coordinación con el Área de Responsabilidad para la Protección de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes, brindará atención psicosocial y asistencia material a niños, niñas y adolescentes en riesgo, y promoverá una atención integral.
Alojamiento, energía y enseres: se realizaran cuatro tipos de intervenciones: dotaciones y mejora de infraestructura a centros de tránsito en áreas cercanas a la frontera y fortalecimiento de su gestión;  extensión o reparación de viviendas individuales de personas que viven en condiciones de hacinamiento; capacitaciones sobre construcción segura y distribución de lámparas solares y enseres.
Educación: con el fin de promover el derecho a la educación y prevenir riesgos de protección relacionados con la desescolarización de niños, niñas y adolescentes, se prevé incrementar las dotaciones y la rehabilitación de infraestructura en las escuelas de las comunidades vulnerables. 
Agua y saneamiento: mejora de las condiciones de agua y saneamiento de las comunidades más afectadas, especialmente comunidades indígenas, mediante la provisión de tanques de agua, tabletas de cloración, filtros de agua y kits de higiene. Realizará capacitaciones a las estructuras comunitarias sobre purificación y tratamiento seguro del agua e higiene.
Seguridad alimentaria: se trabajará en acciones que mitiguen el hambre, en este sentido  entregará alimentos preparados y no preparados a personas en riesgo de desnutrición, a personas con necesidades específicas  y a familias con algún miembro en riesgo de desnutrición. También realizará evaluaciones nutricionales y sesiones informativas para maximizar el uso de ingredientes nutrientes y técnicas que incluyen productos autóctonos para la elaboración y conservación de alimentos.

project_name: Reducir la morbimortalidad materna, embarazo adolescente, infecciones de transmisión sexual/VIH y violencia sexual en población vulnerable de 8 estados priorizados
project_objective:
El proyecto, se alinea con la estrategia concertada del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS) y el mandato UNFPA. El objetivo es salvar vidas, fortaleciendo la capacidad de respuesta y operatividad   de centros de salud en 8 estados priorizados por el sistema de Naciones Unidas y la estrategia nacional para la reducción de la muerte materna del MPPS.  El proyecto intensifica las acciones MISP ya impulsadas por UNFPA en el marco CERF, ampliándose en esta etapa a los estados Zulia, Táchira, Apure, Bolívar y Guárico, además de Miranda, Distrito Capital y Anzoátegui. Su cobertura abarca 80 centros de salud (21 hospitales y 59 centros de atención primaria) para garantizar servicios de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva y suministros a la población, con especial énfasis en las mujeres en edad reproductiva más vulnerables, como adolescentes, jóvenes y embarazadas. Las actividades están dirigidas a disminuir la morbilidad y mortalidad materna, estimadas entre 77 y 124 muertes maternas por 100.000 nacimientos,  a través del fortalecimiento del talento humano, aseguramiento de equipos e insumos para la respuesta efectiva a  emergencias obstétricas y la prevención del embarazo no deseado, especialmente en adolescentes (22 de cada 100 nacimientos corresponden a madres adolescentes) y la falta de métodos anticonceptivos en la red pública y de farmacias privadas se  estima en  80%. El proyecto también dará respuesta a la necesidad de mejorar la atención del sistema de salud a la violencia sexual, reforzando con insumos y capacidades para el manejo clínico. Asimismo, fortalecerá a la comunidad a través de acciones de comunicación que permitan mayores niveles de información y participación. 
La sostenibilidad y su estrategia de salida están contempladas por el proyecto.
Actividades:
     	1.Procura y distribución de equipos, medicamentos, insumos y  anticonceptivos.
     	2.Actualización en Cuidados Obstétricos de Emergencia, Anticoncepción, Higiene Hospitalaria, ITS, VIH y embarazo, Sangre Segura, manejo clínico de violencia sexual, sistemas para registro y control de insumos, estrategias para uso efectivo de recursos hospitalarios, bajo enfoque integral de derechos.
 	3.Sensibilización e información a la comunidad para el reconocimiento de los signos de alarma durante el embarazo, métodos anticonceptivos reversibles a largo plazo.
  	4.Rehabilitación necesaria para la atención de la paciente obstétrica en cuanto a los servicios mínimos esenciales de agua y luz.
 	5.Fortalecimiento sistema de referencia. 
  
Población dentro del área de cobertura del proyecto:
Mujeres edad reproductiva: 2.000.009
Mujeres adolescentes 10 a 19 años: 529.744
Mujeres embarazadas: 185.823
Mujeres embarazadas con riesgo de complicaciones: 27.874

project_name: Respuesta multisectorial especializada y prevención a la violencia basada en género para mujeres y adolescentes en situación de vulnerabilidad y movilidad
project_objective: El proyecto contribuye a reducir el riesgo de Violencia basada en Género (VBG) para las mujeres y adolescentes venezolanas en situación de vulnerabilidad y de movilidad y contribuye a crear respuestas especializadas y garantizar que las sobrevivientes de VBG tengan acceso a servicios de calidad y oportunamente. El proyecto beneficiará directamente a 300.000 mujeres, niñas, niños y hombres través de estrategias de información y sensibilización en prevención de la VBG. En particular, proveerá de servicios de prevención y respuesta a 3.200 mujeres y adolescentes, quienes acceden a servicios de tipo especializado y personalizado y a 50.000 mujeres y adolescentes que reciben kits de dignidad. Además, el proyecto alcanza indirectamente a 700.000 personas con campañas transmediaticas. Por otro lado, se propone fortalecer capacidades del Sistema de Protección y Justicia y  personal de salud en directrices para la prevención y respuesta de la VBG bajo los estándares internacionales de la acción humanitaria, bajo un enfoque de derechos humanos. El  proyecto articula con el área de salud sexual y reproductiva y fortalece el desarrollo de rutas de remisión y mecanismos de coordinación. El proyecto contribuirá a establecer un mecanismo coordinado de monitoreo de protección, fortaleciendo capacidades para la generación y compilación de información sobre VBG, su sistematización  y armonización con herramientas de evaluación y programación. En este àmbito, promoverà la realizaciòn de anàlisis y evaluaciones sobre la incidencia de la VBG, en estrecha colaboración con la institucionalidad y otras agencias del Sistema de Naciones Unidas. Fortalecerá igualmente la provisión de servicios y la gestión de casos, con un enfoque basado en la sobreviviente, a través del establecimiento de mecanismos y protocolos de atención, rutas de remisión y procedimientos operativos estandarizados (SOPs) intersectoriales . Como estrategia para lograr el empoderamiento y resiliencia de las mujeres y adolescentes, se propone establecer y fortalecer Espacios Seguros exclusivos donde puedan socializar y reconstruir sus redes sociales, recibir apoyo social, adquirir habilidades relevantes, acceder a servicios multisectoriales seguros y  recibir información sobre derechos y salud sexual y reproductiva. Por último, se busca fortalecer las capacidades de de los proveedores de servicios gubernamentales en directrices y procedimientos para la prevención de la VBG en la acción humanitaria, lo que incluye apoyar el desarrollo de un Protocolo Nacional en prevención y respuesta a la violencia basada en género.  El proyecto se localiza en 8 de los 10 estados priorizados con necesidad de protección, con un especial énfasis en los estados frontera con Colombia (Apure, Tàchira y Zulia) y con Brasil (Bolìvar), ademàs del Distrito Capital, Carabobo, Sucre y el estado Miranda. El proyecto se enmarca en los 4 objetivos estratégicos del Sector Protecciòn, a saber, establecer un mecanismo coordinado de monitoreo de protección; proporcionar asistencia y servicios de protección especializados; fortalecer la resiliencia y mecanismos de empoderamiento; fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones del Estado, organizaciones humanitarias y la sociedad civil.  En síntesis, este proyecto propone fortalecer las intervenciones en torno a la prevención y respuesta a la VBG en un contexto de crisis humanitaria, situación que en sí misma produce un aumento en la vulnerabilidad de las mujeres y adolescentes por su condición de movilidad, incrementando el riesgo y la exposición a sufrir algún tipo de violencia, sobre todo violencia sexual. Se trata de una propuesta integral y multisectorial, articulada con otros ámbitos de acción de la respuesta humanitaria, como lo es la salud sexual y reproductiva.

project_name: Improve the coverage and quality of SAM inpatient care in 134 existing Stabilization Centers in Sudan.
project_objective:
WHO project aims to decrease avoidable under five mortality and morbidity related to severe acute malnutrition through improved access and quality of inpatient care for the Sever Acute Malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications in 134 stabilization centers operating in health facilities. The project includes curative, preventive and promotive measures in the same time. The activities will address the clinical life-saving interventions in Stabilization centers targeting the patients/children with SAM and the mothers/care-takers through IYCF counseling and young children nutrition awareness to lower relapse and prevent SAM cases in the same households. The project activities and costing factored in 49 SCs are supported by UNICEF(11 SCs) and Partners NGOs (38). The SCs supported by NGOs will require only Medical kits/ secondary level and lab investigation support, along with IYCF training and counselling, and UNICEF will cover 14% of the caseload through the 11 SCs, most of them in big towns.  
Main activities: Training of the  health and nutrition staff of 85 SCs (all except the ones supported by UNICEF and NGOs) to include  IPD SAM initial training (7 days) and refresher training (3 days), provision of guidelines, Job Aids and IEC materials to all participants from the 85 SCs. WHO will procure and distribute to 123 SCs (all except the UNICEF supported SCs) medicines (SAM inpatient Kits – secondary level care), lab reagents for investigation essential for case-management, medical equipment and other supplies based on the needs identified together with MOH and partners. 
To improve the quality of care and cure rate in SCs, WHO nutrition and public health officers present in all targeted states will conduct jointly with SMOH regular supportive supervisions in all targeted 134 SCs conducting on the job training, coaching, and adherence to the national treatment protocols. 
Routine nutrition surveillance at HF level/SCs, essential for trends and gap identification and effective planning of activities will be enhanced through training, provision of recording and reporting tools for 123 SC (all except UNICEF supported), and better integration into HFs reporting mechanism to promote sustainability. WHO nutrition team will provide technical and operational support to the MOH at federal and state levels to regularly analysis the data of SAM inpatient care services (using the agreed performance indicators) to identify the trends, and challenges dis aggregated by sex and age. The information will be disseminate to all relevant stakeholders through nutrition cluster bulletins, and briefing during the meetings led by UNICEF and MOH. Effective coordination of WHO with all partners (Nutrition, Health, food security) will promote an improved referral system between the SCs, TSFP, OTP, and community. Linkages with communities will be strengthened through raising awareness and social mobilization conducted by trained community mobilizers/CHW in coordination with other UN. The modalities and subjects for these activities will be guided by the community members suggestions collected through exit interview and focus group discussions during supervisions. The project activities also includes small repairs of 25 SCs in order to ensure better environment for work and improved hygiene in the SCs.
