project_name: Relief Food and Livelihood Assistance for Internally Displaced Persons and Returnees in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Merged Districts of KP.
project_objective:
WFP has been assisting the displaced people from merged districts for over eight years now. However, 2016 and 2017 observed a considerable number of displaced people returning to their areas of origin after the launch of the KP merged districts Sustainable Return and Rehabilitation Strategy (SRRS) in April 2015. In response to the phase wise plan around 2.6 million (266,261 individuals have returned to their areas of origin in KP merged districts successfully, with around 699,978 registered individuals (15,833 families) still displaced. An estimated 255,906 individual returnees are members of 42,651 female headed households.  As the government plans to continue with the return of the remaining IDPs in 2019, WFP’s response will need to be aligned with government’s merged districts SRRS for returnees in KP merged districts. WFP will also continue with its relief food assistance to IDPs and returnees which include women (23%), men (23%), Boys under 18 (30%) and Girls under 18 (24%) and the extremely vulnerable.

WFP’s assistance to families returning to their areas of origin will ensue that basic needs continue to be met despite adverse availability and access conditions at home, thereby allowing recovery efforts to proceed, unhindered by immediate food security concerns. The recovery assistance will be initiated upon completion of the six months return food package. The recovery activities include rehabilitation of their livelihood assets through food for assets and trainings. A significant proportion of women will benefit from training on the latest food security and livelihood best practices in their local context. The assistance in recovery phase will be conditional upon work or training. 

Activities or outputs
Relief food assistance is provided on a monthly basis with the general family food basket consisting of cereals   fortified wheat flour or rice (80Kg), pulses (8Kg), salt (0.2 Kg), and vegetable oil (4.5Kg).
 
Special consideration is given to the provision of food assistance to the most vulnerable groups in the communities, including the elderly, sick, disabled, children, pregnant and lactating mothers, and female and child headed households. WFP ensures that general food distribution as well as all programmatic activities are conducted in a safe and dignified manner and in adherence to the WFP Humanitarian Protection Policy (2012), including basic humanitarian and do no harm principles. Separate distribution counters and waiting areas are established at distribution points where female staff are deployed. Assessment teams aim to include women where possible and beneficiary data is disaggregated by gender.

Cash and food transfers will be the primary modalities of assistance. Cash transfers will be used in post shock recovery to help short term food insecurity and encourage market functionality. Food assistance for assets will utilize cash as a modality of support and areas will be targeted based on food security needs, according to local contexts and market conditions. WFP’s VAM unit will further strengthen food security monitoring systems through participation.
Indicators and Targets
Number of assets built, restored or maintained by targeted households and communities;
Number of men, women, boys, girls receiving life saving food assistance to address their immediate hunger needs and nutritional requirment.

project_name: Mejora del acceso de la población vulnerable a los servicios básicos de agua, saneamiento e higiene en los establecimientos de salud y nutrición, instituciones educativas y centros de protección
project_objective:
Con este proyecto, se abordará la mejora de los servicios WASH en las establecimientos e instituciones estratégicas de los servicios de salud, nutrición, educación y protección (incluyendo puntos estratégicos asociados a procesos migratorios, como centros de migrantes, terminales, etc.). 

Este proyecto reforzará el rol del sector WASH como facilitador del acceso a otros servicios básicos de calidad. Desde UNICEF y OMS se incide a todos los niveles para destacar que un establecimiento de salud sin los servicios WASH asegurados no puede ser considerado como establecimiento de salud como tal. En el caso de Venezuela, los servicios WASH en los establecimientos de salud han sido fuertemente afectados. Estudios alternativos indican que un 79% de los establecimientos de salud presentan problemas de acceso a agua potable. Las actividades WASH incluirán medidas de Prevención de Enfermedades Infecciosas en Entorno Hospitalario. 

Para todas las instituciones, la intervención WASH incluye:

-Reparación, rehabilitación y acondicionamiento de instalaciones WASH.
-Fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal técnico asociado a cada institución, para la promoción de la higiene, el mantenimiento y para el tratamiento y conservación del agua en las instituciones.
-Actividades de promoción de la higiene, vinculadas a la estrategia de comunicación para el desarrollo.
-Distribución de suministros básicos para la higiene y para el tratamiento y conservación del agua en las instituciones. 

Específicamente, Las actividades WASH previstas en los establecimientos de salud y de recuperación nutricional son:

-Promoción de prácticas clave de higiene en los pacientes y en personal de salud.

-Reparación de los sistemas de saneamiento y de drenaje y vaciado de fosas sépticas o similares.

-Distribución de productos básicos para la higiene y la limpieza del centro escolar.

-Reparaciones de instalaciones e infraestructuras WASH, instalacion de tanques o distribucion por camion cisterna
-Distribucion de productos basicos de higiene para las familias mas vulnerables

En el caso de centros de migrantes y de terminales, se incluyen acciones de:

-Rehabilitación y reparación de sistemas WASH.
-Formación del personal técnico para la promoción de la higiene y el tratamiento y conservación del agua en las terminales o en los centros.
-Distribución de productos básicos para la higiene y la limpieza del centro o terminal.
-Distribución de productos básicos de higiene y de tratamiento y conservación del agua en el hogar para las familias más vulnerables, en coordinación con el proyecto 1 de UNICEF de WASH a nivel comunitario

-Con Ministerio de Educación y Ministerio de Salud, se implementará una campaña nacional de información y formación en promocion de higiene

project_name: Establecer la Matriz de Seguimiento de Desplazamiento (DTM) en Venezuela.
project_objective:
En Venezuela, la disponibilidad de datos sobre población y necesidades es actualmente muy limitada. Los datos cuantitativos, sistemáticos y actualizados son particularmente problemáticos. 

Se han implementado algunas encuestas posteriormente al último censo de 2011, pero no existe recopilación activa de datos en curso, aquellos recopilados por las autoridades gubernamentales no están disponibles públicamente ni se recopilan de manera bilateral. La información con la que cuentan los actores es parcial. Aunque de manera evidente la población venezolana se ha desplazado a los estados de frontera o ha migrado a las ciudades más grandes, este desplazamiento no ha sido registrado.

La Matriz de Seguimiento de Desplazamientos (DTM, por sus siglas en inglés) es un sistema para rastrear y monitorear el desplazamiento y la movilidad de la población de forma regular y sistemática para una mejor comprensión de los movimientos y las necesidades cambiantes.

Los equipos de DTM identifican áreas de alta movilidad y puntos estratégicos de tránsito. Recogen el dato de informantes clave presentes en el punto de monitoreo de flujo  (personal de estaciones de transporte y servicios, policías, funcionarios de aduanas, conductores de autobuses o los propios migrantes. Un cuestionario básico combinado con observaciones directas permite recoger datos desglosados por sexo y nacionalidad. Los puntos de seguimiento de flujo son elegidos después de consultar con actores nacionales y locales involucrados en gestión de la migración, dependiendo de la ubicación y las características de los flujos que transitan a través de estos espacios.

La activación del programa de DTM en Venezuela serviría como apoyo a los actores humanitarios en el país, respondiendo a las brechas internas de información e integrando y complementando las actividades de recopilación de datos a nivel regional. 

Descripción preliminar de las actividades del DTM:

Estos ejercicios están interconectados y construidos de una manera consistente en fases para proporcionar un nivel adicional de detalles y verificación en cada paso, desde el más rápido hasta el más profundo:

1. Análisis de la situación basado en el análisis de métodos mixtos de datos cuantitativos secundarios y datos cualitativos primarios y secundarios.
2. Investigación cualitativa para abordar temas para los cuales los métodos cuantitativos no son adecuados o para segmentar segmentos de la población a menudo con poca representación en ejercicios de investigación cuantitativa de mayor alcance.
3. Comité de evaluación de necesidades: DTM participará activamente en el Grupo de trabajo de administración de información (IMWG) y liderará un comité de evaluación de necesidades, para armonizar los datos y facilitar el análisis conjunto.
4. Creación de capacidad para aumentar el conocimiento de los datos, desarrollar la capacidad local y cooperar con los socios y las autoridades.
5. Monitoreo de la población (línea de base) que se actualizaría de manera regular (mínimo bimestralmente) y brindará información más detallada sobre la población una vez que se haya establecido.
6. Monitoreo de flujos en puntos clave de tránsito y cruce de fronteras, coordinados con los equipos correspondientes a través de la frontera. La OIM ya ha realizado ejercicios de DTM en las zonas fronterizas de Brasil y Colombia. La identificación de puntos y conteos pueden complementarse con encuestas para perfilar a la población en movimiento.
7. Evaluación de ubicación multisectorial integrada tanto en las zonas urbanas como rurales, independientemente del tipo de asentamiento, cubriendo por lo tanto sitios colectivos como dispersos. Estas evaluaciones tienen como objetivo detallar las necesidades de la población en movimiento, desplazada, retornada y de la comunidad de acogida.
8. Evaluaciones temáticas, formulando evaluaciones temáticas para necesidades sectoriales específicas (por ejemplo, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), auditoría de seguridad, etc.)

project_name: Agricultural productivity and food security for cyclone Idai affected population in Sofala, Manica and Zambezia provinces
project_objective:
The Cyclone Idai weather system swept through five provinces – Sofala, Manica, Tete, Zambezia and Inhambane – decimating livelihoods and leaving a wake of death, destruction and damage. The Cyclone damaged nearly 500,000 hectares of crops, along with other livelihoods, right before the annual harvest. This number is expected to rise as the full extent of the damage becomes known. Extensive livestock losses are expected, as well as widespread damage to fisher folks’ assets. Many assets and structures, including markets in the port city of Beira, have been destroyed. Food insecurity is therefore expected to rise significantly in the months ahead as a result of the destruction and damage. Women in Mozambique play a critical role in agricultural production, providing labour to support the production of food crops and also supporting the production of cash crops. At the same time, women remain responsible for the majority of caregiving. With the caregiving burden likely to increase in the aftermath of the cyclone and floods – as illness and injury have risen – women may have to decrease their agricultural production, further heightening food insecurity.
Goal: Resilience of Cyclone Idai Affected Communities strengthened though general food distribution, own food production, income generating activities and disaster risk reduction.
Lifesaving interventions: Increased access to nutritious food 
Activities: 
• Food distribution
• Food for asset
• Where feasible Cash for work
• Pilot targeted cash transfers.
• Promote vegetable growing through kitchen gardens to increase dietary diversity
Early Recovery: Objective 2: Increased food production 
Activities:
• Agriculture support activities- access to agricultural inputs (drought resistant/ locally adaptable seeds and tools).
•	Livestock support interventions, restocking birds (poultry), small ruminants (sheep and goats), rabbitry, piggery. 
•	Vaccination campaigns 
• Community seed multiplication initiatives linked to markets
• Promote and support good agronomic practices that enhance quality production using techniques that are friendly to the environment
• Promote fertility enhancement and management intervention using organic and compost manure.
• Promote soil and water management structures to control flood and soil erosion.
• Rehabilitation of key livelihood infrastructure such as roads and water facilities (check dams, water catchments and reservoirs)
• Promote and scaling up water use efficient methodologies and technologies such as conservation agriculture; 
• Support agriculture value chains (value addition)- support to develop businesses, promote SME
Objective 3: Increased income to promote self-reliance
Activities
• Establish and promote saving and loan schemes using Saving for Transformation model
• Business facilitation interventions to enable small businesses and other income generating activities to grow and thrive. 
• Entrepreneurship and life skill trainings that enhance their personal competence
• Promote and strengthen Disaster Risk Reduction and mitigation activities.

project_name: Improved Access to Food and Self-Reliance Opportunities for Refugees and Host Communities in Cox Bazaar
project_objective:
The project will: 
1. Ensure and sustain timely provision of life-saving food assistance for Rohingya refugees. 
2. Promote self-reliance opportunities for Rohingya refugees and enhance the livelihoods & resilience of host communities.

project_name: Strengthened humanitarian response capacity in common operational areas through the provision of reliable security communications and Internet connectivity
project_objective: The Emergency Telecommunications Sector aims at fullfilling identified needs for reliable security communications and Internet connectivity services in common operational areas, as well as to enhance the current capacity. The ET Sector also aims at supporting the humanitarian community, in collaboration with inter-sector initiatives, to improve affected population’ access to vital information and communication services

project_name: Assistance alimentaire non conditionnelle aux personnes vulnérables à l'insécurité alimentaire à la suite des chocs divers
project_objective: Dans les provinces à vulnérabilités composites à l’insécurité alimentaire, les populations en phases IPC 3 & 4 aigues à majorité des retournés,  des PDIs, des victimes d'aléas climatiques, maladies et ravageurs des plantes ainsi que d'autres ménages d'accueil sont identifiés pour bénéficier d'une assistance alimentaire non conditionnelle pendant les périodes de soudure. project_name: Peru - RET International
Peru - CARE
Ecuador - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women
Provision of in and out of camp CCCM services to conflict affected populations in Iraq
project_objective:
ACTED’s strategy for CCCM activities in 2019 intends to continue to provide both in and out of camp CCCM services to conflict affected populations throughout Ninewa, Dohuk, Sulaymaniyah and Diayla governorates. Planned interventions are designed based on the CCCM Cluster objectives for 2019.
As such, ACTED as member of the Ninewa Governate Returns Committee as well as the CCCM Cluster Strategic Advisory Group and the co-lead of the Dohuk CCCM Cluster will continue to promote all facets of the Principled Returns Framework. 
ACTED intends to continue to support government and national camp management via its tested mobile CCCM team modality, which can support both formal and informal sites across a large geographical area, and can flexibly be deployed to support existing or any new needs as they arise. This will include 17 camps in the Dohuk governorate, 1 camp in the Sulaymaniyah governorate and 1 in the Diyala governorate. ACTED will tailor its interventions to the needs of the residents in each camp and the capacities of the camp management. ACTED will also continue to support informal settlements including conducting RASPs in Dohuk and Northern Ninewa in collaboration with the REACH initiatives and the CCCM Cluster, on a regular basis as required, or should new displacement take place in these areas. ACTED will also provide an information management and humanitarian coordination via opening a Community Resource Centre in Mosul throughout 2019. 
Under its 2019 CCCM programming ACTED will reach approximately 202.609 conflict-affected individuals (women, men, boys and girls) across four governorates (Dohuk, Ninewa, Sulaimaniyah and Diayala) including internally displaced persons residing in formal camps (190,317 persons), namely Salamyiah 1 and 2 as in Ninewa governorate, Tazade camp in Sulaimanyiah, Qaratu camp in Diyala as well as all Dohuk camps (Berseve 1 , Berseve 2, Derkar, Chamishku, Qadiya, Bajidkandala 1&2, Khanke, Sharya, Kabarto 1 and 2, Essian, Shekhan, Mamrashan, Garmawa , Mamilian, Dawodiya). In informal sites ACTED will reach 12.292 displaced persons in following locations: Sumel, Zakho (Dohuk governorate) and Shikhan, Akre, Tilkaif, and Mosul (Ninewa governorate). The project will also target 10,000 returnees who will benefit from establishment of Community Resource Center in Mosul City in collaboration with OFDA. As at the stage of writing the ACTED was yet finalising the selection process of the location for establishing the CRC, the number of the members of host communities targeted with this element of CCCM programming cannot be estimated.

project_name: NFI and shelter kit distribution for vulnerable households in Kirkuk
project_objective:
This project will target the most vulnerable IDPs and returnees identified by the shelter cluster in Kirkuk governorate with NFI and shelter assistance throughout 2019. HRF will procure adequate stocks of NFI/winterization kits and shelter/SOKs to cover the needs of in and out of camp IDPs and returnees across Kirkuk governorate, provisionally based upon target beneficiary numbers provided by the Shelter/NFI cluster. 

HRF will build on existing relationships with vulnerable groups in Kirkuk which have been developed through existing HRF programmes in the governorate, this is particularly the case with in and out of camp IDPs in the three target districts, Daquq, Kirkuk city and Hawiga.

project_name: Risk Mitigation Information Management Center
project_objective:
The overall objective of this project is to strengthen situational awareness and enhance humanitarian actors’ knowledge on access, risks, and vulnerabilities of populations affected by the ISIS operations and promote principled, coordinated and standardized approaches to information management across clusters and sectors for diverse recipient groups, including maintaining common data and information repositories.

The project also aims to rapidly assess and analyze the level of threat/contamination and the security situation to set up safety, security and risk-free management systems in new contexts and provide rapid onset emergency response information to Humanitarian Actors (HA) involved in the humanitarian responses. In addition, the project aims to provide information ﬂow channels to the IDPs, returnees and host communities about the explosive hazard threats, in order to enhance their security and provide a safer environment.

project_name: Provision of Transitional Shelters for Extremely Vulnerable Families in Zummar Sub-district
project_objective: In line with guidance and priorities determined by the Shelter-NFI (S-NFI ) Cluster, UN-Habitat will provide transitional shelter solutions for extremely vulnerable returnees in underserved and recently retaken areas across Zummar Sub-district in Nineveh Governorate. Technical support and appropriate local materials will be provided for the construction of 400 transitional shelters using dried mud-bricks, prioritizing households whose original homes were assessed as falling within category 3 (severely damaged) and 4 (destroyed) war-damaged houses in the area. Cash for work transfers for the production of bricks and construction will also be provided. Support to Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights will be integrated during the planning and implementation phases of the project. UN-Habitat will ensure the HLP status of beneficiaries in order to prevent any land and property disputes. The project will directly benefit 2,400 extremely vulnerable people needing assistance for a durable return to their areas of origin, including 400 women, 400 men, 800 girls, 800 boys.

project_name: Organised Local Response Program - Protection
project_objective:
The program seeks to respond to the prolonged humanitarian crisis affecting the Palestinian population under occupation, by contributing to the protection of their rights and dignity in accordance with IHL and IHRL, and with a cross-cutting focus on gender and community participation. The program is to be implemented by the Action Group (Protection Cluster Partners) for Organised Local Response, a group of civil society organisations that seeks to promote the localisation of humanitarian response, and to respond to the multiple needs of Palestinian communities in an organised manner, by building on the respective sectoral and geographical strengths of each of its members. The program as a whole is multi-sectoral, and includes actions linked to protection, livelihoods, WASH, education, mental health and advocacy. 

Despite the fact that the program address many sectors, it has been divided in sectoral projects to ease the management of such a comprehensive program. In this sense, the present project include only the protection-cluster-related activities even though the whole program is in line with the strategic objectives of the Protection Cluster as it i) seeks to increase the respect for the IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations as well as ii) to put in place protection mechanisms -as the CPC or the provision of protection services- to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence such as settler violence, property damage and confiscation, blockade and restrictions and violations against children.

The population targeted under the program is highly vulnerable to IHL/IHRL violations due to the presence of their communities primarily in Area C, and to their proximity to settlements, military bases and Israeli checkpoints. The program pays special attention to the different vulnerabilities, needs and capacities of women, men, girls and boys. Of those groups, specific targets are children affected by the conflict, women affected by GBV and vulnerable victims of conflict-related violence such us land workers and youth,

project_name: Rehabilitation Abris Provisoires et Renforcement institutionnel en GRD
project_objective:
Le projet vise les départements de l’Ouest (communes de Tabarre et Croix des Bouquets) et le département du Nord Ouest (commune de Port de Paix).

Les communes de Tabarre et Croix des Bouquets, où COOPI travaille depuis 2010 à niveau communautaire dans le domaine de la GRD, sont affectés par les aléas hydro-météorologiques et géologiques (par ex. tremblement de terre, glissements de terrain, inondations, ouragans et fortes pluies) et aléas anthropiques (par ex. Incendies, pollution, épidémies comme le choléra). Ces aléas sont amplifiés par des facteurs anthropiques (imperméabilisation du sol, constructions dans des zones à risque, exploitation des lits des rivières manque d’un service de gestion des déchets solides, etc). D’autre part les acteurs locaux manquent de capacités et d’instruments pour un processus de prise de décision inclusif et participatif dans l’aménagement du territoire orienté à la Gestion des Risques et des Désastres (GRD). 

L’intervention vise à atténuer l’exposition aux aléas géologiques et hydro-météorologiques répondant aux deux besoins principaux: i) Capacités institutionnelles des communautés et des acteurs locaux; ii) Abris provisoires d’urgence fonctionnels et conformes aux paramètres standards pour la protection des femmes, enfants et personnes en situation de handicap. A partir de cette analyse, les actions visées sont: a) Renforcement de la connaissance en GRD pour les communautés et les institutions locales; b) Réhabilitation des abris provisoires selon les standards SPHERE et renforcement des capacités dans la construction (antisismique et anticiclonique) et dans la gestion des abris de la part des acteurs competents.

Il a été démontré que les femmes, pendant et après une catastrophe, ont possibilité de mourir 14 fois de plus comparé aux hommes, dû au rôle de la femme dans la société, souvent mise à l’écart ou sous éduquée. En plus, elles sont victimes de violences domestiques et sexuelles qui augmentent après une catastrophe; en faite nombreuse femmes nous ont déclaré pendant les activités qu’elles évitaient de se réfugier dans les abris provisoires par crainte d’y être sexuellement agressées. Pour les raisons listés, la méthodologie de l’intervention se focalise sur la leadership des femmes dans la GRD et sur le chantier. Les formations sur la construction antisismique et anticyclonique seront conduites par une association des femmes maçons (Regroupement des Femmes Professionnelles en Constructions en Haity RSOPCH)  à fin de casser le préjugé sur la femme dans ce domaine. 

Notre intervention se situe aussi dans la commune de Port de Paix dans le Nord Ouest, département où COOPI est présent avec un projet de réponse à la sécheresse, qui a ete frappé par un séisme de magnitude 5.9 le samedi 6 octobre à 20h12 causant des pertes en vies humaines et des dégâts matériels importants. COOPI vise à intervenir dans cette zone avec le but de réhabiliter les abris provisoires présent selon les standards SPHERE et renforcer les capacités de construction et de gestion des acteurs communautaires impliqués.

project_name: Integrating Women into Disaster Preparedness and Response (Fanm yo pare)
project_objective:
Given its international experience in disaster risk reduction, resilience and women’s empowerment, Mercy Corps seeks to implement a project that addresses women’s needs and perspectives in local contingency planning in order to pave the way for humanitarian response that will adequately address vulnerabilities and capitalize on positive gender dynamics in target communities. By partnering with women’s organizations that are involved in local humanitarian and development efforts, Mercy Corps will provide them with tools needed to better integrate women’s needs into their planning, as well as better link their planning to department-level DRR plans. 
The “Fanm yo pare” project aims to build capacity of women’s organizations to support women’s empowerment and strengthen the resilience of women to better face natural disasters. The project's activities will be developed and adapted to meet the needs of women in the west (Cabaret and Arcahaie) and the Nippes departments. The project will integrate 750 women and men into gender-focused DRR and humanitarian response trainings, workshops, and working sessions, and also integrate 1250 women and men into VSLAs, which will contribute to gender equity and social cohesion in the target communities. This multi-platform approach will build understanding of gender and protection among civil society at large, and will integrate women, girls, boys and men's needs into contingency planning, which has the potential to improve humanitarian response for the larger community, estimated at about 10,500 direct and indirect beneficiaries. 
Outcomes:
1. Women's organizations have the capacity to ensure gender-responsive disaster-risk reduction planning and action, and emergency response at the community level.

project_name: Renforcement des capacites de production des agriculteurs et les moyens de subsistances des menages
project_objective: Renforcer la  capacite de résilience  des agriculteurs, des familles en situation d'insécurite alimentaire, par formation sur les techniques de production et conservation de produits.

project_name: Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre
project_objective:
The Iraq Internally Displaced Persons Information Centre (IIC) is an inter agency accountability mechanism that allows affected populations to access information on existing and planned humanitarian assistance and convey feedback on and complaints about the humanitarian response in Iraq. 

The objective of this project is to ensure that feedback from callers identifies gaps in assistance, permits ongoing information exchange, influences how information is shared, and shapes how humanitarian assistance is organised and delivered. 

Accountability to Affected People (taking account, giving account and being held to account) lies at the heart of the Iraq IIC.

In 2019 the project will target IDPs in and outside camps and returnees, supporting- together with the other humanitarian actors- the transition to durable solution, but also supporting protection through provision of information and referrals.

project_name: Building Resilience of Conflict-affected people through Agriculture and Livestock Interventions in NW Syria
project_objective:
The objective of this program is to ensure and improve the food security for the conflict affected populations in north-west Syria through the provision of agricultural and livestock support that would contribute to securing the food needs for the beneficiary farmers and livestock keepers. This program comprise the following main components: 

1. provision of agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizer, pesticide and equipment). Target: 6000 farmers (reached as of mid-year: 3700.
2. distribution of animal feed (fodder/barley) to the sheep and goats of vulnerable livestock keepers. Target: 2000 livestock keepers (reached as of mid-year: 1157). 
3. conduct livestock vaccination campaigns immunizing the livestock against different livestock diseases such as: (Enterotoxemia, Foot and Mouth Diseases, and Brucella). Target: 200,000 livestock heads (reached as of mid-year: 2000 heads). 
4. rehabilitation of main infrastructure related to agriculture such as (canals, irrigation systems, markets, storage facilities, bakeries, etc.) Target: 20 projects and 2000 CFW workers (reached as of mid-year: 5 projects and 200 workers).
5. supporting farmer groups/initiatives. Target: 10 groups/initiatives (reached as of mid-year 3 groups).
6. support the provision of extension services. Target: 5000 farmers/livestock keepers (reached as of mid-year: 2500 farmers/livestock keepers).

project_name: Protection for IDPs and hard to reach vulnerable host communities in rural areas of Somalia/Somaliland
project_objective: The project will adopt a system-level approach to provide quality care and outcomes for children by focusing on  gaps at the institutional, community  and household and individual level.  The project will  also address the deep-rooted child well-being issues in Somalia at different levels which are caused by, but not limited to, weak governance mechanism and capacity in child protection, low incentives and awareness to further the child welfare agenda of key stakeholders, and high prevalence of poverty and conflict that force vulnerable families apart in search for livelihoods. Result 1 of the project will focus on supporting the government and institutions to provide quality  child care by supporting the implementation of policies and guidelines, capacity enhancement and vulnerability assessment, training of officials and service providers and developing accountability framework and referral mechanisms. Under this action, WV is deliberate to ensure local ownership from the government to community level to create sustainable and concrete impacts for children. Government as a duty-bearers have an obligation to deliver and protect children's rights. Result 2 of the project focuses on tackling child protection issues at the community and household level. Strengthened child protection service provision at community level will help to complement the institutional effort under Result 1. Raising awareness in communities on any harmful practices against children and strengthening community-based child protection structure in schools and communities such as child protection clubs will reduce children’s risk of exposure to exploitation, advocate for best child protection practice and to create an enabling environment to allow possible integration of vulnerable children. Result 3 will focus on cash based assistance to vulnerable households with children at risk of violence. Income generation through unconditional cash transfers will prevent family separation as care givers search for a source of livelihoods to provide for their children's needs especially during emergencies. Cash based assistance also enables reduction of negative coping mechanisms such as child labour, child marriage, child recruitment by non state armed actors, child trafficking, school drop outs and GBV. The project will target IDPs, excluded minority clans, vulnerable host communities and children with disability.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Malnutrition of Children Aged 6 - 59 Months in the Far North (90,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective:
In the Far North region in Cameroon, Boko Haram insurgencies have disrupted the economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities, causing a depletion of livelihoods and household assets. Consequently, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food and nutrition insecurity have been aggravated. 
The main goal of WFP nutrition programme in the Far North region is to contribute to reduction of undernutrition and associated levels of mortality by 2020. WFP through the implementation of the nutrition programme under its Country Strategic Plan(CSP) will facilitate access to appropriate nutritious foods for vulnerable groups to prevent or treat malnutrition and thus makes a crucial contribution to saving lives and strengthening physical resilience to shocks in affected communities.
Therefore, as a nutrition intervention in the Far North Region, WFP will prioritize integrated approaches for prevention and treatment of acute and chronic malnutrition targeting 87,600 children aged 6–23 months through the blanket supplementary feeding programme (BSFP) in targeted health districts and 2,400 moderate acute malnutrition(MAM) children aged 24–59 months in food-insecure areas with high malnutrition rates for 12 months in 2019.

project_name: Seasonal Food Assistance to the Vulnerable Local Population in the Far North (30,000 Beneficiaries)
project_objective: In the Far North region, the Boko Haram insurgency in Nigeria has displaced 100,504 Nigerian refugees in Cameroon as of October 2018, and 98,590 of them live in the Far North region (UNHCR, October 2018). Boko Haram attacks have also resulted in 227,581 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (UNHCR, October 2018), who are struggling to survive in strenuous conditions in villages or small towns in the area. The region is predominantly arid and regularly hit by drought and seasonal floods. Access to basic services is also more limited than in other regions of the country. The arrival of IDPs in food-insecure areas has severely affected host communities as well. This has put enormous pressure on already scarce community resources and the local economy by reducing farm productivity and access to land and food markets. Boko Haram attacks have disrupted the economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in the Far North region, causing a depletion of livelihoods and household assets. As a consequence, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food insecurity have been aggravated. To support the chronically food-insecure and shock-prone areas during the lean seasons in the Far North region, WFP plans to target the most vulnerable 30,000 local population through seasonal food assistance with half ration from May to October in 2019.

project_name: Emergency School Feeding Programmes
project_objective:
WFP will start the implementation of a complementary school meals programme as means to ensure children’s access to food in times of crisis and enhance diets through increased micronutrient intake. Assistance will take into account protection and safety, and where possible, contribute to their broader protection. During the initial stage, the school rations including nutritionally-fortified date bars, which are culturally-acceptable, programmatically-feasible and can contribute to enhanced micronutrient intake among children, will be provided to 20,000 school-aged children.
Introducing emergency school meals into a platform for nutrition-sensitive and gender-responsive programming that can support local food systems. This programme could also provide food incentives to promote and encourage the enrolment of the children of the migrant population who are living in urban areas.
The programme would review implementation arrangements to strengthen synergies with education and livelihood sectors and increase nutrition-sensitivity, gender-sensitivity, local procurement and community ownership. This would promote community infrastructure, rehabilitation, and reconstruction (including schools and health centres) as well as promote the reintegration of displaced populations and returnees, with special attention paid to the different needs of women and men.

project_objective:

project_name: Provision of Food Assistance, Agricultural Assets and Income Generation for vulnerable Returnees and host community in Ninewa Governorate
project_objective:
Mass disruption of livelihoods due to (repetitive) conflict induced displacement, loss of assets and collapsed markets have made a large share of the Iraq population food insecure (estimated 1,9 million people in 2018). 54% of the returnees in Tel Afar and 50% of those in Sinjar (in total 30,477 families) are categorised as high & very high on the return severity index, indicating a dire livelihood- service provision and security situation in their return area. 
In response to this humanitarian crises, and aligned with FSC Objective 1 “Provide emergency food assistance  to displaced families living in camps and sub-standard accommodation” and FSC Objective 2 “Provide agricultural inputs or services to protect agricultural productive assets and help restore fragile livelihoods of returning or vulnerable families” Dorcas together with World Vision, two active leading NGO’s in the FS sector propose to support 14,400 severely vulnerable returnees and host community in Ninewa Governorate with FS support. 
Partners propose to alleviate the suffering of the most vulnerable/food insecure displaced/returning populations in rural Sinjar, Tel Afar (Zummar & Rabea villages) and rural Hamdaniya and in urban Mosul through distribution of four months food vouchers for 2,400 HH - equalling 85% of the minimum SPHERE.  Partners will simultaneously start activities to ensure access to income (through Cash for Work for 300 HH) and emergency agricultural assets (chicken packages, farm packages, small greenhouses, fodder & vaccines for livestock) for 475 vulnerable households, with a key focus on female headed households, so they are able to (re)start their livelihoods on a short-term and/or gain access to nutrition. Food support is planned for 4 months since the proposed livelihood activities are expected to create agricultural turnover after a 3 to 4 month inception period. 
For the agricultural inputs, specific precedence will be given to female headed households for activities that are culturally appropriate and acceptable for the community. Poultry Gardens and Greenhouses are especially suitable for this target group as activities can take place in close proximity to the house, not only decreasing the risks of violence that women face when leaving their homes but also allowing women to combine agricultural work with other core duties as caregivers. Female staff will be included in all exercises to ensure women’s voices are heard and women specific concerns are taken into account.
Both Dorcas and World Vision have an extensive track record in providing emergency Food Assistance and Agricultural Support to affected communities. Dorcas under the second and third standard allocation of IHPF in 2016, 2017  and 2018 in newly retaken areas (including Hamdaniya). World Vision as key partner of WFP for Food Assistance. These actions, together with other multi-million sectoral projects in i.e. Protection, Health, Education, and WASH implemented in the same areas (rural Sinjar, Tel Afar town, Mosul & rural Hamdaniya) have provided Partners with extensive knowledge of the intervention areas and technical expertise to implement food assistance activities sound and cost-efficient and ensuring a holistic service provision to targeted communities.

project_name: Protection and Assistance to conflict affected and displaced persons in South Darfur, East Darfur and Blue Nile States
project_objective:
The proposed project will create a platform where incidences of women and young girls rape cases will be reduced in the conflict affected states of South Darfur, East Darfur and Blue Nile. The community safety management systems and structures will be enhanced in order to reduce the prevalence of FGM and early marriages. Religious leaders will be engaged owing their wide influence in changing the community practices. Many harmful traditional practices will be handled by this new strategy of engaging religious leaders.
Child Protection risks that leads children to be separated will be responded to using the FTR services through multi-sector and Multi-Agency approach. To ensure the identity of children is well understood, the project will engage the department of Registration to provide birth registration to the deserving children. Awareness to the community and government on dangers of recruiting children by armed groups will continue and ensure no children fall victim for child soldiers. Sexual violence on girls and women regardless of its nature will be discouraged at all levels and addressed through the community safety nets while the weakened and overstretched social institutions will be strengthened to offer adequate services.
The project targets boys, Girls, men and women of all ages since protection is a lifesaving intervention to ensure beneficiaries living in the 9 localities of Blue Nile (3), East Darfur (4) and South Darfur (2) are living their lives without fear of attacks and at risk of exposure to violence. A new strategy of engaging religious leaders as the main audience of choice by WVS called Channels of Hope (CoH) will be employed. This strategy has been found to be very popular among WVI Programs especially in highly religious dominance communities.

project_name: CHILD PROTECTION: Emergency Child Protection Assistance & Prevention in Conflict Affected & High Risk Areas
project_objective:
REVISIONS 11/14/18: All revisions requested have been completed: (1) Budget reduced to $800K & cost/beneficiary improved; (2) Explanation of avoiding overlap with other CP partners explained in Summary; (3) CoP, Acct,Comm sections strengthened.
This project seeks to provide life-saving CP prevention, mitigation & response in alignment with the HRP Strategic Objectives 1, 2 & 3, Protection Cluster Strategic Objectives 1 & 2, and the priority strategic objectives/actions identified by the CPSC. 

The project prioritizes Tier 1 Yambio and Nagero; Tier 2 in Aburoc, Juba; Tier 3 in Tonj East, Twic, Gogrial West, Renk, Nzara & Tambura (prioritizing Tier 1 locations but recognizing the limited resourcing of CP response services in Tier 2, 3 locations for 2019 and World Vision’s operational presence with capacity to respond or integrate with other sectors of programming such as Education and GBV Prevention & Response).

The project will target a total of 350,000 individuals (W: 90,000; G: 100,000 (Adolescent: 50,000); M: 60,000; B: 100,000 (Adolescent: 50,000)), with life-saving child protection assistance to 8,000 girls and boys through case management (incl FTR, CAAFAG) and community based PSS interventions (Girls: 4,000 (Adolescents: 3,000) Boys: 4,000 (Adolescents: 2,000)). Given World Vision South Sudan is also both a GBV and Education partner, specific emphasis on strengthening life-saving assistance meeting the unique and unmet needs of child survivors, specifically adolescent girls, and linking/referring girls and boys in need of child protection services to education opportunities.

The project will include the following key interventions in all locations, based on specific assessed need, disaggregated by sex and age: Comprehensive CP case management (Identification & documentation of children with protection concerns, case management capacity building, family tracing & reunification (FTR) of UASC and placement in alternative care within framework of comprehensive case management, referrals to specialized services); specific case management and provision of focused psychosocial support (PSS) for CAAFAG and other vulnerable children with protection concerns; Capacity building of CP staff, frontline workers, teachers, government/local authorities in CPIE; Strengthening of community based CP structures (CBCPCs); Provision of structured community based PSS through Child Friendly Spaces, peer support for adolescents and other relevant modalities; Community awareness raising on CPIE/children’s rights, incl engagement of adolescents and youth, positive parenting, messaging and campaigns.
 
The project reflects the feedback of beneficiary consultations and includes accountability mechanisms, and considers the unique needs and adapts its design based on gender and age considerations/vulnerabilities (Code 4M). The project approach seeks to place communities at the centre of interventions and contribute to localization through capacity building in all community-based initiatives (i.e. strengthening CBCPCs in monitoring, reporting, CBPSS, referral). The project design prioritizes a Do No Harm approach with an explicit intention to address protection issues experienced by girls and boys, recognizing that respect for children’s rights is an enabler of the South Sudan humanitarian response strategy.

WV will avoid overlap with other CP actors by continuing to prioritize CP prevention/response in existing areas only, which have already been locally coordinated to avoid overlap (i.e. WV & MCC in Renk, WV & CINA in Tambura) or where no other CP actor works in the payam & this has been agreed through state level coordination (i.e. WV will only work in Kodok, Fashoda, only Rajaf in Juba). WV aims to coordinate closely through the CPSC & with CP actors to ensure all avoidance of duplication and reach only those locations with no CP assistance other than that provided by WV.

project_name: Early Recovery for Vulnerable Households in Need in Kariba and Makoni Districts
project_objective: The project seeks to stabilize livelihoods and rebuild the foundation for resilience of the drought affected communities in Kariba and Makoni districts. The response will leverage on on-going humanitarian efforts with early recovery activities that include rehabilitation of productive assets through cash for work, start up grants targeting young people who would have benefited from vocational skills training to grow and recapitalize their small enterprises. AAZ will facilitate rapid scoping studies to identify and map youths skills requirements and gaps and link them with service providers and private organizations that are supporting new skills and providing attachments and certification programs. The intervention will support value chain strengthening initiatives that have been started under the Zimbabwe Resilience Program that are agro-based targeting especially livestock interventions. ActionAid leading a consortium of partners under the Zambezi Valley Alliance name supported communities and stakeholders with IT based early warning systems infrastructure that includes computers, servers, internet connectivity which will be harnessed to provide relevant commodity market situations and support organized farmers to aggregate both inputs and outputs thereby reducing marketing related costs. The same platform will be used to strengthen sub-national capacity especially for Makoni to extent the high frequency monitoring system which was implemented successfully in Kariba District. In Makoni the intervention will strengthen provision of WASH related infrastructure and consider labor saving technologies targeting community institutions and facilities and support software related health interventions. These interventions will be implemented in close collaboration with specific government line ministries at local level, Rural District Council and their related structures and with affected rural, urban and peri-urban communities.

project_name: Food Assistance for Vulnerable Populations (FAV) in Rural Damascus, Deir al Zour and Homs
project_objective:
The FAV project was designed to respond to urgent food security needs in three targeted governorates, Rural Damascus, Homs and Deir Al Zour. These areas have high levels of food insecurity due to the presence of conflict, limited humanitarian assistance, high levels of unemployment and poverty. 
The overall objective is to improve the food security of vulnerable groups. This will be addressed through two outputs; to improve the food security status of 2,000 assessed food insecure households through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance and support self-reliance of 750 affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives in the targeted areas. 
This is will accomplished through the provision of food vouchers to 2,000 vulnerable households, designed to reduce food insecurity in the target areas. Vouchers will enable beneficiaries to access a minimum level of nutritious and a variety of food items for all members of the household. In addition, 750 households will be provided with a small-scale food production kit which will enable a greater amount of food to be produced at the household level, improving food security for the vulnerable household.

project_name: Improving food security of conflict-affected households in Southern Syria
project_objective: This action aims at improving the food security of conflict-affected households in Da’ra governorate, Southern Syria. This will be achieved by providing in-kind or vouchers kitchen garden kits (one for each agricultural season) to 1,200 households who have access to a small piece of land or backyard garden for cultivating. Targeted households will also take part in theoretical and practical training on climate-smart agriculture, planting, harvest, composting. Ultimately, it is expected that the households who will benefit from this project will be able to improve their food security and nutritional status through a self-sufficient and diversified cultivation. 6,000 individuals are expected to benefit from the project.

project_name: Food for Resilience in Northwest Syria
project_objective: The 12-month Food for Resilience in Syria (FOR Syria) will deliver lifesaving food assistance to 14,135 vulnerable displaced households (70,675 individuals in Northwest Syria) in order to increase food consumption, expand nutrition diversity and improve HH resilience. We will target HHs who have been recently displaced (or recent returnees), defined as those displaced or returned within the last one month, as well as those IDPs that have been displaced for a longer period of time and are living in camps, informal settlements, renting or given space by host communities and vulnerable host community beneficiaries. For the recently displaced, emergency food assistance is a critical need while HHs navigate their new environments and assess their available resources. For HHs which are relatively more settled, access to a reliable source of food not only helps them meet their nutrition needs, it will also help stabilize the HH economy and empower them to better plan and manage their assets, diminishing dependency on negative coping mechanisms. The collective impact of these HH-level improvements will increase community resilience, mitigating the potential impact of further influxes of IDPs.

project_name: DRR integrated shelter improvement & maintenance, mid-term shelter construction and sustainable energy program for FDMNs and host community
project_objective:
This project has been designed as part of the shelter/NFI interventions of Christian Aid. Based on the multiple needs assessments conducted by shelter/NFI for both camp and host community shows the larger needs on transitional and mid-term sheltering in terms of Sphere minimum standards. These assessments also exposed the priorities of monsoon preparedness & DRR as well as highlighted very specific priorities to take measures to reduce environmental impacts both for camp and host communities. 

This project, however, complying with all four sector objectives for shelter/NFI sector targeting 13,500 households directly in the camp and host community with 67,500 individuals or family members of these total targeted households. Therefore, this intervention has planned, firstly, to provide lifesaving emergency shelter/NFI support to the affected households by natural disasters or other shocks considering the mid-term shelter needs and distribution of stockpiled emergency shelter kits; This intervention, secondly, will also improve the living conditions contributing to reduced suffering, disaster risk reduction, and enhanced protection, dignity, and safety of the targeted families; thirdly, this intervention has considered both camp and host community based on their practical shelter needs to ensure inclusion or to improve social cohesion and enhance resilience for the community; and finally, planned to fit alternative sustainable solutions to reduce impact on the environment. 

The major focus of this intervention will provide mid-term shelter for 1,000 camp-based households. Also, will cover - 6,000 households with improved lighting solution targeting both camp and host community; and 6,000 households with individual kitchen support i.e. LPG cylinders, gas stoves and periodic refills for the targeted families as part of social cohesion creation and reduction of environmental impacts. Lastly, as part of monsoon and cyclone preparedness will distribute 5,000 in-kind contingency stockpiling of emergency shelter/NFI kit (as per sector standard) for the camp households at risks.

project_name: Inclusive Humanitarian Response to the Needs of Older Men and Women among Rohingya Refugees and Host Community
project_objective:
Humanitarian crises affect each person differently depending on their gender, age, disability and other personal characteristics. Older people and people with disabilities are often overlooked in humanitarian relief and response and they may find it harder than others to access the assistance and protection they need. 
As per survey of HelpAge, around 10% of the camp population are older people (categorized as 50+ old). Total population of Older People (OP) is around 90,000. HelpAge has been serving 20,000 older people in 6 camps that only cover 22% of the population. 78% of Older Population (OP) remains unserved or underserved. Older women and men, including those with disabilities, often experience serious challenges in accessing humanitarian services and information about the services.                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Due to their low self-esteem, physical challenges they are the regular victim of multiple exploitation in having humanitarian services. They are at highest risk of psychological harm. Older People and their inter-section of PwD are excluded in prevention of violence, exploitation and abuse.                                                                                                                       
Finally, a protection mainstreaming approach need to be effectively implemented throughout the response for the older people. Need to initiate specialized services for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV), PSEA should include age-appropriate interventions to allow access for older women and men.  
HelpAge is the global lead on the Age and Disability Capacity Programme (ADCAP) which has resulted in the Minimum Standards for Age and Disability Inclusion in Humanitarian Action.                                                                                         
Targeted community highly vulnerable for landslide, waterlogging, monsoon challenges. To cope with the situation, community need to build their community-based resilient through DRR initiatives.   
10 Age Friendly Spaces (AFS) comprising both static and mobile services will be developed. The AFS will be in closed proximity to health clinics, women’s centers, mosques and other community facilities. The AFS serve as a central point for information provision and referral mechanisms to services including registration, health, food, WASH, Shelter NFI and other essential humanitarian services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
Regarding PSEA, Helpage will facilitate community protection groups, institutional arrangement and will closely work with other actors in camp and Cox’s Bazar.
In addition, there will be direct provision Protection Case Management and recreational and social activities. Each Age Friendly Spaces will have adequate staff alongwith community volunteers roaming between all cluster (block/sub-block).                                                                                                                               
Field teams and community Protection Groups and Volunteers will regularly gather, analyze and share information on protection concerns of older people for action by HelpAge and partner management. In the case of older person specific Protection concerns, case management processes will be in place, particularly around issues related to PSEA, Violence, Abuse and Neglect (VAN) of older people, an issue which HelpAge has global expertise on and will deploy a GBV/VAN Technical Adviser.

project_name: Inclusive Humanitarian Response to the needs of Older Men and Women among FDMN and Host Community
project_objective:
Humanitarian crises affect each person differently depending on their gender, age, disability and other personal characteristics. Older people and people with disabilities are often overlooked in humanitarian relief and response and they may find it harder than others to access age appropriate health services. 
There are clear gaps in treatment of Non-Communicable Diseases and palliative care across the camps, older people and those with disabilities are struggling to get full access to health services. 
Based on HelpAge study (covered 6 camps only) September 2018, 46% of all older people self-reported to have serious psychological distress and access to mental health services and psychosocial support at Primary Health Care (PHC) level as well as community-based prevention, screening and early referral will be considered a priority to improve the mental well-being of the most vulnerable segment of population such as older people and those with disabilities. the study also reviled that 45% of all older people require to take medicine for long term condition and struggle to get medicine and follow up by medical staff in particular those  with NCD,s and have multi-morbidity. For the proper geriatric care, older people need regular home-based care, outreach services, accompaniment support, proper counseling of caregiver, organizing health camp, need to support them for emergency health service like surgery or hospital treatment.
HelpAge and its partners RIC and Youth Power in Social Action (YPSA) currently run 10 Age Friendly Spaces (AFS) in Ukhiya Rohingya camp and host community. The AFSs are static centers where older people can access basic Health screening and referral, Psychosocial Support, Physiotherapy, medicines etc.  Older people has physical challenges specially the intersection of PwD. They have limited mobility. They are facing mountainous challenges in accessing health services from static center. To ensure their services, 50% health staff will work as a mobile medical team to provide outreach and homebased services. 
Age Friendly Spaces, outreach teams and home-based care will provide integrated care for older people as well as promoting inclusion and protection of older people at all levels. Activities include: 
•	Providing preventative, curative and health promotion services for older people and those with disabilities through direct service provision and/or referrals both at the Age Friendly Spaces and through the Health Outreach Teams 
•	Home based care with a specific focus on older people and people with disabilities who are shelter-bound
•	Partnership and technical capacity building with other service providers and ensuring a strong referral pathway and monitoring care plans with other service providers
•	Older people’s participation and community engagement in designing interventions, monitoring and evaluation.
•	Capacity building of local staff and agencies to support older people and those with disabilities
•	Organizing Health camp and awareness campaign 
•	Support older people for emergency health services from hospital.

project_name: Comprehensive technical support for, and direct delivery of, community engagement and accountability services
project_objective:
The project will help to increase the quality and quantity of community engagement and accountability outcomes within the Rohingya response in Bangladesh, both by providing specialist, technical support to all agencies and sectors; and by delivering direct community engagement and accountability activities with refugees and host communities.

The project comprises the continuation and expansion of the existing Common Service for Community Engagement and Accountability; community engagement activities focused on GBV and other protection-related issues; and a new co-created, cross-community initiative focused on building social cohesion and peaceful coexistence.

Together, these activities will seek to reach the entire affected population, ensuring comprehensive accessibility to life-saving information and knowledge; providing actionable, two-way and culturally appropriate multi-sectoral communication resources; and strengthening participation of, and accountability to affected populations.

project_name: Improve livelihood and Food Security of Newly IDPs and Food Insecure Host Communities in AlSalam locality in North Darfur State
project_objective: North Darfur is one of the most hosting returnees and IDPS population in spite of   lacks economic access to food due to limited livelihoods and income sources, limited availability of household food stocks, suffers from reduced dietary diversity and high rates of malnutrition. As Sudan continues to face economic challenges, the food insecurity of IDPs, residents, refugees and returnees is expected to worsen. The intervention project is designed to cover the immediate food insecurity and livelihoods diversification skills, lack of knowledge of improved agriculture practice and wide spread of livestock diseases and management of natural resources.  This intervention will targeted 800 HHs (newly displaced persons and extremely vulnerable, returnees and host) in Dar Alsalam locality mainly focusing with administrative unit: Sag Al Naam,Gadad Wagif , Gamiza and   Hashaba in North Darfur State. The project implementation will cover improvement of food production and productivity of 800 HHS in term of  provision of  agricultural inputs (seeds (standard seeds package – core pipeline; assets and capacity building training through information sessions on sustainable agricultural practices, 200 vulnerable households will received restocking assistance of 600 ruminants(3 each), 100 HHs will be train in food processing and agribusiness skills and provide them with tools and assets to help them diversify their incomes, vaccination of 20,000 livestock, 100 female will be train in efficient stoves , . BPWO will work with those vulnerable women to maximize the profit they make from their goods.  In the way, BPWO will train them on Agro-processing (fuel-efficient stove, production tool kits. The implementation of the activities will help IDPs and host communities improve food security and ability to restore their food and livelihoods security to meet their immediate food needs with diverse foods through positive and resilient coping mechanisms. All activities under this intervention requested by communities when consulted by BPWO in the assessment stage. BPWO will guarantee equal access for women, girls, boys and men, to benefit from the project and will ensure beneficiaries selection will   be based on assessment targeting the highest in need populations with prioritization single female households, BPWO will utilize its internal reporting system, to monitor the project implementation, ensure progress reports, lessons learnt and best practices will be shared on a regular basis with FSL sector lead and other sector partners on the FSL sector meetings at state and federal levels. BPWO M&E Formats will be used to assess the outputs indicator on monthly basis through project/program staff and community volunteers as appropriate along with the results monitoring. The project team will focus on routine activity monitoring to ensure smooth and quality implementation of the activities, throughout the project cycle and recommendations will be implemented in project adjustment. The information obtained will be compiled by the project coordinators at field office to feed into the monthly report to BPWO HQ in Khartoum program staff will conduct   regular field visits. The results obtained through monitoring will be presented and discussed with stakeholders in the field, which includes beneficiaries, other partner agencies and in line ministries in a transparent manner. Reports will be submitted to FSL Sector and Ministry of Agriculture

project_name: Enhanced livelihoods for refugees in El Salaam and Kosti localities, White Nile State
project_objective:
The project’s overall objective will be to improve livelihood capacities and assets of 450 refugees in El redis 2 and Jory camps in El Salaam locality; and out-of camp (in settlement, grouped/scattered) refugees in Kosti locality, White Nile State. Project duration is one year.
The project objective will be achieved through provision of vocational trainings, provision of business start-up kits (in kind), and conducting of trainings, linkages and networking activities to such entities as financial institutions, cooperatives and Saving and Internal Lending Committees (SILC).
Due to women disproportionately bearing the brunt of the effects of limited available livelihood options, the project will target female-headed households, and PLW. Other selection criteria of beneficiaries will include PWD and households with members who are elderly and sickly. Participation of the target refugees will be through community meetings and set-up complaints and feedback mechanisms. The project's duration is 12 months.

project_name: Provision of access to improved essential WASH services for the conflict affected populations of South Kordofan and North Darfur
project_objective:
GOAL provides integrated WASH services and activities as part of its comprehensive health, nutrition, WASH and FSL programming. Specifically in South Kordofan, GOAL will work to provide clean water in targeted health facilities and the communities they serve, improve sanitation and reduce open defecation in catchment areas, and work through community-based approaches to promote improved hygiene practices that contribute to reduction of disease and malnutrition. WASH programming is planned for under-served and conflict-affected areas of Dilling, Delami, Rashad, and Talodi localities. GOAL conducts ongoing and close coordination of all activities through WASH and other clusters in Kadugli and Khartoum, and with partners in the field.  In North Darfur, GOAL proposes to deliver integrated WASH services targeting the most vulnerable populations affected by the conflict in Kutum and Al Waha localities, North Darfur, who are not receiving other comparable assistance, with an emphasis placed on the needs of Internally Displaced pople (IDPs), women and children. The proposed programing will support 74,166 direct beneficiaries (168,671 indirect beneficiaries) comprising of IDPs, rural underserved communities, nomadic pastoralists and host communities experiencing protracted crisis. 
In Kassab and Fata borno IDP camps, building on its success in transitioning the water systems to communities, GOAL will continue to provide technical support to the water committees to ensure access to improved safe drinking water to 30,226 IDPs. GOAL’s continued support to the water committee will ensure that the water committees in the two IDP camps will not fail from delivering sustained access to safe drinking water. A lot has been accomplished in 2017 and with focused technical support (in 2018) on operation and maintenance, linkage with local technicians and supply chain and strengthen cost recovery scheme - the water supply systems managed by the IDP’s water committees will have strong success rate. As part of promoting learnings and scaling up similar intervention elsewhere, GOAL Plans to produce one thorough case study on the two-community managed water supply systems from the two IDP camps and share with the sector/cluster and partners. 
In line with the humanitarian-Peace-development nexus, GOAL will construct a solar pumping water supply system (mini water yard) for communities in Salmai village (West of Kassab IDP camp) benefiting 3,500 peoples. Salmai village hosts Kassab IDP camp. Communities in Salmai village are currently depending on 2 open/unprotected hand dug wells. This intervention will solidify the collaboration between the 25,510 IDP and the host communities. This could even be the best entry point to facilitate further integration between the two communities and open new opportunities for the IDPs to access other natural resources such as farming land, pasture land etc. 
As part of integrated WASH response, GOAL will undertake ground water monitoring, water quality testing and water committees training in all targeted areas in Kutum. 
In 2018, building on its previous successful pilot project, GOAL proposes to partner with local NGO (FPDO) to implement Community Led Total Sanitation programming in 10 communities in the conflict affected rural areas surrounding GOAL supported health facilities to address the high levels of open defecation in this area, reaching 6000 individuals. In addition, GOAL will construct a sanitation facility/latrine in Abdushikur health facility creating access to latrine and handwashing facilities for a total catchment population of 6,304 people. GOAL also plans to construct 3 garbage disposal areas and equip the locality environmental health department with basic tools to improve solid waste management benefiting a total catchment population of 22,517.

project_name: 2019 IAS Resilient Life Saving Provision for Sudan
project_objective:
The main objective is providing access to life-saving and resilient WASH-IWRM, Education and Protection services and advocacy including gender and age concerns, protection guarantees, and environmental enhancement for 61,488 (WASH), 3,000 (Protection), and 3,215 (Education) beneficiaries who are traumatized IDPS, refugees, returnees, host communities, those affected by unsafe water borne disease threats, conflict and/or natural recurring disasters in  South Kordofan,Seirba West  Darfur,  Red Sea states. There will be a special emphasis in targeting vulnerable populations such as women, children, and the elderly. The inclusion of large percentages of women in project initiation, design, planning, execution (including monitoring and evaluation), and close-out activities, is a key objective that will not only save more lives, but improve the quality of services that alleviate suffering for the present situation, add valuable input, help mitigate negative impacts of future life threatening occurrences, and affect truly inclusive decision-making beyond the water maintenance committees. Again, gender, protection and environment will be major priorities.This will set the stage for newly emerging resilient, sustainable IWRM approach to overall water usage and conservation and all that this most basic natural resource impacts.
In order to reach this objective IAS will utilize an Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) approach. IAS has developed a practical field manual on IWRM that serves as guide in the implementation of its WASH programs. Practical examples include: Following hydro geological studies and community consultation, the most sustainable method for water provision will be selected. Drilling of new boreholes equipped with hand pumps are good options in most of the locales. In areas with high demand and adequate water supply solar powered mini water yards will be introduced.  In the areas with rare to limited availability of ground water the best option will be solutions related to the rainfall capture schemes. Every water point implementation or rehabilitation will include beneficiary sanitation and hygiene promotion and training, including hardware mechanic training which will include women and girls,  for recruited water maintenance committees, where we will communicate  that the best prevention to disaster is maintaining resilient, accessible and safe water points. 
Closeout activities will include helping beneficiary water maintenance committees determine the financial cost for actual spare parts so that they can target necessary budgets for ensuring continuous water availability when breakdowns occur. 
IAS interventions in education sector will be  in Seirba- West Darfur ,Rashad - South Kordofan and Haya in the red sea targeting 3215 boy and girls , as more areas became accessible. IAS interventions in the targeted localities aims to improve quality of education environment through activities prioritized in the HRP such as the provision of teaching, learning and recreational materials targeting 3215 in the 3 localities.capacity-building for teachers and PTAs members targeting 470 individuals  in Seirba and Rashad to support community engagement and interaction with schools through training on school management , psychosocial support and disaster risk reduction in order to enhance their skills. TOT training will also be conducted for 80 teacher in Seirba and Rashad . More over IAS will contributes in improving of the healthy environment in the schools through the conduction of awareness campaigns in hygiene promotion, gender sensitive and child protection for 3000 in the 3 targeted localities. 
 Protection is ensured through hygiene awareness sessions to targeted communities and students at schools including children and people with disabilities. IAS will use multi-sector approaches to increase the effectiveness of programming and meet multiple needs of the targeted affected populations in the targeted localities

project_name: Provision of Quality Education for Host Communities and IDP Children in Three Localities (Rokero, Golo and Nertiti) in Central Darfur
project_objective:
Increase access to inclusive and protective lifesaving education (formal and non-formal) for the most vulnerable (7000 children, 4000 in Rokoro, 2000 in Golo, and 1000 in Nertiti) children (pre-school and primary school age children and adolescents) affected by new emergencies and ensure continuity of relevant quality education during sudden onset and aftermath of emergencies.

CRS will conduct the following activities:
1-	Construction/rehabilitation 30 classrooms in nine schools (18 in Rokoro, 6 in Golo, and 6 in Nertiti)
3-	 Construction of 10 gender-sensitive latrines for IDP children - 3 in Rokoro, 3 in Golo, and 4 in Nertiti
4-	Conduct community Mobilizations sessions on topics around girl’s education and education in emergency initiatives. 2 sessions of sensitization meetings will be conducted at each school in 9 IDP communities targeting 500 community representatives (250 male and 250 female). At least 50% from IDP communities. DRDO staff will lead the sensitization sessions with support of project staff and in coordination with MoE .
5-	Provision of a 5-day training for 45 teachers from among the 9 schools (in 3 groups) for 3-day basic teacher training and the 2-day PSS training. MoE master trainers based in Central Darfur will conduct the trainings based on approved Curriculum that includes Basic and advanced teaching methodology and how to conduct PSS.
6-	Description Establish 10 classes of Non-Formal Education (Accelerated Learning Program) 4 ALP class in Rokero, 3 in Nertiti and 3 in Golo benefiting 500 (200 in Rokero, 150 in Nertiti and 150 in Golo) school age children. 
7-	CRS will provide 10 ALP classes for out-of-school IDP children .
8-	Training of 180 PTA members (20 from each of the 9 schools) .
9-	 9 water  tanks for storage, the project will provide one water tank to each school (nine tanks in total) to support sanitation infrastructure of latrines and handwashing stations.
10-	Provision of 20 blackboards for constructed and rehabilitated classrooms in targeted schools (4 in Rokero and 3 in Nertiti and 2 in Golo). 
11-	Provision 400 seating sets to address the needs for seating for new IDP children . 
12-	Psycho-social Supplies - Football, netball, drawing paper, textbooks

project_name: Integrated Livelihoods Recovery, Health, and Nutrition in Um Dukhun Locality, Central Darfur
project_objective: Vulnerable returnees and host communities of targeted villages of Um Dukhun locality have improved access to basic FSL, Health & Nutrition services and increased resilience

project_name: ""Food for All"" Food Security and Livelihoods Initiative in West Kordofan, South Kordofan and West Darfur States
project_objective:
