This intervention links to HRP Need Overview in Sudan 2017-2019 through outcome 2 and 3 by supporting displaced populations, returnees and host communities to meet their basic needs and/or access to essential basic services while increasing their self-reliance (O2), and focusing on vulnerable residents to improve their nutrition status and increased resilience (O3) in West Darfur, West Kordofan and South Kordofan States. This intervention also contributes to FSL sector outputs and activities to achieve the FSL sector strategic objectives by increase equal access to quality basic food, and income option (output 2.1., 2.2.), and improved capacity to prevent malnutrition through community based livelihood interventions. 
The four interrelated pillars of the proposed project: 
1) enhanced food production through access to farm input (seeds, tools, irrigation inputs) and extension services (Farmers Filed School approach) with capacity building in a timely manner 
2) increased the access to essential livelihood services mostly for females through income generating activities and safety net initiatives linking to capacity building and locality/state level existing market systems. Establish community village saving groups/associations, community gardening, skills/vocation training will be implemented that serves the most vulnerable in establishing save income resource. The intervention will ensure that the learnt skills, the established resources get to the local market, through taping on locally available market systems (local markets groups, committees and value chain systems). This linkage will be strengthened during the implementation. 
3) improved nutrition and food diversification for vulnerable households through home gardening, vegetable production, food processing and related skills development. This project component will be linked to the first pillar and will provide an improved variety and quality of seeds and seedlings for beneficiaries with a climate smart gardening techniques (e.g. minimum tillage, organic composting, organic pesticide) so the quality of vegetable production will improve, and it will remain cost effective. This project component also will teach beneficiaries on food processing and food conservation that will contribute to the positive coping mechanisms and reduce the huger gap period. As a result, it will also improve the nutrition and health status of the most vulnerable by providing quality healthy food, during lean season (May, July). During the implementation fuel efficient technologies will be applied to reduce the environment degradation and the negative ecological footprints. 
4) developed skills in forest/tree planting and management to increase regeneration of trees linking to environment protection. This component will strengthen resilience against climate related shocks and stresses for the entire community through tree planning and tree management in and outside of the community. 
The project aims at implementing in West Darfur, West Kordofan and South Kordofan States with integrating in other cluster interventions where possible and feasible.
Gender and environment mainstreaming, and cross-cutting linkage will be established and emphasized during the intervention through priority focus on female participants in the project activities, and while implementing agriculture interventions environment risk management will be considered.

project_name: WASH, Education and Child Protection assistance for IDPs, returnees and Host communities in selected localities in North Dafur and South Kordofan
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to intervene in three sectors, education, WASH and Child Protection in targeted localities in North Darfur (ND) state (Zamzam, Tawila, Kutum, Melit, Elfasher and Dar Elsalam).  The project will focus on strengthening the existing education systems and increase access to basic education, responding to the immediate and critical needs of children at school promoting to improve the school environment in three project targeted localities (Darasalam, Elfasher and Kutum). The project will provide different schools materials in addition to establishing, rehabilitating and constructing learning spaces, gender sensitive latrines and fencing (girls’ schools) in selected schools. The project will also provide trainings in core subjects for teachers, PTAs training and TOT training on main subjects in addition to schools awareness sessions in selected topics.

The project will respond to critical needs on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in the targeted localities (Zamzam, Tawila, Kutum, Melit and Dar Elsalam) in ND. The project will work to increase the access to improved WASH services, through rehabilitation and construction of WASH facilities, including potable water Sanitation facilities, gender sensitive communal latrines in addition to hygiene promotion activities in targeted locations, thereby reducing the prevalence of related water and vector-borne disease. The project will Supporting state and non-state actors’ in ensuring access and continuation to safe gender responsive formal and non-formal emergency education services in line with EIE standards.

The Child Protection intervention will focus on delivering gender responsive lifesaving services to boys and girls affected by protracted emergency in line with CPMS and in coordinated manner in (Zamzam, Tawila, Kutum, Melit and Dar Elsalam) in ND and (Dalling, Elrief Elshargi, Habilla, and Kadogli, Talodi) in South Kordofan. The focus will be on strengthening the community systems i.e. community based child protection networks (CBCPN), work with Social Welfare to strengthen their capacity on prevent and response to physical and sexual violence against boys and girls through training on case management systems to provide quality assistance), promote positive behavior change within households and communities on issues of monitoring and reporting of grave child rights violations, child labor, trafficking, migration, sexual exploitation and abuse; building children’s confidence and understanding to decide on the specific issues which affect their protection and wellbeing , awareness sessions on child rights/protection including (importance of children’s physical, mental, social health and well-being as PSS, risks domestic violence and GBV, Traditional Harmful Practices such as child marriage and female genital mutilation (FGM), and other risks); ensuring better safeguarding for children and youth will be a core pat of the project. The intervention also ensuring Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) with focus on communication with communities (CwC) by assessing the existing communication channels/systems, documenting the good practices and lessons learnt on CwC for scale ups.

project_name: Emergency response to protect livelihoods and foster food security and nutrition in Um Keddada, Mellit, Al Taweisha and Malha localities of North Darfur
project_objective:
This proposed project focus in three localities in North Darfur: Malha, Mellit and Um Keddada and is addressing MYHS objectives 1 and 2, specifically: 
-	Restore and sustain food and livelihood security of vulnerable populations in Malha, Mellit and Um Keddada
-	Supporting displaced populations and host communities in Malha, Mellit and Um Keddada in meeting their basic needs and foster access to essential services to improve livelihood and self-reliance.

project_name: Increased access to WASH services for IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Mellit locality of North Darfur
project_objective:
The principal objective of the project is to restore water access for 4,381 beneficiaries in Mellit locality in North Darfur.
4,381 individuals will benefit from restoring life-saving WASH services including the rehabilitation of hand dug wells, boreholes, MWYs and WYs coupled with hygiene and sanitation activities and efficient VWUC trainings.
Training project staff and LHP on CLTS facilitation, CLTS triggering and post triggering follow-up will be conducted in 4 villages in the targeted locality.

project_name: Promoting the sustainable reintegration of vulnerable returnees in Darfur through durable solutions
project_objective:
In 2019, IOM Sudan is planning to continue providing assistance to returnees in North, South and East Darfur to end displacement situations through the provision of sustainable longer-term support addressing protection, stability, social, livelihood and economic concerns.  Throughout 2018, the security situation in Darfur continued to improve, prompting families displaced within Sudan and refugees from Chad and the Central African Republic (CAR) to return to their areas of origin. IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)  teams, between 2016 and 2018, in coordination with the Return, Recovery and Reintegration (RRR) sector , verified the return of 121,546 individuals in North Darfur and the return of 25,389 individuals in South Darfur. In January 2018, a total of 13,365 returnees were registered in North Darfur across nine localities (Dar el Salam, El Fasher, Tina, Kalamando, Kornoi, Kutum, Malit, Tawilla and Um Baro localities), some returning from Chad, whilst the majority of returnees came from different displacement areas of Darfur, mostly within North Darfur (DTM June 2018 Report ). In South Darfur, during 2018, a total 20,266 permanent returnees were registered in four localities (Awehda, Bielel, Dalami and East Jabel Mara). In East Darfur, even though an increased movement of returnees has been witnessed, no DTM mission has taken place so far to verify and register new returnees.   

The returnee movement is currently happening due to an increase in security and stability in certain areas of Darfur. However, the majority of returnees return to areas and villages where access to basic services, water, health and education, is fairly limited and where socio-economic opportunities become more of a coping strategy rather than a source of income and development. Because of their forced displacement, individuals, households and communities had to abandon their lands and lost their livestock, assets, housing and source of income. Those who decided to remain in their villages are also facing constraints in accessing sustainable income generating activities and basic services, as well as coping with other factors such as climate change. 

IOM is planning to implement a set of activities that aim to strengthen the capacity of individuals, households and communities to better prevent, absorb and recover positively and effectively to future risks and impacts, contributing towards self-reliance, rapid recovery and reintegration. The aim is to continue supporting communities in achieving safer and more secure living conditions and better access to resources and opportunities. 

As part of IOM’s global mandate on mobility and migration, IOM has developed institutional capacity in transition and recovery programming that uses development-principled approaches to comprehensively address root causes driving forced and irregular. This project will reflect IOM’s development-principled programming in line with IOM’s Progressive Resolution of Displacement Situations Framework and the Humanitarian-Development Nexus to maximize opportunities that employ mobility strategies to foster the resilience of displaced persons, migrants and affected communities to support transition towards durable solutions and development. IOM Sudan’s Transition and Recovery Unit will deliver the project drawing on its extensive experience implementing locally-driven and contextualized longer-term development-principled activities that empower affected populations ownership over addressing the conditions of their displacement and restore their ability to make informed mobility decisions and reduce their vulnerability.

project_name: Building the resilience of vulnerable migrants and local communities while promoting their transition to early recovery and socio economic development through community-based agricultural, livestock and food processing business
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to strengthen the critical interface between humanitarian action and economic development while building the resilience and self-reliance of vulnerable communities by delivering sustainable, development focused agricultural and livestock interventions. The project also aims to mitigate the risk of food insecurity and malnutrition among vulnerable communities through food processing activities that promote the synergy between agricultural production and nutrition requirements. The interventions will target the most vulnerable small scale farmers, IDPs, returnees and local communities. The project will focus on seven localities where high rates of displacement or return have been reported and this will include: Umm Dukhun locality, Central Darfur, El Fasher locality, North Darfur, Rahad El Berdi and Um Dafog localities, South Darfur, Talodi locality, South Kordofan, Ghubaysh locality, West Kordofan State and Dourdeb locality, Red Sea State.  These localities have been considered as one of the most vulnerable areas to basic services and livelihood opportunities while there are little humanitarian supports. Local communities in these localities are vulnerable to livelihood opportunities as the results of growing constraints on access to sustainable income generating activities and loss of their assets and rights including access to farm land from last displacement. The majority of migrants and communities in the selected localities are suffering from food insecurity, chronic and severe malnutrition, indeed, the target localities were all classified in Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) phase 3 (Crisis), and the four of them (Doudeb, Umm Dukhun, Talodi, Ghubaysh localities ) were suffered from the high prevalence in IPC phase 3. In addition to this, 21, 247 people from El Fasher, 1,510 from Ghubaysh and 7,909 from Talodi were estimated to be in IPC phase 4 (Emergency). Hence, timely and adequate livelihood interventions to address food insecurity is required while strengthening resilience of community to protect their live and initiate a long term solution for economic growth. 
 A community based participatory approach will be used as an important strategy to encourage communities to take responsibility to participate in identified agricultural and livelihood interventions. The interventions will include: (1) community based agricultural training and practice by increasing knowledge and skills for better agricultural production, addressing climate adaptation technique: (2) provision of improved seeds and farming tools to restore agriculture productive capacity: (3) support sustainable livestock husbandry practice and veterinary services: (4) food processing activities based on local agricultural production. In addition, community-based agricultural training will be designed and implemented through cooperation with diaspora. A Sudanese agricultural expert from abroad will carry out the training to transfer his knowledge and skills in agriculture training to promote sustainable natural resource management.

project_name: Providing Life Saving Health Services and Capacity Building for Health Care Workers
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to respond to the life saving needs and improve the resilience of affected populations by providing essential life saving primary health care 
This project is in line with Health Sector Objectives: “Providing primary health services including referral services for vulnerable population affected by natural and manmade emergencies."" The MBHP includes outpatient treatment of communicable and non communicable diseases, maternal and child health services, facilitated referrals and health promotion activities to ensure aid reaches people affected by crises such as conflicts, outbreaks of disease and natural disasters. “Strengthening the capacities to prepare, detect and respond promptly to public health risks or events at federal, state and locality level.” Developing institutional capacities to address public health threats while strengthening preparedness through staff training on topics to improve prevention and response protocols, surveillance systems and close monitoring of disease trends. “Contribute to the reduction of maternal and child morbidity and mortality among vulnerable populations” by focusing on the needs of children under 5 years, including outpatient treatment, immunization services and comprehensive maternal care. 
The project is in line with Sudan's Multi Year Humanitarian Response Plan Outcome 1: “Populations affected by natural or man made disasters receive timely assistance during and in the aftermath of the shock.” Outcome 2: ""Displaced populations, refugees, returnees and host communities meet their basic needs and/or access essential basic services while increasing their self reliance.”

project_name: Building resilience of SSR and  host community in El Kharasana West Kordofan
project_objective:
The project is intended to provide livelihood and WASH support for South Sudan refugees and host community in El Kharasana to enhance their resilience and self-reliance through diversifying their livelihoods options, improving access to employment opportunities and income generating activities as well as improving their access to water and WASH facilities. The project targets 9,600 individuals (8,000 refugees and 1,600 host community). 
Normally livelihood assets availability in regards to the agricultural land and livestock is mostly owned by host community, but the South Sudan refugees are also playing essential role in accessing these livelihoods assets through renting of agricultural lands and/or working in these lands. Supporting these two components will enhance the host community livelihood assets that also lead to increasing the opportunity of getting employment for refugees and improving food security for both the refugees and the host community. 
Beside livelihood interventions the project will deliver a comprehensive package of WASH services (construction and rehabilitation of water facilities, training packages for the targeted population, and distribution of hygiene kits).
Through these package of interventions, the project will ensure improve WASH services, improved livelihood conditions and self-reliance.

project_name: Food security and livelihood assistance for IDPs, Refugees and vulnerable host communities in Rashad, El-leiri and Talodi in SK state
project_objective: This project addresses urgent needs with regard to food security and livelihoods of newly accessible locations in South Kordofan State, in El-leiri, Rashad and Talodi localities. The selected localities are in urgent need of emergency food security interventions (agricultural & livestock inputs and services), income generating activities and natural resource management. This will be followed by selection of 7050 HH (42,300 people,6,345 men, 15,228 women, 8,418 boys and 12,309 girls) of the most vulnerable households among new and protracted IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable and destitute host communities as direct beneficiaries. Selection criteria such as number of children under 5, women/children headed households, food insecured households with more than 6 members, households with malnourished children, disabled, elderly men and women, landless (for IGAS), chronically poor and minority groups will be part of the selection criteria. Beneficiary (300 HHs) selection for goats restocking will focus on female-headed HHs, HHs with malnourished children, vulnerable HHs with children under the age of 5 and elders; tools distribution (for 6,300 HHs) will focus on vulnerable farmer IDPs and returnees who have lost their production assets due to conflict and displacement; stabilized soil block machines provision and training (150 HHs) will focus on returnees, vulnerable host communities and IDPs men and youth from the targeted communities including persons with disabilities; fuel efficient stoves training will target mainly vulnerable women, girls and youth from IDPs, returnees and host communities including persons with disabilities.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene response to IDPs and host communities in Central Darfur and  South Darfur states.
project_objective: The Darfur crisis is not only protracted but also a forgotten one. Funding has decreased over the years while critical humanitarian and recovery needs remain. External shocks (conflict, natural disasters) as well as poverty, eroded livelihoods and lack of access to essential resources and basic services means that basic living conditions of disaster affected communities is worsening. While longer term development approaches are needed to tackle this situation, excessive mortality linked to such a situation is also to be addressed through live-saving and targeted interventions focusing on most at risk population: The 2019 HNO highlighted that many IDPs, returnees and host communities remain extremely vulnerable to the impact of both natural disasters and conflict-related displacement. Darfur remains the most affected area in the country, and the two states, Central and South Darfur, have large numbers of people in need of humanitarian assistance, 443,311 and 710,775 respectively (HNO2019).

project_name: Saving Access to Education Services for the most Affected and Vulnerable new IDPs Children in new accessible areas at 4 basic schools at Deribat Admin Unit, East Jebel Marra Locality (EJML), South Darfur State (Envelope 1).
project_objective: This project aiming at improve the access to quality protective education services for more vulnerable IDPs children in EJM at (3) basic schools that includes: One school at Jawa Admin Unit namely Soni Mixed School with total of 450 students (189 M, 261 F), the other 3 schools in Deribat Admin Unit namely Dara Mixed School with total of 1,229 students (621 M, 608 F), Elfajer Eljaded Mixed school with total of 413 (M263 F150) Abu hrira 432(m 239 F193)  The total beneficiaries is 2,524 children (1,312 M, 1,212 F). Through this project PBA intervenes directly to provide teaching, learning and recreational materials for 2524 children and provide seating (benches/ desk) for 2524 students, construction of 24 semi-permanent classrooms for 480 student (60 students/ classroom), rehabilitation of 4 existed classrooms for 432 students, conduct 4 training sessions for 120 teachers (50% M, 50% F), 60 participants/ training for 7 days based on SMoE guidelines) on core subjects and another one for 5 Days on EiE including Psycho- social support and child protection, Conduct One training for 60 Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs, 60% M, 40% F) on roles and responsibilities of the committee, school co-management, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and advocacy and networking methods techniques, construction of 6 gender sensitive latrines in schools (6 holes/ unit- 30 girls, 60 boys/ unit) 1080 boys and 540 girls, the total beneficiaries 1620 students, provision of 6 water points (water connection+ 2 tanks 1000 Liters) and 2 hands- washing units that benefiting 2092 students, conduct 6 campaigns on hygiene promotion at the schools targeting 2400 children (each campaign will targeting 400 child/ school through- out the academic year), establishing (3) child clubs focusing on life saving issues, PSS, fine arts, drama & games, peace building & protection, hygiene promotion and leadership skills targeting 60 child/ club totaling 180 children, conduct 6 enrollment campaigns at communities around the targeted schools to sensitize them on the importance of education especially for girls and encourage them to register their children at school age (each campaign will target 400 individuals). All the project activities will be conducted with technical support from line Ministries at State level.

project_name: Provision of  WASH services for the populations affected by conflict and displacement in South and East Darfur States
project_objective:
This project seeks to: 
o	improve access to clean water through sustaining the water infrastructure and supply to meet minimum SPHERE standards both in the target communities as well as in ARC-run primary health care centres (PHCCs) and nutrition centers, emphasizing transition from the fully subsidized operation and maintenance to partial cost-recovery and water user tariff collection approaches. 
o	Improve the hygiene and sanitation conditions for IDPs and host community members, whose coping mechanisms have been affected due to conflict and influx of large numbers of displaced persons. This will be done through promotion and support of construction of emergency latrines and improved household shared latrines with hand washing points. Where feasible the CLTS approach will be used.
o	Promotion of good health, nutrition and hygiene practices in targeted IDP and host communities through the timed targeted counselling approach (ttC), which is a methodology promoting key health, nutrition and hygiene behaviors and practices with the pregnant women and new mothers and their intimate partners and family members to ensure their health and well-being. In the WASH context, the focus will be on improving the chances of survival and normal development/growth of children during the first 1,000 days of life, as per the Baby WASH approach  and in accordance with the UN Every Woman, Every Child Strategy. At the same time, ARC teams will work with communities, volunteers and Community Relief and Development Committees (CRDCs) on reducing the incidence of communicable diseases through curbing the risks associated with environmental factors by ensuring cleanliness of water points, shared latrines and functionality and maintenance of the drainage canals and the solid waste management systems and disposal sites, as well as ensuring the water quality through testing and treatment 
o	Mainstream protection in all WASH activities by paying particular attention to protection needs of different users in the design and use of infrastructure and WASH services by gender, age and diversity to ensure effective access, safety, and dignity of beneficiaries. Through community discussions and analysis of protection needs all WASH activities will be designed to mitigate the protection risks of the beneficiaries.

project_name: Food security and Livelihoods Support for IDPs ,host communities and Returnees in East and South Darfur
project_objective:
ARC livelihood project aims to save the lives of disasters and conflicts affected population in neediest areas of South and East Darfur states which highlighted by the humanitarian work plan for 2018. The project will target a total of 10,000 people aggregated by 50% male (5000) and 50% females (5000) in two states of South (3000) beneficiaries and East Darfur (7000) beneficiaries ,  the  intervention will be through food production, income generating activities such as vegetable gardens and poultry, livestock vaccinations and capacity building of the both farmers and agro- pastorals which will contribute to reduction of acute food and livelihood insecurity for most vulnerable people affected by conflicts in East and South Darfur. The project will target 7 localities which includes Sharyia, Yassin, Adilla and Abukarinka in East Darfur and  Gereida, Elsalam and Beiliel in South Darfur.  
 The locations prioritized for this projects based on HNO severity ranking for the FSL sector. ARC Sudan strategy is committed to create a better future for Sudanese communities in where they live. Hence, in responding to the needs in South and East Darfur, our focus will remain on food security activities integrated with ARC other operation sectors include nutrition, health and WASH. The project fund will be used to support life-saving interventions within South and East Darfur communities through provisions of the required agricultural and livelihood skills needed for the survival of the IDPs and host communities in the targeted areas. 
ARC recently has conducted community consultations assessment in East and South Darfur States in order to highlight the communities’ priorities for Livelihood program which are mostly agricultural driven activities, such as peanut productions, millet and sorghum as most top needs for communities in Adilla, Abukarinka, Alsafia and Yassin. As a result of the assessment, ARC will become in a better place to respond to the demands addressed by the upcoming livelihood interventions for the year 2019. while implementing the livelihood project ARC will consider national and international  standard requirements for livelihood sector include sphere requirements , collective outcomes for Sudan  and livelihood sector priorities as well in addition the project will stick on humanitarian aid principles  ( DO NO HARM ) which will ensure the transparency of the service delivery in way that turn the dividers into linkages peacefully among the diverse communities of IDPs , Returnees and host communities .

project_name: Provision of Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition for Internally Displaced People and host community in South and East Darfur states.
project_objective:
The proposed 12-month project will support provision of quality and high impact lifesaving nutrition interventions to internally displaced people in South and East Darfur states. ARC will provide nutrition services integrated to the primary health care facilities supported by ARC in South and East Darfur states. The nutrition activities will be implemented in an integrated approach with health and WASH. The goal of this project is to contribute to the reduction in nutrition-related mortality and morbidity, and improve access to high-quality multi-sectoral life-saving nutrition interventions for children under five and pregnant and lactating women who are below the emergency threshold. The project will support 23 Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs, 23 Outpatient Therapeutic Programs and 3 Stabilization Centers (SC) including referrals to secondary health care and provision of essential drugs.
ARC will use the mother support group strategy to promote appropriate Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and Social Behavior Change and Communication (SBCC) among the target communities. ARC will also enhance the technical capacity of ministry of health staff through conducting training on CMAM package, IYCF and training on monitoring and reporting of the nutrition activities.

All activities will be implemented in close collaboration with local institutions/ line ministries and communities such Community Relief and Development Committees (CRDC) to ensure sustainability and active community participation.

project_name: Provision of intergrated primary health care services to internally displaced persons and host community in East and South Darfur State
project_objective:
ARC proposed activities are in line with the Outcome 2 in the Humanitarian response plan (HRP), i.e. Displaced populations, refugees, returnees and host communities meet their basic needs and/or access basic services while increasing their self-reliance. The integrated primary  health care interventions will be provided with key objective to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with disease among the children under five years, men, women, adolescent boys and girls, women of child bearing age, elderly men and women and people with disability.

ARC has been implementing comprehensive integrated primary health care life-saving interventions supporting 25 primary health care centers; 10 PHCCs in East Darfur and 15 PHCCs in South Darfur. Under this project, ARC will continue provision of basic primary health care services; Treatment and diagnosis of communicable diseases, reproductive health, support of referrals for both medical and obstetric emergencies to tertiary level, emergency preparedness and response, prevention activities through health promotion activities by community volunteers, routine immunization, provision of essential drugs, medical and non medical supplies, clinical management of rape to gender based violence survivors and provision of Psychosocial First Aid (PFA) services.  ARC will also strengthen community-based approaches to promote positive health seeking behaviors, recognition of illnesses, and care-seeking practices through trained community structures, community relief development committees and health, nutrition and WASH volunteers network.

The project will strengthen institutional capacity through on job training and mentoring to implement sustainable and affordable health interventions that meet the needs of men, women, boys, girls, and children <5 and will utilize the network of WASH, Health and nutrition volunteers to enhance the disease surveillance system including early detection, preparedness and response to emergencies. These activities are in line with the cluster objectives, which are to provide the basic minimum package of primary health care services, including maternal and child health, emergency referral services, training of human resources for health emergencies, and monitoring of health services

In coordination with line ministries, ARC will ensure the health facilities adhere to approved treatment protocols/guidelines, provision and availability of vaccine and vaccine supplies for routine immunization, support during the acceleration campaigns, national immunization days and celebration of global health international events. In addition to improve the quality of services and build the capacity of the health frontline staffs and line ministries, ARC will conduct refresher trainings and  joint monitoring visits with State ministry of health (SMoH) respectively.

Through a well-structured Health Information System (HIS), ARC will capture data and submit weekly epidemiology reports to the SMoH including key health indicators on a monthly basis. Data collected will be dis-aggregated by sex and age.

This project will target the IDPs and host communities in South and East Darfur State. Total population target will include 535, 770; 341,172 IDPs and 194,598 host community. 17% (91,081) will include children under five years and 21,431(4%) pregnant and lactating women including the elderly and people with disability.

project_name: Integrated  Health and Nutrition for vulnerable a affected population including children under five years and pregnant and lactating Womens  in South Darfur, Blue Nile ,South Kordofan and East Darfur States
project_objective:
This project aims to contribute to the reduction of malnutrition cases and preventing malnutrition depletion of vulnerable communities through responding to immediate Health and nutrition needs of the target population in South Darfur,East Darfur , Blue Nile and South Kordofan States. The main objective of the project is to contribute to improve health and Nutrition status of vulnerable conflict-affected populations including Children under five years Old boys and girls and pregnant and lactating women as well as general wellbeing in South Darfur, East Darfur, Blue Nile and South Kordofan States through integrating health and nutrition interventions. In nutrition, a Stabilization Center and several OTPs will be established, MUAC screening will be supported and the local capacities will be improved through training of male and female volunteers in CMAM establishment of mother support groups to promote IYCF, as well as the awareness of the target population will be increased through development and distribution of IEC/BCC materials particularly on IYCF to men and women. Health interventions include support to health and nutrition facilities through provision with facilities, drugs and equipment and strengthening of the available capacities and systems. The capacities of female and male Community Health Workers and Community Health Promoters will be built for both male and female to assist in increasing the communities’ awareness and enhance service provision. As well as surveillance, early warning and rapid response systems will be strengthened to serve both gender. 
World Vision Sudan strategy is to increase coverage and access to quality primary health care and nutrition services in the project area, while improving and consolidating the overall quality and ensuring continuity of those services that are already being provided at established health centers. World Vision Sudan places a strong emphasis on capacity building and training of national staff, and empowerment of communities in order to ensure sustainability of its actions. 
During project period of December January 2019 to December 2019,  World Vision Sudan plans to continue lifesaving Nutrition activities in the above stated areas as well as expand community based management of Health and malnutrition through prevention, integrated Community case management and improved access to quality treatment .
World Vision will work in collaboration with State Ministry of Health and Federal Ministry of Health at state and national level respectively.
In addition, World Vision Sudan is also working towards empowerment of families and communities through strengthening & capacity building of community health workers/networks in health promotion and prevention for both male and female
In all of its activities, World Vision Sudan works to promote adherence to the national standards and policy frameworks established by the Ministry of Health.

project_name: Education Support for Displaced Children in Blue Nile, South Darfur, East Darfur and South Khordofan
project_objective: Having identified the critical needs in Education that includes poor enrollment rate, high dropout rate, poor condition of school facilities, poor sanitation facilities and low quality teaching due to unqualified staffing, this project will provide resources to address partly the felt needs. The project will carry out enrolment campaigns just before each school calendar term dates to marshal parents and community leaders to enroll more children to schools. To ensure children cultivate interest in schools, lifeskills activities will be introduced I schools such as school games, playing materials, school clubs that will ensure children find interest in schools as well as improving the schooling environment. The schools infrastructure such as classrooms shall be constructed to improve the coverage that is generally low either through SIP or classroom construction targeting. Sanitation facilities will not be left behind where more gender friendly toilets will be constructed to ensure privacy for boys and girls.

project_name: Provision of vital communications services in North-East Nigeria
project_objective: The ETS will provide humanitarians across Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states with reliable communications services to enable an efficient and safer response, ultimately saving more lives. ETS services allow humanitarians to implement efficiently their activities and carry out their jobs safely in areas where services from local services providers are unstable or non-operational. In addition, the ETS will continue to build the capacity of local partners and will map the communication needs of the affected population in North-East Nigeria.

project_name: Child Protection in Emergencies
project_objective: OBJECTIVE: Improving the well-being and strengthening the resilience of extremely vulnerable displaced children, adolescent and their families affected by the humanitarian crisis in Borno State through psychosocial support, protection services, community based awareness raising activities and through strengthening the technical and project management capacity of local CP organizations with a special focus to reduce the prevalence of violence against children.

project_name: Provision of food assistance, nutrition and livelihood support to conflict affected families in NE-Nigeria
project_objective:
In line with the Food Security Sector Objective 1, the intervention will aim to support and provide emergency food assistance including condiments, fuel and energy related support to meet the needs of the most vulnerable conflict affected families.  
From the most vulnerable, 20.000 selected beneficiaries will be  provided 9 cash transfers  distributed through  money agents. Selection of beneficiaries is based on their Food consumption Scores, Coping Strategy Index and a score based on their social economic situation. The selected beneficiaries will receive an unrestricted cash transfer  amount based on the 70% MEB as set by the Borno Food security cluster. ZOA will promote diet diversification  through awareness and training among project beneficiaries to increase average dietary diversity. ZOA will work with  community animators to provide this training 

In line with the Food Security Sector Objective 2, the intervention will foster resilience of the communities by an improved agricultural production, strengthening of productive assets and supporting income generating activities 
ZOA plans to use the diet diversification and nutrition training to stimulate beneficiaries to consume healthy food and increase their income by growing rapidly maturing vegetable crops.  ZOA will provide training in small scale cultivation. Along with the training, the 5000 targeted beneficiaries will be provided with the tools, seeds and materials needed to set up their micro garden. Community mobilizers  guide the participants is setting up and maintaining their  gardens. Furthermore, female headed households find it especially difficult to earn an income.  ZOA wants to build  initiatives by selecting women with a proven entrepreneurial mindset and to train them further in business skills and administration and to provide a small cash grant to expand their business. This should lead to an increased income for these women, making them more resilient and less dependent on aid. 

Concerning  PSEA, Standard operating procedures are in place for submission and receipt of complaints, reporting, investigation and victim assistance. ZOA has a focal person in place for its office in Maiduguri and for offices in the field. ZOA staff members have received training on how to prevent and respond  to acts of sexual exploitation and abuse. ZOA is part of the PSEA network in Maiduguri. 

As a humanitarian emergency organisation, ZOA is commited to Accountabilty to Affected Populations (AAP) commitment in the way we are taking and giving account to the people in need we work for. ZOA is doing that by mainstreaming protection in community based interventions taking in account the Age , Gender, Diversity  (AGD) inter-sectorial guidelines. In ZOA projects,  beneficiary  participation, feedback and complaint mechanisms are integrated in all aspects of the  program  starting from the inception phase. Beneficiaries are represented in Community committees trough the whole project cycle which provides channels of communication with the beneficiaries and use them to disseminate information about procedures and processes that affect them, so that they are able to make informed decisions and choices. Examples of mainstreaming protection in our projects are safe spaces to distribute cash using the RedRose platform , the use of local vendors to distribute the cash. having a majority of female cardholders to collect the cash, market assessments and post distribution monitoring processes , compliant and feedback mechanism,  

All ZOA staff are involved in mainstreaming protection within projects of ZOA, however 0.6% of the budget will be reserved for a dedicated protection/GBV/PSEA officer combined with support visits from  a external consultant for further training on  GBV/PSEA/protection.

project_name: Nutrition Sensitive Livelihood Based Emergency Response Project in Central and West Darfur States.
project_objective: This project aims to improve the food security, nutrition and livelihood status of 96,980 individuals (19,630 HHs) of IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in West Jabal Marra (Nertiti), Central Jabal Marra (Golo) and North Jabal Marra (Rokero) Localities in Central Darfur State and Krenik and Habila localities in West Darfur State. According to needs assessment and pre-harvest assessment carried out by VSF-G and partners, post-harvest assessment conducted by the State Ministry of Agriculture and other relevant reports revealed, although there has been an improvement in the rainy season in 2017 from 2016, the targeted localities still experienced rainfall variability and dry spells, as a result, there was extremely poor harvest, affecting mostly vulnerable IDPs, returnees and destitute host communities who have suffered destruction of crops and livestock, loss of livelihood assets & income and market disruptions. High levels of displacement are also placing severe pressure on the host communities, who already face elevated levels of vulnerability and food insecurity. This situation was exacerbated by the volatility of market prices. Deterioration of natural resources, lack of basic infrastructure and services in the targeted localities have affected livestock with poor pastures and disease outbreaks as a result of high concentrations of livestock around limited pastures and water sources. The main objective of this project is to assist vulnerable conflict-affected populations in achieving their own food security and improving their livelihoods by increasing their production and income through integrated FSL and cash interventions. VSF-G will work together with Local Partner (Mubadiroon) to provide emergency agricultural inputs and services to 4,500 farming HHs including: improved seeds of staple cereal crops (22,500 Kg of sorghum and 22,500 Kg of millet), cash crops (45,000 Kg of groundnut) and vegetables (450 Kg of okra, 90 Kg of tomato and 225 Kg of watermelon), hand tools (4,500 rakes and 4,500 hoes) and extension training to 150 farming HHs. The project will also provide fresh meet to 300 HHs in addition to emergency animal health services including: provision of refresher training, veterinary drugs and replenishment of equipment to 30 active CAHWs, vaccination of 250,000 animals belonging to 10,000 HHs, voucher-based treatment of animals belonging to 3,525 HHs and extension services to beneficiaries. Animal health interventions through voucher-based treatment contribute to save livestock assets of poor HHs, selection of beneficiary HHs for this activity will be based on prior assessment. each selected HH will receive veterinary services which include treatment of internal and external parasites and other infectious diseases. This activity will be implemented through the engagement of community members, private pharmacies, CAHWs and the Government. This modality will focus targeting beneficiaries and was selected upon proven VSF-G experience. The project will include supporting vulnerable 225 female-headed HHs from the IDPs and returnees with goats restocking, to provide replacement herd for those who have lost their livestock assets and produce milk for HH consumption. To enhance the productivity of lactating goats concentrated animal feed will be provided for the first three months, additional 300 HHs from DPs and host communities will also be provided with animal feed to improve their milk production. Involvement of the communities in cash for work program (450HHs) to rehabilitate natural resources (rangelands) will help protecting rangelands from further degradation and provide cash injection for vulnerable HHs, while increasing their awareness towards environmental issues through orientation sessions. Extremely poor HHs (300 HHs) who cannot participate in CFW program will be targeted with unconditional cash transfer program to cover part of the HH food basket and improve their food security status.

project_name: Multi-Sectoral Emergency Response Plan for West and Central Darfur
project_objective:
The World Relief Sudan (WRS) integrated project is planned to be implemented in five localities of Central Darfur (Azum, Golo, Nertiti, Rokero, Umdukun) & four localities of West Darfur (Geneina, Kerenik, Kulbus, Sirba). The project mainly focuses on providing lifesaving health & nutrition, food security & access to sustainable WASH services to reduce the morbidity & mortality among, IDPs and conflict-affected people. 

WRS has been operational in Sudan, mainly in West Darfur, since 2004, responding to the severe food insecurity and humanitarian crisis. WRS is currently providing interventions in health and nutrition, FSL, peacebuilding and WASH activities in West Darfur. In 2015, WRS expanded its integrated humanitarian emergency response, recovery and development programs to Central Darfur State in the localities of Azum, Nertiti, Golo & Rokoro and is operating health, nutrition, WASH, & FSL in those areas. Recently the organization further expanded its operation to Umdukun to implement WASH activities through approach of “locality wide wash intervention.”

Food Security and Livelihoods activities are designed to enhance the nutrition & food security of households through increased access to food through agriculture or enhanced purchasing power. In the medium and long-term, they are designed to enhance the resilience of households to external shocks and jumpstart livelihoods activities and increase HH self-sufficiency.

To increase access to lifesaving primary health care services and reduce morbidity and mortality from treatable ailments, WRS plans to support 17 health facilities. Services include providing outpatient services, consultations & treatments, EPI with routine immunization against all national target diseases, cold chain support, & antenatal & post-natal care with SMoH to provide overall operation & management of the health facilities. 

To address high levels of malnutrition and increase community access to nutrition services, WRS plans to rehabilitate, equip & provide nutrition supplies to 35 nutrition centers (OTP/TSFP). Services include providing treatment to SAM & MAM cases, nutritional assessment, growth monitoring, community outreach with IYCF messages for mothers and other caretakers. 

RRR sector mainly focuses in high returnee areas employing integrated sectoral approach to address their basic needs related protection, food, health & water supply.  The project targets Rokero, Golo, & Sirba localities.  This sector mainly focuses on durable solutions that help conflict affected people resume their livelihoods in a sustainable manner. 

WASH objectives focus on three priority areas. The first priority area is enhancing community access to potable water sources through construction of new water sources, upgrading existing water systems & rehabilitating existing water points. The second focus area is the promotion of sanitation through a community-based approach. The third focus area is ensuring the sustainability of WASH infrastructure. 

All interventions will be done in partnership with line ministries, community-based committees, local authorities, community leaders & beneficiaries themselves. As described below, interventions are designed to meet immediate emergency needs of the beneficiaries mainly women, girls & children while employing approaches that increase community ownership & thus sustainability.

WR cash based component focuses on CFW program. This will be implemented in all our proposed localities mainly targeting returnees & vulnerable communities. The number of working days & months vary depending on the type of infrastructure work that we will be doing in the particular area. The CFW mainly done during the months of December to February where the local food price is relatively available & cheaper. Cash will be directly paid to the beneficiaries on monthly basis based on person days completed by the beneficiaries & agreed work norms. Market survey will be conducted to set wage rate.

project_name: Support to Food Security Sector Coordination and Information Management in the NE Nigeria
project_objective: The project aims to strengthen timely, coordinated and integrated food security response through collaborative approaches that enhance local capacities and coordinate with the Food Security Sector partners, stakeholders and other sectoral interventions. It targets at least 85 organizations - FSS partners, national institutions, donors, other stakeholders.

project_name: Projet d’aide d’urgence et soutien au relèvement précoce des populations et communautés hôtes affectées par l’insécurité au Cameroun 2017-2019
project_objective:
Le projet actuel est implémenté depuis avril 2017 et va se terminer en mars 2019. Une proposition a été faite à notre bailleur dans l'optique de démarrer un projet GAC III à partir d'Avril 2019.

Avec le support du MAECD, CARE s’adresse aux besoins humanitaires les plus urgents de près de 31 500 personnes dans la région de l’Extrême-Nord du Cameroun. Les principales activités du projets incluent : (1) la construction et la réhabilitation de 63 points d’eau ; (2) l’organisation de sessions de sensibilisation pour détecter la malnutrition au sein des communautés, bénéficiant à 31 500 personnes ; (3) du cash transfer afin de supporter les activités génératrices de revenu de 300 femmes chefs de ménage ; (4) la construction d’abris d’urgences pour 1200 personnes déplacées.
Les résultats attendus de ce projet incluent : (1) un accès amélioré à l’eau potable, aux infrastructures sanitaires et aux pratiques d’hygiène ; (2) le renforcement des capacités des relais communautaires et des populations vulnérables pour l’identification de la malnutrition et le référencement des cas vers les formations sanitaires pour leur prise en charge ; (3) une amélioration de la capacité des plus vulnérables afin de répondre à leurs besoins de base, en particulier ceux des femmes ; (4) une augmentation de l’accès à des conditions de logement décentes pour les personnes déplacées internes, en particulier les femmes chefs de foyer.
Ce projet permet de sauver des vies, de réduire les souffrances et de préserver la dignité des populations de l’Extrême-Nord du Cameroun.

project_name: Emergency Food Scurity and Livelihoods Assistance for vulnerable communities in Unity, Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective: The project will contribute to all three strategic objectives of the 2019 HRP  and  all three of the FSL cluster objectives through the support of CARE donors and FSL partners to support early recovery, improved livelihoods and resilience for vulnerable women, men, boys and girls by improving access to food consumption in the emergency /catastrophe phase, increasing agricultural production, protecting and building productive assets and restoring livelihoods including use of cash in target areas affected by conflict and natural disasters. It will also provide emergency regular life sustaining and life-saving food assistance, increase vulnerable household food production and strengthen households and community coping capacities by building productive assets and reduce reliance on general food distribution transfers to 100,000 (16,000HH) vulnerable men, women, boys and girls including IDPs/host communities/ returnees. CARE will promote positive coping mechanisms among the most vulnerable beneficiaries including returnees, IDPs and host communities. Targeted vulnerable beneficiaries identified based on IPC classification will be mobilised, assessed and identified based on a widely consulted agreed upon selection criteria for support through appropriate cash / food vouchers after-market assessments have been done to determine which modality is suitable. During community mobilisation, CARE will sensitize households on relevant and context specific messaging on proper nutrition, hygiene and protection, especially for lactating / pregnant women and for children. CARE will also provide season appropriate agricultural inputs i.e. seeds / tools / fishing kits after providing appropriate training, in consultation and collaboration with the targeted communities’ support cash for work activities that will lead to improvement of livelihoods at community level, as well as building longer term community resilience. Special attention will be given to female headed households in providing support for agricultural inputs, protecting and building productive assets and restoration of livelihoods.

project_name: WASH support to populations in Western- and Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Warrap Regions through improved water- and sanitation facilities and improved hygiene practices including waste management
project_objective:
The general context in South Sudan is summarized, based on the Real Time Review (RTR) for the South Sudan Joint Response 4 report 4th October 2018, as that the humanitarian crisis has continued to intensify and expand. As a result of the compounding effects of widespread conflict and violence and a deteriorating economy, 7 million people – more than one in two across the country – need sustained humanitarian assistance. For most of the counties in Western- and North Bahr El Ghazal and Warrap, according to FewsNet (http://fews.net/east-africa/south-sudan), the IPC level in October-December 2018 and projected January to March 2019 is 4, indicating emergency levels of food insecurity. A significant increase in the provision of humanitarian assistance, above planned levels, is needed to prevent more households from falling in to Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5). This is particularly the case in Payam Greater Baggari in Wau County in Western Bahr El Ghazal as the security situation prevented till now much needed assistance. The other proposed areas include Jur River County in Western Bahr El Ghazal, Akon North Payam in Gogrial West in Warrap and Aweil West and Aweil North in Northern Bahr el Ghazal.
The population figures for the proposed areas, as per National Bureau of statistics March 2015 for 2019 estimate, are: Wau County: 230,919 (111,176 Male and 119,743 female). for Jur River County 194,806 (101,017 Male and 93,790 Female), Gogrial West: 196,925 (76,480 Male and 80,445 Female), Aweil West: 244, 667 (117,967 Male and 126,700 female) and Aweil North:196,014 (94,502 Male and 101512 Female). Save the Children reported in the Gurtong newspaper on 18th October 2018 that more than six million people currently need urgent food assistance, including more than one million children. Near-famine conditions are predicted in four of South Sudan’s states, a rapid and worrying increase from 2017, in which famine was only declared in one state. Western Bahr El Ghazal is among the 4 States showing the highest levels of food insecurity. Anticipating improved security in Payam Greater Baggari, Dorcas proposes a WASH project to assist the suffering people in the area. Similarly WASH intervention are proposed for Jur River County, Akon North Payam, Aweil West- and Aweil North Counties. The objectives for WASH sector in the proposed areas are: provide access to safe and sufficient water, adequate sanitation facilities, waste disposal solutions and increase knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. Missing details in this proposal will be filled in during the full proposal stage.

project_name: Integrated Food Security and Livelihoods programme in South Sudan, 2019
project_objective: The proposed project will be implemented in Uror and Twic East counties of Jonglei state, Aweil East and Centre counties of Northern Bar el Ghazal, Mundri East  county of Western Equatoria and Juba in Central Equatoria. The needs across all four states have continued to escalate throughout 2018, with poor harvests and prolonged conflict resulting in depleted stocks. Uror is predicted to remain at Crisis levels (IPC 3) in January –March 2019, Twic East and Aweil East are predicted to reach IPC 4 levels in the same period and Aweil Centre is IPC 3 whereas  Mundri East and Juba are expected to reach IPC IPC 3 IPC 2 and IPC 3 respectively.  Continued armed conflict and insecurity has disrupted livelihoods activities, and severely limited market functionality. The resultant food insecurity has lead to communities turning to negative coping strategies including sharing and borrowing food and foraging for wild fruits and roots (Tearfund post-harvest SMART Survey 2017, Tearfund Rapid Assessment Aweil, 2018). The project will  Provide agricultural inputs and training to vulnerable households to increase household food production, Provide training on pest control management techniques to reduce crop losses, provide fishing inputs and training where appropriate to vulnerable households to improve food security; and provide direct distribution of food rations and Cash to the most vulnerable communities.

project_name: Child protection and psychosocial support services for conflict affected children & communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
War Child Holland has been implementing child protection, psychosocial support, case management and livelihood development projects in Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria, Upper Nile and Unity States targeting communities affected by conflict and violence including IDPs, host communities and people in PoC. Backed with its substantial experience in protection sector, War Child is proposing community base child protection, psychosocial support, case management and cash based programming in Jonglei (Canal), Uper Nile (Fashoda/Aburoch), Eastern Equatoria (Torit) and Unity (Koch) ) with the purpose of prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience as per the protection strategic objective (SO). The purpose of interventions is to contribute to strategic objective of protection cluster through interventions designed to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, abuses and neglect affecting children and promote resilience and recovery from the effects of conflict through psychosocial support and targeted cash based programming. The project envisages to reach a total of 18,200 boys, girls, men and women through interventions presented below. The organization is member of CPSC and relevant TWCs both at national and state levels. Hence, the interventions are aligned with cluster priorities and minimum standards and guidance. Summary of specific interventions planned in the proposed sites included but not limited to:   
•	Conduct protection risk assessment in collaboration with partners 
•	Identification and documentation of 550 children with protection concerns in Aburoch and Canal (Upper Nile), Koch (Unity State) and Torit (Eastern Equatoria).
•	 Support total of 550 Girls and Boys in vulnerable situations through case management and referrals to specialized services
•	Identification and placement of 40 released children in alternative or group care
•	Family tracing and reunification of 250 UASC
•	Identification and placement of 50 UASC children in alternative care
•	Provide unconditional cash support for 300 extremely vulnerable HHs caring for children using broader case management vulnerability criteria 
•	Train 12 CP staff on Child Protection case management 
•	Provide training and mentoring to 50 child protection volunteers and staff on child protection approaches 
•	Conduct capacity building  training for  20 child protection workers and staff on CPiE
•	Conduct capacity building training for 16 non-child protection workers (teachers) on CPiE
•	Provide capacity building  training for  40 government officers/social workers on CPiE in target 4 Counties 
•	Facilitate parenting skills session to 800 caregivers and community members based on existing tools in 4 Counties 
•	Provide structured community-based psychosocial support through 8 CFS for 9,916 boys and girls using both centre and mobile based approach
•	Train and support 8 community-based child protection committees to engage in child protection activities in 4 target Counties
•	Organize  awareness raising sessions and campaigns on prevention and response to child protection issues in 8 communities to reach 18,200 children and adults  
•	Provide life skills and resilience programming to 600 adolescent girls and boys in 4 target Counties 
•	Support adolescents to organize peer support activities to further reach 3,600 boys and girls
•	Mainstream Child Protection and psychosocial support in 16 schools through capacity building events 
•	Design and implement community based feedback/complaint mechanism 


The aforementioned key activities give an overview of What War Child intends to implement in collaboration with community and government structures and in coordination with other cluster members in the 4 Counties. War Child programming is informed by inter-agency guidelines and standards in addition to internally developed approaches and tools which will contribute for protection and psychosocial well being of vulnerable children affected by conflict and violence.

project_name: Child Protection Program for Aweil North
project_objective:
Help a Child proposes an intensive child protection project whose main purpose is prevent, mitigate and respond to the protection risks among the 7,000 vulnerable households in Aweil north through enhanced preparedness and resilience. Help a Child has been implementing a comprehensive child protection program in different locations in Aweil north under the South Sudan Joint Response (SSJR4) program since January 2018 and this proposed project is aimed at reaching out to other locations not currently targeted with child protection interventions from Help a Child and other partners on the ground. Help a Child will make use of its context-based experience, connections and structures in Aweil north to effectively start up the proposed interventions. 
Help a Child and Dorcas Aid International conducted a joint rapid needs assessment in the selected locations in Aweil North to understand the current priority needs which have informed the development of this project. Nevertheless, Help a Child understands the dynamic nature of humanitarian programming and periodic needs assessments will be conducted to ensure that the project is well adapted to the emerging needs of the program locations. Among the key activities planned for implementation under the project include; child protection awareness through campaigns, banners, radios, conducting support sessions and the provision of case management and referral to services for the victims of child abuse and gender based violence in Aweil North. Help a Child will also facilitate the formation and training of the community based child protection networks, (CBPN) who will be able to monitor and make appropriate follow-ups on all the child protection issues in the community. The trainings on child protection will also be extended to the relevant local government officers to ensure their appropriate support to the referral pathway and to enable them respond to child protection issues in the different communities that they are working. 
Household heads under the project will be targeted with appropriate parenting skills so that they are able to take their parental roles in ensuring the safety and welfare of their children. Girls and boys will be imparted with life skills aimed at building their self-esteem and confidence to become productive citizens. The project will also set up school based child protection help desks, which will be able to receive reports of any child abuse cases in schools and make appropriate follow up with the school administration and the parents teachers association. A complaints handling and community feedback mechanism will be developed in order to get community feedback on the community concerns coming from the program implementation. The project will work hand in hand with other cluster partners including the relevant local authorities in the commemoration and celebration of key child protection and gender days like the day of an African child, the 16 days of activism campaign against gender based violence and the campaign against child marriage. Participation in these campaigns will help in raising awareness, strengthening collaboration and consolidate the child protection messages to the targeted beneficiaries. The project will actively participate in the child protection sub cluster meetings, forums and all other relevant cluster technical working groups including psy-chosocial support and gender based violence technical working group.
Help a Child’s comprehensive monitoring and evaluation system will be used to track the performance of the project and to ensure effective reporting of the program outputs to different stakeholders. Data collection tools, which are well aligned to the child protection sub-cluster objectives and indicators, are already developed and are being used in the current project. These tools will be adapted to the specific needs of the proposed project.
