project_name: Food assistance for PWDs ( People with Disabilities) in Homs, Aleppo, and Hama.
project_objective:
Drawn from a countrywide household assessment, an estimated 6.5 million Syrians are food insecure and an additional 2.5 million people are at risk of food insecurity. From the assessed households, an estimated 40 percent of Syrians spend more than 65 percent of their expenditure on food, 57.2 percent of food insecure households reported to have outstanding debt and 65 percent of food insecure people are adopting crisis or emergency negative coping strategies. Eight years into the crisis, the main drivers to food insecurity are prolonged displacements, loss and lack of livelihoods and reduced production capacity which in turn resulted in limited financial access to food, high prices and inflation contributing to reduced purchasing power and continuous depletion of livelihoods assets of the most vulnerable populations. Almost 40 percent of the surveyed households reported to be an IDP or returnee of whom 74.5 percent reported to be displaced for more than 12 months. With an 83 - 89 percent people living below poverty lines , and with cumulative GDP loss of $226 billion between 2011 – 2016 out of which $16 billion in losses and damages attributable to agriculture sector  alone, the relationship between poverty and food security is becoming inseparable.  A monthly food ration with staple items costs at least 80 percent of an unskilled laborer’s monthly salary and 50-80 percent of a public service employee’s monthly salary thus demonstrating the existence of “working poor” in Syria. 

The humanitarian needs in Syria are expected to remain high in 2019 and multiple actions are needed to ensure that all four pillars of food security related to access, availability, utilization and stability of food are adequately addressed through lifesaving, life sustaining, appropriate resilience, and early recovery interventions. 

TdH-IT plans of delivering 40,000 Food parcels (based on IFRC standard) to HHs in need all over Syria through our Implementing Partner SARC, that has already identified that there is a gap in needs coverage especially in North and North east of Syria.

In addition, to a pilot project with SARC as a start up to conduct Food voucher distributions in Hama governorate (1,600 FVs in two locations, recurrence 5 months).
TdH-Italy has pre-assessment for Aleppo , Homs, and Hama since we had different kind of interventions with need assessment for PWDs, and we have a very strong referral system to our projects in the same areas such as the physiotherapy centers in Aleppo to support disabilities with PSS and medication.

project_name: Child Protection for vulnerable children in NE Syria
project_objective:
To address the needs of highly vulnerable children and communities, War Child Holland proposes to work in Raqqa and Deir Ez-zor governorates with three local partners to provide integrated Protection services to children and community members to December 2019. 

War Child and implementing partners will set up CFS in schools where possible, and where necessary, will establish non-formal centres to act as safe spaces for activities. Each of these locations will be assessed against the War Child CFS checklist to ensure they are fit-for-purpose, and lightly rehabilitated where required. They will then be equipped with minimum standard safety equipment, winterization materials, and stationery and recreational kits. Referral pathways will be mapped for all project locations and regularly updated throughout the lifecycle of the project. 

Structured age and gender-appropriate PSS activities (Ideal, Little Fellow, SRA) will be integrated into the lesson structure. For 14-18 year olds, War Child will run a Peace Deal at each centre. Newly tested in Lebanon, with strong evidence to support its impact in enhancing conflict awareness and peacebuilding, the refreshed methodology offers adolescents the opportunity to create and implement their own ‘peace action plan’ and each group will be offered a small grant of $250 to implement their plan. In addition, in two locations, a group of girls aged 12-18 will be invited to join the She Deal, to pilot the intervention in Syria and develop more evidence on interventions designed for adolescent girls, aligned with the GBV sub-working group. Using the safe identification and referral training, children with specific child protection concerns will be referred to dedicated case workers in each location. 

For caregivers and teachers, War Child will offer sessions in their Caregiver Support Intervention (CSI) to assist with addressing their own trauma and build resilience. To develop the capacity of the educational system to accommodate and properly support children affected by conflict, the action will include a coaching programme for educational professionals. In each of the implementation areas, a network of coaches will be trained and supported to conduct classroom observations and assist teachers with their professional development. 

At a community level, mobile teams of facilitators will be trained by a dedicated agency to deliver sessions to both children and adults on prevention and response to ERW. The teams will travel to provide regular activities related to mine risk throughout the identified areas. They will also be utilised to offer basic services to communities not covered by other protection actors (PFA, recreational sessions, awareness raising, protection referrals). Awareness raising campaigns on child rights and child protection issues will be conducted on a quarterly basis. 

For all field staff (including facilitators and teachers), before activities begin War Child will provide training on Safe Identification and Referral, Psychological First Aid, and Child Protection in Emergency Minimum Standards, as well as Child Safeguarding induction (which will be based on the updated WCH policy and disseminated to current and previous WCH partners). In addition, recognising the severe lack of specialized case management services in Raqqa and Deir Ez-zor governorates, War Child will work with its implementing partners to identify case workers, provide intensive case management training, fast track a team of case supervisors, and offer coaching sessions to the case supervisors.

project_name: Emergency and Sustainable WASH Interventions to IDPs and Vulnerable people in North West Syria.
project_objective:
World Vision will continue supporting A'zaz and Afrin districts in Aleppo governorate with emergency and sustainable interventions as follows:
1.	To support lifesaving WASH needs in a number of A’zaz camps ( Bab Al-Salama, Shamaren, Sijjo, Al-Haramen and Al-Rayan with some of informal settlements (Telal Alsham, Alzaytoon, and AlAiwaa), interventions will focus mainly on
•	support boreholes in those camps with operational and maintenance costs (diesel, spare parts ,maintenance, operators)
•	Covering the daily needs of water by providing water trucking according to Syrian cluster standers
•	Emergency repair and maintenance of WASH facilities 
•	Regular garbage removal activities within camps and informal settlements. 
•	Hygiene promotion sessions with regular distribution of hygiene consumable items.
2.	Support resilience in some communities in A’zaz and Afrin districts, by providing WASH-related services: 
•	Support water stations with rehabilitation component. 
•	Provide operational and maintenance costs for targeted water stations
•	Provide all technical support to water committees within these communities to enhance their capacity to operate the station properly and effectively.   
•	Support municipalities within these communities with solid waste management operational cost. 
•	Rehab and construction sewage and rainwater drainage systems within communities, 
•	Providing vehicles for jetting and suction of sewage pipes to enable municipalities to conduct repairing process. 
•	Hygiene promotion activities with communities in coordination with education sector and civil society organizations.

project_name: Agriculture and Livestock Support
project_objective:
Improved food security and livelihoods for conflict-affected HHs and farmers through provision of seeds, tools, livestock, animal fodder, and fertilizer

While the need for ongoing emergency food aid to vulnerable populations in Syria is clear, complementary food security and livelihoods activities that enhance early recovery are also needed to assist these families in building resiliency in the face of ongoing conflict. One essential element of the early recovery effort is a focus on enhancing HH food security in a manner that uses local resources, builds local capacity and avoids dependence on humanitarian aid. This program's goal of increased resiliency for vulnerable, conflict-affected HHs will be achieved through 1) provision of in-kind agricultural inputs for 2,000 HHs (12,000 individuals) in non-camp areas of Northern Syria; 2) livestock and fodder distribution to 1,000 HHs (6,000 individuals); 3) ongoing technical assistance and monitoring for all beneficiaries.

project_name: Child Protection, Youth Empowerment, and Gender Based Violence Intervention in Northwest Syria
project_objective: GC implements integrated protection services to prevent, mitigate, and respond to harm, exploitation, and abuse for the most vulnerable boys, girls, men and women in northern Syria in Idleb and Hama governorates. Under this program, we will manage 13 safe spaces and 16 mobile teams. Safe spaces, in the form of Community Centers (CCs), Child Friendly Spaces (CFS) and Women/Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) will be service centers used to provide consistent services to communities. Mobile teams will support the static facilities to provide services to those not able to access the safe spaces, raise awareness in the wider community, quickly respond to new movements and emergencies, and conduct assessments. Mobile teams will also be ready to respond and provide emergency response services to IDP displacements and any influx of IDPs.  The objective of the project is to enhance the prevention and mitigation of protection risks, and respond to protection needs through supporting the protective environment in Syria, by promoting international law, IHL, HRL and through quality principled assistance.

project_name: Road Graveling for Key Access Roads in Atmeh Camp
project_objective: The planned activities support CCCM strategic objective number one to improve physical conditions in IDP sites. Atma cluster considered one of the biggest IDPs sites clusters. Where more than 76,510 people living in the overall camps (20,012 girls 23,049 boys 17,726 women and 15,723 men) according to CCCM  ISIMM December 2018. New extensions have been established inside the cluster and the humanitarian access to the site is difficult due to the road nature. The project will gravel the opened roads to these extensions. Global communities is the focal point in Atma for the CCCM cluster. The project will be implemented through contractors and GC will ensure the quality of the implementation to meet the CCCM guidelines and international standards.

project_name: Prévention et réponse à la violence basée sur le genre dans la région de Diffa touchée par le conflit au Niger
project_objective: le projet vise à réduire  les risques  de Violences sexuelles et Basées sur le Genre y compris les exploitations et Abus sexuelles vers les persones déplacées (les femmes, les enfants, les adolescentes et les garçons) ,  et assurer la prestation de services multisectoriels de qualité et adaptés  (sexe, âge et statut….) aux survivant(e)s de VBG dans les départements de Bosso, Goudoumaria, Mainé soroa, Diffa et N’Nguigmi dans la région de Diffa affectée par la crise humanitaire

project_name: Livelihoods support for the most vulnerable in Donetsk Region, GCA
project_objective:
This project aims to increase self-sufficiency and subsistence farming capacity of the most vulnerable households in Donetsk region to cover their immediate basic needs by providing small size agricultural grants, training and advisory services.
Needs assessments have been conducted (see chapter needs).

500 small grants for agricultural purposes with related training and advisory activities will be provided over the course of the year to selected beneficiaries residing within 20 km zone of GCA.
Dorcas aims to reach following targets: 500 households assisted
(1250 of individuals), basic business planning and agricultural training provided to at least 500 beneficiaries in Maryinka district, Donetsk region, GCA.

project_name: Child protection support along the contact line and on NGCA of Luhansk region
project_objective: This initiative is a part of the project which is planned to be implemented by a consortium consisting of partner organisations Dorcas and SOS CV UA and possible participation of other implementing partners. Overall objective: To provide emergency assistance and ensure non-discriminatory access to quality essential services for the most vulnerable people affected by the humanitarian crisis in Luhansk and Donetsk regions of Ukraine (along the contact line and on NGCA). SOS CV UA works in the Luhansk region, focusing on child protection, with complementary provision of non-food items to the vulnerable families and wide range of PSS for children and adults. The main aim is to mitigate the impact of conflict on the vulnerable families with children living along the contact line and in Luhansk, NGCA and ensure that children are protected in family environment.

project_name: Reducing stress for children through sports and games
project_objective:
Terre des hommes with the support of partner organisation AICM have assessed potential of interventions for support of the children who are affected by the conflict through activities based on Tdh methodology Movement, Games and Sport (MGS).
The current project aims to relief the stress of children from NGCA, Donetsk and Luhansk, by providing psycho-social activities to over 5000 children. 
The first objective of the project is to support the rehabilitation of the sports facilities (sport halls, town stadiums) in order to provide a more appropriate environment for sportive activities with children.
The second objective is to train 40 sports teachers (or other caregivers who run the activities with the children) in the methodology 
The teachers targeted are using the sports facilities that we aim to renovate together with groups of children who attend schools that have no or insufficient sport facilities,
The third objective is to provide MGS activities to over 5000 children through the teachers trained. This project component includes support/coaching for the newly trained teachers as well as provisions of MGS kits (diverse sport equipment and toys for the implementation of the MGS methodology and sport activities) and, if appropriate, establishment of child-friendly rooms in the schools where the teachers develop their activity.
The MGS activities are designed to compensate lack of social interaction between children and develop social and collaborative skills. The activities are organised with mixed groups of boys and girls and have a cooperative approach. 
The activities encourage girls to participate in the sports activities which leads to empowerment, responding to strategic gender needs that can influence in the future the response to behaviors affected by gender inequality. An example of such activity is Girl Inclusive Football, where the teams are mixed and only the goals scored with the contribution of girls (ex: pass or shoot for goal) are scored.
The MGS methodology encourages to reflect on, express feelings and deal with emotions could be beneficial for boys in a rather patriarchal society, especially in a context where traditional gendered roles might be reinforced because of the conflict.
Overall, the friendliness of the learning spaces in schools will be increased by the implementation of the new methodology in the interactions with the children and the provision of educational materials (related to sportive activities and to MGS games).
Acces to NGCA will be ensured by the implementing partner AICM who is registered and has a track record of health projects in NGCA. AICM will facilitate contact with the relevant local actors (an initial contact was made and needs were identified by discussion with local stakeholders) and will assist in setting up the operations. Together with AICM and local stakeholders involved we will decide the steps to be taken for the implementation of the project. One staff member (at least) will be localised in NGCA. The renovation activities will be organised through local contractors. The ToT will be provided by the Tdh trainers in the NGCA. The Tdh trainers will request acces also with the support of AICM. The monitoring and coaching will be made by the NGCA staff with support from the Tdh team in GCA (Mariupol/Severodonetsk office).

project_name: JORDAN - Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion

The activities are designed to complement ongoing nutrition programs in the target refugee camps with an  aim to contribute to improved nutritional situation of children under 5 and pregnant and lactating mothers. These entail provision of quality services; Community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) for treatment of severe Acute Malnutrition ( SAM) through outpatient therapeutic program ( OTP)s, and  Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) treatment through  Therapeutic supplementary feeding program (TSFP) , Blanket supplementary feeding program (BSFP) and  Community management Mother At risk of malnutrition and Infants (C- MAMI)and Infant and young child feeding in Emergencies (IYCF-E) interventions through skilled counselling in the IYCF-E corners and messaging through various platforms in collaboration with relevant actors and in addition to  active participation  in the sector coordination forums whilst also taking the chairing role for the Infant and young child feeding (IYCF) technical working group forum. The program funding will be supported by UNICEF, UNHCR for CMAM (100%) and IYCF (90%).

project_name: Learning for Life: Community-centred Non-formal Learning for Children, Youth and Families
project_objective:
Across 2019, this project will address the educational needs of Rohingya Refugees in Camps 1E, 1W, 2E, 2W, 3, 4, 5 and 17. Current figures show that cross these camps, over 65,000 children aged 3-14 are out of education.  Furthermore, there is a substantial shortage of appropriate learning facilities across these camps with 781 learning facilities needing to be established.

Mukti Cox's Bazar will address these critical gaps in education in refugee camps by constructing safe and equipped learning centres with gender-sensitive WASH facilities and training teachers, community social workers and community advisors - allowing children with the opportunities to receive basic education and life skills training and youths to receive life skills and vocational training. Home-based training will be delivered for youths with restricted mobility (those with disabilities and caregiving obligations). This intervention will improve learning outcomes and enhance the life opportunities of a total of refugee children and youths in camps.

Furthermore, refugee parents and caregivers will receive basic literacy, numeracy and parenting training in learning centres and through home-based learning for groups with restricted mobility, enhancing their capacity to support their children’s education.

project_name: Protection et renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection des IDPs au Niger
project_objective: Le projet de monitoring de protection permettra de surveiller et analyser la situation et les tendances de protection, de mener des activités de prévention et réponse pour atténuer et adresser les risques et problèmes de protection contre les femmes et les enfants, et mener des activités de coexistence pacifique.

project_name: Lifesaving  service for through provision of integrated WASH Services, Nutrition, Food Security and Livelihoods, Protection and NFIs shelters for IDPs, Returnees ,nomadic pastoralist and Under Served  Host Communities
project_objective:
The project aims to support the IDPs, Returnees, and vulnerable host communities in North, South and East Darfur to improve food security and livelihood, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), Nutrition NFIs/ shelters and protection assistance. The project aims to assist 190,064 beneficiaries (78,880 in North Darfur, 75,220 in South Darfur and 35,964 in East Darfur). The target beneficiaries include internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the camps and rural areas with focus on the newly displaced people and their host community, returnees and nomadic pastoralist community. The project will be implemented  in close coordination with the sector leads and other actors from the INGOs and NNGOs to ensure collaborative and complementarity coverage of the needs and avoid overlap or duplication.
The project activities incorporate humanitarian response by a provision of assistance to save lives and alleviate suffering, and building the target communities’ resilience through livelihood restoration and building household productive assets and develop productive and managerial skills to enable the target beneficiaries to sustain the provided assistance and cope with future changes and reduce vulnerability.

project_name: LEBANON - Medical Teams International

Improve Shelter conditions that provide dignity, improved access and well-being for conflict affected populations through both advocacy and programming, ensuring improved protection and strengthening resilience.
project_objective:
In Iraq, local non-displaced populations, internally displaced people (IDPs) and returnees are considered to be people in need; each of which has their own specific profile and challenges. NRC’s Shelter programme will principally aim to support shelter-vulnerable populations, prioritising those unable to meet their basic needs due to limited access to adequate and stable means of income. Target populations in 2019 must be ‘shelter
vulnerable’, meaning living in a shelter which is inadequate in terms of providing safety, security of tenure, privacy, dignity, protection from the climate, sufficient indoor space and access to WASH facilities. Consideration of both socio-economic criteria and standardised protection criteria will determine target beneficiaries, with a particular focus given to marginalised groups such as female-headed households, suspected IS affiliated households, people with disabilities and families blocked from returns.

project_name: Improving access and quality education for conflict affected children in the central and the northern Mali
project_objective: Conflict affected boys and girls in the central and the northern Mali have access to and receive quality education that links in to the wider humanitarian response and that is empowering and reduces inequalities. Project targets 5,000 children that will have access to non-formal education and 26,000 children into formal schools. Project will support 500 teachers and 3,500 parents including members of school management committees.

project_name: Emergency Food Security Response for displacement affected population in the North West, South West, West and Littoral regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
Vulnerable IDPs and host communities, especially women and youth in the North West, South West, West and Littoral have access to food through direct provision of unconditional cash and agricultural support. The project aims to provide immediate food assistance to save lives and reduce suffering of households unable to access food that meets basic food and nutritional requirements. The project will be implemented in the North West, South West and Littoral regions targeting 4,200 individuals (40% male and 60% female) including IDPs (60%) and vulnerable host communities (40%) affected by the crisis these regions. NRC will pay attention to youth and women affected by displacement. Participation of all beneficiary groups will be key in ensuring ownership of the project. In order to reach people hidden in hard to reach areas, NRC will work with local partner NGOs that have better access to communities. 
To achieve the above objectives, NRC will strengthen the resilience and economic security of vulnerable households through the following activities:
To achieve our objectives, NRC will strengthen the resilience and economic security of vulnerable households through:

1. Provision of cash/voucher to most vulnerable people to meet food needs 
Despite security concerns in the indicated North West and South West regions, local markets in small and medium business centers are accessible by the IDPs. The cash approach will help ensure that households have unrestricted access to food and additional income that would protect their remaining assets and ensuring that the agricultural inputs are not sold and rather used as intended. This food assistance will also allow vulnerable individuals to build their resilience helping households, especially the youth to avoid adverse coping mechanisms. Cash approach will help ensure that households have unrestricted access to nutritious foods and additional income that would protect their remaining livelihoods assets as well as ensuring that the agricultural inputs, livestock or IGA start-up kits will not be sold and that they will be used as intended. This food assistance will also allow vulnerable individuals to build their resilience helping households not to further deplete their productive assets and avoid further use of negative coping strategies. 

2. Reestablishment of agricultural activities
NRC will negotiate with the local communities and where needed secure access to land for targeted IDPs and returnees. Once the access to land secured, NRC will provide small ruminants, seeds, inputs (agricultural tools, fertilizers, etc.) and training. This will improve agricultural production and provide better access to nutrient-rich food. NRC will also promote gardening, which provides households with a source of food or income during the lean season. 

3. Provision of improved stoves 
NRC will also distribute food handling kits that will allow target households to prepare food in a more effective and environment-friendly way. Improved stoves will save households money on firewood and help curb deforestation. For better community acceptance, those stoves will be made locally. They will have a more efficient use of charcoal, thus reducing the quantity needed and reduce the expenses of households for it. 

4.Provision of awareness raising on food hygiene, food diversity, food storage and food preparation  
All emergency activities will be also integrated by sessions to raise the awareness of the targeted populations on food hygiene and diversity, food preparation, and food storage. Through this training, beneficiaries are expected to acquire the knowledge and best practices they need to better use the food and improve the results on their nutritional status.

project_name: Adequate temporary shelter solutions for most vulnerable Gazan households who are displaced/evicted or at immediate risk of displacement/eviction
project_objective:
The project overall objective is to ensure protection for most vulnerable Gazan households who are either displaced/evicted or at immediate risk of displacement/eviction by providing adequate temporary shelter support (Shelter and NFIs Cluster Objective 1). Providing essential shelter support meets basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation (Strategic Objective 2) and strengthens their capacity to cope with the protracted crisis (Strategic Objective 3).
286 families (1.602 individuals) with the worst score of socioeconomic vulnerabilities were identified as being in critical need for temporary shelter support. Factors reflecting socioeconomic vulnerability include socio-demographic and socio-economic data, such as characteristics of the head of household (especially female/widow/elderly/PWD-headed), income and dependency ratio, poverty, debt and the use of other negative coping mechanisms, the status of household assets. 
To quickly restore temporary access to adequate shelter for the identified 286 most vulnerable households already evicted or displaced/in process of eviction/at risk of eviction or displacement, NRC will provide temporary shelter support. This includes cash for rent for a period of up to 6 months, essential household NFIs including water storage, re-integration kits, winterization and summarization NFIs (e.g. shelter kit, bedding kit).

project_name: Shelter and WASH intervention to conflict affected Households residing in Benghazi
project_objective: The main objective is to repair damaged houses and basic communal systems to facilitate safe return for returnees and minimun standards for IDPs. NRC will focus on vulnerable families living in substandard shelter conditions in urban and rural collective sites of Benghazi. Beneficiaries will be vulnerable families (mainly women head of households, returnees and IDPs) living in heavy damaged or unfinished buildings. Those families could own/rent or temporary occupying the dwelling they are living in. Housing, Land and Property component is integrated as part of the Shelter project ensuring due diligence and security of tenure.

project_name: Protección multisectorial para personas afectadas por la crisis humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
Las personas en movilidad enfrentan obstáculos para el acceso a mecanismos de protección, los cuales están asociados a la falta de información que les permita conocer los regímenes migratorios en el país de destino y servicios disponibles, de acceso a servicios legales en Venezuela, y desconocimiento sobre los factores de riesgo en las rutas de migración irregular. 

Por otro lado, las personas con necesidad de protección internacional que residen en Venezuela enfrentan retos al intentar acceder al estatus de refugiado en el país. La falta de información del procedimiento establecido para acceder a la determinación de la condición de refugiado o para optar por un retorno voluntario, los costos de los trámites de documentación, las políticas restrictivas y las limitaciones en el acceso al procedimiento para la determinación de la condición de refugiado dificultan la obtención de un documento de identidad válido e idóneo que posibilite el acceso a derechos y a diferentes programas de políticas públicas y de salud del Estado. 
 
En cuento a la protección de la infancia, los patrones existentes de movilidad dentro y fuera del país han afectado directamente la unidad familiar y, lo que es más importante, a los niños, niñas y adolescentes. El 84% de las comunidades reportaron la presencia de niños, niñas y adolescentes no acompañados o separados, mientras que en el 45% hay presencia de hogares encabezados por niños, niñas y adolescentes (diagnóstico realizado por ACNUR).

Además, el 84% de las comunidades identificaron la ocurrencia de trabajo infantil para contribuir al ingreso familiar. Como resultado, 61% de las comunidades identificaron la existencia de niños, niñas y adolescentes que realizan trabajos que pueden considerarse peligrosos, impidiendo su asistencia a la escuela o afectando a su desarrollo, y exponiéndoles a otras violaciones de derechos. 

Objetivo del proyecto:
NRC va a asistir individuos en tema información sobre el estatus de refugiado, inmigración y / o residencia; pero también asesoramiento y soporte por una asistencia legal. Dependiente de cada contexto y/o persona, estos servicios van a concernir temas como rutas de migración segura, regularización, documentación, ley de víctimas, vivienda tierra y propiedad, acceso a derechos, soluciones duraderas, determinación de condición de refugiados… Uno de los objetivos es proveer asesoramiento legal sobre las posibilidades de obtener protección internacional y el acceso a servicios básicos en el país de destino; y así evitar que se ponga en riesgo su integridad física y sus derechos básicos y fundamentales, que disminuyan los riesgos de ser víctimas de redes de trata de personas, de violencia sexual y de género, de apátrida y de reclutamiento por parte de actores ilegales.

Más específicamente en el centro comunitario de San Antonio, la atención individual se realizará mediante una mesa de información que funcionará diariamente en, así como el despliegue de equipos móviles. También se incluirán actividades lúdicas y pedagógicas con niños y niñas en el centro comunitario, y un espacio privado para madres lactantes y sus bebes. Asimismo, en el centro se realizarán sesiones informativas a grupos de personas sobre temas de asilo, migración segura, regularización, documentación, acceso a derechos, rutas de atención, prevención de la violencia sexual y de género y la protección de la infancia, promoción de higiene, entre otros, así como provisión de agua potable, asistencia humanitaria y alimentaria.

project_name: JORDAN - Nippon International Cooperation for Community Development
REGIONAL - United Nations Development Programme
Improve food availability & accessibility and livelihood opportunities among conflict affected population Project in Blue Nile & East Darfur States
project_objective: Following sharp increases during January 2018, cereal prices either remained stable at their high levels of last month or slightly declined in most markets between February and March 2018. Despite the availability of adequate market supplies from the above average harvest in most of the main production markets such as Al Gadarif, Ad Damazin, and Kosti, the deteriorating macro-economic situation and removal of subsidies from wheat and wheat flour has caused cereal prices to remain atypically high during the post-harvest period. Fuel shortages across most parts of Sudan have been worsened towards the end of March beginning of April 2018, coinciding with the continued high inflation and local currency depreciation following the macro-economic changes in Sudan during January and February 2018. This has led to high transportation cost, which resulted in high prices of food and non-food items across different parts of the country. Sorghum prices decreased slightly in the production markets of Ad-Damazin and Al Gadarif but remained stable at very high levels in the main consumption markets of Om Dorman, Port Sudan, Kassala, El Fasher, Madani, and Ad-Dain. Millet prices decreased slightly in Om Dorman and increased slightly in Port Sudan and Madani markets but remained unchanged in most other main production and consumption markets between February and March Livestock prices either remained stable at high levels or increased slightly in most markets, in line with the recent macro-economic changes coupled with increased demand for sheep and cattle for local consumption and export in advance of Ramadan. Om Dorman, Kassala, Sennar, and El Obeid markets recorded the highest price increases between February and March, with 15 to 30 percent. The current level of livestock prices remained on average over 60 percent above last year and more than doubled compared to the recent five-year average.  South Sudanese refugees continued to arrive in Sudan in March 2018 due to persistent conflict and severe acute food insecurity in South Sudan. More than 4,300 South Sudanese refugees arrived in March 2018, for a total of nearly 15,000 who have arrived in Sudan in 2018 so far. This is slightly below the four-year average of over 18,000 arriving during the same period between 2014 to 2017. East Darfur state reported the highest number of new arrivals during 2018 with the total number of 5,400 followed by South Darfur and West Kordofan states with total arrival of 3,722 and 3,227 new arrivals, respective. The total verified number of South Sudanese refugee population in Sudan currently stands at nearly 769,000. The rate of new arrivals is expected to remain high prior to the onset of the rains in June 2018.

project_name: Supporting livelihoods on both households and communities levels
project_objective: the project aims to Support livelihoods on both households and communities levels through creating income generating activities, supporting the restoring and rehabilitating of assets, and building capacities of youth and enabling them to start their own businesses. In addition to rehabilitating productive infrastructures and contributing to fixing the production cycle of the one-to-two strategic industry or crop through Value Chain methodology. project_name: Promotion of Sustainable Return and Reintegration of Refugees and IDPs in Umdukum, Kornoi and El Genina Localities
project_objective: This project responds to critical humanitarian and early recovery needs in the Um Dukuhn Locality in Central Darfur, Kornoi in North Darfur and El Genina Locality in West Darfur States. The overall objective of the project is to enhance the sustainable and socio-economic reintegration of returnees by creating conducive environment for their peaceful co-existence with other community members, strengthening community-based protection structures and enhancing opportunities for sustainable livelihoods. It will strengthen the self-reliance of returnees and host community members alike and facilitate durable solutions for displaced populations therefore ensuring sustained peace and stability in the target areas. The project will also promote environmentally sustainable natural resource management whilst resolving natural resource conflicts through the strengthening of local collective institutions as well as community-based conflict resolution mechanisms.

project_name: Emergency food support to the detained migrants and refugees
project_objective: The aim of the project is to provide emergency food support on a temporary basis to the detention centers and provision of nutritious food packages to most vulnerable detained migrants and refugees including pregnant and lactating women, children, elderly and people with medical needs.

project_name: Shelter assistance and provision of non-food items to the vulnerable Libyan and non-Libyan populations across Libya.
project_objective: The project aims to provide urgently needed shelter assistance and provision of non-food items to detained or stranded migrants as well as most vulnerable Libyan population in line with three sector strategic objectives. The proposed interventions include 1) provision of essential humanitarian assistance including NFIs, cash-based interventions (CBIs) 2) Shelter repair and rehabilitation 3) provision of generators to enhance access to energy (heating, cooking, lights).

project_name: Protection assistance including specialized services for unaccompanied and separated children, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable Libyan and non-Libyan populations across Libya.
project_objective: The project aims to promote, protect and support the well-being of migrants, IDPs, returnees and host communities in at-risk situations with activities that reduce their vulnerabilities and create enhanced protection environment. This intervention will be made through the reinforcement of tailored case management including referrals to available protection services.

project_name: Improving WASH conditions for migrants and refugees in detention centers and urban settings.
project_objective: The project aims to provide urgently needed WASH assistance to detained or stranded migrants and refugees in detention centers and urban areas in Libya, in line with two WASH strategic objectives focusing on the most vulnerable and affected population. The proposed interventions include: 1) rehabilitation of WASH facilities; 2) provision of essential hygiene items to Libyans and non-Libyans; 3) increased awareness on hygiene practices. Through those activities implemented in urban settings, IOM will also address urgent needs of a very limited number of people requiring assistance within host Libyan communities, as is practically not feasible to separate potential beneficiaries. In addition, IOM will abide by the division of labour agreed with other humanitarian stakeholders in terms of locations for implementation, to avoid potential overlapping.

project_name: Supporting the revitalization of health services for vulnerable migrants, IDPs, returnees and host communities in Libya.
project_objective: The security situation in Libya remains volatile, affecting the main urban centers, with clashes between militia and tribes, absence of rule of law, smuggling and trafficking of all kinds, including migrants. Migrants, IDPs, returnees and host communities, people with special needs including people with mental health problems and rural communities are in severe need of healthcare services. Even those who enjoy some access to health services are not having the able opportunity to avail from a complete package of services in an integrated manner; one main shortcoming is the shortage of medical equipment and medicines. The proposed project will improve access to lifesaving and essential primary health care services among the vulnerable migrants, IDPs, returnees and host communities in Libya.

project_name: Enhancing integrated nutrition humanitarian response among the host community and IDPs in Somaliland, South West and Puntland Regions.
project_objective: The proposed action aims at contributing towards the reduction of mortalities and morbidities associated with Malnutrition among under-five children and pregnant and lactating women by providing preventive and curative nutrition services and enhancing accessibility to nutrition services in Puntland, Somaliland and South Central. The proposed project is geared towards reducing the vulnerability within the fragile contexts of Somalia/Somaliland. The Project will be integrated within the other health care services to enhance the provision of life-saving basic and standard Health Nutrition and WASH services at community level, health facilities and IDP camps in urban areas. WVSOM through the proposed action plans to strengthen preventive and curative services. Continued community mobilization and sensitization will be crucial for awareness creation on the available services thus leading to increased up-take of Nutrition services and the other integrated Health and WASH services at community level. Community engagement and participation will also be crucial throughout the project cycle to ensure ownership and sustainability of the project activities. WVSOM will work with community health workers at community level to support in the implementation of the project. To enhance effective implementation of the projects, WVSOM will actively participate in nutrition cluster coordination mechanisms both at national and Zonal level. The proposed action plans to support early warning mechanisms, alert and response systems/surveillance with close linkages to the respective sectors to ensure early response to prevent the situation from worsening. WV Som will also work towards building the capacity of MOH to spearhead quality service provision to the target communities through support health care workers, trainings, supportive supervisions and through provision of essential drugs, and essential supplies to the target health care facilities.

project_name: Expanding Educational Opportunities for Youth and Adolescents in Host Communities
project_objective:
The proposed project will ensure headways or progress among the youth (ages 15-24) of the host communities of Ukhiya & Teknaf through enhanced life skills and skills training, in cooperation with NRC. Youth and adolescents from the host community will be supported with non-formal education focusing on life skills, and vocational training, under the education and livelihoods umbrella. The project will be a skills training program focusing on formal school dropouts for both men/boys and women/girls, with an opportunity to learn a new skill and start a business based on market needs. Specific activities will include:
• Establishing 50 centres for 2000 adolescent/youth, where they will get life skills and vocational training on IGA. Youth will come to these centres for two hours daily, five days in a week. Time of the sessions will be decided with the consultation of the youth, parents and stakeholders. Two Center Facilitators (CF) will be recruited for each of the centre. S/he will be trained on conducting life skill sessions. They will conduct regular sessions and coordinate all the centre-based activities. They will also receive regular in-service training throughout the course of the project.
• Six months skills training program, skills will include different life skills like self-esteem, problem solving, creativity, child rights, gender, reproductive health, child marriage, eve teasing, dowry, neglect and exploitation, trafficking, drug addiction and abuse, HIV and AIDS. When needed, basic literacy and numeracy will also be provided.
• Market Survey to study the desired trade of youth and adolescents and the saturation of the market in Ukhiya & Teknaf due to newly arrived refugees. The market survey should build on those already conducted by partners (and include collaboration with FSL) as well as include feedback from youth and adolescent focus groups. Youth will also contribute to conducting the assessment and selecting relevant activities.
• Vocational training and financial support on IGA like hygienic food preparation, small machine repairs, cell phone repairs, sewing, plant nurseries/gardening, computer skills, beauty parlour, etc. After the final training, based on the assessment youths will be provided 5 thousand taka grant to start the IGA.

The CF will arrange a community meeting to start the centres at the community. The CF will select the centre place and the youth with the consultation of the parents and local communities. Before starting the activities, the CF will prepare a baseline of the youth on life skill. The project will be managed by a Local Center Support Committee (CSC). The seven members CSC will include parents, the CF, representative(s) from the local government, community leaders and the youth. 
Finally, this project will seek to enhance dialogue between the refugee and host community populations, as well as target particular social cohesion activities related to the environment. The youth and adolescents will be involved in regular recreational activities with the refugee focused on reforestation and environmental management. The youth and adolescents in this program will be community mobilizers spreading awareness on environmental management, but will also be responsible for beautification, tree planting, and gardening activities within the community, targeting a total of 25
schools that will have school gardens planted. Apart from social cohesion between refugee and host communities, the youth centres will also be a place where dialogue is encouraged between boys and girls, men and women ages 15-24. Some life skills courses will be taught jointly in order to encourage mutual understanding between genders, particularly on issues such as street harassment, the value of women's education, and issues related to dowry. However, keeping in line with cultural sensitivities, life skills activities will also be done separately as needed.

project_name: Information management and assessment support for evidence-based humanitarian aid planning and delivery in Ukraine

project_name: Explosive Remnants of War Risk Education in Schools, IDP camps, host communities and Contamination and Casualty Surveys in North Syria
project_objective:
This project will be a continuation of an existing Explosive Remnants of War Risk Education ERW - RE programme in Idleb and Aleppo. Shafak proposes that RE activities continue on and that both Contamination and Casualty Data Gathering are conducted by existing teams. 

Shafak is providing ERW-RE to children in the communities of Idleb and Aleppo. Because ERW’s are a long term problem, Shafak believes that long impact approaches for children must be sustained; the more a child is taught safe behaviours, the more likely it is that they will become ingrained in their day-to-day activity. 

Under the ERW-RE part of the project, 6 teams of 5, each consisting of 2 groups of 2 and a team leader, who have already been trained by Shafak, will target locations in Idleb and Aleppo providing school-age children with RE activities, and materials to inform them about dangers of ERW. They will also provide RE material to the older generation, putting up posters about the ERW risks in the public streets and communities to increase the awareness of ERW threats. Schools and locations that were not reached in previous messaging will be the first priority. 

In addition to, Risk Education will be conducted in IDP camps and host communities. Whilst the sessions will be open to all community members, the teams will be placing particular emphasis on reaching those who are most at risk of accident, including children, young men and IDPs who may not be familiar with the type of threat present in the area. The sessions will be held in both schools and community spaces. The teams will also distribute flyers and posters with Risk Education messaging to reach the wider community. 


In addition to RE, Shafak proposes that teams begin gathering data on contamination and causalities with the use of Kobo. This will require technical training which will be provided via Skype from our office in Gaziantep, Turkey. The teams will gather data by talking to local councils, hospitals and medical centres, who will direct them to affected families and communities. The information collected will be recorded into a database, and Shafak's experience within Syria of data collection and remote monitoring; through it, information will be made available to share with other humanitarian actors. Data collected will then be used as a tool to plan ERW clearance in the future.

This information can then be used to better understand protection gaps and improve future programming. It will also be used in advocacy initiatives.

A referral mechanism will be established whereby those who are identified as being particularly vulnerable, can seek additional protection or support in accordance with international best practice for services and protection intervention. This process is already underway in the area where Shafak has worked to develop relationships with other humanitarian actors, notably with Humanity and Inclusion..

project_name: Provision of WASH Services in Northwest Syria

Efficient provision of life-saving non-food items and safe, appropriate emergency shelter to returnees, IDPs and vulnerable host communities through resilience strengthening and positive coping mechanisms in South Sudan.
project_objective:
In this project, Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) will provide life-saving emergency shelter materials and life-sustaining non-food items to the most vulnerable populations, focusing on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees in Nyirol, Pibor and Uror counties in the former Jonglei State; Morobo and Yei Counties in former Central Equatoria State and Guit, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijar Counties in former Unity State through mobile response modality which will contribute to the reduction of protection risks and exposure to diseases attributed with poor shelter conditions and lack of non-food items. Most importantly, the project will support the existing coping mechanisms of the local community and will build resilience towards other shocks that have indirect effect (such as the worsening economic situation) through a component of a cash-based intervention in Bor South County where PAH currently implements FSL and WASH projects. 

PAH will provide emergency shelter and non-food items to the most vulnerable groups in order to alleviate human suffering in a safe and dignified manner. PAH will focus on targeting female headed households, unaccompanied elderly, people with no links to the community, separated children, women at risk (pregnant and lactating mothers), child-headed households, people living with disability and returnees whose properties were damaged and looted during the conflict. 

The mobile response teams will comprise of experienced ES/NFI officers and protection personnel (50 percent women and 50 percent men). One protection officer will participate in 90 percent of interventions with close coordination and collaboration with the Protection Cluster. The team will implement the interventions jointly with other partners’ especially local partners on ground, more specifically ES/NFI, WASH, FSL and Protection actors and in close coordination with the respective clusters. SFPs and cluster coordinators will be involved in the planning, coordination and reporting of the interventions. 

PAH will conduct in-depth need assessment with the involvement of protection staff and with the participation of the community among the target populations with consultative community meetings, key informant interviews, focus group discussions with men, women, boys and girls, household level and individual interviews, and observations will be conducted by the assessment teams at household level and at markets. PAH will encourage support from volunteers from the community in discussions with community leaders and beneficiaries during verification and registration. Mobile data collection tools will be strongly encouraged during the project for needs assessment, verification and monitoring 

As mobile emergency responses will still be a major modality of the intervention, PAH will also focus largely on increasing cash based projects based feasibility assessed by market research. 

Post-distribution monitoring (PDM) exercise will be conducted 1 month after the intervention (where possible) by the M&E team to measure the impact of the projects and to determine if the assistance reached the most vulnerable groups. During and after the intervention, a complaint mechanism will be in place. PAH will use the PDM report for better programming since we will take into account the lessons learnt, complaints raised and recommendations by the beneficiaries. Rapid monitoring activities will be conducted during every distribution by the M&E team, A M&E officer will be part of the distribution team and all interventions conducting rapid monitoring activities. Security and logistical constraints have made it difficult in the recent past for monitoring teams to go back and conduct PDM therefore rapid monitoring will be conducted during the distribution and few days after the distribution. This will help to measure the quality of the program and know the beneficiaries’ satisfaction.

project_name: Increase access to inclusive education, improve learning quality and strengthening community capacity to support learning outcomes of children and youth affected by emergencies in South Sudan
project_objective:
PAH will employ integrated emergency response strategy to meet the educational needs of the learners in the affected locations, focus will be on providing lifesaving safe and dignified learning facilities and services to learners.
In order to provide quality education interventions to the targeted population PAH will focus on implementation with community involvement through the approach described below:
•	Recruitment and training or refresher of teachers/facilitators to ensure teachers are knowledgeable of the content and methodologies to deliver lessons.  In this appeal PAH will recruit, train, and support teachers to provide learning opportunities to children and young people in the identified areas. 
•	PTA members will be mobilized and engaged to encourage a sense of ownership within the communities. Teachers and PTA members will be trained on school management and other cross cutting issues including protection issues, corporal, inclusion of people with disabilities, this is to promote a safe and enabling learning environment for all children attending lessons.     
•	This appeal will also aim to provide scholastic resources and materials to facilitate learning and recovery among learners and increase the level of enrollment and prevent school dropouts due to lack of materials and facilities.  This will include materials such as textbooks, notepads, pencils, uniforms, bags, and schools in a box for the learners.  To strengthen the education system teachers will also be supported with necessary tools needed so as to do their job such as teaching materials (books, chalks, teaching learning aids etc). This is to promote effective delivery of lessons to the learners.
•	To promote a safe and favourable learning environment this project will also focus on improvement of temporary learning spaces. This will be especially for schools were there are reported high influx of IDPs or in areas affected by conflict whose school infrastructures have been destroyed, much attention will also focus on those areas where learners attend lessons in the open. This will be connected with Conditional General Food Distribution project as part of the integration with food security project.
•	PAH shall also ensure through this appeal addressing key issues affecting schools/learning especially water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs which if not addressed will affect the enrolment and continuity of learners in school. As lack of basic things such as water, sanitation and poor hygiene can lead to diseases outbreak that pose the children and risk of such. PAH will work to renovate and rehabilitate WASH facilities in the schools, this will involve training of teachers on basic knowledge on how to address WASH issues in the school. Hygiene clubs shall also be established in the school to promote good hygiene among the learners to keep them safe from water borne diseases.
•	Focus will also be on menstrual hygiene management, (MHM) PAH will also conduct MHM awareness sessions and training in the schools and provide access to sanitary pads and products to help girls of menstruating age meet there needs. This is to prevent girls from missing lessons and or drop out of school.
•	PAH education project will focus on integration with other sectors within PAH, including WASH, Protection, FSL, Nutrition and with other partners where applicable. Including cash component to supplement school materials will be considered where markets are available.

project_name: Improved protection mechanisms for most vulnerable groups in the West Bank and Gaza through increased access and quality mental health and psychosocial services services with comprehensive and gender sensitive approach
project_objective:
Médicos del Mundo Spain (MdM-S)  will contribute through this project to the achievement of  Strategic Objective No. 2 of the Protection Cluster Strategy, i.e. (2) “Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence”. In particular, this project will tackle protection for the mitigation the effects of occupation and conflict-related violence, risk of forcible transfer in the West Bank, impact of blockade in Gaza, settler violence, etc. through an increased access to quality enhanced public Mental Health services and  MHPSS outreach services at the community level. The project will specifically target population, and in particular children, affected by the conflict in the West Bank and Gaza. This will be done incorporating the IASC MHPSS core principles: human rights and equity, participation, do no harm, integrated support to systems and building on available resources and capacities; and the enhancement of a coordinated and effective response to critical incidents.
MdM intends to pursue the following activities between 2019 and 2020: 
•Provision of Child Protection response, with special emphasis on safe spaces for responsive interventions in emergencies, including case management and PSS for children anf familias, as well as Early Stimulation Programs. 
•Provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial services (MHPSS) for adults and youth, with special emphasis on gender equality.
•Capacity building of public Mental Health Services to address children and adolescents needs following appropriate guidelines and standards. 
•Advocacy initiatives among the international community that aim to address protection concerns; prevent violations or enhance accountability for violations of IHRL and IHL by all duty bearers. 
• Contribute to coordination and participation in the Protection Cluster, CPMHPSS subcluster and progressively increasing contributions to GBV subcluster.

project_name: Community Based Protection Interventions in Yambio and Maban
project_objective:
This project aims to respond to protection and psychosocial needs of IDPs, returnees and Host Community in Maban and Yambio. To do so, JRS will use a comprehensive approach, offering different services and support. It will target an estimation of 8,500 (4150M, 4350F) Persons of Concern (POCs), focusing on vulnerable groups such as: people of specific needs (children with disabilities, elderly, widows...), children and youth.

The intervention will be aligned with the 3 Strategic Objectives for the Protection cluster:

S.O.1: ""Provide lifesaving assistance to address priority protection needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach, and priority areas""	
Under this objective JRS will contribute with (1) material distribution for POCs to help them improve their living conditions, (2) Strengthening and ensuring Safe referrals pathways between JRS and other organizations to ensure a comprehensive respond to POCs’ needs and (3) protection/support for people with specific needs.

S.O.2: ""Prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience""
Regarding this objective JRS will focus on (1) promoting psychosocial wellbeing and strengthening resilience mechanisms of POCs. This will be done through psychosocial support activities (group counselling, individual counselling and basic counselling training), (2) protection awareness activities and (3) workshop for youth to help them develop resilience skills.

S.O.3: ""Enable durable solution for IDPs and other affected populations""
JRS will carry out (1) peaceful coexistence and conflict mitigation activities and work on (2) profiling IDPs to make sure their needs are collected and heard from the humanitarian community.

This project will be implemented with a community based approach, to strengthen its participatory structure so that refugees and host community members are truly partners in the provision of services. For the psychosocial activities JRS will train and recruits IDPs and host community members to spearhead services to the people of concern. Also, the JRS staff will undergo continued capacity building to enable them develop competencies that are required for service delivery. This will allow IDPs and host community members to take control of the services provided to their communities now and in the future.

project_name: Provision of Community-Based Child Protection Support for crisis-affected children in NW Syria
project_objective:
SHAFAK organization will respond to the child protection concerns (death and Injuries due to the ERWs, Child Labor, Child Recruitment and Use by Parties to the Conflict, sexual violence, Child marriage, child separation…etc.) through center-based activities in Child-Friendly Spaces (CFS) and community outreach teams (mobile teams) deployed in Idleb and Azaz district. SHAFAK will deliver case management services for vulnerable children and for their caregivers by providing direct assistances and refer them to a proper care arrangement using the service map for both girls and boys under the 18 years and will deliver the services to the disable children and help them to reintegrate with their communities, and deliver raising awareness sessions/campaigns to the people in the communities about child rights and child protection and risk education. Furthermore, SHAFKAK will organize recreational events in the CFSs and care center to highlight the child concerns in the target communities.
Also SHAFAK will strengthen the capacity of the local communities about the child concerns. Firstly, by establishing the Child Protection Networks (CPNs) in the targeted communities and train the key persons in these communities and the workers in care centers, schools, hospitals and all persons who are in direct touch with children about the Child Protection Minimum Standers (CPMS) and Psychosocial First Aid (PFA), Safe Identification and referral (SIR) taking into consideration the recommendations received from the local councils, children, caregivers to enhance the quality of provided services. SHAFAK will use the monthly reports of the Protection Monitoring task force on the latest developments that threaten child protection and will provide services according to the need there.

project_name: Humanitarian and resilience food security and livelihoods assistance across South Sudan
project_objective: The overall goal of the intervention is to save and protect lives, alleviate suffering and to initiate recovery through building resilience to and preventing future crises by breaking the cycle between crises and vulnerability. DRC food security and livelihood (FSL) activities are heavily inter-linked with Protection and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) response. FSL activities have been designed to ameliorate negative impact on the environment, and to foster local-level, sustainable solutions that build resilience, food security and livelihood development. DRC will encourage and train people on the use of sustainable and climate-relevant agricultural techniques, will encourage resilience through income generation activities (IGA) trainings and will inspire target communities to create businesses to build up local markets. All projects have been linked with information campaigns and trainings, and key topics across all areas will include environmental, protection and gender mainstreaming.

project_name: Integrated Interventions in Food Security, WASH and Shelter for vulnerable host, disaster affected and displaced populations in Somalia
project_objective:
This projects aims to provide integrated multi-sectoral assistance to 6,839 disaster affected households (41,035 people) including displaced and host communities in Somalia. For people recovering from drought, attention will be placed on provision of recovery and sustainable solutions to build their resilience while under-served long term displaced households will be supported with durable solutions related to reintegration. Disaster affected populations will be supported through life-saving emergency interventions. To achieve this the project will focus on mitigating protection risks through a three-prong integrated approach consisting of Food security and livelihoods, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Shelter and House Land and Property assistance. In line with the Somalia Resilience Recovery Framework, long-term displaced populations in prioritized locations in Bosaaso, Garowe, Galkacyo, Qardho, Kismayo, Baidoa and Dollow will be provided with durable solutions to basic services where land is availed by the government. Livelihood and Food security (LFS) intervention will aim at improving access to food through cash-based emergency support in the short term so as to enable people in Emergency and Crisis (IPC3 and 4) deal with the impending situation and mitigate the negative coping strategies. The LFS will support targeted populations especially in hard to reach areas to meet their basic food and non-food needs through provision of emergency and safety net support. This will be achieved through provision of Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCTs), Conditional Cash Transfers where appropriate, and companion programming through awareness raising for good nutrition through promoting diet diversity and safe food preparation, and hygiene practices. All cash transfer programmes (CTPs) will take into account seasonality including agricultural calendar and fluctuating market prices, in order to maximize positive effects of the cash injection in communities and on the market. Livelihood and Food security interventions will reach 17,340 individuals (2890 hhs). The same beneficiaries supported through LFS in addition to others will also receive WASH services. 
Life-saving WASH interventions will temporary provide safe water through direct delivery or restricted cash to enable beneficiaries buy their own water depending on context and market functionality. Provision of hygiene kits through cash or in-kind, household water treatment and/or point of use water treatment to 400 hhs, construction of 100 simple design latrines, latrine emptying (50 latrines) and safe fecal sludge disposal and hygiene promotion will be delivered. Schools and health facilities will be provided with adequate water and sanitation facilities including private space for menstrual hygiene (40 institutional latrines) while hygiene promotion will be through group practicing on good hygiene behavior. All latrine will be installed with handwashing equipment and community sensitized to use soap for handwashing. Women and girls will be involved in identification of sites for facilities to ensure their safety and security is taken into account. Latrines will be gender separated, provided with lockable doors and handwashing equipment. Solar street lights (5 posts) will be provided near water points and latrines to improve the security and safety of women and girls especially in crowded IDP settlements. Long term solutions will include construction and or rehabilitation of water sources including 2 boreholes (1 new) with infrastructure and hybrid energy, 5 shallow wells and 1 river water intake system with water treatment and extension of piped water network. New borehole and river water intake systems construction will be preceded by hydrogeological survey and hydrological studies undertaken by competent staff or consultants. Design of structure will take environmental issues into consideration to ensure safe abstraction. Low scale Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) will be undertaken for new water sources to define and implement environmental mitigation measures for negative impacts. A total of 25,000 people (4,167 households) will be reached with WASH services where some will also receive livelihood and food assistance, shelter and information and legal services. 
Shelter: The project will focus on improving the physical protection and dignity of IDPs, refugee returnees and poor host communities across Somalia through the provision of locally purchased Non Food Items (NFIs to 3000 hhs) and Emergency Shelter Kits (ESKs to 2000 hhs) through cash/voucher/in-kind modalities, construction of Semi-permanent and Permanent Shelters through community driven or owner driven approaches, settlement (re)planning training to reduce congestion and overcrowding, conducting Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for Shelters and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs & ESKs and participation in infrastructure mapping exercises led by Shelter cluster or any other partner. NRC will target total 5345 households (50% female-headed) through different Shelter interventions throughout the year 2019. NRC staff will ensure that the provided cash has been utilized for intended purpose by coordinating with the beneficiaries themselves and conduct follow ups with the support of the community leaders, local authorities and the relevant clusters. NRC will also support the displaced households through provision of Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance to promote security of tenure. 
Design of infrastructure across all sectors will take into consideration the needs of special groups in the community including the disabled, old, children to ensure they have equitable access to the services. Design of latrines will take into account the needs of special groups such as the physically challenged hence depending on needs some will have a smooth ramp, handle and or side rail bars, toilet seat and adequate in size. To enhance sustainability, women and men will be involved in identification of permanent solutions, design and implementation of the activities. Community structures including water committees, Community Hygiene promoters will comprise of both men and women from all community groups including the minority and the marginalized for equal representation who will be trained on management of the facilities provided. For borehole water supplies, Private Public Partnerships (PPP) management system will be adopted for effective management and possible expansion of systems in future. NRC understands the context in the area of operation and will ensure protection issues that include exclusion of the minority and marginalized clans, SRGBV, extortion as well as barriers caused by gate keepers are addressed throughout all the components of this integrated programme. Beneficiaries will be provided with information on NRC’s complaints, feedback and response mechanisms that is managed by an independent M&E unit within the organization. NRC will work with identified local partners especially in hard to reach areas. Our partners will receive on-the-job training especially on enhancing operational systems within their organization, conducting credible assessments, proposal development and reporting.

project_name: Integrated Life saving Humanitarian assistance is provided to disaster affected communities in Somalia
project_objective:
The proposed interventions aim at improving beneficiaries’ access to food through cash-based emergency support in the short term, supporting beneficiaries through the safety net programs, engaging youth in skill development program for livelihoods diversification and establishing small enterprises. These initiatives will enable beneficiaries to deal with the impending situation and mitigate the negative coping strategies on immediate basis and will help beneficiaries to recover from shocks. Livelihoods and Food Security will continue to engage with other like-minded agencies, institutions and respective public sector departments to promote social safety nets and social protection through cash programming, Skills development and establishing small businesses. The cash will be provided as Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCTs) for multiple needs, Conditional Cash Transfers (cash-for-work for small-scale infrastructure repairs) where appropriate, and companion programming for awareness raising around good nutrition through promoting diet diversity, BCC and safe food preparation, and hygiene practices. All cash transfer programs (CTPs) will take into account seasonality including agricultural calendar and fluctuating market prices. 

NRC aims to support and strengthen resilience of vulnerable populations against shocks. This objective will contribute to protecting and conserving natural resources on which lives, and livelihoods depend, such as water, soil, land and forest resources.  This will increase purchasing power of displacement-affected people to enable them meet their minimum needs for food and non-food items and assist in recovery of their livelihoods. NRC will continue to work with such entities to ensure that cash plus transfers are done using more efficient, stronger and locally accountable market-based approaches. NRC will support targeted populations especially in hard to reach areas to meet their basic food and non-food needs. 

NRC is an active member of Somalia Food Security Cluster, the Somalia Cash Working Group, Somalia Cash Consortium and the Regional Food Security & Nutrition Working Group, Guidance from these fora will inform NRC program design and transfer values in each of the proposed regions.

project_name: Prise en charge des enfants non accompagnés et victimes de violence ou à risque d’être victimes et affectés par les situations humanitaires
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à appuyer les enfants non accompagnés venant de la République Dominicaine à travers les 4 points frontaliers officiels et certains points non officiels les plus fréquentés. Cette prise en charge requiert une équipe multidisciplinaires formée des agents de protection de l’IBESR et de la BPM et des travailleurs sociaux des ONGs locales partenaires qui interviennent depuis 2015 dans la prise en charge des enfants arrivés sur la frontière dont 40% viennent des communes autres que la zone de déportations. Ce projet donnera aussi l’occasion de répondre aux besoins des enfants en situation de vulnérabilité et qui sont victimes ou à risque de l’être suite à la situation humanitaire qui exacerbe les vulnérabilités des filles et des garçons, de la pauvreté et du manque de connaissance de la communauté sur la protection des enfants. Les prises en charge seront adaptées selon les besoins des enfants et en tenant compte de l’âge et du sexe de l’enfant.  Les réseaux communautaires existants participeront à la sensibilisation des acteurs et familles afin de susciter l’engagement communautaire pour la prévention de la violence et de la séparation des enfants et pour une meilleure fonctionnalité du mécanisme de protection informel. 
Le projet cible 9100 personnes dont 800 enfants non accompagnés (480 garçons et 320 filles), 3,300 enfants victimes ou à risque (1650 garçons et 1650 filles) et 5,000 individus touchés par les sensibilisations (2,000 femmes, 2,000 hommes, 500 filles et 500 garçons)
