project_name: Apoyo a los servicios básicos de salud materno-infantil para la población vulnerable en los estados priorizados.
project_objective:
El considerable deterioro de la situación económica y social que enfrenta Venezuela ha impactado múltiples dimensiones de los servicios sociales, siendo salud uno de los sectores más golpeados en todos sus niveles: gobernanza del sistema de salud, financiamiento, infraestructura, recursos humanos, suministros y mantenimiento. 

Si bien no contamos con informes que analicen las causas de muerte tanto en recién nacidos como en sus madres, resulta evidente la relación que esto tiene con el elevado número de servicios que no pueden ofrecer la atención básica para el parto y para el cuidado de los recién nacidos. Una reciente observación realizada por UNICEF permitió evidenciar:
- Falta general de medicamentos y suministros médicos esenciales. 
- Debilidades en infraestructura de hospitales y centros de salud. 
- Número suficiente de recursos humanos calificados.
- Deficiencias en las prácticas de limpieza y desinfección hospitalaria.
- Graves deficiencias en servicios de apoyo. 

El objetivo principal de este proyecto es contribuir a que las madres, los recién nacidos y los niños venezolanos, incluidos los adolescentes, estén protegidos contra las enfermedades y muertes evitables mediante un mejor acceso equitativo al paquete mínimo de servicios de salud a nivel de atención primaria de la salud (APS), dirigido a las poblaciones más desfavorecidas y de difícil acceso en los diez estados priorizados en el PRH. Entre ellos se incluyen los que viven en regiones geográficas rurales, los que viven en el quintil socioeconómico más bajo, las poblaciones indígenas y los migrantes internos. Esto está en consonancia con los objetivos estratégicos del sector, el enfoque de equidad del UNICEF en los programas de salud y la visión del acceso universal a la salud.

A través de este proyecto, UNICEF contribuirá a que las mujeres que asisten a control prenatal reciban un paquete integrado básico de atención prenatal que incluye la detección de embarazos de riesgo y la prestación de servicios como suplementos de hierro, pruebas del VIH, profilaxis del paludismo y prevención de la transmisión del VIH de la madre al hijo; los niños y niñas recibirán atención integrada, inmunización sistemática y diagnóstico de los lactantes con el VIH en ambulatorios prioritarios, al tiempo que se asegurará que se establezcan vías de derivación funcionales a la red de hospitales para que reciban una atención más alta o especializada de las personas que lo necesiten.  Se pretende una cobertura de al menos 359 ASIC en los 11 estados priorizados

project_name: Apoyo al Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Educación (MPPE) para la mejora del acceso y la retención escolar en las escuelas públicas de Venezuela.
project_objective:
El objetivo de la intervención es que los niñas, niños y adolescentes de los municipios más vulnerables de los estados priorizados, asistan y permanezcan en centros educativos públicos que mejoran la calidad de la enseñanza y de los contenidos pedagógicos, con base en los enfoques de derechos humanos, género, desarrollo adolescente, interculturalidad y bilingüismo.

Esta acción es parte de una intervención liderada por UNICEF de ejecución directa y vinculado al Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Educación (MPPE) y se focaliza en escuelas dependientes directamente del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Educación (MPPE).
Las acciones previstas se centrarán en: 
•	La generación de condiciones para el acceso, retención, la enseñanza y aprendizaje de NNA en las escuelas a través de la entrega de material educativo para los alumnos y a través de intervenciones priorizadas para la recuperación y puesta en funcionalidad de los servicios de agua y saneamiento en las escuelas , así como de apoyo al transporte de docentes a los centros educativos. 
•	Apoyar soluciones para la entrega de incentivos económicos a docentes que generan condiciones dignas para el profesorado y que contribuyan a la continuidad operativa de los servicios educativos y disminuyan el abandono de los profesores.
•	La formación a los docentes para fortalecer competencias técnicas en el uso de materiales educativos y para fortalecer conocimientos básicos en aspectos relacionados con la protección infantil y la disminución de riesgos en el entorno escolar.

El componente de rehabilitación de infraestructuras de agua y saneamiento contribuye de manera fundamental a la consecución de los objetivos de este proyecto. Su coste será asumido a través de los proyectos presentados por el sector WASH de UNICEF.

project_name: IRAQ - Save the Children
Agriculture revitalization and support to food self-sufficiency in liberated areas (Federal Iraq)
project_objective:
The proposed intervention is in line with the 2019 HRP priority areas defined by the Food Security Cluster. Indeed the proposed project will target Tel Afar, Tilkaif, Hamdanyia.  The project complies with the 2019 HRP Strategic Objective 1: post-conflict transition towards durable solutions.

The main objective of the project is to support return and recovery processes of IDPs in Federal Iraq.

Based on TGH past and ongoing FSL actions, the present project has been designed taking into account the various local contexts and needs that strongly differ from area to another. Considering the diversity of needs calling for tailored need based responses, TGH proposes a range of solutions.
 Past actions implemented both in Federal Iraq and KRI (fodder and animal distributions in Rabia area, mobile veterinary clinics in Tilkaif and Rabia area, partnership with Dohuk Veterinary College) and recent assessments have allowed TGH to develop a strong understanding of agriculture related needs. 

Based on TGH observations in IDP camps (in which TGH implements CP activities) and field assessments, barriers to return for IDPs toward their areas of origin needs to be overcome with an adequate support to allow a durable and dignified return.  Most vulnerable population groups will be targeted by the project (farmers with a limited number of animals, matching a range of vulnerability criteria such as the level of incomes, number of children, etc.). 

Proposing a mix immediate and longer term solutions is mandatory to allow immediate and durable returns of IDPs: they need to be able to quickly restart a productive activity, while the extensive damages on productive private and public assets / infrastructure call for a longer term recovery and rehabilitation approach. To that extent, TGH aims at implementing quick impact activities (e.g.: mobile veterinary clinics, fodder and animals distribution) and working in parallel on sustainable activities such as rehabilitation of water efficient irrigation assets, training of veterinary staffs, implementation of solar powered irrigation, mapping of available irrigation resources for a more sustainable water management, rehabilitation of market chain infrastructures, etc.

Considering the damaged social fabric due to the recent events and the diversity of ethnic groups, TGH will pay a strong attention to the do no harm approach within this project. Equity and transparency in the delivered support will be crucial to avoid fueling or creating tensions. 

Since part of the present project is already funded by the French Development Agency (36 months project- starting early 2019), significant operational and means synergies are expected between the foreseen activities and funds.

Treatment and Prevention of Acute Malnutrition for Affected Communities in NBeG, Warrap and Jonglei
project_objective: In response to the critical malnutrition and food security situation across South Sudan, Action Against Hunger will continues its program for treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition in Warrap, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Jonglei States. According to Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) projections for Sep 2018 - Mar 2019, despite planned humanitarian food assistance and limited relief in the end of 2018, an expected 5.2 million (49% of the population) will be left severely food insecure (IPC 3, 4 & 5). Levels of acute malnutrition are expected to deteriorate in the first quarter of 2019 with an early onset of the lean season, depleting households’ food stocks from their own production. Our SMART surveys, conducted in all major counties of Action Against Hunger’s interventions (sub Gogrial East), show GAM rates above emergency threshold of 15%: Fangak GAM 16.1% and SAM prevalence 2.5%; Gogrial West GAM 26.6% with 5.4% SAM and Aweil East at 21% GAM and 4.9% SAM prevalence. This reality is greatly aggravated by limited availability of food in markets, poor diets, poor harvests, economic crisis, ongoing physical insecurity, poor hygiene and sanitation, and lack of services. The program will directly target 14,769 children under 5 and 6,664 pregnant and lactating women in treatment of malnutrition at 13 of the organization’s existing 35 nutrition sites (OTP/TSFP). 8,680 total caregivers will be sensitized on MIYCN topics. Our static intervention is complemented by our emergency response teams, who provide malnutrition surveillance, treatment and prevention services and related capacity building in areas of high need, as indicated by the Nutrition Information Working Group. Under this program’s treatment component, children with SAM and MAM and PLW with MAM will be treated through Outpatient Therapeutic Programs and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs. Children with SAM and medical complications will be referred for treatment at the organization’s Stabilization Centers in Alek and Malualkon. At nutrition sites, caregivers will receive sensitization and counselling on MIYCN and other health related topics. Caregivers will also receive various crucial gender- and age-sensitive hygiene items. Community volunteers will conduct mass screening at household level to ensure early detection and timely referral of cases of acute malnutrition. During mass screening, community volunteers will also provide valuable sensitization on nutrition and hygiene/sanitation practices, as well as counselling for those affected by malnutrition. Under the community component, the organization will conduct community mobilization activities, such as the training of Community Leaders and holding of mass awareness campaigns (large gatherings, radio spots) around MIYCN topics. Mother-to-Mother Support Groups are formed to inform mothers directly of MIYCN and MUAC measurement (the latter an initiative being piloted for the organization in South Sudan in 2019). These groups will also conduct cooking demonstrations and kitchen gardening activities in order to improve the food security and nutrition statuses of households. Male staff will conduct Male Group Discussions, which will sensitize men on women’s issues and MIYCN, enabling women’s improved access to nutrition services and activities.

project_name: Equitable access to safe water and sanitation services and improved hygiene practices among crisis affected communities in NBeG, Warrap and Jonglei states
project_objective: Action Against Hunger has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs. The strategy of Action Against Hunger addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WASH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon the communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently Action Against Hunger is implementing its program activities in NBeG, Warrap and Jonglei state with established Field Ocer in Malualkon, Alek, Ajogo, Old Fangak and Paguir Payams. WASH projects will be implemented to ensure that the “host communities and returnees has safe access to water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behaviour”. Proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5 and pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WASH and Nutrition response to break the diarrhoea – malnutrition vicious cycle. The proposed objective will ensure the effectiveness of the treatment for malnutrition in the proposed program target area. In order to achieve the overall objective of the project following activities will enable us to reach/provide assistance for approximately 13,670 HH (app. 96,000 individuals). Following activities will be implemented to achieve the overall targets:- • Provide timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water to vulnerable and affected women, men, girls and boys • Enable vulnerable and affected populations to practice safe, sanitary and hygienic living through secure, dignified and gender appropriate sanitation services • Provide WASH minimum package of interventions on an ad-hoc basis, adapted to the specificities of the related-outbreaks, at an institution level as well as for the wider community • Increase knowledge of appropriate hygiene practices among vulnerable and affected populations, to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. Action Against Hunger will implement proposed project in the catchment areas of nutrition sites in NBeG, Warrap and Jonglei states. Baseline KAP survey will be conducted in the target areas to identify the knowledge, attitude and practices of the communities. Further a detail need assessment will be conducted to assess the access of the communities to safe water sources and sanitation facilities. Implementation strategy follows the need assessment and KAP surveys at project start. Additionally, the program will contribute to the ACF multi-sector emergency response throughout the country, by supporting its WASH component. Proposed program strategy takes into account specific gender needs during surveys to ensure the equitable participation of all gender and age groups.

project_name: MA- Reducing Explosive Remnants of War impact on Conflict Affected Communities in former Eastern and Central Equatorial States, January-December 2019
project_objective:
Revision inputs:
1. MRE beneficiaries: the MRE component of the action will target 9,300 beneficiaries, including 2,325 men (out of which 75 male CFPs), 2,325 women (out of which 75 female CFPs), 2,325 boys (out of which 75 PREs), 2,325 girls (out of which, 75 PREs);
2. HA to be surveyed/cleared: the action will handover at least 150,000 smt of land released from ERW, for a minimum of 3 HA surveyed/cleared of 50,000 smt each. Actual number of HAs will depend upon UNMAS tasking and prioritisation;
3. Cluster Objectives and corresponding indicators: in line with HRP strategic objective 2, the project will contribute to cluster objective to “provide immediate lifesaving assistance to address priority protection needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach areas”, by targeting at least 3 HA surveyed/cleared for at least 150,000 smt of land released from ERW threat (target 1.5). In line with HRP SO 2 and 3, the project will also contribute to the cluster objective to “prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience”, through MRE awareness sessions benefiting in total 9,300 beneficiaries (2,325 men, 2,325 women, 2,325 boys, and 2,325 girls) (target 2.5). 
Summary: 
Overall goal of the proposed project is to “increase civilian security by protecting lives and property through removal of explosive remnants of war and sustainable risk education”. During the suggested twelve months of the action, this will be achieved through two main objectives, namely by improving safe access of local communities to land and infrastructure through land release and disposal of explosive remnants of war in suspected contaminated areas; and improving the safety of local communities through increased knowledge and promotion of safe practices on risks associated to ERW. One Multi-Tasking Team will compile Survey and Hazard Report Forms, collecting information from the local communities regarding recent accidents, suspected and confirmed HAs, use and ownership of land, and local security dynamics. Findings from the assessment will support the prioritization of contaminated areas for clearance, to be conducted in line with international standards, national guidelines and DCA SOPs. During the action, DCA will handover to local communities at least 150,000 smt of land released from ERW threat, benefitting approximately 15,000 beneficiaries, including men, women, boys and girls. In support of the CL/RE component, one team will conduct RE awareness sessions, with trainings of Community Focal Points and Peer Risk Educators. Selected representatives among adult and children groups will be trained to deliver safety messages to their families, peer groups and communities, and to identify dangerous areas, and reporting potential hazards to relevant authorities and mine action stakeholders. For this project, DCA plans to reach 9,000 beneficiaries with RE awareness sessions, equally divided among opposite gender and adult/children. Moreover, DCA will train, monitor and support 150 CFPs and 150 PREs in the targeted villages, equally divided among male/female representatives. 
Considering the prioritization of humanitarian needs, contamination severity, accessibility and DCA experience in the country, DCA will target contaminated areas in Former Central Equatoria (Juba county) and Eastern Equatoria States (Magwi and Torit counties), in coordination with MA stakeholders and pending approved tasking from UNMAS as to avoid duplications. Finally, field operations will be pending security clearance, as to minimize risks for DCA staff, beneficiaries and other stakeholders. 
As for targeted groups, beneficiaries will include host community, IDPs and/or returnees, based on priority areas of humanitarian need. Through a participatory approach, DCA will ensure all community groups are involved in the project, paying a specific attention to groups most at risk, such as children, and most vulnerable, such as women.

project_name: Emergency Primary Healthcare Services for vulnerable IDPs, Returnees  & Host Communities of Yei and Morobo Counties
project_objective:
Emergency Primary Health Services IDP & Host Communities is one year aimed to provide integrated basic primary care services for IDPs and host communities in Yei and Morobo Counties. The project will be implemented in 2 Primary Health Care units, 1 Primary Health Care Centre and a Hospital county; and 1 PHCU and 2 Mobile Clinics in Morobo County in addition rapid response missions and community level activities, targeting a total population of 23, 265 and 12,109 individuals in Morobo and Yei respectively.

 The main objective of the project is to provide integrated, lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations (women, children and elderly) focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality. The overarching objective of the project feeds into 3 strategic Objectives of South Sudan Humanitarian response Plan 2019 which includes; 1- Save lives by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs among the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys; 2-Protect vulnerable women, men, girls and boys through provision of specialized and integrated services and 3-Support at-risk communities to promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks

project_name: GBV EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROJECT FOR MUNDRI WEST (Mundri and Kotobi Payam) and MUNDRI EAST (Lakama'di and Kedi'ba Payams)
project_objective:
The overall aim of the project is to contribute to strengthening prevention, mitigation and response to GBV issues as well as strengthening quality of care for GBV survivors. This will build on the already gained milestones from the 2018 that has already enabled AYA to provide community based women and girls friendly spaces in Mundri Payam, Kotobi Payam in Mundri West and Lakama’di and Kedi'ba in Mundri East. Also continuous provision of case management services especially in Lui, Mundri, Kedi’ba and Kotobi. However, these established structures of the centers remained poor, limited W&GFS staffs and increased number of IDPs in the targeted locations.

AYA intends to continue run and equip Women and Girl’s Friendly Spaces established in Kedi’ba, Mundri, Kotobi and Lakama’di. There will be establishment of one additional women and girl’s friendly space in Lui.
Women and girls are the primary target of the project. Community outreaches, psycho-social support services, case management. Young male and young female engagement that will support discussion around the GBV and women rights will be conducted. This will create change in communities that the project aims to support.

AYA will also create awareness to the women and girls during women and girls friendly spaces sessions on the available services for GBV, small income generation as part of psychosocial support, recreational activities with women and girls in women and girls friendly spaces and support building capacity of women and girls especially most vulnerable women and girls in vocational activities for improvement of livelihoods.
There is already existing referral pathway in Mundri West. This project will enable AYA to train the members of GBV Working group on the referral pathways and how to use to support the survivors of GBV and there will be quarterly update of the referral pathways. AYA will create one referral pathway for Mundri East., and update it regularly.

The organization through the previous project, have already trained and positioned its staffs in GBV issues including case management. Therefore, the only refresher training to the staff will be on discussion around child survivors of GBV. This will be done to sharpen their skills on supporting child survivors of GBV.

project_name: Provision of shelter & NFIs for displaced populations in Jonglei, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria in South Sudan
project_objective: In line with the S/NFI Cluster strategic objectives, particularly objective 1 (improve access to safe, appropriate emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to newly displaced or vulnerable populations in secondary displacement) and objective 2 (improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable IDPs in protracted displacement, returnees and host communities unable to meet their S/NFI needs), ACTED will provide emergency shelter and non-food items to the most vulnerable displaced populations and host communities impacted by conflict in an efficient and effective manner in Jonglei, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria states, specifically targeting Akobo, Wau, Jur River, Raja and Yambio counties. Through this project targeted beneficiaries will be given shelter and non-food items either in-kind or through vouchers, or multi-sectorial survival kits depending on their needs and location (e.g. hard to reach areas), to enable quick responses to meet their immediate needs. Cash Based Programming (CBP) will be critical to implementing this programme, and in particular vouchers will be preferred in areas where there is a functioning market and the items are available, and where access humanitarian partners is more consistent. ACTED will utilise the different modalities depending on the context and the needs of the area, as highlighted during assessments that will be conducted.

project_name: Enhance  Food Security Resilience and Recovery Livelihood Assistance for crisis affected vulnerable Households in  Western and Northern Bahr el Ghazal and  lakes state
project_objective:
Aid Support Community Organization will focus on households and community level as delivery platform with emphasis on gender base violence prevention by awareness rising on the accountability to affected population
 Based on September 2018 IPC findings, the project focused locations Wau, Aweil South and Yirol East are facing emergency and crisis phase 4 and 3. ASCO will increasingly  recognize  the response need of the IDPs, vulnerable host  population taking into account  the livelihoods of the affected  population by saving their lives, protecting  and strengthening  their livelihoods  through  increasing their long term resilience  and reduce their vulnerability to future shocks. 
The project will contribute to three cluster objectives: Unconditional food assistance, Food production for the most vulnerable households, transitional emergency food assistance and dependency reduction on food and agricultural input support.
ASCO will engage closely with Nutrition, health and WASH partners on ground to integrate Food security sensitive intervention into other sectors. Food security and livelihood status is compromised where people are exposed to high level of infection due to unsafe and insufficient water supply, limited access to basic healthcare, poor food security and inadequate sanitation.
ASCO will carry out integrated respond by supporting the households within the communities with livelihood kits, dry season response fishing and vegetable kits and tools. ASCO will coordinate with WASH partners on ground to ensure all targeted households follow water treatment and storage, hand washing promotion with soap distribution and hygiene promotion for small stock open defecation free at proximity domiciliary level around the households and the nutrition sites. 
 Women will involve in participation in project design implementation of activities and information sharing to express their views. The project will also increase availability of GBV prevention and response services inWau,Aweil South and Yirol East Counties where many women are suffering from different forms of gender base violence.

 ASCO will collaborate and coordinate with health partners on ground at households’ level distributed with livelihood kits to ensure management of medical complications among children with SAM, provision of infant and young child feeding to children with SAM and vaccination of children under 5years on polio and measles and pregnant and lactating mothers. 
Based on September IPC report released by food and security cluster, SMART surveys, areas affected by conflict people including children under 5years and PLW are severely food insecure and have increased nutritional requirements. ASCO will integrate by advocating for prevention and treatment of malnutrition to children under the age of 5years and nursing mothers, provision of nutrition education at nutrition sites, provide micronutrients supplementation to children under 5 years and PLW and other vulnerable groups including elderly, HIV/AIDS and TB Patients male and female

Project  focus on three humanitarian assistance priorities, food availability, ensuring continued regular access to food, production and trade, nutritional diversity and safe access to natural resources. ASCO will scale up further the provision of main and dry season livelihood kits. Fishing kits, crop, and vegetable kits to the most severely affected households targeting host community beneficiaries men, women, boys and girls including elderly people and disabled by involving or participating in seed distribution.
Right based approach will be used in selecting targeted 20000 beneficiaries constitute of Women 7000, Men 3000, Girls 6000 and boys 4000 to undertake different roles and activities of the project.  Local Authorities of Wau, Aweil South and Yirol East Counties will be involved in the identification and selection of beneficiaries.

project_name: Food Assistance and Early Livelihood Support
project_objective: Jonglei and parts of Eastern Equatoria are currently on IPC 4 category. ACROSS is proposing a project that will swiftly deliver urgently needed but targeted humanitarian assistance while simultaneously rolling out a livelihood recovery for 10,000 households, in Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria states. The purpose of this project is to improve and sustain essential crop production and productivity through direct seed and farm tools and protect and rehabilitate the livelihoods of the most vulnerable groups in the community through essential crops, livestock, and vegetable production as per the livelihood zone capacity in the targeted counties. ACROSS will fully engage community leaders, women’s groups, the youth and others within the community throughout the life of the project. The project is designed and will be implemented with knowledge of the seasonality context and the livelihood calendar. The communities in these regions have limited productive assets, and require immediate assistance to tackle the food insecurity which is high on the cluster agenda. This project will be integrated with SSJR4 Dutch Relief Alliance (DRA) funded and Swedish PMU funded projects that ACROSS is currently implementing in Pibor and Kapoeta counties. The project will seek to diversify the household diet and address malnutrition, which is mostly a problem for children, pregnant and lactating mothers. The provision of improved inputs like seed and agricultural tools in a timely manner will significantly contribute to the restoration of agricultural inputs in remote locations enabling communities to ensure that planting is on time. The project will ensure that vulnerable people have direct access to more food through the provision of vegetable and crop seeds and tools, fishing equipment, animal health services as well as cash for work project planned. The project will integrate and augment responses to immediate needs, restoration of livelihoods, and capacity building to pave the path for long-term recovery in order to enhance communities. ACROSS proposes actions that will connect with the humanitarian response and resilience programs that will target 10,000 households (60,000 beneficiaries) in Jonglei and the Eastern Equatoria States, comprised of 29,400 males (14,406 above and 14994 below 18 years) 30,600 females (14994 above 18 years and 15606 below 18years).

project_name: Improved education opportunities and integrated social services for IDP and host community children and adolescents in Eastern Equatoria and Lakes States
project_objective:
The project intends to provide a holistic, comprehensive and intersectoral response to the problems of the Education System in EES and Lakes State, starting from the assumption that schools represent platforms through which also Protection, Nutrition, Hygiene, Health and Psychosocial needs of vulnerable children can be addressed. Moreover, the intervention wants to support the entire education system, starting from nursery and primary school, up to secondary and Vocational training, including the alternative programs offered by the Accelerating Learning Program (ALP). Therefore, learners and teachers from all the different steps of education system will be supported in an integrated way, by providing scholastic materials, training and sensitization sessions on subjects such as education, child protection, SGBV, health, psychological well-being. Structural interventions will be done in schools to improve the quality and safety of the learning environments, i.e. Temporarily Learning Spaces, renovation of classrooms, construction of latrines and school kitchens, erection or rehabilitation of fences. Schools will be used as an entry point to promote good hygiene and health practices through hygiene sessions, HIV/AIDS prevention and reproductive health sessions. The students and teachers will also be supported in improving their food security status, by receiving training and agricultural inputs for school gardens for their daily consumption. Moreover, the project wants to introduce an innovative intervention to improve the nutrition status in the schools, providing schools with improved stoves with the benefit of limiting the costs for schools and families spent on fire wood for the preparation of school meals and mitigating the use of fuel wood, the most essential local source of energy. Upon successful utilization by the school matrons, similar stoves can be built in the house of these women and presented as a model to neighboring households.
On the basis of a holistic concept of education, the project aims to involve also the other relevant actors in this process, first of all the parents and the communities at large. For these reason, parents, community members, PTAs & SMCs will be involved in Campaigns, Open Days and meeting to promote the importance of education and discuss about sensitive topics such as education for girls, violence and SGBV, child protection, among other.
The objectives of the project are:
•	To improve the quality of education and to ensure access to safe learning spaces for vulnerable children, adolescents and youth
•	To provide access for children, adolescents and youth to integrated social protection services 
•	To promote resilience and capacity building of teachers, parents and community at large 
The beneficiaries of the projects will be students, teachers, PTAs and SMCs from 1 VTC in EES and 61 schools; 50 schools in different Counties in EES, i.e. Magwi County (including Nimule), Ikwoto County, Magwi County (including Nimule), Narus/Kapoeta East County, Kapoeta South County, and 11 schools in Cueibet County, Lakes State.

project_name: Emergency Health Response in Eastern Equatoria and Unity South Sudan
project_objective:
Increased access to integrated emergency essential lifesaving healthcare services focusing on the major causes of mortality for conflict-affected and vulnerable IDP, host community and returnee households in Eastern Equatoria and Unity State  . The interventions will include:

Support to static Health facilities in Pairing with medical, particularly on capacity builing in line with the strategies and priorities of the health cluster (Malaria Treatment, Management of children with SAM with medical complications, Clinical Management of Rape and Mental Health Conditions.

project_name: Improve Health of the community in Leer and Mayendit in former Unity State through the provision of quality health services in primary health care centers, primary health care units and mobile clinics.
project_objective:
This project intends to support communities, IDPS, returnees and host communities. It will target total beneficiaries of 10,000 with health care services in static and mobile clinics around five strategic health centers in Leer and Mayendit County. The project aims at assisting and alleviating the suffering of mix of beneficiaries comprising of returnees, IDPS and host communities to prevent diseases in the two counties of Leer and Mayendit. The project will provide medical support to vulnerable members of the community with 5 primary health care centers, 6 primary health care units and 12 mobile clinics services in order to increase health services accessibilities in remote and unreachable part of the two counties. This support is believed to minimize and control the spread of diseases in the communities affected by the conflict that started in December,2013.

According to Coalition for Humanity assessment, which was done in October 2018 on health specific needs in targeted locations in both Leer and Mayendit counties, the report finding confirm that over 60% of the population are in need of health services more so the maternal health and mother child health. In 2019 it is estimated that 50% of the population in the targeted locations in Leer and Mayendit Counties shall have access to health care through this intervention complementing the work UNIDORS is doing across the two counties.

The two Counties of Leer and Mayendit have been the epic centres of the conflict with population completely uprooted from their homes hence unable to access to basic health care services. Few functioning health centers are situated far away from population especially in areas targeted by this project. During the heat of war, health facilities were targeted and destroyed or occupied by the warring parties, which has made things to be started from scratch. The insecurity have further pushed community to more remote villages which were not serviced by partners before hence averagely a mother or child walking distant of three to four hours to access the nearest health center.
The IPC food security report indicates catastrophe phase 5 of the two counties with likelihood of less diet or general eating deficiency caused by limited food.This has health complications especially for children U5, PLW and the elderly.  The source of income especially cattle in these two counties were taken which led to the high rate of malnutrition in children and elderly people. Any minimal health intervention shall integrate basic nutrition and general public health messaging including WASH and Food security and livelihoods to support the vulnerable population in the counties.
 The population in these two counties has gone through highest level of insecurity and conflict, displaced severally from 2016 to late 2018. These forced the communities to live in hard to reach areas or islands for safety. With recently signed peace, community shall return to their homes and influx expected from neighboring counties, POCs and neighboring countries over stretching on the available health services. Therefore it is in this understanding that Coalition for Humanity will focus on PHCC, PHCU and mobile clinics at the targeting locations with highest needs; the project will also give training to local health personnel and community health workers to building on the volunteers that are willing to support or run these centers. Services shall be provided to vulnerable communities in the selected IDPS setting while extending the same to returnees in their new settlements.
The project is expected to address urgent lifesaving medical support in term of supporting the existing facilities or do temporally structure in the host communities concentrating on IDPS sites such as in islands and other hard to reach areas as well as providing basic health service to those started return to their homes.

project_name: Integrated WASH intervention for IDPS, Returnees and Host communities in Koch, Leer, Mayendit and Panyijiar counties of former Unity State.
project_objective:
This project will seek to meet the emergency WASH needs of IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in Koch,Leer,Mayendit and Panyijiar. The total targeted beneficiaries for this project is 11,000 , approximately 1833 HH . The project beneficiaries is further broken down as follows: Women: 4,000 Men: 1500 Girls: 3,000 and boys: 2500. Coalition for Humanity (CH) plans to support in provision of access to safe water, sanitation and Hygiene services in the transitional setting within the target locations. To do this, Coalition for Humanity (CH) will conduct rapid community consultations to specify WASH needs and reconstitute Community Water Committees in targeted payams within the four counties. Aside from this, Coalition for Humanity (CH) will support rehabilitation of protected community wells in at least 9 payams and sensitize the communities on the need to develop latrines and home waste disposal pits. 
To mitigate the widespread GBV risks in the target areas, Coalition for Humanity (CH) will conduct a gender WASH risk assessment in the communities in order to secure access to water and sanitation points that reduce the GBV  risk to women and girls. Coalition for Humanity (CH) will also distribute MHM kits for women and girls  of reproductive ages. 
As internally displaced persons return , there is a likelihood of pressure piling on the limited water and sanitation facilities, creating a risk of water borne diseases. To minimize the potential for this, Coalition for Humanity (CH) will conduct community hygiene promotion by training community hygiene promoters (CHPs), continuously monitor and report on the condition of water points, provide communities with water storage training, treatment tablets and equipment to ensure water available is safe for domestic consumption. 
Coalition for Humanity (CH) will also intervene in the nearby schools (schools within TPA in Leer Town where there is a population of about 4000 IDPS) as well as in 8 primary schools it is supporting in Guat Payam north of leer town and help to establish clubs that champion good hygiene practices. Activities shall include but not limited to supporting parents, teachers and pupils with messaging about washing hands with soap after visiting the toilet and before meals as well as ensuring that the schools are supported to dig latrines, separate for boys and girls. The latrines will have a hand washing point with Water and soap available.

project_name: Lifesaving health care provision for vulnerable population in  Former Lakes State, Western Equatoria State, Unity State
project_objective:
The project will:
1. Improve access to and responsiveness of integrated frontline health services, focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality affecting the most vulnerable groups.

project_name: IRAQ - Norwegian Refugee Council
Community-led Mine Risk Education in support of host community, returnees and IDPs in Duk and Twic East (Jonglei) and Terekeka (Central Equatoria)
project_objective:
The conflicts which have been experienced by the people of South Sudan have made civilians loose life, fight one another, and commit many atrocities. The decades of conflict have seen the land of South Sudan with explosive hazards and many square meters of land have been thought of being contaminated. The exact extent of contaminated area is unknown with large areas in need of survey and clearance even though as UNMAS tries as much as possible to hand safe land back to the community. At the start of 2018, almost six million people in South Sudan were living with the threat of ERW, including more than 1.8 million South Sudanese internally displaced since the outbreak of fighting in 2013. 163,000 of these people are IDPs and host community members from Twic East and Duk (Jonglei) and Terekeka (Central Equatoria).  According to UNMAS, surveys of internally displaced persons identified a fear of ERW as among the most significant reasons for their inability to return home. UNMAS has claimed that the socio-economic cost of mines and ERW in South Sudan in terms of interrupted agricultural production, food insecurity, halted commerce, and the lack of freedom of movement is “incalculable.” In 2017, agricultural production in South Sudan dropped compared with the previous year, attributed in large part to the mass migration of populations and inability to access safe land to cultivate crops (Min Action Monitor South Sudan 24 July 2018). 
The purpose of this project is to help the individuals and communities living in Twic East, Duk and Terekeka to be safe and live a safe life without threats associated with mine/ERWs. The project will benefit 25,000 people (6,000 women, 4,000 men, 8,000 girls, and 7,000 boys) who include IDPs and returnees, and host community) who have a lot of potential in socio-economic activities which can be of benefit to the nation economic building.

In addition to the threats posed to the safety of the community members, explosive hazards prevent the safe movement of the populations including those who must flee active conflict. During such transitions, the most vulnerable groups such as women, children, the elderly and persons with disabilities sometimes lose their lives on the way if the journey takes too long before they finally find a place to settle. Explosive hazards preclude the effective delivery of humanitarian aid and inhibit socioeconomic development activities. Terekeka, Twic East and Duk have critical mine actions needs and mine risk education (MRE) activities will help provide both direct and indirect protection to the community members. MRE activities are key to ensure that people’s behaviour towards unexploded ordinances and ERW within their surrounding change for better. Funds towards mine action projects by other humanitarian actors will also enable individuals return and settle in their previous homes free of any harm and danger.

project_name: Provision of Integrated emergency  mobile health services to IDPs,Returnees and vulnerable host population Wonduruba in Lainya and Panyikang in Upper Nile State

Emergency mobile services will be extended in Wondruba (Lainya County) where only 4 out 10 facilities i.e. Lainya, Wonduruba PHCC, Katigiri PHCC, Moje PHCC and Mengelle PHCC   are functional with minimal health services provided, the rest closed after destruction during conflict

project_name: Shelter and Non Food Items Assistance to Returnees and IDPS in Jonglei State.
project_objective: In the 12 months of 2019 CIDO plans to provide life-saving emergency S/NFI in a safety and dignity to vulnerable populations ( Men women, boys and Girls ), focusing on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees at HH level .The IDPS targeted are those displaced by the protracted political conflict in South Sudan as well as secondary displacements. The project will target female headed households, unaccompanied elderly, people with no links to the community, separated children, women at risk (pregnant and lactating mothers), child-headed HH, people living with disability and returnees assessed and verified to be in need The counties targeted include Duk, Akobo and Ayod counties of Jonglei State. CIDO intends to implement both static ( specifically in Duk county ) and mobile response activities ( Specifically in Akobo and Ayod) with an overall objective of saving lives which would otherwise been lost as a result of protection risks ,exposure to diseases and harsh weather linked to absence of or poor shelter conditions . Through coordination with other partners and multi sector integration of protection component, CIDO will support positive coping mechanisms among beneficiaries and advocate for durable solutions to S/NFI needs. CIDO will prioratirize CBI in Akobo in lieu of the fact that a high influx of returnees are expected to arrive from the border of Ethiopia and the presence of cross country trade. This will also be determined by the market research. The NFI cluster coordination team both at national and state level will be engaged to support the interventions right from assessments, verification, distribution and PDM. The complaint desk at distribution points and the overall feedback and complaint mechanisms to be established will play a key role in providing critical information for CIDO’s M&E team. The project is estimated to cost $163,500

project_name: Provision of timely and equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for conflict affected IDPs/host communities and returnees
project_objective: The DRC mobile response team aims to support the most vulnerable and underserved populations in hard to reach communities affected by conflict. DRC will provide lifesaving WASH services, ensuring adequate and safe access to sanitation and hygiene services, for newly displaced IDPs, returnees and hosting communities in hard to reach locations. In addition, the emergency response aims to strengthen the local government capacity to manage WASH services through training and community participation. DRC will provide gender and disability appropriate emergency WASH service to the displaced IDPs and affected returnees. DRC will provide training of community members to disseminate hygiene message on good hygiene practice and cholera with a greater focus on critical hand washing practice. All responses are led by a protection centred multisector need assessments including detail analysis of WASH that will determine the exact nature of the response. Through this project, DRC will fund a mobile team based in Juba with a rapid response capability to cover various hard to reach and newly affected areas across South Sudan. DRC will prioritize locations prioritized by the cluster and NAWG. By having a mobile team based in Juba DRC will better be placed to support new displacements and spontaneous returns in areas with no WASH actor or areas with limited WASH capacity.  All WASH supplies will be provided by the cluster pipeline and will not be budgeted under the project.  The response missions will be followed by a rapid monitoring exercise during the response mission in hard to reach locations where access is limited to redeploy team for evaluation or post-distribution monitoring. The PDM and the rapid monitoring exercise will highlight any risks associated with DRC’s WASH intervention as well as draw lessons for considerations for future responses. during the rapid monitoring, exercise beneficiaries will be able to provide their opinions on how DRC's and cluster interventions can be improved and they will be given the opportunity to make a complaint. A formal feedback mechanism will be fed through DRC’s hotline whereby complaints or queries may be logged and responded to remotely.

project_name: Emergency provision of WASH services to conflict affected populations of Budi County, Eastern Equatoria State, South Sudan
project_objective:
Protracted Political conflict in South Sudan has rendered many populations in dire need of humanitarian assistance. Since the Break out of violence in 2013, mass displacements of populations has been witnessed internally raising IDP camps across the country. Many other people have crossed borders to the neighboring countries. 
The conflict has seen mass destruction of the  basic infrastructure and WASH facilities have not been left out. 
There has been lack of essential wash facilities like latrines and water points leading to people resorting to taking untreated and contaminated water from the rivers and earth dams. Open defecation due to lack of latrines has seen the existing water points being contaminated with human waste. This has seen the rise of waterborne disease outbreaks with the latest outbreak of cholera being reported in April 2017 according to WHO situational analysis of April 2017.
Gender based violence and cases of sexual abuse have been reported in Budi County and can be attributed to lack of latrine facilities. Women and Girls tend to relieve themselves in the bushes therefore exposing them to danger of gender based violence and sexual abuse.
Health Facilities and nutrition sites in Budi County lack clean water for drinking and for use. Mothers of the malnourished children use unclean containers to draw unclean water for use. This has increased the disease burden to the already vulnerable populations.
This Project will ensure that the latrines are rehabilitated and others are constructed to ensure that the water points are not contaminated and therefore reduce the cases of water borne disease outbreaks.
The project will also ensure that latrines are segregated and that they have locks to ensure that women and school going children are safe as they use the facilities.
Women and school going children will be supported with menstrual hygiene kits to ensure that their dignity is well preserved.  School going children who miss school and fail to participate in recreational activities during the  menstrual days will be able to interact freely with other people without fear and will also be able to attend school without fear.
The project will also ensure that there is provision of clean drinking water for use to the required standards of 15 liters per day per person by ensuring that new boreholes are dug, and others are rehabilitated to meet the needs of the community.
Water management committees will be formed to ensure that they take ownership of the water points and ensure that the water points are secure and are not contaminated.
Community engagement will be done to ensure that the beneficiaries identify the needs and that they are involved in the implementation of the project.

project_name: Provision of Integrated & Sustainable, Adequate and Improved access to WASH facilities for vulnerable and affected populations in South Sudan (Jonglei : Ayod, Twic East & Pibor, Central Equatoria :Juba and Eastern Equatoria : Ikotos.
project_objective:
According to Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), an estimated 5,712,000 South Sudanese women, men and children will not have access to adequate water, sanitation and hygiene in 2019.  GBI seeks to provide a 12 months Integrated & Sustainable, Adequate and Improved access to WASH facilities for vulnerable and affected populations in South Sudan (Jonglei : Ayod, Twic East & Pibor, Central Equatoria :Juba and Eastern Equatoria: Ikotos. In line with the call by the WASH cluster and the 2019 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), GBI is proposing to scale up an integrated WASH response in these locations through supporting existing nutrition sites, health centres and schools’ sanitation, hygiene and water facilities as well as rehabilitation of dysfunctional ones and passing on critical messages. The project will support a total of 13,500 beneficiaries (men, women, boys and girls) targeted directly with lifesaving WASH and Nutrition interventions, along with sanitation and hygiene promotion activities at household level. The project will target IDPs, Host communities, Returnees and other vulnerable members of the community that may not fall under these categories, broken down as (3645, 5400, 3720 and 735 respectively). 

The overall objective of this project is to contribute to the reduction of mortality, morbidity and impacts of acute malnutrition due to poor sanitation and hygiene amongst children under five and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) through management of acute malnutrition as well as building their resilience. This project is designed to reduce vulnerabilities and risk associated with the current food insecurity and poor WASH conditions in the proposed counties, and it also will complement existing WASH, Health and Nutrition activities that implementing partners are doing in the proposed counties. Increase access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for all, paying attention to the needs of malnourished children, women, adolescent girls and those in vulnerable situation. The project will require $ 445,000 to provide the intended services and activities throughout the intervention period.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Primary Health Care Services to the people in need in Juba, Magwi, Bor South, Panyikan, Baliet and Ikwoto of South Sudan through the delivery of emergency lifesaving health care services
project_objective:
This projects aims to reach 40,155 beneficiaries, 20,238 male and 19,917 female in 6 Counties of Juba, Bor South, Panyikan, Magwi, Baliet and Ikwoto in 2019. Health Link intents to achieve 20.9% of the Cluster target in the selected Counties (Bor South, Panyikan, Magwi, Ikwoto and Baliet and Juba Counties.  In line with the Cluster Objectives, Health Link will implement specific activities under the service delivery areas below;   
1.	 Improving Access and Scale -Up of Responsiveness
-	 HLSS will set up 4 Mobile Clinics that will be manage by 4 Mobile Teams– 1 in Juba, 1 in Bor South, 1 in Panyikan and 1 in Magwi. Each team will conduct integrated mobile outreach at least once every week.
-	Health Link intents to Support 4 Primary Health Care Centres. 2 in Bor South (Bor PoC and Werkok PHCC), 1 in Juba (Rokon PHCC) and 1 in Magwi (Pajok PHCC). 8 PHCUs across the selected Counties and 2 Hospitals, Bor State Hospital and Al-Sabbah Children Hospital.
-	Participate in 3 RRMs along with the HC Partners

project_name: Emergency WASH support to IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Unity, Lakes and Western Equatoria States.
project_objective:

HACO works in the locations of Unity, Lakes and Western Equatoria with bases in the counties of Rubkona, Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Mayom and Panijiar (Unity State), Yirol East (Lakes) and Yambio, Tombura and Maridi (Western Equatoria).  Dire WASH needs have been observed in the locations targeted, mainly as a result of displacements, communal violence and lack of WASH infrastructure in majority of the locations. The project seeks to provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees. With protection at centrality of the implementation, WASH related GBV will be mitigated through WASH specific activities tailored for GBV mitigation.  
The chronic persistence of malnutrition in the areas targeted has been traced to poor WASH standards, resulting in AWDs. The project will further provide WASH in nutrition minimum package of intervention for famine prevention, mainly at the OTP/SC. 
Provision of WASH services as a public health strategy to avoid occurrence of epidemics, or at the occurrence of epidemics to avoid spread is planned. The areas targeted are all disease prone, having experienced previous outbreaks of cholera, and some neighbouring Ebola stricken Democratic Republic of Congo. 

The target group consists of IDPs, vulnerable host communities and returnees. A total of 12,120 people are targeted with SPHERE standard WASH services, 48% of these female. 60% of the beneficiaries planned for are from Unity State, 30% in WES and 10% in Lakes. 56% of these are IDPs, 32% host communities, 12% returnees and other groups. 57% of the WASH component shall be centred around safe and clean water supply at household, community and institutional level, 43% on Sanitation with all beneficiaries receiving support in hygiene promotion.

project_name: Nutrition and Infant Young Child Feeding services in Northern Syria.
project_objective: Across northern Syria, some governorates, including Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir Ez Zor, have the some of the highest ranking of severity of Nutrition needs, according to the WoS Nutrition sector (Humanitarian Needs Overview, 2018). SC offers increased access to quality Health and Nutrition services and knowledge to children and their families. A detailed analysis of the Nutrition situation inside Syria remains largely unconfirmed, due to the long-term insecurity; inaccessibility; and lack of Nutrition responders, who have the capacity to undergo timely and quality representative Nutrition surveys to provide a clear picture of the needs on the ground. With the exception of Idlib, the Ministry of Health has approved a series of SMART surveys to be rolled out across Syria in 2019, including areas within Northeast Syria (NES), to collect representative data on acute malnutrition. Despite the lack of adequate data, one recent SMART survey conducted in Tel Abyad District in Raqqa Governorate (June, 2018), and reinforced by monthly data from the Nutrition sector surveillance system (collected at health facility level) shows a Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate of 2.1% - categorized as “low” according to WHO. The rate reflects similar GAM rates in other areas of Syria over recent years. The stunting rate is alarmingly high (32%), reflecting chronic malnutrition over a sustained period of time. The Raqqa SMART survey recommended to scale up Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) programmes. In September 2018, the Nutrition surveillance in Raqqa found that out of 4,102 children screened (aged 6-59 months), 281 children were identified with Severe Acute Malnutrition and 98 children were identified with Moderate Acute Malnutrition. Apart from IYCF messages delivered by humanitarian actors, SC is currently providing the only IYCF services that go beyond messages with 1-1 counselling and follow up. Continuing and scaling up infant and young child feeding support is fundamental to the overall nutrition response in Syria. Agencies and Health practitioners in NES in particular lack appropriate skills and knowledge to support caregivers with appropriate infant feeding interventions. Capacity strengthening of all responders in IYCF is essential to the Nutrition response inside Syria. Moreover, the need to build capacity and integrate PSS skilled support into feeding counselling is especially needed to provide additional support during feeding counselling, as well as refer caregivers for specialized services if needed. Data concerning IYCF is also lacking inside Syria, and currently relies on anecdotal evidence, observations, key informant interviews, and data in other areas of Syria. In 2018, SC completed an IYCF baseline assessment in South Syria to help better inform the IYCF programme that was supported by a previous OFDA grant. The survey revealed very low exclusive breastfeeding rates (only 3% and 6% in two areas) and poor breastfeeding patterns in relation to frequency. Artificial feeding was high (93% and 76%), with the majority of mothers mixed feeding. Bottle feeding was common and most caregivers cited ‘breastfeeding difficulties’ as the reason for the cessation of breastfeeding. Overall, the dietary diversity was poor, and although there was high consumption of certain individual foods groups (dairy; eggs; tubers; grains), it did not equate to an adequate diverse diet. In Northern Syria, it is expected that IYCF practices are just as poor. The numerous requests by caregivers seeking infant formula for their infants indicates that assessment and urgent protection of the non-breastfed child needs attention, as they are even more vulnerable in emergencies. Barriers to appropriate infant feeding need to be investigated further during IYCF counselling and to provide guidance and support on achieving appropriate dietary diversity as well as improve exclusive breastfeeding, as both are life-saving feeding practices.

project_name: Provision of emergency life-saving health interventions for vulnerable and underserved populations in Panyijiar county
project_objective:
The overall health situation in South Sudan continues to deteriorate, especially in conflict-affected and seasonally hard-to-reach areas due to persistent drought, continued insecurity and other underlying factors. This project will strive to address emergency health needs of marginalized and underserved communities in Panyijiar which includes Ganyliel and Nyal payams with an aim of targeting 19,847 people (25% of 79,388 - the population in Panyijiar). The project aims at improving access and utilization of integrated primary healthcare services, including reproductive health and immunization coverage through support of static facilities with mobile response. Mobile service delivery will concentrate in areas not currently served by static facilities, thus increasing access to health services for marginalized communities. The IRC has been one of the largest providers of aid in South Sudan, delivering emergency relief and post-conflict assistance for over 25 years.
IRC is supporting healthcare services in Panyijar. Under the proposed program, two static facilities (a Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) and a Primary Health care unit in Nyal) and two mobile teams (one  in Nyal, one in Ganyliel) will be supported. Each mobile team will be composed of one Clinical Officer, one Nurse, one Community Health Worker (CHW), one Maternal and Child Health Worker (MCHW), one Drug Dispenser, one Card Registrar and one EPI vaccinator. The Clinical Officer and the Nurse will be delivering health care services to patients while the CHW will be involved in health awareness, case identification and referral in the community. CHWs will also conduct community dialogues to identify key health issues in communities. Community dialogues will target different age groups within the communities and at different times. Critical patients attending the mobile clinics and pregnant women with obstetric complications will be referred and managed at the PHCC. Pregnant women in need of Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmONC) will be referred from the PHCC in Nyal to the IRC-run Reproductive Health Unit in Ganyliel. These facilities are supported through HPF funds except Nyal PHCC.
Support for Nyal PHCC and PHCU under this program may include, but not be limited to recruitment, payment and training of healthcare workers, provision of essential equipment and supplies, and regular supportive supervision. The CHW will be involved in identifying vulnerable and needy community members with other non-communicable diseases including mental health needs and referring them to the nearest point of care. The IRC will integrate prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) of HIV/AIDS and syphilis testing during antenatal care (ANC) visits .All HIV positive cases detected during PMTCT services will be recorded and referred appropriately.
Gender-based violence is linked to a variety of negative health outcomes for women, including severe reproductive and maternal health consequences, like unintended pregnancies, abortions, maternal and neonatal mortality. This program will provide services to GBV survivors through a survivor-centred approach where the survivor’s rights, needs, and wishes are prioritized and respected at all times. A key means to addressing these issues is the support of functional referral systems and training of health providers, ensuring privacy and confidentiality. The expected increase in service provision is likely to increase the amount of waste, mostly sharps. Facilities have sharps boxes, and the 2 major referral facilities have adequate final disposal systems for infectious waste. IRC will ensure that all facilities dispose of sharps and other waste correctly and guidelines are in place and followed. This will also be integrated into supervision support. The mobile team’s medical waste will be taken to the nearest PHCU for incineration, while non-medical waste is disposed of as appropriate.

project_name: Facilitating Assistance to Syria Together (FAST)
project_objective:
SAMS in this project is part of FAST Consortium. Through this project, SAMS in collaboration with consortium members are prioritizing the reduction of morbidity and mortality through improving the access to quality-health care (primary and secondary health facilities, mobile clinics) in 20 health facilities in Aleppo, Idleb and Hama. 

In order to achieve this objective, SAMS will work on supporting the HFs. SAMS will provide recruitment support, capacity building, and ongoing medical supervision to ensure the HFs are staffed with qualified medical personnel and to enhance compliance with standard treatment protocols. Guided by the Do No Harm principle, these initiatives are aimed at ensuring safe, high quality health care for beneficiaries and investing in local capacities and sustainability at the same time. SAMS will continue to provide training to the HFs on a variety of topics, including management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, pharmaceutical supply management, patient data management, and sexual and reproductive health (RH), gender-sensitivity and protection. As per the Essential Primary Health Services Package adopted by the Health Cluster, SAMS will provide the following services: reproductive health services (ante-natal care, post-natal care, family planning, normal deliveries, gynecological consultations, and clinical management of rape), integrated management for child illness, vaccines, prevention and control for communicable and non-communicable diseases, nutrition, MHGAP, health awareness, and basic laboratory and radiology services. 
Services at the secondary health care level will include gynecologic surgeries and caesarian sections, trauma management, major surgeries, hospitalization services, blood transfusion, and intensive care unit. 

FAST partners will continue to coordinate with other health actors through the Health Cluster, Nutrition Cluster and the NGO forum where routine data is gathered and shared through the 4Ws and HERAMS. FAST partners are also coordinating with other humanitarian actors at the field level to assess the needs, strengthen referral pathways, and respond to emergencies, among other ways. Moreover, SAMS and the FAST consortium will closely coordinate to share information about needs, ensure an effective and coordinated response to new emergencies, harmonize the salary scales and staffing structures across HFs, coordinate on immunization campaigns, and verify the quality of pharmaceuticals donated.

project_name: Facilitating Assistance to Vulnerable Syrians In Idleb, Aleppo and Hama (Provision of life-saving services to conflict-affected populations in Northwest Syria, including health care, MHPSS and Physical Rehabilitation)
project_objective:
Syrians have been exposed to extreme levels of violence and have often lost loved ones, livelihoods, and homes, which can cause significant deterioration of one’s mental health. Today many Syrians suffer from mental health and psychosocial (MHPSS) disorders, such as dysthymia and bipolar disorder, yet lack the required treatment due to the limited availability of services. Mental health disorders are increasing substantially, affecting millions of traumatized people; 1 out of 5 Syrians suffer from a mental disorder. 

Moreover, the war in Syria has permanently disabled thousands of people. Conflict-related injuries, psychological stress, lack of primary health care services, and poor management of chronic conditions have severely affected people with disabilities. Specialized care and well-trained professional health workers are required in order to provide suitable services. As the conflict continues and the number of injured people rises, increasing the capacity to deliver long-term rehabilitative care is a must.  Because health facilities have been targeted, Northern Syria is left with few physical rehabilitation centers. These centers are in dire need of support to operate, train and build capacity for local health workers, thereby increasing the quality of services provided. Based on the aforementioned information and situational context, there is an urgent need to implement a comprehensive program that provides life-saving MHPS and physical rehabilitation services and enhances healthcare personnel’s capacity to overcome major health care limitations in Northern Syria.

This project aims to provide life-saving services to conflict-affected populations in Northwest Syria whereas the project has 3 primary goals: 

• To provide life-saving services to conflict-affected populations in Northwest Syria including health care (primary, secondary and trauma) through:
1: Provide primary health care consultations to IDPs and the host community
2: Provide trauma services, including minor and major surgeries, to IDPs and host communities
3: Provide the needed medications, supplies and equipment to maintain the hospital

• To reduce the prevalence of mental health, psychological disorders and functional limitations of people affected by the conflict in Northwest Syria 
This objective will target 11 health facilities. Two Psychosocial Support Workers (PSSWs) will be hired in each facility to provide PS services within the facilities. PSSWs will also conduct outreach activities in communities to provide services to vulnerable groups unable to reach the facilities. Three team leaders will coordinate the workload for all 22 PSSWs. SAMS will strive to mainstream gender in each team. PSSWs will be trained on guidelines produced by the technical group of the health cluster, according to a methodology endorsed by WHO, in addition to other relevant training.

project_objective:

This includes improving women and young and adolescent girls access to obstetric care to reduce the maternal and new-born morbidities and mortalities in conflict-affected areas in northwest Syria. Emphasis will also be on family planning activities and awareness raising strategies aiming at reducing unwanted pregnancies.

SAMS will accomplish these targets by sustaining the provision of services through its four facilities (Maternity Specialized Hospital CEmONC and  Kafr Diryan BEmONC in Idleb district - Tarmala Hospital CEmONC in Al Ma'ra District in rural Idleb and Southern Rural Aleppo Mobil Clinic in Jebel Sama’an district in rural Aleppo) by supporting it with operational costs and ensuring all needed medications, medical consumables and lab supplies, are provided and available for the treatment of patients inside Syria, also SAMS will continue its efforts in building the capacities of the medical personnel on reproductive health protocols and family planning in coordination with UNFPA, it’s worth mentioning that SAMS supported facilities need for 612 RH Kits per year . This project aims to structure the medical education process inside NWS by meeting the different and increasing needs for Midwives. This medical educational program like this was established and
supported by SAMS through the past year and are crucial to addressing the gap in SR Health Care Workers in Syria. This program objective is to provide and secure Syrian civilians with quality health care staff, enhance the livelihoods for medical workers, and work to develop health services and a future workforce for Syria through supporting Midwifery Education in NWS, by implementing two modules of the Midwifery
Training Program due to the strategy which was developed by the SRH-TWG

Moreover, and through this project, SAMS will continue to support Midwifery Education in two locations in Idleb – Al Mara’a located in southern Idleb and Termanin in the north, by implementing a two-year midwifery training program. In Al Mara’a, specialized courses will be held at the institutional arm of the Al Salam hospital and in Termanin, the courses will be held at Atmah Hospital, Al Ferdous Hospital in Darat Ezah and Aleman hospital in Orem. Because the training will take place in hospitals, the program will adhere to standards as defined by the Ministry of Health in addition to the international standards
of midwifery training strategy produced by the reproductive health technical working group in the Health Cluster.

Finally, the project will aim to launch a nursing program that will extend for 2 years
categorized as follow:
- First and Second Academic Year:
- 2 semesters extending for 14 weeks each, followed by 2 weeks of examination periods  
- Summer semester extending for a month and comprised of a clinical training

project_name: Provision of Physiotherapy and MHPSS Services to Assist Victims in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The Survivors of explosive accidents, their families and communities need specialised services to reduce the impact of explosive hazard. 
In order to reduce the immediate threat and long-term impact from explosive hazards to at-risk communities, SAMS through this project will work on achieving the following objectives:
1.	Provide physiotherapy/rehabilitation care to the survivors in Termanin center
2.	Provide MHPSS services to the survivors and their families in Alnafs Almotma’ena facility

project_name: Provision of Integrated GBV Services in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
According to SAMS strategy in integrating GBV services within all SAMS health facilities and supporting the Women and girl’s safe spaces, SAMS through this project aims to Provide support to survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, as well as their extended networks (families, communities, relief workers, care providers, and civil society), in Northwest Syria.

Through achieving the following objectives:

Objective 1: Improve the access to specialized quality GBV services in the health facilities, will be achieved through:

1.2	Provide GBV programming for adolescent girls through group discussions, activities and distribution of IEC materials within 16 health facilities in north west Syria.

2.2	Provision of Awareness Raising activities aims to aware the women and girls from some topics including (GBV, Reproductive Health, and Family Planning)

Objective 3: Build the capacity of the Service Providers will be achieved through:
