project_name: People of Iraq Building Back: Integrating Systems for WASH and Child Protection in unversed Hard to Reach Places in Iraq
project_objective:
This project seeks to capitalize on the capacities and local presence of each consortium member: Leading this consortium is Mission East, an international NGO, working in Iraq in 2003 and again since 2014 until now. Mission East has a strong presence in Kirkuk and Ninewa. ME has implemented a livelihoods/food security  project in Ninewa for 2 years,. ME has mobile case management  teams (WPU) handling GBV and (FPU) handling CP cases. ME operate multipurpose community centres and strengthens capacity of community protection structures, such as local grassroots and volunteer groups of women and youth. ME has been providing comprehensive WASH services to more than 20 villages since 2016. ME has an environmental policy in which Water conservation and environmental awareness is central to WASH programming.
Mercy Hands is Iraq's biggest national NGO with a country wide presence. Established in 2003, Mercy Hands has projects in most of the governorates of Iraq. Relevant to this project MH have offices and activities in Tikrit, Mosul, Baghdad and Erbil. They have strong multi-sector capacities, with experience in: Food security, livelihoods, WASH, CP, GBV, Education, NFI, health centres, legal assistance and cash transfer.  
The Critical Needs Support Foundation (CNSF) is a rapidly growing national NGO which specializes in Shelter, WASH and cash transfer responses. CNSF conducts multiple cash transfer projects across Ninewa, for various sectors. CNSF targets marginalized communities especially in Ninewa. CNSF have completed a successful WASH project in Mosul which included distributing hygiene kits, water trucking to 6500 households and installation of water tanks at 26 schools. CNSF have a strong presence in Ninewa and Anbar, they have a country office in Erbil and Baghdad. 
This consortium will adopt a harmonized approach across two governorates, integrating six activities from two sectors in each location to deliver an integrated programme addressing some of the root causes of the vulnerability of families. This is designed to build on each organization's strengths and experience in Iraq with a specific focus on localization, following Mission East’s strategy for the coming 3 years to build the capacity of national NGO and local volunteer groups. 
In each target location a fully integrated double-sector response will be implemented in targeted, rural and per-urban, under-served returnee locations. WASH and Child Protection (CP) will be holistically addressed. The program is designed to provide synergies between the sectorial responses to support returnee needs in a rounded and comprehensive way.  This will be implemented through pre-existing community protection structures which will be trained to support child protection services including parenting skills training. In all locations mobile child protection case management teams will operate alongside outreach teams who will deliver multi-sector key messaging, covering topics on hygiene promotion, water conservation and child protection. Parenting skills packages will be delivered in each target location with the support of pre-existing community groups. This integrated package will be implemented in under-served returnee locations between Samara district, Sinjar and Telafar,. Targeting a total of 9,000 people.

project_name: Early Recovery response Zimbabwe
project_objective:
The project’s overall objective is to enable early recovery and enhance the resilience of at-risk smallholder farmers and households in rural and urban areas so that they are food, income and nutrition secure in the face of increasing multiple and chronic shocks and stressors.
This will also protect the development gains achieved and yet to be achieved in the implementation of a various personal and development initiatives, ensuring that they do not lose their assets, livestock and/or crops.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood assistance for vulnerable families in Syria.
project_objective:
The project aims to provide a wide-ranging support from emergency to regular food assistance as well as household based agricultural and livelihoods assistance. The project aims to target populations who are both food insecure as well as at risk of food insecurity through multiple but mutually reinforcing activities. 
The project will contribute to the following two objectives of Food security cluster:

Objective 1: Improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance.
Objective 2: Support self reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives.

A total of 30,000 households (150,000 individuals) will be supported through multiple but integrated activities. 

Under first objective for life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance, the project will aim to meet the immediate food needs and also seasonal/supplementary food assistance. The Emergency Response will aim to reach crisis-affected people within 72 hours of the onset of a crisis to cover a minimum of one to four weeks of their immediate food needs through short-term support such as Ready-to-Eat Rations, cooked meals and/or baked bread. 
Baked bread will also be provided to the displaced families living in the camps. this will help to stabilize the market prices. 
further supplementary food assistance will be provided to improve the dietary diversity. such as Ramadan food distribution and Qurbani meat distribution. 

under the objective 2, appropriate agricultural inputs (cereal as well as vegetable production) will be provided along with technical capacity building at household-level to ensure that most vulnerable farming households receive timely inputs as per seasonal calendar to be able to produce and contribute to domestic production requirements. further asset building and asset protection support mainly for livestock keepers and poultry will be provided. This include but not limited to provision of EWE sheep, poultry feed, and vaccination. 

Finally, individuals including youth and people with disability will also be targeted for small scale income generation activities. such as barber shop, female saloon, grocery store etc. 
Local procurement will be encouraged to promote local markets, especially where markets have the capacity to absorb such demands. 
This objective also aim to restore and strengthen productive assets and create livelihood opportunities for the targeted populations, thus contributing to the overall food production and subsequently to food availability in Syria.

project_name: Improving access to malaria diagnosis and treatment for IDPs in Bentiu and Malakal PoC.
project_objective: Our programme aims to reduce the burden of malaria in highly in the highly vulnerable IDP population by delivering malaria testing and treatment to those living in Benitu and Malakal PoC with the aim of improving preparedness and response especially after an increase in transmission (usually after the rains). Malakal has a population of 24,402 residents and there are 114,683 residents in Bentiu and there are 4 and 5 sectors in each camp respectively. Through this programme, 139,085 IDPs will receive access to life saving treatment. Malaria agents will work in each sector of the camp providing malaria testing. All uncomplicated cases will be treated in the first instance and more severe cases will be referred to the health facility in the camp. All pregnant women will also be offered preventative therapy. In additional, comprehensive IEC messages will be delivered to all residents. These will focus on the promotion of LLIN use, ownership, and maintenance, messages on regularly emptying, and cleaning unsealed water containers on a weekly basis campaigns to emphasise the importance of ANC attendance to improve IPTp uptake,  promotion of early treatment seeking behaviours and drug adherence.

project_name: WASH support for the needy families in Northern Syria
project_objective:
The ongoing escalation of conflict in various parts of Syria is causing a continuous high influx of IDP in various safer locations in Northern Syria. Majority of these IDP are living in the settlements, makeshift camps or formal camps. The existing water and sanitation system in Northern Syria are overstretched. With the huge influx of IDP maintaining existing WASH facilities and upgrading to cope with the increasing demands of at risk population is urgently required. This will ensure that people can full fill their basic water, sanitation and hygiene needs and risk of diseases and environmental degradation is minimized. Through the proposed project, IR Syria aims to support those who are in need for wash assistance. 88,000 people will benefit from improved access to water and sanitation facilities. The project is primarily designed based on Humanitarian Need overview 2019. The project will support the formal and informal settlements as well as well host communities with core WASH services.
The activities included in this proposal are in line with the WASH cluster objective which is support to water, sanitation and sewage systems to ensure continuous services for affected people in Syria and deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services to most vulnerable people. IRW prioritizes WASH support interventions for the conflict affected population in the target location to enhance beneficiaries’ resilience in coping with ongoing crisis through the provision of access to clean water as well as supporting them in cleaning the wash facilities in a clean and healthy environment. Below will be the intended activities to achieve the project objectives:
1. Adequate quality and quantity of water: Water supply will ensure through water trucking. IR will sign an agreement with a contractor to supply water to the targeted camps on daily basis (23 L per person will be provided on daily basis). This water will be sufficient to cover the drinking, bathing and household need of the individuals. If required by the targeted families, IR will also distribute Jerry cans. This will be contributed by IR. 
2. Water testing and treatment (chlorination): IR team will conduct water testing and chlorination before it is available for use by the beneficiaries. This will help to eliminate the risk of using contaminated water.
3. Waste removal service (solid waste management): Through a service provider (contractor) IR will ensure to collect the garbage from the camps and deport it to the agreed damp sites on daily basis. This will improve the overall environment and decrease the risk of diseases spread. IR will also place garbage bins 
4. Operation and maintenance of sanitation facilities: Sanitation facilities (latrines and bathing areas) will be gender segregated and will have protection measures this will be considered during the regular maintenance of the facilities (lockable doors, lighting of paths to facilities).

project_name: Provision of Emergency shelters and Non- food items to the most conflict affected communities of Canal, Fangak, Maiwut, Nasir, Pigi, and Uror counties of Jonglei, Upper Nile
project_objective:
The country is turned to a police state where unknown gunmen, arbitrary arrest, eliminations enhanced by economic collapse are the order of the day but cannot be spoken off as required or one risk being call anti-government. As the country yearn to return to stability, Canal (Pigi), Fangak, Maiwut, Nasir, and Uror counties will reverse gear to become the hubs of return and repatriation routes from the refugees and IDPs camps as they have served the exit routes to refugee and reception camps. 

While the guns might be silent countrywide and despite the country becoming independent in 2011, the issues of tribal violence mostly perpetrated by youth have not been address well, especially between the communities. Exacerbated by dismal function of lack of law enforcement institutions, coupled with unruly armed youth, and the impeded traditional leadership and customary law, communal revenges over past killings, cattle rustling between communities, clan feuds, etc remained potential threats to many lives and a genuine concern to the at risk communities. There is therefore a need for an increased effort to reverse this practice because these challenges threaten peaceful co-existence and create fearful living among communities and so are daring concerned to the returning and IDPs communities. Now that the countdown to the implementation of the signed peace agreement began with the colorful celebration yesterday here in Juba, the next question comes forth. The need surely will be enormous with regard to the return, repatriation and reintegration of those in and outside of the country and the vulnerable host community. 

Currently South Sudan government and the humanitarian agencies will engaged in a concerted return, repatriation and resettlement of 4 million refugees and 1.76 million internally displaced person back home to start a new life. This brings the total of conflict displaced persons to over 5.7 million. Humanitarian reports indicate that women and girls are the most vulnerable and at risk of SGBV, according to the protection trends as of April 2017, therefore, gender-based violence (GBV) and its related effect remained the most serious and prevalent protection threats to women and girls in South Sudan. Other forms of sexual violence, abductions and possible sexual slavery, forced and early marriage and harmful traditional practices are major concerns still haunting communities amid strides and strings. 
A partner in NFIs though outside of S/NFI cluster, Nile Hope has been distributing NFIs since 2016 and is added shelters construction for returned IDPs in 2018. It has since served 9,000 Households from Akobo, Fangak, Pochalla and Uror counties with NFIs in the course of its partnership with UNHCR. This year too, Nile Hope engaged in shelter construction for the 251 individual IDPs UNHCR voluntarily repatriated from Bor PoC to New Fangak. 
Partnering with S/NFIs cluster, Nile Hope will further services provisions to the most IDPs, returnees and the host community of Canal, Nasir and Maiwut Counties. And through partnership with S/NFIs cluster, Nile Hope intends to complement its UNHCR supported services Uror County mostly the southern part: Yuai, Weikol, Pamai, Padiek, Panyok and Pajut. In Fangak, Nile Hope will extends its services to the South, Central and western part of the county including Old Fangak, Toch and Juaibor areas. This will avoid overlaps and duplication of services mostly in New Fangak areas to the north and also in areas of Pieri, Motot, Pulchuol, Pathay and Karam of Uror counties. Nile Hope therefore, applies to the cluster for both Shelter (cash) and NFIs (in-kind) to support live saving programming and promote resilience of the 20,000 needy communities across the toward total resettlement and support of the IDPs, returnees, refugees and the vulnerable at risk.

project_name: Supporting the quality reproductive healthcare provision through supporting of a midwifery institution in Atmeh village, Dana sub district, Harim district, Idleb governorate.

project_name: Humanitarian aid for vulnerable Rohingya communities in Cox’s Bazar in the sectors of WASH, Protection, Food Security and Nutrition
project_objective: Integrated multi-sectorial project of a consortium of Alliance2015 partner agencies in Cox's Bazar lead by Concern Worldwide with Alliance2015 partners ACTED and Welthungerhilfe working on WASH hardware and software components targeting refugee and host populations in Teknaf.

project_name: Education in Emergencies Support Project targeting Most Vulnerable Children (Girls and Boys), Men and Women including  Youth in former Lakes, Jonglei and Western Bahr el Ghazal States, South Sudan
project_objective:
The Education Cluster estimates at least 2,808,000 girls and boys between 3-18 years of age in conflict and crisis affected areas are estimated to not have access to pre-school, primary and secondary education in 2019; and at least 42,902 teachers/ volunteers and members of school management committees are in need of humanitarian assistance as they are crucial to deliver education services during emergencies. 

Peace Corps Organization (PCO) proposes to implement this project in Jonglei, Lakes and Western Bahr el Ghazal States. The project will be aimed at increasing access to inclusive and protective lifesaving education (formal and non-formal) for children and youth affected by emergencies, improving the quality of education to ensure continuity of relevant education services for children and youth in emergencies and strengthening the response capacity of communities and education actors to mitigate the impact of emergencies on children and youth (2019 Education Cluster Strategy). This will be achieved through establishment and rehabilitation temporary learning spaces and classrooms, establishment and rehabilitation of gender segregated latrines and water points and hygiene promotion, provision of school-aged children with fortified school meals/take home ration, provision of emergency-affected children with quality education and recreational materials, equipping of teachers with EiE skills to provide an improved teaching and learning experience, training and capacity building of Educators, community members and authorities on psychosocial support and equipping SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management and governance (2019 Education Cluster Strategy). 

The project will support to children and communities facing unprecedented levels of malnutrition, protection, water-borne/ related diseases as a result of cyclic waves of conflict and seasonal flooding by targeting 3,600 beneficiaries comprised of 1,500 girls, 1,500 boys, 300 men and 300 women – includes people with special needs and youth amongst host and IDP communities in areas whilst coordinating with counterpart agencies working in Nutrition/health/FSL/protection sectors. Another key objective is to put in place actions to reduce/prevent incidences of GBV, sexual violence and other protection matters facing thousands of girls, boys, women and men. Cross cutting issues including protection, GBV, HIV/AIDs, Accountability to Affected Populations, protection, gender equity, environmental conservation and youth engagement will be mainstreamed at all stages of the project.

Peace Corps Organization, which has been operational in the proposed areas since 2006 has competent and experienced technical teams and relevant office space in Wau, Pibor, Rumbek and logistics, warehousing facilities; and strong grass root networks that can be easily deployed, including staff redeployment to proposed areas for scale up interventions.

project_name: Lifesaving Emergency WASH Support programme for the most vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities in Western Bahr El Ghazal, Lakes and Jonglei States
project_objective:
The project will support to communities facing unprecedented levels of malnutrition, water-borne/ related diseases as a result of cyclic waves of conflict and seasonal flooding by targeting 24,000
beneficiaries comprised of 7500 girls, 7500 boys, 4500 men and 4500 women – includes people with special needs and youth amongst host and IDP communities in areas where counterpart agencies in Education are providing school feeding program including health centers where nutritional IYC feeding is undertaken by other agencies working in Nutrition/health sectors. Another key objective is to put in place actions to reduce/prevent incidences of GBV, sexual violence and other protection matters facing thousands of women and girls as they undertake their care-giving roles and responsibilities.

These will be undertaken by working closely with schools implementing school feeding programme and partners providing nutrition and health support by rehabilitating water and sanitation facilities(including hand washing), distribution of relevant NFIs and intensive hygiene promotion/cholera preparedness actions. 

In addition 100 men, 100 women, 100 boys and 100 girls will be identified to work as volunteers
to support the provision of life-saving, time-critical WASH support in the targeted locations. The wider community will be reached indirectly through community awareness campaigns and messaging. 

Cross cutting issues including protection, GBV, HIV/AIDs, Accountability to Affected Populations, protection, gender equity, environmental conservation and youth engagement will be mainstreamed at all stages of the project.

PCO has been operational since 2006 in Jonglei Western Bahr el Ghazal and Lakes through UNICEF among other donors and runs the WASH core-pipeline in Pibor in addition to supporting coordination roles across the three states.  The organization has experienced technical teams and relevant coordination offices in Pibor, Wau and Rumbek towns, with logistics, warehousing facilities and strong grass root networks that can be easily deployed, including staff redeployment to proposed areas for scale up interventions.

project_name: Provide life-saving shelter and life-sustaining non-food items to the most vulnerable newly displaced population, returnees, host community in an efficient and effective manner in Central Equatoria Yei and Lakes State in Yirol East, Rumbek North and Rumbek Centre.
project_objective:
Yirol East county is located in the southern part of former Lakes State. The county has seven Payams with an estimated population of 112,0931. The population of Yirol East County practice farming, livestock keeping and fishing for their livelihood and land dispute and cattle raiding. The IPC of February 2018 projected that between May and July 2018, Yirol East would be in emergency phase (IPC level 4. In March and April 2018 there has been a high influx of IDPs (reportedly to be around 28,000 people) in Yirol East County. Their original home area is in Maper county (part of Rumbek North).  The IDPs were displaced as a result of boarder and Land disputes. From several payams in Rumbek North County, including Alor, Madol, Malueth, Maper, Meen and Wurieng whose Properties were also destroyed to the extend you can even observe some undressed women and children. In Yei Central Equatoria State an inter-agency team compressing of eleven humanitarian agencies visited Mugwo County, about 23 kilometers south of Yei town to assess the situation of large influx of people that fled conflicts in Kenyira and surrounding area of Mugwo county in October 2018. Two UN agencies and Nine NGOs participated in the assessment. They include UN OCHA, IOM, TDH, ACROSS, AAH-I, CEFORD, UMCOR, IPCS, SSDO, CAHO and ARD-African. According to assessment report Shelter is critical gap with most of the population sleeping in the open, under trees and a few under makeshift shelter made of palm thatches that barely prevent water from entering within when it rains. The few that were met had corrugated roof on their home are forced to accommodate some others without homes, forcing an average family of between ten and fifteen to share a single room. It was reported that IDPs are mostly women & children families have no utensils and those with saucepan use it to cook their cassavas/yams and put them on leaves when they are ready in order to use the saucepan for preparing their sauce. Women particularly made passionate appeal for kitchen sets and shelter materials. Other outstanding items required are carpets, blankets, mosquito nets
Distribution of tarpaulin/plastic sheets and non-food items—kitchen sets, carpets, blankets and mosquito nets amongst others. People have returned to their pre-war homesteads following multiple displacement and will need construction tools to settle in. In Pibor Jonglei  the main driver of the crisis is cattle raiding. Cattle are central of all community livelihoods but also to their social and cultural systems. The proliferation of guns, the commercialization of cattle and rising bride prices made cattle raiding more violent and more lucrative which increased the insecurity among communities in the area. The current incident mainly affected to two Payam as Lokoromach, Marpoz, Kambolok, Kermeth and Gei of Likuangole County. This has led to massive displacement of about 17,000 populations in different locations of two Payams as Lokormach, Marpoz and Kermeth under Lokormach Payam and Kerimeth, under Gei Payam.The community chiefs/leaders within the community reported that Cattle raiding is a typical incident in this location but this incident was different than the past due to volume of size cattle raiding.

project_name: Integrated WASH Response
project_objective: Integrated WASH Response to IDPs, Returnees and Conflict-Affected Populations in Upper Nile, Central & Eastern Equatorias and Jonglei States.

project_name: Reinforce the capacity skills of health workers in Damascus and Syrian territory
project_objective:
Since the beginning of its presence in the Country, Armadilla has worked in the field of health assistance, with a specific focus on children and persons with disabilities. The Syrian crisis in March 2011, has dramatically worsened the situation, especially for the displaced people that leaving behind the little they owned.  Armadilla has been supporting the work of both the local partner Zahret Al Madan (ZAM) and of the Centre for Prosthesis and Rehabilitation (CPR) of Ibn Al-Nafis Hospital, in implementing rehabilitation activities for people with disabilities (both physical and cognitive), through the provision of specific training to the local health workers with the aim of increasing their professional skills. The Ibn Al-Nafis Hospital, has a huge gap in human resources capacity, as well as technical equipment, in the health sector in general and particularly in the field of rehabilitation services (diagnosis, prosthesis, physical therapy), as many experienced health professionals  were displaced inside and outside Syria. The main objective of the project is the increase of number of physical rehabilitation sessions thanks to the specific trained/re-trained for health staff on related topics. Specifically, the purpose of the project is to strengthen the capacity of technical workers of the Centre for Prosthesis and Rehabilitation (CPR) Ibn Al-Nafis Hospital of Damascus (medical doctors, physical therapists, occupational therapists) through an intensive cycle of training about physical therapy, and prosthesis making, including specific modules on children and youngsters.
The project is integrated with activities related to child protection, implemented by Zahret Al Madan and Armadilla in the Southern Suburbs of Damascus (Midan Kawakibi), which volunteers and workers collaborate on permanent basis with the staff of the CPR for the care and therapy plans for children and youngsters with disability.
Moreover, the project aims to support the establishment of the Occupational Degree in the University Al-Manara of Latakia, through the provision of teaching given by International professors of the University of Modena and Reggio-Emilia (Italy).

project_name: Access to healthcare for the most vulnerable among the displaced population of tribal districts in KP province
project_objective:
The Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is located in the north-west of the country and borders Afghanistan. It comprises 25 districts and five Provincially Administered Tribal Areas (PATA). KP and FATA continue to experience crises and humanitarian emergencies. Numerous operations by Pakistan’s security forces since 2004 as well as violence by terrorist splinter groups (often religiously motivated) have resulted in a complex crisis, leading to the mass displacement of hundreds of thousands of people, mainly from FATA into neighbouring KP. Although the authorities attempted to initiate repatriations as early as 2015, these efforts are far from completed and have been largely unsuccessful. According to official figures, around 90% of IDPs have returned to FATA, but recording methods are, in reality, inadequate and can easily be circumvented. In both KP and FATA there is immense need for healthcare services for the IDPs and the host communities, since owing to the ongoing conflict, there is virtually no public healthcare provision. Statistics indicate that the maternal mortality rate in FATA is 395 per 100,000 live births (FATA household development indicators, 2012/13). 

In May 2018, the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) region were merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Province, therefore integrating FATA, now called Tribal Districts of KP, into Pakistan’s mainland governance structures. Although the government proposition finally found consensus after decades of efforts, with the army support, there are still two distinct authorities’ bodies (ex-FATA and KP), and a granted access to KP still doesn’t imply having access to the Tribal Districts. No real change has thus been acknowledged on the ground until now.

MdM is focusing on primary healthcare and reproductive health issues of communities of catchment area. MdM is also providing therapeutic supplements to under 5 years Malnourished children.
MdM started 2 BEmONC services each at RHC Naryab-Hangu and RHC Gomal-Tank district and planning to start one at RHC Band Korai-D.I.Khan and one at Thall-Hangu as well.
MdM is also providing psycho-social support and support to GBV victims by counselling and first aid treatment. 

MdM divided overall project goal in three results.

•	Result 1: IDPs, host communities and returnees have access at the supported facilities to high-quality, comprehensive primary healthcare, enhanced by staff capacity-building.
•	Result 2: Sexual and reproductive health services (treatment and advice) for women and girls, including obstetrics and neonatal care (in selected healthcare facilities) are expanded and accessible 
•	Result 3: The capacity of beneficiary communities to provide a humanitarian response to disasters, emergencies or disease outbreaks is strengthened through educational initiatives on disaster preparedness, health issues and preventive measures.

project_name: Cash Based Assistance for Haiti
project_objective:
CARE proposes a cash transfer based project to support 10,000 vulnerable hurricane-affected households through a food security intervention to meet their urgent needs while strengthening their livelihoods.
The project overall goal will be achieved through the following strategic objectives: 
1.	Critical and immediate basic needs and economic recovery of the poor households will be addressed and fostered through cash for work activities
2.	Improve community assets (physical, social, human and institutional) for future resilience and economic recovery through community directed public works. 

Indicators and targets:
Indicator I -To address critical and immediate basic needs and foster economic recovery Access to basic needs for 10,000 households through cash transfer and cash for work.
Indicator II – A monthly $60 cash-transfer is made to the 10,000 households in the Grand’Anse department
Indicator III – 5,500 household-heads participate in cash for work activities

project_name: GBV-Increasing access to holistic emergency GBV prevention and response to returnees and vulnerable host communities of Aweil Centre County of NBeG State.
project_objective: The proposed project seeks to deliver holistic emergency GBV prevention and response in Aweil Centre county(Achana,Aroyo,Awada,Awulic & Nyalath Payams) of NBeG state through establishing Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) to support females and GBV survivors access services such as counselling, information sharing, access to socio economic support, confidential referral pathways to medical and legal services and case management in a more discreet manner to avoid stigma. SAADO will target to reach 8,666 people (Women 5000, Girls 1700 Men 1000, Boys 966) in the selected county with GBV services.The location has been chosen because of the existing gaps in GBV programming in selected payams such as Achana,Aroyo,Awada,Awulic & Nyalath as well as the opportunities to promote girls’ protection, empowerment and resilience to mitigate GBV risks and to respond comprehensively to the needs of GBV survivors that are available.  This proposed project will build upon/complement SAADO’s long experience in implementing projects in Aweil Centre county supported by Stromme foundation. Currently, SAADO is implementing a 2.5-year DFID project in NBeG state for building resilience of communities known as BRACE II which is targeting 60% female beneficiaries and this will provide an opportunity to fully integrate GBV prevention in its implementation. The project will also complement SAADO‘s Women and Girls Empowerment intervention in Aweil Centre and Aweil West supported by Stromme Foundation, which aims at skills building targeting adolescent girls and young mothers over a 5-year period. SAADO's intervention will also complement the Life saving activities carried out by other GBV partners in the selected county as well as provide integration with Education(TVET),Livelihoods(community managed savings groups)and nutrition which are all key components of the project SAADO is currently implementing with support from Stromme Foundation and is a key focus of the GBV sub cluster as well as the RTAP where SAADO is a key participant .

project_name: Improving food production for the most vulnerable households in Duk & Bor South, Aweil North and Aweil West Counties of Jonglei and NBeG states, South Sudan.
project_objective:
The proposed emergency food security and livelihoods support project is a dual sector project targeting 4 selected counties of Bor South and Duk in Jonglei state and Aweil North and Aweil West in NBeG state and  will run for 12 months from January –December 2019.The main goal of the project will be to increase food production and access by providing lifesaving emergency livelihood support kits. The proposed project will provide training to most vulnerable households to enhance fishing,crop and vegetable production mainly for consumption at the household level. And, given an increase of market day’s events, sale of surplus at local markets in selected payams of Malual North, Akewic, Wad Wiel and Ariath of Aweil North and Aweil West counties of NBeG state and Bor town, Makuach, Anyidi, Ageer, Payuel and Padiet of Bor South and Duk Counties in Jonglei state which will create extra income for these households. Specifically, this project will target vulnerable households in the above mentioned payams. These payams are chosen due to their suitability for fishing and vegetable production. 
SAADO will target 15,333 households in this proposed response with emergency fishing,crop and vegetable kits. The locations have been chosen because of the needs prevalent in these counties according to the IPC September 2018 and the existence of active programming by SAADO in the areas. The emergency livelihood kits will be obtained from the FSLC-recommended core pipeline to communities affected by the ongoing crisis in Jonglei and NBeG states.
SAADO will put in place a mechanism for effective and participatory community vulnerability mapping in the selected Bomas and use a comprehensive beneficiary selection criteria developed and discussed and agreed upon with the communities to include Men, Women, Boys and Girls. During community consultations at various levels, all men, women boys and girls will be consulted to fully understand and appreciate the impact of the current crisis on men, women and children that would further inform response. “Do no harm” and AAP principles will be applied throughout the duration of the project, so that any possible negative implications of the project at community level are addressed before they occur through integrating a strong Communicating with Communities (CwC) feedback mechanisms. The project will build upon/complement SAADO long experience in implementing livestock disease prevention and control through vaccination and treatment in Bor South & Duk counties with support from FAO as well as implementing the 1st and 2nd allocations of the SSHF IN Jonglei state. It will also complement the Lives Saving and livelihood protection and nutrition activities carried out by SAADO in Aweil North county through the 2.5 year DFID funded BRACE II project as well as the financial literacy training (FLT) project in Aweil West County and therefore provide integration which is a key focus of the FSL cluster. The project will integrate with other FSL partners’ interventions in the counties especially WVI and PUI in Aweil North and Aweil West and CRS, NRC, and VSF-Germany in Bor South and Duk counties in Jonglei state. The proposed activities are necessary and sufficient to achieve the stated cluster objectives for these interventions based on the relevance of each activity in increasing food production for the most vulnerable households in the targeted communities. The indicators selected are SMART and SAADO has in place a strong monitoring and evaluation system/mechanisms to measure these indicators and to ensure the intended results are achieved. The means of verification, such as monthly reports, distribution lists and regular field visits are strongly credible and are currently used by the organization in its MEAL processes across its field offices in the country.

project_name: Supporting primary and secondry health care facilities and providing medwifery training in Idleb governorate
project_objective: The project aims to provide primary and secondary health services for the affected people in Idleb governorate in Syria. Violet aims to support 3 PHCs in Idleb governorate (Abu Thar, Samidoon, Janiet Al Bir) in Armanaz as well as supporting 2 ambulance system in Idleb and Maaret Al Numan. Additionally, Violet will continue supporting the maternity hospital in Ariha as well as continue training nurses to qualify them to work as midwives.

project_name: Mitigating High Food insecurity  through Emergency food security livelihood and resilience light support to 10000 Food insecure households in  Tonj South ( Warrap state) and in Aweil West ( Northern Bahr- El Ghazal state
project_objective:
The project proposal is a one year Emergency Food security and livelihood support  intervention with promotion of  appropriate small scale resilience activities. The implementation period  begins in January, 2019 through to December, 2019i The immediate objective is to enable vulnerable households to have access to food through their own production. The long term objective is to protect vulnerable households from shocks that will affect their ability to access food .The  objectives are in   line with HRP strategic objective 2 ( SO2) and is in support of FSL cluster objective 2 and  FSL cluster objective 4
To deliver the required results, the key program strategy is to  throughdirect distribution of inputs, input trade fairs , training   vaccination and treatment. To ensure Accountability to affected population,  a committee would be formed to address these issues . The project will target mainly vulnerable households in host and IDP areas .60,000 vulnerable people will be supported  mainly from Aweil West and Tonj South Women, boys and children that are mainly at high protection risk will be the main targets

project_name: Strengthening Mechanisms for Protecting HLP Rights in Areas Expecting High Return
project_objective: The project aims at Strengthening Mechanisms for Protecting HLP Rights in Areas Expecting High Return. It contributes to the HRP objective SO 2&3, to enable durable solutions for displaced persons and other affected population in the project locations.  These will be achieved through; (1) conducting HLP assessment to ascertain HLP needs of the displaced persons, refugee returnees and host communities existing mechanisms for HLP disputes resolution, (2) Raising awareness on HLP and the law, on spot monitoring and response to assist IDPs reclaim their land and properties, provision of free legal aid and (4) Establishment of innovative and sustainable community based alternative dispute resolution mechanism. Due to the complex nature of HLP issues and limited information on HLP issues in the project locations, the SSLS intends to carry out assessment, establish innovative and sustainable community mediation groups and provide continuous legal aid services. These interventions require a period of at least nine (6) months to implement and coordinate HLP program. The project targets areas of potential return of displaced person of Malakal, Bentiu, Bor and Juba.

project_name: Provision of Food Security and Livelihoods Support Among Vulnerable Populations in Jonglei and Central Equatoria States
project_objective:
The project aims to support most vulnerable populations comprised of men, women, girls and boys (7,000 households) in Jonglei and Central Equatoria States. These will be supported through provision of agricultural livelihood kits which will be pre-positioned through the core pipeline - crop, vegetables and tools and fishing kits for both main season and dry season response for vegetable and fishing kits. Stop Poverty Communal Initiative (SPOCI) will as well carry out livestock treatment, vaccinations, trainings and capacity building including equipping of Community Animal Health Workers. 
SPOCI aims to respond and by establishing a nexus between Humanitarian response and Resilience programming and responf to the FSL Cluster Objective 2:food production for the most vulnerable households: Increase vulnerable household food production to protect the erosion of livelihoods through  agricultural seeds and fishing inputs; with activities tailored to deliver an integrated WASH, Nutrition, Health, Protection package in liaison and coordination with other agencies on ground .
The project will target 7000 HHs - 15000 girls, 15000 boys, 6000 men and 6000 women drawn from recently arrived internally displaced persons, host community members, returnees among others. These will include elderly persons, pregnant and lactating women, people with disabilities drawn from the most vulnerable households.  These different categories will be consulted and involved in implementation of the project including monitoring and evaluation; while taking into consideration Accountability of Affected Populations, Gender Equity, Protection concerns including GBV and sound environmentally friendly approaches.

project_name: Addressing protection needs of vulnerable community members in Mundri East County.
project_objective:
This project aims at strengthening resilience of 9,960 most vulnerable IDP`S and host community / conflict affected population in 2 payams of Mundri East by the end of December 2019 through: conducting protection assessment and monitoring in Mundri East County, provision of individual / group psycho-social support (PSS) to 200 vulnerable persons, provision of safe referrals to 300 most vulnerable and their family members and disseminate information on available services,  carry out community awareness raising sessions targeting 100 people per week on protection, and sensitization on fundamental human rights, establishing two protection monitoring committees in Mundri East County, provide 90 women, 90 men with life skills and livelihood / income generating activities and link them to VSLA groups, provide training to 60 community leaders on peace building and conflict resolution.


Our approach for this project is based on the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, and impartiality where we shall provide services without discrimination. 
In line with the cluster response priorities of provision of immediate lifesaving assistance to vulnerable populations, this project will meet the needs of the conflict affected communities by ensuring access to protective services. Sudan Evangelical Mission (SEM) will focus on internally displaced persons (IDP`S), host communities and other conflict affected populations to whom we shall address their urgent and unmet humanitarian needs.
SEM intends to use local capacity and resources to address distress and shock amongst the local communities whom we shall directly involve in the project in order to strengthen their resilience. We shall promote their resilience of the IDP`S, host communities and the conflict affected population through a comprehensive strategy that includes prevention, response and sustainability dimensions in full account.
We shall work to ensure that community members especially IDP`S who have found themselves in a new environment are aware of existing services through conducting awareness raising. Messages aim at upholding human rights, legal awareness will be passed to the community.  

The awareness raising will help foster social cohesion and smooth integration of the IDP`S in the community. Through these approaches, SEM will identify and strengthen existing coping mechanisms and support vulnerable community members with PSS and referral to existing services. By training community leaders in conflict resolution and peace building, they will help to improve the security and harmonious co-existence by resolving and diffusing tension that arises within their community. Providing such an avenue, the community becomes empowered to prevent and respond to incidents of protection.

SEM consultation in July 2018 with the community of Lakamadi area on protection issues, we established that persons with disabilities are at risk due to immobility, and improving their mobility through devices like wheelchairs goes a long way to improve their response to distress as they can be able to move independently when the necessity arises. 

SEM will create sustainability by working with and empowering and working with volunteers from the community where we shall implement this project.

project_name: Formal and Non-formal Education Provision to Displaced and Host Community Children in Idleb
project_objective:
The project is designed to fill the education gap in Idleb that has witnessed lately influx of IDPs from Eastern Ghouta mainly. It will provide formal and non-formal education to 3793 host community and internally displaced children aged 6-18. The number of formal education children is 3313(1674 boys and 1639 girls) and 480 non-formal children(255 boys and 225 girls) in nine schools in rural and urban Idleb. The project will also target 198 education personnel(98 males and 100 females). Such an intervention can enhance resilience and a better integration as host communities are most often the front-line responders to populations most in need of help.  Violet will coordinate with Idleb Education Directorate for avoiding any duplication as the Directorate has all the data needed for schools and teachers. MoUs will be signed with the Education Directorate for defining the commitments of both parties. 
The project will ensure improved access and quality education for formal and non-formal education for both girls and boys(IDP or HC) equally without any discrimination. To better ensure a protective learning environment, Violet selected nine schools previously repaired under other projects. Each school will have: teachers, a head teacher, a supervisor, a caseworker, a cleaner and a guard who will be recruited based on hiring criteria and a gender balance approach where males and females have the right to apply and go through competitive procedures in a fair way.

project_name: Emergency school feeding programme for primary school going children
project_objective: SPEDP is proposing an integrated school feeding programme in schools in Renk, Melut, Fashoda and Manyo Counties with the general objectives of contributing to reduction in cognitive underdevelopment and malnutrition, improve attendance and enrollment, and reduce gender disparities. This project will target school going children between 6-18 years in primary schools within Renk, Melut , Fashoda and Manyo for three terms which will expand over a period of 12 months. It targets 16 schools with 10,000 (6500 M, 3500 F school going children, 160 teachers and 48 cooks/kitchen helpers. These 16 schools will be selected based on food security status, literacy statistics, enrollment and attendance data. SPEDP will give due consideration on environmental and economic aspects of the emergency to determine the most affected or most in need of assistance. It will develop programme plans to feed all children within these schools, regardless of their individual circumstances. SPEDP will ensure that protection risks and benefits are considered in emergence school feeding program, as part of all humanitarian assistance and protection. SPEDP promote a community-based protection approach, or meaningful engagement and ideally, leadership, of crisis-affected communities to identify protection risks, self-protection capacities, and joint prevention and mitigation and link to this protection actors seek to mainstream an age, gender and diversity approach to aim for the equal enjoyment of rights by all crisis-affected people, and to integrate this into accountability frameworks.

project_name: Strengthening Food Security and Sustainable Livelihood Promotion in Former Northern Bhar-el Ghahazal State
project_objective:
This food security and livelihood project is a combined response which will run for 12 months from January to December, 2019. Main goal of the project is to strengthen food and nutrition security and resilience among food insecure HHs in former states of NBeG in South Sudan. The project directly targets 34,000 vulnerable households of primarily IDPs (10%), returnees (15%) and host community (75%). The beneficiaries will be targeted basing on vulnerability matrix and context
To achieve this, the project will support the immediate nutritional needs of vulnerable HHs through the provision of cash/vouchers transfers. Using cash transfers, HHs will access, food sufficient food to meet daily caloric and nutritional requirements. This will address the immediate impacts of food insecurity, reducing the incidence of malnutrition and malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality. Transfers will be both unconditional and conditional upon the completion of work to rehabilitate and/or construct communal assets that have the potential to enhance longer term food security and livelihoods including physical assets such as dykes and roads, as well as natural assets. 
In addition to meeting basic and immediate needs, short term  cash transfers will ensure HHs have the energy and time to participate in activities that enhance their ability to deal with disruption and change. By improving the availability and accessibility of these productive assets, the project will strengthen long-term food security by improving agricultural productivity, and supporting the regeneration of the natural resource base. As production increases, availability of food for consumption and/or sale increases, resulting in improved livelihoods and an increase in local, regional and national food security. 
To enhance emergency food production, main season agriculture seeds & tool, fishing gears for Aweil Center, and fast maturing vegetable & crop kits shall be distributed. This project will also contribute to the reduction of pest and crop disease e.g. FAW surveillance, detection, prevention & eradication and also conduct Livestock vaccination; disease prevention & treatment especially zoonotic e.g. RVF; 
To achieve its expected impact, the project will be proactive and supportive (rather than reactive and focused on relief) in providing assistance for target communities to enhance its effectiveness. SPEDP will also do M&E, reporting and coordination with relevant stakeholders to effect complementary, maximize synergies and contribute to project sustainability. SPEDP will also use a community based participatory approach where beneficiary identification and registration process will involve community members.
Project management committees will be established and will take an active role in the beneficiary selection, monitoring implementation and also handling complaints and feedback mechanisms and monitoring of the project, this CFM will be set in place where beneficiaries and non-beneficiaries will be able to able to air out their concerns about the project. Stakeholders will be invited during the launch and all project details will be shared to foster accountability to the affected populations
SPEDPs added value is that the organization has an already established presence in NBeG since 2013 to date has implemented a number of projects since them in different thematic areas. SPEDP is currently implementing FSL SA2 project in Aweil West, FOA-SAFER Project in Aweil Center and North and so is familiar with the local settings

project_name: Integrated shelter and life saving non food items assistance to the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees and the host communities in Counties of Greater Yei
project_objective: The humanitarian situation in South Sudan still remains dire amidst the revitalized peace agreement signed in Khartoum by the government and opposition parties. Several ceasefires have been undermined with continuous clashes between the government and opposition parties across the country hence forced about 1.5 people to flee their homes and took refuge in the neighbouring countries - Uganda, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Kenya, Sudan and Ethiopia while 1.9 million people were displaced within the Country with many more hiding in the bushes and swamps in remote areas. The almost five years prolonged conflict and an entrenched economic crisis have caused severe human suffering in South Sudan with one million in brink of starvation. With the progress of the peace signed in Khartoum, it is strongly believed that the millions of South Sudanese displaced to the neighbouring Countries like Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, DRC, etc including internally displaced persons (IDPs) will voluntarily return to their areas of origin hence high influx of returnees is possible. It is on this background that the 2019 Humanitarian Response Plan for South Sudan projects should hugely increase in the number of people in need that include IDPs, returnees and the host communities whose resources have been depleted or stressed. Nearly 1.9 million people have been internally displaced, 85% of whom are women and children besides millions that have fled the country as refugees to the neighbouring countries. SPEDP proposes a-12 month project targeting at 25,000 vulnerable people(6100 women, 5248 men, 7109 girls and 6543boys)  with emergence shelter, life-saving non-food items and cash based intervention responses to address the different needs of vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in Greater Yei Counties. SPEDP is very familiar working in these Communities without any access constrains. SPEDP will engage with joint mobile response teams including , Lacha Community and Economic Development (LCED), Concern  and TiTi Foundation to address shelter and NFI needs to the affected populations in assessed areas in the project locations. SPEDP will work in close collaboration with above-mentioned partners to establish synergies among the similar initiatives and avoidance of duplication and overlapping. Among the activities include needs assessment, beneficiaries verification and registration, distribution of shelter and NFI materials, Cash-Based Interventions (CBI) as SPEDP has a good reputation in Korijo IDP Camp where 600 emergency shelters were constructed through CBI programme. Market assessments will be conducted in stable project sites like Yei, Morobo and Lainya to establish items available in the market for the cash intervention.  Post distribution monitoring will also be conducted to find out whether beneficiaries are satisfied with the items distributed. SPEDP will assume the role of distribution together with mobile and static partners that may be present in the respective project locations. The proposed project will focus on women headed households, child headed households’, people living with disabilities, elderly people, etc incorporating gender dynamics and specific needs of different groups into needs assessment and response recommendations. SPEDP will equally engage with stakeholders concern and will form a committee that will oversee beneficiaries’ selection criteria of women headed households, child headed households, people with disabilities and the older people. For the safety of the cash, SPEDP will use its previous approach of contracting money transfer agents or be so flexible by doing it directly with the help of identified and contracted vendors.

project_name: TO PROVIDE FOOD ASSISTANCE TO VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS AND POPULATIONS THROUGH A MULTI SECTOR INTEGRATED RESPONSE TO PREVENT FAMINE IN KAJOKEJI, YEI, LAINYA, LAFON, MAGWI AND KAPOETA EAST COUNTIES
project_objective:
The main purpose of the project is to increase agricultural production and build community resilience for the vulnerable food insecure households through a multi sector integrated response to prevent catastrophic consequences like famine which has been caused by the continued insecurity, disrupted markets, animal diseases, low harvests due to pests and worms like fall army worm, natural drought conditions. 
 These populations that consists of mainly IDPS and host communities have been experiencing a confluence of consistent clashes between warring parties in the country especially the most recent which was between September and October 2018 in yei and Lainya which had spill overs into kajokeji leading to displacements into the korijo idp settlements in liwolo payam in western kajokeji. the recent idps who fled the crises from mukaya,Lainya and some parts of yei and sokare in liwolo payam  were forced to settle in korijo which is the newest idp settlement in kajokeji. This report was verified through an IRNA conducted on the 18/10/2018 by Titi foundation teams and partners operating in kajokeji. Given that this areas where titi foundation operates as a static partner in, are also close to the border of Uganda, Kenya and DR.Congo we have experienced an inflow of mainly returnees and some refugees into areas like kajokeji through the moyo and mijale points, magwi  and Lafon through lobone from Uganda and yei where the returnees are hailing from Uganda and DR.Congo escaping the harsh conditions in the  various refugee camps in search for  better living conditions in south sudan.  These locations have not just been experiencing the effects of war alone but also in the 2018 september –october IPC released results we have seen that areas like kajokeji have been classified in phase 4 and the other locations between phase 3-4 which depicts emergency situation and depicting the high need for an intervention in various sectors including food security and livelihoods.These areas have also been unique in that politically some are controlled by both IG and IO parties especially locations like kajokeji, Lainya and partially yei  in central equatoria which has also to a greater extent escalated the suffering of the populations in this areas.
Its in this regard and background therefore that Titi foundation has identified through information gathered from sources like REACH SURVEYS and the recently just concluded IRNA as of 18/10/2018  that the population in some locations like Korijo in kajokeji is hosting a total population of 40294 newly displaced idps and hence there is a high  need for FSL intervention to the vulnerable populations in these locations (according to the October/18/2018 IRNA report). 

 The other objective is to improve food and storage systems plus the animal health in the pastoral communities. This will be done through direct distribution of quick maturing seeds and tools to the farmers in these locations, training of farmer groups on new agricultural technologies, supporting livelihood projects like the( FES ie fuel efficient stoves and briquettes aimed at mitigating GBV risks) of women,men and adolescent girls and boys. They will also be provided with food assistance especially to the idps, returnees, refugees and host community.

 This project is targeting 3000 households who are most vulnerable in host communities, IDPs, returnees and refugees in Kajokeji, Lainya, Yei in Central Equatoria ,Magwi, Lafon and Kapoeta East in Eastern.
Equatoria. During the project implementation, Titi Foundation Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and learning (MEAL) teams will conduct field visits and reports will be developed on the progress of the projects in the selected locations of Kajokeji, Yei, Lainya, Magwi, Lafon and Kapoeta East. This will involve key informants interviews in the various communities and focus group discussions to determine the efficiency and effectiveness of the intervention.

Titi foundation which already has office spaces and implementing  ongoing projects like S/NFI, GBV and protection activities in all this locations will mainstream its activities like the ongoing fuel efficient stoves and briquettes program which is aimed at mitigating gender based violence will be mainstreamed to our planned FSL interventions to ensure that the beneficiaries will also be trained along the (FES) project to reduce on the possibility of gender based violence that they could have been exposed to. Titi will also blend ongoing projects like child protection especially to our FSL beneficiaries to assist targeted beneficiary category such as child headed households and people living with disabilities to acquire psychosocial support (pss) by involving our specialized staffs from the various sectors to assist our FSL beneficiaries acquire our extra services.

project_name: Opérationnalisation d’un mécanisme de plaintes, référencement des victimes et feedback pour les communautés en Haïti
project_objective: La question de la protection des personnes touchées ou menacées doit guider les prises de décisions et l’intervention humanitaire, voire au-delà. Dans le cadre de la stratégie de protection en Haïti, la mise en place d’un mécanisme de plainte, référencement des victimes et feedback des communautés sur les projets (MPRF) est le fondement du renforcement de la protection des citoyens. C’est un outil essentiel permettant la redevabilité envers les communautés, l’efficacité des interventions et l’établissement de liens de communication dans les deux sens.

project_name: Enhancing the food security of Rohingya refugees and host communities through self-reliance and livelihood support
project_objective: SC aims to enhance self-resilience status of Rohingya and Host community through different activities in integrate approach at Teknaf and Ukhia which helps to increases and improves access to nutrition food, diverse income generation options, youth engagement and cohesive between the communities. SCI will implement community lead project covering 20000 individuals in identify location through partnership approach which will build up ownership over programmatic activities and achievements, and thus enables long-term functionality and sustainability.

project_name: Emergency and sustainable WASH intervention to disaster affected IDPs and host communities in Puntland and Hirshabelle of Somalia
project_objective: The overall objective of the project is to provide emergency and sustainable WASH services to the disaster affected IDPs and host communities in Puntland and Hieshabelle of Somalia. At the inception of the project, AADSOM will hold a workshop to the prominent community members including women and IDPs to familiarize them the modalities/objective and roles will be discussed such as project objectives, implementation strategies, scope, feedback and complaint mechanisms, beneficiary selection criteria, beneficiary entitlement and roles. Side meetings with girls, boys, men and women will also be convened to ensure their different needs are addressed. AADSOM will present the project documents to cluster members to avoid overlaps, following the cluster discussions.  AADSOM will provide lifesaving safe water to 1000 IDPs in Bari (500HHs) and Hiran IDPs (500HHs), benefiting 6,000 men, women, girls and boys who have no access of safe water in two months of time. As an exit strategy, the project will rehabilitate the existing water sources (1 borehole, 6 berkeds and 15 shallow wells). In order to keep the sustainability of the water source and to increase the ownership of the community to the rehabilitated of the water sources, AADSOM will train WASH committees and well operators. As cross cutting, AADSOM will conduct community training on DRR and conflict resolution mechanisms. In order to reduce the risk of GBV and discourage open defecation, AADSOM will construct 100 gender sensitive IDP latrines, and 4 lockable, gender sensitive twin block latrines complete with hand washing basins in 2 schools and 2 health facilities with equal access of men, women, boys and girls. AADSOM will carryout hygiene promotion campaigns participating women, men, boys and girls and is planned to reach 35,000 people. The HP awareness campaigns will carry out by CHPs who are trained through this project. Finally, to encourage men, women and children to wash their hands with soap during the use of latrines and to fetch and store the water safely, AADSOM will distribute 1000 HP kits to 1000 IDP HHs (500 HH in Bari and 500 HH in Hiran), who are at risk of AWD and/or HHs with malnourished children and pregnant & lactating women. During the project implementation, AADSOM will encourage women to take part the decision making of the community decisions. AADSOM will make continuous monitoring during the project implementation and will handover the rehabilitated WASH services to the community leaders with the presence of the local authorities. The project is complementarity with  the existing AADSOM food security and WASH projects in Bari and Hiran regions of Puntland and Hirshabelle states of Somalia.

project_name: Réponse de protection dans la région de Tillabéri
project_objective:
Mettre en place des mécanismes de suivi et de référencements communautaires permanents pour intensifier la prise en charge des problèmes de protections dans les zones cibles du projet, afin de faciliter le partage d’information, la prévention et l'assistance individuelle et/ou référencement des cas de protection aux seins des populations hôtes et déplacées.  Renforcer et intensifier la mobilisation communautaire, en s'assurant que la moitié des membres de comité soit des femmes . Reception des cas de protection pour suivi au Centre d'Ecoute et d'Orientation d'Ayerou. 
Résultat 1 : La collecte et le partage des données sur les cas de protection sont systématiques à l'aide des réseaux communautaires mis en place à cet effet, dans la mesure où les données collectées sont complémentaires à celles collectées dans le cadre du monitoring régulier. 
Activités : formation des comités de protection pour l'identification, l'analyse des tendances de protection, mais surtout le référencement des cas identifiés. Les points focaux sont déjà en place, et seront suivis par le partenaire metttant en oeuvre le monitoring dans la région. 
Résultat 2 : Une assistance directe et/ou référencement rapide et efficace sont fournies aux cas de protection identifiés aux seins de populations hôtes et déplacées des zones d'intervention du projet et dans le CEO d'Ayorou.

project_objective: Le projet a pour but de contribuer à la préparation et l’intervention rapide, efficace et flexible en cas d’inondation, en collaboration avec les autorités, pour apporter aux 11 135 personnes affectées dans la région de Diffa une hygiène de base (notamment pour les femmes) et de l’eau potable tout en  favorisant la résilience des populations face à cette crise en renforçant aux travers des activités de sensibilisation et d'information.

project_name: Shelter & NFI Support for Conflict-Affected Iraqis (CRS)
project_objective:
This shelter support and NFI intervention will provide life-saving assistance to 47,880  conflict affected individuals in Iraq, including those facing prolonged displacement, returnees, and vulnerable host community members.

Informed by consultations with men, women, boys and girls in affected areas, program activities and approaches will prioritize the safety, access and dignity of conflict-affected families, mainstreaming protection principles. Through shelter upgrades and repairs to war-damaged shelters, CRS will ensure that conflict-affected households have access to quality living space that is appropriate to their context in either displacement or return. NFI distributions, consisting of both cash and in-kind items, will enable targeted beneficiaries to restore their essential relief items and household assets. Across both shelter and NFI components, where markets are functioning and accessible, CRS will utilize market-based approaches to support local markets and uphold beneficiaries’ dignity, agency and choice.
 
CRS will implement the project in Baghdad, Anbar, Duhok, Kirkuk and Ninewa governorates, working in partnership with Caritas Iraq for implementation in Baghdad and Anbar. CRS has funding for education, livelihoods, and social cohesion programming that will complement that activities proposed for shelter and NFI assistance.

project_name: Emergency Livelihoods Support for Conflict-Affected Iraqis (CRS)
project_objective: This project supports conflict-affected individuals in return areas to restore their pre-conflict livelihoods. Livelihoods restoration is focused on beneficiaries who lost their business due to the conflict and have strong pre-conflict experience and skills; the intervention provides an asset recovery grant paired with light mentorship for beneficiaries to adapt to the post-conflict market. Informed by consultations with women and men in affected areas, program activities and approaches will prioritize the safety, access and dignity of conflict-affected families, mainstreaming protection principles.
