project_objective: Barefoot Counsellors project activities aim at ""helping refugees to help themselves.""

project_name: Integrated Primary Healthcare, SRHR and Comprehensive Maternity Services for Rohingya Refugees at Ukhia, Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
The goal of this project is to provide integrated healthcare services through 9 health posts, a comprehensive maternity center (CMC) and a birthing center to the Rohingya refugees and members of the host community throughout 2019, with technical assistance from Norwegian Church Aid (NCA). 

The facilities will ensure availability of minimum service package (as agreed by Health Sector) through medical doctors and other service providers, including SRHR. The CMC will be operational 24/7, with provision of Normal Vaginal Delivery, C-Section and other maternal and neonatal services. Other services such as EPI and an external referral linkage with secondary service facilities will also be ensured.

project_name: Columbia - United Nations Population Fund
Providing basic community Water services and WASH supplies to the most vulnerable people residents, IDPs and returnees in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates
project_objective:
GVC will intervene in Deir-Ez-Zor and Aleppo Governorates restoring basic water schools’ and community services. In both areas, the Action will target Hard to Reach (HTR) areas where the NGO is present with running programs in WASH and EiE sectors.
The action aims to provide sufficient and safe water to around 137 000 people living in Deir-Ez-Zor  and  Rural Aleppo areas. These projects will ensure access to water to inhabitants and will increase the capacity to cope with the increase number of returnees. Water networks and pumping stations are damaged and overloaded, unable to guarantee the quantity and quality needed to the inhabitants and obliging them to recur to other sources, exposing them to waterborne disease and depleting their already stretched resources. The rehabilitation of WASH infrastructures in 12 schools will guarantee the access to gender and disabled oriented facilities for all the students favoring school attendance. The HP campaign with the distribution of WASh items will allow the inhabitants of the selected areas to adopt adequate hygiene practices by reducing the incidence of waterborne diseases.

project_name: Increase access to safe, inclusive and quality education for school-age children and adolescents in Aleppo and Deir-Ez Zor Governorates
project_objective: Considering the needs and in line with the first pillar of No Lost Generation Initiative,the context analysis and the current demographic trends, the intervention aims at re-establishing basic education community services in the targeted areas.The intervention is tailored to the different operational setting,adapting activities to rural and urban contexts.Areas of intervention are return areas,where population is increasing and services will have to cope with the additional stress of the population growth. Therefore, GVC opts for a community support reducing to the minimum individual assistance.This approach is relevant to returnees’ contexts,preparing the ground for sustainable intervention to benefit boys and girls of 5-17 years old affected by the crises and improving resilience of the reached communities. The intervention aims at increasing access to safe,equitable and quality education for children and adolescents affected by the crisis in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates, relying on GVC expertise in NFE(solid reputational basis and knowledge of the selected areas. First,to increase access GVC will implement a package of tailored activities, targeting out of school children(OOSC) through a spread  Back-to-Learning(BTL)campaign (door to door visits, awareness and information campaigns, dialogue sessions, interactive theatre events to involve OOSC) aimed at encouraging them and their families to re-enrol in school, in cooperation with local partners such as DoE and SARC volunteers. In addition,access to school will be enhanced by providing Remedial classes to children at risk of dropping out, in line with standards provided by Ministry of Education and Education Sector. In line with the same goal, GVC will involve OOSC in Self-Learning programs(SLP)aimed at filling the gaps of those who lost 6 months or more of attendance. Children and teachers attending Remedial classes and SLP will also receive school bags and stationery. Finally, students and OOSC will be involved in edu-entertainment activities which will be implemented both as a part of each one of the over-mentioned initiatives and as ad hoc events aimed at improving life-skills and KSA (Knowledge Skills Attitude) and supporting the psycho-social development of vulnerable boys and girls. More specifically, each event will focus on a different topic, ability or life learning, which may range from stressing the importance of education, promoting hygiene practices to highlighting the relevance of ambition and aspirations to achieve personal goals. Secondly, safe and inclusive education will be guaranteed through rehabilitation and equipment of school buildings, which will include solutions to enable access to students with special needs,and gender and disability-sensitive WASH facilities.The rehabilitation of classes will increase the number of available safe learning places and directly have a positive effect in enrolment rate.In addition, furniture of teaching and learning material will be delivered to schools in need.Finally,the intervention will improve quality education through training courses for teachers in Active Learning/Psycho-social Support (ALT/PSS) and in Risk Education (MRE-Mine Risk Education). This will improve teachers’ skills, contributing to better quality education for girls and boys. The courses will also include training in Self-Learning strategies, so that GVC can rely on trained teachers in ALT when selecting – in cooperation with the DoE– the trainers to provide Self-Learning programs. GVC already implements these “assessing practices” as a successful mean to ensure children are reached by quality information and knowledge.Finally, training in Risk Education will be included in the package and will raise teachers’ awareness of the behavioural changes needed to prevent harm from explosive devices; teachers will share the information and material received with children in their schools,thus contributing to reduce protection risks.

project_name: Increasing protection of children, Teachers, host community, returnees and IDPs living in newly accessible and hard to reach areas in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates through a tailored risk education programme
project_objective:
The extensive use of explosive weapons since the beginning of the crisis generated explosive hazards, posing a grave threat to  kill or injure. Civilians, humanitarian response operators, and livelihood activities. The contamination with Unexploded ordnance (UXO) in the areas affected by the crisis caused injures and loosing life.  Across the country, an estimated 8 million people are exposed to life-threatening explosive hazards, including Aleppo and Deir-ez-Zor Governorates. Such hazards range from landmines, to booby traps and unexploded remnants of war and have devastating consequences on the lives of children and their families.  In 2017 in Aleppo, 383 people were killed and hundreds more injured in similar hazards, having returned to east Aleppo after fighting subsided (https://www.unicef.org/mena/stories/unicef-protects-children-and-their-families-across-syria-against-explosive-hazards.In Deir-Ez-Zor, after 5 years of fighting and periods of siege, in November 2017, the GoS (Government of Syria) took control of the area. Infrastructures are heavily damaged, basic public services suspended, and large part of the city is contaminated by Explosives Remnants from War (ERW). In Rural Aleppo, as big part of it was under fight and siege, infrastructures are  heavily damaged and high level of contamination of ERW still exists.
Therefore, GVC decided to launch the “Risk Education Program” in contaminated areas and in areas of returns, where people will be forced to deal with the risks related to mines and explosive hazards. 
GVC intervention will aim at proving communities and returnees with the proper knowledge and methods to prevent the accidents of explosion contamination.
The planned intervention is in line with GVC’s humanitarian commitment started in 2014 and focused on Risk Education to teachers since 2017, targeting Aleppo Governorate. The planned project will build upon the following achievements: GVC Risk Education training was conducted in Aleppo city and rural and targeted 800 teachers (male and female), as in each training session 20 teachers attended. A pre test and post test took place in order to evaluate the teachers knowledge of the Risk education as subject and its component; the outcome of the tests showed that in each training 15 teachers did not know anything on risk education, and the rest 5 teachers they either had wrong information or they only knew the kind of mining without any clue of  how to avoid and behave properly. At the end of the training 99% of the teachers were assessed as aware and acquired an adequate attitude in the Risk Education. .
All the above encouraged GVC extend the program to target different categories of beneficiaries through different kinds of activities, such as awareness session and theatre activities.
The action will continue targeting Aleppo, while extending to Deir-ez-Zor Governorate.
The “Risk Education Program” is using professional standard where a diverse range of methods are implemented, targeting different categories of beneficiaries that are able to spread the messages to the community as a whole. More specifically, this program will be delivered to teachers, children, and community (men/ women/ persons with disabilities/ elderly) through training and awareness campaign, using material (brochures, guidelines, kits, video contents etc.) provided or elaborated in collaboration with Ministry of Education/Directorate of Education.

project_name: Réponse aux urgences sanitaires dans les zones affectées du Burundi
project_objective: La situation des enfants au Burundi est caractérisée par une forte mortalité infanto-juvénile estimée à 78‰ naissances vivantes (EDS 2016-2017) avec prédominance de causes évitables ou traitables. La crise que traverse le pays depuis 2015 affecte de façon négative la disponibilité et la qualité des services sociaux et le bien-être des populations avec près de 1.77 millions de personnes en besoin d’assistance humanitaire. La mortalité maternelle reste élevée (334 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes, EDS 2016) et demeure extrêmement préoccupante malgré une baisse par rapport à l’EDS 2010 (500 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes). Sur le plan épidémiologique, le Burundi connait depuis plusieurs années des épisodes d’épidémies de paludisme (dans sa partie Nord Est et Centre) et de choléra (dans la partie Ouest du pays), principalement sur la rive du Lac Tanganyika. Le paludisme a dépassé en fin d'année 2018 le seuil épidémique et d'alerte dans 11 et 13 districts sanitaires sur 46. En 2018, le Burundi a notifié 102 contre 336 cas de choléra en 2017. Le risque de nouvelles flambées de choléra reste élevé en raison des mauvaises conditions d'hygiène. Malgré les bonnes performances en matière de vaccination, on note une stagnation, voire une régression des couvertures vaccinales dans certains districts. Lors de l’atelier d’élaboration du HNO conduit par OCHA, l’analyse de la situation a conduit le secteur de la santé à identifier les populations affectées comme étant celles de 10 des 18 provinces du pays (Bubanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cankuzo, Kirundo, Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana et Ruyigi) qui connaissent des épidémies de choléra à répétition, avec morbidite de paludisme plus élevée, les provinces avec des taux moyens de 52% et 29% correspondant respectivement à la capacité de diagnostic et de disponibilité des médicaments essentiels, provinces avec une mortalité maternelle élevée et aussi ceux qui ont connu une détérioration de la couverture vaccinale de la rougeole. Activities et outputs: UNICEF utilisera son expérience dans la mise en œuvre auprès des formations sanitaires et des communautés et son avantage comparatif dans l’appui technique et le monitoring des interventions liées à la santé. La réponse portera sur différentes interventions comme l'appui en médicaments essentiels principalement pour les populations les plus vulnérables que sont les femmes et les enfants de moins de 15 ans, la prise en charge du choléra, le soutien à une vaccination continue ainsi que la prise en charge médicale des personnes victimes des violences basées sur le genre et l’amélioration des Soins Obstétricaux et néonatals essentiels. Les résultats attendus sont les suivants ainsi que les activités y associées (Référence aux activités du plan du groupe sectoriel santé): 1. Les enfants, les femmes et les adolescents ont accès à des services de santé essentiels de qualité pour la prise en charge des maladies courantes et des épidémies ; ont une prise en charge médicale de qualité et un référencement vers les acteurs de protection pour une prise en charge holistique. 2.1. Organisation de la prise en charge médicales et psychosociale des survivants des VBGs ont une prise en charge médicale de qualité et un référencement vers les acteurs de protection pour une prise en charge holistique 2.1. Organisation de la prise en charge médicales et psychosociale des survivants des VBG (Activité3) ; Indicateur : Nombre des survivants des VBGs qui ont été pris en charge par les services de santé. Cible : 3,000 ; 2.2. Appui à l’organisation des réunions de coordination des activités de prise en charge holistique des survivants des VBG ; 2.3. Fournir les soins obstétricaux et néonatals d’urgence de base et complets (SONUB/SONUC) aux filles et femmes en âge de procreer. 3.2. Organisation des séances de stratégie avancée /campagnes de vaccination contre la rougeole dans les aires de santé avec une couverture vaccinale inférieure à 80%.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving emergency healthcare access to vulnerable populations focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality in the former Warrap, Upper Nile and Western Equatorial States in the Republic of South Sudan
project_objective:
The  2017 UNICEF situation report states that the health services in South Sudan remained extremely weak and fragile, and even where functional, only a narrow, ad hoc range of services were available that could be intermittently accessed by people. Many areas remained inaccessible due to the worsening conflict and economic and political crises. In 2017, operational costs also doubled as very expensive air assets were required to enable programmatic responses. Women and children were among the worst affected by this situation, with their very survival at stake. South Sudan has among the highest maternal mortality and child mortality rates in the world. Young children are most prone to common infectious diseases (malaria, pneumonia, and diarrhoea) with high rates of malnutrition increasing the risk of severe illness and death.  The prevailing health systems challenges are exacerbated by lack of adequate water and sanitation, mainly the source of water supply, including water quality control, infection prevention and control measures, poor healthcare waste management, extensive malnutrition and a looming threat of viral hemorrhagic disease including Ebola, necessitating a need for holistic integration of health responses to ensure the necessary health securities to mitigate disease spread and enhance beneficiary experience are in place. 

In 2018, WHO in its 2018 country cooperative strategy stated that South Sudan has some of the worst health outcome indicators globally: Maternal mortality ratio stands at 789 per 100,000 live births, whereas neonatal and under-five mortality rates are 39.3 and 99.2, per 1000 live births respectively (2014). A significant disparity in health status across socio-demographic factors and geographical location is well documented. The country has experienced recurrent humanitarian crises which have deepened and spread since December 2013. Approximately 2.6 million people – about one in every five people in South Sudan - have been forced to flee their homes since the conflict began, including nearly 1.6 million internally displaced people (with more than 50 percent estimated to be children) and more than one million refugees in neighbouring countries. The humanitarian crisis has had devastating effects on food security, child survival, access and utilization of health services and escalation of the economic situation. Some 4.8 million people - more than one in every three people in South Sudan - were estimated to be severely food insecure; 67 out of 80 counties have inadequate or no health care services at all due to dilapidated structures, destruction and closure of health facilities; widespread outbreaks of diseases such as cholera, malaria, measles and other communicable diseases. Communicable diseases remain a major public health problem and are the leading causes of deaths. WVSS will rely on the core pipeline and on its own procured stock of medicines to ensure that health facilities are adequately stocked with essential medicines. 
Through the 2019 humanitarian response plan, WVSS intends to reach the conflict affected  and other vulnerable populations of Warrap state ( Gogrial East, Gogrial West, Tonj North, and Twic counties), Western Equatoria ( Yambio, Nagero, Nzara, Tambura) and Upper Nile (Tambura)  with  primary health services package through PHCUs, PHCCs, and Mobile teams. WVSS will address the looming threat of viral hemorrhagic fever diseases such as Ebola and Rift Valley Fever through prevention and preparedness activities.  WVSS will also address seasonal upsurges in epidemic prone diseases (malaria/meningitis/Hepatitis E) compounded by food insecurity increasing susceptibility to disease and under five mortality. WVSS will also address emerging needs for health assistance fornon-communicable diseases requiring expansion of emergency health assistance including non-communicable pipeline essential medicines and commodities. WVSS will also provide an integrated response to health and protection securities including targeted joint response and evaluation of the implementation of essential clinical packages. WVSS will ensure that there is predictable access to essential health services through targeted risk assessment of communities and health facility functionality.

project_name: STRENGTHENING RESILIENCE OF CONFLICT AFFECTED ADOLESCENTS AND YOUNG PEOPLE IN MMC, JERE, DIKWA, MUNGONU, BAMA & GWOZA LGAs THROUGH QUALITY & NEEDS BASED INTEGRATED PSYCHOSOCIAL SUPPORT.
project_objective:
Going to the Tenth year of the crisis, over 7.7 million people are still in need of life saving assistance and protection, and 1.83 million people are internally displaced across the Northeast (DTM, August 2018). Despite some areas becoming more stable and accessible in 2018, thousands of new arrivals have been recorded in recent months, largely coming from hard to reach areas as a result of insecurity and military operations. Recent displacement to already-crowded areas has a compound effect on severely stretched services.  Currently 41 formal sites across 12 LGAs in Borno are classed as in a ‘high congestion’ status, with 285,000 individuals above camp capacity (OCHA Situation Update, September 2018). In this context, protection needs remain severe, especially for vulnerable groups, children, and adolescents with protection concerns. More, for the 2019 Humanitarian Response Plan, the total population of children in need have been projected to be 3,138,643 while the HRP target is 1,505,647 children (564, 454 boys & 699,414 girls) and caregivers (133, 608 women and 108, 171 men).
From January 2019, GOALPrime Organization Nigeria is proposing to carry project that focuses on providing child care services to the vulnerable children in 10 Adolescents Friendly Spaces  (Camps and Communities) in high priority LGAs of Gwoza, Monguno, Jere, MMC, Bama and Dikwa. The project target to reach 10000 community people with age, gender and culturally appropriate information on child care and child protection; identify and support 15 Community Youth centres, 1500 conflict affected Adolescents with integrated Adolescents Kits for Expression and Innovation in Emergencies Life-Skill programme; 260 conflict affected school children with integrated iDEALS Module Life-Skills Programme in schools; Train 40 school teachers on the implementation of the iDEALS Module and 100 Caregivers of Former CAAGs and SGBV Survivors on Life-Skills (Parents DEAL) as well as Post-re-unification Livelihood Support.

GOALPrime Organization Nigeria shall ensure that the grouping of the Adolescents are age, gender and most importantly, culturally appropriate. The adolescents shall be grouped into younger adolescents (10 - 14yrs) and Older Adolescents (15-18yrs) while for the iDEALS Module, beneficiaries shall be grouped into Children (11-15yrs) and young people (16 - 18yrs). GOALPrime Organization Nigeria shall also ensure that 10% of the target beneficiaries are those with special needs (Disable Adolescents).

GOALPrime will build on the existing community and government structure to develop a community base working and efficient support service to children and adolescents in camps and host communities of priority LGAs.  GOALPrime will work in close coordination with the United Nations Children Fund which it has been supporting in the Capacity Building of Adolescents Kits and iDEAL Module Facilitators in Borno and Yobe States in 2018; as well as in the Roll out of the integrated Adolescents Kits Programme for Former CAAGs in the Borno State Rehabilitation Centre. GOALPrime will set up 12 community based child protection committees and trained them to ensure child protection minimum standards are maintained.  To prevent and respond to family separation of children, the project will organize a community based sensitization of the families to mitigate family separations by providing information to family and children on how to prepare for mass movement as well as teaching children relevant family information.
GOALPrime shall implement this project with the lens of gender, taking into account how the conflict has affected the different gender dimensions such as girls, boys, women, men and the disabled. This will inform and justify the rational for our beneficiaries targeting. GOALPrime shall also deliver the relevant capacity building to both staff and beneficiaries that will foster the mitigation of Sexual exploitation and Abuse to Zero level all through the programme cycle of this project.
GOALPrime shall ensure access to Child Help Desk sessions in the Adolescents Centre. The project will also identify child headed families, women headed families and other vulnerable family and empower them with economic support and support other family to ensure their children remain in the school.

project_name: Multi sector assistance to CAR refugees in Cameroon
project_objective:
1. Fournir la protection internationale aux réfugiés RCA et populations hôtes, plus particulièrement en matière de documentation (enregistrement biométrique), la protection de l’enfance ainsi que la prévention/réponse aux violences basées sur le genre et atteindre les standards internationaux multisectoriels dans l’assistance humanitaire.
2. Renforcer l’accès aux services essentiels de base (éducation, eau, hygiène et assainissement, santé et nutrition) par la construction /réhabilitation des infrastructures communautaires comme des points d’eau et latrines, des salles de classes, des structures de santé dans les zones d’accueil de réfugiés. Cet appui devra également intégrer l’équipement de ces infrastructures.
3. Accroitre des projets d’autonomisation en faveur des réfugiés et populations hôtes fin de diminuer la dépendance à l’aide humanitaire et favoriser l’intégration socioéconomique en attendant un éventuel retour volontaire des réfugiés dans leur pays d’origine, dès que les conditions le permettent.
4. Apporter un soutien institutionnel aux structures étatiques nationales, régionales et locales pour une meilleure prise en charge des réfugiés et populations hôtes sur le long terme à travers toutes les composantes multisectorielles.

project_name: Reducing the impact of malnutrition in Borno state through the provision of curative and preventive services in Magumeri, Bama, Dikwa and Ngala LGAs.
project_objective: The project is intended to provide treatment and prevention services to children under five in Magumeri, Bama, Dikwa and Ngala LGAs, through the establishment and running of various OTP centers where children with severe acute malnutrition will be treated with RUTF. These OTP sites will also be sites where children with moderate acute malnutrition will be supplemented with micronutrient powder. In addition, INTERSOS is establishing a stabilization center in Magumeri LGA and is taking over another in Bama LGA for the treatment of children with complicated Severe Acute Malnutrition. The project intends to mainstream gender-based violence risk mitigation strategies in all of its different parts.

project_name: Education Assistance/Support for Internally Displaced Persons/returnees and host communities in Leer County, Unity States
project_objective: Great commission Operation Mercy is a faith-based national non-profit, humanitarian and development organization, operating in the former Unity and Jonglei states of South Sudan. GCOM’s mission is to support peace and development help grass-root communities and vulnerable groups in the society to get equal access to basic needs and develop their resilience against the effects of conflict, illiteracy, diseases and discrimination. GCOM has operated in Unity states since 2017 Education in Emergency interventions and supported lifesaving assistances to persons will special needs and significant vulnerability assisted. In anticipation for longer-term solutions needs to elevate suffering of the IDPs, returnees, and host communities. This project aims to contribute to the South Sudan strategic objectives ‘’ support at-risk communities to promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks’’ that support recovery and resilient of the affected communities to rebuild and mitigate shocks that associate with lack of essential education supports. The targeted area for this project as per recent findings and reports experience influx of the IDPS and returnees to various payams to start a new lives and livelihoods. GCOM is well positioned to implement the project as per the cluster guidelines and procedures. The organization has trained staff and institutional experience which will give strong leadership to the program and avoid the flaws that fail interventions. Through the experience of the previous projects, GCOM has learnt the importance of closely monitoring the adoption of the key education practices and policies to contribute directly into community development. GCOM presence in the targeted communities will increase the likelihood of success of the project because of the knowledge of the region and experience working in the area. This project is aimed to attract and support most vulnerable returnees and host communities with essential education programmes to rebuild resilience and recovery programs.

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance for Vulnerable Conflict-Affected Populations in Iraq
project_objective: Medair will provide MPCA to vulnerable, conflict-affected populations in Ninewa, Kirkuk and Salah Al-Din governorates, with accessible, functioning markets as well as the possibility for safe cash delivery. One-off cash distributions, multi-month assistance and value vouchers will be provided as appropriate and determined by market functionality. MPCA interventions will be designed with flexibility in order to respond to the changing context; therefore, smart cards, money transfer agents and mobile money transfer will all be considered as potential modalities for distribution. Medair will follow Cash Working Group (CWG) guidelines and standards including the Standard Minimum Expenditure Basket (SMEB) and guidance regarding time and frequency of distributions. Medair has previous experience using mobile money transfer services with AsiaHawala in Tooz district, in Salah Al-Din governorate (2017) as well as with ZainCash in Hawiga district, in Kirkuk governorate (2018). Market assessments and regular monitoring will be conducted to ensure that cash is the most appropriate intervention in each target location.

project_name: Improving the Safety and Security of IDPs in the Mosul Camps
project_objective: This project aims to enhance protection monitoring and support community-based protection initiatives to improve the physical safety and access to services for IDPs and (2) Improve access to legal assistance and legal remedies for highly vulnerable IDPs. Using the methodology of Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP), the project maintains a focus on IDPs with specific protection needs such as persons with perceived IS affiliation and persons at risk of SGBV, and will contribute to the identification, prevention and mitigation of protection risks.

project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle pour les populations affectées par les crises dans le District Sanitaire (DS) de Gao et les Districts Sanitaires de la Région de Ménaka, Nord Mali
project_objective:

Tenant compte de l'évolution des contextes, les modes opératoires et les cibles ont changé.
L'appui portera sur 56 formations sanitaires en SSP ( 30 cscoms du DS de Gao ,3 PSA du DS de Gao , 21 Cscoms de la région de Ménaka ,1 Csref de Ménaka 1 Csref de Gao ) ainsi que 4 cliniques mobiles a Ménaka et 2clinques mobiles a Gao

project_name: Assistance à la protection et au renforcement des moyens d’existence basés sur l’élevage en faveur des ménages vulnérables affectés par la crise pastorale et l’insécurité au Nord du Mali
project_objective: L’objectif global est de rétablir la sécurité alimentaire de 50 000 ménages d’éleveurs (pasteurs et agro pasteurs), soit 300 000 personnes, par un appui à l’amélioration de l’accès aux intrants d’élevage, à l’eau et la promotion de pratiques d’élevage adaptées au contexte de changement climatique

This project is of great importance to the people of Nineveh Province and it is not less important than the provision of food and other basic services. Thus, this project benefits the public and contributes to minimizing the effects of suffering and alleviating the damage that may be inflicted on new generations.
Distributing emergency school teaching/learning materials to vulnerable students
-provide pyschosicial support to children, provide training to teachers, social workers on positive discipline, school code of conducts, PSEA and gender based violence

In accordance with cluster standards, BCF will also support returnee children through psychological support

project_name: School Feeding for Local Children in the Far North (80,000 beneficiaries)
project_objective:
In the Far North region, the Boko Haram insurgency in Nigeria has resulted in 227,581 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (UNHCR, October 2018), who are struggling to survive in strenuous conditions in villages or small towns in the area. The region is predominantly arid and regularly hit by drought and seasonal floods. The arrival of IDPs in food-insecure areas has severely affected host communities as well. As a consequence, the existing chronic vulnerability and structural food insecurity have been aggravated. In addition, access to basic services is also more limited than in other regions of the country including the education.  
WFP will implement a school feeding programme in the Far North region to complement the Government’s education inputs and its work in addressing emergency needs, and to support the education of children affected by crises, particularly girls. It will provide incentives for children to enroll in schools to minimize the risk of forced recruitment into armed groups. The school feeding programme will assist 80,000 school children – of whom 50 percent will be girls – for 165 school days in 12 months with flexibility to ensure that schools in crisis areas are targeted. Home-grown school feeding has been adjusted to 5000 to be piloted in line with recommendations of the Systemic Approach for Better Education Results (SABER). School voucher procurement will incentivize purchases from men and women smallholders to create a value chain.

project_name: Promoting access, inclusive and quality primary education for Nigerian girls and boys, refugees affected by  displacement in the Far North Region
project_objective:
This project aims to contribute to better access, for Nigerian boys and girls refugees affected by displacement, to inclusive and quality primary education relevant to their psycho-social, emotional and cognitive development. 
To achieve our objectives, NRC will promote and support the formal education opportunities at primary level through:
1. The Rehabilitation/construction of school infrastructure: 10 Classrooms will be constructed/rehabilitated and equipped with gender-sensitive desks and blackboards to enable their use. To make these schools safer, sensitive and inclusive, a regard will be done on wash facilities in school (gender sensitive latrines, access to water…) while ensuring access for people with disabilities.
2. Teacher training: In close coordination with the MoE, 100 teachers will be train on P-SEA, Child safeguarding our EIE.  At the end of this training, the teachers who have participated will be better skilled to identify traumatized children and other children with specific needs for possible support or referencing to the appropriate structures.  In order to reinforce protective environment of children, teachers will be trained on DRR in school;
3. Distribution of Learning, teaching and recreational materials: 10,000 school kits and 150 didactic materials will be distributing for pupils and teachers.  In addition, emphasis will be laid on the provision of recreational materials for boys and girls to contribute to their adequate psycho-social development in school.
4. Conduct Alternative Education Program: NRC will conduct in close coordination with the MoE a feasibility study on Accelerated Education Programs for out-of-school and overaged children in the affected areas. The findings of this study will advise NRC and partners on priority needs (out of school children, overaged learners in school or both) and where NRC can respond effectively for 2019. Other activities such as functional literacy and catch-up classes will be developed for children who have had their education interrupted for less than one year will be implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Basic Education (MoE). (target 2000)
5. Revitalisation of governance and dialogue: 10 parents’ teachers’ association (PTAs), 10 mother’s clubs and 10 Children governments will be identified need to train these structures on their roles and responsibilities in school governance and citizenship.
6. Strengthening of pedagogical supervision in the affected areas: NRC will strength the capacities building of the MoE for the organization of pedagogic supervision in order to ensure a good quality of Education
7. Organization of recreational activities: NRC will develop in close coordination with MoE and Ministry of Youth recreational activities within 10 school in order to ensure Children retention in school.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response Project for Conflict affected people in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene
for IDPs/host communities and returnees living in the hard to reach areas of South
Sudan. It will target newly displaced people, returnees and host communities affected by
conflict. The project will focus on providing emergency WASH services to the displaced
persons including most vulnerable host communities and also support the areas of
returns. Focus will be on the repair and construction of Water points, training hand pumps
mechanics, provision of hygiene and dignity kits and  water treatment materials  as well as
hygiene promotion and messaging to increase awareness among the affected population
and reduce the incidence water born diseases. The affected population will also be
supported in the construction of emergency latrines specifically targeting the most
vulnerable and newly displaced people. The project will be delivered through a rapid
response mechanism in project locations selected in line with the cluster prioritizing
process.

The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities for 2019 HRP's SO 1 and SO2. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 14 days for full-fledged delivery of WASH services and other activities per location. The project will also support returnees in settlement as a part of their local integration or returns to their areas of origin. This will be done in an integrated way with other projects being implemented by NRC so that the returnees don’t only receive WASH support but also a source of Food security and Livelihood through the food security projects in the planned locations. Additionally, the project will be implemented together with provision for education in emergencies and Legal Counseling will be made for the returnees where NRC is already implementing such projects e.g. by providing WASH services in schools or communities or return.

 
The WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EP&R) WASH actors where implementation is based on the multi-sector assessments and team involving WASH, Shelter, Food security and emergency Education with protection as a cross cutting theme. In some of the locations, the WASH projects link up with other emergency projects to ensure the beneficiaries receive a comprehensive response package. The project will be implemented in coordination with other players in the sector especially UNICEF for information sharing and use of the cluster core pipeline supplies when needed as well as other WASH cluster members for joint assessments and response when appropriate. The project will also be coordinated with the WASH and Logistics clusters especially in prioritization of locations and delivery of supplies.

project_name: Addressing acute food insecurity in Koch, Leer, Mayendit and Panyijar Counties, Unity State.
project_objective:
In response to the growing humanitarian crisis in Southern Unity, UNIDOR is proposing to enhance the provision of life saving services to 16,000HH conflict affected vulnerable populations in Southern Unity, covering Koch, Leer Mayendit and Panyijiar Counties. These areas are in dire need of humanitarian assistance and UNIDOR already has running projects in these areas providing different interventions. UNIDOR will also integrate food security and livelihood into the already existing UNIDOR's Nutrition, WASH,Protection, Peace and Health programs in Leer, Mayendit, Panyijiar and Koch counties. 
However, based on the March-September 2018 IPC analysis, it is expected that 6.1 million people (59% of the total population) faced Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity at the peak of the lean season (July – August), of whom 47,000 were in Catastrophe (IPC phase 5) and 1.7 million were in Emergency (IPC Phase 4).  
 But with calmness experiencing in many parts of the Country and where agriculture activities took place, food security has improved slightly with the green harvest in September relative to July and August, and further improvements are expected in the post-harvest period between October and December 2018 when the number of people in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse is most likely to reduce to 4.4 million (43% of the total population), with 26,000 in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5).
In the early of the year 2019, an anticipated earlier than normal start of the lean season will result in an estimated 5.2 million (49% of the total population) people in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity between January and March 2019, with 36,000 in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5). KEY IPC FINDINGS: SEPTEMBER 2018- MARCH 2019. Food insecurity continue to rise to yet higher unprecedented levels due to the protracted combination of violence and conflict. The foreseen deterioration can be attributed to a number of factors: these include continuing economic crisis compounded by spiral commodities price increases, continued inflation, poor harvests and early depletion of meager household stocks, continued population displacements resulting from localized violence and conflict, food insecurity, disruption of livelihood activities, collapse of healthcare and social services. The worst affected populations are the conflict affected host communities and Internally Displaced People (IDPs) who are characterized by minimal assets and low purchasing power to satisfy their food needs. In this context women and children, especially girls, represent a vulnerable group. The most vulnerable to hunger are pregnant/lactating mothers, children, elderly and disabled as they may not be able to walk long distances in search of food. The conflict results in gradual erosion of traditional family structures and support mechanisms, domestic violence and child abduction. Girls are at increased risk of early marriage, early pregnancy, contracting HIV/AIDS and dropping out of school. They are exposed to physical, sexual and psychological violence and harassment.
The proposed project will target conflict affected population in Koch, Mayendit, Leer and Panyijiar Counties being supported through provision of cash vouchers/transfer, distribution of crop seeds, vegetable kits and agricultural tools, distribution of fishing kits, Establish demonstration plots,, formation of farmers producers groups, training of farmers of land –harvest, storage and marketing skills, formation of fisher folk groups, training on fish preservation method, marketing skills and provision of cash vouchers/transfer.

project_name: Promoting the inclusion and access of Children with Disabilities to education in the emergency context of the Gaza Strip
project_objective: The current context in the oPt is marked by imposed closures and the stop of peace negotiations between the Israelis and Palestinians. The West Bank is undergoing an acute crisis and continuous demonstrations and clashes. In the Gaza Strip, blockades and political divide continue to marginalize the population. Salary cuts and early retirement have directly impacted most sectors in general, but particularly the education sector. In the 2019 HNO, the Education cluster estimates that children with disabilities are the most affected by the protracted and acute crisis: they lack basic assistive devices that would facilitate their learning in the classroom, and are in need of Psychosocial Support (PSS) and remedial education. Since 2014, HI has strived to improve the access of children with disabilities to education in Gaza. HI also supports 3 special schools to develop child friendly and accessible education environments, to improve the delivery of adapted education services responding to children’s individual needs. In Gaza, the Middle Area and Rafah, HI develops emergency response plans provides PSS and organizes inclusive summer camps in Gaza. Furthermore, HI closely collaborates with mainstream education service providers to build teachers’ capacities to adopt inclusive education strategies. In 2017, HI started directly supporting the capacity-building of educational staff and implemented activities aiming to make schools more accessible. HI also provided specialized education materials and developed technical guidelines on the inclusion of children with disabilities in education. The project’s overall objective is to enhance the access of children with disabilities to inclusive education services in emergencies. This project falls under HRP strategic objectives 2 and 3 and under Education Objectives 1) Increase equitable and safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children and 2) Most vulnerable schools are supported in responding to emergencies through preventive measures, remedial programs and school-based psychosocial services. During this project, HI will work with and technically support 3 partners. The project will respond to the education cluster objectives through the provision of personal support for children with disabilities: enhance their mobility, provide visual and hearing assistive devices, transportation, school kits, education materials and stationaries, school-based structured individual and group psychosocial services. HI will also support the provision of holistic services through referrals to other stakeholders. Furthermore, HI will aim to develop an enabling educational environment through the provision of technical support for mainstream and special education service providers. These will be supported to respond to the needs of affected children through the development of adapted processes and tools benefiting both children with and without disabilities. HI will further provide educational materials, tools and resources and create a welcoming and accessible educational environment for children with and without disabilities. The project will be implemented through partnerships with 3 local organizations in Gaza.

project_name: Improving access to and provision of life-saving maternal and reproductive health services and information to most vulnerable communities in southern West Bank.
project_objective:
This project is aligned to HNO 2018-2020 Cluster Strategic Objectives 1 & 2. UNFPA and its and implementing partners (IPs); Ministry of Health (MOH) and Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) aim to save women’s lives and ensure that, women, men and girls living in Bethlehem and Hebron (H2 and Area C), have access to essential maternal and reproductive health (RH) services, counselling and information, including on well-being and protection from gender based violence (GBV).

This will be achieved through filling gaps in RH services, including access to essential maternal health care and RH service provision and preventing excess mortality and morbidity by;
1) Ensuring a continuum of care and provision of life sustaining RH services, counselling and information including strengthening community preparedness.
2) Provision of essential life-saving maternal health equipment and supplies.
3) Implementation of MISP and training on emergency obstetric care, safe birth etc.
4) Actively engaging communities, strengthening their resilience, supporting coping mechanisms, sensitization, awareness raising and outreach of life saving approaches for RH, including maternal health.
5) Support linking and informing communities to available services with a special focus on marginalized communities and groups including the disabled, elderly etc.

This project is primarily meant to address the immediate response to urgent and critical needs of pregnant and lactating women (around 4,216), especially those living in areas recognized by OCHA as high and medium vulnerable communities (60,310 in area C of Bethlehem, H2 and Hebron). It will also support women of reproductive age (7,245), men (5,175 adults aged 22 years and above), and other vulnerable adolescents; boys (3,060 aged 11-18 years) and girls (5,220 aged 11-18 years), and strengthen the preparedness and resilience of the community and health system for absorbing shocks, saving lives and recovering from crises.

MOH shall serve as the backbone and main partner in establishing and maintaining referral pathways between vulnerable communities and its health facilities. MOH primary care facilities will refer to specialized service provision, particularly secondary health care, including emergency obstetric care, safe birth, and high risk pregnancy management and follow up. PMRS, in close collaboration with Village Council Committees, will use mobile clinics (MCs) to conduct community based RH interventions through service provision and awareness raising in the target areas. 

UNFPA will strengthen RH care and complement UNICEF and WHO interventions targeting <5 and neonates, including nutrition activities. UNFPA will synergize activities for maximum benefit for pregnant and lactating women, women in reproductive age, men and adolescents, to utilize the complete package of life sustaining interventions available. UNFPA will coordinate closely with UNICEF and WHO through the Health Cluster and bilateral coordination meetings that already occur on a regular basis to ensure synergies and avoid duplication. This entails sharing information, coordinating activities for target communities & facilities, and reviewing and verifying equipment and supplies to be procured; to ensure alignment with common frameworks and cooperation plans i.e. Every Newborn Action Plan (ENAP 2017-2020).

The project objectives and activities are aligned with the 2019 health cluster HRP strategy, including responsive and remedial components and is guided by the UNFPA Arab States regional framework for resilience and the UN strategy for Hebron and latest OCHA multi-sectoral needs assessment.  UNFPA aims to improve access to RH services and information, through a strengthened continuum of care, MISP implementation at the primary health care level, support to mobile clinics, reinforcement of referral pathways, increase of community awareness and preparedness for emergencies, and increase of resilience for women, men and girls in these communities.

project_name: Amélioration d'accès adéquat en abris d'urgences et kit/NFI dignité aux populations vulnérables PDIs, rapatriées, retournées, réfugiées et non déplacées dans les zones de retour du nord et touchées par les conflits intercommunautaires et les catastrophes naturelles

Faciliter l’accès au logement des populations vulnérables PDIs, retournées, rapatriées et non déplacées vivant dans les zones de retour du Nord et du centre du Mali. 
Assistance d’urgence aux populations victimes de conflits et catastrophes naturelles permettant leur relèvement rapide.

Les activités visent l'amélioration d'accès au logement et d’abris d'urgence durable et d’urgence aux PDIs, réfugiés, les retournés et les communautés hôtes. Il est estimé que pendant les activités de ciblage, la plupart des personnes identifiées seront

d) Maladie chronique

project_name: Monitoring de protection, Cohésion sociale et Assistance aux vulnérables
project_objective:
L’objectif principal de ce projet est de renforcer la protection des personnes affectées par le conflit armé notamment les rapatriés, les retournés, les PDIs et les populations hôtes dans le centre et le nord du Mali.  Il veillera sur le  respect des droits humains et l’accès égal aux services sociaux de base. 
Le projet permettra la collecte et la documentation des incidents de protection,  le référencement des victimes des violations auprès des structures de prise en charge (humanitaires ou étatiques) et  leur suivi pour des réponses de protection appropriées. En outre, le projet permettra de conduire des analyses de protection par région afin de soutenir la coordination du cluster protection, d'alimenter les discussions de ce cluster, d'orienter les plaidoyers de la communauté humanitaire pour la protection des civils et d'informer les réfugiés maliens dans les pays d'asile sur la situation dans les zones de retour. Le projet identifiera et analysera les types de conflits communautaires et ceux portant sur l'accès aux ressources et organisera des campagnes de sensibilisation en faveur de la cohésion sociale. Le projet contribuera à répondre aux besoins urgents de personnes vulnérables (au travers un appui en activités génératrices de revenus) et aux victimes des violations de droits humains. Enfin, le projet mettra en place un mécanisme de redevabilité afin que les personnes relevant du mandat du HCR et en contact avec le partenaire d'exécution puissent exprimer leur in/satisfaction et déposer des plaintes.

project_name: Supporting Reproductive, Maternal and Newborn health care services in hard-to-reach areas and for all vulnerable people in Libya
project_objective:
As a result of the crisis in Libya, many public health facilities providing reproductive health (RH) care services, including emergency obstetric care are either damaged, difficult to access or suffer from severe shortages in material and human resources leading to compromised access to lifesaving care and consequently increased maternal mortality. Maternal Mortality ratio reached up to 90 deaths per 100,000 live births in some hospitals in Libya.

The overall objective of this intervention is to avert excess Maternal and Neonatal Mortality through implementation of Minimum Initial Services Package (MISP) for Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) in crisis.

The intervention will focus on providing lifesaving care for women and newborns throughout the continuum of care from community to primary healthcare facilities and to hospitals for all people in target mantiqas (Tripoli, Benghazi, Sirt, Al Jufrah, Ghat, Sabha, Ejdabia, Kufrah, Murzuq and Ubari).

Major activities are: deployment of Emergency Medical Teams (EMT) in facilities and through mobile clinics, provision of essential lifesaving medicines, Emergency Reproductive Health Kits and medical equipment, health education on danger signs during pregnancy, delivery and post-delivery care, including safe referral to facilities, support the establishment of a maternal and newborn death surveillance and response (MNDSR) system and effective reproductive health coordination. With significant investment in supporting the capacity of health system and practitioners, this projects offers and opportunity to support system resilience and sustainability.
