project_objective: Islamic Relief Niger (IRN) propose cette intervention de 3 mois en période de soudure pour apporter un appui aux populations sous pression de l’insécurité alimentaire dans les Départements de Ouallam et Dogondoutchi. Le projet vise à améliorer l’accès à une alimentation acceptable. En 2019, les personnes dans le besoins sont estimées respectivement à 90 109  et 20 844. IRN va distribuer des kits alimentaires pour à 4000 bénéficiaires (2000 par département). Aussi, 900 ménages vont bénéficier de Cash For Work et recevoir des kits de résilience composée de semences de céréales et légumineuses.

project_name: Early recovery support to conflict-affected communities in South Syria
project_objective: This project aims at restoring agricultural and urban livelihood opportunities in South Syria in rural and urban areas. In rural areas, this will be achieved through a combination of action at the individual and the community level. At the individual level, agricultural vouchers will be provided to 1,200 mid-size farmers. Vouchers will be redeemed in exchange of seeds, fertilizers and tools to resume their agricultural production. Farmers will also take part to training on climate-smart agriculture and best agricultural practices. At the community level, the project will focus on the rehabilitation of communal agricultural assets which serve the communities living in the area. These will include public or community-based irrigation channels, wells, and other small agricultural facilities which have fallen into disrepair or been damaged by the crisis. In urban areas, 36 existing businesses will be supported with cash grants and training which will enable them to restore or expand their business. An estimated 9,416 individuals will benefit from the project.

project_name: Improving the access to WASh services of both host communities and IDPs in Idleb  governorate
project_objective:
Violet  aims to respond to the increasing needs in WASH activities by implementing the following activities:
1. supporting the water units and water networks by covering the water units personnel salaries, operation costs, maintenance, and rehabilitation to the water systems and water units in Al Ma'ra and Al Janudya. 
2. Expanding the existing sewage system in kafrnbol through the construction of 3000 meters sewage network and link it with the existing sewage system.
3. Garbage collection and expanding the landfill in Salqin. 
4. Constructing 160 latrines in A'aidoon camp replacing the old prefabricated and unfunctional latrines.

The project seeks to make a balance between males and females, girls and boys focusing on disabilities basic needs category. The project aims to meet the specific needs of women and men/ boys and girls by providing equal opportunities to access. Also, gender-sensitive WASH facilities and considering the needs of the disabled and children with special needs will be taken into account by installing ramps in front of the latrines and other WASH facilities. Moreover, sex will be taken into account when constructing the latrines where they will be sex-based separated, to ensure the privacy and dignity as well as the equal access of all project's beneficiaries.
The civil community will be engaged in the project design and implementation through signing MoUs to ensure the local participation and ownership of WASH services and facilities. Moreover, the project will contribute to increasing the awareness of the community concerning the hygiene and good WASH practices either through distributing awareness brochures or through conducting awareness and hygiene promotion campaigns.
Furthermore, in order to ensure the project's sustainability, Violet will rehabilitate WASH facilities (water units, sewage system, and latrines ..etc) and then these facilities will be handed over to the community at the end of the project to be operated by them. Moreover, the managerial skills and cost recovery training will be provided  for the operators, local authorities, and community representatives so they can continue providing the services when the project ends

Additionally, Violet will distribute 2300 Hygiene kits for the newly displaced people who fled to the much safer areas in northern Idleb and northern Aleppo governorates

project_name: Improve Access to Health Services for Pregnant and Lactating Women and Children under five years in Syria
project_objective: The purpose of this project is to reduce the specific vulnerability of pregnant and lactating women and children under five years through improved access to quality, safe and dignified Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescence (RMNCH+A) services and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) in three governorates in Syria (Al-Hassakeh, Rural Damascus, and Aleppo).  Access to primary healthcare services, including RMNCH+A and MHPSS, is a key priority within the health sector where at least 5.2 million women of reproductive age need RMNCH+A services alone. In addition, recent evidence of 137 low and middle-income countries across the world suggests that the cost of neglecting maternal psychosocial risk factors is huge and that addressing psychosocial factors among perinatal women can have a significant impact on child growth and well-being (Fawzi, et al., 2019). Given the distance and safety and displacement risks and the disrupted services, many women were unable to seek medical support for their RMNCH+A needs. Besides, physical hardship and mental trauma often complicate the pregnancy and the delivery, which is also exacerbated by inadequate access to MHPSS. Ensuring a large and safe physical access to those services is key to reducing the risks on pregnant and lactating women and children under five years of age.  Overall, there remains a lack of available, qualified and trained staff, inadequate medical referral systems to address the needs for women who develop complications or require emergency obstetric and newborn care and limited financial means for supporting health education and public health awareness about topics related to these services. Therefore, the project aims to improve access to quality healthcare by strengthening the local institutional primary healthcare capacity in which at least one primary healthcare centre will be rehabilitated, and at least one mobile medical service will be mobilized to reach 10,000 beneficiaries in pockets of vulnerable populations in Rural Damascus, Aleppo and Hassakeh. A total of 30 healthcare staff (of which 15 are males and 15 are females) will be trained and mentored on-the-job to ensure implementation of national protocols and guidelines consistent with quality and resilient primary healthcare delivery. Additionally, prevention and treatment of RMNCH+A and MHPSS conditions targeting PLWs and children under five are provided in the targeted public healthcare facilities and mobile facilities where specific support is strengthened to deliver RMNCH+A and MHPSS services and referral to specialized care for children and women with urgent cases will be strengthened.

project_name: Syrian Education for Access and Quality (SEAQ)
project_objective:
The project aims to increase safe and equitable access to formal and non formal education for crisis affected children and youth (aged 5 17 years) and improve the quality of formal and non formal education for children and youth (aged 5 17 years) within a protective environment. The project will be implemented through ADRA Syria education team, closely in coordination MoE and related DoEs ensuring the protection of all beneficiaries through a ‘do not harm’ approach. ADRA Syria through this project will improve access to formal and non-formal education and learning opportunities for girls and boys by creating safe and protective environments for 15,500 children who have been affected by the crisis. This will be done through education interventions within the governorates of Rural Damascus, Quneitra, Homs, Aleppo, Dara’a and Deir Alzour. ADRA Syria through the project will enhance the formal and non – formal education level for the children, boys and girls, in the same rehabilitated schools. This will include a holistic program with psycho-social, familial and educational support, encouraging the engagement of mothers and fathers in educational activities. 

ADRA will coordinate with key stakeholders to ensure the most vulnerable boys and girls are identified in the target locations, and ADRA will conduct comprehensive needs assessments in the areas identified to locate OOSC and students with priority educational needs.

project_name: Syria Water And Sanitation for Health (SWASH)
project_objective:
This project aims to provide life-sustaining and life-saving WASH services to 350,000 beneficiaries in conflict-affected, newly-accessible or Hard-To-Reach (HTR) areas in the governorates of Idlib, Aleppo, Homs, Deir-Ez-Zor, Rural Damascus, Damascus, Dara’a and Quneitra.  ADRA will provide life-sustaining assistance to 300,000 men, women, boys and girls through the rehabilitation of water networks, sewerage system rehabilitation, the distribution of household and community water tanks and garbage bins as well as debris removal in support of WASH Objective 1. ADRA will provide life-saving assistance through the rehabilitation of WASH facilities in last resort sites including camps, collective centers, transit centers and informal settlements for newly-displaced populations as well as the distribution of hygiene kits benefitting 50,000 men, women, boys and girls in support of WASH Objective 2.

ADRA will target highly vulnerable communities with WASH severity scale of level 4 or above in 7 governorates including Aleppo (Jebel Saman), Deir-Ez-Zor (eastern rural DeZ - Al Mayadeen, Al Boukamal, Al Shaarah, Mo Hasan, Mehkan, Ak Koureyah Sbekhan, and western rural DeZ including Ayash, Al Shmeteya, Al Treef, Al Tebni, Al Khraytah), Rural Damascus ( Kafr Batna, Darayya, Babella, Maliha, Duma, Qatana, Kiswah), Quneitra (Beir Ajam, Breiq), Dara’a (Kherbet Ghazala and Jizeh) and Idlib (Idlib). The target areas for WASH intervention will be either HTR, newly-accessible or conflict-affected and will include newly-displaced populations, self-organized IDP returnees, over-burdened host communities, People with Disabilities (PwDs), female-headed households (FHH) or IDPs residing in last resort sites.

The project aims to increase the resilience of the Syrian population through the provision of WASH services and the mitigation of protection risks to men, women, boys and girls as well as highly vulnerable groups such as older adults and People with Disabilities. In IDP camps and settlements, there is increased risk of GVB for women, young children, children (boys and girls), adolescent and young adult females who must travel distances to WASH facilities often without protective lighting. The lack of household-level access to drinking water places a financial and physical burden upon male and female middle-aged and older adults as well as People with Disabilities to procure safe drinking water. In addition, inadequate needs assessments may result in hygiene services neglecting the needs of young children, children, older adults, and people with disabilities.

SWASH Project will be regularly monitored and evaluated by gender-balanced project staff including technical, social, education and MEAL staff and volunteers to ensure comprehensive and neutral monitoring is achieved. ADRA staff will solicit feedback on project design and implementation from young children, children, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults and older adults to ensure the best coverage of needs and safety of all beneficiaries, particularly for hygiene kits, the location of WASH facilities and garbage bins. Beneficiary feedback and ADRA staff monitoring will guide project modifications in all activities.

project_name: Life saving and sustaining food and livelihood assistance for the most vulnerable households of Dara’a, As-Sweida and Rural Damascus Governorates.
project_objective:
The aim of project is to contribute to ensuring food security in Syria through the implementation of multiple actions that are needed to adequately address access, stable availability and utilization of food. Emergency response support will be provided to respond to the needs on newly arrived returnees (from inside and outside Syria) and newly accessible communities. At the same time, food and lifesaving emergency agricultural assistance will target the most vulnerable population to support them to meet their food and nutritional needs. Finally, the project will provide agro livelihood support to increase self resilience, strengthen resilience and reduce the dependency on aid of the most vulnerable Syrian population.
Lifesaving and life sustaining interventions will contribute to the achievement of the Sector Objective 1”Improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance” through provision of short term food assistance, monthly food assistance and bread.  Resilience building will be supported through distribution of agro inputs (seeds, fertilizer, irrigation kits for instance), provision of Protection Food rations with agro kits, training on farming techniques, provision of poultry kits (including fodder, vet drugs and assistance) and it will contribute to the Sector Objective 2 “Support self reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives”
Activities will be implemented to support the most vulnerable families across the districts of   Dara’a, As-Sweida Governorates and in the districts of Rural Damascus and Duma of Rural Damascus Governorate and will reach a total of 2,250 HHs with short term food assistance response for a period of at least one month. Subsequently to emergency rations and based on their assessed food insecurity, IDPs and returnees HHs, along with food insecure or at risk of food insecurity families among the host communities  will be supported with monthly food assistance for a period of at least 8 months, reaching a total of 3,175 HHs. To decrease the dependency on food assistance and to promote the self resilience and dignity of beneficiaries, the action will provide agro inputs (seeds and poultry) for family consumption to a total of 2,680 HHs, out of the 3,175 HHs. The livelihood activities will only target host community and returnees. 
In the selection of beneficiaries specific focus will be given to IDPs and returnees, but also to those families who have no or limited financial ability to access to food, such as female, elderly and People with Disabilities headed Households and unaccompanied children and to those groups who have only limited access to income to cover food family needs for long period and are forced to adopt negative copying mechanisms (unskilled or seasonal workers for instance).
During the preparation and implementation of the activities, COOPI will ensure the coordination with local authorities and the participation of the communities, also thanks to the constant field presence ensured by the establishment of community kitchens and protection centres in project areas. Coordination will be ensured with the FSA Sector and its members but also with international and national actors active in the same villages in order to implement harmonized response, avoid overlapping and to promote synergies. Synergies will be also promoted by COOPI with other projects submitted to HRP 2019 in the governorates of this Action, such as Rural Damascus, Dara’a and As Sweida to promote an integrated approach to Education and Protection needs within the local communities

project_name: Support to water systems and Emergency water provision and hygiene promotion in the north of Syria
project_objective: The projects aims to provide support to water systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria through support to water quality assurance and operation and maintenance of water supply systems, and to deliver humanitarian WASH supplies, services and improve hygienic behaviour and practices of most vulnerable people through provision of water, distribution of essential WASH NFIs & Hygiene promotion, and improve access to lifesaving/ emergency WASH facilities and services.

project_name: Youth Charity Deir Ez-Zor Mobile Medical Clinics
project_objective:
Deir al-Zour is a city located in the east of Syria, and one of the most affected areas by the Syrian crisis, with a damage exceeds 75% of the city including medical centers and related health sector facilities, with hazardous remnants of war scattered everywhere, such as landmines and unexploded ordnance. However, the area is now considered under government control. 
Deir Ez-Zor including (Al Jourah & Al Qusur and Al Hamidiyyeh with neighboring countryside) is an area that has a population of over 500,000. Most residents are currently very poor and internally displaced after seven years of war and encircle, resulted in more than 105,300 of them need medical care & services. High percentage of the population are children and families who rely on women as their main breadwinners, and Dummar Youth Charity will provide its medical services to 10,000 of the aforementioned 105,300. 
Due to the high population of Deir Ez-Zor including surroundings and the inability of many of them to leave the area (due to security/financial reasons i.e. medical compensations). The project aims at establishing Two Mobile Medical Clinics in Deir Ez-Zor area and surroundings to provide free medical services with referral system, and find job opportunities to jobless people of the area (mainly women).
The exact locations of the two mobile medical clinics in Deir Ez-Zor will be in Al Hamidiyyah near Sqaure and in Al Jourah near Law Faculty Square (respectively). And referral system will be executed in coordination with local hospitals in the area and with hospitals (to beneficiaries who are unable to travel) and in Damascus (to beneficiaries how are able to travel). And medical services do not include medication.

project_name: Promoting the Nutritional status of children under 5 and of women affected by the Syrian crisis
project_objective:
The current crisis in Syria has led to a widespread deterioration in what was a well-functioning and predominantly public healthcare system with the destruction or disruption of health facilities.
Additionally, population movement and the corrosion of public services and infrastructure have increased the risk of outbreaks of previously controlled epidemics. 
Results of MoH (2018) rapid nutrition assessments of children age 6-59 months and PLWs in East Aleppo (2017) shows the incidence of GAM rate is 8.5 % in children and 20.8% maternal malnutrition.
4.70 million girls and boys under five years of age and pregnant and lactating women are at risk of under nutrition and in need of preventive and curative nutrition services in 2018. 84,200 girls and boys aged 6-59 months are acutely under nourished, of which around 19,000 are in the severe category and are 11 times more likely to die than well-nourished children. 865,295 girls and boys under five years of age suffer from micronutrient deficiencies. 3.05 million girls and boys under 5 years of age require optimal feeding for adequate nutrition status while 1.55 million pregnant and lactating women require preventive nutrition services.

project_name: Reinforcement and improvement of the psychological wellbeing of WMGB through structured PSS, PFA, CP and robust Risk education.
project_objective: This intervention is inserted in the framework of the strategic objectives 1, 2 and 3 of the HRP 2019 and is designed to complement the efforts of the Protection sector in Syria. This project aims to contribute to the reinforcement and improvement of the psychological wellbeing of women, men, girls and boys (WMGB) through structured and comprehensive PSS, capacity building, awareness campaign and robust Risk Education. The project targets mainly IDPs and returnees in need of protection in Homs, Hama, Tartous, Lattakia, and Quneitra governorates. This intervention will be implemented in partnership with SARC. The project plans to provide structured PSS to those in need, Case management will also be conducted through  individual assessment and Each SARC team is accompanied by a CM, who would be providing on-site induction/training for SARC volunteers who are acting as activity facilitators, on identification of PoCs with special/ specific needs. So PoCs with special needs are identified and referred to CM by SARC volunteers, also CM through direct observation may identify cases him/herself and may also receive referrals from other partners. CM will then do individual assessment through a session with the PoC, and using TDH standard forms ( based on IASC standards) and decide the action plan for each case. Even though it is a mobile team, we do usually have a temporary facility provided by SARC ( SARC sub-branch, or another facility, including a rented facility as a choice) where privacy for CM sessions could be guaranteed. CM to decide the needs of the case ( provisioning of material, in-kind assistance) and providing what is available through project resources/ funds, and if needs are beyond that, refer case to respective service provider/ parner based on referral mechanism composed on field data of present partners or provided by sector if available. GBV/SGBV cases are also referred to GBV actors. Cases are handled by CM in consultation with TDH PSS expert and technical supervisor in field, and SARC specialists. TdH-IT will conduct Capacity building at the beginning of the intervention (through TdH Expert) on various topics including (PSS, PFA, CP, Resiliency, Life Skills, Communication, and MRE. As per past experience SARC will nominate double the number of volunteers needed, where TdH will build their capacity and select top volunteers for the intervention.

project_name: Provide life-saving assistance to reduce acute humanitarian needs and excess mortality among the most vulnerable people in Somalia
project_objective: The project will provide life-saving and life-sustaining integrated multi-sectoral assistance to vulnerable communities of Awdal , Bakool, Banadir, Bari, Bay, Galgaduud, Hiraan,Lower Juba, Mudug, Nugaal, Sanaag, Sool and aims to reach a total of 550,453 IDPs and host communities contributing to 40%  of the cluster target in the targeted geographies. Its objective is to improve equitable access to quality emergency and essential lifesaving health services for crisis affected aimed at reducing avoidable morbidity and mortality and Mitigate impact and respond to shocks to the affected population as a result of conflict and public health emergencies. This will be achieved by supporting the Somalia governments and communities to be able to delivery essential package of health free services to communities with acute humanitarian needs using developments programs as a platform for immediate responses. The required budget for the delivery of the project is USD 3 million.

project_name: Distribution of winterization kits for vulnerable families in Dar’a, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Der ez-Zor and Al Quneitra
project_objective:
Since the break out of the Syrian conflict more than seven years, Syria has become a battleground for many world and local powers. Armed groups were emerged and the war has left what can be described as one of the worst humanitarian crises of all time.
Millions of people have been killed or forced to flee their homes. Families are struggling to survive inside Syria, or make a new home in neighboring countries. 
Eight years of conflicts were enough to weak the Syrian citizens and create execrable humanitarian situation. The degree of resilience and positive coping mechanism of the affected population have reduced due to the protracted nature of the conflict. The economic and social situation in Syria continues to decline and severely affect everybody especially those who have been displaced from or returned to their homes. Statistics reveal that Two-thirds of Syrians are living in extreme poverty, unable to meet basic food and non-food needs. The main reasons for poverty are loss of property and jobs, loss of access to public services, including health and clean water, and rising food prices.
According to HNO 2019,  over 75 per cent of communities reported that clothing had been unaffordable or unavailable over the last 3 months. Unavailability and unaffordability of individual items are linked, indicating that limited supplies may be driving higher prices.
In spite of the fact that number of PIN in 2018 has decrease comparing to 2019 one, people in Syria are resorting to harmful coping strategies such as depletion of assets and increasing debt in order to meet their needs.
It was reported that 4,403,329 people are in need for NFIs assistances in Syria, 
The purpose of this project is to provide winterization items to people living in the most severity areas as GOPA has access to Dar’a, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Der ez-Zor and Al Quneitra. 
This project will target 50,000 Individual beneficiaries included 20,000 child will receive winter clothes and shoes

project_name: Child and Youth Education Pathways  for vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
NRC’s project will contribute to Education sector HRP objectives 1, 2 and. NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and hybrid modalities. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality

The Education intervention forms part of NRC Syria’s integrated response. The Education team will continue working in close collaboration with the ICLA, Shelter/WASH, and Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) programmes to enable conflict and displacement-affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. We must ensure pathways back to learning and integration into formal education and acknowledgement of previous learning through supportive policies (accreditation, certification, examinations, and documentation).  NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable children and youth across Syria through the delivery of its three-pronged Child Education Pathways (CEP) and Youth Education Pathways (YEP) programmes. Each response modality (Emergency, Transition, and Recovery) is designed to ensure that conflict and displacement-affected children and youth are provided with age and context-specific educational pathways. All three modalities have been designed to provide equal access to and to welcome all out of school children and youth, prioritising those that have been displaced by the conflict and are returning home from both inside and outside Syria. All three modalities include capacity development opportunities for teachers, trainers, facilitators and coaches and will be implemented in cooperation with the ICLA, Shelter/ WASH and LFS programmes and partners. 
The target group of the Education Programme in Syria is defined as conflict and displacement-affected children (aged 6-17) and youth (aged 15-18), including Syrian IDPs, IDP and refugee returnees, host community members, and Iraqi refugees. The exact target group definition will vary for the different response options: 
•	Emergency Response activities will target newly displaced and returnee children (6-14 years) and youth (15-18 years); 
•	Transitional Response will target out of school children and youth in contexts of long-term displacement and prolonged absence from school with activities tailored on their specific context (see more below); 
•	Recovery activities will target vulnerable populations living in post-conflict and/or stabilised non-camp settings (see more below). 
Teachers, facilitators and trainers will also be targeted across the 3 response options, working in NRC programmes in formal and non-formal education settings. Whilst equal access will be provided to both male and female educators, considering the current scarcity of male educators, those present will be actively encouraged to participate, in an effort to provide positive male role models in all activities. 
For all NRC Education activities, civil documentation will not be a pre-requisite to receive assistance.

project_name: NFI Emergency Response for Affected communities in Deir EzZor, Rural Damascus and Aleppo.
project_objective:
Oxfam is proposing a 12 months action aiming to reach the total of 75,000 most vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in worst affected locations of  Deir EzZor (Al Mayadin, Deir-ez-Zor, Khasham,Tabni), Rural Damascus (Kafr Batna) and Aleppo (Hadher, Tall Ed-daman, As-Safira, Menbij) governorates. 
The action aims to: Provide life-saving and life-sustaining NFI and shelter support through a) Provision of core and essential NFIs b) Provision of seasonal and supplementary NFIs and shelter.
The Action is informed by rapid assessments, observation visits, Oxfam's ongoing work in the three governorates, and reliable secondary data, including the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2019. The action is designed to meet specific NFIs needs of affected populations suitable to access situation and security challenges; this includes implementation through reliable and experienced public health promotion volunteers and focal points and Oxfam local partners. 
Oxfam is proposing to deliver 7,500 family winter Jacket Kits (1 kit per family consisting of 1 man, 1 woman and 3 children waterproof jackets) along with 37,500 blankets for 7500 Family (5 blankets per family).
In January 2018, in Deir EzZor , after the area was freed from ISIS, Oxfam was amongst the first few humanitarian actors on the ground providing humanitarian assistance.  Its interventions in the area included the distribution of family winterization kits (25,700 household HHs) and distribution of mini hygiene kits to (20,000 HHs).
In October and November 2018, in Tal Rifaat in Aleppo and Arbin and Harasta in Rural Damascus, Oxfam respectively supported 10,750 IDPs children from East Ghouta and 6,400 children displaced from Afrin with basic clothing.
Oxfam is currently preparing for the distribution of 5,000 family winter jackets and 11,500 blankets in Sheikh Maqsoud area in Aleppo city.
Building on previous experiences and based on Oxfam’s findings and communications with beneficiaries for their urgent needs, Oxfam is proposing to replicate this activity in Deir EzZor, Rural Damascus and Aleppo, specifically providing for all the members in the family including different groups based on gender and age.by procuring kits in advance of winter. Distribution would take place for vulnerable families wherever the need is highest at the time of intervention.
The activity has additional impact, as Oxfam is keen to ensure that the procured NFIs would be locally manufactured focusing on women’s employment (supplier selection criteria would support production of materials by women).  Through the proposed project, Oxfam will be supporting the IDPs and vulnerable affected families as well as returnees through NFIs distribution in Deir EzZor, Rural Damascus and Aleppo in specific areas which experience hard conditions during winter and continue to need seasonal support.

project_name: Pro- Resilient Action inside Syria- Oxfam HRP EFSVL Project
project_objective:
Oxfam aims at addressing systemic risks (agro-ecological, local governance, gender inequalities, social tensions) by enhancing socio-economic rights and capacities of 3000 conflict affected households in Qalamoun- Rural Damascus of Syria; all family members (M&F inclusive) lost the ability to enjoy equal access to livelihood opportunities then fulfill their basic rights. Women and adolescent’s girls may face particularly protection risks as a harmful coping mechanism such as child marriage, physical and sexual harassments, etc.   EFSVL team is addressing this vulnerability through immediate and sustainable solutions for start-up of micro-businesses, efficient linkages with suppliers and markets, entitlements and enhancing community resilience, including local capacities for  social cohesion. 

The results will be achieved through a range of outputs including setting-up 60 greenhouses, 1000 kitchen garden toolkits; immediate support to 1000 conflict affected vulnerable livestock breeders; strengthened productive capacity of 35 dairy, bakery and other food processors; technical and managerial skill building of 35 participants; training of 7 local veterinarian, drilling  3 new wells, powering  3 existing wells with solar system and  rehabilitation of 3 boreholes will provide income generation opportunities to conflict impacted vulnerable women, men and their families ; bring improvements in market services, soil and water conservation; provision of agricultural inputs; technical support for improved agricultural production; collaboration, networking and alliance building with a range of stakeholders and enhancing communities’ capacity to respond to shock and stresses as a result of conflict.
During the project duration, agricultural and food production will focus on two agricultural seasons of critical crops in the targeted locations. These commodities will be selected based on local seasonal calendar, farmers’ skills and their access to inputs, consultation with communities and potential for supplementing food needs and will directly support the targeted beneficiaries and indirectly their supported families (elderly, boys and girls all inclusive).Furthermore, the project design is paying attention to very specific needs of targeted women and men; distributed kits will be designed to accommodate the differences between women and men. Time and distribution locations will be gender sensitive. Special attention will be paid for impact of intervention on power dynamics in targeted communities to avoid stressing the negative social norms in roles and responsivities of women and men.
This action is based on Oxfam’s approach on developing resilient livelihoods, which integrates humanitarian relief, socioeconomic development, and empowered advocacy through improving social protection/safety nets and strengthening market system. This approach provides a coherent and gender sensitive framework to achieve the action objective, through its processes that concurrently address short-term targeted agricultural outcomes and spillover effects from strengthening of market system. 
Through this action, target households will increase capacity to cope with shocks and avoid the harmful survival mechanism such as early, forced and child marriages, child laboring, etc.  It increase the levels of agriculture production and income. Through Oxfam’s approach, this will strengthen community organizations, and enhance their ability to access services.

project_name: NFI distributions to support vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in conflict affected areas in Deir-ez-Zor and Daraa governorates, Syria
project_objective:
This project’s main goal is to provide NFI support to the conflict affected population. The consequences of the conflict have been particularly severe and have converted many parts of the different governorate into extremely hard-to-reach areas, where people suffer from extreme needs, due to the enormous destruction and being cut off from access to markets. Displaced people, returnees and the overburdened host communities face tremendous struggles while trying to provide basic products for their families and ensure a dignified survival. With this NFI support, the living conditions of 198.000 people in areas with high rates of displacement and large scale destruction will be improved and the basics of a dignified life will provided through the distribution of 66.000 NFI kits.
The number of kits, kit components and targeted locations have been determined after assessing the overall situation in the regions, needs of the population and timing of the intervention.
The project is in line with the NFI sector strategic objectives and priorities of this allocation, with a primary goal of delivering urgent assistance to people in need, prioritizing vulnerable groups, according to the identified needs in the areas of intervention.

project_name: Enhance Education basic services and learning environment for children, teachers and volunteers among returnee, host community and IDPs in rural areas of Hama and Damascus.
project_objective:
The hereby action aims at providing life-saving and life-protecting assistance to vulnerable Syrian in Eastern Ghouta, rural Hama and Dara’a, responding to acute needs in the Education sector, more precisely Education in Emergencies (EiE). All targeted governorates have been identified as relevant for intervention, with regards to the needs identified, to the TGH operational capacities, to which add potentialities for new emergency needs, such as population displacement and returns. First, the presence of TGH in the areas targeted will ease the implementation of the different activities. Second, the needs assessment conducted by TGH team attest of acute needs in terms of Education in both governorates, especially regarding the number of Out-Of-School Children, the learning environment (school destructions and damages) and the education staff capacities. In the frame of a resilient and long-term approach, it is necessary to empower the future generation that will be needed in the perspective of the country’s reconstruction.
To respond to the Education needs identified, TGH estimated relevant to focus on Non-Formal Education activities, reintegration of Out-of-School children into the education system, as well as light rehabilitations of schools. 
Most of the teachers, especially in Eastern Ghouta, did not attend any training before being enrolled in the targeted schools and are working there either as “non-formal” teachers or as “volunteers”. Furthermore, the field assessment showed that most of the volunteers are female workers, this project aims at reinforcing their integration into the job market and at the same time to promote gender equality. At this extent, the education staff will be supported through adapted and required training promoting conflict-sensitive approaches. TGH will reinforce schools’ staff capacities regarding their knowledge and capacities in NFE and PSS and accompany them in the implementation of these activities in the targeted schools.
In order to favour the well-being of children attending school and foster the reintegration of Out-of-School Children, education facilities will be improved thanks to light rehabilitations. The provision of school kits and recreational materials will also contribute to improve learning environments, contributing to attract OSS children to go back to school but also convince the parents that their children are safe and that the time they spend in public schools is a well-spent time.
Besides the proposed improvement of learning spaces and the implementation of NFE and PSS activities, remedial classes will be organized in order to complete the curriculum B developed by the MoE. The different components designed within the hereby project will take part to the reintegration of OOS children into the education system but also prevent the registered children to drop-out. 
The identification of Out-of-School children will involve key stakeholders (DoE, Schools’ principals), but also Community-Based Education Child Protection Committees (CBECPC) that will be created within thin project. 
This project will benefit to all the children attending school and NFE activities, with no specific eligibility criteria in accordance with the do no harm principle.

project_name: WASH assistance to conflict-affected and rural underserved vulnerable communities in Syria
project_objective:
The proposed action aims at providing assistance to conflict affected rural underserved vulnerable communities in Syria, in Eastern Ghouta, rural Hama and Dara’a. Through its life-saving component, the action responds to WASH needs through the provisory provision of safe water pending the completion of the rehabilitation of damaged water facilities, within an approach combining emergency response with resilience building. WASH-in-Schools activities are also planned, responding to both WASH needs and WASH-related Protection issues, in particular with regards to gender. The proposed action will complement TGH current activities in rural areas of Hama and Damascus, allowing filling identified gaps and building and scaling up from TGH achievements to date, benefiting to a broaden humanitarian response in Syria. In addition, by targeting the Hama governorate, the action will contribute to the larger contingency plan anticipating potential large return movements from the neighbouring governorate of Idleb. The targeted locations have been selected with regards to TGH current operational capacity, which guarantees an immediate start of the action complying with the demand for rapid answers to the identified needs. The targeted locations however had been initially selected due to their high vulnerability with regards to their recent history in relation to the conflict. Most targeted locations have a 6 score on HNO’s vulnerability scale, and those with a lesser score (3) are in the vicinity of areas prone to conflict and potentially source of new displacement thus humanitarian needs. TGH aims through the hereby proposed action to implement a comprehensive project through WASH activities, meeting basic needs in the sector, but also protection issues faced by the targeted population. Outcomes have been designed with the concern of integrating protection components to the planned activities. 
To respond to the most acute WASH needs identified during the assessment, TGH considers relevant to continue water trucking (WT) activities in the localities where it already operates and where no alternatives exist yet (EG). In accordance with TGH principles, WT must be envisaged as a last resort. The action has been designed in line with this principle and defines a clear exit strategy limiting WT to an emergency response phase. The provision of safe water via trucks will be implemented in support to longer term alternatives such as boreholes and water network rehabilitations – the latter falling within local stakeholders’ responsibility. Following the different coordination mechanisms developed during the assessment period with other humanitarian actors involved in the WASH sector in order to avoid overlaps, TGH identified among its current localities of intervention 3 localities where it will ensure the rehabilitation of safe water sources, and 7 other where other identified agencies will carry out similar interventions. WT is also planned for those locations where no humanitarian agency has plan for restoring the access to water, for a limited period of a maximum 5 months during which TGH, as an active member of the WASH cluster, will inform WASH partners and line authorities of its plans and advocate for their intervention. In Hama and Dara’a, TGH will rehabilitate water systems damaged by the conflict without being engaged in WT, as authorities and private entities already ensure the trucking of water, a situation towards which local communities could develop some resilience. In Hama as in EG, the proposed intervention will allow responding to the current widely spread consumption of unsafe water, pumped in unsafe sources with no treatment systems.

project_name: Provision of NFIs and seasonal items to IDPs, returnees and affected host communities
project_objective: UNHCR as a lead agency coordinating the NFI responses in Syria and from Gaziantep (Turkey), through this project aims to provide life saving and life sustaining NFI support through distribution of NFIs and seasonal supplementary items to IDPs, returnees and affected host communities. Based on the HNO for 2019, the NFI Sector estimates that 4.4 million people require NFI assistance in Syria in 2019. UNHCR’s NFI programme recognizes the different needs and vulnerabilities of boys, girls, men and women of different ages and strives to address the specific needs of each group across the range of NFI interventions. Considering their vulnerability, IDPs living in hard to reach locations, female headed households, persons with disabilities, and elderly persons at risk will form the priority groups of UNHCR's NFI programme, particularly those among the high numbers of newly displaced IDPs and returnees requiring core, including cash/voucher for NFI, supplementary and seasonal assistance (winter/summer items) including cash/voucher for NFIs. UNHCR’s NFI programme aims to assist 520,000 families/2,600,000 individuals with emergency NFIs kits including cash/voucher for NFI and 438,300 household/2,191,500 individuals with the provision of Seasonal NFI kits (winter/summer items) in addition to emergency NFI kits including cash/voucher for NFI. The response will be conducted from Turkey and from inside Syria, UNHCR’s NFI Programme will also prioritize those with longer term needs among the communities requiring resilience oriented support, by supporting the resilience of local communities and households within the humanitarian response by protecting and restoring livelihoods, access to essential services and rehabilitation of socio-economic infrastructure through the local production support and  introduction of voucher scheme: Vouchers in exchange of local manufactured items produced through partner’s livelihood support project  in order to help reduce dependence on harmful coping strategies. In this regard, this project aims to meet life-saving NFI needs, particularly of newly displaced people and area based response to returnees, Beneficiaries are selected based on the degree of eligibility and vulnerability, and priorities are based on the availability of resources.

project_name: Supporting Safe and Adequate Shelters in Gaza: NFIs, Winterization and Rehabilitation
project_objective:
In alignment with the Shelter Cluster (SC) 2019 strategy, objective 2, to decrease vulnerable households (HH) exposure to harsh weather and protection concerns, Development and Peace (D&P) Catholic Relief Services (CRS) and Bayader for Environment and Development Association (Bayader) propose urgent shelter rehabilitation and NFI assistance for 300 HH over 12 months. Completed works will translate into decreased reliance on yearly assistance and a reduced caseload for the humanitarian community. 

Focusing on the distinct needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities (PwD), and the elderly, this intervention uses an approach of accompaniment to promote gender equality and full participation of all household members. The project features an easily scalable approach that emphasizes shared household decision-making and adoption of safe, environmentally responsible shelter practices. 
  
Results from the 2018 Islamic Relief (IR) Community Vulnerability Mapping Study  show that Khan Younis governorate has the highest percentage of HH (33%) living in vulnerable localities among all governorates in the Gaza Strip. More specifically, the data on economic vulnerability—that considers living conditions, including types of housing, average area of the home etc.—shows that Khan Younis has the greatest number of localities deemed economically vulnerable. CRS will thus target Khan Younis governorate, focusing on the most vulnerable HH living in deteriorated shelters and prioritizing female headed households (FHH), HH with PwD, and the elderly. 
To fully engage all HH members, particularly women, girls, PwD and the elderly, local partner Bayader will recruit and train a gender-balanced intern team comprising fresh graduates in engineering and social work to accompany households. Intern teams will provide technical guidance and facilitate discussions to ensure rehabilitation plans reflect all HH members’ needs. These discussions aim to promote gender equality through shared decision making. Additionally, interns will gain valuable, real-world professional experience, thereby improving their livelihoods and that of their family, while increasing their future employability. 
The intervention will build on over 5 years of CRS’ experience in shelter programming in Gaza, emphasizing high engagement of females, PwD and the elderly, as well as improved environmental, health and safety practices. Future learning will be shared with the SC, with the aim of greater adoption of gender and environmentally-responsive approaches by other shelter actors. 

With the option of multi-year funding, CRS would endeavor to influence behavior change by working with other shelter actors to establish best practices in gender-responsive and environmental-responsible approaches relevant to the Gazan context.

This project is a partnership between D&P, CRS, and local partner Bayader. The collaboration between D&P and CRS is rooted in the global Caritas network, where both organizations are partners and work in a consortium providing global humanitarian assistance. Bayader is an experienced D&P and CRS partner with ongoing shelter project activities in Gaza, with demonstrable success. 
•	D&P’s primary responsibilities will include donor reporting, compliance and program oversight. 
•	CRS will be responsible for program quality, beneficiary selection, beneficiary accountability, monitoring and evaluation, liaising with the SC, adherence to protection principles and overseeing environmental, health and safety standards. 
•	Bayader will be responsible for program implementation, including community engagement, project monitoring and managing the livelihoods internship component.

project_name: Enhancing access to safe water and basic sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
Building on the expertise and operational capacity of ACTED staff in Syria, the intervention will provide targeted and effective WASH support to those most vulnerable across the country. The action will focus on restoring cost-efficient, sustained and safe access to quality water to populations. Temporary sources of safe water will be installed where no alternatives to water trucking exist and under-performing water and sanitation infrastructure will be rehabilitated. Rehabilitated assets will be handed over to local actors to increase community resilience. Community sensitization on hygiene practices and water usage will be mainstreamed to heighten the impact of the intervention.

Under the WASH sector, ACTED will build on its expertise conducting multi-faceted WASH programming and will combine elements of emergency response while establishing durable solutions. In Syria, ACTED's WASH approach is based on three layers of intervention. First, immediate interventions aim to meet the emergency needs of those most vulnerable through the distribution of WASH NFIs and the establishment of emergency water treatment units and distribution points. Key WASH-related awareness raising is mainstreamed throughout the approach. A second layer of interventions focuses on improving access to sustainable safe water sources through existing infrastructure. The initial emergency response is thus paired with the rehabilitation of WASH assets such as canals, water stations, and boreholes. Additionally, ACTED provides technical and operational support to the authorities managing the rehabilitated sites. A third layer focuses on ensuring the handover of rehabilitated assets to, and establishment of cost-recovery and water safety plans with, local stakeholders to ensure the sustainability of the self-managed infrastructure.
This intervention will focus on emergency response and sustainable resilience, so as to provide the most adapted and cost-efficient assistance to those most in need. Synergies will be drawn between activities and with other ongoing ACTED interventions. 

ACTED will deliver an integrated package of WASH assistance in Northeast Syria. Water quantity and quality will be improved to SPHERE standards, with a focus on ensuring durable and cost-efficient access to safe water. A particular effort will be put on offering sustainable alternatives to water trucking where no other sources of safe water are available. In turn, it will allow actors currently conducting water trucking to redirect emergency assistance to other areas. Mainstreamed community sensitization on water conservation, usage, and hygiene will contribute to decreasing Water Born Diseases (WBD) concerns. An effective exit strategy will be ensured by working closely with local stakeholders, building their capacity to operate and maintain rehabilitated infrastructure.

project_name: Comprehensive WASH and protection support to vulnerable underserved households in Wadi al Saqa
project_objective:
The proposed action is based on the 2018-2020 HRP specific objective of WASH Sector: “Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable access to safe and sufficient WASH services with dignity for the underserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank.”

Based on recent ACTED assessments, extensive consultations with key stakeholders, and following the recommendations of the Palestinian Water Authority, Coastal Municipal Water Utility (CMWU), the project will target 200 vulnerable households of Wadi al Salqa in Middle Area governorate.

The aim of this project is to restore access to domestic and drinking water for most vulnerable households of Wadi Al Salqa (Middle Area, Gaza Strip), by ensuring their access to drinking water supply, increasing water storage capacity and improving their sanitation facilities (bathrooms and kitchens). This project will also raise awareness and build capacity on good hygiene practices.
By improving access to drinking water, basic sanitation and hygiene awareness, this project will also prevent further deterioration of the households’ conditions of living due to high temperatures and harsh summer weather. This action will benefit to at least 1,120 households members.

The project will be implemented by ACTED in partnership with CESVI and Natuf NGOs. CESVI has been working in Palestine since 1994 and has develop a strong expertise in WASH (South Hebron Hills – adequate access to water in terms of both quantity and quality, introduction and testing of innovative technologies for water, sanitation and hygiene). Natuf NGO has been implementing projects in Gaza since 2010, in particular in the sectors of Food security, WASH, Shelter and alternative energies (solar panels). 

The project will be coordinated with relevant stakeholders, such as the WASH cluster, Palestinian Water Authority, Coastal Municipal Water Utility (CMWU), and the Ministry of Social Development.

Eventually, the project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA), with specific focus on women and vulnerable groups, and a strong Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) component. In particular, beneficiaries will be heavily involved in the action through community based empowered committees, and a comprehensive Complaint Response Mechanism will be deployed. Gender principles will be mainstreamed during the action and Committees will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases with a particular focus given to women and children issues such as related to GBV. An ACTED protection officer will be focal point of the committees to receive and follow-up on cases.

project_name: Restoring and strengthening food security access of the most vulnerable households of Rafah, Khan Yunis and Middle Area, including the Access Restricted Areas (ARA)
project_objective:
The proposed action is based on the 2018-2020 HRP specific objectives in Food Security Sector: “The resilience, food security and productive capacity of vulnerable households are restored/enhanced and livelihoods protected” and “Households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs.”

Based on recent ACTED assessments, extensive consultations with key stakeholders, and following the recommendations of the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) and Food Security Sector (FSS cluster), the project will aim at providing emergency support to the most vulnerable households of Rafah, Khan Yunis and Middle Area, including ARA (total of 2,800 beneficiaries).

Specifically, ACTED will:
•	Restore the productive capacity of 305 vulnerable farmers (Activities 2&3), whose livelihood is located in the communities of Al Shokat (Rafah governorate), Fukhari (Khan Yunis) and Wadi As Salqa (Middle Area), with a specific focus on the ARA which were damaged during the incidents occurring at the border since the March of Return in March 2018. The project will contribute to improve and restore farmers’ productive capacity, households’ access to food security and contribute to increase communities’ resilience capacities, through cash-for-work implementation/cash-for-asset 
•	Increase access to food security of 195 vulnerable households (Activity 4) located in the same communities, through the creation of an emergency food security chain benefiting
•	Strengthen 3 existing Community-Based Agriculture and Protection Committees (CBAPC) in each community, which were established by ACTED under former projects, through capacity-building activities. 

In total, 500 households will benefit from the action (2800 individuals).

Eventually, the project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA), with specific focus on women and vulnerable groups, and a strong Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) component. In particular, beneficiaries will be heavily involved in the action through community based empowered committees, and a comprehensive Complaint Response Mechanism (CRM) will be deployed. Gender principles will be mainstreamed during the action and Committees will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases with a particular focus given to women and children issues such as related to GBV. An ACTED protection officer will be focal point of the committees to receive and follow-up on cases.

project_name: Urgent support to protect the livelihoods of farmers and poultry breeders and make best use of available water resources.
project_objective: The project is designed to provide urgent support to protect the livelihoods of the small scale farmers' owners of open farms, small-scale poultry breeders and provide rehabilitation work and renewable power supply system for water wells and agricultural ponds based on BBB approach to enhance resilience of agricultural sector. The project will target 250 of dunums of open farms for 125 small-scale farmers (80% males and 20%females)  in order restore production and functionality by providing either full and/or partial land rehabilitation, piping and/or irrigation system, seeds and seedlings distribution based on the individual needs assessment of each farm. 3 Agricultural wells will be rehabilitated for the sake of rural communities; 90 farmers "" MoA indicates that available wells needs rehabilitation to the north provide water for 30 farmers as average. 3wells * 30 farmers = 90 beneficiary in average"". The wells will be supported with renewable power supply system (20 Kw each) to increase its functionality and durability to pump water during day time which will improve farmers access to water resources for irrigation purposes. The project will rehabilitate 50 affected old agricultural ponds (concrete plastering and plastic). The project will also provide rehabilitation works for 50 of small scale poultry farms( 95% males and 5% females)  and provide them with renewable power supply system (1.2 kw each) in order to make available the lighting, watering and ventilation required for the chicks.  Protection standards and core humanitarian standards will be fully respected.

project_name: Integration of Life Saving Curative and Preventative Nutrition Interventions in Health Facilities
project_objective:
SAMS in this project is part of FAST Consortium. Through this project, SAMS in collaboration with consortium members are prioritizing the reduction of morbidity and mortality through improving the access to Nutrition Services in 20 health facilities in Aleppo, Idleb and Hama.

As part of its health intervention under FAST, SAMS will support nutrition services (CMAM and IYCF practices), for the IYCF component SAMS will contextually appropriate social and behavior change communication to prevent and manage malnutrition of infants, while via CMAM ractices SAMS will strengthen the capacity of the health staff to integrate these nutrition services in the  facilities. These includes screening and treatment of acute malnutrition, multiple, micronutrients supplementation, The support will be through capacity building of health staff and provision of nutrition supplies for facilities in Hama, ldleb and Aleppo . The targeted facilities will also be part of the nutrition surveillance system.

For the past year, SAMS have been applying CMAM and IYCF-E in the supported facilities. In coordination with the Nutrition Cluster and nutrition actors, SAMS conducted a training
onboth CMAM and IYCF-E for medical staff in the HFs (Pediatricians, midwives and nurses) and CHWs. 

Under FAST, the outpatient departments of the supported HFs and CHWs will provide the nutrition activities which include CMAM and IYCF components such as MUAC screening to children under 5 and PLW in all health facilities, reach the families with IEC materials, Provide preventive and curative nutritional supplies to all health facilities,  IYCF counseling and group sessions. 
Where possible, a dedicated space will be made available in the supported HFs for promoting IYCF practices, especially lactating exercises. Private space to conduct IYCF activities, particularly for teaching mothers how to breastfeed or manage re-lactating issues, is
provided in some health facilities depending on availability of space. In smaller health facilities which do not have space availability, IYCF activities are conducted in reproductive health clinics or labor rooms.

FAST partners will continue to coordinate with other health actors through the Health Cluster, Nutrition Cluster and the NGO forum where routine data is gathered and shared through the 4Ws and HERAMS. FAST partners are also coordinating with other humanitarian actors at the field level to assess the needs, strengthen referral pathways, and respond to emergencies, among other ways. Moreover, SAMS and the FAST consortium will closely coordinate to share information about needs, ensure an effective and coordinated response to new emergencies, harmonize the salary scales and staffing structures across HFs. 

SAMS through this project will target 60,000 beneficiaries disaggregated by gender and age as following: 39,600 Female; 20,400 Male; 42,000 Children under five and 18,000 young adults.

2.	Health systems in implementation area are strengthened

project_name: Safe and inclusive learning environments for Syrian children
project_objective:
The project aims to provide improved quality and protective learning environment for 8120 Syrian boys and girls in 10 schools in Idleb and Aleppo Governorate.  These schools are located in the areas where there is high proportion of out of school children. As per the non-structured interviews with school management, 30% of primary school age children (5-17 years) are out of school. Non-availability of education supplies (school bags, stationary, uniform), child labor, increase trend of early marriages and inappropriate learning facilities are common factors contributing to high percentage of out of school children.
A complete Back to School campaign will be run in the targeted communities. Community volunteers (teachers) will be recruited and will receive monthly stipend to facilitate this campaign.  This campaign will sensitize the parents and caregivers about the importance of education and will bring back 300 children into targeted formal schools. All the children in the targeted schools will be provided with student kit. The sensitization campaign will continue throughout the project period to mitigate the risks of school drop outs. 
The targeted schools will be provided with student kit and education supplies and furniture as per the need. 120 teachers and school management staff will be identified for monthly stipend. These teachers will also include psycho social trainers.  The teachers and administrative staff will also be trained on child protection and psychosocial support. The teaching staff will conduct regular classes in the targeted schools and individual/group psychosocial sessions and recreational activities will be conducted. In additional minor school repair and rehabilitation will be conducted specially to improve WASH facilities in schools. Provision of prefabricated classrooms to ensure that education space is suitable for learning.
The provision of conducive learning environment, improved enrolment rates, psychosocial support, education supplies, student kit, school rehabilitation and regular classes are expected to contribute positively in the overall child development as well as attendance and school performance. 
The project is aligned with the objectives and priorities as set by Humanitarian Response plan. This project will also contribute to the No lost generation initiative by enrolling the out of school children and providing them with protective learning environment.

project_name: Provision of Non-Formal Education for out-of-school/ dropped out children affected by the conflict in Idleb, Ar-Raqqa and Aleppo governorates.
project_objective: In consultation with the Education Directorates (EDs) in Idleb, Ar-Raqqa and Aleppo governorates, and after signing Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with them, 36 Temporary Leaning Spaces (TLSs) - 25 schools and 11 camps - will be established to accommodate 4,500 out-of-school (OOSC) and dropped out children (girls and boys aged between 8 and 15 years old – 10% children with disability). These children will be targeted with Self Learning Program (SLP), Accelerated Learning Program (ALP), Remedial Classes and Catch-up Classes with embedded school-based Psycho-social support (PSS), Life Skills and citizenship activities. 203 education and PSS personnel (females, males, IDPs and Host Community) will be hired and trained to run the 36 TLSs and will be provided with incentives. The overall Objective is to scale up safe and equitable access to non-formal education for crisis-affected children (girls and boys aged between 8 and 15 years old – 10% children with disability) which is in line with the education sector objectives and HRP 2019 outcome statement. The project aims at increasing safe an equitable access to non-formal education for crisis affected children in line with the education sector objective and HRP 2019 Objective-1, through Back To Learning (BTL) campaigns, Open day activity, awareness raising, SLP, ALP, Remedial Classes, Catch-up Classes, light rehab of classrooms and schools as to be disability friendly, the provision of furniture, school bags, stationary, recreation kits, Self-Learning Materials (SLM) including textbooks, transportation and supplementary materials. The project also aims at enhancing the quality of non-formal education for out-of-school/dropped out children ( girls and boys aged between 8 and 15 years old – 10% children with disability) within a protective environment in line with  the education sector objective and HRP 2019 Objective-2, through training teachers and education personnel on SLP, ALP,  Remedial Classes, Catch-up Classes, child-centred protective pedagogy, Education in Emergency (EiE), active learning, classroom management ...etc, and training PSS animators and supervisors on PSS theory, skills and methods, Life Skills and  citizenship. Parents and Teachers Associations (PTAs) will be formed in each TLS. Teachers Learning Cycles (TLCs) will be formed in each TLS. A referral path way will be established to integrate referrals to specialist service providers. A feedback mechanism will be established as well in the TLSs. Meanwhile, the project aims at enhancing resilience through building positive and social norms and generate a sense of connectedness to teachers, peers, parents and caregivers as to cope and thrive in the face of negative events, challenges or adversity, taking into consideration that the community leaders, the local education authorities, the parents and caregivers are involved from the very beginning of the project to the end. Meanwhile, indicators will be set to measure whether the needs are met and the activities are delivered.
