project_name: MA: Priority Clearance of Cluster Bomb Strikes in Juba, Magwi, and Torit counties
project_objective:
PURPOSE: To survey and clear priority cluster munition strikes as well as UXO spot tasks reported by the community in Juba, Magwi, and Torit counties to provide safe access and land in areas with high rates of returns; building resilience by releasing land back to the communities than can be used for agriculture, grazing, and settlement. The project will also educate displaced persons, returnees, and host community members about the dangers of and safe behaviors to adopt when encountering explosive hazards, with an emphasis on reaching men and boys who are most at risk of death or injury. In addition, the project will train community focal points who can provide safety briefings to returnees, while also increasing the number of women in leadership positions in the community. 

TARGET: The multi-task team (MTT) will survey and clear 420,000 square meters of high priority cluster munition strikes and EOD spot tasks, which equates to survey and clearance of 50 hazardous areas, inclusive of spot tasks. The community liaison team (CLT) will provide explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) to 15,000 people (W: 3,959, M; 4,176, G 3,492 B:3,375); and train 100 community focal points (W: 50, M: 50). 

SUMMARY OF ACTIVITIES: MAG will deploy a multi-task team (MTT) and community liaison team (CLT) to Juba, Magwi, and Torit counties during 2020. When appropriate for the nature of the terrain the MTT will be supported by a Bozena with Mulcher attachment. MAG is the only mine action NGO utilizing such equipment for clearance in South Sudan, and as such MAG can deliver clearance of large cluster munition strikes faster and more cost efficiently than manual teams. The CLT will deploy to areas with large numbers of displaced persons, prioritizing people who are likely to return to their home villages to provide explosive ordnance risk education (EORE). 

IMPACT: Clearance increases a community’s resiliency by clearing land that can then be used for settlement, agriculture, and grazing of animals; making communities will be less dependent on food aid. Clearance also provides access to public services and aid. Therefore, mine action activities can improve outcomes across all sectors. EORE provides community members with the means to keep themselves and their families safe and to report potentially hazardous items to keep their communities safe. Training community focal points gives the communities the means to continue to spread safe behavior messages even after the project is over. Through this integrated approach of clearance, EORE, and training community focal points, the project can sustainably prevent and mitigate protection risks. 

MAG’S EXPERIENCE: MAG has worked extensively through Central and Eastern Equatoria, throughout its history in South Sudan. While the crisis of 2016 prevented access for clearance teams focusing on area clearance for a period, MAG returned to Magwi county in September 2018 and has been working in Amika boma—the town centre area—since then. In addition, beginning in July 2019, MAG has deployed six teams (four on a temporary or short term basis) to the outer areas of Magwi county close to the border with Juba county and along the important Juba-Nimule highway, where they have been conducting battle area clearance. In addition, the multi-task team proposed for this project has been working in Juba county along the Juba-Nimule highway—initially in Aru Junction—since December 2018. In addition, MAG’s MineWolf team has been operating in Juba county since October 2017 and is now operating in Torit county. Three of the MAG teams operating in Magwi county are expected to relocate back to their normal area of operations in Terekeka county in the dry season, and therefore this project will continue to provide capacity for BAC clearance in Magwi as well as Juba and Torit counties. This project will allow MAG to continue the high priority clearance working taking place along the important Juba-Nimule and Juba-Torit roads.

project_name: Livelihood assistance for South Sudanese Refugees in White Nile and Eritrean and Ethiopian refugees in Gedaref and Kassala States
project_objective:
Mercy Corps will deliver livelihoods programming for refugees in White Nile, Gedaref and Kassala states, creating market-driven livelihood opportunities in a context where barriers to formal and informal employment severely undermine both the food security and resilience capacities of households. Furthermore, Mercy Corps deliberately designs our humanitarian programs to do better than meet needs on a stopgap basis. While our priority aim is to save lives, minimize suffering, and protect social and economic assets, we will also tackles the proximate and underlying causes of the emergency in order to interrupt repeated cycles of crisis and vulnerability ensuring we are actually mitigating suffering--not just postponing it to a later date. 

Building on Mercy Corps existing livelihood projects in Gedaref: El Fashaga locality  (Umgargur camp); and Kassala: Khashm Ghirba  locality (Girba camp), Wad Sherifey camp and Kassala town; Mercy Corps will strengthen the livelihoods of 4200(White Nile 1020:Kassala and Gedaref 3,180) refugees and 10% vulnerable host community  to gradually reduce dependency on humanitarian aid and assistance, with a view to increase the economic capacity of refugee households and support local integration. Efforts will be made to reduce vulnerabilities, increase and diversify sources of income and prevent negative coping strategies. This project will apply a sustainable livelihoods approach focused on gaining productive assets while building capacities and coping strategies of vulnerable households. This approach recognises that individuals are active agents who make rational decisions and choices about their lives, and in response to social and economic change.  At the practical level, MC will actively involve and listen to the views of the participants and the wider community during the beneficiary selection. The various training opportunities provided under the project will support people to achieve their own livelihood goals, building where possible on their existing coping strategies. Increasing individuals’ access to financial services will enhance individual’s financial assets and increase their resilience to economic and social shocks and stressors. Importantly, this project recognises the significance of power relations that exist both within and between households and communities, the host and refugee communities. Considering this, MC will ensure that 15-20 percent of all project beneficiaries are host community members. This will increase community and government support for the intervention.
Key activities to realising this objective will include market driven vocational training; business start-up support through cash grants; Village Savings and Loans Association (VSLA) strengthening; and provision of improved vegetable seeds for farming. The program will seek to focus on South Sudanese, Eritrean and Ethiopian refugee groups and surrounding host community.

project_name: RÉOUVERTURE DES ECOLES NON FONCTIONNELLES DE LA COMMUNE DANS LA RÉGION DE TOMBOUCTOU
project_objective:
Le projet va  à atteindre   3 780 enfants en difficulté scolaire de à 7 à 18 ans de 14 écoles de la commune de Fitouga  dans la région de Tombouctou.
L’intervention du projet vise à rendre fonctionnelles les écoles non fonctionnelles en proposant des offres éducatives non-formelles et informelles adaptées aux filles et garçons non-scolarisés et déscolarisés du fait de la crise sécuritaire. La stratégie est centrée sur trois axes principaux qui sont : l’accès à une éducation en sécurité, la qualité de l'enseignement et l'apprentissage et le renforcement de capacité des membres des comités de gestion scolaire, du corps enseignant en particulier les Directeurs et Directrices d’écoles.
 Pour parvenir à cela, le projet développe une approche participative et communautaire basée sur une responsabilisation de toutes les organisations communautaires de base  ainsi que les personnes ressources indispensables (notabilités, chefs coutumiers et leaders religieux, ressortissants). Ceux-ci garantiront le dialogue et l’intermédiation sociale en continu pour la fonctionnalité des écoles et veilleront sur l’effectivité et la régularité des enfants à l’école. 

Le soutien et la valorisation des enseignants volontaires communautaires seront aussi au centre des activités. Le contenu de la formation sera axé sur la pédagogie de gestion des CAC (centre d’apprentissage communautaire) approuvée par la Direction Nationale de l’Enseignement Fondamental (DNEF). Elle se focalise sur la participation et la sauvegarde des enfants pour assurer un apprentissage de qualité. Les enseignants seront également renforcés sur la thématique psychosocial pour faire face aux effets de la crise pour renforcer la résilience du corps enseignant et les enfants. Le suivi et la supervision continue des formations sera assuré par les services techniques et Plan International Mali.

Le projet tient compte de la gestion endogène de la vulnérabilité spécifique des filles scolaires.  A cet effet, des campagnes sensibilisations sur la SCOFI seront faites pendant toutes les assemblées générales d’information sur les facteurs sociaux et pratiques néfastes qui font que les filles ne vont pas à l’école ou sont contraintes d’abandonner précocement. 
Le projet dans son approche va renforcer les capacités de communication des filles et des garçons  leur permettant d’instaurer un dialogue social afin de lutter contre les facteurs sociaux entravant leur scolarisation. A travers l’approche paire éducation, le projet va également renforcer les capacités des filles et des garçons en SSR pour mieux contrôler leur corps  et leur sexualité. Les acteurs de la société et l’administration scolaire y compris les parents d’élèves seront mise à contribution à travers l’organisation d’un cadre de concertation sur les VBG. L’objectif est d’amener les communautés à un changement de comportement et à lutter contre toutes formes de violence portant atteinte à la jeune fille et à sa scolarité.
Parallèlement, le projet fournira un appui en matériels en fournitures scolaires, un appui pour la réhabilitions des salles de classe et des kits d’hygiène et assainissement.

project_name: Renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux en réponse à la crise nutritionnelle prolongée à Tombouctou et Taoudenit
project_objective:
Le projet proposé contribue à la réalisation des trois objectifs stratégiques du projet de PRH de 2019 et repose sur une évaluation générale des besoins. ce projet appuiera le système de santé pour absorber les chocs liés aux pics de malnutrition (absorption) ; les interventions seront adaptées en fonction des résultats de la supervision, du suivi et de l'analyse des données des programmes de routine et du suivi de SURGE (adaptation) ; le système de santé sera transformé avec le renforcement du financement local par les services décentralisés et la communauté par le plaidoyer (transformation) ; et le projet permettra de renforcer l'anticipation des pics en suivant SURGE et renforçant la surveillance du site sentinelle et l'analyse des données au niveau des groupes techniques sanitaires et alimentaires tant nationaux que régionaux (anticipation). Cela renforcera les 6 piliers du système de santé du DH tels que définis par l'OMS (RH, prestation de services, infrastructure d'équipement et d'approvisionnement, gouvernance, système d'information sanitaire, financement) en mettant la participation au centre de l'intervention. Les activités WASH renforceront la qualité du traitement dans les centres de santé et la prévention des cas de MAS en améliorant l'hygiène dans les ménages / écoles. Les activités WASH réduiront également les complications dues à la diarrhée et aux rechutes des cas de MAS.
Les aspects genre seront pris en compte dans l'analyse des besoins par sexe et par âge pour chaque secteur. Ces besoins spécifiques s’appuieront sur la description des difficultés des groupes vulnérables notamment les femmes et les enfants, mais aussi les personnes en situation de handicap, les personnes âgées, les femmes chefs de familles, etc. L’assistance sera adaptée aux besoins spécifiques de ces groupes vulnérables aussi bien au sein des communautés que des PDI. Les assistances apportées aux populations affectées seront analysées sous l’angle de la protection transversale pour ne pas nuire aux bénéficiaires (Do not harm) et dans le respect de leur dignité. Un mécanisme de gestion des remontées des informations est disponible au département MEAL d’Action Contre la Faim et permettra de faire le suivi de l’exécution du projet. Les remontées d’information seront recueillies et traitées et un feedback sera communiqué aux individus ou groupes d’individus (requérants). Chaque processus de gestion des remontées d’information sera documenté.
Action Contre la Faim mettra en œuvre son intervention en collaboration avec les acteurs humanitaires intervenant dans les zones ciblées et sous la coordination des groupes thématiques sectoriels présents en région. Les résultats/informations seront régulièrement partagés avec les clusters nationaux qui organiseront des missions de suivi régulières. Les communautés bénéficiaires seront impliquées dans toutes les phases de réalisation du projet, réalisées en étroite collaboration avec les services techniques et les acteurs développement afin de préparer l’appropriation et la pérennisation des activités du projet.
Compte tenu de la crise mondiale due à COVID 19, la promotion et la supervision de l'hygiène comprendront une grande partie à la sensibilisation sur COVID-19. Afin de contribuer au plan régional contre COVID 19 à Tombouctou et dans le districts de Touadénit, AAH mettront en œuvre certaines activités.

project_name: Renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et de plaidoyer pour la protection humanitaire et l’assistance aux populations les plus vulnérables au Mali.
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire demeure complexe et instable, principalement en raison des conflits armés et intercommunautaires dans les régions du Centre et du Nord. Le retard dans la mise en œuvre de l’Accord pour la paix et la réconciliation au Mali paraphé en juin 2015 et dans le processus de désarmement, démobilisation, réintégration (DDR) contribuent à la persistance de l’instabilité sécuritaire dans les régions de Kidal, Gao, Tombouctou, Ségou et Mopti ainsi qu’à l’aggravation des tensions sociales. La présence limitée de l’État et l’insécurité dans ces régions demeurent l’un des facteurs clés obligeant les civils à fuir leurs communautés.
Le nombre de Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) a atteint la barre des 199 385 en octobre 2019 en comparaison aux 80 302 enregistrés en octobre 2018. Les risques et les besoins de protection des populations fuyant leurs communautés sous la pression de la violence armée ou des tensions intercommunautaires, sont élevés. De graves abus et attaques contre les personnes, les biens et les services (écoles, centres de santé) sont régulièrement signalées alors que l’accès aux services appropriés est compromis. Comme les déplacements internes sont durables, les risques de protection et les violations des droits fondamentaux augmentent, en particulier pour les plus vulnérables (femmes, enfants, personnes âgées, personnes handicapées ou malades). De graves conséquences humanitaires ont donc été notées, telles que des taux élevés d’insécurité alimentaire et de malnutrition ainsi que le faible accès aux services sociaux de base.

En référence au Cadre Harmonisé (nov. 2019), à l'heure actuelle, 3,6 million d'hommes, de femmes, de garçons et de filles souffrent d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dont 670 000 souffrent d'une insécurité alimentaire sévère (phase 3 à 5 du Cadre Harmonisé). La situation devrait se détériorer au cours de la période de soudure 2020, avec près de 4,9 million d'hommes, de femmes, de garçons et de filles souffrant d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dont près de 1,2 million de personnes souffrant d'insécurité alimentaire sévère (phase 3 à 5). Les capacités de réponse existantes au Mali représentent plus de 160 organisations humanitaires, acteurs du développement ainsi que des forces militaires (MINUSMA, Forces maliennes de défense et de sécurité, Barkhane, Mission européenne de formation, G5 Sahel). Le contexte susmentionné exigera une coordination efficace et la présence d’OCHA demeure très importante. OCHA maintiendra sa présence à Bamako, Mopti, Tombouctou et Gao et ouvrira une antenne à Ségou tout en couvrant à distance les régions de Taoudénit, Ménaka, Kidal et les régions du sud.

Sept clusters actifs (Éducation, Sécurité alimentaire, Santé, Nutrition, Protection, Abris/BNA et WASH), des sous-clusters et des groupes de travail spécialisés (Accès, CM-Coord, Redevabilité, Genre et Cash) sont en place au niveau national et local. Le Bureau d’OCHA au Mali continuera ainsi à jouer un rôle central dans la mobilisation, la coordination et le soutien des acteurs humanitaires dans les domaines de la coordination, la gestion de l’information, le financement humanitaire et le plaidoyer. OCHA jouera un rôle essentiel dans la mobilisation adéquate des fonds en faveur des personnes dans le besoin, en plus de contribuer à dynamiser les efforts déployés par le gouvernement et les acteurs du développement pour s’attaquer aux causes structurelles de la vulnérabilité.

OCHA continuera à jouer son rôle central dans la mobilisation des partenaires, l’utilisation des instruments et des mécanismes de financement tout en veillant à ce que les besoins humanitaires croissants soient prises en compte. OCHA assumera son rôle clé dans la coordination militaire au niveau national et régional de concert avec les forces militaires présentes dans le pays tout en renforçant les capacités des autorités nationales en matière de coordination et de préparation des interventions d’urgence.

project_name: Provision of essential cooperation and information services on safety & security and access to humanitarian aid organisations in Somalia
project_objective:
The NGO safety program was established in 2004 to support NGOs operating in Somalia in terms of staff safety. In this complex context, NGOs face strong challenges related to access and security, including: a lack of understanding of the context; difficulty to access and to verify information; a lack of information sharing; a lack of security coordination and harmonized security practices; poor security awareness of staff; and a lack of training opportunities. This safety platform is managed since April 2015 by INSO

In response to, and following the guidance of an Advisory Board (which is composed by 4 INGOs and 3 LNGOs), the project focuses in two main pillars of action which can be summarized as Information, Analysis and Advice, and Preparedness and Response. The two pillars are strongly interconnected: NGOs need accurate and timely security information to base their decisions on, while they need the proper safety training to organize and take relevant security decisions. Finally, in case an incident takes place, NGOs receive adequate support
Through INSO’s own network of Deputy safety Advisors and Safety Advisor assistants, NGO reports, collaboration with other security actors and media follow up, INSO collects, verifies, compiles and analyses security incidents. Besides, since 2010, the project has developed a database of more than 33,000 incidents that constitutes a unique tool for data analysis. The INSO Training Team runs training programs which targets both individual safety and management of the organization's security. Finally, INSO field teams help NGOs on the ground to deal with daily security incidents, such as arrests, accidents and threats, while the INSO senior management team can provide support to critical incidents such as kidnappings, abductions and medical evacuations. The extent of INSO involvement is determined by the NGO who requests our services.

Due to the peculiar mandate and mission of INSO, its Nairobi office has a dual role, both as coordination hub and implementer of core INSO activities (such as verbal briefings and production or maps and reports). Likewise, senior management (including the Country Director) are highly involved in the direct delivery of our services: they are not just managers but also direct implementers in their role of advisors to other NGOs. 

The project budget leans heavily in HR costs because the project’s core product is knowledge. That’s in essence what INSO’s beneficiaries receive. When the main output of an organization is information, the organization core cost is HR – same as e.g. an online newspaper or a management consulting firm.

project_name: Community-based Protection in the South of Libya
project_objective:
The objective of the proposed action is to respond comprehensively to the protection risks that vulnerable populations face in the South of Libya. The proposed action will focus on identifying and addressing the needs of vulnerable communities namely, IDP, Returnee and host communities, as well as migrants and refugees. The geographic scope of intervention for the proposed action will largely focus on the South.

ACTED will adopt a community-based protection approach for this project, notably by advocating for the establishment of community protection committees (CPCs). Through the CPCs, ACTED will conduct awareness raising sessions around sensitive protection risks encountered by vulnerable and marginalized population and to strengthen existing community owned protection models. ACTED will also establish a referral service and conduct protection monitoring to reach out to the most vulnerable populations and the most vulnerable areas. Complementary to the referral services, ACTED will provide direct assistance to the most vulnerable cases through a special needs fund (cash for protection). ACTED will provide capacity building to CSOs/local actors on protection principles and practical protection activities, as well as financial support (subgrants) for the implementation of activities aimed at the protection of vulnerable populations.

Concerning protection monitoring, at least 240 HHs or 1,344 individual beneficiaries will be identified and will benefit from protection monitoring services and referral to service providers as required. ACTED also plans to reach an average of 150 individuals through awareness raising sessions and the training of at least 10 local CSO protection staff and 1 community-based protection structures. Through the sub grants, ACTED estimates to reach out to at a minimum 1000 individuals, especially in the refugee and migrant communities.

ACTED has been continuously involved in Libya since 2011, establishing a strong field presence with bases in Tripoli, Benghazi, and Sebha. This has allowed ACTED to develop a cross-regional level of acceptance. The ACTED Libya mission employs 52 national staff and 12 international staff to support operational and strategic implementation. ACTED will rely on a team of international and national staff to implement its protection intervention, under the close oversight of its Protection Coordinator. ACTED has strong project management capacities, including accountability mechanisms, sound financial management, and the ability to deliver quality reporting and adhere to contractual reporting requirements. ACTED also has stringent anti-fraud and code of conduct policies and delivers trainings to field personnel on a regular basis. ACTED likewise has a demonstrated ability to undertake large-scale procurement in Libya. Program staff will be supported by a dedicated team of coordination, grant management, finance, logistics, compliance and security staff in country who will be responsible for sound financial and contractual management of the project. ACTED’s functional logistics team, based in Libya and in Tunis, closely follows the written standard procurement procedures as outlined in the ACTED procurement manual, and has a strong operational vendor management system. ACTED also has well-trained program and AME staff with experience in implementing and monitoring the activities which are proposed in this project.

ACTED actively engages with the humanitarian coordination system in Libya, notably the UNHCR-led Protection Working Group (WG), as well as the Child Protection and GBV Sub-Sector WGs, and the education sector WG. In 2018 and 2019/20, ACTED was accepted as member of the Protection Cluster’s core Strategic Advisory Group (SAG), which addresses critical protection issues in Libya. ACTED will report all activities conducted in the framework of the proposed project within the protection sector and the INGO Forum ‘4Ws’ to ensure a coordinated response.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Providing Essential Life Saving Treatment and Prevention Nutrition Services to the Vulnerable Communities in Somalia
project_objective:
The median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition has remained serious (10 -14 Percent) in the past four seasons: 13.8 percent in 2019 Gu, 12.6 percent in 2018/19 Deyr, 14 percent in 2018 GU and 13.8 percent in 2017/18 Deyr.  Despite the serious nutrition situation, some livelihoods has critical rates of malnutrition due to food insecurity, high morbidity, low immunization and vitamin A supplementation and poor child care and sub-optimal feeding practices. The 2016 Infant and Young Child Nutrition (IYCN) assessment found that only 33% of infants below six months are exclusively breastfed while 46% of mothers continue to breastfeed their infants up to 12 months, only 15% continue to breastfeed the child up to 24 months.
In the 2019 post Gu food and nutrition assessment, pockets of GAM above the emergency threshold of 15 percent were reported in 10 out of the 33 areas surveyed. The majority (51.7 percent) of malnourished children cases concentrated in the six regions of Banadir (14.8 percent) Shabelle (11 percent), Bay (8.8 percent), Hiran (6.1 percent), Woqooyi Galbeed (5.6 percent), and Gedo (5.4 percent).  Morbidity among children was high (≥ 20percent) in 15 out 33 population groups surveyed. These regions also realized below average rainfall and the expected harvest is 68 percent lower than the long-term average since 1995.  
The proposed interventions will cover treatment (Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program for malnourished  children 6-59 months and Pregnant and Lactating Women - PLW) and prevention (Blanket Supplementary Feeding Program for children 6-23 months and PLW, Mother, Child Health and Nutrition (MCHN) for children 6-23 months and PLW in the districts where GAM (Global Acute Malnutrition) is above 15%.
An estimated 1,008,500 children under the age of five years are likely to face acute malnutrition through June 2020, including 178,400 who are likely to be severely malnourished.
The World Food Program is the leading UN agency in Somalia in fighting hunger. In Somalia, WFP together with the Ministry of Health, nutrition cluster and the partners supports nutrition interventions in the treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and prevention of acute and chronic malnutrition. Treatment of MAM prevents children from mortality and deteriorating to Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), which requires extensive medical support; prevent deterioration of maternal nutrition status and subsequent low birth weight. 
Targeted Supplementary Feeding program targets children 6-59 months and pregnant and PLW with MAM.  In IDP and host/urban populations in Dollo, Mogadishu, Baidoa, Guriel, Dhusamareb, Galkayo, Hargeisa, Berbera, Bossaso, Qardho WFP collaborates with UNICEF and MOH to offer an integrated package of nutrition and health. This program follows the Ministry of Health guidelines for treating acute malnutrition in Somalia.  
WFP also implements preventive program:
Seasonal Blanket Supplementary Feeding (BSFP) a seasonal program implemented in areas with high rates of acute malnutrition and food insecurity. The purpose of the program is to reduce the incidence of malnutrition. The target group is non-malnourished children 6-23 months and PLW
Mother and Child Health and Nutrition Program (MCHN) aims at promoting growth by focusing on the first 1,000 days of life which contributes to prevent acute and chronic malnutrition and break the inter-generational cycle of malnutrition. Pregnant mothers also receive an incentive if they deliver their babies at health facilities ensuring safer deliveries under the supervision of a midwife/or skilled health worker. The program also aims at increasing the utilization of antenatal and post-natal services as nutrition services are offered within the health centres.  The target population is children 6-23 months and PLW in the districts where Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) is more than 15%.
Nutrition and health messaging is integrated across all WFP nutrition programs.

project_name: Providing Child Protection in Juba and Yei River State
project_objective:
Terre des hommes (Tdh) is the leading Swiss child relief organization, and has been operating in Juba PoCs since 2014, and in Yei River State since 2016, with extension of its education and child protection services to rural Yei (Mugwo and Otogo counties) since 2019.  It works to improve the living conditions of the most vulnerable children in an effective and sustainable manner, by providing direct child protection services aiming at preventing and responding to cases of abuse, neglect, exploitation and violence against children; as well as by strengthening the resilience of children and communities through a holistic and child-centred approach, considering children’s intersectoral needs in protection, education and WASH. Tdh has embraced a holistic approach to programming whereby an integrated, multi-sectoral program aims to improve outcomes for children and to contribute to the improvement of the broader child protection outcomes, including a focus on improving children’s sense of security and self-confidence. Tdh’s integrated approach links CP interventions with its WASH and education interventions. WASH/CP integration will be achieved by increasing sustainable use of protection sensitive WASH services such as water supply and latrines, alongside comprehensive hygiene promotion and ensuring appropriate, sustainable WASH in Schools, with the aim of ultimately leading towards improved child protection outcomes: children are able to live and learn in a clean and safe environment. The Tdh CP approach will prioritize rigor in assessments and ensuring that programs are directly addressing the specific needs of the targeted beneficiaries. In addition to implementing direct child protection activities, including case management and psychosocial support for specific vulnerabilities among children, particularly UASC and CAAFAG; Tdh will also ensure that CP is mainstreamed in all of its activities, including training other actors on CP concepts. 

In 2020, Tdh will continue to provide direct child protection services to children and to enhance community-based child protection mechanisms. With the objective to handover activities throughout 2020, Tdh will aim to progressively decrease its presence in Juba PoCs and transition to urban response. On the other hand, Tdh will maintain a strong presence in Yei town and will seek to increase its presence in rural Yei, through 2 mobile teams providing comprehensive case management services for vulnerable children. 

As one of the principal CP actors in South Sudan, Tdh is noted for its commitment to effective coordination and communication within the sector. Tdh will continue to coordinate with all CP and Education actors first to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the services available in the targeted areas, and second to avoid any overlap of locations or activities. Tdh shares the experiences related to its projects through the Protection Cluster, the CPSC, the PSS Working Group (WG), the UASC WG, the CAAFAG WG, the MHPSS Technical WG and the GBV Child Survivors WG at national level. Tdh is also a member of the CM Task Force and co-chair of the CPWG at Jubek State with the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Welfare. Through these coordination mechanisms, a strong and effective coordination is in place which ensures information-sharing and effective collaboration among different service providers. Tdh actively participates in 4 clusters in Yei town as the CPSC, WASH and Education clusters. Tdh also works closely with the MoGEI and MoGCSW at county and state level to ensure that national guidelines and strategies are considered during implementation. Given its longstanding presence in Yei River State and Juba PoCs 1 and 3, Tdh benefits from favorable acceptance from the communities and will continue to collaborate with all relevant actors, including through joint needs assessment missions, to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication.

project_name: Appui au renforcement de l’accès aux soins médico-nutritionnels des populations vulnérables, à la redynamisation du système et à la lutte contre le COVID-19, dans les zones affectées par les crises au Nord et au centre du Mali
project_objective:
La crise a déstabilisé le système administratif dans les zones du Nord et conduit à un affaiblissement des services publics dans le domaine de la santé et la nutrition dans les régions de Kidal et de Gao. La présence continue des équipes PUI dans tous les cercles de la région de Kidal et dans le cercle d’Ansongo de la région de Gao à travers des interventions d’assistance médico-nutritionnelles permet de suivre l’évolution des besoins des populations les plus vulnérables. A cause des difficultés de l’Etat (y compris des autorités sanitaires) à administrer la région de Kidal d’une part et à cause de la persistance des conflits et des déplacements de population à Kidal et à Ansongo d’autre part, PUI réaffirme le fait qu’il est indispensable de continuer le soutien aux populations les plus vulnérables à travers l’amélioration de l'accès aux soins médico-nutritionnels totalement ou partiellement gratuits et de qualité dans ces zones. Dans ce cadre PUI favorise, dès que les conditions sont réunies, le passage des centres de santé (CdS) d’une gratuité totale vers une gratuité ciblée. Ainsi dans le cercle d’Ansongo 5 CdS sont passés à la gratuité ciblée sur la phase précédente du projet. Sur cette nouvelle phase PUI pourrait élargir cette gratuité ciblée à 8 autres CdS (après avoir réalisé un diagnostic) du même cercle, et à cela s’ajoute l’intégration dans le projet du CdS urbain d’Ansongo fonctionnant déjà en gratuité ciblé, pour un total de 14 aires de santé passant/fonctionnant en gratuité ciblée. [MR] Grace à une extension, PUI préparera la fin de son appui aux CSCOM de Kidal et élargira sa zone d’intervention  en intégrant  le Cercle de Bandiagara (région de Mopti).  Au total, dans le cadre de ce projet,  PUI appuiera 8 CSCOM à Kidal jusqu’en avril 2020 et 15 CSCOM à Ansongo jusqu’à la fin du projet. Pour répondre aux alertes de déplacements et assurer un accès aux soins de santé pour les personnes vivant loin des centres de santé ou dans des aires de santé non fonctionnelles, PUI déploiera également jusqu’à la fin du projet 5 cliniques mobiles.

Dans un contexte particulièrement complexe et difficile, avec des services de bases déjà très insuffisants voire inexistants, le Mali se prépare à faire face au Coronavirus. Pour répondre à cette pandémie, PUI a déjà entrepris des activités, va en réajuster certaines en a planifié d’autres au niveau de ses bases et des structures appuyées, conformément à sa stratégie d’intervention et celle du CCS.

project_name: Assistance aux populations réfugiées, déplacées et hôtes dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéri
project_objective:
Le présent projet vise à impacter positivement la vie de populations dans deux régions du Niger qui, depuis 2015 notamment connaissent de massifs mouvements de populations provoquées par les attaques de groupes terroristes qui sévissent dans les frontières Sud et Ouest du pays. En outre, des catastrophes naturelles depuis quelques mois telles que les inondations provoquées par les crues de certains cours d'eau, ajoutées à une mauvaise campagne agricole dans lesdites zones, ont exacerbé la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle de ces populations. Soutenir ces milliers de ménages affectés par ces aléas est la vision de WHH. Le projet cible 2700 ménages vulnérables réfugiés, déplacés et leurs hôtes dans les régions de Diffa et de Tillaberi, soit un total de 18 400 personnes qui seront impactées par l'action proposée par WHH. WHH utilisera les interventions monétaires pour restaurer rapidement la dignité des ménages affectés et soutenir leur autonomie à disposer d'aliments répondant à leurs préférences alimentaires. Ainsi, ce sont au total 1 350 ménages qui bénéficieront du cash conditionnel à travers du Cash for work. La modalité cash conditionnel est choisie pour renforcer les liens entre les populations réfugiées, déplacées et hôtes au travers d'activités d'intérêt communautaire qui seront définies de commun accord avec les communautés bénéficiaires. La modalité cash inconditionnel est choisie pour les ménages qui présentent un degré de vulnérabilité élevée (pendant 3 mois). De même, l'intervention de WHH tient à renforcer le statut nutritionnel des ménages à travers les activités agricoles et compte appuyer les ménages avec des semences améliorées pour produire à des fins de consommation et de commercialisation pour améliorer les revenus. Sous le présent projet, WHH s'attache au genre et met au premier plan les personnes les plus vulnérables (femmes, enfants, personnes âgées et avec handicaps) dans l'ensemble du processus: des consultations en passant par la sélection des bénéficiaires, la mise en œuvre du projet et son suivi-évaluation. Pour ce faire, on ne limite pas à désagréger les bénéficiaires par âge ou sexe dans les chiffres mais on démontre dans chaque étape du projet la prise en compte du Genre. Par exemple pour les interventions monétaires inconditionnelles, les femmes seules avec enfants à charge, les handicapés et les personnes âgées seront pris en considération pour bénéficier d'un tel appui. Pour les interventions monétaires conditionnelles (cash for work) et agricoles, les ménages les plus valides et ayant accès à la terre seront les plus considérés. Dans le processus de prise de décision, les avis des groupes les plus vulnérables seront également pris en compte  afin de faire prévaloir leurs besoins spécifiques et d'en tenir compte dans la mise en oeuvre. Un système de suivi-évaluation robuste sera développé à travers des exercices bien planifiés et coordonnés de: Baseline, Post distribution Monitoring et Endline afin de s'assurer de la plus-value que le projet apporte aux populations affectées. De même, des accords de collaboration avec des Institutions de microfinance et les Services techniques de l’Etat afin d’assurer une coordination autour des interventions proposées. Les Institutions de Microfinances pour assurer une distribution efficiente signeront des protocoles d'accord pour organiser et réaliser les distributions de cash aux bénéficiaires. A ce niveau, pour répondre aux questions de protection transversale, WHH travaillera avec les parties prenantes afin de prendre les mesures nécessaires pour une meilleure protection des bénéficiaires, en opérant dans un environnement sécurisé et si nécessaire changer de modalité cash si cela va dans le sens de la protection des bénéficiaires et des équipes de mise en œuvre. Pour les activités agricoles, WHH continuera les accords de collaborations avec les DRA et ICRISAT. *30% de réfugiés couverts par le projet, difficultés à refléter dans le budget en ligne.

project_name: PROJECT WITHDRAWN- Integrated Education and Child Protection for children in Somalia
project_objective:
The proposed intervention will improve access to quality education, increase access to critical WASH inputs and enhance child protection mechanisms in schools for drought- and conflict-affected students and their surrounding communities in Belet Weyne,
, Bulo Burto, Bossaso, Iskushuban, Qandala, Caluula, Garoowe, Eyl and  Gaalkacyo districts  of Somalia. The project will target 12, 100 children (8,685 non-displaced and 3,415 displaced). Among these 12,100 children 6,655 will be boys and 5,445 will be girls) Education specific activities will include the provision of education supplies, emergency take-away food rations for students to meet their minimum caloric needs, emergency teacher incentives to motivate teachers, and sanitary kits for adolescent girls to encourage their regular attendance at school. Specific WASH activities will include increasing schools’ water storage capacity through the provision of PVC storage tanks, safe water delivery to schools, the construction and rehabilitation of latrines and water storage tanks. Specific Protection activities will include case management for separated and unaccompanied children and GBV survivors, mapping and sharing of existing child protection service providers and their respective services to school administrators and communities, strengthening child protection systems in schools, including the recruitment and training of child protection focal persons at each school, linking schools to referral pathway outside the school and facilitating the development of school-level child protection action plans. Relief International (RI), through child protection committees, will deliver messages to schools and communities on key protection concerns affecting the community. These messages will target prevention as well as the response in the event protection concerns arise. RI will provide training to CECs on their roles and responsibilities, food and water management, disaster risk reduction (DRR), civic skills, and child protection in the respective schools. To ensure water availability in the targeted schools, RI will truck safe water to schools but CECs will manage its distribution. Further, the CECs will be trained on DRR to build their capacities and improve school preparedness against future disasters. Child- and gender-friendly latrines in the targeted schools will be rehabilitated or, where necessary, constructed to minimize disruptions in learning for girls and boys. RI will coordinate a back-to-school campaign with CECs and religious leaders to encourage school enrollment with an emphasis on children affected by displacement. RI, in collaboration with the appropriate ministries, will map existing referral pathways and service providers and link schools to these services. Where pathways are weak or non-functional, RI will strengthen them to ensure effective response to child protection concerns. To monitor the effectiveness of the child protections systems implemented and capture lessons learned, RI will facilitate joint review workshops with schools, service providers, and relevant government ministries. Through engagement with ministry officials and CECs, RI will leverage the respective agency apparatus and community assets to raise awareness among children on child protection and the established referral mechanisms which will serve to strengthen child protection in schools and the larger communities.

project_name: UNHCR multi-sectoral program in Libya
project_objective: Libya is and will continue to be a destination and transit country for a large number of refugees and asylum-seekers moving in the context of mixed migration flows and who are perceived by the Libyan authorities as illegal migrants who should either be sent back to their countries of their origin or resettled to third countries. As a result of this restrictive policy and the negative public attitudes that they are subjected to, refugees and asylum seekers are exposed to a wide range of protection risks including arbitrary arrest and detention, police harassment, abuse and exploitation., in addition to facing serious difficulties in meeting their basic needs and those of their family members. Under these circumstances, UNHCR, together with its partners, will continue to provide them with a wide range of life-saving protection and assistance services across various sectors of intervention such as protection, in-kind shelter and NFI support, financial assistance, registration and documentation, public health, while redoubling efforts aimed at securing the release of refugees and asylum-seekers being held in detention and finding durable solutions out of Libya through humanitarian evacuation and direct resettlement to third countries for the most vulnerable of them who will be carefully identified on the basis of pre-established eligibility criteria both from within the urban refugee population and those kept in detention

project_name: Emergency and Relief Intervention - Nutrition Activities in South Sudan by Medair
project_objective:
Medair has worked in South Sudan since 1992. Currently its operations consist of the static projects in Renk (former Upper Nile State), Aweil Centre (former Northern Bahr el Ghazal State) and Leer and Mayendit (former Unity State) with the main objective of decreasing preventable morbidity and mortality due to acute malnutrition by treating children and PLWs with GAM and underlying illnesses, building local nutritional treatment and prevention capacity, and increasing preventative infant and young child feeding practices. In all the sites, Medair’s main activity will be implementing the management of acute malnutrition, according to the national CMAM guidelines, targeting the vulnerable children under 5 years of age and pregnant and lactating women. This will include facility and community level promotion of IYCF-E in line with national MIYCN guidelines as well as training, capacity building and regular supportive supervision at supported Medair sites.  In total, the target for 2020 will be of 6,663 SAM new admissions, 20,479 MAM new admissions and 11,869 PLWs.

In Renk, Medair remains the only long-term nutrition partner and one of the only health actors to respond to the nutritional emergency. In May 2018, Medair conducted a SMART survey in Renk County that revealed GAM and SAM rates above the emergency threshold, with the critical level of 24.4% and 5.6% among IDPs and 32.1% and 8.5% among the host community, respectively. 
Medair performed a SMART survey in Leer County in April 2018 showing a GAM rate of 14.3% (SAM 3.2%). The household food security situation in the Medair catchment areas of Leer appeared dire, with 2/3 (64%) of the households reporting to rely on food aid as their main source of livelihood for the past 3 months prior to the survey.  Household Hunger Scale revealed that more than half of the households surveyed (53%) experienced moderate hunger score, while – worryingly - 33% experiencing severe hunger score. Around 20% of the interviewed households, during the SMART exercise, had already employed crisis coping strategies, while the majority of them (73%) had employed emergency strategies.

In Aweil Centre, the results from the SMART survey of July 2019 showed a prevalence of a GAM at 19.3% (including a SAM prevalence of 1.3%), which is significantly much higher than the GAM rate of 6.3% measured by the SMART survey of July 2018. 
The IPC classification for acute food insecurity  of August 2019 indicates that Aweil Centre is IPC 3 (Crisis), which is a worsening compared to 1 year ago, when it was projected IPC 2 (Stressed). 

In all of these project sites, Medair will ensure the minimum WASH package of safe water and latrine access, including waste management is present and functional. Systematic malaria RDT will be conducted on admission for SAM children, and treatment of malnourished children suffering from malaria will be implemented. Moreover, treatment of co-existing illness will be ensured. Where possible, linkage with the FSL partner will be encouraged, while child friendly spaces and early child development activities will be fostered in order to allow the full neuro-cognitive development of the child and promote the importance of the mother-to-child relationship.


The Emergency Response Team (ERT) responds to nutrition emergencies in South Sudan.
According to the IPC of August 2019, the overall nutrition situation  in terms of acute malnutrition during the lean season of 2019 is critical and worse compared to same period in 2018. Based on the IPC AMN, 58 counties (out of the 79 total counties) were classified as IPC AMN Phase 3 and above. Furthermore, all counties in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Jonglei (except Pibor), Upper Nile (except Maban), Unity and Counties of Gogrial East, Gogrial West, Twic, Warrap, Budi, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North, Kapoeta South, Lafon, Eastern Equatoria State, Awerial and Yirol West, Lakes were classified as IPC AMN Phase 4.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Addressing Acute Food Insecurity in Rural Somalia
project_objective:
6.3 million Somalis are acutely food insecure through December 2019, a 36% increase since late 2018. This includes 2.1 million Somalis in IPC 3-4 (double an average year) and 4.2 million in IPC 2 (the highest on record). The situation deteriorated most significantly in rural areas, where the population in IPC 2-4 doubled and IPC 3-4 tripled. Since 2016, six out of seven rainy seasons have been poor, including Gu 2019 which yielded Somalia’s lowest cereal harvest in decades in southern Somalia. Pastoralists also struggle to recover from significant livestock losses and debt incurred from the protracted drought. 

FAO’s project will directly assist 150,549 households (903,294 people) and deliver countrywide veterinary services, contributing across FSC’s three strategic objectives (SOs). 

To improve immediate access to food (SO1), FAO will deliver cash assistance to 20,000 households through cash-for-work (CFW) to repair community infrastructures and 71,758 households through integrated cash and livelihood programmes (Cash+). Beneficiaries will receive 3-6 monthly cash transfers, based on duration of the lean season and their vulnerability. To support transition out of emergency cash programmes, FAO will offer lighter and longer-term cash and livelihood assistance to 4,500 chronically vulnerable households in districts with high recurrence of IPC 3-4. FAO’s cash programme assists severely food insecure people to meet their food immediate needs, while giving them choice and re-injecting cash into the local economy. FAO delivers cash through mobile money operators and money vendors, adopts rates recommended by the Cash Working Group and regularly monitors the availability and prices of selected food and non-food commodities in local markets through FSNAU.  

To protect and restore livelihoods (SO2), FAO will provide quality production inputs and training to Cash+ beneficiaries and an additional 31 791 vulnerable households. Tailored livelihood support packages will enable farmers to secure a Gu/ Deyr harvest, pastoralists to enhance milk production and coastal communities to improve fish catch and processing. The project will further enhance production and promote climate smart practices through field school approaches, targeting 2,500 farming, pastoral and coastal households that will pass on the knowledge to their wider communities. To protect livestock assets, FAO will conduct country-wide livestock treatment and vaccination campaigns to protect 17.5 million animals; and deliver emergency water supply and animal feed in the case of severe drought (20,000 vulnerable households). 

To build resilience and mitigate new shocks (SO3) at a community level, the project will improve water management and related infrastructure to protect rural populations and livelihoods against flooding (repaired river embankments) and cope with drought (fenced water catchments, animal troughs, canal sluice gates). FAO will also support government and community led efforts to control plant and animal pest and disease outbreaks. This includes (i) stocking State Ministries of Livestock and Livestock Professional Associations with veterinary drugs, water bladders, vector control treatment (in cases of severe riverine floods), PPR vaccines and related test kits to advance PPR eradication in Somalia; (ii) developing an Antimicrobial Resistance Strategy with the Ministry of Livestock; (iii) supporting Desert Locust Units to collect data on locust prevalence during the breeding season; and (iv) mobilizing Ministry of Agriculture extension staff and NGO partners to roll out large field trainings with farmers to control Fall Armyworm in key cereal producing areas.

project_name: Emergency Food Assistance
project_objective:
Access to food in Gaza remains a challenge for a majority of refugees struggling with deteriorating socio-economic conditions. As a result, UNRWA expects that in 2020, around 1,000,000 refugees – with around 50 per cent of them being females – will require emergency food assistance. Hence, in order to mitigate food insecurity, UNRWA is planning to  provide food assistance to approximately 200,000 Palestine refugee families including persons with disabilities and female headed households. This intervention is aligned with Strategic Objective 3 of the HRP i.e. supporting the capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, and the response approach of the Food Security Sector (FSS) i.e. addressing basic food needs of households that are suffering from limited access to food.
The beneficiaries will be surveyed through UNRWA specific poverty based targeting system,  that identifies families living on less than $3.87 per person per day. Gender access to food assistance will be taken into consideration, as approximately 50 per cent of the beneficiaries will be females and as around 17,000 female households will be targeted by the intervention. Eligible refugee families will receive a food basket every quarter that includes a range of basic food commodities. Through its strong monitoring system in place regarding the food distribution process, UNRWA will continue to provide nutritionally improved food baskets while also guaranteeing a fair, equal and consistent distribution.

project_name: Amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire nutritionnelle et réhabilitation des moyens d’existence des ménages pauvres et très pauvres affectés par la crise Centrafricaine dans la province du Logone Oriental.
Manejo comunitario de Enfermedades Crónicas/No Transmisibles mediante acciones de promoción de salud, atención primaria y vigilancia epidemiológica
project_objective:
Según los datos de morbilidad registrados por Caritas Venezuela durante sus Jornadas de Salud realizadas en 2019, el primer motivo de consulta fue la Hipertensión Arterial.  Los trastornos Neuropsiquiátricos y las EBPOC, Asma y otros broncoespasmos se ubicaron entre las primeras 10 causas de consulta general; la Diabetes, entre las primeras 20 causas. Los responsables regionales de Caritas incluyen los trastornos Neuropsiquiátricos entre los primeros 5 problemas que requieren atención prioritaria por su complejidad, y les incluyen entre los 10 problemas de salud más frecuentes en todos los grupos de edad (convulsiones, depresión, Parkinson, Alzheimer, Demencias). A partir de esta información surge la iniciativa de formular e implementar un proyecto de Atención Primaria en Salud -APS- con cuatro componentes: 1) Capacitación de promotores comunitarios para la prevención, identificación y manejo de las Enfermedades Crónicas/No Transmisibles con materiales didácticos e instrumental y realización de encuentros de formación. 2) Asistencia a pacientes con enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles a nivel comunitario por medio de jornadas de pesquisa e ingreso al programa, entrega de medicamentos, educación sanitaria y entrega de ayudas en casos puntuales. 3) Promoción de Salud Mental Comunitaria incluyendo promoción de la salud con materiales impresos, audiovisuales, encuentros de capacitación; consultas de psicología y de orientación en puntos específicos y/o referencia a servicios especializados previa consolidación de redes de atención. 4) Fortalecimiento de sistemas de información y vigilancia epidemiológica.
Considerando que Cáritas Venezuela cuenta con una plataforma para la obtención de data significativa de cobertura nacional que ha venido desarrollando desde 2016 con el Proyecto SAMÁN, y que se mantiene la necesidad de contar con información primaria para la programación humanitaria oportuna y pertinente, el proyecto incorpora fortalecer el  sistema de información de base comunitaria que Caritas lleva para incorporar ahora la alerta, monitoreo y atención de situaciones de salud que vive la población más vulnerable. Esta expansión del monitoreo de la situación en comunidades permitirá, no solamente identificar prioridades según grupos vulnerables para la administración/distribución efectiva de los insumos médicos, sino también direccionar las acciones educativas que emprende Caritas para consolidar las capacidades comunitarias en materia de prevención de enfermedades y promoción de la salud (ENT, ET, SM y Psicosocial). Este componente permitirá también desarrollar competencias comunitarias para el adecuado registro, transcripción y procesamiento de datos a nivel parroquial, diocesano y nacional mediante acciones de motivación, capacitación, dotación con equipos de informática y telecomunicaciones y acompañamiento/tutoría, para la correcta identificación y registro de morbilidades y riesgos, el uso extensivo de una base de datos integrada y el análisis pertinente.
Con este proyecto Caritas coopera en el logro del objetivo 2 del sector de “Fortalecer el acceso a la red integral e integrada de servicios de salud (RIISS) con calidad, para la atención de las necesidades priorizadas, relacionadas con enfermedades no transmisibles (ENT) y salud mental (SM) desde los enfoques de género, edad y diversidad y con participación comunitaria” y a los tres objetivos estratégicos del Plan de Ayuda Humanitaria.

project_name: PROJET D'AMELIORATION DE LA SÉCURITÉ NUTRITIONNELLE DANS LA REGION DE TOMBOUCTOU ET TAOUDENIT(PASEN)
Humanitarian Mine Action in eastern Ukraine 2020
project_objective:
HALO will conduct risk education, survey and clearance operations in eastern Ukraine, to respond to the needs of mine-affected communities across Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, focusing on high-priority areas within the 15km buffer-zone from the line of contact. HALO will also provide training and capacity building sessions for the key mine action stakeholders including the newly established mine action authorities in order to contribute to an effective and efficient mine action sector. 
Risk education sessions are a preventive measure that will inform on the threat related to mines and other explosive items and decrease the probability of accidents. Survey work will establish the extent and nature of mine contamination in the region, while clearance will permanently remove these threats, improving the physical safety and livelihoods opportunities of those affected. HALO aims to clear two million square metres of land contaminated with explosive hazards during 2020.

project_name: Emergency response to COVID 19 for vulnerable small holder farmers
project_objective:
Zimbabwe recorded its first case of COVID-19 on 20 March and  had confirmed 42 cases by 17th of May 2020. The Government of Zimbabwe has also declared the COVID-19 pandemic a national disaster and have introduced several containment measures, including a national lockdown. As part of the lockdown, national borders are closed except for formal imports of essential goods such as food and medical supplies, as well as for returning citizens. Additionally, stringent internal movement restrictions are being enforced except for essential services such as the food industry, health, and security.

Prior to the COVID 19 pandemic Zimbabwe was in the grip of widespread food insecurity caused by the poor performance of the 2019/20 agricultural season which experienced delayed onset of rain, resulting in delayed planting and limited availability of water for productive uses. The weather related shocks had a negative impact on livestock due to poor availability of grazing and limited access to water. Approximately 66 000 cattle succumbed to drought related deaths. The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis conducted for  the period February to June 2020, shows the proportion of rural people facing a Crisis situation (IPC Phase 3-4) is 45 percent (4,3 million). This segment of the rural population currently requires urgent humanitarian assistance.   

FAO is proposing an emergency response project that will support the ongoing efforts of the Government and partners to anticipate the impact of COVID-19 on the food security and rural livelihoods economy.  The project will be implemented in 4 districts targeting 10, 000 households (50,000 people) in IPC phase 3 & 4. The project aims to minimise disruptions to the food supply chain for vulnerable small holder farmers, through improved post harvest management,  provision of crop and livestock inputs, raising awareness among extension workers and farmers to minimise  the spread of COVID-19 and provision of PPE for agricultural extension officers (masks at a minimum).

project_name: Colombia - International Labour Organization
Colombia - Danish Refugee Council
Brazil - UN Women
Provision of Multipurpose Cash to Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Syria
project_objective:
UNRWA estimates that 418,000 Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance in 2020. To contribute to mitigating the consequences of deepening poverty and increasing vulnerabilities, the Agency will provide cash assistance to up to 418,000 Palestine refugees through a targeted approach, which UNRWA introduced in the second half of 2019. This approach assists only vulnerable refugees, and prioritizes those most vulnerable. The four main groups that constitute the most vulnerable group are as follows: families headed by a person older than 60 years; families headed by a person with disability and people with disabilities; families headed by a female; and orphans. The groups can be identified through UNRWA’s registration system. UNRWA estimates that 126,000 Palestine Refugees fall under those four categories. 
 This system will offer two different values of cash assistance to Palestine refugees according to two tiers of vulnerability. The most vulnerable will receive cash assistance amounting to US$ 28 per person per month – thus covering 100% of the official abject poverty gap of US$0.94, while the remaining Palestine Refugees categorized as less vulnerable will get assistance equivalent to US$ 14 per person per month – covering 50% of the official abject poverty gap. The cash assistance aims to help vulnerable refugees meet their basic needs of food and NFI.  Through its partners, comprising a network of banks and private companies present in all regions of Syria, UNRWA will be offering cash assistance in a ﬂexible and timely manner with minimal ﬁnancial risk. In 2020, UNRWA also plans to extend the use of ATM for its cash distribution. Some 40,000 ATM cards will be issued, distributed and credited to selected beneﬁciaries, on top of the 10,000 cards that were already issued in 2019.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Improved equitable access to quality emergency and essential lifesaving health services for the crisis affected population (IDPs) and non-displaced host populations in selected districts of Puntland, Somaliland and South Central Regions of Somalia.
project_objective:
The proposed action will be implemented through existing Government-MOH system to enhance sustainability through health system strengthening (HSS) interventions thus provide quality accessible, acceptable and affordable health services to the target populations; IDPs and host community during humanitarian crisis. The action will aim at enhancing sustainable impact through HSS and therefore deliver quality health services to the target populations. Target locations are Baki and Lughaya districts of Awdal region, Burco and Odweyne districts of Togdheer region both in Somaliland, Garoowe, Burtinle and Eyl districts of Nugaal region in Puntland and Baydhaba and Qansax Dheere districts of Bay region and Dollow and Luuq districts of Gedo region in South Central Somalia. The interventions will seek to improve emergency response during crisis-driven disease and outbreaks e.g. AWD/Cholera and measles through supporting the MoH prepare emergency response plans (ERPs) at regional health authorities level and have rapid response teams (RRTs) with capacity to promptly investigate rumors, confirm outbreaks, notify WHO and MoH, mount an aggressive response, and report promptly. The action will also ensure increased access, utilization and coverage of essential health services by supporting health facilities; making them functional to provide out-patient consultations, immunization services for vaccine-preventable diseases, maternal, new-born and child health services through; capacity building to the health care workers on clinical management of rape,  BEmONC and CEmONC, EPI and cold-chain management, integrated disease surveillance and response (IDSR) and mass casualty management in order to improve their capacity to deliver quality health services; provision of essential medicines including vaccines thus avoiding stock outs and ensure availability and accessibility of supplies; strengthening emergency obstetric and new-born care through adequate staffing to provide BEmONC services in most Health Centers and CEmONC services at selected referral Health facilities, both services provided 24/7, improved case management and referral of sexual & gender-based violence survivors and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS/PFA); scale up of immunization services both routine and campaigns during disease outbreaks. Through this action also, mitigation of impact and response to shocks to the affected populations as a result of conflict and public health emergencies will be enhanced. Referral health facilities will be selected strategically and equipped to enable management of mass casualties during catastrophe and staff trained on mass casualty management. It is envisaged that through this interventions, target populations will have improved access to quality healthcare services during humanitarian crisis and therefore reduce excess mortality and morbidity.
The proposed action will reach 73,800 direct  beneficiaries comprising of the following:
1. Out patient consultations due to disease outbreaks; AWD/Cholra, measles... and out patient consultations of SGBV survivors
2. Children under 5 years vaccinated against measles and Penta 3
3. Health care workers trained on the following:
 - AWD/Cholera and measles rapid response
 - Clinical management of rape (CMR) survivors
 - Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) PFA
 - Nurses and midwives and clinicians trained on BEmONC and CEmONC in order to provide RH services 24/7
 - Community Health resourse persons trained on community mobilisation and referral of cases to the Primary Health Facilities or treatment centres e.g. CTCs and CTUs
4. Health workers and CHWs supported with incentives to provide essential health services during emergency response

project_objective: The project aims to improve access to a safe and quality education system with a focus on girls. The action will facilitate access to education for out of school children and adolescents to enable them to obtain the bases for integration into the formal education system. The component will integrate gender issues and sensitization to gender-based violence, through teacher training, awareness campaigns and the promotion of equal and safe education for girls, boys, IDPs or host communities.
