project_name: Promotion of Rights and Durable Solutions: Ability to exercise and enjoy legal identity and rights to housing, land and property for vulnerable persons affected by the displacement  in the Far North Region
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to improve access to legal identity and housing, land and property rights for returnees, displaced persons and host communities in Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari division in Far North region of Cameroon. 
NRC will assist beneficiaries to access civil and identity documentation, through the provision of information, counselling and legal assistance. 
One of the main targets for these services will be children along with their parents who need birth certificates to sit public exams as well as people affected by displacement who meet obstacles to access civil and identity documents to enjoy freedom of movement and access to other rights and services.
NRC will reinforce its response and provide support to displaced populations and vulnerable host communities to access their HLP rights. 
NRC will assist vulnerable individuals to obtain signed agreements from local authorities and traditional leaders (chief of villages) for beneficiaries at risk of forced eviction. Priority will be given to female heads of household, widows, displaced persons, and vulnerable or affected host community members. This process will contribute to the prevention of forced evictions.

project_name: Improved living condition, promotion of rights and physical safety to promote dignity and protection of refugees of the South West and North West Regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to Improving living condition, promotion of rights and physical safety to promote dignity and protection of returnees, displaced people and hosts communities South West and North West Regions of Cameroon. The project will provide NFIs and emergency shelter kits for the construction of temporary shelters to a total of 10,000 households (with 51% of women head of households). The NFI distribution will be carried out in synergy with WASH hygiene kit distributions in order to provide a comprehensive WASH/shelter/NFI kit to beneficiaries. 
NRC will also support with electronic vouchers for rent when displaced populations are living in rented housing in peri-urban areas in South West and North West, respectively Mezam and Fako Divisions. E-Voucher will be distributed for average 03 months per households assisted.
NRC programme will target IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community’s households who need shelter assistance to improve their living conditions in the project implementation locations.
For IDPs living in the bush in the South West region, the NFI kits will be easy to carry as they move back to their original homes. 
Beneficiary targeting will also aim at reaching the most vulnerable households based on agreed upon selection criteria. 
NRC will prioritize the most vulnerable groups that will include young mothers, persons living with disabilities, women headed households, child headed households, orphans, the elderly, and pregnant women

project_name: Improving access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and hygiene practices for returnees, displaced people and hosts communities in South West and North West Region, Cameroon
project_objective:
The main objective of WASH response is to improve access to safe drinking water, adequate sanitation and hygiene practices for refugee population, returnees, displaced persons and host communities in South West and North West region of Cameroon. 

NRC will build new water points and rehabilitate dilapidated water points to address the gaps associated with access to adequate water supply. In the establishment of new or improved water point/sources, NRC will use consultative ways together with baseline survey to gather information in order to prioritise based on urgency of the needs. The overall activities shall involve rehabilitation and or upgrading of water systems and provision of new water sources.
NRC will ensure that water is safe for drinking through provision of the adequate water treatment equipment, regular monitoring, and continuous engagement of the community in the activities. Water trucking will be explored where appropriate during initial phases of the response but with a clear exit strategy. NRC will form and train WASH Committees on water quality management through the management of chlorination points. This will be blended with trainings on the use of water quality treatment materials, monitoring of safe levels of free residual chlorine.
NRC will facilitate the construction of latrines in schools and intervene in locations requiring emergency latrines. In addition, NRC will promote construction of family/household latrines as opposed to communal latrines that have proven difficult to clean and maintain. While latrine use, cleanliness and maintenance will be the responsibility of the beneficiaries, NRC will support the latter with training, sanitation cleaning/construction tools, and related hygiene promotion activities.
NRC will consult with women and girls before agreeing on appropriate latrine locations while also considering important factors. In order to ensure that interventions are gender responsive, latrines will be located in safe locations within reach of the households, while ensuring that adequate privacy is provided. NRC will also guide on the design, building materials, size, while also ensuring that the target beneficiaries will feel safe while using those sanitation facilities. If those women and girls deem that security measures such as provision of flashlights are necessary, NRC will meet their needs to the extent possible. 
In hygiene promotion, the main focus for NRC will be to address problems and needs revolving around behaviour change practices. Hygiene promotion activities with focus on cholera prevention will be characterized by household visits for hygiene sensitization. Hygiene promotion will also be through the use of information, education and communication posters with messaging on proper hygiene practices like handwashing at critical times, safe excreta and waste disposal, safe water chain and safe water management, with the aim of preventing WASH related diseases. 
NRC will target vulnerable populations affected by displacement, IDP and Host communities, in North West and South West regions of Cameroon.

project_name: WASH en soutien aux populations vulnérables affectées par les conflits dans le cercle de Mopti
project_objective:
La région de Mopti, en proie à des conflits communautaires, comptent 61 083 IDP et 44354 retournées vivant dans les principales communes dont celle de Mopti qui compte aujourd’hui 6776 IDP dans les camps d’IDP et familles d’accueil (CMP, Octobre 2019), engendrant de nouveaux besoins en WASH, provoquant ainsi une pression sur les ressources existantes. Ce qui affecte un accès à l’eau potable déjà faible dans le cercle de Mopti (38.74%, DRH, Décembre 2018) en général et en particulier dans la commune de Mopti (3.77%, DRH, Décembre 2018) où l’assainissement, surtout la gestion des déchets solides reste un défi majeur en ce sens que sur 11 GIE créés par la mairie pour l’évacuation des déchets, seuls 3 sont fonctionnels. Cela favorise la multiplication des dépôts de transit illégaux qui constituent un facteur aggravant des conséquences des inondations qui en 2019 ont touché 6 localités de la région de Mopti, faisant 2635 personnes sinistrées (Cluster WASH, Septembre 2019).
Sur les 27 centres de santé que compte le cercle de Mopti, 33% n’ont pas accès à un système d’approvisionnement en eau potable et 30% (DNS, Octobre 2019) ne disposent pas d’équipements adéquats de gestion des déchets biomédicaux.
Ainsi, les ménages, en particulier les plus vulnérables sans accès aux services minimum de base, sont exposés aux risques de maladies liées à la WASH dans un contexte marqué par l’insécurité et la faiblesse des capacités de l’état au regard des besoins humanitaires grandissant surtout en WASH
Le projet vise à contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations affectées par la crise à travers une réponse en WASH dans le cercle de Mopti et ciblera en particulier :
-les femmes, les filles, les garçons chargés de la corvée de l’eau 
-Les personnes déplacées en familles d’accueil ou dans des camps 
-les enfants souffrant de malnutrition et leur mère / soignant vivant dans une situation de vulnérabilité
- les communautés dans les zones accueillant des personnes déplacées et / ou transhumants.
Des analyses de genre sont menées dans l´identification des besoins pour répondre aux besoins de chaque sexe de façon séparée et des notions d´accessibilité et d´équité dans l’accès aux services WASH intégrées. Les femmes et les hommes bénéficieront des ressources et avantages du projet sur un même pied d´égalité. Des actions encourageant la participation et la représentativité des femmes de manière équitable lors des processus de consultation et de prise de décisions ainsi que leur autonomisation, seront promues.
L’intervention vise à :
-Doter les communautés, les écoles et les centres de santé cibles du cercle de Mopti d’infrastructures WASH.
-Organiser des sensibilisations sur l’hygiène au profit de la communauté. Le changement de comportement sera suscité en dotant les femmes les plus vulnérables de kits d’hygiène et des élèves de kits de gestion menstruelle.
-Appuyer à la gestion des déchets solides par renforcement de capacités des groupes d’intérêt économiques (GIE) et dotation en équipements de travail, et l’accompagnement des communes pour la mise en place et le suivi effectifs de la filière, d’autre part.
-Participer aux réunions de préparation des réponses post inondation et pré-positionner un stock de contingence de 1000 kits d'hygiène.
-Renforcer les capacités des parties prenantes du secteur en vue d’asseoir une bonne gouvernance de la WASH. 
La mise en œuvre du projet se fera avec le partenaire local CAEB.
Des ateliers de lancement et de capitalisation seront organisés avec la communauté afin d’apporter une amélioration continue de l’intervention grâce aux échanges menés dans ces cadres. Des missions de supervision seront organisées avec les services techniques, les autorités locales et leaders communautaires pour un partage effectif d’information sur les activités. La collecte et le traitement des plaintes et doléances des bénéficiaires par le département MEAL de Help aidera à renforcer la redevabilité du projet.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of lifesaving assistance and sustainable solution of safe water sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, for people in crises and their host communities in multiple regions in Somalia.
project_objective:
IOM WASH is proposing to contribute to the provision of emergency and sustainable water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services to overall 350,000 beneficiaries living in vulnerable settlements and communities in multiple regions in Somalia. Twenty strategic water sources will be constructed and/or rehabilitated which will provide reliable and sustainable safe water and mitigate water shortages as result of displacement and recurrent drought/flooding in hotspots districts to be identified. IOM further proposes to construct 2,000 new emergency latrines and rehabilitate/desludge another 2,000 latrines in targeted settlements. 
The project will also strengthen the capacity of the federal/state government officials, community leaders and water committees/technicians for better coordination and sustainability of the constructed/ rehabilitated WASH infrastructures. In addition, the project will nurture community participation in good hygiene practices through training and community sensitization campaigns. The project is aligned with protection mainstreaming to ensure safety and dignity of affected populations without causing harm. Affected populations will further have meaningful access, accountability and participation of activities/beneficiaries design, implementation and feedback mechanism for WASH services. 
Furthermore, the project will be a part of an IOM integrated emergency response program and resilience building, where possible, efforts will be made to integrate IOM health, nutrition, shelter, CCCM and protection activities.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Delivering emergency life-saving primary healthcare to crisis-affected and vulnerable populations including internally displaced persons (IDPs), migrants, and host communities in Somalia
project_objective: IOM's 2020 HRP project for health will increase access and utilization of primary healthcare services among the most vulnerable and crisis-affected populations in the country. IOM will operate 35 static health facilities with integrated community outreach, as well as 10 mobile medical teams; many of the facilities are in areas that are hard-to-reach, remote, conflict-affected and isolated, lack other health actors, and where the population does not have access to basic life-saving health services. IOM will provide comprehensive primary healthcare services in line with the Essential Package of Health Services (EPHS), continuously build the capacity of health workers to ensure high quality of medical service delivery, and preposition medicines and medical supplies in regional hubs to ensure continuous supply to all of IOM-supported health facilities, as well as to the region at large in the event of a sudden emergency. At IOM-operated static facilities, health workers will conduct outreach into the surrounding and nearby communities, including preventative and curative services as well as health education aimed towards behavior change. At many of IOM-supported static clinics (wherever there are gaps), therapeutic services for children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) will be provided through integration of outpatient therapeutic programmes (OTPs) into the healthcare clinics. IOM will upgrade several existing health posts to provide basic emergency obstetric and newborn care (BEMONC) services, particularly in geographic areas where there are no other health facilities for safe deliveries. To mitigate against recurrent and expected shocks and the effects of continued conflict, IOM will conduct mass vaccination at the entry points to IDP sites, thus increasing immunization coverage and reducing outbreaks of communicable diseases. IOM will provide health education at the health facilities and in their catchment communities to effect behavior change in health, nutrition and hygiene practices that contribute to high excess morbidity and mortality, and to increase demand and utilization of preventative services such as antenatal care, facility delivery, and immunization. IOM will address gaps in mental health care and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through mainstreaming and integration of MHPSS into primary healthcare, coupled with community-level approaches (community-based PSS focused in IDP settlements). The project will benefit 526,500 individuals, including 319,001 children under 18 years. The project will be part of IOM’s integrated emergency response program which includes shelter and NFIs, camp coordination and management, WASH, and displacement tracking and monitoring.

project_name: Colombia - Norwegian Refugee Council
Emergency Assistance to Drought Affected Households
project_objective:
A second consecutive year of drought has resulted in wide spread hunger and suffering for poor and vulnerable people in Zimbabwe. The combination of back to back poor harvests, a challenging and
 deteriorating  macro-economic environment  and forecasts for reduced rainfall during the 2019/2020 season point  to  the high likelihood of yet another poor agricultural season with serious consequences that will persist throughout 2020 until the next harvest in 2021. The prices of basic agricultural inputs such as seeds and  fertilisers  have sky rocketed beyond the reach of most farmers. Moreover availability of traditional seed varieties at household and community levels has been eroded due to recurrent droughts. Post-harvest losses remain a major challenge for many smallholder farmers. According to study conducted by FAO About 30 percent of the harvested grain is lost due to lack of appropriate storage facilities. Thus any efforts to support the reestablishment of crop production needs to tackle issues of enhancing access to basic inputs, provision of training and addressing post-harvest losses.

Availability of water and grazing for livestock is very low across most parts of the country and this is affecting productivity and cattle sales. Most poor farmers cannot afford livestock supplementary stock feeds. More so it is not readily available on most markets. Poor cattle conditions coupled with above average disease prevalence are leading to an increased number of livestock deaths, mainly in the low rainfall parts of the country . 
Evidence generated by FAO has shown that when there shocks within a community or household, the worst affected are women who are primarily the providers of household food security. 

FAO is proposing a project that will ""Prevent further deterioration of living standards for acutely food insecure population, by providing emergency agriculture support aimed at ensuring they can achieve food security and resilience to repeated exposure to multiple shocks and stressors. The project will be implemented in 40 districts targeting 100, 000 households (500,000 people) in IPC phase 3 & 4.

FAO’s Response strategy is to provide emergency livelihood support  that will increase sustainable, climate smart agricultural production while promoting the growing and consumption of nutritious and diverse crops. The expected outputs of the project are
•	Crop  and livestock production capacity restored
•	Access to water resources for agricultural production increased
•	coordination in the food security and agriculture sector strengthened

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Provision of Integrated Health and Nutrition Assistance for Displaced and Non-Displaced  Populations in Banadir, Bay and Bakool regions of Somalia.
project_objective:
SOS Children's Villages International (SOS-CVI) is implementing emergency MCH interventions in Banadir and Bay since 1991 providing health, nutrition, and protection services to Internally Displaced People (IDP), returnees and host communities and recently expanded to Bakool. SOS Somalia aims to support the affected population to reduce the burden of diseases, improve equitable access to primary health care and improve nutrition. This will be achieved providing nutrition supplies to field and mobile maternal and child health services; and delivering fixed and mobile Outpatient Therapeutic Programs and referral of severely malnourished children with medical complication to the Stabilization Centers operated by partners. The project’s goal is to contribute towards reducing morbidity and mortality through an integrated emergency nutrition, health responses for disaster-affected vulnerable populations. To achieve this, an estimated 408,000 individuals (163,800 IDPs and 244,200 Host community members), affected by displacement and conflict in Bay, Bakool and Banadir will have improved health and nutritional knowledge and status, through improved access to preventive. Preventive components focus on Infant and Young child feeding (IYCF), Health and Nutrition education, immunization, community mobilization and sensitization. The proposed Health and Nutrition intervention is aligned to both Health and Nutrition cluster HRP priorities to focus on basic life-saving activities and community resilience-building activities in all high GAM/SAM and IDP areas. SOS CV Somalia provides referral to SOS hospital and other secondary health services providers. Services offered to PLWs will focus on the treatment of common diseases during pregnancy and childbirth such as anemia, hypertension, bleeding in pregnancy/postpartum, STIs, abortions, monitoring labour progress, safe and clean deliveries and follow up. Health education will focus on danger signs in pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum.
The project will ensure prevention and control of epidemic-prone and communicable diseases through appropriate detection and diagnosis; laboratory verification; confirmation; proper case management; adequate supplies; health education for patients; and regular vaccination programs and emergency vaccination activities for children and expectant mothers. SOS CV will monitor outbreak potential for diseases under surveillance within Somalia using the standard case definitions. Through extensive presence in communities, the project will sensitize around signs and symptoms of epidemic-prone diseases, mode of transmission, and preventative measures, and encourage early healthcare-seeking behavior. CHWs will be trained or receive refresher training to identify and refer cases of critical communicable diseases; and will be trained at a minimum to administer ORS for AWD. SOS Somalia proposes to address urgent needs and gaps in the health and nutrition sectors by offering free, comprehensive primary health care services in the target areas. SOS will also strengthen the capacity of implementation staff through joint supportive supervision with the Ministry of Health at the health and nutrition facilities. The project will employ an integrated approach to Health, Nutrition through fixed facilities and at community level to address the urgent health needs of vulnerable individuals through scaling up or setting up uninterrupted delivery of free, high quality health and nutrition services. The WASH supports provision of safe and clean drinking water in Nutrition and health sites as well as sanitation facilities. All nutrition sites will have hand washing facilities with soap and water to promote hygiene practices.

project_name: Transferencias efectivas para mejorar la nutrición, el gasto y las oportunidades (Transferencias efectivas para mejoras en nutrición, Gastos y oportunidades - TENGO)
project_objective:
Venezuela enfrenta un deterioro de sus condiciones de vida a causa de la situación socio-económica. La FAO estima que la tasa de subalimentación se ha cuadruplicado y que, cerca de 6,8 millones de personas se encuentran en situación de hambre. En marzo 2019, OCHA confirma que 3,4 y 3,2 millones de personas enfrentan necesidades humanitarias en seguridad alimentaria y nutrición respectivamente y que 2,3 millones de niños están en riesgo de desnutrición. 
Analizando el déficit en el acceso a alimentos se identifica que la brecha en la seguridad alimentaria de los hogares más pobres es de aproximadamente el 65% (35% del acceso se está cubriendo por las transferencias monetarias estatales, los alimentos subsidiados del programa oficial y por el salario mínimo oficial).  
Luego de 4 años de respuesta con un enfoque de asistencia temprana, Caritas Venezuela busca complementar el socorro con intervenciones de protección social como las transferencias monetarias. 
El proyecto tiene como objetivo general contribuir a cubrir las necesidades inmediatas de alimentación de las familias afectadas por la situación humanitaria de Venezuela, a través de transferencias monetarias incondicionales a familias en situación de vulnerabilidad en 5 Estados del país (Apure, Yaracuy, Sucre, Falcon, Delta Amacuro).  
El OBJETIVO ESPECÍFICO es mejorar el poder adquisitivo alimentario de las familias de los niños y mujeres embarazadas atendidos por el programa de protección nutricional “SAMAN” a través de transferencias a una tarjeta de pago valida en expendios de alimentos afiliados al proyecto. Se harán también actividades de promoción de los hábitos de alimentación, higiene y salud y preparación y distribución de comidas en fogones comunitarios. Cáritas aspira utilizar subsecuentemente las transferencias monetarias en la rehabilitación de medios de vida familiar. A tal fin se espera completar evaluaciones que permitan comprender mejor la base de sustento familiar y la identificación de accione relevantes. Cáritas ha puesto en marcha el programa TENGO en el último cuatrimestre del 2019 beneficiando con éxito a 1.710 familias en cuatro Estados del país. Este proyecto piloto marca el horizonte de trabajo en Cáritas a partir del 2020.

project_name: Supporting Peaceful coexistence and self-reliance of the refugees and the host communities
project_objective: The project will focus on enhancing household food, and nutrition security of the poorest and vulnerable households of both the host community and refugee. The targeted households will get support for nutritious food production. The activity will cover vegetable and fruits produced in the homestead with low irrigation facilities. In addition, it will promote self-reliance of the Host Community and refugees with selected beneficiaries who will receive capacity building training on the targeted trade and start-up package support to establish their enterprise. 80% of the targeted beneficiaries will be female from both the host communities and refugees. The project will work for empowering women through exclusively working with the women in the host community and camps for increasing their self-reliance. The intervention will be market oriented and including with the support from social enterprise. Overall, the project will raise awareness of the local institutions and communities for improving social cohesion between the Host Community and refugees.

project_name: Conflict Preparedness and Protection Safety & Risk Education in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Project Objective: Civilians living in high risk conflict-affected communities in the Gaza Strip are better prepared to protect themselves in case of armed conflict and are empowered with the knowledge they need to mitigate risks associated with explosive weapons.

The proposed interventions will be in line with the NPA Palestine Country Strategy 2020-2023 in Gaza and are aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 1: “Prevent and mitigate the effects of the Occupation and conflict related violence.” Project activities are also specifically aligned with Protection Cluster Objective 2 of the HRP, “Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence,” and will contribute to this objective through the provision of Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP) and Explosive Remnant of War (ERW) risk education for civilian residents (adults and children) of the Gaza Strip.

The proposed interventions are planned to take place in 2020, representing the third year of NPA's CPP implementation for 2018-2020. Over three-year programme period, the programme will be implemented using the same methodologies; training adults and children, but for new beneficiaries and new communities which will be prioritized based on Ministry of Education planning and in consultation with the Protection Cluster and the Mine Action Working Group.

project_name: Assistance en abris et NFY aux ménages vulnérables parmi les nouveaux réfugiés et la communauté hôte dans le Département de Barh Sara  (Moissala) au Sud du Tchad.
project_objective:
L’objectif global du projet est de fournir une assistance d’urgence visant la population nouvellement réfugiée de la RCA, et les personnes à besoins spécifiques parmi la population autochtone dans le Département de Barh Sara, Province du Mandoul, au Sud du Tchad. Le résultat attendu de ce projet est : Des conditions de logement décentes et des articles ménagers essentiels sont fournis aux nouveaux réfugiés centrafricains. Il s’agit de créer des conditions de logement décentes aux nouveaux réfugiés centrafricains en utilisant des matériaux locaux et de la main d’œuvre locale. Pour y arriver, 2000 abris semi-durables seront construits et dans lesquels 2000 ménages parmi les nouveaux réfugiés seront installés et des articles ménagers essentiels seront mis à la disposition de tous les bénéficiaires (2 000 ménages réfugiés et 560 ménages de la population hôte. Un mécanisme de suivi évaluation, d’apprentissage et de capitalisation sera mis en place et permettra d’assurer la qualité de l’intervention sur le terrain. Le choix de faire la distribution des articles ménagers (kits NFY) se justifie par la nécessité de contribuer à la couverture de leurs besoins immédiats. En effet, les 2 560 ménages qui bénéficieront de ces kits seront identifiés parmi les nouveaux réfugiés et les populations hôtes les plus vulnérables notamment les pauvres et très pauvres. CARE achètera directement ces articles pour les distribuer aux bénéficiaires. Ce qui limitera les risques d’inflation dans la zone du projet et ; permettra aux ménages d’accéder à tout le kit complet (marmites, plateaux, etc.)
Les bénéficiaires directs du projet sont constitués de 2 640 ménages soit 15840 personnes dont au moins 60% de femmes. Parmi ces bénéficiaires directs, l’on aura : 2 000 ménages des nouveaux réfugiés soit 12 000 personnes (7 200 femmes, 4 800 hommes) ; et, 640 ménages vulnérables de la population hôte.La sélection des bénéficiaires notamment les réfugiés se fera en coordination avec l’UNHCR sur la base de la liste ProGress. En effet, les réfugiés (nouveaux comme anciens) sont enregistrés par l’UNHCR et la CNARR et disposent chacun d’un numéro d’identification.  L’identification des ménages de la population hôte bénéficiaires du projet se basera sur les critères de vulnérabilité selon la méthodologie HEA (Très pauvres, Pauvres, Moyens et Nantis). Lesquels critères seront combinés à ceux qui seront identifiés par les communautés bénéficiaires elles-mêmes. Pour ce faire, un comité d’identification sera mis en place au niveau de chaque village et site/camp. Ce qui permettra une participation communautaire dans ce processus.
Le groupe cible pour lequel une attention particulière sera accordée est celui constitué des personnes à besoins spécifiques notamment les femmes chefs de ménages, les personnes vivant avec un handicap, etc. Les filles / femmes et les garçons / hommes de tous âges, handicapés ou non, peuvent accéder aux activités humanitaires prévues dans le projet s’ils répondent aux critères de vulnérabilité définis par le HEA (pauvre, très pauvre, moyen et nantis) et à ceux définis et validés par les communautés elles-mêmes.

project_name: Legal Aid for Protection at EECPs
project_objective: DRC-DDG aims to implement this legal aid and capacity building project to (a) strengthen protection for conflict-affected people, including IDPs through the provision of needs based legal assistance; (b) to ensure conflict-affected people, including IDPs, benefit from full and non-discriminatory access to high quality legal services. The action will address the legal needs of the most vulnerable displaced and conflict-affected populations in eastern Ukraine through a legal assistance intervention. It will also improve the resilience of conflict-affected population, including IDPs, and strengthen local response capacity through the FSLAC to ensure their access to quality legal services. The project will improve access to legal assistance and legal remedies by targeting persons who reside within GCA (0-5 km) area as well as NGCA (0-20 km) and cross the line of contact (LoC) through the five designated Entry-Exit Check Points (EECP). Beneficiaries will be identified and prioritised (through referral mechanisms when necessary) in cooperation with FSLAC lawyers, working at the EECPs under the existing ECHO project that is being implemented by DRC-DDG. R2P Eastern Ukraine Checkpoint Monitoring statistics for 9 months demonstrate that 94% of people, who crossed the contact line, were NGCA residents with 15% of them living in NGCA 0-20 km. area. According to the State Border Service, almost 15 mln. cross the contact-line at five EECPs annually. It means that on average 119 people cross the contact line each hour at all EECPs in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts (working hours in the fall). Alignment of these two highly credible data sources and their analysis demonstrates that each day of the project implementation may improve access to legal services for 130 NGCA residents living within 0-20 km. area. As there are 250 working days in a year (Ukraine, 2019), the approximate number of NGCA residents (0-20 km.) who would have better access to legal assistance during the project implementation is 32,500. The proposed project builds on DRC-DDG’s strengths and experience in legal aid provision, partnership network, as well as DRC-DDG’s resources and expertise in legal analysis. The proposed Action will be implemented through the five satellite centres to be operated by the Local Centre For Free Secondary Legal Aid Provision (FSLAC). DRC-DDG already has a partnership arrangement with FSLAC under which FSLAC has been providing primary and secondary legal assistance at three EECPs (Mayorsk, Novotroitske, and Marynka) in the past year. The proposed Action will fund these three existing EECPs as well as operationalise the other two EECPS at Hnutove and Stanytsia Luhanska. Full operationalisation of Hnutove and Stanytsia Luhanska EECP is subject to approval of local authorities, security clearance, availability of movable workstations, and access to services including access to utility. As of the date of writing this Action, DRC-DDG and FSLAC is confident of availability of such facilities in Stanytsia Luhanska. DRC-DDG and FSLAC will make best efforts to extract cooperation from all relevant stakeholders to install permanent facilities in Hnutove. In the event that a permanent station in Hnutove is not viable, the Action will cover beneficiaries at Hnutove EECPs through daily mobile clinics.

project_name: Protection of IDPs, IDP and Refugee Returnees and coflict affected communities in Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile States
project_objective:
Despite the recent positive developments in the establishment of a transitional gov., it is expected that Sudan will continue to face severe macro-economic political challenges. Overall, the situation remains fluid and humanitarian needs will further increase as underlying challenges are not expected to change in the immediate future. The humanitarian situation in Sudan will remain a complex mix of IDPs and IDP returnees. The sustainable solutions for the issues of displaced persons ” are prioritized among the “essential issues for peace negotiations” agreed upon the Constitutional Charter for the 2019 Transitional Period, signed in 17 Aug.19  agreeing on transitional arrangements for the forthcoming 39 months. The aim of the Constitutional Declaration is to “end the war by addressing the roots of the Sudanese problem and handling its effects”. 

It envisages the completion of a fair and comprehensive peace in the Sudan no later than 6 months from its signing. As of Nov.19, peace negotiations between the Gov. of Sudan armed groups are ongoing with yet to be determined outcomes. Areas of origin in Sudan have been affected by years of conflict, marginalization and neglect. They often lack basic community infrastructure essential social services, while rural livelihoods were seriously disrupted.

Competition for, and pressures on, natural resources within Darfur, partly due to a history of drought and famine, compound the legacy of the conflict. Communities usually lack resources, structures governance capabilities allowing for different groups, youth in particular, to engage collectively in peacebuilding, dialogue, public service, economic activities. UNHCR will work closely with the gov. on IDP protection and ES/NFI assistance, on safe and dignified vol. return to Sudan, on durable solutions for IDP populations including related peacebuilding initiatives. The main areas of origin include all 5 Darfur, SKS and BNS. Although Sudan has not formally committed to the CRRF yet, the country has de-factor applied several components of the CRRF. 

Operational priorities in 2020 are: 

1. IDP protection

project_name: EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE TO DISPLACED POPULATIONS AND STRANDED MIGRANTS IN CHAD
project_objective:
The revision of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) 2019 sees addressing the needs related to displacement as a priority alongside food security and health. IOM participates actively in the Camp Coordination and Camp Management/Non-Food Items/Shelter (CCCM/NFI/Shelter) Cluster and coordinate activities closely.
Chad’s Lac province has been directly affected by the ongoing conflict with Boko Haram. As of October 2019, 169 003 internally displaced persons (IDPs), 47,364 returnees (either former IDPs or Chadians who returned from Nigeria and Niger) and 5,652 third-country nationals (from Cameroon, Niger, Mali and Nigeria) lived in the three most affected departments of the Lac province either in camps and informal settlements, or in host communities. People are forced to flee their homes very quickly during periods of more intense fighting, leaving behind assets, food and other belongings. There is a consensus among humanitarian agencies involved in the cluster that emergency shelter and NFI assistance is a high priority Humanitarian needs among these populations remain high and not all of the sites have so far been reached with humanitarian assistance due to security issues and related access problems. On October 2019, IOM Emergency Tracking Tool estimated 47,000 new displaced people in the Lake region because of the intensification of Boko Haram activities in the first 6 months of 2019.  
Southern provinces of Chad have been affected by heavy rains and consequent flood during the months of August and September 2019. IOM Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT), as product of the wider DTM department, tracked the movement of around 2700 individuals who are now displaced in host villages or displacement sites (ETT #24, #25 and #27). At same time, in August 2019, IOM Goré received the request of assistance from leaders of Kobiteye villages (Nya Pendé department) as floods destroyed an important number of houses. These displaced people are in need of Shelter/NFI and other kind of assistance. 
During the same period of 2019, IOM ETTs also tracked the movement of around 6000 individuals caused by intercommunal conflict between farmer and herders. The ETT #21 reported 5200 people displaced in the Ouaddai province (Ouara department). The INGO Premiere Urgence Internationale, following IOM ETT alert, conducted a partial rapid evaluation on the affected sites (limited access on all displaced sites because of ongoing rainy season), retrieving 2000 displaced people in need of Shelter/NFI and other humanitarian assistance. Few days after this movement, another group of 1000 people were intercepted by IOM #23 ETT as fleeing intercommunal conflicts in the Moyen Chari province (Bahr-Köh department). To date, no intervention has been reported.
Humanitarian needs also exist among stranded migrants in the north-northwest of the country after military operations that started in early 2018 and continue on 2019 with the aim of evacuate goldmines areas on the Tibesti, who find themselves without any assistance and are extremely vulnerable to become victims of traffickers or smugglers. IOM already assisted around 3000 people in 2019 (600 only between September and november 2019) when more waves of movements are expected to reach Faya in the next months.
IOM suggests the following priority measures: 
Lac and Soutern provinces: provision of 3000 emergency and 150 semi-permanent shelter and distribution of 3500 NFIs for the most vulnerable persons among the above mentioned target groups and host communities.
Northen provinces: Assistance to 3000 stranded migrants coming from Libya and goldmine areas as emergency food, NFI and emergency transportation.

project_name: Education in Emergencies services for critically affected children of Rohingya refugees and host communities
project_objective: Save the Children (SC) aims to continue access for children affected by the displacement crisis to safe, protective, inclusive and age appropriate learning and development opportunities in the camps and host communities under Ukhia and Teknaf  of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh through establishing and maintaining 106 Learning Centres (LCs) incl. 3 in host communities, 140 Community Based Learning Facilities (known as home based learning spaces) and 10 Cross Sectoral Facilities (known as Girl Friendly Spaces) for informal early learning and basic education, enhancing knowledge of parents and caregivers on how to support their children’s learning, development, and well-being, and improving the quality of teaching through continuous teaching-related support. Inclusive aspects of programming including: gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, disability-sensitive as well as integration between sectors including child protection will be mainstreamed in all activities to ensure that different needs of girls and boys will responded to, and they will equitably benefit from the interventions. Special attention will be paid in capacity building of staff on key teaching and Social Emotional Learning (SEL) issues. All the learning facilities will also provided with gender segragated WASH points while physical infrastructure, materials and methodologies will be strengthened to ensure access and equity for children living with disabilities. Being a sector co-lead, SC will continue to play a key role in advocacy, increased quality and sustainability of education services for the displaced Rohingya in Bangladesh.

project_name: Colombia - World Vision International
PROJECT REVISED - Resilience for Food Security and Livelihoods to Drought and Conflict Affected communities in Somalia
project_objective:
According to Somalia response plan (2019), humanitarian situation in the last six months demonstrates the continued unpredictable and volatile context in Somalia . While the unexpectedly plentiful Gu rain season (April-June 2018) led to an overall improvement in the food security outlook country-wide, it also brought severe flooding across vast areas of southern and central Somalia. In May 2018, cyclone Sagar devastated parts of Somaliland and Puntland, compounding humanitarian needs generated by the dispute in Sool and Sanaag.The current humanitarian situation remains  precarious   in Somalia due to repeated climate shocks, continued conflict and violence.Without sustained humanitarian support,most of the poor households including IDPs and returnees might face very poor food security outcomes in the coming months.
Failed /poor 2019 Gu’ (April-June) rains which followed poor 2018 Deyr (October-December) rains and of harsh weather conditions during the dry Jilaal season (January-March). Water scarcity, widespread crop failure and accelerated decline in livestock productivity have seen communities slide into acute food insecurity or worse. Consequently, the number of people in acute food insecurity (IPC 3 and 4) has spiked by ten per cent, to more than 1.7 million in 2019. The number is expected to increase if the prevailing dry conditions persist and the Deyr rains perform below average.

The October-December 2019 Deyr rains, which are forecast to be average, are expected to usher in some food security improvements. In pastoral areas of greatest concern, livestock births are anticipated to increase herd sizes, enabling poor households to engage in some distressed sales of livestock. According to FSNAU and FEWSNET,An estimated 2.2 million people are expected to experience Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) outcomes through September and are urgently in need of humanitarian food assistance and interventions to prevent high levels of acute malnutrition. This number could increase as the dry season progresses. Should the onset of the forecast average Deyr rains be delayed by 20-30 days, agropastoral households in South/Central would experience a third consecutive season of below-average production due to the shortened crop growing period. This would also extend the lean season to January, increase cereal prices to above average, and reduce agriculture labor income. Herd sizes would likely be further depleted through distressed sales and low productivity and reproduction. Emergency (IPC Phase 4) would be sustained in agropastoral of Hiiraan and Crisis (IPC Phase 3) would be widespread in the country.The exception is Guban Pastoral livelihood zone, where herd sizes are lowest and Emergency (IPC Phase 4) is likely to persist.This means that the food security outcomes ,are unlikely to improve until mid 2020.
World Vision is proposing a an integrated food and livelihood security project which will cushion the poor households against sliding into acute food security and destitution while also building a stronger foundation for resilience building.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Improving WASH service delivery for disaster-affected communities in Somalia
project_objective: The Humanitarian Response Plan identified WASH red spot districts which are at high risk to disease outbreak, water scarcity, high latrine safety index owing to high mobility associated with disaster. WV Somalia will target two regions and having worked in Sool, Baidoa, Burtinle and Garowe districts would like to build on its footprints with regards to WASH service delivery. Sool will be targeted from both the Somaliland region (Ainabo district) and Puntland (Baarmmado). WASH programming will be undertaken at community, school and health levels. The program aims to achieve two results/outcomes, that is, firstly increased access to sustainable and safe water supply for poor, vulnerable communities, children in school and in health facilities and secondly target population has access to reliable and sustainable environmental sanitation. WV has a commitment to supporting capacity-building efforts for local people and government line ministries. World Vision currently works with the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources and the Ministry of Health in the implementation of its WASH activities in South West State, Puntland and Somaliland. This deliberate effort at partnering provides a platform for capacity building for the Ministry personnel, and at the same time strengthens collaboration and ensures World Vision strategy is in sync with the mandate and strategy of the local government. WV is mindful of local custom and culture. It is also committed to participatory and sustainable development and to providing assistance impartially. WV acknowledge their accountabilities to those whom they assist and those who provide support to their work and also committed to ensuring that it does not expose intended beneficiaries, including children, to any form of discrimination, abuse or exploitation. To ensure sustainable delivery, WV seeks to encourage participation in decision making processes and skills training so as to ensure that the beneficiaries will act as an active component in the implementation of the program. The WASH program has been deliberate in ensuring its facilities are inclusive and can be used by people with physical disabilities. One of the key areas has been ensuring that latrines are accessible to wheelchair-bound persons by incorporating ramps as standard at doorways and having wide fully opening doors. For public sanitation facilities, ramps and rails have also been installed as standard for the sanitation facilities. Sector integration will also be fostered. The WASH program will work closely with the Education and Protection and Health and Nutrition sectors. The WASH programme in Health Facilities will focus on ensuring all consultations and admissions, including children under the age of 5 have access to clean water and sanitation within the target locations. At each of the health facilities, World Vision will provide an elaborate water and sanitation management programme, which will include incinerators, autoclaves, clean water, and institutional latrines for proper infection prevention and control practices. The schools will be connected to the main water supply and receive occasional water trucking at times when the main water supply is erratic. Children will also be provided with WASH NFIs, including MHM kits that will be given to adolescent girls at the schools to help reduce on the number of girls who drop out of school during their menstrual cycle. Ideally, the 3-star approach will be adopted and guide operations in schools. DRR will include developing capacity of local government to understand, own and trigger demand for WASH through advocacy to take policy decisions to develop a political will that enable a WASH resilience building

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Enhancing integrated nutrition humanitarian response among internally displaced populations (IDPs) and the host community in select districts of Somaliland, Puntland and South Central Regions of Somalia.
project_objective: The proposed action aims at contributing towards the reduction of mortalities and morbidities associated with Malnutrition among under-five children and pregnant and lactating women by providing preventive and curative nutrition interventions and enhancing accessibility to nutrition services at select districts of Somaliland, Puntland and South Central. The action is geared towards reducing the vulnerability among target populations thus preventing or reducing levels of malnutrition within the chronic humanitarian context of Somalia. In order to achieve sustainable impact, the Project will be integrated with other health care services for enhanced provision of basic life-saving interventions and standard Health, Nutrition and WASH services at community level, health facilities and IDP camps in urban areas. Through the proposed action, WVSOM envisages to strengthen preventive and curative services and enhance community mobilization and sensitization for increased awareness on available services leading to increased up-take of Nutrition services and other integrated Health and WASH interventions at community level. Community engagement and participation will be crucial throughout the project cycle for ownership and active involvement during implementation and enhanced sustainability after project phase-out. WVSOM will work with community health workers (CHWs) and volunteer mothers at community level to support in the implementation of the project for early identification, referral and prompt treatment of malnourished children and PLWs for better health outcomes in addition to securing positive behaviour change on infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices. To enhance effective implementation of the project, WVSOM will actively participate in nutrition cluster coordination mechanisms both at national and Zonal level. The proposed action intends to support early warning mechanisms, alert and response systems/surveillance with close linkages to the respective sectors to ensure prompt and early response to prevent excess mortality and morbidity. The action will endeavor to strengthen some aspects of health system strengthening (HSS) by building the capacity of MOH staff, provision of essential drugs and other essential supplies, support the support supervision field visits to target health facilities in order to improve quality service delivery to the target communities.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- GBV Response for IDPs, Refugee Returnees and Host Communities in Bakool, Gedo, Bay, Nugaal, Bari, Togdheer and Awdal Regions
project_objective:
This action seeks to prevent and respond to GBV mainly faced by women and girls who are either internally displaced, refugee returnees, refugees and vulnerable host communities in Bakool, Gedo, Bay, Nugaal and Bari Regions. Protection crisis continues to prevail as a result of the multi-faceted armed conflict and inter-communal violence. This situation is compounded by natural disasters such as drought and floods which further weaken the resilience of the households and community at large. The economic strain faced by households is one of the key drivers of domestic violence and separation of families in search of greener pastures. The formal and informal GBV response system is equally weakened as a result of limited resources and inadequate technical support for survivors of GBV especially  psycho-social support services and inadequate access to PEP kits in remote hard to reach locations of Waajid, Xudur, Luuq, Bardhere, Qansadhere and Buurhakaba. This affects access to targeted and timely response for cases such as rape which require support within 72 hours. Recent assessments conducted by WVI indicate that survivors of GBV especially women and girls continue to suffer from stigma and phenomena like rape and other forms of SGBV is a taboo subject.  WVI existing project reports indicate that most of the GBV cases reported in the IDP camps. Women and girls from host communities who herd animals in far flung areas and fetch water from water points that are at a long distance usually fall prey to the perpetrators of GBV. It has also been reported that intimate partner violence tends to increase at household level as a result of cash based assistance since women are the ones usually registered as household heads. 
It is against this background that WVI seeks to prioritize increasing the geographical reach for life saving services and improving the service provision. Population targeted (33,600) includes boys, girls, women and men mostly in IDP camps and remote locations. Women and girls at risk of GBV will be provided with livelihood support through training (TVET) and cash based interventions. In addition, the project will advocate for and create safe spaces for women and girls. Men and boys will equally be mobilized against GBV. The project will deliberately work with faith leaders to advocate against GBV and eventually partner with them to speak against the vice and reduce stigma. Clan elders and GBV committees will be targeted for capacity building on reporting and referral pathway to ensure services are accessed within the critical window period. GBV medical support at the existing WV supported health facilities will also be improved through capacity building and positioning of staff to offer comprehensive services to survivors.

project_name: Colombia - Mercy Corps
Food Assistance for Conflict Affected IDPs, Returnees and Refugees in South Sudan
project_objective:
Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food
security crises, including those living in POCs, those otherwise affected by conflict and/or
seasonal food insecurity and refugees. 

WFP introduces GFD+ as a modification to GFD as a means for improving emergency food assistance, such that the people we serve are better equipped to fight hunger and improve nutrition. GFD+ encourages the participation of beneficiaries in activities such as trainings for skills development or light public works in conjunction with the receipt of GFD. GFD+ seeks to shift beneficiary mindsets towards building their own capacity to become less dependent on external aid and more self-reliant, while increasing their individual and community resilience to shocks.

project_name: Strengthening Integrated Primary Health Care Service Delivery To Vulnerable Populations in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States
project_objective:
This project is aimed at strengthening integrated primary health care services delivery in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States. These states border Niger, Cameroon and Chad are expected to continue to receive increased numbers of returnees from hard to reach locations within Borno, Chad and Cameroun in addition to the over 1.8 million IDPs these states currently host as a result of on-going 10-year conflict. In Borno state, increased clashes over the past months between armed actors have essentially cut off once accessible locations and populations to humanitarian aid while significantly overburdening safer zones with increased congestion within the available IDP camps.

UNICEF, in partnership with the primary health care agencies, will support vulnerable groups through the provision of an integrated package of primary health care services to children under five years old, women and their families through IDP camp clinics and health facilities in host communities.
UNICEF will work with other NGO partners to support the Government to provide rapid response activities 19 LGAs with a protracted crisis context with high humanitarian needs while supporting Health System Strengthening (HSS) work in the remaining 18 stable LGAs. 

UNICEF will focus on reaching people in need, including returnees, as well as supporting the three states (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe) to implement interventions that will enable the transition from emergency phase to development in stable LGAs. In addition, UNICEF will partner with INGOs that are present on the ground and provide strategic technical assistance in building capacity for resilience at the community level. UNICEF will review existing supplies architecture and focus on the procurement and supply of essential medicines tailoring to the needs on the ground. UNICEF will leverage its comparative strengths to ensure the dovetailing of resources through convergence with other sections within UNICEF and other sectors at the state, LGAs and community levels for the attainment of sustainable and synergistic re-enforcing results.

The following objectives will be met through the project:
•	Meet the immediate health needs of conflict-affected populations;
•	Restore essential health services;
•	Rehabilitate the health system; and
•	Strengthen government led/operated health systems strengthening program

project_name: Investing in Nutrition in Syria, Promoting Infrastructure and Resources in the Economy
project_objective:
Building on GC’s successful OFDA and FFP-funded Syria programs, the Investing in Nutrition in Syria, Promoting Infrastructure and Resources in the Economy (INSPIRE) program will deliver an integrated package of assistance to meet emergency food needs of the most vulnerable, and support HH and community food security in north Syria. INSPIRE will: 1) meet the immediate food needs of vulnerable  individuals through provision of RTERs and monthly food baskets; 2) increase food security for vulnerable  individuals through provision of kitchen garden kits, livestock, fodder, mobile fodder mill, and food production and storage; 3) enhance community food security for people through improved wheat storage and fire control; and 4) support bread production at bakeries through distribution of wheat, flour, and rehabilitation of bakeries and mills. In total, INSPIRE will support 83,225 vulnerable Syrians in NWS.


INSPIRE will: 1) meet the immediate food needs of 2,500 vulnerable HH/ 12,500 individuals through provision of RTERs and 3,125 HH / 15,625 individuals through provision of monthly food baskets; 2) increase food security for 1,200 HH / 7,200 individuals through provision of kitchen garden kits. and 3) support bread production at 5 bakeries serving an estimated 50,000 individuals through distribution of wheat, flour, yeast, and rehabilitation of bakeries and mills. In total, INSPIRE will support 85,325 vulnerable Syrians.

project_name: Provide Lifesaving Assistance through integrated WASH, Nutrition, Food Security and Livelihoods, Protection and NFIs/ES for IDPs, Returnees, Under Served Host Communities and nomadic pastoralists.
project_objective:
The project aims to support the IDPs, Returnees, and vulnerable host communities in
Darfur states (North, South and Central) and Kassala States to improve food security and livelihood, WASH (water, sanitation and hygiene), Nutrition, NFIs/ shelters and protection assistance. The assistant will address the consequences of the conflicts, epidemics, drought and absolute destitution that endanger lives of the target communities and their livelihood resources. The project aims to assist 180,000 beneficiaries (40,000 in North Darfur, 55,000 in South Darfur and 35,000 in Central Darfur and 50,000 in Kassala). The target beneficiaries include internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the camps and rural areas with focus on the newly displaced people and their respective host communities, returnees, vulnerable rural communities and nomadic pastoralist communities. The project will be implemented in close coordination with the sector leads and other implementing actors from the INGOs, NNGOs and relevant governmental departments to ensure collaborative and complementarity coverage of the needs and avoid overlap or duplication.
The project activities incorporate humanitarian response by a provision of assistance to save lives and alleviate suffering, and building the target communities’ resilience to withstand shocks through livelihood restoration and building household productive assets and develop productive and managerial skills for target communities to enable the target beneficiaries to sustain the provided assistance and cope with future changes and reduce vulnerability.

project_name: Provision of school meals to school children in Syria
project_objective:
The School meals programme was introduced as part of WFP’s Syria crisis response in 2014 to meet basic food security needs of girls and boys particularly in areas hosting large number of affected populations with low food security and education indicators.  
The programme includes: 
-	In kind food distribution including daily distribution of fresh meals  or  fortified snacks  to  children in primary schools ( grades 1-6) during school days
-	electronic vouchers to students who were out of school and have returned to education and are enrolled in curriculum B ( 8-14 years old). The provision of the electronic voucher is conditional to students achieving 80% monthly attendance.  
School meals activities covers all children registered in the targeted schools including children with disability attending those schools. The Activities are aligned with the timeframe of the school year, thus, they start in September and ends by May of the next year. Distribution of snacks may continue in the summer to support last chance camps.

The school meals programme aims to restore and stabilize access to education in crisis- affected areas as well as to enhance health and nutrition status of children in targeted areas. By encouraging regular attendance and enrollment, the programme also contributes to providing protection to children from reverting to negative coping mechanism such as child labor and child marriage. Therefore, the programme meets the first obhective of the education sector “Increased safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education for crisis-affected children”

The programme targets school-aged children enrolled in basic education and is implemented jointly with the Ministry of Education and other partners of the education sector in Syria including UN agencies and  National NGOs. with the increase of needs in terms of food security and education severity,  the project will target 1150000 students this year with the same 3 modalities ( in kind : fortified snacks and fresh meals , and Cash transfer).
WFP will continue to reach  the targeted  1,150,000  children  per month  but less frequently due to the current circumstances that lead to closure of schools and lead to less requirement in terms of funding.

The programme does not offer universal coverage to all to all basic education students. In case of lower funding, priority will be given to location where severity scale of food  security and education is more than 
 

1.	WFP will target sub-districts with combined education and food severity of 4-6 
2.     The cost per beneficiary is 54 USD for the whole year 
3.	Estimated % of targeted beneficiaries that may have disabilities : 5%
4.	Total estimated funding the organization received in 2019, USD 32 Million 
5.  The total number of children reached in 2019 was 781,873 children.

project_name: Colombia - Pan American Development Foundation
Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada en Venezuela.
project_objective:
ACH trabaja en Venezuela atendiendo las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables al riesgo de desnutrición aguda: niños y niñas (particularmente menores de 5 años), mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, personas con discapacidades, o con problemas severos de salud y en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes para estas personas la situación de pobreza y sus limitaciones de acceso a alimentos, a condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, y su reducida capacidad de acceso a la salud, la educación y el trabajo. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia -especialmente la de género, embarazos adolescentes, ITS, o criminalidad. Las estrategias de sobrevivencia pueden llevar a reducir la ingesta calórica o de nutrientes, a la venta de activos, y hasta a la emigración. 
A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para reducir el sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas humanas, identificando casos de desnutrición en sus diferentes niveles, y a las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará de manera funcional con instituciones locales, y en particular con escuelas y centros de salud.
ACH trabajará según su programa nacional 2020 en intervenciones articuladas, complementarias e integrales: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda. 2) Salud: equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos, especialmente para las madres y adolescentes.  3) Seguridad Alimentaria: distribución de alimentos/transferencias monetarias/cupones/soporte para la producción de alimentos, apoyo en actividades para resiliencia, formaciones en seguridad alimentaria. 4) WASH: acceso a servicios básicos de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en instituciones educativas, espacios de aprendizaje y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación/ingeniería de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades.

project_name: Renforcement du mécanisme de coordination, de prévention des abus et violences (IDTR, VBG, EAFGA, MRE) à l’égard des enfants affectés par la crise humanitaire et amélioration de l'accès et la qualité de leur prise en charge multisectorielle dans les départements de Diffa, Nguigmi, Bosso, Maine Soroa, région de Diffa, au Niger.
project_objective: Ce projet vise à renforcer les mécanismes de coordination en acteurs, y compris communautaire, la prévention et de réponse multisectorielle aux abus et violences à l'égard des enfants affectés par les crises multiformes dans la région de Diffa, avec un accent sur la prévention des risques de séparations familiales, l'identification, la prise en charge transitoire et la réunification des enfants séparés et non accompagnés, la documentation, la prise en charge alternative et la réintégration des enfants sortis des groupes armés, la réduction de risque et catastrophes en lien avec le secteur éducatif. Ce projet assure aussi le renforcement de l’approche communautaire de protection de l’enfant, notamment dans les zones difficiles d’accès comme Bosso et Toumour, en vue d’offrir aux enfants les plus défavorisés, un accès aux services de protection et une réponse de qualité. Le projet assure également un renforcement des capacités des structures et des acteurs communautaires de protection de l'enfant, notamment sur l'éducation au risque de mines et le référencement de cas abus sexuels sur les enfants et adolescents (CASI).

project_name: Provision of timely lifesaving WASH integrated with nutrition, health and gender-based violence to the most vulnerable communities affected by conflict, disease outbreak, in areas of high malnutrition through integrated response, reinforced protection and community capacity building to increase coping mechanism.
Aide humanitaire pour les déplacés internes et les communautés d’accueil des départements de Tilia et Abalak
project_objective:
Le présent projet - d'une durée de 12 mois - propose de renforcer la capacité des ménages IDP et hôtes à résister aux chocs dans les départements de Tilia et Abalak, affectés par les crises, à travers une assistance humanitaire en cash conditionnel pour 3000 ménages dans le besoin sur le département d'Abalak ainsi que des activités de WASH pour les 22925 IDP qu'accueillent le Département de Tilia.
Plus précisément, il s'agit de :
- Restaurer 1500 hectares de terres pastorales en argent contre travail pour 3000 ménages vulnérables dans le département d'Abalak. Les ouvrages (demi-lunes, banquettes ou zaï) seront ensemencés, plantés et mis en défens

Les  cibles spécifiques de ce projet sont :
- 22 925 personnes déplacées internes dont 11921 femmes, 11830 enfants de moins de 18 ans, 802 personnes âgées et 940 personnes vivant avec un handicap pour des activités de WASH

- 300 personnes vivant avec un handicap et personnes âgées en situation d'urgence pour des activités de cash transfert inconditionnel

project_name: Emergency Education Response for crisis affected children and youth in South Sudan
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to ensure that crisis affected children and youths in South Sudan continuously access quality learning and training opportunities that are relevant to their psychosocial, emotional and cognitive development in a safe, inclusive and protected environment. NRC will ensure that conflict-affected children and youth have strengthened resilience to current and future crises, and can contribute to the peaceful socio-economic development of South Sudan. 

A total of 32,759 (16052 girls/16707 boys) children and youth will benefit from the project. Additionally, 600 PTA members and 800 (20% female) teachers in target schools will benefit from the project through training, awareness raising, support supervision, education materials and monitoring. The target group will include displaced, returnees and host community children, youth, and adults, particularly the most vulnerable, including girls who are most at risk of harm and abuse and children with disabilities who often experience barriers or discrimination in access to and uptake of education services, in government and opposition areas. The project will focus on strengthening and improving quality in delivery of education in emergency affected areas through four strategic response areas: 1) support to formal basic education in static operations; 2) first phase response through the mobile rapid response mechanism; 3) Alternative Education Programme for older children who had dropped out of the education system; and 4) youth education and training. The strategic response will enhance access to quality education and skills programmes for children and youth affected by the crisis in static IDP/PoC sites and host communities, as well as in new emergencies and hard-to-reach locations. The project is in line with the 2020 South Sudan Education Cluster objectives (CO1, 2 and 3), the South Sudan Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies, the South Sudan General Education Strategic Plan 2017-2022 (GESP). Emphasis will be placed on Strengthen the education system response capacity of the community and education actors to mitigate the impact of emergency on children and youth through training of PTA on preparedness and response planning and engagement of community in project implementation, decision-making, accountability, and ownership.

Key project activities will include but not limited to constriction and rehabilitation of temporary learning spaces, provision of teaching and learning materials, staining of teachers on pedagogy and psychosocial; support, provision of school feeding in IPC 3&4  areas, awareness raising on life saving messages and protection, construction of WASH facilities and hygiene promotion as well as  training of PTA. The project will leverage integrated programming to ensure children learn in a safe and inclusive environment. provision of segregated WASH facilities for boys and girls, tree planting, clean school environment, sensitization of school communities on protection, child safeguarding, teachers’ professional code of conduct, as well as referral pathways for reporting cases of abuse. ensure access to legal documentation for ALP students and youth establishing own business. School feeding linked to both health and education outcome.

The rapid response mechanism will target children aged 3-5 yeas old and the primary education will target boys and girls age 6-14 years. This will include children with disability from both IDPs, Returnees and host communities. Adolescent boys and girls 14 years and above will be provided life skills and training support.  Girls are particularly more vulnerable to drop out of school and they will be targeted with protection messages and provision of sanitary kits.

There will be no risk of duplication as the project will target Northern Bahr El Ghazal,Western Bahr El Ghazal, Central Equatoria, Warrap and Jonglei where NRC already has static presence.

project_name: Improving access to quality Primary healthcare services including Sexual and Reproductive Health, Mental Health and Psychosocial support and GBV prevention for women, men, girls and boys in Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast, Eastern Ukraine (GCA and NGCA)
project_objective:
Building on MdM experience implementing lifesaving humanitarian interventions since 2015, MdM will target 50,424 beneficiaries through provision of multi-disciplinary quality healthcare services for the most vulnerable people affected by the crisis in Eastern Ukraine (Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast, GCA and NGCA). The project will particularly target vulnerable women and girls affected by on-going conflict by ensuring
access to Sexual and Reproductive Health services and access to GBV prevention and response services. The project will also contribute to address the high level of mental health problems among internally displaced persons and host populations in conflict affected areas. 

In order to achieve this objective, MdM will target the most vulnerable communities and categories of people affected by the conflict (such as women and girls, elders, people with disabilities, people exposed to conflict -related stressors): 

- The outreach approach in remote locations of Luhansk and Donetsk oblast close to the line of contact will ensure access to PHC, treatment and referral to specialized care. Outreach teams will promote a
comprehensive approach by providing PHC, MHPSS and SRH services and will be integrated within the existing health facilities (ambulatories /feldshers’points). 

- The local health system will also be supported through targeted donations of supplies and equipment and health staff will be trained (with a specific focus on SRH and MHPSS) to face current lack of capacity building opportunities in conflict-affected Luhansk and Donetsk Oblast. The training plan will be developed in line with the ongoing Health Reform and by creating synergies with public training institutes and/or hospitals. 

- Building up on MdM experience in the area MdM will continue supporting local capacities to provide a comprehensive package of services to survivors of Gender-Based Violence including the most vulnerable populations, and raising awareness on health and mental health consequences of GBV, promoting the development of a sustainable referral pathway. 

- MdM mental health and psychosocial interventions based on evidence-based methodology will be expanded and disseminated to support the needs of persons who deal with psychological problems such as: stress, fear, feelings of helplessness, as well as practical readjustment challenges related to conflicts within families, issues with communities and livelihood difficulties.

MdM advocacy efforts will also continue to ensure the integration of MHPSS into PHC in the framework of the current Health Reform. In NGCA, in so-called Luhansk People Republic, where MdM has been registered since October 2017, MdM will continue to support PHC facilities close to the contact line, which have been particularly affected by the conflict. MdM will pursue with donations of life-saving medical equipment to
Emergency departments of hospitals with focus on Children’s health and Sexual and Reproductive Health. A new project of distribution of maternity and new-born kits initiated in 2019 will be expended.

project_name: Provision of air transport service to support access for humanitarian organizations
project_objective: UNHAS operation serves UN organizations, international NGOs and diplomatic missions operating in Libya. By providing safe, reliable and regular access to those organizations throughout the country, WFP, through UNHAS, supports the achievement of humanitarian and development activities contributing to the stabilization and the pacification process in Libya. The service will aim to maintain an air-transport service to all humanitarian organizations operating across Libya, with focus on main hubs such as Tripoli, Misrata, Benghazi and Sabha, based on operational bottlenecks, humanitarian access and presence, in order to facilitate movements and projects implementation within the country.

project_name: Preventing and responding to child protection concerns of affected boys, girls and their families in Cox's Bazar
project_objective: Save the Children (SC) has operated a large and integrated child protection programme in Cox’s Bazar since the start of the Rohingya influx, aimed at strengthening protective factors and reducing risk factors at every level of the child's environment. With funding through the 2020 JRP, Save the Children, in partnership with 3 local NGOs, will maintain critical interventions and services including case management, family tracing and reunification, alternative care, adolescent and PSS programming, with a focus on protecting the most vulnerable children, including UASC, child headed households, married and house bound girls and children with disabilities. Through maintaining and establishing services in both refugee and communities, critical gaps in service delivery will be addressed, and social cohesion strengthened, by targeting inequity of access to services which is a conflict driver in the current context. To reach the most vulnerable children, project interventions will be delivered through static safe spaces (multi-purpose child and adolescent spaces, adolescent friendly spaces, adolescent clubs) and through improved quality and reach of mobile services.
