project_name: Améliorer notre réponse collective à une crise complexe à travers une coordination efficace, souple et fondée sur les principes humanitaires
project_objective:
L’objectif du projet est de renforcer la coordination de la réponse humanitaire au Cameroun afin de sauver des vies, de protéger les plus vulnérables et d’améliorer la résilience des populations. Avec l’aggravation de la crise dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest, le pays est désormais confronté à trois crises humanitaires complexes qui affectent 8 des 10 régions du Cameroun. L’impact de ces trois crises sur les conditions de vie des populations affectées est renforcé par des vulnérabilités structurelles préexistantes qui entravent leur relèvement.

La complexité et l’étendue de ces crises requièrent donc plus que jamais une coordination efficace, adaptée aux différents terrains d’intervention et fondée sur les principes humanitaires. Le projet de coordination d’OCHA Cameroun permettra ainsi d’atteindre une réponse humanitaire mieux financée, plus stratégique et qui centralise les droits humains et la protection des personnes. Il permettra aussi d’atteindre une meilleure complémentarité entre les actions d’urgence et les programmes de développement, afin de combattre ensemble les besoins humanitaires et leurs causes sous-jacentes.

A cette fin, OCHA fournira les services essentiels de diffusion de produits d'information clés, de coordination du Cycle de Programmation Humanitaire et de facilitation d'évaluations des besoins multisectorielles conjointes. Sa présence à Yaoundé, Maroua, Buea, Bamenda et Kousseri lui permettra d'apporter un appui décisif aux mécanismes de coordination et de favoriser la cohérence entre les enjeux opérationnels terrain et les instances décisionnelles stratégiques. Cette position clé lui permet aussi d'avancer les considérations primordiales de Centralité de la Protection et Protection transversale, de Protection contre l'Exploitation et les Abus Sexuels (PEAS) et de nexus humanitaire développement. Depuis ses sous-bureaux de l'Extrême-Nord et du Sud-Ouest et Nord-Ouest, OCHA favorisera enfin la mise à l'échelle de la réponse dans ces régions, notamment à travers la gestion des responsabilités CMCoord et d'accès humanitaire, ainsi que le renforcement des capacités des répondants locaux.

project_objective:
IOM aims to provide humanitarian Shelter/NFI Assistance to 165,000 newly displaced and protracted IDPs across Somalia. 

The  2020 strategy covers three distinct areas: 

1) Contingency Stock with in-kind NFI kits for 12,500 households (for 75,000 individuals). These kits are available for distribution nationwide by NGO partners where need arises and as endorsed by Shelter cluster.
2) Emergency Shelter & NFI support to newly displaced IDPs in Gedo and Bay Region targeting 13,000 households (78,000 individuals). In total, 8,000HH across the regions will receive NFI and 5,000HH will receive emergency shelter provision. Where assessed appropriate, beneficiaries may receive both emergency shelter and NFI provision.  Interventions will be conducted by the IOM SNFI response teams. Geographical priority will be Gedo and Bay regions given the prevalence of high numbers of newly displaced IDPs affected by conflict, drought and forced eviction in these areas. Additional focus will be given to regions such as Lower Juba and Benadir through use of mobile interventions. The target is to have 70% of the beneficiaries stated in the proposal reached out through cash-based interventions, whenever this is feasible and appropriate. The quality programming of this response will revolve around a solid approach to accountability to affected population by promoting community participation in programme implementation and accountability to inform analysis and future response.
3) Transitional shelter support to 3,000 households (18,000 individuals) in Bay region. Improving the durability of IDP shelters to those who already having received basic emergency shelter provision. Shelter responses will be subject to needs assessment, however, will target 3,000HH (18,000 individuals) in Baidoa.

project_name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018-2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

Through cash and voucher assistance, the project will provide economic support to 15,000 households from host communities, allowing them to purchase productive inputs and assets contributing to sustainable and resilient livelihoods. Empowering the parents and caregivers of the children, the project will strengthen the protective factors at all levels of the child’s environment in order to reinforce the child’s resilience and prevent and respond to threats to the wellbeing of children. The project will improve the sustainable livelihoods and self-reliance opportunities for the host communities in Ukhia and Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, through providing soft skills, vocational skills, job linkages support, entrepreneurship development, assets and cash transfer support. project_name: Scaling up primary health care services in conflict effected areas of Libya
project_objective:
In all countries, PHC services are the backbone of preventive, promotive and curative health care. In Libya, strengthening PHC services is a priority. Current efforts to respond only to humanitarian health needs are yielding sub-optimal results because the health care system is weak and fragmented. Many of the leading causes of mortality and morbidity in Libya could be prevented or treated through a high-quality, people-centered health care system that pivots around PHC. According to international standards, three family physicians are required per 10 000 people. Currently, there are only 47 family physicians in Libya, almost all of whom are working in the private sector. 

In December 2017, WHO began implementing a two-year project to improve access to PHC services in all regions of the country. The project, developed in collaboration with the Libyan Ministry of Health (MOH) and the United Kingdom’s Department for International Development (DfID) aims to build the capacity of PHC service providers and managers and thereby improve people’s access to quality PHC services. Three interventions were designed to build the managerial, service delivery and community-care capacities of the MOH. Six PHC centers (two each in south, west and east Libya) were selected to implement the project. In line with WHO’s Regional Framework for Action on Advancing Family Medicine, a comprehensive family medicine model was introduced in each center. A total of 716 health professionals (63% female and 37% male) were trained on the 13 core elements of introducing family practice into PHC. This training allowed each center to respond more effectively to the routine and humanitarian health care needs of host populations and internally displaced people (IDPs). WHO procured essential medicines and supplies and distributed them to all six centers. In parallel, WHO worked with the MOH to strengthen central and regional planning and management. Links were forged between the centers and the communities they served through a network of trained facilitators and volunteers who played an instrumental role in promoting the importance of integrated health care services within their communities. 

Building on the accomplishments of the mentioned interventions and in line with the basic premise of humanitarian and development (H&D) nexus, the proposed project aims to strengthen MoH capacity at both developmental and humanitarian fronts involving strategic interventions at national and sub-national level through the following measures. The project will target 60 PHC facilities, (20 in each of the West, South and East region) across Libya. The selection of PHC facilities will be based on the findings of the recent assessment which was conducted by WHO in preparation for HRP 2020

project_name: Responding to immediate food security and nutrition needs
project_objective:
The March 2020 Cadre Harmonisé highlights a serious deterioration in the food security and nutrition situation in Mali. Needs have increased by 29 percent compared to the same period in 2019 and by 32% comparing the 2019 to the 2020 lean season, the period of the year when food stocks exhausted and resources the most stretched. Currently, 3.6 million men, women, boys and girls are estimated to be food insecure, including 760,000 of them experiencing severe food insecurity (IPC phase 3 to 5). The situation is expected to deteriorate during the 2020 lean season with nearly 5.0 million food insecure men, women, boys and girls including close to 1.4 million severely food insecure persons (IPC 3 to 5). The most affected regions are Mopti (41% of the needs) and Gao/Ménaka (18% of the needs). The Sahelian belt is also affected, especially Kayes region with 15% of the needs as well as Koulikoro region (12% of the needs). 
With a global acute malnutrition prevalence of 10% (SMART results, September 2019), the nutritional situation in the country remains worrying due to, among other issues, poor food practices, food deficit, civil insecurity which limits access to basic social services and the prevalence of diseases linked to poor hygiene conditions.
This alarming food security situation will deteriorate further due to the effects of the COVID-19 epidemic in Mali. 
The latest analyzes of the country's food security situation show a deterioration of the food security and household livelihoods .

Considering the deterioration of income, especially in urban areas, and inflation on imported products; WFP (VAM, regional office) estimates that the number of people in severe food insecurity in Mali could raised up to a range of 2.2 million and 2.7 million: meaning an increase between 0.8 to 1.4 million more people than the Cadre Harmonisé forecasts for the lean season period (June-August 2020). As part of the mid-term review of the humanitarian funding call, the Food Security Cluster (which brings together all the Food Security actors) estimated at 2.4 million the number of people that are now in severe food insecurity, that is 1 million more than the last figures of the March 2020 Cadre Harmonisé. 

In support to the Government and in coordination with other humanitarian actors, WFP will provide food assistance to the most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls in areas identified by ENSAN and the Harmonized Framework as the most affected by food and nutrition insecurity. This assistance will be provided through cash-based transfer (cash or vouchers) and or food distribution depending on the cost-efficiency analysis and operational feasibility. WFP will promote women's participation in this process and in all other discussions related to this assistance so that their specific vulnerabilities and protection requirements are considered. WFP will also continue to provide technical assistance to the Government institutions (CSA, SAP, MSAH, Jigisemejiri) for food security analysis and monitoring, and food security and nutrition assistance.

WFP seeks to involve affected populations, including men, women, boys and girls, in all steps of the programme design, implementation and evaluation. To do so, WFP focuses on three key areas: first, information provision to affected men, women, boys and girls, in a timely and accessible manner. This includes information provision about their rights to provide feedback and be consulted. Second, consultations to seek and include the views of all segments of the affected men, women, boys and girls, including through focus group discussions. Third, through complaint and feedback mechanisms (CFM), that includes, but is not limited to a toll-free number and complaint committees which include women and men, young and old people. These tools are regularly reassessed in consultations with the affected populations, to ensure they are inclusive and relevant.

project_name: Réponse rapide en santé et nutrition auprès des populations affectées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad dans la région de Diffa, au Niger
project_objective:
Pour répondre aux besoins urgents identifiés ci-dessus, Action Contre la Faim propose une approche fondée sur un mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) pour assurer l'accès aux services de santé et de nutrition auprès des populations affectées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad dans la région de Diffa, au Niger. Cette réponse viendra compléter et intégrer les interventions actuelles des autres mécanismes de RRM en cours par d’autres acteurs RRM dans la région de Diffa.
Le mécanisme proposé sera basé sur un système de surveillance et d'alerte construit sur des réseaux communautaires et les informations régulières recueillies directement auprès des centres de santé. Les structures sanitaires ciblées seront appuyées pour intégrer une surveillance de qualité des maladies à potentiel épidémique. Cet aspect sera assuré par l’amélioration des bases de données et métadonnées et de la promptitude de remontée des données épidémiques au Ministère de la Santé Publique. L’approche CMAM SURGE sera mise en place au niveau des structures de santé affectées afin de répondre aux pics de malnutrition.   
Selon la nature de l'alerte, une évaluation rapide sera réalisée pour identifier la nature des obstacles à l'accès local aux services de santé et une réponse appropriée. Les évaluations rapides se feront selon les modalités d’évaluation mises en œuvre dans le RRM et seront couplées dans la mesure du possible à celle d’autres secteurs dans les Zones affectées. Lors de l’évaluation, Action Contre la Faim fournira déjà dans la mesure du possible une première réponse en santé et nutrition avant la réponse multisectorielle conduite après l’analyse des besoins. 
Le paquet minimum d’activités Santé nutrition du RRM reposera sur deux principales modalités de réponse (flexibles) : 
- L’implantation des Cliniques mobiles : des équipes mobiles capables de fournir le soutien nécessaire aux structures de santé affectées et / ou si nécessaire directement aux communautés par le biais de services mobiles équipes. La stratégie mobile sera composée de soins curatifs gratuits pour toute la population (soins de santé primaires, santé de la reproduction, prise en charge de la MAS), des soins préventifs (vaccination, CPN). L’appui psychosocial à base communautaire sera également intégré à la clinique de concert avec l’ONG COOPI qui a déjà de programme de santé mentale dans la région de Diffa ; 
- L’appui Institutionnel Temporaire : qui est déployé pour les structures sanitaires existantes (case de santé, CSI, HD) dans les cas où les personnes déplacées sont localisées non loin de la structure de santé (moins de 5 km de marche) ou la structures de santé n’a pas une capacité de prise en charge suffisante des patients ou encore la structure est bien fréquentée par les personnes déplacées. 
Le paquet santé du RRM va couvrir en priorité les 5 districts sanitaires de la région de Diffa (Diffa, Bosso, Maine-Soroa, Ngourti Et N’guigmi) pour les mouvements de populations et épidémie mais éventuellement le DS de Goudoumaria en cas d’épidémie. 
Un stock d'urgence de médicaments et d'intrants nutritionnels pré-positionnés et gérés par Action Contre la Faim pour la réponse médico-nutritionnelle d’urgence. Action Contre la Faim va également assurer l’évacuation des patients graves et avec des complications vers les structures de santé de la zone d’intervention de concert avec les autorités sanitaires locales

project_name: Strengthening life-saving healthcare services, scale-up interventions to Malarai and other vector and water bourne disease, strengthen the coordination of the health sector.
project_objective:
The Health sector response to recent floods in Djibouti aims to mitigate excess mortality and morbidity through ensuring equitable access to life-saving preventive and curative health services and interventions for the floods affected populations in Djibouti reaching the 25,000 families in 19 districts of the city through the following: (i) strengthening the technical capacities of the health workforce in line with the national standards and protocols through refresher trainings for healthcare workers focused on priority Primary Healthcare areas. As well, the health map of the country will be updated to better locate areas in need of outreach and/or mobile clinic support to improve the accountability of health facilities towards the populations they serve. 
(ii) The health sector including WHO and other partners will establish outreach and rapid response teams, 5 teams will be established in collaboration with the ministry of health.  
(iii) The Health sector will provide in-facility support to ensure appropriate case detection and treatment of malnutrition among children and prevent and monitor deterioration in children’s nutritional status. The Management of the medical complications associated with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) will be expanded; also, technical and operational support for mainstreaming Mental health and psychosocial support.
(iv) strengthen the early detection, investigation and control of waterborne, vector borne, epidemic-prone and vaccine preventable diseases, extending the coverage of the Early Warning Alert and Response Network (EWARN) to ensure countrywide timely detection, investigation and response to epidemic-prone diseases.
(v). onducting refresher training sessions on the case management of Malaria cases; procuring Rapid Diagnostic Tests, reagents for microscopy, anti-malarials and antipyretics Malaria treatment; procuring Long Lasting Insecticide Treated Bed Nets (LLINs); extending the Indoor Residual Spraying to an additional 20,000 households in highly endemic areas and flood affected neighborhoods (6000 households have already been sprayed); organizing chemical and physical destruction of anopheles’ breeding sites; and conducting a Risk communication campaign focused on sensitizing communities on the use of LLINs, the destruction of peri-domestic breeding sites and on better health seeking behavior. 
(vi) The Health sector will scale up the prevention and response to Dengue and Chikungunya through: strengthening epidemiological surveillance; organizing refresher training on the diagnostic and case management of arboviruses; procuring Diagnostic Tests for Dengue and Chikungunya (PCR Reagents); organizing Spatial Spraying in highly endemic areas and flood affected neighborhoods to reduce vector populations; chemical and physical destruction of Aedes’ breeding sites; and conducting a Risk communication campaign focused on community sensitization on how to prevent and control the arboviruses. 
response measures to Waterborne diseases will be scaled up through: ensuring water quality control and monitoring at all levels; strengthening epidemiological surveillance focused on diarrheal diseases and other waterborne diseases; and procurement of medicines and equipment to respond to the eventual increase in diarrhea cases. Finally, the Health sector will conduct a nationwide measles immunization and vitamin A supplementation campaign and it is mandatory to extend the planned campaign for mid-December, which is targeting 6 years to 15 years of age, to include all children in Djibouti age 6 months to 15 years of age.
(vii) Strengthen Coordination of the health sector

Special emphasis will be put on strengthening joint inter-agency coordination, M&E, capacity building, assessment and partnership that will translate to better outcome.

project_name: Prevention and Management of Acute Malnutrition in Vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities in Ayod, Kapoeta East & Yirol West counties (Jonglei, Eastern Equitoria & Lakes states).
project_objective:
CMD plans to implement minimum package of Integrating Out Patient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) within existing health facilities by providing routine treatment using simple medical protocol to SAM without medical complications. This project plans to integrate Health, WASH and FSL into Nutrition targeting the 9 OTP sites and 2 SC’s within Northern and Southern Ayod (Including Pagil, Menime, Normanyang, Kandak, Mogok, Jiech, Gorwai, Padek, Haat, and Kharmun) where CMD has existing health facilities while supporting Pagil and Gorwai SCs to treat  SAM children with medical complications. In Yirol West, CMD will support 6 OTPs in Malek, Tinagau, Adior, Lekakedu, Yali and Pagarau payams and 1 SC in Adior while in Kapoeta East, activities will be integrated within the ongoing Health response to support 6 OTP sites (Narus,Kauto, Katadori, Lotimo, Mogos, Nating) and 1 SC in Mogos . 3,054 SAM, 9,419 MAM and 6,540 PLW’s (Ayod-SAM 1,002, MAM-4,629 PLW-1,966), (Yirol West-SAM 760, MAM 2,573, PLW 1,407) and (Kapoeta East- SAM 1,292, MAM 2,217, PLW 3,167) are planned. 

The project plans to work in collaboration with MoH/CHD, partners and local authorities through supporting initiatives for the decentralisation of OTP and SC sites, increasing awareness through community mobilisation on: IYCF/MIYCN Practices for prevention of Malnutrition, socio-mobilisation for vitamin A supplementation, deworming and advocacy for the proper use of LLITN. 

With UNICEF and WFP collaboration, complemented support will enable CMD provide targeted emergency nutrition supplies and services to a SAM caseload of up to 3,054 (Including children with complicated severe acute cases) in need (< 5 years both boys and girls) and MAM caseload of up to 9,419 (<5 years) and PLW’s caseload of 6,540. CMD will train Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) and Mother-to-Mother support groups from host community to acquire skills and knowledge on Integrated Management of SAM and Maternal Infant and young child feeding practices so as to provide quality nutrition services. Health staff and Nutrition staffs will be capacitated for integration of SAM and MAM management into health programmes especially on malaria screening and referral of severe cases to OTP and Stabilisation centres. 

If the current drivers of food insecurity worsen through the end of 2019, and in the absence of humanitarian assistance, there is a heightened risk of emergency as large populations are already experiencing severe food insecurity.

project_name: Protection and legal assistance for persons in hard to reach and conflict-affected areas in South Sudan
project_objective:
NRC seeks to improve the overall protective environment in South Sudan by not only responding to people’s most acute material needs during a crisis, but also by promoting their safety and dignity and to prevent, reduce or mitigate the protection risks they face. It is also to address the underlying causes of displacement and to contribute to creating conditions conducive to durable solutions for displaced populations. To this end, NRC proposes a graduated approach to support the protection of displaced and conflict-affected populations, including static, mobile, and emergency responses. 

The project will offer the following services:
•	Protection context assessments in all locations and, where possible, community-based protection monitoring, in which community focal points will be trained to report on protection needs and risks. Protection incidents will be documented and analysed to understand trends and evolution in the protection context, and results disseminated to communities and relevant stakeholders.
•	Provision of individual protection assistance (IPA), to persons with urgent protection needs. 
•	Creation of community-driven protection (CDP) mechanisms in hard to reach, underserved areas through mobile, emergency response teams. NRC teams will work with communities to establish a series of local committees, including marginalized groups, through careful selection of representatives to ensure effectiveness and inclusiveness. CDP teams will mobilise community volunteers and solidarity networks to implement community protection initiatives and actions plans.
•	Facilitate improved access to legal identity documentation, including nationality certificates for displacement affected persons who cannot access basic rights and services, especially school-aged children who have challenges applying for state exams. NRC will provide both awareness raising sessions to at-risk populations and individualised assistance in accessing national identity documentation. 
•	Foster improved ability to exercise HLP rights for individuals and groups affected by displacement with priority given to the most vulnerable, including female and child-headed households, the elderly, individuals with physical and mental disabilities, and those who are extremely poor. NRC will target conflict-affected areas and areas of potential return.  NRC will provide awareness raising sessions to communities, as well as offer tailored individual counselling to vulnerable persons requiring further support including cash assistance to access legal services and representation in court.
•	Enable peaceful coexistence and support inclusive resolutions of local conflict through training and mentoring in collaborative dispute resolution (CDR) mechanisms. CDR trainings will target chiefs, youth groups, older people, opinion leaders, customary authorities, local government authorities, and include members of host, returnee, and IDP communities. NRC will ensure that women are well-represented. Trainings will be complimented with monitoring and mentoring, and support to see inclusive solutions realized. 

NRC is in the process of building up this suite of protection interventions, and will focus on piloting projects in selected locations, with the intention to ultimately offer all protection services in all areas of existing static implementation. All services will be offered in Jonglei (specifically Bor and Duk), as well as in Kajo Keji. NRC will focus on expanding community based protection responses in Unity (Mayom).However, NRC will focus exclusively on HLP response in Northern and Western Bahr el Ghazal.  In areas subject to recurrent support from mobile teams a narrower version of the project will be offered, based on local needs and prioritisation and other services available. Emergency responses will focus on protection needs assessments, awareness raising and information, and provision of IPA.

project_name: Unconditional food assistance to food-insecure households affected by shocks
project_objective:
The emergency response, which began in November 2019, is expected to unfold until the end of 2020, taking into account increased lean season needs exacerbated by the current crisis as well as the time needed for WFP to progressively include beneficiaries in new areas and scale up distributions. As such, during this response, a total of 700,000 beneficiaries will receive four months of general food assistance (in-king, cash or a combination of the two) in line with a gradual geographic expansion of WFP’s assistance. 
Acknowledging the country-wide deterioration of the food security situation, WFP’s emergency assistance will be geared towards IPC Phase 4 households across the country, ensuring the overall humanitarian response meets the acute food security needs and stops any further decline in people’s food security status. WFP will adopt a particular focus on areas with a higher proportion of people in IPC phase 4 (roughly 20%) and comparatively lower partner capacity, while promoting complementarities with other actors, including UNICEF and FAO, to ensure the provision of a comprehensive package.
WFP will target 700,000 of the most food insecure people, in line with the HNO, corresponding to approximately 70% of the population classified in IPC Phase 4. A specific focus will be given to vulnerable households with pregnant and lactating women and girls, children under 5 years, elders and people living with disabilities. Complementary regular programming (school feeding, resilience – not within the scope of this Con Ops) will be maintained to support other populations in need, such as IPC Phase 3. These numbers are to be revisited along updated IPC projections.

project_name: Restoration of basic WASH services to ensure equitable and sustainable access to Water and Sanitation in Syria.
project_objective:
Sustainable water and sanitation systems are maintained and/or restored to improve public health and sustain livelihoods. The project aims to increase the resilience of the Syrian population by building the resilience of WASH services and the mitigation the further degradation of WASH basic services in the most vulnerable communities in 14th Governorates including the North East and West of Syria.  Prior to the conflict, almost 100% of the population in Syria was served by well-developed, state-owned and centrally managed water systems. However, after nine years of conflict, access to safe water and sanitation has deteriorated significantly, with only a small minority having access to safe drinking water and full sanitation services. As a result, people in Syria have turned to negative coping mechanisms, such as procuring water from unregulated water operators, who often have a poor quality of water and increase the risk of contamination. Overall, up to 55% of households are relying on alternate and unsafe water sources to meet or complement their water needs. 

The lack of electricity constitutes one of the main bottlenecks for the WASH sector, as it limits the existing water network from being able to effectively distribute existing quantities. As such, the economic and social consequences of the conflict can be summarized as a challenging combination of larger regional challenges which have been compounded by the prolonged conflict: 

•	The Syrian economy became increasingly vulnerable to water scarcity in the decades preceding the conflict. The combination of drought, poor governance, and highly inefficient flood irrigation, combined with that around half of the irrigation water comes from groundwater pumping, has led to a situation of rising production costs as well as depleting groundwater tables.
•	Water shortages were common before the conflict. Potable water coverage was almost universal prior to the conflict; however, most regions suffered from shortages, particularly during the summer when supply was rationed to only for a few hours a day.
•	The conflict has significantly deepened the problems in access to water. Large scale destruction and disruption of water and sanitation systems have further reduced coverage.
•	Water shortages have prompted various coping mechanisms. Syrians have reverted to alternative mechanisms to restore water access, especially during long episodes of public water network outages, such as private wells and water trucking.

project_name: Improving access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and hygiene practices for out of camp refugees, IDP, Host Communities and returnees in Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone et Chari Division, Far North Region/Cameroon
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to improve access to safe drinking water, adequate sanitation and hygiene practices for refugees, IDP, Host communities, Returnees in Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari divisions in Far North region of Cameroon. Indeed, since 2014, these populations have been victims of the Boko Haram crisis in Nigeria, which forced them to move to villages borders in Cameroon. This situation has a direct impact on the satisfaction of basic needs, as presented by several surveys and assessments carried out both by the Cameroonian government and the international agencies and organizations (IOM, UNICEF, UNHCR, NRC,..). the project will be implemented both in the community and in schools.
In the communities where refugees live, we will construct and/or rehabilitate water points in accordance with SPHERE standards and national standards. Each water point will be staffed by a management committee (WMC) that will be trained and equipped with tools for the sustainability of the boreholes. Aware that the drudgery of water is usually done by women and children, each WMC will be composed of at least 50% women. For drilling for more than 2 years ago, NRC will monitor water quality through physical and bacteriological analysis. Households will also be trained on home water treatment and will receive potabilization kits. In each locality, two hygiene promoters (one man and one woman) will be identified and trained on community hygiene promotion. Through home visits, they will raise awareness on good hygiene and sanitation practices. As a result of participatory profiling vulnerable households will benefit from hygiene kits (bucket, soap, ...) while women and girls on reproductive age will receive menstrual hygiene kits consisting of washable sanitary towels, buckets and soap. These will first be trained on the use and maintenance of the kits.
In schools, in addition to the construction and rehabilitation of water points, NRC will build gender-sensitive school latrines equipped with hand washing equipment and maintenance equipment. Under the supervision of teachers, school hygiene club (SHC) made up of 50% of girls will be set up and trained on hygiene promotion in schools. These SHC will develop action plans that will be supported by the project.
Ultimately, the project aims to reach about 27,280 beneficiaries (i.e. 51% women). Approximately 16,891 children under the age of 18 will benefit from the project's actions, compared to 819 elderly (more than 59 years old).

project_name: Improving living condition, promotion of rights and physical safety to promote dignity and protection of out of camp refugees, returnees, displaced people and hosts communities of the Far North Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to Improving living condition, promotion of rights and physical safety to promote dignity and protection of returnees, displaced people and hosts communities in Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Chari divisions in Far North region of Cameroon. Indeed, since 2014, these populations have been victims of the Boko Haram crisis, which has a direct impact on the satisfaction of basic needs, including NFI and Shelter as presented by several surveys and assessments carried out both by the Cameroonian government and the international agencies and organizations (IOM, UNICEF, NRC,..). the project will be implemented both in the community and in schools.
The project will provide NFIs and emergency shelter kits for the construction of transitional shelters. The Shelter kit will be mainly composed on tarpaulin and ropes while bucket, soap, mosquito nets, mats, etc…). a total of 3,000 households (with 51% of women head of households) will benefit from the assistance. The distribution will be carried out in synergy with WASH hygiene kit distributions in order to provide a comprehensive WASH/shelter/NFI kit to beneficiaries. NRC will also support with construction materials the rehabilitation of permanent shelters when displaced populations return to their places of origin or integrate into host communities. A total of 300 shelters are planned, each shelter will also have benefited for one family latrine.
NRC will provide CVA for NFI in Logone and Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga. The aim will be to allow beneficiaries to purchase relevant items needed for their households near of their location. Before CVA implementation, a survey will be done to design the qualifying process, the modality and utilization by beneficiaries.
In the event of a sudden and massive arrival of the displaced, the project will also distribute the NFI and shelter kits
In schools, the project will rehabilitate classrooms and make gender-sensitive benches.
Ultimately, the project aims to reach about 23,100 beneficiaries (i.e. 51% women). IDPs will account for 50% of the target while the host community and returns will be 20% each and out of camp refugees 10%. Approximately 14,322‬ children under the age of 18 will benefit from the project's actions, compared to 692 elderlies (more than 59 years old).

project_name: Food Security and livelihoods support for vulnerable populations in South Sudan
project_objective: The project aims to provide life-saving and recovery food security and livelihoods support to women, men girls and boys affected by displacement in South Sudan. The intervention will contribute to life-saving and livelihoods protection efforts for internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and host communities in order to enable them meet their basic food and other household needs, while protecting their assets and livelihoods and resilience to shocks and stresses.  Target groups will include the most vulnerable households in locations that were projected by the integrated food security and nutrition phase classification (IPC) of August 2019 to be in phase 4 (emergency) and 5 (catastrophe). A highlight for 2020 will be the default preference for using cash programming unless where it has been deemed not feasible. This decision will contribute towards revitalization of local markets as they play a very important role in building livelihoods to areas affected by displacement. With the emergency of new companies offering cash transfer services in South Sudan (e.g. MGurush and NilePay), NRC will engage with them to provide opportunities of using their services to improve cash transfer for both safety nets and livelihoods activities.  With the recorded reduction in conflicts across the country in 2019 NRC will continue setting up static field offices in areas of high humanitarian need which used to be saved by rapid response mobile teams, while keeping the rapid response capacity in areas that still have access challenges.  With its static presence in Jonglei, Unity, Twic, northern Bahr El Ghazal and Western Bahr El Ghazal, the intervention will provide both life saving food security, emergency and recovery livelihoods support improving food production and income generation for target groups.  Community consultations using assessments and community based participatory planning will be used to enable communities identify and prioritize their needs and response strategies and their decisions regarding targeting will be sought in order for the project to reach the most vulnerable groups.  Women and youth will be specifically targeted as they make up some of the most vulnerable groups that have great potential to change their situation around and help in bringing peace to their communities.  The intervention will ensure good understanding of the gender and power dynamics in the target communities with the aim of avoiding doing harm or perpetuating the imbalances.  Gender and age dis-aggregated information will be collected in preparation for, during implementation of activities and monitoring and evaluation of the activities.  This information will be used in designing and implementation of activities in order to provide equitable and relevant support to the different target groups.  The intervention will incorporate safe programming principles in order to protect the target groups and communities from protection concerns that are related to implementation of the activities in conflict situations.  This will include a good understanding of the protection risks related to the intervention and identifying the mitigation measures that should be part of the intervention.  These will  be monitored throughout the implementation phase. Efforts towards integrated approach both targeting same communities and target groups with a variety of food security and livelihoods interventions and with other sectors will be done to strengthen the holistic approach and enhance household and community capacities to anticipate, cope, adapt and recover from effects of conflict and environmental shocks.

project_name: Shelter and NFI response in North - East Nigeria
project_objective:
Under this project IOM will scale-up its provision of shelter assistance targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. To this end, IOM will: (A) ensure access to different types of emergency shelter solutions for displaced populations through the distribution and prepositioning of emergency shelter kits, construction of emergency shelters, rehabilitation of damaged public buildings, etc.; (B) ensure that displaced populations have access to different transitional shelter solutions; (C) ensure that the care, maintenance and upgrading of existing emergency shelters and transitional shelters are conducted for continued safety and comfort of the affected population; (D) ensure that returnee households have access to materials and labour for repairing their damaged houses; and (E) support local construction market through business grants and training for construction traders, as well as through the use of cash and voucher mechanisms. 
IOM’s shelter activities will be implemented in three States of North East Nigeria; Borno (12 LGAs), Adamawa (9 LGAs) and Yobe State (3 LGAs), targeting 229,000 individuals. 
IOM ensures that all shelter activities taken are accountable to the affected population and that the gender-specific needs of project beneficiaries are integrated. Kits and other shelter solutions are harmonized at sector level and coordinated with partners.
The project will also include the continuation and scaling-up of Non-Food Items (NFI) support for people in camp and camp-like settings, in host communities, including for new arrivals. IOM plans to guarantee the participation of Women, Men, Girls and Boys as equals to ensure that the special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and different age groups, and address women's, girls' and boys’ specific needs, especially in terms of protection and access concerns. To illustrate, (1) the content of NFI kits will be tailored in accordance to the needs of different age and gender groups (2) All activities related to this project will equally target the different age and gender groups and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. Regarding assessment, monitoring and evaluation of gender specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels with them where possible, and all activities will be conducted based on Do No Harm principles.

project_name: Reinforcing sustainable WASH response to affected population in Lac Chad Basin of Cameroon
project_objective:
This project aims to strengthen water, sanitation and hygiene response to affected population in Far North region of Cameroon with a focus on IDP camp, communities hosting IDP and returnees. In water domain, construction of small water supply network powered with solar energy will be prioritized. On hygiene and sanitation issues, communities approached for total sanitation will be implemented at municipality level. Construction of community latrines and showers will be limited to IDP sites. The area targeted cover the division of Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari. About 60 000 people will be targeted along these interventions. The main deliverables 
•	10 000 household benefited of WASH kits
•	3 000 women and girls benefited of MHM kits
•	30 Water points constructed
•     40 water point rehabilitated in communities hosting IDP or affected by cholera
•	5 Small scale water supply networks constructed
•	3000 women and girls received menstrual hygiene management kits
•	50% of SAM children who received a WASH kits with key hygiene message in targeted area
rehabilitation of 50 water point in communities affected by cholera in North

This project will also include a component relative to capacity building of WASH actor at regional level on key issues such as design, installation and maintenance of solar system for water supply, cholera response, protection and gender mainstreaming in WASH sector.

project_name: Provision of life saving integrated Gender Based Violence services to vulnerable IDP and host communities in the North West and South West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
In order to respond to needs of women and girls and provide appropriate  response, the funds will help set up a robust humanitarian team in the South West and North West of Cameroon. 
Low capacity of local actors in the two regions continues to hamper efforts to deliver timely and quality GBV/SRH services. 
To address the key service gaps, UNFPA will Support the setting up of “safe spaces” for PSS, case management, social cohesion and life-skills for affected women and adolescent girls. Adolescent friendly spaces will be established at high density displacement areas to address the SRH/GBV service needs of adolescents. Working with local networks and service providers, 3 mobile clinics will be supported to address the needs of women of reproductive age especially pregnant women in areas with severe access constraints. Tents for service provision will be procured to support rapid response to emerging service delivery needs in the two regions. 
Some indications about the calculations of the number of SRH kits requested. 
First, we will require individual delivery kits to be distributed to about 10,000 pregnant women with no access to health facility delivery in the NW and SW. 
Second, about 60 birth attendants in these areas will be given Kit 2B (Midwives and other providers within the displaced communities). 
Third, an extra 15 facilities will need to be provided with rape kits. 
Fourth, the block 2 kits will be used to support activities in the mobile clinics and select fixed clinics. 
Last but not least, three functional hospitals have been targeted for support with Kits 11A, 11B and 12.

project_name: Amélioration de la santé sexuelle et reproductive, y compris la prévention et la prise en charge des VBG chez les adolescentes et jeunes femmes IDPs de la crise anglophone dans les Régions du Littoral et de l’Ouest
project_objective:
Le nombre total de PDI lié à la crise du NWSW s'élève à plus de 700 000, y compris les personnes déplacées en tant que réfugiés au Nigéria ainsi que dans d'autres régions du Cameroun. La situation humanitaire dans le Nord-Ouest et le Sud-Ouest (NWSW) reste intrinsèquement liée à la crise politique, à la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire et au niveau élevé des incidents de protection qui en résulte. Les déplacements continuent d'augmenter, ce qui entraîne une augmentation inquiétante des besoins humanitaires. Plus de 536 107 personnes déplacées sont enregistrées dans quatre régions (Nord-Ouest, Sud-Ouest et Littoral et Ouest voisines); 237 349 retournés sont enregistrés. La situation est caractérisée par des violations des droits de l'homme, y compris les droits sexuels et de la santé reproductive et les violences basées sur le genre (VBG), en particulier les violences sexuelles. Du fait de l’oisiveté, de l’ennui et du stress, des structures familiales déstabilisées, de la séparation et de l’abandon, cette tranche, traditionnellement oubliée lors des crises humanitaires, est confrontée aux risques et fléaux divers. De nombreux adolescents, y compris les plus jeunes, ont recours à la prostitution pour répondre à leurs propres besoins ou aux besoins de leurs familles. Ce qui accroît leur vulnérabilité à l’infection par le VIH/IST et aux grossesses précoces et/ou non désirées en raison de leur forte mobilité et d’une augmentation de la prise de risques (y compris la prise d’alcool et de drogues), aux avortements clandestins.  Les deux sexes sont exposés par ailleurs à la violence y compris sexuelle, à l’exploitation et aux abus sexuels, aux mariages précoces, au sexe transactionnel, etc…
Ainsi abandonnés à eux-mêmes, sans repères et étant parfois obligés de jouer le rôle de chefs de famille, ces divers types d’activités illicites auxquels ils se livrent les rendent encore plus vulnérables, exposent leurs vies et les enfoncent dans le cycle de pauvreté. 
Par ailleurs, du fait des tabous, de la honte, de l’ignorance, des pesanteurs socioculturelles, de la stigmatisation ou de l’influence négative des pairs, de la faible disponibilité des services adaptés, des difficultés liées à l’accessibilité financière, beaucoup d’adolescents et jeunes ne recourent pas systématiquement aux services de santé en cas de problèmes, y compris pour l’accouchement.
Ce projet vise à apporter une réponse adaptée aux besoins spécifiques des adolescents et jeunes en général et des adolescentes et jeunes femmes en particulier en matière de santé sexuelle et reproductive, y compris de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG dans les Régions du Littoral et de l’Ouest

project_name: Provision of Protection Assistance (Emergency Shelter and Basic Domestic Items) to Internally Displaced Persons in the Northwest and Southwest Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
This Project will provide protection assistance in emergency/transition shelters and basic domestic items to internally displaced persons in the North West and Southwest Regions of Cameroon. The project ensure the most vulnerable displaced population and host families are reached with timely, appropriate life-sustaining emergency shelter support, the most vulnerable displaced population and host families are reached with timely, appropriate life-sustaining emergency shelter support, the most vulnerable displaced population are reached with rental subsidies and the most vulnerable displaced population and host families are reached with timely, appropriate life-sustaining with NFIs support					

Specifically the project will 

1) Meet basic needs and essential services, providing populations with basic domestic items. In this case the project will move from a baseline of 20% of persons in need to 33% of households whose needs for basic and domestic items are met. The project target 12,000 households to be provided with core relief items. 30% of these households will be provided with cash assistance in form of Voucher for NFIs. This represents 3600 household out of the 12,000.  A Cash Feasibility study carried out by UNHCR revealed that Vendors of NFIs are familiar with Vouchers, considering that other partners like IRC have implemented Vouchers for NFI and Wash sectors successfully. UNHCR will therefore follow this method and Implement it Via Direct Implementation as a compliment to other shelter/NFI activities by our Implementation partners. 

2)  Shelter and infrastructure established, improved and maintained . This target reaching 10,000 households with a variety of shelter assistance including emergency shelter kits, rental subsidies and assistance in shelter materials for construction. Rental Subsidies will be provided to Urban IDPs via Cash transfer. UNHCR Cameroon is already in a contractual agreement with MTN Mobile Money, to facilitate cash based assistance. A feasibility studies to assist IDPs in Cash was conducted in November 2019 lead by a UNHCR cash based intervention Officer and a Multi-Functional team. The objectives were to access the feasibility of Vouchers, Cash transfers and Cash in envelop to support victims of SGBV and internally displace persons in need of Shelter and NFI . A market analysis suggested that vendors and suppliers of NFI items were more comfortable with vouchers as many have had previous experience with other projects within the Context of the Crisis. On the other hand, Cash transfers were found to be more suitable for rents assistance for urban IDPs.

project_name: Emergency assistance to conflict-affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon: Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
project_objective:
Maintain and strengthen the system of data collection in the Far North region of
Cameroon through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the
coordination of humanitarian activities. The DTM aims to provide reliable and up-to-date information on the numbers, locations of displaced populations, displacement trends and
reasons for displacement to better inform humanitarian response. The assessed groups consist of internally displaced persons, out-of-camp refugees and returnees. The data will be disaggregated by
age and sex. The DTM has the potential to be expanded and/or modified to take into account changes in the regional context.

project_name: Direct and rapid humanitarian response for affected displaced populations of the North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon: shelter / NFI assistance
project_objective: The proposed action aims at providing tailored Shelter and/or Non-Food Items (NFI) assistance to the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations identified through needs assessments. The modality of intervention and vulnerability criteria will be in line with the NFI/Shelter Cluster guidelines and standards.

project_name: Unconditional food assistance to 250,000 Internally Displaced People (IDPs), local population in the North-West and South-West Regions
project_objective:
The Project aims to provide immediate unconditional 12-month in kind food assistance to the most vulnerable IDPs and local populations affected by crisis in the North-West and South-West. The number of people hiding in bushes is hard to identify or access without signiﬁcant risk. In the absence of a formal platform for beneﬁciary registration and selection, WFP is implementing a beneﬁciary selection tool to enhance the household targeting of food assistance activities in the South West and North West regions. The process involves coordination with other partners and communities to identify and select beneﬁciary households based on the following vulnerability criteria: Household demographic status; Household dependency ratio; Displacement status of households; Accommodation status of the household; Access to income.
Local support committees established at community level prepare lists of beneﬁciaries respecting the vulnerability criteria. The beneﬁciaries interviewed, and information veriﬁed WFP plans to meet the immediate food and nutritional needs of the population affected by the crisis through unconditional food assistance and enhance the capacity of our partners. 
In line with the results of the Multisector Initial Rapid Assessment (MIRA), Emergency Food and Security Assessment, and the Cadre Harmonise. WFP will provide food support to 250,000 targeted people affected by the crisis in the South West and North West regions. To save lives and protect the food security and nutrition status these vulnerable people, WFP will provide immediate humanitarian food assistance to the targeted 250,000 IDPs and local vulnerable host populations (180,000 in the NW and 80,000 in the SW) in their various locations in urban, semi urban and bushes. The modality of assistance will be in-kind general food distributions. Special attention will be paid to beneﬁciaries located in rural areas and diﬃcult to access settlements. The food basket and the daily ration are rations of 350 g rice, 100 g pulse, 35 g vegetable oil, 50 g super cereal and 5 g salt per person. to implement the Project, WFP will work though experienced Cooperating Partners that have a good mastery and knowledge of the culture and driving forces of the areas. Organizations World Food Programme Implementing Partners Reach Out; Caritas-Kumba, LUKMEF, COMINSUD, CBCHS, CARITAS-Bamenda, SHUMAS and other NGOs.
During Project implementation, regular monitoring activities will be conducted during food distribution and monthly data collected against performance indicators for reporting through WFP COMET system. During post distribution monitoring, attention will be paid on the role played by men, women, girls and boys including decision-making on food consumption and food security in the household. Nutrition, Gender and protection issues are taken into consideration at all the stages of the project elaboration, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Gender and protection risk analysis will be carried out and the most vulnerable will be targeted, including female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities.
In line with WFP accountability affected populations, targeted vulnerable IDPs and local populations will be closely involved in various stages of including the targeting process, food distribution.
