project_name: United Nations Humanitarian Air Service in Mali
project_objective:
Despite the crucial need for humanitarian assistance, it is difficult for humanitarian personnel to provide adequate assistance to vulnerable people given the precarious security situation in central and Northern Mali. While the intensity of violence is lower than at the peak of the insurgency in 2012, record levels of criminality, terrorism and armed conflict continue to hamper access. Even though the signing of a Peace and Reconciliation Agreement by all parties to the conflict in June 2015 ushered in a relative calm in affected-areas and brought hope of an end to years of unrest, there has been an upsurge in militancy. As fighting increases, threats of a worsening humanitarian situation also increase. With the continued absence of the authorities in the north of the country, degradation of sanitation, shelter, health and food security conditions are likely to be aggravated as the number of IDPs increase. 

The humanitarian needs remain very high in a context where safe access is a challenge for humanitarian staff. The vast distances, undeveloped road infrastructure and insecurity make air travel crucial for humanitarian actors to access the beneficiary populations. Road travel in Mali remains highly risky. Traffic to and from northern Mali is frequently affected by landmines and Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs). Several roads are controlled by armed groups, hampering access to affected communities. The deteriorating security situation and ongoing violence have resulted in further restrictions to the already limited movement of humanitarian organizations in the North and at times the suspension of aid activities. 
 
The problem is compounded by the absence of commercial air operators in the country. UNHAS is often the only way in or out of an area of operation for the wider humanitarian community. Moreover, the humanitarian organizations have increased their presence throughout Mali, with UN agencies and NGOs opening new offices in the northern regions of the country. 

Air travel plays a critical role in allowing humanitarian access to beneficiary populations as a result of poor road conditions in northern Mali. As a result, UNHAS operation plays a key role in supporting the humanitarian community’s ability to implement and monitor a wide range of relief activities to some of the most remote and distressed areas of the northern part of Mali. Every month, UNHAS through airfreight, brings medicine, mail and other relief items to populations in need of assistance across the country.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence pour les populations deplacées internes (extremement vulnérables, très vulnérables et moyennement vulnérables) dans la province du Lac
project_objective:
Situé entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale, le bassin du lac Tchad couvre le Tchad, le Cameroun, le Niger et le Nigeria. Important bassin de production agro-pastorale et halieutique, le bassin du lac-Tchad repose sur un écosystème fragile mais avec une production variée et connaissant une démographie croissante. On estime ainsi à 2 million le nombre d’habitants vivant directement des ressources du bord du Lac. 
La Province du Lac est l’une des zones les plus vulnérables au Tchad car difficile d’accès, insuffisamment desservie par les services sociaux de base et sujette de façon récurrente aux effets du changement climatiques caractérisés par les sécheresses et les inondations qui sont parmi les aléas les plus importants.  Les conséquences de catastrophes qu’elles engendrent pèsent lourdement sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages. A cela s’ajoute une crise qui perdure depuis 2009, causant de pertes en vies humaines, des déplacements forcés des populations, des pertes des actifs productifs, des pressions sur les ressources naturelles et une des articulations de l’économie engendrant ainsi des conséquences sur l’emploi en particulier pour les jeunes. 
D’après l’aperçu des besoins humanitaires (HNO) 2020, plus 640,000   personnes   nécessitent   une   assistance alimentaire d’urgence au Tchad, dont 144,220 personnes vulnérables dans la province du Lac. Dans la province du Lac, les attaques dans les villages par les groupes armés et les opérations militaires au premier semestre 2019 ont occasionné des nouveaux déplacements de plus de 43,000 personnes.  Ces événements ont, entre autres, entravé l’accès des populations aux productions vivrières et rentières et affectés les moyens de subsistance de ces populations vulnérables. La situation de cette zone reste préoccupante en matière de sécurité dans les zones insulaires, car le contexte continue d’être volatile et précaire. 
Afin d’appuyer ces populations vulnérables, le PAM apportera une assistance alimentaire d’urgence aux populations déplacées internes dans la province du Lac. Cette assistance sera adaptée selon le profilage socio-économique des ménages déplacés (extrêmement vulnérables, très vulnérables et moyennement vulnérables) vivant dans les départements de Fouli, Kaya et Mamdi. De plus, cette assistance sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: Provision of Humanitarian Air Service in Cameroon (9,600 Beneficiaries)
project_objective:
UNHAS started operation in Cameroon in November 2015, following a request from the Humanitarian Coordinator as the provision of assistance by aid organizations was hampered by vast distances, insecurity and poor road infrastructure. In the years that followed, the security situation further deteriorated and made access to northern parts of the country, particularly the Far North extremely difficult and hardly reachable via roads and unreliable flight connections. The introduction of UNHAS flights has therefore been vital in enabling humanitarian organizations to scale up their response and reach more people in need. WFP-led aviation services being a key component for the whole humanitarian response in Cameroon, a country torn by three distinct geographical crises, connecting Yaoundé to two cities in the northern part of the country, all the way to N’djamena and beyond to other cities of Chad, therefore UNHAS route is critical for humanitarian actors to reach this remote affected part of the country
UNHAS aims:
1. To provide NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations and diplomatic missions in Cameroon with safe, effective and efficient access to beneficiaries and project implementation sites;
2. To transport light cargo, such as medical supplies, information and communication technology (ICT) equipment 
3. To provide adequate capacity for medical and security evacuations of humanitarian staff. UNHAS supported 100 % all requests, a total of 5 medical evacuations as of November 2019. 
Target for 2020: 9,600 Passengers; Cargo (24 MT); 60 Organisations; 8	Locations served and 100%	Medevac

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood improvement for Resilience Building Project
project_objective:
The insurgency in Nigeria continues to affect the population living in the North-East. According to the Needs Overview by the Early Recovery & Livelihoods sector(August 2019) an estimated 5.5 million people are in need of early recovery assistance, 1 million are IDPs in host communities, 1.5 million IDPs and returnees, and 2.9 million people in host communities. This includes 1.5 million girls, 1.3 million boys and 0.9 mullion women in the most affected states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe State.

Several LGAs have been prioritized based on the levels of damages and service delivery burden associated with high numbers of returnees and IDPs in host communities: Damboa, Konduga, Monguno (Borno State); Madagali, Mubi North, Hong (Adamawa State); and Gujba, Potiskum and Fika (Yobe State).
The 27th round of the Displacement Tracking Matrix (IOM - May 2019), estimated the number of IDPs and Returnees to be 3,602,943 (1,980,036 IDPS and 1,622,908 Returnees), 92.6% of whom have been displaced due to the Boko Haram insurgency in the North East. The number of returnees went up by 64,850 to take the total number to 1,622,908 (or 265,649 households) from 1,558,058 returnees that were assessed in the last round of assessment conducted in January 2019. Out of the total number of displaced people, 133,003 IDPs and 1,622,908 Returnees are currently in Yobe State (The 27th round of the Displacement Tracking Matrix (IOM - May 2019) Ongoing crisis has worsen the situation including disruption of market supplies and livelihoods, and significantly limiting the populations having access to livelihoods. IOM estimates that 60% of the IDPs reside with host communities. 
As situation in Yobe state is stabilizing, COOPI proposes livelihood activities in Yusufari,Geidam, Potiskum, Fika and Gulani LGAs. The project will target 5,865 households
 
(approximatively 24,173 beneficiaries) in the project. Beneficiaries will be supported in order to foster the transition from emergency to resilience as COOPI is committed to apply the humanitarian-development nexus approach and ensure coherence between the actors. COOPI intends to protect and rehabilitate livelihoods of most vulnerable groups, pre-identified through COOPI’s ongoing food assistance and CBT activities funded by other donors, through technical trainings on adapted livelihood practices where possible in coordination and complementarity with ongoing line ministries and sector. COOPI will complement proposed activities with EU funded early recovery programs in NE. COOPI is implementing EU supported Yobe package and will supplement all livelihood activities and link to the humanitarian development nexus.
COOPI forecast strong potential for humanitarian development nexus through its presence in Yobe and particularly in proposed LGA. COOPI has already developed liaison and MOUs with state government’s line departments as well as providing capacity building opportunities to government institutes. COOPI will also consider the livelihood action to be linked with other sectors which are planned to be executed as multiyear response mainly to ensure transition from emergency to recovery and rehabilitation including conflict management. COOPI will consider to work through local NGOs. Implementation of current activities in the area have revealed a deterioration in livelihoods sources primarily due to frequent conflicts and inherent hardships in the state as well as climactic conditions and increased market demands. COOPI, following Early Recovery and Livelihood sector's objectives, intends to protect and rehabilitate livelihoods of most vulnerable groups, identified through technical trainings on adapted practices and formation and training of livelihood beneficiaries focusing on women groups who are already engaged with various small enterprises. COOPI will ensure that composition of sectors is defined based on COOPI Community Based Participatory Planning sessions.

project_name: Projet de prevention et reponse contre les incidents et risques de protection pour les enfants filles et garcons affectes par les conflits a  Diffa & Talaberi.
project_objective: Cet projet a comme objectif principal de prevenir et de repondre aux risques de separation des enfants affectes par les conflits et ameliorer ainsi les services de prise en charge dans la region de Diffa.  Les enfants separes, non accompagnes et ceux a risques separation sont la cible prencipale de cette proposition.  La cible secondaire sera composer par des familles d'accuiels temporaires et spontanees qui ont recus ou recoivent les enfants separes dans les sites concernees par cette proposition.  Pour prevenir et repondre aux risques de separation, les interventions de ce projet tournent autour de la sensibilisation sur les risques de separations, de la formation des familles d'accueil et des familles biologiques sur les bonnes pratiques parantales pour reduire les abus et autre forme d'exploitations des enfants dans les familles soit d'accueil soit biologiques. Afin d'ameliorer les conditions d'accueil, un appui logistique et financier ( cash de prise en charge) sera octroyer aux familles d'acceuil et celles biologiques pour permettre aux enfants concernes de continuer a acceder aux services sociaux de base surtout  scolaire et sanitaire.  Les enfants separees, non accompagnes ansi que leurs familles recevront un accompagnement en appui pyschosocial et des sessions de competences de vie afin de leur permettre d'etre plus resilient aux problemes de la vie et de trouver des solutions qui leurs permettent de garder espoir. Une cartographie sera faite pour comprendre les conditions d'accueil des enfants dans les familles d'accueil et les resultats permettront aux partenaires etatiques de prendre des precautions necessaires pour ameliorer les services de prises en charges transitoires.  les enfants survivants de violences sexuelles seront pris en charge hollostiques et reinserer dans le circuit social. Les ecoles seront formes afin de protection un environnement protecteurs et une collaboration efficace avec les structures communautaires composees par celles des adolescents et celles des adultes.

and environmental hygiene for 1,350,000 most vulnerable conflict, WASH related epidemics
and natural disaster affected non-refugees’ population and hosting communities in North, South, East, West and Central Darfur, South, West and North Kordofan, Blue Nile, White Nile, Sennar, Kassala,

project_name: Child protection services for IDPs and host communities in Darfur states, Blue Nile, Kordofan states and Abyei
project_objective: In line with the Sudan Multi-Year Humanitarian Strategy 2017-2019, and the associated annual Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) , UNICEF continue to support children affected by conflict in a context of chronic underdevelopment, particularly in hard-to-reach and new accessible areas where children’s needs are most acute. Sudan’s ongoing violence in the Darfurs, the Kordofans, Blue Nile and Abyei has forced more than three  million people to flee their homes, including some 1.9 million children. Displacement has resulted in high levels of family separation, leading to over 2300 active cases of unaccompanied, separated, and missing children during 2019 among IDPs population. Recruitment, mobilization of children to take part in armed conflict continues to be a high risk in the targeted states including in tribal conflicts. More than 400 children released from armed forces/groups will need to be enrolled in a reintegration program to enable them to return to their normal life in addition to many other vulnerable children. While UNICEF continues working to ensure that all children are released and reintegrated, many children are still recruited or associated with armed forces and groups.  A communication strategy to end the recruitment and association of children with armed forces and groups. Sexual and Gender based Violence specially against girls, is another serious violation that needs to be addressed specially in the newly accessible areas in Darfur. Displacement and family separation during flighting further exacerbates the risk of SGBV. Other grave violations such as abductions, killing and maiming are another major risk facing children in the conflict affected states. Children in the newly accessible areas in south Darfur, Central Darfur, north Darfur, south Kordofan and Blue Nile are in urgent need of lifesaving child protection emergency services such as psychosocial support (PSS), family reunification, as well as protection from grave child rights violations including sexual violence, abductions and recruitments.

project_name: Building Resilient Communities for Child Survival, Growth and Development in 15 States
project_objective:
This project aims at building the resilience of the poorest, most-in-need and hardest-to-reach children. It targets 1,500 communities and 329,000 vulnerable children (50% girls and 2% children with disabilities) with below breakdown:
•	IDPs Children: 54,000
•	Returnees Children: 23,000
•	Vulnerable Residents: 252,000
The project should provide integrated and sustainable assistance through interventions that promote resilience amongst affected populations and strengthen human security. The whole child approach using the Child Friendly Schools (CFS) framework needs to be clearly reflected with the following five thematic components: (i) Inclusiveness; (ii) Effective Teaching and Learning; (iii) Safe, Healthy and Protective Learning Environment; (iv) Gender Responsiveness; (v) Community and Child Participation.
The activities will be implemented under three outcomes as follows:
Outcome 1: More out-of-school children, especially girls, marginalized groups and those in the most vulnerable situations, are enabled to access quality pre-primary, primary and alternative learning opportunities with zero tolerance to hazards
To increase enrolment and reduce dropout of children from schools, multitude of interventions will be provided in a customised package based on actual underlying reasons. Target schools will be supported to enrol additional 50,000 Out of school children, to open ALP classrooms for 50,000 children and to establish ECE centres/ pre-school classrooms for 75,000 Children. Also, 6,580 Children with disabilities will be targeted in an integrated manner whether through training of teachers, providing specialized supplies, adding rams to Classrooms and latrines, etc... 
Schooling supplies will be provided in form of Teacher kits, student kits, Recreational Kits, ECD kits, dignity Kits for girls, uniform sets, books and school furniture for a total of 329,000 children to attend schools. Cash assistance to 100,000 vulnerable children (1,000 SDG per school year) and income generating activities to women-headed households and to children with disabilities will be provided to support continuity of learning.
Outcome 2: Individuals, Education providers, parents and communities have improved knowledge, skills and pro-social capacity to contribute to quality learning outcome.
Building capacity of 1,500 communities and civil society to promote, enable and sustain behaviour change related to access to quality education. 22,500 PTA members will be trained on School Improvement Planning SIP before being supported with school grant (max 270,000 SDG per school) for income generating activity that will cover local school feeding, teachers’ incentives (ALP, Pre-School, School), school running costs and at least 50% reduction in school fees.
Also 1,500 school clubs will be formed and trained on upshift programme to build skills and create opportunity for the most disadvantaged young people and empowers them to identify challenges in their communities and create entrepreneurial solutions to address them. Also, the package of Unlocking literacy programme including its assessment pre- and post will be scaled up to support quality learning at 1,500 schools/ communities
Outcome 3: More communities have strengthened mechanisms to protect children from violence, abuse, and exploitation including FGM/C and child marriage for inclusive, safe and protective school environments.
The integrated approach of Education and Child Protection will be reflected in all education activities. It targets increasing awareness of 150,000 education personnel and community structures on the CP issues with signing of Code of Conduct (CoC).  Moreover, safe referral pathways and complaint mechanisms between CBCPN, PTA and Education personnel will be established with estimated 6,000 cases referred to CP agencies/networks by education staff each month from the target 1,500 schools.

project_name: Provision of quality life-saving and high impact health services to the most vulnerable children and mothers in 112 targeted localities in Sudan
project_objective:
UNICEF will support the humanitarian actors to strengthen the capacity of the health system, with a focus at the primary health care levels including at the community level to avail quality, life-saving and high impact interventions to 2,668,000 boys and girls (children under the age of 15 years) and pregnant and lactating women in humanitarian situations. UNICEF will support diversified service delivery modalities including through fixed health facilities, outreach sessions, mobile medical clinics and community-based health service providers to ensure access to quality lifesaving health services, which will include preventive, promotive and curative care for the most vulnerable. 

Through this project, UNICEF will support the humanitarian actors to avail integrated primary health care packages of services including immunization, integrated management of childhood illnesses, maternal and newborn health (Antenatal Care, skilled delivery, postnatal care). In addition, UNICEF will support the humanitarian actors in timely responding to any shocks including outbreaks of communicable diseases, flood, displacements and others as they arise. 

To achieve this, UNICEF will build the capacity of the state and locality level health sector managers, implementing partners, health service providers in a wide range of programmatic areas to ensure service delivery and its support systems are in place. UNICEF will provide the essential medicines, supplies and commodities which includes vaccines, medicines, medical kits, cold chain equipment, bed nets, registers, reporting formats and other M&E tools. At the community level, UNICEF will enhance community engagement to strengthen community’s resilience, enhance utilization of health services and promote healthy practices. In addition, to deliver these services and ensure synergetic impacts, UNICEF will promote and support the implementation of integrated programs in collaboration with the other sectors including nutrition, WASH and others.

project_name: UNICEF lifesaving Nutrition interventions to address the most vulnerable population needs
project_objective:
Sudan faces one of the highest rates of malnutrition in the regions and according to the 2020 draft HNO about 522,000 children suffer from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in Sudan. This project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition among highly vulnerable population and communities through the provision of high impact nutrition interventions. In 2020 UNICEF will further scale up its support for the delivery of life saving treatment to children suffering from SAM, the prevention of malnutrition through community-based counselling on good infant and young child feeding (IYCF) and care practices while focusing on the quality of services delivered. This will include the provision of treatment to 290,467 children suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) including the procurement of 348,560 cartons of Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) and support for operational support including the expansion of the current number of Outpatient Treatment Program (OTP) sites including capacity building of key cadres of staff responsible for service delivery to increase the coverage of services in high burden areas. UNICEF will further strengthen for the early case finding and referral by using Mothers Support groups (MSGs), community health workers, health facility staff, health promoters & hygiene promoters.
To prevent malnutrition more generally and reduce the risk of readmissions UNICEF will strengthen the linkage between the national curative and preventative nutrition services, specifically the linkages between CMAM and the provision of IYCF counselling by improving the referral mechanisms. UNICEF will further scale up the cIYCF program currently existing of more than 3000 Mothers Support Groups (MSGs) to counsel 860,785 caregivers while improving both the reporting system and introduce a supportive supervision structure. UNICEF will continue to provide vitamin A supplementation to 3,830,884 children aged 6-59 months through subnational and national vaccination campaigns while aiming to develop an alternative distribution strategy. To prevent anemia among vulnerable women during pregnancy, UNICEF will provide iron folate supplementation to 374,786 pregnant women in collaboration with the health sector.
UNICEF will support health system strengthening through efforts to strengthen supply chain management for RUFT from national level to health facility level, gradually moving towards a transitioning of the supply chain management from UNICEF to FMOH except for the procurement and by strengthening the national capacity for state and locality level monitoring of the CMAM program and continue to build capacity to utilize data for assessing and improving performance. UNICEF will also support the further strengthening of nutrition information systems to provide accurate and timely data from OTPs and MSGs. In new emergencies UNICEF will support the undertaking of timely rapid assessments to inform response actions.

project_name: AMELIORATION DE LA COMPRÉHENSION DE DÉPLACEMENT AU TCHAD À TRAVERS LA GESTION D’INFORMATION ET LE RENFORCEMENT DES CAPACITES NATIONALES EN GESTION D’INFORMATION
project_objective:
Au Tchad, l'OIM met en œuvre les activités de la matrice de suivi des déplacements (DTM – Displacement Tracking Matrix en anglais) depuis 2014, à la suite de la crise en RCA et de son afflux important de retournés tchadiens au Tchad. Depuis lors, l'OIM a progressivement étendu ses activités DTM à la fois géographiquement (2015 : lac Tchad, 2017: nord du Tchad) et par programme (points de suivi des flux le long de la plupart des frontières tchadiennes, outil de suivi d'urgence à l'échelle nationale, indice de stabilité, les enquêtes sur les intentions de retour dans les zones à fort déplacement de Lac et du sud, etc.). Tous les produits sont disponibles pour la communauté humanitaire dans son ensemble et sont utilisés par les partenaires du système de groupes humanitaires et du secteur du développement. Une enquête sur l’utilisation des informations produites par la DTM a indiqué que 90 pour cent des partenaires utilisent les produits de la DTM et à 67 pour cent ils les utilisent pour des réponses humanitaires.  Cette enquête a aussi démontré que ces informations orientent les discussions dans différentes réunions des partenaires : les réunions des clusters (pour 52% des partenaires), les réunions des internes aux organisations (50% des partenaires) et la coordination inter cluster (pour 43% des partenaires). Ceci est une indication sur l’importance des informations fournies à travers la DTM pour la communautaire humanitaire dans son ensemble.
A travers la DTM, l’OIM fournit des données précises et opportunes pour éclairer les processus de prise de décision des acteurs tant humanitaires que de développement. À cette fin, l’OIM a collaboré étroitement avec la Banque mondiale, la Commission du bassin du lac Tchad (CBLT), l’Union africaine (UA) et les partenaires humanitaires pour fournir des données sur les dimensions de la mobilité au Tchad afin d’éclairer le cadre d’assistance pluriannuel de la Banque mondiale, la stratégie de stabilisation UA-LCBC du bassin du lac Tchad, le plan de développement et de sécurité Gouvernement-UE-PNUD pour la province du Lac, du cadre d'aide au développement des Nations Unies (UNDAF), le plan de réponse humanitaire (HRP) et la revue de besoins humanitaires (HNO).

Afin de continuer à fournir des informations cruciales sur les dimensions des déplacements, l'OIM propose une intervention de 18 mois centrée sur trois piliers principaux.
1. Fourniture d'informations pertinentes, cohérentes et précises les déplacements des populations ;
2. Recherche documentée sur les liens entre les facteurs d'instabilité et d'insécurité avec la mobilité au Tchad ;
3. Renforcement des capacités gouvernementales dans la gestion des données sur le déplacement des populations.
En étroite coordination avec les partenaires du Comité de coordination Intercluster (ICC), l'OIM a toujours examiné différents indicateurs pour déterminer les moyens les plus conviviaux et accessibles afin d'adapter au mieux les informations fournies pour orienter les réponses humanitaires. Cela s’est avéré particulièrement utile pour les crises soudaines observées dans l’est du Tchad depuis juillet 2019, où des réponses rapides ont été déclenchées par les acteurs humanitaires à travers des alertes rapportées par l’outil de suivi des urgences de la DTM. 
Les piliers proposés à travers ce projet vont se concentrer dans des zones à fort déplacement des populations : le Lac, l'Est et le Sud.

project_name: Intervention médicale d’urgence visant à prendre en charge les complications médicales liées à la malnutrition aigüe pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans y compris les enfants nomades tout sexe confondu
project_objective:
La crise de la malnutrition et de l'insécurité alimentaire touche chaque année les habitants de la ceinture sahélienne du Tchad et la malnutrition aiguë sévère (MAS) reste une préoccupation humanitaire essentielle dans la ceinture sahélienne où le taux de malnutrition aiguë dépasse les seuils acceptables depuis de nombreuses années dans le monde. Selon la récente enquête nutritionnelle menée en 2019, la malnutrition aiguë globale dans 9 provinces de la ceinture sahélienne dépasse 15% et la malnutrition aiguë sévère dépasse 2% dans 6 provinces s. Selon les projections Cluster Nutrition,
15 465 cas de MAS et MAM  21 755 sont attendus en 2020 dans les sites de rapatriés et de réfugiés. Le taux élevé de mortalité observé aux Unités  de nutrition thérapeutique est principalement dû à l’impact des maladies transmissibles d’une part et, d’autre part, au statut de malnutrition qui affaiblit la capacité des enfants à lutter contre les maladies transmissibles et les épidémies. De plus, les provinces  de la bande sahélienne sont les plus touchées par le manque d'accès aux services de santé de base. La plupart des villages de ces provinces  sont situés  à plus de 30 km des centres de santé et certains à environ 100 km. Plus de 20% de la population est nomade, ce qui a entraîné un faible accès aux services de santé de base. Le manque d'accès aux services de santé de base est la principale raison qui explique les taux élevés de mortalité infantile (180/1000) et élevé de mortalité maternelle (860/100000)

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence aux populations les plus vulnérables en insécurité alimentaire sévère pendant la période de soudure
project_objective:
L’analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2019 prévoit pour la saison de soudure 2020 une dégradation de la situation par rapport à la soudure de 2019. Le nombre de personnes en insécurité alimentaire sévère est passé de 649 801 personnes avec 11 départements (dont 5 en bande sahélienne) en phase crise en 2019 à 1 112 112 personnes avec 15 départements (dont 15 en bande sahélienne) en phase crise et plus en 2020.
Ce changement est principalement dû à l’insécurité dans le grand nord du Tchad qui a causé la fermeture des frontières ayant un impact négatif sur les marchés qui étaient normalement approvisionnés par la Libye, le Soudan, la Nigeria, la RCA et le Niger.
La campagne agricole a été perturbée par des longues séquences sèches dans certaines zones et par des inondations dans des autres zones qui ont détruit une grande partie de la production attendue. 
Le PAM planifie appuyer 623 647 personnes avec une assistance alimentaire pour trois mois avec rations complètes dans 15 départements déclarés en phase 3 et plus. Cette assistance sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des réfugiés nigérians touchés par la crise de Boko Haram à travers la réponse intégrée aux Violences Basées sur le Genre et l’autonomisation des femmes et filles dans la province du Lac
project_objective:
L’instabilité sécuritaire causé par le secte Boko Haram a occasionné l’arrivée des Nigérians installé dans la province du Lac. On dénombre 11 949 réfugiés. Parmi cette population, 56% enfants : soit 28% des filles et 28% des garçons ; les adultes représentent 40% dont 25% des femmes, les personnes âgées constituent 4%. Le nombre de ménages est de 3 609. Ces ménages sont dirigés par les hommes, quelques-uns sont dirigés par les femmes, il y a a aussi des ménages dirigés par des mineurs. Ils sont installés dans le département de Kaya (camp de Dar el salem, à Ngouboua et Tchoukoutalia). Parmi cette population, il y a de personnes vivants avec handicap et autres catégories de vulnérabilités : personnes âgées, femmes à risque, malades chroniques..., qu’il faut développer une approche spécifique pour leur intégration.
Avec la recrudescence des attaques, les perspectives de retour ne sont pas envisageables. 
Cette situation de déplacement compromet la vie de ces réfugiés qui se retrouvent un autre territoire que le leur avec plusieurs besoins multisectoriels.  
Dans un tel contexte les VBG sont inévitables, toutes les formes de VBG (violences sexuelles, agressions physiques, dénis de ressources, d’opportunités et de ressources, le mariage précoce/forcé) sont perpétrées et pour la plupart du temps sur les femmes et filles.
Les auteurs sont de la communauté, des groupes armés, des acteurs de développement/humanitaires, des acteurs économiques et aussi des agents de forces de sécurité. 
Le présent projet vise à renforcer la résilience de ces populations affectées. Ainsi le projet permettra de :
-	Prévenir les risques de VBG dans la communauté
-	Faciliter de l’accès aux services essentiels de qualité pour les personnes survivantes de VBG 
-	Le renforcement des connaissances sur les notions de compétences de vie courantes
-	Renforcer les capacités de personnes à risques pour leur autonomisation 
Les cibles sont : i) les personnes survivantes des Violences Basées sur le genre (VBG) (réfugiés Nigérians et les communautés d’accueil) ; ii) les personnes à risques et aussi toutes les couches sociales dans les communautés par le transfert des connaissances sur les notions de compétences de vie courantes, iii) et tous les réfugiés à travers le renforcement des connaissances sur le bien-être familial à travers la promotion de droits et l’élimination des VBG.
Le projet cible les femmes et filles, les hommes et garçons, ainsi que les leaders communautaires (religieux, traditionnels et société civile) 
Les stratégies développées respecteront les principes de la protection transversale et la prise en compte de genre, âge et la diversité (handicap et autres catégories vulnérables). Le projet sera mis en œuvre selon le principe de ‘’ne pas nuire’’ avec une approche participative impliquant fortement les bénéficiaires pour un meilleur transfert de compétences afin de faciliter l’accès pour tous et mettre en valeur la notion de redevabilité y compris l’utilisation de mécanisme de plaintes.

project_name: Strengthening humanitarian coordination, advocacy and quality of humanitarian assistance
project_objective: (i) expanding humanitarian access to deliver life-saving assistance and protection in Diffa, Tillabery, Tahoua and Maradi a complex operating environment where the security situation remains volatile; (ii) Better coordination of the response in other parts of the country during peaks of malnutrition, food insecurity, epidemics and flooding to update needs and highlight gaps; (iii) establishing an efficient humanitarian coordination mechanism in Diffa, Tillabery and Thoua (iv) optimizing the cooperation with the Government of Niger and development actors trough the operationalization of the humanitarian / development nexus, capitalizing on the willingness of government of Niger to take the lead on humanitarian issues while considering how to further support them in terms of capacity building; (v) ensuring adequate funding for humanitarian activities in all humanitarian sectors, including by working closely with donors towards more support and funding tools to national responders, and the scaling up of cash-based programming; (VI) reinforce coordination and communication on the Liptako Gourma and Lake Chad Basin situation; (VII) conduct discussions for a possible revision of the coordination mechanisms after the 3 years strategy and support national NGOs to be better organized in view of their representation in the HCT and the Humanitarian Forum.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre sa mission à travers ses fonctions clés que sont la Coordination, Gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP) et la PSEA, la préparation aux urgences et le plaidoyer pour plus de visibilités et de mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) à travers le bureau OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois Sous bureaux à Abéché, Goré et Lac. Il sera également renforcé l’opérationnalisation du nexus humanitaire, développement et paix dans le cadre de la nouvelle façon de travailler., 

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire efficace et performante permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’ informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial  de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services in Sudan
project_objective:
According to the 2020 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) some 9.3 million people – 23 per cent of the population – will need humanitarian assistance in 2020. The transitional government is prioritizing peace and ending the economic crisis, issues closely intertwined with the drivers of humanitarian need in the country.
While incidents of fighting have reduced considerably in recent years, the situation of people displaced due to decades of conflict remains unresolved. Some 1.87 million IDPs and 1.1 million refugees and asylum seekers  continue to need humanitarian assistance and protection support, both in camps and host communities.  Pockets of armed conflict continue in Darfur, and sporadic inter-communal conflicts also continue. In neighbouring Central African Republic (CAR), ongoing intercommunal conflicts have escalated since June 2019, with reports indicating large populations of internally displaced populations along the border with Sudan, near Central and South Darfur, which are anticipated to continue into 2020. 
Across Sudan, basic services are lacking, and natural disasters, like floods, affect people each year. But it is a deepening economic crisis, following years of stagnation and little investment in already-weak public services, that is driving worsening food insecurity, deteriorating healthcare, and other needs across Sudan. 
Throughout Sudan, most people – 58 per cent of households – cannot afford a basic daily food basket. Over 2.4 million children suffer from acute malnutrition.  Medical facilities across the country are not functional due to lack of essential drugs. 
In 2019, Sudan faced a worsening economic crisis that will continue to drive humanitarian needs  into 2020, even as the transitional government works toward economic reforms. Prime Minister Hamdok has noted the country needs up to $8 billion in support over the next two years to cover imports and rebuild the economy.  While the transitional government is committed to stemming the economic crisis,  reforms  may involve subsidy cuts which could have a further impact on families who are already struggling to cope. Basic service provision, already weak and underdeveloped, has been dangerously degraded by the economic crisis. This has affected people directly, impacting households’ ability to buy food and cover basic needs. It has also deepened already existing needs – including among existing vulnerable groups like displaced people, returnees, and refugees – and may cause new people to fall into humanitarian need

project_name: Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services
project_objective: The project is aimed at coordinating effective, timely and principled humanitarian action through enhanced situation analysis, empowered leadership, and increased public information and advocacy for humanitarian financing and protection of civilians.

project_name: Fortalecer la coordinación y abogacía humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
En 2020, OCHA en Venezuela seguirá con el objetivo de reforzar las estructuras de coordinación y apoyar el Ciclo de Programa Humanitario (HPC). Esto incluirá nuevas evaluaciones de necesidades para el HNO, monitoreo regular de la respuesta y mejor comunicación sobre la situación general. OCHA planea expandir aún más su abogacía para facilitar el acceso a las áreas más vulnerables y movilizar más fondos para la respuesta.

OCHA también proporcionará capacitación sobre los principios humanitarios, la coordinación humanitaria, el HPC y temas transversales como rendición de cuentas a la población afectada, prevención contra la explotación y abusos sexuales y género.

La estrategia de OCHA Venezuela para 2020 se centrará en las siguientes prioridades:
-	Mejorar la comprensión de la comunidad humanitaria de las necesidades humanitarias, a través de evaluaciones periódicas y monitoreo de necesidades.
-	Establecer un sistema de monitoreo para el HRP y producir productos regulares sobre la respuesta.
-	Fortalecer los foros de coordinación para garantizar una respuesta humanitaria oportuna, efectiva y basada en los principios humanitarios.
-	Desarrollar la capacidad de los socios humanitarios para participar de manera efectiva en el HPC y proporcionar una respuesta más efectiva.
-	Fortalecer la comunicación humanitaria, para mejorar la comprensión de los principios humanitarios, los esfuerzos de respuesta y la aceptación de las organizaciones humanitarias.
-	Fortalecer los centros de coordinación en terreno, para asegurar que cubran efectivamente su área geográfica, mejorando las capacidades de evaluación, respuesta y monitoreo y la coordinación con los socios y partes interesadas.
-	Mantener el clúster de Logistica, para fortalecer la coordinación entre los socios, el intercambio de informaciones puntuales sobre temas logísticos, apoyar la abogacía con las contrapartes institucionales, y promover soluciones conjuntas para mejorar la capacitad operacional y de respuesta.
-	Aumentar el nivel de apoyo financiero proporcionado por los donantes.
-	Mejorar el diálogo con todas las partes interesadas para facilitar la aceptación y el acceso.

project_name: Humanitarian Coordination in Libya
project_objective: OCHA will in 2020 continue to support the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC) and the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in coordinating the humanitarian response to meet the (protection) needs of the most vulnerable people affected by the conflict / crisis in Libya. Through Inter-Sector and Area-Based coordination, OCHA will provide mechanisms and support to ensure that the interventions of humanitarian organisations are well coordinated and based on robust and timely evidence. OCHA will further facilitate and advocate for humanitarian access, the respect of humanitarian principles and ensure that the protection of people in need is effective.

project_name: Protection of conflict-affected girls, boys and women exposed to child protection risks and gender based violence in South Sudan
project_objective: The UNICEF Child Protection programme provides support to the extremely vulnerable, conflict-affected girls, boys and women in South Sudan who are exposed to child protection risks and gender-based violence. The programme includes providing case management and family tracing and reunification services, psychosocial support, reintegration interventions for children associated with armed forces and groups (CAAFAG), mine risk education (MRE), monitoring of grave child rights violations through the monitoring and reporting mechanism (MRM), gender based violence interventions, and critical, frontline emergency services, through integrated rapid response mechanisms (IRRMs). Within the programme budget $12m is needed for CPiE, $2.5m for GBV and $1m for MRE.

project_name: Creation and rehabilitation of household/group-based and communal-level productive assets, human capital development, and enhancement of food systems
project_objective:
WFP Syria’s interim Country Strategy Plan (iCSP) 2019-20 envision an increase in livelihood programming to support almost 2 million beneficiaries. The project activities provide an overarching chapeau under which a range of interventions will serve to strengthen livelihoods at household/ group-based and community-level. The project will support food insecure and vulnerable households with two activity pillars via Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) and Food Assistance for Training (FFT). 
1.	Food Assistance for Assets (FFA)
FFA aims to restore and rebuild livelihoods of vulnerable Syrian households and communities through household-level productive assets, income generation activities and rehabilitation of communal infrastructure to enhance agricultural production. 
The project is planning to support the targeted households through two types of interventions a) provision of household, group and community-based productive assets; and b) rehabilitation of communal agrarian infrastructure; 

Pillar 1a: Household and Group-Based Productive Assets: 
Provision of agricultural inputs and technical assistance to households in rural areas to improve and diversify household food consumption and provide income generating opportunities. 
Pillar 1b – Rehabilitation of Communal Agrarian Infrastructure 
The project aims to rehabilitate and fix irrigation and other agricultural infrastructure in the rural areas. Its’s critical to encourage smallholder famers to return to cultivation, improve agricultural productivity, and revitalize local markets. 

2.	Human Capital Development/Vocational Skills Training via FFT
FFT aims to enhance human capital and skills development, with a focus on urban women and youth. Active labour market support activities will provide participants with technical and vocational skills training (VST) based on local labour market needs and post-training support to enter the labour market or establish small businesses.
3.	Enhancement of food systems,
 strengthening local economic recovery and basic service provision, with the aim of stimulating economic employment opportunities for vulnerable communities and providing WFP an opportunity to encourage and/or facilitate the employment of members from vulnerable, food insecure households. Where WFP support is targeted at businesses related to food production and sales, WFP support will directly increase community access to, and consumption of, food commodities, thereby enhancing local food security

project_name: Internally Displaced Population in South Sudan supported through advocacy, provision of protection and targeted assistance to promote resilience and achievement of solutions
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen a rights-based protection response for IDPs, IDP returnees and to a lesser other affected populations, in particular those most vulnerable; through stronger advocacy, timely life-saving activities, streamlining prevention-oriented initiatives and evidence-based planning, with a focus in expanding outreach and developing the capacity of affected communities to cope, recover, contribute to and achieve Solutions.
The targeted population for UNHCR’s 2020 Programme consists of 680,000 internally displaced persons and returnees directly benefiting from assistance and delivery of protection services. The project also foresees benefiting the entire  displaced population and returnees through continuous advocacy and support in the area of Law and Policy, fostering the successful engagement with the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (TNLA), the Ministries of Justice; Home Affairs, Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management and other relevant executive bodies (such as RRC, ROSS, etc.) with a focus on the approval and implementation of the new IDP Act; as well as related policy and regulatory frameworks; and building upon previous efforts of the Operation on capacity building and technical assistance to Parliamentarians and members of the Executive that culminated in the passing of the Kampala Convention and the final draft of the IDP Act in 2019.
The 2020 programme is designed to ensure that the Operation is fit-for-purpose, aiming for increased operational presence (static or mobile); efficiency in performance; as well as improved response and delivery, both in quality and speed. UNHCR has expanded its field protection unit to ensure systematic mobile protection monitoring and a strong presence in integrated missions and rapid assessments as well as mobile interventions. While response and monitoring will continue to cover POC and collective sites; coverage will also continue to expand to the 190 identified priority locations, including remote or hard-to-reach areas, in full support to the Protection Cluster Strategy for mobile assessments and response. Resources and advocacy will have a primary focus on Solutions, either durable or transitional (where the former is not yet possible), including activities planned to rapidly assess needs, risks, intentions, feasibility of returns, relocations or integration; family reunification, absorption capacity of host communities; while also strengthening community-based structures, HLP initiatives, promotion of livelihoods and peaceful coexistence. Improving coordination and quality of assessments and monitoring will be a key component; using the mobile tools for population profiling for more accurate and quicker data collection and triangulated analysis, which will improve the relevance of information products, leading to a more fitting risk-mitigation approach, reduced response time; while underpinning protection mainstreaming across other operational interventions, including of other Clusters. UNHCR will continue to make the best of its key membership of the protection cluster and ensure regular reporting to the clusters’ 5W and strong participation and contribution in the different clusters’ working groups (i.e. SAG, HLPWG, MPCF) to ensure coordination and complementarity of interventions, avoiding duplication with other members and ensuring regular sharing of reports with the cluster, as per the common practice pursued so far. UNHCR has been leading the coordination efforts in protection response in several locations in 8 of the 10 States across the country and it will continue fostering this important role to ensure that a more coordinated planning and response enhances efficiency and efficacy of programmes; successfully addressing gaps and targeting those in need in a timely manner.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action Response in Sudan
project_objective: This project will reduce risks posed by explosive hazards, enabling the affected population to safely access productive land, natural resources and basic services. Additionally, the project aims to provide assistance to landmine/ERW survivors for socioeconomic reintegration. Landmine/ERW contaminated areas will be surveyed and cleared, securing access to 10,000,000 square meters of priority land for safe movement of refugees and IDPs and/or productive use by the local populations. 300,000 vulnerable populations will learn how to adopt safe behaviors in landmine contaminated areas. 250 landmine/ERW survivors and other persons with disabilities (PWD) will be empowered by gaining psychological support, physical mobility and means for livelihood. Through this project, the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) will support the Government of Sudan to meet its commitment to the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention (APMBC) by strengthening the institutional capacity of the National Mine Action Center (NMAC). In this endeavor, the project will continue to build the national capacity in mine action by providing training to national partners including NMAC and non-governmental organization (NGO) staff members.

project_name: Reduce morbidity and mortality among the Rohingya population and host community in Cox’s Bazar district through strengthening essential healthcare services, prevention and control of outbreaks, risk communications and coordination of health sector
project_objective:
WHO’s response strategy is aligned with the overall Health Sector Strategy as articulated in the Joint Response Plan 2020. The activities prioritized under this project have been selected based on the Health Sector needs highlighted by the mid-term review of the Joint Response Plan 2019, Joint Multisectoral Needs Assessment (JMSNA)- September 2019, and Population In Need figures (ISCG, November 2019).  WHO remains the only actor in support of the MoHFW with the mandate and capacity to set priorities, minimum standards, and support quality health service delivery.
 In 2020 WHO, as the lead of the Health Sector, will continue to work towards equity and quality of services, advocate on behalf of the Health Sector on inadequately addressed issues, strongly engage government in localization efforts and stimulate documentation and publication of lessons learned in the crisis.
WHO will focus on quality service delivery as part of efforts to sustain what is achieved over the last two years of the response while maintaining capacity to continue support response to needs that result from emergencies due to natural disasters and disease outbreaks in this protracted humanitarian crisis as well as to ensure continuity of emergency services during the monsoon and cyclone seasons. 
Going forward, WHO intends to not only address the immediate needs, but also providing regular and timely information on public health risks and requirements and filling gaps through effective coordination of partners and effective response ensuring access to life saving interventions mediated by rationalized health service delivery system.
The underlying principles will be to liaise with national government on the governance and leadership through Civil Surgeon’s office and MOHFW Coordination Cell, support in developing standards, guidelines and protocols, extending of national programs to the FDMN settings and; avail of health workforce, vaccines and essential technology, health information, service delivery based on minimum services package, for boys and girls, women and men in both the Rohingyas and host community.
The planned interventions will be guided by periodical service availability assessments and external independent reviews and assessments will be used as an opportunity for the Rohingya and host community populations to review the work of WHO

project_name: Livelihood assistance for vulnerable community in El Salam and Sunta localities in South Darfur State
project_objective:
Mercy Corps (MC) will deliver livelihoods programming for vulnerable community members in El Salam and Sunta states, creating market-driven livelihood opportunities in a context where barriers to formal and informal employment severely undermine both the food security and resilience capacities of households. Furthermore, Mercy Corps deliberately designs our humanitarian programs to do better than meet needs on a stopgap basis. While our priority aim is to save lives, minimize suffering, and protect social and economic assets, we will also tackles the proximate and underlying causes of the emergency in order to interrupt repeated cycles of crisis and vulnerability ensuring we are actually mitigating suffering--not just postponing it to a later date. 
Building on Mercy Corps existing livelihood projects in South Darfur; Mercy Corps will strengthen the livelihoods of 4500(El Salam 1100:Suunta 3,400) vulnerable community  to gradually reduce dependency on humanitarian aid and assistance, with a view to increase the economic capacity of the vulnerable community households and support local integration. Efforts will be made to reduce vulnerabilities, increase and diversify sources of income and prevent negative coping strategies. This project will apply a sustainable livelihoods approach focused on gaining productive assets while building capacities and coping strategies of vulnerable households. This approach recognises that individuals are active agents who make rational decisions and choices about their lives, and in response to social and economic change.  At the practical level, MC will actively involve and listen to the views of the participants and the wider community during the beneficiary selection. The various training opportunities provided under the project will support people to achieve their own livelihood goals, building where possible on their existing coping strategies. Increasing individuals’ access to financial services will enhance individual’s financial assets and increase their resilience to economic and social shocks and stressors. Importantly, this project recognises the significance of power relations that exist both within and between households and communities. Considering this, MC will ensure that 50 percent of all project beneficiaries are female community members. 
Key activities to realising this objective will include market driven vocational training; business start-up support through cash grants; Village Savings and Loans Association (VSLA) strengthening; and provision of improved vegetable seeds for farming.

project_name: Improved access to timely care and treatment of children suffering from malnutrition among displacements people in The Lake province, Chad
project_objective: This project aim to reduce the mortality and the mortality due to malnutrition by offering adequate treatment of severe acute malnutrition among for displacements people in The Lake province affected by the Nigerian crisis

project_name: Appui à la prévention de la malnutrition aigüe sévère à travers la mise en œuvre des activités WASH In Nut dans les provinces en situation d’urgence nutritionnelle
project_objective:
Dans le cadre de prévention de la malnutrition aigüe sévère et pour accompagner la prise en charge intégrée de la malnutrition (PCIMA), le programme WASH propose une réponse intégrée aux besoins 86,250 enfants (filles et garçons) de moins de 5 ans souffrants de la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS).
L’assistance WASH aux filles et aux garçons de moins de 5 ans souffrants de la MAS dans les zones prioritaires sera focaliser sur trois activités prioritaires conformément a la stratégie nationale WASH In Nut de 2017 révisée en 2018, 
Cette réponse multisectorielle vise à sauver les vies des 76,130 enfants MAS, représentant 51% de la cible du cluster WASH, et à améliorer leurs environnements ainsi que la résilience de leurs communautés et consiste à :
1-	Accompagnement des couples mère/accompagnant-enfant 
2-	Promotion des activités à base communautaire dans les zones de provenance des enfants MAS 
3-	Amélioration des conditions WASH les centre de nutrition (UNA/UNT)
Les provinces prioritaires qui seront couvertes par ce projet sont les provinces en situation d’urgence nutritionnelle suivante : Barh El Ghazel, Kanem, Salamat, Sila, Tibesti, Hadjer Lamis, Lac, Ndjamena
Les enfants, filles et garçons ainsi que les membres de leurs communautés y compris les hommes, les femmes et les personnes âgées seront assite selon leurs besoins spécifiques par les activités de ce projet qui visent 86,250 enfants de moins de 5 ans (43988 f et 42262g) et 172,500 personnes dont 67,275 Femmes (4485 âgées), 62,100 Hamme (4,140 âgés), 20,700 Garçons et 22,425 filles dont

project_name: Access to quality education to the children of Syria
Improve equitable access to preventive and curative services for under five years children, pregnant and lactating women in Syria
project_objective:
Under the Nutrition Humanitarian framework, this project aims to provide preventive and curative nutrition services for under five years children, pregnant and lactating women in Syria with a special focus in high risk areas and IDP camps inside Syria. The services will be delivered through fixed and mobile teams run by our implementing partners (IPs) which include Local and International NGO’s and Government health directorates. UNICEF will provide IPs with essential lifesaving nutrition supplies to treat and prevent malnutrition and prevent deaths among vulnerable children and women. Nutrition services will also focus on raising awareness among vulnerable mothers and care-givers on prevention of malnutrition, breast feeding and improving Infant Young Child Feeding practices. The project will also provide capacity building for health staff
and community volunteers to ensure quality service delivery. At the national level support will focus on strengthening the system to provide services through producing strategic documents (Nutrition Strategy, IYCF guidelines) and evidence generation to inform programming (e.g Nutrition surveillance, Iodine deficiency survey among school children 6-12 years).

project_name: Strengthening Child Protection Services including Risk Education and GBV for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria.
project_objective:
UNICEF Child Protection programme in line with the “No Lost Generation” framework will build on the investments of previous years to enhance equitable access to quality child protection services, including for children with disabilities, through two main intervention priorities: 1) Improving the quality of community-based child protection through behavior change and awareness raising on specific child protection risks & structured psychosocial support interventions for 415,000. 2) Expand  the reach & improve the quality of child protection specialized services for 22,000 child survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect & abuse (child laborers, child GBV survivors & unaccompanied or separated children) through case management  to address those critical needs & restore normalcy to the lives of children & 62,000 parents /caregivers provided parenting programmes to prevents  further distress & restores wellbeing &recovery from various violence they experienced/witnessed .
 UNICEF shall engage in strategies for direct services delivery through partnership with other actors & build capacity of actors & servicers providers to deliver comprehensive package of CP services based on minimum standards & IASC guidelines.  Furthermore, strengthen the capacity of 2,600 CP social workforce by training on core child protection areas including case management approach, conduct advocacy on critical or unprecedented issues & caseloads, evidence generation for better programming & multi-sectorial collaborations and coordination across sectors for comprehensive CP responses which addresses needs of most vulnerable children & their families. 
 UNICEF shall contribute to expanding availability & quality services for girls, boys, women & men in targeted locations prioritizing areas with greater needs in higher severity scale 3-6 focusing on children & women internally displaced in communal shelters, host communities & refugees in camps across the country ensuring prevention & response to needs of affected population, provision of equitable services delivery using static facilities & mobile services providers. 
Due to reported high contaminations of civil areas with explosive ordinances, over 10.2 million people are living in at risk communities and needs Risk education (RE) sessions to raise awareness on the dangers of explosive hazards to prevent incidents & accidents which would lead to injuries, maiming &even deaths of people unless correct preventive messages are disseminated to them. RE messages shall be provided to 2,380,000 people through both humanitarian actors & public service providers using both static facilities & mobile teams to reach populations most affected especially children, boys & men. UNICEF shall build capacity of 3,600 RE partners staffs to provide quality RE that is age, gender & disability appropriate. Furthermore, provide child victims assistances to mitigate negative impacts on their life & wellbeing to enable them realize their full potentials.
UNICEF in addressing Gender Based Violence (GBV) shall adopt holistic approach including conducting awareness raising to 287,000 people to prevent GBV through child friendly spaces & use of mobile teams in communities, provide case management services for 200 child survivors to address negative consequences of GBV, mitigate risks of GBV & build safer environments women, girls & boys. Complement rolling out of IASC Guidelines Integrating GBV into Humanitarian action across sectors ensuring responsiveness to needs of girls & boys.  Support Prevention of Sexual Exploitation & Abuse mechanisms to protect beneficiaries & build capacity humanitarian actors to address needs of the population in efficient, transparent and accountable manner.
The programme shall be implemented in close collaboration and coordination with other actors especially aligned to  protection sectors AoRs for mine action, GBV & Child Protection strategies & results framework. All standard adhere to delivery results

project_name: Providing critical life-saving GBV prevention and response activities to Crisis -affected women and girls in South Sudan
project_objective:
While the intensity of conflicts have shown a relative decline and clashes have been majorly contained in many regions of the country, the humanitarian situation continues to be critical with impacts spilling through 2020 further elevating the need for protection assistance with 805,535 as the target population for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) assistance according to the 2020 HRP.  Women and girls remain the priority groups targeted by GBV in emergency programming. Out of 805,535 people in need of GBV assistance, 386,657 (48%) are women and 418,878 (52%) are children. Of the total population identified for urgent humanitarian assistance, UNFPA estimates the number of women in the reproductive age group in the conflict-affected areas to be 231,384. Overall, UNFPA intends to reach 233,334, the majority (60%) of whom are adult women of reproductive age, 20% young women, 10% young males and 10% adult.

Gender-based violence (GBV) is one of the most pervasive human rights abuses.  GBV encompasses a wide range of violations, including rape, sexual assault, physical violence, emotional violence, denial of resources, services and opportunities, forced marriages (including early marriage) and other harmful practices. Vulnerability of women and girls to GBV in South Sudan is exacerbated by—and particularly acute in—the conflict crisis, where the “peacetime” risks of violence are compounded by the realities of the humanitarian situation, including years of conflict, displacement, breakdowns in particular social norms and protection mechanisms, changing roles within the family, famine, and cultural beliefs.  Following years of conflict and displacement, formal systems of protection and justice weakened and disrupted; separation of families and communities occurred, shock-absorbing capacities depleted putting women and girls at increased risk of multiple forms of GBV. GBV primarily affects women and girls, who represent 99 per cent of the reported incidents in the first half of 2019 as stated on the GBV IMS report.

UNFPA proposes to continue strengthening the provision of the on-going critical GBV in emergency programmatic interventions to crisis-affected populations by focusing on GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response services.  South Sudan remains in a severe humanitarian crisis due to the cumulative effects of years of conflict and violence against civilians. Nearly 4.5 million people have been forced out of their homes in search of safety and security. Within South Sudan, UNOCHA Situational report of October 2019 places the number of internally displaced people at 1.5 million.


Survivors of GBV need access to lifesaving medical, psychosocial, safety and legal services to meet their complex and multiple needs. The reduced access to essential and lifesaving reproductive health services coupled with the lack of basic items which respond to the hygiene and reproductive health needs of women and girls, make living very difficult for displaced women and girls to maintain acceptable hygiene standards which lead to discrimination, forcing girls in some instances to quit schools for fear of being stigmatized by their fellow boys and men. Displaced women and girls need basic items to interact comfortably in public and maintain their hygiene, particularly menstrual hygiene. Without access to culturally appropriate clothing and hygiene items, the mobility of women and girls is restricted, and their health might be compromised. Without certain items, women may be unable to seek essential social services, including humanitarian aid, which may increase their vulnerability to GBV.

project_name: Appui au rapatriement volontaire et a réalisation des possibilités d'intégration plus durable
project_objective:
Depuis 2013, les mouvements de rapatriement volontaire des femmes, filles, garçons et hommes réfugiés maliens continuent à être observés même si le HCR estime que les conditions pour un rapatriement organisé ne sont pas encore réunies du fait de la recrudescence de l’insécurité, la détérioration des infrastructures de base et l’absence des autorités étatiques dans certaines zones de retour. 
Au 31 octobre 2019, le gouvernement en collaboration avec le HCR a déjà enregistré plus de 74.390 femmes, filles, garçons et hommes réfugiés maliens. Pour l’année 2019, le chiffre de planification du retour des rapatries est de 12500 rapatries. 
Conformément aux dispositions des accords tripartites signés, des mécanismes doivent être mis en place pour assurer le suivi des rapatriés et garantir qu’ils ont recouvert leurs droits. Afin de permettre un rapatriement dans les conditions acceptables et de trouver des solutions à l’amélioration du rapatriement des réfugiés maliens, le HCR va continuer de maintenir la coordination transfrontalière avec les autorités des pays d’asile et celles du pays d’origine. En 2020, le HCR tiendra 12 réunions de commissions tripartites avec le Burkina Faso, la Mauritanie et le Niger (dont 6 au Mali) et 6 réunions transfrontalières (dont 3 au Mali). Ces réunions sont essentielles parce qu’elles s’inscrivent dans l’optique d’une coordination étroite et de partage d’information entre le Mali et les pays d’asile pour permettre aux femmes, filles, garçons et hommes réfugiés de prendre une décision libre et consentie sur leur rapatriement volontaire. Les réfugiés maliens avant de quitter les pays d’asile reçoivent le VRF et un viatique de USD 70 pour chaque femme, fille, garçon et homme pour assurer les coûts de transport. Au Mali, le viatique est complété par une somme de USD 130 pour les adultes et USD 70 pour les enfants. Cette intervention en espece aux rapatriés femmes, filles, garçons et hommes leur évite de devoir vendre leurs maigres ressources pour se procurer de l’argent nécessaire afin de répondre aux besoins de base. Conformement aux standards du HCR, quatre (4) semaine apres chaque distribution, une post distribution monitoring est organisee afin d’ evaluer le niveau d’atteinte des résultats immédiats attendus, comprendre l’usage  que les bénéficiaires font de cette assistance, apprécier le niveau de satisfaction  que les ménages en tirent, analyser la satisfaction des besoins sectoriels grâce à l’intervention du HCR, apprendre globalement du projet, notamment sur l’approche et la qualité de la mise en œuvre et collecter les suggestions d’amélioration des parties prenantes, pour des interventions futures.
Les PDIs, Retournés, Rapatriés et une tranche de communautés hôtes impactées par la crise de déplacements spontanés, et facilité sur laquelle les localités prioritaires indiquées déterminent la gravité de la situation et de façon inclusive. L'implication effective des acteurs étatiques, des partenaires locaux et des partenaires de développement dans les abris / NFI, les activités de protection et d'assistance, ainsi que dans les structures de coordination (pôle Protection, pôle Logement) doit être renforcée. L'intégration effective de la protection dans les projets humanitaires reste également un aspect important à renforcer. Les composantes sont l'assistance en BNA, le Cash et Nexus. 
La situation securitaire et humanitaire de plus en plus precaire aux zones des trois frontières - Niger - Mali - Burkina Faso ( https://www.humanitarianresponse.info/en/operations/niger/protection) affecte la qualité de l’asile accordée aux réfugiés maliens vivant au Burkina Faso et au Niger. Au cours du dernier trimestre 2019, le HCR a enregistré les intentions de rapatriement de pres de 10000 refugies vivant dans les camps et zones d’accueil situés tout au long de cette bande frontaliere. En 2020, cet engouement devrait se poursuivre, d’où la necessité de mettre en place ce projet.

project_objective:
