project_name: APPUI A LA PREVENTION ET A LA PRISE EN CHARGE INTEGREE DE LA MALNUTRITION AIGUE SEVERE AU MALI
Protéger les enfants touchés par le conflit armé et COVID-19 au Mali
project_objective:
Les enfants comptent parmi les premières victimes du conflit. L'exposition à la violence, la perte ou la séparation de leurs proches et le déplacement ont un impact significatif sur leur bien-être et développement. De nombreux enfants dans les zones touchées par le conflit ne disposent pas d’accès aux services publics tels que la santé et l’éducation notamment parce qu'ils n’ont pas d’acte de naissance.  La pandémie de COVID-19 a exacerbé les facteurs de risque des enfants déjà vulnérables, alors que l'accès aux enfants dans le besoin devient plus difficile.  
Le projet vise à protéger les droits des enfants dans les zones les plus touchées par le conflit au Mali, en fournissant aux enfants les services d’appui médical, psychosocial et de réintégration nécessaire pour atténuer les effets négatifs à long terme. 
L’objectif spécifique est d’offrir des services de protection et de réinsertion en faveur de 300 enfants sortis des forces et groupes armés et 700 enfants non accompagnés et séparés, y compris à cause de la COVID19, pour la prise en charge transitoire holistique (médicale, psychosociale, alimentaire, vestimentaire) et l’appui à la réintégration socio-économique. En outre, 190,000 enfants affectés par les conflits ou la COVID19 recevront un soutien psychosocial, individuel ou à base communautaire dans des espaces sécurisés.  
L'UNICEF veillera à ce que 500 violations graves des droits de l’enfant par les parties au conflit soient documentées, vérifiées et rapportées en étroite collaboration avec la MINUSMA et d’autres membres du Groupe de Travail National sur le MRM. Les nombre de violations graves des droits de l’enfant (meurtre et la mutilation, le recrutement par les forces et groupes armés, viol et autres formes de violence sexuelle, enlèvement, attaques/occupation contre des écoles et des hôpitaux et déni d’accès humanitaire) est en augmentation significative avec la dégradation du conflit au centre du Mali. 
Le projet vise également 400 survivants de VBG/EAS dans les zones touchées par la crise, où les personnes deviennent plus vulnérables à la violence sexuelle, aux abus et à l'exploitation avec les mouvements de la population, et la COVID19. Ils recevront une assistance holistique (soutien médicale et psychosociale, réintégration socio-économique selon leurs propres besoins). En outre, 40 000 membres des communautés touchées par la crise seront sensibilisés sur la protection des enfants de la violence, le signalement des violations et la réponse aux enfants affectés.
15.000 enfants dépourvus certificats de naissance recevront une aide pour l'obtenir par le biais des campagnes d’information et de sensibilisation dans les zones touchées par le conflit et COVID-19, ainsi que par une évaluation des enfants non enregistrés. L’UNICEF collaborera étroitement avec les partenaires gouvernementaux ainsi que les agents de l’état civil pour assurer que leurs capacités soient développées. 
En répondant aux besoins des enfants les plus vulnérables, ce projet garantira que les enfants, le futur du pays, seront protégés et pourront ainsi contribuer à la paix et au développement durable en assurant leur dignité et leur accès aux services nécessaires. La redevabilité vis-à-vis des communautés ciblées sera intégrée aux activités, y compris via un mécanisme de plainte. Outre les activités spécifiques visant à traiter directement la réponse et la prévention de l'exploitation et l'abus sexuelle (EAS), tous les partenaires d’exécution recevront une formation sur la PSEA conformément à la stratégie de l’UNICEF concernant l’évaluation des partenaires récemment introduite. 
Tous les partenaires d’exécution du projet mettront en œuvre les activités selons le SOP dans le contexte de COVID-19 avec la capacité et l'équipement appropriés. 25,000 personnes (partenaires étatiques et non-étatiques, acteurs communautaires, etc.) seront sensibilisées sur la COVID-19.

project_name: Assurer une continuité éducative aux enfants affectes par la crise sécuritaire et la pandémie de COVID-19
project_objective:
La situation éducative demeure préoccupante dans les zones affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions du nord et centre du pays. Dans ces régions, les infrastructures, le matériel et les ressources éducatives sont la cible de fréquentes attaques et menaces. Au mois de mars 2020, 1,261 écoles étaient fermées à cause de l’insécurité, ce qui représente une nette augmentation par rapport à la rentrée scolaire 2019-2020, en octobre, qui comptait 1 051 écoles fermées (ce qui représentait déjà une augmentation par rapport à la fin de l’année scolaire avec 920 écoles fermées). Plus de 378,000 élèves et 7,500 enseignants sont affectés par ces fermeture. Les écoles du Nord et du Centre disposent de moyens insuffisants : classes surchargées lorsqu’elles sont ouvertes, enseignants volontaires pour pallier l’absence des enseignants titulaires, équipements réduits, qualité de l’enseignement insuffisante notamment en raison du manque de formations etc. 
La pandémie de COVID-19 est venue donner un coup d’arrêt aux efforts pour la réouverture des écoles et la mise en place d’offres alternatives d’éducation. Le gouvernement a décidé de fermer toutes les écoles à partir du 19 mars pour une durée initiale de 3 semaines, prolongée d’un mois. Début mai, le gouvernement annonçait la réouverture des écoles pour les classes d’examen le 2 juin, alors que toutes les autres écoles restaient fermées jusqu’à nouvel ordre.
Dans ce contexte, tous les enfants scolarisés et tous les enseignants sont affectés (environ 3.8M d’enfants et 90,000 enseignants. 
2 millions d’enfants en dehors de l’école n’ont plus accès à des possibilités d’intégration scolaire et toutes les activités de réponse humanitaire dans le domaine de l’éducation planifiées n’ont pu être menées (affectant directement les 565,000 enfants et enseignants dans le besoin).
Pour le reste de l’année 2020, l’UNICEF continuera à suivre la stratégie d’intervention pour répondre aux besoins humanitaires en éducation des enfants tout en prenant en compte les effets de la pandémie de COVID-19 et de la fermeture de toutes les écoles. UNICEF continuera à se focaliser sur les enfants affectés par la fermeture des écoles (insécurité) et les déplacements de population mais en ajoutant les besoins et en adaptant la stratégie et les modalités de réponse en lien avec le COVID-19.
Activités
Promouvoir l'accès à une éducation formelle et non formelle de qualité y compris à travers l’éducation à distance pour 500,000 enfants (240,000 garçons et 260,000 filles) dans les zones touchées par le conflit et le COVID-19: Koulikoro, Ségou, Mopti, Tombouctou, Taoudéni, Gao, Ménaka et Kidal et certaines zones touchées seulement par le COVID-19 : Kayes et Sikasso.
La mobilisation communautaire en faveur de la réouverture des écoles fermées notamment par la mise en place des cadres de concertation au niveau local regroupant les communautés et leurs leaders religieux et traditionnels avec l’implication des Comités de Gestion Scolaire et Associations des parents d’élèves dans la réouverture des écoles. 
Promouvoir le 500 dialogue communautaire et la mobilisation sociale (à travers la radio et les sessions présentielles) et adapter l'offre d'éducation à la demande des communautés par le biais de stratégies éducatives alternatives telles que les Medersas, les espaces d'apprentissage temporaires, PAASU, etc.
UNICEF vise à créer 500 Centres d’Apprentissage Communautaire (y inclus Medersa) afin de mitiger la situation des enfants en dehors du système scolaire dû à l’insécurité. Ces activités seront adaptées au contexte COVID en incluant notamment le soutien de l’éducation à distance et le retour à l’école au sein des sessions de mobilisation communautaire et en réduisant le nombre d’enfants par espaces / salles de classe pour respecter les mesures de protection contre la maladie. Le ratio 1/30 (enseignant/élevés) est le taux standard de la classe pour l’UNICEF dans le contexte de COVID19. Utiliser des stratégies novatrices.

project_name: Improving Economic and Climatic Resilience of Vulnerable Communities in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
Targeting: The project primarily addresses the impact of the refugee crisis on the livelihoods and natural resource base of 49,711 unserved beneficiaries (of which, 48% women) comprised of 9,038 farming households of the host communities in the targeted areas (FSS ReportHub). The project aims to provide inputs and innovative technology support that will develop and promote productive and climate smart technologies, which will enhance farm profitability and household incomes.  Moreover, the capacity building support to the public and private extension agents will enhance the GOB’s efforts to integrate nutrition-sensitive and gender-inclusive agricultural extension services to the targeted communities. FAO will continue to support the actors of the Food Security Sector, through its role as co-chair of the Livelihoods Working Group, to improve the targeting of all of the humanitarian response and development actors in 2020.    
                                                                                                                                                                  Approaches to Food and Nutrition Security: For food security and nutrition enhancement, FAO has identified two distinct approaches for achieving the FSS JRP 2020 outcome one: (1) The first approach targets individual, marginal and smallholder farmers and groups that are not currently in a viable position to enter into commercial farming.  This approach focuses on food diversity and nutrition awareness amongst the poorest households. These farmers will receive appropriate inputs and technical support to increase farm production and household income. (2) The second approach targets agricultural groups with higher potential for commercial or collective production. These farmer groups will see investments in their technical capacity to benefit from the ongoing market expansion due to the increased demand. Increased local farmer incomes will contribute to social cohesion in areas around the camps. 

Women and Markets: In addition, the project will work closely with the public and private sectors to identify market opportunities and strategies to expand crop production into new and underdeveloped areas with the potential to increase household incomes, improve nutrition and contribute to greater economic empowerment of women.  

DRR and Environmental Rehabilitation: One of the main environmental issues has been widespread deforestation due to the collection of firewood as a source of fuel to cook food. More than 2 000 hectares (5 000 acres) of stripped forest area has been severely damaged. Water resources have also been put under considerable pressure and are a source of social conflict between the Refugee and host communities.  FAO will continue to address the increased vulnerability to landslides and floods and play a major role in coordinating host community needs through its role as co-chair of the Energy and Environment Technical Working Group.

The project aims to work closely with government and non-government partners, including other UN agencies, to promote erosion control and watershed management strategies, and to identify areas vulnerable to landslides in achieving outcome two.  Land stabilization and reforestation activities are planned for 500 hectares of degraded lands inside and outside the camps are designed to contribute to the immediate protection of communities by reducing risks of flash flooding and landslides.  The restored tree cover will also help to recharge ground water and protect from cyclone wind damage. The effects of the last two-year’s plantation efforts are already proving effective in this regard.  

Accountability to Affected Participants: FAO will continue to utilize its existing internal systems of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) to ensure that all activities incorporate measures of information sharing and recognition of vulnerable groups, as well as grievance gathering and address.

project_name: Emergency assistance to vulnerable households of Bedouin communities in the Gaza Strip to prepare them for harsh weather conditions
project_objective: The proposed action is based on the 2018-2020 HRP Strategic Objective 2 ” The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under International Humanitarian Law” and Strategic Objective 3 ” The capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”. The project aims at providing emergency support and winterization assistance to vulnerable Bedouin communities living in the Gaza Strip. Bedouin communities are among the most vulnerable communities living in the Gaza Strip. Most of them live in temporary houses built out of metallic sheets which are not suitable to stand harsh weather conditions. They lack basic infrastructure and services, such as electricity, water and sewage networks. With the help of the local partner, PARC, the project will increase the access to safe and secure shelters for vulnerable Bedouin households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns in the Gaza Strip. It will enhance the households’ capacity to cope with the risk of deterioration of living conditions by improving their shelter standards. In total, 450 HHs will be assisted with winterization assistance and NFI. A total of 2,673 beneficiaries (2,565 people befitting from shelter intervention, 90 volunteers and 18 Community-based Protection Committee's members) will benefit from the project.

project_name: Emergency response to improve the access to public WASH facilities for the most vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
This project implemented by Action Against Hunger (AAH) will support vulnerable families in the Gaza Strip (GS) (including women, men, children (boys and girls), elderly) who suffer from a shortage of domestic water and are prone to stormwater/wastewater floods during emergencies to ensure their safe access to the basic WASH services. The aim of this project is to reduce the negative impacts of public health risks associated with poor water quality, poor wastewater collection and treatment, lack of stormwater infrastructure and lack of proper hygiene practices. Interventions (meeting the Strategic Objectives 1, 2 and 3 and WASH Cluster Strategic Objective 1) will focus on sustainable domestic water supply, basic sanitation and proper winterization preparedness to mitigate the harsh winter weather and flooding. The recurrent flooding poses a threat of contamination of sources of water and of overflowing of the sewage systems, increasing the risk of waterborne disease. 
Under the proposed intervention, Action Against Hunger (AAH) will support the targeted communities with emergency preparedness service contract (operating) for conducting critical emergency repairs for WASH facilities and will carry out electrotechnical repairs for critical WASH facilities prone to stormwater floods. 
Public awareness campaigns will be organised to address hygiene practice issues at the household level to improve the capacity the families in the targeted locations to effectively respond to emergencies. 
AAH will advocate to support the service provider to overcome operation and maintenance obstacles (lack of financial resources, lack of spare parts and shortage of fuel of emergency uses).
The proposed intervention ensures protection mainstreaming as it is guided by protection principles and is taking into account safety and dignity; meaningful access; accountability as well as participation (through regular meetings, focus group discussions and workshops throughout the project) and empowerment.

project_name: PREVENT WATER-BORNE DISEASE OUTBREAK AND IMPROVE WATER QUALITY BY DISINFECTION OF WATER RESOURCES IN THE GAZA STRIP
project_objective:
The project aims at providing the entire population of Gaza, including women, men, boys and girls of all age groups with access to safe drinking and domestic water that is free from biological contamination by ensuring over 99% disinfection efficiency of all water system in the Gaza Strip for six months until CMWU are able to secure additional resources in future. This includes: 284 water wells, 55 water reservoirs, 26 water lifting and booster stations, 2,987 km of water networks and carrier lines, 48 small-medium sized brackish water desalination plants (50m3/day to 1000m3/day), and three connections of Mekorot water supply across the Green Line with Israel with average total annual supply capacity of 10MCM.
These water facilities are distributed across 25 municipalities of five governorates and will all be targeted in this project except for the two seawater desalination plants as they have special arrangements and already covered by disinfection materials and chlorine. 

This will be achieved through the following set of activities: 
ACTIVITY #1: Supply sufficient quantities of the following water disinfection materials/chemicals:
- Sodium-Hypo chlorite-(10-12%active Chlorine) for water disinfection of all water facilities (284 Water wells and desalination plants and water networks)  
- Hydrochloric Acid 33% for 48 desalination plants
- Caustic Soda 50% for 48 desalination plants
- Anti-fouling Agent, Antiscalant, Sodium Hexa meta Phosphate 40% for 48 desalination plants
- Sodium Metabisulfite for 48 desalination plants

The provision of these chemicals is essential to the operation of the desalination plants, and contributes significantly to the improvement of water quality for women, men, boys and girls in Gaza.
Human Appeal will procure the above items and devise a delivery plan in consultation with CMWU to ensure its adequate and efficient use for water distribution, and the operation of 284 water wells and public desalination plants. Chlorine and chemicals will be procured from private sector without the need for prior coordination; as they are not 'dual use' materials.

Supplied quantities of water disinfection materials will be sufficient for period of six months during which CMWU will continue to secure resources needed to cover the rest of the year. 
ACTIVITY #2: Carry out regular and consistent water quality testing for six months
Samples from 580 locations across the Gaza Strip will be tested for water quality and/or residual chlorine level on a monthly basis to monitor water quality & ensure safe water delivery to the population of Gaza. All test results will be logged into the monitoring database to inform actions required for water safety plans.
ACTIVITY # 3: Supply spare parts, equipment and maintenance necessary for water disinfection systems
Regular preventive and corrective maintenance will be conducted for all water disinfection systems in the water facilities across the Gaza Strip and any faulty chlorinators, disinfection dosing pumps or other parts will be replaced to ensure effective functioning of the water disinfection system. This will be carried out through: 
Provision of chlorinators and its associated spare parts for the operation and maintenance of 284 water wells in the Gaza strip;
EXPECTED OUTPUTS: 
OUTPUTS:
Output 1.1
• 540 M3 of Chlorine is delivered to all water facilities (wells, reservoirs, networks, and booster pumps) across the Gaza Strip
• 10 Tons of Hydrochloric Acid 33% are delivered to water desalination plants in the Gaza Strip
• 30 Tons of Caustic Soda are delivered to all desalination plants in the Gaza Strip
• 50 Tons of Antiscalant 40% delivered to 48 public desalination plants across the Gaza Strip
Output 2.1
• At least 580 monthly water quality tests are performed for water facilities from all across the Gaza Strip
Output 3.1
• 90% of disinfection systems in 284 municipal water wells are maintained  
• Essential spare parts for water disinfection systems are delivered

project_name: Home Upgrading for Vulnerable Households Headed by Women
project_objective:
The Home Upgrading for Vulnerable Households Headed by Women  in the Gaza Strip is a twelve months project aims at supporting vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns to meet their basic needs and enhance their coping capacity. The project comes in line with HRP strategic objectives 2,3, and in accordance with the Shelter and NFIs Cluster Objective 2.The project will target 200 women-headed households living in substandard housing conditions whom are at risk of exposure to extreme weather and protection concerns identified by SIF annual assessment and updated of the data base of orphans sponsored households of in August 2018. SIF also, conducted a rapid shelter assessment with focus on summarization and winterization elements on 2nd September 2019 targeting a sample of 62 HHs identified by the annual assessment as living in poor shelter condition. The assessment found a need for urgent shelter upgrading intervention in 2020. These households are at risk of exposure to extreme weather conditions and living below shelter minimum standards.
The project has been designed in accordance with the SIF extensive experience in the field and in close consultation with beneficiaries as well as the shelter cluster to support families with the needed urgent summerization rehabilitation works such as replacing or rehabilitating of roofs made of metal or asbestos sheets, fixing or replacing windows and doors for bathrooms and bedrooms to maintain privacy, closing holes in the houses walls for safety and weather protection, maintaining basic WASH facilities and electrical network and installing renewable power supply system to improve coping capacity of the families during the summer season and electricity cuts. Based on actual need and priority, each HH will receive an individualized rehabilitation plan corresponding to the specific needs of their shelter and beneficiary preferences in order to make it comply with summerization minimum standards. SIF project through rehabilitating of metal roofs and broken windows and doors as well as installing emergency power energy will contribute to improve the Gender-Age and GBV related concerns as well as protection at the household’s level by increasing the privacy and designate more space for specific gender and age group and children. 
The project will apply contracting approach as the contractor will furnish all skilled workers, materials, equipment, and tools to complete the work in compliance with the required quality and in timely manner

project_name: Assistance alimentaire non conditionnelle aux réfugiés congolais dans les camps au Burundi.
project_objective:
Le Burundi compte près de 86 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d'asile, dont 99% originaires de la République démocratique du Congo. La plupart des réfugiés congolais résidant au Burundi ont fui la violence dans la région du Sud-Kivu de RDC. Malgré les élections apaisées de 2019 en RDC, la sécurité à l’Est de ce pays reste précaire pour donner espoirs à des retours massifs aux réfugiés dont certains ont déjà fait plus de 10 ans dans le pays. La purulence des groupes rebelles et l’intensification des activités de ratissage par l’armée congolaise maintiennent la région dans un climat de tension et d’insécurité qui n’offre pas encore des espoirs palpables de retours. 
Le dernier JAM de 2019 estime que rien n'indique que le flux de réfugiés diminuera durant l’année 2020 avec des effectifs globaux pouvant atteindre jusqu’à 100 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile.
Au cours de l’année 2020, le PAM apportera une assistance alimentaire régulière toute l’année à une population d’environ 55 000 réfugiés dont environ 49 000 sont déjà dans les 5 camps (Kinama, Musasa, Bwagiriza, Kavumu et Nyankanda) dans les provinces de Ngozi, Muyinga, Cankuzo et Ruyigi.  
En l’absence d’opportunités pour développer des activités de subsistance propre (pas d’accès à la terre, pas d’opportunité de cash, communautés hôtes vulnérables), les réfugiés ne comptent que sur l’assistance alimentaire pour leur survie.
Une des recommandations du dernier JAM 2019 est que le PAM devrait veiller à ce que le panier alimentaire respecte la ration énergétique minimale recommandée de 2100 kcal et assurer son approvisionnement régulier (mensuel). 
L’objectif de ce projet d’assistance alimentaire aux réfugiés vise à assurer la survie de 55 000 congolais vivant dans 5 camps pendant toute l’année 2020. 
L’assistance alimentaire comprendra un montant en cash pour des compléments nutritionnels à travers l’achat des vivres frais (légumes et autres).
D’après le JAM 2019, les gaps de financement auraient des conséquences néfastes en raison d’une situation déjà précaire dans les camps, dont : 
•	Manque de Supercereal qui est essentiel pour atteindre l'apport quotidien recommandé.
•	Panier alimentaire réduit de 2120 kcal par personne et par jour à 1932 kcal, (contre 2100 kcal apport journalier recommandé).
•	Déjà en 2019, l’insuffisance des financements a privé les réfugiés du montant de cash destiné à l’achat des vivres frais pour le supplément nutritionnel.
•	Les problèmes de financement en 2019 déjà ont contribué à la réduction du nombre de réfugiés ayant un score de consommation alimentaire acceptable (de 83% en 2017 à 67% en 2018), les femmes chefs de famille étant touchées de manière disproportionnée, une réduction de 81% à 54%.
•	Aussi déjà en 2019, la malnutrition chronique est élevé  chez les enfants en raison des lacunes nutritionnelles à Kinama (47%), Kavumu (52%), Musasa (38%) et Bwagiriza (37%).

project_name: Colombia - World Food Programme
Ecuador - Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society
Emergency Cash for Work
project_objective:
The current socioeconomic conditions compounded by the blockade, energy crisis, salary cuts for PA employees and the ongoing impacts of the Great March of Return demonstrations are affecting all aspects of life in Gaza. As a result of such deteriorating living conditions, UNRWA saw a threefold increase in the number of new applications for its Cash for Work (CfW) programme in 2019, increasing the current average waiting time for a family to receive a short-term job opportunity to more than four years.  Soaring rates of unemployment and weak income are key drivers to poverty and food insecurity among the population.
In line with Strategic Objective 3 of the HRP i.e. supporting the capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, and the response approach of the Food Security Sector (FSS) i.e. assisting households with limited access to income opportunities, UNRWA, through its CfW programme, aims to support Palestine refugees in Gaza coping with protracted threats and shocks, and mitigate food insecurity through offering short term employment opportunities to approximately 14,000 poor Palestine refugees (equivalent to 79,800 total beneficiaries considering the average household size of 5.7 members). These will be equal to more than 1,430,000 work days, and will inject over US$ 17,6 million into households, generating almost 5,000 full time job equivalents (FTEs). The short term job opportunities will include more than 10,000 unskilled positions, more than 3,800 skilled positions and around 170 professional positions. In order to ensure gender access to these opportunities, UNRWA will aim to provide 40 per cent of skilled and professional job opportunities to women. CfW positions will be located in a number of locations throughout Gaza, including UNRWA installations, partner Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and other service-providers.

project_name: Emergency Health and MHPSS
project_objective:
The ongoing Great March of Return (GMR) demonstrations further deteriorated the health sector in Gaza, on top of the devastated socioeconomic conditions compounded by the blockade, energy crisis, salary cuts for PA employees; high unemployment and volatile security situation in Gaza. 

The public hospitals are overstretched with urgent treatments for GMR related cases, and expanding the capacity of the health services to absorb increasing needs is necessary to ensure access of vulnerable population to health services. Furthermore, the people in Gaza are in need of psycho-social support to cope with the impact of current and potential man-made and natural disasters. Meanwhile, the Agency's ability to respond to emergency health needs in Gaza is greatly constrained by the tight funding situation compromising its ability to respond as needed.

In light of these conditions, this proposed intervention aims to support the provision of critical healthcare for Palestine refugees in the Gaza Strip through (1) supporting health interventions received outside UNRWA facilities, (2) expanding the healthcare services within UNRWA facilities by providing lifesaving medicines and hiring emergency surged staff to cope with increasing demand, (3) providing necessary assistive tools to children in need, and (4) providing mental health and psycho-social support especially women as well as trauma and GMR-affected cases.

project_name: GP/HLP - Enhancing the protective environment for individuals and communities affected by conflict and displacement in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Given the ongoing protection crisis in South Sudan, DRC will continue to work with individuals affected by conflict and displacement, and other relevant stakeholders to enhance the protective environment of individuals and communities, and identify, prevent and address protection risks. Overall, the project will target a total of 120,000 IDPs, returnees, and host communities. The main objectives of the project, aligned with the Protection Cluster objectives, are: 
- Enhance protection assessment and monitoring to inform protection and overall humanitarian response. 
- Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience.
- Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other affected populations. 
- Ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialised services through an integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, boys, and girls in hard to reach and priority geographical areas. 
The project is designed to alleviate suffering of the most vulnerable individuals, and ensure safety and well-being of conflict-affected communities are prioritised and achieved. The project will focus on three main components: 
-	Protection analysis and advocacy: DRC will focus on protection data collection and analysis to ensure an in-depth understanding of the protection environment, allowing for appropriate prevention and response activities. In parallel, DRC will ensure protection concerns are captured in protection information products, such as assessment reports, monitoring reports, and protection snapshots, allowing for appropriate and relevant advocacy with the clusters, humanitarian partners, and other main stakeholders. DRC protection programming will ensure evidence-driven interventions, at the individual and community levels, ensuring appropriate and principled action is taken to prevent and respond to protection risks. 
- Protection risk prevention: DRC will continue to work closely with communities, particularly existing community structures, and vulnerable groups and individuals, to identify protection risks, coping strategies, community and individual intentions, and resilience among the affected population. DRC will work with community-based protection networks, facilitate focus group discussions, awareness raising, trainings on human rights and protection mainstreaming, and establish community-driven action plans, aiming to prevent and mitigate identified protection risks. 
- Protection response: DRC provides tailored protection responses to individuals at risk and communities affected by violence and displacement. The responses include community-based protection monitoring and referrals, individual protection assistance (IPA), case management, and mobile responses, identification and support to vulnerable individuals at risk, psychosocial support, service mapping and referrals, community based protection networks, and other necessary interventions based on needs in various locations, such as housing land and property (HLP) and legal aid. 
DRC’s approach in South Sudan is both through static presence (mainly in Upper Nile and Unity States) and mobile teams, who rove throughout the country based on new shocks and movements of populations. In Unity State, DRC forms part of a group of agencies implementing the “Beyond Bentiu Response” strategy, which aims at assessing locations beyond the Bentiu POC, and providing services to hard-to-reach communities in different counties. DRC adopts an integrated approach, linking general protection and HLP with sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) prevention and response, food security and livelihood (FSL), shelter and non-food items (SNFIs) and camp coordination and camp management (CCCM). DRC will continue to engage with other humanitarian partners and the relevant clusters to coordination and ensure aid effectiveness, as well as focus on mainstreaming protection.

project_name: FSL: To increase the food security and livelihoods of conflict affected households in South Sudan
project_objective:
The overall goal of the intervention is to provide emergency food assistance and livelihood support to protect lives, alleviate suffering and to improve people’s living standards. This will be achieved through building resilience by increasing household (HH) positive coping strategies and providing them with tools to recover from crisis and shocks. 

The proposed FSL activities have been designed to improve the food security of people living in IPC 3 and higher locations by increasing access and availability of food, HH purchasing power by distributing agricultural inputs, provision of cash based interventions (CBI), and encouraging resilience through the support of income generating activities (IGA) and skills trainings. 

DRC aims to reduce the negative impact on the environment, and to foster local-level, sustainable solutions that build resilience, food security and livelihood development through a circular bio-economy approach. DRC will advocate for and train people on the use of climate-smart agricultural techniques (CSA). All projects have been linked with information campaigns and trainings, and key topics across all areas will include environmental, protection and gender mainstreaming.

DRC vision is to provide a dignified life for all people affected by displacement. As such, DRC Food Security and Livelihood (FSL) activities are sectorial inter-linked with Protection [(including sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV)] and Armed Violence Reduction (AVR) response.

project_name: Amélioration de l’accès aux soins de santé primaires et de référence aux populations vulnerables ( réfugiés, deplacés internes, retournés et population hote) dans les  districts sanitaires dans 3 régions du Niger (Diffa, Tillaberi, Tahoua).
project_objective: L’action de ce projet vise à réduire la morbidité, la mortalité et la fragilité excédentaires liées aux urgences de santé publique suite aux conséquences de crises multiples dans les zones frontalières en crise (Diffa, Tahoua et Tillaberi) au Niger, grâce à l'amélioration de l’accès aux soins de santé primaires et de référence aux populations vulnerables ( deplacés internes, retournés et population hote) dans les  districts sanitaires de 3 régions affectées. Ce projet est en lien avec les objectifs stratégiques n°2 et 3 du HRP 2020 en rapport avec l'amélioration des conditions de vie et la restauration des moyens de subsistance d'au moins 58% de personnes dans le besoin ainsi que le sauvetage et la préservation de la vie et la dignité de 1,3 millions de personnes affectées par les conséquences humanitaires liées au bien-être physique et mental, à travers la fourniture de services préventifs, promotionnels et curatifs multisectoriels d’ici fin 2020. Il répond aussi aux objectifs spécifiques et du cluster santé retenus pour 2020. La situation sécuritaire reste précaire au Niger et marquée par des attaques répétées, dans la région de Diffa, le long du périmètre des trois frontières Mali-Burkina Faso-Niger et des tensions intercommunautaires impliquant du côté du Niger cinq (5) départements (Ouallam, Banibangou, Abala, Ayorou et Bankilaré) de la région de Tillaberi et deux (2) départements (Tassara et Tillia) de la région de Tahoua et dans les différents départements de la région de Diffa. Suite à la persistance des menaces terroristes et de groupes armés non étatiques, l'état d'urgence a été régulièrement et systématiquement étendu à douze (12) départements en décembre 2018, couvrant dix départements (10) dans la région de Tillaberi et deux (2) dans la région de Tahoua. L'état d'urgence déclaré a interdit l'utilisation de la moto dans lesdits départements, a instauré un couvre-feu à partir de 19h00 pour les véhicules, et à partir de 22h00 pour les piétons.  Depuis mai 2019, la région de Maradi, dans le département de Guidan Roumdjii, accueille des réfugiés des États de Sokoto et Zamfara au Nigeria, situés entre 500 mètres et trois kilomètres de la frontière. Pour faire face à la situation évoquée si haut et répondre aux besoins en santé dans ces 3 régions affectées, ce projet se propose principalement de: (i) Appuyer à la continuité de la gratuité des soins  pour toutes les populations vulnérables y compris le renforcement prise en charge intégrée des maladies de l’enfant (PCIME) dans les districts sanitaires affectés, la prise en charge des complication des MAS chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans, (ii) Appuyer à l'amélioration de l'accès aux soins pour les populations vulnérables par les cliniques mobiles dans la région de Diffa, (iii) Apporter un appui aux soins de santé primaires et de référence pour les populations vulnérables de la région de Diffa,(iv)Assurer la formation du personnel de santé en matière de gestion des risques sanitaires courants  et des risques de catastrophes en santé, (v) Pré-positionner des Kits sanitaires d'urgence interangences (IEHK), en kits traumatologiques et autres médicaments essentiels/équipements médicaux de base, dans les districts sanitaires affectés par les crises,(vi) Organiser des campagnes de vaccination contre la rougeole pour les enfants dans les zones de déplacement (vii)  Rendre opérationnel les centres de santé non fonctionnels dans le milieu du retour par la réaffectation du personnel et dotation des médicaments essentiels .

project_name: Assurer l'accès à une formation professionalisante de qualité à 3000 adolescents (filles/garçons) dans les deux régions affectées par les effets de la crise malienne (Tahoua et Tillabéri)

Ce projet permetttra la formation des formateurs sur plusieurs thématiques, l'achat des intrants pédagogiques, le paiement des formateurs, la mise à disposition de kits post formation pour l'insertion à travers la mise en place de groupements d'intérêt économique gérés par les sortants pour faciliter l'auto-empli.

project_name: UNHCR Refugee Response Plan for Sudan
project_objective:
Despite the recent positive developments in the establishment of a transitional gov., it is expected that Sudan will continue to face severe macro-economic and political challenges. Overall, the situation remains fluid and humanitarian needs will further increase as underlying challenges are not expected to change in the immediate future. The humanitarian situation in Sudan will remain a complex mix of asylum-seekers and refugees. Sudan is also a source, transit and destination country for mixed migratory population movements. Continued small to medium scale refugee influxes from CAR, SS, Eritrea are anticipated in 2020. Sudan hosts over 900,000 ref. from over 7 countries within the region, in addition to hosting refugees asylum seekers on the move and irregular migrants as Sudan is a transit country using the East African North-bound migratory route. The eastern part of the country is the main entry point for Eritrean asylum-seekers although about 63% move on before finalization of their asylum applications. The voluntary return sustainable solutions for the issues of displaced persons and refugees” are prioritized among the “essential issues for peace negotiations” agreed upon the Constitutional Charter for the 2019 Transitional Period, signed in 17 Aug.19 agreeing on transitional arrangements for the forthcoming 39 months. The aim of the Constitutional declaration is to “end the war by addressing the roots of the Sudanese problem and handling its effects”. It envisages the completion of a fair and comprehensive peace in the Sudan no later than 6months from its signing. As of Nov.19, peace negotiations between the Gov. of Sudan armed groups are ongoing with yet to be determined outcomes. Areas of origin in Sudan have been affected by years of conflict, marginalization and neglect. They often lack basic community infrastructure essential social services, while rural livelihoods were seriously disrupted. Competition for, and pressures on, natural resources within Darfur, partly due to a history of drought and famine, compound the legacy of the conflict. Communities usually lack resources, structures governance capabilities allowing for different groups, youth, to engage collectively in peacebuilding, dialogue, public service, economic activities. 
 BNS. Although Sudan has not formally committed to the CRRF yet, the country has de-factor applied several components of the CRRF. 

Operational priorities in 2020 are: 

1. Refugee protection, with a focus on ref. registration, documentation, protection monitoring and interventions, CP 
 SGBV, CBP, scaling up CBIs for ref. (MP sectoral). 

2. Voluntary return; durable solutions for refugees hosted by Sudan. 

3. Stabilization of existing ref. populations through transition from emergency response to longer term interventions, including integration with national service systems in the spirit of the CRRF, and interim solutions for populations in Khartoum Open Areas.

4. Emergency preparedness for refugee influxes, and sudden onset emergencies (Cholera) through enhanced protection capacity, pre-positioning, the management of the Common NFI Pipeline of the Humanitarian Country Team.

project_name: Améliorer notre réponse collective à une crise complexe à travers une coordination efficace, souple et fondée sur les principes humanitaires
project_objective:
L’objectif du projet est de renforcer la coordination de la réponse humanitaire au Cameroun afin de sauver des vies, de protéger les plus vulnérables et d’améliorer la résilience des populations. Avec l’aggravation de la crise dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest, le pays est désormais confronté à trois crises humanitaires complexes qui affectent 8 des 10 régions du Cameroun. L’impact de ces trois crises sur les conditions de vie des populations affectées est renforcé par des vulnérabilités structurelles préexistantes qui entravent leur relèvement.

La complexité et l’étendue de ces crises requièrent donc plus que jamais une coordination efficace, adaptée aux différents terrains d’intervention et fondée sur les principes humanitaires. Le projet de coordination d’OCHA Cameroun permettra ainsi d’atteindre une réponse humanitaire mieux financée, plus stratégique et qui centralise les droits humains et la protection des personnes. Il permettra aussi d’atteindre une meilleure complémentarité entre les actions d’urgence et les programmes de développement, afin de combattre ensemble les besoins humanitaires et leurs causes sous-jacentes.

A cette fin, OCHA fournira les services essentiels de diffusion de produits d'information clés, de coordination du Cycle de Programmation Humanitaire et de facilitation d'évaluations des besoins multisectorielles conjointes. Sa présence à Yaoundé, Maroua, Buea, Bamenda et Kousseri lui permettra d'apporter un appui décisif aux mécanismes de coordination et de favoriser la cohérence entre les enjeux opérationnels terrain et les instances décisionnelles stratégiques. Cette position clé lui permet aussi d'avancer les considérations primordiales de Centralité de la Protection et Protection transversale, de Protection contre l'Exploitation et les Abus Sexuels (PEAS) et de nexus humanitaire développement. Depuis ses sous-bureaux de l'Extrême-Nord et du Sud-Ouest et Nord-Ouest, OCHA favorisera enfin la mise à l'échelle de la réponse dans ces régions, notamment à travers la gestion des responsabilités CMCoord et d'accès humanitaire, ainsi que le renforcement des capacités des répondants locaux.

project_name: Provision of primary and secondary health services for IDPs and host communities in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
Through this project this NGO will implemented an integrated health and mental health response in Northeast Syria. Primarily the project will support the provision of critical health services in areas where needs and gaps have been identified and the population largely depend on supported facilities for daily health services. Primary and secondary health services will be provided through four hospitals and six primary healthcare clinics (PHCs) in Aleppo (Ain al Arab), Ar Raqqa (Raqqa City, Al Qahtaniyeh, Akirishi, Abo Qobeih), Deir Ez Zor (Kesrah, Al Harmoushiyeh, Jazra Bu Hamayid) and Al Hassekeh (Al Malikeyeh, Tal Baydar).  Health services will include provision of basic primary health services, including treatment of common acute and chronic illnesses and injuries, management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, including local endemic diseases and health education. It will also provide basic SRH services such as ANC and PNC, family planning services focusing on women and girls of reproductive age, in addition with closely coordination with WHO will provide vaccination services for children under five. PHCC’s will also provide a referral system to enable referral of cases that need further services to secondary and tertiary levels. Through the Kidney Centre at Raqqa National Hospital, the project will provide critical lifesaving hemodialysis services to huge catchment area in NES. The project will increase access to more than one million people including IDPs and host communities.

Mental health needs continues to be highly unmet due to shortage of qualified work force and resources, even though the needs continue escalating across the globe. The prevalence of depression, anxiety, PTSD, psychosis and trauma continues to be high in NES. Massive displacements a due to  a protracted period of war, has put pressure on already unavailable resources. The clients will be provided with mhGAP care using trained practioners, whom will also be provided with psychotropic medications. mhGAP intervention is suitable in this kind of setting due to the shortage of psychiatric doctors and comprehensive mental health care. This will also be supported with awareness of common mental health conditions and mhGAP community toolkit which shall raise level of awareness and consumption of the services.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Consolidating protection and durable solutions in Somalia through the promotion and protection of HLP rights
project_objective:
The challenges confronting displaced communities in Somalia are entrenched and cumulative, while meaningful strides are being made by the government and international partners to address the displacement situation, these efforts are being continually reversed and/or undermined by a generalized inadequate protection of HLP rights, including widespread evictions. A little over 200,000 individuals have been evicted across Somalia in 2019 alone (HLP Sub cluster). Forced or otherwise, evictions have enormous impact on the victims’ dignity, physical security, livelihoods, and most importantly, their search for durable solutions to displacement. In addition to the enormous cost in humanitarian investments, the consequences range from secondary displacements and total destruction of livelihood strategies and assets, to the disruption of established life routines and social networks. Widespread tenure insecurity and general inadequate legal and policy frameworks remain the primary underpinning factors, but development-induced evictions, inability to pay rent, and dispute over ownership between competing land owners are among the reasons most cited for evictions. Eviction as a problematic phenomenon remains a foundational imperative to addressing the issue of displacement in Somalia in a realistic, comprehensive and sustainable way. It suffices to conclude that efforts to strengthen protection and contribute to durable solutions to displacement in Somalia will be incomplete and/or undermined without addressing the issue of eviction concurrently and systematically.

It is within this broader strategic framework that the current project, which seeks to facilitate enhanced protection of displaced communities from evictions, has been conceptualized. Project services and customized assistance packages will benefit 191,762 individuals in 21 districts across 15 regions. In terms of delivery modalities and outputs, the overarching objectives of the project will be achieved through a combination of complementarily reinforcing set of actions that are framed around the following eight core pillars.

1.	Strengthening ongoing eviction monitoring systems to enhance analysis, data availability and usability.
2.	Scaling up and consolidating eviction risk mapping to inform advocacy and response. 
3.	Supporting proactive engagements to negotiate improved tenure arrangements and/or facilitating dignified relocations for populations of concern.
4.	Mitigating protection risks exacerbated by evictions by providing different forms of tenure security support to displaced populations, including facilitating issuance of documentations at both household and group levels. Documentation will also seek to reduce risks to HLP assets on which local livelihood initiatives are dependent. 
5.	Supporting extremely vulnerable victims of evictions cope with post-eviction stress (PES) through the provision of multi-sectoral cash assistance, specialized counselling and legal assistance services. 
6.	Mobilizing and supporting government’s effort to address evictions, including robust engagement with landlords, gatekeepers and community leaders. 
7.	Facilitating access to information designed to assist IDPs access services, navigate complex procedures, and utilize existing remedies in areas of displacement to enhance their protection. 
8.	Strengthen coordination as well as the functional and operational capacity of the HLP sub cluster.

project_name: Mine Action—Removal and Disposal of ERW and Provision of EORE to Enhance Safety and Security for At-Risk Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
In alignment with the Humanitarian Response Plan 2020 and the United Nations Strategy on Mine Action 2019-2023, UNMAS will field four Quick Response Teams (QRT) with embedded Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) Officers and Community Liaison Officers (CLOs) to provide the following services: explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) spot tasks, survey and clearance of confirmed hazardous areas (calculated in square meters, as well as conduct Explosive Ordnance Education (EORE). UNMAS intends to deliver EORE session to 45,000 beneficiaries disaggregated as follows 13,500 boys, 13,500 girls, 11,250 women and 6,750 men. During the EORE sessions, further information will be gathered by the EORE and CLOs on suspicious hazards, which will then be shared with the clearance teams for surveying, marking and clearance. EORE alerts communities on how to identify, avoid and report explosive hazards they may encounter to reduce their threat of injury or death. Additionally, the clearance teams will survey and clear 600,000 square meters of land. 
The four clearance teams will be highly mobile in order to respond to urgent and prioritized tasks throughout South Sudan. The teams will provide survey and clearance of explosive hazards as well as provide risk education to women, men, boys, and girls to mitigate the threat of injury or death from explosive hazards. During the quick response tasks, the EORE component of the team will also deliver risk education to the surrounding communities.

project_name: Protection of the civilian population and humanitarian actors through Humanitarian Mine Action in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
As a result of the ongoing conflict, the population and humanitarian response in northeast Nigeria are affected by the presence of explosive devices such as victim operated IEDs and Explosive Remnants of War. The impact remains unabated. According to the UNMAS database, from January to October 2019, 111 civilians died due to explosions and 181 have been injured. Access is also hampered due to the presence of IED along roads.
Primarily a humanitarian project, the activities will also contribute to the humanitarian-development nexus.
In order to contribute to the protection of individuals and communities from the risks and socio-economic impact of explosive hazards in the context of the Humanitarian Response in northeast Nigeria, the project will be articulated around four pillars. Through the coordination of Mine Action and the management of related information, UNMAS proposes to support the delivery of effective, efficient and safe lifesaving activities by Mine Action partners in close coordination with the humanitarian community and Nigerian authorities and in compliance with the 2020 Humanitarian Response Plan. Through the delivery of Explosive Ordnance Risk Education to 80,000 civilians – including 55% women and girls and Conflict Preparedness and Protection, UNMAS also aims will strengthen community-owned protection and resilience. UN actors and humanitarian actors operating in northeast Nigeria will also benefit from Explosive Hazard Awareness sessions. The delivery of 40 non-technical surveys focused on accessible areas will allow delineating dangerous areas while allowing using safe lands for their primary purpose and in support of the humanitarian-development nexus. The support to the development of Nigerian capacities, through localization and training of institutional mine clearance capacities, will reinforce the global response.

project_name: Prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée chez 75,000 enfants de 6-59 mois et 25,000 Femmes modérement malnutris.
project_objective:
Le taux de Malnutrition Aiguë Globale (MAG) est estimé à 5,1% dont 1.1% de MAS (malnutrition aiguë sévère), selon les résultats de la dernière Enquête Nationale sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et de Sécurité alimentaire (ENNSAB) de janvier 2019 utilisant la méthodologie JANFSA (Joint Nutrition ,
 Food Security Analysis), ce qui place la situation nutritionnelle dans la catégorie « moyenne » (précaire) selon les nouveaux seuils de l’OMS. Ce taux atteste d’une détérioration de la situation nutritionnelle puisqu’il était de 4,5% en 2018 dont 0.9% de MAS selon les résultats de l'Enquête sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et le taux de mortalité, Janvier 2018.  Selon l'ENNSAB 2019, les provinces les plus affectées par la MAG sont respectivement Gitega (6,3%), Rutana (6,2%), Rumonge (6,2%), Cankuzo (5,8%), Makamba (5,8%), Mwaro (5,3%), Bujumbura (5,2%) et Ngozi (5,2%). L’analyse des besoins effectuée par les acteurs humanitaires a permis d’identifier cinq provinces (Kirundo, Ruyigi, Ngozi, Muyinga et Cankuzo) prioritaires à besoins humanitaires élevés ; ce qui fait que le PAM en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Lutte contre le Sida à travers le Programme National Intégré d’Alimentation et de Nutrition ont jugé bon de continuer par la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée dans les provinces de Cankuzo, Kirundo, Ngozi et Rutana où le taux de prévalence de la MAG est comprise entre 5% et 9% avec des facteurs aggravants tels que la persistance du paludisme sous forme épidémique,  l’insécurité alimentaire, la densité élevée et  les déplacements fréquents des populations. Le budget total estimé est de 5,497,819 US$ pour le traitement de 75,000 enfants de 6-59 mois et 25,000 FEFA modérément malnutris.

project_name: Assets creation project to support Early recovery and Resilience for 42,500 people through livelihood activities in crisis-affected areas in the East, Adamaoua and North regions
project_objective:
The Project aims to improve access to food and contribute to improve social cohesion and building resilience of vulnerable and food insecure communities affected by the CAR crisis in East, North and Adamaoua regions. This project will address immediate food needs of 42,500 vulnerable people including refugees (70%) returnees and local populations (30%) that have been severely affected by crisis that disrupted economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in these regions. The implementation of livelihood activities, Community-based Participative Planning (CBPP) sessions are carried out together with local community members (both women and men) to identify actual needs and priorities of local communities that will support the affected populations to come up with their own response strategies and build resilience. This people-centered approach ensures the provision of effective solutions together with beneficiaries and reduce the dependency on relief. 
Assistance through for FFA, will be implemented using cash modality for 15,500 beneficiaries and in-kind Food for 27,000 beneficiaries for three months. Therefore, the cash transfer value is aligned with the in-kind food ration. It considers beneficiaries' food preferences for the commodities and prices on the local market. The transfer value is calculated based on the identified food gap and is designed to assist beneficiaries to reach the recommended minimum calories intake of 2,100 Kcal per person per day. The use of cash-based transfers is expected to improve the cost-effectiveness of WFP's operations, while seizing the economic opportunities of local markets, with particular consideration for the beneficiaries’ choice and dignity. 
WFP will collaborate closely with Government technical ministries, cooperating partners and communities to ensure project implementation and sustainability. Nutrition, Gender and protection issues are taken into consideration at all the stages of the project elaboration, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Gender and protection risk analysis will be carried out and the most vulnerable will be targeted, including female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities.
Project sites will be in secure areas and at convenient distance from the homes of the beneficiaries.
To support smooth project implementation and ensure sustainability, capacity strengthening sessions will be organized for all stakeholders on gender and protection policy, project management, monitoring and nutrition.

project_name: Psychosocial support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse of children affected by the Lake Chad Basin crisis, including support to children formerly associated with armed groups, in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava, and Mayo Tsanaga
project_objective:
In 2019, the increase in threats and attacks by armed groups in Cameroon's Far North Region continued to lead to major population movements, increased difficulties in access to basic social services for children and lack of opportunities for adolescents and youth, and further weakened community ties. 
According to the latest DTM report at the time of writing this proposal (Round 19, August 2019), the displaced population is estimated at 428,289 individuals in the Far North region (270,870 IDPs, 46,845 out-of-camp refugees from Nigeria and 110,574 returnees). It is estimated that children account for 62% of the displaced population. 

With the majority of populations in need being children internally displaced, returnees, but also children from communities hosting IDPs and returnees, the child protection (CP) response needs to be maintained in order to continue to assist new children returning to Far North Region taking into account that separation from family members continue to take place and affect children, protect all those vulnerable from violent extremism and gender-based violence but also assist in their reinsertion into their communities while mistrust, stigmatization and suspicion of collaboration and affiliation with Boko Haram are still present.

The key result of the project which is in line with the objectives of the protection sector, is that 181,365 conflict-affected children among whom 92,496 girls, are protected from violence, abuse and exploitation and live in a protective environment in the targeted localities of in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava, and Mayo Tsanaga Divisions of the Far-North Region of Cameroon. 

The project builds on previously established dynamics and community structures and will provide psychosocial support (PSS) to 181,365 children, 92,496 girls and 88,869 boys.

During the child friendly spaces activities, partners will continue to identify unaccompanied and separated children (based on previous trends and on partners capacities, the project plans to assist around 263 UASC including 60% of new cases), ensuring and providing those children with PSS, alternative care arrangements with the capacity building of foster families, reunification with their families of origin and reinsertion in their communities. All will benefit from close individual follow-up. 
To address both social norms but also to ensure smooth community reinsertion, the project will work at strengthening community mobilization and will organize community activities around prevention of gender-based violence including activities to abandon child marriage, intergenerational dialogue, social cohesion. Based on the projections, a total of 362,700 persons (women, men, girls, boys) are planned to be reached through community mobilization activities. Partnership with religious and traditional leaders, and chiefery including female stakeholders will be an important channel to display messages and address complex issues. In complement, the work on youth empowerment and youth participation will enable to merge with the other members of the communities and promote prevention and protection of children from violence and exploitation.
Following up on strategic planning with Far North regional decentralized and deconcentrated authorities, the issue of conflict-affected children without a birth certificates came out strongly. 
The project aims at supporting 9,000 conflict-affected in obtaining a birth certificate.
165 children suspected of association with armed groups are expected to be identified, will receive PSS, and will be supported for family and community reintegration.
UNICEF will continue to closely work with civil society implementing partners, providing them with capacity building, supporting the setting up SOPs for case management and referral. UNICEF will also strengthen the coordination mechanism led by the Regional Delegation of Social Affairs ensuring a merging  with justice and law enforcement authorities.

project_name: COVID-19 PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE IN CCCM / DTM
project_objective:
With the overall objective of reducing the vulnerability of displaced populations in north-east Nigeria against Covid-19 and contribute to the containment of a possible outbreak, IOM CCCM aims to support the overall COVID-19 preparedness and response efforts through facilitating the immediate, adequate and equitable delivery of critical services to the displaced population in camp and camp-like settings.
CCCM activities will continue to provide site facilitation support and site level coordination in formal and informal camps in the following Borno locations: MMC, Bama (including Banki), Dikwa, Gwoza (including Pulka,) Ngala, Monguno, Mafa, Jere, Kala Balge (Rann), and Damboa; and in the following Adamawa locations: Yola North, Yola South, Girie and Song.

In collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) and the State Ministry of Health for Borno, DTM will be collecting point of entry (POE) data for all person moving through the border locations in Ngala, Monguno, Damasak, Kala Balge, Bama and Pulka. DTM will produce monthly dashboards to show all the movements recorded and all the data will also be shared with the health partners. DTM will conduct mapping of partners including emergency contacts to be shared with all persons using the POEs. Furthermore, DTM with its wide network in the North East, North West and North Central will produce periodic maps to show restrictions imposed on all states in the selected regions.
