project_name: Providing comprehensive emergency assistance to support Burundian communities affected by natural and humanmade disasters
project_objective:
This project aims to address one of the biggest gaps in humanitarian emergency response capacity in Burundi: the lack of pre-positioned stock to implement a rapid response in case of emergency. To support the needs of internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities and crisis-affected communities, this project proposes to (1) create a shelter and non-food item (NFI) pipeline that would pre-position both shelter and NFI kits in case of a major event; 2) reinforce the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Emergency Event Tracking system, 3) provide basic food needs to affected populations; and 4) improve access to safe water and prevention of diarrhoea by providing critical WASH-related information to crisis-affected populations, prioritizing the most vulnerable women and children. These four components together will create the capacity to respond in case of an emergency in a way that respects the minimum
standards of quality.

Outcome 1: Improved life-saving assistance and emergency shelter and NFI goods are made available to populations affected by disasters

Outcome 2: Natural hazards are regularly identified through the DTM Emergency Event Tracking system

Outcome 3: Increased ability of crisis-affected populations, internally displaced people (IDPs) and returnees in targeted areas to meet their basic food needs

Outcome 4: Improved access to safe water and sanitation facilities and prevention of diarrhoea by providing critical WASH-related information to targeted populations

project_name: EMERGENCY WASH RESPONSE TO THE COVID19 OUTBREAK IN BORNO STATE, NIGERIA
project_objective:
In Borno State, structural needs are compounded by the needs triggered by the COVID crisis, leading to an increased vulnerability of the conflict-affected people. The State lacks adequate water supply infrastructure and the quantity of water p/d is below the 15L SPHERE standards necessary to cover basic water needs in areas within Monguno and Dikwa LGA. COVID19 transmission amongst these highly vulnerable will ramp up the transmission risks and threaten the continuity of the already challenging humanitarian response. In addition, most people within the State are not aware of the handwashing and other key behaviours to protect themselves from COVID-19. 

Therefore, SI is proposing an intervention that will contribute to contain the spread of the COVID 19 pandemic while decreasing morbidity and mortality amongst affected populations (global humanitarian response plan COVID 19 – Strategic Priority). For this purpose, SI will improve knowledge on covid 19 prevention and spread, and ensure that people are able to implement IPC measures within camps and host communities. Learning from the successful management of the last cholera outbreak, SI will continue to play a key role in WASH/COVID coordination.   

Under the proposed project, SI will prepare and respond to the COVID-19 outbreak in its areas of operation, namely Maiduguri, Dikwa, Ngala and Monguno. The project is built on different strategic objectives as follows:
o	Provision of items necessary to implement IPC measures: SI will distribute COVID/hygiene kits to the most-vulnerable/affected people and in pre-identified hotspots. Latrine maintenance kits to disinfect this infrastructure will be distributed to already established sanitation committees. 
o	Increased safe water: through reticulation of water points, chlorination of water points and water trucking; in community and health facilities. SI will also conduct regular water quality tests. 
o	Increased knowledge on COVID 19 prevention and spread: Communication and mass awareness raising campaigns will be carried out with strong community involvement; including production and dissemination of IEC materials on COVID-19. The strategies that will be implemented include door to door hygiene messaging, dialogue with religious and traditional rulers as advocate and champions of COVID 19 preventive message dissemination and use of megaphones to spread the messages widely in camps. 
o	Promote and sustain healthy environment to prevent the survival of the virus: Hand washing stations will be set up at strategic points like markets, latrines in Monguno, Dikwa, Maiduguri and Ngala. SI will disinfect wash infrastructures and markets on a regular basis. 
o	Efficient coordination and information management

In addition, SI as lead of the Cholera/COVID TWG will strongly contribute to the efficiency of the COVID coordination in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa States.

project_name: Supporting COVID-19 Outbreak Response to Vulnerable Populations in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe State. (An Addendum to UNICEF HRP 2020)
project_objective:
This project is aimed at supporting the response to COVID-19 pandemic in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe states. The COVID-19 pandemic broke out in China and declared a pandemic in January 2020. It is  caused by the 2019-nCOV, a new type of coronavirus that started in China in December 2019. This virus has infected over three million persons worldwide and recorded over two hundred thousand deaths with an estimated global case fatality rate (CFR) of 6.95 percent as at April 28, 2020. The first case in Nigeria was recorded on February 27, 2020, with a total of 1,532 cases and 44 deaths, a CFR of 2.87 percent at April 28, 2020. The index case in the conflict affected BAY states was recorded on April 18, 2020, with a quick rise in the number of cases to 47 cases and 7 deaths recorded with a CFR of 14.89 percent in Borno as at April 28, 2020. 
The current pandemic presents a unique set of challenges to the vulnerable populations in the conflict affected North-East Nigeria and will further compound the already challenged and weak health system and its ability to respond to the needs of the population. The effects could be dire, particularly to those displaced and/or living in camps and camp-like settings who are often faced with specific challenges and vulnerabilities with an already suboptimal functioning health service, poor and inadequate shelter and poor hygiene conditions. These populations are often exposed to stigmatization, may face challenges accessing health services and the COVID-19 outbreak threatens to exacerbate these challenges and thereby disrupting protection, human rights and public health services. The BAY states also suffer from a greatly debilitated health system which is currently being strengthened through close collaboration between humanitarian actors and government with significant gains over the past two years. It is therefore critical that the COVID-19 outbreak readiness and response strategies, plan and operations extend to all persons regardless of status and ensures inclusiveness as well as protecting and sustaining the progresses made in health systems strengthening (HSS) through a multisectoral approach.
UNICEF in partnership with state government agencies (SPHCDAs and SPHMBs) and the State Ministries of Health of the BAY states, will support the COVID-19 outbreak response through the procurement and distribution of essential commodities such as PPEs and drugs required for case management and infection prevention and control (IPC). UNICEF will also ensure that sustained integrated PHC services continue to be available to the vulnerable populations especially in IDP camps as they are still exposed to other morbidity and mortality causing conditions which are only going to be worsened by the pandemic. 
The objectives of this interventions are 
•	To mitigate the risk and contain the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic and decrease morbidity and mortality in Northeast Nigeria.
•	Ensure continuous and sustained provision of basic integrated PHC services in IDP camps and to underserved populations during the COVID-19 outbreak response.

project_name: Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan
project_objective:
The current security and humanitarian situation in South Sudan affected 299,162 refugees in South Sudan as of September 2019. The majority of them originated from Sudan (276,531) followed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (16,055), Ethiopia (4,409) and the Central African Republic (2,041). They reside in 21 camps and urban locations in Upper Nile, Unity, Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria, and Jonglei regions. South Sudan maintains an open-door policy for refugees and grants those arriving from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Cong, and the Central African Republic prima facie refugee status. There are additionally 3,266 asylum-seekers from Ethiopia, Eritrea, Somalia, Burundi, and other countries waiting for a determination on their individual refugee claims. Daily border crossing continues with more than 8,000 new arrivals registered in 2018 (as of September 2019) from Blue Nile and South Kordofan States of Sudan. 

Refugees reside in conflict-affected regions where security remains precarious with fragile relations with host communities. The continuous economic decline, weak rule of law, limited development support and lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as the conditions in the refugees’ areas of origin mean that refugees will continue to rely on lifesaving humanitarian assistance and on social cohesion with and acceptance by the host community for protection.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions from UNHCR and its partners, including individual registration and documentation. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While food, water, health and education services are available for all refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of refugees in need of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services. 

UNHCR and partners will continue the delivery of protection and multi-sectoral assistance to refugees. UNHCR and partners will continue programs ensuring refugees’ access to healthcare services, education, WASH, livelihoods, food and NFI distribution. Access to reproductive health and HIV services will be ensured through complete ANC coverage, health facility deliveries and skilled health workers, as well as comprehensive HIV/AIDS programs allowing refugees to have access to ant-retroviral treatments (ART) through ART centers in all camps and the two referral hospitals. 
Initiatives to strengthen SGBV prevention and response mechanisms and child protection will be further promoted. While facilitating traditional justice mechanisms, such as conflict resolution committees and joint customary courts, UNHCR will support the re-establishment of statutory courts in refugee sites.

project_name: Humanitarian assistance to 75,000 conflict affected and vulnerable people in Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, and Jonglei States
project_objective: This project aims at providing life-saving frontline for most vulnerable population including IDPs and returnees with sufficient attention given to women and children, especially girls by improving the living environment with provision of WASH and GBV support to IDPs, returnees and hosting community residents.

project_name: Provision of Safe, Protective and Inclusive Education to Conflict Affected Boys and Girls in South Sudan
project_objective:
Access to education remains as a significant challenge in South Sudan in the context of protracted conflicts. The entire education system, which was already under-resourced, with a low percentage of children enrolled in schools, is further weakened by the long-lasting conflict, which has pushed hundreds of thousands of children out of school. One in three schools has been damaged, destroyed, occupied or closed since 2013. South Sudan has at least 2.2 million out-of-school children who are exposed to protection risks and may need psychosocial support. Based on projections, this number could easily increase to 2.4 million by 2020, if no action is taken. 
Therefore, in view of the above this project seeks to provide safe, protective and inclusive education to conflict affected boys and girl in South Sudan in alignment with HRP Strategic Objectives 1, 2 & 3 and Education Cluster Strategic Objectives 1, 2 & 3. 
World Vision proposes to implement the project in the counties of Baliet, Fashoda, Melut and Renk (Upper Nile); Tonj South, Tonj East,Tonj North (Warrap); Yambio, Nagero, Tambura (Western Equatoria) and Juba in Central Equatoria which are geographical areas affected by conflict, displacement or facing acute food insecurity levels. WVSS continue to give focus to emergency affected rural and urban areas with significant IDPs presence. It is worth noting that WVSS has presence in these locations and is able to deliver quality education programming. Majority of the locations are part of UNICEF Education PD. However, not all schools are covered by the project, so there is room for collaboration. WV is willing to share information with UNKEA. 

In line with the Education Cluster Response Plan, WVSS will ensure that through this project, 33,000 girls and 22,000 boys have access to quality education and 1,300 teachers (780 female and 520 male) and PTA’s will be trained and supported with supplies and materials. WVSS will also prioritize establishment of learning structures with gender-segregated WASH facilities, and other supplies/materials/kits that will be supportive and will enhance motivation of children to go to and remain in school with a particular emphasis on girl’s education. In addition, recreational opportunities will be established and implemented to support the recovery of children and youth and promote their overall wellbeing. All learners will be given equal access to education despite gender, disability or ethnic background.

PROJECT REVISED-Emergency Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene interventions for emergency affected and vulnerable populations in Somalia
project_objective:
Humanitarian needs remain acute in Somalia as result of continued conflict and repeated climatic shocks. According to FSNAU’s 2019 Post Gu assessment The2019 Gu rains season performed poorly and forecasted up to 2.1 million people across Somalia are expected to face food consumption gaps, high acute malnutrition, or depletion of assets indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes through December 2019. An estimated 2.6 million people are internally displaced (IDPs)further jeopardizing the survival and well-being of children, and without urgent assistance, we face the risk of a major nutrition and food-security crisis unfolding during the long dry season of 2020.  
According to the recent WASH cluster analysis, more than 9 million people are affected by the prevalent poor WASH conditions in Somalia. The same document also estimated that 2.7 million people are in severe (2.5M) and extreme (0.2M) need of humanitarian WASH assistance.  An estimated 700,000 people along Shabelle and Juba basins are also identified as highly susceptible for flooding and need of acute life-saving WASH interventions during the 2020 Gu and Deyr rainy seasons. Cholera is endemic in Somalia, from December 2017 till 15th Sept 2019, a total of 8,719 cases and 46 deaths reported from 25 districts and 6 regions of Somalia, which is attributed to protracted displacement, drought, flooding together with poor water supply and sanitation services and poor hygiene practices. 

During the long dry seasons, major water sources like boreholes, shallow wells, hand-dug wells, berkads, dams, water pans and springs became extremely unreliable. This resulted in higher water supply access costs to households during the dry season. For example, during May 2019 the water prices ranged from 4.5 USD to 23 USD for one cubic meter water which very high compared with water prices in neighbouring countries.

A combination of poor access to safe drinking water, lack of adequate sanitation facilities and poor hygienic practices especially in IDP settlements, contribute significantlly to overall public health risks in Somalia . Open defecation rates stand at 49 per cent in rural areas and 28 per cent at national level. Handwashing practices with soap are very low.

Lack of clean water and poor sanitation and hygiene practices not only cause diseases but also create huge burden on women and children as women and girls perform most of the unpaid labour associated with WASH in households and communities which reduces the time they have available for education, economic activities and leisure. Women and girls are often vulnerable to harassment or violence when they travel long distances to fetch water, use shared toilets, or practice open defecation. In addition, lack of proper hygiene supplies like soap and sanitary pads affects dignity of women and girls.

This emergency WASH project will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, emergency WASH response, strengthening partners’ capacity, cluster coordination and information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving support for emergency affected and vulnerable populations throughout Somalia by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere standards and minimize the suffering of the displaced populations and vulnerable host communities. The project will focus on assessing the WASH situation in the emergency affected areas, emergency water trucking/water vouchers, rehabilitating and upgrading urban and rural water facilities, provision of emergency sanitation services for IDPs and vulnerable communities, hygiene promotion and flood and cholera prevention and preparedness activities. The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs and government ministries in areas affected by different emergencies. To reach the total targeted population of 1.2 Million People a total of 39.6 Million USD is required for the year 2020.

project_name: Strengthening the response to Gender Based Violence in northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Since the beginning of the humanitarian crisis in North-East Nigeria, affected populations have been suffering from a continued deterioration of living conditions, a disruption of pre-existing protective mechanisms and a lack of access to essential services. They have accumulated protracted stress and experienced extreme violence, and loss of family members, social connections, and property. Displaced populations face grave protection risks and abuse including different forms of gender-based violence (GBV), exploitation, family separation, restrictions on freedom of movement and insecurity. These vulnerabilities are exacerbated by pre-existing and emergency-induced problems faced by the affected population. This is particularly true in terms of the most vulnerable sub-groups of the population, including the elderly and chronically ill, persons with disabilities, female and child-headed households, unaccompanied and/or separated children, adolescent boys and girls, pregnant and/or lactating women and people returning from captivity. 
Under this project, activities will focus on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and stand-alone protection interventions through MHPSS teams and resource centres/safe spaces, capacity building for humanitarian actors and GBV risk mitigation. IOM’s MHPSS Mobile Teams and safe spaces will implement GBV prevention and response services in camp and camp-like settings.

The action will be implemented through a distribution of micro-enterprise, self-employment, self-sustenance and vocational training grants to IDPs and vulnerable populations such as persons with low income, families with many children, households with disabled members, single-headed households etc. The activities will also prioritize unemployed, women, young adults (youth) and persons with disabilities derived from the conflict. project_name: Treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition in South Sudan.
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to present a complex humanitarian and food and nutritional security situation, characterized by national and localized conflicts, displacements, poor infrastructure and a deteriorating economic climate. As a indirect and direct result, acute malnutrition continues to be prevalent across the country. An estimated 1.8 million children under five years and pregnant & lactating women are acutely malnourished. The Food Security and Nutrition Monitoring System (FNSMS, R24) indicated 16.2% global acute malnutrition (GAM), an increase from 13.3% in 2018 lean season. National rates of acute malnutrition in women of reproductive age are at high levelof 18.9% , with similar prevalence (18.8%) for pregnant women . Geographically, four out of the ten former states had prevalence of wasting ranging from 15% to 23.8%.  The states with highest prevalence of wasting among women coincide with that of acute malnutrition in children (0-59 months), namely Unity, Jonglei and Warrap, showing how impactful the inter-generational of cycle of malnutrition is on child nutritional status. Similarly, 4.5 million people (39% of the population) are estimated to be facing crisis, emergency or catastrophe level (IPC Phases 3, 4 and 5) acute food insecurity (IPC, 2019). The persistent high malnutrition levels are attributed to high levels of food insecurity, displacements, conflict and poor infrastructure which hamper availability and access to basic health and nutrition services, low harvests, dysfunctional markets, poor infant young child feeding (IYCF) practices and high morbidity. 
The project will ensure that populations affected by conflict and displacement have access to emergency nutrition services in order to prevent morbidity and mortality due to moderate acute malnutrition. WFP will continue to work with cooperating partners to support an emergency nutrition response through a preventive supplementary feeding programme and treatment services for moderate acute malnutrition targeting children aged 6-59 months, pregnant & lactating women, and people living with HIV/TB across South Sudan. Prevention and treatment services are provided both to IDPs and host populations. WFP also conducts direct delivery of life-saving nutrition services in hard-to-reach areas under the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). The project implementation will use an integrated approach through synergies with activities supported by other clusters (health, education, FSL, WASH).

project_name: Fournir aux enfants maliens, pendant l'année scolaire, des repas scolaires dans des zones ciblées
project_objective:
Le projet vise 3 objectifs :
1. Soutenir les élèves vulnérables des zones post conflits à avoir accès à la nourriture toute l’année ;
2. Encourager les inscriptions des élèves et la fréquentation scolaire ; et
3. Réduire les disparités de genre entre garçons et filles

Au Mali, le droit à l’éducation est garanti à chaque citoyen. Toutefois, il existe des disparités entre les régions, les
Campagnes et entre les genres qu’il convient de réduire. Dans l’enseignement fondamental, l’Etat s’était fixé d’atteindre au moins 95% de Taux Brut de Scolarisation (TBS) à l’an 2010. Malgré les efforts consentis, ce taux était de 80% en 2010 2011 avant de chuter à 72% en 2014-2015 à cause principalement de l’insécurité dans le nord. Le développement des cantines a été une des stratégies pour améliorer cet indicateur. 
En 2009, le Gouvernement du Mali a adopté une Politique Nationale d’Alimentation Scolaire (PNAS) et une loi règlementant l’alimentation scolaire en 2019 qui met l’accent sur le soutien à l’éducation primaire, l’appui aux communautés locales et l’usage de produits locaux. Depuis 2016, malgré des besoins élevés, les repas scolaires ne peuvent être fournis dans de nombreuses écoles du Centre et du Nord du pays, qui font face à des défis importants. Dans ces régions, l’insécurité persistante a déjà conduit à la fermeture de 1051 écoles fermées affectant près de 300 000 enfants . La région de Mopti, à elle seule, enregistre plus de la moitié de ces écoles.
La fourniture de repas scolaires vise à renforcer les avantages d'un environnement sûr et sécurisé pour les enfants vulnérables afin de contribuer à leur rétention scolaire. Ainsi le PAM se donne pour objectif général : « Un accès équitable à une éducation fondamentale de qualité à travers l’alimentation scolaire au Mali » dont l’atteinte passera par l’amélioration de l’accès à une alimentation saine, nutritive et suffisante tout au long de l’année. Pour 200 000 enfants vulnérables dans les zones à insécurité alimentaires à travers l’alimentation scolaire pour un budget global de 15 185 000 de dollars américains. Le programme sera mis en œuvre sur toute l’étendue du territoire malien avec un accent particulier  ou les écoles fermées dans les zones du central et du nord. La cantine scolaire contribue à la réouverture des écoles dans le contexte d’urgence.
En outre, l’indice de parité filles/garçons reste faible particulièrement au niveau des zones rurales. La faible scolarisation des filles trouve sa justification dans les travaux domestiques, le petit commerce, le mariage précoce et la religion. Aujourd’hui au Mali, sur 10 filles, moins de 6 entrent en première année de l’enseignement fondamental et seulement 4 complètent le 1er cycle du fondamental. Pour renverser cette tendance, il faut créer à l’école les meilleures conditions d’apprentissage et d’infrastructures. Ceci ne peut se faire qu’en travaillant en synergie avec les autres partenaires de l’éducation. Le PAM est disposé à développer ces complémentarités avec les autres acteurs. C'est donc l'action combinée des repas chauds servis à la mi journée et les autres interventions que le problème de scolarisation en général et la réduction des écarts entre garçons et filles peut être résolu.

Pour y parvenir, le PAM aura besoin de mobiliser des ressources financières pendant 180 jours à transférer aux comités de gestion scolaire pour la prise en charge de 100% des bénéficiaires qui fonctionneront en mode cash et pour les actions de renforcement de capacités, coût d’exécution et autres. L’ensemble du budget s’élèvera à 15 184 000 dollars.

Ces activités seront réalisées dans ce projet : 1) mettre à la disposition des CGS sur une base trimestrielle les fonds destinés aux repas scolaires des élèves ; 2) préparer et servir quotidiennement les repas aux élèves présents ; 3) Fournir au CGS le kits ustensile pour la cuisine ; 4) organisation des séances de sensibilisation sensible à la nutrition et formation des CGS

project_name: Provision of quality multisector humanitarian assisstance for Refugees and host communities  in Sudan
project_objective:
The humanitarian response aligns with UNHCR’s strategic directions 2017-2021 by emphasizing protection; accountability to the people we serve; participation; mainstreaming of age, gender and diversity; and increased focus on the promotion of durable solutions. In line with the Strategic Objective of the 2020 Refugee Response Plan, Save the Children will build self-reliance among the CAR, Chadian, and South Sudanese refugees by strengthening community-based structures and integrating livelihoods. As a cross cutting issue, environmental protection will be mainstreamed throughout the project cycle.
Save the Children has articulated the following objective for 2020: To provide basic services and assistance for refugees in South Darfur, South Kordofan and Centeral Darfur, in line with humanitarian standards, and promote durable solutions.
The project will target 66,921 (17052 girls,15740 boys, 17406 women, and 16723 men) individuals (3500 Chadian refugees, 12144 CAR refugees, and 37145 SSR) in need living in 6 localities within 3SCI priority states including Centeral Darfur, South Darfur, and South Kordofan The project will be focusing in provision basic health care services and nutrition assistance to affected people and children with severe and moderate malnutrition, provision of water supply at community and institutional level including construction, and contribute to elimination of open defecation within our operation areas Provision support of UASC, provide support for families of EVIs children, training for  newly animators and CBCPNs, establishment and strengthen the CMS. Rehabilitation and construction of basic and secondary schools and provision of teaching and learning materials to targeted schools to support school retention. The project will be focusing also on supporting refugees and hosting communities to restore their livelihoods and integration process.
The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $2,475,000.

project_name: Renforcement des moyens d’existence des agropasteurs pour l’amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire à l’Est du Tchad
project_objective:
L’Est du Tchad (Ouaddaï, Wadi Fira et Sila) est affecté par une crise multidimensionnelle où l’insécurité alimentaire, la malnutrition et la présence prolongée de réfugiés soudanais s’ajoutent à un contexte de faible développement et d’accès limité aux ressources pour la sécurité alimentaire exacerbé par l’état d’urgence dû au conflit intercommunautaire observé dans le Sila et le Ouaddaï.
En 2019, selon les résultats de l’Enquête nutritionnelle nationale SMART, menée par le ministère de la Santé et ses partenaires entre juillet et août, les résultats révèlent que, sur le plan national, la prévalence de la MAG est de 12,9 % (12,1 – 13,7) contre 13,5 % en 2018. Cependant, la prévalence du MAG a légèrement diminué dans le Ouaddaï, Wadi Fira. Malheureusement, l’état d’urgence instauré dans ces provinces limite les échanges transfrontaliers et résulte en la baisse des prix du bétail. Ces restrictions compliquent les transhumances et les transactions commerciales pour le bétail et contribue à la détérioration des termes de l´échange en défaveur des éleveurs. Ce qui pourrait entamer l’état nutritionnel des populations déjà fragilisées.
En tenant compte du niveau élevé de malnutrition des enfants et du rôle important des femmes dans l’économie familiale, les principaux bénéficiaires directs des actions des projets seront les femmes, en particulier les plus démunies qui, marquées par leur vulnérabilité due à plusieurs facteurs, ont des revenus faibles et des difficultés économiques importantes. Il s’agit des femmes chefs de familles, les femmes pauvres avec des enfants mineurs, les femmes seules ou âgées vulnérables mais capables de mener des activités de production et des AGR.
A l’est, 321 283 personnes dont 18 272 en situation d’urgence seront affectées si aucune action d’appui à la reconstitution de leurs moyens d’existence n’est prise.
En matière de protection transversale, toutes les actions seront axées sur les quatre éléments clés dans la mise en œuvre de ce présent projet. Surtout dans sa politique relative à la redevabilité, la FAO mettra en facteur les équipes de plaintes qui pourront remonter toutes les actions susceptibles de nuire à la bonne la dignité des bénéficiaires à travers cette opération. Dans le cadre de ce projet, l’objectif de l’intervention est d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire des agropasteurs à travers le renforcement des moyens d’existence. Plus de la moitié des bénéficiaires estimés à 7500 ménages (45 000 personnes) ou 14% des personnes vulnérables seront choisis parmi les femmes chefs de ménages vulnérables, les ménages ayant des enfants et des vieilles personnes. Ceci permettra de mieux protéger toutes ces couches qui sont souvent très vulnérables par rapport aux chocs et aux catastrophes.

Mejorar y ampliar los servicios de Protección para NNA y cuidadores afectados por la situación humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
A través de la presente intervención UNICEF quiere continuar a apoyar las diferentes instituciones del sistema de Protección de NNA en brindar servicios y programas a NNA y sus cuidadores afectados por la situación humanitaria con un enfoque de género, edad e inclusión. Las actividades implementadas contribuirán para alcanzar los 3 objetivos estratégicos del Plan de Respuesta en estas componentes: OE1: UNICEF y sus aliados brindarán servicios de apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal a NNA en riesgo y cuidadores; OE2: UNICEF y sus aliados facilitaran el acceso a certificados y registros de nacimiento en hospitales, unidades sanitaria y en comunidades con un enfoque también a NNA de población indígena; OE3: UNICEF y sus aliados contribuirán a fortalecer los mecanismos institucionales y comunitarios para prevenir, mitigar y responder los riesgos de protección de los NNA y sus cuidadores afectados por la situación, de acuerdo a los principios humanitarios y al respeto de los derechos humanos. UNICEF trabajará también apoyando la coordinación inter-cluster a través del Área de Responsabilidad de NNA y sus actividades con un enfoque en armonización de abordaje en las diferentes temáticas diseminando las Normas Mínimas y criando procedimientos estándar en temáticas estratégicas como la Gestión de casos y el cuidado alternativo. 
A través del proyecto UNICEF junto con sus aliados implementará estas actividades: 
•	Fortalecimiento de instituciones del Estado y ONGs en temáticas de protección de NNA incluyendo Normas Mínimas, gestión de caso, apoyo psicosocial, violencia de género, cuidado alternativo, trata y trafico entre otras. 
•	Expansión de la oferta y calidad de servicios de protección para NNA en riesgo que incluyen entre otros: gestión de caso por los consejos de protección, acompañamiento de casos por parte de ONGs, apoyo en emisión de certificados y registros de nacimiento, apoyo a adolescentes en conflicto con la ley. 
•	A nivel comunitario, UNICEF y sus aliados trabajaran fortaleciendo los conocimientos sobre temáticas de protección de NNA incluyendo la prevención de la separación familiar y la diseminación de informaciones sobre servicios de protección existentes.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of lifesaving emergency reproductive, maternal, new born and child health services including disease prevention and strengthening national and regional emergency preparedness and response capacities
project_objective: This project will deliver lifesaving emergency health services including maternal, neonatal and child health and contribute to disease prevention and strengthening national and regional emergency preparedness and response capacities in the three zones of Somalia for an estimated 968,388 out of 3 million crisis affected population in need of healthcare. Through deployment of trained health workers including midwives and community health workers in facilities and mobile teams, primary health care services including treatment of common childhood illnesses, as well as emergency obstetric and neonatal care for pregnant and lactating women will be provided. The proposed action complements UNICEF's core interventions in Somalia and the intervention focuses on an integrated, multi-sectoral response to drought, displacement and conflict, providing life-saving services. To maximize impact, this project will provide evidence-based curative, promotional and preventive services and will enable complementarity with nutrition including priorities such as deworming, breastfeeding, complementary feeding, vitamin deficiencies, & micronutrient supplementation. In collaboration with Health Cluster, UNICEF will support the appropriate management of children with SAM and cholera co-morbidity admitted in AWD/Cholera treatment centres. Scaling up the WASH component as part of an integrated and coordinated response, will focus on disease outbreaks, especially cholera. Thus, the integrated action focuses on increasing response in areas of highest need and lowest levels of predictable access in Somalia. UNICEF supported health facilities will be equipped with essential medicines and equipment and trained staff will provide quality services. Emphasis will be laid on Maternal and Child Health, including Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care and Expanded Programme on Immunization to IDPs and most vulnerable communities and attention will be paid on application of treatment guidelines as per the Essential Package of Health Services and Primary Health Care. Support to outreach immunization for hard to-reach areas will be promoted to ensure equity and reaching a wider catchment. UNICEF will deliver comprehensive reproductive health care to women of reproductive age, men and adolescent boys among the target beneficiaries and promote health seeking behaviour including adoption of preventive practices through campaigns, health and hygiene education sessions for men and ado. UNICEF will also integrate surveillance and emergency preparedness ensuring adequate stocks for epidemic outbreaks of AWD/Cholera and measles are prepositioned. The project will also contribute to strengthening early warning disease surveillance through weekly submission of Communicable and Disease Surveillance reports from all the functional supported health facilities. Referral system for patients seeking secondary healthcare services will be strengthened. The project will also refer GBV victims to health facilities for comprehensive care and psychosocial support.

project_name: Accessible clean and potable water and improved hygiene practices in vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The intervention will improve access to drinking water for social and economically vulnerable Households (HHs) and improve hygienic conditions and practices at poor HHs in 6 communities in the Gaza strip. The interventions will respond to the shortage of household drinking water through improving drinking water storage capacity for 1,000 vulnerable households.  Moreover, the proposed interventions aim to improve access to hygiene services through rehabilitation of sanitation facilities inside 300 homes and 40 KGs, including adaptation of WASH HH sanitation facilities for PWDs. In order to ensure the best use of the interventions and ensure the sustainability and the logic of the whole project, the aforementioned interventions will be complemented through the hygiene promotion activities such as awareness activities and distribution of hygiene kits to the most vulnerable girls, boys, women, men, elders and people with disabilities. The hygiene promotion activities will prioritize girls and women needs, including menstrual hygiene management (MHM).
The project will target the vulnerable HHs in Bani sohailah, Al Qarara/Khan Younis, Al Bayuk/Rafah, Dair Albalah/Middle Area, Al Qararh and waadi Gaza/Gaza. The proposed intervention will directly target 14400 persons (6981 children and 7419 adults - 7073 F and 7327 M).

project_name: Integrated response to end gender-based violence against vulnerable women and adolescent girls in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The project will target vulnerable and affected population staying in ECA, Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, GCA. UNFPA has already built the key elements of a response mechanism as part of its humanitarian interventions and is keen to continue strengthening this mechanism. It will place a greater emphasis on assistance, strengthening community resilience, and improving access of humanitarian actors to the affected population. Special attention will be given to supporting the most vulnerable population: people with disabilities, people living in isolated settlements (in particular 0-5 km) with limited access to government service providers, social services, and single women-headed households along the contact line.
Differentiated approaches to programming will continue to be applied in 2020 considering the prevailing humanitarian situation:  
The primary focus for humanitarian response will remain to be on the communities 0-5 km and 5-20 km the contact line (Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts).  
Critical security/safety needs of the most vulnerable IDPs and comers from ECA communities will be prioritized in 20+ area, where durable solutions for GBV response are implemented in a safe and survivors-oriented manner. 
Due to restricted humanitarian access to NGCA for protection activities, the project will seek alternative partnership opportunities with local actors; will reach out to those in need through remote solutions; will use existing access points such as healthcare facilities for delivering aid.  
Four main project implementation areas that are in line with SOs will include:
Assistance – developing a network of accessible, affordable and accountable shelters, safe spaces, day-care centres for DV / GBV survivors based on needs assessment of the vulnerable population. These protection solutions according to needs assessment are the most relevant for 5-20 km and 20+ km zones due to security issues and the presence of capable service providers. 
Protection – capacity building and sensitization of service providers; awareness-raising within the general population, training and developing distant learning solutions for actors responsible for GBV response; strengthening accountability to affected population (AAP) mechanism, providing updates on Minimal Standards on GBViE. 
Resilience – supporting the development of community-based early warning system (for 0-5 km, 5-20 km zones as a priority), involving humanitarian actors, community activists; SGBV coordination to strengthen the response and prevention systems, to improve referral pathway and to ensure AAP.
Access – supporting targeted PSS MTs interventions, awareness-raising/sensitizing sessions and events in selected settlements (with emphasis on isolated settlements and those in 0-5 km zone).
UNFPA supported models of service delivery will eventually build trust in those services among survivors and trigger their willingness to report their cases (as a part of AAP) and seek help. Engagement of non-state actors (local NGO’s, FBO’s, CBO’s) to act as service providers at the local community level will strengthen the prevention pillar of the overall GBV response strategy.  
A monitoring and evaluation plan, defined through previous interventions to manage the process of assessing and reporting progress against project targets, is used to ensure the quality of project results. A feedback mechanism from project beneficiaries will be operating, including through regular GBV WGs and GBV SC meetings, National Toll-Free Hotline. 
In order to achieve maximum complementarity, the project will seek to coordinate, and to the extent possible work jointly, with other complementary projects and initiatives in the area of gender equality and GBV or those working to rehabilitate and develop local social infrastructure and institutional capacity.

project_name: Provision of shelter assistance to internally displaced and conflicted affected communities in east Ukraine
project_objective: There is an ongoing armed conflict in east Ukraine with daily shootings and shelling as well as localized flare-ups such as in Avdiivka and Novoluhanskoe in 2017 and Zolote in 2018. The conflict damages or destroys housing and civilian infrastructure, necessitating an emergency response in terms of shelter and basic needs, especially for persons with specific needs. To provide shelter and NFI support to displaced and conflict-affected persons with specific needs in a timely manner, UNHCR will preposition acute emergency shelter kits as well as non-food item (NFI) in the area most affected by shelling, which is the 'contact line'. In GCA, UNHCR’s emergency response will be coordinated closely with local authorities and complementary to their efforts to respond. UNHCR will also continue its shelter repair and reconstruction in 2020 and will prioritize households with protection and specific needs living on both sides of the 'contact line'. UNHCR will make sure that it will mainstream protection into its shelter assistance (including housing, land and property rights).

project_name: Appui à l'Education de base et à la scolarisation des filles au Tchad à travers des programmes novateurs d'Alimentation Scolaire
project_objective: Ce projet soutient les objectifs à long terme du Plan national d’éducation du Tchad, à savoir: (i) améliorer l’accès à l’éducation des personnes vulnérables et (ii) réduire les disparités entre les sexes à l’école. Il contribue à l'objectif 2.1 de l'objectif de développement durable (ODD) 2 (éliminer la faim) (Tout le monde a accès à la nourriture). Il contribue également aux objectifs de développement durable 1 (éliminer la pauvreté), 4 (éducation inclusive et qualitative et à l'apprentissage tout au long de la vie), 5 (égalité des sexes) et 17 (partenariat pour la mise en œuvre des objectifs de développement durable). Au total, 120 000 bénéficiaires directs et indirects seront ciblés dans les régions sahéliennes de Bahr-el-Ghazal, Batha, Guéra, Kanem, Ouaddaï et logone Oriental où l'insécurité alimentaire la malnutrition prévaut.

project_name: Building resilience of vulnerables communities in Chad
project_objective: The Project aims to reinforce the resilience of vulnerable household living in targeted zone of interventions mainly the Sahelian Belt of Chad through asset creation or rehabilitation, Food/cash transfer and Capacity strenghtening.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence aux populations réfugiées très vulnérables et moyennement vulnérables du Nigeria, Soudan et de la RCA
project_objective:
Le Tchad accueille depuis plus de 15 ans un nombre important de réfugiés (estimé aujourd’hui à plus de 441 000) dans la province du Lac, les zones du Sud et de l’Est. Cette population, pour laquelle les perspectives de rapatriement dans les pays d’origine sont très limitées, continue à bénéficier d’une assistance humanitaire dans les secteurs essentiels et vitaux tels que l’assistance alimentaire, la nutrition, l’eau, la santé, l’éducation et la protection.
Le PAM apportera une assistance alimentaire d’urgence aux populations réfugiées Nigériennes, Centrafricaines et Soudanaises. Cette assistance sera basée sur les résultats de l’exercice de profilage socio-économique 2017-2018 et adaptée aux vulnérabilités des ménages réfugiés (très vulnérables et moyennement vulnérables) vivant dans les provinces du Lac, Logone Occidental, Logone Oriental, Ouaddai, Sila, Wadi Fira et Ennedi Est. 
Cependant, les réfugiés des camps des provinces du Wadi Fira et de l’Ennedi Est n’ont pas encore accepté les résultats du profilage. Les autorités locales et les dirigeants des réfugiés se sont engagés à poursuivre les négociations en vue de faire en sorte que les réfugiés comprennent et acceptent le passage à une assistance fondée sur la vulnérabilité et à communiquer plus clairement la nature de l’assistance à laquelle différentes catégories de réfugiés.
Une stratégie de transition vers le renforcement de la résilience / self reliance des bénéficiaires sera développée et mise en œuvre afin de les appuyers à moyen et long terme. Le PAM soutiendra les réfugiés “les moins vulnérables” par la création et la réhabilitation d’actifs productifs, ainsi que par des transferts monétaires et des kits de moyens de subsistance pour encourager l’agriculture, l’élevage, et le commerce.

project_name: Projet d’assistance nutritionnelle aux enfants 6-23 mois et femmes enceintes et allaitantes pendant la période de soudure au Sahel
project_objective: Les résultats de l’enquête SMART de septembre 2019 indiquent la prévalence de la MAG au niveau national est estimée à 12,9% ; ce qui représente une situation préoccupante d’après la nouvelle classification de l’OMS. Dans neuf (9) des vingt-trois (23) provinces du pays la prévalence de la MAG dépasse le seuil critique de 15% fixé par l’OMS. Quant à la prévalence de la MAS, elle a atteint le seuil d'urgence de 2% dans treize (13) province. Au Tchad l'insécurité alimentaire constitue l'un des facteurs les plus importants qui cause la malnutrition chez les enfants et les femmes surtout durant la période de soudure où les ressources alimentaires s'amenuisent. C'est pour cela que le PAM met en oeuvre un plan de réponse comprenant un ensemble de services destinés à prévenir la malnutrition chez les enfants et les femmes afin de les aider à couvrir leur besoins nutritionnels durant la période critique de soudure.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving and essential Maternal, Newborn and Child health care and nutrition services for vulnerable population in Libya
project_objective: UNICEF in partnership and coordination with health partners including Ministry of Health, National Center for Diseases Control and UN agencies and NGOs will focus on institutional and human resource capacity building enabling them to provide responsive lifesaving and essential health and nutrition services. The activities focus on meeting the needs of the vulnerable children and their families in undeserved and remote areas of the country and in the detention centers. The target population include children under five and Pregnant and Lactating women. The protracted emergency and weak health care delivery exposes most of the population to preventable morbidity and mortality. The health institutions in most of the districts is unable to provide health services to the people in need. The SARA 2017 report remain relevant where average general service readiness based on amenities, equipment, and medicine is 69 percent in hospitals and 37 percent in PHC centers. About 31 percent of the health facilities have no capacity at all to provide any health services. The immunization supply chain system has drastically suffered from the conflict and severe shortage of vaccines have been reported at all levels exposing children to vaccine preventable diseases. During 2019, small scale diseases outbreaks were reported especially in south (Morzuq), Misurata and Benghazi. The national centre for disease control monthly surveillance report shows 590 suspected and 180 confirmed measles and 50 Rubella cases (from Jan to Nv 2019) and also EWARN shows trend of meningitis suspected cases, mainly in Benghazi. Multi Sector Needs Assessment 2019 also indicates urgent need for vaccination and nutrition intervention. In addition, Libya is at risk of polio importation from neighbouring countries (outbreak declared Niger and Chad). In the given situation there is urgent need for strengthening health system for providing preventive and curative lifesaving and essential services to most vulnerable population in the country. This project is expected to contribute significantly in prevention of maternal, neonatal and child morbidity and mortality including vaccine preventable diseases.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Water and Sanitation Services to IDPs, Returnees, Refugees, Migrants and Asylum Seekers.
project_objective:
The project aims to provide life-saving WASH assistances to 100,000 IDPs, migrants, and refugees in the in-need and hosting communities including other locations where humanitarian WASH assistance is needed (such as Al Jabal Al Gharbi, Sabha, Tripoli, Ubari). The project will preposition essential WASH supplies that is sufficient to respond to some 20,000 people in case of emerging humanitarian WASH needs across the country in a timely manner. The project activities include: a) provision of safe water supplies through water trucking, minor rehabilitation of water networks, and installation of water storage tanks. b) provision of safe sanitation facilities through installation of emergency latrines, emptying septic tanks, fumigation of potential areas of contamination, decommissioning of emergency latrines c) Prepositioning and distribution of hygiene items.
The Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) is designed to deliver immediate, life-saving supplies to affected families, most notably food (immediate Response Rations), drinking water and hygiene kits, dignity kits with a focus on women and girls of reproductive age, NFIs, mother/baby kits, basic lifesaving maternal health care kits and vaccines. These services will be provided to persons on the move or displaced due to the armed conflict, hard-to-reach areas, caught at checkpoints or stranded between front-lines within 72 hours of receiving DTM reports, or DTM verification of the needs highlighted by government or non-government partners in letters of assistance submitted to the consortium. The overall goal of the Libya Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism is to save lives and mitigate negative impact of acute crisis on lives and dignity of affected groups with emphasis on vulnerable groups especially women and children. It is expected that RRM will be able to reach affected population with hygiene kits along with other necessary critical supplies at the early onset of a crisis. The intervention will be a geographical focus based on a vulnerability in given locations of displacement and will precede or complement the sectoral response, but delivery will remain affected by insecurity, accessibility, logistics…etc.

project_name: Strenghtening sector coordination mechanism to support the humanitarian response in Libya
project_objective:
Operating in Libya remains challenging, with numerous security, logistical and access constraints. Strong and effective sector coordination mechanism is required to ensure humanitarian action is timely, effective & meets the needs of vulnerable people. Collaboration with national/International Humanitarian actors and Human Rights organizations are critical to ensure that assistance is provided safely and respects people’s dignity.  
Functional sectors and inter sector coordination group support humanitarian actors with coordination, information management, needs assessments, advocacy for access, safety and protection. It will benefit the entire humanitarian community to effectively and timely reach the most vulnerable people in Libya, as well as to sustain and extend their members’ operational reach and impact.

The annual review of existing common coordination mechanisms and structures, includes the review of the sectors and the Inter-Sector Coordination Group, ensuring that the system is fit per purpose and able to deliver as expected.  
Information management products, Periodic Monitoring Reports, dashboards and snapshots are key elements well functioning sectors and ISCGs should deliver as they constitute the primary source of information for planning and decision-making.

project_name: Provide air services to the humanitarian community
project_objective:
Because safe overland and air transport options are limited, WFP will continue to run the
United Nations Humanitarian Air Service to enable humanitarian workers to reach most
areas. The service provides regularly scheduled fights to 61 destinations each week, with
special flights for IRRM teams, special visits and emergency evacuations. It trains civil
aviation personnel and supports an air traffic management project to improve the safety
of South Sudanese airspace.

project_name: Provision of Protective Services to Children and Caregivers Affected by the Conflict
project_objective:
Ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine continues to weaken child protection systems creating
new risks for affected boys, girls and their caregivers. To respond to the urgent needs,
UNICEF is planning to strengthen child protection systems (C01) and to provide direct
services to affected children and their families (CO2). Specifically, UNICEF will continue to
provide psycho-social and protective services to children and their caregivers (including to
survivors of gender-based violence, to children affected by violence and to children
affected by mines and unexploded ordinance) (P02), invest in activities aimed at
prevention (violence, mine-risk education) (P01) and ensure capacity building to
community professionals working with children (P02). In addition, UNICEF will carry out
activities directed at improving parenting skills among caregivers to improve and
strengthen relationships between caregivers and their children. Taken together, these
activities are aimed to strengthen local response systems, including availability of
specialized services, as well as to ensure direct service provision where needed services
are not available.

project_name: UNICEF Humanitarian & Recovery WASH response in Eastern Ukraine 2020
project_objective:
UNICEF intends to support the Coordination in the WASH sector, essential to strategize and optimize the intervention of all actors in WASH.
After reviewing different assessments, keeping in view the situations in East, needs, capacity and comparative advantage, UNICEF is planning to respond the needs of 1.6 million individuals in the two conflict affected areas of Donetska and Luhanska oblasts (GCA and NGCA), with provision of safe drinking water, improving access to safe sanitation and hygiene supplies, dissemination of critical water and hygiene related messages on communities located on both side of contact line in Donetsk and Luhansk, in Eastern Ukraine. This will be implemented through the water utility companies (centralized network of primary and secondary water suppliers) and decentralized structures (in NGCA). A particular focus will be made on WASH in social institutions (education/health facilities) on both GCA and NGCA.
The different activities take into account the gender, age and disabilities specificities and promote equality, especially on gender. People reached with more than one activity are only considered once to avoid duplication in counting beneficiaries.

project_name: UNICEF Education in Emergencies Response 2020
project_objective: UNICEF response will serve children and teachers with essential interventions that will ensure continuation of education in the time of protracted conflict and address its immediate and cumulative impacts. 43,500 boys and girls will benefit from a range of activities that ensure their access to safe, inclusive and enabling learning environment and improve quality of teaching and learning. Over three fourths of these boys and girls live and learn in NGCA where humanitarian needs are most severe. 700 education professionals in NGCA and GCA will be trained on identified priority topics that enable them to deliver conflict-sensitive, risk-informed and life-skills-based education. UNICEF will work with the Ukraine Education Cluster partners to contribute to the policy and advocacy efforts aimed at the Government’s signature and implementation of the ‘Safe Schools Declaration’, a political commitment to protect schools during armed conflict.

project_name: Emergency Food Security  and livelihood assistance to conflict affected population in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The regions surrounding the Lake Chad basin have been embroiled in a decade-long conflict with the three North East Nigerian states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) bearing the brunt of the violence. The conflict has severely disrupted food production systems resulting in high levels of displacement and extensive human and socio-economic losses. According to the Recovery and Peacebuilding Assessment (RPBA) undertaken by the World Bank in 2016, the conflict has resulted in losses of USD 3.7 billion caused by the destruction of farmland, animals and infrastructure.
Acute food insecurity persists at alarming levels. Findings of the October 2019 Cadre Harmonisé analysis highlight that, between October and December 2019, approximately three million people in the BAY states will face acute levels of food insecurity (Phase 3 and above).Moreover, the prevalence of acute malnutrition is high, with GAM rates in Yobe (11.5 percent), Borno (8.1 percent) and Adamawa (7.2 percent) under pressure. As a result, the mortality rate in all three states is equally under pressure.   

FAO has had a permanent presence in the BAY states since 2015, implementing lifesaving interventions in the form of emergency food security, nutrition and livelihoods support to IDPs, returnees and host communities affected by the crisis. Despite these ongoing efforts, without sustained and expanded humanitarian assistance the number of people experiencing acute food insecurity is projected to increase by up to 50 percent by the onset of the 2020 lean season (June – August).  

The overall objective is to improve food security and nutrition among conflict-affected communities through the restoration, protection and promotion of sustainable and environmentally friendly Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral-based livelihoods. This will be achieved via the distribution of essential inputs/assets and capacity building targeting vulnerable households in both rural and urban / peri-urban communities; the creation of sustainable livelihood opportunities and decent employment in the agriculture, livestock and aquaculture sectors; and the promotion of value addition via the formation of cooperatives, group savings and loans, and market linkages. In addition, Safe Access to Fuel and Energy (SAFE) will be promoted
More specifically, the proposed intervention includes the following activities:

•	Support to land preparation including distribution of rainy season and dry season kits (seeds and fertilizer) for crop production as well as essential inputs for backyard vegetable gardening to restore/protect agricultural livelihoods and promote household nutrition.

•	Animal restocking targeting women and youth with goat, sheep and poultry packages for income generation and improved nutrition.

•	Vaccination campaign to control animal diseases aimed at protecting livestock-based livelihoods; biosecurity/biocontainment training for disease control, food safety and animal welfare to key associations/groups of animal workers.

•	Distribution of aquaculture kits (tanks, feed, fingerlings) to unemployed fisherfolk linked with the provision of fish processing assets (smoking kilns) and training to vulnerable women’s groups.

•	Distribution of assets (bulls and ploughs) and training to unemployed rural youth to promote entrepreneurship in land development services.

•	Establishment/upgrading of fuel-efficient stove production centres and distribution of fuel-efficient stoves to households facing heightened protection and health risks; mitigate poor energy access and adoption of negative coping strategies. 
More Specifically the proposed intervention includes the following activities;

•	Organization of beneficiaries into local agribusiness cooperatives supported with training and seed money towards establishing group savings and loans to promote upscaling and resilience building

project_name: Providing multi-sectoral assistance in and improving living conditions of IDP sites in north-west Syria
project_objective:

The project aims to address the Objective 1 (Provide and coordinate streamlined humanitarian lifesaving, multi-sectoral assistance and strengthen the basic infrastructure support in IDP sites) through:

The project plans to meet the Objective 2 (Improve the management quality in and accountability of IDP sites) through:

The project would contribute to the Objective 3 (Strengthen household and communal coping mechanisms in IDP sites) through:

Finally, the project aims to meet the objective 4 (Inform the CCCM response of cluster members) through:

The project will be directly managed, in cooperation with CCCM Cluster Coordinator, by IOM Turkey cross border team based in Gaziantep. IOM will directly implement the blended remote CCCM training, and for the rest, IOM will work in partnership with well-experienced local NGOs in each specific activity in camps and camp-like settings as implementing partners, selected from active members of the CCCM Cluster.

project_name: Projet d’appui au relèvement précoce sur les moyens d'existence et au renforcement de la résilience aux chocs des communautés vulnérables du Mali
project_objective:
Le Cadre Harmonisé de Mars 2020 met en lumière une grave détérioration de la situation de sécurité alimentaire au Mali. Les besoins ont augmenté de 29 % par rapport à la même période en 2019. Plus frappant encore, les besoins ont également augmenté de 32% par rapport à la période de soudure de 2019 à 2020, période de l'année où les stocks alimentaires sont épuisés et les ressources les plus sollicitées. À l'heure actuelle, on estime que 3,6 millions de personnes souffrent d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dont 760 000 en situation de grave insécurité alimentaire (phase 3 à 5 du ICP). La situation devrait se détériorer pendant la période de soudure 2020, avec près de 5 millions de personnes en situation d'insécurité alimentaire, dont près de 1,4 million en situation d'insécurité alimentaire grave (IPC 3 à 5). Les régions les plus touchées sont Mopti (41% des besoins), Gao/Ménaka (18% des besoins). La bande sahélienne est également touchée, en particulier la région de Kayes (15% des besoins) et celle de Koulikoro (12 % des besoins). La situation nutritionnelle globale du pays reste également préoccupante avec 10 % de MAG (SMART Sept ; 19). 
L'insécurité alimentaire n'est plus saisonnière mais affecte les personnes toute l’année.  Les chocs climatiques (sécheresses et inondations) et les ravageurs et maladies agricoles (légionnaire de chenille ou ver de l'armée) affectant la bande sahélienne du Mali aggravent la situation de sécurité alimentaire et de nutrition en 2020. 
Bien que l'insécurité alimentaire soit principalement associée aux chocs de production, depuis 2018 et en 2019, le conflit et l'instabilité sont devenus de plus en plus les principaux moteurs de l'insécurité alimentaire, en particulier dans le centre du Mali où l'on estime que 30 % de la population y vit.
Cette situation de sécurité alimentaire déjà alarmante devra se dégrader davantage à cause des effets de l’épidémie de COVID-19 au Mali. Les dernières analyses sur la situation alimentaire du pays montrent une dégradation de la sécurité alimentaire et des moyens d’existence des ménages. En effet les résultats de l’enquête mVAM (mobile Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping) réalisée à distance entre le 17 avril et le 5 mai 2020 auprès de 972 ménages dans le cadre du système de suivi de la situation de sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle mis en place par le Système d’Alerte Précoce avec l’appui du PAM, FEWSNET, FAO et les clusters sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle indique une détérioration de la consommation alimentaire des ménages de 6 points par rapport à la dernière évaluation nationale réalisée entre février et début mai 2020 et un recours accru aux stratégies d’adaptation négatives en raison des effets combinés de la saisonnalité et de la COVID-19.
Les activités de résilience nécessitant les grands regroupements sur le terrain ont été dans suspendues en application des mesures anti-COVID-19 prises par le gouvernement. Les autres activités ne nécessitant pas de grands regroupements ont été adaptées. Des kits anti-COVID ont été fournis afin de réaliser les distributions de cash. Trois mois après la suspension, l’ensemble des activités de résilience reprendront en s’adaptant au contexte COVID. Le PAM souhaite cibler les communautés vulnérables qui font face de façon récurrente à l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle en leur fournissant un paquet intégré visant à renforcer sur le moyen terme leurs moyens d’existence et leur résilience aux chocs ainsi que la cohésion sociale dans les zones affectées par le conflit. Le PAM continuera également à renforcer les capacités du Ministère de l’Agriculture et des services techniques décentralisés sur les questions de ciblage, de mise en œuvre de programmes de réhabilitation d’actifs productifs, de suivi et d’évaluation. Conformément à la politique du PAM sur l’égalité du Genre "" engagements renforcés en faveur des femmes “, la protection et l'autonomisation des femmes seront une priorité programmatique

project_name: Food assistance to conflict-affected populations across Northern Syria
project_objective:
In light of the acute needs outlined above, PIN proposes an integrated, multi-sector intervention to support the most vulnerable in Northern Syria to meet their basic needs in the aftermath of rapid onset crises, improve their food security, and (re)establish livelihoods. Interventions will be informed by detailed needs, market, and protection risk assessments, with geographical and household (HH) targeting based on the severity of needs and HH economic analysis. PIN will provide life-saving and life-sustaining cash-based assistance in support of basic needs and food security, drawing on extensive experience in cash-based assistance, food security and livelihoods to maximize response impact and mitigate risks. 
First-line emergency response activities (mainly distributions of RTERs) are anticipated to be largely focussed on Idlib and Western Aleppo governorates; however, PIN will retain capacity to launch rapid responses in NES as required. Activities will be underpinned by emergency preparedness and response plans developed in coordination with relevant clusters, working groups, and partners – including the Cash Working Group (CWG), Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), WASH, S/NFI and CCCM clusters – to promote timely, efficient and joined-up responses that seek to maximize geographic and sectoral coverage and minimize gaps. Result 2 will focus upon assisting vulnerable, conflict-affected households to meet their basic food needs and (re)establish livelihoods. Activities will target the most vulnerable households in communities chronically affected by the adverse impacts of the conflict, using common assistance modalities and selection criteria, as established in the FSL and Early Recovery Clusters and CWG. Under this result PIN will plan to reach beneficiaries with monthly food assistance (food baskets, food vouchers), agriculture vouchers and farmer field schools and bakery support. 
PIN does not target based on status, including both Internally Displaced People (IDPs) and host community members meeting eligibility and vulnerability criteria, to avoid creating tensions within and across communities. Selection criteria have been elaborated in consultation with the affected communities, as well as based on evidence from previous project monitoring and community feedback obtained through the Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM), and include low income families from the following groups: Female-headed households (HH); Child-headed HH; Elderly-headed HH; HH with disabled and chronically ill members; HH with high dependency ratio; Unemployed male and female youth; Poor farming HH. PIN is aware that needs are different amongst gender and age groups, and other vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities. 
PIN aims to provide most needed assistance to such groups through: employing a wide spectrum of different activities to meet distinct need, establishing beneficiary selection criteria to prioritise inclusion of those most vulnerable and adapting its assistance delivery to promote access for the most vulnerable people. PINs programmes are carried out in coordination with local authorities at various levels – from cross-border, to hub, to district and village level. PIN engages in regular dialogue with authorities to ensure transparency, accountability, and protection mainstreaming. This includes consultations and briefings on needs, humanitarian principles, PIN procedures, and beneficiary selection at the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation stages of projects.
