project_name: Mine Action in Syria
project_objective:
The HALO Trust will continue to deliver a comprehensive approach to Mine Action in NW Syria through three implementing partners, involving Enhanced Contamination Impact Survey (ECIS), Risk Education (RE), and Victim Assistance (VA). HALO will also extend the scope of its activities to include Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and the disposal and clearance of Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) in NW Syria, and also aim to expand operations into areas controlled by the Government of Syria (GoS).

In late 2020, HALO will complete its ongoing ECIS work in NW Syria, surveying the remaining 225 accessible communities across Idleb and Aleppo. The continuation of this activity through 2020 will provide ERW contamination data that will immediately improve community ERW awareness and safety, as well as identify priority areas for RE and future NTS and disposal/clearance.

HALO will provide RE to 43,400 beneficiaries in 2020 (8,212 men, 6,538 women, 15,829 boys, 12,821 girls), with 1,372 ‘Training of Trainer’ (ToT) trainees (e.g. other NGO workers and Community Focal Points) being included as RE beneficiaries. A particular emphasis will be put on those who are most at risk of accidents (including children, young men, and IDPs). As part of this effort, RE ToT trainers will continue to support NGOs and Community Focal Points currently delivering RE to vulnerable communities and IDPs, improving the relevance, integration, and reach of RE messaging across all relevant humanitarian sectors.

HALO will continue to collect information about ERW accidents and victims through Victim Data Collection (VDC) to better understand how and why accidents occur and provide referrals to survivors in need. This will enable HALO and other actors to better tailor ECIS, RE, and VA activities to the needs of the beneficiaries.

In 2020, HALO and two of its implementing partners will continue to implement VA activities in NW Syria. HALO’s initial reach will be 4,542 beneficiaries through 3 x rehabilitation centres run by HALO’s partner, providing physiotherapy, psycho-social support (PSS), peer support counselling, orthopaedic services and speech therapy, 3 x mobile units, and multi-purpose assistance. Referrals to 3 x prosthetics centres run by other health organisations will also be provided. To promote workplace inclusion, up to 7 survivors will be recruited, trained, and employed by one of HALO’s partners, while inclusion training to other NGOs and a small apprenticeship pilot will also be run. Through another partner, HALO will provide inclusive livelihood opportunities and referrals to specialised services. 240 beneficiaries (185 men, 55 women) will participate in vocational training, workplace internships and be eligible for micro-business grants, or receive agricultural/livestock assistance. Case management staff will assist a further 240 beneficiaries by referring them to other specialised services. Overall, HALO and its implementing partners will reach 5,022 beneficiaries across its 2020 activities.

HALO will also introduce an NTS and ERW disposal capability in NW Syria, implemented through at least one of its partners. This capability will expand directly on the outcomes of HALO’s ECIS work and will be based on its experience in southern Syria in 2018. HALO, through its Turkish partner, has engaged with Turkish authorities at the governorate level and has received informal positive feedback, official approval will not occur until the project has been approved.

Additionally, subject to obtaining registration from GoS, HALO seeks to contribute to the introduction of a pilot ERW clearance capability in areas controlled by GoS. HALO will aim to prioritize areas highly impacted by the conflict where widespread ERW contamination is expected.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of quality health services to conflict affected host communities and IDPs in Banadir, Bakool, Lower Shabelle, Nugaal and Bay regions in Somalia
project_objective:
The proposed project will be implemented in 4 districts in Bakool (Xudur,wajid,rabdhuure and Elbarde), 3 in Banadir (Kahda,hodan,abdiaziz) ,1 in Lower Shabelle region (Afgooye) , 2 districts in Nugaal region(Garowe and Eyl) and 1 district in Bay region (Baidoa) to cover Health needs of internally displaced people and host community women, men, boys and girls.
The project seeks to reduce Reduce of excess morbidity and mortality due disease outbreak driven by climatic shocks and conflict among 1.6 million IDPs and non-displaced by 5% by end of 2020 emergency levels of acute malnutrition through integrated multisector response in line with 2019 strategic objective 2 for Somalia. The primary targets of the project are U5 boys and girls and pregnant and lactating women in 11 districts in Somalia. In line with the Essential Package of Health services. Action Against Hunger will through support to Ministry of Health and direct delivery of services provide the following core services through 3 levels of service delivery i.e Health centre, Primary Health unit (PHU) and Community outreach.
A.	Maternal, reproductive and neonatal health
 Action Against Hunger will provide basic obstetric and neonatal care in supported Health centres. The supported facilities will be equipped with maternity beds for 24 hour observation of post delivery cases. Other services which will be provided through the health centre would include; family planning counseling and service delivery, antenatal care, post natal care, safe delivery care, immunization, nutrition (Micronutrient supplementation and education) etc.  
B.	Child health
ACF will train the medical staff of the health center so as to diagnose and treat childhood illnesses based on the IMCI guidelin Health centres., The following services will be provided to children: treatment of acute respiratory illness (ARI), Diarheal diseases and Management of Anemia. ICCM package will be provided at the community level by CHWs. 
C.	EPI
Routine immunization for both underfive children and women of reproductive age will be provided. Mid- year micro planning involving the local community through the Health Committee and the MOH would be held. 
The project will integrate with other sectors such as WASH, food security and protection. The program’s approach involves both men and women while acknowledging their respective roles and needs, and fostering mutual awareness and partnership. Recognizing that child care in Somalia is mainly considered a female role, the project will take into account the socially constructed roles for each gender ensuring that women do not spend so much time in the project at the expense of their other children who are not malnourished, while also seeking to influence them. The project will also target men to encourage them to take an active role in better child care practices, while also improving women’s knowledge on infant feeding and care. The project seeks to enhance the capacity of community and Ministry of health staff to provide life saving services and build community resilience . The activities will be implemented in line with Ministry of health/WHO/UNICEF guidelines. A total of 1,492,108 persons including 298422 women of child bearing age ,151195 boys and 152195 girls, , 60 staff (20 men and 40 women) will be targeted for a period of 12 months.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Acute Malnutrition for Affected Communities, Especially Girls and Boys Under Five and Pregnant and Lactating Women, in South Sudan
project_objective: Despite a period of relative stability over the past year, the malnutrition and food insecurity situation across South Sudan remains critical. According to Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) projections for January - April 2020, over 5.5 million people (47% of the population) are predicted to be severely food insecure (IPC 3, 4 & 5), even considering the presence of humanitarian assistance. Levels of acute malnutrition and food insecurity are expected to rise in early 2019 as post-harvest stocks become depleted.  Recent SMART surveys conducted in all major counties of Action Against Hunger’s interventions show GAM rates above the emergency threshold of 15%: GAM prevalence in Fangak, Gogrial West, and Aweil East was 16.2%, 20.1%, and 15.5%, respectively, while SAM prevalence was 3.3%, 4.3%, and 1.6%, respectively. Ongoing insecurity, poor hygiene and sanitation infrastructure, limited availability of diverse and nutritious food in local markets, low coverage of health and immunization services, and constrained and livelihoods opportunities exacerbate these conditions. To address these issues, Action Against Hunger will continue its programs for the treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition in Warrap, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Jonglei States in 2020. The program will directly target 40,772 children under 5 and 26,106 pregnant and lactating women in treatment of acute malnutrition at 3 stabilization centers and 33 nutrition sites (OTP/TSFP). In total, 33,833 caregivers will be sensitized on MIYCN topics. Treatment programs will prioritize the identification and treatment of children under five with SAM and MAM, as well as PLW with MAM, through outpatient therapeutic programs (OTP) and targeted supplementary feeding programs (TSFP). Stablization centers (SCs) in Alek, Malulakon, and Paguir will provide treatment to children with SAM and medical complications. In the hard-to-reach area of Paguir, we will also introduce ICCM and mobile delivery of OTP/TSFP (ICCM+) to increase coverage for communities facing seasonal stress migration. Caregivers will receive sensitization and counselling on MIYCN, health, and hygiene/sanitation practices, and critical gender- and age-sensitive hygiene items. To ensure early detection and referral of acute malnutrition, community volunteers will be trained to lead active screening and referral at the household level. During these screenings, volunteers will also provide sensitization on nutrition and hygiene/sanitation practices. Prevention activities will focus on community mobilization and sensitization as well as addressing the underlying causes of malnutrition. These activities include training community leaders, hosting mass awareness campaigns around MIYCN and hygiene/sanitation topics, promoting mother-to-mother support groups (MtMSG), and facilitating men’s discussion groups (MGDs) to encourage discussion among male caregivers on critical nutrition and health subjects. To address underlying causes of undernutrition, Action Against Hunger will train lead mothers of MtMSGs in kitchen gardening and cooking demonstrations. In addition to these static interventions, Action Against Hunger’s emergency response teams will also continue to provide malnutrition surveillance, treatment and prevention services, and capacity building throughout the country in areas of highest need as identified by the Nutrition Cluster’s Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism.

project_name: Programme de prévention contre les dangers liés aux engins explosifs et aux armes légères et de petit calibre
project_objective:
En 2019 et au début de l’année 2020, le contexte socio-politique et humanitaire du Mali a été marqué par la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à travers des attaques armées contre plusieurs villages dans le centre du Mali, accouplé à la recrudescence des incidents liés aux engins explosifs, incluant les Restes Explosifs de Guerre (REG), les Engins Explosifs Improvisés (EEI), les mines ; mais aussi à la prolifération des Armes Légères et de Petit Calibre (ALPC). Ces menaces sont une préoccupation réelle en terme de menace à la vie, mais aussi de contrainte d’accès des populations aux services humanitaires et sociaux de base, et multiplient les conflits armés intercommunautaires dont le nombre de victimes civiles ne cesse de s’accumuler.

En effet, 151 des 251 incidents d’engins explosifs improvisés (EEI) enregistrés sur la période (60%) ont eu lieu au centre du Mali, et représentent 92,5 % des victimes civiles identifiées (221 des 239 victimes).
Les engins explosifs improvisés posés généralement sur les principaux axes routiers, créent des restrictions majeures pour les déplacements des acteurs humanitaires et de la population. Les axes reliant Mopti, centre du pays, avec les régions du nord sont particulièrement touchés (axes Mopti-Douentza-Boni-Mondoro, Mopti-Douentza-Tombouctou et Mopti-Gossi-Gao). L’attaque du 7 juin 2020 sur la route de Douentza en est une illustration avec une soixantaine de victimes, dont 7 morts et 53 blessés. 
Grâce aux efforts des acteurs humanitaires dans l’éducation aux risques, une réduction du nombre de victimes de REG a été enregistrée, d’où la pertinence de la continuité des activités de sensibilisation et de prévention.
En plus d’un contexte sécuritaire fragilisé, le contexte sanitaire s’est détérioré avec l’épidémie du Covid-19 qui affecte et menace gravement la vie de milliers de personnes sur l’ensemble du territoire du Mali. 
Les acteurs de la lutte antimines continueront la sensibilisation des populations sur les dangers liés aux engins explosifs et aux ALPC, en vue d’avoir un comportement adéquat et contribuer à la réduction des incidents. Ils cibleront les populations à risque, notamment les agriculteurs, les éleveurs, les nomades, les PDIs, les retournés et les rapatriés, et les personnes en situation de handicap. Vu que les enfants sont une catégorie à risque et que plus de 1000 écoles sont fermées en 2019, affectant plus de 300 milles élèves, les séances d’éducation aux risques cibleront en plus des élèves les enfants non- scolarisés.
Il visera aussi à renforcer les capacités des ONGs locales en éducation aux risques, enquête non technique et liaison communautaire pour le rapportage, l’identification et le référencement des victimes.
Ce projet sera mis en œuvre avec la participation des acteurs locaux (ONG nationales et les institutions publiques) et impliquera les communautés bénéficiaires pour les informer et les impliquer dans les différentes étapes du processus de planification, mis en œuvre et évaluation. Un accent sera mis sur l'analyse de la vulnérabilité des besoins liés au genre et sans aucune forme de discrimination.
Activités :

1. Education aux Risques des Engins Explosifs (Mine, REG, EEI) et des ALPC: la stratégie de l’éducation aux risques (ER) des engins explosifs des communautés en situation d’urgence sera adaptée en fonction des besoins, des disponibilités, des coutumes et des croyances tout en observant les mesures barrières dans le cadre de la prévention du Covid-19. 
2. Enquêtes Non Techniques : les NTS seront effectuées dans les localités pour évaluer le niveau de la menace explosive. Les enquêtes se feront à travers des entretiens au niveau communautaire et les informations sont analysées afin de planifier les interventions en terme d'actions spécifiques.
3. Liaison communautaire
4. Identification et référencement des victimes d’engins explosifs et d’ALPC

project_objective:
Le présent projet d’Urgence Santé Nutrition, qui s’appuie sur les résultats de la dernière enquête SMART diffusée par le MSSP en janvier 2020,  s’inscrit dans un contexte d’Insécurité Alimentaire et un taux de prévalence de la MAG supérieur aux seuils acceptables, contribuera à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité liées à la malnutrition chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans par une approche de renforcement des capacités des structures de santé existantes et des communautés à travers les ASCP (sous la supervision du personnel de santé du MSPP). Ce projet, avec des activités de sensibilisation, prévention, formation et distribution de nutriments,  aura un impact sur toute la population, avec un focus sur les parents ou donneurs de soin des enfants de moins de 5 ans, les femmes enceintes et allaitantes, qui bénéficieront de messages d’éducation nutritionnelle pour promouvoir les bonnes pratiques nutritionnelles, d’hygiènes et d'enregistrement des naissances. Le projet cible aussi les adolescents ainsi que les hommes au cours des activités de sensibilisation sur l’ ANJE et l’hygiène. Cela permettra de créer une masse critique de personnes sensibilisées pour assurer la transmission des messages clefs au niveau communautaire et pérenniser ainsi les interventions du programme.

project_name: Project to support the fight against acute malnutrition in the health district of Tillia, Tahoua Region, Niger-  2020
project_objective:
Le projet s’inscrit donc dans une logique de continuité du projet en cours avec une note SR, dans le District Sanitaire de Tillia, où la situation sécuritaire demeure toujours précaire. Action Contre la Faim propose pour ce faire une intervention intégrée en santé/Nutrition et Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA) qui visera l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations hôtes et déplacées, victimes du conflit et se déclinera tout d’abord, au niveau des structures de santé, par un appui au niveau de l’aire de santé du Telemcès du district sanitaire concernant la PEC de la MAS et par l’amélioration des conditions d’hygiène. L'objectif est de soutenir le système de santé dans la prise en charge et le suivi de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants 6 à 59 mois en formant le personnel du CSI de Telemcès, dans le DS de Tillia, en partageant des outils de contrôle du stock et en gérant les ressources humaines. Les supervisions formatives (coaching) seront toujours d’actualité et viendront en complément dans le but de renforcer de manière individualisée les compétences des professionnels de santé. La présence régulière des équipes d'ACF a pour principal objectif de garantir l'application correcte du protocole de PCIMA tout en renforçant les compétences et l'autonomie des agents de santé. Un renforcement des installations des centres de santé sera fait avec du matériel médical et des outils nécessaires pour assurer une prise en charge de qualité. Une supervision formative quotidienne devra être mise en œuvre. Pour compléter cet appui, un accent particulier sera porté sur les indicateurs de la santé de la reproduction au regard de la situation sus-décrite et des besoins qui en découlent. Il s'agira d'appuyer les formations sanitaires pour la délivrance d'un paquet de soins prénataux de qualité (CPN effective) aux femmes enceintes comprenant la supplémentation en fer acide folique, le traitement Préventif et Intermittent (TPI) du paludisme, les conseils nutritionnels, la promotion de l'allaitement maternel exclusif, le déparasitage et la vaccination antitétanique. L’accouchement par un personnel qualifié et le suivi post-partum (CPON) seront mis en amont afin de réduire les décès maternels et néonatals. La communication pour le développement sera la pierre angulaire de la réussite de cette action. Pour ce faire, 17 matrones seront identifiées et formées sur l’alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant (ANJE), de la FEFA, et le suivi de la grossesse. Aussi, elles joueront un rôle primordial dans la diffusion des messages et le suivi quotidien des femmes enceintes et allaitante. ACF prendra en charge les évacuations sanitaires des urgences obstétricales pour les couches vulnérables. Afin de prévenir les grossesses à risque et les décès maternels en raison des grossesses rapprochées, ACF mettra un point d’honneur sur la sensibilisation et l’éducation des femmes afin de rehausser le taux d’adhésion aux méthodes contraceptives modernes d’ici la fin de la seconde phase du projet.
L’intervention WASH proposée vise à accompagner les structures de santé du district sanitaire de Tillia dans la prise en charge et la prévention de la malnutrition aigüe sévère. 
Il s’agira d’assurer le suivi du paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé pour l’amélioration du traitement de la MAS et aussi de développer les capacités des acteurs de la santé et des communautés en matière de prévention de la malnutrition. Ceci se fera à travers :  
- Le renforcement de capacités et accompagnement du personnel (agents de santé et hygiénistes) sur la gestion des déchets biomédicaux et la prévention et désinfection du choléra / Hépatite E
- La distribution de kits WASH aux couples mères-enfants malnutris admis dans le programme de traitement de la malnutrition aiguë
- La construction et/ou réhabilitation des ouvrages d’eau et d’assainissement au niveau des structures de santé et dans les villages appartenant aux aires de santé en fonction des besoins i

project_name: Support to Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit (FSNAU) of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
project_objective:
Given the precarious food security, nutrition and livelihood situation across Somalia, conducting timely assessments and analysis on a regular basis and continuous monitoring of the situation remains vital. At present, the Government of Somalia has limited institutional and technical capacity to generate and provide such data. To fill this gap, the FAO-led Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit (FSNAU) provides critical and timely information and analyses on the food security and nutrition situation in Somalia to a broad range of stakeholders.  FSNAU information and analyses facilitate and support effective evidence based decision-making in support of humanitarian, recovery and development interventions. 

FSNAU identifies food insecure populations by livelihood and by district, pinpoints the specific challenges facing vulnerable groups, including women in achieving food security and reports on the population’s nutritional status to support targeted interventions. In addition to its early warning function, FSNAU carries out relevant baseline livelihood studies for an improved understanding of underlying causes of food, nutrition and livelihood insecurity. Gender analysis is an integral part of FSNAU’s data collection analytical process. FSNAU also provides food security and nutrition related technical and institutional capacity development support to Somali government institutions and other key actors.

In 2020, FSNAU will continue to provide information and analysis on current and emerging food security and nutrition situation in Somalia in a manner that supports prioritization and targeting of appropriate response. FSNAU will also provide additional information through its Early Warning Early Action Dashboard in order to support timely and prioritized response. Staff of relevant government institutions at Federal level, Federal Member State level and Somaliland will also be trained and supported to participate in seasonal food security and nutrition assessments and analyses.

FSNAU information products are disseminated through the FSNAU website (www.fsnau.org), mailing list and through regular as well as ad hoc presentations to stakeholders, including the Somalia Humanitarian Country Team.

The main beneficiaries of the information and analysis generated by FSNAU under this project will be government line ministries, UN agencies, local and international NGOs and resource partners. FSNAU currently has 2 365 users on its mailing list.  The FSNAU website also attracts visits from a large and diverse number of users (over 38 000 visits in 2018). Indirect FSNAU project beneficiaries will be the 6.3 million food insecure people (based on October-December 2019 projection) who are expected to benefit from humanitarian assistance and livelihood support provided by the Government, UN agencies, local and international NGOs and resource partners.

FSNAU and REACH provide complementary information and analysis to IASC Clusters in and the HRP/HNO process in Somalia. FSNAU primarily provides information and analyses that support the Food Security and Nutrition Clusters and REACH provides support to the other IASC clusters in Somalia.

project_name: Enhancing livestock value chain development to restore and diversify vulnerable livelihoods in North East Nigeria
project_objective:
The now decade-long Boko Haram insurgency has exacerbated an already fragile socio-economic and livelihood system in North East Nigeria, with Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) states the most affected. The conflict has negatively affected livelihoods, social cohesion, human security, the natural environment, and the overall growth prospects of people in the region. The result has been the loss of lives, high levels of food insecurity and malnutrition, the depletion of livelihoods and high levels of displacement. 

Findings of the October 2019 Cadre Harmonisé analysis highlight that, between October and December 2019, approximately three million people in the BAY states will face acute levels of food insecurity (Phase 3 and above) and will be in urgent need of assistance. 

The interventions will involve livestock restocking, value chain development and veterinary support. Vulnerable households will be targeted with bulls, ewes/rams, goats or poultry interventions. Targeted populations will include IDPs, returnees and agro-pastoralist communities with minimal assets. Through this intervention, FAO will build the capacity of state veterinary services and community-based animal health workers in the region. These groups will provide animal health services to project beneficiaries and to other vulnerable livestock owners. 

The crisis has also severely affected households who depend on the livestock value chain and has had a significant impact on the availability of highly nutritious food such as meat, milk and eggs. Many IDPs whose livelihoods relied solely on animal production have had their animals rustled or killed. There is, therefore, a crucial need to restock key income generating livestock assets such as goats, rams, sheep, bulls and poultry. This will enable households, particularly women and youth IDPs, to revive and boost their livestock production. This intervention is also aimed at supporting the targeted beneficiaries especially youth and women with bulls as an alternative source of livelihood opportunities and income generation from the sale of bulls after fattening.

project_objective: Concern will continue to support preventative and curative services in Aweil West and Aweil North in NBeG, Bentiu PoC and Guit in Unity and Juba PoC in Central Equatoria. Concern will emphasise prevention of MAM and SAM in this response through focus on behaviour change communication to improve MIYCN practices. In NBeG, the Health programme will support lead mothers and MCAs to improve health practices to reduce common illness that result in malnutrition. project_name: Appui à la population vulnérable pour la prévention et à la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans et les femmes enceintes
project_objective:
Ainsi Concern s'engage à accompagner et à soutenir les deux districts de Tahoua et les deux CRENI (CRENI du CHR et CRENI du Centre de Santé de la Mère et de l'Enfant de Tahoua) à pouvoir maintenir un mécanisme pérenne de prévention et de traitement de la malnutrition aiguë sévère et modérée. En s'appuyant sur les actions des projets de ce type mises en œuvre en 2018 et 2019, tournant autour des actions de renforcement des capacités au niveau des structures de santé (cela au travers de l'implémentation des approches novatrices ayant fait ses preuves : Approche CMAM Surge, Approche collaboratif PCIMA).
Au cours de l'année 2020, nous tablerons sur une plus grande implication et l'appropriation du niveau communautaire, l'implication plus importante et renforcement des capacités des COGES, et aussi le plaidoyer à tous les niveaux en faveur de la nutrition à travers trois résultats.
Le résultat 1 concernera le renforcement des capacités des agents de structures de santé appuyées à assurer la PCIMA au sein de 2 Districts Sanitaires au travers de l'accompagnement des structures à gérer les urgences et les pics de la malnutrition. Concern souhaite permettre l'accès du couple mère-enfant à un paquet minimum de prestations médicales axées sur une approche préventive multisectorielle et curative de la Malnutrition Aiguë afin de garantir la prise en charge nutritionnelle de qualité et une action couplée en sécurité alimentaire en faveur des populations les plus vulnérables et s’appuiera aussi sur d’autres projets financés par d'autres bailleurs dans la même zone d'intervention et mises en œuvre par Concern (Financement de l'Union Européen en consortium avec le GRET : ""Projet d'Appui à la fortification des aliments au Niger"" et projet Wadata Al'umma sous le financement du gouvernement Irlandais. L'accessibilité géographique restant une barrière à une couverture adéquate de PCIMA, Concern travaille à un élargissement de la couverture PCIMA dans les Centres de Santé (CS) éloignés en mettant en œuvre l'approche iCCM+ implémenté en pilote par l'ONG ACF-E au Niger et qui consistera à proposer une prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère au niveau des CS par du personnel qualifié sous quelques modalités de suivi et de monitoring stricts mis en place en collaboration avec la Direction de la Nutrition. Le résultat 2 constituera à continuer à soutenir les Districts Sanitaires dans la gestion des intrants nutritionnels avec un transfert de compétence et de responsabilité aux DS à travers l'appui d'un expert en gestion d'approvisionnement. Les stratégies foraines seront renforcées avec un paquet complet de soins (CPN, CN, vaccination, curatif, PF, et Nutrition...) et Concern travaillera à accompagner les DS à la systématisation du dépistage de la MAG lors des activités en stratégie avancée.
Le 3ème résultat vise à réduire les risques liés à la sous-nutrition au travers du renforcement de l'implication et de l'engagement des populations contre la sous-nutrition par la mobilisation communautaire. Concern renforcera les réseaux de groupes de soutien ANJE en travaillant sur leur engagement à continuer les activités au-delà de la durée de vie du projet. Aussi, au travers de l'extension de la stratégie PB mères/ménages pour la détection précoce des cas et ainsi favoriser une réaction rapide et à mobiliser les autorités du Niger et leurs partenaires pour un financement adéquat de la nutrition, en passant par l’implication des communes à assurer la supervision des activités de prévention et prise en charge nutritionnelles, aussi en s'assurant de l'implication des COGES dans l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre des micros plans des structures de santé. Dans ce cadre Concern aidera les autorités communales et sanitaires à analyser les besoins, les coûts et les dépenses sur des activités liées à la nutrition et le plaidoyer auprès d'eux et les collectivités pour leur participation financière à travers leur PAA et PIA.

project_name: The resilience and protection of girls and boys affected by the conflict is strengthened, and vulnerable and at-risk children are receiving targeted support including strengthened capacity of caregivers and the community
project_objective:
After over seven years of violence, the Syrian war remains one of the most dangerous conflicts for children. The child protection needs across Syria are immense, far outweighing the available provision of necessary services. Conflict affected girls, boys and their families are facing appalling protection, neglect and deprivation risks on a daily basis, exacerbated by conflict related stress, exclusion or separation from their families. Report shows many IDPs have been displaced up to 10 times during the past years (IRC protection monitoring report) and therefore have adopted negative coping mechanisms to sustain themselves.
The SC will provide life-saving assistance and promote a protective environment for conflict-affected children and their families through  strengthening resilience and protection. Establishing or strengthening existing community-based child protection mechanism provision of specialised child protection services and through child protection capacity building and integration shall be the key focus for this project..
Best practices in systems strengthening through community-based child protection approach  in North Eastand South Central Syria shall be replicated in North West Syria.  Trainings, regular meetings and action planning to identify, prevent and respond to child protection issues by the Child protection committees at the community level. Structured psychosocial support activities at the child and adolescent friendly spaces Outreach sessions   to ensure social inclusion of that vulnerable  including children with disabilities will be delivered to communities. These sessions shall v raise awareness  on  violence against children, mine risk education  and the prevention of family separation.
In order to strengthen children’s protective environment SC shall engage parents and caregivers in  parenting without violence session  and mother- toddler groups, with priority given to child mothers and vulnerable caregivers.Case management will be delivered by trained and technically supported case workers through coaching and supervision to reach vulnerable and at-risk children, including unaccompanied and separated children, child survivors of sexual and gender based violence  and child labour, SC will promote and advocate for appropriate alternative care for UASC, with a focus on community-based and family-based care. Capacity building to  case management teams, relevant authorities and foster parents to strengthen the quality of  care. In both NE Syria and NW Syria, SC has conducted UASC assessments to review the alternative care systems and to advocate for best practices. 
At the inter-agency coordination level, SC will continue coordinating with other protection actors in the implementation of CP activities and will maintain active participation in sub-cluster meetings and other relevant coordination forums including Protection Working Group in NE Syria.and camp-level case management meetings. The lead role on child protection coordination in Al Hole will soon be with SC . In NW Syria, SC remains an active member of the Child Protection Sub Cluster. At the WoS level, SC plays a key role in WoS child protection coordination, while formal meetings are not taking place. SC will lead on a number of technical initiatives, including the development of case management SOPs, Information Sharing protocols training and roll out f CPIMS+ database for NE that is due in the first quarter  and on the development of alternative care guidance. In the Turkey hub, SC is on the technical review committee under the Child Protection Sub Cluster. SC also works closely with other actors to raise awareness on safe identification and referral, and in turn, also works with actors to refer children to basic services.

project_name: Mejora de los servicios esenciales de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene de las personas en situación de desplazamiento afectadas directa o indirectamente por la situación en Venezuela, NRC.
project_objective:
NRC Venezuela tiene como objetivo reducir riesgos de salud pública y la prevención de enfermedades relacionadas con el agua y el saneamiento inadecuados, garantizando el acceso al derecho al agua y al saneamiento, reduciendo los riesgos de protección ligados a la situación humanitaria en Venezuela. El programa ASH llevará a cabo una primera fase de evaluación y análisis de las necesidades, y propone modalidades de (a) respuesta de emergencia, (b) respuesta con soluciones duraderas basada en un enfoque comunitario, y (c) una respuesta Integrada con otros programas de NRC tales como: Educación, Seguridad Alimentaria e ICLA. 
La respuesta ASH de NRC estará centrada en la provisión de un mínimo de servicios ASH durante la Respuesta de Emergencia. Por otro lado, durante la Respuesta con Soluciones Duraderas se pretende mejorar la resiliencia en comunidades meta, fomentando la participación de comunidades en el diseño e implementación del programa, desarrollando sus capacidades locales, y asegurando la sostenibilidad del programa.
La componente de AGUA incluirá: (a) Construcción de puntos de agua potable temporales y permanentes para personas en tránsito y comunidades de acogida. NRC capacitará a la municipalidad e instituciones locales para mantener los puntos de agua y garantizar la calidad del agua, y se donarán kits de análisis de agua como parte de la estrategia de creación de capacidad; (b) Provisión de agua segura (a nivel del hogar) a través de kits de tratamiento de agua para el hogar y/o kits de manejo de agua); (c) Provisión de capacitación y sensibilización (tratamiento, calidad del agua y uso seguro). La componente de SANEAMIENTO incluirá: (a) Provisión de baterías de baños y duchas culturalmente apropiadas, desagregados por género y estaciones de lavado de manos. Las instalaciones se ubicarán en áreas públicas o institucionales en zonas clave de flujo migratorio; (b) Provisión de activos NFIs de saneamiento (mantenimiento / limpieza); (c)Provisión de contenedores de basura para gestión de residuos sólidos. La componente de HIGIENE incluirá: (a) Provisión de kits de dignidad e higiene, junto con sensibilizaciones sobre su uso apropiados; (b)Provisión de campañas de sensibilización sobre higiene personal, prevención de enfermedades, higiene menstrual y protección; (c) Creación, capacitación y sensibilización de comités ASH en colegios y comunidades que servirán como apoyo a la promoción de higiene.
La respuesta ASH de NRC pretenden ser Integradas a otros programas como: (a) EF-LH, mejorando el suministro de agua para actividades agropecuarias, etc.; (b) Educación que apunta a una mejora de la calidad de la educación, inclusivas e integradas con el programa ASH centrándose en la mejora de la infraestructura ASH, para garantizar las instalaciones satisfagan las necesidades de todos los grupos de NNAs, profesores y personas con discapacidad.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood assistance for vulnerable families in Syria.
project_objective:
The project aims to provide a wide-ranging support from emergency to regular food assistance as well as household based agricultural and livelihoods assistance. The project aims to target populations who are both food insecure as well as at risk of food insecurity through multiple but mutually reinforcing activities.  The project will contribute to the following two objectives of Food security cluster: 
 
Objective 1: Improve the food security status of assessed food insecure people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance. Objective 2: Support self reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives. 
 
A total of 30,000 households (150,000 individuals) will be supported through multiple but integrated activities.  
 
Under ﬁrst objective for life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance, the project will aim to meet the immediate food needs and also seasonal/supplementary food assistance. The Emergency Response will aim to reach crisis-affected people within 72 hours of the onset of a crisis to cover a minimum of one to four weeks of their immediate food needs through short-term support such as Ready-to-Eat Rations, cooked meals and/or baked bread.  Baked bread will also be provided to the displaced families living in the camps. this will help to stabilize the market prices.  further supplementary food assistance will be provided to improve the dietary diversity. such as Ramadan food distribution and Qurbani meat distribution.  
 
under the objective 2, appropriate agricultural inputs (cereal as well as vegetable production) will be provided along with technical capacity building at household-level to ensure that most vulnerable farming households receive timely inputs as per seasonal calendar to be able to produce and contribute to domestic production requirements. further asset building and asset protection support mainly for livestock keepers and poultry will be provided. This include but not limited to provision of EWE sheep, poultry feed, and vaccination.  
 
Finally, individuals including youth and people with disability will also be targeted for small scale income generation activities. such as barber shop, female saloon, grocery store etc.  Local procurement will be encouraged to promote local markets, especially where markets have the capacity to absorb such demands.  This objective also aim to restore and strengthen productive assets and create livelihood opportunities for the targeted populations, thus contributing to the overall food production and subsequently to food availability in Syria.

project_name: Emergency food assistance for new IDP
project_objective:
The hostilities in northwest Syria continue to heavily impact the lives of civilians, who have endured nine years of crisis, violence, multiple displacements, and economic downturns. The humanitarian situation, particularly in the Idleb de-escalation area, continues to deteriorate as a result of the hostilities that escalated in late 2019. From December 1st, 2019, almost 1 million people were displaced in northwest Syria, mostly from the southern parts of Idleb governorate; 80 percent of whom are women and children. People were forced to flee their homes within a matter of hours and without most of their belongings. The majority of the newly displaced have stayed within Idleb moving to either urban centers, such as Idleb city of Ariha, or to areas where vast IDP populations have already settled, such as Dana, Maaret Tamsrin, and Atareb. Approximately 45,000 of newly displaced individuals chose to move to areas in northern Aleppo governorate to seek safety and to reach services. 
Through this project, IR Syria plans to reach 2,290 families (11,450 individuals) who are newly IDP in Idleb and Aleppo governorates. The targeted families will be assisted with:
•	2kg of baked bread daily for 60 days, and

project_name: Faciliter l'accès aux logements, en Eau Hygiène et Assainissement aux personnes déplacés internes (PDIs) et populations hôtes affectés par le conflict au Nord et au Centre du Mali.
project_objective:
Durant l’année 2019, le contexte sécuritaire du Centre et Nord Mali ont été marqué par la recrudescence des violences de la population. Ces violences ont occasionné de nombreux déplacés internes vivant dans des conditions précaires. Les differents rapports d’évaluation rapide et conjointe produit par les inter-agence humanitaires ressortent que 03 ménages de sur 04 n’ont pas d’abris. Le problème d'accès en eau potable dans ces sites de déplacés n’a pas été épargné. Cet accès limité à l’eau ainsi que les conditions d’hygiène et d’assainissement précaires favorisent les maladies d’origine hydrique et à potentielle épidémique dans les sites des déplacés où familles d’accueils. Ce qui explique un besoin fort en abri et de EHA.
Pour palier à ces besoins, NRC propose à travers ce projet d’apporter sa contribution afin d’améliorer les conditions des personnes touchées dans un environnement sécurisé avec un accès aux logement et aux infrastructures Wash. 
NRC construira et réhabilitera des points d’eau, forages, puits, et mettra également en place des comités EHA et Abris avec 50% de femmes accompagné d’un mécanisme de suivi. NRC mettra en place les latrines d'urgence accessibles aux handicapés avec des kits de lavage des mains en tenant de l’aspect genre et de protection avec un emplacement visibles et separées entre les femmes et les hommes. Des poupelles pour la gestion des ordures seront mise en place dans les sites. 
Le projet se focalisera sur une reponse avec la formation sur les techniques de construction des maisons/abris suivi d’une distribution de kit abri constitué de matériaux locaux adaptés aux zones. Les différentes couches d’âges de déplacés bénéficieront de cette formation. Pour le cas des déplacés vivant en location dans les zones urbaines, NRC se pensera sur une possibilité d’une assistance de Cash. Ce Cash pouvant contribuer à soulager les charges de loyer des déplacés. Au niveau des sites inappropriés et appropriés, le respect des normes de construction et de sécurité des logements seront prise en compte dans son appui technique nécessaire aux déplacés pendant l’auto construction des maisons. Il veillera au respect de la distance prevue entre abris et infrastructures. Il se convergera sur le renforcement au respect du genre par les communautés à travers des sensibilisations sur l’égalité des sexes. NRC mettra en place plusieurs activités en commençant d’abord par une évaluation de base, des enquêtes CAP permettant d’avoir des informations de référence, les prises de contacts avec les partenaires et les leaders communautaires des déplacés. Cela dans le but de définir les approches à mettre places et les critères de ciblage. NRC ciblera la population extrêmement vulnérables avec un accent sur le genre et les personnes a besoins spécifiques. Ces groupes de personnes représentent un risque de protection plus élévé Lorsqu’elles sont dans une situation de deplacement. NRC s’assurera que son assistance ne nuira pas à la sécurité de ces personnes y compris l’environnement dans lequel ils vivent. 
NRC optera à une méthodologie de sélection des bénéficiaires en tenant compte des orientations des partenaires externes. Les aspects protection et sécuritaire ne seront pas négligés. Ces partenaires, bénéficiaires seront impliqués dans le processus de ciblage. Pour éviter toute exclusion lors du processus de ciblage, une analyse des risques de protection liée à la réponse de NRC sera entreprise. Des mecasnismes des plaintes sera mise en place.
Pour maintenir la collaboration et les efforts entre les acteurs dans le secteur Abri et Wash, NRC participera activement aux réunions de coordination et forums humanitaire au niveau national et régional organiser par OCHA, les 2 Clusters, des instances gouvernementales et niveau des sites des déplacés pour discuter des questions problématiques liées aux déplacés. Il participera à la conception des outils d’évaluation, aux évaluation des besoins, au rapportage, à l’harmonisation des kits.

project_name: WHO Emergency health response to consequences of the conflict in Ukraine – 2020
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in eastern Ukraine has a devastating impact on the health and well-being of the affected population showing signs of long-term consequences. The conflict has isolated rural health facilities in Government-Controlled Areas (GCA) from major health centers located in urban areas in Non-Government Controlled Areas (NGCA). Of the approximately 3.3 million people living within the 20 kilometres of the contact line, 38 per cent of households in the 20 km area along the ‘contact line’ and 57 per cent of households in the 5 km area along the ‘contact line’ (GCA) reported having problems accessing healthcare and require life-saving and essential health services.   The insecurity, lack of maintenance of outdated health facilities and medical equipment, shortage of medicines and medical supplies, understaffing and curtailed access to referral hospitals and pharmacies undermine the health care system’s ability to cope with both new and pre-existing health care needs
The ongoing process of health care reform in Ukraine impacts the access of the population to essential medical services on both sides of the ‘contact line.’ The decentralization of the healthcare system in GCA and the centralization of primary health care in NGCA have the potential to further exacerbate the difficulties to access health care services.
The lack of access to primary, secondary and tertiary health care services particularly affects vulnerable populations such as women, children, elderly, people with disabilities, those living in isolated settlements. This is further compounded by the lack of qualified medical staff and brain drain. Those who remained are confronted with the significant challenges to access quality professional education and continuous training. Health care workers are also exposed to traumatic events and are being overlooked by the health system and humanitarian organizations. 
It is difficult to ensure quality management of the healthcare system, since standardized protocols and operational procedures, based on the globally accepted guidelines are not being widely deployed or even tailored to the local context. Patient safety is also a major source for concern, given that little standardization occurs in the management of diseases, infection prevention and control measures, administration of the healthcare facilities. Essential medicines, renewables, equipment, and core medical technologies are also lacking. In 2019, WHO assessed the emergency medical services in eastern Ukraine, and 85 percent of the patients stated that the ambulance service was free, they did however had to pay up to the equivalent of one-month salary (UAH 3,600) for hospital care. 
The underdeveloped health information system prevents evidence-based practices for the improvement of the health system’s performance and epidemiologic surveillance is seriously challenged by the security, limited availability of the trained personnel and supplies, difficulties in timely detection of the cases and their laboratory confirmation. This also affects the early warning and response system for public health threats.

To respond to the humanitarian needs, WHO will continue implementing the following key activities, which are based on the strong cooperation with health authorities:
1- Technical advice to health authorities in using evidence-based tools to promote emergency preparedness and readiness, improve quality of healthcare at all levels and improve access of the vulnerable population
2. Support to primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities through the distribution of medical supplies and equipment, development of capacity building programs and rehabilitation of health infrastructure. 
3. Reinforcing technical capacities of health care workers in mental health and psychosocial support.
4. Improving trauma care and emergency medical services based on the result of WHO EMS Survey (WHO 2019)
5. Supporting Public Health system and preparedness mechanism

project_name: Safe and dignified living conditions for IDPs and migrants in Libya.
project_objective:
This project seeks to strengthen the protective environment for vulnerable, conflict affected persons in Libya by improving the living conditions for IDPs and migrants through tailored shelter solutions, material assistance and capacity building in site management.  
Shelter solutions: Access to safe shelter arrangements can be extremely fraught for both IDPs and migrants, due to inflation, increasing rent prices and landlords exploiting the war economy, especially in densely populated areas such as Tripoli. Many are forced into paying high rental prices for low standard or overcrowded housing. Unfinished buildings, construction sites and warehouses/industrial buildings have all been used for shelter. Lack of privacy, exposure to elements and dangerous building conditions all impact the lives of vulnerable inhabitants. Therefore, working on a case by case, or site by site basis, DRC will provide tailored shelter solutions to those in need. This will involve the selection of appropriate interventions, ranging from shelter repairs or shelter sealing (through either contracted services or sealing off kits) to the running and management of collective shelters for temporary accommodation, to the provision of cash for rent or placement into a host family. The inclusion of those we assist will be paramount, with discussions on designing and implementing shelter solutions throughout the intervention. Both unskilled and skilled labour will be sought from the communities themselves. DRC will continue to monitor their shelter arrangements through site management activities where appropriate, ensuring longevity of assistance and creating community driven durable solutions. 
Material Assistance: In addition, many vulnerable households lack basic items, either due to their loss or destruction. Many migrants, on leaving detention centres or returning from the sea have little to no material possession. As such DRC will provide either individual items, or kits of items to households, based on an understanding of their needs. Kits and items will range from lights, kitchen sets, cooking sets, to beds and clothing. The items are intended to fill the immediate needs of the vulnerable households. Through regular community and household discussion DRC can further tailor items and kits to the needs of vulnerable households. 
Capacity Building: Finally, many vulnerable households are reliant or semi-reliant on either community focal points or municipality leaders for the management of their shelter arrangements. Semi-formal or informal shelter arrangements are often run by self-appointed or community elected focal points or municipality leaders. Through workshops and training sessions, identified site focal points will be provided with training on protection mainstreaming, site management and shelter skills, in order to better assist the communities, they represent or manage.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of integrated Health care services for internally displaced persons (IDPs), Returnees and Host communities in Luuq and Garbaharey Districts of Gedo region, Somalia.
project_objective:
Access to adequate health services, particularly for women and children, is extremely restricted by social barriers, poor infrastructure, poor service quality, high levels of insecurity, and a limited number of health facilities and trained health workers. Relative security in Luuq and Garbaharey towns, provides an opportunity to significantly improve health services in both districts. This proposal specifically focuses on the urgent health care needs existing in Garbaharey and Luuq districts (Northern side), to be implemented over one year. The project targets 32,048 (16,280 female, 15,768 male) beneficiaries from both host and IDP communities with healthcare services out of which 1,602 beneficiaries are people with disabilities. This project will directly contribute to the Health cluster objectives of reducing excess morbidity due to diseases outbreak, contributing to improvement in physical and mental wellbeing of the affected population, and improving case management and referral services for GBV survivors. It is also aligned to the Ministry of Health (MoH) strategic plan Objective 1 and 4 which focuses on improving the health of the Somali population with a special focus on maternal and child health and the cluster objectives. Towards this end, Trocaire will work jointly with DHBs to improve the capacity of staff and health facilities, including mobile clinics to provide essential healthcare. This will include building the capacity of DHBs and MoH to provide these services fully in the near future, equipment of health facilities, widening the reach by breaking geographical, infrastructural, cultural and economic barriers to access to health, investing in prevention measures through vaccination exercises and community awareness raising, and prepositioning of supplies in anticipation for crisis. 

The intended impact of the programme is to: contribute towards the improved health status of the Somali population, particularly women of childbearing age and children under-five, through the provision of health care services at the targeted facilities in Garbaharey and Luuq Districts.
The programme builds on Trócaire’s 27 years of experience operating in Gedo and will work closely with the Ministry of Health and the community, through community structures- District Health Boards (DHBs)-, to provide quality healthcare services that meet MoH and Health cluster standards. The DHBs are community-based governance structures that have proven to be an effective and sustainable model in the provision of healthcare services in the region. This programme complements Trócaire’s existing programme delivering the EPHS in three districts (Belet Xaawo, Luuq, Garbaharey and Dollow) of Gedo.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Access to clean Water, Sanitation and Improved Hygiene to vulnerable populations in Gedo, Somalia
project_objective: The project proposes to improve access to safe water, sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices for 3,825 female and 3,675 male beneficiaries in underserved and hard-to-reach areas. The target districts of intervention include Belet Hawa and Luuq districts in Gedo.  A gender analysis conducted in September 2019 in Gedo by Trocaire has informed the different needs of women, girls, men and boys, noting a lack of access to clean water as the biggest problem in Gedo. The location of WASH facilities such as toilets in camp- like setting presents unique protection concerns thereby increasing the vulnerability of women. Another finding is that women and girls are rarely involved in the design, or in determining the location of these facilities. This project will aim to address these gaps by ensuring inclusion of women and girls in the design of the project, determining locations of WASH assets, and through measurement of the satisfaction of all social groups with the project deliverables. The project aims to contribute to the achievement of two specific objectives of the WASH cluster: delivering lifesaving WASH assistance to reduce acute needs, and providing/ restoring sustainable access to safe water services in target locations. This will be done through construction of one hybrid water system with piping to communities, construction of 25 permanent gender-sensitive latrines with handwashing stations, hygiene promotion sessions with distribution of hygiene kits, and environmental cleanup campaigns. In addition, Trocaire will conduct water testing and treatment of water facilities in target locations, and conduct trainings and refresher trainings for representative Water Management Committees while equipping them with tools necessary for effective management of water points. Lack of access to safe and adequate water due to under performance of successive rainy seasons and the resultant drying up of Dawa and Juba Rivers, low sanitation coverage coupled with poor hygiene knowledge and practices puts these communities at risk of waterborne diseases and loss of life. On the flip side, the flooding of these two rivers presents a high risk of waterborne diseases especially during Gu and Deyr seasons. Trocaire will collaborate with Somali Humanitarian Relief Action (SHRA), a national NGO with strong experience in implementing WASH projects in Gedo, in delivery of this project in the two target districts.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Provision of emergency GBV prevention and Child protection services for Men, women, boys and girls in drought and conflict affected areas in Bari, Sanag and Sool Regions
project_objective:
The proposed project is designed to contribute to Somalia HRP 2019 and TASS's efforts to support the
drought-induced affected populations (Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities) in
Sool, Sanaag and Bari regions through community based programming and strengthening of GBV and
Child Protection response systems and promoting community cohesiveness. which will promote
