project_name: Improving access to water and sanitation services for newly IDPs in camps in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
Due to continuation of recent hostilities in Syria, tens of thousands of civilians have fled from governorates Idleb, Aleppo, and Hama to Northern Idleb and Aleppo which are already densely populated of IDPs having previously fled to these areas. Also displacement in winter months is further exacerbating the vulnerability of people in need. Many of those who fled are in urgent need of humanitarian support. In light of the high population density and the dependence of civilians on alternative sources such as water trucking, which are absolutely unsafe, new concerns arise from the spread of diseases due to the lack of water, especially among children. The most urgent need currently is the safe drinking water, in addition to personal hygiene items, and sanitation facilities (latrines).
BALAD is planning to implement and provide WASH services to about 15000 of newly IDPs in camps.
Balad has a good experience in providing WASH services due to implementation of two WASH projects in 37 camps in Idlep (more than 30,000 BNFs), in addition to providing other services ın camps such as installing tents and water tanks and distributing NFI kits.
The project aims to increase the number of water taps according the number of IDP families, the distribution of water trucking will be on daily basis for 5 months. 
Project will ensure water is safe by testing water samples in sources, trucks, and in household level. 
Project will work on WASH facilities by construction of latrine in accordance with the standards of allocation WASH cluster and sphere taking into consideration gender sensitive by building separate blocks, safe accessible, lighthouse and its doors provided with income locks, also taking into consideration persons with disabilities by building latrines and showers that suit their needs. 
In addition to desludging all septic tanks in the targeted camps once a week for three months
Project also will provide containers for solid waste, communal garbage bins and small garbage bins for each tent, also trucks will periodically collect garbage and transport it to designated places to be processed by sorting the contents so as not to damage the environment and surroundings.
Project also includes conducting hygiene promotion sessions to raising awareness about personal hygiene, the campaign will be done by trained team on HP principles and presentation skills. Throughout session team will distribute materials printouts and stickers in public spaces in targeted camps, in addition to distributing hygiene kit for every family.

project_name: Protection in Emergency services to vulnerable communities in Northwest Syria.
project_objective:
The proposed project will provide protection services to vulnerable communities in northwest Syria, who are subject to, or at risk of, protection concerns including child protection issues, gender-based violence and/or sexual violence, PWDs, through mobile outreach teams and structured preventive as well as responsive and remedial services. In addition, the project will provide those who are subject to or at risk of the heavy bombardment and shelling through conducting voluntarily reallocation to safe areas. Moreover, Violet will provide referral services to the most vulnerable and also raise their awareness on available services and rights. Awareness-raising activities will be conducted through direct contact with the affected community, with either individuals or in-group sessions. The sessions activities will include provision of information sharing to the services available via distributing leaflets , small information cards, posters and drawings to ensure participation and meaningful access , special cases will be handled by the Case workers who will conduct the necessary risk mitigation issues , refer and follow-up
Those will be socially and culturally appropriate and aim at increasing their knowledge of protection issues and how to address those individual or with community support. Outreach visits also will identify individual cases for case management and proper reporting and follow up per the SOPs. To focus on sustainability, despite the deteriorating situation, Violet seeks to establish community protection committees, who will become the community-component of the proposed project and will play a key role in community resilience towards protection risks. 
A GBV technical specialist will be responsible for providing support for the GBV caseworkers on the field, in order to support their activities and provide guidance. The GBV (case) workers will screen and identify cases, from the community and the recent displacements IDPs, conduct risk assessment and refer the identified cases both internally to benefit from the PSS activities and externally to other static service providers in the area using the service mapping tool. 
The PSEA focal point in Syr will be reporting directly to the focal point in Turkey in regards to investigations issue, whereby will report to the project manager in matters related to case identification, technical issues and follow-up. In addition, Violet will invest in its trained volunteers to provide the voluntary relocation support and services through transportation and associated protective package for people to move safely and in dignity away from hostilities to safe destinations; taking into consideration family unity and attention to the needs of most vulnerable groups, including female-headed households as well as PWD. Guaranteeing effective referral at the earliest possible opportunity for medical emergencies and unaccompanied children. The latter will be referred to child protection actors on the ground for an appropriate course of action inconsistency with the best interest of the child;
For all activities, GBV SOPs, PSEA guidance, and case management policies for the Syrian crisis will be used. PSS targeting adults, youth and children will enable them to identify positive coping mechanisms besides their current situation. Also, the project will roll out training and capacity building on protection key elements and protection mainstreaming to ensure that all Violet’s non-protection staff and volunteers are in a position to mainstream protection in all project cycles and especially emergency response projects.
Violet will provide PFA support, based on displacement and needs of newly arrived IDPs, Violet will respond in areas of new arrivals. Furthermore Violet will provide referrals pathway services including CP and GBV centers, for 1.500 cases

Multi-sector assistance will range from emergency food support to life-sustaining regular food support and restoring the source of livelihood. It will also include the provision of necessary non-food items, shelter intervention (described in the SNFI document).

SARD will ensure newly-displaced families have improved access to life-saving assistance through an effective and efficient response mechanism, implemented with a protection lens, the action will also include gender-sensitive activities as well as ensure that people with disabilities have safe and secure access to the aid.

- Emergency food support is provided to up to 35 000 individuals in the form of cooked meals or on-off cash the modality will be according to the situation f the families as well as the market and the security environment.
- Monthly food assistance targeting 20 000 food insecure beneficiaries through in-kind, voucher or cash assistance depending on the best-adapted option for up to  8 months. The action provides up to 8-months multi-sector assistance with food for selected most
vulnerable persons including IDPs and host communities. Vulnerability is identified and prioritized through a selection and scoring mechanism.
Identification is based on a set of eligibility criteria such as household vulnerability, shelter conditions, possession of productive assets and food security level (livelihood coping strategies).
Identification is based on a set of eligibility criteria such as household vulnerability, shelter conditions, possession of productive assets and food security level (livelihood coping strategies).

project_name: WASH service provision for Rohingya and host communities
project_objective: NGO Forum in partnership with NCA and AAR will respond to the WASH needs where refugees are living amongst the host community focusing in Teknaf areas. The security context in the target area has recently deteriorated, with increasing tensions between host communities and refugees, exacerbated by environmental disasters, lack of access to income-generating activities and pressure on local resources, such as water and agricultural land. NGO Forum/NCA will consult with the refugees and host communities in order to prioritise activities that will integrate the needs of the communities. The Teknaf area suffers each year from water scarcity during the dry season and, because the Master Water Network planning process will not begin before 2020, therefore the proposed project will include contingency capacity for water trucking to cover drinking-water needs. NGO Forum/NCA/AAR will maintain and improve water and sanitation infrastructures and services to support rights holders in coping with natural disasters. The project will continue with hygiene promotion activities and distribute Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) items based on latest REACH survey identified women preferences, and explore the use of the voucher system in conducive market environment. As an integrated programming approach, NGO Forum/NCA/AAR will train and sensitise the WASH team, especially the community volunteers, on SGBV topics enabling them to identify cases and do referrals.  Specific gender concern in the WASH program: Within the humanitarian community itself, site planning and WASH infrastructure planning/design processes have mainly been dominated by male architects and engineers, often with gendered assumptions about the user. In general, latrine provision in the initial stages of the response was largely determined through an engineering lens or from the perspective of quantitively reaching minimum standards, and did not always incorporate women and girls’ needs, gender disparities and socio-cultural constructs. The proposed project will aim to strongly focus on the consultation aspect during the initial deisgn phase of a gender segregated latrine construction, to address the major issues identified in prior WASH and gender specific research, namely the sharing facilities, lack of sex-segregation, distance, privacy, dignity, and difficulties to manage menstruation. The expected impact of the gender focused WASH activities will be the improved qualitative WASH indicators and a reduction in the percentage of households (women and men) facing problems accessing latrines and bathing facilities, and a reduction of percentage of women and men reporting feeling unsafe while accessing latrine facilities, as well as an overall increase in the percentage satisfaction of WASH services provided.

project_name: Provision of shelter solution and shelter related NFIs for displaced  and most vulnerable families

Syria, despite the unpredictability and the risks of working in areas with security threats.

The assessment conducted 2019/2020 show that NFI/hygiene items ranked as households’ main priorities for the next 3 to 6 months. NFI needs are diverse and include winterization kits, clothes, kitchen sets, bedding units and hygiene items. About 69% of the households shelter assistance as one of their main priority for the next 3 to 6 months.
Implemented with a protection lens, and addressing gender and disabled specific needs, the shelter response is aiming at providing housing options to primary emergency to life-sustaining situation, the activities ranging from emergency support in camps setting or temporary shelter solutions in open-field to life-saving upgrade of transitional shelter and life-sustaining house rehabilitation through self-help approach. The modality of intervention will be adapted to the urgency, the situation, the needs and the HLP situation of the beneficiaries. SARD is committed to promoting social cohesion : shelter programming is based community approach and include community project of common interest. The shelter activities will include :
-Distribution of tents and camps settings (including appropriate site planning)
-Emergency shelter option with distribution of kit or quick fixing in the sub-standard settings by SARD team
-Collective shelter upgrade and unfinished building repair through contractors under SARD technical supervision
-House rehabilitation through self-help – cash grant under SARD supervision
-Community projects through contractors.
As part of the HLP procedure, SARD will ensure free of charge security of tenure from 6 months in emergency temporary settings to 18 months in transitional/permanent shelter options.
Shelter response is integrated with basic shelter related NFI support, adapted to the needs of the assessed and eligible families. The modality of intervention will range from in-kind to cash/voucher intervention according to the market accessibility and availability, family capacity and needs. Door to door distribution is the preferred option to ensure specific needs and security is addressed to girls, women, elderly and people with special needs.

project_name: Improving the living conditions and livelihoods of the most vulnerable conflict-affected people
project_objective:
The response is designed to provide humanitarian assistance to 20000 most vulnerable people (30% IDPs and 70% are host-community ) in North-west Syria, to alleviate suffering in addition to increasing the resilience of affected communities by improving multi-sectoral access to integrated assistance, over a period of 12 months.

The project will aim at addressing the life-sustaining response, enhancing the resilience of conflict-affected persons (host -community, and IDPs). The action will also improve access to public services and facilities on community level and revive the local economy through community utility projects that will benefit rather the entire community (although focusing on the most vulnerable people in need). The project is aiming at improving the public infrastructure, supporting up to 20000 individuals at community level, through the rehabilitation of essential public infrastructure implementing 10 different community-projects. 
To include as a key elements in our social cohesion program design, the project will include a conflict analysis to help us understand what the relationship between or amongst different groups is,  a conflict sensitivity analysis to help us implement programs in a way that does not cause or increase harm to project staff and project participants, a stakeholder analysis  to help us understand the different stakeholders in the area of implementation, and how the stakeholders could affect the project and what we should to manage stakeholders so that the project is successful.
Identification of specific groups is undertaken to better target the beneficiaries groups, based on findings of a conflict analysis in their area of implementation.   Dialogue is also a key approach across projects, including integrating dialogue processes into the community mobilization process.

Finally, with the Income Generating Activities (IGA) part of the project, SARD aims at supporting families to restore their livelihood by restoring their own income-generating activities through micro/small businesses, with tailor-made suitable support on how to establish and manage their IGA.

IGA project will focus on the skills, capacities, and interests of adult men and women as well as youth in terms of potential IGAs to be restored and run within the community. 1000 IGAs will be selected where only activities and businesses that were existing before the war and/or lost due to the conflict will fall under this project (damaged workplaces, loss of material and light machinery, etc.).

project_name: Emergency GBV Response to Conflict Affected Women, Girls, Men and Boys in Borno State, North East Nigeria
project_objective:
The proposed intervention is implemented jointly by Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) and its local partners-Ekklesiya Ya’uwa Nigeria (EYN), Federation of Muslim Women Association (FOMWAN) and Jireh Doo Foundation (JDF) in 7 conflict affected Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Borno state, Nigeria.

The proposed intervention focuses on provision of life-saving GBV assistance to the most vulnerable populations (women, men, girls and boys) in conflict affected areas, as well as to strengthen the resilience of the affected population.  
The proposed intervention feeds into the Humanitarian Response Plan 2020-2021 (HRP) and is coordinated through respective GBV sub sector cluster with lead agencies as well as other partners in the target areas. All partners are particularly focused on actions designed to enhance physical and mental wellbeing, improve living standards and coping mechanisms of the affected population.   
The affected populations (women, men, girls and boys) are in the center of the intervention and participatory methods are used throughout the project cycle management to ensure ownership and sustainability of project results. On top of that, NCA GBV intervention focuses in strengthening of the GBV response through capacity building and development of guidelines and trainings especially in specialized GBV programming that will allow all GBV partners in Borno state to provide better services.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- WASH and Protection assistance for IDPS/ host communities in Banadir, Lower Shabelle, Nugaal and Gedo regions
project_objective:
The project aims to improve access to basic WASH services and address protection
concerns of Internally displaced Persons affected by armed conflict and violence and
destitutions triggered by climatic shocks. Vulnerable groups that including; people with
disability, people with medical conditions, children, the elderly and lactating mothers will
be supported to access services. Protection will be mainstreamed in the delivery of WASH
services to ensure that the populations in need targeted for this intervention are safe and
their dignity upheld in observance of their human rights and rights to basic services.
NCA and partners will implement temporary emergency. Sustainable WASH solutions
through water trucking, bore hole system with solar power and water poins, desalinization
of water, rehabilitation and expansion of water supplies systems, improve subsurface
dams/berkards. Gender-balanced WASH committees will be established and capacitated
to maintain WASH facilities functionality. Water jerricans and household treatment
options given ensure safe collection/storage as well consumption of water. Adequate
sanitation facilities, gender segregated and lockable from inside will be rehabilitated/
constructed where scarce to reduce morbidity and mortality. Hygiene promotion will be
conducted emphasising hand washing at critical times. People with incontinence will also
benefit from services to improve their dignity.
Projects will be implemented in line with the SPHERE and WASH/MoEWR guidelines/ To
reduce risk of violence upon facility users, special attention will be given to reducing
distance from households to WASH facilities as per the SPHERE standards and ensuring
that outputs are gender and disability sensitive. PHAST and CHAST approaches will seek
to promote an understanding of the connection between hygiene and health, as well as
the means to mitigate the impact of poor hygiene on health. MHM sessions for women
and girls will accompany distribution of hygiene kits.

project_name: Early Recovery Livelihoods assistance to IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable host communities in Canal/Pigi & Fangak Counties, former Jonglei State.
project_objective:
This project is designed to link NPA’s life-saving emergency food assistance (General Food Distribution and Blanket Supplementary Feeding Program) with early recovery livelihoods activities and compliment in-kind food assistance to meet both the life-saving emergency assistance needs as well as early recovery and protection of livelihoods of conflict affected populations in Canal/Pigi & Fangak Counties. 
As per August 2019 IPC report, Canal/Pigi and Fangak Counties of Jonglei State are classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and Crisis (IPC Phase 3) respectively while both locations persist IPC AMN 4 for Acute Malnutrition . Former Jonglei State in general has the highest number of people facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) and Emergency (IPC Phase4) acute food insecurity with an estimated 1.25 million people, representing 64.8 percent of the state population.
NPA’s PDM report conducted in three locations of Canal/Pigi and Fangak Counties (Atar 3, New Fangak and Kurwai) revealed that respondents expressed their dissatisfaction over the quantity of the food items being not enough and untimely to satisfy the food need of the family due to sharing of food assistance with relatives, extended family sizes and returnees who have come from Sudan sharing their rations.
In this project, NPA is proposing to distribute combined vegetable, crop and fishing kits to 9,750 HHs (58,500 people) in Canal/Pigi County and 15,615 HHs (93,690 people) in Fangak County as per the HRP 2020 FSL targets. This will be followed by provision of training on improved agronomic practices as well as fish preservation, marketing and group dynamics to 5,000 farmers/fishermen (2,000 Canal & 3,000 Fangak). The trained farmers/fishermen will be expected to pass on their knowledge to the remaining farmers/fishermen. The knowledge gained from these trainings will be of importance in building the community resilience to future shocks. These activities are aimed at improving production of vegetables, crop and fish hence contributing towards reducing malnutrition rates. The vegetable, crop and fish products will go a long way in restoring the nutritional status of the affected population, through increased food consumption and better dietary diversity score. 
Beneficiaries of this project are household members who are extremely food insecure individuals classified in IPC 4 and IPC 3. NPA will follow a community-based approach by setting up a “Beneficiary targeting committee”, whereby the community take up the role in the selection of eligible households, particularly internally displaced households and returnees, while also including vulnerable members of host communities. A vulnerability selection criteria will be used where communities also participate in discussing and endorsing the beneficiary selection criteria. 
Community will be the prime movers of the implementation process through their continuous engagement in the project. In addition to being responsible for beneficiaries’ targeting, they will take part in periodic community meetings, Project Management Committees and Post Distribution Monitoring assessments, where NPA will ensure that the voices and concerns of all groups are captured. Further, to promote accountability, NPA will continue using the community based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide platforms for beneficiaries' active involvement in the project and avenues to voice any issues or concerns.

NPA has worked in South Sudan since 1986, and currently runs three programmes: Emergency Response Food Security Response, Rural Development and Partnership with Civil Society. NPA has extensive experience in majority of the Country in the area of Food Security and Livelihoods and is endowed with excellent reputation, robust relationship with local authorities & communities in South Sudan.

project_name: Facilitating Assistance to Syria Together
project_objective:
SAMS Health program for the year 2020 comes in line with the Health Sector objectives 1 & 3 targeting both increasing the access to life-saving and life-sustaining health services to the most vulnerable and in need while also strengthening the current health system capacity so it can continue supporting community resilience to respond to the ever changes in the in context. In this program, SAMS will prioritize the reduction of morbidity and mortality through improving the access to quality health care (primary and secondary health facilities, specialized hospitals, mobile clinics, and an ambulatory system) in 36 health facilities within both Aleppo, Idleb, Ar Raqqa governorates.

To achieve these objectives, SAMS will support facilities on different levels including coverage of staff incentives, running costs, provision pharmaceuticals and other medical and non-medical commodities, and assisting with repairs and rehabilitation to maintain the health network. SAMS will provide recruitment support, capacity building, and ongoing medical supervision to ensure the HFs are staffed with qualified medical personnel and to enhance compliance with standard treatment protocols. 

SAMS will increase the capacity of the HFs so that minimal inputs will be required to sustain the services. As per the Essential Primary Health Services Package adopted by the Health Cluster, SAMS will provide the following services: reproductive health services (ante-natal care, post-natal care, family planning, normal deliveries, gynaecological consultations, and clinical management of rape), integrated management for child illness, vaccines, prevention and control for communicable and non-communicable diseases, nutrition, MHGAP, health awareness, and basic laboratory and radiology services. Services at the secondary health care level will include gynecologic surgeries and cesarean sections, trauma management, major surgeries, hospitalization services, blood transfusion, hemodialysis and intensive care units. 

Moreover, to reduce the prevalence of mental health, psychological disorders and functional limitations of people affected by the conflict in Northwest Syria. This objective will target 24 health facilities with Psychosocial Support Workers (PSSWs) in each facility to provide PS services within the facilities. This program will also provide cancer treatment to Breast, colon, Hodgkin, and non-Hodgkin Lymphoma patients in NWS. Additionally, SAMS will support the ambulatory system consists of 10 ambulances working in two shifts to ensure 24/7 covering Ehsem, Ariha, Dana subdistricts in Idleb governorate. The program will also Increase access to prosthesis services and rehabilitation care in NWS through maintaining activities launched at Azaz Prosthesis centre including.

In addition, as part of SAMS focus on contributing to its goal of increasing the capacity of the health care professional in NWS through advancing SAMS’ investment in its education program, SAMS will contribute toward achieving this objective through the continuation of supporting three major medical education components:
Supporting Residents Doctors to start or resume their specialities studies in a variety of specialities.
Supporting Midwifery Education in NWS, by implementing two modules of the Midwifery Training Program due to the strategy which was developed by the SRH-TWG;
Supporting Nursing Education in Syria.

Similar to all SAMS projects, SAMS will seek all efforts possible to coordinate with all health actors through the Health Cluster whether through the routinely gathered data in 4Ws and HeRAMS. or through its constant participation and active membership within the following TWG: SRH, MHPSS, Non-Communicable Diseases, Syrian Immunization Group, Midwifery Capacity Building Strategy for NWS, Secondary Health Care, and Drug Supply Line notwithstanding its membership in the NGO Forum, SNA and other bodies. SAMS always coordinate and consult its operations with the HDs.

project_name: Emergency and post-emergency response to protection needs of conflict-affected populations in Syria
project_objective:
Through its integrated Mine Action/protection component, the organization will seek to alleviate and/or mitigate the accidents related to the presence of explosive ordnances (EOs) in contaminated areas and increase the protection of at-risk persons through direct and indirect risk education activities, contamination impact surveys, and through the identification, marking and disposal of EO spots.
 The organization will address the protection-related risks associated to the high level of land contamination by EOs in Syria. The INGO will provide Risk Education for most at-risk populations living and working in highly contaminated areas in Syria. Based on context, access and needs analysis, Risk Education will be conducted either through direct RE sessions at households’ level or through Trainer of Trainers (ToT) to improve community participation and sustainability. The organization will identify key and influential community focal points (teachers, imam, community leaders, head of farmers, survivors) as to enable them to dispense life-saving messages and become advocates for the protection of their peers.  This activity aims to strengthen the skills of key local actors in order to ensure the appropriation of the messages disseminated and thus the sustainability of the activity. In addition, safety briefing will be proposed to humanitarian workers to spread RE knowledge within the humanitarian community and thus to promote safe behaviors and minimize the risk of accidents among aid workers as they provide services to affected population.  Risk Education Teams will conduct RE activities, Contamination Impact Survey (CIS), Accident and Victim surveys in affected communities, mosques, community centers, educational facilities, IDP camps and other public places in an effort to reduce immediate threats caused by Explosive Ordinance (EOs). Priority will be given to at-risks persons living in contaminated areas, to ensure they have the necessary information to be able to adopt safe behaviors and reduce the threats posed by the presence of explosive hazards. Safety briefings will be provided to other humanitarian actors (local and international NGOs) to raise their awareness about risks and the consequences of explosive hazards they could face when in the field. 

Finally, the Organization will produce and externally disseminate evidence-based advocacy factsheets so as to mobilize and persuade local, national, regional and International stakeholders and raise key humanitarian and protection issues for populations and humanitarian actors in Syria.
In clearance, Non-Technical Survey (NTS) teams and clearance teams will identify, mark and dispose EOs. Surveys will be conducted to obtain more accurate information on presence, type, distribution & level of contamination, and will be prioritized dependent on the presence of IDPs in communities, the identification of visible EOs in areas and/or accidents that have occurred in that community over the past 6 months and where people are living and/or returning. 
The organization will also implement clearance activities in Raqqa Governorate, while maintaining the possibility of deploying Clearance teams to Deir Ezzor if the context allows. In this perspective, NTS activities will only be carried out in Deir Ezzor if demining operations in the area is confirmed.
During the provision of Risk Education, people who need multi-disciplinary rehabilitation services will be internally referred to supported rehabilitation centers in Hasakeh, Raqqa and Deir el Zour governorates, where they will have access to a variety of services depending on the outcomes of their needs assessment process. The organisation’s advocacy team will continue to lobby for the ban of the use of Explosive Weapons in Populated Areas (EWIPA) as well as the shelling of hospitals/health facilities to prevent death and injuries to civilians. These activities will be funded by different donors and will complement the proposed HMA project

project_name: Provision of Health services for Conflict Affected Population in North West Syria 2020
project_objective:
Shafak's health program aims to contribute in the provision of access to life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian health services for people in need and conflict affected population in northern Syria. The proposed intervention will prioritize internally displaced people and other vulnerable populations especially (women ,children and people with disabilities) in the targeted areas. The intervention will be implemented through:

1. Continue supporting a comprehensive package of health services including: Primary Health Care, and Mental Health in one of the existing health facilities in northwest Syria. The motivation of this project is to continue providing health services in the already established and equipped centers to the population in western and southern rural Aleppo with outreach and referral activities to the higher level of health services. The project will comprise two convergent components: primary health and mental health care, and their activities will be provided through the following health centers: 

a)-  Comprehensive PHC Center with basic obstetric and neonatal care (level 4)


2. The provision of Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EMONC) services and
management of SRH-related diseases in addition to the pediatric health care through supporting the specialized hospital for women and children which provides maternal and child health services to most vulnerable people in the rural of Idlib, Marretmasrin and through outreach teams.   (HF-Code: G0700073). 

3- Continue Supporting 2 dialysis centers 1 in Idlib and 1 in Qah with running costs
and dialysis kits. In addition to conduct capacity building and training for the medical
staff of the two centers: 

a)- Qah Dialysis center in Al-Hydaya Hospital. 
b)- Shafak Dialysis center-Idleb: (HF-Code: G0700074). 

4- Continue Provision of Secondary Health Care and obstetric services through Expanding an existing health facility in rural Idleb to Include a Surgical Unit and a Labor Ward.

5- Continue Support the implementation of social mobilization activities for the Routine Immunization & Campaigns funded by UNICEF and implemented by Syrian Immunization Group (SIG) and ACU. 

By achieving the above components, Shafak aims to contribute to enhancing the health status in the targeted areas.

project_name: Building Resilience to the Vulnerable Crisis-Affected Population in North-West Syria
project_objective:
The projects intends to provide a multi-faceted response  in an integrated and coherent way. Firstly, by stimulating local production through provision of agricultural inputs, targeted farmers will be able to restart and/or increase production, increase their income and improve the availability in the market. Secondly, by supporting livestock herders with inputs they will be able to maintain their current asset base while increasing income. This will also support availability of local dairy products and animal based proteins in the market. Thirdly supporting creating short term income and labour opportunities with fixed-term wages. Finally rehabilitation of related value chain infrastructure to protect and maintain community productive assets (e.g: irrigation channels, mills, bakeries, storage, fodder mixers, feeder roads and silos). Shafak's proposal is designed to supporting farmers and livestock herders needs of the vulnerable IDPs, returnees and HCs.  The project comprises the following components:

- Providing agriculture inputs (winter crops, summer crops, , olive value chain, pistachio value chain and forage crops).
- Purchasing wheat.
- Providing fodder, vaccines and treatment.
- Rehabilitating value chain related infrastructure.
- Providing short-term employment opportunities through Cash-for-Work activities.

ER1: 13,500 Targeted households are able to resume agricultural activities, increase household income and improve consumption through: i) provision of agricultural inputs, including improved access to water; olive harvesting and pruning and ii) improving/restoring agricultural infrastructure (for example irrigation / drainage), IV) Cash for harvest, V) extension services, VI) purchasing wheat.
ER2: 7,000 Targeted households are able to increase household income and maintain livestock activities through: i) provision of livestock inputs (500 kg of fodder per beneficiary 3,000 beneficiaries) ; ii) associated training, iii) vaccination campaigns per health care calendar (4 campaigns, 200,000 head per campaign owned by 4,000 beneficiaries)
ER3: 500 Targeted households stabilize, maintain or increase their income through Cash-for-Work activities, which build and strengthen community related value chain infrastructure , disaster risk reduction, mechanical pest and vol control  and olive trees harvesting .
ER4: Rehabilitation of related value chain  infrastructure, irrigation channels, Mills, bakeries, storage, fodder mixers, feeder roads and silos.

project_name: Protecting Livelihoods and Building Resilience of affected Populations in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
This program aims at supporting the resilience of the conflict affected people in northwest Syria, particularly in Idleb and Aleppo governorate. Shafak's proposed is designed to contribute to supporting the transition to the early recovery phase, as it supports the targeted communities with long-term assistance activities, programs that focus on building/restoring the communities' infrastructure, local economic empowerment, and initiatives that ensure engagement and participation of the community in recovering from the protracted crisis. This program will achieve its objectives through the following:

a) Providing short-term employment opportunities through Cash-for-Work activities to 2000 HHs in two rounds.
b) Offering rural micro-financing opportunities to 250 HHs, each beneficiary will receive 750 USD.
c) Providing vocational and skills training to 1500 youth, men and women applicants and then support successful trainees (Expecting 800 trainees) with small-scale cash grants to enable them restart/initiate their small enterprises, each grant total will be 600 USD per beneficiary.
d) Rehabilitating the local economic, public and social infrastructure (7 Projects) through linking with the Cash-for-Work activity or through service providers. Each project cost will be about 15000 USD
e) Supporting local community and social cohesion initiatives.

project_name: Reducing the Impact of Explosive Remnants of War Risk Education in Schools, IDP camps, host communities across Aleppo and Idleb and provide improved support to survivors of ERW.
project_objective:
Shafak will deliver a comprehensive approach to Mine Action involving Risk Education (RE), and Victim Assistance (VA). This project will be a continuation of an existing Explosive Remnants of War Risk Education ERW - RE programme in Idleb and Aleppo. Shafak proposes that RE activities continue on by existing teams.
Shafak is providing ERW-RE to children in the communities of Idleb and Aleppo. Because ERW’s are a long term problem, Shafak believes that long impact approaches for children must be sustained; the more a child is taught safe behaviours, the more likely it is that they will become ingrained in their day-to-day activity.
Under the ERW-RE part of the project, 4 teams of 5, each consisting of 2 groups of 2 and a team leader, who have already been trained by Shafak, will target locations in Idleb and Aleppo providing school-age children with RE activities, and materials to inform them about dangers of ERW. They will also provide RE material to the older generation, putting up posters about the ERW risks in the public streets and communities to increase the awareness of ERW threats. Schools and locations that were not reached in previous messaging will be the first priority.
In addition to, Risk Education will be conducted in IDP camps and host communities. Whilst the sessions will be open to all community members, the teams will be placing particular emphasis on reaching those who are most at risk of accident, including children, young men and IDPs who may not be familiar with the type of threat present in the area. The sessions will be held in both schools and community spaces. The teams will also distribute flyers and posters with Risk Education messaging to reach the wider community.
Furthermore, a “Training of Trainer” (ToT) Trainer will provide RE training to Community Focal Points (CFPs) in affected communities, and RE teams and other workers from NGOs across all humanitarian sectors, to improve the relevance, integration and reach of RE messaging across NW Syria. This information can then be used to better understand protection gaps and improve future programming. It will also be used in advocacy initiatives.

Also, the project will also enhance the resilience of people living with injuries and disabilities (PLWDs), focusing on ERW survivors, through referrals to specialized services.

the Project will target 65,850 individuals by MA services

project_name: Responsd and mitigate the protection risks faced by Syrians affected by Conflict in North West Syria by provision of comprehensive Protection Services
project_objective:
Shafak Organization proposes to mitigate/respond to the protection risks faced by the conflict-affected people in Daret Azza, and Azaz sub-districts in Aleppo governorate, as well as in Salqin, Dana and Idleb sub-districts in Idleb governorate through a community center and community outreach teams.  The purpose of this project is to empower local communities and conflict-affected individuals in North West Syria, and support their role in building society and in determining their future, through the provision of protection services and emergency protection services to 57940 displaced people and host community at a community center and through mobile outreach teams. The provided protection services will comprise both mitigation and response services as well as specialized and non-specialized protection services. The project technical staff composed of 38 (Female and Male), will be providing the protection activities in Salqin and Idleb community centers and through eight mobile teams in Daret Azza, Dana and Azaz districts. 
The proposed project will offer gender and age disaggregated general protection services, PSS/recreational activities, case management, Referral, awareness raising, vocational training, legal assistance and legal awareness raising sessions of 
HLP and CSD, protection monitoring, and to community networks support. In case of emergencies, the project activities will be shifted to respond to the emergency protection needs of new displaced people delivering the protection emergency package like: PFA, referrals and case fund support to respond to the urgent needs of IDPs. 
Training on HLP and CSD will be delivered to partners’ legal staff and community actors in Syria and Turkey by specialized legal staff in accordance with the protection cluster and HLP WTG guidance and SOPs. 400 legal staff and humanitarian actors will be trained on CSD and HLP. 
These protection services will be offered to vulnerable IDPs in Salqin, and Idleb sub-districts via community centers, as well as Daret Azza, Azaz, Dana, sub-districts will be targeted through protection outreach activities. The proposed intervention will be implemented with particular emphasis on quality services to People with Disabilities (PwDs) and elderly women and men. 
Shafak will consult with the community members at the beginning of the project to introduce the project activities and have them involved in the selection of the community centers locations, as well as Shafak will establish community committees from the same communities and train them on protection topics such as; CPMS, Safe identification and referral and communication skills to enable them identify and refer people in need to the case management team. Moreover, the community committees will play a significant role in raising protection issues that are faced by the community and mobilizing them to participate in project activities. 
The activities will emphasize equity and non-discrimination, reinforcing the basic social and human rights of participants while taking into consideration the cultural, historical and social specificities of targeted populations.

project_name: Multi-disciplinary Rehabilitation and mental health-psychosocial support services for conflict affected populations and support to health structures in Syria.
project_objective:
The project aims to reduce vulnerability and improve physical and mental well-being of crisis-affected population with particular attention to the specific vulnerabilities linked to gender, age and disability.  The organization’s action will focus on providing multi-disciplinary health services tailored to the needs of people with physical and functional limitations and their caregivers through direct intervention or through the support of local partners in North-West, North-East and GoS-controlled parts of Syria. 
The intervention includes the provision of a multidisciplinary physical rehabilitation services (including the provision of assistive mobility devices, prostheses and orthoses and education sessions for caregivers) and the provision of psychosocial support services to physical rehabilitation beneficiaries and their caregivers.
The organization will consolidate and strengthen its support to health facilities so as to set up sustainable physical rehabilitation and prosthetic & orthotic services while the organization’s outreach teams reach out to IDPs; remote and underserved communities; as well as persons who are incapable of reaching the service centers. These mobile teams will work on assessing and referring beneficiaries to relevant health service providers. In GoS- controlled areas, the organization will focus on developing rehabilitation services in areas where services are not present or functioning through the support of registered local health partners.
These services not only help in the recovery of physical rehabilitation beneficiaries and the improvement of their functional independence but also targets caregivers in a holistic approach in order to alleviate stress, fatigue and other psychological impacts related to their new caregiving responsibilities. 
The organization’s intervention in GoS- controlled areas and North-west of Syria will also include the provision of MHPSS to people suffering from psychological distress without having physical rehabilitation needs. MHPSS services include psychological first aid, psychoeducation, and individual and/or group session therapy.
In parallel, and in order to ensure the sustainability and quality of the action, the organization will provide support to its local health partners through technical, financial and managerial support as well as the development of capacity building plans tailored to the needs of these partners. 
The organization’s services include:
1- Physical and functional rehabilitation (including physical and functional rehabilitation sessions, provision of assistive devices, education sessions for caregivers), 
2- P&O services (fitting sessions and provision of P&O items),
3- PSS sessions to people with functional limitations and their caregivers
4- MHPSS services (psychological first aid, psychoeducation, individual session therapy or MHPSS group sessions).
5- Capacity building plans for local partners.

project_name: Provision of emergency life-saving assistance through safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education services for children in NW Syria
project_objective:
Shafak, in line with education cluster’s objectives and in coordination with involved authorities as well as targeted communities, will focus on achieving two major goals:
- scaling up access to formal and non-formal education for Syrian crisis-affected children
- enhancing the quality of formal and non-formal education within a protective environment
Access strategies will include small-scale rehabilitation of damaged schools and establishment of other safe temporary/alternative learning spaces through a gender-sensitive and disability-friendly approach. It is critical to improve the access to quality education services for IDPs in camps and within communities and ensure that these services are sufficiently linked to Child Protection interventions including the integration of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and other specialized protection services. It is increasingly critical to expand access to psychosocial support and recreational activities for vulnerable children, particularly in areas of high severity of need.
Shafak will support formal education in 22 schools targeting approximately 7920 students (4196 boys and 3724 girls) where this intervention will minimize the risk of students dropping out, where monthly incentives to teachers will be provided, as they don’t have any alternative fund in addition to provision of education materials for students and teachers and providing schools with necessary operational costs (including heating for winter). 

As education is one of the very basic children’s rights, Shafak is planning to provide access to education for children with disabilities by providing transportation services and improve school environment by provide targeted assistance within the schools in order to encourage these children to continue their education and integrate them with their peers.
Non-formal education opportunities and pathways back to inclusive education at age appropriate levels are increasingly required to address the complex learning needs of children.
Thus, non-formal education will target school girls and boys (aged 8-12 and gender disaggregated) to fill in existing needs, where 16 Non-Formal Education centres will be supported targeting approximately 4400 children (2000 boys/2400 girls, 8-12 years old) to provide literacy and numeracy along with PSS sessions; the PSS activities will be selected from I-Deal curriculum; the Curriculum used for Non-Formal Activities will be Curriculum B, that combines 2 academic years in one or, the Self Learning Programme (SLP) and will run in one cycle in summer time. 
Children and youth accessing formal and non-formal education are not experiencing quality teaching, and there are growing concerns that the toll of the crisis in its many forms is preventing children from attaining foundational literacy and numeracy skills as well as those skills relevant to cognitive, social and economic empowerment. Hence, teachers will be equipped with the skills in non-formal education modalities, child-centred pedagogy, and positive classroom management to cope with overcrowded classrooms, address and accommodate host community, displaced and returnee children within their classes. 
Stakeholders in the project implementation site, including children, adolescents and older persons, including PwDs and their opinions are taken into account while developing the project design, implementation of activities so that they have better access to humanitarian services and information in accordance to their specific situation.
The project will make sure that children engaging in child labour or recruited for military purposes, or living with older or disabled caregivers or adolescent girls at risk of early or forced marriage are given special attention and have their own space to participate in the project activities and are properly referred as per Protection cluster guidelines.

project_name: Provision of Adequate Shelters and Non-Food Items for Vulnerable Groups in Northern Syria
project_objective:
This project aims to enhance the living conditions of vulnerable groups thorough providing a comprehensive Shelter and NFI services for vulnerable IDP households and host communities through the following:

-	rehabilitation of emergency shelter spaces in collective centers, unﬁnished buildings, and damaged houses reaching 1730 households, where 380 medium-damaged houses will be rehabilitated in Maret Tmasrin sub district, 150 unﬁnished houses will be upgraded in Daret Azzeh and Maaret-Tmasrin sub districts, 200 light-damaged houses will be rehabilitated.
-	Distribution of shelter kits to 1000 HHs (IDPs and host communities).
-	Distribution of 2,000 new arrival kits/NFIs for 2,000 IDPs households (12,000 individuals disaggregated by gender: 1850 men, 2150 women, 3650 boys and 4350 girls) in Atareb Harem, Salqin, Armanaz, Kafar-Tkharim, Idleb and Maret Tmasrin sub-districts.
-	Distribution of 3000 winterization kits/vouchers to 3000 HHs/ 18000 individuals disaggregated by gender (2850 men, 3150 women, 6250 girls and 5750 boys).

project_name: Provision of health assistance to most vulnerable population
project_objective:
The program is a continuation of existing IMC activities through static clinics and medical mobile teams.
-	Masakeh Barzeh static clinic is operational since 2008, Jaramana and Sanamayn clinics since 2013. Barzeh was established to respond to the needs of the Iraqi refugees, while Jaramana and Sanamayn targeted conflict affected population. 
-	Mobile clinics are deployed in different areas based on assessed needs; current areas of intervention are 8 villages in Nashabiye (since October 2018); Babella, Yalda and Beit Sahem (since January 2019); Medira, Misraba and Beit Sawa (since May 2019); shelters and open communities in Dummar, Nahr Eshe and Al Zahera (since June 2019). Additional 2 mobiles are planned to be deployed in Zamalka and Sabqa based on needs assessments conducted during the last quarter of 2019 (pending approval). 

IMC plans for 2020 are to continue provision of comprehensive PHC services to most affected population including hosting communities, displaced and returnees through its static clinics (existing) and mobile medical teams (5 operational, 2 planned), while also expand its work by providing support to PHC public facilities through capacity building, provision of supplies and equipment.  While the specific support to public facilities will be determined based on findings of needs assessments, IMC will seek to prioritize newly accessible areas and areas assessed with highest gaps in primary healthcare service provision and will coordinate with other humanitarian actors (either bilaterally or through the cluster) in order to complement and avoid overlapping. 
Although specific services vary based on the facility (either static or mobile), generally IMC provides the following services - related to preventive and curative healthcare for both communicable and non-communicable diseases: internal medicine, pediatrics, gynecology, ENT, ophthalmology, dental care, provision of medications, basic lab services, health education and malnutrition screening. Services such as gynecology, pediatrics and screening for malnutrition target specifically women and children. Some of the facilities (2 static and 3 mobiles) also provide case management for MH and GBV related cases, with available advanced support as needed. 
Through private service providers, IMC financially support referrals to advanced care (consultations, surgeries, specialized diagnostic services) for most vulnerable population and provides mobility/disability NFIs (including hearing aids, wheelchairs, crutches, diapers, medical consumables) to people in need, based on internal SOPs and available budget. Selection criteria for the referrals include: socio-economic vulnerability; necessity and duration of the suggested treatment; concomitant diseases and age; feasibility and evidence base of the treatment plan; prognosis. For provision of NFIs, criteria vary based on the item to be provided, but all require IMC doctor to examine the patient.
All services at IMC clinics, both static and mobiles, are provided free of charge to all population. On average among all facilities, female represent 60 to 70% of the total beneficiaries served; children below 5 years of age are approximately 15% and beneficiaries below 18 years of age about 30%. Consultations to people with disability amount to approximately 2% of total consultations. Based on previous trends, approximately 65% of the consultations are related to NCDs.
IMC is part of the health cluster as well as the MHPSS sub-group and shares regularly 4Ws regarding implemented activities both to Health and Nutrition clusters as well as IMCI monthly reports. IMC also coordinates with the MoH regarding the Early Warning and Response System (EWARS), aimed at strengthening the national surveillance system and early detect epidemic threats.
The proposed response is in line with the sector priorities for 2020, overall focusing on sustaining and expanding quality healthcare services at primary, secondary and tertiary levels.

project_name: Integrated community based interventions to enhance protection for most vulnerable categories of Syrian population
project_objective:
IMC proposes to continue its current programming implemented within its community center (RAC – Recreational Activity Center) in Jaramana, through 2 mobile teams deployed in 3 areas of Eastern Ghouta and 2 shelters in Damascus. In addition, IMC aims at scaling up its activities by deploying 2 additional mobile teams (locations to be determined based on needs assessments) to reach those most vulnerable categories facing a range of different barriers to access these services.
While case management services will be provided within the mobile teams, Jaramana community will be able to access these services at the IMC PHC clinic located in the same neighborhood. 
PSS activities will be conducted both at the RAC and through the mobile teams and include non-formal education and skill development (such as literacy, English and Arabic courses), social and recreational activities (such as handcraft, music, theatre and art classes) targeting children, youth and adults. 
Specifically for children with intellectual disabilities and developmental delays, IMC will continue implementing its rehabilitation and inclusion program while also targeting their parents/caregivers with training programs aiming at strengthening their capacities in assisting their children's mental, physical and educational development. 
Other positive parenting skills programs such as Early Child Development (ECD) programs, Caregivers Skills Training (CST) will be offered at the RAC. 
Both at RAC and mobile teams, IMC will also organize and conduct awareness raising activities on different topics related to mental health, child protection and GBV.
Overall this intervention will create opportunities for the target communities to establish new positive coping mechanisms and strengthen the existing ones, ultimately contributing in improving their wellbeing, reduce protection related risks and enhancing their resilience.

project_name: Emergency WASH intervention through provision of hygiene promotion activities and distribution of essential WASH NFIs in North East Syria and Hama.
project_objective:
In alignment with 2020 WASH Sector strategy, International Medical Corps (IMC) proposes to build upon its emergency hygiene promotion programming and provide emergency WASH assistance and capacity-building support to conflict-affected populations in North East Syria and in Hama. The proposed program will target 205,027 beneficiaries (53,307 males, 79,961 females, 28,704 boys, 43,055 girls). Sixty percent of them are IDPs, 20% returnees and 20% are hosts, whereby IMC will continue its close work and coordination with Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC) branches in Deir-Ez-Zor, Al Hasakeh and Hama to respond to the emerging needs of the newly displaced populations, displaced population living collective shelters and camps, and other vulnerable population. IMC and SARC teams identified the following locations and areas for 2020 intervention: In Al Hasakeh, the proposed program will target 88,727 individuals (23,069 males, 34,603 females, 12,423 boys, 18,632 girls) residing in 62 IDP shelters, Al Hole and Areeshe camp. In Deir-Ez-Zor, the teams will target 55,100 individuals (14,326 males, 21,489 females, 7,714 boys, 11,571 girls) residing in Kharita, Zghir Shamiyeh, Ashara Gharibeh and Mahkan host communities, while in Hama, teams will target 61,200 individuals (15,912 males, 23,868 females, 8,568 boys, 12,852 girls) residing in Taqsis, Maar Dis, Tiba Elemam, Tiba Elesm, Zwr Al Massaleq and Karnaz. These areas have been selected based on the priorities areas identified within the 2020 HRP by the WASH Sector as well as the findings of the rapid needs assessments conducted by IMC, in areas where IMC has secured access through SARC.
In order to help communities in  maintaining a healthy and safe hygiene environment, the intervention will adopt a resilience-oriented approach and through training and capacity building activities, will directly engage target populations in efforts to promote best hygiene knowledge, attitudes and practices.
Recognizing the specific health and protection concerns of conflict-affected women, men and adolescents (boys and girls) the proposed program will be open to all population segments, ensuring their meaningful participation in the design, implementation and monitoring of the intervention. Through education and training of  community volunteers (especially females) the program will contribute in empowering them to become not only beneficiaries but also service providers within their own conflict-affected communities.

project_name: Support to self-reliance and livelihood through vocational training
project_objective:
International Medical Corps have addressed the importance of livelihood and vocational skills needs of internally displaced and host Syrians in alleviating mental stress, GBV and exploitation by offering a variety of training courses of varying lengths. The proposed program aims at improving the livelihoods and resilience of the targeted population beneficiaries (450 Syrian youth and adults) by increasing their skills with the view of improving their livelihood opportunities through vocational training (VT).
The choice of training will be based on each beneficiary background, interests and future aspirations. 
Beneficiaries will be identified and selected as follows:
-	Internal referrals with other IMC programs (specifically MHPSS, Protection and Health activities) 
-	External referrals from other organizations such as Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC) and other NGOs. 
Main criteria for selection will be: 
	internally displaced person;
	female heads of household;
	youth who have dropped out from schools
	members of low-income/large families
	survivors of gender-based violence
	people experiencing mental health challenges.

The courses will be delivered in officially certified institutes registered with the General Association of Syrian craftsmen. All successful participants will therefore receive a certificate that is recognized by Syrian employers upon completion of the program. Based on the specifics of the course, participants will receive start-up kits to support them in establishing their income generating activity. Besides building the technical capacity of the participants, the VT courses are also designed to help the beneficiaries mitigate the negative effects of the crisis on their mental and psychosocial well-being. In addition to contribute to improve beneficiaries’ livelihoods, the program also aims at reducing their vulnerabilities by engaging them in a team of peers and therefore helping them make new friends; the increase of knowledge and skills will enable participants to improve their self-esteem, become more self-reliant. In this aspect, the VT has proved very effective in improving the beneficiaries’ social lives. For youth out of school, who might be at risk of exploitation, illegal migration, armed recruitment or being engaged in illegal or other risky activities, VT also represent an opportunity for them to provide an income for their family.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Assistance to Conflict Affected Populations in Idleb and Aleppo governorates.
project_objective:
The proposed action seeks to protect and enhance food security and livelihoods of and protect conflict-affected highly vulnerable IDPs and host communities in North West Syria (NWS). This will be achieved through an integrated programme of assistance including repeat mixed-modality life-sustaining food assistance (monthly assistance to the most vulnerable households) and emergency life-saving food security assistance in addition to livelihoods support. The complementary package of livelihoods support will increase household resilience through the promotion of entrepreneurship and the development of small businesses and to improve agricultural production and increase the ability of targeted households to meet food needs.

The proposed action seeks to target an estimated total of 108,510 beneficiaries, of which 58,192 are female and 50,318 are male. Further breakdown of beneficiaries as follows: 
-Females (0-4) = 9,311
-Males (0-4) = 8,051
-Females (5-17) = 18,681
-Males (5-17) = 16,151
-Females (18-59) = 28,222
-Males (18-59) = 24,405
-Females (>59) = 1,978
-Males (>59) = 1,711 

With reference to livelihoods, funding is sought to support the Olive Value Chain (OVC) to improve the livelihoods of 1,500 households / 9,000 conflict affected people in Idleb and northern Aleppo.  A comprehensive program of assistance is planned to benefit 750 small-scale olive farmers and create income generation opportunities for an additional 750 acutely vulnerable IDP and host families through Cash for Work (CfW). The project will support self-reliance, protect and build productive assets and increase access to inclusive livelihoods. Proposed activities are complemented by our existing Food Security programming in Idleb and northern Aleppo which provides repeat, in-kind food assistance to the most vulnerable households, and by our ongoing Emergency Response (ER) interventions which will continue to provide timely, life-saving assistance to new arrivals. Funding is also sought to promote entrepreneurship and Small Business Development in Idleb and Aleppo governorates. The NGO proposes to support entrepreneurship and the growth of small businesses through working with stakeholders in the business community and the relevant local authorities / LCs to promote an environment conducive to and supportive of economic development and entrepreneurship. The project will promote entrepreneurship and the development of 500 small businesses through provision of micro-grants, peer-to-peer networks and entrepreneur support packages that facilitate business start-ups and investment.

project_name: Integration of Protection Services into Health Facilities
project_objective:
SAMS through this project aims to continue providing support to the female and male survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, as well as their extended networks (families, communities, relief workers, care providers, and civil society) in Northwest Syria including the provision of safe spaces for women and girls in health facilities in NW Syria, provision of specialized GBV services to survivors, including case management and referrals for health and MHPSS services, enable the empowerment of GBV women survivors and their families through group discussions, various activities and the distribution of IEC materials, and introduce service providers to proper GBV screening processes and techniques. 

SAMS will work on supporting VA services in Termanin and Alnafs Almotmaenna facilities, SAMS will support also outreach team in number of supported health facilities, each outreach team will consist of 2 PSS workers and 2 Physiotherapist, in addition to one team leader which will be leading the outreach teams; SAMS will refer the cases to the specialized services (MHPSS,  Physiotherapy, and any other services as needed);  SAMS will procure assistive products and consumables to support the direct and indirect victims; Means of transportation services will be provided to GBV survivors and direct and indirect victims. SAMS will build the capacity of service providers.   

Through this project, SAMS will work on achieving the following objectives: 
Objective 1: Improve the access to specialized quality GBV services for both female and male in the supported locations (HFs and safe space)
Objective 2: Enhance strategies to empower women and girls and raise awareness about GBV in North-West Syria. 
Objective 3: Increase the number of direct and indirect victims of explosive hazard accidents receiving needs-appropriate assistance in northwest Syria 
Objective 3: Build the capacity of the Service Providers

Continue Implementation Plan section: Mine Action:  Provide Physiotherapy consultations and treatment sessions to EH victims. Provide Assistive products and consumables to victims. Provide individual mental health consultation. Provide group sessions and self-care sessions to victims and their families. Provide community-based VA services through outreach team in areas near facilities. 6. Refer the victims to specialized services as needed. SAMS will monitor the project’s activities in terms of achievement and percentage of progress against the targets and will conduct quarterly monitoring visits to the supported faculties. SAMS developed a new Monitoring tool for the GBV activities (which respect the privacy and sensitivity of the cases) it will be used under the supervision of the GBV specialist, SAMS will monitor the quality of the project also, through KAP surveys and semi-annual FGDs. For the VA services, will use Functional Independence Measure, and WHO DAS.

project_name: Improved Access to Healthcare services in Dar'a, Quneitra, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Deir ez-Zoor, Homs and El-Hassakeh governorates
project_objective:
Dorcas plans to intervene in the South of Syria through rehabilitation of eight health units,
fully equipping them and training MoH staffs, running two mobile and two static health
facilities as well as support private health facilities in Aleppo, Homs, Rural Damascus, El-Hasakeh
through the provision of medical equipment and medical supplies.

project_name: Integrated Protection Assistance for Women, Children, PwD, PwSN and Elderly in Aleppo, Homs and Rural Damascus
project_objective: Dorcas plans to implement integrated protection assistance projects targeting women, children, people with disabilities, people with specific needs and elderly through targeted assistance. General protection, child protection activities, PSS activities in group and/or individual sessions, as well as mine-risk education activities are planned to children, their parents, women, survivors of GBV and elderly. Services are provided by trained staff according to the social work methodology.

project_name: Livelihoods support to vulnerable households in Aleppo and Homs
project_objective: Dorcas aims to support 160 breadwinners in Aleppo and Homs to be able to support their households independently

project_name: Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the Most Crisis-impacted Communities in Syria
project_objective:
The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities  impacted by the crisis. 
Communities, particularly those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain control over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than 5,000 Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale

The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5. Social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

project_name: Enhancing preparedness and response capacity for prevention and control of potential epidemic of high thread pathogens in Syria
project_objective:
Detecting and responding rapidly to signals that could indicate outbreaks of epidemic-prone diseases is a priority of health intervention to minimize mortality from communicable diseases. Syria has suffered from a disrupted health system, which has created vulnerabilities in the host and IDP populations. Deterioration of living conditions, including limited access to clean water, electricity, vaccines and basic healthcare services, have increased the susceptibility of epidemic-prone diseases. This project’s aim is to reduce morbidity/mortality from preventable infectious diseases among emergency affected populations by enhancing emergency preparedness and response capacities. 
In response to the conflict and population displacement in Syria beginning in 2011, WHO, the MOH and partners established an Early Warning Alert and Response System (EWARS) in 2012. The system has expanded from 120 to 1328 reporting units, with a presence in all 14 governorates. EWARS has largely replaced the legacy national surveillance systems. However, coverage varies among governorates, depending on security and access. This project aims to enhance surveillance systems through continuously-updated electronic solutions using a web-based interface with integration of other vertical surveillance systems to detect unusual events that might signal an outbreak. 
Successful detection, characterization and tracking and management/control strategies of disease outbreaks require accurate lab confirmation. However, there are major gaps in laboratory diagnoses for epidemic-prone diseases and biosafety practices in public health labs. This project will enhance the knowledge and skills of lab techs to improve detection and confirmation of high threat pathogens, which is essential for timely response. 
WHO leads investigation and outbreak response including technical expertise, capacity building, operational and logistic support according to the needs and in collaboration with the health authorities and the implementing health partners.

project_name: COVID-19 PREPAREDNESS AND REPONSE IN WASH
project_objective: To prepare for and respond to an outbreak of COVID-19 in North-East Nigeria, IOM will scale up the ongoing WASH intervention (HNGA20-WSH-161691-1) through: (a) Provision of safe, equitable and adequate water, including repair and upgrading of water systems, water trucking, chlorination/disinfection of water points, and support health facilities with the provision of water; (b) Provision of safe and digniﬁed sanitation facilities, including care and maintenance of sanitation facilities, regular desludging of latrines, and installation of handwashing stations; (c) Public health awareness/hygiene promotion and disease containment through risk communication and community engagement, including risk communication through the door-to-door campaign, installation of a public-addressing system, production of Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials and provision of personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation, and hygiene materials and tools to community volunteers and WASH committees; and (d) Provision of basic WASH/hygiene items, including procurement and distribution of basic Hygiene Kits at household level and cleaning supplies for latrines, home and health facility disinfection.

project_name: Inspiring new futures in the Syrian Environment (INFUSE)
project_objective: Although there are significant gaps in the emergency response, particularly in hard to reach areas, other areas have been free of conflict for some time. In many of these areas, households lost their productive assets and are currently reliant on emergency food assistance, despite having the capacity, experience, willingness and skills to develop their own businesses and increase their self-reliance. Providing livelihood assistance in the form of the restoration of productive assets lost due to the crisis offers a cost-efficient way to improve resiliency and self-reliance among vulnerable households beyond the life of the project. The INFUSE project targets a total of 950 men and women for small business training, followed by the provision of a livelihood restoration in-kind grant for 662 households. A total of 3,598 individuals are expected to benefit from the project.

project_name: Health in Emergencies Assisting Lives (HEAL)
project_objective:
The Health in Emergencies Assisting Lives (HEAL) Project will benefit 25,000 highly vulnerable individuals, including 7,000 men, 7,000 women, 5,500 boys and 5,500 girls through the restoration of access health services through the rehabilitation of five health centres in the governorates of Deir-ez-Zor, Aleppo, Homs and Rural Damascus.
The HEAL Project will target underserved, overburdened host communities with a high IDP population, urban and rural communities with no current access to local health facilities and areas with high numbers of vulnerable individuals including women, boys and girls, older adults, pregnant and lactating women in addition to areas with high morbidity rates and health risks. Where possible, ADRA will implement health centre rehabilitation as part of an integrated approach including WASH, livelihood, food security or education activities. The project emphasizes an integrated approach to consider MHPSS, GBV, BCD , referral etc.

project_name: WASH Assistance To Enable Resiliency (WATER)
project_objective:
The WASH Assistance To Enhance Resilience (WATER) Project will target approximately 385,000 vulnerable individuals, including 107,800 men, 107,800 women, 84,700 boys and 84,700 girls, with urgent WASH assistance in areas of high severity across the governorates of Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor, Homs, Rural Damascus, Quneitra and Dar’a. This project aims to provide both life-saving and life-sustaining assistance to communities underserved by the humanitarian community with critical WASH needs including difficulty of access to safe and sufficient drinking water in a sanitary environment due to infrastructural damage and disrepair and increased pressure on local water resources.
