The WATER Project will provide life-saving assistance to highly vulnerable IDPs in the context of an emergency response through the rehabilitation of WASH facilities and hygiene kit distribution. Life-sustaining assistance will target highly vulnerable conflict-affected or overburdened communities with a high IDP/ spontaneous returnee population or those underserved by the humanitarian community and having experienced a recent change in control with life-sustaining activities. Community-level vulnerability will be assessed according to the presence of highly vulnerable groups such as the elderly, people with disabilities, female-headed households, women and children, and with high numbers of individuals resorting to negative coping mechanisms due to economic impoverishment. Activities will include the rehabilitation of water and sewerage systems, including boreholes and pumping stations, the provision of Reverse Osmosis units to communities with high nitrate levels, community and household water tanks, and solid waste management. 
This project will adopt a participatory, community-based approach ensuring the participation of vulnerable men, women, boys, girls, people with disabilities, the elderly, and female-headed households in the design, implementation and evaluation of the project.

project_name: Security Support to Humanitarian Response in 2020 for Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) States, Nigeria
project_objective: This project is to provide reliable security coverage for UN AFPs and Implementing Partners (IPs) presence and operations in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) states of Nigeria. It is absolutely vital and relevant as the majority of agencies have significantly expanded their existing programmes and personnel presence in terms of capacity and geographical location. This will place additional security burden on  UNDSS in the BAY states. The capacity of UNDSS needs to be expanded to meet this demand.

project_name: Protecting Women, Adolescent Girls and Boys through the Provision of Comprehensive SGBV Prevention and Mitigation Response Services in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
Shafak protection strategy in 2020 aims to strengthen protection interventions to support the overall protection cluster objectives in addition to sub-clusters GBV towards the provision as well as the response of integrated GBV specialized services with focusing on most vulnerable people such as adolescent girls, elderly and PwDs.  Shafak through this project will continue to support GBV activities within women and girls safe space (WGSS) centers called Makany at Maarat Misrin, and Qurqania, in addition to two community center called Makany and Alkarameh at Idleb city; also, within RH facility in Maarat Misrin; finally, at Azaz reception center at Azaz city. Shafak will deepen the commitment to protection programming, to projects that support GBV, Women Empowerment, and social GBV advocacy projects to support women and girls at risk in NW Syria. The GBV delivery points will be able to provide response and mitigation services to a total of 5000 women and girls on a monthly basis. The project activities will include prevention, mitigation, and response GBV activities where the outreach teams under prevention/mitigation activities will be responding across the locations, wherever the need arises by conduct the following activities:

1- safety audits in the sector of GBV informed camps in the target locations (two camps each location, quarterly bases), 
2- PSS non-structures sessions where the recreational activities will be part of PSS (a total of 2000 girls, 2000boys, 500 women, and 200 men will be targeted), 
3- GBV awareness-raising sessions/campaign to target women, men, boys, and girls (the teams will use GBV tool kit who develop by GBV sub-cluster as a method to target men and adolescent boys) a total of 1000 girls, 500 boys, 1000 women, and 200 men will be targeted), 
4- Furthermore, as part of response activates the outreach teams will conduct Psychological First Aid (PFA) within camps, reception centers, and other IDPs collective places. 

On other hands, the centers teams will deliver comprehensive GBV services including prevention, mitigation, and with focus on GBV specialized response services as follow: 
1- PSS structured /non-structured services (2000 women, and 1500 Girls), 
2- Women and girls’ empowerment activates (life skills, vocational training) (2000 women, and 500 girls), 
3- Young mothers club activity (500 girls), 
4- GBV case management (there will be three caseworkers each center and they deal with 60 GBV cases each month), 
5- Individual and group counseling. Shafak will engage men and boys in GBV prevention activities by mobile GBV activities, which aimed to mitigate the GBV risks, besides, to make the community more supportive of GBV issues. 

Shafak GBV response strategy is in line with the protection needs overview and in coordination with the GBV Sub-Cluster. Shafak is committed to coordinate with women-led organizations in the target locations who operating GBV projects and respond closely with their needs specialty technical GBV capacity building training.

project_name: Food and Cash-based Assistance for Vulnerable Populations in Somalia
project_objective: Enlargement of Project # 159360: The figures consider, in addition to WFP reprogramming, increased needs based on new IPC data (500,000) and approximately 6,500 confirmed cases targeted through WHO-supported treatment centers. , Total estimated beneficiaries = 1448984

project_name: COVID-19 Logistics support to the humanitarian community in Somalia
Sustaining and enhancing access to primary healthcare in Aleppo and Idleb through Atareb, Sarmada and Termanin PHC centers
project_objective:
The project is a continuation of a series of projects funded by MTI, WHO and SCHF (through SRD and RF) in 2019. The objective of this project is to sustain access to primary healthcare services to the populations of Termanin, Sarmada, and Atareb in northern Syria through the following 3 facilities:
- Sarmada PHC (Sarmada PHC Center!G0703011)
- Termanin PHC (Tarmanin PHC Center!G0703028)
- Atareb PHC (Atareb PHC Center!B0200001)
The objective is to provide an adequate health response to the waves of IDPs arriving in northern Idleb, support the referral network and implement the essential components of the standard package of primary health care services, according to the package adopted by the health cluster in Gaziantep.
Under this project UDER proposes to continue addressing the critical needs for referral network and primary healthcare in northern Syria, by supporting the same facilities for 1 year. UDER will continue providing the health facilities with running costs, essential salaries, emergency maintenance costs and referrals for the period from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2020. With this support UDER will ensure that the health facilities will continue to operate, staff will be retained, referrals will be followed and health services will continue to be provided to people in need in northern Syria. This is necessary to provide essential life-sustaining and life-saving primary healthcare services. 
All the proposed 3 health facilities are referral centers for more than 100 community health workers providing services for the population of their communities. The PHCs are essential for ensuring effective community health services and for functional referral systems. Identification of cases that need further medical care starts at the community level, then the health facilities provide the necessary health services, which makes community health services and facility-based primary health care services complementary to each other. On a monthly basis, the community health workers refer the following to the 3 PHCs:
•	225 pregnant women for antenatal care consultations;
•	550 children-under-5 for vaccinations;
•	80 children-under-5 and 40 pregnant women for nutrition services;
•	130 patients for hypertension care
•	70 patients for diabetes care

project_name: Protection risk response, prevention and mitigation amongst conflict- and displacement-affected communities in Syria
project_objective:
DRC will respond to the endemic and acute protection needs of up to 35,000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community members in locations with 3 or above on the severity scale. The focus will be on at-risk women and girls, boys, men of recruitable age, the elderly and people will disabilities. The overall objective is to provide people of concern with protection and humanitarian assistance while being supported to identify durable solutions. This will be achieved through the delivery of four key outcomes: to increase the psychosocial wellbeing and reinforce coping capacities of displacement- affected individuals; to ensure displacement-affected individuals have access to rights and safe, inclusive, participatory humanitarian assistance through protection mainstreamed services; to mitigate the impact of protection threats affecting displacement-affected individuals, and to strengthen self-protective capacities and empowerment by building and supporting community-based protection mechanisms.
Structured courses that address key PSS needs will be delivered to improve psychosocial and general wellbeing, enhancing capacities to cope with the shocks and stressors of protracted displacement and acute emergencies. This will be supported by one-to-one counseling for more complex psychosocial cases requiring and other group-based activities. Safe locations will be provided where people can meet and socialize with semi-structured activities. Facilitators will be present to provide space where people can take the lead in developing social networks which can eventually extend beyond DRC operational spaces. Activities will be delivered to increase awareness of basic protection and humanitarian principles across the response through protection mainstreaming and tailored protection capacity building. Further efforts will be committed to the analysis of trends in the changing protection environment in Syria, with a view to better informing both programming and advocacy.
DRC will address the concerns of children and vulnerable men and women through the delivery of case management and individual protection assistance (IPA).
DRC will implement community-based protection involving the participation of communities to identify risks and propose solutions, offer peer support and inform programming and advocacy. This includes supporting community-based structures such as protection committees. DRC will also address the threats posed by the presence of Unexploded Ordinance in populated areas, for 50,000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community members, to improve the physical safety for Syrians living in, moving through, returning to or settling in contaminated areas through life-saving Humanitarian Mine Action response

project_name: Shelter assistance to Returnees and IDPs
project_objective:
Returnees are assisted in compliance with the Sector Minimum Standards. Installation of durable material at the place of origin by selected local construction companies in the governorates of DRC intervention. This is a needs-based intervention taking into account vulnerability criteria in the selection of people beneﬁting from this intervention. DRC target number for 2020: 36.000 individuals
IDP assistance follows Shelter Sector Standards and is executed in the governorates of DRC intervention. Emergency  IDP assistance may be provided in camp settings, collective shelters, and private unﬁnished/demolished buildings ( where the needs do arise ) in both, urban and rural areas. Newly displaced populations get prioritized as emergency response, according to the Sector’s directive. DRC target number for 2020: 17.500

project_name: Integrated Emergency Nutrition Services for Malnourished Children under Five Years and pregnant and lactating women in Greater Bagari, Wau Western Bahr el Ghazal
project_objective:
The goal of this intervention is to contribute to the collective effort to reduce the GAM rate to less than 10% in Greater Bagari through the provision of quality lifesaving CMAM interventions to children 6-59 months and Pregnant and Lactating
Women in all 14 Bomas of Greater Bagari (Baggari, Bazia, and Besselia).
Through this project, Johanniter will screen over 90% of children under five years 10,946 (5,691 girls and boys 5,254) and also over 90% of pregnant and lactating women 4,170 for malnutrition in the 14 Bomas of Bagari and Besselia areas. Additionally, a total of 7,531 women and 796 men will directly be reached through MIYCN messaging and counseling at the community level. The project will reach at least 80% of SAM and MAM in girls and boys 6-59 months; 80% of PLW. The estimated number of SAM cases is 1,174 and MAM in children under five years 3,577 and MAM in PLW 978. Indirect beneficiaries of this project will include 790 males who are caretakers of children under five, County health department staff, health workers and Community nutrition volunteers (CNVs).

The project will be a continuation of the current emergency nutrition response in Bagari, Bazia and Besselia by Johanniter under the SSHF 2018. The project will be complemented by on-going UNICEF and WFP projects in Wau and Jur River, and a GBV project privately funded under Johanniter which will support with protection services.

In an effort to address the prevailing humanitarian situation in the Baggari, Bazia, and Besselia area, Johanniter is requesting SSHF funds to continue the current emergency nutrition intervention which has already seen nutrition centers established, staff trained, increased outreach activities, the formation of mother to mother groups, reporting, and referral system set up. This will also complement the on-going UNICEF and WFP projects to provide integrated nutrition services to the affected and vulnerable populations. At the moment, Johanniter is in the final stage of development of the PCA with UNICEF and FLA with WFP to cover the OTPs and TSFP activities in Baggari for the period of 2020. 

The 187,500 USD that is being requested will ensure that there are no gaps or interruption in services to the population that has been greatly affected by prolonged insecurity, limited access to basic services and displaced. Under this funding, Johanniter will scale up outreach activities, train health workers on CMAM and MIYCN, recruit more nutrition staff to meet the minimum standards in the nutrition sites, integrate WASH interventions particularly messaging and WASH supplies at facilities so as to reduce on WASH-related diseases, setup feedback mechanisms at the facilities, referral system for both complicated medical cases and GBV cases. The amount being requested will not be able to cover all the planned activities however it will be complemented by UNICEF and WFP budgets.

project_name: WASH COVID-19 response
project_objective: Access to WASH in isolation wards and health facilities, increased access to WASH in vulnerable spaces and vulnerable and highly impacted communities, access to hygiene and COVID-19 messages on prevention and access to services, emergency support for the safe, continous operation of centralized water supply systems

project_name: Increase access to safe, inclusive and quality education for school-aged children and adolescents in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates
project_objective: The targeted sub-districts in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor governorates are severity 4-6.The estimated cost per beneficiary is around 33 USD.Estimated 2% of targeted beneficiaries may have disability Total funds received in 2019: around 1.1 m USD.Total estimated number of beneficiaries reached in 2019: 36,691 individuals.The project is not funded at this stage.Considering the needs and in line with the first pillar of No Lost Generation Initiative,context analysis and demographic trends, the intervention aims at re-establishing basic education services in the targeted communities, which are return areas where services have to cope with the additional stress of population growth. GVC opts for community support, preparing the ground for durable intervention to benefit boys and girls and improving resilience of the whole communities. The Action aims at increasing access to safe, inclusive and quality education for children and adolescents affected by the crisis in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor governorates,relying on GVC expertise in NFE(Non Formal Education),solid reputation and knowledge of the areas. First, to increase access to education, GVC will implement tailored activities targeting out of school children (OOSC) through a Back To Learning (BTL) campaign (including door to door visits, information sessions, interactive theatre) and PSS (Psychosocial Support) events to encourage them and their families to re-enrol in school, possibly, or consider alternative education pathways as well as identify children in need of additional support. The activities will be carried out in cooperation with Directorates of Education (DoEs) and Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC) in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor. Access to school will be enhanced by providing Remedial classes (RCs) to children at risk of drop out, in line with the standards set by the Ministry of Education (MoE) and the Education Sector. In line with the same goal, GVC will involve OOSC in Self-Learning Programs (SLP) supporting the re-enrolment of girls and boys who are out of the school system.Children and teachers in NFE programs will also receive stationery and school bags.Students and OOSC will be involved in PSS activities during the NFE classes and as community outreach events aimed at improving children’s life-skills and KSAs (Knowledge Skills Attitude).Safe and inclusive education will be ensured through rehabilitation of schools, which will include solutions to enable access to students with special needs,and gender and disability-sensitive WASH facilities.The rehabilitation works will increase the number of available learning spaces,having a positive effect in enrolment rates.Furniture, teaching and learning materials(school desks and School in a Box)will be delivered to the schools in need.Finally,GVC intervention will contribute to quality education by training teachers in Active Learning (AL), PSS and Risk Education (RE). The trained teachers will provide SLP and RCs, under the supervision of GVC.

project_name: Increasing protection of children and communities living in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates through tailored risk education program and community outreach activities
project_objective: The project aims at developing a comprehensive Protection program in Aleppo (sub- districts of Jebel Saman, Al-Khafsa, Hadher, Maskana, Menbij, Tall Ed-daman) and Deir- Ez-Zor city, focusing on Risk Education (RE) and Child Protection (CP) as key pillars to carry out tailored community-based activities. Regarding RE, the extensive use of explosive weapons since the beginning of the crisis generated explosive hazards, posing a threat to kill or injure civilians, humanitarian response operators, and disrupting livelihood activities. As school is the most suitable environment to deliver RE to children, teachers need to be properly trained. For this, the Action includes training of 150 teachers in protection-related topics of RE, allowing them to raise children’s ability to deal with threats related to IEDs, landmines and ERW. Each trained teacher will be able to transfer the acquired knowledge to an estimated number of 50 children, reaching a total of 7,500 students, GVC will constantly monitor the training and implement focus group discussions with children to evaluate the impact of the information transferred by their educators. Standardized training materials and kits to deliver awareness sessions to children will be provided by UNICEF and approved by the Ministry of Education (MoE). A second component of the Protection program foresees community-based outreach activities focusing on a wide range of protection needs and tailored to different groups based on age, gender, social role and responsibilities. GVC, supported by Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC), will carry out events and outreach initiatives to raise awareness and stimulate critical thinking on: inclusive education; risks related to early marriage; threats linked with the presence of IEDs, landmines and ERW; psycho-social wellbeing of vulnerable children through PSS support activities. The events will be structured in a way to adapt to different target groups of beneﬁciaries and to the speciﬁc context (e.g. rural/urban) and social dynamics of the community where they take place.

project_name: Providing light rehabilitation of existing water supply services and emergency WASH items to the most vulnerable populations in Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor Governorates
project_objective: GVC will intervene in Deir-Ez-Zor and Aleppo Governorates providing light rehabilitation and repair of water supply services in schools and at community level. In both Governorates, the Action will target Hard to Reach (HTR) areas where the INGO is present with running programs in WASH and Education in Emergency sectors (all ranked 3 to 5 as per WASH severity scale). The Action aims to provide sufficient and safe water to around 76,000 people (25,080 women, 20,520 men, 13,680 boys and 16,720 girls) living in Deir-Ez-Zor city and rural Aleppo areas (sub-districts of Al-Khafsa, Membij, Jebel Saman, Maskane). The Action will ensure access to water to communities and improve the capacity to cope with the increasing number of returnees and/or IDPs. In particular, the following activities are foreseen to guarantee enough quantity and good quality of water for the population: 1) rehabilitation of 1 water pumping station in Jebel Saman sub-district (Handarat); 2) rehabilitation of 1 water reservoir in Al Jafra neighbourhood (Deir-Ez-Zor city); 3) light rehabilitation of existing water networks in case of emergencies as rapid response mechanism within the sub-districts of intervention, based on needs identified case-by-case in coordination with local Water Boards. In addition, the rehabilitation of WASH infrastructures in 12 schools (5 in Deir-Ez-Zor city, 7 in rural Aleppo) will guarantee safe and dignified access to girls and boys thanks to gender-oriented WASH facilities and dedicated toilets for children with disability, thus favouring school attendance for all students. The emergency distribution of family hygiene kits at household level, including jerry cans, and community WASH items, such as water tanks and latrines, will include Hygiene Promotion sessions to the targeted population in the selected areas -tailored on age and gender when feasible- to boost the adoption of correct hygiene practices and consequently reduce the incidence of waterborne diseases.

project_name: Treatment of severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and improvement of Maternal infant Young Child (MIYCN) through Outpatient therapeutic  Program  (OTP) in Yirol East County, Lakes State
project_objective:
In Yirol East County of Lakes State, Help-e.V has been running nutrition services explicitly out-patient management of severe acute malnutrition to under five years old children(OTP) and IYCF messaging in 11 of 12 health facilities. Help e.V is already deploying CMAM intervention. Up to 30th September 2019. Current, Admissions: 1544 children - Yirol East with SAM (Severe Acute Malnutrition) were admitted to the program (1) Oedema (+, ++); (694); MUAC <11.5cm; (717) ""WHZ scores/<-3SD RELAPSE/RELAPSE (61). Whereas, Exits: 1285 children 6-59 months discharged across the eleven (11) operational Out-Patient Therapeutic Posts in (1183 Cured; 5 Deaths, 78 Defaulters and 19 non-respondents) across the eleven (11) operational Out-Patient Therapeutic Posts. Help e.V intends to further develop this multi-dimensional approach by increasing the number of CNVs and MCGs in Yirol East aiming at covering an increasing number of PLW’s of the Ward, opening 3 OTP Outreaches. As a whole CNW and CNV’ will integrate Help’s outreach component to ensure closeness with the community by diffusing key messages. CNV’s will particularly focus on PLW and Mother Care Groups animation while CNW’s will ensure the whole outreach component.  
Albeit, the food security situation slight improvement during the 2019 lean season compared to the 2018 lean season. This improvement was driven by reduced conflict and improved access to livelihoods, markets and humanitarian assistance. Unfortunately, the Former Lakes State has continued to experience high levels of inter-communal violence, which disrupts livelihoods, and it is expected that some households were in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5) in Yirol East during the peak of the lean season. It’s reported that in overall, the proportion of people in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or outcomes has decreased from 73% to 58% between the two years.
In March and April 2018 there has been a high influx of IDPs (reportedly to be around 31,578, people) in Yirol East County. Their original home area is in Mapper County part of Rumbek North. 20191001_IOM_DTM_R6_first_resultes_IDP_RET_Dataset_admin1_2_3
The food security situation for the IDPs is poor all are relying on milk from cows, wild foods, and handouts from the host community. The wild food stocks are severely depleted, including coconut and greens. The host community’s stocks of sorghum and maize have also been eroded. The main coping strategies include; borrowing food from friends and relatives in locations where IDP’s are integrated with hosts (Yali, Advisor, Lekakudu, Malek, Tin Agau and Pagarau), reducing meal portion size, eating less preferred foods and adults eating less so children can have enough. 
Help-e.V conducted a pre-harvest SMART survey in June 2018 in Yirol East and the result showed increased food insecurity at the household level, and high rates of acute malnutrition with of GAM rate of 22.6% and SAM rate of 6.5% among children 6-59 months. Acute malnutrition prevalence among PLWs measured by MUAC (<23 cm), was 25.7%. Infant feeding practices were poor with only 25.8% of children 6-8 months receiving complementary foods and almost no dietary diversity 
Women are not given the chance to take a lead in any decision and still subjected to forced marriages and given out to the man for marriage on auctioning where a woman is taken by the highest bidder. There is still no well-established policy that protects women from sexual abuse and sought women empowerment.

project_name: Strengthening secondary healthcare services for the affected communities in Syria
project_objective: Strengthening and sustaining delivery of standard secondary health care services addressing obstetric care, Neonatal Resuscitation services, and advanced medical and surgical interventions and referral services across the country for men, women, boys and girls requiring life-saving surgical interventions and secondary health care, in addition to women of reproductive age requiring emergency obstetric care. The project also includes improving access to essential medicines and strengthening the capacity of secondary care at hospitals’ level to cope with the emerging demands is important.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Increased life-saving and sustainable access to water, sanitation and hygiene for Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs) in Somalia targeting men, women, boys and girls
project_objective: DRC proposes to undertake a life-saving and sustainable assistance to Disaster-Affected Communities (DACs) through provision of emergency and sustainable WASH interventions (water, sanitation and hygiene). Areas that are mostly affected by droughts, floods and armed conflict will be targeted in the emergency interventions. DRC shall target areas within its intervention and where DRC has presence. DRC has field offices in Mogadishu, Hargeisa, Baidoa, Dollow, Kismaayo and Beletweyne. There are also several small offices across Somalia which will support the proposed interventions. Proposed key activities to be implemented include water trucking through water voucher, rehabilitation of strategic water sources, supply of fast-moving parts for pumps and generators targeting boreholes, construction of emergency latrines and other related WASH activities. DRC defines DACs as people who are internally displaced and are affected by drought and other factors and returnees seeking for reintegration. Therefore, DRC targets IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities. DRC understands that the primary displacements in Somalia is as a result of natural disasters and man-made conflict. However, secondary displacements are now a common reality due to either military offensive or forced evictions by government. These displacements are the key driver of humanitarian WASH needs in Somalia. IDPs are currently residing in urban and Peri-urban informal crowded settlements, with insufficient access to WASH services that raise protection and health concerns. Therefore, DRC will ensure that, where IDPs settle they get immediate assistance of life-saving interventions. These will include water trucking where there is no safe water source, emergency latrine, sanitation and hygiene kits and rapid hygiene promotion. On the other hand, DRC targets Host Communities - to ensure peaceful coexistence between the local population and target groups and also because many of them are equally vulnerable and in need of humanitarian assistance. Refugee returnees are also targeted with durable solutions in which case DRC will focus on governance and overall management of water and sanitation facilities. In this case, DRC will ensure there is a robust market system in place for continued service provision. For the case of water, DRC will encourage existing water source owners – both private and government, to extend water services to the settlements of DACs. For the case of sanitation, DRC will encourage a market-based approach – looking at creating demand for latrine construction and building capacity of the supply side to ensure enterprise-creation and therefore sustainable services beyond the project period. Hygiene promotion in durable solutions will include messaging and house to house sensitization of safe hygiene practices with emphasis of hand-washing at critical times, safe handling of food, and environmental sanitation. Specific to cash-based interventions (CBIs) and vouchers, DRC proposes to have water vouchers instead of blanket water trucking. DRC has experience in using water vouchers in previous projects. For WASH NFIs (hygiene kits and sanitation kits), DRC will prefer to give cash to households so that they can buy items of their choice. In both voucher and cash, DRC will engage a strict beneficiary selection process based on targeting the most vulnerable households. The beneficiary selection criteria shall be discussed with settlement/camp committees and agreed on. Then vouchers will be designs based on household codes and loaded with cash to collect water for the period. For hygiene kits, each household will receive cash to buy items and this will be followed with a PDM to assess how the cash was used. For sanitation kits, risk analysis will be undertake to determine if WASH committees can buy the items or in-kind distribution is done by DRC.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Improved Protection of  vulnerable girls, women, boys and men affected by conflict and climatic shocks in Somalia
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to strengthen the protection of most vulnerable girls, boys, women and men affected by conflict and climatic shocks by reducing risks and vulnerabilities and increasing community capacities. Key to this action will be a focus on improving capacity for immediate response to violations and remedial action as well as strengthening the protective environment in Somalia.

On immediate response, the action will aim to address acute protection needs of girls, boys women and men, stemming from violence, including GBV, child rights violations, as well as coercion, and abuse. Using a survivor centered multi-sectoral approach DRC, vulnerable women and girls will receive GBV services through Women and girls safe spaces, psychosocial support ( PSS) and case management.

To enable recovery and restore dignity of individual and community victims of violence, neglect, abuse and exploitation and to improve positive coping strategies and prevent further violations, DRC will establish child friendly spaces through which psychosocial support will be provided. In addition, material assistance and livelihood skills training for GBV will also be provided.
On environment building, DRC will reinforce formal and community institutions for better legal and community-based protection of vulnerable groups from violence, coercion and abuse. Key to achieve this objective, activities will include awareness-raising and outreach among communities on protection issues, capacity building and training for duty bearers, service providers and humanitarian workers on GBV, CP and HLP. In addition, DRC will map out civil identification documentation required in Somalia to obtain/access government services such as national identity cards, passports, driver's licenses, title deeds as well as birth and death certificates. The mapping will also establish the cost of obtaining the documents and issuing agencies at Federal and Regional State level. The information will be disseminated to strengthen governance structures and to support service delivery to affected populations. 

On advocacy, DRC will strengthen coordination of protection services and enhance advocacy on protection with relevant stakeholders. Key activities will include strengthening of referral pathways, mapping of service providers and Protection Monitoring of rights violations. DRC will further identify and provide protection-oriented support to people with disabilities in the target locations. 

The proposed action will reach 108,400 persons in Somalia (22,50 girls, 18,250 boys, 39,550 women and 28,350 men).

project_name: Food Assistance for Training
project_objective: With Libya in a state of protracted conflict, WFP’s Interim Country Strategic Plan (ICSP) aims to introduce programmes that would support the resilience of vulnerable communities across the country. The reduction in available migrant labour, both skilled and unskilled, combined with the instability of Government salaries, has left many Libyan families reliant on coping mechanisms in order to meet their basic food needs. In this context, WFP Libya is scaling-up the Food Assistance for Training pilot, which started in 2019, matching people in need with skills trainings that prepares them for available work in the local job markets. Conditional food assistance is provided as long as minimum attendance requirements are met, giving an immediate boost to food security. After the training, if successful, food security levels should be improved, with less reliance on coping strategies. Household resilience to future shocks should also be improved due to an improved asset base through greater skills, tools, and savings.

project_name: Protection and assistance to Nigerian refugees in the Maradi Region
project_objective:
The intervention will focus on protection including level 2 registration of all refugees, advocacy for continued access to territory by refugees, improved reception conditions, protection monitoring, border monitoring and community protection. It will also focus on registration and civil documentation, refugee status determination, psycho-social support, child protection and SGBV response, assistance to persons with specific needs, education and social cohesion.
The intervention is aligned with the Government’s strategy to avoid the creation of camps and host refugees in villages instead. However, most refugees are settled in villages close to the border which are prone to incursions from armed groups and are therefore not safe. Therefore, UNHCR and its partners, in agreement with the Government, started implementing in October a voluntary relocation plan to “opportunity villages” far from the border to ensure refugees’ safety. Key priorities for relocated refugees are food security and nutrition, access to drinking water and latrines, access to healthcare services and shelter. Regarding host populations, partners will work together to support with housing, domestic energy and core relief items. 
As such, UNHCR will facilitate the relocation of refugees within the region and safeguard the protection space. The intervention largely considers the humanitarian-development and peace nexus to ensure the assistance also benefits host communities who need it most. UNHCR will bolster resilience among refugee communities, paying attention to infrastructure development, access to economic opportunities and harnessing of natural resources. Partners will also promote dialogue and positive interactions between the refugees and the host communities.

project_name: Foster access to water for vulnerable communities in Rural Aroma, North Delta, Telkok and Hamashkoraib localities of Kassala state
project_objective: In Kassala State, the recurrent and prolonged periods of drought, accompanied by sporadic torrential rains that cause flooding and destruction of the vegetation cover, increasingly deteriorate the subsoil, reducing its capacity to absorb water. The lack of adequate water structures for the supply of safe water for domestic use constantly exposes the population to various diseases that further worsen the harsh living conditions. Many water stations are unusable and require rehabilitation and training of local management and maintenance personnel to ensure their sustainability. This project aims to facilitate access to water for the most vulnerable populations in the four locations targeted.

project_name: COVID-19 preparedness and response activities
Supporting IDP and host community children's access to quality education in a protective learning environment in the Mopti, Timbuktu and Gao regions
project_objective:
The project aims to “Ensure quality inclusive education in a protective learning environment for X girls and boys in the Mopti, Timbuktu and Gao regions”. 

Output 1.1: Schools’ capacity in host communities has increased enough to absorb displaced girls and boys and students have necessary school materials to adequately attend schools 

The project will respond to the educational needs of all children through equitable access to inclusive quality education. The project will contribute to enhancing the quality of educational supply and expanding existing structures to better address the strong demand in the IDP, refugee and returnee hosting areas in central and northern Mali, considering the specific needs of girls and children with disabilities, the aspects related to protection and the retention of girls.

The protection of IDPs, refugees and returnees especially girls as well as vulnerable children and those with basic needs who do not have or no longer have adequate access to quality education in a secured environment, remains an utmost necessity in the Sahel region. In recent years, UNHCR has dedicated itself and will continue to take appropriate action to address child protection needs through education by facilitating the integration of IDP, refugee and returnee children into the national education system as outlined in the UNHCR Strategy, “Refugee Education 2030: A Strategy for Refugee Inclusion”, which was developed after two years of consultation and collaboration with UNHCR stakeholders, United Nations, NGOs, education networks, multilateral organizations and governments. The aim is to ensure the equitable and sustainable inclusion in national education systems for IDPs, refugees and returnees; that IDP, refugee and returnee, and host community students are equitably prepared for success in national systems, no matter where they live; and that the specific learning needs of displaced and host community students are met by expanding existing programs and partner investments in innovative local solutions.

Further, the UNHCR strategy sets out a vision for the inclusion of displaced children in a fair and quality education system, which contributes to their resilience and prepares them with youth to participate in social cohesion. It further aims at fostering conditions, partnerships, collaboration and approaches bringing IDPs, refugees and returnees in these communities to fairly and equitably have access to an education enabling them to learn, flourish and develop their potential.

Output 1.2: Primary and post – primary school environment is safe for girls and boys

In collaboration with the Mopti, Timbuktu and Gao Education Offices and the Ministry of Education/Teaching Resource Centres (CAPs), teachers and education personnel will receive training on inclusive education, psychosocial support (PSS), special needs education, peace education and Education in Emergencies (EiE), and consequently monitored on their pedagogical practices within classrooms. They will be supported by educational advisers to improve their learning processes. Moreover, efforts will be also focused on awareness raising and community mobilization for the reopening of schools in these zones. 
 
Their capacity to protect themselves and their community from the risk of explosive ordnances and weapons will be also enhanced.

Latrines with water points will be rehabilitated and made accessible. Special attention will be paid to girls in terms of hygiene and sanitation. In a more suitable WASH environment, we observed that pupils remain at school by improving their health condition. Especially girls can attend school even during their menstruation period and children with disabilities can be enrolled as they simply have access to the facilities.

project_name: Emergency shelter and wash response for Returnees from the United Republic of Tanzania
project_objective:
This project aims to address the current gaps on shelter needs identified by UNCHR
Protection Monitoring teams, by: Providing emergency shelter and wash assistance to
returnees from the United Republic of Tanzania through the voluntary repatriation;
Four (4) types of assistance will be provided:
(1) Emergency shelter repair kits (material and tool kits), including Construction and
Rehabilitation of VIP latrines
(2) Grants for rental/host assistance
(3) Hygiene sensitizations
(4) Support refugee returnees to obtain documentation on the land and/or house
property titles
The assistance will be determined by an evaluation of houses by IOM’s shelter team. The
response will be based on the results of the evaluation and prioritize, by vulnerability, the
households that do not have shelter or that are creating a significant burden on host
families.
Targeted areas: The locations of the shelter response for returnees are Rutana, Kirundo,
Cankuzo, Ruyigi, Muyinga, and Makamba.

project_name: Lutte contre la traite au Burundi
project_objective:
Le projet, connu sous le nom de lutte contre la traite des êtres humains au Burundi 2019-2022, renforcera les efforts du gouvernement pour lutter contre la traite des êtres humains et d'autres délits transfrontaliers. Le projet de 3 millions USD, financé par le Royaume des Pays-Bas, s'étalera sur trois ans.
Le Burundi est un pays de depart, de transit et  d'exploitation pour les personnes victimes de la traite, selon le rapport américain sur la traite des personnes. Les adultes et les enfants peuvent être contraints au travail forcé, à la servitude domestique, à la prostitution et à d'autres formes d'exploitation sexuelle dans la région et ailleurs dans le monde.
Ce projet  servira de mécanisme de coordination pour les ministères et les reliera à la police nationale et à la société civile pour mettre en œuvre des mesures de lutte contre la traite. Les activités du nouveau projet comprendront le renforcement du système national de référence pour la protection et la fourniture d'une assistance à la réintégration aux victimes de la traite.
Tout en engageant activement les communautés frontalières, le projet contribuera à renforcer la capacité des differents grades des forces de l'ordre à réduire et à prévenir efficacement la traite des personnes et la criminalité transfrontalière, à sensibiliser aux droits fondamentaux des populations et à créer des procédures opérationnelles standard pour les parties prenantes chargées de l'application des lois sur le traitement des cas de TiP.

project_name: Provision of emergency child protection, child and youth centered resilience building in conflict affected States of Western Bahr El Ghazal and Jonglei
project_objective:
The project will provide support to the most vulnerable, conflict-affected girls, boys, youths, women, and men in South Sudan who are exposed to child protection risks in targeted areas of Raga, Wau, Baggari, Jur River and Pochalla counties of Western Bahr El Ghazal State and Jonglei State respectively.

The project will be provide the following key sub-thematic services to at risk and vulnerable children, youths, and community members in the targeted areas: provision of comprehensive case management (CPMS standards 18, 11, 13); provision of family tracing and reunification for UASC (CPMS standard 13); provision of quality age and gender appropriate psychosocial support (PSS) through community based interventions to extremely vulnerable girls, boys and their caregivers (CPMS standards 10, 15); establishing and supporting of referral mechanisms (CPMS standard 17); capacity building to frontline service providers and volunteers on Child Protection including PSS, case management and general CPiE (CPMS standards 2, 18); strengthening of community structures and mechanisms including community based child protection committees (CBCPC) and child protection desks (CPMS standard 16, 17); conduct child protection awareness-raising & prevention messaging and Peacebuilding and peaceful coexistence activities; conduct child protection assessments and monitoring using the existing and recommended tools (CPMS standard 6).


Hold the Child will use both static and mobile (especially in hard to reach areas) responses to provide the above-outlined services to the targeted populations with support from the cluster and subcluster.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency Mobile Health Services to IDPs, Returnees and vulnerable host populations of Lakes and Central Equatorial State(Yirol West County and Morobo County)
project_objective:
This response plan will be provided through emergency mobile lifesaving health care services that aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic prone diseases, improve access and scale-up response to integrated quality essential health care services to vulnerable populations in hard to reach areas while increasing access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled and mental health disorders by ensuring that its activities are  integrated with WASH, Nutrition, FSL and Protection including MHPSS and provision for the disabled and displaced into essential primary health care services to vulnerable populations of Morobo and Yirol West Counties of CES and Lakes State. Ebola Prevention messaging will also be disseminated across areas of operation owing to their proximity to Ebola hotspot areas and countries (DR Congo).

The response will entirely focus on both IDPs, and host communities owing to the high mortality rate of under 5 children (90.7/1000 - South Mortality statistics - 2016), maternal mortality rate (789/100,000 - South Sudan Mortality Statistics - 2016) people with disabilities and mental disorders will be  included as vulnerable groups owing to their high risk during emergencies coupled with infrastructural impediments.

During this response, an estimate of 6,667 vulnerable individuals (IDPs and Host communities) accounting  for  29% of the total target in the 2 counties (Morobo and Yirol West) are expected to be reached with emergency life saving mobile care services, in line with the health cluster target 2020. Precisely, 5,030 (2,465 men and 2,565 women) of Yirol West while 802 men and 835 women (1,637) of Morobo counties will form the target for this response. The response will attract four hundred thousands United States Dollars (400,000 USD) costed at 59.9 USD per beneficiary to run for the 12 months.

In this response, CIDO will ensure that provision of integrated life saving mobile emergency health care services and quality emergency curative, prevention and referral services through mobile clinical package is enhanced through training of frontline service providers on discharge of emergency mobile package and strengthening of referral system for rape survivors to have access to CMR and psychological first aid. CIDO will also ensure that epidemic-prone disease are detected on time, responded to and reported  immediately.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Nutrition Response to Malnourished Children under 5 years and Pregnant and Lactating Women and Girls in Ezo County
project_objective:
This project will respond to the high nutrition needs of the most vulnerable groups of the population in hard to reach areas of Ezo county especially U5s and PLWs.
CIDO will implement the proposed emergency response for twelve months through complementing the existing nutrition services in the static nutrition facilities by establishing 12 mobile OTP/TSFP outreach sites in hard-to-reach areas of Ezo county while coordinating with existing nutrition partners to improve the nutrition response coverage though rapid response and referral mechanisms. Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) will be engaged to conduct routine active case finding, rapid assessments, and continue with surveillance of the nutrition situation to ensure the targeted population has access to timely, appropriate and treatment care on a needs basis. Supported by CIDO, the CNVs will also conduct massive community mobilization and mass screening, by use of MUAC approach to ensure early detection, identification and referral of Severe Acute malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute malnutrition (MAM) cases among children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs). Under the technical support of CIDO’s Nutrition specialist, 60 Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) will be trained on Community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN), while an orientation training on GBV and child protection for all nutrition staffs will be conducted. CIDO will recruit, train and deploy additional 18 nutrition assistants to ensure timely and appropriate management of acute malnutrition service is provided to all children 6-59 months and PLWs who are acutely malnourished identified at 12 outreach sites while providing s service for five days a week. To improve the quality of services and ensure sustainability of the program, CIDO will provide refresher trainings for 60 CNVs and 24 Nutrition assistants on CMAM and Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN). These will be recruited locally in those Payams where the mobile sites have been established.
This will be in response to low service coverage of nutrition services as a result of inaccessibility for people living in hard to reach areas to enhance focused rapid response mechanism through provision of lifesaving nutritional services in the identified hard to reach areas of Ezo County. Along with the provision of treatment services and care for children 6-59months and PLWs identified with acute malnutrition, CIDO’s mobile teams will provide gender-sensitive MIYCN counselling and support sessions for mothers and fathers, with key focus on breastfeeding; nutritious complementary foods for infants and young children; care and feeding of malnourished children; referral to health services for care and growth monitoring; and information on safe storage and treatment of water, proper hand washing, and sanitation.
CIDO will use the group model approach by forming 30 Mother Support Groups (MSG) for promotion of optimal MIYCN practices. CIDO will focus on dissemination of key nutrition promotion and prevention messages to the targeted community in Ezo County. To ensure that the nutrition services are provided in accordance with national and international standards, the CIDO will print and distribute to all nutrition staffs guidelines, reference tables, and look up tables with relevant key nutrition messages and cut offs, while providing regular supportive supervision to the nutrition staffs. CIDO will rely on UNICEF, WFP and others partners and CHDs to provide nutrition supplies for treatment of SAM and MAM beneficiaries respectively, whilst ensuring timely request, receipt and prepositioning of all nutrition supplies to the nutrition sites.
All children and PLWs identified with Acute malnutrition will be treated in accordance with SS CMAM guideline.

project_name: Emergency WASH support to IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable Host Communities in Yei, Kajo Keji, Morobo, Terekeka, Bor South and Twic East
project_objective:
Food insecurity and malnutrition needs are strongly linked to poor WASH standards especially amongst PLW and Under 5s.  IPC projections for the first quarter of 2020 indicate a decline in food security in the locations targeted, with populations estimated to be in phase 3 and above as follows; Twic East – 70% (81,905), Bor South – 60% (196,549,) Terekeka 45% (110,916) Yei – 20% (54,239), Morobo – 25% (26,026) and Kajo Keji – 20% (44,380).   An increasing number of people face severe food shortages in the locations targeted; The increased number of people facing acute food insecurity (IPC AFI Phase 3 and above) in the projection period are also expected to contribute to increased prevalence of acute malnutrition that require urgent and significant scale-up and intensification of humanitarian services.
Access to safe water in the locations is less than 30%, with less than 20% of the populations practicing safe excreta disposal.   Provision of WASH services will reduce occurrences of malnutrition amongst U5s and PLW as well as reduction of gender based violence in the quest for water. 
CIDO targets 20,000 persons with much needed WASH services inline with the cluster strategy of Integrating WASH in nutrition response through famine prevention minimum package; 
Integrating WASH in health response to control outbreaks at wider community level; 
Provision of timely/sustainable, equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs, host communities and returnees and mitigate WASH-related gender-based violence . 
The latest economic update indicates a significant decrease in the number of households that receive income from casual (skilled and unskilled) labor thereby unable to purchase essential WASH NFIs such as soap. 
Protection issues related to access to WASH further hinder access to WASH services with the project targeting mainly women and the elderly. 
Community Initiative for Development Organization (CIDO) is a national NGO with adequate footprint in the counties of Yei, Morobo, Kajo Keji, Terekeka, Bor South and Twic East and is currently implementing interventions in the thematic areas of Nutrition, Health, NFIs, WASH, Protection and livelihoods. We work with mainly the most vulnerable targeting mostly female-headed HHs and have reached over 20,000 people with Equatoria and Jonglei with humanitarian support. 
CIDO believes an integrated response will ensure visible gains in the areas targeted and will work with cluster leads UNICEF and NRC to ensure adherence to strategy, standards and practices. 
The project targets 20,000 people (65% female) as follows: Yei – 5,000; Morobo – 3,000; Kajo Keji – 2,000; Terekeka – 2,000; Bor South – 4,000; Twic East – 4,000. 58% of these are IDPs, 5% PWDs.

project_name: Provision of GBV Services in Central Equatoria , Lakes and Jonglei States ( Yei, Yirol East, Yirol West and Duk counties)
project_objective: This project is targeting  Returnees ,conflict affected host community and IDPS living in Yei county in Central Equitoria , Yirol East and Yirol West of Lakes State and Duk county of Jonglei State who are at high risk of gender based violence, death, injury and life threatening diseases like HIV/AIDS, STIs and reproductive health related illnesses aggravated due to violence. The primary purpose of the project is to address compounding effects of converging factors i.e severe food insecurity /loss of livelihoods, economic decline, protection threats and lack of services which contributes and aggravates the prevalence of GBV . CIDO will adopt an integrated approach and coordinate with WASH, Health, MHPSS, FSL, Education and Nutrition partners to prevent protection risks and to provide timely GBV response services to men, women, boys and girls affected by conflict. As such CIDO will use its leadership role to prioritize joint safety audits, capacity building sessions and GBV mainstreaming activities with multi sector partners CIDO will also ensure that the project staff adhere to the AAP principles as well as PSEA principles while delivering the activities at the project sites. The target population is 12000 individuals broken down as 500 boys and 3000 girls, 8000 women 500 men. The project has a special focus on adolescent girls and boys, female headed households and people living with disability The project will be implemented for a period of 12 months with an estimated budget of USD 360,000. CIDO will implement this project directly in the proposed locations in collaboration with the target population, the administration in counties and partners on ground to promote durable solutions, sustainability and achieve maximum project results. The project activities are designed in line with the four GBV Sub cluster HRP 2020 cluster objectives and the activities focus on mitigating GBV risks, preventing and responding to GBV cases through; WGFS programming, Case management / Individual PSS, community Outreach and dialogues, EMAP and safe referrals. It is expected that by the end of the project period, lives of vulnerable women and girls will be saved, they will have increased access to  multi sector services , life skills and positive coping mechanisms entrenched in them. It is anticipated that through EMAP boys and men will be better informed on GBV prevention mechanisms in emergencies and will make meaningful sustainable contribution to the prevention of GBV and overall population needs of safer dignified lives.

project_name: Provide timely access, availability and utilization of multi-sectoral services to vulnerable and conflict affected women, girls, men and boys to strengthen coping mechanisms and live a dignified life in Leer, Nasir , Akobo, Fangak, Maiwut and Nyirol Counties of Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei states.
project_objective: Given the ongoing protection crisis in South Sudan, Nile Hope will continue to work with populations affected by conflict and displacement and provide timely access, availability and utilization of multi-sectoral services to vulnerable and conflict affected population in Nasir, Leer, Akobo, Fangak, Maiwut and Nyirol Counties of Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei States, and other stakeholders to enhance the protective environment of individuals and communities especially women and girls, and identify, prevent and address protection risks. The project objective is aligned with the Protection Cluster and Humanitarian Response Plan objective by providing immediate lifesaving assistance to address priority GBV needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach areas. The project will target a total of 23214(Men 5538, Women 8177, Boys 3562 and Girls 5937) IDPs, host communities, and returnees. This project  is designed to improve responses to cases of GBV, enhance the ability of survivors to recover  from GBV, and make progress towards changing the social norms that perpetuate GBV, with the intent of fully mitigating the effects of GBV and preventing future cases. It will provide GBV response services and address critical gaps in information and knowledge among women and girls on GBV response, which limit access to services and heighten GBV risk. Nile Hope will encourage health-seeking behaviors among GBV survivors, facilitating referrals, and creating supportive structures to prevent GBV. Nile Hope will work in collaboration with local partners and will establish and operationalize women and girls’ friendly spaces and provide periodic individual and group psycho social support for women and girls. This will include dialogue sessions, psychosocial support through group counseling sessions, skills building, production of reusable sanitary pads using locally available materials, information sessions on pertinent issues to women and girls on access to available services, sexual and reproductive Health issues on safe deliveries, family planning and post abortion care, personal hygiene, menstrual hygiene management, decision making and peer to peer support. This project will support the healing process of GBV survivors by providing community based case management and psychosocial support services and engage men and boys in community dialogues and awareness raising sessions on GBV, its effect and consequences and their roles in prevention. Protection interventions will be integrated within Nile Hope’s Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, Peace building and FSL programmes to compliment holistic assistance to communities through static and mobile services. Nile Hope will ensure commitment to diversity and gender equity as Nile Hope’s Protection sector’s core business is premised on women and girls’ empowerment and therefore will strive to periodically carry out gender and protection analysis including assessments of vulnerabilities related to age, sex and diversity, and will give priority to vulnerable population. Nile Hope will ensure protection from sexual exploitation and abuse for beneficiaries through awareness and training to Nile Hope’s staff, partners, volunteers, vendors, contractors and awareness to ensure beneficiaries are aware of PSEA and reporting mechanisms. The project will ensure that women are engaged and supported to become first responders within their communities. Nile Hope will work to advance women’s rights, voices and leadership through increasing their knowledge and their participation in humanitarian coordination. This will contribute to women’s protection and empowerment and will transform women’s position in emergency response and resilience, while helping to address the core issues that affect communities in emergencies.

project_name: Provision of Synergized and Integrated multi-sectoral quality and protective Education to Children and Youths (age 3-18) in South Sudan.
project_objective: The increased access to basic quality education with Integrated and synergized quality Education response programme with focus to Uror, Nyirol, Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor and Twic Counties, South Sudan. The programme will seek to improve the access to quality education amongst the crisis affected children and youths as an effort to promote sustainable quality education with incentivised enrolment and attendance to learning, reduce risks of cognitive underdevelopment and malnutrition, and provide access to safe and protective learning environments. The project will target a total of 45 schools with 15,661 total beneficiaries desegregated into 14,761 children and youths (8,119 B & 6,642 G), 450 teachers (250 M, & 200 W), 450 PTAs/SMCs (250 M, & 200 W); the response aims at provision of scholastic materials, establishment and renovation of TLSs, capacity building of teachers & PTAs/SMCs, providing school feeding, restoring and providing safe and protective education among boys and girls while integrating with already existing projects in intra-sectors (especially Health, Nutrition, FSL, WASH, and Protection). The project equally hopes to enhance psychosocial development of learners besides improving hygiene and sanitation. The project will use its existing M&E system to monitor report, feedback, document, and share evident lessons. The project is also designed to ensure maximum impact is achieved through the proposed interventions besides ensuring accountability to the affected population. The project will also sort to address the protection and SGBV challenges in schools besides incorporating comprehensive sexuality education into the integrated programme while linking and strengthening into the existing community based referral pathways.

project_name: Stabilizing the livelihoods of conflict affected returnees, internally displaced persons and the host communities in the Equatorias, Lakes, Jonglei, Unity, Greater Bahr el Ghazal and Greater Upper Nile through integrated emergency and static Food Security and Livelihood response.
project_objective:
This project aims to meet the  immediate, medium and long-term food security needs of the target communities in Eastern Equatoria, Lakes, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Jonglei and
  Central Equatoria states that were affected by armed conflict, insecurities,
  climate change and displacement. This will be achieved by: 
a) Access to cereal seeds’ kits: to ensure the target communities recover from hunger, the distribution of cereal seeds’ kits and tools will be conducted. Accompanied by agricultural extension activities, focusing on good agronomic practices (such as season of planting, seedbed preparation, planting and spacing, weed management, irrigation, integrated pest and production management, harvesting and post-harvest management). This intervention will be delivered using lead farmers and farmer field school approaches with demonstration plots. 
b) Access to vegetables’ kits: in areas with access to suﬃcient water for vegetable growing, beneficiaries will be provided with vegetables’ seeds’ kits containing a variety of species. The distribution will be conducted with extension training on good agronomic practices including seed and nursery bed preparation, seed planting and spacing, irrigation, integrated pest and production management, harvesting and post-harvesting management. 
c) Access to fishing kits: in areas with access to swamps, rivers or lakes, non-food kits with tools for fishery will be provided. Fishing has the potential to immediately address food security needs. It enables people to immediately harvest fish from the rivers and swamps in the areas. 
d) Improving the capacity of farmer field schools: lead farmers and extension workers will be trained as trainers for community farmers. The lead farmers and extension workers will then facilitate discussions and demonstration on good agronomic practices for the vegetable and cereal crops producer groups. 
e) Setting up irrigation systems: Farmers who grow vegetables will be provided with treadle pumps, watering cans at household levels. Drip irrigation systems will be established at farmer field school gardens or demonstration plots. Drip irrigation systems together with community training on their adequate and sustainable use will enhance the copying mechanism during the dry season. 
f) School feeding program: Food for education and school feeding programme will be considered in the project areas where PAH carries food security and livelihood activities with seeds distribution and vegetable and cereal crops production. 
g) Conditional General food distribution: as a modality is already being developed and submitted awaiting approval. This will target the most vulnerable food insecure population with limited access to markets and having a poor road network. h) Cash Programming: will be based on initial market and community assessments, considering cash vouchers or cash for work. Food for asset/cash will be conducted in the areas where there are the need and local markets can support the project targeting the establishment of community structures and facilities like schools and infrastructures like community road projects and communal farms establishment. 
i) Integration: For more a holistic approach, PAH will integrate interventions with sectors of WASH,
  nutrition, education, protection and S/NFI through combined hygiene and nutrition promotion in addition to screening and referral to nutrition partners. Education and health will be integrated through training of school hygiene clubs and school gardening and awareness at the schools, nutrition and health centres. PAH will work with nutrition and health partners like Johanniter in Wau, RMF in Boma while the PAH ERT will integrate the WASH, S/NFI and FSL as in the projects in Magwi, Boma, Koch and Jur River counties since 2017. Protection will be mainstreamed across all sectors and additional protection team will be supporting the community where PAH implements FSL and others

project_name: Support immediate lifesaving assistance by addressing key general protection, GBV and child protection needs of the most vulnerable populations in hard to reach areas through mobile and static responses across South Sudan
project_objective: Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) project aims to provide timely and appropriate integrated responses in the field of general protection, child protection and GBV through responses in areas of needs for IDPs, returnees and host communities to increase resilience and coping mechanisms including risk reduction. PAH will focus to support GBV survivors through the provision of transport services to access health and psycho-social services as well as provision of dignity kits. Child protection will be integrated mainly with Education projects with key focus on psycho-social support. PAH will ensure mainstreaming protection across sectors of WASH, S/NFI, FSL, Education and Nutrition. Mainstreaming activities will be implemented at all stages of the project by conducting protection assessments to inform the intervention modalities and context dynamics. The project will be implemented in conflict affected areas such as Jonglei State, Central Equatoria State, Eastern Equatoria State, Western Equatoria State, Unity State, Northern and Western Bahr-El-Gazal States, Lakes State and Upper Nile State. These areas are where PAH mobile and static teams have been working since 2006. Depending on local dynamics and accessibility of locations, the mobile response teams shall deploy across South Sudan. Hence, the above locations are areas where PAH has experience with multisector interventions but other locations may be flagged for responses during 2020. Support to GBV survivors is planned in areas of static presence, particularly in Jonglei and other areas or PAH's experience. The project will mainly target communities with poor access to safe water supply, communities with poor hygiene and sanitation practices, nutrition centres, schools, health units, and other locations targeted with FSL, S/NFI and Education activities, to ensure more holistic approach. As part of GBV response, women friendly spaces will be established with skills training provided, ex. fuel energy stoves making, mat waving, etc. (integrated with FSL, SNFI, WASH sectors). The project will promote inclusion of women, people with disabilities and girls through distribution of WASH-NFIs, Shelter NFIs with specific package that address issues of dignity for women and girls. This project will closely address the protracted inclusion and support of displaced people and returnees mainly women, girls, children, elderly and people with disabilities to participate freely in appropriate sectoral activities through participatory needs assessments, awareness creation on hygiene and sanitation including GBV, nutrition, child protection, child’s rights, peaceful coexistence. As part of child protection, PAH team will support family reunification in both static and mobile responses. In static locations, child friendly spaces will be established within the schools with key activities, including sport events and crafts. Psycho-social support training will be provided to the teachers, PTAs, and key community members. Project will be implemented through static presence and mobile teams based in Juba that will be deployed to field location where recommended responses for protection and other sectors of PAH’s activities (S/NFI, FSL, WASH, Education) will be flagged. To ensure continuity and improve the quality of protection services, PAH will continue to work with existing protection structures and volunteers, building their capacities through training and coaching to equip them with the relevant skills to continue addressing protection issues. PAH will conduct service providers and stake holders’ mapping to draw a clear referral pathway including coordinated response in all the project communities. PAH will promote peaceful co-existence between IDPs, returnees and the host communities under the do no harm principle, this will be achieved through working closely with key leadership at every stage of the response.

project_name: SAVING AND PROTECTING WOMEN AND GIRLS’ LIVES IN CONFLICT AFFECTED AREAS OF SOUTH SUDAN
project_objective:
Gender-based violence (GBV) is alarmingly present in all corners of South Sudan. GBV – including rape, sexual assault, domestic violence, forced and early marriage, sexual exploitation and abuse, abduction and other harmful practices – is a widespread, chronic and persistent violation of the basic human rights of girls and women. GBV is both a human rights and public health issue. GBV prevention and response is a precondition for equitable and inclusive recovery, sustainable development and human rights, as well as an important development objective.
Hence, CARE seeks to implement GBV prevention, response and risk mitigation activities by providing quality and timely age appropriate case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors in Yambio, Upper Nile, Unity (Koch, Rubkona, Leer, Mayom, Abiemnom) Jongolei (Twic East, Panyagor, Uror, Duk, pachola, Pibor) Eastern Equatoria (Lafon, Ikwotoes, Magwi, Nimule,Torit and Lopa). As conflict in South Sudan enters its seventh year in 2020, ongoing fighting and surges of violence in some parts of the country have led to widespread human rights violations, forcing people to flee their homes (many multiple times). The compounding effects of widespread violence, recurring famine and sustained economic decline have further diminished the capacity of people to face threats to their health, safety and livelihoods and exacerbated gender based violence. In the recent What Works report up to 65% women experience physical and sexual violence in their life time in areas of conflict and 33% of women in the POC's experience sexual violence from non-partner and many of the incidents are associated to raids, displacement or abduction. Across the country there is increasingly desperate situation for women and girls, with an increased presence of soldiers and numerous checkpoints leaving women and girls fearful and at risk of GBV. Safety audit reports show that women and girls are beaten, raped, abducted, tortured and looted when collecting firewood and when accessing markets for basic needs. The proposed project contributes to the CARE 2020 and the Strategic Action Plan (SAP) for South Sudan strategy outcome, “strengthening individual voices” by supporting people of all genders and ages to make choices assert their voices and realize a life free of gender based violence. CARE will encourage health seeking behaviours among GBV survivors facilitating referrals, and creating supportive structures to prevent GBV. CARE will work in collaboration with local partners and will establish and operationalize women and girls’ safe spaces and provide periodic individual and group psycho social support for women and girls. This project will support the healing process of GBV survivors by providing community based case management and psychosocial support services and engage men and boys in community dialogues and awareness raising sessions on GBV, its effect and consequences and their roles in prevention. Protection interventions will be integrated within CARE’s health, nutrition and FSL programmes to complement holistic assistance to communities through static and mobile.

project_name: Monitoring de protection dans les régions du nord et du centre
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire dans le nord et le centre du Mali, principalement touchée par les conflits intercommunautaires, la criminalité et l’extrémisme violent, est de plus en plus critique et crée un environnement difficile et précaire pour les populations. Le deuxième trimestre de 2019, qui a enregistré un nombre d’incident encore jamais atteint au Mali, démontre cette dégradation de la situation : en comparaison avec une moyenne trimestrielle de 250 incidents documentés par le monitoring en 2017 et 2018, le deuxième trimestre de 2019 en dénote 606. Ces incidents sont à l’origine de mouvements de populations civiles dans certaines localités de ces régions du nord et du centre. Des évaluations des besoins des populations civiles et de l'analyse de la situation de protection conduites par les acteurs humanitaires au Mali en 2019, on estime à 2 802 423 le nombre de personnes dans le besoin de protection (HNO2019).
L'absence ou le retrait des institutions judiciaires et des forces de sécurité maliennes est l’un des facteurs majeurs de l’insécurité croissante. Il laisse un espace libre aux groupes armés criminels et extrémistes se disputant le contrôle du territoire et le trafic illicite. Ces groupes armés profitent de la situation pour accroître le recrutement et leur légitimité auprès de la population en quête de sécurité.
A la date du 30 septembre 2019, les partenaires de la Commission Mouvement Population (CMP) ont comptabilisé 74 205 rapatriés, ce qui correspond à une augmentation de 5 227 personnes par rapport aux données de septembre 2018. En parallèle, 187139 personnes déplacées internes, soit une augmentation de 110 093 personnes, par rapport aux données de septembre 2018. 561 606 personnes retournées ont été enregistrés, soit une augmentation de 35 101 par rapport aux données de la même période de 2018 et 138 402 réfugiés maliens dans les pays limitrophes, soit une diminution de 1 874 par rapport aux données de septembre 2018.
L’environnement de protection des populations civiles dans ces régions demeure toujours précaire et marqué par la présence des criminels armés et des organisations radicales, la circulation des armes légères et de guerre, les confits inter et intracommunautaires et les violations des droits humains (extorsion, vol, coups et blessures, assassinat, enlèvement de personnes, etc.). Dans de nombreuses zones, l'assistance aux communautés affectées par le conflit repose toujours entièrement sur l'aide humanitaire internationale.  
L'impunité renforce les violations de droits humains. Des cas d’atteintes au droit des enfants sont signalés, ainsi que les violences basées sur le genre. Au cours du premier semestre 2019, le monitoring de protection a collecté 1065 incidents de protection (contre 600 à la même période en 2018) affectant les civils. La présence des mines, des Restes Explosifs de Guerre (REG) et d‘Engins Explosifs Improvisés (EEI) a été notée affectant les forces armées nationales et internationales, aussi bien que les populations civiles parmi lesquelles des enfants. 
En 2016, 2017, 2018 et 2019, le projet de monitoring a fortement contribué à l’analyse constante de l’environnement de protection dans les régions du nord et du centre.
