Pour l’année 2020, le projet compte toujours évaluer, analyser et partager les données sur les incidents qui affecteront environ 2880 personnes parmi les 1 428 661 de personnes cibles identifiées.

project_name: Improved access to quality and protective learning environment for Returnees, IDP and Host Community children in Unity State (Panyijar and Rubkona counties) and Western Equatoria State (Mundri West and Mundri East counties)
project_objective:
The proposed emergency response project seeks to promote school enrollment, increase attendance and retention through providing emergency school feeding, preventing and reducing disease outbreaks in Unity State, Panyijiar and Rubkona counties as well as in Western Equatoria State Mundri West and East Counties. Project participants will be constituted of Returnees, IDP and host communities.  Mercy Corps has on-going integrated emergency response programs in four sectors of education, WASH, FSL and Child Protection in the proposed counties. The proposed project will implement the following
A: Construction and Repair of classrooms: The project will construct 10 new TLS and repair 15 blocks of existing damaged classrooms to improve the learning environment for 10,500 (5,500 girls and 5,000 boys) children in the selected counties.
B: Emergency School feeding to reduce malnutrition and promote school enrollment, attendance and retention of conflict affected boys and girls in Panyijiar. Under this intervention, Mercy Corps will engage local community stakeholders, PTAs, local leadership, youth to jointly identify 10 schools and/or learning spaces to participate in emergency school feeding. Other activities that will be conducted during the inception phase (month 1) of this project include minor repairs of school kitchens and warehouses, mobilization for coordinating provision of community contributions such as labor, firewood and additional cooking utensils; training community members on nutrition, health and food handling. From month two going forward, the project will distribute hot cooked meals based on the WFP food basket to boys and girls in 10 primary schools for 5 days a week. To mitigate the risk of school drop out for girls in upper primary classes, the project will distribute take- home rations senior girls in the 10 schools. 
C: The WASH in schools interventions will focus on preventing and reducing the outbreak of cholera and other water borne diseases. The project will repair school latrines and install hand washing facilities in 25 schools Unity and WES. Moreover, the project will conduct hygiene promotion session messaging on cholera symptoms, modes of transmission, prevention and referral pathways to health care centers for cholera treatment. Additionally, the project will request dignity kits for school girls and soap for handwashing from the WASH Cluster core pipeline for distribution. 
D: Capacity strengthening is a cross-cutting aspect in this emergency response project. The project will mobilize and train of 325 community members (200 women; 125 men) PTAs, youth and local administration on psycho-social support, WASH, nutrition, disease prevention and life-skills. Mercy Corps will also train 200 teachers (80 F and 120 M) and 325 PTA on school management, record keeping and PSS.  In addition to this training, the teachers will also be train in EiE methodologies, pedagogy and learner centered approaches. 60 % of the project will be implemented in Unity while the remaining 40% will be in WES.

project_name: Empowering and strengthening the resilience of children and adolescents in Rubkona County, Unity State
project_objective:
After 5 years of civil war in South Sudan, the 2018-signed peace agreement provides hope. Yet, the country’s humanitarian crisis goes on: 3.71 million people are displaced, including 1.47 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). Among this population, 61% are children. Children and adolescents (particularly those between 10–19 years) are especially vulnerable to the violent crisis in Unity State, specifically in Rubkona County, due to the lack of protective structures and systems, psychosocial distress, being associated with armed forces or groups, as well as Gender-Based-Violence (GBV) and gender inequalities that have increased with the prolonged violent conflict. 

Within this context, Mercy Corps (MC) proposes a project that contributes to achieving South Sudan’s HRP objectives and the objectives outlined by the Protection Cluster and Child Protection Sub-Cluster (CPSC) for South Sudan for 2020 by providing critical protection-related assistance and specialized services to the most vulnerable; preventing and mitigating protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience; and enabling durable and sustainable solutions. 

More specifically, MC proposes a 10-months project with the objective to provide critical Child Protection (CP) services to empower and strengthen the resilience of children and adolescents affected by the crisis. This will include the provision of socio-economic reintegration support to children associated with armed forces and groups (CAAFAG) and other children and adolescents in need in key hot spot areas in Rubkona County. 

In particular, the intervention will address factors associated with voluntary and forced participation of children and adolescents in armed forces and armed groups, especially the social alienation of this age group, and the lack of livelihood and educational opportunities. The ultimate aim is that children and adolescents will safely transition to adulthood, become a full member of the society and have lasting positive multiplier effects on their families, communities, and social and economic structures.

The project activities will be based on four components specifically aiming to:
1. Provide quality age and gender-appropriate focused and non-focused psychosocial support (PSS), as well as comprehensive case management services to children and adolescents in need in safe spaces;
2. Strengthen the skills of adolescents to be able to seek healthy livelihoods and income-generating opportunities;
3. Strengthen community-based mechanisms to prevent and respond to violence against children and adolescents and help build a protective, enabling, integrating and peaceful environment for them;
4. Empower and enhance the safety and well-being of specifically vulnerable girls through GBV risk mitigation and prevention activities

Through these activities, the project aims to target a total of 22,619 people (6,440 boys, 5,690 girls, 5,484 men, 5,005 women,) who will benefit from different types of activities.

By focusing on the most vulnerable and at-risk children and adolescents in key hot spots in Rubkona County, the proposed project will fill an important gap in providing critical child protection services to the most vulnerable and affected children and adolescents in need of protection assistance.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Integrated Healthcare Services to IDPs, Returnees and Host communities Affected by Humanitarian Crisis in Morobo & Uror Counties
project_objective:
Lack of national health sector blueprint based on the 6 WHO building blocks of Health system and limited government contribution to national health budget of 1.8% as given rise to a huge burden of epidemic prone diseases such as Malaria, Cholera, Meningitis, Anthrax and vaccines preventable diseases such as Measles, Yellow Fever, Whooping Cough, Rubella [Health Cluster] despite fatigued donor contributions of 10% for meeting health needs in South Sudan. Implementation of the R-ARCISS by warrying parties is giving humanitarian actors and the citizen mixed scenarios due to delays in implementation of major milestones as the date of formation of government of national unity on November 12th 2019 is approaching. The ongoing returns of IDPs and refugees to their homeplaces from within and neighbouring countries is increasing the risk of outbreaks and is worsening the already overstressed broken health system with lack of access to basic services such as healthcare, water, education, food etc. from high risks countries [IOM DTM September 2019]. In the past week, from 14 to 20 October, 21 new confirmed Ebola virus disease (EVD) cases were reported from five health zones in two affected provinces of North Kivu and Ituri in the Democratic Republic of the Congo [WHO 22nd October 2019].  With the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Eastern Dr Congo, THESO will continue working with partners in Ebola response preparedness, prevention and control interventions in high risks location of Morobo County which is the nearest border area with closer proximity to locations such as Ariwara approximately 40 miles away with confirmed case on June 30 2019 [USAID 18 July 2019]. Currently, flooding which started in mid-June 2019 continue to cause fatalities, destruction of homes, infrastructure, water sources and crop fields in Uror County. As of October, an estimated 25,000 people have been displaced and severely affected by the floods across the county of Uror [ACAPS October 2019]. The flooding is putting at risks lives of returnees and host communities to waterborne and water related diseases that can leads to outbreaks such as Malaria and Cholera, etc. [ACAPS 20 October 2019]. With the national high mortality rate of under 5 children (90.7/1000) and maternal mortality rate ((789/100,000), vulnerable groups such as children under-fives, women of reproductive age, people with disabilities and mental disorders are being prioritised as high-risk group in this project to be supported during implementation. 
In 2019 THESO has been responding to the emergency health needs of 0ver 50,000 direct beneficiaries in Paluony Boma of Yuai Payam – Uror County from March 2019 and in Morobo county from September 2019 with funding from SSHF SA1 and SA2 allocations respectively. In 2020, THESO intend to strengthened the current emergency healthcare deliveries in the counties of Morobo and Uror where it is currently providing lifesaving emergency healthcare services with funding from South Sudan Humanitarian Fund and support from Medair. This 2020 HRP will strengthen emergency healthcare services deliveries and conduct active disease surveillance and response in case of any disease outbreak in Morobo and Uror counties while complimenting and strengthening current services deliveries at fixed facilities & mobile clinics reaching the last miles populations. This 2020 plan aim at contributing to the three cluster objectives addressing the major causes of morbidity and mortality, Capacity building, diseases prevention & control as well as outbreaks response ensuring lifesaving emergency healthcare meeting 2020 HRP.  THESO in collaboration with government structures at State and County level, will use health cluster strategic approach of PHCC, PHCU & Mobile Clinics to provide lifesaving emergency healthcare services to the IDPs, returnees and host communities in 2020.

project_name: Appui égalitaire à la réintégration par l'assistance Multisectorielle en Biens Non Alimentaires, Abris, Wash et la Riposte au COVID-19
project_objective:
La crise prolongée du Mali depuis 2012 implique une dégradation continue de l’environnement de protection en dépit des efforts entrepris pour limiter les troubles et les violences généralisées. Il est confronté au phénomène des mouvements mixtes et déplacements spontanés et reste toutefois à être un lieu d'accueil et de retour avec un faible accès aux services de base, à la justice et à la sécurité pour tous. La crise sanitaire mondiale du COVID-19, vient s’ajouter au contexte sécuritaire, avec une évolution progressive cumulée à 1978 cas confirmés depuis son apparition (source SitRep#90 de l’INSP/OMS). Le taux de létalité est de 5,6% avec 111 décès. Cette pathologie est susceptible dans un milieu où le cadre de vie est précaire avec une promiscuité élevée dans l’habitat, les attroupements sur les sites informels et formels, l’accès limité à l’eau potable, les conditions sanitaires déplorables et la méconnaissance de normes barrières.
La tendance démographique a évolué à 565,905 Personnes Déplacées Internes selon rapport de la CMP du mois de Mai 2020.
L’objectif principal de ce projet consiste à Protéger et Renforcer l’accès à l’habitat, à l’eau potable, à l’hygiène et à la prévention du COVID-19 par la riposte en situation d’urgence et relèvement aux groupes de familles vulnérables.
Le projet apportera une assistance égalitaire, juste et inclusive en Biens Non Alimentaires, Abris d’urgence, transitionnels, la réalisation, réhabilitation et implantation des points d’eaux par la coordination. Puis les campagnes de mobilisation sociale pour la sensibilisation dans la riposte au COVID-19, la réduction de la densité humaine, le désengorgement des sites et l’appui aux structures sanitaires régionales dans l’identification des espaces d’isolation et structures d’accueil et de traitement.
L’action passe par la synergie avec les acteurs des clusters et services techniques de l’Etat et appui technique aux acteurs étatiques dans les structures des clusters. Enfin, les priorités porteront sur la promotion du genre, la diversité et le handicap sur tout le processus de l’action humanitaire qui vise la centralité de la protection et le respect de l’éthique pour que l’action ne nuise pas à la dignité et à la vie des personnes affectées.
Les personnes à besoins spécifiques, en particulier les filles, les garçons, les femmes et les hommes de toutes les catégories sans distinction de leur croyance, religion ou de leur minorité auront accès aux services sociaux de base en articles non alimentaires, abris, les installations Wash et Kits de prévention conformes à leurs attentes. Le rôle des femmes pour avoir une place dans la famille et un pouvoir de prise de décision avec l’implication dans le processus de sélection, d’évaluation et orientations basées sur leurs problèmes fondamentaux et plaintes dans la planification et la mise en œuvre qui s’alignent sur au cadre de redevabilité.
Les personnes affectées seront évaluées sur la base de sévérité regroupant les PDIs, Retournés, Rapatriés et une tranche de communautés hôtes impactées par la crise dans les cercles prioritaires.
L'implication effective des acteurs étatiques, des partenaires locaux et des partenaires de développement dans les abris / NFI, Wash, les activités de protection et d'assistance, ainsi que dans les structures (pôle Protection, pôle Logement) qui seront renforcées. L'intégration effective de la protection des projets humanitaires reste également un aspect important à renforcer en analyse genre.
Les composantes du projet passent par une forte concentration sur les modalités mixtes de réponse pour impacter positivement la vie des familles vulnérables à envoyer leurs progénitures à l’école, l’accès à la santé et la dignité des enfants abandonnés et les victimes de VBG à travers les transferts des actifs en espèces qui visent à inciter l’intégration socioéconomique et le relèvement qui cadrent aussi avec l’approche du Nexus.

project_name: Eﬃcient provision of life-saving non-food items and safe, appropriate emergency shelter to returnees, IDPs and most vulnerable host communities through integrated, resilience building response in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) will provide emergency shelter and life-saving non-food items to newly displaced groups or populations with new vulnerabilities. Key focus will be put on  increased number of returnees, internally displaced persons and most vulnerable host communities through coordinated and timely joint responses in Central Equatoria State, Jonglei State, former Unity State, Upper Nile State, in Western Equatoria State and in Lakes State. PAH will use both in-kind (26,000 Ind ) response modality and CBI modality (14,000) in the areas of returns with functional markets. PAH will construct 200 transitional shelter to reduce protection risks and exposure to diseases attributed with poor shelter conditions and lack of household non-food items. The project will support the sustainable existing coping mechanisms and community initiatives for local resource mobilization through a component of multi-purpose cash-based interventions in locations where PAH currently implements FSL, Education and WASH projects. Training in leadership, HLP concepts combined with specific skills training with community leaders and beneficiaries will be conducted in order to build resilience. PAH will also build the capacity of the new cluster partners on response methodology and CBI modality in order to ensure high quality and coordinated response. Mobile data collection tools and bio-metric system will be used throughout the project cycle.

PAH will provide equitable and dignified access to multi-sectorial basic needs through integrated, multi-sectorial approach and these include; emergency shelter/ non-food items, WASH NFIs, Health, nutritional items and multi-purpose cash assistance to the most affected populations with new vulnerabilities in order to meet household basic needs and alleviate human suffering in a safe and dignified manner. 
PAH will focus on timely, joint and coordinated missions within the humanitarian hubs, with logistic cluster and  CCCM cluster in targeting female headed households, unaccompanied elderly, people with no links to the community, separated children, women at risk (pregnant and lactating mothers), child-headed households, people living with disability and returnees whose properties were damaged and looted during the conflict. The mobile response teams will comprise of experienced ES/NFI oﬃcers (50 percent women and 50 percent men). The protection team will participate in 80 percent of interventions with close coordination with the protection Cluster and static partners. The team will integrate the interventions jointly with partners, more specifically nutrition, WASH, FSL and Protection actors and in close coordination with the respective clusters through SFP. 
PAH will conduct timely, joint and coordinated in-depth multi-sectorial needs analysis, rapid market assessment with focus on protection risk analysis with participation of the community-led committees. The needs analysis teams will conduct interviews at household level with consultative community meetings, key informant interviews, observations, focus group discussions with men, women, boys and girls . 
Peer Post-distribution monitoring will be conducted 1 month after the intervention in the mobile response and in CBI modality by M&E team. This will measure the quality of the response, impact of the project, HLP, conflict sensitive issues and will determine if the assistance reached the most vulnerable groups. Complaint/feedback mechanism will be in place throughout the project cycle. PAH will use the PDM report for better programming since we will take into account the lessons learnt, complaints raised and recommendations raised by the beneficiaries. Security and logistical constraints have made it diﬃcult in the recent past to conduct PDMs therefore close coordination with clusters partners and joint planning will be emphasized.

project_name: Provision of Integrated lifesaving nutrition assistance to conflict affected and vulnerable populations in IDPs and Host Communities in Malakal PoC, Malakal town, Aburoch, Juba PoC, Juba AL Sabah hospital and Nyal Panyijar County in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Through the proposed responses, International Medical Corps will continue providing integrated lifesaving nutrition responses to conflict affected resident and displaced populations in six locations: Juba PoC, AL Sabah hospital, Malakal town, Malakal PoC, Aburoch and Nyal Panyijar County. The proposed response will focus on life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years of age, PLW, and chronically ill persons as the most vulnerable groups to acute malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs through management of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), at OTP/TSFP nutrition facilities. Prevention activities that address the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition will be enhanced particularly Mother support groups and community nutrition volunteers will be supported and used as entry point to reach caregivers/mothers. International Medical Corps will continue capacity building of the nutrition team, MoH staff, to equip and respond to nutrition emergency on timely management of SAM and MAM cases. IMC emergency nutrition response will expand on nutrition specific interventions, as well as reinforce integration and linkages with other clusters to address the key drivers of malnutrition: food insecurity, sub-optional child care and feeding practices, morbidity, and lack of safe water and sanitation. The response attentions on areas where high prevalence of acute malnutrition, conflict and internal displacement coexist. 
Through the proposed humanitarian response plan projects, International Medical Corps will reach 22,994 children under five and 10,188 PLW beneficiaries with acute malnutrition in Juba PoC, AL Sabah hospital SC, Malakal town, Malakal PoC, Aburoch and Nyal Panyijar County. The project will provide lifesaving nutrition services focusing on the most vulnerable, especially PLW and children under five. IMC will reinforce and promote access to integrated nutrition, health and WASH, FSL responses and will will ensure that most of the nutrition sites are functional at the health facility, and others through outreach activities, as well will work closely with other partners providing WASH, FSL and Health to ensure that mothers/caregivers receive additional services at facility level.
International Medical Corps with already established Nutrition surveillance team, will undertake nutrition assessments that provide robust information on the nutrition situation of a given population, this information will be key in responding effectively to nutrition needs in the project area. FY 2020 survey plan, IMC is one among the potential survey partners requested to conduct SMART surveys in both IMC operational and non- operational areas. 3 SMART Surveys will be conducted within IMC’s supported project intervention sites while 5 SMART surveys will be conducted in priority counties with high information gap, as identified and assigned by the Nutrition Cluster and NIWG. 
IMC will engage the affected population to participate fully in the project design and implementation to ensure communities have clarity and have their say on the objectives of the nutrition response, the activities, the location, and their entitlements, through formation of Quality, Accountability of Affected population committees in each site in Juba PoC; AL Sabah hospital SC, Malakal town, Malakal PoC, Aburoch and Nyal Panyijar County. Community consultative sessions will be organized on a quarterly basis by field nutrition managers, site managers and field M&E officers, to receive feedback and draw an action plan on areas to improve program implementation.
IMC has already started the process of 2020 Field level agreement with WFP for TSFP supplies in managing moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) cases and had signed PCA with UNICEF until 2021 to support severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases covering in Juba PoC, AL Sabah Hospital, Malakal town, Malakal PoC and Nyal Panyijar County.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving GBV prevention and response services for women and girls affected by conflict in Panyijiar, Aweil East and Rumbek Center
project_objective: The project will provide lifesaving GBV services and prevention activities in Aweil East, Rumbek Central, and Panyijiar counties targeting 38,850 (19,425W, 9,712G, 5,828M, 3,885B) IDPs and host community. IRC will promote access to lifesaving services through the provision of comprehensive case management, referrals, individual and group psychosocial support services at the women's and girls’ friendly spaces (WGFS). The intervention will emphasize on the provision of and access to holistic survivor-centered services and collaboration with service providers to ensure that the host community and IDP women and girls receive appropriate care in response to their needs, and in line with global best practices and minimum standards. The IRC will continue to use the existing WGFS in Nyal and Kol payams (Panyijiar) and through the UNICEF guidelines on WGFS establish more centers in Rumbek central (2) and South (2). The centers will host age-appropriate group psychosocial and skills-building activities; weekly information sessions; and recreational activities to promote healing, strengthen social cohesion, and support networks for women and girls from both the host community and IDPs. These different sessions will provide women with opportunities to share their experiences and build support networks as well as provide a safe place to openly talk about issues of concern for women and girls, which cannot easily be spoken about at home. Additional PSS activities will be integrated into these sessions and will include modules on life skills, self-esteem, communication and identifying coping mechanisms. Specialized PSS group sessions through the IRC Women Rise curriculum, with a focus on healing from trauma, will be conducted with women and girls who have experienced or face threats of violence. The IRC will continue to provide age-appropriate services to adolescent girls including information sessions on reproductive health and life skills using the Girl Shine curriculum which will be contextualized to address the prevailing needs of the girls in each project site. The sessions are meant to mitigate their vulnerability to multiple forms of GBV and offer support systems and access to information. This will be pivotal in reducing women's and girls’ isolation and boosting their self-confidence. Caregivers will also be engaged to introduce the adolescent girls (AG) programming (for new girls) and to help them understand key aspects that will help them support the girls. To promote resilience and enhance economic well-being, women will be consulted and supported with, livelihood interventions through the utilization of IRC Economic and Social Empowerment Model (EA$E) to improve access to food and basic needs including hygiene and sanitary items and reduce vulnerability for female and child-headed households, elderly, women with disability and those that who are chronically ill. The economic empowerment through livelihood interventions will enhance household purchasing power and economic capacities of beneficiaries to access food commodities of their choice and basic needs from the local market. The IRC will work to mitigate and respond to the needs of women, girls, men, and boys affected by conflict by reducing GBV risks through frequent joint community-based safety audit assessments, address risks identified, and strengthen community-based support mechanisms, creation of safe and meaningful access to relevant services, and advocacy with other humanitarian actors on GBV mainstreaming. The IRC will also provide material support such as dignity kits and survival kits to the most vulnerable women and girls in the targeted project sites and also ensure that within the women.

project_name: Provision of comprehensive GBV services to affected populations in Kapoeta north, Bungu and Ganji payams of Juba county - central equatoria state.
project_objective:
The project will target vulnerable populations in Kapoeta north and payams of Bungu and  Ganji of Juba County- CES where most affected populations; Returnees, Internally Displaced Persons and host communities are experiencing sexual and gender based violence mostly rape, sexual assaults, sexual abuse, child marriages and various IPV forms placed upon them due to armed conflict, displacement. The one year GBV interventions will focus on increasing women and girls access to lifesaving GBV case management, psychosocial support (PSS) and enhancing protection services with focus on GBV risk reduction activities. MaCDA would also be conducting safety audits and protection monitoring in order to understand the GBV trends and ensure risk mitigation measures are put in place through advocacy by relevant clusters. Establish, train and supervise community based protection networks CBPNs to increase women and girls friendly spaces access to information about GBV risks, services and risk mitigation. Provide a platform would be conducting community dialogues on protection and GBV related topics, development of community based mitigation plans, GBV prevention messaging (early and forced marriages). Establishment of four  women and girls friendly spaces for vulnerable women and adolescent girls to access information on both prevention response services with focus on restoring hope, acceptance, normalcy and enhancing resilience in women and their children. Strengthen the provision of case management services in a timely, effective and efficient manner through establishment of efficient and defined referrals pathways for survivors. Participate in Coordination meetings, GBVWG and services mapping.
Build the capacity of community protection focal points and service providers mostly social workers, community volunteers, police and health workers on GBV prevention and response trainings, GBV case management using IASC guidelines. 
MaCDA past experience. MaCDA implemented a GBV prevention and response activities to both IDPs and host communities with support from IOMRRF on a GBV project, Dec 2018 to March 2019 at Rokon and Dolo counties; phase out. MaCDA implementing GBV project with a component of Menstrual hygiene management ( MHM) at Kapoeta South payams. we have been conducting trainings for community protection focal points on GBV prevention and response, training case workers, case management Officers health workers and community volunteers on GBV case management using IASC guidelines. Targeted 1,500 women and girls from kapoeta town, Longeleya and Nachilagur to be trained on making sanitary towels. So far, 638 women have been trained on how to make sanitary towels,  some of them have already passed to next levels of making Nickers. It is a pilot project with support from WFP July to December 2019; status ongoing. therefore MaCDA would be using its vast knowledge and practical experience in the field of protection and GBV, Livelihood skills in replicating the same experience to the GBV  project MaCDA is about to bring at Bungu and Ganji payams of Juba county- CES.
The total number of Direct beneficiaries targeted is 6,838 individuals.

project_name: Strengthen CCCM activities in Wau collective sites to improve delivery of humanitarian services and protection of IDPs through efficient and effective multi-sectoral response in Wau
project_objective:
Internally displace persons (IDPs) in Wau continue to live in the five collective centers due to unresolved political conflict in the country. The population of Wau and surrounding areas have been particularly affected significantly by outbreaks of violence and political conflict since early in the years resulting in significant influxes into collective sites.   In Western Bhar el Ghazal, there are 13,034 in five collective sites in Wau (Lokoloko, cathedral, Nazereth, St. Joseph, Hai masna) and 3,843 in camp like setting located at Agok, Bazia roadside, Diem Zubier and Alel chok (CCCM Cluster Tracking August 2019).  This project will target 13,034 beneficiaries (3,512 boys, 3,573 girls, 2,870 men, and 3,079 women) in 5 collective sites of Wau who have limited access to livelihood activities and in dire need of humanitarian assistants which is provided by various humanitarian actors. Therefore, its crucial to ensure timely, coordinated and need based humanitarian assistance are provided to the affected population through effective and efficient camp coordination and Camp management response mechanism. In 2020, AFOD will continue to provide extensive camp management support services in the five collective centers in Wau to meet the needs of the affected population through: continued community sensitization and mobilization, basic site maintenance and repairs; strengthening community structures and leadership for self-management, improve coordination and management of services with other partners; information management, sharing and advocacy for IDPs rights, and community engagement for self-management. AFOD will adopt combination of strategies for the CCCM response such as service delivery through effective stakeholders’ coordination, capacity building, and integration of CCCM services with Health, FSL, Education and protection of beneficiary by community for complementarity and synergy. Key stakeholders shall be engaged in implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the project including establishment of complaint feedback mechanism and complain desk, community dialogue meetings to obtain comprehensive feedback. Further to the current interventions, the primary focus remains mobile CCCM response that will deliver capacity building of site management committees (SMC), local authorities and support to ensure that dedicated skills are in place to manage the camps in an equitable manner, mitigate protection risks and play a vital role in facilitation of all sectors’ activities. AFOD together with the CCCM cluster seeks to address the anticipated and outstanding lifesaving needs of displaced, vulnerable populations in collective centres, camps and camp-like settings in and around Wau.
AFOD as an exit strategy will be working closely with RRC who is the camp administrator responsible for safety and protection of the collective sites, allocation of land for IDPs in collaboration with the community and ensuring safe return of the displaced persons into their communities.  IDP leaders and local authorities have been trained on leadership and governance and will continue to develop their capacity for self-governance. Similarly, AFOD is going to increase the number of outreach assistants who shall be identified within the IDPs as an exit plan. Coexistence of the IDPs with host communities and durable solution for safe return of IDPs are formulated and strengthened through stakeholder engagement and dialogues.

project_name: Strengthening CCCM Response in Sites and Camp-like Settings for Conflict Affected Populations in Unity and Jonglei State
project_objective: The project will ensure equal access and needs based assistance to improve the quality of integrated services for populations affected by displacement, well-coordinated and integrated humanitarian intervention to 30,000 IDPs (5000 men, 15 000 women, 3000 boys and 7000 girls) to improve their well-being, their resilience and participation in decision-making processes. It will respond to emergency needs by empowering community and strengthening the capacities of local actors to have access to both essentials camp management service. Several strategies will be used including joint interventions with other clusters such as FSL, WASH, ES/NFI, and ensuring that our activities and the whole intervention complements other sectors and partners activities and not duplication. HRSS using CCCM cluster strategy and initiative of cash for work will provide a cash based intervention to enhance resilience building and copying mechanisms. HRSS through a multi-sectoral approach will mainstream and integrate protection, health, WASH, Nutrition, Education, FSL in its intervention through intentional massaging, joint missions among others and will integrate HLP, MHPSS, PSEA, and GBV issues and ensure gender balanced teams. Hope Restoration has experience working in Panyijiar and Nyirol implementing CCCM and protection. If funded, the project will contribute significantly to service delivery in hard-to-reach location through organizing, carry out multi-sectoral needs assessments, create site level  service map and protection of people with special needs in coordination with actors; and strengthening community structure by training community members on CCCM and humanitarian response.

project_name: Improving emergency Shelter and Non-food items response to newly displaced IDPs and Returnees in Fangak, Ayod County of Jonglei State;  Koch and Mayendit Counties of Unity State of South Sudan.
project_objective: Fangak, Ayod (in Jonglei State); Koch and Mayendit Counties (in Unity State) – all bordering The Sudan - have been identified as cantonment sites. Thousands of returnees are expected back home in these counties in 2020, based on high prospects of a revitalized peace in South Sudan. The presence of these cantonment sites in the mentioned counties is a source of vulnerability to the returnee population. Civil population will be exposed to protection risks such as forced and voluntary recruitments into the army; exposure to GBV risks; interference during access to civilian humanitarian services; occupation of civilian infrastructure; availability, exposure and spread of weapon; misuse of humanitarian aid (including deviation, looting and exploitation); violation of housing, land and property right; lack of political will and support - targeted mocks on civilians. As flood-prone areas, the locations almost always experience floods, resulting in human displacements. Besides, man-made disasters are recurrent: tribal attacks and escalation of conflict between warring parties. Historically, the mentioned States have been experiencing massive displacement of people, killing of children, women, the elderly and loss of livestock and property, including burning of houses. In 2019, an estimated 35,000 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) were quarterly displaced in these States. 75,000 people returned from PoCs in Bor, Malakal , Juba, Ethiopia and Sudan . In 2020, thousands more are expected back home in the mentioned States.This project aims to ensure provision of S/NFIs to the most affected population of conflict and disaster, vulnerable categories in the mentioned counties, especially the IDPs and the most affected vulnerable host communities. These are based on the Humanitarian Needs overview (HNO) and Humanitarian Response Plans (HRP) for South Sudan. The project will target a population of 30,000 individuals in Fangak, Ayod Counties of Jonglei State; Koch and Mayendit Counties of Unity State. It targets populations in four locations:  Fangak (12, 000); Ayod (6,000); Koch (6,000) and Mayendit (6,000) individuals respectively. Due to the magnitude of the displacement, about 70% of households are expected to be women-headed, with no less than one third widows, plus the housewives whose husbands will be relocating to cantonment sites, seeking for military service or promotions within the army with an intention of earning more money for their households left behind in home villages. IDPs and returnees are (as of 2019) settled in Old Fangak, New Fangak, Ayod, Koch and Mayendit. Several joint assessment and responses conducted from 20th July to 5th Sept 2019 reported IDPs lacking essential NFIs services. Other IDPs had health related issues, especially diarrhea, vomiting, skin diseases, and fever, especially amongst children. IDPs were reportedly sleeping in Kangas and shawls, with about ten or more individuals sharing with one host household. Many children who were attending school were out of school in the locations where IDPs have settled. Children are also at risk of neglect, child labour, gender based violence (GBV), recruitment into armed groups, forced marriage (for girls) and family separation especially after going through the violence when fighting broke out. Over 60% of the most-at-risk IDP populations in these areas will mainly be women and children, with family shelter and NFI needs. The humanitarian imperative is: provide S/NFI to these IDPs and host populations, the basis of this proposal. Upon project approval, ADA will send pipeline requests for the S/NFI supplies to the Logistics Cluster who will share the request with the S/NFI Cluster. The latter will approve or seek clarifications from ADA who will respond to the queries. Once approved, the Logistics Cluster will update the items to be sent to the field and notify ADA accordingly. ADA will liaise with field teams/bases to ensure supplies are received and distributed.

project_name: Improving access and strengthening the provision of emergency lifesaving health care services in Cueibet, Jur River, Mayendit and Leer counties through the provision of 2PHCCs, 2PHCUs and 4 mobile clinics response.
project_objective: Since the situation in South Sudan as created a high demand of health care service, this project is aiming at enhancing access and strengthening the provision of emergency lifesaving health care services in Cueibet, Jur River, Mayendit and Leer counties through the provision of 2PHCCs, 2PHCUs and 4mobile clinic response. Although the current security situation is relatively calmed in Tonj north, there are still pockets of IDPs in Cueibet county that were displaced from Tonj north due to inter-clan fighting and that is still raising the need of health care services in the county. Despite the ongoing health care response in Jur River county, there is still a wider gap in health service delivery because HPF3 is only supporting 31 health facilities leaving out 20 HFs. The communities that were served by the 20 HFs are now moving to seek health care from those payams that have functional health facilities. Given the fact that security situation is currently stabled in Leer and Mayendit counties, so many returnees are reported coming back from Sudan and IDPs camps in Bentiu and Juba on daily basis and this has created a high demands on health care service in the two counties. This project proposal will be targeting a total of 81,024 beneficiaries of which 20,422 individuals in Jur River, 25,552 in Cueibet, 11,886 in Leer and 23,164 in Mayendit counties respectively. This project will benefit all gender groups including, 31,761 men, 33,059 women, 7,940 boys and 8,264 girls across the four project catchment Counties. Projections from IPC of August 2019 to April 2020 as estimated 6.35 million people (54% of the population) are classified in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, among whom an estimated 1.7 million people are facing Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and 10,000 people are in Catastrophe (IPC phase 5). The Aug 2019 to April 2020 IPC projection has shown Cueibet and Jur River falling under IPC Phase3 or worse acute food insecurity. In Leer, Medair conducted a SMART survey in April 2019 with GAM rate of 14.3 %( 10.8 - 18.6 95% C.I.) While SAM stood at 3.2 %( 1.8 - 5.5 95% C.I.). The Aug 2019-April 2020 IPC projection shows that the food security situation remains a concern in the four counties of Mayendit, Guit, Koch and Panyijiar due to persisted pockets of insecurity, cattle raiding, high food prices, flood related destruction of crops and disruption to market access.  The prevalence of major illnesses reported among the surveyed children include: fever (49 percent), Cough/ARI (26 percent) and Diarrhea (22 percent). The prevalence of fever/malaria in all ten former States is consistently high. The provision of this primary health care service shall include OPD curative consultations and IPD services at the 2PHCCs of Rocrocdong and Leer TPA, 2PHCUs of Dablual and Duony in Mayendit and Cueibet counties and 4mobile clinics of Pandiet in Cueibet, Dhorlek in Mayendit, Payak in Leer and Rocrocdong in Jur River counties. We will also support the psycho social and basic mental health services through case identification, first aid counseling, treatment and referral of the clients to nearby health county or state hospitals.

project_name: Delivery of Integrated emergency lifesaving health care to 2,500 IDPs and Host communities in Nyirol, Uror, Akobo and Pibor Counties – Jonglei State
project_objective:
1.	The project aims to mobilise resources to improve access to integrated emergency health care services and shall be focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality affecting the most vulnerable communities including malaria, Acute watery diarrhoea, Acute bloody diarrhoea, Acute Respiratory Tract infection (ARTI) and neonatal and maternal health conditions.
2.	It aims to reduce inequity; it will also focus on health promotion and prevention, screening and early intervention; and improve quality, safety, performance and accountability.
3.	As a strategy to detect, prevent and response to epidemics prone diseases outbreaks and in line with the current cluster strategy and objectives, this project will use multidisciplinary approaches such working with WASH hygiene promoters, Boma Health Committees, Religious leaders, extension workers and Mother to Mother support groups to widen the surveillance network.
4.	Promote healthcare services integration with nutrition, WASH, FSL, and protection especially Sexual Gender Based Violence (SGBV) to enhance intervention effectiveness and its impact on the most vulnerable communities.
5.	The project will integrate the ongoing development focused intervention to narrow the huge gaps in the health care provision and to ensure outbreaks and other emergencies impacting on health are timely and effectively prevented, addressed and contained.

project_name: Increasing equitable access to integrated preventative and lifesaving nutrition services for crisis affected populations in Fangak and Nyirol Counties
project_objective:
The overall goal of this project is to scale up activities aimed at effectively decreasing suffering, morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable populations in Fangak and Nyirol Counties. This is pegged on the fact that acute malnutrition has been a protracted problem in the targeted counties and thus one that requires sustained investment. The relevant literature reviewed reveal that the needs are substantial and widespread, and it is apparent that there are numerous challenges associated with availability and access to nutritious foods which require urgent interventions.

This proposed CMA response will, therefore prioritize life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years of age, PLW, and chronically ill persons as the most vulnerable groups to acute malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs. Similarly, prevention activities that address the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition will be enhanced. Further, this response will expand on nutrition specific interventions, as well as reinforce integration and linkages with other sectors to address the key drivers of malnutrition: food insecurity, sub-optimal child care and feeding practices, morbidity, and lack of safe water and sanitation. It will prioritize the unreached payams in Fangak & Nyirol where high prevalence of acute malnutrition, conflict and internal displacement coexist. The project will also enhance activities around nutrition monitoring, analysis and utilization of early warning information for timely coordinated response decision making. 

Using static and mobile outreach approaches the project will scale-up services in the designated 12 OTP-TSFP sites. The response strategies will be (1) carry-out case-finding screening using the MUAC method (including malaria testing for SAM patients) from static units and through outreaches to PHCUs and admitting under 5 SAM and MAM patients and PLW MAM patients to SC, OTP and TSFP services (2) conduct mobile outreaches to inaccessible locations beyond the reach of static services (3) deliver MIYCN services to PLW and care-givers of children U23 months through counselling MtoM support groups, including vitamin A supplements and de-worming (4) fully integrate nutrition, health and WASH services, and partially integrate FSL, Education and Protection activities. SAM with medical complications and requiring malaria treatment will be referred to PHCCs.

In order to improve this project’s responsiveness to evolving and varied needs of the affected population, CMA will adopt a people-centered approach by mainstreaming protection, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), disability inclusion as well as emphasis on gender and age considerations. In order to build a ground for sustainability, this project will seek to strengthen local capacity, including County Health Department at county level, project staff and community nutrition volunteers through targeted training. Since insecurity creates risks for PLW and U5s, CMA in collaboration with the targeted communities will implement protection practices to reduce risk of SGBV. By applying IASC guidance, measures to identify specific needs of men, women, boys and girls and mainstream gender and protection will be adopted and utilized.

In this project, CMA will provide mechanisms through which affected populations can receive the information they need to make informed decisions on accessing nutrition services, provide feedback on the nutrition interventions, share concerns and submit complaints. CMA will work closely with all stakeholders e.g. local authorities, community leaders, beneficiaries etc. to ensure their inclusion in program decision-making and participation in planning, implementation and monitoring the delivery of nutrition services.

project_name: Provision of emergency shelter and non-food items for newly displaced, protracted displaced, returnees, and vulnerable and affected non-displaced populations in Jonglei, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria in South Sudan.
project_objective:
ACTED will aim to implement emergency shelter and non-food items interventions in 2020 in Jonglei, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria, in line with the following S/NFI cluster objectives:
1.	Improve access to safe, appropriate emergency shelter and lifesaving NFIs to newly displaced or populations with new vulnerabilities.
2.	Enhance the community’s dignity by increasing their ability to respond to new shocks and building on existing skills. 
3.	Improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable protracted IDPs, returnees, and host communities/affected non- displaced, who are unable to meet their S/NFI needs.

To fulfil the above objectives, ACTED will provide emergency shelter and non-food items to the most vulnerable displaced populations, returnees, and affected non-displaced populations, specifically targeting Jur River, Bor South, Uror, Akobo and Tambura counties. Targeted beneficiaries will be given shelter and non-food items either in-kind or through vouchers/ cash, depending on their needs and location, to enable quick responses to meet emergency need. Cash-based programming and vouchers will be preferred in areas where there is a functioning market and items available. ACTED will utilise different modalities depending on the context and needs, as highlighted in needs assessments. Cash-for-work approaches will be utilised to ensure the most vulnerable recipients are supported to build shelters, and where appropriate host communities will be included as beneficiaries of this to ensure shared benefits. 

ACTED’s S/NFI intervention will be closely integrated with multi-sectoral response, including mobile Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), depending on needs. This will be delivered through our ‘hub of resilience’ model, which is an area-based model aiming to holistically meet emergency needs of vulnerable communities, supporting them to recover from shocks and rebuild resilience. ACTED feels that these multi-sectoral settlements-based responses enhance impact across all sectors, and mitigate against misuse of SNFI items. Responses will be conducted through mobile missions (lasting 6-8 weeks) in tandem with the mobile CCCM response team, in addition to semi-static responses based out of ACTED’s existing static bases in Jonglei, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Western Equatoria. 

ACTED highly prioritises Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), ensuring at least a medium term presence in communities (expected minimum 6 weeks) to ensure in-depth assessment and understanding of issues like SEA and HLP. This also enables strengthening of community leadership structures (under the CCCM component) in a way that improves community resilience. Furthermore, ACTED implements a Complaints and Response mechanism in all interventions, ensuring that community feedback is encouraged and acted upon. ACTED’s mobile missions also implement community based complaints mechanisms to ensure sustainability and accountability of leadership to community needs. To further strengthen feedback and response, rapid monitoring will be conducted following distributions, with several full post-distribution monitoring exercises to ensure collation of evidence and lessons learned.

ACTED’s project team utilizes a do no harm matrix during assessment which has a focus on HLP analysis. ACTED will consult the SNFI cluster HLP due diligence guidelines and checklist to ensure that HLP issues fully underlie our do no harm response, and will also collaborate with HLP actors in areas of intervention.

project_name: Supporting durable solutions through housing, land and property support for IDPs in Juba, South Sudan.
project_objective:
ACTED will aim to improve access to HLP services for IDPs through 2020. This will support the Protection Cluster Objective 3: Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other population. Activities will be coordinated by ACTED in its role as camp manager of the Juba PoCs, and will be focused in urban Juba including the peri-POC site area and Mangateen.
To fulfill the above objective, ACTED will focus on the following:
1.	Awareness raising and information dissemination activities in the PoC regarding HLP rights and services.
2.	Coordination of protection, in particular HLP, partners in the PoC through a designated focal point.
3.	Logistical support to HDC (primary HLP partner) to enable them to upscale and expand services, as well as referrals to HLP partners.

ACTED’s protection intervention will be closely integrated with its multi-sectoral response, particularly Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) and ongoing plans to adapt approaches to essential service provision (health and education). As camp manager, ACTED is convening a consortium to operate a project in the peri-PoC area and Mangateen to improve services and therefore equalise the service provision disparity with populations outside of the PoC. This will be linked with wider efforts on durable solutions, supporting PoC populations who wish to return to urban Juba – and potentially to other parts of South Sudan - to do so. Support to HLP services will be integral to ensuring that this project is able to holistically support IDPs who voluntarily seek durable solutions.

project_name: Provision of integrated and equitable lifesaving nutrition service for children under 5 and pregnant and lactating women in Renk (Upper Nile), Pariang (Unity) and Fangak (Jonglei), South Sudan
project_objective:
The provision of integrated emergency lifesaving Nutrition services to the vulnerable children U5s; 8,367 Boys, 11,780 Girls, and 10,487 Women (PLWs) through fixed sites and mobile approaches in Fangak (Jonglei), Pariang (Unity) and Renk (Upper Nile) during 2020. 

Within a 1 years of implementation, the project is anticipated to utilize $760,000; This project will contribute to the 4 cluster objective; (1) Contribute to the reduction of mortality, mortality and child suffering from protection threat through increasing access and equitable utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific service delivery for Children U5s with severe and moderate acute malnutrition and pregnant & lactating meeting the admission criteria will be enrolled into the CMAM program; Provision of special nutritious foods, Maternal infant Young Child Nutrition, Micro nutrients supplementation and behavioral change communication approach; (ii) To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment; Active and passive screen for malnutrition at community level through the community nutrition volunteers and Maternal Infant Young Child Nutrition Promoter focusing on the prioritized locations of Pariang (Unity) Renk (Upper Nile) and Fangak (Jonglei) by the end of 2020.
 
(2) Ensure safe and equitable access to critical integrated basic services to enable [number] prioritized target people to meet their basic needs; (1) To increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and joint programming targeting vulnerable groups; through conducting malaria screening and treating, Strengthening livelihood skills with kitchen gardening, and demonstration gardens to support on complementary feeding for children under five both girls and boys.

(3) Regular monitoring of the nutrition situation in the project area implemented and the information used for appropriate actions at the project level; Through monthly capacity building for staffs on how to use the NIS software and Quality of data submitted to National and Nutrition cluster for proper informing and planning purposes.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods of Vulnerable Agro-pastoralist Communities in Nassir, Maiwut, Longichuck and Ulang Counties of Upper Nile State
project_objective:
African Humanitarian Corps is planning a one year emergency food security and livelihood response targeting Nassir, Maiwut, Longichuck and Ulang of Upper Nile State composing main and dry season campaign. At least three fourths (77%) of South Sudanese are facing unprecedented levels of food insecurity across the country (South Sudan IPC update September 2019). This has been compounded by a soaring inflation, reduced purchasing power and increased household expenditure on food, with monthly expenditure on food at 64%; and reduced/ same incomes among 90% of households for the past one year (FSNMS Round 24). These have been attributed to a combination of a protracted and escalating conflict in Greater Maiwut( Nassir, Longichuck, Maiwut and Ulang Counties)   and increasing armed movements across the Sobat corridor (South Sudan Humanitarian Bulletins September 2019) and below average harvests due to recent Fall Army Worm invasion.
Poor agricultural production capacities, dysfunctional markets, poor terms of trade and soaring inflation have led to worsening food and nutrition security situation, with populations resorting to negative coping strategies.
The project aims at enabling the most vulnerable men, women, girls, boys and youth (male and female) among IDPs and host communities (including elderly and disabled) in Nassir, Maiwut, Ulang and Longichuck Counties of Upper Nile State to access life-saving services and income opportunities so as to improve immediate and medium term household food and nutrition security and enhance their resilience, preparedness and self-reliance. This will also reduce their reliance on negative coping strategies such as distressed sale of high value assets and unsustainable exploitation of forest resources that lead to environmental degradation.
The proposed activities will involve support to emergency distribution of crop, vegetable and fishing kits for the main season and vegetable and fishing kits for the dry season production targeting 21733 Households - 130,398 beneficiaries (20000 girls and 20000 boys) and adults (30000 men and 60,398 women). Light training will also be included in the project implementation. The project will mainstream cross-cutting programmatic approaches that include application of Accountability to Affected Populations principles, protection including GBV/ Sexual exploitation mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conflict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention, environmental conservation and sustainability.

project_name: Provision of GBV prevention, mitigation and response services in Wulu county of Lakes state South Sudan
project_objective:
In response to the growing humanitarian crisis in Lakes State. WAV Gender Based Violence project plan will directly target 10294 vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Wulu county with a total of 6176 females, 1029 males,1029 boys and 2059 girls 5% of the target population will include people with disability,female headed households,pregnant and lactating women and the elderly .The project aims at providing quality GBV services to GBV survivors and reduce suffering of women, girls, men and boys by providing timely and integrated multi-sector assistance and services to reduce acute needs and promote and sustain their resilience to recurrent shocks. 

The prioritized objectives to achieve the overall goal will include: 
CO 1: Ensure the provision of critical protection-related assistance and specialized services through an
integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas
CO 2: Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience.

The main activities to be carried out to realize this objectives and achieve the overall goal will include : 

1)Training of the case workers and community protection volunteers on comprehensive case management and psycho social support (PSS) to strengthen safe referrals, including information dissemination on available services.
2) Establishment of Women & girls friendly spaces with PSS ,case management and skill building interventions which will also be supported through women safety committees, women groups and Community-based protection groups to strengthen support in protection, coordination and community awareness raising and sensitization. 
3) Conduct community outreach targeting 10294 community members to raise awareness.
4) Establishment and strengthening the referral pathway mechanisms for Wulu county.

project_name: Integrated and lifesaving essential health care aimed to reduce morbidity and mortality amongst  vulnerable populations, including conflict affected, SGBV survivors, persons with disabilities and mental health disorders, in Greater Upper Nile State, South Sudan
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve access to integrated and lifesaving services through static (PHCCs, PHCUs) and mobile health and nutrition facilities amongst vulnerable populations of Maiwut, Nasir, Ulang and Longechuk in Upper Nile.
The intervention will focus on screening, prevention and treatment of communicable and non-communicable diseases through outpatient consultation and mobile outreach, preventive health promotion campaigns, injury management, SRH and MNCH services (incl. ANC and PNC), safe delivery in facilities and community through skilled birth attendants/mid-wives, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services, clinical management of rape (SGBV services), regular and routine disease surveillance, reporting and prompt response to outbreaks, routine and outreach immunization services and strengthened referral pathways. Protection will be mainstreamed across interventions. Health services will be provided through close collaboration with the CHD and in coherence with BHI. More female staff and volunteers will be recruited to ensure that women’s health needs are addressed
The project will integrate WASH and Nutrition into health programming in order to ensure positive and sustainable health outcomes. Community mobilization and sensitization will be strengthened on health-related messages, through integrated messaging that includes WASH and nutrition messages. The proposed project will ensure early detection and treatment of Tuberculosis and HIV cases in the community and management of SAM with medical complications. Communities in the targeted counties will be engaged throughout project life cycle to ensure programme ownership and sustainability. Health worker capacities will be enhanced in immunization, disease surveillance, BEmoNC, MPHSS, SGBV/CMR, IMCI and case management. This project will complement RI World Bank project in Longechuk and Maiwut in management of communicable diseases, immunization, save motherhood (PNC, ANC and deliveries), disease surveillance, management of SGBV, and Mental health problems among others which are part of WB project activities.
Approx. 92,444 vulnerable hosts, IDPs and returnees are living in Upper Nile and Jonglei states. (Maiwut- 6778 people - 3321 male and 3457 females; Nasir County - 17202 people 8429 male and 8773 females; Ulang County 63,048 people – 30894 male and 32155 females; and Longechuk county 5416 People – 2654 male and 2762 females 
In this project, RI will engage communities during the selection of Mobile medical (MMUs) locations, identifying storage spaces for essential drugs and MMU equipment such as Metallic trunk for keeping drugs and registers, table, chairs, mats and contributing with space and locally available material for establishing the MMUs. MMUs and health facilities (PHCCs and PHCUs) will be equipped with medical equipment such as sphygmomanometer, Stethoscope, Respiratory beat timers, weighing scale, Fete scope, thermometers and data collection and reporting tools. In addition, MMU will store essential drugs and test kits, such as MRDT, rapid test for syphilis among others, and medical equipment for quality services provision. MMUs will be staffed with local health workers and build their capacities. Staff in each MMU will have a work plan for weekly visits to all reachable villages and weekly reporting. The community mobilizer will mobilize the village ahead of the MMU team visiting the village for providing consultations and other services responding to community needs. Integrated service provision, that includes WASH and nutrition services required for positive health outcomes, will specifically address protection concerns of the most vulnerable groups in the community. Staff will be trained in humanitarian protection principles of “DO NO HARM” and beneficiary feedback will be encouraged and captured. Monitoring visits by RI and community representatives/ local authorities will ensure needs and rights-based service delivery.

project_name: To enhance emergence food assistance, production  and strengthen vulnerable population’s ability to absorb shocks in Maban, Nasir, Ulang, Maiwut and Longochuk, Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
With an estimated 54% of the population in crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, amongst whom an estimated 1.7m people are facing Emergency (IPC Phase 4), high levels of food insecurity continue to persist in South Sudan during the 2019 lean season as compared to the same period in 2018. Persistent acute food insecurity is attributed to unusually high food prices, localized conflicts, climate shocks, slow recovery from prolonged asset depletion, limited access to markets and high number of returnees from Sudan and Ethiopia, putting additional pressure on available resources and livelihoods. 
Between January and April 2020, 14 counties are projected to be in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity: Jonglei State is expected to have the highest number of people (1.18 million) estimated to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, followed by former Upper Nile State (765,000 persons). Lack of roads and basic infrastructure for accessing essential services and commuting as well as continued insecurity related to inter-communal conflicts, cattle raiding, child kidnapping, particularly in Nasir, Ulang, Maiwut and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State, have significantly disrupted access to markets and fishing. While the operational environment in targeted areas remains challenging, life-saving support in key sectors is critical for internally displaced persons (IDP), refugee, returnees and host communities. RI’s proposed program, “Food assistance, production and strengthening ability shocks” aims to deliver lifesaving humanitarian assistance through provision of food assistance that meets short term hunger gaps while helping households build longer term food security and resilience against future shocks and stresses; prioritizing cash in areas with functional markets and in-kind transfers where cash programming is not appropriate. The proposed program is expected to enable the most vulnerable to address immediate food needs and reduce negative coping mechanisms, thus addressing protection concerns while preventing malnutrition and further depletion of productive assets. A multi-sectoral model will be applied, integrating livelihoods, nutrition sensitive food security and dietary diversity and resilience building interventions while addressing hygiene and safe sanitation and mainstreaming protection. Further, the proposed program aims to contribute to Food Security and Livelihoods cluster objectives - CO1, CO2, and CO3 that are aligned with the SDG 2 “End Hunger - achieve food security and improved nutrition, and promote sustainable agriculture.”

The program will target vulnerable populations, especially women, girls, elderly, disabled, PLW, children U5, HIV & the chronically sick amongst IDPs, refugee, returnees or host communities. RI is well placed to implement the above program as it has been operating in the location since 9 years, having established a strong working relationship with local authorities, built trust with communities, delivered inclusive and impactful programs that mainstream gender and protection, aiming to providing quality services amongst the most vulnerable and marginalized populations. RI is an active member of national and county level coordination mechanisms and ensures community participation in all phases of the program cycle. The project will enable RI to strengthen its emergency food security and livelihoods activities to deliver integrated emergency assistance to vulnerable populations while strengthening synergies with its health and WASH activities being implemented in the proposed target areas. WFP supported GFD in Longechuk, TSFP and IFP support in Maiwut and Nasir will further help RI address food security and nutrition concerns amongst vulnerable groups. RI’s integrated approach-health, nutrition and WASH, supported by OFDA, BPRM, UNHCR, UNICEF, WFP and FAO, will strengthen synergies the impact of the proposed project in the same locations.

project_name: Integrated and lifesaving emergency nutrition services aimed to increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition and early detection and treatment of girls and boys under five years of age and pregnant and lactating women affected by acute malnutrition in Maiwut, Longechuk, Nasir, Ulang, counties of Upper Nile State (UNS).
project_objective:
RI’s integrated programme aims to prevent and treat malnutrition and under nutrition and promote good health among vulnerable groups. In 2020, RI will scale up integrated services among nutrition, FSL, health and WASH sectors through the implementation of its projects in Greater Upper Nile. This strategy will help address interrelated and under-lying causes of malnutrition, such as food insecurity, suboptimal childcare and feeding practices, and lack of safe water and sanitation. 
Compared to 2019, RI will increase the volume of preventative activities and build on the successes of community-based management of acute malnutrition.
RI’s aim is to support South Sudanese including refugees, internal displaced persons, returnees and vulnerable population. Our response will prioritize life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years and pregnant and lactating women, in compliance with relevant national guidelines, these being the most vulnerable groups in terms of malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs. Geographically, our response will prioritize the greater upper Nile (Maiwut, Nasir, Ulang and Longechuk) characterized by a high malnutrition, food insecurity (IPC Phase 4 and 5), conflict and internal displacement. RI Nutrition sites will act as hubs for integrated programming. While its health activities sector will provide malaria testing and treatment among severely acute malnourished children being treated at the Nutrition sites, WASH activities will provide access to safe water and NFI kits to severely malnourished children’s families and the food security activities will improve dietary diversity through kitchen gardens at nutrition sites to demonstrate recommended feeding practices. RI nutrition sites will integrate early childhood development stimulation activities and will be considered as potential entry points for identifying and responding to GBV survivors and helping them access referral pathways to be established by RI. 
To further localize RI’s response and to ensure sustainability, RI will strengthen the County Health Department (CHD) responsibilities to oversee nutrition interventions, to coordinate the response with various stakeholders at the county level and provide stakeholder capacity building on the new national guidelines of community based management of malnutrition and maternal, infant, and young child nutrition. 
RI will provide technical support to CHD to review county level nutrition intervention strategy that is expected to include nutrition referral needs of all payams and Boma of targeted counties. RI will reinforce the nutrition information system and use of nutrition data at the county and community level by employing gender-sensitive approach to mitigate obstacles compromising women and girls’ ability to receive nutrition support. Women’s participation will be encouraged in programme design and feedback mechanisms. RI will also collaborate with existing and planned development interventions on nutrition, such as those funded by the World Bank in the greater upper Nile.  RI aims to achieve four objectives, including: (i) Increasing equitable access and utilization of quality life-saving nutrition services to address acute malnutrition amongst the most vulnerable and at-risk U5 children and pregnant and lactating women; (ii) Preventing under-nutrition by increasing equitable access to early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition amongst maternal, infant and young children; (iii) Increasing access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH, FSL and protection interventions; (iv) Enhancing nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information for early warning and decision making.

project_name: Integrating WASH in nutrition and health response to ensure equitable and safe access to water, sanitation and hygiene among vulnerable IDPs, host communities and returnees in Upper Nile and Central & Western Equatoria States.
project_objective:
RI’s proposed 2020 Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) intervention is designed to contribute to improved health and nutrition outcomes, addressing key factors of wider community disease outbreaks, vicious circle of malnutrition, timely and equitable access to safe WASH and mitigation of related GBV, amongst 250,000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in Upper Nile, Central and Western Equatoria states in South Sudan.

The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with RI’s health and nutrition programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to improve people’s lives and well-being, thus contributing to South Sudan WASH Cluster objectives and the 2020 Humanitarian Response. Recognising WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. RI’s integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition by targeting SAM and MAM children and families and contribute to controlling disease outbreak.

Additionally, RI will ensure equitable, timely and sustainable access to improved safe and adequate water and sanitation facilities that address the vital WASH needs, public health and protection issues, respect sphere standards; engage communities in design and ownership, improve knowledge on appropriate hygiene practices to reduce and prevent WASH-related diseases including cholera, AWD, typhoid, skin diseases etc.

RI will construct gender-sensitive water supply systems, mainly solar powered, boreholes through manual drilling, extensions to bring water points closer to vulnerable households, rainwater harvesting systems at schools, health and nutrition facilities, rehabilitate damaged / nonfunctional boreholes, increase access to safe water and mitigate the risk of GBV at WASH facilities. Comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) and Health & Nutrition facility staff. RI will work with existing WUCs to reinforce technical skills for water point O&M (operations and maintenance), establishing new WUCs where relevant. Solid waste management training will be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns. RI will also construct incinerators for medical waste disposal at health facilities.

At the household level, RI will construct 1,000 household/family shared latrines, with owner contribution, amongst displaced, returnee, and conflict-affected communities to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. 

Latrine construction will adhere to protection standards as elaborated in the guidelines for WASH Cluster partners in South Sudan. RI will also promote hygiene awareness aimed to support behavior change in hygiene practices through house-to-house hygiene education sessions, training of hygiene volunteers, and distribution of household packages for famine prevention which will include: one 20-liter bucket with tap for proper water storage, one 20-liter bucket without tap or jerry can for water collection, filter cloth, water purifier (PuR), and soap for six month consumption.

project_name: GBV – Prevention and response to sexual and gender based violence in conflict and displacement affected locations in South Sudan
project_objective:
DRC plans to implement Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) prevention and response activities in hard-to-reach conflict areas in South Sudan, through static and mobile responses. DRC strives to contribute to the two Protection cluster strategic objectives: 
-	Provide immediate lifesaving assistance to address priority protection needs for the most vulnerable populations in hard-to-reach areas
-	Prevent, mitigate and respond to protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience
DRC will provide SGBV response activities for identified cases, including case management and psychosocial support (PSS). The SGBV response element will follow a survivor-centered approach, following the Inter Agency Standing Committee (IASC) GBV guidelines, and ensuring DRC staff are well trained and qualified to handle sensitive and confidential cases. The prevention activities will focus on promoting community engagement and ownership in addressing sexual and gender-based violence, while ensuring communities are aware of GBV services available.
