Awareness raising sessions, community activists’ trainings, mass awareness campaigns and information campaigns will be organised to ensure GBV messaging is consistent and effective, as well as community-led. DRC uses the SASA! methodology, developed by Raising Voices, which aims to address one of the root causes of GBV and HIV, the power imbalance between men and women, through community mobilisation and activism. DRC will also engage in advocacy with the GBV sub-cluster at the state-levels, and with the relevant authorities, such as the minister of gender, to ensure buy-in and support from the main and relevant stakeholders. These activities will be linked with the food security and livelihood activities, which will focus on women empowerment and resilience, while engaging with men on improving gender equality.

DRC has static presence in Unity State, operating from Bentiu, and in Upper Nile, operating both in Maban and in Malakal, Aburoc and several locations on the West bank of the Nile. In addition, DRC operates three mobile protection teams, which conduct integrated protection analyses, identifying SGBV risks and issues in hard-to-reach areas and among populations affected by conflict and displacement (targeted locations identified by GBV sub-cluster). In Upper Nile and Unity States, the GBV program will focus on increasing access to services for survivors and setting up safe spaces for women, where they can discuss their concerns, and alleviate stress and trauma through PSS activities. In all target locations, beneficiaries engaging in awareness raising and activism will be selected based on their motivation to support to behavioural change in the power relations between men and women, while survivors will not be sought out but supported based on need and referrals. Through the intervention, DRC intends to ensure women and men are equally sensitised on the issues concerning gender based violence and gender inequality, while providing life-saving assistance to survivors, encouraging help-seeking behaviour, and support to vulnerable men and women. Overall, DRC aim to reach approximately 40,000 vulnerable individuals affected by displacement and conflict, including approximately 6,400 men, 19,200 women, 4,400 boys, and 10,000 girls.

project_name: Strengthening Nutrition-Sensitive Productive Assets and Resilience to Shocks in Aweil East and Gogrial West
project_objective: South Sudan has experienced above-emergency levels of food insecurity, and even famine at times, since civil conflict broke out in 2013. Protracted insecurity and economic crisis has driven more than 4 million away from their homes, with 2 million internally displaced and 2.2. million residing in neighboring countries as refugees. The August 2019 IPC analysis indicates 6.35 million facing severe food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+_. Despite favorable climatic and geophysical conditions for large-scale cultivation, more than 80% of the country is dependent on subsistence agriculture. Moreover, hyperinflation combined with limited livelihoods alternatives has led to extremely eroded household purchasing power. These conditions combined with combined with a lack of physical and water infrastructure as well as poor hygiene and sanitation practices has led to a high disease burden and emergency rates of malnutrition. Action Against Hunger’s food security and livelihoods strategy is centered on long-term reduction in the burden of undernutrition. Therefore, in direct response to the crisis in the Bahr el Ghazal region of South Sudan, the organization will increase access to food and dietary diversity levels by providing opportunities for beneficiaries to improve their agricultural knowledge/practices and food preparation practices. Additionally, access to sources of food will be improved through the improvement of community infrastructure, diversification of livelihood sources including access to credit/loan for increased supply of nutritious foods. To improve the efficacy of nutrition and health programs, our FSL intervention will be fully integrated with local nutrition and health programs, targeting households with children and pregnant and lactating women facing acute malnutrition. Moreover, the program will be linked with local WaSH interventions (e.g. hygiene promotion) to promote prevention of disease and, in turn, positive nutrition outcomes.

project_name: Ensuring equitable access to safe water, sanitation and  hygiene services among malnutrition-affected communities of NBeG, Warrap and Jonglei
project_objective: Action Against Hunger (ACF) has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs. Our strategy addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WaSH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently ACF is implementing program activities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states with established field offices in Malualkon, Alek, Old Fangak and Paguir Payams. In 2020, WaSH projects will be implemented to ensure that host communities, IDPs and returnees have safe access to water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behavior. Proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5 and pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WaSH and Nutrition response aimed at breaking the diarrhea – malnutrition vicious cycle. This project will ensure the effectiveness of addressing malnutrition in the proposed target area by reducing disease burden in communities as well as availing safe, potable water for use in appetite tests at nutrition sites. To achieve the overall project objective and objectives of the HRP, we will provide critical services to 120,000 individuals, including 100,000 at the village level and 20,000 (non-double counted) beneficiaries in targeted Nutrition Sites and SCs. These 4 main activities include: 1) Providing timely, equitable access to safe and sufficient water to vulnerable and affected women, men, girls and boys. 2) Enabling vulnerable and affected populations to practice safe, sanitary and hygienic living through secure, dignified and gender-appropriate sanitation services (household and site level latrine construction). 3) Providing a WaSH minimum package of interventions, adapted to the specificities of the related outbreaks, at targeted nutrition sites and catchment areas. 4) Increasing knowledge of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WaSH-related diseases. ACF will implement the above in the catchment areas of its 36 nutrition facilities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states. Baseline KAP surveys will be conducted in all target areas to identify the WaSH-related knowledge, attitude and practices of the communities. Detailed needs assessments will be conducted to assess community access to safe water sources and sanitation facilities. The implementation strategy will align with the needs identified in assessments and KAP surveys at project start. Additionally, the ACF multisector emergency response throughout the country will include a WaSH component to complement its nutrition work. The proposed program strategy takes into account specific gender-related needs during surveys and activity implementation to ensure the equitable participation of all gender and age groups.

project_name: Strengthening Accountability for GBV and Enhancing Gender Mainstreaming in Multi-sector Emergency Programs in South Sudan
project_objective: South Sudan continues to face extremely high prevalence of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), driven by a rigidly patriarchal system and historic marginalization of women. It is imperative that humanitarian interventions are sensitive to this reality, given that they may both cause and exacerbate the incidence of GBV cases. As such, Action Against Hunger proposes to: a) continue its efforts to mainstream GBV and gender considerations in its programs, and b) support the humanitarian community in South Sudan to remain accountable for GBV and gender-sensitivity. We will additionally expand our work on GBV mainstreaming in nutrition to WaSH programs, capitalize on achievements made in 2019 and support the WaSH Cluster and other interested clusters. In 2020, the organization will conduct Gender Analyses in all of our areas of intervention to evaluate programmatic changes initiated by their previous iterations (e.g. Men Group Discussions) and continue to monitor gender dynamics and protection risks on the ground. Other actors will also benefit from this analysis (and they can be done upon request from specific partners). In collaboration with relevant clusters, we will continue to conduct semi-annual Safety Audits primarily for nutrition / health / WaSH services, to assess protection concerns and enable improvements. Through sensitization of men and boys, and engagement of men caregivers on a dialogue on protection issues in Men Group Discussions, the project will tackle gender stereotypes and some of the root causes of gender inequality. These discussions will also facilitate an enabling environment for women’s access to basic services. In 2020, Action Against Hunger will continue to train all staff at community, site, and base levels on recognizing forms of GBV and strengthening awareness on existing referral mechanisms, in addition to Psychological First Aid. This is especially important as our staff are actively solicited for counselling on GBV cases that are reported at nutrition sites. The project will directly capacity-build 753 individuals and directly benefit 16,000 persons (75% women). Working with other partners through respective clusters, and leveraging our participation in the GBV sub-cluster, we will amplify this impact. Due to the project’s focus on mitigating risks for the beneficiaries of Action Against Hunger’s programs in South Sudan, 223,616 individuals will benefit indirectly from project results, by receiving more appropriate and accountable humanitarian services.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood: Emergency response, Recovery and  Resilience Building for the people in need in Morobo, Lainya and Wonduruba in CE: Panyikang, Baliet, Akoka, Fashoda, Manyo, Malakal, Melut and Canal in GUN.
project_objective:
In line with strategic cluster objectives 2: CLO2 Enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop seeds and fishing and livestock support and objective 3, SO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks; RuCAPD seeks to help the populations in Panyikang , Manyo, Fashoda, Baliet, Akoka, Malakal and Melut in Upper Nile state, Juba(Wonduruba), Lainya and Morobo in Central Equatorial as well as Canal Pigi in Jonglei state move through recovery and resilience toward development through own food production livelihood support and livestock health services. This project is designed to effectively contribute to the protection and rehabilitation of livelihoods of the most vulnerable and affected population in Greater Upper Nile and Central Equatoria States. The project is a 12-month project targeting 68,929 HH equal to 413,570 vulnerable individuals IDPs – 41,357, returnees 248,142 and host community 124,071; of whom  90,985 are Men, 95,121 are women, 111,664 are boys and 115,800 are girls. The targeting will be done with gender lens and consideration of incorporation of Accountability to affected population. We expect to train a total of 300 HH on different agronomy practices as well as 140 Community Animal Health Workers (CAWHs) for the livestock aspect of the project. Vouchers will be used in the seed fair project sites. The beneficiaries will use them to get the seeds they want and the traders will then redeem them for cash. The program implementation will ensure that Do No Harm principle is adhered to as transparency and accountability to the affected population is placed right at the centre of beneficiary targeting and provision of support. RuCAPD extensive presence and history in Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Jonglei coupled with an in-depth understanding of the community conflict dynamics and context tailored approaches to specific communities will help identify, analyze and manage risks as well as reduce any potential negative impacts of the project and any protection issues.
The project will receive pipeline supplies from FAO whilst the requested funding from SSHF will be used to provide front line services. The project will use direct distribution to the targeted groups through a transparent process of identification and distribution. In case of security hitches, RuCAPD has extensive network of how to reach the targeted beneficiaries.

project_name: Community Aid for Fisheries and Agriculture Development Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) new interventions (DL) in Uror (Jonglei), Nyirol (Jonglei), Lafon (Eastern Equatoria)
project_objective:
Description of intervention: The interventions are aligned to the novel COVID 19 pandemic and the threat of the second wave of desert locust destruction of crops later in the year. The project is aimed to stop/prevent the spread of the corona virus during distribution, mobilization and sensitization through provision of handwashing facilities, soap/detergent/sanitizers, provision of IEC materials and messaging from the RCCE TWG including banners, fliers and printed clothing (tshirts, caps and khangas). To minimize the crowding during disctribution of the inputs measures like allocating not more than 100 persons  at any given time on the distribution point, delivering the inputs directly to the bomas, extention of the days for distributions.  Where condition permits, protection mainstreaming will be done with focus on People with Special Needs particularly elderly, chronic sick and those with underlying health issues by distributions being made directly to their homes. In cognisant of the effects of COVID 19 effects on flow of goods, emerging vulnerabilities in IPC 2 & 3 HHs due to their dependence on markets for food purhcases, scaled up to support these households in especially peri-urban locations in Uror County.
PRP Pillar: 
Geographical coverage: Uror (Jonglei), Nyirol (Jonglei), Lafon (Eastern Equatoria)
Activity: 1) Reducing pest and crop disease including Desert locust surveillance, detection, prevention & eradication 
2) Reduction in post-harvest losses and introduction of appropriate technologies
3) COVID messaging and use of IEC materials: # of women, men, girls and boys reached by hygiene promotion messages for risk communication and Covid-19 prevention , Total estimated beneficiaries = 5000

project_name: Provision of Intergrated Emergency Shelter and Non Food Items Assistance targeting New IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities living in (Duk, Pibor,Akobo, Nyirol, Pochalla .Yirol East and Yirol West Counties) of Jonglei and Lakes States
project_objective: CIDO intends to deliver static life-saving integrated S/NFI activities targeting male and female returnees, IDPs and host communities in 5 Counties of Jonglei State and 2 counties of Lakes State within a span of one calendar year.The counties targeted are (Nyirol, Pibor,Pochalla,  Duk and Akobo) of Jonglei State and (Yirol West and Yirol East) of Lakes State. The total number of beneficiaries, men, women, boys and girls targeted by the project are 20,000 approximately 3,500 HHs  the mainly composed of new IDPS, the Returnees and 5% of host community.Specifically CIDO will reach the target using in-kind and CBI modalities ; 16 000 individuals will be reached with GIK and 4000 with CBI. The project will be guided by international standards such as IASC and CERF life saving criteria and S/NFI cluster strategy. The main goal of the project is to increase access to S/NFI items, promote resilience of the new and most vulnerable returnees, host communities, and IDPs through integrated service delivery and engaging affected population in discussions for durable solutions building on existing skills and resources. The proposed activities will be implemented   in synergy / joint mission with other S/NFI partners on the ground like ADA, ,Medair, Plan International PAH, LWF and HDC who are operating as static and mobile partners in Duk,Pochalla,Nyirol, Akobo, Pibor, Yirol West and Yirol East Counties, Additionally CIDO will work closely with Jonglei and Lakes  State Focal Persons (SFP’s) all through the project life to avoid duplication and maximize the use of scarce resources. CIDO’s team will focus on inclusivity of female headed households, persons with special needs, unaccompanied elderly, people with no links to the community, separated children, women at risk (pregnant and lactating mothers), child-headed HH, people living with disability assessed and verified to be in need .CIDO will promote sustainability and durable solutions through coordination with other partners and multi sector integration of protection,WASH, Nutrition, CCM and FSL,  CIDO will deliver CBI in coordination with the cluster Cash working Group and cash leading Organizations like, PAH, LWF and ADA. The cash component will be determined by the outcome of market assessments and will be coordinated well with FSL partners implementing cash programming in the proposed counties. S/NFI cluster coordination team both at national and state level will be fully engaged to support the interventions right from assessments, verification, distribution and PDM. CIDO will use clear and useful  Complaint Response\Feedback (CRFM) desk which will be established and made operational right from the initial Phase of the analysis all through the beneficiaries identification, registration ,ditribution and during PDM as it  will play a key role in resolving beneficiaries’ queries, complaints and compliments in a proactive manner while providing critical information on CBI like transfer value, vendors SOPs, code of conduct and PSEA documents. This will be useful to CIDO’s M&E team as well as provide lessons learnt to be shared with multi-sector partners, cluster and ICWG. CIDO will adhere to the AAP principles both in all the Counties and the respective locations all through the project life span While embracing the policy of Community Communication and Engagement (CCE) and ensuring that communities access clear and useful information to promote positive coping mechanisms and entrench resilience.Additionally CIDO will give support to returnees in understanding their HLP rights. CIDO will make the necessary interventions and consultations with local authorities on the use of the land before NFI distribution.  In addition, CIDO will work hand in hand with HLP partners in all the counties  to mitigate its operational challenges referring to the cluster formulated laws and policies on HLP to benefit all the marginalized groups.

project_name: EMERGENCY FOOD SECURITY LIVELIHOOD WITH RESILIENCE LIGHT INTERVENTIONS TO 10000 VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS IN HIGH FOOD INSECURE AREAS IN WAU , JUR RIVER (WESTERN BAHR EL GHAZAL), TWIC (WARRAP) AND RUBKONA  ( UNITY ) STATE IN SOUTH SUDAN.
project_objective:
Cisda is proposing an Emergency and Resilience light support interventions in three major hot spots food insecure former States of  Unity, Warrap and Western Bahr- El Ghazal . The proposed project runs from January 2020 to December, 2020. .
The key objective of the project are to increase Vulnerable household access to food through support to increased food production and to reduce the level of vulnerability amongst malnourished children through linkage of  nutrition related activities to Food security activities. This linkage will involve supporting mothers of malnourished children with training and vegetable seeds for their own production; whilst at the same time linking the same households with resilience intervention such as goat, chicken restocking though another implementing partner. The project is line with HRP strategic objective 2 ( SO2) and is in support of FSL cluster objective 2 and FSL cluster objective 4

The project will target mainly IDPs and Vulnerable host population in these areas. A total of 60,000 people will be targeted in the three States. The program will be delivered through direct distributions of inputs, resilience training in improved vegetable production and vaccination with treatment  of livestocks. These activities are mainly agricultural and livestock related and they will be targeted 
Women , children, girls that are at high protection risks throughout the implementation of the project . Additionally the project has major consideration for the accountability to affected population, as it will work through Accountability to affected community  AAP committees. Feedback mechanisms will be established in the community so that beneficiaries are well informed about the project actions

CISDA has over four  years strong experience in implementing similar Emergency food security and livelihood projects in the same geographical context-.there activities has been funded by diverse donors such as FAO , SSHF and IOM. The project thus will leverage on the experiences gained during the past implementations inorder to adequately address the food insecurity problem.

The project will integrate or work closely with both the protection cluster and the nutrition cluster. With protection cluster, the project will support beneficiaries identified by the protection partner that are high protection risk. They will be mapped out and supported during implementation. With the nutrition project, the project will set up demonstration sites at OTP centers and train households with malnourished children. These households will also be supported with high nutritious vegetables which they will produce to address the nutritional needs of their malnourished children.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving Child Protection services to vulnerable and conflict-affected children in Ayod County, Jonglei State.
project_objective:
The population in Ayod State is predominantly Nuer with very few groups of individuals from other locations/tribes. Others groups include Dinka, Shiluk, Anyuak and Darfurian. They are neighbouring to Eastern Jonglei i.e. In general, the population of Jiech, Mogok and Karmoun has an estimated population of about 15 ,000-25,000 inhabitants in each county.  The children make up at least half of this population with the prevalence of young mothers as many of them are given compelled to marriage by force or lack of an alternative. 
INTERSOS has been implementing Child Protection in Ayod state since 2017 through SSHF funding until August 2019. This was in response to the protracted and dire protection needs in regards to protection. During this project INTERSOS identified and registered 240 UASCSs (107 of them female) in the CPIMS. The project also revealed that lack of exclusive CFS and PSS for children and adolescents has also contributed to levels of distress among the two sets as they are forced to use the airstrips or very limited excluded spaces that expose them to safety hazards. Inaccessibility to the remote locations such as Karmoun and Mogok makes it all the more difficult to reach these cases except by foot which is about 3 hrs and 8hrs journey respectively.
INTERSOS intends to continue addressing the Child Protection needs in  Jiech, Mogok, Karmoun Longor, Kandak, Luadiew and Gorwai. The locations were selected in view of the similar context of needs yet there are no Child Protection actors and their proximity to Jiech which serves as the most convenient hub, as all of them fall within 3-8hrs walk from Jiech.
INTERSOS aims to provide child protection to vulnerable, children affected by conflict through a holistic approach consisting of various activities. The primary activity will include lifesaving needs of children through; i) structured and comprehensive case management; and ii) PSS provision including Psychological First Aid and FTR services for girls and boys with protection needs such UASC, CAAFAG, GBV survivors, orphans and children with disability. As an additional channel for the identification of protection needs INTERSOS will also provide activities and space to provide PSS activities, conduct PFA and work with other actors such as nutrition and education partners who observe a high number of children in their activities. The intervention will also be characterized by a focus on community engagement activities such as awareness-raising and risk mitigation achieved through a strong system of Trainer of Trainers whereby INTERSOS will provide training and engage community members in specific techniques for contextualized approaches to strengthen an enabling and protective environment for children. Such trainings for the children will include positive parenting, decision making, foster care, conflict mitigation and peace building, family separation dynamics, and gender equality. INTERSOS endeavours to ensure activities are tailored to the specific gender and age of the target population as detailed in the needs analysis section
The objective of this intervention is to provide at least 800 (400 female) children with comprehensive case management support for CP and GBV and at least 11,000 (5500 female) in PSS and awareness. Past successful approaches have shown that CFS is an important part of the integrated approach of this project. Therefore, INTERSOS child protection interventions aim to reach at least 6,000 (3000 female) children through CBPSS activities, through access to 3 already existing CFS that will be refurbished for usage and establishment of 4 more in the locations not established. Other direct beneficiaries include all the community members targeted in relation to extending child protection by training adult caregivers and other community members on child protection, child rights, parenting skills, and positive discipline methods.

project_name: Integrated approach to reduce high prevalence of acute malnutrition, GBV risks and WASH related diseases in areas affected by conflict, food insecurity and flood.
project_objective:
SPEDP proposes a 12 months humanitarian response plan for the year 2020 with main focus of providing access to safe water, adequate sanitation and hygienic behaviors to mitigate and reduce high levels of malnutrition, water related diseases (ARI, AWD, cholera etc) and gender based violence (GBV) issues among the affected populations in Unity, Jonglei, Western Bhar El Ghazal and Central Equatoria States. This response plan will complement SPEDP’s ongoing health project in Guit, WASH project in Old Fangak, food security and livelihood (FSL) project in Raga and shelter and non-food items intervention in Morobo County.

The proposed intervention will reach a target of 60,000 vulnerable people (14,400men, 16,800women, 13,800boys and 15,000 girls) among internally displaced persons, returnees, and host communities including 1,500 people with disabilities. The project interventions will target 25% individuals for WASH and Nutrition, 45% individuals for WASH and Health, 20% for WASH and GBV and 10% for Access to safe water focusing on four Counties of Guit, Fangak, Raga and Morobo , however, if the emergency would raise in other prioritized Counties, we are ready to change and implement the intervention where it will be most needed. The project aims at centralizing protection to promote principled access to basic services to vulnerable groups at risk, accountability to affected people ensuring that services are delivered in a gender sensitive manner and will consider the needs of different gender and age groups, people living with disabilities, etc. Regualr meetings will be conducted with older people and people with disabilities within the community to monitor safety and access issues to inform the design of WASH facilities.  The activities will include, Construction of new water points after GBV risk analysis; rehabilitation of water points in OTPs and community level after GBV risk analysis; construction and rehabilitation of sanitation facilities in OTPs and community level after GBV risk analysis; installation of hand washing facilities to promote hand washing in order to reduce water and sanitation related diseases; engaging in cholera preparedness and response plan together with cholera task force in respective areas of intervention; hygiene promotion education through door to door visits, participatory hygiene sessions in public places for effective behavioural change; distribution of hygiene kits or household package for famine to mothers or care takers of children admitted for severe and moderate acute malnutrition (SAM/MAM) treatment at outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP)/SC. Menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits will be provided to adolescent girls and women of child bearing age accompanied with menstrual hygiene management sessions so that girls will not miss attending classes during their periods. SPEDP will ensure ownership and sustainability of the response through involvement of the targeted community throughout the life cycle of the intervention. All the WASH temporary and sustainable services will address the vital needs, public health and protection issues through an accountability to affected populations (AAP) community approach to target the acute vulnerabilities based on inter/cross-sectoral evaluations and analyses. This project will focus on the various needs of men, women, boys and girls identified through focus group discussions (FGDs) with all the sex and age groups, people with disabilities and pregnant lactating mothers incorporating gender dynamics and specific needs of different groups into needs assessment and response recommendations. Throughout the response life cycle, SPEDP team will coordinate with the authorities, community and the key partners on ground who are implementing WASH, nutrition, health, and protection for integration of activities to ensure maximum utilization of resources.

project_name: Emergency recovery and rehabilitation project for food insecure households in crisis affected counties of former Northern and Western Bahr el Ghazal States, South Sudan
project_objective:
This emergency recovery and rehabilitation food security and livelihood project is a combined response that will be implemented in a span of 12 months from January to December 2020. Main goal of the project is to strengthen food and nutrition security and resilience among food insecure insecure households of the most disadvantaged and vulnerable households in multiple counties in Northern and Western Barh el Ghazal respectively reaching 24000hh.The beneficiaries will be targeted basing on a vulnerability matrix tool to be agreed on with the stakeholders and community. 
To achieve this, the project will support the immediate nutritional needs of vulnerable HHs through the provision of cash/vouchers transfers. Using cash transfers, HHs will access suﬃcient food to meet daily caloric and nutritional requirements. This will address the immediate impacts of food insecurity, reducing the incidence of malnutrition and malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality. Transfers will be both unconditional and conditional upon the completion of work to rehabilitate and/or construct communal assets that have the potential to enhance longer term food security and livelihoods including physical assets such as dykes and community access roads, as well as natural assets. In addition to meeting basic and immediate needs, short term cash transfers will ensure HHs have the energy and time to participate in activities that enhance their ability to deal with disruption and change. By improving the availability and accessibility of these productive assets, the project will strengthen long-term food security by improving agricultural productivity, and supporting the regeneration of the natural resource base. As production increases, availability of food for consumption and/or sale increases, resulting in improved livelihoods and an increase in local, regional and national food security.
To enhance emergency food production, main season agriculture seeds & tool, ﬁshing gears and fast maturing vegetable & crop kits shall be distributed. This project will also contribute to the reduction of pest and crop disease e.g. FAW surveillance, detection, prevention & eradication and also conduct Livestock vaccination; disease prevention & treatment especially zoonotic e.g. RVF; 
Through these interventions, this project will be contributing to the FSL 2020 strategy of preventing famine and building households coping capacities by increasing food production and restoration of productive assets for more diversified livelihoods. Special attention will be given to the marginalized people like persons with disability, the elderly, chronically ill, orphans, girls and women to make sure they are not left out in the distribution of inputs); 3) basic agronomic training and extension support. Here, demonstration plots will be established at nutrition centres where beneficiaries will be taught  how to prepare nutritious food, through community-based extension workers; SPEDP will also use a community based participatory approach where beneficiary identification and registration process will involve community members.
Project management committees will be established and will take an active role in the beneficiary selection, monitoring implementation and also handling complaints and feedback mechanisms and monitoring of the project. Stakeholders will be invited during the launch and all project details will be shared to foster accountability to the affected populations.
SPEDP will strive to integrate with other projects like health, WASH and nutrition through passive referrals and also establishment of demonstration plots at nutrition sites.
SPEDPs added value is that the organization has an already established presence in NBeG and WBeG since 2013 to date has implemented a number of projects since them in different thematic areas. SPEDP is currently implementing FSL SA2 project in Raja, FOA-SAFER Project in Aweil Center and North and so is familiar with the local settings.

project_name: Provision of Food Security and Livelihoods Support Among Vulnerable Populations in Jonglei and Central Equatoria States
project_objective:
Extreme levels of acute food insecurity are projected to persist in Central Equatoria and Jonglei  due to bureaucratic impediments, operational interference and access constraints attributed to insecurity and cases of Gender Based Violence along major roads; with humanitarian agencies facing challenges to reach displaced and vulnerable people. Extreme food insecurity is projected to continue through 2020 with IPC Phase 3 or worse projections (IPC Sept 2019; FSNMS, 2019). A large number of returnees including displaced populations reported lack of food, seeds, tools, shelter among other basic life support amenities (IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, April 2019; OCHA South Sudan Situation Reports, 2019).

Stop Poverty Communal Initiative (SPOCI) aims to provide and support emergency food security and livelihoods via emergency provision of crop, fishing and vegetable livelihood kits that will provide immediate and short terms access to food and incomes among targeted  households.

SPOCI is a national NGO with over 5 years programmatic presence in Greater Equatoria and Jonglei and has in addition currently implementing SSHF and UNICEF funded projects in these regions. SPOCI is a member of National NGOs Steering Committee, member of the ICWG and Accountability to Affected Populations Technical Working Group and Monitoring and Evaluation Working Group. In addition, SPOCI has for the past five years supported over 55,000 vulnerable populations with WASH/ Education /FSL interventions through UNICEF, SSHF among other partners support in Jonglei and Equatorias. Through these, the organization has fostered strong linkages with communities, state/county line ministries of Livestock and Fisheries, Agriculture. This is in addition to strong and competent team including staff redeployment to scale up interventions based on needs.

Proposed activities will enable children (boys and girls), youth, men and women including people with special needs recover have improved and diversified access to food, incomes and improved livelihoods in addition to strengthening community capacities to coping with threats. Targeted beneficiaries will be consulted and involved in implementation of the project including monitoring and evaluation; while taking into consideration Accountability of Affected Populations, Gender Equity, Protection concerns including GBV and sound environmentally friendly approaches and do no harm ethos.

Activities will ensure delivering a package of integrated activities through linkages with other sectors and complementing programs in WASH, Education, Health, Protection to address the high level of food insecurity and malnutrition, by targeting SAM/MAM children and their families; coordinate Relief and Rehabilitation Commission other NGO partners. SPOCI will further integrate the project with other Health-related priorities such as Ebola Task force, WASH, acknowledging that poor WASH services are a key driver to poor health, and ultimately resulting in high malnutrition. This is in addition to regular assessments to mitigate GBV risks including sexual exploitation and abuse.

project_name: Improving Access to Quality Health Services Focusing on Major Causes of Morbidity in Nasir, Ulang, Maiwut, Akobo, Longechuk, Tonj North and Gogrial East Counties; Jonglei, Upper Nile, & Warrap States
project_objective:
Improving Access To Quality Health Services Focusing on Major Causes of Morbidity in Nasir, Ulang, Maiwut, Akobo, Longechuk, Tonj North and Gogrial East project seeks to improve access to integrated emergency primary and secondary health care including management of victims of Sexual Gender-Based Violence (SGBV). The project targets 25,000 (12,950 women:12,050 men) people in need with a total cash value of $1.5 million. Of the 25,000 people; 8,000, 7000, and 10,000 people will be IDPs, returnees and host communities respectively.
The project will support the provision of Basic Package of Health and Nutrition services through a network of 12 PHCUs, 7 PHCCs, 1 Hospital, and 8 mobile clinics in hard to reach locations. The Project interventions will focus on prevention and case management of epidemic-prone diseases such as malaria, pneumonia, acute watery diarrhea, cholera, and measles through both static and outreach services; provision of essential medicines and medical supplies; capacity building of staffs through on-job and classroom training; disease surveillance,  and routine monitoring of health information through strengthening the DHIS2 system. 
The clinical package will include; Health education and promotion, curative outpatient and inpatient services, routine immunization including supplementary immunization activities focusing on measles and polio, Maternal Newborn and Child Health Services (MNCH), and HIV/TB services including e-MTCT. The project will integrate Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) at PHCCs and Hospital, management of severe cases of malnutrition with medical complication at the stabilization centers, identiﬁcation, and referral for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), and Water Hygiene and Sanitation (WASH) at the health facilities.
The project aims at; Improving access and scaling-up responsiveness to integrated essential healthcare needs of the vulnerable populations focusing on major causes of morbidity and mortality; Preventing, detecting and responding to epidemic-prone disease outbreaks; Increasing access to essential clinical health services among vulnerable populations targeting SGBV, and SAM with Medical Complication; and Improving resilience among vulnerable populations by increasing access to mental health and psychosocial support services.
This project is a result of community needs assessments, cluster prioritization strategy, and consultations with the communities in the targeted locations that indicate a dire need for emergency health services for women, girls, men, and boys.

project_name: Addressing widespread severe WASH needs of IDPs, vulnerable host communities and returnees through an integrated response in Health, Nutrition and GBV in Pariang, Panyijar, Guit, Yirol East, Fashoda and Panyikang Counties.
project_objective: UNIDOR is presently, in collaboration with national, state line ministries/counterparts, local government and other humanitarian NGOs, complimenting humanitarian response to critical WASH needs of conflict affected IDPs, vulnerable host communities, returnees in 6 counties: Pariang, Rubkona, Koch, Mayendit, Leer and Panyijar of Unity State. Training of WASH management committees, Community hygiene/health promoters etc. is ongoing in those counties and to be followed by major rehabilitation and solarizing of deep-boreholes, targeting concentrated returnees’ locations that are experiencing water stress, to commence in early November 2019. And through its combined 7 multi-sectoral programmes, Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection, Food Security and livelihood (FSL), Education and Peacebuilding and Conflict Mitigation, UNIDOR at present operates through integration  approach in 10 counties: Pariang, Rubkona, Koch, Mayendit, Leer and Panyijar of Unity State; Cueibet and Yerol East of Lakes State;  Jur River of Western Bahr el Ghazal State and Gogrial East of Warrap State, South Sudan. As a long time HRP partner, UNIDOR is compelled by widespread severe WASH situation in 6 counties of 2020 HRP WASH Cluster priority, namely Guit, Pariang and Panyijar in Unity State; Yirol East in Lakes State and Fashoda and Panyikang in Upper Nile State. UNIDOR intends to address the WASH needs through an integrated response in health, nutrition and GBV in those 6 counties where WASH needs are extremely demanding. In Guit County, UNIDOR will, in collaboration with nutrition partners on ground address WASH needs in an integrated approach in nutrition and will easily access the selected project locations/Payams from Bentiu/Rubkona where UNIDOR has a strong presence/field office and with WASH activities being implemented in neighboring Rubkona county. UNIDOR is already on ground in both Pariang and Panyjar counties, scaling up water, sanitation and hygiene needs through an integrated approach in nutrition and GBV targeting IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities. UNIDOR will continue addressing the WASH needs in both counties of Pariang and Panyijar if considered for funding in the next round. In Fashoda and Panyikang Counties, UNIDOR will compliment in the mitigation of WASH-related gender-based violence in an integrated approach with GBV partners on ground, targeting women and girls at risk/in need of core GBV services. In Yirol East County, UNIDOR will integrate WASH in health to address the acute WASH needs and to control water related disease outbreaks, in collaboration with state line ministries and government counterparts as well as other implementing partners on ground. Yirol East will be accessed from Yirol West where UNIDOR has presence on ground addressing nutrition needs. This project will address the vital WASH needs, public health and protection issues through an AAP community approach to target the acute vulnerabilities based on inter/cross-sectoral evaluations and analyses. It will provide timely/sustainable, equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for conflicted affected IDPs, vulnerable host communities and returnees in Guit, Fashod, Panyikang and Yerol East Counties, where UNIDOR is expanding, through rehabilitation of existing handpumps and institutional gender disaggregated latrines and knowledge on key hygiene promotion messages that promote good hygiene practices. The project will also complement the integrated approach of scaling up water, sanitation and hygiene needs in nutrition and GBV targeting IDPs, returnees and vulnerable hosts in Pariang and Panyijar counties where UNIDOR is currently scaling up water, sanitation and hygiene needs in nutrition and GBV targeting IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through an integrated approach.

project_name: Integrated Lifesaving Shelter and NFI response to vulnerable populations in Warrap (Tonj North & Tonj East) and Lakes (Rumbek East, Rumbek  North, Yirol East, Yirol West, Cueibet, Rumbek Center, Wulu and Awerial)
project_objective:
This proposed project will address emergency shelter and non-food items needs of conflict affected vulnerable populations both displaced and in secondary displacement. The project will target 5000 HHs or 30,000 individuals both IDPs and host communities, disaggregated as follows (Men 3,600, Women 7,200, Boys 8,400 and Girls 10,800) for emergency shelter and NFIs activities response in Warrap (Tonj North and East) and Lakes (Rumbek East, Rumbek North, Rumbek Center, Cueibet, Wulu, Yirol East, Yirol West and Awerial) most vulnerable populations in need (after an assessment). About 56% of the target population will receive Gift In-Kind assistance which will be prepositioned from the Cluster Core Pipeline.  After assessment has been done, and an analysis report submitted through the SFP to the Cluster at the National level, a pipeline request will be submitted. After an approval, items will be transported to respective CCOSS storage facilities and subsequent distributions. CCOSS will coordinate with other cluster partners in respective locations for effective response. 

Despite the advent of the revitalized peace agreement and the promise of better times to come, the cumulative effects of the conflict have translated to sustained poverty and persistent humanitarian and protection needs for more than 7 million people in South Sudan. Warrap and Lakes states have continued to remain one of the most difficult locations especially for humanitarian agencies to operate. This is due to drivers and multipliers of crisis have remained present over time. These include insecurity and violence, local and inter-communal violence (IVC), ongoing displacement, sparse basic services, disease, climate shocks, flooding, economic instability and insecure access to food and livelihoods. Some places such as Yirol East have been categorized under Catastrophe IPC 5, making communities here more susceptible to famine. 

CCOSS will also ensure that there is proper coordination especially in locations where there is more than one implementing partner. County cluster meetings will be held weekly to ensure proper coordination, to avoid double counting and as well reduce duplication of efforts. CCOSS is a key member of other clusters working within the same locality. 

CCOSS will use humanitarian hubs for coordination meetings and other related humanitarian activities. CCOSS will be working with other partners who are operating in the same areas or locations on the issues affecting vulnerable populations in hard to reached areas through mobile response in collaboration with other partners on the ground. CCOSS will also work with other partners on area based approaches through open forum during cluster meetings where partners would highlight activities being implemented and locations of operation to avoid duplication activities. This would be achieved through coordination of the cluster and support of CCCM, coordinating the activities of partners to avoid overlaps of same activities in one location.   

General Operation & other direct costs include costs associated with providing direct management & other support functions at the Main office in Juba. This includes management staff salaries, communication, stationary, rents etc. The Indirect project costs include bank charges, staff recruitment & servicing costs, auditing and consultancy costs.

project_name: Information management and assessment support for evidence-based humanitarian aid planning and delivery in Ukraine
project_objective:
The project will contribute to improved aid coordination and delivery (both humanitarian and longer-term recovery planning). To continue informing the humanitarian programming cycle with field evidence, REACH will provide information management and assessment support to the humanitarian coordination architecture. Capitalizing on the work implemented in 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2019, REACH will provide the inter cluster coordination group and humanitarian partners with support for multi-sector needs assessment analyzing gender, ability and age disaggregated data in both government and non-government controlled areas, in addition to continuing the provision of ad hoc information management technical expertise.
Initial findings from the Humanitarian Trend Analysis 2019 indicate a downward trend in the frequency of security related incidents and conflict related civilian casualties in 2019, most likely linked to increased political engagement between Ukraine and the Russian Federation. Overall indicators in the target areas showed slight improvements compared to 2018. The proportion of HHs reporting shelling as a protection concerns in the 5km area dropped from 86% to 60% and the proportion of HHs that are severely or moderately food insecure in the same geography went from 13% to 9%. However, some areas are showing continued deterioration as in 2018, specifically healthcare where the proportion of HHs reporting challenges in accessing health facilities increased from 43% to 54%. These overall trends did not change the geographic difference found in previous years. Using a multi-sector needs indicator inspired from the Joint Interagency Assessment Group, the proportion of HHs in need in rural areas within 5km of the contact line was close to 2 times higher than those in urban areas further away (44% vs 23%).  It is crucial that timely and accurate information about the severity of these needs continue to be made available to aid actors. 
In line with commitments from the Grand Bargain, the Ukraine humanitarian community with support from REACH has been able to rely on ‘Improved joint and impartial needs assessments’ to develop the humanitarian needs overview and humanitarian response: to further increase the localization of assistance REACH will continue to strengthen local level capacities in information management and Geographic Information Systems through its ‘IM_HUB’ which is run out of three technical centers in Slovyansk, Severodonetsk and Mariupol.
In line with Accountability to Affected Populations commitments, REACH will also collect data on the knowledge about/availability of complaints and response mechanisms in conflict-affected areas where aid actors operate, and maintain its efforts to ensure survey participants can raise complaints to an anonymous hotline with the phone number distributed after all surveys.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Provision of integrated approach service for preventing and responding to child rights violations and gender based violence (GBV) for the displaced persons and most vulnerable host communities in Benadir and  Lower Shabelle Region
project_objective:
Droughts and regular conflicts in have increased protection concerns especially for displaced populations on transit routes, in areas of displacement and newly accessible areas. Analysis of SOYDA registrations of separated, unaccompanied and missing children peaked during conflict and flooding displacement periods throughout 2018 and 2019; this puts boys at higher risk of recruitment into armed groups, as well as potentially perpetrators of sexual violence. Furthermore, the South West Sate Child Protection Working Group (CPWG) analysis indicates that the mostly common coping strategy adopted for Unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) is through the kafala/traditional foster care system; this is especially true for girls who are often ""hidden UASC"" and hence at risk of exploitation and other forms of abuse. Most of the people perceive that sexual violence had increased since the last offensive and that girls are most commonly stressed by this risk. Analysis of South Central Gender based violence information management systems (GBVIMS) trend analysis (Jan 2018-Sep 2019 ) shows that 42% of cases were rape and sexual assault and 44% physical assault with the majority of survivors being IDPs (83%) and female

The objective of this intervention is to strengthen case management through direct service provision to unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), children at risk of protection violations and referral services for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV). This includes providing training and mentoring to the CP and GBV staffs of SOYDA including CPiE especially targeting in Daynile, Dharkenley, Kahda   districts of Mogadishu, and Afgoye and Marka district of lower shabelle IDP camps. The project aims to provide immediate lifesaving assistance to vulnerable populations. Beneficiaries will receive comprehensive case management and psycho-social support (PSS), including emergency care, referral to SOYDA medical teams trained in clinical management of rape (CMR), access tailored material assistance, basic emotional support, and follow up on the services. Capacity building of CP community structures and committees to strengthen and improve identification of cases. The key focus will be to scale up prevention and response to separation of children from their families through family tracing and reunification activities and gender based violence survivors.

The project will establish referral system in schools and support community-based Child Protection Mechanisms for quick and efficient referrals of children with protection needs through service mapping within the community and in the schools (community child protection committees and School Management Committees). This project will strengthen service mapping to facilitate appropriate referrals, coordination and linkages in service delivery to ensure quality comprehensive services to unaccompanied and separated children and gender based violence (GBV) survivors

In addition,  in Daynile, Dharkenley, Kahda  districts of Mogadishu, and Afgoye and  Marka district of lower shabelle. Region, SOYDA will conduct and strengthen protection monitoring in areas of settlement of returnees and IDPs through community based protection monitors working with CSOs in order to ensure that quality evidence based reports about protection issues and human rights violations and systematic collection of protection related data are produced to inform better response and advocacy.

project_name: Provision of integrated essential Health Services for vulnerable and under served populations in Aweil East, Panyijar, and Koch counties
project_objective:
South Sudan has been afflicted by protracted conflict, emergent crises, and harsh environmental conditions notably seasonal flooding. These have contributed to weakening of the health system over the years resulting in reduced access to and utilization of quality primary health care services. South Sudan has some of the worst indicators globally including a maternal mortality rate of 789 per 100,000 live births. The most vulnerable groups in the society including women and girls, children under five years of age, people living with disability (PWDs), mental health illness, and the elderly among other vulnerable groups continue to be among the most affected. The proposed project targets 17,247 (8,968 F; 8,279 M) people in need as follows; 10,845 (5,639 F; 5,205 M) in Aweil East County, 1,594 (829 F; 765 M) in Koch County and 4,809 (2,501 F; 2,308 M) in Panyijar County. This will be inclusive of 5,174 IDPs spread out as follows in Aweil East County (20%), Koch County (8%) and Panyijar County (72%) and 1,897 IDP returnees as follows in Aweil East County (2.6%), Koch County (72%) and Panyijar County (25.4%).
The proposed project will target 2 static health facilities in Aweil East; Majokaken PHCU and Malualdit PHCU. In Koch, the project will target Patit PHCU and in Panyijar County, the project will operate 1 mobile health team which will offer gap filling services in villages which are cut off from essential health services by seasonal flooding and the swamps. In Nyal Payam, Panyijar County the IRC will run one Stabilisation Center based at the Nyal PHCC which will serve as a referral nutrition facility for the County. The SC will support the continuum of care for children under 5 diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition with medical complications before discharging them to outpatient treatment facilities. IRC will leverage on existing linkages to support clients accessing services in supported health facilities to reduce missed opportunities and ensure holistic care. Referral for tertiary level health care will be supported using existing referral pathways through the County Health Departments. Vunerable populations including unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) will be linked to existing IRC child protection programs.
The IRC through recruitment of qualified health workers in particular to support maternal and health services will result in improved maternal and child health outcomes. The IRC will integrate and strengthen the prevention of mother to child transmission PMTCT of HIV/AIDS and screening of pregnant mothers of Syphilis during Antenatal visits. All complicated new cases identified will be referred for appropriate care at the PHCC. The project will leverage on existing IRC projects in the counties covered to provide integrated holistic care for vulnerable populations including women and girls. Children screened positive for acute malnutrition will be referred to IRC static and mobile nutrition sites for continuity of care whereas women and girls will be subjected to a voluntary GBV screening at the consultation clinics and referred to the nearest GBV one stop center for psychosocial support and other services. 
The support will further include training staff on IDSR, EWARS, IPC, Disability inclusion in health care and CCSAS training to ensure quality health services are provided. The project will support the procurement of drugs and medical supplies inclusive of psychotropic drugs for the treatment of mental health disorders. Regular supportive supervision will ensure quality of care is maintained by conducting regular QOC assessments. The proposed project will conduct a rapid WASH assessment of supported health facilities and through consultation with key stakeholders including the health committees, the project will seek to rehabilitate solid waste management facilities. Medical waste generated will be disposed according to internationally acceptable standards.

project_name: An Integrated Emergency Nutrition Response for Vulnerable Populations in Aweil East, Aweil South, Panyijiar, and Rumbek East Counties
project_objective: This proposed response plan will focus on addressing the nutritional needs of the most vulnerable groups of the population in Aweil East, Aweil South Rumbek east and Panyijiar especially U5s and PLWs. The IRC will implement the proposed emergency response in 2020 for 12 months  through strengthening the existing 68 static nutrition sites (65 OTPs and three Stabilization Centers), and by deploying six mobile teams in hard-to-reach areas (two in Aweil East , two in Panyijar  and two in Aweil South) to improve the nutrition response coverage through rapid response mechanism. IRC has field offices located in Aweil East, Aweil South, Panyijar, Rumbek and Pamir and has longstanding relationships with the government, local authorities, and communities in these geographic areas. Furthermore, IRC provides health and nutrition programming in each of these states(Unity and NBEG), offering a foundation upon which to build strengthened nutrition service. This project will address life-saving humanitarian needs in Aweil East, Aweil South and Panyijar Counties, which are some of the counties with chronically high GAM rates of above the WHO emergency threshold. In Panyijiar County, GAM levels have consistently been above 15% as a result of insecurity and influx of IDPs from Leer and Mayendit counties as aggravating factors. In Rumbek East, IRC has scaled up the nutrition response from 3 to 23 OTP and the coverage of services increased the number of acute malnutrition enrolled in the nutrition program. The deteriorating food security in Rumbek east will continue aggravating the nutrition situation in the county. The project will integrate the health, child protection, WASH and food security sectors supported by UNICEF, WFP, OFDA, and HPF in the counties. The main components of this project are 4 and they include;1) Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) among children under five years of age; 2) Management of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five years of age; 3) Management of malnutrition among Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW); 4) Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergency (IYCFE).  Treatment will directly target children under 5 years of age (without discrimination between boys and girls) and PLWs. IRC will reach a total of 21, 611 (AE: 7,353, AS: 4,748, RE: 5,305, Pany: 4,205) SAM children; and 41,155 (AE:13,933, AS: 7,571, RE: 7,064, Pany: 12,587) under-five and 1,4704 (AE: 4,678, AS: 2,590, RE: 5,467, Pany: 1,970) PLW with MAM. Similarly, IRC plans to reach a total of 39,843 (AE: 12,315, AS: 2,1309, RE: 13,629 , Pany: 7130) primary caretakers of 0-23 months old children through MIYC and 140, 589 (AE: 66,005, AS: 4,748, RE: 38,488, Pany: 14,788 ) children 6-59 months though vitamin A supplementation. The project will work along with the health sector through a collaborative approach to ensure stabilization kits for SAM with medical complications are provided. Nutrition Cluster partners will provide malaria screening and referral/treatment for SAM and MAM cases. Through layering and collaboration of activities, the WASH Cluster will support partners in the county to ensure the provision of clean and safe water for OTP/TSFP services, including appetite tests, hand washing, and appropriate ablution facilities. FSL Cluster partners in the county shall conduct general food distribution sessions that target households with SAM and MAM beneficiaries. Throughout the project cycle, community outreach and mobilization will be conducted to ensure early detection and improved coverage of the nutrition services in the targeted areas by the mobile and outreach teams.

project_name: Up-scaling and strengthening Community Based Structures to provide lifesaving Comprehensive Child Protection services to UASC and other at risk children/families in former Lakes, Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Upper Nile States
project_objective:
Years of conflict, displacement and underdevelopment have limited people’s livelihood opportunities, marginalized women’s formal employment opportunities, and weakened families’ ability to cope with the protracted crisis and sudden shocks, like the death leading to psycho-social distress and mental health conditions. Five years of the most recent conflict has forced nearly 4.2 million people to flee their homes in search of safety, nearly 2 million of them within and 2.2 million outside the country. While the intensity of conflict may have reduced recently, and clashes contained to certain regions, vulnerable children and families will continue to experience the impacts of the conflict through 2019 and beyond. United Nations reports indicate that all parties to the conflict have repeatedly violated international humanitarian law and perpetrated serious human rights abuses, including gang rape, abductions, sexual slavery of women and girls, and recruitment of children, both girls and boys. People affected by the conflict, including the more than 300,000 refugees in South Sudan, repeatedly identify security among their primary needs (HNO 2019).

Approximately 61% of the affected population are children, of which 1.9 million boys and girls face acute and severe protection risks. Boys and girls continue to be exposed to threats of recruitment, psycho-social distress, family separation, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and sexual and physical violence. Since 2013, over 100,000 children in South Sudan have been affected by 3,500 verified Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism incidents, of which killing and maiming accounted for 12%; denial of humanitarian access 10%; rape and other grave sexual violence accounted for 8%; abduction 8 %; and attacks on schools and hospitals 7%. Over 20,000 children are estimated to have been recruited to armed forces and armed groups and more than 1 million children have been affected by psycho-social distress and at risk of developing mental health conditions. Needs remain high particularly in former Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Lakes states which are also locations prioritized in this project. Among the IDP population, women and children more vulnerable due to gender roles and dynamics in the communities and the protection risks and further affecting the protective environment of children and support networks (HNO 2019).

In response to the above needs, Save the Children will support the most vulnerable children and their families with the provision of comprehensive case management services to 4,000 affected children (boys: 2,120, girls: 1,880); provision of resilience building psycho-social support (PSS) activities to 22,151 beneficiaries (boys: 9,200, girls: 12,951); community mobilization and engagement; training and facilitation of community based structures to develop and implement child protection community action plans; structured awareness and sensitization on child protection and cross cutting issues to 47,200 people (boys: 10,624, girls: 11,876, men: 11,754, women: 12,946); advocacy and mainstreaming child protection in other sectors in line with CPSC, revised CPMS standards and IASC Centrality of Protection principles among other key quality standards.  The project will be implemented in Jonglei (Bor South, Akobo and Nyirol), Eastern Equatoria (Kapoeta East, South & North, Magwi and Lafon) Lakes (Rumbek Centre and Rumbek East) and Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil East) States, building on SCI's long-term presence and ongoing programs in these areas. 

The proposed activities will contribute to CO1: Ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialized services through an integrated approach among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach areas;CO2: Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced  resilience  and CP Objective 3: Strengthen the capacity and resilience of children and community mechanism.

project_name: Provision of essential primary health care services to people in need in Central Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, Jonglei and Warrap States
project_objective:
Save the Children proposes to support primary and community health care services, including the prevention and control of epidemic prone diseases in vulnerable communities in Central Equatoria (Yei, Morobo and Lainya), Eastern Equatoria (Kapoeta North, Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Budi, Lafon and Torit),  Jonglei (Akobo and Nyirol) and Warrap states (Twic and Abyei) tomeet the following objectives:

1.	Reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic prone diseases.  
2.	Improve access and scale-up response to integrated quality essential health care services to vulnerable populations. 
3.	Increase access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled and mental health disorders. 

Save the Children will respond to the most urgent needs of the beneficiaries, including emergency clinical service provision, community health care and maternity (supporting FP services, SGBV, ANC, PNC, normal delivery, BEMONC services and newborn care), health and protection services to support MHPSS services, WASH in health facilities, outbreak investigation and response for epidemic prone diseases and the provision of essential medical supplies.

The proposed activities contribute to CO1: Reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic prone diseases, CO2: Improve timely access and scale-up response to integrated quality essential health care services to vulnerable populations and CO3: Increase access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled, mental health disorders and monitoring health insecurities. With an overall financial requirement of $2.5 Million, Save the Children intends to provide essential health care services to 41,667 beneficiaries.

project_name: Lifesaving Nutrition Response in Eastern Equatoria,Jonglei and Warrap states in  South Sudan
project_objective:
Save the Children International (SCI) in South Sudan proposes this lifesaving nutrition project in contribution to the reduction of morbidity and overall mortality of children under-five and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) due to acute malnutrition in Eastern Equatoria, Jonglei and Warrap states in South Sudan. SCI will provide timely and quality management of acute malnutrition and Mother, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) services embedded in CMAM program. The program will reach a total of 15,961 U-5 SAM, 37584 U-5 MAM, 31,388 MAM PLW, BSFP 27765, BSFP PLW 13,212 acute malnourished beneﬁciaries through management of acute malnutrition and MIYCN interventions integrated with ongoing health, WASH, FSL and child protection interventions. 
The response will be focusing to achieve the result of Children and PLW screened end detected and referred to appropriate nutrition centers. This will be done through active case ﬁnding using CNV/HHP, provision of acute managements of nutrition service through   OTP and TSFP static sites supplemented by RRM and mobile team to the area where service is not accessible.
This project will complement the nutrition cluster response objectives through implementation of emergency nutrition program mainly using four main intervention strategies contribute to decreasing suffering, morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable populations in South Sudan to; 

1) increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific service delivery for children, adolescents and women in prioritized but more specifically in Eastern Equatoria, Jonglei and Warrap states 

11) increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and pregnant and lactating women affected by acute malnutrition in prioritized by the Cluster and Save the Children 

111) To increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and joint programming targeting vulnerable groups in prioritized locations by the Cluster and Save the Children.

 1V) To strengthen nutrition information system for evidence-based nutrition response by the end of 2020.

project_name: Livelihood based emergency responses to food insecure communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
Save the Children proposes this livelihood based emergency project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in eight counties, which are known for track records of severe food insecurity and malnutrition in three States in South Sudan. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, therefore improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks. The project targets primarily conflict affected children and their families in the internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and host communities.

The key interventions proposed through this action are food assistances (conditional general food distributions, food for assets), cash/voucher assistances, agricultural inputs provisions and productions with training packages on improved agronomic practices, and livestock vaccinations and treatment against diseases greatest economic importance. The livelihoods support will help target beneficiaries in meeting lifesaving and immediate food needs and also contributing to agriculture productions and livelihoods diversifications and building disaster management capacity of vulnerable communities. The improved agricultural and livestock productions can increase the availability and affordability of nutritious food and hence improve dietary diversity to women and children. Combinations of food security and livelihoods support will help the target households to improve their food and nutrition status, build resilience and reduce vulnerability to malnutrition and other shocks. 
The design of the proposed project is informed by findings of the multi-partner and multi-sectoral assessments, official appeals of the government, security and risk analysis and recommendations which have been conducted and released for the last six months. Most of the proposed interventions are accessible and currently multiple projects are being implemented by Save the Children. 
The proposed counties are selected based on food insecurity and malnutrition status, SCI’s operational presence and experiences in the areas, good partnership and potential integration with ongoing multi-sectoral programs in the areas.
The proposed emergency response is also developed in line with Cluster Objectives (CO1, CO2 and CO3) of FSL Cluster and Strategic Objectives (SO 2 and SO3) of HRP 2020, minimum guidelines, priorities, and considering the minimum standards where relevant.                                                                                  
Starting from 01 January 2020, the proposed action will be implemented for 12 months in three States of South Sudan, specifically Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil East), Jonglei (Akobo, Nyirol), and Eastern Equatoria (Lafon, Budi, Torit, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North) targeting a total of 234,000 people, which fall under IPC 5, 4 and 3.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition Integrated Response in Koch, Rubkona (Bentiu PoC) - Unity State and Fangak (Jonglei State)
project_objective:
The proposed project will prioritize life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years of age (U5s) and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) vulnerable to malnutrition in Bentiu PoC, Koch, and New Fangak.  

The activities will primarily focus on Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) to increase equitable access and utilization of lifesaving nutrition services:  early detection through screening and the treatment of SAM and MAM cases.  World Relief South Sudan (WRSS) currently operates 2 Nutrition Centers in Bentiu; 8 in Koch; and 6 in New Fangak.  Two of the centers (one in Koch; one in New Fangak) also have Stabilization Centers.  This project seeks to support outpatient therapeutic feeding program (U5-OTP), Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP – U5 MAM and PLW) and Mother, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) programming in these 16 sites by including community outreach and mobile interventions. The project will also increase the capacity of OTP/TSFP sites through improved infrastructure and maintain the number of Stabilization Centers in Koch and Fangak Counties.

Prevention activities will also be incorporated to address the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition. This will be primarily through onsite nutrition education to mothers and caregivers on use of treatment nutrition supplies and promoting dietary practices will equip them with knowledge and skills to prevent malnutrition and make healthy food choices within their context. Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) will also promote improved MIYCN practices. Subject to funding available, additional community components, such as Mothers’ Support Groups, will be supported.

Program integration shall be ensured by establishing kitchen gardening in selected nutrition sites, PLWs beneficiaries linked to FSL to receive vegetable kits where possible and they will also benefit from cooking demonstrations. For WASH, proper sanitation facilities (latrines), safe drinking water, handwashing stations and ECDE materials will be mainstreamed across nutrition sites, towards Education. Towards Health, SAM children will be tested for malaria and other illness (URTI, UTI) and referred/linked to adjacent PHCC/Us for comprehensive treatment. The program shall be sensitive to the needs and safety of women, boys and girls by creating a friendly and sanitary atmosphere.

project_name: Emergency Health Integrated response in Unity State (Koch and Rubkona Counties) and Jonglei State (Fangak County)
project_objective:
This project will provide lifesaving emergency primary healthcare access to vulnerable populations in Patit and Lablabni in Koch County; Sector 2 PHCC and Sector 5 PHCU in Rubkona County; and Tiep, Wicmuon and Buom in Fangak County focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality. This will be through the modality of supporting two PHCUs in Koch; one PHCC and one PHCU in Rubkona; and three PHCUs in New Fangak to serve the catchment areas, all of which are not currently served under existing HPF or World Bank projects. Four health facilities will be renovated at Patit, Tiep, Wicmuon and Sector 2 while Lablabni and Buom will need basic construction. The project will target a total of 39,925 direct beneficiaries, particularly women and children, who would otherwise not have access to basic health services.

Once established, the facilities will be supported to provide the full package of care for a PHCC or a PHCU, including maternal and child healthcare services, immunization programs, disease surveillance, and infection prevention. Services will particularly focus on addressing the top three morbidities of malaria, acute watery diarrhea (AWD), and acute respiratory infection (ARI), as well as prevention of epidemic-prone diseases like measles, EVD, and other outbreaks. With established OTP and TSFP services in these locations, as well as Food Security and WASH projects in the county, World Relief will be able to easily integrate the responses through other projects, those of WR and other actors.

In line with the purpose of the Standard Allocation for 2020, this project will implement health sector activities in the prioritized locations of Koch, Rubkona and Fangak Counties. The objectives of the project align with those of the health cluster and the fund’s strategic objectives.

The project will deliver a frontline health response meeting the cluster’s objectives of improving access and scaling-up response to integrated quality essential health care services to vulnerable populations and reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic prone diseases and health insecurities; strengthening local capacity to prevent, detect and respond timely to outbreaks and public health risk events; and integrating activities with WASH, Nutrition and Protection sectors to provide timely and promptly lifesaving interventions to vulnerable population in the prioritized locations. Strong referral mechanisms will be established or enhanced toward the care of vulnerable people with specific needs like SGBV survivors and SAM children with medical complications.
