To establish WASH activities at health facilities will be complementary to hygiene and sanitation messaging to improve disease control and infection prevention systems.

Capacity building for staff will be an important component, with trainings provided on key topics to include diseases outbreak prevention, IMNCI protocols, CMR protocols, and medical supply management strategies. Outreach interventions will be organized to harder to reach locations from the PHCUs. All these activities will be monitored through well-coordinated supervision strategies together with the Ministry of Health and UN Agencies. Activities will be monitored by Area Coordinators who will receive support from Juba office. The reports will be shared to the health cluster and the Ministry of health through the County Health Directorate.

project_name: Building Resilience in Food Security and Livelihood Support to Vulnerable Populations in Koch County, Unity State and Fangak County, Jonglei State
project_objective:
This project aims at building resilience in livelihoods by supporting vulnerable populations in Koch County, Unity State and Fangak County, Jonglei state. To achieve this, the project will be implemented in line with the food security and livelihoods cluster objectives. The project will enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop seeds and fishing and livestock support to populations in stressed, crisis or emergency levels in the IPC classification. To achieve this, the project will directly distribute livelihood support kits to 154,180 beneficiaries in both Koch and Fangak counties. These beneficiaries will be provided with crop, vegetable and fishing kits. 
Secondly, the project will strive to reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs by supporting and strengthening households’ ability to absorb shocks. To achieve this objective, the project will train 23,130 beneficiaries on improved agronomic practices. The training will focus on three key areas; appropriate agronomic practices, pest and disease control, and post-harvest handing and preservation. Fishing training will focus on appropriate net making, preservation of breeding grounds as well as fish preservation to avoid post-harvest losses. 
The project will also support 3,000 beneficiaries with small ruminants (sheep or goats) or poultry (chicken) to give them an opportunity to re-establish their stocks after losing their livestock during the years of protracted fighting. These livestock beneficiaries will be organised into small groups for group management of the provided livestock but also for training and follow-up. The project will also support these livestock beneficiaries with training. Livestock training will focus on livestock routine management practices and disease control.
The project will have a strong coordination and integration component. Coordination with other stakeholders will be done at both the Juba level and the county level to avoid duplication and reach out to as many beneficiaries as possible. Integration will involve working with Nutrition, WASH, and Protection programs to ensure beneficiaries are served more effectively. This will involve working with caregivers of patients admitted in the OTP and TSFP programs to ensure that they can continue producing enough food and avoid relapses once discharged from the Nutrition programs. It will also involve working with beneficiaries to improve hygiene and sanitation at home to ensure proper food utilization. Integration will also ensure mainstreaming protection concerns in this project to ensure prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse as well as general protection to ensure accountability to affected population. As a Nutrition and WASH partner in the proposed locations, World Relief will be able to integrate sectors easily with existing programs.

project_name: Responding to the Protection Needs of the Most Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Gaza (GBV, Child Protection and Great March of Return)
project_objective:
Poverty, the consequences of past hostilities that continue to be felt, displacement, political instability, weak protection systems, sub-standard housing and overcrowding continue to increase vulnerabilities, especially for women, children and persons with disabilities. In addition, needs arising from GMR continued to raise with more than 33,690 people injured - including at least 8,003 children (OCHA figures, 14 October 2019), posing serious concerns in terms of civilian protection and access to emergency health.
Through its programmes and services, UNRWA will mitigate the impact of the erosion of coping mechanisms and increasing poverty, which heightens protection risks for the most vulnerable. 
Thematically, specific Agency efforts will focus on Gender Based Violence (GBV), child protection including child labour, children out of school, children with disabilities, child marriage and the aftermaths of the ongoing Great March' mass demonstrations.
Operationally, UNRWA will seek to strengthen inter-programme coordination and cooperation, referral systems, protection mainstreaming, and internal capacity. The training of front-line staff will continue, focusing on protection principles, referral systems for individual protection cases such as children and victims of GBV (response, mitigation and prevention) in emergency situations. UNRWA will also raise awareness on the protracted and current humanitarian crisis in Gaza and its protection implications for Palestine refugees through inter-agency coordination and direct contact with external interlocutors. In particular, the Agency will take advantage of visits by foreign delegations to Gaza, providing up-to-date information on the humanitarian and protection environment and advocating for refugee rights.

project_name: Access to quality inclusive education in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: The project will provide access to quality inclusive education for 50,000 children of age 6-17 in the Northeast Nigeria.

project_name: Peru - United Nations Population Fund
WaSH response to IDPs and Host communities in Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, Jere and MMC LGA’s.
project_objective:
The complex emergency and conflict in North East Nigeria started in 2009 and has resulted in the displacement of over 2 million people (DTM Aug 2019). Overall, 7.68 million people are in dire need of assistance across Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) states; In which, 45% being IDPs and returnees, 38% host communities and the remaining part being inaccessible populations (HRP 2019-2021). The situation of host communities and IDPs is critical, as the IDPs are living in severely congested temporary camps, prone to regular epidemics, rain, flooding and fire incidents, while the host communities are having the tension of not properly intervened as a result of prioritization of IDPs and returnees. 
Solidarites International (SI) is proposing the continuation of its current provision of WaSH services through a one-year WaSH project that will address critical gaps in WASH activities for a highly vulnerable population among the People in Need (PiN) at both host communities and IDPs camps level in the Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, MMC and Jere LGAs, Borno State, Nigeria. 
Due to ongoing conflict and security operation in Borno state; Ngala, Dikwa and Monguno still remain “hard to reach” LGAs with the least access to health services, permanent shelters, safe water, sanitation facilities and the highest rate of malnutrition and protection issues (REACH - November 2018 - April 2019). Some sites in those 5 LGA’s still have access to less than 7L/pers/day of safe water and a huge gap noted in terms of sanitationreferenced tothe WASH Sector Gap matrix in the“hard to reach” LGAs do not comply with the SPHERE standard of 50 pers/functional latrines.

SI is thus proposing to intervene in Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, MMC and Jere LGAs under this project so as to achieve its specific objective which is “to improve to sustainable Safe Water, Sanitary facilities n and Hygiene Services to the affected population in Monguno, Dikwa, Ngala, MMC and Jere through:
-	Rehabilitation, operation and maintenance of water points in the most vulnerable camps as well as host communities in the 5 LGA’s
-	Drilling of water points in Ngala and Dikwa LGA
-	 Construction and rehabilitation of emergency blocks of latrines and bathing facilities in vulnerable camps and host communities in all the locations.
-	
-	Hygiene promotion activities and campaigns with support of IEC materials
-	Menstrual Health Management activities 
The annual target population for this project is 506810 individuals in a ratio of 45:55 of male: female gender proportion

project_name: Provide unconditional cash-based assistance; Provision of food to isolation/treatment centers; Raise awareness of communities; Procure and pre-position stocks; Strengthen market monitoring system; Engage in advocacy and coordination efforts
project_objective: Provide unconditional cash-based assistance to people living in urban and semi-urban areas; Provision of food to isolation/treatment centers; Raise awareness of communities/stakeholders using MISAU-approved package for COVID-19; Procure and pre-position stocks in order to anticipate/ mitigate potential supply chain disruptions that may results from a lockdown policy; Assess vulnerability to food and nutrition insecurity through indirect means, including mobile Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (mVAM); Strengthen market monitoring system by reporting on retail prices of the main markets, provide qualitative insights of retail markets that will explain the impacts on prices and foresee future challenges; Engage in advocacy, coordination efforts with partners to ensure that standardized safe operations are implemented in the delivery of food and agricultural inputs

project_name: Provision of Shelter and Non-Food Items to Households affected by Conflict in the Former States of Unity, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria, and Warrap in South Sudan
project_objective:
World Vision plans to support 60,000 individuals (6,000 men, 12,000 women, 18,000 boys and 24,000 girls) comprised of IDPs, returnees, and affected people in host communities with shelter and non-food items in some of the locations of severe needs. These include some counties in Unity, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria and Warrap States. This project will also benefit some locations through cash-based interventions through the unconditional but restricted modality due to the likely presence of functional markets. The specific areas to benefit from this are Tambura and Yambio in Western Equatoria State, and Tonj North in Warrap State. The cash based-intervention modality will contribute to rebuilding of local economies, hence improving community resilience and coping mechanisms, which on the other hand contributes to achievement of Cluster’s objectives of supporting the most vulnerable, returnees, IDPs, host communities with lasting solutions.

World Vision will use approaches that enhance effectiveness of the project. This include close coordination with the S/NFI Cluster at both national and sub-national levels. Prior to NFI distribution, the Pipeline Unit will be kept informed on caseload targets especially during needs assessments and desk reviews to enable adequate prepositioning of NFI materials. All requests for NFI will be done one week in advance to give ample time for Logistics planning and delivery of items to communities. Also, the response team will closely coordinate with the Logistic Cluster and community on daily basis to enable timely deliveries. Community engagement will be boosted by identifying and strengthening the existing community structures responsible for local issues. Further, Local community committees will be formed and trained on community resilience, coping mechanisms and mobilization of community members for local projects. This local committees will help cascade the knowledge widely in the community. Also, multi-sectoral integration will be the cornerstone of the project which will help communities to realize durable solutions. World Vision's mobile team will take part in multi-sectorial interventions in order to leverage the efforts of the various sectors. Joint missions will be planned together especially during community awareness exercises, where the World Vision mobile team will provide messaging on health, WASH, nutrition, and food security and livelihood (FSL) sectors. Gender and protection issues related to House, Land and Property (HLP) will similarly be identified and addressed accordingly during the project lifespan. During joint mission responses, World Vision and partners will make the use of the Humanitarian Hubs like Ayod, Nasir and Fangak to support hard-to-reach locations. These Hub locations will be used as logistics and communication centers to urgently respond to emergency needs, for example, planning of missions, preposition of NFI materials, and supplies of other sectors like Health, WASH. World Vision will also collaborate with CCCM partners by sharing information regarding the both formal and informal settlements, as there is a likelihood of increased movement of people across communities. Where possible, Biometric Registration (BMR) will be used to verify beneficiaries before distribution takes place.

project_name: Promotion of Peace for Vulnerable People Affected by Protracted Conflict in South Sudan 2020
project_objective:
According to the IRNA report (2019), the main driver of the current crisis has been the armed conflict (between the Government and opposition forces) from 2015 - 2018 which led to multiple displacements of civilian populations resulting in a total loss of livelihoods.
Furthermore, the competition for natural resources is the main cause of violent intra/inter communal conflicts in the some states. Pastoralist communities compete for access to grazing land, water, fishing areas and these drivers are exacerbated by civilians having access to guns, erosion of moral authority of local and traditional leaders, weak states institutions to protect the population and a culture of cattle rustling. The majority of the youths that participate in conflicts have less education, are not employed and have disengaged with the traditional authorities. This makes it easy for the youths to be easy targets for recruitment into the army or local militia groups.
Local conflicts and militarization are linked to increasing poverty, sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), psychological abuse, denial of education and economic opportunity, have a profound effect on women and girls.  It is currently estimated that 50 % of girls in South Sudan are married off before 18 years and 7% marry below ages of 15. Girls are usually considered as a means for transfer of wealth (dowries). Adolescent birth rates in South Sudan are estimated at 300/1000 females aged 15-19. SGBV is promoted by a culture of silence and stigma, linked to masculine identity tied to cattle raiding, bride price, no access to legal recourse, and customary practices that promote crimes like rape. The ineffective justice system limits access to justice for victims and prosecution of perpetrators of violence.  
The proposed project will help enable durable solutions for IDPs and other population on peace building and peaceful co-existence. World Vision will conduct awareness raising activities and trainings on conflict resolution and peacebuilding with women, men, girls and boys in the former states of Warrap, Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Western Equatoria. World Vision will work on reducing barriers to engagement in resilience building, food security and income generating activities, especially for women and youth; increasing anticipatory, absorptive, and adaptive capacity with respect to disruptive events including natural disasters and conflict as well as create cohesion among community members in the target counties so that conflicts will be reduced.

project_name: Enhancing Access and Social Inclusion to Quality Protection/Child Protection/Gender-Based Violence Services in Conflict-Affected Communities in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The project will address the needs of both IDP and Host Communities in the countryside of Idleb and Western and Northern countryside of Aleppo with an emphasis on continuity of current projects. SRD will provide integrated protection activities within health facilities, prevention and risk mitigation activities through awareness-raising sessions, in addition to response activities through case management approach (case disclosure, specialized GBV PSS, case management, referral, case follow up and close cases) and solid referral pathway. Psychosocial Support Services (PSS) will be provided in the currently functioning safe spaces to enhance the resilience of survivors and vulnerable women and girls. 
SRD will provide protection, child protection, and GBV services through women and girls safe space WGSS or Community Centers in addition to community-based outreach services in rural Idleb (Termanin, Aqrabat, and Kelly communities) and Northern Aleppo (Albab, Alsalamah, and Qabasin communities). While SRD provides integrated GBV, Psycho-Social Support, and Early Childhood Development services in currently functioning SRD health facilities. Integrated protection and shelter teams are collaborated to improve living conditions through the repair of 500 damaged houses while integrating protection mechanisms to ensure accessibility, privacy, and safety for persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups. SRD provides center-based services and outreach services in the affiliated areas including community-based protection, CP and GBV structured awareness sessions through outdoor activities.
Integrating the two and streamlining outreach activities will increase access and reduce barriers for vulnerable groups. Health centers proved to be a safe and confidential access point to access GBV services and this successful model is therefore replicated and continued under this project. SRH services will include a focus on adolescents and family planning (in response to child marriage) raising awareness of relevant services available which include psychosocial support, clinical management of rape cases and providing safe spaces for women and girls.
The objectives of this project are aligned with the most crucial protection needs as indicated by the Protection Cluster, as it will increase and ensure continual access to GBV services and alleviate suffering of those requiring critical care in countryside Idleb, Western and Northern countryside Aleppo. 
Qualified and trained psychosocial workers will be present in the safe spaces and PSS rooms to manage the activities and provide private sessions for GBV survivors, referred cases, or other individuals seeking focused specialized PSS services. The work will include instruction on integrated case management, communication skills, community protection practices, behavior change communication, maternal and child health, hygiene promotion, nutrition, GBV survivor support, reporting techniques, cultural sensitivity, and referral pathways. Protection awareness messages will be delivered to beneficiaries through daily household visits, prioritizing messages of child labor, child marriage, and GBV. Referrals will be made for those with protection needs or other forms of support to facilities and services providers within the referral pathway to minimize the risks of vulnerability. Provision of specialized and community-based child protection services considering what shall be in the best interests of the child through case management services, integrated Emergency Response Outreach Team, structured and unstructured PSS, referrals, and addressing children and caregivers’ vulnerabilities that are related to disability, physical/psychological injuries, severe neglect, lack of appropriate care.

project_name: ESSENTIAL SUPPLIES FOR COVID 19 RESPONSE FOR FRONTLINE HUMANITARIAN WORKERS IN BORNO, ADAMAWA AND YOBE STATES, NORTH-EAST NIGERIA
project_objective:
This project supports the overarching strategy for COVID-19 risk management in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States by identifying the humanitarian frontline workers in the high-risk LGAs and equipped them with the essential medical supplies.  Procure and Prepositioning of PPEs at the LGAs levels and ensuring all humanitarian worker are provided with infection prevention and control materials.  All the supplies would be received at the various central warehouses in the 3 States and sent to the selected LGAs stores for prepositioning for the staff. Within a period of 6 weeks, the supplies could be received and within 2 weeks distributed to all affected LGAs.  The activities of this plan augment the three (3) preparedness and response plans of the SMoHs. These activities are vital in prevention and enhancing the level of COVID-19 response in Nigeria also. 
The main objectives of this project are:
1.	To provide Frontline Humanitarian Workers with essential Supplies for COVID 19 Response under the relevant interventions including coordination, epidemiological surveillance and Point of Entry surveillance, risk communication/community engagement and psychosocial as well as logistics services. 
2.	To support the Frontline Humanitarian Workers with guidelines for coordinated public health mitigation and response measures for the COVID-19 pandemic.
3.   To procurement and preposition of COVID-19 PPEs, alcohol-based hand sanitizers, and other responses commodities to enhance testing, isolation, treatments, quarantine and prevention.

The project aims to reach 3,843 health personnel across 49 LGAs in the BAY States

project_name: Enhancing access and delivery of integrated primary and secondary health services for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities affected by conﬂict in northern Aleppo Syria
project_objective:
The project will participate in fulfilling the health needs of both IDP and Host Communities in
Northern Aleppo and Afrin district through continuing current projects and health facilities and provide equipment, medications, supplies and operational costs (salaries, fuel, etc.) for six primary health care facilities, three maternity and child hospitals, three medical mobile clinics, three RH mobile clinics, two MHPSS centers, one MHPSS unit with two MHPSS mobile teams, one TB center, one dialysis center, one rehabilitation center and three immunization centers in addition to implement referral system for emergency and non emergency patients transportation through sixteen ambulances and six non-emergency patients transportation vehicle, as well participate in improving infection control through operating central incinerator for medical wastes for operational health facilitates in northern Aleppo mainly Afrin, Azaz and Albab.

project_name: Provision heating fuel and repairing the shelter units for vulnerable people In Northern Aleppo-Syria
project_objective:

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- Integrated lifesaving and livelihood support for Population affected by Emergencies and Crisis (IDPs, Agro-pastoral and Riverine & urban poor) in Somalia
project_objective:
Despite concerted efforts to avert food insecurity & emergency conditions, many parts of Somalia continue to register food insecurity and malnutrition. An estimated 2.1 million Somalis are in Crisis and Emergency (IPC Phases 3 & 4) and face significant consumption gaps through December 2019, an extended hunger season following the poor performance of the 2019 Gu season rainfall (FSNAU Set, 2019)..An estimated 2.6 million Somalis across Somalia remain displaced primarily due to conflict, lack of livelihood opportunities and drought. Mercy Corps field assessment in target regions reveal deepening effect of drought and conflict have led to high food consumption gaps and loss of livelihood assets.

Against this background of fragility and vulnerability. This project aims to provide 10,423 most vulnerable HHs (IDPs, agro pastoral, riverine & urban poor) with urgent lifesaving interventions to improve HH immediate access to food and livelihood support to mitigate risks of adoption of negative coping strategies. The project is designed to advance towards the food security cluster 2020 response strategy and priorities and proposed interventions are based on the principles of centrality of protection.The cash response interventions will be based on market assessments and guidance of the CWG and FSC recommendations. Mercy Corps will coordinate with other cash actors to leverage and avoid overlap in cash  support

project_name: WASH Cluster Coordination & Information Management
project_objective: This project aims to ensure appropriate and effective WASH preparedness, a strong capacity for emergency response towards a coordinated and integrated approach in all WASH‑related interventions, in concert with all WASH actors, as well as to strengthen national WASH governance system in accountability, advocacy, evidence‑based planning and inter/intra‑sectorial coordination. The Cluster coordination support interventions for enhancing the WASH gender and protection-response programme including disability mainstreaming and accountability to affected population in WASH actions. The project also aims at strengthening cross sectoral information management practices such as WASH and Health data analysis, but also to better monitor the quality of the WASH response through dedicated systems (response monitoring, quality assurance, feedback and complaints mechanism) for operational gap analysis.

project_name: Preventing school drop out for  low achievers affected by humanitarian situation  in Gaza
project_objective:
According to the education 2020 HNO, there will be an increase in the need for humanitarian assistance in 2020. This is based on an analysis of trends over recent years which revealed a marked deterioration in the overall humanitarian situation in oPt, which has pushed more families into poverty, undermining their ability to afford basic education supplies and transportation costs for girls and boys, and increasing the risk of drop out. This project responds to Cluster Objective 2: Most vulnerable schools are supported in responding to emergencies through preventive measures, catch-up classes and school based psychosocial services. Arabic and Math classes will be provided to 5,000 boys and girls between 8-12 years old and enrolled in grades 3, 4, 5, and 6, who are at risk of dropping out in vulnerable public schools in the Gaza strip. The out of school report (2017) showed that more boys than girls are at risk of dropping out of school. Low achievement is given as one of the main reasons for dropping out of school. 

The project will enhance their basic skills in Arabic language and Maths as a way to strengthen their abilities both in these and other subjects. A training will be provided to around 210 teachers (50% females) on remedial education. Learning materials and stationery will be provided to learners and teachers to run the classes. These activities are categorized under the responsive and remedial objectives of the HRP education cluster.

This intervention has been developed in consultation with relevant stakeholders, targeted teachers, students and parents. All of them showed great needs for this intervention as it provides the children with a safe access to education and protecting them from dropping out. Moreover, a consultation was made with the counseling team from relevant stakeholders and UNICEF child protection to provide the targeted children with a safe access to counselling services provided by relevant stakeholders or family centres supported by UNICEF. In addition, several assessments were conducted in this regard and showed the great impact of remedial education on the students’ performance such as the evictions in the Gaza Strip- Needs Assessment Report conducted by NRC in October 2018 which stated that “[t]he need for support in covering basic school-related expenses and paying for remedial classes for their children to positively impact their academic achievements.”

Project Locations: The criteria of schools’ selection will include the following - located in 116 vulnerable localities identified by the vulnerability mapping conducted by Islamic Relief, UK, 2017 and considered by relevant stakeholders with low learning outcomes. In order to mainstream child protection, targeted schools will be those close to the family centres to allow vulnerable children in need for protection or those who were injured in the “Great Return March” to be referred to the family centres for protection. The 60 vulnerable and marginalized public schools located in the directorates with low achievements amongst children and these are: Beit Lahia and Jabalia in North Gaza Directorate, Gaza city in West and East Gaza Directorates, Al Maghazi, Deir Al Balah, Al Zawayda in the Middle Area Directorate, Khan Younis city in Khan Younis Directorate, Abasan, Bani Suhaila, Khuza’ah, Al Qararah, East Khan Younis Directorate, and Rafah Directorate.

project_name: Emergency WASH interventions for unconnected vulnerable communities in Area C
project_objective:
The project will target the most vulnerable communities in Area C with humanitarian interventions aimed at alleviating the challenging living conditions of the target population. These vulnerable communities suffer from limited access to water services due to the Israeli restrictions on construction and development in the area. The proposed interventions will target unserved and underserved communities with essential WASH services that will also protect the most vulnerable families under threat of forcible transfer. The main targeted areas of the project are the farming and herding families who depend on livestock and agricultural activities to maintain their livelihoods. The most urgent need for these communities is the lack of access to safe water, at the required quality, availability and affordability at the household level. Families have developed coping mechanisms to respond to the limited access to water - mainly through rain water harvesting and the collection in cisterns to deal with the water shortages they are suffering from. This has also forced the families to reduce their water consumption to less than 30 l/c/d and to reduce their expenditure on basic services, such as health and education to cover high water costs.

Deteriorating socio-economic conditions, increasing poverty and heightened protection risks are compromising the rights and living conditions of families in the Hebron City and the H2 area as reflected in the 2018 OCHA led H2 household survey. According to the UN Strategy for Hebron, approximately, 40,000 Palestinians (20% of the total population of Hebron City) reside in H2. Four Israeli settlements in H2 inside the city with approximately 500 settlers. This is in addition to the presences of Israeli forces and the segregation of roads and restricting access to education, health services and water supply, all this has led to the closure of businesses and abandonment of houses and therefore the displacement of the inhabitants of H2 area. There are 1409 Palestinian families in the H2 area living within the Israeli security restricted area in severe conditions due to the Israeli restrictions against movement, shelters rehabilitation/maintenance and community services development. 

The intervention will target unconnected households in Area C communities to increase their capacity to treat and safely store water at the household level and to increase the quality of water consumed. This will be ensured through the installation of water filters; hygiene practices will also be promoted and improved through awareness sessions especially for those practicing open defecation. Also, the most vulnerable community institutions in Area C and H2 area will be targeted, through rehabilitation/construction of the WASH facilities in 10 institutions (schools, clinics, youth and women centers).

The proposed interventions ensure protection mainstreaming as all activities are guided by protection principles and considers safety and dignity, meaningful access, accountability, as well as participation and empowerment. Gender and protection mainstreaming are Integrated as per the checklists facilitated by the WASH Cluster. The full intervention will also consider safety and dignity of affected population, meaningful access for all WASH facilities, accountability, participation, empowerment and claiming of rights.

project_name: Integrated psychosocial support and child protection services for the most affected boys and girls in Gaza, especially those impacted by  ‘the Great March of Return’
project_objective:
This project is in line with and contributes to the Protection Cluster Objective Two, which calls for putting in place protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence. This project will support the delivery of quality, integrated child protection and psychosocial support services to the most vulnerable boys and girls aged 4-18 in Gaza, especially those associated with injuries during the ‘Great March of Return’ protests. The crisis has demonstrated the almost absence of available child protection services to address critical needs. The project will ensure that 12 family centres and 30 outreach sites in Gaza, are fully operational, responding to the pressing mental health and psychosocial, as well as child protection needs, of affected children. Service delivery will be targeted to the most affected locations and the most vulnerable children through a coordinated continuum of services in Gaza. Each family centre will be connected to a community-based child protection committee that informs the family centre of community needs and acts as a focal point for identifying vulnerable children for referral. Family centres will operate through established Community Based Organizations (CBOs) and mobile units, and will assess/screen and refer children for further services through: 
1) a case management approach for the worst affected;
2) referral of complex child protection cases to child protection services (relevant stakehoders and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs); and
3) referral of children with further psychosocial support needs to more focused and specialized psychological support services.
Services will also strengthen outreach capacities to detect and link up children in need with service providers, whilst providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) support through the family centres.

project_name: Provision of urgently needed lifesaving Health and Nutrition interventions for vulnerable women, boys and girls in Gaza
project_objective:
The project objective is to respond to the Health and Nutrition cluster objective to ensure the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of essential lifesaving health services to the most vulnerable communities in Gaza including through health system strengthening, preparedness and community resilience building.

This project aims to provide urgent response to immediate health needs by ensuring access to health services for the most vulnerable patients (pregnant, lactating women, neonates and children under age of five; boys and girls) through the provision of medical supplies, and targeted outreach postnatal home visiting services. 

The project will respond to the key components of the Health and Nutrition cluster emergency response plan, namely procurement of essential medical supplies to increase the availability of drugs, disposables, and medical equipment to ensure accurate diagnostics and treatment for high risk pregnant and lactating women including victims of or at risk of Gender Based Violence (GBV), newborns and children under the age of five (boys and girls) across the five governorates in the Gaza Strip. Furthermore, access to quality newborn and child health care will be improved through further enhancement of health workers’ (doctors and nurses; females and males) capacity on lifesaving health interventions, including essential newborn care, and provision of early intervention services to children with developmental delays and disabilities and strengthening communities’ preparedness, response and resilience, especially during crises. The project will be implemented in close coordination with Health Cluster partners including WHO, UNFPA, MAP-UK and local NGOs to ensure complementarity of the interventions for the improvement of maternal, newborn and child health care.

The total number of women and children that will benefit from the HRP funding will be 62,100 across the five Gaza governorates over a twelve-month period. It is estimated that 17,000 high-risk women and caregivers and 45,000 children under age of five (22,950 boys and 22,050 girls) and 100 health professionals (doctors and nurses; female 60 per cent and 40 per cent males) will benefit from urgently needed lifesaving health interventions.

project_name: Response to emergency nutrition in Haiti through management of acute malnutrition and promotion of Infant Young Child Feeding practices in Emergency situation (IYCF-E) within West including Metropolitaine Area, North -East and North departments.
project_objective:
1: Reinforcing the management of acute malnutrition 
UNICEF has been supporting the MoH to revise the current protocol for the management of acute malnutrition to integrate the mobile outpatient treatment at community level. This approach will enable to cover hard to reach children suffering from acute malnutrition and living in vulnerable geographic areas. To do so, the departmental capacity will be supported to deliver life-saving nutrition services to children under five suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). The integrated package and provided at health facilities and community level using mobile Outpatient treatment with the support of Community health agents comprises three pillars: identification of malnutrition at community level through active screening, outpatient care with ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) and routine medicines for SAM cases without medical complications, and inpatient care with therapeutic milk and specific drugs for SAM cases with medical complications. Therapeutic milk and medicines will be procured offshore using UNICEF resources while RUTF will be procured locally at MFK (Meds and Foods for Kids) factory located in Haiti. Management of MAM will be carried out at the same outpatients’ sites with the same health providers. Thus, it is planned to treat a total of 82,961 children aged 6-59 months (33,109 SAM and 49,861 MAM) however focused will be put on children aged 6 to 23 months suffering from acute malnutrition. Based on the results of SMART survey, an estimated of 46,607 children aged 6-23 months will be suffering from acute malnutrition (22,033 SAM and 24,574 MAM). To date, in the three departments there are 109 nutrition facilities (13 in-patient’s facilities, 96 outpatient centers). 
2: Improving access to integrated package of preventive interventions   
The grant will contribute to promote and sustain recommended Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices in emergency context, promotion of Hygiene and support the provision of multiple micronutrients to children aged 6-23 months. Mothers and or care givers will receive messages on best nutritional practices such as optimal breastfeeding, complementary feeding practices, how to use multiple micronutrients and hygiene practices, that are essential actions to prevent the deterioration of children’s nutritional status into acute malnutrition. Though this will be done at various points of contact at facility and community level, the main platform for delivering this integrated package will be through community agents using IYCF counselling material. Customized multiple micronutrient powders will be procured offshore. Decentralization will help overcoming the issue of inadequate staffing and high workload at health facility level and inadequate quality of counselling of care takers.
3: Nutrition surveillance, program coordination, management and monitoring are reinforced 
One sentinel site will be established within North and North-Est departments while 2 will be put in place in metropolitain area and the remaining of the West department..Monthly coordination meetings have proved to be instrumental in enhancing information sharing, identifying gaps and partners, avoiding duplication of efforts, and disseminating technical standards and best practices. Support will also be provided to Departmental Health Offices to analyze nutrition data and statistics to monitor program performance and quality, identify low performing sites/areas, and develop action plans for quality improvement. These desk reviews will be completed by regular field visits to supervise implementation of activities, assess compliance with technical protocols and standards, assess beneficiaries’ satisfaction and complains, and monitor progress. Also, regular meetings will be held with MOH.

project_name: Strengthening Surveillance, Case Investigation and Rapid Response for COVID-19 in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States of North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
The project- Strengthening Surveillance, Case Investigation and Rapid Response for COVID-19 in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States of North-East Nigeria is aimed at slowing down the community spread of COVID-19 through stronger surveillance approaches, prompt case investigations and rapid response to alerts. In order to address the increased risk of COVID-19 outbreak within the BAY states of North-east Nigeria, through this project, WHO will support the state governments to enhance epidemic preparedness and capacity building to effectively respond to emergencies in the targeted areas through:
The deployment of mobile technologies at wards and LGAs level to improve disease surveillance and reporting by the deployment of mobile phones. Based on the lessons learned in previous initiatives and leveraging the deployment of health service delivery platforms in the affected communities, WHO will increase capacity of the MHT and CORPs to quickly notify potential outbreaks and alerts through the procurement and distribution of mobile phone equipped with specific alert notification application. The clinician in the MHT who is usually a nurse or midwife will be responsible for reporting and carrying out surveillance. While for the CORPs, which is one-man team, each member will be assigned with responsibility of reporting diseases among children under 5 years of age in their community. The identified personnel  will be trained on case definition, detection and timely reporting of diseases of priority through the use of mobile technology disease surveillance.

Surveillance actions will focus on rapid detection of imported cases, comprehensive and rapid contact tracing, and case 	identification. In a scenario in which sustained community transmission has been detected, the surveillance coverage will be 	expanded to include monitoring the geographical spread of the virus, transmission intensity, disease trends, characterization of 	virologic features, and the assessment of impacts on healthcare services. Robust COVID-19 surveillance data are essential to 	calibrate appropriate and proportionate public health measures. The existing EWARS/IDSR mechanisms with more than 200 	reporting sites will be strengthened for timely collection of alerts and disease data from the health facilities.

Actions will target 2,989,473 persons across the BAY states.

project_name: Closing Gaps in Essential Health Services for vulnerable migrants, IDPs, and host community memebrs in Libya
project_objective:
Due to protracted crisis and lack of capacity, the Libyan health system is almost entirely unable to meet the health needs of the Libyan population. Particularly vulnerable are migrants, IDPs, persons with disabilities, whose access to healthcare is severely obstructed. 

The proposed project will improve access to lifesaving and essential primary health care services among the vulnerable migrants, IDPs, returnees and host communities in Libya through a series of measures, ranging from primary healthcare service provision through mobile clinics to populations most in need, MHPSS services, referral to secondary and tertiary healthcare, to support to existing state-run health facilities in order to strengthen their ability to provide health services.

project_name: Provision of emergency shelter and non-food items assistance to migrants, IDPs and returnees
project_objective: The project aims to provide emergency lifesaving assistance to detained or stranded migrants as well as the most vulnerable Libyan IDPs, returnees and host communities through provision of emergency shelter kits and essential non-food items (NFIs).

project_name: Enhancing Humanitarian Information Management via Provision of Evidence-Based Information on Migration and Displacement in Libya and Capacity Building of National Counterparts
project_objective:
The project aims to support humanitarian information management in Libya via sustained implementation of the IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) programme and via capacity building of local and national Libyan counterparts. DTM supports the humanitarian community in Libya by provision of data, information and analysis on the population mobility and its impact on the affected populations. The information and analysis provided by DTM in Libya covers internal displacement as well as international migration. Under this project DTM will continue to monitor internal displacement via emergency tracking, assess the priority needs of the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) via rapid assessments, and by continued implementation of Mobility Tracking publish bi-monthly information packages on IDPs and returnees in Libya. Similarly, DTM will continue to monitor migration trends and dynamics, and conduct assessments of migrant vulnerability and humanitarian needs in Libya. Information products such as flash updates, detailed analytical reports and public datasets in addition to bilateral sharing of operational information with OCHA and partners of Rapid Response Mechanism (IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF, and WFP) will facilitate enhanced humanitarian information management. 

Furthermore, DTM will undertake capacity building activities aimed towards supporting local and national Libyan counterparts in the implementation of improved humanitarian information management.

project_name: Primary and Secondary Healthcare Services for Conflict-Affected Households in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
The IRC will deliver life-saving and life-sustaining primary healthcare services for 252,524 conflict-affected populations in northeast Syria (Ar Raqqa, Al-Hasakeh and Deir ez-Zor governorates). The IRC’s PHC services are in line with the Essential Health Service Package for northern Syria and WHO guidelines for Syria and include prevention and management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, integrated management of childhood illnesses, reproductive health, pharmacological and non-pharmacological MHPSS, health education and behavioral change communication. The IRC will contribute to disease surveillance through systematic collection, analysis and reporting of health data and weekly reporting through Early Warning and Alert and Reporting System (EWARS) to inform preparedness and response planning for potential outbreaks in the target locations. The IRC proposes to continue implementing services in Ar Raqqa (Ar Raqqa city, Al Hisha/Jdida, Hazima, Mahmoudly, Turkman, Koromaza); Deir ez-Zor (Abu Khashab); and Al-Hasakeh (Al Hol camp, Areesha camp, Abu Rasin, Amuda, Qahtaniya PHCC, Roj camp, Newroz camp, Derek, Jawadia and Washokani). Services will be delivered through 12 static health facilities and 10 mobile medical units - the latter will allow the IRC to rapidly shift programming to meet emerging needs.
In addition, the IRC will deliver pediatric in-patient care services through a 24/7 unit in Al Hol camp. The IRC estimates to reach 279,162 individuals in 2020.

project_name: Improvement of access to basic primary health care for the most vulnerable population in Aweil East and West, Northern Bahr El Ghazal, South Sudan

project_name: Strengthening Community Resilience and Response to Protection risks using a community-based response approach in six governorates
project_objective: After nine years of crisis, in Syria 13.6 million of people are still in need of protection services (5.7 million children, 11.6 for MRE) and support due to continue exposure to new hostilities (NW and NES), forced displacement to seek safety, presence of explosive hazardous weapons, facing obstacles in accessing services, livelihood opportunities and digniﬁed living conditions. The erosion of coping mechanism for individuals and families, the lack of availability of support services to the most vulnerable population caused a major strain on community support structures. Although protection needs vary in the country, protection assistance has been thinned, especially the services for children and women and PwSN causing an increased risk of CP and GBV and generating high levels of psychological distress. In line with the sector priorities deﬁned in the HNO draft for 2020, the intervention is designed to support the existing protection community structures and contribute to the psychological wellbeing of the targeted individuals and communities, establishing community prevention mechanism  for GBV, CP and MRE though awareness, capacity building for humanitarian actors and local partners, training and community response initiatives. The project targets a total number of 11979 individuals without discrimination on status (IDPs, returnees and host communities) and in need of protection,   in sub – districts of Madiq Castle, Suran, Hamra, Karnaz, Oqeirbat, Muhradah (Hama Governorate), in the sub – district of Ma’rrat Al Numan (Idleb Governorate) in sub – districts of Jabel Samaan, (Aleppo Governorate), in sub – districts of Kafr Batna, Duma, Harasta, At Tall, , Kisweh, Jaramana, Nashabieh, Qatana, Qudsaya (Rural Damascus) and Dar’à sub district and Deir Ez Zor. All those subdistricts have a severity scale between 4 and 5. The project will be implemented by INTERSOS in partnership with SARC;  INTERSOS will provide its own expertise of working in the most crisis affected regions of the world and guarantee a proper follow up to implementation and monitor the process and achievements to ensure the respect on international protection standards.  While INTERSOS is planning to make awareness sessions into hard to reach areas of Aleppo, Idleb and Deir Ez Zor governorates, in Rural Damascus, Dar’à and Hama, the modality will be a mobile approach in combination with the opportunity of temporarily static interventions using trained protection mobile teams where there are no protection services available and complement other existing services by strengthening them, when are available. The protection teams will provide PSS to children, man and women in ad hoc CFS/WGFS (identiﬁed safe space in the community) through scheduled sessions and will educate on CP and GBV prevention. In areas where there are no existing CFS or WGFS, INTERSOS will promote community- based intervention for child protection and GBV though the creation of temporarily safe spaces (either mosque, school or any other community structure) involving the community in design &implementation and will train community volunteers as facilitators to have a more sustainable response. For MRE INTERSOS will provide awareness sessions to target communities, involving community leaders, existing protection committees, as well involving CFS, WGFS and schools. An intensive needs assessment exercise will be conducted at the start of the project to confirm the actual locations of service provision. During the implementation findings and lessons learned will be shared with the sector to enhance coordination and response by humanitarian actors. The selected areas of intervention are part of INTERSOS Country strategy and integration with other possible interventions ongoing (NFI winterization distribution) and will be promoted also to grant cost/efficiency as well as a more comprehensive response.

project_name: Improving Displacement Management and Camp Coordination and Camp Management in North-East Nigeria Summary* (Max. length is 4000 characters)
project_objective:
IOM aims to facilitate the immediate, adequate and equitable delivery of services to the displaced population in camp and camp-like settings through camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) services, information management mechanisms, and sector coordination of partners and stakeholders. 
 
CCCM activities will continue to provide site facilitation support and site level coordination in formal and informal camps in the following Borno locations: MMC, Bama (including Banki), Dikwa, Gwoza (including Pulka,) Ngala, Monguno, Mafa, Jere, Kala Balge (Rann), and Damboa; and in the following Adamawa locations: Yola North, Yola South, Girie and Song.
 
The Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) will continue to provide mobility tracking in the six conflict-affected northeastern Nigerian states, with the Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) deployed mainly in Adamawa, Borno, and when necessary, in Yobe due to fluidity of population movement. Biometric Registration will remain a priority in selected camps to assist partners for verification (WFP) and support other organizations and their distributions. Finally, detailed assessment surveys for return locations will continue in selected areas.  DTM will strive to strengthen regional collaborations in place with emerging needs as well.  

As Sector Co-Lead, IOM with UNHCR, is accountable for the overall CCCM, Shelter and non-food items (NFI) responses in North-East Nigeria. The sector will continue to ensure access to multi-sectoral assistance in camps and camp-like settings, advocating and identifying durable solutions for the displaced families and affected communities; and building national capacity through CCCM trainings for national authorities and local partners.

project_name: Appui aux populations vulnérables affectées par les crises et prevention et lutte contre la malnutrition dans les régions de Koulikoro et Mopti au Mali
project_objective:
A travers ce projet, IRC appuie les populations les plus vulnérables (enfants de moins de 5 ans et femmes enceintes et allaitantes) pour contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité dans les régions de Mopti et Koulikouro.
Dans la région de Koulikoro, IRC prend en charge les de malnutrition aiguë sévère et modérée chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans via l’application du protocole simplifié et l’intégration de la Prise en Charge Intégrée de la Malnutrition Aigüe (PCIMA) dans les centres de santé. IRC participe également au renforcement de la prévention de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire au sein du District Sanitaire de Nara (référencement, alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant, allaitement maternel exclusif, etc.).
Dans la région de Mopti, IRC appui les districts sanitaires de Ténenkou et de Youwarou pour l’accès aux soins de santé primaire et secondaire de manière globale. Les activités nutritionnelles sont basées sur un appui au système de santé pour une prise en charge de qualité de la malnutrition aigüe des enfants de 6 à 59 mois et la prévention au niveau communautaire de la malnutrition aiguë des enfants de moins de 5 ans.

project_name: Multisector emergency intervention for vulnerable Zimbabweans affected by the protracted drought and socioeconomic crisis.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the emergency intervention proposed by Action Against Hunger (ACF)
 and its 2 implementing partners Nutrition Action Zimbabwe (NAZ) and Africa Ahead Zimbabwe (AA), is to address multisector acute needs of the most vulnerable population affected by the ongoing protracted drought and socioeconomic crisis
The specific objective is to ensure the access to food and nonfood basic needs and protect the livelihoods of the most affected women, men, boys and girls in the Southeastern part of Zimbabwe. The expected outcomes are:
1. Men, women, boys and girls are able to cover their minimum basic needs (food and non-food)
2. Targeted households (HH) are able to bounce back and recover their livelihoods 
3. The targeted households are able to prepare themselves for future shocks and/or for potential worsening of socioeconomic crisis 
The intervention will target 2 districts including both urban and rural areas in Manicaland, Midlands, Matabeleland South or Masvingo in coordination with other stakeholders and based on ongoing field needs assessment. 
The target groups will be poor urban and rural HH at risk of negative coping mechanisms. Special attention will be given to female, child and elderly-headed HHs and to HHs with high number of U5 children, PWD and chronic illness as more vulnerable to shocks. Targeting the participants to community-based groups will ensure that women, youth, PWDs and elderly are represented and equally benefit from the intervention. Women and youth will be specially targeted as agents of change to improve healthy behaviors, but men will be also engaged, as they are often the final decision-maker.
ACF and its partners will use flexible approaches to be adapted following the rapidly evolving context and in coordination with national and international stakeholders. 
All activities will be refined based on beneficiaries’ main concerns and following the ongoing feasibility study outcomes.
Gender and age /Protection :
Due to the on-going situation (protracted drought and macroeconomic crisis) women, children, youth, elderly and persons living with disability or chronic illnesses are exposed to increased risks of mortality and morbidity and to negative coping mechanisms. Children suffers from poor diet (only 13% of children consumed minimum acceptable diets at national level according to 2019 ZimVac RLA), level of stunting prevalence reached the high prevalence threshold in some rural areas like Manicaland), jeopardizing the future development of the children. Adults are also affected and reduced the frequency or diversity of meals (only 23.8% of rural households had an adequate HDDS). With a drop in casual labor opportunities - main source of income in urban areas - and of agricultural livelihoods in rural areas, children, youth and adults have no choice than to resort to negative mechanisms. Those include migration (women and youth), begging (elderly, adults and children), sex work (women and children), interruption of medication (for HIV/AIDS, TB, hypertension, diabetes), early marriage (32% of women are married before 18 yo) and taking children out of school. With water shortage, children and women wait long hours at water points with higher risk of sexual harassment or violence. Cases of human trafficking, targeting women and children, are frequent in Zimbabwe, and it is likely that those will increase. 
All ACF partners adhere to the do no harm principle and will implement preventive and protective measures. They will also ensure to know what do in case they face any protection issues – endangering particularly women, adolescents and children, people with disabilities or chronic illnesses and elderly – through a referral system with protection actors.
The intervention will ensure a contiguum between emergency and development (so that progress made so far is not jeopardized) with strong links with ongoing and planned development initiatives from the national and international organisatio

project_name: Child and Youth Education Pathways for vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
63% of targeted sub districts that are currently severity 4, 5, 6
Cost per beneficiary: $156 per beneficiary
10% of beneficiaries that may have disabilities 
Estimated funds received in 2019 was 12.4 million.
Around 95,884 children, youth and teachers reached in 2019
Approximately 98% of the project is funded to date.

The original scope of this project was reduced due to the overall limitations of the Education Sector’s budget ceiling. The original budget was $17,023,009 with a target of 108,679 people. NRC has the capacity and ability to implement the original project.

NRC’s project will contribute to Education sector HRP objectives 1, and 2 NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and hybrid modalities. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality

The Education intervention forms part of NRC Syria’s integrated response. The Education team will continue working in close collaboration with the ICLA, Shelter/WASH, and Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) programmes to enable conflict and displacement-affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. We must ensure pathways back to learning and integration into formal education and acknowledgement of previous learning through supportive policies (accreditation, certification, examinations, and documentation).  NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable children and youth across Syria through the delivery of its three-pronged Child Education Pathways (CEP) and Youth Education Pathways (YEP) programmes. Each response modality (Emergency, Transition, and Recovery) is designed to ensure that conflict and displacement-affected children and youth are provided with age and context-specific educational pathways. All three modalities have been designed to provide equal access to and to welcome all out of school children and youth, prioritising those that have been displaced by the conflict and are returning home from both inside and outside Syria. All three modalities include capacity development opportunities for teachers, trainers, facilitators and coaches and will be implemented in cooperation with the ICLA, Shelter/ WASH and LFS programmes and partners. 
The target group of the Education Programme in Syria is defined as conflict and displacement-affected children (aged 6-17) and youth (aged 15-18), including Syrian IDPs, IDP and refugee returnees, host community members, and Iraqi refugees. The exact target group definition will vary for the different response options: 
•	Emergency Response activities will target newly displaced and returnee children (6-14 years) and youth (15-18 years); 
•	Transitional Response will target out of school children and youth in contexts of long-term displacement and prolonged absence from school with activities tailored on their specific context (see more below); 
•	Recovery activities will target vulnerable populations living in post-conflict and/or stabilised non-camp settings (see more below). 
Teachers, facilitators and trainers will also be targeted across the 3 response options, working in NRC programmes in formal and non-formal education settings.  
For all NRC Education activities, civil documentation will not be a pre-requisite to receive assistance.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED - Providing Emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers to Vulnerable Households in Baidoa and Diinsoor
project_objective: The underperforming Gu rains in 2019 have heavily impacted the lives and livelihoods of households in Baidoa and Diinsoor which has led to an increase in the number of households in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) and IPC Phase 4 (emergency). Rural populations in the hard-to-reach and undeserved areas around Diinsoor have been severely affected as result of poor agricultural production and limited access to services due to limited coverage by aid agencies. While in Baidoa IDPs require increased cash support to enable them to access food. Due to this dire situation, ACTED proposes an emergency short-term response to address the acute food insecurity and alleviate the humanitarian needs. The project will provide life-saving support to 3,333 vulnerable and drought affected households (20,000 individuals) through unconditional cash transfers in Diinsoor and Baidoa. ACTED plans to distribute four-months of consecutive unconditional cash transfer. Unconditional cash transfers act as a measure to prevent further deterioration of the food security of households and act as a buffer against the continued impact of the failed rains. These unconditional transfers in Baidoa and Diinsoor provide a quick response to increasing needs and enable households to access the functioning markets in Baidoa and Diinsoor.

project_name: Projet d’appui à la redynamisation et à l’autonomisation du système de santé dans la région de Kidal
project_objective:
L’intervention de PUI à Kidal a commencé en aout 2015 pour assurer l’accès aux soins dans 8 aires de santé du district sanitaire. Elle s’est renforcée à partir de 2016 en intégrant, en plus des cliniques mobiles, l’appui aux centres de santé et à la stratégie avancée.  En raison d’un arrêt de financement pour la région de Kidal, PUI, en concertation avec toutes les parties prenantes, la Direction régionale de la santé (DRS), la Fédération régionale des ASACO (FERASCOM)/ ou le Comité santé à Kidal (CSK) et les Comités de Gestion (COGES), a élaboré une stratégie de sortie pour permettre une reprise progressive du fonctionnement autonome de la santé par les acteurs locaux. Ce projet veut appuyer cette stratégie de sortie par :
-	l’autonomisation du système de santé par la réduction progressive de l’appui de PUI, avec l’accompagnement continu des comités de gestion des CSCom et une mise en place progressive du recouvrement des coûts
-	la pérennisation de l’accès au soin par la population de la région de Kidal renforcée par la mise en place des soins essentiels communautaires (SEC) à travers la stratégie des agents de santé communautaires (ASC)
-	L’amélioration de l’environnement sanitaire dans les centres de santé appuyés par la construction ou réhabilitation d’infrastructure sanitaire.

Bénéficiaires:

project_name: Provision of timely, equitable and integrated emergency WASH services to the conflict, epidemic and natural disaster affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in South Sudan remains sudden, unpredictable and recurrent despite the overall stabilization of the political context. That is the reason why the RRM mechanism remains the appropriate way to address the needs to the most vulnerable and affected populations. The current capacities of the EP&R and other existing Rapid Response Mechanism systems are insufficient in comparison to the existing needs. Thus, the proposed project aims at contributing and scaling up the RRM mechanism.
Through this project, SI will be able to deploy rapid assessments to evaluate all the newly identified crisis: epidemic, movements of population, flood, or in life threatening humanitarian crisis like in Aburoc, Upper Nile.
These assessments will be mainly oriented to assess the WaSH needs and gaps, but will include an integrated approach strategy with comprehensive data collection regarding other sectors such as health, nutrition, food security or protection mainstreaming. These assessments will be carefully reported and shared through the WaSH Cluster and any other relevant forum. SI is already an active member of the EP&R working group and will share its main findings to its partners.
Afterwards, if needs are confirmed, the EP&R actors will decide collectively, according to the situation, to deploy a RRM response or to advocate towards other sectors or static actors. 
Another aspect to this project is the deployment of full WaSH package responses. Indeed, depending on the findings of technical assessments, SI will improve the water supply, mainly through repair, rehabilitation, cleaning and chlorination of the water points. At the same time, SI will scale up the access to toilets with repair and rehabilitation of the sanitation infrastructures at household and institutional levels. Furthermore, WaSH NFI and MHM kits will be distributed to the most vulnerable in order to ensure the consumption of safe water. Finally, the community will be directly involved in the project implementation and will actively participate in hygiene promotion campaigns, awareness sessions and through the recruitment of Community Hygiene Promoters.  All these activities will be dealt with a strong gender-sensitivity approach, to prevent GBV issues around the WaSH services and facilities and in respect of the Do No Harm principle.
The interventions will be based on specific triggers. Indeed, it can be expected more movements of population will happen during the dry season. The specificity of the RRM mechanism will allow to address the needs of the recent displaced population, either IDPs or returnees.
 These movements, added to the insufficient rains registered for 2019 so far, will add pressure on the existing water sources. This could impact the refill of the ground water table or the availability of surface water, with potential shortage of drinkable water to be expected. Furthermore, the period of the project could partially cover the lean season when the population could be in vulnerable livelihood situation. 
The RRM capacity is a strong added-value when it is well coordinated. A close follow-up of the needs and alerts, a clear communication and information sharing and an accurate analysis of the local capacities can enhance the efficiency and the relevance of this EP&R mechanism.

project_name: Shelters and NFI humanitarian life-saving and emergency response for new returnees and IDPs in West and Central Darfur
project_objective:
By enhancing the access to NFIs and shelters for vulnerable people, TGH will improve living conditions of new returnees, IDPs and conflict/natural disaster affected population in West and Central Darfur. The distribution of Improved Emergency Shelters (IES), sleeping mats and blanket by TGH will ensure beneficiaries are protected from wind, cold and rain and thus reduce the beneficiaries’ health hazards. Jerry-cans and soaps will have a positive impact on the prevalence of water borne diseases, particularly acute during the rainy season. Cooking sets will help the beneficiaries sustaining basic living standards and to cook in hygienic clean containers to improve food safety. With the introduction of “dignity items” specific to women/girls hygiene and security needs TGH will provide a specific answer to women’s needs. Persons with special needs will also receive items adapted to their specific disabilities i.e. crutches, canes, walkers and food millers.
The organization of NFI fairs through vouchers modality enables to respond to dire NFI needs while giving the choice to the beneficiaries to procure what they really need and therefore to restore their dignity and support more efficiently people in need.
Fire prevention activity will be implemented along the shelters distribution. Fire prevention tool will be distributed to a fire warden unit and sensitization sessions will be conducted among the communities.

This project will target 5.000 beneficiaries through NFI fairs; 400 individuals with special needs, 2.000 beneficiaries with IES distribution and 4.000 beneficiaries will be covered by the buffer stock modality. This project targets West Darfur state, i.e. Geneina, Kreinik and Beida localities and Central Darfur state, i.e. Um Dukhun, Bindizi and Jebel Marra localities.

project_name: Apoyo a los servicios básicos de salud materno-infantil en los estados priorizados y fortalecimiento del programa nacional de inmunización
project_objective:
La recesión económica y la disminución de la inversión en Venezuela han llevado al deterioro de la infraestructura y los servicios públicos, siendo salud uno de los sectores más golpeados en todos sus niveles. 
Si bien no contamos con informes que analicen las causas de muerte tanto en recién nacidos como en sus madres, resulta evidente la relación que esto tiene con el elevado número de servicios que no pueden ofrecer la atención básica para el parto y para el cuidado de los recién nacidos. Los resultados de una encuesta de UNICEF en 49 establecimientos de salud, incluidos 21 hospitales, en los estados de Bolívar, Zulia, Miranda y Distrito Capital sugieren una falta general de medicamentos y suministros; uso oportunista de antibióticos; un número inquietantemente bajo de enfermeras de cuidados neonatales, entre otras preocupaciones. Esto se ha agravado por la falta de limpieza y desinfección de los entornos neonatales, lo que aumenta el riesgo de mortalidad y morbilidad. También hay daños estructurales significativos en las instalaciones junto con la disponibilidad limitada de agua, que empeora durante o después de los frecuentes cortes de electricidad.  
La situación actual en Venezuela también amenaza la continuidad y la cobertura de las actividades de inmunización rutinaria, resultando en el resurgimiento de brotes de enfermedades prevenibles por vacunación como el sarampión y la difteria. Las principales razones del debilitamiento de la inmunización sistemática son la insuficiencia de los recursos financieros y el deterioro del sistema de la cadena de frío, debido en gran medida a los frecuentes cortes de electricidad.  
A través de este proyecto, UNICEF contribuirá a que las mujeres que asisten a control prenatal reciban un paquete integrado básico de atención prenatal que incluye la detección de embarazos de riesgo y la prestación de servicios como suplementos de hierro, pruebas del VIH, profilaxis del paludismo y prevención de la transmisión del VIH de la madre al hijo; los niños y niñas recibirán atención integrada y diagnóstico de los lactantes con el VIH en ambulatorios prioritarios, al tiempo que se asegurará que se establezcan vías de derivación funcionales a la red de hospitales para que reciban una atención más alta o especializada de las personas que lo necesiten. Además, en coordinación con la OPS/OMS, UNICEF adquirirá y distribuirá vacunas primarias para la poliomielitis, el sarampión, la tuberculosis, la fiebre amarilla y la difteria (Td). Estas vacunas cubrirán una población infantil de alrededor de 3.200.000 niños menores de 5 años a nivel nacional. UNICEF continuará fortaleciendo la capacidad de la cadena de frío a través de reparaciones de infraestructura, instalación de equipos tales como generadores de energía, aires acondicionados, sistemas eléctricos y de alarma, etc., en almacenes a nivel central y estatal. UNICEF también diseñará e implementará campañas intensivas de comunicación y movilización social en colaboración con la OPS/OMS y el Ministerio de Salud para satisfacer la demanda de vacunas de inmunización de rutina.

project_name: Atención nutricional de niños y niñas menores de 5 años, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia en 9 estados
project_objective:

Tamizaje para la determinación de anemia a 50,000 niños menores de 2 años y 22,000 MEL; c. Desparasitación a 1,150,000 niños y niñas de 2 a 14 años y 25,000 embarazadas en 2T y 3T de gestación, d. Suplementación con micronutrientes a 400,000 niños y niñas de 6 a 59 meses y 110,000 MEL; e. Consejería en alimentación del lactante y el niño
pequeño a 100,000 familias de niños y niñas de 0 a 23 meses de edad; g. Promoción de prácticas clave en salud, higiene y nutrición en 700,000 familias de las zonas priorizadas. 
2.Tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda y deficiencias de micronutrientes. La atención se realizará con los servicios de salud ambulatorios y hospitalarios adscritos a las autoridades únicas de salud y MPPS, respectivamente. Incluye el a. Tratamiento ambulatorio a 12,000 niños y niñas con desnutrición aguda moderada y severa sin complicaciones y apoyo en la transición al manejo ambulatorio. c. Tratamiento de la anemia nutricional en 60,000 niños, niñas menores de 5 años y 11,000 MEL. 
3. Promocionar y apoyar prácticas adeacuadas para la Alimentación del Niño Pequeño en Emergencias (IYCF-E por su siglas en inglés) con enfoque multisectorial durante la emergencia mediante mecanismo efectivos de coordinación, servicios de alta calidad y apoyo técnico calificado. a. Fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales en salud e instituciones no gubernamentales para la promocion de la alimentación del niño pequeño, niños, niñas menores de 5 años y MEL, con especial enfoque en la promoción de la lactancia materna exclusiva en menores de 6 meses  b. Entrenamientos de entrenadores en nutrición en emergencias prevención y tratamiento de la desnutrición y prácticas adecuadas para la Alimentación del Niño Pequeño en Emergencias (IYCF-E por su siglas en inglés) con enfoque multisectorial (salud, nutrición y WASH) durante la emergencia a socios implementadores de Unicef. 
c. Fortalecimiento del monitoreo y reporte de temas del estado nutricional de los niños, niñas y MEL y capacitaciones en a personal de salud y de socios implementadores.

project_name: Enhancing Shelter Assistance to support Crisis Affected Population in Zimbabwe
project_objective:
Eight months after Cyclone Idai, the humanitarian crisis is still unresolved, and it has been exacerbated due to the economic context, the severe drought and the limited resources to cope with the situation. IOM has recognized the necessity to continue the humanitarian response, developing a furthermore comprehensive multisectoral intervention in Chimanimani, Chipinge, Buhera and Mutare districts, which are the most affected amongst the 12 districts hit by the Cyclone Idai in March 2019.
IOM October 2019 Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments continuously monitor the affected areas, showing that approximately 91,009 identified IDPs are still displaced and in need of shelter support in the camps and in host communities. 
Provision of emergency shelter and transitional shelter structures will be constructed for IDPs remaining in camps to assist those living in host communities, targeting  55,509 individuals and 11,102 HH totally and partially destroyed households to overcome the rainy season. 
IOM's intervention will prioritize the most vulnerable households and settlements, those most at-risk due to social economic conditions, as well as their capacity for self-recovery. Cluster coordination will also be key to ensure no exclusion, coverage and accessibility to all the people targeted, regardless of gender/age or disabilities, promoting and appropriate targeting of shelter to ensure that the different needs of the displaced population are met. The shelter model house planned for the intervention will be adjusted to the family needs and in compliance with SPHERE guidelines, aiming to achieve minimal and safe habitable living standards.
