project_name: Emergency Nutrition Response in North West and South West Regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
UNICEF Nutrition strategic approach is to urgently deliver of lifesaving nutrition assistance in order to avert further deterioration and to address critical needs of boys, girls and women, particularly internally displaced persons (IDP), and host community members in remote areas with limited access in the North West and South West regions.   
UNICEF Nutrition planned nutrition response aims at addressing critical gaps in maintaining good coverage of critical lifesaving interventions for treatment of acute malnutrition and prevention of under nutrition in North West and South West Regions. This is in tandem with the with the nutrition cluster response priorities which are (i) treatment of acute malnutrition in children aged 6 -59 months; (ii) Prevention of malnutrition (IYCF-E, deworming, Vitamin A supplementation etc.) ;(iii) Strengthening nutrition surveillance system and (iv) Strengthening coordination and information management. 
UNICEF and partners will conduct community screening of children under-5 for acute malnutrition and appropriate treatment consistent with the national protocols and guidelines.  This will also include promotion of infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E) as key strategy to support and protect optimal breast feeding in the ongoing response in the NWSW.  UNICEF will also support micro-nutrient supplementation especially Vitamin A supplementation with the aim of addressing micro-nutrient deficiencies and this will be provided both routinely and during health campaigns. To reinforce partners and the community’s capacity to deliver basic nutrition services to affected communities UNICEF will prioritize capacity building initiatives.  To inform evidence-based programming, UNICEF will strengthen the nutrition surveillance system by collating screening data, SAM admission data from the nutrition partners and conduct a rapid nutrition assessment (RNA) to complement the programme data if access and security improves.  Furthermore, UNICEF aims at strengthening nutrition cluster coordination and also enhance linkages of nutrition services with health, food security and WASH activities in order to address the underlying factors that contribute to deterioration of the nutrition situation.
The target groups will include boys and girls under-five for community-based screening, referral, children with SAM, Vitamin A supplementation and deworming. Caregivers for children aged 0 -23 will be targeted for the Promotion and protection feeding practices through sensitization. Health workers and community health workers will be targeted for trainings on SAM management (mobilize, screen and refer acutely malnourished) and IYCF-E.

project_name: Réponse d’urgence aux populations, de N’Djaména et aux nouveaux déplacés dans le Lac, affectés par la pandémie à Covid-19
project_objective:
Au Tchad, la propagation de l´épidémie de covid-19 vient s´ajouter à une situation de grande vulnérabilité des populations caractérisée par des crises alimentaires et nutritionnelles récurrentes (HRP, 2020) un très faible accès aux infrastructures sociales de base (eau, hygiène, assainissement, éducation, routes, etc.), par un grand déficit des services publics sanitaires (hôpitaux, centres de santé), et enfin, par une situation sécuritaire très volatile (Lac Tchad, l´Est et Sud). 
Selon la matrice de suivi des déplacements (DTM), publiée par l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) en mars 2020, fait état de la présence de 272. 478 personnes déplacées, soit 59.761 ménages, sur 160 sites et 44 communautés dans la province du Lac. Parmi eux, 208.382 personnes déplacées internes (PDI), 33.602 retournés de l'étranger, 24 630 retournés (anciens PDI) et 5.864 ressortissants de pays tiers (TCN). Lors de l'ajout du nombre de nouveaux déplacés internes de Boma, un total de 293.284 personnes sont actuellement en situation de déplacement au Lac. Après l’attaque de Boma du 23 mars 2020 et le lancement des opérations militaires contre des groupes armés non étatiques dans les zones insulaires de la province du Lac, plus de 20.800 personnes se sont déplacées dans 11 sites autour de Diamerom et Toboro, dans le département de Fouli (où Oxfam intervient depuis 2016). 
La réponse pour faire face à cette crise a pour ambition de :
- Soutenir les efforts visant à prévenir la propagation de la maladie et renforcer les réponses sanitaires
- Protéger les groupes les plus vulnérables face à l’augmenation de violence du au contexte d’insécurité
- Soutenir l’accès aux denrées alimentaires
Objectif Général : Contribuer à réduire la morbidité et la mortalité dues à la pandémie de Covid-19 dans les zones en crise nutritionnelle de Ndjamena et au Lac.
Objectifs Spécifique : Améliorer la situation alimentaire, nutritionnelle et renforcer l’application des mesures préventives de la Covid-19 et la protection des communautés contre les violences à ’Ndjamena et au Lac.
Lieu : dans la ville de N’Djamena et la province du Lac.

Distribution du cash inconditionnel à 200 ménages vulnérables
Cette activité a pour objectif d'améliorer le pouvoir d'achat des ménages les plus affectés par la pandémie du COvid19 en leur permettant de s'approvisionner en denrées alimentaires essentielles et diversifiées sur les marchés locaux. Le transfert monétaire sera réalisé à travers une institution financière de la place (Express Union avec qui Oxfam travaille depuis 3 ans sur tous les projets impliquant des transferts monétaires), directement dans des sites de distribution, choisis par les comités et Oxfam sur base de règles minimum de sécurité et de protection des bénéficiaires, des staffs d’Oxfam et des agents de la société financière.

project_name: Complimentary Education in Emergencies support through provision of sanitation facilities and hygiene education in Mingkaman, Awerial County, Lake State.
project_objective:
This project aims at improving learning performance and health of schoolchildren, through improved sanitation facilities and hygiene education. WASH in Schools is a pathway to healthier schools and better performing children. The project will complement FCA’s ongoing education support, and help children fulfil their right to health, education and participation. One of the major challenge in Mingkaman IDP schools is lack of latrines. Some schools have toilets, but in disrepair and without hand-washing facilities or soap, others have none. Poor sanitation and inappropriate hygiene behavior is unfavorable to health of children who spend long hours in school. The physical environment and cleanliness of a school can significantly affect the health and well-being of children . FCA is currently establishing learning spaces & rehabilitating classrooms, training teachers, paying incentives and building capacity of PTAs and county education staff. The proposed WASH component will not only promote hygiene but also increase access to quality education.   
Output 1: Increased enrolment and retention in target IDP schools in Mingkaman, Awerial County.
FCA will establish/rehabilitate gender-segregated latrines, hand-washing stands & provide sanitation facilities in targeted schools. Learning environments equipped with latrines & hand-wash facilities allow children to learn in a safe & healthy environment, and have the opportunity to practice appropriate hygiene habits taught in class. In addition, WASH facilities encourage hygienic behavior, such as using a toilet and washing hands. Experience has demonstrated that enrolment and retention rates are high in schools equipped with WASH facilities.

Output 2: Enhanced awareness on WASH practices by integrating life skills education, focusing on key hygiene behaviors. 
FCA will focus on life skills-based hygiene education to enable children to learn about water and sanitation related behavior. As a result, change in children’s hygiene behavior will stimulate their positive influence on hygiene practices in homes and the wider community. The project will establish school hygiene clubs to support messaging and awareness on safe use of latrines. This will improve children’s health and resistance to infectious diseases that would keep them from attending school, indirectly contributing to educational achievement by increasing school attendance and retention.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire non conditionnelle aux personnes vulnérables à l'insécurité alimentaire à la suite des chocs divers
project_objective:
Ce projet du PAM apportera une assistance alimentaire directe non conditionnelle à environ 510440 personnes regroupant les catégories de retournés, des déplacés intérieurs et les victimes des aléas climatiques diverses (surtout les glissements de terrain et inondation). Dans tous les cas, une attention particulière sera accordée aux vulnérabilité spécifique (situation d’handicap et vulnérabilité liée à l’âge au sexe) pendant le ciblage et l’organisation de l’octroi de l’assistance.
Ce projet est motivé dans le cadre du premier objectif sectoriel visant à améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et l’état nutritionnel des personnes les plus vulnérables à travers l’apport direct en vivres et/ou en transferts monétaires non conditionnels, également en ligne avec l’objectif global du plan de réponse humanitaire pour 2020 visant à réduire l’extrême vulnérabilité à l'insécurité alimentaire de 540 000 personnes.
Au niveau de la zone géographique d'intervention, le projet se concentera prioritairement sur les  provinces du nord-est et de l’est qui sont des zones comptant l'essentiel des retournés et déplacés intérieurs alors que déjà en situation de sécurité alimentaire fragile selon les derniers rapports d'analyse de la sécurité alimentaire. La priorité sera également accordée aux provinces particulièrement affectées par les aléas climatiques à savoir les inondations et glissement de terrain surtout à l'Ouest.  En effet, ces provinces sont également considérées comme zones de retour, sujettes à une forte incidence de paludisme et touchées par des épidémies de choléra.

project_name: Fortalecimiento comunitario y asistencia humanitaria a personas con necesidades específicas en comunidades priorizadas de Venezuela.
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivos la prevención, mitigación de riesgos y protección de la población en 69 comunidades priorizadas de Venezuela. Se trata de un proyecto multisectorial. 

Protección: ACNUR brindará orientación y asistencia psicosocial y material a personas en movilidad y asistencia legal a personas en riesgo de apatridia; apoyará a las estructuras comunitarias en la organización de iniciativas solidarias, las cuales podrán consistir en actividades de promoción de derechos y medios de vida. Se llevarán a cabo capacitaciones sobre identificación de riesgos, enfoque diferencial, rutas de atención, prevención de enfermedades (incluidas enfermedades crónicas, como el VIH/SIDA) y purificación y tratamiento del agua e higiene a las estructuras comunitarias, las cuales diseminarán mensajes claves a sus comunidades. ACNUR apoyará mesas de información móviles sobre temas de protección, manejadas por ONGs. ACNUR también proveerá asistencia material a personas con necesidades específicas, especialmente a la niñez en riesgo y a personas sobrevivientes de violencia de género. 

Alojamiento, Enseres y Energía: ACNUR construirá o rehabilitará espacios de alojamiento temporal de personas en movilidad y casas seguras para sobrevivientes de violencia de género; también apoyará la gestión de estos espacios y proveerá enseres a personas con necesidades específicas. ACNUR realizará capacitaciones a las comunidades sobre construcción segura y rehabilitará espacios comunitarios y mejorará viviendas de las familias de acogida de personas en movilidad. Por último, ACNUR distribuirá lámparas y paneles solares, entre otros enseres, como mosquiteros, kits de cocina, colchones, etc.

project_name: Supporting the humanitarian community in Ukraine in fulfilling their own mandates through the provision of essential humanitarian access, security coordination and information services including flash reporting, periodic analysis and briefings, safety related statistics, immediate expertise, and crisis management assistance.
project_objective:
The action assists humanitarian aid organizations in fulfilling their mandates through the provision of essential access and security coordination, information services and the availability of expertise. As a result, NGOs and humanitarian partners will better understand, design, and manage their operational capacity and to improve humanitarian access while reducing the risks that will confront them.
The monitoring mission provides scheduled and on-demand services. INSO reporting targets audiences are operating or planning to operate in areas of high risk and local engagement. 
The mission delivers a monthly analytical report which includes thematic topics and analysis, data and trend information and mapping, and flash alerts and security reports. Monthly meetings will take place at NGO hubs. Members can access to our independent safety advisors for data, research and expert technical advice, and assessments.  Coordination and representation on common and prevalent issues within the beneficiary and partner group, and with authorities, such as civil-military representatives, is a structural component of the mission. 

Monitoring services:
•	24/7 Threat Warning System (Flash alerts) and security reports on conflict and access incidents affecting the humanitarian community;
•	Monthly analytical reports;
•	Monthly meetings;
•	Independent Security Advisory services.

Our standardized collection and verification of data feed the INSO Ukraine database of 45199 conflict and access incidents (affecting humanitarian action) verified and recorded between August 1, 2015, and October 2019 (as of 15 October 2019). INSO Ukraine data informs INSO’s global information products, such as INSO Key Data Analysis and Safety and Access Review, reaching 871 organizations worldwide (approximately 10,000 email recipients).

INSO services are free of charge. INSO does not and will not charge NGOs to become members or to access any INSO services.

Since beneficiaries are organizations, not individuals, issues of gender balance will not arise. In addition, most of our beneficiaries are working with highly vulnerable people.

The NGO community in 2015 directly requested the action, and the modified action agreed in 2018 by members and donors. 

We expect that NGO safety will remain vulnerable in areas affected by conflict and specifically for frontline NGOs. INSO Ukraine is a scalable response and, where resourced sufficiently, can respond if needs increase. INSO Annual planning 2020 will determine the continuation of the action and similar cost. In addition to our current donors USAID/OFDA and German MFA, INSO has begun discussions with GAC Canada, amongst others, for additional partnership in 2020.

The mission focuses on Donetska and Luhanska regions of Ukraine and will maintain its coordination office in Kyiv to engage partners at the capital level. INSO deploys field monitors at locations in government and non-government-controlled areas of Donetska and Luhanska Oblasts.

project_name: Education support to IDPs and returnees
project_objective:
HNO 2019 estimated 2.1 million out-of-school and 1.3 million children at risk of dropping out. Over 5.8 million school-aged children and over 120,000 teachers need education assistance inside Syria. The HNO found that hostilities have resulted in over one in three schools being damaged, destroyed, no longer accessible or occupied for shelter and other purposes.  Furthermore, the crisis and escalation of violence has led to increased war related psychological trauma for children, their families and education personnel, negatively affecting the overall learning outcomes.  
This project aims to increase safe and quality access to education to crisis affected children aged 5-17 years by rehabilitating damaged schools in a gender and disability sensitive modes and providing teachers and other education personnel with a child- centered -psychosocial support programme training. UNHCR’s will use needs based approach to programming to implement the rehabilitation of schools in areas with high education severity scales. School rehabilitation will be undertaken in most affected locations in 54 sub- districts in Governorates of Rural Damascus, Aleppo, Dara’a, Hama, Homs, Der- er- Zor, Latakia and Al – Raka including in locations with increased trend and / or potential areas for refugee returnees. Of the total target for intervention, 83 % will be carried out in areas of severity scales of 4, 5 and 6 across 45 sub- districts while the remaining 17% will be undertaken in nine (9) subdistricts falling under severity scale of 2 (4%) and 3 (13%) respectively. Interventions in sub- districts below severity scale 3 will accommodate education needs of refugee and IDPs children returning to areas of places of origin where relative security and stability have been attained. 
The rehabilitation activities will target light and moderately damaged classrooms and WASH facilities with  gender sensitive and disability friendly approach to safeguard the protection of boys and girls and ensure adequate access to the school premises and WASH facilities. This project will build capacity of 3,000 teaching staff and education personnel on child – centered social counselling, non- violent communication, behavior modification, active learning and other life skills to redress psychosocial needs and / or other special needs of children in schools. UNHCR pays specific attention to the future adolescents and youth populations that are able to contribute to resilience and social cohesion in their communities as the result of provisions of education opportunities through access to schooling and thus empowering adolescent girls and boys to inspire and lead changes in their communities. In line to AGD, AAP and rights-based approach, UNHCR will reach out to children and their parents during project monitoring activities and through focus group discussion seeking feedback including receipt of complaints regarding the project.   Through the project 112, 200 children (52% girls and 48% boys) of whom an estimated 2,587 (2.3% of project beneficiaries) are children with disability and 3000 teachers will directly benefit. 
UNHCR financial requirement to undertake the education project is USD 8,105,727. Of the total cost USD 5,352,500 is needed to rehabilitate 65 schools and USD 825,000 for training of 3,000 teachers and other education personnel.  Based on direct activity budget, the cost per beneficiary is rated at USD 55. At the writing of the project proposal USD 56,955  have been  secured.  In 2019, UNHCR rehabilitated 33 damaged schools and provided 2,314 teachers, social counselors, administrative and other education support staff a training on school-based child – centered psycho-social support programmes. 73,920 children are expected to have benefited from 33 rehabilitated schools and other 106,444 indirectly benefited from the training that teachers and other education personnel has received on psycho-social support.

project_name: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities.
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities to enjoy rights, legal and physical protection and access to services through advocacy, identification of risks and response, coordination and provision of community-based protection services.  It will capitalize on UNHCR’s community- centers network in Syria to help identify protection needs and facilitate response to people in need of protection and access to services to enhance their legal and physical protection. As such protection interventions including legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, psychosocial support, GBV prevention and response, child protection, case management, in- kind assistance covering basic needs of elderly and persons with disabilities, education support to vulnerable children, campaigns and awareness including on mine education for communities targeting women, men, boys and girls and capacity building of first responders working in communities, volunteers, partners and government counterparts will be provided through the project. Outreach to communities will be convened through static and mobile facilities including outreach volunteers, through which people in need of protection services in areas of SGBV, CP, civil documentation, psychosocial support and community empowerment will be provided and enhanced. Activities on community initiatives will also be implemented engaging communities to address own protection concerns and enhance participation, inclusion, ownership and social cohesion.  Legal aid interventions will enhance access to civil/HLP documentation of IDPs and refugee returnees and provide support in legal matters related to GBV, CP and other protection risks. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of community- based complaints mechanism to receive feedback with regards to programmes delivered through the project and complains including regarding sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and the redressal of incidents.  

Intervention to refugee returnees will focus on humanitarian assistance, legal aid, coordination with government counterparts and UN and NGO stakeholders, information management and return tracking systems and sub – district profiling to better inform return programming and interventions. In addition, the project will support coordination fora between protection actors ensuring coordinated protection interventions as well as providing technical training to local stakeholders and HLP Technical Working Group. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. In North West Syria, it will lead Protection Monitoring Task Force (PMTF). 

Through the project intervention approximately 3 million IDPs, returnees and affected host communities (60 %, 25 % and 15% respectively) will be reached in government and non-government-controlled areas redressing their protection concerns.  3,000 humanitarian workers and local authority staff will be trained, and 2,700 communities consulted through FGDs and 2,310 communities through protection monitoring. 30% of the project beneficiaries are girls, 25% are boys, 24% are women, and 15% are men and 3% elderly women and 3% elderly men. 840 humanitarian workers and local authority staff are to be trained and 120 communities will be assessed through protection monitoring activities. 

The project will ensure GBV prevention through community-based mechanisms, such as women committees.

project_name: Provision of NFIs and seasonal items to IDPs, returnees and affected host communities
project_objective:
UNHCR as a lead agency coordinating the NFI responses in Syria and from Gaziantep (Turkey), will provide through this project the lifesaving and life sustaining NFI support, through distribution of NFIs and seasonal supplementary items to IDPs, returnees and affected host communities. 

This project aims to assist 434,940 families/2,174,700 individuals with emergency NFIs kits including cash/voucher for NFI and 251,200 household/1,256,000 individuals with the provision of Seasonal NFI kits (winter/summer items) in addition to emergency NFI kits including cash/voucher for NFI. The response will be implemented from Turkey and from inside Syria. 

Based on the draft HNO for 2020, the NFI Sector estimates that 3.42 million people require NFI assistance in Syria in 2020. UNHCR’s NFI programme recognizes the different needs and vulnerabilities of boys, girls, men and women of different ages and strives to address the specific needs of each group through a range of NFI interventions. Beneficiaries are selected based on the degree of eligibility and vulnerability, with priority given to newly displaced, IDPs living in hard to reach locations and returnees. Within these population groups most vulnerable members like female headed households, persons with disabilities, and elderly persons at risk require core assistance, supplementary and seasonal assistance (winter/summer items) including cash/voucher for NFIs. 

Emergency NFI response will be provided through inter-agency convoy deliveries to hard-to-reach locations and through distribution of seasonal and complementary items.

The overall project target reflects targets for two types of assistance package, however a portion of beneficiaries will receive both types of kits, depending on their needs and the season in which assistance is provided. NFI kits will be provided to IDPs, returnee families and host communities, in line with vulnerability criteria. A standard winter kit will be provided as one-time distribution in addition to the NFIs. Additional supplementary items consisting of sleeping bags and adult winter jackets will be provided to most vulnerable IDPs residing in sub-standard shelters. If family is assisted for the 1st time during winter season, it will receive both standard NFI kit and additional supplementary winter items. The families who have received standard NFI kit before winter will receive only additional supplementary items during winterization program.

UNHCR’s NFI Programme will also prioritize those with longer term needs and support the resilience of local communities and households within the humanitarian response by protecting and restoring livelihoods, access to essential services and rehabilitation of socio-economic infrastructure through the local production support and introduction of pilot voucher scheme. Pilot voucher scheme in exchange of local manufactured items produced through partner’s livelihood support project will help reduce dependence on harmful coping strategies. In this regard, this pilot project aims to meet lifesaving NFI needs, particularly of newly displaced people and returnees through area-based approach. The pilot project is currently in the phase of the market assessment; however, the implementation is conditional to receiving approval by the Government.

project_name: Increasing access to gender responsive Sexual and Reproductive health services that meets Human rights standards for quality and equity
project_objective:
The provision of Reproductive health services including ante- and postnatal care, family planning and the management of sexually transmitted infections have all collapsed due to the ongoing conflict. There has been an alarming increase in rates of cesarean sections throughout the country. Mental health remains chronically neglected and there are only two partially functionning public mental health hospitals in the entire country. Due to the closure of health facilities and lack of health staff most of patients are now referring to private health facilities that is making out of pocket expenditure more catastrophic, especially for IDPs, migrants and people living in conflict zones.
This project is designed to provide emergency reproductive and sexual health services to 75,800 women of child bearing age among conflict affected, IDPs and migrant population and host communities. The services are planned to be provided in conflict affected municipalities / geographical areas ranked as 4 and 5 on the severity scale with a focus on un(der)served population, where the target population and host community live. EmONC services will be provided to an estimated 12,128 Pregnant women. The target population are scattered in these conflict- affected municipalities. Considering the humanitarian situation in the country, scarcity of midwives and OBGYN specialists, low capacity level and limited availability of female healthcare providers (especially specialized nurses and midwifes) to provide quality SRH services and unavailability of SRH supplies in the health facilities, there is clearaly a need for a humanitarian complemantory service package. The services that will be provided through this project will be in line with minimum initial services package (MISP) for life saving sexual and reproductive health services. UNFPA will work with its partner agencies, stakeholders, communities and local authorities to provide the following:

1. Prevent excess neonatal and maternal mortality and morbidity among conflict affected population
2. Prevent Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV / AIDS
3. Provide clinical management of rape survivors and establish a center of excellence for CMR services and referral mechanism between health facilities and Tripoli forensic medicine hospital.
4. Develop the capacity of health care providers and managers (with a focus on female health cadre) on coordination, assessment, planning and provision of basic and comprehensive SRH services 
5. Provision of emergency reproductive health kits, essential medicines and supplies to health facilities to maintain minimum healthcare provision.
6. Psycho-social service provision at health facility and community level through female health workers.
7. Increase awareness of migrants, IDPs and returnees through female health workers and establish a referral pathway from community to health facility and hospital levels.
8. Distribution of clean delivery kits to pregnant women on the move.
9. Strengthening referral system for emergency obstetric care services
10. Deploy mobile medical teams along with skilled birth attendance to provide basic EmONC services
11. Ensure coordination and leadership for the Reproductive Health Sub-working group under the health sector co-chaired jointly with the Ministry of Health;

project_name: Support to Safe and Quality Education in North East Syria
project_objective:
Syria is now in its ninth year of conflict and while the Education system is slowly recovering in some areas, 2.1 million children are still out of school and 5.9 million are in need of educational support. In
North East Syria (NES) most of the schools which were not heavily damaged or destroyed have re-opened and are lightly supported by the self-administration but large gaps still remain and the recent crisis from October 2019 has further stretched the capacity of the formal system. With the recent events, 810 schools have closed, disrupting the education of over 86,000 children. 

The organization reached around 7110 beneficiaries in 2019 with a budget of 1,600,000 USD.
The Proposed action is covering around 8900 beneficiaries with a cost of 180$ per beneficiary, the estimated percentage of target beneficiaries that may have disabilities is around 3-4 %.
The proposed Action will offer Non-Formal Education (NFE) opportunities in three subdistrics in NES namely Raqqa,Thawra and Kisreh with a 66 % severity 5 and 33% severity 6 and a target of 1104 children and adolescents between 8 to 17 years who are out of school or in school in a very low grade for their age. Children will receive literacy, numeracy and Social-Emotional Learning sessions. The NFE will help them build the skills required to transfer to formal education or to catch up for missed years.
The project will include tailored NFE activities in the different previously mentioned locations:

1) NFE Centres will be open where possible to target OOSC from 8 to 14 years old to support with an
Accelerated Learning Programme for 9 months. The aim will be for children to reintegrate formal
Schools.
2) Homework support groups with remedial programme for former OSSC attending school in a lower
Grade for their age. This can be done in the NFE Centre or within the schools in the afternoon while
there is no teaching. The support will be designed for 3 months but could be extended according to the needs to ensure the children can catch up with their age peers.
3) NFE in collective centres or informal settlements in locations with a possible reintegration to formal schools. This will be done for 6 to 9 months according to the level of the children and their previous education. The project will ensure strong involvement of the host community to ease school reintegration.
4) Female and male adolescent groups (14 to 17 years old) with only male or female facilitators providing a catch up programme and reinforced protection and life skills sessions. This will allow this vulnerable age group exposed to risks of early marriage, military recruitment and hard unskilled labour, to be supported and empowered to protect themselves and build their personal project. According to the level and personal interests, the project will support for transition back to school (late primary or secondary) and vocational training/school.

According to their needs, the families of children receiving NFE will be supported by parenting sessions and the access to specialized services; if a child is joining the NFE activities, the household will be assessed to receive food, shelter, NFI assistance or vocational training opportunities to ensure the support is comprehensive and barriers to education access are reduced.

The project will also support formal education by holistic assistance for 10 schools in Raqqa and Derzor covering around 7000 children and 250 formal teachers. These schools will be made physically safe with essential repairs to WASH facilities and infrastructure, ensuring SPHERE minimum standards are met. Teachers working in these schools along with other education personnel that may include supporting mechanisms such as parents-teachers associations, mothers-students associations, and school management associations will be trained on the Teachers in Conflict Context training  and regularly supported through a mentorship programme in addition of receiving teaching and learning materials.

project_name: Life-saving and life-sustaining health assistance to the population in NES - Phase IV
project_objective:
North East Syria (NES) continues to experience conflict and displacement and access to health care has
been further eroded due to the on-going Turkish military operation started on Oct. 2019, particularly in
conflict areas and IDPs camps/settlements in Hassakeh, Deir-ez Zor, Raqqa and Aleppo Gov.
Through this Action, in continuation with previous phases (Jun.’17-Apr.'20), UPP aims to ameliorate living conditions and save lives of war-affected persons in NES. Action will improve safe and equal access to primary and secondary care and referral management system, together with increased health and protection prevention and outreach. The Action continues support for primary health care facilities in Raqqa and Areesha, Abu Khashab and Mahmoudli camps, expanding its support to Al Hol camp. Access to quality and timely emergency care and secondary health care will be further improved through the set-up of a NES-wide Emergency Management Coordination Center for an enhanced ambulance referrals management system.
Self-protection capacities of war-affected NES population will be enhanced through increased protection
mainstreaming, awareness-raising, and capacity building of local actors. Through community-based
approaches partners will provide prevention outreach in health and protection to support local resilience. It
will provide health and all other services to all free of charge.
The expected result is to reach 100.000 beneficiaries (IDPs, returnees, refugees, local population) over 12 months. 180 local staff (management, medical, non-medical, protection) are expected to be trained on combined health and protection capacity building programmes. In such a volatile context Action provides the capacity to quickly adapt to emerging health needs in other NES locations.

project_name: Improve Food Security and livelihood opportunities for vulnerable people across Syria
project_objective:
Nine years into the crisis, the food security situation in Syria in 2020 has deteriorated compared to 2019. The number of food insecure people has increased from 6.5 million (2019) to 7.9 million (2020); approximately a 20% increase with an additional 1.9 million people at risk of food insecurity. AAH Food Security and Livelihood project is a combination of food assistance, food security and livelihoods support. The main target group for the provision of supplementary food items as a one-off action include recently displaced households and returnees; the priority target will be pregnant or lactating women and children under five, elderly and people with special needs in terms of nutrition and care. A second target group are host communities, which often have similar needs. Beneficiaries will receive food parcels or Ready to Eat Rations. Food aid will be delivered in collaboration with SARC and/or other local partners. In order to reduce dependence on food assistance, host communities will be specifically targeted by activities aimed at improving their food security and/or strengthening their livelihood opportunities. AAH will place increased attention on longer-term drivers of vulnerability and capitalize on opportunities to rejuvenate social and economic dynamics, while continuing to focus on humanitarian needs. Based on needs identified, the distribution of FSL inputs (including seeds, seedlings, tools, fertilizer, livestock fodder, irrigation equipment) together with technical capacity building and pilot projects on novel agricultural techniques will be implemented to improve the household food security status and/or support the restoration of previous Income Generating Activities or the establishment of a new initiative to achieve sustainable livelihoods. In order to mitigate protection risks and to ensure safe programming, beneﬁciary selection committees will be established, including female representation – this body will be prepared relating to beneficiary selection criteria and the selection process. Mechanisms to receive feedback from the population will be promoted and all distributions planned to take place close to beneficiary locations; beneficiaries will be also timely informed about the planned date and time for distributions. The livestock sector is a significant livelihood activity – especially in areas where there is limited rainfall and poor land quality. The predominant focus for the livestock sector will, therefore, be the provision of fodder (as feed barley, high-protein pellets or grazing) to retain females of reproductive age within the flock, ensure ideal reproductive levels and prevent animal deaths by ensuring the animals are fed an adequate diet. Access to veterinary services will be promoted to reduce animal mortality and avoid the rapid spread of disease (distribution of para-vet kits); coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture and Agrarian Reform (MAAR) will also be conducted to support the ministry to implement a livestock vaccination. As complementary component, access to water for irrigation of field crops will be increased by rehabilitation of existing irrigation. AAH will target the most vulnerable households based on a set of defined selection criteria. Priority will be given to women headed households, families with children under 5, PLWs and elderly family members. The deﬁnitive areas of intervention has been deﬁned based on needs assessments.
Baseline and endline surveys of specific activities will enable AAH to assess the degree of change associated with the project. Regular onsite monitoring will be conducted:  Post Distribution Monitoring of inputs provided; FGD to assess in quantity and quality of the inputs; market prices monitoring; post-harvest monitoring. 
AAH will ensure that relevant age/sex groups are considered with all data sex disaggregated throughout the project cycle from assessment and implementation to monitoring and evaluation.

project_name: Aide Alimentaire Programmée pour les Populations Vulnérables du Cercle de Bourem _2020 - 2021
project_objective:

A cela s'ajoute les conséquences de la pandémie du COVID-19 accentuant de facto la vulnérabilité des populations notamment dans la région de Gao. En vue de soulager les souffrances des populations triplement meurtries, l'Ambassade de France s'est proposée de financer le présent projet qui sera mis en oeuvre par l'ONG Action Contre la Faim. L'objectif global vise à contribuer à la sauvegarde et à la réhabilitation des conditions de subsistance des populations en insécurité alimentaire et à la réponse aux besoins alimentaires et nutritionnels les plus urgents.
De manière spécifique, il vise à améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, et renforcer les moyens d'existence de 1000 ménages agro-pasteurs vulnérables des communes relevant des cercles de Bourem et de Almoustrat à travers (i) la couverture des besoins alimentaires de base en période de soudure et (ii) la restauration des moyens d'existence.

project_name: Prevención y respuesta multisectorial especializada a la violencia basada en género para mujeres y niñas en situación de vulnerabilidad en Venezuela.
project_objective:
El proyecto contribuye a reducir el riesgo de VBG para las mujeres y niñas venezolanas en situación de vulnerabilidad y de movilidad. Además, el proyecto contribuye a crear respuestas especializadas y a garantizar que las  personas sobrevivientes de VBG, incluyendo hombres y niños y principalmente mujeres y niñas en riesgo de VbG tengan acceso a servicios de calidad de manera oportuna. El proyecto contribuye a los objetivos estratégicos 1 y 3 del Sector de Protección, en ocho estados de Venezuela. Beneficia directamente a través de la provisión de servicios de prevención y respuesta a la VBG a un total de 176.390 mujeres, hombres, niñas y niños. De estas, 3.570 mujeres, niñas y adolescentes (incluyendo hombres y niños sobreviventes), acceden a servicios de tipo especializado y personalizado. Asimismo, 16.000 mujeres y adolescentes reciben kits de dignidad. Se estima crear cuatro (4) Espacios Seguros para mujeres y niñas. 15.500 personas (hombres, mujeres, NNA) serán sensibilizadas e informadas para prevenir y mitigar la VBG. El proyecto prevé el fortalecimiento de las capacidades institucionales y de la sociedad civil abordando a un total 1.820 mujeres y hombres. El proyecto tiene un enfoque intersectorial con el área de salud sexual y reproductiva, con énfasis en el manejo clínico de la violencia sexual y fortalece el desarrollo de rutas de remisión y mecanismos de coordinación. 
El proyecto se estructura alrededor de 4 objetivos específicos.

1)	Establecer mecanismos de coordinación de las intervenciones GBV que sea efectivos y eficaces a nivel nacional y local 
La coordinación aspira a armonizar la recopilación de datos sobre GBV, promover el intercambio seguro y ético de los datos de GBV reportados para mejorar la respuesta, creando un sistema estandarizado interinstitucional. 
Además, UNFPA liderará el diseñar de rutas de remisiones y procedimientos operativos estandarizados inter-sectoriales en todos los municipios priorizados. 
2)	Establecer mecanismos y capacidades de prevención de la VBG a nivel institucional y comunitario
El trabajo de prevención promovido por UNFPA incluye como una de las modalidades de sensibilización para la prevención de la VBG el abordaje de población en general (Mujeres, Hombres, NNA). 
Una actividad central es la creación de Espacios Seguros exclusivos para mujeres y niñas adolescentes donde ellas puedan: socializar y reconstruir sus redes sociales; recibir apoyo social; adquirir habilidades relevantes; acceder a servicios multisectoriales seguros y no estigmatizantes; recibir información sobre derechos y salud sexual y reproductiva.
Además, UNFPA entrena mujeres promotoras comunitarias para reconocer y prevenir la VBG, 
En tercer lugar, se realizan actividades comunitarias de información para incidir en temas de VBG, que se acompaña del diseño, impresión y distribución de materiales informativos y campañas transmediaticas. El proyecto preve aa distribución de kit de dignidad a mujeres y niñas adolescentes. 
3)	Proporcionar asistencia y servicios de protección especializados 
El proyecto establece mecanismos y servicios de gestión de casos de VBG conforme al enfoque centrado en la personas sobrevivients y a los Lineamientos Inter Agénciales de Gestión de Casos de VBG. Además, UNFPA establecerá servicios de apoyo psicosocial y primeros auxilios psicológicos para sobrevivientes, incluyendo principalemente a mujeres y niñas adolescentes, además de hombres y niños que puedan ser sobrevivientes o estar en riesgo de VbG. 
4)	 Fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones del Estado, organizaciones humanitarias y la sociedad civil
El cuarto componente se enfoca en fortalecer las capacidades y asesorar a los proveedores de servicios gubernamentales y otros actores humanitarios sobre el enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, técnicas de apoyo psicosocial y gestión de casos,  Directrices para la prevención de la VBG en la acción humanitaria y otros lineamientos relevantes.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of emergency life-saving health interventions for vulnerable and underserved populations in  Deynille , Daykenle , Karan, Hawwadag districts  in Benadir  region
project_objective:
The overall health situation in Somalia u continues to deteriorate, especially due to conflict-affected and seasonally hard-to-reach areas due to persistent drought, continued insecurity and other underlying factors. This project will strive to address the emergency health needs of marginalized and underserved communities in Deynille, Daykenle, Karan, Hawwadag districts in the Benadir region with an aim of targeting 50,420 people (20% of-252,101 of the population). The project aims at improving access and utilization of integrated primary healthcare services, including reproductive health and immunization coverage through the support of static facilities with a mobile response. Mobile service delivery will concentrate in areas not currently served by static facilities, thus increasing access to health services for marginalized communities. 
IRC is currently supporting integrated healthcare services in Deynille, Dharkenley, and Karan andHawlwadag. Under the proposed program, four static facilities (4 Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) and) and two mobile teams will be supported. Both facilities currently have the necessary equipment and infrastructure to provide basic medical, surgical, laboratory, nutrition screening, and pharmacy services. Critical patients attending mobile clinics and pregnant women with obstetric complications will be referred and managed at the health facilities. Pregnant women in need of Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmONC) will be referred from the PHCC to Benadir hospital. Support for PHCC under this program may include, but not be limited to recruitment, payment, and training of healthcare workers, provision of essential equipment and supplies, and regular supportive supervision, provision of comprehensive reproductive healthcare services: through Female skilled birth attendants.. Pregnant mothers will be mapped and targeted information will be provided by CHWs at the community to refer them to ANC and prepare for safer births. The CHW will be involved in identifying vulnerable and needy community members with other non-communicable diseases including persons with mental health needs who will be attended to at the health facilities since all clinicians within IRC supported facilities have been trained on the WHO Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP). This program will provide services to GBV survivors through a survivor-centered approach where the survivor’s rights, needs, and wishes are prioritized and respected at all times.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED -Refugee Chapter
project_objective:
Refugees and asylum seekers lack the clan affiliation enjoyed by host community members and this exacerbates the protection risks they face. In theory, they have access to the justice system, but many disputes in Somalia are settled through the clan system and refugees and asylum-seekers accessing the formal legal system often face retaliation. Lack of education and marketable skills for many refugees and asylum-seekers reduces the economic opportunities available to them, particularly Ethiopians. As a result, they engage in informal manual labour that further exposes them to abuse from the host community and violations of their labour rights.
Joint engagement and working in partnership with national and international actors will be pursued to support the Government in working towards improved protection of refugees and asylum seekers while laying the groundwork for the future attainment of durable solutions.  This will entail an integrated approach that aims at mainstreaming protection and solutions, underpinned by a strengthened evidence based interventions through improvements in Information Management initiatives. Engagement will be guided by a focus on inclusion, national capacity building, and sustainable, long-term and multi-partner planning; and principles and objectives of the CRRF and other applicable frameworks such as the NDP and relevant national and FMS legislation and policies.
Inclusion will be key,  and partners will be encouraged to take rights rather than status based approach, and to -include refugees and asylum seekers in their programmes and strategies.

project_name: Improving water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) conditions for the affected communities in Libya including the migrants and refugees in detention centers and urban settings
Accelerating and integrating efforts to overcome the impact of communicable diseases, neglected tropical diseases, Surveillance and AMR in Libya
project_objective:
In 2019, continued conflict, migration, displacement, and collapsed health system increased outbreaks of communicable diseases (CDs), and the limited capacity of surveillance and response system added to the burden of the CDs. 
WHO supported Communicable Diseases (CDs) and Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) control programmes in Libya over the past years by strengthen capacity, improve access to medicines and enhanced surveillance. The National Centre of Diseases Control (NCDC) works in a siloed manner with no coordination between different programmes. Cross-cutting interventions can be improved to work across programmes to deliver in a more inclusive manner. Combining expertise in disease-specific areas with cross-cutting issues such as surveillance, capacity building, advocacy and medical supply management can enhance NCDC control programmes. This project aims to streamline and integrate approach of NCDC programmes to:
•	Support the development and updating of evidence-based norms, standards, policies, guidelines and strategies and research for prevention, control and elimination of CDs and NTDs in order to chart a course for reaching the related targets set in resolutions of the Health Assemblies.
•	Provide prompt diagnostic testing of all suspected cases of CDs, NTDs and notifiable diseases. 
•	Enable improvement of supply chain management in particular through forecasting, timely procurement of quality-assured medicines, facilitating importation, customs clearance and improve stock-management systems. 
•	Strengthen epidemiological surveillance system of CDs and NTDs through the Integrated Data Platform to collect, validate and analyse data from different programmes.

project_name: Un camino multi-sectorial de regreso al aprendizaje y la integración en la educación formal para NNA afectados por la situación humanitaria.
project_objective:
La intervención educativa forma parte de la respuesta integrada de NRC Venezuela. El equipo de Educación continuará trabajando en colaboración con los programas Información, Orientación y Asistencia legal (ICLA), Agua Higiene y Saneamiento (ASH) y Medios de vida y seguridad alimentaria (LFS) para permitir que las poblaciones afectadas por la situación humanitaria y desplazamientos satisfagan sus necesidades básicas, disfruten de sus derechos y se beneficien de los caminos hacia soluciones duraderas. La acción propuesta por el NRC tiene como objetivo garantizar la permanencia y los caminos de regreso al aprendizaje y la integración en la educación formal. NRC responderá a los diversos problemas y necesidades que enfrentan los niños y adolescentes vulnerables en tres estados en Venezuela (Tachira, Bolivar y Zulia) a través de una estrategia de respuesta basada en tres pilares principales: Programa de Educación infantil (CEP), Programa Puente (PP), con el objetivo de preparar la base para la implementación de una versión contextualizada del NRC Better Learning Program (BLP). Esta estrategia se basa en tres modalidades de respuesta (Emergencia, Transición y Recuperación) diseñada para garantizar que los niños y adolescentes afectados por la situación humanitaria y desplazamientos reciban vías educativas específicas para edad y contexto. Las tres modalidades han sido diseñadas para proporcionar un acceso igualitario y reinsertar a todos los niños y adolescentes que no asisten a la escuela o en riesgo de abandonarla. Las tres modalidades incluyen oportunidades de desarrollo de capacidades para maestros, formadores, facilitadores, entrenadores y se implementarán en cooperación con los programas y socios de Protección, ICLA, WASH y LFS.
Las actividades de respuesta a emergencias incluirán la rehabilitación ligera de las estructuras escolares y campañas de sensibilización educación e higiene que también incluirán mensajes clave de protección / CP y el programa de comedores escolares. 
La Respuesta de transición se centrará en los niños y adolescentes fuera de la escuela o en contextos de ausencia escolar prolongada con actividades adaptadas a su contexto específico (ver más abajo); 
Las actividades de recuperación se centrarán en poblaciones vulnerables con un enfoque MHPSS (ver más abajo).
Los maestros, facilitadores y capacitadores también serán seleccionados en las 3 opciones de respuesta, trabajando en programas de NRC en educación formal y no formal. Para todas las actividades de educación de NRC, la documentación civil no será un requisito previo para recibir asistencia.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence pour les populations pauvres et tres pauvres affectées par les impacts du Covid19.
project_objective:
Selon l’analyse effectuée par les experts gouvernementaux pendant l’élaboration du Plan National De Réponse d’Urgence, il est évident que pendant la phase ou le virus se propage et que les mesures se resserrent pour enrayer sa propagation, le système alimentaire sera mis à rude épreuve dans les semaines et les mois à venir. Les restrictions de transport et les mesures de quarantaine sont susceptibles d'engendrer des défis logistiques et d’entraver l'accès des producteurs aux marchés. 

Selon les résultats de l’analyse du dernier cycle du CH qui s’est déroulé du 09 au 14 Mars 2020 à N’Djamena, les populations identifiées en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle en milieu rural pour la situation projetée (Juin - Août 2020), seraient estimées à 1 017 358 personnes dont 134 884 en « phase urgence » et 882 474 en « phase crise ». Ces populations seraient dans une situation de déficit de consommation alimentaire considérable, avec des taux de malnutrition supérieurs au seuil d’urgence. A ce nombre de personnes en situation d’insécurité alimentaire sévère, il s’ajoute 1,128,308 personnes en besoins alimentaires dû aux effets socioéconomiques liés à la crise COVID19 sont repartis comme suit entre milieu rural et urbain : 411 792 personnes en milieu rural et 716,516 dans les grands centres urbains, tels que N’Djamena et Abeche. Soit un total de 2,145,666 personnes (Population en insécurité alimentaire CH mars 2020 et populations affectées par les impacts Covid)

Sur la base de ses estimations, le PAM planifie assister 433,459 personnes dans les zones rurales des provinces du Barh el Gazal, Batha, Guera, Kanem, Lac, Logone Oriental, Logone Occidental and Wadi Fira ainsi que 347,666 personnes en zone urbaine à N’Djamena avec une assistance alimentaire pour trois mois.

Afin d’assurer une intervention qui réponde aux nécessites d’application des mesures-barrières face au COVID-19, le PAM a développé des directives et des procédures standard pour ses distributions alimentaires et nutritionnelles qui sont adaptées aux mesures recommandées par le Gouvernement. Le personnel du PAM et de ses partenaires sont sensibilisés sur les mesures et les procédures à suivre dans la préparation des sites et pendant la distribution de l’assistance alimentaire. Les outils et les procédures à suivre ont été partagés avec les membres du Cluster Sécurité alimentaire afin qu’une approche standard soit appliquée lors des interventions dans les prochains mois.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items assistance in Greater Equatoria, through in-kind and cash modalities
project_objective:
LCED will target 30,000 individuals (6900 men, 10620 Women, 5412 boys, 7068 girls) with cash and in-kind modality (30%) in Mundri West, Tambura (WES), Yambio, Torit (EES), and Yei (CES), and only in-kind (70%) in Mundri East and Morobo Counties (CES), due to lack of functional markets. The vulnerability matrix include IDPs (48%), returnees (42%) and host community households (10%, DTM round6). Beneficiary targeting will be guided by the SNFI Cluster criteria of multiple vulnerabilities; PLWs, children <5, the elderly, PWN/PWDs, high number of dependents, combined with multiple displacement, lack of ties with the local community/purchasing power, and GBV risk associated with S/NFI needs. LCED will scale-up its cash-for-work modality, initially implemented in Yei County as pilot project, targeting 200 women/youth for training in Fuel-Efficient Stoves (FES) construction.
The choice of modality is informed by LCED previous experience in the target Counties, and the need to scale-up CBI as an avenue to recovery&resilience. 3 successful CBIs were implemented in Yei and Mundri West, while market assessment findings from Tambura (LCED, Mar19) revealed cash feasibility and cost ineffectiveness of road transport for in-kind assistance.
To implement CBIs, a $225,000 multipurpose cash fund will be needed for procurement of shelter materials (poles/grass/tools) and NFIs from the local market, allowing 1100 vulnerable families to repair their partially/totally destroyed homes, and ensuring adequate shelter/protection and dignified life. This activity will require unskilled/semi-skilled labor, since in remote areas framing material is not accessible to vulnerable beneficiaries due to protection concerns, hence the project will include a small CFW component targeting 200 individuals for training in shelter construction by the LCED local shelter expert, with secondary benefits for host communities (financial empowerment and conflict risk reduction). HLP and CCCM partners on mobile response will be engaged to minimize conflicts over land and shelters, as well as using an integrated response for camp-like settings in order to benefit groups of IDPs, following the HLP due diligence guidelines.
Multipurpose cash voucher distribution (restricted/unconditional) will include an initial $70 installment and a second one of $30, allowing households to purchase SNFIs as per their priority. Financial service providers will be mapped out in the project sites, and distribution facilitated by LCED staff. Female heads of household will be prioritized, to ensure financial empowerment of intended people and GBV risk reduction. 
For in-kind response, pipeline items will be requested upon approval of S/NFI analysis report by the SNFI Cluster coordinators, and delivered to agreed distribution sites close to the beneficiaries allowing access, targeting 3,700 vulnerable households in areas without access to local market or local shelter material. Of those, 1,750 HHs in long-term displacement will be targeted with shelter repairing/NFI replenishment, considering the 6 month life-span.
To measure the project success and take evidence-based decision on the course of action, continuous monitoring and end of line evaluation (third party monitoring) will be conducted jointly with community members/local leaders as part of a Feedback and Complaint Mechanism.
Coordination with the S/NFI cluster through the SFPs on by-monthly basis, and with other  humanitarian partners utilizing humanitarian hubs in Mundri, Torit, Yambio and Yei in order to take part to joint responses, will minimize duplication, and promote integrated response, gender and protection mainstreaming, GBV referrals, risk mitigation, and incorporation of HIV/AIDS and EVD/cholera messaging where possible. As alternate WES SFP, Greater Mundri SiFP and DFC focal point for UN OCHA, LCED will lead humanitarian interventions through the cluster methodology, lead humanitarian coordination and refer need/gaps to ICWG.

project_name: Protection of Palestine Refugees Affected by the Occupation and Forced Displacement in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem).
project_objective:
The impact of over 50 years of continued military occupation in the West Bank on the protection of Palestine refugees is wide-ranging. Palestine refugees face a range of serious protection threats, including: threats to life; liberty and security; destruction or damage to homes and other property; forced displacement and restrictions on freedom of movement and access to natural resources, markets and other livelihood opportunities. 

This action is based on UNRWA's protection mandate for over 843,931 Palestine refugees in the West Bank. Particular focus is given to the needs of Palestine refugees living in 19 refugee camps, where the Israeli Security Forces conduct repeated military operations. The action has two core objectives to (1) monitor and document IHL & IHRL violations affecting Palestine refugees, using this as a basis to engage in targeted protection advocacy to promote accountability and enhance the protection of affected persons, (2) to respond to the acute needs of Palestine refugees exposed to the risk of displacement and/or forcible transfer through the provision of cash assistance and an integrated case management response.

In relation to the first objective, the aim is to enhance the protective environment for Palestine refugees exposed to protection threats through protection advocacy - through persuasion, mobilisation and denunciation, and based on monitoring and documentation of protection incidents and related analysis. The tools and approaches are determined by the HCTs protection advocacy strategy. The aim is to promote both protective policies and practices as well as the accountability of duty bearers.

In relation to the second objective, this action responds to protection threats by mitigating their consequences and reinforcing the resilience of affected persons. UNRWA will provide dedicated case management services to affected persons; also facilitating access of these persons to cash transfers depending on the identified needs. Cash assistance addresses immediate needs linked protection threats, whilst case management services improves access to other UNRWA services and specialised partners, and reinforces the resilience of affected persons.

This action works directly towards two out of three of the strategic objectives of the HRP:

Strategic Objective 1: The rights of Palestinians living under occupation, including those living under the blockade and other restrictions, are protected, respected and promoted in accordance with IHL and IHRL.

Strategic Objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

project_name: Water provision to communities and WASH services in camps in NWS
project_objective:
Prior to the conflict, the water and sanitation resources in Syria were under pressure due to population growth and urbanization.  Syrian water resources faced significant managerial challenges and had been prioritized by the Syrian government for modernization.  Water utilities were heavily subsidized and as of 2006 were only covering 55% of their operational costs and were unable to gain funds for investment.   The sector was further challenged by its complex management structure with different Ministries and sectors having overlapping responsibilities and functions.  The protracted conflict has significantly worsened the situation.  Unreliable electricity, damaged water infrastructure, the influx of IDPs, threats from militant groups inside Idleb, and households with few financial resources are all challenges facing the water sector. 

NGO X has been supporting the operation of four Water Units serving the conflict-affected population of Idleb Governorate since 2014.  An estimated 676,225 individuals rely on the water pumped by 50 water station within the four units for their households’ drinking and hygiene needs. The programme will continue to provide inputs and technical expertise to allow for the continuation of services while strengthening the financial and management capacity of local stakeholders to manage the utility and continue on a path towards sustainability.  In addition, NGO X will provide emergency assistance to recently displaced households to allow them to meet their basic hygiene needs. This activity is funded until 31st March 2020 and NGO X is working with the donor to secure new funds for the coming year. 

In June 2019, NGO X procured emergency funds to support an additional 14 water stations that provide water to approximately 141,174 individuals in Idleb governorate. As a result, NGO X is currently supporting 64 water stations by providing water to approximately 817,399 individuals in Idleb governorate. This activity is funded until January 2020 and NGO X is working to secure new funds to continue to support 14 water stations until June 2020. 
NGO X is planning to replace two generators at the two pumping stations that serve Idleb City (estimated population 175,000). 



The desired outcome of this project is that community water systems are efficiently and effectively managed and the community is informed, invested and supportive of local institutions and has sustained access to safe drinking water and hygienic conditions.  

Key activities include:
•	Providing inputs (fuel, oil, HTH, salaries) to enable the stations to pump water for over 107 villages. 
•	Intense organisational capacity building to ensure water units and stations have the financial, administrative and management skills necessary to manage the stations in a transparent manner that prioritises accountability to customers, the community and donors.  
•	Stations develop realistic and achievable cost recovery targets based on financial analysis and communicate the approach to communities. 
•	Continue using the modality of ‘Infrastructure Stability’ fund that water stations can apply to for upgrading or investing in their stations and water networks.  Maintains resources to enable emergency repairs conducted by NGO X. 
•	Supporting recent arrivals into Idleb with hygiene kits and hygiene promotion.  

NGO X is also planning to support one camp in northern Aleppo with a comprehensive WASH response which will include water supply, solid waste management, sanitation and hygiene promotion for 3,500 individuals.

NGO X has secured 34% of the funding required for this project and is awaiting donor approval of the remaining sum.

project_name: Niger Country Strategy Plan: appui alimentaire à 29 200 élèves dans les écoles affectées par la crise
Niger Country Strategy Plan
project_objective: This CSP aims to contribute all year-round to: Crisis-affected populations to meet their basic food and nutrition needs during and after the crises; Food insecure school-age children, to access adequate and nutritious food; Vulnerable groups (children, pregnant women and adolescent girls) to have enhanced nutritional status; Food insecure populations and communities to have more resilient livelihoods and sustainable food systems; Capacity strengthening of National institutions; Humanitarian and development partners to access common services unti appropriate an sustainable alternative are available.

project_name: Niger Country Strategy Plan (IDPs and host communities)
project_objective:
Crisis affected populations including refugees, IDPs, host communities and returnees in targeted areas are able to meet their basic food and nutrition needs during and in the aftermath of a crisis. This category of emergency assistance in WFP's Country Strategic Plan allows WFP to intervene for the host and IDP communities who are food insecure or at risk of food insecurity. Based on the government Cadre Harmonisé assessment, WFP plans to assist up to 412 000 people from host communities and IDPs countrywide trough unconditional emergency and lean season response. The country strategic plan will be gender-equitable and will incorporate gender-transformative approaches to achieving zero hunger, including through the economic and social empowerment of women. Accountability to affected populations, protection, conflict sensitivity and social and environmental considerations are cross-cutting themes of the plan. Through respect for humanitarian principles and community engagement, WFP will increase its access to hard-to-reach locations. Reinforced partnerships with the Government, United Nations agencies, financial institutions, regional, sub-regional and non-governmental organizations, academia and local communities will be the foundation of WFP’s interventions for vulnerable hosts and IDPs. This project will also address the most urgent food security needs of the IDP and host communities that are newly displaced through the RRM response.
