project_name: Improving living conditions and safety for crisis-affected people in the Far North Region of Cameroon
project_objective: This project aims to provide assistance to the populations affected by the Lake Chad Basin crisis in the Far North region of Cameroon, particularly in the divisions of Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga, and Logoné-et-Chari. The ongoing violence carried out by armed opposition groups has had widespread impact on livelihoods and food security, limiting communities’ ability to meet their basic needs and exposing them to various protection risks. The proposed intervention will to continue the implementation of activities already underway by the IRC through previous support from OFDA over the past two years, aiming to provide direct support to beneficiaries to meet their basic needs across multiple services areas. These include provision of drinking water, promotion of hygiene and sanitation, the restoration of livelihoods and the introduction of actions to promote protection and prevent gender-based violence (GBV). The previous OFDA funded projects have allowed IRC to develop an in-depth knowledge of beneficiary communities and the humanitarian needs confronting them. Based on the successes and lessons learned from its experiences working with these communities, the IRC plans to support and strengthen established structures and its local relations in order to improve the quality and scope of actions, while maintaining its capacity to react to spontaneous movements with mobile services that enable access hard-to-reach areas in persistent and precarious environments. The activities proposed by IRC are part of the mandate and mission assigned by OFDA/USAID for the response to the needs of the Lake Chad Basin.

project_name: Assistance WASH au profit des populations vulnérables du cercle de Douentza
project_objective:
La crise sociopolitique et sécuritaire depuis 2012 et les conflits communautaires à répétition depuis 2018 font de Mopti la région au plus grand nombre de personnes déplacées internes au Mali, avec 69 679 d’IDPs.
Cet afflux continu de populations dans les zones d’accueil affecte les moyens de subsistance des populations hôtes et contribue à l’accroissement de leur vulnérabilité.
La dégradation de la situation humanitaire se manifeste au niveau de la WASH par une pression sur les infrastructures EHA déjà insuffisantes car selon la Direction Nationale de l’hydraulique, le taux l’accès à l’eau potable dans la région était de 61% en 2017. Ainsi, les personnes les plus vulnérables sont contraintes de recourir aux sources alternatives non protégées.
Sur le plan de la sécurité nutritionnelle, la région de Mopti est l’une des plus affectées par la malnutrition avec une prévalence de malnutrition aiguë globale égale à de 9%.
Le cercle de Douentza à l’image de la région n’est pas épargné par cet afflux de populations qui affecte négativement la vie des ménages car d’une part, il plonge les déplacés et retournés dans une situation de vulnérabilité accrue à travers la limitation de l’accès aux services sociaux de base tels que les vivres, la santé, le WASH, et d’autre part contribue à accroître la vulnérabilité des communautés hôtes du fait de l’amenuisement des ressources dû à l’augmentation des besoins.  
Avec un taux d’accès à l’eau potable de 51%, le cercle de Douentza abrite à son sein 6036 personnes déplacées et 25 896 personnes retournées 
La pression sur les infrastructures WASH insuffisantes au regard du taux d’accès à l’eau potable du cercle, contribue également a baissé le taux de fonctionnalité de ces infrastructures qui était de 62% en janvier 2016, affectant davantage l’accès à l’eau potable pour ces populations. 
La pratique de la défécation à l’air libre est très répandue au regard du taux d’accès national à l’assainissement en milieu rural qui était de 16% en 2015. 
La situation nutritionnelle avec une prévalence de 8.9% pour la Malnutrition Aiguë Globale et 7.3% pour la Malnutrition Aigüe Modérée, est jugée précaire selon le rapport d’enquête SMART 2018 
Au regard de cette situation, le besoin d’une réponse dans le secteur EHA pour ces populations est réel car elle permettrait d’améliorer l’accès à la WASH de ces personnes vulnérables exposées à des risques élevés de maladies liés à l’eau et aux mauvaises pratiques d’hygiène. Le lien entre la malnutrition et les mauvaises conditions d’accès à l’eau potable, d’hygiène et d’assainissement n’étant plus à démontrer, dans un contexte de vulnérabilité accrue, l’intégration WASH et nutrition améliorerait davantage les conditions de vie des populations en particulier des enfants de moins de 5 ans. 
Des analyses de genre sont menées dans l´identification des besoins pour répondre aux besoins de chaque sexe de façon séparée et des notions d´accessibilité et d´équité dans l’accès aux services WASH intégrées. Les femmes et les hommes bénéficieront des ressources et avantages du projet sur un même pied d´égalité. Des actions encourageant la participation et la représentativité des femmes de manière équitable lors des processus de consultation et de prise de décisions ainsi que leur autonomisation, seront promues.
Pour plus d’impact, cette réponse ciblera aussi bien la communauté, que les centres de santé et les écoles du cercle de Douentza et visera la réalisation de trois (3) résultats : 
-L’accès à l’eau et l’assainissement est amélioré dans les communautés, les écoles et les centres de santé.
-Les connaissances et les pratiques d’hygiène dans les écoles, les centre de santé et dans les communautés sont améliorées.
-Les capacités des structures de gestion dans la communauté, les écoles et centres de santé et des autorités communales sont renforcées.
Cette proposition a reçu l’approbation du Ministère Allemand des Affaires Etrangères qui en assurera le financement

project_name: Appui  aux  populations de la région du Lac (Tchad) et de la région de Diffa (Niger) affectées par la crise de Boko Haram dans les domaines de WASH, abris et de la sécurité alimentaire
project_objective:
Ce projet est la suite d'un projet en cours (Projet AA n ° S09-40-321.50 NGA 04/17). Les nouvelles composantes du projet proposées ici du côté nigérian du lac Tchad complètent les mesures WASH de notre organisation partenaire AHTD, en vigueur au Tchad depuis mai 2017 et qui seront poursuivies avec de nouveaux groupes cibles à partir de 2019.
Pour ce projet, Help et AHTD, en coordination avec le Cluster WASH, OCHA et d'autres acteurs locaux, prévoient d'aider à améliorer les conditions WASH et la sécurité alimentaire dans la région du lac Tchad pour les ménages vulnérables. Du côté tchadien, des activités doivent être mises en œuvre notamment sur les îles du lac Tchad et du côté nigérian dans les départements de Bosso et de Nguigmi.
Les mesures proposées ici visent à améliorer l'accès à l'eau potable des réfugiés, des personnes déplacées à l'intérieur de leur propre pays et des communautés d'accueil dans les départements de Bosso et Nguigmi (Niger) (environ 60 000 bénéficiaires) et dans les départements de Mamdi, Kaya et Fouli (environ 30 000 bénéficiaires) par des installations sanitaires, nourriture, articles ménagers de base et conditions de vie améliorées et hygiéniques.

Les activités prévues comprennent la réhabilitation des points d'eau, les travaux d’optimisation et de branchement hydrauliques et la construction de 40 latrines publiques au Niger, ainsi que la construction de 40 nouveaux points d'eau et la réhabilitation de 40 points d'eau existants au Tchad. De plus, la population est aidée pour l’entretien des forages/puits et la construction de 700 latrines familiales. Outre la distribution de kits d'hygiène, de NFI et de produits alimentaires, des campagnes de sensibilisation ciblées sur les questions d'hygiène ont lieu dans les villages et les camps.

project_name: Food assistance for acutely food insecure individuals in Beitbridge,Matobo and Murehwa districts
project_objective:
Save the Children proposes voucher project aiming to address the most critical and unmet humanitarian needs for 30,000 individuals in 3 districts( Beitbridge, Murehwa and Matobo) in Zimbabwe from January to December 2020. These districts are at the moment in crisis and according to FEWSNET report of 13 December, the countries in Southern African will need food assistance for the whole of 2020. The rains as from March will below normal. These district are already among those which are in crisis.
The proposed action will be achieved through provision of food vouchers and integrated protection interventions supporting safe and dignified access to food. The action will provide 62% calculated to meet the monthly basic food basket as agreed by the working group. Beneficiaries will be selected from the most food insecure wards in districts where there are no other players. The Action will prioritize food voucher distribution for vulnerable HHs with children >5, child headed HHs, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), people living with disabilities and the chronically ill. An assessment of protection risks in using vouchers as a modality will be implemented to ensure that the correct mitigation measures are put in place to provide a safe and dignified approach for the most vulnerable persons. Systems will be developed in child safeguarding and Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and the programme will be connected to referral pathways and response programming should there be any reports made. Consideration will be made to ensure that feedback mechanisms are age and gender appropriate and confidential.

project_name: COVID19: Enhancing the delivery of quality protection services by improving the protection environment and supporting durable solutions for IDPs, IDP returnees and refugee returnees in North East Nigeria.
project_objective:
The project aims at enhancing the delivery of quality protection services, improving the protection environment and supporting durable solutions for IDPs, IDP returnees, refugee returnees and vulnerable host community members in North East Nigeria in the context of COVID-19. 

UNHCR interventions will strengthen the protection environment by identifying and minimizing protection risks to which the affected populations are continually exposed in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic, and by expanding the breadth and quality of protection response in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa through: 
1. Protection Monitoring in COVID-19 affected areas,
2. In-kind assistance to vulnerable & COVID-19 affected persons of concern or those at risk,
3. COVID-19 Personal Protective supplies and equipment in support for partners, protection desks and other protection safe spaces,
4. COVID-19 intensive awareness-raising and sensitization,
5. Advocacy for Protection,
6. Provision of individual documentation,
7. Provision of birth certificates,
8. Border-monitoring and entry point surveillance,
9. COVID-19 intensive Human-rights monitoring

project_name: Preventing and responding to COVID-19 outbreak in refugee camps and host communities of Cox's Bazar
project_objective: Save the Children (SC) plans to establish a health facility in camp 21 with up to 60 beds to provide isolation and treatment for patients with COVID-19 infection. The facility will serve both the Rohingya refugees and the host communities.  The objective is to provide quality care for moderate and severe cases, and to contribute to the reduction of mortality from the disease. This intervention will also reduce transmission rates in the community by isolating sick patients. In order to have maximum impact on health outcomes, the isolation and treatment center will be run in parallel to community approach that includes the continuity of essential non-COVID-19 services, acknowledging that challenges including increased demand for consultations, isolation requirements will be increased. Additionally, SC's facility-focused health programme will be complemented by a network of community health workers who will promote key health messages, identify and refer cases. Given that COVID-19 is a fast spreading respiratory infection, SC will strengthen the services of health posts and primary healthcare center including medical screening services to identify any acute or chronic medical conditions including reproductive health and basic MHPSS conditions. SC is working with WHO to develop community-based approaches for the management of severe cases at household level. SC’s approach is to have Community Health Workers linked to Mobile Medical Units, comprised of Medical Assistants, who are licensed to prescribe, and who can initiate antibiotics, analgesia and palliative care drugs as required. SC ensures active engagement and participation of women, men, youth and children (boys and girls). SC acknowledges within the targeted beneficiaries the different needs of women/girls and men/boys, analyzes these needs within the needs assessment and integrates these needs into the planned activities and outcomes. SC ensures that the principles of protection, gender equality and inclusion and accountability to affected populations are central and cross-cutting in the proposed actions and implementation.

project_name: Preparing and responding to COVID-19 crisis through improved WASH services
project_objective: Save the Children (SC) strategizes its response activities after the COVID-19 appears as pandemic. To ensure the continuity of WASH services in the refugee camps, SC plans to maintain the already constructed Decentralized Waste Water Treatment system (DeWATS) and water supply systems, and desludge latrines. Based on the presumption that refugees have an adequate supply of soap and clean water, SC intends to strengthen the provision of community outreach on hygiene practices through maintaining social distancing. Additionally, SC involves volunteers to disinfect the surfaces to restrict the spread of COVID-19.

project_name: Sustain and expand the WASH basic life saving  service to Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nations and the Bangladeshi host communities population in Cox's Bazar district
project_objective: The project will target the Rohingya and the host communities in Cox's Bazar through WASH service provision with more emphasis on community engagement while sustaining the access to basic life-saving output but also the expanding and improving the quality of the infrastructures with social inclusiveness. The project will target the beneficiaries and the caseloads that are not covered by the funds provided through UN agencies. In host communities, the project will support the efforts of social cohesion and attempts to integrate the services between the camps and the host community program. Additionally, this project will address the concurrent pandemic COVID-19 issue regarding the WASH facilities in the camp area and host community as well through strengthening the existing effort, particularly in awareness-raising, hand washing practicing, social distancing. This project will use the WASH sector strategies and the guidelines in all the stages of the implementation.

project_name: Equitable and Integrated WASH Intervention in Response to COVID-19 for the Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities
project_objective: This project targets 26,071 beneﬁciaries and is focused on addressing COVID-19 crisis. The impact of this disease could be more devastating in densely populated and crowded settlements such as the Rohingya regugees camp in Cox’s bazar, Bangladesh, which is the largest in the world. As hand washing with soap and water and social distancing are the key targeted and recommended preventive measures to fight against the COVID virus by WHO, this project is designed mainly to implement the activities related to hygiene promotion that will help to avert infections and promote the health of the people.  To achieve the goal of this project, the activities will provide both hand wash NFI supplies (HK, Gloves, Mask, Soap etc) and facilities like latrine, hand washing devices and water supplies through deep tube wells which will be repaired to ensure consistent water supply. The project will be implemented in camps 19 and 13  where WVB is already implementing WASH activities.

project_name: Protection and assistance to Nigerian refugees in Diffa
project_objective:
L’intervention en faveur des réfugiés présents a Diffa va se décliner autour de 3 objectifs suivants : 1- Maintenir et renforcer un environnement de protection favorable (protection monitoring et réponse de protection, dont child protection, SGBV, PBS, apatridie, enregistrement/documentation), améliorer les capacités d’intervention des autorités nationales pour délivrer des services de protection conformes aux standards internationaux et maintenir ouvert l’accès au territoire nigérien et aux procédures d’asile.2 – Assurer une assistance d’urgence et une capacité adéquate au niveau du camp de Sayam Forage  et améliorer l’accès aux services sociaux de base. 3 - Renforcer la recherche des solutions durables et l’intégration socio-économique des réfugiés installés au Niger notamment via le programme urbanisation et la construction de logements pour les plus vulnérables. .
La stratégie de réponse est conforme avec les orientations du Gouvernement du Niger en termes d’alternatives aux camps et avec le Pacte Mondial pour les Réfugiés. Le nexus humanitaire – développement est au cœur des réflexions qui accompagnent la mise en œuvre de la réponse. Cela suppose le renforcement de la capacité d’absorption des services de base pour alléger les pressions, et l’accompagnement de la coexistence pacifique, en parallèle d’une réponse multisectorielle urgente. Alors qu’une assistance de type communautaire est développée pour l’accès aux services de base tels que l’eau ou la santé, c’est le niveau de vulnérabilité et non le statut qui régit progressivement l’assistance individuelle.

project_name: Supporting evidence-based humanitarian assistance in Libya
project_objective:
REACH, a joint initiative of ACTED, IMPACT and UNOSAT, has been providing assessment and information management services to humanitarian actors in Libya since 2011, initially in the aftermath of the first conflict and then later establishing a full-time presence in the country in 2015. In light of the dynamic context in Libya, it is necessary to maintain the flow of updated evidence in order to develop efficient and adequate programming to address the needs and vulnerabilities of affected populations. Through this project, REACH will ensure that critical information on the humanitarian situation in Libya is provided through a Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA), through the delivery and coordination of Rapid Needs Assessments and through technical support to sector-led assessments, thereby informing more effective planning and immediate responses to sudden crises. 

Multi-Sector Needs Assessment: The basic methodology of the MSNA is expected to stay consistent in 2020 with previous years, to ensure the comparability of data. The main component will be a quantitative data collection exercise (i.e., a HH survey) conducted in partnership with local CSOs, followed by a smaller qualitative data collection exercise that will triangulate and build on the survey’s findings. Also, for consistency’s sake, the 2020 MSNA is expected to target the same three population groups as in previous years: IDPs, returnees and the non-displaced. That said, REACH will consult and coordinate with the sectors, the IMWG, the ISCG and the HCT around the details of the 2020 MSNA methodology, including geographic coverage and the choice of indicators. Once the survey data is collected and analysed, presentations of preliminary results will be given to the sectors, so that sectors may use the data as they develop their strategic plans for 2021. Subsequent presentations of results (e.g., to the HCT) will include more advanced analysis and will be conducted in time to feed into the 2021 HNO/HRP process. The final, written outputs will include a final report, plus a set of fact sheets for each sector and targeted mantika.

Rapid Needs Assessments: REACH proposes to conduct rapid assessments at the onset of humanitarian emergencies in Libya, to inform effective and rapid humanitarian action. This activity will directly benefit the humanitarian community, including the inter-sector coordination group (ISCG), UN agencies, and international and national NGOs, and ultimately vulnerable communities in need of assistance in Libya. In coordination with humanitarian coordination structures such as the ISCG, REACH will activate its network of Key Informants to collect information and release findings in the form of a report and (if relevant) accompanying maps on an accelerated timeline after the sudden crisis. These findings will provide humanitarian rapid responders with a timely and up-to-date situation overview, as well as information on priority needs, allowing humanitarian actors to implement an informed response.
 
Technical Support to sector-led assessments: REACH proposes to provide technical support and capacity building to the humanitarian sectors active in Libya, as they plan, design and implement their own assessments in 2020. The objectives of this support will be to help ensure that the assessments that REACH supports produce high-quality, relevant and actionable outputs, as well as to strengthen the sectors’ long-term capacity to collect, analyze and share data. The ultimate goal in providing such support will be to assist the humanitarian sector in producing a more diverse pool of up-to-date data and analyses to draw upon when planning and implementing activities in Libya. This technical support is not meant to replace the sectors’ important leadership role in conducting these assessments, but rather to enhance it by providing sectors with a valuable resource that will help them achieve their assessment objectives.

project_name: Protection environment for Libyans and non Libyans is enhanced, and capacity of local communities and actors is strengthened
project_objective:
The IRC will  provide  an  immediate  response  to  vulnerable  people in need of protection services – including Internally Displaced People, refugees, migrants, returnees, and vulnerable non-displaced Libyans, with a specific focus on women and girls, children and people with mental health-related issues in urban areas and in detention. Building on IRC’s successful integrated model, the IRC will use its Reproductive Health teams as an entry point to identify and create trust with women and girls, thus creating a space of trust for disclosure of potential GBV incidents in Tripoli, Misrata (and surroudings), Ghat and Ubari. IRC will do so in PHCs, women and girls' safe spaces, or through local CSOs. 
With the MHPSS component that bridges from Health to Protection the IRC will ensure the continuity of service provision across all sectors, with specialized GBV and Case Management capacity, in addition to General Practitioners trained on mhGap, and clinical psychiatrists available in multiple PHCs. 
Similarly, the availability of pediatricians in the teams will be an excellent entry point for child-protection activities. IRC teams will have child protection and facilitators who will carry out recreational and PSS activities with children while their family members are in the PHCs, while visiting local schools and communities, or in children safe spaces.
In addition to the integrated approach with Health, the Protection teams will also maintain a stand-alone capacity by working with local CSOs, local authorities (MOSA, and schools) and in children and women safe spaces that will target exclusively children and women and girls respectively. 
Mobile Teams activities will be complemented by robust community outreach activities to raise awareness on availability of services. This strong link between the community and the public facilities allows for better follow up of cases, case management, and referrals. 
The teams activities will include protection led GBV and psychosocial support services, creating a service package of case management, mental health and psychosocial support services to survivors of SGBV. Additionally, SGBV case workers will be trained alongside the health staff on clinical care for sexual assault survivors (CCSAS) and mental health gap action plan (mhGAP) to promote comprehensive care for survivors.
The IRC will work to strengthen its existing referral systems with local and international actors to maximize the number of people who receive appropriate next levels of protection care. 
The IRC will provide technical trainings and assistance to local actors, including local CSOs, public stakeholders, community leaders and community volunteers to effectively respond to emerging needs and improve the urban and community based protection space. Working with targeted communities of migrants, the IRC will support the development of CBP action plans, and fund identify actions to strengthen community based resilience.

project_name: Prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë moderée chez les enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes
project_objective:
La malnutrition aiguë demeure un problème de santé publique majeur au Tchad avec une prévalence de malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG) estimée à 12,9% et, avec une prévalence de la malnutrition aiguë sévère (MAS) estimée à 2.9%. On note de fortes disparités régionales avec douze (15) provinces sur les vingt-trois (23) que compte le pays, ayant une prévalence de la MAG dépassant le seuil critique de 15% fixé par l’OMS et ou MAS au-delà des seuils d'urgence.
Le traitement de la malnutrition aiguë modérée s’inscrit dans le cadre global de la prise en charge intégrée de la malnutrition aiguë qui comporte d’autre composantes telles que la mobilisation communautaire pour l’identification et le suivi des cas de malnutrition et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère en ambulatoire et en hospitalisation. C'est pour cela que le PAM a inscrit dans son plan de réponse pour l'année 2020 une assistance nutritionnelle aux enfants 6-59 mois et aux femmes enceintes et allaitantes souffrant de MAM afin de les réhabiliter.

project_name: Contain the spread of the COVID-19 epidemic and decrease morbidity and mortality in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
By 29th April 2020, from the onset of the infectious Corona virus disease (COVID-19), 3,018,952 confirmed cases and 207 973 deaths were reported globally, with the WHO Africa Region reporting 23,254 confirmed cases, and 903 deaths . In Nigeria, as of 30th April 2020, 1,932 confirmed cases were reported, with 58 deaths. UNICEF’s water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) humanitarian response in northeast Nigeria,  which plays two roles: as service provider; and as the provider of last resort (POLR), is going to be adapted to ensure critical services are continued, while incorporating new interventions, as well as modifying on-going activities to contribute to COVID-19 transmission risk reduction. 

UNICEF’s interventions will have specific target IDP camps in Maiduguri Metropolitan City and 10 LGAs (Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Jere, Kara Balge, Konduga, Mafa, Mobbar, Monguno, and Ngala), targeted under the on-going HRP. In addition to these locations, UNICEF’s WASH support will also target the whole HRP PIN, by supporting the WASH sector coordination, as well as making available critical supplies as POLR to address sector gaps across the 3 BAY states. project_name: ASISTENCIA ALIMENTARIA Y PRODUCTIVA EN 9 COMEDORES Y 720 PATIOS PRODUCTIVOS DE LA CIUDAD DE MARACAY, ESTADO ARAGUA
project_objective:
El presente proyecto plantea el desarrollo de asistencia alimentaria en poblaciones  vulnerables de la ciudad de Maracay del estado Aragua, con problemas de acceso físico y económico a la ingesta alimentaria básica (2300 Kcal/pers/día) , y con imposibilidades de desarrollar una actividad económica y agrícolas por la situación país. La propuesta establece, el suministro de una comida diaria a los niñas y niños, adultos mayores, personas especiales y mujeres en situación de riesgo y la producción familiar en dichos grupos o grupos complementarios seleccionados para estas actividades, para obtener alimentos de importancia calórica y proteica.
La propuesta comprende tres acciones: 
1) Elaboración y entrega de alimentos a los grupos de riesgos, mas necesitados, de las poblaciones de los comedores de las Instituciones, Alimenta La Solidaridad A C y la Iglesia Evangélica Pentecostés La Vid Verdadera, en los comedores ya constituidos, con ampliación del 151% y 300% respectivamente, y al menos 80 patios en producción alrededor o cercanas a cada comedor, para 720 patios totales.
2) Establecimiento de Subsistemas de Producción, en familias que reciben alimentos o complementarias o relacionas a los comedores, que entregarán parte de la producción a los comedores, los sistemas productivos serán: 2.1) Animal: Cunícola y aves ponedoras (gallinas y codornices) y 2.2) Vegetal: maíz jojoto, leguminosas, batata y hortalizas diversas. 
3) Establecimiento de Subsistemas post cosecha y transformación, familias que reciben alimentos o familias complementarias, que entregarán parte de la producción a los comedores, capacitándolos en manejo postcosecha y procesamiento de alimentos: aliños, salsas, concentrados, mermeladas etc. 
 La Facultad de Agronomía de la Universidad Central de Venezuela (FAGRO-UCV) se encuentra en  Maracay, ciudad donde están ubicación  los comedores, posee amplia experiencia y expertos (con más de 15 años de experiencia) en el desarrollo comunitario y los trabajos de extensión agrícola.

project_name: Fortalecimiento comunitario para la seguridad alimentaria y protección de población vulnerable, en 8 estados de Venezuela
project_objective:
Buscando dar respuesta a la situación alimentaria y nutricional que afecta a Venezuela, desde el año 2016, Meals4Hope desarrolla, en zonas pobres del interior del país, programas para fortalecer la resiliencia y brindar seguridad alimentaria y protección a familias vulnerables, atendiendo prioritariamente a niños, niñas, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL). 
Estos programas (Casas Comunitarias, Comedores Escolares, Ollas/Comedores Comunitarios) se adaptan a las necesidades y características de cada zona. En ellos, se apoya y capacita a mujeres de las comunidades para la auto-gestión. La participación activa de las comunidades y las alianzas locales son elementos fundamentales en el éxito y sostenibilidad de los mismos.
El presente proyecto busca fortalecer y ampliar la cobertura de programas en marcha en 8 estados del país, atendiendo un total de 6.500 personas vulnerables. Con enfoque multisectorial, se desarrollan actividades de seguridad alimentaria, agua e higiene y protección.  
Con enfoque humanitario y de desarrollo, se promueve la organización comunitaria y el empoderamiento de las mujeres; se brinda alimentación nutritiva diaria (buscando asegurar el 45-50% de los requerimientos diarios de energía y proteínas) y protección integral los niños/as, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes y a sus familias, incluyendo apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal. 
Se promueve, también, la producción agropecuaria de escala familiar/comunitaria para obtener alimentos de importancia proteica y calórica - aves ponedoras, pollos de engorde, huertos de hortalizas y leguminosas- que se dirigen a los programas de alimentación y familias participantes.
Como apoyo a la nutrición, se propone la promoción/orientación en materia de agua segura y condiciones de higiene adecuadas y la distribución de productos de higiene. El mejoramiento del agua, higiene y saneamiento de los centros en los que trabajamos, se plantea en el proyecto complementario ‘Techos de Esperanza’, propuesta presentada junto con la Fundación TECHO. 
El presente proyecto trabaja y asegura la perspectiva de género y plantea el monitoreo y evaluación participativa como instrumentos de aprendizaje y rendición de cuentas.

project_name: Food assistance for vulnerable populations affected by the Beirut port explosion.
project_objective:
WFP will provide immediate, life-saving in-kind food and cash assistance for to up to 420,000 vulnerable beneficiaries in order to: a) protect the food security of the vulnerable blast-affected population through the provision of in-kind assistance; and b) to meet food needs of the most vulnerable populations whose livelihoods have been affected by the triple shock of the blast, COVID-19, and economic crisis. 

In the immediate response to explosion-affected populations who lost their homes in the blast, WFP will provide hot meals through support to communal kitchens, and take-home rations to up to 5,000 families, who will reive a 60kg food parcel, which includes rice, pasta, bulgur, chickpeas, vegetable oil, sugar, and salt, enough to feed a family of five for one month. 

WFP will target up to 150,000 explosion-affected vulnerable, food in-secure individuals with a cash-based transfer to cover food needs, plus a multi-purpose cash top-up to meet the essential needs.

In addition, WFP will target up to 270,000 food-insecure individuals affected by the triple shock of the blast, COVID-19, and economic crisis, with a cash-based transfer to cover food needs.

project_name: Caritas Lebanon - Beirut Blast (shelter)
project_objective:
The overarching aim of this project is to ensure the protection of vulnerable populations, to provide access of vulnerable households, for both displaced and host communities, IN ADDITION TO MIGRANT WORKER POPULATIONS, to physically adequate and safe shelters with security of tenure. This is accomplished through the provision of protection-focused shelter assistance that addresses the inadequacies in terms of the safety of vulnerable households.
This project will apply the standards set through technical guidelines on selected shelter activities drafted by the sector working group, UN partners and LRC to maximize impact, complement services and avoid duplication.

In response to the crisis, Caritas Lebanon (CL) will provide cash for shelter activities and minor renovation direct interventions to enable vulnerable households whose shelters were damaged to carry out essential repairs to ensure protection from the elements. The assistance will be provided as direct renovation interventions through a preset renovation methodology and quality assurance guidelines.

The intervention will ensure that rehabilitation of shelters will not lead to evictions or rent increases (do no harm) for the tenants. Finally, this intervention will be accompanied by services provided by other projects that fall under other sectors such as psychological first aid and psychosocial support.

Caritas Lebanon (CL) will organize trainings and ongoing technical capacity building through direct mentoring all along the project’s implementation. 

The emergency response will assist 2180 AFFECTED HOUSEHOLDS (approx. 10,900 INDIVIDUALS) in the economically vulnerable neighborhoods of Beirut and Metn. Eligible households will be selected impartially strengthening social cohesion in the affected areas.

The selection criteria will include
-	Inclusion: This sector will primarily target the general need of shelter of the vulnerable population affected by the blast while ensuring the inclusion of different age groups, gender and diversity, ESPECIALLY THE DISPLACED AND MIGRANT WORKER POPULATIONS.
-	Targeted assistance to the most vulnerable households: Caritas will determine eligibility based on the needs assessment reports set out by UN Habitat and LRC. Special attention will be given to
o	Female headed households
o	Elderlies
o	Household with PWD
o	Household with dead family member
o	Household with heavily injured member
-	Coordination with local actors: Understanding the holistic needs of affected communities requires inter-sectoral collaboration. Shelter assistance will be coordinated between partners within the sector and with activities of other sectors for improved impact and complementarity of interventions where applicable, including but not limited to protection and health concerns.
-	Safeguarding social stability and livelihood: Coordination with the above mentioned partners to ensure adequate housing conditions

project_name: Building resilience and self-reliance of Rohingya refugee women and adolescent girls and livelihoods opportunities for host community women and adolescent girls
project_objective:
This project aims to increase resilience, self-reliance and socio-economic empowerment of Rohingya and host community women and adolescent girls through enhanced skills training, start-up support and marketing opportunities.
It generates better opportunities for women and adolescent girls to learn, develop skills and access services, through context specific learning programmes of life and livelihood skills combined with income generation activities, tailored not only to their needs as learners, but also towards their future as earners. Based on the needs assessment/baseline, adolescent girls and women will learn livelihood skills (a mix of vocational, technical and business skills during 6 months courses ) and will be supported to participate in self-reliance/livelihood activities and cash for work programs that will help them contribute income to their family. These activities will be organized initially in UN Women’s five existing Multi-Purpose Women’s Centers in the camps, which provide basic social and GBV counseling/ referral services for women, and in three additional MPWCs in the host communities.  Each center will organize four courses for two groups during the project life. Selection of participants for these activities will be done on improved criteria, so that the most marginalised women/girls, including women with disabilities and female headed households, will be selected for these activities.
Addressing immediate needs of refugees, UN Women has opened and runs five multi-purpose women’s centres (MPWCs) in camps 3, 4, 4 extension, 5, and 18, and will establish three new MPWCs in the host community, for comprehensive services for women and girls as well as for women to receive livelihoods and portable skills training. Based on the needs assessment/baseline, adolescent girls and (young) women will learn livelihood skills (a mix of vocational, technical and business skills during 6 months courses ) and will be supported to participate in income-generating/livelihood activities and cash for work programs that will help them contribute income to their family. Rohingya and host community women and adolescent girls who complete the livelihood training will be provided with in-kind support to start or expand self-reliance/livelihood activities. Women’s Centres will have production units that women can join for collective production of goods (e.g. reusable sanitary pads to supply to humanitarian agencies, or crafts to be sold in commercial outlets) that will be used in the camps.  At the same time, central cooking facilities will be established for women to use to run snack making and catering services following the current pilot in Camp 4. Joint socio-economic activities will also be conducted between Rohingya and host community women and adolescent girls in order to promote social cohesion. One of the Women’s Centres will have a “Women’s Market Place” established for both Rohingya and Host community women to buy and sell their goods and products. Market driven self-reliance/livelihood interventions will be explored to promote socio-economic self-reliance and reducing over-reliance of refugees on in-kind humanitarian assistance.

project_name: Beirut Temporary Port Operation
project_objective:
WFP will contribute to the continuity of operations at Beirut Port, through two inter-linked components: a) provision of wheat flour through the Port of Beirut and b) temporary deployment of bulk grain handling equipment to facilitate the arrival and discharge of bulk grain. Most of the grain will be discharged directly to the facilities that will process the grain though they may be a need to have some storage capacity in the port when direct delivery is not possible.  
WFP will provide a one-time injection of 12,500mt of wheat flour to fill the immediate gap in the wheat supply chain, to be distributed via the national bread distribution channels, in order to stabilize the price of bread across Lebanon.
Through its port operation, WFP will temporarily augment the capacity at Beirut Port by providing temporary bulk grain handling equipment that will allow for the handling of at least 3,000mt of grain per day, such as grain evacuators, grain grabs, forklifts, front-end loaders, along with temporary bulk storage capacity. This will enable the continued flow of grain into Lebanon, and ensure there is no disruption in the commercial food supply chain.
The focus on the bulk grain handling capability and storage capacity will restore key capabilities that were lost during the incident in the Beirut port. The bulk grain handling capability will support the commercial sector to continue to bring in the grains necessary to run their operations that are critical to maintaining stable food prices, in particular bread prices.

project_name: Improve community safety & accelerate the return of displaced households to their homes through rapid stabilization of evacuated structurally damaged residential buildings as a precursor to structural repair.
PROJECT REVISED - Provision of Shelter/NFI to vulnerable beneficiaries in Jubaland State.
project_objective:
The project targeting 4 districts in Lower Juba seeks to improve access and be responsive to the shelter needs of displaced populations, especially those that have been in protracted displacement. 

 Kismaayo is believed to have the largest IDP population in the region mostly located in Farjano and Fanole areas. Recent IDPs profiling conducted by Norwegian Refugee Council indicated that there are 6,059 IDPs households in Kismaayo towns in 80 settlements. In Dhobley and its surroundings, there are 6 settlements with approximately 1,380 households.Considering Kismayo has the highest rate of IDPs emanating from Lower Shabelle, Banadir, Gedo, Bay and Middle Juba the area will be given more emphasis. 

As of July 2019, 51,000 new internal displacements were monitored by the UNHCR-led Protection and Returns Monitoring Network (PRMN). Of the 244,000 new displacements monitored year-to date, drivers include insecurity (126,000), drought related (101,000), floods (6,000) and other reasons (10,000). In 2019, conflict/insecurity and drought are the biggest causes of displacement with 126,000 and 101,000 respectively.  Lower Juba counts as among the top ten in arrivals in 2019, and fifth in July 2019. 

HAPEN assessment indicate a high prevalence of households living in poor quality makeshift shelters ( made of simple twigs covered with tattered pieces of old clothes, and polythene), which offer little structural integrity and protection from the vagaries of nature. Poor shelter conditions also raise serious protection concerns as households are more vulnerable to crime, GBV and child protection issues. According to REACH initiative, shelter was listed as a priority need by 48% of households, with over half of households listing it as a priority in nine regions. Shelter was highlighted by 60% of IDP households as a priority need, the second most commonly identified need after food (89%).

In the project area they are settling, the UNHCR, Protection, Monitoring and Return Network cite high levels of human rights violations, including increased GBV incidents With those who have settled in Lower Juba being predominantly returnees, the projects will be designed to ensure the interventions are protection responsive. The interventions will target the most vulnerable giving emphasis to households with under five children, pregnant and lactating women Persons with Disabilities and old people. 

Aligning to strategic and Shelter&NFI clusters strategies, HAPEN aims at improving the living conditions and protection of IDPs and returnees in sites whilst ensuring equitable access to services and assistance for the drought and conflict displaced IDPs.

In alignment with other clusters, HAPEN 1) build better coordination mechanisms structures at site/community level 2) protection mainstreaming through awareness raising and trainings, and creation of proper referral pathways for GBV survivors.

HAPEN will provide shelter/NFI assistance to 60,000 vulnerable beneficiaries. The beneficiaries support will include;Distribution of NFI Kits(10,000), distribution of emergency shelter kit (4,000), provision of transitional shelter assistance (900), and construction/rehabilitation of community infrastructure (10 infrastructures benefiting 5,000). 

HAPEN will use CVA to deliver significant portion of the interventions. In this regards, in all projects with the CVA component, working with clusters, ICCG, and Cash Working Group HAPEN will undertake assessment to ensure the appropriateness and identify the best modality to use.  In line with the in-kind programming, shelter-specific cash programming will be coordinated through the shelter program with any shelter integrated through ICCG.  HAPEN shall report on agreed cash monitoring indicators in the 3W matrix and by sharing post-distribution monitoring reports with the respective clusters.

project_name: Providing Quality Integrated Primary healthcare including reproductive healthcare services to conflict affected IDPs and host communities in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States
project_objective:
The IRC will continue to build and consolidate on the gains achieved through OFDA, ECHO, SIDA and NHF/OCHA funding in response to the protracted crises in the North-east which has resulted in influx of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and negatively impacted host communities in the BAY states. The IRC seeks to strengthen provision of comprehensive primary healthcare services including and reproductive healthcare services for internally displaced persons and host community members through direct treatment at IRC supported health facilities both in IDP camps and selected government health facilities in all the IRC targeted LGAs (Maiduguri, Monguno, Akira-uba and Gwoza, Bama, Mafa, Konduga, Magumeri LGAs in Borno state, at Yobe at Damaturu, Gulani and Gujiba LGAs with potential to expand to Adamawa LGAs.)  
In addition, the IRC will further strengthen the provision of health care services by improving the referral system to access secondary care and strengthen community based surveillance and optimize community engagement through working with community health workers increate demand for service utilization and increased coverage.    
The provision of integrated primary health care services which includes reproductive health service targeting adolescent girls and boys, women of child bearing age, and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), family planning, post abortion care, clinical management of rape for all identified cases of gender based violence, (GBV) ante-natal services, post-natal services, and syndromic management of sexually transmitted infection (STIs) services and psychosocial support.
The IRC, in the case of a disease outbreak will be flexible in preparation and response to respond through its existing Country Emergency Team (CET) adapting its programming to effectively respond with support of existing community structures and propositioned medicines and supplies/products.
The IRC hopes to reach a total of 302, 475 individuals disaggregated as follows men 72,594 women 108, 891 boys 48,396 and girls 72,594

project_name: Improving lifesaving health ,nutrition and psychosocial services of  vulnerable mothers and children in area C in West Bank
project_objective: The overall objective is: “To improve the health of vulnerable mothers and children in Area C in Hebron and Nablus through community preventive health and nutrition intervention services. “The specific objectives: • Vulnerable children <5 , neonates , pregnant and lactating women have access to life sustaining interventions Mental health and psychosocial services are provided to vulnerable mothers and to vulnerable children at schools. The project responds to the First cluster objective “Ensure the availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of essential lifesaving health services to the most vulnerable communities in Gaza and the West Bank /EJ including through health system strengthening, preparedness and community resilience building.” The selected interventions will be implemented at three levels; households, schools and community; using a multidisciplinary health approach. project_name: Improved WASH services to the conﬂict affected population in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
Nigeria’s North-East continues to experience intricate and multi-faceted humanitarian crisis in the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector, as a result of the ongoing protracted conflict, unpredictable and continuous large-scale population displacements, recurrent large-scale cholera epidemics and seasonal flooding, and fierce storms and winds. 
The main drivers of vulnerabilities related to WASH are closely linked to the conflict, including recurrent, unpredictable and continuous population displacements. They are also a result of pre-existing low levels of WASH services.

In response to the needs identified and in contribution to strategic Sector objective 1, 2 and 3 of the WASH sector, IOM will scale-up its provision of WASH services targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host community in camp and camp-like settings. 
To this end, IOM will (A) Ensure safe access to safe water facilities and services through the drilling, installation, maintenance and rehabilitation of boreholes; (B) Ensure safe access to sanitation facilities (latrines, showers, handwashing stations) through the operation and maintenance of existing facilities and the construction of additional gender segregated facilities; (C) Promote improved water and sanitation outcomes in targeted settings through the systematic promotion of hygiene messages and the support for increased capacity of established community-based committees..; (D) Ensure environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in operation area through establishment of WASH Committee including- male and female community members, procurement and distribution of tools and equipment; (E) Distribution of WASH non-food items (NFI); and (F) Capacity building and partnership with WASH partners and stakeholders 
 
The IOM WASH project will be implemented in three States of North East Nigeria: Borno (8 LGAs), Adamawa (5 LGAs) and Yobe State (4 LGAs), targeting 150,047 individuals. 
IOM ensures that all WASH activities take into consideration the age, gender as well as disability -specific needs of project beneficiaries. Through this project, IOM will guarantee the participation and special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and age group, and specifically address women and girls’ specific needs, such as Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM). All activities related to this project will equally benefit women and men, girls and boys and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. In regard to assessments, monitoring and evaluation of gender, age and disability specific needs, and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels where possible. IOM will ensure that “Do No Harm” principles are adhered to throughout the WASH interventions, particularly in WASH activities pertaining to latrine and water point locations and construction.

project_name: Provision of Life-saving Primary Health Care, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, and Outbreak Response Services for Vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and Affected Host Communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
Since the beginning of the conflict in December 2013, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has been providing lifesaving humanitarian assistance to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees and host communities in conflict affected locations across South Sudan. The proposed project will build on IOM's significant experience in the provision of health and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services, and will continue to support rapid response mechanisms, which provide lifesaving health services to conflict-affected populations in hard-to-access areas. In 2020, IOM will continue to provide and scale up the provision of integrated primary health care (PHC), and MHPSS services through eight static Primary Health Care Units (PHCU), five mobile clinics, fourteen immunization focused static/mobile clinics and through eight rapid response team (RRT) deployments. The different modalities of response and conflict sensitive approaches enable IOM to ensure that services are accessed by both IDPs and conflict affected host communities, prioritizing the greatest needs.

Through static and rapid response teams, IOM will continue to provide essential preventative and curative PHC and MHPSS services in Bentiu, Malakal and Wau Protection of Civilian (PoC) sites, and other locations across South Sudan, targeting a total of 182,531 beneficiaries, of which 80,000 will be reached through mobile rapid response teams, and 102,531 will be reached through IOM’s static PHCU facilities. Health services will be provided in line with the Health Cluster’s essential health care package for PHCUs and Mobile Teams.

project_name: Common Transport Services for Humanitarian Partners in South Sudan
project_objective:
The Common Transport Services (CTS) is a free-for-user service that transports key humanitarian supplies on behalf of humanitarian actors. CTS serves as a critical link in the supply chain, enabling products and materials that arrive from regional and international suppliers to rapidly move onwards to partners located deep in the field. 

IOM has been managing the CTS on behalf of the Logistics Cluster since 2011, during which time the project has significantly grown from delivering 2,000 MT of humanitarian cargo in 2011 to a total of approximately 30,000 MT by the end of 2019, highlighting the increase in the use of road transport as access improves. IOM has continued to maintain flexibility and adaptability to the operating environment in South Sudan. 

IOM works with more than 80 unique agencies in key operational locations in Jonglei, Unity and Greater Upper Nile Region, in Humanitarian Logistics Hubs (Malakal, Melut, Bentiu) and in Rumbek, Bor, Juba and Wau. IOM will maintain heavy vehicles and transport cargo from the main ports of dispatch via air, road and river and will continue warehouse management in key operational locations. These logistics hubs will support service provision to priority locations.

IOM will also ensure to adjust their service provision to accommodate Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) preparedness efforts, which was already the case in 2019 with the provision of a dedicated UNHAS EVD aircraft and common logistics services (cargo movements and warehousing) in high risks locations.

Through the effective management of the CTS, IOM aims to support organizations’ preparedness measures to mitigate risk associated with increased insecurity, looting/theft of humanitarian supplies, critical access impediments to very vulnerable people and reduce expensive air and road transport costs, which ultimately supports the timely response to the needs of the affected populations. In 2020, IOM will directly work with 80 humanitarian organizations located in different areas enabling them to deliver critical life-saving humanitarian services and assistance items.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of Camp Coordination and Camp Management services to men, women, boys and girls in displacement sites in Somalia
project_objective:
It is estimated that there are 2.6 million internally displaced persons in Somalia. Successive years of drought exacerbated by a prolonged conflict has resulted in an enduring humanitarian crisis that demands urgent life-saving interventions. But at the same time, the protracted nature of this crisis requires a strategy that sees beyond the immediate needs and incorporates durable solutions throughout the response. With this project IOM will provide camp management and camp coordination services to men, women, boys and girls in displacement sites in the districts of Baidoa, Kismayu and Doolow to ensure that the most urgent needs of the IDPs are met, while also working towards the achievement of durable solutions for displaced families.

Latest estimations of displacement conditions in Somalia indicate that around 1.8 million people have settled in almost 2,000 IDP sites, most of which are informal, small and scattered settlements in urban or peri-urban areas. Living in private land often means that IDPs are at constant risk of eviction, which further stresses their already vulnerable situation. Protracted conflict-driven displacement aggravated by natural disasters, limited livelihood opportunities, limited availability of public services and limited access to durable solutions all contribute to the continued increase in the number and vulnerability of IDPs. 

Baidoa hosts the largest number of IDPs after Mogadishu with more than 362,000 displaced persons living in 435 sites. Recently government authorities have allocated public land for IDPs which has enabled IOM and other humanitarian/development partners to relocate families at risk of eviction, linking traditional CCCM activities with an approach tailored towards the achievement of durable solutions. As more public land becomes available to IDPs, IOM plans to support more families to relocate. However, for the foreseeable future the majority of families will remain in makeshift sites under the constant threat of forced eviction.

In Kismayu, 59,200 IDPs are hosted in 133 sites. These sites are privately owned and most IDPs have to pay to live there; however, these agreements do not prevent families from the risk of being evicted. Most of these IDP sites are overcrowded and lack basic infrastructure; living conditions are poor with overstretched services and shelters often made of locally available materials such as plastic and worn-out clothes.

Doolow is currently hosting around 50,700 IDPs in two makeshift sites located in public land: Kabasa and Qansaxley. The high population density in these camps and the subsequent concentration of service provision makes service monitoring and coordination key aspects of CCCM related needs. In addition, community mobilization and the enactment of representative governance structures are needed to facilitate dialogue between service providers and affected populations, and to enhance accountability towards them.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Informing humanitarian planning and response to the needs of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Somalia through baseline assessments and population-based surveys
project_objective:
Maintain and strengthen the system of data collection in Somalia through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the coordination of humanitarian activities. The DTM provides reliable and up to date information on the number of displaced populations, their location, profile, displacement trends, reasons for displacement, and needs disaggregated by age and sex to better assist and inform the governmental and humanitarian response. The DTM has the potential to be expanded and/or modified to take into account changes in the national context and need to inform durable solutions.

Needs Assessment: Somalia continues to be affected by a humanitarian crisis triggered by natural and man-made factors. While the drought crisis and floods have subsided, the effects of these shocks are still felt across affected areas and residents remain internally displaced. Latest displacement estimates place the number of IDPs in Somalia at 2.6 million people. This continued displacement puts further pressure on areas and populations recovering from previous crises. Protracted conflict-driven displacement, aggravated by natural disasters, limited returns to areas of origin, limited self-sufficiency, and limited access to durable solutions contribute to the continued increase in the number and vulnerability of IDPs. Given access constrains in Somalia, overall IDP figures and needs are calculated through the triangulation of multiple data sources (including IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix). Each data source uses different methodologies and indicators which makes the creation of a commonly agreed overview of the situation cumbersome and likely unprecise. In addition, Somalia remains characterized by the lack of systematic displacement tracking tools and limited information on IDPs residing in host communities, potentially hampering the effective delivery of humanitarian assistance to a significant part of the IDP population. As such, IOM intends to assist in the implementation of CCCM Cluster tools and to complement them by filling gaps in displacement-related information through its DTM and ad hoc surveys informing durable solutions. In addition, while multiple actors work in Information Management, an under-served need relates to the reinforcement of Government operational capacities in data collection and Information Management. As such, IOM intends to work closely with relevant Government authorities to reinforce their capacities, including through the implementation of joint surveys, and the provision of technical assistance, as well as the support in designing Information Management tools and products.

project_name: Improved food security and strengthened resilience of vulnerable households affected by conflict and displacement in Syria.
project_objective:
NRC’s project will contribute to Food Security (FS) sector HRP objectives 1, 2 and 3   . NRC will implement its FS activities through a combination of direct and partner-led modalities, depending on context and access. The NRC Food Security project seeks to build resilience by providing a pathway from acute food needs to greater self-reliance and livelihood recovery, with a focus on the restoration of agricultural livelihoods related to food production and commercialization.
Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level (including the Cash Working Group), and access.  
NRC will provide Food Security assistance to vulnerable conflict and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities, IDP and refugee returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the conflict.  
1.	Emergency Response:  Vulnerable households can meet basic needs. 
To ensure the protection productive assets of displacement affected households and to ensure that households can meet basic needs and reduce negative coping strategies.  

Cash Based Assistance: Unrestricted Cash Based Assistance as a primary response modality to empower households to define and attain their own specific needs whenever appropriate. 
Information and Behaviour Change: Cash based assistance will be accompanied by information about the importance of dietary diversity and nutritious dietary choices to increase the impact of cash in promoting food security outcomes

2.	Economic Recovery: Vulnerable households achieve self-reliance through own-food production and/or income generation. 
To facilitate the transition of displacement affected populations from humanitarian assistance to self-reliance. NRC will use market-based approaches to facilitate access to demand driven income generation activities.   

Home-Based Food Production: targeted grants (cash or in-kind) to support home-based food production and training in food production techniques.  
Income Generation: Access to income-generation activities through access to temporary emergency income and grants (cash / in-kind) to support income generation, and basic business skills training.   

3.	Inclusive Markets: Households achieve resilience through sustainable livelihoods and inclusive markets.
 To promote the development and access to inclusive markets that enable displacement affected populations fully restore their sustainable livelihoods.  

Sectoral Market Based Support:  Sectoral Market Based Support interventions to focus on the development of agricultural livelihoods. Targeted grants (or kits) supported with training, mentoring, and market access support to maximize impact.
Market Access Support: NRC will focus on the following core areas to promote inclusive markets for Conflict Affected Syrians: Employment Facilitation, Entrepreneurship, Local Capacity Strengthening and Infrastructure Rehabilitation

project_name: Supporting the most marginalized households in the camps and the communities that experienced the recent IDP influxes  through multi-sectoral Protection interventions
project_objective:
The project will prioritize the most marginalized within the IDP camps and the communities who have exhausted their resources and coping mechanism, and at higher risk of losing or damaging their lives and dignity. Household vulnerability are interrelated, one aspect could lead further constrains, multiplying vulnerability of the marginalized groups. 
Therefore, the proposed project aims at abbreviating household vulnerability through integrated protection interventions), addressing the particular needs of the most marginalized households within the IDP camps and communities that have recently experienced IDP influxes. The project places special attentions on outreaching the person with functional difficulties, that is now estimated to be 10-15 % of prevalence in the Syrian society. While their functional levels and capacities vary, the severely affected are considered not having adequate access to humanitarian assistance, and at blink of further deterioration of their conditions. The project ensures at least 1200 (20 % of the direct beneficiaries) are persons with functional difficulties and consequently, their families’ members also get benefits from the project, in total, over 6000 people will be reached. 
As only few facilities are providing specialized service, the project will engage mobile outreach modality to provide specialized supports (physiotherapy, PSS, nursing, assistive devices) to outreach 700 persons living with functional difficulties in the camps and the communities. 
In addition, the mobile outreach teams  following survivors consent will conduct referrals to GBV specialized services if they come cross a GBV cases . Through in-house health referral mechanism to HIHFAD center that annexed to Maternity and Children Hospital as well as collaboration with other GBV actors, survivors of GBV will have access to service in a timely manner. 
Case management supports 300 persons living with functional difficulties, including referral and vocational training opportunities for 25 beneficiaries. 
Throughout the project, inclusion mainstreaming will be enhanced. The project will provide inclusion mainstreaming training to the humanitarian actors based in Syria, thus they can provide more accessible service across their on-going interventions. 
In order to fight against social stigma, inclusion awareness sessions will be widely conducted in the communities and in camps, in addition to four community-based inclusion events will be organized with direct inputs from the beneficiaries. The project also establishes a peer support group among the caregivers of the children with functional difficulties, so they could exchange their experiences and create a mutual support network.
HIHFAD is committed to promote inclusive employment, six persons with functional difficulties will be employed, four within HIHFAD and two with other organizations with their salary substituted by the project.
This project also aims to enhance the psychosocial wellbeing and protection of 400 children and 400 care giver through conducting child resilience programme activities in the already existing child spaces (integrated with rehabilitation centers in Armanz and Albab that also provide Physical rehabilitation, PSS, Peer Support and Speech Therapy).

project_name: Support in Food Security and Livelihoods for Vulnerable Populations in Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA), South Sudan
project_objective:
The proposed projects seeks to support 5,000 vulnerable households (30,000 individuals) to regain their livelihoods by providing farming inputs and training on better agricultural methods in crop production as well as vegetable production. From this number, 300 female headed household (1,800 individuals) will be purposefully targeted for to receive additional support in the form of an unconditional cash transfer. In addition, the project will also target 1,000 (6,000 individuals) fisher folk households with training on better fishing methods accompanied with distribution of fishing kits. Therefore, in total, 6,000 households (36,000 individuals) will be targeted. Part of the selection criteria of beneficiaries will be based on the Food Consumption Score (FCS) and Coping Strategy Index (CSI). WFP approved tools will be used to ensure that the correct data is collected.
Activities will be aligned to the seasonal calendar and based strictly on the livelihood activities of target communities in the target area i.e. farming and fishing. During lean periods, vegetable farming will be promoted while crop farming will be carried out during the rainy season. In between, fishing activities will be promoted to complement both crop farming and vegetable farming. This mix of activities is aimed at protecting crop seeds from consumption and also serves as a protection strategy towards discouraging adoption of negative coping practices within households. The expected outcome of the intervention is the rebuilding of livelihood assets for target population as well as improving their dietary intake. The multiplier effect of this is the improvement of the coping capacity of target beneficiaries. IDPs, returnees and host communities will all be targeted since the project is needs driven.
To avoid duplication of efforts, activities will be coordinated through Food Security and Livelihoods cluster at county, state and national levels. Regular and timely reporting will be provided through progress reports as well as though the 5W matrix.

Elle intègre une approche multisectorielle visant à contribuer à la couverture des besoins de base et au renforcement des moyens d’existence des populations vulnérables, notamment réfugiées et retournées, affectées par les conflits et l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dans les provinces du Lac (départements de Mamdi, Wayi et Kaya), du Logone Oriental (départements des Monts de Lam et de la Nya Pendé) et du Batha (département du Batha Ouest).
Cette approche se décline suivant les résultats ci-dessous :
Résultat 1 : Les besoins alimentaires et non alimentaires de base de 3 200 ménages en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle affectés par les aléas climatiques et/ou les conflits, dont 70% ayant au moins un enfant de moins de 5 ans et/ou une FEFA, et 30% dirigés par une femme, sont couverts à travers une réponse intégrée en transferts monétaires multi-usage et en WASH, dans les provinces du Batha, du Logone Oriental et du Lac
Résultat 2 : Les capacités de prévention, préparation et d’adaptation face aux chocs agro climatiques et liés aux conflits de 5900 ménages vulnérables à l’insécurité alimentaire nutritionnelle dont 20 % dirigés par des femmes, sont renforcées dans les provinces du Batha, du Logone Oriental et du Lac
Résultat 3 : La surveillance humanitaire et contextuelle est assurée et une réponse est apportée à 500 ménages, en cas de choc dans les zones d'intervention 
Les activités proposées sont adaptées pour répondre aux besoins spécifiques des groupes de populations (femmes, enfants, jeunes, réfugiés, retournés, population locale et hôte). SI a fait le choix de favoriser l’implication communautaire pour la définition des activités de résilience à mettre en œuvre, via la réalisation de diagnostics communautaires, durant lesquels les communautés mettent en lumières leurs vulnérabilités, leurs besoins prioritaires et leurs capacités et ressources, permettant de prioriser les actions à mener.
Cette stratégie d’intervention intégrant des actions EHA et SAME sera réalisée en coordination avec les autres acteurs des zones concernées, afin de maximiser la couverture, la complémentarité entre acteurs et ainsi l’impact sur les communautés. Des complémentarités fortes sont prévues avec les interventions soudures qu’Acted mènera dans la province du Lac, les actions nutritionnelles menées par la CRF/CRT dans la province du Batha, ainsi qu’avec le projet DIZA en cours et mis en œuvre par SI (lead Caritas Suisse) dans la province du Logone Oriental.
Un mécanisme de suivi-évaluation sera mis en place et permettra le suivi de l’atteinte des indicateurs et de l’avancement des activités, avec des données désagrégées par sexe et par âge.
Un mécanisme de gestion des plaintes sera mis en place, prenant en compte les spécificités et préférences des différents groupes de population (population locale, réfugiée, retournées, hommes, femmes, jeunes, etc.). Ceci permettra une remontée d’informations auxquelles SI apportera une réponse systématique, renforçant la redevabilité.
