project_name: Provision of integrated primary health care services to internally displaced persons and host community in East and South Darfur States
project_objective:
ARC proposed activities are in line with the Outcome 2 in the Humanitarian response plan (HRP), i.e. Displaced populations, refugees, returnees and host communities meet their basic needs and/or access basic services while increasing their self-reliance. The integrated primary health care interventions will be provided with key objective to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with disease among the children under five years, men, women, adolescent boys and girls, women of child bearing age, elderly men and women and people with disability.
ARC has been implementing comprehensive integrated primary health care life-saving interventions supporting 24 primary health care centers; 10 PHCCs in East Darfur and 14 PHCCs in South Darfur. Under this project, ARC will continue to provide basic primary health care services; treatment and diagnosis of communicable diseases, reproductive health, support of referrals for both medical and obstetric emergencies to tertiary level, emergency preparedness and response, prevention activities through health promotion activities by community volunteers, routine immunization, provision of essential drugs, medical and non-medical supplies, clinical management of rape to gender based violence survivors and provision of Psychosocial First Aid (PFA) services. ARC will also strengthen community-based approaches to promote positive health seeking behaviors, recognition of illnesses, and care-seeking practices through trained community structures, community relief development committees and health, nutrition and WASH volunteers network. The project will strengthen institutional capacity through on job training and mentoring to implement sustainable and affordable health interventions that meet the needs of men, women, boys, girls, and children <5 and will utilize the network of WASH, Health and nutrition volunteers to enhance the disease surveillance system including early detection, preparedness and response to emergencies. These activities are in line with the cluster objectives, which are to provide the basic minimum package of primary health care services, including maternal and child health, emergency referral services, training of human resources for health emergencies, and monitoring of health services.
In coordination with line ministries, ARC will ensure the health facilities adhere to approved treatment protocols/guidelines, provision and availability of vaccine and vaccine supplies for routine immunization, support during the acceleration campaigns, national immunization days and celebration of global health international events. In addition to improve the quality of services and build the capacity of the health frontline staffs and line ministries, ARC will conduct refresher trainings and joint monitoring visits with State ministry of health (SMoH) respectively. Through a well-structured Health Information System (HIS), ARC will capture data and submit weekly epidemiology reports to the SMoH including key health indicators on a monthly basis. Data collected will be dis-aggregated by sex and age.
This project will target the IDPs and host communities in South and East Darfur State. Total population target will include 535,770; 341,172 IDPs and 194,598 host community. 17% (91,081) will include children under five years and 21,431(4%) pregnant and lactating women including the elderly and people with disability.

project_name: Provision of WASH services for the populations affected by conflict and displacement in South and East Darfur States
project_objective:
This project aims to achieve sustainable improvement in access to quality water supply, sanitation condition and hygiene practices among IDPs and host communities in East and South Darfur states of Sudan. The project will focus on subsectors of water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, environmental health and WASH Non-food Items (NFIs) with the aim to achieve the following objectives: 
o	Maintain and improve access to safe and clean water in both in the target communities and health and nutrition facilities through new water points, and upgrade and maintenance of existing water infrastructure and services to meet minimum SPHERE standards communities.
o	Continue improvement of the hygiene and sanitation conditions for the targeted beneficiaries in the rural communities and IDPs camps. This will be done through promotion and support in construction of emergency latrines for most vulnerable families, and improved household shared latrines with hand washing points, and promote good hygiene practices among the targeted beneficiaries.
o	Reduce the disease prevalence and health risks of communicable diseases by sustaining water safety and quality through testing and treatment.
o	Promote improved hygiene and sanitation in conjunction with the health and nutrition messaging in target IDP and host communities.
o	Mainstream protection in all WASH activities to protect the population from all potential risks associated with WASH services. 
In order to improve the water supplies in targeted area of operation, environmentally friendly technologies will be used namely water provision through installation of solar pumping systems, monitoring water quality on daily and bi-weekly bases through chlorination and bacteria tests for ensuring safe drinking water provided.  community based operation and maintenance approach will be applied to ensure long lasting water service provision. In design and locating of water sources, more consideration will be given ensure safe and easy access to the water points by women and girls, as they are in most cases the ones tasked with fetching water. Such considerations will include: distance to water points, time for water distribution, waiting time at water points, and safety and protection of users.
In Sanitation and Environmental Health: Latrines will be provided at household level with considerable community contribution in terms of labor for ensuring easy access, enhanced dignity and protection especially for women, girls, children and old-aged. Solid waste management and vector control activities planned to integrate with other sanitation services to cut short sanitation transmission chain and improve health status of refugees and host community, voluntary hygiene promotors and community women groups will be assigned to supervise these activities.
In regard to hygiene promotion: Community hygiene promotion volunteers and the Community Relief and Development Committees (CRDC)s will mobilize men and women from the community to participate in community level hygiene awareness events focused on cleanliness of water points, and water safety at household level through testing of the free residual chlorine in water at household water storage using user-friendly pool testers. 
Vulnerable individuals to receive the proposed hygiene kits will be identified through a community co-creative process, including HHs with disabled people, elderly and female- and child headed HHs. WASH NFI provision will be implemented with the objective of reducing incidence of water borne diseases through improved quality of collection and storage of drinking water; contributing to the psychosocial and physical wellbeing of women and girls, by including items such as intimate hygiene items and pads ensuring dignified living conditions of women and adolescent girls.

project_name: Food Security & Livelihoods Support for IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in East and South Darfur States
project_objective:
This ARC food security and livelihoods (FS&L) project aims to provide emergency FS&L services for IDPs, Returnees and host communities in East and South Darfur so as to improve their well-being and promote self-reliance. 15,000 people will be targeted by the project in East and South Darfur states. 
The project will be a 12 months’ intervention that will run from 1st April 2020 to 30th March 2021. ARC envisions the establishment of a long-term comprehensive livelihoods and economic recovery program to support Sudan’s transition to longer-term development through: a) reducing dependency on humanitarian relief support; b) increasing self-reliance and resilient economies; and c) promoting peace and cohesion between Refugees and Sudanese populations.  This intervention will target total  populations 558,137  in the locaties of  El Daein, Adilla , Alferdous  , Assaliya , Yassin , Shariya,Abukarinka  and Abu Jabra in East Darfur and Bielel , Gereida  ,Elsalam , Kalma camp , and Dimsu  localities  in South Darfur base on FSL ranking by Humanitarian need overview for 2019 .
In East Darfur ARC continuing providing food security and livelihoods services for refugees out of camp , returnees and host communities in Adilla , Elferdous , Assaliya and Abujabra localities for over 5000 people  .
The project interventions aim and focus on  : 
(i)	reduce acute food and livelihoods insecurity of newly displaced and affected by crises and natural disasters 
(ii)	restore and sustain the food security and livelihoods of vulnerable people in protracted displacement 
(iii)	build the resilience of the food and livelihood insecure by reducing vulnerabilities to conflict and disaster risks; and 
(iv)	 strengthen the capacity of national partners to address food and livelihoods insecurity and improve coordination in FSL core functions at national and state levels. 
The intervention will focus on mobilize communities (IDPs, returnees, host communities) to participate in programming interventions that address their needs and mainstreaming gender diversity of women (widows, orphans, divorce, female headed house hold and Survivor of SGBV), men, people with special needs and disables through setting appropriate activities that meet their needs and choices while the proposed activities will be market aware to promote longer-term self-sufficiency. The proposed intervention will contribute to key area of collective outcome for Sudan (Economic development and Sustainable Livelihoods) indicated that by 2022 communities and households benefit from increased production and productivity that lead to sustainable livelihoods, sustainable access to food systems and improved nutrition status with emphasis on the agriculture sector as a driver. ARC committee to coordinate with the humanitarian actors working at the field to avoid duplication of resources and efforts and maintain the core principles

project_name: Provision of integrated and comprehensive primary health care services to internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and host community affected by displacement and conflict in North & South Darfur States.
project_objective: Kuwaiti patients Helping Fund (KPHF) proposes to assist protracted displacement population, returnees, new arrival and host communities affected by displacement and conflict by supporting 22 PHC centers 3 in Draij  &  Otash IDPs, 3 in Dimsu and 3 in Gereida in South Darfur State and 2 in El Fasher rural, 4 in Twella ,4 in Daresallam and 3 in Sarfomera localities in North Darfur State. The Project will support provision of quality, high impact lifesaving primary health care Interventions to above targeted communities .The proposed programming will support 342,647 direct beneficiaries including men(60,200), women (220,500), boys(30,970) and girls(30,977 ) comprising of protracted IDPs, returnees , new arrival and host communities experiencing protracted crisis and low access of primary health care services. The project will intervention through provision of basic primary health care services under these activities which include outpatient consultations, essential medicine, basic laboratory investigation, referrals of severe cases to secondary care level, improve access to maternal and child health care services, provide EPI services and IMCI services. Also provide reproductive health services which include ANC & PNC services, safe and clean delivery, family planning and EmOC services. In addition to, KPHF will strengthen the capacity of project and SMoH staff through medley and intensive trainings and on-the-job trainings related to management and delivery of primary health care services, contribution in early detection, preparedness and response to emergencies and public health threats and make sure that surveillance system is in place and that epidemics are prevented, reported and controlled. In the same context, the above mentioned staff will be trained on disease surveillance, prevention and control. Accordingly, they will send weekly EWARS reports to the SMoH and WHO and report any outbreaks within 72 hours. KPHF along with SMoH will conduct community awareness campaigns in these targeted camps and surrounding areas on different topic such as AWD, STIs, RH and others to promote good health and hygiene practices and to reduce the risk of outbreaks of communicable diseases. KPHF has taken into account men, women, boy and girls in assessing the needs for and design of this project, and will continue to do so throughout its implementation. KPHF is very cognizant of the importance of gender equality and will provide equal access for men, women, boys and girls to health care services at the clinics and ensure that health education is provided to both genders. As women and children are considered the most vulnerable, KPHF will prioritize maternal and child health services KPHF strongly believes in shared responsibilities, strong linkage and communication among partners including SMOH, national and international NGOs and the community. To find common solutions to problems, and exchange ideas and experiences, KPHF will continue to participate in the weekly health coordination meeting chaired by WHO and SMoH at national and state levels.

project_name: Provision of basic livelihood needs to IDP & host communities in Zamzam, Tawila and Kutum, North Darfur, Sudan
project_objective:
Prolonged conflict and instability in Darfur and the surrounding regions has caused mass displacement and necessitated the establishment of Internally Displace People (IDP) camps. 
The proposed project aims to intervene in the sector of livelihood, supporting 73,612 families become self-sufficient through income generation activities, targeting vulnerable households both IDP and host communities. 
In Kutum Plan implementing peacebuilding and community stability project. This project is complementing mentioned peace project for optimal impact on affected people in the area.
Since the peace building working on community structuring and building relations between community groups, this project will use the same community structure for livelihood improvement which would push on enforcement of marginalized category for example empowerment of women will enable them participate actively in decision making and community dialogue and conversations the same will be for youth groups.

project_name: Delivery WASH basic needs to IDP, Returnees and host communities in Tawilla, Mellit and Dar Elsalam – North Darfur
project_objective: Prolonged conflict and instability in Darfur and the surrounding regions has caused mass displacement and necessitated the establishment of Internally Displace People (IDP) camps. Indicated inadequate access to safe water supply, shortfalls in Sphere standards in terms of gender-sensitive sanitation facilities with large number of old and non-functional latrine; poor hygiene practices such as open defecation is widely practiced particular among children, particularly IDP and vulnerable host communities are extremely exposed to vector and water-borne diseases. Plan International will implement activities to improve access to improved WASH services, including potable water, Sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion in targeted locations is thereby reduce associated prevalence of water related and vector-borne disease. Gender equity will be incorporated throughout detailed project design and implementation strategies, including emphasis placed on ensuring the participation of women and children and all other community groups are involved. In addition, women and girls will be engaged in leadership, PTAs, WASH committees, and mothers committee. Therefore, community awareness raising about gender roles and relationships will be conducted to promote (aspirations for) gender equality by providing opportunities for women and men in community committees to discuss gender relations and to set their own a agenda for change. Adding to that to the project will strengthen project team’s understanding of gender analysis to develop practical skills for gender monitoring and collect sex disaggregated information. During the project implementation Plan International will keep all the relevant WASH partners including NGOs, government, Humanitarian Aid Coordination (HAC), and UN agencies informed during the scheduled periodic coordination sector meetings taking place at community, state and federal level. This will ensure avoiding duplications of efforts, create better coordination, and learn from other organizations experiences, particularly in Cash Based Programming (CBP).

project_name: Strengthening child protection systems and services in Kutum, Malliet Tawilla and Darasalam localities of North Darfur
project_objective: Prolonged conflict and instability in Darfur and the surrounding regions has caused mass displacement and necessitated the establishment of Internally Displace People (IDP) camps. The proposed project aims to intervene in Child protection sector which will focus on improving existing child protection networks, respond to the immediate needs of vulnerable children and promoting provision of protective environment for IDPs, returnees and host communities’ children in the four targeted localities (Darasalam, Tawila, Mellit and Kutum), who are placed on continuous insecurity and vulnerability due to Darfur conflict and emergency situation. Through community awareness raising about gender roles and relationships will be conducted to promote (aspirations for) gender equality by providing opportunities for women and men in community committees to discuss gender relations and to set their own a agenda for change. Plan has been working in Darfur since 2005 and since March 2011 Plan has been responsible for Zamzam camp coordination and management. This role includes, coordination, and mobilization of the camp residents ensuring that common policy frameworks, and humanitarian standards are applied.

project_name: Provision of Integrated and comprehensive life-saving Nutrition services for IDPs ,returnees and host communities in North & South Darfur States.
project_objective: Kuwaiti patients Helping Fund (KPHF) proposes to assist vulnerable population affected by conflict, displaced and malnutrition by supporting 25 OTPs, 27 TSFPs and 4 SCs in El Fasher ,Tawella , Daresalam and Sarfomera in North and Dimsue , Greida , Nyala and Nyala North ,Tulus ,Kubum  in South Darfur States. The project proposed to support 176,165 beneficiaries including (8,224 boys & girls with SAM,1,252 boys & girls with SAM and medical complication, 22,540 boys & girls with MAM and 12,870 PLW with MAM) comprising of IDPs, returnees and host communities experiencing with displaced and malnutrition problem. Malnutrition remains a critical problem affecting the North and South Darfur States. KPHF will provide health services through SCs and nutrition services through OTPs and TSFPs. Nutrition services to cover SAM and MAM cases for U5 and PLW which include screening at admission, medical treatment of severely acutely malnourished (SAM) children with and without medical complication, dietary management and individual child follow up, among others. It will also cover the administrative (support) cost of case management of moderate acute malnourished (MAM) girls and boys of 6-59months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Furthermore, nutrition education and counseling will be provided for mothers/caregivers in Infant and Young Child feeding (IYCF) practices and hygiene promotion as well as MSGs will built to facilitate of nutrition education and contribution in MUAC screening activities. Selected trainings will be provided on SC case management, CMAM, NiE, identification of medical complications at OTPs and TSFPs level, community screening and follow up. In addition to, women club, women cornea and community awareness session campaigns will be conducted under nutrition program.

project_name: Nutritious Food Assistance and Recovery of Livelihoods for Those Affected by the Beirut Port Blast
project_objective:
The explosion that hit Beirut happened during very tough times that Lebanese are economically living. It left people homeless, internally displaced and there are also those who remained in their destroyed houses where electricity and water infrastructures were also ruined. In addition to the trauma that everyone has to deal with, costs of rehabilitation are huge and most probably not affordable by people living in somehow deprived neighborhoods. Knowing that the economic crisis led to inflated prices in the market, food items currently cost a fortune. In addition, cooking utensils, plates and cutlery are no longer available in most of these houses, whereas those who still have them, are in a bad shelter condition where cooking or setting up a fire is truly dangerous.
As such, and since IOCC was the first NGO to initiate the community kitchen model and the delivery of hot meals to vulnerable Syrian and Lebanese households since 2013, developed this modality when it co-chaired the FS sector since February 2016 until 2019 and has been part of drafting the hot meals modality with the Global Food Security Cluster; IOCC is proposing to activate a community kitchen in Beirut in order to be able to cater nutritious hot meals to the families. The modality will consist of joining forces with a local NGO in Beirut that has the premises of an equipped kitchen where women will be recruited by the local NGO for the cooking activity, enabling them to access income-generating activities. IOCC team would set a weekly diversified menu and deliver the meals to the identified families. The activity of locally purchasing the needed ingredients also contributed to an improved economic cycle within the community.
The distribution will happen on a door-to-door basis rather than having the beneficiaries queue in order to obtain the meals. This modality will ensure respect to the families’ privacy and will preserve their dignity.
Meals are to be placed in re-usable, heat resistant food containers that will be kept at the families’ premises and collected at the second distribution date in order to have it cleaned and washed again at the kitchen so that food safety is sustained and hazards are eliminated.
Every family meal also includes a bread parcel and is tailored for a family size of 4 people. However, meals can be adjusted when families are bigger or smaller, trying to include all those who need this assistance in the program.
The total target for the hot meals food assistance is equal to 2500 Households

Knowing that all food-service chains like restaurants, snacks and pubs were severely damaged due to the heavy explosion that hit Beirut, IOCC acknowledges that livelihoods within this specific sector were conjointly affected. The economic crisis is not making it any easier whether to employees or to business owners to cope with this sudden situation that has been worsening since a while. IOCC is suggesting to support the most affected through the reconstruction and the rehabilitation of the infrastructure as well as by providing and installing water filters systems within their kitchens for improved food safety. 
IOCC aims at helping 6 food businesses recovering their status pre-explosion.

project_name: Rehabilitation of Residential Apartments and Institutions in the Areas Affected by the Beirut Blast
project_objective:
Having witnessed the damages that the explosion caused in Beirut, and based on the rapid needs assessment that IOCC conducted, the organization is suggesting to provide full rehabilitation works to residential apartments as well as to primary health care centers and schools in the areas that were most affected by the explosion.
The aim of this intervention is the restore people's home, protection and dignity by rehabilitating their shelters. It will also reduce the percentage of internal displacement and minimize the costs of rehab on the affected families especially during the economic crisis that Lebanon is passing through.

On the other hand, facilities and institutions that were accessed by vulnerable population such as Primary Health Care Centers (PHCs) and Public Schools were also heavily damaged and currently put out of service. IOCC is proposing a full rehabilitation  for these institutions so that they can soon enough operate again and receive people who need support.

This intervention will target 150 residential apartment and 10 institutions

project_name: Improving access, quality and coverage of PHC for conflict-affected communities in 3 governorates of Syria.
project_objective:
Increasing equitable access to health care is imperative to prevent morbidity/mortality/disability and further deterioration of vulnerabilities after more than 8 years of protracted conflict and disruption of health system in Syria. INTERSOS proposes to ensure re-establishment of disrupted essential care services for women children and elderly. A comprehensive quality PHC package of interventions will be implemented by rehabilitation of 4 HFs in Dier-az-Zor; Dar’a (Izra, H’rak); Rural Damascus (Kisweh, Qatana, Said Zeinah), including repair of WASH facilities and electricity and supply of medical equipment; support to treatment of conditions with high impact on maternal, neonatal and child survival, and clinical and psychosocial services for victims of trauma, violence/abuse. The intervention package targets approximately 585,000 PIN (105,350 U5 children and 24,580 PLW) in IDPs, returnees and host communities. Although minimum level of services is being maintained, urgent renovations will offer safe and inclusive access to beneficiaries, including PwD/CwD. Capacity development of health staff on First Aid, RMNCH and MHPSS, NCD, support to mobile teams, awareness campaigns to increase community resilience for positive health outcomes from pregnancy to adolescence and adoption of safe family health behaviors at household level will be carried out.  INTERSOS will abide by Health Sector priorities and Guidance Notes committing to active inter-agency coordination, info-sharing, coordination of services and referrals, and feedback to affected populations.
Targeting approach and vulnerability criteria are described here below: The interventions will be rolled out in six sub-districts of three governorates (Rural Damascus, Dara and Dier-ez-Zor) categorized under health sector severity of 5, 4 and 3 and will support highly vulnerable returnees, IDPs and host populations with safe access to health services.  INTERSOS, together with its national partner, proposes to support minor rehabilitation of health facilities damaged by the war and contribute to restoring health services through 4 static units and provide outreach through 2 mobile teams in six sub-districts.  The project is designed to target 585,272 highly vulnerable individuals (men: 158,024; women: 175,582; Boys below 18: 134,613; girls below 18: 117,054) with a focus on families who have faced multiple displacement, women-headed households, children under-five, people with special needs/CwD/Pwd, PLW and the elderly taking into account age and gender. The protection concepts will be included as part of the overall initiative

project_name: Securing livelihood opportunities and promoting social cohesion through creation of job opportunities and vocational training for youth and women in the Governorates of Rural Damascus and Hama
project_objective:
This intervention contributes signiﬁcantly to the 2020 HRP sector objectives 1,2,3 and is in line with MoSAL and ER&L sector priorities, guidelines and minimum standards for proposed activities. INTERSOS will provide assistance based on need to approximatelly 13200 persons (IDPs, host communities and returnees) in sub – districts of Suran, Hamra, Karnaz, Oqeirbat, Muradah, As Saan, As – Sukalabaya (Hama Governorate) and Kafr Batna, Harasta, Arbin, Duma (Rural Damascus Governorate). The present intervention will focus on peri - urban or purely agricultural communities to reach the most in need population. Among the targeted subdistricts the 73% has a sector severity scale above 3, being 45% above severity scale 4. The project will promote an AGD approach to respond to the speciﬁc needs of the population, with a speciﬁc focus on youth, women and PwSn. The proposed activities are aimed to re-establish livelihood opportunities for the most affected population such as: youth who have interrupted educational process, women at risk of GBV or survivors and  PwSN who are prevented to access to income generating opportunities. The intervention is part of the INTERSOS Syria 2020 Country strategy whose pillars are protection and primary health - ER&L component is hence designed with a strong protection maintreaming with the aim at impacting on the most vulnerable group of population. 
Through the rehabilitation of schools, the intervention will enhance the access to basic social services and will provide temporary job opportunities through cash for work modalities. The creation of job opportunities in depressed areas, especially with agricultural traction, will help families and communities to reestablish their income and the creation of positive coping mechanisms and strategies. Skills and vocational trainings will be based on existing labor market opportunities, identifying local sectors of economic growth or gaps in available goods/ services. Those trainings will target youth and women and PwSn to support them in restoration of their livelihood and to support the opportunity of accessing to the job markets. Other vocational training for youth graduates or youth who are not receiving any type of education due to economic lack of opportunities, will be supported to seek employment locally or starting their own small - business activities. Community acceptance for targeted livelihoods activities will be ensured through participatory process in selection of community-based initiatives/community projects as well as in the deﬁnition of the criteria for beneﬁciary selection. INTERSOS will ensure full cooperation with relevant stakeholders, local authorities, SARC and sector members in order to avoid overlapping with other interventions and promoting the knowledge sharing of previous experience among partners.

project_name: Education in Emergencies for vulnerable children
project_objective:
With this project FCA proposes to contribute to the well-being of children in Syria by the provision of equitable education interventions, Most vulnerable children and underserved areas in Dara'a governorate will be reached through comprehensive approach project and based evidence-based needs identify the gaps.
Proposing 1) professional teacher development 2) Remedial classes for students at risk dropping out 3) Catch up classes for OOSC 4) stationary distribution to support the families in enrolling the children in schools 5) Schools Rehabilitation to improve the access along with education services there will be provision of protection components to protect the children in& outside the schools such as; Awareness sessions and PSS activities to create integrated communities as well as preventing the dropping out, early marriage, child labour and recruitment.

project_name: Protection Services and Interventions for Palestine Refugees in Syria
project_objective:
In 2020, UNRWA will continue to provide critical protection assistance to Palestine refugees, including to those who are displaced and those returning to their habitual residence in Syria. The Agency will seek to improve the protection of Palestine refugees in Syria through various interventions. Mainstreaming protection within UNRWA services will remain a priority. Corresponding to needs, protection training, including on disability inclusion, GBV, PSEA, addressing violence against children, will be delivered to a wide range of staff and volunteers. In addition, UNRWA will continue to build the capacity of programmes to strengthen case management and referral processes for high-risk protection cases, including unaccompanied/separated Palestine refugee children, cases of early marriage, persons with disabilities, older persons and those affected by violence (including women), GBV, abuse and neglect. Dedicated programmatic responses will be implemented through regular service-delivery and stand-alone initiatives to support the needs of vulnerable populations including those related to psychosocial distress. Areas most affected by conflict-related violence as well as displaced and returning populations will be prioritized. Legal support services will be offered while prioritising women and children experiencing GBV by assisting them in obtaining civil documentation and referrals to external partners. Mine risk awareness campaigns will continue throughout the country targeting students and other community members, with a specific focus on areas of spontaneous returns. 

Protection monitoring, reporting and advocacy will continue to be prioritised through the participation of UNRWA in global protection mechanisms and the international human rights system (IHRS). This will be done through the interaction with relevant stakeholders, including the protection sector of the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in Syria. In parallel, UNRWA will focus specifically on monitoring the return of Palestine refugees displaced within and outside Syria.

project_name: Assistance en abris et biens non-alimentaires pour les réfugiés nigérians à Maradi au Niger
project_objective:
Dans le cadre de ce projet, OIM en tant que co-lead du Groupe de Travail Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires va apporter une assistance humanitaire d’urgence aux populations le plus vulnérables des réfugiées ainsi qu’aux familles d’accueil les plus vulnérables des zones/villages d’accueil. Les ménages seront assistés en abris d’urgence démontables pour la population réfugiés, appuis-en-cash pour la population d’accueil et en kits de biens non-alimentaires pour les deux populations cibles. Les appuis-en-cash auront lieu avec des coupons et pourront être utilisés pour acheter des matériels de construction chez les vendeurs locaux. Dans l’optique de prévenir les potentiels conflits qui peuvent découler de ce projet, des consultations communautaires avec la population hôte et population réfugiés seront organisées avant les distributions afin d'informer la population de l'intervention et des modalités y afférentes. Le profilage des bénéficiaires est effectué selon les critères de vulnérabilité prédéfinis par le groupe de travail. 
Les bénéficiaires, par l’intermédiaire des groupes de discussion, seront consultés et impliqués tout au long de la mise en œuvre du projet. En outre, le niveau de satisfaction des bénéficiaires à l'égard de la réponse, sera une préoccupation de l’OIM tout le long du projet. 
Afin d’apporter une réponse adéquate aux besoins de ces populations vulnérables, l'OIM achètera et distribuera 1 000 abris d’urgence démontables dans les villages affectés, au profit d'environ 7 000 les plus vulnérables personnes réfugiées. L’IOM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre utiliseront pour cette réponse l’approche du transfert monétaire à travers des coupons. 
L’OIM anticipe l’appui à 400 plus vulnérable ménages hôtes d’environ 2 800 personnes.  Cette stratégie permettra aussi de renforcer l’économie locale à travers l’injection de cash dans la zone. Ce renforcement de capacité sera mis en œuvre à travers l’achats des matériels avec les vouchers pour la reconstruction des abris pour les ménages hôtes les plus vulnérables, pour une valeur de 150 $ USD par ménage (140 $ USD voucher et 10 $ USD frais administratifs pour la mise en œuvre de système de voucher).
En plus, l’OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre achèteront et distribueront 1 400 kits BNA au profit de 1 400 ménages de 9 800 personnes environ avec soit 7 000 étant réfugiés et 2 800 personnes dans les familles d’accueil. 
Enfin, la mise en œuvre du présent projet fera l’objet d’un suivi régulier de la qualité des interventions réalisées mais aussi de l’implication des bénéficiaires. Pour cela, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers les évaluations post distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparés par genre et âge. project_name: Brazil - Associazione Volontari per il Servizio Internazionale
Colombia - Adventist Development and Relief Agency
Colombia - Americares
Local Water Supply for Frontier Communities (LWSFC)
project_objective:
The severity of humanitarian needs within the Syrian crisis has been well documented with an unprecedented level of declining access to essential service such as water and sanitation. Access and usage of water for hygiene, sanitation and drinking will remain a pivotal issue for 6.2 million people within Syria (UNOCHA, HNO, 2019) limiting the extent to which quality of life and the economy can be improved in the country. Regular access to water challenges persist, particularly, in rural areas where people are relying on unsafe water sources to meet their requirements. Thus, medium-term options to improve the drinking and sanitation water situation are urgently needed within rural areas.

The project aims to enhance access to sustainable, clean and equitable water supply for 14,844 male and female individuals (3,110 IDPs and 510 returnees) within the eastern countryside of Hama province in central Syria. The water strategy under this project will implement a localized system which takes into account prevailing supply infrastructure and growing local demand. By sourcing, treating, storing, and distributing water locally, the water supply system will be able to adapt to sudden shortages or outages of the target areas, thereby ensuring quality, equitable access to water and reducing the need to externally source water which is of questionable quality and often not accessible during periods of water shortage.  The increase in water reserve capacity will be able to reach an appropriate total catchment of 14,844 individuals within Barri al Sharqi Sub-District. 
In order to facilitate community access to equitable and improved usage of water services for communities in the target villages, the proposed action proposes maintaining active community engagement within project design and implementation through the creation of a community water management committee. This is important to promote long-term sustainable water services of rural households. Furthermore, to address the limited access to sustainable water service provided by local authorities, water service systems will be strengthened to improve the quality and usage of these services. For this purpose, the project will focus on improving the technical and managerial capacities of male and female water technicians who are mainly from the local authorities in the target Sub-District.

The main project activities include; (1) drill 1 deep groundwater borehole in Barri al Sharqi village and provide equipment necessary for the operation of this deep water well, (2) install primary water treatment and Reverse Osmosis (RO) units, (3) established  a voluntary community water management committee representing the communities within the target villages and (4) Hand over the water treatment facilities and equipment to the Water Local Authority in Barri al Sharqi Sub-District.

project_name: Escaping poverty through increasing self-resilience in access to food for the most vulnerable households in Dara’, Hama and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to support self-resilience of HHs in Rural Damascus, Hama and Dar'a through distribution of agro-kits and poultry kits. The Action will strengthen resilience of the affected HHs and reduce the dependency on aid of the most vulnerable Syrian population living in these areas. The Project will contribute to the Sector Objective 2 “Support self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives” in order to reach 1.2 million people in 2020. 
To decrease the dependency on food assistance and to promote the self-resilience and consequently the dignity of beneficiaries, the Project will provide agro inputs (seeds) and poultry for family consumption to a total of 10,000 HHs. Agro-inputs will be delivered to those families who have an access to their land, ensuring that lands are free of UXOs, while in the areas still UXOs affected or for the families who do not possess land, poultry kits will be delivered. 
In the process of beneficiary’s selection specific focus will be on returnees and local population (host communities). Special attention will be given to female headed HHs, elderly, HHs with People with Disabilities, unaccompanied children and to those groups who have only limited access to income to cover the family food needs and are forced to adopt negative copying mechanisms, unskilled or seasonal workers for instance. 
The most common negative coping mechanism detected by COOPI during the implementation of the current projects and through last post harvesting assessment (September 2019) are: not buying clothes, not buying uniforms for children attending school, taking loans, requested support from relatives, waiting for aid coming from INGOs and SARC, families sent their children to work.
 During the preparation and implementation of the activities, COOPI will ensure the coordination with local authorities and robust participation of the communities giving them a voice to express desired modalities of implementation (the design of similar projects have been already successfully tested by COOPI in Dar’a and Nashabiyeh). Coordination will be ensured with the FSA Sector and its members but also with international and national actors active in the same villages in order to harmonized the response, avoid overlapping and to promote synergies. Synergies will also be promoted by COOPI through other projects submitted to HRP 2020 taking place in the governorates of this Action. 
Additionally, the same approach will be implemented in NES and NW if access is granted to INGOs.

project_name: PROJECT WITHDRAWN- Improving Education of Somali girls and boys affected by crisis in South West State of Somalia.
project_objective:
READO proposition aims to ensuring that 2915 girls and boys (1465 boys, 1450 girls) affected by the crisis have uninterrupted access to education in 7 identified schools in 2 Districts of South West State, particularly in 5 schools  in Baidoa (Barwaaqo Primary School, Yaiyow Kooyow IDP School, Jaraale Primary School, Barare IDP School and Awdinle Primary School) and 2 schools in Dinsoor (Holwadaq Primary School and Waaberi Primary School). 
The project envisages 2 Outcomes and intends to improve the educational attainment, safety of Somali girls and boys affected by crisis, contributing to resilience building within increasingly peaceful, secure & democratic environment. 
Outcome 1: Equitable access to education for emergency-affected children and youth is increased 
Community Outreach Initiatives (COI), distribution of supplementary food, construction/rehabilitation of 7 learning spaces, distribution of teaching and learning material, learners’ kits, safe transport for children will be implemented. Moreover, READO will provide the schools with tanks to store water in order to promote sustained access to water while constructing latrines and hand washing facilities in the target schools.

Outcome 2: Learning outcomes are improved for emergency-affected children and teachers should be in the position to act as role models for the children, to give them the strength to imagine for themselves a better future and to thrive for it. 
In Somalia, teachers are often working on volunteer basis or underpaid, therefore READO will provide capacity building for 85 school personnel [52 teachers (21 female) and 33 CECs (16 female) and teachers’ incentives over a period of 12 months.
Protective learning environments are established and strengthened for emergency-affected children at school level: READO will conduct trainings on psycho-social care of the children and child protection for schools’ personnel, promoting awareness and coordination on child protection.
Communities are more resilient to shocks and prioritize education for children
Communities will enhance their capacities to cope with shocks, particularly drought and conflict. Emergency preparedness committees will be formed in each partner schools and tasked to monitor, evaluate and report to inform appropriate action for both prevention and response on child protection issues as a child safe-guarding mechanism.

project_name: #LOVEBEIRUT_ Restoring Access to Education
project_objective:
Following the request from local authorities, the Head of municipalities and Moukhtar and Religious leaders, in coordination with the Inter-Agency, since 5 August, AVSI has been assessing: Achrafieh (Geitawi and Rmeil); Mar Mikhael; Gemmayze; Furn Chebbak; Burj Hammoud; Medawar. AVSI deployed a team composed of technical and logistic staff, social workers, education, protection, MHPPS staff; supported by a team tasked with management, coordination, monitoring.
The Rapid assessment of the structural and physical damages, of the MHPSS and vulnerability level of the population aimed at providing immediate relief, basic assistance, support/referral, and shelter. AVSI reached 94 households (209 members); 95% Lebanese, 5% Syrian, PRL. 78% of them did not receive assistance: of those who did: 81% got food, 12% health; 6% financial assistance.
Out of the HHs (70%F, 19% <14yo, 9%>14<18 yo, 28 % < 18yo; the majority aged >40): 7% PwDs (20% physical, 20% hearing, 60% intellectual impairments); 24% with chronic illness; 6% with life-threatening conditions. 
20% of the HHs were injured by the explosion: 79% mild, 21% moderate/severe injuries. 53% of the HHs are unemployed; 27% are studying. 8% have a university degree, 48% only completed the primary education; 7 HHHs lost their shops and the income. 
Thanks to its Lebanon Emergency #LOVEBEIRUT, campaign, AVSI has been providing emergency shelter and livelihood and MHPSS to these families already.
Although not part of the immediate response, AVSI assessed the education in the area: evidence shows it has been affected severely. There are 410 schools in the area (CERD), including public, semi-private and private; the number of Non-Formal Education Centers is unknown. The IA assessment identified 20 public TVET centers damaged, attended by. 8000 youths. 120 public and 67 private (12 with heavy damages) schools reported damages, including buses, school equipment and material. This affects 55,000 children. Loss of education can lead to permanent drop-out, increase of child labor and long-term decrease of income earning opportunities.
Many families and schools have lost also IT assets that would allow implementing remote/blended education, likely to happen from September onwards due to the high level COVID infection (Lebanon recorded the highest rates in August).
NFE centers and private schools, that often provide free education to the most vulnerable children are on their own at the moment. While supporting the Sector with its technical capacity (100+ schools rehabilitated, equipped, 100,000+ children supported with FE, NFE and CP/PSS), AVSI propose:
•	To assess to private and semi-private schools, and NFE offering free/affordable education to vulnerable OOSC and school children
•	Rehabilitation 10 schools, and 3 NFE centers including equipment, WASH and COVID infection prevention measures, 
•	provision IT equipment, including data bundle to schools/centers/families to undertake the blended/ distant education until education premises are available. AVSI will use I Learn From Home and Can’t Wait to learn for NFE ECE, BLN, Retention. The systems are already in place and tested during the COVID response.
Interventions will be in line with the ESP (Effective School Profiles), GOL, MEHE, PMU, Sector standards. 
The Project will support approx. 5,000 students and 900 OOSC attending NFE, 1180 families, 250 schools/learning centers staffs. Direct beneficiaries 7330 (80% children, 79% Leb, 21% non-Leb, 51% Females, 4% PWD). Activities mainstream Protection and CP, gender and environment. AVSI adopt a Child-centered and Participatory Approach. Schools/Learning centers will meet safety and safeguarding standards, be child friendly and inclusive. 
Staff will increase knowledge and skills on CP, enabled to safely identify and refer children at risk of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation. Caregivers and community will be engaged in preventing/addressing CP concerns improving the child wellbeing

project_name: Shelter assistance and protection mainstreaming response for vulnerable Lebanese and non-Lebanese individuals affected by Beirut Port Blast
project_objective:
On August 4th 2020, a warehouse in the Port of Beirut, reportedly containing 2,750 tons of ammonium nitrate, exploded causing devastation and grave damages across the city. As per MoPH  records, at least 190 people were killed, over 6,000 wounded, and over 300,00 people left homeless.
From August 5th 2020, AVSI has: 
•	Immediately responded with emergency shelter activities; 
•	Conducted a need assessment for 130 vulnerable households in the areas affected by the blast, considering the structural, physical damages and the socio-economic vulnerability. 
•	AVSI pre-identified households in need of immediate support. 
•	AVSI mobilized its private funds and the technical teams begun working immediately on repairs; in one week from 9 to 15 August, AVSI completed repair for 10 residential units. As a result, 30 people were already able to return home. Thanks to its fundraising campaign and granted fund from UNDP, AVSI IS CURRENTLY CONDUCTING minor repair for 115 residential units for a total of 375 individual supported.1 The total secured fund is 417,700$. MOREOVER, AVSI IS EXPECTING A FUND FROM ITALIAN DONORS EQUAL TO 110 000$ TO CONDUCT MINOR REPAIR FOR ADDITIONAL 50 RESIDENTIAL UNITS.
WITH MORE FUNDING, AVSI can still help more families to mitigate suffering through an integrated quick response in two priority areas: shelter, and restoration of essential needs.
WITH THIS FLASH APPEAL FOR A TOTAL OF 527,700$, AVSI FORESEE TO PROVIDE:
•	MINOR REPAIR FOR 165 RESIDENTIAL UNITS includes fixing nonstructural damages, defined as first and second level damage according to the IA Shelter Strategy. THAT CAN BE AND NOT LIMITED TO: INSTALLATION OF GLASS, WINDOWS, DOORS, REESTABLISHMENT OF WINDOWS FRAMES, FIXING OF FALSE CEILING, ESSENTIAL PLUMBING AND ELECTRICAL WORK…. CONSIDERING THAT SHELTER SUPPORT WILL BE CUSTOMIZED AS PER THE NEEDS AND PRIORITIES OF EACH RESIDENTIAL UNIT.  THE PROJECT MIGHT ALSO FORESEES THE PROVISION OF DOMESTIC EQUIPMENT DESTROYED BY THE BLAST. The aim is to secure houses and to make them habitable, and to ensure decent dwelling for vulnerable families;
•	Protection mainstreaming in the assessments and response to promote holistic approach. The assessment and rehabilitation support provided to the affected beneficiaries will be used as an entry point for the identification of specific cases in order to ensure needed pathways for people needing case management and specialized services (psychological, medical, legal etc.): the aim is to mitigate the psychosocial distress that families are living after the chock, to promote fast recovery, and to foster the community and individual resilience.

AVSI is coordinating with Beirut Forward Emergency Room, with the Shelter, livelihood, protection and CP WGs to ensure synergies and avoid duplications. AVSI will particularly coordinate with the shelter WGs for the geo-split of response within the radius of the 138 Zones identified by the LRC. The priority will be given to zones at 1 to 3 Km from the blast and most vulnerable zones as per UN Habitat  vulnerability map. The selection of beneficiaries will be based on: Sphere Protection Principles and Core Humanitarian Standards, the socio-economic vulnerability criteria coupled with the technical criteria in line with the interagency definitions of the emergency shelter. 
AVSI will reach the beneficiaries through the daily presence of AVSI social and technical team on field and the established connection with community stakeholders (such as Municipality members, religious leaders, Moukhtar). Target group will be composed from: Lebanese and non-Lebanese, 60% female and 40% male, while 7% of the target group will be Person with Disabilities.
Direct beneficiaries are as follow:
•	From minor repair: 165 residential units, with an average of 3 individuals per households, for a total of 495 males and females.
•	Among these households’ members, those who are in need will be benefiting from protection services.

project_name: Enhancing accountability to affected populations by strengthening communication and community engagement mechanisms
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen the coordination of community engagement across all agencies by focusing on mainstreaming and harmonizing existing tools and linking community input to decision making. The Communication and Community Engagement (CCE) Working Group will be the forum where these activities will take place. ACTED, as a co-chair of the CCE Working Group, in coordination with the other two co-leads, Internews and IOM, will link the Working Group to the humanitarian coordination architecture by strengthening the links between the group and the different clusters. `
To enhance program quality at every stage of the humanitarian programme cycle and contribute to strengthening accountability to affected population, the project will ensure that affected communities are adequately engaged and provided with timely and accurate information about how and why humanitarian aid is available to them, know and demand their rights from the humanitarian responders. The CCE activities also ensure the inclusion of the different vulnerable groups, such as women, elders, persons with disabilities and children, by making sure they are informed about their rights; they are aware of the available complaints and feedback mechanisms; by facilitating awareness raising campaigns, including the strengthening of prevention of SEA. 
The role of the CCE Working Group remains essential in this process since despite the existence of some mechanisms at an agency level, coordinated messaging, complaints and feedback systems, enhancing two-way communication systems through the promotion of a standardized platform where partners can obtain meaningful analysis on complaint and feedback systems across the humanitarian response remains essential and yet under-performed.
Under this project, ACTED will lead the capacity building component of the suggested activities always in coordination with Internews and IOM.

project_name: Rehabilitation of Al-Birr Hospital
project_objective:
Al-Birr Hospital was built, operated and owned by Al-Birr Association since 1994 in order to provide all health services (primary and secondary) to all citizens, especially the poor patients and the patients from northern rural Homs, with high quality and in a manner, that preserves their dignity without any discrimination. 
The hospital has 150 beds. It is the largest private and charitable hospital in Syria.
Before the crisis in Al-Waer, Al-Birr hospital was visited by a patients from all of Homs city (60% of them from rural Homs) since it's equipped with modern equipment, and has the best staff of doctors and nurses; especially after the damage of most public health centers and public hospitals. Al-Birr hospital was providing all kind of health care including primary, secondary and even tertiary health care services. It was providing all kinds of surgeries and medical care including open cardiac surgery, cardiac catheterization, and specific operations such as neurosurgery.

During the crisis period, the hospital was severely affected because of its location in Al-Waer area, which forced the association to stop working in some departments and limit the services to some services such as dialysis, especially in the last five years.
After the agreement of Al-Waer neighborhood, A lot of people returned to their homes in Al-Waer, so Al-Birr has started rehabilitating this hospital after years of operating another hospitals in Homs city (Farkouh, Mahattah, Al-Kindi and Al-Shawi).
Till now, there is no enough public care centers in Homs city, where most of public hospitals there is just providing some primary services such as outpatient clinics and laboratory, while urgent secondary care services are not provided so patients have to transfer to other private hospitals out of Homs to get services.
Anyway, the kind of services will be provided in Homs city  and will help people not just in Homs governorate but also in other governorates since Homs is in the middle of Syria and people do not have to travel to Damascus for obtaining necessary and urgent health services such as catheterization, neurosurgery, lithotripsy and other services.
Because of the great damage in the hospital, the difficulty of full rehabilitation of its building, and the desire to provide health services to the increasing number of returnees Al-Birr has rehabilitated a dialysis department, emergency department which includes an operation room and ICU, out-patient clinics, radiology and laboratory departments. Al-Birr plans to rehabilitate other departments in the hospital (ICU, NICU, surgical department, cardiosurgery and catheterization, surgical ICU, hospitalization rooms, gynecology, pediatrics departments.

project_name: Shelter and infrastructure assistance for IDPs, returnees and affected population in Syria
project_objective:
As shelter lead agency, UNHCR is coordinating the emergency shelter responses and implementing the 2020 shelter programme from inside Syria, as well as from Gaziantep (Turkey).  Through this project UNHCR will support the communities of returnees in specific targeted areas ( some 1,357,000 persons) through emergency response and long-term shelter solutions, from inside Syria as well as from Gaziantep (Turkey). 

Project indicator targets represent a sum of Syria and Gaziantep hub targets, outlined below:
The shelter Programme aims to improve housing and related community/public infrastructure addressing shelter needs of 15,000 vulnerable households/75,000 individuals through basic house repairs. Returnee communities will be supported with debris removal and installation of solar street lights in 67 neighborhoods to support 837,500 individuals/167,500 returnee families and host community. 

Through emergency response shelter conditions will be improved for 67,500 individuals/13,500 households with 13,500 emergency shelters kits, as well as through provision of emergency shelter to 150,000 individuals/30,000 households ( tents distribution, camp construction and collective shelter rehabilitation). 

UNHCR’s cross-border shelter programme aims to provide emergency shelter (tents) to 43,000 households/215,000 individuals and address shelter needs of 2,000 vulnerable households/10,000 individuals through basic house repairs through shelter material/kits. The component of Gaziantep hub constitutes 23% of the project.

The role and responsibility of the local and national authorities will continue in close partnership with MoLAE and partners (NGOs/INGOs) in the implementation of shelter and infrastructure works. Project management capacity and technical skills of 2,000 engineers from local government will be enhanced through a training. 

UNHCR area-based approach, is well adapted to the immediate needs of communities, consolidating protection, shelter, access to basic infrastructure and basic services to ensure maximum impact through integrated integrated interventions in targeted communities.  Affected population will be empowered and capacitated at all stages to participate in programme planning, needs assessment, implementation, monitoring and evaluation in order to design acceptable, appropriate, sustainable and culturally-sensitive shelter programmes.

project_name: Provision of CMAM and IYCF services for vulnerable populations in Southern area and Northern area of Syria.
project_objective:
Terre des Hommes ( TDH Italy ) proposed nutrition project seeks to address not only the inadequate coverage and quality of life-saving services for the treatment of acute malnutrition in children under five and vulnerable pregnant or lactating women (PLWs) , but also some of the key determinants of malnutrition through promotion of improve infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices and healthy behaviors linked to unnecessary deaths amongst vulnerable populations in (Izra, Al Tal, Al Hasakeh city, Qahtaniyyeh, Tal Tamer, Shadadah). By integrating CMAM program into the already established PHC clinics of the implementing partner in or establishing new CMAM centers supported by outreach team to screen and identify cases of malnutrition among boys, girls and women amongst IDPs and host community, so unmet needs of the acutely malnourished boys, girls and women amongst the vulnerable returnees, refugees and IDPs in can be served.
SAM classification and treatment will also be supported and strengthened in referral clinic through training and supervision as needed. Critical IYCF practices as well as promotion of appropriate health seeking and preventive behaviors for the main diseases will be targeted through the establishment of a mothers’ group network.
The project plans to conduct focused trainings for SARC volunteers to build their capacity, to provide structured CMAM and IYCF services and activities to those in need, case management and referral, capacity building activities to local partner SARC through the training of the volunteers and community members, and support facility and community based 1-1 counselling on WHO recommended Infant and Young Child Feeding practices.
The intervention is interested in the framework of the strategic objective 1,2 and 3 of the HRP 2020.
Total beneficiaries include the following:
Children under 5, Pregnant and Lactating Women, Refugee Returnees, Trainers, Promoters, Caretakers, committee members, etc.
Indirect Beneficiaries: Family members of mother group participants who are anticipated to benefit from the healthier practices of the mothers group participants.
Project Beneficiaries: 
PLWs: 20,220 pregnant or lactating women who will be screening for malnutrition using MUAC (Middle upper arm circumference) and will receive awareness raising sessions, peer to peer sessions and care group module.
PLWs MAM: 1,415 pregnant or lactating women identified with moderate acute malnutrition who will receive treatment and follow up.
Children under five years: 45,597 who will be screened for malnutrition using MUAC (Middle upper arm circumference).
Children under five years MAM: 1,012 children identified with moderate acute malnutrition who will receive treatment and follow up.
Children under five years SAM: 434 children identified with sever acute malnutrition (both with and without medical complications) who will receive treatment and follow up.
The nutrition sector in the 2020 HRP and other documents has prioritized the treatment of acute malnutrition in the most under-served, conflict affected areas for scale-up of coverage and effectiveness in those provinces with the highest burden and worst access. The targeted beneficiaries will be the IDPs, returnees, refugees and vulnerable host boys and girls under 5 and pregnant and lactating women. The beneficiaries of CMAM services will be identified by their anthropometric classification (MUAC, Weight for height and edema check) of severe and moderate acute malnutrition as per national guidelines. The selection of the intervention areas and the targeting of beneficiaries in informal settlements and other vulnerable areas will be based on a gap analysis from a secondary data review and a screening exploratory phase which to be conducted by the implementation partner.

project_name: Provide Food Support and increase resiliency of vulnerable communities and Households including PWDs in Aleppo, Dara'a and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
The Project aims to improve the food security and livelihood status of most vulnerable people through life-sustaining food assistance and income-generating opportunities ( linked to 1st and 2nd HRP 2020 targets) with special focus on female-headed households, and people with disabilities through distribution of Food vouchers targeted 2,050 Household in 3 high severity scales locations in Aleppo, Rural Damascus and Daraa, the amount of each voucher will be 45,000 SYP according to WFP Minimum Expenditure Basket for 8 Cycles according to Food Security Sector minimum standard,
In the purpose of providing income-generating opportunities, 30% out of the targeted beneficiaries will participate in specialized vocational training mainly of them PwDs and Female-Headed households for three months in the training centre in the same locations,hence100 beneficiaries out of the total beneficiaries who are targeted in the vocational training will participate in Cash for Work project which aims to provide temporary jobs in the targeted locations in close coordination with community committees in each location and provide 5 cycles of payments for each beneficiary, the amount of each payment will be 80,000 SYP, in order to support the well-being of the families, as well as providing income-generating for the most vulnerable people in the targeted communities.

project_name: Life-saving integrated food security and livelihoods support for Somaliland and Puntland communities
project_objective:
The project is responding to humanitarian needs of drought affected community in target locations of Puntland and Somaliland through cash injection to address the immediate food needs of the people. Cash transfer programming will be used to reach households that are in IPC 3 and above. While focusing on life-saving interventions, the project will also support recovery and resilience building of the people where possible. 

Improving food availability through support to agricultural production in Awdal and strengthening existing resilience work under SomRep in Sool and Sanaag regions of Somalia is seen as an entry point to diversify pastoral livelihoods of those two regions. This plan involves also supporting communities’ recovery and livelihoods diversification interventions through creation of VSLA, livestock support with vaccination and treatment and Improving Agricultural Production/Food Security. 

Livestock production was severely affected by the drought leading to substantially reduced herds; which is the country’s prime investment especially in rural communities. The mains reasons leading to the death of livestock were water shortages and lack of pasture.  In view of this situation the project will explore fodder production techniques trained to women groups to ensure fodder is produced in those location but also conservation and preservation of fodder. Oxfam will prioritize livestock vaccination and treatment which will be closely coordinated with ministry of livestock and FAO. These include promotion of carrying capacity for sustained production. These actions will be coupled with Cash for Work activities which will be used for communal asset development linked to natural resource base rehabilitation aimed to reduce effect of climate change on NRM and promotion of land productivity. 

In improving livelihoods/ food security, the project will use conservational agriculture model as a climate smart agriculture technology to facilitate regeneration of agricultural production among agro-pastoral households. The beneficiaries will be given seed to improve seed security for the coming farming season. Farmers will be trained in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture on agricultural techniques to obtain optimal yields from their fields. Upon harvesting farmers will be able to reserve part of the harvest as seed for next season. 

In times of shock and more critical food insecurity, Oxfam will utilize multi-purpose cash transfers to meet the immediate emergency needs of at-risk communities. Oxfam will strengthen government capacity to anticipate and respond to slow onset crises through supporting mobile early warning data collection, dissemination back to community to enhance preparedness measures.

project_name: Protection assistance for vulnerable children and communities in WoS in 2020

Under this action, War Child would respond to urgent Child Protection needs in Idleb and Aleppo, and expand the service provision for highly vulnerable children in Raqqa and Deir Ez Zor through CFS, structured PSS, awareness raising, and developing specialized service capacity within local partner organisations, so that they can deliver a quality case management service. 

This prevention and response approach will address immediate and urgent identiﬁed child protection risks while contributing to long-term change. project_name: Improve Access to Housing, Basic Infrastructure and Cadastral Services for Displaced, Hosts and Returnees through an Urban Area-Based Approach in Rural Damascus, Daraa, Deir-Ezzor, Hama, and Aleppo
project_objective:
The rationale of this area-based housing project is derived from experience gained from previous pilots and shelter projects, and in light of Shelter Sector’s evaluation and interventions, as well as challenges emerged during the last years, concluding that
•	Targeting individual housing units scattered across cities, reduces the desired impact of emergency response to enhance stability and social cohesion in areas,
•	Restoration of services and infrastructure, simultaneous to rehabilitation of living space, is a key factor in reviving the affected neighborhoods and improving stability,
•	Community (and municipality) involvement in project identification and planning processes is a prominent element in emergency assistance, as it serves to mitigate possible tensions arising from perceived or real discrimination in selection processes. It is however essential to manage expectations of beneficiary populations, thus to boost positive impact of outcomes of delivered assistance,

Objectives:
Through the area-based housing approach, UN-Habitat aims to boost sustainable access to housing, restoration of essential infrastructure and access to cadastral services to displaced-, host- and returnee- populations in selected neighborhoods in Rural Damascus, Daraa, Deir-Ezzor, Hama and Aleppo. In practice, the approach consists in rehabilitation of roads, sidewalks, and debris removal in damage-affected neighborhoods, which are prioritized through ‘Neighbourhood Action Plans”, developed through the municipality-led MTOS (Municipal Technical Office Support) program. The holistic notion to serve entire conflict-affected, vulnerable communities through improvement of essential infrastructure and related services, under the objective to revive neighborhoods, is at the core of this project

Project Components:
Based on the municipalities’ neighborhood action plans, the project targets to:
•	Light repair and maintenance of roads (mainly the Asphalt layer) in residential areas
•	Rehabilitation of sidewalks (including tiling, and replacement of damaged curbstones)
•	Debris removal
•	Provision and installation of solar street lighting
•	House connection activities including connecting buildings with public networks of sewage and drinking water
•	Support to local cadastral departments to restore its functions and to provide services in regards of ownership and tenure documentation to all citizens.
