project_name: Provision of tailored are-based shelter assistance to the vulnerable individuals most heavily impacted by the Beirut Port Explosions
project_objective:
The proposed response aims to tackle the immediate shelter needs emerged as a result of the explosion, providing access to safe and liveable residential units to the affected communities of the Beirut Lebanese, migrant and refugee population, while also contributing to the multi-sectoral longer term rehabilitation of areas affected, in close coordination with national and local actors. 
Tapping into the overall coordination mechanisms of the shelter sector and Lebanese institutions, as well as initiatives on the ground, this programme proposes area-based and punctual assistance to estimated 21,190 individuals (10,172 men and 11,018 women; of which 5,297 are elderly; 10,595 between 18-65; and 5,298 under 18) need via:
a)	Emergency weatherproofing assistance to an estimated 300 target HH beneficiaries 
b)	Provision of conditional cash for rent to 1000 individuals 
c)	Minor repair of 1200 residential / non-residential units 
d)	Rehabilitation of 500 residential shelters. 
e)	Rehabilitation of 100 common areas within residential units
f)	Rehabilitation of structural damages within 20 residential buildings
g)	Implementation of 5 community support projects in affected areas
h)	Capacity building of 30 national institutions and organizations on shelter response
i)	Production of 10 assessment studies that are made accessible and widely disseminated
This program aims to complement other ACTED implemented/planned intervention across other sectors (such as Food Security, WASH, Protection and Health) and will target zones 71-74 and 104-110 in Bourj Hammoud, zones 66-69 in Basta el-Tahta and zones 6-8 and 10-12 in Karantina where ACTED’s historical presence and long term programming in the target areas (since 2013) made it one of the first and key responders to provide immediate relief to the Beirut Port Explosion. Within the first days of the response and in coordination with the Shelter sector, ACTED supported the implementation of the LRC MSNA assessment, jointly with the distribution of emergency weatherproofing kits. To date, ACTED has distributed 1064 core relief items (including 217 sealing off kits, dignity and baby kits) and removing over 1232 tons of debris from the streets and HHs of Beirut. 
Through its shelter programs ACTED will enhance its ongoing coordination with Lebanese institutions and initiatives who have played an integral role in the immediate shelter response. In the aftermath of the disaster, ACTED provided GIS support to the Beirut Municipality through the provision of an expert to improve their efficiency of building safety checks; and a solid waste management expert was deployed to support the Beirut Municipality and their contractor to improve management of the waste dumps. Moreover, ACTED has engaged with Beirut Urban Labs, the Order of Engineers and other prominent urban planners and initiatives in Lebanon to ensure the response is people centred. ACTED has supported many local initiatives in the response (such as Arcenciel, Bassma, Migrant Community Center), through provision of resources to expand the shelter response and/or recycling efforts. 
As a shelter sector actor part of the immediate response, and member of the Cash for Rent and Rehabilitation Task Forces, ACTED will ensure each form of shelter programming will align with sector harmonized packages and adhere to sector guidance to prevent generating conflict due to lack of harmonization of assistance. ACTED will continue to coordinate closely with the shelter sector to implement programs at a zone level and coordinate with all actors within the same zone. As co-lead of the Urban WASH Working Group, ACTED will continue to coordination to ensure a harmonised WASH and shelter response at HH level.  Additionally, ACTED will continue to support local institutions and initiatives to contribute towards discussions within the sector to ensure harmonisation of the response beyond the sector actors.

project_name: Supporting the Lebanese health system recuperate post-blast and enhancing its preparedness against COVID
project_objective:
This project aims to support the physical rehabilitation of the severely damaged hospitals, to provide them with HR support, and to procure needed equipment for hospitals in order to enable them to restart service provision. The project also entails the establishment of proper medical waste management at affected health facilities. Support to the reconstruction of the central drug warehouse will be included in the project in order to ensure the warehouse’s urgent functionality. 
The Beirut explosion caused further depletion medical supplies and PPEs as facilities were overwhelmed with casualties of the blast and utilized supplies while caring for injured individuals. Through this project, WHO will procure  trauma kits and  surgical kits to replace the depleted stocks in the hospitals that received trauma cases, and to ensure their preparedness to receive casualties resulting from the clashes happening in riots and protests. In addition, the country is currently is in the community transmission phased of the COVID outbreak and the number of cases in increasing; a cumulative number of 10 952 positive cases was reported on 20 August. Thus, it is of utmost urgency to replenish the stocks of PPEs for 20 hospitals receiving COVID-19 cases in and outside Beirut. 
WHO will also contribute through this project to the strengthening of primary health care services with a focus on ensuring establishment of community mental health centers to respond to the emerging and rising needs in mental health. Furthermore, WHO will support the integration of mental health into the primary health care package. This is in line with the National MHPSS action plan and will be implemented in close coordination with the National Mental Health Program at the MOPH. After the blast, the need for essential medications (acute, chronic, and mental health medications) increased by at least 25% based on initial rapid assessment. Therefore, WHO will procure 3 months’ worth of stock of essential medications for the PHCs in close coordination with the PHC Department at the MOPH. Moreover, WHO will be supporting the environmental assessment of the impact of the explosion and will develop guidance based on the results of the assessment.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response Project for conflict affected people in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene
for IDPs/host communities and returnees living in the hard to reach areas of South
Sudan. It will target newly displaced people, returnees and host communities affected by
conflict. The project will focus on providing emergency WASH services to the displaced
persons including most vulnerable host communities and also support the areas of
returns. Focus will be on the repair and construction of Water points, training hand pumps
mechanics, provision of hygiene and dignity kits and water treatment materials as well as
hygiene promotion and messaging to increase awareness among the affected population
and reduce the incidence water born diseases. The affected population will also be
supported in the construction of emergency latrines specifically targeting the most
vulnerable and newly displaced people. The project will be delivered through a rapid
response mechanism in project locations selected in line with the cluster prioritizing
process.

The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities for 2019 HRP's SO 1 and SO2. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 14 days for full-fledged delivery of WASH services and other activities per location. The project will also support returnees in settlement as a part of their local integration or returns to their areas of origin. This will be done in an integrated way with other projects being implemented by NRC so that the returnees don’t only receive WASH support but also a source of Food security and Livelihood through the food security projects in the planned locations. Additionally, the project will be implemented together with provision for education in emergencies and Legal Counseling will be made for the returnees where NRC is already implementing such projects e.g. by providing WASH services in schools or communities or return.


The WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EP&R) WASH actors where implementation is based on the multi-sector assessments and team involving WASH, Shelter, Food security and emergency Education with protection as a cross cutting theme. In some of the locations, the WASH projects link up with other emergency projects to ensure the beneficiaries receive a comprehensive response package. The project will be implemented in coordination with other players in the sector especially UNICEF for information sharing and use of the cluster core pipeline supplies when needed as well as other WASH cluster members for joint assessments and response when appropriate. The project will also be coordinated with the WASH and Logistics clusters especially in prioritization of locations and delivery of supplies.

project_name: Améliorer durablement la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populatios et la résilience des populations des Mayo Sava et Mayo Tsanaga les plus affectées par la crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad.
project_objective:
Contexte 
L’Extrême Nord (EN) du Cameroun est le théâtre d’actions de groupes armés occasionnant des mouvements massifs de réfugiés nigérians et de populations camerounaises. Dans un contexte marqué par des sécheresses récurrentes, l’EN fait face à des défis structurels importants. Les populations migrantes et leurs hôtes se trouvent démunis et leurs moyens d'existence profondément affaiblis. Les chocs continuent de survenir, accentuant la vulnérabilité de ces populations. 
Selon la SMART de 2019, dans l’EN les prévalences de MAG sont de 5.2% et de MAS 1.4%, traduisant une situation d’alerte avancée. La même enquête révèle qu’avec une prévalence de malnutrition chronique de 38.2% et une insuffisance pondérale de 20.2%, la région de l’EN est dans une situation d’alerte pour la malnutrition aiguë globale et le retard de croissance chez les enfants de moins de 05 ans. Cette situation est révélatrice des difficultés d'accès à la nourriture des ménages les plus pauvres, due aux faibles revenus monétaires et à un accès limité aux facteurs de production. Si l'insécurité nutritionnelle est chronique dans le Sahel, elle s'accompagne de crises alimentaires particulièrement sévères en période de soudure (de mai/juin jusqu’à septembre/début octobre).
Capacité de réponse
PUI, forte de son expérience multisectorielle en WASH, abri, sécurité alimentaire, moyens d’existence et de ses projets en réponse aux urgences, notamment dans la mise en place du Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) sous financement ECHO (ECHO/AF/BUD/2018/92045), propose de continuer de renforcer les conditions de vie des populations les plus affectées par la crise et les mouvements de populations, dans les départements du Mayo-Sava et du Mayo-Tsanaga. 
PUI, à travers une réponse de lutte contre l'insécurité alimentaire aggravée par les mouvements de populations,  se propose d’agir sur l’accès direct à la nourriture des ménages les plus vulnérables pendant la période de soudure (Résultat 1), ainsi qu’après un choc si aucun partenaire en assistance alimentaire n’est engagé (Résultat 2). La stratégie d’intervention vise à rendre la dignité et l’autonomie des bénéficiaires par des méthodologies d’intervention basées sur l’implication des communautés pour augmenter durablement leurs capacités de résilience.

project_name: Supporting Stabilisation in Libya through Humanitarian Mine Action
project_objective:
In Libya, the presence of explosive remnants of war (ERW) poses a significant protection concern to the civilian population. ERW continue to threaten physical security, restrict movement, impede livelihood opportunities, and prevent access to basic services. Following the escalation of violence in April 2019, active fighting largely concentrated on Tripoli means that the level of contamination continues to grow. 

The HALO Trust has introduced mechanical clearance to Libya. Despite previous efforts by several humanitarian mine action organisations to remove unexploded ordnance and provide risk education to those living in areas impacted by ERW, the technical knowledge for large-scale clearance was missing. Drawing on its 30 years of experience in mechanical clearance, HALO has introduced the equipment and skills necessary to work systematically through potentially contaminated rubble and collapsed buildings. HALO is upgrading and armouring civil engineering machinery including excavators, front loaders, and dumper trucks. Operations currently focus on the coastal city of Sirte, the former Gaddafi stronghold and last bastion of ISIS in North Africa until their defeat in 2016. HALO’s first mechanical clearance teams in Sirte received full accreditation by the Libyan Mine Action Centre (LibMAC) in October 2019. 

In addition to ERW contamination of urban areas, unsafe storage of weapons and ammunition in destroyed facilities remains a threat to civilians as well as to stabilisation efforts in Libya and the wider region. During the 2011 NATO campaign in support of the Arab uprisings, hundreds of Ammunition Storage Areas (ASAs) across Libya were targeted by NATO airstrikes. The airstrikes on ASAs threw huge stores of damaged munitions into urban areas in close proximity to critical infrastructure. Thrown out weapons and ammunitions are being used by both state and non-state actors to further their objectives throughout Libya and the region. The volatile security situation, continued presence of non-state armed groups, and a political power vacuum throughout most of Libya facilitate the movement of weapons and munitions throughout the region.

Building on HALO’s expertise in mechanical clearance in Sirte and ERW hazard mapping in Tripoli, HALO aims to expand its mechanical clearance capacity to launch a comprehensive clearance project in Misrata. While plans are underway to extend operations to several other locations, including Tripoli and Benghazi, HALO seeks to clear ASAs in Misrata first, as HALO already has an established presence there, including office facilities and good relations with the municipal authorities. The project does not only reduce the risk to the local communities living close to the storage facilities but also curbs the threat of illicit proliferation of weaponry in the region.

HALO is currently implementing an innovative ERW mapping and information management (IM) project in Tripoli. By using open source data collation and verification tools, HALO aims to create heat maps of conflict hotspots and to establish a live database logging information on ERW contamination. The goal is to provide IM capability to advise the LibMAC, UN and humanitarian organisations working in Libya on the extent and nature of ERW contamination, including information on types of ammunition and weapon systems and frequency of ERW accidents. This enables the LibMAC to coordinate and direct specialist clearance capacity to the most highly contaminated areas as soon as fighting ceases. Once fighting stops, HALO will be able to move into the zone to conduct on-the-ground survey and plan clearance operations. Teams that were trained in EOD and mechanical clearance in Misrata can then be redeployed to Tripoli. 

HALO is also authorised to work in the East and seeks to commence operations in Benghazi in 2020.

The return of people to their homes of origin will add to the already overwhelming humanitarian crisis across South Sudan communities. Therefore through this project, African Christian Kush Aid Program will use approaches that also contribute to long term community solutions by ensuring proper coordination within the Cluster and stakeholders at community level. project_name: Program Based Approach / Preventing and Responding to protection and basic needs in the South West, IRC Cameroon
project_objective:
This project includes 2 main components:

Component 1 - The Programme-based approach (PBA) funding in its 3rd year of implementation will pursue the scale up of the IRC multi-sectoral programming, building on successful implementation of emergency basic needs, WASH, and protection programming. The IRC will prioritize its response to the divisions of Ndian, Memeand Fako. Depending on confirmation of complementary funding for the southwest, the flexibility of the PBA funding would be leveraged to begin programming in Lebialem division, a hard-to-reach area, enhancing scale, reach and capacity for responsive and adaptive programming in the volatile context of the SW. In the NW, the IRC will prioritize its interventions in Mezam and/or Momo divisions in complementarity with other funding sources to provision of basic needs and services to targeted populations,  where the PBA funding will be used to build on its small-scale programming to ensure stronger foundation and programming sustainability in Mezam and/or Momo division. The IRC will remain flexible to shift geographic focus within these all those divisions, based on confirmation of most recent needs and gaps analysis, clients’ feedback and IRC’s operational capacity – including the confirmation of complementary funding which would allow for scale up of response. In addition, a contingency line will be kept for SW/NW to allow for rapid response to emerging needs in a flexible manner. 


Component 2- The humanitarian crisis in the Southwest and Northwest region of Cameroon has exposed the local population to large scale protection risks and human rights violations, and impacted vulnerable households’ capacity to meet their emergency food needs. Through this Action, the IRC seeks to improve the protection and food security status of vulnerable people affected by the crisis in Southwest Cameroon, assisting the most vulnerable people to stay safe, access assistance, recover from violence and claim their rights. The IRC will do this through an integrated program of Protection prevention and response activities including food voucher programming to mitigate further protection risks resulting from the use of negative coping mechanisms. Prevention activities will include information provision, awareness-raising, and sensitization activities on protection risks and available safe protection, legal and administrative services, while strengthening the capacity of community-based organizations and justice actors. Response activities include provision of Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) for emergency needs, emergency psychosocial support (PSS) services to GBV survivors within safe spaces in health facilities, and support for health service fees and transport costs for identified emergency protection cases. Furthermore, the IRC will provide emergency food assistance to the most vulnerable and at risk of additional exposure to potentially life-threatening protection risks due to reliance on negative coping mechanisms to meet emergency food needs. 

In addition, as co-lead of the Protection Cluster in the South West, the IRC will work closely with protection actors to ensure harmonized information sharing, capacity building, and effective operational and programmatic coordination to ensure synergies are systematically explored and enabled.

project_name: WASH Assistance in Quneitra, Rural Damascus, Rural Hama and Rural Aleppo
project_objective:
After nine years of conflict, WASH systems have suffered from damages owing to years of functioning at high capacity where large numbers of IDPs overburdened the system, limited or no maintenance, destructions, displacement of technical staff and effects of climate change and poor water resources management. WASH infrastructures and service provision thus require significant investments, repairs and operational support. Though affecting the overall population, individuals with little immunity such as children, pregnant women and elderly are particularly at risk as dysfunctional or lack of WASH facilities increase the risk of widespread waterborne diseases and directly threaten their health.

Through the proposed intervention, SIF will directly contribute to SO1 through improving access to safe water for drinking and domestic purposes through the rehabilitation of sewage networks in some of the highest severity ranking sub-districts of Duma (Rural Damascus), As-Saan and Muhardeh (Rural Hama) and Eastern Kweires and Jebel Saman (Rural Aleppo). The intervention will mainly consist in replacing sewage pipes, excavating manholes and connecting sub-sewage lines to the general sewage network. Moreover, SIF will contribute to SO4 through rehabilitating WASH facilities in 8 public schools in Shafuniyeh (1), Qahtanieh (1), Karnaz (1), Mourek (1), Eastern Kwaires (2) and Jabel Saman (2) sub-districts. The intervention will consist in rehabilitating existing WASH facilities, supplying new toilet blocks and fountains and providing toilet blocks for students with disabilities including ramps and steel handrails. These localities were selected based on their level of accessibility and the severity of needs as per 2020 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), SIF field assessments and consultations with local authorities and municipalities of each targeted sub-district.
This intervention is based on SIF’s experience over the past 8 years implementing WASH projects in Syria. In 2019, SIF reached a total number of 56,401 beneficiaries through various WASH interventions such as rehabilitation of water and sewage networks, distribution of water tanks and rehabilitation of boreholes across Rural Damascus, Hama, Dar’a and Aleppo governorates.
Regarding sewage network rehabilitation, the intervention will directly benefit: 
-	1,500 individuals in Rural Damascus (50% men, 50% women), including 550 children, 600 adults and 350 elderlies;
-	12,750 in Rural Hama (50% men, 50% women), including 3,825 children, 5,100 adults and 3,825 elderlies;
-	8,500 in Rural Aleppo (50% men, 50% women), including 2,550 children, 3,400 adults and 2,550 elderlies.
The above-mentioned figures are based on preliminary estimations and could change during the implementation.  Besides, upgraded WASH facilities in public schools, including improved access to water supply and sanitation facilities, will benefit to an estimated number of 3,200 children (50% men, 50% women), with approximatively 400 children per public school. Regarding GBV/PSEA, SIF will pay specific attention to children by providing them with quality gender and disabled friendly WASH facilities taking into account menstrual needs and including locking doors and lighting in public schools. SIF will also ensure to provide WASH facilities accessible for children with disabilities. This integrated project will be implemented in close collaboration with Education, Shelter and Protection sectors, and will aim at rehabilitating private houses and public schools, and providing non-formal education, psychosocial support (PSS) and child protection awareness sessions to children and adolescents inside public schools. This WASH project will thus participate in fostering returnees’ movements towards their home town through providing quality sewage services and improving children access to education through providing quality WASH facilities inside public schools.

project_name: Provision of Emergency WASH Assistance for Affected Populations in South Sudan
project_objective: This project intends to provide integrated and equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services to IDPs, host communities and returnees in the affected areas. The project will build on existing WASH services and emergency response mechanisms that will be coupled with GBV risk mitigation and accessibility inclusion components. IOM will ensure WASH services benefit conflict-affected populations in hard-to-reach areas in Protection of Civilians (PoCs) sites located in Bentiu, Malakal and Wau, including the collective centres in Wau. IOM WASH services will target 149,608 beneficiaries (40,394 women, 34,410 men, 39,347 girls and 35,457 boys). IOM will continue providing and maintaining WASH services through operation and maintenance of safe and accessible water supply systems; care and maintenance of accessible and secure sanitation and handwashing facilities; and solid and liquid waste management. IOM will sustain and improve the promotion of hygiene and public health, focusing on community ownership methods. Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPnR) teams will expand access to WASH services to underserved and vulnerable populations in remote and hard-to-reach locations lacking access to basic services, as identified by the Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG), Inter-Cluster Working Group (ICWG) and in coordination with WASH Cluster coordination mechanisms. The intervention aims to target 214,628 beneficiaries (57,950 women, 49,364 men, 56,447 girls and 50,867 boys). IOM will ensure provision of safe water through borehole rehabilitation, manual drilling of boreholes, rehabilitation of surface water treatment systems, distribution of water treatment supplies and water trucking. IOM will ensure the sustainability of water supply through the formation and training of water management committees, pump mechanics and the provision of spare parts for ongoing care and maintenance of boreholes. For manual drilling, IOM will ensure the community members are engaged throughout the process, through site selection, accessibility and safety, selection and training of drilling crew members from the community, and through contributions such as food for drilling team. IOM will additionally promote good hygiene and sanitation practices through hygiene promotion activities and distribution of basic household hygiene items, including training and distribution of menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits to women and girls of menstrual age. IOM will ensure that prevention and mitigation of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and AAP activities are mainstreamed throughout activities. As mitigation plan, IOM will continue with the EVD surveillance and preparedness activities along South Sudan, Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda through community hygiene and health promotion, and installation of handwashing and sanitation facilities in the point of entries (PoE) and health facilities. This intervention will target 57,470 individuals (15,517 women, 13,218 men, 15,115 girls and 13,620 men). IOM also plans to expand WASH and mitigation and prevention GBV services to assist IDPs outside PoCs and collective centers, and returnees and host communities through community participation and engagement. IOM will facilitate the reintegration at community level by improving access to WASH services as most infrastructure was destroyed during the conflict, including GBV risk mitigation activities. Through capacity building, IOM will ensure that communities are trained and able to respond during diseases outbreaks or conflict-affected displacement before humanitarian organizations are able to access and provide additional support.

project_name: Management of WASH Core Pipeline supplies to strengthen WASH sector’s preparedness and integrated response in South Sudan
project_objective:
This project aims to bolster the WASH cluster’s capacity to respond to emerging humanitarian response in locations with greatest needs through the management of the portion of the WASH core pipeline. In 2020, IOM will continue its commitment to support the WASH Cluster by aiming to procure and manage core pipeline supplies to benefit 722,844 people targeted to be assisted with lifesaving WASH emergency assistance. The project activities are in line with Strategic Objective (SO) 1, 2 and 3 of HRP 2020, as well as the WASH Cluster Objectives 1, 2, and 3. IOM Pipeline will procure, transport and manage the supplies needed for the WASH Cluster minimum packages for quality interventions integrated across sectors, targeting the acute vulnerabilities in South Sudan. Supplies procured will include items indicated by WASH Cluster as key basic supplies needed in WASH frontline response, such as household water treatment and storage, water quality testing supplies, bulk water treatment and storage, hand pump spare parts and tool kits, latrine materials, basic hygiene supplies Type of responses to be supported will include both static and mobile responses, covering response locations within and outside PoCs in South Sudan. 
IOM Pipeline will work closely with the WASH Cluster and State Focal Points to ensure prioritized and coordinated coverage across the country, minimizing gaps and overlap of services. IOM will also maintain strong coordination with other Clusters such as the Shelter/NFI, Health and the Logistics to ensure more vulnerable and underserved populations have access to WASH core pipeline supplies to maintain their basic WASH standard. The common pipeline system implementation in South Sudan has been effective as it optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. Through the management and provision of core pipeline supplies, IOM supports the inter-sectoral collaboration which mainstreams the key-cross cutting issues such as gender equality, AAP, protection, disability inclusion and GBV prevention and mitigation, including SEA prevention effectively in every response. IOM common pipeline ensures the provision of reliable and quality gender-sensitive items such as menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kit and hygiene kits

project_name: Support Shelter-NFI Cluster’s capacity to improve access of targeted beneficiaries to safe and appropriate life- saving Shelter and NFI supplies in South Sudan.
project_objective: IOM, as Cluster Lead Agency, has been successfully managing the Shelter and NFI (S-NFI) Core Pipeline since 2011 and has the capacity to continue providing critical services to Cluster Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP)partners. Based on its experience and on-the-ground presence, IOM will ensure swift delivery of life saving assistance to partners and beneficiaries through effective supply chain management. Under the HRP 2020, S-NFI Cluster Pipeline plans to reach 823,251 (80% of total target) beneficiaries across South Sudan. SNFI Pipeline is responsible for procuring, transporting and storing S-NFI materials. Upon S/NFI Cluster endorsement, the Pipeline will receive and process partners’ requests for distribution and prepositioning. The Pipeline team will coordinate with the Logistics Cluster, to ensure cargo movement for planned responses and for stock prepositioning. Further, the Pipeline team will ensure transport and storage from Juba to the main logistics hubs; ensure support to distributing partners on cargo movement by road; and coordinate with the Logistics Cluster for cargo shipment by air. The Shelter-NFI Pipeline provides partners with rapid access to critical materials to meet the emergency needs of most vulnerable populations. In order to allow partners timely access to S-NFI supplies, items are procured centrally by one organization and prepositioned in strategic locations, mainly Bentiu, Bor, Wau, Malakal and Rumbek, but also Torit, Mundri, Yambio, in order to expedite the process by which items are moved to the final distribution sites in field location. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The Pipeline will conduct a survey with partners to gather feedback on efficiency, appropriateness and coverage of the pipeline, the findings of which will be utilized to adjust programming as appropriate. It will also collect beneficiary’s feedback through Post Distribution Monitoring and Rapid Monitoring conducted by its partners on quality, appropriateness and usage of supplies.

project_name: Supporting Survivors and Addressing Risks and Root Causes of GBV in Conflict-Affected Areas of South Sudan
project_objective:
Recent studies indicate a high prevalence of GBV in South Sudan (IRC, 2017; IOM, 2017). The needs for GBV services are high, yet availability of multi-sectoral GBV services across the country is low, and access remains a challenge for women, especially in rural communities. In the context of protracted conflict, displacement, and the dire economic and food security situation, individuals and families have resorted to risky coping mechanisms, such as increased forced and early marriages and survival sex.  Areas of return and locations of displacement outside camps are often underserved by services, which heighten risks for women and girls. 

The prevalence of GBV is underpinned by a patriarchal social system reinforced by other harmful gender norms. The conflict and economic collapse have affect men’s ability to provide for and protect their families. For those unable to live up to idealized norms of masculinity, acts of violence and crime are used to express their authority and control. Youth gangs, blamed for increase in crime including GBV, have increase in urban centres of Wau and Juba, as traditional leadership has been eroded. There is a need to engage men and boys, particularly disenfranchised youth in being part of the solution to prevent GBV, particularly in transitional and recovery locations. 

IOM works to ensure a consistent and robust approach to addressing gender-based violence in crises, utilizing IOM’s institutional framework (2018). This project will contribute significantly to protection and gender equality and includes conscious strategies for inclusion of marginalised groups. IOM will contribute to Protection Cluster Objectives PO1 and PO2 through the following activities in Juba, Wau, Twic (Warrap) and Magwi:
•	GBV response: Providing psychosocial support and case management, Establish and operate women and girls friendly spaces (WGFSs), awareness raising on available GBV services, build capacity of multi-sectoral service providers, provide dignity kits to strengthen protection outcomes. 
•	GBV prevention: Conduct GBV behaviour change and harmful social norms programming utilizing EMAP, empower women and girls through targeted livelihoods, leadership and life-skills activities.
•	GBV risk mitigation: Build skills and attitudes among WASH, livelihoods and peacebuilding actors on risk mitigation, women’s participation and to address the gender gap in humanitarian employment opportunities.

project_name: Projet intégré d'appui à la résilience des populations vulnérables réfugiées, déplacées, retournées et hôtes de la région de Diffa, Niger
project_objective:
Ce projet de 36 mois (02/01/2019 au 01/01/2021) mené en consortium avec IMPACT, Welthungerhilfe, Concern Worldwide sous le lead d’ACTED vise à appuyer la stratégie d’urbanisation mise en œuvre par l’UNHCR et du CISP dans 6 communes de la région de Diffa au Niger. L’objectif général du projet est d’améliorer les conditions de vie, la résilience des populations vulnérables et la cohésion sociale à travers le relèvement économique, social et gouvernemental des 6 communes. 
Pour l'année 2020 (année 2 du projet), 15 750 personnes soit 2 250 ménages (au total pour les 3 années du projet ce sont 42 000 personnes soit 6 000 ménages) déplacés, retournés, réfugiés et hôtes (8% réfugiés et 92% de déplacés/hôtes/retournés) dans 6 communes de la région de Diffa recevront un appui à travers une assistance multisectorielle : infrastructures communautaires, sécurité alimentaire, renforcement des moyens d’existence, appui à la coexistence pacifique, pour renforcer leur résilience et accompagner leur installation durable sur les nouveaux sites urbanisés. Un volet AGORA cherchera en parallèle à renforcer les capacités des acteurs locaux et appuyer les cadres de concertation entre les parties prenantes du projet. 

Les objectifs spécifiques du projet sont :
- Objectif spécifique 1 : Améliorer l’accès des ménages et groupes vulnérables aux infrastructures et services sociaux de base (eau/assainissement, santé/nutrition et éducation) 
- Objectif spécifique 2 : Améliorer durablement les capacités des communautés, des ménages et des personnes les plus vulnérables à anticiper, absorber et se relever des chocs affectant leur sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle 
- Objectif spécifique 3 : Assurer une gouvernance décentralisée forte en renforçant les capacités des autorités et services techniques 
- Objectif spécifique 4 : Renforcer le développement local à travers la création d’opportunités économiques et le développement des capacités économiques locales.
- Objectif transversal : Promouvoir la coexistence pacifique et faciliter la communication entre les différentes couches de la population

• Extend the coverage of the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) in the 17 districts of Cabo Delgado and in the other affected districts in Neighboring provinces (Nampula and Niassa), utilising permanent teams on the ground and utilising and strengthening key informant networks to provide monthly baseline assessments in all locations and multi-sectoral location assessments (MSLA), paired with household assessments, to support the response, in close coordination with all clusters. 
 • Provide reporting and analysis on a monthly basis, including dashboard, maps and multisectoral reports on needs of displaced populations;
 • Use the DTM Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) to capture new and sudden displacement trends on a weekly basis, including arrivals and departures; and the publication of flash updates on a regular basis to support the rapid response from the Government and humanitarian community. 
 • Undertake training for local authorities, partners and to extend key informant networks to ensure access to hard to reach areas as well as to increase capacities.

project_name: Appui à la sécurité alimentaire et aux moyens d’existence des personnes vulnérables des provinces du Lac et du Logone Occidental
project_objective:
L'objectif principal du projet est d'améliorer la sécurité alimentaire des populations touchées par des crises au Tchad à travers une assistance alimentaire et la mise en place de systèmes agricoles résilients.   
 En outre le projet vise à renforcer la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations déplacées et retournées dans 3 départements (Fouli Kaya et Mamdi)  de la province du Lac Tchad.  Le même objectif sera poursuivi dans le Lac Wey. Enfin les activités du projet viseront à renforcer la capacité de résilience des ménages vulnérables du département du Kaya à travers un appui agricole.  
Ces objectifs seront remplies grâce aux activités suivantes: 

- Distribution générales de vivres dans le Fouli (province du Lac) et distribution d'intrants alimentaires aux enfants de 6 à 23 mois. 
- Distribution de cash et d'intrants alimentaires aux enfants de 6 à 23 mois dans les départements du Kaya et du Mamdi (province du Lac)
- Distribution de cash dans le département du Lac Wey
- Appui à 10 groupements agricoles dans le département du Kaya (province du Lac).

project_name: Supporting socio-economic development in Benghazi, Libya, through integrated Mine Action
project_objective: The city of Benghazi has serious need of clearance of the explosive remnants of war, so that critical infrastructure including schools, hospitals, electricity and water supply, as well as residential areas, to enable reconstruction and for those displaced to make a return. Both children and Adults require risk education to teach them the dangers of unexploded ordnance and how to adopt safe behaviour in such an environment. Additionally, medical professionals need support in victim assistance and their clinics lack a supply of equipment for victims of unexploded ordnance. DCA have worked in Libya since 2011 and have consistently had an office in Benghazi, from which national and international staff deliver a wide range of projects both through direct implementation and through our civil society organization partners. For this project; DCA will select and train 2 teams of deminers/searchers and then lead and mentor them in the clearance of UXO in priority areas of the city, so that essential services can be reopened and the citizens of Benghazi can access them safely; DCA will, through its CSO partner, deliver risk education to children and youth in schools, colleges and universities, and to adult workers, and female headed households; DCA will also continue to work with medical professionals involved in victim assistance and provide further support to them in terms of training and additionally provide walking aids and wheelchairs to specialist clinics and in coordination with the Ministry of Health and Libyan Red Crescent. In essence the project will address 3 critical pillars of mine action and benefit men, women, and children in areas most affected by conflict and suffering from contamination from UXO. The project will be delivered by DCA’s national and international staff in Benghazi and have a duration of 18 months.

project_name: Protection of Children from COVID 19 and provision of Child Protection services for Children with specific needs and vulnerabilities
project_objective:
COVID-19 is having an unprecedented impact around the world, both in terms of the need to drastically scale public health preparedness and response, as well as putting measures to protect vulnerable populations.  Nigeria as the most populous country in African with high population density in many cities, coupled with a weak health system, poor hygiene practices and an ongoing humanitarian crisis in the North East makes it particularly vulnerable to outbreaks like COVID-19. 

UNICEF and partners will ensure timely identification, documentation, tracing and reunification of UASC children as a result of  conflict and COVID 19 those exposed to conflict related violence including CRSV, children living in IDP camps who are likely to be affected in the event of an outbreak, children recruited and used by armed groups, and other vulnerable children to be provided and referred for immediate assistance. UNICEF will support partners to implement COVID19 mitigation measures and response for children and community members and  conduct close monitoring for the adoption of negative coping mechanisms fueled by COVID-19. 

The response will include  other interventions such as raising awareness of COVID-19 and putting in mitigation measures at Child Friendly Spaces Safe Spaces and  Interim Care Centres. Remote and restricted MHPSS services andcase management services for UASC will be provided for children in high risk areas. Children and caregivers will be provided with radios for COVID-19 messaging and girls who have been exposed to sexual gender based violence would be support with among others, dignity kits. Cash transfer modalities or payments may be provided to caregivers who are providing alternative care for UASC and children while monitoring grave violations against children.  

Child Protection will support with remote training (e-learning), CPIMS mobile reporting of COVID-19 affected children. Further, referral pathways will be developed, and  technical guidance provided to social workers and community volunteers to enhance their skills in identifying cases of severe distress and protection concerns linked to COVID-19. Messages on positive coping strategies will also be shared as this is critical particularly for children in alternative care and interim care centres, to mitigate negative economic effect of lost livelihoods for household members in isolation, or to reduce the economic burden of children reintegrated from armed groups.. Overall, Best interest of the Child and ‘Do No Harm’ principles will be applied across the response.

project_name: Improvement of the Protection of People of Concern in North East Nigeria Through the Provision of Shelter and NFI Assistance.
project_objective: This project will target IDPs and returnees in three affected states, Yobe, Adamawa and Borno with provision of emergency shelters, Non-food Items (NFIs), transitional and shelter repair kits as protection live-saving assistance aligned with Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM Sector strategic objectives for the HRP 2019. In 2019 UNHCR continued to effectively respond to shelter needs and aims to target a total of 69,569 households, 347,846 individuals in formal and informal camps and newly accessible areas by the end of the year. As the number of returns and displacement increases due to military operations, there is need to provide shelter related assistance for returnees who are residing in their plots and as well as for host families whose resources have been overstretched. Subsequently acknowledging that the humanitarian situation is still unpredictable; there is need to provide shelters and NFIs for life-saving emergency assistance to promote the protection, safety and dignity of affected Persons of Concern (PoCs). Despite the achievements in the past, the continuous needs for IDPs, though shaped by very different dynamics, revealed that quite a significant majority of people are living in congested camps. The needs assessment conducted in 2019 by Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM sector indicated that as of end of June 2019, 3809 IDP households were living without shelter and NFI assistance since their arrival. In addition to that, 7593 households living in partitioned communal shelters needed NFIs and dignified emergency shelters. The ongoing and protracted displacement leaves the affected people in need of other humanitarian assistance such as Food, WASH, and Health among others. In 2020, UNHCR shall build upon progress being made in 2019 and proposes to respond to unmet needs in Adamawa (Mubi North, Mubi South, Madagali, Michika, Yola South and Yola north); Borno (Bama, Banki, Damasak, Damboa, Dikwa, Jere, konduga, Gwoza, Pulka, Maiduguri, Mobbar, Monguno, Rann and Ngala) and Yobe State (Damaturu and Gujba,) through provision of; - (1) 7,000 Emergency shelters (2) 52,129 NFIs kits to IDPs in both formal and informal camps (3) 10,440 Shelter repair kits to returnees with the provision of conditional CASH component of NGN 30,000 Naira adequate to cover for the cost labor and molding of mud bricks among other unforeseen needs. All the shelters are designed to cater for Women, Men, Girls and boys, persons with specific needs and partitioned to mitigate SGBV cases. The selection of beneficiaries will be based on needs assessment and vulnerability screening in the locations at the time of implementation. Identification and verification of beneficiaries are guided by UNHCR’s Protection principles, and endorsed by community leaders, NEMA, and SEMA officials at LGA areas. UNHCR will reinforce a transparent process of beneficiary selection and the prioritization of needs of vulnerable groups. The project targets the IDPs and Returnees households suffering from protracted displacement and returning home. UNHCR will work to ensure that potential beneficiaries are aware of their responsibilities during the project and of options available to them. It is important to recognize that not everyone can manage the construction/ repair of their own house and that their time might be better used to generate income. The families’ decision to participate in this programme will be achieved through sensitization meetings, detailed assessments, participatory planning and prioritizing the provision of technical training and capacity building. A community-based feedback mechanism through regular mass meetings and focus group discussions will be established to enable IDPs express their opinions on issues affecting their assistance need. The discussions will also provide beneficiaries the opportunity to understand the shelter selection and allocation process.

project_name: Strengthen Emergency Response through Camp Coordination and Camp Management in North East
project_objective: The project seeks to fill the gaps of CCCM Sector in line with the centrality of protection strategy and will target 120,000 women, men, boys and girls IDPs living in the camps, camp-like settings, IDPs out of camps and host community that received the IDPs and dwelling in their houses. The project will cover 4 LGAs in Borno (Ngala, Munguno, Banki and Damasak), 4 LGAs in Adamawa (Yola South, Yola North, Mubi and Madagali) and 2 LGAs in Yobe state (Damaturu and Gujba). The breakdown of the target for this CCCM project is 97,298 individuals (19,460HH) for IDPs and 22,702 individuals (4,540 HH) for returnees distributed as follow: 46% (male), 54% (female), 60% (children), 36% (adult) and 4% (elders). The CCCM Project will be addressing the gaps of tracking movement of population (new arrivals and returnees) particularly the most vulnerable including unaccompanied and separated children, assessing the needs of the women, men, boys, girls, adolescents and older displaced persons in a participatory manner and based on age, gender and diversity mainstreaming, supporting the coordination of response of service providers, capacitating the communities through their effective participation and ownership of activities and developing the resilience and self-reliance when they are still in displacement. The project will also focus on the sensitization of IDPs especially youth, boys, girls, adolescents and women who are facing different problem of protection. The CCCM project will improve the quality of management of the women, men, boys and girls IDPs within the camp settings, monitor and assist those out of camps and some vulnerable persons in host community. The project will support systematic follow up of the IDPs and returnees new arrivals particularly vulnerable women and girls. The project seeks to provide quality services during the registration process and will ensure that reception facilities are equally accessible to women, men, boys and girls newly arrived. Camp managers will ensure proper relocation of new arrivals from the reception centers to the shelters constructed taking into account the needs of the most vulnerable. Through this project, CCCM interventions will also assess, analyze and report on all protection gaps and needs to be addressed by different sectors in order to improve the living conditions of women, men, girls and boys displaced. The CCCM project will promote the participation of the IDPs based on age, gender and diversity in the life cycle of camps particularly care and maintenance of infrastructures, small scale drainage, etc.

project_name: Humanitarian and Life-saving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Assisstance for IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in Sudan
project_objective: This project is aligning with cluster objectives that aiming to provide timely life-saving WASH assistance to crisis affected people to reduce mortality and morbidity, and to contribute to building resilience to recurrent shocks and improving vulnerable people’s access to basic WASH services, as well as enhancing the prevention and mitigation of protection risks and respond to protection needs, strengthen community resilience, and enhance risk mitigation measures. The project will target 92570 (23587 girls,21773 boys, 24077 women, and 23133 men) individuals in need living in 18 localities within 7 SCI priority states including Blue Nile, North Darfur, North Kordofan, South Kordofan, Centeral Darfur, West Darfur, and Red Sea states. The project will be focusing in provision of water supply at community and institutional level including construction, upgrading, improving, and rehabilitation of water sources, in addition to connection of water to schools, health facilities, and child friendly spaces. The project will contribute to elimination of open defecation within our operation areas through enhance the capacity of local communities and mobilizing targeted communities to construct their own latrines, this inline with the construction of emergency latrines during emergencies for people affected by crises. The project will also contribute to solid and medical management efforts through provision of garbage and collection tools, support disposal of solid wastes, construction of medical incinerators at health facilities to facilitate safe disposal of medical wastes. The project will focus on improving hygiene situation and status within the targeted communities to mitigate and reduce the risk of diseases outbreaks as a result of poor WASH services through general hygiene campaigns, awareness sessions, home visits as well as strengthening the capacity of local community committees such as hygiene promotors, conduct training and establishing hygiene clubs at schools and child friendly spaces. The project will create synergies ,complement, and integrate with Health, Nutrition and Food security within the targeted areas and worked with other sectors to address root causes of malnutrition and factors contributing to diseases outbreaks. The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $2,314,268.

project_name: Humanitarian life-saving health services for IDPs and host communities in Sudan
project_objective: This project is aligning with cluster objectives that aiming at increase equitable access to humanitarian life-saving and life-sustaining health services for those most vulnerable and in need, strengthen health sector capacity to prepare and deliver timely response to affected population by conflict, natural emergencies, and disease outbreaks, and strengthen health system capacity to support continuity of care, strengthen community resilience, and enhance risk mitigation measures. The project is targeting 480,035(112904 boys, 122313 girls, 117513 men & 127503 women) individuals in need living in 20 localities in 8 SCI priority states including Blue Nile, Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur, South Kordofan, West Kordofan, North Kordofan and Red Sea.  The project will deliver package of primary health care services including the treatment of communicable and non- communicable diseases, ensuring the availability of essential medicines, provision of MIPS for RH to support reproductive, neonatal, and child health, strengthening the expanded program of immunization EPI, infection prevention, health education, and mental- psychosocial support in addition to supporting referral to the secondary care services. The project will contribute to strengthening surveillance system and responding to disease outbreaks, including training and supporting Rapid Response Teams (RRTs), ensure weekly surveillance reports, supporting CTUs in the areas of high risk of cholera outbreaks. Drinking water in the targeted facilities will be chlorinated and monitored regularly. The project will contribute to building capacity of health care workers by conducting trainings to strengthening skills of staff to implement quality services. The project will be planned, implemented and monitored jointly with targeted communities and Ministry of Health. The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $3,000,000.

project_name: FSL I:  Emergency Food Security and Bakery Support Programme
project_objective:
FSL I aims to contribute to increased food security for vulnerable displaced and host community households in Idleb and Aleppo Governorates. FSL I comprise of two components: Household Food Security and Bakery Support. 
 
Within the Household Food Security component NGO X targets an average of 35,000 HH, 175,000 food-insecure individuals per month with in-kind food assistance (food kits) or cash modality (food restricted vouchers) and 4000 HH, 20,000 individuals with one off ready to eat kits. The regular food assistance is to the value of 70% of the food SMEB (Survival minimum expenditure basket) or 70% of the Sphere minimum standards of 2100 kcal/p/day.  
 
The Bakery Support component provides an approximate 300,000 individuals living in supported bakeries’ catchment area with bread at a reduced and stabilised price. This is achieved through subsidising up to 50% input (flour and yeast) of bread production thus supporting local bakeries to produce a stable quantity of bread that meets local needs. This support is conditional upon the selling of this bread in the local markets at a reduced and stabilised price agreed with and monitored by NGO X’s Cash and Markets, and Monitoring Teams. Approximately 22 bakeries are targeted to benefit from this assistance in FSL II.  

NGO X will implement the proposed project in partnership with NGO Z. Please note that NGO Z will input into the OCHA HPC separately under this project. This decision was agreed between both parties and submissions have been coordinated to ensure there is no duplication with regards to either budget or beneficiary targets. 

NGO X will target 5,296 children 6-59 months with daily energy and micronutrient dense nutrient supplements for approximately 6 months in IDP camps which are also targeted with regular food assistance. 

 NGO X has secured total funding for this project. NGO X has permission to operate in all proposed locations.

project_name: Cash-Based Interventions in the East, West, and South of Libya
project_objective:
This project aims to reduce the vulnerability of conflict-affected populations in the Western, Eastern and Southern regions of Libya through the provision of unconditional multi-sectoral cash assistance to internally displaced, non-displaced, and returnee households and improve their access to essential goods and services of their choice. This project will provide three installments of unconditional multi-sectoral cash assistance to approximately 400 vulnerable internally displaced, non-displaced, and returnee households in conflict-affected areas in the West, East, and South of the country.
In cooperation with coordination structures, notably the Cash and Market Working Group (CMWG), REACH proposes to conducting market monitoring and analysis in 2020 through its Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI). Through the monthly monitoring and analysis of prices and market systems, the initiatives improves the understanding among humanitarian agencies and organizations of how markets in Libya are functioning and reacting to the crisis. The JMMI also supports and facilitates the planning, implementation, and evaluation of cash-based interventions (CBI) in Libya by giving accurate information on the prices and availability of key Food and Non-Food Items.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED- READO protection project for GBV survivors and children victim of violence through comprehensive case management and mentoring
project_objective:
Overtime READO has realized that because of the widespread and severity of GBV cases in Baidoa, it is important for actors to lay the ground for offering or addressing the post practice using a strong foundation while efforts are directed at preventive and curative measures.
READO has health facilities and referral centers in Baidoa especially where statistics show is still hugely affected by the GBV practice and women rights abuse. It also operates in most IDP settlements surrounding Baidoa town. It has developed network with medical practitioners, legal aid, religious support system, local actors, IDP leaders and local administration to establish a solid network of support to strongly approach issues dealing with GBV and blatant violation of the rights of women, men, boys and girls.
READO will develop unique approach based on each area of target of the project. For counseling services of the GBV affected victims the organization will establish the current data base of the possible victims based on the available estimates. This is because GBV cases will be reported daily and counseling services offered as well as referrals in cases that require higher level of medical attention especially GBV and mental cases or other related cases. To do this the organization will need rough estimates based on the flow of similar statistics for the past 3 months which will enable the organization to set up the required outlets for the counseling services and referrals and assigning the right number of staff for the activity within the required time period. Awareness activities shall be held monthly and during national events. During these times, the local Somali professional especially medical practitioners will be used to showcase the dangers of the harmful practices. The messages shall also be posted in popular Somali websites and local May-May language radio stations to increase the reach of the message. These events shall be carried out in coordination with the local authority, local actors and the community structures within the project areas. The events shall also be done with the support and participation of GBV working groups who might want to participate in the events to maximize impact.
Planned activities also include distribution of emergency NFIs through in-kind distribution, Distribution of dignity kits through in-kind distribution and Training of READO humanitarian staff interacting with populations on Psycho-social First Aid and principled referrals besides awareness campaigns.
