project_name: Beirut Blast Shelter Response and Recovery Programme
project_objective:
According to the Shelter Sector, the 4 August blast impacted an estimated 72,265 apartments in 9,700 buildings located within three kilometres of the epicenter. It is believed that 29,771 apartments (89,313 individuals) fall within level 1 damages - minor damages, 17,100 apartments (51,300 ind.) fall within level 2 - moderate - and 1,144 apartments (30,660 ind.) fall within level 3 - heavy damage. The explosion also affected communal areas, shared open-spaces and minor infrastructure, further impacting community self-recovery capacity. 

With shelter needs at the core of the crisis, UNHCR will support men, women, girls and boys, both Lebanese and other nationalities, who were affected by the blast. UNHCR's response includes immediate weatherproofing temporary solutions, followed by a phased approach to support individuals and families to repair or rehabilitate houses and to sustain rental payments for those displaced. In addition, through community support projects and common area rehabilitation, UNHCR will enhance the safety, security, dignity and resilience of communities.

Speed and appropriateness of interventions, maximizing flexibility through rapid utilization of cash as a key modality for implementation, combined with ongoing response monitoring, will help ensure nimble and flexible interventions that are built on evolving needs. Community engagement will be at the centre of the response, ensuring effective participation. Beneficiary selections will also be based on the LRC emergency needs assessment in addition to UNHCR shelter partner assessments within allocated areas of intervention. According to CAS/ILO (LFHLC Survey), Beirut residents are comprised of about 7% children below 5 years of age, 13% between 5 and 14 years old, 15% between 15 and 24, 43% between 25 and 59, and 22% above 60 years old. In addition, 54% are female and 46% male. Age and gender considerations will thus guide the response, including with special considerations on the selection of beneficiaries and implementation modalities to address specific needs of particular groups. The response adopts a whole-population approach, targeting the most affected and most vulnerable households and individuals – including Lebanese, refugees and migrant workers – as well as their communities in the hardest hit and vulnerable areas affected by the blast. Do no harm, conflict-sensitivity and PSEA will be integrated throughout the response.

project_name: Scaling-up Shelter and NFIs for IDPs (New Arrivals) in Camps and Host Communities in Borno State
project_objective:
The protracted insecurity in Borno state has great shelter and NFIs impacts on the displaced population.
Following the recent and alarming surge in insecurity in northern and eastern Borno State and parts of Northeast, many persons have been displaced and push to find refugee in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) and other LGAs in the state. Many have since  arrived in MMC and other part of Borno have been staying without any form of NFIs.
This project aims to meet the immediate life-saving humanitarian needs of an estimated newly
displaced people from other part of Borno into MMC and camps in other LGAs, most of whom are living in deplorable conditions and urgently require humanitarian assistance especially NFIs and Shelters
The proposed project is targeting new arrivals who have fled inaccessible areas and are in dire need of aid and emergency shelters.
This project will be focusing only on the provision of Emergency Shelters and improved NFI kits to the most vulnerable in MMC and other LGAs in Borno state and the activities will include, community social mobilization, need assessment, beneficiary registration, procurement, warehousing, transportation, emergency land mapping and layout for emergency shelters, distribution of NFIs and post distribution monitoring every two weeks after distribution as the distribution will be done on a rolling-on-going bases according the the needs and sector directives.
In implementing this project GREENCODE will work closely with the Sector and the nationally approved guidelines and standard as uploaded in the Humanitarian Response Info will be used. 
Given the emergency shelter and NFI needs for the new arrivals in the MMC  and other LGAs and considering the important of providing lifesaving assistance, the project will procure, transport and distribute improved NFIs kits to the most vulnerable 700 households such as female and child headed HHs among IDPs (new arrival) in MMC based on needs of the gaps jointly identified/agreed by GREENCODE and Shelter/NFIs sector in Borno state. 
The distribution will be on a rolling/on-going basis as GREENCODE team will continue to assess, verify, and deliver assistance according to identified needs to affected populations wherever they are in MMC, and most likely in some in locations with gaps as directed and agreed with the Shelter/NFIs sector. 
In all stages of the project protection issues such as SGBV and child protection will be closely monitored and referred to appropriate partners for counselled and refer, also during distribution of NFIs.
GREENCODE will work with IOM, SEMA, UNHRC and Protection sector to ensure gender and age awareness including in the dis-aggregation of data and the targeting of female¬ headed households, incorporating gender dynamics and the specific needs of different groups into needs assessments and response recommendations. Further, GREENCODE will pay special attention recognising the different needs of women and children as well as men and boys of different ages, we will ensure targeting criteria are taking into consideration specific vulnerabilities and needs. Also, in procuring NFIs and ensure that kit contents procured for this project are gender sensitive as well as easy to use by women in performing daily tasks.

project_name: Increasing the Coping Capacity of the Most Vulnerable Conflict-Affected Populations in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in Eastern Ukraine is entering its sixth year, and multiple attempts at ceasefires having yielded little respite from ongoing violence. Conflict has compounded pre-existing economic and social vulnerabilities which challenge the ability of the population – particularly the most vulnerable groups, including women – to achieve economic prosperity or even economic security.
In GCA, the food security situation has overall not improved over the past 2 years; food insecurity levels remain high compared to pre-2014. Within 5km of the line of contact (LoC), the number of food insecure people ranges seasonally from 30,000 to 50,000, noting widespread erosion of coping strategies during and following winter.
The humanitarian community, including ACTED, has been engaged in a large-scale effort to meet the basic needs of the most vulnerable, particularly in the 5km area where 49% of HHs have received international assistance in the past 12 months (REACH 2018). On the one hand, it is essential to reach those who have not yet received assistance yet are in need. On the other hand, noting that the conflict continues to protract, it is also essential to assist some of most vulnerable in restoring their subsistence capacity, and decrease conflict-affected communities’ dependence on humanitarian aid through livelihood activities.
ACTED therefore proposes an intervention to increase the coping capacity of some of the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations within 5km of the LoC in Eastern Ukraine.
First, ACTED will address levels of food insecurity among conflict-affected populations just following winter, when household resources are depleted; and during the next winter, when food insecurity levels are observed to be highest. The project thus aims to reduce food insecurity of the most vulnerable conflict-affected individuals within 5km of the LoC. Targeting settlements with access to functional markets, ACTED will provide unconditional cash transfers to 6,500 individuals at the value of 825UAH/person/month in 2 distributions: 3 months of assistance in spring 2020 to 2,400 individuals (in 1 tranche), and 3 months of assistance in winter 2020 to 4,100 individuals (in 1 tranche).
Second, ACTED will distribute subsistence grants to support the most vulnerable HHs restore their livelihoods, targeting specific gender and age categories based on vulnerability analysis (women, heads of households who are unemployed but ineligible for pensions, single mothers…). ACTED will target the most vulnerable within 5km of the LoC: where this caseload is today almost exclusively targeted under short-term (e.g. cash) assistance programmes, ACTED will look to restore livelihoods through cash/voucher/in-kind grants (depending on beneficiary preferences and access to markets/inputs in given locations). 80 beneficiaries will be supported thus with grants valued at 1,200 USD. Based on the results of a livelihoods assessment conducted by ACTED in September 2018, ACTED expects that approx. 30% of its livelihood grant beneficiaries will be over 50 years old (noting pre-pensioners’ particular economic vulnerability given the economic situation in Donbas, but also cognizant of older people’s possible limited ability to engage in livelihoods activities: ACTED will encourage home based production for this group, and ensure at assessment stage that selected beneficiaries have the capacity to participate in the programme).
Ultimately, by increasing access to food and restoring livelihoods, ACTED will increase coping capacity.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Early Recovery of Livelihoods for the Most Vulnerable IDPs and Conflict affected along the Line of Contact
project_objective:
More than five years after the conflict had been started, the affected population’s needs in affected areas of eastern Ukraine are great, exceeding the capacity of Government of Ukraine (GoU) and requiring continuation of strong assistance from international humanitarian community. Data collection and analyses conducted as part of NRC’s responses over 2017-2019 years show that number of food insecure people, although somewhat decreased, is still very high. In average, the share of severely food insecure ranges around 1% of population in conflict affected areas, whereas in localities next to the Line of Contact (LoC) it is estimated to be at least 50% greater. As confirmed by several analyses done by relevant stakeholders, the most vulnerable groups are single member and elderly households, families with several children or with disabled members, and those whose breadwinners are chronically unemployed or without regular employment. In addition, residents of rural areas are significantly more vulnerable and surprisingly more often food insecure compared to

those living in urban or semi-urban areas. Due to various factors, such as limited access to land, difficult access to markets, unfavourable prices and depleted savings, agricultural households can hardly maintain their own food production. In addition, given the high unemployment rate in the country, especially IDPs have difficulties in getting a job, and therefore, according to IOM, in March 2019 only 48% of IDPs were employed. To be able to meet their basic needs, these categories regularly resort to negative coping strategies; according to IOM, 62% of IDPs were applying at least one coping strategy in February 2019 in GCA. To address these various needs of conflict affected population, NRC will continue its comprehensive support to the most vulnerable conflict-affected population in GCA to enable their: (1) access to food, (2) restoration of productive assets, and (3) employment and income generation opportunities. NRC has been implementing activities addressing access to food and early recovery in east Ukraine GCA since 2016. Programme activities are aligned with relevant GoU strategies and attempt to create synergies/linkages with the activities of recovery/development actors (HDN). Targeting primarily the most vulnerable IDPs and conflict-affected host communities along the LoC, beneficiaries will be selected from different age and social groups prioritizing elderly, female-headed and/or households with 2 or more children, persons with disabilities/medical cases and with no regular incomes.

project_name: Protection and multisector humanitarian assistance to highly vulnerable conflict-affected older people living in Donetska and Luhanska Oblasts
project_objective:
PAH will implement multisector programme to meet acute needs of 7584 highly vulnerable conflict-affected older people residing in Luhanska GCA as well as Donetska GCA and NGCA in such sectors, as protection, multipurpose cash assistance, WASH, food security and livelihood, and health. 
Donetska and Luhanska GCAs. PAH community-based volunteers will provide group PSS in three rounds to 2200 conflict-affected older people through operation of 8 Community Centres and 4 Community spaces. At the same time, PAH will provide individual PSS to the most vulnerable older people through two modalities: 1) home visits of community workers to conflict-affected home-bound older people; 2) individual psychological consultations provided by PAH psychologists upon beneficiaries’ request and via phone hotline. Moreover, 550 most vulnerable older people will be provided with assistive devices, so that it will contribute to the improvement of their physical and psychosocial (PS) well-being. 3000 persons from among PSS beneficiaries will be provided with MPCA during three months to meet their acute needs according to eligibility criteria developed by PAH. At the same time, 450 of the most vulnerable older people will be additionally provided with cash grants for healthcare expenses during 4 months, which will contribute to their physical and PS well-being and will allow beneficiaries to reduce their expenditures on medicines and treatment. PAH will also provide trainings on agriculture for those having plot and willing to do agricultural activities. As a result, 550 most vulnerable conflict-affected older people will be provided with one-time vouchers, which are to be redeemed during March-April 2020 to use them during agricultural season. WASH intervention within given programme is focused on WASH rehabilitation of 7 social and health institutions, so that their residents will have improved access to adequate sanitation. During the rehabilitation, PAH will address needs of people with disabilities. Moreover, safety requirements accordinr to Sphere Minimum Standards will be fulfilled: most of the lavatories will be separate for men and women, lavatory entrances will be adapted for people with disabilities, where possible. According to beneficiaries’ registration data as of October 2019, 48% of older people are people with disabilities in the light of the Washington Group Short Set of Question on Disability. While implementing the programme, PAH will address needs of persons with disabilities, where it is possible, and will ensure system of data collection on people with disabilities using Washington Group Short Set of Questions.
Donetska NGCA. PAH through its local partner will provide social home-based care, e.g. assistance with shopping, changing a light bulb, cleaning, paying bills, cooking etc. to 2800 highly vulnerable immobile older people or those with mobility restrictions. In addition, 550 most vulnerable home-bound older people will be provided with assistive devices, which will make them less dependent on external support. Social home-based care will be supplemented by provision of food kits and WASH NFI kits based upon recommendations of FSL Cluster and WASH Cluster respectively. Moreover, WASH NFI kits will be gender-sensitive. Food kits will be provided in three rounds, while distribution of WASH NFI kits will be one-time. In addition, in order to meet specific needs of people with disabilities, PAH will provide hygiene diapers to 300 beneficiaries with mobility restrictions in need. 
Combination of psychosocial support, multipurpose cash assistance, sanitation in institutions and agriculture and food security assistance shall reduce vulnerabilities of the conflict-affected older population living in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts through improved access to and provision of humanitarian assistance, early recovery and overall well-being.

project_name: Emergency WASH for the IDPs, host communities, returnees, GBV affected, risk of famine and outbreak affected population in South Sudan
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services for conflict affected people, vulnerable host communities and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. Over all the project will reach to about a population of 800,000 with WASH services and facilities. 

This emergency WASH project will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, frontline emergency WASH response, strengthening partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination as well information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere Standards. 

The project will focus on addressing the following: 

- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country 
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.) 
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related GBV.

The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs and CBOs in areas highly affected by the conflict to ensure basic services are provided and long-term capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_name: Provision of critical Shelter and NFI assistance to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
Under this project IOM will focus on shelter/NFI activities that ensure protection for population at risk of being affected by the COVID 19 pandemic, targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. 

To this end, IOM will: 
(A)	Support CCCM in enhancing reception capacities by providing quarantine facilities
(B)	Ensure access to different types of emergency shelter solutions for displaced populations through the distribution and prepositioning of emergency shelter kits,
(C)	 Contribute to decongestion through construction of emergency shelters, and rehabilitation of damaged public buildings, etc.;
(D)	 Ensure that the care, maintenance and upgrading of existing shelters are conducted for continued safety and comfort of the affected population;
(E)	 Ensure that households in host communities have access to materials and labour for repairing their damaged houses; 
(F)	Ensure IDPs in host communities are supported through cash for rent and security of tenure 
(G)	Ensure that households in IDP camps and host communities and returnees have access to basic and improved NFI kit
(H)	Support IDPs in camp, host communities, new arrival households and individuals at quarantine and Isolation centres with loose items
(I)	Supporting IDPs living in camp and host communities through Cash for improved NFIs 


IOM’s shelter activities will be implemented in two States of North East Nigeria; Borno (11 LGAs) and Adamawa (9 LGAs), targeting 88,000 individuals. IOM ensures that all shelter activities taken are accountable to the affected population and that the gender-specific needs of project beneficiaries are integrated. Shelter solutions are harmonized at sector level and coordinated with partners.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of Emergency Lifesaving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene services to Conflict Affected Communities in Benadir and Lower Shabelle Region.
project_objective:
The proposed Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) intervention seeks to contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity, related to the poor access to drought condition among IDPs and Host population in Daynile, Kahda districts in Mogadishu and Afgooye corridor of Lower Shebelle region. This will be achieved through increased access to adequate, safe and sustainable water and supporting and promoting a culture of good hygiene practice in order to reduce the related protection and diseases risks especially among women and girls in target locations.

The project will ensure and provide emergency and sustainable WASH services (latrines with hand washing facilities and safe drinking water through water trucking. For sustainable safe water services, SOYDA will upgrade one borehole equipped with hybrid to improve its water quality and reduce its running cost, in order to receive water in affordable cost. SOYDA will replace hybrid borehole and construct 5 water kiosks nearer to the IDP settlements supplied water through piping network to avoid the risk of rape against women and girls. The project will also promote adaption of good hygiene and sanitation practices through carrying out comprehensive hygiene promotion awareness & hygiene kit distribution and construction of 100 gender-sensitive and flood proof IDP latrines with lockable doors and hand washing facilities, rehabilitation of 30 IDP latrines and establishment of faecal sludge management (FSM) sites and systems to the Daynile and Kahda districts ; the team is composed 6 persons shared equally by men and women. Systems will be composed of trained FSM teams equipped with personal protection equipment, safe excreta transportation system (trash pump and donkey cart with tank) and a final disposal site designed so as to avoid contamination of water points. The FSM team also will serve as mobile sanitation team in case of AWD/Cholera outbreak in the camps and will be trained on AWD/Cholera preparedness.
Due to recurring floods SOYDA will make use of early warning systems to provide early warning messages in case of flood risk and to also create effective response. SOYDA proposed WASH project would develop synergies with other ongoing health, protection and nutrition projects targeting the same areas in order to maximize the impacts. SOYDA will attend all coordination WASH meetings at all levels as well as have close coordination and collaboration to line ministries of Federal government and state authorities.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Emergency and Sustainable WASH Support to Crisis affected IDPs and host communities in Puntland, Hirshabelle and Southwest states of Somalia
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to provide emergency and sustainable WASH services to the crisis affected IDPs and host communities in Puntland, Hirshabelle and Southwest states of Somalia. The target population of the project is 40,000 crisis affected community who have not safe WASH services. At the inception of the project, AADSOM will hold a workshop to the prominent community stakeholders including women, disabilities and IDPs to familiarize them the modalities/objective and roles such as project objectives, implementation strategies, scope, feedback and complaint mechanisms, beneficiary selection criteria, beneficiary entitlement and roles. Side meetings with girls, boys, men and women will also be convened to ensure their different needs are addressed. AADSOM will present the project documents to cluster members to avoid overlaps, following the cluster discussions. The project will reduce people’s needs, risks and vulnerabilities and increase in their resilience, to be achieved over a period of 3-5 years. They are designed to strengthen coherence and complementarity between humanitarian and development efforts, and ultimately aim to reduce needs and vulnerabilities to a point where humanitarian action is no longer required. In this project, 

Water:
AADSOM will provide lifesaving safe water trucking to 1,000 IDP households in Bari, Hiran and Bakool regions, benefiting 9,000 men, women, girls and boys who have no access to safe water for a period of three months. As an exit strategy, the project will rehabilitate 3 boreholes, 6 berkeds and 20 shallow wells. In order to keep the sustainability of the water source and increase the ownership of the rehabilitated water sources, AADSOM will conduct series training to 29 WASH committees and 46 well operators. As cross cutting, AADSOM will conduct community training on DRR and conflict resolution mechanisms. AADSOM will conduct continuous water treatment, chlorination and routine water quality testing to reduce the AWD/cholera diseases

Sanitation and hygiene:
AADSOM will also construct 200 gender sensitive and flood proof IDP latrines, and 6 twin block latrines complete with hand washing basins in 3 schools and 3 health facilities with equal access of men, women, boys and girls.  In order to reduce the risk of GBV against women/girls and discourage open defecation. 
AADSOM will carry out hygiene promotion campaigns participating women, men, boys and girls and is planned to reach 40,000 people. The HP awareness campaigns will carry out by 300 CHPs who are trained through this project. Finally, to encourage men, women and children to wash their hands with soap during the use of latrines and to fetch and store the water safely, AADSOM will distribute 1,500 HP kits to 1,500 IDP HHs who are at risk of AWD and/or HHs with malnourished children and pregnant & lactating women. During the project implementation, AADSOM will encourage women to take part in the decision making of the community decisions. AADSOM will make continuous monitoring during the project implementation and will hand over the rehabilitated WASH services to the community leaders with the presence of the local authorities. The project is complementarity with the existing AADSOM food security and WASH projects in the target locations.

project_name: Strengthening emergency care and trauma in the oPt
project_objective: The WHO trauma and emergency care programme is an extensive series of interventions that aim to improve the management of traumatic injuries, from the post of injury, at the prehospital level all the way to hospital care, including emergency departments and surgery, to rehabilitation and recovery. By investing systematically in the health system, this approach aims to strengthen the system by building in resilience to be able to deal with future shocks and disasters as well. The broader set of interventions involve an array of humanitarian development nexus activities, but in this proposal, only the humanitarian elements have been presented. For 2020 HRP, WHO aims to (1) strengthen prehospital care by upgrading the centralised ambulance dispatch centres and cadre of paramedics to allow for a timely response to all acute cases in the opt through training of over 250 paramedics from PRCS and MoH (2) continue to provide some support to the 10 trauma stabilisation points through simulation exercises and small scale provision of supplies (top up supplies) in Gaza (3) Enhance the level of care at six key emergency departments in Gaza and up to four emergency departments in the West Bank through clinical, practical and theoretical coaching on mass casualty management (4) provide essential training to surgeons on acute surgery, with a particular attention to damage control surgery (5) provide essential services for specialised services such as limb reconstruction in Gaza; to be able to treat approximately 500 complex limb reconstruction patients per year (6) continue coordination efforts in the trauma working group in Gaza providing support to over 20 agencies. Finally, the project will also aim to enhance the level of preapredness in case of mass casualty events through prepositioning essential life saving supplies at the prehospital and hospital level.

project_name: Supporting Life-Saving Health Interventions in Gaza
project_objective:
The Health and Nutrition Cluster partners estimated that 1.3 million people are in need of humanitarian health interventions across the oPt, of whom two out of every three are in Gaza (HNO 2020). The partners identified that within Gaza, the population requires humanitarian interventions for reproductive, maternal, neonatal and child health services including nutrition, treatment for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including mental health and psychosocial support. Meanwhile, the health system is struggling to cope with the ongoing influx of conflict-related trauma casualties each week, as part of the Gaza Mass Demonstration. However, infrastructure, human resources, and the referral system remain only partially functional after 12 years of blockade, inadequate to cope with the growing needs. 
The project aims to ensure access to essential life-saving health services of the most vulnerable affected population in Gaza through provision of essential drugs and medical supplies and implementation of early essential newborn care. A total of 188,000 men and women, including 5,000 newborns and their 5,000 mothers in the Gaza Strip will be targeted by the provision of life-saving medicines and access to interventions in emergency departments and maternities. Additionally, the WHO will initiate a robust supply monitoring and emergency storage management to inform humanitarian decisions and ensure better monitoring of donated supplies.

project_name: Emergency assistance & building resilience for the most vulnerable drought-affected households in Zinder
project_objective: Plus de 70% de la population de la région de Zinder dépendent des ressources agro-pastorales pour leur subsistance. Aujourd’hui ces ressources sont confrontées à une multitude de facteurs : sécheresse, inondations, changements climatiques qui bouleversent le calendrier agricole, engendrant ainsi l'insécurité alimentaire dans la région. Les résultats de projet pilote CISRI (climate information services research initiative) mis en œuvre par Mercy Corps en 2018 dans la région de Zinder ont révélé un certain nombre de défis dont le manque d’une meilleure connaissance des informations climatiques et leur importance dans la prise de décision et la planification des activités agricoles. D’autres contraintes sont le manque d’intrants (semences, engrais, etc.), dégradation des terres, insuffisance de l’appui en termes de formation, manque d’accès à l’information climatique limitant le développement économique dans la région.  Selon les prévisions de la météorologie nationale de juin 2019, des cumuls pluviométriques étaient déficitaires dans la région de Zinder se traduisant par des déficits de productions et hausse des prix des denrées alimentaires. Les résultats préliminaires du Cadre Harmonisé (CH) de novembre 2019, indique que la région de Zinder est l'une des zones les plus touchées par l’insécurité alimentaire avec les départements de Tanout et Goure qui font des zones les plus touchées. La situation projetée de la période de Soudure 2020 (Juin-Aout) dans les deux départements indique qu’ils seront en phase crise. Avant que les ménages ne commencent à adopter des stratégies d'adaptation négatives, la vente des actifs productifs, il est urgent de prendre des mesures pour assister ces ménages. Le projet vise à i) fournir une aide d’urgence et une aide au relèvement rapide aux ménages touchés par la sécheresses les départements de Goure et Tanout afin de réduire la vulnérabilité des populations et améliorer la sécurité alimentaire, ainsi que leur capacité à supporter les périodes difficile, ii) renforcer la résilience des ménages à se préparer et à agir sur les risques climatiques. Le projet ciblera 2000 ménages vulnérables (ciblés à travers la méthodologie HEA) dans les départements de Goure et Tanout (région de Zinder).

project_name: Emergency water, sanitation, and hygiene intervention to most vulnerable and conflict affected IDPs and Host Communities, Yirol East, Lake State
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to help improve access to safe and clean drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene of targeted IDP and host individuals, households, population/communities affected by impacts protracted and complex crisis in Yirol East, lake state, South Sudan. The affected population includes Internally Displaced Peoples (IDPs), and most vulnerable host communities’ households and individuals including not limited to poor female headed households, households with persons living with disability, those with low income, and the most food insecure households suffered with malnutrition cases particularly Pregnant and Lactating Mothers and under five children. 
Women, men, boys, girls, and Children, are at the center of this project. Targeting will be based on humanitarian principles of humanity and impartiality to save lives and alleviate suffering. And, aid will be provided based on need alone. For this, efforts will be made to deliver assistances in proportion to identified needs. 
To achieve this, CAFOD protection and safeguarding framework will be used which considers safety, meaningful access, dignity, and inclusivity. A participatory and consultative approach will be used to agree on targeting criteria in the way it can ensures most vulnerable individuals/households are identified and benefited from this support. This will be implemented by building on past targeting methodology which has been used in previous CAFOD response and recovery interventions. To realize the inclusion of persons with disability, the project will make, at least, 10 percent of the beneficiaries’ households will be targeted according to membership of person living with disabilities. 

The project planned will allow CAFOD to provide immediate lifesaving assistance as per the needs and this will be delivered through repair and rehabilitation of critical broken boreholes, house-to-house hygiene promotion through project volunteers, training of water users committees to aid sustainability of access to safe drinking water and refresher training for handpump mechanics which will be conducted by CAFOD humanitarian staffs. To support girl-child education, the project will provide sanitary kits for adolescence girls in primary school to curb menstrual hygiene-related absenteeism from school and mediocre performance. The project will also train women, girls and boys on the making of re-usable menstrual pads (RUMPS). This will be a source of income generation for the concerned individuals.
Children being social agents for change, the project would establish and train school hygiene clubs to pass on good hygiene practices to their peer in school and eventually to the entire community. The main messages would revolve around personal, food, environmental hygiene, safe water chain and safe disposal of solid and human waste amongst others. Mass hygiene campaigns in public places such markets, health facilities, village centers and schools would also be conducted to enlighten the communities on environmental and public hygiene. At the same time, the project will engage strategically to address the drivers of vulnerabilities and underlying structural issues across the targeted state. Besides, the project will collaborate and complement with other stakeholders implementing in the area to address WASH in Nutrition, WASH for GBV mitigation and WASH for IDPs and vulnerable host communities.

project_name: Project Title: Emergency Food Security and Livelihood support project to most vulnerable and conflict affected IDPs and Host Communities, Yirol East, Lake State
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to reduce food insecurity of targeted 6,100 household (36,600) people IDPs and host communities affected by impacts of complex crisis including effects of the recent civil war, ethnic conflicts over resources, worsening economic situation across the country, poor farming skills, loss of productive assets during the conflict, climate variability induced droughts and flooding and in Yirol East of Lakes State, in South Sudan. The project seeks to re-establish the self-reliance capacity of communities in own food production systems by improving the agricultural productive capacity of farmers who hitherto were able to produce their own food before the upheavals caused the recent crises referred to above.
This will be achieved through improving farming skills of household farmers who will be organized into farmer support groups. The farmers will be trained in various areas including promoting sustainable agricultural practices, climate resilient agricultural practices, farmer extension services and promotion of kitchen gardens. 
During lean hunger periods from July to August the project will support distressed households with immediate life saving assistance through voucher and cash based interventions. 
 
The project will benefit 6,100 households (36,600 people) who are Internally Displaced Peoples (IDPs) who will constitute about 75% of the beneficiaries and vulnerable host communities’ households. Targeting will be based on humanitarian principles of humanity and impartiality to save lives and alleviate suffering. A participatory and consultative approach will be used to agree on targeting criteria that ensures the most vulnerable individuals/households are identified and benefited from this support. The selection criteria based on CTP’s SADI (Safety, Access, Dignity and Inclusivity) Framework will be used to ensure inclusion of groups such as poor female headed households, households with malnourished children, Pregnant and Lactating Mothers, households with persons living with disability, those with low income, and the most food insecure households. To realize the inclusion of persons with disability, the project will make, at least, 10 percent of the beneficiaries’ households will be targeted according to membership of person living with disabilities.
The project will collaborate and work with other agencies to achieve synergy. It will collaborate with WFP or its partners such as CRS involved in food distributions in the area. The project will work closely with the agricultural ministry whose staff together with CTP and partner staff will play a key role in farmer training and extension services. The project will also collaborate with health and nutrition actors to target and support households with malnutrition cases with vegetable gardening.

project_name: Integrated WASH response to returnees, IDPs and host communities in Unity State (Panyijar, Rubkona and Koch) and of Western Equatoria State (Mundri West and East) South Sudan
project_objective:
The proposed project aims reduce WASH related suffering (including morbidity, mortality, and insecurity), to integrate WASH and Nutrition to prevent malnutrition, WASH and Gender Based Violence (GBV) to mitigate risks associated with GBV of conflict affected community through timely, sustainable and equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services including distribution of WASH NFIs and Menstrual hygiene management for IDPs, host communities and returnees. The proposed project is inline with objectives as there are outlined by the WASH Cluster for South Sudan 2020. This project will be targeting about 130,000 individuals in Unity (100,000) and Mundri West and East (30,000). 
The main components of the program will be: 
Timely provision of adequate safe and equitable water supply to households, community, health, nutrition and protection structures through ensuring access to water infrastructures that include rehabilitation of broken/damaged boreholes, regular water quality monitoring and capacity building  pump mechanics and water management committees.
Provision of dignified sanitation infrastructure using community participation strategy to host communities and returnees and construction of semi-permanent structures for IDPs with tailored designs for people with disabilities/older adults and children. 
Extended, all-inclusive hygiene promotion with a focus on behavioral change interventions and menstrual hygiene and NFIs distributions that address acute basic needs and facilitate individual ownership of personal and community health and well-being.
Health, nutrition, food security, and WASH integration to mitigate malnutrition, gender based risks, WASH-related illness and morbidity through referral systems and integrated outbreak response planning. Coordination with Health, Nutrition and Protection clusters to ensure an integrated timely response to any need. Mainstreaming of Menstrual Hygiene Management among school going children with an aim to increase school enrolment among girls.

project_name: Protecting Vulnerable Populations in Bentiu, Malakal, Juba and Maban from Epidemic-Prone Vector-Borne Diseases
project_objective:
The proposed programme aims to provide protection from malaria and other vector-borne diseases (VBDs) to the highly vulnerable Internally Displaced People (IDPs) population in Bentiu PoC (Rubkona), Malakal PoC (Unity) and Juba PoC (Central Equatoria) as well as the host community in Maban. To achieve this, The MENTOR Initiative will focus on preventing diseases-transmitting vectors from multiplying and entering the VBD transmission cycle, which causes a great deal of morbidity and mortality. Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS), larviciding and fly control measures will be employed as tools to disrupt disease transmission. In addition, MENTOR will adopt an integrated approach and the camp inhabitants will not only be educated on the diseases itself and how to prevent infection, but also on the impact of water and sanitation on disease transmission as well as (mal-) nutrition and associated disease severity. This will be achieved through delivering targeted IEC/BCC campaign and health education sessions. Lastly, health facilities in the camp as well as those serving the nearby host community will be supported by offering comprehensive trainings on malaria and other VBDs differential diagnosis and case management for nursing and medical staff to improve the quality of health service delivery. The MoH and PSI plan to conduct a mass distribution of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) in 2020, and MENTOR proposes to support the campaign through IEC/BCC in the target locations.

MENTOR is an HRP member and the mentioned activities were planned and implemented in SSHF Allocation Round 1 and 2 in Bentiu PoC in 2019, with significant results achieved.

To align with the 2020 Health Cluster targets, MENTOR plan to reach 25,000 people in the targeted areas. However, the proposed activities are community-based, and based on previous programmes and experiences, we estimate that up to 282,611 people could directly benefit from them.

project_name: Integrated Humanitarian Health, Nutrition and WASH Assistance to Conflict Affected and Vulnerable Populations of West, Central and South Darfur, Blue Nile and South Kordofan states
project_objective:
IMC will implement its integrated programme in five states, West, Central and South Darfur, South Kordofan and the Blue Nile covering around  1,947,257 people. The proposed intervention will address gaps in the provision of primary health care and nutrition services. Under the health intervention, International Medical Corps will be providing basic PHC and nutrition services, including outpatient consultations, reproductive health services (antenatal care, delivery service, post-natal care, and family planning), and immunization through 89 health care facilities across the targeted 5 states. In addition to facility care, community-based health interventions including; health and hygiene education, referral of cases, and campaigns will also be provided. In collaboration with SMOH, WHO, and HAC, IMC will respond to seasonal outbreaks such as AWD, measles, and malaria in all targeted areas. Health facilities will be prepared with necessary human resources and equipment (including laboratory equipment and materials) to enable them to respond to outbreaks and related emergencies. IMC will be implementing community-based interventions such as the promotion of child and maternal health, health education, community mobilization for EPI, mass MUAC screening and other activities through local partners.
Under the nutrition intervention, IMC will support SCs, OTPS, and TSFPs, IMC (in conjunction with the Ministry of Health) will provide nutrition services to the most vulnerable groups- children under 5 and PLWs- among the IDPs, returnees and host population and refugees in the targeted localities. The active and passive screening will be done to determine the children that should be enrolled for treatment. Treatment will be provided based on the national guidelines for the management of acute malnutrition (MAM). Children 6-59 months found to have SAM without complications will be treated in the OTPs and those with medical complications or children below 6 months will be transferred to SC where they will receive medical and therapeutic nutrition.
To promote optimal IYCF practices, including exclusive breastfeeding, timely complementary feeding, and dietary diversity, individual counseling and group sessions for caretakers of children 0 to 23 months will be provided. Nutrition, health and hygiene education will also be provided for caregivers of all children admitted in the CMAM program, women attending antenatal and post-natal services, and when immunization services are provided. Key messages will be on recommended feeding and child care practices, improving dietary diversity using locally available foods, and improved water, sanitation, and hygiene practices. Community outreach activities will result in improved timely access to treatment, program coverage, and community engagement and contribute to the prevention of malnutrition. 

The health facilities will be made fully functional by the rehabilitation of the structure, provision of drugs, nutritional supplies, medical equipment and capacity building of State Ministry of Health (SMoH) staff on the provision of nutrition-specific and health care services. The aim is to facilitate access to quality health and nutrition services for all, with a focus on the most vulnerable groups. 
The WASH intervention will be done at the health facility and community level to ensure adequate access to safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene in an integrated and comprehensive approach, whilst providing preventative measures to mitigate the risk of other potential outbreaks i.e. cholera, Chikungunya, Malaria, and Dengue. Hence, the focus of WaSH intervention will be the health facilities supported through IMC for health and nutrition interventions. WaSH in health facilities will be including the provision of a sufficient amount of safe water, provision of gender-segregated latrines, medical waste management facilities, and hygiene promotion.

project_name: Sudan Multi-Sector Emergency and Recovery Assistance Program
project_objective:
The proposed intervention builds off of existing RI activities and targets  45,659 vulnerable communities (29,318 IDPs and 16,341 host communities) within North Darfur State (localities: El Fasher, El Kuma, El Malha, El Taweisha, Kebkabiya, Mellit, and Saraf Omra) and Blue Nile State (localities: Bau and Geissan) to reduce morbidity and mortality rates through direct service provision of emergency services and providing capacity building trainings across sectors and provision of sustainable infrastructure to build resilience. RI proposes integrated programming covering Health, Nutrition, WASH, FSL, and Education. 
The interventions will support all three Strategic Objectives. SO1 Emergency Life-saving Assistance will be supported through free services within PHCCs/BHUs and an Emergency/Rapid Response Mechanism under Health, and within SCs, OTPs, and TSFPs under Nutrition; associated capacity building of staff and infrastructure improvements will be made to implement services. SO2 Resilience Building will be supported through access to basic water and sanitation services with accompanying hygiene promotion under WASH emphasizing community management and sustainability; FSL activities integrate nutrition-sensitive kitchen gardening, livestock production training and CAHWs support, and multi-purpose cash assistance emphasizing supporting a HH's ability to build foundational skills and meet immediate HH needs; and increasing access to quality Education through classroom building, training materials dissemination, and training with an emphasis on girls' education to build the communities' human capital and long-term capacity. SO3 is addressed through protection mainstreaming across interventions.

project_name: PROJECT WITHDRAWN- Increased access to quality education and support services for  IDPs and host communities in Banadir and Galmudug states.
project_objective:
Due to the protracted crisis in Somalia, several generations have lost access to basic quality education and there is a clear correlation between the household level of education and enrolment of children in school. 39% of families where at least one person has a university degree report that all their children are enrolled in school, while only 29% of families with at least one person having a primary school education report the same, and only 11% in families where no one has completed any education (JMCNA) 2019, REACH. The proposed 12-month intervention will improve access to quality education, enhance child protection mechanisms and increase access to critical WASH inputs/ enhanced school learning environment in 30 schools for conflict-affected IDP’s and host community learners in Banadir, Galmudug States of Somalia Federal Government. The project will target 11,646 (Boys 5795 & Girls 5851) of school going age in the three regions. CISP will deliver a comprehensive Education in Emergencies (EiE) through inclusive education interventions with a special focus on children leaving with disabilities. This will project will make deliberate attempt to sensitize displace & non-displaced communities on the need to education all children through the lense of equal access to education for all children. Education specific activities will include the provision of education supplies, emergency take-away food rations for students to meet their food and energy needs, emergency teacher incentives to motivate teachers to stay in the schools, and sanitary kits for adolescent girls to encourage their regular attendance at school. Specific WASH activities will include increasing schools’ water storage capacity through the provision of PVC storage tanks, the construction and rehabilitation of latrines, and improving hygiene practices among children through recreational activities, CISP will train the hygiene promoters, psychosocial support (PSS), and child protection and safeguarding. Specific Protection activities will include the mapping and sharing of existing child protection service providers and their respective services to school administrators and communities, strengthening child protection systems in schools, including the recruitment and training of child protection focal persons at each school, and awareness raising and training of community education committees (CEC) on child protection. CISP will also continue to engage with Ministry of Education Culture and Higher Education (MoECHE)
CISP will provide training to CECs on their roles and responsibilities, food and water management, disaster risk reduction (DRR), civic skills, proposal development, and child protection in the respective schools. Further, the CECs will be trained on DRR to build their capacity and improve school preparedness against future disasters. Disability and gender-friendly latrines in the targeted schools will be rehabilitated or, where necessary, constructed to minimize disruptions in learning for girls and boys. CISP will coordinate a enrolment drives through MoE and with CECs and religious leaders to encourage school enrolment with an emphasis on children affected by displacement. CISP education department will utilize the existing synergies with CISP protection department to will assess the existing child protection mechanisms at the start of the project, and, as determined from the assessment results, targeted schools will develop appropriate action plans to address areas of concern. To measure the effectiveness of the child protections systems implemented and capture lessons learned, CISP will conduct an end line assessment. Through the CISP protection department engagement with CEC’s and the regional Gender Focal Points (GFP’s) of MoECHE, CISP will leverage the agency's apparatus and community assets to raise awareness among children on child protection and the established mechanisms which will serve to strengthen child protection in schools.

project_name: Treatment of acute malnutrition for pregnant and lactating women and people living with HIV/TB
project_objective: Emergencies typically exacerbate existing conditions that contribute to food and nutrition insecurity. The nutritional status of other vulnerable groups, beyond young children, can deteriorate rapidly in an emergency setting. Pregnant and lactating women (PLW) and people living with HIV (PLHIV) are disproportionately affected by emergencies. The response in Zimbabwe requires comprehensive support to restore food and nutrition security. While scaling up general food assistance is essential, it is equally critical to scale up WFP’s emergency nutrition response. The intervention will complement existing UNICEF-supported acute malnutrition treatment services that support children under-five. WFP's nutrition component will target malnourished PLW and PLHIV/TB with treatment support to promote recovery, reduce acute malnutrition rates and long-term consequences of malnutrition include increased risk for mortality. Targeting PLW is in line with the first 1,000 days, ensuring that the intergenerational cycle of malnutrition is broken.

project_name: COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Project for FDMN and Host Communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
""As of 29th of April, total confirmed cases of COVID-19 in Bangladesh is 7103 and out of them 163 died. Till Today, a total of 21 cases has been confirmed in Cox’s Bazar district and out of them, one patient has recovered (2 from Chokoria, 4 from Teknaf, 2 from Ukhia, 10 from Maheshkhali, 2 from Cox's Bazar town, and 1 from Bandarban district). In total 1031 test has been performed in Cox’s Bazar and at present the lab has the capacity of performing maximum 96 tests per day. The overcrowded and unhygienic conditions increase the potential for the rapid spread of disease and non-availability of basic measures to prevent the spread of the virus will result in a large-scale outbreak in the densely-packed refugee camps. Rohingya refugees in Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazilas who are currently residing in 34 overcrowded, makeshift camps are highly vulnerable to COVID-19. The nearby host community people, especially people living in lower income quartiles in these Upazilas are also vulnerable due to proximity and similar living conditions.
UNHCR indicates that there are more than 31,500 refugees age 60 or older who are at higher risk for severe illness. The refugee population relies on humanitarian assistance and the preparedness for a wide scale outbreak and continuation of lifesaving services is critical. The construction of isolation and treatment facilities for refugees and adjacent Bangladeshi communities has been highlighted as an urgent priority by the Inter-sector Coordination Group (ISCG). Large-scale outbreak of coronavirus in the densely-packed Rohingya refugee camps is highly likely and would lead to thousands of deaths. 
IRC is going to establish a 60-bed SARI Isolation and Treatment Center (ITC) as per WHO guidelines within the refugee camp, which will be accessible to both refugees and host communities. The location of the ITC will be camp 23 (Shamlapur). There will be separate beds for women and girls to maintain the privacy and the dignity. Focus will be given on the clients with any disabilities, and also for the vulnerable sex and age group. Any GBV related issues will be addressed by the protection case worker who will be visiting the ITC from the PHCC. Separate Community health volunteers (CHV) will be recruited for the SARI ITC and will be capacitated on Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), enabling real-time information to community members, overcoming negative perceptions, improving health seeking behavior and compliance with COVID-19 preventative and mitigation measures. 
The project will works with and supports boys, young men and adult men increase their understanding and involvement in promoting gender equality. It will addresses the needs of children, adolescents, youth and adults in all their diversity (gender, age, disability, ethnicity and other exclusion factors relevant to the project scope and context) during this COVID-19 crisis time. 
The project design is informed by community engagement, collection of feedback, and assessments. The IRC is currently operating one Women safe space (WFS) and one Primary Health Care Center (PHCC) which form the basis for community engagement. During this Covid Period as the community engagement activities are limited due to applied restriction from the GoB, the PHCC CHVs are conducting awareness session and Health Education activities inside the Health Facility. The community leaders (majhi), local camp authorities (CIC) and local administration (sub-district and district administration) are involved throughout the project. The IRC will develop a detailed M&E plan in line with the Logic Model and Performance Measurement Framework of this project. M&E data and information on beneficiaries will be disaggregated (by sex, age and disability and other exclusion factors).
Besides, IRC is also supporting the MoH led Ramu Isolation and Treatment Center by providing HR support (2 Medical Doctors, 4 Nurses, 3 Cleaners, and 2 Security Guards) for three months.

project_name: Respuesta a la Emergencia en Salud y Nutrición en Venezuela
project_objective:
El Estado Nutricional (EN) comprendido como un proceso garantiza en gran medida, que la persona pueda desarrollar su potencialidad de manera integral en las actividades cotidianas. El EN, tiene 3 determinantes condicionantes: la disponibilidad alimentaria, la ingesta saludable de alimentos y aprovechamiento biológico de nutrientes. EN es multifactorial y debe ser abordado con un enfoque intersectorial y integrando acciones de Salud, Nutrición y Protección.

La situación política, económica y social de Venezuela durante los últimos años, ha producido drásticos cambios en el perfil epidemiológico de la población, impactando de forma importante en la salud de las poblaciones y especialmente en ciertos grupos sociales por edad, género y discapacidad (ej: recién nacidos, primera infancia, mujeres embarazadas, adultos mayores, personas con discapacidad). Las intervenciones enlazadas integralmente en una respuesta en Salud, Protección y Nutrición deben trascender lo curativo asistencial y alcanzar dimensiones de protección ante las deficiencias nutricionales y la vigilancia integral nutricional junto con medidas de detección temprana y mejora nutricional de emergencia como en la prevención, promoción y atención sanitaria y nutricional adecuada en las mujeres embarazadas, lactantes, recién nacidos, niños/as menores de 5 años, adolescentes y adultos mayores.

La prevalencia de malnutrición por déficit en mujeres gestantes y lactantes y menores de 5 años debe ser atendida a través de atención nutricional directa, apostando a intervenciones de respuesta rápida que puedan sostenerse en el tiempo y cuyos efectos sean medibles. El proyecto de Médicos del Mundo VENEZUELA es una propuesta de intervención nutricional y sanitaria, desde el acompañamiento técnico de las comunidades organizadas y redes comunitarias conjuntamente con los servicios de salud pública. Permitiría la ejecución de acciones en las áreas de nutrición intrafamiliar, salud colectiva y protección. 
La propuesta contemplaría: diagnóstico, planificación, ejecución y evaluación, iniciando con la construcción de una Evaluación Nutricional Rápida con muestreo randomizado (Nutrition Rapid Assessment) para desarrollo una línea base en contexto a partir del levantamiento del diagnóstico de la situación alimentaria - nutricional colectiva y la identificación de las necesidades específicas de los grupos priorizados, a través del tamizaje nutricional. A partir de la línea base, se planificará y ejecutará un plan operativo de prevención, atención y tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda en menores de 15 años y el tratamiento con programas terapéuticos alimentarios de embarazadas anémicas y con bajo peso, enfatizando en la prevención de la parasitosis y la consejería nutricional a la familia y especialmente a cuidadores de menores de 2 años. Con el propósito de fortalecer las capacidades en el ámbito familiar, comunitario y micro-área local, se contempla la formación de redes comunitarias de salud nutricional, con enfoque de vigilancia epidemiológica y alerta temprana de riesgos nutricional en los grupos vulnerables.
1. Componente de Fortalecimiento de Red integrada e integral de Salud(RIIS) a partir de la
recuperación de capacidades de la ASIC con énfasis en servicios de atención sanitaria y consejería como en tamizaje nutricional en  mujeres embarazadas, mujeres lactantes y recién nacidos, niños/as menores de 5 años y adolescentes. 
2. Componente de Redes comunitarias de Emergencia nutricional y salud colectiva: asociadas a la formación de redes barriales para prevención riesgos nutricional, promoción y vigilancia comunitaria de riesgos nutricionales y promoción de salud-salud materna y derechos humanos. 
3- Componente de mesas locales de co-gestión y coordinación intersectorial entre actores sociales, comunitarios, de los servicios de salud pública y Médicos del Mundo para toma de decisiones basadas en evidencia científica-sanitaria y rendición de cuentas a cada fase del proyecto.

project_name: Ensuring safety, dignity, and access to Multi-Purpose Cash Interventions for conflict-affected individuals in the Mezam Division in North West, Cameroon
project_objective:
Cameroon’s South West (SW) and North West (NW) regions began to experience social instability and unrest following protests against the government’s treatment of the Anglophone population and the government’s response to this unrest in 2016. The resulting socio-political crisis gradually turned into insecurity and armed violence as early as October 2017, which has only escalated. Since 2018, civilians have had to endure heightened tensions and erupting conflict between the area’s separatist militias and the country’s national security forces. Since the SW/NW conflict began, over 500,000 people have been internally displaced, and more than 1.3 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance . The continuous offensive by Government forces against non-state armed groups (NSAGs) has also pushed almost 40,000 Cameroonians to seek refuge in Nigeria.  By the end of 2018, UN agencies had declared a Level 2 emergency owing to the worsening humanitarian situation in the SW and NW. 
In a context of insecurity, the protection of civilians is particularly at risk. Between January and July 2019, protection actors identified and reported over 3,700 protection incidents through protection monitoring and assessments conducted in two thirds (seven) of the NW/SW divisions. Among these incidents 2,300 were recorded in the SW and 1,400 in the NW. In both regions, Mezam, Fako, Meme, Lebialem and Manyu were the most affected divisions, with 84% of incidents; 55% of the victims were females and 13% were children. The most frequent incidents were violations of the right to property through house destruction, which constitutes about 50% of the incidents.

To respect the Do-No-Harm principles and to achieve the objective stated above the proposed project will partner with and work within the framework of the WFP’s Multi-Purpose Cash assistance activities to provide a complementary protection component, which will be carried out through the following activities:

Activity 1. Conduct Do No Harm risk assessments and support  Protection Mainstreaming Action Plan implementation 
The IRC will undertake an initial protection risk assessment and do-no-harm assessment at the beginning of the project to identify main protection risks faced by people in their daily life and issues related to the cash assistance transfer cycle. After identifying risks faced by populations, IRC and WFP will develop an Action Plan proposing mitigation measures, to address risks and the barriers as well as ensure meaningful access to assistance. This assessment will also include the validation and/or review of WFP vulnerability targeting criteria with affected communities. 

Activity 2: Conduct protection mainstreaming training and ToTs for beneficiary sensitisation
To ensure implementation of a ‘Do-No-Harm’ (DNH) approach and protection mainstreaming plan, the IRC will develop training modules and conduct a joint training with WFP at the beginning of the project for relevant staff and local partner, on their own code of conduct, protection principles, and specific measures to ensure implementation of a DNH approach and specific measures for protection mainstreaming during project implementation (including protection-sensitive management of complaints and feedback mechanisms). The pre-test and post-tests are part of the training component. All participants to IRC training organized with partners will undergo these tests before and at the end of the training in order to verify that they have achieved the learning objectives. 

Activity 3: Supporting and reinforcing feedback mechanisms for clients and accountability mechanism
The IRC's protection staff and accountability and feedback mechanism staff will support the strengthening of WFP’s existing complaints and feedback mechanism (CFM).

The multipurpose cash component of the project is implemented by WFP.

project_name: Accès à l'éducation pour les enfants et jeunes déplacés, réfugiés et de la communauté hôte dans les régions de Maradi et de Tillabéri
project_objective:
A la suite des récents mouvements de populations à la frontière avec le Nigéria dans la région de Maradi et les mouvements dans la région de Tillabéri le long des frontières avec le Mali et le Burkina Faso, NRC souhaite apporter une réponse en éducation en situation d'urgence (communément appelée EiE) et aux structures de formation professionnelle. Cette réponse vise à améliorer l'accès à une éducation de qualité dans des espaces d'apprentissage sûrs et inclusifs pour les enfants et adolescents descolarisés/non scolarisés et ceux également impactés par la crise dans les zones identifiées. 
Pour cela, NRC souhaite élargir ses interventions auprès des écoles primaires et auprès des Centres de Formations aux Métiers (CFM).  
Ainsi, les activités en Education en Situation d'Urgence (EiE) viseront la mise en place d'espaces temporaires d'apprentissage à Maradi pour l'accueil de 3,500 enfants nouvellement descolarisés et l'appui des écoles à Tillabéri pour la réintégration de 1,200 enfants nouvellement descolarisés. La distribution de kits aux élèves/enseignants permettra d'insérer et d'assurer la rétention des élèves déplacés/réfugiés/de la communauté hôte dans les espaces d'apprentissage ciblés par NRC. La qualité de l'éducation sera adressée à travers la formation des enseignants et la réhabilitation des écoles, y compris les équipements scolaires, latrines et points d'eau. Des classes de remédiation seront organisées pour les enfants réfugiés et vulnérables pour leur remise à niveau et pour leur (ré)intégration dans le système scolaire. La participation, sensibilisation et formation des communautés et parties prenantes de l'éducation permettra aux écoles et aux associations de parents d'élèves et autres membres de gestion de l'école d'assurer la continuité des activités mises en oeuvre par NRC. 

NRC vise également à accroître l'accès à une formation professionnelle de qualité et à l'accès au marché du travail pour 400 jeunes déscolarisés, vulnérables et déplacés à Tillabéri. Le but principal de l’intervention est de leur fournir des opportunités de formation professionnelle et de leur assurer une place dans la société à travers la réinsertion professionnelle. Cela se fera en soutenant l'accès, la qualité, et en soutenant l'accompagnement des jeunes jusqu'au développement d'une activité professionnelle.
Les principales activités liées à la formation professionnelle seront les suivantes: mise en place de sessions de formation pour les jeunes, distribution de fournitures aux centres de formation, distribution de kits d'apprentissage aux jeunes, distribution de start-up kits, alphabétisation et formation des jeunes aux compétences de vie, accompagnement des jeunes à l'acquisition d'un stage et mentorat (orientation professionnelle) pour soutenir la création d’entreprises et l’employabilité.

L'assistance aussi bien aux structures de formation ainsi qu'aux apprenants  a pour objectif de permettre la poursuite de l'apprentissage  et également d'engager les enfants/jeunes à jouer un rôle actif dans la société tout en contribuant à la résilience de leurs communautés.

project_name: Lifesaving preparedness and response to infectious disease outbreaks of Cholera and Malaria in the most affected/at-risk health districts of Burundi
project_objective:
Burundi is estimated to have an annual cholera incidence rate of 4 per 1000, experiencing 19,943 cases with 758 deaths (Case Fatality Rate 3.8%) annually and around 4.9 million people living in areas at risk of cholera (Ali et al, 2015). Outbreaks have occurred every year since 1978, with the worst outbreaks reported in 2011 and 2013. The outbreaks recorded in 2017/2018/2019 have been primarily reported in the provinces of Cibitoke, Bubanza, Rumonge, Bujumbura and Makamba.
Burundi recorded the first case of cholera in 1978. Since then and every year, it has been reported resurgences of cases in the provinces along the Lake Tanganyika (also called the Imbo plain). As of July 2019, Burundi has already declared two cholera outbreaks with the latest still on-going and occurring during the dry season. This outbreak is a critical concern since it is not contained yet and new hotspots are still being identified.
The main objective of the project is to prevent and respond to outbreaks of infectious diseases through the provision of health and WASH services complemented with activities related to risk communication and community engagement through hygiene promotion. It proposes to build community resilience and address these issues through a coordinated and holistic response to affected communities including health facilities and schools.

Soutenir la prévention et la réponse immédiate aux cas et risques des violences, abus et exploitation contre les enfants affectés par les situations humanitaires aux Burundi
project_objective:
Une des résultantes des crises que traverse le Burundi depuis plusieurs années, en particulier celle de 2015 est la détérioration du tissu économique et social dont les séquelles restent perceptibles sur le bien-être des enfants et des femmes à travers le pays. Les situations humanitaires telles que les catastrophes naturelles et la pandémie du COVID-19 renforce la pression sur les populations les plus vulnérables. 
Les effectifs des enfants hors de l’environnement scolaire y compris les adolescents sont de plus en plus élevés et l’insuffisance des alternatives et opportunités de réinsertion poussent un nombre de plus en plus croissant dans la rue et dans d’autres activités dangereuses y compris le travail domestique ou l’implication dans des réseaux de prostitution et de traite d’êtres humains. 
Depuis 2017, le Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies aux Réfugiés (HCR) a soutenu le retour volontaire de 92 170 (fin aout 2020) personnes dont environ 56% ont moins de 18 ans. Leur réintégration au sein de leurs communautés respectives et l’accès des plus vulnérables aux services de base reste un des défis majeurs de la réponse humanitaire au Burundi. Selon l’analyse des besoins humanitaire faite par le secteur de la Protection, près de 244 623 enfants seront affectés ou susceptibles d’être affectés par des violences physiques et/ou morales, la négligence, la maltraitance, les abus et auront besoin d’être soutenu. L’une des causes majeures qui limitent l’accès de ces enfants aux services de base et à la protection est le manque d’extrait d’acte de naissance.
Les partenaires et structures communautaires de protection seront soutenus sur le plan technique, financier et logistique pour renforcer les aspects de sensibilisation au niveau communautaires y compris pour la prévention et réponse au COVID-19 (prévention des séparations familiales, appui psychosocial pour les enfants renforcés, lutte contre le stigma, etc) et renforcer le suivi de la situation des enfants y compris les rapatriés et retournés volontaires et renforcer l'environnement protecteur et la résilience des ménages face aux chocs humanitaires.  

Bénéficiaires du projet :
Le projet prévoit d'atteindre au moins 130,000 enfants dont 68% viennent de la population hôte, 25 % sont des enfants rapatriés, 5% de PDI et 2% toute autre catégorie qui auront accès aux services urgents et critiques de protection y compris en réponse au COVID-19 ; et 20.000 adultes.
-      Appui à l'opérationnalité de la Ligne 116 pour renforcer l'accès aux services de protection d'urgence des enfants affectés par les situations humanitaires et autres enfants 
-      Appui aux équipes mobiles de psychologues pour l'appui psychosocial y compris en réponse au COVID-19 
-      Appui au renforcement de l'environnement protecteur dans les écoles et à la provision d'appui psychosocial par les enseignants et acteurs communautaires de protection de l'enfance
-	L’identification, la recherche familiale et la réunification des ENAs/ ES ou l’organisation de leur prise en charge alternative d’urgence
-	L’accès aux activités récréatives et la provision de soutien psychosociale aux enfants présentant des signes de détresses psychologique y compris les victimes et témoins des violations des droits de l’enfant y compris les enfants survivants des VBG
-	L’appui légale aux enfants victimes d’arrestation arbitraire 
-	L’accès aux extraits d’acte de naissances pour les enfants non enregistrés à la naissance y compris les enfants rapatriés.
L’intervention comprends aussi le renforcement des capacités techniques et opérationnelles des acteurs de protection et de structures communautaires de protection (Comité de Protection de l'enfant/ CPE et Groupe de Solidarité /GS) qui prennent de plus en plus de responsabilités dans la réponse aux besoins des enfants affectés par les situations humanitaires.

project_name: WASH support for the needy families in Northern Syria
project_objective: Through the proposed project, IR Syria aims to support those who are in need for wash assistance. 88,000 people will beneﬁt from improved access to water and sanitation facilities. The project is primarily designed based on Humanitarian Need overview 2019. The project will support the formal and informal settlements as well as well host communities with core WASH services. The activities included in this proposal are in line with the WASH cluster objective which is support to water, sanitation and sewage systems to ensure continuous services for affected people in Syria and deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services to most vulnerable people. IRW prioritizes WASH support interventions for the conﬂict affected population in the target location to enhance beneﬁciaries’ resilience in coping with ongoing crisis through the provision of access to clean water as well as supporting them in cleaning the wash facilities in a clean and healthy environment. Below will be the intended activities to achieve the project objectives: 1. Adequate quality and quantity of water: Water supply will ensure through water trucking. IR will sign an agreement with a contractor to supply water to the targeted camps on daily basis (23 L per person will be provided on daily basis). This water will be suﬃcient to cover the drinking, bathing and household need of the individuals. If required by the targeted families, IR will also distribute Jerry cans. This will be contributed by IR.  2. Water testing and treatment (chlorination): IR team will conduct water testing and chlorination before it is available for use by the beneﬁciaries. This will help to eliminate the risk of using contaminated water. 3. project_objective:

Also IR will ensure to have a robust complaint and feedback mechanism.

project_objective:

down from 14% of post Gu 2018 and 17.4% of post Gu 2017. The corresponding median
SAM prevalence are: 2.3% (Gu 2019), 2.2% (Gu 2018) and 3.2% (Gu 2017). The FSNAU report indicated a critical GAM (18.3%) and serious SAM (2.8%) prevalence were recorded in Gedo region while health services in Elwak and Garbaharey districts are facing stock out of emergency medical supplies.The proposed project will be implemented in Gedo region particular Elwak and Garbaharey districts where ARD is implementing health and WASH. ARD will provide free outpatient consultations to 30,000 drought/AWD affected communities including 9000 girls, 9000 boys, 7500 women and 4500 men. Provision of emergency obstetric care including ANC, skilled delivery and PNC to 3000 eligible women and improve referral system through provision of transportation. The organization will conduct routine and supplementary immunization services to 20% of target population approximately  6000 children under the age of five years. In addition, the capacity of 35 staff will be improved through training while 350 community members will also be increased their knowledge and skills on disaster risk reduction, AWD prevention, identification of cases and early referral to health facilities. The organization is active health cluster member in Gedo and Mogadishu and will actively share information with health cluster members. The project will also be integrated into ongoing WASH project as integrated package of intervention. The target district is accessible, and the organization has active PCA with UNFPA in reducing maternal mortality rate through skilled deliveries and strengthening referral system in Somalia. There are reporting system that links to the EWAR system within the national surveillance system.
