project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Provision of life saving emergency response to most vulnerable populations in emergency and referral setting by delivering free ambulance services
project_objective:
Somalia is suffering from a complex humanitarian emergency for over two decades of internal conflicts. The prolonged conflict destroyed most of the basic social services infrastructure including hospitals and healthcare facilities. This has led to the flight of doctors, nurses and other medical professionals and the Somalia National Government needs international support to renovate and restore necessary services (Landinfo, 2018).  Although the FSNAU post GU 2019 findings showed that marginal decrease in the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition(GAM of 13.8% down from 14% of Post GU 2018 and 17.4 post Gu 2017. However, over million children suffer from acute malnutrition of whom 178,000 children are projected to be affected with life threatening severe acute malnutrition across the country/ The report further cited the lack of life saving medical emergency services to the populace in Banadir region as well as poor and inadequate health referral system.
Aamin organization is currently implementing SHINE project under consortium led by ACF through support of DFID in Banadir region. Aamin Ambulance provides a twenty four hour, unparalleled free ambulance service in Mogadishu, Somalia. From July to September 2019, Aamin ambulance transported and facilitated 638 affected people (427 female, 211 male) within the ten districts covered by the SHINE project. This was a significant increase compared to last quarter by 284. The increase can be attributed to increased awareness of the availability of the free ambulance service in the ten districts. Therefore, Aamin ambulance seeks to bridge the gap of unreliable health and emergency response system through this free ambulance and first aid system to the people of Mogadishu. We take cognizance of the needs the vulnerable in the community and hence our project also plays focus on the needs of the vulnerable in the community including women and children. Through a recent needs assessment conducted by Aamin ambulance, it was established that over 2100 expectant mothers in our target districts are in need of maternal health services (including referrals) to ensure a safe pregnancy and delivery, including emergency obstetric services. The situation is even life threatening when the mothers are in need of these emergencies during the wee hours of the night. Our emergency project hence seeks scale up efforts in ensuring that no woman or new-born dies during birth by avoiding prolonged labour. Currently Aamin ambulance has 16 fully equipped ambulances staffed with qualified and well trained professionals to provide pre-hospital care to patients. The project currently operates in Mogadishu with a future plan to expand operations to three other states; Hirshabelle, Southwest, Galmudug and Jubbaland.  Through this project Aamin ambulance will targets 22,270 affected people with OPD consultation, treatment of common illness, incidences, and early referral (e.g. complicated deliveries/2100 pregnant women) for further treatment and care.   The target group will be disaggregated based on the monthly outcome. 
Aamin Ambulance will adopt mobile clinic strategy to reach out to vulnerable people in IDPs areas and bring service close to their community. The team will provide Out-patient services to the people at the convenience of their villages. The composition of the health expert that will be attending the mobile clinic will include Medical doctors, nurses and clinical officers. Aamin Ambulances target to reach out to 20,000 people through our mobile clinic OPD services with a composition of: 5,000 women, 6,000 girls, 6,000 boys and 3,000 men. Since Aamin will go further to the most remote area, we believe we will attain the set target and deliver high quality service the community has been yearning for. However, since the gap for health service is big, Aamin ambulance will bridge it by bringing service close to the people and providing free referral services for people in critical condition.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED-Strengthening provision of  emergency lifesaving Primary Health Care Services to IDP and host communities population in Banadir, Lower Shabelle, Bay and Bakool Regions
project_objective:
The availability of basic health services in health facilities are limited, a situation exacerbated by low governance and scarce resources. Many areas do not even have any access to health services. OCHA’s 2019 Humanitarian Need Overview reported Somalia has less than 40% of its target of two health facilities per 10,000 population and has only 19% of its target skilled health workforce. Furthermore, communities may not be aware of the availability of, and/or have confidence in the health services; and even if they do, they usually lack awareness to identify health danger signs and seek appropriate care in good time. Limited knowledge of appropriate health practices at household level also increases the health risks of preventable causes. OCHA estimated 2 out of 5 people are in need of urgent life-saving health service throughout 2019 (Nov 2018). Except for limited access to health care, the quality of services appeared poor.


Somalia is reported to have the world’s highest child mortality rate and faces the sixth highest lifetime maternal death risk in the world despite most of those are preventable (World Bank, 2017). One out of every 22 Somalia women is likely to die due to pregnancy or childbirth-related causes during her life course; the under 5 mortality rate (U5MR) of 137 per 1,000 live births is presently the third worst in the world. According to the OCHA 2019 Humanitarian Needs Overview – Somalia (Nov 2018), approximately 45% of death among children under five takes place in the neonatal period. Many diseases that contribute to high morbidity and mortality are vaccine preventable yet nearly 54% of health facilities do not provide an “expanded programme on immunization services”, driving coverage below 50% (OCHA, Nov 2018). DPT3 coverage is well under 50% in 2014. Measles-containing vaccine first dose coverage in recent year is estimated only at 46% across Somalia. 


Communicable diseases such as AWD/ cholera and measles continues to be a common and recurring health threat to Somalia. From January 2019 to August 2019, a cumulative total of 169 725 cases of AWD/ Cholera were reported from health facilities to the early warning, alerted network (EWARN). Also, a total of 3402 suspected measles cases were reported, of which 502 were during August 2019 in Banadir region. The need for health service provision will also become high in the coming months. REACH’s assessment established 84% of the interviewed households were reported having child or adult with specific health problem such as malaria, stomach pain, AWD and fever 30 days prior to the assessment; sadly, 27% of them reported limited capacity to access health facility to respond to the issue.


The principle of Do-No-Harm approach is used during the entire project cycle. Community (men, women and youth) will be involved and will be fully participate in all project cycle. HIJRA is planning to reach and and provide basic health care services to women (90168), Men (86632),  under five children (Girls 53199 and Boys 59113) and through the provision of primary health care services, strengthening of the referral system and increasing community awareness/collaboration by static health facilities and mobile clinic in target areas. HIJRA will coordinate other actors in the area to avoid overlapping and will also be used referral for cases so as to be complementary each other and to maximize impact.


HIJRA in collaboration with MoH plans to implement the project in Banadir, lower Shabelle and Bakool through already existing community health and community structures while leveraging of the already existing programs to ensure complementary and avoid the duplication of effort and resources. The project objective is increase access to emergency lifesaving primary services particularly IDPs and host communities with emphasis on disease prevention, treatment and health system strengthen in Banadir, Lower Shabelle, Bay and Bakool Regions.

project_name: Provision of basic nutrition services for management of acute malnutrition in Lower Shebelle and Bakool regions.
project_objective:
According to FSNAU, the humanitarian situation in Somalia is still critical as per September 2019.  Nearly up to 4.8 million are facing food insecurity while closely 2.1 million people across Somalia are expected to face food consumption gaps, high acute malnutrition, or depletion of assets indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes through December 2019. Moreover, current estimates indicate that 1 in 10 children under the age of five are acutely malnourished with the median National GAM of 13.8%, translating to 1.08 million children; of which 178,000 are affected by life threatening severely malnutrition while 830,000 are moderately malnourished. From FSNAU technical release, Pockets of GAM above the emergency threshold of 15% were reported in 10 out of the 33 areas surveyed in the 2019 assessment; with the majority (51.7%) of malnourished children cases concentrated in the six regions of Banadir (14.8%) Shabelle (11%), Bay (8.8 %), Hiraan (6.1%), Woqooyi Galbeed (5.6 %) and Gedo (5.4 %). These regions also realized below average rainfall and the expected food harvest is 68% lower than the long-term average since 1995.



Hudur and Bakool region, the GAM rate is 15.1% and a SAM rate is 3.8%, with the rural and urban people are approaching serious and critical GAM levels. In September FEWS NET technical release, it is indicated that 1,000 IDPs and 25,000 people from rural areas are in Emergency (IPC4) while 31,000 people are in Crisis (IPC3) in Food Insecurity.


Afgoye and Wanlwayn areas in Lower Shabelle, the GAM rate is 15.8% and SAM rate is 17.1%. While 36,000 people are in an Emergency level (IPC4) and 108,000 people are at a Crisis stage (IPC3). Failure of crop production and poor harvest with a protracted climate shocks in Lower shabelle resulted food insecurity and malnutrition. 

The efforts will be focused on maximizing benefits and avoiding harms for the most deprived and vulnerable groups including children and women within the targeted regions. The project will be aimed focus on the ''Do No Harm'' principle to protect the beneficiaries from exploitation at any given level. The project will implement activities aimed at obtaining full respect for the rights of all individuals in accordance with international law. There will be continuous sensitization both internally and externally on child protection to ensure that the rights of the children within the target communities are not violated at any given point. The proposed action will be implemented to promote meaningful access safety and dignity of the target populations to the project services.



People with disabilities often face exclusion, increased vulnerability and barriers in accessing their fundamental human rights. The project will ensure inclusion of people with disabilities, preventing stereo typing, discrimination and enhancing their access to the project intervention irrespective of the disabilities. HIJRA will make deliberate effort to ensure the project sites are closer to the community to enhance access to the services by the disabled and vulnerable population thus reducing walking distances and exposure to harm.



HIJRA Will scale basic nutrition services in priority to IDPs and their host communities and other socially marginalized groups in Hudur, Tayeeglow, Afgooye, Marka and wanlaweyn.Community (men and women and youth) will be involved and will be fully participate in all project cycle and decision making processes. HIJRA is planning to reach and treat acute malnutrition, a total 39131 children 6months to 59 months boys and girls, 12643 pregnant and lactating women as well as promoting IYCF practices to care givers through static OTP and mobile OTP in target areas.

project_name: Life-saving and Sustainable WASH services for conflict and natural disaster-affected communities of Northern Bahr-El-Ghazal (Aweil North, Aweil East, Aweil South Counties) and (Raga County in Western Bahr-El-Ghazal State).
project_objective:
The intervention is located in Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Western Bahr el Ghazal states. An estimated 5.2 million people urgently need WASH support services in 2020 and only 3 million people are targeted for humanitarian intervention support in the same year. The WASH cluster figures for women and girls in need of WASH related gender based violence are 2.5 million only 1.1 million are targeted in 2020 interventions.  This project is targeting to provide 33,500 people with timely, sustainable, equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDP’s, host communities and returnees.  16,851 women and girls are targeted for WASH related gender based violence. 
Years of conflict have increased the vulnerability of women and girls, with significant cases of Gender Based Violence. Some of these abuses occur when women and girls undertake domestic chores, such as fetching water or firewood. The needs are closely related to conflict (political conflict and inter-communal conflict) as well as natural shocks. These have contributed to internal displacements and economic downturn, which has affected the macroeconomic situation further straining the limited WASH services. In some cases WASH infrastructures have been deliberately targeted by armed actors during conflicts, further aggravating the WASH situation.  Many years of war in South Sudan have indirectly affected Northern Bahr el Ghazal, especially community resilience and coping mechanisms. The current economic crisis has also impacted negatively on the ability of the communities to sustain/maintain WASH services. The region has experienced flooding which resulted in displacement of people who have integrated with host communities, putting stress on the limited WASH services. The scattered settlement pattern in this region makes it difficult to mitigate the distance to the services e.g. access to water at sphere standard of 500m. Western Bahr El Ghazal (Raga County) has been severely affected by the war that has been going on. A lot of displacement has taken place in Raga, according to WASH Cluster 2019 severity analysis matrix, 5,907 people are IDPs, 601 are returnees while 7,586 are host the community. Raga is ranked among the most severely affected Counties in terms of access to safe water and faced with Gender Based Violence by the WASH Cluster.
The project targets the host communities, IDPs and Returnees. The total beneficiary figure is 33,500 people. The targeted recipients of this response are disaggregated as follows:  6,700 Women, 10,151 Girls, 6,599 Men and 10,050 Boys. The beneficiary figures are inclusive of the persons with disabilities in the communities. The intervention aims at increasing access to WASH services through drilling of boreholes, rehabilitation of non-functional hand pumps and solar powered Mini Water Yards. Hygiene and sanitation will be improved through formation and training of water management committees, CLTS triggering, sensitization and awareness campaigns in cross cutting issues like GBV, human rights, conflict mitigation and peace building.

project_name: Providing access to emergency food security and livelihoods support to vulnerable Agro-pastoralists households in Aweil North and Cueibet Counties in NBeG & Lakes States.
project_objective:
The proposed emergency food security and livelihoods support project is a dual sector project targeting Aweil North County of NBeG state and Cueibet County in Lakes state and will run for 12 months from January –December 2020.The main goal of the project will be to provide access to emergency food security and livelihoods support to vulnerable agro-pastoralists households by providing lifesaving emergency livelihood support kits. The proposed project will provide training to the vulnerable households to enhance fishing, crop and vegetable production mainly for consumption at the household level and sale of surplus at local markets in selected payams of Malual North, Jaac, Malual centre in Aweil North County and Abiriu, Mayath, Cuibet, Malou Pec payam in Cueibet County in Lakes state which will create extra income for these vulnerable households. These payams are chosen due to their suitability for fishing and vegetable production. SAADO will target 20,250 individuals in this proposed response with emergency fishing, crop and vegetable kits. The 2 locations have been chosen because of the needs prevalent in these counties according to the IPC August 2019 and the existence of active programming by SAADO in the areas. The emergency livelihood kits will be obtained from the FSL Cluster-recommended core pipeline to communities affected by the ongoing food crisis in NBeG and Lakesstates.
SAADO will put in place a mechanism for effective and participatory community vulnerability mapping in the selected payams and bomas and will use a comprehensive beneficiary selection criteria developed, discussed and agreed upon with the communities to include Men, Women, Boys and Girls. During community consultations at various levels, men, women boys and girls will be consulted to fully understand and appreciate the impact of the current crisis on men, women and children that would further inform response. “Do no harm” and AAP principles will be applied throughout the duration of the project, so that any possible negative implications of the project at community level are addressed before they occur through integrating a strong Communicating with Communities and Engagement (CCE) feedback mechanisms. The project will build upon and complement SAADO's long experience in implementing General food distribution(GFD) since 2014 and the 2.5 year DFID funded BRACE II projects in Aweil North County as well as the current 2nd standard allocation food security and livelihoods project supported by SSHF in Cueibet County in Lakes state. It will also complement the Lives Saving and livelihood protection and nutrition activities carried out by other FSL partners’ interventions in the counties especially WVI and PUI in Aweil North county and VSF-Germany in Cueibet County of Lakes state. The proposed activities are necessary and sufficient to achieve the stated cluster objectives for these interventions based on the relevance of each activity in increasing access to emergency food security and livelihoods support for the most vulnerable households in the targeted communities. The indicators selected are SMART and SAADO has in place a strong monitoring and evaluation system and mechanisms to measure these indicators and to ensure the intended results are achieved. The means of verification, such as monthly reports, distribution lists and regular field visits are strongly credible and are currently used by the organization in its MEAL processes across its field offices in the country.

project_name: Food Assistance for affected population by the Beirut Explosion
project_objective:
The explosions occurred as Lebanon was already coping with a multifaceted crisis of economic
contraction, increasing poverty rates and rising prices of basic commodities. The destruction of Beirut
Port and accompanying structures, such as animal and plant quarantine facilities, has had a direct effect
on the country’s food availability. Lebanon’s grain silos, holding up to 120,000 metric tonnes, were
destroyed. Lebanon depends heavily on imports, including food supply. Prior to the explosions, the
country imported 80 per cent of its wheat, most through Beirut Port. Estimates suggest that four to six
weeks of grain supply reserves remain. A three-month supply is standard to ensure food security.

Through this project IRW is planning to distribute more than 30,000 food parcels to more than 22,000 most affected HHs, also providing cash assistance through cash for work modality to more than 1,000 affected person/ families facing food insecurity.

project_name: Supporting the most vulnerable with in kind food assistance, multi purpose cash assistance, and ensuring economic resilience of MSMEs
project_objective:
Blanket distribution of hot meals in areas severely affected by the explosion, through local NGO partners with industrial or community kitchens and existing food safety standards; provision of provision of ready to eat packages for families without access to cooking facilities. Distribution of food parcels for affected and displaced families, including high vulnerability groups like FHH and the elderly, who are at high risk of COVID or have no access to markets. Parcels also include essential hygiene items including menstrual pads, and baby items. Targeting for hot meals and food parcels includes area-based coordination with the Food Security sector, priority for locations with known economic vulnerabilities and/or explosion-effected, and categorical targeting of households with children, female-headed, and other high risk groups. For food parcels, eligibility related to income poverty will also be calculated.
Multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) enables the most vulnerable families to meet their basic needs with dignity, and prepares them with financial stability and increased choices to access decent work. This activity is essential both in terms of economic stability while Lebanon continues to address COVID-19 pandemic and aftermath of the Beirut blast, and as a response to ongoing economic distress. Social assistance is a right for the most vulnerable, and for those with labor capacity it is also an essential stepping stone for families to pursue future livelihoods and decent work. For families directly affected by the explosion, a separate cash envelope will also be available as an immediate protection need, in line with sector guidance.
Finalizing a coordinated and joint assessment with 8 other international and national NGOs to assess the damage to MSMEs in areas most affected by the Beirut blast. This assessment will conclude in a report as well as determine eligibility of the MSME for a cash grant, the value harmonized with other livelihood agencies. Small to medium cash grants and in-kind rehabilitation to MSMEs to help restart their business that have been damaged by the explosion, addressing damage to structures, assets, restocking, and other immediate needs to reopen. Only viable businesses are eligible, meaning they must meet certain criteria related to customer base and cash flow, and have the capacity to recover within the current economic context. Priority will be given to MSMEs in productive sectors or those linked with provision of essential goods and services such as food and vegetables, or repair services such as carpentry, electricity, etc. Grants will be combined with business development services, including tailored coaching sessions on business risk resilience, to continue in Phase III.
Targeting mothers and children under two years, those that influence and support their decisions (men, fathers, grandmothers) with integrated approaches to address the many underlying causes of malnutrition so to increase access to safe and nutritious food, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection, and ensure that women are supported so to make the right decisions for their children and themselves. This will be achieved through partners and referrals, aligned with the Nutrition Sub Working Group members to improve the delivery of quality nutrition services, including Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. Providing support to mothers and caregivers to navigate difficult conditions in a humanitarian setting so they can feed and care for their youngest children safely, and we do this through different actions at the household, community, health system and national level. Establishing private and secure breastfeeding safe areas as needed, with trained IYCF staff to support mothers to initiate and continue recommended IYCF practices. Training volunteers and community workers to conduct support and education sessions for families with young children on IYCF topics.

project_name: Colombia - World Health Organization
Strengthening the resilience of communities to natural disasters in Bangladesh
project_objective:
Bangladesh is one of the most vulnerable countries worldwide to natural disasters. Two districts, Cox’s Bazaar (Teknaf) and Bandarban (Alikadam) are two of the most affected regions, suffering cyclically from cyclones, flooding and saline infiltration, and landslides, rodent attacks and earthquakes; all of which negatively impact of local population’s livelihood opportunities. The populations in these regions are mostly reliant on agriculture, livestock and daily labour as their main form of income, with limited additional means of income diversification. Additionally, there is a general lack of preparation in regard to natural hazards, at household, community and local authorities’ levels. Awareness on risks and mitigation measures is low, while early warning systems remain incomplete despite some means and efforts deployed from governmental and non-governmental actors. In Teknaf specifically, the considerable influx of Rohingya refugees fleeing Myanmar exacerbated existing vulnerabilities within the population, impacting the labor market and depleting local resources such as water and wood, creating a rise in social disaccord. Therefore, this project will be able to achieve the following objectives;
* To promote diversified and resilient livelihoods for marginalized farmers and livestock owners.
* To enhance the economic opportunities and livelihoods diversification of the most vulnerable HHs through disaster resilient IGA and market assessment.
* To strengthen individual, households and communities’ capacity to adapt and recover from natural disasters and stresses/shocks.

project_name: Emergency support through agriculture-based interventions for vulnerable communities in the West Bank affected by emergency crises.
project_objective:
The proposed intervention (approved 2019 HRP HPSE19-FSC-150062-1) will target the food security and livelihoods needs of the most vulnerable farming and herding communities affected by protection threats in Area C of the West Bank. The activities will contribute to their enhanced protection from forcible transfer by improving the main factors involved in food production (roads, water, livestock shelter) and agricultural inputs. By doing so, the proposed intervention will contribute to improving the food security of marginalized families living under the poverty line.
The project activities will beneﬁt all members of the household, including women and children, and will be carried out on two levels: at household level through the rehabilitation of animal shelters and the supply of agricultural inputs; and at community level by improving the access to water and the communities’ accessibility (road rehabilitation).
The proposed intervention will deal with the protection threats to the livelihoods of the targeted families. Fomenting a community participation approach in the assessment, design and implementation of the activities, all the community’s sub-groups will participate in different focus group discussions, technical assessments and in the implementation process. The communication with communities (CWCs) will mitigate potential security and protection risks and, ultimately, empower the beneﬁciaries at community, family and individual level.
As outlined, the proposed intervention ensures protection mainstreaming as it is guided by protection principles and considers safety and dignity; meaningful access; accountability to affected population (AAP) as well as participation and empowerment.

project_name: Child Protection for Child affected due to Beiurt Blast
project_objective:
The Beirut Blast had significant consequences on the most vulnerable Lebanese and non-Lebanese communities, already struggling to cope with existing challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the socio-economic crisis. Many individuals have little-to-no capacity to respond to the destruction of their homes, new medical needs, increased food insecurity or lost livelihoods. Initial reports indicate that mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) needs are acute among vulnerable groups impacted by the blast. Children are particularly at risk. Displacement, loss of family members and high levels of stress at home can have significant consequences on children. SCI is implementing highly integrated programmers (CP, education, shelter and FSL), ensuring appropriate convergence and addressing family needs a holistic way as possible leveraging SC’s multi-sectoral expertise. Psychological First Aid (PFA), psychosocial support (PSS) and continued case management are urgently needed. Mental Health and Psychosocial Support will be prioritized integrated across child protection, education, livelihoods and shelter interventions. SC will provide immediate Psychological First Aid to caregivers and children in Child Friendly Spaces temporarily established as a specific response to the Beirut blast. 
SC will continue to deliver MHPSS packages for both children and their parents/caregivers.  Activities will be focusing on alleviating all the psychosocial distress suffered during explosion, COIVD-19 pandemic and on-going economic crisis, through community-based interventions as well as focused care for those children and caregivers whose needs exceed the capacity of community-based responses. The promotion of emotional wellbeing, recovery of the sense of normalcy, and alleviating the stress caused by a number of crises, and psycho-education would be the main focus on these tailored interventions. Packages to also be tweaked to the different needs of girls and boys as they can both be disproportionally affected and hence have different needs, interests, priorities, vulnerabilities and risks.  Strengthening of community-based MHPSS response capacity, through PFA, Peer to peer PFA, Home-based MHPSS, Child and Youth Resilience package and Heart training.  
Expanding the range of MHPSS interventions on offer, with a specific focus on person-focused interventions, through the recruitment of mental health professionals (psychologists), as well as training, coaching and supervision of paraprofessionals including CPCM teams and partners 
Strengthening internal and external referral pathways and mechanisms including to specialized mental health services and paraprofessional counselling. 
The PSS sessions will allow facilitators to safely identify children and/or caregivers requiring more specialized mental health support who will be referred internally to specialized MHPSS i.e for group MHPSS sessions or for individual sessions that will be facilitated by a clinical psychology. Caregivers and children under case management will benefit from this specialized MHPSS sessions. In addition, to provision of comprehensive case management for children at risk including referrals to specialized services. Children who have suffered any form of neglect, exploitation or abuse are entitled to care and non-discriminatory access to services. This will include the following:  Provision of specialized case management, using components of Steps to Protect Common Approach, focusing on those most affected by the Beirut blast, the COVID19 pandemic and its secondary impacts, including vulnerable girls and boys who lost their parents and/or caregivers, experiencing domestic violence, GBV and at risk of child marriage, including adolescent girls and those who are already married/pregnant and working children. Referrals of children with disabilities and children who had new impairments resulting from the blast, to also be considered for them to access specialized services.

project_name: Cash-based interventions for the most vulnerable refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees and host communities in Libya to meet basic needs
project_objective:
UNHCR and its implementing partners propose to target - for cash assistance - refugees, asylum seekers, as well as the most vulnerable conflict-affected Libyan nationals (IDPs, returnees, and non-displaced) referred by central and local authorities and actors. Following the initial referrals, multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) will be provided to people that have been assessed against harmonized socio-economic-protection vulnerability criteria based on a household-level scorecard. These criteria (and/or their significance) will be tailored to different population groups and to identify the most vulnerable. The assessments will continue to help ensure that scarce resources are directed to those most in need, and not based on their status only.
In particular, UNHCR  and its implementing partners will provide MPCA through unrestricted multi-month cash grants to the aforementioned target populations in the form of gift- or pre-paid cards, and one-off (one-time) MPCA for the vulnerable recently displaced, shipwreck survivors and released from detention centers.
UNHCR implementing partners will identify eligible households and individuals using vulnerability scorecards, thresholds and cash transfer values endorsed by the Cash and Markets Working Group (CMWG). 
Through the proposed project UNHCR and its implementing partners will, therefore, mitigate the need of the most vulnerable conflict-affected persons of concern to resort to negative coping mechanisms, by helping them to address their basic needs through facilitated access to basic goods and services available in the market, empowering them and promoting the dignity of choice of its recipients, stimulating local markets, and reducing operational costs of assistance delivery (compared to in-kind modalities). 
Last but not least, by targeting the extremely vulnerable families, MPCA will play an essential role to bridge the potential time gap when transitioning from humanitarian assistance to social safety net inclusion, therefore reinforcing the complementary with the MoSA vulnerability model. The adoption of scoring models and the diversification in terms of the number of cash transfers will facilitate a more granular response that recognizes the varied socio-economic-protection needs of families who live below the poverty line across the different Mantikas in Libya. Finally, the MPCA response intends to maintain the capacity of responding to the socio-economic needs of households affected by sudden emergencies/crises and make provisions to provide as soon as possible after the event (based on access).

The proposed project is in line with the EIEWG education 2019 framework objectives 1 and 2 and the protection objective related to legal aid in West Bank. The project aims to provide protection of vulnerable children affected by conflict and other situations of violence, particularly those at risk of denied access to educational services and individual and mass forcible transfer in the West Bank. The project will target 61 most vulnerable Ministry of Education and Higher Education (MoEHE) schools supporting children access to a protective and enabling educational experience and will be four-fold: 1) provision of psycho-educational support through training of teachers on how to manage a classroom with children who have gone through stressful and traumatic events, how to better support under-achievers and training of counsellors to support students with chronic nightmares that severely affect their school functioning thought the NRC flagship ‘Better Learning Program’ (BLP); 2) provision of emergency school kits to support crisis-disaster risk reduction in tandem with capacity building; 3) delivery of legal information sessions through awareness raising of students, school staff and parents about legal rights and protection as well as response to incidents/violations through documentation, including response and referral mechanism to document interferences/impediments to the delivery of education in schools, and strengthen the legal response of the ‘Alert Mechanism’; and 4) advocacy pursuing enhanced protection from violations of the right to education.

project_name: WASH emergency preparedness and resiliency of new returnees, IDPs and hosts communities in Central and West Darfur
project_objective:
Overall Project Objective is to ensure timely emergency and sustainable WASH response to reduce mortality and morbidity and prevent disease to vulnerable, conflict or natural disaster affected communities of Central and West Darfur. 
In the current Darfur context characterized by a complex, protracted and forgotten crisis, TGH designed a WASH intervention through the lens of the emergency- development humanitarian nexus. The project therefore includes:
- Installation and running of Emergency Water System whenever necessary (conflict or disaster related population displacement)
-Rehabilitations aiming to facilitate the transition from emergency to more durable water supply services as well as to expand and improve access to protected water sources in returnee and IDP settlements where access to safe water is below the emergency standard of 7,5 L/p/d
- Community capacity building on water supply management and cost-recovery system in order to empower community stakeholders and ensure sustainability of the water points
- Prepositioning of EPR WASH buffer stocks to mitigate disaster risks (water systems, water treatment kits, latrines, etc.)
- Sensitization on Hygiene Promotion through HKPs in order to mitigate consequences of bad hygiene behavior 
- Distribution of WASH items to people with special needs and dignity kits for women and girls 

TGH will pay particular attention in including women in the water committees as they are mostly the ones fetching the water they have key inputs in that matter. TGH will also ensure that at least 50% of the trained HKPs are women in order to ensure women and girls are directly targeted by hygiene promotion events.  
This project will target  135,463 individuals in Central Darfur (Um Dukhun, Golo, Bindizi and Mukjar localities) and 72,577 individuals in West Darfur (Beida, Kreinik and Geneina localities).

Strengthening SGBV prevention & risk mitigation, and improving the quality of response to survivors
project_objective:
Purpose: 
The project aims at strengthening SBGV prevention and risk mitigation interventions, increasing the accessibility of integrated services, and improving the quality of SGBV response services to Rohingya refugees, minority Hindu refugees, and the affected host community populations in Cox’s Bazar district.  

Interventions & Target: 
The interventions focus on increasing meaningful participation and community engagement through sustainable, innovative and adapted approaches, while engaging with key government authorities, SGBV and non-SGBV actors in preventive, risk mitigation and response measures. 
•	Prevention will be strengthened through proven and adapted community activism methodologies (incl. SASA! Together), sensitization and awareness-raising on SGBV, as well as life-saving information on available services. The engagement of men and boys (as informed through meaningful consultations with women and girls) along with the empowerment of women and girls, will be prioritized. 
•	Meaningful participation, community consultation and engagement will be pursued through the reciprocal research methodology developed by the University of New South Wales (Global Compact for Refugees – Refugee Women and Girls’ Project) in participatory assessments at all stages of SGBV programming (design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation). Protection as well as age, gender and diversity mainstreaming (AGDM) efforts will be further enhanced.
•	Pursuant to UNHCR Bangladesh’s Action Plan on SGBV Mainstreaming 2020, the revised IASC Guidelines on Integrating GBV Interventions in Humanitarian Action will be progressively mainstreamed across all sectors within UNHCR and its partners’ programmes. This would be in complementarity to the GBV SS’ efforts. 
•	A robust component of the intervention will address the need for building capacities through on-the-job coaching, mentoring, needs-based/prioritized training of trainers and step-down training of UNHCR staff, partner organizations, government authorities and the affected communities on SGBV prevention, risk mitigation and response. This is aimed at improving the quality of case management, timely and effective referrals to appropriate, holistic and integrated services (including medical, psychosocial support, legal and security, livelihoods, sexual and reproductive health, and other services), as needed and wished - in accordance with the survivor-centred approach and the best interests of the child (in cases involving child survivors of SGBV). 
•	With the bulk of existing services focusing on women and girls, the project will also include the enhancement and/or expansion of entry points where male survivors, LGBTI survivors of SGBV, as well other diverse and/or marginalized groups (including persons with disability), will find meaningful, equal and impartial access (including differentiated access as needed) to specialized support and services in a safe, confidential and dignified manner. 
•	Integrated services and assistance provided within the existing 38 community and counselling facilities managed by UNHCR’s partners - including 15 Women & Girls-Friendly Spaces - will be strengthened based on monitoring and evaluation reports, the feedback received from clients, and the results of the GBV Sub-Sector’s safety audits. Community-based safe shelters established in complementarity to a partner-run safe shelter, will be accessible to SGBV survivors in need of refuge.  
•	Ensure the integration of SGBV interventions in emergency preparedness & response plans, and disaster risk reduction initiatives 
The modalities of implementation will be directly through UNHCR SGBV specialized staff, qualified and skilled partners, and through community-led/supported groups whose capacities have been built over the past years and will be progressively enhanced.

project_name: Provision of PPE and hygiene kits to the most at risk older people and people with disabilities affected by the Beirut port blast
project_objective: In response to the Beirut explosion that happened on the 4th of August accompanied by a drastic increase in the number of COVID19 positive cased, HelpAge International is proposing a project to promote better hygiene practices in areas affected by the explosion targeting the most-at-risk older people and persons with disabilities identified by an outreach team of community volunteers through 1) the provision of hygiene kits for 500 households living in the target areas with an older family member and/or person with specific needs, 2) the provision of 250 elderly kits to older people identified to be in need for the kits’ items based on specific assessment criteria, 3) provision of 500 PPE kits to the affected households to reduce the risk of COVID19 transmission, and 4) raising awareness through community volunteers on COVID19 risk mitigation practices emphasizing on good hygiene practices. The project will be linked up with other projects implemented by HelpAge under the Health and Protection sectors to complement the intervention and ensure a comprehensive response to the emerged needs.

project_name: Understanding sanitation defects caused by the Beirut Port explosion
project_objective: The Beirut Port explosion affected the built as well as the social environment of major parts of the capital and its northern suburbs, namely infrastructure. In a multi-sectoral approach to respond to this crisis, UN-Habitat, along with relevant local and international partners, has engaged with several sectors such as shelter, information management, protection, and WaSH. After conducting several field assessments and coordinating with the Municipality of Beirut (current custodian of the sewage networks of the city) and the Governor of Beirut, it is deemed critical to thoroughly investigate the impact of the explosion on underground wastewater networks, particularly as sewage and rainwater networks are not separated. According to the Head of Municipality of Beirut Engineering department ""the explosion caused most of the sewage manhole covers to pop open in the immediate surrounding areas, indicating the underground network is severely impacted"". Subsequent to a desk review exercise, the total estimated length of affected lines is 90 kilometers, ranging from dislocated pipes, broken connections, leakages, etc. In view of these potential sanitation problems if not addressed (high possibility of inundation and sewage flood will occur as first rains arrive), coupled with increased number of COVID-19 cases, and the necessity to enhance adequate hygiene practices in this current complex health and emergency context, it is critical to investigate the unseen WASH damages likely incurred by the explosion. As such the project entails identification of wastewater networks deficiencies and propose immediate/medium/long term solutions in order to prevent potential sanitation and public health emergencies, including the spread of COVID-19, particularly during the upcoming autumn/ winter rains.

WVL will also ensure that affected households have access to water and sanitation services through the rehabilitation of damaged water tanks and pipes as well as the distribution of clean water to households when needed.

Coordination on exact locations will be ensured through the sector coordination mechanism.

project_name: Shelter Repairs to Households directly affected by the Beirut Blast
project_objective:
In line with CARE Lebanon´s Emergency Response Strategy, CARE will engage with experienced local partners to provide essential repairs to the homes of the most vulnerable households directly affected by the Beirut Blast, subject to minor and medium damage (window and doors blown out, or damaged sanitation facilities such as bathrooms, kitchens and toilets). Both categories, minor and medium damage, will be considered in this intervention. 

CARE will prioritise women and girls and carry out all work with gender and protection mainstreamed. The repairs and rehab will be achieved through a combination of cash programming and technical support. Furthermore, CARE´s intervention will encompass restricted cash for shelter in the form of rent for those whose houses are seriously damaged and un-inhabitable, including protection referrals. This component will mitigate evictions and support those most at risk of Housing and Land Property Rights violations, linking to the NRCs legal support unit ICLA. Targeted groups include direct affected population by the Beirut Blast, including vulnerable families already impacted by the economic crisis, migrant workers, female-headed households, elderly and those with specific needs. 

The shelter implementation modality also involves engaging local youths in carrying out the assessments repairs and rehabilitation under the supervision of engineers, through a cash for work modality directly managed by the partner. This intervention will benefit Beirut based vendors from being chosen suppliers for the project subsequently boosting the market. This approach will both address the urgent needs of the targeted beneficiaries, ensure that supplies and services are procured and delivered at local level, and create income generating activities which should boost an already devastated economy weighed down by hyperinflation and months of lockdown due to the coronavirus pandemic. It will thereafter ensure sustainability and long-term impact beyond the duration of the project.

project_name: Supporting Healthcare services in Bab Al Hawa Hospital
project_objective:
The project aims to support healthcare services in Bab Al Hawa Hospital by providing financial support along with providing all medicines and medical consumables needed, to provide people in need with all required services, this includes local communities and IDPs, women, children and elderly people.
Bab Al Hawa Hospital is considered the biggest specialized hospital in NW of Syria, and it’s now considered the main referral health facility for all primary health facilities in NW of Syria.
The services provided at the hospital includes but not limited to: Emergency unit, Renal Dialysis unit, CT-Scan and X-Ray unit, GI Endoscopy unit, Laboratory and Blood Bank, Neonatal unit, Neurology unit, Cardiology unit, Ophthalmology unit, and Outpatients Clinics, and Specialized Operations unit which includes General Surgery, ENT Surgery, Neurology Surgery, Orthopaedic Surgery, Thoracic Surgery, Maxillofacial Surgery, Urology Surgery and Paediatric Surgery, which will be all supported by this project.
The hospital facilitates the services provision for women by preparing a specialized reception utilities and isolated room for privacy, in addition to the availability of women in the hospital staff.
In addition, the hospital is the authorized referral point to Turkey for the most complex cases. Bab Al Hawa Hospital has provided over the past six years from its founding in 2013 to the end of 2019 more than 1.200.000 beneficiaries.

project_name: Provide of multidisciplinary rehabilitation and psychological services to the most affected and vulnerable women, girls, men and boys with disabilities and injuries in Gaza and West Bank
project_objective: The proposed project will work towards increasing access to basic and specialized services for the most affected population of persons with disabilities living in area C of the West Bank, and persons with injuries due to great return of March (GRM) in Gaza by providing multidisciplinary rehabilitation services; through outreach and in home services, including but not limited to, basic chronic rehabilitation services, post-operative and psychological services. The package of services will be based on pre-identification and assessment of person’s needs. The project will adopt the interdisciplinary approach safeguarding the combination of well trained and skilled rehabilitation professionals. The project will promote accessibility through the implementation of home adaptation for the beneficiaries who developed permanent disabilities, and also for preidentified primary healthcare centers to increase and ease access of persons with disabilities to those centers to benefit from the services as their peers. This ultimately will improve community participation for the targeted population through progressing of their independency, and regain well recovery. The project will support preparedness efforts via prepositioning of assistive devices and hygiene kits in terms of crisis eruption. Besides, increase rehabilitation mobile teams’ knowledge on safety practices to support mitigation of health attacks (includes movement restrictions) in particular in area C of the targeted governorates of the West Bank. Nonetheless, the project will work on a holistic approach to ensure proper and better access to other needs beyond project deliverables for the targeted beneficiaries through the coordination mechanism of local referral networks. This also will support the implementation of a rehabilitation task force under the health cluster management to ensure that rehabilitation minimum standards are well promoted and at least three local/international actors are adopting those standards through HI intensive follow up and technical support. At the level of prevention, and detection the project will increase the awareness raising on disability mainstreaming for healthcare professionals. In addition, to increase mobile teams’ competencies on gender-based violence Gender based Violence (GBV) detection including boosting referrals mechanism for persons with disabilities to increase their access to the GBV services required as per their identified needs and demands.

project_name: Enhancing Reproductive Health Services in NES - 2020
project_objective:
This project started in late 2017 and, in its efforts to deliver safe and sound reproductive health services to war affected population in urban/rural areas and camps proved successful. However, service provision remains challenged by fighting and displacement (most recently due to Peace Spring Operation), and it emerges more important than ever giving continuity to strategic activities until full stabilization of the situation. To ensure a coordinated and lifesaving response UPP continues to support a work focused on improving standards of Reproductive Health through supporting and building the capacity of network of health staff that have been working with high results for more than two years. The intervention is multifaceted: on the one hand, mobile delivery units are particularly relevant in the current context of changing environment (as a piece of the health system and associated with a strong referral system), especially to provide integrated SRH/GBV services for displaced communities in remote villages, informal settlements and in collective centres recently established. However, secondary care remains a main concern, especially in populous urban areas that have experienced considerable influxes of IDPs from conflict zones. Management of intrapartum complications and performing C-sections in a safe environment constitute crucial needs in context where
surgical interventions are operated almost exclusively by private facilities at prices absolutely unaffordable for the majority of people. The key activities will include provision of essential SRH services, including Basic and Comprehensive EmONC, to 4 National hospitals, 1 PHC, and 2 mobile delivery unit. Furthermore, UPP will support the provision of essential RH equipment, medicine and supplies. UPP will also aim to strengthen existing referral mechanisms at health district level and coordinate standardization of services through continued development and validation of protocols and guidelines.

The project extends across 4 governorates and targets 50,000 beneficiaries with service
delivery during a year:
45,000 Women
5,000 Girls (<18)

Selection criteria for beneficiaries will include who lives in the catchment area. Considering the nature of SRH services, UPP focuses on women and girls of reproductive age who represent about 25% of the population, and are considered among the most vulnerable by the health sector in Syria HNO 2019. SRH services are open to all women and girls, men and boys who are in need. Through EmONC, the essential neonatal services will also contribute to save the lives of newborns. Health care providers will be direct beneficiaries for most trainings, including basic and comprehensive EmONC trainings for midwives gradually conducted in UPP supported facilities across the 4 governorates of North East Syria. The action is tailored to maximize delivery of SRH services to the beneficiaries living in the targeted governorates, who have limited resources, experience barriers to access health facilities due to security and cultural issues, and experience protection risks identified in the needs assessment. The action will also focus on responding to newly displaced people and returnees. Therefore, the
importance of flexible response and coordination of humanitarian actors on the ground to reach the population is essential.

project_name: Conflict-affected households in North Syria benefit from safe and dignified WASH services and hygiene conditions.
project_objective:
Mercy Corps (MC) will respond to priority needs with life-saving and life-sustaining WASH assistance across the governorates of Al-Hasakeh, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Deir-ez-Zor and Idleb. 

MC will improve access to basic water services through the identification of critical gaps and the rehabilitation of water supply infrastructure and solid waste management, in particular in areas with a high number of IDPs and returnees (Ar-Raqqa and DEZ), and areas we anticipate significant inward displacement (Dana, Daret Azza and Atareb in Idleb and north Aleppo). Identification of gaps and needs will be carried out through ongoing coordination with WASH cluster and working group, local councils and  other agencies. A special focus will be given to water quality assurance and treatment before the distribution. MC will actively seek solutions for operation and maintenance (O&M), through support to local committees and water authorities directly after the completion of water supply rehabilitation. Water tanks and toilets will complement more comprehensive HH shelter activities, providing safe and dignified accommodation standards for displaced and for those who have chosen to return. Where no other option exists, MC will provide access to safe drinking water through trucking for a period up to 3 months until alternative low-cost and sustainable solutions are implemented. Water interventions will be complemented by solid waste management services. Additionally, MC will support sanitation through repairs to community-level sewage networks and desludging of septic tanks in camps and out of camps. Hygiene promotion, using carefully tailored messages, and the distribution of hygiene kits will complement WASH infrastructure rehabilitation, water trucking, and solid waste management interventions. MC will also distribute multi-purpose cash assistance to conflict-affected households based on regional SMEB values, which include hygiene items.

project_name: Nutrition in Emergencies assistance for IDPs in Fangak (Jonglei) , Panyikang ( Upper Nile ) and Twic ( Warrap) counties .
project_objective: Despite a period of relative stability over the past year, the malnutrition and food insecurity situation across South Sudan remains critical. According to Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) projections for January - April 2020, over 5.5 million people (47% of the population) are predicted to be severely food insecure (IPC 3, 4 & 5), even considering the presence of humanitarian assistance. Levels of acute malnutrition and food insecurity are expected to rise in early 2019 as post-harvest stocks become depleted.  Recent SMART surveys conducted in Jonglei, Warrap and Upper Nile show GAM rates above the emergency threshold. Ongoing insecurity, poor hygiene and sanitation infrastructure, limited availability of diverse and nutritious food in local markets, low coverage of health and immunization services, and constrained and livelihood opportunities exacerbate these findings. To address these issues, the program will directly target 4,772 children under 5 and 6,106 pregnant and lactating women in the treatment of malnutrition at 13 nutrition sites (OTP/TSFP). 13,833 total caregivers will be sensitized on MIYCN topics. Treatment programs will prioritize the identification and treatment of children under five with SAM and MAM, as well as PLW with MAM, through outpatient therapeutic programs (OTP) and targeted supplementary feeding programs (TSFP). Caregivers will receive sensitization and counseling on MIYCN, health, and hygiene/sanitation practices, and critical gender- and age-sensitive hygiene items. To ensure early detection and referral of acute malnutrition, community volunteers will be trained to conduct mass screenings. During these screenings, volunteers will also provide sensitization on nutrition and hygiene/sanitation practices. Prevention activities will focus on community mobilization and sensitization as well as addressing the underlying causes of malnutrition. These activities include training community leaders, hosting mass awareness campaigns around MIYCN and hygiene/sanitation topics and promoting mother-to-mother support groups (MtMSG.

project_name: GBV - Increasing access to GBV prevention and Response services for Conflict affected population in Ayod and Canal/Pigi  Counties of Jonglei State.
project_objective:
CAO propose to target conflict-affected and GBV survivors, Host community, IDPs and returnees living in Ayod and Pigi /Canal. The purpose of this project is to prevent protection risk and provide quality service in a timely manner to women, girls, men, and boys in the two Counties cutting across 8 params. The target population is 12,000, (7000 Women, 3000 Girls, 1000 Boys, and 1000 Men. The project will run for a period of 12 months, with a budget of USD 300,000. The other  activities to be conducted include:  case management , WGFS programming ,creating awareness in the community on the effects of GBV to the whole community  to build resilience and mitigate GBV risks and direct effects it causes on the survivors, training men and women in the community on  PFA/PSS, GBV principle guidelines, training more frontline workers on case management ,PFA and PSS , directly support survivors of GBV through direct support depending on their needs, coordinate with other actors to update referral pathways  and conduct appropriate  integration and  referrals to Health, Nutrition, WASH, Child Protection and Education sectors. In addition, CAO will Conduct comprehensive case management to the women and girls of GBV survivors, establish WGFS. Among the direct beneficiaries will be men, women, girls, and boys. 
CAO maintain strong presence in canal/Pigi and Ayod has it been implementing protection project on the target counties for the last 4 years with support from UNICEF. CAO will scale up its operation especially in the hard to reach areas of the locations where the caseload is high.

project_name: Closing humanitarian gaps for sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services in the protracted emergency regions in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
UNICEF’s water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) humanitarian response in northeast Nigeria,  plays two roles: as service provider; and as the provider of last resort (POLR). Beginning in 2019, the WASH sector in Northeast Nigeria began evaluating the geo-location assigning of partners to ensure effective accountability in the delivery of humanitarian WASH services.  Under this mechanism, the humanitarian response from different WASH partners is coordinated by UNICEF and the State Ministry of Water Resources so partners provide specific WASH services to IDP camps and host communities allocated to them.  Additionally as provider of last resort, UNICEF may have to cover LGAs where critical needs/gaps arise due to new displacement or WASH related diseases or gaps left by diminished capacity/departure of other WASH partners.  This may include interventions in two other states (Adamawa and Yobe) as well. 
Through this project, UNICEF will have specific target IDP camps in Maiduguri Metropolitan City and 10 LGAs (Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Jere, Kara Balge, Konduga, Mafa, Mobbar, Monguno, and Ngala).  UNICEF will adhere to the SPHERE standards in the humanitarian WASH services it provides, and scale up the sustenance of the services as needed.  

To meet the demands of the POLR responsibility, UNICEF may need to mobilize additional resources.  Through this project UNICEF will provide the initial life saving response to fill the gaps, prioritizing areas receiving newly displaced people or under an outbreak of cholera, hepatitis or other WASH-related diseases.   UNICEF will strive to sustain the basic initial WASH services until further response becomes available from other sector partners.

The project objectives and targets are:
1) Affected people have safe and equitable access to a sufficient quantity of water for domestic needs, as per SPHERE standards.  This objective aims at scaling up sustainable water supply coverage in IDP camps to reach 15 litres per person per day.  Target: 200,000 people.
2) Affected people have safe and dignified access to improved sanitation facilities, as per SPHERE standards.  This objective aims at scaling up sustainable sanitation coverage in IDP camps to reach latrine coverage standard of 20 users per latrine.   Target: 500,000 people.
3) Affected people benefit from community tailored gender- and age-sensitive hygiene messages aiming at hygienic behavior and practices as per sector’s standard.  This objective aims at reaching 1,126,800 people in IDP camps and host communities with risk informed behaviour change communication messages in 2020.
4) Affected people benefit from basic gender- and age-sensitive hygiene items including top-ups as per sector standards.  This objective aims to provide new arrivals in IDP camps with initial response hygiene kits and long term IDPs replenishment kits in IDP camps in target LGAs, including cash for hygiene kits in MMC and Jere LGAs. Target: 1,126,800 people.

project_name: Support Acute Mental Health Inpatient and Two Mobile Units in North of Syria
project_objective:
The proposed project is to keep running the acute mental health unit in Sarmada/Idleb for seven more months with the two mental health mobile units. The main goal of the project is to promote specialized mental health service to address more severe mental health disorders. 
Upon the need of the affected people to specialized MH services which are not sufficiently  available in the area, UOSSM contributed to the response by establishing an acute MH inpatient and outpatient unit where services are provided for the most urgent presentations of severe mental health disorders, like schizophrenia (acute psychotic episodes), bipolar disorder (manic episode), severe depression, suicidal risk, severe substance misuse disorder and severe behavioral disorder related to mental health problems which cannot be managed and addressed in the community, in addition to providing a multidisciplinary mental health service in the community (outpatient psychiatric units, psychiatric supervision, follow up and case management, individual, couple and group psychotherapy and tele-mental health supervision), and receiving referrals of more severe and complicated psychiatric beneficiaries from other agencies and health providers.
Also, to cover as many areas as possible, the acute MH unit is linked with two MH mobile clinics, where MH interventions are provided by doctors trained on MHGAP program for beneficiaries of children and adults with signs and symptoms of mild and moderate mental health disorders, in addition to psychosocial support activities for children, which are: self-recovery techniques, coping skills with different situation skills, emotional expression techniques, PFA and PFA for children. Also, to facilitate of awareness campaigns on mental health and protection concerns, such as (detection of signs and symptoms of mental disorders, early marriage, GBV prevention. etc.). Not only the detection and referral of the serious and severe beneficiaries to the acute MH unit in Sarmada, but also the referral of beneficiaries or families to community resources to help in recovery from mental or physical illnesses, and to facilitate access to services provided by other humanitarian actors.
 Objectives of the Project:
•To respond to the most urgent acute and serious mental health problems of the affected populations in the area
•To facilitate an access of the affected populations to long-term specialized MH services 
•To enhance and promote the affected communities’ healthy coping mechanisms for both locals and IDPs
•To facilitate access for the affected populations to the available services in the area through an active referral pathway.

project_name: Support  Specialized Secondary Health Facilities in the North of Syria
project_objective:
Most health centers in northern Syria provide similar services, but there are some specialized quality services that people desperately need and that cannot be dispensed and that are provided in primary care centers such as / dialysis - tuberculosis treatment - advanced diagnosis - blood bank - thalassemia treatment /
The number of centers is six, but because there are two centers that provide the services of Thalassemia and Blood Bank, the number of services becomes five.
The project aims to support health care services in five specialized health care centers in northern Syria which  provide the following services:
1-  TB center services in Idleb city
2- Blood bank and thalassemia services in Idleb city and Kafrnobol.
3- Renal dialysis services in Idleb city.
4- Advanced diagnostic services in Idleb.
5- Physiotherapy and prosthetic services in Sarmada.
What distinguishes this project is the following:
a  - It provides life-saving services and prevention of serious complications  b- It provides quality and uncommon services as is the case with health centers  there c- It is integrated in terms of diversity and there is no repetition of it within the project to avoid duplication
 d- It is integrated within the single center, and there is no shortage of the single service delivery chain e- It is geographically dispersed in the north of Syria, achieving a fair distribution of healthcare f- It is considered a referral center for many primary and even secondary care centers that need these specialized services
These centers will provide services for 72,000 beneficiaries per year, most of whom will be affected, who have only these centers to save them from complications of their diseases and injuries.

project_name: Rehabilitation/repair of damaged shelters and safe rubble and debris removal
project_objective:
The proposed project consists of 1) support to building repairs for vulnerable affected households and 2) safe rubble and debris removal/disposal from damaged and destroyed houses. These components contribute to the shelter sector log frame Outcome 2 (Contribute to longer-term repair or rehabilitation and occupancy of damaged buildings) and Outcome 3 (Support multi-sectoral approaches to rehabilitate affected areas) respectively.

For the first component, rehabilitation and repairs of housing units/homes affected by the Beirut port blast in the vulnerable affected areas will be undertaken in coordination with UN-Habitat and other shelter partners. This component will contribute to the shelter sector Objective 2. The detailed activities include:
- Detailed technical assessments of damaged buildings in coordination with partners of the Shelter Sector and relevant authorities in the targeted area
- Rehabilitation and repair of damaged houses for affected vulnerable households
 

The second component will include environmentally sound safe removal and disposal of rubble and debris from damaged houses within the city of Beirut. The project will also closely coordinate with UN-Habitat on the ground-level. This component will contribute to the shelter sector Outcome 3. The detailed activities include:
- Collection of debris and rubble (bricks, glass, concrete, asbestos, steel) from around the damaged and destroyed houses in the affected areas and transportation to “temporary” sites assigned by the government/municipality
- Technical assessment of rubble and debris from destroyed houses for safe and environmentally sound removal and disposal

Both activities will be built on the UNDP's years of experience and presence on the ground in the relevant fields as well as the extensive network with national partners. The project is not funded yet as of August 23.

project_name: Provide free legal assistance to survivors of the blast and safeguard the rights of the most vulnerable
