project_objective:
The proposal  will support the most affected communities with a holistic approach that includes community and homes repair, light rehabilitation and cleaning (when needed), through short term work opportunities for vulnerable unemployed people, Lebanese and Migrant, refugee women and men, as well as youth and with involvement of PWD when possible. Workers will be from directly affected families who lost their jobs, ensuring a target of at least 25% female workers. The intervention will also complement the support to families with the provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) to families in need. The initiatives will support approximately 2,000 families and the repair, cleaning and light rehabilitation of approximately  community structures as well as homes (meeting the applicable safety criteria) to allow displaced people to return to their communities. The working conditions (including working hours) will comply with the Lebanese labour law and regulations. Labourers will be supported with: 
- PPE equipment CFW PPE
- Protective kits and tools for CFW (gloves, boots, jacket/hat etc.) 
- Training on safety measures regarding COVID-19 as well as safety at work
- Workman insurance
While this is an emergency action, the impact in the long term is 
- 2000 families have have livelihoods support and regained resilience
-  Community structures and homes cleaned and repaired;
- MHPSS, Protection interventions, will support community and individual resilience, while providing focused and specialized support to those in need through referral 
Output: Short term employment opportunities for food insecure people through cash for work in repair, light rehabilitation of community infrastructure and houses as well as cleaning and remaining waste/debris removal: Generation of short-term employment for vulnerable and food insecure Lebanese and migrant families, women, men and youth through the identification of local labourers who lost their jobs and by engaging them in labour-intensive activities (cash for work) with support of skilled manpower to ensure a rapid response in the affected communities in Beirut and surrounding areas. Psycho-social support will be provided to the affected women, men and, youth and children with Responsible of Psychological Fist Aid (FPA)).

project_name: Efficient Provision of timely and equitable access to lifesaving WASH Service in a Dignified Manner to the most vulnerable communities affected by conflict, disease outbreak, and areas of high malnutrition to mitigate WASH related diseases in Morobo, Pibor, Kapoeta South and Ikotoes.
project_objective:
Under this project, The Rescue Mission will conduct life-saving WASH activities which will contribute to the reduction in morbidity and mortality resulting from waterborne diseases, by increasing access to safe water, sanitation and better hygiene practices among displaced populations, vulnerable communities, and host communities in Morobo, Pibor, Kapoeta South, and Ikotoes Counties.
TERM’s activities  in this project  will include safe water provision through water point rehabilitation (hand pumps), Water yards rehabilitation water quality monitoring and treatment of contaminated water source, provision of household water filters, depending on the needs); provision or rehabilitation of sanitation infrastructure (latrines, hand washing facilities and solid waste management); hygiene promotion (hand washing campaigns in communities and institutions, safe water chain and jerrycan cleaning campaigns); capacity-building of community institutions (pump mechanics, water user committees, community hygiene promoters, school's hygiene clubs), and distribution of WASH NFIs (soap, hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene kit, water containers, water purification filters, PUR or others).
Delivery of this lifesaving intervention will help in increasing knowledge and capacity to prevent outbreak of WASH related diseases including cholera and diarrhea that undermines and threatens lives of children such as under 5, people living with disabilities, pregnant and lactating women in areas affected by severe acute malnutrition. The project will also reduce the risk of GBV associated by women and girls walking long distances in search of water, the repair of water sources will reduce chances of young girls dropping from school to collect water while children in school will have opportunity to WASH services that seek to improve their health. The intervention is designed to build community resilience
The proposed intervention will reach a target of 30,000 vulnerable people (7500 men, 8500 women, 7000 boys and 7000 girls) among internally displaced persons, returnees, and host communities including people with disabilities in the targeted locations
Throughout the response life cycle, TERM team will coordinate with the authorities, community and the key partners on ground who are implementing WASH, nutrition, health, and protection for integration of activities to ensure maximum utilization of resources.
The intervention will include detailed needs assessment to identify the needs, affected gender, age and diversity groups, the vulnerabilities of the targeted community and coping strategies employed by the affected population. Based on the assessment report, interventions will be designed accordingly with TERM capacity, response with other partners will be planned.

project_name: Provision of Inclusive & Protective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children in Ayod, Ulang and Longechuk Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States.
project_objective:
The overall objective of this one-year life-saving intervention is to increase access to and stabilise regular attendance in 43 primary/ECD/ALP schools (Ayod-26, Ulang-9, Longechuk-8) for 17,143 conflict-affected children and youth (7,371 girls) in IDP, returnee and host community areas, especially girls, through provision of sustaining activities such as school meal; and life-saving WASH in schools activities in Ayod, Ulang & Longechuk Counties of Jonglei and Upper Nile States. 8,572 learners will be supported in Ayod, 5,143 in Ulang and 3,428 in Longechuk. 

The envisaged activities include establishing rapid project baseline to map out gaps for inception ; construction of temporary learning spaces to provide safer and protective for additional learners; provision of quality ECD teaching & learning resources, equipment and educational materials to 15 ECD Centres in Ayod (8), Ulang (4) & Longechuk (3); training 430 volunteer teachers on Child Rights, Child Protection and Prevention of Gender-based Violence (GBV) and Psycho-social support(PSS); enhancing the technical capacity of 3 County Education Departments (CEDs) in Ayod, Ulang & Longechuk; establishment/rehabilitation of school WASH facilities including provision of soap; setting up 43 School WASH Clubs to improve and sustain school WASH efforts. 1,548 girls will be provided with menstrual hygiene products/sanitary towels for dignity and continuity of schooling; (Including training); sensitising 1, 693 community members (Ayod-846, Ulang-508, Longechuk-339); and training 129 local education officials (CEDs/PES) on supportive school supervision.

1,956 local actors will be directly involved to provide a focus and structure to the schoolchildren. 81 county education officials will be involved to provide much needed first legal and social interface with the affected population and prepare local education systems for resilience in the face of unforeseen crises. School WASH Clubs will be strengthened to help disseminate key life-saving messages on cholera prevention, food crisis/ rationing and referral pathways for learners requiring psychosocial support. Overall, upwards of 22,980 individuals are planned to benefit directly through this plan.

project_name: Emergency WASH support to IDPs and Vulnerable host communities in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective:
WASH needs are directly linked to high levels of malnutrition, disease, food insecurity and protection risks, with communities in Greater Upper Nile and Eastern Equatorial displaying high levels of malnutrition, food insecurity and disease. Provision of adequate WASH services is key to achieving sustainable solutions to communities in emergency while equipping communities with abilities to mitigate and respond to shocks. 

Christian Mission for Development (CMD) works in Greater Upper Nile and Equatoria regions and plans a response aimed at reaching internally displaced persons, returnees and vulnerable host communities with water, sanitation and hygiene services. 

Spanning a period of 12 months, the project targets the locations of Ayod, Duk, Nyirol, Uror, Fangak and Twic East (Jonglei), Ulang, Maiwut and Longechuk (Upper Nile) and Kapoeta South, Kapoeta North, Kapoeta East and Budi (Eastern Equatoria) with WASH services, to address identified needs, public health and protection issues. 

The response aims at mitigating WASH related GBV by providing gender appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities and tackling issues surrounding gender, safety and WASH. Persistence of food insecurity, and malnutrition signaled by high GAM rates, with <5s and PLW mainly affected will be mitigated by the provision of WASH in nutrition centers, through targeted WASH minimum packages at OTP/SC mainly for mother/caretaker – malnourished children. 
Water related disease outbreaks have been traced to health facilities and community infrastructures/settings without adequate WASH facilities. 

The project targets a total of 120,000 people; 61,800 of these in Jonglei (51.5%); (Ayod – 14,400; Duk – 10,200; Nyirol – 12,000; Uror – 8,400; Twic East – 6,000.); 23,160 in Upper Nile (19.3%); (Ulang – 6,960; Maiwut – 4,800; Longechuk – 11,400) and 35,040 in Eastern Equatoria (29.2%); (Kapoeta North – 7,440; Kapoeta East – 9,600; Kapoeta South – 13,200 and Budi – 4,800). 58% of those targeted are females, 28% of them girls. IDPs consist of 52% of those targeted.

project_name: Emergency WASH  assistant  to  7,200 conflict affected populations in Fangak  County Jonglei State and Panyikang County Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
The overall objective of this project is to address the immediate WASH related needs of the most vulnerable and isolated populations especially Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees and the host communities living in vulnerable, hard to reach community sites in Jonglei and Upper Nile States.
Africa Development Aid (ADA) will target a total of 7,200 individual beneficiaries living in the two 2 Counties. It will address the urgent WASH needs of the vulnerable populations while empowering the community to become technically knowledgeable in WASH infrastructures as well as role models for community hygiene best practices. 
The proposal is premised on the high prospects of peace holding in South Sudan in 2020, especially after the 2018 signing of the revitalized peace agreement between the Government and the opposition parties (IO, SOA, political detainees) plus the expected formation of Government of National Unity (GNU) in November 2019. Based on these assumptions, 2020 will witness arrival of returnees from various internal and external locations to their respective places of origin. 
On-and-off years of civil war destroyed almost all sectors of the economy, including WASH infrastructure and management systems throughout war-ravaged communities. Fangak in Jonglei State and Panyikang in Upper Nile State are amongst the highly needy locations in terms of basic WASH facilities, yet they are expected to be epicenters of 2020 returnees from several PoCs in South Sudan and from immediate neighborhoods of The Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda. 
Mass returnee populations and IDPs in these two locations put serious strain on an already burdened WASH infrastructure and management systems, thus creating new WASH dynamics to handle.  ADA intends to respond by improving and increasing access to safe drinking water. Besides, it proposes to enhance proper, culturally acceptable sanitation and hygiene practices that promote dignity for the targeted population in Fangak Jongolei State and Panyikang Upper Nile States. 
ADA intends to conduct mass community mobilization and sensitization on community WASH concerns. Other activities include: training of water management committees;  production and distribution of WASH IEC materials; construction or rehabilitation of community WASH facilities; provision of water purification  kits; promotion of CLTS in communities; distribution of basic hygiene and MHH kits to schools and vulnerable groups; and other basic training in promoting community hygiene for  safe, healthy and secure communities, as a central vision of Africa Development Aid.

ADA seeks to use WASH Cluster tools, management structure at different levels,  partnerships, networks , logistical and technical backups as well as other agencies on the ground to create meaningful synergies in realizing the 2020 WASH HRP in the two States. ADA has the staff, experience, hardware and practical presence in the two States, thus creating a conducive environment for successful operations

project_name: Contribution à la réponse aux urgences sanitaires au Burundi
project_objective:
La situation des enfants au Burundi est caractérisée par une forte mortalité infanto juvénile estimée à 78‰ naissances vivantes (EDS 2016-2017) avec prédominance de causes évitables ou traitables. La mortalité maternelle reste élevée (334 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes, EDS 2016) et demeure extrêmement préoccupante malgré une baisse par rapport à l’EDS 2010 (500 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes). Les Burundais de tout le pays, en particulier les femmes et les enfants, restent vulnérables aux crises humanitaires due à des niveaux élevés de pauvreté. Cette situation précaire est aggravée par les catastrophes naturelles (c.-à-d. inondations, glissements de terrain et déficits pluviométriques), comme le choléra et les pics de paludisme ainsi que le risque qu’Ebola se propage dans le pays. Quelque 1,74 million de personnes, dont 993 000 enfants, sont en crise humanitaire et le ralentissement économique, et nécessiteront une aide humanitaire en 2020.
Sur le plan épidémiologique, le Burundi connait depuis plusieurs années des épisodes d’épidémies de paludisme (dans sa partie Nord Est et Centre), de rougeole dans les camps et orphelinats et de choléra (dans la partie Ouest du pays), principalement sur la rive du Lac Tanganyika. Le paludisme a notifié plus de 8,8 millions de cas et a dépassé en fin d'année 2019 le seuil épidémique et d'alerte dans 35 et 06 districts sanitaires sur 47. En 2019, le Burundi a notifié 1,195 contre 102 cas de choléra en 2018. Le risque de nouvelles flambées de choléra reste élevé en raison des mauvaises conditions d'hygiène. Malgré les bonnes performances en matière de vaccination, on note une stagnation, voire une régression des couvertures vaccinales dans certains districts. Lors de l’atelier d’élaboration du HNO, l’analyse de la situation a conduit le secteur de la santé à identifier les populations affectées comme étant celles de 10 des 18 provinces du pays (Bubanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cankuzo, Kirundo, Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana et Ruyigi) qui connaissent des épidémies de choléra à répétition, avec morbidité de paludisme plus élevée, les provinces avec des taux moyens de 52% et 29% correspondant respectivement à la capacité de diagnostic et de disponibilité des médicaments essentiels, provinces avec une mortalité maternelle élevée et aussi ceux qui ont connu une détérioration de la couverture vaccinale de la rougeole.  Le plateau technique des services de santé maternelle et néonatale est insuffisant et le pays dispose de capacités limitées d’offre de soins obstétricaux d’urgence de base complet. Les ratios de décès maternels et taux de décès néonataux sont excessifs selon les données de la surveillance intégrée de la maladie et la riposte, soit 234 décès maternels et 690 décès périnatals notifiés jusqu’à la 40ème semaine de l’année 2019
Activités et outputs: 
UNICEF utilisera son expérience dans la mise en œuvre des activités auprès des formations sanitaires et des communautés et son avantage comparatif dans l’appui technique et le monitoring des interventions liées à la santé. La réponse portera sur différentes interventions comme l'appui en médicaments essentiels principalement pour les populations les plus vulnérables que sont les femmes et les enfants de moins de 15 ans, la prise en charge du choléra, le soutien à une vaccination continue ainsi que l’amélioration des Soins Obstétricaux et néonatals essentiels.
