project_name: Emergency Shelter/NFI response for populations affected by disasters and/or climate change (including returnees and internally displaced persons (IDPs))
project_objective:
This project aims to address the current gaps (according to the 2020 HRP) in returnee response and emergency shelter/NFI needs identified by the Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) of IOM-DTM Unit, by:

a) Reinforcing the capacity of national and local authorities on emergency response
b) Creation of Early warning system and Strengthening the rapid assessment capacity
following natural disasters, including monitoring of IDPs
c) Distribution of Emergency Shelters and NFI response to returnees from the United Republic of Tanzania and people affected by natural disasters, including cash-based intervention to support during construction process
d) Providing Transitional Shelters and Repair Shelter kits to the most vulnerable
households returning from the United Republic of Tanzania and/or affected by natural disasters, including cash-based intervention to support during construction process
e) Reinforce Emergency Communication with Community mechanism in country,
specifically the Emergency Hotline (109) hosted in the premises of the Burundian Red Cross.

In addition, this project will reinforce the IOM’s Emergency Event Tracking system (EET) for rapid assessment following natural disasters and other displacement events, including the development of an emergency response team dedicated to assessing life-saving shelter needs of returnees.

The project, as well as the Emergency Event Tracking (EET) will covering the 18
provinces of Burundi, namely Makamba, Rumonge, Bubanza, Cibitoke, Kayanza, Ngozi,
Ruyigi, Rutana, Gitega, Bururi, Mwaro, Murumvya, Karusi, Cankuzo, Muyinga, Kayanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural.

project_name: Peru - Caritas Switzerland
Mitigating C-19 secondary impacts on food security and livelihoods in urban areas
project_objective: The project seeks to mitigate the secondary impacts of COVID-19 on vulnerable households through cash transfers in large cities of Zimbabwe (Harare, Mutare, Bulawayo). Due to the extended lock down and movement restrictions urban households who subsist in the informal economy are disproportionately affected as it is taking time for the informal economy to be fully opened. More so some of the  beneficiaries have been affected by the demolitions that were effected by the city councils while others have their value chains being disrupted by the movement restrictions internally as well as cross border trade.

project_name: Livelihood support for vulnerable families in Aleppo and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
Through this intervention ZOA will effectively and efficiently respond to urgent and identified livelihood needs in Aleppo and Rural Damascus. With local partners, ZOA will provide vocational training for 300 members of vulnerable households in Aleppo and Rural Damascus, set up a sewing factory in Douma, Rural Damascus, for women with sewing skills, and rehabilitate 36 small shops in Arbin, Rural Damascus, to provide income and support local economic infrastructure.  The approach is based on the specific context in each location.
ZOA prioritises communities with high severity of needs, and selects vulnerability and selection criteria in line with sector standards.  ZOA vulnerability criteria also incorporates analysis of protection concerns. Issues or concerns highlighted during assessments feed into project and implementation planning to ensure a mainstreaming approach and impactful support to households. Beneficiaries are selected after consultation with local authorities. Project committees are set up in Arbin and Douma to oversee the project implementation and take ownership of the project activities after project end.
For vocational training, vulnerable households will be selected, and one person from each household will receive a vocational skill training. The topic will be decided based on the wishes of the attendees as well as the economic situation in the community, with the goal of providing an income after the training. Participants receive cash for attendance, to support their families during the training. The vocational training is supplemented by lifeskills training, and each participant will receive a relevant toolkit. Families with members with disabilities will be targeted, and training will be explored that is relevant for people living with disabilities to gain an income independently.
In Douma, Rural Damascus, there are many skilled seamstresses. The area once hosted multiple sewing factories, which are no longer operating. This project will establish a sewing factory to employ 50 skilled women. A further 25 women will be trained in sewing. 
In Arbin, Rural Damascus, shops have closed during the last years. By rehabilitating 36 small shops, the local economy will be supported. Each shop owner is required to employ at least one person from a vulnerable household.
Projects will be monitored and adjusted accordingly by ZOA and local communities.  Combining vocational training in topics deemed relevant in the local communities with rehabilitation of shops and establishing a factory will give ZOA important insight into the effectiveness of each modality in a Syrian context towards the objective of improved livelihoods for vulnerable families.

project_name: WASH life-saving and life sustaining assistance for conflict affected IDPs, returnees and host communities
project_objective:
The conflict in Syria has created and exacerbated large-scale humanitarian needs around water, sanitation, and hygiene. 10.7 million people are still in need of access to safe water (53% of the population), with 28% considered in acute need and exposed to life threatening health risks. Up to 42% of the population relies on alternative and often unsafe water sources to meet or complement their daily needs. Water quality is poor, increasing the risk of contracting water borne diseases. The combination of lack of rehabilitation and poor maintenance of destroyed or damaged water and sanitation systems affects equal and safe access to basic WASH services for returnees and host communities, leading to an increased dependency on water trucking. Access to sufficient and affordable safe water, adequate sanitation, solid waste management and/or hygiene supplies remain a challenge for newly or protracted displaced populations. Women are disproportionately affected by a lack of access to WASH services and forced to adopt inadequate coping strategies. IDPs leaving in formal or informal settlements remain highly dependent on continuous humanitarian assistance including for WASH services, whose disruptions would have direct negative impact on their physical and mental well-being and protection consequences, specifically for women and girls. Poor hygiene conditions lead to disease outbreaks, especially in areas of high concentration of IDPs and camps. Moreover, gender-specific sanitation needs are considerably higher among displaced people compared to the rest of the population, with over-crowding, cleanliness and protection concerns. 
Considering the forecasted contextual scenario combined with the severity of needs, AAH aims at achieving an impact in the short-term, while reducing the vulnerability of targeted communities in the medium to long-term increasing the access to sustained and equitable WASH basic services, thus promoting the right to dignity and safety. AAH will implement life-saving and life-sustaining activities through repair and maintenance of water and sanitation systems coupled with emergency WASH services and distribution of NFIs - including water trucking, distribution of jerry cans and gender-specific hygiene kits, installation of water tanks, provision of de-sludging/latrine cleaning services, SWM and rehabilitation/maintenance of sanitation facilities, including in schools and PHCs. AAH will prioritize the maintenance and/or rehabilitation of existing water supply systems (water stations, boreholes, networks), including water quality testing. Given the lack or irregular distribution of electricity in many parts of Syria, gen-sets and/or Solar Photo Voltaic systems might be provided as main or complimentary source of power. Rehabilitation works of sewage systems, including waste-water plants and sewage networks, will also be conducted to prevent public health risks and the contamination of water and soil due to the discharge of raw sewage. Communities with no access to water and populations affected by new or protracted displacements will be supported with emergency WASH services such as, water trucking, the distribution of jerry cans, and the installation of communal water tanks. AAH will also protect the health and hygienic environment through the rehabilitation and/or the maintenance of WASH facilities (including in schools and PHCs) and the provision of services such as de-sludging and solid waste management. Emergency hygiene kits will be distributed in collaboration with SARC, coupled, whenever possible, with hygiene promotion awareness sessions. AAH can cover needs across all Syria, with priority to 8 Governorates (Dar’a, Rural Damascus, Hama, Homs, Aleppo, Raqqa, Deir ez Zor, Hassakeh), in benefit of 820,000 vulnerable conflict-affected host communities, returnees and IDPs, i.e. 213,760 men, 243,840 women, 168,800 boys and 175,600 girls. AAH response is in line with the 1st and 2nd 2020 WASH strategic pillars.

project_name: Safe and secure shelter conditions provided for Women, Girls, Men and Boys (WGMB)
project_objective: Medair has already been involved in the Shelter response through distributing 2144 emergency shelter kits to affected households. The project will re-establish secure shelter conditions for households affected by the Beirut port explosion through conducting minor repairs and rehabilitations of houses/apartments; providing safety and security for the families and protection from the elements. The project will also rehabilitate common areas and take special consideration of the accessibility needs of People with Specific Needs (PwSN). Medair aims to partner with local initiatives and NGO's to help build capcity through this project (in line with the objectives of the Shelter cluster).

project_name: Improved protection mechanisms for most vulnerable groups in the West Bank and Gaza through increased access and quality mental health and psychosocial services services with comprehensive and gender sensitive approach
project_objective:
Médicos del Mundo Spain (MdM-S) will contribute through this project to the achievement of Strategic Objectives No. 2 and No.3 of the Protection Cluster Strategy.
In particular, this project will strengthen resilience, improve access to services and pursue for long-lasting solutions, thus mitigating the effects of occupation and conflict-related violence in the West Bank and of blockade in Gaza.  The project focuses in increasing the access to quality enhanced public Mental Health services and MHPSS outreach services at the community level. The project will specifically target population, and in particular children, women and adolescents, affected by the conflict in the West Bank and Gaza. This will be done incorporating the IASC MHPSS and GbV guidelines, the Minimum Standards for Ch.P. in HA (CPWG), applying as core principles: human rights and equity, participation, do no harm, integrated support to systems and building on available resources and capacities; and the enhancement of a coordinated and effective response to critical incidents and MHPSS support to survivors of GbV and Child Abuse. 
MdM intends to pursue the following activities between 2020 and 2021: •Provision of Child Protection response, with special emphasis on safe spaces for responsive interventions in emergencies, including case management and PSS for children and families, as well as Early Stimulation Programs. 
•Provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial services (MHPSS) for adults and youth, with special emphasis on gender equality and detection and referral of GbV. 
•Capacity building of public Health Services and Mental Health Services to address children and adolescents needs following appropriate guidelines and standards.
 •Advocacy initiatives among the international community that aim to address protection concerns; prevent violations or enhance accountability for violations of IHRL and IHL by all duty bearers. 
• Contribute to coordination and participation in the Protection Cluster and progressively increasing contributions to GbV subcluster.

project_name: Malnutrition Prevention and Treatment for Vulnerable groups in Pibor County
project_objective:
The proposed project seeks to address acute malnutrition among vulnerable groups through an integrated community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and Maternal Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) that combines prevention and and lifesaving treatment measures in Pibor County. The project will target 38,927 children aged 6-59 months for malnutrition screening, with a target of 5,368 for SAM. In terms of nutrition preventive activities the project will target 30,634 children 6-59 months for Vitamin A supplementation. The project will further target 73,107 primary caregivers of children aged 0-23 months for MIYCN counselling. Early prepositioning of nutrition supplies will be undertaken to prevent rupture of essential supplies in all OTP sites.  

Key components of the project include; (i) the promotion of equitable access to nutrition specific preventive service delivery; (ii) screening and treatment of acute malnutrition cases in children U5 and PLW; (iii) advocacy and coordination to enable integration of nutrition sensitive services with WASH, food security, health and protection services and (iii) information collection and analysis to strengthen evidence based nutrition response in the County(iv) capacity building to Ministry of Health to establish Nutrition System within County Health Department (CHD). 
 
Efforts will be put in place to station all nutrition services within existing health systems and where health systems do not exist, strong collaboration will be made with health partners to offer health mobile clinics at all nutrition sites. Integrated nutrition services will involve the health sector for treatment of childhood illnesses specifically malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea as well as preventive health services such as immunization, growth monitoring and deworming. Growth monitoring will be done for children aged 0-59 months to monitor growth faltering and action taken timely.  WASH activities will be integrated in all health and nutrition sites which includes provision of safe water, hygiene promotion activities and sanitation including distribution of hygiene kits to families of children with SAM and MAM through collaboration with WASH partners. FSL will be integrated in all health and nutrition sites and demonstration gardens will be established for training of primary caregivers to gain knowledge and skills in establishing home gardens in living places. MSGS will be supported to carry out cooking demos with primary caregivers of children aged 6-23 months to develop competency in complementary food preparations and feeding to improve MIYCN indicators.  All health and nutrition sites will be made child friendly through provision of Baby Friendly Spaces (BFS) to offer Early Childhood Development (ECD) activities including equipping them with toys. Early detection and treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases will be through screening and admission to the OTP program while addressing underlying causes of acute malnutrition by counseling on appropriate childcare practices, improving sanitation practices and provision of micronutrient supplementation and deworming. 

Gender mainstreaming in nutrition program will be enhanced to ensure more females are recruited in the program to implement child care activities especially in MIYCN. Accountability to Affected Populations will be enhanced though Complaint Response Mechanism (CRM). Community members will be consulted before implementation to help in designing feedback mechanism that is culturally sensitive to the context. 

In order to monitor and identify evolving needs and facilitate timely nutrition responses, the project will strengthen its monitoring and reporting to the cluster and support nutrition surveillance activities, FSNMS and conduct pre-harvest SMART survey.

project_name: Improving Food and Livelihood Security for Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to address immediate food and livelihood needs of 696,347 people facing severe acute food insecurity in several states across South Sudan including Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity and Warrap. This intervention will combine the direct delivery of food assistance to affected people with provision of emergency livelihood inputs targeted at revitalizing local food production as well as resilience building measures. The consumption stability achieved through the food assistance will safeguard livelihoods and assets and provide households leeway to engage in additional productive livelihood activities. This measured result, along with the project’s support for appropriate emergency livelihood inputs, community participation in value added actions, skill building and technical assistance will lead to recovery of agricultural and pastoralist livelihoods and the development of durable and productive assets. This will in the long term enhance food security, restore livelihoods, and build resilience to future shocks.

The project’s target is 696,347 people, anticipated to be in crisis or worse acute food insecurity in 2020. They include; 221,132 in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, 92,040 in Warrap, 173,685 in Jonglei and 209,490 people in Unity.  Project participants will be selected through a rigorous community-based process with deliberate emphasis on vulnerable groups such as female and child headed households, households with children in curative centres, people with disability, the elderly and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). 

Specific interventions include: a) General food distribution with value added activities meant to ensure access to adequate and nutritious food to meet immediate hunger needs and address ongoing food insecurity  b) Cash For Assets - that will be used as a resource for increasing community capacity to organize and engage in value-added and asset creation activities such as restoration of crop lands, flood control and natural resource management actions; c) emergency agricultural livelihood support consisting of crop, vegetable kits and fishing inputs in conjunction with agricultural skill trainings will help vulnerable households enhance own food production. The increased availability of vegetable and fishing produce will promote diet diversification. The adoption of better farming and fishing methods will contribute towards food self-sufficiency and reduced dependency on food assistance in the long run.

To attain optimal food security results, the project will promote complementary programming approaches, using the opportunity to interact with target groups beyond the activity of food and livelihood inputs transfers. The project will take advantage of all community mobilization platforms to disseminate key messages and actions on nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), gender and protection especially during targeting, community based participatory planning meetings, asset creation discussions and during food distribution. 

JAM will ensure participation of women at all levels of the project. The project will ensure that at least 50% of the beneficiaries are female. To achieve this, female headed households will be prioritized during beneficiary registration and efforts will be made to ensure that during distributions, food is placed directly in the custody of women. Distribution sites selection and timing will take into consideration location centrality and protection concerns of women and children. The project will support the equal representation of females in local community institutions such as Project Management Committee (PMC) both at membership and leadership position levels. 

The project will invest in capacity building of local actors including community members such as PMCs to ensure they have sufficient technical and managerial skills to plan and implement similar programs beyond the project period.

project_name: Provision of equitable access to safe and adequate water, dignified Sanitation, and safe hygiene practices to mitigate WASH related GBV and Malnutrition for the internally displaced populations (IDPs)
project_objective:
CMC aims at provision of equitable access to safe and adequate water, dignified Sanitation, and safe hygiene practices to mitigate WASH related malnutrition and GBV through integrated WASH intervention reinforcing protection, enhancing resilience, communities coping mechanisms and sustainability to achieve cluster strategic objectives 1, 2 & 3 (SO 1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 3:1) , and cluster objectives (CO1 and CO3) tackling 70% WASH-nut and 30% WASH-GBV in the areas of Pibor and Kapeota South targeting crises affected population, IPC3 to IPC4 population, mainly IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable host communities in Likuangole, Gumuruk, verteth, Pibor town in Jonglei and Kapeota South in Eastern Equatoria, to reduce morbidity and mortality resulting from WASH-related GBV and malnutrition within the affected population. CMC focuses on lifesaving WASH activities mainstreaming protection, accountability to affected population (AAP) and strengthening the beneficiaries copping mechanism and building resilience through training of different groups of people in the community including; pump mechanics, Water management committee, women groups, community leaders, the AAP focal persons, teachers, pupils and nutrition workers. The project targets 25,000 (16,000 Direct, and 7,000 indirect) beneficiaries facing IPC3&4  and GAM ranging at 20.8%, the IDPs, most vulnerable host communities affected with conflict and natural disasters, and malnutrition patients with limited access to WASH services and food insecurity, through supported coordination and complementation of WASH needs in the targeted areas, achieving Sphere standards, the core humanitarian standards and the WASH cluster objectives CO1 and CO3, and contributing to eradication of the IPC.
CMC aims at structured, effective preparedness and response programme through improving access to safe water, enhancing community awareness on safe hygiene and sanitation practices within population with limited access to WASH services and food insecurity, supporting institutional WASH Services through coordinations with nutrition, protection and FSL partners to intergrate WASH in their interventions by enhancing the knowledge of mothers and children with equitable WASH practices to mitigate WASH related GBV and malnutrition within the population. Enhancing sustainability and resilience by building capacities of the communities to cope with current shocks through sustaining livelihoods linkages with development action to promote ownership, perticipations, and accountability to affected people through benficiaries centered aproaches. 
CMC will ensure that services delivered are gender-sensitive, considering people with special needs and disables by establishing strong feedback and complain mechanisms at all stages of the implementation, training of the AAP focal point dominated by the beneficiaries, and the CMC M&E team to ensure feedbacks and complains are addressed. Initial needs assessments will be conducted in consultation with the WASH cluster. the activities includes; safe water supply through water point repair and rehabilitation, provision of sanitation facilities at institution levels, hygiene promotion focusing on key messages that encourages the used  of locally available materials and CAT-method of  excreta disposal at households and institutional hygiene promotion. Capacity-building of community through trainings (pump mechanics, water user committees, community hygiene promoters, school's hygiene clubs, the AAP focal points, nutrition workers), distribution of WASH NFIs and MHM kits to the most vulnerable population.
Ensures strong M&E mechanisms, active citizenship, AAP score cards are used to evaluate activities being implemented. CMC protection team will be involved at all stages of designing, planning, implementation and evaluation of every proposed activities to ensure maximum protection mainstreaming and Mitigate GBV threats. Recruiting staffs at field to avoid Logistical constraints.

project_name: Improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable protracted IDPs, returnees and host communities /affected non- displaced who are unable to meet their S/NFI needs in areas of Upper Nile, Jonglei and Warrap State.
project_objective:
The project seeks to improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable newly displaced, protracted IDPs, returnees and host communities /affected non- displaced who are unable to meet their S/NFI needs in areas of Upper Nile(Ulang, Nasir and Maiwut), Jonglei (Akobo West) and Warrap State (Tonj North and Twice ). 
According to UNOCHA more than 908,000 people have been affected by unusually heavy rainfall and subsequent flooding since July of whom 620,000 people are in need of immediate humanitarian assistance. The Government of South Sudan declared a state of emergency in the affected areas on 27 October. 
Other than flooding, some of the driving factors on the ground that triggered present displacements include; Inter Communal Conflicts in settlement areas, inter-communal/tribal fighting in refugee camps in neighboring countries, signing of the revitalized peace agreement in 2018 giving hope for peace and the continuous flooding in almost every part of the country as a result of heavy rains.
Floods caused by torrential rains have worsened the living conditions of South Sudanese people in many parts of the country in the past few months. The heavy rains have destroyed shelters, crops, water sources, public infrastructure like schools and health facilities, increased the risk of water-borne diseases among communities, and rendered many roads impassable, constraining access to affected areas.
TADO response will be jointly in  collaboration with Humanitarians partners e.g  SSUDA, Nile Hope,Medair,PAH, CIDO ,CHADO, ADA, CCOSS, NCA and World Vision International in the identified affected counties with highly  severity and  gaps after SSHF-A2 intervention by the partners. The mode of intervention will be in-kind since there are no markets and previously existing markets have been destroyed by either floods or conflicts.
The organization intends to target 20,000 direct beneficiaries segregated as follows, Ulang 7500, Nasir 4,600, Akobo West 3000, Tony North and Twice  2900 and Maiwut 2000, comprising of newly displaced people, (IDPs) in protracted settlement , returnees and most vulnerable  host communities that are unable to meet their S/NFI needs. Further, it will target lactating and pregnant women, households with malnourished children, unaccompanied children and unaccompanied elderly and persons with disabilities. The project will undertake timely delivery of life-saving assistance through the deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities outlined in the Humanitarian Response plan 2020 (HRP).
TADO has a static presence in both Ulang and Nasir  counties of Upper Nile state ,Gogrial East in Warrap,Akobo West in Jonglei state, and was thus recently nominated as site focal point for Eastern Upper Nile.
The project team will adopt conflict sensitive approaches embracing “Do No Harm” principles through community engagements on GBV, HLP and integrating the work across other clusters where TADO and other partners on the ground are active. 
TADO will significantly  mainstream GBV throughout all stages of S/NFI response, to ensure gender and protection risks are addressed directly thus mitigating chances of exacerbated vulnerabilities.

project_name: Integrated Response for Conflicted Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) III
project_objective:
This project seeks to build on gains made through programming in 2015–2019, meeting the needs of approximately 111,180 conflict and famine-affected individuals (53,366 males and 57,814 females) in South Sudan through an integrated Nutrition, Agriculture and Food Security, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response.  

The areas of South Sudan targeted for this project include Mayendit, Abiemnhom and Mayom Counties. To increase adequate access to clean water, hand pumps will be rehabilitated, a manual drill will be utilized to drill additional wells, and existing water points will be upgraded to solarized systems to enhance water yields for increased beneficiary coverage. In addition, water-management committees (WMCs) will be formed and hand pump mechanics will be trained in a bid to foster community ownership and sustainability of the water infrastructures.  With regard to efforts to improve health and hygiene practices, communal and HH latrines, and gender-segregated bathing shelters will be constructed, and trainings will be conducted on better health and hygiene practices.

project_name: Improve access to dignified income generating activities and build marketable skills for conflict-and displacement-affected populations in Syria
project_objective:
DRC will deliver Early Recovery assistance to persons of concern (PoCs) targeting conflict-affected youth and adults, men and women, including people with disabilities, to develop skills and increase income-generating opportunities with an aim to strengthen their access to livelihoods. PoCs with protection related concerns and vulnerabilities will be particularly targeted, and internal and external referrals will be made to ensure that protection services are provided in parallel based on identified needs.   Initial needs assessments will be conducted jointly with MoE, MoSAL, and SARC field staff, when applicable. These assessments will allow DRC to select specific locations for its interventions where multi-sectoral assistance will respond to specific priority needs identified on the ground. In addition at the beginning of 2020, a labor market assessment will be conducted to be informed on the type of training/internship services to provide, as well as to the type of businesses to priorities within the business-start up support. 

The eligibility of applicants will be based on a combination of their vulnerability and suitability for the Economic Recovery activity of their interest. 
Delivery of skills development trainings (vocational trainings (VTs), internship placements, employability skills) will be implemented by DRC in collaboration with the MoE, the MoSAL, and SARC. Awareness-raising on the rights and responsibilities of employers and employees will be provided in collaboration with the DRC Protection department. 
Market analysis will be conducted to understand the market needs, gaps, and opportunities. Business Skills Development Trainings will be delivered targeting PoC who lost their productive assets due to the conflict. Upon successful completion of the training, each business plan will be assessed by a panel, and those selected will be provided with MicroGrants (MGs) (Assets restoration). Micro Business owners group formulation will be assisted to facilitate its linkage with existing MSMEs, investors, and Chamber of Commerce for business development opportunities. 
MGs, VTs, and internship activities will be provided to PWDs and women in rural and urban areas. Community-based peer groups of Micro Business owners will be formulated to facilitate experience sharing and to provide Life skills and PSS sessions. (In coordination with Protection).
To promote equal and open participation of the interested population, DRC will advertise the Economic Recovery activities in each area, with clear beneficiary selection criteria, details of the activities and deadline for the submission of applications. The outreach will be conducted through displaying banners at the prominent places in the targeted area, radio messages (if allowed), and flyers distribution. Additionally, local authorities will be contacted to inform them about the program and seek their support for information dissemination.

project_name: Shelter and NFI response to the most vulnerable conflict-affected populations in northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Through this project, NRC aims to provide immediate and reliable response to unmet need in the Northeast Nigeria including Dikwa, Munguno, Damasak and Mubi and other newly accessible areas.
In accordance with the NRC’s operational location and its program response strategy, NRC will implement shelter and NFI provision to enable targeted households to access timely the improved better living and protective living condition. The NRC shelter response will also include emergency shelter package, which will consist by providing the emergency shelter and NFI kits while the most and adapted robust shelter response will be designed. The NRC response strategy will also include technical training to enable local carpenter to build and maintain better the provided shelter and the provision of habitability measure training and awareness for the improvement and maintaining the healthier living environment.
Following the NRC community base approach, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the traditional leaders, the affected group representation and other stockholders (on ground humanitarian actors including the CCCM agency) to establish the Beneficiary Selection Committee (BSC) through which NRC will emphasize about the project objectives and beneficiary selection criteria. In order to strengthen the project impact, NRC will coordinate the response with other partners through the shelter sector in providing rapid and timely delivery and avoid gaps and duplication of efforts

project_name: Education in Emergency and ‘Better Learning Program’ in Gaza
project_objective: This project is a roll over project from 2019 HRP HPSE19-EDU-150687-1. The proposed project is in line with the education sub-cluster framework objectives 1 and 2 and aims to ensure that boys and girls have access to a protective and enabling educational experience in vulnerable MoEHE schools in the Gaza Strip. This project - fitting under a broad multi-year NRC education intervention applying psycho-social support in formal schools- is intended to focus specifically on Education in Emergency (EiE) based on the following three-fold approach: i) provision of technical support through the constitution of an Emergency Task Force under the Education sub-cluster to steer the EiE priorities; the mapping of teaching and non-teaching staff around the Designated Emergency Shelters (DES); the provision of tailored EiE training; and the delivery of pre-positioned educational kits to 20 school assigned Designated Emergency Shelter (DES); ii) implementation of the psycho-educational ‘Better Learning Program’ (BLP) reinforcing the system through the training of new cohorts of BLP Master Trainers at General and Educational Directors, Subject Supervisors and Head of Departments levels; contributing to the evidence based improved well-being and learning outcomes by finalizing the development of the M&E BLP toolkit; capacity building of teaching and non-teaching staff in 30 target MoEHE schools; provision of emergency kits to the schools, awareness sessions for parents; and provision of a ‘Supporting the Supporters’ package for teaching and non-teaching in need; and iii) Advocacy pursuing enhanced protection from violations of the right to education.

project_name: Life-saving and essential support for vulnerable populations in the West Bank and Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) will contribute to Health and Nutrition Cluster objective 1, as its purpose is to provide quality lifesaving and essential services to the most vulnerable Palestinian communities, while strengthening the local health system though emergency preparedness and other types of trainings in specialties lacking in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT). 

Through mobile clinics, volunteer specialist physicians will give direct medical aid to the most vulnerable, provide free medication, and organize referrals for over 200 cases in need to hospitals in East Jerusalem and Israel. Medical teams will travel to Gaza 8 times for two to three days, in coordination with the Palestinian Ministry of Health and local NGOs. PHRI doctors will also carry out 100 surgeries in Gaza, including of patients wounded during March of Return demonstrations. In the West Bank, mobile clinics of doctors will visit villages and areas with limited access to specialized care once a week, conducting health screenings in some of the clinics. In 2020, PHRI doctors will provide direct services to about 12,000 patients, 60% of whom are women and girls who will also benefit from specialized women-only clinics. 

For those patients who need treatment unavailable in the OPT and whose Israel-issued exit permits have been denied, and for health staff needing to exit the OPT for training, PHRI will intervene to reverse these denials in 350 cases. PHRI will sometimes use legal action combined with a range of advocacy tools to tackle individual cases and will also resort to strategic litigation to challenge general criteria according to which permits are denied. 

While providing medical aid, the intervention also aims to enhance preparedness within the health sector and reinforce the capacity of the Palestinian health system. Health professionals will be trained as per their own priorities, based on academic and practical gaps identified in collaboration with the Ministry of Health. Trainings will take place through hands-on surgical coaching, simulation-based coaching, and conferences. The surgery coaching in the key fields of orthopaedics, vascular and chest surgery (among others) will benefit around 50 Palestinian surgeons and health staff in Gaza. In between visits, PHRI’s surgeons continue to provide advice and support to their colleagues in Gaza via calls and emails. In addition, 20 medical professionals will participate in hands-on training at MSR, the Centre for Medical Simulation at Sheba Medical Centre in Israel. PHRI will also facilitate six large-scale medical conferences in the West Bank and Gaza with over 1,000 participants in total, bringing up-to-date medical knowledge to meet the needs of medical professionals.

The intervention will also address the Health and Nutrition Cluster strategic objective 2, carrying out advocacy to protect the right to health of the most vulnerable. Palestinian prisoners detained in Israel will be supported to overcome barriers to health and access medical treatment. Particular focus will also be given to persons with disabilities and children in PHRI’s advocacy work. Indeed, PHRI found out that over 60% of children in need of treatment outside of the OPT must travel without their parents who are denied permits. The presence of the parent, however, is essential during medical treatment, and compromise on this accompaniment constitutes a violation of his right to health. In 2020, PHRI will carry out a wide range of national and international advocacy activities to tackle this issue. Similarly, PHRI will advocate for the right to health of orthopedic patients from Gaza, most of them persons with disabilities, who require life-changing interventions such as spinal surgeries and whose permits have been consistently denied on grounds that the expertise for these surgeries is available in Gaza.

project_name: Increasing and strengthening emergency preparedness and response of Middle Area and Khan Yunis communities in Gaza, through NFI prepositioning and community empowerment
project_objective: The proposed action is aligned with the 2018-2020 HRP priorities in the Shelter/NFI sector for Gaza Strip (speciﬁcally Objectives 2 and 3): “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL” and “The capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued.” It is also in line with the Shelter/NFI cluster third objective in oPt: “Capacity to respond to natural or manmade hazards in a timely, eﬃcient and effective manner is increased”. The proposed project will increase preparedness and response capacity of Middle Area and Khan Yunis communities in case of future escalations of hostilities, speciﬁcally through the prepositioning of Emergency NFI kits for Internally Displaced People (IDPs) in Designated Emergency Shelters (DES) and Host Communities (hosting IDPs); establishment and capacity- building of a Community-based Emergency Response Network (CERN), based on existing community-based associations, providing of an Emergency assistance (including NFI distribution and protection mainstreaming) to IDPs and to Host Communities during escalations of hostilities. Based on assessments of the international community since 2014, and extensive consultation with key stakeholders, i.e. Shelter Cluster and Palestinian Authority in charge of 22 DES in the Gaza Strip, and currently ongoing project, the project will focus on Middle Area and Khan Yunis governorate. In case of hostilities’ escalation, it is expected that large-scale movement of individuals will occur from North East to Mid and South West of Middle Area and Khan Yunis, but also from Northern governorates (Gaza, North Gaza), based on past 2014 trends. In total, the project will beneﬁt 13,074, including 11,571 IDPs and 240 hosting households in Middle Area and Khan Yunis governorate: 2,270 IDPs and Host-community households are expected to be assisted by 2,270 Emergency NFI lots prepositioned during the project and distributed to affected households in case of crisis. Based on a standard calculation using as reference the average of 1 NFI Lot/HH, a minimum of 12,939 IDPs and Host individuals will beneﬁt from NFIs, based on Palestine’s standard average of 5,7 members/HH in GS. ACTED Project team expects to reach a higher target since some beneﬁciary HHs will not receive the full NFI Lot including 6 NFIs kits, but part of it, based on HHs’ proﬁle and vulnerability identiﬁed during rapid needs assessment following ACTED trigger for the deployment of Emergency Response; and 135 community members (including CBOs, CBPCs and community volunteers) will be engaged under the Community-based Emergency Response Network (CERN) and trained in Emergency Response. The project is supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach, with speciﬁc focus on women and vulnerable groups, and a strong Accountability to Affected Populations. Gender principles will be mainstreamed, CERN will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases with a particular focus to women and children issues i.e. GBV. ACTED Protection Oﬃcer will be focal point of the committees to receive and follow-up on cases. During and after the project, ACTED will remain the ﬁrst Emergency Responder for Middle Area and Khan Yunis governorate to trigger and  supervise the Emergency Response plan to be deployed by CERN members. This project builds on a similar project that ACTED is currently implementing in Rafah governorate, funded by OCHA. The currently ongoing project which aims at strengthening the capacity of Rafah community to face escalations of conﬂicts, is proving to be very successful and generated large engagement among Rafah community members and volunteers.

project_name: Integrated WASH services for vulnerable conflict and disease prone-affected communities in Warrap (Tonj East and Tonj North) and Lakes (Yirol East & Awerial)
project_objective:
This proposed project will address short- to-midterm WASH concerns of conflict, emergency and disease prone affected populations by providing integrated WASH services to vulnerable populations. This will improve water supply, sanitation and hygiene behavior for the affected populations and host families and reduce waterborne diseases. The project therefore intends to contribute to the reduction of avoidable mortality and morbidity through the provision of lifesaving integrated WASH services to vulnerable populations, especially women, girls, men and boys through a flexible, responsive and synergistic approach. 

This project will be targeting 40,000 individuals (Male: 4,800, Female: 9,600, Boys: 11,200 and Girls: 14,400) in Tonj East, Tonj North, Yirol East and Awerial 

Prior to project implementation, CCOSS will conduct, focus group discussions (FGD) with women, men, boys and girls at targeted community settlements will be conducted to get feedback on design, implementation, and monitoring of sanitation facilities, ensuring safety and mitigation of Protection / GBV risks, especially for females. These FGDs will also be utilized to trigger community action towards ending open defecation. 

The project will be achieved through the following interventions 
•	Construction of two stance block latrines at key health facilities, market places, and crowded settlement areas. 
•	Rehabilitation of non-functioning boreholes 
•	Clean- up campaigns to improve environmental sanitation at schools, health facilities, market centres and settlement areas since these are key areas where people gather and transmission of infectious diseases such as cholera is at a heightened risk. 
•	Conduct hygiene awareness campaigns each month of implementation to improve hygiene practices and health-seeking behaviour for WASH-related infectious diseases. The awareness shall also provide knowledge on appropriate behaviours to prevent and mitigate WASH related diseases and encourage good hygiene practices. 
•	Train community hygiene promoters (60% of them women) on hygiene awareness and promotion. These hygiene promoters will be identified and recruited through participatory approach with the community members playing a central role. 
•	Assess and identify at least 2000 most vulnerable households in Tonj East, Tonj North, Yirol East and Awerial for distribution of WASH non-food items (NFIs) such as jerry cans, buckets, PUR tabs and soap. A needs assessment will be conducted at the beginning of the project implementation phase

project_name: Preventing and responding to GBV in Mayendit County, Unity State and Yei River State
project_objective:
An increasing number of IDPs are continuing to explore options for return and relocation. Especially at the outset, people may return temporarily or seasonally to farm and access assistance and livelihoods. However, a highly militarized environment, and the frequent cattle raiding and revenge killings among the different clans and tribes exacerbate the risk of GBV in South Sudan. Similarly, displaced women and girls in the targeted locations are at risk of being raped, beaten or killed as they fetch water, firewood and other essential goods and services they need for domestic purposes. Furthermore, lack of recognition of GBV as violation of fundamental human rights perpetuates a culture of impunity throughout the country. Gender-based violence (GBV) cases, including sexual violence, are under-reported by survivors due to stigma, shame, low confidence in the rule of law to ensure justice for perpetrators, limited service availability, and reliance on informal justice structures which due to cultural norms can be an impediment to resolving some of the cultural issues around GBV. 
INTERSOS will therefore implement GBV prevention and response activities targeting 35,895 beneficiaries in Yei, Laniya, Morobo and Kajo-Keji counties in Yei River State, and in Mayendit County, Unity State in the following payams: Madol 1, Pabuong, and Malkuer. In its response activities, INTERSOS will provide to all survivors of GBV a safe and confidential environment in GBV corners in Primary Health Care Centers/Units (PHCC/PHCU) and Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS). In the latter, survivors will be able to easily access psychosocial support services in form of peer-to-peer support, individual case management and recreational activities. All activities will focus on overcoming trauma and psychosocial distress by strengthening individual coping mechanisms, resilience and social network. Cases will be identified through the Community Mobilizers and community-based protection networks and will be referred to trained and skilled GBV Caseworkers. In order to comprehensively address GBV cases, INTERSOS will both conduct/update a service mapping to set up/strengthen the referral pathway as well as provide in-kind support to survivors to ensure their basic needs are covered in the cases in which referrals might not feasible. To ensure uptake of services, INTERSOS will conduct community awareness about available GBV services. Awareness raising sessions, together with community dialogues, will also play a preventive role by encouraging discussions with the community around social norms/behaviors and gender.

project_name: Preventing, mitigation and responding to GBV in Duk County,Jonglei state
project_objective:
Prevailing social norms, patriarchal gender roles,localized conflict, a highly militarized environment, and the frequent cattle raiding and revenge killings among the different clans and tribes exacerbate the risk of GBV in South Sudan. Protection concerns such as generalized violence and insecurity, access to food, water and firewood, expose women to a high risk of GBV. There is, therefore, an urgent need to enhance GBV prevention efforts with additional strategies to mitigate risks. Furthermore, lack of recognition of GBV as violation of fundamental human rights continues a culture of impunity throughout the country.
Notwithstanding the advancing of the peace process, it is important to continue to raise awareness, reduce prevalent stigmas in the communities and increase identification and documentation of GBV cases as well as providing survivor’s access to psycho-social support and other services for their recovery and healing. SAADO's GBV intervention aims to ensure the provision of critical GBV related assistance and specialized services through an integrated/mainstreamed approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas and prevent and mitigate GBV risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience.  SAADO will provide psycho-social support services, women and girls friendly spaces, CBP preparedness and protection risk mitigation. Where the people of concern will access psycho-social support services in form of peer-to-peer support, individual case management and recreational activities. All activities will focus on overcoming trauma and psycho-social distress by strengthening their individual coping mechanism, resilience.Cases will be identified through the community engagement groups, local authorities, community based protection networks and community mobilizers and will be referred to trained and skilled GBV Caseworkers. Furthermore, SAADO will continue to support the economic empowerment of women through income generating activities that support their livelihood through mainstreaming GBV in to FSL activities currently being implemented in Duk County. A selected group of women that is interested in starting their own businesses will attend regular business skills training. In order to confront social norms that drive GBV, SAADO will specifically focus on engaging men and boys through EMAP strategy in its programming to become change agents for shifting gender roles. The discussion around gender and social norms will be facilitated in regular workshops, including influential community leaders to reflect on masculinity and the reasons behind their violence towards women, gender, sexuality, and substance abuse. In addition, SAADO will conduct awareness campaigns addressing specific problems affecting girls such as early and forced marriage and the low inclusion of girls in school. There will be specific awareness campaigns in primary and secondary schools for the promotion of girls’ enrollment and to reduce the drop out from schools due to early marriage and sexual exploitation and abuse.
SAADO will play an important role in strengthening coordination among humanitarian actors present in Duk County and will link coordination with the GBV Working group, SAADO is working on establishing SGBV referral pathway in Duk with Support from the national GBV Sub-Cluster 2019. The coordination is deemed fundamental to elaborate a common strategy for the GBV sector, including partners’ joint activities and to prevent duplication or overlapping. SAADO's GBV interventions will be aligned with the GBV Sub-cluster Strategy. To effectively respond to GBV, SAADO will collaborate with partners to contribute to the provision of the basic package of multi-sectoral GBV services at community level and build capacity of service providers to deliver quality GBV services in line with best practices and minimum standards for humanitarian settings

project_name: Strengthening emergency integrated response to life threatening malnutrition in remote areas of  Jonglei States, South Sudan
Emergency Health Interventions for Vulnerable Populations in Eastern Equatoria, Western Bahr El Ghazal, Northeren Bahr el Ghazal and Unity States
project_objective:
Increased access to integrated emergency lifesaving healthcare services
focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality for conflict-affected and vulnerable IDP, host
community and returnee households in Eastern Equatoria, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Western Bahr el Ghazal and Unity State . The interventions will include: 
1. Provision of essential primary health care services targeting the most vulnerable populations through various clinical packages (Hospital, PHCCs, PHCUs, mobile clinics and ICCM)
2. Implementation of outbreak investigation and response for epidemic prone diseases in locations where CARE works. 
3. Support to static Health facilities in Eastern Equitoria, and Unity States particularly on essential medical supplies and capacity building in line with the strategies and priorities of the health cluster 
4. Mainstream accountability to the affected populations.

project_name: Improve access to safe, lifesaving and appropriate shelter and non-food items to returnees, newly displaced persons, non-displaced persons in host communities in Torit, Rumbek Center, Yei, Cueibet, Kajokeji, Morobo, Lainya and Magwi Counties to enhance their resilience to respond to new shocks and rebuild their lives
project_objective: TF seeks to improve access to safe, lifesaving and appropriate S/NFIs to returnees, newly IDPs, and affected non displaced persons. The project will equip beneficiaries with skills and knowledge on disaster risk reduction to enhance their resilience to cope with new shocks. TF will also support affected communities with durable S/NFIs solutions to rebuild their lives including training women and girls on making Fuel Efficient Stoves (FES). Vulnerable youth will be trained on making bricks, beds, chairs and tables using local materials. S/NFIs Solutions training will be complemented with environment awareness to mitigate negative effects of climate change. The project will target Torit, Rumbek Center, Kajokeji, Yei, Morobo and Lainya, Magwi, Yirol West and Cueibet for GIK and CBI. GIK will target locations with new displacements and no functional markets while CBI will focus on locations experiencing spontaneous returnees, increased number of affected non-displaced people and have functional markets. For CBI, TF will work jointly with SPEDP, PAH and LCED. A total of 25000 (18000 F) beneficiaries will be reached with GIK and CBI intervention. For GIK, a total of 22000 beneficiaries are targeted as follows: Rumbek Center (2000), Torit (1900), Kajokeji (4500), Yei (2500), Morobo (2100), Lainya (3000), Magwi (3000), and Cueibet (3000). For CBI intervention, a total of 3000 beneficiaries are targeted as follows: Rumbek Centre (700), Yei (600), Torit (900), Magwi (400), and Cueibet (400). Totals for each county being as follows: Torit: 2800(1800 F); Rumbek Centre: 2700(2200 F) Kajokeji: 4500 (3000 F); Yei: 3100 (2000 F); Morobo: 2100 (1500 F); Lainya: 3000 (2300 F); Magwi: 3400 (2500 F) and Cueibet: 3400 (2700 F). Due to high level and concentration of S/NFIs needs in these locations, TF project staffs will dedicate 8 weeks in each location with the communities to better understand their pressing S/NFIs needs and coping mechanisms, jointly craft alternative S/NFIs durable solutions, train community based S/NFIs Committees on resilience-enhancing messaging such as Housing Land and Property (HLP). The project prioritizes safety, dignity, inclusive participation and encouraging complaints and feedback. A key focus for this intervention is AAP through CFM embedded in project activities. CFM will be established upon contact with the affected community and during implementation process to receive, acknowledge and address complaints. Protection is mainstreamed through HLP Messaging, safety audits, sharing GBV information and referrals, training women and girls on FES and engaging protection partners while implementing CBI activities to mitigate potential violence as a result of CBI.TF will liaise with the SFPs and NFIs partners to coordinate the response, share experience and ideas for better and cost effective response. To integrate the response, TF already has funding support for FSL, Wash and Protection for Yei, Cueibet and Kajokeji. S/NFIs staffs will participate in Joint Missions with Nutrition partners (ARC) in Kajokeji to deliver malaria messaging, distribute mosquito nets to mothers with children under 5 years and conduct life skills training at Nutrition outreach and stabilization centres. S/NFIs staffs will work with FSL partners in Kajokeji, Lainya, Magwi, Rumbek Centre, Torit, Cueibet and Yei to introduce the concept of FES and Briquettes to farmers and fishermen groups and to mitigate misuse of mosquito nets (for fishing and fencing gardens). In locations at risk of Malaria, diarrhoea, Pneumonia, Skin Infections, Ebola and HIV and AIDS, TF staffs will work closely with health partners to deliver lifesaving messages. S/NFIs intervention will be coordinated through SFPs based in Juba, Rumbek and Torit. To ensure an integrated response, TF will share information, coordinate and participate in joint missions with CCCM partners in Kajokeji.

project_name: Protection des enfants non accompagnés et ceux victimes ou a risque de violences dans les situations humanitaires
project_objective:
L’insécurité alimentaire, affectant 1 haïtien sur 3, et la précarité économique menace le bien-être des familles et de la communauté. Les situations humanitaires exacerbent les vulnérabilités déjà existantes chez les enfants et le stress quotidien au sein de la famille engendre la violence envers les enfants. L’insécurité alimentaire/économique (suite à la situation socio-politique) peut contribuer également à la séparation des enfants de leurs parents. Les enfants sont à risque de placement auprès de tierces personnes lorsque leurs parents ne peuvent plus subvenir à leurs besoins. Cette précarité augmente aussi le risque de migration pour les enfants – soit pour aller à l’école en République Dominicaine ou même pour y chercher du travail.
Ce projet vise à fournir une prise en charge holistique pour les enfants non accompagnés ainsi que ceux à risque et/ou touché par la violence dont les violences sexuelles suite à la crise socio-politique et la crise alimentaire qui affectent tout le pays a des niveaux différents.  Trop souvent, les principales victimes pendant des crises sont les enfants. Cette prise en charge se fera à travers un paquet des services dont la gestion de cas, l’appui psychosocial, la recherche et la réunification familiale, la réinsertion a l’école et l’assistance médicale selon les besoins individuels. Pour renforcer les capacités des parents de prendre en charge leurs enfants en toute sécurité le projet supportera les transferts monétaires au profit de 1,000 familles vulnérables.      
La prise en charge sera adaptée selon les besoins des enfants et en tenant compte l’âge et le sexe de l’enfant. Elle requiert une équipe multidisciplinaire qui est composée des agents de protection de l’IBESR et de la BPM, Polifront, et des travailleurs sociaux des ONGs locales qui interviennent dans la protection des enfants et qui constituent des maillons importants dans la chaine de protection de l’enfant en Haiti. 
Les réseaux communautaires existants participeront dans la sensibilisation pour une prise de conscience des acteurs et familles qui a pour but de susciter l’engagement communautaire pour la prévention de la violence et de la séparation des enfants afin d’avoir l’engagement communautaire et la fonctionnalité du mécanisme de protection informel en renforçant les cellules d’alerte et de référencement des cas de protection.

project_name: Integrated Response to Life Threatening Malnutrition to crisis affected population in South Sudan
project_objective:
During January to April 2020, food security situation is expected to deteriorate throughout Jonglei state, and Crisis outcomes are expected to persist in Uror, Pochalla and Twic East Counties. Admissions to Tearfund Feeding Centres continue to rise even in the post-harvest season when typically, malnutrition rates dip as the dry season brings improved access for nutrition and health services as well as humanitarian assistance, and a reduction in morbidity and outbreaks of disease. The high levels of food insecurity seen among children under 5 in the targeted areas can be partially attributed to the scarcity of food and the consequent lack of variety in diet. This is further compounded by the lack of knowledge of minimum dietary diversity required. 
Tearfund is the sole organization supporting nutrition interventions in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla.  Tearfund is currently responding to the crisis in Uror, Twic East and Pochalla, supporting 26 Feeding Centres and 5 Stabilization Centres. This project will continue to address high rates of GAM through the provision of Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP) services, thus alleviating malnutrition and reducing susceptibility to other health issues, including water-borne diseases. As children under 5 and pregnant and lactating women and girls are the most vulnerable to MAM and SAM, these individuals will be the primary target group for this intervention. A total of 6548 children under 5 will be targeted for treatment of SAM (1,226 Pochalla, 1,384 Twic East, 3,937 Uror). A further 21,888 children will be targeted for treatment of MAM (4,376 Pochalla, 6,922 Twic East, 10,590 Uror). As part of the MAM and IYCF component, a total of 29,684 PLWs will be targeted (17,679 Pochalla, 11,059 Twic East, 16,736 Uror).
Tearfund’s MIYCN component will address the issue of malnutrition and encourage prevention through mothers’ groups both within the community and at the feeding centres. Furthermore, Tearfund’s wider nutrition programme integrates WASH, GBV and FSL components, including training on kitchen gardening, which increases access to more diverse food items.  Without this response, GAM rates would inevitably rise and morbidity and mortality would increase.

project_name: Protection of Vulnerable Women and Girls Survivors of GBV in the Gaza Strip Through Coordinated and Multisectoral Responses
project_objective: The project objective is “Improved protection and respect of rights of acutely vulnerable women 18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years survivors of GBV and increased access to essential services based on IHL and IHRL.” WAC partners with RCS4GS and WEFAQ to make incremental changes in situation of women and girls, community and duty bearers as reflected in project outcomes:1. Vulnerable women>18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years manifested well-being, knowledge and confidence, good health status, economic self-reliance, legal enablement and protection; 2. Targeted communities actively engaged in GBV prevention and protection; and 3. Duty bearers are accountable to vulnerable women >18-59 and >59 years and girls <18 years and CBOs and increasingly act to protect them and reduce incidence and impact of human rights violations against them. The project targets 6693 direct beneficiaries (3775 women and 1335 men>18-59 and>59 years, 1343 girls and 240 boys<18 years) identified based on defining vulnerability and acutely vulnerable groups according to their location, status, gender, protection risks and needs severity. Beneficiaries are selected from most affected locations in North (Arab Maslakh Beit Lahia, Siafa, Jabalia east in Ezbet Abed Rabo and Jabal Rayyes, Ezbet Beit Hanoun, Beit Hanoun ARA) handled by RCS4GS; Gaza (Gaza City: Shijaia and Zaitoon, Juhor adDik, Sabra, Daraj) and Deir ALBalah (Bureij camp, Nuseirat camp, Mussadar, Deir Al Balah) managed by WAC; and Khan Younis (Bani Suhaila, Fukhari, Qarara, Abasan AlKabira) and Rafah (Shuket Elsoofi, Rafah camp, Rafah, Mawasi) handled by WEFAQ. The project links to HRP2020 Strategic Objective 1 and Protection Cluster Objective 2, and standard activities/indicators. Partners introduce an effective partnership model that consolidate their human capital to implement responsive, remedial and environment-building activities to address urgent needs of women/girls reflected in HNO/ HRP 2020 and achieve project objective/outcomes. Activities are: group psychological support and recreational days for 1056 women and 528 girls; individual psychological counseling to 150 women and 75 girls; referral of traumatized 63 women and 18 girls; psycho-therapy for 254 couples; group legal counselling to 1056 women and 528 girls; individual legal counseling to 120 women and 30 girls; legal representation to 180 women and 45 girls; emergency hotline for (420) women and (170) early married girls; emergency health care for 540 women and 240 girls; cancer diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration for 90 women survivors of cancer; case management to 30 women; dignity kits for 300 women and 90 girls; training and grants to 48 women; awareness for 1056 women, 1056 men, 528 girls and 528 boys; training of 25 women and 25 men of local women CBOs; periodical monitoring and coordination with GBV humanitarian key actors; and 3 advocacy initiatives. This project is in line with HRP multiyear strategy and “do no harm” principle. It is designed based on documenting lessons learned from community engagement (CwC,AAP) like 9 community meetings, 18 FGDs, complaints mechanism, 3 radio ads, 9900 brochures, 3 fact sheets, 9 press releases and pre post evaluation. Partners follow 4W activity tracking matrix to coordinate with organizations executing activities in project locations in a way that ensures humanitarian needs are met, complementarity with ongoing projects, resilience of beneficiaries, participatory monitoring GENDER/AGE differences, environmentally neutral, protection mainstreaming, innovation process and principles, inclusion of WWDs/GWDs, security and full access to project services

project_name: Providing elective surgeries to patients registered on the waiting list at the Ministry of Health – Gaza Strip - OPT
project_objective:
The idea of the project is to provide surgical services to patients on the waiting lists at the MoH, this idea meets the 1st HC SO & the 2nd HRP SO, adding to HNO 2020. Statistics of MoH 2019 indicated that 9,000 patients are registered on the waiting list including 2,500 patients in need of ENT surgeries. Knowing that the HC is planning to target 4500 patients in 2020.
The project aims to conduct 1500 moderate & major electives surgeries targeting women, men, girls, boys, elderly & PWD from all over the Gaza Strip (GS), representing 33% from the targeted beneficiaries in 2020. The services will include medical examination, lab. & radiological services, surgical operation, hospitalization & medication. Psychological support services will be provided to patients of all categories, especially children pre & post-op.
To facilitate the access of beneficiaries from different locations in the GS, the services will be provided in 2 UHWC’s health facilities: Al-Awda Hospital–Northern GS & Al Awda Health Center–Southern GS.
This project is a continuation of a previous project funded by HF which targeted 827 patients from the MoH waiting lists in 2018-2019. By the implementation of this project the No. of beneficiaries from surgical op. services at UHWC’s facilities will be increased from 5494 in 2018 to 6994 in 2020.
Upon the importance of involving the local community in determining the needs & priorities, the UHWC held 5 FGs in 2019 targeting different categories of gender & age groups. The result of these FGs indicated that there is a need for the patients who are registered on the waiting lists at MoH to undergo surgical operations in order to reduce their suffering & prevent complications.
Another 5 FGs will be held in the mid of the project to evaluate the first phase in order to adjust the project activities if any deviations are found in achieving the objectives. Moreover, 5 FGs will be held at the end of the project targeting beneficiaries form the project with different gender & age groups including PWD to assess the project activities & measure immediate impact on them. While 100 questionnaires will be distributed to the beneficiaries to measure their satisfaction. This feedback will be used as direction to design future interventions.
There is also complaint boxes in each health facility to receive the beneficiaries’ complaints & to take the necessary action to address them.
To achieve the principle of protection, the project will target different age groups, including boys, girls, men & women, as well as elderly & PWD, without discrimination. To respond to gender needs, medical staff of both sexes (M & F) will be available. Moreover, pediatric surgeons will be available to respond to the age needs. At the level of PWD, the environment of Al Awda Hospital is prepared to receive them.
To meet the principle of (DO No Harm), the cases will be targeted upon the list that will be sent by the MoH, where the project will ensure that the beneficiaries are not harmed during the provision of the services, by providing quality health services under the supervision of highly qualified specialists. Adding to providing stable psychological situation for the beneficiaries by the provision of psychological support pre & post-op. A special guide pre & post-op will be distributed to all cases. To achieve the highest level of Do No Harm, a training course will be held for 12 persons from the medical staff in order to train them on the Sphere Standards related to health services & the principle of Do No Harm.
To reach accurate & easily accessible information, HIS system will be used, as UHWC is currently working on designing it & by 2020 it will be operational. In terms of documenting project activities, photography & audio-visual report will be prepared taking into consideration the dignity & privacy of patients.
It is worth mentioning that the activities of this humanitarian intervention has been designed according to Sphere Standards.

project_name: Health under protection (HUP): Emergency health and nutrition assistance to people living in communities whose rights are inadequately protected in the West Bank (WB).
project_objective:
CARE/partners (Palestine Medical Relief Society “PMRS” and Health Work Committees “HWC”) will respond to the  health needs  with a comprehensive intervention that combines elements of direct service delivery to the identified vulnerable communities, with special focus on women and children, elderly, and people with disabilities. The proposed intervention will be targeting 37 vulnerable communities in the WB that were identified by CARE/partners and the HNC (including Ministry of Health-MoH) during the recent HRP 2020. CARE/partners, with  close coordination with MOH, will provide life-saving/basic health services in targeted communities in the WB through the use of mobile clinics/teams that will deliver basic curative and preventive level II PHC services, including women’s health, reproductive health (ante and post-natal care, obstetric care, family planning, etc.), general practice care (GP), health awareness with focus on communities’ urgent needs and priorities, basic lab tests, home visits, children health, in addition to the Psychosocial/mental health services that will be provided as part of the mobile services package. The team will be trained on basic life support and first aid and will be provided with emergency kits that enable them to respond to emergency incidents in these communities while working in the clinics to ensure lifesaving before transferring to the hospitals. The project will build the capacity/preparedness of the targeted communities to better respond to emergencies through conducting first aid training for selected community members (Focal Point) and equip them with necessary first aid kits.
The protection specific activity aims to report all incidents of violations of IHL and IHRL that are related to access to health such as access of staff to the communities, access of patients to health services, injuries due to settlers and IF violence, etc. This will help working toward coordinated advocacy, mainly through AIDA, for accountability for those violations with HNC and relevant stakeholders/actors. Moreover, CARE/partners will identify, report and refer identified GBV cases in line with the national referral mechanism. CARE will continue working with trained community representatives (focal points) and project staff to report/refer these violations using agreed upon mechanism. 
The project is designed in full coordination and cooperation with other actors mainly MOH, HNC, Medico, and UNRWA. CARE had MoU with UNRWA to provide the health services to refugees in Barta’a enclave and in Khallet an Nu’man in Bethlehem, and other locations since many of the targeted communities have big number of refugees and UNRWA can’t reach these communities. A new agreement will be signed once the project approved, to l ensure better use of the resources, covering some of the gaps resulted in seizing UNRWA mobile clinics, avoid duplication, ensure synergy and complementarity with other actors, and maximize the number of beneficiaries/communities in need in the most effective and equitable manner.
