project_name: Mitigation the farmer struggles and  suffering resulting from the Israel's  occupation and settlers attacks in area C in West of Salfit
project_objective:
The project aims to mitigation the farmer struggles and suffering resulting from the 
Israel's occupation and settlers attacks in area C in West of Salfit by targeting farmers 
who highly vulnerable and lack access to basic services, The specific objective is to increase the well being and income of women and men engaged in small-scale agriculture in vulnerable communities through improved agricultural and access to land and market. The project support 1647 individual beneficiaries  (840 M, 807 F) of the communities and families to build their capacity to absorb shocks, including access to land through facilitate these essential services through reclamation 150 dunums of agricultural land, construct 6 kilo of agricultural roads and rehabilitate 7 water cisterns in Kafr al Dik, Bruqin and Deir Ballut to ensure threats to food security, income and life in general are minimized. More precisely, this will contribute to: 
1- Support farmers’ resilience in the targeted locations to be able to withstand settlers 
attacks and the occupation practices on their land's productivity. 
2- Improve farmers' livelihood sources in the targeted locations. 
3- Prevent farms and trees from wild pigs which mainly brought up by settlers. which become an extra risk for farmers mainly women when attending their lands
4- Direct access to food by unemployed through working in agricultural land. 
The entire area are severely suffers from occupation threat and settlers attack like land confiscations, so the entire targeted communities will have access to better and more water, better access to their land through the rehabilitated roads, which will serve as well as alternative and saver roads whenever the main roads are closed by the occupation and its settlers.

project_name: Emergency Housing Rehabilitation for Women Headed Households and Vulnerable Families in Area C
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project over 12 months is to respond to the immediate shelter needs of vulnerable populations in Area C communities surrounding areas A and B of the West Bank. This response will be through self-help approach for the most vulnerable families to provide shelter repairs and transitional shelter solutions close to existing homes, in order to: 1) Promote self-reliance, maintain, and support most vulnerable families who live with the effect of violence, coercion, and deprivation with shelter related solutions. 2) Enhancing the protection and reducing the likelihood of displacement or forced eviction. 3) Contributing in solving the problem of overcrowding houses by creating new spaces through rearrangement to ensure privacy and dignity 4) promoting more environmental friendly housing, cost and energy efficient building practices and reducing the cost of living by adopting green approaches. 5) Extend the life span of existing shelters; insight of the nullity of the issuance of building permits in Area C. 6) supporting access to job opportunities in Area C and creating short-term employment opportunities. 7) Better understanding of the scope of the need for urgent housing rehabilitation in Area C and the way to address them, advocacy and awareness raising trainings. Thus, complying with the second HRP strategic objectives “SO2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”. And complying with the shelter cluster strategic objectives “Vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns are supported to meet basic needs and enhance their coping capacity” and “Capacity to respond to natural or manmade hazards in a timely, efficient and effective manner is increased”.
This project complies with PHC’s Rehabilitation Program objectives, aiming at contributing of elimination some poverty effects on vulnerable women HH’s, improving the quality of the proper housing stock, reducing land designation for housing and infrastructure by restoring the existing housing stock and improving the social, economic, and health conditions for the beneficiaries. The project will provide urgent housing rehabilitation to 50 FHH or vulnerable families in Area C of the West Bank whose shelter is unfit for weather conditions, overcrowded, and/or unsafe as described hereafter.

project_name: Capacity Development Support for Integrated Humanitarian Mine Action in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The project will address current gaps in the establishment of a comprehensive Ukrainian
humanitarian mine action response. The project will provide strategic capacity
development and direct technical support for humanitarian mine action in Eastern Ukraine
to enhance integrated planning, coordination, and operational efficiencies amongst the
different humanitarian mine action stakeholders presently active in the Oblasts of
Donetsk and Luhansk. Specifically, technical operational advice; survey and marking;
information management; mine risk and survivor assistance; and linking mine action to
early recovery and development in accordance with Humanitarian-Development Nexus
concept will be the focus of activities.

project_name: Addressing urgent protection and psychosocial needs of children and adolescents through mobile response in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Plan International’s mobile programming has been effectively used in its German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) funded project in 6 LGAs of Borno State. Plan proposes using the mobile unit approach in the four targeted LGAs of Borno. The mobile response ensures the deployment of the mobile team within 72 hours of a specific request, or of a report from relevant humanitarian clusters groups of acute needs. In cases of first response, the mobile unit will be deployed for a period of 6 and up to 12 weeks to provide urgent lifesaving assistance including provision of cash transfer. The mobile team currently is based in Maiduguri and serves LGAs within Borno state. They are being deployed in Kaga, Damboa, Bama, and four different locations of Maiduguri Metropolitan City-Jere, Madinatu, Bolori and Teachers village camp. The team can also be stationed in other field locations like Mubi, Dikwa, Pulka or Gwoza and be deployed from there. The mobile protection team will conduct a participatory rapid needs assessment, engaging the affected population to identify immediate needs. The outcome of the rapid assessment will be used to determine the line of response and also to identify existing community based services. Based on the findings of the assessment a rapid referral pathway will be developed to guide the provision of protection services to the children and adolescents. The referral pathway will be disseminated among stakeholders and will be used to coordinate actors providing services on the ground especially during the first line of response which will include provision of direct case management services. 
In addition, the mobile team will set up rapid complaints and feedback response mechanism to address issues of protection of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) as well as advocate for services that are needed and not available. Communities will be engaged to identify the most suitable and safe mechanisms to raise complaints and provide feedback on both services and operations of the mobile team and other available community services. The mobile team will provide targeted response for high-risk children including children with no suitable caregivers, children at risk of abuse in their current care arrangements, and UASC

project_name: CMAM and IYCF interventions in Borno
project_objective: The purpose of the project is to reach the most vulnerable children and their households in Borno by providing timely integrated (nutrition, protection, water, sanitation and hygiene) assistance to unaccompanied and separated children, malnourished children, and other children with protection risks. Nutrition activities will save the lives of the most vulnerable malnourished children and PLWs, by providing treatment for SAM cases and prevention of malnutrition through protection, promotion and support of IYCF practices. WASH interventions will be implemented I locations where SC is implementing nutrition program to ensure that the population has access to clean, safe water and sanitation facilities and promote essential hygiene messaging to reduce communicable diseases that exacerbate malnutrition

project_name: Emergency response to protect students from vulnerable communities in the West Bank’s Area C through emergency school rehabilitations and psychosocial support interventions.
project_objective:
The proposed project (approved 2019 HRP HPSE19-EDU-150611-1) aims to provide emergency response to the most vulnerable schools in Area C through integrated and targeted protection.
The response will be implemented by upgrading the educational environment in schools through the rehabilitation of classrooms and WASH facilities. It will also supply and construct new classrooms in overcrowded schools to facilitate separate spaces for students from different grades. Activities will also target the schools’ staff and parents to improve their capacities in delivering knowledge as well as dealing with risk reduction; risk mitigation (settlers attacks, clashes and natural hazards); and to give the students the needed support in the face of these risks and hazards (evacuation procedures, ﬁrst aid, etc).
Simultaneously, the project will respond to psychosocial issues faced by students and teachers alike as a result of the coercive environment they are subjected to. The proposed psychosocial response will be innovative; various artistic and recreational tools targeting students, teacher and parents, will be adopted to ensure the maximum effect on the targeted students.
The proposed interventions are in line with Education Cluster 2020 Strategic Objective 1 ""Increase equitable and safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children” and objective 2 ""Most vulnerable schools are supported in responding to emergencies through preventive measures, catch-up classes and school-based psychosocial services"".
The project uses a community-based approach, with students (girls and boys) and teachers participating in all stages of the project including at the assessment, design and implementation stages. Hence, the students, teachers as well as parents’ fears, needs and ideas will be discussed and analysed to inform effective technical and psychosocial activities considering gender and age disaggregated data, resulting in adapted assistance.
As outlined, the proposed intervention ensures protection mainstreaming as it is guided by protection principles and considers safety and dignity; meaningful access; accountability to affected population (AAP) as well as participation and empowerment.

project_name: Emergency Medical Assistance to Host and displaced populations in Borno State
project_objective:
Médecins du Monde France (MdM) responds to the emergency situation resulting from the violent armed conflict in the North-eastern part of Nigeria, in order to improve access to free comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC) services including Nutrition, Mental Health and Gender Based Violence (GBV) services for the most vulnerable conflict affected populations in Borno State. In terms of operational approach, MdM first considers direct support to MoH and SEMA, wherever a health facility is still available or functional, to reinforce the health management capacities and maintain quality of care. Indeed, MdM is supporting two MoH HFs in Azir and Gumsuri, in Damboa LGA, with provision of drugs and medical equipment, basic rehabilitation, and capacity building and incentives to MoH staff. 

Where there is no health facility, MdM set up a temporary clinic to cover the essential and most urgent healthcare needs of the affected population in IDP settlements and informal camps in Maiduguri, Jere and Damboa LGAs. During the calendar year 2020, MdM intends to run five clinics: two in Maiduguri LGA (Kawar Maila and Garba Buzu IDP camps), one in Jere LGA (El-Miskin IDP camp) and two in Damboa LGA (Hausari and GTS IDP camps). Also, MdM has an Emergency Response Team that has complete mobility to deploy to respond to emergencies (epidemics outbreaks and influx of populations). 

Each clinic provides a comprehensive package of PHC services which include: 
- PHC: medical curative consultations, sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and immunization. 
- Nutrition services: MdM runs an OTP in Garba Buzu and Kawar Maila clinics. In all clinics, MdM screens children under five and refers SAM cases to nutrition partners for their admission in OTP or SC. 
- Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services: individual counselling, group support sessions and referral to secondary healthcare facilities. 
- GBV services: medical care for GBV survivors (Clinical Management of Rape), MHPSS counselling, and case management by social workers.

project_name: Emergency Education and MHPSS
project_objective: It is estimated that 80 per cent of 282,360 students (145,867 boys and 136,493 girls) registered at UNRWA schools in the 2019/20 school year in Gaza require assistance in overcoming a variety of challenges, including poverty, additional learning needs, access restrictions and electricity shortages at home. Recurrent hostilities and the blockade continue to have a deleterious impact on the learning environment for Palestine refugee children in Gaza, who are accommodated in 276 schools, 70 per cent of which operate on a double-shift basis. In response, the Agency-wide Education in Emergencies (EiE) approach provides inclusive, equitable, quality and safe education to Palestine refugee children and youth in times of emergencies. In addition to implementing the EiE approach across all UNRWA schools in Gaza, UNRWA will: (i) recruit and train 600 support teachers to provide learning support to more than 70,000 students in grades 3 and 4 who are struggling to meet minimum academic standards in Arabic and mathematics, out of them, more than 17,000 students will also receive remedial materials to assist their learning; (ii) ensure that 80 percent of students have access to basic school and learning materials through the distribution of basic stationary; and (iii) ensure that all students have an access to mental health and psychosocial support at school.

project_name: Improving accessibility to a comprehensive health services for women with breast cancer in Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
The main problem that this project seeks to address is “Limited access of breast cancer patients to timely, well-designed and high-quality breast cancer care”.

The project aims at improving the accessibility of women at risk of having or developing breast cancer to vital preventive, diagnostic and treatment services, leading to an improved 5-year survival rate. This is to be achieved at all levels of service: primary, secondary and tertiary, as follows:

Primary care: this begins at the community level and covers awareness of early signs and symptoms, through conducting organized health educational workshops at the community level and also other awareness activities that include disseminating brochures and releasing media materials.

Secondary care: this involves advanced diagnosis and staging for women referred from the communities and women visiting health centers (mainly the biopsy, and histopathology) in coordination with the partner PRCS through its hospitals.

Tertiary care: treatment, follow-up, and rehabilitation. Treatment with medications will be provided in coordination with the Ministry of Health. Rehabilitation and Post-op care services will be provided by PRCS including Physiotherapy and PSS activities. Distribution of services will take place in a way that geographic coverage will be maintained.

project_name: Availing PreventivemPrimary and Referral health to Refugees and immediate host communities
project_objective: The project seek to build up and expand the ongoing the currative, preventive and promotive primary and secondary health care services (including SRH and MHPSS services) to refugees and surounding host communities. Outreach services will be provided through Community Health Workers and Community Psychosocial volunteers. Facility based primary healthcare (including MHPSS and SRH services) are implemented through 22 camp based PHCs and HPs which cater for the needs for women, men boys and girls; services provided are aligned to the essential health service package endorsed by the health sector and MoH. Medical referral support to access secondary, and tertiary health care will be provided for 50% of the camps. Outbreak/emergency preparedness and response will be strengthened, procurement of medicine and medical supplies including the contingency stocks will be undertaken. Health sector coordination will be supported through CHWG, MHPSS WG, field coordination and other sector coordination forums.

project_name: Reduction of morbidity and mortality through provision of water, sanitation, environmental health and hygiene services in Rubkona and Guit, Unity and Aweil West and Aweil North, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, and Yei, Central Equatoria, South Sudan
project_objective:
Despite the R-ARCSS and opportunities for recovery, the cumulative impacts of conflict, destroyed livelihoods and persistant insecurity meant that 7.1 million people were in need of humanitarian assistance in South Sudan. IDPs still remain in PoCs due to uncertain security conditions preventing return to home locations with Bentiu PoC having the highest population of 115,960 people (IOM DTM Oct 2019). Intercommunal tensions continue to result in displacement particularly in Rubkona, Guit and Koch. Continued conflict between armed groups in Yei has resulted in displacements. An estimated 5,712,000 people did not have access to water and sanitation services in 2019 and only 29% have population could access an improved water source (HNO 2019) and these trends are likely to continue in 2020. In Unity, high morbidity is due to illness from waterborne diseases as much of the water and sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed by conflict. This results in high malnutrition rates. Bentiu PoC remains the most populated IDP site in the country and there is a need to continue to support WASH services on site so IDPs have access to water, environmental health services, and sanitation services.. With displacement, many households do not have access to latrines leading to open defecation. NBeG, remains one of the locations of morbidity of 157/1,000 in children under-5 in South Sudan compared to a national level of 99.2/1,000 (WHO 2017). As well has poor health services this is also due to poor access to sanitation and hygiene practices. In DRC, there is currently an EVD outbreak and for locations in South Sudan bordering DRC there is critical risk of EVD spreading. The government health services are unable to deliver adequate risk prevention activities and poor water and sanitation infrastructure and practices on IPC and hygiene mean increase risks of EVD. 
The aim of this programme is to reduce the risks of morbidity and malnutrition to conflict affected and vulnerbal populations through rehabilitation, operation and maintenance of water upply and sanitation facilities and improving hygiene behaviours. Where Concern implements Nutrition programmes, nutrition beneficiaries will be spefically targeted to reduce risks of waterborne illness causing malnutrition. Concern will provide 
WASH services in Sector 5, Bentiu PoC and in BBR locations in Rubkona urban areas and Guit. In Leer, Concern aims to establish a partnership with Coalition for Humanity to support WASH interventions. In Bentiu PoC sex-segregated latrines and bathing shelters will be constructed and BBR locations an adapted CLTS for emergencies will be implemented. Environmental health activities will foucs on rubbish collections in Bentiu PoC and Rubkona urban areas. Hygiene promotion will involve house-to-house visits and mass campaigns implemented by HHPs and volunteers from Concern’s Nutrition programmes such as CNVs, lead mothers and Male Change Agents. In NBeG, this WASH response will be linked with Concern’s Health and Nutrition programme. Safe water access, sex-segregated latrines and medical waste disposal facilities will be ensured at health facilities. An adapted CLTS approach will be implemented in communities. Hygiene promotion will be conducted by CNVs, lead mothers and Male Change Agents from Concern’s Nutrition programme. In Yei, Concern will focus on WASH in health facilities to reduce risks of through providing improve water and sanitation infrastructure and in communities supporting improved hygiene practices with an emphasis on IPC of EVD and other infectious diseases. WASH activities will focus on reducing security, safety and protection risks when accessing water points and using latrines. Concern will continue to  be the Unity State WASH Cluster co-coordinator to coordinate the overall WASH response and coordinating with state clusters in NBeG and Central Equatoria and the national WASH Cluster.

project_name: Improved food security and dietary diversity to vulnerable conflict affected and food insecure populations in Aweil West and Aweil North, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Bentiu PoC and Guit, Unity and Juba PoC, Central Equatoria South Sudan 2019
project_objective:
Despite the R-ARCSS, 6.45 million people are currently at crisis level or worse of food insecurity. By December 2019 it is anticipated that 50.5% of the population will be at Crisis or Emergency Levels of food insecurity (IPC Aug 2019). The high levels of food insecurity are due to prolonged conflict severely disrupting food production and livelihoods opportunities, erratic weather patterns and deeply rooted poverty. Macroeconomic decline and high inflation have severely decreased households’ purchasing power, with vulnerable households reliant on markets to purchase food commodities. Beginning of June 2019, heavy rains , resulting in massing floods and destruction of infrastructure (schools, water and sanitation), cropps and shelters in NBeG and Unity (OCHA, August 2019). Guit is currently at Crisis level of food security, and will remain at this level through May to July 2019. cThere is also the potential for returnees into areas that have seen some stabilisation recently such as NBeG and some areas of Unity who will be reliant on humanitarian assistance to reestablish their livelihoods as they have lost productive assets during the conflict. 

While the programme will not directly support FSL Cluster objective 1, Concern will coordinate with WFP who will partner with other organisations to identify completary activities such as supporting food production and improving nutrition practices. Concern will also partner with WFP to implement cash for assets in Aweil West and Aweil North, NBeG where beneficiaries will receive cash transfers to meet needs during the hunger period for constructing community prioritise assets. The response will support achieving the FSL Cluster objectives 2 and 3. For objective 2, Concern will support vulnerable IDP, returnee and host community households with emergency access to agricultural and fishing inputs to improve food production and access to nutritious foods. In Aweil West and Aweil North, NBeG, Concern will continue to provide access to seeds through voucher fairs where beneficiaries will have more choice to purchase seeds according to their preferences. Community Agricultural Extension Workers and lead farmers will be supported to train vulnerable farmers on Climate Smart Agriculture, biopesticide production and post-harvest handling. Concern will support dry season vegetable production to support income generation opportunities and access to nutritious foods. In Juba and Bentiu PoC, Concern will build on its approach of nutrition gardens to support improving dietary diversity through training lead mothers on sack gardening where space is limited in PoCs and they will train Mother-to-Mother Support Groups. Focus will be on households with members in OTP and TSFP. In Guit, Concern having supported vegetable gardens to improve access to nutritious foods will expand its FSL interventions considering the gaps in FSL support and most of the population being dependent on food assistance. Vegetable production and fishing will be supported to provide income generation opportunities and increase dietary diversity. 

The response will contribute to cluster objective 3 through seed fairs for providing emergency access to seeds under objective 2 where local markets will be supported in NBeG. Although fragile, the relatively stable security situation in NBeG allows for Concern’s emergency programmes to be linked with integrated longer-term resilience programmes. These programmes focus on adapting to climate change through promotion of climate smart agriculture and natural resource management; and addressing high morbidity and malnutrition through increasing access to water and sanitation infrastructure and improving nutrition, health and hygiene practices. In Unity, beneficiaries of this response will also be targeted by Concern’s Nutrition and WASH programmes and in Juba PoC, Concern will coordinate with WASH parnters to ensure Concern’s FSL beneficiaries are targeted.

project_name: Improving food security and livelihoods of most food insecure households and save the lives of 3,000 households vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in Nasir County of Upper Nile State and Ayod County of Jongeli State South Sudan
project_objective: This project will seek to build on gains made in ADA projects supported by CARITAS GERMANY in 2017 to 2019, meeting the needs of approximately 18,000 conflict-affected individuals (indirect beneficiaries) and 3000 Households (direct beneficiaries) through Food Security and Livelihoods response. Food assistance distribution was active through April, 2018 to March 2019. Agricultural inputs and fishing kits and capacity building is active from April to December 2019. Therefore, this FSL Programming is aimed at enhancing emergency food production through complementary cropping, vegetable gardening, fishing and capacity building through agronomic best practices to reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs and diversify livelihoods through fish production and to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks that affects beneficiaries. Nutrition training sessions and food demonstrations will also be provided and incorporated into the capacity training tool in order to help mitigate the underlying causes of poor or under nutrition, and complement the current FSL activities.

project_name: Provision of Inclusive Education to Crisis-affected Children of Nasir County of Upper Nile State and Fangak , Cana/Pigi Counties of Jonglei State , South Sudan.
project_objective: This integrated education project by a national partner in South Sudan Education in hard-to-reach areas aims to ensure that children and youth (boys and girls) have access to quality education and those already in schools are retained in Nasir County (Upper Nile State); Fangak and Pig/Canal (Jonglei State). The following interventions are envisaged: establishing safe learning and recreational facilities in 12 locations – 4 in each County; teacher training to enhance the teaching/learning function supported in schools; providing monthly stipends to 120 volunteer teachers - 40 teachers per County; campaign for education, encouraging children, especially girls to return to school; and provision of school feeding programs to enhance attendance and retention at school.  Response priorities will include gender-segregated WASH facilities, provision of learning materials, capacity building of School Management Committees (SMCs) and Parents Teachers Associations (PTAs), life-skills and recreational opportunities to support the recovery of children and youth to promote their overall well-being. Equal access to education will be prioritized regardless of gender, disability or ethnic background. Through introduction of school feeding programme, the project will seek to address one of the top causes of school drop-out. School feeding will help increase and maintain school enrollment and attendance, and reduce risks of death, disease and cognitive underdevelopment. School feeding will also improve protection of in-school and out of school children by keeping them away from potential recruitment into armed groups, child labour, early marriage, exploitation, sexual violence and abduction while on their way to school and back home. The project will seek to support cholera prevention through rehabilitation/construction of hand-washing facilities and latrines, provision of soap, hygiene messaging on cholera symptoms, modes of transmission and prevention to children and their parents. This will help to reduce morbidity and absenteeism, support retention in schools and children to help sensitize their communities. Crisis-affected youths and Host communities will be engaged in basic education and recreational activities in order to create an enabling environment for their critical development and positive engagement with the community. Youths will catch up on primary education through accelerated learning programmes (ALP) to improve their literacy and numeracy, technical and vocational training, and life skills. The project will seek to include physically and mentally challenged children; girls and boys vulnerable to recruitment into armed groups, and child labour; youths; adolescent heads of households; young mothers; and children from different ethnic groups. Teachers, SMCsand PTAs will be trained on life skills and referral pathways to enhance the protective aspect of education in emergency (EiE) intervention. The project will include early childhood development program across schools in the project sites. The projects will also targets host community children who will be enrolled in schools and some of the youths will attend ALP program, others as volunteer teachers.  PTAs and SMC will be formed from host communities. Education services mapping (in partners, activities, locations, target groups, added value, breadth and depth etc.) will be done through clusters coordination meetings in targeted counties and states were ADA operate to ensure that there is synergy, cooperation, amongst partners and that duplication is avoided in all locations.  The project targets at least 255 children (m=127; f= 128) in each of the 12 schools in the three projects locations.

project_name: Provide child protection services to affected boys, girls and their caregivers in Ayod, Fangak and Nasir counties
project_objective:
This project will seek to provide immediate lifesaving response to vulnerable crisis affected children from returnees, IDPs and host communities of Nasir, Ayod and Fangak counties through strengthened comprehensive case management including family tracing & reunification; referral for services; provision of critical age and gender appropriate psychosocial support services in a timely, holistic and child friendly manner as well as to the traumatized adult caregivers whose children are also facing trauma, coordination monitoring and assessments of child protection related risk at entry points and in the community including prevention from and response to GBV related risk to girls and boys under 18 years old  e.g. abuse, exploitation, rape, violent and earlier or force marriage to children under 18 years old. The projects will also conducts awareness raising activities on prevention of family separation. 
 ADA under these projects will provide critical age and genders appropriate psycho social support services in individual and group sessions including Psycho social support to caregivers of children who are traumatized and undergoing PSS activities, identification, registration, interim care, family tracing & reunification to unaccompanied and separated children, advocate for the GBV related risk prevention including early marriage, Sexual abuse, exploitation and violent, referral to other services such as health, education, nutrition, shelter and NFIs among others to those at risk and other vulnerable children including those facing  other forms of violence, orphans and children associated with armed forces and armed groups (CAAFAG) in a timely, holistic and child friendly manner and also promote resilience to the traumatized ones. 
The project will also seek to enhance the protection environment of vulnerable crisis affected girls, boys and youths to enable durable solutions through establishment of community based child protection networks, foster family groups, youth/adolescent clubs, Child Friendly Spaces, child rights clubs, and recreational centers. This will create enabling conditions for realization of solutions and prevention of further displacement which leads to family separations; identification of risks, dangers and impediments; advocacy and mitigation measures, psycho social support, peaceful co-existence initiatives and resilience.
A total of 15,000 people (7,500 males and 7,500 females) will benefit from this project.  Out of this, 10,000 (75%)   will be children (5,000 girls; 5,000 boys) and 5,000 (25%) will be adults - 2,500 males and 2,500 females. However, 3,500 of the total beneficiaries (25%) will be from host community while 7,000 (45%) will be from Returnees and 4,500 (30%) from IDPs.

project_name: Humanitarian response to food needs in Gaza
project_objective: The project will target 1000 food insecure families in the Gaza Strip to improve their access to diverse and safe food. This will be done through the distribution of E-vouchers for food (vegetables, groceries, protein source). The project also will build the capacity of 3 vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip to undertake innovative community-led collective actions/initiatives to address community-based humanitarian needs, foster preparedness for emergencies and reduce potential risks and threats.

project_name: Health and Nutrition Assistance to the Affected Populations in Khartoum, South/West Kordofan, East/North Darfur States
project_objective:
This project aims to continue the delivery of CMAM services for SAM and MAM cases within the existing health system in Khartoum(umbada,Sharg Elnile,and Jabal Awlia locaities), S Kordofan (Abujubiha,Dilling,Liri,Kadugli and Alabasia localities) /W Kordofan( Lagawa) , E Darfur(Assalaya,B.Elarab,Eldeein,Elfardous,Yassin,and Abujabra localities) /N Darfur (Melliet, and Alfasher localities) States, through the provision of full package of treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among (boys & girls) U5 and PLW. The project targets acutely malnourished children (SAM with or without complication and MAM) either through treatment or rehabilitating services. Improve  the  capacity  of MOH staff to provide  quality services  and  community volunteers ,CBOs  to mitigate  the  risk towards  food insecurity  and  reduction of  malnutrition, the  project  enhancing  the  need  analysis  of  the  nutrition situation  through  conducting rapid nutrition surveys involving  the  target communities  in  identifying the  needs , planning  and  in implementation as  well as  monitoring  of  project  on regular  basis. Moderate Acute malnutrition and the underlying causes of malnutrition will be managed through participatory nutrition education activities using the Nutrition Impact & Positive Practice approach (NIPP) through targeting predominantly mothers and fathers of moderately malnourished children. The NIPP circles emphasize behavior change, communication & counseling (for improved awareness), livelihood (for improved food/nutrition security) and cooking demonstration using locally available foods (for improved feeding and care practices). Community screening of cases will equally target boys and girls & depending on their nutritional status they will be referred to the OTP or NIPP circles based on the admission criteria.
Mother to mother groups where a group of mothers with malnourished children, grandparents group) to help empowering Mothers to solve issues related to the nutrition with focus on IYCF practices and knowledge and coordination with relevant sector (for multi-pectoral nutrition activities). Mainstreaming child protection through reflecting in the assessment, design, monitoring and evaluation of the project. Girls and boys of all ages and their caregivers, especially pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, have access to awareness about women and child rights for the prevention of malnutrition Gender, HIV/AIDS and the environment are mainstreamed throughout the project activities. 
The ultimate goal of the project “save the lives” of acute malnourished children U5 in IDP ,host communities and refugee sites at the targeted states.
In addition the project is seeking to provide the medical treatment and referral for the vulnerable populations in the targeted states, through construction or rehabilitation of existing health facilities, purchase of medical equipment and referral of cases to the health facilities in the areas.

project_name: Improve Food security for vulnerable small scale breeders and mixed farming Households living in Area C of West Bank
project_objective:
The project will contribute to the HRP strategic objective 1, and the FSS cluster strategic objective 1. It will do so by providing Food Security support to small scale breeders and mix farming families living in Area C of West Bank who are particularly affected by the political situation since they are continuously under the risk of demolitions, displacement and increasing settlers' violence. Expansion of the settlements, restriction of movements and access to land and water undermine the livelihoods of these communities.
The project is based on a needs assessment conducted by MA’AN in July-August 2019 as part of the design of its Humanitarian Strategy in Area C, within which the present proposal is framed. the needs assessment includes updated statistics from the Palestinian Authority (PA) Ministry of Agriculture and from UN/OCHA data (OCHA Vulnerability Profile Project/VPP 2013), in addition to updates and additional information based on MA’AN’s direct engagement in the Food Security Sector. MAAN’s own findings from previous field assessments (e.g. those of previous projects funded by the HF/OCHA, AMENCA3) are also included. The need assessment identified the Breeders rely mainly on fodder purchase for the animal nutrition due to the limited access to grazing areas. Expenditure for the fodder is the largest cost of herder households and restricted access increases also the cost of other inputs, such as water, and veterinarian assistance. Losses of assets due to diseases and reduction of flock production due to the decrease of quality and quantity of input provided by the herders to their animals to cope with the current situation, are putting at risk of livelihood insecurity the breeders households.
In order to respond to the identified needs and to contribute to the HRP and FSS cluster objectives, MA’AN proposal aims at addressing the vulnerability of the Palestinian living in area C communities through a comprehensive humanitarian relief approach that includes livelihood/food security and protection-related humanitarian responses to increase communities’ resilience. The intervention has been structured in three interrelated components: One component will tackle the high rates of animal mortality and diseases,  and increasing the awareness and the knowhow on preventive measures and providing livelihood related infrastructure to the most vulnerable families. A second component will provide small scale breeders and mix farming families  living in area C with means to maximize the use of the land available, thus increasing the productivity of the land and decreasing the risk of its confiscation.  A third component will endow the communities with response mechanisms to address and object to the Israeli military orders by increasing the awareness among communitarians and duty bearers and providing tools and means to put those response mechanism in practice.
The proposed project builds on current interventions being implemented by MA’AN and partners, and predominantly aims to alleviate poverty and food insecurity for the most marginalized farming households in Area C. While another proposed intervention predominantly focuses on farmers with damages from settler violence and occupation regime. This projects focuses on vulnerable Farming HHs  with demonstrated protection and socio-economic vulnerabilities, with a particular focus on herders and livestock rearers. 
The proposed governorates and interventions aim to complement ongoing interventions by MA’AN, and have been proposed based on consultations and recommendations by the MoA and its directorates and other actors to serve the needs of farming households in Area C.

project_name: Emergency shelter support for the most vulnerable households in Area C of the Jordan Valley and Tubas
project_objective:
The aim of this project is to respond to emergency shelter needs of vulnerable households, mainly in Area C of the Jordan Valley, with provision of timely and adequate shelter and NFI solutions through a comprehensive integrated approach that supports building resilience, reinforcing protection, and supporting the steadfastness of the most poor and vulnerable households at risk of displacement or exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns. 
The intervention will addresses immediate needs, as well as the underlying conditions that give rise to those needs through a multi- pronged approach that includes; (i) Establishment of community based protection committees and provision of tailored capacity building to empower affected people to cope with sudden and protracted shocks and stresses, increase accountability, information dissemination and transparency specifically to report protection concerns, disseminate DRP practices with the inclusion of training on SPHERE standards and monitoring of intervention. (ii-a) provision of durable climate protection shelter materials and technical rehabilitation support and oversight to the most vulnerable households whom are exposed to harsh weather or protection concerns or at risk of displacement. (ii-b) Prioritized Shelter rehabilitation with full technical support and oversight for Persons with disabilities and widowed, separated or abandoned female headed households through MA’ANs local technical team. (iii)  Stockpiling and prepositioning of adequate shelter/NFIs stocks, and protective shelter material for HHs under risk of displacement, , and temporary displacement due to military training closures, and/ or at risk of exposure to natural or manmade hazards or settler violence and increase the capacity to respond to natural and manmade hazards in a timely, efficient and effective manner.
The intervention is built on MA’AN and ACTEDs Community Protection and emergency response approaches, & previous shelter rehabilitation experience in the area, placing emphasis on the themes of (1) Engagement at the community level with a focus on community ownership and responsiveness (2) Community Driven Resilience focusing on Protection mechanisms for vulnerable groups in communities.  To ensure effectiveness of intervention, targeted communities and neighborhoods have been coordinated with the shelter cluster, other partner organizations and actors working in the area to avoid overlap of assistance and ensure best reach in emergencies. MA'AN has prior experience and good understanding about the current legal situation for the construction in Area C and employs strategies in employing a low profile including: Rehabilitating structures from the inside of shacks and tents, Carrying out work at night, Staggering assistance over a prolonged period of time, coordinating with households and key communities members to stay updated with IOF activity in the area. Moreover, As the communities are subject to ongoing threats, and harassment, Project Management will also supervise the promotion and public announcement of the project among the inhabitants of the targeted communities to ensure an update of priority households in the database at the project start. Women in these communities will play an integral part in the selection of beneficiaries as part of the established CBPC , other members include village council heads and representatives, Mokhtar ( village head), and community members. Project Management unit will ensure that CBPCs and selected households are well informed about their rights, obligations and potential risks involved regarding housing, land and property issues and provide their consent to all proposed project activities.

project_name: Protect the livelihoods of acutely vulnerable residents in the Access Restricted Areas and build farmers’ resilience to cope with recurrent shocks and continued violations of IHL and IHRL.
project_objective:
This project focuses on conflict-affected vulnerable households engaged in farming or fishery in the Access Restricted Area (ARA). It is designed to protect the livelihoods of ARA-dependent households and build their resilience to cope with protracted protection threats and economic shocks. Vulnerable households affected by the IHL/IHRL violations and/or other types of shock such as economic or environmental and engaged in farming or fishery will receive conditional cash assistance (CCT) to help them restore their production capacity and sustain their livelihoods, while the most acutely vulnerable beneficiary households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities will be supported with unconditional cash-based assistance to cover their immediate basic needs. PUI focus also on the infrastructural challenges for resuming agricultural livelihoods in the ARA such as shortages of electricity and water in agriculture through provision of irrigation water using solar PV system on agricultural wells. The Action will enable vulnerable households engaged in farming or fishery, including vulnerable women, to re-launch or enhance their agricultural activities through different activities such as solar energy for irrigation and CCT to purchase agricultural inputs. The proposed intervention is part of a multi-year program. The planned action was closely coordinated with the Food Security Sector and the Ministry of Agriculture, as well as with other relevant local actors. The project will contribute to the following overarching country strategic objectives: SO2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL. SO3: The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. CO1: Livelihoods of vulnerable households are protected, and their resilience, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced CO2: Households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs. 
PUI coordinated its planned interventions with FSS and MoA. Coordination with key actors in the area of intervention took place with ICRC, Action against Hunger, ACAD, PARC and UAWC.

project_name: PROJECT REVISED - Shelter and NFI response to displacement effected population including IDPs, refugee returnees and vulnerable host communities across Somalia
project_objective:
The project will focus on improving the physical protection and dignity of IDPs, refugee returnees and poor host communities across Somalia through provision of locally purchased Non Food Items (NFIs) and Emergency Shelter Kits (ESKs) through cash/voucher/in-kind modalities, construction of Transitional and Permanent Shelters through community driven or owner driven approaches, settlement (re)planning training, conducting Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for Shelters and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs & ESKs and participation in infrastructure mapping exercises led by Shelter cluster or any other partner.
For the beneficiaries’ selection and registration, NRC will use an electronic mobile data collection tool called Kobo tool box, which provides an accurate and real time data. The data received through Kobo is easily manageable and transferable. 20% to 30% Poor host community members will also be selected to ensure 'DO NO HARM' principle ensuring other humanitarian principles including humanity, neutrality, impartiality and
independence. For the provision of NFIs, each HH will be provided with a cash of $100 as per cluster agreed standard NFI kit while for the provision of ESKs, each HH will be provided with a cash of $145 (80% or $116 as first installment and remaining 20% or $29 as second installment) as per cluster approved ESK design. NRC will acquire the services of local telecom companies (viz. Hurmuud telecom in South and Central Somalia and Somtel & Golis in Puntland and Somaliland) for the cash transfers. NRC will provide a complete list of selected beneficiaries to respective telecom companies for their cross checking purposes. This list will include all details of selected beneficiaries including their telephone numbers and token numbers. After reviewing and cross checking, respective telecom company will transfer specified amount of money to selected beneficiaries through mobile transfer facility.
Beneficiaries will be selected through predetermined beneficiary selection criteria prioritizing the Extremely Vulnerable Individuals (EVIs) including female and single headed HHs, orphans, chronically ill, aged and child headed households. Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age and diversity dis-segregated data. NRC will target total 111,300 individuals (50% females) consisting of 54,900 in South and Central Somalia, 43,200 in Puntland and 13,800 in Somaliland through different Shelter interventions throughout the year 2020.
NRC staff will ensure that the provided cash is to be utilized for intended purpose by coordinating with the beneficiaries and conduct follow up visits with the support of the community leaders, local authorities and the relevant cluster partners. A Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs and ESKs and Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for semi-permanent and permanent Shelters will be conducted to analyse outcomes, the beneficiaries’ level of satisfaction and draw lessons learnt for future programming.

project_name: Meeting the Protection Needs of Vulnerable Children Affected by conflict in the Gaza Strip through Child Protection Case Management System
project_objective: Palestinian children older than ten years old living in Gaza have now witnessed three conflicts in their short lives. Children aged 11 or less have only known life in Gaza under closure, resulting in an increase in the number of children displaying high levels of stress-related symptoms, requiring additional family and community-based support and individualized interventions aiming at reducing vulnerability and increasing protection. A Child Protection Rapid Assessment was conducted by Tdh (2018) shows that violence against children is common across Gaza. The Assessment found psychosocial distress as a main child protection concern, manifested by aggressive behaviour, unusual crying, and unwillingness to go to school. OCHA (2019) has identified providing mental health and PSS to children who could resort to a negative coping mechanism or could be the victims of harmful practices, including children survivors of GBV, victims of conflict, children victims of abuse and key humanitarian response. On top of the chronic crisis, since March 2018, Gaza has been witnessing a progressive deterioration of the political, social and security environments as a result of the ""Great March of Return (GMR)"" Demonstrations. The GMR Demonstrations have further compound to already fragile situation of the impoverished families making them unable to provide their children with basic life necessities. Up to August 31, 2019, a total of 46 children were killed by Israeli forces since the beginning of GMR Demonstrations, along with 15 children who were killed in other circumstances. Along with a total of 7947 injuries (7394 boys and 553 among girls (OCHA September 2019; MoH, 2019). With such context, it is undoubtedly that the need for the provision of responsive and remedial protection responses for affected children and their families, such as case management and PSS are highly demanded. This Action is a response to such need and it is consistent with Cluster Objective 2 which is Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict-related violence. The proposed activities will include the provision of responsive and remedial child protection responses, including case management, psychosocial support to 600 children, including 150 injured children during GMR, 150 children survivors of GBV, and 300 children who have different child protection concerns. In total, the provided protection services will be timely and of good quality protection responses that are tailored according to children's needs and the best interest of boys and girls, equally. Under this Action, a total of 8000 persons will benefit from awareness-raising for persons at risk of GBV (5000 persons) and how to deal with traumatized children victims of the current situation and general child protection (3000 persons). The total allocated budget for this project is USD 332,100. The targeted beneficiaries, including children and adults from different age groups, including seniors were involved in the design of the project, including the proposed activities. Additionally, both men and women from different targeted localities were involved in the project by identifying the needs and activities. During the implementation, beneficiaries will be involved in monitoring the project activities. The activities of the project are tailored according to the specific needs of children, taking into account their gender. To closely monitor and follow up on the results and achievements of the project, a Project Monitoring and Evaluation Plan will be developed at the start of the Action with the participation of the five partner organizations. The plan will comprise the indicators, assessments, and means of verification tools defined in the logical framework.

project_name: Responding to the Protection Needs of Vulnerable Children Victims of Child  Labour and School drop out in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
In a context characterized by prolonged strain and economic isolation-de-development-, vulnerable families, including those with a large number of children, female-headed households and families with people with disabilities, have adopted different coping mechanisms to deal with the high level of poverty and vulnerabilities. According to OCHA (2019), the deteriorating socio-economic condition in Gaza has a negative consequence on children’s rights and their ability to access education and protection services as manifested in an increase of school drop-outs and child labour (OCHA, 2019, UNICEF 2018, and Tdh 2019). This Action involves multi-sectoral interventions that are consistent with the strategic objectives of Protection, Education, and Food Security Sector. The project aims to eliminate child labour in the Gaza Strip and to increase children's access to formal education system and other vocational training opportunities through provision of child protection services, psychosocial services, educational reintegration, family support and increased community mobilization toward the issue of child Labour and dropout of schools. Along with protecting children's rights to access to education, this project focuses on the right of the child to be protected from economic exploitation and from performing any work that is likely to be hazardous and could negatively affect their overall wellbeing and development. The project will target 8985 beneficiaries, including 700 working and or dropped out of school children (450 boys and 250 girls).
The proposed activities will include responsive and remedial protection activities. The responsive activities will include: (1) provision of structured PSS for working and or dropped out of school children that aim to increase their feeling of safety, connectedness, to be emotionally assured, and to assess and identify the main psychological and mental health needs.  (2) provision of child protection case management, including provision of remedial classes, provision of individual and group counseling sessions, joint child-parent interaction activities, life skills, integration into schools and vocational training centers, referral to specialized mental health services. (3) Provision of economic support to 50 families of working children through food voucher conditional restricted cash transfer as in-kind modality (285 persons). Finally, training sessions to 7925 community members, mainly caregivers, on the importance of eliminating child labour (3963 men and 3962 women). The project team will provide services to the identified cases through the child protection centers, distributed across the Gaza Strip, one in each governorate. A high level of coordination with relevant ministries and relevant clusters, including Protection and Education. Finally, Tdh will report its intervention to Protection cluster, UNRWA, Child Protection Area of Responsibilities Working Group, and FSS. Tdh will be actively involved in cash-programming working group and will closely coordinate with FSS team, relevant ministries, and all other relevant actors. The total project budget is USD 432,000.

project_name: Urgent assistance to vulnerable food-insecure farmers, women female-headed and GMR-affected households in Khan Younis and Rafah
project_objective:
This project aims to urgently respond to the current emerging needs among acutely vulnerable farmers, breeders, GMR-affected and female-headed households in order to enhance their access to food, other essential basic goods, and restore livelihood capacities through urgent cash assistance. Through this project, Mercy Corps will target  508 vulnerable households (2,896 individuals) from Khan Younis and Rafah. The two governorates were selected as both areas have vulnerable groups that match the intervention criteria. Khan Younis is the second-highest percentage (55%) with people with accumulated Loan and Debt (SefSec, 2018), as well as farmers in Khan Younis and Rafah severely suffer from agricultural challenges including, high cost of production, and water crises in terms of scarcity, salinity, accessibility and availability of underground water wells (Annex 1). Additionally, 44% of the official GMR injured people list are from Khan Younis and Rafah. The selection also considered the logistical issue when targeting Khan Younis and Rafah, as targeting two nearby governorates reduces some of the operating costs and makes the project more cost-effective.  

The project will target 88 female-headed households with limited economic opportunities, 200 crises-affected farmers impacted by the economic deterioration and at risk of losing their livelihood, 50 venerable farmers severely affected by power and irrigation water crises, 20 small poultry breeders who’s their livelihood in urgent need for rehabilitation and has incurred losses resulting from high-cost alternative energy and 150 vulnerable GMR-affected households.  Mercy Corps will identify, assess eligibility, and distribute cash assistance to each household in monthly installments to eligible vulnerable farmers to rehabilitate open land,  or rehabilitate water ponds and have durable photovoltaic solutions. Breeders will receive cash to rehabilitate their farm and will be provided by durable photovoltaic solutions.  Women and Female-Headed households will receive two-months Cash-for-Work opportunities. Vulnerable GMR-affected households will receive an urgent unconditional and unrestricted multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA). 

This urgent cash support will allow vulnerable farmers, poultry breeders to have reliable, and timely financial support to addresses their urgent needs, restore their livelihoods, build resilience and improve agricultural production cycles; women, female-headed and GMR-affected households will have improved access to food and other essential basic goods for themselves and their dependents. 

Through well-defined vulnerability criteria, Mercy Corps, in partnership with two local NGOs [Al Foukhary Association for Country Development (in Khan Younis) and Yaboos   Charity Society (Rafah)], will identify, assess and verify eligibility to select vulnerable  households to receive designed assistance, monitor activities, and ensure full  coordination and engagement with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), Disability Working Group (DWG),  Cash Working Group and all relevant stakeholders.

In this project, ATAA’s concern is towards the dropped-out children, those at the risk of being dropped out and the newly displaced as a result of frequent displacement and difficult living conditions. The project will provide FE & NFE opportunities including TVET for 12553 children (Female; 6390, Male; 6163) as follows  545 ECCD,  8900 FE, 2540 NFE, 168 CWD, 400 TVET in addition to 623 educational personnel includes headteachers, teachers, cleaners and guards (Female; 283, Male; 340), the percentage of students (51% females and 49% males), the percentage of staff (45% females and 55% males).

project_name: Comprehensive WASH and protection support to vulnerable underserved households in Middle Area
project_objective: The proposed action is based on the 2018-2020 HRP speciﬁc objective of WASH Sector: “Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable access to safe and suﬃcient WASH services with dignity for the underserved, underserved and most vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank.” Based on recent ACTED assessments and extensive consultations with key stakeholders (WASH Cluster, PWA, CMWU, MoDS), the project will target 200 vulnerable households (1,140 individuals) in Middle Area governorate. ACTED and CESVI have successfully covered the needs emerged in 2019 for Wadi al Salqa community through an ongoing project funded by AICS (Italian Agency for Development and Cooperation). Based on new assessed needs, ACTED, CESVI and Natouf are now proposing a similar intervention targeting vulnerable households in other communities of Middle Area governorate. The aim of this project is to restore access to domestic and drinking water for most vulnerable households of Middle Area (Gaza Strip), by ensuring their access to drinking water supply, increasing water storage capacity and improving their sanitation facilities (bathrooms and kitchens). This project will also raise awareness and build capacity on good hygiene practices. By improving access to drinking water, basic sanitation and hygiene awareness, this project will also prevent further deterioration of the households’ conditions of living, reduce the protection risks related to bad and inadequate WASH facilities such as exposing to public health and nutrition risks, adopting coping risking mechanisms (purchase of water from unreliable vendors or using open or semi-open spaces as toilets).  The project will be implemented by ACTED in partnership with CESVI and Natouf. CESVI has been working in Palestine since 1994 and has developed a strong expertise in WASH (South Hebron Hills and ongoing project in Gaza in partnership with ACTED – adequate access to water in terms of both quantity and quality, introduction and testing of innovative technologies for water, sanitation and hygiene). Natouf has proven track experience in implementing WASH program as installing water desalination plants, distributing hygiene kits for households in rural areas, building capacities and raising awareness in WASH issues to achieve a positive impact on public health issues. The project design has been coordinated with relevant stakeholders, such as the WASH Cluster, WASH Focal Point for Middle Area (GVC), Palestinian Water Authority, Coastal Municipal Water Utility (CMWU), and the Ministry of Social Development. The project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA) during the targeting selection (individual vulnerability-based assessment), the implementation methodology (support to reparations to HH’s WASH facilities unable to overcome the workload), the monitoring (respect of shelter and WaSH protection principles and minimum standards) and the accountability in the action (identification of arising difficulties through the establishment of a Complaint Response Mechanism). Gender principles will be mainstreamed during the action and Committees will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases with a particular focus given to women and children issues such as related to GBV. ACTED Protection Oﬃcer will be focal point of the Committees to receive and follow-up on cases. Through this intervention, ACTED, CESVI and Natouf have indeed proposed a project design that will simultaneously address the urgent WASH needs of vulnerable populations, while concurrently empowering members of the community to become knowledgeable in WASH infrastructure and good hygiene practices.

project_name: Provisión de equipo crítico y suministros médicos a la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos del Hospital Materno Infantil Dr. Pastor Oropeza de Caricuao, Caracas
project_objective: Acción Solidaria ha estado analizando y monitoreando la situación de la UCIN del HMI de Caricuao desde el año 2018. La Unidad está actualmente operando con deficiencia, lo que lleva a una brecha significativa en la atención especializada para recién nacidos y bebés prematuros.  La crisis del sector salud tiene como uno de sus causas la falta de renovación / mantenimiento de equipos y la cantidad de trabajadores calificados que renuncian. Este tipo de unidad especializada se ha visto desproporcionadamente afectada, y la red de estos servicios en Caracas y otros estados se encuentra en una situación similar. Acción Solidaria en coordinación con las autoridades y médicos del HMI propone la siguiente intervención: 1) comprar equipo médico (incubadoras, ventiladores, bombas de infusión, monitores de signos vitales, lámparas térmicas y equipo de radiología portátil)  para lo cual Acción Solidaria ha avanzado en el desarrollo de un presupuesto con la compañía Meditrón C.A. la cual cumple con los estándares requeridos y las capacidades de mantenimiento; 2) comprar suministros médicos y medicamentos para respaldar su funcionamiento durante un mínimo de 6 meses; establecer la Unidad en asociación con UNICEF y OPS; monitorear la operación de la Unidad a través del personal del Hospital. Esta intervención tiene un componente importante para salvar vidas, pero también se espera que el equipo esté operativo durante varios años. La unidad atiende a un promedio de 125 recién nacidos anualmente, pero las estimaciones del hospital sugieren que la cifra podría aumentar hasta 200 anualmente si la Unidad está operativa. El equipo médico está comprometido con la reactivación de los servicios en la unidad. Esta intervención se alinea con el objetivo de fortalecer la capacidad operativa y funcional de los servicios críticos y esenciales de los establecimientos de salud del HRP 2020 (aún en borrador)

project_name: Building Resilience to Enhance Food Security & Livelihood Restoration for vulnerable men, women, boys and girls affected by the protracted conflict and economic shocks in Rubkona and Panyijiar Counties of the former Unity State of South Sudan.
project_objective:
Based on the August- September 2019 IPC analysis, it is expected that 6.5 million people in South Sudan (54% of the total population) face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity. In the post-harvest period of January to April 2020, the food security situation will deteriorate as households’ food stocks start depleting and an estimated 5.5 million are likely to face Crisis phase or worse acute food insecurity Unity state where the project falls has 71.3% or 214,000 people in emergency or catastrophic phases of the IPC classification and a further 395,000 in phase 3. This project is therefore developed to address the food insecurity issues. 

Through this project, Mercy Corps is planning to target the most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls in Rubkona and Panyijiar for IGAs through distribution of livelihood inputs to support beneficiaries during the dry season hunger gap, which will be from February – April 2020 (three months earlier than normal). The business start-up grants will be complemented by low input vegetable gardening and staple crop production (from March to May) as a means to promote household self-reliance and immediate food provision through own food production for both home consumption and sale of surplus. The project will also contribute to sustainable, equitable production, income and employment for the vulnerable through market-led production.

Mercy Corps appreciates that emergencies affects people differently. In South Sudan women, children and elderly are the worst affected with the conflict and economic shocks. As such in terms of targeting or selection, women, child headed households, elderly, PWD and the chronically ill will be highly preferred during the process. All activities including targeting, post distribution monitoring, valuations will engage women separately to ensure adequate contribution to issues affecting them. All reports will be presented with information dis aggregated by gender. The project will target a total of 10,830 households that comprises approximately 65,000 individual beneficiaries.
The proposed project will contribute to the Food Security and Livelihoods Cluster Objectives 2 and 3 namely:
- Cluster Objective 2: Enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop seeds and fishing and livestock support.
- Cluster Objective 3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen household’s ability to absorb shocks.
Cash for work grants to most vulnerable households with labor ability will avail temporary income for vulnerable households to meet their immediate food requirement while community common resource properties like dykes are rehabilitated to combat flood events.
Cash programming will be complemented by vegetable farming and staple crops inputs as a means to diversify their diets. Livelihood promotion will include the following activities:
- Support vulnerable households towards short-cycle vegetable food production systems for home consumption and sale of surplus by distributing livelihoods assets e.g. vegetable seeds and tools, pro-resilience livelihood business start-up grants aimed at diversifying livelihood options. 
- Where possible, livelihood activities are supported to improve household income aimed at immediate improved household purchasing power of diversified food of choice and working capital of other livelihood options. 
- Communities are supported in preferred livelihood supply chain management and livelihood value chain development aimed at strengthening their resilience to the causes and effects of the common disasters.

project_name: Provision of Nutrition Assistance to Vulnerable, Conflict-Affected Communities in Sunta, Katyala and El Salam localities in South Darfur State
project_objective:
Mercy Corps (MC) will deliver nutrition programming to conflict affected people in South Darfur State.  Furthermore, Mercy Corps deliberately designs our humanitarian programs to do better than meet needs on a stop-gap basis. While our priority aim is to save lives, minimize suffering, and protect social and economic assets, we will also tackles the proximate and underlying causes of the emergency in order to interrupt repeated cycles of crisis and vulnerability by mitigating suffering and not just postponing it to a later date. 

Building on Mercy Corps (MC) current nutrition project in East Jebel Marra South Darfur, MC propose to implement a community based nutrition program that aims to improve the infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices of communities, using a mother-to-mother support (MtMSG) model targeting 16,696 in Sunta , El Salam and Katyala localities within South Darfur state. IYCF practices, especially exclusive breastfeeding and complementary feeding, has been identified as the single most important intervention in a package of essential child survival interventions recommended for emergency contexts characterized by high levels of child undernutrition and mortality rates. Exclusive breast feeding is essential from 0-6 month given that the colostrum found in the mother’s breast helps build   the child immune system during the first fragile 6 months of the child’s existence.   Given the urgent nutrition needs and inadequate  community based support as evidenced by 2020 Refugee Response Plan (RRP) Needs Overview, MC will use a community-based model to promote healthy behaviours that improve IYCF practices, with a primary emphasis on the first 1,000 days of life (from conception up to age two). This program will build on existing community groups wherever possible and will be based on the MtMSG model This is a peer-based nutrition promotion program that aims to create individual and community behaviour change in nutrition behaviours among at the community through dissemination of key nutrition messages. This model has proven to be extremely effective and cost-efficient in reducing child malnutrition, mortality and morbidity in emergency and development settings. Furthermore, it facilitates a broad coverage of beneficiaries by messaging through a cascade structure. Given the high prevalence of malnutrition and limited options for the treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition in the target areas, MC proposes to support the Ministry of Health (MoH) to provide treatment services to malnourished children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) by implementing a Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) program in the target locations. CMAM is an an approach that enables community volunteers to identify and initiate treatment for children with acute malnutrition before they become seriously ill. This approach has been endorsed by UNICEF, the WHO and the MoH in Sudan
MC will work with the relevant stakeholders to develop a referral mechanism to enable children experiencing acute malnutrition to access necessary treatment and support. A screening system will be put in place with a local partner organization with mobile capability, to ensure children identified as malnourished are referred for appropriate treatment. In addition, six nutrition centres in both administrative units will be rehabilitated. MC will complement these activities with targeted distribution of restricted multipurpose cash assistance vouchers to 400 mothers of children with SAM cases and extremely vulnerable households. The vouchers will be exchanged for locally available nutritious foods at predetermined vendors.

project_objective:
The project aims to scale up integrated field nutrition, child protection, health and hygiene promoting services through 16 Rapid Response Teams in coordination with the respective clusters in high severity communities and IDPs hosting areas where the project will target the IDPs camps in Dana through 2 teams, Al-bab through 2 teams, one team in I’zaz, 4 teams in Jisr Shugur, one in Harim, 4 in Salqeen and 2 in Maaret tamesrin/ Maret El Ikhwan sub-districts.
Each team, consisting of a nutritionist, and 3 community health workers and one data entry will introduce the following integrated services:
Nutrition: Provide IYCF-E counselling for mothers with moderately malnourished children, distribute micronutrients for preventing of anaemia and malnutrition among children, pregnant and lactating women, disseminate messages (IEC/BCC) on IYCF-E recommended feeding practices, and monitor distribution and use of breast milk substitutes, support health/nutrition inclusive education and promotion refer the needed cases and follow up the referred cases. Besides, they will distribute breast covers for PLWs to encourage them feeling more privacy and support the exclusive breast-feeding.
Protection: identify the children with disabilities; cases exposed to abuse or violence via the visual signs on the children under five and PLWs bodies to refer the discovered cases to the child protection CP and GBV case management teams of SEMA or other NGOs working in the nearest areas according to the service mapping
Health: Screen and refer CU5 and PLWs with danger signs and Medical problems, where the referred cases will receive the medical care under the supervision of professional doctors such as paediatrician or general practitioner.
WASH: support hygiene promotion and raise the awareness through providing key messages about the hand washing and food processing. Hygiene kits will distributed to the most needed beneficiaries.
Messages about the RH module will be provided by the CHWs for PLWs. Besides, 1000 Breast covers will be distributed to the PLWs to encourage them and to raise the awareness about the importance of exclusive breastfeeding.
The nutritionist will provide consultations, referrals and monitor the upload of data before the data entry uploaded the data directly through KOBO link to the Information Management Unit IMU in the main office in Gaziantep; while the community health workers CHWs will screen the children under five years CU5, and PLWs (pregnant and lactating women), provide messages, and distribute brochures about the importance of the exclusive breastfeeding to raise the awareness in the targeted locations.
After finalizing the recruitment process, the staff will be trained on the protocols and templates, in coincidence with conducting Communities (Camps) Mapping by CHWs under supervision of the supervisor to prepare the detailed work plan.
