project_name: Fortalecer el acceso al agua e higiene en comunidades vulnerables en Venezuela
project_objective:
El deterioro de la infraestructura de agua en el país se ha acelerado en los últimos dos años y el acceso al agua, al saneamiento y a prácticas de higiene se ha convertido en una dificultad para muchos venezolanos. Las personas que viven en áreas urbanas se ven afectadas por el deterioro de la red del sistema de agua y los cortes de energía también están impactando.  
Este proyecto tiene como objetivo responder a las necesidades inmediatas de las personas venezolanas en cuanto a acceso, disponibilidad, calidad y accesibilidad del agua en consonancia con los objetivos del clúster y empoderamiento de la población para el acceso a enseres de higiene, así como la adopción de prácticas adecuadas en las comunidades donde las condiciones de saneamiento están por debajo de los estándares mínimos.  

IOM distribuirá enseres de higiene a población vulnerable, incluidos enseres de higiene menstrual para mujeres y niñas adolescentes en edad menstrual. La distribución de los enseres será acompañada por la diseminación de materiales de información, educación y comunicación, así como actividades que promocionen buenas prácticas de higiene y saneamiento y enseñen el uso de los enseres distribuidos con el fin de mejorar las condiciones de vida y bienestar físico.

Además, IOM buscará mejorar el acceso a agua y saneamiento en lugares comunitarios de alta confluencia y de tránsito, en consultación con la población en movilidad y el cluster WASH. Para ello, IOM llevará a cabo la mejora y habilitación de infraestructuras que proveen servicios básicos de WASH en las comunidades con mayores necesidades. Asimismo, OIM monitoreará su uso y tratamiento con el fin de asegurarse que el agua sea segura y potable, conforme con los estándares mínimos Esfera. 
El proyecto se implementará en 10 estados: Anzoátegui, Apure, Bolívar, Distrito Capital, Falcon, Guárico, Mérida, Portuguesa, Táchira y Zulia.

project_name: Provisión de salud primaria y psicosocial en las comunidades de origen, transito y destino en Venezuela
project_objective:
En Venezuela, la infraestructura de los centros de salud se ha deteriorado y se reporta una escasez de medicamentos, equipos médicos y personal capacitado, ya que muchos profesionales han abandonado el país. La situación se agrava aún más por la escasez de energía, el suministro irregular de agua y saneamiento. Además, el aumento del estrés, la ansiedad y la depresión han afectado la capacidad de las personas para llevar a cabo actividades diarias de manera adecuada.
Por ello, OIM organizara campañas de sensibilización y prevención de VIH/SIDA, TB, ITS, y temas ligados a salud sexual y reproductiva en las comunidades priorizadas, en coordinación con las autoridades locales y con las redes de salud.  Eso será complementado por la formación y despliegue de brigadas de salud para fortalecer la atención primaria, a través de evaluaciones de salud y tratamiento básico, además de referimiento de casos en comunidades. Además, estas brigadas organizarán actividades de promoción de salud y prevención de enfermedades. La OIM les brindará apoyo a través de distribución de medicamentos, insumos y métodos anticonceptivos. Además, la IOM formará líderes comunitarios y trabajadores en salud para fortalecer la educación sobre el tema de salud a los beneficiarios en las comunidades y para la identificación y referimiento de casos de salud primaria y psicosocial a servicios existentes. 
Las actividades de apoyo psicosocial fortalecerán esta respuesta: equipos interdisciplinarios serán formados y desplegados en las comunidades identificadas, para brindar apoyo psicosocial, a través de evaluación, orientación, promoción de salud mental, y actividades recreativas para abordar necesidades psicosociales y fortalecer las redes comunitarias en las zonas identificadas. 
Como último, la OIM proporcionará generadores y otros insumos de salud a los establecimientos de salud en las comunidades o parroquias donde operan los líderes comunitarios y equipos de salud mental y apoyo psicosocial.

project_name: Mejora de las condiciones de vida de las personas vulnerables de Venezuela a través de la provisión de alojamiento, servicios básicos y protección.
project_objective:
Basados en las actividades de 2019 en temas de rehabilitación y gerencia de espacios de alojamiento temporal y la distribución de enseres (NFIs) en Zulia, Táchira y Apure, la OIM busca ampliar su respuesta cubriendo otras áreas geográficas, como Bolívar, Sucre, Falcon y Distrito Capital. En 2020, la OIM también diversificará el tipo de asistencia provista en dichos centros, con el fin de cubrir las necesidades humanitarias y de protección de las personas vulnerables.

Para ello, la OIM implementará su respuesta en 10 espacios de alojamiento temporal ubicados en Zulia, Sucre, Táchira, Apure y Bolívar, proveyendo una gama completa de diferentes servicios a las personas vulnerables. Esto consiste en la rehabilitación de la infraestructura de los centros, suministro de equipos, la asistencia en forma de alojamiento y el acceso a servicios básicos como alimentos, instalaciones de saneamiento, y distribución de NFIs. Asimismo, se incrementará la capacidad de los socios encargados de la gestión de albergues con el fin de garantizar los estándares mínimos de asistencia.

Además, OIM trabajará para abordar las necesidades de protección de los venezolanos en dichos centros mediante la distribución de información que salva vidas y actividades de conciencia sobre los riesgos y la prevención de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG), trata y otros riesgos de explotación y abusos, así como orientación e información sobre el acceso a la documentación. OIM también facilitará vías de referencia a los servicios especializados disponibles en las zonas donde se encuentren los centros.
OIM también proveerá asistencia a hogares que alojan a miembros de sus familias y se encuentran en situación de hacinamiento. Para ello, IOM mejorará sus condiciones de vida mediante el suministro de materiales. La asistencia proporcionada consiste en la mejora de estructura de la vivienda (ampliando baños, cocinas, cuartos), y dotación de equipamiento, artefactos del hogar (colchones, cama, fregadero, cocina etc) según las necesidades. 

La OIM también distribuirá enseres tanto en espacios de alojamiento temporal como a personas en comunidades de origen y de acogida.

project_name: Mitigar, prevenir y responder a riesgos de protección a través de espacios seguros y campaña de sensibilización
project_objective:
Con el fin de proveer servicios multisectoriales seguros, de calidad, y que salvan vidas que estén disponibles a personas vulnerables y personas en riesgo, la OIM construirá y/o instalará tres espacios seguros en comunidades con alta incidencia de incidentes o riesgos de protección, en San Cristóbal, Maracaibo y Santa Elena de Uairen. Los espacios seguros son lugares estructurados que proveen un punto de entrada seguro y de empoderamiento para mujeres y niñas con el fin de acceder a información, servicios especializados, referencias a servicios de salud y protección, así como otros servicios a determinar, dependiendo de las necesidades manifestadas por las mujeres y niñas de las comunidades seleccionadas. En los espacios seguros las mujeres y niñas pueden buscar, compartir y obtener información, acceder a servicios, espacios de expresión, proteger su seguridad física y emocional, ser referidas a servicios de salud, protección y otros especializados, mejorar su bienestar psicosocial, crear una red segura comunitaria que reduzca el aislamiento y refuerce la integración de estas en la vida comunitaria.  Los servicios también incluyen la provisión de formaciones profesionales para desarrollar habilidades específicas, por ejemplo, la fabricación de jabón, tecnología de la información, sastrería/costura, estética, repostería, etc. Los servicios que se proveerán en los centros dependerán de las necesidades destacadas por las mujeres y niñas de las comunidades seleccionadas. En los espacios se garantizará un contexto apropiado de mitigación de riesgos, orientación y referencia a servicios de asistencia especializada a sobrevivientes de VbG, así como víctimas de trata y otros abusos. Esto incluye apoyo psicosocial con el fin de guiar a las sobrevivientes de VbG y de trata y tráfico en el proceso de recuperación y recibir información sobre servicios disponibles. Bajo los principios de derechos humanos, genero, edad y confidencialidad, la OIM hará: 1. Valoración de caso detectado y preparación para la entrevista. 2. Entrevista tomando en cuenta en principio de no hacer daño y otros relacionados a la seguridad física de la víctima potencial y la de su familia inmediata, 3. Análisis y valoración de riesgo para la persona y su familia, 4. Plan de Intervención inmediata: acceso servicios básicos: atención psicológica, ropa, abrigo, albergue, alimentación, salud primaria, seguridad. La OIM cuenta con herramientas internas que serán la base para la atención de los casos detectados en el marco de este proyecto. El manual de identificación de vulnerabilidad, así como el manual de protección a víctimas de trata orientaran la asistencia y protección a la victimas detectadas o las personas en mayor riesgo de serlo.  
OIM se hará cargo de la gestión de estos centros y del fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal para brindar atención de calidad. OIM también llevará a cabo referencia a otros servicios especializados cuando sea necesario, incluyendo apoyo psicosocial. Además, OIM facilitará acceso a la documentación legal a través de acompañamiento (traslados), y referenciación a las instituciones legales competentes y orientación sobre requerimientos y procesos para realizar trámites legales en comunidades de tránsito y de origen. 
Para responder al desafío de la falta de conciencia sobre riesgos de protección y de método de mitigación y prevención, la OIM trabajará para crear un entorno más seguro a través de campañas de sensibilización sobre mitigación y prevención de riesgos de protección como VbG, trata y tráfico en puntos de alta confluencia y tránsito para alcanzar grupos de edades, genero, vulnerabilidades diferentes.
Por último, el proyecto propone brindar varios servicios de asistencia mencionados arriba a hogares monoparentales o compuestos por adultos mayores y NNA cuyos progenitores han emigrado y presentan alto grado de vulnerabilidad, incapacidad de generar ingresos suficientes y con un deterioro de las condiciones de vida.

project_name: Expandir la cobertura y profundidad de la Matriz de Seguimiento de Movilidad (MTM) en Venezuela.
project_objective:
Con el fin de responder a las brechas de información sobre la movilidad interna y las necesidades de las personas afectadas en Venezuela, la OIM planea ampliar sus operaciones de recolección y análisis de datos en el país a través de la Matriz de Seguimiento de Movilidad (MTM, por sus siglas en inglés). La MTM es un sistema para rastrear y monitorear la movilidad de la población de forma regular y sistemática para una mejor comprensión de los movimientos y las necesidades cambiantes. 
Para hacer esto, los datos se recopilarán a través de múltiples metodologías, como entrevistas a informantes clave (líderes comunitarios y autoridades locales), así como el uso de datos de registros e información de los socios, seguido por un proceso de verificación y triangulación de datos. La OIM utilizará estos datos juntos con los complementarios recopilados a nivel de hogares en puntos clave mediante cuestionarios estandarizados, para dibujar rutas de movimiento pendulares e interno, compilar estadísticas y proporcionar información confiable sobre la movilidad en Venezuela y con los países confinantes. El contenido de los datos recopilados en 2020 se ampliará a las nuevas necesidades y las brechas más significativas en la asistencia.
Las ubicaciones se seleccionan en función de las áreas de alta movilidad en términos de llegadas y salidas de población, y representativas de la situación de desplazamiento. La OIM planea ampliar la cobertura MTM de tres a cuatro estados en su siguiente ronda, agregando el estado Bolívar, Distrito Capital, Táchira y Zulia; alcanzando la cobertura nacional al final del del 2020. Para ello, se planean establecer 10 hubs: Distrito Capital (cubriendo Caracas, Miranda, Vargas, Aragua, Carabobo, Yaracuay); Táchira; Bolivar (cubriendo Delta Amacuro y Amazonas); Apure; Anzoátegui (cubriendo Nueva Esparta, Sucre y Monagas); Falcón (cubriendo Lara); Portugesa (cubriendo Cojeales y Barinas); Guarico; Merida (cubriendo Trujillo); y Zulia.

project_name: Safer and resilient communities in central Mali
project_objective:
The security situation in Central Mali has further deteriorated, with an increasing number of incidents affecting civilians. Intercommunal conflicts and tensions continue to lead to population displacements. Violence has been taking place between the pastoralist and farming communities in the Center, leading to loss of several lives. According to the latest CMP’s data for April 2020 there were 250,998  IDPs in Mali, with about 45% of these in the Mopti and Segou regions.
There is an increasing proliferation of Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALWs), Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) and Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) due to the presence of violent extremist groups targeting the concentration of national and international armed forces in Central Mali. Civilian populations, using the same roads as the militaries have been hit by IEDs with several casualties. Facing this situation, people need really to be made safer through Risk Education direct sessions and radio messages.  
In addition to the above, the food security situation has continuously deteriorated since 2016. The frequency of shocks and aggravating factors (climatic, environmental, economic, security) accentuates the deterioration of livelihoods for poor and very poor households and increases significantly their level of vulnerability, while greatly reducing their resilience. According to the “Cadre Harmonisé November 2019”, in the Mopti region 422,198 people are under IPC phase 2 (Stressed) and 158,881 people are already under IPC 3 (Crisis). Consequently, poor and very poor households need assistance to face the lean season and in longer term perspective to improve their resilience to recurring shocks. 
Overall Project Objective: To Build Safer Communities and contribute to social cohesion, resilience, and peaceful coexistence in central Mali.
Objective 1 (Protection Cluster/HMA Sub-Cluster): Communities and individuals are safer and social cohesion is strengthened.
Objective 2 (Food Security/Livelihoods Cluster): Communities are more resilient, and the most vulnerable people have improved livelihood and food security.
Objective 3 (Protection Cluster/HMA Sub-Cluster): Communities and CSOs have strengthened capacities to mitigate risks and violent conflicts and support economic recovery.
Target groups:	Underserved and insecurity affected communities, IDPs and returnees, Women headed households, very poor farmers and pastoralists, CSOs. 60,000 people.
To reach these objectives, the following activities will be implemented:
SO1: ERW/IED/SALW risk education, community safety action plans, microprojects to strengthen community safety (pastoral tracks, pastoral calendars, social cohesion events, disaster risk reduction), early warning, mediation & dialogue forum.
SO2: Community resilience action plans development & implementation (resilience microprojects: in-kind distribution of seeds, farming and fishing equipment and mills, creation/rehabilitation of family gardening plots, clearing of irrigation canals via cash for work, ponds, distribution/repairs of pumps and water pumps ), distribution in kind and in cash or vouchers to vulnerable households during the lean period, vocational training for the youth, support for local businesses.
SO3: Training of social cohesion committees on participatory evaluation, community safety planning, conflict prevention and conflict management, training of community focal points on risk education, training of teams on Community Violence reduction and ERW/IED/SALW Risk Education, capacity building of CSOs Mine Action.
COVID component: To save lives by preventing COVID-19 infection and supporting the most vulnerable communities in conflict zones in Mali through sensitization of populations, provide emergency assistance hygiene kits to the IDPs and host communities and facilitate their access to food through cash assistance and IGA to endure socio-economic impact of COVID-19 outbreak.

project_name: Improved access to life saving Shelter and Non-Food Items (S-NFI) services to affected population across South Sudan
project_objective:
Faced by an estimated 7.5 million persons in dire need of humanitarian assistance across South Sudan, IOM plans to reach up to 116,489 most vulnerable individuals with shelter and NFI assistance (Shelter 10,799 NFIs 78,111 settlement project 6,000 and protracted 21,579). IOM will target the affected population who lack the capacity to anticipate and cope with conflict stresses. The project will provide support to targeted affected communities which includes newly displaced persons, IDPs in protracted displacement in Protection of Civilians (PoCs) and collective centers (CCs), IDPs living with host communities, returnees, and affected non-displaced host communities.  The proposed activities align with Shelter Cluster Strategic Objective 1, 2 and 3 of 2020 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP). 

Since January 2019, IOM as the S-NFI cluster leading agency, was able to provide S-NFI assistance to 190,884 individuals across the country. In 2020, IOM will respond to 11 percent of the Cluster target caseload and provide shelter, NFI and settlement support to a total of 116,489 individuals across South Sudan through its mobile as well as static teams. IOM will implement inclusive community-based approaches to ensure that the needs of people with disabilities, men, women, boys and girls are considered throughout the project cycle. IOM will further improve its program quality by designing evidence-based intervention through improved monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning including rapid monitoring, PDMs, end-line evaluation and success stories; and implemented as appropriate respecting market capacity, financial infrastructure, beneficiary preferences, as well as principles of do no harm. Also, IOM plans to strengthen the coordination with cash partners as its capacity of Cash Working Group (CWG Co-lead). 

IOM will expand its provision of Housing, Land and Property (HLP) services to vulnerable individuals who lack the capacity to secure land, settle ownership disputes, lack awareness and/ or are attempting to return or resettle after protracted displacement. Technical support to Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (MHADM) will be provided in developing national and sub-national disaster management plans.

In line with the Cluster objective for durable solutions and rebuild lives through community-based shelter and NFI solutions, IOM aims to enhance resilience of the target population in conjunction with addressing their S-NFI needs. The project intends to replicate the settlement project model to other areas, including Rabkuna, Raja, Yambio and Renk with the plan to reach a total of 6,000 people (62% of the Cluster’s total settlement target). IOM will continue to expand its cash-based interventions (CBI) approach and plans to reach 48,245 (41%) individuals through CBI. IOM works in close coordination with solutions working group encourages area-based coordination for integrated multi-sectoral projects with all other sectors or partners on ground including CCCM and Protection. IOM will ensure service delivery improvement with all sectors by leveraging the contribution of additional partners in settlement and integration including coordination with CCCM.  Through advocacy component and area based approach of the project IOM aims to ensure access of the affected communities to more sustainable livelihoods, health, education, nutrition, water supply and sanitation facilities, and protection against physical and violent threats. 
IOM as Cluster lead agency will further enhance national and sub-national level coordination between government and partners, as well as continue to advocate for adequate funding to meet the S-NFI needs of affected people. The S-NFI Cluster will continue to invest and explore effective avenues to strengthen the capacity of both established and new cluster partners through technical support, training, joint responses and standardized data collection tools.

project_name: Establishment of Humanitarian Hubs in South Sudan
project_objective:
Since the signing of a renewed peace agreement in September 2018, active conflict has been noticeably reduced and an increase in returns has been observed. Humanitarian organizations continue to provide support and assistance as prospects for peace and development improve and confidence is generated for durable solutions, including returns, relocations, or local integrations. Unfortunately, a lack of accommodation, work space and other key facilities often hinders humanitarian operations and a sustained presence in key strategic deep field locations.
In response, IOM will establish humanitarian hubs to enable the expansion of operations across hard-to-reach areas of South Sudan through an increase in static humanitarian presence in key strategic deep field locations. Based on lengthy consultations with field offices and State Inter Cluster Working Groups (ICWG), sixteen potential locations were proposed, of which eight have been selected as proposed locations, namely Jiech, Kajo Keji, Kodok, Leer, Mandeng, New Fangak, Pieri, and Raja.
The eight priority locations would provide field working facilities, accommodation and warehousing to enable agencies to maintain a continuous presence on the ground and international staff to overnight in these locations, as well as allow care of overflow of staff who are unable to find any other accommodation.
IOM will work closely alongside NGOs that will assume responsibility for the running of the hubs. IOM will hand-over the management of the hubs and work on building the capacity of NGOs and local partners to ensure sustainable management of the humanitarian hubs subsequent to the conclusion of the intervention.

project_name: Support to COVID-19 Affected Vulnerable Households in Cox's Bazar District (Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities)
project_objective: This support for the JRP 2020 project, aims to enhance the COVID-19 response by ensuring targeted COVID-19 affected households have access to a range of basic non-food items (NFI) including floor mats, blankets, solar lights, 3mm rope, mosquito nets and tarpaulin. In addition, the shelter mobile team will be trained on IOM's code of conduct, PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) and COVID-19 distribution guidelines (e.g. maintaining proper social distancing while distributing NFI). The Shelter team will distribute NFI to the families in home-care and quarantine centres. A brief orientation (compliant with social distancing measures) will be conducted. Similarly, emergency response activities would also include a brief orientation to the beneficiaries. This trained shelter mobile team would ensure that any shelter repair, upgrade or new construction undertaken is aligned with construction site safety recommendations in light of COVID-19 by the S-NFI sector. The above mentioned activities will be undertaken in Camps 8W, 9, 10, 11, 12, 18, 20, 20 extension, 22, 23, 24 and 25.

project_name: Improving short-term and long-term food availability and livelihoods access in Jonglei, WBeG, Lakes, Warrap, Upper Nile, and Western Equatoria through investment in food production assets, and utilization and strengthening of local capacities.
project_objective:
ACTED will aim to implement FSL interventions in 2020 with the following objectives:
1.	To provide immediate short-term food assistance to 431,477 vulnerable individuals in Greater Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile and Lakes states, to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies. Immediate food assistance will be done through GFD + distributions either in-kind or through cash, complementary with BSFP where appropriate.
2.	To enhance emergency food production, livelihoods and build resilience against future shocks of 47,037 beneficiaries in targeted communities by provision of unconditional cash transfers, conditional cash transfers, and seeds and tools input. Conditional cash transfers will not only improve purchasing power of beneficiaries, but will also contribute to creation, construction and rehabilitation of key livelihood assets such as water catchments and dykes to manage floods. Restricted cash will focus on purchase of livelihood inputs and assets such as seeds and tools to enable beneficiaries invest on their lands thereby increasing amount of land planted, and addressing the challenge of seeds scarcity. ACTED will also provide the most vulnerable HHs with fish, vegetables, and crop kits and respective appropriate tools. 
3.	To reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs through long term investment on productive assets through resilience programming. ACTED will adopt the APFS model to encourage transfer of knowledge and skills in modern farming techniques, encourage community engagement through participatory risk assessments, toward participatory planning and joint ownership of resources. Such an investment will be pegged on utilization of local capacities and knowledge, which will then be reinforced through interactive sessions toward realizing improved livelihoods, reduced gender inequality, inclusive economic and social growth, and overall transformation of communities. ACTED will target 20,486 beneficiaries under this objective.

project_name: Provision of Information, counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), and enhancing the protection of civilians affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
Provision of information, legal counselling and legal assistance (ICLA) on Civil Documentation (CD) and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights to people affected by crisis and displacement inside Syria. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable populations throughout Syria through the delivery of a multi-faceted response.  Through its Capacity Building Programme and ICLA core competency NRC’s work is intended to contribute to HRP Protection Sector Objectives 1 and 2.
NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and mixed modalities. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality. 

Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable crisis and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities, IDP and refugee returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the crisis. All interventions will seek to prioritize the most vulnerable households and pressing needs. 

NRC’s intervention forms part of integrated programming inside Syria, in close collaboration with the Shelter & WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) and Education programmes, NRC will aim to meet its overall objective of enabling conflict and displacement-affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. The NRC response in Syria will consist of two components:

a)	Increased Knowledge and Capacity to Respond:  Legal research and analysis, capacity building, HLP and CD coordination and preparation for durable solutions including return
b)	Direct Assistance: NRC will assist target groups on issues that link to accessing essential services and CD, as well as improving protection in accessing livelihoods and HLP rights. In 2020, NRC will increase its support for Collaborative Dispute Resolution (CDR) techniques, such as mediation and negotiation. NRC will continue to carry out HLP due diligence to support shelter/WASH, education and livelihood interventions

project_name: Direct and rapid humanitarian response for affected displaced populations of the North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon: shelter / NFI assistance
project_objective: Enlargement of Project # 163101: Upgrade spontaneous displacement sites in the Far-North region to improve site safety and hygiene and ensure livelihoods are sustained, which includes installing required WASH infrastructure, ensuring affected populations have access to emergency shelters and NFI in order to address health and protection risks (including activities such as ensuring adequate spacing between shelters). If required, develop tools and guidance for site planning, including for contingency spaces for expansion of services such as isolation areas, burial sites, and quarantine areas in the spontaneous displacement sites and other vulnerable areas of the Far-North region.

project_name: Enhancing access to safe water and basic sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Northeast and Northwest Syria.
project_objective: According to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2020, 10,7 million people in Syria are in need of WASH assistance, with 3 million in acute need . This represents the largest need by sector in the Whole of Syria, with the most severe needs concentrated in areas of ongoing conflict or areas with large numbers of IDPs. As a result, to address the needs of the most vulnerable households, this intervention will focus on providing targeted and effective WASH support in Northwest and Northeast Syria, areas that witnessed a large influx of IDPs, combining elements of emergency response with the establishment of durable solutions. Indeed, immediate interventions will be provided through the distribution of WASH NFI kits and the establishment of emergency water treatment unit, aiming at meeting the most pressuring needs of the most vulnerable. These interventions will be paired with an improved access to sustainable safe water sources, with a particular effort to offer sustainable alternatives to water trucking through the rehabilitation of WASH assets, such as water stations, and boreholes. An effective exit strategy will also be ensured by working closely with local stakeholders, building their capacity to operate and maintain rehabilitated infrastructure. Furthermore, water quantity and quality will be monitored to meet SPHERE standards, enhancing the access to safe water. Lastly, community sensitization on water conservation, usage, and hygiene will be conducted, contributing to decrease Water Born Diseases (WBD) concerns. This intervention will benefit a total of approximately 373,760 individuals, 93,418 in Northeast and 280,252 in Northwest Syria respectively.

project_name: Boys, Girls and Adolescents are safe and protected from violence, abuse and exploitation in the humanitarian response in Cox's Bazar.
project_objective:
Plan’s International Bangladesh (PIB) Child Protection Program will focus on two interlinking components: case management and community based child protection (CBCP). The services will ensure boys, girls and adolescents in Cox’s Bazar are safe and protected from violence, abuse and exploitation.

The activities will provide support to vulnerable children and adolescents in the Rohingya camps and host communities in Ukhyia and Teknaf. Case management activities will target unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), child-headed households, children in psychosocial distress, children with specific needs, child victims of trafficking and child survivors of GBV.  In this regard, PIB will mainstream child protection in education by ensuring safety and dignity of beneficiaries and avoid causing harm to the children. The EIE unit will refer children with protection concerns to child protection for case management as well as for life skills opportunities.

CBCP activities will be structured around establishing and supporting CBCP mechanisms embedded in the refugee and host communities. These activities will be structured through feedback from community consultation and participation to ensure inclusion and ownership by both the host community and the refugee community. PIB will work with a range of stakeholders in the community, including children, adolescents, caregivers, community and religious leaders, as well as government representatives. The interventions ensure inclusion of children, adolescents, persons with disability and the youths in the CBCP mechanism and their empowerment. Community-level interventions will include working directly with the refugees and host communities to promote social cohesion, supporting families and strengthening self-protection of children. In order to address harmful practices and attitudes related to child rearing and parenting, PIB will invests in active community participation, empowerment, inclusive feedback and in providing support to caregivers and families. 

PIB is accountable to the communities that it serves and will ensure that system of complain and child friendly feedback mechanisms are in place with strong emphasis on PSEA and Child Safeguarding.  Specifically on child safeguarding, PIB has a Safe Guarding Specialist totally dedicated to the response in Cox’s Bazar and continuously linked to the Global Safe Guarding Unit of PI and to the Country Safe Guarding Advisor in Dhaka.  Regarding to the specific prevention and combating Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, Plan International has a PSEA  Focal Point in Cox’s Bazar who is here on a long term and continuously participates in the activities of the PSEA Network in Cox’s Bazar. PIB also has a code of conduct to ensure protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse as well as Child Safeguarding and the humanitarian principle of DO NO HARM. PIB will ensure its partners have PSEA policies and the same is implemented to the core taking into consideration measure in case of breaches.

 PIB is committed to coordinating the response through active participation in Child Protection Sub-Sector, Case Management Taskforce, other sectors and working groups such as Education, GBV, CwC to ensure meaningful access, prioritization of safety and integration of services. The response will also be coordinated on the field level both with partners and other stakeholders including government bodies and local communities.

The services offered will be in line with Child Protection Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Action, Child Protection Sub-Sector localized Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Bangladesh, interagency case management tools and referral pathway. This will be ensured by provision of structured training to PIB staff to enhance competencies in providing quality gender-responsive and timely services to children and adolescents.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire pour les déplacés internes, populations hotes, et refugiés maliens suite à la crise sécuritaire et des personnes vulnérables pendant la période de soudure alimentaire au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Au Burkina Faso, la période de juin à septembre représente une période critique sur le plan alimentaire pour les populations en milieu rural du fait d’un déficit alimentaire chronique due à la faiblesse des récoltes. Cette difficulté a été fortement aggravée par la crise sécuritaire au sahel marquée par des attaques récurrentes des hommes armés non identifiés. Face à cette crise complexe, le nombre de personnes vulnérables qui a besoin d’assistance s’est fortement accru. Il en est de même pour les réfugiés maliens et les personnes déplacés internes du fait de l’insécurité. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement du Burkina Faso a invité l’ensemble de ses partenaires nationaux et internationaux à la solidarité pour apporter une réponse à la crise. En réponse à la sollicitation du gouvernement, le PAM apporte une assistance alimentaire et un soutien nutritionnel dans 6 régions du Burkina, à savoir la boucle du Mouhoun, la région du nord, la région du sahel, la région de l’Est, la région du centre nord et du Centre Est. 
De façon spécifique, entre janvier 2021 et Décembre 2021 Le PAM va assurer :
-	Une assistance alimentaire ou en cash base Transfer aux personnes vulnérables pendant la période de soudure dans les 6 régions conformément aux recommandations du cadre harmonisé
-	Apporter une assistance alimentaire ou en cash base Transfer aux personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et ménages hôtes des PDI.
-	Assurer une assistance alimentaire et en cash base Transfer des réfugiés maliens au Burkina Faso 
-	Assurer une assistance dans le prelevement precoce des PDIs dans leurs zones d’origine ainsi que dans les zones de deplacement.
Les besoins globaux pour ces activités sont plus de 212 million de dollars.

project_name: Life-saving food assistance and Livelihoods support in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
WFP will provide unconditional food-assistance to the most food-insecure, crisis-affected populations.  Life-saving general food assistance (in-kind food and cash-based transfers) will be delivered to IDPs, returnees and host populations in North-East Nigeria (Borno, Yobe and Adamawa States).  Early recovery and resilience to shocks will be promoted through asset creation and preservation, increased livelihoods opportunities, and enhanced agricultural value chains. Joint multi-sectoral assessments and Emergency Food Security Analysis will be conducted regularly to monitor the nutrition, food security, and markets situation in crisis-affected states.  

A gender-transformative approach that reflects the needs of women, men, girls and boys will be adopted. WFP will mainstream protection throughout its work, supported by a solid understanding of the operational context and protection analysis. Training and capacity building of staff and partners in protection and humanitarian principles will include on-the-job coaching. WFP will ensure that affected populations (women and men) will be consulted throughout the programme cycle; beneficiary feedback mechanisms will be tailored to their preferred means of communication. Beneficiaries will continue to be empowered with knowledge on their food assistance entitlements and their rights, including WFP’s zero tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be embedded in M&E tools, complaint feedback mechanisms and training of partners and staff.

The WFP protection and AAP unit is made up of two national protection officers and two international protection officers. This would need to be correct as it currently states 6 national protection officers and three international protection officers. 

WFP will continue the collection of key information on beneficiaries and assistance provided as part of its M&E activities. Monthly monitoring will include distribution and activity site management; beneficiary and entitlement verification; and ensuring adequate protection and gender measures. Lessons will be regularly drawn from monthly process and biannual outcome monitoring and reporting, and periodic reviews and evaluation to inform strategic and operational decisions.

WFP will further consolidate partnerships to enhance national and state-level emergency preparedness and response systems, including in food security and nutrition assessment and monitoring, early warning, protection, gender analysis, targeting and registration processes, safety nets, cash-based transfer capacities and supply chain.

Where security and access to land allows, increasing livelihood activities will complement food assistance to support access to productive assets, income generating activities and self-reliance in the long-term. Assistance will be coordinated with government distributions, to ensure food assistance is complementary and fills gaps.

project_name: Restoring livelihoods of crisis affected population in Syria through light rehabilitation of irrigation infrastructure at community level
project_objective:
The United Nations (UN) estimates that the number of crisis-affected people in need of humanitarian assistance in Syria is 14.2 million, of which 6 million are in acute need. The above figure of people in need includes 6.7 million protracted internally displaced persons (IDPs); estimated 320,000 spontaneous IDPs return; 75,000 refugees return; 438,000 Palestine refugees and the rest overburdened host communities.  

More than 75% of the number of people in need of humanitarian assistance are accessible from within Syria. Overall, 12.4 million of people are estimated to be food insecure (including 1.27 million severely food insecure) and 1.9 million people at risk of food insecurity. 

In this context, FAO has designed a project to assist 120,000 vulnerable crisis-affected food insecure farming households (equivalent to 750,000 people) in Syria. About 15% of the targeted householders will be selected from those who receive food support to help them shift from depending on food assistance to producing their own food and enhancing their self-sufficiency. The objective of the proposed action is to protect and enhance the livelihoods of vulnerable farmers and IDPs through the restoration of critical irrigation infrastructures to increase household food production and security. The project outputs include:

•	Output 1: Local small-scale irrigation infrastructures in the targeted governorates are assessed and light rehabilitation undertaken. 
•	Output 2: Capacity of technical staff and relevant stakeholders strengthened.

A training programme on enhancing irrigation management, water use efficiency in small-scale irrigation, agricultural land management will be based on FAO standards and approaches. It is expected that stakeholders and farmers (water user association) will join this training. 

This project is expected to contribute to increasing access to irrigation water for crisis-affected farmers and their families in the targeted areas through the light rehabilitation of local small scale irrigation infrastructure. Cultivation and other agricultural practices, including livestock and animal feed production, will consequently benefit from the water supply plans as an emergency response to crisis. The proposed intervention will strengthen household food production capacities and knowledge and address immediate food security and nutrition needs through increasing local availability and supply of food.  This may in turn promote flourishing of agricultural based livelihoods in the rural community, which would contribute to social cohesion, peace and stability. The project seeks to utilize intensive labour in order to maximize community participation and inject cash into the local community.  
FAO as part of the CWG will discuss at project level with the group to identify the rate, modality, etc. of the cash intervention to be in line with the CWG and to achieve the purpose of the intervention

The DRC mobile response team is composed of Protection, S/NFI, WASH and CCCM sectors.  DRC as a protection focused agency will mainstream Protection, Gender Based Violence (GBV) mitigation and prevention and AAP to enhance the overall quality of S-NFI response in 2021. According to shelter-NFI cluster strategy, DRC will participate in joint missions among others to avoid duplication and better coordination among the Shelter-NFI cluster partners and other clusters. DRC will draw on both its own funds to procure distribution items and the SNFI cluster pipeline as most appropriate to ensure an efficient and timely response. In accordance with SNFI cluster priorities, there will be an ongoing focus on monitoring, evaluation, assessment, and learning (MEAL) activities through post-distribution monitoring activities and integrating quick monitoring exercises conducted for all distributions done by mobile teams.

project_name: Improving the protective environment and supporting access to HLP rights for the most vulnerable conflict affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
In response to identified priority protection needs, including HLP needs, DRC will deliver General Protection services for conflict and displacement affected communities. DRC will implement protection activities in a variety of locations including hard to reach locations through both static, outreach and mobile modalities. In doing so DRC aims to contribute to the overarching intersectoral strategic objectives for the 2021 HRP through contributing to the four protection cluster strategic objectives of:
- Ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialized services through an integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas
- Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience
- Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other population
- Enhance protection assessment and monitoring to inform protection and overall humanitarian response
DRC general protection activities will ensure protection services are available to women and girls, boys and men. DRC will facilitate access to life-saving protection assistance by working with community networks to identify and strengthen positive coping mechanisms and develop mitigation strategies for identified protection risks. DRC will strengthen referral mechanisms for specialised services; conduct awareness raising and information campaigns focused on rights including HLP rights, assistance opportunities and threats; establish or support Community Based Protection Networks (CBPN) for primary prevention and monitoring; provide capacity building support to duty bearers, including on HLP and provide IPA based on needs, including for resolution of HLP related concerns. Evidence-based programming and advocacy across the response will be be supported through regular protection monitoring and protection assessments, including HLP monitoring and HLP assessments, based on pre-identified triggers, with mechanisms to ensure inclusion of persons with specific needs such as persons living with disabilities, elderly people, adolescent girls at risk, and female headed households.
DRC currently has strong static presence in Unity and Upper Nile State. DRC will continue to provide static and outreach services in these locations. DRC also currently has 2 Mobile Protection Teams that respond to emergencies in hard to reach locations where there are limited services and high needs. These mobile teams will also provide General Protection services outlined below. As such the locations listed as targeted areas for intervention include those locations where DRC has static presence as well as locations where DRC may respond as part of the country wide mobile protection response team capacity.
DRC activities in the sectors of SNFI, FSL, CCCM and other sub sectors of protection including GBV will complement protection services and allow for multi-sectoral service delivery in response to multi-faceted protection needs. DRCs multi sectoral capacity will allow for opportunities for strong integration between SNFI and HLP in particular which is crucial to ensure a do no harm approach to service delivery. 
Overall, DRC aims to reach approximately 34,800 vulnerable individuals affected by displacement and conflict.

project_name: Comprehensive, safe and dignified SGBV prevention and response services for conflict and displacement affected individuals and communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
In response to identified priority needs of protection risk mitigation and protection service provision, DRC will deliver Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) prevention and response services for conflict and displacement affected communities. DRC will implement SGBV prevention and response activities in a variety of locations including hard to reach locations through both static and mobile modalities. In doing so DRC aims to contribute to the overarching intersectoral strategic objectives for the 2021 HRP through contributing to the four-protection cluster strategic objectives:
-	Ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialized services through an integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas 
-	Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience 
-	Enable durable solutions for IDPs and other population 
-	Enhance protection assessment and monitoring to inform protection and overall humanitarian response 

DRC GBV program activities will ensure GBV prevention and response services are available to women and girls, boys and men, those who are survivors or at risk of GBV. DRC prevention activities will include risk mitigation through protection awareness raising and information dissemination, distribution of dignity kits, capacity building for duty bearers and strengthening of community-based protection capacities. Gender-responsive action will include mobilising communities in the prevention of violence against women and girls through the SASA! community mobilization program, working with both men and women to challenge the negative consequences of gender inequality and harmful power dynamics. SGBV response activities will include case management for survivors of SGBV and focused non-specialized individual and group-based counselling for women and girls. DRC will also support where appropriate the establishment of community based safe shelters and/or safe homes. DRC will strengthen or support the establishment of safe referral pathways in areas of both static and mobile operation.  DRC currently has eight Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) and/or Multi-Purpose Protection Centres (MPCs) located in Unity State and Upper Nile state. DRC will continue to provide services in these DRC established, women and girls owned, spaces. SGBV response services will be mainly provided in these static locations given the crucial need for confidentiality, privacy and ability to follow up when delivering such activities in order to avoid doing harm. DRC mobile SGBV services will focus mainly on prevention activities where response services are available. DRC currently has 2 Mobile Protection Teams that operate in hard to reach locations that have limited access to services. These mobile response teams will provide GBV prevention services where there are already response services available. As such the locations listed as targeted areas for intervention include those locations where DRC has static presence as well as locations where DRC may respond as part of the country wide mobile protection response team capacity.
 DRC activities in the sectors of SNFI, FSL and other sub sectors of protection including HLP and General Protection will complement SGBV prevention and response services and allow for multi-sectoral service delivery in response to multi-faceted protection needs.  
Overall, DRC aims to reach approximately 14,290 vulnerable individuals affected by displacement and conflict, including approximately  2,010 men, 7,290 women, 1,420 boys, and 3,570 girls.

project_name: Information Management, Site Management and Site Development Programming Inclusive of Disaster Risks Reduction Measures for Refugees and Host Communities across Ukhiya and Teknaf
project_objective:
The project aims at continuing and strengthening Site Management (SM), Site Development (SD), Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and informed humanitarian decision making within the Ukhiya and Teknaf areas through direct implementation and partnerships with international and national NGOs. Through this project Rohingya refugees and the host community will benefit from improved service provision, Disaster Risk Reduction measures, site improvements and site planning interventions which contribute to ensuring equitable access to assistance, protection, and services for refugees living in the sites, improving  their quality of life and dignity during displacement.  

Site Management activities will continue to lead the SMSD Sector within the ISCG, and support the office of the Camp-in-Charge, ensuring services are monitored and coordinated, and community engagement activities are appropriate, target those with vulnerabilities and special needs, and are an effective avenue for two-way communication with the affected population. Providing humanitarian and development actors with data and information on needs that supports informed decision making, the project ensures targeted and appropriate humanitarian service provision within the camps as well as the host community. DRR will also be streamlined into site management & development programming, with a focus on community based community response and referral mechanisms, camp level contingency planning and mitigation measures in place for all seasonal risks present in the camps. NPM will continue to provide support to humanitarian contingency planning and operational programmes and support the monsoon response through incident tracking. 
Site development works implemented through IOM, its partners, and its involvement in the Site Maintenance & Engineering Platform (SMEP), will contribute to a safer, more dignified, and more accessible living environment for the camp population, working to ensure further community involvement in the identification of priority works. It is expected that the specified programme activities will result in reinforcing the overall capacity of unions in Ukhiya and Teknaf  and surrounding host communities to cope with natural disasters like floods and cyclones and respond better through strengthening structures to manage natural disasters and emergency situations.  Approaches used to reach the overall goal of the project will mainly focus on community participation, age, gender, diversity inclusion, social interaction and peaceful co-existence. project_name: Food Assistance for conflict affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP camps, and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity.

WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying  mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan. 

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities, or other solution. 

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19 have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_name: Logistics Cluster activities in support of the humanitarian community in South Sudan
project_objective: The Logistics Cluster as a service-based cluster and provider of last resort aims to facilitate the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations through its logistics coordination support, information management, preparedness and provision of common services to the humanitarian community in South Sudan.

project_name: Provide air services to the humanitarian community
project_objective: Due to lack of safe overland and air transport options in South Sudan, the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) under WFP will continue to offer air passenger transport services to enable humanitarian workers to reach most areas of the country. The service will provide weekly flight schedule to 57 destinations combined with ad-hoc special flights for Rapid Response Teams, special field visits, COVID-19 response and emergency evacuations. UNHAS will also provide trainings to civil aviation personnel and support air traffic management projects to improve safety the the South Sudanese airspace.

project_name: Protection and prevention services to the most vulnerable children (boys and girls) in the West Bank, and documentation of protection incidents in Israel and the State of Palestine
project_objective:
This project will ensure the most vulnerable Palestinian children (boys and girls aged 12-17 years old) exposed to conflict-related violence are reached with protection, impact mitigation and prevention services in the West Bank. It will also foster increased respect for IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations against children through documenting and monitoring violations to inform advocacy and increase accountability. 

This project is in line and contributes to the Protection Cluster objective that aim to ensure vulnerable Palestinians have access to protection services that mitigate the effects of occupation and conflict-related violence.

The main objective of this child protection project is for children in the West Bank to be safe, protected and secure from violence, exploitation and grave violations. The project will:
•	support initiatives to engage vulnerable and at-risk children positively in structured recreational, educational, awareness-raising, life skills and resilience building activities to improve their resilience and coping mechanisms. 
•	support protective services and awareness-raising for at-risk children and families to inform children and families about their rights and where to seek assistance in case of violence, arrest and/or detention. 
•	support vulnerable children previously arrested and detained by Israeli Forces with integration and rehabilitation services especially structured counselling and MHPSS support. 
•	support capacities of families, community members and leaders to identify, prevent and respond to violence against children through families and community groups discussions, counselling and awareness raising sessions, and trainings.
•	support incident monitoring, data analysis and reporting on grave violations trends related to child protection concerns in Israel/Occupied Palestinian Territory (the WB) to provide evidence and inform advocacy. Data collection and monitoring will be enhanced through documentation of testimonies of children in military detention.

project_name: Lifesaving Wash Emergency Response and restoration of basic WASH services to ensure equitable and sustainable access to Water and Sanitation in Syria
project_objective:
The proposed project will contribute to mitigating the degradation of services that has resulted from the physical destruction of water and sanitation infrastructures. The challenge for the WASH sector in Syria will be to identify strategic entry points to restore WASH service delivery. If not dealt with in time, “vicious cycles” of lack of repair and maintenance services, damage and destruction, lack of service delivery may render the restoration of services unfeasible. The accumulation of incremental degradation leads to progressive deterioration of any service and an associated cumulative negative impact on people’s lives. The “vicious cycles” of cumulative impact on all three components (people, hardware, and consumables) during the current protracted armed conflicts in Syria can lead to a condition that is too technically difficult or simply too expensive to reverse.  
UNICEF will therefore work to support the repair and rehabilitation of critical parts of water supply systems and infrastructure while being guided by the principle of “Minimum reliable services for All – rather than All services for Some”. The projects supported will be guided by the findings from needs-based vulnerability mapping. Several criteria will be used for the project identification and selection both from an overall and participant perspective, including cost per participant, level of project complexity, neutrality, accessibility, severity scale, number of returnees, quality and quantity of water and sanitation services currently available. 

Of note, UNICEF will not support ‘rebuilding’ activities. UNICEF’s strategy in Syria aims at reducing WASH service degradation that resulted from the physical destruction of WASH infrastructure and the reduced Operation and Maintenance of WASH facilities. As such, instead of ‘rebuilding’ WASH infrastructure and ‘promoting capacity building measures for utilities’, UNICEF focuses on conducting light repairs on the critical parts of the water supply and sanitation systems/infrastructure and supporting their operation and maintenance (mainly through the provision of supplies, including water disinfectants). Wherever feasible, UNICEF will explore sustained operation and maintenance of WASH services through capacity development of Water Units and by facilitating establishment of water tariff collection and accounting system. These interventions do not restore the WASH systems to their pre-war levels which can only be achieved through large-scale reconstruction programs. However, UNICEF is able, through these small-scale targeted interventions, to restore a minimum level of service for a high number of beneficiaries. 

UNICEF will continue providing life-saving WASH interventions such as emergency provision of water, sanitation, and solid waste facilities and services, WASH-related supply (NFI) distributions as well as improving hygienic behavior and practices of the most vulnerable people. Preparedness actions and contingency planning will also be kept up to date and at sufficient levels to enable timely response to emerging needs, especially in light of anticipated rapid changes in the level of access and possible new mass displacements, that in particular might affect north-west and/or northeast Syria. Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA) will be promoted in the northwest, as an alternative to supply of hygiene kits and/or other WASH services.

project_name: BRAC's humanitarian response in Cox's Bazar: Education support
project_objective:
The project aims to address specific needs of 16,355 boys, girls and children with disabilities of ages 3 to 24 years in the Rohingya community, and ages 4 to 24 year in the host community. Overall at least 51% are girls. 
In order to ensure inclusive access through equitable, gender-responsive learning, the project will construct single and double storied learning centres for the Rohingya learners with proper drainage and gender segregated WASH facilities. 700 differently-abled children will be identified and provided with PWD devices as per their need, and learning centres made disable-friendly with support structures. Host community will continue to be supported through pre-primary, non-formal primary centres, learning opportunities for adolescents and youth through adolescent centres and multi-purpose community learning centres. This will contribute to increasing the number of school going children and skills development among the adolescents. Involving the host community children in different learning activities will contribute to ease tensions and improve social cohesion between the communities.

In adherence with the Education Sector standards and frameworks, quality education will be ensured through: staff capacity development - teachers basic, refresher and, subject based training in LCFA & Myanmar Curriculum, Teachers Learning Circle (TLC); construction of training centres. Through participatory approach in material development, so that contents are gender and culturally sensitive. Rigorous monitoring will be key along with coordination with ISCG and relevant government authorities to ensure smooth operations. Awareness sessions and C4D activities to sensitize the community on different social and education issues will be done to minimize pre-existing socio-cultural norms  hindering children’s education and ensue community’s ownership. BRAC’s partner organizations will be capacitated as required, to scale interventions and impact children’s education in both communities. The Sector’s contingency plan will be contextually updated and applied to prepare for natural calamities and other incidents.

project_name: Support life-saving & life-sustaining MHPSS interventions to mitigate self-harm and risky behaviors undertaken by Palestinian youth in Area A-B &C, H2, East-Jerusalem, and Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to contribute to the Health Cluster Objective # 1, aligned to the HNO Strategic Objective # 2;

More precisely, the project will emphasize on the following speciﬁc objectives:
1-	Promote psycho-education and public health awareness in conﬂict-affected communities about youth vulnerability with regards to self-harm, risky behaviors, and suicide. 
2-	Support the responding capacity of the 'Emergency SAWA Hotline 121' in oPt- for an extended period beyond the current December, 2020 timeframe- in detecting, supporting, and referring youths presenting self-harm, risky behaviors and suicide vulnerability
3-	Strengthen Mobile Clinics (MCs) capacity in Area C& EJ (Health Work Committees and SAWA) in responding to GBV, medical, and MHPSS needs for youth.
4-	Integrate MHPSS at ER department at general hospitals in both the WB and Gaza for better detection, response and referral for youth risky behaviors.
5-	Enhance the specialized MHPSS provision of care to vulnerable youths (especially youth with YLD) at CMHCs level.

The project will mainly target Palestinian youth- aged from 15 to 29 years old- presenting MHPSS concerns, due to chronic exposure to violence related to the protracted conﬂict and/or due to C-19 infection, social stigmatization, and distress imposed by the C-19 pandemic on patients in most vulnerable communities. A 2014 Birzeit University study conducted in both West Bank and Gaza, on the psychosocial health of adolescents, showed that 16% of them show moderate to severe level of distress, while the 2016 UNFPA study highlighted higher rates of psychological distress in young women as age increases, due to the heaviness of social norms in the Palestinian society. 

A recent WHO survey on C-19 impact shows that people with pre-existing mental health issues become more susceptible to virus infections, and their infections are more often severe and can lead to death (WHO, 2020). Moreover, and based on a mixed study conducted by MdM-CH during 2019 on the risk factors of attempted suicide patients and prevention strategies in Palestine, it was found that 52% out of the total attempted suicide patients was youth amidst 16-25 years old. C-19 enlarges this vulnerable group to include infected patients, as the virus causes various mental and neurological complications, including delirium, agitation, and strokes (WHO, 2020). As such, the project will coordinate with WHO partners working on C-19 response to consolidate efforts and complement the work already implemented. We have also coordinated specifically with MdM-France and UNFPA, who have complementing activities but with different partners (for mobile clinics)/ and different hospitals (we will target ER departments with a focus on attempted/ suicide). 

The project activities will be implemented in: 
West Bank (Area A-B, & C, H2, & EJ) and the Gaza Strip, in an effort to reach people the most in need of MHPSS interventions, including the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. 

The project proposes activities based on the 5 speciﬁc objectives above mentioned, aiming to:
1.	Decrease stigma related to Self-Harm and Suicide, as well as stigma related to disability caused by attempted suicide, in Palestine and increase detection and referral of vulnerable cases to specialized MHPSS care, through speciﬁc actions at institutional (MoH hospitals) and community level (MCs and CMHCs).
2.	Enhance the SAWA Emergency hotline in detecting, supporting, and referring youths presenting self-harm and risky behaviors.
3.	Support HWC and SAWA MCs in front-line screening and detection of youth at risk of self-harm and/or suicide.
4.	Integrate MHPSS at the ER department of general hospitals in all oPt to better detect, respond, & refer risky behaviors to save lives and decrease YLD (years lived with disability), by emphasizing on mhGap intervention.
5.	Enhance specialized MHPSS provision of care for youth at CMHC's and specialized hospital level.

project_name: Food & Cash-based Assistance for Vulnerable Populations in Somalia for 2021
project_objective:
Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas.  As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation.  The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

Humanitarian needs could increase further in 2021 due to the influence of a La Niña that is currently developing (75 percent chance through Feb 2021). Potential drought conditions will likely develop as a result of below average 2020 Deyr (Oct-Dec), a harsh 2021 dry Jilaal (Jan-Mar) season and a possible delay and/or poor performance of the 2021 Gu (Apr-Jun). 

Continued emergency relief alongside a further scale up of support to increase resilience is required in order to avert the hardship situation. WFP is therefore seeking resources in 2021 to sustain the on-going efforts and enable households meet immediate food needs and help build resilience against shocks. WFP is planning to implement unconditional and conditional transfers to improve access to food under integrated multi sectoral assistance to meet needs of vulnerable girls and women, pregnant and lactating women, boys and men and leverage resources with other partners to meet the level of humanitarian assistance required. WFP will continue to participate in cluster, joint planning, assessments and regular meetings with other humanitarian actors in Somalia. WFP employs gender sensitive beneficiary targeting in all its projects and prioritizes female and single headed households. Community consultations are carried out with men and women to ensure that their voices are heard. Accountability to affected populations ensured through information sharing, surveys and beneficiary feedback mechanisms. Beneficiaries are targeted and registered through biometric SCOPE system that provides real time data.

project_objective: Ensure that NGOs operating in Somalia are receiving relevant and efficient support and preparation in terms of security through information and training
