project_name: Provision of WASH assistance to vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
The purpose of the WASH intervention is to deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services to most vulnerable people, and provide support to water, sanitation and sewage systems to ensure continuous services for affected people in Syria. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable populations throughout Syria through the delivery of a multi-faceted WASH response. The different components of NRC’s WASH project are intended to contribute to the following HRP WASH Sector Objectives: 1 = 1.3 repair and rehab of sanitation/sewage and solid waste; 2 = 2.1 distribution of hygiene materials and messaging on COVID; 2.3 – market based assistance for WASH services; 4= support for WASH facilities in schools. 

NRC will deliver this project through a direct implementation modality:
Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable conflict and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities and refugee/IDP returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the conflict. All interventions will seek to prioritize the most vulnerable households. Where appropriate, multi-sectoral vulnerability scoring techniques will be used that integrate vulnerability indicators

This project includes: 
-	Emergency response through the provision of one-off support as part of an integrated, multi-sector response in accordance with the Emergency Preparedness and Response Plans (EPRPs). Comprises of three Result Areas: Temporary WASH services, household assets (Hygiene NFIs) and support to Education in Emergencies (WASH Services for Temporary Learning Spaces).
-	The provision of medium-term shelter support at household and settlement-level to populations living in and out-of-camps. Comprises of two result areas:  Provision of WASH infrastructure, services and hygiene items in camps and communal shelters. 
-	The provision of longer-term assistance at household and settlement-level in urban and peri-urban out-of-camp areas. Comprises of three result areas: community WASH infrastructure and services, rehabilitation of household WASH facilities, and school rehabilitation (WASH Facilities) (see NRC’s Education project submission).
Project will include consultation with community, KIIs as well as with relevant authorities. Special attention will be given to ensuring that interventions are accessible by all and that there are functional complaint and feedback mechanisms set in place.

project_name: Increased access to education for out of school IDP and rural children in Puntland and South Central Somalia
project_objective: According to education cluster need analysis note 2021, an estimated three-million school-aged children and youth (six-18 years) are out‐of‐school. Enrolment rates are lowest for the most vulnerable children such as girls, rural and internally displaced children (IDP). Middle Shabelle and Mudug are part of the regions with the lowest attendance rates. Other locations with high out of school children includes areas that host Internally Displaced Persons including Galkayo and Bosasso and hard to reach rural areas such as Callula, Qandala among others. Children with disability are cut off from mainstream education system. The project will target rural/hard to reach areas and IDP locations to address this gap. Girls are disproportionally being negatively affected, due to increased chores and responsibilities, as well as GBV risks including FGM, early marriage, sexual and physical violence. In Somalia’s patriarchal society where gender inequality shapes gender roles and responsibilities, girls’ education is barely prioritized by caregivers. Girls consistently face greater challenges to accessing education. While the gender parity for enrollment at primary school level is 0.91 (1 is equal enrolment) it drops to 0.83 at the secondary level. In times of crisis such as the current economic crisis due to COVID 19, girls are the first victims of family’s economic stress, experiencing school dropout and early marriage. Other barriers that affect girls’ access and retention in school include; lack of sanitary kits, unfriendly school latrine for use during menstrual periods, harassment from boys among others. The project intends to work at school, family and community level to mitigate barriers faced by girls to continue their education. At the school level, the project will work with teachers to promote gender responsive and inclusive teaching practices and with CECs to promote a conducive learning environment for all children. In particular the provision of education materials and food rations will directly address economic barriers to girls’ education. The rehabilitation of WASH facilities at school will be done with a gender and disability lens to ensure that girls, including those with disabilities, are safe and feel comfortable to go to school, including when they are menstruated. The provision of sanitary kits will contribute to address to prevent adolescent girls’ absenteeism during their periods.   The strong focus on protection will ensure that girls are safe when going to school. COVID-19 school closure had affected 1.1M children enrolled in the schools across the country from March to August 2020. This impacted not only their learning but also their wellbeing as schools also contribute to psychosocial wellbeing and protection of learners. When families cannot afford to pay tuition or other expenses associated with education, children drop out of school. These repercussions can lead to child labor, child marriage and other negative outcomes, RI will use Cash assistance to address the economic barriers to education. Barriers to access for children with disabilities are considerable and includes negative attitudes towards children with disabilities, unfavorable learning environments compounded by teachers lacking training on inclusive education, bullying by peers among others. An estimated 216,004 school aged children in need of humanitarian assistance are living with some form of disability though there is insufficient data on children with disability. The project will train teachers on inclusive education and create positive learning environment for children with disability and work with school management to ensure school facilities are disability friendly. Schools will be supported to serve as a critical entry point for critical lifesaving services, including access to safe drinking water, food, AWD/cholera prevention, protection mechanisms and psychosocial support which is critical for learners to recover from crisis.

project_name: Réponse d’urgence aux besoins de santé, nutrition et santé mentale pour les  sinistrées à cause des  inondations dans le DS de Niamey 4, au Niger
project_objective:
L’objectif principal du projet est de réduire les risques de protection et préserver la vie et la dignité des personnes sinistrées fournissant une assistance holistique en santé et en NFI. Le projet veut réduire la morbidité et mortalité évitable par la prise en charge des maladies courantes, l’appui psychosocial, la vaccination et la prévention des maladies liées à la promiscuité, à la mauvaise hygiène et à l’insalubrité du milieu y compris le COVID-19. Cela améliorera les conditions de vie des sinistrés dans le site d’hébergement (Hippodrome) par l’organisation de l’offre de soins par le déploiement d’une clinique mobile permanente ainsi que la collecte et l’évacuation des déchets, l’approvisionnement régulier en eau, l’entretien des toilettes et la fourniture des produits d’hygiène aux ménages. 
Ensuite, pour améliorer les conditions de survie des sinistrés, le projet procèdera à la distribution des biens non alimentaires (NFI) tels que nattes, couvertures, seaux, casseroles, gobelets, moustiquaires, bidons, jet d’ustensiles de cuisine.
Enfin, l’action s’appuiera sur le comité de protections locales dont les membres recevront une mise à jour sur les aspects de premiers secours psychologiques et accompagnés par l’équipe de psychologues du projet pour réduire les risques de protection. De même, les kits de dignité seront distribués aux filles et femmes en âges de procréer, afin de réduire leur vulnérabilité et assurer leur hygiène intime. Les principaux résultats attendus sont :
Résultat 1 – Les risques de protection sont réduits sur le site et les cas de protection et de violences basées sur le genre sont pris en charge de façon adéquate.
- Séances de sensibilisation sur le risque de protection et de maladie liées à l’insalubrité et la promiscuité
- Distribution de kit de dignité pour 880 filles et femmes en âge de procréation et NFI à 850 familles, les plus vulnérables
- Prise en charge psychosociale et référencement pour une prise en charge complémentaire (médicale, judiciaire, sécuritaire et insertion socio-économique)

Résultat 2 – La morbi-mortalité évitable est réduit par la prise en charge médicale des courantes, le soutien psychosocial, la vaccination et la prévention des maladies liées à la promiscuité, à la mauvaise hygiène et à l’insalubrité du milieu y compris le COVID-19.
- Déploiement d’une clinique mobile permanente pour l’offre des soins médicaux et le soutien psychosocial aux sinistrés dans la ville
- Référencement des cas graves ou avec complications vers le CSI et hôpital national
- Appui psychosocial aux victimes des inondations
- Sensibilisation sur la disponibilité des services, les risques d’épidémies et troubles psychosociaux (santé mentale)

project_name: Acción integral contra las minas en Antioquía, Boyacá, Cauca, Casanare, Caquetá, Meta y Nariño.
project_objective: El proyecto busca brindar una respuesta integral (acompañamiento jurídico, acompañamiento psicosocial, rehabilitación física, inclusión socio-económica, educación al riesgo de minas y desminado civil humanitario) a las necesidades de los sobrevivientes y las víctimas indirectas de minas y restos explosivos de guerra, las personas con discapacidad y otras personas vulnerables en situaciones de conflicto, post conflicto o crisis prolongada, teniendo en cuenta los diferentes impactos en los hombres, mujeres, niños y niñas en los departamentos de Antioquía, Boyacá, Cauca, Casanare, Caquetá, Meta y Nariño.

project_name: Providing critical life-saving GBV prevention and response Services for Crisis -affected women and girls in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The project aims to provide critical life serving GBV response and prevention services through the provision of comprehensive case management including psychosocial support services, legal services, medical care, safety and security within UNFPA established One-Stop Centers (OSC), other UNFPA supported GBV service provision centres and Health facilities as well as enhance referrals where GBV services are not available.
The project will strengthen existing GBV referral systems and establish new ones where there is none to ensure survivors receive the recommended care. 
UNFPA will implement Women and Girls Friendly Space programming as an entry point for women and girls to receive more psychosocial support and other empowerment activities. Cram activities, such as knitting, beadwork, crocheting and embroidering bed sheets, and tea discussions, will be introduced as the women often enjoy these activities, so they are a good way to bring them together encourage conversation and relationship-building with each other. On the other hand, some of these activities will be introduced as income-generating activities to allow women and girls to earn some income to meet their basic needs and referrals for livelihood support with other programmes supporting women and girls. 
Response services will complement Dignity Programming, which will be used as an entry point to bring women and girls together to discuss important issues such as GBV risks, receive information on available GBV and SRH services and targeted assistance and referrals for livelihood projects available in the project areas.
The project will also support existing GBV prevention activities by engaging communities through awareness-raising and focusing on transforming harmful social norms that contribute to gender inequality and conducting GBV assessments and coordinated GBV safety audit. 
Prevention and response strategies will also include men to increase the understanding of the value of gender equity and promote long-lasting changes in gender relations. Thus engaging men and boys in GBV prevention activities will also be supported by the project. 
Also, the project will provide capacity building to frontline service providers on GBV guiding principles. This project will also support the training of non-GBV actors on minimum standards of GBV in emergencies in locations where GBV actors are not in the area.
All awareness-raising will consider the COVID 19 prevention measures, including crucial prevention messages on the same. The numbers of beneficiaries per session will be reduced to ensure social distancing is possible. The project will ensure that all beneficiaries are reached by increasing the numbers of sessions and megaphones in the community. Staff will be trained to refer beneficiaries who show signs and symptoms of COVID 19 to the nearest health facility for support.
It is important to note that as a result of the degradation of community protection systems and the inadequate GBV lifesaving services, women and girls have increased exposure to various forms of violence, including rape, sexual assault, psychological abuse, physical violence, child and forced marriage, denial of opportunities, resources and services where some basic services exist. Also, livelihood options are increasingly limited due to the ongoing conflict, exacerbated with COVID 19, disproportionately affecting adolescent girls and young women, resorting to harmful coping mechanisms that include child marriage, survival sex and sexual exploitation and abuse.
Survivors urgently need to access specialized services, including case management and psychosocial support services. A clear referral pathway needs to be established to facilitate the survivors' access to critical life-saving services. 
In the areas with critical humanitarian needs, the health situation of women and girls is made worse by limited access to services or non-existence.

project_name: Emergency Food Assistance in Gaza
project_objective: The unique socio-economic conditions of blockade, with its movement restrictions and destruction of productive capacity, are further compounded by repeated cycles of conflict and political instability and now the COVID-19 pandemic, undercutting employment and livelihood opportunities in the Gaza Strip and abroad. UNRWA’s emergency food assistance operation provides a critical humanitarian lifeline to over one million Palestine refugees who depend on food aid to meet their most basic food security needs. It accounts for approximately 200,000 Palestine refugee families including families with persons with disabilities and female headed households. In quarterly bases, eligible families will receive a food basket that is composed of a range of basic food commodities. Through its well-established monitoring system, UNRWA will continue to evaluate the food distribution system including the distribution modality that follows strict safety and security measures responding to changing environment around COVID-19 emergency, while guaranteeing a fair, equal and consistent support to food-insecure Palestine refugees in Gaza.

project_name: Projet de réponse aux besoins alimentaires et d’amélioration des moyens d'existences des personnes réfugiées centrafricains dans le département de la Kadey (EST - Cameroun)
project_objective:
Action Contre la faim (ACF), dans le but de contribuer à la réduction de l’insécurité alimentaire dans la région de l’Est, propose de couvrir les déficits alimentaires de base à travers une approche Cash and Food vouchers et de renforcer les moyens d’existence des ménages à travers l’amélioration de la production (distribution de semence céréalière). L’action pour objectif d’adresser les besoins alimentaires de base identifiés chez les réfugiés centrafricains vulnérables installés dans la Kadey suite à l’instabilité politique et l’insécurité dans les zones frontalières de la RCA et du Cameroun. Elle vise également à appuyer les bénéficiaires à contribuer dans la production des denrées alimentaire au niveau des communauté d’accueil. Afin de diminuer la pression sur les ressources alimentaires.

Cette réponse est basée sur les besoins humanitaires identifiés par le HNO 2020-2021, et la projection des besoins mené par le MINADER en Juillet 2020. De près de plus de 150 000 réfugiés centrafricains qui seront dans une situation d’insécurité alimentaire sévère dans la région de l’Est pour lapériode de soudure de 2021. Pour cela, Un apport alimentaire à hauteur 60 000 FCFA par ménage vulnérable identifié (cf : seuil de survie, ZME de la région) ainsi qu’un apport en semence céréalière de 2,5 Kg par ménage réfugié ayant accès à la terre pour la campagne vivrière 2021. 
Pour la couverture des besoins alimentaire de base via cash & vouchers, les ménages recevront 70% de du montant ci-dessus mentionné en cash pour l’achat des produits secs et 30% en vouchers pour l’achat des produits frais dans les principaux marchés du département. Ces montant seront transférer via le système YUP (mobile money pour le cash) et le système électronique Kache/RedRose pour les fresh food vouchers. Pour les semences, chaque bénéficiaire ayant soit accès un accès la terre, soit un accès au métayage, recevra 2,5 kg de semence céréalière en amont du semis de la campagne agricole de mars 2021. Ce projet aura pour effet immédiat de:
•	Couvrir le déficit alimentaire des ménages vulnérables impacter par les chocs dans les départements classés en crise alimentaires dans la région
•	Relancer les marchés alimentaires locaux impacter par le disfonctionnement occasionner par la crise de la COVID 19
•	D’appuyer la relance de la production agricole et améliorer la disponibilité alimentaire dans la Kadey

Le projet cible 11 900 femmes et hommes (soit 3 000 ménages) dans le département répartis dans 3 communes: 4 550 à Kentzou, 4 200 à Ketté et 3150 à Ouli. project_name: Population affected by displacement increase ability to exercise and enjoy legal identity & HLP rights and achieve durable solutions in far North region
project_objective:
The main objective of this project is to improve access to legal identity and housing, land and property rights for returnees, displaced persons, refugees and host communities in Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga and Logone-et-Chari divisions in Far North region of Cameroon. 
Violence perpetrated by armed groups in the Far North of Cameroon has led to forced displacement of populations and caused many human rights concerns. In Round 21 of the DTM, a total of 78,386 households of 494,144 individuals were identified, including 321,886 IDPs, 48,769 out-of-camp refugees and 123,489 returnees. The mobile population in the region increased by 8% compared to the previous round (December 2019). This increase confirms the worsening climatic and security conditions in the Far North in recent months, leading to more displacement. The Abuja Action Statement was signed in 2016 between the four countries of the Lake Chad Basin and is highlighting the issues of Protection of IDPs and host communities in the region. 
For instance, according to the National Civil Status Registration Office (BUNEC), an estimated 400,000 pupils in the Far North do not have birth certificates and more than 41,000 pupils in the last year of primary school will not be able to take national examinations during the academic year 2019/2020 due to lack of birth certificates. Moreover, according to a baseline study conducted in July/August 2019 by NRC in 20 localities of the Far North region, a rate of 31,5% birth registration was reported including 23,2% for women and 42% for men. According to men, women, girls and boys, during 2020 November assessment, the birth certificate remains by far the civil document they need most. The National Identity Card (CNI) comes second for both women and men. The reasons mostly given by respondents to explain the low birth registration rate and low possession of civil documents in the region are the lack of income; the increased distance to civil registration centers as many have been closed due to the conflict so people have to go further; as well as the limited knowledge on procedures and conditions to obtain legal and civil documentation by refugees and IDPs.  However, for the community as a whole, COVID has not brought about any change in this process.
According to NRC assessment in august 2019 made in 20 villages affected by displacement in the Far North region, only 21% of displaced persons reported having secured access to farming land. Moreover, conflicts between IDPs/refugees and host communities are frequent in these localities. 20,6% of people affected by displacement has access to land with a certain level of security of tenure, and 50 % of refugees reported having experienced HLP related conflicts with host communities. In general, IDPs and refugees arrange informal agreements to access land or rent houses and farms. As such tenure is rather insecure, this can result in forced evictions. Another HLP issue in the Far North is related to military operations conducted by the Cameroon army against armed groups. In fact, trenches were dug by the army to hinder armed groups from entering the Cameroonian territory. Those military operations affected around 7500 households who were either evacuated from their homes and access to their farming lands was blocked. 
The project targets to reach 7100 persons (3479 M, 3621 F) including 3550 IDPs (1740 M, 1811 F); 710 refugees (348 M, 362); 1420 Host communities (696 M, 724 F); 1420 Host Communities (696 M, 724 F). Assistance will target primary children in exam classes, girls, child heads of households, women heads of households, the elderly, widowed women, and people living with disabilities.

project_name: Provision of essential non-food items and shelter assistance to most vulnerable families in north-west Syria
project_objective:
This project aims to support the SNFI response to the immediate needs of the most vulnerable displaced populations in northwest Syria through the (1) distribution of essential non – food items (NFIs) and (2) improve the basic infrastructure and shelter conditions in and out of camps.
The distribution of NFI activities include:
I. Provision of essential NFIs to 60,000 households (300,000 individuals) in northwest Syria through IOM’s rapid response mechanism (RRM) in coordination with the SNFI and CCCM clusters (Sub activity 1.1.1) through both in-kind and cash modalities. 
II. Provision of tents to 20,000 households (100,000 individuals) in northwest Syria through IOM’s RRM in coordination with the SNFI and CCCM clusters (sub-activity 1.3.2).
III. Providing procurement, storage and logistics support to humanitarian partners operating inside Syria under the Single Source Procurement (SSP) pipeline, supplying 58,572 NFI kits to reach 292,860 individuals (Sub activity 1.1.1). 
IV. Provision of 30,000 winter cash payments for NFIs and winter clothing, reaching 150,000 individuals (Winterization) (Sub activity 1.2.1).

The basic infrastructure and shelter activities include:
I. Rehabilitation of 2,000 unfinished shelter units (Sub Activity 1.4.2)
II. Repair of 2,000 damaged shelter units (Sub Activity 2.1.1)
III. Winterization of 4,000 family tents through internal thermal insulation, external weatherproofing, and raising the ground raising and levelling through gravelling (Sub Activity 1.2.2) 
IV. Repair of 1,200 damaged shelter units in collective centres (Sub Activity 1.4.1)
V. Construction of 600 transitional shelter units (Sub Activity 2.1.3)
VI. Camp infrastructure upgrades for 30 informal sites. Infrastructure works include gravelling of roads, construction/rehabilitation of drainage channels and culverts, gravelling of tents off the ground (Sub Activity 1.3.3)
For the shelter activities, the project intends to reach 109,000 individuals in Idleb and Aleppo governorates. 
Overall, the project intends to reach 1,044,000 individuals targeting most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls and prioritize family members with high vulnerabilities according to the beneficiary selection criteria (IDP status, no source of income and support, persons with disabilities, elderly, female/single/child-headed households) and identified priority geographic locations).

project_name: Providing multi-sectoral assistance in and improving living conditions of IDP sites in north-west Syria
project_objective:
IOM CCCM activities plan to contribute to all the four CCCM Sector objectives for 2021 and to improve the coordination of humanitarian lifesaving, multi-sectoral assistance.
The project aims to address the Objective 1 through:
• Maintaining and managing three Reception Centres (RCs);
• Maintaining and managing eleven Planned Camps (PCs);
• Implementing small scale care and maintenance activities in 25 informal sites; and
• Identifying and collecting information about IDP sites in Idleb and Rural Aleppo, including multi-sectoral gap analysis and referral to IOM Cross-Border Unit for multi-sectoral response and assistance.

The project plans to meet the Objective 2 through:
• Enhancing camp management capacity of camp management in informal settlements in Idleb and Rural Aleppo under the Site Management Support (SMS) project; and
• Enhancing camp management capacity of NGOs through the provision of remote CWC and community engagement trainings for humanitarian workers based in Syria.

The project would contribute to the Objective 3 through:
• Enhancing communal capacity of informal settlements in Idleb and Rural Aleppo to address fire risk through the provision of fire safety measures and training under the SMS project.
Finally, the project aims to meet the objective 4 through:
• Collecting information on IDP movements and displacements in Idleb and Rural Aleppo and reporting to Cluster members.
The project will be directly managed, in cooperation with CCCM Cluster Coordinator, by IOM Turkey cross border team based in Gaziantep.  IOM will work in partnership with well experienced local NGOs in each specific activity in camps and camp-like settings as implementing partners, selected from active members of the CCCM Cluster.
In case of underfunding, IOM CCCM will prioritize the support of the affected community in the 11 planned camps by ensuring the continuation of multi-sectoral response and including strengthening the community governance, care and maintenance, fire safety and camp management capacity. Currently, the 11 camps are hosting highly vulnerable beneficiaries selected during the project designing and still in need of humanitarian support.
The continuation of CM activities in receptions centres will be highly impacted by the reduction of funding. In that case, IOM CCCM will work closely with both partners and beneficiaries to identify better shelter solutions for the affected community hosted in RCs. This will require assessment on beneficiaries’ intentions and ‘needs along with the identification of viable shelter solutions before closing the centres. 
Additionally, the reduction of CCCM activities in informal sites will likely increase their vulnerability- having already been suffering from the lack of or limited humanitarian assistance- IOM will be unable to continue the coordination of an integrated response in case of a fire or flood incident, including referral to protection or health partners. This will also affect IOM's ability to provide training in first aid and site risk reduction, including distribution of fire and first aid equipment, to the affected community living in informal and self-settled sites.

project_name: Provision of humanitarian WASH assistance and improving basic WASH infrastructure in IDP sites in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to support the WASH response of the most vulnerable displaced populations in Northwest Syria through implementing the following set of activities:   

i) Provision of emergency WASH services to 40 IDP sites (informal camps, planned camps, and reception centres) regularly supporting 80,000 individuals (40, 800 females, 39,200 males, 10,400 young children (<5), 28,000 children (5-17), 33,600 adults (18-59), 8,000 elderly (>59), 22,400 persons with disabilities). Activities include the provision of water trucking, solid waste management, desludging, care and maintenance of latrines, provision of water storage tanks, garbage containers, and WASH NFI kits, as well as hygiene promotion sessions.  

ii) Construction/rehabilitation of sewage networks, including the construction of septic tanks to provide an initial treatment of wastewater produced in informal camps. This specific intervention will target 15 informal IDP sites supporting 30,000 individuals (15,300 females, 14,700 males, 3,900 young children (<5), 10,500 children (5-17), 12,600 adults (18-59), 3,000 elderly (>59), 8,400 persons with disabilities).  

iii) Enhanced water quality assurance, operation, and maintenance of water supply systems through the provision of solar energy in eight IDP sites, supporting 22,000 individuals (11,220 females, 10,780 males, 2,860 young children (<5), 7,700 children (5-17), 9,240 adults (18-59), 2,200 elderly (>59), 6,160 persons with disabilities). 

iv) Implementation of COVID-19 response activities in collective centres and planned camps through the provision of water trucking and the distribution of COVID-19-adapted hygiene kits. In total, the COVID-19 response will target 80,000 individuals (40, 800 females, 39,200 males, 10,400 young children (<5), 28,000 children (5-17), 33,600 adults (18-59), 8,000 elderly (>59), 22,400 persons with disabilities).  

Overall, the project is supporting the following strategic objectives set out by the WASH Cluster:  
-Support to water, sanitation/sewage and solid waste management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria,  
-Deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services, and improve hygienic behaviour and practices of the most vulnerable people.  

In total, the project aims to target 110,000 individuals individuals (56,100 females, 53,900 males, 14,300 young children (<5), 38,500 children (5-17), 46,200 adults (18-59), 11,000 elderly (>59), 30,800 persons with disabilities) in Idleb and Aleppo governorates.

project_name: Enhanced Resilience to Food Security and Improved livelihoods In Somalia
project_objective:
The protracted humanitarian crisis in Somalia is among the most complicated around the globe. Ongoing armed conflict and insecurity, with recurring climate shocks, has resulted in protracted economic vulnerability across the country as well as fragmentation and weakening governance structure. Violence and limited access to humanitarian assistance in hard-to-reach areas propel large number of Somali moving toward urban and peri-urban areas, straining the limited resources of the host communities.  Food security and nutritional needs remain high in all of Somalia.
According to the UN,Without sustained assistance, up to 3.5 million people in Somalia could face severe food insecurity through September 2020.COVID-19 control measures and the associated worsening of socioeconomic conditions are further eroding the protection environment in Somalia.Desert Locust affected rural livelihoods in Northern and Central regions and presents a risk (serious) to the South. The 2020 Gu seasonal flooding (river flooding) contributed to loss and damage to property, housing, farmland and infrastructure.
WV is proposing an integrated assistance to rural and peri urban populations,including IDP populations with livelihoods assets support,cash assistance to help them rebuild their livelihoods and become more resilient to frequent shocks in Somalia.There is a possibility of the food security and nutrition situation worsening for the most vulnerable HHs in rural areas , as populations who are currently in IPC 2 are likely to deteriorate to IPC 3, and IPC3 to IPC 4 if they lack assistance. 
To prevent further deterioration of productive assets and mitigate the need for HHs to engage in negative coping strategies to meet basic food needs, WV will target IPC 3 and IPC 4 populations in the proposed regions.
WV will engage project participants during selection of infrastructure to rehabilitate under the CfA activities to ensure that only community owned structures are prioritized and targeted to ensure sustainability and continued ownership of the structures after rehabilitation. In order to ensure that the assets rehabilitated are well maintained and remain operational beyond the project period, the project will put in place the following measures: 1- The project will only target to rehabilitate infrastructure (e.g. feeder roads, check dams and water catchments) that is important to the community and contribute to improving HHs food security and self-reliance. 2- The project will put in place community project management committees and train them on their roles and responsibilities, technical & managerial skills and operations & maintenance of rehabilitated assets to ensure they continue applying the same beyond the project life. 3- The project will be horizontally linked with relevant government institutions and line ministries where they exist to provide technical support and oversight for selected CfA activities. This will ensure continuation of support from the government and other prospective donors beyond the project period.

project_name: Vulnerable and at-risk girls and boys in IDP camps and in host communities have access to quality child protection      prevention and response     services
project_objective:
Boys and girls including adolescents, children with disabilities in IDPs and host communities, facing life-threatening risks of abuse, neglect, violence, exploitation, and severe distress have access to well-coordinated and disability, gender-sensitive quality child protection services. This will be achieved through   strengthening community-based child protection structures to raise awareness, prevent, respond and refer cases of violence against children, providing case management support and referral services to children with protection concerns including SGBV, providing FTR services to UASC and alternative care arrangements. In addition, families under stress will receive activities that ensure the mental health and psycho-social wellbeing of affected children, through intensive child protection activities within child friendly spaces including structured child resilience building sessions and other psychosocial support for children; parenting sessions with care providers; and training to increase capacity of staff and key government stakeholders. Trainings on child protection, SGBV and MHPSS will be delivered to sector staff (Health, Education, Nutrition, WASH and Livelihoods) to ensure mainstreaming of CP and improved coordination of services. Efforts will be made to ensure equal participation of minority groups like excluded clans, women, girls and as well as people and children with disabilities. According to Somalia Humanitarian Needs (HNO) 2020 Overview, an estimated 480,000 people in need live with disability; physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments, and as a result, face serious risks of exploitation, ill-treatment, neglect and stigmatization. The 2021 HNO states that families of children disabilities regularly chain their children and in the assessment 28% of caregivers stated that the practice is necessary to protect the children from harm such as car accidents, falling into pits/trenches, discrimination, physical and sexual abuse, hurting other people or being hurt.
Explosive hazard accidents continue to affect the civilian population across the regions in South and Central Somalia. Although the Federal government of Somalia recently ratified the treaty on Convention on the Rights of People with Disabilities, persons and children with disabilities continue to be largely absent from the political and development agenda and their needs are not properly addressed by the authorities. Due to prevailing misconceptions about disability, both children and adults with disabilities are stigmatized, segregated and referred to with derogatory names. Survivors of landmines/explosive remnants of war (ERW) and other persons with disabilities continue to suffer the absence of adequate services including emergency medical care, rehabilitation and reintegration. 
Children with disabilities face many barriers to inclusion including inaccessible physical environment, lack of awareness in the communities, insufficient teaching skills, negative attitude and stigma, poverty, and a severe shortage of assistive devices and mobility aids. Girls with disabilities are particularly vulnerable, as boys with disabilities tend to get the few opportunities available.
The project will ensure that children with disabilities are actively targeted during the selection of most vulnerable children. It will also ensure community awareness raising is done on issues of protecting children with disabilities against sexual abuse. Laws adversely affecting children with disabilities will be part of the advocacy on legal reforms plan.
SC will comply with the relevant sector standards and promote good practice by including PSEA and child safeguarding measures at all phase and programming activity. SC shall promptly and confidentially record and report allegations of sexual exploitation and abuse, or any reasonable suspicion or allegations of child safeguarding violations of which it would have been informed of or become aware of to the donor.

Strengthen the collective humanitarian response through effective, agile and efficient coordination, based on humanitarian principles in North-West and South-West regions
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to strengthen the coordination of the humanitarian response in Cameroon to save lives, protect the most vulnerable and improve the resilience of populations. With the worsening crisis in the North-West and South-West regions, Cameroon now faces three complex humanitarian crises affecting eight of Cameroon's ten regions. The impact of these three crises on the living conditions of the affected populations is reinforced by pre-existing structural vulnerabilities that hamper their recovery, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions. In the North-West and South-West regions, on-going violence has had a major impact on the regional economy. Violence and insecurity have resulted in major displacement, affecting agricultural yields in the North-West and the abandonment of large parts of fruit, palm and rubber plantations in the South-West. However, unlike the North-West, the South-West has maintained a certain level of economic activities. Ethnic and political tensions between farmers and herders persist. The border with Nigeria, Africa’s greatest economy, is officially closed, making trade increasingly difficult. In the North-West and South-West regions, high levels of insecurity continue. The presence of national security structures - police, gendarmerie, army - is concentrated along the main roads and cities, leaving most rural areas under the influence of NSAGs.
The complexity and the scope of these crises therefore require more effective coordination, adapted to the different intervention areas and based on humanitarian principles. OCHA Cameroon's coordination project will thus make it possible to achieve a humanitarian response that is better funded, more strategic and that centralizes human rights and the protection of people in the North-West and South-West regions. It will also enable a better complementarity between emergency actions and development programs, in order to fight together the humanitarian needs and their underlying causes. To this end, OCHA will provide the essential services of disseminating key information products, coordinating the Humanitarian Programming Cycle and facilitating joint multisectoral needs assessments. Its presence in Yaoundé, Bamenda and Buea will enable it to provide decisive support to coordination mechanisms and promote coherence between operational issues in the field and strategic decision-making bodies. This key position will also enable it to advance the overriding considerations of the Centrality of Protection and Cross-cutting Protection, Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and nexus humanitarian development. From its sub-offices in the North-West and South-West regions, OCHA will also support the scaling up of the response in these regions, including through the management of CMCoord and humanitarian access responsibilities, as well as capacity building of local responders.

project_name: Increase preparedness and improve response for affected women and children from C19 at Quarantine Centers and home quarantine in the Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
This project is ensuring that protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic containment measures and deteriorated health, socio-economic conditions targeting 12,680 beneficiaries in Gaza Strip. 
Through this Action, Save the Children (SCI), and in partnership with AISHA, seeks to facilitate the access of vulnerable women and children in the quarantine centres and home quarantine to GBV and MHPSS support services.  This will directly contribute to improving the level of progress towards recovery in addition to enhancing the resilience of the people during the current and upcoming stage of COVID-19 breakout. 

The project will provide case management and support mechanisms using appropriate remote modalities according to the different categories of target groups.  This is  to ensure continuity of services in providing child-friendly and holistic care for children experiencing violence.  

Moreover, the project will provide Child Protection, including MHPSS, Multi sectoral Services and cash assistance to children and adults, focusing on communities affected by quarantine and home isolation. 

Additionally, SCI and its partner AISHA will maintain safe family-based alternative care arrangements and other mechanisms using appropriate remote modalities to prevent family separation and identify and refer unaccompanied and separated children. Moreover, the project will provide capacity development for specialized child protection service providers on remote counseling services during COVID-19.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination, Advocacy and Common Services in South Sudan
project_objective: OCHA plays a critical role in the leadership and coordination of humanitarian action in South Sudan based on a people-centered approach.  OCHA brings together different stakeholders to facilitate coordination and analyze the evolving needs and adjust response operations where needed. This includes assessing and documenting humanitarian needs, negotiating humanitarian access, and compiling and synthesizing qualitative and quantitative data to produce a wide range of information products.

project_name: Essential and Life-saving integrated Health assistance for Vulnerable Populations in Somalia
project_objective:
The project will provide essential and life-saving integrated health assistance to vulnerable communities in Awdal, Bay, Bakool, Banadir, Bari, Galgaduud, Hiraan, Lower Juba, Mudug, Nugaal, Sanaag, Sool, Toghdeer, Woqooyi Galbeed and aims to reach a total of 455,658 IDPs and host communities contributing to 16% of the cluster target in the targeted geographies. This will be achieved by providing both fixed and mobile health services supporting 4 regional hospitals, 11 Referral Health Centers, 103 Primary Health Centers/Health Centers/MCHs, 140 Primary Health Units as well as 101 mobile clinic sites.
The project will seek to contribute to a 5% reduction in excess morbidity and mortality rates from crisis-driven diseases and outbreaks among target vulnerable communities by end of 2021 while scaling up provision of regular health services and providing safe, dignified and meaningful access life-saving assistance (provided directly or through referral) with sensitivity to age, gender and disability status.
This will be achieved by supporting the Somalia governments and communities to be able to delivery essential package of health free services to communities with acute humanitarian needs using developments programs as a platform for immediate responses. The proposed project has also been designed with full awareness of the prevailing gender norms and deeply rooted gender inequalities in Somalia that limit women and girls from accessing basic services such as health and nutrition, and expose them to a higher risk of Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV). In order to address these challenges, Save the Children will identify and work to remove the physical, cognitive and social barriers by collaborating closely with the communities and particularly the influencers and gatekeepers. We will also address the intersectionality of vulnerability factors, for example women with disabilities or from minor clans who are likely to face multiple levels of discrimination. Save the Children will also include appropriate child safeguarding measures at every phase and within every programming activity.

project_name: Promoting the inclusion and access of Children with Disabilities to education in the emergency context of the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The current context in the oPt is marked by imposed closures, high political tension linked to Annexation Plan, and an on-going global pandemic.  In the Gaza Strip, blockades and political division continue to marginalize the population and the lock-down imposed deteriorated the already fragile economic situation reaching a poverty rate of 54% of the population. In the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), the Education Cluster
identified children with disabilities as one the affected by the protracted and acute crisis: besides their lack of basic assistive devices and technologies that would facilitate their access to education and required psychosocial support (PSS) and remedial education. COVID-19 situation and the closure of schools pushed boys and girls with disabilities in special and mainstream schools to be neglected by the distance learning modalities due to the lack of its inclusivity enhancing the high risk of drop-out. Through its running education projects, HI piloted a distance learning modality (presented as good practice at the international IASC conference) that includes the use of online distance learning and offline education support for those families with no access to internet. The action will replicate and upscale the current experience to ensure children access to accessible and inclusive online and offline distance learning modalities.
Building on the previous experience the project’s objective is to increase the access to quality inclusive education for children with disabilities in improved education facilities. The first component focuses on community actors to identify and provide tailored services for out-of-school and those at risk of drop-out children with disabilities and their families to support children’s enrolment and continued access to education. The second component will aim at building the capacities of schools, teachers and parents to respond to the needs of affected children. The project falls under Education Cluster’s objectives 1) increase equitable safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children and 2) – Children and school staff in vulnerable schools are supported in preparing and responding to emergencies.  Through preventive measures, remedial programs and school-based, remote and outreach psychosocial services. HI will financially and technically support Teacher Creativity Center (TCC) as local implementing partner, that is a main actor in supporting the development of Inclusive Education in UNRWA and MoE schools, besides their networks with teachers and communities. The project will respond to the first and second Education Cluster objectives through the identification of out-of-school children, the provision of personal support for children with disabilities: enhance their mobility, provide visual and hearing assistive devices, transportation, school kits, education materials and stationaries, school-based, remote and outreach structured psychosocial services. HI will also support the provision of holistic services through referrals to other stakeholders. Furthermore, HI will aim to develop an enabling educational environment through the provision of technical support for mainstream and special education service providers. These will be supported to respond to the needs of affected children through the development of adapted processes and tools benefiting both children with and without disabilities. HI will further provide educational materials, tools, and resources and create a welcoming and accessible educational environment for children with and without disabilities.

project_name: Shelter and NFI Assistance for IDPs and host community members in Northern Syria.
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to address emergency and more sustainable shelter and NFI needs of vulnerable households with acute needs (both IDPs and host community
members) in Northeast and Northwest Syria. Through contractors, ACTED will rehabilitate private off-camp private shelter units in Ar-Raqqa, Aleppo and Idleb governorates. Ar-Raqqa governorate will also be targeted with Cash for repairs interventions to conduct small rehabilitation works under ACTED supervision and support. In addition, ACTED will address the needs of displaced households in IDP and last-resort sites, including newly displaced households, through the provision of tents, emergency shelter kits and tent insulation kits. Under this intervention, households will be provided with tents across Northeast Syria; while emergency shelter kits will be distributed in Idleb and Northern Aleppo governorates. Idleb governorate will also be targeted with the distribution of insulation kits across the northern and western camp clusters, to better equip the residents for winter. In addition, NFI kits, composed of tarpaulin, jerry can, mattresses/sleeping mats, blankets (single and double), solar lamps, floor mat, stove, cooking pot, bowl for food, and cutlery, will be distributed across Idleb and Northern Aleppo governorates, as well as winterization support kits, including heating fuel, starting in December 2021. The intervention will target a total of 139,361 beneficiaries under shelter activities, and 231,665 beneficiaries under NFI activities.

project_name: Enhancing access to safe water and basic sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Northern Syria.
project_objective:
According to the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), 12.2 million people in Syria are in need of WASH assistance, with the most severe needs concentrated in areas of ongoing conflict or areas with large numbers of IDPs. As a result, to address the needs of the most vulnerable households, this intervention will focus on providing targeted and effective WASH support in Northwest and Northeast Syria, combining elements of emergency response with the establishment of durable solutions. 
In-camp, where residents are heavily reliant on humanitarian assistance for their water needs, ACTED’s intervention will focus on life-saving WASH support and delivery of basic services for IDPs residing in camps across Aleppo, Idleb, and Al-Hasakeh governorates. This will include hygiene kits distribution, as well as emergency water trucking for camps and communities deprived of access to water networks. In addition, ACTED will continue its provision of in-camp sanitation services and solid waste management services, through the operation and maintenance of wastewater systems, the installation of latrine blocks, the collection and disposal of waste, and the deployment of communal bins.
Off-camp, ACTED’s intervention will integrate a more sustainable component, with a focus on long-term improvement of access to safe water sources, through the rehabilitation of WASH assets, such as water stations and boreholes, across NES and NWS. ACTED will work in close collaboration with local stakeholder, including technical department, to build their capacity to operate and maintained rehabilitated infrastructure.
To complement WASH services delivery, ACTED will organize hygiene promotion sessions, both in and out of camp, including sessions specifically dedicated to Covid-19. This intervention will benefit a total of approximately 389,580 individuals across Northern Syria.

project_name: Répondre aux besoins immédiats de sécurité alimentaire
project_objective:
En appui au Gouvernement et en coordination avec d'autres acteurs humanitaires, le PAM fournira une aide alimentaire aux hommes, femmes, garçons et filles les plus vulnérables dans les zones identifiées par l'ENSAN et le Cadre harmonisé comme les plus touchées par l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle. Cette assistance sera fournie sous forme de transferts en espèces (coupons de valeur) et / ou de distribution de nourriture en fonction de l'analyse coût-efficacité et de la faisabilité opérationnelle. Dans certains contextes, où certains produits pourraient ne pas être disponibles ou à un prix élevé sur certains marchés, le PAM optera pour une combinaison en nature et un soutien CBT. Le PAM encouragera la participation des femmes à tous les processus liés à la préparation, à la mise en œuvre et au suivi de la distribution. Elles seront incluses dans toutes les discussions liées à cette assistance afin que leurs vulnérabilités et exigences de protection spécifiques soient prises en compte. Le PAM continuera également à fournir une assistance technique aux institutions gouvernementales (CSA, SAP, MSAH, Jigisemejiri) pour l'analyse et le suivi de la sécurité alimentaire, et l'assistance en matière de sécurité alimentaire et de nutrition.
Le PAM se concentrera sur les zones caractérisées par des taux élevés d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle et ne bénéficiant que d’une faible couverture des besoins pendant la période de soudure par le Plan national de protection sociale. Des municipalités supplémentaires peuvent être identifiées en collaboration avec Jigisemejiri (programme national de protection sociale) selon les besoins, conformément à la stratégie nationale de réponse au COVID-19. Le ciblage proposé permettra d'élargir la couverture actuelle des filets nationaux de sécurité et, si les conditions le permettent, également du registre social (RSU) dans ces zones. Cette approche s'aligne sur le concept de protection sociale «adaptative» et s'articule autour de deux axes étroitement liés: 1) renforcer la résilience des ménages les plus vulnérables aux chocs; 2) Établir des liens avec le programme intégré de résilience.

project_name: Fourniture de services aériens humanitaires au Mali
project_objective:
1.	Malgré le besoin crucial d'aide humanitaire au Mali, il est devenu de plus en plus difficile pour le personnel humanitaire de fournir une assistance adéquate aux communautés vulnérables étant donné la situation sécuritaire précaire dans le centre et le nord du Mali. En effet, l'accès reste l'un des plus grands défis pour les partenaires humanitaires au Mali, en particulier pour la chaîne d'approvisionnement et la fourniture de services vitaux et d'assistance aux communautés touchées par le conflit ou déplacées dans le centre et le nord du pays. Bien que l'intensité de la violence soit plus faible qu'au plus fort de l'insurrection en 2012, les niveaux record de criminalité, de terrorisme et de conflit armé continuent d'entraver l'accès, avec des progrès limités suite à la signature de l'accord de paix et de réconciliation par toutes les parties au conflit en juin 2015. On observe notamment une recrudescence des incidents de sécurité, y compris ceux qui visent la communauté humanitaire depuis 2018, avec des incidents visant directement les travailleurs humanitaires ou les entrepreneurs enregistrés en 2020. Alors que le conflit et l'insécurité s'intensifient et s'étendent plus au sud du pays, les menaces d'une aggravation de la situation humanitaire augmentent également, risquant de dégrader davantage les conditions d'assainissement, d'hébergement, de santé et de sécurité alimentaire, d'autant plus que le nombre de personnes déplacées continue d'augmenter. 

2.	Les besoins humanitaires restent très élevés dans un contexte où l'accès en toute sécurité est un défi pour le personnel humanitaire. Les vastes distances, le manque d'infrastructures routières et l'insécurité rendent les voyages aériens indispensables pour que les acteurs humanitaires puissent accéder aux populations bénéficiaires. Les déplacements par route au Mali restent très risqués. Le trafic à destination et en provenance du nord du Mali est fréquemment affecté par les mines terrestres et les engins explosifs improvisés (EEI). Plusieurs routes sont contrôlées par des groupes armés, ce qui entrave l'accès aux communautés touchées. La détérioration des conditions de sécurité et la violence permanente ont entraîné de nouvelles restrictions aux mouvements déjà limités des organisations humanitaires dans le Nord et parfois la suspension des activités d'aide. 

3.	Le problème est aggravé par l'absence d'opérateurs aériens commerciaux dans le pays. Les UNHAS sont souvent le seul moyen d'entrer ou de sortir d'une zone d'opération. De plus, les organisations humanitaires ont accru leur présence sur l'ensemble du territoire malien, les agences des Nations Unies et les ONG ayant ouvert de nouveaux bureaux dans les régions du nord du pays en réponse à la détérioration du contexte humanitaire. 

4.	Le transport aérien joue un rôle essentiel pour permettre l'accès humanitaire aux populations bénéficiaires en raison du mauvais état des routes dans le nord du Mali. En conséquence, les opérations des UNHAS jouent un rôle clé dans le soutien de la capacité de la communauté humanitaire à mettre en œuvre et à contrôler un large éventail d'activités de secours dans certaines des zones les plus éloignées et les plus en difficulté du nord du Mali. Chaque mois, l'UNHAS, par le biais du fret aérien, apporte des médicaments, du courrier et d'autres articles de secours aux populations qui ont besoin d'aide dans tout le pays.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence pour les populations deplacées internes dans la province du Lac
project_objective:
Situé entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale, le bassin du lac Tchad couvre le Tchad, le Cameroun, le Niger et le Nigeria. Important bassin de production agro-pastorale et halieutique, le bassin du lac-Tchad repose sur un écosystème fragile mais avec une production variée et connaissant une démographie croissante. On estime ainsi à 2 million le nombre d’habitants vivant directement des ressources du bord du Lac. La Province du Lac est l’une des zones les plus vulnérables au Tchad car difficile d’accès, insuffisamment desservie par les services sociaux de base et sujette de façon récurrente aux effets du changement climatiques caractérisés par les sécheresses et les inondations qui sont parmi les aléas les plus importants. Les conséquences de catastrophes qu’elles engendrent pèsent lourdement sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages. A cela s’ajoute une crise qui perdure depuis 2009, causant de pertes en vies humaines, des déplacements forcés des populations, des pertes des actifs productifs, des pressions sur les ressources naturelles et une des articulations de l’économie engendrant ainsi des conséquences sur l’emploi en particulier pour les jeunes.
Dans la province du Lac, les attaques dans les villages par les groupes armés et les opérations militaires ont occasionné des nouveaux déplacements en 2020 et il y a plus de 336 000 personnes déplacées nécessitent une assistance alimentaire d’urgence
Ces événements ont, entre autres, entravé l’accès des populations aux productions vivrières et rentières et affectés les moyens de subsistance de ces populations vulnérables. La situation de cette zone reste préoccupante en matière de sécurité dans les zones insulaires, car le contexte continue d’être volatile et précaire.
Afin d’appuyer ces populations vulnérables, le PAM apportera une assistance alimentaire d’urgence a 336 124 personnes déplacées internes dans la province du Lac. Cette assistance alimentaire sera adaptée selon les résultats profilage socio-économique des ménages déplacés (extrêmement vulnérables, très vulnérables et moyennement vulnérables) vivant dans les départements de Fouli, Kaya et Mamdi. De plus, cette assistance sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: United Nations Humanitarian Air Service
project_objective:
Since 2018, the security situation in Burkina Faso drastically deteriorated with the expansion and intensification of activities of non-state armed groups (NSAGs), exploiting pre-existing inter-communal tensions. A further escalation was observed in 2020, with a greater toll on human lives and on vulnerable populations. The non-state armed groups (NSAGs) are fragmented, with multiple internal players; and there are increased external players linked with the regional dynamics (i.e. Central Sahel countries). This has led to massive population displacements and has had a severe impact on already vulnerable populations. 
As of November 2020, over 1 million persons have been displaced and new displacements are reported daily, marking a 250 percent increase in over a year. The security situation has had repercussions on the overall food and nutritional security of the country. Food security and nutritional situation has been impacted by the growing crisis affecting vulnerable populations. Particularly, the food security situation has observed an almost ten-fold increase in number of people in Cadre Harmonise / IPC Phase 3+ - therefore, people in need of food assistance.  
The unprecedented humanitarian emergency has left 2.9 million persons in need of humanitarian assistance – according to the draft revised Humanitarian response plan. Health services, schools and markets have been closed due to growing insecurity in several parts of the country, seriously affecting the population’s ability to sustain healthy lives. Across the country, over 95 health centers have closed and 199 are operating with reduced services, affecting over 1.2 million people.  No less than 2,512 schools were forced to shut down, depriving over 350,000 children of education.  COVID-19, and measures taken by the Government from March 2020, added another layer of vulnerability. 
Humanitarian access to vulnerable populations in need of assistance is restricted by threats posed by non-state armed groups, counterterrorism operations, the presence of Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) planted on roads and the damage or destruction of key road infrastructure (bridges targeted in attacks in the Sahel region for instance). In addition, access is hindered by restrictive counter-terrorism legislation preventing negotiation with NSAGs. Many humanitarian actors have left areas which remain impeded by serious access constraints. To safeguard neutrality and the perception of it, humanitarian workers in Burkina Faso do not use military escorts, particularly since the national Security Forces (FDS) remain the primary target of armed groups. 
In order to support the planned humanitarian response and enable access to the populations in need and project implementation sites, UNHAS aims to provide a safe, effective and efficient passenger air service to the entire humanitarian community and their implementing partners, principally NGOs, UN agencies, red cross/crescent movement, donor organizations and diplomatic missions.
Upon the need and decision of the Steering Committee, UNHAS currently offers three weekly flights rotations - Dori, Gorom-Gorom, Arbinda; Djibo, Titao, Ouahigouya; Fada N’Gourma, Gayéri – and special flights all departing from Ouagadougou airport. The service  is accessible to all humanitarian actors upon registration transporting personnel or cargo aimed to support targeted populations. A cost-recovery mechanism will be developed in 2021. Orientatively, the service will aim to transport over 3,500 passengers and 60 mt of cargo.

project_name: Strengthen Resilience building through Livelihoods improvement for IDPs, Returnees and Host communities in Yobe and Borno States, North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
The frequent conflicts, aggravating climatic conditions and COVID-19 pandemic are adversely affecting most socio-economic infrastructures and private business enterprises in the North-East BAY States (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe). There are inadequate levels of access to livelihoods, economic opportunities and basic public services (MSNA 2019). As a result, the deprivation of resources and market price skyrocketing are further fuelling inter-communal tensions between IDPs, returnees and host communities, prompting them to adopt negative coping mechanisms to meet their basic needs. 
	In light of the above, COOPI’s goal is to contribute to the economic and communal stabilization through synergic livelihoods activities and peace-building sessions. The project will target 25,630 beneficiaries distributed in 7 LGAs, notably Askira/Uba (Borno State), Bade, Damaturu, Geidam, Jakusko, Potiskum, Yunusari (Yobe State), which have been prioritized based on the levels of damages and service delivery burden with high numbers of returnees and IDPs in host communities. The project will put great emphasis on livelihoods rehabilitation of most vulnerable groups with a special attention to women and children who have been pre-identified through COOPI’s ongoing food assistance and CBT activities funded by other donors. In doing so, COOPI ensures to carry out its activities in close coordination with the ERL sector as well as in complementarity with the ongoing EU-funded ERL program (BRICC) in Yobe State. Furthermore, COOPI will cooperate with national/state authorities, most of which it has already developed MOUs with, providing capacity-building opportunities to government’s institutes, thus deeply contributing to the state system’s strengthening. Equally relevant, the proposed intervention will reflect the recommendations of the Yobe State Socio-Economic Reform Agenda (YOSERA), the Buhari Plan and the Borno State’s 25-year Development Framework.
	COOPI aspires to converge the livelihood and economic recovery action with other sectors, including conflict-mitigation, restoration of local government administration and rehabilitation of basic infrastructures, to foster social cohesion and the transition from emergency to long-term development. COOPI is committed to concretely apply the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus approach, forecasting a strong potential in the proposed LGAs where COOPI boasts a consolidated experience since 2015. In alignment with the 2021 ERL Sector's Objectives, COOPI will provide an integrated multi-sectoral intervention, promoting the protection of the conflict-affected population through participatory community engagement, in order to strengthen local resilience to vulnerabilities and to promote social cohesion, safe durable solutions and overall peaceful co-existence among IDPs, returnees and host communities. As a proof, to achieve its goals, COOPI will most rely on working through local NGOs, thus strongly contributing to the paramount localization process. Last but not least, COOPI will mainstream COVID-19 contingency measures in all its interventions to ensure the sustainability of its action.
