project_name: Provision of primary health services to vulnerable conflict-affected populations in Idleb and Aleppo
project_objective:
The proposed project will strengthen access to lifesaving and life-sustaining essential health services and COVID-19 response in northern Aleppo and northern Idleb.  The proposed activities are in line with the needs and gaps identified by beneficiaries and DDD assessments in the target locations as well as Health Custer priorities by providing life-saving humanitarian assistance and protection to the most vulnerable people with an emphasis on underserved areas with high severity of needs. It is also in line with HRP Strategic Objective 2: provide life-saving humanitarian assistance and protection to the most vulnerable people with an emphasis on underserved areas with high severity of needs.

DDD’s project focuses on strengthening service provision for the most vulnerable groups in urban settings and in and out of camps who have limited access to regular services, through a targeted comprehensive Essential Health Service Package: PHC services, SRH, and MHPSS, and COVID-19 testing through fixed clinics and laboratories. These services will be complemented by outreach services such as health promotion activities by Community Health Workers, home-based specialized medical care focused on people with chronic conditions, people living with disabilities, and at-risk pregnancies, as well as ongoing efforts to expand in-demand MHPSS services. PHC services will also be supported through DDD’s 4 laboratories. A total of 309,387 individuals are expected to directly benefit from this intervention (direct beneficiaries). An estimated 668,783 catchment population will indirectly benefit from the intervention. 

The project builds on existing DDD programmes and targets 17 locations currently served by DDD and partners in Afrin district in Aleppo (3 static, 3 mobile) and Harim district in Idleb (12 static) to both IDPs (in and out of camps) and residents in dire need of health services. In March 2021, these areas received among the highest IDPs to both camps and communities. Static PHCC's HeRAM codes are: DDD Sarmada PHC! G0703184, Morek Alaez camp PHCC/ Morek Alaez Camp!G0703051, Dier Hassan camp PHCC/ Dier Hassan Camp!G0703088, Aldana PHCC/ Aldana village!G0703087, Alsalam camp PHCC/ Alsalam Camp!G0703101, Qah village clinic/ Qah village!G0703049,  Aljolan camp PHCC/ Aljolan Camp!G0703048, Al Thawrah PHC/ Dental clinic 10!G0700049,  Hay Al Jam3a PHC!G0700036, DDD Jalma comprehensive PHC!B0203087, Afrin PHC 9!B0203070 and Jandairis PHC 3!B0203069.

The proposed project has been developed to respond to priorities and needs identified by the community itself. This project will support emergency preparedness steps to ensure appropriate health service coverage and capacity to increase service availability in case of massive IDP arrival. The project has also been designed in close coordination with the Health Cluster, COVID-19 Taskforce, MHPSS Working Group and humanitarian actors in the area to ensure that integrated and relevant services are provided to the targeted population. This includes conflict-affected children under 12 years old, high risk pregnant women, older people, people living with disabilities , people living with chronic conditions and other vulnerable groups with limited access to health care. 

DDD (also known as DoTW-T) is one of the largest providers of health care services in NWS. It is also one of the only NGOs providing PCR testing. DDD clinics have been responding to the health needs of IDP and host community residents in Dana sub-district since 2012 and in Afrin since 2018. It has strong links with the local community. Support of for these 17 facilities in 2021 is essential to maintain availability of services to returning patients and people depending on the services, and to respond to the health needs of new IDPs arriving in the areas served by the clinics. Moreover, adaptation of services to respond to the specific needs of the most vulnerable groups severely impacted by hostilities and displacement is essential.

project_name: Projet d’assistance nutritionnelle aux enfants 6-23 mois et femmes enceintes et allaitantes pendant la période de soudure au Sahel
project_objective: La malnutrition aiguë demeure un problème de santé publique majeur au Tchad avec une prévalence de la Malnutrition Aiguë Globale au niveau national est estimée à 10% ; ce qui représente une situation préoccupante d’après la nouvelle classification de l’OMS. Au total seize provinces sur 23 sont en situation préoccupante avec une prévalence de la malnutrition aigüe et un taux mortalité élevés supérieurs aux seuils sévères ou critiques. Elles constituent les provinces prioritaires d’intervention. Parmi elles, 13 sont en situation d’urgence car elles présentent des taux supérieurs au seuils critique de l’OMS pour la malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG ≥ 15 %), la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS ≥ 2%) et la mortalité (Taux brute de mortalité ≥1/10000 personnes/ jour et Taux de mortalité des enfants de moins de 5 ans ≥ 2/10000 enfants de moins de cinq ans/jours). La situation du retard de croissance est très élevée avec une moyenne nationale se situant à 30.5% et des prévalences dépassant le seuil critique de 30% de l’OMS dans douze des vingt trois (23) provinces.

project_name: Critical agricultural livelihoods support to conflict- and pandemic-affected households in northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
In 2021, FAO will improve food security, nutritional status and incomes among vulnerable, conflict- and pandemic-affected households in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states in Northeast Nigeria. The now more than decade-long insurgency has decimated agricultural livelihoods upon which more than 80 percent of the population relies as a primary source of household income. The COVID-19 pandemic has further compounded this already highly vulnerable humanitarian context, generating interconnected vulnerabilities that negatively affect availability and access to food, agriculture inputs, finance, farming land, extension services, markets and the fundamental viability of agricultural livelihoods. 
Support to crop production and the rebuilding of a robust crop value chain have been identified by FAO as key to the restoration of livelihoods and to improving the food and nutrition security of vulnerable populations in the BAY states. FAO will support vulnerable households with critical inputs for rainy and dry season cultivation as well as for micro-/backyard gardening and seed production.   
Prior to the insurgency, close to 80 percent of households in northeast Nigeria reared livestock and/or poultry as a vital source of food and household income. The conflict has caused the wide-scale loss of these assets either through looting, property destruction, disease, or abandonment when fleeing attacks by armed insurgents. In addition to being a source of income generation through breeding for sale, livestock and poultry restocking increases the availability of meat, milk and eggs at the household level. FAO will increase support to livestock and poultry production in 2021 in support of affected households.
Prior to the crisis, the fisheries sector had significant economic importance and fish from the northeast were supplied to the rest of Nigeria. With increased land and areas retaken by the military, the return of IDPs to their communities of origin is ongoing, thereby enabling some to access fishing grounds and resume their traditional livelihood. However, the lack of quality inputs remains a limiting factor for the majority of fishers who continue to rely on humanitarian assistance to meet their food and livelihood needs. By leveraging FAO’s extensive experience and capacity, conflict-affected fisherfolk households will be supported to resume their livelihoods and meet their food and nutritional needs. 
The ongoing crisis is also termed a ‘protection crisis’ with vulnerable social groups – particularly children, women and the elderly – disproportionately affected by the impact of the ongoing conflict and the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and are at heightened risk of adopting negative coping strategies such as child labour, borrowing, street begging, basic needs deprivation, transactional sex, early and forced marriage as their families seek to reduce the number of mouths to feed in their homes, and collection of fuelwood in insecure areas, which remains a high-risk livelihood. FAO will support vulnerable households by way of fuel-efficient stoves to reduce exposure to potential protection risks, and stove production and briquette production centres for income generation. 
Access to credit is a particular challenge for vulnerable groups in Northeast Nigeria, particularly women. Through the establishment of Group Savings and Loans Associations (GSLA), in 2021 FAO will extend its GSLA programme and will identify vulnerable groups to enhance their access to credit and financial services as an important social safety net.  
FAO is the co-lead of the Food Security Sector (FSS) which plays a critical role in coordinating food security programming in the BAY states. Food security data collection and analysis are also key and upon which food security actors base their intervention. In 2021, FAO will continue to support and host the Food Security Sector to facilitate the required coordination and analyses required to reach people most in need.

project_name: Provision and Management of WASH Core Pipeline Supplies for Emergency Preparedness and Response in South Sudan.
project_objective: UNICEF WASH core pipeline supplies project will reach 1,375,000 beneficiaries through provision of  people (IDPs and communities affected by other emergencies) with immediate WASH needs through planning, procurement, prepositioning, distribution, and management of critical WASH supplies.  the project will contribute to Cluster objectives 1,2 and 3 through provision water treatment chemicals, spare parts for hand pump rehabilitation/repair, latrine slabs (squatting pans), plastic tarpaulins for latrine construction, latrine digging kits, hygiene kits (jerry-cans, buckets, soap, menstrual hygiene health materials, and dignity items).  UNICEF will procure the WASH supplies and in coordination with the WASH Cluster pre-position them in strategic locations throughout South Sudan. Supplies will be released to partners through the approval of the WASH Cluster, and the receiving partner will be responsible for distribution of the supplies. The WASH supplies will be accessible to all WASH partners currently operational in South Sudan through WASH Cluster structures at national and state levels. The project will distribute WASH supplies as per Sphere and South Sudan WASH Cluster standards and in coordination with other cluster (Health, and Nutrition). Through this project UNICEF will focus on delivering rapid assistance in all counties and population affected by a sudden- or rapid-onset disaster  and targeting at county level will be done through WASH Cluster updates or using various assessment findings (IRNAs, NAWG recommendations, WASH Vulnerability maps. Follow-up monitoring and capacity building of partners will be conducted throughout the project period to ensure proper management of supplies at various warehouses. UNICEF in coordination with beneficiary partners will conduct end user monitoring of the supplies to ensure that supplies distributed are reaching the vulnerable communities and are being used properly.

project_name: Preventing and Responding to Gender-Based Violence within COVID-19 impact on women and girls in Gaza Strip
project_objective: While all populations of the globe are vulnerable to COVID-19, yet there are those who are the most vulnerable including the elderly, women and children who are generally disadvantaged compared to others and most subject to increased GBV under crises when there is increased unemployment, restrictions of mobility and heightened tensions, fears and anxieties creating more demand for already limited services. Also, as the incidents of violence were increased during COVID-19 emergency situation, there was a need to continue responsive services to GBV survivors and enhance their resilience to the circumstances. The project is a response to the affected women and girls by the emergency situation and COVID-19 impact, especially women and girls with disabilities, and elderly women by providing them multi-sectoral services remotely and physically. The services include health, psychosocial, legal, cash assistance, support to small businesses for GBV survivors, awareness and support for special-need survivors. The project also will focus on providing access to women and girls with disabilities and elderly women. On the other hand, the project will focus on raising awareness and knowledge of GBV topics for service providers in NGOs and ministries, in addition to focusing on PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) during delivering the services and dealing with the survivors.

project_name: Protection Assistance to Vulnerable Populations in the East and South of Libya
project_objective:
The objective of the proposed intervention is to respond to the acute vulnerability of conflict-affected populations, inclusive of refugees and migrants living in urban settings. The action aims to achieve this through protection assistance whilst building community resilience and self-reliance by empowering Libyan civil society organizations.
As a result of the protracted conflict in Libya and the constant population movement that is a characteristic of it, many Libyan residents – including host community members, returnees, and displaced persons – and non-Libyans face heightened vulnerability in the absence of access to effective protection assistance. The conflict and its effects have substantially affected the population’s well-being and physical, psychological, and emotional health. At the same time, public service provision has faltered as a result of the conflict. In response to these challenges, ACTED will provide protection assistance by conducting protection monitoring in the East and South of Libya, and by maintaining and strengthening its local referral pathways. In addition, ACTED will support the resilience and self-reliance of vulnerable communities by supporting Libyan civil society organizations technically and financially to carry out community-based protection initiatives.

project_name: Legal Assistance for Vulnerable People in Libya
project_objective: This project will provide legal assistance to vulnerable people in Tripoli, Benghazi and Ajdabiya - both Libyans and non-Libyans. By targeting key thematic areas including housing, land and property issues; complex legal documentation cases; residency and status; and employment disputes, legal assistance will be targeted at reducing vulnerability and improving positive coping mechanisms, in support of durable solutions and resilience. A strong emphasis will be placed on negotiation and mediation, and engagement with community dispute resolution mechanisms in order to achieve positive outcomes for beneficiaris. The project impact will be achieved through the provision of information, counselling, legal assistance, training and through a Call Centre for refugees.

project_name: WASH Assistance for Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities in Teknaf, Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
The project aims to ensure for all refugees living in camps 24 block G and 27 block A and for the affected host communities:
- regular, sufficient, equitable and dignified access to safe water for drinking and domestic needs.
- adequate, appropriate and acceptable sanitation facilities (including household waste).
The proposed project will be implemented in an impartial and non-discriminatory manner promoting the safety, dignity, and integrity of the beneficiaries. Actions are taken to ensure that the beneficiaries understand that they are entitled to free, fair, and certain assistance. 
Gender and age often determine the actual access that people have to WASH services. They can also determine how limited or inadequate WASH services affect different groups. It is important to understand these differences and to offer services that address all demographics. The WASH-infrastructure will be set up inclusively, with consideration given to special needs. The hygiene workshops will be broken down by gender and age and will address the special needs of the individual groups.
Safety, privacy and dignity in accessing and using of WASH facilities and services will be at the heart of WASH strategy and programming. Protection strategies in WASH will ensure that all groups of people facing additional vulnerabilities including girls, women, older people, people with disabilities, have adequate and safe access to water collection and use; functional latrines and bathing units with safe and accessible pathways, solid doors, locks and other inclusive features such as screening and lighting; and safe spaces for practicing Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM).

project_name: Provision of integrated lifesaving nutrition services to boys and girls with acute malnutrition including pregnant and lactating women focusing on IDP settlements and host communities in Somalia.
project_objective:
The humanitarian situation in Somalia remains critical due to the impacts of ongoing displacement, conflict and seasonal floods. It is expected that the Desert Locust, COVID-19 pandemic and the anticipated below average rain will contribute towards the deterioration of agricultural production outputs and social economics increased vulnerabilities of households which will further aggravate the already poor malnutrition status of children. It is estimated that 5.1 million people are facing food insecurity of whom 2.1 million people across Somalia are expected to be in Crisis or Emergency Status (IPC Phase 3 or higher). The potential consequences of severe food insecurity will affect the most vulnerable people particularly children under 5, women, elder and disable people who may experience deterioration of their nutrition and health status due to weak immunity system, poor feeding practices and limited access to basic services including water and sanitation. 
The post Gu 2020 nutrition assessment findings showed marginal decrease in the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) of 11.8 % down from 13.8% of post GU 2019 and 14% of post Gu 2018. The corresponding median SAM prevalence are: 1.8% (Gu 2020) down from 2.3% (Gu 2019), 2.2% (Gu 2018). The post GU 2020 nutrition assessment has also indicated critical malnutrition situation among the IDPs particularly Bossaso, Banadir, Garowe and Galkacyo IDPs. Internally displaced persons (IDPs) are disproportionally affected by nutrition crisis compare to host communities because majority of the IDPs are poor and live in urban areas in desperate conditions and have limited access to livelihood assets and social services. Overall, children affected by severe acute malnutrition are nine times more at risk of death compared to those who are well-nourished. According to UNICEF Somalia Situation Report of Sept 2020, Nutrition Programme treated 15,755 children with severe acute malnutrition (56% being female) in UNICEF supported programmes, despite a month-on-month decline in the number of children screened for malnutrition since April as a result of COVID-19 limitations. This brings the total SAM cases reached from Jan to Sept to 181, 242, which surpassed UNICEF annual target by 35.7%. The nutrition cluster estimated that 962,000 children under the age of five are likely to be acutely malnourished through October 2021, including 162,007 who are likely to be to be severely malnourished. Under UNICEF HRP, out of the 162,007 children with SAM, UNICEF will target 75% of Cluster target which is estimated at 121,500 (61, 965 girls, 59,535 boys) and 25,000 children with moderate acute malnutrition under the simplified protocol for the management of acute malnutrition in close consultation with WFP. 
Gender inequality exacerbates food insecurity, malnutrition and poverty in humanitarian crises. UNICEF recognizes that girls, boys, men, women and people with disabilities have different nutritional needs at different life stages with different capacities and risks in accessing nutrition services. Therefore, UNICEF will ensure provision of nutrition services through life cycle approach and target nutrition sites will function as a platform for the delivery of integrated multi sector services particularly WASH, C4D, health, GBV and safety net. Key interventions of this HRP will aim to deliver promotive and preventive services (Micronutrient supplementation, deworming, IYCF, PLW) and early detection and referral for treatment of SAM targeting in priority rural and IDP communities with equal access to boys, girls, and women. UNICEF as main provider of  nutrition supplies for management of severe acute malnutrition, will ensure procurement of nutrition supplies for nutrition cluster partners in Somalia (e.g. SHF, SHINE, Consortium and those with UNICEF PCAs) including the 25% buffer stock at any given time in the year.

project_name: WHO Emergency response to COVID-19 and consequences of the conflict in Ukraine – 2021
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in eastern Ukraine has a devastating impact on the health and well-being of the affected population showing signs of long-term consequences. The conflict has isolated rural health facilities in Government-Controlled Areas (GCA) from major health centers located in urban areas in Non-Government Controlled Areas (NGCA). Of the approximately 3.3 million people living within the 20 kilometres of the contact line, 38 per cent of households in the 20 km area along the ‘contact line’ and 57 per cent of households in the 5 km area along the ‘contact line’ (GCA) reported having problems accessing healthcare and require life-saving and essential health services.   The insecurity, lack of maintenance of outdated health facilities and medical equipment, shortage of medicines and medical supplies, understaffing and curtailed access to referral hospitals and pharmacies undermine the health care system’s ability to cope with both new and pre-existing health care needs.
The ongoing process of health care reform in Ukraine impacts the access of the population to essential medical services on both sides of the ‘contact line.’ 
The lack of access to primary, secondary and tertiary health care services particularly affects vulnerable populations such as women, children, elderly, people with disabilities, those living in isolated settlements. This is further compounded by the lack of qualified medical staff and brain drain. Those who remained are confronted with the significant challenges to access quality professional education and continuous training. Health care workers are also exposed to traumatic events and are being overlooked by the health system and humanitarian organizations. 
A pandemic of COVID-19 has seriously affected the health conditions of the population in both GCA and NGCA directly and indirectly. People observed 
received additional stressing factors: fear of getting infected with unknown pathogen; many controversial information about the disease; strict isolation measures introduced by authorities; closure of health care facilities to reserve beds for COVID patients, and many others. Health services received additional burden that seriously affected health workers as well as the organization in a whole. Growing numbers of new cases of infection and deaths of COVID, shortage of laboratory capacities, test systems, personal protection equipment, oxygen supply, and other vital equipment as well as lack of the knowledge and practice in treating patients are keeping health care workers in a very stressed condition for months.
It is difficult to ensure quality management of the healthcare system, since standardized protocols and operational procedures, based on the globally accepted guidelines are not being widely deployed or even tailored to the local context. Patient safety is also a major source for concern, given that little standardization occurs in the management of diseases, infection prevention and control measures, administration of the healthcare facilities. Essential medicines, renewables, equipment, and core medical technologies are also lacking.
To respond to the humanitarian needs, WHO will continue implementing the following key activities, which are based on the strong cooperation with health authorities:
1.	Support to primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities through the distribution of medical supplies and equipment, development of capacity building programs and rehabilitation of health infrastructure related to COVID-19 response and beyond it. 
2.	Support to Public Health sector through the capacity building of the laboratories with a primary focus on improvement of detection of COVID-19
3.	Reinforcing technical capacity of health care workers in mental health and psychosocial support

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action in eastern Ukraine 2021
project_objective:
The HALO Trust will conduct risk education, survey and clearance operations in eastern Ukraine, to
respond to the needs of mine-affected communities across Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts,
focusing on high-priority areas within the 15km buffer-zone from the line of contact. HALO
will also provide training and capacity building sessions for the key mine action
stakeholders including the newly established mine action authorities in order to contribute
to an effective and efficient mine action sector.
Risk education sessions are a preventive measure that will inform people about the threat related to
mines and other explosive items in order to decrease the probability of accidents. Survey work
will establish the extent and nature of mine contamination in the region, while the marking of minefields further prevents accidents from happening. Clearance will permanently remove these threats by making land safe, which improves the physical security of people in eastern Ukraine. Clearance of land also improves livelihoods by releasing land that can be used for productive purposes. HALO has thus far released seven million square metres of land previously contaminated with explosive hazards and aims to clear another two million square metres in 2021.

project_name: Enhance Protection Environment and access to essential services for conflict affected communities in Southeast of Libya.
project_objective:
The project’s objective aligns with Libya Protection Sector Strategy Objectives for 2020-2021 by enhancing the protection environment and provide integrated and specialized protection services for the highly vulnerable people and population at risks. The project includes activities which aim to address the protection needs of the communities affected by the conflict by the provision of integrated protection assistance to reduce vulnerabilities at individual level, sensitization and awareness on protection issues and concerns faced by the community and provision of protection information management reports. The access to services will be ensured in synergy with other ongoing PUI’s projects implementing in the area and through an integrated response including protection, psychosocial support, health and socio economical support to the most vulnerable persons and persons at highest risks. The project aims also to reinforce community’s capacities by ensuring sensitization on key protection issues and participatory approach during the whole project implementation .  
 The project targets both Libyans and non-Libyans populations, IDPs, returnees, Refugees, migrants (including highly vulnerable persons, conflict affected persons, persons at risks and  population exposed to protection risks due to the COVID-19 pandemic…)
PUI’s analyses of the context and needs aims to be Age, Gender, Diversity sensitive and will ensure to implement the interventions in a way to address specific needs identified and ensure equal access to services. Humanitarian principles will guide the implementation of this project to promote safety, dignity and rights of affected people, respect age / gender diversity and protection mainstreaming, and mitigate exposure to additional risks through conflict sensitive and do not harm approaches.

project_name: Reincorporación social y económica de excombatientes a través de acción integral contra minas
project_objective:
En 2016, el Gobierno de Colombia y las FARC-EP firmaron un Acuerdo de Paz, finalizando uno de los conflictos más longevos de la región. Sin embargo, uno de los principales desafíos en su implementación es lograr la reincorporación social y económica sostenible de los ex combatientes. En este contexto, UNMAS Colombia lidera la implementación de un proyecto que promueve la acción integral contra minas como una herramienta para la reincorporación socioeconómica de los excombatientes, mediante la formación y el empleo en el sector. El Proyecto tiene tres líneas de acción:

- Fortalecimiento organizacional y operacional de una organización de personal en proceso de reincorporación para que puedan operar como una organización civil de desminado humanitario en el país.
- Promoción de la reincorporación de excombatientes de las FARC-EP, a través de su entrenamiento técnico y acreditación para realizar actividades de acción integral contra minas, según los estándares definidos por la Autoridad Nacional Descontamina Colombia/OACP.
- Liberación de tierras de la sospecha de contaminación por artefactos explosivos previniendo la ocurrencia de accidentes e incidentes asociados a su presencia.

La primera fase del Proyecto fue financiada por el Fondo Multidonante de las Naciones Unidas para el Posconflicto (MPTF). El proyecto de 23 meses financiado por MPTF comenzó el 5 de febrero de 2018 y se dividió en dos componentes principales: desarrollo de la capacidad organizacional y desarrollo de la capacidad operacional. La segunda fase del proyecto financiada por la UE, se enfocará en fortalecer la capacidad del equipo de Humanicemos DH para implementar las políticas y procedimientos que se desarrollaron durante la primera fase del proyecto, fortalecer la capacidad de gestión organizacional y operacional, el despliegue de operaciones de desminado humanitario y la realización de actividades de educación en el riesgo de minas. 

El proyecto es un modelo de acción complementaria de la acción humanitaria, la construcción de paz y el desarrollo. Se espera que los ex combatientes a través del desminado humanitario y otros componentes de la acción contra minas, eliminen la amenaza de los artefactos explosivos en las zonas más afectadas y de esta forma se mitiguen los riesgos de accidentes para la población y se mejore a su vez sus condiciones de vida.

project_name: Improve access to inclusive and relevant quality education for children (girls, and boys) affected by displacement in the Far North region including host communities, IDPs and returnees.
project_objective: The project aims to improve access to safe and quality education for crisis-affected children, with a particular focus on girls. The action will facilitate access to education for out of school children and adolescents to enable them to obtain the basis for integration into the formal education system. It is urgent to re-engage out-of-school children with the education system since, as these children grow up, their chance and ability to resume school decreases. The project will address gendered barriers to education and sensitization on gender-based violence, through teacher training, awareness campaigns and the promotion of equal and safe education for girls and boys, regardless of their status (IDPs, returnees or host communities.) To achieve this, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the decentralized services of basic education in Cameroon, and will ensure a conflict-sensitive approach while ensuring respect for Do No Harm principles. The project result will be achieved through activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of education actors at the community level and ensuring the protection of children and adolescents. To ensure a consistent and comprehensive response, the project will be developed through the lenses of gender and conflict mitigation, which are two concomitant perspectives to the dissemination of the principles of protection in the project. At the end of the action 20 000 persons including IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community’s children will benefit the above package of education assistance in order to scale up their access to qualities education opportunities.

project_name: Mejora de los servicios esenciales de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene de las personas en situación de desplazamiento afectadas directa o indirectamente por la situación humanitaria
project_objective:
NRC Venezuela tiene como objetivo reducir riesgos de salud pública y la prevención de enfermedades relacionadas con el agua y el saneamiento inadecuados, garantizando el acceso al derecho al agua y al saneamiento, reduciendo los riesgos de protección ligados a la situación humanitaria en Venezuela. El programa ASH continuará una post-fase de evaluación y análisis de las necesidades, y propone modalidades de (a) respuesta de emergencia, (b) respuesta con soluciones duraderas basada en un enfoque comunitario, y (c) una respuesta Integrada con otros programas de NRC tales como: Educación, Seguridad Alimentaria e ICLA.

La respuesta ASH de NRC estará centrada en la provisión de un mínimo de servicios ASH durante la Respuesta de Emergencia (COVID-19 y crisis humanitaria venezolana). Por otro lado, durante la Respuesta con Soluciones Duraderas se pretende mejorar la resiliencia en comunidades meta, fomentando la participación de comunidades en el diseño e implementación del programa, desarrollando sus capacidades locales, y asegurando la sostenibilidad del programa. 

La componente de AGUA incluirá: (a) Construcción de puntos de agua potable temporales y permanentes para personas en tránsito y comunidades de acogida. NRC capacitará a la municipalidad e instituciones locales para mantener los puntos de agua y garantizar la calidad del agua, y se donarán kits de análisis de agua como parte de la estrategia de creación de capacidad; (b) Provisión de agua segura (a nivel del hogar) a través de kits de tratamiento de agua para el hogar y/o kits de manejo de agua) y rehabilitación y sistema de tratamiento de agua a nivel comunitario; (c) Provisión de capacitación y sensibilización (tratamiento, calidad del agua y uso seguro). La componente de SANEAMIENTO incluirá: (a) Provisión de baterías de baños y duchas culturalmente apropiadas, desagregados por género y estaciones de lavado de manos.

Las instalaciones se ubicarán en áreas públicas o institucionales en zonas clave de flujo migratorio; (b) Provisión de activos NFIs de saneamiento (mantenimiento / limpieza); (c)Provisión de contenedores de basura para gestión de residuos sólidos. La componente de HIGIENE incluirá: (a) Provisión de kits de dignidad e higiene, junto con sensibilizaciones sobre su uso apropiados; (b)Provisión de campañas de sensibilización sobre higiene personal, prevención de enfermedades, higiene menstrual y protección; (c) Creación, capacitación y sensibilización de comités ASH en colegios y comunidades que servirán como apoyo a la promoción de higiene.

La respuesta ASH de NRC pretenden ser Integradas a otros programas como: (a) EF-LH, mejorando el suministro de agua para actividades agropecuarias, etc..; (b) Educación que apunta a una mejora de la calidad de la educación, inclusivas e integradas con el programa ASH centrándose en la mejora de la infraestructura ASH, para garantizar las instalaciones satisfagan las necesidades de todos los grupos de NNAs, profesores y personas con discapacidad.

project_name: Multi-sector humanitarian assistance to crisis affected populations in Northwest and Southwest Cameroon
project_objective:
The NWSW regions of Cameroon continue to have hundreds of thousands of individuals affected by crisis and in need of humanitarian assistance. DRC is proposing a multi-sector humanitarian response to meet the most urgent needs of affected populations, including a response to protection, shelter, WASH, NFI and food security needs. 

Through emergency WASH, shelter and NFI support, vulnerabilities will be mitigated in the immediate term for those permanently or chronically displaced by conflict in highly vulnerable, hard to reach areas. The proposed action aims to address some of the most critical gaps in assistance through the provision of cluster standard shelter, NFI and WASH assistance to 6,500 households.

The crisis is threatening to produce a lost generation of children who have been highly exposed to violence and conflict, without any form of education, and are caught in an environment where community and family structure degradation is pervasive, leading to high needs for psychosocial support. DRC will expand on the demonstrated success of its current child protection programming to continue to meet the social and emotional needs of children affected by conflict through community-based child protection programming, and individual child protection assistance. This will produce an improved protection environment for over 10,000 children in the immediate and medium term.

The crisis in the southwest has created diverse and widespread protection needs that are in critical need of being chronicled and addressed. DRC has had dedicated protection monitoring and response capacity in the southwest since January, 2019. The proposed action will allow DRC to expand coverage of monitoring and response, building the capacity for evidence based advocacy, and improving the protection environment for individuals and communities in the longer term. Protection needs will be addressed through psychosocial support including psychological first aid, with immediate protection cases being supported through individual protection assistance, as well as community based protection assistance through Community Based Protection Committees and community protection assistance. Protection monitoring and reporting will allow DRC to continue to gather important information on the protection environment in highly vulnerable communities informing both advocacy and response.

To respond to the urgent food security needs in NWSW regions, DRC will provide food security assistance through paper and e-vouchers to the 2,600 most vulnerable households. 

As a result of the proposed intervention, crisis affected households will have better capacity to meet their basic needs, and the protection environment for both children and adults will be improved in the longer term.

project_name: Enhance provision of integrated comprehensive healthcare services to vulnerable host and IDP populations in Dharkenley, Howl-wadag, Deyniile, Karan districts in Benadir regions, Beletweyne in Hiiraan region and Galmudug regions.
project_objective:
The Gu rainy season flooding in 2020 directly affected 548,339 individuals and displaced 279,108 people in nine regions across the country. The floods have worsened the humanitarian health situation at a time when responders are overwhelmed by COVID-19 responses. The COVID-19 has added to the mental suffering of the affected population and aggravated gender and interpersonal violence (GBV/IPV). The Displaced population, mostly women and adolescent girls, face significant barriers to access reproductive health and malnutrition services during this flooding season as compared to other groups. In 2021, 1.3 million boys and girls and pregnant and lactating women will suffer from high acute malnutrition, with 180,000 children under 5 affected by life threatening severe malnutrition, thus requiring emergency nutrition services. Children under the age of five and pregnant and lactating women and girls (PLWGs) are among the most vulnerable people in the event of humanitarian crises, The proposed intervention will scaleup the provision of health services in Benadir, Galmudug and Hiiran regions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host communities. The project will support 4 health centres in Benadir, 2Galmudug and one health center Hiiraan with an aim of targeting 63,025 people. Integrated essential lifesaving preventive and curative services will be provided through outpatient consultations for children under-five and those above age five, in addition to laboratory and pharmacy services, reproductive health, basic emergency obstetric services, immunization, and community health education. The IRC aims to increase access to quality life-saving GBV services for women and girls, while enhancing GBV prevention in host and IDP communities. IRC will provide GBV training to the psychosocial first aid (PFA) volunteers.  The proposed intervention will support provision of maternal health care and newborn care including safe deliveries, emergency obstetric (BEmONC & CeMOC), and SRH services (including management of STD/HIV treatment and SGBV particularly in geographic areas. The Critical patients attending the mobile clinics and pregnant women with obstetric complications will be referred and managed at the health facilities. Pregnant women in need of Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care will be referred from the PHCC to tertiary hospital. Community dialogues will target different age groups within the communities and at different times. the proposed intervention will address immediate needs i.e.  mitigating the spread of COVID-19 and supporting the public health consequences of the pandemic in target locations including Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) including awareness raising through media and training more community health workers on case definitions as well as to scale up hygiene response in the targeted areas. 
Creating access to services: The facilities will receive drugs, pharmaceuticals to accommodate various morbidities.
Ensuring quality of services: The IRC will continue to work to improve the reproductive healthcare through the provision of the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP), limited to basic emergency obstetric and neonatal care (BEmONC) services, especially targeting ANC, PNC, family planning/birth spacing, syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections and referral of high-risk complected pregnancies. 
Increasing demand for services: This will be done through health promotion, community engagement The IRC will also continue building the capacities and skills for the CHWs to enable community health staff to provide a rapid, effective response in case of a health emergencies disaster like in the current situation, COVID-19. The CHWs will work to dispel rumors, fears and misconceptions received/heard in the community about COVID-19 using the existing community structures and channels of influence, including religious leaders and other respected community leaders.

project_name: Humanitarian Demining activities in Putumayo, Colombia (2nd Phase)
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivo, en el corto plazo, contribuir a garantizar la seguridad territorial y mejorar la confianza de las comunidades mediante la reducción del riesgo de accidentes por MAP/ MUSE en las comunidades de Puerto Asís y San Miguel afectadas por la presencia o sospecha de estos dispositivos, a un nivel en el que las personas puedan vivir sin sentirse amenazadas. Esto a través de la implementación de diferentes fases del Desminado Humanitario (DH), teniendo en cuenta los Estándares Nacionales y los Procedimientos Operativos Estándar aprobados en la CCCM.
Los beneficiarios directos del proyecto serán los propietarios de las tierras liberadas y las personas que las utilizan, así como los participantes en las actividades de Educación en el Riesgo de Minas - ERM - y las víctimas y/o familiares atendidos. Al final, toda la población de los municipios se beneficiará en alguna medida de las actividades, ya que estas permitirán la recuperación de tierras productivas y la libre movilidad por diferentes zonas de estos municipios.

project_name: Reducing Protection Risks and Meeting Basic Needs for Conflict-Affected Communities in the Far North Region Region in Cameroon
project_objective: The project aims at ensuring the that women, girls, boys and men are safe in their communities and receive support when they experience harm in the targeted locations in the Far North region. The project will provide gender-based violence (GBV) and protection programming to beneficiaries to help them be safer in their communities, and receive support when they experience harm

project_name: Assistance alimentaire et appui à l’amélioration  des moyens d’existence de  6800 ménages déplacés internes et hôtes dans les régions du Nord et  du Centre- Nord
project_objective:
Suite à la crise sécuritaire que connaît le Burkina depuis 2015 induisant ainsi une augmentation du nombre de déplacés internes, Help a débuté ses interventions vers cette cible depuis 2019. Elle a déjà réalisé des interventions dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun dans le secteur des abris et des Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME).
A la date du 10 novembre 2020, on enregistrait 1 049 767 personnes déplacées internes reparties dans l’ensemble des 13 régions du pays. Cependant les régions du Sahel, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun restent avec celles du Sahel et de l’Est, les régions qui accueillent la grande majorité des PDI. Help va poursuivre ses interventions dans les régions du Centre Nord, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. L’appui sera apporté dans les communes de Barsalogho et Pissibla, Boussouma et Kaya (province du Sanmatenga), de Yalgo  et Tougouri (province du Namentenga), de Thiou, Oula, Barga (province du Yatenga).
Il faut juste rappeler que toutes ces populations n’ont pour profession que l’agriculture et l’élevage et les jeunes qui sont issus des ménages PDI constituent un réservoir potentiel de recrutement pour les groupes armés à cause de leur manque de revenus et de perspectives.
A cette situation sécuritaire difficile est venu s’ajouter la maladie à Corona virus au début du second trimestre de l’année faisant 2252 cas et 68 décès à la date du 17 novembre 2020. Outre les impacts sanitaires de la maladie, le Gouvernement a pris des mesures qui ont eu des effets négatifs sur l’économie pour réduire les contaminations. 
La réponse de Help dans ce secteur de la sécurité alimentaire consistera en la conduite d’actions vigoureuses à travers le cash transfert conditionnel et inconditionnel, des appuis en facteurs de production agricole, des appuis pour l’intensification des productions maraichères dans les zone propices (péri-urbain et au abord des plans d’eau)  et le développement d’autres types d’activités génératrices de revenus porteuses sont alors prévues par Help dans les deux régions sus citées. Un soutien sera également apporté aux ménages qui ont été impacté par les effets du  COVID 19 par un renforcement de leurs moyens d’existence. L’ensemble des activités seront mises en œuvre de façon participative avec une implication directe des PDI, de la population hôte, des services techniques et des collectivités locales dans tout le processus.

project_name: Protection and humanitarian assistance to recently displaced people and confined communities in Colombia.
project_objective:
Este proyecto pertenece al consorcio MIRE (Mecanismo Intersectorial de Respuesta a Emergencia) en el cual se encuentran vinculadas 6 organizaciones. NRC, DKH, APS, ACH, MDM y Plan Internacional. Busca ofrecer ayuda humanitaria en los sectores, protección, salud, educación en emergencias y agua y saneamiento básico, a comunidades afectadas por situaciones relacionadas por el conflicto o con la ocurrencia de situaciones de desastre de origen natural.

Pretende asegurar que las necesidades humanitarias urgentes no satisfechas de las poblaciones vulnerables puedan ser cubiertas en los sectores de intervención del consorcio. La implementación se realiza a través de un equipo móvil que se despliega por todo el país y seis puntos focales de campo humanitario estratégicamente ubicados en Nariño, Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Córdoba, Norte de Santander y el Guaviare vigilarán permanentemente la situación humanitaria, identificarán a los individuos desplazamientos, apoyar a los equipos móviles y coordinar con las entidades locales.

Las acciones de MDM buscan disminuir las brechas existentes en el acceso a la salud, lo cual incluye atención en salud física, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial, entrega de medicamentos, remisiones a especialidades y evacuaciones médicas. Las atenciones en salud física corresponden a consultas de medicina general, salud sexual y reproductiva, asesoría en planificación familiar, atenciones de casos de VBG, procedimientos menores

project_name: Améliorer les conditions de vie, la dignité et la protection des PDI et des communautés hôtes les plus vulnérables touchés par les déplacements au Burkina Faso par la fourniture d’abris d’urgence et transitoires et une assistance en AME.
project_objective:
Ce projet vise d’améliorer les conditions de vie, la dignité et la protection des 45 150 personnes dont les PDI et des communautés les plus vulnérables touchés par les déplacements au Burkina Faso par des solution d’abris grâce à la fourniture des abris d’urgence et transitoires et une assistance en AME.

L’action de NRC consistera à fournir une assistance basée sur des approches communautaires et participatives qui tiendra compte de la contribution des communautés grâce aux consultations communautaires. La coordination avec les acteurs de terrain au travers les groupes de travails et cluster, permettra la réalisation de ce projet sur base des leçons tiré des expériences passées et des orientations et directive du cluster.

Grace à la mutualisation des efforts, NRC proposer de consolider ses efforts dans la région du Centre Nord et du Sahel, visant des personnes déplacées et des vulnérable de la communauté hôte. NRC travaillera directement avec le CODESUR pour assurer que la sélection des bénéficiaires tienne compte d’information harmonisées.

NRC s’assurer une mise en œuvre directe des activité abri, au travers des approches monétaires là où le marché le permettra et procèdera à la fourniture des kits abris (in-kind) suivi d’un support technique pour la réalisation des ouvrages de qualité. Des séances de renforcement de capacité feront partie de la réponse proposée par NRC afin de s’assurer de la meilleure utilisation des abris, de leur maintenance et de leur amélioration pour une durabilité de l’action.

project_name: Apporter une assistance WASH aux réfugiés, retournés, PDI et famille d’accueil dans les régions de Maradi, Tillabéry et Diffa
project_objective:
Dans ce projet, NRC vise de contribuer au renforcement de l’accès aux services d’eau d’hygiène et d’assainissement en vue de réduire le risque et l'exposition aux maladies diarrhéiques auprès de 56 000 personnes dont des femmes, hommes, refugiées, retournes et famille d’accueil touchés par les déplacements, les inondations et les épidémies grâce à un meilleur accès à l'eau potable en qualité et quantité, à des installations sanitaires appropriées et aux pratiques d'hygiène. Les interventions WASH de NRC se feront dans les village d’accueil, les sites d’accueil des déplacés et les écoles.  La cible souhaitée est d’attendre 20% refugies, 25% déplacés internet et 5% retournes et 45% population hôtes. La réponse intègrera la réponse COVID-19. La réponse visera les ménages refugiés, PDI, retournes et population hôte.  Le plan de réponse prévoit de réhabiliter et de construire des nouveaux systèmes d’approvisionnement en eau potable utilisant les technologies à énergie renouvelable comme le solaire, et là où cela sera nécessaire l’approvisionnement en eau par du water-trucking, le traitement d'eau en situation d’urgence sur les sites temporaires, des infrastructures d’assainissement et des campagnes de sensibilisation de masse seront organisées pour le changement de comportement. Pour améliorer la gestion de l’eau, NRC créera et ou renforcera des comités de gestion des points d'eau avec une participation active des femmes visant d’atteindre 50% de participations des femmes dans les comités de gestion. Ces comités comprendront au moins sept membres, hommes et femmes, choisis par une assemblée villageoise.  NRC construira des blocs de latrines et douches dotées chacun d’un dispositif de lavage des mains dans les sites temporaires, dans les familles d’accueil vulnérables et dans les écoles ciblées par ce projet. Des kits d’entretien des latrines seront distribués aux ménage pour le nettoyage et l’entretien des latrines. Les latrines et les douches seront séparées par sexe pour atténuer les problèmes de protection, garantir la dignité des femmes et des jeunes filles et améliorer l'accès gratuit et sûr aux installations.
Pour améliorer l’hygiène en milieu scolaire, NRC mettra en place du paquet d'infrastructure minimum WASH dans les écoles et centres de santé le cas échéant. Des campagnes de sensibilisation pour la promotion de l'hygiène seront organisées afin de promouvoir le changement de comportement et d'encourager les meilleures pratiques d'hygiène personnelle. Pour ce faire, NRC va identifier, former et équiper des relais communautaires d’hygiène en collaboration avec les structures sanitaires avec au moins 50% de femmes. Des kits d'hygiène comprenant des kits d'hygiène familiale et des kits de dignité pour les femmes seront distribués aux ménages ciblés. NRC métra en place des comités d'hygiène et d’assainissement dans les sites temporaires pour une bonne gestion des structures d’assainissement. Les relais communautaires et les comité d’assainissement vont conduire des campagnes de sensibilisation dans les communautés, les écoles et dans les camps. Les matériels d'IEC et les kits d’hygiène seront conçus par le biais d'une consultation communautaire et après une enquête initiale sur les connaissances, attitudes et pratiques (CAP) menée par le NRC en coordination avec la DRHA, les districts sanitaires afin de se concentrer sur les problèmes les plus pertinents mis en évidence par les communautés et où les résultats de l'enquête montrent les plus grandes faiblesses des pratiques. NRC veillera à ce que les relais d'hygiène communautaires soient formés sur les méthode de communication/sensibilisation au niveau communautaire et équipés avec des matériels IEC. Cela inclura des démonstrations sur les pratiques de lavage des mains, le nettoyage des latrines et des douches, la chaîne de collecte de l'eau salubre (y compris le nettoyage des bidons) afin de conduire vers le changement de comportement parmi les communautés ciblées;

project_name: Promotion des opportunités d’apprentissage inclusives et sûres pour les filles et garçons d’âge scolaire dans les 6 régions  à fort défis sécuritaires du Burkina Faso.
project_objective:

project_name: WaSH en soutien aux populations vulnérables affectées par les conflits dans le cercle de Mopti

Help – Hilfe Zur Selbsthilfe au Mali, a commencé son intervention dans la région de Mopti en Janvier 2020 à travers un projet intitulé Amélioration de l’accès aux soins gratuits et de qualité de la Santé de la Reproduction (SR), Planning Familial (PF), VIH/SIDA, Prévention et Prise en Charge des Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG) qui couvre les cercles de Mopti, Djenne, Bandiagara et Douentza.
A l’instar d’autre cercle, Le cercle de Mopti fait partie des entités du Mali où la situation humanitaire s’est dégradée comme conséquence de la crise sécuritaire que connait le Mali depuis 2012. Le cercle est le théâtre d’importants mouvements de populations faisant suite à la crise socio-politique plus aigüe dans le nord du pays où des populations fuyant les régions de Gao et Tombouctou, se sont réfugiés dans la région de Mopti en général et le cercle de Mopti en particulier depuis l’éclatement des conflits intercommunautaire et la présence des groupes radicaux dans la région.
