project_name: Improved food security for people affected by displacement in South Kordofan State
project_objective:
The planned project will contribute to the Sudan humanitarian response plan focusing on addressing life threatening needs through timely provision of life saving food and/or cash/vouchers assistance to reduce mortality and morbidity of the affected people.  Most vulnerable households will be provided with food kits or cash/vouchers to enable them access food to meet their minimum food requirements.  Analysis of the situation in terms of gaps, capacities and market functionality will precede response in order to inform the project on the most suitable modality.  This activity will precede and overlap with the food production activities in order to build an exit strategy that is based on self-reliance of the targeted households. Nutrition awareness messaging with special focus on food hygiene and diet diversity will be developed and shared with the target groups.
Secondly, the project seeks to address life-sustaining needs to improve vulnerable people's access to livelihoods focusing mainly on food production and related value chain.  The project will promote activities that support production of food at household level.  This will range from small backyard nutrition gardens to field-based staple and other crops production, food processing and preservation. The project will consult the target beneficiaries and other stakeholders in order to find appropriate farming methods and promote technologies that will allow those with limited access to land for production to participate.  Nutrition information will be used to influence the type of crops that will be grown in order to contribute towards improvement of the household’s nutritional status.  Food processing and preservation training will be conducted in collaboration with organizations such as Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the state Ministry of Production and Economic Resources and relevant local organisations to promote preservation of food to cover the normal food deficit periods. The project will use market-based approaches to provide target groups with agricultural inputs including inputs for reforestation . The food production activities will be preceded by training in the correct and improved practices using extension methods that support local structures. NRC will not replace the local extension system but instead work to strengthen especially the community level extension services through training of community based extension workers.  
The project will be implemented in South Kordofan targeting new and old internally displaced persons (IDPs) and the most vulnerable host community households. The project will target households that are most vulnerable in terms of demographic and socio-economic characteristics.  The project will engage with the target communities in deciding on the vulnerability criteria for beneficiary selection.  NRC’s general selection criteria includes age, gender, disability and nutrition status.  Children under the age of five, pregnant and lactating women, all gender types, the youth, women, girls, people with disabilities, the elderly and chronically ill people make up a special target group for NRC’s food security projects.  The project will design in collaboration with the target populations, strategies for complaints and feedback handling in order to be accountable to the affected people and also to ensure recording and follow-up of sexual exploitation and abuse cases related to the project implementation.  The monitoring and evaluation activities will also be designed to capture achievements not only on outcome and output indicators but also on target beneficiaries’ satisfaction of their engagement and treatment during project implementation. The project seeks to contribute to durable solutions by building self-reliance of the target groups so that they are ensured of an adequate standard of living, including at a minimum access to adequate food, water, housing, health care and basic education.

project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des populations affectée par l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle à cause des conflits armés dans la région de Mopti
project_objective:
Ce projet le renforcement de la résilience des communautés d'accueil et des personnes déplacées dans le centre du Mali soit environ 12 500 personnes (7 000 hommes et 7 000 femmes), en particulier : en sécurité alimentaire : 10 000 personnes, dont 50 % de personnes déplacées et 50 % de communautés d'accueil. 
Mesures génératrices de revenus : 2 000 personnes issues de ménages particulièrement vulnérables (femmes et mineurs, personnes âgées, malades chroniques, handicapées physiques ou mentales, femmes enceintes et mères allaitantes), jeunes adultes (15-40 ans). Les mesures de travail contre rémunération pour 500 personnes particulièrement vulnérables

project_name: Assistance d’urgence aux populations vulnérables affectées par la crise humanitaire dans la région du Sahel/Tillabéri et Diffa , République du Niger
project_objective:
La fragilité de l'environnement sahélien, alliée à la récurrence des chocs et défis (naturels ou d'origine humaine) rencontrés par les populations de Tillabéry et de Diffa, conduisent à des situations cycliques d'insécurité alimentaire aggravée pour les plus vulnérables.
WHH se propose donc d'assurer la sécurité alimentaire de ces ménages pendant la période critique de la soudure, mais également de renforcer leur sécurité nutritionnelle.
Le projet vise à fournir le plus rapidement possible à 6.000 ménages (42.000 personnes) particulièrement vulnérables et ayant des enfants < 5 ans et/ou FEFA et qui sont en phase 2 et 3 de l'insécurité alimentaire, un accès aux denrées alimentaires. Les ménages vulnérables peu ou pas aptes au travail dans le besoin, et qui n'ont pas de membres de la famille qui travaillent, WHH mettra en œuvre des actions de distribution de cash , de distribution de semences et d'aliment de bétail afin de fair face à l'insécurité alimentaire.

project_name: Strengthening GBV prevention and response integrating child protection through life-saving services for women, girls and children affected by conflict in south Sudan
project_objective:
The project will strengthen lifesaving gender based violence (GBV) prevention and response in Koch, Pariang, Rubkona, Wau, Akobo, Bor South, Duk, Pibor, Twic East, Ikotos, Magwi, Torit and Juba. The proposed project will ensure provision of multi-sectoral coordinated GBV prevention and response services to women and girls including addressing the psychosocial needs of women and girls including survivors of GBV and to mitigate and prevent the risks faced by women and girls in the humanitarian crisis. Men and boys will be an integral part of the programme as allies in GBV prevention and response.
The project will target an estimated persons comprised of IDPs and host community members affected by conflict to;
- Increase access to lifesaving GBV specialized services including case management and psychosocial support (PSS) services for women and girls including adolescent girls.
- Strengthen capacities of frontline staff to ensure quality and comprehensive services to women and girls.
To ensure GBV survivors’ recovery and healing process is realized, CARE will work closely with implementing partners and service providers to ensure survivors of GBV have timely access to comprehensive and quality services and increase awareness on the availability of services to ensure timely access of available services.
The WGFS will offer specialized GBV case management and psychosocial support basic counseling, age-appropriate, individual and group-based support, information sessions, psychosocial support/recreational activities, and skills-building/livelihoods courses and activities for women and girls to gain knowledge and skills for positive coping including making healthy life-choices. CARE will also provide tailored PSS activities for adolescent girls to mitigate their vulnerability to multiple forms of GBV and offer support systems and access to information. This will be pivotal in reducing women and girls’ isolation and boosting their self-confidence.
Livelihood opportunities including income generation activities have greatly contributed to improving gender equality and reducing GBV risks particularly among women and adolescent girls. In this project, women, youth, and adolescent girls in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps and in the host communities will be supported to generate income and assets through a range of potential avenues. The start-up package will allow beneficiaries to sustain their new skills and activities beyond CARE’s support.
CARE will through this project continue to strengthen the capacity of frontline workers on the technical aspects of quality GBV response, including training on GBV core concepts where necessary, Inter-agency standing committee (IASC) Guidelines on GBV case management, caring for child survivors (CCS), psychological first aid (PFA) GBV pocket guide, referral pathways, etc.
CARE will partner with UNIDOR to implement CP activities to provide case management, PSS, referrals to support child GBV survivors.

project_name: Emergency medical care in conflict affected communities near the contact line in Luhansk region
project_objective:
The project is designed to provide emergency medical services and primary medical treatment to conflict affected communities people living in the 5-km area from the contact line and in the “gray zone” as well as for those crossing the contact line both ways in the Luhansk region. 
1. Supporting InterMediCare's existing capacities for emergency and primary health care services to people crossing the contact line in both directions and living in the 5-km area along the contact line in the GCA and in the ""gray zone"" in Luhansk region (3 emergency medical care posts at the Stanytsya Luhanska, Zolote and Shchastya EECPs) and 3 mobile emergency medical care teams (ambulances).
2. Establishment of 3 standard emergency medical care posts at the 3 EECPs opposite Stanytsya Luhanska, Zolote and Shchastya EECPs in the NGCA to provide emergency and primary health care services to people crossing the contact line in both directions.
3. Supporting of local efforts to combat COVID-19 in particular through thermal screening and health referral proceedings at the Stanytsya Luhanska, Zolote and Shchastya EECPs as well as through mobile emergency medical care teams' capacities. 
4. Establishment of 39 workplaces for the population of the Luhansk and Donetsk regions through full or partial employment of health professionals, regardless of their age or gender in the project.
The project focuses primarily on target groups living in isolated settlements in the 5-km area along the contact line and in the ""gray zone"". Medical assistance will be provided to everybody on the basis of medical ethics and medical secrecy, regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, linguistic choice or presence of mental illnesses, including to the LGBT community representatives and people with HIV/AIDS.

project_name: Addressing Needs and Enhancing Protection of Rohingya Refugee and Host Community Women and Girls through women’s empowerment and participation, and better services and promoting social cohesion in Cox's Bazar
project_objective: The project aims to enhance protection and empowerment resilience of Rohingya women and adolescent girls in the refugee camps, as well as promote social cohesion between host communities and refugee communities. It will also strengthen capacities of humanitarian actors, government, law enforcement, media and women's and LGBTIQ rights organisations/groups on gender equality and addressing GBV, essentially towards ensuring: i) women and adolescent girls, including LGBTIQ persons and women with disabilities, both Rohingya and host community have access to key life-saving and protection services, are resilient leaders, and are able to address and build social cohesion through constructive joint participation and dialogue ii) technical assistance is provided to Camps-in-Charge through Gender field Officers so they are better equipped to address women’s protection and empowerment needs and ensure linkages with elected and self-mobilised women leaders, iii) potential women leaders are capacitated with the leadership skills to contribute to community representation, while they are supported by an enabling environment promoted through social norms change and community engagement initiatives, iv) Community Security and gender-responsive policing is enhanced through capacity building ( gender and GBV ToT, mentoring, monitoring) of Armed Police Battalions and Bangladesh Police, setting up of women and children help desks , and supporting the Bangladesh Women Police Network, and v) Capacity of journalists are improved to promote gender-responsive journalism for improving positive narratives in the media promoting social cohesion and women’s involvement in humanitarian response. All partnership agreements signed between UN Women and  Implementing partners include commitment to PSEA. UN Women is an active member of the inter-agency PSEA network and all UN Women staff have been trained on PSEA including Gender field Officers who serve as camp level PSEA reference points and who have further trained all UN Women Rohingya volunteers on PSEA and inter-agency code of conduct.

project_name: Improved access to quality child protection and gender base violence services for children and adolescents affected by conflict in north-east Nigeria.
project_objective:
UNICEF Child Protection project, in line with the Minimum Standards for Child Protection and Gender-Based Violence in Humanitarian Actions, will focus on strengthening access to quality preventive and responsive child protection services that address the needs, rights and dignity of children and their caregivers’ in the conflict affected states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe. UNICEF child protection project will ensure that emergency response prioritizes the most vulnerable including at-risk children and their families. UNICEF’s efforts to address CPiE and GBViE is part of its over-all strategy on prevention and response to all forms of violence against children (VAC) through adopt community-based approaches, system strengthening and localization strategies throughout the project lifespan.   The present project module is part of ongoing efforts to provide a comprehensive, multi-year child protection and gender based violence programme interventions that aims to support the psychosocial wellbeing of conflict affected children, quality case management services for Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC) and survivors of violence, and reinsertion together with community-based reintegration of children and adolescents formerly associated with Non State Armed Groups (NSAGs) within their communities. Girls and boys’ survivors of gender-based violence (GBV), including conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) will also have access safe spaces and benefit from case management, information and referral systems to specialized services as needed. All interventions will adapt the COVID19 prevention guidelines issued by Nigerian authorities and WHO.  
This project aims to prevent violence against children and respond with child protection services building on previous experiences and lessons learned in north-east Nigeria including child protection response during the COVID 19 pandemic.The project will empower affected communities to break the culture of silence and bring about significant change in social norms through awareness raising on child protection issues and GBV education. In addition, the project will further focus on child protection system mapping, system strengthening such as the domestication of federal Child Rights Act (CRA) and enhancement of the capacity of the social service workforce to improve the quality and coordination of response and sustain the outcomes. The System building approach will complement the humanitarian-developmental nexus approach of UNICEF and the Resilience Integrated Child Protection Programming for Children in north-east Nigeria. The project will strengthen the localization agenda working with both international, national NGOs and civil Society organizations to strengthen capacity for local and sustainable development in the North East.Results will be achieved by providing integrated child protection case management services for children affected by conflict including UASC &  delivering quality socio-economic reintegration services to children formerly associated with NSAGs as well as other vulnerable children and their families. Conflict-affected children will have access to community-based MHPSS,including structured recreational activities and adolescents’ life skills education to build and retain their resilience to shock. The project will also contribute to strengthening capacity of service delivery to GBV survivors. Child survivors of GBV will in addition will have access to comprehensive minimum lifesaving GBV services including health, psychosocial and safety and protection services and access to legal aid be. Children and caregivers living in explosive hazards contaminated areas will be provided with risk education information’s through schools and child friendly spaces with the support of Mine Action sub sector. The geographic locations will be prioritized according to the severity of needs and access

project_name: Children and youth education and resilience
project_objective: The overall objective of the NRC education programme in Bangladesh is to ensure that displacement-affected Rohingya and host community children and youth enjoy quality education and life-long learning opportunities that will ensure they are able to live and work in dignity. NRC’s education programme will target adolescents and youth (14-24 years old) including Rohingya refugees displaced by the conflict in Myanmar, host communities and Bangladeshis affected by climate displacement. Out of school Rohingya refugee and host community adolescents and youth will be supported to access relevant, quality learning opportunities. Host community children and youth at risk of dropping out will be targeted through retention programme that will be implemented in the public schools. Climate internally displaced children and youth will be targeted through an emergency programme that will provide a safe space for them to connect and share experiences. Teachers, learning facilitators, trainers and education personnel will be targeted through continuous professional development. NRC will focus on intensive professional development programmes for females in order to overcome the barrier of the female participation in the programme. NRC will consolidate and expand its youth programming. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable children and youth in Bangladesh through the delivery of various programmes that will create different learning pathways. Education team will provide the most vulnerable children and youth with basic skills, including literacy and numeracy, remedial classes, life skills and vocational skills. The team will also work on strengthening existing systems — via teacher professional development, asset provision to schools, supporting school governance structures, and more to support the retention and improve the wellbeing of students in schools. The team will ensure first-phase education response to climate displacement by strengthening protection, social connectedness, and learning.  Education will continue to develop alternative methods to reach children and youth with learning opportunities such as self-learning and e-learning modules if access is restricted as during COVID. NRC will construct temporary learning centres, the TLCs are equipped with WASH facilities and water source, disability access, solar power for ventilation and lighting, fencing etc. All possible in the camp setting disability-inclusiveness measures will be taken - including physical measures as well as training of the learning facilitators. Every learning facility is managed by an education committee that consists of 7 community members consisting of at least 2 women, parents of the learners, influential members of the community and the Host teacher. They committee meets biweekly to discuss the learning process and give feedback. NRC will train learning facilitators on identification and referral of possible protection cases. Referral pathways will be identified for each TLC and HBLC; both staff at learning centres and NRC staff trained on the use of the referral pathways. NRC does not take responsibility of management of the cases, and only refers them to identified protections services.

project_name: Assistance humanitaire d’urgence (kits abris d’urgence, AME, WASH, protection et prise en charge psychosociale) des populations nouvellement affectées par les chocs dans les régions du Centre Est, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de l’Est à travers le mécanisme de réponse rapide aux mouvements de populations au Burkina Faso (RRM)
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire au Burkina Faso reste préoccupante notamment dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Centre Est, du Centre Nord, de l’Est, du Nord et du Sahel.  Le nombre de personnes déplacés du fait des incidents sécuritaires a été estimé à 1,03 millions de personnes (dont 22,9% de femmes, 16,7% d’hommes et 60,4% d’enfants de moins de 18 ans) et sont pour la plupart concentrées dans ces six régions prioritaires du HRP/HNO (CONASUR, Septembre 2020).
La majorité des PDI est constituée d’enfants de moins de 18 ans et de femmes qui se retrouvent parfois toutes seules avec leurs enfants pour devenir chef de ménage de fait, en l’absence de nouvelles de leurs conjoints. L’insécurité a affecté profondément le fonctionnement des services sociaux de base ; ce sont environ 2000 écoles qui sont fermées et 300 000 personnes affectées (OCHA, mai 2020), 95 formations sanitaires fermées avec environ 1,2 millions de personnes affectées, etc. (OCHA, en Août 2020), limitant ainsi leur accès notamment aux populations les plus vulnérables (femmes, enfants, personnes handicapées, personnes âgées ainsi que des réfugiés). L’accès aux services d’eau et d’assainissement, déjà limité dans les zones affectées par la crise a été exacerbé par les mouvements de populations et auraient entrainé une diminution globale de 11% de l’accès à l’eau potable dans les communes accueillant la majorité des déplacés. D’une manière générale, la majorité de ces PDI (80%) vivent dans des conditions de logement très précaires. En outre, ces populations dans leur fuite face aux menaces, n’ont pas pour la plupart des cas, la possibilité d’emporter leurs biens alimentaires ou non alimentaires déjà limitées du fait de leur vulnérabilité parfois structurelle. Pour apporter une assistance adéquate à ces personnes affectées, les acteurs humanitaires en collaboration avec le gouvernement ont élaboré un plan de réponse 2021 en cours de finalisation. Les besoins qui sont immenses et variés, concerneront entre autres, 1 422 364 personnes (soit 325 721 femmes, 237 535 hommes, 859 108 enfants) dans le secteur des abris/AME, environ 1 600 000 personnes du WASH (dont 366 400 femmes, 267 200 hommes, 966 400), 1 535 429 personnes en besoin de protection (dont 351 613 femmes, 256 417 hommes, 927 399 enfants).
La présente action a été proposée vise à « fournir une assistance humanitaire d'urgence aux PDI affectées par les chocs dans les régions du Centre Est, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de l’Est » dans les secteurs de abris/AME (86 100 personnes dont 19 717 femmes, 14 379 hommes, 52 004 enfants soit 5,4% des populations dans le besoin) en collaboration avec les autorités locales , de la WASH (86 100 personnes dont 19 717 femmes, 14 379 hommes, 52 004 enfants soit 5,4% des populations dans le besoin) et la protection  (86 100 personnes dont 204 femmes, 149 hommes, 538 enfants soit 0,1% des populations dans le besoin). En fonction des besoins à couvrir dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Sahel et dans d’autres région du pays, le RRM pourra se déployer en dernier recours.

project_name: Emergency and post-emergency response to protection needs of conflict-affected populations in Syria
project_objective:
The organization seeks to alleviate and mitigate the accidents related to the presence of explosive ordnances (EOs) in contaminated areas and increase the protection of at-risk persons through direct and indirect risk education activities, and through the identification, marking and disposal of EOs spots. The risk education (RE)component includes three key activities as follows:
-	RE Sessions’ which aim that the at-risks persons, living in contaminated areas, have the necessary information to be able to adopt safe behaviours and reduce the threats posed by the presence of explosive hazards. Based on context, access and needs analysis, this is conducted either through direct RE sessions at households’ level or through Training of Trainers to strengthen the skills of key local actors and ensure the proper dissemination of the messages through a sustainable approach. Noting that the sessions include the COVID-19 key messages, and the provision of the personal protection equipment while maintaining the preventative measures to mitigate the risk of virus transmission. 
-	Contamination Impact Surveys which aim to identify locations that have experienced a certain level of bombing, shelling and fighting.
-	Accident and Victim surveys which aim to identify the areas in which the accident occurred, and the type of weapon that is suspected to be the cause of the accident. An accident could result in one or more victims or even no victims at all.
During the provision of RE activities, people who need multi-disciplinary rehabilitation services are internally referred to supported health centres, where they can have access to a variety of services depending on the outcomes of their needs assessment process. In addition, safety briefings are provided to humanitarian actors (local and international NGOs) to raise their awareness within the humanitarian community about risks and the consequences of explosive hazards they could face when in the field to minimize the risk of accidents among aid workers.
In Parallel, Non-Technical Survey and clearance teams identify, mark and dispose EOs. It starts in the collection of surveys to obtain accurate information on the presence, type & level of contamination in the areas. Prioritization is dependent on the presence of IDPs in communities where there are visible EOs in their area or the presence of any community in areas where the accidents that have occurred within the past 6 months. Currently, the organization implements clearance activities in Raqqa, while maintaining the possibility of deploying Clearance teams to Deir Ezzor if the context allows. 
Finally, The organisation’s advocacy team continues to lobby for the ban of the use of Explosive Weapons in Populated Areas and produce then disseminate evidence-based advocacy factsheets to mobilize and influence local, national, regional and International stakeholders by raising key humanitarian and protection issues for populations and humanitarian actors in Syria.

project_name: Perfectionnement et amélioration de la gestion et la coordination des sites d’accueil temporaires des personnes déplacées internes
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire au Burkina Faso s’est fortement dégradée ces dernières années déclenchant une crise de déplacement massive dans différentes régions du pays, notamment le Centre Nord, le Sahel, le Nord, l’Est et la Boucle du Mouhoun, avec dépassant la barre d’un million de personnes déplacées internes (PDI) depuis le 8 Aout 2020 réparties à travers 257 communes d’accueil selon les chiffres publiés par le CONASUR.
Plus d’une centaine de sites d’accueil temporaires ont été recensés à travers les régions du Centre-Nord, du Sahel et du Nord et selon les données du CONASUR, avec un pourcentage d’à peu près 22% de la population déplacée dans les familles d’accueil. Une grande majorité des sites de personnes déplacées internes fait état d’un taux élevé de niveau de congestion, augmentant les risques de protection et de violences basées sur le genre. La capacité d’accueil des population hôtes devient de plus en plus restreinte entrainant le déplacement des personnes déplacées dans les familles d’accueil vers les sites. L'absence de l'accès à de nouvelles terres reste une contrainte essentielle de décongestionner les sites ; l'encombrement des sites est aggravé par l'afflux continu de nouvelles de nouvelles arrivées en grande partie, en provenance de zones inaccessibles des régions du Sahel, du Centre-Nord, du Nord et de l’Est.

La coordination et la gestion des sites d’accueil temporaires sont essentielles pour assurer que les interventions sur les sites sont cohérentes, coordonnées, et se conforment aux normes internationales, tout en évitant les doublons et les lacunes. Le secteur du GSAT estime que 955 829 (dont 31.10% de filles, 31.20% de garçons, 20.50% de femmes, 13.50% d’hommes, 2.00% sont des femmes âgées et 1.70% sont des hommes âgés) doivent nécessiter d’un soutien ciblé en gestion des sites d’accueil temporaires et des services de 2020 à 2021.
Cependant, cette crise de déplacement généralisé et continue est caractérisée par l’ouverture de sites d’accueil temporaires planifiés ou non, par des déplacements secondaires mais également des déplacements internes d’une région à une autre. Ces nouvelles caractéristiques, couplées à la multiplicité des acteurs humanitaires et à une capacité de réponse encore faible, nécessite une approche zonale (area-based) intégrale pour la gestion et la coordination des personnes d’placés en site et hors site. A tout ceci s’ajoute l’absence de coordination de la réponse multisectorielle dans les sites d’accueil temporaires et centres collectifs.
Le programme de l’UNHCR pour la réponse d’urgence à la situation des PDI appuiera le CONASUR dans la gestion du déplacement interne dans les communes les plus affectées par le déplacement interne dans les régions affectées. Cette gestion comprendra (i) la collecte et la dissémination des données désagrégées sur les PDI, (ii) la redevabilité envers les communautés comme la communication (information sur les services disponibles, mise en place et gestion de mécanismes de plaintes et de feedback, (iii) l’évaluation continue des besoins des PDI et des lacunes dans la réponse et (iv) l’analyse des profils et enquêtes d’intentions afin d’ébaucher une stratégie de solutions durables. Au regard du caractère multiple des déplacements internes, l’UNHCR mettra en place une gestion mobile des sites d’accueil temporaires par axe en s’appuyant sur les outils de gestion notamment la cartographie des sites, la cartographie des services par axe ou zone de déplacement.

project_name: Prévention et traitement de la malnutrition aigüe sévère chez les enfants de moins 5 ans dans les 16 provinces les plus vulnérables au Burundi
project_objective:
Selon les résultats de l’Enquête sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et la Mortalité (ENSNMB2020), le taux de Malnutrition Aiguë Globale (MAG) est estimé à 6,1% dont 1.1% de MAS (malnutrition aiguë sévère). Cela place la situation nutritionnelle dans la catégorie « précaire  » selon les nouveaux seuils de l’OMS. Ce taux atteste une détérioration de la situation nutritionnelle car il était de 5,1% dont 1,1% de MAS en janvier 2019 selon l’Enquête Nationale sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et de Sécurité alimentaire (ENNSAB) utilisant la méthodologie JANFSA (Joint Nutrition, Food Security Analysis). 
L’analyse des besoins effectuée par les acteurs humanitaires du secteur de la nutrition a permis de retenir 16 provinces prioritaires avec un taux de MAG supérieur à 5 % à savoir Bubanza ,Bujumbura,Bururi,  Cankuzo , Cibitoke, Gitega, Kayanza, Karusi, Kirundo,Makamba, Muramvya, Mwaro, , Ngozi,Rutana, Ruyigi et Rumonge .
L'UNICEF appui le Ministère de la Santé pour la prevention et le traitement des enfants atteints de malnutrition aigue severe (MAS) à travers les activités de dépistage actif, de la promotion des pratiques familales essentielles, l'achat et l'approvisionnement des districts sanitaires en intrants nutritionnels . Ce Projet permettra le dépistage de 110,000 enfants ( filles et garçons ), l’achat des intrants nutritionnels et l’approvisionnement des districts pour  le traitement  58,898  enfants MAS(filles et garçons ) dans les  16 provinces .De plus , 98,000 personnes ( femmes et hommes)  seront sensibilisées sur les pratiques familiales essentielles dans le cadre de la prévention de la malnutrition sous toutes ses formes.

project_name: Protection and Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon
Renforcer l’environnement de protection a travers la vulgarisation de la loi portant asile au Tchad
project_objective:
Le Tchad a toujours été traditionnellement un pays d’accueil pour des populations opprimées fuyant les conflits armés, les guerres et autres calamites à la recherche de paix et de sécurité.
 A la date du 31 janvier 2021, le Tchad abrite sur son sol 919,112 personnes relevant du mandat de l’UNHCR dont 478 651 réfugiés de nationalités diverses et 336 124 déplacées internes. 
Cette politique d’asile généreuse à l’endroit de milliers de réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile originaires en majorité des pays de la sous-région en particulier le Soudan et la RCA traduit l’engagement du Tchad à œuvrer, sans relâche, au renforcement de l’environnement de protection internationale.
C’est ce qui ressort des Engagements (8 au total) pris par le Tchad lors du Forum de New York en Décembre 2016 mais aussi du Processus de Rabat dont l’un des objectifs du Plan d’Action de Marrakech consiste à « renforcer la protection des réfugiés et des personnes déplacées internes.»  
Bien que ces personnes aient toujours continué de jouir des droits et devoirs attachés à leur statut respectif, il n’en demeure pas moins que ces prérogatives n’étaient pas formalisées voire encadrées par une norme juridique. Après d’intenses plaidoyers et avec le soutien de la CNARR et d’autres acteurs, celle-ci a finalement vu le jour. Il s’agit de la loi portant asile au Tchad.
Avec l’adoption de cette loi par l’Assemblée Nationale du Tchad en décembre 2020, le Gouvernement tchadien entendait par-là combler un vide juridique et en même temps manifester sa ferme volonté de renforcer l’environnement de protection internationale des refugies et d’autres personnes relevant de l’UNHCR. 
Ainsi, après avoir déterminé les conditions générales d’asile en République du Tchad , elle indique, en son article 31, que  tout réfugié a droit à la délivrance, par les autorités compétentes, des documents dont une carte d’identité pour réfugié et un Titre de Voyage de la Convention.
Les dispositions de cette loi ne sont pas encore suffisamment connues ni par les refugies eux-mêmes, ni par les autorités locales, ni le public encore moins les partenaires du HCR et même le personnel. 
C’est la raison pour laquelle, le HCR envisage de définir un cadre d’action a travers co projets en fixant des objectifs ainsi qu’un budget previsionnel afin de renforcer le cadre juridique de la protection des refugies et demandeurs d’asile vivant au Tchad.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Item kits for the most vulnerable displaced populations in North-West, South-West of Cameroon
project_objective:
IOM plans to provide tailored shelter/non-food item (NFI) and cash assistance through rental subsidies to the most vulnerable Internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees identified through vulnerability assessments in the North-West, South-West (NWSW) regions throughout 2021, to increase the overall capacity of the cluster/sector to address urgent needs and alleviate suffering. Vulnerability characteristics will be based on various household criteria, including household size and current state and condition of existing shelter.  Interventions will be in line with the Shelter/NFI cluster guidelines, be done through different intervention modalities applicable to Cameroon (directing in-kind distributions, cash interventions, vouchers, among others), as well as be aimed at the targeted populations depending on vulnerability criteria.
IOM will use the displacement data collected through its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) and notably the Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) in NWSW regions to target and provide rapid emergency shelter/NFI support to the most vulnerable, newly displaced populations and returnees. The sectoral assistance will focus on addressing the needs of individuals who are forced into repeated short-term displacements and are seeking refuge in makeshift shelters or agricultural structures in the surrounding bushes of their villages. Repeated displacements, even if short-term, are forcing the affected populations to sell their assets to survive and resort to negative coping mechanisms, which in turn increases their vulnerability.
Meanwhile, and in response to the regular ETTs updates reported by the DTM on the most recent displacement situations, IOM seeks to preposition NFI and Emergency Shelter kits in its warehouses in Kumba and Bemanda in NWSW ensure rapid and effective response in both regions to crises and shocks. The NFI and shelter kits will be distributed to most vulnerable beneficiaries with the support of trusted and experienced local partners to increase operational access to hard-to-reach affected areas, based on experience developed through UN CERF funded shelter/NFI emergency interventions since early 2020 in the NWSW. The NFI kits composition will be based on the sector standards for the region. In addition, IOM will provide a 3-month rental subsidy for affected populations living in urban areas. The specific amount disbursed to beneficiaries will be defined  in coordination with the shelter/NFI sector partners.
The specific activities and targeted results will be as follows: 
Outcome: Conflict-affected populations in North-West, South-West regions benefit from an immediate improvement of living standards, well-being, and dignity.

project_name: Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The project “Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine” (2019-2021) aims to improve food security, hygiene conditions, preparedness to winter and psychosocial well-being of conflict-affected populations in the 5-km zone along the 'contact line' in Eastern Ukraine (GCA of Luhanska and Donetska oblasts). 
Whereas the project’s food, hygiene and winterization components are implemented by ASB Country Office Ukraine, the psychosocial support (PSS) is provided by ASB’s local partner, Samaritan Union of Ukraine (SSU). The project is currently funded by the Federal Foreign Office of the Federal Republic of Germany
Within the framework of the food security component of the project, vulnerable beneficiaries will receive cash for food assistance. 
ASB will target primarily households of older men and women, persons with disabilities, chronically ill, persons aged 40-60 with no employment as well as men and women with compound vulnerabilities. Depending on the availability of funding and food needs, the cash for food will be provided during the first half of 2021 or throughout the year. 
Since ASB Country Office Ukraine is already operating in the area, it has immediate capacity and access to implement the planned activities also in 2021. Moreover, ASB has secured funding to implement the cash for food activities in the first half of 2021. The planned activities will be coordinated with other FSLC partners and follow the principles of do no harm, disability inclusion and accountability to affected populations (AAP). In the time of COVID-19 pandemic, all activities will follow the COVID-19 Ukraine Assistance Delivery Protocol. 
The project activities contribute to the FSLC Objective 1: “Ensure immediate access to food for the most vulnerable people affected by conflict and/or СOVID-19”.

project_name: Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
This project is the WASH component of a multisectoral response of ASB in the 5-km zone along the ‘contact line’ in the GCA of Donetska and Luhanska oblasts. Overall, the project “Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine” (14 June 2019-13 June 2021) aims to improve food security, hygiene conditions, preparedness to winter and psychosocial well-being of conflict-affected populations in the 5-km zone along the 'contact line' in Eastern Ukraine (GCA of Luhanska and Donetska oblasts). Whereas selection criteria are similar for some project components (e.g. food, hygiene and winterization), some vulnerable people benefit from several project activities. Such approach strengthens synergies between different components of this multisectoral project.
Whereas the project’s food, hygiene and winterization components are implemented by ASB Country Office Ukraine, the psychosocial support (PSS) is provided by ASB’s local partner, Samaritan Union of Ukraine (SSU).  
Within the framework of the WASH component of the project, vulnerable beneficiaries receive cash and/or in-kind hygiene assistance. The vulnerable households in the 5-km zone near the ‘contact line’ will be provided with cash for hygiene to cover their basic hygiene needs (soap, washing powder, toothpaste, etc.). Moreover, people in need of adult diapers will be provided with hygiene kits for persons with special needs and, depending on a need, small family hygiene kits/PPEs. These project activities contribute to the WASH Objective 2: “Provision of critical hygiene-related supplies and information for the prevention of infectious diseases”.  
The project is currently funded by the Federal Foreign Office of the Federal Republic of Germany.

project_objective:
The project “Hygiene, Nutrition and Winterization as Cash as well as Psychosocial Support for Conflict-Affected People in need along the Contact Line, Eastern Ukraine” (2019-2021) aims to improve food security, hygiene conditions, preparedness to winter and psychosocial well-being of conflict-affected populations in the 5-km zone along the 'contact line' in Eastern Ukraine (GCA of Luhanska and Donetska oblasts). 
The psychosocial component of the project is implemented by ASB’s local partner, Samaritan Union of Ukraine (SSU). Through provision of psychosocial support (PSS), the project aims at to reduce social isolation and loneliness of conflict-affected older people, children and adolescents as well as to increase their resilience to stress. 
The project is currently funded by the Federal Foreign Office of the Federal Republic of Germany.

project_name: Informing humanitarian planning and response to the needs of persons affected by displacement in Somalia through baseline assessments and population-based surveys
project_objective:
The project aims to contribute to evidence-based decision making for humanitarian operations in Somalia through IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM). 

Under the coordination of the Information Management and Assessments Working Group (IMAWG) and in collaboration with all clusters, DTM will provide reliable and up to date information on the number of displaced populations, their location, profile, displacement trends, reasons for displacement, and needs disaggregated by age and sex to better assist and inform the governmental and humanitarian response. In particular, DTM’s data will feed into the 2021 roadmap of the IDP Working Group in order to provide regular updates on the IDP stocks across Somalia. 

DTM tools have the potential to be tailored to take into account changes in the national context as well as information needs of responders working across the HDP nexus.

project_name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, 
 programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to:
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018-2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity.
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food.
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

project_name: Protection assistance for conflict affected population in the South West of Cameroon
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in the Southwest region of Cameroon has exposed the local population to large scale protection risks and human rights violations and impacted vulnerable households’ capacity to meet their emergency food needs. 
Through this Action, the IRC seeks to improve the protection status of vulnerable people affected by the crisis in Southwest Cameroon, assisting the most vulnerable people to stay safe, access assistance, recover from violence and claim their rights. The IRC will do this through an integrated program of Protection prevention and response activities to mitigate further protection risks resulting from the use of negative coping mechanisms.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso continue de se développer rapidement, étendant sa portée à de nouvelles zones et aggravant ses impacts sur les populations touchées. En août 2020, le nombre de personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays en raison du conflit, de l'insécurité et du manque d'accès aux services de base a grimpé en flèche pour atteindre plus d'un million, plus des trois quarts vivant dans des conditions précaires sans accès à un abri adéquat ou à l'eau et à l'assainissement. L'insécurité et les déplacements sont des facteurs clés qui entraînent une forte augmentation du nombre de personnes ayant besoin d'aide, exacerbant l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle chronique. La présence de la COVID-19 est aussi autre facteur d’augmentation des besoins. Au milieu de l'année, le nombre de personnes ayant besoin d'aide humanitaire (PiN - Population in Need) était passé à 2,9 millions dans les cinq régions ciblées par la communauté humanitaire dans le cadre du Plan de Réponse Humanitaire 2020 (HRP). Pour 2021, le pays aura à soutenir 3,5 millions de personnes dans un besoin humanitaire dans 6 régions.
Le bureau de pays du Burkina Faso va appuyer le la mise en oeuvre des activités
prioritaires dans les cinq domaines d'intervention de OCHA, notamment
• Renforcer la coordination humanitaire au niveau stratégique et aux niveaux
opérationnels et assurer un leadership dans de la coordination
humanitaire, y compris la coordination civilo-militaire (UN-CMCoord) ; le suivi et le
plaidoyer en matière d’accès humanitaire ; l'engagement communautaire et la redevabilité
envers les personnes affectées ;
• Renforcer le plaidoyer humanitaire, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées
internes et les personnes non déplacées ;
• Soutenir l'application pratique de la politique humanitaire et les bonnes pratiques, y
compris la promotion de la collaboration entre l'humanitaire, le développement et les
acteurs de la consolidation de la paix tout en respectant la distinction et l'intégrité de
l'action humanitaire ;
• Faciliter une mobilisation cohérente et coordonnée du financement humanitaire ; 
• Fournir une gestion de l'information de haute qualité et pour soutenir le leadership
humanitaire et la prise de décision.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Acute Malnutrition for Affected Communities, Especially Girls and Boys Under Five and Pregnant and Lactating Women, in Jonglei, Warrap and Northern Bahr el Ghazal states.
project_objective:
The cumulative effects of years of prolonged conflict, the COVID-19 Pandemic, chronic vulnerabilities and weak essential services have left over 6 million people in need of humanitarian assistance in South Sudan. The country remains in a critical period of severe food insecurity with 7.24 million people projected by the IPC to be facing severe acute food insecurity in the first half of 2021 and will be in need of urgent assistance. While, around 2.5 million will be in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) with very high acute malnutrition and excess mortality. Around 1.4 million children aged between 6 months and 5 years are likely to be acutely malnourished in 2021 and will need life-saving treatment. This includes 313,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition and more than a million children suffering from moderate acute malnutrition. At the same time, 483,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women are expected to be acutely malnourished and in need of treatment. 
Under this project, the proposed activities include prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition in children U5 and pregnant and lactating women using the national CMAM and inpatient guidelines; provision of basic health services at our Stabilization Centers (SC) and community based healthcare using iCCM approach through the outreach clinics; and provision of minimum WASH services to beneficiaries at nutrition sites and at community level. The program will directly target 78,473 children under 5 and 15,623 pregnant and lactating women in treatment of acute malnutrition at 3 stabilization centres and 40 nutrition sites (OTP/TSFP). 
To ensure early detection and timely referral of acute malnutrition, community volunteers will be trained to facilitate screening and referral at the household level through Family MUAC approach. During these screenings, volunteers will also provide sensitization on nutrition and hygiene/sanitation practices. Prevention activities will focus on community mobilization and sensitization as well as addressing the underlying causes of malnutrition. In total, 44,881 caregivers will be sensitized on MIYCN topics. These activities include training community leaders, promoting mother-to-mother support groups (MtMSG), and facilitating men group discussions (MGDs) to encourage discussion among male caregivers on critical nutrition and health subjects. To address underlying causes of undernutrition, Action Against Hunger will train lead mothers of MtMSGs in kitchen gardening and cooking demonstrations in collaboration with our FSL program. In addition to these static interventions, Action Against Hunger’s emergency response teams will also continue to provide malnutrition surveillance, treatment and prevention services, and capacity building throughout the country in areas of highest need as identified by the Nutrition Cluster’s Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism.
Disaster Risk Reduction is a key element of the proposed project given the locations and both natural and man-made disasters experienced frequently in these areas. South Sudan continues to face extremely high prevalence of Gender-Based Violence (GBV). Hence, it is imperative that humanitarian interventions are gender sensitive. Action Against Hunger proposes to:
a) continue its efforts to mainstream GBV and gender considerations in its Nutrition, WaSH, FSL and health programs, and b) support the humanitarian community in South Sudan to remain accountable for GBV and gender-sensitivity.
All the proposed project activities will be carried out following the COVID-19 prevention protocols and guidelines provided by the ministry of health and nutrition cluster.

project_name: Provision of integrated equitable access to sufficient safe water, sanitation and  hygiene services among malnutrition, GBV at risk/affected and food insecure communities of Northern Barh el Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states.
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger (ACF) has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs. Our strategy addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WASH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently ACF is implementing program activities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states and COVID-19 response in Juba with country office in Juba, and established field offices in Malualkon, Alek, Old Fangak and Paguir Payams. In 2021, WASH projects will be implemented to ensure that host communities, IDPs and returnees have safe access to sufficient water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behavior. Proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5, pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WASH and Nutrition response aimed at breaking the diarrhea – malnutrition vicious cycle. This project will ensure the effectiveness of addressing malnutrition in the proposed target area by reducing disease burden in communities as well as availing safe, potable water for use in appetite tests at nutrition sites. To achieve the overall project objective and WASH cluster Sectoral objectives of the HRP, ACF will provide critical services to 87,599 individuals, including 70,079 at the village level and 17,520 (non-double counted) beneficiaries in targeted Nutrition Sites and SCs.  All work will be done per WaSH Cluster strategy in close coordination with line ministries’ guidelines for implementing WaSH during the COVID-19 Pandemic. The project has 6 Main objectives;
1)	CO1 WASH integrated intervention starting at nutrition facilities targeting the couple “mother/care-taker – severely malnourished child” until HH level aiming at breaking WASH-related diseases transmission cycle. Tonj East, Aweil South, Pigi/Canal, Gogrial west, Gogrial East, Fangak and Aweil East)
Through provision of WASH kits to SAM and MAM cases a total of 65 functional nutrition facilities are targeted, this include 25 new OTP/ST; 16 in Fangak county, 4 in Aweil East 3 in Aweil Center and 5 in Tonj East. Activities will include; conducting hygiene promotion activities at nutrition sites, household and wider community level, improving access to safe water especially in high GAM prevalence counties through; borehole rehabilitation and or, where necessary/feasible drilling of new water points, latrines rehab/construction of semi to permanent based on need according to WASH cluster resilient sectoral objective guidelines. 2) CO2  Reducing prevalence of WASH-related diseases and risk of outbreak by transmission contexts upon epidemiological investigation, 3) CO3 Access to basic services (WASH) in emergencies, 4) CO4 WASH specific activities for GBV mitigation
5) CO5 Provide permanent access to water and sanitation services for IDPs, returnees, hosts and chronically affected by floods and (pre-) famine conditions and 6) CO6 Improve access to safe water and promote safe hygiene practices in communities showing high prevalence of GAM and high WASH vulnerabilities.
Range of selective activities will be implemented in different counties from emergency, semi-permanent to permanent/long term activities as described in the activities section.

project_name: Increasing access to essential reproductive health and immunization services and improving the nutritional status for pregnant and lactating women and children in Syria
project_objective:
The project will work to reduce maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality through provision of ANC, safe delivery, early initiation of breastfeeding, and PNC. Services will be provided through the reproductive health units/clinics within the supported nutrition centres. SC will train midwives on IYCF-E concepts and best practices with special focus on early initiation of breastfeeding and skin-to-skin contact, including within the first few hours after delivery. To address the challenges to follow-up visits, community health workers (CHWs) will be trained to conduct basic ANC and PNC visits at household level and/or virtually, and to support with referrals and transportation. In light of COVID-19, new protocols and operational guidelines have been adopted for the clinics including limiting waiting room areas to 3-4 people and ensuring distancing between health staff and beneficiaries.

To ensure that the target population has sufficient immune protection against any wild polio virus transmission, SC will aim at 95% vaccination coverage among children 6-59 months of age against WPV in target areas (OPV3) while contributing to reduced morbidity and mortality due to other vaccine-preventable diseases by restarting the routine vaccination program (DPT3) through supporting multiple EPI centers in North West Syria.

Furthermore, the following ANC/PNC services will be will be provided through mobile units/clinics within IDP camps and hard-to-reach areas, and with the support of community health workers:
- Antenatal iron and folic acid supplementation 
- Prescription for antenatal calcium supplementation
- Tetanus toxoid (in coordination with vaccination team), women will be referred to the nearest vaccination team after assessing their tetanus vaccination status.
- Basic blood tests (RH group, blood glucose) (available in the mobile clinics)
- Ultrasound scans, monitor foetal growth and movement (available in the mobile clinics)
- Screening for pregnancy-induced hypertension. 
- Postnatal care checks for women who recently gave birth, check against main mother and baby danger signs, and refer cases accordingly.

Adolescents will be targeted in project activities - mainly by providing them access to the reproductive health,  family planning and post-abortion care. Furthermore, activities will be implemented in areas easily accessed by PWD, and supporting people with physical disabilities to have access to the health services. The staff also will receive basic PSS training that can support in supporting the identification of people with mental health disorders. People with living with disability will be referred to service providers, if they are available in the area. Emergency cases are referred through the allocated ambulance car in the center, with the referral forms filled for each, while for non-emergency referral is made by community health workers and/or facilities staff, through indicating the health facilities where the patient can seek the specific type of services in.

project_name: Common Transport Services for Humanitarian Partners in South Sudan
project_objective:
The Common Transport Services (CTS) is a free-for-user service that transports key humanitarian supplies on behalf of humanitarian actors. CTS serves as a critical link in the supply chain, enabling products and materials that arrive from regional and international suppliers to move onwards to partners located deep in the field rapidly. IOM has been managing the CTS on behalf of the Logistics Cluster since 2011. During this tie, the project has significantly grown from delivering 2,000 MT of humanitarian cargo in 2011 to a total of 17,773 MT by the end of 2020, making a yearly average of 25000 MT since the beginning, highlighting the increase in the use of road transport as the most cost-efficient mode of transportation as access improves. IOM has continued to maintain flexibility and adaptability to the operating environment in South Sudan. Through CTS, IOM works with more than 80 unique agencies in key operational locations in Jonglei, Unity, and Greater Upper Nile Region, in Humanitarian Logistics Hubs (Malakal, Bentiu), and Rumbek, Bor, Juba, and Wau, which are part of intersectoral severity counties level 4 to 5 and prioritized counties according to the HNO 2021. IOM will maintain heavy vehicles and transport cargo from the main ports of dispatch via air, road, and river and will continue common warehouse management in key operational locations. 

Through the effective management of the CTS, IOM aims to support organizations' preparedness measures to mitigate risks associated with increased insecurity, looting/theft of humanitarian supplies, critical access impediments to vulnerable people, and reduce expensive air costs, which ultimately supports the timely response to the needs of the affected populations. With this funding, IOM will directly work with 80 humanitarian organizations located in different areas, enabling them to deliver critical life-saving humanitarian services and assistance items.

project_name: Integrated Multi-AoR protection services for high at risk groups in Jebel Saman, Aleppo
project_objective:
The intervention is part of a project aiming at securing the basic needs and providing integrated community-based protection activities in Karm Jazmati, Seken Shebebi, Karm al Tarrab, and Dahret Awwad. The project is held by Caritas Germany (CS), back-funded by the German Federal Foreign Ministry (GFO) and implemented from 01.04.2019 -31.12.2022 by Caritas Syria (CS). It was initially designed based on the results of a needs assessment conducted in Karm Jazmati in January 2019, and has been, upon extension and top-up in 2021, adjusted to changing needs as per M/E results. In course of the project phase two, which started on 01.04.2021, the project locations have shifted: While Jazmati is still the main project location where the Community Center is based, Jabal Badro has been taken out of the intervention since there have been other actors providing basic assistance and CS has, under another project, started implementing Livelihood and Early Recovery activities. Coordination meetings with other (I)NGOs as well as the sub-sectors FSL, and protection, three new neighborhoods bordering Jazmati, have been included in the project. In direct and continuous contact with the FSL and protection sector, CS has started to implement BA and protection activities in the new areas as of April 2021 and is considered the main actor for these sectors in Jazmati, Seken Shebebi, Karm al Tarrab, and Dahret Awwad.
Following a participatory approach, the needs have been regularly assessed, i.e., via PDMs applying a proportional piling method, and FDGs. Furthermore, a robust FCM has contributed to ensure the engagement and thus self-identification of the needs in the community. Hence, throughout the project lifetime, the engagement of all community members has been promoted, establishing a two-way communication with the community. This has ensured a timely incorporation of community feedback. 
The regular coordination with the Aleppo-based sub-sectors Protection, CP, GBV, and FSL as well as the application of a protection scoring system,CS ensures the inclusion of high at-risk groups in protection activities while avoiding duplication of efforts. The community center in Jazmati has been well received by the residents of Jazmati since its opening in 2019 and continues to be the central point for the provision of integrated community-based protection services, to women, adolescent girls, children and elderly. 
The center follows an open-door policy, ensuring the active engagement of the community, allowing real-time evaluations and timely adjustments of activities as per beneficiaries’ feedback.  In response to the feedback collected from beneficiaries, i.e. via PDMs, satisfaction surveys, and FGDs, and following the strategy of the protection sector, the activities are adjusted in 2021-22. Following an inclusive approach, non-specialized PSS, and awareness sessions for women, children, elderly, and men are planned. Contributing to the reduction of GBV risks, literacy courses for women will be provided. Applying interactive learning approaches, informal education activities (Maths, Arabic, and English) for school-aged children will contribute to reducing child protection risk factors. Further, capacity strengthening activities for the CS team will be offered to further increase the responding capacity of CS.

project_name: Improved protection mechanisms for most vulnerable groups in the West Bank and Gaza through increased access and quality mental health and psychosocial  services with comprehensive and gender sensitive approach
project_objective:
Médicos del Mundo Spain (MdM-S) will contribute through this project to the achievement of Strategic Objective No. 2 of the Protection Cluster Strategy, i.e. (2) “Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence”.

In particular, this project will tackle protection for the mitigation the effects of occupation and conflict-related violence, risk of forcible transfer in the West Bank, impact of blockade in Gaza, settler violence, etc. through an increased access to quality enhanced public Mental Health services and MHPSS outreach services at the community level. The project will specifically target population, and in particular children, affected by the conflict in the West Bank and Gaza. This will be done incorporating the IASC MHPSS core principles: human rights and equity, participation, do no harm, integrated support to systems and building on available resources and capacities; and the enhancement of a coordinated and effective response to critical incidents. MdM intends to pursue the following activities between 2021 and 2022: •Provision of Child Protection response, with special emphasis on safe spaces for responsive interventions in emergencies, including case management and PSS for children and families and PWD, adopting appropriate measures to mitigate risks related to COVID19 •Provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial services (MHPSS) for adults and youth, with special emphasis on gender equality and PWD. •Capacity building of public Mental Health Services to address children and adolescents needs following appropriate guidelines and standards, using online training when needed to mitigate COVID19 related risks. •Advocacy initiatives among the international community that aim to address protection concerns; prevent violations or enhance accountability for violations of IHRL and IHL by all duty bearers. • Contribute to coordination and participation in the Protection Cluster, Education Cluster,  CPMHPSS subcluster and progressively increasing contributions to GBV subcluster. MdM signs the MoUs directly with the MoE and MoH; and at the same time, we strengthening the exchange of good practices, lessons learned, methodologies and resource guides among the different local COBs with responsibility in Protection in the areas of intervention.
ACCESS
1.MHPSS services 
Long experience in direct implementation in the Bedouin communities. Trust and acceptance built: the communities share their main problems, concerns, and challenges. Special attention to children and adolescents for managing emotions, detecting cases with special needs, appropriate referral and close follow up of the cases. Strengthening the resilience of the most vulnerable groups to provide PSS, applying the emergency protocol designed by MdM in collaboration with other national and international actors (PCC, YMCA, UNRWA).

2.Psychoeducation sessions 
Strengthening capacities of local focal points and schools through integration of MHPSS in education, through training and improvement of infrastructure (safe spaces). In WB the project is implemented with PCC and in coordination with the MoH and MoE
MdM and PCC began their partnership in 2017 strengthening skills in Psychological First Aid (PFA) of school counselors. Since then, have worked systematically to strengthen the psychosocial care capacities of school counselors in the Governorate of Jericho and to improve CP mechanisms through training of teachers and parents.

QUALITY
1. Capacity building to improve detection, first management and referral of MH cases, and self-care for staff in MHPSS, PHC, Education and CBOs. Gender and disability approaches are integrated both in Gaza and the WB, following international guidelines and standards (IASC, Sphere, HCS and others).
2. Design and adapt specific spaces for MH first response for children and adolescents affected by conflict-related violence in schools and CMHC.

project_name: Ensure effective ISCG coordination for a responsive implementation of the Joint Response activities
project_objective:
Humanitarian actors are supporting the Government of Bangladesh’s efforts to ensure a timely and efficient response, unimpeded humanitarian access, a common analysis of needs, and a voice for Rohingya refugees, women, men, boys, and girls, and affected host communities.

In 2021, UNHCR will continue to lead and coordinate actors engaged in the humanitarian response. This includes ongoing advocacy for the protection of refugees regardless of their legal status and location through active participation in and staffing support to the ISCG based in Cox’s Bazar.

In addition, in line with the recommendations of the coordination review and consultation with the sectors and working groups, UNHCR’s engagement with the Government and humanitarian actors will further increase, in a way that fosters an integrated approach across all sectors, including protection, field, and technical and operational support. Management and sector linkages will be reinforced, ensuring a timely, coordinated, and adequate response to the humanitarian situation.  

UNHCR in collaboration with the relevant Agencies will streamline and improve the efficiency of the humanitarian response through effective coordination and leadership. In 2021, UNHCR will support the cost-sharing of technical support, staffing and administrative operational costs of the ISCG as well as the implementation of the joint MSNA (Multi-Sector Needs Assessment) for refugees with UNHCR partner(s).

UNHCR will ensure the centrality of protection and protection and gender mainstreaming through inclusive coordination and leadership of the overall humanitarian response, with a key focus on PSEA. Through the coordination efforts, UNHCR will bolster inclusion through support to host communities, addressing the broader challenges that undermine protection space while promoting peaceful coexistence and social cohesion. UNHCR will empower Rohingya refugees by placing them at the centre of the response, building community capacities for leadership, self-management, and engagement with the Government and the humanitarian community.

project_name: Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance to Rohingya and Host Communities in Realisation of Rights to Legal Identity and HLP Rights.
project_objective: The project is designed to positively increase access to identity/civil documentation (mainly birth, death, marriage, and divorce certificates), documents required for accessing essential services, and HLP including tenancy rights in the refugee camps and host communities, whilst also mitigating and addressing tensions between the Rohingya and local communities generated by HLP disputes. This objective will be achieved through the increased capacity of refugees and host communities to exercise/claim their identity and HLP rights and improved access to and use of collaborative dispute resolution mechanisms. NRC will provide legal counselling and assistance based on individual needs to enable target beneficiaries to overcome legal, procedural, and documentation challenges, including referral to specialized case management actors as it may be required; combined with information dissemination and awareness-raising initiatives to empower target beneficiaries to claim their rights and access available justice mechanisms. Improvement of the relationships between refugees and host communities, and within the Rohingya community itself, will be achieved through the local leaders` capacity building in HLP dispute resolution. Key staff, volunteers, and other stakeholders, including target communities whenever possible, will be involved to identify existing and emerging threats to safety, dignity, and rights faced by different sex and age groups among the refugee and the host populations. Special attention will be paid to threats and vulnerabilities generated or exacerbated by COVID-19 and the associated containment measures. This information will be analyzed and used for evidence-based advocacy and will also be shared externally with other protection actors and stakeholders.

Le présent projet cherche à améliorer la protection et autonomisation des femmes affectées par les conflits à travers la prévention et la réponse intégrée assurant aux survivants de VBG l’appui psychosocial, matériel et économique (selon les besoins). Les femmes, les filles, les hommes, les garçons victimes de VBG, fréquentent les services de prise en charge psychosociale, médicale et légale et y reçoivent un soutien adéquat, tandis que les mécanismes de prévention des VBG sont renforcés.
