project_name: Soutien Psychosocial des déplacés et autochtones dans les régions de Sahel, l’Est et le Centre-Est.
project_objective:
Action contre la Faim prévoit de reconduire son intervention en santé mentale et soutien psychosocial pour les populations affectées (DPI & population hôtes) par la détresse psychologique due à la crise humanitaire dans les régions du Sahel, de l'Est et de Centre-Est. 
Prise en charge trauma : l’assistance sera focalisée sur les troubles de stress post-traumatiques, de la dépression et les troubles anxieux aussi bien pour les enfants que les adultes (les protocoles sont spécifiques selon la cible soit les enfants ou les adultes). Il s’agira notamment d’animer des séances de psychoéducation pour la normalisation des symptômes de stress post traumatique et identifier des personnes en détresse pour leur admission au programme de prise en charge. Ces services seront offerts dans la communauté pour faciliter l’accès aux services et mieux garantir la confidentialité des bénéficiaires. L’intervention sera basée sur le protocoles trauma de ACF. L’équipe des psychologues et des travailleurs psychosociaux suivront la structuration des protocoles de ACF pour accompagner les bénéficiaires lors des séances thérapeutiques. Des échelles d’évaluation psychométriques permettront le suivi de l’amélioration du bien-être des bénéficiaires.  

Sensibilisation communautaire : les sessions de sensibilisations seront animées au sein de la communauté sur la thématique de la santé mentale pour promouvoir la compréhension sur ce que c’est que le service de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial et comment avoir accès à ce service. Cette intervention vise à édifier la communauté sur les besoins en santé mentale et atténuer la stigmatisation dont sont victimes les personnes en détresse psychologique.

Psychoéducation : le service de psychoéducation sera offert au niveau communautaire et ouvert à toute la communauté pour partager les symptômes de la détresse psychologique qui se développent suite à un choc émotionnel. En plus de la normalisation de ces symptômes chez les hommes, femmes et enfants, c’est aussi un cadre d’identification des personnes en besoin de soutien psychologique et ou psychosocial spécifique.  

Formation soutien psychosocial : les personnes clés de la communauté seront formés en compétences de Premiers Secours Psychologiques. Pour renforcer durablement les savoir-être et savoir-faire afin de pouvoir apporter un premier support aux personnes vulnérables, identifier les personnes qui nécessitent une prise en charge spécifique et les référer vers les services de soins adéquats. 
ACF a participé à l’élaboration du manuel de l’OMS « Les Premiers Secours Psychologiques : guide pour les acteurs de terrain » qui est donc le document de référence pour la réalisation de cette activité.

project_name: Protection and Assistance to Persons of Concern
project_objective:
UNHCR will provide protection and seek solutions for IDPs and IDP-returnees, while working with partners at inter-agency level for provision of additional support, as follows:
-	IDP response will be characterized by enhanced protection monitoring (at community and household levels) and analysis, support to community-based protection networks and community reconciliation committees, tangible support to persons with specific needs (e.g. legal aid, civil documentation, or referral to psycho-social support, or cash-based interventions), youth programming, quick impact community support projects in IDP hosting and returnee receiving areas, and will contribute to durable solutions profiling and planning.
-	Coordination leadership of the Protection Sector will be reinforced, through working with partners and authorities to bolster preparedness including early warning, as well as protection assessment, analysis and response capacities. 
-	The Centrality of Protection will be championed within the UN/HCT, including through UNHCR serving as secretariat for the HCT Protection Task Force (HCT PTF), which oversees the implementation of the HCT Protection Strategy. UNHCR will work with the HCT PTF, and any new protection coordination forums established under UNITAMS, on advocacy related to protection of civilians, peacebuilding and durable solutions, particularly during the UNAMID drawdown and transition to an integrated mission. UNHCR will also bolster its advocacy with GoS on ensuring that laws and policies conform with international standards, and will support implementation of GoS’ National Plan on Protection of Civilians, at national and state-levels. These advocacy efforts will be buttressed by analysis of protection needs, threats and trends. 
-	The UNHCR/UNDP co-led Durable Solutions Working Group will prioritize the collection of relevant data to inform the inter-agency and governmental drive toward durable solutions, complemented by monitoring of returns by UNHCR to ensure they adhere to minimum standards of voluntariness, safety and dignity.  
-	UNHCR will strengthen the integration of PSEA actions, and maintain its active contributions to the RC/HC’s PSEA Network, and actively contribute to Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) approaches through co-leadership of the newly established AAP/Community Engagement WG under the ISCG.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and NFIs Support to Persons of Concern
project_objective:
There is inadequate available shelter to provide temporary as well as long-term shelter solutions for IDPs and host community. Hence, in preparation for any influx situation, it is critical for UNHCR to have an adequate stock of emergency shelter kits as well as non-food items (NFI)  prepositioned to intervene in any emergency while at the same time meeting the shelter needs of persons of concern already present in Sudan.

UNHCR will continue to provide emergency shelter materials and non-food items (NFI) to people who are newly displaced as a result of conflict or natural disaster. In situations of protracted displacement faced with natural disaster such as food or conflict situation, UNHCR will provide transitional shelter or durable shelter trough cash or in kind materials according to market assessments exploring direct cash or vouchers according to what is more economically efficient for the locality and distribution. The overall objective is to improve the shelter conditions of the POC by providing them trainings on build back better and shelter upgrades to be more resilient to natural hazards like floods or fire and reduce the risk of mayor loss of basic household items and shelter destruction. UNHCR will also support returnees and protected IDPs living in substandard shelters to improve their shelter conditions with the provision of shelter upgrades/repair activities and provision of durable shelter.

project_name: Emergency Health Response for Vulnerable Communities in Sudan
project_objective: The main drivers of the humanitarian health crisis in Sudan include, but not limited to, armed conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks, and floods. Three groups of epidemics dominated the disease outbreak in Sudan for the last decades: water and sanitation related, vector-borne and vaccine preventable. The humanitarian health response project focuses on addressing major risk factors and providing free-of-charge essential and life-saving health services to vulnerable populations affected by natural and manmade disasters at community, primary and secondary level of health care delivery points strengthening the locality and community level structures. In so doing, WHO’s preparedness and response to health emergencies will be consistent with the national health sector and health cluster strategies and adheres to national and international standards. The WHO in Sudan has well-established country office and 12 field offices located across Sudan. Technical and operational support will be provided by the WHO to strengthen the SMOHs coordination and emergency response teams up to community. The collection, centralization, analysis and dissemination of essential health data disaggregated by sex and age-groups will be maintained and strengthen by WHO field teams jointly with all partners. The WHO procure and distribute free of charge medicines, medical supplies and laboratory reagents to support the NGOs and SMOH in dealing with humanitarian case load at all levels. Training of health workers on topics directly related to prevailing humanitarian situations such as on surveillance and case management and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) will be provided based on the needs assessed. The project supports small repair and rehabilitation of damaged health facilities and supporting operational costs for humanitarian health services as necessary. The project supports community mobilization to promote healthy behavior. Besides, the project adopts an integrated approach that facilitates access to health services to all age groups, male and female with their specific health needs adapted to the local cultural customs, including advocacy and synergic linkages with ongoing recovery-development interventions (GBV, FGM, Protection, FSL, WASH, Nutrition, NFI, and Education). Optimal capacity for early notification, investigation, confirmation and immediate response to public health threats (outbreaks) is another priority contributing to the health security of targeted groups and beyond. This is achieved through technical and operational support for EWARS, epidemic alert investigation and response operations by supporting the RRTs; supporting response vaccination campaigns and strengthening the routine immunization; providing laboratory reagents and medicines to fill in the gaps during eventual outbreaks. The project targeted 5.6 million people residing in 107 localities with severity ranking level of 4 and 5 for humanitarian health response. The activities related to outbreak control are not restricted only to the 107 targeted localities, the WHO will intervene wherever the needs arise under its mandate for health security and protection of health. COVID-19 community transmission is likely to continue in all states of Sudan in 2021 stressing the vulnerable populations and their access to health care. As of its mandate, WHO has integrated in this proposal interventions to contain the outbreak and to support adequate health services for the target population. This includes among others infection prevention and control, isolation center support, scale up of access to testing also in remote areas and outbreak alert investigations. These interventions are cost intensive and contribute to a large extend to the over-proportional increase of the requested budget.

project_name: Improved access to safe water and vector control activities for the vulnerable, nutritionally affected and underserved population in Sudan
project_objective:
The situation in Sudan is complex with a combination of protracted emergencies, political instability, and economic crisis. All populations in Sudan are at high risk of two or more vector-borne diseases and the emergence of mosquito-borne arboviral diseases in many states caused thousands of cases and deaths. In 2020, malaria continued to be the leading cause of morbidities and mortalities, representing an average of 15 – 20% from total consultations. In particular, the Anopheles stephensi spread and invasion is a growing public health concern in Sudan as it risks increasing the transmission of Malaria. With this project, WHO aims to reduce the transmission and the burden of arbo-viral diseases among the vulnerable populations through scale up of vector surveillance, support to chemical and physical vector control measures by procurement and supplies as much as operational costs, capacity building and support to community based vector control measures. Around one-third of the population in Sudan still practices open defecation, only 38.54% have access to improved sanitation. There is a huge gap for the technical expertise due to the high turnover of the staff resulting from the administrative changes and continuous exemption of MoH staff, and migration of trained staff to other countries. Most health facilities do not have strong WASH systems, with reported waste being mixed up with general waste and disposed of at a landfill or near to health facilities. The WHO, MOH, will implement water quality activities and WASH partners at the state and locality level with sustained support from WHO.  WHO will continue the successful 2020 approach in strengthening the water quality system at localities levels to promote efficiency.  WHO will continue to support identified vulnerable families in cholera hot spots to ensure water quality and safety at the household level and distribute mini water filtration units, whilst UNICEF and other WASH partners will distribute WASH supplies. . The overall project including integrated vector control and WASH interventions is targeting 2.4 million people for a total project budget of 9,565,000 USD.
WHO will ensure the ease of access to the targeted population, without any constraints such as discrimination, or any other restraints. WHO will apply the standard measures for the containment of vector control remedies to ensure safety and dignity and avoid causing harm. WHO through its capacity building program is delivering key messages on increasing community ownership and leadership to ensure efficiency and sustainability of the project. The team structure is well aligned and linked to community leaders, and the communication tree established for the work will facilitate receiving community complaints, with the intended sequence to the higher level ensuring privacy. This timely feedback is aiming to inform the community on the deficiencies, their impact on health, and the responsible body for undertaking corrective measures. 
This project is targeting 2.4 million people. The total project budget is 9,565,000 USD. Vector transmitted arbo-viral diseases and unsafe access to drinking water are important factors contributing to the high disease -burden among vulnerable populations. With the proposed project and budget, WHO aims to ensure that early action can be assured in rainy season and high transmission period and aims to scale up interventions. As of its mandate, WHO will address the most urgent gaps in water quality assurance and vector control due to the limited capacity of the FMOH to deliver the required interventions for vulnerable populations.

project_name: Renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et de plaidoyer pour la protection humanitaire et l’assistance aux populations les plus vulnérables au Mali.
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire demeure complexe et instable, principalement en raison des conflits armés et intercommunautaires dans les régions du Centre et du Nord. Le retard dans la mise en œuvre de l’Accord pour la paix et la réconciliation au Mali paraphé en juin 2015 et dans le processus de désarmement, démobilisation, réintégration (DDR) contribuent à la persistance de l’instabilité sécuritaire dans les régions de Kidal, Gao, Ménaka, Tombouctou, Ségou et Mopti ainsi qu’à l’aggravation des tensions sociales. A cause des activités des acteurs armés, l’accès humanitaire demeure difficile mais fluide dans certaines zones. 

La présence limitée de l’État et l’insécurité dans ces régions demeurent l’un des facteurs clés obligeant les civils à fuir leurs communautés. La grogne sociale qui a conduit au changement de régime en août 2021 prouve l’inaccessibilité des populations maliennes aux services sociaux de base et l’aggravation de leur vulnérabilité à laquelle s’ajoute le poids de la pandémie de COVID-19. 

Le nombre de Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) a atteint la barre des 311,191 en octobre 2020 en comparaison aux 199 385 enregistrés à la même période en 2019 et 80 302 en 2018.  Les risques et les besoins de protection des populations fuyant leurs communautés sous la pression de la violence armée ou des tensions intercommunautaires, sont élevés. De graves abus et attaques contre les personnes, les biens et les services (écoles, centres de santé) sont régulièrement signalées alors que l’accès aux services appropriés est compromis. Comme les déplacements internes sont de longue durée, les risques de protection et les violations des droits fondamentaux augmentent, en particulier pour les plus vulnérables (femmes, enfants, personnes âgées, personnes handicapées ou malades). De graves conséquences humanitaires ont donc été notées, telles que des taux élevés d’insécurité alimentaire et de malnutrition ainsi que le faible accès aux services sociaux de base.

Avec près de 4,7 millions de personnes affectées par l’insécurité alimentaire, dont 2,3 millions personnes avec des besoins d’assistance d’urgence, l’année 2020 a été, selon les résultats des exercices du Cadre Harmonisé (CH), l’année la plus fortement marquée par l’insécurité alimentaire depuis 2014. Les conséquences de cette détérioration resteront perceptibles sur le niveau de vie de populations en 2021. Les capacités de réponse existantes au Mali représentent environ 200 organisations humanitaires, acteurs du développement ainsi que des forces militaires (MINUSMA, Forces maliennes de défense et de sécurité, Barkhane, Mission européenne de formation, G5 Sahel). Le contexte susmentionné exigera une coordination efficace et la présence d’OCHA demeure très importante. OCHA maintiendra sa présence à Bamako, Mopti, Tombouctou et Gao ainsi que son antenne de Ségou tout en couvrant à distance les régions de Taoudénit, Ménaka, Kidal et les régions du sud.

Sept clusters actifs (Éducation, Sécurité alimentaire, Santé, Nutrition, Protection, Abris/BNA et WASH), des sous-clusters et des groupes de travail spécialisés (Accès, CMCoord, Redevabilité, Genre et Cash) sont en place au niveau national et local. Le Bureau d’OCHA au Mali continuera ainsi à jouer un rôle central dans la mobilisation, la coordination et le soutien des acteurs humanitaires dans les domaines de la coordination, la gestion de l’information, le financement humanitaire et le plaidoyer avec un accent accru dans le domaine de Civilo-Militaire et d’accès humanitaire afin de garantir la conservation et la consolidation de l’espace humanitaire. project_name: Rehabilitation of key agricultural assets and cash assistance to improve food security in the South of Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger (AAH), together with the Union of Agricultural Work Committees (UAWC) and Gaza Urban & pre-Urban Agricultural Platform (GUPAP) propose to provide immediate relief responses to support vulnerable households across 3 governorates of the Gaza Strip (Rafah, Khan Younis and Middle Area) to cope with shocks that affect their food security status; enable to protect their livelihoods, increase productivity and improve their food and nutrition security status. This includes households who base their income on agriculture activities and cannot maintain or rehabilitate their key productive assets, and farmers who are at risk of food insecurity, whose livelihoods were affected by the current situation, with family members unable to work (with physical or mental disabilities, medical cases), with a high number of dependents and do not have a stable source of income. This project has been developed to contribute to the achievement of the three Food Security Sector (FSS) objectives of the oPt HRP: (O1) Livelihoods of vulnerable households are protected, and their resilience, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced, (O2) Households suffering from limited of access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs, and (O3) FSS activities, including advocacy and awareness, are planned and implemented in a coordinated manner, and partnership with key national ministries is strengthened, and to align with strategic priorities of the Ministry of Agriculture, and has been coordinated with similar interventions within the target area. Firstly, AAH will focus on rehabilitating productive 
assets, such as damaged greenhouses, water ponds and installation of new solar energy units for irrigation pumps, partially done using the cash for work (CfW) modality and with the support of UAWC. This will enable 558 households to increase their resilience to man-made, covid-19 restriction measures and natural shocks, make use of the available natural resources for their agricultural activities and reduce the costs associated while gaining an income for those employed in cash for work activities. Secondly, 60 female headed households will be supported by AAH through enhancing existing home gardening and increased knowledge of home garden techniques. This will contribute to food security at household level while increasing the dignity of the women targeted. Finally, GUPAP and AAH will organize awareness sessions at community level to include food security issues, including barriers faced by small producers and women producers to promote local production. These will result in advocacy materials being developed for national and international audiences. The project will reduce the food insecurity and improve livelihoods of an estimated 3,399 people (745 men, 949 women, 805 boys, and 900 girls) and provide them with the means to show resilience in the face of these challenges. Small scale farmers,  who have accumulated levels of debts and decreased income from recent restrictions and inability to restore productive assets will be prioritized in the first activity. Female headed households with high dependency ratio with existing home-gardens will be prioritized to be supported further in improving their food security (activity 2). Accountability and participation will be ensured through a detailed MEAL framework specifically developed to ensure that beneficiary selection is conducted in a transparent and accountable manner and through applying AAH’s thorough Feedback and Complaint Mechanism to guarantee the inclusion of communities and individuals’ suggestions into the project. AAH seeks to achieve equal and impartial access to vulnerable populations, aiming for all community members to be involved and consulted as much as possible including through community consultations to further achieve beneficiaries’ empowerment and sustainability beyond the project’s lifetime

project_name: Improved Child Protection and MHPSS service provision for Women, Children and families affected by conflict-related violence and GBV in Area C of the West Bank
project_objective:
This project aims to strengthen the protection and social safety net and resilience of children, caregivers, and communities in the face of chronic exposure to conflict-related violence by: (1) providing community-based and specialized child protection case management and psychosocial and mental health services to children and their families, (2) providing specialized package of services to GBV survivors and girls and women at risk, (3) surge emergency capacity of community-based organizations on psychosocial and child protection interventions and specialized MHPSS services, including online modalities, and (4) addressing IHL and IHRL violations through advocacy initiatives targeting all duty bearers and based on documentation of grave violations. This project targets Palestinian children directly and indirectly exposed to violence and abuse related to the Israeli Occupation, including settler violence, unsafe school environments, home and school demolitions, and displacement. War Child Holland (WCH) and partners the Psycho-Social Counseling Center for Women (PSCCW) and the Palestinian Counselling Center (PCC) will be targeting acutely affected children and families living in the most marginalized areas of Area C in the West Bank with specific focus on the Northern West Bank and Bedouin Communities located in the below:
- Area C of Nablus governorate covering Duma, Qaryout, Beita communities, 
- Area C of Salfit Governorate Bourqin, Rafat, Hares, Kfil Hares and Kufer Al Deek 
- Area C and Bedouin communities of the Jordan Valley under Tubas and Jericho governorates, including Kardalla, Bardalla, Ain El Beida, Al Aqaba, Al Jiftlik with special focus on Al Musaffah and Ash-Shuneh, Gharb al Muthallath, Abu al Ajaj, Fasayel including Fasayil al Wasta and Fasayil Al Fauqa, Marj Naji, Zbeidat, and Al Auja with focus on Ras Ein al ‘Auja. Outreach CP and PSS activities will be also be provided to Khirbet Tell el Himma, Ein al Hilwa – Um al Jmal,Hammammat al Males- Al Burj, Hammamat al Males- Al Meiteh, An Nuwei’ma al Fauqa Bedouin Communities.
- Area C and Bedouin communities of Bethlehem Governorate, Beit Skaria Job Al Theb, Al Taquo including the surrounding Bedouin communities like Rashaydeh and Kisan, Al Maasara, Al Walajeh 
- Area C and Bedouin communities of Hebron: Marginalized communities of Masafer Yatta
The project partners will target 23 CBOs distributed among the six above-mentioned Governorates. The areas were selected based on previous experience of consortium partners in those areas and needs identified as well as on the OCHA Vulnerability Profile of Palestinian Communities in Area C. 
In addition to specific Protection interventions, War Child and partners will mainstream PSEA and Protection in Covid19 response efforts, in line with local infection and prevention control (IPC) measures and global guidance notes produced by the Alliance for Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (e.g. CPHA Note on the Protection of Children during Covid19 outbreak and annexes), and IASC PSEA during COVID-19 Response Technical Guidance Note.

project_name: Provision of school meals to children in formal and non-formal education in Syria
project_objective:
The school meals programme aims to restore and stabilize access to education and to enhance health and nutrition status of children in targeted areas particularly areas hosting large number of affected populations, IDPs and returnees with low food security and education indicators. By encouraging regular attendance and enrollment, the programme contributes to providing protection to children from reverting to negative coping mechanism such as child labor and child marriage in addition to the education, health, and nutrition benefits. The programme meets the first objective of the education sector “Increased safe and equitable availability and access to in-person and home-based formal and non-formal education for crisis-affected children and youth”
The School meals activity includes: 
-	In kind food distribution including daily distribution of fresh meals or  fortified snacks  to  children in formal education pre and  primary schools during school days and to children enrolled in non-formal education, including children in Self learning centres in North East Syria camps. In addition the programme provides support to children coming from crossline and cross-border locations to sit for National exams.
-	Provision of electronic vouchers to students who were out of school and have returned to education and are currently enrolled in curriculum B or nonformal education   programmes. The provision of the electronic voucher is conditional to student’s attendance rate of 80%.  

School meals activities will target boys and girls aged 5-15 years in formal and non-formal settings, including children with disability, who are attending the targeted schools and learning centres.  The Programme is implemented in coordination with the Ministry of Education and other partners of the education sector in Syria including UN agencies and National NGOs. Considering the high needs and limited resources, the project will focus on areas with acute and immediate needs of humanitarian assistance. Targeted sub-districts will be prioritized based on food and education severity of 3 and above.  In case of lower funding, priority will be given to locations where severity of food security and education of more than 4 and to newly accessible areas where education sector is picking up its activities. 
The Activities are aligned with the timeframe of the school year, thus, beginning in September of the current year and ending  by May of the next. Distribution of snacks may continue in the summer to support last chance camps.

project_name: Providing Comprehensive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Assistance to Crisis Affected Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
This project aims to provide humanitarian WASH assistance to 450,000 beneficiaries (148,500 women, 112,500 men, 94,500 girls, 94,500 boys - 12% of whom are estimated to be either elderly or disabled) to mitigate the suffering of populations affected by natural or manmade disasters and reflect all 3 objectives of the 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan. 

Under Objective 1, IOM will aim to assist crisis-affected population (approximately 200,000 individuals) by ensuring dignified and equitable access to basic WASH services. Emergency assistance will be provided to people newly displaced by conflict or natural disasters through the implementation of early recovery approaches where possible, connecting the need for short-term emergency interventions with long-term solutions by working directly with local communities to facilitate ownership and accountability. The objective is to not only focus on WASH emergency interventions but gradually contribute to socioeconomic inclusion of forcibly displaced populations and returnees by directly increasing access to basic services for the displaced and host communities and indirectly increasing employment opportunities.

Under Objective 2, IOM seeks to improve and sustain access to safe water in target communities (approximately 150,000 individuals), including returnees, especially in Blue Nile, east Sudan, Abyei, North Darfur and South Darfur as these communities primarily rely on agriculture and livestock, therefore water is critical to their livelihoods. 

Under Objective 3, improving and sustaining access to safe water and sanitation facilities and hygiene messages will address malnutrition related risks and increase community resilience to disease outbreaks for approximately 50,000 individuals. IOM will consider emergency water provision, access to proper sanitation facilities and hygiene campaigns; coupled with the establishment and rehabilitation of water points. This will include environmental impact mitigation such as the provision of solar technology to power water points and monitoring ground water to moderate depletion levels. Exit strategies will be developed to alleviate aid dependency in protracted emergencies by strengthening self-reliance and facilitating community solutions in a more holistic approach.

project_name: Preventing and mitigating the spread of COVID-19 through an integrated WASH and Mental Health Psychosocial approach in Benghazi
project_objective: AAH has started a 5-month project in Benghazi funded by SDC, which aims at reducing the impact of Covid-19 and its psychological and psychosocial consequences, through strengthening the capacities of community members and frontline workers to face the psychological and psychosocial distress related to COVID-19 risk and spread, and to adopt appropriate behaviours to avoid contamination from COVID-19. Through this project, AAH is targeting 3000 individuals, including 50 Health workers/CBO workers and 2000 vulnerable people in need of psychosocial and psychological services. At this early stage of its mission in Libya AAH has opted for a mental health project integrated with RCCE and IPC activities, not yet including a purely health approach. This first project will allow AAH to better understand and analyse the health context for a better future response.

project_name: Comprehensive Shelter and NFI Support for Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
IOM will continue to support refugees and host communities aiming at reaching 96,684 households living in 18 camps of IOM’s Area of Responsibility (AoR) and 11,936 host community households with Shelter, NFI and LPG interventions.   
IOM will continue providing emergency shelter, distribution of tie-down kits, response to cyclone with the emergency shelter kits for cyclone response in all 18 camps directly, through pipeline partners and in coordination with other shelter partners. IOM will also aim at having dedicated personnel for 6 catchment areas where IOM is in charge to ensure the coordination to respond the needs.  Support will be also provided to those at home care/quarantine with NFI package and LPG delivery.
IOM will implement TSA2 programme which includes trainings on DRR and construction techniques and distribution of shelter materials, construction of 2-storey steel frame shelters, mid-term shelters (where/when it allowed), community shelter repair and maintenance, provision of NFIs through voucher approach, household solar lights and distribution of LPG refills and stoves. LPG activities will be implemented in host communities in addition to camps to improve environmental management.  IOM will ensure involvement of women, older persons, persons with disability in our activities so that they can take part in the appropriate activities. 
In all Shelter/NFI and LPG activities, IOM will ensure protection mainstreaming in line with IOM’s Gender-Based Violence in Crisis Framework and its concurrent Action. Community feedback mechanisms with complaints desks, community mobilizations, regular project monitoring and post distribution monitoring will be deployed to ensure the complaints and feedback received are responded and changes are incorporated for the on-going future programming. All data collected during assessment and monitoring activities will be sex and age desegregated and particular information regarding vulnerabilities such as female and child headed households, persons with disabilities will be collected to provide additional support during the implementation.

project_name: Health & Nutrition assistance for IDPs, returnees, PINs and host community in East Darfur and South Darfur
project_objective:
Health: The integrated primary health care interventions will be provided with key objective to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with disease among the children under five years, men, women, adolescent boys and girls, women of child bearing age, elderly men and women and people with disability. ARC has been implementing a comprehensive integrated primary health care life-saving intervention supporting 24 primary health care centers in South and East Darfur. Under this project, ARC will continue to provide basic primary health care services; treatment and diagnosis of communicable and non-communicable diseases, reproductive health, support of referrals for both medical and obstetric emergencies to tertiary level, emergency preparedness and response, disease prevention activities through health promotion activities by community volunteers, routine immunization, provision of essential drugs, medical and non-medical supplies, clinical management of rape to gender-based violence survivors and provision of Psychological First Aid (PFA) services. ARC will also strengthen community-based approaches to promote positive health-seeking behaviors, recognition of illnesses, and care-seeking practices through trained community structures, community relief development committees and health, nutrition and WASH volunteers network. The project will strengthen institutional capacity through on-the-job training and mentoring to implement sustainable and affordable health interventions that meet the needs of men, women, boys, girls, children, elderly, and persons with special needs.

Nutrition: The nutrition project is designed to meet the needs of nutrition services for internally displaced people and vulnerable host community in Belil, Alsalam, Gereida and Dimso localities in South and Assalaya, Adilla, Abukarinka, Elferdous and Yassin in East Darfur states. ARC will provide nutrition services integrated to the primary health care facilities supported by ARC in South and East Darfur states. The nutrition activities will be implemented in an integrated approach with health and WASH. The goal of this project is to contribute to the reduction in nutrition-related mortality and morbidity, and improve access to high-quality multi-sectoral life-saving nutrition interventions for children under five and pregnant and lactating women who are below the emergency threshold. The project will support 23 Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs, 23 Outpatient Therapeutic Programs and 3 Stabilization Centers (SC) including referrals to secondary health care and provision of essential drugs. ARC will follow CMAM approach to implement the intended interventions. ARC will use the mother support group strategy to promote appropriate Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and Social Behavior Change and Communication (SBCC) among the target communities. ARC will also enhance the technical capacity of ministry of health staff through conducting training on CMAM package, IYCF and training on monitoring and reporting of the nutrition activities. All activities will be implemented in close collaboration with local institutions/ line ministries and communities such Community Relief and Development Committees (CRDC) to ensure sustainability and active community participation.

project_name: WASH & S/NFI assistance for IDPs, returnees, PINs and host community
project_objective:
This project aims to achieve sustainable improvement in access to quality water supply, sanitation condition, hygiene practices and distribution of essential life-saving NFI and emergency shelters among IDPs and host communities in East and South Darfur states as well Khartoum State, the project will focus on subsectors of water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, environmental health and NFI and emergency shelters. In order to improve the water supplies in targeted area of operation, innovative and environmentally friendly technologies will be used namely water provision through installation of hybrid powered solar pumping systems and construction of roofing hafir, monitoring water quality on daily and bi-weekly bases through chlorination and bacteria tests to ensure safe drinking water is provided.  Community based operation and maintenance approach will be applied to ensure long lasting water service provision. Furthermore, WASH services and facilities will be given consideration COVID-19 mitigation measures ranging from increasing handwashing facilities in high risk public places and communicating culturally appropriate messages to foster behavior changes to cash-based interventions and in-kind distribution of hygiene supplies, ARC is strengthening and adapting WASH services in camps and host community settings, healthcare facilities, and schools.
ARC will continue to provide access to safe water in communities suffering from malnutrition above emergency thresholds for IDPs as well as the vulnerable host communities impacted by the presence of IDPs through context specific technologies such as surface water treatment systems and sustainable Point of Use water treatment solutions appropriate for a highly mobile population. ARC will provide means for safe excreta disposal through the installation of gender appropriate sanitation facilities and will conduct hygiene promotion activities to support effective behavior change. For ES/NFI intervention this project seeks to provide of timely shelter solutions and NFI assistance to people affected by crisis to reduce mortality and morbidity, mitigate health threats, and improve living conditions and support the transition to recovery by improving vulnerable people’s access to shelter solutions.

project_name: Protection assistance for IDPs and host community
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in Darfur region of Sudan remains unresolved since it broke out in 2003 up to now .More than 1.97 million  internally displaced persons are residing in about 55 camps  and other non-camp settlements across Darfur.ARC protection department is proposing an intervention focused on strengthening the protection of 550000 IDPs, host communities and returnees affected by conflict and displacement through improved and sustainable access to basic protection services and durable solution. The proposed intervention will focus and provides community-based protection services to the IDPs and host communities in South and East Darfur states of Sudan. This proposed 12-month project will enable ARC to provide a full package of preventive and direct protection services to the target communities (the IDPs and host communities) both state (ED and SD). 

The overall objective of the project will be to promote and support community self-management, durable solutions, support for persons with specific needs and highly vulnerable households and conduct protection and returnee monitoring amongst IDPs and host communities and other relevant communities to identify their basic needs.
ARC will support the strengthening of community structures (CBPNs, youth and women groups) and facilitate the development and implementation of community-based protection action plans for durable solutions and support to vulnerable community members. Community structures will be established and strengthened through capacity building and supporting to promote equal and meaningful access to these facilities, monitor protection concerns and develop a community-based response. ARC will contribute to the participation and information of displaced and returnee communities in the planning and implementation of durable solutions, through the profiling of IDP and returnees and promoting access of IDPs and returnees to information required to enable them to take informed decisions. Also ARC will support Community members need to be empowered through capacity building initiatives to work with Persons with Specific Needs (PSN), conduct protection monitoring and reporting as well as their own advocacy and assistance delivery monitoring.

project_name: Strengthening Child Protection Services including Explosive Ordinance Risk Education and Prevention, Empowerment and Response GBV for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria.
project_objective:
UNICEF CP will be in line with the CP AOR strategy for Syria as well as with the “No Lost Generation” framework, targeting 161 high severity (3 to 5) and 96 low severity scale sub-districts. The geographical prioritization based on communities
 in sub-districts with medium to high severity and large number of people in need; UNICEF’s Child Protection strategy for Syria in 2021 will follow its 3 pillar structure in its prevention and response interventions:1) Improving the quality of community-based
 CP through behaviour change and awareness raising on specific child protection risks, and structured psychosocial support and parenting programmes for boys and girls and parents/caregivers. 2) Expand the reach & improve the quality of child protection specialized
 services for survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect & abuse through case management to address those critical needs & restore normalcy and wellbeing  to the lives of children 3) Sustained capacity building of frontline CP responders to build  sustainable
 CP workforce ensuring minimum standards.UNICEF shall contribute to expanding the availability of quality CP services for girls, boys, women & men in targeted locations, focusing on children & women, internally displaced, host communities & refugees in camps/
 settlements where possible  as well as adapted delivery modalities for CP during the COVID-19 pandemic.Based on 2021 HNO MSNA, approximately one in two people are at risk from explosive contamination, and a third of the communities are potentially contaminated
 by explosive ordnance. Contamination severely impacts lives, livelihoods and amplifies social and economic crisis aggravated by  COVID-19 pandemic.Based on Joint Mine Action and CP inter-sectorial analysis nearly 1 out of 4 recorded victims is a child. RE
 messages shall be provided to children and adults through both humanitarian & public service using both static facilities & mobile teams as well as adapted delivery modalities during COVID19 pandemic to reach affected populations. UNICEF will build capacity
 of RE partners to provide quality EORE -age, gender & disability appropriate, also provide child victims assistance to mitigate negative impacts on their life & wellbeing.UNICEF in addressing Gender Based Violence (GBV) shall adopt holistic approach in GBV
 services, including prevention, empowerment and response, to affected population through Community Centres, Women and Girls Safe Spaces and Child Friendly Centres.Adapted delivery modalities will be utilized during the COVID-19 pandemic. Support will be provided
 for the PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries & build capacity humanitarian actors to address needs of the population in efficient, transparent and accountable manner. The programme shall be implemented in coordination with other actors (Child Protection,
 GBV and Mine Action) strategies & results framework.As part of Accountability to Affected Population (AAP), protection needs assessment through MSNA are conducted through engagement with the affected population at household level and with the key informant
 at community level to accurately capture the conditions affecting the affected populations. UNICEF, together with the partners, will ensure that  AAP agenda will be included throughout the programme cycle by monitoring and consultation with beneficiaries on
 the quality of service.


The project will continue to advocate for and improve collaboration with other sectors to address key CP concerns e.g. child labour with ERL and violence in schools with education.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination in Libya
project_objective:
OCHA will in 2021 continue to support the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC) and the
Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in coordinating the humanitarian response to meet the
(protection) needs of the most vulnerable people affected by the conflict / crisis/ impact of COVID-19 in Libya. Through Inter-Sector and Area-Based coordination, OCHA will provide mechanisms and
support to ensure that the interventions of humanitarian organisations are well coordinated and based on robust and timely evidence. OCHA will further facilitate and advocate for humanitarian access, the respect of humanitarian principles and ensure that the protection of people in need is effective.

project_objective:

-Appui à la réhabilitation nutritionnelle des enfants de 6-59 mois, femmes enceintes et femmes allaitant un enfant de moins de 6 mois dans les zones à forte prévalence de malnutrition aiguë globale. 
-Promotion des pratiques d’hygiène, d’alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant durant les séances de dépistage et de prise en charge nutritionnelle.  
-Appui à la mise en œuvre d’une plateforme communautaire pour la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée par les ASC 
-Renforcement de capacité des acteurs sur la prise en charge de la nutrition aiguë modérée
-Appui à la fonctionnalité des systèmes de gestion de l’information sur la nutrition à travers le renforcement de capacité des acteurs du système de la santé sur l’utilisation de la plateforme DHIS2
Appui aux accompagnants des enfants hospitalisés en URENI : 
-Assistance alimentaire aux accompagnants des enfants admis dans les URENI et services de pédiatrie des Centre de Santé de Référence ou hôpitaux régionaux à travers la distribution de de coupons alimentaires 
-Appui à la mise en place des mesures de prévention contre l’épidémie de Covid-19  
Appui au renforcement de la gouvernance du secteur de la nutrition:
-Renforcer les capacités de la DGS/SDN, des DRS et des Districts sanitaires de santé sur les modalités de mise en œuvre du programme de prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée
-Fournir un appui à la DNS/DN, des DRS et des Districts sanitaires de santé pour le suivi et l’évaluation des programmes de prise en charge
-Fournir un appui à la DGS/SDN, des DRS et des districts sanitaires de santé pour la mise en place de mesures d’ajustement qui garantiront la continuité des programmes de prise en charge et limiteront la propagation de l’épidémie Covid-19.

La protection sociale étant l’ensemble des mesures préconisées pour assurer la prise en charge des risques sociaux de la population sera au 1er plan dans l’exécution de nos interventions. Ce qui serait pour nous une gamme d’actions protectrices en réponse à la vulnérabilité

project_name: Building Resilience and Strengthening Protection (BRSP) Project
project_objective:
This IOM Protection project aims to contribute towards the achievement of Strategic Objectives 1 and 3 of the Protection Cluster. SO2: Ensure safe, equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services to enable populations to meet their basic needs in locations of severity level 4 and 5 and S.O.3 requests to enable vulnerable people to recover from crisis, seek solutions to displacement, and build resilience to acute shocks and chronic stresses through targeted programming to support coping capacities and livelihoods in prioritized areas.

The project seeks to provide protection assistance to the most vulnerable focusing on IDPs, host communities and returnees in Warrap, Unity, Western Bahr El Ghazal, and Central Equatoria states. The project focus will be on continuing the current support to community-based protection, provision of access to justice, protection assistance to victims of trafficking, and housing, land, and property assistance. The components to be implemented at each project site will be based on assessments and community consultations in order to address specific needs. Aside from supporting the Protection Cluster Objectives, the project is also a part of IOM’s Protection Strategy. The counties to be targeted include in Warrap State: Twic, Tonj North, Tonj South; in Western Bahr el Ghazal State: Wau, Jur River; and in Unity State: Leer. These locations have been prioritized by the cluster and have also been confirmed by needs assessments.

Objective 2: CO 1: IOM will ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialized services through an integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas.

IOM Protection will specifically undertake to support vulnerable  girls, boys, women, men, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other persons with specific needs at risk of, or who have experienced violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect, including gender-based violence and are in hard-to- reach geographical areas, through the provision of specialized protection and multi-sectoral services by the following:

(a) Provision of protection assistance including targeted assistance to victims of trafficking, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through of case management services, access to justice for survivors of gender-based violence and other vulnerable persons as determined by joint needs assessments with other partners. This will be achieved through static as well as through mobile interventions integrated with GBV as well as with other sectors such as WASH and S-NFI.

(b) Awareness raising on protection, rights and entitlements, disability inclusion, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse including sensitization of community structures on protection risks and mitigation and working with community protection committees on referrals.

In regard to SO 3 IOM will facilitate conflict- and gender-sensitive access to safe housing, land, and property for women, men, girls, and boys, with a sufficient security of tenure. IOM will do this through:

(i) Provision of legal awareness raising including on Housing, Land, and Property rights and responsibilities;

(ii) Provision of legal counselling;

(iii) Legal capacity building to dispute resolution mechanisms at the community level; and 

(iv) Use of cash-based assistance to ensure individuals will not have rights denied due to lack of funds.

The project is intended to assist the beneficiaries to claim their rights and to build the capacity of the authorities to protect and provide access to rights of the affected populations.

Overall the project will target 28,925 individual beneficiaries, of these 15,665 will benefit from the HLP component of the project and 13,260 from the GP component of the project. The overall budget for this project is USD 867,750 - which averages 30USD/beneficiary.

project_name: Assisting conflict-affected boys, girls, and their families to meet their basic needs in eastern Ukraine (GCA and NGCA)
project_objective:
SCI will meet the most vulnerable families’ basic needs in GCA and NGCA by using a multi-sectorial approach and distributing coal, winter NFIs, hygiene NFIs and multi-purpose cash, based on the families most critical needs. Lifesaving activities are prioritised in areas affected by the conflict and COVID-19, especially in times of difficult economic situation aggravated by COVID-19 pandemic. Check Points remain limited for crossing for more than 6 months, and in addition to internal COVID-19 related restrictions people have no opportunity to cross the LoC to get access to their pensions and social benefits. The situation in GCA with zoning system (green, yellow, orange and red) remains tense and numbers are increasing day by day, posing an increased pressure on population, especially the ones living across the contact line with limited movement opportunities in case lockdown is activated. The intended aid will alleviate burden for vulnerable HHs with children.
SCI has been implementing similar activities for years with great success and at high levels of quality. SCI will target 14,700 beneficiaries in GCA (0-5km) and Donetsk NGCA, with a total budget of USD 1,500,000. SCI has been operating in Donetsk NGCA since 2015, having a strong team of professionals, and will be able to deliver the proposed activities in partnership with local organisations on time, on budget, with compliance and quality.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods interventions in Blue Nile, West and Central Darfur states, World Relief Sudan
project_objective:
World Relief Sudan (WRS) is currently providing integrated humanitarian emergency response, recovery and development programs in health, nutrition, education, protection, peace building, WASH and FSL activities funded bilateral and multilateral donors including SHF, OFDA, DFID, SIDA, UNICEF, WFP, MoFA of Netherlands and private donors.
This Food security and livelihoods (FSL) project is designed with the objective of saving lives and building resilience of the most vulnerable HHs and reducing acute food insecurity and malnutrition through ensuring availability of nutritious food to 88,854 HHs in nine localities in the three states including El Kurmuk, Geissan Baw localities of Blue Nile, El Geniena, Beida and Kreinik in West Darfur and Nirtiti, RoKero and Gollo of Central Darfur. In alignment with the FSL sector objectives, the project also focuses on two major areas. The first focus area is that ensuring conflict and other disaster affected people in the three states including IPDs, returnees, host communities and nomads receive timely, adequate and required assistance during and in the aftermath of a shock. The other focus area is improving availability and accessibility to sufficient, quality and nutritious food to individuals impacted by protracted crisis. To achieve these objectives, World Relief (WR) conducted a comprehensive assessment in Blue Nile. The assessment includes community level discussion, field visit, discussion with government line ministries, UN agenies, NGOs operating the area and review of various data. In West and Central Darfur WR conducted community based participatory planning and project plan has been prepared with active involvement of the community and activities are prioritized for implementation based on community priorities and triangulated with data from different sources. IDPs, returnees and extremely vulnerable host communities are the central focus of the project. Provision of agricultural inputs, improving livestock veterinary services & water schemes, income generating activities, various capacity buildings, saving and loan schemes, restocking, promotion of FFA activities and gender & environment are the main focus areas.
Even though women are heads for almost half of the households, they are often hindered by many traditional norms from making real progress which make it difficult for them to access new agricultural technologies as well as improved livelihood opportunities. This project will mainly target women in order to build their capacities thus allowing them to sufficiently increase their productivity beyond consumption. 

The organization recognizes the importance of the human rights of refugees, returnees, IDPs and especially the most vulnerable groups such as women, girls and minority groups. While implementing this project, the organization will make conscious and intentional efforts to avoid all situations that expose beneficiaries to risk, threat, violence and abuse of their rights.

All interventions will be done in partnership with government line ministries, community-based committees, local authorities, community leaders and beneficiaries themselves. As described further below, interventions are designed to meet immediate emergency needs of the beneficiaries mainly women, girls and children while employing approaches that increase community ownership and thus sustainability.

project_name: WR Sudan Integrated Health and Nutrition Response In West and Central Darfur, Khartoum and Blue Nile States
project_objective:
The World Relief Sudan (WRS) health and nutrition project planned to be implemented in five localities of central Darfur (Azum, Golo, Nertiti, Rokero & Umdukun), five localities of West Darfur (Geneina, Kerenik, Habila, Beida and Sirba), four localities of Khartoum ( Bahri, Karari, Khartoum and Jebel Awulia) and four localities of Blue Nile states (Demaine, Kurmuk, Bau, Rosaries). The project mainly focuses on improving vulnerable households’ access to sustainable health and nutrition services to reduce the morbidity and mortality attributable to poor access to health and nutrition services among, IDPs, returnees and conflict-affected people.  

WRS started its operational in Sudan since 2004, responding to the sever food insecurity and humanitarian crisis. WRS is currently providing interventions in health and nutrition, FSL, peace building, education protection, and WASH activities. The health and nutrition project of WRS aims to address the immediate needs of 634316 people (310,815 men, 323501 women, 348874 children, 63432 elderly, and 15857 people with disabilities) returnees, IDPs and vulnerable host communities. WRS conducted the SMART and KAP surveys in March 2019 using the standard tools and procedures with the objective to determine health, nutrition and WASH related knowledge, attitude and practices and to know the prevailing needs of children, women and adults, specifically on health & nutrition in the Jebel Maraa Localities. Furthermore WR conducted detail needs assessment in Khartoum and Blue Nile states to determine needs and priorities of the states. Furthermore, in 2020 World Relief conducted integrated and multi indicator survey in West and Central Darfur states. 

WRS’s Needs Assessment reveals poor access to health and nutrition services, low capacities of health and nutrition staff, disease outbreaks, high rates of malnutrition, and poor hygiene and sanitation situations. To address these challenges, WRS will provide life-saving interventions in the Health and nutrition sectors, which will be integrated with FSL, protection and WASH sectors that is ongoing in the in the proposed states using resources obtained from different donors. To increase community access to primary health care services, WRS plans to rehabilitate, equip and provide medical drugs to 38 health clinics. Services include providing outpatient services, medical consultations and treatments, expanded program of immunization (EPI) with routine immunization against all national target diseases, cold chain support, and antenatal and post-natal care with SMoH to provide overall operation and management of the health facilities proposed to be supported by this grant. In Addition, Mobile clinic services will be conducted, reaching out to populations who are unable to access the static facilities, thus ensuring that individuals afraid or unable to move to the static facilities are not denied assistance or services. 

Regarding nutrition sector, the primary focus is reducing and maintaining mortality level below the emergency threshold by implementing CMAM & IYCF activities in order to improving the nutritional status of vulnerable members of the communities especially children under five years of age and PLW. The project will be implemented by, identifying, screening and treating malnourished boys and girls under-five, pregnant & lactating women, and providing preventive nutrition services. The project will implement its nutrition program by supporting 63 (35 WD, 16 CD, 7 Khartoum, 5 Blue Nile) nutrition centers in the four states.  

All interventions will be done in partnership with government line ministries, community-based committees, local authorities, community leaders and beneficiaries themselves. As described further below, interventions are designed to meet immediate emergency needs of the beneficiaries mainly women, girls and children while employing approaches that increase community ownership and thus sustainability.

project_name: WASH Assistance for IDPs, Returnees and Host Community in Khartoum, Blue Nile, Central & West Darfur States in Sudan.
project_objective:
This project is planned to be implemented in 7 localities of Central Darfur (Zalinge, Azum, Golo, Nertiti, Rokero, Bendesi & Umdukun), & 6 in West Darfur (Genina, Kernik, Kulbus, Habila, Beida & Sirba), 6 in Blue Nile (Kurmuk, Geissan, Bau, Wad Almahi, Tadamon & Damazine), and 4 in Khartoum (Bahri, Khartoum, Um-Durman, & Jebel Awlia) targeting 294,760 crisis-affected people (66,144 women, 63,550 men, 84,183 girls, 80,882 boys). The project focuses on improving vulnerable households’ access to sustainable WASH services to reduce the morbidity and mortality attributable to poor water, hygiene and sanitary conditions among IDPs and conflict-affected people. These vulnerable residents are prioritized based on the most severe needs related to WASH borne epidemics, floods, food insecurity, undernutrition, COVID-19, and access to WASH services.
Firstly, this project aims to improve access to basic water services for crisis-affected populations. Under this objective, the interventions ensure drinking water from an improved source with a collection time of not more than 30 minutes roundtrip, including queuing. People targeted with basic water services will benefit from new installations and maintenance, operations, and rehabilitation of existing handpumps, water yards, protected wells including check-dams, and hafirs. KAP assessments by WRS in 2020 show that in the dry season, women and children walk far distances to fetch water. Women and girls face explicit risk of sexual violence as they go about their daily task of collecting water. Therefore, to mitigate such risks, the project will ensure that water sources are close to homes. Furthermore, the project will ensure that the different committees either established or strengthened by the project consist of at least 40% women.
Secondly, the project aims to ensure improved access to adequate, protected, and gender-sensitive sanitation services for conflict-affected populations. Interventions will ensure the installation, rehabilitation, and use of ventilated improved pit latrines (VIP), pit latrines with slabs, composting toilets, and flush/pour pit latrines where possible. Household latrines (basic), latrines shared between two households (limited), communal latrines, and institutional latrines will be considered. For sustainability, community volunteers will be trained on CLTS. To ensure effective behavior change, community based hygiene promotion volunteer networks will be established and supported to disseminate hygiene messages and monitor household hygiene practices.
Thirdly, to ensure access to hygiene promotion services, water quality and environmental health interventions will be provided to 208,000 crisis-affected populations. The targeted population will receive hygiene promotion messages focusing on handwashing with soap through household visits, campaigns, and media coverage. Half of the targeted population will be provided with soap and jerry cans. Handwashing facilities will reach people in communal setups. Women and girls who are part of the newly displaced population will receive personal hygiene materials such as reusable sanitary pads or culturally appropriate menstrual hygiene supplies. Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) affected children, along with their households, will be reached with WASH supplies such as soap, jerry cans, buckets, and point of use water treatment materials, including aqua tabs and PUR along with appropriate hygiene promotion messages in the OTPs and Stabilization Centers (SCs). People located in the epidemics and flood-prone areas will be reached with PoUWT and water treatment at the source, followed by water quality monitoring to check on the contamination levels. Environmental health interventions, such as solid waste management and vector control, will be implemented in risk-prone areas.

project_name: Quality Education for Most Vulnerable Children in Central Darfur, Blue Nile, Khartoum and South Kordofan
project_objective:
The project aims to(1) support disaster affected children to improve access quality basic education (2) to support having safe, protective and responsive learning environments to the needs of vulnerable children including children with disabilities. This includes strict adherence to COVID19 safety measures and fostering children’s resilience during emergencies.
The project will target a total of 216498 in four states and 12 localities. Four localities in Central Darfur state; west, north and central Jebel Jebel and Zalingi. Three in Blue Nile; Tadamon, Wad Elmahi and Damazine. The third state is Khartoum, in Karri and Jebel Awlia and in South Kordofan, localities of Abujibiha, Elirrie and Kadogli. 
Save the Children has opted to work on these location to build on its interventions already established there as well as to counite responding to serious education gaps. As an example, in Nertitie West Jabal Marra-where an EiE intervention funded by ECHO is implementing, it has been communicated that at least 19 schools in this locality were damaged because of conflict, and this is why students number per a class in functioning schools could reach as much as 150 students. Add to this, the seating is a challenge as many schools face shortage in seating, in an emergency context this becomes worst with many students sitting on the ground again Jebel Marra localities are good examples of this. Also serious shortage in basic learning and teaching materials were recorded for more than a third of the schools in Sudan. for instance, in some areas of Sudan, in particularly with the emergency context, such as Central Darfur, Blue Nile and South Kordofan, most of the students’ books are not available, when are available the student book ratio could have reached 10:1, ironically in some areas of Jebel Marra some communities thought the books are for teachers only! Also the other supplies i.e. note books, pens, pencils have put a huge burden on families, enforcing many children to withdraw from the schools, with girls being more affected. Add to this, parents and caregivers have to contribute to school operations in term of chalks and the related school supplies, through some fee paid monthly. Also teachers’ guidance books are not enough, and sometime no available at all. In addition, teachers have to buy the notes for the lessons preparation. Again this might put more burden on schools and might also be transferred to the parents in terms of using some of parents’ contribution to buy such items.  Add to this, the teachers training has been a challenge all the way through. For instance, findings from South Kordofan-EQUIP Project EUD funded- has shown that 50-60% have received training in subjects, but very few have received training on code of conduct and child protection issues. 
To this effect, this HRP activities were designed to support access include rehabilitation and construction of classrooms, and TLS, latrines, hand washing facilities, as well as seating provision and all learning, teaching, and recreational materials, add to this, uniforms and PPE will be be also availed. In addition, the the teachers are going to be trained in child centered approach, positive discipline as well as the protection issues include the PFA and schools as zone of peace(Save School Declaration). Also in all targeted schools referral path will be established, and also grants to support COVID 19 are considered. Considering the necessity of community engagement, PTAs are going to be trained as well as Mother Groups are going to be established in some schools where the education was absent for many years such as Rokero in Central Darfur.  The implementation of all activities are going to be guided by the INEE, Sphere and Save the Children Quality Learning Framework (QLF) that put the children wellbeing at the heart of the education intended outcomes, and this why CP is well integrated and mainstreamed.

project_name: Emergency Livelihood Response Programme
project_objective:
The aim of the Emergency Livelihood Response Programme (ELRP) is to improve food security in Luhansk oblast, among the communities most  affected by conflict, including those affected by October’s 2020 wildfires, to enhance households food production, reduce the degree and frequency with which households depend on external food assistance, and strengthen their capacity to absorb shocks. 
The wildfires intensified the impact of the conflict in the communities, resulting in a decrease of food production compounded by the additional challenges of economic recovery. 
The ELRP will set the foundation for enhancing the long-term adaptive capacity of communities and strengthens the synergies among FAO’s short- and long-term strategies to build resilience; Linking the ELRP with FAO’s wider resilience programmes in Donetsk oblast will contribute to the strengthen of the East region adaptive capacity.
The ELRP is developed in accordance with the “New Way of Working”, acknowledging calls for integrated, context-specific, multi-partner actions led by local actors, as well as the adoption of joint programming with United Nations agencies wherever possible.
The project will target 3 000 households (6 840 people) from Luhansk oblast’s conflict affected villages located within the area of 0-5 km from the contact line, including those affected by the wildfires. 
Households targeted to benefit from emergency livelihood support will be those facing from food insecurity that possess basic knowledge and skills in crop and vegetable production and have sufficient access to land and water. Priority will be given to the most vulnerable, including women-headed households and households affected by the wildfires.
•	FAO Technical capacity
FAO food security and agriculture experts, emergency response officers, monitoring and evaluation specialists and area coordinators will ensure beneficiaries receive inputs that are tailored to their needs and agro-ecological zones.
•	Results framework
Through the implementation of the ELRP, FAO aims to protect the livelihoods of vulnerable communities and enhance food production while strengthening their resilience. This will be achieved through the following outcomes: (i) protect the livelihoods of vulnerable households and enhance their food production; and (ii) strengthen absorptive capacity and build resilience at household and community level.
•	Humanitarian–development nexus 
FAO’s emergency response programme is part of the Organization’s broader resilience-building efforts, bridging the divide between humanitarian and development outcomes. Recognizing the role of humanitarian livelihoods interventions in building a foundation for resilience, the ELRP seeks to go beyond input provision where it is stable enough to do so and where partners are on the ground to deliver. It is expected that this will contribute to a longer-term vision for food security in selected locations, including the creation of better linkages between short- and long-term interventions to enhance impacts and contribute to longer-lasting outcomes. Community engagement will be enhanced to improve participatory planning, thereby increasing beneficiary ownership of the activities and strengthening FAO’s commitment to accountability to affected populations. This is expected to streamline needs identification, targeting and key messaging down to the local level. 
•	Implementing Partners
FAO, as the specialized agency of the United Nations for agriculture and key expert in food security, will implement the Project with the support of the local implementing partners (IP). Based on the established selection process, FAO will identify and select the local NGO to to organize supply of inputs, undertake community mobilization activities in the field, ensuring gender-sensitivity of the providers of community mobilization activities. For community-based trainings, FAO will procure services from academia institutions to ensure high quality of outputs.

project_name: Syrian Education for Access and Quality (SEAQ)
project_objective:
The project aims to increase safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education for crisis affected children and youth (aged 5-17 years) and improve the quality of formal and non-formal education for children and youth (aged 5-17 years) within a protective environment. The project will be implemented through ADRA Syria’s education team, in close coordination with MoE and related DoEs, ensuring the protection of all beneficiaries through a ‘do not harm’ approach.  Through this project, ADRA Syria will improve access to formal and non-formal education and learning opportunities for girls and boys by creating safe and protective environments for 14,644 children who have been affected by the crisis. These education interventions will be implemented in the governorates of Rural Damascus, Quneitra, Homs, Aleppo, Dara’a and Deir Ez Zour (all targeted  sub-districts are in the areas of Education severity levels 3-5). ADRA Syria will enhance the formal and non–formal education level of the students - boys and girls - in the schools rehabilitated by ADRA. This will be accomplished through a holistic program with psycho-social, familial, and educational support, encouraging the engagement of mothers and fathers in educational activities. The average cost per beneficiary is estimated at $75. The total number of targeted beneficiates is 14,644 individuals, of which 5% (732 individuals) are people with disabilities. 

ADRA will coordinate with key stakeholders to ensure the most vulnerable boys and girls are identified in the target locations. Further, ADRA will conduct comprehensive needs assessments in the areas identified to locate out-of-school children (OOSC) and students with priority educational needs.
- In 2020, ADRA received a total of USD 2,013,504 for education activities. 
- in 2020, ADRA reached an estimated 15,654 individuals through it's education activities.  
- Thus far, in 2021, ADRA secured a total of approximately USD 900,000.

project_name: Provision of timely, equitable and integrated WASH services to the conflict, epidemic and natural disaster affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
South Sudan protracted crises have left 7.5 million people in dire need of humanitarian assistance in 2020 despite the signature of the Revitalized peace agreement, and continues to face conflict, natural disasters and climate instability, food insecurity, and lack of basic services. As per the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2021, lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in South Sudan will negatively impact an estimated 5.6 million people in 2021.
Since 2006, SI has become a key WASH actor in South Sudan, implementing emergency lifesaving response and providing integrated WASH services to crisis-affected populations in the areas thanks to its static presence in Juba County, Nyirol County, Fashoda County, Raja and Wau Counties. Since 2012 SI has played a key role in the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) strategy in South Sudan, implementing multi-sectoral assessments and delivering emergency responses to crisis-affected populations all over the country. In 2021, SI will aim at improving timely, equitable and integrated access to WASH services to the conflict, epidemic and natural disaster affected populations in South Sudan.
