project_name: Assistance pour les populations déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes dans les régions du sahel, Centre Nord et Nord du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La région du sahel du Burkina connait depuis 2015 des conflits qui affectent la population entraînant des mouvements des populations des zones d'origines vers des villes plus sécurisées. Selon le cadre harmonisé de Novembre 2020, 496 469 personnes de la région du sahel ont actuellement besoin d'une assistance alimentaire et ce nombre atteindra 655 836 au moment de la soudure agricole. 
les populations des provinces de l'Oudalan, Seno, Soum et Yagha sont difficilement accessibles par les monde humanitaire rendant encore plus la situation alarmante. Des ONG telles DRC avec des stratégies d'intervention communautaires et de respect des principes humanitaires arrive encore à apporter l'aide dans ces zones. 
Hors mis les chefs lieux de provinces et de certains chefs lieux de communes tout le territoire du sahel est inaccessible ce qui rend difficile les interventions des acteurs humanitaires. Le cadre harmonisé estime qu'actuellement dans l'Oudalan 22% (69 219 personnes) de la population est en situation de crise alimentaire, dans le Seno 28%(113 740 personnes), dans le Soum 45% (245 514 personnes) et dans le Yagha 27%(67 997 personnes). Et ces chiffres vont augmenter durant la période de juin à Août 2021 et atteindre 30% de la population dans l'Oudalan, 35% Seno, 63% Soum ( 23 en phase d'urgence).
Cette situation est similaire dans les régions du Centre-Nord specifiquement dans la province du Namentenga avec 24% (120387 personnes) de la population en situation d'insécurité alimentaire actuellement et dans la région du Nord specifiquement le  Lorum avec 25% soit 54 039 personnes.
Face à ces situations de sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle catastrophique dans ces régions DRC préconise une assistance alimentaire dans ces zones afin de soulager ces populations vulnérables.

project_name: Education first: An Integrated Approach to Enhance Access and Quality of Education in vulnerable and Underserved Communities Within Syria.
project_objective:
As part of its education response, PUI is targeting vulnerable and underserved communities with a bundle of activities, with the overall objective of enhancing the access to quality education provided in protective and suitable learning environment for affected children, to ensure that they don’t become a lost generation. Indeed, with the protracted crisis approaching its tenth year in Syria, an entire generation of children and youth is being subject to persistent lack of opportunities to access quality education. This situation could have long-term negative consequences, affecting children’s mental health and wellbeing and preventing them from developing in good and safe conditions, as well as gaining essential life skills and knowledge. 

The proposed project in brief:
-	Will target locations where high education needs are documented by Education Sector.  63 % of the locations have a severity score of 4, while 31 % have a score of 3.  PUI also will target Al Haffa which has as score of 2 as per above mentioned document; however, according to PUI observations the needs are high and proposed intervention will complement PUI interventions under other sectors. 
-	The cost per beneficiary is 27.24 USD.
-	It is estimated that 353 individuals of targeted beneficiaries may have disabilities. 
-	Total funding the organization received in 2020 for education is about 4.5 USD from non UN donors. These funds are for two years, which means it will also cover 2021 activities PUI plans to implement. Additionally, PUI is currently in the process of fund raising, thus 2021 budget might increase. 


This project aims at encouraging out of school students and dropped-out students to resume their education through tailored back to learning campaigns and empowering those children with self-learning program conceived as transition programs to enable them to catch-up and reintegrate the formal education system after this transition period. In addition, PUI will assist children in their education by providing them with kits, education supplies and remedial classes to cover for any gaps and ensure every child’s educational needs are met and to prevent them from dropping out of school. Furthermore, PUI will contribute to enhancing the quality of education by providing capacity building activities to teachers and MoE staff, training them on active learning, PSS, and life skills. PUI will also initiate an awareness campaign for 11,400 children and their parents on health and hygiene, with a specific focus on COVID-19 protection. Lastly, in parallel to the above-mentioned activities, PUI will ensure that children have access to safe and protective learning environment where they can access quality education by rehabilitating damaged schools in targeted locations.

project_name: Sewage networks rehabilitation in Northern and Southern districts of Dayr Hafir
project_objective:
On the 11th year of conflict, the scale & diversity of needs, overall PiN in Dayr Hafir 19,350, which is complemented by figures presenting specific WASH needs related to water quality 3.3, quantity 1.4, sanitation 3.2, solid waste management 4.1, and heavy financial burden linked with purchasing water 7.5 or hygiene supplies 6.4 million people [HNO 2021]. Rescate is currently implementing a project of public market in Dayr Hafir which is under GoS since 2017. The security prevails and there are no access restrictions. Rescate aim is to provide integrated service in the town while safeguarding people's health. Severity scale is 3 and the current sewerage and sanitation systems in the targeted area are non-functional and flooding to the streets, putting populations at risk for epidemic-prone diseases HENCE need arises for lifesaving sanitation intervention. The situation in this neighborhoods is that sewage is flooding into the streets, hence vehicles and public transportation are eventually carrying the residues to outside the district which is spreading sickness and diseases to others. population in the target areas come from all walks of life, employees, students of all ages, workers, etc. who are prone to sanitation born diseases.   
The main objective of this intervention is support sanitation management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in South & North districts in Dayr Hafir (160 and 116 hectares) inhabited by 5700 individuals including 600 elderlies, men 1110, women 1240, children and adolescents 2750 (boys 1450, Girls 1300), and PWDs 32 . The network rehabilitation is an urgent lifesaving need to ensure safe disposal & waste management. Lines of 2,210 ML are broken due to destruction to the conflict between 2012-2017 upon which people returned to the area and lack of maintenance. Replacement of the broken pipes will start with detailed inspection then cleaning the tunnels & re-cover the pipes per the approved technical standards. This will save local community & HHs returnees while the sanitation was not functioning from serious health risks.
Access to safe sanitation system is compromised based on the fact of lack of maintenance & rehabilitation of the networks which are not functioning due to un-addressed damages, consequently increasing the likelihood of waterborne diseases spreading due to poor sanitation & limited ability to practice good hygiene. The project impact with improved sanitation infrastructure & will support Covid-19 response as locality hygiene is a main requirement to ensure pandemic & contagion control. As Rescate is working on the public market project in Dayr Hafir, the main goal is to provide integrated response to help in building resilience & creating sense of stability for the returnees & population in the town. Rescate will deliver the services of pipelines rehabilitation through reinforcement of available service providers related to WASH sector. A candid review of the rapid technical assessment to ensure detailed BOQ inclusion in the tender call for the works. Rescate intervention in response to 3 severity score city (SYRIA 2021 HNO). This project will enhance beneficiaries’ resilience by enabling them to direct their resources to more tangible needs & to safeguard their health & hygiene under the current deteriorated health pandemic especially Covid-19. Rescate will enter agreement with experienced local contractors to provide works under close supervision of Rescate experience team. A claim mechanism will be introduced M&E officer will monitor implementation & prepare reports about progress, maintain track of works vs budget & action plan, & about beneficiaries’ segregation (gender, age & PWDs) & social impact. A questionnaire to assess beneficiaries’ satisfaction during & after the project implementation. Rescate maintains a schedule for financial & narrative, share info via WASH Sector.

project_name: Increase food security and resiliency of vulnerable communities and Households including PLWs and PWDs in Aleppo, Rural Damascus and Hama
project_objective:
As the food security situation in Syria continues to worsen, with a further deterioration of key food security indicators seen over the first two months of 2021, Syrian households rely on increasingly severe negative coping strategies to cover their essential food needs. The Project aims to improve the food security & livelihood status of most vulnerable people through life-sustaining food assistance & income-generating opportunities with special focus on female-headed households, people with disabilities, elderly people, &daily workers who lost their jobs during COVID-19 outbreak, through the distribution of food vouchers targeted 5125PIN (1025HHs) in the highest severity scales locations in Aleppo, Rural Damascus, & Hama.
In purpose of providing supplementary food assistance to Persons with Specific Needs (PSN) through appropriate modalities & based on the conducted assessment in the targeted locations, TdH will distribute specialized Food voucher (Malnutrition voucher) for cases of malnutrition (identified by other TDH project in the area of implementation) in order to support the malnutrition treatment, especially when they are fully dependent on food aid. The size & composition of the food voucher is tailored to local preferences, demographic profile, activity levels, climatic conditions, local coping capacity, existing levels of malnutrition. It is designed to meet the nutritional requirements of a population rather than individuals (who can be targeted through tailored nutrition programs). When people are fully dependent on food assistance, the standard is to provide 2,100 calories per person,10-12 percent of which come from protein, 17percent from fat (according to WHO/FAO guidelines), micronutrients such as vitamin A, iron, iodine & zinc. As for beneficiaries who are partially dependent on the food aid, the program only aims to “top up” food that is available, based on an understanding of current access to food. A supplementary ration is mostly given to a vulnerable group such as malnutrition children under 5 years of age and/or PLWs.
The amount of each voucher will be 200,000 SYP according to WFP Minimum Expenditure Basket for 8 Cycles/Months according to Food Security Sector minimum standard & CWG.TdH will Conduct a market assessment in the targeted locations and contracting with the appropriate once.
In the purpose of providing income-generating opportunities & based on the conducted assessment in the targeted location, Tdh will conduct specialized vocational training for 420persons (60 from each location) mainly for PwDs & Female-Headed households & daily workers for three months in a training center in the same location taking into consideration COVID-19 Prevention measures. Training subjects will be chosen based on the outputs of the conducted needs assessment in the targeted locations & beneficiaries list from the food vouchers distributions will be nominated by the community committees & verified through household visits by the local partner volunteers in order to avoid any duplication with any humanitarian actors working in the same neighborhoods.
Tdh will coordinate with other FSA actors to ensure there is no duplication in receiving the services. TdH regularly participating to the cash working group, & we will share 5Ws report reflecting the achievements with food sector for more efficient & effectiveness in response & coordination. All the activities will be supervised by TdH staff and will be carried out in coordination with the local partner to guarantee a continuous collaboration, also M&E staff will conduct field visits regularly, also, M&E Officer will make active calls or personal interviews to a random sample of beneficiaries (20% of the targeted beneficiaries) to collect information, feedback from beneficiaries on how they feel about the project. Moreover, determine whether the local partner adhered to the agreed targeting criteria and the level of beneficiary participation in the targeting process

project_name: Emergency food security and livelihood assistance to IDPs, flood affected and vulnerable households in West Kordofan, South Kordofan, West Darfur, Kassala and Gedaref States
project_objective:
The proposed intervention links with and contributes to 2021 HRP Strategic Objective 1: Provide timely multi-sectoral life-saving assistance to crisis affected people to reduce mortality and morbidity and Strategic Objective 2: Improve vulnerable people’s access to livelihoods and life-sustaining basic services by supporting displaced populations, returnees and host communities to meet their basic needs and/or access to essential basic services in West Darfur, West Kordofan, South Kordofan, Kassala and Gedaref States. This intervention will also contribute directly to the first FSL sector strategic objectives by addressing life threatening needs and addressing life sustaining needs. In addition, it will indirectly contribute to FSL sector strategic objective 3, protection.  In the five-targeted states, a lack of investment in agriculture, protracted displacements, frequent insecurity, impacts of climate change, lack of investment in social services have condemned a large number of people to food insecurity and lack of livelihood opportunities. The continued insecurity in the state means that access to agricultural land remains limited as farmers abandoned their farms due to insecurity. The latest IPC report (Nov 2020) indicates that there are 1,715,282 persons are in need of food and livelihood security assistance. The project will support the people with agriculture, livestock, IGA, MPCA and vocational training intervention to improve food security and provide opportunities to earn incomes
This project will target 63,750 persons that include, IDPs and vulnerable host community members at a total cost of $ 4, 143,750, which is about 1% of the $426,480,000 needed to support 80% of the persons in need in 2021.  The budget has been arrived at using the FSL cluster estimate of $65/beneficiary. 
In the five states, the project will support vulnerable households affected by manmade and natural disasters, IDPs, returnee communities with limited access and availability of adequate, sufficient and nutritious food and small-scale farmers who face production and market constraints as projected by HNO 2021 report. There will be deliberate focus on women, beneficiaries as they are marginalized and socially excluded and thus bear the greatest burden of food insecurity.  
The purpose of the project is to support food insecure households to access food, improve food production, increase access to incomes, enable households meet their basic needs and provide livelihood opportunities and strengthen their resilience to further shocks and stresses. The intervention seeks to provide food assistance and cash assistance, material support (inputs) and increase the knowledge and skills of the targeted households in agricultural production, income generation and livelihood opportunities in order to increase household food availability, improve food diversity and have diversified income and livelihood opportunities

project_name: Providing basic WASH services for IDP’s, returnees and host community in Rural Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, Hama, As Sweida, Dar’a and Deir Ezzor
project_objective:
The project’s main objective is to provide access to WASH basic services for  985,000  displaced people, returnees and overburdened host community at risk within the highly neglected sub-districts in the aforementioned areas Located in:

Deir Ezzor, Khasham, Tabni, Abukamal, Jalaa / Deir Ezzor   Governorate
As-Sanamayn, Ash-Shajara, Da'el, Mzeireb, Tasil, Jasim, Izra’ / Dar’a Governorate
Jebel Saman, ,Zarbah, As-safira / Aleppo Governorate  .
Duma, Kisweh,  Nashabiyeh  / Rural Damascus   Governorate.
Masyaf, Muhradah/ Hama Governorate
Salkhad, Shahba, As-Sweida, Qarayya / As-Sweida Governorate 
Qaryatein , Foroqles, Taldu, Ein Elniser, Tadmor / Homs Governorate 

Based on HNO 2021/WASH in Homs, those sub-dsitricts Qaryatein (4) , Foroqles (3), Taldu (3), Ein Elniser (3), Tadmor (3) with severity scale (3-4). And after coordination with local authorities and municipalities, which indicate that there is a huge need to WASH services especially since the targeted sub-directorates are still witnessing a steady number of returnees, but they face great difficulties in resettlement in their communities, due to the enormous extent of destruction. 

The consequences of the conflict and the outbreak of Covid-19 have been particularly severe, as many parts of different governorates have been transformed into hard-to-reach areas, where people suffer from a lack of basic water, sanitation and hygiene needs to survive, due to the massive destruction of the Wash and sanitation services. Loss of livelihoods and income, high cost of basic commodities, and a sharp devaluation of the currency. Displaced people, returnees and overburdened host communities face massive conflicts as they try to provide basic water, sanitation and supplies for their families.

project_name: Provision of in-kind food assistance to Vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
UNRWA estimates that 418,000 Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance in 2021. In a context of rising inflation and additional economic hardship caused by COVID-19, Palestine refugees are more and more affected by food insecurity and therefore increasingly depend on UNRWA assistance to meet their minimum food needs. Due to the vulnerability of Palestine refugees in the current socio-economic crisis, compounded by COVID-19, in 2021 UNRWA will expand its food programming and provide all 418,000 Palestine refugees with in-kind food assistance  through three distribution rounds. The Agency will continue to monitor the availability of food on the markets and will retain operational flexibility to adjust to a changing context as appropriate.

The composition of the food basket was developed based on WFP guidelines and in view of meeting ~ 50% of daily nutritional needs for 4 months.

UNRWA's original plan is to distribute 3 rounds of in-kind food assistance, each round covering a period of 4 months. However, this depends on the availability of funds. Until May 2021, UNRWA received or confirmed pledges are only sufficient to cover the first two rounds of 2021. The Agency will continue to mobilize resources to ensure funding for the third round is also secured.

In 2021, the number of people estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance including for food needs is 418,000 Palestine refugees to strengthen their resilience and prevent further deterioration into acute food insecurity. As per its emergency planning, UNRWA aims to provide food assistance as well as multipurpose cash assistance, and protection interventions at both household and community levels, as well as the coordination of these activities across the different Sectors framework.

UNRWA has been providing life-saving humanitarian aid to Palestine refugees since the start of the crisis in Syria. The in-kind food assistance program remains one of the most important forms of UNRWA emergency support to stabilize the food security status for Palestine refugees in Syria, as it helps them meet part of their basic nutritional and survival requirements (~50% of kcal/person/day) which will increase resilience, and reduce humanitarian needs and the spiraling food insecurity levels.

project_name: Operating Al-Birr Hospital
project_objective:
Al-Birr Hospital was built, operated and owned by Al-Birr Association since 1994 in order to provide all health services (primary and secondary) to all citizens, especially the poor patients and the patients from northern rural Homs, with high quality and in a manner, that preserves their dignity without any discrimination.
The hospital has 150 beds. It is the largest private and charitable hospital in Syria.
Before the crisis in Al-Waer, Al-Birr hospital was visited by a patients from all of Homs city (60% of them from rural Homs) since it's equipped with modern equipment, and has the best staff of doctors and nurses; especially after the damage of most public health centers and public hospitals. Al-Birr hospital was providing all kind of health care including primary, secondary and even tertiary health care services. It was providing all kinds of surgeries and medical care including open cardiac surgery, cardiac catheterization, and specific operations such as neurosurgery.

During the crisis period, the hospital was severely affected because of its location in Al-Waer area, which forced the association to stop working in some departments and limit the services to some services such as dialysis, especially in the last five years.
After the agreement of Al-Waer neighborhood, A lot of people returned to their homes in Al-Waer, so Al-Birr has started rehabilitating this hospital after years of operating another hospitals in Homs city (Farkouh, Mahattah, Al-Kindi and Al-Shawi).
Till now, there is no enough public care centers in Homs city, where most of public hospitals there is just providing some primary services such as outpatient clinics and laboratory, while urgent secondary care services are not provided so patients have to transfer to other private hospitals out of Homs to get services.
Anyway, the kind of services will be provided in Homs city and will help people not just in Homs governorate but also in other governorates since Homs is in the middle of Syria and people do not have to travel to Damascus for obtaining necessary and urgent health services such as catheterization, neurosurgery, lithotripsy and other services.

The rehabilitation process is an urgent issue to integrate the health services that Al-Birr hospital provides. These services will match the critical needs and will present with high quality.
Al-Birr hospital has all the equipment since it did its best to save its equipment. While many of these equipment are working, some of them need maintenance or is old-fashioned and need to be updated. AL-Birr will provide primary and secondary health care to all people in need.
This project is to maintain essential devices, operate the different sections of the hospital and provide various health services for free for people in need.

project_name: Provision of NFIs to the most vulnerable households in Deir-Ez-Zor Sub-district
project_objective:
The main goal of this Action is to ensure targeted crisis-affected households, including those in underserved communities, have their core and the essential non-food item needs met, in accordance with the sector’s outcome indicator. The Action will provide mid-to-long-term sustainable resilience to those most in need for items assistance, to maintain their health, privacy and dignity. 
WWGVC plans to distribute essential and supplementary NFIs kits to 15,000 highly vulnerable adults and children, including IDPs and returnees in Deir Ez Zor Sub-district: 2000 HHs (15,000 ind, 7,290 males and 7,710 females) will receive a core NFI kits (A.1.1), supported by the distribution of core winter NFI kits (A.1.2)
The distributed items comply with the Shelter / NFI specifications. Beneficiaries will be selected according to vulnerability criteria set in close consultation with the target population. Different stakeholders, including people in need, community leaders and other local actors will participate in setting these criteria, to ensure transparency, acceptance and accountability. Selected HHs will include female-headed HHs, HH including elderly people, and/or people with disabilities, and/or infants. 
In order to respond to the latter, and to integrate the action with education and protection programs currently delivered by GVC in Deir-Ez-Zor, the project targets the most vulnerable HHs among GVC’s beneficiaries’ database. identified through WWGVC’s Education program’s database of out of school children or children at risk of dropping out.  The intervention is also designed based on WWGVC’s needs assessment conducted on families of children targeted by GVC education programs. The analysis revealed that a high percentage of HHs do not have the ability to afford the basic necessary non-food items and clothing.  GVC has a base in Deir-Ez-Zor able to implement and closely monitor the proposed activities. All contents of the kits are purchased from local vendors in Syria.  
The Action will be conducted adopting safe measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19, in line with relevant Sectors’ standards, stated in the Recommendations for adjusting NFI & Emergency Shelter Distributions in the context of Covid-19 outbreak (May 2020). 
GVC will coordinate with SARC, MoE, NFI and WASH Sectors as well as other present humanitarian actors (including UN Agencies, i.e. UNICEF and UNHCR) to ensure information sharing, and avoid any duplication and overlapping during implementation.

project_name: Protection of girls and boys in conflict and post-conflict areas in Sudan through quality preventative and remedial interventions
project_objective:
Across Sudan, girls and boys and their families face risks associated with conflict, violence and displacement including family separation, Sexual Gender-based Violence (SGBV), mine risk, psychological distress, and child labour. 
Save the Children will ensure the provision of timely and rights-based child protection services to the most deprived and marginalized girls and boys, especially those affected by conflict and displaced from their homes.  These services will include Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) for Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC); prevention and response to the needs of child victims of Sexual and Gender Based violence (SGBV); material support, vocational training, support services, and life skills training for extremely vulnerable children and adolescents affected by conflict; and safe places for play, recreation and the provision of psychosocial support to children displaced or affected by conflict.
To prevent and mitigate child protection risks in communities affected by conflict and displacement, Save the Children will strengthen the capacity of social workers, teachers, and law-enforcement staff, as well as investing in capacity building of the National Council on for Child Welfare and other humanitarian partners.  In order to reinforce the resilience of communities and strengthen capacity of child protection institutions, Save the Children will support community based child protection mechanisms and civil society organisations to disseminate information on relevant services and contribute to advocacy and the referral of child protection cases; and to promote safer environments for children.

project_name: Emergency Education and MHPSS in Gaza

The new school year of 2020/2021 was ready to start with over 287,000 registered students between 1st to 9th grades in 278 UNRWA schools throughout the Gaza Strip, yet again disrupted upon the announcement of lockdown measure due to the detection of locally transmitted COVID-19 cases on 24 August 2020. As of end of October 2020, UNRWA is finalizing the resumption of Education plan taking into consideration COVID-19 circumstances and developments that are expected to continue throughout the academic year 2020/2021. In order to ensure that no child is left behind and that access to education is available to all students regardless of their available resources under this circumstance, UNRWA will provide: (1) support classes for Arabic and Mathematics  including supporting materials , (2) mental health and psychosocial support to students and parents by experienced school counsellors through tele-counselling and in person if the situation allows , (3) support to special education for children with disabilities through Community Based Rehabilitation Centers,  (4) application of preventive measures including school hygiene and physical-distancing requirement to be compatible with the WHO and MoH regulations related to COVID-19 , and (5) self-learning support to assist students’ learning experience at home.

project_name: Supporting sustainability of response and community resilience in Volnovakha raion, Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
After seven years of conflict, frontline communities in direct vicinity of the Line of Contact (LoC) such those located in the area covered by theVolnovakha raion are bearing the brunt of the protracted crisis. The resources of communities acting as administrative centers in Government-Controlled Areas have been thinly stretched to provide an array of key services (social services, justice, counselling, administrative) for local populations living both in Government (GCA) as well as residents of Non-Government-Controlled Areas (NGCA) of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts who cross the line of contact (LoC) to seek services in GCA. As COVID-19 has added further pressure on communities and local authorities, increased needs for e.g. Psycho-social support (PSS) have been identified and reported as a priority by local representatives.

ACTED, in partnership with Right to Protection (R2P) and the Red Cross (RC), aim at supporting the resilience of communities in three prospective Hromadas, totalling 67,000 individuals, located in Volnovakha raion (Myrne, Olhynka, Volnovakha) through capacity-building and provision of protection services for vulnerable populations, including Internally Displaced People (IDP) and host communities. Activity design has been informed by the experience of partners in the target areas and, in line with Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) principles, community inputs have been sought and inputted into project design and modalities. Community participation will take place during the entire duration of the project, through public communications, transparency for targeting and eligibility, and partners will maintain Complaint and Response Mechanisms (CRM) to ensure that community members, including people who were not supported, can voice their concerns and receive information in return. Data collected by partners will be disaggregated by gender, age, special needs and type of vulnerability for accountability to affected populations and to inform project modalities. 

The proposed intervention includes Capacity-Building of Local Authorities (LAs) to address the needs of the vulnerable population and strengthen provision of essential services such as community-based PSS in cooperation with the Local Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) branch and heads of settlements. The project will contribute promote the development of volunteerism, self-support and social cohesion in the conflict affected communities, thereby contributing to preparing for a humanitarian exit in GCA

Planned PSS and social services activities will be implemented in synergy and contribute to improved resilience for vulnerable people. The services provided by trained local volunteers with the support of the local URCS Branch and regular consultations with LAs before, during and after the project, together with activities aimed at improving access to and the quality of social services, will enhance capacity of LAs to take responsibility for and work with communities to find durable solutions to strengthen social cohesion, well-being and other significant protection concerns.
 
1/RC activities will aim at strengthening protection, including prevention and mitigation of rights’ violations for conflict-affected people, including IDPs. RC jointly with LAs will provide PSS and outreach support as well as community spaces for older persons, persons with disabilities, and people with conflict-related trauma.
RC will improve social cohesion and resilience in Volnovakha communities, including IDPs, through community-based protection interventions and identification of durable solutions. 
2/R2P’s component will contribute to building capacity of LA representatives. R2P’s approach will address disruption of services networks and increase the CAP satisfaction with basic social services, including vulnerable groups (single women, people with disabilities, elderly) host communities and persons who cross the contact line at EECP Novotroitske.

project_name: Information management and pilot capacity building for evidence-based, sustainable response in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
In response to the crisis in Eastern Ukraine, the intervention proposed by ACTED, jointly with IMPACT Initiatives and the Danish Red Cross is aimed at a) informing the humanitarian community for evidence-based planning of the humanitarian response, b) piloting a project to strengthen coordination and capacity-building mechanisms for improved response by and transition of responsibility to local actors in Volnovakha raion.

The armed conflict in the East remains protracted and local communities in frontline areas still bear the brunt of the shock of the active conflict.. To address heightened vulnerabilities in these communities, especially for women and the elderly, it is critical to mobilize and support initiatives from authorities, communities, volunteers and active citizens, contributing to better collective resilience and preparedness to mitigate the effects of shocks. ACTED, in partnership with the Danish Red Cross, plans to support coordination and strengthen local capacities of the Ukrainian Red Cross Society volunteer network in Volnovakha raion as a pilot, community-based approach to support the sustainability of the response in Eastern Ukraine.

Building upon their experience with communities and local authorities in frontline communities of Donbas, and in line with the area-based/localized approach which integrates the needs of the most vulnerable, particularly women and the elderly, partners plan to provide an additional layer of support in Volnovakha raion through material support for first responders, including the local branch of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) for Disaster Risk Reduction/Management (DRR/DRM), and recently or to-be established hromada administrations within the boundaries of the Volnovakha raion. 

It is also planned that communities (volunteers, CSOs) be provided with information products developed by ACTED and IMPACT to further support the local capacity for evidence-based planning.

Furthermore, REACH will inform the humanitarian programming cycle and coordination, and promote better integration of highly vulnerable groups incl. women and the elderly, by systematically-collecting perspectives of affected populations disaggregated by key demographic data including gender, age, and disability markers.  Building off of work conducted since 2016 and with adaptations to COVID-related dynamics, REACH will support the inter cluster coordination group and humanitarian partners with inter-sectoral needs assessments analyzing household needs, with a focus on gender, ability, and age disaggregated data in government (GCA) and non-government controlled areas (NGCA).

Through this project, REACH will be able to contribute to a more nuanced understanding of how COVID-19 measures may have exacerbated existing inequities and/or have led to new vulnerabilities, and considering multiple compounding vulnerabilities such as age and gender, while monitoring humanitarian trends and refining a multi-sectoral understanding of humanitarian needs. In line with commitments from the Grand Bargain, REACH will continue supporting the Ukraine humanitarian community with joint and impartial needs assessments to develop the HNO and HRP, while also continuing to strengthen local level capacities through its Information Management Hub technical trainings.

Beyond the immediate impacts on population health and the health system, the secondary and medium-term effects of COVID-19 are only beginning. The planned REACH activities will therefore aim to provide timely and relevant analysis, which include gender and age specific considerations, as information needs evolve in 2021, and the pilot to be run by ACTED and the Danish Red Cross in Volnovakha is aimed at supporting populations with an additional safety net at the community level to increase resilience, empower communities and encourage local ownership of the response to shocks.

project_name: Increasing water safety and access to COVID-19 hygiene items in conflict-affected areas close to the line of contact in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
As the conflict remains protracted in Eastern Ukraine, it is vital to invest in the resilience of populations affected by the conflict and at risk of humanitarian disaster. With 3.4 million people in need of humanitarian aid and noting the potential negative impact from a major prolonged disruption to local infrastructures and systems, compounded by the risk of COVID-19 infection which requires access to water and hygiene for effective prevention and control, the risk of humanitarian disaster in conflict-affected areas is high.
Currently, millions of Donbas residents who are dependent on central water systems are at risk if/when critical infrastructure fails. Since 2014, critical water and sanitation facilities close to the line of contact (LoC) have been under constant attack, disrupting access to water for millions of people on both sides of the LoC, with 65 incidents affecting the utility supply in 2019 and 57 incidents in 2020 in the first 7 months of the calendar year. Notably in July 2020, 3 pipelines from the Siverskyi Donets Donbas channel, which supply water to 3.2 million people, were severely damaged as of a result of shellings (WASH, 2020). Water safety risks stemming from damage to infrastructure due to conflict are compounded by the consequences of the global pandemic. COVID-19 has heightened the sensitivity and urgency of securing clean and reliable water. 
In addition to problems related to large networks, which require regional and/or national action, municipal/communal water and wastewater systems are also in disrepair. ACTED found that several regions in the area, incl. settlements in the Bakhmutski and Popasna raions, are at high risk of experiencing dysfunctions in their sewage systems, and water treatment and pumping station buildings continue to need support to operate at satisfactory capacity in most raions in the area (ACTED, WRA, 2020).  Considering difficulties in undertaking adequate repairs of water supply systems or damaged power lines, local authorities and the humanitarian community have had to fill the gap in water provision through water trucking, while communities consume water from non-potable sources. The impact of water-related risks is also compounded by state responders’ limited capacities and planning, partly due to insufficient resources. 
In response, ACTED will implement a water safety project to a) assess water risks in targeted communities close to the line of contact; b) develop – jointly with local authorities (LA), communities, and public utility companies (PUCs)– water safety plans; and c) provide targeted material support towards the implementation of the plans, and/or community-led projects which aim to increase the quantity or quality of water.  Through the water safety planning approach, ACTED aims to ensure its humanitarian response leads to a strengthening of regional and local response capacity by continuously working in tandem with LA/other local actors to enable them to then take up responsibility for the response and continue to provide clean and safe drinking water to their constituents.
Beyond water, COVID-19 transmission mitigation measures also require soap and other hygiene items. Therefore, to complement its water safety interventions, ACTED will distribute hygiene kits to individuals and cleaning kits to institutions to support them to implement key infection prevention and control measures. Additionally, ACTED will operate and maintain hand washing stations in selected locations (or cover them through sanitizer distribution when capacities to maintain the station during and beyond project end are insufficient). 
Leveraging in-country and global capacity, and based on needs and gaps identified, ACTED aims to – through a community-based approach – mitigate some of the WASH hazards that conflict-affected communities are vulnerable to and which could trigger or compound a cascading disaster, including the spread of communicable disease.

project_name: Equitable access to quality education and improved learning opportunities for the most vulnerable crisis affected girls and boys
project_objective:
Conflicts, climate change, locust invasion and the COVID-19 pandemic have been drivers of vulnerability, which have led to access to basic social services being extremely low in Somalia. This has left communities with socio-economic vulnerabilities behind, negatively affecting their children’s access to education services. Vulnerable girls, boys and adolescents have consequently been denied access to inclusive quality education in a safe and protective learning environment.
The 2018-2019 EMIS shows the national Gross Enrolment Rate (GER) for primary education is at 30% for primary level and 18% in rural areas. The 2019 Somalia Joint Multi Cluster Needs Assessment indicates 58% of girls in host communities and 75% of IDPs girls were not attending schools.  The dropout rate in host communities is around 30% and among IDPs around 17%. The disparities between access and attendance to school in urban and rural communities are also significant, with marginalized groups such as girls, IDPs, children with disabilities, children in hard-to-reach areas being the most affected. 
There is major concern of high number of children not accessing schools and increased number of children at risk of dropping out of school. The shortage in educational opportunities exacerbates protection risks, putting children at great risk of harmful practices, including child marriage, child labor and recruitment by armed groups, as well as exposing them to other vices.
The COVID-19 pandemic led to 5-months school closure. The secondary impacts of COVID-19 has exposed children to higher risks of abuse and increased psychosocial distress as a result of confinements. The COVID-19 pandemic has indirect impacts on human capital formation through deteriorated educational outcomes as it affects enrolment, age-appropriate attendance and educational grade achievements. This impact will have long term effects on the delivery of educational services. The 2020 GBV/FGM Assessment and 2020 UNICEF survey underscore that protection risks have been further compounded by the school closure due to the COVID-19 outbreak. The prolonged closure of schools was not only a loss of education but also many children’s main source of sustainable access to food, clean drinking water, social care and a safe haven for play and interaction. 
 The UNICEF survey indicated an increase in child labor with 12% of children engaged in forced labour without pay, while 35% of children experiencing violence at home. 20% of boys and girls faced sexual abuse and harassment and many vulnerable children still face challenges that work against their re-entry to school, including financial struggles. The secondary impact of COVID-19 on already impoverished families has been severe placing them at greater risk of deepening poverty and long-term negative impacts on their social and health situations. 46% of parents are unable to provide basic needs for their children as well as support their access to education services, due to the diminished economic opportunities and the weakened social institutions (Save the Children survey 2020). It highlights 20% of children reporting negative impact on children’s psychosocial well-being due to being out of school.
UNICEF’s Emergency Education project will work closely with Child Protection and WASH to promote an integrated approach. Attention will be laid on enhancing safe and protective learning environment that are inclusive, and which meet the needs of vulnerable girls, women, boys and men, including those of persons with disabilities, for both displaced and host communities. UNICEF’s education response will focus on mitigating the impact of emergencies on education by ensuring improved access to education, retaining children in schools, and building the government’s capacity education in emergencies. 160,000 (80,000 girls) most vulnerable and marginalized children with 16,000 (8,000 girls) being children with disabilities will be targeted.

project_name: Community-based protection and assistance close to the contact line
2021 Multi Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in occupied Palestine territory (oPt)
project_objective:
Through this proposed action, REACH (a joint initiative of ACTED, IMPACT Initiatives and UNOSAT) will support the coordination and technical implementation of a Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in the West Bank and Gaza. The assessment will consist of a multi-sectoral household survey employed among a representative sample of the affected population in both the West Bank and Gaza. The MSNA will be conducted in partnership with OCHA oPt and within the framework of the wider development and humanitarian architecture. The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS) will be the partner accountable for completing data collection.  

The proposed MSNA will aim to achieve the following objectives:
1.	Directly inform joint humanitarian-development response planning based on the nexus approach that the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) has adopted for next year, through the provision of comprehensive, multi-sectoral household data. MSNA data will therefore aim to inform the development of both the 2022 HNO/HRP and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework planned for 2023-27;
2.	Provide a detailed inter-sectoral analysis of the magnitude and severity of humanitarian needs among crisis-affected populations in oPt, to support the calculation of sectoral and overall People in Need and severity calculations
3.	Provide a detailed vulnerability analysis to identify at-risk and ‘furthest left behind’ population groups, as well as geographic areas with the most acute needs and vulnerabilities, to subsequently inform assistance targeting and response planning efforts; and
4.	Support inclusive and people-centred assistance provision based on the principles of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), through the collection of information regarding preferred communication, information sharing, and assistance modalities.

REACH will produce the following key outputs: 1 household dataset; 1 static summary findings dashboard; series of presentations to key stakeholders; package of sectoral factsheets; and 1 final analytical report.

project_name: WASH Assistance To Enable Resilience II (WATER II)
project_objective:
The WATER project will provide approximately 450,000 vulnerable individuals with WASH assistance including 126,000 men, 126,000 women, 99,000 boys and 99,000 girls in areas of high WASH severity across the governorates of Homs, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Idlib, and Deir-ez-Zor. The project aims to provide both life-sustaining and life-saving WASH interventions for the most critically in need including IDPs, newly-returned returnees, and vulnerable conflict-affected hosting communities. Communities will be selected based on a detailed needs assessment and those with the highest need and underserved by the humanitarian community will be prioritized for assistance. Life-sustaining activities will include water/sewerage network rehabilitation in conflict-affected areas where access to household-level water is limited or where the sewerage system is damaged and poses a significant risk to the local population. Reverse Osmosis units will be provided to communities in East Ghouta with high levels of nitrate while debris removal will be conducted in areas where it poses a significant health and protection risk to the local population, with a focus on Deir-ez-Zor, Homs and Aleppo governorates. 
Life-saving activities will also be implemented to ensure immediate relief for vulnerable IDPs and returnees and those affected by the spread of COVID-19 including water tank distribution, and the provision of COVID-19 kits and cleaning kits for vulnerable families. 
The project will use a participatory and integrated approach ensuring that the needs of men, women, boys and girls are includeding from project design stage through to implementation and post-implementation monitoring of the works. Children, adolescents, young adults, middle-age adults and older adults will be solicited during the initial needs assessment for the project and post-implementation. Each age and gender group will have an opportunity to provide timely feedback to ADRA on the intervention through regular contact with ADRA monitoring staff. 
 The needs of young children, children, adolescents, young adults, middle-age adults and older adults will also be taken into consideration as children, adolescents, middle-age and older adults may require a higher amount of water for cleaning, cooking and for children who play outside and require more frequent hygiene practices.

project_name: Strengthening Health Cluster coordination to deliver quality emergency health action in Syria
project_objective:
The project will address human resources required for coordination and information management to enhance health sector coordination for equitable health response for people in need, with the emphasis on strengthening protection and increasing access to sustainable and resilient health services in Syria. It also covers the sustenance of health sector coordination mechanism at country and hub level.  The project will ensure effective and efficient carrying out of health coordination core functions. The cluster plays vital role in collecting, analysing the data and production of information products.  The main interventions of the cluster will be supporting service delivery to the people in need, mapping of partners presence (4Ws), information management, health needs assessment, informing strategic decision of HCT, developing HNO and HRP for the health sector, advocacy on behalf of cluster members, contingency planning, monitoring and reporting on monthly basis, and ensuring accountability to the affected population.
The cluster coordinate work of various technical working groups and task forces, including COVID-19, advocacy and communication, MHPSS, NCDs, trauma and disability, community health workers, dialysis, tuberculosis, referrals, sexual and reproductive health and health information systems. 
The project is aims to maintain coordination structures at Whole of Syria, central and hub levels.  Whole of Syria health cluster coordination plays a vital role in coordinating all the hubs and unifying and integrating the data and advocacy cross the hubs.  
The coordination structure exists at Whole of Syria, Damascus, Gaziantep and the hubs (Aleppo, Qamishli, Deir ez Zor, Homs and Lattakia).
The effective coordination at all levels will ensure quality delivery of health care to 12.4 million people in need of assistance in all the governorates.

project_name: Supporting food security and Livelihoods of vulnerable farmers, agro pastoral, pastoral and fisheries’ communities in Darfur, Blue Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan, Kassala, Red Sea, Gedarif, Sennar and White Nile States in Sudan
project_objective: The project objectives are considering the FSL Sector objectives and will provide immediate support to save lives and support vulnerable people to sustain their lives while building their reliance to withstand future stresses and shocks on the short and long term. This will have different strategic responses. The project interventions include addressing immediate lifesaving humanitarian needs as first top priority, through emergency agricultural assistance including crop, livestock and veterinary and fishery inputs and extension services targeting 2,350,000 people. This will include as well building the capacity of governmental institutions and sector partners to improve preparedness and response for new emergencies. The second priority is provide support for vulnerable people to restore and improve food and nutrition security and enhance self-reliance to cope with current and future shocks and stresses. Agricultural production will be improved through provision of climate-smart crop production, livestock and veterinary inputs and support to services. Similarly, small scale farmers will be targeted for reduced food losses and strengthened post-harvest techniques through improved food and crop storage and processing facilities. On and off farm livelihood assistance will be diversified and managed and coordinated to respond to food chain threats including animal and plant pests specially locust; In addition, communities will be involved in building, restoring and maintaining productive assets through cash and/or food for assets schemes. About 18,000 people will be targeted for cash transfer. Accountability to affected populations and environmental concerns will be mainstreamed into the proposed activities,  also risk to GBV will be taken into consideration and application of the PSEA measures in will be applied in collaboration with sister UN agencies.

project_name: Enhance food security through the delivery of an integrated assistance package for refugee and host community populations in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
WFP will provide life-saving food assistance to the entire Rohingya refugee population (approximately 860,000 people) through General Food Assistance. Beneficiaries will receive entitlements that can be redeemed from WFP-contracted local retailers across the camps. E-vouchers provide more flexibility, dignity and greater dietary diversity for the refugees while also creating market linkages with the host community and the wider Bangladeshi economy. To ensure an effective and efficient emergency intervention, WFP will preposition enough in-kind food to rapidly respond to the needs of approximately 13,000 households should they be displaced by monsoon, cyclone or conflict. 
In addition to providing large-scale food assistance, WFP makes sure to address the needs of the most vulnerable households through providing access to fresh food and promoting income generating activities in the camps and host communities. WFP will provide complementary food vouchers to 260,000 extremely vulnerable individuals through Fresh Food Corners and Farmers’ Markets. WFP will also engage 32,500 Rohingya refugee households in skills development training and provide inputs for mask making, sanitary pad production, homestead vegetable production, community aquaculture and the recently launched recycling project. In cooperation with the Government of Bangladesh, WFP will support 30,000 women with monthly subsistence allowance and business development support in Ukhiya and Teknaf.

project_name: ""Jiguitugu"": Porter assistance aux populations déplacées internes dans la région de Mopti
project_objective: L’action proposée vise à renforcer la protection des populations déplacées, réfugiées et des communautés hôtes affectées par le conflit intercommunautaire et l’insécurité dans la région de Mopti, en améliorant leur accès aux services de protection, en répondant à leurs besoins les plus urgents, et en soutenant les initiatives de réduction de risques de protection. Le projet ciblera certaines zones urbaines de la région (à Mopti/Sevare, Bankass, Koro et Douentza). Il contribuera à analyser l’évolution des besoins de protection et des risques affectant les populations déplacées et les communautés hôtes via un monitoring de protection constant, et à proposer une réponse d'urgence et adaptée (assistances individuelles de protection aux besoins assurée par des équipes spécialisées en PSP/PSS, avec un focus sur la PEC des groupes à vulnérabilités spécifiques (femmes et enfants). L'assistance sera déployée sur des zones où les services sont limités et souvent difficiles d’accès pour les personnes non-résidentes (ex: sites d'accueil spontanées, familles d'accueil). Cette action s’inscrit en synergie des priorités programmatiques du mécanisme RRM soutenu par ECHO et OFDA, et en complémentarité du projet de DRC cofinancé SDC/DANIDA et également déployé dans les cercles de Koro, Douentza, Bankass et Bandiagara. Le projet permet également de suivre / compléter la première prise en charge d’urgence menée par les partenaires du RRM, acteurs de protection ou les équipes de DRC, par une réponse de protection menée de manière suivie sur le moyen terme. L’analyse trimestrielle proposée par le projet permettra de mieux évaluer les besoins de protection des PDI, leurs évolutions, et les sites non-couverts; de plus, la composante de réponse du projet contribuera à apporter une réponse individuelle aux cas le nécessitant, atténuant ainsi les conséquences négatives des déplacements sur l’intégrité physique et psychologique des personnes concernées (réponse directe apportée par DRC, référencement). Enfin, cette action renforcera les liens programmatiques et stratégiques déjà existants entre les acteurs humanitaires, techniques et étatiques intervenant auprès des PDIS et communautés d'accueil ou hôte affectées par les déplacements, notamment en ce qui concerne le référencement mutuel des cas de protection (ex: cas d’enfants sans documentation civile vers NRC ; cas médicaux vers les CesRef/ CEScom ou autres acteurs de santé spécialisés, cas nécessitant une prise en charge psychosociale vers DRC etc). DRC contribuera également à renforcer les compétences des différents partenaires (membres du mécanisme RRM, services techniques, acteurs de la santé, et associations locales actives sur la réponse aux déplacements sur le centre du pays) en appui PSS et premiers secours psychologiques d’urgence . La redevabilité envers les personnes affectées sera garantie par la mise en place d'un mécanisme efficace de remontées de feedbacks et plaintes permettant de capitaliser sur les activités et en faire ressortir des leçons pour le futur.

project_name: Humanitarian assistance to 100,000 people (25,000 women, men 23,000, girls 25,500 and 26,500 boys) affected by conflict and disasters (38,000 in Central Equatoria, 31,000 Eastern Equatoria, and 31,000 in Jonglei States in 2021
project_objective: This project aims at providing life-saving frontline for most vulnerable population including IDPs and returnees with sufficient attention given to women, girls  and children,  by improving the living environment with provision of basic WASH services, reducing malnutrition cases  and mitigating GBV risks among IDPs, returnees and vulnerable hosting community residents in targeting Bor South, Pigi and Duk, Juba, Lainya, Yei,  Terekeka, Magwi, Torit and Ikotos Counties in the 3 states of Jonglei, Central and Eastern Equatoria States.

project_name: Installation of 10 mobile desalination units
project_objective: Installation of 10 mobile desalination units for brackish water by reverse osmosis in container with solar power that can be hybridized with thermal energy between 1,000 and 3,000 people depending on the flow rates.

project_name: Support for the population affected by the conflict in Eastern Ukraine (NGCA) in winter.
project_objective:
The project provides for the restoration of the thermal circuit of households affected by the fighting, through the repair of roofing.
It also provides for the provision of winter kits (NFI) to residents of villages and towns that were affected by the fighting.

project_name: Ensuring food security of population NGCA of Donetsk oblast during the COVID-19 pandemic
project_objective:
The project supposes assistance in providing food and goods necessary for agriculture, the population that has become vulnerable due to the ongoing military conflict, and the decline in economic indicators in the region. The economic and humanitarian situation in NGCA is also expected to worsen further as a result of additional COVID-19 restrictions.

Firstly, it is planned to promote the medical system by providing food vouchers to medical workers involved in the response to COVID-19. Taking into account the isolation of the local health system and the lack of qualified personnel, it is planned to provide resource support to medical workers in order to increase their motivation by providing vouchers of $ 100 for food products. Such assistance helps to maintain the health system's efficiency and will allow health workers who are engaged in a critical public service and receive an average of $ 80 to $ 200 to meet their food needs.

Secondly, support for the population that take care of themselves through agriculture: provision of feed, greenhouses, seeds, poultry and agricultural equipment, etc.to improve and stabilize them in winter, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic (increased isolation, loss of sources of income).

The results of the project are expected, firstly, to increase the sustainability of the local health system, reduce the outflow of doctors, due to the support of doctors responding to COVID-19; secondly, to increase food security due to resource assistance to households engaged in agriculture in the winter period.

project_name: Creating conditions for maintaining the centralized sewerage system in the city of Yenakievo and providing water supply to paramedic midwifery centers located in rural areas
project_objective:
The response capacity of communities living on NGCA to the threat of COVID-19 is reduced due to the humanitarian crisis, that has been ongoing for seventh year. The fighting, capital outflow and economic blockade of the region led to the desolation of WASH infrastructure. Protecting human health during outbreaks of infectious diseases, including coronavirus infection (COVID-19), requires the creation of safe sanitary and hygienic conditions and the supply of water. A significant contribution to the prevention of human-to-human transmission of COVID-19 virus infection will be made through consistent and evidence-based implementation of WASH and waste management practices at the community, household, and social institution levels.

The purpose of this project is, firstly, to provide sewer cleaning systems and personal protective equipment (protective suits, gloves, boots, glasses \ face shields and masks \ respirators) to housing and maintenance offices of the city of Yenakievo. This will allow the community to better service the sewer systems of their city, thereby reducing the likelihood of accidents, as well as significantly speed up the pace of their elimination, which directly affects the preservation of the city's sanitary and hygienic system.

Secondly, it is planned to provide access to water supply to paramedic and midwifery centers that provide basic medical services to rural residents. These institutions are extremely important for the population of villages remote from regional centers, they provide uninterrupted access to medical services. It is also planned to provide these points, their staff and visitors with disinfection products and PPEs in order to reduce the risk of the spread of COVID-19.

The project's beneficiaries will be 25,600 people, and USD will be required to meet these needs.

project_name: Program to support preschool institutions affected by the conflict in Eastern Ukraine (NGCA)
project_objective: The project presupposes the repair of preschool institutions (restoration of window and door blocks, restoration of roofs, restoration of WASH infrastructure, etc.). It also provides for the provision of these institutions with equipment, furniture, soft equipment and toys to improve the quality of services provided to children.

project_name: Providing grants of animal production and cultivation of vegetables in Al-Qusair and Tal- kalakh
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to support the ability of the population in Al-Qusair and Tal-Kalakh to withstand and live under the prevailing conditions through improve the economic situation of the population, and help them obtain income-generating sources through providing grants of animal production and cultivation of vegetables in Al-Qusair.

Al-Birr response is based on supporting the food security and agriculture in Al-Qusair and Tal kalakh through provide the livestock and agricultural grants that suit the nature of the region and the population, by two kinds of grants
one of them depends on providing 400 grants related to livestock to produce meat and milk by providing two sheep with its fodder for 6 months, utensils for animal feed, and periodic visits by veterinarians to supervise sheep health and treat them if needed. 

The other grant will be agricultural grants to 600 beneficiaries to support the agricultural production which includes tilling the farmlands of beneficiaries, providing seeds of vegetable for the cultivation, and trickle irrigation network to cultivation 1 donum, while the grants will be monitored by periodic visits by agricultural engineers to ensure that the grants are going well.

Al-Birr will monitor the project activities by two M&E staff to ensure that the project is on the right track and it is achieving its goals according to the specified indicators.

Al-Birr will conduct tenders to providing the inputs and items of the grants, to deliver them to the beneficiaries, so there are no cash transfers or e-vouchers to them.

project_name: Unconditional life-saving food assistance to vulnerable Libyans through in-kind & e-voucher transfers and through monthly general food assistance and one-off rapid responses
project_objective:
Provide Unconditional food assistance (in-kind or cash-based transfer) to crisis-affected vulnerable Libyan IDPs, returnees and non-displaced populations in the East, West, and South of Libya. 

WFP through local partners provides food assistance to food insecure and vulnerable people in Libya, including newly displaced persons through the inter-UN Rapid Response Mechanism. In 2020, WFP reached over 155,000 unique beneficiaries across all regions – 38 per cent more than the annual target, due to emergencies developing in Libya and increased socio-economic burden on people living with COVID-19 fears and restrictions necessitating unconditional food assistance to the increased number of vulnerable people in Libya. 

Prioritization exercises are applied to the project based on the duration of displacements, the assistance provided by local authorities or other food security sector members, and accessibility and the selection of assistance modalities was guided by protection risk assessments and quick needs assessments depending on whether populations had access to cooking facilities.

Under the 2021 HRP. WFP plans to prioritize its unconditional life-saving food assistance to a monthly average of 68,064 vulnerable Libyan, including those crisis-affected, IDPs, returnees, non-displaced populations. Apart from the monthly general food assistance, WFP will keep its capacities to respond to urgent food needs of 37,239 newly displaced persons through the emergency Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) implemented jointly by IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP (up to 20,000 beneficiaries) and WFP own emergency responses (up to 17,239 beneficiaries).

Beneficiaries themselves, as members of local crisis committees, are involved throughout the food distribution process. Targeting is implemented geographically, mainly based on the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment findings and household demographic characteristics such as gender, age group, and the presence of women, men, boys and girls living with disabilities as well as Household Food Consumption Scores.

The general food assistance (GFA) basket is designed to provide families with 30-day food entitlements covering 75 per cent of daily energy requirements per person per day; the basket included enriched pasta, fortified wheat flour, rice, white beans, tomato paste, fortified vegetable oil and sugar. WFP Libya has rolled out the commodity electric voucher to the general food assistance since April 2020. Under this project, 27% of the monthly general food assistance beneficiaries (18,666 beneficiaries in West and East) will receive their food entitlement via the commodity e-voucher. 100% of the Emergency Food Assistance will receive their food assistance through in-kind transfer. 

WFP will put its programmatic quality control and assurance measures in place, which include the following:
I) training of its Cooperating Partners and its own staff in cross-cutting issues such as gender, GBV, PSEA, Protection and Conflict Sensitivity; 
ii)	WFP’s output monitoring through the verification of distribution reports and spot-checks and WFP’s outcome monitoring through annual post-distribution monitoring; 
iii)	WFP’s distributions of leaflets and visibility materials to raise the awareness of participants and non-participants about the Common Feedback Mechanism.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire aux vulnérables (IDPs, retournés, personnes vivant avec handicap et autres déshérités ...) dans les provinces du Nord Est et de l'ouest particulièrement affectés par les chocs divers y compris l'impact socioéconomique de COVID 19
project_objective:
A travers ce projet , 737 000 personnes bénéficieront d'une assistance alimentaire non conditionnelle pour préserver leurs vies et pour leur éviter la dégradation de leur statut nutritionnel pendant la période cruciale de survenue de chocs. Le projet procédéra par un ciblage rigoureux pour éviter les erreurs d'inclusions et d'exclusions en érigeant des critères clairs et précis pour que l'assistance arrivent aux plus nécessiteux notamment les déplacés, les retournés, les vulnérables structurelles et autres déshérités affectés particulièrement affectés par les chocs.
Au delà de la survie, l'assistance veillera à une certaine synergie avec les autres interventions pour s'assurer de la remise sur pied des vulnérables assistés notamment en cherchant une complémentarité avec l'appui en restauration et protection des moyens d’existence perdus ou affaiblis à la suite des chocs.  

Le ciblage des bénéficiaires se fait à deux niveaux de priorisation à savoir : (1) par un ciblage géographique des zones prioritaires avec le ratio le plus élevé de personnes en situation de crise et d’urgence alimentaire (IPC phase 3 et 4)   (2) par un ciblage des catégories particulièrement exposées à l’insécurité alimentaire par manque de moyens d’existence consistants/durables à la suite d’un choc (y compris et en particulier de l’impact socio-économique de la Covid-19), de déplacements ou d’autres vulnérabilités (personnes vivant  avec handicap, les personnes âgées sans assistances, les femmes et enfants seuls et sans assistance, les sans-terre, les minorités ethniques, etc.).

Sur le plan géographique la priorité sera accordée aux provinces du nord-est, de l'est et de l’ouest où au moins un ménage sur cinq a besoin d’assistance alimentaire. Au niveau du ciblage des catégories les plus vulnérables, sur les 737 000 bénéficiaires bénéficiant de l’assistance sectorielle, les retournés représentent 24 pour cent, les PDI représentent 14 pour cent et les autres vulnérables dans la communauté hôte représentent 62 pour cent. Les vulnérables dans la communauté hôte comprennent ceux affectés par les chocs (inondations et glissements de terrain à l’ouest, le déficit hydrique à l’est au nord-est et à l’ouest, l’impact socio-économique de la Covid-19 surtout dans les zones frontalières avec la Tanzanie et la RDC, la chenille légionnaire d’automne (CLA), etc.) ainsi que les familles hôtes des retournés et les autres vulnérables structurels dans les zones de retours des réfugiés burundais.

project_name: Unconditional in-kind food assistance to 61,200 vulnerable CAR refugees in East, Adamaoua and North Region
project_objective: Through this project WFP will providing unconditional food support to 61,200 Central African refugees in the East regions. In line with WFP Cameroon Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2018-2020 extended to 2021), life-saving assistance will be provided CAR refugees in East. The transfer modality of food assistance to the beneficiaries will be a mix of in-kind distribution and cash-based transfers through unconditional monthly food distributions to support CAR refugees’ households’ access to adequate and nutritious food, therefore prevent them from adopting negative coping practices. The daily food rations will comprise 350g cereals, 100g pulses, 35g vegetable, and 5g salt to cover their needs of 2,100 kcal energy per day per person for the beneficiaries who entirely rely on humanitarian food assistance.
