project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services in Sudan
project_objective:
According to the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) some 12.3 million people  will need humanitarian assistance in 2021. 
While incidents of fighting have reduced considerably in recent years, the situation of people displaced due to decades of conflict remains unresolved. Some 2.5 million IDPs and 1.1 million refugees and asylum seekers continue to need humanitarian assistance and protection support, both in camps and host communities. Pockets of armed conflict continue in Darfur, and sporadic inter-communal conflicts also continue. In neighbouring Central African Republic (CAR), ongoing intercommunal conflicts have escalated since June 2019, with reports indicating large populations of internally displaced populations along the border with Sudan, near Central and South Darfur, which are anticipated to continue into 2021.
Across Sudan, basic services are lacking, and natural disasters, like floods, affect people each year. But it is a deepening economic crisis, following years of stagnation and little investment in already-weak public services, that is driving worsening food insecurity, deteriorating healthcare, and other needs across Sudan. While the transitional government is committed to stemming the economic crisis, reforms may involve subsidy cuts which could have a further impact on families who are already struggling to cope. Basic service provision, already weak and underdeveloped, has been dangerously degraded by the economic crisis. This has affected people directly, impacting households’ ability to buy food and cover basic needs. It has also deepened already existing needs – including among existing vulnerable groups like displaced people, returnees, and refugees – and may cause new people to fall into humanitarian need

project_name: Fortalecer a nivel operativo y estratégico la coordinación humanitaria y abogacía en Venezuela
project_objective:
En 2021, OCHA en Venezuela continuará reforzando las estructuras de coordinación (Equipo Humanitario de País –EHP-, Grupo Inter cluster, cuatro centros de coordinación de terreno y grupos de trabajo temáticos, incluyendo CASH, gestión de la información –GTMI-, Comunicación Humanitaria, rendición de cuentas ante las poblaciones afectadas –AAP- y la red de puntos focales de protección contra la explotación y abusos sexuales -PEAS). Para la implementación del Ciclo de Programa Humanitario 2021 (HPC), OCHA apoyará las evaluaciones y el monitoreo de las necesidades en el terreno; facilitará la identificación conjunta de las prioridades de respuesta y el monitoreo regular de la respuesta; y contribuirá a mejorar la comunicación conjunta sobre la situación general, incluyendo avances y retos en la respuesta humanitaria. OCHA planea expandir aún más su abogacía para facilitar el acceso a las áreas más vulnerables y movilizar más fondos para la respuesta.

Para apoyar las capacidades operativas de los diferentes actores humanitarios y promover el respeto por los principios humanitarios, OCHA con el apoyo de otras organizaciones, ofrecerá formaciones e iniciativas de desarrollo de capacidades sobre los principios humanitarios, la coordinación humanitaria, la coordinación civil-militar, herramientas de gestión de la información, metodologías para la evaluación de necesidades, el HPC y temas transversales como AAP, PEAS y género.

Las prioridades dentro de la estrategia de OCHA Venezuela para 2021 son:
-	Mejorar el panorama conjunto de la comunidad humanitaria sobre las necesidades humanitarias, mediante el monitoreo de necesidades y evaluaciones periódicas, que facilite la priorización de las actividades humanitarias.
-	Fortalecer el sistema de monitoreo del HRP y publicar productos regulares sobre los avances y retos de la respuesta.
-	Fortalecer los foros de coordinación para alcanzar una respuesta humanitaria oportuna, efectiva y basada en los principios humanitarios.
-	Desarrollar la capacidad de los socios humanitarios para participar de manera efectiva en el HPC y proporcionar una respuesta más efectiva.
-	Fortalecer la comunicación humanitaria, para mejorar la comprensión de los principios humanitarios, los logros de la respuesta y la aceptación de las organizaciones humanitarias.
-	Fortalecer los centros de coordinación en terreno, para asegurar que cubran efectivamente su área geográfica, mejorando las capacidades de evaluación, respuesta y monitoreo y la coordinación con los socios y partes interesadas.
-	Acoger al clúster de Logistica, para fortalecer la coordinación entre los socios, el intercambio de informaciones puntuales sobre temas logísticos, apoyar la abogacía con las contrapartes institucionales, y promover soluciones conjuntas para mejorar la capacitad operacional y de respuesta.
-	Contribuir al aumento del nivel de apoyo financiero proporcionado por los donantes.
-	Mejorar el diálogo con todas las partes interesadas, incluyendo autoridades civiles y militares, para facilitar la aceptación y el acceso.

project_name: Humanitarian Field Officers
project_objective:
This project will support cross-border operations from Turkey into Syria to tap into sources of information and share it for use by the humanitarian community through a team of humanitarian field officers in NSAG-controlled areas. The team will be managed by the HFOs management team based in Gaziantep, Turkey in consultation with OCHA Turkey. The project is designed to broadly support the formal coordination system, especially the clusters/ICCG, as It is based on four pillars.

1-Information gathering
This pillar focuses on gathering data from the ground to produce reports about the humanitarian situation and context and inform response and advocacy. The data is shared with the OCHA coordination unit for use in various platforms and products. Info on unmet needs, including urgent cases, will be shared with clusters to address
2-Support to monitoring of SCHF funded projects.
The HFOs will monitor projects funded by the SCHF. These monitoring missions will be conducted upon the request of the SCHF and based on SCHF monitoring criteria. Monitoring of SCHF projects directly improves the quality and accountability of the inter-cluster response, as projects funded by the SCHF are reviewed through the clusters. The HFAs will also receive a training on M&E tools and methods to ensure accurate and relevant information are gathered by them.

3-Community Engagement
The HFOs will conduct community engagement to strengthen humanitarian response through facilitating meetings with the affected community and the humanitarian community and other stakeholders; obtaining feedback from the community on their needs and the response; and providing information to affected people through awareness sessions and other means on the humanitarian response and the community’s rights and role in it. Community engagement informs the overall inter-cluster response and in some cases is organized on behalf of clusters.

4-Service Mapping
The existing service map app for mobile phones will get an upgrade to ensure ease of use and better accessibility such as “text-to-speech” for visually impaired people, and more visually-illustrated materials to assist people with reading/writing difficulties. The app will include a virtual information center that will 1)work as an awareness platform disseminating information on key issues such as AAP, COVID-19, and CHS  2)create an accessible repository of information for all affected persons and humanitarian actors to receive support and information to avoid duplication. 

The project builds on the outcomes of a previous project completed earlier in 2021. The information-gathering component is well-established and in recent months the mechanism for sharing specific needs data with clusters was streamlined and has resulted in individual cases receiving assistance. SCHF monitoring activities carried out so far have been well-received, resulting in one of the HFOs becoming largely dedicated to this work and the processes for monitoring becoming more formalized which will be further enhanced. Direct engagement with communities facilitated by the HFOs has allowed senior leadership, including the ERC, to provide high-level advocacy from key constituencies including women and PWDs. The service map app is now available in four languages and hosts over than 2,600 distributed between medical, educational emergency, and other types of services. It is also hosting ads from humanitarian actors, and hundreds of people have registered seeking for training. The app has been well received by people in need, clusters, and other stakeholders. Building on this success, B&Z is planning to conduct a promotion campaign to promote the service map application to ensure it is used by the relevant stakeholders as much as possible. A handover plan will also be set to shift the support of the app to another donor to ensure its sustainability.

project_name: Assistance aux populations vulnérables affectées par la crise humanitaire dans les provinces du Bam et du Gourma
project_objective:
Welthungerhilfe, propose une intervention ciblée ayant pour objectif principal de contirbuer à l'amélioration des conditions de vie des populations les plus vulnérables avec une réponse intégrant trois secteurs d'intervention : La sécurité alimentaire, la nutrition, et l'eau, hygiène et assainissement.
OS1 : La relance des moyens de d'existence adapté au climat est assurée.
OS2 : Prévenir, en colaboration avec les districts sanitaire, l'augmentation des taux de malnutrition des FEFA et enfants<5ans ainsi que la mortalité et la morbidité associés
OS3 : Prévenir, avec des interventions en eau, hygiène et assainisement, les risques de malnutritions et des maladies associées.
WHH porte une attention particulière aux groupes nécessistant un appui spécifique ou de protection : filles / femmes soumises à des pressions familiales et sociales fortes, voient leur études réduites et devant faire face à une charge de travail plus importante, auquel vient s'ajouter le risque plus élevé de perte de vie ou d'être victime de violence et d'exploitation sexuelle, les garçons / hommes dont les attentes sociales sotn également fortes, pouvant avoir des comportements plus à risque pour subvenir aux besoins de leur famille et se voient assumer de nouveaux rôles en temps de crise, ils bénéficient généralement de très peu de soutien en cas d'abus sexuel, les personnes âgés pouvant souffrir d'isolement, de problème de santé et voient leur stratégie de subsistance perturbées, les personnes vivants avec un handicap, ont plus de difficultés à accèder à l'assistance et aux infrastructures de base, ont moins d'accès à l'information et ont une grande dépendance, ils sont souvent stigmatisés, risquent d'isolement et manque d'inclusion.
WHH intègre la protection transversale en consultant les différents groupes de personnes, en répondant à leur besoins spécifiques, en mettant ces populations au centre dela réponse et en les impliquant dans les différentes activités en fonction de leurs capacités ainsi qu'en tenant compte des rôles et dynamiques de pouvoir en cherchant à réduire les barrières sociales liées au genre et à la discrimination.
WHH intègre également la participation et la redevabilité dans les différentes phases du cycle de projet. Les représentants des communautés feront partie du mécanisme de redevabilité en collectant les feedbacks et les plaintes. Des comités au niveau de chauque commune d'intervention seront directement en liaison avec le responsable de la redevabilité auprès du bureau pays de WHH. Des réunions périodiques seront instaurées avec les autorités locales, les services techniques décentralisés et les représentants des bénéficiares pour la restitution des réalisations du projet et les avancements relatifs aux différentes plaintes et recommendations reçues de la part des communautés.
Ces stratégies de cohésion sociale, de protection transversales et de participation des acteurs permettrons de réduire les risques et d'améliorer la qualité de la réponse humanitaire en tenant compte du principe de Do No Arm.
Dans le cadre du Nexus, WHH se coordonne tant avec les acteurs d'urgence que de Développement.

project_name: Improving Access to equitable Health care to the Internally Displaced Populations of the North and South West regions of Cameroon
project_objective: The North West and South West regions of Cameroon are affected by a complex humanitarian crisis that has resulted in system wide breakdown of infrastructure and services especially in the health sector. MSNA data from August 2020 estimate that 269 out of 933 (29 percent) health centers are no longer functional. Likewise, with attacks targeting health personnel and destructing medical equipment, the technical capacity and availability of staff to work in these areas is very low.  The two regions lack emergency medical and psychological units, necessary to provide emergency surgical management of those wounded and to provide psychiatric and psychosocial support to those traumatized by the violence. Finally, the incidence of rape increased dramatically in North-West and South-West regions with 490 cases reported in 2020 compared to 17 in 2019. This situation has been worsened by the COVID-19 Pandemic which has increased the burden on a health system that has already been fragilized by the humanitarian crisis.  In the most of affected areas, health services are not available while less affected areas have health services of poor quality. The present project aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality of internal displaced population (IDP) in the North West and South West regions of Cameroon affected by the humanitarian crisis by ensuring a timely and equitable access to health care services. The project will target 473,069 IDPs members of host communities (51% of this target are women, 16% are children under 5, and 11% are people over 60 years old). The areas of intervention will be Fako, Meme, Manyu, Ndian and Kupe - Muanenguba divisions in the South-West, Mezam, Momo, Bui, Ngo-ketunjia and Boyo in the North-West region, Mungo and Wouri in the Littoral region and in the West region, Menoua, Mifi, Ndé and Noun divisions. The project will emphasize on timely access to equitable health care for men and women (taking into consideration the distance to the closest health facilities for women, children under 5 and people above 60) and quality of interventions (assistance by skilled attendant, referral of cases).

project_name: Provision of Emergency Health Services for The Populations in Need
project_objective:
A total of 3864 confirmed COVID-19 cases including 104 deaths reported in Somalia (10 Oct 2020), with the majority from Banadir, Somaliland and Puntland. Since the first case reported, WHO Somalia is supporting the MoH responding to the outbreak through coordination, technical support; procurement & distribution of PPEs, medicine, medical equipment; establishing four PCR laboratories; epidemiological data collection, analysis and regular information sharing for evidence-based decision making to guide the response activities. 
Currently the most affected areas by Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD)/cholera include 23 flood affected districts of Hirshabelle, South-West states and Banadir region. Since January 2020, a total of 5,872 AWD/Cholera cases were reported, including 30 deaths (CFR 0.5%) in 23 flood-affected districts. Of the 5,872 cases, 2,584 (44%) are children aged below 2 years while  3,288 (56%) are female and 2,584 (44%) males. In Banadir alone, 3,374 cases, including 19 deaths, have been reported. In Baidoa, a total of 680 cases with 3 deaths have been reported amongst displaced communities since April 2020.
Since onset of the pandemic, EPI program is one of the worst affected among the health programs. There is a drop both in number and proportion of children immunized in 2020 compared to the previous year. Over the period of January to September 2020, Penta 3 and Measles vaccination coverage have reduced by approximately 10%-12%. This growing number of un-immunized children poses a greater risk of vaccine preventable disease (VPD) outbreak. As an example, an increased number of suspected measles cases (296 cases during the period of epi week 27 to 35) mostly from the IDPs were reported from Kismayo. 
Mental health remains unprioritized and a significant public health challenge. One in every three people in Somalia have experienced some kind of mental health illness  and 2.8 millon people are in stress among the IDPs . Only 4 hospitals in Somalia provide basic mental health services with limited integration of MH services by the PHC providers.
The project aims to provide increased access to life-saving essential health services to the most vulnerable communities in Somalia across all the states, with the focus on mitigating the negative health consequence of recurrent flooding, locust infestation, COVID-19 pandemic and communicable disease outbreaks in Somalia. Through this project WHO will continue to advocate for equity and to ensure access for the people living with disabilities.

The WHO Somalia HRP 2021 will focus in 51 high risk districts on the following strategic and specific objectives: 
1.	To strengthen integrated community based disease surveillance and response network
•	To build capacity of the community health workers in integrated disease surveillance and response 
•	To strengthen the reporting network through real-time /online platform for immediate follow up and actions. 
•	To increase community awareness in responding to a disease by accepting and practicing the mitigation measures
2.	To prevent and control the communicable disease outbreaks
•	To increase the preparedness and response capacity of the health facilities responding to the communicable disease outbreak
•	To increase the capacity of health care workers on case investigation and integrated management of outbreak prone diseases 
•	To increase the EPI coverage among the vulnerable population
•	To promote public health prevention measures including improved hygiene practice, safe water and sanitation 
3.    To provide Mental Health and Psychosocial Support
•	To advocate for mental health services including de-stigmatization and inclusion of population with psychosocial disabilities during any emergencies
•	To increase the capacity of health care workers, and the health system to offer appropriate psychosocial support
•	To deliver adequate psychosocial support at all level of health care delivery platforms

project_name: Support to vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host families to Improve their food security, economic and social well-being in Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga, Logone and Chari.
project_objective:
The purpose of the project is to improve food security, economic and social well-being of vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host families in the target area. 
NRC Cameroon’s Livelihood and Food Security (LFS) programme will target displacement-affected people based on vulnerability criteria and not their displacement status only (out-of-camp refugees, IDPs, returnees (former IDPs, and host communities). NRC will apply social and economic vulnerability criteria to identify vulnerable households most at risk to food insecurity. The social vulnerability criteria applied will include female-headed households, child-headed households; households, pregnant and breastfeeding women; elderly people (60 and above); households with a person with physical or mental disability or debilitating chronic disease. For the economic vulnerability criteria, NRC will use as a reference: poor or limited food consumption score; no food stock, number of meals per day, no productive assets, and loss of income. For agricultural restoration activities, NRC will also include the following criteria: having at least one able-bodied person in the household who can farm land. NRC’s LFS programmes will also target as far as possible vulnerable youth and women for vocational training and economic empowerment. 
To address the intermediate needs of affected populations NRC will use cash, vouchers or in-kind assistance based on the results of market analysis and cash feasibility studies. To maximise the chances of success in this activity, NRC will as far as possible couple livelihoods interventions with food assistance to meet basic food needs. Moreover, NRC will implement complementary activities such as training and awareness raising sessions to support target households. Programme activities will gradually scale down and phase out so that by the end of the projects, communities have the skills and resources needed to be more resilient to shocks and crises in the medium and long term. NRC will work in coordination with local partners such as local technical and administrative structures and will collaborate closely with them so they can provide technical support during programme implementation and continued follow-up after the programme ends. 
The LFS programme will include cash assistance, livelihoods promotion and enhancement applying a market-based approach (MBA) that refers to local traders so to improve access to income and revive/strengthen the local economy. The intervention will be geared towards supporting the most vulnerable displacement-affected households and at the same time building their capacity in food production, food transformation and marketing.

project_name: SCI Children’s Emergency Seed Fund
project_objective:
This CSF allocation will be used to scale up our response in Arauca and Valle del Cauca. The allocation will be used to cover a small percentage of technical staff time (CP Technical Advisor and MHPSS Technical Advisor) to train or build staff capacity. CSF allocation will also be used to purchase protective PPE equipment for key response office staff to maintain staff safety and comply with biosecurity protocols for the COVID-19 pandemic. Supplies, transport and implementation (capacity building, planning and strategy activities) will also be provided.

With regards to Programme Activities, CSF allocation will be used to implement the following activities:
1.	Perform a conflict sensitivity needs analysis – CSF funds will be used to work with a Colombian think-tank Fundación Ideas para la Paz specialised in conflict analysis to support conflict sensitivity analysis and interview key stakeholders. This analysis will support us to better understand our context, anticipate and plan for future events, and ensure our response strategy adequately and appropriately addresses the needs of affected boys, girls and families.
2.	Emergency assistance for displaced families – CSF funds will be used to scale up emergency response to purchase emergency shelter and family hygiene kits to meet the immediate needs of displaced families and vulnerable families affected by conflict. Project assistants will also provide immediate Psychosocial First Aid to displaced boys, girls and families.
3.	Child Protection awareness-raising activities in communities– As part of an integrated Education and Child Protection response, CSF funds will be used to raise awareness of Child Protection risks (with a particular focus on recruitment and use of children including sexual exploitation) amongst boys, girls, parents, caregivers and community members and relevant CP referral pathways. CSF funds will be used to purchase material for these activities (including printing of relevant information in accessible and friendly language and local radio campaigns). Early activities will focus on Arauca and Valle del Cauca targeting internally displaced Colombian populations and irregular Venezuelan migrant populations who are often most at-risk from recruitment, use and/or sexual exploitation by non-state armed actors. SC Colombia field offices which will be involved in these early activities will be: Arauca (Arauca) and Cali (Valle del Cauca).

project_name: Integrated Protection and GBV Assistance for Returnees , IDPs and host community in South Darfur , Blue Nile , East Farfur  and South Kordofan
project_objective: This project aims at providing immediate life saving protection and GBV assistance to vulnerable 68363 Women, Men, Boys and girls mostly IDPs, Returnees and host communities in four states of South and East Darfur, South Kordofan and Blue Nile. The Project intervention will target the most vulnerable population through provision of IGA, Construction of Women and Girls safe spaces/ Community multipurose centers, capacity building  and awareness campaigns on SGBV, Child protection activities such as FTR to respond to unaccompanied and Separated children. Case management will be done at community centers. Community based child protection mechanisms will be established and their capacity enhanced to respond to SGBV and child protection issues while improving the household income through IGAs and lifeskills development.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Humanitarian Response to the Rohingya and Host Community Population in Cox’s Bazar. Delivering Health, Nutrition and Livelihood, and Protection services for Rohingya Refugees and vulnerable host communities in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh.
project_objective:
The project aims to improve dietary diversity at household level and particularly targeting those households with pregnant and lactating women and children under 2 years, older people over 60 years, people with disabilities and female-headed households, in Rohingya Refugees and host communities through home gardening and provision of poultry. Households with children under two and PLW are targeted because these population groups have increased nutrition needs. In addition households with limited livelihood options such as the elderly, women headed households and people living with disabilities will be targeted. Supporting home gardens and small livestock will ensure that households have improved access to diversified nutritious diets. 
The project has a SBCC component to increase knowledge on nutrition and improved MIYCF practices. The project will support awareness sessions with pregnant and lactating women, husbands and mother in laws of Mother Care Group members to assist them for IYCF activities and practices. Furthermore, caregivers (mothers and fathers) who specific challenges with IYCF will be identified and referred for individual one to one counselling on IYCF.
In the project areas, Concern will institute a strong system to accountability to affected population (AAP), during the startup phase Concern will give information to project beneficiaries, provide channels for beneficiaries to provide feedback on project activities. During implementation, participatory methodologies will be used including focus group discussions with the different populations groups. 
 To ensure that communities are resilience sustainable activities such as gardening, livestock rearing will ensure that communities are prepared for any shocks. Key information on monsoon will be shared with the communities for them to be ready and prepared. This project will be implemented within the sector guidelines and reports and program updates will be shared with the nutrition sector to ensure there will be no duplication of activities with other partners. Concern Worldwide have a contingency plan for each of the project activities. When any disaster happen Concern will continue support to the beneficiaries.

project_name: Improved food security and dietary diversity of vulnerable conflict affected and food insecure populations
project_objective:
Although the formation of transitional government of national unity in February 2020 resulted in improved security however the subsequent shocks including COVID-19, flooding, inter-communal violence and political conflict in part of country continue to exacerbate the already fragile humanitarian context in South Sudan. The livelihood and food insecurity was prompted by years of conflict, climate shocks, wrecked economy and extreme poverty. According to the IPC situation analysis released on 18, December 2020, an estimated 6.35 million people (52.6% of the population) faced Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worst acute food insecurity, over two million faced Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and 24,000 people were likely in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5). The projection for the lean session estimate that over 60% of population will likely to be in IPC Phase 3 or worse.

The proposed FSL interventions aim to improve food production, strengthen the household’s ability to enhance their productive assets, create livelihood opportunities, build resilience and contribute toward overall improved nutrition status of the affected communities. Concern will support vulnerable IDP, returnee and host community households with emergency access to agricultural and fishing inputs to improve food production and access to nutritious foods. In Aweil West and Aweil North, NBeG, Concern will continue to provide access to seeds, agriculture tools and crop production through block farming as well as technical support and training on seed multiplication and seed saving. Community Agricultural Extension Workers and lead farmers will be supported to train vulnerable farmers on Climate Smart Agriculture, bio-pesticide production and post-harvest handling. Concern will support dry season vegetable production to support income generation opportunities and access to nutritious foods. In Juba IDP camp and Bentiu PoC, Concern will build on its approach of nutrition gardens to support improving dietary diversity through training lead mothers on sack gardening where space is limited in IDP/PoC sites and they will train Mother-to-Mother Support Groups. Focus will be on households with members in OTP and TSFP. In Rubkona and Guit, Concern having supported vegetable gardens to improve access to nutritious foods will expand its FSL interventions considering the gaps in FSL support and most of the population being dependent on food assistance. Vegetable production and fishing will be supported to provide income generation opportunities and increase dietary diversity. Considering asset depletion, crop losses due to flooding, inflation and limited access to livelihood, hunger  is expected to deepen due mainly to depleted food stocks and high food prices therefore Concern in partnership with WFP in NBeG continue to provide emergency food assistance through General Food Distribution, School Feeding Program and Cash/Food for Asset program.

project_name: Improving access to inclusive and quality primary education in protective and inclusive learning environments for children in the Far North region, Cameroon.
project_objective:
The project “Improving access to inclusive and quality primary education in protective and inclusive learning environments for children in the Far North region, Cameroon” is proposed to support children out of school and those at risk of dropping out as a direct result of the attacks on education (children, teachers, parents, school infrastructure, etc.) and insecurity. The actions will focus on creating and maintaining the protective learning environment for children and teachers, as well as strengthening their knowledge and skills cope with threats and attacks; special focus will also be put on developing and expanding relevant non-formal and informal education opportunities for the adolescents. Cash transfer as a modality will also be applied to support parents and communities in enrolling and retaining their children in school and learning centers. 
The project will target children, girls and boys (3-18 years) affected by the crisis in the Far-North Region, particularly in Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga and Logone-and-Chari divisions.
This project is designed to carry out activities in collaboration with the Ministry of Basic Education aimed at ameliorating the situation of children with focus on education in emergencies.  
Equitable access to safe and protective learning environments shall be facilitated through the Construction (classrooms, latrines and water points), school facilities built and used by all students, girls and boys, including children living with disabilities.
Access to quality alternative education adapted to the needs of girls and boys (3-18 years old) who are out of school because of the crisis shall be reinforced through learning or training activities.
Rights of girls and boys shall be protected from immediate and future threats through access to conflict-sensitive education, disaster and conflict risk reduction, strengthening psychosocial coping and protecting schools from attack.

project_name: Emergency lifesaving interventions for most vulnerable affected populations in IPC phase 4 and 5 to meet food and livelihoods needs
project_objective:
The proposed HRP 2021 intervention will target locations with IPC 4 and 5 with emergency food security and livelihoods assistance for the most vulnerable populations affected by shocks including floods and conflict, which has contributed to the elevation of food security outcomes to include Famine Likely. The convergence of shocks including floods, conflict and hyperinflation of prices for basic commodities compounded with the social and economic impacts of COVID-19 have increased the population's vulnerability deepening the humanitarian situation. The proposed interventions are aligned to cluster objectives 1: Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations (in IPC 5, 4 & some 3 and 2), and 2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support. The delivery of the assistance will be via two modalities (IRRM and static operations) in the proposed locations: Jonglei (Akobo, Nyirol) and Greater Pibor Administrative areas (Pibor). 

With the impact of interwoven shocks, the population of South Sudan is in dire support of humanitarian assistance. Years of conflict have ravaged the country and the population's resilience capacity to withstand shocks without humanitarian assistance has been depleted. As a consequence of the conflict, there are multi-dimensional outcomes which have aggravated the suffering of the most vulnerable households and communities, who have been exposed to recurrent inter-communal violence due to a security vacuum, limited access to food due to reduced farming capacity as a result of displacement and depleted households farming inputs (seeds). The prices of commodities have skyrocketed due to devaluation of the local currency and limited flow of supplies due to insecurity as well as physical inaccessibility resulting from poor road networks. The proposed HRP project is designed to ensure the most vulnerable households have access to immediate food and livelihood assistance to avert the worsening food security outcomes in IPC phase 4 and 5. The proposed interventions will focus on livelihoods assistance and access to food. Livelihood assistance will be implemented for the main season and dry season to ensure continuous production of food at household level, to enable vulnerable households and communities meet their dietary needs. The proposed activities are designed to achieve the objectives of the HRP 2021. The interventions will integrate safe programming principles of Do No Harm, COVID-19 SOPs, and ensure Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP). 

The project will be implemented by Oxfam directly but in close coordination with key Clusters, including FSL cluster, TWGs AAP and partners operational in targeted project locations. At field level, the coordination will be with county line departments of agriculture and fisheries and other stakeholders. This coordination will be of essential importance to ensure that the project delivery consistent with AAP principles, avoidance of duplication of exclusion of vulnerable communities. The project will pay attentions to other cross cutting issues in delivery of the assistance such as safe programming with Do No Harm lenses, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, inclusion of other groups such as disability and conflict sensitive programming.

project_name: Amelioration de  l'acces  a l'education et a  la formation professionnelle des enfants, jeunes et des femmes  vulnerables  des regions de Tahoua et Maradi
project_objective:
Ce projet vise d'une part,  a améliorer l’Environnement d’apprentissage sûrs et protecteur pour  15 360  enfants  dont  7680 filles et garçons, 645 handicapes  affectés par les crises humanitaires  pour leur bien-être physique et psychosocial  et d'autre part a renforcer la  résilience des écoles, enfants, et des communautés à travers le développement des plans de préparation et de réponses aux risques conjointement élaborés par la communauté éducatives (élèves, enseignants, CGDES) dans les regions de Maradi et Tahoua.  il s'agira aussi de promouvoir l’accès à des offres innovantes  d’éducation inclusive et de qualité pour les garçons et filles de 4 à 17 ans affectés par les crises avec un accent particulier sur le développement professionnel de 307 enseignants retournés, déplacés et réfugiés dans les 51 ecoles ou  centres de regroupement des ecoles.
La reponse aux besoins de ces   15 360  enfants filles et garcons, 307 enseignantes et enseignants,  familles  touchees par les  differentes crises securiatires et sanitaires se  fera en terme  d'appui en infrastrures d'acces,  mobiles ou fixes,  par l'amelioration de l'environnement d'apprentissage sur, invclusif, securisant et portecteur qui favorise la protection et le bien-être congnitif, emotionnel et psychosocial des apprenants, particulierement les filles,  des enseignants et des autres personnels de l'education. Une place de choix sera accordee a la formation des eneignants, la  gestion des risques et de catastrophe par la mise en place des plans de prévention, de préparation et de réponse aux risques de catastrophes et de conflits armés et de la COVID 19, soutien  aux familles vunerables surtout les femmes. Enfin, le projet appuyera les centres de regoupement des ecoles pour leur assurer les minmums de conditions d'ensEIgnement et d'apprntissage et leur  suivi par les encadreurs pedagogiaues.

project_name: Emergency Child Protection, GBV & Mine Action: Prevention, Mitigation & Response in Conflict-Affected & High Risk Areas of South Sudan in 2021
project_objective:
The integrated CP. GBV and MRE project is in line with the Protection Cluster Objectives, the project will ensure provision of critical protection-related assistance and specialized services; and prevent and mitigate Protection risks through enhanced preparedness. The project targets to reach an average of 60,000 (CP), 10,000 (GBV) and 8,600 (MRA) boys and girls and their 1200 caregivers.  The project will also engage 90,000 individuals (30,000 boys and 25,000 girls, each, and 20,000 men and 15,000women) in awareness raising meetings focused on CP, MRA and GBV, in partnership with the CP community structures.
The CP component aspires to enhance access to comprehensive case management services for vulnerable girls and boys with protection concerns such as UASC; provide vulnerable girls and boys, their caregivers and families, with quality age and gender-appropriate PSS, following community-based approaches and best practices, and strengthen capacity of girls and boys, their caregivers, families, and communities, to prevent and respond to violence through systems and community-strengthening mechanisms; FTR of UASC and placement in alternative care within framework of comprehensive case management, referrals to specialized services);  focused PSS for CAAFAG capacity building of CP staff, frontline workers, teachers,  government/local authorities in CPiE; strengthening CBCPCS  and case management (identification & documentation of children with protection concerns, case management capacity building) – reflecting the Child Protection Sub Cluster’s overall strategy and objectives.  
For GBV, the project will strengthen life-saving assistance meeting the unique and unmet needs of child survivors, specifically adolescent girls, and engaging male/female youth and adolescents in GBV prevention. The project will include the following key interventions in all locations, based on specific assessed need, disaggregated by sex and age: GBV case management; provision of PSS; safe referrals (medial, legal, livelihood, other); provision of legal advice to survivors; GBV information management; engagement of and advocacy to police and justice actors (formal and traditional) to strengthen access to justice; monitoring of GBV risks for prevention/mitigation through safety audit & safety perception mapping; community engagement interventions to prevent and respond to GBV such as establishment of Women & Girl Safe Spaces & comprehensive programming per the WGSS South Sudan Guidelines; establishment/strengthening of community based protection/GBV structures and systems including women’s groups; community based advocacy and awareness raising, especially engaging male/female youth as change agents in adoption of positive masculinities, respect for women and girls’ equal rights, ending of social acceptance of violence (especially sexual/physical violence) and positive attitudes/behaviours that promote the end of GBV.
The project will also implement MRE activities, according to IMAS, NTSG, World Vision approved MRE SOPs and in alignment with the MASC – MRE Working Group and South Sudan National Mine Action Strategy 2018-2021: Training and accreditation of MRE Teams through approved third-party trainer/training programme; MRE Assessment; Community engagement / mobilization of women, girls, men and boys; Provision of integrated MRE and Community Liaison, linked with Child Protection and Education to particularly reach girls and boys in and out of school, and facilitate integration of MRE in schools; Use of approved/standard MRE materials (i.e. banners, leaflets, warning signs, etc) and age-appropriate/gender-sensitive means of communication; Use of all IMSMA tools and forms for complete and timely information management/reporting per SOPs; Implementation of Quality Monitoring System including Quality Assurance (internal, external) and Quality Controls; Advocacy to greater prioritize MRE as a life-saving humanitarian intervention, especially for children.

project_name: UNHCR Multi-Sectoral Project in Libya
Provision of lifesaving integrated primary health services; prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks among the vulnerable populations in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The project aims to contribute to the reduction of excess morbidity and mortality resulting from common
infectious diseases, vector-borne diseases, and epidemic-prone diseases because of multiple shocks (effects of Covid-19 restrictions, economic crisis and high food
prices, impact of flooding on livelihood, and sub-national violence) among the vulnerable populations in South Sudan. This aim will be obtained through the provision of time-critical, life-saving frontline quality health services, capacity building of health care workers, and strengthening of disease surveillance systems in targeted locations. The WHO emergency Mobile Medical Team (eMMT) provides integrated health services in deep field locations through mobile medical outreach modality. The eMMT comprise of experts from different fields of medicine often deployed strategically to provide gap-filling services in areas with serious unmet health needs. Such areas may include locations without static health facilities or those with no active health partners, locations with access constraints and those receiving high numbers of returnees, IDPs or refugees. The mobile clinics will offer outpatient consultations for common conditions, minor procedures, screening and treatment for malnutrition, immunization services, and referral services. Besides, WHO will train community health care workers to ensure continuity of health service provision in targeted locations. Rapid assessments will be conducted to identify the unmet health needs in project locations. meanwhile, the Rapid Response Teams (RRT) will be deployed alongside the eMMTs to conduct case verification and investigation of suspected disease outbreaks. In addition,
WHO will enhance capacity for disease surveillance and reporting to enhance detection of epidemic-prone diseases and continue to provide timely technical support for appropriate response by the Ministry of Health and other health partners.
The routine surveillance system will be enhanced through the deployment of mobile phone-based EWARS reporting by the static and mobile clinics attending to the needs of the community. This will enhance weekly reporting by facilities to ensure early detection of and response to disease outbreaks.
WHO will also conduct a risk assessment for common diseases such as measles and cholera to ascertain the need for preventive vaccination campaigns and guide the planning process for preventive vaccination campaigns as well as secure adequate vaccines as guided by the risk assessment findings.
Through its network of experts, both within and outside the country WHO will conduct targeted and focused capacity building of health workers working in the health facilities. The proposed capacity building will cover how to run mobile outreach programs, disease surveillance and outbreak response, case management, and infection prevention and control (IPC) within health facilities, and Clinical
Management of Rape. This project will also aim to procure and distribute emergency health kits to support health partners responding to emergency health needs across the country.

project_name: Préparation et réponse sanitaire aux principales maladies à potentiel épidémique et catastrophes au Niger
Strengthening Health Sector Humanitarian response in Zimbabwe
project_objective:
The project will contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality due to multi hazards in the priority districts in the country. This will be done through the procurement and distribution of essential medicines for primary health care facilities.  The primary health care facility shall also receive capacity building on case management for conditions associated with drought , COVID-19 and other hazards. To improve early detection of priority conditions, the project will also seek to strengthen laboratory capacity to detect priority disease conditions including COVID-19.  The project will also seek to strengthen disease surveillance in the priority districts through capacity building on Intergarted disease surveillance and response.
To respond to child health issues, the project will also seek to reduce vaccine preventable diseases through supporting vaccination campaigns especially in districts will low vaccination coverages.

project_name: Provision of Humanitarian Air Service in Cameroon
project_objective:
This project aims to support the overall humanitarian response by enabling and enhancing access to beneficiaries and project implementation sites through a provision of air service. 

Its main objectives are:
•	To provide NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations and diplomatic missions in Cameroon with safe, effective and efficient air service;
•	To transport light cargo, such as medical supplies, information and communication technology (ICT) equipment;
•	To provide adequate capacity for medical and security evacuations of humanitarian staff.

UNHAS was established in Cameroon in November 2015 to provide air transport services to the entire humanitarian community and their implementing partners principally NGOs, UN agencies, red cross/crescent movement, donor organizations and diplomatic missions. Ever since, UNHAS has offered safe humanitarian flights on a regular weekly basis to Adamaoua (N’gaoundere), the North (Garoua) and the Far North (Maroua), as well as to Tchad (N’Djamena).  As the conflict worsened in the Northwest and Southwest regions, and following a request from the Steering Committee, UNHAS extended its operations in September 2019 to serve the locations of Bamenda, Mamfe and Tiko.
As the continued insecurity, vast distances and poor road conditions remain the main constraints to the provision of assistance by aid organizations, but also the prevailing Covid-19 pandemic worldwide and in Cameroon in particular, the continuation of UNHAS in 2021 will be vital in enabling humanitarian organizations to access the populations in need and project implementation sites

project_name: Coordination of the Humanitarian Response in Colombia
project_objective: OCHA plays a critical role in monitoring humanitarian developments at territorial level; coordinating the response and providing key analysis to inform decision making.  The current coordination architecture includes 12 Local Coordination Teams (LCTs) and 2 Humanitarian local Teams (HLTs) in the border departments of Guanía and Vichada with OCHA leading four of these LCTs. OCHA also provides information management support to LCTs in other areas led by other UN agencies.  Information gathered from all territories is centralized and analyzed regularly to generate information products related to the various emergences taking place in the departments and the status of the response. OCHA leads inter-cluster coordination efforts, a new Access Working Group as well as an inter-agency working group to analyse displacement and confinement figures which are published monthly. OCHA also co-leads a working group that analyses conflict dynamics and the classification of armed groups. OCHA also supports the HCT in strategic decision making.  It maintains close coordination with the Refugee and Migrants Response coordination mechanism in country to ensure coordinated actions as well as with the RCO and the Peace Mission to facilitate linkages between humanitarian, development and peace building efforts in country. OCHA also maintains close relations with the OCHA office in Venezuela and the focal points in Peru and Equator, particularly in relation to analysis of cross-border dynamics and coordination of some response efforts. OCHA will continue to play a key role in planning, coordinating and monitoring the COVID-19 response together with WHO.  Furthermore, OCHA supports the coordination of the response to natural disasters with the state’s National Unit for Disaster Risk Management to complement Governments efforts and fill potential gaps in the response. In 2021 OCHA will maintain its presence with coordination staff in 10 departments - those most affected by humanitarian crises.

project_name: Provision of WASH services for displacement and conflict-affected Libyans, migrants and refugees
project_objective: The intervention aims at enhancing safe, equitable and dignified access to basic WASH services and containing the COVID-19 outbreak, to protect displacement and conflict-affected Libyans and non-Libyans (migrants and refugees).

project_name: WASH services for returnees in Burundi
project_objective:
Le projet se chargera de répondre aux besoins humanitaires en Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement dans les communautés où une grande partie des retournées sont concentrés. En l’occurrence dans les provinces de Muyinga , Cankuzo, Ruyigi et Rutana. Pour améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable, l’hygiène et l’assainissement dans ces zones cibles, World Vision International Burundi dans ce  projet se focalisera sur la disponibilisation de l’eau en construisant des sources d’eau au niveau de la communauté mais aussi sur la promotion de l’hygiène par des sensibilisations contre les maladies des mains sales, leurs moyens de prévention et par la construction des latrines dans ces zones où il intervient déjà dans ses différent programmes visant à répondre aux besoins des communautés vulnérable. De plus, pour faire face à la pandémie de COVID-19 dans ces localités, le projet mettra en place des dispositifs de lavage des mains dans des differents endroits public,  comme  des centres de santé et des écoles.
Il est supposé que des nombreux mouvements des personnes déplacées internes et des rapatriés exercent une pression sur le minimum d’infrastructures en place concernant le WASH surtout dans ces provinces mentionnées qui sont connu pour une capacite en WASH qui laisse à désirer, d’où le besoin criant d’intervenir afin de mettre en place des mesures préventifs et/ou de réponse à ces besoins pour éviter des vulnérabilité cause par un manque d’eau potable.
Ainsi donc, 139,674 personnes rapatriées et 131,336 PDIs seront pris en charge par ce projet ou des activités prévues seront mises en œuvre pour aboutir aux résultats éscomptés. Ces activités sont entre autres : 
-	Donner de l'eau potable aux populations  vulnérables avec un manque criant en eau potable. Le projet prévoit trouver des sources d’approvisionnement d’eau potable et/ou faire des traitements avant distribution mais également faire un aménagement des points de puisage temporaire.   
-	250  latrines d'urgence en matériaux disponibles localement seront aménagés, mais également 250  cabines de latrines mobiles prédisposés afin d’assurer une réponse rapide en cas d’urgence. 

-	10,495 kits Wash principalement constitués des savons, bidon de stockage de l'eau, seaux, les aquatabs pour traitement de l'eau à domiciles, etc.…qui seront distribué aux ménages les plus vulnérables 
	
-	Des  4 séances de sensibilisation à travers plusieurs canaux de communication sur les bonnes pratiques d'hygiène seront organisés dans les provinces cible 

-	Les systèmes de lavages des mains au savon dans les écoles  à travers la distribution des sceaux a robinet et du savon 
-	3  blocs de latrine pour l'accès à un assainissement dans les écoles ayant connues des inondations seront construits

-	3  Latrines séparées pour femmes et hommes et autres infrastructures d’hygiène adéquates seront construites  au niveau des centres de santé dans les provinces cibles.

project_name: Cash and livelihoods assistance to households facing crisis and emergency
project_objective:
Save the Children (SC) aims to provide support in line with the spectrum of the Somalia food security cluster strategic objectives of:
1.	Improved Access to Food and Safety Nets (IASN): SC will provide unconditional unrestricted cash assistance and food vouchers where appropriate to improve access to immediate food needs for the most vulnerable and marginalized households with emphasis on pregnant and lactating women (PLW), HHs with U2 and U5 children and households with disability. The cash transfer will be delivered through mobile money platform to minimize protection risks. 
2.	Protecting and restoring livelihoods related to food security and income sources. SC will provide livelihood inputs to the two main sources of livelihoods in Somalia i.e. crop and livestock agriculture. In the crop agriculture sector; seed inputs, tools, agriculture trainings, tillage hours, rehabilitating main agriculture related infrastructure e.g. canals will be done while in livestock agriculture, livestock treatment, provision of water and restocking where and when is possible. 
    
Save the Children adopted mobile money transfer back in 2014 and in Somalia context Mobile money is a feasible transfer mechanism for a number of reasons, including wide community acceptance and strong private entities (eg Hormuud, Golis and Somtel), efficient and timely and fast set up, and safe and secure means for HHs to receive and manage cash transfers. Across Somalia in general, and in proposed program areas specifically, mobile money is a mechanism widely accepted for payments with a broad array of vendors operating as mobile money agents. According to findings from SC post distribution monitoring, shops and cash-out agents are generally available within a 30 minute to 1-hour walk for most HHs, with the exception of pastoralists who might take longer pending their location. Beneficiaries are able to both cash-out their accounts, or but make direct purchases through mobile money without cashing out, depending on their preferences.
Mobile money enables a timely and efficient transfer for cash to target as it restricts the shop/vendor and food commodities to be transferred to beneficiaries. It also offers improved safety and security compared to in-kind or cash transfers, which can expose HHs and women, as primary beneficiaries, to greater risk. It also minimizes unnecessary beneficiary movement and profiling at the point of payment. 

SC will mobilize and sensitize mothers through IYCF sessions on how to utilize cash received to purchase quality and variety of foods for better nutrition outcomes for children, particularly in the first 1,000 days, as the primary cash recipients. SC will also carry out other bulk messaging on Fraud awareness creation, cash diversion and COVID-19 awareness messages to take advantage of the larger reach of cash transfer beneficiaries.
Cash programing will enable HHs to purchase preferred foods (rice, sorghum and wheat) from a wide number of shops and markets while also strengthening local drought-affected shops and markets, with a potential broader impact on markets than voucher programming, which typically works with only a few commodities and or vendors. In addition, cash is most appropriate to address reduced purchasing power through improved food access, while also increasing demand in local markets with resultant stimulation of market growth and increase of trading opportunities. 
SC has been monitoring the market situation at key markets (both intervention and supply markets) in all target regions since June 2018.

project_name: Improving access to emergency life-saving  and  sustainable WASH services to vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Gedo, Somalia
project_objective:
The proposed project will improve access to sustainable WASH services namely safe water, sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices for 7,846 female and 7,539 male beneficiaries in underserved and hard-to-reach villages and IDP camps in Belet Xawa, Dollow, Garbaharey and Luuq districts in Gedo. Among the target beneficiaries will be 2,308 persons with disabilities (1177 male, 1131 female).
The below-average rainfall forecast for the upcoming Deyr season (Oct to Dec) which may be compounded by a harsh Jilaal dry season in 2021 calls for a greater focus on WASH and a re-prioritization of life-saving approaches in Gedo. Access to improved water sources remains low in Gedo with a significant portion of the population relying on the rivers and other seasonal streams as their primary water sources. A joint multi-sectoral assessment led by Trócaire in Dollow riverine communities in December 2019 indicated that 90% of households consume untreated water from the Juba river. The same assessment identified poor latrine coverage as a challenge, with 80% of the population lacking access to latrines. This results in wider open defecation, which is suspected to be one of the factors contributing to the frequent occurrence of diarrheal diseases in the area. A detailed site assessment by REACH in February 2020 further reported widespread open defecation at 64 and 100 percent respectively in assessed sites in Luuq and Dollow. The most severely affected community members are women and girls, who are often forced to use nearby bushes, putting them at a greater risk of SGBV. The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has further compounded WASH needs in communities, with Trocaire noting serious gaps in knowledge, skills and resources to prevent and control the pandemic especially in IDP and rural communities. 
The project aims to contribute to the achievement of specific objectives of the WASH cluster: delivering life-saving WASH assistance to reduce acute needs, and restoring access to safe and equitable basic WASH services in target locations. This will be done through the construction of one (1) solar powered shallow well with piping to communities in Dollow, rehabilitation of one flood-damaged water system in Dollow and provision of Genset, construction of 110 permanent gender-sensitive latrines with handwashing stations, desludging of 85 latrines, hygiene promotion sessions with distribution of hygiene kits, and environmental cleanup campaigns. In addition, Trocaire will conduct water testing and treatment of water facilities in target locations, and conduct trainings and refresher trainings for representative Water Management Committees while equipping them with tools necessary for effective management of water points. Trocaire will collaborate with Somali Humanitarian Relief Action (SHRA) and Active in Development Aid (ADA), national NGOs with strong experience in implementing WASH projects in Gedo, in delivery of this project in the four target districts.
Trocaire shall work closely with local partners identified to promote protection of beneficiaries and ensure access to services especially for people living with disabilities. The Water Management Committees will particularly be sensitized on inclusivity in water access for people with disabilities and their families. Hygiene promotion outreach teams will be trained to identify and deliver services in homes with people living with disabilities. Gender inclusivity will be ensured through creation or support to adequately representative community structures, as well as working closely with women groups in target location. All data collected will be dis aggregated by gender, age and disability, to inform adaptive programming in meeting the different needs of the different social groups reached.

project_name: Protéger les enfants touchés par les conflits armés et COVID19 au Mali
project_objective:
Les enfants comptent parmi les premières victimes de l’insécurité et des conflits armés au Mali. Ils sont exposés à des risques élevés de violences, abus, exploitation et violations graves de leurs droits. La pandémie de COVID19 et ses impacts sanitaires et non-sanitaires ont exacerbés les vulnérabilités existantes. L’objectif général de ce projet est d’assurer la protection des enfants dans les zones les plus touchées par le conflit au Mali, en fournissant aux enfants les services d’appui médical, psychosocial et de réintégration nécessaire pour atténuer les effets négatifs à long terme.  

Le projet vise à offrir des services de protection en faveur de 600 enfants sortis des forces et groupes armés et 1000 enfants non accompagnés et séparés, y compris à cause de la COVID19, pour la prise en charge transitoire holistique (médicale, psychosociale, alimentaire, vestimentaire) et l’appui à la réintégration socioéconomique. 1500 enfants victimes de violences physiques ou sexuelles bénéficieront des services de prise en charge appropriés. En outre, 300,000 enfants affectés par les conflits ou la COVID19 recevront un soutien psychosocial, individuel ou à base communautaire dans des espaces sécurisés. 

L'UNICEF veillera à ce que 900 violations graves des droits de l’enfant par les parties au conflit soient documentées, vérifiées et rapportées en étroite collaboration avec la MINUSMA et d’autres membres du Groupe de Travail National sur le MRM. Les nombre de violations graves des droits de l’enfant (meurtre et la mutilation, le recrutement par les forces et groupes armés, viol et autres formes de violence sexuelle, enlèvement, attaques/occupation contre des écoles et des hôpitaux et déni d’accès humanitaire) est en augmentation significative avec la dégradation du conflit au centre du Mali. Le projet vise également 400 survivants de VBG/EAS dans les zones touchées par la crise, où les personnes deviennent plus vulnérables à la violence sexuelle, aux abus et à l'exploitation avec les mouvements de la population, et la COVID19. Ils recevront une assistance holistique (soutien médical et psychosocial, réintégration socioéconomique selon leurs propres besoins). En outre, 30,000 membres des communautés touchées par la crise seront sensibilisés sur la protection des enfants de la violence, le signalement des violations et la réponse aux enfants affectés et 40,000 personnes seront touchées par des actions de prévention des VBG/ EAS. 15.000 enfants 0-17 ans dépourvus de certificats de naissance recevront une aide pour l'obtenir par le biais de jugements supplétifs et une meilleure collaboration avec la santé dans les zones touchées par le conflit et la COVID-19, ainsi que par une évaluation des enfants non enregistrés.  

L’UNICEF collaborera étroitement avec les partenaires gouvernementaux ainsi que les agents de l’état civil pour assurer que leurs capacités soient développées. En répondant aux besoins des enfants les plus vulnérables, ce projet garantira que les enfants seront protégés et pourront ainsi contribuer à la paix et au développement durable du pays, en assurant leur dignité et leur accès aux services nécessaires. 

La redevabilité vis-à-vis des communautés ciblées sera intégrée aux activités, y compris via un mécanisme de plainte. Outre les activités spécifiques visant à traiter directement la réponse et la prévention de l'exploitation et l'abus sexuelle (EAS), tous les partenaires d’exécution recevront une formation sur la PSEA conformément à la stratégie de l’UNICEF concernant l’évaluation des partenaires récemment introduite. 

Tous les partenaires d’exécution du projet mettront en œuvre les activités dans le contexte de la COVID-19 avec la capacité et l'équipement appropriés. 30,000 personnes (partenaires étatiques et non-étatiques, acteurs communautaires, etc.) seront sensibilisées sur la COVID-19 et 400 travailleurs de protection et agents communautaires seront dotés en équipements individuels.

project_name: Continuité des services et soins de sante dans le contexte de la pandémie de Covid-19
project_objective:
Contexte:
Le contexte humanitaire malien continue de s’aggraver avec les effets combinés des conflits, l’insécurité multiforme et les aléas climatiques (inondations et sécheresses).  A ces trois chocs s’ajoute l’urgence sanitaire liée à la pandémie de la COVID 19 qui vient exacerber les vulnérabilités préexistantes avec des conséquences socioéconomiques importantes à court, moyen et long terme. Ces chocs conjoncturels récurrents et de magnitude toujours plus élevée se superposent à des facteurs structurels contribuant à l’aggravation de cette crise. Ainsi 12,9 millions de personnes sont affectées par la crise, parmi lesquelles désormais 6,8 millions sont en besoin d’une assistance alimentaire pour répondre à des besoins vitaux, à l’accès aux services sociaux de base et conditions de vie, ainsi qu’au renforcement de leurs capacités de Relèvement et résilience face aux chocs.

Objectifs du Projet
L’objectif principal est de contribuer au renforcement du système de santé prenant en compte le contexte de la pandémie de la maladie a corona virus et insécurité. 

Objectifs Specifiques:
•	 Prévenir la propagation de la maladie et améliorer le plateau technique des structures de santé pour une meilleure prise en charge des cas ;  
•	Assurer la continuité des services essentiels de santé et VIH pour réduire la morbidité et mortalité des mères et les enfants, en particulier les plus vulnérables ;
•	  Supporter le système de santé communautaire à mieux se prendre en charge après la COVID19.

Interventions:
-	Renforcer les capacités des établissements de santé par la mise à disposition des équipements, du matériel et des médicaments ainsi que des formations de recyclage pour les prestataires de soins de santé primaires sur la détection, l'orientation des cas de Covid-19 et la prise en charge des cas de Covid-19, afin de fournir des soins de santé de qualité aux populations, y compris vulnérables et difficiles.
-	Soutenir la capacité du laboratoire national par la mise a disposition des tests. Cela comprend l'achat d'équipement, de réactifs et de matériel de détection, le renforcement des capacités et la gestion des données au niveau central et décentralisé.
-	Soutenir la continuité des services de santé maternelle et infantile pour sauver des vies. Cela comprendra la prise en charge des maladies infantiles courantes, le renforcement des activités de vaccination, et la promotion et la fourniture de soins obstétricaux et néonataux d'urgence de base et complet prenant en compte la PTME et les soins pédiatriques du VIH. 
-	Appuyer les districts sanitaires à assurer la surveillance à base communautaire des maladies sous surveillances et renforcer les activités de riposte aux épidémies. 

Beneficiaires:
500,000 dont 175,000 femmes enceintes et 325,000 enfants de 0 a 59 mois (165,750 filles et 159,250 garcons)

project_name: Delivering life-saving health care to vulnerable children, mothers and other affected populations in humanitarian situations and partnering with Governments at all levels to strengthen the local health system for emergency preparedness and response
project_objective:
This health project will provide emergency life- saving health care services to persons affected by humanitarian situations with focus on children, women and vulnerable populations including internally displaced, elderly, those with disabilities, refuges and returnees for a period of 12 months. The direct beneficiaries to be reached by UNICEF across all health interventions will be 1,231,055 (31%)of the 3.9 million people in need targeted by Health cluster. This includes persons with disabilities (estimated at 15%)  Outpatient consultations will be provided to  1,096,305  of which 515,263  will be under 5 years of age  (263,113 girls and 252,150 boys) 350,818 women and 230, 224 men;  49,334 pregnant women will be targeted for skilled birth attendance; 83,320 (45,826 girls and 37,494 boys.) under 5 to be vaccinated against measles  and  2,096 (1,174 females and 922 males) frontline health workers will benefit from capacity development to improve service delivery.  Twenty -nine districts are proposed in nine priority regions (Bakool, Banadir, Bay, Galgadud, Gedo, Hiraan, Lower Jubba, Lower Shabelle, Middle Shabelle)
based on trends of cyclic humanitarian shocks and crises such as floods, droughts, conflicts and outbreaks. UNICEF will support services through Primary health care facilities, outreach and mobile teams to treat those in underserved areas including the elderly and persons with disabilities who have limited ability to reach the fixed health facilities. Health care interventions  will be based on the Essential Package of health services (EPHS)  with the delivery of antenatal and post- natal services, emergency obstetrics and neonatal care, immunizations both routine and  campaign  such as OPV, measles and cholera as required ,outpatient consultative services  for under 5  children with focus on common childhood illnesses and care for adults including the elderly. Services will be tailored to address the impacts of above-mentioned outbreaks like AWD/Cholera (through CTCS, CTUS and ORPs), COVID-19 ,malnutrition and other co-morbidities while strengthen referral systems for management of complications and for access to comprehensive care and psychosocial support for those affected by Gender based violence. In partnership with the nutrition cluster preventive and curative nutritional services for malnourished children (MAM and SAM) and women, deworming, breastfeeding services for PLW and micronutrient supplementation will be provided in the health facilities and outreaches. Skills of frontline health care workers will be built on case management of common illnesses, GBV survivors and clinical management of rape, protection against sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA),disease surveillance. Additionally, capacity development will be provided for Infection Prevention and control with focus on both medical and non-medical cadre and in the context of COVID-19 improve triage and handwashing activities in supported HFs. Community health workers will be capacitated to provide key messages on outbreaks and services available and support disease surveillance activities in the communities.  Health interventions to be provided will be done in a consultative manner through use of NGOS  with presence in the area and Civil societies and community development committees which cuts across women , men and youth groups. This will be done in partnership with the UNICEF communication for development team and the Risk Communication and Community Engagement  pillar. Whilst different groups will be involved in the design and implementation UNICEF will provide supported health facilities with essential medicines, kits, PPE, IPC supplies and equipment for emergency response. UNICEF will work with FGS/MoH, SMoHS and NGOS/CSO, the national health cluster and sister UN agencies in public health assessments, planning, coordination and implementation of preparedness and response (P&R) measures with focus on district level team (DHMT) strengthening.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle rapide aux besoins des nouveaux déplacements de populations
project_objective:
NRC depuis 2016 met en œuvre un projet de réponse rapide aux besoins de communauté affectées par le conflit armé et les catastrophes naturelles. 

Dans le but de répondre aux besoins urgents de communautés affectées par le mouvement, le mécanisme de réponse rapide(RRM) se fixe comme stratégie le pré positionnement des équipes, des moyens et de capacités afin de répondre dans l’immédiat aux besoins des communautés affectées. Cette stratégie consiste à mettre des équipes dans des localités près de zones de crises et de mettre en place des capacités de déploiement au moment de crises à travers l’établissement des contrats cadre avec des fournisseurs ayant un accès aux zones affectées afin d’acheminer l’assistance humanitaire. Pour rester dans la logique de l’urgence, des capacités financières seront pré positionnées afin de répondre aux besoins immédiats et urgents de populations déplacées.

La seconde stratégie se fonde sur une veille humanitaire et des évaluations multisectorielles des besoins à travers la mise en place des points focaux humanitaires au niveau de communes et des comités de veille et de crise au niveau des cercles afin d’avoir un système de remontée et de triangulation plus fiable sur le terrain avec ces acteurs locaux. Ce système consistera à travers les points focaux de remonter les alertes vers comités de veille et de crise (CVC) et qui après à travers procéder à la triangulation, alerte le NRC pour une diffusion avec la coordination humanitaire afin de mobiliser les acteurs autour d’une évaluation rapide des besoins. Cette évaluation est multisectorielle avec la participation de l’ensemble des acteurs disposés à y prendre part et les acteurs du cadre commun de la santé de la zone concernée.

La dernière consiste à apporter après les évaluations multisectorielles des besoins, une réponse multisectorielle coordonnée dans les différents secteurs identifiés présentant des vulnérabilités pour les personnes affectées et cela dans un délai court. Cette coordination se fait auprès de OCHA afin de mobiliser les acteurs pour couvrir les différents besoins identifiés. Le RRM se focalisera sur les BNA et un premier cycle d’assistance en vivre et le PAM sera sollicité pour couvrir les autres cycles après mise à jour du contexte et des besoins. 


Le RRM priorisera une coordination autour des activités de la veille humanitaire à la réponse multisectorielle en privilégiant des échanges étroits avec les acteurs humanitaires afin de répondre de façon efficace aux besoins des communautés.

project_name: Améliorer les conditions de vie des PDIs et des populations hôtes affectées par les conflits et les inondations au Nord et au Centre du Mali, par la facilitation de leur accès aux Logements et en Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement.
project_objective:
Ce projet compte apporter une réponse à 5600 bénéficiaires à travers les axes suivants :
Axe 1 : Accès à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement
Le premier axe de la réponse se focalisera sur la réalisation/Réhabilitation des points d’eau avec la mise en place (ou redynamisera) des comités de gestion des points d’eau (avec 50% de femmes). NRC formera des artisans réparateurs pour assurer la maintenance des ouvrages et l’octroi de kits de maintenance pour la gestion durable de ces ouvrages. NRC appuiera les communautés hôtes à construire des latrines familiales et les sensibilisera sur les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et d’assainissement. NRC Construira de latrines et des douches communautaires d’urgence/transitoires en tenant compte des personnes à besoin spécifiques avec une approche communautaire.

Axe 2 : Accès à l’Abris 
 Le second axe se focalisera sur une réponse en terme de formation sur les techniques de construction/réhabilitation des maisons ou abris accompagnée d’une distribution de kits abris constitués de matériaux locaux adaptés aux zones (les sites inappropriées ou spontanés) où vivent les déplacés et/ou du Cash à ceux-là qui vivent dans les maisons louées ou extension des maisons/abris dans des familles d’accueils en zones urbaines. Ce Cash contribuera aux charges de loyer des déplacés en zones urbaines et péri-urbaines.
