project_name: UNHCR Operation and Refugee Response Plan
project_objective:
The UNHCR refugee response aligns with the key priorities and solutions raised by targeted refugee populations through UNHCR’s annual Participatory Assessment exercise. It aims to ensure that the protection and humanitarian needs of refugees and asylum-seekers are addressed, while promoting solutions through integration, resettlement and voluntary repatriation opportunities where possible. UNHCR will advocate for the adherence of international protection standards by expanding civil, social and economic rights to refugees, including through increased self-reliance opportunities for solutions.
UNHCR will advocate to improve refugees’ access to freedom of movement, labour markets, land and assets. Timely delivery of protection assistance, including access to registration, documentation and reception services will bolster refugees’ access to their basic rights, including access to lifesaving assistance. Capacity building and sensitization initiatives with local authorities, host communities and service providers will be used to address discrimination and social cohesion issues.
In camps, individual and household-level assistance will be provided to address ongoing needs in protection, shelter, NFIs, energy, health and WASH. UNHCR will work with COR, and with relevant line ministries where possible, to ensure the sustainability of interventions. This also includes greater participation by refugees in camp management, shelter and latrine construction, protection and security functions within their communities, community mobilization and service delivery.
The response will also seek to integrate cash-based interventions (CBIs) across all locations where feasible to support stabilization of existing assistance programs and complement self-reliance initiatives. This is especially important for refugees in urban areas, where they often form part of the “urban poor” and struggle to meet their basic needs which leaves them at heightened risk of harassment, exploitation and abuse, with women and children being particularly at-risk.
To enhance sustainability of service provision particularly in the WASH, Health and Energy sector UNHCR will invest in sustainably energy sources particularly solar energy and energy efficient stoves to reduce the environmental footprint. This will reduce the dependency on an unreliable supply of fuel and address protection risks coming from a lack of lighting and the need to collect firewood outside the village.

project_name: Increase access to equitable quality essential health services for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable population in South Sudan through provision of immunization core pipeline and use of the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM).
project_objective:
In line with our organizational Core Commitment to Children in Emergency, UNICEF will continue to provide the population of South Sudan especially children, pregnant and lactating women, with quality preventive, and curative services as well as outbreak response activities. The IRRM enables UNICEF, through direct implementation, to provide high impact lifesaving emergency response in inaccessible and conflict affected areas. UNICEF will ensure availability of core pipe line vaccines and cold chain supplies to respond to vaccine preventable disease outbreaks.

This project aims to increase access to quality equitable essential primary health care interventions through IRRM and provide a core pipeline to increase access to quality equitable immunization services by vulnerable populations living in host communities and IDPs living in Protection of Civilian Sites (POCs), formal IDP camps or host communities in conflict affected areas as well as refugee returnees.

The activities to be implemented are:
• Procurement and distribution of emergency vaccines.
• Procurement, distribution and maintenance of cold chain 
equipment.
• Technical support for improved vaccine and cold chain 
management
• Conduct 10 IRRM missions

The expected beneficiaries of core pipeline supplies are 500,000 vulnerable children living in camps, PoCs, formal IDP camps or host communities in conflict affected areas and refugee returnees. The children will benefit from emergency vaccination to sure up their immunity to vaccine preventable diseases. Vaccines against measles, meningitis, and cholera as well as cold chain equipment and devices will be procured.

28,000 children are expected to be reached during the Rapid Response Missions. These will include children aged 6 months-15years who will be reached with immunization services and curative consultations and pregnant women who are expected to benefit from ANC services, tetanus toxoid vaccination, curative consultations and the provision of long-lasting insecticide treated nets (LLITN).

project_name: Improvement of living conditions, social cohesion, enhancement of resilience to new arrivals, refugees in the camps and host communities through provision of lifesaving shelter and NFIs
project_objective:
UNHCR and partners (BRAC, CARITAS, DRC) will continue shelter interventions to improve the living conditions of refugees households taking into account AGDM and individual specific needs across all camps under UNHCR's AoR. Shelter actors are planning to assist 1,500 refugee households with double storey shelter in 14 camps and 3,000 refugee households with mezzanine shelter in registered camps. During the identification of beneficiaries for planned Shelter assistance, PwSN and EVIs are prioritized based on the list provided by UNHCR.   

UNHCR and BDRCS will ensure the provision of NFI for new arrivals and households who need items to be replaced in all UNHCR managed camps. Distribution of LPG sets and refills as well as associated approved cooking equipment will continue in camps and host communities’ areas. 

In addition, UNHCR will ensure the prepositioning of emergency shelter materials and NFI as a contingency for households affected by various natural disasters and protection incidents. Shelter / NFI focal points in disaster management committees are enhancing capacity and involvement of refugee volunteers as part of the overall camp level emergency preparedness and response, and DRR activities. 

UNHCR interventions will focus on community-based approach and gender mainstreaming, engaging more with community groups, thus increasing community ownership and improving support for vulnerable households. UNHCR will increase its capacity for more effective coordination and participation with CiCs as part of the capacity sharing initiative. 

In relation to AAP, complaints and feedbacks related shelter and NFI related activities are mainly channeled through Complaints, Feedbacks and Referral Mechanisms (CFRM) as well through protection hotline, Community Outreach Members (COM) volunteers, SMS partners referrals and bloc leaders. Mandatory online and in-person trainings on CoC and PSEA are facilitated by UNHCR and dedicated partners focal points. Partners need to comply with the Checklist for the assessment of the PSEA capacity of partners. 

Each distribution exercise take place in a distribution point that is gender and age sensitive: segregated waiting lines and WASH facilities, covered / shaded waiting areas, porter services as needed, emergency exit,  security provided. PDM are also conducted so distribution processed are improved and more inclusive.

project_name: Emergency Health and Nutrition Interventions to the Locusts, COVID 19 and Flood displacement affected Communities in Somalia
project_objective:
According to the last FSNAU report on May 9, 2020, – Up to 2.7 million people across Somalia are expected to face food consumption gaps, high acute malnutrition, or depletion of assets indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3)1 or worse outcomes through December 2020. Moreover, an estimated one million children under the age of five are likely to be acutely malnourished through mid-2020. An estimated 2.6 million people across Somalia remain internally displaced which will worsen humanitarian needs. Current high levels of food insecurity are driven by drought conditions and compacted by continued displacements and conflict. Data obtained from UNHCR indicates that an estimated 126,000 people were displaced be-tween Jan and March 2020, mainly because of insecurity (76%), mostly affecting Lower Sha-belle, Bay, Galgaduud and Gedo regions. As of 26 October 2020, according to Somalia’s Ministry of Health and Human Services, Somalia has a total 3941 cases and 14 deaths. Data obtained from the Somalia Nutrition Cluster indicates a 13 percent increase in monthly new admissions of acutely malnourished children between January and March 2020 compared to the first-quarter average monthly admission for 2016-2019. This can be attributed to sporadic disease outbreaks (acute watery diarrhea-AWD/cholera and measles out-break), and worsening of the food security situation in many areas.
Maternal and child health indicators are among the worst in the world in Somalia, with maternal mortality rates at 732 per 100,000 live births, under-five mortality rate at 137 per 1,000 live births and skilled delivery rates of only 29.7% (UNICEF Somalia Annual Report 2017). The Nutritional surveys conducted by FSNAU in June and July 2019 indicate the persistence of widespread acute malnutrition in Somalia due to a combination of factors, including food insecurity, high morbidity, low immunization and vitamin-A supplementation, and poor care practices. At the national level, the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) has remained Serious (10–14.9%) over the past three seasons (13.8% in 2019 Gu, 12.6% in 2018 Deyr and 14.0% in 2018 Gu). Concern has directly run Health and Nutrition programmes in multiple regions Banadir (Mogadishu) and Afgoye communities. Lower Shabelle and Gedo since 2008 and developed long-standing, trusting relationships with key actors including communities served, MoH authorities, peer Non-Government Organizations and UN. In 2019 Concern undertook direct service provision in 10 integrated health and nutrition facilities in Banadir (6) and Lower Shabelle regions (4), including over 100,000 Out Patient Department (OPD) consultations for children and adults, serving a total catchment population of 400,000. Furthermore, since late 2017 Concern has managed the stabilization center at the National Referral hospital in Mogadishu, which provides treatment for children with life-threatening complications of severe acute malnutrition. project_name: Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan
project_objective:
As of January 2021, there are more than 314,000 refugees from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, as well as the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, including from Sudan, Democratic Republic of Congo and Central African Republic.

At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for long-term stability, some 357,500 South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since November 2017, 122,000 of those in 2020 alone. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan at this stage, the increase in numbers warrants a scaling-up of support following an area-based approach, including strengthening linkages with development actors, to help returnees and the communities they settle in live in safety and dignity, with greater security and services.

Refugees largely reside in conﬂict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction of basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.

Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will beneﬁt from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Speciﬁc protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identiﬁed at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with speciﬁc protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as veriﬁcation exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the eﬃciency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to beneﬁt from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_name: Projet d’Appui à la lutte Contre la malnutrition aigüe dans les districts sanitaires de Tillia, Bouza et Madaoua ( Région de Tahoua) et  le district sanitaire de Mayahi (Région de Maradi) au Niger dans le contexte de pandémie de COVID 19
project_objective:
L’action s'inscrit dans une logique programmatique d'Action contre la Faim visant à renforcer l'accessibilité et la qualité de la prise en charge et à prévenir la malnutrition aigüe au Niger et en particulier dans les départements de Tillia, Bouza et Madaoua (région de Tahoua) et le département de Mayahi (région de Maradi). L'objectif visé est d'accroître l’accès aux soins curatifs et préventifs intégrés et de qualité de la malnutrition aigüe sévère pour les enfants de moins de 5 ans (filles et garçons). 
Il s’agira d’assurer le suivi du paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé pour l’amélioration du traitement de la Malnutrition Aiguë Sévère (MAS) et aussi de développer les capacités des acteurs de la santé et des communautés en matière de prévention de la malnutrition. Les couples mères enfants répondant aux critères d’admission CRENI seront ciblés prioritairement par les actions WASH. Par ailleurs, face à la pandémie du COVID-19, Action Contre la Faim Niger se propose également d’apporter son appui aux structures de santé des Districts sanitaires ciblés en termes de renforcement de capacités et dotations pour accompagner les activités de prise en charge de la MAS dans les CRENAS et dans le CRENI.  De manière spécifique, l'intervention se fera à travers :                                                                                  
- la facilitation de l’accès à une eau potable dans les ménages MAS et leurs communautés (construction et/ou réhabilitation de points d’eau, mise en place COGES/AUSPE, Promotion de la bonne gouvernance de l'eau, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              - la mise en place d’un paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé de la zone d’intervention  ( système de stockage d'eau, maintenance périodiques des infrastructures, Gestion des déchets, Construction/réhabilitation d'ouvrages d'assainissement, dotation des kits WASH, etc)                                                                                                                                   - le Renforcement de capacités des centres de santé et du personnel en matière de prévention covid-19  (formation sur les méthodes préventives du covid-19 et la désinfection des lieux, dotation en kits de prévention et riposte au covid 19, etc)                                                                                                                                                                                  - la promotion du changement de comportement auprès des communautés cibles sur les bonnes pratiques en matière d'hygiène et Assainissement (traitement de l'eau à domicile, Promotion du lavage des mains et respect des mesures barrières de prévention Covid-19).

project_name: Action éducative d'urgence pour les enfants du centre du Mali (Mopti)
project_objective:
Le projet « Action éducative d'urgence pour les enfants du centre du Mali » Aligné aux politiques et stratégies nationales d’éducation du Mali , à savoir le  Programme Décennal  de Développement de l’Education et de la Formation  Professionnelle  (PRODEC 2 )  dans son  axe renforcement de de la capacité de résilience du secteur , au cadre de suivi  du  Plan de Réponse Humanitaire (HRP 2021) et à la Stratégie  du Gouvernement  contre le Covid -19 en milieu scolaire , le projet « Action éducative d'urgence pour les enfants du centre du Mali » vise à proposer une offre d’éducation alternative adaptée aux besoins d’apprentissage des enfants qui sont affectés dans la région de Mopti dans le centre du Mali, Cercles de Mopti, Bandiagara et Tenenkou ce  dans une approche partenariale qui caracéérise toutes les interventions de SCI et basée sur les complémentarité  techniques entre acteurs . Le projet présente deux (2) solutions pratiques pour améliorer la qualité de l’éducation dans les localités qui seront ciblées par l’intervention. 1) Un apprentissage accéléré d’au moins 6 mois de cours pour les enfants ayant abandonné l’école ou les enfants qui vivent dans les localités où l’école est non fonctionnelle. L’objectif de l’apprentissage est de préparer ces enfants bénéciaires à une réintégration scolaire dans le système formel. Des espaces d’apprentissage temporaire seront installés dans les localités ciblées de préférence a proximité des écoles existantes ou dans tout autre lieu sécurisé où les enfants pourront apprendre et les animateurs pourront enseigner sans perturbations majeures. A la fin  de la période d’apprentissage, les enfants seront directement intégrés dans les écoles formelles de leurs localités selon un processus d’intégration bien coordonner qui prendra en compte le suivi des espaces d’apprentissage par les autorités éducatives de la zones d’interventions. 2) Les cours de soutien / rattrapage seront une solution offerte aux enfants bien que scolarisés qui sont très en dessous du niveau scolaire de la classe qu’ils fréquentent. En effet, du fait de la scolarité perturbée par les grèves des enseignants, l’absence provisoire ou durable d’enseignants dans les écoles, la qualité des enseignants, le manque de matériels et manuels d’enseignement, le manque de matériels et manuels d’apprentissage, etc., de nombreux enfants ont un très faible rendement scolaire. Les cours de rattrapage se tiendront 6 heures dans la semaine, soit 2 à 3 fois selon le programme qui sera prédéni par les acteurs de la localité. 
 Le projet travaillera  en étroite collaboration avec les services étatiques pour affiner, renforcer et opérationnaliser les systèmes existants au Mali, soutenir le renforcement des capacités des responsables gouvernementaux pour garantir l'accès à une éducation sûre et de qualité pour toutes les filles et tous les garçons. 
Dans la mise en œuvre du projet, notre action visera à favoriser d’avantage les enfants les plus vulnérables (en particulier les lles et jeunes lles) et à assurer une inclusion des enfants déplacés et retournés. La protection s’articulera à identier les enfants ayant les besoins spéciques d’assistances puis à mettre en place un mécanisme d’accompagnement et de prise en charge des vulnérabilités. Ces enfants vulnérables seront intégrés dans l’assistance éducative que le projet propose avec l’intention qu’ils continuent normalement leurs scolarités après la n du projet. Un appui substantiel sera octroyé aux écoles à proximité des espaces d’apprentissage temporaire et aux écoles dans les lesquels les cours de rattrapage seront conduits
Bien plus , Save the Children  fort de  ses  politiques et des procédures bien établies de sauvegarde des enfants ainsi que la Protection contre l’Abus et l’Exploitation Sexuelle (PSEA) afin d'atténuer les risques de préjudice et de répondre de manière appropriée aux incidents impliquant le personnel du projet, les partenaires , les volontaires  et autres parties prenantes.

project_name: Assistance en abris et bien non-alimentaires aux ménages affectés par les déplacements forcés et populations hôtes dans les zones Centre et Nord du Mali.
project_objective:
L’OIM et les partenaires de mise en œuvre (IP), interviendront pour renforcer l’accès aux Abris/BNA. Les activités seront basées sur des besoins définis par la Commission Mouvement de Population (CMP) sur la base de la Matrice de Suivi de des Déplacements (DTM) et le cluster Abris/BNA. Les interventions seront ciblées, locales et communautaires, répondront aux besoins les plus urgents, amélioreront la durabilité de l’intervention et la résilience des communautés face aux déplacements.
L’OIM assurera l’accès à différentes solutions en abris d’urgence en distribuera 2,000 abris d’urgence résistants aux populations déplacées identifiées prioritaires suite aux évaluations. La dimension de l’abri distribué sera recommandée de 21 m2 conformément aux normes Sphère, sur la base de 3,5 m2 par personne.
L’OIM fournira 5,000 kits de BNA dont la composition sera conforme aux normes du cluster Abris/BNA et décidé en fonction des consultations menées auprès de la population touchée afin de s’assurer que sont adaptés au contexte. Les distributions seront effectuées par les IP en raison des contraintes d’accès. L'équipe abris de l'OIM travaillera avec les acteurs de protection pour s'assurer de l’intégration de la protection dans ses interventions et la prise en compte des risques de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) pour les atténuer.
En tant que membre du groupe de travail Logement, Terre, Propriété et Ressources Naturelles (LTPRN), l’OIM soutiendra 2,000 ménages déplacés sans accès à la terre avec une assistance en solutions foncières. L’OIM aura le soutien de l’expert global de l’OIM, spécifiquement pour la réalisation d’une fiche de profil du pays.
L’OIM appuiera la construction d'abris durables avec des transferts monétaires pour 1,000 ménages. Les ménages bénéficiaires font partie aussi de l’activité d’assistance en solutions foncières.
En tant que co-lead du cluster Abris/BNA, l’OIM assurera la coordination des activités des partenaires d’Abris, y compris les membres du Mécanisme de réponse rapide (MRR) et d’autres partenaires locaux afin de maximiser l’efficacité de la réponse et de surmonter les contraintes d’accès potentielles. De même la collecte, analyse et partage des données seront coordonnées. La deuxième activité que mènera l’OIM, sera l’appui technique aux partenaires et les formations données, incluant l’appui technique dans les sites d’accueil temporaire.
Pour faire face aux préoccupations liées à la protection émises par les personnes interrogées lors de l’enquête DTM d’octobre, l’OIM assurera l'intégration de mesures pour l’atténuer des risques de la lutte contre les violences VBG dans la réponse Abris/BNA:
-Par le suivi et la remontée de plaintes, à travers des mécanismes de plaintes et des activités de suivi post-distributions (PDM)
-En veillant à ce qu’une perspective de genre soit incluse dans les procédures RH afin de s’assurer que les travailleurs communautaires et le staff de l’OIM incluent les femmes
-En s’assurant que toutes les questions de protection qui incluent la non-discrimination, l’absence de préjudice, l’accès significatif, la sécurité et la dignité soient intégrées. L’OIM s’efforcera de garantir la participation active des groupes vulnérables (notamment personnes handicapées et à besoins spécifiques) à toutes les étapes du cycle du projet
Ces activités seront menées avec la Direction Régionale du Développement Économique et Social (DRDES) et en incluant les communautés dans un souci de renforcer la redevabilité vis-à-vis des populations affectées.
Tous les partenaires ainsi que les partenaires de mise en œuvre s’engageront à respecter la politique de la PSEA (Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse). Conformément à son Cadre institutionnel de lutte contre la violence basée sur le genre en situation de crise, l’OIM intégrera des mesures visant à atténuer les risques de violence sexiste tout au long de ses interventions, et veillera à ce que les interventions ne causent pas de tort.

project_name: Renforcement de la protection des populations vulnérables à travers le relèvement, la réintégration et la mise en place des solutions durables en matière d’abris
project_objective:
Le projet de l’AICRL en partenariat avec la Croix-Rouge Malienne s’inscrit dans le cadre des axes prioritaires en matière d’abris. Dans ce cadre, les interventions s’articuleront autour des modalités programmatiques et opérationnelles suivantes : 

1.	Population cible, Approche et Stratégies : 
 
Les interventions cibleront les ménages les plus vulnérables parmi les personnes déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées mais aussi certaines populations non déplacées dont les habitats ont été détruits ou endommagés dans 5 cercles prioritaires de la région de Tombouctou.

	1 200 ménages parmi les plus vulnérables soit environ 7 200 personnes déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées à travers la fourniture en abris transitoires (case peulh, case type milieu humide)
	200 ménages parmi les plus vulnérables soit environ 1 200 personnes déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées en cas d’afflux spontané ou d’inondations, à travers la fourniture en abris pré stockés

L’AICRL articulera son approche sur les modalités suivantes : 

•	Interventions basées sur les besoins et sur la vulnérabilité des populations déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées ou autochtones, notamment les personnes en situation de grande vulnérabilité et en prenant en compte les critères de ciblage suivants : 
o	Situation et statut : retourné, rapatrié, vulnérable non déplacé
o	Date de retour sur site des retournés (< ou > à 1 année)
o	Vulnérabilité socio-économique (handicap, maladie chronique, veuf/veuve, personne âgée, orphelin, indigent)
o	Etat de l’habitat/abri
o	Pression sociale sur le ménage
o	Surpeuplement du ménage  

•	Intégration et complémentarité de la mise en œuvre et mise en place des synergies : l’AICRL en lien avec la CRM s’attèlera à acter une complémentarité et une concentration de ses interventions, en synergie avec les autres projets en cours notamment à Tombouctou, afin de maximiser le rapport coût-efficience et l’impact sur les populations cibles ainsi que les communautés d’accueil qui bénéficieront également des effets multiplicateurs des différentes interventions. 

•	Participation, Acceptation et Appropriation : la participation, l’engagement et l’adhésion des bénéficiaires et communautés cibles ainsi que des communautés d’accueil constitueront un gage majeur de réussite de la mise en œuvre des interventions tout au long de la durée de vie du projet (notamment lors de la sélection et validation des bénéficiaires, notamment lors du traitement des plaintes éventuelles, etc.), et contribuera à un renforcement de l’acceptation des interventions parmi les communautés participantes et bénéficiaires, ceci au-delà de la vie du projet. 

2.	Principaux Résultats: 

Résultat 1 : Renforcement de la fourniture en abris transitoires de type « case végétale » ou « case pour milieu humide » au profit des populations nomades ou semi-nomades parmi les personnes déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées dans les régions de Tombouctou 

Le projet fournira 1200 abris transitoires pour la région de Tombouctou. Les interventions en lien avec ce résultat permettront de couvrir les besoins en abris transitoires pour environ 7 200 personnes déplacées, rapatriées ou retournées.

Résultat 2 : Renforcement de mécanismes de réponses d’urgence en matière d’abris pour répondre aux besoins d’afflux spontané de personnes déplacées ou retournées ou en cas d’inondations avec impact sur les abris dans les régions de Tombouctou. 
Le projet mettra en place un stock de contingence de 200 kits cases peulh kits visant à apporter un appui ponctuel aux communautés vulnérables (population déplacée et hôte) notamment au cours de la période hivernale et en cas de situation d’urgence liée à la destruction ou l’effondrement des abris non ciblés par le projet et/ou suite aux inondations. Ces kits abris de contingence seront pré-positionnés et stockés dans l’entrepôt de la CRM à Tombouctou. Cette modalité permettra de couvrir les besoins d’urgence en abris pour 1 200 personnes.

project_name: Assistance monétaire aux ménages vulnérables dans la région de Mopti
project_objective:
Le présent projet   vise à soutenir 3 000 ménages les plus affectés par le conflit et l’insécurité alimentaire (PDI et ménages hôtes, dont 33% dirigés par des femmes) par des transferts monétaires inconditionnels et réhabilitation de points d’eau et abris. 
CRS propose de permettre aux ménages n’ayant bénéficié d’aucune assistance ou d’une assistance d’urgence il y a plus de 12 mois dans les cercles de Bandiagara et Koro, d’acquérir les intrants d’abris nécessaires grâce à du cash conditionnel (60 000 FCFA par ménage). Une enquête sexospécifique des besoins sera conduite afin de confirmer les besoins des PDIs sur place et de s’assurer de la non-perturbation des marchés. Cette assistance permettra de réhabiliter les abris d’urgence et transitionnels de 3000 ménages, dont 33% étant dirigés par des femmes. Ce montant sera remis en deux tranches. La première avec 60% du montant afin que les ménages achètent une partie des intrants nécessaires.  Des séances de sensibilisation seront faites en amont, durant lesquelles les communautés seront invitées à aider les femmes cheffes de ménages, renforçant l’entraide sociale entre les communautés. Le paiement de la deuxième tranche est conditionné par la vérification physique que l’argent de la première tranche a été utilisé pour commencer la réhabilitation de leurs abris.
Afin d’accroitre la capacite financière des ménages ciblés à répondre à leurs besoins urgents pendant la période de soudure et limiter l’adoption de stratégies néfastes de survie, des transferts monétaire inconditionnels seront réalisés. Ainsi, les ménages ciblés (hôtes et PDIs) bénéficiant de l’assistance en abris ou en kits EHA, recevront deux transferts monétaires mensuels entre les mois de juin à septembre 2021. Le montant reçu sera lié à la taille du ménage. CRS et Caritas Mopti utiliseront les prestataires locaux et si le réseau téléphonique le permet, procèderont à un transfert par Mobile Money, ce qui pourrait permettre de répondre au problème de mobilité, y compris en zones d’insécurité. Les bénéficiaires seront aussi sensibilisés sur l’importance du rôle de la femme dans la gestion des ressources au sein du ménage pour contribuer au bien-être de la famille. Cette assistance sera accompagnée de sensibilisation concernant la nutrition (allaitement, règles d’hygiène, diversité des aliments, etc.). Les messages clés seront présentés à l’aide d’images simples afin que la sensibilisation soit accessible pour l’ensemble des participantes et participants.

project_name: Appui aux populations vulnérables affectées par les crises dans les régions de Mopti et de Ménaka au Mali et dans le cadre de la réponse à la COVID-19
project_objective:
Par ce projet, IRC intervient dans les régions de Mopti (Cercles de Ténenkou et de Youwarou) pour les populations vulnérables affectées par les crises, notamment les enfants, femmes enceintes et populations déplacées internes. L’insécurité grandissante, la multiplication des groupes armés radicaux et des forces armées, et l’augmentation des conflits inter- et intracommunautaires, notamment dans le centre du Mali, engendrent des déplacements de populations importants et limitent l’accès aux services sociaux de base encore fonctionnels, déjà fortement limités dans les cercles de Ténenkou et de Youwarou, zones enclavées et accessibles uniquement en pinasses entre juillet et février. L’intensification de la présence des groupes armés avec de manière corollaire, la multiplication des prêches des radicaux, des taxations arbitraires, des menaces, des assassinats et enlèvements ciblés, ont engendré des mouvements de population, exacerbant la vulnérabilité des communautés, en particulier des femmes et des enfants (mariage précoce, VBG, etc.) tout en amplifiant la pression sur les rares ressources disponibles. 
Ainsi, dans les Cercles de Ménaka, Inékar, Ténenkou et Youwarou, IRC continuera de déployer une stratégie Mécanismes de Réponse Rapide (RRM) développée en coordination d’autres partenaires, pour mieux anticiper et répondre aux crises récurrentes affectant les populations vulnérables du Nord et du Centre du Mali en tenant compte de l’environnement COVID-19. Cela permettra de fournir un appui d’urgence à 2 000 ménages vulnérables affectées par un choc en fonction des besoins identifiés lors de l’évaluation des besoins qui suit la confirmation de l’alerte RRM. IRC pourra fournir un appui d’urgence via la distribution de cash pour les besoins alimentaires de base ou la distribution de kits NFI ou de kits WASH.

project_name: Integrated Primary and SRH Health including COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Project for Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
""IRC Bangladesh is one of the crucial health partners of Health Sector in Cox’s Bazar in Rohingya response and providing Maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health (MNCAH), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH), Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) including MHPSS and Communicable Diseases (CD) health services from 03 Primary Health Care Centers (23 and 25; Camp 8E is in construction stage), 02 BEmONC Centers (1 in serving in Camp 26; another one is on the process), 17 Referral Hubs (12 active and 5 upcoming), 39 Women Friend Space (WFS) (23 active and 16 are in planning stage), 05 Women and Girl’s Safe Spaces (WGSS) and one (1) 60 beds SARI Isolation and Treatment Center at the camp level (Camp 23). 
Barriers faced by women and girls in seeking care, especially BEmONC and SRH services, will be addressed through outreach activities. The services include the ANC, PNC, FP (Both long- and short-term methods), NVD, and emergency referral to Secondary Health Care Centers. IRC Community Outreach officers will work with Community Health Volunteers to increase their capacity to both increase knowledge related to SRH and how gender norms influence health seeking behavior. Male engagement activities in family planning (FP) and SRH will be periodized. Additionally, needs of children, adolescents, youth and old in all their diversity (gender, age, disability, ethnicity) will also be addressed. IRC will focus on Sex, Age and Disability Disaggregated Data (SADDD) for program quality improvement.
The Referral Hub (RH) project of IRC is to ensure patients with emergency obstetric conditions and other medical emergency cases will be able to access to PHCC/BEmONC facilities through rapid referral services. This project is fully funded by UNFPA
Besides, IRC is working in Host Community to support Upazila level health facilities at Teknaf and Ukhia upazila of Cox’s Bazar through logistic and Human Resources. The support is dedicated to support ITCs in these hospitals (30 beds Ukhia and 34 beds in Teknaf; total 64 ITC beds). ""

project_name: Health-related vulnerabilities of Rohingya and Host Communities are reduced through increased quality access to comprehensive health services
project_objective: The aims of IOMs’ health interventions aim to respond to the lifesaving needs and improve the resilience of affected populations, with special attention to gender and age considerations, and vulnerable groups. In the camps,34% Rohingya refugee populations, have reported going into debt to pay for health expenses, and 27% seeking lower-quality care or medication, due to a lack of money (Joint Multi-Sector Needs Assessment J-MSNA 2020). This demonstrates some challenges in the already strained health service system in Cox’s Bazar. To address this, this intervention aims to contribute  to  i) increased safe, dignified and meaningful access and utilization of quality comprehensive healthcare services, focusing on sexual, reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health; mental health and psychosocial support; and non-communicable diseases (NCD); ii) improved health seeking behavior, encouragement of  healthy living and promotion of the  utilization of essential service package and community engagement, with special attention to vulnerable groups iii) measures to prepare and (timely) respond  to health emergencies, during disaster (including monsoon and cyclone) and outbreaks of communicable disease (e.g.  COVID-19 and AWD). IOM also aims to contribute to the improvement of quality of services through performance monitoring, evaluation, coordination and capacity building.

project_name: Improvement of WASH services for the most vulnerable populations in Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazilas of Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh
project_objective:
The project will implement activities as per the following description to achieve the objective of people in need having access to water and sanitation. The three subsectors of the intervention are presented below:                                                                                                                      
Water Supply: aligned with WASH Sector’s Plan 4 small scale solar-powered piped water networks will be installed in Camp 20 Extension to provide safe water to the beneficiaries. O&M of existing tube-wells in IOM’s AoR, water network in Camps 12, 13, 19, 24 and 20 Extension will be continued. Emergency stocks will be procured to prepare for cyclones or other natural disasters. A study will be conducted to assess the current water supply approach, gaps and identify potential sources to cover the gaps in the host community and refugee camps in Teknaf. Additional reservoir/sedimentation tanks will be constructed to increase the treatment and distribution capacity in the Leda surface water treatment plant. However, new Tube Wells will be installed based on the needs in four host community villages under Ukhiya and Teknaf.
Sanitation: based on need, durable latrines will be constructed, and old latrine will be upgraded to minimize desludging and health risks in both refugee and host communities. These include provisions for gender-inclusivity and usability for Persons with Disabilities (PwD). Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Systems (DEWATS) will be constructed to address coverage gaps, and few old Fecal Sludge Management (FSM) systems will be upgraded along with regular O&M of existing FSM systems. Additional bathing facilities and high platform septic tank latrines will be constructed in the developed valley. WASH Facility disinfection activities will be continued to reduce the risk of COVID-19 disease transmission. Solid waste management will be strengthened by focusing on reduction and recycling of waste produced–promoting household waste separation, small and large-scale composting, and recycling of plastics in both host and refugee community.
Hygiene Promotion and Epidemic Control: Critical supplies of hygiene items (soap, water containers, Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) materials, etc.) will be provided, together with community education and mobilization activities targeting all age and gender groups at the household and community level. Communities will be more engaged in O&M of WASH facilities, waste segregation and preventing COVID-19 disease transmission. A real time service monitoring and community feedback mechanisms will be established to ensure timely response for any WASH-related health risks, and emergency response stocks will be maintained in case of any Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) or other outbreaks.

project_name: Strengthening GBV prevention mechanisms and provision of comprehensive and lifesaving GBV for population in need in Sudan
project_objective:
The main humanitarian needs in Sudan result from different underlying root causes and drivers including instability and multiple conflicts, recurrent natural disasters including droughts and floods as well as disease outbreaks. women and girls continue to suffer disproportionately from GBV due to violations of basic rights, insecurity, low economic status, denial of livelihood opportunities, lack of community awareness on women's rights and GBV as well as due to negative cultural and societal norms. Rape, physical violence, FGM, early/ forced marriages, denial of resources opportunities, and verbal abuse are some of the common violations perpetrated against women and girls.  The 2021 HNO indicated that there are 2,287,484 People in need of GBV services, out of which the GBV Sub Sector is targeting 890,303.
 As a continuation of the incredible achievements in GBV programming reported in 2020, UNFPA Sudan will  contribute to the three GBV Sub -Sector objectives: 
1- Strengthen the provision of life- saving specialized quality GBV services, for survivors of GBV and vulnerable women and girls. (with a focus on women and girls with disabilities and adolescent girls (Linked to HRP Strategic Objective 1), through the provision of different services to vulnerable women & girls including GBV survivors (Case management, PSS, referrals), assessments, community awareness-raising, and programming, provision of dignity kits, and capacity building of GBV frontline actors.
2-Enhance strategies for community resilience through the empowerment of women and girls and strengthened community-based interventions(Linked to HRP Strategic Objective 2), by supporting women centers, community protection networks, and  training of women & girls on vocational skills, 
3- Promote GBV risk mitigation into all aspects of the humanitarian response (Linked to HRP Strategic Objective 3), by training on GBV for Non-GBV actors.

 Overall target : 400,000 (45% of GBV SS Target).

project_name: Restore access to safe and quality education opportunities during COVID-19 pandemic in safe operating environment
project_objective:
This project aims at building the resilience of the poorest, most-in-need and hardest-to-reach children. It targets 881 communities and 549,712 vulnerable children (50% girls and 2% children with disabilities) with below breakdown:
•	IDPs & Returnees Children: 163,000
•	Vulnerable Residents: 386,712

The project should provide integrated and sustainable assistance through interventions that promote resilience amongst affected populations and strengthen human security. The whole child approach using the Child Friendly Schools (CFS) framework needs to be clearly reflected with the following five thematic components: (i) Inclusiveness; (ii) Effective Teaching and Learning; (iii) Safe, Healthy and Protective Learning Environment; (iv) Gender Responsiveness; (v) Community and Child Participation.

project_name: Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) for Conflict Affected People in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
Through its Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) activities, NRC Ukraine will ensure that its beneficiaries have increased knowledge of and access to rights related to legal documentation, pension payments, access to services, IDP registration, freedom of movement, and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights and durable solutions. ICLA’s efforts will be organized with a key focuses on sustainability through local partnerships and providing services to hard-to-reach and contact-line communities as well as increasing the outreach to conflict-affected population via digital and remote means of communication.

NRC ICLA aims to support conflict-affected population in eastern Ukraine (CAP), broadly defined as individuals who have suffered harm, including physical or mental injury, emotional suffering, economic loss or substantial impairment of their human rights and fundamental freedoms as a direct result of the conflict in eastern Ukraine. CAP include: IDP (registered or not); people at risk of displacement and people who are unable to flee; returnees; host families or communities. 

With the aim to address the humanitarian protection needs in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, NRC will implement a multi-faceted response. NRC will maintain a significant level of the direct implementation of protective legal aid to CAP, while strategically moving forward with a transition of service delivery to local partners via a series of activities aimed at transferring key skills and experience, enhancing relevant capacity and establishing a localized paralegal network.

NRC will maintain the current direct legal aid modalities like in-person reception of beneficiaries in Legal Aid Centres, field visits and hotline maintenance, while also improving the provision of legal aid via such digital means as email, Skype and messengers in order to maintain the former to tackle the challenges imposed by the COVID-19 Pandemic. 

The network of paralegals – activists providing free legal aid services to member of their respective settlements, will be established in order to enable access to justice and free legal aid provision in the contact-line communities and build resilience of local communities. 

As the current beneficiary caseload could not be fully catered by the national actors only, ICLA will embark on a holistic technical and institutional capacity enhancement initiative with the aim to enable sustainable and resilient transition process. Thus, the target group for such activities will include
duty-bearer beneficiaries - central, regional and local legislative, executive and judicial authorities responsible for various aspects of the CAP issues, and other stakeholder beneficiaries - professional national associations/institutions (Law Faculties and Legal Aid Clinics, Free Legal Aid Centres) and nation-wide, long-standing NGOs, as well as local civil society organisations / initiatives / associations representing interests of conflict-affected people. 

NRC will tie the mentioned activities together through advocacy on key protection issues impacting Ukrainians affected by conflict through working groups, technical forums, and by supporting partners in strategic litigation.
NRC Ukraine will ensure that a strong emphasis on reaching the most vulnerable beneficiaries will be put, while also securing the sufficient level of gender mainstreaming efforts within all its activities via involvement of different age and gender groups into Programme response design. The vulnerable target groups will include (but not limited to), women/single headed households, especially with a large number of children, elderly (particularly living alone), people with disabilities or limited mobility, extremely poor and no-income families, people of pre-retirement age, people living in rural or remote areas. It is important to stress that this will include persons from GCA and NGCA, the latter being targeted through a range of modalities.

project_name: Providing immediate WASH assistance to health facilities and conflict-affected populations in Ukraine
project_objective:
Water and access to sanitation continues to be a major priority for 2021. Interruptions in water supply in villages along the contact line prevent communities, households, and schools from having access to safe water and sanitation facilities  affecting over 1.1. million people on both sides of the contact line increasing health risks. Water scarcity is particularly acute in communities within 5 km of the contact line as some communities have lost complete access. Prior to the conflict, communities were able to drill wells as an alternative to access potable water for drinking, hygiene and irrigation but climate change and conflict has rendered that option impossible.   

Risks associated with lack of access to reliable water sources and sanitation facilities across the contact line have been exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic. Communities were already lacking adequate access to healthcare as many health facilities had been damaged by the conflict. However as demand for health services due to the Covid-19 pandemic went up, the lack of adequate sanitation facilities at health care facilities is now a potential source of infection for the population; only 84.2% of Health Care Facilities have access to water points, of which 75% requires some forms of repair and only half of HCFs had enough handwashing stations.  With health services and emergency medical care in conflict-affected Luhansk and Donetsk Oblasts already underfunded pre-Covid and with regional and local authorities in these areas focusing on Ukraine’s second wave of infection which is expected to peak in the winter of 2020, it is critical HCFs catering to highly vulnerable individuals including the elderly are resourced. Of particular concern are EECPs where the risk of infection among the elderly is high due to overcrowding. 

In response the Norwegian Refugee Council Proposes the project “Providing immediate WASH assistance to health facilities and conflict-affected populations in Ukraine.” The project aligns with the WASH cluster’s strategic Objective 1. “Provide emergency and time-critical assistance and ensure access to basic essential services to 2 million conflict-affected people with humanitarian needs.” Through a three-pronged geographic approach (communities along the contact line, Health Care Facilities & Social Service Institutions, and EECPs) the project will “Increase the resilience of communities affected populations by strengthening the humanitarian WASH response to provide adequate access to water and sanitation in communities along the contact line.”  The specific objectives of the project are: 
•	Access to safe water through decentralized systems in communities along the contact line is improved
•	Communities along the contact line adopt best water management practices.
•	Health Care Facilities have improved WASH infrastructure to respond more effectively to Covid-19
•	Risks of infectious disease transmission including Covid19 at Health Care Facilities are mitigated.
•	Risks of Infectious Disease Transmission including Covid19 at three EECPs in Luhansk are mitigated through handwashing stations and improved WASH facilities.
The project will benefit 70,000 individuals in communities located within 5 & 20 kms of the contact line in Luhansk and Donetsk Oblasts. It will also address immediate humanitarian WASH needs in communities beyond 20 kms to prevent the spread of Covid-19.

project_name: Whole of Syria PSEA Program
project_objective:
Since its initiation by the Syria Strategic Steering Group in 2017, the Whole of Syria (WoS) Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Program has supported the interagency humanitarian response in the joint implementation of international PSEA commitments. The WoS PSEA program was the first of its kind – a multi-donor, comprehensive response, designed to address the risks of SEA posed by the complex and protracted humanitarian emergency in Syria. The PSEA program is designed to cover diverse contexts, including the remote management context of the cross-border operations in northwest (NWS), the humanitarian response in northeast (NES), and the South & Central Syria response. Through an established, robust interagency PSEA Network consisting of more than 140 UN agencies, INGOs and NGOs, the program strives to decrease the risk of crisis‐affected communities experiencing incidents of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) by humanitarian workers and provide technical and operational support to humanitarian actors to prevent and respond to SEA cases.

The program aims to build upon and deepen the impact of the PSEA program implementation in previous years. While integrating the recommendations from the recent WoS PSEA Program Evaluation, the project intends to:
- Maintain the coordination capacity for the WoS PSEA program with systematic engagement with dedicated staff leading the PSEA network hubs in Northeast Syria (NES), Northwest Syria (NWS), and Damascus, and expand outreach to include more organizations. Close coordination between the three hubs will continue and they will meet regularly to share updates, best practices and resources.
- Build the PSEA capacity of humanitarian workers through interactive trainings and deepen the impact of capacity-building initiatives to ensure the sustainability of PSEA programming.
- Provide technical assistance, mentoring and capacity building to organizations in responding to and investigating SEA cases.
- Integrate PSEA indicators and minimum standards for project development and design and ensure a PSEA lens into third-party monitoring activities.
- Support partners to conduct assessments, consultations, awareness-raising sessions and advanced training with affected populations and humanitarian workers in Syria.
- Expand project scope to reach the full range of actors engaged in humanitarian assistance, including local authorities and service providers.
- Maintain the interagency PSEA call center along with other established referral pathways, with a focus on safe referrals and provision of survivor services through GBV mechanisms.
- Strengthen PSEA mainstreaming into the humanitarian infrastructure, through the integration of PSEA messaging into key multisectoral tools, assessments, and guidance documents used by organizations in the WoS response.

project_name: Provision of life saving comprehensive sexual reproductive health and rights services, including information and access, for Rohingya refugees and host communities in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
To improve equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving and comprehensive sexual reproductive health (SRHR) services for Rohingya refugees and host communities, UNFPA will continue to strengthen health systems and community engagement through coordination and partnership within the health sector and key players, including the gender based violence [GBV] Sub-Sector and community health worker [CHW] Working Group actors to provide strategic, technical and programme guidance related to provision  and delivery of  a continuum of care package for  essential SRHR services to the last mile.

UNFPA will ensure continuous availability of family planning and other related SRH commodities, supplies and equipment through improved supply chain management, including contraceptives to meet the unmet needs of refugees and host communities.        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     The project will improve and maintain the quality of services provided, strengthen referral pathways and transfer of obstetric emergency cases, maintain continuous supply of life saving SRHR commodities and  client centered quality midwifery led and respectful antenatal care, safe birth, postnatal care, menstrual regulation, cervical cancer and obstetric fistula screening and treatment, adolescent SRHR, quality assurance and referral for obstetric emergency care provided through mentorship and support to service providers. Health providers' capacity will be strengthened in the provision of integrated client centered quality services, including family planning. In addition, community based SRHR services and behavioural change approaches will be strengthened.             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     The COVID-19 pandemic continues to stretch the health system and widen the existing gaps in the provision of the comprehensive SRHR services and key interventions. To ensure the continuity of provision of SRHR services during COVID-19, interventions will be continued, including operationalisation of maternity red zones and Isolation Treatment Centres [ITC] with maternity care. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 UNFPA will also strengthen readiness to meet SRHR needs during disasters through capacity building, stock prepositioning, and SRHR policy formulation.

project_name: Addressing GBV in Syria
project_objective: The project aims to ensure the provision of quality GBV response services to survivors and women and girls at risk throughout Syria as well as ensuring measures are put in place to prevent and mitigate the risks of GBV.

project_name: Increase access to lifesaving sexual and reproductive health services to vulnerable population affected by Conflict and COVID19 pandemic in Libya.
project_objective:
In 2020, 3.5 million population lacks consistent access to primary and secondary health care services. This is due to the reason that more than half of the functional health facilities in 2019 are closed due to the intensification of conflict and the onset of COVID19 in 2020. Lifesaving health services such as reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent Health (RMNCAH) and mental health services have been severely disrupted, neglected and underfunded in the past many years. The situation amid COVID19 pandemic is further compounded by lack of personal protective equipment (PPEs), delays in payment of salaries to the health care providers, and closer of many health facilities or the suspension of operations especially in maternity hospitals in urban areas. The supply chain management for medical supplies, equipment and pharmaceuticals are globally and locally disrupted and it has closed many public health facilities. Due to this situation, majority of the patients are now referring to private health care facilities, which is making out of pocket expenditure more catastrophic for the people, especially for IDPs, migrants and people living in conflict zones or along the migration routes in Libya.

This project is designed to maintain and provide emergency reproductive and sexual health services amid covid19 pandemic to 53,800 women of child bearing age, among conflict affected, IDPs and migrant population and host communities. The services are planned to be provided in severely affected municipalities / geographical areas ranked above 3 on the severity scale with a focus on un(der)served population. The project intends to provide EmONC services to an estimated population of 9,157 pregnant women. Services will mainly target migrants, refugees, returnees and IDPs and host communities in Tripoli, Benghazi, Sebha, Misurata and Sirt and people in need among none-displaced and migrants are more specifically targeted in affected municipalities or hard to reach areas of Ghat, Sirt, Murzuq, Alkufra and Aljufra.
Considering the humanitarian situation in the country, scarcity of midwives and OBGYN specialists, low capacity level and limited availability of female healthcare providers (especially specialized nurses and midwifes) to provide quality SRH services and unavailability of SRH supplies in the health facilities, there is clearly the need for a humanitarian complementary service package. The services that will be provided through this project are in line with minimum initial services package (MISP) for life saving sexual and reproductive health services of UNFPA and Essential Health Service (EHS) package of WHO issued for the context of COVID19 pandemic. UNFPA will work with its partner agencies, stakeholders, communities and local authorities for the following:

1.	Provision of Lifesaving Essential Maternal, sexual and reproductive health services to prevent excess neonatal and maternal mortality and morbidity among affected population.
2.	Coordinate Sexual and Reproductive Health Services to ensure continuous provision of essential SRH services 
3.	Provision of Essential medicine, medical supplies and equipment to sustain health SRH services
4.	Increase access to SRH services through the deployment of mobile medical teams and enhance the performance of existing primary healthcare facilities and community health workers in targeted areas of vulnerable population.
5.	Strengthen health sector and community resilience to ensure social protection and sustainable and equitable access to quality SRH services.

project_objective: Improved access to quality and free primary healthcare and MHPSS for populations without access to healthcare in areas affected by armed conflict in Arauca

project_name: Providing Essential Life Saving Treatment and Prevention Nutrition Services to the Vulnerable Communities in Somalia
project_objective:
At the national level, the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) has remained Serious (10-14.9%) over the past three seasons (11.8% in 2020 Gu, 13.1 in 2019 Deyr, and 13.8% in 2019 Gu). 
Despite the serious nutrition situation, some livelihoods have critical rates of malnutrition due to food insecurity, high morbidity, low immunization and vitamin A supplementation and poor child care and suboptimal feeding practices. The Somalia 2020 Micronutrient Survey shows that there is an increased susceptibility of mothers and children to malnutrition. It indicates that around 40.2% of non-pregnant women and 47% of pregnant women are anemic and similarly around 43% children below five years are anemic, and both these indicators reveal a serious public health challenge. The same survey shows that the situation of Infant & Young Child Feeding practices is well below the acceptable standards. The prevalence of exclusive breastfeeding is at a low level of less than 20%.
In the 2020 post Gu food and nutrition assessment, pockets of GAM above the emergency threshold of 15 percent were reported in 9 out of the 37 areas surveyed:East Golis, Bosasso IDPs (Bari), Garowe IDPs (Nugaal), Galkacyo IDPs (Mudug), Beletwein Urban, Shabelle Riverine, Mogadishu IDPs (Banadir), Juba Riverine, Elberde pastoral).  Morbidity among children was high (≥ 20percent) in 11 out 37 population groups surveyed.
The proposed interventions will cover treatment (Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program for malnourished children 6-59 months and Pregnant and Lactating Women - PLW) and prevention (Blanket Supplementary Feeding Program for children 6-23 months and PLW, Mother, Child Health and Nutrition (MCHN) for children 6-23 months and PLW in the districts where GAM (Global Acute Malnutrition) is above 15%.An estimated 849,900 children under the age of five are likely to be acutely malnourished through August 2021, including 162,000 who are likely to be severely malnourished.
The World Food Program is the leading UN agency in Somalia in fighting hunger. In Somalia, WFP together with the Ministry of Health, nutrition cluster and the partners supports nutrition interventions in the treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) ,prevention of acute and chronic malnutrition and treatment of HIV/TB malnourished individuals. Treatment of MAM prevents children from mortality and deteriorating to Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), which requires extensive medical support; prevent deterioration of maternal nutrition status and subsequent low birth weight.
WFP collaborates with UNICEF and MOH to offer an integrated package of nutrition and health. This program follows the Ministry of Health guidelines for treating acute malnutrition in Somalia.
WFP also implements preventive program: Seasonal Blanket Supplementary Feeding (BSFP) a seasonal program implemented in areas with high rates of acute malnutrition and food insecurity. The purpose of the program is to reduce the incidence of malnutrition. The target group is non-malnourished children 6-23 months and PLW.
Mother and Child Health and Nutrition Program (MCHN) aims at promoting growth by focusing on the first 1,000 days of life which contributes to prevent acute and chronic malnutrition and break the inter-generational cycle of malnutrition. Pregnant mothers also receive an incentive if they deliver their babies at health facilities ensuring safer deliveries under the supervision of a midwife/or skilled health worker. The program also aims at increasing the utilization of antenatal and post-natal services as nutrition services are offered within the health centres. The target population is children 6-23 months and PLW in the districts where Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) is more than 15%.Worldwide 50% of people living with HIV/TB are malnourished, WFP aim to promote adherence and uptake of treatment.Nutrition and health messaging is integrated across all WFP nutrition programs.

project_name: Provision of Humanitarian Air Services in Somalia
project_objective: Due to the ﬂuid security situation in Somalia, air access is a necessity. The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) provides safe, reliable, eﬃcient and cost-effective inter-agency air transport services regular scheduled ﬂights and special ﬂights) to key locations for over 100 UN agencies, NGOs and Donor organizations providing humanitarian assistance in Somalia, thereby supporting life-saving relief programmes.

project_name: Provide food assistance to vulnerable migrants in urban settings in Libya based on face-to-face/web-based surveys analysis
project_objective:
Due to a lack of access, transparence, the impossibility to monitor, and given that, according to international law, individuals under detention in a country must be provided the means to live with dignity by the government of this country, WFP, along with the partners of the Food Security Sector took the decision not to intervene in detention in order not to legitimize detention and provide assistance blindly where access and monitoring is impossible. 

Consequently, alternative forms of assistance to vulnerable migrants have been developed and this project, targeting food insecure migrants outside detention centers, has been designed to support the food security and nutrition status of migrants while preserving them from any form of exposure, stigmatization and discriminations, ensuring their protection and promoting their inclusion within the local communities.

WFP and IOM have built its functioning partnership since November 2019 to provide food assistance to vulnerable migrants in Libya based on analyzed data. A total of 25,800 food boxes were distributed between November 2019 and May 2020. The most food insecure non-detained migrants were identified in close partnership with IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Unit and Migrant Resource and Response Mechanism (MRRM) Unit. 

Based on the built success, under the 2021 HRP - Food Security Sector, WFP is looking to work with IOM and local NGO partners to maximise the impacts, outputs and outcomes for people in need, while targeting the one-off life-saving assistance to 27,324 vulnerable and non-detained migrant individuals in urban settings.  

Through its distribution cycles in April 2020-May 2020, WFP experienced in reaching vulnerable migrants under situations having the COVID-19 restrictions. Adaptation measures such as masks, disinfection, social distancing, temperature checks were systematically applied. These experience will be applied to this proposed project in 2021. 

Beneficiaries will be disaggregated by Gender. The experience in WFP's food assistance to vulnerable Libyan in the past years indicates that the ratio of beneficiaries is 69% men / 31% women. For comparison, migrant population in Libya ratio is 89% men / 11% women. Women-headed households are proven to be more food insecure. Consequently the proportion of supported women is higher in this programme.

To enhance the quality and the impact of the assistance, building on the successful collaboration between IOM and WFP, including release of the WFP-IOM joint-publication on Migrant Food Security in Libya, WFP looks to strengthen the collaboration with IOM in joint analysis of IOM's face-to-face flow monitoring surveys on food security WFP’s web-based Migration Pulse surveys.

project_name: Services logistiques communs aux acteurs de la réponse d’urgence dans les régions prioritaires du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
A la demande de la communauté humanitaire du Burkina Faso, une analyse des lacunes et des besoins logistiques a été initié en juillet 2020 afin de déterminer de l’activation du Cluster Logistique pour renforcer la réponse logistique à la crise humanitaire. Cette analyse s’est appuyée sur l’expérience et les témoignages de partenaires et a abouti à l’activation officielle du Cluster Logistique en octobre 2020. Afin de renforcer la transition d’une réponse de développement à une réponse humanitaire, le Cluster Logistique apporte son expertise et ses moyens opérationnels pour mutualiser les besoins et accroitre la capacité de réponse des partenaires. Conformément à son mandat, le Cluster Logistique intervient sur les thématiques suivantes :

- Apporter un support en coordination nationale et provinciales auprès des acteurs logistiques humanitaires afin de fluidifier le partage et la circulation d’informations entre les différents mécanismes de coordination et les organisations afin de minimiser les « overlaps » et mutualiser les ressources pour optimiser l’opérationnalité des actions. 
- Apporter un support en gestion de l’information grâce à la présence d’un « Information Manager Officer » qui s’assure du partage des informations selon les standards et d’accroitre la visibilité et la transparence des activités auprès des acteurs humanitaires de la communauté internationale. Cette normalisation des outils de communication engendre une capitalisation et un archivage des informations afin de pouvoir mesurer notre impact et la corriger si nécessaire, mais aussi de pouvoir l’améliorer.
-Apporter des capacités de stockage temporaire au plus près des populations bénéficiaires pour réduire la dépendance logistique vis-à-vis de la capitale et minimiser le temps de réactivité des partenaires en mettant à disposition des acteurs humanitaires des unités de stockages mobiles dans les régions.
- Renforcer les capacités des transporteurs locaux sur les principes humanitaires, les principes de l’approvisionnement logistique en situation d’urgence et améliorer la transparence des relations envers les organisations.
- Renforcer la collecte de données logistiques concernant les contraintes d’accès pour l’approvisionnement en s’appuyant sur les transporteurs locaux et les partenaires humanitaires pour réaliser et diffuser des cartes détaillées afin d’optimiser et rationaliser les circuits d’approvisionnement en biens et produits humanitaires dans les régions prioritaires du Burkina Faso

project_name: Unconditional food assistance to 250,000 Internally Displaced People (IDPs), local population in the North-West and South-West Regions
project_objective: Through the project WFP will be providing unconditional food support to 250,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the North-west and south-west (NWSW) regions. In line with WFP Cameroon Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2018-2020 extended to 2021), life-saving assistance will be provided IDPs in NWSW. The transfer modality of food assistance to the beneficiaries will be in-kind food through unconditional monthly food distributions to support refugees’ households’ access to adequate and nutritious food, therefore prevent them from adopting negative coping practices. The full ration of the in-kind distributions will provide 2,100 kcal energy per day per person for the beneficiaries who entirely rely on humanitarian food assistance The daily food rations will comprise 350g cereals, 100g pulses, 35g vegetable, and 5g salt

project_name: Food assistance to vulnerable refugees outside Detention Centres
project_objective:
As of November 2020, Libya hosts over 45,000 registered refugees and asylum-seekers from Eritrea, Ethiopia, Iraq, Palestine, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria and Yemen. Some 2,000 migrants and refugees/asylum-seekers are being held in government-run detention centres in Libya. Of these, 666 are persons of concern to UNHCR. Libya faces multiple challenges, including low cash liquidity and fuel shortages, further compounded by lockdown restrictions due to COVID-19 earlier in 2020. The 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview estimates that 604,307 individuals people 7,213 refugees are in needs for food assistance. 

Due to a lack of access, transparency, the impossibility to monitor, and given that, according to international law, individuals under detention in a country must be provided with the means to live with dignity by the government of this country, WFP, along with the partners of the Food Security Sector took the decision not to intervene in detention in order not to legitimize detention and provide assistance blindly where access and monitoring are impossible.

Consequently, alternative forms of assistance to vulnerable refugees have been developed and this project, targeting food insecure migrants outside detention centres, has been designed to support the food security and nutrition status of refugees and asylum-seekers while preserving them from any form of exposure, stigmatization and discriminations, ensuring their protection and promoting their inclusion within the local communities.

WFP and UNHCR have built its functioning partnership since June 2020 to provide food assistance to vulnerable refugees and asylum-seekers in Libya based on analyzed data. As of November 2020, over 17,000 food boxes have distributed since June 2020. The most food-insecure non-detained refugees were identified in close partnership with UNHCR. WFP mobilized its full capacities to provide its ready-to-eat food assistance to some 1,000 urgent cases who were freshly released from detention centres. 

Based on the built success, under the 2021 HRP - Food Security Sector, WFP will work with UNHCR and local NGO partners to maximize the impacts, outputs and outcomes for people in need, while targeting the monthly life-saving assistance to a monthly average of 7,213 vulnerable and non-detained refugee/asylum-seekers in urban settings.

Through its distribution cycles in June-November 2020 and under the separate partnership with IOM in April - May 2020, WFP experienced in reaching vulnerable non-Libyan under situations having the COVID-19 restrictions. Adaptation measures such as masks, disinfection, social distancing, temperature checks were systematically applied. These experience will be applied to this proposed project in 2021. 

The experience in WFP's food assistance to vulnerable Libyan in the past years indicates that the ratio of beneficiaries is 69% men / 31% women. For comparison, non-Libyan population in Libya ratio is 89% men / 11% women. Women-headed households are proven to be more food insecure. Consequently, the proportion of supported women is higher in this programme.
