project_name: Juntos para evitar el COVID-19: Respuesta de emergencia, contención y prevención de COVID-19 y la crisis migratoria en la región fronteriza de Colombia, en los departamentos de Guajira, Vichada y Guainía, y en Venezuela, en el Estado de Amazonas.
project_objective:
Esta intervención de respuesta humanitaria será ejecutada por el consorcio: Alianza Humanitaria ""Juntos para prevenir el COVID-19"", compuesto por el Consejo Noruego para los Refugiados (NRC), Médicos Du Monde (MDM), y Acción contra el Hambre (AAH). Esta acción es complementaria de la acción a pequeña escala proyecto presentado a la ECHO para apoyar al departamento de Amazonas (Colombia) en la prevención y la contención de la enfermedad. La pandemia sigue siendo una situación amenazadora para la vida y los medios de subsistencia de muchas personas vulnerables comunidades de la región fronteriza de Colombia, afectadas también por la crisis migratoria de Venezuela.

Por lo tanto, el Consorcio considera que es imperativo proporcionar ayuda humanitaria y mejorar las capacidades locales para hacer frente a los desafíos de COVID-19. Esta acción se centrará en los departamentos de Guajira, Guainía y Vichada (Colombia); y el departamento de Amazonas (Venezuela - Puerto Ayacucho). La Guajira se incluyó para llevar la intervención a regiones que están siendo profundamente afectadas, tanto por la pandemia y las corrientes migratorias mixtas. Los departamentos actuales, aunque no son los grupos de los brotes más preocupantes y tienen pocos casos en comparación con otras regiones, tienen una población en un alto grado de vulnerabilidad. La marginación, la pobreza, la falta de acceso a los servicios esenciales y la debilidad La capacidad institucional prevalece en todas estas regiones. Además, la mayor parte de su población está compuesta por grupos indígenas de ambos países, con una larga tradición de libre circulación de un lado a otro otro, lo que hace que sea más difícil contener la infección. Por lo tanto, esta intervención tiene un enfoque de prevención-contención, con el objetivo de proteger a los grupos muy vulnerables. 

Las actividades de salud se llevarán a cabo fundamentalmente a través de las Brigadas de Atención Primaria de Salud, que consisten en atención en la medicina general, incluidos los niños menores de 5 años de edad; la atención sexual y reproductiva y salud mental, triaje para detectar los síntomas de COVID-19, y derivación a la ruta oficial en caso de que sea positivo casos. Los psicólogos de MDM proporcionarán atención a la salud mental con un enfoque diferencial considerando la cultura, los contextos y las necesidades de la población. Además, el MDM entregará medicamentos y otros suministros médicos a los beneficiarios siguiendo las políticas de seguridad, los reglamentos y las estrictas normas internas procedimientos. El MDM prestará especial atención a la identificación y atención médica de la violencia sexual y casos de violencia de género de mujeres y niñas de poblaciones migrantes e indígenas, la debida remisión a las instituciones oficiales para la protección. Otra actividad clave será la comunicación y la capacitación en la definición de casos, el diseño y la aplicación de los protocolos de la IPC para el personal de atención de la salud y los dirigentes comunitarios, en coordinación con las autoridades sanitarias locales. 

Por último, se capacitará como primeros respondientes a los gestores de salud que trabajan en las comunidades y en los centros de salud de primer nivel de las zonas afectadas por el proyecto (Guainía y Vichada). Esos centros de salud y/o comunidades estarán equipados con un equipo de primeros auxilios adaptado a la región y al contexto, a fin de mitigar la falta de acceso efectivo a la respuesta sanitaria inmediata.

project_name: Provisión de asistencia alimentaria y reactivación inmediata de medios de vida para personas afectadas por la prolongada pandemia del COVID-19 y las tormentas tropicales Amanda, Cristóbal, Eta y IOTA.
project_objective:
La intervención busca complementar la respuesta humanitaria del gobierno para ayudar a las familias más vulnerables cuya seguridad alimentaria y nutricional se ha deteriorado. El proyecto cuenta con dos componentes que permitirán a las familias mejorar su acceso equitativo a alimentos nutritivos y seguros y fomentar la reactivación inmediata de activos que contribuya a la recuperación socioeconómica.

El primer componente tiene como meta brindar asistencia alimentaria de emergencia durante tres meses aproximadamente a 300,000 personas. Según proyecciones de la CIF, 1.04 millones de personas estarían en inseguridad alimentaria (fase de crisis y/o emergencia) para el periodo de junio a agosto de 2021, lo cual es indicador de que es necesaria asistencia alimentaria de manera inmediata para evitar que la situación de familias vulnerables se deteriore aún más. En esta actividad, a través de transferencias de base monetaria, se proporcionará acceso directo a alimentos sanos e inocuos de manera inmediata y oportuna a familias afectadas por el COVID-19 y por fenómenos climáticos . Para contribuir a la selección, adquisición y consumo de alimentos adecuados, se realizarán acciones de educación alimentaria y nutricional que motiven a las familias a la adopción y práctica de hábitos alimentarios adecuados y a la correcta manipulación de los mismos, contribuyendo al cuidado de la salud de los mismos y a la reducción de desperdicios de alimentos por su manipulación y conservación inadecuada.

El segundo componente consiste en la implementación de acciones para la reactivación inmediata de medios de vida, teniendo como meta alcanzar a 35,000 personas. El hecho de que 1.04 millones de personas se encuentren en fase de crisis alimentaria o peor, según la proyección de la CIF, indica que algunas familias están usando o han utilizado estrategias de afrontamiento peligrosas, como la venta de activos productivos, lo cual es claro reflejo del proceso de transformación que las comunidades atraviesan luego de un impacto (shock), como la pandemia y los choques climáticos que afectaron a El Salvador en 2020. Por ello, bajo este componente, se restaurarán bienes naturales, se iniciará la producción de alimentos nutritivos a nivel comunitario (distribución de semillas, herramientas y otros bienes productivos), y se restablecerán los ambientes necesarios para la reconstrucción de medios de vida. Este proceso productivo, se desarrollará con un enfoque sensible a la nutrición, acompañando a las familias con procesos de educación que contribuyan a optimizar la producción de alimentos para diversificar la alimentación y aplicar buenas prácticas de gestión del agua para la producción y consumo, aumentando así la resiliencia física y comunitaria antes las crisis.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Acute Malnutrition in South Sudan
project_objective:
The food insecurity and malnutrition situation in South Sudan has continued to deteriorate because of unresolved conflicts at national and sub-national level, recurrent natural disasters, compounded by climate change and poor disaster management capacity. In 2020, several acute crises hit South Sudan, further aggravating the pre-existing protracted crises and creating an unprecedented humanitarian situation: a desert locust upsurge, several episodes of flooding, and the COVID-19 pandemic. These further exacerbated the already fragile malnutrition situation in country.  

In response to the high nutritional needs in South Sudan, WFP's project will facilitate the provision of curative and preventative nutrition services to populations affected by conflict and displacement.  The project will ensure that IDPs, PoC populations, returnees and residents have access to emergency nutrition services in order to prevent morbidity and mortality due to moderate acute malnutrition. WFP will continue to work with cooperating partners to support an emergency nutrition response through a preventive supplementary feeding programme and treatment services for moderate acute malnutrition targeting children
aged 6-59 months, pregnant & lactating women, and people living with HIV/TB across
South Sudan.

In hard to reach areas, WFP will conduct direct delivery of life-saving nutrition services through the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). The project implementation will be coordinated closely with the Nutrition cluster and use an integrated approach through synergies with activities supported by other clusters (health, education, FSL, WASH).

project_name: Food Assistance for Refugee populations in South Sudan
project_objective: WFP will provide year-round nutrition-sensitive food assistance through general food distributions or CBTs to up to 300,000 people in refugee camps. On the basis of nutrition screening, WFP will provide specialized nutritious foods for refugee children aged 6–59 months and pregnant and lactating women and girls with moderate acute malnutrition to prevent acute malnutrition. It will ensure that nutrition-sensitive messaging accompanies general distributions and is disseminated by cooperating partners, and that persons with disabilities and other vulnerable people are accommodated in dignified, safe ways.

project_name: Food Security, Livelihood, and Agriculture Support to Communities Affected by Multiple Shocks
project_objective:
Overall, around 5.82 million people are in need of food security and livelihood assistance across 39 districts in three provinces (Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) in Pakistan, of which around one million people (17% of the overall people in need) will be targeted through food/cash and agriculture-based livelihoods assistance packages in 2021. The PIN has been determined by undertaking a severity analysis of the population in each vulnerable districts experiencing multiple shocks recently such as (drought, monsoon rains/flooding, winterized emergency, locust infestation and  COVID) which has affected their food security security situation. Based on available information, two indicators have been used to estimate the people in need: IPC acute food insecurity  phase classification, and percentage of households who have inadequate resources to buy food. The severity analysis classified the proportion of the population in each district into minimal, stress, severe, extreme and catastrophic categories, and 39 districts with up to 4 natural hazards/ shocks and pre-existing vulnerabilities are prioritized across three provinces (Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) in Pakistan. Thus, the final PIN is estimated based on the proportion of the people in JIAF severity level 3 and above and considering the experience of recent multiple natural hazards/shocks and pre-existing vulnerabilities.
Of the 5.82 million people in need, most of them are in 12 districts in Sindh province (2.75 million), primarily because of their exposure to multiple shocks ( monsoon rains/floods 2020, locust 2019-2020, drought 2018-2019), and being in JIAF severity level three and above. Similarly, in Balochistan, around 1.9 million people are in need in 14 districts, because of experience of multiple emergencies such as drought 2018-19, monsoon rains/floods 2020, flash floods/snow 2020, and locust 2019-20). In KP  province, 1.17 million people are in need in 13 newly merged areas and they experienced conflict, displacement, instability in the past and recently locust infestation. The most-affected population groups are refugees, Temporary Displaced Persons (TDPs), and Returnees, people living in districts with a high risk of recurrent natural disasters, migrants (Afghan Citizen Card Holders, Undocumented Afghans), poor and food-insecure households, small farmers and livestock holders, daily wage-earners and small businesses, under-five malnourished children, malnourished pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, and elderly population. The combined effects of multiple shocks and food insecurity vulnerabilities are adverse on the most vulnerable groups owing to their inability to meet their food consumption and other basic needs and over-reliance on negative coping strategies.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Malnutrition in Children Under 5 and Pregnant and Lactating Women & Girls in Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to: 
1.	To ensure the provision of quality, lifesaving nutrition services for acutely malnourished children (boys and girls 6 - 59 months of age) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) among highly vulnerable communities
2.	Improve equitable access to integrated program interventions for the prevention of under nutrition among affected communities
The project targets children aged 6–59 months and Pregnant and Lactating Women and Girls with specialized nutritious foods and social and behaviour change messages aimed at the prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition across selected states and localities in Sudan.
A comprehensive package of food and non-food-based interventions are provided taking into account nutritional vulnerabilities.
The proposed response from WFP is in line with the Nutrition Sector Strategy and with the Multi-Year Humanitarian Response Strategy of Sudan. Through this project, WFP will be responding to the nutritional needs of targeted beneficiaries under Outcomes identified by nutrition sector.
With a particular focus on Do No Harm and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) principles, WFP Sudan strives to enhance protection mainstreaming through the following priority areas: 1) Training and capacity building of key WFP and Cooperating Partners (CP); 2) protection risk analysis focused on safety, dignity and integrity of beneficiaries; 3) integration of protection indicators into program tools, notably Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) tools; 4) design, implementation and adjustment of programs in line with identified protection concerns particularly for those disabled and with special needs; and 5) strengthened partnerships and coordination on protection issues.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan
project_objective:
UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.  The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services for conflict affected people, vulnerable host communities and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster standards.

The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related GBV.

The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_name: Maternal, Infant and Child Nutrition Emergency Response in South Sudan.
project_objective:
According to the IPC analysis released on December 2020, between December and March 2021 about 5.8 million people (48.3 per cent of the population) faced Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity. Of this population, 1.8 million people faced Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity, with 11,000 people likely in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5) acute food insecurity, specifically in the Pibor Administrative Area. The nutrition situation is critical, with 53 counties (68 per cent) classified as IPC Acute Malnutrition (AMN) Phase 3 and above in November 2020 to March 2021. Out of this, 29 counties are in IPC AMN Phase 4, and 24 counties in IPC AMN Phase 3. Of the counties in IPC AMN Phase 4, nearly 80 per cent are in Greater Upper Nile with the next largest proportion in Greater Bahr el Ghazal. About 1.4 million children under five years are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition in 2021, including 313,391 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM). 

The cumulative effect of many years of conflict, displacement, economic meltdown, and lack of basic services perpetuates the underlying causes of malnutrition, thus limiting the impact of treatment. Acute malnutrition is attributed to persistent high food insecurity, poor maternal nutrition and poor infant and young child feeding practices, as well as high morbidity due to a weak health system, poor sanitation and lack of safe water.

In response, UNICEF nutrition experts will collaborate with actors in health and WASH to reinforce preventative activities and treat severe acute malnutrition. These activities will include securing safe water through: rehabilitation of non-functioning boreholes; distribution of water treatment kits to secure safe water; hygiene promotion through distribution of soap; growth monitoring and promotion (GMP) and early child care and development (ECCD); counselling on appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices; promotion of kitchen gardens and cooking demonstrations  to ensure normal physical and cognitive developments; malaria testing and treatment; vaccinations, micronutrient supplementation and deworming to boost immunity; and community engagement to encourage greater utilisation of available services.

To improve community participation and awareness among caregivers and other community stakeholders, UNICEF will use multiple channels to mobilise communities around key behaviours to prevent undernutrition. These channels will include home visits, community meetings, mother-to-mother support groups, outreach in markets and cattle camps, public address systems, road shows, theatre for development, and announcements in churches and mosques. 

Given the current nutrition situation and in response to humanitarian needs in South Sudan, UNICEF and nutrition implementing partners plan to reach 3,726,852 people (2,588,549 children under five and 1,138,303 pregnant and lactating women). The estimated total cost of delivering this UNICEF nutrition project is US$ 54,444,733 in 2021.

project_name: Protection of conflict-affected girls, boys and women exposed to child protection risks and gender-based violence in South Sudan
project_objective: The UNICEF Child Protection programme provides support to the extremely vulnerable, conflict-affected girls, boys and women in South Sudan who are exposed to child protection risks and gender-based violence. The programme includes providing case management and family tracing and reunification services (FTR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), reintegration interventions for children associated with armed forces and armed groups (CAAFAG), explosive ordnance risk education (EORE), monitoring of grave child rights violations through the monitoring and reporting mechanism (MRM), gender-based violence interventions, and critical, frontline emergency services, through integrated rapid response mechanisms (IRRMs). Within the programme budget $10.5M is needed for Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE), $6.5M for gender-based violence (GBV) activities and $600,000M for EORE.

project_name: Internally Displaced Population in South Sudan supported through provision of protection and targeted assistance to promote resilience, protection advocacy and achievement of solutions.
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen community and rights-based protection response for IDPs, IDP returnees and vulnerable persons within their host communities. The project will focus on providing physical and legal protection through advocacy, timely protection monitoring, life-saving protection response based on identified needs and solutions. The project will address Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights issues through the provision of legal assistance, facilitate issuance of property and identity documents, and work with mediation mechanisms to support HLP related dispute resolution. Community-based networks will be utilized as part of the protection response to foster community buy in and ownership of protection. The project will use evidence-based planning to expand outreach and develop the capacity of displaced communities to cope, recover, contribute to and ultimately achieve solutions. Out of 1.6 million IDPs, 475,000 IDPs and IDP returnees will be supported with protection interventions and assistance in seven (7) states and an administrative areas. Recognising the protection concerns linked to food insecurity, the Agency activities also include a scaling-up of activities in South Sudan’s highly food insecure and prioritised locations, i.e. Pibor County, Akobo, Aweil South, Tonj East, Tonj North, Tonj South. There will be continuous advocacy and support in the area of law and policy with relevant government bodies such as the   Ministries of Justice Home Affairs, Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management, and the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) to ensure the centrality of protection, enact the “Protection and Assistance to Internally Displaced Persons Act 2018” (IDP) Bill, National Framework on Returns, and various HLP initiatives. The relevant line ministries will also receive capacity building and technical assistance. Building on UNHCR’s existing operational presence in Bentiu Bor, Juba, Malakal, Wau, Yambio, Yei, the Agency will continue to advance on the 2020 geographic expansion of IDP activities by leveraging both static and mobile presence through 15 partners to Central Equatoria, Unity, Upper Nile, Joinglei, Western Bahr El Ghazal, Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Lakes, Western Equatoira, Eastern Equatoris and Warrap. Response and monitoring will cover 19 identified priority counties and Pibor Administrative Area, including remote or hard to-reach areas, in full support to the Protection Cluster Strategy for mobile assessments and response. Partners comprise of both national and international organizations, with selection undertaken on the basis of their pre-existing presence, access to populations of concern and capacity to carry out static and remote protection monitoring and response. While not all proposed activity locations fall under the severity 3, 4 or 5 in terms of food insecurity, recognizing the fluidly and unpredictable nature of sub-national violence in South Sudan, UNHCR’s protection by presence approach requires presence in areas affected by conflict as well as areas of potential return in light of increased momentum in terms of solutions 
Resources and advocacy will focus primarily on protection response and solutions, either durable or transitional (where the former is not yet possible), including assessments on needs, risks, and intentions and feasibility of durable solutions, while also strengthening community-based structures, supporting HLP initiatives, promotion of livelihoods and peaceful coexistence. Improving coordination and quality of assessments and monitoring will be a key component. A mobile tool was introduced in late 2019 that has enhanced data collection and triangulation of information through timely collection and analysis capabilities, which will further improve information products, leading to a more fitting risk-mitigation approach, reduced response time; while underpinning protection mainstreaming across other operational interventions, including of other Clusters.

project_name: Targeted support to displaced persons with specific needs with lifesaving non-food items and emergency shelter in hard to reach areas and areas of IDP returns
project_objective: The UNHCR ES/NFI project for 2021 is focused on responding to the humanitarian needs of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and ensure humanitarian standards are maintained. IDPs continue to be exposed dire living conditions with limited livelihood options, the lack of access to markets and often more than one displacement.  The need for provision of basic and domestic items remains a priority. Families are often displaced without substantial household items, fleeing with little more than they can carry. Inadequate shelter may also lead to increased protection risks and susceptibility to diseases. In addition, populations in situations of protracted displacement require replenishment of assistance to ensure basic humanitarian needs are met. With COVID-19 preventive measures mainstreamed, considerations for decongestion of sites and number of persons per shelter shall be taken into account in consultation with the CCCM cluster and other stakeholders. Emergency stocks need to be replenished and prepositioned on a regular basis in order to allow rapid response to the identified protection and assistance needs. UNHCR’s material assistance will continue to be targeted and protection focused, to ensure that the most vulnerable displaced households are not left without basic material support, including the specific needs of women and girls are catered for. In 2021, UNHCR will continue to identify the most vulnerable IDPs (up to 30% of the priority target) through protection monitoring, community-based mechanisms, and outreach efforts, to implement targeted interventions aimed at reducing the burden on communities. UNHCR both directly and through partners, will leverage their expanded operational coverage to ensure protection monitoring and participation of populations of concern in RPAs, IRNA and RRM. These assessments, ES/NFI analysis tools, and inter-cluster discussions will reinforce the centrality of affected persons to decision-making, and help determine the most appropriate methodology of distribution, taking each unique context into consideration. The project will focus on delivery of timely life-saving activities, streamlining prevention-oriented initiatives including COVID-19 preventive measures, evidence-based planning, and strengthening community-based protection for capacity development of displaced communities to cope, recover, contribute to and achieve solutions. In efforts to minimize risks including SGBV, prevention/response activities will continue with a focus on community engagement, strengthening referrals and prevention with awareness raising. At the same time, there is an increasing trend and willingness of IDPs to return to their homes. It is anticipated that more development-oriented programming will be implemented in South Sudan considering the R-ARCSS, 2019-2020 UN Cooperation Framework, and the 2018-2022 National Development Strategy for South Sudan. In order to increase the absorption capacity of receiving communities, UNHCR will focus support at the community level, maintaining targeted assistance at the individual level to persons with specific needs (PSNs) and the most vulnerable. UNHCR will use its age, gender and diversity policy and ES/NFI analysis tools, to ensure the entire population is reached, the voices of marginalised members of the community are taken into consideration and the response does not place any person at heightened risk. In 2021, UNHCR aims to reach 50% of the projected IDP population equal to 800,000 persons with targeted assistance to 200,000 persons. IDP and refugee returnees often face additional challenges of finding their houses damaged, destroyed and/or occupied. The need for decent shelter in areas of return is critical to realizing transitional and durable solutions. UNHCR will work with the Protection Cluster and HLP working group to address HLP rights issues through the provision of legal assistance, issuance of property and identity documents, and mediation mechanisms.

project_name: Provision of multi-sectoral protection, assistance and solutions to refugees, asylum seekers and refugee returnees and stateless population and those at risk of statelessness in Somalia.
project_objective: In 2021 UNHCR will continue to focus its intervention on providing protection and assistance and working towards the attainment of durable solutions for refugees, asylum-seekers and returnees working in close partnership with the Government, international and national actors. In addition to 28,002 refugees and asylum seekers and 109,989 refugee returnees (of these 18,050 are expected to be assisted with return to Somalia in the course of 2021) that are estimated to be in need of variety of protection, assistance and solutions support in 2021, UNHCR will also focus its efforts on working closely with the Government of Somalia for identification and protection of stateless people, as well as prevention and reduction of statelessness. The study on statelessness is yet to be conducted, thus the scope of the statelessness is not yet known for Somalia. UNHCR will continue to provide technical support to the Government of Somalia in that endeavor.

project_name: Delivery of emergency and essential lifesaving primary healthcare services to crisis affected and vulnerable populations including internally displaced persons (IDPs), migrants, host communities and non-displaced populations in Somalia.
project_objective:
IOM's 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) project for health will contribute to improved equitable access and utilization of emergency and essential lifesaving primary healthcare services among the most vulnerable and crisis-affected populations including IDPs, migrants, and non-IDP host population in the targeted locations in the country. IOM will support operation of 33 fixed health care facilities with integrated community outreach, and expand 18 mobile  teams in targeted areas, many of which are in hard-to-reach, remote, or conflict-affected areas with limited or no health actors and thus the population does not have access to basic life-saving health services. The project will benefit directly 596,700 individuals (51% female; 49% males), including 361,535 children under 18 years in the areas of implementation. Health services will be provided in line with the national Essential Package of Health Services (EPHS) framework for service delivery. IOM will strengthen the capacity of health workers to ensure delivery of high-quality medical service through provision of trainings on relevant health topics including outbreak response, and national treatment guidelines among other. The project will also support basic infrastructure rehabilitation and renovation to existing health facilities to ensure HF functionality and safe environment. IOM will also preposition essential medicines, medical supplies in particular for common outbreaks such as AWD/Cholera and measles to ensure uninterrupted supply. Medical equipment, PPEs and IPC supplies will also be prepositioned for swift response in the event of an emergency. To mitigate against recurrent and expected shocks and the effects of continued conflict, IOM will conduct mass vaccination at the entry points to IDP sites, thus increasing immunization coverage and reducing outbreaks of communicable diseases. IOM will also facilitate deployment of rapid response teams at key points of entry to enhance surveillance at points of entry through screening and referral in the event of a public health emergency especially one of international concern. IOM will support provision of maternal health care and newborn care including safe deliveries, emergency obstetric (BEmONC and CeMOC), and  sexual and reproductive health  services (including management of STD / HIV treatment and SGBV particularly in geographic areas where there are no other health facilities for safe deliveries. IOM will provide health education at the health facilities and during mobile and outreach sessions in the catchment communities to raise awareness and enhance behavior change in health and hygiene practices that contribute to excess morbidity and mortality, and to increase demand and utilization of the emergency and life saving health services level. IOM will integrate mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) at facility level and the community (in IDP settlements and non -IDP surrounding host communities). The range of MHPSS activities will aim to improve the local capacity response to meet the MHPSS needs of Somalia’s crisis-affected populations by building the capacity and skillset of first responders and community gatekeepers. The project will establish and support referral pathways including at the community level through the use of trained community volunteers and Community Health Workers (CHWs). This  project will be part of the wider IOM’s integrated emergency response program.

Staff and office costs associated with implementing a project are allocated through projectization, which allows for proportionate allocation of staff and office costs to projects based on the amount of time staff spend working on these projects and to ensure staff have the tools they need to ensure they can fulfil their responsibilities (see budget - International staff costs, National staff costs, Office costs).

project_name: Provision of lifesaving assistance and sustainable solutions through safe Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services, for people in crises and their host communities in multiple regions in Somalia.
project_objective:
IOM WASH is proposing to contribute to the continuation and restoration of access to safe and equitable basic WASH services to overall 380,000 beneficiaries from vulnerable IDP and host-communities in multiple regions in Somalia. 

Specifically, the project will target 228,000 Nondisplaced people (children 107,160; men 41,040; women 36,480; elderly 9,120 and disabled 34,200) and 152,000 displaced populations (children 71,440; men 27,360; women 24,320; elderly 6,080 and disabled 22,800). 

IOM will rehabilitate 50 strategic water sources for multi-use that will provide continued, equitable, safe, sufficient and sustainable water to regions, targeted by the cluster, prone to natural disasters. 

IOM further proposes to construct 3,000 new emergency sanitation facilities (following cluster specifications) targeting populations without access to basic sanitation and hygiene.

The project will also strengthen the capacity of the Federal Government of Somalia and Federal Members States, community leaders and water committees/technicians for better coordination with government authorities and communities and sustainability of the constructed/ rehabilitated WASH infrastructures. In addition, the project will nurture community participation in good hygiene practices through training and community sensitization campaigns.  All trainings, awareness raising and capacity building activities will follow national guidelines on COVID-19 preventive measures, e.g. on physical distancing, to avoid mass gatherings and minimize risks of exposure.

The project is aligned with protection mainstreaming to ensure safety and dignity of affected populations without causing harm. Affected populations and all relevant stakeholders including men, women, boys, girls, elderly and people with disability will be involved in decision making throughout the project activities/cycle. 

Furthermore, the project will be a part of an IOM integrated emergency response program and resilience building, where possible, efforts will be made to integrate IOM health, nutrition, shelter, CCCM and protection activities.

project_name: Improved food production and livelihoods of IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable host communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
In line with the South Sudan HRP and the FSL Cluster priorities, NPA will support vulnerable and food-insecure Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees and vulnerable host communities in IPC 4 locations in Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Pochalla & Bor South Counties of Jonglei State,  Rumbek East, Rumbek Center, Rumbek North, Cueibet, Yirol East, Yirol West and Awerial Counties of Lakes State, Terekeka County of Central Equatoria State and Kapoeta North County of Eastern Equatoria State. The project aims to improve their food security and livelihoods through provision of timely and appropriate main season inputs/kits (Crop, vegetable and fishing), training in improved agronomic and fishing practices. NPA will provide emergency assistance and livelihoods support to save lives and avert total collapse of livelihoods in the target Counties. The provision of agricultural and fishing inputs/kits, training in agricultural production and fishing is expected to improve the food production and in turn the food security of the target households (HHs) thus supporting them to recover from crisis and placing them on an accelerated path to early recovery and resilience to acute shocks.
 
NPA seeks to support 93,714 HHs (562,285 individuals) in the targeted Counties with agricultural and livelihood kits. Some of the kits will be provided by FAO and some will be procured and distributed directly by NPA. Training on improved agronomic and fishing practices, marketing and group dynamics will be done through model farmers and fisher folk who will undergo a Training of Trainers (ToT) and subsequently train the farmers and fisher folk in their communities. The knowledge gained from these trainings will improve the agricultural and fishing practices of the target HHs thus improving food production, addressing their immediate food security needs and building their resilience to future shocks. The provision of agricultural inputs and fishing kits and subsequent enhancement of agricultural production and fishing is expected to contribute to improvement of the Household Diversity Score (HDDS) and Food Consumption Score (FCS) of the target HHs. The proposed interventions are aligned to the FSL cluster objective 2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support.

NPA will employ a community-based beneficiary selection approach which will entail establishing Project Management Committees (PMC’s) to lead the selection of eligible beneficiaries based on the beneficiary selection criteria. Vulnerable HHs with severe food insecurity including female, child, disabled/chronically ill headed HHs; persons living with or at risk of HIV/AIDS and survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) will be targeted in this project. 

The target communities will be the prime movers of the implementation process through their continuous engagement in the project. NPA will hold regular meetings with the PMC’s and community members and conduct Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to get their feedback on the project implementation. NPA will ensure that their feedback is incorporated in the implementation of this project and design of future projects. Further, to promote accountability to the affected populations, NPA will use the community-based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide a platform for beneficiaries to voice any issues or concerns.

project_name: Rétablissement de l'accès aux soins de santé pour les personnes affectées par la crise sécuritaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La région de l’Est a connu une hausse de déplacement de population soit environ 68 0276 déplacés internes dont 443 598 sont dans le besoin dans le district de FADA. Ces déplacements sont dus aux incidents. Au vue du changement de situation sécuritaire dans la région, la tendance risque d’être à la hausse.
Cette insécurité agit également sur l’accès aux services sociaux de base à deux niveaux, notamment en santé : 1) une inaccessibilité progressive aux services sociaux de base à cause de barrières  sécuritaires 2)  Le recul de l’état dans certaines zones avec des mouvements/fuite des employées ont été restreints suite à des incidents sécuritaires 3) l’incertitude des manifestations post électorales car une grande partie de la population n’a pas pu voter à cause des menaces et la suppression des localités. L’accès au service de santé s’est particulièrement détérioré avec la fermeture de 71 centres de santé dans le pays, et 75 autres qui ne peuvent assurer qu’un service minimum. 
La région de l’Est a particulièrement été affectée par des incidents sécuritaires ces deux dernières années. La situation est particulièrement complexe car plusieurs dynamiques s’entremêlent dans cette région charnière avec le Niger, le Togo et le Bénin. En effet, d’une part, à l’Est opère l’État islamique au Grand Sahara (EIGS) mène des attaques complexes et très violentes. Ainsi, une embuscade contre un convoi transportant des employés d’une société minière canadienne dans l’est du Burkina Faso a fait mercredi 38 morts et 60 blessés. Il s’agit de l’attaque la plus meurtrière enregistrée dans le pays depuis le début des violences djihadistes il y a près de cinq ans. Les groupes radicaux ont également menés plusieurs attaques sous fond de considérations religieuses ou ethniques qui risquent d’embraser la région avec l’attaque d’une église évangélique dans une localité à la frontière avec le Niger. Les assaillants ont opéré des tirs indiscriminés contre les fidèles dont des enfants, des femmes et des responsables de l’église faisant au moins 14 morts. 
Les besoins sanitaire dans la région de l’Est sont les mêmes que ceux dans le reste du pays. En effet, l’isolement de certains centres de santé, l’insuffisance de matériel et de personnel qualifié, l’absence de plans de contingence et le difficile accès aux soins pour une importante partie de la population, sont autant d’élément qui fragilise grandement les capacités de réponses sanitaires à une situation humanitaire déjà alarmante. Les indicateurs de santé, de couverture sanitaire et d’utilisation des services montrent une aggravation de la situation sanitaire sur la zone, en parallèle de la dégradation de la situation sécuritaire.
Le district sanitaire manque les capacités pour faire face aux énormes difficultés dont entre autres : la baisse globale de la couverture sanitaire et la réduction de l’accès aux soins pour les populations, le Mauvais état des infrastructures sanitaires, l’Insuffisance des équipements et matériels médico-techniques, la ruptures fréquentes en médicaments essentiels et génériques et rupture en produits sanguins labiles, le manque de formation continue des agents de santé, Défaillance du système de référencement et contre-référencement, le recouvrement des coûts et la gratuité des soins, l’absence de prise en charge de déplacés internes et les violences basées sur le genre. l'objectif général de l'intervention: Contribuer  à la réduction de la morbidité des populations affectées par la crise au Burkina Faso et spécifiquement, elle aidera à Améliorer l’accès à des soins de santé de qualité pour les populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans le district sanitaire de Fada
