project_name: Provision of lifesaving assistance and sustainable solution of safe water sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services for vulnerable population in multiple regions in Somalia.
project_objective: The proposed project aims to respond to water, sanitation and hygiene needs of IDP and host communities in Bossaso, Caluula, Bandar Beyla, Garowe, Gaalkacyo, Goldogob, Baki, Borama, Lughaye, Zeylac, Hargeisa, Burco, Ceel-Afweyn , Ceerigaabo, Belet Weyne, Baidoa,  Buur Hakabe, Xudur, Kismayo districts. The project will provide a holistic response to ensure affected families and their children have access to necessary WASH services to prevent water related disease outbreaks and address acute water shortage, sanitation and hygiene needs among disaster affected communities.  The WASH activities are designed to be implemented at household and institution levels considering people with disabilities and elderly, safety of children as well as dignity and privacy for women and girls. The household level approach will target families affected by flood, drought and conflict. The health facilities level approach will contribute to improve access to quality healthcare and improve nutrition outcomes. The communities will have access to safe water supply through drilling of new strategic boreholes with hybrid power system, rehabilitation of boreholes, pipeline extensions and water trucking. Moreover, Save the children (SC) will ensure sex-segregated latrines at IDPs by rehabilitation/construction of improved shared household sanitation facilities with hand washing stations. At health facility level, SC will try to cover the main gaps through construction of VIP latrines, pipe line extensions including installing water storage tank, water trucking, regular water quality monitoring and waste management. Both approaches include hygiene promotion activities that will focus on community involvement in hygiene sessions, household visits and community awareness campaigns and provision of hygiene kits to the most vulnerable group and distribution of sanitation tools for waste management. Additionally, the project will build community resilience and increase sustainability of WASH services by enhancing the capacity of village level water and sanitation management committees to manage operate and maintain water and sanitation facilities.SC will ensure participation and active engagement with people with disabilities in all stages of the programme. The project will address barriers and risks faced by people with disability when accessing WASH services through consultations, organizing meeting in physically accessible venues and programme outputs are accessible to children and adults with disabilities, such as WASH infrastructure and distribution of hygiene kit distribution sites are accessible to all members of the community, including the most vulnerable groups. Moreover, Hygiene promoters will deliver key hygiene messages through various communication means to reach people with disability through Door-to-door visit. Total target beneficiaries are 116,000 of which 17, 403 (9572 female, 7831 male ) are people with disabilities. Save the Children has extensive experience targeting and seeking positive impacts for gender equality through its programming. Men, women, boys and girls will be involved in all phases of programming, during need assessment, implementation and monitoring of the projects. Women, men, boys, and girls will get equal opportunities to participate and give them special needs keeping the equity of the beneficiary targeting through monitoring and tracking data and ensuring gender segregation. In Addition to this, at the time of NFI distribution, site selection of the latrines consultation and decision-making was given equal opportunity and mostly giving opportunity to the vulnerable and marginalized groups of the community composed of children and women’s  SC will continue to participate in coordination and assess the needs on the ground to ensure that the proposed activities continue to be appropriate to the changing needs and the specific factors that may increase women’s, girls’, individual risk.

project_name: Provision of life-saving ESKs and NFIs to IDPs in Lower Juba and Gedo.
project_objective:
The project is a response to increasing shelter and NFI needs of newly arrived IDPs and those whose shelter and NFIs were damaged by prolonged flooding, displacements due to conflict, drought, forced eviction and inability to repair/ replace them owing to their poor economic situation.

The project targets 2,600 households with lifesaving assistance in Lower Juba and Gedo. In the target sites, newly arrived IDPs continue to construct shelter using cardboard, clothes, plastic sheets and wooden stick that does not provide privacy and protection against weather elements. Women and girls feel unsafe in such shelters while IDPs living in protracted displacement situations in IDP sites, live in makeshift shelters and need emergency shelter and NFI assistance. The small makeshift structures not only compromise physical security but also privacy and leave women, girls, men, boys, elderly and people with disabilities exposed to rain, temperature fluctuations from cold to extremely hot and diseases. 
 
Under the proposed project, HAPEN will distribute 2,600 ESKs and 2,600 NFIs to newly arrived IDPs, protracted IDPs and in the spirit of inclusion and Do No Harm, to affected hosts who have been affected by drought and floods and have not received any support for the last 1 to 2 years. This will benefit 15,600 people including 5,304 boys, 4,992 girls, 2,496 men and 2,808 women. 

The project will also carry out basic site planning to reduce congestion and increase adherence to Shelter Cluster and SPHERE Standards relating to provision of essential services, access, drainage, site planning, fire safety, common areas, etc.
 
The proposed target IDP sites are located in Kismayo and Afmadow (Lower Juba), Dollow, Garbahaarey, Luuq and Belet Hawo (Gedo).

The selection criteria will include newly arrived IDPs, pregnant and lactating women, women headed HHs, physical and mental disability, child headed households, elderly and households with a large number of children under 5 years. People living with disabilities and hosts may constitute up to 10% and 8% of the beneficiaries respectively. 

A participatory process of beneficiary selection will be employed. Activities will be preceded by consultations with the local administration and organizations involved in providing assistance in the respective areas in order to ensure coordination and avoid duplication. HAPEN will team up with site management committees and ensure all teams participating in the selection are trained on the outlined vulnerability approach. 

HAPEN has noted that in Kismayo and Belet Hawo, the materials are locally available and will issue vouchers.   In the rest of the target sites where the materials are not locally available, HAPEN will source for the materials and provide as in-kind contribution. Distribution of the ESKs and NFIs to the selected IDPs and select hosts will be planned to adhere to Covid-19 prevention guidelines.

HAPEN will empower the beneficiaries to undertake construction of their shelters and repair them in future through onsite training and owner-driven approach by engaging the recipients in constructing emergency shelters.

Protection will be mainstreamed throughout the project process. HAPEN key staff are trained in protection and will in turn train all those involved to ensure integration of all necessary aspects. As participation of women is enhanced, inbuilt protection considerations will address any resulting exposure to sexual exploitation and abuse. Distribution sites will be planned to avoid overcrowding and to ensure women, girls and boys do not cover long distances.  

Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) and Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) will be conducted after distribution and construction respectively to provide beneficiary feedback on the effectiveness of the distribution. 90% of the beneficiaries will take part in the exercise to ensure proper representation. Complaints and feedback desks will be established in addition to hotlines.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Shelter Kits and NFIs to the Newly displaced population and the IDPs living in high risk sites in Lower Shabelle region
project_objective:
According to JMCNA 2020, Shelter is the first priority need of more than half of the population. 3.15 million People are in need of shelter and NFI assistance mainly due to inadequate shelter conditions, overcrowding, economic hardship and lack of security of tenure. Lower Shabelle is among the hotspot areas for shelter needs due to its being areas with most frequent and high risks of newly displacement and IDPs living in a high risk sites because of the floods, conflicts, droughts and evictions. In 2020, Lower Shabelle was badly affected by floods which drove more 85000 people out of their houses, destroyed shelter and washed away NFIs particularly in Afgooye, Wanla Weyn, Qoryooley and Kurtunwaarey, most of the needs were not addressed due to fund insufficient, these needs along with the growing needs due to the upcoming seasonal and security related conflicts are to be responded in 2021. Therefore, this project will deliver emergency shelter and NFIs service to   3000 HH (18,000 people  4200 male, 4200 Female  4800 Girls and 4800 Boys) to the people of newly displaced population and people of IDPs living in high risk sites in Lower Shabelle region by distributing 3000 ESK Shelter kit and 3000 NFI kit  due to the unavailability of the NFI kits in the local markets and surroundings in the target area, alternatively, AYUUB will precure basic Non Food Items through Tender process in Bakara and Suuq Ba’ad Market. . During the project implementation, the partner will strongly consider site planning/decongestion activities in the IDPs sites to mitigate the risks of diseases including WASH and the Covid19 epidemic and other social risks, such fire outbreaks and to facilitate the easy passage of the IDPs in the sites.
By ensuring to meet with the Shelter Cluster two objectives in 2021 which are to Ensure that persons affected by conflict and natural disasters have protection from the weather and privacy through provision of  shelter and NFIs and to Improve the quality of shelter and NFI assistance and ensure accountability through effective complaint and feedback mechanisms, the project will closely collaborate with the community key leaders, local authorities in  a better design of the modality of the project through giving an open ear to the beneficiaries in community feedback mechanism that AYUUB has already put in place via the hotline number 2288, enabling the beneficiaries to channel their inquiries and complaints for a better accountability to the affected population  
AYUUB will prioritize the Most vulnerable people in the Targeted areas through employing AYUUB Selection criteria Procedure to meet with the most needy and appropriate households by the project, with special consideration to the disable people, minority groups, female headed house hold and families with orphans.

project_name: Shelter and NFI Assistance for Persons Affected by Conflict and Natural Disasters in Somalia
project_objective: In the midst of increasing displacement caused by conflict and natural disasters in Somalia, AVORD is submitting this proposal with the aim of enhancing the living conditions of affected communities through the provision of shelter and NFIs and rehabilitation of critical infrastructure. Program activities will target 6,040 households (36,240 persons) from affected communities in need in Afgoye, Marka, Benadir, Baidoa, Belet Weyne, Jowhar, Balad, and Belet Xaawo. Combined, these districts host 737,537 IDPs, or 30% of the IDP population in Somalia. Where market conditions allow, AVORD will use a cash/voucher modality for implementation. Otherwise, an in-kind modality will be used during which AVORD will distribute NFIs and emergency shelter kits directly to beneficiaries.

project_name: Emergency and sustainable lifesaving WASH services to crisis affected vulnerable and underserved communities in Puntland, Hirshabelle and Southwest states
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to provide emergency and sustainable WASH services to the crisis-affected IDPs and host communities in Puntland, Hirshabelle, and Southwest states of Somalia. The target population of the project is 40,000 crisis-affected communities who have not safe WASH services. At the inception of the project, AADSOM will hold a workshop to the prominent community stakeholders including women, disabled persons, marginalized communities, and IDPs to familiarize them the modalities/objective and roles such as project objectives, implementation strategies, scope, feedback and complaint mechanisms, beneficiary selection criteria, beneficiary entitlement, and roles. Side meetings with girls, boys, men and women will also be convened to ensure their different needs are addressed. AADSOM will present the project documents to cluster members to avoid overlaps, following the cluster discussions. The project will reduce people’s needs, risks, and vulnerabilities and increase their resilience, to achieve over a period of 3-5 years. They are designed to strengthen coherence and complementarity between humanitarian and development efforts, and ultimately aim to reduce needs and vulnerabilities to a point where humanitarian action is no longer required. In this project,

Water:
AADSOM will provide lifesaving safe water trucking to 2,000 IDP households in Bari, Hiran, Lower Shabelle, and Bakool regions, benefiting 12,000 men, women, girls and boys who have no access to safe water for a period of one month. As an exit strategy, the project will rehabilitate 3 boreholes, 12 berkeds and 20 shallow wells. In order to keep the sustainability of the water source and increase the ownership of the rehabilitated water sources, AADSOM will conduct training to 35 WASH committees and 70 well operators. As cross cutting, AADSOM will conduct community training on DRR and conflict resolution mechanisms. AADSOM will conduct continuous water treatment, chlorination and routine water quality testing to reduce the AWD/cholera diseases. AADSOM will conduct rehabilitated/constructed water source treatment, chlorination and routine water quality testing to reduce the AWD/cholera diseases.

Sanitation and hygiene:
In order to reduce the risk of GBV against women/girls and discourage open defecation, AADSOM will construct 250 gender sensitive and flood proof IDP latrines including 40 latrines with disabled people, and 12 twin blocks latrines complete with hand washing basins in 6 schools and 6 health facilities with equal access to men, women, boys and girls including disabled persons and marginalized communities. 
AADSOM will carry out hygiene promotion and COVID-19 prevention and protection campaigns participating women, men, boys and girls in all groups, which is planned to reach 40,000 people. The HP and COVID-19 awareness campaigns will carry out by 300 CHPs who are trained through this project. Finally, to encourage men, women and children to wash their hands with soap during the use of latrines and to fetch and store the water safely, AADSOM will distribute 3,000 HP kits to 3,000 IDP HHs who are at risk of AWD and/or HHs with malnourished children and pregnant & lactating women. During the project implementation, AADSOM will encourage women and disadvantaged people to take part in the decision making of the community decisions. AADSOM will make continuous monitoring during the project implementation and will hand over the rehabilitated WASH infrastructures to the community leaders with the presence of the local authorities. The project is complementarity with the existing AADSOM food security and WASH projects in the target locations.

project_name: Promote equitable access to services and durable solutions for the Internally Displaced People in Somalia
project_objective:
Somalia continues to face a huge internal displacement crisis. According to UNHCR, there were 2,648,000 Internally Displaced Persons in the country by the end of July 2020. The displaced, most of them women and children, live in informal and unplanned settlements where living conditions are extremely poor and forced eviction is a common threat. Overcrowded and spontaneous IDP settlements are often at risk of fire, flood, and disease outbreaks due to improper site planning and absence of viability assessment at the time of site creation. Chronic lack of DRR tools prohibits IDPs from mitigating natural disasters especially at rainfall when floods damage critical facilities such as latrines and clinics and result in the loss of lives. Poorly maintained drainage and waste disposal systems don’t only cause serious environmental degradation in IDP sites, but also harm health and create safety risks as well as conflict with host communities. 
In this context, AVORD is submitting this proposal with the aim of improving coordination, service delivery and overall living conditions of Internally Displaced People (IDPs) in Benadir, Bay, Bakool, Hiran, Galgadud, Gedo, Middle and Lower Shabelle regions of Somalia. By delivering a number of interrelated activities to enhance information gathering at site level, stakeholder coordination, camp management, settlement planning, and structure, the project will significantly enhance the living conditions of the IDPs and foster durable solutions to their plight.

project_name: Support for Life Saving and Restoration of livelihoods for Vulnerable Populations in Benadir, Lower Shabelle and Galmudug Regions.
project_objective:
Somalia continues to face a dire humanitarian situation, with an estimated 5.2 million people in need of humanitarian assistance. This is attributed to cumulative shocks, including erratic 2020 Gu season, widespread and severe seasonal flooding, desert locust infestation, socio-economic impacts of COVID-19 and protracted conflict and flood-related displacements.

According to the 2020 Post Gu Seasonal Food Security and Nutrition Analysis for September (FAO/FSNAU), an estimated 1.3 million people are facing Crisis or worse (IPC Phase 3 or higher) outcomes through September 2020. This number is expected to increase to 2.1 million people through December 2020, in the absence of humanitarian assistance. An additional 2.5 million people are Stressed (IPC Phase 2), bringing the total number of people experiencing acute food insecurity to 3.8 million. In addition, 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition over the next 12 months (September 2020 to August 2021), including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

The ongoing Deyr rains in parts of central regions of Galmudug pose a high risk of flash flooding especially in low-lying areas. In Baxda village, Caddado district, Mudug region, one person died following heavy rains that collapsed their house. According to a multi-agency assessment in Adado district in May 2020, about 1,350 IDP households and 350 households from vulnerable host community need food security intervention. Seasonal Hagaa flooding since July has resulted in the displacement of nearly 342,000 people, inundated 294 villages and destroyed property and about 15,000 to 20,000 hectares of assorted crops, mainly in rural areas along the Shabelle river valley according to the UNHCR-led Protection and Return Monitoring Network (PRMN) in Somalia. 

Desert locusts continue to cause havoc in different parts of Somalia. In Galmudug, adult locusts continue to spread in rural villages in Galkacyo, Hobyo, Cabudwaaq, Cadaado, and Dhuusamarreeb. The locust problem has a wide range of impacts that worry Galmudug pastoralist as the region’s economic mainstay is livestock rearing. The locust will have a long-term impact on grazing lands and the poor performance of the rainy seasons may lead to depletion of pasture and acceleration of the dry season. 

CPD plans to reach 23,400 people facing severe acute food insecurity in Galmudug, Benadir and Lower Shabelle regions, mainly IDPs and host communities affected by the impacts of floods, desert locusts, conflicts and socio-economic impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic by improving access to food through unconditional and conditional transfers. Weak, vulnerable members of the IDPs and the host communities such as women and child-headed households, people with disability and the elderly will receive unconditional support through mobile cash transfers as per the CWG recommended transfer values per region (Benadir $70, Galgadud $110, Lower Shabelle $60, Mudug $80).  The men and the youth will be engaged in conditional transfers e.g. cash/food-for-work for livelihood interventions that will support community recover their livelihood and meet their immediate needs. Activities include rehabilitation and establishment of community infrastructure such as water catchments i.e. water pans.

CPD will protect and restore livelihoods related to food and income sources for the target communities through skills training to increase household income; rehabilitation and support for productive capacities of communities through agricultural inputs (e.g. quality seed, farm tools, training, land preparation and irrigation support) and livelihood strengthening and diversification (e.g. fishing).

Project will be inclusive by incorporating people with disability, women, youth and marginalized groups in all project phases in the target areas. Covid-19 measures and guidelines will be incorporated in project implementation.

project_name: Support disaster affected populations in Hirshabelle, and Puntland states to protect their livelihoods and food security
project_objective:
In June, Crisis (IPC 3) or Stressed (IPC 2) outcomes persist across the country. Nearly 20 percent of the total 2.7 million people in need of food assistance did not access it, including in riverine and rural areas of the South, where humanitarian access is low. The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Somali economy is significant. Poor urban and IDP households, as well as pastoralists in northern Somalia, are likely to be most affected by an estimated 30-50 percent decline in annual external remittances, anticipated 25-35 percent decline in annual livestock exports, lower labor demand, and above-average imported staple food prices. In most IDP settlements and urban areas, at least 20 percent of the population still face food consumption gaps or are engaged in negative livelihoods coping strategies indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) even after food assistance distributions. Additionally, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected from June to September in parts of central Somalia, where livestock holdings are lowest, and in northeastern Somalia, where the economy is more dependent on livestock, seafood, and frankincense exports. The erratic distribution of rainfall during the April to June gu season has worsened Gu cereal production prospects in south-central Somalia. During the July to September dry season, up to 3.5 million people are anticipated to be unable to meet their minimum food needs and in need of urgent humanitarian food assistance. Further, the NOAA/CPC NMME forecast predicts an increased likelihood of a below-average deyr rainfall season from October to December 2020. FEWS NET’S research shows the NMME forecast has a strong capability to predict below-average rainfall during the October to December rainfall season in eastern East Africa. Combined with the persistent threat of desert locust, the impact of below-average rains on crop and livestock production is expected to lead to widespread deterioration to Crisis (IPC Phase 3) in northern and central pastoral areas and southern agropastoral areas in the absence of sustained food assistance. The conflict between insurgents and the FGS – supported by AMISOM and other forces – and conflict between clans over the control of land and resource management is expected to continue to periodically restrict humanitarian access, cause loss of life and assets, cause displacement, and disrupt trade and population movements. Conflict is most likely to affect Bakool, Bay, Galgaduud, Gedo, Hiiraan, the Jubas, and the Shabelles regions. Thus, AADSOM will support disaster-affected populations in Hirshabelle, and Puntland to protect their livelihoods, support local food production, and prevent the adoption of crisis strategies. AADSOM will carry out the following activities to reach the above objectives:
1. AADSOM will increase access to food and improve nutrition through Unconditional Cash Transfer to crisis-affected and underserved 1,000 IDPs and host communities HHs in Bari, and Hiran regions, benefiting around 6,000 women, men, boys, and girls including disabled people and marginalized communities. The supporting period will be 3 months and the rate is 60% Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) which corresponding to 60 USD. 
2. Supporting 2000 farmers in Hiran and Bari regions with land preparation and input distribution; 
3. To keep the sustainability of the project and increase the production of the beneficiaries, AADSOM will train 100 selected lead farmers on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) to increase their livelihoods production and adapt the new technologies. 
4. Rehabilitation of  5 primary canals in Hiran region through CFW, benefiting 500 workers for a period of three months, benefiting around 3,000 (450 men, 600 women, 900 girls, 900 boys and 150 disabilities). 
During the project implementation, women, men, children, disabled, marginalized communities, and IDPs will be heard their voices and consulted.

project_name: Improving the Protective Environment and access to well-coordinated and gender-sensitive quality child protection in emergency (CPiE) services for children affected by floods whom are facing life-threatening risks (including abuse, neglect, violence, exploitation, and severe distress) as well as family tracing for those separated from families in Benadir and Lower Shabelle Region
project_objective:
The proposed project is designed respond to child protection needs by addressing multiple protection risks faced by girls and boys through a comprehensive set of activities in well-coordinated and gender-sensitive approach by supporting children at risk and survivors including unaccompanied or separated children through case management services that meets their unique needs, as well as preparedness measures for speedy family tracing and reunification (including psycho-social support). 
The project will also work with volunteers to prevent and mitigate risks to children by building their capacity on rights approach of whom support identification and basic support to vulnerable children (including psycho-social first aid - PFA). SOYDA will also work with caregivers on positive parenting as well as provide psycho-social support to vulnerable caregivers affected by floods and made worst by the pre-existing emergencies related to conflict in Somalia as well as COVID-19. Additionally, the project will engage with the community on protection awareness raising on prevention messages on recruitment/or use of children by armed actors, gender-based violence, harmful practice, family separation and risk of dangers in the community (including in IDP camps or the local community) while coordinating with the CP AoR in service mapping operation of the standardized thematic tools and procedures.
The project will establish referral system in schools and support community-based Child Protection Mechanisms for quick and efficient referrals of children with protection needs through service mapping within the community and in the schools (community child protection committees and School Management Committees). This project will strengthen service mapping to facilitate appropriate referrals, coordination and linkages in service delivery to ensure quality comprehensive services to unaccompanied and separated children.
In addition, in Daynile, Dharkenley, Kahda districts of Mogadishu, and Afgoye and Marka district of lower shabelle. Region, SOYDA will conduct and strengthen protection monitoring in areas of settlement of returnees and IDPs through community-based protection monitors working with CSOs in order to ensure that quality evidence-based reports about protection issues and human rights violations and systematic collection of protection related data are produced to inform better response and advocacy. 
SOYDA will involve staff to promote the welfare of children and protect them from harm by ensuring child’s family, cultural background is respected while activities and process are in a manner that does not put the child at risk of harm. Participation of boys and girls, will be facilitated in a responsible and ethical manner. SOYDA will disseminate guidelines on prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) and reporting mechanism. In the long run protecting children from maltreatment, preventing risks contributing to impairment of children’s health or development, so as to grow up in circumstances consistent with safe, effective care with action to enable children have the best outcomes.  
SOYDA will actively support the rights of all boys and girls to participate and express their views in all matters affecting them in accordance with their gender, age, maturity, and capacity. Different participatory methodologies will be applied for different ages (i.e. younger children, adolescents). Effective participation recognizes children and adolescents as rights-holders, it builds their capacity and resilience, and allows them to protect themselves and their peers.
Through non-discrimination principle will ensure procedures wich support and advocate for the access all, displaced and including children to protection systems, regardless of their age, gender, ethnicity, religion, nationality, or disability. Approach ensures that all persons of concern, including boys and girls children and adolescents, enjoy equal rights, recognizing diversity.

project_name: improved access to Water, hygiene and sanitation services to communities affected by drought and at risk of AWD/Cholera in Afmadow and Badhade Districts Lower Juba Somalia.
project_objective:
The humanitarian context in Somalia has remained fragile for a number of seasons; the impact of the prolonged 2016-17 drought is still being felt. Subsequent hurdles, including poor Deyr rains in 2018 (October-December), an unusually hot dry Jilaal season in 2019 (December-March), and abnormal, erratic rainfall during the same year's Gu rainy season (April-June). Even as this needs overview is being written, flash flooding is currently affecting 540,000 people across Middle and Lower Juba, Bay, Lower and Middle Shabelle, and Hiraan - of these, 370,000 have already been displaced. Climatic shocks, combined with other persistent drivers of needs - such as armed conflict and/or displacement - have left around five million Somalis in need of humanitarian assistance.
Shelter and non-food item (NFI) needs are also very high, especially in IDP sites where many IDP households live in makeshift shelters. These makeshift shelters do not provide adequate privacy and protection against weather elements. Lack of tenure security, random evictions and fire incidents further exacerbate the shelter needs of IDPs. About one-third of the Somali population lack essential NFIs.
Access to improved water supply in Somalia is estimated at 32%, while populations with improved sanitation are estimated at a staggering 24%, one of the lowest in the world. Recurring droughts, now a common natural feature of Somalia, combined with internal displacement and a deteriorated network of water points to compound poor access, forcing supply needs often to be met through emergency operations, such as water trucking. Lack of access to clean and safe water has exacerbated incidences of water-borne diseases especially cholera which is endemic in Somalia. This has contributed to a high under-five child mortality rate of 133 per 1,000 live births. Climate change continues to negatively impact Somalia’s ability to achieve food and water security. In rural areas, an inadequate network of pastoral water structures that supply both domestic and livestock water remains the major cause of conflict between pastoralists and settled communities.
The organization proposes sustained solution to improve access to WASH services of the affected people in line with Somali WASH cluster response plan:
1. Provision of sustained access to safe drinking water through construction/rehabilitation of boreholes and water pans. the water pans will done using cash for work. Three strategic boreholes will be equipped with hybrid solar system, this will reduce the fuel cost which has pushed the cost of water upwards. This will benefit 15,000 drought affected men, women, girls and boys in Afmadow and badhade district. 
5 shallow wells will also be rehabilitated and fitted with hand pumps.  To ensure the sustainability and the management of water facilities, WASDA will ensure to enhance the capacity of WASH committees to keep the maintenance and operation of the water source after the project is faced out. WASDA will ensure the maintenance and the appropriate use of water facilities in close coordination with IDPs mainly camp committees (men and women). 
WASDA will also construct 100 flood proof gender sensitive latrines with hand washing facilities and with inside and outside lockable door to ensure the privacy of women and girls. The toilet will also be PLWD friendly. comprehensive Hygiene and promotion awareness campaign will also be carried out to promote adoption of good hygiene and sanitation practices to the affected men, women and children.   
WASDA will closely work with people living by including in the project committees and beneficiaries which will be captured in the data segregation during targeting and registrations. Project staff will be trained on how to identify and mitigate barriers and risks faced by the PWD. To create positive gender inclusion WASDA will facilitate participation of women, girls, boys and men through out the implementation of the project.

project_name: Distribution of essential food parcels to affected and IDPs families in Deir Ez- Zor, Rural Damascus, Dar""a.
project_objective:
About ten years of continuous armed and economics conflicts in Syria were enough to weaken the Syrian communities. The war has left one of the worst humanitarian crises of all time. Millions of people have been killed or forced to flee their homes. Families are struggling to survive inside Syria, or make a new home in neighboring countries.
The economic and social situation in Syria continues to decline and severely affect everybody especially those who have been displaced from or returned to their homes. The humanitarian needs in Syria are expected to remain high in 2021 as several factors still worsen the economy situation that make people in front of a big daily challenge to secure their basic food needs. The Economic pressures are key drivers of need, with large groups stating that the most widespread challenges are inability to afford needed food items and following negative coping strategies.
The purpose of this project is to provide food parcel to most vulnerable Syrian people in Rural Damascus, Der ez-Zor, and Dar'a, as according to HNO 2021,  an estimated 14.2 million people in need of some form of food and agriculture assistance, compared to 9.8 million in the previous year. The food insecurity PiN has risen by 45 per cent in the last year. 
Our contribution to this objective is to reduce the vulnerability of affected population through the provision of general food assistance (which its content designed based on SO1 response package) in targeted areas of this project by distributing food parcels three times during project life, with a purpose of assisting the very vulnerable population in these areas.
The food parcels (including wheat, rice, pasta, raw chickpeas, beans, tea, brughul, vegetable oil, sugar, salt, canned tuna ,canned sardin, halawa, canned meat and lentil)
As an outcome for this project The well being of 12,000 vulnerable families (around 60,000 individuals) in need who will receive 12,000 essential food items four times during the project life.

project_name: Prise en charge de la malnutrition Aiguë Modérée de 81,900 enfants de 6-59 mois et 28,208 Femmes Enceintes et Allaitantes au Burundi.
project_objective:
Le taux de Malnutrition Aiguë Globale (MAG) est estimé à 6,1% dont 1.1% de MAS (malnutrition aiguë sévère), selon les résultats provisoires de l’Enquête sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et la Mortalité (ENSNMB2020) ; ce qui place la situation nutritionnelle dans la catégorie « moyenne » (précaire) selon les nouveaux seuils de l’OMS. Ce taux atteste d’une détérioration de la situation nutritionnelle puisqu’il était de 5,1% dont 1,1% de MAS en janvier 2019 selon l’Enquête Nationale sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et de Sécurité alimentaire (ENNSAB) utilisant la méthodologie JANFSA (Joint Nutrition,
Food Security Analysis) et de 4,5% dont 0.9% de MAS en 2018 selon les résultats de l'Enquête sur la Situation Nutritionnelle et la Mortalité, Janvier 2018. L’analyse des besoins effectuée par les acteurs humanitaires a permis de retenir 12 provinces prioritaires à savoir : Ruyigi (7,4%), Kirundo (7,0%), Rutana (6,2%), Rumonge (6,2%), Cankuzo (5,8%), Makamba (5,8%), Mwaro (5,3%), Ngozi (5,2%), Bujumbura (5,0%) et Muyinga (4,9%) avec MAS de 1,1%. Le PAM en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Lutte contre le Sida à travers le Programme National Intégré d’Alimentation et de Nutrition ont jugé bon de continuer par la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée dans les provinces de Cankuzo, Kirundo, Ngozi et Rutana où le taux de prévalence de la MAG est compris entre 5% et 9% avec des facteurs aggravants tels que la persistance du paludisme sous forme épidémique, l’insécurité alimentaire, la densité élevée et les déplacements fréquents des populations. Le budget total estimé est de 3,954,261 US$ pour le traitement de 81,900 enfants de 6-59 mois et 28,208 FEFA modérément malnutris et renforcement des mesures de prévention de la Covid-19 dans les communautés et dans les formations sanitaires. Le Projet permettra le traitement des enfants pour une période de trois mois et cinq mois pour les femmes enceintes et femmes allaitantes.

project_name: Emergency Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene interventions for emergency affected and vulnerable populations in Somalia
project_objective: The objective of the project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services for conflict, drought, flood and Covid-19 affected people, vulnerable host communities and people in disease prone areas, mainly women and children including strengthening of communities’ resilience to cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. During the proposed emergency WASH project design and implementations women and girls will be consulted and WASH facilities will be designed and located to ensure the specific needs like privacy, safety and dignity of women and girls. In addition, the project is also targeting to reduce the risk of violence against women, children and vulnerable groups while accessing water and sanitation facilities by providing gender segregated and disability friendly WASH facilities and establishing water supply facilities within 500 meters’ distance of the settlements and sanitation facilities within 50 meters. The emergency WASH response will also be implemented by considering the needs of people with disabilities. People with disabilities will be represented in the community consultation process,  beneficiary identification and on design and location of WASH facilities. In addition a certain percentage of emergency WASH facilities will be constructed with disability friendly components like ramps and support facilities to cater for people with disabilities

project_name: Provision of critical child protection services to boys and girls affected by the humanitarian crisis in Somalia
project_objective: Conflict, natural disasters and COVID19 continue to deter Somalia from making significant development strides to benefit the most vulnerable population. The humanitarian context remains fragile for millions of Somalis and protection issues affecting children have increased. According to the protection cluster 5.9 million people need humanitarian assistance. At least 1.8million are in need of critical protection services. Children are the most affected due to exposure to extreme violence which includes recruitment and use by parties to the conflict and killing and maiming. A trend analysis by the Country Task Force on Monitoring and Reporting shows that sexual violence increased by 35% when compared to the same period last year. Killing and maiming increased by 77% during the first 6 months of 2020 when compared to the same period in 2019. Displacement due to conflict, droughts and famine have triggered separation of children from their families and exposed them to exploitation, violence and abuse. Most families and children have resorted to negative copying mechanism. Boys and girls continue to endure multiple protection risk such as family separation, sexual and gender-based violence (GBV), child recruitment, mental and psychosocial distress. IDPs and minorities including children with disabilities remain particularly vulnerable. Integrated community-based prevention and response services that address the needs of vulnerable families and survivors of violence remain a key priority for child protection agencies in Somalia throughout 2021

project_name: Sustain and expand life-saving basic WASH services for the vulnerable drought, flood, AWD and conflict affected and displaced populations in Somalia
project_objective:
ARD is intending to sustain and expand the provision of basic WASH services to drought, flood, AWD and conflict affected populations in Bakol and Lower Shabelle regions in Somalia through the provision of water, sanitation and hygiene services in communities, schools and health/nutrition facilities. The proposed project is also designed to ensure equitable access to Water, sanitation and hygiene promotion services considering people with disabilities and elders, safety of children as well as dignity and privacy for women and girls. Coordination will be maintained with WASH clusters at national and state levels, in addition to coordination with key actors in target areas. The project will contribute to emergency lifesaving and live sustaining   of WASH   as well as recovery and resilience of the target communities and institutions by ensuring participation of beneficiaries in the project cycle. The project will address gender issues and collect sex and age disaggregated data which will be analyzed to identify gaps, provide gender sensitive interventions and ensure participation and empowerment of women and people with disability The accountability to affected populations will be ensured by involving communities, information sharing and engaging them in the complaints and feedback system special consideration will be given to people with disability . Protection of beneficiaries will be ensured during access and utilization of services reducing further risks. The interventions also fit under the sector specific objective to sustain and expand WASH services for IDPs and the affected population.
The proposed project activities will include construction of strategic water sources, provision of operation and maintenance tools, construction/rehabilitation of sanitation facilities, emergency water supply as well as provision of comprehensive hygiene promotion targeting the most vulnerable household in emergency in the target villages, IDPs and institutions, trainings and dissemination of hygiene best practice through IECs with and distribution of hygiene kits to  most vulnerable people  while special consideration will be given to people with disability, ARD will ensure 10% of the proposed  activity intervention is reserved for people with disability while also ensuring their contribution is incorporated in project design, implementation and monitoring phase hence enhance inclusion in decision making process

project_name: Provision of Immediate food assistance to crisis and locust affected vulnerable IDPs and Host Community in Garowe, Eyl,  Dangorayo and Godobjiraan Districts.
project_objective: The response will cover Nugaal Region and target 28,500 beneficiaries (13,965 male and 14,535 female). The project will target mainly internally displaced households, refugee returnees and very poor host community households severely affected by droughts and conflicts across the populations groups of IDPS, Rural Pastoralist, Agro-pastoralist and fishing in the 4 target Districts of Garowe, Eyl, Dangorayo and Godobjiraan. The specific activities will largely include cash based interventions that will target emergency crisis affected households of above IPC 3 level. The planned cash transfers which will include both conditional and unconditional transfers aimed to increase households’ purchasing power and improve access to food and basic need based on the calculated Minimum Expenditure Basket for Nugal (USD 116 according to the latest FSNAU urban mainin markets for September 2020). In addition the response will undertake livelihood protection activities consisting of seasonal farming input, livestock support and diversification of livelihood source to enhance the recovery initiatives of drop out pastoralist, farming and fishing households just emerging from the droughts, COVID-19 pandemic livelihood related disruptions and also cyclones that have hit the Coastal Districts of Nugal Region. The design of the structures and outputs of the project will be required to conform to the required to conform to SPHERE standards including the construction. The project will utilize the Somalia Cash Working Group (CWG) recommended work norms to ensure labour output and compensation based on individual labor input. Women and the disabled shall be prioritized and given suitable jobs within the rehabilitation works. The project is also designed to main stream protection principles and to promote access, safety and dignity for all beneficiaries and in particular women and girls from IDP camps and others who have faced increased risk of SGBV since the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic. The project is also designed to main stream protection principles and to promote access, safety and dignity for all beneficiaries and in particular women and girls from IDP camps and others who have faced increased risk of SGBV since the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic. This will include promoting safety and dignity and avoiding to cause harm and ensure impartial and neutral services delivery all the targeted beneficiaries based purely on needs as per the protection requirements for livelihood programming. The project will equally ensure gender mainstreaming approaches remains key to its implementation. Wide consultation will also be made with the community leadership to develop an all accepted selection based on Community Based Targeting (CBT) selection criteria that will prioritize the most vulnerable households as beneficiaries prioritizing women and children access to the support. These will include women headed households, households with elderly and disable individual and large size poor families and IDP households, rural and fishing households with none or minimal sources of income. Provision of Seasonal inputs: The project will provide seasonal inputs consisting of farming seeds, harvest storage bags to cut on post-harvesting losses, fishing inputs for the fishery livelihood group in Eyr District and veterinary and feeds support to pastoralists in the 4 target Districts. The project will put in place a feedback mechanism to help get the beneficiaries share information related to the project. This will be an important component of the project as it will help guide the implementation process, capturing important details relating to changing needs by beneficiaries especially in view of the locusts and drought situation which has the potential to worsen.  The feedback mechanism shall also to collect complaints expressed by the beneficiaries for action by the project management.  In future the beneficiary data should be encrypted.

project_name: Provision of CCCM services to displacement affected communities in Bay, Bakool & Lower Shabelle regions, Somalia.
project_objective:
For almost 3 decades, Somalia has been faced by political instability, power vacuums, recurrent and devastating droughts and armed conﬂicts that has exacerbated the situation especially for IDPs and made the environment for returning of refugees unpredictable. Latest estimations of displacement conditions in Somalia indicate that around 2.3 million people have settled in around 2,400 IDP sites, most of which are informal, small and scattered settlements in urban or peri-urban areas. Living in private land often means that IDPs are at constant risk of eviction, which further stresses their already vulnerable situation. Protracted conﬂict-driven displacement aggravated by natural disasters, limited livelihood opportunities, limited availability of public services and limited access to durable solutions all contribute to the continued increase in the number and vulnerability of IDPs.
The main objective of the proposed action is to strengthen camp coordination and camp management at the site level, improve information management, and empower community engagement in order to improve access to life-saving services for displaced persons. Through the delivery of comprehensive CCCM assistance, CESDO aims to facilitate better living conditions and protection of IDPs, while facilitating clear focus on moving towards durable solutions with full community participation. CESDO will continue to strengthen its existing site coordination and management in Baidoa, Berdale, Bay region to provide life-saving services to flood and drought affected IDPs.
This project will target Baidoa/Berdale, Waajid, Wanlawayn and Afgoye districts, Somalia and the objectives are to support the improvement of conditions in IDP sites through strengthening the predictability and effectiveness of service provision and protection for displaced populations, to enhance community self-management and information sharing between all stakeholders. CESDO will ensure that all displaced persons are enabled to partake meaningfully in the governance structures and management of the sites by facilitating sites maintenance through cash-for-work and establishment or strengthening of an inclusive community governance structures and support on Camp Coordination and Camp management capacity buildings. Through this project CESDO will reach more than 4,000 HHs - 50 % female, ensure disability inclusion at all stages of the project, Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the speciﬁc consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age and diversity dis-segregated data.

project_name: Multi-sectoral Emergency Response for Vulnerable Populations in White Nile
project_objective:
Nutrition Sector data for HNO HRP 2021 for the two localities (Guli and Ad Diwaim) in White Nile being proposed for this intervention is as follows (on a scale of 1-5 with 5 being worst): For U5 GAM rate, Ad Diwaim ranks 5 and Guli 4; Both localities rank 5 for stunting rate, rank 4/5 for overall nutrition sector severity, are at IPC level 3 and above for food security needs. Majority of the population are practicing open defecation due to inadequate WASH facilities, being exacerbated by recurrent floods affecting White Nile (being on banks of river Nile) and people's deteriorating purchasing power due to collapsing economy and rising inflation rate. The impact of COVID 19 in 2020 has wreaked havoc on basic needs of vulnerable populations in White Nile.
AAH is present in Sudan since 2018, with operational bases in Khartoum, White Nile, Central Darfur and South Kordofan states. AAH is currently implementing two emergency interventions in White Nile State as part of the COVID-19 response (funded by GFFO) and flood response (funded by SIDA).
Overall objective of proposed intervention is Reduce severe undernutrition on children & PLWs of emergency-affected & highly vulnerable households through multi sectoral life-protecting interventions.   Project targets already vulnerable (in terms of nutrition, health and WASH indicators)14 communities in 2 localities, comprising of around 190,209 people, recovering from shocks in 2020 (i.e. floods emergency and COVID 19 and its cascading impact on economy and livelihoods) while these communities were not fully recovered from prior shocks (for instance, 2019 floods emergency). Assistance will be in form of nutrition (support to essential primary health care and nutrition public services, as well as integrated community case management), WASH at health facility and community levels (improving access to basic water services, adequate (basic or limited) protected, and gender-sensitive sanitation services and hygiene promotion services), and mental health care practices gender protection (IYCF, sensitisation on gender discriminatory harmful traditional practices such as FGM and early marriage). Community participation will be fostered via capacity building, mobilization and follow-up of community volunteers that will engage in sensitization activities (related to nutrition, health, hygiene, sanitation, gender). Some volunteers will also be supported to identify and manage cases of undernutrition and common childhood illnesses in the community. Select volunteers will be provided training to be able to facilitate participatory vulnerability capacity assessments (PVCA) at their community levels. Community volunteers will conduct screening and referral of malnourished children and PLW; they will identify, treat and refer children with common childhood illness, do rapid IYCF assessment at HH level and refer PLWs with IYCF problem, conduct home visit, defaulter tracing and community sensitization.  AAH and their local partner in White Nile, CAFA, will co implement this project together, as per AAH localization strategy in Sudan. The proposed intervention will encompass emergency preparedness activities for sustainability of this intervention and as exit strategy - AAH and CAFA will establish Water Sanitation User Committees (WSUC), Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Committees at community levels, in addition to Mother-to-Mother support groups, and provide extensive trainings to community volunteers on several essential topics. All volunteers will be trained on needs assessment and AAH complaint response mechanism. 
Target population is based on HNO 2021 data and White Nile MoH data, with vulnerability selection criteria focusing on very poor and vulnerable households. Key beneficiaries are 14 OTPs and 56 staff (4 per center); 150 community volunteers; Mass Screening: 32,336 (16,491 girls & 15,845 boys) ; 4300 HH receiving hygiene & dignity kits; soft activities to target all 14 village populations.

project_name: Provision of Emergency integrated Nutrition and Health interventions to Vulnerable population in Borno and Yobe states, Nigeria
project_objective:
The aim is to reduce mortality, morbidity and undernutrition by providing life-saving nutrition, health and WaSH services in facility and communities. 
•	Improved access to healthcare services in the target areas to reduce mortality and morbidity.
•	To ensure that affected populations have access to nutrition treatment and preventive services through strengthening the capacity of health facilities.
Based on the needs identified, nature and living conditions of the affected population, local capacity available, the feasibility analysis of services provision, the program will be focusing on; support government to  one PHC per Ward approach in health system for  provision of primary health care services that includes basic management and prevention of communicable for all age groups from children to adults, antenatal and postnatal care services, support to uncomplicated vaginal delivery services and minor perinatal complications, support to referral services. As well as support to Routine Childhood Immunization in collaboration with SMOH and WHO, support to provision of clinical management of minor physical injury, and prepositioning for Cholera and Measles outbreak in the targeted LGAs and finally provision of nutrition services. Providing medical equipment, supplies and pharmaceuticals and nutritional supplies to the health facilities through the award and in coordination with SMOH and LGA authorities. Reinforcement of technical capacity through sector/sub-sector specific technical trainings for quality service delivery. Building institutional and community capacity for promotion and provision of appropriate IYCF-E integrated with priority health and hygiene practices. 
Target:
1. 	Children: 0-59months of age for malnutrition treatment and other children for provision of primary health services. Prevalence of malnutrition, communicable and water-borne diseases are high. The project will significantly change the condition of children in the area by providing health care, CMAM treatment or access to improved water and sanitation, and by triggering behaviours change in both caretakers (e.g. mothers’ feeding practices) and children themselves (e.g. school sensitization). 
2. Women: Women and children are over-represented among the most vulnerable categories of those affected by the crisis and compose more than half of the IDP population. At least 30% of IDP households are headed by women and 40% of IDP women are pregnant and lactating, requiring special nutrition support to meet their food needs.  Women-headed households, with no adult males and high dependent ratios, are vulnerable to seeking negative coping strategies. Despite being producers and income earners for their families, women’s traditional gender roles mean they face reproductive burdens, limits on their mobility, decision making power, access to and ownership of land, capital, information and technology, and limited representation in community management committees. The conflict, insecurity and over-crowdedness of IDP camps has also increased GBV significantly. Women will therefore be a key target of the project, both in its direct activities (e.g. Care Groups), as well as with the women empowerment agenda applied across the project.
3. Men:  Also, men in the communities are provided with primary health care services for the management of non-communicable diseases (NCD) and communicable disease.
