project_name: Emergency WASH Support to returnees, IDPs and host communities in Unity State (Panyijar, Rubkona and Koch) and of Western Equatoria State (Mundri West and East) South Sudan
project_objective:
Mercy Corps has established long term static presence and excellent reputation in the above proposed locations on long term basis. Presently, Mercy Corps is undertaking implementation of emergency lifesaving activities using grants from OFDA, UNICEF, RSRTF and SSHF in the above mentioned locations. In order to move forward and build on the ongoing activities, Mercy Corps proposes a 12 months Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Promotion services to the returnees, host and IDPs communities in Unity State (Panyijar, Rubkona and Koch) and Western Equatoria (Mundri West and East).

The Program goal is to reduce and/or mitigate potential further escalation of WASH-borne or WASH related suffering of already much affected and vulnerable population (including but not limited to malnutrition, diseases, suffering, morbidity, mortality and violence), to provide integration between nutrition and WASH activities, WASH and Gender Based Violence (GBV) to drastically reduce risks relating to GBV of populations being affected by triple shocks of flooding, conflict and COVID-19 through timely, sustainable and equitable access to clean and safe water, sanitation and hygiene services including distribution of WASH NFIs and Menstrual hygiene management for IDPs, host communities and returnees. This is in line with the South Sudan’s HRP objectives and more specifically the objectives being outlined by the 2021 South Sudan WASH Cluster. The program will be targeting about 45,000 individuals in Unity State (25,000) and Mundri West and East (20,000). 

Below are the main components of the WASH program: 
•	Timely provision of adequate clean, safe and equitable water supply to the affected population including households, health facilities, nutrition centers and protection structures by ensuring access to water infrastructures through rehabilitation of broken water points, regular water quality monitoring and capacity building water technicians and WASH-Protection Committees. 
•	Provision of dignified sanitation facilities in a participatory manner to IDPS, host communities and returnees and construction of semi-permanent sanitation facilities with careful consideration of appropriate designs for persons with disabilities, elderly and children. 
•	Promotion of participatory and inclusive hygiene services with much emphasis on behavioral change interventions, menstrual hygiene management and incontinence as well as NFIs distributions that meets lifesaving needs and facilitate individual ownership of personal and community health and well-being.
•	Health, nutrition, food security and livelihood, and WASH integration is crucial to mitigate malnutrition, gender based risks, WASH-related illness and morbidity through referral systems and integrated outbreak response planning. Mercy Corps will coordinate with Health, Nutrition and Protection clusters to ensure an integrated timely response to any need. Mainstreaming of Menstrual Hygiene Management among school going children with an aim to increase school enrolment among girls. 

It should however be noted that, the project will also aim at developing a unique strategy termed as ‘user fee model’ within this project period to ensure future sustainability of WASH activities through placing much emphasis on strengthening the capacity of the affected populations especially in host communities hosting returnees and in some IDP sites (Non-POC and refugees settings) by forming female dominant WASH-Protection management committees since women and girls are the major users of WASH facilities, fencing of water points and setting time table for usage even for boreholes.

project_name: Protección a comunidades afectadas por desplazamiento forzado y en riesgos de desplazamiento, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, personas solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas en El Salvador
project_objective:
La violencia generada por el accionar y el control territorial de pandillas, combinada con la falta de mecanismos efectivos de prevención y protección de parte de las autoridades sigue generando desplazamiento forzado en El Salvador. El desplazamiento forzado tiene un efecto negativo multidimensional en el ejercicio de los derechos. Para mitigar los riesgos, las personas afectadas por la violencia suelen limitar sus movimientos cayendo en una vulnerabilidad más profunda y afectando sus fuentes de ingreso. Una vez que huyen de su comunidad, las personas dejan atrás sus propiedades, pertenencias, educación y oportunidades de empleo. Además, el desplazamiento da como resultado la pérdida de las redes sociales, comunitarias y familiares, al tiempo que genera nuevos retos relacionados con el establecimiento de la familia en un nuevo lugar. 

Durante procesos de diagnósticos participativos realizados por el ACNUR y sus socios, con población de interés, se evidencia que las mujeres, las niñas, los niños y los adolescentes corren un mayor riesgo de ser blanco de pandillas. Las personas informaron que enfrentan barreras para acceder a servicios como educación, salud y espacios recreativos. Las mujeres y las niñas mencionaron de una falta de conciencia sobre los derechos sexuales y reproductivos, especialmente entre las adolescentes y los jóvenes. Las personas mayores informaron sentirse excluidas, mientras que los jóvenes expresaron su preocupación por el acceso limitado a oportunidades de empleo como obstáculos clave para sostener la economía de familias enteras, lo que a su vez contribuye al riesgo de trabajo o reclutamiento forzoso de niños, adolescentes y jóvenes por pandillas. Esto tiene repercusiones a largo plazo para su acceso a la educación, al empleo y su independencia financiera. Los niños, adolescentes y jóvenes enfatizaron la necesidad de servicios locales, espacios seguros, mecanismos de respuesta a crisis y oportunidades de generación de ingresos para los hogares que experimentan desplazamiento forzado y para las personas retornadas con necesidades de protección internacional y sobrevivientes de violencia de género.

A través de este proyecto el ACNUR y sus socios se involucrarán en todo el espectro del desplazamiento forzado, esforzándose por promover el acceso a la protección y abordar los factores que pueden contribuir a un mayor desplazamiento. Se fortalecerá la respuesta oportuna a las comunidades afectadas por el desplazamiento forzado y en riesgo de desplazamiento, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, personas solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas en El Salvador. Las redes de protección para la identificación y referencia de casos con necesidades específicas de protección se fortalecerán, a través del establecimiento de 4 equipos móviles de protección, una red de 140 voluntarios comunitarios para operar en 55 comunidades priorizadas, así como un centro de llamadas y 4 centros comunitarios donde 39,490 personas desplazadas forzadamente y en riesgo de desplazamiento, así como comunidades de acogida, tendrán acceso a información, asistencia, manejo de casos y referencia a servicios especializados, efectivo multipropósito y programas de medios de vida. Además, se trabajará con el gobierno y una amplia gama de actores del sector humanitario, de desarrollo y privado para fortalecer el acceso a derechos, con especial énfasis en el acceso al trabajo y el empleo para mejorar la autosuficiencia de las personas de interés. Al mismo tiempo que, se buscará fortalecer la gobernanza del desplazamiento, apoyando a las instituciones gubernamentales en la creación de programas, marcos legales y políticas de prevención y protección, bajo un enfoque de edad, género y diversidad con especial énfasis en protección a la niñez, atención a sobrevivientes de VBG, empoderamiento comunitario y soluciones duraderas.

project_name: Mejorando la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de familias vulnerables de municipios de Huehuetenango y Chiquimula (5 meses)
project_objective: Debido a las restricciones en la movilidad para frenar el contagio del COVID-19 tanto en 2020 como en 2021, cuyos efectos se reflejaron en la pérdida de empleos tanto para familias del área urbana como rural, el presente proyecto busca cubrir las principales necesidades alimentarias de las familias más vulnerables, que además pudieron ser afectadas por la emergencia de ETA/IOTA en noviembre de 2020 y que debido a la debilidad institucional del país, aún no han sido atendidas y que por lo tanto, continúan deteriorando sus medios de vida. De esa cuenta, el proyecto brindará transferencias monetarias condicionadas y no condicionadas durante 6 meses (septiembre – octubre 2021 / febrero – mayo 2022), de forma diferenciada de acuerdo con el número de miembros del hogar, principalmente para la cobertura de alimentos y otras necesidades básicas. A su vez, dentro del grupo de familias atendidas, se identificarán aquellas que necesitan un apoyo extra para restablecer sus medios de vida agrícolas y no agrícolas, por medio de la entrega de paquetes de insumos agrícolas o bien, mediante el apoyo con capacitaciones técnicas (albañilería, carpintería, fontanería, etc.) que les proporcionen mejores oportunidades de acceso a empleo. Estas actividades se realizarán en los municipios de Cuilco, San Ildefonso Ixtahuacán y Tectitán del departamento de Huehuetenango, así como en Jocotán, Camotán y Chiquimula, del departamento de Chiquimula, lugares en donde Acción contra el Hambre ha trabajado con diferentes financiamientos, lo que ha permitido contar con conocimiento del contexto, así como con las alianzas a nivel municipal y departamental con diferentes instancias de Gobierno y organizaciones no gubernamentales.

project_name: Las poblaciones afectadas por crisis en Guatemala pueden satisfacer sus necesidades esenciales durante una crisis y forman parte integrante durante todo el año de sistemas alimentarios sostenibles y resilientes ante el clima, en los que se tienen en cuenta la nutrición y las cuestiones de género.
project_objective:
Durante el período de hambre estacional, de mayo a agosto de 2021, cerca de 3.5 millones de personas se encuentran en Crisis o Emergencia (Fase 3 de la CIF o peor), y requieren acciones urgentes. Esta cifra se proyecta que disminuirá a 2.5 millones, durante el período de menor inseguridad alimentaria entre septiembre 2021 y enero de 2022.
Hasta agosto de 2021, 16 departamentos son clasificados en Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF): Alta Verapaz, Baja Verapaz, Chimaltenango, Chiquimula, El Progreso, Huehuetenango, Izabal, Jalapa, Quetzaltenango, Quiché, San Marcos, Santa Rosa, Sololá, Suchitepéquez, Totonicapán y Zacapa. 
Mientras que, de septiembre 2021 a enero de 2022, se proyecta que 5 departamentos continúen en crisis (Fase 3): Alta Verapaz, Chiquimula, Huehuetenango, Quiché y Totonicapán; y 11 mejoran a una situación de inseguridad alimentaria Acentuada (Fase 2 de la CIF). 
La población más vulnerable y priorizados en este proyecto son hogares agrícolas de infra y subsistencia con pérdidas de ingresos por daños provocados por las tormentas ETA y IOTA durante el mes de noviembre 2020., pequeños comerciantes informales, jornaleros agrícolas afectados por las limitaciones derivadas de la Pandemia del COVID-19. Estos hogares se ven obligados a utilizar estrategias de afrontamiento de crisis y emergencia para solventar sus brechas alimentarias, como venta de activos y uso de sus ahorros. 
Este plan contempla la atención de 260 mil personas a través de las siguientes actividades 
-Actividad 1: Prestar asistencia directa, teniendo en cuenta la nutrición y el género, a las poblaciones afectadas por crisis: El PMA prestará asistencia oportuna a las poblaciones afectadas por acontecimientos repentinos o de lenta evolución a fin de salvar vidas, proteger los medios de vida y facilitar la recuperación. La asistencia consistirá principalmente en transferencias de base monetaria no condicionadas a los hogares que padecen inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional, aunque se podrá recurrir a la asistencia alimentaria en especie en el caso de que se vean perturbados los mercados o el acceso físico a los alimentos se vea limitado. Para la selección de los beneficiarios, el PMA pondrá especial cuidado en incluir a los hogares con niñas y mujeres embarazadas y lactantes y niños y niñas menores de 5 años.
-Actividad 2: Proporcionar capacitación, equipo, transferencias de base monetaria y asistencia técnica a los pequeños agricultores vulnerables, las comunidades, las cooperativas y las instituciones locales: Esta actividad prestará apoyo a personas, hogares y organizaciones para fortalecer la capacidad de resiliencia a la inseguridad alimentaria y las perturbaciones de origen climático, aplicando un enfoque integral basado en medidas atentas a la nutrición, equitativas y transformadoras de las relaciones de género y resilientes al clima, que se adapten a las necesidades y condiciones específicas de las comunidades destinatarias, así como tendiendo puentes entre intervenciones que aborden las necesidades inmediatas e iniciativas sostenibles de fomento de la resiliencia. La actividad fortalecerá la capacidad de supervivencia, adaptación y transformación de los beneficiarios seleccionados. Se seleccionarán hogares vulnerables con miras a garantizar la participación y la adopción de decisiones en condiciones de igualdad entre mujeres y hombres, que recibirán TBM condicionadas a cambio de crear activos acordados para la conservación del medio ambiente y la contribución a otras inversiones productivas. El PMA utilizará un enfoque de planificación comunitaria participativa y un análisis integrado del contexto. Los activos contribuirán a la gestión sostenible de los recursos naturales, a las prácticas respetuosas con el medio ambiente y a la conservación y restablecimiento de la biodiversidad natural, en particular del suelo, los bosques y las cuencas hidrográficas, para proteger a las comunidades vulnerables de los efectos de la degradación de los ecosistemas.

project_name: Protección integral a personas en situación de movilidad humana en Guatemala.
project_objective:
Guatemala presenta un contexto de protección marcado por el impacto de una crisis compleja y multidimensional cuyas causas fundamentales se relacionan con la pobreza sistémica, la profunda desigualdad socioeconómica y de género, la persistencia de la violencia, los desafíos que plantea la movilidad humana y la capacidad limitad del Estado para responder a los desafíos de protección que enfrenta la población. Se estima que hay mas de 220.000 personas con necesidades de protección en Guatemala. Hasta diciembre de 2022, el proyecto del ACNUR busca responder a las necesidades de protección de 190.000 personas.
Este proyecto tiene como objetivos: i) mejorar el entorno de protección e implementar soluciones para personas refugiadas, solicitantes de asilo, con necesidades de protección internacional en movimientos mixtos, personas retornadas y de las comunidades de acogida; ii) fortalecer los mecanismos de protección para nacionales guatemaltecos y sus comunidades para la prevención del desplazamiento o riesgo del mismo. 
Se busca garantizar el ejercicio efectivo de derechos y acceso a servicios esenciales de la población de interés para mitigar riesgos de protección y favorecer su integración local, particularmente de la población en mayor situación de vulnerabilidad (mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes, personas LGBTIQ+, personas con discapacidad) bajo un enfoque comunitario, de edad, género y diversidad y con la finalidad de fortalecer su resiliencia, autonomía e inclusión. Paralelamente, se pretender fortalecer la capacidad del estado para brindar respuestas efectivas de protección, en cooperación con organizaciones de la sociedad civil y comunidades afectadas, garantizando la sostenibilidad de las respuestas. 
Para el efecto, ACNUR 
●	Proporcionará asistencia a través de transferencias monetarias y en especie, así como alojamientos temporales, asegurando la satisfacción de necesidades básicas en el marco de la respuesta de una respuesta integral de protección; 
●	Brindará servicios de información, orientación legal y atención psicosocial inclusivos y accesibles para la identificación de necesidades de protección, la activación de rutas de respuesta y manejo integral de casos de protección.
●	Brindará apoyo técnico a actores e instituciones estatales, a nivel central y local, para mejorar la respuesta estatal en temas de protección mediante el desarrollo de capacidades y el establecimiento/fortalecimiento de sistemas y mecanismos de protección  en temas de protección internacional, acceso a la justicia, protección social, violencia basada en género y protección de la niñez. 
●	Fortalecerá los medios de vida de las personas de interés, a través de iniciativas para su acceso e inclusión en el mercado laboral, fortalecimiento de capacidades y apoyo a emprendimientos para la generación de renta, disminuyendo los riesgos asociados con la adopción de estrategias negativas de supervivencia.
●	Fomentará la protección a nivel comunitario a través del fortalecimiento del tejido social, brindando apoyo técnico y material para el fortalecimiento de las capacidades comunitarias a través del trabajo conjunto con  organizaciones y redes comunitarias, líderes y lideresas, y desarrollo de actividades de inclusión en las comunidades donde se identifiquen mayores riesgos de protección, con especial enfoque en los riesgos de desplazamiento forzado, la violencia de género y el reclutamiento forzado de NNAs.

project_name: Quality of integrated and equitable health service delivery and effective coverage  to support the health and well-being of children under 5 years and their mothers, including those infected and affected by HIV through strengthening the district and upazila health systems, in Rohingya Refugee Camps and Host Communities.
project_objective: UNICEF will provide support to ensure quality, equitable and gender-sensitive maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health services, sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services including counselling and referral for GBV and support to pregnant and lactating women inclusive of children with HIV, with attention to people with disabilities. The project targets a vulnerable population of 357,414 people across the Rohingya refugee and host communities. To respond to the basic health and nutrition needs of Rohingya and host community women and children, UNICEF will continue providing harmonized health services through the 13 health facilities in the camps (5 PHCs, and 8 HPs) and 3 Diarrhoea Treatment Centres (DTCs) – two of which are hibernated) as well as strengthening government health systems and facilities in adjacent host communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf (2 union sub-centres and 16 community clinics). A special focus will continue to support the continuation of well-functioning Newborn Stabilization Unit (NSU) with Kangaroo Mother Care in Ukhiya andTeknaf UHCs, Chokoriya Upazila Health Complexes. Support will continue to the special newborn care unit (SCANU) at the District Hospital as a referral center with focus on providing comprehensive primary health care services through the Essential Services Packages (ESP) as per Government’s Guideline and SOPs including maternal, newborn care, immunization, integrated management of childhood illnesses, nutrition, acute watery diarrhoea prevention and management, prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and community engagement. UNICEF will also strengthen the Health Management Information System (HMIS/DHIS2) through technical support with 01 HMIS Consultant (based in Civil Surgeon Office) and capacity building of services providers on DHIS2 in coordination with all health sector partners including government counterparts, and coordinate with team at National level in Dhaka to address technical issue in the system. UNICEF has developed the Emergency Response Plan to provide support during the emergency/disasters.

project_name: Access to safe, confidential and timely life-saving services for survivors of Gender Based Violence (GBV) in vulnerable, ethnic populations in conflict affected departments, during COVID-19 pandemic
project_objective:
El proyecto del UNFPA está dirigido a mujeres y niñas en edad reproductiva, mujeres embarazadas y sobrevivientes de violencia de género. El proyecto ayudará principalmente a mujeres y niñas indígenas y afrodescendientes con necesidades humanitarias críticas como consecuencia del conflicto armado que incrementó los niveles de violencia de género (VBG), en particular la violencia sexual, la violencia de pareja íntima (VPI) y la pandemia COVID-19 en zonas remotas y semiurbanas sin una respuesta estatal eficaz, con escasa, nula presencia o baja capacidad de establecimientos de salud y servicios multisectoriales de VG.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo garantizar servicios integrados de SSR / VG, particularmente 1) Fortalecer la respuesta multisectorial que salve vidas; 2) Reducir la violencia de género y los riesgos de SSR; 3) Reducir la mortalidad materna y 4). Reducir los embarazos no planeados y otros daños a la salud sexual y reproductiva. Esto se logrará mediante cuatro productos que, en conjunto, forman un enfoque holístico e integrado de la protección y la salud, en VBG, se espera que i) Las sobrevivientes de VG tengan acceso a una respuesta integral a las necesidades y a servicios multisectoriales que salvan vidas (salud, apoyo psicosocial, protección) a través de la gestión de casos de VG y que iv) Las mujeres y las niñas hayan fortalecido los mecanismos de protección y mitigación de riesgos contra la VG.
Los servicios y suministros de SSR y VG se proporcionarán principalmente a través de equipos móviles en áreas rurales y espacios seguros en zonas urbanas. Con respecto a la respuesta a la violencia de género, seguirá el Marco de rendición de cuentas de la violencia de género y los estándares mínimos de la violencia de género con un enfoque centrado en las sobrevivientes que responda a la necesidad de fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta directa multisectorial a la violencia de género, incluidos los establecimientos de salud (Gestión Clínica de la Violación), otras instituciones de protección y  autoridades indígenas. Con equipos de protección se brindará Manejo de Casos de VBG y Apoyo Psicosocial, incluida la distribución de efectivo incondicional de emergencia para sobrevivientes de VG y kits de dignidad contextualizados a las necesidades locales específicas adaptadas a la pandemia de COVID-19 y sensibles para la población indígena.
Además, se establecerán espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas para promover la protección y el empoderamiento de las mujeres enfocándose en la mitigación del riesgo de VG a través de la distribución de información que salve vidas para grupos de mujeres / comunidades en las áreas más vulnerables.

project_name: Reduce morbidity and mortality due to infectious and non-infectious conditions within the Rohingya population and adjacent host community in Cox’s Bazar through support to government and partners
project_objective:
WHO’s response strategy is aligned with the overall Health Sector Strategy as articulated in the Joint Response Plan 2021. The activities prioritized under this project have been selected based on the Health Sector needs highlighted by the mid-term review of the Joint Response Plan 2020, Joint Multisectoral Needs Assessment (JMSNA)- September 2020, and Population In Need figures (ISCG, November 2020).  WHO remains the only actor in support of the MoHFW with the mandate and capacity to set priorities, minimum standards, and support quality health service delivery.
 In 2021 WHO, as the lead of the Health Sector, will continue support government and partners respond to COVID-19, to work towards equity and quality of services, advocate on behalf of the Health Sector on inadequately addressed issues, strongly engage government in localization efforts and stimulate documentation and publication of lessons learned on COVID-19 pandemic and the Rohingya humanitarian crisis in general
WHO will focus on bringing the COVID-19 outbreak under control through innovations like vaccines, therapeutics( as they become available), and other measures already deployed and support revitalization of the utilization of essential services with quality service delivery as part of efforts to sustain what is achieved in the two and half year before the COVID-19  while maintaining the capacity to continue support response to emerging needs that result from emergencies due to natural disasters and other disease outbreaks in this protracted humanitarian crisis over and above ensuring continuity of emergency services during the monsoon and cyclone seasons. 
WHO intends to continue providing regular and timely information on public health risks and requirements and filling gaps through effective coordination of partners and effective response ensuring access to life-saving interventions mediated by a rationalized health service delivery system.
The underlying principles of WHO’s work remain and will be reinforced to liaise with national government on the governance and leadership through Civil Surgeon’s office and MOHFW Coordination Cell, support in developing and adopting standards, guidelines, and protocols, extending of national programs to the camp settings and; avail of the health workforce, vaccines, and essential technology, health information, service delivery based on minimum essential services package, for neonates, children, boys and girls and women and men in both the Rohingyas and host community. Support will also be extended to institutions that offer access to specialized services including the Institute of Epidemiology Disease Control and Research, IEDCR Field Laboratory at the Cox's Bazar medical college, Cox's Bazar Sadar hospital, and others.
The planned interventions are guided by initial and periodical service availability assessments during implementation, beneficiaries will participate as volunteers in pre-implementation planning and delivery of the project activities as the technical capacity of the different age group and gender will allow for example as guides, volunteers, mobilizers vaccinators during routine activities and campaigns, among others. External assessments and reviews will be utilized as opportunities for the Rohingya and host community populations to directly review the work of WHO. Indirectly through the various organizations, the yearly health sector performance review will also contribute to influencing the coordination of the health service delivery for the affected populations

project_name: Providing Shelter assistance to displacement effected population including IDPs, refugee returnees and vulnerable host communities across Somalia
project_objective:
The project will focus on improving the physical protection and dignity of IDPs, refugee returnees and poor host communities across Somalia through provision of locally purchased Non Food Items (NFIs), Emergency Shelter Kits (ESKs) and construction of Transitional Shelters through cash/voucher/in-kind modalities, through community driven or owner driven approaches, settlement (re)planning training, conducting Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for Shelters and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs & ESKs and participation in infrastructure mapping exercises led by Shelter cluster or any other partner.
For the beneficiaries’ selection and registration, NRC will use an electronic mobile data collection tool called Kobo tool box, which provides an accurate and real time data. The data received through Kobo is easily manageable and transferable. 20% to 30% Poor host community members will be selected to ensure 'DO NO HARM' and other humanitarian principles including humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. Similarly, 15% Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) will also be condisered in each project. For the provision of NFIs, each HH will be provided with a cash of $100 as per cluster agreed standard NFI kit while for the provision of ESKs, each HH will be provided with a cash of either USD247 (for ESK Type-1 with a size of 380 cm x 550 cm) or USD213 (for ESK Type-2 with a size of 360 cm x 440 cm) depending upon the area of land available. If the area available is less, ESK Type-2 will be selected esle ESK Type-1 will be proiratized.  The cash for ESKs will be distributed in two subsequent installments (50% as first installment and remaining 50% as second installment). NRC will acquire the services of local telecom companies (viz. Hurmuud telecom in South and Central Somalia and Somtel & Golis in Puntland and Somaliland) for the cash transfers. NRC will provide a complete list of selected beneficiaries to respective telecom companies for their cross checking purposes. This list will include all details of selected beneficiaries including their telephone numbers and token numbers. After reviewing and cross checking, respective telecom company will transfer specified amount of money to selected beneficiaries through mobile transfer facility.
Beneficiaries will be selected through predetermined beneficiary selection criteria prioritizing the Extremely Vulnerable Individuals (EVIs) including female and single headed HHs, orphans, chronically ill, aged and child headed households. Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age and diversity dis-segregated data. NRC will target total 75,900 individuals (50% females) consisting of 43,200 in South and Central Somalia, 18,000 in Puntland and 14,700 in Somaliland through Shelter interventions throughout the year 2021. Based on the ground requirements and assessments conducted, NRC will target same beneficiaries with provision of both NFIs and ESKs but in locations where only NFIs or ESKs are needed, only respective assistance will be provided.
NRC staff will ensure that the provided cash is to be utilized for intended purpose by coordinating with the beneficiaries and conduct follow up visits with the support of the community leaders, local authorities and the relevant cluster partners. A Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises for NFIs and ESKs and Post Construction Monitoring (PCM) exercises for Tranisitional Shelters will be conducted to analyse outcomes, the beneficiaries’ level of satisfaction and draw lessons learnt for future programming.

project_name: COVID-19: Supporting the outbreak response, access to essential health services and right to health for the most vulnerable in the oPt
project_objective:
According to the Health Cluster, more than 1.45 million Palestinians across the oPt have been identified as requiring health-related humanitarian assistance in 2021, two-thirds of them in the Gaza Strip and one third in the West Bank. This year health humanitarian interventions in the oPt will be dominated by the operational response to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuring that the most vulnerable affected population has uninterrupted access to life-saving health interventions in a safe and dignified manner. More specifically, WHO will focus on scaling up COVID-19 laboratory testing, case management, including MHPSS, infection prevention and control and risk communication, targeting an estimated 350,000 Palestinians across the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. WHO will also support the MoH, health authorities and partners in the provision of mental health and psychosocial support, trauma and emergency care and early essential newborn care to an estimated 226,000 people. WHO will also aim to strengthen respect, protection and fulfillment of the right to health for all Palestinians in the occupied Palestinian territory through enhanced monitoring and documentation of barriers, capacity building with the Ministry of Health and partners, and enhanced advocacy. An estimated 122,000 people will benefit. Finally, WHO will support the MoH in preparedness for any other future outbreaks through the provision and prepositioning of medical supplies and capacity building of staff, to benefit up to 7,000 Palestinians in the first 3 months in case of an outbreak. WHO's project has been coordinated at various levels with all counterparts involved in the activities:
(1) COVID-19 response with the MoH and through the inter-agency response plan,
(2) MHPSS activities - with the MoH and through tri-cluster MHPSS technical advisory body,
(3) EENC activities - with the MoH and UNICEF, WHO, UNFPA coordination mechanism
(4) Trauma activities - with the MoH and Health cluster Trauma WG,
(5) Right to Health - with the MoH, counterparts, and partners of the Advocacy WG.

project_name: Libya C-19: Strengthening Libyan authorities’ capacity to address C-19 related challenges and ensure protection of Libya’s population, including vulnerable groups.
project_objective:
The project will achieve its overall objective by coordinating the financing and response actions needed to reduce avoidable mortality and morbidity and reduce the economic, social and security impacts of the pandemic for both migrants and the Libyan population especially prioritized geographical areas (severity scale 3,4 and 5)  . The main challenges faced by the population post C-19 are the result of the failure to rapidly mobilize financing for appropriate detection and response efforts. This will result in increased mortality and morbidity, significant economic consequences, and reduced resilience. By focusing on the containment, diagnosis and treatment of patients, this Project seeks to help control the pandemic and limit socioeconomic losses. 
In addition, by strengthening the public health subsystem’s capacity to provide health services, the Project will also contribute to enhancing citizens’ access to proper health care. Project activities fall into the categories of biomedical equipment and supplies for ICUs and isolation facilities, laboratory diagnostics, supplies and reagents, PPE for health care workers involved in the case management of C-19 patients, HR and training and capacity building of health personnel involved in defining national protocols for managing the pandemic.
Immediate outcomes will include focusing and strengthening the already established coordination mechanisms since the beginning of pandemic, improving detection through surveillance, taking preventive measures to decrease risk and protect vulnerable groups, and improving the response to the public health crisis and humanitarian needs. The specific objective of this action is to improve the capacities of the Libyan authorities to address C-19 related challenges as well as assist the vulnerable population of Libya, including migrants, IDPs and conflict-affected communities with protection and life-saving support
The overall goal is to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and reduce avoidable morbidity and mortality in Libya. This Action will support the following direct beneficiaries: 
• Relevant Libyan authorities from the Ministry of Health (MoH), NCDC, Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Local Government, Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of Education. 
• Vulnerable populations of Libya, including persons affected by C-19, IDPs, returnees, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, host communities and conflict-affected populations, especially children, women, and groups with specific needs. 
• Direct beneficiaries: At least 643,332 beneficiaries will benefit from this action. 
• Indirect beneficiaries: An estimated 4.8 million people reached through RCCE and 1.7million people living in prioritized geographical areas classified as 4 and 5 on the severity scale.  
The overall goal is to prevent the spread of C-19 and reduce avoidable morbidity and mortality in Libya.
The specific objective of this action is to improve the capacities of the Libyan authorities to address C-19 related challenges as well as assist the vulnerable population of Libya, including migrants, IDPs and conflict-affected communities with protection and life-saving support.
Activities under three main outcomes are operationalized that would be delivered by this Action can be broadly categorized as follows, based on the nine pillars of the C-19 defined in  operational planning guidelines to support country preparedness and response document for COVID19 Strategic Preparedness Response Plan . 

1. Strong national and subnational coordination is focused and strengthened to deliver strategic, technical, and operational support through existing or public health emergency management mechanisms and partnerships.
2. Awareness raised to prevent the spread of C-19 in the population though a risk communication and community engagement strategy to limit exposure. 
3. Enhanced epidemic intelligence through real-time surveillance systems for the rapid detection of suspected cases .

project_name: Livelihood support in Area C vulnerable Communities
project_objective:
The Overall Objective of the proposed intervention is to support vulnerable communities in Area C of the West Bank by protecting the productive capacity of their agricultural activities affected by the deteriorating socio-economic conditions, Israeli violations against Area C communities and exacerbated by the COVID 19 crisis.  The project will be implemented by Oxfam and its three local partners (ESDC, MA’AN and LRC). The project is in line with the country strategic objective three (SOP3): “The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued: The project is in line with the Food Security Sector (FSS) objectives  1- “The resilience and the productive capacity of vulnerable households are restored/enhanced and livelihoods protected”; 2“Households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs”  and 3 “FSS activities, including advocacy and awareness, are planned and implemented in a coordinated manner, in fair partnerships among concerned parties, including civil society organizations, key national ministries and concerned donors’. The project will carry out the following interventions towards the achievement of these objectives: 
•	Activities that will address Objective 1: Support Area C farmers by enhancing and restoring productive capacities: includes rehabilitation of agricultural lands, agricultural roads, improving access to and decreasing water wastage for agriculture through installing irrigation networks, and carrier lines, rehabilitating water wells to obtain more efficient access to water using renewable energy, and rehabilitation of livestock sheds. 
•	Activities that will address Objective 2: Creating temporary cash for work opportunities for farmers and agricultural workers, and support small scale farmers/herders' cooperatives to access domestic markets including food parcels purchase and distribution to vulnerable households, and elderly centers. 
• Activities that will address Objective 3: Provide legal awareness and legal support to 
target communities, in full coordination with Ministry of Agriculture, Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, land and water authorities, Ministry of Social Development and the Food security sector partners/ In addition to carrying out policy and advocacy 
activities that will address the root causes.

project_name: Access to inclusive quality education for all Syrian Children and support to teachers affected by the humanitarian situation.
project_objective:
The UNICEF education project plans to reach a total of 2,904,400 (or 55%) of the children and adults identified in the HNO 2021 under severity scale 3-5 (199 sub-districts). 

This proposal suggests access to inclusive and quality education-as-a-basic-service measures for children affected by the Syrian humanitarian crisis. The below activities are designed to help children realize their right to education, as well as to cope, learn and contribute to their communities in a context characterized by multiple risks and crisis: conflict, the global pandemic, and economic shocks. UNICEF prioritizes the following activities in line with 2021 HNO/HRP: (1) scaling up safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education; (2) enhancing and monitoring the quality of formal and non-formal education for children and youth (aged 3-17 years) within a protective environment; and (3) strengthening the capacity and the coordination of stakeholders, partners and education personnel to build resilience and effective response. The proposal (including for the selection of damaged schools) focuses on Sub-Districts ranked as Severity Scale 3-5. 
UNICEF is committed to Accountability to Affected Population (AAP), and it considers the input of beneficiaries in all phases of the project cycle and makes deliberate efforts to incorporate their ideas, concerns, and feedback throughout. Practically this is done by continuous engagements throughout the project-life cycle to affected populations and their representatives. This is done to ensure that needs of various groups including women, men, girls and boys are known and appropriate response is designed. In addition, UNICEF adheres to the ‘Do No Harm’ principle for the design and implementation of projects. 
For the project implementation phase, UNICEF’s accountability strategy is based on five pillars: transparency, community engagement, learning, and evaluation and feedback mechanisms. 
GAM is also included in the project.
UNICEF’s package for supporting learning activities has several core elements which have been selected based on their impact on children’s participation, retention and learning-namely:

1- Back to Learning Campaign (BTL 
2- Safe, inclusive learning environment
3- Trained, Capable, motivated teachers 
4- Availability of learning supplies: 
5- Assessment of (learning) outcomes  
6- Recreational activities 
7- Distance Education Modalities 
8- Supporting participation in National School Exams of Grade 9 & 12 children from cross-border and crossline locations.

All the above activities will be inclusive ensuring the integration of children with disabilities through: 
•	Light rehabilitation and provision of furniture to the learning centres/schools to ensure access of CwD 
•	Provision of specialized learning materials that support the specific need of different type of disabilities 
•	Capacity development of teachers and educators to enhance their skills and equip them with the needed competencies to work with CwD
•	Awareness session for parents, care givers, and community members on the importance of education
•	Support diagnosing services for early intervention 
•	Provision of educational sessions  for CwD
•	M&E to ensure monitoring reporting referral mechanisms

project_name: Addressing Gender based Violence (GBV) in Northern Mozambique
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims to increase availability and accessibility of quality life-saving GBV prevention/response in conflict-affected locations where women and girls have very limited access to survivor-centered GBV multisectoral services and to basic needs such as Shelter, Food, Wash and dignity kits. Additionally, lack of privacy, crowded living conditions, inadequate lighting compound with the COVID 19 restrictions contributed to increased GBV risks for women and girls. 

The project aims to establish new and sustain existing WGSSs, offering comprehensive PSS support services including GBV case management and in-kind/CBIs as well as GBV awareness sessions, increase free access to integrated GBV/SRH services (with a focus on CMR services) through mobile brigades/static health facilities are the key priority interventions. The use of existing hotlines and GBV focal points/women networking will be strengthened too. 

UNFPA will continue supporting and co-leading the GBV SC coordination, strengthening the GBV Capacity of GBVSC members, services providers (including security personnel), volunteers, social activists, GBV focal points and women led organization. IASC GBV guidelines sensitization/workshops will be also provided to non-GBV actors. 

Furthermore, UNFPA commits to procure dignity kits and post-rape kits to cover the needs of the affected areas. Target groups are IDPs/host most vulnerable women/girls including GBV survivors and those left behind unable to leave conflict areas with a focus on female headed households (widows, divorced), adolescent girls, women/girls with disabilities and older women. Men and boys are also included. 

It is anticipated that UNFPA may take part in ad-hoc Rapid Responses or declared Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) for which substantial Dignity Kits are planned for blanket distribution to fleeing families (especially single mother head of households, older women, single young mothers, etc.) aiming at mitigating risks to GBV.

project_name: Responding to Emergency Sexual and Reproductive Health Needs of Women and Girls in Northern Mozambique
project_objective:
The project, to be implemented in the three provinces of Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula, aims to provide displaced and vulnerable young adolescent girls (10-14 years) and women of reproductive age (15-49) in the Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) relocation sites and host communities, with life-saving and life-sustaining Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal, and Newborn health (SRMNH) services.

The project, to be implemented through Government and Civil Society implementing partners, aims to provide immediate life-saving access to SRMNH services guided by IASC Minimum Initial Service Package for Reproductive Health principles.

The project will also equip health facilities in the 3 provinces with essential reproductive health commodities and supplies in order to establish sufficient capacity for provision of Emergency Obstetric Care to prevent avoidable Maternal and Newborn deaths.

Lastly, this project will establish capacity for and support skilled birth attendance through training of reproductive health service providers in the three target provinces.

project_name: Support Health Sector response to improve access to health care including the ongoing support to COVID-19, strengthening health system recovery and promote humanitarian-development linkages.
project_objective:
As the crisis in northeast Nigeria enters its 11 years, the operational environment remains complex. Despite significant counter-terrorism efforts by the Nigerian military and its partners, access to affected areas remains challenging due to insecurity. The humanitarian community continues to struggle to respond to urgent humanitarian needs with the already overstretched available capacity. The response capacity to a crisis of this scale is not commensurate to the needs of the affected population especially the new influx and forced displacement of communities. Overcrowding in camps continues to be prevalent with over 40 per cent of camps in Borno State remaining over congested. As military operations are expected to intensify in the coming months across Borno State, further evacuation and displacements of civilians is expected. This situation will likely worsen the overcrowding situation and have a direct impact on the health situation of the population especially in light of the ongoing measles and cholera outbreaks in the region. The onset of the rainy season coupled a weak sanitation infrastructure further increases the risk of a cholera outbreak further exacerbating the situation, especially in IDPs camps. In addition, Lack of shelter and food has a direct impact on people’s health especially children, pregnant women, the elderly and other vulnerable groups exposed to harsh weather conditions.
The Health sector, in collaboration with development partners including the State MoHs and Ministries/Committees of Reconstruction, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (MoRRR), will support a comprehensive recovery strategy for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of health facilities with the overall objective of health system restoration and with the underlying principle of “building back better”. Moving away from geographically and thematically fragmented interventions. The program is designed with flexibility to respond and adjust to situation changes and to address the health needs of each community. Provision of well-measured training and incentive packages to health professionals, to offer essential uninterrupted health care services in the communities is an additional priority of the health sector.
•	The COVID-19 response is based on eight key response pillars to address all prevention, preparedness and response actions. WHO and Health Sector Partners are supporting the government led COVID-19 response also in collaboration with WASH, CCCM, Shelter and all other sectors for a coordinated response including the construction of quarantines and isolation centres, social distancing mechanisms, early warning and alert systems for the timely containment of transmission and facilitate joint inter-sectoral interventions. An incident management team is already working at the level of Public Health Emergency Operation Centre (PHEOC), supporting on key priority actions including rapid deployment of designated staff from state and partner organizations in high-risk areas for priority preparedness and response actions, monitoring the POE surveillance, scaling up of IPC measures, development and dissemination of IEC materials etc. Minimum requirements are in place, including functional triage system and isolation rooms, trained staff (for early detection and standard principles for IPC); and adequate IPC materials, including personal protective equipment (PPE) and WASH services/hand hygiene stations.

project_name: Increase the provision of life-saving integrated activities of Formal and Non-formal Education, ECCD, and TVET opportunities to the most vulnerable individuals in NW Syria including IDPs and CWDs
project_objective:
In this project, ATAA is planning to target children and youth including ECCD in locations as follows:
•	Idleb governorate: Dana, Harim, Maaret Tamsrin, Teftnaz, Badama, Jisr Ash-Shugur sub-districts.
•	Aleppo governorate:  Al Bab, Jarablus, Aghtrin, Atareb, Daret Azze sub-districts.
The schools located in Aleppo are 9 (5 off-camps & 4 in camps) whereas 28 schools located in Idleb (5 off-camps & 23 in camps). The proposed project will target children and youth from the age of 3 till 24 who are in the ECCD, Basic, Secondary Vocational Education (Pre-school, 1st & 12th grade) including CwDs to the most vulnerable. These communities prioritized based on 1) its high and med severity, 2) the concentration of new IDPs, 3) gaps in education and its infrastructure, 4) the security stabilization, 5) accessibility by ATAA 6) high rates of illiteracy and dropout, 7) affected by COVID-19. 
In the proposed project, ATAA’s concern is towards the dropped-out children, those at the risk of being dropped out and the newly displaced as a result of frequent displacement and difficult living conditions. The project will provide FE, NFE, ECCD, & TVET opportunities for 15997 (Female;7661, Male; 8020, CWD Female; 127, CWD Male; 189) in addition to 670 educational personnel includes trainers, headteachers, teachers, cleaners and guards (Female; 297, Male; 374), the percentage of students (51% females and 49% males), the percentage of staff (45% females and 55% males).
The project will focus on enhancing the infrastructure by constructing 6 learning centers along with WASH facilities from prefabricated and concrete materials, the other learning spaces based on a rehabilitation need assessment will be provided with minor rehabilitation and school furniture to be friendly environments to achieve safe, equitable and protective education considering COVID-19 measures. The project will be cost-efficient as some of the targeted schools are equipped with furniture, fuel tanks, heaters, book corners, solar panels, textbook, and internet routers, etc.
FE (SIG curriculum) will be provided and NFE (ALP including Curriculum B, Remedial, Catch-up and SLP) to those who have been out of school more than one academic year based on age and period of dropping out, TVET will be given to the dropped out and OOSC who are between 16 and 24 years since they are at the risk of being recruited to armed groups, early marriage and child labour. There will be an MoU signed with ED to recognize the students who got NFE in order to be referred to FE. 
CWDs will be provided with tailored activities and facilities to come back to education. project_name: Enhancing WASH services to host and IDPs in communities and camps in Idleb and Aleppo governorates through sustainable water and sewage infrastructure
project_objective:
In North West of Syria (NWS), deteriorating economic conditions remain a challenge for vulnerable communities and households in accessing safe and equitable WASH services, notably for those that have to purchase services like water from private water trucking vendors. 74% of the off-camp HHs using water trucking as the main water supply modality spend more than 5% of HH’s income on purchasing water only, while the combined costs for water and sanitation services should not exceed 5% of a household’s income. The overall estimated average expenditures on WASH services and supplies (water, hygiene items, garbage removal and desludging) make up to 15% of HHs’ income in some governorates and could be much higher at the individual HH-level. Depreciation of Syrian currency erodes households’ purchasing power and subsequently household spending capacity on WASH services, supplies and consumables.
Through this project, ATAA will be reaching 140,316 beneficiaries (57%female-42%male)- (56% under18 - 44% above18) in:
1- Idleb, Idleb, Maaret Tamsrin: Maaret Tamsrin, and Kelly camps.
2. Idleb, Harim, Dana camps.
3- Aleppo, Al Bab, Suran.
4- Aleppo, A'zaz, Kafr Kalbein.
ATAA, through implementing this project, aims to secure sustainable and sufficient clean water for IDPs and host communities in the communities and surrounding IDPs camps by establishing a sustainable drinking water system and connect it to the main water stations, and support the operation cost for the water stations, the water system will be connected to the chlorination unit, the outlet of the chlorination unit will connect to the (ground, or high) main water tanks, and ATAA will connect this main water tanks to the main water networks.
ATAA will establish water units in the targeted locations and provide them with O&M training, and work closely with the local councils to establish the tariff system for sustainability of the water system, and MoU will be signed with the local councils.
By operating the water stations, the drinkable water will reach IDPs, and Host in communities and camps, and the operation cost will be decreased by providing PV solar system based on the required operating hours in each location.
The providing of drinkable water through the water network will provide good conditions to operate the sanitation system in the targeted locations, which will make the need to rehabilitation all damaged lines is critical and required, ATAA will rehabilitate the sanitation systems.
In the camps, ATAA will connect the camps to the main and closely sanitation system.
This project will ensure protecting project beneficiaries from the spread of diseases by providing garbage bins and renting garbage trucks to collect garbage daily, as well as improve hygienic behavior by providing Hygiene kits to all families, in addition, conduct hygiene promotion sessions about COVID-19 pandemic and hygiene awareness messages.
It is worth to mention during the implementation of the project, if the targeted locations receive more IDPs, ATAA will target the newly IDPs with all project activities, and the project activities will help to decrease the disturbances that emerged between host and IDPs.
ATAA will conduct FGDs with targeted BNFs and especially with PWDs, as well as Local councils and other stakeholders to inform them about the goal, outcomes, and, activities of the project.
Brochures and banners will be used to share information with the communities.
ATAA will set a community-based mechanism to make sure that community members can submit their complaints and feedback. Feedback tracker will be prepared on a monthly basis.
Specific monitoring activities: rehabilitate water networks and chlorination in the communities and camps, confirming the distribution of H.Ks through onsite monitoring, monitoring report, and confirming beneficiary verification for their access to cleaned and chlorinated water, feedback, and satisfaction.

project_name: Continue the provision of life-saving Protection services to the most vulnerable individuals in NW Syria
project_objective:
ATAA aim to continue providing emergency Child Protection services, integrated with Education and FSL, within IPDs densely populated locations in Idleb and Aleppo, after starting delivering those services in 2020. In addition, ATAA will add new Protection services to the most vulnerable adults, including the elderly and those with disabilities, to ensure inclusive intervention and to leave no one behind. ATAA also aim to mitigate the risk of UXOs in targeted locations.
Protection activities will deliver emergency services to most vulnerable girls, boys, women, and men in Jarablus, Maaret Tamsrin, Teftnaz, and Dana Sub-districts, which are rated 3/5,4/5 and 5/5 or the Protection severity scale, through 4 static community centers within 4 relatively densely populated communities, in addition to 8 mobile units. ATAA will ensure the services are accessible by PwDs and will consider all possible precautious measures (social distancing and using the PPE) and Cluster guidelines
related to adapting Protection services delivery modalities in light of COVID-19, to ensure the safety of staff and beneficiaries and avoid causing harm. Protection services will be delivered to nearly 15700 children (7850 girls) , and to 2400 of their parents/caregivers (1200 women). There will also be coordination with local service providers from other sectoral services (FSL, WASH, Education, and Health-Nutrition actors) to facilitate access of persons with specific needs to those services through referral. The outcome of the proposed Protection intervention will be; Contribute to saving the lives of conflict-affected and most vulnerable GBWM, including PwD, through delivering Protection, Child Protection, and Humanitarian Mine Action services. This Outcome has been informed by the ASO 2, as outlined in the 2021 1st SA paper.
Protection services include Protection and CP case management, awareness-raising on Covid-19 and Protection/CP issues, parenting programming, supporting community-based child protection committees, case management/child protection trainings, Protection monitoring, and Risk Education.
They will provide a secure and supportive environment, building on existing capacities within the local communities and expanding the population of the ATAA response team. ATAA Protection Teams will implement all Project activities directly with support from ATAA Turkey Office

project_name: Provision of food assistance for the most vulnerable households in Idleb and Aleppo governorates in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
Mercy-USA proposes to implement this project with the following three components: 
1) 4,766 in-kind monthly food baskets distribution per SPHERE and FSL country level recommendations of micro and macro nutrients and a minimum intake of 2,100 kcal per person. 
2) Up to 15 distributions per month (once every other week) of bread for IDPs living in camps due to limited access to bakeries by removing flour from their monthly food baskets; 
3) Pre-positioned, emergency aid of 8,000 Ready to Eat Rations (RTER) distributions for newly displaced IDPs. All components of the project would be implemented in the sub-districts of Idleb City, Maaret Tamsrin, and Jandaris with support to 1,000 HH each within and outside IDP camps.

project_name: Improving the resilience of the affected IDPs and vulnerable host residents by distributing free  bread in Jandairis SD and the camps in al Harim SD
project_objective:
The project will increase the resilience of IDPs and HC in areas with a large bread shortage by supplying wheat flour from Turkey to areas that suffer from the scarcity of the flour and high prices.
For two years, the SADAD organization has been distributing free bread to camps and communities in Jandairis SD, nevertheless that the distributed quantities do not meet the growing need in the area as a result of high influx of IDPs to the area, 90 % of the total population are considered IDPs, the decreased flour quantities in NWS as all and the high inflated of the SYP in the past 6 months.
The designed project aims to support bakeries with 2000 tons of local wheat flour to bake, and distribute free wheat flour bread to the most vulnerable IDPs in camps and IDPs and host residents in communities in Jandairis SD on a daily basis of 6 days a week for 8 consecutive months with an average of 250 ton per month.
The process of baking will be based on a public tender to select the bakeries with proven experience, capacity, and good reputation in the area. Besides selecting the flour supplier based on another public tender to be announced on the public newspaper, and social media.
The project will support an estimated ~7600households average of 5 persons per family estimated (36404individual) in Jandairis SD in 10 communities (Bayada-Deir Ballut-Haj Eskandar -Jalma- Kafr Safra-Mhamadia-Nisriyeh-Tal Slur-Upper Diwan-Western Eshkab-Zanda) besides 11 camps (Aljamiaa Altawniah -Alwadi- Masrat Kafar Safra- Kherbit Aloush-Tareek Alhamam-Janadirsi Entrance-Yalnquz Road-Al Muhamadyeh2- Ashkan-Sundianki-Mamal Blook Kafar Safrah)
and 12camps in AL Harim SD (Act and Impact -Ain Jaloot-Al Aasy -Al-Bayan (Qah)-Al Fateh Al Araby-Al Qalaa -Al Nawaeer(Qah)-Al Ikhlas wa Al Taqua-Al Hurriya wa Adalah-Al Fateh Al Araby-Act and Impact Extension-Farajak Yarab)
The project will target those most in need of food support and highly at risk of food insecurity and persons with disabilities regardless of their ethnic background and based on specific selection criteria, typology of the affected population (IDPs, Returnees, Host, etc) and based on vulnerability (unaccompanied children, separated children, families of children with special needs, single-headed household, pregnant and lactating women, older persons at risk, and extremely food insecure individuals)
This project will be implemented directly by Sadad staff and will provide ~7600HHs from the IDPs and Vulnerable host residents with free wheat flour bread for 8 months, Sadad will conduct the distribution through 33small distribution points at each village and camp.

19830, Boys: 35892, Girls: 37398) stayed camp cluster in northern Idlib in the last six

project_objective:
In line with the Shelter and NFI cluster guidance, SECD is planning to sustain and save the dignity and lives of the targeted people by implementing timely, needs-based, and effective interventions
the people in north-west Syria are living in a very diﬃcult situation, the area experienced one of the biggest displacement waves, more than 700,000 people left their houses in search of a safer place to save the lives of the women, children, elderly, PWD, and other families members
through these interventions, SECD is planning to support 35500 People ( 7675 Men, 9010 Women, 9219 Boy, and 9596 Girl) based on in-depth need assessment, with focusing on responding to the critical needs of people with considering the access, the functionality of the markets and the community engagement approach by consulting the people in need about the proposed interventions

- Prioritize the cost-effective interventions
- Ensuring the participation of the beneﬁciaries in all the intervention stages

project_name: Provision of accelerated survival Nutrition Services in the context of COVID-19 pandemic to the IDPs in NWS throughout the deployment of Rapid Response Teams in  Idleb, Harim, Jisr-Ash-Shugur, A'zaz, Jarablus, Al Bab, and Jebel Samaan Districts.

project_name: Innovative Socio-Economic Development in NW Syria
project_objective:
This project is a multi-pronged approach, serving at both individual and community levels in both basic sectors, Livelihood Support for the target beneficiaries and Early Recovery by stimulating the economic growth of the target communities.
The project is going to be implemented within 12 months to achieve: 
The Overall Objective is To reform and strengthen the performance of the local economic system and scaling-up the community resilience in NW Syria.
Takaful will work to achieve this objective through four main interventions:

1st: Providing a grant of 1,000$ to 700 beneficiaries to establish new business projects or repair or resume existing ones that are heavily affected by the war or the current Covid-19 pandemic.
Initial beneficiaries (M/F), women-headed households, PWDs, and other vulnerable segments as families having child-labour are a priority, to be targeted, where 2-day sessions, be conducted to developing the Business Plans ""BPs"" and applying to the grant, and then, Takaful team be evaluating the submitted proposals, select the best projects to be supported, and identify the final beneficiaries of the grants.
Afterwards, providing to the finally selected beneficiaries a 5-day Training Program on Entrepreneurship Skills to build their capacities in managing and sustaining their businesses.
The grant is to be provided in the form of CASH for assets and into several payments to ensure that the beneficiary is committing, achieving good progress, and be businesslike to receive the next payments. Additionally, TAS, to provide 200$ to the most successful 70 projects, (representing10% of BNFs), as additional monetary bonuses, be given based on hard work and noticeable progress.

2nd: Providing Vocational Training (VT) for 300 male and female and PWDs, paid for three months, and then, providing Internship Training within the private sector, also paid for 3 months, to link them to the market.
The appropriate professions and training are according to two groups:
1. The professions do not require any qualifications e.g. Hairdressing and Sewing.
2. The professions require relevant experience e.g. Computer Maintenance and Web Development.
Three months paid internship are to be provided by contracting with business owners in the private sector, who are willing to accommodate the trainees and provide them with the Internship, and TAS will provide allowances to the beneficiaries for three months of VT and three months of Internship, $120 a month (totalling $360), which is empowering the beneficiary to gain the trust of the employer and gain the practical experience.

3rd: Improving community access to markets for 63274 (M, F) through repairing and paving three main roads leading to markets (totalling 8km in Dana, Salqin, Jindires, and Azaz sub-districts), be contracting with specialized contractors according to detailed technical plans with the direct supervision of TAS engineering team.

4th: Supporting Community Initiatives through CFW modality, to adorn and improve 8 trading roads which facilitate people's access to the markets within the target four sub-districts (totalling 8 km, 2 in each) mindset supporting 300 (males and females) with short-term employment opportunities for 44 days, to working in cleaning, rubble removal, and painting sidewalks, where each beneficiary be paid 100$ a month (totalling 200$). 

Within the continuous Covid-19 pandemic, TAS be supporting and ensure all precautionary measures through disinfecting meeting venues before and after each meeting, distributing masks to attendees, printing guiding instructions and caution signs everywhere, and also, selecting suitable venues that be primarily accessible by women and PWDs and having all comfort facilities for both genders.

project_name: Increase life-saving and resilience of the most vulnerable groups in northwest Syria through improved access to protection  service and a community-based resilience building
project_objective:
The project will build on previous achievements of the HIHFAD and continue to provide integrated supports to the vulnerable groups in an accessible way. The project integrates with other on-going HIHFAD projects funded by ECHO, German Foreign Offices and contribute to a broader coverage of comprehensive services integrated with General Protection, GBV, CP and MA . 
Built on HIHFAD’s previous success in harnessing self-reliance among the most marginalized group as well as in promoting disability inclusive approach among the humanitarian organisations and the communities, the proposed project aims at increasing resilience of the persons with disabilities and IDPs through community and beneficiary participation.  

The project will include following components.
1)	Benefiting and empowering people with amputations directly through prosthetic supports in Northwest Syria.
2)	 Enhance participation of the persons with disabilities through the community inclusion networks and promotion of disability inclusion approach among non-protection actors/NGOs, such as Education, CCCM, WASH, FSL, ER.
3)	Decrease barriers to livelihood opportunities through customized supports of their choices for the persons with disabilities with case managements, apprenticeship programme and engagement of the private sector. 
4)	Address GBV needs in health facilities by providing GBV training to health staff and supporting WGSS annexed to maternity and children hospital. 
5)	Provide training on PSEA for humanitarian workers. 

Provision of 200 prosthesis 
During 12 months, a P&O centre will install 200 prosthesis.
The beneficiaries will be selected from HIHFAD beneficiary list or through referral channels, after determining their ability to receive a prosthetic limb based on their K-level(a rating system used to indicate a person's rehabilitation potential).
The selected beneficiaries will undertake required physical rehabilitation at the HIHFAD rehabilitation centre prior to receiving prosthetics.
Transportation will be provided for the beneficiaries in need throughout the whole process
In addition to existing 14 community networks for disability inclusion, the project will add one more network, and all of them will further progress towards community-based rehabilitation (CBR) mechanism and act as ‘champions’ on disability inclusion via
- Engage schools to build disability inclusion capacity at education facilities through peer supports and child resilience activities
- Provide training and awareness sessions on inclusion of people with disabilities in communities
- Identify and refer people with disabilities
- Become an agent of advocacy in their communities for rights of people with disabilities
- Plan and conduct community events of their choices
- Conduct accessibility audits in selected camps/IDP sites/schools

Address barriers to socio-economic opportunities and livelihood through customized supports of their choices for the persons with disabilities with case managements, apprenticeship programme and engagement of the private sector. 
-	500 beneficiaries and their families among the most vulnerable households will benefit through case management, protection assistance, referrals, and access to socio-economic activities. 
-	Engage the private sector on inclusive employment awareness raising and conduct barrier mapping)
-	Apprenticeship will offer training and working experiences with other organization on substituted salary while the beneficiaries can gain competitive working skills and knowledge. Upon the completion of apprenticeship, HIHFAD will promote inclusive employment among other humanitarian agencies, and it will advocate cooperating organisations to retain them.

project_name: Food Assistance for Training
project_objective: With Libya in a state of protracted conflict, WFP’s Interim Country Strategic Plan (ICSP) aims to introduce programmes that would support the resilience of vulnerable communities across the country. The reduction in available migrant labour, both skilled and unskilled, combined with the instability of Government salaries, has left many Libyan families reliant on coping mechanisms in order to meet their basic food needs. In this context, WFP Libya is scaling-up the Food Assistance for Training pilot, which started in 2019, matching people in need with skills trainings that prepares them for available work in the local job markets. Conditional food assistance is provided as long as minimum attendance requirements are met, giving an immediate boost to food security. After the training, if successful, food security levels should be improved, with less reliance on coping strategies. Household resilience to future shocks should also be improved due to an improved asset base through greater skills, tools, and savings.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence aux populations les plus vulnérables en insécurité alimentaire sévère pendant la période de soudure
project_objective:
L’analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2020 prévoit pour la saison de soudure 2021 que 1 148 995 personnes seront en insécurité alimentaire sévère pour la phase projetée de juin a aout 2021. 
Sur le plan économique, trois-quarts des ménages en milieu rural et neuf ménages sur dix dans la ville de N’Djamena ont rapporté avoir subi des impacts économiques des mesures barrières contre le COVID-19, qu’il s’agisse de la perte totale de l’emploi (4,1% en milieu rural et 15,2% à N’Djamena) ou partielle en termes de fréquence et revenus dégagés (53% en milieu rural et 68% à N’Djamena) ou encore par rapport à la hausse des prix des produits alimentaires de base. Les perturbations dans les activités économiques ont affecté les revenus tirés des activités de nombreux ménages (pour 63% des ménages en milieu rural) et des bénéficiaires des transferts provenant des parents ou des émigrants (pour 72% des ménages dépendant des transferts). 
L’accès difficile aux marchés a joué négativement sur la disponibilité des intrants agricoles ainsi que leurs prix. Bien que les aléas climatiques constituent cette année, une des principales contraintes à l’agriculture (29%), dans de nombreux ménages agricoles, le manque de ressources (24%), la disponibilité et le niveau élevé des prix des semences (21%) ont fortement perturbé le déroulement des activités agricoles pendant cette campagne. 
Les résultats du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2020 font ressortir qu’aucun département ne serait en « phase urgence ». Cependant, 54 458 personnes seraient dans cette phase, en situation de déficit de consommation alimentaire considérable, avec des taux de malnutrition supérieurs au seuil d’urgence. Tandis que quatorze (14) départements (Bahr El Ghazal Nord, Borkou Yala, Borkou, Kanem, Nord Kanem, Fouli, Kaya, Mamdi, Wayi, Tibesti Est, Tibesti Ouest, Megri, Biltine et Dar Tama) et près de 1 094 537 personnes seraient en « phase crise ». Ces personnes seraient en situation de déficit considérable avec des taux de malnutrition supérieurs au seuil d’urgence. 
Le PAM planifie appuyer 551 756 personnes avec une assistance alimentaire pour trois mois avec rations complètes dans les provinces du Barh el Gazel, Batha, Guera, Kanem, Lac et Wadi Fira. Cette assistance alimentaire sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: Provision of PHC services and support to the public health system
project_objective:
IMC plan to continue provision of comprehensive PHC services through its 3 static clinics (Masakeh Barzeh is operational since 2008, Jaramana and Sanamayn since 2013) and 6 mobile facilities deployed in various areas of Damascus and Rural Damascus. Funding for the mobile clinics is secured until June 2021. 
Furthermore, IMC is supporting public PHC facilities in Hama governorate, through capacity building and technical support, provision of supplies (including COVID 19 supplies) and medical equipment aimed at enhancing service provision and quality of healthcare. Two mobile facilities are also planned to be supported in the most underserved areas. Specific services vary based on the facility; IMC provides preventive and curative healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases, specifically: internal medicine, pediatrics, gynecology, ENT, ophthalmology, provision of medications, basic lab services, health education and malnutrition screening. Some of the facilities also provide case management services for Mental Health (in addition to Protection- GBV and Child protection), and related advanced PSS. Through private service providers, IMC support referrals to advanced care (consultations, surgeries, specialized diagnostic services) and provides mobility/disability NFIs to targeted vulnerable categories of the population. On average among all facilities, female represent 60 to 70% of the total beneficiaries served; children below 5 years of age represent 15% and beneficiaries below 18 years of age about 30%. Consultations to people with disability amount to about 2% of total consultations. Approximately 65% of the consultations are related to NCDs, highlighting the increased needs for uninterrupted treatment and support for medications.
Areas of intervention are selected based on assessed needs and gaps. IMC clinics are open to all population and provide services and medications free of charge. Specific services require selection of the beneficiaries. Selection criteria for the referrals include: socio-economic vulnerability; necessity and duration of the suggested treatment; concomitant diseases and age; feasibility and evidence base of the treatment plan; prognosis. For provision of NFIs, criteria vary based on the item to be provided, but all require IMC doctor to examine the patient. 
IMC is part of the health cluster as well as the MHPSS sub-group and shares regularly 4Ws regarding implemented activities both to Health and Nutrition clusters as well as IMCI monthly reports. IMC also coordinates with the MoH regarding EWARS, aimed at strengthening the national surveillance system and early detect epidemic threats. The proposed response is in line with the sector priorities for 2021, overall focusing on sustaining and expanding quality healthcare services and addressing barriers related to cost of care, through mobile facilities, strengthening of the public system, and collaboration with private service providers.
