project_name: Integrated Livelihood program for enhanced recovery, increased resilience and sustainable stabilization of severely conflict affected communities in northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The crisis in NE Nigeria continues to disrupt and limit access to livelihoods of millions of people, undermining opportunities for durable solutions. As a result of the continuous conflict, which generated a situation of widespread unemployment that has been further aggravated by the COVID-19 pandemic, many households lack sufficient income to meet their basic needs, and livelihood opportunities remain scarce. Although the need for essential life-saving assistance is still widespread, IOM recognizes the urgent need for early recovery interventions, including restoring livelihoods & access to essential services, including access to justice, to strengthen the self-reliance of affected populations, especially girls, youth, women, & the elderly, against future vulnerabilities & shocks. These elements are also crucial for creating conditions for durable solutions for IDPs & restoring social cohesion. Without those pre-conditions, a premature return of displaced populations may lead to secondary displacement, deepen IDPs’ vulnerability, & exacerbate tension & social polarization between IDPs, host comms. & returnees. The inadequate capacity in areas experiencing return is by IOM considered a direct risk to the overall progressive resolution of displacement in the north-east. This project seeks to contribute to the recovery & resilience building of conflict-affected populations through a series of community support interventions. As people continue to return to their places of habitual residence from before the insurgency, there is urgent and significant need to restore infrastructure, promote early recovery, including through economic & livelihoods restoration, & facilitate a robust resilience building process. Livelihood interventions under this project will include Cash for Work (CFW). Cash-based interventions are a more dignified way of assisting affected populations, as they empower people to determine their own needs and the best way of meeting them. They can also promote peaceful co-existence between IDP, returnee & host communities, as well-designed & run cash-based interventions have a multiplier effect, jointly engaging all members of the community & directly benefiting the local economy. In addition, vocational skills training & skills enhancement activities for youth will be organized as per outcome of a labor market assessment to create human capital as necessary for the early recovery phase, with a special focus on youth. Each targeted beneficiary will also receive business start-up capital to establish small scale business. CFW & skilled labor schemes will support activities such as comprehensive neighborhood upgrades & light community infrastructure rehabilitation to directly contribute to recovery in conflict-affected areas. In addition, this project will work towards enhanced coordination & complementarity between humanitarian, stabilization & development partners, through a people-centered approach. To supplement economic recovery interventions, the project will additionally support restoration of social cohesion & local governance mechanisms in the areas of intervention. To this end, the project aims to provide technical & logistical support to community peace committees to address social cohesion concerns. Furthermore, at the ensure protection is ensured in recovery efforts, the project will build the capacity of law enforcement bodies, including traditional/religious leaders, to prevent and respond to SGBV crimes in compliance with human rights standards & through a victim-centered approach. IOM will align its response plan to the 4 strategic objectives of Early Recovery and Livelihoods Sector as follows:
•	Support Livelihood Stabilization
•	Promote inclusiveness and peaceful co-existence among IDPs in Host Comms. & Returnees.
•	Support Restoration of Local Governance Administration and Services
•	Improve Access to Infrastructure & Basic Social Services through Rehabilitation and Reconstruction of Public Service

project_name: Assistance en soins de santé primaire et secondaire pour les personnes affectées par la crise dans la région de l'Est du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso est au cœur de plusieurs crises humanitaires qui affectent ce pays déjà fortement impacté par des problématiques structurelles. La région de l’Est subit directement les effets de l’insécurité. Les populations civiles voient leur accès aux services sociaux de base, tout en étant sujettes aux risques épidémiques et à la malnutrition. Les CSPS ne sont plus en mesure d’assurer leurs stratégies mobiles à cause de l’insécurité ce qui impacte gravement l’accès aux soins des populations. Le système d’évacuation médicale est compromis et les ruptures en médicaments essentiels sont systématiques. Le défi est important, du fait du délabrement des infrastructures sanitaires, du manque de ressources humaines, financières et matérielles, et de l’incapacité de l’Etat et des collectivités à pouvoir assurer le relèvement du système, faute de ressources.

PUI se propose la continuité de son appui dans le district sanitaire de FADA, avec une clinique mobile en réponse aux besoins sanitaires (préventifs et curatifs) des populations vulnérables déplacées des sites, en coordination avec les acteurs du district. Le paquet des soins préventifs sera composé : de la promotion à la santé à travers les sensibilisation, les visites à domicile, le suivi de la croissance des nourrissons, le dépistage de la malnutrition, suivi du calendrier vaccinal des enfants et femmes enceintes, les consultations pré-natales pour les femmes enceintes et d’autre part, au travers de soins curatifs avec la prise en charge des maladies courantes dont le paludisme, les diarrhées, les infections respiratoires et toute autre pathologie diagnostiquée par le médecin de la clinique mobile pouvant se soigner en ambulatoire. pour cette les interventions, un accent sera mis sur les mesures barrières recommandées par les autorités sanitaires du pays.  
L’objectif de l’intervention est de : Contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et la mortalité de la population affectée par la crise dans la région de l’Est au Burkina Faso. Spécifiquement : Apporter une réponse rapide aux besoins en soins de santé primaire en assurant la provision du paquet minimum d’activité, en supportant le continuum de soins et en améliorant les conditions de prise en charge des populations affectées par la crise dans le district sanitaire de FADA.

project_name: Assistance sanitaire aux personnes vulnérables dans les zones en situation d’urgence au Burkina Faso
project_objective: La crise humanitaire que traverse le Burkina Faso depuis 2016 a connu une intensification en 2018 et 2019. Face à cette insécurité croissante, 6 régions ont été classées en urgence : l’Est, le Sahel, la Boucle du Mouhoun, le Nord, le Centre Nord et le Centre-Est. A la date du 10 Novembre 2020, le CONASUR estimait à 1 049 767 le nombre de personnes déplacées internes dans le pays dont 237 812 femmes et 236 674 sont des enfants de moins de 5 ans. Les zones de concentration de ces déplacées sont principalement le Sahel, le Centre Nord et l’Est. La commune de Djibo est celle qui rassemble le plus grand nombre de PDI. Cette crise est caractérisée par une atteinte significative des moyens d’existence pour les populations sinistrées avec une exacerbation de la pauvreté et une limitation de l’accès aux services sociaux de base notamment la santé et l’éducation. Dans ces régions, le niveau de couverture de ces services était déjà problématique avant la crise. A la date du 25 Octobre, le cluster santé estimait à 91 le nombre de formations sanitaires fermées dans les régions en urgence et 232 fonctionnant à minima. Les districts les plus affectés par les fermetures des centres de santé restent Djibo, Gorom-Gorom et Titao privant de soins 964 235 personnes à travers le pays. Selon les prévisions du cluster santé, 2 505 478 personnes seraient dans le besoin d’une assistance sanitaire au cours de l’année 2021 au Burkina Faso. La plupart des évaluations conduites dans le cadre du RRM auprès des personnes affectées précisent les problèmes de santé en termes de faible accès aux soins de santé primaires, faible accès aux soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive, une atteinte psychologique des proches des victimes, une persistance de la malnutrition avec un faible accès à la prise en charge nutritionnelle. La crise humanitaire a été aggravée à partir de mars 2020 avec l’apparition des premiers cas de COVID 19. Cette pandémie a éprouvé le système de santé dans son ensemble avec une atteinte à sa capacité d’offre de soins. Les mesures mises en place par le gouvernement dans le cadre de la prévention de la maladie ont affecté les moyens d’existence des populations dans la quasi-totalité des secteurs vitaux et la relance économique est lente. A partir du mois de septembre 2020, le nombre de nouvelles contaminations communautaires s’est accrue. La quasi-totalité des mesures préventives ont été levées et désormais, la pandémie est sous surveillance active avec un risque éventuel de rebond. Dans la plupart des zones en urgence, plusieurs organisations humanitaires apportent une assistance, mais les besoins sont loin d’être couverts. IRC intervient dans plusieurs de ces localités dont Djibo dans le Sahel, Nouna dans la Boucle du Mouhoun et dans les DS de Yako, Gourcy, Titao et Ouahigouya dans le Nord. Les activités mises en œuvre couvrent les soins de santé primaire, le renforcement de la santé communautaire, l’amélioration de la qualité des soins en SR et la prévention de la COVID 19. Le programme proposé ici vise plusieurs résultats afin d’apporter une assistance de qualité aux populations déplacées et hôtes de ces zones en urgence à savoir i) le renforcement de la qualité des soins de santé au niveau communautaire, ii) le renforcement de l’accès et de la qualité des soins préventifs, curatifs et promotionnels en santé de reproduction, iii) le renforcement de l’accès des populations sinistrées à la santé mentale et iv) le renforcement de la prévention de la pandémie de la COVID 19. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ces activités, IRC se mettra en partenariat avec des ONG et associations nationales en vue d’accroitre l’accès aux zones difficiles et de renforcer les capacités du partenaire local. IRC dispose d’une liste de potentiels partenaires de mise en œuvre. La sélection finale interviendra au moment de la programmation et cela prendra en compte la zone d’intervention de ces partenaires, leurs capacités et ressources disponibles

project_name: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Response for Drought and Flood-affected communities in Bari, Nugaal, Sanaag, Mudug, Galgaduud and Hiraan regions of Somalia.
project_objective:
The proposed intervention seeks to improve access to safe water and sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices in an effort to improve the health status of 24,100 people in Puntland, Galmudug and Hiraan regions. This will be done through the rehabilitation of solar boreholes, the extension of pipelines and water tank construction for communities and health facilities to improve access and storage, installation of desalination machines to purify water, rehabilitation of shallow wells, and provision of temporary access to water through voucher. The intervention will also promote household water treatment and safe storage (HWTs) to improve the quality of drinking water and reduce water-borne diseases (using cost-effective and context-appropriate treatment technologies such as filters and disinfectants). 
The IRC also proposes to construct/rehabilitate latrines with handwashing stations in IDPs and health facilities to improve safe excreta disposal, hygiene and sanitation promotion, distribution of basic hygiene kits including menstrual management materials, promoting solid waste disposal, and training hygiene promotion volunteers to support the effective implementation of hygiene promotion activities and best use of WASH facilities. 
WASH services are at risk of being disrupted by the COVID-19 outbreak; the proposed intervention will address the immediate need to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and the public health consequences of the pandemic in target locations including Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), and focus on opportunities to strengthen recovery especially supporting local communities/actors with the tools and resources needed to maintain critical WASH services in the longer term
The proposed intervention will also take into consideration gender concerns by ensuring implementation of activities are delivered in non- discriminatory ways that promote the safety, dignity and integrity of affected men, women, boys , girls and people with disabilities. The project will be designed in such a way that the water points and latrines are constructed close to settlement areas thus reducing the distance travelled by women and children (especially girls). The project will consult marginalized groups including women and people with disabilities on site selection, establishing water management structures and will prioritize inclusion of women (60%) in water- user committees to strengthen their participation in water related decision-making. The project will ensure all the latrines to be constructed in IDP camps and settlements are gender- segregated, lockable from inside and have adequate lighting. The latrines will be equipped with assistive devices such as toilet chairs and ramp to increase access for people with disability to ensure the WASH programming contribute to greater coverage and gender equality in terms of access and use of WASH facilities and services.

project_name: Strengthen the Stability of Health Services including PHC and STHC services in NWS
project_objective:
With this project, UOSSM seeks to contribute to achieving the following:
Increase access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable humanitarian health services for those most vulnerable and in need.
Strengthen health sector capacity to prepare for, detect and deliver timely response to disease outbreaks.
Strengthen health system capacity to support continuity of care, strengthen community resilience, and respond to IDP movements and changes in context.
This project will contribute to strengthening the health care and wellbeing for conflict-affected communities in NS by improving access and ensure the sustainability and quality of health services targeting Syrians including the hosts and IDPs with more focus on the most vulnerable people including women, children, and the elderly as well as the PWDs by supporting 28 HFs (4 hospitals,4 specialized centers, 5 CCTCs, and 15 PHCs) in Idleb and Aleppo. As such, this project will mitigate the economic burdens that patients face in securing medicines, especially for patients with chronic diseases, children, and pregnant women. The intervention will also contribute to response to the COVID-19 by providing the HFs with PPE and early detecting of the suspected cases and refer them to PCR Labs and through CCTCs.
The above-mentioned HFs are equipped and staffed but have a lack of medicine mainly, the HFs located in areas with high priority according to health cluster and the TWGs, where distributed in densely populated and accessible locations, most of the people are IDPs with a very low level of medical care and bad economic situation. 
All of the HFs were included within the central referral network as the capacity of the HFs gives them an important role in the referral system, and the HFs have close coordination with IPC central desk as well as HFs commit to sharing the health data through HIS, 4Ws monthly.
Supporting and upgrading capacity of the HFs is very important in light of their strategic locations in addition to the size and variety of health services provided through these HFs that include:
PHC services: management of childhood illness, management of NCDs and CDs, providing RH services, providing dental services, applying IPC measures, vaccination services, lab tests, and bandage services).
Hospital services: general surgical, obstetrics, RH services, internal medicine, laparoscopic services, urinary surgeries, orthopaedic, and ophthalmic services their related surgeries.
Specialized centers services diagnostic, treatment, and blood transfusion services for thalassemia patients, specialized radiography services, dialysis services, and providing patients with blood products and blood transfusions for them as well as providing the surrounding hospitals with blood units though the blood bank.

The centres are ongoing and funded by OCHA until end of Aug 2021, CCTCs provide services for treating mild and moderate cases of COVID-19, as they are considered the largest percentage of confirmed cases, ensuring that the severe cases in which the morbidity is high will be referred to the case management hospitals and ICU.

project_name: Provision of Protection, Child protection and Gender based violence services to affected men, women, boys and girls in Northwest Syria
project_objective:

The main objective of the project is to enhance the prevention and mitigation of protection risks and respond to protection needs through: * supporting the protective environment in Syria. * provision of quality and integrated protection services with a focus on community-based approaches, including awareness-raising, psychosocial assistance. * Individual Protection Assistance targeting people with protection, CP, GBV concerns *support other community initiatives through community centers and outreach mechanisms to address particular protection issues/concerns as identified through protection monitoring. Provision of PFA support and structures PSS support, including case management. *Provide legal advice/counselling and legal representation on civil status documentation /registration as well as on housing/land/property issues. *Expand the availability and quality of protection"" CP and GBV services"" in targeted location accordance to strategic priorities of the 2020 GP, CP, MA and GBV. As well to ensure the protection of the population affected by the crisis is improved through community-based and individually targeted protection interventions and advocacy with duty bearers, Increased access for boys and girls to quality child protection interventions in targeted locations in line with the child protection minimum standards in Humanitarian Action "" by providing Specialized child protection services (case management) for girls and boys. Provide quality specialized GBV services for survivors to prevent and mitigate risks of GBV, e.g., case management, psychosocial support and establish referral pathways. Enhance strategies to empower women and girls and prevent GBV, with a particular focus on adolescent girls and to reduce the impact of explosive hazards. The project aims to strengthen the capacity of humanitarian actors and duty-bearers at the national and community levels to assess, analyze and address protection risks and needs and to respond to child protection concerns in Syria and Build the capacity of GBV specialist and non-specialist to respond, prevent and mitigate GBV.

project_name: Integrated Emergency WASH Response to IDPs and communities in NWS
project_objective:
Objective 1:  Deliver humanitarian WASH supplies, services and improve hygienic behavior and practices of most vulnerable people
•	Supply safe and adequate water through trucking This intervention will secure safe access to clean, sufficient and adequate water for drink and hygiene purposes, improve proper hygiene practices of 86,061 IDPs (41,759 male, 44,302 female) living in 71 camps in Harim, Salqin, Dana, Kafr Takharim, Maaret Tamsrin, Qourqeena and Atareb sub districts throughout the entire project duration. Each individual will receive 35 liters per day. In Total 64,546 cubic meters.
•	Water quality monitoring through testing at three levels: water sources, water trucks, and household to ensure water is according to standards. 
•	Installation of water tanks: IYD will procure and install 38 new galvanized water tanks between 71 sites to address a current shortage. Each tank is equipped with multiple taps to serve more than one person simultaneously
•	Desludging of grey water, this grey water will be discharged from the septic tanks in 71 targeted camps from the latrines and showers which connected to those septic tanks
•	Daily cleaning of 366 latrines blocks which constructed by pervious projects.
•	Solid waste removal will be organized from each of the 71 camps .All waste will be disposed into a communal landfill after the consent of the respective local council
•	Provision of 370 garbage bins: to improve the hygienic conditions in the targeted camps 
•	Distribution of essential hygiene materials; 
•	Hygiene promotion and awareness. Strengthen hygiene promotion activities and IEC materials with focus on COVID-19 preventive key messages and proper hygienic practices.
Objective 2: Support to water and sanitation systems to ensure regular services for affected people in NWS  
•	Improved operation and maintenance for water supply systems: This activity will have two parts one in the camps and another in the community as the following:
o	In the camps:  this project will include the expansion works for the existing water network to reach the camps around the well who are depending on the water trucking to ensure their daily water need, increase the pumping capacity by equipping the well with electrical and mechanical equipment such as generator, submersible pump and electrical control panel, installing a renewable energy system(solar power system) 
o	In the host community: Through the supporting of eight water stations in Idleb, Dana and Teftanaz subdistricts, and by operation costs (fuel, spare parts, lubricants oil, and supporting of the water stations operators, water networks operators’ salaries for three months. 
•	Improved access to sanitation services: Through support to sanitation systems  with the rehabilitation of the existing sewerage lines In Idleb city and replacing the damaged and old parts of the sewerage network

project_name: Cash Based Emergency Assistance and Livelihoods in Afrin and A’zaz - WASH Cluster
project_objective: The main goal of the proposed project is to deliver immediate humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable IDP people in camps and member of host communities (HC) in Afrin complemented with a livelihoods activity to improve the resilience of 50 households through small grants. The project intends to integrate livelihood, food security and wash using cash as a modality. In North-West Syria (NWS), the price of basic food commodities remains volatile and is subject to speculation. Disruptive events, specifically displacement and COVID-19 have harmful and immediate consequences on the households’ economy andmay result in reduced consumption and exclusion, requiring the adoption of a framework of priorities and actions that are focused on livelihoods. Proposed intervention has 2 components:(1) distribution of cash to internally displaced persons(IDPs) in camps and vulnerable HC members to cover their urgent lifesaving needs (2) Small grants for 50 women to improve their resilience towards external shocks through a sustainable livelihood. First component of project aims at covering the needs of IDPs in camps in areas of food security and hygiene (multi-sectoral) through cash distributions. The primary objective of the activity is to ensure that vulnerable families have access to food and WASH items to fulfill the immediate needs. Cash will be provided through a money transfer agent following procedures agreed in SoPs including C19 preventive measures. Value of cash transfers will be $90 per HH for 8 months, following cluster recommendations. The activity will be implemented in/off camps in Afrin sub-district and Suran Sub-district. The activities proposed are aligned with ASO2 (FSL part) and ASO3 (WASH part) of this standard allocation. Complementary to the above proposed component, WHH aims at improving the resilience of 50 women through the provision of small business grants. Each grant will be worth 500 USD and enable the beneficiaries to start her own small business. Potential areas of business are textile, handcrafts, livestock, agriculture, and others. The women will receive a training that educates the beneficiaries in (a) basic profit/loss accounting and (b) marketing. WHH will further assist with market analysis. To avoid that the grant is used for ineligible own-consumption purposes, the grants will be provided in two tranches. After completing the first phase of the activity, the grantees will receive the second tranche. Moreover, the women will be assisted for eight months with cash vouchers in line with the activity introduced above.

project_name: Cash Based Emergency Assistance in A'zaz and Afrin
project_objective: The main goal of the project is to deliver immediate humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable IDP people in/off camps and member of host communities (HC) in Azaz and Afrin. It is planned to assist nearly 10,000 people through food voucher assistance to cover their needs in areas of food security. project_name: Improving food security in the northern rural of Aleppo
project_objective:
According to the latest humanitarian need assessments in Syria in 2021 , the number of food insecure people has increased approximately 45 percent from last year which reflects the deteriorated situation in NW-Syria as a result of the ongoing war. While the fact in the ground is harsher as the households in the conflict areas from their homes daily from seeking security in the safer areas which is mainly crowded by the IDPs. Also, inflation and currency depreciation pose a major threat to food security and livelihoods in Syria as well as the unemployment rates are believed to be at 50 percent, with only 16 percent of women working in the labour force.

The project aims to meet the food needs as an urgent humanitarian response in Aleppo province- Suran subdistrict through distributing  of 1000 food baskets to 1000 households for eight months sequentially. The beneficiaries in the intervention will be mainly from IDPs with a percentage of the host community of the most in need households in the target areas including the newly displaced in order to contribute to strengthening their ability to tolerate the situation through providing food assistance that meets their basic needs. The food baskets will provide the families with 2100 Calories which is equal to 100% per person per day as Sphere standards. The project location will be as the following:

Aleppo Governorate – Azaz District – Suran Subdistrict.
This intervention will target the families which meet the selection criteria and at the same time we are going to focus on the families that have not received any food assistant during the last three months. The food basket’s weight is approximately 80 Kg. Thus, the food baskets will be distributed to the IDPs to their living places. In addition, the food basket will be procured inside Syria in order to support the local markets

project_name: Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the Most Crisis-impacted Communities in Syria
project_objective:
The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain control over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than 5,000 Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale


The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5. Social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

project_name: Increase safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education services for children in NW Syria.
project_objective:
Shafak, in line with education cluster’s objectives and in coordination with involved authorities as well as targeted communities, intends to focus on achieving two main goals for a total of 21,856 school children (age, gender and disability disaggregated):
- scaling up access to formal and non-formal education for Syrian crisis-affected children
- enhancing the quality of formal and non-formal education within a protective environment
Access strategies will include small-scale rehabilitation of damaged schools and establishment of other safe temporary/alternative learning spaces through a gender-sensitive and disability-friendly approach. It is critical to improve the access to quality education services for IDPs in camps and within communities and ensure that these services are sufficiently linked to Child Protection interventions 
Formal education activities in 28 schools targeting approximately 17248 students (8107 boys and 9141 girls) through classroom learning modality (with plan B to resort to distance learning modality, based on developments of COVID 19). This intervention will minimize the risk of students dropping out, where monthly incentives to teachers will be provided, as they don’t have any alternative fund in addition to provision of education materials for students and teachers and providing schools with necessary operational costs (including heating for winter and school safety equipment).
As education is one of the very basic children’s rights Shafak is planning to provide access to education for children with disabilities by providing transportation services and improve school environment by provide targeted assistance within the schools in order to encourage these children to continue their education and integrate them with their peers.
Non-formal education opportunities and pathways back to inclusive education at age appropriate levels are increasingly required to address the complex learning needs of children through classroom learning modality (with plan B to resort to distance learning modality, based on developments of COVID 19), making use of 4 BTL campaigns conducted for that end. Thus, non-formal education will target school girls and boys (aged 8-12 and gender disaggregated) to fill in existing needs, where 12 Non-Formal Education centers will be supported targeting approximately 4608 children (2166 boys; 2442 girls) to provide literacy and numeracy along with PSS sessions; the PSS activities will be selected from I-Deal curriculum; the Curriculum used for Non-Formal Activities will be Curriculum B, that combines 2 academic years in one or, the Self Learning Programme (SLP). 
Children and youth accessing formal and non-formal education are not experiencing quality teaching, and there are growing concerns that the toll of the crisis in its many forms is preventing children from attaining foundational literacy and numeracy skills as well as those skills relevant to cognitive, social and economic empowerment. Hence, teachers will be equipped with the skills in non-formal education modalities, child-centred pedagogy, and positive classroom management to cope with overcrowded classrooms, address and accommodate host community, displaced and returnee children within their classes. 
Stakeholders in the project implementation site, including children, adolescents and older persons, including PwDs and their opinions are taken into account while developing the project design, implementation of activities so that they have better access to humanitarian services and information in accordance to their specific situation.
The project will make sure that children engaging in child labour or recruited for military purposes, or living with older or disabled caregivers or adolescent girls at risk of early or forced marriage are given special attention and have their own space to participate in the project activities and are properly referred as per Protection cluster guidelines.

project_name: Providing lifesaving preventive and curative nutrition services for vulnerable population groups with attention to children and women with special needs in NW Syria.
project_objective:
In response to the demonstrated nutrition needs on the ground, Human Appeal Turkey (HAT) and Social Development International (SDI) proposes to jointly operate 11 nutrition rapid response teams (RRTs) across North West Syria (NWS) targeting the children under 5 (CU5) and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) among others of the most vulnerable groups within the areas of priority (As per the nutrition cluster and this allocation paper) with essential life-saving curative and preventative nutrition services as follows:

- HAT: Establishment and operation of 4 RRTs in Dana sub-district for a duration of 11 months (Locations are coordinated with the nutrition cluster).

- SDI: Operation of pre-existing 7 RRTs: 2 in Afrin, 1 in Maaret Tamisrin, 3 in dana, and 1 in Salqin sub-districts for a duration of 12 months.

The project will be implemented in 23 communities across 4 sub- districts (Dana, Maaret Tamisrin, Afrin and Salqin) provide nutrition services for 83546 beneficiaries including (19200 Pregnant and lactating women 44800 children under five years and 19546 other caregivers (men and women)) (79918 IDPs and 3628 HCs) (1800 PWDs).

HAT and SDI will collaborate to promote the ultimate utilization of the pre-existing resources and expertise relevant to the intervention including the use of the trained staff at both organizations and the shared usage of the assembly points, warehouses, OTPs as well as the exchange of relevant technical expertise and measures of access and coordination at the field level. It’s imperative to mention that both HAT and SDI will make sure that the above will not result in increased costing of the proposed intervention. On the contrary, having such complementarity measures in place will potentially lead to overall cost effectiveness of the project.

project_name: Enhance Safe Access to Education for School-Aged Children in NW Syria
project_objective:
The proposed intervention's overall objective is contributing directly to the education sector 2021 HRP objectives by improving equitable access for school-aged children to safe, inclusive, and quality learning environments to foster their resilience. This will be achieved through implementing a package of education activities to 25 schools in NW Syria which are located in underserved and high-needs areas, where 15000 children (6000 boys and 9000 girls 'including 300 CwD ~2.5%', 5-17 years old) are enrolled (70% IDPs). By supporting a quality learning environment, IRD seeks to increase children's enrollment in the targeted schools. To achieve this, IRD will conduct digital Back
To Learning (BTL) campaign 'to minimize gathering and as a precautionary measure for COVID-19'. The enrolled students will receive formal/non-formal education services & undergo ASER test. To improve the students’ well-being during the project lifetime, all enrolled students will receive recreational activities. All teachers and education personnel (550: 300 men & 250 women) will be provided with monthly incentives to increase their motivation and ensure their retention in schools. The project will cover the schools’ monthly operational costs, including recreational materials, refreshment, cleaning, hygiene materials, and stationery, and the provision of students' and teachers' kits. Adding, conducting small-scale rehabilitation works. The quality of education will be improved through contextualized and targeted teacher training and further support to their professional development within each school by delivering (CSG, TiCC, PSEA, COVID-19) trainings. Parents Teachers Associations (PTAs) will be a component in the activities of this project. Quarterly meetings for PTAs members will be held to discuss what was achieved in the last period and set with IRD’s staff plans for the upcoming period. Due to COVID-19, there will be comprehensive precautionary measures in the 25 schools, including periodic sterilization process for classrooms and WASH facilities, awareness sessions for students, training for teachers and educational staff, and sterilization provision materials for all schools.
The project secured fund for 2021 is 700,000 USD

project_name: Strengthen provision of secondary and tertiary health care across Syria.
project_objective:
Strengthening and sustaining delivery of standardized secondary and specialized health care services addressing obstetric care, Neonatal Resuscitation services and referral services across the country. The main objectives are to Improving sustainable and quality life-saving secondary health care, Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CemOC), Neonatal Resuscitation services and referral services across the country men, women, boys and girls requiring life-saving surgical interventions and secondary health care, in addition to women of reproductive age requiring emergency obstetric care; and to improving access to essential medicines and strengthening the capacity of secondary care at hospitals’ level to cope with the emerging demands is important. 
Proposed HRP project is focusing on improving the quality of care for trauma, secondary and tertiary healthcare services in Syria through the provision of continued education and training, endorsement of standardized clinical guidelines, treatment protocol, and standard operation procedure of different subdivision of secondary healthcare services including trauma, emergency, and critical care services and Comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care (CEmONC). Furthermore, the project aims to infection prevention and control activities through delivery of Basic IPC training, provision of technical support, field monitoring, and measure the quality of healthcare in terms of inputs, the material, resources needed to provide IPC standard measures, and outcomes of the activities based on IPC assessment framework (IPCAF) for health facility. In addition, the WHO will focus on supporting critical gaps of secondary and tertiary health care, based on a needs assessment to ensure the vulnerable population has access to emergency care services.
Within the integration approach to essentially service delivery the access to quality care and referral to specialized health services will be introduced through implementation of this project, which includes dialysis, cancer and thalassemia treatment, as well as trauma care and rehabilitation, including provision of life-saving medical supplies and medicine required for the provision of specialized and trauma services.

project_name: The emergency response through quick rehabilitation for the affected physical access roads to IDP sites during winter in Idleb Governorate
project_objective:
This project delivers a strategic emergency-based intervention to overcome the access-based obstruction to IDPs' sites in the severe risky sub-districts in Idleb Governate (Dana, Qourqeena, Maaret Tamsri, Armanaz and Salqin).
Its main objective is to ensure uninterrupted physical access to IDP sites during winter and as when emergency situations arise. Maram Foundation MF will undertake strategic planning with response functions to ensure the delivery of the humanitarian goods to those in need, at the right time, in the right place. In order to create scientific-based response and well-planned intervention during the disaster, MF will design communication plan and risk analysis in order to prognose the risks and engage the stakeholders in planned response. A contingency plan (CP) will be designed, which involves making decisions in advance about the management of crisis, coordination and communications procedures. This plan should lead to timely and effective disaster-relief operations. The CP will be designed for Idleb gov. and those that characterize higher probability that a disaster/emergency situation may occur. The CP will be including:
•Determine the risk that are most likely to occur
•Prioritize the identified risks and rank them based on the probability they will occur.
•Develop realistic scenarios for the highest ranked risks and their impact
•Create a timeline for when the scenarios might occur
•Specify a trigger point to put the CP in action
•Determine the proper action to be undertaken to mitigate the impact of the disaster and allow the humanitarian assistance to access.

In order to design this CP, MF will establish a strong coordination network of stakeholders targeting the sub-districts of Idleb governorate, especially those that are identified as the highest risky flooded/hazarded locations. The established committee will be consisting of the Local Council (LC) some managers in the related sub-districts and MF response team. 
The committee members will convene coordination meetings and follow up on activities in the affected communities. The committee will assist in finalizing the CP, updating the climate severe conditions in their areas and call for the response on the trigger point.
Based on the outcomes of the committee, MF will be targeting the highest risky locations with awareness signs and signals to draw the attention of those access roads’ users to the possible risks and guide them for safer access/exit. MF Rapid Response Teams RRT will conduct site visits to the locations to have an accurate overview about the site and access roads and to identify whether there are humanitarian organizations acting on the ground for a better response and notification coordination.

Additionally, as per the outcome of this committee, MF will design a map-based dashboard to identify the risky locations and accordingly locate the procured service providers machineries nearby them in the call up time. MF is intending to procure service provider/s in each sub-district in order to cover the majority of Idleb governate principally in the risky location. Once the crisis occurs, MF will be informed by the focal points (members of the crisis committee). Urgent information and description of issue will be delivered. Accordingly, MF will assign its RRTs and the procured contractor/s to response within 24-48 hours. The response will be in terms of soft road graveling, excavations, blockage (large stones) furnishing, and others.

The project will have a positive impact on all beneficiaries in the selected areas , where the total number of the targeted persons approximately: 54,221 IDPs (12471 men, 13555 women, 17351 Boys, 10844 Girls) from different age groups (Young children, Children, Adolescents, Young, Middle-aged adults and elderly).
This includes about 2,530 Persons with Disabilities; 2,530 IDPs (624 men, 678 women, 686 Boys, 542 Girls)

committee consists of IHH &INSAN team members in addition to agricultural experts will check the

project_name: Detection and Control of Leishmaniasis Amongst Conflict-Affected Communities in Northern Syria
project_objective:
Under the purpose of reducing the burden of leishmaniasis, strengthening community resilience, and responding to Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) movements in north Syria, MENTOR implements the following activities: 
MENTOR provides and equips 136 Health Facilities (HFs) in North Syria with leishmaniasis diagnostic and medical commodities, strengthens the capacity of health care workers (HCWs) by providing trainings on leishmaniasis case management and supervision, enhances disease surveillance by coordinating data collection across HFs and mobile clinics (MCs) to ensure robust epidemiological data reporting, operates MC in areas that lack access to HFs or areas that host a large number of IDPs, and improves the communities’ awareness about leishmaniasis detection, control and prevention through Information, Education and Communication/Behavioural Change Campaign (IEC/BCC) activities. The proposed activities to detect and control leishmaniasis will be complemented by a preventative WASH sector project aiming to reduce the disease burden through Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS). 
MENTOR supports each HF with leishmaniasis medications, medical supplies and consumables, and diagnostic tools for both Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) and Visceral Leishmaniasis (VL). To improve leishmaniasis control in the HCWs, MENTOR conducts 2-day trainings that include all the required protocols and guidance for the HCWs to detect and treat CL and VL based on the updated World Health Organization (WHO) guidance. MENTOR follows up with the trained HCWs to discuss complicated cases and ensure the correct implementation of the guidance. MENTOR’s MCs aim to increase the beneficiaries’ accessibility to leishmaniasis services, in particular that of vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities and those who cannot afford transportation costs to the nearest HF that provides leishmaniasis service. 
In addition, MENTOR works to strengthen leishmaniasis surveillance, and regularly shares the data with WHO, EWARN, the Health & WASH clusters, the Health Working Group (HWG) and other stakeholders to improve coordination and synergize the humanitarian efforts against leishmaniasis.
MENTOR also runs combined IEC/BCC campaigns to ensure targeted communities have enough knowledge about leishmaniasis and disseminate key messages about leishmaniasis detection, control and prevention. MENTOR applies a comprehensive IEC/BCC approach through social media and various printed materials, such as leaflets and brochures, that are displayed at supported HFs, MCs and main areas of targeted communities. MENTOR also approaches key community people to deliver leishmaniasis messages in order to ensure a sustainable project and to improve the dissemination of the key messages with a long-lasting effect. Both IEC/BCC staff and trained key community people are asked to refer suspected leishmaniasis cases to supported HFs and/or MCs. 
In 2021, MENTOR plans to support 136 HFs and 14 MCs and train 325 HWCs. MENTOR expects to conduct 580,000 leishmaniasis consultations and treatments, serving 65,325 beneficiaries across northern Syria.

project_name: Prevention and Control of Leishmaniasis Transmission in Northern Syria
project_objective:
In order to continue to address the burden of the leishmaniasis epidemic across northern Syria, The MENTOR Initiative will continue to partner with stakeholders and communities to ensure that the most vulnerable receive:

1. Prevention of leishmaniasis transmission within their homes. MENTOR strives to provide protection to 992,630 households through an Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) campaign in northern Syria in Idleb, Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, Ar-Raqqa and Deir-ez-Zor governorates.

2. Information about leishmaniasis and its transmission. MENTOR will run combined Information, Education and Communication / Behaviour Change Communication (IEC/BCC) to ensure households are empowered to prevent leishmaniasis transmission within their household. This will be done through various media and delivery strategies, to maximize uptake and correct utilization of leishmaniasis prevention and case management services.

project_name: WASH Intervention to war affected people in Idleb and Aleppo
project_objective:
The project supports IDPs and host communities in Idleb and Rural Aleppo with WASH services, both emergency services for IDPs in camps and out of camps. People in camps will receive drinking water through water trucking or water pumping where possible, water storage tanks, constructing septic tanks, latrine blocks, desludging, garbage bins and garbage collection in addition to conducting hygiene promotion sessions. Hygiene kits and diapers for the elderly and PWD will be distributed three times.
In communities out of camp, both IDPs and host communities will benefit from rehabilitation and operation of water pumping stations, and the rehabilitation of sewage network. This project will contribute to the improvement of the COVID-19 preparedness and prevention capacity of IDPs and host community residents, through ensuring the continuity of the WASH services and provide hygiene and protective materials as per the recommendation of the COVID-19 Global Humanitarian Response Plan to prevent the transmission of COVID-19.

project_name: Scaled-up access to basic food needs in high-needs and underserved areas by providing cash for food and food voucher assistance.
project_objective:

The project target 3200 families with regular (monthly) food assistance through two appropriate modalities:
A- Cash for food: GAN will target 1600 most vulnerable families in village and camps with cash for food, the cash intervention is feasible in these camps as they all have access to different main markets in the targeted communities, eight rounds of cash for food will be distributed, each round consists of 20 days for distribution and 10 days for validation and PDM, 60$ will be allocated for each family as recommended by FSL cluster and CWG, the data gained form the FSL cluster indicate this areas as high priority ranking and no partner plan to target the same vulnerable and underserved camps, according to the needs assessment, the first priority is food, the proposed modality is a cash for food, as it is considered one of the most effective modality since the markets are available near camps.
B- E-voucher for Food: GAN will target 1600 most vulnerable families in the village with food voucher with the aim of saving lives and ensuring continued and regular access to food for 8 months for most vulnerable groups, beneficiaries could replace the monthly top-up assistance (60$ per family) with the main food items from the markets contracted with GAN and will be able to buy among 40 specified items with restricted amounts that allowed us to fulfill the calories min standard set by the WFP.
Monthly market assessment in terms of availability of the items, prices, and accessibility will be conducted to ensure the local markets are functioning and all beneficiaries have good and equal accessibility to the different goods.

project_objective:

GAN aims to enhance resilience of affected communities in Mare and Aghtrin through provision of livelihood opportunities and to have community resilience strengthened:
GAN aims to support the livelihoods of vulnerable crises- affected communities, by starting with Market mapping which aims to identify market gaps and needs, and then announce and selection of participants according to eligibility and vulnerability criteria and giving priorities to women headed HHs, PWDs when possibile and later provide vocational training for 160 persons on topics that will be identified according to the market mapping with giving priorities to vocations related to PPEs production and other locally produced general covid19 protection related items such as hygiene items.

project_name: Improve the food security situation and livelihood status for vulnerable and people in need in North West Syria
project_objective:

assistance as well as household and community based agricultural, livestock and

project_name: Enhancing the protective environment for crisis affected populations in NW Syria through provision of quality and comprehensive protection services
Capacity Development support for Syrian response community
project_objective:
As part of IOM’s contribution to effective coordination and the UN's localization efforts, IOM aims to support capacity-building initiatives to strengthen the quality of humanitarian programming in Syria. Strengthening local and national partners' ability to respond to humanitarian needs effectively and efficiently in Syria is also in-line with its commitments in the Grand Bargain. With Clusters and UN agencies depending heavily on the network of NGOs to implement activities, it is vital to support these partners to continue to grow and improve in the delivery of humanitarian assistance to people in need. Furthermore, in the event of non-renewal of the UN Security Council resolution, INGOs and NGOs would be required to scale up their operations further in order to continue supporting the affected communities in northwest Syria. INGOs and NGOs will be expected to maintain the delivery of quality humanitarian response activities and ensure effective coordination. As such, it is paramount to continue building the capacity of INGO and NGO partners across technical and cross-cutting topics. This past year IOM supported its partners with training on project development, report writing, governance and legal compliance with Turkish law. In addition, IOM supported the S/NFI cluster with NFI distribution guidance document in the NWS context and also developed the e-learning course for humanitarian in-kind distribution that guides the humanitarian field staff responding in NWS.  In-line with commitments under the Grand Bargain, IOM continued to support and invest in the institutional capacities of local and national responders across preparedness, response, and coordination efforts. IOM also supported its IPs by building their institutional capacity by providing HR coaching, working with IPs to improving their Human Resource unit policies and procedures based on their individual needs.

Based on the organizational capacity assessment (OCA) that IOM conducted in late 2020 with its implementing partners, humanitarian organizations continue to require capacity building in sector-specific technical thematic areas, but also need broader support to maintain the high standard of the humanitarian response in project management and administrative areas. Furthermore, IOM aims to build the capacity of implementing partners and Cluster partners on cross-cutting topics such as humanitarian principles, access negotiation, community engagement, and disability inclusion. Building on its capacity development activities in 2020, IOM will organize 39 trainings and coaching sessions on project cycle management, finance, and procurement topics. IOM will also organize community engagement training of trainers (TOTs) for CCCM cluster partners in Turkey, and training sessions for field staff in Syria on community engagement topics. In addition to the above trainings, IOM will also support the partners’ development of organizational and operational policy and procedures. All activities will be coordinated with relevant Clusters, Technical Working Groups, and other coordination fora.

project_name: Enhanced access to basic WASH services through sustainable solutions in Northern Syria
project_objective:
In line with the acute needs and the Sector strategy for 2021, PIN plans to respond to the WASH needs in Northern Syria by delivering humanitarian WASH supplies, services and improve hygienic behavior and practices of most vulnerable people. PIN will focus on both distributions of essential WASH NFIs & Hygiene promotion and improved access to humanitarian lifesaving/emergency WASH facilities and services. Interventions will primarily target newly displaced/returned populations in informal settlements, host communities, and camps, based upon coordination with relevant cluster partners to maximize response coverage and minimize gaps. Technical design and proposed level of services provided through these interventions will follow acceptable standards such as SPHERE and those established by the Northern Syria WASH Cluster and consider varying needs among different groups in the community, such as women, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities. Capacity building for local councils will be provided by PIN staff through field coaching sessions focusing on operational aspects and management of water systems and solar power plants.
PIN is planning to implement WASH activities in Schools and Health facilities, taking into consideration the following locations: Locations with WASH infrastructure damaged by war, locations with high IDP population, locations with non-functioning WASH infrastructure indirectly affected by war - unstable electricity supply, lack of maintenance, lack of skilled staff for maintenance, etc., locations where non-existent or malfunctioning WASH infrastructure presents a significant risk to the environment and public health. 
PIN is aware that needs are different amongst gender and age groups and other vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities. PIN aims to provide the most needed assistance to such groups through employing a wide spectrum of different activities, establishing beneficiary selection criteria to prioritize the inclusion of those most vulnerable, and adapting its assistance delivery to promote access for the most vulnerable people. PIN’s programmes are carried out in coordination with local authorities at various levels from cross-border, to hub, to district and village levels. PIN engages in regular dialogue with authorities to ensure transparency, accountability, and protection mainstreaming. This includes consultations and briefings on needs, humanitarian principles, PIN procedures, and beneficiary selection at the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation stages of projects.

project_name: Access to quality education and child protection services for conflict-affected children in Northern Syria
project_objective: The proposed action seeks to increase the access and quality of education and PSS services in target areas by implementing a combination of formal (non-accredited) and non-formal education activities that complement each other where possible. PIN takes an integrated and holistic approach to address the Education in Emergencies (EiE), and Child Protection needs. PIN will employ a dual approach to supporting  education, including through establishing temporary learning centres (TLCs) for provision of PSS and non-formal education using the cluster-approved Self-Learning Programme (SLP) curriculum in areas with acute concentrations of OOSC – including in IDP camps and informal settlements; and assistance to non-accredited schools where education has been disrupted through providing light repairs, equipment, teaching and learning materials, support for running costs, and provision of after-school catch-up and remedial classes to support pathways into education and reduce drop-out. Specific consideration will be given to particularly vulnerable households with Out of School Children or children at risk of education disruption, who will be provided with psychosocial support and pathways for (re)integration into education. PIN takes an evidence-based approach to programming based on rigorous feedback loops to promote accountability and enhance impact. All activities will be implemented in line with relevant Education cluster tools, materials, and approaches, in addition to core INEE and Sphere standards, with a focus upon promoting safe learning spaces and essential WASH facilities and maximizing accessibility for those at risk of education disruption, including girls and children living with disabilities. Teaching and student kits will be provided to facilitate quality learning opportunities and minimise education barriers for children from low-income HH. PIN also provides ECCD classes for adult TVET students’ children from 3 to 5 years old to help caregivers overcome barriers in attending the TVET courses while providing essential support during the developmental phase of pre-school-aged children. Geographical targeting will occur through further in-depth needs assessments in areas pre-identified in cooperation with the Education Cluster. These will determine schools and communities most in need of educational and child protection support. The process will ensure the participation of relevant stakeholders to consider local priorities while also ensuring that transparency is at the forefront and that PIN is accountable to the populations in its areas of intervention. Assessments will be conducted by PIN staff and engineers in collaboration with local authorities, where relevant. PIN will target communities where education services have been disrupted due to conflict, where there is no, or limited, access to education. Experience highlights that in such areas, significant gaps also exist to meeting teachers’ and students’ needs for safe and quality learning. Throughout the entire cycle, there will be a strong focus on community outreach and engagement, including caregivers. All activities have the final aim of reintegrating children into education through non-formal accelerated learning programmes and the creation of child protection safety nets.The organization plays an active role within several clusters and working groups across Northern Syria, including the Cash Working Group, the Protection working group, and the Education cluster, of which PIN has played a vital role as a member of the Strategic Advisory Group in Gaziantep.

project_name: Integrated Emergency WASH Response to IDPs in camps and informal settlements
project_objective:
Based on the HRP 2021 report, access to enough and affordable safe water, adequate sanitation, solid waste management, and/or hygiene supplies will remain a real challenge for 1.9 million people living in IDP sites that are highly dependent on continued humanitarian assistance. Disruptions and quality of services in IDP sites have direct negative physical and mental well-being and protection consequences, notably on women and girls.
MF in Turkey office is remotely managing the delivery of integrated WASH assistance with main-streamed protection and advocacy in Idleb and Aleppo Governorates. Timely humanitarian relief and enhanced protection to the vulnerable is delivered to those affected by emergency situations in the settlements. Basic WASH assistance is delivered to the targeted community by taking into account the different needs of men, women, boys, and girls, in addition, to take into consideration the special needs for disabilities people, especially during the infrastructure designs.
Due to the huge needs of WASH intervention in the camps and referring to emergency needs in addition to camps management request from WASH cluster in order to provide the main WASH services in Idleb and Aleppo camps through INGOs and NGOs, Maram Foundation seeks to provide emergency needs as much as possible to help the people in need in different locations at Idleb and Aleppo camps with coordination and collaboration by WASH cluster, local authorities, and camps management in the area.
Maram Foundation is applying for HPC to provide WASH response in many locations in Idleb and Aleppo areas as a result of the large influx of IDPs and limited access to services.
Since Maram has current WASH projects to provide around 106,000 individuals (19,272 households HHs) living in 20 camps and 2 communities in Idleb and Aleppo governorate including with basic WASH services till the end of March 2020. So, MF is applying for HPC to continue the current intervention and provided the emergency WASH services, in addition, Maram will constantly be targeting new arrivals at all the project's phases.
The provided WASH activities will be drinking water, solid waste removal, de-sludging latrine septic tanks, construction or rehabilitation latrines, Hygiene kits distribution, and hygiene awareness sessions. The project design will be according to SPHERE standards and WASH guidance in line with current priorities 
Furthermore, the planned intervention will mainstream protection principles especially (Do no harm) throughout the project cycle by considering the different needs of men, women, young children, children, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults, and older adults. The provision of sanitation services will be consulted with the targeted camps and communities, and take into account the specific needs of each group. Maram Foundation also revised the content of hygiene kits by involving the women and girls through Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) during previews implemented projects.
The Project also designed to provide disabilities, elderly and another vulnerable group with accessible handicap infrastructure too by taking these groups needs into consideration during the design phase of these infrastructures, with particular focus on vulnerable people such as ‘People with Special Needs’, in addition, to provide access to proper gender-sensitive and disability WASH facilities in camps, schools, child-friendly spaces, and health facilities.
MF will contribute to the mitigation of the effects of the COVID 19 in NW Syria by taking COVID19 prevention measures with regards to sterilization, provision of PPE, appropriate water quantities to promote handwashing and hygiene, social distancing in general and during distributions, health screening of IDPs and sensitizing them to follow precautionary procedures.

project_name: Provision and upgrading of shelter, infrastructure and Non-Food Items for Vulnerable Groups in Northern Syria
project_objective:

1-	Installing of water-rain drains in 5 IDPs sites affected by floods in A’zaz, Aghtarin, Suran, Ghandourah, Jarablus and Albab sub-dsitricts. During the first quarter of 2021, Shafak completed the installation of 2 water-rain drains.

project_name: Provision of WASH services to the affected people in Aleppo and Idleb Governorates
project_objective:
The project will provide comprehensive WASH services for affected people in northwest Syria living in IDP sites and host communities.  The project will focus on providing emergency WASH services in the short term and provide a sustainable services in the long-term to the affected people in Aleppo and Idelb governorates. 
Shafak through this project will provide emergency WASH services for 240,000 individuals living in camps.

In addition to conducting rehabilitation, maintenance, and upgrade for WASH facilities and infrastructure to link the remote sites (camps and neighborhoods) with sustainable WASH services. Focusing on the rehabilitation of the infrastructure will ensure the sustainability of access to WASH services for 315,985 people and maintain the efficiency of the infrastructure to be able to receive more subscribers and avoid any damages which might be very difficult for the local authorities to fix it. 

The project will comprise the following components:

a) Rehabilitation of 15 water pumping stations including equipping the stations with all electrical equipment and install renewable energy systems to reduce the running costs. In addition providing monthly running costs for the stations (fuel, chlorine, engine oil, and incentives for workers) and apply a cost recovery system.
b) Provision of WASH emergency services for 240,000 individuals living in camps including water trucking and water quality monitoring, water containers, construction of emergency latrines and maintenance, desludging of septic tanks, and solid waste management.
c) Rehabilitation of sewage networks to connect the remote sites, schools, and health centers (isolation centers) in addition to replace the damaged sewer lines.
d) Rehabilitation of water networks to connect the remote sites, schools, and health centers(isolation centers) in addition to replace the damaged water lines.
e) Supporting the local operators and municipalities to continue the garbage collection and disposal of the waste from 20 communities, schools, health centers and surrounded IDPs sites. This support will cover providing fuel for garbage vehicles, and maintain/repair of the broken ones in addition to support worker’s incentives.
f) The hygiene promotion will implement awareness sessions about the improvement of hygiene practices and behaviors.
g) 60,000 hygiene kits will be distributed for the IDPs and host communities who don’t have the capacity to secure hygiene materials.

Shafak will ensure support the innovative solutions as possible in its proposed interventions. Shafak will apply solar-powered systems for operating the water pumping station and support the hybrid system to reduce the operating costs in the water pumping station. Moreover, Shafak will develop the design of septic tanks and support construction water treatment plants where there is no possibility to link the camps with the sewage networks.
The proposed intervention directly contributes to Syria's HRP strategic objectives, through providing WASH emergency services and provide sustainable access to WASH services through linking the remote sites with WASH facilitates and improves the infrastructure in the host communities.

project_name: WF2021 - SNFI/Integrated Assistance and Safe Shelter Provision - Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The humanitarian situation remains dire as the additional strains related to the COVID-19 pandemic and the economic downturn in Syria continue to impact the 4.1 million people living in northwest Syria. A decade of conflict marked by multiple displacements, economic shocks, military operations, and violence is continuously eroding the resilience of the population. An estimated 2.8 million people rely on humanitarian assistance to meet their basic needs such as shelter, food, water, and health.

This plan aims to provide key and complimentary services to cover the immediate needs of the most vulnerable newly displaced groups, supporting their resilience and preparedness.
This plan responds to the need of the most vulnerable groups including women, men, boys, and girls of all ages, both IDPs and host-vulnerable communities as well as people with disabilities as the following breakdown:
IDPs [90,500] Host groups [10,000] Returnees [13,000]
- Girls 25,000- Boys 22,000 - Females 30,500 - Males 36,000
People with disabilities 1,400.
It is to respond to the Sector basic objective of ""Provide life-saving and life-sustaining shelter and NFI support
Reaching the most severe communities the main outputs of this plan are:

1- Providing Refugee Housing Units - 1,000 units (RHU) for 1,000 households ""5,000 individuals"" to support hosting the newly displaced households who do not have safe and secure shelter.
(Aleppo Rural and Idleb Governorates)

2- Rehabilitation works for 1,000 (houses), 1,000 households ""5,000 individuals"" including the most vulnerable host and displaced families.
(Aleppo Rural and Idleb Governorates)

Camp’s key administrative and critical humanitarian infrastructure: Solar power installation in camps public facilities, firebreaks and fire points, admin offices, distribution points, and warehouse, installation of external fences, rain drainage systems, safe spaces for women and children.
-	Camp operational and Regular maintenance activities.
-	(Emergency cost included in the CCCM submission - other regular costs will be included in Shelter/NFI Cluster WATAN HRP 2020)

5- Providing NFI and Shelter kits for 4200 vulnerable IDPs, ""21,000 individuals"".
