Based on a technical assessment proving the availability of essential services (such as markets, public services, infrastructures…), also, taking into consideration HLP rights, WATAN will be operating in vulnerable communities following the Protection, vulnerability, and prioritizing the most in need Reference for Northwest Syria guidance and the AAP framework.

Also, in line with humanitarian principles, this plan's impact is supporting the reconstruction targets for the affected communities to avoid raising violence within the crises hosting communities that produce more armed conflicts and fewer protection conditions.

project_name: Humanitarian Response in Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa for displaced children and teachers
project_objective:
Since 2017, Cabo Delgado province has been facing insecurity caused by non state armed groups/insurgents. This has resulted in the destruction of individual houses, disruption of basic social services such health, education, and displacement of large groups of the population to safe areas and abandonment of farms and water projects under construction.  Currently most of the districts in the north of the province are affected by the insecurity situation. Recently the security situation deteriorated significantly with many attacks recorded between January – October 2020 and now they seem to be daily. 
UNICEF through this proposal is planning to implement life facilitating activities in the Education area focusing on the IDPs children (3-15 yrs) and teachers.
Since classes were suspended in March 2020, UNICEF has been supporting DPE through CERF on learning supplies for schools in hosting communities and on PSS for teachers to provide access by children to continuing education by distance with a special focus on vulnerable children such as girls and children with disabilities and IDPs children. Also, personal hygiene kits will be provided to help children prepare for a safe and gradual return to schools.
Target groups:
ECE -1,770
Teachers- 1,110
IDPs including host families – 176,924(90,356 women and 86,568 men)

project_name: Providing emergency life-saving WASH and Shelter assistance to the most vulnerable populations in North West Syria
project_objective:
Aligned with the Syria HRP 2021 objectives and according to the Humanitarian Needs Assessment Programme (HNAP), the proposed project aims to provide life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable people affected by the escalation of violence in southern Idleb and western countryside of Aleppo, Most IDPs (in camps, informal settlements and among host community members in villages) continue to face critical WaSH needs and their Shelter locations lack water tanks and sustainable solid waste solutions (garbage bins, sewage networks). This is particularly problematic in light of the COVID pandemic. Findings from the CCCM Cluster confirm that, despite the humanitarian presence, WaSH needs are still not fully covered in Azaz. In fact, according to Humanitarian Needs Assessment Programme (HNAP) report of Dec 2020, 40 % of IDPs in NWS report that water is their first priority. In terms of infrastructure, at least 70% of sewage is discharged untreated, while at least half of the sewerage systems are not functional and 26% of garbage is inappropriately disposed within communities (HNO 2020), with 64% of water stations not functional, according to the Syrian Water Resources Platform.

SI addresses identified needs with a dual approach:
1. Provision of comprehensive WaSH package for IDPs in Mare, Aza, Suran and Akhtarin camps and Informal Settlements
• Daily supply of safe, sufficient and treated water in the form of water points for an average of 35 Litter per person per day through water trucking and pumping (running cost). Water distribution and quality monitoring will be implemented in the full respect of the WASH cluster technical recommendations;
• Procurement, distribution and installation of water storage containers for water domestic use and hygiene behaviors
• Solid waste collection and management through provision of adequate solid containers
• Life-saving hygiene promotion awareness will be ensured within and beyond recently displaced people to prevent water and vector borne diseases. 
• Distribution of 3000 comprehensive Hygiene-COVID kits in alliance with COVID response for 3,000 HHs (15,442 individuals)
• Water network rehabilitation in Suran village. 

2. Shelter rehabilitation and gravelling
• SI will rehabilitate 100 partially damaged shelters based on a technical assessment in all of the locations where we provide WaSH services. This work consists of gravelling works for vulnerable damaged shelters, totaling an average of 350 USD.
• Gravelling works for roads, Specifically, the activity the gravelling of the roads in Azaz area, covering 1,463 beneficiaries in the targeted locations. Please refer to the design 

Targeting will be based on needs analysis, inter-agency coordination, and SI ability to maintain humanitarian safe and principled access. Beneficiary selection criteria for individual activities will vary, but always be based on needs and vulnerabilities. Gender equality will be prioritized and beneficiary engagement throughout the project cycle will ensure transparency and awareness of project activities.

project_name: Food security and livelihood support to vulnerable and multiple crises affected households in Jonglei and Upper Nile States
project_objective:
This 12-month project plans to complement 2021 FSLC objectives; CO1: Food assistance, CO2: Emergency food production; and CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs in Ayod, Nyirol, Uror, Duk, Fangak, and Renk (IPC 3 & 4) target Counties, in a way that prevents COVID-19 spread. The project is designed to support 7,503 vulnerable HHs (45,018 individuals) composed of IDPs, Host communities and Returnees, PWDs, and minorities through life-saving food assistance, own food production, livelihood support, and livestock health services. 13,955 men, 22,058 women, 4,052 boys and 4,953 girls are targeted. 

Implementation for food assistance (CO1) will be through general food distribution in Ayod and Duk counties targeting 1906 and 2185 households respectively.  
The implementation of CO2 to enhance food production will be through in-kind distribution of crop, vegetable and fishing kits to 11,124 households (Ayod 2,000, Nyirol 1,553, Uror 1,761, Duk 2,300, Fangak 2,019 and Renk 1,492), livestock support; treatment and vaccination campaigns to 5,561 HHs in Ayod (1,612), Uror(2,100) and Nyirol (1,850) counties targeting a total of 163,000 livestock heads through 105 trained Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) (35 per county), and livestock restocking program in Ayod, Nyirol, and Fangak for 500 households in each of the three counties.
In light of resilience building and reducing dependency on food and agricultural inputs aids (CO3), this will be realized through training of farmers (750), fisher folks(360), 20 VSLA groups (20 member each), and through local procurement of seeds from through seed fairs. The trainings will cover good and climate-smart agronomic practices, countering post harvest losses, sustainable income generation activities, value addition with special emphasis on minimising spread of COVID-19. Seed Fairs (SFs) for Crop Seed procurement will be done from 1,500 seed producer groups/traders in Renk county where seeds will be procured locally from these farmers and distributed to the community farming purposes. 

Beneficiary targeting will be through the AAP committee with mainstreaming of gender, persons with disabilities, minority and marginalised groups. This project will benefit the most vulnerable; Child-headed, Elderly and Female-headed households under IPC 3,4, and 5 suffering from food insecurities and malnutrition. Protection will be mainstreamed in order to reduce risks and exposure to Gender-Based Violence and ensure the Do No Harm principle is followed during beneficiary targeting and provision of support. There will always be timely, routine and well-established feedback mechanism channels from the beneficiaries throughout the project cycle. 

Sustainability plan of the project will be achieved through community engagement in the design and implementation of the project in collaboration with County Agricultural Department, ROSS office, and other local authorities. Awareness and risk mitigation in view of COVID-19 will be raised through training and engaging community members on specific techniques for contextualized approaches. Project staff will support assessments initiated by the FSL cluster and Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries and will monitor crop disease, pest outbreaks, Fall Armyworm (FAW), and desert locust and make referrals to FSL cluster and MAF. Complementary programming will be advanced in the counties, working closely with nutrition and health partners. The project will receive pipeline supplies from FAO whereas the requested funding will be used to provide front-line services.

project_name: Provision of Equitable Access to Protective & Quality Education in Emergencies to Vulnerable Children & Youth in Ayod, Duk & Bor South Counties (Jonglei State) and Ulang & Longechuk Counties (Upper Nile State).
project_objective:
This 12 months’ project plan is to provide safe, protective, and equalised participation and learning outcomes across gender and disability for 18,355 (10,830 girls) children and youth children aged 3-17 through the provision of school facilities, quality delivery of curriculum, safe teacher conduct and community participation in 52 primary & secondary schools; 5 County Education Departments (CEDs) maintaining teacher quality built on continuous professional development and teacher evaluation systems for 468 (154 female) primary & secondary school teachers; 468 PTA members (154 female) and 50 (10 female) local education leaders developing education service delivery & improvement plans to reduce the risk to fail in the long- term in Ayod, Duk & Bor South Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang & Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State, South Sudan.

Key project activities include enrolling 18,355 (51% girls) children in Pre-primary, Primary and secondary schools/learning centers; establishing 20 temporary learning spaces and classrooms; rehabilitating 20 temporary learning spaces and classrooms; providing 5,513 (2,811 girls) children aged 3-5 children with ECD kits; establishing 30 gender segregated latrines and water points and hygiene promotion; rehabilitating 20 gender segregated latrines and water points and hygiene promotion; procuring and supplying 130 sets of Sanitation and Hygiene materials (hand washing soap, sanitizers, masks, etc.) to students 1,985 (1,171 girls)  for ECD; 14,057 (8,294 girls) for primary; and 662 (232 girls for secondary); procuring and supplying 130 sets of sanitary and hygiene materials (hand washing soap, sanitizers, masks, etc.) to teachers- 201 (70 female) for Ayod; 56 (19 female) for Duk; 66 (23 female) for Bor South; 98 (34 female) for Ulang; and 47 (16 female) for Longechuk); providing emergency-affected 18,355 (51%) children with 50 quality education recreational materials; training 1, 200 (400 female) teachers in EiE pedagogical skills and child-centered methodologies to improve teaching-learning process for emergency-affected children; training and update 1, 200 teachers and 50,116 learners on PSS and the impact of COVID-19 and its protection mechanisms; training 1, 200 (400 female) teachers and 50 (10 female) education personnel on referral pathways on protection/GBV, COVID-19 and health and nutrition; training 1, 170 (520 female) SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management and governance, psychosocial support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)Print and distribute appropriate Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials (i.e. posters, leaflets) on COVID 19 prevention and mitigation measures; and organizing 10 back to learning campaigns in Ayod, Duk, Bor South, Ulang & Longechuk Counties (2 each).

There will be 24 schools in Ayod County targeting enrollment of 8,448 (4,007 girls) children aged 3-17 years; supporting 201 teachers (70 female), 201 (70 female) members of 50 PTAs & 10 (2 female) local education leaders. In Duk County, 6 schools will enroll about 2,183 (1,580 girls) children; support 56 (19 female) teachers, 56 (17 female) PTA members, and 10 (2 female) local education leaders. In Bor South 7 schools will provide access to 2,244 children (1,854 girls); support 66 (23 female) teachers, 66 (20 female) PTA members & 10 (2 female) local education leaders. Ulang County will have 10 schools with 3,620 (1,878 girls) children; 98 (34 female) teachers, 98 (31 female) PTA members, and 10 (2 female) local education leaders. Longechuk will have 5 schools as well but with about 1,860 (835 girls); 47 (16 female) teachers, 47 (13 female) PTA members, and 10 (2 female) local education leaders.

project_name: Prevention and Management of Acute Malnutrition in Vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities in Ayod, Akobo and Bor South Counties -  Jonglei State.
project_objective:
In projection period of August to December 2020, and in the total absence of humanitarian food assistance, an estimated 409,850 people (67% of the population) will face Crisis acute food insecurity or worse, an increase of 8% from the 201,866  people (63% of the population) from the same period in 2019. The recent survey conducted by ACF in Akobo, Bor South and FSNMS (in Ayod),reported that critical nutrition situations with global acute malnutrition (GAM) prevalence of 19.4% in Akobo West, 25.5 % in Ayod and 20.0% in Bor South and above, the World Health Organization emergency threshold. Humanitarian situation in Jonglei (Ayod , Akobo West and Bor South Counties ) remains critical due to repeated devastation, displacement and at the same time returnees. 

Previous nutrition responses have been stretched by an influx of IDP’s and host community. Most families are without employment; most population heavily reliant on humanitarian assistance. (WFP 2018-2020). 

CMD will be implementing minimum package of Integrating Out Patient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) within existing health facilities by providing routine treatment using simple medical protocol to SAM without medical complications. In addition, CMD will integrate Health, WASH and FSL into Nutrition targeting the 26 OTP/TSFP sites and 3 SC’s within Northern and Southern Ayod this includes Pagil, Menime, Normanyang, Kandak, Mogok, Jiech, Gorwai, Padek, Kuachdeng, Haat, Kharmun, Mhaar, Ayod town, where CMD has existing health facilities while SC will be situated in  Mogok, Gorwai and Padek to treat 780 SAM children with medical complications. In Bor South and Akobo West CMD will integrate OTP/TSFP services and leverage on its ongoing responses on thematic areas of WASH, Health and Education. CMD currently runs WASH interventions in Ayod ,in Bor South and Akobo, provision of nutrition services through integration of WASH and Health within the existing health facilities. CMD proposes to continue delivering nutrition services in Ayod County, Akobo West and Bor South  in collaboration with MoH/CHD, partners and local authorities through supporting initiatives for the decentralization of OTP/TSFP and SC sites, increasing awareness through community mobilization on: IYCF/MIYCN Practices for prevention of Malnutrition, socio-mobilization for vitamin A supplementation, deworming and advocacy for the proper use of LLITN. Provision of Hygiene Kits and livelihood kits to caregivers admitted with SAM/MAM Children into the Program. 

With UNICEF and WFP collaboration, they will enable CMD provide targeted emergency nutrition supplies and services to a SAM caseload of up to 5787 (Including 1020 children with complicated severe acute cases) in need (< 5 years both boys and girls) and MAM caseload of up to 13,261(<5 years) and PLW’s caseload of 12,902. 

CMD will train Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) and Mother-to-Mother support groups from host community to acquire skills and knowledge on Integrated Management of SAM and Maternal Infant and young child feeding practices so as to provide quality nutrition services. Health staff and Nutrition staffs will be capacitated for integration of SAM and MAM management into health programmes especially on malaria screening and referral of severe cases to OTP and Stabilization centers.

project_name: Improve access to essential primary health care services for the host communities and IDPs in Jonglei, Upper Nile, Unity and Eastern Equatoria states through static health facilities, mobile outreaches and community based case management approaches
project_objective:
Despite the relative calm in the country since the signing of peace in September 2018 & the subsequent partial formation of the Revitalized governments in 2020, access to health services has never improved. Protracted communal conflicts, cattle raiding due to lack of rule of laws, economic hardship coupled with flooding & COVID-19 effects have continuously devastated the lives and wellbeing of people in 2020 & expected to worsen in 2021. Jonglei & Upper Nile states are among the states with the highest health access gaps and the already weak health care system infrastructures in the counties have additional waves of devastation by triple shocks in 2020 causing displacements, hence more hindrance on access & utilization of services. IPC analysis of Oct 2020-Jul 2021 based on the data from the nutrition monitoring system, SMART surveys, & the trend of admission in 2020, reported 1.4 Million under5 children expected to suffer from acute malnutrition in 2021, the highest since the eruption of conflict in 2013. Multi-sectoral IRNA conducted by partners including CMD in Akobo West, July 2020 reported lack of static health partner. Data from the KIs interviews reported common morbidities in the area as Malaria, AWD, ARI & some communicable diseases such as HIV & TB plus the NTD as Kala-azar. 
87% of locations this project targets are in IPC phase4 & 11,000 persons expected to be in IPC pahse5 in Akobo county alone. The continuous rise of water levels, lack of latrines in the displaced settlements (highlands) increases the risk of outbreaks of waterborne diseases as Acute Watery Diarrhea/Cholera, an increasing surge of malaria. The absence of EPI services increases the risk of outbreaks for vaccine-preventable childhood illnesses like measles & Poliomyelitis. COVID-19 preparedness & response requires scaling up of services to include the provision of sufficient spaces in the health facilities to ensure adherence to social distancing, provide PPEs to frontline health workers. WASH facilities as part of IPC. Multi-sectoral humanitarian assistances particularly the essential health care services therefore needed to save lives and avert more suffering in these counties in 2021.
CMD, an NNGO with over 15years of experience in providing humanitarian & developmental health services has vast expertise in the local context and a significant presence sub-nationally. CMD plans to implement this project in Akobo, Ayod, Bor South, Duk, Canal/Pigi, Ulang, Kapoeta North & Guit counties. This project aimed at directly targeting 37,500 host communities & IDPs including 19,125 women & girls, 6,750 under5 children, 5,625 persons with disabilities through static health care facilities, mobile outreaches & community-based case management with an estimated cost of 5 Million USD. Disease prevention, detection, surveillance and reporting, case management & BEmONCs services where Skilled Birth Attendants deliver 80% live births. 1,875 mothers receive ANC4 visits & post-natal services. 80% of SGBV survivors will receive Clinical Management of Rape, basic psychosocial support services & a strengthened referral system. Deployment of qualified health workers to maintain & continuously improve the quality of care to mothers of childbearing age, children & persons with disabilities. Beneficiaries, stakeholders’ involvement & capacity building of CHDs and health workers. Inter-sectoral synergies with WASH, Protection & GBV, Food Security & Livelihood & Nutrition will be incorporated through close coordination mechanism. Use EWARS and weekly IDSR system of reporting to monitor the morbidities and trends of outbreaks. Utilize the HMIS & other internally improvised tools to ensure the quality & consistency of data. Obtain beneficiaries` feedback by supporting the existing Health Facility Committees and establish committees in health facilities that do not currently have. Install suggestion boxes in the health facilities & CMD offices, organize FGD as part of AAP.

project_name: ASSISTANCE AUX VICTIMES DES INONDATIONS DE GATUMBA
project_objective:
En date du 19 Avril et 1 Mai 2020, des inondations sévères ont touché la zone de Gatumba dans la commune de Mutimbizi de la province de Bujumbura Rural. Ces inondations sont dues à la montée des eaux de la rivière Rusizi; sept (7) quartiers (Kinyinya I, Kinyinya II, Mushasha I, Mushasha II, Muyange I, Muyange II and Gaharawe) de la zone de Gatumba ont été touchés par les inondations. Cette catastrophe naturelle a affecté 45 681 personnes (soit 8543 ménages) et causé le déplacement de 24 037 personnes (soit 4 544 ménages) qui sont installés dans trois (3) sites. Les points d’eau sont inaccessibles et sous l’eau, besoin urgent d’eau potable et d’ustensiles de collecte et stockage de l’eau. Les latrines sont également inondées et les déchets se sont mélangés avec l’eau stagnante. Ce qui expose la population aux risques des maladies d’origine hydrique. Au niveau des zones de rassemblement, une insuffisance, voire même quasi-absence, des latrines et la défécation à l’air libre s’observent et mettent en danger la vie des personnes qui vivent aux environs. 
Les interventions du secteur WASH seront concentrées sur la continuité de la réponse en cours en attendant des solutions durables :

	Par l’aménagement des latrines d'urgence, pour 2 000 ménages donc 12,015 personnes (à raison de 50 personnes par latrine selon les normes sphères)
	L'approvisionnement et la distribution de l’eau par camion-citerne pour 2 000 ménages pendant 60 jours. Le besoin journalier en eau est de 450 m3 soit le minimum de 7,5 litres par jour par personne selon toujours la norme sphère.
	La distribution d'articles non alimentaires (NFI) et de kits d'hygiène seront également organisées pour doter les victimes d’une certaine capacité de traitement et de stockage de l’eau de boisson, de cuisine et d’hygiène corporelle pour résister et limiter les épidémies de sante publique ;
Ces distributions seront toujours accompagnées des campagnes de sensibilisation pour promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d'hygiène, et prévenir les infections des maladies dont le COVID-19 ; 
Après stabilisation de la situation, le secteur WASH est également disposé à organiser un processus d’assainissement total piloté par la communauté (ATPC) pour une réponse à court et à long terme. Cette approche permettra à la population de se construire mutuellement ou librement une latrine par ménage et contribuera à augmenter le niveau de résistance au choc des inondations et des éventuelles maladies. L’approche aura également contribuer à la remise en service des infrastructures publique d’eau actuellement endommagé au niveau des écoles.

project_name: Providing Employability and Apprenticeship Livelihood Support to Urban Youths in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The Employability and Apprenticeship Livelihood Support for Urban Youths in Northeast Nigeria is an IRC project targeted at providing support on 2 key livelihoods pillars: Employability Support and vocational apprenticeships. On the first pillar, youth will be supported with tailored employability training which will focus on workplace preparedness, personal and professional development skills, as well as CV/Resume writing and interviewing skills training. Under the second pillar, participants without adequate educational training to seek formal employment received vocational training and were linked to local vocational trade artisans to understudy various vocational trades. This group of youths will be further supported with start-up kits to commence their trades.
The program will target youths between the ages of 18-35 years in urban centes where IDP’s have been integrated into host community settlement with minimal livelihood opportunities. 
The project will focus on five LGA’s cutting across the BAY states namely: Jere and MMC in Borno, Yola North and Yola South LGA’s in Adamawa and Damaturu LGA in Yobe State.
The project will leverage on key Government, private sector local partners to deliver both theoretical training as well as practical apprenticeships.

A total of 400 youths will be targeted will be targeted in these areas to receive livelihood support under this intervention. 150 will be targeted under the Employability track and 250 youths will be targeted for the vocational training and apprenticeship support.

project_name: Provision of Common Services
project_objective:
The deterioration of the humanitarian situation in northern Mozambique has led to an estimated 1.3 million people in need of emergency assistance (HRP 2021). The security context deteriorated in early 2020 and worsened by June 2020 as several non-state armed groups (NSAGs) continued to attack both civilian population and government forces. The NSAGs expanded their areas interventions, which resulted in the capture of several district capital cities and intensified the level of violence over the past few months (ACLED data: more than 500 security incidents with around 1,800 fatalities). Of note is that the presence of the Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP) has been acknowledged by the Mozambican authorities on 24 April 2020.

In light of the situation in Cabo Delgado, more than half a million Mozambicans are considered to be internally displaced according the latest DTM Round 7 report from October 2020 (560,000 people according to Government estimates). Amongst them, 51 percent are children under the age of 18 and 27 per cent are women. The majority of them are located in Cabo Delgado and neighboring Niassa and Nampula provinces where nearly 90 percent of IDPs live in host communities amongst family members or acquaintances. The remaining 10 percent are in overcrowded camp-like settings without appropriate living-conditions. Nearly 800,000 host communities have also been directed or indirectly impacted by the crisis, including the displacements. 

As a result, key protection risks and incidents, including against children and women, have been reported as displacement further exacerbates the vulnerability level of the affected populations. 

Heavy rains and subsequent flooding experienced in early 2020 caused widespread infrastructure damage in Cabo Delgado including the destruction of the main bridge over Montepuez river that connects the northern districts to Pemba. Although some bridges have been repaired, the current, 2021, rainy season has exacerbated access to these locations via routes not yet repaired. 

Insecurity has hampered access by road to most of the areas from Nacala or Pemba hubs, between the districts or within the districts themselves. Consequently, the following districts are largely isolated either wholly or partially: Mocimboa da Praia; Palma; Macomia; Muidumbe; eastern part of Meluco; Mueda (periphery villages); Ancuabe (periphery villages) and Matemo most recently. The combination of insecurity, displacement, COVID-19, cholera, and extreme weather presents a significant challenge that requires an immediate review of the logistics arrangements which includes the use of sea and air operations to be able to transport personnel and humanitarian commodities to the affected areas. It is expected that access will be limited to the districts of, Nangade, Palma, and Mocimboa da Praia due to high levels of insecurity. The districts of Mueda and Macomia can potentially be accessed during the rainy season (provided that security conditions allow). 

The most northern and coastal districts of Cabo Delgado have been considered hard-to-reach areas and/or partially accessible due to the sharp decline of the security context. This concerns districts such as Palma, Ibo, Nangade, Mocimboa da Praia, Muidumbe, Macomia and Quissanga.  

WFP Logistics remains operational across borders and ports for transportation however, logistical challenges continue to arise, particularly as the humanitarian operation expands to reach more people people fleeing the conflict. The project aims to address these challenges by providing logistics information sharing, storage and transport of humanitarian items and passenger movement facilitation.
