project_name: NRC Shelter/NFI Response in Borno and Adamawa States
project_objective:
NRC’s shelter project objective is to adopt a participatory-based approach to improve the living conditions, dignity, and physical protection of the most vulnerable people affected by conflict in targeted areas of Northeast of Nigeria. In response to the protracted nature of the crisis, NRC will increasingly work in an integrated manner, bringing in Shelter and any other relevant competencies to collaborate on providing more durable and holistic solutions to displacement and return. Considering the complexities of displacement and return in both urban and rural areas, NRC will adopt a flexible approach to target specific needs with adaptable shelter options and incorporate safe programming principles in order to mitigate and respond to any potential adverse effects, which might result from the proposed shelter solution. The following include the overall area for the focus of the project:

1.	Emergency Response: Responding to the urgent shelter/NFI needs of IDP and returnee population occurring due to unforeseen reasons such as security incidents, communal clashes, natural disasters (flooding, fire, etc) or premature return or resettlement; 

2.	Protracted Displacement Response: Improving the shelter conditions in camps and camp-like sites by decongestion of camps and improving the emergency/transitional shelters habitability conditions; 

3.	Return Context Response: Contribution and facilitating safe and dignified return of IDPs by provision of adequate shelter conditions and exploration of diverse shelter modalities in host communities and areas of return.  

Based on its mandate, NRC will target the people directly impacted by the conflict, especially the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host-communities living in inadequate dwellings. Based on humanitarian analysis and internal assessment results, NRC in collaboration with the shelter sector will select areas of intervention using defined specific selection criteria, which will consider physical access and security in addition to the presence of IDPs in the area, and the areas offering opportunity for safe and voluntary return. NRC will target and select beneficiaries using a community-based approach, to promote the commitment of leaders and involvement of the host community and target groups. The target group will be defined and identified as follows:

	Most vulnerable IDPs: NRC seeks to target 6,000 IDPs households (HHs) divided into three following LGAs that NRC has currently a presence in: Maiduguri/Jere, Dikwa, Damasak, Monguno, Gwoza/Pulka, Mubi & Yola.

1.	Newly displaced needing emergency protection against the elements and those living in makeshift shelters; 
2.	IDPs who have been protractedly displaced and have no prospect for a clear durable solution, safe and voluntary return to areas of origin or local integration.  
3.	IDPs choosing integration in displacement areas and identified in coordination with local authorities or relevant sectorial mechanisms. Amongst this group will be those who have consented for integration or delocalization.
	Most vulnerable returnees: 3,500 HHs will be targeted amongst those already returned in their area of origin but living either with a host family, in destroyed houses, or in other alternative solutions. NRC will also target those who are newly returning facing secondary displacement and in need of emergency shelter/NFI assistance. LGAs included for shelter assistance to returnees are Maiduguri/Jere, Dikwa, Damasak, Monguno, Gwoza/Pulka, Mubi & Yola.

	Host communities: 500 vulnerable HHs that regularly host IDP families and that provide preliminary assistance by sharing their living space, food, and access to their lands. Maiduguri/Jere, Dikwa, Damasak, Monguno, Gwoza/Pulka, Mubi & Yola LGAs with high urban concentration of IDPs and returnees are selected for shelter assistance to the vulnerable host community.

project_name: Gender-Based Violence prevention and response assistance for host and refugee communities in Ukhiya Upazila.
project_objective: In 2021, DRC GBV will retain case management for women and girls, male survivors and child survivors in Camp 6, Rajapalong wards 6 and 9 and Palongkhali wards 5 and 6. DRC will establish 2 safe spaces through using existing infrastructures in Camps 2W and 10 for case management as well provide outreach sessions and psychosocial support for women and girls in Camp 6 and Rajapalong wards 6 and 9 and Palongkhali wards 5 and 6. Men and boy engagement activities will scale up in Camp 6 and Rajapalong wards 6 and 9. These activities will be introduced in Camp 8E and 8W. In Palongkhali, the biweekly hijra safe space will continue and one hijra safe space will be established in Camp 6. DRC will continue to involve the beneficiaries in each stage of planning and implementation for identifying the needs, vulnerabilities, priorities, and coping mechanisms. In all locations, outreach will be designed to include the disabled, and third gender with specialized outreach and participation modules by focusing protection mainstreaming in each stage.  DRC GBV technical expertise will be available to build the capacity of local GBV actors, including local authorities and local NGOs based on tailored needs assessments, and PSEA will also be shared through trainings. Also, DRC will continue to develop and map a partnership strategy through linking government, local NGOs, and private organisations and align the ISCG sector strategies for mainstreaming the activities. DRC will diversify the service accessibility fund in place for contingency needs. A hotline for case management support will be available throughout the year. The selection of locations is based on analysis of GBV-SS mapping and complements DRC’s other sectoral programme. DRC will set up CFRM in the host locations and direct to DRC CoC or CFRM as appropriate in refugee camps for AAP.

project_name: Multi-sectoral Response for the provision of protection and assistance to the refugee and asylum seeker populations living in Pakistan
project_objective:
Approximately 1,436,521 million Persons of Concern to UNHCR, including over 1.4 million Afghan refugees holding a Proof of Registration (PoR) Card and asylum seekers and refugees of various nationalities in Pakistan, continue to require some humanitarian assistance and solutions. 

The voluntary repatriation of over 1.4m Afghan refugees continues but has been limited due to the ongoing insecurity and instability in their country of origin and is further influenced by the peace process. They are still in need of international protection and multi-sectoral assistance with projects that consider their age, gender and diversity, to enable them to lead lives in dignity, in a protective environment.

In partnership with the GoP, Ministry of SAFRON and the Commissionerate for Afghan Refugees; UNHCR works to ensure the overall protection, security, assistance, management and administration of the Afghan refugee population residing in the refugee villages and urban areas. This includes voluntary repatriation activities and activities related to health, education, livelihoods, water and sanitation, community-based protection (CBP) and other services.

project_name: DRC (Danish Refugee Council) 2021 Integrated Response (multi-sector)
project_objective:
In Sudan, DRC's country-wide program purpose is designed to Respond to Conflict-Induced Emergencies, Protect Human Rights, Promote Sustainable Livelihoods and Foster Social Cohesion for Displacement Affected Communities and Host Communities.

The program revolves around three platforms which contribute to 1) immediate humanitarian assistance through emergency response, 2) recovery and resilience-building through durable solutions , and 3) helping communities working towards longer-term goals by addressing the root causes. 

Activities funded under this project would allow DRC to work alongside local authorities and affected communities in providing social and protection services and meeting basic needs (encompassing food security, shelter and non-food items and WASH).

Under this project, DRC will primarily be targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees either in current areas of interventions or in newly accessible areas in Central Darfur and South Kordofan. DRC will also build on its current program (Protection, GBV, Livelihood) currently delivered mixed-background communities living in under-served areas of Khartoum state. With that in mind, it is worth noting that host communities are also support where and when needed as our projects are implemented using community-driven and conflict-sensitive approaches

In addition to direct and immediate humanitarian assistance, DRC remains committed to supporting communities in achieving durable solutions following years of conflict and displacement. Recognizing that durable solutions are not something that can be achieved in isolation, DRC’s strategy in Sudan is to build partnerships around durable solutions projects, working closely to offer holistic opportunities on durable returns, by assisting displaced and returnee communities.

Throughout its interventions, DRC works closely with national humanitarian actors and relevant Government of Sudan ministries to ensure that the activities planned are in line with government broader standards and plans as well as community needs, and that local duty bearers have the capacity to build upon the integrated program that DRC will implement and sustain its positive impacts.

project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle aux populations vulnérabilisées par la crise au nord du Mali, dans la région de Tombouctou
project_objective:
Cette intervention vise à renforcer le projet d’urgence entamé en 2018. L’intervention d’ALIMA/AMCP-SP (A/A ci dessous) en 2021 vise contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et mortalité des populations hôtes et déplacées affectées par la crise dans la région de Tombouctou (DS de Goundam et Diré). Dans les DS visés par A/A, l’action vise à améliorer l’accès et l’utilisation des soins médico-nutritionnels gratuits et de qualité pour les populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire et ses conséquences socio-économiques. L’action se concentrera sur les femmes enceintes et allaitantes, les enfants de moins de 5 ans et les populations déplacées, qui sont les groupes de personnes les plus vulnérables. 23 CSCOM et 1 CSREF seront appuyés. A/A renforcera les activités curatives pour les populations qui n’ont pas accès aux soins
primaires à travers 4 cliniques mobiles, dans le DS de Goundam, pour les populations dont l’accès aux
centres de santé est limité par la distance géographique (populations au-delà de 15km des CSCOM),
pour les populations dont le CSCOM n’est plus fonctionnel (manque de matériels, RH...), et auprès des
PDI dans les 5 communes du DS de Diré accueillant des PDI. Ainsi 2 cliniques mobiles seront en place
dans le DS de Goundam et deux dans le DS de Diré. Bien que prévu pour les 5 communes du DS de
Diré, A/A se réserve la possibilité d’intervenir sur d’autres communes et sites au besoin (augmentation
nombre de PDI ou urgence). Le volet communautaire sera également renforcé, en incluant une
campagne de formation PB mères pour les femmes en âge de procréer ainsi que la reprise de la
formation et du dépistage actif des ReCos dans le DS de Goundam. A/A apportera une contribution à la
veille sanitaire et humanitaire et pourra participer à la réponse aux situations d’urgence à travers le
RRM.
Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le COVID-19, A/A va intervenir au niveau communautaire et dans les structures de santé déjà appuyées. A/A va donc former les staffs à la PCI, va fournir des EPI et revoir les circuits patients. Des salles d'isolement dans les CSREF de Goundam et de Diré seront mises en place avec tout le nécessaire pour en faire des salles de transit en attendant de référer via des ambulances spéciales COVID-19 à l'hôpital régional de Tombouctou. Dans les communautés, des messages de prévention seront disséminés grâce aux radios locales et aux crieurs publics en langue locale. La même chose sera mise en place à l'hôpital de référence du CHU de Kati suite à la demande des autorités sanitaires nationales.
A/A ne fera pas de prise en charge.

project_name: Bâtir le futur à travers le développement holistique des jeunes enfants
project_objective: Le présent projet s’inscrit dans les réformes importantes en cours dans les domaines de la santé, éducation et du social. Au niveau national, ce projet vise à un alignement total avec les priorités de développement définies par le gouvernement du Tchad, y compris au travers de ses politiques et stratégies de planification, à savoir le Plan Intérimaire de l’Éducation (PIET-2018-2020), le Programme protection de l’enfant (2017-2021), le Plan national de développement sanitaire (PNDS 2018-2021), et le Plan stratégique de santé communautaire 2015-2018, le Plan National de développement (2017-2021), la Politique nationale Genre (2011 adopté en 2017) et sa Stratégie nationale de lutte contre les violences basées sur le Genre en cours d’adoption. Il s’agira ici notamment de s’inscrire dans le cadre du Plan sécurité et développement du Lac (en cours de finalisation sous l’égide du gouverneur avec l‘appui PNUD). Ce projet est aussi aligné aussi à la Politique Nationale de Santé (PNS) 2016-2030 dont l’un des axes stratégiques vise particulièrement la « promotion de la santé communautaire dans toutes les zones de responsabilités », sur le Plan Intérimaire pour l’Education, le Programme protection de l’enfant, la politique nationale Genre comme mentionné précédemment. Au niveau provincial, le projet s’aligne sur le Plan Régional de Développement Sanitaire (PRDS) et le Plan d’Action Opérationnel du DS de Bol ainsi que le Plan sécurité et développement du Lac.

project_name: Asset creation (including Disaster Risk Reduction) Project and Site Maintenance Engineering
project_objective: Through the Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) programme and Site Maintenance Engineering Project (SMEP), WFP will work with Rohingya refugee and host communities to prevent and reduce risks from natural disasters, enhance accessibility and strengthen resilience. The project will provide targeted food assistance for Rohingya refugees and enhance food security in host communities through asset creation (including Disaster Risk Reduction) by building and rehabilitating assets that will create a healthier natural environments, reduce the risks and impact of climate shocks and strengthen resilience to natural disasters over time. Also ensuring inclusive approach integrated with gender equality, women’s empowerment and protection principles including strong coordination at the camp-level (with SD focals and SMS) and to coordination at Cox’s Bazar with sector.

project_name: Renforcement de capacités et réduction des risques des VBG pour les PDI de Bagasola
project_objective:
Le Tchad continue à faire face à des défis sécuritaires importants émaillés de la présence des groupes armés dans la province du Lac Tchad notamment et qui y occasionnent des déplacements des populations. Cette situation a des conséquences sur le bien-être physique et mental, les conditions de vie et, de manière transversale, à la protection de la population. 
Tchad compte au 31 décembre 2020, 917 534 personnes relevant de la compétence du HCR soit 477 720 Réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile, 336 124 personnes déplacés internes et 69 343 retournés tchadiens. Tous les 336 124 personnes déplacés internes sont tous localisés dans la province du Lac
La situation de protection continue de se dégrader dans la province du Lac en raison de l´augmentation des incidents de sécurité liés aux conflits armés (781 incidents de protection et 1 236 cas de violences basées sur le genre notifiés entre janvier et août 2019). 
La faiblesse du développement et des investissements dans plusieurs secteurs et les changements climatiques expliquent en partie la persistance des crises humanitaires affectant les conditions de vie des populations
Dans ce contexte de conflits armés, d’insuffisance d’infrastructures sociales et de dysfonctionnement des structures sanitaires, les violences basées sur le genre y compris les violences sexuelles affectent de manière plus sévère les personnes en situation de déplacement et communauté hôte.
En effet, l´activisme de ces groupes armés et les mesures de sécurité mises en place par le gouvernement tchadien pour lutter contre la violence extrémiste restreignent d´avantage la liberté de mouvement de la population vers des zones d’opportunités. Ceci entraîne l´insécurité alimentaire et par conséquence les cas d´exploitation et d´abus sexuel, la prostitution forcée, les mariages forcés, ainsi que le recours aux moyens de survie néfastes comme le ´´sexe pour survie´´. La rareté des ressources domestiques notamment les bois de chauffe exposent les femmes et les filles à des risques de SGBV qui parcourent des kilomètres pour s’en procurer.
Le projet de renforcement de capacités et pour l’atténuation des risques des VBG dans les sites de DPI portera sur la prévention, l’atténuation et la réponse aux violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre et touchera la communauté hôte dont des IDP et des retournes de Dar Es Salam. Ceci est en droite ligne le plan de réponse pour les PDI au Tchad HRP 2021 et le plan de réponse du sous cluster VBG.  
Le projet, dans sa composante de renforcement de capacités, portera sur les activités de formation, mobilisation communautaire, le renforcement du système communautaire de prévention des VBG et la formation des acteurs étatiques (autorités administratives et judiciaires, l’autorité sécuritaire et le personnel éducatif) en vue de la mise en place d’une plateforme d’assistance holistique des survivants.   
Ainsi, l’atténuation des risques d’exposition aux VBG doit porter sur l’amélioration de l’accès durable aux sources d’énergies vertes et l’autonomisation des femmes et filles. La mise en place de cadres sûrs leur permettra d’acquérir des compétences de vie en vue d’avoir des conditions de vie dignes et des opportunités pour réaliser des activités économiques. Enfin, la réalisation de leur autonomie financière sera accompagnée conformément à la Politique National Genre. 
Le projet se focalisera sur les sites de la sous-préfecture de Bagasola. Lors de la mise en œuvre du projet, le HCR travaillera dans une approche inter-agence avec UNFPA pour la mise en œuvre de la stratégie du sous-cluster VBG. 
Ainsi, dans le cadre de mise en œuvre des objectifs et réponses sectorielles du sous cluster VBG, le HCR prévoit de renforcer ses interventions en matière de lutte contre les VBG dans les sites de PDI et les villages des communautés d’accueil qui sont dans les environs du camp de refugies (rayon de 10 km). Ceci permettra d’assurer la complémentarité avec les mêmes efforts qui y sont initiés.

project_name: Basic Needs Support Programme: Winter Clothes for Children
project_objective:
The scale, severity and complexity of humanitarian needs have become even more extensive due to the economic downturn, the rising cost of commodities, the devaluation of local currency; all compounded by the socio-economic impact of COVID-19 and ongoing hostilities. This has created devastating consequences for already vulnerable populations across the country, particularly displaced populations and returnees.  This situation has left many families unable to provide for the basic needs of the children, particularly during the critical wintertime. This is particularly true for families who have been displaced several times and continue to live in dire conditions.  

It is estimated that 1.9 million are living in an informal settlement and planned camps, representing a 20% increase since January 2020 (HNO 2021). During 2020, an estimated 448,000 IDP returned to their places of origin and 38,200 refugees returned to Syria (HNO 2021).  Children who have been displaced and continue to live under dire conditions in poorly insulated houses and overcrowded makeshift shelters are particularly vulnerable.

The main objective of the programme is to protect children affected by the crisis and displacement in Syria from harsh weather conditions through the provision of winter clothes. The right to adequate clothing is a universal human right and a basic necessity, which is recognized in various human rights instruments.

This project aims to reach 250,000 children 0 to 14 years of age with winter clothing kits. The targeting strategy of the programme is geographical and primarily focuses on children from the internally displaced communities living in camps, informal settlements, abandoned or unfinished buildings or collective shelters. Clothing kits are age-appropriate and are procured locally. They are divided according to eight standard age groups within the 0-14 years old category. Items in the kits are gender-neutral in terms of colour and style. Each winter clothing kit contains nine items, while each baby kit contains 19 items.  

The programme strategy is in line with the shelter/ NFIs sector result framework 2021 and related activity. Accountability to beneficiaries is ensured through a three-pronged approach:  (i) Complaint & Response Mechanism (CRM); (ii) Post- Distribution Monitoring surveys (PDMs) (iii) on-site monitoring activities.

The project target 250,000 girls and boys disaggregated as the following:
56% of IDPs, 10% of host communities, 34% of returnees.
52% females and 48% males 
5% of persons with disabilities

The average unit cost is $ 38 for a winter kit, $78.5 for baby kits

project_name: Provision of Protective Services to Children and Caregivers Affected by the Conflict
project_objective:
Ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine continues to weaken child protection systems creating
new risks for affected boys, girls and their caregivers. COVID-19 pandemic as well as quarantine restrictions added new challenges for conflict-affected families, whose resources are already scarce. To respond to the urgent needs, UNICEF is planning to strengthen child protection systems (C01) and to provide direct services to affected children and their families (CO2). Specifically, UNICEF will continue to 1. provide psycho-social and protective services to children and their caregivers (including to  survivors of gender-based violence, children affected by violence and  children and caregivers affected by mines and unexploded ordinance) (P02), 2.  implement activities aimed at prevention of violence and  mine-risk education) (P01),  and 3. ensure capacity building to
community professionals working with children (P02). In addition, UNICEF will carry out activities directed at improving parenting skills among caregivers to strengthen relationships between caregivers and their children and promote their  wellbeing. Taken together, these activities are aimed to strengthen local response systems, including availability of 
specialized services, as well as to ensure direct service provision where needed services
are not available.

project_name: Provision of holistic education and protection support to conflict affected children in eastern Ukraine.
project_objective:
With the assumption of temporary localised school lockdowns on both sides of the contact line, Save the Children (SC) will build on previous phases of Schools as Zones of Peace project implementation to expand support to boys and girls with specific focus on the schools along the contact line. The approach of setting up School Safety Committees (SSC) consisting of parents, children and teachers to identify safety risks, train them on child rights, child participation, gender equality etc. and implement action plans to increase the safety of the school will be implemented. Recognizing the higher severity of needs in NGCA as per the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview, SC will increase its presence through local partner which has experience of implementation of education projects in NGCA. 

Special attention will be given to protective measures against COVID 19 and Safe School reopening following expected waves of localised school lockdowns. SC will also support distance learning by strengthening teachers’ capacities to deliver online classes. Recognizing differences in local response to COVID-19 and barriers to accessing remote education, a school-by-school approach will be taken to support children (including children with disabilities) access learning safely (whether in person in line with the Safe Back to School Practitioner’s guide or remotely). These options could be supplying teachers with equipment to deliver classes online or print learning materials for children who cannot access the internet, hygiene kits, awareness raising etc.).

Teachers will be trained to provide in different topics to ensure they have knowledge and skills to ensure children and their own wellbeing and to contribute to resilience building and disaster risk reduction processes. Parents, teachers and children’s capacity will be built on child rights and inclusive education (for children with disabilities, including those injured in the conflict), in particular for children who might have been left behind during distance learning.  
In the context of COVID-19 where it is highly likely that cases of domestic violence and violence against children has increased during and following lockdowns, SC will build use its experience to support existing referral mechanism recognising protective role of education. 

Save the Children will continue delivering trainings on the Safe Schools Declaration and Guidelines to Protect Schools and Universities from Military Attack in Armed Conflict to civil military officers and Ukrainian Army officers. SC will continue looking for opportunities to deliver online innovative Safe Schools Declaration trainings. SC will continue advocating on setting up of the inter-ministerial taskforce consisting of key ministries in charge of the implementation of the SSD. SC will support the Government in clarifying their policy on the use of schools and universities during armed conflict as part of the SSD national implementation plan to be adopted by the GoU. SC will contribute to global advocacy mechanisms by submitting report to relevant treaty monitoring bodies and working with the UN Ukraine mission in global fora. 

In 2021 SC will support transition of the Education Cluster functions to relevant stakeholders on both sides of the contact line through consultations and capacity building events.

project_name: Strengthening the livelihoods and resilience capacities of internally displaced young women and men, affected by conflicts in the South-West region of Cameroon through the establishment of income-generating activities and psychosocial activities .
project_objective:
This proposal aims to meet the urgent needs of strengthening livelihoods in the increasingly unstable south-western region of Cameroon on the security front. This instability causes a deficit in the socio-economic level of the population, more particularly young women and men. This degradation of the socio-economic situation and this fear installed at the level of the population creates major distress among young people in particular. Through this project, Action Against Hunger (AAH) aims to revive and strengthen livelihoods through the establishment of a mechanism for the economic and social integration of young women and men as well as psychosocial support in the Southwest region.

Beyond the aspect of emergency socio-economic integration and psychosocial support,, AAH aims to consolidate the achievements of previous projects in relation to nutrition / health by taking into account experiences for adapt the approach and targeting of these young people and their households. This project aims to strengthen local capacity through the positive economic benefits of income-generating activities (IGA) that will be put in place to support young people. The municipalities will be targeted according to pockets of needs and in relation to the Harmonized framework of March 2021. The aim is to cover the real needs in relation to the changing context of the region. This support targets 1,000 households (ie 7,000 displaced women and men) in the most vulnerable villages in the region. The targeting criteria will be adapted to better capture the following people:
• Young women and men aged between 18 and 30 in households with non-existent sources of income and who have experienced a direct impact of the Anglophone conflict in the region.
• Young people, among the criteria mentioned above, showing signs of psychological distress
• Young single-parent household head with no sources of income
• Household with at least one youngster with one or more malnourished children
• Households with a high adaptation strategy above the acceptable threshold
• Young women and men internally displaced to flee conflict and without any means of subsistence.

It should be noted that the integration of the MHPSS component in this youth support project will make it possible to take care of people in psychological distress and the most vulnerable to facilitate this process of economic integration in a stable and sustainable manner.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de servicios de Protección y Salud Inclusiva para retornados y población en riesgo en Venezuela
project_objective:
La intervención tiene como objetivo  incrementar el acceso a programas de rehabilitación física y funcional y servicios de la salud mental y apoyo psicosocial para retornados y población vulnerable en Venezuela, con un enfoque particular en personas con discapacidad y adulto mayor. Esto se realizará mediante la identificación y apoyo a personas vulnerables a través de la asistencia directa o las derivaciones, y del monitoreo de sus necesidades de protección y orientación a servicios. Al mismo tiempo se pretende fortalecer los servicios de rehabilitación física y de salud mental y apoyo psicosocial en las áreas geográficas seleccionadas, San Francisco (Zulia) y La Pastora (Caracas).  Asimismo, la intervención fomentará la participación de las personas con discapacidad en los programas de ayuda humanitaria mediante el apoyo a otras agencias y ONGs para la inclusión de personas con discapacidad dentro del ciclo de sus programas a través de capacitaciones y apoyo técnico. Esto con el fin de desarrollar una respuesta humanitaria más inclusiva, y contribuir a proporcionar datos de calidad para fomentar la programación inclusiva basada en evidencia. La estrategia de respuesta está compuesta por las siguientes actividades/sectores:
- Protección inclusiva a personas con discapacidad, NNA, adulto mayor, y sus cuidadores: derivación a rehabilitación física y funcional; distribución de ayudas técnicas (sillas de ruedas, muletas, andaderas, etc.) según necesidades; provisión de servicios de la salud mental y apoyo psicosocial; sensibilización comunitaria sobre la salud mental y temáticas de discapacidad; identificación y orientación a servicios específicos de proteccion;
- Acción humanitaria inclusiva y los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: capacitación y apoyo técnico a organizaciones locales e internacionales, grupos de trabajo, clusters, sobre Acción Humanitaria Inclusiva para incluir personas con discapacidad dentro de sus programas.

El proyecto pretende alcanzar los siguientes beneficiarios:
Personas vulnerables con necesidades específicas  evaluadas y provistas de orientación e información sobre servicios, y derivados a servicios especializados: 1,100 individuos; de los cuales (tomando en cuenta que cada persona puede recibir más de un servicio):
       - Personas apoyadas (pago de servicios y/o transporte) a acceder servicios especializados de salud mental: 500 individuos
       - Personas recibiendo apoyo psicosocial comunitario: 200 individuos
       -Personas apoyadas (pago de servicios y/o transporte) a acceder servicios de rehabilitación física y funcional: 400 individuos
       - Personas recibiendo sesiones de sensibilización sobre temáticas de discapacidad a nivel comunitario:  200 individuos
       - Personas recibiendo ayudas técnicas (sillas de ruedas, muletas, andaderas, bastones, asientos adaptados, etc.): 140 individuos
       - Personas apoyadas (pago servicio y/o transporte) a acceder servicios de protección: 100 individuos
Personas recibiendo asistencia psicosocial de emergencia a traves de una linea de atencion de Emergencia: 1,850 individuos
Centros y organizaciones de Rehabilitacion física y/o SMAPS recibiendo apoyo (financiero/de conocimiento/técnico): 5 organizaciones
Personas recibiendo capacitación en Acción Humanitaria Inclusiva: 500 individuos
Organizaciones recibiendo apoyo técnico para que sus programas sean inclusivos de personas con discapacidad: 8 organizaciones

Esta propuesta ha sido desarrollada de acuerdo a la estrategia de respuesta humanitaria dispuesta por el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria (HRP) con Panorama de Necesidades Humanitarias (HNO) 2020 para Venezuela, y  tiene como objetivo complementar, fortalecer e integrar otras intervenciones a nivel regional respondiendo a la crisis Venezolana, así como otras agencias y ONGs trabajando en Venezuela.

project_name: Life-Saving WASH and Resilience Rehabilitation Program in Syria
project_objective:
A leader in the fight against malnutrition, AAH implements gender-sensitive life-saving WASH interventions and provide communities with access to safe water and sanitation as sustainable mitigation for hunger causes. After decade of conflicts, drought, economic stagnation and the recent pandemic, basic services infrastructures in the country are facing unprecedented stress and deterioration. AAH continuously assess the basic needs of different communities across the country. Access to water, adequate sanitation and proper access to health and education were found as top priorities. AAH mandate consists of supporting the functional authorities in responding to crises and regaining resilience and preparedness capabilities, in this scope AAH prioritizes sustainable resilience WASH projects, however, provides life-saving rapid WASH (Water trucking, distribution of water storage containers and hygiene items) when access to the basic WASH needs becomes severe or critical.  

AAH operates through three field offices in Damascus, Aleppo and Hassakeh, and provides wide range of WASH services. AAH keeps a close contact with SARC and Ministry of Water resources in addition to other governmental institutions (Ministries of Local Administration and Environment, Education and Health, Governorates and local administrations) in order to coordinate efforts and involve the functional authorities in program design, implementation, capacity building and monitoring. In NES, AAH coordinates with UNICEF and NES WWG for its interventions in Hassakeh, and Deir El Zor.  

WASH resilience response includes rehabilitation of more than 21 water and 6 sewage systems (networks, pumping stations and treatment plants).  AAH also targets public institutions and intends to intervene in 75 schools and 7 public health centers with rehabilitation of WASH facilities, hygiene promotion campaigns and COVID19 response. AAH will provide water trucking in Hassakeh city, rural Idlib and rural Aleppo (areas under GoS) and Daraa, and provide comprehensive WASH intervention in two IDP camps (Areesha and Abo khashab) through direct support to beneficiaries using remote operation modalities.  

Rehabilitation works will be coupled with capacity building on operation and maintenance, and provision of water safety plans. While distribution will be paralleled with behavioral change promotion sessions and messaging. All activities will respect the COVID19 guidelines.  

AAH intervention will focus on the locations with WASH severity 3 and higher as per the HNO, and the identification of potential projects will be done through MEAL and technical needs assessments, as well as through focus group discussion, Key informant interviews, referrals and requests from relevant authorities and sectors. However, the identification of WASH interventions in public institutions will be based on the severity scores of the relevant sectors being Health and Education (i.e. rehabilitation of schools and PHCs in Hama). AAH WASH will target 1,321,900 beneficiaries in total of which 674,174 females (>18 y.o. 310,308; <18 y.o. 363,866) and 647,726 males (>18 y.o. 298,140; <18 y.o. 349,586). AAH will reach 29,600 students in mixed-gender and gender-disaggregated schools of which 15,096 are females, and around 24K in emergency response of which 12,240 are females.

Community engagement throughout the program design and implementation will be encouraged, and consultations with stakeholders will be carried out in order to avoid duplication and to target the most vulnerable communities. Protection, GBV, PSEA, Climate change and green technologies will be mainstreamed, and a functional feedback mechanism will be maintained to collect complaints and suggestions feeding the monitoring and learning process. 

Post intervention monitoring, and satisfaction surveys will measure the accomplishment of the project indicator, impact and acceptance of the aid provided.

project_name: Multisector humanitarian assistance to highly vulnerable conflict-affected older people living in Donetska and Luhanska Oblasts
project_objective:
PAH will provide multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable conflict-affected older people (60+ years old), residing in Donetska Non-Government Controlled Area (NGCA) and Donetska and Luhanska Government Controlled Areas (GCAs).
In Donetska NGCA, PAH proposed program that is focused on covering the most acute needs of older people residing in Donetska NGCA through provision of food and hygiene assistance. In total, 5000 older people planned to be covered under the project. With support of Partner, the clients of the local Territorial Centers of Social Services, who are the most vulnerable elderly people living in project locations, will be assisted. Each person will receive three food kits that will cover their needs during three months’ period, ensuring their full nutrition requirements (2100 Kcal per day per person). Also, each older person will receive a three-month hygiene kit including hygiene promotion component. Additionally, 1000 older people with special needs will be provided with hygiene kits for people with special needs. The materials on mitigation of risks of COVID-19 transmission will be provided and presented to the beneficiaries during distributions. Taking into consideration the COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine, the distribution will be based on COVID-19 Ukraine Assistance Delivery protocol.
In the areas along the “contact line” in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts in GCAs, PAH will run 12 Community Centers to provide psychosocial support services to older people, suffering from social isolation and psychological distress. PAH’s psychologists will provide group structured PSS, as well as individual structured PSS at home or remotely to those older people who have a complex psycho-emotional state, such as increased anxiety, depression and others. Psychologists will be also providing individual consultations. At the same time, PAH community workers will provide individual PSS sessions based on a simplified programme at home or remotely to older people, who have slight and moderate mobility, or slight and moderate problems with hearing, vision, speech, and attention, as well as home-based care services, including psychosocial support, to those beneficiaries who have severe mental and / or neurological problems and / or serious mobility problems, such as dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, effects of a stroke, etc. Primary legal assistance will be also provided to those older people who have no access to legal services, for example, to obtain benefits for caring for a person with disability, to restore passport, etc. Moreover, 300 assistive devices and 200 WASH NFIs will be provided to the most vulnerable older people. At the same time, 500 most vulnerable older people with disabilities will be provided with individual protection assistance in cash. Multipurpose cash assistance will be provided to 1250 the most vulnerable people to decrease the use of negative coping mechanisms by covering basic needs which in its turn will contribute to the improvement of their psychosocial well-being. Beneficiary group has access to local market, as essential goods and services are mostly accessible on the local markets along the “contact line” in Donetska and Luhanska GCA, although not always affordable for elder people due to high prices (for 60,6% of respondents) and problems with transportation (for 13,0% of respondents). All above mentioned activities will be implemented in line with COVID-19 restrictions and relevant recommendations from the Clusters on reducing the risk of transmission. 
Combination of protection, multipurpose cash assistance, WASH and food security assistance shall reduce vulnerabilities of the conflict-affected older population living in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts through improved access to and provision of humanitarian assistance and improving their overall well-being.

project_name: Support local healthcare system to respond to the covid-19 pandemic while enabling access to quality health care services to  conflict-affected population at both sides of the line of contact in Donetsk oblast
project_objective:
In order to respond to emergency health needs of the conflict-affected population, PUI intends to continue its emergency intervention in Entry-Exit Check Points (EECPs) and in various rayons of Donetsk oblast both in government and non-government controlled areas. 
In particular, to improve quality of care and stay conditions in health facilities (HF), PUI will ensure donation of medical/non-medical supplies, rehabilitations including Wash rehabilitations, NFI winterization support and capacity building of staff. In order to increase access to health services for the most vulnerable ones, PUI will provide a cash-based support to children < 5, to PLW, to adults > 60 and to individuals in need of emergency assistance. In addition, financial support will be provided to HF to ensure referrals of patients from the different levels of care. Where possible and relevant, PUI teams will also promote the use of alternative models of care such as e-health. 
At EECP level, PUI will continue to ensure people have access to drinking water, sanitation facilities (incl. hand washing stations) and emergency health services. PUI will continue to work with authorities for the hand-over of these activities. 
In order to support national response to COVID-19 and ensure HF/SI compliant with minimum WASH standards, PUI will support HF/SI via donation of essential medical/non-medical equipment, consumables, PPE sets and cleaning kits. Facilities will be supported in the implementation of screening and triage protocols. At EECP level, PUI will ensure that suspected COVID-19 cases are able to be temporarily isolated and properly referred to designated infrastructures. Both at facility and EECP level, activities will be completed with awareness raising activities related to COVID-19 and good hygiene practices. Staff of facilities will be briefed on how to ensure infection, prevention control and based on needs identified related rehabilitations/arrangements will be conducted. Individual material support in terms of hygiene kits will also be provided to vulnerable individuals including immobile and partially mobile people that would be identified by partner HF/SI. Synchronously with the integration of MHPSS into PHC in the framework of the current Health Reform, PUI will strengthen capacities of health care workers in mental health and psychosocial support. Individual psychosocial support will also be provided to people in need including community’s members and health providers.
Health is a fundamental human right and for this reason, project will aim to ensure that all people of the targeted areas have access to essential health services and that those services are of good quality. A specific focus will nevertheless be placed on the most vulnerable populations including children under 5, adults over 60, people with disabilities, PLW and health workers. It should be noted that women will constitute the biggest part of project beneficiaries considering that they are over represented among health workers and people over 60.  Based on PUI’s field experience, women are also more eager to use MHPSS services. In addition, it is worth noting that among HF/SI, PUI will support in priority pediatric/maternity wards and nursing homes.
PUI multi-sectorial approach combining assistance in the sectors of health, WASH and NFI winterization will ensure people have access to health services of good quality and that health facilities offers safe and dignified conditions of visit/stay for patients and working conditions for health providers. Responding to wash gaps in HF will ensure the adoption of infection prevention and control (IPC) measures and the reduction of nosocomial infection risks. Similarly, PUI combination of health and wash assistance at EECP level, ensure that people crossing have access to comprehensive services including clean water, adequate sanitation facilities, first aid services and information related to COVID-19.

project_name: Reinforcing the provision of comprehensive Emergency Life-saving and Life-sustaining Healthcare in the context of COVID-19.
project_objective:
INTERSOS has been implementing lifesaving health activities within Borno state in covering 4 LGAs: Bama, Magumeri, Dikwa and Ngala since 2017 by providing free primary health care services to vulnerable populations both IDPs and host community. In Bama LGA, INTERSOS is currently providing free primary health care services (General OPD consultations, rapid diagnosis of common morbidities such as malaria and cholera, SRH services and referral of patients in need of secondary/ specialized health care services) at the GSSSS IDP camp and OTP at the Bama MCH facility, and is the only health actor in Magumeri LGA.

Through this project, INTERSOS intention is to strengthen the existing health system by providing support to the MCH health facility (in Bama LGA), and Magumeri General Hospital and its catchment PHCs in the remote hard-to-reach (H2R) parts of Gajiganna. INTERSOS will support MOH to ensure the continuation of health services by deployment of heath staff, provide performance-based stipends and capacity building / training, essential medical equipment and supplies, support in reproductive health services including BeMoc and SGBV services for survivors of sexual assault. The project will facilitate the referral of patients in need of secondary / specialized health care facilities to Maiduguri. INTRESOS will also engage in community mobilization and engagement through the CHV to provide health education, active case finding and referral of patients to the health facility. In addition, INTERSOS will mainstream protection, GBV, inclusion and COVID-19 risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) throughout the stages and activities of the project. Through the NHF funding, INTERSOS proposes to support increasing and the local health systems capacity for readiness and response for cholera, malaria and other epidemic prone diseases like hepatitis E, meningitis and measles. This includes procurement and pre-positioning of cholera kits, essential drugs and supplies in the supported facilities. The interventions seek to reinforce community dialogue and engagements in all health activities to systematically collect and provide answers to questions coming from the community and facilitate community-led response planning. In addition, the intervention will strengthen capacity of the existing CHWs to be able to detect and report suspected cases in support of the EDPT strategy of disease prevention. For a sustainable approach that will promote easy takeover by the MOH, INTERSOS will recruit only professional health positions, while the government will provide CHEWs and other support but INTERSOS will pay a performance- based incentive.

By addressing those unfunded gaps (through this proposal to NHF) in a well-coordinated rights-based approach that engages the target communities, government (SMOH, the Emergency Operations Centre [EOC] etc.,), UN agencies and the existing coordination structures: - a complete package of quality lifesaving and life-sustaining health services will be provided the most vulnerable populations in Bama GSSSS IDP camp and the host community. All services will be provided in accordance with guidelines approved by the health sector, SMoH, NCDC, WHO, SPHERE and other international standards, and in accordance with humanitarian principles -- free from all forms discrimination, based on prioritized need, avoiding duplication and with a focus on specific vulnerabilities, including pregnant and lactating women (PLW), persons with disabilities, elderly, chronically ill, IDPs and IDPs.

In order to provide an integrated multi-sector services, INTERSOS will implement the proposed activities in the same geographical areas and populations targeted by the nutrition, WASH and Protection proposals.

project_name: Strengthening sector coordination mechanism to support the humanitarian response in Libya
project_objective:
Operating in Libya remains challenging, with numerous security, logistical and access constraints. Strong and effective sector coordination mechanism is required to ensure humanitarian action is timely, effective & meets the needs of vulnerable people.
Collaboration with national/International Humanitarian actors and Human Rights organizations are critical to ensure that assistance is provided safely and respects people’s dignity. Functional sectors and inter sector coordination group support humanitarian actors with coordination, information management, needs assessments, advocacy for access, safety
and protection. It will benefit the entire humanitarian community to effectively and timely reach the most vulnerable people in Libya, as well as to sustain and extend their members’ operational reach and impact.

project_name: Shelter Assistance and provision of Non-food items to the most vulnerable population in Libya
project_objective:
In 2021, the Shelter and NFI sector will continue both with emergency response as well as more durable and tailored support depending on the specific needs of the population targeted.
In order to prevent further deterioration of the shelter and NFI availability situation of the most vulnerable populations of concern, the sector’s response will be delivered in accordance with the following objectives and UNCHR projects will be focusing on the same below objectives too:
•	Objective 1: Provide humanitarian life-saving and life-sustaining shelter and NFI support
•	Objective 02: Contribute towards the resilience of communities and households by improving housing and related community/public infrastructure.

The first key objective for this project will be to save and sustain lives through the provision of timely, targeted and appropriate shelter assistance and relief items. 
In-kind assistance will be prioritized in the forms of family NFI packages during emergency responses and for long-term displaced populations in need of support. Seasonal items will also be distributed to sustain lives and reduce the impact of exposure to extreme conditions and will be one of the main focuses of the NFI response.

In response to COVID-19 needs, UNHCR will ensure the continuation of periodic assessments to all IDPs settlements in Libya to ensure the needed quantities of hygiene kits are provided as well as other items which contribute to increase the hygienic environment such as mattresses, blankets…etc.  
UNHCR is estimating to assist 39,922 individuals with both shelter and NFIs projects with the above objectives and with a cost of 2,789,831 USD.

project_name: Projet d’appui à la gouvernance inclusive et participative de la réponse nutritionnelle (PAGIPNUT)
project_objective:
L'objectif général du projet est d'améliorer de manière durable la situation nutritionnelle des populations du District sanitaire de Tombouctou et de la région de Taoudéni.
L'objectif spécifique est de renforcer les capacités des organes de gestion et de gouvernance locale pour la prévention, la détection précoce et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë au niveau de Tombouctou et Taoudéni.
Cela se fait dans le cadre d'une stratégie d'intervention conçue autour de l’accompagnement et de la 
 responsabilisation :

project_name: Enhancing the delivery of quality protection services by improving the protection environment and supporting durable solutions for IDPs, IDP returnees and refugee returnees in North East Nigeria.
Improvement of the Protection of People of Concern in North East Nigeria Through the Provision of Shelter and NFI Assistance.
project_objective: This project will target IDPs and returnees in three affected states, Yobe, Adamawa and Borno with provision of emergency shelters, Non-food Items (NFIs), transitional and shelter repair kits as protection live-saving assistance aligned with Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM Sector strategic objectives for the HRP 2019. In 2019 UNHCR continued to effectively respond to shelter needs and aims to target a total of 69,569 households, 347,846 individuals in formal and informal camps and newly accessible areas by the end of the year. As the number of returns and displacement increases due to military operations, there is need to provide shelter related assistance for returnees who are residing in their plots and as well as for host families whose resources have been overstretched. Subsequently acknowledging that the humanitarian situation is still unpredictable; there is need to provide shelters and NFIs for life-saving emergency assistance to promote the protection, safety and dignity of affected Persons of Concern (PoCs). Despite the achievements in the past, the continuous needs for IDPs, though shaped by very different dynamics, revealed that quite a significant majority of people are living in congested camps. The needs assessment conducted in 2019 by Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM sector indicated that as of end of June 2019, 3809 IDP households were living without shelter and NFI assistance since their arrival. In addition to that, 7593 households living in partitioned communal shelters needed NFIs and dignified emergency shelters. The ongoing and protracted displacement leaves the affected people in need of other humanitarian assistance such as Food, WASH, and Health among others. In 2020, UNHCR shall build upon progress being made in 2019 and proposes to respond to unmet needs in Adamawa (Mubi North, Mubi South, Madagali, Michika, Yola South and Yola north); Borno (Bama, Banki, Damasak, Damboa, Dikwa, Jere, konduga, Gwoza, Pulka, Maiduguri, Mobbar, Monguno, Rann and Ngala) and Yobe State (Damaturu and Gujba,) through provision of; - (1) 7,000 Emergency shelters (2) 52,129 NFIs kits to IDPs in both formal and informal camps (3) 10,440 Shelter repair kits to returnees with the provision of conditional CASH component of NGN 30,000 Naira adequate to cover for the cost labor and molding of mud bricks among other unforeseen needs. All the shelters are designed to cater for Women, Men, Girls and boys, persons with specific needs and partitioned to mitigate SGBV cases. The selection of beneficiaries will be based on needs assessment and vulnerability screening in the locations at the time of implementation. Identification and verification of beneficiaries are guided by UNHCR’s Protection principles, and endorsed by community leaders, NEMA, and SEMA officials at LGA areas. UNHCR will reinforce a transparent process of beneficiary selection and the prioritization of needs of vulnerable groups. The project targets the IDPs and Returnees households suffering from protracted displacement and returning home. UNHCR will work to ensure that potential beneficiaries are aware of their responsibilities during the project and of options available to them. It is important to recognize that not everyone can manage the construction/ repair of their own house and that their time might be better used to generate income. The families’ decision to participate in this programme will be achieved through sensitization meetings, detailed assessments, participatory planning and prioritizing the provision of technical training and capacity building. A community-based feedback mechanism through regular mass meetings and focus group discussions will be established to enable IDPs express their opinions on issues affecting their assistance need. The discussions will also provide beneficiaries the opportunity to understand the shelter selection and allocation process.

project_name: Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et restaurer les moyens de subsistance agro-pastoraux des populations vulnérables hôtes et déplacées dans les régions de Tahoua et Diffa touchées par les crises sécuritaire et climatique
project_objective:
L’objectif général du projet est d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et de renforcer les moyens d’existence et la résilience des populations déplacées et hôtes, affectées par les crises sécuritaires dans les régions de Tahoua et de Diffa, en fournissant une assistance humanitaire et un support pour le renforcement des moyens d’existence aux communautés les plus touchées par les crises sécuritaires, les déficits pluviométriques et les faibles productions agricoles et pastorales en 2021. 
L’Action répondra aux besoins alimentaires immédiats des ménages vulnérables pendant les périodes critiques (pré soudure et soudure pastorale et agricole) et soutiendra les principaux moyens d’existence des ménages les plus vulnérables. Elle ciblera les localités agro-pastorales et pastorales des départements de Diffa, Nguigmi, dans la région de Diffa, et le département de Tilia, région de Tahoua, les plus affectées par les crises sécuritaires (nombre de déplacés, taux d’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle) et climatiques (déficit agricoles et pastoraux). Les activités bénéficieront directement à 5 600 ménages (39 200 personnes) déplacés, hôtes, identifiés comme les plus vulnérables selon une approche de ciblage participative (Household Economy Approach) impliquant les communautés, les services techniques, les autorités locales, les partenaires locaux, et les organisations paysannes.

Dans le cadre de cette intervention, le premier axe d'intervention sera la réponse aux besoins urgents de sécurité alimentaire des ménages les plus vulnérables des départements de Diffa, Nguigmi (Diffa) et Tillia (Tahoua) par une assistance alimentaire sous forme de Cash for Work. Les transferts d'argent liquide permettront aux bénéficiaires d'avoir accès à une nourriture de qualité et ainsi de faire face à l'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. En effet, selon tous les acteurs rencontrés (services techniques, autorités locales, partenaires locaux et communautés) lors de l'évaluation interne des interventions FSLH de Diffa réalisée par ACF, le changement le plus significatif apporté par les activités CFW a été l'amélioration de la situation alimentaire des ménages grâce à l'augmentation du nombre de repas (jusqu'à 3 repas par jour), et l'augmentation de la durée des stocks alimentaires des ménages. Au niveau de Tillia, l'évaluation des besoins menée par ACF a montré que le besoin d'assistance alimentaire était l'un des besoins prioritaires cités par les communautés, en particulier parmi les personnes déplacées.
Le deuxième domaine d'intervention consistera à protéger et à renforcer les moyens de subsistance des populations les plus touchées dans les zones ciblées.  Les activités prévues sont basées sur les principaux moyens de subsistance des populations. L'agriculture (32,5% des ménages bénéficiaires), le petit commerce (31,7%) et l'élevage (19,9%) constituent les trois (3) principales activités des bénéficiaires (source : ACF, précédents projets).  Au niveau de Tillia, l'activité principale reste l'élevage et la zone a une vocation pastorale selon la classification du gouvernement du Niger. Ainsi, les activités s'articuleront autour de la restauration et du renforcement du patrimoine pastoral des communautés du département. Afin de renforcer les activités agricoles des bénéficiaires à Diffa, un soutien sera apporté à la culture maraîchère et à l'agriculture pluviale.

project_name: Protection and assistance to Nigerian refugees in the Diffa region  (Situation Lake Chad)
project_objective:
L’intervention en faveur des réfugiés présents à Diffa va se décliner autour de 3 objectifs suivants : 1- Maintenir et renforcer un environnement de protection favorable (protection monitoring et réponse de protection, dont child protection, SGBV, PBS, apatridie, enregistrement/documentation), améliorer les capacités d’intervention des autorités nationales pour délivrer des services de protection conformes aux standards internationaux et maintenir ouvert l’accès au territoire nigérien et aux procédures d’asile.2 – Assurer une assistance d’urgence et une capacité adéquate au niveau du camp de Sayam Forage et améliorer l’accès aux services sociaux de base. 3 - Renforcer la recherche des solutions durables et l’intégration socio-économique des réfugiés installés au Niger notamment via le programme urbanisation et la construction de logements pour les plus vulnérables. .
La stratégie de réponse est conforme avec les orientations du Gouvernement du Niger en termes d’alternatives aux camps et avec le Pacte Mondial pour les Réfugiés. Le nexus humanitaire – développement est au cœur des réflexions qui accompagnent la mise en œuvre de la réponse. Cela suppose le renforcement de la capacité d’absorption des services de base pour alléger les pressions, et l’accompagnement de la coexistence pacifique, en parallèle d’une réponse multisectorielle urgente. Alors qu’une assistance de type communautaire est développée pour l’accès aux services de base tels que l’eau ou la santé, c’est le niveau de vulnérabilité et non le statut qui régit l’assistance individuelle.

project_name: Prevention of and Response to Gender-Based Violence (GBV) for women and adolescent girls in the Rohingya Camps and affected Host Community in Cox Bazar Bangladesh.
project_objective: CARE proposes an integrated approach to gender-based violence and sexual and reproductive health that will reach 52102 women, men, boys and adolescent girls specifically targeting groups with diversity of need including persons with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity, and person with disability living in Camps 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and Palonkhali and Jaliapalong Host Community in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh through 12 WGSS along with PNGO OPCA. The project will provide sexual and reproductive health services and undertake prevention and response to gender-based violence activities include Case Management, Structured Psychosocial support services (PSS), Skill building of the women and girls, capacity strengthening of the community activists and service providers, local partner NGO, local Government (Chairman, Member). Additionally through community mobilization with proven strategies, to address negative social norms that fuel GBV among the population and awareness on COVID-19, DRR, and monsoon. Beneficiary accountability is embedded in all CARE's emergency response and interventions. CARE’s feedback/ complaint mechanism has been developed in line with CARE's quality and accountability framework and operational context. CARE raises awareness and training on PSEA to staff, volunteers, beneficiaries and community people. Internally CARE has a strong PSEA policy as well as reporting and investigation mechanism. Throughout project implementation, CARE will promote/ensure downwards accountability by consulting with communities and local authorities to ensure community voices are heard and tensions mitigated amongst different groups to ensure Do No Harm and conflict sensitive programming. CARE will seek feedback from affected populations and ensure the local voices feed into annual reviews of the project in order to actively shift our program design on the basis of local feedback from our target groups to maintain the AAP. Groups will be engaged in mixed, and age and sex-disaggregated fora and interviews to ensure that all voices are represented, to ensure the social cohesion.

project_name: Life-preserving winterization response to the needs of communities, social institutions and health care facilities in conflict affected areas of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts.
project_objective:
The objective of the proposed project is to address the urgent winterisation needs of vulnerable households and improve service delivery through rehabilitation of social institutions and health care facilities in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts in both government and non-government-controlled areas. 

The project includes both winterisation Non Food Items (NFI) kits and door to door coal distribution to vulnerable families and social institutions with inpatient capacities. Coal continues to be the primary winterisation support requested from the de-facto authorities to humanitarian partners operating in the NGCA. IOM intends to match the amount of support provided to affected communities in winter 2019/2020. 
. The coal to be provided to 12, 000 vulnerable households will amount to 3 tons/household in Donetsk and 2.5 tons/household in Lugansk, in line with the amounts distributed by the respective de facto authorities. The amount of coal  is estimated to support the targeted households through the most severe months of winter to meet their heating needs, though IOM’s post-distribution monitoring reports have revealed across the years that these set amounts might not be sufficient for all vulnerable families. 

Winterisation kits will also supplement the needs of households and in patients at social institutions (to be provided to 3,400 vulnerable households and 95 institutions). Winterisation kits will be comprised of household and personal items that will be determined through needs assessments conducted at the household and institutional level. Post-distribution monitoring reports have highlighted the preference for personal items such as hats, shawls and warm socks as well as other household items including blankets and warm linens.  Additionally, in response to frequently reiterated requests for winterization assistance by communities located along the contact line in the government-controlled side of Donetsk Oblasts IOM will distribute much needed electric heaters to 250 households, which are expected to reduce the household heating expenditure and allow family members to use the savings to address other critical needs (food, medicines, clothing, etc.). The inability of households to manage their winter needs as been consistently highlighted across many of IOM’s project interventions during monitoring visits. 

Finally, IOM will continue with the rehabilitation of 78 social institutions and health care facilities for winterisation purposes, which is an activity that IOM has long standing experience with. Due to lack of funds in regional and de facto administrations, social institutions suffer from lack of maintenance and infrastructural rehabilitation/improvement, which leaves them unfit to meet adequate indoor temperatures to ensure the comfort and health of residents and patients. The envisaged rehabilitation works will focus on  both external structural improvements – such as, amongst the others, roofing,  installation of doors and windows to maintain indoor heat – and internal rehabilitations, which are most likely to include the upgrading of heating systems to ensure both water and indoor climate are sufficient to meet heating needs. 

All proposed activities are in line with cluster priorities for HRP 2021 on winterisation.

project_name: Accès à l’éducation de qualité aux filles et aux garçons IDPs dans un environnement sur et inclusif dans les régions de Tillabéri et  Tahoua (Situation Sahel Central)
project_objective: L’intervention proposée contribuera à mettre en œuvre mobiliser les efforts/ les actions pour maintenir l'accès à des offres éducatives de qualité dans un environnement sûr, inclusif et équitable, au cycle d’enseignement Préscolaire, Primaire et Secondaire aux enfants IDPs.  Les interventions cibleront 15 193 enfants de 4 à 17 ans dont 8 885 filles (58%) et 6 308 garçons y compris 1718 enfants handicapes ( 1106 filles et 612 garçons) au sein des populations déplacées Internes dans  les régions de Tillabéri et Tahoua. Les activités tiendront compte du contexte, de la vulnérabilité et de la demande des populations et seront vers les axes stratégiques identifiées par le Cluster et qui sont en adéquation avec la Stratégie Sahel élaborée par le HCR pour contribuer à la réponse en éducation dans le Sahel. Il s'agit de :  1) Accès équitable et inclusif des enfants affectés au sein des environnements d’apprentissage sûrs et protecteurs, qui contribuent à leur bien-être physique, au développement mental et psychosocial. 2) Améliorer l'accès à des offres éducatives de qualité (enseignement et apprentissage) et à des opportunités de formation professionnelle pour les enfants retournés, déplacés, réfugiés et des communautés d’accueil vulnérables. 3) Renforcer la capacité de résilience des écoles à travers le développement des plans de prévention, de préparation et de réponse aux risques de catastrophes et de conflits armés et 4) Assurer la protection des droits à l'éducation, à la culture de la paix, la cohésion sociale avec focus sur les enfants à besoin spécifique et les abus et violations graves commis contre les enfants.

project_name: Protection and assistance to Nigerian refugees in the Maradi region (Situation north-west Nigeria)
project_objective:
L’intervention se concentre sur 3 composantes. La première vise le renforcement de l’environnement de protection. En vue de prévenir les risques de protection et d’apporter une réponse de qualité, les actions prioritaires visent : l’accès à l’asile ; le maintien du caractère civil de l’asile; la relocalisation des réfugiés; la collecte systématique des informations sur l’environnement sécuritaire, les incidents de protection et les mouvements des populations; la réponse de protection avec une attention particulière sur les volets GBV, Child Protection et PBS, ainsi que la réponse psycho-sociale ; le renforcement de la protection à base communautaire et la coordination des acteurs pour garantir la transversalité de la  protection. Du fait de l’éparpillement des réfugiés, ce dernier axe est fondamental pour le monitoring des incidents de protection, la prévention et la réponse. Les sensibilisations et le renforcement des capacités des autorités (administratives, civiles, judiciaires), des forces de défense et de sécurité, des acteurs humanitaires et des communautés sur les thématiques autour la protection internationale permettront d’assurer une compréhension commune du contexte et de faciliter la collaboration. 
La seconde composante vise à assurer une réponse d’urgence au niveau des villages d’accueil. La réponse multisectorielle d’urgence continuera de se réaliser en complémentarité avec les autres acteurs. Le focus du HCR se fera sur les volets abris d’urgence et biens non alimentaires ainsi que sur la réponse en santé au niveau des villages d’accueil (stock de médicaments, appui en ressources humaine). 
La troisième composante concerne le processus de relocalisation et les villages d’opportunités. L’objectif ici est d’une part de consolider les villages d’opportunités existants (Chadakori, Dan Dadji Makaw et Garin Kaka) notamment en termes de renforcement des services et infrastructures de base (EHA, éducation, santé) répondant aux normes nationales, d’accès aux opportunités économiques et a l’énergie domestique, ainsi que l’appui en abris durables. Des villages d’opportunités additionnels seront également aménagés pour accompagner le processus de relocalisation. Une réponse d’urgence sera fournie à chaque ménage relocalisé et aux ménages les plus vulnérables déjà relocalisés. La stratégie de réponse est conforme avec les orientations du Gouvernement du Niger en termes d’alternatives aux camps et avec le Pacte Mondial pour les Réfugiés. Le nexus humanitaire – développement est au cœur des réflexions qui accompagnent la mise en œuvre de la réponse.

project_name: Assistance en santé au profit des personnes déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes affectées dans les régions du Centre Nord, du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Est et de l’Est, couplée avec une assistance en soutien psychosocial, sous le cluster protection
project_objective:
Le présent projet s’inscrit dans le cadre de la réponse humanitaire d’urgence conduite au Burkina Faso avec pour objectif général de fournir un accès aux services de santé primaire ; notamment dans les domaines de la prévention à la COVID et en santé mentale, aux points d’entrée du pays et dans les régions du Centre-Nord, du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Est et de l’Est. 

Le premier axe du projet relatif aux activités en santé mentale s’articulera avec l‘intervention de l’OIM en assistance psychosociale sous le Cluster Protection et répondra au besoin avéré de prise en charge clinique des personnes présentant des troubles mentaux. La stratégie de ce projet sera basée sur des interventions de niveau 2 ; 3 et 4 de la pyramide des interventions pour la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial dans les situations d’urgence issues des directives du comité permanent inter organisations concernant la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial dans les situations d’urgences.  Le projet a pour objectif de renforcer et augmenter l’accès à des services de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial aux personnes déplacées internes et communautés dans les régions humanitaires et se décline en trois activités principales :
 i. Renforcement de la capacité des formations sanitaires en termes de services de santé mentale. 
ii. Prise en charge des cas de santé mentale ; 
iii. Promotion de la santé mentale au sein des populations déplacées et affectées par la crise humanitaire.

Le second axe proposé permettra à l’OIM de participer à l’endiguement de la transmission de la COVID-19 et à atténuer l'impact de l'épidémie sur le pays et sa population notamment pour en minimiser l'impact social.

project_name: Assurer les services de prévention et de réponse aux enfants filles et garçons les plus vulnérables, en particulier ceux à risque ou affectés par la violence, l’exploitation et les abus.
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire au Burkina Faso se détériore rapidement notamment avec une hausse régulière des attaques engendrant des déplacements massifs de population. Les menaces croissantes de groupes extrémistes et une série de manifestations sociales ont gravement affecté la réalisation des droits des enfants et les exposent à de nouveaux risques de protections tels que la séparation familiale, la détresse psychosociale, les abus, d’exploitation et la violence, y compris le recrutement par les groupes armés et les violences sexuelles. La situation est d’autant plus inquiétante que les déplacements de population ont délité les mécanismes communautaires habituels      de protection de l’enfant.  Au 10 Novembre 2020, 1, 049,767 personnes (60.8% sont des enfants) sont déplacées internes.     . Les enfants séparés de leurs parents et des autres membres de leur famille comptent parmi les plus vulnérables.

Par ailleurs,      les déplacements massifs des populations ont un impact sur l’accès des enfants aux principaux services de protection, notamment les services sociaux, d’éducation de santé et autres, et les rendent vulnérables aux abus et à l’exploitation, notamment le recrutement par des groupes armés et l’exploitation dans les pires formes de travail. Les filles sont particulièrement exposées aux violences sexuelles, aux mutilations génitales féminines et aux mariages précoces. 

Pour répondre aux besoins urgents des enfants, l’UNICEF, à travers ses partenaires de mise en œuvre offrira des services de préventions et de réponse aux besoins des enfants dans les régions du Sahel, Boucle du Mouhoun, Nord, Est, Centre Nord et Centre Est. Un certain nombre d’activités de prévention et de réponses seront mises en œuvre en lien avec les objectifs sectoriels de l’action qui sont (i) la protection des enfants affectés par la crise humanitaire et l’assurance du respect de leurs droits humains (prévention), et (ii) l’amélioration immédiate des conditions de vie des enfants affectées par la crise et en priorité les plus vulnérables (réponse).

project_name: Provision of emergency lifesaving and nutrition services to improve and prevent the deterioration of the nutrition status of nutritionally vulnerable Syrian women, girls and boys
project_objective:
The Nutrition preventative programme aims to address urgent and life-saving nutrition needs of mothers and children in Syria, located in high severity areas across the entire country. The programme targets all affected populations, including IDPs, host communities and returnees with high severity food insecurity and nutrition indicators. 

The Nutrition preventative activities aim to: 
- Support improved and equitable access to life saving nutritional services for food insecure and vulnerable children (boys and girls) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) at community and facilities level to stabilize and/or reduce malnutrition (acute, chronic and micronutrient deficiencies) in the target population.
− To prevent acute, chronic malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in children 6-23 months
− Improve diet diversity amongst pregnant and lactating women within food insecure and vulnerable families.

WFP aims to target boys and girls aged 6- 23months and PLWs, including those with disability, through its preventive programme.  The Programme is implemented in coordination with the Ministry of Health and other partners of the nutrition sector in Syria including UN agencies, National and  International NGOs. Considering the high needs and limited resources, the project will adopt a context and severity-based approach to prioritize sub-districts identified with high nutritional and food insecurity severity, mainly those with severity level 3,4 &5.  In case of lower funding, priority will be given to locations where severity of food  security and nutrition of is more than 4 and to newly accessible areas.

project_name: Access to quality treatment for children suffering from severe acute malnutrition among population affected by Nigerian crisis in The Lake province, Chad
project_objective: This project aims to reduce the mortality and the morbidity due to malnutrition by offering adequate treatment for 15,111 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition among displacements people in The Lake province due to attacks by non-state armed groups and military operations in borders with Nigeria and Niger.

project_name: Sustain the WASH Cluster's capacity to enhance access to safe and appropriate WASH solutions for vulnerable populations in South Sudan through the management of the WASH core pipeline program.
