project_objective: Under the Humanitarian Response Plan 2021, IOM will sustain its strong support to the WASH Cluster's capacity to respond to South Sudan's humanitarian needs by managing a portion of the WASH core pipeline. To provide life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable people affected by multiple humanitarian crises, IOM will continue its effective WASH Core Pipeline management by providing emergency supplies that will improve access to clean water and adequate sanitation and hygiene materials, targeting 1,215,000 people in need. The project activities are in line with the WASH Cluster objectives and will serve to support timely, safe, dignified, and equitable access to WASH services to contribute to the prevention of famine, malnutrition, and disease outbreak, such as COVID-19, cholera, and dysentery, and will prioritize the most vulnerable population affected and/or displaced by conflict; recurrent sub-national violence; heavy season rains and massive flooding, food insecurity and malnutrition prevalence related and GBV risks

project_name: Provision of safe, equitable, and dignified WASH services for communities living in Protection of Civilian/Internal Displacement Camps and affected by acute emergencies
project_objective: The project aims to provide integrated, safe, equitable, and dignified access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services to IDPs, host communities, and returnees in the most affected areas of South Sudan. It builds on IOM's existing WASH service provision systems in camp settings while capitalizing on IOM's well-established emergency and preparedness response mechanism. Where possible, IOM will seek to complement humanitarian activities with transition and recovery elements to assist the establishment of sustainable solutions. Activities will be complemented with GBV risk mitigation and accessibility inclusion, designed in a conflict-sensitive manner and with protection considerations in mind. As the largest direct WASH service provider in camp settings, IOM will continue servicing conflict-affected populations in the Bentiu and Malakal Protection of Civilians (PoCs) sites and Wau's Naivasha Internal Displacement Camp (IDP), benefitting a total of 137,579 people. IOM will ensure the provision of WASH services through the operation and maintenance (O&M) of safe and accessible water supply systems, care and maintenance of accessible and secure sanitation and handwashing facilities, and management of solid and liquid waste. IOM will also continue investing in cost-effective and climate-resilient means of ensuring adequate service provision within these settings by setting up, maintaining, and scaling up water supply solar systems and biogas schemes. To account for the ongoing PoC re-designation and transition process, IOM will focus on transitioning from WASH service provision based on humanitarian assistance towards community-based ownership, through a participatory approach, with a focus on women’s empowerment and on the strategic needs of the most vulnerable. This will be done by:  professionalizing the existing cadre of WASH volunteers’ and setting up new and/or build on existing community-based WASH groups; training and providing institutional support to local pump mechanics and representatives of local authorities to gradually transfer O&M responsibilities to the mandated authorities; and. exploring and designing durable solutions based on pro-poor cost recovery principles and market-based programming elements, where possible. As an extension of service provision to urban centers within the vicinity of PoCs and IDP camps, IOM will target 268,486 people. In tandem, IOM will also continue operating its Emergency, Preparedness and Response (EP&R) program, expanding access to WASH services to underserved and vulnerable populations in remote and hard-to-reach locations with high morbidity/mortality related to nutrition and health, and/or where WASH is the main stand-alone driver of the crises, and/or where the population has been affected by a sudden- or rapid-onset disaster (flooding, high food insecurity). Temporary and semi-permanent WASH solutions will be prioritized, and where identified, they will be designed in a climate-resilient way while focusing on instilling community ownership for operation and maintenance. This potentially includes borehole rehabilitation and/or drilling of boreholes, and/or rehabilitation of surface water treatment systems, hygiene promotion, and WASH Non-Food Items (NFIs) distribution, including training and distribution of menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits to women and girls of menstrual age. IOM will also ensure the sustainability of water supply through the formation and training of water management committees. Geographical targeting will be done through WASH Cluster updates and/or using various assessment findings (IRNAs, NAWG recommendations, WASH Vulnerability maps, etc.). IOM estimates reaching 75,000 people. IOM will ensure that prevention and mitigation of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and COVID-19 prevention measures are mainstreamed across the project cycle.

project_name: Assistance en abris et articles ménagers essentiels des ménages affectés, déplacés et hôtes dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre-Nord, Nord, Centre-Est et Est
project_objective:
L’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en abris, articles ménagers essentiels et activités d’amélioration des conditions de vie physiques des ménages affectés, déplacés et hôtes à travers la distribution de 7,500  kits d’Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME) complets et standards, la distribution et la construction de 5,500 abris d’urgence ossature en bois à pignons , à travers une approche communautaire. Enfin l’OIM prévoit de soutenir l’amélioration et réhabilitation des conditions d’abri à travers la distribution de 3,000 kits de réhabilitation en nature ou en cash. A travers toutes les activités mises en œuvre l’OIM tiendra compte de la prévention de la COVID-19 en assurant la disponiblité de 1,000 dispositifs de lave main et de savons sur les sites aménagés et non aménagés .
Toutes ces activités seront menées en étroite collaboration avec le Conseil National de Secours d'Urgence et de Réhabilitation (CONASUR) et en incluant les communautés dans un souci de renforcer la redevabilité vis-à-vis des populations affectées et pour favoriser l’inclusion des plus vulnérables. 

Forte de sa présence de longue date au Burkina Faso avec plus de 80 staff, un bureau principal à Ouagadougou et cinq sous-bureaux répartis dans les régions, notamment à Kaya (Centre-Nord), Dori (Sahel), Ouahigouya (Nord), Fada (Est) et Tenkodogo (Centre-Est), l’OIM est engagée dans la réponse collective afin d’aider le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso à faire face aux besoins multisectoriels générés par la situation humanitaire. Pouvant compter sur son expertise globale, le support de son siège et de son bureau régional et son rôle au sein du Cluster Abri Global y compris en qualité d’agence lead des Groupes de travail Projets Abris et Diaspora et d’agence co-lead du Groupe de travail  sur l’Inclusion des personnes handicapées dans les programmes abris, l’OIM a une équipe d’urgence en place depuis 2019, qui comprend notamment deux chargées des projets d’urgence, dont une formatrice de Coordination et de Gestion de Camp (Camp Coordination and Camp Management-CCCM), et un assistant abris basé à Kaya. 

L’OIM est un membre actif du Cluster abris et AME depuis ses débuts et est engagée dans toutes les discussions stratégiques récentes.

En 2019 et 2020, l’OIM a reçu des financements pour construire plus de 1,500 abris d’urgence dont la construction est achevée ou en cours dans les régions du Sahel, Nord et Centre-Nord.

project_name: Protection des ménages affectés - déplacés et hôtes - dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, de l’Est et du Centre-Est au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
L’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en protection pour les ménages affectés, déplacés et hôtes, les réfugiés, et autres personnes affectées à travers différentes activités de protection ciblées et transversales. 

Forte de sa présence de longue date au Burkina Faso avec plus de 80 staffs, un bureau principal à Ouagadougou et cinq sous-bureaux répartis dans les régions, notamment à Kaya (Centre-Nord), Dori (Sahel), Ouahigouya (Nord), Fada (Est) et Tenkodogo (Centre-Est), l’OIM est engagée dans la réponse collective afin d’aider le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso à faire face aux besoins multisectoriels générés par la crise. L’OIM a une équipe de protection en place depuis plusieurs années, qui travaille notamment à l’assistance aux migrants et depuis la détérioration de la situation au Burkina travaille à assister toutes les populations affectées, déplacées et hôtes, les réfugiés, et autres personnes affectées par la crise en cours.

En complément des programmes d’urgence de l’OIM déjà existants principalement centrée sur la distribution de kits d’abris et d’articles ménagers essentiels (AME), la protection et l’accès aux moyens d’existence, la réponse de l'OIM dans le secteur de la protection en 2021 sera axée sur les services et activités de soutien psychosocial (SPS), la lutte contre la traite d’êtres humains en situation de crise, le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et du soutien ciblé aux femmes et aux filles, y compris l’atténuation des risques, la réponse et la prévention des violences basées sur le genre (VBG). En outre, vu l’augmentation constante du nombre de personnes déplacées internes (PDI), l'OIM mettra en œuvre la matrice de suivi des déplacements (DTM) afin d'aider le gouvernement burkinabé et les partenaires humanitaires à collecter des données précises et documentées, régulièrement actualisées et exploitables dans un contexte de déplacements évolutif et en évaluant les tendances, en complément d’un côté de l’enregistrement conduit et géré par le Conseil National de Secours d’Urgence et de Réhabilitation (CONASUR) avec le soutien du Haut-Commissariat aux Réfugiés (HCR) et de l’autre côté des activités d’évaluation et de la gestion de l’information menées par d’autres acteurs sur le terrain.

Toutes les activités proposées par l’OIM sont alignées sur l’objectif sectoriel du Cluster Protection de « Coordonner et renforcer le mécanisme de collecte et de partage des données, d’analyse des incidents de protection, d'orientation, de référencement et contre référencement pour la prise en charge des personnes affectées pour un suivi efficace des cas individuels de protection y compris l’accès à la justice » pour l’année 2021.
L’approche de l’OIM pour la mise en œuvre de ce projet est fondée sur les besoins démontrés et tenant compte de la situation de conflit: elle prend en compte le contexte local. En utilisant l'approche « Ne pas nuire », l'OIM veillera à ce que l'assistance qu'elle fournit cible tous les groupes ethniques de la communauté, soit sensible à l'âge, au sexe, au genre, et aux capacités et à la culture. L’OIM veillera tout au long de la mise en œuvre des activités à engager les communautés locales et promouvoir la gouvernance locale. Les équipes de projet sur le terrain et au contact des bénéficiaires seront formées pour pouvoir répondre d’une manière éthique et sûre à des différents incidents de protection, notamment dans des cas de VBG et elles seront composées de personnel féminin et masculin

project_name: CCCM Assistance to Displaced Persons in South Sudan
project_objective:
The displacement context in South Sudan remains fluid. The country continues to
experience conflict and natural disaster-driven displacements in communities in both
urban and hard-to-reach areas. Former PoCs, including those which have been re-designated
as IDP sites, and collective sites continue to host IDPs in a protracted
displacement situation across the country. Concurrent with this are spontaneous returns
and relocations of IDPs and refugees, the latter of which can end up finding themselves in
a new displacement situation once back in South Sudan.

Of the 1.2 million persons in need in 2021 IOM CCCM will target 435,000 of the 900,000 to be targeted by the CCCM Cluster. IOM will focus on providing camp coordination and camp management under the following areas:

I. Static Operations in former PoCs (Including re-designated IDP sites) and Collective
Centers: As CM agency in Bentiu and Wau, and care and maintenance focal point in
Malakal, IOM will continue to improve the living conditions and meet the basic needs of
affected populations in these sites.

Output 1: IDPs living in former PoCs, IDP camps and CCs have improved and dignified
living conditions in support of a conducive environment for durable solutions and with
meaningful community engagement.

II. Deploy mobile teams to new and unreached displacement sites as prioritized by the
Cluster.

Output 2: Deployment of sustainable mobile responses to unmanaged sites to ensure
coordination and community ownership in camp-like settings or spontaneous settlements.

III. Co-Lead the Camp Coordination and Camp Management Cluster
Output 3: Fully functional, staffed, and well-managed CCCM Cluster supports partner
agencies in accountable CCCM responses and systems.

project_name: Food security and livelihoods support to host and IDPs populations affected by recurrent shocks in Somalia
project_objective: Action Against Hunger provide Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) support to pastoralist, agro-pastoralist, peri-urban/urban and internally displaced (IDP) populations affected by persistent periods of armed conflict, political instability as well as environmental and economic shocks in Somalia. The 2021 FSL project target 81,873 individuals (21,615 male, 32,729 female, 16,047 boys and 16,702 girls) living in Bakool (Xudur, Elbarde, Wajid, Rabdhure), Sool (Xudun), Lower Shebelle ( Afgooye), Banadir (Khada), Hiraan (Beletweyne) and Nugaal (Eyl, Garowe) regions. The project plan to reach 65,304 individuals (displaced and non-displaced)  in integrated phase classification (IPC) 3, 4 and beyond with immediate lifesaving interventions including unconditional, conditional cash assistance and fresh food voucher to meet their immediate acute food needs to mitigate shocks/stress. Further 16,570 individuals’ (IPC 2) will be supported with seasonal livelihood inputs support for agriculture and livestock activities to build and strengthen their resilience capacities  to meet their immediate recovery needs, leverage on existing assets to withstand the effects of a shock and lay the foundation for future economic growth activities. In order to foster more sustainable stress mitigation mechanisms, ACF activities will focus on creating greater resilience for the beneficiary population by promoting economic growth activities. These activities capitalize on the foundation laid under strategies designed to enhance absorptive and adaptive capacity and promote a pathway to income generating opportunities while ensuring that the systems that support economic growth are appropriately developed and protected for future sustainability.

project_name: Disease Prevention Program for Conflict and Disaster Affected Communities of Cabo Delgado, Mozambique
project_objective: Communities most impacted by escalating conflict, displacement and disrupted health service access are at significant risk to life threatening diseases. Based on thorough coordination with NMCP/MISAU/Clusters/partners, MENTOR propose to conduct indoor residual spraying to protect 500,000 people and technical training for 230 APEs.

project_name: Enhancing Humanitarian Information Management by providing Information on Migration and Displacement in Libya and Capacity Building of National Counterparts
project_objective: The project aims to support humanitarian information management in Libya via sustained implementation of IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) system and via capacity building of local and national Libyan counterparts. DTM supports the humanitarian community in Libya by provision of data, information and analysis on the population mobility and its impact on the affected populations; DTM Libya also co-chairs the Assessment Working Group (AWG). The information and analysis provided by DTM in Libya covers internal displacement as well as international migration. Under this project DTM will continue to monitor internal displacement via emergency tracking, assess the priority needs of the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) via rapid assessments, supporting multi-sectoral assessments coordinated by the AWG and by continued implementation of Mobility Tracking publish bimonthly information packages on IDPs and returnees in Libya. Similarly, DTM will continue to monitor migration trends and dynamics, and conduct assessments of migrant vulnerability and humanitarian needs in Libya. Information products such as flash updates, detailed analytical reports and public datasets in addition to bilateral sharing of operational information with OCHA and partners of Rapid Response Mechanism (IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF, and WFP) will facilitate enhanced humanitarian information management. Furthermore, DTM will undertake capacity building activities aimed towards supporting local and national Libyan counterparts in the implementation of improved humanitarian information management.

project_name: Improving the early recovery capacities and livelihoods protection of vulnerable  communities and IDPs in Gao and Segou
project_objective:
In a context of climate change, security degradation and economic and health crisis (particularly related to Covid-19), the food and nutrition situation in the circles of Niono (Ségou), Ansongo and Bourem (Gao) is characterized by great insecurity and major population displacements are expected.
The project will contribute to maintaining a social protection floor linked to the seasonality of vulnerability via electronic MT (R1). The action will also provide emergency assistance to IDPs (R2), a complete package in NFI, food and WASH will be provided to IDPs and other people in Ansongo, Bourem (Gao) and Niono (Ségou) and (R3) relates to nutrition.

project_name: Provision of emergency food to vulnerable migrants at disembarkation points and emergency meals and nutritious packages to vulnerable migrants and refugees in detention centres.
project_objective:
Evidence suggests that the likely prolonged restrictions implemented by the Libyan authorities to control the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic across the country will continue to have an impact on international and domestic food supply chains. Mobility and supply chain limitations, combined with the general economic impacts of COVID-19 have resulted in higher prices, as well as loss of income due to increasing unemployment and prolonged disruptions to businesses and people’s livelihoods.

Migrants and refugees are particularly vulnerable to these risks, as they often rely on daily labour. According to DTM’s Migrant Emergency Food Security Report, released in May 2020, 72% of migrants relying on daily casual labour stated that it had been difficult to find work due to movement limitations linked to COVID-19. According to the same report, 56% of all migrants in Libya had to compromise their food intake during the difficult months of the pandemic.

The situation is even more complicated and unpredictable for those in detention centers, where the nutrition needs of the vulnerable continue to grow. In 2020, on average 3,000 migrants and refugees were detained in government-held detention centers in Libya at any given time. 

The aim of the project is to provide emergency meals and nutritious packages to vulnerable migrants and refugees upon disembarkation at DPs and in DCs, including pregnant and lactating women, children, elderly and people with medical needs.

project_name: Closing Gaps in Essential Health Services for the Most Vulnerable Migrants, IDPs, and Host Communities in Libya
project_objective: 2.	Libya continues to be a complex crisis. It continues to be one of the most fragile and conflict-affected countries in the region due to the ever-present threat of large-scale hostilities, the presence of foreign armed groups, the trafficking of drugs and migrants, uncontrolled borders, organized crime and corruption. The dire humanitarian situation has been exacerbated by the continuing spread of COVID-19 in Libya and the efforts to reduce transmission is hampered by the weak health system and by the difficulty to ensure prevention measures such as social distancing and proper sanitization amongst the 392,241 internally displaced people (IDPs) recorded by DTM, and the 584,509 migrants and refugees. Many migrants, displaced populations and refugees live in cramped locations with poor sanitation and hygiene. This is only likely to increase as the socio-economic impact of COVID-19 unfolds. Many also suffer significant barriers when trying to access public or private healthcare, including, but not limited to, stigmatization and discrimination.

project_name: Provision of specialized protection services, including mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and community-based assistance to vulnerable migrants in Libya
project_objective: Migrants living in Libya face significant protection risks for a wide range of reasons, including violence, exploitation, hazardous living conditions, and abuse at the hands of smugglers and traffickers. IOM will work to ensure that migrants requiring specialized assistance as well as mental health and psychosocial support are appropriately supported while alleviating suffering and maintaining human dignity. The project’s main line of work is related to service provision to vulnerable individuals on the one hand, and capacity building of duty bearers and contributing to an enabling environment for migrants on the other hand. In addition, in depth analysis underpinned by accurate data is crucial and IOM will produce evidence base that can serve to inform programming and advocacy purposes as well.

project_name: Provision of emergency core and essential non-food items and shelter support to migrants, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and returnees
project_objective: The project aims to provide emergency life-saving assistance to detained or stranded migrants as well as the most vulnerable Libyan IDPs, returnees and host communities through provision of essential non-food items (NFIs) and rehabilitation of damaged houses. The total requested amount of USD 4,700,000 split between the two above-mentioned activities will cover the needs of a total of 70,637 beneficiaries including 19,443 migrants, 15,304 IDPs, 27,411 returnees and 8,479 non-displaced population in the East, West and South of Libya.

project_name: Integrated life-saving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and COVID-19 response to strengthen the resilience of most vulnerable migrants, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and hosting communities in Libya.
project_objective:
This project addresses the urgent life-saving water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs of the most vulnerable peoples in Libya during the COVID-19 pandemic. The project targets detained or stranded migrants in detention centers (DCs), migrants in transit centers (TCs) and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) that have integrated into urban areas including, but not limited to, Tripoli, Misrata, Zuwara, Alazzawaya, Sebha and Benghazi. Gender and protection will be mainstreamed throughout the project, besides that GBV risks will be mitigated  through enhancement of participation of women and girls by for instance site selection, determining suitable protective location and design for latrines within DCs and TCs, being recipients and providing feedback on the content of the of hygiene -and dignity kits. IOM in doing so adheres to the do no harm principle. The objective and targeting approach are coherent with the Humanitarian Response Plan’s (HRP) strategic objectives of the WASH Sector for 2021. 

In addition, this project will enhance the capacity of the local/national government partners and international/national non-government organizations (I/NGOs) with training sessions on emergency planning preparedness, WASH in emergency settings and infection prevention and control (IPC). IOM will adopt an integrated WASH approach connecting access to water, sanitation aspects more clearly with hygiene promotion and awareness sessions. Furthermore, awareness raising on hygiene promotion, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) on COVID-19 preparedness and mitigation will be a key part of the project approach, to reduce health hazards such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Thereto, all distribution and training activities will follow national and international guidelines on COVID-19 prevention measures, such as the observation of physical distancing measures.

project_name: PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF MALNUTRITION
project_objective: The project will provide basic nutrition services to children under five and pregnant and lactating women. The project aims to contribute to the reduction of acute malnutrition (severe and moderate) rates and underweight prevalence among children under 5 years while improving the nutritional status in pregnant and lactating women and increasing beneficiary households’ knowledge on health and nutrition.  The project will ensure services to all eligible beneficiaries disaggregating beneficiaries by gender and age taking into account special needs such as disability and  other vulnerability. Complaints and feedback mechanisms will be in place to ensure accountability to affected populations including help desks, hotlines, post and process monitoring

project_name: Assistance abris d’urgence, abris semi-durable et articles ménagers essentiels aux personnes déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes des régions du Sahel, du Centre-Nord, du Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Centre Est, et de l’Est du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Au 10 novembre 2020, le nombre de personnes déplacées internes (PDI) s’élève a 1,049,767 personnes qui ont été enregistrées individuellement par le Conseil national des secours d'urgence et de la réhabilitation (CONASUR). Face à cette situation, le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso et les acteurs humanitaires se sont immédiatement mobilisés pour apporter une réponse humanitaire coordonnée. L'un des aspects essentiels de cette réponse concerne les conditions d'hébergement des personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays. En effet, l'impact négatif de la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire sur les conditions de logement des familles déplacées ayant des besoins aigus persiste. Selon le CONASUR, 95 064 ménages ont vu leur abris endommagés et/ou détruits et leurs articles ménagers essentiels (AME) abimés en 2020. Ainsi, les acteurs humanitaires sont intervenus pour obstruer et augmenter la capacité d'accueil des ménages de PDI vivant dans des familles d'accueil. Pourtant, jusqu'à ce jour la situation persiste et le nombre de déplacés internes continue d’augmenter. Le HCR, avec ses partenaires, a pu assister au cours de l'année 2020 plus de 20 000 ménages avec différents types d'abris et la provision d’AME dans des zones où les capacités d'hébergement sont saturées.  Le pourcentage de contribution du HCR est très considérable par rapport aux réalisations due clusters abris et AME. Le HCR fait les mêmes projections dans le Plan de Réponse Humanitaire (PRH) 2021 pour les abris et les AME. Par conséquent, les personnes qui ont fui et sont définitivement privées de leurs moyens d'hébergement précédents manquent d'intimité et sont exposées à des risques pour la santé, la violence basée sur le genre (VBG), entre autres, et ne recourent pas à des stratégies de survie extrêmes dans des environnements de déplacement. En interne, en particulier les femmes et les filles, qui ont du mal à faire face à la promiscuité chez elles.

Le projet vise à fournir une aide d'urgence immédiate avec des abris adéquats et des AME à 147,000 personnes, soit 21 000 ménages touchés par les déplacements internes dans 15 communes des six régions (Sahel, Centre-Nord, Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun, Centre-Est et Est) en proie à la crise humanitaire. À moyen et long terme, la réponse d'urgence facilitera l'accès à des conditions de vie décente et contribuera à la diminution de certains risques de protection pour les populations affectées (personnes déplacées internes, familles d’accueil et le cas échéant retournés) dans le secteur Abris-AME. La résilience face aux conditions météorologiques difficiles de certains autres types d'abris utilisés jusqu'à présent (abris d'urgence, logements pour réfugiés, etc.) a été un défi de taille.

De manière spécifique, il s’agit de renforcer la résilience des populations affectées à travers la fourniture d’abris (construction d'abris d'urgence abris d’urgence type UNHCR et d’abris semi-durable à travers l’approche CBI) ou à travers d’autres modalités, qui répondent aux recommandations du Comité Technique Abris et la fourniture de kits standards d’AME ou l’équivalent monétaire.

En  coordination avec le CONASUR  et à travers une approche complémentaire avec les partenaires opérationnels en ligne avec la stratégie du groupe sectoriel Abris/AME du Burkina Faso, le HCR fournira son appui aux autorités burkinabés et aux acteurs humanitaire dans la recherche et la mise en œuvre de solutions d‘urgence et durables à travers la collecte, l’analyse et le partage des données afin de faciliter l’orientation des interventions de logements adéquats et d’AME dans les zones affectées par la crise.

project_name: Supporting Survivors and Addressing Risks and Root Causes of GBV in Conflict-Affected Areas of South Sudan
project_objective:
The impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly the increased economic instability and school closures, along with expected high levels of food insecurity in 2021, flooding, and conflict-related displacements, continue to exacerbate the already existing high levels of gender-based violence (GBV). IOM's programmatic assessments  indicate that the COVID-19 prevention measures and economic contraction have had a significant impact, particularly on adolescent girls and young women, especially related to increased use of harmful coping mechanisms, such as sexual exploitation and forced marriage, resulting in increased adolescent pregnancies. 

The current humanitarian context is exacerbated by a high prevalence of violence against women and girls, particularly conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), intimate partner violence (IPV), and forced marriage, including child marriage. This violence is structurally underpinned by a patriarchal social system, connected to the political economy of bridewealth (Luedke, 2019), with harmful gender norms underpinning cycles of violence within and between communities, particularly affecting the rights of women and girls. 

Furthermore, the needs for GBV services are high, yet the availability of multi-sectoral GBV services across the country is low, and access remains a challenge for women, especially in rural communities. Key barriers for survivors include distance to services, availability of qualified service providers, social restrictions over the women and girls movement, and high levels of social stigma and possible harmful repercussions for disclosure (including the threat of divorce and marriage to perpetrators). 

IOM aims to contribute to strengthening the humanitarian response to GBV contributing to HRP objective 2.4. IOM’s approach is to work closely to build national capacities to implement GBV prevention and response programming based on the Interagency GBV minimum standards. This includes strengthening community-based referral mechanisms to improve access for GBV survivors, establishing women and girl friendly spaces with tailored and age-appropriate activities for awareness, skills-building and psychosocial support, provision of GBV case management, psychosocial and legal counselling. For outreach and GBV prevention, IOM utilizes messaging developed with communities based on key issues identified and primary prevention approaches including Engaging Men through Accountable Practices and with school-age children, with significant capacity building and supervision requirement to ensure real behaviour change is created on these issues. Finally, IOM builds capacity among IOM outreach teams and partners on PSEA, community-based complaints and feedback mechanisms as well as working with organisations of persons with disabilities and elderly persons to improve inclusivity of GBV programming.

project_name: Provision of life-saving primary health care, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and outbreak response services for vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and conflict-affected host communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
Since the beginning of the conflict in December 2013, IOM has been providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach locations across South Sudan. In 2021 IOM will continue to provide integrated emergency life-saving primary health care, routine immunization, and surveillance and response to disease outbreaks to underserved and conflict-affected IDPs, returnees, migrants/travelers, and host communities through six static clinics, 15 mobile clinics, eight rapid response team (RRT) deployments and one PoE screening site. The static and mobile clinics are located in Wau (Western Bahr el Ghazal State), Malakal (Upper Nile State), and Bentiu (Unity State) protection of civilians (PoC) site, as well as outside of PoC locations. The health RRT will be deployed to any area across South Sudan that faces acute man-made or natural disasters with unmet health needs. IOM will use the DTM intention to return survey results to quickly deploy the health rapid response team to areas of highest return so that acute returnees get the appropriate basic health care that supports them to settle in the area of return. IOM integrates comprehensive HIV/AIDS/TB prevention, care, and treatment, systematic nutrition screening, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), clinical management of rape services (CMR), and COVID-19 screening, prevention, and mitigation activities in any of its health interventions. MHPSS services are provided in 13 recreational and counselling centres in Wau Naivasha IDP site, Bentiu PoC, Malakal PoC, and in respective host communities in the greater Wau area. Recently, IOM has started MHPSS programming in the Abyei Administrative Area (AAA) as well.


In addition to the direct service delivery mentioned above, IOM plans to strengthen the Ministry of Health (MoH) capacity through a diaspora health project whereby South Sudanese diaspora communities will be engaged in the provision of direct health services and on-the-job training of MoH staff on selected priority medical intervention, including an emergency maternal, child and neonatal care. IOM will also work closely with the MoH Directorate of the International Coordination Office to strengthen port health and conduct a survey to understand the perceptions of the border communities and institutions on COVID-19 preparedness and response. The outcome of this survey will inform MoH and humanitarian actors on the strength and gaps observed in the current response.

project_name: Build resilience through improved housing solutions, NFIs and flood mitigations support to affected population of South Sudan
project_objective:
In 2021, IOM South Sudan's Shelter and Non-Food Items Unit (SNFI) seeks to fill immediate and long-term housing and household needs across the country. IOM plans to respond to the multi-faceted needs of displaced, returnee and host populations through the provision of life saving and life-sustaining SNFIs, as well as community support services such as capacity building disaster preparedness, dispute resolution and referral services. Support will be provided through numerous modalities, such as in-kind distributions and cash- and voucher-based interventions, while ensuring vulnerable populations are prioritized and reached in every response activity. IOM's responses align with cluster priorities and objectives and are targeted to geographic areas experiencing the most significant shelter and NFI needs. IOM plans to target 154,592individuals with the provision of shelter and NFI support and flood mitigation programming. IOM continues to support communities that include new and protracted IDPs, returnees, host communities, and people affected by floods. As site focal point for IDP Naivasha camp and collective Centers in WBeG, IOM will provide SNFI assistance, shelter upgrade to new and protracted IDPs.  IOM plans to expand its cash-based interventions in areas with functional markets.  In 2021, IOM aims to assist 28 per cent of its target beneficiaries through cash-based modalities in Wau, Bor and other areas. Being Cluster lead, IOM as last resort will deploy teams to any location in the country, if no partner is available.

Using the Linking Relief with Recovery and Development (LRRD) framework, IOM undertakes long-term settlement programming alongside its emergency interventions. Since 2019, IOM has facilitated the formation of seven village development committees and constructed more than 500 permanent, low-cost shelters for returnees and host community members. IOM plans to expand and strengthen its settlement programming through enhanced coordination with other units and humanitarian partners, linking essential services such as WASH infrastructure, livelihood resources, mental and physical health services. Focusing on areas of return and locations with relative stability and security, this settlement planning model allows communities to build their resilience and access a network of services, creating enhanced stability peace and prosperity.
Communities in the Nile basin experienced extensive property losses, livelihoods and life due to the second year of intense seasonal flooding. In anticipation of future flooding events, IOM will strengthen and expand community-based preparedness and planning mechanisms while linking community members to early warning systems and data-based predictive modelling. IOM plans to construct flood mitigation infrastructure in Bor and other flood-affected areas that will benefit 80,000 individuals. IOM will establish and strengthen DMCs at the Boma level and, form new committees at the county and state levels. Parallel to IOM's work undertaken at the community level, the SNFI team also works with national policymakers and national political leadership structures to advance progressive and meaningful South Sudan legislation. IOM has been deeply engaged in the process of developing and finalizing a National Land Policy. IOM has also aided in the review and finalization of a National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy. IOM is dedicated to continuing in its commitment to support national and sub-national governmental authorities working in matters of land, housing, shelter, displacement, and disaster.
Lastly, IOM continues to lead the Shelter and NFI Cluster, a role it has held since 2011. IOM also hosts and co-leads the National Cash Working Group and the Housing, Land and Property Technical Working Group. IOM mainstreams HLP, AAP, CfM, GBV and numerous other programming elements into every programmatic activity and seeks to foster community capacity and resilience in every intervention.

project_name: Establishment of Three Humanitarian Hubs in Deep Field Intersectoral Prioritized Locations- (Leer, Kajo Keji and Raja)
project_objective: Since the signing of the Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS) in September 2018, active conflict has noticeably reduced, and an increase in returns has been observed. Humanitarian organizations continue to provide support and assistance as prospects for peace and development improve, and confidence is generated for durable solutions, including returns, relocations, or local integrations. Unfortunately, a lack of accommodation, workspace, and other key facilities often hinders humanitarian operations and a sustained presence in strategic deep field locations. In response, IOM will establish humanitarian hubs to enable the expansion of operations across hard-to-reach areas of South Sudan through an increase in static humanitarian presence in key strategic deep field locations. Based on lengthy consultations with field offices and State Inter Cluster Working Groups (ICWG), sixteen potential locations were proposed, of which eight have been selected as priority locations, namely Jiech, Kajo Keji, Kodok, Leer, Mandeng, New Fangak, Pieri, and Raja. IOM will provide field working facilities, accommodation, and warehousing to enable agencies to maintain a continuous presence on the ground and international staff to overnight in these locations, as well as allow care of the overflow of staff who are unable to find any other accommodation. Based on the eight proposed locations and further security/technical assessments undertaken, five pilot locations have been identified for 2021, namely Kajo Keji, Kodok, Jiech,Raja and Leer, at which the initial hubs will be set up; best practices and lessons learned will inform the establishment of humanitarian hubs in the other five sites identified. The establishment of the pilot hubs at Kodok and Jiech are being funded by DFID and Jiech by SSHF, so IOM will support the establishment of hubs in Kajo Keji, Raja and Leer under this project. IOM will work closely alongside the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) and UN OCHA, as well as NGOs that will assume responsibility for the running of the hubs. IOM will hand-over the management of the hubs and work on building the capacity of NGOs and local partners to ensure sustainable management of the humanitarian hubs subsequent to the conclusion of the intervention.

project_name: Apoyo integral para la mejora del acceso a la educación de calidad y de la permanencia escolar de alumnos y docentes.
project_objective: Este proyecto pretende mejorar las condiciones ofrecidas en las escuelas referentes a alimentación escolar (para 406,338 niños, niñas y adolescentes- NNAs), disponibilidad de material educativo para incentivar el acceso y la asistencia regular de los estudiantes (1,250,000 NNA). También pretende mejorar las condiciones de trabajo y la capacidad técnica de los docentes mediante actividades de formación y distribución de incentivos (23,734 docentes) que reduzcan el absentismo y la deserción de los docentes. El proyecto ofrece soluciones 150,000 NNAs que han abandonado el sistema escolar para que se reincorporen a la escuela o a oportunidades de aprendizaje alternativas. Igualmente se ofrecen actividades recreativas a 200,000 NNA fuera del horario escolar y apoyo psicoeducativo para 300,000 NNA. También se pretende fortalecer las capacidades del sector para alcanzar a 400,000 con actividades de educación a distancia y llegar a 70,000 adolescentes con actividades de nivelación escolar y la promoción de habilidades para la vida. Todas estas actividades se desarrollarán primando un enfoque intersectorial que tenga en cuenta aspectos de protección infantil, WASH, nutrición y componentes de sensibilización dirigidos a promover cambios de conducta, todo ello con un enfoque inclusivo y de protección de derechos.

project_name: Proyecto de prevención y respuesta a la COVID-19 en salud
project_objective:
La recesión económica y la disminución de la inversión en Venezuela han llevado al deterioro de la infraestructura y los servicios públicos, siendo salud uno de los sectores más golpeados en todos sus niveles. Dentro del contexto de necesidades humanitarias de la población general, la emergencia de la pandemia por COVID-19 ha impuesto una carga adicional al ya debilitado sistema de salud venezolano.
Durante el 2019 se evidenció cómo las necesidades de atención adecuada de los casos  de infección por SARS Cov2, generó un cierre de facto en buena parte de los servicios de salud esenciales, tales como las consultas prenatales y las actividades de vacunación, además del cierre de todas las consultas y actividades quirúrgicas electivas, ya casi durante 8 meses a esta fecha. Las cifras oficiales de casos de COVID-19 se vieron limitadas a los resultados de las pruebas de laboratorio aplicadas, sin embargo, la demanda de atenciones en los centros centinela se vio rápidamente incrementada y surgieron nuevos centros centinela para la atención de los casos sospechosos o confirmados de infección por SARS COV2. Las acciones de las organizaciones humanitarias como la distribución de Equipos de Protección personal para el personal de salud de primera línea, el suministro de medicamentos e insumos esenciales, materiales de limpieza y desinfección y las capacitaciones en su adecuado uso fueron factores fundamentales para el incremento lento, pero progresivo de las consultas preventivas, especialmente en materia de salud materna e infantil. Para contribuir a satisfacer la demanda de atenciones por consultas de emergencia de la población general UNICEF distribuyó kits de emergencia y equipos de soporte respiratorio, entre otros, en sus centros priorizados, con los cuales fueron atendidos NNA, mujeres, hombres y adultos mayores.  De un total de 65 centros centinela acordados con las autoridades de salud, al inicio de la pandemia, UNICEF logró alcanzar 360 centros mediante la distribución directa de insumos, o a través de sus aliados en el terreno; beneficiándose centros hospitalarios de todos los niveles de atención, centros de atención médica ambulatoria, todas las consultas del Programa de ITS/VIH a nivel nacional, ONG's que trabajan con pacientes trasplantados, servicios de emergencia de alcaldías y personas en tránsito a nivel fronterizo.
Para 2021 UNICEF espera poder mantener el aporte regular de insumos básicos de protección para el personal de salud en 360 centros de salud y beneficiar a 2,398,626 personas, en especial mujeres embarazadas, niños y niñas y  personas de alto riesgo por condiciones de salud subyacentes, personas  en tránsito fronterizo, personal de servicios básicos a nivel comunitario y a los aliados de implementación en el terreno, para contribuir a garantizar el acceso universal a los servicios de salud, aún manteniéndose el escenario de la pandemia por COVID19, en todos los estados del país, a través de:
1.- Compra, distribución y entrega a hospitales y ambulatorios de equipamiento, insumos,medicamentos, equipos de protección personal para el manejo de casos sospechosos, probables y confirmados de COVID-19.
2.- Fortalecimiento de las capacidades del talento humano en prevención, detección y manejo de casos de COVID -19.
3.- Atención de casos sospechosos, probables y confirmados de COVID-19 (medicina general, medicina especializada, enfermería, salud mental y psicosocial, nutrición, apoyo terapéutico).
4.- Realizar acciones de monitoreo de los cambios de situación, necesidades de recursos, disponibilidad de servicios, y aplicación de protocolos en comunidad y establecimientos de salud.
5.- Mejoramiento de la cadena de frío en los centros priorizados, con miras a fortalecer las inmunizaciones de rutina y contra el COVID-19 para personas de alto riesgo.

project_name: Community Revitalization & Resilience through Early Recovery and Livelihood interventions in northwest Syria
project_objective:
IOM will contribute to community revitalization and resilience through supporting local economic recovery, improving access to basic/social services and promoting community engagement and social cohesion. The project will strengthen access to livelihoods by creating income-generating opportunities and by improving access to production and market infrastructure to restore local economy recovery. This comes in line with both Early Recovery and Livelihood Sector 2021 objectives.

IOM will contribute to the rehabilitation and restoration of disrupted livelihoods by providing skills, income opportunities, and access to markets in camps and/or host communities for beneficiaries in NWS. IOM will improve access to markets by establishing new market areas in four Planned Camps. IOM will also provide financial or in-kind support to IDPs for entrepreneurial activities, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and community groups, to establish their business in the newly built markets. Additionally, IOM will provide vocational training and SME support business grants to vulnerable IDPs and host community members. Furthermore, IOM will provide income generating activity through Cash for Work (CFW) programmes. Lastly, IOM will improve the livelihood opportunities and community engagement for IDPs and vulnerable communities through the continuation of the Community Enhancement Center (CEC) and establishment of Community Engagement Teams (CETs) in Afrin, A’zaz, Harim, and Idleb sub-districts.

project_name: Enhancing conditions for economic inclusion, sustainable incomes and livelihoods and well-being for refugees and affected populations in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
IOM will implement a range of livelihoods and self-reliance activities for affected Rohingya and host communities including those living inside camps focusing on addressing immediate needs of the vulnerable populations to meet basic necessity and providing sustainable economic development support to ensure strategic approach which aimed to promote social cohesion and peaceful coexistence and accountable for affected populations. 
IOM will continue with providing income generating activities and portable skills development for Rohingya in 18 IOM managing camps and Tekanf and Ukhiya Upazilas in Cox’s Bazar District by linking up with government extension officers and utilizing existing initiatives for on/off farm activities following technical guidance from the Food Security Sector. IOM will diversify vulnerability criteria and extend support including those persons at risks due to protection related concerns, climate change, environmental degradation and COVID-19 through multi-dimensional interventions in coordination with different sector expertise of IOM. It will include the most vulnerable in camps and host communities especially single mothers, female headed households, families with dependent children/persons with disabilities.  
Quick impact projects through cash-based interventions will be provided by creating innovative initiatives with youth and vulnerable households to promotes environmental, localization and diversity inclusion. 
Study/needs assessment/mapping will be conducted in partnership with organizations and agencies to analyze different needs of post-COVID and coping mechanisms in camps and host communities with sex, age, disability disaggregated data.

project_name: Winterization and Shelter Rehabilitation Program for the most vulnerable IDPs and Host community in the North West Syria 2021
project_objective:
Mercy-USA for Aid and Development will support internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host community in Maarrat Tmasrin, Idleb, Dana, Jandairis and Afrin Sub-districts with winterization support with mixed modalities in-kind and E-vouchers (based on markets functionality), to provide eco-friendly biofuel, and stove kits (in line with SNFI activity 1.2 Provision of seasonal and supplementary NFIs and shelter assistance (e.g. winter clothing, fuel, winter-specific shelter upgrades; or summer/flood assistance including cash/voucher for these items)
From January to March 2021, Mercy-USA targeted 8,076HH, 41,525individuals (Men 8,321- Women 9,131- Boys 11,206- Girls 12,861) with winterization by using in-kind modality. 

From October till December 2021, Mercy-USA will target 3500HH, 17,995 individuals (Men 3,606- Women 3,957- Boys 4,856- Girls 5,576) by using with in-kind and E-vouchers methodologies for implementation.

Total target 11,576HH, 59,521 individuals (Men 11,927- Women 13,088- Boys 16,062- Girls 18,443)

Mercy-USA will target each household with in-kind or value E-voucher with 900 kg of olive pit fuel and stoves for one time throughout the winter months (November, December, and January) A distribution/redemption  of 300 kg per month along with stoves or the most vulnerable households. 
On the other hand, Mercy-USA will target 200 HH (Men 200, Women 220, Boys 270, and Girls 310) in Idleb Sub-district with shelter rehabilitation and repair for slightly damaged houses due to fighting on this area, in order to enhance safe access to shelter such as repair windows and wall holes without extreme damage taking in our considerations HLP issue prior to any house selection can be made by using contractor with cost no more than 1000 USD per HH.

project_name: Strengthening IDPs communal coping strategies in Maaret Tamsrin Camps
project_objective:
This project aims to strengthening IDPs communal coping strategies during the winter season by Equipping and training emergency responders and IDP committees in IDP sites about first aid and fire response. 
The training will include live demo in collaboration with white helmets to show participants in the training how they can deal with the fire from the beginning to the end including:
1- Fire extinguishing,
2- First aid to the injuries 
3- Evacuate the trapped IDPs inside the tents to safer area to avoid being affected with the fire.

Furthermore, under this project will provide fire extinguishers and first aid kits to each camp in order to establish fire point accessible to all IDPs with presence of trained person nearby to respond immediately to any fire incident.

These activities will be implemented before the winter seasons as proactive preparation for the winter season  which caused increase fire incidents due to improper use of the stoves and fuel.

Mercy-USA will focus on Maaret Tamsrin camps based on the trend of fire incident reports provided by CCCM cluster in 2020 which highlighted big need for such intervention to mitigate fire risks.

Also, Mercy-USA has plan for winterization project in the same camps, moreover, we have monthly food assistance project which gives Mercy-USA advantage to follow up the training impact on regular basis and provide advices whenever needed, so this will reflect complementarity and integration approach for strong sustainability. 

Mercy-USA will target 3500HH, 17,995 individuals (Men 3,606- Women 3,957- Boys 4,856- Girls 5,576) in 50 camps 



Prioritization of activities in case of underfunding will be:
1-Conduct one training and cancel the refresher training 
2-Provision of fire extinguishers and first aid kits is top priority
3- Reduce place for the fire points to two instead of three in each site 
4-Reduce staff cost 

So the prioritizing will be scale down activities rather than remove any activity

project_name: Response to winterization needs to the newly IDPs in the north of Idleb and Aleppo.
project_objective:
The project aims to distribute winterization heating means, stoves and fuel for 2000 families in NWS which have registered highest number of severity scale, the targeted population are the newly IDPs who are living the camps and in inappropriate shelter (unfinished/bad conditions), in addition to most vulnerable locals (15% of beneficiaries) and the targeted families are who hosting displaced persons (vulnerable groups who should have special concern as described in HNO 2021), the selected winterization items are the life-saving heating means in its minimum, in the areas where (-4) is the lowest registered degree with some coverage of snow in different locations and (4) the average degree in winter, the winterization heating items will be distributed in a timely manner as:

1- Heating stoves: (diesel, coal, firewood, and Perrin) stoves will be distributed with their accessories according to the cluster guidelines and recommendation and by the mid of November 2021 GAN could finalize the distribution of stoves.

2- Heating items: GAN will respond to life-saving winterization needs for the beneficiary: Based on the PDM results and last project and lesson learned, one type of heating fuel did not achieve the expected benefit, families that live in tents prefer to use firewood and/or Perrin for heating others prefer diesel, so GAN will provide heating items according to the preferences of the beneficiaries. 

In term of fuel suppliers: according to the assessment result and our ongoing project there are limited fuel suppliers that could support the project, and GAN should be strict in term of fuel quality and beneficiaries dignity (ensure that the distribution points not far away from their homes), so GAN will contract with fuel supplier(s) to supply the needed quantities of high-quality diesel to avoid any harm to beneficiaries health and save their dignity, as a result, the e-voucher modality will be used in distribution points

GAN had a project covered winter 2020-2021 so 16.6% of this project is secured.

project_name: Enhancing resilience of conflict-affected communities in Northern Syria while providing sustainable WASH solutions and increasing aid effectiveness to the IDPs in camps through emergency response intervention and long-term approach
project_objective:
The project intends to provide an integrated emergency and sustainable WASH intervention package to host communities and IDPs in the communities and in the camps and informal settlements northern Syria.
In response to the costly and short-term water supply in northwest Syria and to reinforce the most urgent life-saving interventions, Watan Foundation aims to enhance the long-term WASH infrastructure alongside with the emergency response services for certain period of time.  
This improvement targets host communities and IDPs in 50 camps and 5 communities hosting approximately 300,000 individuals. 
Through this project, WATAN will provide water trucking (max. three months) as a transition service, installing networks and connecting to nearby water and sanitation systems, including introducing solar energy, solid waste management, desludging latrines septic tanks (max. three months), constructing new latrines for persons with disabilities and persons without disabilities, operation and maintenance for the existing and new constructed latrines, distributing garbage containers, hygiene kits distribution and hygiene promotion.

As for the host communities, in five communities, WATAN will cover the rehabilitation and operational support to water and sanitation systems, including expansion of water and sanitation networks, rehabilitation of WASH facilities of the critical utilities (schools, HCFs,..), establishing tariff systems, introduce the solar energy modalities in water systems, solid waste management and distributing garbage containers, 

The project subscribes to WATAN strategy of alleviating the suffering of people in need from Syria in order to maintain a healthy life and reduce the transmission of water-borne diseases.

project_name: Providing adequate life-saving shelter, NFI kits, and sites infrastructure upgrading for crisis-affected camps and communities in northwest Syria
project_objective:
The project is designed for promoting cohesion and recovery by reducing shelter vulnerabilities of residents, host communities, returnees, and IDPs for both insides of camps by restoring basic infrastructure to mitigate the risks of oods and outside of camps by building transitional sheltering units (TSUs) and rehabilitation of damaged houses.

The main achievement for the proposed interventions is to enhance the situation for the current shelter in order to improve the living conditions for those IDP’s who are living in the informal settlements, self-settled sites, and managed camps in order to avoid the negative
effect of the weather uctuations along the different seasons which might lead to ood and losing their shelters, in addition, to enhance the privacy for the targeted bene ciaries
to ensure their protection and safety as well. This achievement can be achieved by conducting the following activities:

a. Provision/Replacement for the worn tents.

b. Conduct Ground, internal and external insulations for the tents in the IDP’s sites. c. Construction of community infrastructures in camps (drainage, ground preparation/leveling of the site, etc.)

d. Provision for seasonal assistance such as stove, heating fuel, thermal blankets, and winter clothes either in-kind or as Cash vouchers restricted to be used to maintain the access for the service.

e. Provision for NFI kits which includes essential items to the IDP’s such as kitchen kits. f. Providing a transitional shelter unit solution (TSUs) that in a digni ed shelter would contribute to the elevation and promotion of the living conditions of IDPs. g. Rehabilitation/repair of houses/apartments.

project_name: Reduce the impact of the negative effect of fire incidents for the IDP's living in informal settlements in Aleppo and Idleb governorate.
project_objective:
The project is designed for promoting cohesion and recovery by reducing shelter vulnerabilities of residents, and IDPs for camps by reducing the impact of the negative effect of fire incidents for the IDP's living in informal settlements in Aleppo and Idleb governorate.
35000 IDPs (7500 Men, 8000 Women, 9500 Boys, and 10000 girls ) will be benefitted from the proposed fire response intervention in the 50 targeted camps, in addition to 100 IDPs will be benefitted from the technical capacity building for fire prevention.
All the IDPs will also be benefitted from the formed emergency intervention groups.
The project will cover the enhancement of the capacity of the camps' representatives in the targeted informal settlements to prevent, mitigate and respond to the fire incidents by conducting FGDs and awareness-raising sessions with the camp management and beneficiaries taking into practice and account the COVID-19 preventive measures during the awareness-raising sessions and FGD's along with developing fire warden systems in the targeted camps. Additionally, the project will ensure the provision of fire extinguishers and fire blankets to enhance the capacity of the people on firefighting by providing them with the needed materials in the targeted informal settlements in case of any fire incident occurring by Constructing of fire units in camps and equipping them with recommended tools and equipment by Fire TF.
The main activities:
-Forming Fire Warden Representatives committees FWRs with female representatives.
- Provide capacity building and ToT for community leaders and committee members for fire prevention.
- Establishing 50 equipped fire points and identifying the emergency procedures for any possible incident with setting up a fire response.
- Distributing fire blankets
-Conducting 100 fire prevention training sessions.
- Awareness-raising campaign for fire prevention for 35,000 IDPs in the camps through training for HHs and camps committee taking into account all the CCCM, SNFI and WASH clusters recommendations to ensuring physical distancing and COVID-19 related measures.
Regarding vulnerability criteria, the activities will be for all the IDPs inside the targeted camps, however, the selection criteria for the committees will be focused on: (after coordination with the CCCM cluster)
1- Community acceptance from the sector in the camp.
2- Age between 25 to 45 years.
3- The ability to act as a focal point for any issue related to the camp and assist in the mediation of disputes.
4- The ability to liaise between IDPs and humanitarian service providers;
5- Ensure effective information dissemination among site residents and empowers IDPs and encourages participation in decision-making.
All the mentioned activities are a top priority under CCCM. Forming FWRs committees, and establishing equipped fire points with Awareness-raising will be prioritized if HRP won't be fully funded.

project_name: Building Resilience to the Vulnerable Crisis-Affected Population in North- West Syria
project_objective:
The projects intends to provide a multi-faceted response in an integrated and coherent way.

 Shafak's proposal is designed to supporting farmers and livestock herders needs of the vulnerable IDPs, returnees and HCs. The project comprises the following  Key intervention areas: 

ER1: 9500 Targeted households are able to resume agricultural activities, increase household income and improve consumption through: i) provision of agricultural inputs, including improved access to water; olive harvesting and pruning and ii)improving/restoring agricultural infrastructure (for example irrigation / drainage), IV) Cash for harvest, V) extension services, VI) purchasing wheat, VII) forage cultivation
ER2: 5500 Targeted households are able to increase household income and maintain livestock activities through: i) provision of livestock inputs (500 kg of fodder per  beneficiary 1500 beneficiaries) ; ii) associated training, iii) vaccination campaigns per health care calendar (4 campaigns, 200,000 head per campaign owned by 4,000 beneficiaries)
ER3: 3000 Targeted households stabilize, maintain or increase their income through Cash-for-Work activities, which build and strengthen community related value chain infrastructure , disaster risk reduction, mechanical pest and vol control and olive trees harvesting, Purification of wheat fields, and afforestation. 
ER4: Rehabilitation of related value chain infrastructure, irrigation channels, Mills,
bakeries, storage, fodder mixers, feeder roads and silos.
ER5: 4500 HHs to be supported with regular food basket over 8 rounds
ER6: 6000 HHs to be supported with Cash for food Voucher: 
ER7: 15000 RTE to be distributed as response to emergencies and shocks
ER8: 5000 MPC to be distributed to affected populations after emergencies. 
ER8: 2000 MT of flour to be distributed to bakeries to subsidize prices.
ER9: 500 farmer will be supported with Cash/inkind productive assets

project_name: Food assistance to Support vulnerable people in northern of Syria
project_objective:
Takaful has designed this program aims to support the food security of the most vulnerable IDPs and part of the host community in Idleb and Aleppo governorates,
Main interventions:
First: providing most vulnerable IDPs and HCs standard food baskets on monthly basis, targeting 9000 HHs 45000 individuals (9640 men -10776 women – 11260 boys -12524 girls ) in Idleb and Aleppo governorate, The distribution will be conducted at specified food distribution points (FDPs), safe FDPs will be chosen, away from the military centres with enough and safe distance and beneficiaries have easy access to them. For beneficiaries who have difficulties to reach to distribution points such as families headed by child or Disabled persons, the baskets will be transferred to their location using light vehicle. The HHS who live in camps will receive baked bread in. the HHS which will receive the bread will be 1000, 5000individuals (men 1080 - women 1222 - boys 1320 - girls 1378). 
Second: providing newly IDPs with Ready to Eat rations (RTE) which enable them to provide their families with required food for the first week of the displacement. This intervention targets 5000 HHs 25000 individuals (5480 men - 6332 women - 6420 boys 7068 girls ) The identification of these IDPs is the responsibility of the Takaful MEAL team, who track the movements of the IDPs, collect their data, and verify these data. 
Third: Cooked Meals: In this intervention, Takaful Al-Sham will provide 5,000 cooked meals to 5,000 individuals (1296 men, 1466 women and 1653 girls 1584 boys), The new IDPs from the areas that have been displaced by the recent military operations will be targeted. The meal will contain the calories agreed to in the standards set by the Cluster. Takaful will coordinate with the food security cluster and with other organization who works in the same sector and field to reach the right beneficiaries and avoid any duplication. The project will ensure equal access for both genders with the priority for women, children headed household, disabled person, sick, PLW and elderly in addition the project staff will include female and male members trained on the protection principles and gender equality.

project_name: Shelter and NFI response for most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls of IDPs and their host community in NW Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to respond to 16,900 HH with a total of 96,000 disaggregated roughly as (21,120 men, 23,040 women, 25,920 boys, 25,920 girls) of  the most vulnerable conflict-affected  IDPs, and host communities in Idleb and Aleppo governorates, and prioritizing  households headed by female, child, disabled, or elderly, then households with severely ill or disabled members, children below 5, elderly, pregnant or lactating women; with special attention to those recently displaced or living overcrowded.
The project contributes to providing life-saving and life sustaining shelter & NFI assistance through the following activities:
1- provide 6,300 HH with seasonal and supplementary NFIs and assistance including winter clothing, stoves, and fuel in Al-Bab, Afrin, and Azaz subdistricts, and camps.  Each household will receive voucher of 150$ and prioritize its needs of these items accordingly. Moreover, 2000 HH will also receive their assistance through in kind modality.    
2-Provision of emergency shelter through instalment of 3,500 tents with associated infrastructure in (Azaz, suran) in Aleppo governorate, (Dana, Maaret Tamsrin) in Idleb governorate. 
3- Upgrading of 500 unfinished building with average cost of 850$ per unit in Aleppo (Al Bab, Suran, Daret Azza), Idleb (Harim, Salqin, Iskat, Kafr Takharim, Dana).
This project will also Contribute towards the resilience and cohesion of communities and households by improving housing through rehabilitation of 700 of partially damaged houses with an average cost of 750$ per house in (Harim, Salqin, Iskat, Kafr Takharim, Dana) in Idleb governorate, (Azaz, Al-Bab) in Aleppo governorate.
 4-Construction 400 transitional shelter (concrete blocks) for 400HH in Azaz and Al-Bab districts.
 Needs assessment was conducted early this year to identify the project locations. 
In all activities SDI considers the protection of the beneficiaries, so the distribution centres and the shops provide the assistance will be prepared with functional firefighting equipment, brochures of safety and security practice will be distributed to beneficiaries, Moreover female staff will be recruited and trained  to ensure more protection from exploitation and sexual abuse for girls and women and to deal with any GBV cases may encounter during the project. 
Most importantly SDI pays high attention to people with disabilities, elderlies, and people with special needs and for those assistance will be delivered to home.
Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights of shelter sites, shelter beneficiaries, and house owners will be considered throughout all stages of shelter repair interventions, and agreement will be signed to guarantee the rights of the beneficiaries. Coordination with SNFI cluster and other active members is essential to ensure geographical separation and avoid overlapping/duplication.

project_name: Improving living conditions for the most vulnerable population by providing adequate shelter/NFIs, and Winterization support in Aleppo and Idlib Governorate.
project_objective: IYD proposes this project to improve the shelter status for those are living in damaged and unfinished houses to meet the minimum standard of shelter provided by Shelter/NFI cluster and to enhance the daily living for new IDPs by distributing the requirements items, also support them in winter to face the harsh weather by providing commodity electronic vouchers (e-vouchers) to IDPs in camps to enable them to purchase a defined quantity of either diesel or coal to fuel heating stoves to heat their homes during the winter months, IYD will focus on a more durable solution, focused on shelter rehabilitation, to reduce protection risks for the most vulnerable, This project will target 400 damaged houses, and 200 unfinished houses(3500 individuals, 750 men, 878 women, 800 boys,1072 girls)  and 1000  new IDPs individuals in two governorates Idlib and Aleppo, Idlib, Jsr Alshoghur, Dier Hassan located in Idlib governorate, Azaz, and Aghtarin located in Aleppo governorate, These communities are managed by local councils where the local councils responsible for providing all services to the people and maintain and implement the infrastructure in the Areas.  IYD has a complete and complementary plan in the shelter sector to rehabilitate both damaged houses and unfinished houses, this plan consists of 6 steps: Project Preparation, Coordination & Community Selection, Beneficiaries Selection & Technical Need Assessment, Tendering & Contracting, Implementation & Quality Management, and Documentation. These haphazard shelter solutions increase protection risks to women, young girls, and children because they lack privacy and utility services like water and electricity often do not function. NW Syria has the highest for HHS reporting shelter inadequacy issues the most significant barrier to making shelter repairs was the expense; either that repairs required a professional, which households could not afford, or that households are able to make repairs, but the materials are too expensive- this was more commonly reported than a general lack of shelter materials, Shelter/NFI cluster data. clearly demonstrates that shelter units and more adequate shelter space are one of the most critical gaps with a need for increased support directed towards host communities to safeguard coping mechanisms and improve the standard and availability of shelter. Through this project IYD is planning to intervene in two locations at the district level, Aleppo governorate, Azaz, and Albab district, those two locations have many damaged houses. Under this project, IYD will rehabilitate 400 partially damaged houses between 40 % – 70 %, 100 houses in Jsr Alshohgur, and 300 in Idlib, Aleppo governorate, and 200 unfinished houses in Azaz, by reconstructing the destroyed walls, install new doors, and windows, and rehabilitate the water services, the estimated total number of targeted beneficiaries 3,000 individuals, also, IYD under this project will construct a wall to form separate rooms and provide new materials doors, windows, and lighting systems, in addition, the rehabilitation of the water services will be done by providing water tanks, toilets, and baths. IYD finds that residents are willing to contribute to improvement projects; specifically, to provide labor to support the repair and rebuilding of the accommodations. During conducting technical need assessment for shelter rehabilitation, IYD team will be focusing on the basic needs for the most vulnerable families, this is to identify the most required NFIs kits to be distributed for those families in the priority for new arrival families which they need, IYD planning to distribute new arrival kits, kitchen kit, and comprehensive kit, the distribution process will be through registration of the families and doing the verifications for the beneficiaries, the program team will prepare the distribution lists in coordination with the local council, each family will distribute  NFI standard kit.

project_objective:

Through this intervention, Takaful will conduct need assessments on a wide-range of sectors to ensure covering all needs and requirements inside IDP sites. The results will show gaps and will describe the actual quantities required to cover this gap. than Takaful will cover the needs according to available fund within the organization, but as for the gaps that cannot be covered by Takaful, a referral system will take place to ensure coordinating with other active NGOs to deliver the missing services, making sure to cover the targeted site with full package of services and coordinating with relevant clusters. This intervention will take place in 5 IDP site inside Maaret Tamsrin, Idleb, Harim, Dana, and Salqin subdistricts. Total estimated beneficiaries will be 3600 HHs.

Regarding the fire mitigation measures, Takaful is planning to cover 10 IDPs sites with full package of fire mitigation related services through constructing firefighting points inside the camps, as well as creating a team trained and assigned for fighting fire incidents with the required trainings and tools, finally spreading the awareness on how to decrease the accuracy of the fire incidents and how to protect lives when they occur. the project is planning to target camps in Daret Azza, Atareb, Al Bab, Afrin, A'zaz, subdistricts. Total estimated beneficiaries will be 3000 HHs (3375 men, 3600 women, 4350 boys, 3675 girls).

Takaful during 2021, beside delivering life-saving activities and emergency response, will work on increase the self-reliance and resilience of IDPs inside camps, through creating opportunities for them to secure a source of income to support their families, this is planned to take place within their residing sites (inside camps) through create short term job opportunities to camp residents through implementing maintenance and care activities to the infrastructure available inside camps, including maintaining latrines, roads, water networks, sewage networks, lighting, lands and basically all public service assets. The population benefitting from maintenance are 4000 HHs (4500 men, 4800 women, 5800 boys, 4900 girls). as for the population that will benefit from short term job opportunities are 400 individuals. the targeted location for these 2 components will be Maaret Tamsrin, Idleb, A'zaz, Harim, Dana, and Salqin subdistricts.

In the same context of empowering self-reliance, Takaful Is aiming In this project to support the self-governance of 20 IDPs sites, by supporting the creation of local bodies that are participatory management committees (including active participation by women). this will be followed with consistent support for these local bodies Including relevant trainings' delivery, handover of required tools and assets, etc.

Takaful will monitor the implementation of activities done by contractors or by contracted workers on a daily basis, to ensure quality and consistency of performance.
