project_name: Improving the access of vulnerable Lebanese and migrant populations to food and non-food needs across the country
project_objective:
Aligned with the Food Security sector's strategy, this action aims at alleviating the most urgent food and non-food needs of 3250 vulnerable Lebanese and Migrant households across the country. 

1- Provision of unconditional and unrestricted cash assistance to 2650 (2250 Lebanese, 400 Migrant) 
households (respectively 9600 Lebanese individuals, 1800 Migrant individuals) in the form of Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) over a period of six months.

This action is an expansion of AAH’s ongoing Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) portfolio. AAH will identify potential beneficiaries through the existing nationwide referral systems in addition to direct referrals from other NGOs, self-referrals received through the AAH hotline, and referrals from municipalities as well as recent MPCA vulnerability assessments conducted for ongoing projects. For the migrant community specifically, AAH has started to engage with IOM which agreed to collaborate on a referral mechanism and to set up key communication channels for the outreach to migrant communities in the project areas. Beneficiaries will be selected through AAH’s pre-defined vulnerability criteria based on core context-related indicators aligned to FS and BA sectors guidelines (eligibility survey including core indicators such as the Food Consumption Score, reduced Coping Strategy Index, Persons with special needs, etc.). To complement AAH's nutrition programming under the ERP, 40% of the targeted HHs will include pregnant women, lactating women, and/or caregivers of children under 5.

As recommended by the FS chapter under the ERP, monthly cash transfer of an approx value of 1,600,000 LBP per household according to the household size (300,000 per person per month to cover food needs and LBP 400,000 for non-food needs per household based on a family size of four) will be provided to the target population. Cash transfers will be redeemed through the LOUISE platform operating with Banque Libano-Francaise (BLF) which enables AAH to benefit from a preferential exchange rate (currently set at 17,000 LBP/USD) and allows to target beneficiaries without IDs, which is essential to reach migrant communities. On an exceptional and case-by-case basis, cash envelopes may be provided to extremely vulnerable HHs who cannot safely access the Financial Service Provider. AAH will closely monitor transfer amounts and coordinate with the Food Security and Basic Assistance Working Groups, of which it is an active member, to ensure assistance is of value and well-coordinated with other actors and stakeholders. Contingent upon reactivation of the Migrant Workers Coordination Group and Cash Task Force AAH will ensure close collaboration with those entities as well.

2- Provision of a 6-month assistance package including dry food parcels to 600 Lebanese households through the LHF.

In line with the LHF strategy and using OCHA's unified vulnerability targeting tool, AAH will provide nutritionally balanced food assistance through dry rations paired with WASH kits to mitigate hygiene risks for a duration of 6 months in Baalbek-Hermel, Bekaa, South, and Nabatiyeh.

3- Provision of one-off dry food parcels and hygiene kits to COVID-19 affected households through the LHF.

As part of its ongoing COVID-19 response, AAH will provide nutritionally balanced food assistance through dry rations to 100 households (regardless of nationality) as per the agreed geosplit between the partners in the South governorate (Sector 6 and 7). An additional caseload will be considered as a contingency plan based on the evolution of the COVID-19 pandemic and variants.

project_name: Appui d’urgence à la production agro-pastorale et Protection des moyens d’existence des personnes vulnérables affectées par la crise sécuritaire et les chocs climatiques au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire au Burkina Faso continue de se développer rapidement, s'étendant et s'approfondissant à de nouveaux domaines. À partir d'août 2020, l'insécurité croissante et les déplacements aggravent encore l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle chronique et entraînent des besoins sans précédent en termes d'accès aux abris et aux services sociaux de base. Dans cette crise de plus en plus caractérisée par des conditions de surpopulation dans les zones d'accueil, l'arrivée de COVID-19 souligne encore plus la nécessité de décongestionner les sites et les communautés qui accueillent des personnes déplacées. En novembre 2020, le nombre de personnes déplacées a atteint 1 049 000 sur une population de 2,9 millions de personnes ayant besoin d'assistance. Les résultats du Cadre harmonisé (mis à jour en juillet 2020) indiquent également qu'environ 3,3 millions de personnes (15 % de la population) sont confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë à un niveau de crise ou pire (phase 3 et plus). Cela représente une augmentation d'environ 57 % par rapport à la projection précédente (mars 2020), dont plus de 500 000 personnes en phase d'urgence et plus de 11 000 en risque de famine
La stratégie de la FAO en réponse à cette crise est de répondre rapidement aux besoins humanitaires des populations vulnérables directement touchées par l'insécurité avec deux types d'interventions spécifiques : 1) Réponse rapide des personnes touchées par le déplacement en leur fournissant une aide financière polyvalente pour leur permettre de couvrir leurs besoins humanitaires urgents et 2) renforcer les activités de protection et de réhabilitation des moyens de subsistance.
. 
Face à cette problématique de sécurité alimentaire, la stratégie de la FAO face à a pour objectif de répondre de manière rapide aux besoins humanitaires des populations vulnérables, directement affectées par l’insécurité à travers d’une part des activités d’assistance rapide, de protection et réhabilitation des moyens d’existence et d’autre part la mise en place de mécanisme de collecte et d’analyse des données agro-sylvo pastoraux et d'alerte précoce afin de mieux coordonnées les interventions.

Ainsi, le projet devra permettre d’atteindre le résultat ci-après :

-	Protéger et renforcer les moyens de subsistance des populations vulnérables par l’appui et la distribution d'intrants agricoles pour la production agricole, le déstockage des troupeaux dans les zones à risque de surpâturage et  soutien à la santé animale et soudure pastorale. 

Le projet sera mis en œuvre dans les Régions du Sahel du Nord, de l’Est et du Centre-Nord et du Centre-Nord le ciblage prendra en compte l'aspect genre dans les activités avec plus de 40% pour les femmes et 60% homme pour toutes les activités de production agro-pastorales.

project_name: Improving access and availability of food while building resilient systems to improve living conditions of Somali Households affected by crisis.
project_objective:
Through implementation, ACTED intends to save lives and improve the ability of Somali households to meet their basic needs through multi-purpose cash transfers for severely disaster-affected populations and to show progress towards the long-term goal of a Somali safety net. Through this project, the Somalia Cash Consortium, of which ACTED is a member, intends to address the needs of the most vulnerable disaster-affected households by providing multi-purpose unrestricted cash transfer. ACTED’s involvement in this project aims at supporting vulnerable households in Baidoa IDP sites of bay region, El-Afweyn and Erigavo districts of Sanaag region, through unconditional cash transfers through six months of mobile money transfers. The Consortium will target the most vulnerable households with life-saving multi-purpose unconditional cash transfers. The Action will specifically target populations in IPC 3, 4 and 5, especially newly displaced and worst-affected Pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities. In addition, this Action seeks to provide life-saving assistance to food insecure communities in Bay, Gedo and Lower Juba regions while implementing recovery and resilience activities to
restore livelihoods and respond to the needs of IDPs and rural communities in Baidoa, Kismayo, El-Afwayne, Badhan, Diinsoor and Buurhakaba districts who are impacted by floods and drought, lack sustainable livelihoods, at risk of displacement and with limited access to adequate WASH and shelter services.

project_name: Emergency Relief for Vulnerable IDP, Returnees and Host Communities in Kismayo, Somalia
project_objective:
Somalia has been affected by a combination of climatic and non-climatic shocks: conflicts, droughts, floods, protracted displacement, inequality, marginalization and poverty. For instance, heavy and erratic Gu’ rainfall that started in April 2020,  caused flush floods which contributed to displacement of an estimated 893,000 people across Somalia  while in  Kisimayo District  alone had 9,560 families affected by flash floods of which about 370 families were displaced, leaving their original settlement area for higher grounds. Some 2.6 million internally displaced persons (IDP) living in 2,000 sites in Somalia face serious risks of evictions, marginalization and exclusion; and lack access to essential services such as shelter, water and sanitation  (OCHA Somalia, 2020). IDPs comprise 30% of Somalis in IPC 3 and 4 requiring lifesaving assistance in 2021 (FSC HNO page). Kismayo District hosts over 7,000 IDPs spread over 139 IDP camps. It is the third largest city in Somalia and the capital of both the Lower Juba region and the Jubaland State. Many IDPs and returnees have ended up settling in Kismayo where they can get assistance from international organizations as well as get open spaces where they can set up temporary shelters – albeit as squatters with no defined tenure. The dire humanitarian situation in Somalia has been exacerbated by the Covid-19 global pandemic which has caused suffering and death in virtually all corners of the globe. Somalia has not been spared and has so far suffered 3,847 confirmed infections and 99 Covid19-related deaths as at beginning of October, 2020. The pandemic has also had a devastating effect on food security and livelihood for the millions of Somalis who are not able to go about their life normally. Prior to the floods in the early part of the year, the population in Kismayo District were affected by impact of the COVID-19 directives that led to increase of prices of food and Non-Food Items (NFIs). According to market assessment done by CARE International in April, prices of food items increased by an average 17 percent while those of Non-Food Items (NFIs) increased by 12 percent following COVID-19 related restrictions.
SIF has planned an integrated response to the on-going humanitarian crises in Kismayo, Lower Juba through contributing to improvement of livelihood and food security among the IDPs, poor host communities and returnees in the area. The project will focus on addressing their weakened capacity to recover from effects of conflict and cyclical climatic shocks by implementing activities that will improve immediate access to food and non-food items and to promote activities that ensure that the vulnerable households being supported are able to have sustainable livelihoods beyond the emergency support. Currently, the basic foodstuffs are available from the local markets which are well supplied by both local producers as well as from outside Kismayo area. 
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the improvement of food security and livelihood of the most vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), poor host communities (HC) and returnees in Kismayo. The project has two specific objectives: (i) Improve access to food through provision of UCT to 900 vulnerable IPD and poor host community households (7,200 individuals); and, (ii) improve livelihood opportunities and resilience for 600 vulnerable IDP and host community households (4,800 individuals).
Beneficiaries will be assessed using the following criteria: They must (i)be from the geographically targeted areas; (ii)be considered poor or very poor; (iii) come from households with large family size (7 persons or more); (iv)hail from a vulnerable HH headed by woman, elderly, PWDs, child, or chronically ill persons; (vi) newly arrived/displaced IDPs; and/or (vi) households that are living in temporary shelters due to lack of means.

project_name: Atención nutricional integral comunitaria para niños, niñas y mujeres afectados por la crisis en Venezuela
project_objective:
Entendiendo que: i) la malnutrición aguda es la principal causa de mortalidad para los niños menores de 5 años (U5), y los efectos en su desarrollo motriz, psicológico y cognitivo son a largo plazo; ii) las mujeres/adolescentes en gestación o lactancia son una población en riesgo de sufrir malnutrición y trasladar los efectos nocivos al bebé, Save the Children ha considerado que la mejor estrategia de respuesta es: i) incrementar el acceso a los servicios de nutrición, teniendo en cuenta obstáculos de género y conflicto; ii) dar tratamiento directo no clínico a los niños U5 y madres embarazadas o lactantes; iii) mejorar el conocimiento y las prácticas de Alimentación al Niño Pequeño y Lactante (ANPL).

Sensibilización en rutas disponibles para servicios de protección para NNA; mitigación de la VBG, masculinidades positivas y derechos de salud sexual y reproductiva serán realizados con las comunidades de intervención, en donde se incluyen grupos menores de 5 años, entre 5-15 años, adultos jóvenes y de edad contemporánea, para ambos géneros.

project_name: Programa para el Apoyo Nutricional y Alimenticio en Comunidad (PANAC)
project_objective:
Somos una Asociación Civil sin fines de lucro, creada con el propósito de integrar esfuerzos de la iniciativa privada y agregar valor a los procesos de responsabilidad social de las empresas, en alianza con las organizaciones de desarrollo social (ODS), autoridades y comunidades, con el fin de impulsar acciones que mejoren la calidad de vida de las personas en Venezuela.
Formamos parte de la red de solidaridad mundial United Way, una organización presente en 40 países que tiene como objetivo mejorar las condiciones de vida de las personas en distintas regiones del mundo, que reúne a más de dos millones de voluntarios en actividades de responsabilidad social.

Desde hace 3 años el DVC lleva a cabo programas de alimentación, formación y restauración en las distintas comunidades alrededor de Venezuela, donde el trabajo en estas tiene gran alcance en poder atender no solo a los niños de la primera infancia, sino a las familias de cada uno.
Con este enfoque buscamos abarcar una necesidad latente en temas de seguridad alimentaria en los Estados Falcón (58.188 personas), Táchira (1.031.158 personas) y Apure (674.000 personas), donde la población objetivo esta discriminada en el PIN poblacional del clúster de Seguridad Alimentaria.

La grave situación que viven las poblaciones más vulnerables en Venezuela nos obliga a cubrir la necesidad de atención para los mismos desde: 
1. Proporcionar alimentación a 3.000 niños y niñas por medio de un desayuno y un almuerzo, proporcional al 70% del requerimiento nutricional diario (aporte de calorías y proteínas) para niños en riesgo de malnutrición. 
Estos tiempos de comida se les entregará a los niños y niñas dentro de la institución, todas las mañanas y a la hora del mediodía, para así impactar positivamente la asistencia escolar y el rendimiento dentro del aula. 
Previo a la aprobación de las instituciones se realiza un estudio socioeconómico de la comunidad, y a su vez, se realizan pruebas antropométricas, donde se determina un diagnostico nutricional para evidenciar el estado inicial del beneficiario y del grupo de atención en general, y luego esta misma evaluación se realiza de manera trimestral para determinar el impacto del alimento, verificando así algunas variables en el crecimiento y en el desarrollo del niño.
Las docentes y madres colaboradoras (representantes que son voluntarias en la institución para elaborar la comida) reciben una inducción por parte de nutricionistas en la elaboración de los alimentos y las porciones que se deben manejar desde los mismos. Esto con el fin de estandarizar todas las prácticas y técnicas culinarias de estas madres colaboradoras, para así garantizar conocimientos básicos en áreas sanitarias, nutricionales y dietéticas, que a su vez corresponda al aporte de macronutrientes en la dieta diaria de los beneficiarios.
2.  Entrega mensual de bolsas de comida para las familias de los niños beneficiados con el programa de alimentación y para el personal docente y administrativo de los centros educativos, así como también a las madres colaboradoras que hacen vida en los los mismos; lo cual representaría 69 toneladas de alimentos mensuales.
 Esto como complemento en la alimentación de las familias y del personal que interviene en la educación del niño, mitigando también la deserción escolar y paleando el estado de inseguridad alimentaria presente en los grupos familiares de estos estados, siendo estos últimos los pilares fundamentales para que la educación se lleve a cabo de forma exitosa, protegiendo todo el entorno del niño.
3. La formación y la capacitación técnica profesional a cargo de expertos en el área dirigida al personal de las instituciones educativas que funcionan como Escuelas Granjas o como Escuelas Técnicas, lo que permitirá  potenciar las destrezas en oficios de agricultura, así como generar una estrategia de agricultura comunitaria, capacitando la potencialidad de la zona donde se desenvuelven estas instituciones.

project_name: EMERGENCY FOOD SECURITY AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT FOR THE IDPs, HOST/RETURNEES IN BORNO STATE
project_objective:
Under this grant, SI will support the most vulnerable households to improve their livelihood and enhance their resilience. This will be accomplished through the provision of multi-purpose cash grants (MPCG), implemented through vouchers. SI FSL team will also impart training for the beneficiaries to earn a living, thereby contributing to beneficiary households' resilience. Projects will be implemented in MMC/Jere, Monguno, Ngala and Dikwa LGAs. 
Under the proposed project, SI will also respond to the vulnerable populations' emergency food needs through food vouchers for food assistance, in coordination with the Food Security Sector recommendation. To support early recovery, SI proposes distributing small livestock to the most vulnerable and women-headed families to enhance their income and improve the nutrition for the family members, especially children under 5 years. 
Host community members/returnees and IDPs staying with host communities will be targeted in priority for these interventions, as per the FSL sector guidelines. Through the proposed projects in the areas, SI will ensure that adequate Do No Harm analyses are being conducted and that participatory methods in all aspects of the project cycle are implemented. All services to be provided will be designed to ensure safe and easy access for all vulnerable persons with specific needs (women, children, elderly, etc.).
SI has developed monitoring tools that include protection mainstreaming indicators and has included questions related to protection mainstreaming in all its surveys to measure that humanitarian assistance is delivered in a safe, accessible, accountable and participatory manner.

project_name: Enhancing food security and livelihoods of conflict affected population in Yobe and Borno States, Nigeria
project_objective: ACF is proposing to deliver cash-based for emergency food assistance, support income-generating activities through cash grant and business skills training and development for livelihood, and improve agriculture production through seeds and other inputs, and transformation of skills for food and livelihoods to households in Yobe & Borno States of Nigeria. Social protection and social safety net in the form of cash/food voucher transfers aim to support IDPs and conflict-affected households to meet their food basket needs or the cost of maintaining a nutritious diet. Complimentary sessions on sensitization will focused on good nutrition and hygiene practices for pregnant and lactating women, as well as training on income-generating activities, best agricultural practices aim to strengthen affected populations' food production and nutrition security to support the establishment of their livelihoods and build their resilience to prevent the use of negative coping strategies.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire pour les personnes les plus vulnérables de Niono et Goundam
project_objective:
L'objectif de l'intervention proposée est double: D'une part il s'agit de fournir une réponse adaptée aux différents besoins des populations touchées de façon conjoncturelle à différents types de choc: déplacements, inondations) et d'autre part, il s'agit de contribuer à l'amélioration de la résilience des personnes ayant subi ce choc. 
Les cibles sont les populations en situation de déplacement, en situation de vulnérabilité économique et nutritionnelle.
La réponse d'urgence s'organise avant tout selon une modalité de transferts monétaires à hauteur de  20 000 CFA par ménage suite à un ciblage des ménages réalisé sur la base de critères de vulnérabilité économique ou de status pour les déplacés. 
Parallèlement, une réponse liée à la résilience se développe à partir d'activités plus longues dans la mise en oeuvre et orientée à partir des potentialités de production et de commercialisation des zones ciblées. ce type d'activité s'adresse soit à des déplacés soit des populations hôte, selon les critères de sélection tels qu'un un minimum de capacité de production ainsi que des critères de vulnérabilité. 
Plus précisément, il s'agira de cibler les zone de Goundam et de Niono de la façon suivante: 
Sur Goundam, la localité de Gargando accueille environ 700 ménages de déplacés venus de la région de Niono suite aux différents types de conflits en cours dans cette zone. Ces 700 ménages bénéficieront de d'un appui en cash de type RRM permettant de couvrir les premiers besoins alimentaires. la modalité choisie par SI demeure la distribution de cash. 
Dans un deuxième temps, afin de garantit le suivi de ces déplacés, SI organisera, en coordination avec les autres acteurs présents dans la zone et de façon à éviter tout overlapping, les distributions de cash post RRM sur les deuxièmes et troisièmes mois. 
Simultanément, la zone de Goundam abrite aussi des ménages affectés par les crues du Niger en cours. Des évaluations précises sont en cours au moment de l'écriture de ce projet mais des centaines d'hectares de riz non encore récoltés dans la zone du cercle de Diré serait potentiellement détruits suite à ces inondations. 
Pour ces ménages, vivant dans un environnement aux faibles avantages comparatifs, dépendant essentiellement de l'agriculture de décrue et de l'élevage, ces inondations sont synonymes de pertes financières non négligeables car faisant potentiellement basculés ces ménages déjà pauvres dans une vulnérabilité exacerbée. 
Pour ces ménages, l'action proposée se compose  d'une part de transferts monétaires (modalité de distribution en cash) destinés à couvrir les besoins immédiats en nourriture et, d'autre part, d'appui en intrants et en assets (outils, semences) en nature ou en cash selon les zones et les préférences des bénéficiaires. 
Sur la zone de Niono, si les types de choc sont globalement semblables (inondations et conflits), de même que la nature de la réponse (RRM, post RRM, assistance alimentaire et recapitalisation en intrants productifs) l'ampleur demeure plus importante à la fois en matière de nombres de personnes impactées par les conflits en cours et par les inondations des derniers mois. là aussi des évaluations précises sont toujours en cours et ont pris un peu de retard suite aux difficulté d'accès liées à la volatilité du contexte. 
Enfin, ces deux zones ont aussi été impactées par les conséquences négatives du covid 19 en termes de diversification des ressources de revenus informelles, contribuant d'autant plus à la vulnérabilté globale de la zone et à l'exacerbation des difficultés économiques ayant en premier lieu un impact sur l'accès et la disponibilité en alimentation. 
Les Activités de Solidarités International sont systématiquement accompagnées de messages de sensibilisation sur les gestes barrières et ces gestes sont aussi intégrés dans l'approche.

project_name: Provision of Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) services to men, women, boys and girls in displacement sites in Somalia
project_objective:
It is estimated that there are 2.6 million internally displaced persons in Somalia (2020 Humanitarian Needs Overview). Successive years of drought exacerbated by a prolonged conflict has resulted in an enduring humanitarian crisis that demands urgent life saving interventions. Concomitantly, the protracted nature of this crisis requires a strategy that sees beyond the immediate needs and incorporates durable solutions throughout the response. With this project IOM will provide camp management and camp coordination services to men, women, boys and girls in displacement sites in the districts of Baidoa, Kismayu and Doolow to ensure that the most urgent needs of the IDPs are met, while also setting the foundation for the achievement of durable solutions.

Latest estimations of displacement conditions in Somalia indicate that around 2.3 million people have settled in around 2,400 IDP sites (CCCM Cluster HRP 2021 Guidance note), most of which are informal, small and scattered settlements in urban or peri-urban areas. Living in private land often means that IDPs are at constant risk of eviction, which further stresses their already vulnerable situation. Protracted conflict-driven displacement aggravated by natural disasters, limited livelihood opportunities, limited availability of public services and limited access to durable solutions all contribute to the continued increase in the number and vulnerability of IDPs. 

Baidoa hosts the largest number of IDPs after Mogadishu with more than 392,300 displaced persons living in 517 sites (CCCM site verification exercise). In 2019 government authorities allocated public land for IDPs which has enabled IOM and other humanitarian/development partners to relocate families at risk of eviction, linking traditional CCCM activities with an approach tailored towards the achievement of durable solutions. As more public land becomes available to IDPs, IOM plans to support more families to relocate. However, for the foreseeable future the majority of families will remain in makeshift sites under the constant threat of forced eviction. 

In Kismayo, 64,000 IDPs are hosted in 144 sites (CCCM site verification exercise). These sites are privately owned and most IDPs have to pay to live there; however, these agreements do not prevent families from the risk of being evicted. Most of these IDP sites are overcrowded and lack basic infrastructure; living conditions are poor with overstretched services and shelters often made of locally available materials such as plastic and worn-out clothes. 

Doolow is currently hosting around 62,600 IDPs in two makeshift sites located in public land: Kabasa and Qansaxley. The high population density in these camps and the subsequent concentration of service provision makes service monitoring and coordination key aspects of CCCM related needs. In addition, community mobilization and the enactment of representative governance structures are needed to facilitate dialogue between service providers and affected populations, and to enhance accountability towards them.

project_name: Provision of Life-Saving Shelter and Life Sustaining NFI to Vulnerable Populations in Somalia
project_objective:
Due to the ongoing humanitarian crisis, Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) needs remain consistently high, with an estimated 3.1 million Somalis with SNFI needs according to the Humanitarian Needs Overview 2021, especially in Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) sites where many households (HHs) live in makeshift shelters. Oftentimes, these makeshift shelters do not provide adequate privacy and protection against weather elements, whilst a lack of tenure security, random evictions and vulnerability to fires further exacerbate the shelter needs of IDPs. It is therefore estimated that around one-third of the Somali population lack essential NFIs. 

Therefore, SNFI needs are the subject of much collaborative efforts; Collective Outcome 2 of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) aims ‘to reduce the risks and vulnerabilities, and build resilience of displaced and host communities to reach durable solutions’, whilst Specific Objective 2.2 aims to scale-up and provide CCCM, WASH, education, health, nutrition, shelter and NFI services for 1.6 million people in established IDP sites across 68 districts by the end of 2021.

For the 2021 HRP, 75,000 individuals (12,500 households with an average of 6 individuals per household) will receive NFI support through a mixed-methods strategy of in-kind contingency stocks provision to be undertaken with contingency stock partners and direct implementation of Cash-Based Intervention (CBI) for NFI needs. A further 75,000 individuals will receive shelter support through emergency shelter, in-kind shelter kits, and CBI for shelter needs. Finally, 15,000 individuals will receive infrastructure support, both in-kind and through CBI. The transfer mechanism for CBI   will be evidence-based and linked to market assessment and needs analysis. The breakdown of the planned intervention is as follows: (1) the provision of contingency stock with in-kind NFI and shelter kits for 10,000 households (NFI: 7,500, Shelter: 2,500), available for distribution nationwide by shelter cluster partners where need arises; (2) emergency/transitional shelter (Emergency: 7,500; Transitional: 2,500) and NFI (5,000) support to newly displaced IDPs in the Gedo and Bay region targeting 15,000 households; (3) infrastructure support to 2,500 households in Gedo and Bay region.

project_name: Appui au renforcement des  moyens d’existence des agropasteurs pour l’amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire à l’Est du Tchad
project_objective:
Le Tchad à l’instar des autres pays touchés par la pandémie du COVID-19 a pris des mesures pour protéger sa population contre la propagation de la pandémie COVID-19. Malheureusement certaines de ces mesures ont entraîné un dysfonctionnement dans les chaînes d’approvisionnement en denrées alimentaires et intrants agricoles, des hausses de prix de certaines denrées, etc. 
Face à cette situation, le Gouvernement a élaboré un plan d’action d’urgence pour contenir la pandémie de COVID-19 et limiter son impact. Le Ministère de l’Agriculture, tout en contribuant à l’élaboration du plan d’action global du gouvernement, a insisté sur la spécificité du secteur agricole et le risque qui pèse sur le pays en cas d’une mauvaise production à la sortie de cette campagne agricole. 
La situation d’invasion acridienne a été préoccupante au cours de l’année 2020 à l’Est et au Nord-Est du Tchad. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du plan d’action régional d’urgence acridienne (juin-août 2020), la FAO et le Ministère de l'Agriculture à travers l’Agence nationale de lutte antiacridienne (ANLA) au Tchad, ont déployé un hélicoptère destiné à renforcer les opérations de prospection/lutte. Le déploiement de l’hélicoptère a renforcé le dispositif déjà mis en place par le gouvernement sur un itinéraire de 19 868 km.
La situation acridienne demeure relativement calme sur l’ensemble du pays. Cependant, des ailés solitaires, isolés, immatures, en cours de maturation et matures, à faible densité ont été observés autour d’Arada, Kalait, Bahaï, Fada et le sud de Mao. En outre, des larves de 2ème et 6ème stades sont présents entre Kalait et Fada ainsi qu’à Beurkia près de Kouba Olanga. Cette situation est issue des activités de reproduction à petite échelle qui a commencé dans ces localités de la fin du mois d’aout à la fin du mois de septembre 2020. 
En octobre, une reproduction à petite échelle a eu lieu et des larves solitaires de tous les stades étaient présentes dans les zones centrales de Beurkia, dans le centre et à l’Ouest de Fada dans le Nord-Est. Des ailées solitaires immatures et matures en faibles effectifs étaient disséminés principalement entre Beurkia, Kalait et Fada et dans une moindre mesure dans l’Ouest près de Mao et dans l’Est près de la frontière Soudanaise et Iriba. Au cours de la dernière semaine, des adultes transiens ont été observés en accouplement près de Fada. Cette situation avec l’apparition des acridiens adultes, pourrait menacer la sécurité alimentaire.
Le gouvernement s’est fixé comme objectif de produire cette année environ 3 132 642 tonnes de céréales pour couvrir les besoins céréaliers de la population en 2021. Il est également prévu de produire 1 881 546 tonnes pour d’autres produits vivriers (arachide, sésame, manioc, taro, igname, etc.). La production céréalière prévisionnelle de la campagne agricole 2020/2021 est estimée à 2 901 683 tonnes. Elle est presque équivalente à celle de l’année dernière (-0,8%), mais enregistre une légère hausse de 3,7 % par rapport à la moyenne quinquennale. Toutes les spéculations ont enregistré des hausses à l’exception du maïs qui est resté équivalent. Cette légère augmentation cache cependant des disparités entre les provinces. Toutefois, ce niveau de production est en baisse de 7,4% de l’objectif fixé par le Ministère pour cette campagne.

project_name: Supporting early recovery efforts in the Northwest, Southwest, Littoral and West Regions
project_objective:
The objective/outcome of this project is to support vulnerable people among IDPs, returnees and host communities affected by the NWSW crisis in the Northwest, Southwest, Littoral and West Regions to be more resilient to environmental, social and economic shocks through the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus.

Output 1: Improve economic capacity of vulnerable persons and households
Activity 1.1 Strengthen economic capacity of vulnerable people like youth and women among IDPs, returnees and host communities through labour-intensive activities like cash for work for community recovery/development
Activity 1.2 Rehabilitate/construct basic economic infrastructure (e.g. boreholes and markets)

Output 2: Promote sustainable empowerment of vulnerable people through multi-sectoral and inclusive economic recovery activities with the environmental respect
Activity 2.1 Provide training on economic integration such as technical expertise, business management, transversal issues of life and environment protection/respect
Activity 2.2 Provide inputs including kits and capital for sustainable economic activities
Activity 2.3 Establish/strengthen community savings systems
Activity 2.4 Strengthen the capacity of socio-economic institutions such as training centres and market management structures

Output 3: Strengthen institutional, community and individual capacity to improve resilience and to Promote risk prevention and management
Activity 3.1 Strengthen the capacity of key stakeholders such as local authorities, community and religious leaders and associations of youth, women, farmers, herders and IDPs in risk prevention and crisis management
Activity 3.2 Strengthen the capacity of individuals in communities for risk prevention and crisis management through training, awareness raising events, local initiatives, debates and forums

Main target: vulnerable people like youth (18-34 years old) and women among IDPs, returnees and host communities, and authorities such as government officials and religious/community leaders

project_name: Shelter / NFI Support to Rohingya Refugees
project_objective:
Bangladesh is currently hosting more than one million stateless Rohingya refugees accommodated in overcrowded refugee camps in Cox's Bazar District (CBD) and highly vulnerable to landslides, tropical cyclones, flash-flooding, and communicable disease outbreak. The monsoon season continues to impact the Rohingya refugees, with heavy rains and strong winds severely diminishing quality of life. 

Next Year AMAN has the initiatives to enable the Rohingya refugees and vulnerable host  Communities in Cox's Bazar through providing Emergency shelter assistance, Provision of HH level solar lights, Provision of NFI (Floor Mat, Mosquito Net, Bucket, Mug, Plate, Bowl, Glass, Blankets, Sweater, Shawl, Socks) and above all involving women, older people and other forms of gender diverse population reaching to 17,016 individuals (Whole Camp 17). To reach these targets, AMAN’s estimated budget is $888,248.

AMAN has experience in assisting refugees with shelter and NFI support since 2017. Next year AMAN is planning to build 40 two storey MTS based on the approved design and based on the site plan coordinated with UNHCR, camp 17.  AMAN always emphasizes on capacity building trainings and its concerned staff has already attended in different training by the initiatives of Shelter /NFI, other sector focal and stakeholders that is the strength of AMAN to achieve the targeted objectives to ensure project sustainability. Moreover, AMAN’s field staff will be trained in PSEA to ensure proper protection mainstreaming.

Systematic process of program Monitoring using participatory methods is what AMAN will do next year to deliver the project and to ensure beneficiaries inclusion in the project design and implementation. Before intervention any projects, we will conduct baseline survey, FGD, KII, etc. Collect and analyses and use disaggregated data and analysis on gender, age and diversity and equally consult with women, girls and marginalized groups, including during assessments and in the overall response monitoring. Overall, AMAN will coordinate with UNHCR Shelter Focal point in camp 17 for the emergency assistance and other shelter activities for proper implementation, monitoring and supervision.

project_name: Mejora de las condiciones de vida de las personas vulnerables de Venezuela a través de la provisión de alojamiento, servicios básicos y protección.
project_objective:
El proyecto visa contribuir a mejorar las condiciones de vida y un acceso seguro a bienes y servicios esenciales a las personas en movilidad, incluyendo personas retornadas en el contexto de la pandemia COVID-19.

La Plataforma Regional de coordinación Inter agencial para refugiados y migrantes estimaba en abril 2020 que 5.1 millones de personas migrantes y refugiadas venezolanas han abandonado el país en busca de asistencia humanitaria, protección, acceso a los servicios básicos y oportunidades laborales, y que la gran mayoría se ha establecido en países de la región. 

Con la pandemia del COVID-19 y el impacto en sus condiciones y medios de vida se ha observado un aumento de venezolanos retornando a su país. Desde el cierre de la frontera en marzo 2020, alrededor de 130.000 venezolanos han retornado y el protocolo sanitario define el cumplimento de una cuarentena preventiva en los centros de atención a los retornados y personas en movilidad.

En septiembre se han empezado a reportar un aumento de venezolanos que se dirigen hacia la frontera, y al no tener medios de transporte lo hacen a pie y esperan cruzar la frontera por caminos irregulares. Se ha observado cambios al respecto del grupo familiar que incluyen personas adultas, jóvenes, niños y niñas y los elevados riesgos de protección que enfrentan. 

El proyecto fortalecerá y ampliará la red de centros de alojamientos temporales, actividad iniciada en 2019 en los estados fronterizos de Zulia, Táchira y Apure y en 2020 incluimos estados en el oriente del país, Bolívar y Sucre. Para 2021 OIM ampliará la acción a los estados Barinas y Falcón. En 2021, la OIM diversificará el tipo de asistencia en dichos centros, con el fin de cubrir las necesidades humanitarias y de protección de las personas vulnerables. 

Para ello, la OIM implementará su respuesta en 14   centros  de alojamiento temporal ubicados en Zulia, Sucre, Táchira, Apure y Bolívar, Barinas y Falcón proveyendo una gama completa de diferentes servicios a las personas vulnerables. Esto consiste en la rehabilitación de la infraestructura de los centros, priorizando los trabajos de agua y saneamiento, suministro de equipos, la asistencia en forma de alojamiento y el acceso a servicios básicos como alimentos, instalaciones de saneamiento, y distribución de NFIs (Kits de Higiene). Asimismo, se incrementará la capacidad de los socios encargados de la gestión de albergues con el fin de garantizar los estándares mínimos de asistencia.

Además, OIM trabajará para abordar las necesidades de protección de los venezolanos en movilidad en dichos centros mediante la distribución de información que salva vidas y actividades de conciencia sobre los riesgos y la prevención de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG), trata y otros riesgos de explotación y abusos, así como orientación e información sobre el acceso a la documentación. OIM también facilitará vías de referencia a los servicios especializados disponibles en las zonas donde se encuentren los centros.
 La OIM también distribuirá NFI´s (Kits de Higiene) con artículos para la prevención y control de infecciones en los centros de alojamiento temporal como a personas en comunidades de origen y de acogida.
OIM también proveerá asistencia individual a hogares más vulnerables, con la distribución de NFI’s en las comunidades priorizadas. 

Kits de higiene y kits institucionales serán distribuidos en centros de alojamiento temporales manejados por OIM y, eventualmente, los centros de atención a los retornados y personas en movilidad, y en centros de salud/ambulatorios para que de esta manera se pueda garantizar la sanitización de estos espacios, así como también se hará distribución equipos de protección para el personal encargado de la atención en centros de salud seleccionados (PPE).

project_name: Fortalecimiento de habilidades socioemocionales de jóvenes en riesgo de abandono escolar,  garantizando inclusión y permanencia educativa e inserción socio laboral
project_objective:
Las intervenciones de la Emergencia se han enfocado en la primera infancia y en la niñez, lo cual ha supuesto desatención del joven. Fe y Alegría y Asociación Civil Huellas unen capacidades para intervenir educativamente en Estados priorizados por el PRH. 
En Fe y Alegría está una apuesta por la formación técnica de adolescentes y jóvenes, es por ello que, de 121 centros educativos, 87 (71%) atienden educación media técnica, desarrollando competencias específicas en cinco especialidades y 20 menciones en las áreas de salud, agropecuaria, industrial, servicios y artes. 

Sin embargo, los estudios del BID permiten conocer la demanda de habilidades no sólo técnicas sino también socio emocionales que los empleadores hacen. Es por ello que en la educación técnica es vital incorporar aprendizajes en torno a: inteligencia emocional, liderazgo, resolución de problemas, trabajo en equipo, pensamiento flexible, creatividad y emprendimiento; que incentiven personalidades productivas y faciliten a los jóvenes construir su proyecto vital, lograr la inserción socio laboral y participar como ciudadanos en el desarrollo sustentable.

Con este proyecto, desde el enfoque de derechos , las dos organizaciones fortalecemos habilidades socioemocionales y técnicas en 27.667 jóvenes de 11 a 19 años, en riesgo de abandono escolar, de escuelas técnicas de 97 instituciones de Fe y Alegría de 14 Estados, garantizando su inclusión, permanencia educativa e inserción laboral, por medio de estrategias presenciales y on line. Pero, además, instalamos capacidades en esas instituciones a través de la formación de jóvenes (27667), docentes (776), jóvenes-guías (388), personal administrativo (194), adultos significativos (13834) y en los beneficiarios indirectos proyectados de la campaña musical (110 mil personas); todos ellos en conjunto construyen una red de ciudadanos con expectativas, habilidades y horizonte común, motivados a participar en procesos de fortalecimiento educativos comunitarios.

project_name: Apoyo en Manejo de Información al Foro de ONGHI
project_objective:
Apoyo para las organizaciones del Foro de ONGHI en el manejo de información y análisis de datos para la respuesta en los contextos de desastres, conflicto y desplazamiento y la respuesta a la COVID-19. El apoyo se basa en orientar y facilitar el manejo de información y análisis de datos del FONGHI. Este apoyo incluye un oficial de manejo de información (IMO) de soporte directo para las organizaciones del Foro, así como una dedicación del resto del equipo de iMMAP en SIG, desarrollo web, análisis de datos, evaluaciones, capacitaciones y coordinación.

El apoyo en Manejo de información al incluye:
• Apoyo en la recolección, procesamiento, sistematización, y análisis de datos primarios y secundarios para la gestión de información.
• Generación de reportes informativos y periódicos de acuerdo con las actividades del Foro. 
• Productos de información de acuerdo con la respuesta y alcances establecidos con el Foro que pueden incluir: bases de datos con información secundaria relevante, dashboards, mapas, visualizaciones, infografías y desarrollo de herramientas digitales de información
• Acompañamiento técnico en las evaluaciones sectoriales e intersectoriales
• Acompañamiento al Foro y sus socios para el reporte y monitoreo estructurado, sistemático y de calidad de las actividades en el 345W, incluyendo el aseguramiento de calidad y rendición de cuentas.
• Acompañamiento al Foro  y sus socios para el reporte y monitoreo estructurado que lleve al aseguramiento de calidad y rendición de cuentas en la respuesta, creando medios para la captura de información (opiniones, visiones e inconformidades) por parte de las comunidades.
• Capacitaciones para los miembros del Foro y sus socios implementadores en los pasos de la cadena del flujo de la información, incluyendo aseguramiento de calidad y rendición de cuentas.
• Apoyo e incidencia en la determinación del HRP 2022, esto incluye identificación de vacíos de información y brechas, metodologías para el cálculo de población objetivo, metas y consolidación de indicadores.
• Uso de herramientas innovadoras y métodos alternativos de información para mejorar la respuesta humanitaria y la coordinación dentro del cluster.

project_name: Support to Saida Governmental Hospital in the COVID-19 response, engagement of local communities to improve preventive healthcare and support to outreach workers
project_objective:
The proposed action is a COVID-19 emergency response intervention and contributes to the allocation strategy in providing life-saving emergency assistance to vulnerable populations in Lebanon by supporting COVID-19 case management and improving community engagement in the governorate of Saida. The intervention complies with the overall strategy of the Health sector under the ERP 2021-2022, namely to provide essential short-term support to meet vulnerable people’s critical needs in terms of health care, support the response capacity of the Lebanese health system in coping with the COVID-19 emergency, and enhance assistance for migrants.
The proposal is based on assessments and visits conducted by DPNA in Saida and by ARCS in Saida Governmental Hospital (SGH) between January and June 2021, with the full support of the hospital’s staff and administration. Visits and assessments have identified key priorities and operational practices to better contribute to the overall project objective. Specifically, the project will provide SGH with medical equipment and PPEs for COVID-19 case management and will empower and protect vulnerable population of Saida through community awareness activities on preventive healthcare practices and COVID-19 immunization, including support to vaccine registration, mapping of services and referral mechanisms. In addition, the project intends to address the energy crisis and to contribute to Objective 2 under the ERP (Health) ""Support health facilities to maintain operations during the ongoing emergency context"" by providing SGH with a solar panels system, which will sustain critical wards and laboratories, including the dialysis center, vaccination and PCR labs. 
The proposal, closely coordinated with the MoPH, UNHCR and WHO, is in line with the priorities defined by the “COVID-19 Lebanon Appeal” issued by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs in July 2020, and contributes to the Sector objectives, insofar as it focuses on supporting public hospital through the provision of equipment and on strengthening health promotion and community outreach on relevant health topics. By supporting the hospital through medical equipment and PPEs provision, the project increases the preparedness and capacity of SGH to safely cope with new waves of COVID-19 while contributing to the smooth functioning of the remaining wards and units operating in the facility. The equipment procured for COVID-19 response will then serve the hospital’s needs in the post COVID-19 phase and will increase the quality of services for vulnerable population accessing SGH, which reflects the added value of the project in terms of sustainability. In parallel, the project will contribute to lower the COVID-19 pressure on public hospitals by supporting the immunization campaign, and diffusing information and practices on preventive healthcare. Activities under objective 3 and 4 are fully covered by LHF and will be implemented between 01/08/2021 and 31/01/2022. The activity foreseen under objective 2 is requiring extra funding and intends to be implemented between 1/02/2022 and 31/05/2022. Thus, the overall project is already funded by 57%.
The project will reach a total of 8,249 direct beneficiaries, including around 4,000 hospitalised patients, 249 hospital's employees and additional 4,000 vulnerable individuals (1000 vulnerable households) of Saida governorate.

project_name: Humanitarian WASH Response in Somaliland and Puntland Regions, Somalia
project_objective:
Unreliable access to a temporary and/or inadequate WASH facility remains an important feature of the humanitarian landscape in Somalia. In 2020, over 4.6 million people (1.16 million IDPs and 3.36 million host communities) don’t have sufficient quantity of water and adequate sanitation (HNO 2020). This dire situation is even worsened by the COVID19 pandemic which require more water for frequent handwashing for prevention and containment. Schools in Somalia are reopening and due to COVID19, a number of schools are requesting urgent water supply for both students consumption and to support frequent handwashing. 

The water supply coverage in Somalia is strongly dependent on rainfall performance. In the last two rainy seasons namely 2019 Dayr and 2020 Gu, the performance of rains has improved slightly (SWALIM/FAO). From 2017 onwards, the water coverage has shown slight improvement due to improved rain performance. The National WASH Cluster estimates 59% as having sufficient drinking water with 66% of those with access walk less than 15 minutes for a water point and 20% having challenges to access the minimum quantity of safe water. (JMCNA ). 48% access their own improved latrines, while 52% use either unimproved latrines or practicing open defecation (22%) posing a huge public health risk. Furthermore, 2% used soap with water at latrines, 52% use soap at household level while 40% use other substitute for handwashing. 45% of women/girls access MHM materials. 
On the other hand, Oxfam needs assessment conducted late 2019 in Sool, Sanaag and Togdheer regions indicates that over 40% of both IDP and host communities rely on purchasing water from commercial trucks. There is no well-organized and reliable government data that shows the coverage of water, sanitation, and hygiene in Somalia. In December 2019 and January 2020, Oxfam and FAO/SWALIM conducted a WASH inventory in all regions of Somaliland. The inventory focused on sustainable and strategic water sources in the country including boreholes, springs, and protected shallow wells. The functionality of these sources is critical. However, the current functionality rate is estimated to be much below 70% and decreases as the stress level goes up during the drought period. The analysis of the final report is not yet finalized but expected to inform the sector on ways to increase functionality and reduce interruption of services. The COVID19 outbreak has increased the need for water to support frequent handwashing practices and this will further stress the few existing water sources. 
People living in the riverine areas in Somalia and other areas adjusted to seasonal rivers are affected by floods. The worst most recent flash-floods were reported from the Shabelle river basin particularly in Beletwayn town, Hiraan Region, and Qardho town of Puntland State. Until the end of May 2020, over 412,000 people are displaced by the floods (UNOCHA, Flood Bulletin). The capacity of regional states and the federal government is limited only to response instead of constructing large scale flood protection structures. 

Somalia is one of the worst hit Horn of African countries by COVID19. So far, over to 3,864 cases and 99 deaths are recorded. However, the figures are believed to be much higher since testing capacity is limited to only few major towns. The situation in Somalia is different compared to other countries with a strong governance system in the horn of Africa. Only 31% of people in Somalia reported having a functional handwashing facility with soap (WASH Cluster, March 2020). This estimate is based on an assessment conducted before the Covid19 lockdown. The federal government and humanitarian agencies confirmed the increased market price of soap and other detergents and 11% contraction of national GDP in the country. Covid19 prevention requires frequent handwashing and social distancing which both are difficult in Somalia context.

Women and girls continued to report protection-related risk

project_name: Assistance alimentaire et protection des moyens d’existence des ménages affectés des régions du Centre Nord et du Sahel.
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso a connu ses premières attaques des groupes armés non étatiques (GANE) en 2015. Depuis 2016, le pays est soumis à une crise humanitaire sans précédent avec une projection qui sera maintenue voire exacerbée en 2021 par les facteurs principaux : (I) l’insécurité et la prolifération des GANE principalement dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, de l’Est et de la Boucle du Mouhoun qui entrainent des morts d’hommes, des déplacements massifs de population civile ; (ii) La crise sécuritaire vient se greffer à une crise alimentaire devenue chronique pour laquelle l’Etat a du mal à trouver une réponse structurante. Les moyens de subsistance des populations déplacées interne ont été affectés ; les populations vivant dans les zones affectées par la crise souffrent des restrictions d’accès à la terre pour la conduite des activités agro-sylvo-pastorales Le cadre harmonisés de Novembre 2020 estime la population ayant besoin d’une assistance immédiate (Phase 3 à 5) à 2 020 039 soit une augmentation de plus 800 000 personnes par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. 
Ces populations qui représentent 9,2% de la population totale analysée sont concentrées dans les régions du Centre-Nord (25,0%), du Sahel (24,6%), de l’Est (16,8%) et du Nord (8,5%). Elles sont constituées en partie de populations déplacées à cause de l’insécurité civile qui les a contraints à abandonner leurs terres de culture, leurs bétails et autres moyens d’existence.
Objectif : couvrir les besoins alimentaires et protéger les moyens d’existence des ménages affectés par la crise sécuritaire et alimentaire des régions du Centre-Nord et du Sahel

project_name: Appui aux ménages pastoraux et agropastoraux (communautés hotes et des PDIs ) faisant face à l'insécurtié alimentaire, nutritionnelle et pastorale structurelle
project_objective:
Le projet a pour objectif général d'apporter une assistance sociale aux populations structurellement en insécurité alimentaire, nutritionnelle et pastorale indépendamment du statut résidentiel des chefs de ménages. Cette assistance sera intégrée de manière cohérente avec l'évolution du contexte particulièrement le fonctionnement des marchés, les principaux moyens d'existence des populations, la situation sécuritaire et les bonnes pratiques locales. Cette approche permettra de faire le pont entre l'humanitaire, le développement et la paix. L'assistance touchera principalement les couches vulnérables dont les capacités endogènes ne suffisent pas pour satisfaire leurs besoins alimentaires, nutritionnels et pastoraux sans recourir à des stratégies de survie néfastes. Ces ménages vivent généralement dans un cercle vicieux de pauvreté et d'insécurité alimentaire/nutritionnel et pastorale dont ils ne sauraient se relever dans un appui extérieur.  
Spécifiquement le projet vise à:
- Sauver des vies en apportant une assistance alimentaire, nutritionnelle  et pastorale d'urgence en nature ou à travers un programme de transfert monétaire selon le degré de fonctionnement des marchés, le niveau sécuritaire et les préférences des populations à près de 5000 ménages vulnérables avec une discrimination positive pour ceux dirigés par des femmes;
- Proteger et renforcer les moyens d'existence des couches vulnérables à travers un appui en intrants agricoles et zootechniques ainsi en noyaux reproducteurs de petits ruminants de 50% des ménages ayant reçu l'assistance d'urgence.
Cette assistance sera donnée proportionnellement à la taille du ménages ou au nombre de bétail appartenant aux ménages cibles et couvrira au moins 80% des besoins alimentaires des humains et de leur bétail afin de réduire les risques de mortalité du bétail, de décapitalisation ou d’hypothèque des actifs productifs. En outre, elle envisage d'amorcer le relevement des ménages les plus vulnérables via un appui en intrants et en noyaux de reproducteurs de petits ruminats. Ceci permettra de protéger leurs principaux moyens d’existence et de favoriser leur relèvement.

project_name: Respuesta en salud para el acceso de servicios de atención a poblaciones vulnerables de seis departamentos del país.
project_objective:
En noviembre de 2020, la República de Honduras fue impactada directamente por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, que ocasionaron daños de diversa magnitud e importancia en 16 de los 18 departamentos del país, afectando alrededor de 4 700 000 de personas, obligando a la evacuación de 363 762 personas, y el alojamiento en albergues de 172 798 personas, con un recuento final de 99 personas fallecidas. El Valle de Sula, en el departamento de Cortés, localizado al norte del país, fue la zona del país más afectada, junto con los departamentos de Atlántida, Colón, Gracias a Dios, El Paraíso, Santa Bárbara y Yoro. De forma simultánea, el país también ha sido afectada por la pandemia de la COVID-19 y por la epidemia de dengue. De acuerdo con el análisis de daños y necesidades del sector salud posterior al impacto de las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, del total de personas afectadas, 500 000 personas, aproximadamente, tenían acceso limitado o carecían de servicios de salud, debido a los daños a la infraestructura de la red de servicios de salud. Más de 393 establecimientos de salud fueron afectados y al menos 10 reportaron pérdidas totales en el equipamiento de la cadena de frío, equipamientos, insumos y vacunas. 
En 2021, persisten personas con necesidades en salud, en particular en regiones postergadas e impactadas por las tormentas tropicales. 
En este sentido, el proyecto pretende fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta del sector salud mediante acciones de rehabilitación de los servicios afectados por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota y además reforzar la respuesta ante la epidemia de dengue y COVID-19 en el país, para beneficiar a 100 000 personas con necesidades en salud, incidiendo en la reducción de indicadores de morbilidad y mortalidad, así como en las brechas de género, edad, discapacidad y etnicidad en la atención.

project_name: Improving the nutrition security of Lebanese and migrant caregivers and young children through provision of preventive and treatment nutrition services
project_objective:
This project aims to address the increasing nutrition insecurity conditions in the country, in particular those affecting the most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant communities. The response of AAH under the Nutrition Sector Response is divided into interventions that cover both prevention and treatment of malnutrition. In order to ensure that services aiming to prevent and treat malnutrition complement each other, the response entails improving nutrition knowledge, in addition to implementing preventive and treatment nutrition services, alongside provision of nutrition supplies. As AAH always aims to achieve amplified impact of nutrition interventions, especially in the current context, AAH will also support the most vulnerable households, based on in-depth assessments, with multi-purpose cash assistance under its Food Security Response, especially households with Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) and children U5 that may be more nutritionally vulnerable. AAH will also dedicate efforts to ensure that multi-sectoral needs expressed by targeted communities are actively referred and followed up, especially that impact on nutrition outcomes are amplified when WASH, food security, protection, GBV, health, especially mental health, are simultaneously addressed. Interventions under this program will target communities in Beirut, Bekaa, and South governorates, though it is important to note that not all interventions included here below will be implemented in all 3 governorates concomitantly, but depending on the needs, context, as well as AAH's capacity.
Overall, 2500 caregivers and 2000 infants and children will be targeted, inclusive of LHF activities. As AAH is newly targeting migrant communities and given that the proportion of PLW, infants and children is not high among this community and more importantly in AAH's areas of intervention, a maximum of 5% of the targets will dedicated to support migrant communities.
In order to address malnutrition prevention, prioritizing pregnant and lactating women and caregivers of young children with nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and hygiene promotion and counseling is a priority in modalities that meet the needs and concerns of the communities supported, whether individually or in groups, in health facilities or in the community, all while mobilizing the community. To complement these interventions, ensuring that caregivers are empowered to assess and follow-up on their U5 children's malnutrition status is as crucial. For this reason, training teams on the use of Family Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) & in return, training caregivers to use this approach will be prioritized. Caregivers will also be supported to seek timely medical attention in the nearest malnutrition treatment centers accordingly. Both PLW and children U5 will also be supported with nutrition supplies that aim to boost their energy, vitamin and mineral intake, respectively. In parallel, AAH staff and stakeholders, including health facilities, will be supported to create and maintain enabling environments that protect, promote and support breastfeeding and optimal feeding practices. For this reason, they will be trained on IYCF principles and oriented on the implementation of Law 47/2008 that aim to ensure proper use of breastmilk substitutes, while facilities will also be supported to create safe, private spaces to support breastfeeding. Last but not least, as UNICEF will be planning to conduct a training to support hospitals to provide quality and timely in-patient treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition treatment, AAH is planning to complement this initiative but coaching, supporting and supervising three of the targeted hospitals to maintain these quality services and strengthen the referral pathway from malnutrition treatment centers to in-patient treatment as needed, as well as engage the community.
All interventions prioritized by AAH are in line with the ERP's Nutrition Sector's response.

project_name: Nutrition prevention for 1000 migrant children in Beirut and Mount Lebanon
project_objective:
This project is part of the LHF-funded food security and nutrition project entitled “Food security for 665 migrant households and nutrition prevention for 1000 migrant children in Beirut and Mount Lebanon”, under the 2021 first standard allocation. This is a summary of the nutrition component only.
The food security component targets 665 migrant households in Beirut and Mount Lebanon (collectively considered to be ‘Greater Beirut’) with monthly dry food rations as well as local produced, seasonal and long shelf-life fresh vegetables in order to ensure the best nutrition outcomes.
All migrant households with children who are in the 665 households targeted by the food security component will automatically be eligible for nutrition education (roughly 366 children below the age of 5); an additional set of households with 634 children will be identified through migrant-led initiatives to reach the target of 1000 migrant children for nutrition education.
Malnutrition of 1000 migrant children aged 6-59 months will be prevented through the provision of micro-nutrient supplements to ensure adequate nutrition, whether or not they are also receiving fresh and dry food through food distributions. 
Early detection and referral for treatment of moderate or severe malnutrition, with strong referral pathways to referent malnutrition treatment centres in nearby PHCs (Bourj Hammoud and Mazraa) will be done through the family MUAC approach; targeting the mothers and caregivers of 1000 migrant children aged 6-59 months. 
IYCF awareness raising will be provided to pregnant and lactating women and the mothers and caregivers of children under 23 months, in close coordination with IOCC for both training and accessing lactation specialists.
All households with children aged 6-59 months that receive food through the food security component will also receive cooking demonstrations tailored to cultural food and cuisine preferences, bearing in mind that the targeted households come from 22 different nationalities. Cooking demonstrations will be delivered by migrants from these diverse nationalities.
Information, Education and Communications materials that underpin nutrition education, such as IYCF counselling cards, flyers, recipe booklets and general information on malnutrition and how to screen for it will be translated into selected migrant languages. All are already available in Arabic, most in English, and some in other languages; Concern will ensure they are all translated into Bengali, Singhalese, Amharic, English and French. Additional IEC materials on vaccinations, COVID-19, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse will also be translated into these languages. All translated materials will be made available to any organisation who need them, trough the relevant working group.
UNICEF will provide the micro-nutrient supplements, MUAC tapes and IEC materials. The project is closely coordinated with the nutrition working group, IOCC and the Ministry of Public Health
This project is embedded within Concern’s strategic approach to working with migrant workers in Greater Beirut, which combines addressing immediate and basic needs with long term efforts to address the underlying and structural causes of migrant vulnerability, and works with and through migrant-led initiatives in a migrant-community based, bottom-up approach. 
The project will work with 9 members of three Migrant-Led Initiatives (Mesewet, Together Forever and African United Communities in Lebanon), and focus on building their capacity in nutrition education, accountability to affected populations and referrals; ensuring benefits that last beyond the duration of the project.

project_name: Plan de respuesta humanitaria ante las necesidades básicas de las personas desplazadas de sus hogares en Honduras (5 meses)
project_objective:
Entre el 01 y el 16 de noviembre del 2020, Honduras se vio afectada por dos fenómenos naturales, el primero la depresión tropical ETA y días más tarde el huracán IOTA, que impactó como Tormenta Tropical. Ambos generaron fuertes impactos en diversas áreas del país, como consecuencia más de 400,000 personas fueron desplazadas a un albergue temporal, llegando a habilitarse más de 1,000 a nivel nacional. La zona norte y Atlántico del país reportaron los mayores daños. El Valle de Sula 
(localizado en el noroccidente del país) compuesto por 18 municipalidades fue gravemente afectado, alrededor de 2 millones de personas viviendo en la zona sufrieron fuertes inundaciones y la mayoría de ellos se abocaron a un albergue. 
 En este contexto, el proyecto se centrará en dos actividades principales a) brindar apoyo a las personas desplazadas que vivieron o que siguen habitando en albergues oficiales y no oficiales, asentamientos espontáneos o similares. Esto con el fin de procurar un servicio de protección y asistencia humanitaria de forma digna, asegurando los enfoques de género, edad y diversidad. b) Incentivar a las familias afectadas por medio de transferencias de efectivo multipropósito considerando la gran necesidad existente en insumos básicos, materiales para el hogar o costo de renta de un hogar temporal. Esta segunda actividad tiene como objetivo promover la elección y la dignidad en los beneficiarios, utilizando las capacidades y la autonomía de las familias afectadas para que sean agentes de cambio en su propia recuperación. Se pretende que mediante la participación de los beneficiarios en la identificación y mejoramiento básico de las infraestructuras comunitarias que sirven de albergues, se logre crear resiliencia en ellos y prepararlos para enfrentar la temporada de emergencia, considerando las diferentes necesidades de género, edad, discapacidad y pertenencia étnica de las personas. El proyecto pondrá gran énfasis en la premisa que estas poblaciones afectadas están en el centro de su propia recuperación.

project_name: Provision of Non-Food Items (NFIs) and Shelter Assistance to Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Syria
project_objective:
Palestine refugees continue to struggle after ten years of con ict. As stated in 2021 Humanitarian needs overview (HNO), it is estimated that sixty percent have been displaced at least once and 40% remain in protracted displacement, with Yarmouk, Ein El-Tal and Dera’a Palestine refugee camps still largely in ruins. A number of Palestine refugees have been spontaneously returning to these camps and to other places of habitual residence, despite the challenging conditions. UNRWA estimates that 418,000 Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance in 2021. Many among them struggle to secure basic shelter and NFI need, and will be supported by UNRWA through this project, as part of the 2021 Humanitarian response plan

NFIs (including mats, mattresses and blankets) will be provided to approximately 27,000 Palestine refugees affected by shocks and emergencies, including newly displaced persons and those directly impacted by new or increased hostilities. Families and individuals spontaneously returning to newly accessible areas that were severely affected by the confliict and/or lacking basic services will also be eligible for NFIs based on assessed needs. Cash for winterization will be provided to 187,000 individuals (55,000 Palestine refugee households).

Small-scale shelter repair initiatives will be implemented in selected locations to support 1,7000  of the most vulnerable refugees whose shelters have been damaged during the con ict (about 500 shelters). The targeted locations would be Ein El Tal, Yarmouk and Dera’a, Palestine Refugee Camps depending on the return rates and our capacity to secure the necessary approvals are secured. This will contribute to protecting the most vulnerable while preserving their resilience, decreasing the burden created by rent on their ability to provide for their basic needs. A self-help approach will be applied. This modality directly involves the families whose shelters are being repaired, respecting their dignity and generating employment within the local economy, whilst supporting cost effective shelter repair. Each family will receive on average US$ 3,000 for their shelter repair.

project_name: Preventing and Responding to GBV in Borno and Yobe States, North-East Nigeria
project_objective: The project aims at ensuring that SGBV survivors have access to essential services, including medical, psychosocial and livelihood support. The project includes an explicit focus on strengthening capacity within civil society - including but not limited to CBOs, community-based committees, schools, youth and women groups, religious groups/associations – and governmental counterparts to mitigate risk factors and coordinate a survivor-centred response which includes early identification, timely and well-coordinated referral to specialized services. The project seeks to provide survivors and people at risk - with particular attention to women, girls and boys – with life skills and access to income generating activities to help establish support networks and livelihood opportunities.

project_name: Strengthening treatment and preventive services of acute malnutrition and provision of nutrition SBCC in Yobe and Borno State
project_objective:
The project contributes to the prevention of Severe Acute Malnutrition and provision of nutrition SBCC, in Yobe and Borno States, among children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) by ensuring adequate food intake, improved diet diversification, early detection of SAM and referral, improved Infant and Young Children Feeding Practices (IYCF).

In addition the project intends to contribute to the nutrition sector of HRP for Nigeria by:
- Strengthen the quality and scale of preventative nutrition services for most vulnerable groups through supplementary feeding activities, appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, micronutrient supplementation and optimal maternal nutrition.
- Improve access to quality curative nutrition services through the most appropriate modalities, systematic identification, referral, and treatment of acutely malnourished cases in collaboration with the health sector to enhance sustainability.
- Reinforce appropriate coordination with other sectors and strengthen situation monitoring by undertaking joint assessments and analysis, while strengthening integrated response that mainstreams protection.
- Capacity building and training for MoH health workers in Yobe and Borno and community mobilizers in all the target areas.

project_name: Enhancing the resilience of conflict-affected children and adolescents through access to educational services and psychosocial support in Yobe and Borno States, North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen the resilience of  20,000 conflict-affected children and adolescents by providing equitable access to quality and conflict-sensitive educational services. In order to respond to the cumulative disruptions triggered by insurgency, seasonal natural disasters and COVID19 pandemic on the educational systems of Borno and Yobe States, the proposed intervention seeks to ensure the continuation of basic education by targeting out-of-school IDPs, returnees and host community children/youth in the following target areas: Maiduguri (Borno State), Damaturu and Geidam LGAs (Yobe State).
	To achieve the abovementioned goal, COOPI proposes a holistic intervention which converges the provision of formal/informal educational programs and child protection services with the construction/rehabilitation of learning spaces and WASH facilities. More specifically, the project will focus on: I. improving children’s access to alternative education programs to enable them to reintegrate in the formal school system; II. training teachers on risk education and psychosocial first aid in order to recognize signs of distress and other protection concerns in children to refer them to appropriate professionals; III. training youth on vocational/entrepreneurship skills and providing start-up kits to enhance their future employment opportunities; IV. construction/rehabilitation/equipment of Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS)/Classrooms with provision of didactic/recreational kits, schools’ furniture and WASH facilities, with a special focus on the needs of girls and children with disabilities; V. capacity-building sessions for communities, School-based Management Committees (SBMCs) and Government Ministries and Agencies on school management and risk reduction planning. 
	The proposed activities are meant to be carried out through a proper mainstreaming of cross-cutting issues of gender, protection and inclusion within the EiE. A child and youth protection-safeguarding approach will be prioritized to protect their rights from abuse and exploitation. An integrated approach to EiE and CP will be promoted in all areas of operation, providing psychosocial support for most vulnerable children as well as COVID19 awareness campaigns, including the disinfection of schools. The purpose is to create a safe, inclusive and protective learning environment able to ensure the physic-mental wellbeing of learners and educational personnel in a manner that does not contravene the social distancing protocol and COVID19 protection measures.
	In order to ensure more harmonized and impactful outputs, the response will be implemented in close coordination with the ERL, WASH, Child Protection (including GBV) sectors, meaningfully engaging with the Ministry of Education, State Universal Basic Education (SUBEB) and State Ministry of Youth, Sport and Social Development. Equally relevant, the action will build on the best practices and learnt lessons from COOPI’s previous EiE/CP projects funded by AICS and OFDA in 2017 in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC), Borno State.
	In light of the above, the proposed intervention is deeply aligned with the 2020 Nigeria HRP Specific Objective 1.2 (to ensure access to quality basic services, such as education and health), the Yobe State Socio-Economic Reform Agenda (YOSERA) as well as with Borno State’s 25 Year Development Framework. In line with the Grand Bargain, the program is designed to be delivered through the engagement of local entities, thus enhancing the localization approach, the government educational systems’ strengthening and overall communal psychosocial wellbeing.

project_objective:
