project_name: Emergency life saving and quality education for conflict affected IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable host communities in Warrap, Lakes and Jonglei states of South Sudan.
project_objective:
Peace Corps proposes an emergency education response programme focused on provision of life saving safe and quality protective education interventions to school going children(3-17 years) in Jonglei (Pibor), Lake (Rumbek East) and Warrap (Tonj North ) of South Sudan. This project targets 9,140 beneficiaries of which 8580 will be school going children aged 3-17 years (3783 boys, 4797 girls ), and 560 adults (316 Male, 244 Female) This project will run for a period of 12 months covering the three terms and the targeted 18 schools in selected counties. This education project will incorporate and complement life-saving components such as psycho-social support, disaster risk reduction and COVID-19 prevention and mitigation measures. positive disciplining to prevent corporal punishment, referral mechanism, and availability of gender-sensitive WASH in schools is essential for keeping children in the classroom and ensuring their safety and well-being, with clean and secure separate toilets for girls and boys and hand-washing facilities to both students and teachers. PCO will collaborate with other clusters like WASH, Protection, Nutrition, Health and stakeholders to ensure coherent, coordinated and integrated responses driven by the assessed education needs of affected populations. PCO will also synergize with health and nutrition cluster partners who manage the health facilities and OTPs centers in the counties of operation, by offering outreach services to supported schools.  
The Key activities of this project will include setting up/rehabilitation of temporary learning spaces (TLSs), providing psycho-social support, providing learning materials, providing WASH facilities, provision of MHM to Adolescent girls to maintain their dignity, training PTA members and teachers on psycho-social support, provision of ECD services to 3-5 years children, training of teachers on EiE, basic pedagogy and learner-cantered methodologies, training of community education committee members and Education officials in school management, monitoring and record keeping and providing, training of youth and adolescents (14-17 years) in life-skills and basic vocational courses.  PCO will also set-up a simple, safe and accessible Community Based Complaints Mechanism for SEA and protection of school children to add efficiency to strengthen reporting mechanism by incorporating local solutions into the overall SEA reporting system.
The organization will involve SMCs, PTAs and Community leaders in community sensitization efforts focusing on access to education services, school WASH and protection messages, and prevention of SEA with the aim to increase access to education for boys and girls as well as preventing and reducing protection risks for children on their way to and from school. Community members will also be involved in the design of TLS, identification of a safe location for construction of TLS and monitoring teachers and pupil attendance through the PTA.
The project will also mainstream gender, GBV, conflict sensitivity and protection with hopes of contributing towards protection of children from risks, GBV and other protection challenges that have a potential of disrupting their education, enhance their psycho-social development, improve hygiene and sanitation and alleviate strains on their academic performance.
PCO is currently implementing education project in 42 schools in Wau and Jur River counties supported by WFP running up to December 2021, implementing integrated Education and Protection project in 8 schools in Pibor GPAA supported by SSHF 1st Allocation and Multi Year Response Education Programme project in 20 schools in Gogrial West and Tonj North Counties funded by ECW and so is familiar with Jonglei and Warrap States. PCO is the education cluster Co-Lead in WBeG, WASH Cluster Co-Lead and WASH/UNICEF Core Pipeline Manager in Pibor GPAA and has established presence across the entire 2 States and PCO is best placed to implement this project.

project_name: Emergency Food Assistance for underserved communities in Aweil South , Aweil East and Panijiar Counties of South Sudan
project_objective: The purpose of the project is to enhance emergency food production, diversify food consumption and strengthen the resilience of targeted communities. The project aims to achieve this purpose by distributing crop and vegetable seed kits, agricultural tool kits, fishing kits, provide agronomic training for 8,400 households, approximately 50,400 individuals. Food production trainings will be through provision of farmer extension services, establishment of farmer field schools and vegetable gardens in schools and nutrition centers. Diet diversity will be achieved by increased consumption of vegetables, increased availability of fish at household level and local markets as well as through targeted sensitization on food preparation (cooking demonstrations), IYCF and basic household hygiene. Further, the resilience of the target communities will be strengthened by encouraging them to participate in construction or rehabilitation of community assets through cash for asset approach. This approach is supplementary expected to provide an alternative source of income to targeted individuals. Additional measures of addressing underlying causes of food insecurity shall include capacity building in disaster risk reduction, natural resources management and establishment of referral pathways to other services including nutrition health care, education, protection, and WASH.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items Interventions to newly displaced and highly vulnerable populations, protracted IDPs, returnees, host communities and community’s dignity in Fangak, Nyirol & Ayod Counties of Jonglei State; Mayendit county of Unity state, Nasir County of Upper Nile state and Kapoeta North of Eastern Equatorial State in South Sudan
project_objective:
ADA -HRP aims at addressing emergency shelter and non-food items needs of newly & highly vulnerable populations, protracted IDPs, returnees and host communities through a multi-sector and single response approach to holistically restore community dignity. The project directly targets 24,000 individuals; 6,000 in Ayod, 4,400 in Fangak, 4,000 in Nyirol counties of Jonglei state, 4,000 in Nasir county of Upper Nile State, 1,600 in Kapoeta North county of Eastern Equatorial State and 4,000 in Mayendit county of Unity state. Fangak, Ayod and Nyirol counties are found in north of Jonglei State; Mayendit County South of Unity State; Nasir county in South East of upper Nile state and Kapoeta North in east of eastern Equatorial state, and these counties have been identified at emergency IPC (or IPC 4 counties).
In the multi-sector approach, ADA plans to collaborate with partners; ACTED is to implement CCCM, and ADA to implement an integrated ES/NFI and MaCDA to implement Protection program in Kapoeta North County in Eastern Equatorial State. While ADA proposes to response alone in Ayod, Nyirol, Fangak, Nasir and Mayendit counties through a single sector approach. The overall project goal is to ensure that the target communities have safe and dignified access to CCCM, shelter & NFIs and protection services. The project will directly target 24,000 conflict and disaster affected persons in Ayod, Fangak, Nyirol, Mayendit, Nasir and Kapoeta North counties through integrated S/NFI, CCCM and protection services and support. During the project implementation, ADA will deliver assistance through a static response in Ayod, Fangak & Nasir and mobile response in Nyirol, Mayendit and Kapoeta North counties. 
In Kapoeta North County, ADA, ACTED and MaCDA will implement a joint and integrated response aimed at crosscutting protection monitoring to inform all responses; that is to say protection mainstreaming, including on community infrastructures like housing, land and property issues, to all S/NFI responses; establish community social networks and safety nets and conduct protection trainings to committees to implement, and conduct mine risk awareness sessions through the committees to ensure safety to the community. All services (Protection/CCCM/SNFI assistance) will be implemented within Kapoeta North county and priority will be given to areas where high vulnerabilities exist to ensure a holistic programming. In Ayod, Fangak, Nirol, Nasir and Mayendit counties, ADA will implement a SNFI single sector approach, however will ensure integrating it with protection mainstreaming, and land, housing and propertyh and covid-19 guidelines, besides engaging all key stakeholders to achieve holistic service delivery to the affected communities in all target areas.
In all project areas, ADA, ACTED and MaCDA aims to address CCCM, protection & SNFI needs of newly & highly vulnerable conflict and disaster affected communities through in-kind S/NFI assistance, for both repairs and maintenance. ACTED will continue to strengthen the cluster state level coordination through SNFI State Focal Point in Eastern Equatorial State, which is under the technical guidance of ACTED. MacDA will implement the general protection and HLP activities, including identification of PSNs, referrals to service providers, information dissemination on key protection needs, advocacy for gaps and life skills training, hence these will complement other ongoing protection efforts done in Eastern Equatorial state by partners. ADA, through a mobile approach will coordinate responses with partners and SFPs and monitor both the single and multi-sector services through its static and roving teams to deep field locations in all its project areas. 
The project will be implemented over a period of 12 months in both counties through single and multi-sector interventions, which will be boosted by Agencies' existing funding streams.

project_name: Provision of life-saving equitable access to WASH services for the disaster affected population in Pibor and Raga in South Sudan
project_objective:
CMC aims at provision of equitable access to safe and adequate water, dignified Sanitation, and safe hygiene practices to mitigate WASH related malnutrition and GBV through integrated WASH intervention mainstreaming protection, enhancing resilience, communities coping mechanisms and sustainability, targeting population with extreme needs under WASH vulnerability (PIN) 4 and 5 mainly disaster (Flood, Conflicts, Famine) affected population within the IPC 3, 4 and 5  to achieve cluster strategic objectives 1, 2 & 3 (SO 1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 2:2, 3:1) , and cluster objectives (CO1 and CO3) tackling 70% WASH-nut and 30% WASH-GBV in the areas of Pibor, Pochalla and Raja targeting crises affected population, IPC3 to IPC5 population, mainly IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable host communities in Likuangole, Gumuruk, Verteth, Manyibol town, Pochalla in Jonglei and Raja County in Western Bahr Al Ghazal to reduce morbidity and mortality resulting from WASH-related GBV and malnutrition within the affected population incorporating COVID 19 new normal and WASH cluster standard operation procedures. CMC focuses on lifesaving WASH activities mainstreaming protection, accountability to affected population (AAP) and strengthening the beneficiaries copping mechanism and building resilience through training of different groups of people in the community including; pump mechanics, Water management committee, women groups, community leaders, the AAP focal persons, teachers, pupils and nutrition workers on WASH practices. The respond will take into account close coordination with the WASH cluster EP&R partners, the FSL, Health, Nutrition and Protection cluster partners in order to deliver integrated, complementary and well-coordinated responses to mean the multi-sectoral needs of the population

The project targets 16,750 (Pibor=11,000, Raja=4100, Pochalla=1650 direct beneficiaries and 3,850 indirect beneficiaries facing IPC3&5and GAM ranging at 20.8%, the IDPs, most vulnerable host communities affected with flood, COVID 19, inclusive natural disasters, and malnutrition patients with limited access to WASH services and food insecurity, through supported coordination and complementation of WASH needs in the targeted areas, achieving Sphere standards, the core humanitarian standards and the WASH cluster objectives CO1 and CO3, and contributing to eradication of the IPC. Instigating WASH sustainable solution, enhancing cost-recovery mechanism through market integration and maintaining high level of quality infrastructures with adherence to conflict sensitivity analysis taking into account disability inclusion approaches and beneficiaries centered approaches throughout designing and undertaking all related activities in an aim to close gender gaps in WASH.
CMC aims at structured, effective preparedness and response programme through improving access to safe water, enhancing community awareness on safe hygiene and sanitation practices within population with limited access to WASH services and food insecurity, supporting institutional WASH Services through coordination with nutrition, protection and FSL partners to integrate WASH in their interventions by enhancing the knowledge of mothers and children with equitable WASH practices to mitigate WASH related GBV and malnutrition within the population. Enhancing sustainability and resilience by building capacities of the communities to cope with current shocks through sustaining livelihoods linkages with development action to promote ownership, participations, and accountability to affected people through beneficiaries centered approaches.
CMC will ensure that services delivered are gender-sensitive, considering people with special needs and disables by establishing strong feedback and complain mechanisms at all stages of the implementation, training of the AAP focal point dominated by the beneficiaries, and the CMC M&E team to ensure feedbacks and complains are addressed.

project_name: Protecting Vulnerable Populations in Bentiu PoC and Renk from Epidemic-Prone Vector-Borne Diseases
project_objective:
The proposed programme aims to provide protection from malaria and other vector-borne diseases (VBDs) to the highly vulnerable Internally Displaced People (IDPs) population in the Rubkona/Bentiu Protection of Civilians (PoC) site and the host, IDP and returnee community in Renk. To achieve this, The MENTOR Initiative will focus on preventing disease-transmitting vectors from multiplying and entering the malaria and other VBD transmission cycles, which cause a great deal of morbidity and mortality. Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS), mosquito larviciding and fly control measures will be employed as tools to disrupt disease transmission. In addition, MENTOR will adopt an integrated approach and the target population will also be educated on the diseases itself, their signs and symptoms, and how to prevent infection, as well as on the impact of water and sanitation on disease transmission, (mal-) nutrition and associated disease severity. Owing to the still fragile nature of the COVID-19 pandemic, respective awareness messages will also be disseminated. All of this will be achieved through delivering targeted IEC/BCC campaigns and health education sessions. MENTOR will incorporate messages in the IEC/BCC campaign in order to ensure consistent use, care and maintenance of LLINs through IEC/BCC in the target locations after distribution by NMCP and other implementing partners. Lastly, health facilities in the target locations will be supported by offering comprehensive trainings on malaria and other VBDs differential diagnosis and case management together with Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) of Covid-19 for nursing and medical staff to improve the quality of health service delivery. 

MENTOR is an HRP member and the mentioned activities were planned and implemented in SSHF Round 1 and 2 in Bentiu PoC in 2019 and Round 1 in Ulang and Renk in 2020-21 with significant results achieved.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Healthcare Service (IEHCS)provision to IDPs, Returnees, and Host communities affected by food insecurity and floods in Akobo, Ayod, Nyirol, Pibor  Counties in Jonglei state, Maiwut, Manyo, and Panyikang Counties in Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
In 2013 South Sudan descended into a civil war that displaced more than 4 million people into the neighboring countries, Uganda, Kenya Sudan, DRC, and Ethiopia. This political instability affected health service delivery and destroyed health infrastructure. This has led to millions of South Sudanese lacking life-saving health services increasing maternal mortality rates and child mortality rates to unmatchable figures around the globe.
Communicable disease burden is a challenge whereby malaria, measles, acute watery diarrhea, and others continue to ravage the country causing untold suffering to vulnerable and affected populations in the country. Access to health facilities and medical supplies is also a big challenge with populations having to walk more than 7 hours in some cases to access health facilities that also lack essential medical supplies and qualified middle health cadres.
6.37 million South Sudanese citizens are seriously food insecure which is more than 52.6% of the total population and thus becoming even more vulnerable to diseases (IPC OCT 2020). The overall GAM rate in the country is more than the 15% WHO emergency threshold this also increasing vulnerability due to high rates of malnutrition.
The country has been hit by severe flooding which has led to the destruction of health facilities loss of medical supplies and displacement of populations. The floods have affected almost half of the counties in the country displacing almost 1million people in 33 Counties with 11 counties in Jonglei severely hit by the floods.
Immunization services are very poor in the country and also utilization of maternal-child health services is wanting. Cold chain availability and functionality low and transmission of infections prevented by immunization like measles remain very high. In 2019, there were more than 17 counties that had confirmed measles outbreaks and in 2020 the country had 8 counties with measles outbreaks as reported in IDSR reports in week 52 as shared by the health cluster.
Despite efforts by health partners and the ministry of health to improve health service delivery in the country only less than 50% of the population are able to access health services with SARA report in 2019 showing that 44% of the populations in South Sudan are able to access health services. This clearly shows the need to improve health service delivery through static health facilities and also mobile clinics.
Medicair will ensure that in line with the Health Cluster strategic objectives improve access to health services to the vulnerable and affected populations in Akobo, Ayod, Nyirol, Pibor, Manyo, Panyikang, and Maiwut Counties that have been hard hit by floods. Medicair will deploy 4 mobile health teams in Akobo, Ayod, Nyirol, and Panyikang counties to improve the accessibility of health services to the populations affected by floods. Medicair will have 3 PHCUs in Pibor, Manyo, and  Maiwut Counties.
Medicair will offer consultations and management of common illnesses like malaria with ACT, diarrhea with Zinc for children U5. Deliveries will be attended by skilled birth attendance to ensure reduced maternal mortality rates. Immunization services will reduce vaccine-preventable infections, health education especially in the context of COVID 19 will be very key to ensure that key prevention messages of COVID 19 are passed to the community.
Medicair will train health workers on IPC, IDSR, integrated WASH to ensure that the health workers have the knowledge to attend to health emergencies.
Medicair will screen children for malnutrition and give necessary management and refer them to nutrition centers for further management.
The project will target 8,035 ( 3937 male and 4098 female) with 1205 people with disability beneficiaries in Manyo, Maiwut, Nyirol, Panyikang, Akobo, Ayod, Pibor Counties. this will be in Coordination with other partners and County Health Departments.

project_name: Amélioration de l'accès et de la couverture des services de la santé sexuelle et reproductive pour les personnes déplacées internes du Lac
project_objective:
Pendant les crises, de nombreuses femmes et jeunes filles et adolescents font face aux besoins non satisfaits des services de la santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR). Les besoins des hommes n’est sont pas suffisamment prise en considération et leur accès aux informations sur la SSR pour favoriser le soutien a la prise des décisions sur la SSR de leur partenaire, sont aussi limité. 
En réponse aux besoin critique, en particulier pendant cette période de la pandémie de la covid-19, l’objectif général de ce projet est d’améliorer l’offre, l’utilisation et la couverture des services SSR de qualité aux personnes déplacées internes (IDPs) dans les 3 districts sanitaire du lac (Bol, Baga-Sola et Liwa).  En appuyant les structure sanitaire et communautaire toute en respectant les mesures de la prévention de la covid-19, le projet à comme cible les femmes en âge de procréer (15 à 49 ans), les femmes enceintes, les femmes avec les complications obstétricales, les filles et garçons adolescentes (10 à 19 ans), les jeunes femmes et hommes (20 à 24 ans), les hommes adultes et sexuellement active (Plus de 18 ans). 
Considérant plus spécifiquement nos cibles, la mise en œuvre du Dispositif Minimum d’Urgence (DMU) est pertinente afin de prévenir la mortalité, la morbidité et le handicap.
A travers les prestataire des service SSR et les violence sexuelle (VBG) qualifié, les activités proposés par le projet vont d'une réponse intégrée à prévenir la VBG et répondre aux besoins des victimes, y compris la gestion clinique de viol; prévenir la transmission et réduire la morbidité et la mortalité en raison du VIH et d’autres infections sexuellement transmissible (IST) ; prévenir la surmortalité et la sur morbidité maternelles et néonatales par la mise en place de soins obstétricaux et néonatals d'urgence de base et complets (SONUB et C); assurer la disponibilité des préservatifs  gratuit et les méthodes de contraceptive moderne pour prévenir les grossesses non désirées ; la partage des informations et sensibilisations sur la SSR et VBG relatives aux femmes et aux hommes.  
Il est aussi également pertinent d’assurer la mise en place des services compréhensive de la SSR/ VBG et des services SSR adaptés au adolescentes et jeunes (SRAJ). Par conséquent, conformément au mandat du l’UNFPA, l'assistance sera adaptée pour l’atteinte les groupes concernés par: i) le recrutement de sages-femmes qualifié, dans les formation sanitaire (FOSA) couvrant les sites des IDPs ; ii) la fourniture aux FOSA des matériel, équipements et de médicaments (y compris des contraceptifs modernes et les kits SR d'Urgence); iii) la production locale d'équipements de protection individuelle-EPI (visières, bonnets et tabliers parmi d’autres) et l'achat international; iv) l'organisation des campagne de sensibilisation sur la disponibilité des services à travers les mécanismes de communication locale et les outils ; v)La mise en place d’une stratégie avancée avec les cliniques mobiles pour les zones d'accès difficiles; vi) le renforcement de la fonctionnalité et la maintenance des ambulances dans les 3 structure sanitaire de référence de Bol, Baga Sola et Liwa (centre de santé), pour le renforcement du système de référence; vii) l’organisation des ateliers de formations pour les prestataire des service sur la prise en charge clinique de la SSR et la VBG et la bonne gestions des données ; viii) former les agents de santé communautaires pour appuyer les FOSA et les espaces sûrs; ix) Renforcement de la fonctionnalité des services SRAJ.
Afin de s’assurer de la bonne réalisation des activités proposées et l’obtention de la satisfaction des groupes ciblés, le projet tient à ce que les populations affectées participent à la mise en œuvre et à l'évaluation du projet. Ceci se fera à travers la participation des agents de santé communautaire au actions y compris les activités de suivi et d’évaluation.

project_name: Renforcement de l’accès aux services de prise en charge des survivants de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et de la résilience communautaire pour la population déplacés et retournés de la province du Lac
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire dans la province du lac est très précaire et reste marquée par les attaques des groupes armés Boko Haram et les opérations militaires des FDS qui cherchent à ramener la sécurité. L’on constate des déplacements qui sont de plus en plus importants. La population est exposée aux risques de protection. Cette situation vient exacerber les conditions de vie des plus vulnérables qui subissent déjà de discriminations et de violences causées par les normes socioculturelles, le sous-développement et la méconnaissance des textes de lois. La plupart de cette couche défavorable sont les femmes et les filles comme l’attestent les évaluations sur le terrain et la base de données GBVIMS. La pandémie de la COVID19 avec ses effets et les mesures sanitaires affectent la vie des populations, les restrictions prises par le gouvernement ont de conséquences sur la vie socio-économique de la population déjà affectée. Aussi, quelques VBG enregistrés au cours de l’année 2020 ont un lien avec le contexte de la COVID19. 
Le projet vise à :
-	Prévenir les violences basées sur le genre à actions au sein des communautés
-	Offrir un paquet de services holistiques de qualité aux survivants de VBG
-	Renforcer les compétences et capacités des femmes et filles pour leur autonomisation et leur participation aux actions visant à maintenir la sécurité
-	Renforcer la capacité des acteurs communautaires de terrain pour la prise en compte des aspects de VBG 
Les actions prendront en compte le contexte de la maladie à coronavirus  
Les bénéficiaires seront les personnes survivantes de VBG et aussi, les hommes, garçons, les femmes et filles actives des communautés qui acquièrent des connaissances et compétences pour bâtir une vie sans violences

project_name: Appui aux solutions durables en abris pour les Personnes déplacées de la province du Lac
project_objective:
Le Tchad reste affecté par l´insécurité résultant de l´insurrection des groupes armés. Les attaques ciblées des villages et les opérations militaires menées par l´armée tchadienne et les forces multinationales mixtes (FMM) continuent d´affecter négativement la stabilité de la province du lac. De nouveaux déplacements de populations suites aux des attaques ciblées sur les populations civiles aggrave la situation humanitaire.
La province du lac compte 336.124 PDI et 30.422 retournés selon les statistiques de DTM de OIM et 16,013 réfugiés au 31 décembre selon l’UNHCR. Les possibilités de retour des PDI sont faibles en raison de l’insécurité, des attaques répétées et des violences dans les zones d’origine. Les perspectives de solutions durables, dont le retour dans la sécurité et la dignité ainsi qu’un accompagnement pour une réintégration, ne semblent pas être envisageables dans un proche avenir.  
Selon l’enquête de IOM en 2020 sur les intentions de retour, 90% des PDI disent ne pas être prêts à retourner dans leurs villages d’origine. Ainsi, la solution durable la plus probable et offrant le plus d’opportunités pour les PDI semble être l’intégration locale. 
La faiblesse du développement et des investissements dans plusieurs secteurs y compris le secteur agricole et de l´élevage aggravée par le contexte de crise économique de 2017, les changements climatiques expliquent en partie la persistance des crises humanitaires affectant les conditions de vie des populations. 
L´analyse de sévérité des besoins faite sur base des indicateurs multisectoriels et sectoriels fait ressortir la province du Lac comme un des zones qui sont en sévérité catastrophique en raison notamment des mouvements de population, du faible accès aux services sociaux de base, à la prévalence de la malnutrition aigüe globale et sévère et à la fréquence des incidents de protection.
Considérant les indicateurs des besoins liés aux conditions de vie, à savoir les besoins à moyen terme comme l´accès à l´abri sécurisé et durable, la province du Lac fait partie des zones qui reflètent de sévérités catastrophiques au même titre que l’accès aux services sociaux de base, aux moyens d´existence.
Le projet d’assistance en abris durable pour les PDI sera mis en œuvre en premier lieu dans les sites installés depuis 2015 dans les départements de Kaya, Fouli et Mamdi soit 70 sites dont la population est estimée à 150,855 soit 33,704 ménages. 
Le projet portera sur l’objectif sectoriel d’amélioration des conditions de vie des personnes déplacées internes et des retournés et sera échelonné sur plusieurs années vu le nombre assez élevé de besoins. L’assistance et la recherche de solutions se faisant à travers une approche de responsabilité sectorielle et dans le cadre de coordination inter organisations, l’intervention du HCR en matière d’assistance en abris durable et en eau potable se focalisera principalement sur les sites dont la population a été poussée au déplacement par les attaques des GANE. 
La relocalisation des DPI pour une consolidation des sites plus viables, accessibles et sécurisés constituant la vision de l’autorité de la province du Lac et des acteurs humanitaires serait la base de la mise en œuvre du projet parce que s’inscrivant dans la durabilité.  
L’assistance en abris proposé par le projet s’inscrit dans la stratégie globale de protection en lien avec la réduction de la vulnérabilité liée aux crises humanitaires, renforcer la redevabilité envers les populations affectées et promouvoir leur accès aux solutions durables.
Le projet s’inscrit dans la perspective du nexus humanitaire-développement et entre en droite ligne avec la vision du gouvernement pour la promotion de villages durable. Le programme PARCA est une des opportunités qui pourra soutenir les objectifs de ce projet.

project_name: Disminución de la morbimortalidad materna, embarazo adolescente, infecciones de transmisión sexual/VIH y violencia sexual en población vulnerable de 8 estados priorizados.
project_objective: El proyecto está alineado con la estrategia del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud y objetivos estratégicos del clúster de Salud. Tiene por objetivo salvar vidas con acciones ya impulsadas por UNFPA durante 2019 y 2020, ampliándose a los estados priorizados por el MPPS y por el panorama de necesidades, Apure, Bolívar y Guárico, además de Miranda, Distrito Capital, Anzoátegui, Zulia y Táchira. Estados. Miranda y Distrito Capital, con importante densidad de población y con el mayor número de casos por COVID 19, 12.177,20.431 respectivamente (11nov) Zulia y Táchira estados fronterizos, áreas importantes para el paso de los migrantes y retornados, en condiciones de alta vulnerabilidad. Guárico ha sido un estado incluido a solicitud del MPPS, con necesidades en atención de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR) que no ha recibido apoyo por el SNU y donde UNFPA ya viene trabajando con reforzamiento del talento humano en temas clave. En estos 8 estados se abarcará a 21 hospitales y 105 centros de atención primaria para el fortalecimiento de su operatividad y respuesta oportuna, garantizando la disponibilidad y acceso a los servicios y suministros de SSR, beneficiando a una población total estimada de 900.000 personas, con énfasis en mujeres en edad reproductiva más vulnerables, en movilidad, adolescentes y embarazadas en contexto de pandemia por COVID 19 y población indígena. Las intervenciones del Sistema Nacional de Salud al inicio de la Pandemia se enfocaron en fortalecer los servicios críticos y contener y mitigar el impacto de la pandemia por COVID-19, por lo que se dejaron desatendidas áreas importantes como la SSR. los suministros esenciales, de higiene menstrual y anticonceptivos a menudo no son asequibles. La información y cuidados relativos a planificación familiar, salud materna, protección y tratamiento de la violencia sexual a menudo se pasan por alto. Las actividades enmarcadas en este contexto están dirigidas a disminuir la morbimortalidad materna, estimadas entre 77 y 124 muertes por 100.000 nv, a través del fortaleciendo el talento humano, y de su protección con insumos para Equipos de Protección personal, aseguramiento de equipos e insumos hospitalarios para la respuesta efectiva de emergencias obstétricas y la prevención del embarazo no deseado con anticonceptivos, especialmente en adolescentes (22 de cada 100 nacimientos son de madres adolescentes en el país). La escasez de métodos anticonceptivos se estima que puede llegar hasta un 67% y las necesidades insatisfechas de planificación familiar en 38%. Se dará respuesta a la necesidad de mejorar la atención clínica a la violencia sexual, reforzando con insumos y capacidades acordes al Protocolo Nacional. Se toman en cuenta estrategias y actividades para la disminución de las Infecciones de Transmisión Sexual (ITS), Sífilis congénita y transmisión vertical del VIH. Se fortalecerá a la comunidad con acciones que permitan mayores niveles de información y participación para prevención de Covid 19, sexualidad responsable, y temas claves SSR. La sostenibilidad y estrategia de salida están contempladas: el personal y centros con capacidades mejoradas pertenecen al Sistema Nacional de Salud. Actividades: Procura y distribución de equipos, medicamentos, anticonceptivos, pruebas diagnosticas Sifilis/VIH, equipos de protección personal e higiene femenina. Actualización para el personal de salud en Cuidados Obstétricos de Emergencia, Anticoncepción, prevención de ITS, VIH y embarazo no deseado, manejo clínico de violencia sexual, bajo enfoque de derechos y en contexto de COVID 19. Sensibilización e información a la comunidad en temas clave SSR y prevención de COVID 19. Se ejecutarán acciones de rehabilitación para mejorar el acceso de agua, iluminación y climatización en áreas obstétricas y para el fortalecimiento del sistema de referencia.  Población meta total 900.000 personas, 80.000 embarazadas, 662.000 mujeres, de las cuales 167.000 adolescentes, 243.000 hombres.

project_name: Provision of Education Services to Emergency-affected children in South Sudan
project_objective:
The UNICEF frontline services project will contribute to the Education Cluster objectives CO1, CO2 and CO3 to improve equitable access to safe and protective education services and improve the quality of education services for emergency and COVID-19 affected IDPs, returnees, spontaneous refugees, and host community children including children with disabilities, and youth (girls and boys) by 2021 in counties under IPC 4 and 5.  To achieve the objectives, the project will enroll 346,156 children in Pre-primary, Primary and secondary schools/learning centers; Establish  195 temporary learning spaces and classrooms; Rehabilitate 104 temporary learning spaces and classrooms; Establish 995 gender segregated latrines and water points and hygiene promotion; Train 1,560 teachers in EiE pedagogical skills and Child-centred methodologies to improve teaching -learning process for emergency-affected children; Train and update 1,560 teachers on PSS and the impact of COVID-19 and its  protection  mechanisms; Train 1638 SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management and governance, psychosocial support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR).   The proposed budget for the project is USD 23,538,632 with a cost per beneficiary unit of USD 68.                                                                                                       

As mentioned in the 2021 HNO, the protracted crisis coupled with COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 resulted in unprecedented challenges and closure of schools in South Sudan affecting 1.9 million children.  It is worth-noting that the closure of schools not only interrupted educational progresses, but also affected livelihood and hindered children’s access to essential basic needs and services including school feeding, health information on disease prevention, protection and access to clean water and sanitation services.  The project will contribute to the Education Cluster objectives CO1 and CO2 to improve equitable access to education for emergency/crisis affected boys and girls aged 3-17 years (40 per cent girls) but also improving the quality of education services in the country.  

Over the years, South Sudan has been confronted with many challenges including protracted conflict, floods, large population displacements, hyperinflation, and severe food insecurity (HRP 2020 Education Cluster Narrative). The already fragile education system drastically deteriorated at both the systems and service delivery levels and is characterized by high numbers of out-of-school children and adolescents, particularly those affected by conflict and other emergencies estimated to be 2.2 million (UNESCO 2018, Global Initiative on OOSC: South Sudan Country Study).  With the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact, the appalling education situation of the country has been severely aggravated, hence the need for resources to address it. 

Through the project, children and youth (3-17 years) will enroll in pre-primary, primary and secondary schools/learning centers; establish/rehabilitate temporary learning spaces with gender sensitive WASH facilities; train teachers on EiE, basic pedagogy and learner-centered methodologies; train and equip SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management and governance; and provide schools with appropriate IEC materials on COVID-19 prevention and mitigation measures.                                     

The importance of ensuring that the right for equitable access to quality education for all children (boys and girls} in South Sudan, particularly the most vulnerable and those affected by conflict and floods are safeguarded. Without the provision of education, the future of children will be at stake.

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria en agua y promoción de la higiene por emergencia para 5 municipios del corredor seco de Guatemala.
project_objective:
La respuesta se enfocará en 5 municipios de 2 departamentos del corredor seco de Guatemala donde los sistemas de agua fueron dañados por eventos naturales o ampliaciones para el mejoramiento de los mismos.
La implementación será a través de socios nacionales o locales que coordinarán y fortalecerán a las municipalidades y comunidades buscando que mejoren sus capacidades de respuesta a emergencia, vincularse al desarrollo con sistemas de información pertinentes y oportunos en cuanto a WASH se refiere.
Se realizarán sistemas de agua y saneamiento sostenibles con participación activa de las partes, que incluyan el enfoque de resiliencia, vinculado con actividades de cambio de comportamiento de manera inclusiva y participativa. La orientación del proyecto es a personas con mayor vulnerabilidad como población rural, mujeres, niñas y personas con discapacidad.
Además, se coordinará con los clústeres de nutrición, salud, educación y protección para generar una respuesta cohesiva e integral y generar sinergia con las otras acciones que se integran dentro de este proyecto, las principales acciones se realizarán en conjunto con UNICEF y ONU Mujeres.
Las acciones más relevantes son:
- Fortalecimiento de capacidades para la sostenibilidad de los sistemas a funcionarios municipales de WASH, responsables de AOM de sistemas comunitarios e integrantes del hogar en sistemas unifamiliares.
- Rehabilitación, mejora y construcción de sistemas de agua a escala familiar y comunitaria.
- Mejora de la calidad de agua en sistemas en hogar, comunidad, escuelas y establecimientos de salud.
- Promoción y vinculación del triple nexo en acciones WASH relacionados con captación de agua lluvia, uso de recursos hídricos, tratamiento de aguas para consumo y residuales para reciclado.
- WASH en escuelas y establecimientos de salud abordando las necesidades de higiene menstrual.
- Campañas de comunicación para promover la práctica de hábitos de higiene, desinfección, uso y manipulación del agua.

project_name: Protecting Rohingya and Host Communities by facilitating meaningful access to humanitarian assistance, dignity and human rights
project_objective:
IOM’s Protection Project for the 2021 JRP connects four strategic objectives with a series of activities to benefit the most vulnerable Rohingya and host community persons, to reach the elderly, widows, single-headed households, persons with disabilities, and persons with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity, and expression, and to target authorities and partners in a way that does no harm, assists based on needs, and prioritizes respect for human rights, safety and dignity. 
IOM will be the Protection focal point lead in nine camps, directly implementing most activities. IOM’s protection monitoring activities will facilitate beneficiaries’ meaningful access to all humanitarian assistance, dignity and human rights. IOM will strengthen community-based protection through engagement, awareness raising, and sensitization; case management and specialized Protection services for individuals in need.  IOM’s core counter-trafficking activities - prevention, protection and capacity building - will be implemented in 18 camps and 10 host communities. These activities strive to have sustainable impact and improve peaceful coexistence between communities. 
For disaster risk reduction, IOM will work with a range of partners, including other Sectors, community-based protection networks in the camps, and relevant authorities to identify extremely vulnerable individuals or households needing specialized assistance and preparation before a disaster. IOM will verify the needs of EVIs, coordinate services, and support other partners to mitigate harm during disaster response. IOM will continue leading the Protection Emergency Response Units in nine camps.  
IOM’s protection mainstreaming activities will promote a holistic lens, incorporating age, gender, and diversity needs of the affected population in Cox’s Bazar into programming through capacity building, training, as well as activity monitoring and modification. Finally, IOM will continue to co-chair the Sector’s Anti-Trafficking Working Group, and be a proactive member of the PWG, the Protection Task Team, and other related working groups.

project_name: Self-reliance through ensuring food security and addressing vulnerability of the affected host and Rohingya community with emphasis on restoration of fragile environment
project_objective:
The proposed project will work to contribute on achieving the JRP objectives 2021 along with BRAC’s strategic objectives 2021 i.e.  Localization of humanitarian efforts, resilience building of the affected FDMN and host community and strengthening coordination among the humanitarian actors and stakeholders. BRAC will undertake a holistic humanitarian approach, in combination with other partners and stakeholders, to enhance livelihoods and resilience of vulnerable host community, promote self-reliance of Rohingya refugees and strengthen sustainable natural resource management for Rohingya and host communities. The response towards enhancing livelihoods and resilience building will include technical capacity building on livelihoods strategies such as homestead gardening, livestock, aquaculture with inputs and service supports and market linkage; skill development and job placement for ensuring self-reliance. To ensure sustainable natural resource management inside and outside of the camps. BRAC will consider community based mixed plantation and tree saplings distribution to ensure biological land stabilization through increasing forest coverage. 
Focus on gender inclusion will come into a new dimension through equity and equality based on the needs and prospect of engaging in income generating activities. In addition, strategies such as consultation and participation with different age and sex group people and their experiences will be an integral dimension of the project cycle to ensure that women and men can benefit equally from development interventions and inequalities are not perpetuated. The project will ensure inclusion of protection principles in the general project management and as core principles in delivering humanitarian aid by incorporating protection principles into project cycle management through protection mainstreaming indicators for each component. The project will collect baseline data based on age and sex disaggregation though which it will be ensured participation of different age and sex oriented people with special emphasis on persons with disability, elderly people, female-headed households, and single mother.

Cross-cutting issues like empowerment, inclusivity, linkage to other critical services (such as protection and health), ensuring safe environments, as well as long-term well-being, linked to resilience to climate-induced vulnerability to natural disasters and portable skills will be the high priority areas in BRAC’s food security and self-reliance interventions. Consisting of Agriculture and Environment, Ultra-Poor Graduation Program, Skill Development Program and Ayesha-Abed Foundation, JRP 2021 will target 27,230 beneficiaries (female 23,380 and male 3850) and the total estimated budget is 7.29 million USD.

project_name: Enhancing Access to Protection, Community Safety and Peaceful Coexistence for Refugees and Host Communities
project_objective: The main objective of the project is to improve protection, safety and security and enhance access to justice and peaceful coexistence between refugees and host communities in 10 camps in Cox’s Bazar, with particular attention to vulnerable groups such as youth, women, elderly, people with disabilities . The project will provide a forum through which refugees and host communities will have improved access to protection services and conflict resolution mechanisms, as well as access to legal assistance and victim support services. The expected results will reinforce the capacities of actors that are currently working on community safety and security, justice and protection in both refugee and host communities, focusing on addressing crime, promoting women’s empowerment, and preventing and responding to SGBV in a more inclusive and sustainable manner in accordance with national legal and local administrative structures and refugee protection standards. The interventions proposed are based on the findings of a community safety pilot project carried out in two camps in 2020, which emphasized the need for increased police presence in the camps and involved training on humanitarian law, protection principles and community safety. The pilot also focused on establishing community safety forums in the two camps to enable partnership and dialogue develop local solutions to problems identified jointly by refugee and host communities and strengthen different forms of social accountability. The project will be jointly implemented by UNDP, UNHCR and IOM in close collaboration with the RRRC and Camp in Charge officials, APBn, District Police and local government institutions in Cox’s Bazar. Further the project will work closely with UNHCR and IOM Protection sector and staff in the camps, SGBV staff and Camp Management.  The multi-stakeholder approach will focus on achieving refugee protection through more predictable and sustained support to both refugees and the communities hosting them.

project_name: Assistance à la réintégration holistique des rapatriés burundais les plus vulnérables dans leur zone de retour
project_objective: Ce projet permettra de renforcer les structurés de prise en charge communautaire et aussi de sensibiliser la population sur les risques de violations, abus et exploitation, violence sexuelle et basée sur le genre et les opportunités de réponse existantes pour les assister au mieux concernant leur  opérationnalité, assurer le suivi de cas qui sont référés et  la fourniture des services de qualité aux survivantes. Des services de gestion de cas mobile seront assurés par IRC en collaboration avec les animateurs communautaires pour permettre aux survivantes de VBG à accéder aux services disponibles et assurer la protection de leur sécurité. Le challenge reste très présent puisque la réintégration des rapatries reste difficile dans leur zone de retour, le temps passée sur les zones de transit ne leur permet pas d`avoir accès à tous les services compte tenu de la courte durée de cette étape et les survivantes de GBV ne connaissent pas non les services disponibles à leur arrivée dans leur zone de retour finale, elles n`ont parfois pas la possibilité financière ou le moyen de déplacement à disposition pour se rendre à l`hôpital ou pour obtenir les services dont elles ont besoin, que cela soit un soutien psychosocial, un suivi médicalisé, un kit PEP ou même un hébergement d`urgence si le retour à domicile se passe mal.

project_name: Improve Access to Housing for Displaced, Hosts and Returnees in Rural Damascus, Dara’a, Deir-Ezzor, Hama, Homs, and Aleppo.
project_objective:
The rationale of this area-based housing project is derived from experience gained from previous pilots and shelter projects, and in light of Shelter Sector’s evaluation and interventions, as well as challenges emerged during the last years, concluding that
• Restoration of services and infrastructure, simultaneous to rehabilitation of living space, is a key factor in reviving the affected neighbourhoods and improving stability,
• The return, and the subsequent rehabilitation of damaged properties, are tied to demanding procedures and steps to be taken by returning families including the rehabilitation permission, approvals of relevant authorities, civil and tenure documentation, as well as technical matters to restore their damaged homes including damage assessments and classifications, technical specifications, costs, technical designs, business management and so on. 
• Community (and municipality) involvement in project identiﬁcation and planning processes is a prominent element in emergency assistance, as it serves to mitigate possible tensions arising from perceived or real discrimination in selection processes. It is however essential to manage expectations of beneﬁciary populations, thus, to boost positive impact of outcomes of delivered assistance.
Objectives:
Through this area-based housing approach outlined herein, UN-Habitat aims to boost sustainable access to housing, through rehabilitation and restoration of community  infrastructure (roads, street lighting and debris removal) and support returning and affected families with housing-related services and facilitations (housing support units and support cadastral services) for later rehabilitation phase in Rural Damascus, Daraa, Deir-Ezzor, Hama, Homs and Aleppo. 
The holistic notion to serve entire conﬂict-affected, vulnerable communities through improvement of essential infrastructure and housing -related services, under the objective to revive neighborhoods, is at the core of this project.

Project Components:
In alignment with the municipalities’ recovery plans, the project targets to:
• Light repair and maintenance of roads (mainly the Asphalt layer) in residential areas
• Rehabilitation of sidewalks (including tiling, and replacement of damaged curbstones)
• Debris removal
• Provision and installation of solar street lighting
• Support the formation of Housing Support Units which is a virtual entity comprising representatives from municipality, local community, cadastral department, and technical experts. This unit aims to mobilize collective efforts of housing stakeholders to assist the returnees in housing-related services at community level including obtaining rehabilitation permits, conduct rapid damage assessment of houses/buildings, obtaining/restoring tenure documents, and all kinds of other technical services related to housing rehabilitation work. Supporting the restoration of cadastral services will be part of this activity wherever needed.

The targeted sub-district locations are:

project_name: Shelter and infrastructure assistance for IDPs, returnees and affected population in Syria
project_objective:
UNHCR’s interventions will cover accessible areas in all Governorates, with specific focus on areas hosting large number of returns. As lead agency for the Shelter Sector, UNHCR is coordinating the shelter responses from inside Syria as well as from Gaziantep (Turkey), and acting as the last resort for the Sector when resources are available. Through this project UNHCR will support the communities of IDPs and returnees in targeted areas through emergency response and long term shelter solutions from inside Syria as well as from Gaziantep (Turkey). The project is in line with both the priorities of the HRP and 2021 Sector Strategy and the project will be completed in line with Sector guidance. Project indicator targets represent a sum of Syria and Gaziantep hub targets, outlined below:
The shelter programme aims to improve housing and related community/public infrastructure addressing shelter needs of 10,000 vulnerable households/50,000 individuals through basic house repairs. Returnee communities will be supported with debris removal and installation of solar streetlights to support 837,500 individuals/167,500 returnee families and host community.

Through emergency response in North East and North West, 228,500 individuals/45,700 households will receive with emergency shelters kits, and 150,000 individuals/30,000 households will benefit from tents distribution, camp construction and collective shelter rehabilitation
UNHCR’s cross-border shelter programme aims to provide emergency shelter (tents) to 35,000 households/175,000 individuals and improve IDP sites conditions with road, drainage and lightening provision. The target for the road improvement in IDP sites is 80 km. The role and responsibility of the local and national authorities will continue in close partnership with MoLAE and partners (NGOs/INGOs) in the implementation of shelter and infrastructure works. Technical training will be provided to 2,000 engineers from local government.

project_name: Emergency provision of cereals and pulses production to vulnerable food insecure farmers in Syria
project_objective:
The United Nations (UN) estimates that the number of crisis-affected population in need of humanitarian assistance in Syria is 14.2 million (48.7% male and 51.3% female), of which 6.0 million are in acute need. This figure of people in need, includes 6.7 million protracted internally displaced persons (IDPs); estimated 320,000 spontaneous IDPs return; 75,000 refugees return; 438,000 Palestine refugees and the rest overburdened host communities. More than 70% of the population in need of humanitarian assistance are accessible from within Syria.  
Overall, 12.4 million of people are estimated to be food insecure (including 1.27 million severely food insecure and 9.5 million moderately food insecure) and 1.9 million at risk of food insecurity. In this context, FAO has designed a project to assist 192,000 vulnerable crisis-affected food insecure farming households (equivalent to 1,152,000 people) in Syria. The objective of the proposed action is to improve access to staple foods for vulnerable farmers through increased cereal and pulse production. The project outputs include:
Output 1: Access to agricultural inputs to facilitate production of cereals and pulses for 185,500 households increased. 
The response package under this output will be in line with sector recommendations for provision of 200 kg of wheat/barley seeds (adequate to plant 1 ha), 50 kg NPK 10:10:10 (adequate for 1 ha). An additional 40 to 50 kg of various legume seeds (adequate to plant approximately 0.25 0.4 ha) or 200 kg per dunum for potatoes will be provided per household. 
Output 2: Skills for cereal and pulses production of 185,500 targeted households enhanced. 
This output aims at building the capacity of the 185,500 households that will benefit from cereal and pulses production inputs. Beneficiaries will receive training to support use of the inputs and the training programme will be built on the following FAO concepts: “Save & Grow”, climate-smart agriculture and conservation agriculture.
Output 3: Enhanced production and preservation of high quality wheat seed for 6,500 households. 
This output aims to enhance wheat seed production and preservation capacity through training and input provision.
It is expected that the introduction of agriculture-based livelihood protection support in current protracted nearly ten years crisis will be able to increase local availability of food, self-reliance and improve food and nutrition security of the Syrian people, especially the most vulnerable ones.

project_name: Shelter and NFI emergency support for conflict affected households in Quneitra, Rural Damascus and Aleppo
project_objective:
In 2020 ZOA implemented projects in multiple sectors including NFI, reaching a total of 35,081 beneficiaries. In 2020 ZOA was able to secure $4,439,160 in funding, of which $1,331,000 was SHF funding. In 2021 ZOA has to date secured $3,888,000 with around 2 million USD secured for NFI interventions. The cost per beneficiary is estimated to be $68.

Currently, ZOA is distributing around 4,000 NFI kits in Quneitra Governorate. The price for each NFI kit is about $150. For the winterization planned activities the kits estimation prices are as follows: Winterizationa kits - $140 (Jackets, boots etc.), SOK (Light) - $ 40 and heaters (multifunctional) – Although it is in kind, but the collected prices from the markets range is $48-$135.


ZOA is proposing winterization activities to reach households susceptible to the harsh winter conditions in underserved conflict affected communities in Rural Damascus, Aleppo and Quneitra. Based on community based needs assessments and sector guidance, ZOA will target the most vulnerable households with an emphasis on those in areas with high severity of needs in the target locations of Rural Damascus, Aleppo and Quneitra. Proposed activities are aimed at minimising vulnerable households’ exposure to harsh weather conditions, negative coping mechanisms as well as health concerns especially in light of the COVID-19 outbreak. Interventions will ensure that households susceptible to the harsh winter conditions are well equipped with the necessary resources to survive the winter period. Proposed activities based on needs, market assessments, sector guidance and beneficiary preference include the distribution of heaters, vouchers for heating fuel (coal), provision of commodity based vouchers for sealing-off kits and winterization kits and/or MPC, the modality will be decided once the locations are finalised and based on the rapid market assessment. ZOA has wide experience in CVA activities worldwide and in Syria. We also have prepared a full risk analysis for CVA activities. The assistance will be prioritised for newly displaced vulnerable families (including people displaced multiple times), people living in sub-standard shelters and spontaneous returnees. Assistance will be prioritised to the most vulnerable groups that include female-headed households, persons with disabilities and the elderly. Assistance is targeted at about 7,000 households.

The proposal is aligned with Sectoral Objective 1 which is to provide life-saving and life sustaining shelter and non-food items (NFIs) support.

All the targeted sub-districts have the severity score 3-4 and this is according to the HNO 2021 Severity Mastersheet. Apart, during the past months ZOA has implemented different projects in the same subdistricts and done assessments, therefore we are aware of the needs in the targeted areas. The number of the targeted beneficiaries are also identified based on these assessments, sector needs as well as feedbacks collected from different ZOA projects.

project_name: Projet de renforcement de la préparation et réponses aux urgences sanitaires aux Tchad
project_objective: Ameliorer la sante des refugies, des retournes et des deplaces dans les provinces du Lac , logone occidentale et orientale en donnant les medicaments et equipement aux structures d' accueil, en renforcant la capacite du personnel et en ameliorant la sante neonatale.

project_name: Approvisionnement en eau potable et assainissement de base en faveur des populations affectees par les conflits dans la province du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
L’attaque de Boko Haram dans le bassin du lac Tchad et l'offensive de l'armee gouvernementale a Boma a augmente le nombre des refugies nigerians, nigeriens et des personnes deplacees dans la province du Lac.  Ce projet permettra d'ameliorer les conditions de vie et de sante des personnes retournees, IDP's et les communautes hautes a travers l'approvisionnement en eau potable, assainissement et la promotion des bonnes pratiques d'hygiene y compris les mesures barrieres de la COVID-19  dans la province du Lac affectees par les attaques de Boko Haram. Les femmes et les enfants representent plus de 50% de cette population affectees.   
Le projet reponds aux besoins identifiés par le Cluster WASH pour  une population cible de 100 000 personnes  en assurant l'accès à l'eau potable et un paquet d'interventions WASH pour les nouveaux déplacés, les retournés et les populations hotes dans la Province du Lac.

project_name: Emergency nutrition response to people affected by food and nutrition crises in the Sahel belt of Chad
project_objective: The 16 priority provinces for 2021 are targeted to strengthen the national capacity to improve access to treatment for 265,141 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition in the existing nutrition treatment units, both the outpatient (OTPs) and inpatient units (IPFs). The preventive nutrition services will be strengthen at community and health facility levels. This will include provision of much needed supplies and equipment, capacity building of frontline health staff and technical support within the health system and quarterly field monitoring visits. At the community level, the actions will integrate early detection of growth faltering and referral while building the capacity of mothers and caregivers on essential nutrition actions including adequate young child feeding practices to prevent all forms of malnutrition. The ministry of health will be supported to reinforce the coordination mechanism at both national and provincial level. This action will also contribute to the measles response through Vitamin A supplementation for 813,403 children and reduce micronutrient deficiency for 99,324 children.

project_name: Appui à la protection des Enfants vulnérables affectés par les situations humanitaires dans les provinces du Lac et Logone Oriental
project_objective:
Le Projet vise à renforcer le soutien aux filles/garçons et femmes affectés par les situations humanitaires en créant un environnement protecteur à travers le renforcement du système de protection de l'enfance mis en place dans la Province du Lac et dans le Logone Oriental.
Ce projet renforcera et consolidera le système de protection de l'enfance mis en place dans les Provinces du Lac et du Logone Oriental. 
Il prend en compte la pandemie du COVID-19 ainsi que les besoins restants à la suite des interventions en 2020 dans les domaines d’appui psychosocial ; de séparation et réintégration familiale ; des violences, exploitation et des violations graves contre les enfants (Résolution du C.S. 1612), surtout l’enrôlement des enfants par les groupes armés non étatique ainsi que le l’enregistrement des naissances des enfants à l’Etat civil.
La protection des enfants et de leurs familles (les meres/soignantes) sera appuyée en renforçant les capacités des acteurs de protection de l’enfant et des autres entités étatiques (nationales/ décentralisées) et la résilience communautaire. 
Cet appui vise aussi à harmoniser le paquet de services auxquels auront accès les enfants et les femmes vulnérables à travers la mise en œuvre des guidances sectorielles :
-	Sur la prise en charge psychosociale groupale et communautaire dans les espaces amis des enfants mobiles et des espaces surs.
-	L’identification et la prise en charge des enfants et femmes victimes ou a risque de protection y compris les survivant des violences basées sur le genre.
-	Identification, prise en charge et réunification des enfants séparés et non accompagnes et les enfants associés aux groupes armés.
-	L’enregistrement des naissances a l’état civil des enfants non déclarés.
Un accent sera mis sur la réinsertion socio-économique des enfants ENA/S, des adolescentes et EAFGA afin d’accélérer la transition de la réponse humanitaire à la programmation de développement. 
Il prend en compte les différents besoins des femmes, filles et garçons, y compris les enfants et femmes vivant avec handicap, les enfants chefs de ménage, les femmes chefs de ménage,  les enfants vivant avec les personnes âgées ainsi que la protection transversale.
De même, ce projet soutiendra la mise en place des structures de protection communautaire, qui auront comme responsabilités la détection des cas d’enfants victimes de violence, abus ou exploitation. 
Afin que les enfants aient accès aux différents services présent dans ces deux provinces. Un accent sera mis sur les séances d’induction et renforcement des capacites pour les différents secteurs inclus dans la reponse humanitaire sur le référencement et la prise en charge adequate des enfants et des meres et aussi sur la Prevention de l'Exploitation Sexuelle et Abus. 
Enfin, des actions de préparation et de réponses aux urgences seront mises en œuvre afin d’accroitre la résilience des enfants affectés. L’action ciblera les enfants des communautés hôtes, les déplacées internes ainsi que les retournés. Certaines interventions liées à la préparation et la réponse aux urgences seront mises en œuvre

project_name: Prevention of the forcible transfer of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem through humanitarian assistance and evidence-based advocacy
project_objective:
This multi-sector Project will support the West Bank Protection Consortium (the Consortium) to deliver assistance to 50,924 Palestinians at risk of forcible transfer in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem due to recurrent violations of international law. Building on previous risks and vulnerability analyzes, the Action addresses the protection needs of persons and communities of concern through a multi-sectoral approach that reduces vulnerabilities, builds capacities and responds to threats. 
Specifically, the Project aims at: (1) preventing and responding to protection incidents  (demolitions, settler-related, military operations) with emergency assistance (cash and in-kind) and protective measures (RESPONSIVE ACTIVITIES); (2) mitigating protection risks for highly vulnerable communities (150) through synergizing community-based protection, the provision of basic and social infrastructure, legal aid and stakeholder mobilization, including mitigating the risk of Covid-19 through the delivery of WASH and health infrastructure, and hygiene and RCCE awareness materials (REMEDIAL ACTIVITIES); and (3) promoting increased respect for IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations through coalition advocacy undertaken with Third States, International Organizations, Palestinian authorities and media outlets (ENVIRONMENT-BUILDING ACTIVITIES).
Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Policy Framework and facilitates coordination with other actors addressing the humanitarian and protection needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers for demolitions and settler-related incidents. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSL, legal aid and emergency responses and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs.  Consequently, the Project is envisaged to contribute to the realization of the following HRP objectives: 1. Increased respect for International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL) and accountability for violations; 2. Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence.
Implementing partners will also submit projects as individual agencies, which will include some of the same activities (including legal aid services; shelter upgrades). Some of these projects will complement this Project’s assistance, but will respond to a logic of ‘contiguity’ rather than ‘continuity’, since they are informed by different rationales and approaches. For this reason, financial resources will be kept separated. Our planning, monitoring and reporting systems prevent any duplication

project_name: Provision of  Lifesaving Food Security and Livelihood Support to Crisis-Affected IDPs and Host Community in Banadir and Middle Shabelle of Somalia.
project_objective:
According to FSNAU Technical Release of September 30th 2020, up to 2.1 million people across Somalia are projected to face food consumption gaps, high acute malnutrition, or depletion of assets indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes through December 2020, should humanitarian assistance not be available. An estimated 849 900 under the age of five are also likely face acute malnutrition through August 2021. The report further projects additional 3million people will to be Stressed (IPC Phase 2), bringing the total number of people facing acute food insecurity to 5.1 million. The report attributes this to combined effects of widespread and severe flooding, Desert Locust infestation, socioeconomic impacts of COVID-19 and the cumulative impacts of previous shocks.
The 2020 Deyr (October-December) rainfall season is projected to perform be below average to average across the country, which could lead to drought and trigger a worse humanitarian situation if the 2021 Gu (April-June) season rainfall delays or under performs.
The situation is exacerbated by continued displacement of persons in the country, with key drivers being cyclical climate shocks, including drought and flooding, which is challenging traditional rural livelihoods, and ongoing conflict. 2.6 persons are currently displaced out of whom 893,000 were displaced between January and August 2020 due to conflict, flooding and lack of livelihoods. Compounding this is high poverty rates among the urban poor which account for 64%. This is likely to go up by 10% should there be slightest trigger of economic and climatic shock (HNO, FSC page)
The 2020 Gu seasonal flooding (river flooding) contributed to loss and damage to property, housing, farmland and infrastructure. The riverine areas of Hiran, Middle Shabelle, Lower Shabelle, Gedo, Middle Juba and Lower Juba were some of the worst-affected areas. The COVID-19 pandemic and associated socio-economic impacts also contributed to the food insecurity situation in Somalia. Conflict/insecurity led to further population displacement and disruption to 2020 Gu season agriculture in some areas, including Lower Shabelle and Middle Juba.

Aid Vision proposed project is aimed at providing access to lifesaving and sustaining food security and livelihood interventions to 25,000 crisis affected population in Banadir and Middle Shabelle Regions, Aid Vision has presence in the two regions for over two decades and established networks of community structures and  with local authorities. The project will provide Cash Based interventions, rehabilitation of farming infrastructure through canal rehabilitation, provision farm equipment and tools, supply of certified seeds, fuel subsidies, and training of farmers on contemporary farming techniques, provision of fertilizers and provision of agricultural extension services. It is envisioned that the interventions will go a long way in improving food security in the target regions and enhance community resilience to shocks in future.

project_name: Addressing Acute Food Insecurity in Gedo and Galgaduud regions in Southern Somalia
project_objective:
6.3 million Somalis are acutely food insecure through June 2020, a 36% increase since late 2019. This includes 2.1 million Somalis in IPC 3-4 (double an average year) and 4.2 million in IPC 2 (the highest on record). The situation deteriorated most significantly in rural areas, where the population in IPC 2-4 doubled and IPC 3-4 tripled. Since 2016, six out of seven rainy seasons have been poor, including Gu 2019 which yielded Somalia’s lowest cereal harvest in decades in southern Somalia. Pastoralists also struggle to recover from significant livestock losses and debt incurred from the protracted drought. ADA’s project is expected to directly assist 20,549 households (123,294 people) spread across the two regions of Gedo and Galgaguud, Somalia hence contributing across FSC’s three strategic objectives (SOs).

To improve immediate access to food (SO1),ADA will deliver cash assistance to 7800 households through cash-for-work (CFW) to repair community infrastructures and 8200 households through integrated cash and livelihood Programmes (Cash+). Beneficiaries will receive 3-6 monthly cash transfers, based on duration of the lean season and their vulnerability. To support transition out of emergency cash programmes, ADA will offer lighter and longer-term cash and livelihood assistance to the most chronically vulnerable households in the target districts with high recurrence of IPC 3-4. ADA’s cash programme assists severely food insecure people to meet their food immediate needs, while giving them choice and re-injecting cash into the local economy. ADA delivers cash through mobile money operators and money vendors, adopts rates recommended by the Cash Working Group and regularly monitors the availability and prices of selected food and non-food commodities in local markets through the support of FSNAU.

To protect and restore livelihoods (SO2), ADA will provide quality production inputs and training to Cash+ beneficiaries and an additional 2460 vulnerable households. Tailored livelihood support packages will enable farmers to secure a Gu/ Deyr harvest, pastoralists to enhance milk production and coastal communities to improve fish catch and processing. The project will further enhance production and promote climate smart practices through field school approaches, targeting 1044 farming and pastoral households that will pass on the knowledge to their wider communities. To protect livestock assets, ADA together with FAO and the Somali Ministry of Livestock and Veterinary Services will conduct region-wide livestock treatment and vaccination campaigns to protect thousands of animals; and deliver emergency water supply and animal feed in the case of severe drought (1045 vulnerable households).

To build resilience and mitigate new shocks (SO3) at a community level, the project will improve water management and related infrastructure to protect rural populations and livelihoods against flooding (repaired river embankments) and cope with drought (fenced water catchments, animal troughs, canal sluice gates).

project_name: Improved Food Security and Provision of Seasonal Livelihood Inputs for Food In-secure Households In Lower-Shabelle and Galgaduud Regions.
project_objective:
Due to the combined effects of widespread and severe flooding, Desert Locust infestation, socioeconomic impacts of COVID-19 and the cumulative impacts of previous shocks, up to 2.1 million people across Somalia are expected to face food consumption gaps or depletion of assets indicative of Crisis                (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes through December 2020 in the absence of humanitarian assistance. In addition, 849 900 children under the age of five are likely to be acutely malnourished through August 2021-(FSNAU-Technical Release-Sep-2020). The 2020 Deyr (October-December) rainfall season is likely to be below average to average across the country, which could lead to drought and trigger a worsening of the humanitarian situation if the 2021 Gu (April-June) season rainfall is also delayed or performs poorly. Severe riverine and flash floods in April and early May caused significant population displacement and damage to property, infrastructure, farmland, and crops. Atypically heavy rain since July led to further riverine flooding and flood-related damage. The proposed project aims at life-sustaining interventions and other life savings which will include conditional and unconditional cash transfer. The project also proposes recovery initiatives such as skills development for women and youth, livelihood assets creation, provision of agricultural inputs for improved production. The food security project works in close collaboration with stakeholders from the humanitarian organizations, local authorities, and both the public and private sectors to promote the cash programming support.
