ARC will Provide 10 Strategic boreholes in drought-prone locations in lascanood, telex and Cel- Afweyen district with Generators, submersible pumps, cable wires and control panels to ensure drought affected peoples have access to safe, adequate and reliable water.ARC will establish  6 Pipeline water extensions to identified IDPs Camps and non- IDPs camps including construction of elevated water storage tanks, installation of solar powered systems  and water kiosk with a minimum of 6 taps  to ensure increased access to adequate water by the IDPs and Non-IDPs.
ARC will construct/rehabilitate 2000 gender-segregated, disability-friendly communal latrines for IDPs and vulnerable host community members who have no access to any sanitation facilities.
ARC will construct for the targeted sex-Disaggregated, Disability Inclusive 40 Institutional latrines with water and Handwashing facilities for 24 target schools and 15 health centers.
Hygiene promotion will remain a key component of the intervention to prevent the spread of Covid 19 and others WASH-related diseases through risk communications and community engagement promoting behavior changes. Hygiene kits and basic MHM kits will be provided to adolescent girls in schools and villages/camps. ARC will target approximately 71, 800 beneficiaries from North and south-central Somalia (11488 women, 7180 men, 22165 boys, 23069 girls, 5744 disabled, and 2154 elderly people).
ARC will consult men, boys, girls, elderly, and people with disabilities on their needs and preference regarding the type, Design and location of the water and sanitation facilities to address barriers relating to access. ARC will involve women, boys, girls and disabled people in the project monitoring and feedback sought.

project_name: Provision of protection services to the most vulnerable IDP in Middle Shabelle, Lower Shabelle and Bay Regions, Somalia
project_objective: Covid-19 pandemic, coupled by Gu 2020 seasonal flooding and sustained conflict in Middle and Lower Shabelle and Bay Regions has impacted to increased numbers displaced populations in  IDP camps  where they live in informal and unplanned settlements under very deplorable living conditions. Women and Young Girls' condition are worsened by increased exposure to violence, exploitation and discrimination and other forms of abuse worsened by very serious risks and threats to their safety and security.  Of particular focus are persons with disabilities face increased risks of exploitation, abuse and discrimination while accessing assistance meant for them hence strong need for their inclusion in the project right from the beginning of the project throughout the implementing period including monitoring, till completion. Its against this background that the project intends to provide timely and  appropriate protection services to increase protection of boys and girls and vulnerable displaced  and marginalized women as well as those with disabilities. The project targets total of 9190 women including GBV survivors  those those with disabilities.

project_name: Scaling up of protection services to vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons in Banadir region.
project_objective: Most of the 2.6 million IDPs in Somalia live in informal and unplanned settlements where living conditions are poor and forced eviction is a common threat. Safety and security concerns remain a high priority for all affected populations, with displacement contributing to immediate and heightened exposure to violence, exploitation and other forms of abuse. Serious risks and threats to safety and security. The protection needs in Somalia changed and evolved over time. The current crisis affects individuals of all ages and genders, as well as from diverse social backgrounds, in different ways and scale. The most vulnerable groups include people with physical, sensorial, intellectual and mental disabilities, adolescent girls and boys, pregnant and lactating women and girls, female and child-headed households, unaccompanied and separated children, persons from minority clans, older persons without caregivers, persons missing documentation, persons facing eviction, persons living in areas with armed conflict and violence. Women and adolescent girls from 18 – 50 years old (including those living with disabilities) are subjected to Intimate Partner Violence, rape, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment and abuse. Low reporting of GBV cases persist due to stigmatization, victim blaming, shame and interference by clan and religious leaders, slow access to justice and weak or lack of legal framework for the protection of women and girls from GBV. Persons with disabilities face various physical, attitudinal and institutional barriers to access food, health, shelter and protection on an equal basis with others. Persons with disabilities are estimated to be at least 15% of the population and  the majority are among the poorest part of the population. They also face disability-based discrimination, which is exacerbated in situations of crisis, and when it intersects with other factors, such as poverty, gender or age. To mitigate the above mentioned challenge, SSWC will conduct  meetings and consult with people living with disabilities throughout the project phases.  Transportation plans for people living with disabilities will be made for easy access to our centres and our field monitors will ensure that they target households with people living with disabilities in their daily visits within the target areas. Up to 66 per cent of the population in need in Somalia are children who continue to be exposed to threats of recruitment, abuse, neglect, abduction, exploitation and violence. Hence, 1.88 million children including 10% of children with disabilities need immediate child protection services. Boys and girls of all ages in Somalia continue to endure multiple protection risks and violations of their rights including family separation, sexual and physical violence, killing and maiming, psycho social distress, worst forms of child labor, widespread recruitment and use of children, forced and protracted. SSWC wants to address GBV and child protection programming due to high number of Incidents of GBV this is as a result of reported cases, predominantly in IDP sites throughout the country. The objective of the project is to fill up  the existing critical gaps in protection targeting 50,000 beneﬁciaries in Banadir district. The purpose of the intervention is to significantly reduce the incidents of GBV, promote awareness on prevention and response to GBV and provide child protection services to the community living in Banadir. Protection activities include provision of psychosocial support, Medical referrals, legal aid counselling, distribution of emergency social assistance (dignity kits), awareness and sensitization on GBV prevention and response, Capacity building for community structures on GBV prevention and response and comprehensive case management services at the Women Wellness centers and Safe houses.Establishment of Child friendly spaces, facilitation of psycho-social support for children including play therapy, art work and drawing.

project_name: Shelter and NFIs Assistance for Crisis-Affected Populations including IDPs, Returnees and Poor host communities in Banadir, Lower shabelle, Bay and Hiiraan regions- Somalia.
project_objective:
According to draft 2021 HNO that revealed that 3.15 million people are in need of shelter and NFIs assistance due to prolonged humanitarian issues caused by recurrent drought, conflict, and floods and due to inadequate shelter conditions, overcrowding, economic, hardship, and lack of security of tenure. 

In consideration of severity factors, this project is to strengthen the protection and address life-saving needs of IDP families and poor host communities through Shelter and NFIs response in Kaxda and Daynile districts of Banadir region, Lower Afgoye and Marka districts of Lower Shabelle region, Baidoa district of Bay region, and Beledeweyne of Hiiraan region in South and Central Somalia including women-headed household families, extended families, families with disabled and elderly persons who are most in need of humanitarian assistance to mitigate risk and its consequences on crisis-affected populations at the target areas. The main objective is to improve the living conditions and safe access to services of IDP families including refugee returnees and poor host communities in the targeted locations. HINNA aims at providing 4800 ESKs and NFI kits to 4800 HHs (28,800 beneficiaries/Individuals) while 2,880 (10%) people of them will be poor host communities through in-kind distribution to improve the living conditions of the target beneficiaries who faced inadequate shelter/NFIs conditions. The reason we can't use cash transfer programming for this project is that we have had several meetings with the communities in some of the project target areas and most of them have told us that this type of program can cause insecurity, family violence that can lead to family breakdown and other things including missing kits or rising market prices.
Through this project disaggregation of gender will be promoted in full consideration with protection mainstreaming. The total beneficiaries of the project (28,800 people) of the drought, floods, and conflict-affected populations in Banadir region (Daynile and Kaxda districts), Lower Shabelle region (Afgoye and Marka districts), Bay region (Baidoa district) including (4320 women, 4320 men, 9504 boys, and 9504 girls) including 1152 elderly people (4%) will directly be receiving any benefits of the project based on their need of shelter and NFIs assistance through selection criteria set by the shelter cluster.

project_name: Increased Access to WASH Services by Vulnerable IDP and Host Communities in Jubaland, Banadir and Galgadud
project_objective:
The project aims to increase WASH services to the over 4.6M people in need in Somalia targeting districts that are categorized as stressed or severe in the severity scale, those that are hard to reach and those that have reported AWD/cholera cases. The project targets approximately   7,164 vulnerable IDPs 16,716 host communities with a special focus on vulnerable segments of the community including 5, 383women, 12, 895children 3582 PLWD and 1194 elderly people. 
In line with HRP strategic objective 1, specific objective 1.2, this project will contribute to the WASH cluster objective of delivering life-saving WASH assistance to reduce acute needs among most vulnerable settlements and communities through emergency water tracking, water vouchers, provision of hygiene kits and hygiene promotion activities. Lifesaving Wash assistance will target hard to reach communities in Garbaharey and Elwak districts and IDPs households in Banadir, Kismayo, Dolow Belet Hawa.  This project is also aligned to HRP strategic objective 2, specific objective 2.1, contributing to WASH cluster objective of restoring access to safe and equitable basic WASH services to vulnerable communities and in schools. This will be achieved through rehabilitation of water infrastructures including shallow wells, water pipe network, elevated tanks and water kiosks. Solar pumping systems will be installed in boreholes and shallow wells to reduce the O&M of community water systems. Community mobilizations and capacity building in management of water projects and O&M of solar system will be done to ensure active community participation in the implementation and management of the water facilities. This project will also contribute to the WASH cluster objective of restoring access to basic sanitation and hygiene in schools in Abudwak and Dussammarreeb, through rehabilitation of gender segregated latrines with lockable doors from inside with hand washing facilities.  
All the WASH infrastructures proposed in this project are designed with consideration of the safety, equity and easy accessibility by vulnerable groups such as women, girls, PLWD and the elderly. The target beneficiaries will actively participate in the selection of the sites for water facilities in their locations that will be strategic to serve households within approximately 500m distance that will be in open and clear places to ensure safety of users. Additionally water kiosks will be designed to ensure easy water collection by girls, women, elderly and those with disabilities. For water trucking water collection points will be selected by the beneficiaries and will be at about 500m from the households and in open places for safety purposes. The water collection will be planned such that the elderly and PLWD will have separate times to collect their water. The latrines constructed in schools will be strategically located to ensure safety of users and dignity of users. Hygiene kits will be collected from reasonable distances from the beneficiary households for safety of the beneficiaries as they carry them home. Use of water and hygiene kits vouchers will further enhance safety and equity of vulnerable groups targeted in this project. Mainstreaming of protection and gender in this project will contribute to HRP strategic objective 3, specific objective 3.1 as well as the WASH cluster objective of maintaining safety, equity and accessibility of the vulnerable groups (including women, boys, girls, elderly and people with disabilities) when accessing WASH services. This project will build on WASH and COVID 19 interventions implemented by NAPAD (2019 and 2020) in Galgadud, Jubaland and Banadir regions that includes rehabilitation of water infrastructures such as water tanks, water pipe networks, installation of solar water pumping systems, installation of hand washing facilities, provision of hygiene kits and mass hygiene promotion using the mass media and door to door promotion by community hygiene

project_name: Provision of Emergency life-saving Primary and Secondary Health care, for crisis affected populations in Baardhere, Ceelwaaq, Garbaharey, Dollow in Gedo and Banadir region Somalia
project_objective: This project seeks to support 5 mobile outreach and 9 static health facilities  to reach out  most vulnerable women  men, boys and girls  through provision of health services in 4 districts including Bardhere, Elwak, Doolow and  Garbaharey to populations including IDPs and hard to reach communities , conflict and drought affected people by ensuring access to Universal Health Care covering primary and secondary health care through 8 facilities, 3 in Bardera District which is Bardhere District Hospital, Ali cato MCH/ Geriley MCH IDP,4 facilities in Elwak which include Elwak District Hospital, Dhamasa MCH, Geriley MCH and Husqurun, one facility in Dollow which is Doolow MCH/Kabasa IDps  and Garbaharey –Buurdhuubo Health centre MCH in Garbaharey District through the provision of services including outpatient consultations for both males and females (boys and girls included), child health services, immunizations for both children under five and Women of Child Bearing Age; Reproductive health services including Family planning promotion and integrated method mix counseling and service delivery, Focused Antenatal Care HDC proposes to undertake a life-saving emergency primary and secondary healthcare services to Disaster-Affected Communities (DACs) IDPs, returnees, and host communities in Baardhere, Ceelwaq, Garbaharey, Dollow in Gedo and Banadir Region. The humanitarian situation in Somalia has remind Fragile; due to wide-spread insecurity, lack of resources and fragmentation of the health sector in Somalia particularly in Baardhere, Garbaharey, Ceelwaaq and Dollow, makes it difficult the availability and access  of emergency live-saving primary and secondary healthcare services to crisis affected populations. The current impact of the new threats of Covid-19, locust infestations and floods compounds an already dire situation. Furthermore, Maternity services are lacking in 74% of IDP settlements. In particular, displaced and marginalized groups face barriers to healthcare and higher exposure to diseases. Somalia has a high mortality rate for children under 5 years old (U5MR) at 27.2 per 1000 live births; the leading causes are reported to be pneumonia (24%), diarrhea (19%) and measles (12%), as well as neonatal disorders (17%), which are predisposed by malnutrition. In addition, Somalia has less than 40% of its target of two health facilities per 10,000 population and has only 19% of its target skilled health workforce. Proposed project location usually experience cases of gender based violence mostly against women and girls. There is heightened gender based violence (GBV) risks for displaced women and girls in Ceel Waaq, Baardhere, Dollow, Garbaharey and Banadir districts who are currently living in makeshift shelters and have no adequate food, water and sanitation services. The major GBV risk to IDP women and adolescent girls is a threat of sexual violence. Health services for GBV services is only available in the main towns which is distant from the IDP locations where the recently displaced population live. Major gaps in GBV services includes lack of safety and security services; safety facilities are cited as being unavailable. Priority needs are safe shelters, gender segregated and designed to reduce risks of violence for women and girls. Access to health GBV responses need to be improved through increased community awareness of existing services and referral transportation provision. Furthermore, high stress situation caused by poverty, violence such as rape and abuse against women, lack of jobs and use of drugs and stimulants such as khat causes mental illness in project target areas. Men, women and the youth are pre-disposed to this distress situations. HDC will provide treatment and psychosocial support and counselling to affected men, women boys and girls. Integrate psychosocial support (PSS) services into the community services offered by Care Group volunteers and facilitate to provide mental health services .Case fatalit

project_name: Enhancing Child Protection response services with focus on unaccompanied/ separated boys and girls in Banaadir, Lower Shebelle, Lower Juba and Gedo Region.
project_objective:
The Project Objective is to reduce child protection risks faced by conflict-affected children & adolescents through the provision of well-coordinated, gender-sensitive appropriate & quality child protection services. The key focus will be to prevent and respond to separation of children from their families by strengthening community based child protection mechanism for prevention of separation and build capacity of protection service providers and stakeholders to facilitate appropriate referrals and strengthen coordination in service delivery to ensure quality comprehensive services to unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). 

The project will support 3500 Unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) through comprehensive in family tracing and reunification in line with minimum standards and inter-agency (IA) information and management systems (IMS), initiate appropriate alternative care arrangements & train 500 foster families (All women) to provide interim care & temporary foster care support targeting 80% of UASC identified children. 500 foster families will be provided with food and Nutritional support to ease the economic burden on the families. Community sensitization /outreach services will be conducted targeting caregivers on prevention of family separation, child recruitment, risk education, targeting education and community members. In addition, the project will seek to increase the capacity of target communities to identify, report, and refer children with urgent child protection concerns as well as to provide psychosocial support services in the long term. Activities will focus on the establishing community-based child protection mechanisms training and mentoring them and raising awareness about existing referral pathways.          

The implementation of the above-mentioned activities is expected to reduce the risks which are currently faced by the targeted children boys and girls in these areas. This will further enhance and improve the coordination and support of the existing services which are being provided by other local and international NGOs working in the area. With the above mentioned needs, the proposed project is designed to improve the living conditions of boys and girls living in conflict affected population by providing child protection response targeting 24,000 vulnerable children in Banaadir, Lower Shebelle, Lower Juba and Gedo Regions.

The proposed intervention has been designed in a way to enable children to fully access and enjoy their rights, safety and dignity, while at the same time avoiding harm. All project activities will be carried out in accordance with AGDM principles: equal participation of girls, boys will be integral part of the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the overall project. NoFYL will ensure that key cross-cutting issues are mainstreamed into the proposed intervention including age, gender, diversity, environment and human rights. Gender and disability inclusion will remain a key focus, guaranteeing consultation with children when undertaking protection assessments through staffs accessing them and identifying their needs. 

The safety and dignity of children will be prioritized by ensuring confidentiality, prioritizing the best interests of the child and respecting the wishes of parents/caregivers, where they do not endanger the child further. All measures to respect and adhere to the Do No Harm approach will be taken during the process of beneficiary selection, service provision and data collection and management. Specialized services and useful information about service providers will be provided to all beneficiaries that meet the vulnerability criteria, including both IDP and host communities.

project_name: Providing NFI and shelter assistance to the displaced and affected population in Bay, Bakol, lower juba & Lower Shabelle in south central Somalia.
project_objective:
Climate shocks including drought and flooding as well as ongoing conflict contributes to internal displacement in Somalia, with an estimated 2.6M men, women, girls and boys who are currently displaced. This people/ IDPs are now living in IDP camps with lack of enough basic services including shelter, The 2020 Gu’ Season flooding has caused several displacement, damage of properties, housing, farmland and social amenities and also Massive displacement especially in the river rine areas of Middle Lower Shabelle areas. 
This areas are also prone to conflict crises particularly in South Central Somalia where part of it is under al-shabaab control hence contributes to more displacement and increase the need of the IDPs who were already in need 0f basic services, this also contributes to the protection concerns of vulnerable groups e.g. women, girls and  people with specific needs and also people with disabilities.
 Through this project, Juba Foundation aims to address the humanitarian needs of the displaced IDPs and poor host communities in poor shelter conditions in south central Somalia.
The project will focus on improving the lives & dignity of IDPs and poor host communities across Somalia through the provision of locally purchased Non food items (NFIs) Emergency shelter kits (Esks) through in-kind distribution where feasible and if there is functional market with shelter and NFI materials cash or voucher can be an option. But at the moment Juba Foundation is Flexible to use either cash or in-kind Distribution. 
For the beneficiaries’ selection and registration, juba foundation will give consideration to the female headed Household. People with specific needs among other households. The host communities will also be given consideration with selection of 20 – 30 %, similarly 15% will be selected from persons with disabilities in each project.
Juba Foundation will ensure the affected population will have full protection and improve their dignity and living conditions through the provision of appropriate emergency shelter kits (Esks) for each household will receive ESK( type 2 with a size of 4.4m x 3.6m)  depending on land availability. For the provision of NFIs each household will be provided with one NFI kit as per the cluster guidelines along with the Esks. 
The proposed intervention will focus on providing of Esks (1,500) and NFIs (1,500) that consist of 1 plastic sheet, 3 blankets, 2 sleeping mats, 1 kitchen set, 1 solar lamp, 1 mosquito net and 2 jerricans. That will total up to 9,000 Individuals.
Juba foundation will train the camp leaders and camp committees on selection of beneficiaries, HLP issues, site planning to ensure all shelter and NFI projects meet the required cluster standard.

project_name: Strengthen safe access to multi sectorial services at site level through improved site management and coordination through Improvement of living conditions of displaced people through site development, care and maintenance and self-management within selected districts of Lower Juba, Gedo, Bay, Bakool, and Lower Shabelle Region of south central Somalia
project_objective:
In the midst of increasing IDP caseload in Somalia, Juba Foundation is submitting this proposal with the aim of enhancing the living conditions of the Internally Displaced People (IDPs) through enhanced coordination, access to information and multi-sectoral services at site level, site maintenance, and durable solutions. Proposed interventions will covers IDPs in need in Bakol, Bay, Lower Shabelle, Lower Juba, and Gedo . Combined, these regions host 1,337,000 IDPs, or 51% of the entire IDP population in Somalia (OCHA HNO 2020). This project aim is to focus on Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) activities undertaken in selected districts of Bay, Bakool, Gedo, Lower Juba and Lower Shabelle by enhancing the overall protective environment for flood affected population, increasing access to basic services linked to different sectors, reducing the risk thereof, and availing specialized support assistance to beneficiaries to help them address other interconnected protection concerns. 

To achieve cluster objectives, Juba Foundation will undertake a number of interrelated and complementary activities including setting up and strengthening of camp governance structures where necessary to enhance information-sharing and foster system-wide coordination among service providers. Besides, we will support community-led site maintenance activities through cash for work schemes to ensure upkeep of sites, enhance hygiene and sanitation levels and contribute to overall reduction in communicable diseases. Where necessary, JF will implement emergency site improvement projects to minimize protection risks and ensure safety. Key program activities will also include service mapping and site monitoring processes that will be carried out in close coordination with the CCCM cluster and other partners to effectively address existing gaps and maximize eﬃciency of the humanitarian response. Compiling of a master list of sites and mapping of both accessible infrastructure and partners operating in sites will be prioritized to enhance service delivery and coordination. In the selection of beneficiaries to participate in program activities. We will adapt a systematic approach with a clear criterion to prioritize most vulnerable households including the marginalized, single headed-households, large families and/or families with children under the age of 5, women at risk as identified by protection oﬃcers and those with special needs. Data collected to inform beneficiary selection will be segregated by gender to ensure that no group is left-out. The effectiveness of the aid package will be evaluated through monitoring of activities thus ensuring that beneficiaries access their services safely and in a dignified manner. Protection will be mainstreamed throughout project duration by closely coordinating with other partners operating Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) crisis centers and facilitating principled referrals where necessary. An elaborate feedback and complain mechanism will be setup to ensure accountability to the affected population.
JF with the presence in the targeted regions/ districts will ensure that there is proper coordination to ensure quality service delivery to the beneficiaries. JF has focal points in each of the district of which they have often participated in the assessments within the settlement schemes where IDPs have settled. therefore JF has proper access to the targeted areas proposed.

project_name: Reduction of morbidity and mortality related to severe acute malnutrition through integrated outpatient therapeutic feeding programs among IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Lower Shabelle and Bay regions of Somalia.
project_objective:
Across Somalia, current estimates indicate that 1 in 10 children under the age of five is acutely malnourished with the median National GAM of 13.8 percent at Serious level, translating to 1.08M boys and girls of which 178,000 are affected by life threatening severely malnutrition while 830,000 are moderately malnourished. A further 832,000 pregnant and lactating women are estimated to be in need of nutrition assistance. Poor nutrition conditions amongst both these population groups are the result of both shock and underlying factors, with conflict, political instability, displacement and changing climate conditions continuing to put immense pressure on access to basic services and intensifying exposure to nutritional deprivations. This includes sub-optimal access to health services, poor childcare practices, seasonal food insecurity, limited access to potable water, and poor hygiene and sanitation practices. For example, the Joint Multi-Cluster Needs Assessment conducted across Somalia shows that 73% of households reported that at least one child was ill, with malaria being the most common condition reported, whilst 26% of non-displaced households and 41% of IDP households reported inadequate access to water.
In this project, NWO will improve the access and utilization of Emergency integrated Nutrition services for women and children living in the most affected areas in Lower Shabelle and Bay regions using both static and mobile sites. The static nutrition sites will be strengthened by integrating WASH and health Services, provision of nutrition supplies and the improvement of staff capacity. Remote villages will be reached through mobile clinics; community mobilizers and CNWs will be recruited and trained. Among the activities that NWO will be providing include: Immunization to under 5 children; Treatment of uncomplicated malnourished cases i.e SAM; Promote the adoption of good health and hygiene practices to the affected communities; Breast feeding promotion and support for infant and young child feeding; Identify and assist in the training of community volunteers on nutrition promotion and education; MUAC screening and identification of malnourished children; Distribution of standard IEC materials for social mobilization; MUAC screening for all children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW); Treatment of SAM cases without medical complications; Referral of SAM cases with medical complications and failed appetite test. Under this project, NWO will scale up its intervention through fixed integrated Nutrition sites and mobile services targeting 47,757 drought affected people IDPs and Host communities. The project will target all gender groups such as Pregnant Women, Boys and girls will be able to use the services of the nutrition facilities. Community Nutrition Workers and project staff to be trained will be composed of male and female. Men and women will be given equal opportunities when recruiting staff for the project. All social groups, including, youth (male and female), community elders, representatives of minority/marginalized groups and people living with disability will be involved in the project activities. Persons living with disability and members from marginalized communities will be given special consideration in staffing. NWO will promote accountability and provide information to line ministries and donors about the progress of the project in terms of project activities. New ways will collect and use data dis-aggregated by sex, age and diversity to effectively inform programming.  NWO will work with the donor to ensure public trust and establish a system of transparency, community participation in conducting monitoring and evaluation. NWO will facilitate a dialogue between NWO and its affected populations over information provision.

project_name: Provide lifesaving WASH support for crises affected IDP and host communities in Somalia
project_objective: The 2021 WASH response aims to provide continuity of life-saving support for the most vulnerable host and internally displaced persons (IDP) communities affected by undernutrition, WASH related disease outbreaks, COVID-19 and climate/human induced disasters but will be adapted to shift the focus on activities addressing the direct consequences of COVID-19 and floods. While many shocks continue to have an impact on WASH, acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) and the COVID-19 crisis remain a current threat in Somalia and the situation is unlikely to change for the better as the 2020 Deyr season (October/November) is predicted to be below average to average and La-Nina is expected with a likelihood of drought.  Somalia will therefore most likely be faced with rising water scarcity, which requires greater investments in emergency water services and restoration of basic water supply services. The WASH response will contribute to prevention of a further increase in AWD, as well as raise awareness to prevent the spread of COVID19 through risk communication and community engagement, and support compliance to recommended measures through hygiene promotion, hygiene kits distribution and increased access to water and soap. To further improve the contribution of WASH to the achievement of health outcomes, the proposed WASH response will invest in improvements in hand hygiene behaviour and access to WASH facilities in health care facilities and other public institutions. The response will pay particular attention to the different WASH needs of vulnerable groups among the targeted IDPs and non-IDPs including the elderly, persons living with disabilities, women, girls and boys and closely engage them through targeted FGDs, KII and extensive consultations to plan and agree on age and disability-friendly WASH infrastructure designs and installation locations. ACF will support the establishment and training of committees to oversee the operation and management of communal WASH infrastructure. ACF will work with the communities targeted to ensure that the committees are representative of all groups within the community paying particular attention to gender, age, ethnicity, socioeconomic group, disability and tenancy agreements to ensure that the unique needs of each group are put into consideration. The response will target a total of 60,185 (17,033 Men, 16,490 Women, 13,331 Boys and 13,331 Girls) in Bakool, Lower Shabelle, Nugaal, Banadir, Hiran and Sool regions.

project_name: Réponse d'Urgence en SR pour 250000 femmes et filles parmi les plus vulnérable
project_objective:
La situation de pandémie de la COVID-19 couplée au nombre croissant des rapatriés qui arrivent au Burundi, parmi lesquelles on note un nombre important de femmes et filles, dans une situation de système de santé qui nécessite beaucoup d'appuis pour répondre aux besoins les plus élémentaires et parmi lesquels on retrouvent les gestes qui sauvent des vies, UNFPA se propose de cibler 250.000 femmes et filles en âge de procréer dans les provinces de Kirundo, Muyinga, Makamba, Ruyigi et Cankuzo. Plus spécifiquement le projet soumis se focalise sur les aspects de:
1. Renforcer les capacités techniques de 100 cadres des formations sanitaires des 5 provinces sur le Dispositifs Minimum d'Urgence (DMU), y compris la prévention de la COVID-19, particulièrement chez la femme enceinte,
2. Renforcer les capacités techniques de 100 prestataires de soins issus des centres de santé des cinq provinces sur le DMU, la prise en charge médicale des victimes de VBG y compris la prise en charge médicale des victimes de viol, la prévention de la transmission du VIH, la promotion de la Planification Familiale, .
3. Positionner des kits d'urgence en santé de la reproduction dans les hôpitaux et les centres de santé des cinq ainsi que des kits de dignités chez les femmes et filles en âge de procréer dans les provinces d'intervention du projet,
4. Organiser 5 campagnes de sensibilisation en ligne, via les radios communautaires, sur les thématiques en rapport avec la santé de la Reproduction, la Santé sexuelle et reproductive des jeunes et des adolescents, la prévention de la COVID-19, la prévention du VIH et des VBG.
5. Acquérir et distribuer des équipements de protection personnelles contre la COVID-19 pour le personnel des FOSA des provinces d'intervention du projet.

project_name: Renforcement de l’accès aux soins de santé primaires intégrant la santé sexuelle et reproductive des populations vulnérables dans un contexte de crise humanitaire et de COVID-19, au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à renforcer l’accès aux soins de santé primaires intégrant la santé sexuelle et reproductive des populations vulnérables dans les régions du Sahel, Centre Nord, Nord, Est, Centre-Est et la Boucle du Mouhoun fortement touchées par la crise humanitaire. Le résultat ultime sera d’améliorer la santé des populations, et surtout des femmes et adolescentes, à travers une augmentation de la couverture des services des soins de santé primaires incluant la santé sexuelle et reproductive dans les régions 6 régions fortement touchées par l’insécurité mais également touchées par la COVID-19. Les résultats intermédiaires seront de garantir l’accès aux services de soins de santé primaires et santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant la violence basée sur le genre et la violence sexuelle et l’utilisation des services de santé disponibles par les populations des régions ciblées spécialement les femmes et les adolescentes. 
Immédiatement dans la période de l’intervention : • Le projet assure la disponibilité des services des soins de santé promotionnels, préventifs et curatifs de qualité pour la population ciblée ; • Les activités communautaires ciblant toute la population mais avec des approches adaptées aux besoins spécifiques des femmes, des hommes, des adolescent-e-s, des filles et des garçons, sont structurées et organisées régulièrement et répondant aux besoins de la population en tenant compte de la COVID-19 ; • Les femmes, les adolescentes et les filles qui subissent des violences incluant des violences sexuelles bénéficient d’une prise en charge sanitaire de qualité et des références appropriés aux services complémentaires, avec le soutien de la communauté ;
• Les soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive de la population, de la femme et de la jeune fille sont renforcés au travers de la surveillance intégrée des maladies et la riposte, y compris la COVID-19. Les extrants ci-dessous seront rendus possibles à travers les interventions suivantes :
• Les formations sanitaires sont dotées en médicaments et matériels médicotechniques y inclut les intrants de laboratoires pour améliorer l’offre des soins de santé et Sexuelle et Reproductive de qualité incluant la VBG ; • Les personnels de santé et les réseaux communautaires des ASBC sont capacités et équipés pour assurer l’offre des soins de qualité pour la population y compris les besoins spécifiques des femmes et adolescentes en SSR ; • Les réseaux communautaires locaux sont capacités pour assurer l’organisations des séances de mobilisation et d’orientation communautaire sur les attitudes et changement de comportement face aux maladies à potentiel épidémiques y compris la COVID-19 et les violences faites aux femmes et aux filles ; • Les voix des femmes et des adolescentes sont au centre de l’élaboration et de la mise en œuvre du projet, et elles sont amplifiées en créant des plateformes de prise de parole et de décisions pour elles, tout en accompagnant les hommes et les adolescents pour qu’ils soutiennent les démarches de leadership féminin, Ces efforts nécessitent la création de lieux d’échanges et de débats sur les questions liées aux rôles traditionnels et actuels des femmes, des hommes, des filles et des garçons mais aussi des personnes âgées et des personnes en situation de handicap. • Les activités de mobilisation communautaire sont soutenues pour la diffusion d'informations et de messages clefs et adaptés aux différents groupes d’âge et sexe incluant le PDI sur la planification familiale et des informations sur les différents types de Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG), les conséquences sur la santé des femmes et des filles mais aussi sur les familles et la société au travers des réseaux communautaires ; • Les populations, les femmes et adolescentes en particulier bénéficient d’un soutien psychosocial et matériel pour la prévention des violences basées sur le genre ; A la fin du projet, 1 052 300 bénéficiaires directs seront touchés dans les 6 régions ciblées.

project_name: Soutien à la préparation et la prise en charge initiale des Urgences Sanitaire dans 8 provinces sanitaires cibles au Burundi
project_objective:
Le Burundi est périodiquement frappé par diverses épidémies dont les flambées les plus importantes sont le choléra, le paludisme, la rougeole, les méningites à méningocoque, et les zoonoses telles que la rage, avec le plus souvent, une mortalité et une morbidité élevées. A titre d'exemple, en 2019, le Burundi a été touché une importante épidémie de Choléra dans une dizaine de districts sanitaires du pays (en particulier les district sanitaires situés le long du Lac Tanganyika, répartis sur 6 provinces parmi les 18 que comptent le pays) qui ont fait 1258 cas avec une létalité estimée à 1%.  Lors de cette épidémie de choléra de 2019, la tranche d'âge la plus touchée est de 19 à 50 ans avec un sexe ratio égale à 1.  Ce phénomène de récurrence des épidémies au Burundi ne concerne pas seulement les maladies hydriques comme le choléra. En effet toujours en 2019, le pays a été touché une épidémie de paludisme avec  8 892 300 épisodes de paludisme enregistrés  parmi la population burundaise et 3 294 décès liés à cette pathologie. En 2020, c'est 4 726 501 épisodes de paludismes qui ont été enregistré dans le pays avec 2 711 décès.

Le contexte favorable à la survenue des épidémies, se justifie par de nombreux facteurs, en particulier, une succession de crises complexes, qui ont contribué à annihiler les efforts de l’Etat dans le secteur de la santé et à installer une bonne partie de la population dans un état de précarité chronique les exposants aux maladies transmissibles à fort potentiel épidémique. Parallèlement à ce contexte socio-politique particulier, le Burundi, tout comme les autres pays de la Région des Grands Lacs est en proie à plusieurs Urgences Humanitaires (rapatriement, déplacement des populations par suite de catastrophes naturelles comme; les  inondations, glissements de terrain…) qui exposent les victimes de ces aléas et les communautés hôtes à l’émergence ou la ré-émergence de plusieurs maladies à fort potentiel épidémique (voir même pandémie). Si on prenait que l'année 2020, une succession de catastrophes naturelle ont touché la province de Bujumbura et ses environs, occasionnant beaucoup de dégâts dont près de 50 000 personnes affectés (avec des déplacements des populations), un délabrement de 6 formations sanitaires  et une douzaine d'écoles inondées, plus particulièrement dans la localité de Gatumba (province de Bujumbura).   
   
Afin d’identifier les principaux défis en termes de préparation et de réponse aux différentes Urgence Sanitaires, plusieurs évaluations ont été menées et ont montré que malgré les avancées notables en termes de préparation du pays à la prévention, la détection et la réponse rapide, un décalage important demeure entre le niveau central et le niveau périphérique (niveau district et province sanitaire).

L'objectif de ce projet est de renforcer les capacités du Burundi dans la préparation et réponse initiale à la prise en charge des urgences de santé publique y compris des épidémies, avec un accent particulier au niveau périphérique. Cette préparation va être concentrée essentiellement dans 8 provinces sanitaires qui sont à l'Est du pays le long du lac Tanganyika (Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cibitoke, Bubanza et Rumonge) et ceux du Nord (Muyinga, Makamba et Ruyigi) qui reçoivent un nombre conséquent de retournés, de réfugiés et de déplacés interne. Rien que pour l'année 2021, près de 100 000 rapatriés sont attendus.

Même si le projet cible un nombre de total de bénéficieras de 191 513 personnes (suivant la population ciblée comme dans le besoin dans le plan de réponse humanitaire de 2021), les activités du projet auront un impact direct sur le reste de la communauté hôte des provinces cibles (faisant ainsi un parfait lien entre l'humanitaire et le développement). Cette population est estimée à 5 880 430 personnes, dont 2 924 485 femmes et 2 955 945 hommes.  Sur cette population, 102 921 personnes sont des déplacés internes, 130 139 des retournés et 63 454 des réfugiés.

project_name: Maintien des services essentiels de santé pour les populations les plus vulnérables dans les situations d’urgence humanitaire dans 8 provinces sanitaires du Burundi.
project_objective:
La santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et de l’adolescent(e)s a connu des progrès significatifs au Burundi au cours de ces deux dernières décennies. Cependant, la mortalité dans ce groupe vulnérable reste toujours élevée par rapport aux cibles des Objectifs de Développement Durable.
 En effet, selon la dernière Enquête de Santé et Démographique (EDS-III), le Ratio de Mortalité Maternelle et Néonatale sont passés respectivement de 500 à 334 décès maternels pour 100.000 naissances vivantes et 31 à 23 décès néonatals pour 1000 naissances vivantes entre 2010 et 2016. Le même rapport montre qu’au cours de ces cinq dernières années, un enfant sur 20 meurt avant son premier anniversaire et un enfant sur treize meurt avant d’atteindre son cinquième anniversaire soit un quotient de mortalité infanto-juvénile estimé à 78‰ avec un risque plus élevé en milieu rural qu’en milieu urbain. Au Burundi environs six enfants sur dix sont atteints de malnutrition chronique (56%). Sur ce fond de malnutrition chronique trop élevée, la morbidité chez l’enfant de moins de 5 ans est principalement dominée par les trois maladies courantes de l’enfant: le paludisme, la pneumonie ainsi que les maladies diarrhéiques. A cela, il faut ajouter l’infection à VIH sida et les anémies. etc... ce qui rend d’avantages la vulnérabilité des enfants pendant les situations d’urgence.

Si les besoins des femmes, des enfants et des filles ne sont pas intégrés dans la réponse de santé publique en situation d’urgence y compris lors de cette pandémie de la COVID 19, et une priorisation proportionnée des ressources pour la santé sexuelle et reproductive, la santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et des jeunes et des adolescent(e)s(e)s cela pourrait entraîner des augmentations substantielles de la mortalité évitable.  

Parallèlement à ce profil sanitaire particulier, le Burundi subit des catastrophes d’origine humaine (conflits), naturelle (inondations, sécheresse) et des épidémies (choléra et paludisme). Il doit faire face à des déplacements de populations et à la réintégration de populations rapatriées. Les épidémies passées ont démontré que le manque d’accès aux services de santé essentiels en raison de la fermeture des services non liés à la lutte contre l’épidémie, peut donner lieu à plus de décès que ceux qui sont causés par l’épidémie elle-même. 

L’OMS va capitaliser son rôle normatif et de coordination en matière de santé et son expérience dans l’appui à la mise en œuvre des interventions intégrées de gestion intégrée des cas dans la communauté ou « Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) » sans oublier la réponse aux épidémies de paludisme afin d’accompagner les interventions proposées dans ce projet pour contribuer à l’accès et au maintien des services de santé essentiels de qualité de la mère, du nouveau-né, de l’enfant et de l’adolescent(e)s et au renforcement du système de santé. La réponse sera focalisée sur : (i) l’accès et l’utilisation des services essentiels de santé de qualité (ii) la disponibilité des intrants (iii) la décentralisation du traitement du paludisme à travers l’iCCM (iv) le renforcement du partenariat (v) le suivi et évaluation ainsi que (vi) la gestion et la coordination de la réponse à l’urgence. Ces activités seront mises en oeuvre dans 8 provinces sanitaires du pays à savoir Cankuzo, Rutana, Karusi, Muyinga, Kirundo, Rumonge, Cibitoke et Makamba.

Même si le projet cible en particulier les femmes en âge de procréer-les nouveaux nés-les enfants et les adolescents, tous les groupes de populations vulnérables (y compris les personnes à besoins spécifiques) seront pris en compte dans la mise en oeuvre du projet.

project_name: Amélioration de l’accès équitable aux soins de santé de qualité pour les populations affectées par la crise causée par Boko Haram Dans la Région de l’Extrême-Nord Cameroun

Supporting the Emergency Response Health Cluster in Cameroon by strengthening the capacities of the public health system for preparedness and response to COVID-19, giving technical support for mobility mainstreamed coordination tools and national action plans, and the provision of mental health and psychosocial support for the most vulnerable populations affected by displacement.
project_objective:
Following IOM’s manual of community-based mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) in emergencies and displacement, the Organization will target conflict-affected populations in the North-West, South-West as well as the Far-North regions of Cameroon to address their many related needs. IOM will first conduct an MHPSS assessment to identify the available, resources and key stakeholders, then implement community-based mental health and psychosocial support activities (art-based, sports and play, socio-cultural) in targeted communities, with inter-disciplinary teams,  to address needs and strengthen community networks, as well as to aid victims of gender-based violence. Additional support will be given to strengthen local capacities to carry out community-based MHPSS activities ensuring sustainability for the future.  
By incorporating a client-centred approach and delivering culturally sensitive services, which are also tailored to the age and gender of beneficiaries, IOM contributes to reducing psychosocial vulnerabilities and promoting community resilience and ownership. Through additional capacity building,, IOM also contributes to ensuring that  key MHPSS providers including existing local government and civil society structures provide support to survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and other types of victimization affecting the regions.

Continuing from its technical support to the government in the framework of the COVID-19 pandemic, IOM plans in 2021 to pursue using its specialized health capacity to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic at points of entry in Cameroon, as well as to strengthen public health preparedness in preparation for future health crises. This will be done building on existing strong partnerships with WHO and the Ministry of Health, continuing to provide operational and technical assistance through the strengthening of both technical and material capacities at priority PoEs in Cameroon, with the promotion of cross-border coordination and collaboration for standardised bilateral and regional public health frameworks, and the continued technical and coordination support for national pandemic emergency preparedness planning.

Continuing IOM’s co-lead role with the government for the Point of Entry working group for COVID-19 preparedness and response in Cameroon, IOM aims to expand its public health interventions at priority PoEs and PoIs along mobility corridors to curb the spread of the virus in Cameroon and to neighbouring countries, as well boost preparedness for future health crisis with a body of information and publications on mobility trends and practices.
In addition, a further capacity building campaign led by the Government of Cameroon with IOM and WHO in support will be conducted based on the new release of the outcoming SOPs, in preparation for the effective and streamlined screening of suspect COVID-19 cases as well as future health crises.
The strengthening of government capacities in both material and non-material ways will also be implemented at specific priority PoEs to effectively detect and respond to suspected COVID-19 cases, and to mitigate the risks of COVID-19 via large scale public communication, community engagement and community support including psychosocial support at key PoEs and PoIs.
Proposed activities in Cameroon will target a strategic selection of additional prioritized sights identified by further participatory mapping processes and previous mapping exercises and research. Priority sights for further public health interventions along mobility corridors and at specific PoEs will be selected based on a number of criteria, including mobility size, mobility type, proximity to large urban centres, proximity to large areas of disease infection, capacity gaps of the national, regional and local level, and any further selection criteria decided upon within the Cameroon Working Group on Points of Entry or in partnership with the Government of Cameroon, IOM and WHO.

project_name: Intervention d'urgence pour lutter contre les épidémies de méningite, de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune, de rougeole , d'Ebola et de la Pandemie de la COVID19 au Tchad
project_objective:
Objectif du projet est de réduire les taux de morbidité et de mortalité dus aux épidémies de méningite, de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune et de rougeole et autres épidémiesLe Tchad reste un pays qui fait face aux épidémies récurrentes et aux catastrophes naturelles tels que les inondations. En 2019 le pays a enregistré plus de 20000 sinistrés dont plus d’une dizaine de morts et disparus suites aux inondations. Le taux de morbidité et mortalité reste élevé. Le taux de mortalité élevé observé lors des épidémies est dû à la faiblesse du système de surveillance, au manque de stratégies de santé appropriées, au manque d’accès des patients aux services de santé et à la mauvaise qualité des services de santé existants.
Méningite : chaque année, le pays est confronté à une vague d'épidémie de méningite dans le sud et l'ouest du pays. En 2012, la vaccination avec le nouveau vaccin MenAfriVac, qui couvrait l’ensemble du pays, a réduit le risque de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype A). Cependant, le risque d'épidémie de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype W135) persiste. En 2019 les districts sanitaires de Goundi et Bedjondo dans la province sanitaire du Mandoul, ont connu une épidémie de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype W135) avec plus 500 cas suspects dont 52 décès. Depuis le début de l'année 2021 plus de 544 cas suspects dont 48 décès ont été notifiés.
La couverture vaccinale contre la rougeole est faible (37%), ce qui a entrainé une épidémie de rougeole. Il s'agit d'une menace sérieuse pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans dans un contexte de forte prévalence de malnutrition chronique. 252550 cas avec 294 décès ont été notifiés.
Choléra : Le choléra apparaît pendant la saison des pluies dans les régions entourant le lac Tchad. En 2011, 17 000 cas de choléra ont été notifiés par 37 districts de santé touchés sur 62. En 2014, 172 cas de choléra ont été notifiés dans les régions de Lac, Mayo Kebbi et N’Djamena. En 2017 plus de 1000 cas ont été notifiés dans le Sila et Salamat. En 2019 les provinces sanitaires du Mayo Kebbi Est et Ouest ont connu une épidémie de choléra avec au total 96 cas notifié. Compte tenu des faibles niveaux d'accès à une source d'eau durable améliorée (52%) et à un assainissement amélioré (12%), il est probable que cela continue d'être un problème chronique.
En 2013, le Tchad a connu une épidémie de fièvre jaune. Plus de 900 000 personnes ont été vaccinées. En 2016, 334 cas suspects ont été notifiés, dont un confirmé et en 2018 426 cas suspects ont été notifiés. Des le début de l’année,2021, 471 suspects avec 5 décès dont 1 confirmé ont été notifiés
En outre, le pays connait des flambées de cas de paludisme notamment chez les enfants et les femmes. En 2019, plus de 1 000 000 de cas ont été notifiés
L’épidémie d’Ebola en Afrique de l’Ouest et centrale, et la proximité du Tchad avec cette région de l’Afrique nécessitent des mesures de surveillance adéquates ainsi que des actions de prévention et de préparation.
Afin de contrôler ces épidémies et de réduire les taux de morbidité et de mortalité dus aux épidémies de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune, de rougeole et de méningite, ce projet vise à prendre en charge de nouvelles épidémies en réalisant une campagne de vaccination de masse de l'ensemble de la population vulnérable( hommes et femmes vulnérables , enfants, garçons et filles , handicapés) sans distinction d’âge en mettant un accès sur les femmes, les enfants de moins de 5 ans
Depuis Mars 2020 le Tchad comme le reste du monde fait face à la pandémie de la COVID 19 avec plus de 2000 cas et plus de 100 décès

project_name: Shelter and NFI response in North - East Nigeria.
project_objective:
Under this project, IOM will scale-up its provision of shelter assistance targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. IOM will: 
(A) Ensure access to different types of emergency shelter solutions for displaced populations through the distribution and prepositioning of emergency shelter kits, construction of emergency shelters, rehabilitation of damaged public buildings, etc.; 
(B) Contribute to decongestion of camps/camp-like settings through construction of emergency shelters, and rehabilitation of damaged public buildings, etc.; 
(C) Ensure that displaced populations have access to different transitional shelter solutions. 
(D) Ensure that the care, maintenance and upgrading of existing emergency shelters and transitional
shelters are conducted for continued safety and comfort of the affected population. 
(E) Ensure that returnee households have access to materials and labour for repairing their
damaged houses; and 
(F) Empower the local market/vendors through the use of Cash and Voucher modalities.

IOM’s shelter/NFI activities will be implemented in three States of North East Nigeria; Borno
(13 LGAs), Adamawa (8 LGAs) and Yobe State (3 LGAs), targeting 522,500 individuals. IOM ensures that all shelter activities conducted are accountable to the affected population and that the specific needs of project beneficiaries are considered, including those related to gender. IOM will ensure that kits and other shelter solutions are harmonized at sector level and coordinated with partners.
The project will also include the continuation and scaling-up of Non-Food Items (NFI) support for people in camp and camp-like settings, in host communities, including for new arrivals. To ensure the timely response to the emerging needs incase of influx of new arrivals and locations that has the risk of being affected of heavy rains and/or fire outbreaks, IOM will preposition NFI kits in/close to critical locations, where IOM has MoU with partner warehouses.
IOM plans to guarantee the participation of Women, Men, Girls and Boys as equals to ensure that the special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and different age groups, and address women's, girls' and boys’ specific needs, especially in terms of protection and access concerns. To illustrate, (1) the content of NFI kits will be tailored in accordance to the needs of different age and gender groups (2) All activities related to this project will equally target the different age and gender groups and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. Regarding assessment of gender specific needs, monitoring and evaluation and to measure the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations and set-up communication channels with them where possible, and all activities will be conducted based on Do No Harm principles.

project_name: Increase access to quality Gender Based Violence Prevention and Response services in North East Nigeria
project_objective: The project seeks to strengthen access to quality integrated GBV prevention and response services both in the contexts of protracted crisis and CIVID-19 pandemic in the conflicted affected states of northeast Nigeria. This includes provision of lifesaving multi-sectorial services that will address the medical, psychosocial, legal and protection/safety needs of GBV survivors in IDP camps, host communities and communities of return, as well strengthening community protection mechanisms to mitigate and prevent GBV. The project will focus of expanding and maintain services in safe spaces/shelters and one-stop-centre (OSC), improving referrals to medical services including clinical management of rape (CMR), strengthening case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) as well as legal and protection services, procurement and distribution of menstrual, dignity kits, cultural appropriate clothings, and strengthening field coordination including referral pathways and ethical data management. Other complementary activities will focus on strengthening community resilience and promoting GBV/SEA risk mitigation mechanism in humanitarian setting. Our target is to reach 50% (650,000) of the  sectors targeted (1,300,000) population in the BAY States, owing from the fact that UNFPA and its implementing partners reached about 40% of all beneficiaries of GBV services in 2020. Special emphasis will be put on strengthening joint inter-agency coordination, M&E, capacity building, assessment and partnership that will translate to better outcome.

project_name: Integrated WASH services reinforcing resilience across sectors of food security, nutrition, health and protection for communities affected by conflict, disasters, disease outbreak, in areas of high food insecurity.
project_objective:
The ongoing instabilities in most parts of South Sudan, combined with effects of floods and lack of food security and livelihood opportunities result in the displacement of communities and the economic downturn and have put a further strain on already limited WASH services.
PAH is a very experienced organization with broad portfolio of successfully implemented projects in various sectors. PAH will use is strongest expertise in WASH to provide assistance to vulnerable communities across the country by providing accessing to water, improving and sanitation both as single approach as well as in multi-sectoral responses PAH always seeks the synergies with other actions, as WASH sector covers the needs crucial for other aspects of life too. 
PAH will mainly target people facing high level of WASH vulnerability, those in IPC levels 3, 4 and 5, displaced or returnees and host communities with over-stretched resources. PAH will focus on rehabilitation and building water sources in institutions and those prioritized by community members. Sanitation will be provided on institutional level. PAH provides hygiene promotion, combined with protection, health, nutrition elements, with cross-sectoral topics adjusted to the needs of the groups. This capacity building is always based on community members chosen to be promoters, water user committees and other engaged people within the community. PAH holds itself accountable to affected population and ensures its ownership of project results.
Recognizing the cross-cutting nature of WASH, PAH combine the described activities with other sectors by providing dignity kits and NFIs, PAH works to improve protection status of women and girls. While improving access to water PAH takes care of irrigation needs for farmers and water for livestock, which contributes to improvement of food production and contain elements of diseases prevention. By improving sanitation and water access in nutrition sites and schools, PAH contributes to work in those sectors. 
Concerning the beneficiaries breakdown, while planing the responses PAH will follow OCHA population aggregation.

project_name: Stabilizing the food access and livelihoods of conflict and disasters affected returnees, internally displaced persons and the host communities in South Sudan through integrated emergency and static Food Security and Livelihood response.
project_objective:
This project aims to meet the immediate, medium and long-term food security needs of the target communities of IPC level 3,4 and 5, also having the focus on restoring livelihood, enhancing food production, building resilience and strengthening capacity of the targeted population.
This will be achieved by various means. One of them is access to cereal and/or vegetable seeds’ kits and tools, accompanied by agricultural extension activities, focusing on good agronomic practices. This intervention will be delivered using lead farmers and farmer field school approaches with demonstration plots. Lead farmers and extension workers will be trained as trainers for community farmers. This methodology ensures ownership and long-lasting effects, as the capacity of trainers stays within the community. PAH will introduce different irrigation methods including drip irrigation systems together with community training on their adequate and sustainable use to enhance the copying mechanism during the dry season. 
Additionally, to traditional plots, PAH will encourage setting up small-scale vegetable gardens, which can be established next to the houses. This facilitates planting and irrigation, allows higher diet diversity and minimize the protection risks in case of women walking long distances to access the plots. 
Access to fishing kits and learning of fishery practices is another means to improve food security and livelihood. Fishing has the potential to immediately address food security needs. It enables people to immediately harvest fish from the rivers and swamps in the areas. 
Conditional general food distribution may be considered within the project in case the targeted population is strongly affected by food insecurity. Food distribution will target the most vulnerable food insecure population with limited access to markets and having a poor road network. Contrary, in the communities with access to market and availability cash programming, will be considered. The decision will be based on initial market and community assessments, considering cash vouchers or cash for work. Food/cash for asset will be conducted in the areas where there are needs and local markets can support the project targeting the establishment of community structures and facilities like schools and infrastructures like community road projects and communal farms establishment.
Food for education and school feeding programme will be considered in the project areas where PAH carries food security and livelihood activities with seeds distribution and vegetable and cereal crops production. 
For a more  holistic approach, building resilience and long-lasting effects, PAH will integrate interventions with sectors of WASH, nutrition, education, protection and S/NFI through combined hygiene and nutrition promotion in addition to screening and referral to nutrition partners. Education and health will be integrated through training of school hygiene clubs and school gardening and awareness at the schools, nutrition and health centres. PAH will work with nutrition and health partners on the local level. Protection will be mainstreamed across all sectors and additional protection team will be supporting the communities.
Concerning the beneficiaries breakdown, while planning the responses PAH will follow OCHA population aggregation.

project_name: Protecting Civilians through Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in Syria has been exacerbated by the widespread use of explosive ordnance (EO), posing significant risks and requiring different mitigation strategies to reduce its impact on the civilian population and the humanitarian sector delivering aid to those in need. While the full scale of contamination is not known, preliminary findings for the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview estimate that 1 in 2 people is at risk from EO, and a third of communities are potentially contaminated. EO contamination in essential civilian infrastructure, agricultural land, roads and private property is a lethal barrier to safe movement which deprives civilians from accessing essential basic services, hampers delivery of humanitarian assistance, endangers those seeking refuge from violence or returning to their areas, and precludes resumption of livelihood activities, thus amplifying the social and economic crisis aggravated by the COVID-19 pandemic. A comprehensive humanitarian mine action response is a humanitarian necessity and vital precursor for delivering humanitarian aid and early recovery.

The overall aim of UNMAS project is to reduce the impact of EO on the civilian population and humanitarian workers through effective sector coordination and implementation of humanitarian mine action activities, in line with humanitarian priorities as identified in the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), and within the framework of agreements between the Syrian State and UN agencies, funds and programmes, as well as Security Council resolution 2504 (S/RES/2504, 2020). 

Under this project, in accordance with the HRP, UNMAS will lead, manage and coordinate humanitarian mine action activities as defined by International Mine Action Standards (IMAS). 

All components of humanitarian mine action (risk education, victim assistance, survey and clearance) remain critical, but in 2021, UNMAS will focus on expanding survey and clearance, as the only way to permanently remove the threat posed by EO and subject to access and funding.

The delivery of EO Risk Education (EORE), tailored to age, gender, localized threats and activity patterns of different at-risk groups, is a critical, life-saving activity for raising the awareness of civilians and humanitarian personnel about the dangers of EO, thus directly contributing to HRP strategic objective 1: “Save Lives” and strategic objective 2: “Enhance Protection.”  As the Syrian crisis has been characterized by large-scale conflict and displacement, survey, data collection, and mapping of EO are critical to informing humanitarian programming, needs-based prioritization, and the expansion of clearance to remove the contamination threats, particularly in high-priority areas. UNMAS will support the expansion of victim assistance and provision of specialized services for persons with disabilities, including survivors of EO and their families, thus contributing to strategic objective 3: “Increase Resilience and Access to Services”.
