project_name: Emergency Health support for vulnerable Lebanese and Migrants
project_objective:
Medair’s health work has been operating since 2014, supporting both refugees and vulnerable Lebanese through health centres and community outreach. Whilst originally focussed within health centres within Social Development Centres as part of the Ministry of Social Affairs, since the beginning of 2021, Medair has expanded operations to the South / Nabatiye and working with an additional 15 health centres within the Ministry of Public Health network, particularly for routine vaccinations. Medair opened a COVID mass vaccination centre in Saida in June 2021. There is a growing focus on nutrition activities such as IYCF, which are detailed under the Nutrition sector of the ERP.
Health activities that are aligned under the health sector of the ERP include the provision of medication, PPE provision and IPC training for health centres, and integrated messaging through community health volunteers (CHVs). 54 CHVs focused on reaching Lebanese populations will be mobilised from pre-existing Medair networks, and while the remaining number 46+ (additional figures contingent on anticipated future funding) will be newly recruited (with additional CHVs as part of the LCRP). These Community Health Volunteers will reach all populations within their geographic areas of intervention (around the supported health centres).
Medair has seen a four-fold increase in the usage of medication in recent months as more Lebanese are dependent on medication in the public sector due to shortages within pharmacies. Medair therefore aims to provide more medication through supplying pharmacies in supported health centres – expanding the number of centres supported. Medication will be provided free of charge to all those accessing the centres. Medair acknowledges the challenges with procuring medicines in the current context given we do not hold an importation license, yet is actively participating in coordination conversations with other agencies to explore alternative options for procurement of imports as well as engaging with advocacy efforts at the humanitarian and governmental levels. Medair will also include a small cash-for-health component for vulnerable people needing to access medication from other locations, which has been piloted through a blockchain modality in the Bekaa over the past six months. Medair also has experience in cash-for-health programming within the Middle East region, in addition to cash programming within Lebanon. 
Medair’s existing COVID programming already supports health centres with the provision of PPE and IPC training for staff and will be expanding this to a further 10 health centres. For more information on the centres, please see the list sent to the Health Sector. 
Medair also has an active shelter team who cover water and sanitation components, in addition to expanding into alternative energy options. The health and shelter teams have recently been jointly assessing the health facilities to consider how to ensure the continuation of health services, including WASH and solar options – both fridges for cold chain, and for the whole centre to enable lights, equipment and the internet (to access PHENICS) to function. Medair is therefore well placed to provide integrated health, shelter and WASH solutions.
Medair is an active part of the health sector, and has close working relationships with both the Ministry of Public Health, the Ministry of Social Affairs and other key stakeholders listed in the ERP. Medair has programming operating across Lebanon, including in BML and the North/Akkar, although the majority of health programming under this ERP is anticipating to take place in Bekaa/Baalbek and the South/Nabatiye.

project_name: Improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable populations in Renk, Leer, Pibor and any other location across South Sudan.
project_objective: The Medair WASH Project will be implemented in Pibor, Renk, Leer and any other priority locations identified by UN-OCHA, WASH Cluster, NAWG and ICCG across South Sudan. Medair has been running multi-sectoral response in Renk and Leer counties since 2011 and 2015 respectively and will continue supporting these locations in 2021. According to the HRP2021 and WASH Cluster severity mapping, the WASH sector needs and gaps in Pibor country are highlighted as severity level 4 and at critical condition. As a result, Medair has started long term multi-sectoral responses in Pibor County (Lekuangole and Gumuruk). Additionally, the emergency response team delivers rapid assistance in areas identified as WASH severity level 3, 4, and 5 and IPC 4/5. Medair aims to integrate WASH activities with nutrition and health to maximise the impact and reduce excessive morbidity and mortality of children under five and to contribute to the overall WASH cluster objectives. Medair will provide standard WASH NFI kits along with hygiene promotion to 14,551 SAM/MAM children and their family/caretakers at facilities and depending on the COVID-19 situation follow up visits will be conducted for households hosting the children. The WASH NFIs include household water treatment products, a bucket with lid, a bucket with tap and lid, soap, and filter cloth. The WASH NFIs are intended to improve access to safe water and safe hygiene practice for three months. In addition, Medair provides access to safe water and sanitation facilities to 43 nutrition facilities. Medair also supports communities that are showing high prevalence of GAM rate through improving access to safe water and promoting safe hygiene practices. WASH activities will also be integrated into health activities in the context of disease prevention and response. It aims at breaking the transmission cycle of water related diseases including diarrhoeal, cholera, vector borne diseases and COVID-19. This is intended to be achieved through multiple integrated approaches (improving access to safe water and hygiene promotion) and ensuring minimum IPC WASH in health facilities in each supported facility of Renk and Pibor. The emergency response team employs the same WASH technical strategies stated above and supports people in need of life saving WASH services across South Sudan. Medair will work with protection and disability focused partners, community leaders and religious leaders to identify people with disabilities, elders, marginalised and financially disadvantaged community members. Then, focus group discussions will be conducted with these groups of people or their representatives to identify their needs, barriers, and obstacles that limit them from accessing WASH services. During project design, these groups of people or their representatives will engage with Medair and forward their views and opinion and design preference. In all the project locations including health and nutrition facilities, Medair will thoroughly assess protection concern related to women and girls accessing WASH services and take robust action to mitigate the risk of exposing women and girls. Depending on the contexts, Medair will install 14 new water points where there is low coverage, operate four SWATs, upgrade six existing handpumps with solar power system, rehabilitate 65 existing water points and/or distribute water filters or household water treatment products. Medair employs a Care Group network approach in its static locations and conducts general community wide hygiene promotion in any other emergency locations across South Sudan. Hygiene promotion at community level emphasising disease prevention (such as COVID-19, cholera and AWD), safe excreta management (and advocating for cathole method), safe water storage and handwashing with safe water and soap. 30 communal toilets will be constructed in crowded settings where their absence will create a public health risk. The toilets will be maintained by the community.

project_name: Emergency Health Interventions for Vulnerable Populations Wau, Pariang, Abiemnhom, Akobo and Pibor Counties.
project_objective:
This project will provide Integrated, life-saving, emergency health interventions for populations affected by flooding, conflict, disease outbreak and displacement. The project will focus on women, girls, boys and men among the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), Returnees and host populations with limited or no access to health services. The project will ensure improved access to integrated emergency lifesaving healthcare services focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality for conflict-affected and vulnerable IDP, host community and returnee households in the two states of Western Bahr El Ghazal and Unity and the two administrative areas of Greater Pibor (GPAA) and Ruweng (RAA).

The proposed interventions under this project will include the following:
1.	Provision of essential primary health care services targeting the most vulnerable populations through various clinical packages (Hospital, PHCCs, PHCUs, mobile clinics and ICCM)
2.	Implementation of outbreak investigation and response for epidemic prone diseases in locations where CARE works.
3.	Support to static Health facilities in Western Bahr el Ghazal and Unity States particularly on essential medical supplies and capacity building in line with the strategies and priorities of the health cluster
4.	Mainstream accountability to the affected populations

project_name: Nutrition Interventions for Disaster affected populations in Abiemnhom, Mayom, Pariang, Koch and Rubkona
project_objective: In 2021, four of the 5 counties that CARE works in are projected to have proxy GAM levels above the WHO emergency threshold of 15%. These are: Rubkona (25.00%), Pariang (19.59%), Koch (17.80%) and Abiemnhom (15.28%). The only exception will be Mayom which has a proxy GAM rate of 11.11%). In addition, the recently released IPC analysis indicates that between December 2020 and March 2021, the 5 counties will be in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) while between April and July 2021, Abiemnhom, Pariang and Rubkona will be in IPC 4 while Mayom and Koch will remain in IPC 3. This project will provide Integrated, life-saving emergency nutrition interventions for children under the age of 5 and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) in the above 5 counties. Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Returnees will be of special interest to this project because of their high levels of vulnerability. Number of beneficiaries targeted for the project will be 258,015 and the total budget for the project will be $ 1,272,961.

project_name: Provision of integrated essential  Primary and secondary Health care services to the vulnerable  population in 3 counties of Gogrial East,Gogrial West and Twic  Greater Warrap  State,South Sudan
project_objective:
The action will be for a period of 12 months and will address the prevailing gaps and needs in service provision taking into account the prevailing risks such as insecurity and COVID-19. The main purpose is to contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality due to preventable diseases in the vulnerable populations in  3 Counties of Greater Warrap State namely Gogrial East,Gogrial West and Twic Counties through provision of integrated essential Primary and secondary Health  care services  in accordance with the Basic Package of Health and Nutrition services. The intervention will target  the existing vulnerable  populations and person's in need estimated to be about 163,445. The project will supplement and compliment service provision in 59 static Health facilities which are currently being supported by the HPF project. The project will ensure PHCUs, PHCCs and secondary health facilities  deliver promotive, curative, and preventive outpatient and inpatient health services to all community members seeking services in these facilities free of charge. The main objectives of the project are:
1.	To reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic-prone diseases and health insecurities
2.	To mprove access and utilization of integrated life-saving quality health care services to crisis-affected and vulnerable populations through static, mobile and community-based health service delivery systems
3.	To increase access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled, mental health disorders and the elderly.

project_name: Respond to COVID-19 Pandemic Through Supporting CCTCs
project_objective:
With this project, UOSSM seeks to contribute to achieving the following objectives:
- Increase access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable humanitarian health services for those most vulnerable and in need.
- Strengthen health sector capacity to prepare for, detect and deliver a timely response to disease outbreaks.
The project aims to address the gap in response to the COVID-19 pandemic in Northwest Syria by supporting 5 CCTCs which are the most prioritized centers recommended by the COVID-19 task force. The centers are ongoing and funded by OCHA until end of August 2021, the CCTCs provide services for treating mild and moderate cases of COVID-19, as they are considered the largest percentage of confirmed cases, ensuring that the severe cases in which the morbidity is high will be referred to the case management hospitals and ICU. The screening will be conducted for all suspected cases of COVID-19 that meet the criteria, the swab (PCR) will be taken and if it is confirmed, the mild and moderate cases will be admitted, isolated, and treated (except those that are asymptomatic with suitable home circumstances for quarantines), thus containing the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic and reducing morbidity and mortality rates. The project also includes educating patients on how to use PPE and training them in practice on healthy behavior.  
Each center will be as WHO/HC model that includes 4 areas:
- The screening areas: This area is an entry point, in which under strict IPC precaution measures patients will be checked based on screening questionnaires. Patients who are negatively screened (i.e., they do not fill the case definition criteria) will be referred to the health facilities, while suspected cases matching case definition criteria will be referred to observation areas for further medical assessment.
- The observation areas: For cases that were highly suspected cases of people having been in contact with suspected cases and they underwent laboratory confirmation testing, (the admission, referral, or home isolation) decision will be taken. 
- The patients will be sorted according to the preliminary results of the examination, either for isolation and treatment, or for being referred to a higher level of care or sent home, as for very mild cases, and if the conditions in the home are suitable for isolation, the patient will be transferred to their home and followed by the community volunteer in their area as a part of coordination plan of the health cluster with partners  
- Isolation and case management section:  cases will receive medical assessment and supportive therapy for confirmed cases with mild symptoms and without underlying chronic conditions.
- Recovery area: cases received final assessment and preparation for discharge cases.

project_name: Community based education promoting conducive learning environment for vulnerable boys and girls in Syria
project_objective:
-	100% targeted location 3 and 4 as per Education Sector Severity & PIN_HRP 2021 (Kafr Zeita n/a)
-	Cost/BNF 77USD
-	10% CwDs
-	INTERSOS didn’t receive any funding for Education in 2020: 0USD
-	195,000USD received by INTERSOS for 2021 (Edu sector)
-	Target achieved 2020 is 0 since INTERSOS didn’t implement prior projects in Education
INTERSOS Action tackles identified problems and unmet needs through an EiE response targeting the most vulnerable population in areas with high severity conditions in Hama, Homs, Aleppo, Rural Damascus Governorate. In line with Sector 2021 Syria HRP, the Action aims to improve 1) safe and equitable access to formal and NFE services; 2) enhance the quality of teaching and learning; 3) enhance communities’ capacities and role in promoting the establishment of conducive learning environments to ensure boys and girls continuation of learning. INTERSOS aims at outreaching a total number of 8370 beneficiaries (B 4150; G4150; M35; W 35). The programme is starting in May 2021 and will be continuing throughout 2022. Despite being the first Action implemented in the EiE sector in Syria, INTERSOS is building on its extensive expertise in the delivery of NFE and supporting formal school systems in the Middle East region (Iraq, Lebanon, Jordan). INTERSOS is currently working under a bilateral MoU with SARC and negotiation for a bilateral MoU with MoE are in the final steps. To maximize the impact of the Action and enhance local sustainable response capacity, INTERSOS carries out integrated action where Protection and CP principles are mainstreamed along with GBV preventive messages. INTERSOS will work through multiple approaches promoting boys and girls ACCESS to formal and NFE through: SLP, remedial classes (after school for children at risk of drop out and in TLS/learning center for OOSC). INTERSOS promotes an inclusive environment enhancing access of CwDs (target 837) and providing the community with the skills to support CwDs inclusion in the learning environment. Educational kits are delivered to all the children enrolling in the classes (stationary and SLP). Classes are arranged based on a flexible schedule to accommodate the needs of children supporting the family with work/ house chores. Regular classes are alternated with PSS sessions aimed at promoting boys and girls’ wellbeing and retention. QUALITY of teaching and learning is promoted through training to formal and NFE personnel on Active Learning, Inclusive Education, Curriculum and Planning, Pedagogy, Teachers’ role and well-being, CP principles (last 4 subjects are already included in INEE standard TiCC training). INTERSOS has developed a response strategy based on a strong COMMUNITY-BASED APPROACH coupled with a robust capacity building programme to enhance the quality of services delivered to the affected individuals. PTAs will be established and/or supported and their members will be trained on: CP elements, PSEA, Safe identification and referral, education outreach and monitoring, gender mainstreaming in education. Once trained they become the first initiators of: i. education monitoring (outreaching activity) and ii. Back to Learning (B2L). Through consultations with the community and HH assessments, the education outreach volunteers identify Out of School Children and individual causes for being OOS. Such methodology promotes the definition of individual pathways for re-enrolment through NFE. The education outreach volunteers also contribute to identify boys and girls at risk of drop out in formal/NFE environment, along with main causes and mitigation measures. Finally with the starting of COVID-19 INTERSOS started integrating health and hygiene promotion and infection prevention and control in its action providing holistic knowledge and capacities to the targeted communities. INTERSOS will target the most vulnerable boys and girls at risk of drop out and OOSC privileging overage students, adolescents girls and boys, IDPs and CwDs.

project_name: Winterization Campaigns in Vulnerable Areas of Hama, Rural Damascus and Idleb
project_objective: INTERSOS proposes a tailored and gender-sensitive winterization response in Hama, Southern Idleb and Rural Damascus, where its ongoing humanitarian programme will ensure a comprehensive and holistic approach to the needs of the most vulnerable. The proposed action is targeting vulnerable HHs living in dire conditions in Hama, Idleb and Rural Damascus Governorates. This intervention has been designed based on outcomes of needs assessments conducted by SARC Hama Branch in prioritized areas, ad-hoc consultations with SARC Livelihood Department; Rapid Need Assessment (RNA) conducted in January 2020 with a follow-up in July and September 2020 in the Hama Governorate as well as 2021 a Labor Market assessment (LMA) in Suran and Muardeh sub-districts. Findings shed the light on soaring poverty, food insecurity and lack of income-generation opportunities. The NFI emergency assistance continues to be essential, where the sector reports 4.7M PiN for 2021, 0.3 more than 2020. This increase is due to the unprecedented economic downturn, rising food insecurity and increasing cost of basic items. Of this, 2.70 million people (57%) are residing in areas of severity 3 or higher with a concentration in 73 out of 270 sub-districts. According to the MSNA, 90% of families at the end of 2020 reported diminished access to NFI’s with unaffordability being the main driver"". (2021 NFI sector strategy). Following internal regulations and in compliance with minimum standards in the country for the sector of interventions (NFI), beneficiaries will be selected if multilevel of vulnerabilities are assessed and found. Consequently, over the beneficiaries’ selection process, INTERSOS and SARC will apply a multi-sector vulnerability criteria, including clusters' criteria for NFI in the country and guaranteeing protection mainstreaming (ensuring specific attention to the specific needs of vulnerable groups such as female head of HHs, pregnant/lactating women, elderly, persons with disabilities). Winter-relief items will be distributed to the targeted HHs to reduce the impact of exposure to extreme weather. The kit composition will be tailored according to the specific needs of beneficiaries, each geographical area, availability of items and materials. The NFI kits are set as per NFI sector recommendations: winterization kit specifically costs between $150 and $170/HHs. Each basic kit is composed of winter clothing (children and adults), winter jackets (for men and women), thermal blankets and extra plastic sheets.  Additional items such as items for babies, boots, tarpaulins, flashlights and buckets may be added according to need, availability and budget. The composition of the kit has been done using the NFI Sector standard composition. A total of 1650 NFI winterization kits are distributed combined with awareness sessions on COVID 19 prevention. In September 2020, surveyed communities reported different NFI needs among different groups, based on gender and age. For instance, boys and girls are in greater need of clothing and shoes. Men are in greater need of heating fuel, light sources, and water containers. Women and girls need sanitary pads and kitchen-related items, whereas the elderly reported requiring blankets, energy, and light sources. These findings demonstrate the wide range of items that HHs continue to struggle to access and which become particularly urgent in winter season. A PDM exercise is carried out after the distribution, usually about 2 months after in order to survey beneficiaries on their satisfaction and usefulness of the distributed items feeding sector's info sharing and continuous understanding of the needs. As part of the action, INTERSOS staff and SARC volunteers are provided with briefing sessions on core concepts and policies related to humanitarian principles, Child Protection and PSEA. Moreover, awareness-raising sessions are delivered on hazards, risks, preventive and mitigation measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name: Assisting conflict affected boy, girls and their families including parents, males and females, to increase their resilience and reduce protection risks in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts (both GCA and NGCA) with a special focus on the contact line.
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to increase resilience and reduce vulnerability of the conflict-affected boys, girls and their families, caregivers, males and females, through lifesaving direct support/assistance, MHPSS activities, informal education and recreational activities by strengthening protective environment and improving access to child protection services. Save the Children has several years of filed work experience and has good presence and acceptance on the ground. Most staff of the case management unit are also engaged with the state social services in Druzhkivka. Their capacity is built by SCI in line with international best practice on case management and therefore this knowledge will remain in the state social service. The unit in Druzhkivka is the municipal centre of social services. Save the Children also makes effort to involve state social workers in all relevant trainings and working closely with the CM unit. 

Special attention will be given to protective measures against COVID 19, namely sharing all the relevant and life-saving information on the disease, transmission modes, and how to mitigate other respective risks, providing printing materials, supporting with personal protective equipment, disinfecting materials, etc.

project_name: Enhancing access to essential health care services for vulnerable population in Hama and Rural Damascus Governorate
project_objective: Implemented in cooperation with the Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC), INTERSOS Health program follows an integrated approach which is aimed at building resilience and capacities of communities affected by the crisis in Syria. INTERSOS will implement multi-sectoral actions where health will be integrated with components of Protection (child protection and GBV) and Education. Health projects aim to achieve the following main results: strengthening skills and capacities of health personnel on PHC and COVID-19 related topics (IPC, Triage), enhancing access to essential health services, raising awareness on good health behavior and practices in the Governorates of Hama and Rural Damascus. The action applies a combined mobile and static approach whereby static health facilities are enhanced and equipped alongside with the deployment of mobile health teams in hard-to-reach areas with no health clinic available. As a final result, access to quality PHC services for vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas will be increased and expanded. A special focus will be also given to prevention and response mechanisms related to the COVID-19 pandemic to minimize health risks and provide necessary information and equipment. A comprehensive capacity building program will contribute to strengthen Health Workers and first-line responders’ skills to decrease health risks, protect and assist vulnerable individuals with high-severity needs. Specific, tailored, technical trainings and capacity building sessions will be provided to SARC Health staff and volunteers as well INTERSOS community mobilizers on relevant COVID 19 health topics, PHC, common childhood illnesses, basic emergency obstetric and new-born care and health education and promotion. A static Health Facility (HF) an unserved area (Morek, Hama Governorate) will be supported through minor rehabilitation (guaranteeing the necessary physical and sanitary conditions for the provision of health services) and provision of essential medication and equipment. As a result, the HF will fully function to serve the related catchment population. INTERSOS will facilitate and monitor the delivery of health services to beneficiaries through SARC health workers and INTERSOS medical staff to ensure continuity and availability of PHC services through diagnosis and treatment of common illnesses among children, adolescent, adult, elderly and PLW according to the national protocols. 3 Mobile Health Units will be deployed in Hama Governorate in Murek, Suran and Mohardeh where vulnerable people will have access to consultations and basic medical supplies. In addition, RCCE and behavioral change campaigns will be launched and rolled-out on COVID-19 prevention and response as well as on other prominent heath-focused issues. This will be conducted through a network of community mobilizers and local influencers on the ground. In addition, vulnerable students will be supported in some areas where target schools have been identified. Awareness sessions for students, parents and other community members will be provided in Hama on nutrition practices, hygienic practices (including IPC related to Covid-19), Infant and young child feeding and other health seeking behaviours.

project_name: Child and Youth Education Pathways for vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
NRC’s project will contribute to Education sector HRP objectives 1 and 2. NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and hybrid modalities. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality.
The Education intervention forms part of NRC Syria’s integrated response. The Education team will continue working in close collaboration with the ICLA, Shelter/WASH, and Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) programmes to enable conflict and displacement affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. We must ensure pathways back to learning and integration into formal education and acknowledgement of previous learning through supportive policies (accreditation, certification, examinations, and documentation). NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable children and youth across Syria through the delivery of its three-pronged Child Education Pathways (CEP) and Youth Education Pathways (YEP) programmes. Each response modality (Emergency, Transition, and Recovery) is designed to ensure that conflict and displacement-affected children and youth are provided with age and context-specific educational pathways. All three modalities have been designed to support all out of school children and youth in entering the formal education system and succeed in their learning pathways, prioritizing those that have been displaced by the conflict and are returning home from both inside and outside Syria. All three modalities include capacity development opportunities for teachers, trainers, facilitators and coaches and will be implemented in cooperation with the ICLA, Shelter/ WASH and LFS programmes and partners. The teacher training packages include NRC Better Learning Programme.
The target group of the Education Programme in Syria is defined as conflict and displacement-affected children (aged 6-17) and youth (aged 15-18), including Syrian IDPs, IDP and refugee returnees, host community members, and Iraqi refugees. The exact target group definition will vary for the different response options: 
•	Emergency Response activities will target newly displaced and returnee children (6-
14years) and youth (15-18 years); 
•	Transitional Response will target out of school children and youth in contexts of long-term displacement and prolonged absence from school with activities tailored on their specifi c context (see more below); 
• Recovery activities will target vulnerable populations living in post-confl ict and/or stabilised non-camp settings (see more below). 
Teachers, facilitators and trainers will also be targeted across the 3 response options, working in NRC programmes in formal and non-formal education settings. For all NRC Education activities, civil documentation will not be a pre-requisite to receive assistance.

project_name: Health and PSS assistance to affected population in Lara State, Venezuela
project_objective:
Project aims to assist affected population by Venezuelan Crisis in Lara State, Venezuela, by providing necessary primary and sexual and reproductive health care services as well as psycho social support to vulnerable population, specifically targeting women and girls but also including  men and boys. The assistance is directed to health care centers in Lara State, which PUI will support by providing basic medicines and medical supplies, capacity building and infrastructure rehabilitation (this component in consortium), further PUI will implement community activities targeting vulnerable populations in the suburban areas of Barquisimeto by organizing health campaigns directed to sexual and reproductive health care and primary health care activities in schools targeting children in vulnerable areas. Targeted throughout a local partner, AVESSOC, the 2 health facilities were assessed: ADS Centro Monseñor Alejandro Zaini - dispensary in Duaca; ADS Centro Maria Auxiliadora Dispensary in Barquisimeto and 3 schools: one pre-school of  ADS Centro Maria Auxiliadora Dispensary and 2 Fe y Alegria high schools in Pavia (Irribarren Municipio) and Carora (Torres Municipio).
The beneficiaries in health facilities will be children, adolescents and youth up to 18 years old and pregnant and childbearing age women, in schools, children and adolescents of both sexes and within the communities, girls and women in child bearing age. The medical staff and management of the 2 health facilities will also benefit from capacity building; health staffs will be coached on clinical protocols and community agents will be trained in IEC/CBC technics, health and hygiene promotion.

project_objective: The objective of the project is to address survival needs of the most vulnerable crisis-affected households through the provision of  rapid response, Multi- Purpose Cash grants. The project will target 3,185 HHs, representing an estimated 19,110 individuals, and will aim to provide short term or seasonal support to communities facing emergency gap in humanitarian service provision and the inability to meet their survival needs.

project_name: Multi-purpose Cash Assistance that (regular and one-off) addresses food security, WASH, nutrition, shelter and other basic needs of the conflict-affected internally displaced, returnees and host communities in North West Syria
project_objective:
Through this action, NGO X will address the multiple vulnerabilities that households and communities are facing after ten years of conflict. At the household level, the program design creates links between its multi-donor funded emergency response program to its food security, nutrition, winterization and shelter programming, and complements food assistance programming (food vouchers and kits) with basic needs assistance via Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA). NGO X has included two MPCA components under this submission; the first is the one-off emergency MPCA with full SMEB value and the second is the repeated MPCA to cover the basic needs except the food items. The second MPCA component was deviated from the full SMEB value as it is a complementary approach to the regular food assistance activities. The value per HHs with the repeated MPCA component is $31 per HH for 6 rounds, which is complementing the food assistance activities which is equal to 70% of the food SMEB value which is in line with food security cluster’s recommendations. 


The proposed intervention is in line with the objectives and strategic direction of the various Northwest Syria Cluster Response Plans. These activities have been informed by Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSRNAs) conducted in Idleb and North Aleppo during 2020 as well as lessons learned from previous projects, ongoing monitoring, feedback from beneficiaries and other assessments conducted by NGO X.
Overall target:
The proposed activities outlined below will target approximately 69,396 HHs/346,980  vulnerable displaced and resident individuals in North West Syria (in Idleb and North Aleppo).
Project budget across sectors for the one-off MPCA is (based on the SMEB): 
· FSL: 70 % 
· SNFI: 15% 
· WASH: 15% 
The cash value of the MPG will be aligned with the SMEB. However, in terms of the regular MPCA for basic needs which is meant to cover 30% of SMEB (except food). The currency applied is USD. The number of households beneficiaries who will be target with one-off emergency MPCA is 17,421 HHs/87,105 individuals. The number of households beneficiaries who will be target with repeated MPCA is 51,975 HHs/259,875 individuals.
Prior to launching any response window/round, NGO X will coordinate response locations with CWG, SNFI, WASH, and FSL cluster partners/members to avoid overlaps and duplications. The sub-districts were included in the response locations are the locations where NGO X have access to and currently responding in. NGO X is following area/location-based coordination.  NGO X will also explore the potential for NGO X’s e-platform system to become interoperable with other platforms used by donors’ partners, maintaining the integrity of data protection and sharing key findings with the same donor.
The total budget of this submission is $15,290,431. $12,760,902 is contributing to repeated MPCA component which includes support and HQ costs, and $2,529,529 is contributing to one-off emergency MPCA which also includes support and HQ costs.

project_name: Ensure access to protection services to most vulnerable people living in underserved areas in Northern Syria.
project_objective:
The proposed program aims to enhance the wellbeing and resilience at affected population by providing a holistic approach psychosocial support intervention and prevention. In addition to the mental health treatments for people who are suffering from psychological disorders or concerns through a safe referral to specialized services within 23 PHC centers, in eight districts of Aleppo and Idleb governorates; Afrin, Al Bab, Harim, Azaz, Jarablus, Idleb, Jabal Saman and Tell Abiad, targeting reproductive-aged women, PLWs, and U5 children of the host and IDP communities.
IDA will provide integrated protection services, including specialized gender-based violence and child protection case management, advanced and focused, and/or those who are survivors or at risk of gender-based violence and abuse – especially women and children. The program will target at least 23,950 beneficiaries, 10672 W, 4146 M, 5412G, 3720B(1755 PWD), Attention will be given to appropriate entry points such as existing women’s groups and support networks. Areas of operation are selected in coordination with Clusters and health directorates.
Case management services will be tailored to beneficiaries’ individual needs and youth taking into consideration family and caregivers. Psychosocial support will help beneficiaries to improve their coping mechanisms, manage stress, and find solutions to their challenges. 
Group work will provide space for beneficiaries with similar issues, problems or circumstances to come together for mutual support. Outreach services will spread information on positive mental health and protection risks, as well as assist in reaching the most vulnerable in communities and making appropriate referrals to services. 
Training will target both community members and front-line service providers to increase their capacity to help and support others. 
Awareness-raising activities aim to decrease stigma around accessing services through encouraging people to be more aware of protection risks faced.
Activities will be accessible by all, efforts committed to creating an accessible environment for PWD and elderlies and balanced between the staff gender for better inclusion the communities.
the PWD rights are monitored through:
-	Mainstream disability into existing monitoring tools to ensure that violations for persons with disabilities specifically are being collected, analyzed and understood to inform programming and highlight the need for risk mitigation measures.
-	Collecting data on key rights to access and engagement.
-	Violations of rights of persons with disabilities to be monitored in auditing procedures.
for persons with disabilities and violations faced in relation.
The activities are covering; psychosocial support, community outreach, group work, awareness-raising activities, training for service providers and community members on mental health and protection topics, and integrated mental health services for the most vulnerable people, including people with disabilities, people facing mental conditions, psychological distress and trauma, also will target children and women assessed to be at high risk of abuse, exploitation, neglect or violence, children found to be associated with armed forces and armed groups, unaccompanied or separated children, persons with mental disorders or psychological distress, the elderly, chronically ill and people with disabilities.
All activities will be based upon the principles of the IASC Guidelines on MHPSS in Emergency Settings, Minimum Standards for Child Protection, and Guidelines for Integrating Gender-Based Violence Interventions in Humanitarian Action and GBV SC SOPs and guidelines. The NGO will work to improve the availability of holistic response for the most vulnerable by conducting training targeting a range of humanitarian actors in order to strengthen response with a survivor-centered approach.

project_name: Provision of protection services to vulnerable children and adults in North East Syria
project_objective:
We will continue to deliver comprehensive, service-based protection programs prioritizing the needs of the most at-risk and vulnerable individuals including IDPs, children, adolescent girls, and persons with disabilities in line with specific objective 2.1 of the HNO (Specific protection needs are mitigated through the provision of quality and integrated protection services). We will expand our case management program and referral system to ensure at-risk individuals are provided with holistic inter-sectoral support. For complex protection cases requiring specialist protection services, we refer cases to other agencies within NES in line with interagency guidelines on referral pathways. Likewise, other humanitarian actors in NES refer cases to the protection team. Finally, the protection team receive referrals from other sectoral programs within the organisation. We will ensure meaningful access through our outreach Program and mobile case management team. We will expand support to isolated communities in the western countryside of Deir-ez-Zor which are currently underserved by humanitarian actors while also expanding our existing outreach and case management capacity in Manbij, Kobani, Raqqa and Tabqa where we are one of the few NGOs providing these services.
We will continue to support some of the most isolated IDP settlements in NES by operating a minimum of 12 child-friendly spaces (CFS) and adolescent friendly spaces with an increased focus on Deir-ez-Zor. These spaces provide structured and systemic PSS activities to children and adolescents and educate parents on parenting skills and protection-related topics to build resilience through learning positive coping mechanisms. These spaces also help us develop community acceptance in newly accessible areas, in turn strengthening the outreach program by providing us with sustained and extensive access throughout the community.

project_name: Assistance en abris et Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) aux personnes déplacées vulnérables dans les régions de Diffa et Maradi
project_objective:
Le projet proposé par l'OIM vise la poursuite d'une réponse coordonnée pour couvrir de façon adéquate aux besoins en abris et en Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) aux populations affectées par la crise du basin du lac Tchad qui affecte les régions de Diffa et Maradi. L'objectif est de contribuer à l'amélioration des conditions de vies des populations déplacées à travers: i) la fourniture d'abris aux ménages vunérables, la distribution de kits BNA, dont  3 000 kits d'abris d'urgence et 3 000 kits de BNA à Diffa puis 1 000 kits d'abris d'urgence et 1 000 kits de BNA à Maradi, dans le cadre du HRP 2021. ii) Mettant à disposition 3 000 kits de BNA  et 2 000 kits d'abris  à titre de renouvellement des abris endomagés et Kits NFI n'existant plus, respectivement à Diffa et Maradi à travers l'option transferts monétaires conditionnel. 5 000 kits de Biens non-alimentaires seront distribués aux ménages à travers cette même modalité. iii)  La mise à disposition de 3 000  abris transitionnels qui seront  fournis  à Diffa pour améliorer les conditions de vie des ménages dont le retour dans les villages d'origine est incertaine du fait de l'insécurité dans cette région. En tant que Co-Lead du Secteur abris et BNA  l'OIM va continuer d'assurer la coordination du Groupe de travail abris et Biens non-alimentaires en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de l'Action Humanitaire, en  renforçant la collecte des informations de façon régulière dans le souci d'informer les intervenants sur la localisation, la nature et l'ampleur des besoins exprimés et des activités de réponse, de continuer à appuyer les partenaires et membres du secteur pour mener les activités dans le respect de la strategie du Groupe de Travail et des principes humanitaires et d'appuyer les services étatiques dans leurs rôles de coordination et suivi des activités du secteur.
Les activiés de la réponse d'urgence se conformeront aux Principes de Protection tranversales et au Cadre institutionnel de l'OIM de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre en situation de crise (VBV) , intégrera des mesures visant à assurer la sécurité, la dignité et le bien-être de la population touchée, et intégrera le respect strict de principe de tolérance zero pour toute exploitation et abus sexuels. Ce projet s'inscrira dans le respect des principes humanitaires et portera une attention particulière au principe ne pas nuire, de sécurité et non-discrimination. Les activités du projet seront mises en oeuvre dans le respect soutenu des règles de lutte contre la COVID 19 par l'observation de mesures barrières telles que le port du masque, le lavage des mains, le respect de la distanciation sociale afin d'endiguer tout risque de contamination et de propagation de la maladie aupres des bénéficiaires. Un système de gestion de mécanisme de plaintes sera mis en place afin que les plaintes sensibles soient traitées conséquement dans le but d'apporter une assistance respetant l'égalité et la dignité des communautés bénéficiares.  Dans le cadre de la redevabilité de sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées avec les beneficiaires,la phase d'évaluation de besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, la communication avec les communautés et les autorités locales sur les criteres de ciblage seront organisées et apres intervention, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que les actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires en affichant les compositions de kits BNA et Abris. A cet effet. Une collaboration étroite sera faite avec les acteurs de protection aura lieu. Le cout total du projet sera de 9.563.333 USD.

-All targeted sub-districts are considered high severity.
-The Cost per student is about (100 USD).
-The project targets 23,253 beneficiaries about 2 % of them are disabled.
-During 2020, GAN received about (5 M USD) in general, (1.650 K USD for education).
-So far in 2021, GAN has secured about  (0.6 M USD). War Child Holland and THF.

(20 K) beneficiaries in Education.
This project aims to address the following education needs which are considered as gaps in 18 of the targeted areas:
-Provision of formal and non-formal education for children.
-Rehabilitation / establishment of classrooms / TLCs in camps.
-Provision of stationary and learning materials for teachers, schools and students in
formal and non-formal settings.
-Provision of operational and running costs including fuel for heating.
-Training of teachers in emergencies
-Teaching essential life-saving skills and support provision of information on GBV and
other forms of violence, anti-trafficking, unexploded ordnance, diseases, nutrition, health,
hygiene and psychosocial health.
-Provision of schools’ furniture and students’ desks.
This project contributes to increasing access to education for girls and boys by addressing the needs identified in HNO 2021 and based on needs assessment conducted by GAN (April 2021). The project will provide safe and attractive education and learning environment in targeted areas and schools. It’s worth to be mentioned that GAN will rehabilitate schools and TLCs to be easily accessed by children with disabilities by providing rumps and special toilets and WASH facilities.
If the funding secured is lower than what is requested, GAN will conduct the same proposed activities targeting the same kind of beneficiaries but will decrease the targeted communities and/or schools depending on the most schools in need for rehabilitation and/or schools’ furniture.
ASER test will be conducted to help us better plan and focus on the needed type of educational activities based on ASER results, also to capture the impact of the intervention, also to capture the impact of the intervention, children will be provided with learning materials (bag, stationery, notebooks…etc.) the quantities and colors will be differentiated according to the level, gender, and age.
Following formal education will be followed by the project manager in cooperation with a consultant to provide periodic training TOT to supervisors in schools to train teachers in schools then evaluate the performance and provide additional training as required.
Teachers and education personnel will be provided with teaching and learning material and incentives for 9 months, and schools also will receive the needed tools, on the other hand, the PSS activities will be provided for students (1– 8 grades), one session a week using I-deal, little fellow, and children will be trained on the safety and security plans.
The education system, which has already suffered immensely as a result of the crisis, remains fractured and under-resourced limiting the ability of children to access education services. The curriculum used is SIG and a high level of coordination with ED and other working organization will be ensured to avoid duplications, the whole project activities will be implemented following the EiE, INEE guidelines, and CHPs.(HNO)
To ensure project quality, including beneficiary accountability, GAN MEAL system is such one that stresses regular and systematic consultation with beneficiaries about the project's different activities to ensure their relevance and appropriateness to the needs, so that beneficiary feedback contributes to the project quality monitoring and consequent improvement. Setting up the MEAL plan will help to identify needed monitoring activities and responsible staff for data collection,data analysis, and data reporting.

project_name: Support for voluntary repatriation of Undocumented Afghans
project_objective:
The presence of over 1.4 million registered Afghan refugees, and approximately 1.24 million Undocumented (840,000 Afghan Citizenship Card holders and 400,000 Undocumented Afghans), Pakistan hosts one of the largest protracted refugee situations globally. IOM supports the Government of Pakistan in the implementation of cross-border programming, with voluntary repatriation as one of the key elements, together with integration support, which aims at preserving space for Undocumented Afghans and promoting peaceful co-existence with host communities. 

More specifically, IOM activities have focused on (i) support to the Government during the Documentation Exercise; (ii) advocacy for inclusion of ACC holders and Undocumented Afghans to inform and plan aid assistance; (iii) support for ACC and Undocumented Afghans through livelihood and skills trainings; (iv) facilitation of voluntary and safe returns; (v) access to healthcare; and (vi) protection and assistance to the most vulnerable. 

To respond more effectively to the joint vision between Afghanistan and Pakistan for return of Afghan migrants, including anticipated multifaceted challenges posed by the complexity of large-scale cross border flows in 2021, IOM Pakistan aims to facilitate safe, dignified and voluntary returns of Undocumented Afghans from Pakistan to Afghanistan through a cohesive cross-border programming approach. In addition to creating an environment conducive for voluntary repatriation, IOM will also introduce them to skills development opportunities during their stay in Pakistan, to ensure access to livelihood opportunities in host communities as well as for sustainable reintegration in Afghanistan. 

IOM requires $40 million to address the immediate needs of 1,240,000 Undocumented Afghans in 2021 and beyond. Of this amount, $29 million included in this appeal is urgently needed for the provision of cash grants to returnees to ensure repatriation is made more sustainable.

ECW seed funding will initiate the implementation of the MYRP by focusing on reaching girls and boys in the States of Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe. In total, over 482,000 girls and boys will access learning opportunities, including some 48,000 girls and boys in early learning programmes, 341,000 at primary level and some 93,000 at the secondary level, in both formal and non-formal education settings. 
Save the Children has been selected as grantee/implementing partner along with Plan International and 2 NNGOs to implement the ECW MYRP in the 3 States.
Save the Children will target; 
•	168,000 girls and boys will access learning opportunities, including 
•	16,800 girls and boys in early learning programmes, 
•	119,350 at primary level and 
•	32,550 at the secondary level
These children will be reached through both formal and non-formal education settings.
Save the Children will focus on over 60% of the children and adolescents targeted with ECW funds are girls and the programme will also ensure at least 10% of beneficiaries are children and adolescents with disabilities. 10% of the ECW funds support Early Childhood Education for the youngest learners. Over the three-year period, implementation will contribute to achievement of both MYRP results and the overall EiE Strategic Plan.
This will be achieved through following outcome interventions; 
Outcome 1 Increased access to quality, inclusive, holistic education for crisis-affected girls and boys (including adolescents)
Outcome 2 Increased continuity of education for crisis -affected girls and boys (including adolescents) is through improved transitions to formal education from alternative provision
Outcome 3 Existing learning environments are child-friendly, gender-responsive, equitable, disability-friendly and inclusive 
Outcome 4 Improved quality of learning for crisis-affected girls and boys, including adolescents
Outcome 5 Safe and protective learning environments for crisis-affected girls and boys are established 
Outcome 6 Improved coordination mechanisms to respond to education in emergencies 
Outcome 7 Improved rates of enrolment and learning outcomes for girls, including adolescent girls 
Outcome 8 Sufficient resources are available to implement all MYRP strategies and enable the handover of the beneficiary caseload to development and government partners
SCI will complement its interventions and resources to achieve overall goal of ECW MYRP through following key initiatives; 
•	Continued delivery of strong education in emergencies programming; 
•	Mainstreaming of learners into formal education; 
•	Addressing key crosscutting issues, with a special focus on gender, disability and mental health and psychosocial support; 
•	Strengthening educator and school leader capacities and motivation:
•	Strengthening local leadership to take full ownership of delivery and transitions to formal education:

project_name: Improved safe back to school access to inclusive and quality education for most vulnerable children and teachers in oPt
project_objective: The COVID-19 spread implications affected all life aspects in oPt, particularly education, which overwhelmed the education system with extra burden in addition to challenges facing education in oPt over the last decades. In Gaza escalations and blockade is continuing for 13 years, increasing poverty and unemployment rates, lack of resources and protection concerns. In WB and Jerusalem, checkpoints and the Barrier impede access to education for children living in the “Seam Zone” and in East Jerusalem communities isolated by the Barrier. In addition, recent years witnessed an increased number of Israeli attacks on schools located in Area C and Hebron H2. All of these factors put children at huge risk of losing access to education with increased possibilities of drop-out and be left behind for the marginalized groups of children mainly CWDs and children living under poor conditions. Therefore, SCI will focus on supporting Safe Back to School actions by supporting 10,000 vulnerable and underserved children and 450 teachers through supporting their continued access to quality education, psychosocial support, improved emergency and adaptive infrastructure in schools, and support MoE and UNRWA teachers on remote learning aspects. Furthermore, it will support conflict-affected students with disability with assistive devices to ensure their equal access to inclusive quality learning opportunities, in addition to supporting 300 parents on self-care, stress release and supporting children in times if emergencies.

project_name: Community-based Mine Action in Somalia
project_objective:
The goal of the Community Based Demining (CBD) project is to clear explosive remnants
of war (ERW) according to humanitarian need, and to promote development by creating
large scale employment. These two activities combined will help to promote stability and
security through the destruction of ERW: 1) which explosives can be harvested and sold
on the black market, or kill/injure civilians; and 2) through the employment of fighting age
people who may otherwise be vulnerable to recruitment by terrorist networks.

In addition to direct implementation of clearance activities, HALO will partner with local NGO Shabelle and Hiran Mine Action Consortium (SHAHMAC) to conduct Risk Education, and will support SHAMAC in the delivery of explosive ordnance disposal callouts, and non-technical survey of contaminated areas. This will help support local capacity, with HALO staff local to Hiraan building the capacity of the LNGO, in direct mentorship.

In addition to the durable solutions and intervention targets detailed in the response plan, this project seeks to improve the inclusion of those with disabilities, reduce the risk of further disabilities, and provide coordination of victim assistance interventions. It will achieve this through:
- Provision of job opportunities to people with disabilities which do not affect manual labour (as deminers)
- Provision of job opportunities to people with disabilities which hamper manual labour (as watchmen, cooks, and support staff)
-Reduction of further disabilities by the clearance of contaminated land and destruction of explosive ordnance which is the root cause of disabilities
-referral of victims within area of operations to victim assistance services at a state and national level

project_name: Prevención y respuesta multisectorial especializada a la violencia basada en género para mujeres y adolescentes en situación de vulnerabilidad en Venezuela
project_objective:
El proyecto contribuye a reducir el riesgo de VBG de mujeres y adolescentes venezolanas en situación de vulnerabilidad y movilidad, ofreciendo respuestas especializadas para sobrevivientes de VBG, incluyendo hombres y adolescentes y principalmente mujeres y adolescentes en riesgo de VbG, garantizando que tengan acceso a servicios de calidad de manera oportuna. El proyecto contribuye a los objetivos estratégicos 1 y 3 del Sector de Protección, en siete estados de Venezuela, (Anzoátegui, Apure, Bolívar, Distrito Capital, Miranda, Táchira y Zulia), siendo los estados priorizados por el HNO/HRP 2021. La intervención beneficia directamente a través de la provisión de servicios de prevención y respuesta a la VBG a un total de 115,392 personas (mujeres, hombres y adolescentes) de las cuales 5137 mujeres y adolescentes (incluyendo hombres y niños sobreviventes), acceden a servicios de tipo especializado y personalizado. Asimismo, 70.000 mujeres y adolescentes reciben kits de dignidad (adaptados con EPP de COVID-19).  Se estima crear 4 Espacios Seguros para mujeres y niñas. 113.643 personas (hombres, mujeres, NNA) serán sensibilizadas e informadas para prevenir y mitigar la VBG y 2.300 personas con discapacidad serán incluidas tanto en las acciones de sensibilización como de respuesta. El proyecto prevé el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de 2635 trabajadores/as humanitarios de instituciones públicas y de la sociedad civil. Adicionalmente, la iniciativa plantea garantizar la calidad de los servicios ofrecidos a través del fortalecimiento de las capacidaes del personal implementador de VBG de UNFPA (83 personas) mediante sesiones de cuidados para el personal y modalidades de atención remota para sobrevivientes de VBG. 
El proyecto tiene un enfoque intersectorial con el área de salud sexual y reproductiva, con énfasis en el manejo clínico de la violencia sexual y fortalece el desarrollo de rutas de remisión y mecanismos de coordinación. 
El proyecto se estructura alrededor de 4 objetivos específicos.

1)	Fortalecimiento de mecanismos de coordinación de las intervenciones GBV que sean efectivos y eficaces a nivel nacional y local.
UNFPA liderará la actualización regular de las rutas de remisiones y POEs, creación de grupos temáticos de trabajo (Gestión de Casos, Transferencias Monitenarias de VBG y Trata y Tráfico), la armonización de la data de VBG y análsis de necesidad conjuntos. 
2)	Fortalecer los mecanismos y capacidades de prevención de la VBG a nivel comunitario a través de: i) modalidades de sensibilización comunitaria para la prevención de la VBG el abordaje de población en general (Mujeres, Hombres, NNA),con énfasis en violencia sexual y masculinidades positivas; ii) mantenimiento y creación de nuevos Espacios Seguros para mujeres y niñas; iii) entretamiento a promotoras comunitarias para identificar y prevenir la VBG; v) distribución de kit de dignidad a mujeres y adolescentes.
3)Proporcionar asistencia y servicios de protección especializados que incluyen: i) servicios de gestión de casos; ii) servicios de apoyo psicosocial y primeros auxilios psicológicos para sobrevivientes de VBG y afectadas por el COVID-19; iii) de orientación jurídica. 
4)	 Fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones del Estado, organizaciones humanitarias y la sociedad civil sobre el enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, técnicas de apoyo psicosocial y gestión de casos y directrices para la prevención de la VBG en la acción humanitaria.

project_name: Appui multisectorielle d'urgence, et soutien à moyen et long terme aux populations au sein du Mali touchées par les déplacements forcés.
project_objective:
Le HCR Mali poursuivra et accroîtra ses opérations d'aide aux personnes déplacées, retournés et populations hôtes avec une approche multisectorielle: interventions d'abris, EAH, Santé et Éducation, et intégration transversale de la Protection. Une approche holistique sera suivie pour répondre à l'urgence et promouvoir également le rétablissement des services de base et le développement durable afin de permettre leur consolidation et la réduction des facteurs de vulnérabilité et de conflit au Mali.

ABRIS
Réponse d’urgence
Plaidoyer auprès des autorités pour l'identification des parcelles où les personnes déplacées peuvent être installées, distribution de Kits d’abri et kits BNA-ménage.
Réponse à moyen terme
Case de type traditionnel. Les capacités seront développées pour pouvoir bâtir très rapidement cette solution d'abri semi-durable afin de l'utiliser comme solution d'urgence plus durable. Le HCR fournira les matériaux critiques et du cash pour acheter localement les autres matériaux et payer la main-d'œuvre spécialisée; les bénéficiaires participeront à la construction.
Réponse à longue terme
Solutions pour favoriser l'intégration des populations déplacées au sein des populations d'accueil et réduire des conflits à travers de programmes qui favoriseront le développement: réhabilitation des maisons; aide monétaire pour la construction de logements; construction conjointe entre personnes déplacées et communautés d’accueil; etc.

EHA
Amélioration de l’accès à l’eau potable qui remédie l’urgence et qui conduise à une situation durable: évaluation d’état des infrastructures existante; réhabilitation/construction de points d’eau en priorisant infrastructures modernes et pérennes.
Infrastructures d’assainissement d’urgence au niveau des espaces publiques et communautaires pour éviter la défécation a l’air libre; aires séparées Homme-Femmes et dispositifs de lavage des mains et de gestions des déchets solides. Construction de latrines familiales par les bénéficiaires qui recevront du matériel de construction et appui technique.
Promotion de l’hygiène et la gestion de l’hygiène menstruelle via les relais communautaires déjà formés et la mobilisation/formation des relais additionnels. Distribution de kits aux ménages les plus vulnérables et transition vers les transferts monétaires. Accent particulier sur la gestion de l’hygiène menstruelle dans les communautés et dans les écoles pour assurer la dignité des filles et des femmes à l’âge de procréation.

SANTÉ
Objectifs:
-Améliorer l’accès aux soins de santé primaires des déplacées internes, rapatriées et retournées.
-Contribuer à l’accès des personnes déplacées à la couverture médicale.
Interventions :
-réhabilitation de 2 centres de santé dans les zones de retour et fourniture des médicaments et équipements médicaux pour améliorer le plateau technique.
-Réintégration des déplacées internes, rapatriées et retournées dans les systèmes nationaux de prise en charge.
-Prise en charge médicale des Personnes à Besoin Spécifique vivant avec des maladies chroniques, en appuyant l’Etat et les services de santés.

ÉDUCATION
Le HCR vise à éliminer les barrières entravant l’accès des enfants au système éducatif formel à travers une approche holistique:
-10 écoles: Réhabilitation et équipement de salles de classes, latrines, etc; formation et appui en cash aux Comités de Gestion Scolaire favorisant la promotion d’environnements sûrs et propices à l’apprentissage indépendamment de leur statut, sexe ou handicap.
-120 enseignants, conseillers pédagogiques et volontaires seront formés en éducation inclusive, appui psychosocial et pratiques pédagogiques protectrices et innovantes centrées sur l’élève.
-Renforcement des opportunités éducatives alternatives pour 1,200 enfants déscolarisés et non scolarisés à travers la mise en place de 40 centres d’éducation accélérée.
-Distribution de 30,000 kits scolaires et sensibilisation sur le rôle de l’éducation dans le développement des jeunes garçons et filles.

project_name: Generación de capacidades para la gestión del riesgo de desastres en el sector Salud.
project_objective:
Se sumarán esfuerzos con comunidades, organizaciones sociales y autoridades territoriales de salud, para el incremento de capacidades y conocimientos del sector salud, incluida la comunidad en la identificación, alerta y respuesta oportuna a riesgos para la salud, se apoyará técnica y operativamente la disponibilidad y funcionamiento apropiado de los servicios esenciales de salud, así como el refuerzo de las acciones de salud pública ante emergencias o desastres.
El proyecto tiene tres ejes fundamentales:
I. Preparación del sector salud para la respuesta en emergencias y desastres:1.Desarrollo de capacidades técnicas sectoriales y comunitarias para el conocimiento del riesgo. Incluye procesos de formación del talento humano de salud y organizaciones comunitarias, así como dotación de elementos para la preparación y respuesta a emergencias. 2. Promoción y fortalecimiento de procesos participativos. 3.Diplomado con enfoque diferencial (Preparación para la respuesta en emergencias y desastres, primeros respondientes, ERI y vigilancia comunitaria). 4. Procesos formativos a personal de áreas ambientales, personal sanitario y líderes comunitarios, sobre potabilización del agua, control de calidad de esta y prevención de enfermedades transmitidas por vectores y EDA y 5. Implementación de la estrategia Hospital Seguro. 6. Sistematización de las experiencias y comunicación del riesgo.

II. Atención en salud a población vulnerable en el marco de las emergencias:
 1. Apoyo al desarrollo institucional de jornadas de salud con equipos móviles (médico/a general, pediatra, psicólogas(s), nutricionistas, gineco-obstetras odontólogas(os) enfermeras(os) y vacunadores).Se hará especial enfasis en la población más vulnerable como son las gestantes y primera infancia, priorizando a los menores de 5 años con desnutrición aguda,  para lo cual se fortalecera la capacidad del personal de salud en la identificación y tratamiento oportuno  y donación de FTLC para los casos que lo ameriten, de acuerdo con las  directrices nacionales, así como el fortalecimiento de  factores protectores como lactancia materna y alimentación complementaria.  Adicionalmente se desarrollarán acciones de fortalecimiento de  la capacidad de respuesta institucional y mantenimiento en la prestación de servicios esenciales de salud sexual y reproductiva y salud materno infantil. 
 2. Apoyo en la gestión para la atención de pacientes. (articulación interagencial para la complementariedad). Acciones de prevención y mitigación de la morbilidad materna extrema y reducción de muerte materno perinatal y  embarazo en adolescentes , a traves del fomento de servicios de salud con enfoque diferencial, articulando la respuesta institucional y comunitaria.  (Entrega de kits e insumos para la atención, generación de rutas de atención diferencial, acciones de fortalecimiento de capacidades técnicas, acciones de seguimiento y canalización)
3. Fortalecimiento de rutas para la atención a la Violencia interpersona, Violencia Basada en género, especialmente Violencia Sexual con enfoque diferencial (Incluye espacios de formación, fortalecimiento de rutas, definición de protocolos, entrega kit PEP y definición estrategias de comunicación)
4. Formación a actores comunitarios e institucionales en primeros auxilios psicosociales individuales y comunitarios. Implementación de una estrategia de primeros auxilios psicosociales con enfoque diferencial. 5. Apoyo al desarrollo de jornadas de intensificación de vacunación. a través del fortalecimiento de los equipos de vacunación móviles, contratación de vacunadores, supervisores y apoyo a la movilidad de estos equipos 
6. Apoyo al fortalecimiento y adecuación de servicios de vacunación institucional.

III. Recuperación de las emergencias desde el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de resiliencia:1. Diálogos comunitarios e institucionales para la consolidación e implementación de planes de recuperación.

project_name: Humanitarian Assistance for Rohingya Refugees in Camps and Livelihood Recovery Support for Affected Host Community in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
The project intends to provide lifesaving/humanitarian assistance to refugees in camps, livelihood recovery, and resilience-building support for the host community population, targeting the most vulnerable population such as poor households relying on wage labor, households with no or very limited productive assets, households affected by disasters (Covid 19, cyclone, heavy monsoon, influx, etc.). Households with a high dependency ratio, headed by women, children, chronically sick persons and households having an individual with special needs like PWD, PLW, elderly persons will get priority while targeting beneficiaries. The ultimate goal of the project is to contribute to ensuring food and nutrition security through emergency assistance, livelihood recovery support to promote income for both refugees and the host community population. To achieve the goal, the project intends to undertake food security and livelihoods interventions such as (1) Food assistance (cooked meals); the main target for cooked meals from the community kitchen is Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), Children under 5 years, adolescents, elderly person, persons with a disability could be entitled to this support  (2) Livelihoods assistance; support for homestead based food production, nutrition education, food safety, and hygiene sessions,  Business plan development, Livelihood/IGAs grant support, and Livelihoods restoration activity are planned to reach this activity (3) Self-reliance; technical training and inputs support for kitchen gardening, food processing, and small business are planned to reach this activity  (4) Skill development (support for skill-based technical training and inputs) (5) Disaster Risks Management through small scale risk mitigation measures. CFW will be linked with small-scale risk mitigation measures to reduce disaster risk as well as to provide temporary employment for the affected population. 
The project will ensure a safe environment by upholding gender equality as per IASC Gender and Age Marker. Protection mainstreaming principles are some of the measures taken to ensure gender-responsive programming. The project will give priority to special groups; female-headed households, PLW, under 5 children, PWDs, and the Elderly during the implementation of project interventions according to their needs. Sex and Age Disaggregated data will be collected, analyzed, and used to understand the needs of men and women. Those needs will be taken into account during service delivery to the project participants. Creating an enabling environment for the women participants is another key consideration and it will be taken into account in all service facilities including capacity building training in training centers. 
The project will ensure the active participation of the community in different activities. The project will have a contingency plan to respond to man-made and natural disasters (monsoon flood, landslide, and cyclone) with close collaboration with all stakeholders.

project_name: Strengthen Emergency Response through Camp Coordination and Camp Management in North East
project_objective: The project seeks to fill the gaps of CCCM Sector in line with the centrality of protection strategy and will target 120,000 women, men, boys and girls IDPs living in the camps, camp-like settings, IDPs out of camps and host community that received the IDPs and dwelling in their houses. The project will cover 4 LGAs in Borno (Ngala, Munguno, Banki and Damasak), 4 LGAs in Adamawa (Yola South, Yola North, Mubi and Madagali) and 2 LGAs in Yobe state (Damaturu and Gujba). The breakdown of the target for this CCCM project is 97,298 individuals (19,460HH) for IDPs and 22,702 individuals (4,540 HH) for returnees distributed as follow: 46% (male), 54% (female), 60% (children), 36% (adult) and 4% (elders). The CCCM Project will be addressing the gaps of tracking movement of population (new arrivals and returnees) particularly the most vulnerable including unaccompanied and separated children, assessing the needs of the women, men, boys, girls, adolescents and older displaced persons in a participatory manner and based on age, gender and diversity, (AGD) mainstreaming, supporting the coordination of response of service providers, capacitating the communities through their effective participation and ownership of activities and developing the resilience and self-reliance when they are still in displacement. The project will also focus on the sensitization of IDPs especially youth, boys, girls, adolescents and women who are facing different problem of protection. The CCCM project will improve the quality of management of the women, men, boys and girls IDPs within the camp settings, monitor and assist those out of camps and some vulnerable persons in host community. The project will support systematic follow up of the IDPs and returnees' new arrivals particularly vulnerable women and girls. The project seeks to provide quality services during the registration process and will ensure that reception facilities are equally accessible to women, men, boys and girls newly arrived. Camp managers will ensure proper relocation of new arrivals from the reception centers to the shelters constructed taking into account the needs of the most vulnerable. Through this project, CCCM interventions will also assess, analyze and report on all protection gaps and needs to be addressed by different sectors in order to improve the living conditions of women, men, girls and boys displaced, including the vulnerable populations in out of camp status. The CCCM project will promote the participation of the IDPs based on age, gender and diversity in the life cycle of camps particularly care and maintenance of infrastructures, small scale drainage, etc.
