project_name: Providing support to centralized and decentralized water supply and wastewater systems in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts in eastern Ukraine.
project_objective:
This project aims at addressing WASH-related needs of the conflict-affected population in Donetska and Luhanska oblasts in eastern Ukraine. Within the framework of the project NW will provide multipurpose assistance at different levels, including community, institutional as well as household level. The intervention will not only significantly contribute to the safe and qualitative service delivery to the conflict-affected communities, but will enhance their resilience in light of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. 
The project activities will contribute to the WASH Objectives set for 2021: 
-	Ensure immediate and sustainable access to sufficient safe water, and minimal levels of sanitation provision for conflict- and COVID-19-affected people; 
-	Provision of critical WASH-related supplies and information for the prevention of infectious diseases;
-	Promote resilient, recovery and sustainable access to sufficient safe water, minimal levels of sanitation provision, and minimum hygiene standards in conflict- affected oblasts. 
The project activities are designed to cover needs of all vulnerable categories of the affected population considering gender and age aspects. In particular, it refers to construction works in public institutions as well as distribution of hygiene kits to HHs.
The project intervention will contribute to address WASH needs of around 128,000 people of communities in Luhanska and Donetska oblasts on both sides of the LoC. For that purpose NW is going to attract 2.2 M USD in 2021 within the humanitarian response to the crisis in eastern Ukraine.

project_name: Strengthening Health, Community Resilience and Livelihoods in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts
project_objective:
In its seventh year, the armed conflict in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts in eastern Ukraine continues to have a devastating effect on people, with 3,4 million in need of humanitarian assistance and protection. The Covid-19 pandemic has been further aggravating humanitarian needs, particularly for people living in rural areas close to the contact line and most notably elderly, who lost access to humanitarian assistance and social payments due to travel-restrictions, are unable to cover their basic needs amid rising prices, and resort to negative coping strategies. With overlapping vulnerabilities and multiple needs, the protracted crisis in Ukraine requires a multisector approach that links the alleviation of immediate basic needs with measures that increase resilience and promote recovery at community level

The project is aimed to contribute to sustaining and safeguarding of the lives of vulnerable populations and internally displaced Ukrainians at conflict-affected communities in Donetsk and Luhansk regions through sustainable recovery and resilience measures. The contribution is supposed to make through two strategic objectives:
•	SO1: Vulnerable conflict-affected households (HHs) along the contact line in non-government controlled areas (NGCA), especially FHHs & HHs with elderly people, are able to secure their basic needs and sustain their lives. (56% female, 44% male)
•	SO2: Vulnerable conflict-affected HHs along the contact line in government-controlled areas (GCA), especially FHHs & HHs with elderly people, have improved their health and resilience amid Covid-19 and recovered their livelihoods towards increased sustainability. (70% female, 30% male).
Target group: Direct target group: 12,820 individual unique beneficiaries (7,858 women, 4,962 men) living close to the contact line in Donetsk and Luhansk in government-controlled (GCA) and non-government controlled areas (NGCA). Indirect target group: 1,382 indirect individuals living close to the contact line in GCA.
Project Geography:  Valuiske, Makarove, Vilhove and Zolote-4 in Luhansk oblast, and Novobakhmutivka and Novoselivka in Donetsk oblast, Ukraine.
Expected results: 
1.1.	At least 1,440 vulnerable households of IDPs and host population in NGCA have improved living conditions through winterization support and hygiene assistance. (56% female, 44% male)
2.1.	At least 300 highly vulnerable people with special needs in GCA have improved their hygiene conditions through the provision of hygiene kits, 150 of whom have additionally improved their physical health through the provision of homecare services. (70% female, 30% male).
2.2.	At least 240 vulnerable people (including 150 highly vulnerable people with special needs who receive homecare services) benefit from improved psychosocial well-being (75% female, 25% male).
2.3.	At least 480 people in 6 target settlements benefit from improved community cooperation to support their resilience towards the effects of the ongoing conflict and the Covid-19 pandemic. (70% female, & 30% male) 
2.4.	 At least 9.000 people in 6 target settlements in GCA, especially women and elderly, have increased awareness about Covid-19 related risks and prevention measures, 1.200 of whom have decreased vulnerability against the pandemic by obtaining PPE kits. (63% female, 37% male)
2.5.	At least 60 residents (80% women and 20% men) of IDPs and host population have improved capacity to start and re-start businesses, 30 of whom engage in income generating activities based on increased knowledge, skills and business grants.
2.6.	At least 45 staff of implementing partner organisations operating in GCA or NGCA have increased capacity to implement interventions that mainstream gender and protection and follow a community development approach.

project_name: Provision of security communications and data connectivity services to the response community
project_objective:
In 2021, the ETS will continue to provide overall coordination through developing and implementing plans, reporting activities, and identifying needs as the situation evolves. The ETS will hold regular Working Group meetings to ensure plans, activities and gaps are shared and discussed with partners and will act as a forum where partners can exchange information, best practices, access technical expertise and support. The ETS will also continue to publish and share regular, accurate operational Information Management products with partners and relevant stakeholders to support decision-making, avoid duplication of efforts and strengthen advocacy.

The humanitarian community’s demand for reliable communications services remains a priority. To address this, the ETS will continue to provide security communications and data connectivity services across all common operational areas to support the humanitarian and enable the provision of digital assistance to affected communities. The ETS plans to install cyclone-resilient towers which will significantly improve the radio communications capacity (multiple simultaneous talk channels) but also the access to data connectivity services, in collaboration with the Bangladesh Telecommunications Regulatory Commission (BTRC). The ETS also plans to install back up solar power solutions in all sites to ensure the full operability and sustainability of its services.
In addition, the ETS will engage with the “Communication with Communities” initiative to assess and possibly support them with ICT requirements.

To strengthen local emergency communications expertise and skills on the ground, the ETS will continue to assess the needs of staff on the ground and conduct capacity building exercises tailored to those needs. One specific skillset that requires further capacity is the implementation and maintenance of VHF and HF radio infrastructure and networks in line with UN standards. This will also ensure the sustainability of services in Bangladesh in the future.

project_name: Prévention et reponse VBG pour la communauté d'accueil dans le ZAR d'Intikane, région de Tahoua
project_objective:
Le projet proposé vise à intervenir dans les secteurs de la VBG, sur les principaux risques et besoins identifiés, en particulier les mariages précoces, l'exploitation et la violence sexuelles, la violence conjugale.
Spécifiquement le projet vise à mettre en place 1 mécanismes communautaires de prévention et signalement des cas de violences basés sur le genre et conjugales ; realiser 50 séances de sensibilisations sur la thématique de VBG pour une prise de conscience au sein de population ; identification et référencement 30 cas de VBG au niveau communautaires auprès des structures de prise en charge et documentation appropriées ; formation des 20 personnes (personnels de santé et acteurs de protection dans la zone) sur la prise en charge holistique des cas de VBG ; distributions de 400 kits de dignités aux filles et femmes à risques; accès à la fotmation professionnelle et aux AGR pour 30 femmes.

project_name: Enhancing resilience of conflict-affected population for future crises in eastern Ukraine through community mobilization
project_objective:
The community mobilization project aims to support grassroots initiatives of vulnerable communities to increase community-based protection (with immediate impact on civilian protection) and meet their social cohesion needs. The project is directly aiming at supporting organic efforts within the communities, and increasing dialogue with key authorities and stakeholders, to increase their resilience and find sustainable solutions to their issues.  
All project activities are based on the analysis of protection issues and needs (based on age, gender and diversity approach), and prioritization of protection risks and solutions in every particular community. Community mobilizing seeks to empower communities to develop their own community-based coping mechanisms, to exercise their rights, and to find solutions for the most pressing issues of protection mainstreaming in their communities. Communities will mobilize themselves when they have trust and confidence in the process and when they see benefits emerging from their own efforts. Through local ownership, inclusive participation and community-based approach the community engaged projects are to create social cohesion in fragile communities and have more sustainable effect.
Activities will include facilitation of community coming together to prioritise their needs and realise their community-based protection and social cohesion projects. Activities will also include trainings and support to local activists, so they can continue community mobilisation in the longer-run, and engage in dialogue with authorities and other key stakeholders. Activities will also include, from individual empowerment perspective, working with local partner(s) to help with legal assistance and similar support to the most vulnerable individuals in the communities: this is to ensure, not only basic legal protection, but also to foster a rights-based consciousness that will enable inclusive participation in community life and further advocacy. Activities will finally include evidence-based advocacy: raising the voices of the communities, up to national level advocacy, on the main issues they face and to promote proper protection mainstreaming in humanitarian response.
Throughout its action, PIN will pay special attention to Accountability to the affected population. PIN will do so by actively engaging women, girls, boys and men, individuals in their diversity without discrimination (with due regard to underlying inequalities) in the identification and prioritization of their needs through extensive consultations and facilitation of community actions. PIN will also strengthen its established Community Feedback and Response Mechanism, including with strengthened response to complaints as well as referrals, as well as internal learning cycles to ensure that affected populations’ feedback is integrated into project proposals, strategies, monitoring and evaluations, trainings and performance tracking management, partnership agreements etc. PIN will continue to provide accessible and timely information to beneficiaries on organizational procedures, structures and processes that affect them to ensure that they can make informed decisions and choices, and facilitate a dialogue between an organization and its beneficiaries over information provision.

project_name: Most vulnerable communities and residents have improved access to safe and affordable water, sanitation and hygiene, prevention and reduction of risks of COVID-19 proliferation
project_objective:
The WASH project aims to improve access to sufficient safe water and enable adequate sanitation and hygiene practices for the most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men in conflict-affected areas and put at greater risks in the face of COVID-19. Through enhanced targeting of particularly underserved communities and enhanced community-based approach, the project covers both actions of immediate relief and longer-term resilience and self-sufficiency, and will invest special attention and efforts to support both transition in GCA and responding to enduring humanitarian needs in NGCA.
The project first aims to improve access to sufficient safe water to the most vulnerable left with chronically unmet water needs in conflict-affected areas, through a dual approach. The project will first focus on improving the water system infrastructure (including repair/maintain centralized, decentralized and private water supply in public infrastructure and social institutions and/or organizing new access to sustainable/alternative water source). It will do so through the facilitation of partnerships among communities, authorities and water utilities for an inclusive and accountable implementation. The project will then keep an agile approach to respond to the life-saving needs for safe drinking and technical water of the most underserved and vulnerable communities and individuals through water trucking, installation of water tanks, and in case of shocks and emergencies, distributions of water bottles. To help transitioning the response to ensuring the sustainable provision of access to safe water, the project will include to foster community-based and multi-stakeholder engagement on water governance, as well as to amplify advocacy with local, regional, national and international stakeholders on water quality.
The project also aims to improve access to adequate sanitation by initiating support for community-driven waste management. This will include to facilitate and support partnerships between communities, CSOs, the local administrations and other local stakeholders on improving solid waste management in selected communities. This will also include to test community-based waste management activities in the most vulnerable, underserved locations where over-accumulated solid waste is presenting a serious public health threat. 
The project finally aims to enable adequate hygiene awareness and practices, especially in the face of COVID-19 risks, to the most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men. It will do so by keeping here as well an agile approach enabling different modalities of assistance, through the provision of hygiene kits, vouchers and promotion through risk communication and community engagement actions.
Throughout these actions, PIN will maintain a robust Community Feedback and Accountability Mechanism though its community-based approach and engagement with women, girls, boys, men, elderly and people with disabilities to raise their voices; enhanced consultations and testing of participation and social accountability mechanisms; feedback and complaints hotline, response, referrals and analysis for further adjustment of the assistance.

project_name: Comprehensive humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations affected by the military conflict in eastern Ukraine and / or COVID-19 with a focus on access to food and income opportunities
project_objective:
The FSL project aims to improve the food security for the most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men in conflict-affected areas and put at greater risks in the face of COVID-19, and support women and men engage in sustainable livelihoods, in the agriculture and in other sectors alike. Through enhanced targeting of particularly underserved communities and enhanced community-based approach, the project covers three levels of actions, from immediate relief, through self-sufficiency, and longer-term resilience. It will invest special attention and efforts to support both transition in GCA and responding to enduring humanitarian needs in NGCA, and integrate the age, gender and diversity factors influencing food security and livelihoods, including factors of feminised poverty and care dependency.
At a first level the project aims to ‘ensure immediate access to food’ for the most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men living along the ‘line of contact’ in both Luhansk and Donetsk NGCA. The assistance will take the form of food vouchers, and be organised through quarterly rounds to take account of seasonal variations. In addition, PIN will provide short-term, immediate assistance in the form of food kits for those most at risk in the face of COVID-19. Through this modality, those individuals with greater health risks and no direct support system will have access to food items while minimising their exposure to COVID-19 infection risks.
At a second level, in GCA the project will then aim to improve longer-term, sustainable food security for women and men and their households with access to small landplots near the LoC. Such assistance will take the form of seasonal activities, with distribution of vouchers for seeds, of drip irrigation kits, and delivery of trainings. It will enable smallholder farmers in underserved communities to increase their self-sufficiency throughout the year. As such the project will directly contribute to the cluster objective to ‘Improve food security through the provision of emergency and time-critical agriculture assistance’.
At a third level, in GCA the project will eventually aim to support access to employment and micro-, small businesses for women and men in communities near the LoC. Trainings will be held, not only on employment, vocational and business-related topics, but also to foster individual empowerment. Special attention will be paid to support women- and youth-led entreprises for equal access to opportunities and as vectors of development for their entire communities. On short-term and seasonable basis, cash-for-work opportunities will be created around community needs, whether to rehabilitate priority infrastructure or realise other community-based initiatives, account taken of age, gender and diversity. This will serve both poverty reduction, community social cohesion and living conditions in the communities. As such the project will directly contribute to the cluster objective to ‘Enhance resilience of vulnerable people affected by conflict and/or COVID-19 through restoring of non-agriculture livelihood and promote resilience to shocks (including wildfire, unemployment, higher prices, and other hazard) at community level’. 
Throughout these actions, PIN will maintain a robust Community Feedback and Accountability Mechanism though its community-based approach and engagement with women, girls, boys, men, elderly and people with disabilities to raise their voices; enhanced consultations and testing of participation and social accountability mechanisms; feedback and complaints hotline, response, referrals and analysis for further adjustment of the assistance.

project_name: Ensure Effective Coordination Response to Support Detection and Treatment Facilities for Aid Workers
project_objective: The project seeks to support the coordination and COVID-19 preparedness and response to front-line NGO aid workers in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. Support mechanisms will ensure inclusion of distance consultations and detection and treatment referral pathways and improvement of health facilities.  The facilities that will be made available will allow for testing of the virus and be equipped to address the needs of NGO aid workers should they test positive for COVID-19 and need urgent assistance.

project_name: Strengthening child protection prevention and response mechanism through enhancing community-based child protection and to safeguard children in Rohingya and host communities
project_objective:
IOM’s Child Protection Project in 2021 aims to continue to prevent and respond to child protection issues and empower vulnerable girls, boys, parents and caregivers  in camps and in the host community by strengthening the protective environment. 
To achieve the objectives IOM’s activities will focus on enhancing community-based protection  including capacity building, engagement, awareness raising and promoting participation by supporting community-led activities; specialized child protection services, such as case management, structured PSS for children and MHPSS for parents and caregivers, supporting child survivors of GBV in the camps and in the safe shelter; strengthening Community-based Child Protection Mechanisms and capacity building of child protection duty bearers in local government level (Union, Wards). 
IOM CP programming incorporates age, gender, and diversity needs of the affected population to respond to specific needs, especially to enable girls and boys, children and adolescents, children with disabilities to be instrumental in improving the quality of their life and mitigating risks and dangers in their community and living environment.
             Services will be provided through implementing partner Terre des hommes (Tdh) in camp 13, 20, 20 extension, in the host community in Ukhia/Palong Khali, IOM directly implement in camp 9 and 23, in Ukhia (Ratnapulong) and Teknaf (Nhila, Sabrang) and in camp 7,9,17, 18, 20 extension, 23 in the Child Friendly Corners of the Women and Girls Safe Spaces. 
With a cross-cutting approach IOM CP closely cooperates with other sectors  (Health/MHPSS, Shelter, WASH, Site Management, Transition and Recovery Division ) to mainstream child protection, disability, to coordinate disaster preparedness and emergency response and to strengthen the PSEA and Community Feedback Mechanisms to ensure accountability for the affected population.
IOM CP is committed to child protection inter-agency efforts and contributes to the CP Sub-Sector, CP Case Management Technical Working Group, MHPSS Working Group and PSEA Network.

project_name: Improving Displacement Management and Camp Coordination and Camp Management in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
IOM aims to facilitate the immediate, adequate and equitable delivery of services to the displaced population in camp and camp-like settings through camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) services, information management mechanisms, and sector coordination of partners and stakeholders.

CCCM activities will continue to provide site facilitation support and site level coordination in formal and informal camps in the following Borno locations: MMC, Bama (including Banki), Dikwa, Gwoza (including Pulka,) Ngala, Monguno, Mafa, Jere, Kala Balge (Rann), and Damboa; and in the following Adamawa locations: Yola North, Yola South, Girie and Song.

The Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) will continue to provide mobility tracking in the six conflict-affected northeastern Nigerian states (,Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe). with the Emergency Tracking Tool (ETT) deployed mainly in Adamawa, Borno, and when necessary, in Yobe due to fluidity of population movement. Biometric Registration will remain a priority in selected camps to assist partners for verification (WFP) and support other organizations and their distributions. Finally, detailed assessment surveys for return locations will continue in selected areas. DTM will strive to strengthen regional collaborations in place with emerging needs as well.

As Sector Co-Lead, IOM with UNHCR, is accountable for the overall CCCM, Shelter and non-food items (NFI) responses in North-East Nigeria. The sector will continue to ensure access to multi-sectoral assistance in camps and camp-like settings, advocating and identifying durable solutions for the displaced families and affected communities; and building national capacity through CCCM trainings for national authorities and local partners.

project_name: Protection et recherche de solutions durables pour les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile vivant au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
En 2021, plus de 19400 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile maliens vivront dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. 
La totalité des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile vivent au sein des communautés hôtes du fait de l’insécurité grandissante qui a causé en 2020 le retour au Mali de plus de 4.900 réfugiés et l’auto-relocalisation principalement dans les villes de Djibo et Dori de près de 9.000 réfugiés. Du fait d’une accalmie relative autour du camp de Goudoubo, des conditions difficiles de séjour des réfugiés dans les villes de Dori et Djibo, de la situation sécuritaire extrêmement précaire aux alentours du camp de Mentao, près de 7000 réfugiés des provinces du Seno, de l’Oudalan et du Soum ont émis le souhait de se relocaliser dans le camp de Goudoubo/province du Seno sous conditions de sécurisation par les autorités et de la réhabilitation par l’UNHCR des abris infrastructures détruits par l’usure et le vandalisme. Les 12.400 autres réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile vivront dans les 3 régions au sein des communautés d’accueil et des déplacés internes. 

La crise de la COVID19 ajoutée à cette insécurité a eu un impact négatif certain sur la protection et l’assistance des réfugiés vivant dans ces régions avec les restrictions à la liberté de circuler, la violation du caractère civil et humanitaire des camps, les suspicions avec comme corolaire la stigmatisation des réfugiés et les arrestations arbitraires, les risques de refoulement, les atteintes à la vie ou à l’intégrité physique, les violences basées sur le genre et la violation des droits à l’éducation de l’enfant et le difficile accès aux services sociaux de base. Ce contexte est également venu anéantir les efforts et perspectives d’autonomisation dans un contexte de pression sur les ressources disponibles pour les populations hôtes et les personnes déplacées internes.

Le présent projet vise à fournir une protection et une assistance ainsi que la recherche de solutions durables aux réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile maliens vivant dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. Les activités de protection et d’assistance seront essentiellement  le monitoring des frontières pour s’assurer de l’accès au territoire des personnes ayant des besoins de protection internationale, l’enregistrement des demandeurs d’asile, le monitoring de protection des réfugiés, le renforcement des activités visant la protection de l’enfant et la protection contre les violences basées sur le genre, l’éducation, la relocalisation des réfugiés vivant dans les provinces du Soum, de l’Oudalan et du Seno vers le camp de Goudoubo, la documentation des réfugiés et l’inclusion de ceux vivant hors camp dans les programmes d’assistance humanitaire et de l’assistance multisectorielle dans le camp de Goudoubo ainsi que les activités visant la cohabitation pacifique avec les communautés d’accueil. La recherche de solutions durables demeurera également une priorité.

project_name: Strengthening EPI program in Syria and protect against outbreaks of Deadly Vaccine Preventable diseases
project_objective:
Strengthening routine vaccination activities is still an essential concern to increase the national coverage rate at national and governorate level, regular routine immunization activities is provided in all governorates, the vaccination activities are continued in coordination with all related partners (including UNICEFf and NGOs) to cover the needs of children under 5 and to increase the community immunity especially among all vulnerable groups , WHO has facilitated the delivery of vaccines( by road& Air ) to all governorates in addition to support the operational cost of the filed work including :transportation cost, incentives for mobile teams , operation cost , which will facilitate the field work of the EPI program at national, governorates and district level. Capacity building will be provided to the healthcare workers and managers involved in the reporting, planning, implementation, and monitoring of the immunization activities. MOH is providing vaccination services to all children of Syria (target 2021 is 572,825 children under the age of 1 year) in all 14 governorates. Several tactics are used for service delivery through fixed vaccination sites and mobile teams as well in coordination with the local communities to facilitate the access for the families and service providers; WHO and partners support in the coordination, technical and financial support of the activities including the IPC material procurement and cascade training for service providers and supervisors capacity building for quality services and gain community trust as well.
In northwest Syria, WHO supported re-establishment of EPI services, and has increased the number of active vaccinations centers from five in March 2017 to 93 in 2021. WHO supports the operational costs of 40 of these centers, covering 62 of a total of 134 vaccination teams. This work has been impeded by security issues leading to huge population movements at the beginning of 2020 and loss of accessibility to some areas. The latter issue necessitated the reallocation of 23 EPI centers to new areas to serve displaced populations inside NWS. 
Within implementation of this HRP project WHO in cooperation with Syria Immunization group (SIG) and in close collaboration with UNICEF and other NGOs/INGOs actors in the north of Syria is planning to sustain services of the Expanded Program on Immunization EPI in the NWS, including routine re-mapping of communities and new settlements to be able to follow population movements inside the country. 
All EPI activities held in Syria is according to the set plans preplanned prior to the beginning of the year. Those plans are valid for all territories under the government of Syria including the Self administrated areas of NES. WHO and UNICEF do have also representation in the 5 hubs to support the MOH further in the implementation and the monitoring of the EPI program. For the implementation of the vaccination plan in northwestern Syria focus will be on: mapping high risk areas with low routine immunization performance and developing special strategies to close gaps; training new vaccinators and providing on-the-job refresher courses for existing vaccination teams; and outreach efforts, especially to nomadic populations, IDPs and hard-to-reach communities.
Monitoring and evaluation on the other-hand, is also supported by WHO and UNICEF, the MOH does conduct regular monthly visits to from the central level and governorate level  to the district and health centers based on a preset plan the findings are being shared with the field level workers for immediate adjustments and follow up. 
One of the reasons for the increased cost for this project, including the monitoring cost, is the inflation rate and the devaluation of the Syrian pound which had an impact on the program cost in terms of transport for personnel and vaccine across the country. All incentives have been increased based on the official request sent to the UN agencies (since September 2020).

project_name: Increasing the efficiency of the humanitarian demining process in East Ukraine through the implementation of national Capacity Building
project_objective:
In 2018 an initiative by a group of deminers created a national non-governmental (non-profit) veterans-orientated organization Ukrainian Deminers Association (UDA). The main purpose of this organization is to solve state problems in the field of mine action (MA).
For this purpose, the UDA is coordinating on all levels: local, national and international. The UDA is a permanent member of MA activities (meetings, round tables, conferences, etc.) under international organizations (UNDP, OCHA, PCU OSCE, etc.) and (MoD, MoI, Ministry for the reintegration of TOT, etc.). The UDA has close cooperation with local Administrations of the Donetsk and Luhansk Oblasts.
In response to Ukraine's challenges and threats related to the explosive remnants of the war (see “Needs” section), UDA's experts have developed a plan aimed at increasing the efficiency of the humanitarian demining (HD) process in East Ukraine through the implementation of national capacity building for explosive ordnance risk education (EORE), non-technical survey (NTS), technical survey (TS), and explosive remnants of war (ERW) clearance. 
For these purposes, the UDA will deploy 3 HD teams and 2 EORE teams. Moreover, the main equipment of deminers will be provided by UDA’s American partner as a temporary importation of property which in turn will significantly reduce the cost of HD in East Ukraine and allows UDA’s quick deployment.
UDA has teamed with US-based company Tetra Tech and will implement activities based on a MoU between organizations. Tetra Tech currently holds the US State Department global MA contract and offers a wide range of international development services including capacity building support to local national organizations in a wide range of specialities. The primary aim of the Tetra Tech personnel managing this project is to optimize efficiency, effectiveness, and safety, skills transferal and ensuring good stewardship of donor funding. A key aspect of this is conducting training and mentoring of UDA personnel to enable them to manage operations independently in compliance with their own SOP’s, national standards, IMAS and donor regulations.
The M&E process during the implementation of this project will be provided by U.S. company Spilna Mova. UDA signed an MoU with Spilna Mova earlier this year and is already jointly implementing a US Government funded mine action project. 
Cross-Cutting Issues:
While developing organizational capacity, UDA will train Ukrainian veterans to perform as a humanitarian demining operator. UDA is looking after the interests of representatives of a large group in the modern Ukrainian society, approximately 400,000 veterans. In addition to physical and mental healthcare issues, a major problem for Ukrainian veterans is finding employment for and enabling their successful reintegration into society. 
UDA will also include a strong gender component in 2021 development plan. Inclusiveness and gender will be one of the main points during the implementation. These indicators will be tracked and reported throughout the program.
One of the most energizing capacity development components will be the participation of American counterparts in the training and implementation as consultants and advisors on the best practices on humanitarian demining, organizational and project management, M&E, strategic communications and gender. 
UDA understands that effective mine action will contribute to Ukraine’s economic development and, ultimately, to the country’s stabilization. This project focuses on three objectives to support this goal : (1) build a sustainable Ukrainian mine action capacity through well-trained teams operating in compliance with IMAS; (2) increase access to safe land by prioritizing clearance areas for maximum socio-economic impact through proactive and effective coordination with stakeholders; and (3) reduce mine/ERW accidents through robust community liaison (CL) and effective EORE.

project_name: Addressing urgent humanitarian needs of communities affected by the wildfires in Luhansk oblast GCA
project_objective:
The objective of the proposed project is to address urgent shelter needs of vulnerable households severely affected by the October 2020 wildfires in the government-controlled areas of Luhansk Oblast. 

To assist households in fire affected areas, IOM proposes to distribute construction kits to enable the households who had their homes destroyed by the fire to rehabilitate the structures. 

IOM intends to target 5 out of the 15 villages that were affected by the September fires with a total of 450 homes that have been completely destroyed. During the distributions of tools for the removal of debris of destroyed or damaged houses in the immediate aftermath of the fires, IOM  identified that construction kits were the primary request from local authorities and community memebers. To facilitate the development of construction kit content, IOM civil engineers will carry out assessments of the locations to assess the content and quantity of supplies required for the construction kits for the damaged households. 

As many of the residents of affected areas are elderly, IOM will also provide conditional cash grants to enable the residents to hire labourers who can assist in the reconstruction of the damaged houses. IOM discussions with affected community members indicated that they would probably be able to manage the reconstruction through communally pooling their collective skills. However, given the level of damage, a conditional cash grant will facilitate a more rapid recovery for the communities by enabling them to hire in additional assistance. 

Lastly, IOM intends to provide support to the forestry and emergency services for them to conduct training with local communities at risk on fire management to mitigate against future risks. IOM will support through essential equipment provision for the emergency services as well as through training and awareness raising among community members with the intended outcome that communities will be better capacitated to manage future fire threats and protect their properties and livelihoods.

project_name: Rehabilitation of critical WASH infrastructure in key social institutions and community sites of Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts
project_objective:
This project aims to support health and social institutions, as well ask key community sites in the field of WASH in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts through most needed rehabilitations of WASH-related infrastructure. This will allow targeted institutions to conduct their lifesaving, life-preserving and regular work more safely and effectively.

After six years of simmering conflict in Easter Ukraine, WASH infrastructure in areas close to the contact line is severely impacted by the shelling, as well as from the protracted lack of maintenance resulting from unavailability of public resources, reprioritization of expenditure and difficulties in accessing affected areas. As a result, many settlements on both government and non-government-controlled areas have remained cut out from water supply or must deal with the consequences of frequently disrupted supply. This has a great impact on the communities’ capacity to access running water and means to maintain proper hygiene behaviour. The most affected are vulnerable community members who reside or seek services in medical and social institutions, with precarious structures, inadequate water and sanitation facilities, as well as affected by chronic underfunding to address maintenance needs and replace obsolete or non-functioning WASH equipment. 

In response to the critical need for improved access to water and sanitation facilities in social and medical institutions of Donetsk and Lugansk oblasts (both GCA and NGCA), IOM proposes to capitalize on its extensive experience to continue conducting WASH-related structural rehabilitations in 80 facilities serving the most vulnerable community members affected by protracted armed conflict and including COVID-19 cases. Targeted facilities are most likely to include, amongst others, hospitals, outpatient clinics, IDP centres and institutions for the elderly and people with disabilities. The envisaged medium-size interventions will consist of, but are not limited to, the replacement and/or repair of water supply elements, sewerage and wastewater management systems, rehabilitation of sanitary structures with installation of appropriate plumbing equipment, as well as repair or substitution of water containers and boilers.

Given the frequent damages to the water supply systems at the settlement level, which cause disruption of water supply for individual households and social and medical institutions, IOM also intends to conduct WASH-related structural interventions of relatively high complexity in 19 community sites. These activities, which will focus exclusively in the NGCA of Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts, might include cleaning, repair, drilling of wells for water supply, installation of water towers, replacement and/or repairing of water supply, sewerage and heating systems at community level, rehabilitation of water reservoirs, installation of septic tank disposals, replacement and start-up of pumps, pumping stations and frequency converters to ensure efficient power consumption by water supplying equipment. IOM has a proven track record in rehabilitations in NGCA and GCA and is scaling up GCA WASH rehabilitations in response to the increased need for functioning WASH facilities in social/medical facilities in light of COVID-19.

project_name: PROBES (Provision of basic essential quality health care services to affected IDPs, returnees and host population in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States)
project_objective:
The PROBES project is in line with WHO’s strategic shift to the Global programme of work13 (GPW13) goal which focuses on 3 interconnected strategic priorities aimed at ensuring healthy lives and promotion of wellbeing at all ages i.e Achieving universal health coverage (UHC), addressing health emergencies and promoting healthier population. All this aligns to the Health Sector priorities i.e Maintenance and continuation of essential health care services in all priority locations and IDP camps and expansion of health services in hard to reach accessible areas and underserved communities. The project will take into consideration the current needs and gaps in the ongoing humanitarian situation in the BAY states and undertake measures to decrease morbidity and mortality among vulnerable groups, including older people and those with underlying health conditions and disabilities. 

PROBES is a 12 months’ project aim at reducing mortality and morbidity in areas with low and no health service coverage by ensuring increase access to high impact health and nutrition services for the targeted population. It more particularly aims at:
•	Delivering of extended basic and essential health packages in areas with low/no access through a modulation of health delivery platforms taking into account the situation in the targeted areas (security, number of facilities, population, etc.) to ensure comprehensive access to quality care combining treatment of common ailment, antenatal care to pregnant women, immunization, vitamin A and deworming to children, screening of children for malnutrition, health promotion activities and outbreak detection, integrated Community Case Management of childhood illnesses (incl. treatment of malaria, pneumonia and diarrhea, screening for potential high-risk health conditions, health education services and referral to health and vaccination services) and medical support for non-communicable diseases, including GBV, HIV, STI, mental health, etc.
•	Establishing strong ambulance service and referral links between the complicated lifesaving health services and the secondary levels of care available in the targeted states to ensure progressive integration of the services provided through the MHT and CORPs into a strengthened state health system 
PROBES will target 783,00 people distributed as 250,560 IDPs, 156,600 Returnees and 375,840 Host community in BAY States. The project implementation will be achieving through various platforms of service delivery to include: Hard to reach mobile health teams (HTR MHT) providing basic essential PHC services, Community Oriented Resource Persons (CORPs) dealing with integrated community case management of childhood illnesses within children homes in the community, interventions to curtail the burden of malaria, strengthening PHC services to provide mental health and GBV services as well as having a robust referral system to secondary and tertiary health institution for further care. 
The proposed intervention has been designed with measures to prevent or minimize any unintended negative effects and protection concerns for women and children would be ensured at all health care services including Gender based Violence interventions would render with dignity.
WHO is committed to promoting Accountability to the affected population, for the project by involving the beneficiaries in the design of the project and taken into account feedback from the beneficiaries in the monitoring of the intervention.

project_name: Improved access of COVID-19 affected population to Primary Health Care, essential health services including MNCH, RH, EPI and communicable and Non-Communicable diseases, services in the district of Shangla, KP, Pakistan.
project_objective:
Due to the current global pandemic of COVID-19 Like many other countries globally the health system in Pakistan is overwhelmed due to required response to COVID-19. Therefore, there is an urgent need to support and compliment government efforts for coping with the current pandemic alongside with continuity of essential health services including MNCH, RH, EPI and Non-Communicable diseases. Project aims to reduce avoidable morbidity and mortality as a direct or indirect consequence of COVID-19 outbreak. 

The proposed project is designed according to the health needs of local population of district Shangla and health cluster strategic objectives, to avoid preventable morbidity and mortality among the affected population by ensuring access of locals and other vulnerable groups to essential life-saving Health Care services, infection prevention and control (IPC), alongside with continuity of essential health services including MNCH, RH, EPI and Non-Communicable diseases, provision of life-saving medicines and other medical supplies. The propose project will support communities through IPC, Primary Health care and MNCH and other essentials health services in selected villages in the catchments of health facilities (THQs, RHCs, BHUs and CDs) in the tehsil of Besham and Alpurai.
 
Major interventions/activities in the proposed Project are:
•	Revitalization and operationalization of health systems in target areas through provision of facility based and mobile health services, necessary equipment and medicines.
•	Continuation and strengthening of Primary Health Care services in selected villages of vulnerable population in areas of Tehsils Besham and Alpurai of district Shangla.
•	Establish communicable disease surveillance and response mechanism to mitigate morbidity and mortality among affected population through infection prevention control.
•	Provide life-saving critical MNCH and reproductive health services through treatment of children under (boys and girls), PLW and referral mechanism will be established for high risk cases.
•	Provide mental health and psycho-social support to the affected vulnerable groups like women, children, chronically ill and disabled.
•	Provide essential life-saving medicines and supplies necessary for effective service delivery to affected population
•	Conduct Health and Hygiene sessions to raise Health and Hygiene awareness among the targeted Population to counter COVID-19 in communities.
•	Provision PPEs to health staff and communities include hygiene kits

project_objective:
The aim of the project is to strengthen health information systems for emergency response and resilience across the country. The information generated from the health
information systems provide up-to-date information on functionality of facilities, availability of services, and accessibility of beneficiaries. All health partners are/would

To ensure quality health information products; WHO conducts joint monitoring visits with MoH to health facilities to follow up on HIS issues at health facility level (reporting, challenges, needs…) in addition to HeRAMS internal and external evaluation exercises.
In northwestern Syria the information system HeRAMS is used to track the functionality, accessibility, infrastructure, services and staffing levels of hospitals and health care facilities. WHO uses this information to strengthen facilities in areas shown to be in greatest need. The information generated from the health information systems provide up-to-date information on functionality of health facilities, availability, and accessibility of services. project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des personnes touchées par les inondations à travers la réponse intégrée aux Violences Basées sur le Genre
project_objective:
Les inondations sont récurrentes au Tchad pendant les années où la pluviométrie est élevée. Malgré que ces phénomènes soient récurrents, les dispositions ne sont pas toujours prises pour minimiser les effets, la population est toujours surprise par l’eau, avec de pertes matérielles (habitation, récoltes, biens, …) ainsi que de pertes humaines. En 2020, la saison des pluies a enregistré des précipitations records, le mois d'août en particulier a provoqué de nombreuses inondations sur la plupart du territoire national : au centre, au sud, à l'est, au Lac et dans la capitale N'Djamena. Les statistiques du Gouvernement indiquent que les inondations ont affecté près de 388 000 personnes dans l’ensemble du pays, dont 60 000 personnes poussées au déplacement dans la province du Lac. L’on enregistre de pertes en habitations, des champs inondés, des récoltes agricoles endommagées, … Les sinistrés trouvent refuges dans des établissements scolaires ou autres lieux publics et ne doivent y vivre que pour quelques temps (3 mois maximum pour les lieux publics). Avec la pandémie de la maladie à coronavirus, cet attroupement ne respectent pas les mesures sanitaires. L’absence d’abris porte atteinte à l’intégrité physique et à la dignité des personnes. La promiscuité des populations est un précurseur de trouble psychologique et d’exposition aux violences sexuelles. 
Dans un tel contexte les VBG sont inévitables, pendant la phase, de relocalisation, il est urgent de mettre en place ou renforcer les services de prise en charge holistiques de VBG ou un système de référencement fonctionnel et organiser des séances d’informations sur les VBG et les conséquences. La mise en place de d’auto-soutien des femmes et filles avec des activités concourant à des solutions durables est aussi nécessaire pour promouvoir la dignité et la sécurité des femmes et filles.
Le présent projet vise à renforcer la résilience de ces populations affectées. Ainsi le projet permettra de :
-	Préparation des populations vivant dans de zones à risques sur les risques possibles de VBG pendant les inondations 
-	Prévenir les risques de VBG 
-	Améliorer l’accès aux services essentiels de qualité pour les personnes survivantes de VBG 
-	Le renforcement des connaissances sur les notions de compétences de vie (santé sexuelle et reproductives, connaissance sur les droits et textes législatifs, les VBG et les voies de recours, …) et la COVID19
-	La distribution des kits de dignité
-	Renforcer les capacités de résilience des femmes et filles affectées par l’inondation ainsi que la cohabitation.

Les cibles sont les personnes survivantes des VBG ; et aussi les hommes, femmes, garçons et filles des communautés par le transfert des connaissances sur les notions de compétences de vie courantes.

project_name: Access to life-saving sexual and reproductive health services for women in reproductive age
project_objective:
El proyecto del UNFPA está dirigido a mujeres y niñas en edad reproductiva y mujeres embarazadas y sobrevivientes de violencia de género. El proyecto ayudará principalmente a mujeres y niñas indígenas y afrodescendientes con necesidades humanitarias críticas como consecuencia del conflicto armado, los desastres naturales y la pandemia COVID-19, en zonas remotas y semiurbanas sin una respuesta estatal eficaz, con escasa, nula presencia o baja capacidad de establecimientos de salud.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo garantizar servicios integrados de SSR / VG: 1) Fortalecer la respuesta multisectorial que salve vidas; 2) Reducir la violencia de género y los riesgos de SSR; 3) Reducir la mortalidad materna y 4). Reducir los embarazos no planeados y otros daños a la salud sexual y reproductiva. En SSR  se logrará mediante dos resultados i) Las mujeres embarazadas han mejorado el acceso a servicios maternos y neonatales de calidad, que incluyen el parto seguro e higiénico, asegurando que las instituciones de salud manejen adecuadamente las complicaciones obstétricas y neonatales, garantizando rutas de derivación seguras y funcionales 24/7, desde la comunidad a los servicios de salud y para hospitales de referencia. ii) Las mujeres en edad reproductiva tienen acceso a otros servicios y suministros esenciales de SSR como se describe en el Paquete de servicios iniciales mínimos (PSIM), como anticonceptivos e información para prevenir embarazos no deseados. 
Los servicios y suministros de SSR y VG se proporcionarán principalmente a través de equipos móviles en áreas rurales. La prestación de servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva se garantizará con un equipo de salud y en alianza con el Ministerio de Salud, se apoyarán los establecimientos de salud (Atención Obstétrica y Neonatal Básica de Emergencia (BEmONC)) en el área de cobertura, con equipos y suministros básicos de SSR, incluyendo equipos de protección personal. se fortalecerán los asistentes de partos tradicionales (TBA) y las derivaciones de SSR. El equipo móvil de SSR garantizará los servicios de planificación familiar, la atención esencial para las mujeres embarazadas y la información que salve la vida de las necesidades de mujeres en edad fertil.

project_name: Accès aux services de santé de la Reproduction dans le contexte de crise au Niger
project_objective:
L’objectif général de ce projet est d’améliorer l’accès aux services et à l'information des soins de santé de la reproduction, notamment les soins obstétricaux et néonatals d’urgence y compris le référencement des complications obstétricales la prise en charge clinique des viols pour une cible de 1 392 751 personnes dont 348 188 femmes en âge de procréer dont 75 487 naissances attendues ; 264 623 adolescentes de 10 à 19 ans ; En bref l'intervention consistera à offrir des services de qualité en rapport aux accouchements assistés. Sur les  30 195 naissances attendues cibles le projet vise à toucher 40% en accouchements assistés soient  12 078  accouchements assistés qui seront réalisés dans les 54 CSI des régions de Tillabéry, de Diffa,  de Tahoua et de Maradi. Le projet prend en compte la crise Covid-19 et assurer toutes les mesures de protection individuelles et renforcer la prévention des infections afin d’assurer la continuité des services. Le projet vise aussi à assurer les 7 fonctions des soins obstétricaux et néonatals d'urgence dans les 29 CSI identifiés des 4 régions soient 6 à Diffa, 12 à Tillabéry, 4 à Tahoua et 5 à Maradi. La résilience des communautés passe à travers l'offre de la planification familiale faire face aux problèmes récurrents d'insécurité alimentaire avec une conséquence directe sur la malnutrition des enfants de moins de 5 ans. Le projet assurera la prise en charge clinique des viols  par la formation des agents en prise en charge clinique des viols et la mise à disposition des PEP kits  enfin le projet va renforcer la lutte contre les IST/VIH/sida parmi les populations jeunes. 
La mise en œuvre de toutes ces interventions nécessiterait au préalable l'approvisionnement en kits SR au dernier kilomètre, l'appui en personnel de qualité notamment les sages-femmes et la mise à niveau des maternités pour augmenter la capacité d'accueil et la mise en place de certaines commodités tel que des sources d’eau et de lumière et certains équipements médicaux essentiels permettant d'assurer la qualité des services.

project_objective:
The project aims to contribute to lifesaving and life-sustaining health assistance in NWS with focus on the most vulnerable groups, including IDPs and host communities in the target area. Another aim is to contribute in recovering the largely disrupted public health services across areas of displacement. The project will contribute to the following two objectives of Food security cluster: Objective 1: Increase access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable humanitarian health services for those most vulnerable and in need. Similarly, it is related to 2021 HRP Strategic Objective 1: Provide life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable people, with an emphasis on those in areas with a high severity of needs.
The project will start off with a thorough field needs assessment, consulting with health facilities and personnel, communities, local stakeholders, and health directorates. The assessment will include collection of data on infrastructure, staff and available specializations, current health support provided, available medical equipment and assets, and type of medical supply needs. One of the main challenge to overcome is the recruitment of female health workers, due to that there is a relatively small numbers of whom are certified. Nevertheless, IR Turkey will aim to recruit around 25% female workers, depending on the availability of female workers at the time of signing the MOUs. Moreover, the assessment will also focus on protection risks faced by the target population and communities, and collection of SADDD will be ensured throughout.
