project_name: Agricultural and Livestock Support and Emergency Response to most vulnerable IDPs in Northern Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to provide a wide-ranging support from emergency to regular food assistance as well as household based agricultural and livelihoods assistance. The project aims to target populations who are both food insecure as well as at risk of food insecurity through multiple but mutually reinforcing activities. The project will contribute to the following two objectives of Food security cluster: Sector Objective 1: To Scale-up and sustain minimum food consumption needs through life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance. Sector Objective 2: Support self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives. 
A total of 25,000 households (125,000 individuals) will be supported through multiple but integrated activities.

Under ﬁrst objective for life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance, the project will aim to meet the immediate food needs and also seasonal/supplementary food assistance. The Emergency Response will aim to reach crisis-affected people within 72 hours of the onset of a crisis to cover a minimum of one to four weeks of their immediate food needs through short-term support such as Ready-to-Eat Rations, cooked meals and/or baked bread. Baked bread will also be provided to the displaced families living in the camps. this will help to stabilize the market prices. further supplementary food assistance will be provided to improve the dietary diversity. such as Ramadan food distribution and Qurbani meat distribution
Under the second objective; The proposed project seeks to improve the livelihood situation of 2,000 households through livestock and agricultural support in Harim and Idleb District of Idleb Governorates. The project is developed based on the primary need assessment conducted through focus group discussions and key informant interviews in nine communities. 1,000 families to be provided with agricultural input (winter) including wheat seeds, fertilizers and basic tools. These families will be provided with ongoing technical support to improve their knowledge and practices to get best yield. The estimated yield will be sufficient to cover the food needs of the household and any excess can be sold in the market to create income generation. In addition, 1,000 families (who have existing livestock) will be provided with concentrated feed. During the gestation period sheep will be provided feed. This will be in beginning of the winter period when the feed is most expensive and unaffordable. The sheep will be vaccinated against prevent them from contagious diseases. The households will also receive livestock health and milk kit. The expected milk production is sufficient to cover the household diary needs and any excess can be sold in the market to contribute to the income. 
Both beneficiary groups (livestock and agriculture) will continue to receive follow-up advice and training over the course of the project from field project team hired for this purpose.

project_name: Mitigating the impact of COVID 19 by ensuring uninterrupted access to quality Sexual Reproductive Health & Rights (SRHR) for displaced and vulnerable women, girls, youth & adolescents in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: To mitigate the impact of COVID 19 on the health care of Women, Girls, Adolescents and Youth: This project will increase access to lifesaving basic Sexual & Reproductive Health (SRH) services for vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host communities in the three conflict affected States of Adamawa, Borno and Yobe. Comprehensive Sexual reproductive health services including family planning will be provided to women of reproductive age including pregnant women, adolescent’s girls, young people and men in communities and health facilities observing strict COVID 19 Infection Prevention Protocols (IPC), using appropriate Information Education & Communication (IEC) as well as Behavioural Change Communication (BCC). The survivors of obstetric complications will also benefit from supported referral and specialized services. Medical equipment, supplies, Reproductive Health Kits, dignity kits and other items essential for SRH services will be procured and prepositioned to ensure uninterrupted service amidst COVID 19 restrictions to access and attendant utilization of essential Human Resources for Health. To ensure smooth coordination, advocacy and leadership of the sexual and reproductive health (SRH) working group under the health sector is to be strengthened to channel support to the maternal health programme and other specific SRH response; advocate at health sector level to ensure uninterrupted access to maternal health, and non-diversion of healthcare resources at the expense of pregnant and lactating women and adolescent in dire need of SRH services.

project_name: Promotion des droits au Logement Terre Propriété (LTP) au profit des personnes affectées par le déplacement dans les régions du Centre-Nord et Sahel au Burkina-Faso
project_objective:
Le Burkina-Faso, depuis 2015, suite aux attaques terroristes et conflits intercommunautaires, est confronté à un déplacement massif des populations qui ont été contraintes d’abandonner leurs champs, terres et biens, pour chercher refuge dans de nouvelles zones. L'augmentation de la fréquence des déplacements, en particulier dans les régions du centre-nord du Burkina Faso et du Sahel, a à occasionnée de multiples problèmes LTP auxquels sont confrontées les personnes déplacées. Ce sont, le manque d'espace dans les villes et les zones rurales, les occupations irrégulières, l'hébergement dans des espaces réduits et sur des sites inappropriés, la promiscuité dans les familles d'accueil des personnes déplacées, la précarité, la fragilité et la perméabilité des abris, les expulsions forcées, les loyers élevés, le manque d'espace et de ressources naturelles, les tensions intra et intercommunautaires, l'absence de documents de propriété et la méconnaissance des droits des personnes déplacées. 
En effet, dans la région du Centre-Nord,      les problèmes d’abris se posent avec acuité dans les communes de Barsalogho, Boussouma, Bourzanga, Kongoussi et de Nasséré. Cette situation est liée au fait qu’elles sont des communes d’accueil pour de nombreuses populations déplacées suite aux attaques perpétrées par les HANI dans leurs localités d’origine.  Nombreuses de ces populations déplacées, depuis leur arrivée, n’ont toujours pas d’abris. Il s'agit de certains PDI de Petabouli auxquels s’ajoutent les nouvelles PDI venues du village de Soum-Bella dans la commune de Koutoukou et qui sont actuellement au secteur 02 de Djibo. Ce sont 125 ménages de 991 personnes déplacées du fait des attaques des GANI dans leur localité. 
 Dans le souci de promouvoir le droit d’accès aux logements, terres, biens et ressources naturelles aux femmes, hommes, filles, garçons et personnes en situation d'handicap/groupes minoritaires affectées par la crise dans les régions du Centre-Nord et du Sahel  et garantir la sécurité de tenure en vue de les  protéger contre toute éventuelle éviction, NRC organisera des campagnes de sensibilisations sur  les droits  relatifs aux LTP;  fournira des conseils juridiques aux PDIs en vue de les aider à surmonter les obstacles les empêchant d’exercer et de jouir de leurs droits LTP, mènera des plaidoyers pour leur faciliter l’accès temporaire ou durable aux droits  LTP et renforcera les acteurs locaux impliquées dans la prévention et résolution des conflits fonciers.

project_name: Sustaining life-saving sexual and reproductive health services, by supporting response, preparedness and resilience of Gaza community and health system to crises including COVID-19.
project_objective:
As evidenced in the 2021 HNO, the needs for sexual and reproductive health “SRH” remains high considering the protracted crises and the lock down due to COVID-19 outbreak, associated with redirection of resources (human, medical and logistics) from the provision of SRH services have affected around 80,000 additional vulnerable women. This project is aligned to HNO 2021 Health Cluster Strategic Objectives 1, Ensure the availability of acceptable and quality essential healthcare services to vulnerable communities across oPt, and is directly linked to Strategic Objective 2, meeting health needs and providing basic health services. The project is also well aligned with Health Cluster Strategic Objective 2, Strengthen the healthcare system's capacity to respond to emergencies and build community resilience to cope with the impact of current and future crises, and is directly linked to Strategic Objective 3, building the capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome the protracted crisis. The project contributes to preventing excessive maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality, which have early indications of increasing over the last three years. The project will increase access to healthcare and nutrition services and ensuring that clean and safe delivery, and emergency obstetric and newborn care services are available at all times. The project will complement previous and ongoing UNFPA projects; CERF and HPF 2020, first standard allocation and other projects; by expanding coverage of health system capacity to endure continuation of essential SRH and maternal care services at primary and secondary health care levels and community. 
The project will: -
-	Ensure continuation of SRH services, enhance access to quality SRH care and strengthen SRH management and counselling, including the operationalization of relevant COVID-19 guidelines and protocols.
-	Build the capacity of health providers on life saving SRH issues including emergency obstetric care, high-risk pregnancy, pre-conception care and family planning etc.
-	Improve SRH services coordination among various stakeholders/providers, including mainstreaming disability, protection and GBV in SRH service provision and community outreach.
-	Combat social, cultural and economic factors/stigma, restricting free access to and choice of services by women.
-	Actively engaging communities, supporting coping mechanism, sensitization, awareness raising and outreach.
-	Support linking and informing communities to available service, including protection from GBV and psychosocial support, with special focus to marginalized communities and vulnerable groups including PwD, young girls, the poor and elderly etc.
-	Strengthen the preparedness of the health facilities, fill gaps and replenish life-saving SRH equipment, drugs, commodities and supplies including PPE.
While this project is meant to address immediate response to urgent and critical needs of Gazan’s women’s, and young girls, especially those in marginalized areas, it will also support men and other vulnerable adolescents and strengthen the preparedness and resilience of both the community and the health system for absorbing shocks, saving lives and recovering from crises.
UNFPA coordinates with active stakeholders including UN sister agencies (WHO and UNICEF), MOH and major NGOS to ensure complementarity. UNFPA will with MOH, Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) and other NGOs as needed to implement this project. UNFPA has been approached by Union of Health Works Committees (UHWC), who is applying for a project to support reproductive health services targeting women in their centers’ catchment areas in Gaza, to ensure coordination. UHWC was encouraged to apply, and to continue coordination and sharing experience and information on localities and target groups upon project implementation to avoid duplication and ensure synergism with UNFPA and other projects

project_name: Responding to Humanitarian Needs of GBV in East Jerusalem and Area C
project_objective:
With the existing health worldwide crisis of COVID19 and its long term impacts, the number of women in need for GBV services is increasing. In Palestine, the heightened political situation is exacerbating the situation mainly in areas like East Jerusalem and area C, especially the Jordan valley and northern district of the West Bank. In addition, the approaching threat of annexation and its impact on Government services in Area C further compounds the situation. Based on the needs identified through the HNO process, and several analysis of the humanitarian situation specifically in the aforementioned areas, the project and its interventions will aim to strengthen and empower women exposed to GBV.  The project will also enhance the approach of remote service provision through hotlines and other means in case the current situation of COVID 19 persists, also there will also be readiness to provide face to face services anytime feasible. During 2020, UNFPA has already conducted a series of online capacity building workshops on providing services using hotlines. Those workshops targeted a number of GBV services providers including governmental partners; this experience will be  advanced during 2021
 On the other hand, the project will target the GBV survivors as well the providers to match the scaling up of emergency GBV services with building the capacity of government and non-government actors to provide quality survivor-centred GBV services. the project will continue to use the multi-sectoral approach in providing the GBV services and build on past UNFPA achievements.

project_name: Improve the quality and coverage of inpatient care for Severe Acute malnutrition under five children in Stabilization Centers all over Sudan during 2021
project_objective: WHO project aims to decrease avoidable under five mortality and morbidity related to Severe acute malnutrition through improved access and quality of inpatient care for the Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications in 139 stabilization centers currently Operating in health facilities. The project includes curative, preventive and promotive measures in the same time. The activities will address the clinical life-saving interventions in Stabilization centers targeting the patients/children with SAM and the mothers/caretakers through IYCF counseling and young children nutrition awareness to lower relapse and prevent SAM cases in the same households. The project activities and costing factored in 36 SCs are supported by NGOs. The SCs Supported by NGOs will require only Medical kits (1st and 2nd line medicines) and technical support.. Main activities: Training of the health and nutrition staff of 103 SCs (all except the ones Supported NGOs) to include IPD SAM initial training (7 days) and refresher Training (3 days), provision of guidelines, Job Aids and IEC materials to all participants from the 103 SCs. WHO will procure and distribute to 139 SCs; medicines (SAM inpatient Kits – first and secondary level care), , medical equipment and other supplies based on the needs identified together with MOH. To improve the quality of care and cure rate in SCs, WHO nutrition and public health officers present in all targeted states will conduct jointly with SMOH regular supportive supervisions in all targeted 139 SCs conducting on the job training, coaching, and adherence to the national treatment protocols. Routine nutrition surveillance at HF level/SCs, essential for trends and gap identification and effective planning of activities will be enhanced through training, provision of recording and reporting tools for the SCs in 11 targeted states, and better integration into HFs reporting mechanism to promote sustainability. WHO nutrition team will provide technical and operational support to the MOH at federal and state levels to regularly analysis the data of SAM inpatient care services (using the agreed performance indicators) to identify the trends, and challenges disaggregated by sex and age. The information will be disseminated to all relevant stakeholders through nutrition cluster bulletins, and bring during nutrition sector meetings led by MOH and UNICEF. Effective coordination of WHO with all partners (Nutrition, Health, food security) will promote an improved referral system between the SCs, TSFP, OTP, and community. Linkages with communities will be strengthened through raising awareness and social mobilization conducted by trained community mobilizers/CHW and MSG in coordination with other UN. The modalities and subjects for these activities will be guided by the community members suggestions collected through exit interview and focus group discussions during supervisions. The project activities also includes small repairs of 15 SCs in order to ensure better environment for work and improved hygiene in the SCs.

project_name: Provision of Life Saving Nutrition Interventions for Rohingya children, women, and vulnerable host population in Bangladesh through strengthening systems-based programming to ensure life-cycle based continuum of care.
project_objective:
UNICEF aims to transform the lives of vulnerable people, especially children and women, adolescent girls, by improving their nutritional and health status, given that these groups often have the greatest unmet needs. UNICEF Nutrition programming seeks to enable a child's full capacity through addressing preventative and curative needs at the age of 0-59 months. A high incidence/prevalence of malnutrition is often reported in children with disability, however, nutrition and disability are rarely linked. Children with disabilities scarcely have the same level of access to health and nutrition services; are often unaware of, do not plan for, and are unable to communicate effectively. UNICEF pursues to provide children and their families through lifecycle-based programming that addresses the holistic nutritional needs of every child at each stage of life including the special needs of children with disabilities. UNICEF’s aims to provide life-saving treatment through supply provision of ready-to-use therapeutic foods and works with partners to manage the urgent treatment of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition in the camp.

UNICEF will ensure that women and children have access to supplementation to address micronutrient deficiencies. To improve access to the quality nutrition services UNICEF will promote micro-gardening at household-level, with an emphasis on vegetables and fruits that is rich in nutrients. Additionally, knowledge and practices on appropriate food and nutrition practices will be improved through nutrition education sessions which will include cooking demonstrations for increased consumption of nutrient-rich foods produced at household-level in the host community. Therefore, UNICEF will support counselling and establish safe spaces within integrated nutrition facilities for promoting infant and child feeding in camps. UNICEF will support timely nutritional assessment and surveillance systems in order to track malnutrition rates and improve programme performance. The interventions will also promote speciﬁc and sensitive nutrition needs from an integrated multi-sectoral lens (including Water and Sanitation Hygiene, Health, and Gender) to ensure fulﬁllment of rights for each stage of the lifecycle for the most vulnerable and marginalized women and children. The project will ensure integration of Accountability of Affected People (AAP) through a multi-channel Complaints Feedback and Response Mechanism where feedback and complaints will be processed, analyzed and shared on a regular basis.

Mitigation measures are critical during the pandemic to ensure malnourished children continue to have access to nutritious foods and essential nutrition services in the context of COVID 19. UNICEF will ensure to prepare and respond to the COVID-19 pandemic by intensifying the public awareness, protection, promotion and support of appropriate and safe feeding for all breastfed and non-breastfed children and use all opportunities to include hygiene messages, key messages on COVID-19 symptoms, and Infection, Prevention and Control (IPC) measures. To mitigate any adverse weather incidents a contingency plan is developed and accordingly a buffer stock of supplies and medicines will be prepositioned in the INFs for the rapid deployment in situations of flood and cyclones. In addition, intensifying pre-positioning (with a minimum buffer stock of 2 months) of essential commodities for nutrition programming nutrition facility and community level in anticipation of supply chain disruptions. Furthermore, strengthen and reinforce the capacity of mothers and caregivers to detect and monitor their children’s nutritional status. As sector lead, strengthening coordination and partnerships with other institutions involved in the Rohingya response will also be an important aspect of UNICEF's interventions.

project_name: Sustaining the continuation of essential lifesaving sexual and reproductive health services for women, girls, boys and men in Area C, East Jerusalem, and H2 area in the West Bank during emergencies.
project_objective:
This project aims to mitigate the COVID 19 outbreak impact on the integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health services (SRH) and ensure the life-saving care for the residents of the most vulnerable communities of Area C and East Jerusalem of the West Bank. The project will do this through three main areas:
1.	Provision of health services that are needed due to the humanitarian crisis by a.) supporting MoH and PMRS to run primary health care level 2 mobile clinics including provision of SRH services for women, girls, young people including people with disabilities and b.) supporting emergency needs in fixed health facilities in the target areas, particularly H2.
2.	Community outreach on essential SRH and COVID19 information, ie. danger signs in pregnancy, family planning, etc. COVID19 will be integrated into the information and community outreach in regards to how it impacts SRH.
3.	Improved coordination of SRH humanitarian partners in close collaboration with MOH.

project_name: Strengthening food security and livelihoods of vulnerable communities affected by humanitarian crisis in Upper Nile, Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria in South Sudan
project_objective: The project will provide life-saving and integrated multi-sector assistance through multi-purpose cash assistance and livelihoods support (Cluster Objectives 1 and 2), aiming to increase access to food through cash and increased food production. It will also promote access to basic services through market support and referral pathways as well as reduce aid dependence through introduction of sustainable approaches to income generation and food production (Cluster Objective 3). Protection and inclusion principles are mainstreamed throughout all activities.

project_name: Improvement of effectiveness of Sexual and Gender Based Violence prevention and response  services and mechanisms in emergency  affected areas  of Pakistan
project_objective:
The 2017-18 Pakistan Demographic and Health Survey highlights 28% of women experience physical or sexual violence, 34% of ever-married women experience spousal violence, whether physical, sexual, or emotional. For provinces struggling with human insecurity such as Baluchistan, Newly Merged Districts and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the data are more alarming; respectively 49 %, 66% and 53 % suffer directly from partner violence of all kinds. Although demographic data are missing, programmatic work indicates that the situation is not better for the 1.4 million registered Afghan refugees holding a Government of Pakistan issued Proof of Registration card; of these a third living in 54 refugee villages (32%) and two-thirds (68%) of the registered Afghan refugees and asylum seekers that live in urban or peri-urban areas alongside their Pakistani host communities. An increase of gender-based violence (GBV) victims by 20% due to COVID-19 pandemic has been registered globally. A country already plagued by some of the highest rates of domestic violence and GBV in the world, Pakistan is struggling to respond to increased cases of such violence in the context of managing the COVID-19 outbreak for its 200 million citizens and about 1.4 million refugees mostly found in Baluchistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Approximately 8 million women face some form of GBV in one year in Pakistan. Pakistan is prone to natural disaster and rapid needs assessment conducted for Floods in Sindh province highlighted significant protection sector needs with more women and girls at risk compared to men (including S/GBV) with 56.9 percent in rural and 50 percent in urban areas. In order to respond to this situation, the following activities are proposed; 
1.	Facilities in targeted districts will be selected through proper assessment to be upgraded and strengthened to provide integrated GBV and SRH services to women and adolescent girls including CMR through trained staff. 
2.	The selected health facilities will provide access to women and adolescent girls to integrated Mental Health and Psychosocial Support services/ Psychological first aid in health facilities such as RHCs/BHUs including Women (Health) Friendly Spaces. The selected facilities and trained staff will provide case management through multi sectoral referral mechanisms to be established at the district level in coordination with relevant stakeholders.  
3.	Awareness raising and sensitization sessions in the catchment population will be conducted with women, girls, men and boys in catchment population on different forms of GBV (SRH) and available prevention and response related services. The outreach community sessions will include mobile services including community based psycho social support sessions, referral services to GBV and SRH services, access to people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups such as transgender, women and elderly headed households at the door step. These services will be aimed at development community based protection mechanisms.  
4.	Public media campaigns on GBV awareness and available services including electronic, social media and IEC material will be carried out to reach out to a large segment of population. Information on GBV will be further linked with COVID-19 and other humanitarian issues. 
5.	Coordination mechanisms and structures will be established at national, provincial and districts level to establish and strengthen multi sectoral GBV coordination mechanism in close coordination and collaboration with relevant government departments. 
6.	GBV focused helplines will be established or strengthened with services including remote psycho social support services, referral and remote case management services. 
7.	The frontline GBV workers and auxiliary staff will be protected against COVID-19 through trainings on IPC and provision of PPEs.

project_name: Lifesaving SRH-GBV integrated response with COVID-19 prevention and protection to ensure continuity of SRH services
project_objective:
4,7 million women are estimated as currently pregnant in Pakistan. 66% deliveries occur at health facilities, 22% of them are at government facilities.  3,5 million births expected by end of December, 2020. 
10%-20% decline in service coverage of essential maternal health care (ANC and post-natal care) may result in increasing of maternal deaths up to 2,056 -3,135 cases respectively.
There was not a tangible decline in institutional deliveries observed in the provinces where UNFPA mobile units are functional.  However, the number of ANC and Postnatal visits decreased by 30% due to lockdown and accessibility of the services. 
Distribution of COVID 19 positive cases among male and female population is unequal in different age groups. Most prevalent cases observed among male population in middle age group (65%). The impact of pandemic is frequently discussed by the government but more in economic terms and yet there is negligible mention of women or the gendered effects of the coronavirus. ‘The government’s approach towards women has always been paternalistic, and it is no different now; women are viewed as passive victims of a socio-economic and healthcare disaster’. 

Assessment conducted by OCHA in 2020 in collaboration with other UN organizations/agencies has unfold a gloomy picture of the health systems which also comes with some noticeable geographic disparities;  for instance; 
- Only 26.9% of the health facilities in Sajawal were having medicine available and on the other hand 88.9% of the health facilities in TM Khan were having medicine available in the health facility.
- Only 32.9% of deliveries take place in health facilities and 27.7% of post-natal care is provided by trained health staff. Recent estimates reveal that over 2.2 million people have limited or no access to essential health care services including women at reproductive age (15-49 years) 
- Access to health facilities by pregnant women is poor. For instance, only 52% in TM Khan and 28.2% in Sajawal have access to a health facility that assisting with birth 24/7, (Joint UN assessment 2020). 

Overall, 27% of the health facilities were reported as nonfunctional in the flood affected communities. Out of the functional health facilities only 27% providing 24/7 health care services. Overall, 52% of the respondents reported medicine available at the nearest health facilities, while 48% reported medicine were not available at the health facility.
The above situation is aggravated by:
- The ongoing outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan has increased burden on the already weak health system. Many of the existing resources (human, equipment, infrastructure, funds etc) have been diverted to support COVID-19 response. This and the additional financial resources allocated from routine health programmes have impacted negatively on the delivery of health services particularly those entrapped in protracted crises, such as, Afghan Refugees and Temporary displaced persons.   
- The non-pharmaceutical response to COVID-19 especially restriction to movements have adversely  affected  access to health services by the disaster affected population because repeated lockdowns with resultant supply chain breakdowns not only hampered services availability but also restricted population access to these services - Since, Health sector workforce including doctors from public and private sector, nurses, paramedics staff and pharmaceutical experts, lab technicians are at the forefront of Coronavirus. The workforce is facing disruptions and closure of the health care system for non-COVID related illnesses like routine immunization, maternal and childcare in many locations. Therefore, using national level PDHS 2017-18 Data, UN (2020) Socio-economic Impact assessment of COVID-19 on the Most Vulnerable Population has drawn two kinds of scenarios for the impact of COVID 19 on SRH services. According to the assessment report, if there is 10% reduction in the continuity of current services

project_name: Ensuring access to life-saving, essential GBV risk mitigation and response services for women and girls, men and boys  in remote and hard to reach areas in 26 drought affected districts
project_objective:
The protracted drought, compounded by the economic crisis and socio-economic Impact of COVID19, will continue to expose most vulnerable women and girls, men and boys, to exacerbated risks of GBV and harmful practices in 2021.

Between March and October 2020, the National GBV hotline has recorded an average increase in GBV calls of 60%, with 94% being females and 90% of cases being IPV. As a result of the multi-hazard crisis and its socio-economic impact, more than 1,700,000 women and girls and 560,000 men and boys will face increased risks of exposure to GBV in 2021.

GBV vulnerability assessments conducted between March and October 2020 reported that drought is contributing to modify daily routine patterns (e.g. water fetching and firewood collecting) which forces women and girls to walk long distance and spend long hours away from home, generating tension on the homestead, and leading to increased IPV. In the eastern provinces, where Apostolic faith sectarianism is predominant, girls are increasingly exposed to early marriage, as lobola (bride price) is often the only alternative household income source. SRHR consequences include      increased teenage pregnancy rates, and increased risks of ante and post-natal complications, which can be  fatal. 

Bordering towns also represent hotspots for GBV, as women and girls are exposed to trafficking and illegal migration, while female headed households become the most frequent target for SEA. IDPs in the eastern provinces that were affected by Cyclone Idai in 2019 continue to face increased GBV risks as they continue to be hosted at temporary camps with limited GBV risk mitigation measures. Women and girls with disabilities are also among the most vulnerable to GBV risks, and face further challenges of mobility to reach essential services.

The protracted drought, compounded by the economic hardship, hyperinflation and related basic goods price Increase, and the constrained access to cash, further contributes to reducing the capacity of survivors to sustain transport fees to reach services. The gradually decreasing availability of basic health services further contributes to the pre-existing critically low access to life-saving essential GBV services. According to the ZIMVAC rural livelihood assessment (October 2020), 68% of Individuals have no access to GBV services. When available, GBV multi-sectoral services remain fragmented, and mostly available at provincial and district level, often resulting out of reach for those living in most remote areas. De-prioritization of GBV services Is a documented result of unavailability of services, especially in remote areas. The proliferation of traditional healing systems deriving from the health system constraints, also results in an increased SEA risks.

In order to respond to the heightened GBV concerns, UNFPA with support from
international and local NGOs will scale up GBV mitigation and response interventions
targeting a total of 337,472 individuals (74% women and girls, 26% men and boys, 7% PWDs) in 26 districts.

The proposed interventions aim at:

1) Enhancing effectiveness of community-based GBV risk mitigation mechanisms;
2) Strengthening the availability and accessibility of life saving multi-sectoral survivor-centered
GBV services for GBV survivors in the most hard to reach areas
3) Improving the capacity of GBV specialized and non-specialized humanitarian actors to
integrate GBV and PSEA interventions across programs, to avoid unintended GBV
consequences and ensure DO-NO Harm.

project_name: Prevention and Response to GBV among most vulnerable men and women residing along the contact line in Eastern Ukraine
project_objective: The project will target vulnerable and affected population in conflict-affected eastern Ukraine, Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, ECA (GCA). With a focus on humanitarian and development issues in GCA it aims to design and implement durable solutions as part of humanitarian-development nexus. UNFPA has already built core elements of a response mechanism as part of its humanitarian interventions and is keen to continue strengthening this mechanism. It will place a greater emphasis on assistance, strengthening community resilience, and improving access of humanitarian actors to the affected population. Special attention will be given to supporting the most vulnerable population: people with disabilities, people living in rural areas, people living in isolated settlements (in particular 0-5 km) with limited access to government service providers, social services, and single women-headed households along the contact line. Differentiated approaches to programming will be applied in 2021 considering the prevailing humanitarian situation, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The primary focus for humanitarian response will remain to be on the communities 0-5 km and 5-20 km the contact line (Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts). Critical security/safety needs of the most vulnerable IDPs and comers from ECA communities will be prioritized in 20+ area, where durable solutions for GBV response are implemented in a safe and survivors-oriented manner. Due to restricted humanitarian access to NGCA for protection activities, the project will seek alternative partnership opportunities with local actors; will reach out to those in need through remote and silent solutions; will use existing access points such as healthcare facilities for delivering aid. Project implementation areas will include: Assistance – developing a network of accessible, affordable and accountable safe spaces for DV / GBV survivors living in areas close to the contact line (also along the contact line) These protection solutions according to needs assessment are the most relevant for 5-20 km and 20+ km zones due to security issues and the presence of capable service providers. Protection – capacity building and sensitization of service providers, community activists along the contact line and isolated settlements; awareness-raising within the general population, training and developing distant learning solutions for actors responsible for GBV response; strengthening accountability to affected population (AAP) mechanism. Resilience – supporting the development of community-based early warning system (for 0-5 km, 5-20 km zones as a priority), involving humanitarian actors, community activists; SGBV coordination to strengthen the response and prevention systems, and to gradually transfer to national ownership over provision of humanitarian assistance Access – supporting targeted PSS MTs interventions, awareness-raising/sensitizing sessions and events in selected settlements (with emphasis on isolated settlements, rural areas, and those in 0-5 km zone). UNFPA supported models of service delivery will eventually build trust in those services among survivors and trigger their willingness to report their cases (as a part of AAP) and seek help. Engagement of non-state actors (local NGO’s, FBO’s, CBO’s) to act as service providers at the local community level will strengthen the prevention pillar of the overall GBV response strategy. A monitoring and evaluation plan, defined through previous interventions to manage the process of assessing and reporting progress against project targets, is used to ensure the quality of project results. A feedback mechanism from project beneficiaries will be operating, including through regular GBV WGs and GBV SC meetings, National Toll-Free Hotline. In order to achieve maximum complementarity, the project will seek to coordinate, and to the extent possible work jointly, with other complementary projects and initiatives in the area of gender equality and GBV.

project_name: Addressing critical gaps in sexual reproductive health service delivery for most vulnerable women and adolescent girls affected by the armed conflict in Eastern Ukraine, including COVID-19
project_objective:
The needs for sexual and reproductive health (SRH) remains high considering the protracted crises and the lock down due to COVID-19 outbreak, associated with redirection of resources (human, medical and logistics) from the provision of SRH services The project aims to fill critical gaps in sexual reproductive health services delivery for conflict affected population and enhance provision of essential quality SRH services according to the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for RH standards. The project complement previous and ongoing UNFPA projects, CERF-2019, will be implemented in cooperation with local health administrations and local government and will continue implementing key activities targeted on promotion of emergency preparedness and response, and provision of outreach SRH service to the vulnerable population in condition of COVID-19 pandemic:
1.To provide technical assistance and advocacy to local health authorities and local governments in emergency preparedness and provision of  SRH service according to The Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) tool. 
2.To provide technical guidance on reinforcing infection control measures within maternity hospital, including triage flow and segregation of neonatal and maternal health units.
3.Essential supply of drugs, commodities and supplies including PPE to increase capacity of local health facilities on provision of maternal and new-born life-saving service. Provision of Female Health Workers Sanitary kits for woman health workers working in COVID-19 frontline facilities
4. Provision of outreach minimum essential SRH, GBV and internal medicine services in rayons and cities along the contact line Donetsk and Lugansk oblast (GCA) by three mobile SRH teams in cooperation with governmental COVID-19 mobile teams.
5.Increase capacity of health providers and managers in planning and provision of emergency SRH service including STI, GBV/SGBV and addressing SRH needs of woman with disabilities, improvement of IPC control.
6.Inform the population (community level) and pregnant women on sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, sexual and gender based violence prevention, and referral pathways and COVID-19 risks, symptoms and transmission and prevent discrimination of people that present with COVID-19 like symptoms.
Since the onset of the crisis, UNFPA Ukraine is leading the humanitarian response to reproductive health needs of most vulnerable women and adolescent girls, providing life saving supplies and ensuring accessibility of medical services to those in need, in particular in remote areas and near the contact line.
7. Provision of qualified OBGYN surgeon to perform OBGYN surgeries 210 OBGYN surgeries on severe cases uterine prolapse and fibromioma to 6 rayon hospitals and Avdyivka city hospital (GCA)

project_name: SRHR and GBV Response for Refugees & Asylum Seekers in Sudan
project_objective: Sudan has more than 1 million refugees with the recent experiences of floods and refugee influx from Ethiopia due to the conflicts in Tigrey Region. In any emergency and humanitarian situation, the risks of maternal death and increased risk of gender based violence are already well documented by GBV expert (IASC GBV in Emergencies). The project will contribute in three strategic goals, Life-saving (78%), protection (20%) and Living conditions (2%), of the country Refugee Response Plan in Sudan. The specific objective of this project is to address the critical life-saving and essential reproductive health and Gender Based Violence (GBV) services to prevent maternal death, GBV, and enabling conducive environment for women and girls accessing information and services. The project targets refugees, asylum seekers and host communities in the prioritized localities, identified by RCF for 2021 Humanitarian Response for refugees in 11 States (37 localities). The key interventions are integrated SRHR -GBV service delivery (Health, especially SRHR, Clinical Management of Rape, MHPSS and GBV Case Management and referrals), strengthening women center activities, community based protection networks, women's groups, SRHR supplies and commodities, Dignity Kits, Capacity building of Key health psycho social service providers, mobile/temporary clinics, Community Awareness and campaigns, strengthening referral mechanism with government service delivery points for GBV-SRHR. The project budget has dedicated 60% for SRHR, including the CMR; and 40% for GBV prevention and response; from which 20% of the services will be directed to the vulnerable host communities, adjacent to the refugee sites to mitigate conflicts over competing resources. The implementation of the activities will be conducted through (I)NGOs and Government partners with the consistent technical support from UNFPA, including maintaining the field presence.

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving SRHR services for most vulnerable and in-need population, Sudan, 2021
project_objective:
The provision of Sexual and Reproductive Health services is essential in humanitarian setting, it is an effective approach for preventing deaths, diseases, and disabilities associated and resulted from unintended pregnancy, obstetric complications, sexual and other forms of gender-based violence, HIV infection, and a range of reproductive disorders. UNFPA jointly with partners, will ensure the provision of comprehensive SRH services in humanitarian settings, with utmost consideration to the COVID19 prevention and response measures. 
The intervention primarily targets women, girls in reproductive age, youth and adolescents, and men and boys.  Sudan HNO 2021 indicates total people in need at 8.1 million, health sector target is 5.7 million. UNFPA will target 1.6 million with more than 80% are women and girls in reproductive age. The geographical coverage follows the HNO identified locations with severity ranking three and above. 

All SRHR intervention will be implemented simultaneously through coordinated actions with all relevant partners. The planned interventions prioritize and aim reducing SRH mortalities and morbidities through: timely provision of Emergency Obstetric care and save delivery services, timely referral to lifesaving services, support the availability of Family Planning services, improving Clinical management of rape for survivors of SGBV, availing HIV and STIs prevention and response, improving Antenatal and postnatal care, Post abortion care, and other SRH services.  These will be achieved through strengthening the capacity of SRH care providers with emphases of midwifery services, timely availability of lifesaving SRHR supplies, timely deployment of temporary clinics and mobile clinics, supporting the referral system, and demand creation through awareness raising and educational activities. Maternal Morbidities such as Obstetric fistula will be given especial attention by UNFPA. 

The implementation of activities will be conducted through NGOs and Government partners with the strong technical support from UNFPA, including maintaining the field presence.

project_name: Access to Humanitarian life-saving child protection and GBV response services in North Darfur, North / South Kordofan and White Nile states
project_objective: The project objective is to protect people from violence, neglect, and exploitation by providing access to life-saving child protection and GBV response services to targeted communities in White Nile, North Kordofan, and North Darfur. In order to accomplish this, Plan will provide high quality protection services and contribute to community stabilization and resilience. Protection services and capacity building activities will include: CP and GBV case management, distribution of dignity kits to vulnerable girls, multi-purpose cash transfer to vulnerable households and hosting UASC, and referrals mechanisms including to Family and Child Protection Units, training of social workers and partner staff on GBV, CP, and referral pathways, and psychosocial support to conflict affected children and youth. The provision of protection services must be paired with activities to increase knowledge of and access to those services. Therefore, Plan will also establish/strengthen and equip Community Based Child Protection Networks (CBCPNs), conduct community awareness session of CP, FGM, SEA and child marriage risks, and conduct sensitization on GBV prevention and response. Plan will foster communal stability and resilience by providing life skills training, parenting sessions, conducting community awareness sessions on peacebuilding and conflict transformation, and training duty bearers and community leaders on peacebuilding.  Additionally, Plan will establish child-friendly community feedback and response mechanisms so that all project beneficiaries are able to provide feedback and file complaints.

project_name: Health and Nutrition Assistance to the Affected Populations in Khartoum, South/West Kordofan and East Darfur States
project_objective:
This project aims to continue the delivery of CMAM services for SAM and MAM cases within the existing health system in Khartoum (Umbada, and Jabal Awlia localities), South Kordofan (Abujubiha, Liri, Talodi and Rashad localities) /West Kordofan (Lagawa), East Darfur (Assalaya, B.Elarab, Eldeein and Abu-Karinka localities), through the provision of full package of treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among (boys & girls) U5 and PLW. The project targets acutely malnourished children (SAM with or without complication and MAM) either through treatment or rehabilitating services. Improve  the  capacity  of MOH staff to provide  quality services  and  community volunteers ,CBOs  to mitigate  the  risk towards  food insecurity  and  reduction of  malnutrition, the  project  enhancing  the  need  analysis  of  the  nutrition situation  through  conducting rapid nutrition surveys involving  the  target communities  in  identifying the  needs , planning  and  in implementation as  well as  monitoring  of  project  on regular  basis. Moderate Acute malnutrition and the underlying causes of malnutrition will be managed through participatory nutrition education activities using the Nutrition Impact & Positive Practice approach (NIPP) through targeting predominantly mothers and fathers of moderately malnourished children. The NIPP circles emphasize behavior change, communication & counseling (for improved awareness), livelihood (for improved food/nutrition security) and cooking demonstration using locally available foods (for improved feeding and care practices). Community screening of cases will equally target boys and girls & depending on their nutritional status they will be referred to the OTP or NIPP circles based on the admission criteria.
Mother to mother groups where a group of mothers with malnourished children, grandparents group) to help empowering Mothers to solve issues related to the nutrition with focus on IYCF practices and knowledge and coordination with relevant sector (for multi-pectoral nutrition activities). Mainstreaming child protection through reflecting in the assessment, design, monitoring and evaluation of the project. Girls and boys of all ages and their caregivers, especially pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, have access to awareness about women and child rights for the prevention of malnutrition Gender, COVID19, HIV/AIDS and the environment are mainstreamed throughout the project activities.

project_name: Renforcer les interventions de prévention, d’atténuation des risques et de réponse à la violence basée sur le genre et particulièrement  dans un contexte de COVID- 19 dans les six Régions humanitaires du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer les services qui sauvent les vies des survivantes, des femmes et des filles à risques de VBG par l’adaptation  et le renforcement de la disponibilité et de la qualité des services, de prévention, de mitigation des risques. Les survivantes de violence basée sur le genre auront accès à des soins de santé adaptés, y compris des services de santé pour les survivantes de violences sexuelles et conjugales et d’autres formes de VBG. Des services d’orientation pour prévenir et/ou réduire les effets de la violence seront fournis par les prestataires de santé étant donné qu’ils sont souvent les premiers et parfois le seul point de contact avec les survivantes. Cela se fera à travers une bonne coordination et un soutien à la continuité de l’offre des services de santé de prise en charge des violences sexuelles et les autres formes de VBG. A cet effet, en collaboration avec les districts sanitaires des Régions ciblés par le projet, un paquet d’activité sera déroulé afin de fournir une prise en charge de qualité aux survivantes de VBG. Le soutien psychosocial étant une étape primordiale dans la prise en charge des cas de VBG, ce service sera intégré à l’offre de service médical par la mise à disposition des centres de santé des travailleurs sociaux, préalablement formés sur le soutien psychosocial y compris la gestion des cas de VBG. Ces travailleurs sociaux bénéficieront de matériel permettant la mise en œuvre de la gestion des cas de VBG à distance (téléphone, smartphone, crédit de communication…). Ainsi les survivantes auront accès à des services de gestion de cas appropriés et de qualité. L’accompagnement des survivantes par les travailleurs sociaux sera essentiellement basé sur la base de l’approche axée sur les survivantes et ces principes directeurs. 
Le projet préconise et soutient l’intégration de l’atténuation des risques de violence basée sur le genre. Le numéro vert de dénonciation des cas de VBG et d’orientation des survivantes vers les services de prise en charge sera renforcé. Les agents de la ligne verte seront formés sur la prise en charge des cas d’abus et d’exploitation sexuels. Des stratégies communautaires seront développées pour surveiller en toute sécurité et combattre les risques liés à la VBG et inscrire une tolérance zéro de l’exploitation et de l’abus sexuels et  leur dénonciation dans les messages communautaires de sensibilisation. Un plaidoyer encourageant l’élaboration, l’adoption et l’application de codes de conduite interdisant toutes les formes d’exploitation et d’abus sexuels sera mené auprès des partenaires de mise en œuvre mais aussi auprès des différents secteurs humanitaires. 
Pour permettre aux femmes et aux filles de préserver leur dignité, des lampes et kits de dignité seront distribués dans les zones d’intervention du projet.
Des espaces sûrs à l’usage des femmes et des filles seront installés dans les sites d’accueil temporaire et au sein de la population hôte, afin que les survivantes de VBG et les femmes et les filles à risques puissent accéder en toute sécurité à l’information et à l’orientation vers les services de prise en charge. Les groupements de femmes seront formés sur les VBG y compris la protection contre l’exploitation et l’abus sexuels et la Violence Infligée par le Partenaire Intime (VPI). Ces groupements féminins auront pour tâche de sensibiliser la communauté sur les conséquences de la VBG, le mécanisme de référencement et les services disponibles. 
Les hommes et les garçons seront impliqués dans les activités de prévention à la VBG par la mise en œuvre des activités de promotion de la masculine positive permettant de susciter un changement de comportement et le renforcement des mécanismes endogènes de protection en mettant au premier plan les leaders coutumiers et religieux. La coordination du sous-secteur VBG sera renforcée au niveau national et régional pour s’assurer que la réponse aux VBG est faite conformément aux normes requises.

project_objective: This Action aims to implement life-saving activities for vulnerable women and girls at risk in the context of armed conflict and COVID-19 in Cameroon. The interventions under this Action aim to reach 180,000 internally displaced persons and members of host communities with integrated protection services (medical, psycho-social, legal and protection). Furthermore, the Action will ensure the implementation of infection prevention and control measures (IPC) in 18 health facilities (7 in the NW, 5 in the SW, 3 in the Littoral and 3 in the West) in order to reduce the risk of transmission and spread of COVID-19 in hospitals and in local communities. project_name: Strengthening mechanisms that prevent violence against women, men, girls and boys and provide protection services to survivors of gender-based violence, while ensuring specialised GBV services are accessible and vulnerability to GBV is reduced
project_objective:
In 2020, dramatic changes in the operational context, including a shift in the conflict and the COVID-19 pandemic further exacerbated the humanitarian crisis in Libya. COVID-19 forced the country to adopt stringent measures, including full lockdowns, roadblocks, partial or full closure of facilities (including schools and health facilities), and severe limitations in provision of services and availability of basic goods. The pandemic affected people’s mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, particularly women, children, migrants and refugees. COVID-19 exposed not only fears but also heightened distress and feelings of hopelessness and helplessness. Conflict-related displacement continued throughout 2020. The escalation of the conflict further exacerbated the threat from Explosive Hazards (EH). Parties to the conflict have increasingly relied on the use of heavy and explosive weaponry in densely populated settings. During the month of June alone, nearly 28,000 people were displaced following an intensification of the conflict, bringing the total number of IDPs in Libya to 392,241.  600,392 migrants   and 46,247  refugees are currently in Libya. Violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law against migrants and refugees remain a grave concern. Migrants and refugees continue to be subjected to torture, sexual violence, abduction for ransom, trafficking in persons, forced labor and unlawful killings throughout Libya.
The fragile economic situation, further hampered by the pandemic, has reduced individual and family income, and increased risks linked to livelihoods and security of tenure. The majority of tenants do not have written lease agreements, leaving them exposed to predatory behaviors by landlords, including arbitrary increases in rent and threats of, or actual evictions.
Women and girls have been disproportionally impacted by the economic crisis and pandemic. Increased food insecurity may place women, who have the primary responsibility to prepare food for the family, at heightened risk of intimate partner violence due to tensions in the household and being in confinement with their perpetrator. Female-headed households are at heightened risk of not being able to access services and meet basic needs. Migrant and refugee women, many of which have no recognized status and face language barriers and discrimination, have an increased risk of sexual exploitation and abuse. Movement restrictions, curfews, closures of services and limitations in social contacts led to a stark increase of GBV risks and risk of not receiving timely care. Reduced access to sexual and reproductive health information and services lead to increased risky behavior, especially among youth. Finally, the limited services available has reduced safe entry points for survivors to receive timely and quality care.
The breakdown of the electricity, water, oil, and cellular network systems affect the provision of and the accessibility to life saving services. This is particularly concerning for survivors of intimate partner violence due to the imminent danger of living with their perpetrators. The economic impact of the closures of businesses due to the conflict and the pandemic has resulted in a loss of livelihoods, especially for women often working in the informal sector. Female headed households are at high risk of not being able to cover their rent and thus face evictions and homelessness which is exacerbated for IDPs, migrants, and refugees. The stigma exacerbated by gender and ethnic discrimination leaves women and girls from migrant and refugee communities with limited financial options and renders them vulnerable to sexual exploitation and abuse, including requests for sexual favors by landlords, taxi drivers, and public service providers. The presence of humanitarian actors, even on a small scale, was in itself providing some form of protection by presence in the hard-to-reach areas and detention centers.

L'intervention intégrée proposée par ce projet répond aux conséquences de la crise centrafricaine dans les régions de l'Adamaoua et de l'Est aux besoins urgents des communautés en termes de protection et de sécurité alimentaire et moyens de subsistance. En effet, la protection des populations affectées par la crise centrafricaine reste un défi majeur, notamment concernant le mariage précoce des jeunes filles, les VBG, la déscolarisation ou non-scolarisation des enfants, le manque de documentation civile, etc. De plus l'assistance alimentaire fournie par l'aide internationale a drastiquement diminué alors que les besoins restent conséquents.

En vue d'assister les populations affectées par la crise, ainsi que de maintenir la cohabitation pacifique et la cohésion sociale avec les communautés hôtes, bien que la pression sur les ressources et sur les services augmente, cette intervention permettra d'appuyer la réduction des stratégies de survie négatives et de favoriser l'accès aux moyens de subsistance basé sur les vulnérabilités des individus et des ménages à travers l'intégration avec l'action déjà en cours de renforcement des mécanismes de protection à base communautaire et d'amélioration de l'environnement protecteur.

project_name: Food Assistance for Vulnerable Lebanese Households in Beirut and South Lebanon
project_objective:
In response to growing humanitarian needs in Lebanon caused by the socio-economic impacts of the economic crisis, the proposed intervention will provide life-saving assistance to 315 vulnerable Lebanese households living in Palestinian gatherings in Beirut (Said Ghawash, Daouk and Sabra) and South Lebanon (Kfarbadda, Jal el Bahar and Wasta). MCC together with its national implementing partner Popular Aid for Relief and Development (PARD) will distribute monthly food assistance in the form of a food voucher for a period of six months from September 2021 through February 2022. A higher proportion of beneficiary households will be from the targeted Beirut gatherings (64%) where there is higher reported incidence of food insecurity.

Each household will receive a food voucher of 220,000 LBP per household member, in line with the current WFP transfer value and the estimated food security sector fresh food basket cost, to be redeemed at shops contracted by the project in the project areas.  The food assistance will be accompanied by nutrition and hygiene awareness sessions and distribution of multi-sectoral messaging on nutrition and hygiene, as well as mental health and reproductive health.

project_name: Provision of protection and assistance to refugees and asylum seekers in Zimbabwe
project_objective:
The project is to support Government efforts in providing protection and assistance to refugees and asylum seekers in Zimbabwe while also ensuring containment and prevention of the spread of COVID-19. This will be guided by multi-cluster HRP strategic objectives. The project focuses on preserving unhindered access to territory to refugees and asylum seekers while ensuring fair and efficient asylum procedures. The Response activities will promote, the full enjoyment of rights for refugees and asylum seekers, ensuring provision of support to the Government for protection of refugees and asylum seekers in Zimbabwe. Multisectoral assistance and essential services will be provided to refugees and asylum seekers with particular attention to the most vulnerable individuals, and resilience and self-reliance will be strengthened among refugees and host communities. This will ensure that refugees and asylum seekers are self-reliant and improve in terms of their dietary ad nutritional requirements.

 With the negative impact of COVID and the overcrowding prevalent in the refugee camp, health needs of refugees will be prioritised. This will ensure that refugees have access to basic health care services. As preventative measures , WASH in the Tongogara refugee camp will be strengthened through provision of adequate water per persons per day, construction of latrines to reduce the impact of open defecation and promote hygienic practices for refugees and asylum seekers. Education remains a key protection measure for refugees ensuring that refugee children of school going age have access to quality education. Despite the impact of COVID which have left many leaners out of school, there is need to strengthen innovative e-learning opportunities for school going children. 

The capacities of national institutions will also be strengthened including supporting the government in creating conducive conditions for sustainable solutions in areas of refugee returns, in collaboration with humanitarian and development actors, as one of the key areas. 

The 2021 response will target the overall refugee population, which   based on the population projection,  is estimated to some 15,405 refugees and asylum seekers. In addition to the provision of life-saving humanitarian assistance, the response will cover the areas of access to territory, reception, registration, refugee status determination and documentation; access to justice, and access to quality education for refugee children.

project_objective:
This project aims to provide all the populations in need (Vulnerable host communities, IDPs and returnees)  in the target high risk states and localities, with basic humanitarian services, through a comprehensive and holistic approach that integrates the sectors of Health, Nutrition, WASH, FSL and Education, to ensure all essential needs are covered and accessible.
The project will target the 12 states and 26 localities of: Abyei PCA, Blue Nile (Altadamon, Baw localities), East Darfur (Assalaya, Alfirdous and Yassin localities), Gedarif (Alfashaga and Alfao), Kassala (Reifi Hamashkoreb and North Detla), Red Sea (Haya and Sinkat), South Darfur (Dimso, Umdafoug, Elsalam and Alradoum), South Kordofan (Alburam, Al Leri and Umdurein), West Kordofan (Alnuhood and Lagawa), River Nile (Shendi), Northern State (Algolid) and White Nile state (Aljabalen and Alsalam).
The Health interventions include the provision of primary health care (PHC), reproductive health (RH) and strengthening of expanded program of immunization (EPI) through support health facilities in the target locations with needed medical supplies and equipment. The interventions will also focus on COVID19 response through provision of needed support to the health facilities (for case management) and the communities (for risk communication and infection prevention and control IPC). The nutrition interventions include provision of CMAM services for all the target populations and treatment of SAM cases, with or without complications for children under 5 and MAM cases for CU5 and PLWs. The project further intends to improve the public health of these targeted communities by providing WASH services for these target communities through promotion of hygiene, and construction/rehabilitation of communal and institutional latrines (in target HFs, OTPs, SCs and schools). In addition to improving the access of the target population to safe drinking water to minimize the risk of contracting infections. The Food Security and Livelihoods interventions will aim to lower the impact of the economic crisis and the COVID19 pandemic on the livelihoods, and consequently the food security, of the most vulnerable target beneficiaries, through provision of suitable vocational trainings, vouchers and cash and general food distributions. The education component in this project intends to contribute to the return to schools after a long period of schools shutting down (the civil unrest in 2018 followed shortly by the COVID19 lockdown) through rehabilitating/constructing and furnishing of schools and classes and restoring them to original status prior to the lockdown. The education interventions also include provision of all needed kits, supplies and uniforms to children in the target primary schools, and provide the teachers at the target schools with needed support. 
Through these integrated interventions the vulnerable populations (vulnerable host communities, IDPs and returnees) will be targeted with the services and improve their accessibility to the services. All while ensuring that gender, protection and disability mainstreaming is an integral part of implementation, and working on strengthening the resilience and integrating the IDPs and returnees within the target communities. This project will also take into account the environmental factors and risks that may be influenced by the proposed activities and devise the appropriate mitigation methods to minimize the effects on the environment.
