project_name: Provision of psychosocial support and social cohesion assistance to conflict affected communities in eastern Ukraine
project_objective:
The project refers to the following strategic and cluster objectives:
SO1. Provide emergency and time-critical assistance and ensure access to basic essential services, to XX million people affected by the conflict, exacerbated by COVID-19.
PCO1. Ensure conflict-affected people, including IDPs, benefit from full and non-discriminatory access to quality essential services and enjoyment of their rights, with particular attention to people with specific needs.
and
SO3. Ensure an implementation of humanitarian exit strategy in GCA from 2021-2023. 
PCO3. Improve resilience of conflict-affected people and system of service provision.
PIN will work with partners to provide free psychosocial support to the most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men in the most underserved areas. Such support will focus on the most vulnerable based on analysis of individual compounded (through age, gender and diversity-sensitive assessments engaging women, girls, boys, men, people with disability…) with contextual vulnerabilities (most underserved areas with unmet needs). PIN will in particular, and with partners, review needs which might traditionally be overlooked and need to be addressed still with emergency – including in particular from gender and age lenses (e.g. engaging men and boys and addressing toxic masculinities). Access to services will be ensured through the activation of mobile teams of psychologists and social workers to the conflict zone, PSS hotline, group activities with special outreach and individual support.
PIN will also work to build capacity of PSS practitioners and prepare sustainability of access to essential PSS services in underserved through community-based approaches and enhanced coordination and referral systems. PIN will coordinate with communities, local social and psychological services and partners to prioritise gaps in service provision in the most underserved (isolated) areas. PIN tested a sound cooperation on PSS provision with a local NGO partners, a localised approach that PIN aims to expand and compliment with other community-based solutions. To keep offering support to the affected population and work towards exit strategy solutions, PIN together with selected NGO partners and community structures will provide PSS along LoC. PIN will also support the realisation by community interest groups of inclusive initiatives for community’s social cohesion and resilience. 
Throughout its action, PIN will pay special attention to Accountability to the affected population. PIN will do so by actively engaging women, girls, boys and men, individuals in their diversity without discrimination (with due regard to underlying inequalities) in the identification and prioritization of their needs through extensive consultations and facilitation of community actions. PIN will also strengthen its established Community Feedback and Response Mechanism, including with strengthened response to complaints as well as referrals, as well as internal learning cycles to ensure that affected populations’ feedback is integrated into project proposals, strategies, monitoring and evaluations, trainings and performance tracking management, partnership agreements etc. PIN will continue to provide accessible and timely information to beneficiaries on organizational procedures, structures and processes that affect them to ensure that they can make informed decisions and choices, and facilitate a dialogue between an organisation and its beneficiaries over information provision.

project_name: Strengthening Core Capacity of Points of Entry for Emergencies
project_objective:
Assessment by WHO and IOM shows “limited capacity” of designated PoE having access to appropriate medical services including diagnostic facilities for the prompt assessment and care of ill travelers and with adequate staff, equipment and premises. The availability of portable water and solid and liquid waste management are absent. In few places like Ras Al Jadir and Wazan land cossing point, there was no vehicle for transportation of ill travelers. Similarly, it was observed that “no” national public health emergency contingency plan exists for responding to public health emergencies occurring at points of entry. 

Libya shares a border with six countries and has a total of  24 PoE inclduding eight (8) airports, nine (9) seaports and eight (8) ground crossings points. 

The COVID-19 outbreak, which has had  unprecedented effects on global mobility patterns, has tested health screening practices and capacities at PoEs. Border staff are playing an increasingly critical role in the implementation of key COVID-19 and general public health measures, such as disease surveillance, screening and testing. 
IOM, as a co-lead of the Migration Health-Sub working group and as a lead on PoE pillar of the COVID-19 strategic response, conducts regular PoEs’ assessments and plays a leading role in supporting PoEs to respond to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. As part of its support to PoEs across Libya, IOM has already installed high resolution thermal cameras at five (5) Po Es (Ras Aljadir, Amsad and Wazen land crossing point; Misrata and Benina airports) as well as prefabs for temporary/transient isolation at  two (2) PoEs (Ras Aljadir and Wazen and in progress at Mitiga, Benina and Amsad). Additionally, 99 PoE health staff from the above POEs have been trained so far.

This project aims to continue strengthening the health system’s capacity at Libyan PoEs through the provision of screening equipment (thermal cameras), Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and capacity building of PoE staff on Infection Prevention and Control (IPC). IOM will target 8 PoEs in total, 4 airports and 4 ground/land crossing points. This project will also support the establishment of isolation spaces at PoEs including provision of human resources, establishing handwashing facilities and disposal of waste mechanism. Finally, the project will ensure the provision of lifesaving emergency services at 1 high- and 2 medium- active disembarkation points.

project_name: Lifesaving health interventions for vulnerable & underserved populations (Aweil East, Mayendit, Panyijar, Koch, Rumbek East Counties.)
project_objective:
Prolonged conflict, natural disasters and limited government investment in health services have resulted in weakened health systems in South Sudan. Poor health facility infrastructure, inadequate human resources for health, and inadequate health financing has resulted in limited access to equitable and quality health services across the Country. This intervention will target underserved and vulnerable populations in Aweil East County (Northern Bahr El Ghazal State), Rumbek East (Lakes State) and Panyijar, Koch, and Mayendit Counties (Unity State).
Through this proposed intervention, the IRC will support 2 static primary health care centers (PHCC), 3 integrated Rapid Response Mobile (RRM) outreach teams and 40 Boma Health Workers (BHWs) in Aweil East County. In Lakes State, the intervention will constitute 2 integrated RRM teams and 40 BHWs in Rumbek East County to serve hard to reach populations. In Unity State the intervention will provide essential integrated lifesaving health interventions as follows; support 1 PHCC, 1 integrated RRM outreach Clinic and support 40 BHWs in underserved areas of Koch County, 2 integrated RRM Outreach teams and 40 BHWs in Mayendit County, and 1 PHCC, 4 RRM outreach teams and 40 BHWs in Panyijar County.

The intervention will work closely with the County Health department structure as the custodian of health and nutrition services at the County level to foster coordination and collaboration with key actors in health and nutrition in the target Counties. This will also support County led services mapping to ensure complementarity of interventions proposed by this project with other ongoing health and nutrition services delivery partners. County led micro-planning, disease surveillance and epidemic preparedness and response activities including for the COVID-19 pandemic will be integrated into this intervention to ensure rapid response to epidemic prone diseases at the County level and mitigate associated mortality and morbidity.

The RRM teams will work through a flexible approach to reach underserved and displaced populations residing outside a 5km radius of the nearest health facility. BHWs will provide community level treatments for common causes of childhood morbidity and mortality i.e. malaria, pneumonia and diarrhea while also supporting health promotion, screening for immunization defaulters and acute malnutrition while providing referral linkages to the nearest health facilities. The IRC will recruit qualified health personnel to support quality health services delivery at the supported static PHCCs, PHCUs, the RRM mobile clinics, and they will receive in service training on key areas including use of the South Sudan Treatment guidelines, Rationale prescription of drugs, Integrated management of childhood and neonatal illnesses (IMNCI) and Clinical management of Rape (CMR). The intervention will take into account COVID-19 risk mitigation measures through provision of Personal Protective equipment (PPEs), stringent Infection prevention and control (IPC) measures including bi-weekly support supervision using the WHO’s IPC-At Facility checklists and strengthen risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) activities across all service points. BHWs will be trained in no-touch techniques and provided with job aids to support community based surveillance. This will be linked at the facility level to the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR), Early Warning, Alert and Response System (EWARS) to strengthen County level disease surveillance. Strengthened pharmaceutical supplies management will be the backbone of the intervention through adequate supplies forecasting and preposition in hard to reach areas to minimize the risks of tracer medicine stock outs, while ensuring continued service delivery throughout seasonal variations.

The intervention will mainstream COVID-19 risk reduction measures across all service delivery channels to ensure reduction in transmission.

project_name: Improved access to and utilization of integrated emergency lifesaving primary health services in Upper Nile State
project_objective:
This intervention is aimed at improving access to and utilization of health services through five fixed primary health care facilities including Rirnyang PHCU in Ulang County, Kiechkuon PHCC, Makak PHCU, and Wandeng PHCU in Nasir and Jekow PHCU in Maiwut. To scale-up health care services in Nasir, Longechuk, Maiwut, and Ulang Counties. RI will also establish eight MMUs and ICCMs to serve the hard-to-reach population with lifesaving health care services. In total the project will target 99,094 vulnerable individuals.
RI will recruit and deploy qualified health workers including clinical officers, nurses, midwives, community health workers, and vaccinators to all supported fixed facilities and mobile medical units. Alongside this, Boma Health Workers will be selected within the targeted communities to implement ICCM activities. 
The intervention will further focus on continuous screening and treatment of communicable and non-communicable diseases through patient consultations. Additional services provided will include antenatal care, skilled deliveries, postnatal care, and clinical management of rape (SGBV services) in the health facilities and mobile medical units. The intervention will also integrate and strengthen mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and services for people with disabilities.  
The project will continue streamlining and strengthening the referral pathways for mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), sexual and gender-based violence survivors and, maternal and child health emergencies. RI’s health team through this response will conduct routine and outreach immunization services to children under 59months of age. 
This project will engage all communities in the targeted counties throughout the implementation stages to ensure the sustainability of the program. Beneficiary exit satisfaction interviews will be conducted at fixed facilities and MMUs and community feedback mechanism meetings will be conducted to facilitate feedback from the communities. This project builds on RI's existing static and mobile health interventions, are locations and static facilities not services by other actors - serving the most vulnerable, and hard to reach IDP, host and returnee community in Upper Nile State.

project_name: Upscaling and strengthening community based structures to provide life-saving comprehensive child protection services to UASC and other at-risk children/families in Jonglei, Warrap and  Northern Bahr El Ghazal
project_objective:
The project will upscale provision of comprehensive child protection services including case management, family tracing and reunification, reintegration support for CAAFAGs, psychosocial support for children and their families and community-based child protection to target communities where Save the Children has presence and that need to be strengthened, or require expansion into new geographical locations that lack child protection services and yet have been flagged as locations with acute emergencies.
Children, youth and families in the selected locations have experienced trauma, gender-based violence, forced displacement resulting from conflict or floods, risks of recruitment and abduction of boys, child forced early marriage, among others.
Through this one-year project, Save the Children will identify children with critical protection needs to receive appropriate and targeted support and provide access to girls and boys to child protection services, coordinated assistance, referrals and community-based interventions to ensure that girls and boys affected by complex and multi-faceted humanitarian crisis (including armed conflict, famine, flooding and the impact of COVID-19) in South Sudan, are protected from all forms of violence, abuse and neglect. In all new locations the community based child protection networks(CBCPNs) will be formed and where they are existent, they will be strengthened; by training on their roles and responsibilities 
The project will work in collaboration with the community based child protection committees that are existing and those that will be set up in the new areas where they are non-existent, to ensure that they participate in identification and referral of unaccompanied and separated children to initiate tracing. The local partners and administration will also be oriented on the FTR process to make it participatory. The case management system will take the lead in FTR process during case plan implementation and also ensure that appropriate alternative care options are availed to the children in process. The alternative care system will also be a major focus of the CBCPN in collaboration with the local administration and participation of the larger community; foster care givers will be identified and oriented, closely monitored and supported by the community mobilisers and case workers.
During the community awareness campaigns or dialogue events with the CPCPN, will ensure that the messages that are shared and discussed are in line with the prevalent child protection issues and incidents in the community. They will be factored into the routines of the community such as market days or any gathering that brings community together while observing the COVID-19 protocol. This will focus on both prevention of the incidents and response that the different stakeholders should undertake.

project_name: Ensuring availability of life saving maternal, newborn child health and essential immunization services, also COVID-19 response with more focus on prevention of COVID and continuity of essential health services in high burdon districts of Pakistan
project_objective:

Most disadvantaged districts of Balochistan, Sind and KP are more prone the emergencies, which have already having very poor development indicators including health. Ongoing COVID19 Pandemic has further deteriorated the situation as the country is faced with both direct and indirect morbidities and mortalities due to COVID pandemic. Health services in the country are already resource constrained and there is a need to support national government for strengthening essential health services with more focus on MNCH and essential lifesaving immunization. The Following interventions will be prioritized.

The project will also strengthen community outreach of life saving immunization and MNCH services through outreach teams (LHWs, Vaccinators, CMWs) and engaging local CSO partners. Digital platforms will be used for delivering of PSS while there are movement restrictions in place. The Psychosocial support will be provided at three levels tailored to the needs of target population:
2.	 Community based integrated (Nutrition, WASH, Health) essential MNCH and Immunization services will be established for the most disadvantaged population ,  with support from LHW Program and involvement of local CSOs focusing on provision of  life saving essential health services at the door step of communities. 
3.	Risk Communication and Community Engagement: Risk communication and community engagement is another area, where awareness raising campaign on COVID and IPC will be launched through community-based health workers like LHWs, CMWs and other CHWs. engaging local Influential and religious leaders orienting them on COVID-19 prevention and importance of seeking healthcare.

project_name: Provision of Safe lifesaving Nutrition services for Severe Acute malnourished children 6 to 59 months without complications for vulnerable population in Pakistan.
project_objective:
""Under the proposed nutrition-specific project UNICEF will support the government to contribute to the reduction of COVID-19 related morbidity and mortality by protecting the nutritional status of the most vulnerable individuals and families across most affected areas through enhanced access to safe promotional, preventive and curative lifesaving nutrition services for people affected by and people at risk of coronavirus infection, while implementing appropriate infection prevention and control measures with below specific objectives.
1- Ensure all severe acute malnourished girls and boys less than five years of age have access to life-saving therapeutic treatment services.
2- Ensure that Mothers and caretakers in targeted communities’ access skilled support for appropriate maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN).
3- Ensure all girls and boys less than five years of age and pregnant and lactating women access multimicronutrient supplements for the prevention of micronutrient deficiencies.""

project_name: Children (girls and boys) and their families affected by disaster are protected against violence, abuse, exploitation, discrimination and other violations of their rights.
project_objective:
Child protection issues are exacerbated during disaster, requiring immediate protection services to bring normalcy back in the lives of girls, boys and women. Measures to prevent abuse and violence and respond to cases of survivors of violence and exploitation need to be strengthened by providing safe access to protective services. Likewise, psychosocial distress experienced by people at the onset of any emergency requires professional care and support. Hence, the project provides mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and coordination as a core area of response. An increase of CP risks is being observed in the current COVID-19 pandemic as well. Some of these may include: Physical and emotional maltreatment, Gender-based violence (GBV), mental health and psychosocial distress, child labour, unaccompanied and separated children and social exclusion. Following are some of the interventions:

1.	Establishment of protective spaces to cater the needs of vulnerable girls, boys and women including disable. The protective spaces will be run by trained facilitators and provided with recreational and learning materials. It will offer opportunities for girls and boys to build resilience and recover from their experiences, provide a daily routine and a sense of normalcy.
2.	Provision of Psychosocial Support (PSS) is primarily aimed at those individuals or group of people who require care and support including those in isolation or quarantine in case of the current COVID-19 situation. Digital platforms will be used for delivering PSS while there are movement restrictions in place. The PSS will be provided at three levels tailored to the needs of target population:
•	Within facilities receiving suspected/infected people for care and support including isolation and quarantine facilities.
•	Community based support in areas identified with suspected/infected people or receiving people exiting isolation/quarantine facilities and going through the social reintegration phase. Families, relatives and caregivers of such people will also be able to avail such services and support.
•	Referral pathways in collaboration of case management for accessing social protection services/packages.
3.	People demonstrating exacerbated distress and signs of mental health concerns or adverse reactions, would be referred to specialized mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). Digital platforms will be used for delivery of MHPSS while movement restrictions are in place. 
4.	Provide CP monitoring and outreach social mobilization through dedicated and trained CP monitors and facilitators in coordination with community-based CP structures and CP Working Groups and Govt. counterparts;
5.	Establish and strengthen coordination amongst key stakeholders and community-based CP structures for the identification of vulnerable girls, boys and women, including missing, unaccompanied, separated and disabled children, and promote their access to protection, social and psychosocial services through an effective and efficient case management and referral system;
6.	Capacity building of relevant service providers, Govt. officials including DMAs, CSOs, rights-holders and duty-bearers in Child Protection in Emergency (CPiE), psychosocial support and strengthening advocacy and support for girls, boys and women affected by disaster to achieve enhanced protection for them;
7.	Dissemination of critical information for prevention of violence against children (VAC) using different communication channels. In the current context, service provision will prioritize prevention of stigma, labelling and discrimination of people who are perceived to be infected or affected by COVID-19. The promotion of correct information and addressing emerging myths and rumors including positive understanding and behaviours about ‘social distancing’ should therefore include actions that support people to adopt and maintain healthy and rationale lifestyles.

project_name: Provision of continuity of learning and ensuring access to safe learning in formal and non-formal across Pakistan
project_objective:
Abrupt school closures on March 13 and then again November 26 caused by the global COVID-19 pandemic have forced 42 million learners in Pakistan out of school and heavily disrupted their learning. In a country with an already existing large number of out of school children, prolonged school closures and loss of learning will have a detrimental effect on enrolment, learning, retention, and dropout rates in Pakistan. A youth perception study report recently conducted in Pakistan with support from UNICEF indicated that young people are concerned that economic distress because of COVID 19 will likely force more of them into (child) labour and early marriage. In addition, constrained access to regular activities such as going to school and playing has a negative impact on children’s opportunities to socialize and play with their peers and physical contact, all which is critical for their psychosocial wellbeing. 
 
There is growing consensus that school closures combined with increased economic stress on families will widen learning inequalities and disproportionately harm vulnerable children and youth, especially girls. The experience of past shutdowns reveals a high risk of students, especially girls, dropping out of education – once they are out of school for extended periods of time, there is a risk that they will not return. As school closures forced children to stay at home and boys have had more access to education opportunities compared to girls who have been involved in household and child-care activities. “Girls’ education and COVID-19 in Pakistan”, a report commissioned by Malala Funds outlined gender disparities amongst boys and girls while they spent time at home during school closures. According to the report, 40 per cents girls reported being involved in household chores compared to 11 per cent of boys. The report also highlighted that girls found it more difficult to access distance learning opportunities and electronic devices during school closures compared to boys. 
 
In the first wave of COVID-19, UNICEF supported coordination mechanisms both at federal and provincial level to ensure oversight and monitoring of the response. UNICEF directly reached out to School Management Committees (SMC) members, teachers and education personnel with COVID-19 prevention messages via SMS, robocall and social media. SMCs were trained on safe school reopening and teachers on safe school reopening and mental health and psychosocial support. As part of continuity of learning, UNICEF provided access to learning opportunities to the most vulnerable children and adolescents through supporting distance learning modalities such as sharing of learning curriculum-based video lessons, take home material and ‘catch up’ learning interventions. 
 
To mitigate the impacts of the pandemic for the most vulnerable, UNICEF will continue to support the Education departments in all the four provinces with continuity of learning, safe return to schools and ensuring adherence to the Standard Operating Procedures for children in formal schools as well as in Alternative Learning Programmes (ALPs). As a sector lead organization UNICEF will also be supporting training of sector members on humanitarian response, coordination and planning for the education sector. UNICEF Pakistan prioritizes supporting 535,500 beneficiaries including 512,00 children (307,200 girls), 8,500 teachers (5,100 female teachers) and 15,000 SMC members (9,000 female members) in humanitarian response to COVID-19. If schools remain closed, children and adolescents need access to remote learning opportunities - including low-tech opportunities as radio or no-tech opportunities as take- home learning packages for those who do not have access to digital learning solutions. As schools reopen, safe opening protocols will need to be implemented and monitored, including collaboration with communities, SMCs, teachers and students to ensure a safe and accessible learning environment in schools.

project_name: WASH services for the communities affected by natural disasters and COVID-19
project_objective:
The aim of the UNICEF’s WASH project is to reduce mortality and morbidity within the affected population through increasing access to and provision of essential WASH services. Water and sanitation are among the immediate priority needs of populations affected by any disasters. It is estimated that up to 50 percent of the affected population in a disaster will require water, sanitation and hygiene services. UNICEF WASH response will target critical needs of the most vulnerable (including those of children, women and people with special needs) and will be guided by humanitarian principles and priorities, including the Sphere Guidelines. 
UNICEF’s assistance package for natural disaster will include the following: 
Provision of safe water: 
Target population of around 530,000 people (119,462 men, 124,338 women, 140,238 boys and 145,962 girls) including people with special needs will have access to sufficient water of appropriate quality and quantity for drinking, cooking and maintaining personal hygiene (benchmark: 5 -15 L/person/day), through water trucking, immediate restoration of damaged water supply systems and provision of household level water filtration solutions where water is available but contaminated.
Provision of Sanitation Facilities:
Target population of around 390,000 people (87,906 men, 91,494 women, 103,194 boys and 107,406 girls) including people with special needs will have access to toilets and washing facilities that are culturally appropriate, secure, sanitary, user-friendly and gender-appropriated (Benchmark: 20 people/hygienic toilet), through installation of temporary latrines, bathing cubicles, and solid waste collection points. 
Hygiene Promotion: 	
Target population of around 560,000 people (126,224 men, 131,376 women, 148,176 boys and 154,224 girls) including people with special needs will receive critical WASH-related information and supplies to prevent child illness, especially diarrhea, through interpersonal hygiene sessions, mass media campaigns, distribution of IEC material  and the provision of WASH related non-food items (NFIs). 
WASH in Schools:
Around 45,000 children (22,050 boys and 22,950 girls) will have access to safe water and sanitation facilities and follow safe hygienic practices in their learning environment, child friendly spaces through installation of water and sanitation facilities and interpersonal hygiene session


UNICEF’s assistance package for COVID-19 will include the following:
Target population of around 51,000 people (including staff of HCF and patients) will have access to appropriate WASH facilities in health care centers, through new installation and repair/rehabilitation of water and sanitation facilities.
Target population of around 440,000 people (99,176 men, 103,224 women, 116,424 boys and 121,176 girls) including people with special needs will have access to information on preventive measures against COVID-19 through social and mass media campaigns, radio jingles, distribution of IEC materials and television shows. 
Target population of around 110,000 people will have access to hand washing stations installed at key public places.  
A target of 11,000 people key frontline workers will be trained on measures related to COVID-19, to ensure the safety, comply with SOPs and follow precautionary measures about related to COVID-19.

project_name: AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES AUX SERVICES INTEGRES DE PRISE EN CHARGE DE VBG
project_objective:
Les efforts et stratégies sont mises en place pour améliorer l’accès des femmes et des filles, les hommes et les garçons et les personnes en situation de handicap aux services intégrés de prise en charge des VBG. Toutefois un nombre important de besoins restent non couverts. Pour remédier à cette situation, UNFPA envisage la mise en œuvre d’un projet intitulé « l’amélioration de l’accès aux services intégrés de prise en charge de VBG » 
L’objectif du projet est de contribuer à réduire les violences basées sur le genre à travers l’accès aux services de prise en charge holistique. Ce projet va s’articuler a réduire durablement les VBG à travers les campagnes de sensibilisation, l’organisation des cliniques juridique et psychosociales, l’aménagement des espaces surs, les activités de formations professionnelles de base et d’appui économique pour les femmes et les filles. Le renforcement des activités de prévention dans les communautés. Le renforcement  des mécanismes de référence et d’assistance juridique des personnes déplacées et des communautés hôtes ayant besoin de protection juridique (détention arbitraire, documentation civile, survivante de VBG)  le renforcement des capacités des sectorielles étatiques, et  les organisations des femmes, des filles des jeunes, des personnes en situation de handicap.  La réalisation des audits de sécurité et la cartographie des risques et de vulnérabilité etc. En outre, il s’agit  de répondre à travers une prise en charge holistique (médicale, psychosociale, juridique, sécuritaire) aux besoins des femmes, des filles des hommes, des garçons et des personnes en situation de handicap.  Et de manière spécifique  la réinsertion socio-économique des femmes et des filles. 
Les objectifs spécifiques de notre intervention sont les suivants :
	Renforcer les mécanismes de prise en charge holistique et intégrée à travers la mobilisation des réseaux communautaires de prévention et de réponse aux VBG 
	Améliorer la protection et le respect des droits fondamentaux des personnes affectées par les crises en donnant la priorité aux femmes , filles exposées aux risques de violences , d’abus et d’exploitation sexuelle .

Le projet va prendre en compte les déplacés  internes (IDPS) et les communautés hôtes (femmes, filles, hommes, garçons et personnes en situation de handicap) les données seront ventilées par sexe, et tranche d’Age,
Pour garantir la prise en compte des besoins des personnes vivant avec un handicap, il sera question de diffuser les directives pour l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap auprès des sectorielles gouvernementales les associations des femmes, des jeunes. Les indicateurs sur le nombre de personnes en situation de handicap sera ventilé sexe dans toutes les activités.  
Pour assumer une meilleure redevabilité, le projet sera mis en œuvre avec la participation de toutes les parties prenantes à savoir les bénéficiaires (femme –filles – hommes- garçons et personnes en situation de handicap). Ces derniers seront associés aux décisions qui les touchent en  leur permettant de formuler des feedbacks et la gestion des plaintes à travers la mise en place des boites à suggestion ou ces derniers pourront dénoncer les cas d’abus et d’exploitations sexuelles. Les sensibilisations seront menées dans les communautés pour expliquer le rôle de ces boites à images en langue locale.

project_name: Emergency interventions to improve access to basic WASH services for the most vulnerable unserved/underserved communities in the West Bank
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve the access of the most vulnerable communities including children in Area C in the West Bank to safe access to water and sanitation. The interventions will contribute to reducing the targeted communities WASH vulnerability with focus on children and persons with disabilities (PWD),especially girls as they are considered the most vulnerable and more in need of these critical services. The proposed interventions will target unserved and underserved communities with essential WASH services that will also protect the most vulnerable families under threat of forcible transfer. The intervetions will focus on improving the communities’ access to: 1) adequate and safely managed water services; 2) sanitation services and 3) WASH facilities in schools;  4) safe and adequate tankered water in underserved communities including schools; and 5) increased storage capacity of the unconnected households. All interventions will be implemented in parallel with the provision of hygiene materials and hygiene awareness sessions in schools and communities.

The project interventions were developed based on the WASH Cluster eligible actions for HRP 2021, and targeting the most vulnerable communities according to WASH 2020 vulnerability mapping. Therefore, UNICEF and its implementing partners are proposing to implement:

•	Construction/rehabilitation of water infrastructures (pipes and cisterns) (19  communities).
•	Construction/rehabilitation of household wash facilities (latrines and handwashing stations) (55 of households)
•	Construction/rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools. (21 schools)
•	distribution of tankered water to most vulnerable unconnected communities including six schools in Area C for at least five months, developing capacities of water distribution chain stakeholders at local, regional and national levels.
•	Provision 459 household Poly Ethelene (PE) water tanks in most vulnerable unconnected communities in Area C benefitting from the tankered water.
•	Provision of hygiene materials and hygiene awareness sessions in schools and communities. (21 schools and 24 communities)

UNICEF and its partners will adopt several implementation methodologies that consider the targeted communities’ locations, proposed response technical standards, and UNICEF's accessibility and partners to these communities. Therefore, UNICEF and the partners will adopt and consider beneficiary/community implementation mechanisms for household interventions such as construction/rehabilitation of household WASH facilities and cisterns. Implementation through suppliers/contractors will be adopted for WASH facilities in schools and water community water infrastructures activity. 

Moreover, the proposed interventions will consider the targeted groups' socioeconomic, protection and COVID-19-related  vulnerabilities. UNICEF will target the communities under the risk of demolition and forcible transfer in Area C, the families under the poverty line, and the communities highly affected by the COVID-19 outbreak. The proposed interventions will improve the targeted groups' capacities and resilience to deal with the challenges mentioned above.

UNICEF and its partners will carefully consider the special and persistent needs of women, children, elders and PWDs. Thus, these vulnerable groups will be consulted during the planning, design, and implementation of the interventions. Therefore, UNICEF and its partners will propose the sufficient response of these groups that consider the different social and traditional characteristics in the targeted communities.

project_name: Improved access to education, and well-being for children and adolescents in Area C, Hebron and East Jerusalem
project_objective:
Children and adolescents in the West Bank including East Jerusalem face severe and chronic protection challenges going to and from school. They cross Israeli military check points and closed military zones or pass by settlements where they may experience harassment and violence. The project will contribute to the 2021 HRP Education Objective 1: increase equitable safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children. Children, adolescents  and teachers facing obstacles to access schools or students exposed to risks of harassment will be supported to have safe access to schools; 15,000 students aged 6-16 and 250 teachers in H2, South Hebron Hills, Bethlehem, South Nablus, East Jerusalem and other selected areas in the West Bank will be targeted. This intervention has been developed in consultation with the affected communities and will also be coordinated with the Protection Cluster. It supports efforts to operationalize the guidelines of the Safe Schools Declaration creating a safer learning environment for children.

Several assessments continue to show the realization of the right to education remains severely compromised in these locations. In response, families may adopt negative coping mechanisms, such as taking students  out of school to limit their exposure to Israeli violence and harassment, a practice more common among girls than boys. The lack of safe access has significant negative consequences for student’s schooling and results in a decrease of school hours, an increased drop-out rate of children, discouraging teaching staff and the displacement or separation of families as they seek solutions in getting their children in schools elsewhere. These negative factors affect children’s and adolescents’ well-being. The findings of a UNICEF evaluation of protective presence (March 2020) emphasized the need for a comprehensive approach to safe access to schools that complements protective presence with other mechanisms such as local solutions by communities. The project will be expanding the format so that interventions ensure and respond to issues of access, equity and gender equality, increased continuity of education and protection of crisis-affected children and adolescents.  UNICEF will support the most vulnerable schools in the WB and EJ in the development and operationalization of a holistic schools plans where objectives, priorities and coordination mechanisms are clear for all actors, for the protection, wellbeing and safe access of students and teachers.

Interventions will include:
i)	Establishment/strengthening of school management committees (SMCs), including training on how to provide a protective learning environment and safeguarding of children’s and teacher’s access to school.
ii)	Training of teachers on how to provide Life Skills and psychosocial support with those identified as needing protection services referred to relevant protection service providers;
iii)	Provision of school recreational and life skills activities for children and adolescents in schools or local community centers to serve as safe hubs;
iv)	Support to the development and operationalization of holistic schools plans for safeguarding of student’s and teachers’ safe access.

The COVID-19 outbreak which resulted in school closures since the 6th of March 2020 has led to the exacerbation of existing needs among children and to emerging psychosocial needs which will be addressed as part of these interventions. The project will ensure equal opportunities for both girls and boys to participate in the activities as events will be announced publicly, encouraging participation of any gender. Recognizing that participation of girls in some communities is socio-culturally more sensitive, interventions will be adapted to ensure access and acceptance by girls and caregivers. Methods will be re-adjusted to respond better to the different needs of male and female students, SMCs and teachers, appropriate to the local context.

project_name: Strengthening emergency response to public WASH facilities in Gaza and prevention flooding in winter
project_objective:
The current humanitarian situation in Gaza under 13 years of closure, internal political divide, and most recently, COVID-19 outbreak is marked by increased deprivations of basic rights of around two million Palestinians (a half of whom are children) living in Gaza, including their access to adequate water and sanitation. 

Over the last years, there has been a constant lack of investment in Gaza’s basic infrastructure, due to recurring escalations of the conflict as well as inability to bring in repair materials.  As a result, the supply of basic services has been unable to keep up with the increasing demand caused by Gaza’s population growth, whilst the conditions of the infrastructure have been deteriorated because of general decay over time and damages inflicted during the periodic hostilities. 

This project will improve the vulnerable communities’ access to safe drinking and domestic water, and safe access to sanitation and hygiene services, and will support the preparedness and response measures to protect the vulnerable communities living in high flood prone areas from the risk of displacement, damage of property, lack of access to public services, and public health impact. It will strengthen the response to routine and sudden essential WASH services and increase the preparedness for winter season in order to avoid flooding and shortage of critical equipment and spare parts. In addition, it will mitigate the health risks related to the COVID 19 epidemic as it will ensure that WASH facilities continue to function in case of further deterioration of the situation.

Through this project, UNICEF aims at providing WASH preparedness and response to the most vulnerable communities in Gaza in order to avoid the discontinuity of WASH facilities operation and maintenance which would have an adverse public health impact.  

The planned activities consist in the provision of critical spare parts and specialized services for repairs and refurbishment of water and wastewater facilities to reduce and eliminate the risks of public health deterioration and environmental pollution through: 
1)	Providing essential operation and maintenance materials and tools for the critical water and wastewater facilities to ensure public WASH facilities are safe and well equipped to respond to floods; and
2)	Rehabilitating storm water drainage systems and sanitation networks, including installing storm water, wastewater pipes, manholes, repairing drainage systems, removing solid waste and sludge from the valley streams and the collapsed sand dunes from storm water collection/infiltration ponds to enhance infiltration capacity.

project_name: Enhanced Maternal, Emergency Obstetrical and Newborn Care
project_objective:
The project will contribute to two strategic objectives of the health cluster: 
SO1: Ensure the availability of acceptable and quality essential healthcare services to vulnerable communities in oPt; and,

SO2: Strengthen the healthcare system's capacity to respond to emergencies and build community resilience to cope with the impact of current and future crises. 

The project will serve a total of approximately 78,750 people including; 5,000 children under five, including 500 neonates; 9,000 high risk pregnant and lactating women; 14,750 men; 500 health professionals; 50,000 adults suspected of the COVID-19 infection. 

UNICEF ensured the coordination with relevant authorities in the assessment of medical supplies and equipment needed at targeted health facilities in H2.

project_name: Provision of Information, counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), and enhancing the protection of civilians affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
Provision of information, legal counselling and legal assistance (ICLA) on Civil Documentation (CD), Housing, Land and Property (HLP) and Livelihoods rights to people affected by crisis and displacement inside Syria. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable populations throughout Syria through the delivery of a multi-faceted response focusing on protection of the rights to legal identity and security of tenure. Through its Capacity Building Programme and ICLA core competency NRC’s work is intended to contribute to HRP Protection Sector Objectives 1 and 2.
NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and mixed modalities which will include provision of legal awareness sessions as well as individualised counselling and legal assistance. Partner names have not been included in this submission for reasons of confidentiality. 
Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable crisis and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities, IDP and refugee returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the crisis. All interventions will seek to prioritize the most vulnerable households and pressing needs. Key needs include the issuance of basic civil documentation such as birth, marriage and death certificates which are necessary in order to access education, health care and humanitarian assistance.  Groups with highest needs include children without proof of legal identity and women with missing or deceased spouses who require confirmation of their legal status and that of their children. Other basic needs include protection of tenure security and legal support to prevent arbitrary evictions. 
NRC’s intervention forms part of integrated programming inside Syria, in close collaboration with the Shelter & WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) and
Education programmes, NRC will aim to meet its overall objective of enabling conflict and displacement-affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. The NRC response in Syria will consist of two components:
a) Increased Knowledge and Capacity to Respond: Legal research and analysis, capacity building, HLP and CD coordination and preparation for durable solutions including return b) Direct Assistance: NRC will assist target groups on issues that link to accessing essential services and CD, as well as improving protection in accessing livelihoods and HLP rights. In 2021, NRC will increase its support for Collaborative Dispute Resolution (CDR) techniques, such as mediation and negotiation. NRC will continue to carry out HLP due diligence to support shelter/WASH, education and livelihood interventions.

project_name: Improving food security in Jonglei and Unity South Sudan
project_objective:
In line with the South Sudan HRP and cluster objectives 1 and 2, the project will save lives by addressing the acute severe food insecurity of 57,000 conflict and natural disaster affected people in IPC3+ in Jonglei (Pigi/Canal, Bor) and Unity State (Rubkona and Guit) through distribution of food vouchers to 2,500 HH and enhanced and sustained food production through distribution of seeds, crop and fishing kits, training and cash for work to 9,500 HH. In support of nutrition centres, kitchen gardens will be established to improve the nutritional status of people. This will allow severe and acute food insecure people in IPC3+ to meet their immediate food needs whilst allowing them to rebuild their assets. In addition, by improving people's food security, acute malnutrition will be reduced. All the selected locations are affected by different natural and man-made disaster, showing high and multiple vulnerabilities and are priority areas as they are in IPC3 or worse, confirmed by Cordaid assessments. Assessments also showed that women (incl. PLW), children (incl. children under 5), PWD, elderly and chronically ill are impacted differently and are bearing the brunt of conflict, droughts/ floods and COVID-19. The project will therefore target these most vulnerable groups through inclusive assistance, and will ensure that protection, gender and COVID-19 is mainstreamed in the proposed activities. 
Protection will be mainstreamed throughout the project cycle to ensure beneficiary safety & dignity, avoiding doing harm as result of the intervention, providing meaningful access to all sets of beneficiaries and ensuring all groups are actively involved and participate in the project in an inclusive manner. Additionally, the project will ensure all necessary Covid-19 measures and protocols will be adhered to; for example, during distributions, beneficiaries will be encouraged to maintain safe social distance, always wash their hands and wear face masks.
Cordaid has been responding to the increasing humanitarian needs in all 4 areas providing WASH, FSL and ES&NFI assistance and is fully operational in the 4 areas with offices in Malakal, Bor and Bentiu.

project_name: WASH coordination among WASH cluster partners during planning, design, and implementation of WASH humanitarian responses
project_objective:
WASH Cluster has 47 WASH partners including 23 INGOs, 13 LNGOs, 4 UN agencies, 3 Educational institutions, 4 local authorities. All partners operate at different levels in the WASH sector and many of them are contributing to several humanitarian planning initiatives such as HRP, COVID-19 response plan and WASH contingency plans. 

UNICEF aims to ensure the maximum operational integration and technical harmonization among these partners, which will be facilitated through the WASH Cluster. It also aims to enhance the WASH coordination system, mechanisms, and tools to ensure that 1) the WASH humanitarian needs in Palestine are identified, 2) all the WASH partners develop their response projects to address these needs, and 3) all the proposed WASH responses satisfy the national and international standards and match  national priorities.  

Through this project, UNICEF as Cluster Lead Agency is proposing to implement several interventions that aim to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the WASH humanitarian project cycle in Palestine: 1) needs and technical assessments to identify the most vulnerable groups with limited access to basic WASH services; 2) capacity building programs for WASH Partners to improve partners capabilities to address the identified WASH needs; 3) developing WASH coordination mechanisms and tools to ensure efficient communication between the Cluster partners and humanitarian country team; and 4) leading and coordinating the development of national and sub-national humanitarian response and contingency plans. 

UNICEF will allocate three specialized staff members to handle all the tasks mentioned above on national and sub-national levels; these staff members will work directly with all WASH Cluster partners to ensure quality coordination of WASH interventions in Palestine, providing them with technical support.

The WASH Cluster team will also carry out tasks related to monitoring, evaluating and reporting of Cluster partners planned, ongoing and implemented activities. It will also ensure the maximum accountability of WASH Cluster partners to the beneficiaries, local authorities, and humanitarian country team. Moreover, the Cluster will support and encourage its partners to mainstream protection, gender, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities in their plans and responses to ensure the appropriateness of the assistance provided for all the vulnerable groups.

Moreover, the WASH Cluster will track and monitor the application of the relevant age, gender and diversity mainstreaming in partners WASH plans and responses during 2021, and ensure that all the technical guidance, proposed and implemented WASH interventions satisfy the special needs of these vulnerable groups.

project_name: Ensure safe and accessible channels for reporting Sexual Exploitation and Abuse to beneficiaries of humanitarian assistance  in Zimbabwe
project_objective: In 2020  Standard Operation Procedures for reporting and processing SEA complaints have been developed and endorsed by Zimbabwe HCT. Under the leadership of the Resident Coordinator, and with technical support of a dedicated PSEA Coordinator, the PSEA Steering Committee as well as the PSEA Network, composed by 52 PSEA Focal Points, have initiated activities such as trainings. However, some barriers to safe and accessible  reporting  of SEA by beneficiaries  have been identified. These barriers are linked with low awareness of the reporting channels amongst beneficiaries, affected communities’ fear of retaliation including fear of suspension of humanitarian assistance, lack of  training for field staff on how to handle end refers the complaints, limited dissemination of PSEA related tools and messages. Therefore, the project aims to fill the above mentioned gaps through innovative and effective communication strategies towards beneficiaries,  establishment of diversified  and easily accessible reporting channels, and  enhancing  field staff capacities.  The project will target all communities in the 10 Provinces , with a special focus on women and girls as most frequent victims of SEA.

project_name: Provision of remedial education and learning support to vulnerable school aged children in Gaza
project_objective:
The project aims to support vulnerable children in elementary grades from two to six by providing remedial classes on two core subjects of Arabic Language and Mathematics. This project will contribute to the 2021 HRP Education Objective 2: “Increase equitable safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children” 

The remedial classes will assist the low achieving children to master the foundational numerical and reading skills. According to the 2021 HNO, a total of 18,989 are in need of remedial education in the same year. It is anticipated that the COVID-19 outbreak which resulted in school closures of the second semester of the academic year 2019-2020 from March 2020 will further increase the number of boys and girls in need of remedial education, especially amongst the vulnerable poor children without internet and necessary devices to access distance learning opportunities, since schools have been re-opened using a blended approach that combines distance and face to face learning. 

UNICEF will support 5,000 vulnerable school children to improve their learning achievements through the provision of remedial education lessons in Arabic Language and Mathematics. It is expected that improving their grades in these core subjects will reduce their risk of dropping out of school. According to UNICEF’s Out of School Report (2018), low achievement is given as one of the main reasons for dropping out of school.  
The intervention has been developed in consultation with relevant stakeholders, targeted teachers, students and parents. All of them expressed a great need for this intervention as it reduces the risk of school dropout. Under this project, 5,000 children will be supported with remedial education by 220 newly hired teachers (50% females) from university graduates who will receive training on remedial education teaching methods and formative assessments in classrooms and during self-study at home in case of re-closure of schools due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Teachers will also be trained on how to provide psychosocial support and outreach for children who do not return to classrooms, in addition to UNICEF course on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse. Parents will be oriented about remedial education, health protocol for safe school operations, and how to be engaged to support their children’s learning during their self-study and remote learning at home. The project will also contribute to the reduction of the high unemployment rate among youth in Gaza (60% according to World Bank report 2014) since it provides working opportunities for the university graduates and facilitates their future recruitment by the relevant education authorities.

Target children will be selected through the examination of the learning achievement records in most vulnerable schools and from those who have shown continuous or rapid drop in learning achievement over the past five months. The project will focus on foundational skills in the Arabic language and Mathematics as key priorities among core subjects where students have been falling behind. The project will target particularly those who are failing to meet minimal standards in the subjects. Therefore, special customized tests will determine which students are in need of support. 

The project will build on catch-up/remedial programmes implemented by UNICEF between 2015 and 2019 and will benefit from materials developed and tested in partnership with relevant stakeholders. These materials considered the recent changes in the curriculum and have been completely updated as of 2019. UNICEF will use methodology already proven effective through the on-going and previous interventions implemented with relevant stakeholders. Children will be instructed in each school by three teachers, one teacher being from the targeted school itself and the other two support teachers who are university graduates who obtained high scores in the final university exams.

project_name: WASH Support to at Risk Communities in Zimbabwe
project_objective:
The IRC will provide WASH support to 60000 people in communities within the 3 districts who are facing environmental sanitation problems especially open defecation and have no access to water sources of sufficient quality. The water supply intervention will be focused across the 3 districts where the average percentage of households of households whose water supply situation is classified as severe is 22%. The environmental sanitation interventions will however be targeted to Beitbridge, Chiredzi and Chipinge Districts. In view of the on-going COVID -19 pandemic, the IRC will target all the 3 districts with risk awareness and community engagement activities (RCCE). 

The IRC will target whole communities with water supply infrastructure prioritizing communities whose access to safe clean water is low. Sanitation interventions will directly benefit vulnerable households particularly households with people living with disabilities, the elderly, child headed and headed by women. These will be used as demonstration sites for latrine construction whilst encouraging other households to replicate.  Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) will be implemented through Community Health Clubs (CHC). Target communities will be selected through district and community level coordination structures to ensure that the right beneficiaries are targeted.

project_name: Amélioration de la réponse de protection et assistance, recherche et mise en œuvre des solutions durables pour les refugies centrafricain à l’EST du Cameroun
project_objective:
Ce projet vise l’amélioration de l’environnement de protection et la mise en œuvre des solutions en faveur de 622 réfugiés (85% des femmes et enfants et 15% des hommes) et les populations hôtes (30 %) dans les régions d’accueil des réfugiés où environ 554.000 personnes sont affectées directement ou indirectement par les déplacements forcés. Les activités seront mises en œuvre sous le leadership du gouvernement et en collaboration avec les acteurs humanitaires, de développement, les organisations de la société civile et du secteur privé dans un esprit de complémentarité d’actions. 
Le HCR et ses partenaires comptent renforcer les interventions afin d’assurer un meilleur environnement de protection aux réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile dans les régions de l’Est, Adamaoua et le Nord. Dans le contexte crise humanitaire et situation économique, l’impectus sera mis sur les activités qui garantissent la jouissance des droits humains fondamentaux aux femmes, aux hommes, aux filles et aux garçons de tout âge et ceux ayant diverses vulnérabilités. 
Les domaines d’intervention sont notamment : la documentation, la protection de l’enfance, la prévention et la réponse aux violences sexuelles et sexistes, l’accès aux services sociaux de base (santé, éducation et eau), accès à un abri décent et aux biens domestiques essentiels. L’ensemble de ces actions permettra aux populations cibles de vivre dignement dans un environnement protégé avec comme finalité la réduction de leur dépendance chronique à l’assistance. 
A cet effet, le HCR et ses partenaires :
1.	Apporteront la réponse aux besoins critiques de protection en assurant l’accès à l’asile, la documentation, la prévention et la réponse aux VBG, l’accès à l’éducation, aux moyens d’existence et à l’inclusion socio-économique, ainsi que le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de la coexistence pacifique avec la communauté hôte.
2.	Mettront en œuvre les solutions durables en renforçant la résilience et les moyens d’existence. Le HCR continuera à faciliter le retour volontaire des réfugiés dans leur pays d’origine, à identifier les cas de réinstallation, et à faire le plaidoyer pour l’accès des réfugiés aux voies complémentaires.  
3.	Assureront la Mise en œuvre des engagements du Forum Mondial sur les Réfugiés (GRF) dans le secteur de l’éducation, de la protection, de la santé, de l’emploi et des moyens d’existence, de l’apatridie (adhésion du Cameroun aux conventions de l’ONU sur l’apatridie, régularisation des personnes vivant sans certificat de naissance, etc.) ;
4.	Mettront en œuvre la réponse aux situations des urgences afin d’absorber les chocs et améliorer la résilience de personnes affectées.  Ces actions seront mises en œuvre en synergie avec les autorités camerounaises, les partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Les bénéficiaires ainsi que les communautés seront directement impliqués dans la conception des réponses, leurs réalisations et suivis.
Les interventions du HCR et de ses partenaires s’aligneront aux priorités définies par le gouvernement (stratégies nationales de développement 2020-2030 et sectorielles). Elles s'inscrivent aussi dans le cadre de sa contribution à l'atteinte des ODD, à la réponse du système des Nations Unies relativement à l’UNSDCF et au principe de ne laisser personne pour compte. Un accent sera mis sur l’inclusion des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile dans les cycles de planification et de programmation d’autres acteurs : gouvernement et communes, la Banque Mondiale, AFD, GIZ, etc.

project_name: Provision of life-saving quality reproductive and maternal health services for the vulnerable displaced and crisis affected communities in Somalia.
project_objective:
Somali has one of the highest and protracted internally displaced persons worldwide and every year communities are displaced by conflict and natural disasters like drought and flood. IDPs and marginalized communities including disabled persons have lower access to healthcare and social services than others. In 2020 COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted health system gains and further exacerbated population vulnerabilities. As of September 26th 2020, Somalia has confirmed 3,588 cases of COVID-19, including 187 health care worker infections; with a case fatality rate of 2.7 percent. With a medium attack rate for COVID-19 over the course of 2021, an estimated 20% of the Somali population (2.5 million) will need to be reached with some form of COVID-19 response action; from awareness, preventative to testing and treatment services. One in three people are or have been affected by mental health disorders in Somalia (WHO, 2016), a rate higher than other low-income and war-torn countries. Also the COVID-19 has added to the mental suffering of the affected population and aggravated gender and interpersonal violence (GBV/IPV). According to the Somalia health cluster, over 3.9 million Somali people require lifesaving essential healthcare and health protection services. 

Sexual and reproductive health remains huge concern in Somalia. Over a Somali woman’s lifetime, she will face a one in 14 chance of dying from complications related to pregnancy or childbirth; facing the sixth highest lifetime maternal death risk (692 deaths per 100,000 live births) in the world (SHDS, 2020); the country has one of the world’s highest rates of under-five mortality at 177/1000 live births (UN IGME, 2020). despite most maternal deaths being preventable. The risk of childhood mortality is highest in the neonatal period, accounting for over 60 percent of deaths among children under age five (UN IGME, 2020). Women and children are particularly exposed to elevated health risks. Access to birth spacing services is limited, and up to 99 percent of women experience Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting (FGM/C) (SHDS, 2020). Survivors of gender-based violence (GBV), reported as 77 percent of IDPs and 20 percent from the host community, face fear of reprisals, stigmatization and difficulties accessing safe and appropriate services (JCMNA, 2019). Negative coping practices as a result of poverty, displacement and isolation due to the crisis, that have also been exacerbated by COVID-19, place the affected at increased risk of violence, abuse and marginalization; as well as negatively affecting their health care choices and access. Care for expectant mothers throughout their pregnancy remains particularly poor, with only 32 percent of births attended by skilled health personnel (SHDS, 2020); these gaps in reproductive health services along with appropriate referral care is essential to prevent the high incidence of maternal and infant death.

Thereafter, UNFPA and its partners will implement this project to respond those needs with the primary focus to provide life-saving quality reproductive and maternal health services for the vulnerable displaced and other crisis affected communities in Somalia. The following are the specific objectives of the intervention: 
a)	To ensure access to quality emergency obstetric and newborn care services for the IDPs & crises affected communities including COVID19 pandemic.
b)	To provide promotive and preventive sexual and reproductive health care including maternal nutritional services among women of childbearing age in the affected population
c)	Enhance the capacity of service providers for sexual and reproductive health including Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) and COVID-19 prevention and control.
d)	Support the procurement and supply chain management for the sexual and reproductive health commodities including RH kits, PPEs, Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) and COVID-19 testing equipment and supplies.

project_name: Ensuring access to quality, timely and confidential services for GBV survivors and strengthening coordination for GBV mitigation and prevention in Somalia
project_objective:
Needs:
GBV continues to be an issue of great concern in Federal members States Galmudug, South West State, Jubaland, Hirashebelle Puntland and Somaliland with the event of the COVID19.  Recent spikes in the increase of Intimate Partner Violence, rape, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment and abuse have multiplied GBV risks for women and girls with worsening impact on women and girls living with disabilities. In IDP camps and host communities – inadequate physical infrastructure, distance to water points, markets, health facilities and schools, poor lightening, lack of doors on toilets and lack of disaggregation of sanitary facilities are some of major factors that increase GBV exposure. In addition, distance to distribution centers and lack of specific measures to ensure women’s inclusion and participation in food distributions, continue to worsen levels of exposure of women and girls to GBV risks. In the July 2020 “GBV/FGM assessment during the COVID19”, 38 percent responders indicated that there has been an increase in GBV incidents; 35 percent indicated GBV incidents are the same.  The number of GBV survivors call in to hotlines for help also increased by 283% in FMS and 767% in Somaliland despite the inactivation of some of the hotlines in the states. 

In addition, GBVIMS 2020 data reports a trend indicating an increase of GBV noting that over half (61%) of reported GBV incidents were Physical Assault, 13% Rape, 12% Sexual Assault, 6% Psychological/Emotional Abuse, 5% experienced Denial of Resources, and the remaining 3% percent Forced/Early marriage.       Furthermore, Anecdotal media and programming report has indicated a spike in rape of women and girls including a specific targeting of recent on boys. Majority of Women and girls fleeing violence in Somalia do not have options for safety and protection. In 2020, there has been significant efforts to broaden women and girls’ safe spaces, however, this has been severely impacted by funding limitations and also due to COVID. 

GBV service provision remains low as compared to the need and geographical landscape. Recently, worsening relations between communities and service providers exacerbated by the heightened political atmosphere impacted provision of GBV services or coordination. GBV service provision in Somalia has historically been characterized by limited specialized services such as rape treatment for rape survivors, psycho-social support and higher levels of mental health care for traumatized women and girls are major hindrances to expanding provision of timely, confidential and quality GBV services. Also, lack of actors to provide specialized services undermines efforts invested to assure access to GBV services by survivors. At present, the GBV AoR in Somalia has 58 partners that reports on the 5Ws.

UNFPA interventions will target the displaced and non-displaced communities including all age groups and persons with disabilities, and with the following specific objectives: a) Facilitate access to comprehensive multi sectoral GBV services (medical, legal, psychosocial) for 6000 women and girls. B) Enhance the capacity/and mobilize 200 PSS counsellors; 150 health workers to provide timely, quality and confidential PSS and rape treatment. C) Promote mobilization of women and girls to access services through the establishment of 15 safe spaces for women and girls (WGSS) to reach 3000 women and girls. D) Support the operationalization of integrate referral pathways for dissemination and access to services reach 2000 women, girls, boys and men. E) Provide 2,000 dignity kits and 36 post rape kits dignity protection for women and girls and treatment of rape. F) Support 200 women and girls’ survivors of GBV with cash voucher assistance and grants for livelihood. G) Support the mainstreaming initiatives on IASC Guidelines for cluster programming on GBV for 300 cluster-coordinators at national and sub national levels.

project_name: Integrated WASH assistance to water service providers for enhanced sustainable and safely managed access to services for the most vulnerable population in the governorates of Bethlehem and Hebron.
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims to contribute to reduction of WASH vulnerability in marginalized communities while simultaneously responding to COVID 19 financial impact and PAs reduced capacity to provide sustainable and scalable efficient solutions to prolonged challenges in the chain of water provision disproportionately impacting vulnerable HHs in the West Bank. 

The intervention components respond to the 2021 HRP SO2 and SO3, in addition to the WASH cluster O2, and O3 through its integrated approach to strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacities designed to address root causes contributing to HH WASH accessibility vulnerability. The intervention will further contribute to enhance target communities capacities to deal with WASH related shocks during emergencies and beyond. 
The intervention will achieve the aforementioned through two main components that respond directly to the identified 2021 WASH priorities: i) Improving Access to water ii) contributing to enhance governance of WASH sector. Through:

i.a) Support the operations and maintenance material and tools for 14 water service providers servicing the entire populations of 14 of the most WASH vulnerable communities in the Governorates of Bethlehem and Hebron ( inclusive of Areas C, A&B) for efficient water provision. A total of 310391 persons, of which 218183 are WASH vulnerable, will directly benefit from this component across age groups and gender including PWDs.

ii.a) Piloting new techniques to improve access to WASH Services: ii.a.1) assistance in developing zoning systems for detection of losses and efficient network management in the Yatta and Tuqu. ii.a.2) provide the targeted 14 water service providers with tech and software solutions for improvement of distribution, management, billing and customer service based on individual needs assessment of capacity. 

ii.b) Conduct Technical capacity building on provided assets, and systems through 6 centralized topic oriented trainings on ( Network manager, customer service, cost recovery, inspection, tariff calculation, and billing and collection systems) for 94 staff of water service providers and regulator(WSRC) of which at least 5% are PWDs.

ii.c) Conduct technical WASH assessment to analyze Supply-Demand Hydraulic on water sources (Fresh and Treated) vs consumption needs at a national level thus informing design of a national plan for carrier pipes network that would improve water distribution and address the imbalances between water supply and demand.

MA’AN has designed and proposed the above intervention to serve an aid gap in WASH sector at the community level and further to complement the current and foreseen work of partners and other WASH aid actors in their interventions at the HH level. The intervention was designed based on consultations with relevant WASH Sector stakeholders, decision makers and Water service providers at the community level. Due to the nature of proposed program, an equal impact/ benefit on beneficiaries ( including those of marginalized groups) is foreseen. MA’AN will ensure, where relevant, to consult with relevant demographics in the communities the proposed response targets.

project_name: Improving the WaSH Situations in Marginalized Communities and Schools in the West Bank
project_objective:
The project aims at securing sufficient and safe drinking water quantities for 2822 households (14,110 individuals) of the targeted communities and families living in Area “C” and “B” of the West Bank for household purposes, including 6,905 women and girls, in addition it aims at improving WaSH conditions in 10 public schools serving 3373 students (2270 males and 1105 females) also improving sanitation conditions for 39 households living in area “C” and ""B"", and increase hygiene awareness through trainings and workshops for 360 persons (180 females and 180 males) in 3 localities as well as the provision of  150 household hygiene kits for the benefit of 125 households in area “C” and ""B"". in total, this project serves more than 17597 inhabitants (8975 males and 8622 females) 280 persons out of them are with disabilities.
The initiative responds to needs highlighted in the 2021 HNO and it is also fully in line with the oPt. Response plan, contributing to the WASH Cluster Objective 2: Ensure equitable, affordable, and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians communities. Access to safe WASH service is a main concern in the West Bank, specifically In Area C, where around 105,000 people receive less than 50 liters of water per capita per day, while over 50,000 people are unconnected to a water network and over 402,000 people are unconnected to a wastewater network.
The initiative has been endorsed by PWA, it is in line with the PWA Strategic Plan (2017-22) and in compliance with the Water Master Plan for Area C. The action is in line with the Sustainable Development Goals, specifically contributing with “Goal 6: Ensure access to water and sanitation for all”.
Further, the initiative allows to reduce and more effectively address the core vulnerabilities of communities and educational institutions in need, increasing water access and availability for unconnected and underserved communities in area “C” and “B” of the West Bank as well as improving sanitation conditions, precisely in Nuba, Adh Dahiriya, Kurza, Idhna, Deir Samit, Beit ar Rush al Fuqa and As Samu in Hebron Gov., Ein Ayoub Bedouins, Ein Jaryout, Ein Qiniya Bedouins and Kobar Bedouins in Ramallah Gov., Iraq al Sakhra, Muhaajir, Wadi Qana, Kifl Haris and Salfit City in Salfit Gov. and in Arab Al Khouli in Qalqilya Governorate.

project_name: Emergency Action to Improve Sanitary Situation for the Residents in Tulkarem Governorate (Area C) and six Schools in Jenin Governorate
project_objective: The project aims at improving sanitary situations (known as WASH) in the selected Areas of the suburb of Shweikeh town (Tulkarem Governorate) and 6 schools located in Area C of Jenin Governorate. The improvement of the sanitation situation in the target areas is essential for a stable life with basic services that will help the residents and the students of these schools to suffer less and to gain better education when town and school is served with sanitation facilities. Based on a recent survey conducted by House of Water and Environment (HWE), more than 2473 people will benefit from this project directly (1510 males and 963 Females).
