It has been estimated by House of Water and Environment that more than 3000 people will be benefit from the proposed project indirectly. The targeted areas of Shweikeh town are located in Zone C. These lands are outside the boundaries of the areas normally served by Tulkarem municipality. These areas suffer badly from a lack of wastewater collection system as 95 % of their residents rely on septic tanks and cesspits, which cause unsanitary conditions and pollution of soil and groundwater resources in addition to affecting negatively on the public health and safety of the women, men, children elderly and disabilities of these areas. Therefore, there is an urgent need to mitigate the bad sanitary conditions in these areas through installing wastewater collection system to serve the targeted population in Shwaikeh area and to promote good access to environmentally sound municipal wastewater services. The targeted schools require their sanitary facilities and drinking water facilities to be rehabilitated. It is proposed in this project to build new sanitation units. So that, those six schools will enjoy having access to adequate sanitary and water units with services for disabled students. Public awareness campaigns will be conducted to address hygiene practice issues at the household level to improve the capacity of the families in the targeted areas to effectively respond to emergencies and reduce tensions across the communities. It worth to mention that, transmission of COVID-19 and other water borne diseases will be lowered. The proposed interventions ensure protection mainstreaming incorporating protecting principles and promoting meaningful access, safety and dignity; accountability as well as participation and empowerment through conducting regular meeting and focus groups.

project_name: Améliorer les conditions d'accès à l'eau, à l'assainissement et à l'hygiène des populations déplacées et hôtes touchées et par la crise du lac Tchad dans la région de Diffa - Niger
project_objective:
La stratégie d'intervention d'ACF vise à apporter une assistance humanitaire en eau, hygiène et assainissement aux populations déplacées et hôtes en tenant compte des
besoins des femmes, hommes, garçons et filles dans les départements de Diffa, Mainé Soroa et Nguigmi.
L’objectif principal du projet est d’améliorer les conditions d’accès à l’eau, l’assainissement et l’hygiène pour les populations affectées par la crise du Lac Tchad dans la région de Diffa. Il se décline en trois objectifs spécifiques:                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
'- Faciliter l’accès à l’eau potable par l’aménagement des points d’eau au profit des personnes déplacées et hôtes dans les zones cibles ( construction/Réhabilitation de points d'eau et mise en place de comités de gestion mixtes)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
- Réduire le péril fécal par la réalisation d’infrastructures d’assainissement (construction de latrines familiales, mise en place de comités d(hygiène et de salubrité mixte, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                                    - Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène parmi la population cible avec un focus sur les méthodes barrières de prévention Covid-19 ( sénaces de sensibilisations, VAD, focus groupe de discussion, messages radio communautaires, affiches, etc.). Les messages porteront sur la salubrité des points d’eau; le transport et le stockage de l’eau; le lavage des mains avec savon dans les moments clés; l’entretien, le nettoyage des latrines et leur utilisation; l’hygiène au niveau de ménage; l’hygiène corporelle; la gestion de déchets; l’hygiène menstruatruelle chez les femmes en âge de procreer; la gestion des selles des enfants; et le traitement de l’eau à domicile. Afin de faciliter les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène au niveau ménage, des kits WASH seront distribués aux ménages les plus vulnérables.                                                                                                                                                               
Sachant que les femmes sont particulièrement touchées et que le déplacement a accru leur vulnérabilité, le projet vise à favoriser leur accès aux installations WASH poroposées. Les femmes étant aussi principales responsables de l'approvisionnement en eau, de la cuisine et de l'hygiène domestique, la priorité leur sera donnée pour les messages de promotion de l'hygiène.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
ACF continuera concentrer son intervention sur les populations hors des camps (dans les villages accueillant les populations déplacées ou les villages de retour). Le choix des sites d'intervention sera guidé par des besoins humanitaires spécifiques, de l'accès humanitaires, de la densité des personnes déplacées, de la présence de
lacunes dans la couverture WASH, et en tenant compte des interventions des autres acteurs de la zone.

project_name: Prise en charge et prevention de la malnutrition dans le district sanitaire de Takeita (Region de Zinder)
project_objective: GOAL soutiendra les activités de nutrition curative (CRENAS/CRENI) au niveau des centres de santé ainsi que celles de la prevention de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire (relais, PB mères etc) tout en renforçant la coordination des acteurs. L’appui concernera 5 CSI, l’unité de stabilisation(CRENI) du DS Takeita et ciblera 2000 enfants 0-59 mois. Les actions se focaliseront sur le renforcement de capacité des acteurs communautaires et des agents de santé. Les activités qui seront appuyées comprennent le depistage de la malnutrition et le referencement des cas, la vaccination, les construction/ réhabilitations(CRENI,latrines, Incinerateurs), mise en place des dispositifs de lavage des mains, Approche PB meres, les sensibilisations ANJE/PFE et supervision conjointe nutrition à assise communautaire dans 25 villages de la zone d’intervention

project_name: Renforcement de capacités et accompagnement des acteurs pour l'intégration des paquets minimum WASH au sein des CRENAS et communautés touchées par la malnutrition aigüe sévère des régions de Maradi, Tahoua et Zinder.
project_objective: L'enquete SMART réalisée en 2018 a montré que la prévalence de la malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG) est de 15,0% IC à 95% [13,6-16,6] et celle de la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS) est de 3,2% IC à 95% [2,6 - 3,9]. Cette prévalence de MAG correspond à une situation critique sur l’échelle de classification de l’OMS. Elle varie d'une région à une autre. Les régions ayant le plus fort taux sont Diffa, Zinder, Tahoua, Maradi, Agadez et Tillabéry. Le CISP, intervenant dans la WASH IN NUT depuis plus de 8 ans à Tillabéry et Diffa, désire cette fois-ci intervenir dans les Régions de Maradi, Tahoua et Zinder. Les activités que nous prévoyons à travers nos animateurs et superviseurs sont entre autres : des séances de sensibilisations au niveau des centres de santé, au niveau ménages, dans les écoles et autres institutions publiques, des distributions d'intrants aux couples mères/enfants malnutris, des suivis du chlore résiduel au niveau des ménages servis en intrants, des dotations en kits d'hygiène et de protection au niveau des structures sanitaires, des formations des acteurs du projets,... pour ne citer que cela. Il faut noter que l'ensemble de ses activités se feront en étroite collaboration avec les autorités et services techniques de la santé, de l'hydraulique et de l'assainissement et du plan et développement communautaire. Aussi, pour la pérennisation de ces réalisations, le CISP envisage d'associer les responsables des structures sanitaires de la zone d'intervention, les hygiènistes, les COGES, les COSAN et les relais communautaires. Tout au long du projet, nos animateurs et superviseurs récolteront les données terrains (des fiches seront mises à leurs dispositions), donneront des appuis conseils au besoin aux bénéficiaires et les accompagneront pour s'assurer que tout se déroule convenablement. Une synthèse mensuelle sera faite pour sanctionner les activités réalisées au cours des mois, un rapport intermédiaire rédigé pour un projet de plus de 3 mois et enfin, un rapport final sera fourni par le CISP à la fin du projet.

project_name: Appui à l’amélioration de la nutrition des enfants, adolescentes, femmes enceintes et allaitantes à travers la mise en œuvre d’un paquet d’interventions communautaires dans les départements de Bagaroua et Illela, Tahoua, Niger.
project_objective:
Le projet propose une approche communautaire pour les soins préventifs et promotionnels assurés par des acteurs locaux à fin que les enfants, les jeunes filles, les femmes enceintes et allaitantes puissent couvrir tous leurs besoins en énergie, en éléments nutritifs de base et en micronutriments. Etant donné que la population, la plus vulnérable, a été fragilisée par le conflit en cours, le risque du COVID-19 et la barrière financière aux soins de santé, la stratégie, basée sur l’intervention des relais communautaire, groupe de soutien à l’ANJE, est l’approche la plus appropriée pour atteindre les populations dans les zones les plus reculées. Les acquis en termes de connaissance et d’organisation lors de la mise en œuvre du projet contribueront à la pérennisation des activités promotionnelles après la finalisation du projet. Le projet s’articule autour de 4 résultats:
Résultat 1. Les connaissances des femmes et autres donneurs de soins sur les pratiques ANJE au niveau des communes de Bagaroua et Tajaé sont améliorées.
-	Organisation des sessions de sensibilisation sur l’ANJE par la communication pour le changement de comportement (CCC)
-	Diffusions des spots sur ANJE et PFE
-	Séances de démonstration culinaire
Résultat 2. L’accès des bénéficiaires aux services de nutrition est amélioré
-	Pour approcher les services des ménages, les relais communautaires effectuerons des visites à domicile pour identifier, enregistrer et suivre les enfants de 6 à 23 mois et les filles de 10 à 19 ans dans la communauté
-	Dépistage et PEC des enfants de moins de 5 ans MAS/MAM dans les CRENI/CRENAS
-	Dépistage et PEC de femmes enceintes et allaitantes admises pour traitement dans les CRENAM
-	Supplémentation nutritionnelle préventive pour les enfants 6-23 mois et les FEFA 
-	L’appui des ECD dans le ravitaillement  des relais, groupes de soutien, CSI/CS en MNP, Vit A, FAF, Outils ANJE.
-	Appui aux structures de santé CRENI/CRENAS  pour l’intégration de l’approche fortification à domicile à travers les poudres de multi micronutriments MNP.
Résultat 3. L’amélioration de la qualité des données et complétude des rapports statistiques 
-	Mise en place des outils de collectes des donnes 
-	Appui aux rencontres mensuels de transmission des données entre acteurs communautaires (RECOP et groupe de soutien à l’ANJE) et les équipes des CSI
Résultat 4. L’amélioration de la qualité des services
-	Formation et/ou recyclage des agents de santé sur l’ANJE, relais communautaires sur l’ANJE, mise en place et formation des groupes de soutien à l’ANJE, briefing des agents sur le remplissage des outils de collectes des données et de gestion d’intrants

project_name: Renforcement de l’accès aux services de prévention et de prise en charge des cas de protection de l’enfance et de VBG pour les IDPs et les populations hôtes dans la région de Tillabéri
project_objective: L’intervention proposée est une réponse d’urgence aux problématiques de protection de l’enfance et de VBG dans la région de Tillabéri, en particulier dans les départements d’Abala, Ayorou, Banibangou, Filingué, Gothèye, Ouallam, Téra, Tillabéri et Torodi. Elle est articulée autour des activités de prévention et de prise en charge des cas de PE et de VBG, s’alignant ainsi sur les priorités des cadres sectoriels des deux sous-clusters. Le projet touchera 30 672 bénéficiaires directs dont 14 200 pour le sous-secteur PE et 16 472 pour le sous-secteur VBG. Sous-secteur PE : a) sensibilisation : 8000 personnes, dont : 2600 enfants (1300 femmes, 1300 garçons) et 5400 adultes (3000 femmes, 2400 hommes) ; b) PSS : 6000 enfants et adolescents, dont 3600 filles et 2400 garçons ; c) prise en charge ES/ENA) : 200 enfants, dont 90 filles et 110 garçons. Sous-secteur VBG : a) 48 personnes formées (24 femmes et 24 hommes) pour offrir des services de qualité aux survivantes (santé -Psychosocial - juridique) ; b) 5500 personnes y compris les enfants et adolescents/adolescentes atteintes avec au moins un service essentiel de qualité (psychosocial, santé, justice, sécurité, AGR) ; c) 10 personnes formées en santé mentale et appui psychosocial ; d) 10700 personnes atteintes avec les activités de sensibilisation sur les VBG et l’ESA  ; e) 50 mécanismes communautaires intégrant les femmes, les filles les hommes et les garçons pour la prévention des VBG/ESA fonctionnels ; f) 400 femmes et de filles ayant bénéficié d'un appui en AGR ; g)  50 femmes et de filles survivantes des VBG et des personnes à risque de VBG ayant bénéficié d'une insertion socioprofessionnelle. La coordination sectorielle et intersectorielle sera renforcée à travers la participation au Cluster protection et aux GT locaux ; les communes des départements ciblés seront au cœur de l'intervention afin d’insérer les problématiques PE et VBG dans les PIA et un financement pour les Comites Communaux PE. Compte tenu du risque COVID-19, le projet prévoit des activités de prévention et la dotation matériels spécifiques (DLM, savon). Cette intervention est complémentaire aux interventions en cours de COOPI dans la région, en particulier dans le secteur de la EiE et celles du RRM en santé/nutrition.

project_name: Preparation et Interventions d'urgence EHA pour personnes victimes des inondations dans les Régions de Maradi, Dosso et Diffa au Niger
project_objective: ADESA  se propose  dans le cadre de ce projet, une intervention EHA, dans les Régions de Maradi, Diffa et Dosso  qui sont  confrontées à la récurrence des inondations afin de renforcer la résilience de la population vulnérable en permettant l’accès à l’eau potable et aux infrastructures d’assainissement avec une attention particulière pour les besoins spécifiques des femmes,des personnes handicapées  et des enfants, la constitution des stocks de contingence des purifiants d’eau ainsi que la sensibilisation de toute la population de cette zone sur l ’éducation à l’hygiène et les mesures de prévention en ciblant spécialement les femmes en ce qui concerne la sensibilisation à l’usage domestique de l’eau. La pandémie à Coronavirus pourrait affecter les populations prédisposées aux inondations en 2020. En effet, suite aux inondations, les populations qui ont perdu leurs maisons se retrouvent dans des classes ou dans d’autres sites aménagés par l’Etat et ses partenaires ; La forte concentration des populations dans ces circonstances, les expose aux risques de contracter la maladie à coronavirus. Cela pourrait avoir des conséquences négatives sur la production agricole car la personne malade sera indisponible à participer aux travaux champêtres et aux activités pastorales et de même, les membres de sa famille seront tout aussi confinés pendant au moins deux (2) semaines. Aussi, le risque d’autres maladies hydriques telles que le paludisme et les maladies diarrhéiques n’est pas écarté surtout pour les personnes les plus vulnérables (enfants, personnes âgées). La pandémie à coronavirus peut modifier significativement nos stratégies habituelles de gestion des inondations. C’est pourquoi des mesures spécifiques doivent être prises dont, entre autres la promotion à l’hygiène.Pour faire face à celà ADESA veut réduire le taux  de la morbidité et mortalité des personnes affectées par les inondations à travers la préparation et mesures d'intervention rapide et d'urgence pour le rétablissement de l'accès à l'eau potable et à l'assainissement de base amélioré au Niger.

project_name: Appui à l'amélioration de l'accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et l’hygiène dans les sites des déplacés et communautés hôtes dans les régions de Tillabéri et Diffa
project_objective:
Ce projet proposé a pour objectif de protéger les personnes contre les maladies liées à l’eau, l'assainissement et à l'hygiène, au bénéfice des populations déplacées et des communautés hôtes résidant dans les zones ciblées. Le nombre des bénéficiaires de ce projet est estimé à 15 000 personnes dont 55% seront les filles et femmes  et 10% de refugiés (1000 ). Le projet sera mis en oeuvre à travers les activités clés ci-après:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
-  Construction/ réabilitation des points d'eau(forages , PEA, mini-AEP...)
- Contruction des latrines d'urgences et durables incluant les kits d'entretiens
- Promotion de l'hygiène incluant la distribution  des kits d'hygiène...
La mise en oeuvre du projet prendra en compte  les aspects de genre et redevabilité  de manière à assurer un accès équitable et sécurisé au profit des bénéficiaires. il faut noter que ce projet tiendra également  en compte de l'approche cash transfert.
 
Le suivi et évaluation sera assuré par l’Officier en charge avec l’appui du conseiller national de suivi-évaluation en étroite collaboration avec le coordonnateur WASH. Sur le terrain, un suivi de contrôle qualité sera assuré conjointement avec les services techniques déconcentrés de l’Etat et les différents membres des structures de gestion communautaires. IRC soucieux de la qualité de son travail, mettra à la disposition des équipes des applications spécialisées dans la collecte des données et de leur traitement. (Kobocollect, CommCARE...).

En vue  d'assurer la durabilité/perennisation  des infrastructures WASH , IRC se propose d'impliquer fortement les membres des comités de gestion des infrastructures (CGPE, AUSPE, relais communautaires...) , les services techniques de l'Etat (DRHA) et les communes ainsi que les leaders communautaires des zones ciblées. IRC  prevoit également des mises en place/ renforcement de capacité / recyclage des comités de gestion des points (pour l'accès durable aux infrastrucures) en accord avec la DRHA et les communes concernées.

project_name: Assistance d'urgence aux ménages déplacés et populations hôtes affectés par les conflits et les catastrophes naturelles dans les régions de Diffa, Maradi et Tillabéri au Niger.
project_objective: Le présent projet envisage de contribuer au bien-être et à la restauration de la dignité des populations affectées par les conflits via l’assistance en abris et BNA. Les populations ciblés sont les déplacés, les réfugiés et les communautés hôtes des régions de Diffa, Maradi et Tillabéri. Afin d'identifier les besoins, des évaluations sectorielles seront réalisées dans les localités affectées accueillant les populations. Une coordination sera faite avec les autres acteurs sur le terrain notamment l'UHNCR pour assurer une réponse intégrée et multisectorielle aux besoins de ces populations. L’assistance se fera sur la base de la vulnérabilité. 9 000 ménages vulnérables (63 000 personnes) seront assistés en biens non alimentaires et en abris transitionnels et d’urgences. Les modalités de réponse seront définis en fonction du contexte dans les zones du projet.  Le projet assurera la participation effective des populations dans la mise en œuvre des activités. Ceci passera notamment par leur consultation et leur implication lors de l'identification des bénéficiaires, la mise en place de comité de plaintes et des monitorings post-distributions afin de recueillir leur retour sur l'assistance. Les leaders locaux et les représentants des communautés affectées seront fortement impliqués dans l’ensemble du processus partant des évaluations des besoins jusqu’à la réponse. Aussi, IRC s’appuiera fortement sur son équipe protection qui fera des analyses des risques chaque fois que cela s’avèrera nécessaire afin de réduire les impacts négatifs que pourraient engendrer les interventions de l'organisation. Les interventions réalisées contribueront à renforcer la protection des bénéficiaires notamment à travers la fourniture des abris dignes et sûrs conformes aux standards du GT ABNA au Niger. De plus, les abris transitionnels vont contribuer à la résilience des communautés cibles. Les personnes à besoin spécifique (femmes cheffes de ménage, personnes âgées, personnes en situation d’handicap) seront prioritairement ciblées au cours de la mise en œuvre du projet. Ces personnes seront appuyées dans la construction de leurs abris. Une attention particulière leur sera portée lors des opérations de distribution afin d'éviter qu'elles n'attendent longtemps dans les rangs. Les abris distribués seront équipés de porte pour renforcer la sécurité des ménages bénéficiaires. L'IRC veillera à ce que les espaces entre les abris construits respectent les standards mais aussi que les sites d'installation des personnes ciblées ne soient pas inondables. Aussi, compte tenu de la pandémie de la COVID-19 qui touche aussi le Niger, IRC s’assurera de mettre en place des mesures de prévention et de réduction des risques au cours de la mise en œuvre des activités du projet. Ces mesures comprendront entre autres : le port du masque pour les staffs, la mise en place des dispositifs de lavages de mains avec du savon lors des assistances, la sensibilisation des bénéficiaires sur les gestes barrières.

project_name: Facilitation de l'accès des enfants déplacés internes et communautés hôtes aux services d'éducation dans trois régions du NIGER
project_objective:
Le système éducatif nigérien reste impacté par des crises humanitaires multiples et complexes, de nature chronique pour certaines et aiguë pour d’autres : crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle, catastrophes naturelles et épidémies auxquelles s’ajoutent des mouvements de populations dus essentiellement aux conflits dans les pays voisins et aux conséquences d’attaques perpétrées par des Groupes Armées Non Etatiques (GANE), sur le sol nigérien. 
Or, l’éducation, perçue comme outil essentiel de formation du capital humain, peut jouer un rôle fondamental dans la réduction des risques de catastrophes naturelles et de conflits. Elle peut contribuer à accroître la résilience des communautés face aux risques de catastrophes naturelles et de conflits, protéger les enfants des dangers et de l’exploitation, de disséminer des informations vitales et d’atténuer l’impact psychosocial des situations d’urgence en offrant une structure essentielle à la stabilité, le rétablissement pacifique et l’espoir en l’avenir.
Dans le cadre du présent projet, ICAHD International entend contribuer aux cotés des partenaires de l’éducation à faciliter l’accès à un nombre plus important d’enfants à l’éducation au Niger.  En effet, La communauté internationale a réaffirmé son engagement en faveur d’une éducation inclusive et de qualité pour l’après 2015 et ceci, à travers le Cadre d’action pour l’Éducation 2030, adopté au cours du Forum mondial sur l’éducation, tenu à Incheon en Corée du Sud en mai 2015. Cet engagement nécessite une mobilisation soutenue de tous les acteurs pour construire des systèmes éducatifs solidement intégrés dans le processus de développement durable des nations. Il s’agira pour ICAHD International de souligner son intervention à travers des actions  en lien avec :
- Le Renforcement des capacités des structures techniques affectées à faire face aux chocs et le développement des plans de prévention, de gestion et de réponses aux risques de catastrophes et des conflits armés. 
- La facilitation de l'accès des enfants d’âge scolaire (4-17 ans) à une protection de qualité dans un environnement sûr et protecteur ;
-  Le Renforcement des capacités des acteurs de protection et du personnel d'encadrement en vue de fournir une protection de qualité dans un environnement sûr et protecteur ;       
- Le Renforcement des capacités des communautés dans la protection des enfants dans les écoles ciblées.                                                                                                                                                         
  Au terme du projet, ce sont quelques 37 891  personnes dont 19 203 PDI et 18 688  personnes de la communauté hôte, qui seront concernés par les interventions de ICAHD International dans les trois régions d’intervention.

project_name: Building Resilience of Conflict affected communities through a multi-sectoral approach for Women, men, Boys and Girls in Yobe and Borno states.
project_objective: The project will focus on the recovery of the crisis-affected populations through the provision of inputs for improved agricultural production as well as income generation activities for the development of sustainable livelihood opportunities. Action Against Hunger will contribute towards improvement in food security, nutrition status and improve household income for the most vulnerable people in the targeted locations through pro-poor economic empowerment initiatives and improved all year round agricultural production of diversified nutritious foods. The proposed project aims at improving the capacity of the vulnerable populations to be less dependent on aid and transit to a more sustainable livelihoods. The project will foster the resilience of Affected Communities by developing social cohesion through developing social networks and resilience of the displaced and integration with the host communities by developing social protection programs. The rebuilding and creation of community assets, as well as basic service infrastructure, which will build the capacity of communities to cope with crisis; infrastructure development includes, health facilities and WASH infrastructure as well as retraining and strengthening existing systems of government and capacity for relevant Ministries, local authorities and State actors to respond to the needs of conflict-affected populations. The project will prioritize the needs for different age-groups and sex will be prioritized and the protection of beneficiaries will be ensured during the implementation of activities.

project_name: Protection of rights and freedoms of the population affected by conflict in Eastern Ukraine  in the context of the COVID epidemic
project_objective:
The multicomponent project, designed for protection and advocacy of rights and freedoms of the population affected by the conflict in Eastern Ukraine and consists of 3 components:
Component 1. Operating Hotline for the conflict-affected population on wide range issues.including consultations on a wide range of issues related to COVID-19
Component 2. Legal support for the conflict-affected population, especially in the context of legislative changes related to COVID-19
Component 3. Expert support to the governmental bodies and Advocacy of rights and freedoms of the conflict-affected population

project_name: Provision of Basic Emergency Integrated Primary Health Services for vulnerable and underserved IDP, Host and Returnee populations, in Aweil North, Aweil South, Terekeka and Magwi Counties
project_objective:
Impact Health Organization (IHO) proposes the Provision of Basic Emergency Integrated Primary Health Services for vulnerable and underserved IDP, Host and Returnee populations, in Aweil North, Aweil South, Terekeka and Magwi County project under the South Sudan Humanitarian plan in the year 2021. The project will meet the cluster response activities with aim to improve access to and utilization of essential health care services by all people in need, in order to reduce excess morbidity and mortality.  According to the Interagency assessment, as well as IHO needs assessment in Magwi Eastern Equatoria, Terekeka County, Central Equatoria, Aweil North and Aweil South County, Northern. Bahr el. Ghazal South Sudan, concluded that the health systems in the four locations were not only challenged with limited access to human resource medicine and other supplies but also limited access to blood transfusion services, obstetric care service, mental health services but also limited access to WASH services but the referral system is hampered by poor roads. The community has limited access to health education, Immunization coverage is still low. The leading causes of morbidity include Malaria, Pneumonia, and Watery Diarrhea among children, HIV/AIDS and Tuberculosis.
The IPC analysis December 2020 classified Aweil south under IPC phase 5, Terekeka, Aweil North under IPC phase 4 and For May-August 2020 projection analysis it was reported that the acute malnutrition situation of Magwi County is likely to deteriorate during the lean season. With exception of Magwi County, the 3 counties of Aweil South, Aweil North and Terekeka have been hit by heavy floods that have left scores displaced and the health system and access to health services in dire state.  In order  to encounter the above risks,  the project seeks to decrease excess morbidity and mortality rates from illnesses, such as malaria, diarrhoea, acute respiratory infections, and vaccine preventable illnesses, such as measles, IHO undertaking managment of illiness including malaria RDT screening  and treatment and as well as measles vaccination campaign. The project will also provide access to life-saving essential healthcare, including mental health to women, men, girls and boys, including ability challenged persons including deliveries conducted by skilled birth attendants, provide OPD consultations, provide mentally ill persons with MHPSS services and SGBV health. To reduce vulnerability of women, men, girls and boys at risk of mortality and morbidity as well as protection incidents/threats in priority areas the project will undertake protection monitoring, advocacy, awareness raising and risk mitigation,  The project will integrate water, sanitation and hygiene, nutrition with health, including sexual and reproductive health to improve access and utilization of integrated life-saving quality health care services.  To reduce the suffering of girls, boys, women, men, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other persons with specific needs at risk of, or who experienced violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect, including gender-based violence, the project will increase access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled, mental health disorders and the elderly. To strengthen the feedback mechanism, the project will consult the population groups targeted to receive assistance throughout the entire cycle of the response by establishing community feedback mechanism and lastly the project will strengthen coordination and contextual analysis of needs by working closely with the state ministry of health an county health departments to meet the emergency needs of 19483 individuals (Men 3897, Women 4871, Boys 5260 and Girls 5455) 20% Terekeka, 25% Magwi, 30% Aweil South and 25% Aweil North.

project_name: Emergency food security and livelihood response for Aweil South County, NBeG
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to grapple with food insecurity crisis; between October and November 2020, 34 counties across the country were classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity. Greater Upper Nile region had 20 counties classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4), Greater Bahr el Ghazal region had 10, and Greater Equatoria region had 4 counties classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4). Of the remaining counties, 51 were classified in Crisis (IPC Phase 3), and 12 were classified in Stressed (IPC Phase 2). In the first projection period of December 2020 to March 2021, 22 counties were classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4), with the number likely to increase to 33 counties in the second projection period of April to July 2021.
In Northern Bahr el Ghazal state, Aweil south county was projected to further deteriorate to IPC phase 5 with an estimated population of about 13,849 people likely to face famine between April and August 2021.
The high levels of acute food insecurity in the country are driven by flooding, insecurity, population displacements, declined crop production, diseases and pests (including the desert locust that affected parts of East Africa), the economic crisis, the effects of COVID-19, limited access to basic services, and the cumulative effects of prolonged years of asset depletion and loss of livelihoods. 
The continuing currency depreciation and associated impacts on commodity prices and incomes coupled with the effects of COVID-19 continue to erode the purchasing power of vulnerable households who rely on markets to purchase food and other basic needs. Seasonal scarcity of food, the flooding in 2020 (with limited recovery from the previous floods and Aweil South localised cyclical foods from River Wathmouk that bursts its banks ), and the much lower than required humanitarian food assistance in the face of increased needs, will likely result in an increase of acute food insecurity during the projection periods, especially during the lean season.
In line with the FSL cluster priorities, Help restore Youth (HeRY) is proposing an integrated emergency food security and livelihoods intervention in Aweil south county covering all the 8 payams; Tiaraliet, Gakrol, Tarweng, Panthou, Nyieth, Watmouk, Ayai and Nyocawany.
The project targets 8,079 HHs with interventions including; distribution of emergency livelihood kits; vegetable, crop, fishing kits and farming tools intended to stimulate food production to save lives while building resilience.
Agricultural production shall be integrated with nutritional education focusing on food preparation and utilisation  demonstrations to support households improve nutrition especially for expectant, lactating  mothers and children under five years of age.

project_name: Strengthened Coordination and support for WASH services to most vulnerable populations in Jonglei State.
project_objective:
African Development Aid Interventions in this component are designed to increase demand for health services by educating individuals, households, and community and local leaders so that they can play their roles more effectively. The Project employs expanded health mobilization strategies that promote awareness, information, and advocacy to promote behavior change, adoption of healthy norms and practices and structural orientations, including supporting appropriate policies.
African Development Aid will collaborate with the ministry of health to sensitize PHCU, CHWs and WASH Committee members on Community Lead Total Sanitation and cascade to the household level. The Project will continue to promote access to improved water sources, sanitation and hygiene at community, schools and households.  The Project will continue collaborating with other stakeholders to promote WASH activities and advocacy to strengthen the linkages and working collaborations. 
The project will also build the capacity of WASH Committee members to develop community action plans on CLTS and for sub-committees comprised of the women, PWD, Youths, men and the elderly to monitor implementation. These structures will use community dialogue days and community outreaches to reach out to community members. 
Through strategic partnerships, we will continue to capitalize on existing opportunities to make a lasting contribution to improved health outcomes with full community ownership focusing on: building local skills and supporting systems for sustainability; improving health service demand, access, and quality, reducing barriers for most vulnerable groups,  and leveraging social determinants of  health to improve health outcomes. The Project will continue this relationship with the states, counties and Payams but engage even much more with each of them in a dialogue that ensures that project resources will achieve the highest level of efficiency and effectiveness in contributing towards agreed goals and objectives.  
A lean local staffing structure will be maintained to provide the skills needed for effective technical assistance. Senior managers will ensure that work plans are implemented in accordance with WASH Cluster guidance and with stringent adherence to time tables and budget ceilings. The location that characterizes ADA WASH with a target of 28,000 beneficiaries will be maintained and its contributions, with a focus on continuity of critical services rather than on expansion and scale up.

project_name: Access to emergency SNFI and durable solutions for displaced populations of Greater Equatoria and Jonglei State
project_objective:
YEDA will target 26,600 indivuduals with cash and in-kind modalities in Morobo, Yei and Mundri East Counties, and only in-kind in Terekeka, Pibor and Nagero, due to lack of functional markets and access constraints.
The response modality is informed by YEDA’s previous experience, and the need to scale-up CVA as an avenue to recovery&resilience. All interventions will be carried out following Covid-19 preventive measures; social distancing, use of PPE and preventive messaging through IEC. YEDA will maintain static presence in Mundri East, Pibor and Yei Counties, which will also allow delivering assistance to the other targeted areas through mobile response within two weeks from alert.
Beneficiary targeting will be guided by the SNFI Cluster criteria; PLWs, children <5, the elderly, PWN/PWDs (30%), high number of dependents, multiple displacement, lack of ties with the local community/purchasing power, GBV and COVID-19 risks associated with SNFI needs. 
The response will improve access to safe and appropriate S/NFIs to 12,000 new displacements/people with new vulnerabilities, improve the living conditions of 4,800 vulnerable individuals in protracted displacement/host populations through ES upgrade and NFI replacement and 2000 through CVA, support vulnerable 5,400 returnees and affected host community with ES upgrade and NFI replacement and 1,800 with CVA, and assist the 600 most vulnerable returnees/host communities with durable solutions through construction of 100 transitional shelters, and increase the ability of  people to respond to new shocks through CBIs, including CFW and multipurpose cash vouchers.
For in-kind response, pipeline items will be requested upon approval of SNFI analysis report by the SNFI Cluster coordinators, and delivered in areas without access to local market/shelter material. The CVA will include the creation of a multi-purpose cash fund for procurement of shelter materia/NFIs from the local market, allowing vulnerable families to repair their homes, and ensuring appropriate shelter, protection and dignity. Since in remote areas framing material is not accessible due to protection concerns, hence the project will include a small CFW component targeting 200 individuals for training in shelter construction by the YEDA local shelter expert, with secondary benefits for host communities (financial empowerment and conflict risk reduction). Risk of conflict over land will be mitigate by identifying land ownership/tenure arrangements and local mechanisms for settling land disputes, involving all relevant local authorities and local stakeholders to handle eventual cases of disputes, and training staff, volunteers and communities in HLP access rights.
Multi-purpose cash vouchers will be distributed in two istallments of $70 and $30, allowing households to purchase SNFIs as per their priority. FSPs will be mapped out in the project sites, and distribution facilitated by YEDA staff. Female heads of household and PWDs will be prioritized, to ensure financial empowerment of intended people and GBV risk reduction.
To measure the project success and take evidence-based decision on the course of action, continuous monitoring and end evaluation will be conducted jointly with community members/local leaders as part of a Response, Feedback and Complaint Mechanism, on weekly and monthly basis.
Coordination with the SNFI cluster through the SFPs on by-monthly basis, and with other humanitarian partners utilizing humanitarian hubs in Mundri, Pibor, Yambio and Yei on monthly basis in order to take part to joint responses, will minimize duplication, and promote integrated response, gender and protection mainstreaming, GBV referrals, risk mitigation, and incorporation of HIV/AID and COVID-19 prevention messages. As alternate WES SFP, Greater Mundri SiFP and DFC focal point for UN OCHA, YEDA will lead humanitarian interventions through the cluster methodology, lead humanitarian coordination and refer need/gaps to ICWG.

project_name: Improving and scaling up response to integrated quality essential health care services to vulnerable populations in Mayendit and Manyo Counties.
project_objective:
Two years after the signing of the revitalized peace agreement, its implementation has not reduced the humanitarian needs of the South Sudanese people. South Sudan remained a protection crisis in 2020. Lack of durable peace and limited investment in basic services are holding people back from stability and sustainable development.(HNO2021)
In 2020, communities were hit hard by the triple shock of intensified conflict and sub-national violence, a second consecutive year of major flooding, and the impacts of COVID-19. Some 1.6 million people remained internally displaced and another 2.2 million as refugees in the region. (HNO 2021).
The health situation has further worsened due to last year’s intensified conflict and sub-national violence, a second consecutive year of major flooding, and the impact of COVID-19. In 2021, the Cluster will target 5.2 Million People in Need (as per 2021 HNO).
According to OCHA’s Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) for 2020, there are over 51,000 people with significant humanitarian needs in Mayendit County, representing approximately 95% of the county’s total population, according to population estimates listed in the HNO. Mayendit is listed as one of nine counties in most “dire” need of health services (HNO 2020).
Mayandit was among the areas that were vastly affected by flooding in Unity State. An inter-agency flood assessment mission that was conducted comprising of a CCCM team revealed 1,652 individuals displaced by the current flooding in Mayandit were coming from different Payams including Madol, Malkuer, Pabuong, and Bathjiop.(IOM CCM Sep 2020).
Mayendit is Vast with very poor communication, road and referral network. The area is flood prone during the rainy season. 
CASS is the current implementer of primary health care services in the County with a network of 12 health facilities and one outreach site with Funding from HPF.
CASS with funding from health cluster intends to strengthen primary health care services, emergency preparedness and response in the county by reaching, 100% of the IDPS (12,066) and 100% of Displaced (12,066) and 100 % of the host community (31,128) a total population of 55,260 (Male 27,995, Female 27,265)
 This will be done through provision of primary health care services at 1 PHCC (Mayendit), 2 PHCU’s (Paboung, Madol) and 1 mobile team. 
Manyo County borders the South Kordofan and White Nile regions of Sudan to the north and west respectively, Renk and Melut Counties to the east, and Fashoda County to the south.(HNO 2020)
The cumulative impact of this interruption to services has been a significant humanitarian burden. OCHA’s Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) for 2020 estimates that there are over 52,000 people with significant humanitarian needs in Manyo County. This represents 41% of the estimated population of the county reported in the HNO and reflects an increase compared to previous years. (CRSF 2020).
There is limited access to health and Nutrition services in Manyo County. No physical presence of humanitarian partners apart from CASS. Access to health facilities especially during rainy season is by speed boat which is very expensive. 
CASS is the current implementer of primary health care services in the County with funding from World bank. CASS support a network of 6 health facilities (3 PHCC and 3 PHCU’s). 
CASS with funding from health cluster intends to strengthen primary health care services, emergency preparedness and response in the county by reaching, 100% of the IDPS/ Displaced (6,947) and 50 % of the host community (1,269) a total population of 8,216 (Male 4206, Female 4,010).
During rainy season access to most of the facilities is through water transport using speed boat, the facilities are about 3 to 4 hours apart. The support from Health cluster will help improve referral, boost immunization services and access to primary health care services through 1 PHCC (kaka), 1 PHCU(Thorgwang)  and a mobile team.

project_name: Support for the prevention and treatment of malnutrition for girls and boys aged 6 to 59 months in the Far North Regions, Cameroon.
project_objective: The project tile “Support for the prevention and treatment of malnutrition for girls and boys aged 6 to 59 months in the Far North Regions, Cameroon” is proposed as response to the nutritional situation of the Far North Region where the GAM rate is 5.2% and SAM 1.4% alert threshold (SMART 2019). Firstly to provide a package of specific nutrition interventions such as: food supplementation, micronutrient fortification, breastfeeding practices, complementary feeding and treatment of global acute malnutrition. Secondly by nutrition sensitive interventions such as: food security, agriculture, WASH, child protection, basic health care services and family planning… Among all preventive interventions in health and nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) has a great potential in child survival with an average investment of USD 175 for each life protected. Positive Deviance Household (PDH) is a community approach based on treatment of MAM (household rehabilitation) through local foods and improve food security through the support of beneficiaries on the establishment of home   gardens to make vegetables and fruits available in order to better diversify their diet. Support the beneficiaries on the breeding of small cattle and IGA for their empowerment. Despite all these interventions, the problem of malnutrition is not only due to the lack of intervention or food scare in the region, it is also a matters  of foot habits and behavior  hence the importance of implementing all these preventive actions through social base communication change (SBCC) community-based treatment of malnutrition.

project_name: Provision of a daily school meal
project_objective: Provision of a daily school meal for 150,000 pupils in the EPP in the 8 IPC 3 and 4 districts

project_name: Provision of emergency food security and livelihoods support for vulnerable Agro-pastoralists households in Terekeka and Bor South Counties in Central Equatoria & Jonglei States.
project_objective:
The proposed project will provide training to the vulnerable households to enhance fishing, crop and vegetable production mainly for consumption at the household level and sale of surplus at local markets in selected payams of (Bor town, Kolnyang, Anyidi, Makuach, Jalle and Baidit) in Bor South County of Jonglei state and (Nyikabur, Tukoro, Yokara, Bori, Bokana and Lojora) payams in Terekeka County of Central Equatoria state which will create extra income for these vulnerable households. These payams are chosen due to their suitability for fishing, crop and vegetable production.
SAADO will target 9,000 households in Bor South County and 7,000 households in Terekeka County in this proposed response with emergency fishing, crop and vegetable kits support. The 2 locations have been selected because of the needs prevalent in these counties according to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) January 2021 which shows both Counties in IPC 4 extreme levels of food insecurity and the existence of ongoing food security and livelihoods supported by FAO-ELRP, Cash for Seeds, Livestock vaccination and treatment and WFP supported Food for Assets programming by SAADO in the proposed areas. The emergency livelihood kits will be obtained from the FSL cluster recommended FAO core pipeline.
 SAADO will put in place a mechanism for effective and participatory community vulnerability mapping in the selected payams and bomas and will use a comprehensive beneficiary selection criteria developed, discussed and agreed upon with the communities to include Men, Women, Boys and Girls. 
During community consultations at various levels, men, women boys and girls will be consulted to fully understand and appreciate the impact of the current crisis on vulnerable men, women and children that would further inform our proposed response. “Do no harm” and AAP principles will be applied throughout the duration of the project, so that any possible negative implications of the project at community level are addressed before they occur. This will be done through integrating a strong Communicating with Communities and Engagement (CCE) feedback mechanisms. 
The proposed project will build upon and complement SAADO's 11-year experience in implementing food security and livelihoods programmes in the proposed counties of Terekeka and Bor South Counties including; Terekeka County:  General food distribution (GFD), School Feeding Programme (SF), Food for Assets Project-2020 to 2022 (FFA) supported by WFP, Emergency Livelihoods Response Programme (ELRP) 2020 to 2023; Cash for Seeds project 2020 to 2023; Livestock vaccination and treatment supported by FAO 2018 to 2021. In Bor South County: Emergency Livelihoods Response Programme (ELRP) 2020 to 2023; Cash for Seeds project 2020 to 2023; Livestock vaccination and treatment supported by FAO 2018 to 2021.
SAADO’s proposed emergency response will also complement the lifesaving, livelihoods and nutrition activities carried out by other FSL partners in the two counties such as ADRA in Terekeka County and VSF-Germany in Bor South County of Jonglei state. The proposed activities are necessary and sufficient to achieve the stated cluster objectives for these interventions based on the relevance of each activity in increasing access to emergency food security and livelihoods support for the most vulnerable households in the targeted communities. The indicators selected are SMART and SAADO has in place a strong monitoring and evaluation system and mechanisms to measure these indicators and to ensure the intended results are achieved. The means of verification, such as monthly reports, distribution lists and regular field visits are strongly credible and are currently used by the organization in its MEAL processes across its field offices in the country.

project_name: Provision of WASH Services to vulnerable populations in Cox's Bazar District.
project_objective: The purpose of the intervention is to provide vulnerable populations with equitable access to safe water supplies, dignified and safe latrines and bathing facilities and to provide information on critical hygiene promotion information and training with the aim of changing behaviour away from potentially harmful practices. The provision of the services will focus on inclusive access for all and will consider especially the needs of women, children, the elderly and people living with disabilities. The target population are 243,151 Rohingya refugees living in 8 refugee camps and 100,000 Bangladeshi people living in Cox's Bazar district who are affected by the refugee influx.

project_name: Enhanced and tailor-made community engagement and strengthened accountability to the affected people in Cox's Bazar including in the Rohingya camps.
project_objective: Integration and institutionalization of C4D/Communication with Communities (CwC) approaches and interventions into health, nutrition, WASH, education, and child protection for sustained long-term and at-scale efforts. Strengthening the role of key influencers such as religious leaders towards increasing community ownership and participation in host and camps. In 2021, UNICEF will also focus on the integration and mainstreaming of Gender, Persons with Disability(PWD) and DRR in the key programme strategy and in behavioural matrix rapid community engagement and sensitization. C4D will develop key information package highlighting children in DRR. Enhanced and continued support to strengthen and reinforce community social accountability through information and feedback centres and closing the community feedback loop. Promoting social cohesion, confidence and resilience-building in the host communities through community engagement interventions in Ukhiya and Teknaf Sub-districts. As part of the global commitment, UNICEF will promote and operationalize Accountability to Affected Populations(AAP) theory and concept across the organization in Cox's Bazar including in C4D for enhanced accountability and broader organizational strategy with tailor-made and contextualized AAP interventions and plans i.e IFC. Supporting the capacity building efforts of local governance structures to improve results for children at the community level through the Local Governance for Children (LGC) programme.

project_name: GBViE Response, Prevention and Risk mitigations among Refugees and affected host community in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
UNICEF will improve the access of adults, adolescents and child survivors to quality services  through, i) capacity development, mentorship and coaching of service providers, ii) strengthening institutional systems to provide multisectoral services, iii) maintaining 21 safe spaces for women and girls in camps and host community to provide services and referrals, iv) engagement of community to address negative social norms, v) Mitigating GBV risks in sectors and through safety audits, vi)  strengthening Child and adolescent survivors initiative and vi) advocacy for equitable access to justice and social services. 
70,000 women, men, boys and girls including persons with disabilities, will be reached with GBV response, risk mitigations and prevention interventions, targeting 80% from refugees and 20% host population to enhance social cohesion.
Of which, 10,000 girls, boys and women will access Multi-sectoral GBV services (Case Management, Psychosocial support, referral for medical, legal and safety) in survivor-centred approach and in the best interest of the child, while 8,000 women and girls will be engaged in structured skills activities to mitigate GBV risks and to build their resilience and 20,000 women and girls will receive dignity kits to uphold their dignity and reduce GBV risks.
Community outreach mobilizers, volunteers and community groups will play a crucial role in reaching 45,000 women, men, boys, girls, religious and community leaders, Manjis and other stakeholders with messages on COVID-19, GBV prevention and risk mitigation, using EMAP, SASA and other strategies to address negative social norms, and mitigate GBV risks and other forms of violence among children and women. 
UNICEF will preposition front liners and supplies for emergency preparedness and response during natural disasters while strengthening engagement with WASH, Nutrition, CP and Education sectors to further mitigate GBV risks in programming.  
UNICEF will continue to enhance accountability to the affected population by strengthening PSEA and feedback mechanisms.

project_name: Improving access to quality Primary healthcare services including Sexual and Reproductive Health, Mental Health and Psychosocial support and GBV prevention for women, men, girls and boys in Luhanska and Donetska Oblasts, Eastern Ukraine (GCA and NGCA)
project_objective:
Building on MdM experience implementing life-saving humanitarian interventions since 2015, MdM will target 85,724 beneﬁciaries through the provision of multi-disciplinary quality healthcare services for the most vulnerable people affected by the crisis and exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic in Eastern Ukraine (Luhanska and Donetska Oblasts, GCA and NGCA). The project will particularly target vulnerable women and girls affected by on-going conﬂict by ensuring access to Sexual and Reproductive Health services and access to GBV prevention and response services. The project will also contribute to addressing the high level of mental health problems, as well as COVID-19 related additional mental and psychological burden on the population and healthcare workers, among internally displaced persons and host populations in conﬂict affected areas. 
In order to achieve this objective, MdM will target the most vulnerable communities and categories of people affected by the conﬂict (such as women and girls, elders, people with disabilities, people exposed to conﬂict -related stressors). 
The outreach approach in remote locations of Luhanska and Donetska GCA close to the line of contact will ensure access to PHC, treatment and referral to specialized care with due respect to the COVID-19 prevention measures. Outreach teams will promote a comprehensive approach by providing PHC, MHPSS and SRH services and will be integrated within the existing health facilities. 
The local health system will also be supported through targeted donations of supplies and equipment, including life-saving COVID-19 equipment and consumables, and health staff will be trained (with a speciﬁc focus on SRH and MHPSS) to face the current lack of capacity building opportunities in conflict-affected oblasts. The training plan will be developed in line with the ongoing Health Reform and by creating synergies with public training institutes and/or hospitals. Modalities and operational design of the capacity building events will fit the reality based on the current epidemiological situation in the area. 
Building up on MdM experience in the area MdM will continue supporting local capacities to provide a comprehensive package of services to survivors of GBV, which was dramatically increased in the conflict affected areas, including the most vulnerable populations, and raising awareness on health and mental health consequences of GBV, promoting the development of a sustainable referral pathway. 
MdM mental health and psychosocial interventions based on evidence-based methodology will be expanded and disseminated to support the needs of persons who deal with psychological problems such as stress, fear, feelings of helplessness, as well as practical readjustment challenges related to conﬂicts within families, issues with communities and livelihood diﬃculties. Moreover, MDM will provide crucial mental health and PSS assistance for health workers who faced COVID-19 related stress, etc. 
MdM advocacy efforts will continue to ensure the integration of MHPSS into PHC in the framework of current Health Reform. In Luhanska NGCA, where MdM has been registered since 2017, MdM will continue to support PHC facilities close to the contact line, which have been particularly affected by the conﬂict. MdM will pursue donations of life-saving medical equipment to Emergency departments of hospitals with a focus on Children’s health and SRH. The distribution of maternity and new-born kits initiated in 2019 will be expended. In addition, through COVID-19 related donations of medical equipment, supply and consumables MDM will support the health system in Donetska and Luhanska NGCA. 
To ensure the response and considering the relatively costly actions (donation of medical equipment, etc), MdM has an efficient operational presence in Donetska and Luhanska GCA, and Luhanska NGCA. For 2021 and strategically, MdM is in the process of negotiations to have access to and presence in Donetska NGCA.

project_name: Integrated Mobile and Static Protection Response in South Sudan
project_objective:
This project is expected to provide integrated GBV mobile and static services through an integrated approach with Health in remote and hard to reach locations in Longechuk, Nasir and Maiwut Counties of Upper Nile State in South Sudan where static and mobile services are not accessible. RI provides life-saving services in Upper Nile State since 2006 and key sectors are Health and Nutrition, FSL, WASH and Protection. Health services are delivered through Medical Mobile Units (MMUs). Since September 2020, RI piloted an integrated model comprising Medical Mobile Units and Mobile Protection Units to deliver life-saving services in Longechuk and Nasir in Health and Protection (GBV).  In other Counties, RI continues to provide other services except Protection. So far, RI is running a total of 7 MPU teams out of which 2 are in static locations with support from BHA. Both MMUs and MPUs follow the same schedule and rotation, however, gaps still exist. Despite numerous constraints, lesson learned shows that mobile service delivery is the most appropriate approach to deliver services to communities that have been displaced or are unable to access the static services due to a myriad of barriers and risks that hinder safe access to humanitarian services.
RI proposes to form additional MPU teams to address GBV gaps in the 3 locations, alongside adding CP to its current mobile units. In Maiwut, although it’s one County nationally on the ground it is split by two administrative areas, Jekow is IO controlled while Maiwut Centre is controlled by the government. It’s important to ensure that both areas receive similar services to manage local political dynamics. A total of 12 MPUs will be formed-3 in each projection site comprising of 1 static team and 2 mobile teams. A target of 40,650 beneficiaries will be reached by this project. Key activities will include; static and mobile case management, PSS and referral services, outreach activities on GBV, risk mitigation activities (dignity kits distribution and training and supporting women and girls with fuel efficient stoves and establishment and of WGFSs. This proposed project is built on RI’s baseline protection survey conducted in all three proposed locations in December 2020. 
It is against this background that RI proposes to implement mobile GBV services to improve community access to life-saving GBV response and prevention services in remote areas of Upper Nile State.

project_name: Integrating WASH in nutrition, health and protection response to ensure equitable and safe access to water, sanitation and hygiene among vulnerable IDPs, host communities and returnees in Upper Nile State, South Sudan.
project_objective:
RI’s proposed 2021 Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) intervention is designed to contribute to improved health and nutrition outcomes, addressing key factors of wider
community disease outbreaks, vicious circle of malnutrition, timely and equitable access
to safe WASH and mitigation of related GBV, amongst 250, 000 IDPs, returnees and
vulnerable host communities in Upper Nile state in South Sudan.

The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with RI’s
health , nutrition , protection and FSL programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to improve people’s lives and well-being, thus contributing to South Sudan WASH Cluster objectives and the 2021 Humanitarian Response. Recognizing WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH
services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based
provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. RI’s integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition by targeting SAM and MAM children and families and contribute to controlling disease outbreak.

Additionally, RI will ensure equitable, timely and sustainable access to improved safe and adequate water and sanitation facilities that address the vital WASH needs, public health and protection issues, respect sphere standards; engage communities in design and ownership, improve knowledge on appropriate hygiene practices to reduce and prevent WASH-related diseases including cholera, AWD, typhoid, skin diseases etc. RI will construct gender-sensitive water supply systems, mainly solar powered, boreholes through manual drilling, extensions to bring water points closer to vulnerable households,  schools, health and nutrition facilities, rehabilitate damaged / nonfunctional boreholes, increase access to safe water and mitigate the risk of GBV at WASH facilities. Comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) and Health & Nutrition facility staff. RI will work with existing WUCs to reinforce technical skills for water point O&M (operations and maintenance), establishing new WUCs where relevant. Solid waste management training will be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns. RI will also construct incinerators for medical waste disposal at health facilities.

At the household level, RI will construct 1,500 household/family shared latrines, with owner contribution, amongst displaced, returnee, and conflict-affected communities to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. Latrine construction will adhere to protection standards as elaborated in the guidelines for WASH Cluster partners in South Sudan. RI will also promote hygiene awareness aimed to support behavior change in hygiene practices through house-to-house hygiene education sessions, training of hygiene volunteers, and distribution of household package for famine prevention which will include: one 20-liter bucket with tap for proper water storage, one 20-liter bucket without tap or jerry can for water collection, filter cloth, water purifier (PuR), and soap for three months consumption.

project_name: Provision of Sustainable and Life- saving WASH services for people in need in Yambio and Ezo Counties (WES), Aweil South County (NBEG) and Bor South County (Jonglei State)
project_objective:
This project targets 4 Counties in 3 States.  These include Yambio and Ezo Counties in Western Equatoria, Aweil South County in Northern Bahr El-Ghazal and Bor South County in Jonglei. 
The project aims to integrate WASH response with Health to reduce morbidity and mortality caused by water borne/related diseases, increase access to WASH services and build WASH resilience through offering sustainable solutions (long lasting water points), establishment of water committees, registration of water points in national registry, GBV mitigation, disability inclusion and conducting conflict sensitivity analysis prior to implementation.
The prolonged conflict and limited Government investment have had a devastating impact on the country’s infrastructure and basic service delivery. The main drivers of WASH needs include limited physical infrastructure, sub-national violence and recurring flooding in many parts of the country. In addition, spikes in national violence, COVID-19 that has had a devastating and multi-faceted socio-economic impact on people, including severe economic contractions, soaring in prices of basic commodities, loss of livelihoods particularly in urban areas, increased protection risks, and disrupted access to basic services. Therefore, living standard and wellbeing of an estimated 5.6 million people will be negatively impacted by lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in 2021. (HNO, 2021)
The project targets the host communities, IDPs and Returnees. The total beneficiary figure is 57,872 people. The targeted recipients of this response are disaggregated as follows: 11,574 Women, 17,535 Girls, 11,401 Men and 17,362 Boys. The beneficiary figures are inclusive of the persons with disabilities in the communities. The intervention aims to reduce morbidity and mortality through integrating WASH response with Health, provide safe, equitable and dignified access to WASH services through increasing access to quality WASH services by drilling boreholes, rehabilitation of non-functional hand pumps, rehabilitation of solar powered Mini Water Yards,  establishment of water committees, mitigating GBV, promotion of community hygiene and sanitation through CLTS triggering, WASH related disease prevention including COVID 19, solid waste and excreta management. 
The project will build resilience of beneficiary communities by strengthening existing structures and establishing long lasting water points.

project_name: Promote access to quality and inclusive education for IDP children living in the PoC sites in South Sudan through an integrated approach
project_objective:
The project will promote Access to Basic, Quality, Protective and Inclusive education to 10,400 children (5,304 G; 5,096 B) aged 3 to 18 living in the PoC of Bentiu, Malakal, Bor and Juba 1 and 3. The program will seek to incentivized enrollment and attendance to learning, reduce risks of cognitive underdevelopment while providing access to safe and protective learning environments through a wash and protection build-in components. 
The intervention seeks to build on the good practices and results achieved through the UNICEF education project implemented by INTERSOS between 2018 and 2020, where over 75, 000 children including 28,000 girls were enrolled in pre-primary, primary, secondary and accelerated learning schools in 5 different states including Upper Nile, Jonglei, Unity, Central Equatoria and Western Equatoria. The   project aims at addressing holistically the needs of schools to ensure a protective environment and will include three different components of WASH, protection and education. Through the WASH components it is expected the spread of COVID19 and cholera as well as other water born diseases will be reduced in the school environment. The education component will seek to ensure the return of all children to school after COVID19 trough the rehabilitation of TLS to ensure the respect of social distancing and the provision of PPE for learners and teachers. Additionally to responde to the generalized problem of school dropout, learners in South Sudan face due mainly to displacement, general poverty and early marriage/ teen pregnancy for girl that has been exacerbated during the pandeminc the project foresees  the payment of teachers’ incentives, the provision of education material  and the provision of remedial classes for children having dropped out. Furthermore, support to accelerate learning programs to ensure older teenagers have access to educational opportunities is also foreseen.  This will be done in close collaboration with Juba University given the overall good results of the partnership in the former project. 

Finally, the project hopes to enhance the protection environment of learners through the presence of caseworkers in schools identifying and directly observation  vulnerable cases at risk of drop out or other child protection threats while closely leasing with general protection services for a complete response. Additionally the case worker in the school will support   the training of teacher in live-skills, PSS and PSEA mechanism.

project_name: Prevention and response to S/GBV through Risk Reduction, Women Empowerment and Enhancement of Access to Services and Opportunities in Jonglei and Unity state.
project_objective:
In  Jonglei and Unity state, the risk of GBV is continuously exacerbated by a myriad of factors including  prevailing cultural norms, traditional gender roles, regional conflict, a highly militarized environment, and the frequent cattle raiding and revenge killings among the different clans.
 Protection concerns such as generalized violence and insecurity, limited access to food, water and firewood, expose women to a high risk of GBV, specially in county with high severity needs such as Pibor, Akobo, Nyriol, Canal/Pigi and Ayod. There is, therefore, an urgent need to enhance GBV prevention efforts with additional strategies to mitigate risks, such as fuel strategies and protective accompaniments. Furthermore, lack of recognition of GBV as violation of fundamental human rights continues a culture of impunity throughout the region. Therefore, notwithstanding the advancing of the peace process, it is important to continue to raise awareness, reduce prevalent stigmas in the communities and increase identification and documentation of GBV cases as well as providing survivors access to psychosocial support and other services for their recovery and healing. 

Through this project INTERSOS aims to strengthen the prevention and response to GBV risks in some of the counties with the GBV severity index of 5 (Akobo and Pibor), 4 (Ayod, Canal/Pigi, Nyirol) and 3 (Mayendit). The intervention will seek to  adress the immediate needs of GBV survivors  through the provision of safe spaces, Case management services, PSS  and the enhancement of access to services and opportunities, empowering women across locations through skill acquisition trainings. To promote durable solutions a strong component of GBV prevention has also been foreseen in the form of mass awareness through a community approach and the engagement of men on accountable practice training.

project_name: Provision of Comprehensive and Integrated Health Services to Conflict-affected, Displaced and Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
As part of continued efforts to improve access to life-saving health care services among internally displaced, conflict-affected and vulnerable population, International Medical Corps (IMC) will continue to provide a comprehensive package of health care services following static and mobile approaches in South Sudan. IMC’s main strategy is to support static essential health services that is complemented by regular outreach to increase and expand equitable coverage and access, especially for mobile or hard to reach populations with intermittent periods of stability and weather-constrained access. Aligned with the 2021 HRP for South Sudan, the National Action Plan for Health Security (NAPHS) 2020 – 2022, and the Global HRP for COVID-19, IMC’s health care interventions are designed to: (1) increase access of approximately 139,731 conflict-affected, displaced and vulnerable people in Juba, Malakal and Wau displacement camps, as well as in Canal/Pigi, Akoka, Baliet and Panyikang Counties to preventive and curative health services, (2) improve the capacity of the country’s health system to cope with the COVID-19 pandemic, other disease outbreaks and emergencies, and ultimately, (3) to prevent and reduce excess mortality and morbidity in the country.

IMC will continue to provide 24/7 free primary and secondary integrated health care services across its 26 supported health facilities in the aforesaid locations. These services will include outpatient consultation for the management of common causes of morbidities and mortalities, endemic diseases, trauma and injuries; health education at the facility and community level; provision of essential pharmaceuticals and medical commodities; support to the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI); sexual and reproductive health services; and community surveillance and referral services to ensure continuum of care. IMC will also support the health facilities through maintaining trained health care providers; further capacitating them and carrying out monthly clinical supervisions by IMC Medical Doctors, Clinicians and Site Managers. Moreover, IMC will also integrate MHPSS into primary health care activities across its 26 supported health facilities, in line with the WHO and Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) guidelines. 

Additionally, while ensuring the continued provision of lifesaving health care services to the populace, IMC, being the co-lead of TWG on Case Management, IPC and Safe Burial, will further bolster the capacity of 3 COVID-19 supportive care facilities / isolation units in the country to cope with the increasing number of COVID-19 cases, namely, Dr John Garang Infectious Disease Unit in Juba, Malakal Teaching Hospital and Al Muktah PHCC in Wau. IMC will also form and deploy an Emergency Rapid Response Team (ERRT), in close coordination with MoH, that can quickly respond to health emergency/potential outbreaks, including Cholera, AWD, Measles, COVID-19, Ebola and conflict-related injuries/wounds, as well as to natural calamities.

Meanwhile, due to the volatile security, continuous displacement of the population, and difficulty in accessing static health care facilities in Canal/Pigi, IMC will deploy four Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) across the five Payams of Korwach, Wunlith, Alam, Khorfulus and Atar. The MMUs will support the need for increased capacity and accessibility of locally available health services in six static facilities, which IMC is currently supporting under the UNICEF/World Bank-funded program. Each MMU will consist of 1 Clinical Officer, 1 Nurse, 1 Midwife, 1 Vaccinator, 1 Data Recorder and 1 CHW. They will be integrated with the Mobile Nutrition and Protection teams of IMC, which will also be positioned in Canal/Pigi. The integrated Units will visit the different hard-to-reach Bomas and IDP camps within the five Payams. To increase the chances of patients coming from distant communities, each Unit will remain on the spot for 2 full days, providing services.

project_name: Emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene support to vulnerable communities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Western Bahr El Ghazal, Lakes and Warrap States of South Sudan
project_objective: The South Sudan humanitarian needs overview of 2021 notes that an estimated 5.6 million people will be negatively impacted by lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices within the year. Some of the main drivers of WASH needs include limited physical infrastructure, sub-national violence and recurring flooding in many parts of the country. As of the 2021 WASH severity mapping, 1.9 million people spread across different counties and states in the country are currently in WASH severity level 5 while 4 million are in severity level 4. Centre for emergency and Development Support (CEDS) is proposing to carry out WASH interventions in Aweil East, Aweil South and Aweil North Counties in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Toni East and Tonj South counties in Warrap State, Cueibet and Rumbek counties in Lakes states, Jur River and Wau counties in Western Bahr El Ghazal in response to the humanitarian needs to contribute to mitigation of WASH related morbidities and mortalities. CEDS intends to reach a total of 45,720 beneficiaries (19,217 males, 10,401 females and 16,002 children) with different WASH interventions for a period of 12 months as from March 2020. We propose to carry activities including but not limited to minor and major rehabilitations of boreholes and water points in and around nutrition facilities, form or re-establish and strengthen the capacity of water user committees, construct and or rehabilitate sanitation facilities and carry out hygiene and sanitation promotion in the targeted locations.
