The WASH and Nutrition integration is intended to rehabilitate and construct boreholes and intuitional VIP latrines at or near OTP/TSFP sites, conduct training of Nutrition team members on minimum WASH aspects and distribute lifesaving WASH NFIs/ household famine prevention packages to the mothers/Caregivers of children with MAM/SAM cases. CEDS will intentionally ensure that Covid-19 preventive measures are integrated within this programming and Covid-19 preventive guidelines and regulations are observed throughout these project implementations. It is expected that after this intervention, the targeted communities will have access to safe and accessible portable water, as well as dignified and context appropriate sanitation facilities. It is also expected that the targeted communities will have knowledge and will be practicing good hygiene and sanitation practices.

project_name: ''NDIGA'', Appui à la continuité de l'apprentissage inclusif et de qualité pour les enfants affectés par les situations d'urgence
project_objective:
Le projet vise à contribuer pour la continuité de l’apprentissage pour les enfants affectés par les situations d’urgence au Burundi. Le dernier HNO réalisé en 2020 pour l’élaboration du HRP 2021 a fait état de 157 283 enfants dans le besoin de services adaptés leur permettant d’accéder à un enseignement inclusif de et de qualité. Le secteur de l’éducation a été secoué par des catastrophes naturelles qui ont endommagé plusieurs centaines de salles de classes ainsi que du matériel d’apprentissage et d’enseignement, conduisant à la perturbation des activités scolaires dans plusieurs localités du pays. En plus, la pandémie COVID 19 devient de plus en plus une menace dans le système éducatif. Il est très urgent de renforcer la prévention de cette pandémie dans les écoles, notamment à travers l’amélioration des conditions d’hygiène dans les écoles et particulièrement de l’accès à l’eau potable dans les écoles.
En 2021, la réponse humanitaire dans le domaine de l’éducation se focalisera sur deux objectifs :
- Garantir à 157 283 enfants en âge scolaire (de 3 à 16 ans) affectés par les mouvements de populations et autres chocs ou issus des populations hôtes un accès équitable à une éducation inclusive de qualité et adaptée à leurs besoins socio-émotionnels.
- Renforcer les capacités de 6 621 personnes du secteur éducatif dans la gestion de l’éducation dans les situations d’urgence.
La réponse proposée par l’UNICEF s’est référée aux planifications d’autres acteurs du secteur de l’éducation et se focalise sur les besoins qui ne sont pas couverts par ces planifications. Elle privilégiera la coordination de l’assistance avec les autres secteurs humanitaires, notamment les secteurs WASH et Protection de l’enfant. Elle consistera essentiellement à l’appui de la réhabilitation d’infrastructures scolaires endommagée, à l’aménagement de salles de classe temporaires dans des localités affectées par les situations d’urgence en attendant la construction de salles durables, à l’appui matériel en kits scolaires pour les enfants les plus affectés par les situations d’urgence, ainsi qu’au renforcement des mécanismes de référence pour faciliter l’accès des élèves affectés aux services de prise en charge psychosociales et de protection adaptés à leurs besoins. Dans tous les sites qui seront construits ou réhabilités, nous collaborerons avec nos collègues de WASH pour y installer des dispositifs de lavage des mains et autres kits d’hygiène, et nous collaborerons avec nos collègues de la Protection de l’enfance pour assurer que les besoins de protection des élèves sont pris en compte. Notamment, dans les activités de construction/réhabilitation et d’aménagement des dispositifs hygiéniques, une attention particulière sera mise sur la prise en compte des besoins spécifiques des enfants vivants avec handicap et des filles.
La réponse proposée couvrira les provinces priorisées par le HRP 2021, à savoir Bujumbura, Cankuzo, Kirundo, Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana, et Ruyigi.

project_name: Positionnement des stocks de contingence sectoriel pour les reponses humanitaires
project_objective: Le secteur eau-hygiène et assainissement (EHA) a considéré pour les besoins d’assistance les groupes de population suivant : les personnes déplacées internes (PDI), les rapatriés pour l’année 2021; et les autres personnes vulnérables aux épidémies de choléra ou généralement d’origine hydriques. Chaque groupe a été pris suivant un indicateur de besoins liés au secteur. Les besoins en eau potable et assainissement de base. Les 139 674 personnes rapatriées actuels et planifiés sont pris en compte par le secteur EHA dans le calcul de la population dans le besoin. Cela pour atténuer la pression exercée par ce groupe sur le minimum d’infrastructure en place afin d’éviter une chute de la situation WASH surtout dans les provinces avec un faible taux d’accès en eau potable. Ces données vont être superposées aux effectifs des rapatriés actuel et planifiés pour déterminer les PIN des rapatriés seulement dans les provinces avec un taux de couverture en eau potable inferieur à la moyenne nationale (Kirundo, Muyinga, Cankuzo, Ruyigi et Rutana).Les personnes déplacées internes suite aux catastrophes naturelles tel que les inondations, glissement de terrains, vents violents et autres. Ce groupe comme les rapatriés exerce une pression sur les infrastructures EHA des communautés d’accueil et selon les analyses de vulnérabilité/besoins conduites, ce groupe se retrouve dans des conditions de précarité d’hygiène. Le secteur considère alors la totalité de 131 336 PDIs comme étant en besoin. Concernant les urgences dues aux épidémies des maladies d’origines hydriques dont le cholera ou diarrhées pour les enfants de moins de 5 ans s’inscrit dans le groupe des autres populations vulnérables. Le secteur considère le maximum de cas enregistré au cours des 5 dernières années (2016 -2020) entre le choléra et les diarrhées des enfants. Ils totalisent un effectif de 269 667 personnes. Toutefois, il faut noter que les interventions du secteur WASH vont au-delà des cas de choléra ou diarrhées enregistrés donc dans les communautés d'origines des cas, les projections se réfèrent aux règles de planifications de l’OMS sur les risques de contaminations en fonctions des cas enregistré (1cas met 500 personnes à risques de contaminations de cholera ou autres maladies diarrhéique), ceci est compté parmi les autres personnes vulnérables prises en totalité dans le calcul du PiN. Pour chaque province, le PiN est la somme des PiN déterminé pour chaque éventuelle situation d’urgence de cette province. La population globale dans le besoin pour le secteur WASH est donc traduit par la somme des populations dans le besoin d’assistance humanitaire des différentes provinces du pays. Le secteur WASH alors par le present projet positionner les stocks de contigence pour se rassuerer qu'il a la capacite de contenir tous les besoins humanitaires en 2021, principalement dans l'approvisionnement en eau, l'acces au sanitaires et les sensibilisations sur les bonnes pratiques d'hygiene.

project_name: Contribution à la réponse aux urgences sanitaires au Burundi
project_objective:
La situation des enfants au Burundi est caractérisée par une forte mortalité infanto juvénile estimée à 78‰ naissances vivantes (EDS 2016-2017) avec prédominance de causes évitables ou traitables. La mortalité maternelle reste élevée (334 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes, EDS 2016) et demeure extrêmement préoccupante malgré une baisse par rapport à l’EDS 2010 (500 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes). Les Burundais de tout le pays, en particulier les femmes et les enfants, restent vulnérables aux crises humanitaires due à des niveaux élevés de pauvreté. Cette situation précaire est aggravée par les catastrophes naturelles (c.-à-d. inondations, glissements de terrain et déficits pluviométriques), comme le choléra et les pics de paludisme ainsi que le risque qu’Ebola se propage dans le pays. Après une diminution marquée des besoins humanitaires en 2019, ces derniers ont connu une augmentation au cours de l’année 2020. La survenance des désastres naturels, les impacts socio-économiques de la Covid-19 sur les plus vulnérables et les retours des réfugiés burundais en provenance des pays limitrophes ont contribué à cette augmentation. A cet effet, les projections pour 2021, les désastres naturels (désormais réguliers) et une intensification du processus de rapatriement sont attendus tandis que des maladies comme le choléra et le paludisme demeurent des risques importants en raison de leur caractère endémique. L'impact de la Covid-19 devrait également se faire sentir pendant l'année 2021. Prenant en compte ces besoins et risques, le nombre de personnes en besoin d’assistance humanitaire est passé de 1,74 million à 2,3 millions (donc 1,06 millions ciblés par les acteurs humanitaires) de personnes, entre 2020 et 2021, représentant ainsi une augmentation de 35 pour cent par rapport à l’année dernière. 
Sur le plan épidémiologique, le Burundi connait depuis plusieurs années des épisodes d’épidémies de paludisme (dans sa partie Nord Est et Centre), de rougeole dans les camps et orphelinats, de plaies ulcéreuses dans les provinces de Muyinga, Maramvya et Mwaro et le choléra (dans la partie Ouest du pays), principalement sur la rive du Lac Tanganyika. Le paludisme a notifié 4.4 millions de cas en 2020 contre plus de 8,8 millions de cas en fin d'année 2019. Le Burundi a notifié 1,195 cas de choléra en 2019 contre 139 en 2020. Le risque de nouvelles flambées de choléra reste élevé en raison des mauvaises conditions d'hygiène. Le pays a notifié près de 10.000 cas de plaies ulcéreuses principalement dans les provinces de Muyinga, Mwaro et Maramvya. Malgré les bonnes performances en matière de vaccination, on note une stagnation, voire une régression des couvertures vaccinales dans certains districts. Cette baisse de performance pourrait expliquer les deux épidémies de rougeole de 2020, avec un total de 1,879 cas notifiés et une vingtaine de districts sanitaires en épidémie. Lors de l’atelier d’élaboration du HNO, l’analyse de la situation a conduit le secteur de la santé à identifier les populations affectées comme étant celles de 16 des 18 provinces du pays (Bubanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cankuzo, Cibitoke, Kirundo, Makamba, Muramvya, Mwaro, Rumonge, Rutana, Gitega, Karusi, Ngozi Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana et Ruyigi). Ces provinces sont priorisés du fait de la récurrence des désastres naturels et leurs conséquences sur les déplacements internes, les maladies à potentiel épidémique, les impacts socioéconomiques de la Covid-19 et l’insécurité alimentaire qui contribuent à la sévérité des besoins intersectoriels dans ces localités. Le plateau technique des services de santé maternelle et néonatale est insuffisant et le pays dispose de capacités limitées d’offre de soins obstétricaux d’urgence de base complet. Les ratios de décès maternels et taux de décès néonataux sont excessifs selon les données de la surveillance intégrée de la maladie et la riposte, soit 288 décès maternels et 2,036 décès périnatals notifiés jusqu’à fin 2020.

project_name: Renforcement des systemes de prevention et de Reponse au Cholera sur les cotes du lac Tanganyika en province Rumonge
Provision of child protection services to children and caregivers living in central Equatoria  state ( Lainya and Yei counties) and Jonglei State  ( Pibor and Akobo Counties)
project_objective: The project intends to deliver  life saving static and mobile  services to the most vulnerable children and their caregivers affected by floods, conflict that causes displacement ,diseases and famine. This comprises of returnees, Host community and internally displaced population ( men women, boys , girls , young people and adolescents) living in Jonglei state ( Akobo and Pibor counties ) and Central Equatoria State ( Lainya and Yei counties). The total target population is 28,000 most vulnerable individuals ( 10,000 girls, 9000 boys, 5000 women and 4000 men). The primary purpose of the project is to address compounding effects of converging factors i.e severe food insecurity /loss of livelihoods, economic decline, protection threats and lack of services which contributes and aggravates the prevalence of violence against children This project will focus on both preventive and responsive aspects of Child protection and work closely with GBV , FSL, Health ,S/NFI WASH, Education and Nutrition partners to ensure an integrated approach for a holistic service delivery that entrenches resilience  and sustainability of the services rendered to the affected children and their care givers affected by multiple shocks. The intervention will be guided by the IASC guidelines for child protection  ,national SOPs and cluster strategy.The response is strategic to the attainment of Cluster objectives and align to activities, indicators, and outcomes of the HRP 2021.The project activities focus on mitigating child protection risks, preventing and responding to child protection cases through; CFS programming, capacity building of frontline service providers on CPiE, Case management  including FTR services , Structured/non-structured PSS, community Outreach and dialogues,  and safe referrals. It is expected that by the end of the project period, lives of vulnerable women and girls,young people and their caregivers will be saved, they will have increased access to multi sector services , life skills and positive coping mechanisms entrenched in them.

project_name: Integrated Response for Conflict-Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) WASH
project_objective: The WASH component of the program is aimed at improving the overall health and wellbeing of 39,000 individuals including 11,340 IDPs. Water supply, Sanitation and hygiene education and promotion activities are designed to complement Nutrition and Livelihoods programs in order to deliver comprehensive health and wellbeing support to the targeted beneficiaries.

project_name: Provision of basic health care and services to children and mothers in the North West and South West regions.
project_objective:
The situation in the North West and South West (NWSW) regions of Cameroon escalated in October 2016, when the Anglophone population started making political demands leading to protests and strikes. This unrest emerged from historically perceived marginalisation of Anglophone Cameroonians. A year later, on October 1st, 2017, secessionists declared independence from the Republic of Cameroon. Since then violence has escalated and Internally Displaced People (IDP) targeted are living in the forest or host communities in villages, urban or peri urban areas in the NWSW regions. These IDPs lack basic social services. The most vulnerable population are women, pregnant women, newborn babies, children under five, young children both boys and girls. This security situation in the NWSW has had a direct impact on access to health services for vulnerable women and children. Those functional are not sufficiently equipped. Due to mass displacement with many people seeking shelter in remote forested areas access to even basic health services is almost impossible. Furthermore, more than 40 per cent of Community Health Workers (CHW) are no longer working in insecure health districts.
UNICEF alongside partners will deliver essential health services aimed at increasing access to basic health maternal, newborn and child-care and services where health facility is functional and mainly in communities and hard to reach areas. 
OVERALL GOAL/OBJECTIVE
Increase coverages of basic maternal, newborn and child health preventive and curative and promotional package amidst the COVID-19 pandemic 
SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES 
•	Increase vaccine coverage in routine immunization in the 6-59 months (pentavalent 3, measles) 
•	Increase vaccine coverage for routine immunization in pregnant women
•	Provide treatment the three main childhood killers for children under 5 years old ( Malaria, diarrhoea, and Respiratory tract infections)
•	Provide prevention care to pregnant women and Children: anti anaemics, Vit A supplementation, deworming
•	Provide malaria prevention tools: LLINs and Intermittent preventive treatment to families 
•	Improve quality of maternal and newborn care with the provision of basic kits for mothers and newborns, training and coaching of health care providers
•	Build capacities of health care providers, health facilities and communities on COVIC-19 prevention and infection prevention Control;
Direct beneficiaries: 
-	1,000 newborns 
-	7,000 Pregnant women 
-	50,000 children under five 
-	20,000 families/households corresponding to about 100,000 people

project_name: Psychosocial Support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse for children affected by the North-West and South-West crisis in Cameroon
project_objective:
Since the crisis escalation in late 2017, the North-West and South-West regions (NWSW) have experienced a drastic deterioration of living conditions, putting children and women at high risk of various forms of abuses, exploitation and violence. 
Girls and boys are the primary victims of the current crisis. This translates into serious violations of their fundamental rights and constant insecurity, causing both visible and invisible trauma in the short and long-term, separation from their families and limited access to basic social services such as education, for the past three years. Being direct or indirect witnesses of violence linked to the conflict, their wellbeing, both physical and psychological, is fundamentally at stake.

As of September 2020, the crisis in the NWSW has caused the displacement of an estimated 200,000 children within those two regions, and an additional 155,794 children are estimated to be displaced in West, Adamaoua, Littoral and Centre regions. Adolescent boys and girls, children with specific needs and unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) remain the primary categories at risk among all affected groups of IDPs, returnees and affected host communities, especially in rural areas and hard-to-reach areas. Lack of access to basic social services including child protection services remains a key risk factor especially for children in rural areas, hard to reach areas and most remote localities such as the ones along the Nigerian border where access and insecurity prevent protection actors from implementing any program. 
In order to protect children affected by armed conflict from violence, abuse and exploitation, as a priority and main intervention, UNICEF will work on the offer of services and provide psychosocial support to 340,000 children and caregivers. Psychosocial support will be provided to caregivers as well when necessary and to the extent possible so that they are better equipped to protect their children. 
As a direct corollary, based on previous years trends, an estimated 10,200 unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) are foreseen to be identified during the implementation of the project. All the 10,200 children will benefit from case management, appropriate alternative care arrangements, support and individual follow-up while due to the difficult access and insecurity UNICEF plans to reunify a minimum of 990 unaccompanied or separated children with their family.
UNICEF with its implementing partners will run sensitization campaigns with the aim to reach out to 169,000 persons, with specific attention to parents to pass on messages on child protection in emergencies, trauma early warning signs for children affected by armed conflict, effects of family separation, GBV in emergencies and other types of violence children are at risk of at the community level so that parents and community members can play an active role in child protection in emergencies.
UNICEF and its partners will also provide support to an estimated 1,200 conflict-affected children who do not have a birth certificate, as they are particularly vulnerable to various forms of discrimination and abuse because of the lack of birth certificates.
In urban and peri-urban areas, both in NWSW and outside where IDP children and families from NW/SW are present, support will be provided to 2,700 families identified as at-risk to protect children from child labour and exploitation. Support will be provided to children already engaged in child labour (including WFCL, such as sexual exploitation and recruitment by armed groups and armed forces) with case management and referral to multisectoral services.
UNICEF as lead of the Child Protection Area of Responsibility will continue to consolidate the coordination, build capacities of members and ensure alignment and complementarity of interventions in the field of child protection.

project_name: Reinforcing sustainable WASH response to affected population in Lac Chad Basin of Cameroon
project_objective:
This project aims to strengthen water, sanitation and hygiene response to affected population in Far North region of Cameroon with a focus on IDP camp, communities hosting IDP and returnees. In water domain, rehabilitation of boreholes and construction of small water supply network powered with solar energy will be prioritized. On hygiene and sanitation issues, communities approached for total sanitation will be implemented at municipality level. Construction of community latrines and showers will be limited to IDP sites. Hygiene promotion with distribution of minimum WASH kits will be implemented in target communities. The area targeted cover the division of Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari. With these interventions, this project targets 60,000 people for access to safe water, 44,000 people for acces to adequate basic sanitation and 150,000 people reached with critical WASH supply (including hygiene items) and services. 
This project will also include a component relative to capacity building of WASH actor at regional level on key issues such as design, installation and maintenance of solar system for water supply, cholera response, flood response, protection and gender mainstreaming in WASH sector.

project_name: Prevention of all forms of malnutrition and Treatment of life-threatening forms in the context of Lake Chad Basin, Cameroon
project_objective:
Children, adolescents and women have access to diet, services and practices that support the nutritional status in the humanitarian context of Lake Chad Basin, Far North Region
43,786 children (21,455 boys and 22,331 girls U5 admitted for SAM treatment)
88,000 children (43,120 boys and 44,880 girls) U2 admitted in the Homebased Food fortification programme
125,000 people (M/W) sensitized including 25,000 women trained for SAM detection 
(mother MUAC)
50,000 adolescent girls receiving weekly iron and folic acid supplements
25,000 pregnant women receiving weekly iron and folic acid supplements
Activities or outputs
•	Caregivers of children aged 0-23 months are supported to adopt recommended infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices, including both breastfeeding and complementary feeding
•	Children aged 0-59 months have improved nutritional intake and status through age-appropriate nutrient-rich diets, micronutrient supplementation, home-fortification of foods and deworming prophylaxis.
•	Adolescent girls have access to community-based package of interventions that includes at a minimum: iron and folic acid supplementation, deworming prophylaxis, nutrition education, counselling and support.
•	Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers - with special attention to pregnant adolescent girls and other nutritionally at‑risk mothers – have access to a package of interventions that includes at a minimum: iron and folic acid/multiple micronutrient supplementation, deworming prophylaxis, weight monitoring, nutrition counselling, and nutrition support.
•	All children aged under five years in affected areas are screened regularly for the early detection of severe wasting and other forms of life‑threatening acute malnutrition and are referred as appropriate for treatment services.
•	All children aged under five years suffering from severe wasting and other forms of life-threatening acute malnutrition in affected areas benefit from facility and community-based services (Fix or mobile) that provide effective treatment.

project_name: Improving Access to Primary Health care services in Vulnerable Population in North West and South Regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
For the past 4 years, Cameroon has seen a socio-political crisis emerge in the North West and South West Regions of the country known as the Anglophone Regions. The unrest which started in 2016 has progressively escalated into an armed conflict between secessionists and government security forces, disruption of basic services and public infrastructure, and subsequent large displacement of population which has led to increased food insecure homes. 10 % of IDPs are living remote areas, often in farm huts, bushes and the forests. (MSNA September 2019).The onset of covid19 pandemic in   March 2020, introduced new threats to children and vulnerable communities worsening the situation in the NW/SW regions.   
Morbidity (malaria, cough and diarrhea), poor sanitary conditions remained accelerated in 2020. Access to health care still remains a challenge due to insecurity and persistent attacks on healthcare as this constituted a huge threat to the availability of essential health care to the populations. 71% of the facilities are functional with majority (58%) of IDPs not able to access health care due to distance (45%) and financial constraints (17%). Furthermore, weak disease surveillance system has put the population at risk of epidemics with late detection and limited response capacity with repeated pockets of cholera outbreak have been reported in SW (MSNA, 2020). 26 % of persons affected by the NW/SW crisis are going. 
SHUMAS intervention will be designed to reduce morbidity and mortality of children under 5 years, adolescent boys and girls and pregnant women affected by the crisis in 4 health districts in the NW/SW for 12 months through consultations and treatment of 3 killer diseases in children (Malaria, Diarrhea and Pneumonia), provision of Vitamins and deworming medications, vaccination coverage, provision of baby and delivery kits and psychosocial support. 
The aim of this project is to contribute towards the reduction of morbidity and mortality rates among children under 5 years, adolescent boys and girls and pregnant women in the affected 6 districts in the NW (Kumbo East, Kumbo West, Ako, Ndu and Nkambe) SW (Mamfe) regions of Cameroon. This will be by improving access to basic curative and preventive health care services for vulnerable IDPs and host through provision of primary and secondary sexual and reproductive, mental health services, epidemiological surveillance and psychosocial support for 12 months.
And the specific objectives are;
•	To improve timely access to basic curative and preventive health care services in children less than 5 years (3000M, 5000 M), pregnant women (1000) affected by crisis in 6 health districts in NW (Nkambe, Kumbo East, Kumbo West, Ndu, Ako) and SW (Mamfe) region for 12 months through consultation and treatment for 3 killer disease, distribution of LLINs, sensitization on Essential Family Practices.

•	To strengthen epidemiological surveillance/ Vaccination coverage from below 50% to 80% in children 6-59months, adolescent boys and girls, pregnant women affected by crisis in 6 health districts in NW(Nkambe, Kumbo East, Kumbo West, Ndu, Ako )SW (Mamfe) region for 12 months through measles vaccination, outbreaks and search for loss to follow up children.

•	To improve access to Sexual Reproductive Health services (Assisted deliveries by skilled personnel/ management of pregnancy related complications) in adolescent girls (500) and pregnant women (500) affected by crisis in 6 health districts in NW (Nkambe, Kumbo East, Kumbo West, Ndu, Ako) SW (Mamfe) region for 12 months through provision of baby and delivery kits, ANC cards.

•	To provide mental health and psychosocial support to trauma victims affected by crisis in 6 health districts in NW (Nkambe, Kumbo East, Kumbo West, Ndu, Ako) SW (Mamfe) region for 12 months through referral and counter-referral of GBV survivors.

project_name: Improve access to quality inclusive education through equipped school infrastructures including wash in school in 22 communities in the Far North.
project_objective: This Project derives from the Cooperation Programme between UNICEF and the Ministry of Basic Education. It aims to improve the learning environment in 22 schools (70 classrooms) from 03 subdivisions by acting on two levels. Firstly, the project intends to alleviate the overcrowdness of classrooms and provide additional infrastructures for the enrollment of out-of-school children. Secondly, the project will improve access and utilization of quality wash in school infrastructures by constructions of 86 latrines and 22 water points.

project_name: Psychosocial Support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse for children affected by the Lake Chad Basin crisis, including support to children formerly associated with armed groups, in the Far North Region
project_objective:
The year 2020 was marked by a clear increase in the number of protection incidents affecting children in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga in the Far North. In addition, significant flooding, as well as measures to mitigate the risks of the spread of the Covid-19 pandemic, have exacerbated pre-existing child protection problems such as GBV. Significant population movements continue to be recorded adding to the pre-existing difficulties of access to basic social services for children as well as the lack of opportunities for adolescents and youth to develop their potential in a region where 64% of the current displaced population are children. 
This project will support formal and community-based CP systems, placing particular emphasis on (i) capacity building of adolescent girls and boys as agents of change for conflict and violence prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of intergenerational and interreligious dialogue, (ii) capacity building of deconcentrated CP structures in a humanitarian/development Nexus approach focusing on case management, referral, psychosocial support, and family/community reintegration of vulnerable children girls and boys   and (iii) increased coordination at all levels, under the leadership of the Regional Delegation of Social Affairs (RDSA). 

The key result of the project which is in line with the objectives of the protection sector, is that 132,000 conflict-affected children and caregivers are protected from violence, abuse and exploitation in armed conflict settings and live in a protective environment in the targeted localities of Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga, Mayo Kanyi and Mayo Danay Divisions in the Far-North Region of Cameroon. 
The project builds on previously established dynamics and community structures and will provide PSS to 132,000 children and caregivers. PSS will be provided both through a one-on-one approach (through social workers or other trained child protection actors) and through community-based approaches, such as CFSs, adolescent clubs, and intergenerational dialogue.
Implementing partners will continue to identify unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). Based on previous trends and on partners capacities, the project plans to assist around 1,250 UASC including 60% of new cases, ensuring and providing those children with psychosocial support, alternative care arrangements, reunification with their families of origin and reinsertion in their communities. All will benefit from close individual follow-up. 
To address both social norms but also to ensure smooth community reinsertion, the project will work at strengthening community mobilization and will organize community activities around prevention of GBViE including activities to abandon child marriage, to promote intergenerational dialogue and social cohesion. Based on the projections, a total of 70,000 persons (women, men, girls, boys) are planned to be reached through community mobilization activities. Partnership with religious and traditional leaders, and chiefery including female stakeholders will be an important channel to display messages and address complex issues. In complement, the work on youth empowerment and participation will enable to merge with the other members of the communities and promote prevention and protection of children from violence and exploitation.
The issue of conflict-affected children without a birth certificates was confirmed to still be a major issue. 
The project aims at supporting 10,000 conflict-affected children in obtaining a birth certificate. 
150 former CAAFAG are expected to be identified, will receive PSS, and will be supported UNICEF will continue to closely work with civil society implementing partners, providing them with capacity building, supporting the setting up of SOPs for case management and referral. UNICEF will also strengthen the coordination mechanism led by RDSA.

project_name: Access to protective learning routines for 90.000 conflict and extremism affected children and adolescents through operational primary and Secondary schools hosting IDP and refugees children in the Far North.
project_objective:
The project targets 90.000 children and adolescents in school and vocational training. It will build the capacities of 1.900 teachers from primary and secondary schools on PSS and C/DRR, for them to use adequate pedagogical and in-class practises. In order to generate foster school-based risk informed humanitarian action and evidence generation, the project will also conduct a Protective Learning Environment study. 
The needs need to be expanded: how many children are in primary and secondary school and what are the challenges faced by teachers who work in context of insecurity? 
Include cash transfer for the most vulnerable children (poor/disabled)Include materials for children with disabilities (for motorial and learning).

project_name: Safe and equitable access to inclusive education for 616,187 conflict-affected girls and boys age 3 - 17 years and an additional 15,000 youth in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States of North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
OVERALL OBJECTIVE: 
Strengthen access and improve inclusive, quality and equitable basic education for 616,187 conflict-affected displaced, returnees, host communities, school-aged girls and boys aged 3 to 17 years and an additional 15,000 youth in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe states of North-East Nigeria.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVE: 
1.	Strengthen basic education for 616,187 children (ensuring 50% girls, 130,460 children who are 3-5 years old and 20,000 children from Tsangaya and Islamiyah schools ) through the provision of essential teaching, recreational materials, support to enrolment drive campaigns (EDC) and Girls for Girls (G4G) programme.
2.	Improve the capacity of 12,324 teachers and volunteer teachers (at least 40% females) in psychosocial support, education in emergencies, inclusive education, quality Early Childhood Development (ECD), classroom management and pedagogy (including Teaching at the Right Level/TaRL to improve learning outcomes).
3.	Increase access to safe learning spaces with gender-sensitive WASH facilities and water for the benefit of 438,300 children.
4.	Provide access to learning, training and skills development for 15,000 youth (50% females; aged 15-24)
5.	Enhance the response and protection capacity of education service providers in school governance in emergencies through establishing and/or activating Monitoring of School-based Management Committees (SBMC) in targeted LGAs and building the capacity of 822 SBMC (40% females; 4,110 members) on SBMC effectiveness and provision of education services to out-of-school children, education-in-crisis, and education for vulnerable children including girls and children with disabilities with a focus on hard-to-reach areas.

project_name: Building Resilience to Shocks through Capacity Strengthening and Reducing the Economic Impact of COVID-19
project_objective: The COVID-19 contingency fund      will strengthen systems and the capacity of government and communities to respond to and recover from the impact of COVID-19 and build resilience to future shocks.  This 18-month programme will support 1,000 households, 500 farmers, 400 youths and 40 Savings and Loans Groups (SLGs) in Yobe State.  The proposed  €1,000,000 programme will build the absorptive and adaptive resilience capacities of 2,900 community members (725 men, 725 women, 725 male youth, and 725 female youth) whilst engaging with communities and local leadership to create the conditions to facilitate systemic change.  Mercy Corps will leverage its expertise in fostering resilience in complex environments and strong track record of relief and early recovery programmes in Yobe State, enabling a smooth and rapid start-up to implement the COVID-19 response programme.

project_name: Inclusive Protection Assistance to Crisis-affected Populations in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
Continuing to address complex, acute, and multilayered needs, HI proposes to foster a safe and protective environment with the provision of specialized and community-based services to Rohingya refugees and host community through a twin-track approach: 
- Accessible community static points established and operated, where community members, including persons with disabilities and adolescents, access group PSS/Protection, rehabilitation, SRHR, and COVID-19 awareness sessions. 
- Mobile units composed of qualified Social Workers, nurses and midwives, physiotherapists, psychologists and protection officers deployed to identify and provide tailored individual assistance, and community based sessions, to the most vulnerable individuals and their caregivers.
Both tracks are supported by community based volunteers. In addition, to strengthen community based protection of persons with specific needs, the project will mobilize peer to peer support groups of women and men with disabilities. The project will provide technical support to ensure they are sustainable, and empowered to claim their rights, which will strengthen community structures, and foster their resilience.
This approach integrates safe and timely referrals to both internal and external services. It has been developed, reviewed and consulted with beneficiaries including persons with disabilities. It has proven effective to reduce barriers and empower communities to achieve their rights with safety and dignity.
To strengthen disaster risk reduction, HI mobilizes seasonal Protection Emergency Response Unit in several camps, participating in an effective early action system to any sudden-onset disaster. 
COVID-19 protection measures will continue to be adopted and its awareness will be prioritized especially for people with limited access to information.
HI will continue its active participation in Protection Working Group, Task Force, MHPSS Working Group, and Age Disability Working Group. With HI’s standardized and accessible Complaints Feedback and Response Mechanism, it ensures promotion of its PSEA policy.

project_name: Enhancing Resilience and Livelihood Opportunities for Affected Population through Agriculture and livelihood interventions in Idleb and Aleppo
project_objective:
The proposed project is aiming to contribute in achieving the SO3 and SO1 by achieve two goals:
1) Supporting the widows camps in addition to the most vulnerable populations (IDPs in Camps) in Idleb and Aleppo.
2) Enhancing wheat value chain in two governorates (Idleb and Aleppo), and consequently enhancing food security in the target areas through inter-linked components.
The project was built on achievements of the previous interventions of HIHFAD (irrigated farmland, a farmer association, agricultural inputs for the vulnerable households and free bread distributions) in the target areas.
10300 HHs in total will directly benefit from this project.
The project consists of five main components:
1) Supporting 800 vegetable farmers with supplementary irrigation costs (Using of diesel vouchers modality), access to irrigation channels located in the Al-Rouge plain, an area of 2 Donums of vegetables agricultural land will be supported for each farmer in addition to do a light rehabilitation to 20 km of the water canals which serving a 800 hectares of strategical agricultural lands in Alrouge plain area, the project engages cash for work scheme for the irrigation works.
2) Supporting the wheat value chain through purchasing wheat seeds from the local harvesting session, where the project is aiming to purchase 1000 MT from 1000 farmers (700 from Idleb and 300 from Aleppo).
3) Supporting 4000 farmers (2800 in Idleb and 1200 in Aleppo) with agriculture inputs (wheat seeds purchased from the local farmers and supplementary irrigation) to support the wheat cultivation in the Al-Rouge plain in Idleb and Albab Subistrict in Aleppo.
4) Providing training on good agriculture practice, storing, marketing and strategic planning for 1270 farmers and staff of the Farmers Associations in addition to members from the local entities at the area of Idleb and Aleppo as well.
5) Processing 455 MT of purchased wheat into 347 MT of wheat flour and distribute it as a fresh bread bundles over 4500 HHs, this component will target the widows camps at the targeted subdistricts in addition to the IDPs in camps for 6 months of distribution 26 days per month via contracting local bakeries.
GAP sessions will train Bas regarding the appropriate and recommended dosage and amount of pesticide and fertilizer to make sure they have good results and benefits of them and decrease the negative impact on the environment.
In order to avoid an escalation of any tensions and to enhance social cohesion, the project will clearly inform the selection criteria to the target communities, and let the communities understand that the vulnerable households are prioritized through the project. 
The FB Beneficiaries and worker in all of CFW activities will be selected from the IDPs and HC in coordination with the field local authorities via public registration and according to a specific criteria: 
-Households with member/s with disabilities
-Women headed household
-The families with no income source
-Age more than 18.
-Have the capability to carry out such works.
-Host families who are hosting IDPs
also HIHFAD will build on the already existing beneficiary committee in Al Rouge plain and the agriculture offices in Albab Local council, where HIHFAD will make sure that it includes people from the host community and the IDPs in addition to women in order to reach all groups in the targeted, where the selection criteria for the farmers will be:
1. Full access to land
2. Land size (in Dunum) between 5 to 10 Dunums for wheat and 2 Dunums for vegetables 
3. Settled in the relevant location for a minimum of 6 months in case of IDP.
4. Previous experience in relevant crop farming.
5. Access to the irrigation system for the vegetables.
6. Agriculture is the main source of income for the household.
where the priority will be given to the vulnerable households from the applicants.
the Project is considered under planned.

project_name: Time critical response to save  agricultural livelihoods and food  security in the Gaza Strip through renewable energy  sources
project_objective:
The overall objective of this project is to protect food production capacities and income 
sources in locations that are most at risk due to the chronic electricity deficit in the Gaza 
Strip. The rationale of this project is to target areas most impacted by the increasing 
electricity deficit in order to protect current levels of food and agricultural production, 
livelihoods and food security by providing vulnerable agricultural producers in the Gaza 
Strip with a consistent, clean and renewable source of energy to guarantee sufficient 
electricity for essential food production. The intervention pays particular attention to the impact of electricity deficit on female-headed households and the workload of women and youth. This intervention responds to the first need under 
the Agri Livelihoods section in the Food Security Sector Response Plan, which indicates 
the need for interventions that prioritize responses to the electricity shortage in the Gaza 
Strip. The intervention falls under Strategic Objective 3 of the HRP 2018-2022 as it invests 
in solar energy sources to ensure that targeted farmers have a consistent electricity supply 
as and when required in order to cope with frequent energy cuts as part of the protracted 
crisis. As an emergency intervention, this project aims to minimize damages and losses to 
domestic crop production in the current season and to enable normal levels of cultivation 
in subsequent seasons. In doing so, this project will protect agriculture based livelihoods, 
food security and domestic food production that are at risk given the chronic electricity 
deficit and will enable normal levels of cultivation if electricity supply to the Gaza Strip is 
further reduced.

project_name: Addressing acute malnutrition among vulnerable IDP and host communities in Gedo Region
project_objective:
The FSNAU Post Gu 2020 food security and nutrition survey for Somalia show improvement of the nutrition outcomes but still 1.14 million  are in need for treatment services and 1.16 million for preventive services. This number includes children under the age of five and pregnant and lactating women and girls. The national median GAM prevalence in children was reported to be around 13.8%. In Gedo the GAM rates are at serious levels of between 9.2% and 12.8%. PLWs and children are prone and vulnerable to the consequences and impacts of the lack of access to basic livelihood and other social facilities such as primary health care services, access to safe drinking water and sanitation services. 

Trocaire is implementing an integrated health and nutrition response in Gedo in four districts of Dolow, Luuq, Belethawa and Gabaharey covering host, IDP and marginalized communities in hard to reach areas. 

This project will focus on lifesaving management of acute malnutrition through provision of treatment services in line with the Somalia IMAM framework. This project will target approximately 18,453 malnourished boys, girls, pregnant and lactating women with OTP and TSFP services in twenty sites in the four districts as well as address some gaps in other sites in coordination with the nutrition cluster. Children with SAM with complications will also be supported within stabilization centers. Additionally, the project will focus on a preventive approach through education, sensitization and awareness on nutrition with a focus on IYCF targeting beneficiaries as well as their caretakers. Women being the main custodians of the family health will form a key target audience for community sensitization messages on IYCF .They will also form part of community volunteers that effectively manage the community based nutrition activities. Men will be involved in these IYCF community based activities since they are key decision makers in promoting early health seeking behavior. 

Activities proposed include the following: Screening  and referral for  acute malnutrition among children 6-59 months and PLW; treatment for Severe acute malnutrition with complications; treatment of acute malnutrition; treatment of moderate acute malnutrition for both children under 5 and PLW; community mobilization and sensitization at community level to promote adoption of age appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices; community mobilization and sensitization at community level to promote adoption of age appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices; individual IYCF counselling to both mothers and caretakers including fathers; hiring of one outreach team and staff to support TSFP/OTP services in Garbaharey; hiring of 10 additional community health and nutrition workers; capacity building of staff and community health and nutrition workers; and monitoring and evaluation activities.

project_name: Assistance for access to drinking, cooking and personnel hygiene water and emergency sanitation in the face of natural disasters and epidemics
project_objective:
In 2021, the WASH sector will target globally 540 678 people, including 131 336 internally displaced persons following natural disasters or other shocks as cholera epidemies, 209 471 vulnerable and members of host communities as well as 70 049 returnees. The assistance will be carried out according to two sectoral objectives which are as follows:
• Provide emergency WASH assistance to people affected by epidemics and natural disasters including host communities. This objective aims to provide drinking water and emergency sanitation infrastructure (latrines, showers) as well as to distribute hygiene kits to affected people. These interventions will make it possible to respond to essential WASH needs in order to guarantee survival considered to be physical and mental well-being, but also the protection and dignity of vulnerable people.
• Ensure access to WASH services for 131 336 people including internally displaced persons, members of host communities as well as people living in areas of return of returnees and those at risk of water-borne diseases. This objective aims to improve WASH services for communities in order to reduce the use of negative adaptation mechanisms such as the use of surface water (river and lake water), air defecation practices which constitute a risk of pollution of the sources as well as other bad hygienic practices favoring the occurrence and the persistence of epidemics.

project_name: Improving Child Protection for vulnerable populations in Somaliland, particuarly IDPs in Hargeisa and Togdheer
project_objective: In 2021 humanitarian response, Plan International will improve protection environment and promote child rights in Somaliland for IDP and vulnerable populations, particularly at-risk children. The country has one of the lowest child and gender indicators in the world with only one-quarter of girls – 24% aged 15-24 considered as literate, 45% married before 18 years and 98% subjected to female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C). The COVID19 quarantine measures to prevent and control the spread of COVID-19 exposed children and women to increased protection risks, particularly within the home, owing to increased stress caused by the outbreak, exacerbating existing gender inequalities and violence. Child Protection Areas of Responsibility in collaboration with UNICEF conducted a child protection survey in April 2020 showed more than half of the CP agencies (57%) reported an increase in physical violence particular on girls. There has also been increased exposure to violence especially to girls through FGM/C. According to the United Nations Population Fund, COVID-19 could have far reaching impacts on the effort to end FGM/C, with a potential 2 million FGM/C cases occurring over the next decade that could have otherwise been averted.  Plan will work with CSOs and other partners to effectively promote and support improving community-based child protection mechanisms. Key interventions will target young girls and boys, their parents and other decision-makers to raise awareness on child protection and GBV, establish and strengthen referral mechanisms for case management and other services including MHPSS and financial support, and capacity building and advocacy with local authorities and for national agenda on centrality of protection  (e.g. importance of child protection and campaigns on GBV, adoption of the positive discipline techniques, inclusion of children with disability) and distribution dignity kits. Plan and partners will also promote PSS for children and adolescents affected by crisis, support youth-led DRR initiatives, and establish girls groups to prioritize creating safe spaces for dialogue and peer friendships. Plan and partners will provide age-appropriate, gender-sensitive, and disability inclusive services that address the different impacts of emergencies on adolescents and young children, boys and girls and promote the potential for positive transformation of gender norms. Plan and partners will maintain child-friendly feedback and complaint mechanism and promote transparency across all activities.

project_name: WFP South Sudan Bor, Jonglei State Dykes and Road Repair Project
project_objective:
Every year in South Sudan, heavy rains cause widespread flooding which devastate lives and livelihoods of the nearby communities living alongside the River Nile’s banks. In 2020, seasonal floods reached unprecedented levels, affecting over 400,000 people in Jonglei and more than 125,000 people in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area. The floods caused damage to infrastructure, housing agriculture and livestock. 

The situation intensified in Jonglei in July 2020, when the dyke built to control the flow of the River Nile collapsed at multiple locations, exacerbating the rising flood levels in Bor Town and parts of Greater Bor. As a result, despite being at the height of the dry season, parts of Greater Bor remain flooded. Displaced households are unable to return and rebuild their home. Furthermore, significant sections of the main road that serves as the gateway from Bor to the rest of Jonglei are submerged by water, cutting off the main route to supply goods. Consequently, humanitarian access has been severely restricted and humanitarian support cannot reach the local populations in Bor. Access to this region is absolutely critical for WFP and all Logistic Cluster partners, who utilize the dry season to preposition supplies prior to the heavy rains, before access is further limited. Therefore, WFP and all humanitarian actors operating in Jonglei State require the flooded area to be drained, to allow for the rehabilitation of the dyke and road, to ensure communities can resettle and humanitarian actors, include WFP, can access the region, prior to the rainy season. Additionally, it is essential that this area is drained and restrictions lifted, so commercial access is possible. Providing commercial access will contribute to critical commercial and market growth in this region.

project_name: Accès inclusif et durable à une éducation de qualité pour les enfants et jeunes déplacés et de la communauté hôte affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions de Maradi et de Tillaberi
project_objective:
ette proposition de NRC s’aligne sur les principales priorités de la Stratégie nationale de réponse aux vulnérabilités du système éducatif 2020 en apportant une contribution spécifique aux populations les plus vulnérables dans le cadre des crises identifiées dans la Stratégie en termes d’Accès, de Qualité et d’amélioration de la Gouvernance dans le secteur de l’éducation dans les régions de Maradi et de Tillabéry. L’action vise à soutenir l'éducation de 25 000 enfants et jeunes âgés de 6 à 17 ans touchés par la crise et le déplacement, tout en atténuant la propagation de COVID-19. Le NRC privilégie l'utilisation des normes minimales de l'INEE pour assurer une programmation de qualité dans tous les résultats.
NRC facilitera la réouverture des écoles au sein des communautés d'accueil et à fournir l’accès à un environnement d’apprentissage de qualité à tous les enfants touchés, y compris les enfants des communautés d'accueil et les enfants déplacés/réfugiés. L'intervention du NRC pour soutenir l'éducation formelle comprend des actions relatives au renforcement de la résilience des parties prenantes, à la sécurisation de structures éducatives fonctionnelles et à la construction et l'adaptation des infrastructures éducatives existantes et de l'environnement scolaire afin de se préparer aux multiples risques qui peuvent affecter le système éducatif, y compris le risque de catastrophes naturelles et les risques sanitaires, par exemple par la construction/réhabilitation de systèmes WASH (eau, hygiène et assainissement). Afin de répondre aux besoins des enfants qui ont manqué l'école à cause du conflit et du déplacement, le NRC introduira des cours de rattrapage ou de soutien scolaire de courte durée ainsi que des PEA pour les élèves réfugiés, déplacés et vulnérables afin d'assurer leur réintégration, leur maintien et leur progression dans le système officiel, tout en étant en accord avec les directives du gouvernement d'accueil. L’intervention de NRC visera aussi à offrir des possibilités de formation professionnelle aux jeunes déplacés internes et aux jeunes vulnérables non scolarisés dans notre zone d'intervention ciblée au Burkina Faso. Cela se fera en soutenant l'accès, la qualité et l'offre d'éducation, et en soutenant la création d'entreprises pour les personnes qui terminent leurs études (mentorat).

Afin de garantir le respect et la dignité des personnes assistées et surtout de nous rassurer que nos interventions ne nuisent pas à leur bien-être (Do Not Harm), NRC veillera à consulter systématiquement les communautés bénéficiaires avant toute intervention et activités sur le terrain. Des mécanismes déjà mis en place dans certaines de nos communes d’interventions (Ligne téléphoniques, boites à suggestions…) seront d’avantage renforcée en 2021 au sein des écoles et des communautés afin que les communautés puissent signaler et reporter toutes formes de nuisances du fait de NRC ou de ses partenaires de mise en œuvre.
Notre intervention prend également en compte les questions de Nexus Humanitaire – Développement à travers le renforcement des structures de gouvernance et de dialogue scolaire, ou encore la mise en place des solutions durables dans nos interventions.

project_name: Réponse aux besoins en Eau Hygiène Assinissement des populations déplacées, retournées et des communautés hôte dans les zones affectées par les crises dans les régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua, Maradi et Diffa au Niger (MVT - MUL)
project_objective:
En se basant sur son implantation durable sur le terrain et son positionnement auprès des communautés dans les régions ciblées, ACTED continuera de soutenir les populations les plus vulnérables au Niger en 2021 avec des activités Eau Hygiène Assainissement (EHA). ACTED envisage de délivrer les activités suivantes : 
1/ Réhabilitation de 40 points d'eau :
Chaque point d'eau réhabilité bénéficiera à environ 500 personnes, pour un total de 20 000 bénéficiaires directs, comprenant principalement des populations déplacées et des communautés hôtes. les activités prendront place dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa, Tahoua et Maradi
2/ Sensibilisation aux bonnes pratiques d'hygiène et distributions de kits d'hygiène
activités auprès des ménages dans les 40 communautés. Les kits d'hygiène cibleront les ménages les plus vulnérables sur les plans sociaux économiques. En fonction de la situation des zones d'intervention (capacité d'absorption des marchés, sécurité et accès, ACTED pourra considérer de donner de l'argent aux ménages bénéficiaires plutôt que des kits ""in kind"". Cette analyse sera réalisée au début des interventions à travers des évaluations des marchés. D'autres évaluations des marchés seront conduites au cours du projet pour confirmer que la méthodologie est toujours la plus adaptée et que l'intervention (distribution d'argent en espèce) ne dérègle pas le marché local.
3/ Construction de latrines individuelles et communautaires 
activité dans les 40 communautés cibles susmentionnées.
4/ Mise en place de systèmes de gestion des déchets 
activitié dans les 40 communautés : construction de parcs de gestion des déchets et mise en place de comités de gestion des déchets

Il est attendu que ces activités ciblent les mêmes bénéficiaires que les activités de réhabilitation des points d'eau afin de fournir un soutien plus complet aux personnes affectées.  Sur le plan de l'accessibilité, les infrastructures, de par leur conception et leur localisation viseront à faciliter l'accès physique et à réduire les risques de protection pour les utilisateurs et utilisatrices. Des comités de gestion dont les membres sont issues de la communauté seront créés pour permettre aux bénéficiaires d'entretenir et de s'approprier les installations, les comités des gestion communautaires permettront aussi une meilleure redevabilité envers des populations affectées.
Plus largement, la réponse d'ACTED pour le secteur EHA fait partie d'une stratégie multisectorielle à destination des populations les plus vulnérables, qui couvre aussi e.g. la sécurité alimentaire, la formation professionnelle et les activités génératrices de revenus. 
En tant que co-facilitateur du Cluster EHA au Niger, ACTED sera en position idéale pour s'assurer de la bonne coordination des activités EHA avec les partenaires humanitaires afin d'éviter la duplication des efforts et pour developper une réponse en lien direct avec les objectifs et priorités du Cluster EHA.

project_name: Contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations vulnérables au Niger - RRM
project_objective:
Depuis sa mise en place 2015 par IRC, puis avec DRC, ACTED et ACF, le RRM a démontré son efficacité dans la réponse de première intention aux besoins des populations nouvellement déplacées dans les régions de Maradi, Diffa, Tahoua et Tillabéri. Le mécanisme est financé par ECHO (le RRM est une priorité dans le HIP 2020 et dans la version préliminaire du HIP 2021) et USAID, avec le soutien de l’UNICEF pour la fourniture de kits Abri et BNA supplémentaire. Les secteurs d'intervention RRM sont les ABNA, l'EHA, la protection et la sécurité alimentaire et la réponse du Consortium s'inscrit en lien direct avec les différentes stratégies de réponses sectorielles développées par les organes de coordination humanitaire au Niger. Le projet est aussi en lien direct avec la stratégie de réponse des autorités nigériennes, et en particulier le Ministère de l'Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes (MAH), qui est le ministère de tutelle pour les partenaires du RRM. Le projet proposé pour 2021 vise à répondre aux besoins urgents en ABNA des populations les plus vulnérables déplacées depuis moins de 3mois (et/ou accessibles depuis moins de 3 mois). Au total, le consortium RRM vise a distribuer 4612 kits Abri, 14400 kits BNA et a lancer un pilote cash pour 850 bénéficiaires, pilote qui permettrait de renforcer la liberté de choix des bénéficiaires, et qui est aussi influencé par les préférences des bénéficiaires. Le projet soumis par ACTED a été élaboré en coordination directe avec le GT ABNA et avec UNICEF, qui fournit en in-kind une partie des kits BNA listé ci dessus. Les kits Abri sont couverts par UNICEF. La réponse proposée par ACTED et les ONG partenaires du RRM, complémentaire de celle d'UNICEF couvrira 3 512 ménages, soit environ 24 584 personnes pour le secteur des BNA.
La réponse du Consortium RRM commence par une veille humanitaire et une série d'évaluations multisectorielles (MSA) afin d'identifier les secteurs dans lesquels des intervention d'urgence sont nécessaires pour chaque site accueillant des déplacés. Un réseau de points focaux est mis en place par chaque partenaire dans ses zones prioritaires d'intervention pour relayer les alertes de déplacements de populations. Les alertes sont triangulées par les partenaires RRM qui s'appuient sur leur réseau d'informateurs clés, au premier rang desquelles se trouvent les autorités locales et nationales, dont le MAH. Une MSA (évaluation multisectorielle) ou une évaluation flash sont ensuite déclenchées dans les 24h suivant la confirmation de l'alerte, et les rapports d'évaluation sont transmis à la communauté humanitaire à travers OCHA et les GT/Clusters dans les 72h. Ce partage des informations permet d'assurer la bonne coordination avec les partenaires et leur positionnement afin couvrir des besoins complémentaires. Cela permet aussi, le cas échéant, de couvrir les besoins quand l'intervention n'est pas du ressort du RRM. Si les seuils de déclenchement sectoriels calculés à travers la MSA sont atteints, une intervention RRM est lancée (toutes les activités se font suivant le principe ""do no harm"" en respectant les SOP relatives au COVID pour préserver les bénéficiaires et les agents) et des consultations avec les communautés et leaders communautaires prennent place pour prioriser les besoins. Le ciblage des bénéficiaires se fait de manière participative pour réduire les risques de tensions communautaires, et sur des critères de vulnérabilité établis, en prenant en compte les ménages hôtes affectés. Le prépositionnement d'intrants et la disponibilité des équipes et des ressources financières garantissent une mobilisation dans les 7 jours suivant l'alerte. Dans les 30 jours qui suivent l'intervention, une évaluation post intervention mesure l'impact et la satisfaction des populations supportées (respect de la sécurité et dignité lors de l'intervention) ces évaluations participent à améliorer les interventions et assurer la redevabilité vis à vis des personnes affectées.

project_name: Scaling Education in Hama city and rural
project_objective:
In this project, SCS will implement an intervention in non-formal education aiming to enhance safe and equitable access and improve quality of education. This will be achieved through 5 community learning centres: 2 in Hama city (Al Fayhaa and Riyadi) and 3 in its rural in Hamra, Harbanifse, Suran in which SCS will secure child-friendly, safe and inclusive spaces, including classrooms, vocational training rooms, gender and physical disability sensitive WASH infrastructure and recreational spaces. All of these districts were selected based on their level of accessibility and the severity of needs as per the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) with all the localities being rated 3 on the severity scale. The project is not funded at this stage. The centres will increase access to education for 6200 children (50% female) of different ages (5,700: 6-17 years and 500: 18-24 years) with estimated cost 90 USD per student (6% of targeted beneficiaries have physicals disabilities). Moreover, 100 teachers (50% f) will benefit from teacher training and 3,000 parents and caregivers will benefit from Back-to-Learning campaign (BTL). 

In 2020, SCS implemented 3 projects in cooperation with UNHCR, UNICEF and WFP in many sectors with total budget 3,275,795 USD. These projects were able to emergency respond to the displaced, returnees and residents in most of Hama city and rural and were able overreached their target numbers to 453,158 beneficiaries. Social Care Society is one of the leader NGOs in Hama that has practiced humanitarian work in providing Protection, WASH, Health, Education, Food and Livelihoods services since 2013. 
According to SCS humanitarian experience in these locations for 3 years: a generation of children and youth are disconnected and unable to access their right to learn. The most significant contributing factors that prevent access to safe and protected learning environments are poor resources. Also, a lack of decent work and safe livelihoods for family members often results in children being removed from learning and sent to work. Importantly the same challenges are being experienced by teachers, facilitators and trainers who also struggle to cope with their own trauma. In this vein, this project will contribute in three of the Immediate Response Priorities as in Syria 2021 Needs and Response Summary: ""1) To ensure learning in safe environments, particularly given COVID-19 and other factors, new learning spaces and WASH facilities need to be established ... Basic winterization measures should be in place (heaters with fuel, ventilation, cemented floors, etc.). 2) To ensure that out of school children can catch-up, non-formal education services must be expanded and have clear pathways to formal education ... 3) To enable families to prioritize education, the direct and indirect costs of children attending school needs to be addressed through cash and voucher-based education assistance and teaching and learning supplies, including teacher incentives provided to schools.""

project_name: Emergency Health Support to Vulnerable population in Koch and Rubkona Counties in Unity State and Fangak County in Jonglei State, South Sudan
project_objective:
It is estimated that the total number of people in need of critical health services for 2021 in Fangak, Koch and Rubkona counties is 306,199 (Male:149,942; Female:156,257), out of which 58091 (Male: 29,580; Female: 28,511) are children under 5 years old (U5). An unusually high level of flooding in 2020 and now in 2021 continues to exert pressure on the already fragile health systems in Fangak and Koch counties. With basic social facilities destroyed such as WASH and health and nutrition facilities, the affected population is in critical need of health services. Bentiu Protection of Civilians (PoC) is transitioning to an internally displaced (IDP) camp and there could be possible challenge in accessing quality health service. Malaria is very high in Bentiu PoC during the raining season and health facilities are usually congested which make following social distancing difficult.  
The project will target a total of18,283 (Male:8227; Female: 10056) people as direct beneficiaries, particularly women and children and other underserved community members. The health service will be through Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs), Primary Health care Centers (PHCCs) and Mobile health units (MHUs). Services will particularly focus on addressing the top three morbidities of malaria, Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD), and acute respiratory infection (ARI), as well as prevention of epidemic-prone diseases. Likewise, there will be a focus on maternal and child healthcare, routine immunization, disease surveillance, and infection prevention and control.  
The project will deliver health responses to meet health cluster objectives with focus on strengthening local capacity to prevent, detect and respond timely to outbreaks and public health risk events. Where possible, the project will involve integrating of health activities with Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), Nutrition, Food Security and Livelihood (FSL), and Protection sectors to provide holistic lifesaving interventions. Strong referral mechanisms will be enhanced toward the care of vulnerable people with specific needs like SGBV survivors, mental health and SAM children U5 with medical complications. Training for staff will be provided on key health and nutrition topics and other integrated programs. Outreach interventions will be organized to reach hard to access locations from the PHCU sites through MHUs. Activities will be monitored through coordinated strategies jointly with the County Health Directorate (CHD), Ministry of Health (MOH) and UN Agencies. Within WR, activities will be monitored by project staff and the Area Coordinator with support from the Juba office through Supportive Supervisions. Reports will be shared with the Health Cluster and MOH through the DHD. Community based compliant mechanisms will be established within the health facilities and at community level to ensure accountability to the affected population. 
To respond to these immediate health needs, this project will ensure scaling up of lifesaving emergency health service to populations in need in each of the target locations.

project_name: Improve access and utilization of integrated life-saving quality health care to affected vulnerable populations through PHC, in Jonglei, Warrap and Northern Bhar El Gazel states leads to the reduction of morbidity/motarlity, respond to outbreak (COVID-19, Measles, Cholera,) by reaching 84,465 men, women, boys and girls.
project_objective:
This project will aim at reducing high morbidity and mortality from common diseases (such as malaria, diarrhea, pneumonia, COVID-19, measles, cholera, that are aggravated by high burden of outbreak, severe food insecurity, lack of functional health facilities scarcity of medicines and other medical supplies and flooding, insecurity incidents, the macro-economic crisis, and the effects of COVID-19 measures. Between October and November 2020, 34 counties across the country were classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity. Greater Upper Nile region alone had 20 counties classified in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and 1 county (Pibor catastrophe (IPC phase 5). The project will take into account the gender disparity and try to improve the accessibility to most disadvantaged group in the community, HFO will make sure the community stakeholders are sensitized and informed during project initiation, implementation and monitoring & evaluations. The project will ensure intergrated with other sectors (WASH, FSL, Nutrition, Protection, GBV)
The project shall target a population of 84,465 men, women, boys and girls, through provision of essential primary healthcare services in Mobile responses, and Juaibor, Keew PHCCs and Paguir, Chotbora PHCUs in Fangak Ayod town PHCC+ and Kharmun PHCU in Ayod and Diel, Atar PHCUs in Canal/Pigi and Ayai and Nyoc Awany PHCUs in Aweil South and Ajondit PHCU in Tonj Noth as compelmentarity, using qualified staff to do consultation, Antenatal care, maternity-clean and safe delivery and new born care, home base care for COVID-19 with support from WHO, Health cluster, MoH and County health department (CHD) and community leaders and members for the purpose of ownership and accountability to affected populations it positively anticipated  the planned project will achieve it stipulated goals as HRP and health cluster strategic and specific objectives. HFO multi-sectoral approach helps in ensuring that we meet most of the needs of the targeted.

1. Reduce excess morbidity and mortality of epidemic-prone diseases and health insecurities, there will be proper and timely disease outbreak investigation and response and sharing information with public health Laboratory for confirmation and inform health cluster and CHD, MoH surveillance system for all alerts.

2. Improve access and utilization of integrated life-saving quality health care services to crisis-affected and vulnerable populations through PHC MT (Mobile Team) and community-based health service delivery systems. Exsiting gaps will be addressed in HFs and create more robust outreach that will tend to reach all.

3. Increase access to services for survivors of SGBV, disabled, mental health disorders and the elderly.
The project locations will be Fangak, Canal/Pigi and Ayod Counties of Jonglei, Tonj North Warrap state and Aweil South of NBG state respectively. HFO’s Environmental Policy for all programmatic and logistic activities is firstly do no harm’ to the environment as well as to people. 
Monitoring and evaluation will be conducted before, during and after the implementation commences, All report will be shared with Health cluster-WHO, MoH and Donor for better informed and further decision making.  HFO and the partners will manage the predictable threat to the project, will try as much as possible to mitigate them. Monitoring and evaluation will include integrated disease surveillance and response data, early warning alert and response system data, assessment reports from initial rapid need assessments, multi-cluster/sector initial rapid assessment, public health situation analysis, health service functionality, 5Ws, IDSR, HMIS/DHIS2, the health resources availability monitoring system, public health risks, outbreak investigation reports, mortality and morbidity estimates, and other relevant data analysed from monitoring visits and such information will be shared with donors and partners (HC-WHO MOH.

project_name: Lifesaving Child Protection response for the most vulnerable and at-risk children and their caregivers in Panyijar, Koch, Aweil South, Aweil East and Pariang Counties in South Sudan.
project_objective: The IRC Child Protection (CP) program will provide life-saving immediate support to the extremely vulnerable and conflict-affected children in South Sudan who are exposed to abuse, exploitation, neglect, and violence to support them heal, recover and feel safe again when they do experience harm. The IRC CP program will reach 40,000 (17,903G, 15,106 B, 4,894 W, 2,097 M) people through an integrated response in the priority locations (severity three and four) of Panyijar, Koch, Aweil East, Aweil South and Pariang Counties of Unity State, Northern Bahr el Ghazal State and Ruweng Administrative Area respectively. The proposed CP responses are linked with the strategic objectives one and two of the HRP, the cluster objective one and two and the three priority areas of the CP sub-cluster for the HRP period in 2021. The comprehensive case management service will be provided to children with protection concerns, family tracing and reunification (FTR) services, and alternative care arrangements for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) and cash assistance to meet the basic need of children. The mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) service will be provided for children and caregivers with psychological distress using a combination of approaches such as safe healing and learning space (SHLS) and schools for social and emotional learning, families make the difference curriculum for parenting skills of caregivers, supporting adolescents and their families in emergencies curriculum (SAFE) for life skills of adolescents, and IRC’s brighter futures model for malnourishment and children with protection concerns. Finally, the community-based child protection (CBCP) structures will establish/strengthen the lower structure of the community, community outreach on CP awareness and COVID-19 prevention messages and capacity building of the frontline staff and community volunteers.

project_name: Lifesaving WASH interventions for vulnerable and undeserved populations in Pariang
project_objective:
Armed conflict in South Sudan has declined since the parties to the civil war signed a peace agreement in September 2018; and the political situation remains fragile, and millions remain displaced both inside and outside of the country. The humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains fragile due to a multiplicity of vulnerability drivers including inter communal violence, climatic shocks, population displacement, commodity price fluctuations, and pre-existing vulnerabilities such as malnutrition, WASH related diseases, limited access to basic services and high protection risks. The 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) illustrates that about 2.2 million people are in need of WASH services in the country and negatively impacted by lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices. National access to safe water is at 35 per and only 10 per cent of the population has access to improved sanitation. This intervention targets underserved and vulnerable population in Pariang County which is security level 3 according to the WASH cluster 2021 severity map and stressed severity stage in humanitarian conditions shown in 2021 HNO. However, Pariang hosts a significant number of refugees whose needs require urgent attention.
