project_name: Provision of educational opportunities for Lebanese and Migrant children affected by the crisis in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Baalbeck/Hermel Governorates
project_objective:
The multiple crises impacting Lebanon and its institutions have left thousands of children without the basic right to education and are faced with major protection risks threatening their immediate/long-term wellbeing and opportunities. As an emergency response, the proposed project will promote equitable access to inclusive educational opportunities for socio-economically vulnerable Lebanese and migrant children impacted by the crisis in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Baalbeck/Hermel Governorates. 

Recognizing the link between child protection and educational outcomes, the project will fully integrate CP in Education to support children and families severely affected by the crisis cope with the stressors of the situation through protective, safe, and inclusive environments. Building upon TDH IT’s long-lasting experience in preventing and responding to protection threats faced in various communities, this education project will make use of the technical expertise, guidelines and tools developed by TDH IT in collaboration with UNICEF and the CP WG. CP and Inclusion specialists will be part of the implementation of this project, providing training, guidance and tools to be used by Education staff to ensure that children with disabilities are not excluded from education/CP services provided, and are provided equal opportunities to benefit from the project. This approach focuses on enhancing the skills, knowledge and tools available for staff to better assist each child and family, while enhancing families and community awareness of children’s rights and how the crisis is affecting them. 

Community Support [SO1] For Lebanese communities, in response to the limited data available on the educational status and barriers faced by Lebanese children as a result of the crisis, a comprehensive needs assessment will be conducted considering both in-school and out-of-school Lebanese children in specific locations where TDH IT has years of experience implementing Formal/NFE/CP programs, as well as strong connections with the communities. TDH IT’s CP-Education integrated approach will allow the identification of households’ educational gaps and the child protection risks families are exposed to. The needs assessments will take place through inclusive outreaching strategies where communities will be sensitized on key educational and CP messages, and be referred to required basic services available. Engagement with municipalities, school principals, and other key local stakeholders will also take place. 

Specifically for migrant children, the intervention will aim at building a strong evidence-base and understanding of their needs in terms of Education and Child Protection. A comprehensive needs assessment will be conducted in close collaboration with civil society organizations supporting various migrant communities, with a particular focus in Beirut and its surrounding areas. A tailored educational intervention considering the specific child protection needs of each specific community will be co-designed with stakeholders with prior experience and knowledge of the specific legal, protection, social and economic challenges faced by each group to ensure its relevance. 

Improving Formal Education opportunities [SO2] To address some of the new barriers to FE created by the crisis, TDH IT will work together with MEHE and targeted communities to identify the most impacted public schools in need of assistance within the areas where TDH IT already works to create synergy with its existing intervention. 

Engagement of key stakeholders and duty-bearers at community and governance levels will take place to increase their accountability in upholding children’s rights and foster inclusion during this emergency response.

The project will be implemented in line with Sphere Protection Standards and CHS, and National Sectors technical guidelines and SOPs. 

This intervention will complement pre-existing response funded by other institutional donors.

project_name: Effective Coordination for Education in Emergencies Response in Gaza and the West Bank
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project will contribute to education cluster objective 2 of the HRP strategic objective, by  supporting and coordinating a coherent and effective Education humanitarian response. This includes the coordination of needs assessments; development of a response strategy, long-term planning, cross-sector collaboration and advocacy. 
Specifically, the project will ensure uninterrupted implementation of the core cluster coordination functions including: 
1. 	Supporting service delivery and coordination 
2.	Informing strategic decision-making of the HC/HCT for the humanitarian response
3.	Planning and strategy development
4.	Advocacy
5.	Monitoring and reporting
6.	Capacity building in contingency/preparedness planning

In the context of Palestine and especially with the recent COVID 19 pandemic, authorities lack national coordination mechanisms for addressing the enormous challenges facing the education system; each education system in East Jerusalem, Area C and Gaza has different duty bearers and face different significant protection challenges. The Education Cluster will support the relevant duty bearers to ensure that children (age 8-12) 50% girls, youth (13-18) and teachers in the most vulnerable communities can safely access schools that meet minimum humanitarian standards and provide a protective environment in the context of protracted conflict. All interventions planned through the 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) will be closely coordinated with local communities and meet the requirement of the strong protection mainstreaming and community engagement especially in the needs assessment as well as the implementation of activities.
The Cluster is also planning to strengthen the partners level engagement on gender through joint cluster needs assessments on gender specific needs in the field, joint HRP mid review and related gender analysis, strengthening partners  capacity on data collection and reporting of disaggregated data related to special needs of women, girls, boys or men. Partners will jointly identify the cluster priority interventions and responses based on the gender disaggregated needs assessments, reports and testimonies.

project_name: Accès des déplacés et leurs communautés hôtes aux soins de santé primaires dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre- Nord, de l'EST et du Nord
project_objective:
Le contexte sécuritaire difficile que traverse le Burkina Faso depuis la fin de l’année 2015, met à rude épreuve le fonctionnement du système de santé initialement déjà fragile.
Les incidents sécuritaires récurrents dans certaines régions du Burkina dont le Sahel, l’Est et le Centre-Nord ont entrainé un déplacement massif de populations entrainant une pression sans précédent sur les structures sanitaires d’accueil avec une forte augmentation de la demande. Par ailleurs, la fuite des agents de santé des zones touchées par l’insécurité entraine une réduction de l’offre de santé dans lesdites zones (fermeture des centres de santé ou au mieux formations sanitaires fonctionnant à minima). 
Le présent projet, se veut être une contribution au maintien de l’offre de soins de santé et à la résilience des communautés dans les zones affectées au profit des IDPs, populations hôtes et celles des zones d’accès difficiles. Ce projet appuiera le renforcement de la disponibilité en ressources humaines capables de prodiguer des services essentiels pour sauver des vies (à travers le recrutement et la capacitation d’agents de santé) aussi bien au niveau des structures de santé qu’au niveau communautaire, la disponibilité en équipements, matériels médico-techniques, intrants et médicaments essentiels, la supervision formative.

project_name: Assistance rapide en AME aux populations nouvellement affectées par les conflits dans les régions du Centre Nord, Est, Nord, Sahel, Centre-est, Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective: La situation sécuritaire continue de se dégrader en 2020. Depuis janvier au 12 novembre 2020; 442 incidents ont été enregistrés causant le décès de 651 personnes, dont 31 enfants . La crise sécuritaire, couplée à l’impact de la COVID-19, ont créé une situation humanitaire sans précédent particulièrement dans 6 régions prioritaires du HRP/HNO . Ces crises viennent exacerber les vulnérabilités déjà existantes dans ces régions, causant le déplacement de 1,049,767 personnes , dont plus de 60% d’enfants. Les ménages affectés ont en majorité perdus leurs AME (Articles Ménagers Essentiels), leurs réserves alimentaires et autres moyens de subsistance affectant la survie des enfants et des familles. De nombreux ménages sont actuellement sans abris et ont intégré des familles d’accueil en attendant la remise en état de leurs abris. La majorité (80%) vivent dans des conditions de logement très précaires, avec l’incapacité financière et matérielle pour faire face aux multiples besoins notamment logement, nourriture les frais de scolarité et l’accès aux soins. La fragilité du contexte actuel exacerbe une vulnérabilité aigüe qu'une partie importante de la population locale vit déjà, et contribue à générer une pression accrue sur l'accès aux ressources d’une manière générale. Il apparait donc urgent d’apporter une réponse à cette situation. La présente action s’inscrit dans cette perspective et vise à « fournir une assistance humanitaire d'urgence en articles ménagers essentiels et en apport monétaire aux populations déplacées affectées par les conflits dans les régions du Centre Nord, Est, Nord, Sahel, Centre-est, Boucle du Mouhoun». Il s’agira de : (i) cibler environ 70,000 personnes dans le besoin en leur fournissant assistance rapide en kits AME de première nécessité alignes sur les standards du cluster et en apport monétaire multisectorielle inconditionnel. Le ciblage géographique selon le nombre des enfants déplacés sera combiné avec des enquêtes ménages de base. On utilisera les infrastructures communautaires pour allouer l'aide à des ménages ayant des enfants avec vulnérabilités aigues. (ii) de veiller à ce que cette assistance soit fournie dans un environnement de protection tout en respectant le principe de « Do no harm ». Les femmes seront les principaux récipiendaires des AME.

project_name: Enhancing Health Outcomes in northwest Syria
project_objective:
The already fragile health system in NWS suffered from more than 110 attacks on health care facilities during 2019 and 2020 and has been negatively impacted by large-scale displacements, a shortage of health professionals, and the emergence of the COVID-19. IOM will enhance the health outcomes in northwest Syria by supporting the current health referral system, continuing the operation of three tuberculosis (TB) centres, and continuing two primary health care facilities. 

To strengthen COVID-19 preparedness and response pillars and to enable a safe and effective COVID-19 response, IOM will support the current health referral system by transporting COVID-19 suspected patients to health centres. Additionally, all travellers crossing points of entry (PoE) into NWS from both directions will be screened for COVID-19 and referred and transported as needed. As it is necessary to limit disease transmission by reducing secondary infections among close contacts and health personnel in NWS, vehicles and staff must be disinfected after each transport of COVID-19 suspected cases to mitigate the risk of further infection in NWS. The COVID-19 referral system ensures that vehicles only transport suspected cases, and non-COVID-19 patients are directed to ambulances under the already existing health referral system.

IOM will also improve access to quality, lifesaving and life-sustaining health services in response to growing TB case numbers by operating three TB centres in NWS through experienced implementing partners (IPs). Each centre will provide a package of comprehensive TB services including TB diagnostics, TB treatments, food for patients, case finding, and screening of vulnerable populations. Since the start of the project in 2019 (previously funded by another organization), thousands of people have been tested, more than 800 TB patients have received services, and thousands of IDPs were prevented from catching the disease. Additionally, mobile teams run out of the centres will go into the community to screen and refer suspected TB cases to enable early detection of TB and counter misinformation.

To address critical gaps in health care services and provide essential health services to vulnerable populations, IOM aims to sustain primary healthcare services to the populations in two communities in northwest Syria. The two proposed facilities would provide adequate health response to IDPs and implement essential medical services as outlined by the Health Cluster in the standard package of primary health care services, including basic trauma and injury care, communicable disease and EWARN (disease surveillance system in NWS) reporting, sexual and Reproductive health, child health, basic nutrition, basic mental health and PSS, non-communicable disease management, and curative services. 

All IOM staff will receive personal protective equipment (PPE) and all new staff will receive COVID-19 training on IPC guidelines and protocols as well as SOPs developed by WHO and the COVID-19 task force to ensure patient and staff safety.

project_name: Population has optimal access to education
project_objective:
UNHCR will ensure that Rohingya refugee children, adolescent, and youth from 3 to 24 years have access to equitable quality education opportunities through the continuation of existing programs by maintaining learning facilities, recruitment, training and deployment of teachers, procurement of teaching and learning materials, and expansion of learning facilities by constructing additional double-storied classrooms with sex-segregated latrines and WASH facilities. Looking at implementation beyond the Myanmar Curriculum (MC) Pilot, UNHCR will be developing a comprehensive scale-up concept note and implementation plan outlining the needs and specific actions to be undertaken. Furthermore, considering the COVID-19 pandemic and its implications, UNHCR and its partners will implement EdTech solutions along with caregiver led education and ensure community engagement in the overall project cycle ensuring Age Gender and Diversity (AGD) mainstreaming.

In addition, the transitioning of Learning Competency Framework and Approach (LCFA) level II students to the MC, in grades 1-3will be a critical undertaking for the second half of the year. As a step to ensure the provision of quality education and with the introduction of MC, language and teacher professional development (TPD) training is required to ensure educators and teachers have the required language competencies and expected teaching qualifications, hence TPD incorporating both in-service and ongoing teacher professional development activities, continuation and expansion of language acquisition program for Myanmar and English language as well as certified trainings for teachers and educators in collaboration with BARD college and BRAC University will be undertaken. 

UNHCR will continue its host community support through maintaining and operationalizing the Community Technology Access (CTA) and the satellite teachers training facility, constructing or renovating classrooms and WASH facilities, and provide classroom furniture and supplies. UNHCR further will work with sector and partners to ensure a synchronized student data collection system using proGres database to avoid duplication and ensure reliable education data and analysis.

project_name: Protecting and promoting Mental Health and psychosocial wellbeing of conflict affected population in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
The project aims at continuing and strengthening IOM’s protection and MHPSS response in north-east Nigeria through the following areas of intervention:

1.	IOM’s MHPSS activities will consist of services to populations in need as per standard service package and access to safe spaces, which act as resource centers to the community host IOM’s MHPSS activities, including lay counselling, basic emotional support, life-skills development, language classes, and socio-relational and cultural activities. Small-scale livelihood activities shall be integrated with mental health and psychosocial support to vulnerable groups.

IOM will create and ensure pathways to prevent further family separationand facilitate safety referrals to other
services and MHPSS teams will provide Psychological rst Aid (PFA) to the new arrivals, identify the ones in need of further support, link and guarantee safety referrals to other sectors. IOM will continue to enhance accountability to the affected population by strengthening Protection against sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) and feedback mechanisms.

IOM will, in close partnership with the MAPTIP, continue to build the capacity of counter tra cking stakeholders with the intent to localize and increase ownership of the counter tra cking response in north-east Nigeria. IOM will a;sp seek to improve prevention and response services targeting at risk sub-groups of the crisis affected population and victims of tracking.

2.	To support GBV survivors consenting to access services in camp and camp-like settings, IOM’s Psychosocial Mobile Teams will provide the following array of services: survivors of GBV will be provided with PFA (Level 1 and 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid) in an effort to cover their acute needs; targeted survivors of GBV will be provided with structured psychosocial counselling, either as a stand-alone service or to complement other specialized services (Level 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid); With their consent, survivors of GBV will be referred to specialized services for case management and dedicated follow-up (Level 4 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid); Families of GBV survivors will be provided structured psychosocial counselling and family support sessions (Level 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid). IOM will ensure that safety, confidentiality, respect, and non-discrimination principles are adhered to, to protect the rights and dignity of survivors and promote resilience ..

3.	To mitigate the risk of GBV and other protection threats in camp and camp-like settings,
 
IOM psychosocial Mobile Teams will conduct sensitization and awareness campaigns on GBV and protection threats in the targeted camp and camp-like settings (Level 1 and 2 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid). Campaigns will be tailored to the contextual needs of the community and take into account age and gender categories as well as socio-cultural, ethnic and religious aspects. Moreover, campaigns will be designed in participation with the community community, ensuring the participation of persons facing heightened vulnerabilities and more at risk of being excluded.
IOM will jointly work closely with the IDP safety committees to conduct safety audits and safety mapping to identify and highlight protection and safety concerns within the camp, disseminate protection focused messages, and increase awareness on protection risks.
4. IOM will build the capacities of humanitarian actors, incl. IOM staff, in the areas of MHPSS and Protection, with the overall aim of mainstreaming protection principles in programming and strengthen GBV risk mitigation. IOM will also prioritize strengthening capacity of the community-based structures such as women committees and IDP safety committees.

project_name: Operation and Maintenance of Humanitarian Hubs in North-East Nigeria
project_objective: Since April 2018, IOM has operated and managed  a total of 9 humanitarian hubs composed of a base camp in Maiduguri (Red Roof) and 8 field hubs located in Gwoza, Bama, Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, Banki (2 hubs) and Damasak.  The humanitarian hubs provide humanitarian actors the ability to work with safe and secure accommodation, office space and meeting/training facilities, so that they are able to stay and deliver interventions necessary to saving and improving the lives of hundreds of thousands of Nigerians affected by conflict.  The field hubs also host the internet connectivity service of the Emergency Telecommunication Sector (ETS).  These humanitarian hubs help sustain the access of humanitarian responders to the population affected by the conflict, enabling them to coordinate and provide better assistance to the affected population. The humanitarian base camp in Maiduguri has a total capacity of 142 beds while each of the field hubs except for the second hub in Banki (Banki Hub Extension), has a 15-bed capacity. The Banki Hub Extension has a capacity of 72 beds. All of the hubs have office space and training/meeting facilities available to humanitarian actors.  Under the proposed project, IOM will aim to support the operation and maintenance of eight humanitarian field hubs and the base camp in Maiduguri (Red Roof).

project_name: Responding to the Urgent Needs of IDPs, Host Communities and Returnees in Hard-to-Reach Areas / New Operations Areas in North Eastern Nigeria
project_objective:
IOM will expand its Mental Health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) programme to a more systematic and comprehensive approach with engagement of community volunteers and health promoters. Access to quality reproductive health care services remains a challenge. IOM intends to enhance quality access to comprehensive services through the integration of MHPSS with Primary Health Care (PHC). IOM will also continue working with the health partners in outbreak prevention and response efforts, capacity building of health and mental health professionals, health information management, and emergency referral and support system. As part of the health promotional and preventive activities, IOM will partner with local NGOs to implement health outreach through Health Promoters and community volunteers. Under this action, IOM will also strengthen its collaboration with the State Primary Health Care Development Agency (SPHCDA) and will continue to support the State Ministries of Health.

IOM partnered with the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH) in setting-up and operating a 24-hospital bed and 2-ICU (intensive car eunit) bed isolation center for humanitarian workers in north-east Nigeria.  The center also operates a COVID-19 laboratory that will primarily address the PCR (polymerise chain reaction) testing of humanitarian workers. IOM aims to continue the partnership with UMTH in operating the isolation center and COVID-19 laboratory for humanitarian workers in north-east Nigeria.

In coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Federal Ministry of Health and related departments, World Health Organization and the UN Medical Services; IOM will leverage its health clinic infrastructure and capacity to contribute to the government’s effort to respond to COVID-19. IOM will continue to support the provision of COVID-19 testing services in Borno, FCT (Abuja) and Lagos. Activities include sample collection and testing for the UN staff, staff of International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs), diplomatic community and migrants using existing UMTH facilities.

project_name: Provision of improved, safe and dignified WASH services to the conflict affected populations and host communities in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
As a result of ongoing protracted conflict causing unpredictable and continuous large-scale displacement, recurrent large-scale cholera and acute watery diarrhea (AWD)AWD epidemics, the COVID-19 pandemic, and seasonal flooding, fierce storms and winds, north-east Nigeria continues to experience  multifaceted humanitarian crisis in the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector. The main drivers of vulnerabilities related to WASH are closely linked to the conflict- induced and recurrent population displacement,and are also a result of pre-existing low level of WASH services in the Northeast. An estimated 2.8 million people across north-east Nigeria remain in critical need of sustained and equitable access to clean water and dignified hygiene and sanitation services (WASH Sector Gap analysis and MSNA 2020 data). 1.02 million people receive less than 15 liters of safe clean water per person per day while about 1.06 million people have intermittent water access with over 500 meters walking distance and over 30 minutes queuing time at water points
In response to the needs identified and in contribution to the Nigeria WASH Sector objectives 1,2, 3 and 4, IOM will scale-up its provision of WASH services targeting internally displaced people and returnees in camp, camp-like settings, as well as and hosting community in BAY (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe) States. 
IOM will (A) Ensure safe access to water facilities and services through the drilling, installation, maintenance, rehabilitation and water quality monitoring of boreholes; (B) Ensure safe and equitable access to sanitation facilities (latrines, showers including laundry spaces), handwashing stations) through the operation and maintenance (O&M) of existing facilities and the construction of additional gender segregated facilities and waste water treatment system; (C) Promote improved water and sanitation outcomes in targeted settings through the systematic promotion of personal and environmental hygiene messages (following national guidelines on COVID-19 preventive measures, such as physical distancing) and including COVID-19 preventive measure;  and the support for increased capacity of established gender-balanced WASH committees (D) Ensure environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in operation area through the establishment of WASH Committees including- male and female community members, procurement and distribution of tools and equipment; (E) Distribute WASH NFI following the national/ cluster standards; and (F) Conduct capacity building of WASH partners and stakeholders with an overall aim at also mitigating the risks linked to the COVID pandemic. 
The project will be implemented in three states: Borno (13 LGAs), Adamawa (5 LGAs) and Yobe State (8 LGAs), targeting an estimated 757,620 individuals. 
IOM ensures that design and implementation of all WASH activities take into consideration the age, gender as well as disability-specific needs of project beneficiaries,and specifically addresses women and girls’ needs, such as Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM). All activities related to this project will equally benefit women and men, girls and boys and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. In regard to assessments, monitoring and evaluation of gender, age and disability specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels where possible. Using the IOM WASH Monitoring and Evaluation Framework, IOM will ensure that “Do No Harm” principles are adhered to throughout the WASH interventions, particularly in WASH activities pertaining to latrine and water point locations and construction, through the use of various mechanisms, such as consultations with vulnerable groups.

project_name: Strenghtening Reintegration Capacity for Burundian Returnees through Housing, Land, Property (HLP) and Shelter
project_objective:
This funding will support Burundian returnees from the United Republic of Tanzania and the republic of Rwanda through reintegration projects including, Housing Land and Property (HLP) and Shelter interventions. A community-based approach, including cash-based interventions (CBI), will shape the methodology to support returnees in Cankuzo, Ruyigi, Muyinga, and Kirundo provinces, based on needs assessments. To ensure that social cohesion is reinforced during the reintegration process, the returnees and host community members in the local communities of return in Burundi will be provided with critical HLP support and shelter solutions, contributing to reintegrate returnees and improving social and economic conditions.

The Project will focus particularly on the Housing, Land and Property (HLP) component, as a critical need to address in country, to ensure security of tenure and mitigate conflict level linked to land. This aspect will be covered through sensitization of communities to land right and land registration, and support in the process of obtaining a valid land certificate.

project_name: Enhancing the protection environment of the crises-affected people in North West Syria by provision of comprehensive Protection Services
project_objective:
Shafak Organization proposes to mitigate/respond to the protection risks faced by the conflict-affected people in Jabal Samaan, Jarablus, Afrin, Al-Bab and Azaz districts in Aleppo governorate, as well as in Harem, Jisr-Ash-Shugur, Ariha and Idleb districts in Idleb governorate through a community centers and protection mobile teams.
The purpose of this project is to empower local communities and conflict-affected individuals in North West Syria, and support their role in building society and in determining their future by provision of protection services and emergency protection services to 141700 IDPs and host community members, through four community centers, two protection tents and 25 mobile outreach teams. The provided protection services will comprise both mitigation and response services as well as specialized and non-specialized protection services.
The proposed project will offer gender and age appropriate general protection service including, structured PSS, recreational and MHPSS activities, case management involving life-saving assistance to vulnerable people in ensuring their access to existing services, referral to specialized and non-specialized services, awareness raising on protection related topics, life skills and vocational training to enhance the community resilience and livelihoods opportunities, legal assistance and legal awareness raising session of HLP and CSD through qualified and well-trained legal teams, protection monitoring, as well as supporting community committees. Shafak will maintain gender-balanced team in all its projects in order to facilitate the access of all gender groups to the services in line with the humanitarian principles
Moreover, training on HLP and CSD will be delivered to partners’ legal staff and community actors in Syria and Turkey by specialized legal staff in accordance with the protection cluster and HLP WTG guidance and SOPs. 
These services will be offered to vulnerable IDPs and host community members with particular emphasis on quality services to the following groups:
•	Women headed households
•	Children headed households
•	UASC, CAAFAG and Child labor
•	PWDs
•	Elderly women and men
•	Family has children at risk of child labor
•	UASC and orphans who are being cared for by another family.
•	New IDPs who fled their home and have no financial means
In case of emergencies, the project activities will be shifted to respond to the emergency protection needs of new displaced people delivering the protection emergency package like: PFA, referrals and case fund support to respond to the urgent needs of IDPs
Shafak will consult with the community members at the beginning of the project to introduce the project activities and have them involved in the selection of the community centers locations, as well as Shafak will establish community committees from the same communities and train them on protection topics such as; CPMS, Safe identification and referral and communication skills to enable them identify and refer people in need to the case management team. Moreover, the community committees will play a significant role in raising protection issues that are faced by the community and mobilizing them to participate in project activities.
The activities will emphasize equity and non-discrimination, reinforcing the basic social and human rights of participants while taking into consideration the cultural, historical and social specificities of targeted populations. All static centers will be rehabilitated and well equipped to accompany PWDs.
COVID-19 precautionary measures will be taken in line with WHO, Global Protection Cluster and the Protection Cluster’s Guidance, including strict enforcement of physical distancing, minimizing of participants per activity to maximum eight people and maintaining the social distancing between BNFs and staff, the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) by staff/beneficiaries.

project_name: Improve Access to livelihoods, Protecting Assets and Building Resilience of Crisis affected Populations in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
This program aims at supporting the resilience of the conflict affected people in northwest
Syria, particularly in Idleb and Aleppo governorate. Shafak's proposed is designed to
contribute to supporting the transition to the early recovery phase, as it supports the
targeted communities with long-term assistance activities, programs that focus on
building/restoring the communities' infrastructure, local economic empowerment, and
initiatives that ensure engagement and participation of the community in recovering from
the protracted crisis. This program will achieve its objectives through the following:
a) Providing short-term work opportunities through Cash-for-Work activities to
3500 HHs.
b) Establishing or expanding Small-Micro Enterprises through provision of business skills training and financial or in-kind support to 1000 selected beneficiaries from IDPs and Host communities. Grant total will be between 600-1000 USD per beneficiary.

c) Providing vocational and skills training to 800 youth, men and women applicants and
then support successful trainees (Expecting 500  trainees) with small-scale cash grants to
enable them restart/initiate their small enterprises, each grant total will be between 600-1000 USD per
beneficiary.
d) Rehabilitating the local economic, public and social infrastructure (15 Projects) through
linking with the Cash-for-Work activity or through service providers. Each project cost will
be about 15000 USD
e) Improve access to basic services and Markets through construction of Markets, Roads, rehabilitation Electricity and Water net work, Community led priorities through initiatives. 4 markets will be established
e) Supporting local community and social cohesion initiatives.
f) VSLA: Establishment of Village Savings and Loan Associations  VSLA: an estimated 25 Savings and Loan Groups, each consisting of approximately 10-15 members, will be facilitated to establish. Shafak will follow VSLA methodology, developed by CARE, however, this will be adapted to the Syria and emergency context. Community volunteers will be selected directly from the targeted communities as Savings and Loan Group Facilitators and trained on the formation of the groups. Gender and protection norms will be considered, the groups will constitute a common fund for members to save and borrow to finance a business or pay for living expenses. Groups will follow a standard savings and loan groups methodology, however, this will be adapted to the Syria context. Participants will elect their own group leaders, set their own rules.

project_name: Protection of crises affected boys and girls and their families in NW Syria through provision of Community based and Specialized Child Protection services, as well as reducing the impact of MA by provision RE and Victim Assistance services
project_objective:
CP:
Shafak organization will respond to the increased child protection concerns of the crises affected children including CWDs through center-based activities in five Child-Friendly Spaces and 19 community outreach teams deployed in Harim, Jisr-Ash-Shugur, Ariha and Idleb districts in Idleb and Jabal Saman, Azaz, Jarablus, and Ghandorah in Aleppo. 
Shafak will provide CP case management and referral in the targeted locations targeting children with CP concerns. CM services will be complemented with provision of emergency case fund and CVA to respond to the immediate and urgent needs of children including CWDs. The following CP vulnerability criteria and concerns will be considered for CM and IPA support: 
1-	UASC 
2-	Child labor including its worst forms
3-	CAAFAG
4-	Early Marriage 
5-	Child headed household 
6-	Domestic violence 
7-	Severe Psychological distresses
Moreover, age and gender appropriate structured and non-structured PSS activities for children and adolescents will be organized in and out the CFSs. Different curriculums will be used such as; IRC PSS manual, I DEAL and Child Resilience.
Positive parenting skills sessions will be provided to caregivers to reduce the physical and humiliating punishment of children in the home, and improve the capacity of parents and caregivers to practice positive parenting.
In addition, Shafak will target the communities with awareness-raising activities on PSEA, child rights, and CP issues. Thus, messages will be tailored to gender and age needs in target locations to ensure gender sensitivity and also that messaging is relevant to children at specific age levels.
Finally, Shafak will strengthen the capacity of local communities about the child concerns by establishing CPNs covering all age and gender groups in the targeted communities to prevent and respond to CP needs at the community level. And secondly, train key persons in those communities and the workers in care centers, schools, hospitals who are in direct touch with children about the CPMS, PFA, and Safe Identification and referral.
Shafak will adapt the CFSs and the static facilities to be accessible and friendly for CWDs through establishing ramps and toilets for CWDs.
Overall: the project will target 58450 (5550M, 10300W, 19300B and 19300G) with the CP activities
Mine Action:
Shafak will deliver a comprehensive approach to Mine Action involving Risk Education, and Victim Assistance. This project will be a continuation of Shafak work in Explosive Remnants of War Risk Education ERW - RE programme in Idleb and Aleppo. 
Under the ERW-RE part of the project, 4 RE teams who have already been trained by Shafak, will target IDPs and host communities in Idleb and Aleppo providing school-age children with RE activities, and materials to inform them about dangers of ERW. They will also provide RE material to adults, putting up posters about the ERW risks in the public streets and communities to increase the awareness of ERW threats. 
Moreover, the RE (ToT) Trainers will provide RE training to Community Focal Points (CFPs) in affected communities, and RE teams and other workers from NGOs across all humanitarian sectors, to improve the relevance, integration and reach of RE messaging across NW Syria. 
Furthermore, the project will also enhance the resilience of people living with injuries and disabilities (PLWDs), focusing on ERW survivors, through targeting those victims with vocational trainings and referrals to specialized services to enhance their access to livelihood opportunities and re-integrate them with their communities. Overall, the project will target 25500 individuals (3000M, 5500W, 8500B and 8500G).
COVID-19 precautionary measures will be taken in line with WHO, Global Protection Cluster and the Protection Cluster’s Guidance, including strict enforcement of physical distancing, minimizing of participants per activity to maximum 8 people and maintaining the social distancing between BNFs and staff, and the use of PPE.

project_name: Provide immediate access to water services
project_objective:
In light of the current economic and fuel crises, the intended intervention will aim to support existing infrastructure for water supply system through procurement and supply of chlorine  and other consumables, emergency repair for pumping stations with provision of fuel to maintain minimum operational level and providing the most vulnerable communities with water supply. This approach is deemed to take the most cost-effective pathway to reach a high number of people in need in a short time period. The only way to avoid the complete shutdown of all or part of the water systems in Lebanon is through this intervention and support to pumping stations.  
To identify the communities most affected by the current economic crisis, the water sector is conducting a country wide vulnerability mapping exercise based on two criteria: (1) current access to water, measured in l/c/d; (2) energy source for the water supply system (fuel based, gravity fed, EdL, or PV).
The highly critical communities have been classified as the ones with energy sources relying on fuel exclusively, and currently receiving less than 35 L/c/day based on the Water Sector LCRP minimal standard for water supply in Informal settlements.]

project_name: Provision of life-saving child protection and gender-based violence response and prevention services and cash assistance
project_objective:
The onset of the political and economic crisis combined with the COVID-19 outbreak and general lockdowns, further deepened vulnerabilities of all populations residing in Lebanon (Syrian/Palestinian refugees, migrants, Lebanese), affecting a much larger population, including those living outside previously recognized most vulnerable localities. The deepened vulnerabilities and rapid impoverishment of families, combined with lack of access to basic social services, social safety nets and livelihood opportunities amongst displaced populations and vulnerable Lebanese, contributed all together to an alarming deterioration of the protection situation of children and women.

As a general objective, UNICEF, together with its partners, aims at increasing access and quality of CP/GBV services through strengthening the community-based protective and supportive environment free of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse. 

Based on the above, UNICEF will work in collaboration with line ministries, UN agencies and partners to address the psychosocial needs of more than 40,000 affected girls, boys, women and their families, using a multi-layered approach through the provision of an integrated package of services, including community-based and more focused psychosocial support activities, case management and access to specialized services, such as mental health psychosocial support services.

Moreover, UNICEF will provide emergency cash transfer to approx. 20,000 individuals, primarily children, living in the poorest and most vulnerable areas of the country. The programme will be linked to broader services that vulnerable households will need, particularly child protection. Extensive community engagement, outreach and communication on the programme, efficient payment channel, and clear grievance and accountability mechanisms will be crucial.

All services will be provided through face to face and remote modalities. 

UNICEF will also include timely and consistent AAP mechanisms (Accountability to affected population) to ensure that the programme responds to girls', boy's and caregivers' needs.

project_name: MNCAH Support to most vulnerable communities in Lebanon
project_objective:
Lebanon is facing multiple, unprecedented crises. The COVID-19 global pandemic, in addition to a crippling year-long economic downturn and the acute impacts of the August 2020 explosions in Beirut, has compounded challenges in an already weak public health sector. The cumulative impact has meant that the most vulnerable populations – women and children face even greater hardships and UNICEF’s effort to increase access to quality health services is more critical than ever.  Through this project, UNICEF will seek to minimize the risk of further spread of COVID-19 and communicable diseases among vulnerable Lebanese and migrant populations through strengthening the COVID and communicable diseases intervention at the 5 Border Center Points and increasing the capacities and knowledge of staff working at the all Point of Entry.  This will also enable UNICEF to reach mothers and children from the most vulnerable communities among the Lebanese and migrant workers and aim to enhance their health seeking behaviors and knowledge on MNCAH including immunization.

Thereby, the project will target the 3 layers of enabling environment, demand and supply to support and enhance maternal and child access to qualitative services through:
-	Capacity building of health care providers including community midwives on updated ANC/PNC guidelines
-	Ensuring quality and safety of services especially Immunization services at PHC level through ensuring the availability of safe and effective cold chain (based on the cold chain equipment inventory analysis) and PPEs and supportive immunization service provision at PHC level.
-	Support COVID screening and awareness and routine immunization activities at POEs 
-	Enhancing community health behaviors and preventive practices among vulnerable Lebanese and migrants through capacity building and dispatch of 100 frontline workers who will be providing integrated maternal and child health messaging including immunization and COVID.

project_name: Back to school Campaign in Flood Affected Areas of Sindh
project_objective:
The Back to School Campaign through provision of food aims to encourage return and resumption to education in areas affected by natural disasters, with the aim of reducing barriers in access to  primary school  for boys and girls while supporting their families to meet their basic food needs at home. Targeted beneficiaries  will receive fortified wheat flour of 25 kg (bimonthly) as take-home ration, conditional upon enrolment and regular attendance at schools or temporary learning centers notified by the Government. The project will be implemented in collaboration with Education and Literacy Department, Government of Sindh and target 71,480 children (35,740 boys & 35,740 girls) enrolled in primary boys’ and girls’ schools with 3,574 MT of Wheat Flour in affected areas of districts Badin and Sajawal, Sindh. The project is in alignment with the objectives of Sindh Education Sector Plan and CM’s forthcoming Bokh Mitao Programme and will implemented in areas where WFP’s other interventions (nutrition, food assistance, DRR and social protection) are ongoing. 
 
Justification:
 According to UNDP’s latest Report on Multi-dimensional Poverty in Pakistan the incidence and severity of multi-dimensional poverty is high in the southern part of the province. For instance, approximately 84% of peoples live in multi-dimensional poverty in Badin while it is 68% for Sajawal district. Similarly, according to RNA 2020, 72% of assessed population in Badin and 63% in Sajawal reported inability to buy food and in the case of any emergency the average food stock for their own consumption may last for 5 days only. These districts also host many out of schoolboys and girls of age 5-16 years, and school completion rates are drastically low. Displacement, school damages and discontinuity of educational activities resulting from floods and other disasters further deteriorates education situation in the affected areas.

Disasters’ negative impact on lives, livelihoods, livestock, agriculture, infrastructure, access to social and life-saving services and income generation opportunities is significantly high on the children, women, disabled and elderly peoples. Among others, the incidences of less availability of food for children and women at home, engagement in labor and income generation activities, children dropout from school and early marriages of girls are common in most of the cases. 

WFP’s experience of emergency response in Pakistan suggests that school feeding programmes can play an instrumental role in bringing children back to school while reducing their chances of drop out, engagement in child labor or early marriages. Provision of take-home rations- a means to transfer resources to vulnerable households and subsidize families’ food basket, motivate families to send and retain their children in schools and hence, contribute to increase enrolment, retention and attendance at schools. 

Effectiveness of school feeding is evident from flood response in 2011-12. WFP field monitoring reports of school feeding under indicated that almost 97 percent of students were retained in schools in Sindh. Similarly, analysis of education indicators in WFP assisted vs non-assisted schools in Erstwhile FATA showed that enrolment rates increased at 15% in WFP assisted schools as compared to 3% in non-assisted schools. Moreover, the retention rate in WFP-assisted primary schools in 2016-2017 was as high as 80.1 %, against WFP’s target of 70 % (compared to 24% in all primary schools in erstwhile FATA).

project_name: Integrated Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) response for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), Returnees, and Communities in North East Syria (NES)
project_objective:
The overall goal of the Project is to reduce the threat from explosive ordnance (EO) to IDPs, returnees, and host communities, enabling safe returns, increased access to villages, land, and infrastructure as well as safe livelihood and stabilization activities. Further, MAG aims to contribute to building a substantial national demining capacity as well as laying the foundations for future training facilities that can be utilized by local authorities and other HMA NGOs.

MAG’s strategy in NES aims at developing an integrated response focusing on Humanitarian Mine Action which has been designed to incorporate the necessary skills and technical capacity to address the contamination threat in North East Syria (NES).  This approach is an essential pre requisite for early recovery, stabilization, and safely consolidating humanitarian efforts across NES. MAG will conduct non-technical and technical surveys as well as clearance of land contaminated with explosive ordnance in NES, and delivery of Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) messaging directly as well as by training Community Focal Points.
  
In addition, as existing national mine action capacity remains extremely limited, and the scale of the contamination is very extensive, training of new national clearance teams together with advanced training in management for existing national demining staff members will be a key component throughout the project. Furthermore, MAG will continue to work with national partner organisations, to enhance additional efforts of national capacity building through delivery of Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) and contamination mapping.  The main capacity of the project will be focused and deployed across Hasakeh and Raqqa governorates, with additional resources deployed in Deir Ez Zor to support the overall protection and stabilisation response in NES.

project_name: Multi-purpose cash assistance for IDPs, returnees and host communities in Tripolitania

This project seeks to strengthen the protective environment for vulnerable conflict-affected
persons in Libya through multi-purpose cash assistance. Without access to hard
currency due to the liquidity crisis, a decline in purchasing power due to inflation and covid-19 or no income available to meet their basic needs, vulnerable households suffer the most
from the effects of the protracted crisis, increasing their reliance on negative coping
mechanisms and exposure to protection threats. Therefore, DRC will provide multipurpose,

project_name: Building resilience through supporting basic needs and income-generating capacities within the Syrian Arab Republic
project_objective:
In line with SO1 “Enhance access to market-based livelihood opportunities and production”  DRC will support vulnerable conflict-affected populations toward self-sufficiency.  DRC will aim to achieve the below outcome: “To improve the adaptive capacities and socio-economic well-being of people, civic actors and communities”
Through:
-	 Increasing households’ income, assets, and consumption of needed goods and services. 
DRC believes that households’ income, assets, and consumption of needed goods (including food) and services will increase if people participate in functioning markets which will be restored if people have appropriate skills for income generation and employment; and if people have safe and equal access to capital, markets, and employment; and if business norms enable people’s equitable economic participation.  
-	Creating more cohesive, inclusive, and equitable communities in Syria.
In order for people to achieve cohesive, inclusive, and equitable communities, marginalized groups must be able to exercise social and economic influence equal to those of other dominant groups and participate in decision-making. A total of 1622 beneficiaries will be targeted through DRC intervention in Daraa, Homs, Hama, and Rural Damascus.
DRC will deliver Early Recovery assistance to persons of concern (PoCs) targeting conflict-affected youth and adults, men and women, including people with disabilities, to develop skills and increase income-generating opportunities with an aim to strengthen their access to livelihoods through microgrants for business development (start-up or scale-up), business development skills training, vocational training, distribution of toolkits in addition to the rehabilitation of community infrastructure restore or improve access to spaces in support of livelihoods. PoCs with protection-related concerns and vulnerabilities will be particularly targeted, and internal and external referrals will be made to ensure that protection services are provided in parallel based on identified needs. Initial needs assessments will be conducted jointly with MoE, MoSAL, and SARC field staff, when applicable. These assessments will allow DRC to select specific locations for its interventions where multi-sectoral assistance will respond to specific priority needs identified on the ground. In addition, at the beginning of 2021, a labor market assessment will be conducted to be informed on the type of training/internship services to provide, as well as the type of businesses to priorities within the business-start up support.

project_name: Protection risk response, prevention, and mitigation amongst conflict- and displacement-affected communities in Daraa

By which DRC interventions will assist in increasing access to life-saving emergency and life sustaining assistance, with the aim of maximizing the impact of humanitarian actions. DRC has the main office in Damascus and three working spaces across three governorates: Homs, Daraa, and Aleppo, while maintaining emergency response through Aleppo to Idleb and Hama. A total of 3,920 beneficiaries will be reached in different locations with a 3 and above severity scale where DRC will prevent, mitigate, and respond to acute protection risks aggravated by the COVID-19 pandemic, contributing to a strengthened protective environment for conflict and displacement affected individuals. DRC will achieve this through the following outcomes: 1. The well-being and coping capacities of vulnerable men, women, girls, and boys are enhanced through the provision of psychosocial support services. DRC has developed new PSS curricula to improve the well-being and coping capacities of men, women, girls, and boys, and with more age, gender, and diversity focus such as gender support groups, and stress management and empowerment for adolescents and children, as well as individual counseling for individuals requiring more targeted support.2. Men, women, girls, and boys are protected from the physical, mental, and social impacts of violence, abuse, exploitation, exposure to explosive hazards, and other protection threats through the provision of case management and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education.DRC will provide child protection, and human rights case management support to the most vulnerable men, women, girls, and boys that encounter protection threats such as violence, exploitation, abuse, neglect, psychological, and emotional harm, those at risk of eviction threats, with a view that severity and urgency of threats will be compounded by the effects of COVID-19 containment measures.  DRC will also aim to reduce the impact of EO on civilian populations in Syria, particularly as communities resort to more risk-taking activities as economic pressure heightens as a result of COVID-19 and the economic crisis in Syria. DRC will maintain its inclusive, community-based approaches, implementing activities with physical distancing safeguards in community centres where persons of concern can seek assistance. DRC continues to advocate with the Government of Syria for the expansion of humanitarian access to underserved areas. For access at the local level, DRC engages with mukhtars, governors, line ministries, and SARC branches. DRC has engaged in discussions with the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) for further work on the threat of explosive hazards in Syria.

project_name: Shelter and NFIs Assistance to Crisis affected population in Somalia
project_objective:
The project will target affected population groups (newly displaced populations, IDPs living in a protracted situation, refugee returnees and affected host communities) with shelter and NFI interventions. The interventions include provision of NFI kit, emergency shelter and transitional shelter. 

According to JMCNA 2020, Shelter is the first priority need of more than half of the population. 3.15 million people are in need of shelter and NFI assistance mainly due to inadequate shelter conditions, overcrowding, economic hardship and lack of security of tenure. Those in need of shelter and NFI assistance include IDPs, poor host communities, refugees and asylum seekers and refugee returnees.  Factors that have been considered for calculating the severity and people in need include shelter conditions, type of shelter, overcrowding, availability of NFIs at household level and security of tenure.

UNHCR plans to distribute NFI kits to 90,000 households (HH) in kind/cash, provision of emergency shelters to 25,000 HH and transitional shelters to 500 HH. The project will target 540,000 individuals with NFI kits, 150,000 individuals with emergency shelters and 3,000 individuals with transitional shelters. NFI, emergency shelters and transitional shelters assistance will be provided in cash or in kind and the response modality will depend on the availability of items in the local market, user preference and associated protection risks.

UNHCR will carry out Post Distribution Monitoring and will establish Complaints, Response and Feedback Mechanism for each project. The Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercise will be conducted 4-6 weeks after NFIs and ESKs distribution to analyze the impact of the project, the beneficiaries’ level of satisfaction and establish the lessons learnt for future programming

UNHCR will target vulnerable HH including women headed households, child headed households, households with persons with disabilities and households with the elderly. 

UNHCR will undertake infrastructure support targeting 8,250 vulnerable households (49,500 individuals). Site decongestion through expanding the site using available adjacent land and through basic site planning will be a priority and will be implemented where feasible under infrastructure support. Most of the IDPs live in the sites that are overcrowded and are not planned, leading to the increased risk of fire outbreak, spread of diseases including COVID 19, GBV related incidences and flooding due to the absence of or poor drainage system. 

UNHCR will target a total of 543,000 individuals of the 2.5 million individuals targeted by the Shelter Cluster with assistance. Of the targeted individuals, 83,803 women, 81,616 men, 170,927 girls, 184,794 boys, 21,860 elderly and 81,450 disabled individuals. The project targets 108,600 vulnerable individuals from the host community and 434,400 vulnerable IDPs. The targeting will occur based on UNHCR and Shelter Cluster assessments for those most in need and highly vulnerable. The project will target Bari, Banadir, Bay, Lower Juba, Gedo, Mudug, Hiraan, Nugaal, Middle Shabelle, Lower Shabelle and Woqooyi Galbeed regions. 

The activities will be implemented through partners. UNHCR will monitor the activities through the Implementing Partners. Settlement leaders and local authorities will participate in different phases of the interventions. Monthly project tracking will be carried out and 4W matrix inputs shared on monthly basis with Somalia National Shelter Cluster.
