Así como también DRC cuenta con un instrumento de asistencia individualizado para proveer asistencia en especie de acuerdo con las necesidades identificada (articulo no alimenticios, apoyo en salud incluyendo medicinas, alojamiento de emergencia, etc, a casos identificados previamente en los espacios de atención del proyecto esta asistencia individual de protección denominada IPA por sus siglas en ingles son la fuente principal del trabajo en comunidades e identificación de necesidades especificas por parte del trabajo que DRC realiza en Venezuela.

project_name: WASH emergency response to the most affected Women, men, Boys and Girls in Yobe and Borno state
project_objective: The proposed project for 2021 will contribute to the WASH sector 2019-2021 strategy.  Project will be achieved by increasing sustainable use of gender sensitive emergency WASH services such as water supply and sanitation and hygiene promotion sessions, and ensuring that conflict affected populations receive immediate assistance and operation and maintainace support. The project will provide WASH assistance at IDP in camps and community level as well as in health facilities and schools. It will enable male, female, boys and girls to have improved access to safe drinking water in secure places, enhance their knowledge on WASH practices, prevent COVID 19, reduce prevalence of diarrhea and ultimately also lead towards improved nutrition security.  This will be achieved through a combination of interventions such as construction/rehabilitation of water points, Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), formation and training of WASH COMs with 40-50% female and building capacity of government authorities to effectively provide lifesaving assistance and have improved capacity to meet the immediate needs of newly displaced or returning populations. Throughout the course of the project, the active participation of women in the design, implementation and sustainability of interventions will be ensured and protection needs of women and girls will be identified and integrated into programming

project_name: Integrated Food Security and Livelihoods Protection Project
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support in a way that prevents the spread & transmission of COVID 19 for households classified in Crisis (IPC 5, 4 and some 3) in Panyijiar and Mayendit counties (Unity state), Aweil South (NBeG state) of South Sudan. The IRC proposes to provide a sequence of emergency food production to support the most severe food-insecure households in Panyijiar, Aweil South, and Mayendit counties from the 2021 lean season. To augment household resilience, the program will mainstream gender, conflict sensitivity, disaster risks reduction, and COVID-19 risk mitigation measures to support at-risk households focused on improving crop, livestock, and fisheries production and bolstering resilience towards recurrent shocks and stresses in communities. In pursuit of the program objective, the following activities will be implemented: 
(a) Engagement and consultation of community and local leaders to confirm needs and agree on most vulnerable household’s selection criteria and register beneficiaries. 
(b) Preposition and distribute emergency (short-term maturing) agricultural inputs (seeds and tools) and fishing kits including through input trade fairs (ITF) to farmers where the market is functioning and inputs available. The IRC anticipates the Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO) will provide complimentary in-kind inputs to support the project. ITFs will be utilized to promote restocking of mainly small ruminants (sheep and goats’ assets) and backyard poultry targeting households with malnourished mothers, Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), and most vulnerable households including flood and conflict-affected female-headed households, widows, and widowers, and the elderly. During distribution, IRC will engage community health volunteers to disseminate COVID-19 messages, provide personal protective kits including facemasks, and limit crowd at distribution points following COVID-19 protocols. 
(c) The IRC in collaboration with the County Agriculture Department (CAD), State Ministries of Agriculture, and FAO, will contribute to livestock disease surveillance and monitoring, and facilitate vaccination campaigns, mass vaccination exercises, and treatments to livestock in the three targeted counties. 
(d) Facilitate capacity building to county-level extension agents (CAHWs, AEA’s), local crop producers, pastoralists, and fisherfolks on sustainable production skills and provision of extension services around the package of production inputs and post-harvest handling to be provided through the climate-smart vegetable and crop demonstration gardens established. Also, fisherfolks receive basic training on fish preservation and kit repairs to enhance household’s nutrition and income.
The IRC will mainstream gender equity and promote gender inclusiveness, allowing the most vulnerable and disadvantaged women, girls, boys, and men to have equal participation in the program and to realize benefits for their own wellbeing. A participatory beneficiary identification and selection including agreeing on affirmative action to register at least 70% female beneficiaries. Community-led project feedback and complaint mechanism to established to foster equal chances for female and male to voice their complaints and feedback. Complementary programming will be promoted through vigorous coordination with health and nutrition, protection.
Overall, the IRC will reach 23% of the most vulnerable households’ classified in IPC Phase 5 and 4 in Panyijiar (22,080), Mayendit (29,353) and Aweil South (45,033). This is equivalent to a total of 96,367 (36,936 Women, 23,917Men, 19,258Girls, 16,255Boys) beneficiaries. By program type: 96,367 through input trade fairs, 48,183 through production skills training (50%), 12,833through small ruminants and poultry restocking and livestock vaccinations, 35,350through fisheries.

project_name: Strengthening child protection prevention and response mechanisms for vulnerable and at-risk children, and survivors of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation in Rohingya Camps and host communities through equitable access to quality child protection services
project_objective:
PIB CPiE will focus on vulnerable and at-risk children, survivors of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation, adolescents and youth through two interlinking components – qualitative case management and community-based child protection (CBCP). The services will ensure boys, girls and adolescents in the Rohingya camps and host communities are safe and protected from violence, abuse and exploitation. 
Age appropriate, gender responsive and timely individual Case Management Services will be provided for vulnerable CAYs targeting unaccompanied and separated children, child-headed households, children in psychosocial distress, children with specific needs, and child survivors of GBV.  PIB will mainstream with education team by ensuring safety and dignity of beneficiaries and avoid causing harm to the children, and will build the capacity of EIE staff on referrals. 
CBCP activities will be structured through feedback from community consultation and participation to ensure inclusion and ownership by both the host and the refugee community. The interventions will ensure inclusion of CAYs, persons with disability and the youths. Community-level interventions will include promoting social cohesion and strengthening self-protection of children. Addressing harmful practices and attitudes, Plan will invest in active community participation and positive parenting. 
PIB is accountable and will ensure that child friendly feedback mechanisms are in place with strong emphasis on PSEA and Child Safeguarding.  PIB will ensure its partners have PSEA policies and the same is implemented.
PIB is committed to coordinating the response through active participation in sectors such as Protection, Education, GBV and Child Protection Sub-Sector and other working groups to ensure meaningful access, prioritization of safety and integration of services.  The services offered will be in line with CPMS, interagency tools and SOPs, and will be ensured through structured training enhancing competencies in providing quality gender-responsive and timely services.
Plan will undertake several assessments such as baseline, midterm, impact assessment, and will collect disaggregated data including people with disability. Plan will also use Washington Questionnaire to better understand the need and requirement of people with disability.

project_name: Developing Early recovery And Livelihood (DEAL)
project_objective:
The early recovery and livelihood activities are much needed for the communities in order to respond to the acute need for the communities and enhance their resilience especially in the areas of high severity scale. The areas which witnessed a high level of returnee movements are suffering from lack of basic services like water, electricity, schools and income generation activities given into account the high unemployment rates for the population. 
ADRA Syria has selected the most vulnerable communities, in line with the ERL sector and OCHA guideline and will respond to the most urgent needs within the populations in early recovery in Rural Homs (Rural Al-Qusair) and Rural Aleppo ( Der Hafer, Tal-Ed-daman and Bnan) . These areas have been assessed and considered high severity where resources and services were limited. In addition, ADRA Syria is proposing livelihood intervention through small business grants targeting the most vulnerable communities who lost their assets during the Syrian Crisis and capacity building along with Cash for work for the youth in Rural Aleppo.   
The project will be targeting a total of 45,000 beneficiaries including (12,600 Men, 12,1260 women, 9,900 boys and 9,900 girls) , the project will be also targeting 500 youth including ( 250 boys, 250 girls)  through life skills training sessions and cash for work in order to empower youth and support the families in generating income.
The project will begin from coordination meetings with related stakeholders like local ministries ( MoSAL, MoLA, MoE), to receive necessary approvals and conduct needed technical and vulnerability assessments in the targeted locations. Coordination with SARC, ERL Sector, Protection sector, education sector and GBV subsector throughout the project implementation in order to coordinate the response and avoid any duplication of provided services to the targeted communities. ADRA Syria will ensure proper monitoring of the project activities through developed MEAL plan, monitoring tools and evaluation tools. 
The project activities will be conducted through qualified ADRA female and male staff in close coordination with key stakeholders. In addition, for the livelihood activities ADRA will partner with SARC in order to deliver the needed assistant to the most vulnerable groups among the community including youth girls and boys, women and men, people with disabilities. This will enhance the mitigation and response to address the needs of boys, girls, people with disability and vulnerable communities.

project_name: Protective and adaptive Education Approaches for Children in Emergencies (PEACE)
project_objective:
In recognition that conflict-affected primary school-aged children in Nigeria, Niger, and Cameroon face major challenges to accessing quality education and protection services, IRC Deutschland proposes to partner with ECHO under the Pilot Programmatic Partnership to deliver the 3-year PEACE project. PEACE takes an integrated and adaptive approach to education and child protection, to support 171,065 school-aged boys and girls, their carers and educators, most affected by crisis across target countries to access and learn in safe educational environments. The PEACE evidence-based approach towards improving educational access, quality, and safety builds on previous IRC programming and includes: 
1.	Four core models to expand access to formal and non-formal education that is conflict-sensitive and designed to support children who are most in need;
2.	Support to caregivers and communities so that they may more fully ensure girls’ and boys’ safety, access, and learning; and 
3.	Capacity building of teachers and facilitators in order to improve the quality of instruction and provide safe learning environments for children. 
Child protection measures are integrated throughout PEACE, from individual case management support to individual and group psycho-social support activities for caregivers and children. 
In light of the COVID 19 pandemic, PEACE will adapt programming to ensure the continuity of child protection and learning support in safe environments, as well as COVID-19-specific messaging related to health and or WASH.

project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des communautés dans la prévention et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë dans le district sanitaire de Bokoro
project_objective:
Afin d’améliorer la situation nutritionnelle dans le District Sanitaire de Bokoro, le présent projet a pour objectif global de contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité associées à la malnutrition chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes, et plus spécifiquement, de renforcer la fonctionnalité et la couverture des services sanitaires et communautaires selon l'approche des 1000 jours dans le District Sanitaire (DS) de Bokoro. A noter que les 18 centres de santé (CdS) que recense le DS seront appuyés par le projet.
Pour ce faire, les actions portées par le projet tournent autour de trois résultats : 
•	« La mobilisation communautaire favorise des pratiques de soins favorables au sein des communautés » : Grâce à la mise en œuvre de diagnostics communautaires, les pratiques courantes liées aux soins, à l’alimentation et à l’hygiène seront identifiées et améliorées grâce à la mise en place de groupes de soins (Care Groups) formés notamment sur les Pratiques Familiales Essentielles qui auront pour objectif la promotion de la santé dans leur localité afin de promouvoir le changement de comportement. Cette mobilisation communautaire se traduit par la mise en place de la formation PB-mères qui sera également assurée par les Care Groups au sein de leur communauté dans le but de dépister de manière précoce la malnutrition chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois.  
•	« L’accès et la qualité des services de santé sont améliorés dans le district à travers la fenêtre d’opportunité 1000 jours » : Les 1000 premiers jours de vie d’un enfant sont déterminants pour lui assurer une bonne santé et un développement favorable. Ainsi, il est prévu de renforcer les compétences des agents de santé sur la consultation prénatale et la préparation à l’accouchement afin de surveiller l’évolution de la grossesse des mamans et d’administrer les soins adéquats. Des évaluations des CdS ainsi que des donations en matériels, médicaments et consommables seront effectués afin d’améliorer le fonctionnement des CdS et la qualité des prises en charge dispensées. La qualité des services de soin passe également par une bonne gestion des CdS. C’est pourquoi le projet prévoit également d’assurer la présence et le bon fonctionnement de Comités de Gestion (COGES) et du Comité Directeur pour assurer le bon suivi et la bonne réponse du District Sanitaire. 
•	« Les capacités de préparation et de réponse du système de santé sont renforcées pour faire face aux pics sanitaires » : Chaque année, les structures sanitaires connaissent des pics d’admissions pendant la période de soudure, entrainant ainsi une surcharge de travail pour le personnel de santé ce qui n’est pas sans conséquence sur la qualité de prise en charge nutritionnelle. Pour pallier à ce problème, le projet prévoit le déploiement de l’approche Surge pour assurer la bonne préparation et gestion de pics de la malnutrition aiguë et garantir une bonne qualité au niveau des soins dispensés. Par ailleurs, afin de prendre en compte le contexte sanitaire actuel, le projet prévoit de doter les CdS en kits de protection et prévoit également la mise en place d’un dispositif de triage au sein de chaque centre afin de diminuer la propagation de la Covid-19.

project_name: Strengthening Equitable Access to Inclusive, gender responsive and quality Learning opportunities and Community Support through system strengthening mechanism for Rohingya Refugee and Crisis-Affected Host Community Girls, Boys and Youth in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
In 2021, PIB will continue to support the Cox's Bazar (CXB) Education Sector's JRP in both camp and crisis-affected host communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf . 
Building on the current and prior experience, PIB will continue to ensure and expand education access at all levels, with an extended focus to early childhood education, secondary education, and education for adolescents and youth both in camp and HC. In camps, PIB will sustain its community-based learning facilities (CBLF) and deliver strengthened caregiver-led education approaches in response to the new challenges of COVID-19. 
Capacity building trainings for the relevant education staffs, learning facilitators and teachers both in camps and HC, will aim to strengthen the quality of teaching and learning process through a blended approach across the age spectrum targeted by Education Sector. Regular monitoring of the progress will be ensured through a continuous support of on-the-job coaching and mentoring. In 2021, education staffs and respective Govt. education officials will be further supported to provide better mentoring support to learning facilitators and teachers for inclusive, quality education. 
PIB will continue to ensure community engagement and ownership in education by building the capacities of Learning Facility Committees in the camps to support equitable access to education, safeguarding and protection, DRM including stablishing effective accountability mechanism. Adolescents and youth will be supported to be the champion of the change, to lead social cohesion initiatives to promote values of equality, tolerance and inclusion within the camps and across the HC. PIB has a unique and sustained focus on caregiver engagement in ECD, having rolled out a Parenting Education package in 2021
Finally, PIB will extend support to localization through coordination and capacity building of local partners and Government counterparts with the aim to move to a sustainable quality of education goal and strengthen the respective system.

project_name: Improving the food security of vulnerable communities in Syria
project_objective:
Multiple conflict-related protection risks persist and have been further compounded by the financial crisis and COVID-19 outbreak which has eroded family coping strategies and forced girls and boys who would previously have been in school into harmful practices, including begging, child labour and child marriage. In December 2020, communities reported weather-related challenges, seasonality of production and the increased prices of fertilizers as key barriers to income generation. At the same time, neither the host communities, nor the IDP camp residents reported ongoing livelihood assistance in their respective areas. 88% and 73% of interviewed household reported insufficient income and lack of employment opportunities matching people’s skills. These barriers were coupled with the worsening economic situation resulting in increasing food prices, and the rising cost of the survival minimum expenditure basket (SMEB) (REACH, HSOS Dec 2020). In NES, for example, both IDPs and host communities currently rely heavily on intermittent unskilled daily wage labor with low wages. A high number of adolescents and youth have missed critical years of schooling and lack basic literacy and numeracy skills which are critical for the work-force and entrepreneurship. As a result, many have turned to negative coping mechanisms, such as child labor and skipping meals (WFP Food Security Update, March 2020).

Over the last year in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, food prices across Syria have hugely increased and the value of the Syrian Pound has plummeted. The depreciation of the Syrian pound (SYP) spiraled spiking at a record low of SYP 4,700/USD 1 on 17 March 2021 before stabilizing around SYP 3,700/USD 1 by late March 2021. As a result, it is expected that the food security situation and nutrition status of the most vulnerable will worsen in the coming months (UNICEF Whole of Syria Situation Analysis, March 2021).

To address these needs, Save the Children will target conflict-affected boys and girls and their families with  monthly food baskets. SC will aim to meet the nutritional needs of households as much as possible through providing monthly food baskets which contain 1550 Kcal per person per day (nutritional contribution: 59% of energy to be contributed by carbohydrates, 12% from proteins and 29% from fat). According to the FSL Working Group, there was significant funding gap in NES in food assistance starting from April 2021. After the coordinated effort by the FSL Working Group with all the FSL actors in NES, Save the Children was requested to cover for Tel Samen camp for the duration of April to December 2021. In addition to this, Save the Children will provide monthly food baskets as emergency support to the vulnerable people identified in other locations as well. The most appropriate modality (in-kind support, cash or voucher assistance) will be selected based on the targeted locations, and in consultations with the beneficiaries and local stakeholders. The distributions in camps are made in-kind from the distribution point or tent-to-tent based on the procedure set by the Camp Administration. The food baskets will be distributed targeting the most vulnerable, food insecure households in areas with low service coverage, and the targeted locations will be identified in close coordination with the FSL WG. The targeting criteria will be adapted to the local context in order to identify the most vulnerable food insecure households in the area. In Tel Samen, the distribution is blanket distribution. For other emergency food support, the criteria are child-headed household, single women and people with disabilities. If there is only one person in the family, half basket is provided for a month, 2-6 family members one basket is provided for a month and more than 7 members 2 baskets are provided for a month.

It is estimated that the project will reach 20,000 individuals.

project_name: Humanitarian coordination and provision of CCCM-integrated responses to displacement-affected populations in Juba and Bor former PoC sites (static) and in hard-to-reach areas (mobile)
project_objective:
In line with the CCCM cluster strategy for 2021, ACTED will implement its CCCM interventions through static response in Juba and Bor former PoC sites and mobile responses in locations with emergency needs and in hard-to-reach areas. 

ACTED’s added-value in multisectoral emergency response lie primarily in building resilience through site planning, coordination and advocacy which ultimately empowers the Community.  In particular, the response includes: 
-	Restructuring and capacity building of governance thru representative Community Management Committees.  
-	Communities identify prominent risks in a facilitative process to agree on site maintenance and planning works, as well as contingency plans which mitigate risk of corresponding hazard. 
-	ACTED provides a mapping of service provision and site profiles to be shared with humanitarian coordination forums for advocacy for future action.  
-	Protection Focal Points are trained in the Community to establish a referral pathway identified during service monitoring to be maintained after the intervention. 
-	Communities are supported thru a Community-Led Initiative to improve livelihoods.  
-	Local partners are also trained in coordination and service monitoring

A shock is flagged through clusters, working groups, ICCGs, and/or humanitarian coordination fora. After a shock, ACTED is able to deploy a team in 3-5 days to conduct a scoping assessment, which will last apprx. 3 days to complete. Tools such as site profiles and site monitoring matrix 3Ws are shared with partners. In line with pipeline availability, ACTED will immediately launch a multisectoral response as per the identified needs of the targeted communities. The intervention duration will usually last between 4-6 weeks. ACTED will coordinate with all the clusters, working groups and humanitarian coordination fora as well as reaching out to ECHO and RRM partners to avoid duplication. ACTED will also coordinate with RRC, local partners, mobile partners, and cluster state focal points.  In addition to activities surrounding service monitoring, ACTED will train local partners on coordination mechanisms to avoid duplication of response. Apprx.,2-3 months after an intervention is complete, ACTED will return to the location to conduct a post intervention/distribution monitoring and will share the results with the relevant clusters. 

In addition to the current modality responding to emergencies resulting in displacement, ACTED mobile team will pilot a response to areas of potential and actual returns to improve governance and resilience.  This response will be coordinated with UNHCR’s intention survey, or target sites of shocks from previous years.

ACTED will start to move from static response to semi-static activity provision in former POCs by gradually transferring more responsibilities of camp management to IDP leadership for the purpose of sustainability.

ACTED will conduct border monitoring activities at 8 border crossings in Eastern Equatoria to ensure humanitarian actors have reliable and accurate data to inform programming.

project_name: Provision of quality education services to affected children of IDPs, Returnees and Host communities in Fangak, and Ayod Counties of Jonglei State and Nasir County of Upper Nile State in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project is in line with HRP 2021 objective 1 and 2 and also with cluster/sector specific objectives 1, 2 & 3, Besides, it aligns with the cluster strategy to ‘Ensure safe, equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services to enable populations meet their basic needs in locations of severity level 4 and 5’. This project will improve access to safe, quality and inclusive protective education services to 12,000 emergency and COVID-19 affected children (boys, girls and youths) in Fangak, Ayod and Nasir Counties by 2021. The integrated education project by ADA in hard-to-reach areas aims to ensure that children (boys and girls) have access to quality and inclusive education and those already in schools are retained in Nasir County (Upper Nile State), Fangak and Ayod Counties (Jonglei State). The following interventions are envisaged: establishing safe learning and recreational facilities in 12 locations – 4 in each County; teacher training to enhance the teaching/learning function supported in schools; providing monthly stipends to 84 volunteer teachers - 28 teachers per County; campaign for education, encouraging children, especially girls and people with disability to return to school; and provision of school feeding programs to enhance attendance and retention of children at schools. Response priorities will include gender-segregated WASH facilities with much concentration in COVID-19 prevention measures, inclusion of GBV counselling rooms in the schools, provision of learning, teaching and WASH materials, capacity building of School Management Committees (SMCs) and Parents Teachers Associations (PTAs), life-skills and recreational opportunities to support the recovery of children and to promote their overall well-being. Equal access to inclusive education will be prioritized regardless of gender, disability or ethnic background. Through introduction of school gender-sensitive WASH programme, this project will have established strong WASH facilities in schools. The project will seek to support prevention of COVID-19 through rehabilitation/construction of hand-washing facilities and latrines, provision of soap, face masks, sensitizers and maintenance of social distancing. Carry out messaging on coronavirus signs and symptoms, modes of transmission and prevention to children and their parents.
The project will seek to address one of the top causes of school drop-outs (School feeding) that will help increase and maintain school enrolment and attendance, and reduce risks of death, disease and cognitive underdevelopment. School feeding will also improve protection of- in-school and out of school children by keeping them away from potential recruitment into armed groups, child labor, early marriage, exploitation, sexual violence and abduction while on their way to schools and back home. This will help to reduce morbidity and absenteeism, support retention in schools and children to help sensitize their communities. Crisis-affected children will be engaged in basic education and recreational activities in order to create an enabling environment for their critical development and positive engagement with the community. Youths will catch up on primary education through accelerated learning programmes (ALP) to improve their literacy and numeracy, technical and vocational training, and life skills. The project will seek to include physically and mentally challenged children; girls and boys vulnerable to recruitment into armed groups, and child labour; youths; adolescent heads of households; young mothers; and children from different ethnic groups. Teachers, SMCs and PTAs will be trained on life skills and referral pathways to enhance the protective aspect of education in emergency (EiE) intervention. The project will include early childhood development program across schools in the project sites.

project_name: Mejora del acceso de la población vulnerable a servicios básicos de WASH en establecimientos de salud y atención nutricional, instituciones educativas y espacios de protección
project_objective:
El sector de agua, saneamiento e higiene es esencial en la mejora de los servicios de salud, nutrición, educación y protección y para el impacto de los niños, niñas y adolescentes en términos de salud, nutrición, educación y protección. Todo programa de salud, nutrición, educación y protección debe ir acompañado de un componente de WASH. 
La crisis de COVID19 ha demostrado la importancia de WASH y de estrategias IPC en los establecimientos de salud, e igualmente la vulnerabilidad de la situación en Venezuela. Al analizar la situación actual en Venezuela, las diferentes fuentes destacan el deterioro de las condiciones de higiene del entorno en la atención sanitaria, la falta de acceso a agua en las escuelas que contribuye al absentismo escolar, y considerando el aumento de las tasas de prevalencia de la desnutrición es incuestionable que cualquier medida debe ir acompañada de acciones en agua, saneamiento e higiene en los lugares de atención y de recuperación nutricional.
Con este proyecto, se da continuidad a los esfuerzos desarrollados en 2020 para la mejora de los servicios WASH en las establecimientos e instituciones estratégicas de los servicios de salud, nutrición, educación y protección (incluyendo puntos estratégicos asociados a procesos migratorios, como centros de migrantes, terminales, etc.). 
El OBJETIVO del proyecto es mejorar los servicios de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene en los establecimientos de salud, instituciones educativas y proteción; para contribuir a la reducción de la mortalidad y morbilidad materno-infantil, considerando el contexto de COVID19, y acompañando estrategias de Prevención y Control de Infecciones, Alimentación Escolar, Retorno a las escolaridad, Nutrición y  Protección.
Para implementar WASH en las instituciones, en función del nivel de intervención se incluirán los siguientes elementos para la mejora de los servicios WASH, según la pertinencia y el contexto:
-	Diagnóstico participativo de las instalaciones, incluyendo elementos de género, AAP, discapacidad y participación adolescente. 
-	Reparación, rehabilitación y acondicionamiento de instalaciones WASH, bajo estándares de resiliencia, seguridad y sostenibilidad 
-	Fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal técnico, para la promoción de la higiene, el mantenimiento y para el tratamiento y conservación del agua, bajo criterios de prevención y control de las enfermedades infecciosas, WASHFIT, WASH y NUT y enfoque de 3 estrellas (UNICEF). 
-	Actividades de promoción de la higiene, vinculadas con enfoques comunitarios
-	Distribución de suministros básicos y productos de higiene
-	Mejora del acceso a agua a través de camiones cisterna, realización de pozos, cloradores electrolíticos, instalación de tanques, rehabilitación de sistemas de bombeo, instalaciones intrahospitalarias, etc. 
-	Mejora del saneamiento a través de la rehabilitación de los sistemas y del mantenimiento.
-	Aplicación de estrategias de IPC – prevención y control de infecciones y WASHFIT en establecimientos de salud
-	Aplicación de estrategias de IPC, retorno a las clases y WASH + alimentación escolar.
-	Mejora de los servicios WASH en los Puntos de Atención Social Integral.
-      Adaptación de las respuesta a la evoluación del contexto COVID19. 
El proyecto se implementará en estrecha coordinación con las autoridades responsables de los servicios de agua y saneamiento, tales como Ministerio de Atención para las Aguas (incluye HidroVen y las delegaciones estatales) y Municipalidades, Ministerio de Educación, Ministerio de Salud e Instituciones de Protección. La relación de trabajo con gobierno e instituciones estará basada en la identificación de necesidades, generación de evidencias para adaptar las estrategias, la formación y la asistencia técnica. Todas la respuesta WASH en establecimientos se implementará a través de mecanismos directos y el trabajo con socios, la implicación de las comunidades, el personal técnico de los establecimientos y las autoridades.

project_name: Building Resilience of Vulnerable Populations to Improve Food Security and Livelihoods through Community-Based Agriculture and Livestock Support, Vocational Trainings and Income Generating Activities in Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen the resilience and coping capacities of vulnerable mobile populations, including Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees and their host community to enhance food and livelihood security as well as to mitigate the risk of malnutrition and poverty. This will be achieved through delivering agricultural, livestock interventions vocational trainings and alternative income generating activities. Despite the growing humanitarian needs, the planned activities will promote the synergy between increased agricultural production and the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN). 
The interventions will target the most vulnerable small-scale farmers, IDPs, returnees and local communities with special attention to youths and women. IOM will apply a right based, community centered approach to promote community initiatives and sow the seeds for durable solutions and ensure that planned interventions are met, based on needs and the rights of the vulnerable migrants and community, to access improved economic opportunities. 
The project will focus on ten localities and this includes: El Fasher locality (North Darfur), Geneina and Krenik localities (West Darfur), Al Radoum ,Rahad El Berdi and Um Dafug localities (South Darfur), Ghubaysh localitiy (West Kordofan State), Wad Al Mahi and Ar Rusayris localities, (Blue Nile State) and Dourdeb locality (Red Sea State). Returnees, IDPs and local communities in these localities are vulnerable to food insecurity and limited livelihood opportunities due to limited purchasing power resulting from inflation and high staple food prices. This contributes towards food insecurity alongside chronic and severe malnutrition. The identified localities suffered from the high prevalence in Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) phase 3 (Crisis) and/or phase 4 (Emergency) further highlighting the need for timely and adequate livelihood interventions to address food insecurity, strengthen community resilience to protect lives, and move towards economic self-sufficiency.

Under HRP 2021, this project aligns with Objectives 2 and 3. The planned interventions will include: (1) Community needs assessments and capacity building for local production cooperatives and inputs on agriculture employing climate adaptation techniques whilst promoting synergies with natural resource management and climate change mitigation, alleviating protection concerns and increasing the resilience of communities in coping with disasters. (2) support sustainable livestock husbandry practice and veterinary services (3) small business support and vocational trainings for youth and women on agriculture and other livelihood skills such as food processing activities to enhance community resilience and reinvigorate local economies through the creation of small businesses. IOM has already established a good access to the most of target localities including (Dourdeb, Krenik, Al Radoum, Geneina, Um Dafug, El Fasher), and seeks to continue implementing community stabilization and durable solution initiative activities under UNDAF outcomes. The planned interventions will be delivered in a way to complement past and on-going activities implemented, thereby strengthening links between the HRP Outcomes and UNDAF Outcomes.

project_name: School Meals Programme to support 75,000 school children in the Far North, North, Adamaoua, North West and South West Regions
project_objective:
Through the project WFP will implement a Home grown school meal programme in the Far North, North, Adamaoua, North-West and South-West Regions targeting school children in the most crisis affected divisions. The project aims to provide school meals to 75,000 children to encourage and promote school attendance. A consequence of the crisis in these regions, many schools were closed leaving thousands of children out of school for many years mainly in the targeted divisions. With the improvement observed in the security situation in the areas and thanks to the humanitarian support from UN agencies, and NGOs many children have been able to go back to school. The project will contribute to maintain those who are already in the school till the completion of the primary school cycle. 
The project will consist of providing daily meals using locally produced food to all the children during 165 days of the school year, to encourage them to attend and stay in schools throughout the school year, thus contributing to improve their nutritional status as well as to protect them enrolment by the terrorist groups. The transfer modality of e-voucher will be used. e-voucher rations (Home Grown School Feeding). WFP funds will be transferred directly to schools, to enable them buy food from local suppliers and farmers. This contribute to: 1- increase in local production, promote market access to small farmers; while 2- promoting improving schooling, attendance, performance and completion Funds are transferred from WFP to school accounts. Each school feeding Programme committee manages tenders and purchases food from local suppliers (traders or farmers) with a bank account for school meals.  Parents, local councils, other actors and communities will complement with various items including water, firewood and cooking services and other locally produced food. During the implementation, special attention will be paid to children with disabilities. Their food will be collected and served in at their sitting place.
Various actions will be put in place to support the implementation of the project. Capacity strengthening sessions will be organized on school feeding management, food storage, gender and Protection, for all actors involved in the school canteens management including other partners operating in the targeted division such as local councils, Parent and Teachers’ Associations, mothers’ associations and Government staff form the Ministries of Basic Education, agriculture, Health, Women affairs and social Affairs. In addition, Mothers' associations will be sensitized and trained on nutrition aspects using locally available food.

project_name: Prevention of under nutrition among children 6 23 months,  in vulnerable districts in the Far North region
project_objective:
WFP is implementing a nutrition response frame with stronger focus towards prevention
of malnutrition. The programme focuses on preventing malnutrition amongst the most
vulnerable populations through strengthening supplementary feeding with focus on the first 1000days of life. The programme targets all children aged 6-23 months including
those children suffering from moderate acute malnutrition-MAM) as well as for children
24-59 months with MAM in the most food insecure departments presenting highest GAM
rates in the Far North, North, Adamawa, and East region, while in the North west and south
west region the programme targets children aged 6-23 months and pregnant and lactating
women and girls in food insecure household. The programme activities include:
1.Screening for malnutrition and referral of severe cases for treatment;
2.Promotion of infant and young child feeding practices
3.Distribution of specialized nutritious food to children aged 6-23months and Pregnant
and lactating women and girls(PLWGs)
4.Social and behavioral change communication in favor of good nutrition and health
practices
5.Promotion of the use of the blanket feeding platform or provision of complementary
services including immunization, micro-nutrient supplementation, deworming, malaria and
other childhood illnesses prevention, family planning etc
WFP in 2022 intends to target about 43150 beneficiaries in the Far North region

project_name: Provision of lifesaving integrated Gender Based Violence and Sexual Reproductive Health prevention and response services for Rohingya refugees and host communities in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
UNFPA will continue to promote, coordinate and provide accessible, confidential, survivor-centered services to address GBV in line with the Inter-Agency Standards for GBV in emergency programming with special considerations and programming to DRR and COVID-19. UNFPA will continue supporting 35 Women Friendly Spaces and selected health facilities (13) that offer integrated GBV - SRHR services which include GBV case management, mental health, and psychosocial support services, clinical management of rape, family planning services and counseling, treatment of sexually transmitted infections, and emergency referrals to GBV survivors including vulnerable women and girls. By providing multi-sectorial services, UNFPA enhances the health sector response to GBV with a one-stop-shop model ensuring a rights-based approach to GBV. The integration will also ensure SRH staff are trained on GBV principles including confidentiality and consent. The focus will also be placed on prevention and mitigation strategies, mechanisms, and initiatives to support community-based interventions in line with IASC principles and strengthening guidelines. The project will ensure community engagement and awareness aimed at mobilizing communities.  This includes youth and men by utilizing tested SASA! Together methodology to address negative social norms and to prevent and respond to GBV in a safe and timely manner. SASA! Together methodology involves everyone and engages a critical mass of people across all levels of society in order to create social norm change and social cohesion between refugee and host communities.  As women and girls continue to face protection risks, advocacy and communication for change will be implemented to guarantee their dignity and safety. Through a prioritization towards the safeguarding of beneficiaries, UNFPA will continue to collaborate with the PSEA network to ensure a robust implementation of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse reporting and response mechanisms. 
Under the leadership of UNFPA, the GBV sub-sector will enhance engagement with other sectors and government for integration of GBV prevention, mitigation, and response programming for quality services of GBV survivors using Inter-Agency Minimum Standards. The sub-sector will expand comprehensive GBV prevention and response programs for women, and girls, focusing on case management and multi-sectoral referral systems. Capacities will be enhanced on the IASC GBV Guidelines to sector leads, government stakeholders, and implementing partners fostering effective coordination in planning, implementing, and monitoring essential GBV risk mitigation actions in all humanitarian response and services. This will be supported with regular community-based GBV risk monitoring and joint safety audits. The JRP 2022, will deliberately target disability inclusion in GBViE response.

project_name: La réponse multisectorielle pour les réfugiés au Niger en 2022
Acceso a los derechos y servicios básicos y asistencia humanitaria para las personas refugiadas y solicitantes de asilo, las personas en movilidad y las comunidades de acogida en Venezuela.
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivos la prevención, mitigación de riesgos y protección de las personas de interés del ACNUR en 71 comunidades priorizadas de Venezuela. Se trata de un proyecto multisectorial que trabajará en función a los derechos, servicios básicos y asistencia humanitaria para responder a problemas identificados tales como: 
1. Falta de acceso a servicios de asistencia y asesoría legal, así como a documentación legal. 
2. Incidentes de violencia de género y protección contra el abuso y explotación sexuales, acceso limitado para sobrevivientes a servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva, legales y de atención psicosocial.
3. Dificultades constructivas y de mantenimiento en espacios de alojamiento individual y temporal.
4. Deficiencia en el servicio eléctrico y ausencia de energías alternativas.
5. Limitado suministro del agua, así como su inadecuado almacenamiento, manejo y disposición final.
6. Dificultades de las organizaciones comunitarias para enfrentar sus problemas; falta de espacios para llevar a cabo actividades comunitarias.
7. Insuficientes ingresos familiares para cubrir las necesidades básicas; falta de formación y proyectos dedicados a medios de vida; falta de acceso a asistencia material para necesidades específicas y artículos básicos. 
8. Disminución de la calidad de los servicios de índole social por deterioro de la infraestructura.
ACNUR continuará trabajando en un contexto de población mixta donde los refugiados y solicitantes de asilo, así como las personas en movimiento, las personas en riesgo de desplazamiento, las personas en riesgo de apatridia, los retornados espontáneos y sus comunidades de acogida requerirán intervenciones de protección y salvaguardias. 
La protección basada en la comunidad seguirá siendo la base de la estrategia de la Operación para los grupos de población mencionados y ampliará su alcance geográfico a las zonas con una gran concentración de refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, retornados espontáneos, personas en movimiento y personas en riesgo de desplazamiento debido a las mayores necesidades y riesgos de protección.

project_name: Apoyo a los servicios básicos de salud materno-infantil y de adolescentes en los estados priorizados y fortalecimiento del programa nacional de inmunización.
project_objective:
Con el objetivo principal de contribuir a poner fin a las muertes prevenibles de madres, recién nacidos y niños, al tiempo que se promueve la salud y el desarrollo de todos los niños, en el sector de la salud UNICEF aplicará dos enfoques: abordar las desigualdades en los resultados sanitarios y fortalecer los sistemas de salud, incluida la prevención y la respuesta al COVID-19. Para abordar las desigualdades en los resultados sanitarios, UNICEF, junto con las ONG asociadas, contribuirá a reforzar los sistemas de información y a promover el uso de datos cualitativos y cuantitativos desglosados para identificar a los grupos marginados y ajustar los programas a sus necesidades; esto incluye la mejora de los sistemas de estadísticas vitales en 10 hospitales de referencia, ya que las actividades no supervisadas tienden a carecer de calidad. Simultáneamente, UNICEF apoyará acciones que establezcan mejoras sostenidas en la provisión, utilización y calidad de los servicios, apoyando 150,000 consultas de atención prenatal y las atenciones de parto seguro para 150.000 mujeres embarazadas y sus recién nacidos en hospitales y ambulatorios; proporcionando cuidados intensivos a 7.500 recién nacidos gravemente enfermos, y atenciones pediátricas para 483.820 niños y niñas menores de cinco años. En particular, UNICEF tratará de mejorar y retener la capacidad del personal sanitario a través de la formación en cuidados prenatales, neonatales, pediátricos y de emergencia, incluidos los cuidados de casos complicados del COVID-19, para 14.364 profesionales sanitarios, e incentivos para 500 miembros del personal sanitario de áreas críticas, al tiempo que se refuerza la cadena de suministros para 189 centros de salud, incluidos 114 ambulatorios y 75 hospitales de referencia, con el fin de mejorar el acceso  a los servicios y productos sanitarios neonatales e infantiles de calidad, para reducir la tasa de mortalidad neonatal y materna y dignificar la atención sanitaria. Se proporcionará tratamiento antirretroviral pediátrico ininterrumpido para 1,022 niños menores de 15 años que viven con el VIH y tratamiento para enfermedades oportunistas para 4.970 niños registrados en el programa nacional de VIH, suministros para el diagnóstico precoz del VIH en mujeres embarazadas y niños expuestos, y tratamiento para la prevención de la transmisión materno-infantil del VIH. UNICEF proporcionará ocho vacunas y equipos auxiliares al Programa Ampliado de Inmunización para 1.832.601 niños y niñas de hasta 10 años y 450.681 mujeres embarazadas, y seguirá reforzando la cadena de frío en 24 almacenes regionales y proveyendo refrigeradores para 800 puestos de vacunación para mejorar la capacidad de almacenamiento de vacunas de rutina y las vacunas contra el COVID-19, 24 vehículos para actividades en la comunidad, 7 vehículos refrigerados, 3 botes para áreas remotas fluviales, 25 incineradores para desechos de vacunación y 23 cuartos fríos para mejorar la capacidad del programa ampliado de vacunación. 
•	UNICEF apoyará la rehabilitación de 08 consultorios para el programa de Salud Escolar y de 08 consultas especializadas para adolescentes, para contribuir a reducir las desigualdades en el acceso a los servicios de salud de los niños más vulnerables en zonas remotas o zonas urbanas empobrecidas. Para contribuir a la protección del personal de salud, 60.000 trabajadores de primera línea recibirán EPP. A través de la capacitación del personal de salud y el preposicionamiento de insumos de emergencia, se apoyará al MMPS y  Protección Civil en la gestión de desastres a nivel nacional, con capacidad para atender hasta 960.000 personas, y se rehabilitarán 21 centros de salud que prestan servicios maternos y neonatales para aumentar el acceso de la población más vulnerable a servicios de salud funcionales y dignos. La capacitación y empoderamiento de las comunidades en salud materno infantil y de adolescentes y en preparación y respuesta a desastres será transversalizada en 2022

project_name: Mejora del acceso de la población vulnerable a servicios básicos de WASH en Comunidades, Escuelas, Establecimientos de Salud y Atención Nutricional y Espacios de Protección.
Fortalecer el sistema de protección de NNA con servicios de prevención y respuesta con enfoque en edad, genero y diversidad.
project_objective:
UNICEF mantendrá su enfoque en apoyar a los diferentes integrantes del sistema de Protección para que brinden servicios de prevención y respuestas de calidad con un enfoque en edad, género y diversidad para los NNA y familias más vulnerables y en riesgo. UNICEF mantendrá los esfuerzos en el desarrollo de los objetivos e indicadores sectoriales del Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria 2022-2023, a través de planes de trabajo con socios implementadores nacionales e internacionales. La Protección de la Infancia es la prevención y respuesta a la explotación, abuso, negligencia, prácticas nocivas y la violencia contra los niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA). Está incorporada en la Convención sobre los Derechos del Niño y las Metas de Desarrollo Sostenible. Con un abordaje socio-ecológico, UNICEF y sus socios trabajaran con un enfoque en los NNA, las familias, las comunidades y el sistema de protección formal e informal para que acciones preventivas y de respuestas para temas de protección de NNA sean implementadas en los estados priorizados del país.  El enfoque principal de esta propuesta es la prevención que se realiza no solamente a través de los socios de protección, pero también con el apoyo de otros sectores como nutrición y educación para cumplir resultados de protección infantil. Los principales temas cubiertos incluyen: VbG, separación familiar, violencia en general incluyendo la de género y crianza positiva. Además de nuestro enfoque central en la prevención, UNICEF Venezuela se enfoca en que ningún NNA se quede atrás: trabajaremos con socios para alcanzar a los NNA con mayor riesgo de protección que incluyen NNA con discapacidades, NNA separados y no acompañados, de poblaciones indígenas y afro-descendientes y NNA que sufren otras formas de discriminación y exclusión. 
Donde los NNA están sufriendo violaciones, UNICEF trabajará con socios gubernamentales y no-gubernamentales para fortalecer el acceso a los servicios de respuesta para prevenir reincidencia y brindar atención, apoyo y justicia. Los principales servicios brindados incluyen: apoyo en acceder a registro de nacimiento, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial, gestión de caso incluyendo a NNA sobreviviente de VbG. Una modalidad diferente para alcanzar objetivos de protección será la de las transferencias monetarias, otra componente importante de todas las intervenciones es el enfoque en la calidad y en temas transversales como lo de género, AAP, PEAS y discapacidad. El numero total de NNA alcanzado (sin calcular el apoyo al Ministerio de Salud con EV25) será de 628,536.

project_name: WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC
project_objective:
Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_name: Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan
project_objective:
As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_objective:

The project will also ensure holistic durable solutions approach led by the Government, mainly to enable local integration of IDPs in Borno State, reintegration of refugee returnees from Adamawa origin and support to the host community in building resilience and ease the pressure on them. 
Therefore in 2022, UNHCR shall build upon progress being made in 2021 in providing shelter and NFI support  to respond to unmet needs in Adamawa (Mubi North, Mubi South, Madagali, Michika, Yola South and Yola north); Borno (Bama, Banki, Damasak, Damboa, Dikwa, Jere, konduga, Gwoza, Pulka, Maiduguri, Mobbar, Monguno, Rann and Ngala) and Yobe State (Damaturu and Gujba,) through provision of; (1) 20,000 emergency shelters  (2) 1000 reinforced/transitional,  (3 ) 25,000 NFIs kits and (4) 15,000 emergency repairs targeting IDPs and Returnees households  both in formal and informal settlements,  suffering from protracted displacement and those returning home. To assess and ascertain the level of beneficiary satisfaction with regards to shelter and NFI support, UNHR plans to carry out 5 post construction/distribution monitoring.

project_name: Quality of integrated and equitable health service delivery and effective coverage  to support the health and well-being of children under 5 years and their mothers, including those infected and affected by HIV through strengthening the district and upazila health systems, in Rohingya Refugee Camps and Host Communities
project_objective: UNICEF will provide support to ensure quality, equitable, and gender-sensitive maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and immunization services, as well as provision of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services including counseling and referral for GBV and support to pregnant and lactating women inclusive of children with HIV, with attention to people with disabilities. Focus and emphasis will be on adherence to the Minimum Package of Essential Health Service for Primary Health Centers in the Rohingya refugee camps. We will collaborate with other partners from the health sector to bridge any gap of skilled human resources and supplies ensuring that the minimum package is adhered to. The project targets a vulnerable population of 482,404 people across the Rohingya refugee and host communities. To respond to the basic health and nutrition needs of Rohingya and host community women and children, UNICEF will continue providing a Bangladesh Government approved Minimum package of essential health services through the 13 health facilities in the camps (5 PHCs, and 8 HPs) and 2 Diarrhoea Treatment Centres (DTCs)   as well as strengthening government health systems and facilities in adjacent host communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf (2 union sub-centers and 16 community clinics). A special focus will continue to support the continuation of well-functioning Newborn Stabilization Unit (NSU) with Kangaroo Mother Care, across all Upazila Health Complexes, special newborn care unit (SCANU) for children born with low birth weight and preterm at the District Hospital as a referral center with a focus on providing comprehensive primary health care services through the Essential Services Packages (ESP) as per Government’s Guideline and SOPs including maternal, newborn care, immunization, integrated management of childhood illnesses, nutrition, acute watery diarrhoea prevention and management, prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and community engagement. UNICEF will continue to play her leading role in supporting vaccine logistics and supply ensuring vaccine availability across service provision points in all camps and Cox's Bazar district. We will provide technical support, supply, and transportation of vaccines and logistics, enhancing cold chain capacity and advocacy and social mobilization for strengthening immunization services across all camps.  UNICEF will also strengthen the Health Management Information System (HMIS/DHIS2) through technical support with 01 HMIS Consultant (based in Civil Surgeon Office) and capacity building of services providers on DHIS2 in coordination with all health sector partners including government counterparts, and coordinate with the team at National level in Dhaka to address technical issues in the system. UNICEF has developed the Emergency Response Plan to provide support during the emergency/disasters inclusive of strengthening Infection Prevention Control Measures for containing Covid-19 through SARI-ITC, support IPC measures with capacity building and supplies across the 13 supported facilities and continue to advocate and support COVID – 19 Vaccination programme.

project_name: Strengthened Protection of Children in Rohingya camps and Host Communities
project_objective:
UNICEF will reach 331,137 beneficiaries (2% PWDs) with child protection services, among which are 224,209 children and adolescents, and 96,130 adults. Women and girls will constitute 52% of beneficiaries. 75% of the project target will be in Rohingya refugee camps and 25% in host communities. 

UNICEF will adopt a public health approach to preventing abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect of children, within a social-ecological framework and according to fundamental Protection principles including 'Do No Harm' and the 'Best Interests of the Child'. 

UNICEF will work with government institutions to strengthen child protection systems. We will maintain partnership with the Department of Social Services (DSS) to build capacity of the social service workforce, and provide technical support to justice sector stakeholders including judges, police, probation officers and social workers to improve children's access to child-friendly justice, while promoting juvenile justice principles such as diversion and alternative measures to detention. UNICEF will provide human resources and technical input to the Office of Deputy Commissioner to accelerate Birth Registration through upgraded systems and financing. 

UNICEF will ensure that survivors of abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect - including Unaccompanied and Separated Children and other vulnerable children - have access to case management, care plans and referrals. Family-based alternative care will be promoted. UNICEF will ensure that adolescent girls and boys have access to Life Skills and are engaged as agents of positive change in their communities through access to information, social mobilization and participation in activities centered around Social Hubs, Multi-Purpose Centers and Adolescent Clubs. We will also provide structured and unstructured Mental Health and Psychosocial Support for children and adolescents to build resilience and ability to cope, and Positive Parenting guidance to caregivers. Covid19 mitigation measures embedded within regular programming.

UNICEF will establish and make functional Community-Based Child Protection Committees through trainings, technical guidance and logistical support.

UNICEF will embrace its role as a lead agency in the Child Protection Sub-Sector Strategic Advisory Group, Protection Working Group, Case Management Technical Working Group, Anti-Trafficking Task Force and other coordination forums, ensuring close collaboration with Government, NGOs, Civil Society and the private sector.

Child Safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be mainstreamed. UNICEF will lead the training of implementing partners and ensure mechanisms are in place in line with the humanitarian code of conduct.

UNICEF will mainstream Emergency Preparedness and Response through DRR capacity building for service providers and communities, and through pre-positioning supplies.

This project will give priority to the inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ensuring equal access to services in dignity. 

UNICEF will promote social cohesion and peaceful existence within and between communities through promoting free flow of accurate information, dialogue, coordination, joint activities, sport and recreation.

UNICEF will strengthen Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) by facilitating complaint and feedback mechanisms, and monitoring to ensure that feedback improves programming. Children, adolescents and caregivers - including those with disabilities - will be consulted.

project_name: Quality WASH services for Rohingya Refugees and most vulnerable populations in Ukhia and Teknaf Upazila of Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh
project_objective:
The overall aim of this project is to provide vulnerable populations with quality and equitable, safe water supplies, latrines and bathing facilities, including community engagement on key hygiene behaviours to reduce public health risks. 
Improved access to safe water supply: The water component of the project will focus on water  quality improvements and monitoring at source and point of use.  The project will support the underground water resources monitoring and assessment of the water network coverage to inform future water provision options.  DPHE will be supported to expand the ground water resources monitoring in other parts of Ukhia and Teknaf Upazilla of Cox Bazar District. In the camps,  6 small scaled water networks will be installed in critical areas to ensure equitable distribution of safe water supply to vulnerable populations. UNICEF will support routine repair, operation and maintenance of  existing  water networks and  hand pump wells to ensure functionality of faciliites to meet  the needs of the population.  In addtion, areas not covered by networks will be identified and assessed for options for the continued provision of safe drinking water services. 

Safely managed sanitation: For sanitation, the project focuses on operations, maintenance and improvement of existing latrines and bathing spaces to ensure functionality, quality,  safety, privacy and address the needs of women, girls, PwD, the elderly and other vulnerable people of the community.  UNICEF will construct WASH blocks for inclusive access to sanitation services. WASH infrastructure assessment will be done to identify the needs and address gaps. The operation and maintenance of Fecal Sludge Management (FSM) will be ensured while further assessments of the efficiency of FSM will be supported to improve the quality of treatment or decommissioning of any technology. In the camps, 5 new FSM will be constructed in critical areas.   UNICEF will continue to support an integrated solid waste management in line with the WASH sector strategy/guidelines. UNICEF will support the expansion, operation and maintenance of  SWM sites for  composting and segregation units. UNICEF will support the provision of waste collection bins and materials for household and communal use. 

Hygiene promotion and community engagement : The hygiene promotion will focus on community engagement changing identified high-risk behaviors through the participatory approaches such as CCCPLTH (Clean Camp Campaign-People Let Total Hygiene) and RANAS (Risk, Attitudes, Norms, Abilities and Self-Regulation) approaches as well as supporting participatory community monitoring and feedback mechanisms to contribute to AAP (Accountability to Affected Populations). Gender, GVB and Disability inclusion will be mainstreamed in all interventions.  

Life-saving WASH supplies: The project will continue to support the provision of WASH supplies such as soap, Aquatab and MHM materials. UNICEF will procure emergency WASH supplies for prepositioning and/or replenishment of emergency stocks of supplies for natural disasters and other emergency situations. The target populations are 250,000 Rohingya refugees living in eight refugee camps and 150,000 Bangladeshi people living in Teknaf and Uhkia affected by the refugee influx. 

WASH in host communities:  In the host community, the project will support the provision of safe water supply, development of water safety plans WSP), promotion of good hygiene practices and promotion of MHM among reproductive age of women, and improvement of WASH services in institutions.  In addition, the project will also support the creation of open defecation free (ODF) communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf by installing sanitary latrines.""

Asistencia multisectorial directa para venezolanos vulnerables y fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales locales y comunitarias
project_objective:
La intervención propuesta tiene como objetivo apoyar a la población vulnerable en Venezuela que requiere asistencia humanitaria. La acción se articulará en los sectores prioritarios: Protección, Alojamiento, Enseres y Energía (AEE), Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (ASH), seguridad alimentaria, salud y coordinación, en línea con los principios humanitarios que contribuirá a una respuesta eficaz y eficiente para salvar las vidas de las personas en movilidad. 

El proyecto tiene como objetivo general contribuir a mejorar las condiciones de vida de los venezolanos vulnerables, y a su vez que incrementar su resiliencia. El objetivo específico del proyecto es la provisión de asistencia humanitaria y acceso a servicios para la población vulnerable y fortalecimiento institucional para la asistencia a personas en movilidad, migrantes potenciales y comunidades de acogida. 

Con este proyecto, la OIM brindará asistencia multi-sectorial a personas en movilidad a través de 15 puntos de asistencia móviles instalados en las rutas migratorias y 9 centros de alojamiento temporal administrados por el socio implementador. Los beneficiarios de este proyecto recibirán información que busca reducir el riesgo de trata de personas. También se prevé la recopilación y el análisis de datos para aumentar el conocimiento de las necesidades y vulnerabilidades de las personas en tránsito que se desplazan por todo el país.

Además, la OIM apoyará a los socios para que desarrollen sus capacidades y amplíen los servicios disponibles para las comunidades seleccionadas, incluyendo las comunidades indígenas. El proyecto busca también fortalecer las capacidades de entidades de salud para la prestación de servicios médicos que atienden población vulnerable. Las autoridades nacionales y locales  pertinentes participarán en actividades de capacitación sobre el protocolo para la atención a las Víctimas de Trata (VdT) y actividades de prevención en VbG. 

La acción también está en línea con los objetivos establecidos en el Plan de Respuesta para Migrantes 2022, que tiene como componente integral y transversal la Protección contra la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS). 

Población objetivo: 
- Migrantes en tránsito, retornados, movilidad interna y migrantes potenciales. 
- Comunidades de acogida en especial las mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, jóvenes, LGBTI, personas con discapacidad, personas mayores, mujeres en riesgo, jefas de hogar en situación de vulnerabilidad, NNA en riesgo, solos o no acompañados, fuera del sistema escolar, en situación de calle, en hogares vulnerables, NNA que cuidan a otros NNA y sobrevivientes de violencia de género, trata, abuso o negligencia.

Resultado 1: Las personas en movilidad y las comunidades vulnerables tienen acceso a asistencia humanitaria oportuna y vital en AEE. 
Resultado 2 Las personas en tránsito y comunidades de acogida han mejorado su seguridad alimentaria.  
Resultado 3: Las personas en tránsito y comunidades vulnerables de acogida en Venezuela han mejorado sus condiciones de higiene y de acceso al agua segura. 
Resultado 4: Las comunidades vulnerables y la población en movilidad tienen acceso a la Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial (MHPSS) y atención primaria en salud incluso en los centros de alojamiento temporal.  
Resultado 5: Fortalecimiento de la capacidad de las entidades locales en temas relacionados con la migración y la asistencia en servicios básicos y de protección a los venezolanos en situación de vulnerabilidad. 
Resultado 6: Actores humanitarios tienen acceso a información sobre flujos, necesidades y vulnerabilidades de la población en movilidad.  

Zonas de Intervención: Amazonas, Apure, Bolívar, Delta Amacuro*, Falcón, La Guaira*, Miranda, Mérida, Táchira, Sucre, y Zulia 

*Estados priorizados exclusivamente para coordinación/MTM
