project_name: Amélioration de la réponse multisectorielle en faveur des Réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile et mise en œuvre des solutions durables pour les réfugiés au Cameroun.
project_objective:
Le projet vise l’amélioration de l’environnement de protection, l’accès aux solutions et voies complémentaires pour les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile au notamment en ce qui concerne   l’enregistrement et la documentation, la protection de l’enfance, la prévention et la réponse aux violences sexuelles et sexistes, l’accès aux services sociaux de base (santé, éducation et eau), l’accès à un abri décent et aux biens domestiques essentiels et le renforcement de la résilience.  
Le projet cible en 2022, un total de 460.317 réfugiés au Cameroun notamment : 333,409 réfugiés RCA, 118,996 NIG, 2449 des nationalités minoritaires, 6,788 demandeurs d’asile ainsi que 30% des populations autochtones par la présence des réfugiés dans les régions affectées. 
Au cours de l’année 2021, en dépit du contexte sanitaire marquée par la survenue de la pandémie de la COVID19 qui a négativement affecté l’environnement socio-économiques des populations, la situation sécuritaire fragile en RCA et l’instabilité dans la région du bassin du Lac Chad, le HCR a initié des projets visant à améliorer l’environnement de protection des réfugiés et assurer l’accès aux solutions aux réfugiés. 
Les projets déjà initiés requièrent une continuité dans la mise en œuvre afin renforcer la résilience et l’autonomisation des réfugiés de longue date, assurer leur inclusion effective dans les programmes de développement et donner accès aux solutions mais également apporter la réponse aux nouvelles situations d’urgences. 
Au cours de 2022, il sera mis en œuvre par le HCR, les acteurs humanitaires et le gouvernement des activités qui garantissent l’accès équitable et la jouissance des droits humains fondamentaux aux femmes, aux hommes, aux filles et aux garçons de tout âge et ceux ayant diverses vulnérabilités. 
L’UNHCR compte à travers ce projet : 
₋	Apporter la réponse aux besoins critiques de protection en assurant l’accès à l’asile, la documentation, la prévention et la réponse aux VBG, l’accès à l’éducation, aux moyens d’existence et à l’inclusion socio-économique, ainsi que le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de la coexistence pacifique entre les réfugiés et avec la communauté hôte.
₋	Mettre en œuvre les solutions durables en renforçant la résilience et les moyens d’existence et explorer des opportunités viables par la mise en œuvre des alternatives aux camps notamment dans la région de l’extrême nord.
₋	Le HCR continuera à faciliter le retour volontaire des réfugiés dans leur pays d’origine, à identifier les cas de réinstallation, et à faire le plaidoyer pour l’accès des réfugiés aux voies complémentaires.  
₋	Améliorer le bien-être socio-économique des refugies par la promotion de l’agriculture, la pêche et l’élevage en milieu rural, et la promotion des programmes d’entrepreneuriat et de résilience à travers l’approche communautaire ;
₋	 Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire des POCs et des communautés d’accueil à travers le Cash Based Intervention ;
₋	Favoriser les partenariats, le partage de l'information et la planification conformément aux plans de développement nationaux et locaux ainsi que la stratégie régionale pour la stabilisation, le rétablissement et le développement des zones impactées par les activités de Boko Haram à l’Extrême Nord.
Les interventions du HCR et de ses partenaires s’aligneront sur les priorités définies par le gouvernement (stratégies nationales de développement 2020-2030 et sectorielles). Elles s'inscrivent aussi dans le cadre de sa contribution à l'atteinte des ODD, à la réponse du système des Nations Unies relativement à l’UNSDCF et au principe de ne laisser personne pour compte. Un accent sera mis sur l’inclusion continue des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile dans les programmes du gouvernement, acteurs humanitaires ainsi que les acteurs de développement tel la Banque Mondiale.

project_name: Renforcement des interventions communautaires au profit des populations vulnérables (déplacées et communautés hôtes) dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre- Nord, Nord et de l’Est .
project_objective:
Le contexte sécuritaire difficile que traverse le Burkina Faso depuis la fin de l’année 2015, met à rude épreuve le fonctionnement du système de santé initialement déjà fragile.
Les incidents sécuritaires récurrents dans certaines régions du Burkina Faso dont le Sahel, l’Est, le Nord et le Centre-Nord ont entrainé un déplacement massif de populations entrainant une pression sans précédent sur les structures sanitaires d’accueil avec une forte augmentation de la demande. Par ailleurs, la fuite des agents de santé des zones touchées par l’insécurité entraine une réduction de l’offre de santé dans lesdites zones (fermeture des centres de santé ou au mieux formations sanitaires fonctionnant à minima). A la date du 30 Novembre 2021, le nombre de déplacés était estimé à 1 481 701 déplacés Ces 4 régions totalisent à elles seules 87% des déplacés de tout le pays. Au 30 Octobre 2021, plus de 80% des foration sanitaires fermées du pays se trouvaient dans ces régions avec 54,2% pour le Sahel, 16% pour le Centre-Nord et 8,4% pour la région de l’Est. Aussi, ces 4 régions totalisent 84% des formations sanitaires fonctionnant à minima ((Sahel 31%, Center-Nord 15.2 % et 28,5% pour l’Est). Cette situation fragile du système de santé entraine une réduction de l’offre de santé préventif (vaccination), curatif et promotionnel dans ces régions, avec comme corollaire la recrudescence de certaines maladies évitables par la vaccination comme la rougeole. Aussi, la réduction progressive de l’accès humanitaire couplée à la réduction de l’offre de service au niveau institutionnel oblige à l’adoption de nouvelles stratégies adaptatives s’appuyant sur la plateforme communautaire (recrutement de volontaires communautaires, formation et renforcement du paquet d’intervention des agents de santé à base communautaire avec la délégation des taches) afin de garantir un minimum de continuité de services de santé dans les régions durement touchées par la crise. 
A cette crise humanitaire, vient d’ajouter l’épidémie de COVID-19 qui imposent une réadaptation continue de nos stratégies d’intervention afin de limiter la propagation de l’épidémie à ces groupes déjà vulnérables dont les conditions de vie marquée par une extrême promiscuité sont d’importants facteurs de risques de propagation de la COVID-19.

project_name: Prévention de la malnutrition sous toutes ses formes et prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans  dans  16 provinces du Burundi
project_objective:
Selon la dernière l'enquête sur la situation nutritionnelle et la mortalité de 2020 (ENSNMB 2020) utilisant la méthodologie SMART (Standardized Monitoring and Assessment of Relief and Transition) menée par le ministère de la Santé et le Bureau national des statistiques avec l'appui de l'UNICEF et du PAM, la situation nutritionnelle s'est aggravée au Burundi. La prévalence de la malnutrition aiguë globale (MAG) parmi les enfants de moins de 5 ans est de 6,1 % contre 5,1 % en 2019 et 4,5 % en 2018. Cette prévalence de MAG est au-dessus du seuil d'alerte de 5 % fixé par l'Organisation Mondiale de la Santé (OMS). 1.1% des enfants de moins de 5 ans souffrent de malnutrition aiguë sévère (MAS). Au total, 31 districts sur 47 sont en situation précaire avec une prévalence de MAG comprise entre 5 et 9,9% contre 16 districts en 2019 et seulement 10 en 2018. 
Comparativement, la prévalence du retard de croissance au Burundi reste préoccupante malgré la légère amélioration au cours des 5 dernières années. Un enfant de moins de cinq ans sur deux continue à souffrir d'un retard de croissance, avec une légère diminution de la prévalence du retard de croissance de 54,2 % en 2019 à 52,2 % en 2020. L'évaluation des pratiques d'alimentation des nourrissons n'a signalé que 6,8 % d’enfants de moins âgées de 6 à 23 mois recevant une alimentation minimale acceptable, avec 35% des ménages ayant un accès à une alimentation suffisamment diversifiée (ENSNMB, 2020).
Selon L’Enquête Démographique et de Sante de 2016-2017 (EDS 2016-2017), la prévalence de l’anémie chez les enfants est de 61% tandis qu’elle est de 39% chez les femmes en âge de procréer. 
L’analyse des besoins effectuée par le secteur a permis de retenir 16 provinces prioritaires avec un taux de MAG supérieur à 5%. Il s’agit des provinces Bubanza, Bujumbura, Bururi, Cankuzo, Cibitoke, Gitega, Kayanza , Karusi, Kirundo , Makamba , Muramvya, Mwaro , Ngozi , Rutana, Ruyigi et Rumonge. 
L’UNICEF appuie le Ministère de la santé pour la prévention de la malnutrition sous toutes ses formes et le traitement des enfants atteints de malnutrition aiguë sévère à travers les activités de dépistage actif de la malnutrition, la sensibilisation sur la nutrition , la santé et l’hygiène ,  l’achat et l’approvisionnement des districts sanitaires en intrants nutritionnels pour la prise en charge des cas de MAS , la supplémentation en micronutriments multiples des enfants de 6-23 mois et supplémentation en fer-acide folique chez les femmes enceintes.  Ce projet permettra le dépistage de 224,009 enfants (filles et garçons), l’achat des intrants nutritionnels et l’approvisionnement des districts pour le traitement de 55,071 enfants (filles et garçons) dans les 16 provinces vulnérables. 131,738 enfants de 6-23 seront supplémentées en micronutriments multiples avec les poudres de micronutriments (MNPs) , 148,266 enfants de 6-59 mois supplémentés en vitamine A et 178,488 femmes seront supplémentées en fer -acide folique.  De plus, 85,318 personnes seront sensibilisées sur la nutrition, la sante et l’hygiène pour prévenir la malnutrition sous toutes ses formes. Le budget requis est de 6,818,623 USD.

project_name: Assistance for access to drinking, cooking and personnel hygiene water and emergency sanitation in the face of natural disasters and epidemics including covid 19
project_objective:
In 2022, the WASH sector will target globally 404 756  people, including 23 384  internally displaced persons following natural disasters or other shocks as cholera epidemies, 311 070  vulnerable and members of host communities as well as 70 303 returnees. The assistance will be carried out according to two sectoral objectives which are as follows:
• Provide emergency WASH assistance to people affected by epidemics and natural disasters including host communities. This objective aims to provide drinking water and emergency sanitation infrastructure (latrines, showers) as well as to distribute hygiene kits to affected people. These interventions will make it possible to respond to essential WASH needs in order to guarantee survival considered to be physical and mental well-being, but also the protection and dignity of vulnerable people.
• Ensure access to WASH services for 131 336 people including internally displaced persons, members of host communities as well as people living in areas of return of returnees and those at risk of water-borne diseases. This objective aims to improve WASH services for communities in order to reduce the use of negative adaptation mechanisms such as the use of surface water (river and lake water), air defecation practices which constitute a risk of pollution of the sources as well as other bad hygienic practices favoring the occurrence and the persistence of epidemics including Covid 19.

project_name: Reduce the incidence of acute malnutrition and risks of mortality associated with acute malnutrition in areas faced by emergencies while strengthening systems and building resilience in the Sahel.
project_objective: Chad is experiencing a worrying nutritional situation underpinned by food insecurity, a high incidence of childhood diseases, endemic poverty, and a weak health system. Today, 1.7 million people are affected by health emergencies, with children and pregnant and lactating women being particularly vulnerable. Based on criteria of prevalence (GAM >= 10% and/or SAM >= 2%) and/or mortality (overall mortality rate >= 1/10,000/day and/or under-five mortality rate >= 2/10,000/d), 17 provinces out of 23 are considered priority provinces for SAM treatment in 2022 (Ndjamena, Tibesti, Ouaddaï, Sila, Borkou, Chari Baguirmi, Mayo Kebi Est, Hadjer Lamis, Guéra, Salamat, Batha, Wadi fira, Kanem, Barh El-Ghazel, Ennedi Est, Ennedi Ouest and Logone Oriental). The provinces of Lac, Moyen Chari, Mandoul are also considered as priority provinces due to the aggravating factors such as conflict and population displacement.   There is a problem with securing the supply of nutritional supplies as well as disruptions in the logistical aspects at the international level, which can increase the risk of disruption in the supply chain, leading to frequent stock-outs. In order to respond to the populations affected by the so-called ""Sahel and Health"" crisis, UNICEF proposes to strengthen national capacity to improve access to treatment for 262,335severely acutely malnourished children in existing outpatient therapeutic program (OTP) and inpatient facilities. Preventive nutrition services will be strengthened at the community and health facility levels. At the community level, the actions will integrate the early detection of children under 5 years of age suffering from acute malnutrition and their referral through mothers and caregivers, while strengthening the capacity of the latter on essential nutrition actions, including the optimal feeding practices for young children, in order to prevent all forms of malnutrition. Thus, 1,283 community health workers will be trained on the Mother-MUAC approach as well as on interpersonal communication and awareness raising activities and will be responsible for providing coaching to mothers and caregivers on MUAC screening while ensuring their follow-up. The capacity of nutrition service delivery in the targeted health facilities will be strengthened in additional human resources. The Ministry of Health will be supported to strengthen the coordination mechanism at the national and provincial levels as well as the monitoring and evaluation of interventions through joint supervision missions including End User Monitoring. This action will also contribute to the response to measles through vitamin A supplementation for 420,000 children and reduce micronutrient deficiencies.

project_name: Strengthening the Protection of Crisis Affected Communities through Timely and Effective Humanitarian Interventions in Somalia and Somaliland.
project_objective:
The Humanitarian Crisis in Somalia continues to further aggravate with over 7.7 million people projected to require urgent and life-saving assistance in 2022, a significant increase from 2019 (4.9 million) and 2020 (5.2 million). The principle drivers being the deepened armed conflict in many parts of South-Central Somalia and erratic climatic conditions with flooding and drought happening simultaneously in different parts of the Country. 
This coupled with COVID 19 pandemic, not only hampers access to basic services but also leads to increased marginalization of minority groups, displaced persons and persons with special needs, heightened protection risks, loss of livelihoods and income, and limited freedom of movement. In addition, communities have reduced coping capacities and resilience, with women and girls, minority clan members, and people living with disabilities being disproportionately affected. With the country gearing for state and federal elections, there is the likelihood of displacements and disruptions of lives amid intensified attacks from non-state actors. Recent conflicts and violence in mid-2021 displaced 250,000 people in Banaadir, Bardaale and Badweyn, including nearly 207,000 people who were temporally displaced in Mogadishu owing to election-related violence in April 2021. This against a backdrop of limited and constrained humanitarian assistance will not only result in loss of lives, affected livelihoods and destroyed property, but also increased vulnerabilities and heightened protection risks for vulnerable groups.
Data from the PRMN, SPMS and MRM systems designates heightened protection risks in the country with over 4 million people projected to need lifesaving protection assistance (HNO, 2021).  The GBV AOR reported a spike in Intimate Partner Violence, rape, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment and abuse against women and girls in 2021 most of which are from displacement affected communities. Furthermore, accruing to the MRM data, Somalia is now the most dangerous conflict on earth for children, where over 23,000 grave violations were recorded in the last 5 year, and of concern is the number of child recruitment and abductions far exceeding any other country in the world. 
Thus, DRC will design and implement interventions targeting the most vulnerable persons in the communities including DACs, girls, women, boys, and men at risk of/ survivors of GBVs, minority groups/clans, persons with disabilities, children and adults affected by armed violence including explosive remnants of wars (ERWs) and other explosive devices, people at risk of forced evictions and most vulnerable host communities to strengthening capacity and the commitment of families and communities to protect communities especially children and women from violence, exploitation and harmful practices, through elimination of harmful practices and all forms of gender-based violence, provision of timely holistic and quality age and gender appropriate services to survivors, persons at risks and vulnerable persons including PSNs in addition to strengthened community-based protection systems.
The proposed interventions thus align with the general protection, GBV, Explosive Hazards (EH) and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) cluster objectives and indicators and the Strategic objectives 1, 2 and 3 of 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan.  The interventions will employ participatory and right based approaches, age, gender and diversity (AGD) approach and community-based child protection approaches which will involve, inclusion of children and caregivers from refugee’s/asylum seeker communities, migrants, IDPs, persons with disability and most vulnerable host communities in addition to local authorities in the project management cycle. 
DRC targets to reach 58,500 persons (10,000girls,2,500B,30,000W,16,000M) in selected districts in Somalia.

project_name: Provision of basic health care and services to children and mothers in the North West and South West regions in 2022
project_objective:
The situation in the North West and South West (NWSW) regions of Cameroon escalated in October 2016, when the Anglophone population started making political demands leading to protests and strikes. This unrest emerged from historically perceived marginalisation of Anglophone Cameroonians. A year later, on October 1st, 2017, secessionists declared independence from the Republic of Cameroon. Since then violence has escalated and Internally Displaced People (IDP) targeted are living in the forest or host communities in villages, urban or peri urban areas in the NWSW regions. These IDPs lack basic social services. The most vulnerable population are women, pregnant women, newborn babies, children under five, young children both boys and girls. This security situation in the NWSW has had a direct impact on access to health services for vulnerable women and children. Those functional are not sufficiently equipped. Due to mass displacement with many people seeking shelter in remote forested areas access to even basic health services is almost impossible. Furthermore, more than 40 per cent of Community Health Workers (CHW) are no longer working in insecure health districts.
UNICEF alongside partners will deliver essential health services aimed at increasing access to basic health maternal, newborn and child-care and services where health facility is functional and mainly in communities and hard to reach areas. 
OVERALL GOAL/OBJECTIVE
Increase coverages of basic maternal, newborn and child health preventive and curative and promotional package amidst the COVID-19 pandemic 
SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES 
• Increase vaccine coverage in routine immunization in the 6-59 months (pentavalent 3, measles) 
• Increase vaccine coverage for routine immunization in pregnant women
• Provide treatment the three main childhood killers for children under 5 years old (Malaria, diarrhoea, and Respiratory tract infections)
• Provide prevention care to pregnant women and Children: anti anaemics, Vit A supplementation, deworming
• Provide malaria prevention tools: LLINs and Intermittent preventive treatment to families 
• Improve quality of maternal and newborn care with the provision of basic kits for mothers and newborns, training and coaching of health care providers
• Build capacities of health care providers, health facilities and communities on COVIC-19 prevention and infection prevention Control;
Direct beneficiaries: 
- 3,000 newborns 
- 10,000 Pregnant women 
- 50,000 children under five of age 
- 20,000 families/households corresponding to about 100,000 people

project_name: Improve food security through provision of emergency food and enhance food production of food insecure housholds in Aweil North, Aweil West, Aweil South, NBeG State, South Sudan
project_objective: The project will provide access to food, agriculture inputs and improve agriculture production to prevent famine and support vegetable production and fishing kits to improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations. The project will target 57,430 (33,309 female and 24,121 male) beneficiaries in Aweil North, Aweil South and Aweil West. The integration with other multi-donor funded programmes will help in reaching this target.  Concern will provide access to agricultural inputs and trainings to the 3,000 vulnerable HHs who rely on subsistence agriculture as their main source of food and livelihoods in Aweil West, Aweil North and Aweil South in NBeG. Concern will engage with the County Agriculture Department (CAD), extension workers and lead farmers for training on agriculture extension services and Climate Smart Agriculture practices, informal seeds systems, pest and post-harvest management. The activity will support vegetable production Aweil West/North/South targeting the nutrition sector beneficiaries to increase HHs dietary diversity and contributing to improved complementary feeding practices among children 6-23 months of age. The vulnerable HHs practicing fishing in NBeG will receive fishing kits and training to improve dietary diversity and income source. Considering asset depletion, crop losses due to flooding, inflation and limited access to livelihood, hunger is expected to deepen due mainly to depleted food stocks and high food prices therefore Concern in partnership with WFP in NBeG continue to provide emergency food assistance through General Food Distribution, School Feeding Program and Cash/Food for Asset program.

project_name: Emergency Cash Assistance to Crisis Affected populations
project_objective:
According to FSNAU technical release in Sept 2021 the projection does not look good with anticipated below-average Dyer (October-December) rainfall hence worsening trend projected. Based on the results of household (HH) surveys and field assessments conducted in June and July 2021, more than 2.2 million people face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes in the presence of planned and likely humanitarian assistance during the July to September 2021 period. An additional 3.4 million people are Stressed (IPC Phase 2), bringing the total number of people experiencing acute food insecurity to 5.6 million. From October to December 2021, food insecurity is expected to further deteriorate among poor rural, urban, and displaced populations due to the impacts of anticipated, below-average 2021 Deyr (October-December) season rainfall, continued insecurity and, other food security-related risk factors, including rising food prices and cost of living, declining availability of milk for both consumption and sale, and a likely reduction in agricultural employment opportunities during the forthcoming Deyr season. Without sustained humanitarian food assistance, 3.5 million people across Somalia are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes between October and December 2021. An additional 3.7 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC Phase 2), bringing the total number of people facing acute food insecurity to 7.2 million. 

Rural populations in particular are experiencing multiple declines in food and income sources. The 2021 Gu harvest in southern Somalia is 60 per cent lower than the long-term average for 1995-2020. It is the third lowest Gu harvest since 2010. The lower production in 2021 Gu mainly reflects the impact of the poor rainfall, ongoing civil insecurity, river floods, shortage of farm inputs and pests.  In pastoral and agropastoral livelihood zones, although heavy rains between late April and mid-May partially replenished pasture and water resources, these resources are inadequate to support normal livestock production until the start of Deyr season rainfall in October. Furthermore, floods caused further population displacement and damaged crops and farmland in riverine areas of Hiraan, Shabelle, and Juba regions.  A majority of the estimated 2.9 million IDPs across Somalia are poor with limited livelihood assets, few income earning opportunities, low communal support, and rely heavily on external humanitarian assistance. As a result, one-third of internally displaced persons (in both rural and urban settlements) face moderate to large food consumption gaps through late 2021.   

The project will strive to contribute to Improve access to food for 3.1 million of people facing severe acute food insecurity including million IDPs, 2 million non-displaced people and persons with disabilities in 64 districts. CARE will target 6,500 households with 3000 households with UCT and 3500 CCTs. 

Cyclical climate shocks and ongoing conflict are challenging traditional rural livelihoods and causing
growing number of urban poor and internally displaced people in Somalia.
Displacements due to armed conflict and political tensions, drought, and lack of livelihoods are expected to continue in 2022, further exacerbating food insecurity in many  areas. 
Protection concerns are likely to increase for all groups, mostly manifesting as negative coping strategies, especially for young women and men from extremely poor households as household food security situation deteriorates. In agropastoral livelihood zones, where the main shocks include erratically distributed rainfall and conflict, poor households have experienced substantial crop losses and low income from agricultural employment. With few alternative sources of food and income after current food stocks are depleted, they face moderate to large food consumption gaps through late 2021.

project_name: Improving Food Security, Livelihoods and resilience of conflict affected households in South Sudan
project_objective:
The food & Livelihood insecurity situation in Guit and Rubkona counties of Unity state remain miserable due to prolonged flood situation, existing conflict & insecurity, the impact of COVID-19 and persistent poor macro and micro economic conditions. Localized tensions compelled by Intra and inter community clashes, revenge killings, cattle rustling, burglary, theft continue to pose a great threat towards community livelihoods. Targeted individuals as a result of revenge killings are threatened to pursue livelihoods and economic opportunities and hence continue to remain vulnerable. Almost 90% of the Rubkona & Guit county is inundated in prolonged flooding in the state. It’s very unlikely that the water would recede in near future and water logging in many agriculture lands may become permanent. To address the flood & Conflict induced acute food insecurity situation as well as livelihood need of most vulnerable community, DRC intends to achieve following results –

1.	Agriculture & Food Security: Flood and conflict affected Agro-pastoral IDP & Host communities’ food security and livelihoods are protected and restored through the provision of emergency and early recovery  and flood adaptive agriculture and fisheries practice for most vulnerable households

2.	Economic Recovery & Market System: To ensure improved access to income & livelihood opportunities through Cash / Market based Livelihood interventions vulnerable Households. 

DRC vision is to provide a dignified life for all people affected by displacement. As such,
DRC Food Security and Livelihood (FSL) activities are sectorial inter-linked with Protection
[(including sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV)] and Armed Violence Reduction
(AVR) response. DRC will ensure protection mainstreaming in all the  project activities and assessment tools will also be adopted and specfic criteria for inclusion will be developed to priorities the most vulnerable households in the targeted communities.

project_name: Improving Food security for vulnerable populations in Somaliland, particularly  IDPs in Hargeisa, Togdheer, and Sool
project_objective:
Somalia is facing a growing number of threats to its food security. The ongoing desert locust invasion, socio-economic effects of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and recurrent climate shocks, including frequent flooding and drought, continue to severely impact the lives and livelihoods of the vulnerable population. With this multifaceted crises, 7.7 Million people across Somalia need in emergency food assistance. With humanitarian needs expected to further increase in 2022, it is critical to enhance immediate food access, protect and restore livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable households. Sustained humanitarian assistance is required to prevent the further deterioration of food security and nutrition.
Through this project, Plan International and Partners will effectively provide emergency assistance for food and promote dignity and choices among project participants by increasing purchasing power with short term injection of unconditional cash transfers for 1182 HH (7092 beneficiaries; 3546F, 3546M) for six months. Through field monitoring, government reports, and sector coordination, Plan and Partners will target households in areas identified as IPC3 or worse, risk of drought, and/or IDP communities, including those recently evicted by Somaliland government. These families have insufficient income to cover rising cost of food particularly during periods of drought and other shocks due to COVID19, instability and climate change, and will qualify per criteria, e.g. female headed household, household with person with disability, etc. Partners will ensure the crises affected families receive messages on Infant, Young Child Feeding and Hygiene and have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious foods to meet their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life. Partners have complementary programs running in these areas to enable consultant and selection within communities. By targeting vulnerable families particularly with children and delivering this intervention in a gender sensitive manner, Plan strives for secondary outcomes of improved the protection environment with reduced risks to women and girls.

project_name: Equitable access to quality education and improved learning opportunities for the most vulnerable crisis affected girls and boys
project_objective:
Children in Somalia continue to face acute humanitarian needs due to conflict and environmental hazards such as drought and flooding. COVID-19 pandemic has compounded the challenges exacerbating vulnerability of the crisis-affected populations across the country. These crises have been the drivers of vulnerabilities which have made access to basic social services extremely low in Somalia. According to Somalia Humanitarian Needs Overview, 7.7 million people need assistance in Somalia representing a half of the population of Somalia and 2.9 million people are IDPs. 593,000 people were displaced in Somalia between January and September 2021(PRMN).  
The recurrent violence and climate change have negatively impacted the education delivery. The education sector continues to lack vital learning resources, trained teachers, adequate facilities, and access to safe learning environment is constrained for most girls and boys. Continued lack of financial support has also hindered the delivery of education services. As such the most affected are the vulnerable children, including children with disabilities who have no access to education services. The lack of educational opportunities coupled with an uncertainty due to the crisis leave many children in psychosocial distress and vulnerable to further violence, abuse, neglect, and exploitation.
3 million crisis affected children need education assistance in 2022 (Education Cluster). The increased needs of education assistance are as result of increasing population, COVID-19 pandemic, conflicts, and climate change. An estimated 237,200 (40%) school-aged children have been displaced in 2021. The impact of crisis has adversely affected the education system, which has resulted in many children growing up without the education, protection and support that schools should provide. Girls and boys face steep obstacles in accessing education services, as 41% of IDP settlements have routes to schools that are not perceived to be safe (CCCM Cluster 2021). Education services are inadequate with only 12 per cent of enrolled children in primary schools are from rural areas, while the rural population is over 50% of the national population (HNO). According to the government figures, 34% of Somali girls are married by the age of 18, and 16% before their 15th birthday. 
Teachers, especially in rural areas work within an extremely challenging environment; inconsistent monthly incentives, lack of teaching and learning materials, and inadequate training and supervision, among others. This significantly affects the learning outcomes of the most vulnerable children in Somalia, as teachers are the main and critical component of any education system. The 2018/2019 EMIS shows the total number of qualified teachers is only 35%. 
Access to educational opportunities for children with disabilities is a major challenge. The number of children with disabilities enrolled in primary school is significantly low with only 811 children (47% girls) enrolled in schools; this represents 0.3% of total enrolment (2018/2019 EMIS). The exact number of school-aged children with disabilities in Somalia is not yet known and education system is not yet developed and equipped to meet the varied needs of children with extreme cases of disability.
The 2021 COVID-19 closure of the schools disrupted learning exacerbating already existing disparities within the education system and children lives in Somalia. The impacts of COVID-19 exposed children to higher risks of abuse and increased psychosocial distress and deprived of opportunities for growth and development. The disadvantages are disproportionate for under-privileged learners who tend to have fewer educational opportunities.
The proposed project aims to improve access to quality education for the most vulnerable children including adolescents’ children with disabilities for both the displaced and non-displaced vulnerable communities. It aims to target 220,000 (110,000 girl) in Somalia.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire pour les déplacés internes, populations hotes, et refugiés maliens suite à la crise sécuritaire et aux personnes vulnérables pendant la période de soudure alimentaire au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Au Burkina Faso, la période de juin à septembre représente une période critique sur le plan
alimentaire pour les populations en milieu rural du fait d’un déficit alimentaire chronique
due à la faiblesse des récoltes. Cette difficulté a été fortement aggravée par la crise
sécuritaire au sahel marquée par des attaques récurrentes des hommes armés non
identifiés. Face à cette crise complexe, le nombre de personnes vulnérables qui a besoin
d’assistance s’est fortement accru. Il en est de même pour les réfugiés maliens et les
personnes déplacés internes du fait de l’insécurité. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement
du Burkina Faso a invité l’ensemble de ses partenaires nationaux et internationaux à la
solidarité pour apporter une réponse à la crise. En réponse à la sollicitation du
gouvernement, le PAM apporte une assistance alimentaire et un soutien nutritionnel dans
6 régions prioritaires du Burkina, à savoir la boucle du Mouhoun, la région du nord, la région du sahel,
la région de l’Est, la région du centre nord et du Centre Est (le PAM pourrait intervenir dans d'autres dépendamment de l'évolution des besoins humanitaires).
De façon spécifique, entre janvier 2022 et Décembre 2022 Le PAM va assurer :
- Une assistance alimentaire (en vivres ou transferts monétaires) aux personnes vulnérables pendant
la période de soudure dans les 6 régions conformément aux recommandations du cadre
harmonisé.
- Apporter une assistance alimentaire (en vivres ou transferts monétaires) aux personnes déplacées
internes (PDI) et ménages hôtes accueillant les PDI.
- Assurer une assistance alimentaire (en vivres et/ou transferts monétaires) des réfugiés maliens au
Burkina Faso.
Les besoins globaux pour ces activités sont de l'ordre de 170 million de dollars.

project_name: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities.
project_objective: The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. Situation reports are submitted by all UNHCR Field Offices to their respective Supervising Office and Branch Offices submit a corresponding report to Headquarters.

project_name: Intensifier la protection et l'offre de service pour les femmes survivantes de VBG
project_objective:
L’objectif de ce projet est de soutenir le sous-cluster Violence Basée sur le Genre à atteindre ces 4 objectifs sectoriels à savoir :
1.Assurer et coordonner une collecte de données de qualité et produire une analyse adéquate de la situation de protection …
2.Contribuer à la réduction des vulnérabilités et au renforcement de la capacité de résilience des populations exposées aux risques de protection...
3.Renforcer la coordination des interventions de réponse et les capacités des acteurs pour améliorer la qualité et la couverture géographique des services et apporter une réponse holistique de protection aux personnes affectées…
4.Renforcer le cadre juridique et opérationnel de la protection dans l’action humanitaire. 
Pour l’objectif 1, UNFPA étant lead dans la coordination du GBVIMS au Mali, renforcera l’accessibilité et la disponibilité des données pour une meilleure maîtrise des tendances VBG au niveau national, assurera une meilleure analyse des données afin d’atteindre les survivantes les plus affectées parmi celles identifiées et renforcera la disponibilité d’analyse intersectorielle basée sur des évidences. 

La réponse de l’objectif 2 sera basée sur le renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de réponse aux VBG à travers l’information la sensibilisation en utilisant des messages clés auprès des communautés sur les risques de Violence Basée sur le Genre et d’Exploitation et Abus Sexuels. Le projet s’assurera de renforcer les capacités des communautés y compris les associations des femmes et jeunes sur les questions de VBG, EAS, et la mises en place de CBCM dans les régions. Les zones du projet feront également l’objet d’audit de sécurité VBG afin n d’identifier les potentiels risques de VBG.
 Les objectifs 3 et 4 permettront au projet de renforcer l’accès aux services de prise en charge holistique de VBG à travers le soutien et/ou la mise en place d’unités holistiques de prise en charge VBG, la révision et la dissémination des systèmes de référencement. 
Ce projet vient en complément aux projets en cours d’exécution  par UNFPA dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie  de réponse aux besoins des femmes et filles en matière de services de protection dans un contexte humanitaire fragile marqué par l’insuffisance des services sociaux de base due aux confits intercommunautaires, les violations graves de droits humains tels que les violences sexuelles, l'exploitation et l'abus sexuels, les mariages forcés et celui des enfants, mais également à la crise sanitaire du Covid-19. UNFPA dans sa logique du «Leave no one behind» s’efforcera à travers ce projet, de renforcer l’inclusion des personnes marginalisées, telles que les personnes en situation d’handicap ainsi que des femmes et filles des sites de personnes déplacées n’ayant pas accès aux services sociaux de base. Cette inclusion se fera à travers leur renforcement de capacités sur les thématiques du genre et EAS, leurs orientations et référencement vers les services de prise en charge ainsi qu’un soutien économique et social à travers la mise à disposition d’AGR.

project_name: Improving protection environment and providing lifesaving interventions for children in Somaliland, particularly IDPs inHargeisa, Togdheer, and Sool
project_objective:
In 2022 humanitarian response, Plan International will improve protection environment and promote child rights in Somaliland for IDPs and vulnerable populations, particularly children with protection risks. The country has one of the lowest children and gender indicators in the world with only one-quarter of girls – 24% aged 15-24 considered as literate, 45% married before 18 years and 98% subjected to female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C). The COVID19 quarantine measures to prevent and control the spread of COVID-19 exposed children and women to increased protection risks, particularly within the home, owing to increased stress caused by the outbreak, exacerbating existing gender inequalities and violence. There has been increased exposure to violence especially to girls through FGM/C. According to the United Nations Population Fund, COVID-19 could have far reaching impacts on the effort to end FGM/C, with a potential 1.5 million FGM/C cases occurring over the next decade that could have otherwise been averted. Plan will work with CSOs and other partners to effectively promote and support improving community-based child protection mechanisms. Key interventions will target young girls and boys, their parents and other decision-makers to raise awareness on child protection and GBV, establish and strengthen referral mechanisms for case management and other services including MHPSS and financial support, and capacity building and advocacy with local authorities and for national agenda on centrality of protection (e.g. importance of child protection and campaigns on GBV, adoption of the positive discipline techniques, inclusion of children and policy formulation). 
In August 2021, Plan International has commissioned an assessment that aims to analyse operational context (political, Social, economic, legal and governance) of the civil society and how power dynamics shape their strategic direction in Somaliland. The report findings will inform our CSO strengthening efforts and building influencing alliance. The most recent issue is the forced eviction in Lasanod region. Somaliland forced returns of internally displaced persons from South central Somalia which have had a devastating impact on displaced populations who were already vulnerable due to the intersection of multiple humanitarian crises including drought, conflict and COVID-19. The current situation has also increased the risk of Sexual Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) due to a breakdown in community structures, law and order, and a lack of physical protection. The situation has ignited a war of word between Somaliland authority and Somalia which could lead further eviction and retaliatory response. UN OCHA and the NGOs Consortium which Plan International is a member issued a joint press release expressing their regrets and concern.

project_name: RESPUESTA HUMANITARIA DE EMERGENCIA FRENTE A DESASTRES DE ORIGEN NATURAL O HUMANO Y CONTRIBUCIÓN A LA ESTABILIZACIÓN Y DESARROLLO TERRITORIAL A TRAVÉS DE LA RECUPERACIÓN INTEGRAL, ECONÓMICA Y PRODUCTIVA
project_objective:
Las acciones se enmarcan en el marco de respuesta del programa país de Acción contra el Hambre en Colombia para el 2022, con un enfoque en respuesta humanitaria de emergencia frente a desastres, afectaciones derivadas del conflicto, la COVID 19 y para el mejoramiento de las condiciones socioeconómicas de la población.  La respuesta es multisectorial, enfocada en WASH, SAN, y salud. 
Desde el sector de seguridad alimentaria  nuestro enfoque estará en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas de alerta temprana multirriesgo, considerando la preparación para emergencias, para una mayor capacidad de respuesta, una mejor cobertura de las múltiples necesidades y mejores vínculos con las actividades de recuperación. Nuestra programación para emergencia se basará en el conocimiento de los sistemas locales, las redes con socios desde el nivel nacional hasta el nivel local, el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de los actores locales.  La entrega de asistencia alimentaria de emergencia estará enfocada en solventar las necesidades de las familias afectadas por el conflicto y por los desastres. El número de meses estará sujeto a las condiciones puntuales de las emergencias, sin embargo, se parte de la base de 2 meses a las familias participantes.  
En lo relacionado con las acciones de nutrición se tienen previstas atenciones medico-nutricional para la detección y tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda ambulatoria, remisión de casos con desnutrición aguda severa con complicaciones a la red hospitalaria en niños y niñas menores de 5 años . Fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales para la detección y manejo de la desnutrición aguda, a través de la formación del personal y la dotación con equipos de antropometría. Trabajo articulado con la red de salud y las estructuras comunitarias locales.

project_name: Ensuring access to safe, adequate and appropriate life savings nutritional services for the refugee's children in Northwest & Northcentral Syria
project_objective:
The Project will improve children feeding practices to contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality among infants and young children in NWS & NCS by ensuring access to safe, adequate and appropriate nutrition services in 24 months. 
Anchored on the first 1000 days’ window of opportunity, different project models to target specific development period of a child will be implemented. And in recognition that malnutrition is not solely a health problem, WVSR will push for mainstreaming of nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions. One example of which is creating Income Generating Activities (IGA) opportunities for families with malnourished children and promotion of nutrition-sensitive agriculture such as homestead gardening for micronutrient rich crops, promotion of animal source foods, bio fortification. There will be provision of safe space (Mother-Baby Areas) and Specialized Support at EPI center/camp building on and contextualizing integrated nutrition programming model, the Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergencies component of the project will implement integrated IYCF-E and PSS activities in the camps and EPI sites. IYCF-E staff will be trained in PSS skills to support mothers who are in distress or unable to engage with their infants, and to recognize when a mother needs further, specialized mental health support and also other red flags such as signs of gender-based violence. If Child Protection needs are identified during the assessment, or following, families will be referred to the CP CM program. The intensive counselling and education will be supported by information, education, and communication (IEC) materials that have been developed by or in line with the Nutrition, Protection and FSL clusters.
WVSR will be identifying the right partners who has both nutrition sensitive and nutrition specific interventional capacity to support the intervention as local partner. The national NGO as partner is to be confirmed as soon as the negotiation stage is over with the donor. The activities will be implemented in the North West & North Central Syria in Aleppo, Idleb, Al Hasakeh and Ar-Raqqa. The project will be targeting the households having under five children, PLW as well as adolescent girls (13-18 years) to prevent maternal malnutrition. IYCF approach will target mother and caregivers of children under five on recommended nutrition and feeding practices. It covers promotion of appropriate breastfeeding, quality complementary feeding and feeding during difficult circumstances. In addition, the intervention will target caregivers, Community Health Workers and Community Support Groups for interventional, institutional and behavioral sustainability of the interventions. The project will ensure the intentional target of Women or children with disabilities to support with assistive devices, mainstreaming interventions with access to services and resources in Health Care facilities. 
In addition to nutrition activities, active case finding, referral & treatment of acutely malnourished children under 5 and PLW Community-level screening and referral for treatment of acute malnutrition will be conducted. Children with Moderate Acute Malnutrition and Pregnant and lactating women with a MUAC of less than 23.0cm will be referred to available supplementary treatment programs. Severe acutely malnourished children with complications will be referred for inpatient care at the existing stabilization centers. The project will provide training in nutrition screening and referral services. The project will also ensure that HFs /EPI ceneters are equipped with minimum supplies needed for nutrition screening activities, (e.g. MUAC tapes, registration and reporting format, referral forms, guidelines etc.), promoting and supporting community mobilization and sensitization activities towards nutrition screening program. The PHC and Health Facilities will be equipped with SAM/MAM cases to be treated

project_name: Improve Nutrition  Services  & Response to IDPs ,Returnees & Host Communities in  White Nile and Kassala.
project_objective: This project is aimed at providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to IDPs, refugees and vulnerable communities in White Nile and Kassala - reaching a total target of 22,000 beneficiaries across various activities. It intends to improve the nutritional status for 9,389 under-five children (8,435 girls and 972 boys) in White Nile (773 children in Guli, 1,071 children in Tandaliti and 4,406 children in Eddiwuim) and Kassala state (2,043 in River Atbara and 1,096 North Delta localities). The project will also target 2000 pregnant & lactating women (PLW) in 2 States, particularly those with children aged 0-6 months. It will support the provision of nutrition-specific services through existing structures, in conjunction with maternal and child health services and it will link households with malnourished children and PLW to FSL projects in the same targeted locality. There will be integration of early childhood care and development (ECCD) services among 5 nutrition centres. Furthermore, the project will integrate some of WASH activities into nutrition centres. The project team will also ensure coordination with other similar/ ongoing interventions. The project will deliver these activities through community services adopting the sector objectives. It takes a people-centred approach, with the most vulnerable affected people at its’ core. Vulnerable groups will be specifically targeted through this humanitarian response focused on access to nutrition services with due regard for protection, disability, equitable access, gender equality and environmental sensitivity. The project will be implemented over a period of one year.

project_name: Emergency Lifesaving WASH response to drought affected IDP population in Afder Zone of Somali Region
project_objective:
The WASH Emergency Response in Afder Zone will target populations affected by a prolonged drought after three consecutive failed rainy seasons since late 2020 affecting 6.8 million people living in Oromia, SNNP, Southwest and Somali. An estimated 175,000 people have now been displaced from their homes due to the drought. The conditions continued to worsen with the successive failed seasons in 2021. The next season in March/April 2022 might also be well below normal, making it the fourth consecutive failed rainy season thus leading more people into an alarming situation. According to the Ethiopia HRP 2022 Cluster case load Across the targeted three woredas of (13,948 Barey, 11,378 Qohle, and 5,121 God-God of Afder Zone (drought) IDPs populations have been displaced while the 3,087 people are non-displaced in the three woredas who need humanitarian lifesaving A Total 33,534 are in need of WASH Emergency lifesaving support. With the following gender, age and disability dissegregate.
As in the document of the HRP 2022 location and activities prioritization Guide for the Clusters, the project will target 47,907 vulnerable IDP and host communities in 3 woredas of Afder Zone (Barey, Qohle and God-God) locations where ADRA used to implement multi-years’ food security programs and also Emergency projects of WASH and livelihoods Funded by ADRA’s internal Funds and UN-OCHA–EHF. 
The main objective of the project will be to ensure vulnerable Drought displaced affected people have increased equal and sustained access to reliable safe water, appropriate sanitation and hygiene services. This will not only provide access to humanitarian assistance but also contribute to durable solutions.
To achieve this objective, ADRA will focus lifesaving interventions for 7 months with possible Cluster decision of flexibility to adjust in case of new life threatening crises occurs. This will be done through safe water rationing, water systems rehabilitation while ensuring proper testing and functionality before handover to the regional water bureaus and local communities, basic WASH NFIs and hygiene items like soaps, construction of gender sensitive communal latrines with hand washing facilities and promotion of adoption of positive hygiene practices and measures to prevent and also reduce possible disease outbreaks. To ensure smooth implementation and complementarity ADRA will closely coordinate with the WASH Cluster, regional and zonal authorities, and other operational partners in the targeted communities as the needs are massive and will require concerted efforts. Continuous monitoring will be undertaken in the implementation period to ensure all emerging trends are captured and reported to stakeholders. Community participation will be incorporated during the project design with women and children needs emphasis who mostly form a great percentage of the displaced populations. This approach will continue in the project implementation and lessons learnt incorporated in future responses.

In addition, ADRA will establish a protection committees involving men, women, a community leader, Religious leaders, a representative from the local authority and the police aimed to raise awareness on sexual violence and its impacts in the community; connect GBV and HIV; denounce any abuses of human rights; and share knowledge on how people could protect themselves. 

Humanitarian crises increase the risk that GBV will occur—compounding the challenges already faced by people. Girls and women are disproportionally affected by WASH issues that arise during humanitarian emergencies. Forced to travel long distances to water points or latrines—with existing sanitation facilities often lacking privacy, lighting, or locks—they are at increased risk of sexual assault and harassment. Water scarcity can create tension in the home and heighten the possibility of domestic violence. and a shortage of culturally appropriate and accessible WASH supplies, services and other support.

project_objective:
ADRA have been working for more than 4 decades in Sudan and it is one of the oldest INGOs in this country. Our work is inspired in our main values “justice, compassion and love” to assist Sudanese people in need.  Currently, we have projects in 5 states Khartoum, White Nile, Blue Nile, Central Darfur and West Darfur. All of them have faced hazard events such as flooding and intercommunal conflicts in different areas. This crisis directly affects the community, without exception of gender or age, triggering a dangerous and uncertain environment for the affected people, who suddenly loose their houses, jobs and, in some cases, their lives. ADRA looks for recovering their dignity through this project in terms of S/ NFI, complementing other WASH, FLS and Protection projects that have been developing in same areas.
Our purpose is to assist IDPs and returnees improving their currently emergency shelter through Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA). Additionally, we plan to provide shelter kits and NFI kits, for new IDPs, as we have been doing in other opportunities. 
ADRA will be working in different localities of White Nile (Kosti, El Jabalian, El Salam, Rabak, and Tendalti), Blue Nile (all localities) and West Darfur (El Geneina, Jebel Moon & Kerinik). The emergency shelter kits will be provided to 5,000 households, benefiting more than 25,000 individuals. With the same number of beneficiaries, we are going to work for the NFI kits, benefiting 5,000 households as well. For those IDPs who needs to improve their emergency shelter, we plan to assist 2,000 households, benefiting around 10,000 individuals. Out of the all beneficiaries, ADRA aims at targeting 2000 H with emergency shelter kit through cash modality.

project_name: MNCAH Support to most vulnerable communities in Lebanon
project_objective:
Lebanon is facing multiple, unprecedented crises. The COVID-19 global pandemic, in addition to a crippling year-long economic downturn and the acute impacts of the August 2020 explosions in Beirut, has compounded challenges in an already weak public health sector. The cumulative impact has meant that the most vulnerable populations – women and children face even greater hardships and UNICEF’s effort to increase access to quality health services is more critical than ever.  Through this project, UNICEF will seek to minimize the risk of further spread of COVID-19 and communicable diseases among vulnerable Lebanese and migrant populations through strengthening the COVID and communicable diseases intervention at the 5 Border Center Points and increasing the capacities and knowledge of staff working at the all Point of Entry.  This will also enable UNICEF to reach mothers and children from the most vulnerable communities among the Lebanese and migrant workers and aim to enhance their health seeking behaviors and knowledge on MNCAH including immunization.

Thereby, the project will target the 3 layers of enabling environment, demand and supply to support and enhance maternal and child access to qualitative services through:
-	Capacity building of health care providers including community midwives on updated ANC/PNC guidelines
-	Ensuring quality and safety of services especially Immunization services at PHC level through ensuring the availability of safe and effective cold chain (based on the cold chain equipment inventory analysis) and PPEs and supportive immunization service provision at PHC level.
-	Support COVID screening and awareness and routine immunization activities at POEs 
-	Enhancing community health behaviors and preventive practices among vulnerable Lebanese and migrants through capacity building and dispatch of 100 frontline workers who will be providing integrated maternal and child health messaging including immunization and COVID.

project_name: Prevention and integrated management of severe acute malnutrition in Mali
project_objective:
The nutritional situation in Mali has slightly deteriorated in 2021 compared to 2020 reporting prevalences of GAM and SAM of 10% and 1.8% respectively. In total 8 out of 11 regions are most affected (GAM >10%) including 2 regions in deep crisis (GAM> 15% or SAM >2%), which can exacerbate deaths among children given the existence of many contributing factors such as displacements due to conflicts, recurrent household food insecurity and epidemics  like COVID-19.
With aim to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with acute malnutrition, UNICEF Mali will focus on implementing an integrated package of interventions comprising (i) early detection of acute malnutrition and care for severely wasted children aged 6-59 months, (ii) prevention of stunting, wasting and micronutrient deficiencies; (iii) behaviors change communication in favour of good feeding practices for infant and young children, (iii) strengthening information system  and nutrition assessments, and (iv) coordination of  nutrition interventions. 
Globally, this emergency response will cover 1,713,312 children under-fives who will benefit from mass screening for acute malnutrition,  vitamin A supplementation, and deworming (1,713,312 children aged 6-59 months), treatment of severe acute malnutrition (177,331 children), MNPs supplementation (376,288 children aged 6-23 months), and community sensitization on good family practices (254,808 caretakers). Additionally, 360,126 pregnant and lactating mothers will receive support with micronutrient supplementation and for counselling on infant and young children feeding. Nutrition information gathering will be strengthened through routine data in DHIS2, SMART survey and rapid assessments, then analyzed and disseminated among stakeholders. Lastly, technical and financial support will be provided to ensure well-coordinated nutrition interventions at national and subnational level under cluster leadership.
This requires a total budget of 25,040,632 USD.

project_name: Protéger les enfants touchés par les conflits armés et COVID19 au Mali
project_objective:
Les enfants comptent parmi les premières victimes de l’insécurité et des conflits armés au Mali. Ils sont exposés à des risques élevés de violences, abus, exploitation et violations graves de leurs droits. La pandémie de COVID19 et ses impacts sanitaires et non sanitaires ont exacerbés les vulnérabilités existantes. L’objectif général de ce projet est d’assurer la protection des enfants dans les zones les plus touchées par le conflit au Mali notamment dans le centre et le Nord du pays, en fournissant aux enfants les services d’appui médical, psychosocial et de réintégration nécessaire pour atténuer les effets négatifs à long terme.
Le projet vise à offrir des services de protection en faveur de 600 enfants sortis des forces et groupes armés et 1200 enfants non accompagnés et séparés, y compris à cause de la  COVID19, pour la prise en charge transitoire holistique (médicale, psychosociale, alimentaire, vestimentaire) et l’appui à la réintégration socioéconomique. 1500 enfants victimes de violences physiques ou sexuelles bénéficieront des services de prise en charge appropriés. En outre, 300,000 enfants affectés par les conflits ou la COVID19 recevront un soutien psychosocial, individuel ou à base communautaire dans des espaces sécurisés.
L'UNICEF veillera à ce que 900 violations graves des droits de l’enfant par les parties au conflit soient documentées, vérifiées et rapportées en étroite collaboration avec la MINUSMA et d’autres membres du Groupe de Travail National sur le MRM. Les nombre de violations graves des droits de l’enfant (meurtre et la mutilation, le recrutement par les forces et groupes armés, viol et autres formes de violence sexuelle, enlèvement, attaques/occupation contre des écoles et des hôpitaux et déni d’accès humanitaire) est en augmentation significative avec la dégradation du conflit au centre du Mali. Le projet vise également 600 survivants de VBG/EAS dans les zones touchées par la crise, où les personnes deviennent plus vulnérables à la violence sexuelle, aux abus et à l'exploitation avec les mouvements de la population, et la COVID19. Ils recevront une assistance holistique (soutien médical et psychosocial, réintégration socioéconomique selon leurs propres besoins). En outre, 300,000 membres des communautés touchées par la crise seront sensibilisés sur la protection des enfants de la violence, le signalement des violations et la réponse aux enfants affectés et 40,000 personnes seront touchées par des actions de prévention des VBG/ EAS. 15.000 enfants 0-17 ans dépourvus de certificats de naissance recevront une aide pour l'obtenir par le biais de jugements supplétifs et une meilleure collaboration avec la santé dans les zones touchées par le conflit et la COVID- 19, ainsi que par une évaluation des enfants non enregistrés.
L’UNICEF collaborera étroitement avec les partenaires gouvernementaux ainsi que les agents de l’état civil pour assurer que leurs capacités soient développées. En répondant aux besoins des enfants les plus vulnérables, ce projet garantira que les enfants seront protégés et pourront ainsi contribuer à la paix et au développement durable du pays, en assurant leur dignité et leur accès aux services nécessaires.
La redevabilité vis-à-vis des communautés ciblées sera intégrée aux activités, y compris via un mécanisme de plainte. Outre les activités spécifiques visant à traiter directement la réponse et la prévention de l'exploitation et l'abus sexuelle (EAS), tous les partenaires d’exécution recevront une formation sur la PSEA conformément à la stratégie de l’UNICEF concernant l’évaluation des partenaires récemment introduite.
Tous les partenaires d’exécution du projet mettront en œuvre les activités dans le contexte de la COVID-19 avec la capacité et l'équipement appropriés. 30,000 personnes (partenaires étatiques et non-étatiques, acteurs communautaires, etc.) seront sensibilisées sur la COVID-19 et 400 travailleurs de protection et agents communautaires seront dotés en équipements.

project_name: Appui à l’accès à une éducation de qualité dans un environnement protecteur pour les enfants affectes par la crise sécuritaire et la pandémie de COVID-19 au Mali
project_objective: Le projet vise à promouvoir et faciliter l’accès a une éducation formelle, non formelle et des alternatives de qualité dans un environnement protecteur pour les filles et les garçons vulnérables en âge scolaire affectes par les crises. Pour cela, l’UNICEF mettra en œuvre plusieurs activités complémentaires visant à améliorer les capacités d’accueil des établissements scolaires (établissement de TLS, réhabilitation), l’insertion et réinsertion des enfants en dehors de l’école, l’appui à la réouverture des écoles, la dotation de matériels d’apprentissage, y compris les radios solaires (diffusion de leçons par les radios de proximité et groupes d’écoute), la formation des enseignants ainsi que la mise en place du protocole COVID en milieu scolaire. Le projet prend en compte les besoins spécifiques des filles et garçons en fonction de leur âge. Le projet applique le principe de « ne pas nuire » et prend en compte les risques liés à la protection afin de les réduire, les principes de redevabilité (y compris mécanismes de feedback)seront également appliques. Il cible les enfants les plus vulnérables y compris ceux avec des besoins spécifiques. L’UNICEF est engagée dans la prévention et la lutte contre l’exploitation et les abus sexuels (formation et suivi des personnels et partenaires).
