project_name: Protection et assistance multisectorielle aux réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile, rapatriés et personnes à risque d’apatridie au Mali
project_objective:
Depuis 2018, la Commission Nationale Chargée des Refugiées et le HCR enregistre une augmentation croissante du nombre de réfugiés au Mali en raison de l’insécurité au Sahel, nécessitant une réponse interagence et multisectorielle. En 2022, les projections de planification se présentent comme suit : 67 400 réfugiés, 16 500 personnes à risque d’apatridie, 25 000 réfugiés maliens de retour dans leur pays d’origine en besoin d’assistance, à savoir 10 000 nouveaux individus et 15 000 personnes rapatriées ces trois dernières années et environ 1 200 personnes dans les flux mixtes avec un besoin particulier d’assistance de la part des services d’asile. L’effectif cumulé de ces différents groupes de populations s’élèvent à 110 378 personnes. 
-	Objectif Stratégique 1 : 100% des réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile et personnes à risque d’apatridie ont accès à la protection internationale au Mali dans un délai et des conditions d’accueil optimal 

-	Objectif Stratégique 2 : 100% des réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile, rapatriés et personnes à risque d’apatridie ont accès aux services sociaux de base et aux moyens d’existence et d’autosuffisance dans leurs zones d’accueil, à travers le renforcement des capacités nationales et locales

-	Objectif Stratégique 3 :  Les réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile, rapatriés et personnes à risque d’apatridie reçoivent l’accompagnement requis en vue d’une solution durable effective en fonction de leurs besoins de protection
Le HCR se donne pour objectif d’ici à 2023 que les réfugiés, les rapatriés et les personnes à risque d’apatridie aient accès aux systèmes et services locaux et soient de plus en plus autonomes, tandis que des solutions globales et durables seront trouvées pour au moins 40% de ces personnes.
Ce projet a pour but de donner un cadre pour soutenir le Gouvernement du Mali en 2022 afin qu'il puisse concrétiser ses engagements au titre du Forum Global sur les Réfugiés de 2019 et du Segment de Haut Niveau sur l’Apatridie de la même année, à savoir : (1) renforcer le processus d'éligibilité au statut de réfugié ; (2) adopter une législation visant à transposer la convention de Kampala dans le droit interne ; (3) intégrer les réfugiés dans les plans et systèmes nationaux ; (4) éradiquer l'apatridie ; (5) élargir l'accès à des solutions durables. Il doit finalement permettre de rendre opérationnelles les recommandations du processus de Bamako notamment les conclusions du Dialogue de septembre 2019 suivi de la Déclaration ministérielle d’octobre 2019.
Les activités clés prioritaires peuvent se résumer autour des éléments suivants :
-	pour les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile : 1) Répondre rapidement et efficacement aux nouveaux déplacements en renforçant la capacité du Gouvernement à coordonner la réponse et à fournir une protection internationale aux réfugiés nouvellement arrivés du Burkina Faso et du Niger. 2) Assurer l'accès à l'asile, l'intégrité de la protection des réfugiés et des demandeurs d'asile et la préservation de l'espace de protection par les autorités maliennes dans le contexte d'afflux massifs et de mouvements mixtes. 3) Soutenir la mise en œuvre de solutions durables, y compris le processus d'intégration locale des réfugiés en situation prolongée. 4) Soutenir l'accès à l'état civil, aux documents d'identité et à la nationalité. 5) Mettre à jour les plans d'urgence de l'opération nationale en tant qu'exercice prioritaire et en tant que mesure de préparation aux situations d'urgence, en y associant les principaux acteurs et partenaires. 

-	pour les rapatriés : réaliser les priorités du gouvernement en se concentrant sur 1) permettre aux réfugiés maliens de prendre une décision éclairée concernant leur retour potentiel ; 2) faciliter l'accueil des réfugiés maliens de retour au pays ; 3) assurer leur réintégration socio-économique multisectorielle durable en 2021, sur la base de 5 principes avec une approche centrée sur la nature : Protéger, Répondre, Inclure, Tenir pour responsable et Résoudre.

project_name: Protection, Assistance (abris et biens non alimentaire) et renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection des PDIs au Niger.
Protection and assistance to IDPs, IDP and returnees and conflict affected population
project_objective:
Overall, there are 6,596,342 persons in need of protection support across the country. This includes 3,036,593 IDPs, 969397 returnees, 1,098,272 refugees and 1,492,080 vulnerable Sudanese. New and protracted displacement, lack of basic services and the deteriorating economic situation, have all had profound consequences on conflict-affected persons’ immediate physical and mental well-being, living standards, and their long-term resilience. 
Rule of law, access to justice and government social protection remains weak in conflict-affected areas of Darfur, South Kordofan and Blue Nile including the two areas controlled by nonstate actors. The natural disasters, including disease outbreak and scarcity of resources have further impacted public service delivery and heightened the socio-economic vulnerability of displaced families. 
General protection needs are most severe in the hotspot localities, where inter-communal conflict and factional fighting have been reported throughout 2021 and people remained deprive of access to government services in the two areas. Such chaotic situation is exacerbated by the proliferation of firearms, competition over land and water resources, unregulated migratory routes, and weak systems for land administration. As a result of reported incidents: hundreds of civilians were killed or wounded; HLP damaged, looted, destroyed or occupied; thousands of families displaced; and public facilities destroyed occupied. Furthermore, UNAMID withdrawal at the end of 2020 created a gap in the civilian protection framework in Darfur. This left humanitarian protection mechanisms and services, and durable solutions programming by protection and peacebuilding actors, as the mainstay across Sudan.
Vulnerable groups - such as women, children, elderly, persons with disabilities and chronic illnesses - face a range of challenges unique to their individual circumstances, compounded by their displacement where familial/community support networks not functioning or are overstretched. These and other groups of people suffer disproportionately from various protection risks, including violence, sexual and other forms of exploitation and abuse, and human-rights violations. For women and girls, risks of GBV remain significant, particularly when they are on the move, working in fields, collecting water or firewood. Boys and men remain especially at risk of physical violence, injury and death and arbitrary arrests, as they are often suspected of supporting armed opposition groups. Child marriage and child labor are on the rise. Access to birth registration continues to be a challenge in most locations, placing both IDPs and refugees at significant risk of not accessing basic services. Persons with disabilities continue to be marginalized and neglected, with few government or humanitarian services targeted to meet their unique needs. Access to health care, particularly for the elderly and those with chronic illnesses, who are at heightened risk due to COVID-19, remains limited.
In order to meet the sectoral and intersectoral needs of the targeted population, contribute to the achievement the HRP 2022 protection sector focuses its intervention around the following specific objectives: 
•	Provide protection services to vulnerable crisis-affected people, particularly those with special needs;  
•	Strengthen community-based protection mechanisms to prevent and mitigate protection risks, and to address protection needs where feasible; 
•	Contribute to a favorable protection environment through engagement of and support to authorities, humanitarian and peacebuilding partners.

project_objective:
To improve equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving and comprehensive sexual reproductive health (SRHR) services for Rohingya refugees and host communities, UNFPA will continue to strengthen its implementation of integrated services through health systems strengthening and community engagement, through coordination and partnership within a multi-sectoral approach, with the overarching guidance of the Health Sector and key players.  Family planning will be the center of UNFPA’s strategic, technical and programmatic guidance related to provision and delivery of a continuum of care package for essential SRHR services to the last mile.  This includes strategic collaboration with the Gender based violence [GBV] Sub-Sector, Community health workers [CHW] Working Group and other key sectors/actors.

UNFPA will ensure continuous availability and facilitate accessibility of family planning and other related SRH commodities, supplies and equipment through improved supply chain management, to meet the unmet needs of refugees and surrounding host communities. The project will centralise facilities and community based family planning, improve and maintain the quality of services provided through strengthening of referrals and transfer of obstetric emergency cases, availability and accessibility of life saving SRHR commodities, client centered quality and respectful midwifery led antenatal and postnatal care, safe birth, menstrual regulation, cervical cancer and obstetric fistula screening and treatment, adolescent SRHR services, and quality assurance through mentorship and support to service providers. Health providers' and community health workers’ capacity will be strengthened to provide integrated client centered quality services, including family planning. In addition, these integrated services will strengthen and expand existing behavioural change approaches. 

UNFPA will strengthen readiness to meet SRHR needs during disasters through capacity building, stock prepositioning, and SRHR policy formulation. Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic presented an unprecedented burden on health systems around the world, which Bangladesh is not an exception. It exacerbated existing gaps in availability of comprehensive SRHR services provision and threatened the continuation of these essential services.  Like other health emergencies, as restrictions and lockdowns were put in place to prevent and curtail the spread of the disease increased women and girls’ vulnerabilities. To ensure continuity of comprehensive integrated SRHR services provision during this protracted pandemic, UNFPA will continue its preventative and response interventions, through the operationalisation of maternity red zones and Isolation Treatment Centres [ITC] and provision of integrated SRHR/GBV services in health facilities, communities and women and girls protected spaces.

project_name: Provision of Multipurpose Cash to Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Syria
project_objective:
UNRWA plans to provide up to 420,000 Palestine refugees with cash assistance to meet their basic needs, including food, non-food items (NFIs), and WASH needs. The Agency will continue to provide this assistance based on a targeted approach introduced in 2019, prioritizing refugees assessed as most vulnerable with a higher cash transfer. In 2022, it is expected that around 145,000 Palestine refugees will be assessed as most vulnerable based on the four vulnerability categories used by UNRWA (female headed households, families with persons with disabilities, families headed by an older person and unaccompanied minors/orphans). The remaining 275,000 vulnerable Palestine refugees will receive a lower cash transfer value as explained below. 

Our cash transfer values were calculated while designing our Emergency Appeal 2022 intervening during the last quarter of 2021. The values were based on discussions with the CWG and in consultation with other humanitarian actors and are aligned with CWG recommendations, and more specifically the suggested MEB transfer values. Based on these discussions and recommendations, our cash transfer values were set to  SYP 312,500 per month for a family of five members belonging to the most vulnerable categories   and SYP 225,000 per month for a family of five members belonging to the remaining caseload of vulnerable Palestine refugees. 


UNRWA plans to provide its monthly assistance to Palestine refugees covering twelve months over three rounds of assistance in 2022, with each round covering four months of cash assistance. Ideally, the rounds would start on 1 January, 1 May, and 1 September. In reality, UNRWA might adjust the start date and duration of each round depending on fund availability and taking into account cash flow considerations and donor requirements for the different grants. 


UNRWA plans to conduct two post-distribution monitoring exercise in July and December 2022. UNRWA also has a result-based monitoring (RBM) system which tracks a number of indicators for all programmes and interventions including cash assistance. Quarterly management review (QMR) meetings involving relevant staff, including senior management, are held to track and assess the indicators. Mid-year result review (MYRR) and annual result review (ARR) are also conducted with departments at HQ to add another layer of scrutiny and to provide an overall overview of achievements and challenges.

It is worth mentioning that UNRWA also plans to provide in-kind food assistance to all 420,000 Palestine refugees through three distribution rounds of food baskets. Each food basket includes wheat flour, rice, bulgur wheat, sunflower oil, sugar, chick peas, lentils and milk (aligned with WFP). This intervention is designed to help Palestine refugees in addressing the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, coupled with the socio-economic crisis and the increase in prices of basic commodities, which have severely affected the food security status of Palestine refugees and depleted their comping mechanisms. The details of this intervention are included in a separate project submitted to the Food cluster.

project_name: Provision of in-kind food assistance to Vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
UNRWA estimates that 420,000 Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance in 2022. In a context of rising inflation and additional economic hardship caused by COVID-19, Palestine refugees are more and more affected by food insecurity and therefore increasingly depend on UNRWA assistance to meet their minimum food needs. The Agency will continue to monitor the availability of food on the markets and will retain operational flexibility to adjust to a changing context as appropriate. The composition of the food basket was developed based on WFP guidelines and in view of meeting  50% of daily nutritional needs for 4 months. 
UNRWA's original plan is to distribute 3 rounds of in-kind food assistance, each round covering a period of 4 months. However, this depends on the availability of funds. Until January 2022, UNRWA received or confirmed pledges are only sufficient to cover the first two rounds of 2022. The Agency will continue to mobilize resources to ensure funding for the third round is also secured. In 2022, the number of people estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance including for food needs is 420,000 Palestine refugees to strengthen their resilience and prevent further deterioration into acute food insecurity. As per its emergency planning, UNRWA aims to provide food assistance as well as multipurpose cash assistance, and protection interventions at both household and community levels, as well as the coordination of these activities across the different Sectors framework. The in-kind food assistance program remains one of the most important forms of UNRWA emergency support to stabilize the food security status for Palestine refugees in Syria with the MPC based on complementarity approach considering that MPC transfer value will not cover the full needs of the beneficiaries and the potential unavailability of fund.  , as it helps them meet part of their basic nutritional and survival requirements (~50% of kcal/person/day) which will increase resilience, and reduce humanitarian needs and the spiraling food insecurity levels.

project_name: Emergency Cash for Work in Gaza
project_objective:
Access to food in Gaza remains a challenge for a majority of refugees struggling with deteriorating socio-economic condition compounded with recurrent hostilities and the COVID-19 emergency. Soaring rates of unemployment and limited income are key drivers to poverty and food insecurity among the population. Through the Cash for Work intervention, UNRWA aims to support Palestine refugees in Gaza coping with protracted threats and shocks, and mitigate food insecurity through offering short term employment opportunities to approximately 14,000 poor Palestine refugees. These will be equal to more than 1,430,000 work days, and will inject over US$ 17.6 million into households, generating almost 5,000 full time job equivalents (FTEs). The short term job opportunities will include more than 10,000 unskilled positions, more than 3,800 skilled positions and around 170 professional positions. UNRWA developed a Standard Operation Procedures amidst COVID-19 emergency to ensure that beneficiaries under the Cash for Work programming have access to enhanced occupational health and safety norms for the work they agree to undertake. It identifies the functions and manner in which the Cash for Work modality can be deployed for UNRWA activities safely and in a dignified manner in order to continue providing income generation opportunities to refugees to achieve livelihood objectives.

The project is directly addressing the HRP Strategic Outcome 3: the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Preparedness in Gaza
project_objective:
The unique socio-economic conditions of blockade, with its movement restrictions and destruction of productive capacity, are further compounded by repeated cycle of conflicts and political instability and ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The May 2021 hostilities left significant damages on the already eroded coping mechanisms and people’s sense of hope for the future.
In response, UNRWA aims to provide emergency shelter assistance through: (1) Transitional Shelter Cash Assistance to up to 1,000 Palestine refugee families, still displaced following the May 2021 hostilities and (2) Shelter reconstruction and repair work for 7,200 conflict-affected Palestine refugee shelters; and enhancing emergency preparedness through: (1) provision and stockpiling of Non-Food Items (NFIs) in case of emergencies, (2) maintenance works of existing 54 UNRWA Designated Emergency Shelters (DESs), (3) equipping 25 Mobile Emergency Shelters, and (4) emergency preparedness trainings for 13,000 UNRWA staff.

project_name: Assistance en abris et NFis aux personnes en situation de déplacement dans la région l’Extrême Nord Cameroun
project_objective:
La région de l’extrême depuis 2013 est sujet aux exactions Boko Haram. Ces exactions occasionnent dans la plupart des cas des mouvements de déplacements de personnes, et laisse ces populations nouvellement arrivées et ceux ayant déjà passé de nombreuses années sur les sites dans les besoins incessant en abris et Nfis.
A ce jours 964 sites spontanés et villages au sein desquels les interventions humanitaires ont été apportées par les différents acteurs montrent que 22 % vivent dans des abris de fortune (tige et paille) 40 % dans les familles d’accueil où règne la promiscuité.
Au-delà des nouveaux déplacements, nous enregistrons aussi des ménages qui retournent vers leurs lieux d’origine du fait de l’amélioration de la sécurité dans ces localités d’origine. Ces personnes retournées sont soumises aux conditions de vie très difficile et précaire du fait de la dégradation de leurs habitats après plusieurs années d’abandons. Ce qui les conduits à loger dans les espaces communautaires ou dans les familles d’accueil en attendant des solutions meilleures pour leur habitat.
Les localités les plus vulnérables sont situé dans les arrondissements de Logone et Chari, Mayo Sava et Mayo Tsanaga et compte tenu de l’évolution de la crise, avec la sécurité qui tarde à revenir dans les zones frontalières, nous continuons à enregistrer des déplacements secondaires de IDPs à la recherche des moyens de subsistance vers les départements du Mayo Danay et le Diamaré qui ne sont pas directement impacté par la crise mais dans lesquels les déplacés sont dans les besoins des abris et Nfis.
L’objectif principal étant d’améliorer le cadre de vie des personnes en situation de déplacement à travers :
•	Fournir des abris et des articles non alimentaires pour sauver des vies aux personnes en déplacement et communautés hôtes.
•	Fournir un accès durable aux abris pour les personnes résidant sur les sites IDPs et ménages d’accueils et retournés.
•	Favoriser un environnement propice à la protection et à la cohésion sociale et autonomisation, en améliorant le logement et les infrastructures communautaires et publiques connexes dans les communautés d’accueils et de retour ainsi que dans sites des IDPs.

Activité 1 : Une fourniture en articles de première nécessité et essentiels de base, tels que matelas, bâches en plastique, couvertures, jerrycans, ustensiles de cuisine, lampes solaires. Elle consistera aux ciblages des localités et distribution en nature ou en cash si le marché local est fonctionnel pour les personnes les vulnérables (IDPs, communauté hôtes) dans les localités accueillant de nouveaux déplacés. 
Activité 2 : Fourniture d'abris à travers la construction et installations des abris d’urgence, transitionnels pour les personnes à besoins spécifique.  Pour les autres catégories des personnes une assistance en kits matériaux et outils de construction leur sera donnée. Les modalités CaSH seront utilisées dans les localités ayant des marché fonctionnels et fournis après une enquête faite.
Activité 3 : Pour des ménages résidant dans les familles d’accueils et retournés des accompagnements seront faits pour la fourniture des abris durables afin de réduire la promiscuité pour un meilleur respect de standard de 3,5 m/ personne. Les infrastructures sociales de base (écoles, centre de santé et centre des femmes et jeunes) détériorées lors des attaques seront réhabilitées. Celles  totalement détruites  seront reconstruites,  ceci avec une forte implication de la partie gouvernementale  pour le respect de la stratégie nationale. 
Activité 4 : Des formation théoriques et séance de renforcement de capacités des jeunes volontaires identifiés dans différentes localités d’intervention seront mises en œuvre. Ces jeunes constitués en comité locale seront mis à contribution dans les activités communautaires de construction des abris des vulnerables.

project_objective:
WHO is leading the health sector to support the MoHFW with the mandate and capacity to set priorities, minimum standards, and support quality health service delivery, and subsequently is aligned with the overall Health Sector Strategies delineated in the Joint Response Plan 2022. The activities set under this project have been selected based on the Health Sector needs highlighted by preliminary findings of Joint Multisectoral Needs Assessment (J-MSNA)- October 2021, Health Facility Gap Analysis - October 2021 and Age and Disability Inclusion Needs Assessment May 2021.
 
WHO will continue supporting the Government of Bangladesh and partners towards equity and quality of services, advocate on behalf of the Health Sector on inadequately addressed issues; and to respond outbreaks of communicable diseases including COVID-19 through a well-established response system and strengthening outbreak/pandemic response and routine immunization system in line with national and global structures, while continuing to deliver an effective health response to the Rohingya crisis through increased investment in public/local institutions and capacity development of local government, in addition to that of partners. This is expected to ensure sustainability of interventions and benefit host community as well as Rohingya while contributing to building resilient systems for future unforeseen events and emergencies.
WHO will focus on monitoring and supporting revitalization of utilization of essential services with quality service delivery as part of efforts to sustain what is achieved in the two and half year before the COVID-19, while maintaining capacity to continue support response to emerging  needs that result from emergencies due to natural disasters, man-made and technological disasters and other disease outbreaks in this protracted humanitarian crisis over and above ensuring continuity of emergency services during the monsoon and cyclone seasons and disaster risk reduction, resilience  and contributing to addressing climate change 
WHO intends to continue providing regular and timely information on public health risks and requirements and filling gaps through effective coordination of partners, and effective response ensuring access to life saving interventions mediated by rationalized health service delivery system.
The underlying principles of WHO’s work remain and will be reinforced to  liaise with national government on the governance and leadership through Civil Surgeon’s Office and MOHFW Coordination Centre, support in developing and adapting standards, guidelines and protocols, extending of national programs to the refugee settings and; avail  health workforce, vaccines and essential technology, health information, service delivery based on minimum essential services package, for neonates, children, boys and girls and  women and men in both the Rohingyas and host community.
The planned interventions will be guided by periodical service availability assessments, and external independent reviews and assessments will be used as an opportunity for the Rohingya and host community populations to review the work of WHO

project_name: Strengthening access to health care and detection and response to public health emergencies in Sudan
project_objective:
Since 2019, Sudan is in a transition period and despite the recent peace agreements and efforts to stabilize the situation, the humanitarian health situation remains fragile. The main drivers of the humanitarian health crisis in Sudan include  armed conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks, and floods as much as lack of staff, lack of medicines, medical supplies and equipment as much as lack of operational costs. Disease outbreaks are mostly water and sanitation related, vector-borne and vaccine preventable. The humanitarian health response project aims to address major risk factors, to provide free-of-charge essential and life-saving health services to vulnerable populations and to strengthen the intersectoral multi-hazard preparedness and response. WHO’s preparedness and response to health emergencies is in line with the national health sector and health cluster strategies and follows national and international standards. WHO will provide technical and operational support to the coordination mechanisms on all levels of the health emergency response and will strengthen and support the collection, analysis and dissemination of health related information and data in close collaboration with partners and other stakeholders. WHO will also strengthen the different pillars of disease surveillance with the aim to increase the capacities of early investigation, confirmation and immediate response to public health threats and to contribute to the health security of the targeted population groups and beyond. 
WHO, as provider of last resort, will procure and distribute free of charge medicines, medical supplies, medical equipment, personal protective equipment (PPEs) and laboratory reagents to support the humanitarian health care provided by NGOs and MOH. WHO will also engage in capacity building of health workers on health emergency related subjects such as surveillance, case management and infection prevention and control for diseases with outbreak potential including Covid-19. The project will also include small repair and rehabilitation of health facilities, supporting operational costs for humanitarian health services as necessary and also health risk communication to vulnerable populations. Access to health services to all age groups and gender with their specific health needs adapted to the local cultural customs is promoted, including advocacy and synergic linkages with ongoing recovery-development interventions.  6.4 million people residing in  75 localities with severity ranking level of 4 and 5 for humanitarian health response. The activities related to outbreak control are not restricted only to the 107 targeted localities but WHO will intervene wherever the needs arise under its mandate for health security and protection of health. COVID-19 community transmission is likely to continue in all states of Sudan in 2022 in all parts of the population despite the ongoing vaccination efforts and is likely to continue its impact on access to health care. As of its mandate, WHO has integrated in this proposal interventions to contain the outbreak and to support adequate health services for the target population. This includes among others infection prevention and control, isolation center support, scale up of access to testing also in remote areas, support to scale up vaccination coverage and outbreak alert investigations. These interventions are cost intensive and contribute significantly to the requested budget.

project_name: Malnutrition prevention and treatment programme for refugees and host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
WFP aims to contribute to a reduction in acute and chronic malnutrition rates, and an improvement in nutritional status among refugees and host communities in Cox’s Bazar through the provision of curative and preventive nutrition services for children below 5 years and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). 

WFP will implement its project interventions across 45 integrated in nutrition facilities in all 34 camps: and 129 sites in the host community in partnership with UNICEF, UNHCR and implementing partners. 
WFP will provide targeted supplementary feeding program (TSFP) for moderate acutely malnourished children 6-59 months and PLW to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in both the refugee camps and in the host community. 

An enhanced prevention of malnutrition package will be put in place. This includes provision of the blanket supplementary feeding program (BSFP) for children 6-59 months and PLW to mitigate the increase in prevalence of acute and chronic malnutrition and its associated risks for mortality, morbidity, and child development; a nutrition sensitive cash transfer to a proportion of older children (24-59 months) to enable them access more fresh fruits and vegetables and enhance their dietary diversity in the refugee camps; Social Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) activities and utilization of tools that positively influence behaviour, knowledge and attitudes around nutrition, hygiene and social protection interventions to improve dietary practices and ensure sustained changes for cases of malnutrition.

Prevention of stunting among children 6 – 23 months (the 1000 days window of opportunity) through promotion of recommended Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices (breastfeeding for children below 2 years and complementary feeding for children 6 – 23 months) and appropriate maternal nutrition will also be part of the project interventions. 

Active case finding through community screening, referral and follow up of malnourished children under five and pregnant and lactating women will be done. Additionally, growth monitoring and promotion for children 6-59 months will be part of the project interventions.

The underlying causes of malnutrition will be addressed through integration of nutrition sensitive approaches in ongoing general food assistance, school feeding, self-reliance, and livelihood interventions. 

WFP will promote the prevention of micronutrient deficiencies particularly anaemia through the promotion of dietary diversification. 

WFP will conduct capacity strengthening for partners and stakeholders to improve capacity for implementation of nutrition specific and nutrition sensitive programming. 

WFP will support quantitative and qualitative nutrition assessments to ensure that nutrition programmes are tailormade according to the needs of the targeted populations. 

Project interventions will be adapted to ensure an inclusive approach to promote participation of women, men, older people, people who have chronic health conditions and persons with disabilities. Additionally, protection mechanisms will be put in place including complaints and feedback mechanisms and help desks to ensure accountability to affected populations.

project_name: Enhance food security through the delivery of an Integrated Assistance Package for refugee and host community populations in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
***TOTAL WFP PROJECT BUDGET IS USD 201,680,000, AND THE APPEALING AMOUNT OF 170,000,000 REFLECTS THE BUDGET GAP***
WFP will provide life-saving food assistance to the entire Rohingya refugee population (approximately 900,000 people) through General Food Assistance. Beneficiaries will receive entitlements that can be redeemed from WFP-contracted local retailers across the camps. E-vouchers provide more flexibility, dignity and greater dietary diversity for the refugees while also creating market linkages with the host community and the wider Bangladeshi economy. To ensure an effective and efficient emergency intervention, WFP will preposition enough in-kind food to rapidly respond to the needs of approximately 30,000 households should they be displaced by monsoon, cyclone or conflict.
In addition to providing large-scale food assistance, WFP makes sure to address the needs of the most vulnerable households through promoting income generating activities in the camps and host communities. WFP will provide complementary food vouchers to 250,000 extremely vulnerable individuals through Fresh Food Corners. WFP will also engage 37,700 Rohingya refugee households in training and provide inputs for camps-based needs such as homestead vegetable production, community aquaculture, recycling project amongst other activities. In cooperation with the Government of Bangladesh, WFP will support 29,100 host community households with agricultural and non-agricultural livelihoods activities, including 10,397 women (head of households) with monthly subsistence allowance and business development, capacity strengthening and follow-up support to ex-beneficiaries through market linkage activities in Ukhiya and Teknaf and 18,703 women (head of households) with capacity strengthening, business support and market linkage opportunities.

project_name: Provision of security telecommunications and data connectivity services to the humanitarian community
project_objective:
The ETS will continue to provide overall coordination and will improve communications services to the humanitarian community. ETS services and activities to be provided include coordination, information management, data connectivity, security telecommunications, customer support, and capacity development. The ETS plans to expand and improve each of these services while maintaining current sites provided with ETS services.
The humanitarian community’s demand for reliable communications services remains a priority. To address this, the ETS will continue to provide security telecommunications and data connectivity services across all common operational areas to support the humanitarian community and to enable the provision of digital assistance to affected communities.
The ETS security telecommunications network currently provides VHF radio communications to users from 11 UN agencies. In 2022, the network will be expanded to more areas of the camps in collaboration with UNDSS.
The ETS data connectivity network will continue providing connectivity across the operational areas, to both UN agencies and NGOs as needed, enabling these organizations to carry-out their life-saving activities. In 2022, the network will be expanded to more sites, more organizations, and more users across the three operational areas, with a goal of 70 total sites by the end of 2022.
To strengthen local emergency communications expertise and skills on the ground, the ETS will continue to assess the needs of humanitarians and conduct capacity building exercises tailored to those needs. Activities will include trainings telecommunications and radio communications procedures, trainings on the use of data connectivity services, and other requested capacity development programs where gaps in knowledge or skills are assessed.
A new activity in 2022 for ETS will be the Services for Communities project, aiming to increase engagement with the affected communities and provide an opportunity for ETS to support them through technology. This new activity - a part of the global ETC strategy - will evaluate the possibility of implementing communications services directly to the affected populations by providing a range of services such as access to information, common feedback mechanisms, etc.

project_name: Asset creation (including Disaster Risk Reduction), Project and Site Maintenance Engineering
project_objective: Through the Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) programme and Site Maintenance Engineering Project (SMEP), WFP will work with Rohingya refugees and host communities to prevent and reduce risks from natural disasters, enhance accessibility and strengthen resilience. The project will provide targeted assistance for Rohingya refugees and enhance food security in host communities through asset creation (including Disaster Risk Reduction) by building and rehabilitating assets that will create a healthier natural environment, reduce the risks and impact of climate shocks and strengthen resilience to natural disasters over time. Such activities will ultimately address immediate SD needs through cash transfer modality. Also ensuring inclusive approach integrated with gender equality, women’s empowerment and protection principles including strong coordination at the camp-level (with SD focals and SMS) and to coordination at Cox’s Bazar with sector.

project_name: School Feeding Programme
project_objective: WFP School Feeding Programme aims to improve children’s learning by addressing the root causes of hunger and micronutrient deficiencies that can have consequences on their cognitive growth. In the camps, WFP will provide a packet of 50 g of High Energy Biscuits (HEB) to children enrolled in learning centres every school day. In the host community, WFP will provide HEBs to pre-primary and primary school children in Government schools, approved “madrassas” (Islamic schools) and NGO-run schools every school day. These locally-produced HEBs are fortified with 14 vitamins and minerals, and provide approximately half of the daily micronutrient requirements for a child between 5 and 11 years. WFP also implements literacy, health, WASH and nutrition activities and will conduct awareness-raising activities with parents, School Management Committees, teachers and children on health, hygiene, nutrition and other social issues.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence pour les populations deplacées internes dans la province du Lac
project_objective:
Situé entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale, le bassin du lac Tchad couvre le Tchad, le Cameroun, le Niger et le Nigeria. Important bassin de production agro-pastorale et halieutique, le bassin du lac-Tchad repose sur un écosystème fragile mais avec une production variée et connaissant une démographie croissante. On estime ainsi à 2 million le nombre d’habitants vivant directement des ressources du bord du Lac. 

La Province du Lac est l’une des zones les plus vulnérables au Tchad car difficile d’accès, insuffisamment desservie par les services sociaux de base et sujette de façon récurrente aux effets du changement climatiques caractérisés par les sécheresses et les inondations qui sont parmi les aléas les plus importants. Les conséquences de catastrophes qu’elles engendrent pèsent lourdement sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages. 

La crise dans la Province du Lac a débuté fin 2014 à la suite des premières attaques de groupes armés non étatiques qui ont entrainé des mouvements de populations et bousculé les échanges et équilibres socio-économiques dans cette province, déjà en proie aux effets du réchauffement climatique qui y aggravent notamment l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle. Cette crise qui perdure a causée des pertes en vies humaines, des déplacements forcés des populations, des pertes des actifs productifs, des pressions sur les ressources naturelles et une des articulations de l’économie engendrant ainsi des conséquences sur l’emploi en particulier pour les jeunes.

La dégradation des conditions sécuritaires en raison de l’intensification des attaques des Groupes Armés Non étatiques (GANE) et des opérations de l’armée comme l’attaque de Boma, est la cause principale de la détérioration de la situation humanitaire au Lac, particulièrement dans les départements de Kaya et Fouli qui accueillent les sites les plus importants de populations déplacées. 

Le nombre de personnes déplacées dans la province du Lac est de 457 948 individus en octobre 2021 localisés dans 223 localités dont 166 sites et 57 communautés hôtes (round 16 DTM OIM) avec respectivement 174 920 personnes déplacées dans le département de Fouli, 191 798 personnes déplacées dans le département de Kaya et 91 230 personnes déplacées dans le département du Mamdi. 

Ces événements ont, entre autres, entravé l’accès des populations aux productions vivrières et rentières et affectés les moyens de subsistance de ces populations vulnérables. La situation de cette zone reste préoccupante en matière de sécurité dans les zones insulaires, car le contexte continue d’être volatile et précaire. Le PAM planifie appuyer 350 000 personnes déplacées internes avec une assistance alimentaire d’urgence inconditionnelle. 

Cette assistance alimentaire d’urgence sera adaptée sur la vulnérabilité des ménages déplacés vivant dans les départements de Fouli, Kaya et Mamdi. De plus, cette assistance sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: Appui à l' Enseignement Fondamentale et à la scolarisation des filles grâce à des programmes intégrés d'Alimentation Scolaire
project_objective: Le présent projet soutient les objectifs à long terme du Plan Intérimaire pour l'Education du Tchad, à savoir: (i) améliorer l’accès à l’éducation des enfants issus des ménages vulnérables et (ii) réduire les disparités entre les sexes à l’école. Il contribue principalement à l'atteinte de l'objectif de développement durable n° 2 (Faim Zéro). Il également aux objectifs de développement durable 1 (éliminer la pauvreté), 4 (éducation inclusive et qualitative et à l'apprentissage tout au long de la vie), 5 (égalité des sexes) et 17 (partenariat pour la mise en œuvre des objectifs de développement durable). Au total, 268,797 bénéficiaires directs et indirects seront ciblés dans les provinces sahéliennes de Bahr-el-Ghazal, Batha, Guéra, Kanem, Ouaddaï et logone Oriental enregistrant des taux élevés d'insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition combinés à des indicateurs de scolarisation bas.

project_name: Water and sanitation assistance (WASA)
project_objective:
This project includes several types of intervention, such as water system rehabilitation, boreholes rehabilitation and solar systems installation in locations where household-level access to water is limited due to electricity outages, WASH in schools' repair, debris removal in areas where it poses a significant health and protection risk to the local population, especially in  Deir-Ez-Zor, sewage pumping station or where the sewerage systems that are damaged and pose a significant risk to the local people as well as WASH assistance in camps and distribution of hygiene kits.
WASA will give approximately 560,000 beneficiaries (85000 households) access to safe water and sewage services. The beneficiaries will be selected on a detailed needs assessment, and those with the highest need and underserved by the humanitarian community will be prioritised for assistance. The targeted category includes newly returned returnees, IDPs and vulnerable host communities across the governorates of Homs, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Idlib, and Deir-Ez-Zor. Depsit of Homs low severity scale of Homs ADRA had to include the WASH activities as a complementary for the Shelter project in Al Quseir.
The project will use a participatory and integrated approach to ensure that the needs of men, women, boys and girls are included from the project design stage through to implementation and post-implementation monitoring of the work. Children, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults and older adults will be solicited during the initial needs assessment for the project and post-implementation. Each age and gender group will have an opportunity to provide timely feedback to ADRA on the intervention through regular contact with ADRA monitoring staff. 
 The needs of young children, children, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults and older adults will also be taken into consideration as children, adolescents, middle-aged and older adults may require a higher amount of water for cleaning cooking and for children who play outside and require more frequent hygiene practices.

project_name: Syrian Children Have Open Opportunities for Learning (SCHOOL)
project_objective:
The project aims to increase safe and equitable access to formal and non-formal education for crisis-affected children and youth (aged 5 -17 years) and improve the quality of formal and non-formal education for children and youth (aged 5 - 17 years) within a protective environment. The project will be implemented in close coordination with MoE and related DoEs ensuring the protection of all beneficiaries through a ‘do not harm’ approach. ADRA Syria through this project will improve access to formal and non-formal education, learning opportunities, and Early Childhood Education (ECE) for girls and boys by creating safe and protective environments for 19,580 female and male children and teachers who have been affected by the crisis. This will be done through education interventions within the governorates of Rural Damascus, Quneitra, Homs, Aleppo, Dara’a, Lattakia, Hama, Raqqa and Deir Alzour. ADRA Syria through the project will enhance the formal and non – formal education level for the children, both boys and girls. This will include a holistic program with psycho-social, familial and educational support, encouraging the engagement of mothers and fathers in educational activities. ADRA will coordinate with key stakeholders to ensure the most vulnerable boys and girls are identified in the target locations, and ADRA will conduct comprehensive needs assessments in the areas identified to locate OOSC and students with priority educational needs.

Renforcement de la resilience et développement des moyens d'existence
project_objective:
Le Tchad fait face à des crises majeures résultant des causes conjoncturelles et structurelles qui sont entre autres : les mouvements de populations, la mauvaise production agropastorale, les effets négatifs de l’application des mesures barrière de la pandémie du COVID-19. Ces crises accroissent la vulnérabilité de plusieurs millions de personnes qui sont déjà confrontées au faible développement local et à la pauvreté affectant ainsi leurs capacités de résilience d’où une forte insécurité alimentaire et une malnutrition sévère. Les résultats de l’analyse de la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle (cadre harmonisé, novembre 2021) révèlent que 963,244 personnes seront en phase 3 et plus pour la phase courante d’octobre à décembre 2021 que 1 737 245 personnes en phase crise ou plus (Phase 3 et plus) pour la période projetée de juin à août 2022. La situation nutritionnelle quant à elle, reste globalement critique et préoccupante avec une prévalence nationale de 11 % de la MAG et 2,1 % de MAS. Le bilan céréalier prévisionnel dégage un déficit brut de 482 705 T et un déficit net de 291 341 T. La disponibilité apparente est de 143 kg par habitant et par an. Cette disponibilité est en baisse de 10,1% par rapport à la norme officielle de consommation qui est de 159 kg par habitant et par an.
Dans ce contexte fragile, il est important de concevoir les interventions humanitaires en faveur de ces catégories des personnes à travers un spectre nouveau et d’œuvrer autant que possible au développement des activités nouvelles et complémentaires pour sauver les vies des populations en proie à l’insécurité alimentaire et à la malnutrition. Ces actions s’alignent étroitement avec les objectifs fixés par le Cluster Sécurité Alimentaire et la coordination humanitaire dans la définition stratégique : (i) Sauver des vies et (ii) Renforcer la résilience.
Le présent projet trouve sa valeur ajoutée dans l’appui et le renforcement de la résilience des ménages les plus vulnérables vivant dans 16 provinces et 36 départements identifiés parmi les départements en situation de crise et plus (cadre harmonisé, novembre 2021) et d’autres départements du pays. La stratégie du PAM pour les projets de résilience 2022 est d’appuyer 236,513 personnes issus des départements en phase crise ou plus (Phase 3 et plus) et des personnes issues des départements ne faisant pas partie de ce groupe mais qui étaient déjà appuyées par le PAM dans le but d’assurer la durabilité de nos interventions et la resilience des bénéficiaires. 
Ce projet de résilience consiste à construire ou réhabiliter les actifs productifs, à l’intention des ménages et des communautés, afin de réduire le risque de catastrophe, de renforcer les moyens d’existence et la résilience à long terme et de fournir des transferts directs de type monétaire visant à combler le déficit de consommation alimentaire des plus vulnérables pour leur permettre d’avoir accès à la nourriture à court terme.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_name: Humanitarian Coordination Assistance for the Syria Response Plan
project_objective:
The 2022-2023 Syria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) sets out the framework within which the humanitarian community will respond to large-scale humanitarian and protection needs in Syria, flexibly leveraging the various response modalities.
Capturing these capacities and efforts under a single strategic framework, the plan aims to increase the effectiveness of the response by improving the identification of needs and gaps, reducing overlap and duplication, and monitoring context changes and progress against collective agreed response results. The Humanitarian Coordinator for Syria and the Regional Humanitarian Coordinator for the Syria Crisis lead and coordinate humanitarian action inside Syria. OCHA, in line with its global mandate, supports the humanitarian leadership in effectively coordinating the response inside Syria. To do so, OCHA maintains country offices in Syria and Turkey, and a regional office in Amman.  OCHA Turkey coordinates cross-border humanitarian assistance delivered from Turkey to Syria as mandated by the UN Security Council resolutions 2449 under the leadership of the Deputy Regional Humanitarian Coordinator (DRHC).
OCHA requires sustained levels of funding to be able to maintain and strengthen effective humanitarian response coordination from these various offices, facilitate strategic and operational coordination platforms, provide information management services, manage pooled funds, support humanitarian access analysis and negotiation, ensure civil-military coordination, and provide public information and advocacy on the
humanitarian situation. Funding requirements for this project reflect the needs of OCHA's three offices directly involved in the Syria response.

project_objective:

Our areas of intervention will primarily be Fangak, and Pibor Counties of Jonglei State, Tonj East and Gogrial West counties of Warrap state. All our health facilities will have minimum package of WASH services. We will consider protection aspect and our medical team will be train on SGMV counselling and management We will take into consideration the protection area by providing the first aid care to the SGBV victims and MHPSS as well as identifying and strengthening the referral pathway for clinical management of rape and mental health cases. project_name: Unconditional life-saving food assistance to vulnerable Libyan through in-kind & e-voucher transfers in Libya
project_objective:
WFP finds that approximately 10 per cent of surveyed households had inadequate food consumption, meaning they have an unstable diet that regularly lacks key food groups. Households in the east and south of the country faced significantly higher rates, standing at 32 per cent in Tobruk, 23 per cent in Murzuk, and 15 per cent in Alkufra. Over 70 per cent of women aged 15 to 49 years old consumed minimum dietary diversity, while most children aged 6 to 23 months did not consume a minimum acceptable diet. 

WFP will provide unconditional life-saving food assistance to crisis-affected vulnerable Libyan IDPs, returnees and non-displaced populations in the East, West, and South of Libya based on the assessed vulnerability. The best transfer modality, either in-kind or electric-voucher, will be selected to deliver the food entitlements to the targeted households through WFP's local partners and/or the contracted service providers. 

Targeting is implemented geographically, mainly based on the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment findings and household demographic characteristics such as gender, age group, and the presence of women, men, boys and girls living with disabilities as well as Household Food Consumption Scores. Further prioritization exercises are also applied to the project based on the duration of displacements, the assistance provided by local authorities or other food security sector members, and accessibility. Beneficiaries themselves, as members of local crisis committees, are involved throughout the project planning and the food distribution process. 

WFP will put its programmatic quality control and assurance measures in place, which include the following: I) training of its Cooperating Partners and its own staff in cross-cutting issues such as gender, GBV, PSEA, Protection and Conflict Sensitivity; ii) WFP’s output monitoring through the verification of distribution reports and spot-checks and WFP’s outcome monitoring through annual post-distribution monitoring; iii) WFP’s distributions of leaflets and visibility materials to raise the awareness of participants and non-participants about the Common Feedback Mechanism.

project_name: Provision of school meals to children in formal and non-formal education in Syria
project_objective:
The school meals programme aims to restore and stabilize access to education and to enhance health and nutrition status of children in targeted areas particularly areas hosting large number of affected populations, IDPs and returnees with low food security and education indicators. By encouraging regular attendance and enrollment, the programme contributes to providing protection to children from reverting to negative coping mechanism such as child labor and child marriage in addition to the education, health, and nutrition benefits. The programme meets the first objective of the education sector “Increased safe and equitable availability and access to in-person and home-based formal and non-formal education for crisis-affected children and youth”
The School meals activity includes: 
-	In kind food distribution including daily distribution of fresh meals or  fortified snacks  to  children in formal education pre and  primary schools during school days and to children enrolled in non-formal education, including children in Self learning centers in North East Syria camps.  The fresh meals project will expand to new areas fund permitting
-	Provision of electronic vouchers to students who were out of school and have returned to education and are currently enrolled in curriculum B or non-formal education   programmes. The provision of the electronic voucher is conditional to student’s attendance rate of 80%.  

School meals activities will target boys and girls aged 5-18 years in formal and non-formal settings, including children with disability, who are attending the targeted schools and learning centers.  The Programme is implemented in coordination with the Ministry of Education and other partners of the education sector in Syria including UN agencies and National NGOs. Considering the high needs and limited resources, the project will focus on areas with acute and immediate needs of humanitarian assistance. Targeted sub-districts will be prioritized based on food and education severity of 3 and above.  In case of lower funding, priority will be given to locations where severity of food security and education of more than 4 and to newly accessible areas where education sector is picking up its activities. 

The Activities are aligned with the timeframe of the school year  and  are expended over two calendar years. 
1.	100% of targeted sub-districts that are severity 3,4 and 5. 
2.	Estimated % of targeted beneficiaries that may have disabilities : 3%

WFP will target 450,000 for the date bars distribution and 160,000 for the electronic voucher and 70,000 for the fresh meals in 2022

project_name: Provision of emergency lifesaving and nutrition services to improve and prevent the deterioration of the nutrition status of nutritionally vulnerable Syrian women, girls and boys
project_objective:
The Nutrition project aims to address urgent and life-saving nutrition needs of mothers and children in Syria, located in high severity areas across the entire country, as depicted by the 2022 HNO.  In line with the nutrition sector priorities, the project aims to provide preventative and curative nutrition services to the most vulnerable groups (namely; children U5 and PLWs) amongst all affected populations, including IDPs, host communities and returnees identified with high severity food insecurity and nutrition indicators. The project will, therefore, focus on:
- Supporting an improved and equitable access to life saving nutritional services for food insecure and vulnerable children (boys and girls) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) at community and facilities level to stabilize and/or reduce malnutrition (acute, chronic and micronutrient deficiencies) in the target population.
−	Preventing acute, chronic malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in children 6-23 months
−	Improving diet diversity amongst pregnant and lactating women within food insecure and vulnerable families.

Trough the aforementioned activities, WFP is able to play a key role in strengthening the nutrition resilience of the population in general, and its nutritionally targeted groups in particular, by shielding them from economic volatility and vulnerability, supporting to avoid further asset depletion, while improving their access to high quality nutrition services.
WFP aims to target boys and girls aged 6- 23months and PLWs, including those with disability, through its preventive programme. The Programme is implemented in coordination with the Ministry of Health and other partners of the nutrition sector in Syria including UN agencies, National and International NGOs. Considering the high needs and limited resources, the project will adopt a context and severity-based approach to prioritize sub-districts identified with high nutritional and food insecurity severity, mainly those with severity level 3,4 &5. In case of lower funding, priority will be given to locations were severity of food security and nutrition of is more than 4 and to newly accessible areas.

project_name: Logistics Augmentation and Coordination to Support Humanitarian Operations in Syria
project_objective: WFP, as the lead agency for Logistics Sector, aims to oversee all the strategic objectives from the sector, namely: 1. provide logistics services (transhipment and warehousing) to humanitarian organisations responding to the Syria crisis; 2. maintain regional WoS inter-agency logistics coordination and information management in order to support the overall humanitarian response; 3. Continue the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) to provide safe, reliable and sustainable air access to beneficiaries for the humanitarian community, medical and security evacuations and facilitating the movement of light cargo where required.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Telecommunications Cluster (ETC) Services and Support to Humanitarian Operations in Syria
project_objective:
The overarching goal of the Emergency Telecommunications (ETC) is to ensure that humanitarian actors have access to vital telecommunications services that allow them to perform their work in common UN operational areas. Effective communications systems are critical to support and enhance the safety of the humanitarian community.

Telecommunications infrastructure throughout Syria has suffered significant and ongoing damage due to a decade of devastating conflict. While Damascus maintains good coverage, other locations including Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor, Homs, Hana, Qamishli and Tartous require continued upgrades and maintenance to improve their coverage. In 2022, the ETC will maintain and enhance the operational coverage of Communication System by enhancing the existing VHF network and Deploying Push To Talk (PTT) technology in common operational areas.

There is a need for the continued provision of shared connectivity and telecommunications services to facilitate cross border movement and operations in neighboring countries where Syrians have been forced to flee. The ETC will continue to provide dedicated ICT helpdesk support personnel in the inter-agency response area in Gaziantep, Turkey, and provide technical guidance and support to the response community in Turkey, Jordan and Lebanon as required. 

Reliable connectivity also remains a major challenge throughout the country. In 2022-23, the ETC will continue to provide data connectivity services in Aleppo, Deir-Ez-Zor, Hama, Homs and Qamishli and improve ETC data connectivity services in all interagency hubs where these services are provided. The fuel crisis and a lack of mains electricity remain an urgent issue in the whole country and regular power outages impact on the entire humanitarian communications network in Syria. The ETC continue to deploy solar power systems to support and improve ETC data connectivity services in common hubs.

In 2022-23, the ETC will develop the technical capacity of national humanitarian ICT staff through the delivery of two training courses on IT Emergency Management and technical security communications. The ETC will continue to assess the needs on the ground to support and enable humanitarian activities where and when required. Contingency resources may also be required to support new common operational areas or the extension of common services, based on assessments conducted periodically throughout the year

project_name: Recuperación de los medios de vida agrícolas, la capacidad productiva  y fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de familias vulnerables afectadas por las  Tormentas Tropicales ETA, IOTA e inseguridad alimentaria en 16 municipios de los departamentos de El Progreso, Zacapa, Chiquimula y Jutiapa
project_objective:
Se trabajará en forma conjunta con los otros clústeres,  de esta manera se adopta un enfoque de triple nexo humanitario, complementando acciones de otros sectores. 

Se trabajará  con el 13% de las familias  la metodología de “Estipendio por Acciones”, la cual consiste en  otorgar un estipendio de Q 1,00.00 (US$ 129.00) a cada familia como incentivo por el aporte  mano de obra en el restablecimiento de su unidad productiva.  

El estipendio permite a las familias priorizar sus necesidades y decidir cómo y cuándo gastar el dinero en efectivo.  Proporciona un mejor vínculo entre la respuesta humanitaria y el desarrollo a largo plazo, así como al sistema nacional de protección existente, aumenta el gasto de los hogares en alimentos y  la inversión en insumos y activos;  además  promueve la adopción de mejores prácticas agropecuarias.
Los equipos técnicos del   MAGA y del   proyecto  capacitarán y asistirán técnicamente a las familias.  

Se implementarán prácticas adaptadas al clima para restaurar la capacidad productiva de las familias en su finca (milpa) y en el hogar (traspatio), lo cual les permitirá en corto tiempo disponer de alimentos de origen animal y vegetal para el consumo familiar y venta de pequeños excedentes,  modelos para la cosecha de agua de lluvia y  acciones para la restauración del suelo.

Se rehabilitará la infraestructura productiva protegida (macro túneles, invernaderos, casas malla),  sistemas de riego por goteo y estanques piscícolas, con el objetivo de reactivar y recuperar la producción de hortalizas para el autoconsumo y venta de excedentes.  Se realizarán acciones  para la gestión del conocimiento de las promotorías comunitarias y  equipos de las organizaciones e instituciones socias. 

Se llevará a cabo la incorporación en igualdad de condiciones de las mujeres, en los procesos de recuperación de medios de vida, por medio de capacitaciones para mejorar sus oportunidades de crecimiento y mejora,  fortalecimiento de la autonomía social y económica mediante la implementación de proyectos productivos agrícolas y no agrícolas liderados por mujeres. 

La implementación de las acciones tiene una secuencia o combinación para atender a la misma familia, por ejemplo, una combinación puede ser: recuperación de suelo, sistema de micro riego, cosechador de agua de lluvia; huertos y  gallinas ponedoras. Las combinaciones dependerán de las condiciones de las familias y de la disponibilidad de área en sus parcelas y traspatios.

project_name: Asistencia de emergencia para la recuperación de los medios de vida agrícolas de pequeños productores afectados por las tormentas tropicales ETA e IOTA en 35 municipios en situación de inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional
project_objective:
Según FAO (2021) en su estudio de daños y necesidades en el sector agropecuario el 99% de los productores entrevistados, reportó haber tenido pérdidas en sus cultivos por el impacto de ETA/IOTA, es importante destacar que el 40% destinaba los alimentos de su producción para autoconsumo y 56.73% autoconsumo y venta. En el informe también se detalla que las perdidas en la producción se concentran en porcentaje superiores al 75%, esta situación limitara la capacidad de reservas alimentarias; se espera que los hogares recurran a continuar utilizando estrategias de afrontamiento para el consumo de alimentos. Asimismo, el 87% de los productores entrevistados a junio de 2021, no habían recibido asistencia para reactivar su producción agrícola e indicaron no sentirse preparados debido a los altos precios de los fertilizantes, perdidas de tierra y baja capacidad económica. Los efectos de los huracanes Eta y Iota, y el COVID-19 han provocado un fuerte impacto que ha llevado al incrementado el uso de estrategias de afrontamiento de medios de vida en los hogares. Según la clasificación de inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional (CIF) para los meses de julio y septiembre de 2021, se espera que la situación continúe en donde 3.3millones (35% población) se encuentran en fase 3 y fase 4 requiriendo acciones urgentes.

En este sentido la FAO con el presente proyecto implementara acciones de reactivación y fortalecimiento de los medios de vida a los productores(as) que dependen del sector agropecuaria especialmente de autoconsumo en las zonas con mayor afectación climática y caracterizados en situación de inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional, a través de tres entregables:

Entregable 1. Fortalecimiento de los medios de vida de los hogares más vulnerables; mediante el suministro de insumos agrícolas, herramientas e infraestructura básica, transferencias en efectivo para alcanzar objetivos humanitarios de desarrollo y sostenibilidad en agricultura, seguridad alimentaria y nutricional.

Entregable 2. Asistencia técnica y formación en ejes temáticos; mitigación de riesgo, acceso a mercado, agricultura sostenible, manejo del suelo post desastre, agricultura sostenible, cambio climático y educación nutricional.

Entregable 3. Monitoreo de cultivos en tiempos claves con enfoque de seguridad alimentaria a fin de disponer de información oportuna para estimar la cantidad de población en riesgo que facilite el seguimiento y la adopción de acciones tempranas

Este Proyecto se alinea con la Prioridad Nacional 3 (PN3) del Marco Programa País (MPP) 2019 -2022, “Uso Sostenible de los Recursos Naturales, Adaptación y Mitigación al Cambio Climático y Gestión de Riesgos (ODS12, 13,14 y 15)”, que está alineado con la Iniciativa Regional IR3 “Agricultura sostenible y resiliente”de la FAO para America Latina y el Caribe. Con impacto en los resultados 3.4: Fortalecidas las capacidades de gestión de riesgos de desastres y resiliencia de los medios de vida para prevenir, mitigar y responder a amenazas y crisis que afectan los sectores agrícolas y la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional.
La contribución de la FAO con las directrices, políticas del Gobierno está alineado a El Plan Estratégico de Gobierno (PEG 2018 – 2022) que es una herramienta de planificación de mediano plazo, para avanzar en el cumplimiento de los objetivos y metas nacionales de la Visión de País (2010-2038) y los lineamientos e indicadores del Plan de Nación (2010-2022). El PEG esta alineado con la Agenda Nacional de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (AN-ODS).

project_name: Rehabilitación inmediata de medios de vida y mejora de laresiliencia de las familias vulnerables afectadas en el corredorseco de El Salvador por las emergencias climáticas y COVID19.
project_objective:
De acuerdo, a la Encuesta Nacional de Indicadores de Seguridad Alimentaria y Agricultura,El Salvador 2020 (FAO-DIGESTYC) se estima que de la población vulnerable vinculado ala agricultura es de un 36% representados (225,891, productores(as). En el corto ymediano plazo 39,113 productores(as) de granos básicos necesitan atención deemergencia en los departamentos de Ahuachapán, San Miguel y La Unión (CIF, 2020).
