project_name: Mejorando la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de familias vulnerables de municipios de Huehuetenango y Chiquimula (5 meses)
project_objective: Debido a las restricciones en la movilidad para frenar el contagio del COVID-19 tanto en2020 como en 2021, cuyos efectos se reflejaron en la pérdida de empleos tanto para familias del área urbana como rural, el presente proyecto busca cubrir las principales necesidades alimentarias de las familias más vulnerables, que además pudieron ser afectadas por la emergencia de ETA/IOTA en noviembre de 2020 y que debido a la debilidad institucional del país, aún no han sido atendidas y que por lo tanto, continúan deteriorando sus medios de vida. De esa cuenta, el proyecto brindará transferencias monetarias condicionadas y no condicionadas durante 6 meses (septiembre – octubre2021 / febrero – mayo 2022), de forma diferenciada de acuerdo con el número de miembros del hogar, principalmente para la cobertura de alimentos y otras necesidade sbásicas. A su vez, dentro del grupo de familias atendidas, se identificarán aquellas que necesitan un apoyo extra para restablecer sus medios de vida agrícolas y no agrícolas, por medio de la entrega de paquetes de insumos agrícolas o bien, mediante el apoyo con capacitaciones técnicas (albañilería, carpintería, fontanería, etc.) que les proporcionen mejores oportunidades de acceso a empleo. Estas actividades se realizarán en los municipios de Cuilco, San Ildefonso Ixtahuacán y Tectitán del departamento de Huehuetenango, así como en Jocotán, Camotán y Chiquimula, del departamento de Chiquimula, lugares en donde Acción contra el Hambre ha trabajado con diferentes financiamientos, lo que ha permitido contar con conocimiento del contexto, así como con las alianzas a nivel municipal y departamental con diferentes instancias de Gobierno y organizaciones no gubernamentales.

project_name: Garantizar supervivencia mediantetratamiento para niñas/os co desnutrición aguda y cuidado nutricional integral materno infantil en Chiquimula, Zacapa e Izabal.
project_objective:
Los municipios priorizados presentan incremento de la desnutrición aguda que pone en riesgo la vida. Se implementarán acciones integrales de atención nutricional en emergencias con las cuales el clúster de nutrición ha tenido experiencia desde 2018 para salvar la vida de niños/as que no habían sido detectados anteriormente por salud (hasta un 68%). Es un abordaje estandarizado y monitoreado desde el clúster de nutrición que incluye a la población vulnerable a problemas nutricionales en emergencias (niños/as menores de 5 años, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia, adolescentes y mujeres en edad fértil). A través de brigadas de nutrición que atenderán las comunidades más rurales y lejanas, se hará la búsqueda de niños/as afectados por desnutrición aguda, para brindar tratamiento inmediato para asegurar la supervivencia y se brindará suplementación con micronutrientes, desparasitación y consejería. Se brindará atención nutricional integral a la madre y sus hijos/as durante el periodo prenatal, parto y posparto y también se fortalecerá a los líderes y lideresas comunitarios para la sostenibilidad de la respuesta nutricional en emergencia e instalar un sistema de información de alerta temprana nutricional. La consejería para mejor aprovechamiento de las transferencias monetarias también está considerada. La mujer está al centro de las acciones considerando herramientas para su empoderamiento en la respuesta humanitaria. El proyecto responde a los siguientes objetivos:
• Identificar la población afectada por desnutrición aguda y brindar tratamiento inmediato para salvar sus vidas.
• Mejorar las competencias del personal de salud y otros actores locales para la atenciónnutricional en emergencias
• Brindar insumos necesarios para el cuidado nutricional
• Fortalecer capacidades de líderes y lideresas comunitarias en la preparación y respuestapara la atención nutricional en emergencias
• Activar sistemas de alerta temprana nutricional en la comunidad
• Orientar a las familias sobre el uso adecuado de los programas de protección social y asistencia alimentaria

project_name: Mejorando la Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional de las familias afectadas por la crisis humanitaria.
project_objective:
Acción contra el Hambre (ACH) cuenta con experiencia en la implementación de proyectos en diversas áreas rurales en el ámbito de acceso al agua potable, el saneamiento y la higiene; salud, nutrición, seguridad alimentaria, gestión de riesgos y atención y respuesta a la emergencia. Centra su trabajo en mejorar las condiciones de vida de familias vulnerables afectadas por la situación de crisis humanitaria como consecuencia de los diferentes fenómenos climáticos (sequía, los desastres naturales, el cambio climático) y la situación de violencia generalizada, entre múltiples amenazas y, en consecuencia, el hambre
El proyecto tendrá una duración de 18 meses, diseñado para ser implementado en 2 etapas: La primera etapa en 2021 y una segunda etapa en 2022. Se realizarán transferencias monetarias condicionadas y no condicionadas, cada grupo familiar recibirá al menos 2 transferencias monetarias, de forma diferenciada de acuerdo con el número de miembros del hogar, principalmente para la cobertura de alimentos y medios de vida. La cantidad inversión por familia será de $50 y la máxima de $250.00. Se priorizarán los grupos de familias con mayor vulnerabilidad. Se identificará a las familias vulnerables que tienen habilidades y condiciones para restablecer sus medios, se consideraran los rubros agrícolas y no agrícolas, la entrega se condicionara a paquetes de insumos agrícolas o bien, mediante el apoyo con capacitaciones técnicas que les permita generar ingresos de manera independiente (albañilería, carpintería, fontanería, electricidad, etc.) y que a su vez les proporcionen mejores oportunidades de acceso a empleo.
Estas actividades se realizarán en el departamento de Cortes, específicamente en los municipios de Choloma, San Pedro Sula, La Lima, Villanueva y San Manuel Cortes y en el departamento de Yoro, específicamente en el municipio de El Progreso, lugares en donde Acción contra el Hambre tiene experiencia con diferentes financiamientos, lo que ha permitido contar con conocimiento del contexto, así como con las alianzas a nivel municipal y departamental con diferentes instancias de Gobierno, organizaciones no gubernamentales, actores de la sociedad civil y actores comunitarios como principales aliados.

project_name: Respuesta para restablecer los servicios de agua, saneamiento e higiene de las poblaciones vulnerables en la zona norte de Honduras
project_objective:
Acción contra el Hambre (ACH) cuenta con experiencia en la implementación de proyectos en diversas áreas rurales en el ámbito de acceso al agua potable, el saneamiento y la higiene; salud, nutrición, seguridad alimentaria, gestión de riesgos y atención y respuesta a la emergencia. Centra su trabajo en mejorar las condiciones de vida de familias vulnerables afectadas por la situación de crisis humanitaria como consecuencia de los diferentes fenómenos climáticos (sequía, desastres naturales, el cambio climático) y la situación de violencia generalizada , entre múltiples amenazas y, en consecuencia, el hambre.
La propuesta “Respuesta para restablecer los servicios de agua, saneamiento e higiene de las poblaciones vulnerables en la zona norte de Honduras” tiene como objetivo restablecer los servicios tanto domésticos como comunitarios esenciales para las personas más vulnerables de la zona norte de Honduras, zona afectada por desastres naturales como los ocurridos en noviembre de 2020 con las inundaciones producidas por ETA&IOTA, así como los efectos del cambio climático , que obligan a la población a desplazarse. Además de intervenciones comunitarias en restablecimiento de sistemas de agua, promoción y acceso digno a instalaciones de saneamiento diferenciadas, inclusivas y seguras, gestión de drenajes y excretas, y sensibilizaciones, se prevé, alineados con el Objetivo Sectorial 2, fomentar la sostenibilidad de los servicios WASH en centros educativos y establecimientos de salud. Estas dos tipologías de establecimientos se han visto muy afectadas, en primer lugar, por la crisis sanitaria de la COVID-19 y, por otro lado, por la transformación de los centros escolares en albergues durante los eventos naturales extremos.
Se enmarca en la zona priorizada por el clúster WASH, poniendo su foco en cinco municipios de los departamentos de Cortés, Atlántida y Yoro. Se realizará un diagnóstico detallado en los mismos para poder proporcionar una mejor respuesta adaptada a las necesidades específicas de cada grupo con enfoque de edad, género, diversidad y protección.
Cabe destacar que la perspectiva climática del último trimestre del año 2021 predice posibilidades de algún fenómeno natural peligroso. Por lo que, desde ACH, se va a trabajar paralelamente el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de las estructuras sociales comunitarias (Juntas de Agua, CODEL, CODEM).

project_name: Familias vulnerables de la zona sur de Honduras, fortaleciendo sus medios de vida y su resiliencia después de la afectación de Eta e Iota
project_objective:
Un estudio realizado recientemente por CARE a través del Proyecto ACS PROSASUR en 112 comunidades de 13 municipios del corredor seco, refleja que las intensas lluvias derivadas de las Tormentas ETA e IOTA en la zona afectaron los cultivos de subsistencia principalmente en granos básicos, representando pérdidas estimadas en aproximadamente 36,638 quintales de frijol y 49,632 quintales de maíz. el estudio refleja que el impacto negativo mayor es en los sistemas agro-alimentarios, por la escasez de alimentos a futuro inmediato. Los datos reflejan que el 69% de los caseríos tuvieron una afectación moderada y un 16% de grave; el 88% de las familias consideran que han sido afectadas por las tormentas tropicales, siendo la perdida de alimentos lo más representativo.
Con el proyecto se espera atender una población total de 21,819 personas (4,350 familias) en 10 municipios del corredor seco (7 en Choluteca y 3 en el Paraíso) mediante acciones orientadas a reactivar los medios de vida facilitando el acceso a medios e incentivos de la producción (riegos e insumos) y la seguridad alimentaria de las familias más vulnerables ante los fenómenos hidrometeorológicos; fortaleciendo el liderazgo y empoderamiento individual y colectivo con énfasis de mujeres con un enfoque de género para la resiliencia de los medios de vida y reducir riesgos del impacto de la Violencia, el desplazamiento, efectos de desastres y COVID-19. La asistencia técnica a agricultores a través de promotoría comunitaria (modelo desarrollado y validado con el proyecto ACS PROSASUR).

project_name: Respuesta humanitaria a los impactos de desastres acumulativos en nutrición de la población más vulnerables en Ahuachapán y Sonsonate.
project_objective:
En El Salvador los municipios que están en la franja del corredor seco, son considerados como el territorio en donde concurren niveles de pobreza, vulnerabilidad y condiciones climáticas más severas en términos de ausencia e irregularidad de las lluvias. Según la información proporcionada por el Consejo Nacional de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional (CONASAN), de noviembre 2020 a febrero de 2021, 684,000 personas (10% de la población analizada) se encuentran en Crisis alimentaria o peor (Fase 3 o peor de la CIF) y por tanto requieren acciones urgentes. De estas personas, 589,000 se encuentran en Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) y 95,000 en Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF). El departamento más afectado es Ahuachapán clasificado en Fase 3, el resto de departamentos del país han sido clasificado en Estrés (Fase 2 de la CIF). La población más afectada es aquella que depende de actividades agrícolas y ganaderas debido a pérdidas de ingresos por las restricciones de movilidad y transporte derivadas de la pandemia de COVID-19, así mismo, el sector informal y en especial los pequeños comerciantes que se ven obligados a utilizar estrategias de afrontamiento de crisis o emergencia para solventar sus brechas alimentarias, como la venta de sus activos productivos. 
El objetivo principal del diseño de la intervención es contribuir a mitigar el impacto causado por la prolongada crisis alimentaria y nutricional de los hogares rurales del corredor seco. La respuesta se centrará en brindar respuesta humanitaria mediante la identificación de población en situación de vulnerabilidad sobre todo a niñez y mujeres embarazadas o en periodo de lactancia, que puedan ser atendidas según su necesidad nutricional, con base a mediciones antropométricas para brindar alimento suplementario, y vitamínico según lo requieran. Así como el fortalecimiento de capacidades y equipamiento a personal de salud de los municipios seleccionado.

project_name: Fortaleciendo comunidades educativas y protectoras para la niñez, adolescencia y juventud víctima de violencia y desplazamiento en Honduras
project_objective:
NRC considera que la educación es una herramienta estratégica para la protección de la niñez, adolescencia, juventudes, familias y comunidades. El programa de Educación, que NRC está desarrollando en Honduras desde el 2015, tiene como objetivo fundamental promover el acceso y la permanencia en espacios seguros de aprendizaje para la población afectada o en riesgo por lo que se ha denominado Otras Situaciones de Violencia.

El NRC tiene una estrategia de intervención para asegurar la efectividad de la escolarización de los NNAJ, se plantea iniciar con la identificación de la población que no se encuentran registrados o asistiendo en la escuela; posterior se incorporan al Programa Puente, el cual tiene como propósito motivar a los NNAJ a que se incorporen en el sistema educativo, finalmente dicha población matriculada se atiende en el programa permanencia en el cual se realiza acompañamiento pedagógico tanto a NNAJ y docentes para que la población estudiantil permanezca en la escuela hasta lograr la aprobación del año escolar. Durante el desarrollo del programa Puente y Permanencia se prevée la entrega de kit de protección y kit educativo.

Se contempla la implementación de un enfoque de trabajo integral que fortalezca las capacidades de diversos actores; se capacitará a docentes y funcionarios de la SEDUC a nivel central y departamental en temas vinculados a PEAS y EeE; a padres, madres, cuidadores o encargados de familia en temas vinculados a la protección, PEAS y derechos de la niñez, así como de la importancia de la construcción de espacios protectores que contribuya al desarrollo integral de la población estudiantil. De igual manera se sensibilizará sobre la importancia de enfrentar problemas de abandono escolar para realizar acciones en conjunto para incidir en la reducción de los índices de deserción escolar.

project_name: Renforcement des mécanismes de Coordination et de Plaidoyer pour la protection humanitaire et l’assistance aux populations les plus vulnérables au Mali
project_objective:
En 2021, la crise humanitaire au Mali s'est aggravée en raison de l'augmentation et de l'expansion des de la violence intercommunautaire et des attaques des groupes armés non étatiques (GANE) dans les régions du centre, du sud et de l'ouest. Cette crise a été aggravée par les bouleversements politiques marqués par deux coups d'état en août 2020 et mai 2021, et l'incertitude persistante de la transition politique laisse l'État dans l'incapacité de répondre aux services sociaux de base des populations. 
Les déplacements internes de personnes ont augmenté de 100 000 en 2021, atteignant plus de 401 000 personnes soit quatre fois plus qu'il y a deux ans. Au total, 156 000 réfugiés maliens résident dans les pays voisins tandis que le Mali accueille 48 000 réfugiés et leur fournit protection et assistance. Les gains économiques du Mali se sont érodés, avec 900 000 personnes (0,04% de la population) qui sont retombées dans la pauvreté en raison de la crise socioéconomique de la COVID-19. la capacité des ménages est fragilisée à cause de la perte de revenus, de la réduction des transferts de fonds et à l'augmentation du coût de la vie. 
La Banque mondiale prévoit une augmentation du taux de pauvreté à 4,8 % en 2022. La crise de protection est également aggravée avec une augmentation des incidents de sécurité.  Les acteurs de la violence basée sur le genre (VBG) ont signalé 5 486 incidents de VBG, soit une augmentation de 41 % comparativement à la même période en 2020. Plus de 1 640 écoles sont fermées en raison de l'insécurité, affectant plus de 2,9 millions d'enfants dont 40 % se trouvent dans la région centrale de Mopti. Quatre districts centraux ont signalé que 40 % des écoles étaient fermées. Dans les régions du sud, 10 pour cent des écoles sont fermées à Koulikoro, Koutiala et Sikasso, privant 30 000 enfants de leur éducation. A ce jour, le Mali a rapporté plus de 15 800 cas de COVID-19.
En 2021, 1,3 million de personnes ont connu un niveau élevé d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. le niveau le plus élevé depuis 2015, et 3 055 253 personnes ont été touchées par les mauvaises pluies et une saison de soudure prolongée. La situation humanitaire reste entravée par l'augmentation des besoins et la faiblesse des financements, avec 32 % des fonds mobilisés au 31 octobre 2021. Malgré les contraintes opérationnelles, les partenaires humanitaires ont aidé plus de 2,45 millions des 4,7 millions de personnes ciblées au 30 septembre 2021. 
Les capacités de réponse existantes au Mali représentent plus de 160 organisations humanitaires, acteurs du développement ainsi que des forces militaires (MINUSMA, Forces maliennes de défense et de sécurité, Barkhane, Mission européenne de formation, G5 Sahel). Le contexte susmentionné exigera une coordination efficace et la présence d’OCHA demeure très importante. OCHA maintiendra sa présence à Bamako, Mopti, Tombouctou, Gao et ouvrira une antenne à Ségou tout en couvrant à distance les régions de Taoudénit, Ménaka, Kidal et les régions du sud Est et Ouest. 

Sept clusters actifs (Éducation, Sécurité alimentaire, Santé, Nutrition, Protection, Abris/BNA et WASH), des sous-clusters et des groupes de travail spécialisés (Accès, CM-Coord, Redevabilité, Genre et Cash) sont en place au niveau national et local. Le Bureau d’OCHA au Mali continuera ainsi à jouer un rôle central dans la mobilisation, la coordination et le soutien des acteurs humanitaires dans les domaines de la coordination, la gestion de l’information, le financement humanitaire et le plaidoyer. 

OCHA continuera à jouer son rôle central dans la mobilisation des partenaires, l’utilisation des instruments et des mécanismes de financement tout en veillant à ce que les besoins humanitaires croissants soient prises en compte. OCHA assumera son rôle clé dans la coordination militaire au niveau national et régional de concert avec les forces militaires présentes dans le pays tout en renforçant les capacités des autorités nationales en matière de coordination

project_name: Respuesta humanitaria a los impactos de desastres acumulativos en seguridad alimentaria de población más vulnerables en San Miguel y La Unión
project_objective:
En El Salvador los municipios que son identificados como parte del corredor seco, son considerados como el territorio en donde concurren niveles de pobreza, vulnerabilidad y condiciones climáticas más severas en términos de ausencia e irregularidad de las lluvias. Según la información proporcionada por el Consejo Nacional de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional (CONASAN), de noviembre 2020 a febrero de 2022, Más de 900,000 personas estarán en crisis o emergencia de inseguridad alimentaria aguda en el período previo al de  hambre estacional de marzo-mayo 2022.
Para el período antes mencionado se prevee que la población en condición de Crisis o peor (Fase 3 de la CIF o peor) se incrementará a 985,000 . En ambos períodos, los departamentos de Ahuachapán, La Unión y San Miguel están clasificados en Fase 2 y 3 de la CIF mientras el resto de departamentos se clasifican en condición de Estrés.  El presente análisis toma en cuenta la persistencia de la pandemia de COVID-19, y sus efectos socioeconómicos, que vienen acumulándose desde su aparición en el territorio salvadoreño en marzo del 2020, la variabilidad y alza de los precios en la CBA, combustibles y otros insumos básicos, el inicio de la temporada lluviosa (probabilidad del 65% de ocurrencia del fenómeno de La Niña), período previo al de hambre estacional y desafíos estructurales como la pobreza multidimensional que colocan en una situación de mayor vulnerabilidad a importantes sectores de la población. 
Para el año 2022 se proyecta que  alrededor de 47,000 personas (1%) de municipios a nivel nacional, estarán en Fase de situación de emergencia de inseguridad alimentaria aguda (Fase 4) y 547,000 personas (9%) están en crisis de inseguridad alimentaria aguda (Fases 3), las cuales requieren apoyo urgente con intervenciones de respuesta enfocadas en salvar vidas y medios de vida con un plan de respuesta que incluya ayuda alimentaria, asistencia monetaria, distribución de paquetes a los agricultores, y redistribución de activos, de acuerdo con los factores clave y limitantes identificados.
Se identifica que los departamentos que tendrán la mayor severidad de inseguridad alimentaria aguda en condiciones de crisis o emergencia (Fases 3 o 4) serán:  La Unión (16%), y San Miguel (15%). En términos de la magnitud de crisis o emergencia  de inseguridad alimentaria aguda (Fases 3 o 4), llos departamentos con
mayor población en Fases 3 o 4 serán San Salvador con cerca de 87,000,  San Miguel con casi 70,000.

El objetivo principal del diseño de la intervención es contribuir a mitigar el impacto social y económico causado por la prolongada crisis alimentaria y nutricional de los hogares rurales del corredor seco. La respuesta se centrará en brindar respuesta humanitaria mediante transferencias en efectivo no condicionada tomando en cuenta estándares internacionales para su implementación, así como la identificación de población en situación de vulnerabilidad que puedan ser atendidas con base a la estrategia de respuesta por sequias en el corredor seco centroamericano.

project_name: Protecting lives and restoring livelihoods of vulnerable agro-pastoral and riverine- men, women, boys and girls in Baardhere District, Gedo, Somalia.
project_objective: This proposed intervention in Bardheere district (Gedo Region, Somalia) targets 8,130 vulnerable men, women, boys and girls in 1,355 Non-IDPs (agro-pastoralists & riverine farmers in the rural areas) and IDP households for 12 months (January 2022- December 2022). The project will prioritize the most vulnerable HHs/population including: women (women headed households, single women, pregnant and lactating women-PLW, children, persons with disabilities, persons with minority clan affiliations, older persons, persons with chronic illness, large families and/ or those with babies or with children attending school. The project will select the target vulnerable beneficiaries from 38,960 individuals (in approx. 6,493 HHs) currently under IPC 3&4 in Bardhere district (as per the FSC 2021 Overall targets of People in Need-IPC 3&4 in Bardhere). Project activities are aligned with the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP)/Food Security Cluster (FSC) Objectives prioritizing lifesaving and life-sustaining assistance, as detailed in the UN OCHA (HRP-Somalia. Humanitarian Programme Cycle 2021-Issued in February 2021). The FSC Objective 1 of improving immediate access to food will be achieved through: (i) 600 men, women, boys and girls from 100 vulnerable HHs benefiting from Unconditional cash transfer (UCT) for 3 months ($ 70 per month per HH) and (ii) 4,350 men, women, boys and girls from 725 vulnerable HHs benefiting from conditional transfers-Cash For Work-CFW (rehabilitation of community infrastructure- Irrigation canals)about 70 Kms for 30 days @ $8 per HH per day.  These will improve immediate access to food, prevent selling of assets, bridge the food gap for beneficiary farmers as well as increase skills and ultimately improve food production, soil and water conservation and HH income. The FSC objective 2 of protecting and restoring livelihoods related to food and income sources will be achieved through: (i) 520 vulnerable agro-pastoralists and riverine farmers HHs (3,120 men, women, boys, girls) supported with seasonally appropriate agricultural inputs (e.g quality fodder seeds, farm tools, training on fodder production, conservation and utilization, seed bulking, group dynamics, business skills, DRR; land preparation and irrigation support).  This will ultimately protect and restore livelihoods as well as enhance HH feed security, food security, nutrition, income generation and resilience. The main approaches that will be used will include: Needs/market assessments/baseline survey; community based targeting; adult learning techniques; use of lead farmers as ToTs; conflict sensitive programing; protection mainstreaming; Gender sensitive and human rights based approaches. The main common project activities will include: (i) Conducting internal planning meeting for project staff to acquaint on project objectives, targets and outcome.(ii) Introduction of the project to local authorities and launch .(iii)Conducting community mobilization, sensitization, selection of beneficiaries- in the targeted 5 sites (Mardha, Hureena, Sarinleey, Bender and Shimbiroole); verification and registration (iv)Conducting a baseline survey to determine the benchmark and (v) M&E of project activities. VSF-Suisse has vast experience in  UCT and CFW activities and for over 6 years (2015-2020-through USAID/OFDA(BHA funding): supported 1,700 male & female fodder farmers and 1,270 Irrigation farmers in Gedo Region (including Bardhere district) practicing fodder activities, EWS and DRR; distribution of agricultural inputs and promoted linkages. VSF-Suisse supported rehabilitation of 74 Kms of Irrigation canals through CFW approaches and water supply infrastructure (13 water pans & 12 shallow wells) in Gedo. VSF-Suisse will work closely with stakeholders including communities, local authority/leaders, relevant technical ministries, NGOs and adhere to the FSC cluster & CWG guidelines, LEGS, Sphere standards, while observing CDC, WHO and government COVID-19 health measures.

project_name: Emergency Health support for vulnerable Lebanese and Migrants
project_objective:
Medair’s health work has been operating since 2014, supporting both refugees and vulnerable Lebanese through health centres and community outreach. Whilst originally focussed within health centres within Social Development Centres as part of the Ministry of Social Affairs, since the beginning of 2021, Medair has expanded operations to the South / Nabatiye and working with an additional 15 health centres within the Ministry of Public Health network, particularly for routine vaccinations. Medair opened a COVID mass vaccination centre in Saida in June 2021. There is a growing focus on nutrition activities such as IYCF, which are detailed under the Nutrition sector of the ERP.
Health activities that are aligned under the health sector of the ERP include the provision of medication, PPE provision and IPC training for health centres, and integrated messaging through community health volunteers (CHVs). 54 CHVs focused on reaching Lebanese populations will be mobilised from pre-existing Medair networks, and while the remaining number 46+ (additional figures contingent on anticipated future funding) will be newly recruited (with additional CHVs as part of the LCRP). These Community Health Volunteers will reach all populations within their geographic areas of intervention (around the supported health centres).
Medair has seen a four-fold increase in the usage of medication in recent months as more Lebanese are dependent on medication in the public sector due to shortages within pharmacies. Medair therefore aims to provide more medication through supplying pharmacies in supported health centres – expanding the number of centres supported. Medication will be provided free of charge to all those accessing the centres. Medair acknowledges the challenges with procuring medicines in the current context given we do not hold an importation license, yet is actively participating in coordination conversations with other agencies to explore alternative options for procurement of imports as well as engaging with advocacy efforts at the humanitarian and governmental levels. Medair will also include a small cash-for-health component for vulnerable people needing to access medication from other locations, which has been piloted through a blockchain modality in the Bekaa over the past six months. Medair also has experience in cash-for-health programming within the Middle East region, in addition to cash programming within Lebanon. 
Medair’s existing COVID programming already supports health centres with the provision of PPE and IPC training for staff and will be expanding this to a further 10 health centres. For more information on the centres, please see the list sent to the Health Sector. 
Medair also has an active shelter team who cover water and sanitation components, in addition to expanding into alternative energy options. The health and shelter teams have recently been jointly assessing the health facilities to consider how to ensure the continuation of health services, including WASH and solar options – both fridges for cold chain, and for the whole centre to enable lights, equipment and the internet (to access PHENICS) to function. Medair is therefore well placed to provide integrated health, shelter and WASH solutions.
Medair is an active part of the health sector, and has close working relationships with both the Ministry of Public Health, the Ministry of Social Affairs and other key stakeholders listed in the ERP. Medair has programming operating across Lebanon, including in BML and the North/Akkar, although the majority of health programming under this ERP is anticipating to take place in Bekaa/Baalbek and the South/Nabatiye.

project_name: Provision of Humanitarian Air Service in Cameroon
project_objective:
his project aims to support the overall humanitarian response by enabling and enhancing access to beneficiaries and project implementation sites through a provision of air service.

Its main objectives are:
• To provide NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations and diplomatic missions in Cameroon with safe, effective and efficient air service;
• To transport light cargo, such as medical supplies, information and communication technology (ICT) equipment;
• To provide adequate capacity for medical and security evacuations of humanitarian staff.

UNHAS was established in Cameroon in November 2015 to provide air transport services to the entire humanitarian community and their implementing partners principally NGOs, UN agencies, red cross/crescent movement, donor organizations and diplomatic missions. Ever since, UNHAS has offered safe humanitarian flights on a regular weekly basis to Adamaoua (N’gaoundere), the North (Garoua) and the Far North (Maroua), as well as to Tchad (N’Djamena). As the conflict worsened in the Northwest and Southwest regions, and following a request from the Steering Committee, UNHAS extended its operations in September 2019 to serve the locations of Bamenda, Mamfe and Tiko.
As the continued insecurity, vast distances and poor road conditions remain the main constraints to the provision of assistance by aid organizations, but also the prevailing Covid-19 pandemic worldwide and in Cameroon in particular, the continuation of UNHAS in 2021 will be vital in enabling humanitarian organizations to access the populations in need and project implementation sites

project_name: Intervention en WASH, Nutrition et Assistance d´Urgence pour les communautés vulnerables de Kirundo, Ruyigi et Muyinga
project_objective:
Obj. : Améliorer l'accès à l'eau potable et à l'assainissement et fournir une aide d'urgence immédiate lors de crises humanitaires périodiques
R 1: L'accès à l'approvisionnement essentiel en eau et aux installations sanitaires sûres dans les communautés vulnérables s'est amélioré
R 2: Fournir une aide d'urgence locale et immédiate pour protéger en particulier les enfants, les femmes, les personnes âgées et les personnes handicapées lors de crises humanitaires
R 3: La population cible est en mesure de couvrir ses besoins alimentaires et non alimentaires de base à court terme

Les inventaires de source d'eau,en consultation avec les administrations respectives, détermineront où les points d'eau potable, les latrines publiques et les stations de lavage des mains doivent être construits, réhabilités et/ou étendus en collaboration avec le secteur privé local, et des formations pour leur exploitation et leur maintenance seront organisées avec les communautés. La mobilisation de l'engagement communautaire sera réalisée par la revitalisation des comités d'usagers de l'eau et de l'assainissement. Les personnes âgées et handicapées seront aidées à construire leurs latrines et des kits d'hygiène menstruelle et/ou générale seront distribués à la population concernée. Afin de prévenir la propagation des maladies et d'accroître la sensibilisation à l'hygiène, des campagnes de promotion de l'hygiène et de Covid-19 seront menées, y compris de matériel IEC et PPE pertinent, le cas échéant.   
Des cartes de vulnérabilité à l'échelle du district ou du comté, tenant compte des risques, en particulier pour les enfants (y compris les mineurs rapatriés non accompagnés), les femmes, les personnes âgées et les personnes handicapées, seront créés pour indiquer les zones et les groupes de personnes à risque et ce que la communauté peut faire pour minimiser les dangers. Sur cette base, des plans de préparation aux situations d'urgence seront élaborés et des mécanismes communautaires de détection précoce des sécheresses, des inondations, des famines, des pandémies, des maladies animales, des maladies végétales et des parasites seront mis en place. Selon GHI (2021), la situation nutritionnelle au Burundi est alarmante et la pression sur les ressources existantes (disponibilité de la nourriture, terres) causée par les rapatriés, les déplacés internes et la croissance générale de la population, combinée aux effets du changement climatique, contribue à une aggravation de la situation. 1060 enfants dans 2 provinces (Kirundo, Ruyigi) 4 communes (Busoni, Bugabira, Gisuru, Kinyinya) seront dépistés conjointement par la Fondation Stamm (FS) avec le Bureau provincial de la santé (BPS) et ses services de conseil. Les agents de santé communautaires par commune sont formés et leurs capacités renforcées par le nutritionniste du projet de FS. Les enfants identifiés (grâce au dépistage) comme souffrant de malnutrition aiguë seront référés aux centres de santé plus proches. La distribution de micronutriments en poudre (MNP) est prévue pour les enfants de 6 à 23 mois. Des activités de sauvetage sous forme de distribution d'aide en espèces ou de bons (CVA) et de distribution d'articles non alimentaires pour les retournées en étroite coordination et collaboration avec les structures et organisations locales seront mises en œuvre en cas d'événements graves ayant des effets directs sur la population dans le besoin.
Afin de soutenir la protection des moyens de subsistance essentiels et des biens des ménages et de renforcer ainsi les mécanismes d'adaptation de la population vulnérable ciblée par ce projet seront fournis. ""Argent contre travail"" et des groupes VSLA pour les besoins de base sont étendus pour les personnes vulnerables qui sont capable de travailler dans leur situation, en appliquant l´approche ne pas nuire.

project_name: Operation and Maintenance of Humanitarian Hubs and Enhancing Displacement and Mobility Needs Tracking, Inter-sectorial Needs Assessment and Monitoring for Displaced Populations in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
Since April 2018, IOM has operated and managed a total of 9 humanitarian hubs composed of a base camp in Maiduguri (Red Roof) and 8 field hubs located in Gwoza, Bama, Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, Banki (2 hubs) and Damasak. The humanitarian hubs provide humanitarian actors the ability to work with safe and secure accommodation, office space and meeting/training facilities, enabling them to stay and deliver interventions necessary to saving and improving the lives of hundreds of thousands of Nigerians affected by conflict. The field hubs also host the internet connectivity service of the Emergency Telecommunication Sector (ETS). These humanitarian hubs help sustain the access of humanitarian responders to the population affected by the conflict, enabling them to coordinate and provide better assistance to the affected population. Demand for these services has increased, and IOM has accommodated additional space at hub facilities. The humanitarian base camp in Maiduguri now has a total capacity of 153 beds while each additional  field hub has a 20-bed capacity. Banki Hub added an extension of 72 beds, when the international community needed them. All of the hubs have office  space and training/meeting facilities available to humanitarian actors. Under the proposed project, IOM will aim to support the operation and maintenance of eight humanitarian field hubs and the base camp in Maiduguri (Red Roof).

Through the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), IOM will respond to Inter-sectorial needs Assessment based on Joint Inter-sectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF)  requirements, including having 120 Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), data collection at a household level in 60 Local Government Areas (LGAs) for a total of 8,700 Households (HHs), monitoring of needs on a quarterly basis, Rapid needs Assessment (ad-hoc) upon request by Inter-sector Working Groups (ISWG) and Inter-sector Coordination Groups (ISCG) – for a crisis requiring significant needs assessment. This will be done through regular meetings with ISCG / Assessment Analysis Working Group (AAWG) partners and Individual follow-up to ensure adequate Joint Inter-sectoral Analysis Framework (JIAF) / Inter-sectorial needs assessment methodology and forms. The Geographic priorities are BAY States of Nigeria– Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states (60 LGAs).

project_name: Shelter and NFI response in North - East Nigeria.
project_objective:
Under this project, IOM will scale-up its provision of shelter assistance targeting internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. IOM will:
(A) Ensure access to different types of emergency shelter solutions for displaced populations through the distribution and prepositioning of emergency shelter kits, construction of emergency shelters, and rehabilitation of damaged public buildings. 
(B) Contribute to decongestion of camps/camp-like settings through construction of emergency shelters and rehabilitation of damaged public buildings.
(C)	Ensure that displaced populations have access to various transitional shelter solutions.
(D)	Ensure that the care, maintenance and upgrading of existing emergency shelters and transitional shelters are conducted for continued safety and comfort of the affected population.
(E)	Ensure that returnee households have access to materials and labour for repairing their damaged houses. 
(F)	Empower the local market/vendors through the use of cash and voucher modalities.
(G) Support protection-informed voluntary return, local integration or settlement of IDPs through durable and sustainable shelter solutions; and
(H) Promote local knowledge, locally adaptable technologies, and locally available materials to provide medium- to long-term shelter solutions.
IOM’s shelter/NFI activities will be implemented in three States of Northeast Nigeria; Borno, Adamawa and Yobe State, targeting 445,000 individuals. IOM will ensure that all shelter activities conducted are accountable to the affected population and that the specific needs of project beneficiaries are considered, including those related to gender. IOM will ensure that kits and other shelter solutions are harmonized at sector level and coordinated with partners, under the aegis of the sector.
The project will also include the continuation and scaling-up of NFI support for people in camp and camp-like settings and in host communities, including for newly arrived households, in line with Government instructions. To ensure the timely response to the emerging needs in case of influx of new arrivals and locations that have the risk of being affected by heavy rains and/or outbreaks, IOM will preposition NFI kits in/close to critical locations, where IOM has a MoU with partners’ warehouses. IOM plans to guarantee the participation of Women, Men, Girls and Boys as equals to ensure that the special needs of each group are taken into consideration. The design of activities and services will address specific needs of each gender and age groups, and address women's, girls' and boys’ specific needs, especially in terms of protection and access. To illustrate, (1) the content of NFI kits will be tailored in accordance to the needs of different age and gender groups and in coordination with the sector (2) all activities related to this project will equally target the different age and gender groups and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. Regarding assessment of gender specific needs, monitoring and evaluation and to measure the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations and set-up communication channels with them where possible, and all activities will be conducted based on Do No
Harm principles

project_name: Provision of improved, safe and dignified WASH services to  affected populations and host communities in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
As a result of ongoing protracted conflict causing unpredictable and continuous large- scale displacement, recurrent large-scale cholera and acute watery diarrhea (AWD)AWD epidemics, the COVID-19 pandemic, and seasonal flooding, fierce storms and winds, north- east Nigeria continues to experience multifaceted humanitarian crisis, and severely impacting access to safe  water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) . The main drivers of vulnerabilities related to WASH are closely linked to the conflict- induced and recurrent population displacement, and are also a result of pre-existing low level of WASH services in the Northeast. An estimated 2.8 million people across north-east Nigeria remain in critical need of sustained and equitable access to clean water and dignified hygiene and sanitation services (WASH Sector Gap analysis and MSNA 2020 data). 1.02 million people receive less than 15 liters of safe clean water per person per day while about 1.06 million people have intermittent water access with over 500 meters walking distance and over 30 minutes queuing time at water points
In response to the needs identified and in contribution to the Nigeria WASH Sector objectives 1,2, 3 and 4, IOM will scale-up its provision of WASH services targeting internally displaced people and returnees in camp, camp-like settings, as well as and hosting community in BAY (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe) States.
IOM will (A) Ensure safe access to water facilities and services through the drilling, installation, maintenance, rehabilitation and water quality monitoring of boreholes; (B) Ensure safe and equitable access to sanitation facilities (latrines, showers including laundry spaces), handwashing stations) through the operation and maintenance (O&M) of existing facilities and the construction of additional gender segregated facilities and waste water treatment system; (C) Promote improved  public health outcomes in targeted settings through the systematic promotion of personal and environmental hygiene messages (following national guidelines on COVID-19 preventive measures, such as physical distancing) and including COVID-19 preventive measure; and the support for increased capacity of established gender-balanced WASH committees (D) Ensure environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in operation area through the establishment of WASH Committees including- male and female community members, procurement and distribution of tools and equipment; (E) Distribute appropriate WASH NFI following the national/ cluster standards; and (F) Conduct capacity building of WASH partners and stakeholders with an overall aim at also mitigating the risks linked to the COVID pandemic.
The project will be implemented in three states: Borno (13 LGAs), Adamawa (5 LGAs) and Yobe State (8 LGAs), targeting an estimated 757,620 individuals.
IOM ensures that design and implementation of all WASH activities take into consideration the age, gender as well as disability-specific needs of project beneficiaries, and specifically addresses women and girls’ needs, such as Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM). All activities related to this project will benefit women and men, girls and boys and will be delivered on a sustainable and equitable basis. In regard to assessments, monitoring and evaluation of gender, age and disability specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures on the ground in these locations during missions and set-up communication channels where possible.
Using the IOM WASH Monitoring and Evaluation Framework, IOM will ensure that “Do No Harm” principles are adhered to throughout the WASH interventions, particularly in WASH activities pertaining to latrine and water point locations and construction, through the use of various mechanisms, such as consultations with vulnerable groups.

project_name: Holistic Approach to Livelihood program for sustainable recovery and increased resilience of severely conflict affected communities in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
The crisis in NE Nigeria continues to disrupt and limit access to livelihoods of millions of people, undermining opportunities for durable solutions. As a result of the continuous conflict which generated a situation of widespread unemployment further aggravated by the COVID-19 pandemic, many households lack sufficient income to meet their basic needs, and livelihood opportunities remain scarce. Although the need for essential life-saving assistance is still widespread, IOM recognizes the urgent need for early recovery interventions, including restoring livelihoods and access to essential services, access to justice, to strengthen the self-reliance of affected populations, especially girls, youth, women, and the elderly, against future vulnerabilities and shocks. These elements are also crucial for creating conditions for durable solutions for IDPs and restoring social cohesion. Without those pre-conditions, a premature return of displaced populations may lead to secondary displacement, deepen IDPs’ vulnerability, and exacerbate tension and social polarization between IDPs, host communities and Returnees. The inadequate capacity in areas experiencing return is by IOM considered a direct risk to the overall progressive resolution of displacement in the north-east. This project seeks to contribute to the recovery and resilience building of conflict-affected populations through a series of community support interventions. As people continue to return to their places of habitual residence from before the insurgency, there is urgent and significant needs to restore infrastructure, promote early recovery, including through economic and livelihoods restoration, and facilitate a robust resilience building process. Livelihood interventions under this project will include Cash for Work (CFW). Cash-based interventions are a more dignified way of assisting affected populations, as they empower people to determine their own needs and the best way of meeting them. They can also promote peaceful coexistence between IDP, returnee and host communities, as well-designed and run cash- based interventions have a multiplier effect, jointly engaging all members of the community and directly benefiting the local economy. In addition, vocational skills training and skills enhancement activities for youth will be organized as per outcome of a labor market assessment to create human capital as necessary for the early recovery phase, with a special focus on youth. Each targeted beneficiaries will receive business start-up capital to establish small scale business. CFW and skilled labor schemes will support activities such as comprehensive neighborhood upgrades and light community infrastructure rehabilitation to directly contribute to recovery in conflict-affected areas. In addition, this project will work towards enhanced coordination and complementarity between humanitarian, stabilization and development partners, through a people centered approach. To supplement economic recovery interventions, the project will support restoration of social cohesion and local governance mechanisms in the areas of intervention. To this end, the project aims to provide technical and logistical support to community peace committees to address social cohesion concerns. Furthermore, as protection is ensured in recovery efforts, the project will build the capacity of law enforcement bodies, including traditional/religious leaders, to prevent and respond to GBV crimes in compliance with human rights standards and through a victim-centered approach. IOM will align its response plan to the 4 strategic objectives of Early Recovery and Livelihoods Sector as follows:
•	Support Livelihood Stabilization and income recovered
•	Promote inclusiveness and peaceful co-existence among IDPs, Host Communities and Returnees.
•	Support restoration of local community governance administration and services 
•	Increase access to infrastructure and basic social services in areas of return

project_name: Emergency Lifesaving Cash and Livelihood Support to IDP and Non- IDP Communities in Somalia
project_objective:
Somalia is facing a severe and deteriorating humanitarian crisis as we enter 2022 as a result of the compounding effects of conflict, recurrent climate shocks, diseases and pests outbreaks with increased levels of vulnerability and substantial increase in the humanitarian caseload (Somalia HNO, 2022). There is a serious risk that the impact of consecutive below average to poor rainfall in most parts of the country will develop into a severe drought by early to mid- 2022 with the number of people facing acute food insecurity on the rise. It is likely that minority groups, women, children, people with disabilities, will experience heightened protection risks as a result, unless they are intentionally targeted to receive tailored assistance.

With approximately 3.5 million individuals in IPC 3 and 4 through at least December 2021, FAO proposes to target 160,300 households (961,800 individuals- 91,500 IDPs and 870,300 non- IDPs) in IPC 3 and IPC 4 caseloads respectively. This will include 216,790 women, 254,492 girls, 264,880 boys and 225,638 men and 144,270 people living with disabilities (PWD) across 59 districts in Somalia through its flagship Cash+ approach combining short-term cash transfers with tailored livelihood support in accordance with technical and humanitarian standards. Vulnerable households will identified from at-risk pastoral, agro-pastoral, fishing, riverine farmers, IDPs and Non- IDP communities in IPC 3 and 4 areas. This intervention will integrate short-term cash transfers aimed at enabling the most vulnerable households to meet their immediate needs, with livelihood support to allow crisis-affected households to get back into production. FAO will employ community- led beneficiary selection processes and ensure adequate targeting and representation of extremely vulnerable and minority groups in community committees. Interventions proposed will employ a Do No Harm approach with a gender lens that ensures conflict- sensitivity to reduce protection risks for all individuals, and to mitigate the risk of conflict or community tensions. 

Under Food Security Cluster (FSC) Objective 1, to improve access to food, FAO will deliver lifesaving cash assistance to 160,300 households through a blend of conditional (Cash-for-Work) and unconditional (UCT) transfers. Under UCT, FAO will prioritize Cash+ interventions including Cash+ Agriculture, Cash+ livestock and Cash+ fisheries. These modalities will increase households’ immediate access to food by providing sufficient cash to access the minimum expenditure basket (MEB), while supporting the rehabilitation of critical productive and community infrastructure. It will also boost household food production, increase household incomes and create employment opportunities. Cash transfer values will be informed by the Cash Working Group and are expected to differ per district/ region of intervention. They, however, will be valued at 80 percent of the food MEB, which can range from USD 50- 100 per month. All cash-based programmes will include training on good nutrition practices. 

Under FSC Objective 2, to protect livelihoods and related food sources, FAO will provide in-kind, technical support and tailored trainings to 112,500 HHs to anticipate, mitigate and respond to food security and nutrition threats, including the delivery of integrated cash and livelihood support to targeted HHs. In addition, FAO shall provide transitional cash support to 13,100 HHs across agro pastoral, pastoral and fishing livelihood zones to augment the adaptive capacity of HHs, strengthen and foster resilience to future shocks, cushioning them from food insecurity and malnutrition. Trainings shall be delivered alongside input provision to build skills in sustainable use of resources provided, build skills in livelihoods management including harvest, post- harvest management, linking beneficiaries to long- term interventions that provide them opportunities to enhance their livelihoods and skills.

project_name: Protecting and promoting mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of conflict affected populations in north-east Nigeria
project_objective:
In this project, IOM seeks to prioritize the provision of life-saving protection services, addressing gender-based violence (GBV), and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through prevention, response and risk mitigation activities as well as mainstream protection through provision of assistance in a safe, timely, and dignified manner. 
1.	IOM's MHPSS activities will consist of services to populations informed by assessment of their needs to provide a comprehensive response from a community-based approach, including lay counselling, basic emotional support, life-skills development, language classes, and socio-relational and cultural activities.  IOM will ensure that a multi-layered response system is established that integrates affected populations, government and stakeholders to improve access and provision of quality services; community members' knowledge, socio-relational capacities, and practices are strengthened towards peaceful co-existence and community stability; and people with mental health disorders and needs are referred to the appropriate mental health services and facilities. IOM will implement activities using a holistic approach to design preventive and risk mitigation models to respond to the drivers of MHPSS and protection risk factors that are already identified, with the long-term focus on building local capacities. 
2.	In close partnership with the NAPTIP, IOM will continue to build the capacity of counter-trafficking stakeholders with the intent to localize and increase ownership of the counter-trafficking response in north-east Nigeria. IOM will also seek to improve prevention and response services targeting at-risk sub-groups of the crisis-affected populations and victims of trafficking.
3.	To support GBV survivors consenting to access services in the camp and host communities, IOM's Psychosocial Mobile Teams will provide the following array of services: survivors of GBV will be provided with psychological first aids (PFA) (Level 1 and 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid) to cover their acute needs; targeted survivors of GBV will be provided with structured psychosocial counselling, either as a stand-alone service or to complement other specialized services (Level 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid); With their consent, survivors of GBV will be referred to specialized services for case management and dedicated follow-up (Level 4 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid); Families of GBV survivors will be provided with structured psychosocial counselling and family support sessions (Level 3 of IASC MHPSS Intervention Pyramid). In addition, IOM will ensure that safety, confidentiality, respect, and non-discrimination principles are adhered to protect survivors' rights and dignity and promote resilience. IOM will focus on system strengthening to ease GBV survivors' access to medical, legal aid, safety services, and vulnerable individuals' access to services. To mitigate the risk of GBV and other protection risks in camp and host communities, IOM will conduct context specific sensitization and awareness campaigns on GBV and protection threats in the targeted camp and camp-like settings. 
4. IOM will jointly work with the IDP safety committees to conduct safety audits and mapping to identify and highlight protection and safety concerns within the camps, disseminate protection-focused messages, and increase awareness of protection risks. 
5. IOM will continue to enhance accountability to the affected population by strengthening Protection against sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) and feedback mechanisms.
6.	IOM will build the capacities of humanitarian actors, including IOM staff, as well as community- based structures in the areas of MHPSS, Protection, GBV and counter-trafficking with the overall aim of mainstreaming protection principles in programming and strengthening GBV risk mitigation.

project_name: Support to WASH services and systems through rehabilitation and capacity building in Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Idlib, Hama, Quneitra and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
In 2021 ZOA implemented projects in multiple sectors including WASH, reaching a total of 118,130 beneficiaries. In 2021 ZOA was able to secure $4,732,378 in funding, of which $1,200,000 was SHF funding. ZOA was able to allocate $1,635,000 for activities under the WASH sector, reaching out to 55,000 beneficiaries. In 2022 ZOA has to date secured $2,122,655 with around 1 million USD secured for WASH interventions. 

Through the proposed project for 2022-23 ZOA is estimating to target 156,000 beneficiaries, the cost per beneficiary is estimated $44. In 2022 ZOA is targeting 114,00 beneficiaries (58,140 female, 55,860 male, children 05 - 14,770, 5-17 - 34680, adults 18-59 - 58,630 & 59 older - 5,920). Through this proposal ZOA is aiming at expanding its interventions to reach communities most in need of WASH in underserved conflict affected areas in Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Idlib, Hama, Quneitra and Rural Damascus. All selected sub-districts fall under scores 3-5 on the severity scale, according to the WASH PiN assessment document shared by the sector, also taking into consideration the activity needs in the selected sub-districts. ZOA’s activities focus on the maintenance and/or light rehabilitation of existing WASH systems, specifically prioritizing activities supporting existing water and sanitation systems, including water quality assurance and rehabilitation of infrastructure. Interventions also include solid waste management activities. The overall objective is to provide support to water and sanitation/sewage systems to ensure regular services for vulnerable households in areas with high severity of needs. 

ZOA is proposing the following broad activities:

Support to water systems and services: Rehabilitation of water wells will ensure sufficient quantity and quality water for target beneficiaries. Since electricity is a major hurdle ZOA has taken into consideration the provision of solar energy systems wherever possible. The rehabilitation of Bab Al Nayrab sand filtration system is also taken into consideration upon the recommendation of Aleppo WASH sector and Aleppo Water Establishment.

Support to sanitation/sewage networks: Rehabilitation of damaged sewage pipes to prevent groundwater infiltration as well as sewage leaks which can contaminate the environment.

Support to solid waste management systems:

- Community debris and garbage clean-up in target communities - The solid waste management activities are especially important in light of the COVID-19 pandemic as breathing difficulties can arise from the fungi that develop from garbage that has not been safely disposed of. Solid Waste Management helps to prevent the transmission of bacterial infections at a community level.
- Provision of communal garbage bins so target communities can safely dispose of their household waste.
- Cash for work activities.
- Capacity building of municipalities for operation and maintenance of infrastructure.

The project activities are aligned with the WASH sector: Objective 1: Support water, sanitation / sewerage, and solid waste management systems to ensure regular service for affected people in Syria.

The selected activities are either based on the needs that ZOA team came across during the (evaluation of) activities implemented during 2021, or recommendations by local population, WASH sector and authorities, which ZOA all takes very seriously. Therefore, before the final design of any project ZOA will consult the concerned ministry, local authorities (governor, mayor, moukhtars) and organizes FGDs with different age groups of the community, so that the activities really serve their needs. In parallel, ZOA carries out a quick market assessment or search for a recent assessment done by partners, to define the proper modality that works best in the targeted area. ZOA is also in process of signing an MoU with the Ministry of Water Resources.

project_name: Protection assistance for vulnerable children and communities in WoS in 2022 - 2023
project_objective:
The overall goal of the War Child programme is to increase the resilience and wellbeing among vulnerable children and youth in North East and North West Syria. Under this action, War Child would respond to urgent Child Protection needs in Idleb and Aleppo, and expand the service provision for highly vulnerable children in Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor through CFS, structured PSS, awareness raising, and developing specialized service capacity within local partner organizations, so that they can deliver a quality case management service. This will target 17,500 in NW hub, and 17,500 in NE hub over the two year period. The budget is $1,125,000 for NW each year and $1,125,000 for NE each year. Multiyear planning will enable a flexible response, with the ability to look at longer-term needs, and build a sustainable response with better outcomes. 
This prevention and response approach will address immediate and urgent identified child protection risks while contributing to long-term change. The project aims to reach parents and caregivers as well as local leaders and communities to build a more protective environment for vulnerable children affected by conflict. The project will contribute to multi-sector initiatives (specifically in Education) to support the mainstreaming of Protection outcomes. It will also focus on local organisations to build sustainable technical CP capacity and enhance the quality of the overall response.

project_name: Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela
project_objective:
Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar a través de comida en especie o transferencias monetarias.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.

project_name: Coordinación logística - Clúster de Logística
project_objective:
El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (WFP), liderando el Clúster de Logística, apoyará y complementará las acciones de los socios humanitarios con la coordinación de servicios de logística con el objetivo de contribuir a una respuesta efectiva y oportuna en beneficio de la población más afectada.
La continuidad en las actividades de coordinación y gestión de la información, proporcionando una plataforma de intercambio de información logística relevante y actualizada entre las organizaciones, es una de las prioridades del Clúster de Logística para 2022. A fecha de hoy son 36 las organizaciones que forman parte del Clúster de Logística. Otra de sus tareas para 2022 será la de incluir entre sus miembros a otros actores humanitarios clave, tales como organizaciones humanitarias nacionales; así como también involucrar al sector privado en sus actividades.
Otra línea de acción clave consiste en el acercamiento a las autoridades nacionales y la Cancillería para plantear los desafíos de las organizaciones humanitarias y agencias del SNU, con el objetivo ulterior de desarrollar soluciones en mesas de trabajo con los organismos técnicos institucionales.
En 2022, será prioritario apoyar los esfuerzos de preparación para emergencias (en el Plan de Lluvias) y encontrar medios de mitigación de las barreras logísticas al despliegue en emergencias. Esas actividades se enmarcan bajo el segundo objetivo estratégico. Es necesario un acercamiento con la Dirección Nacional de Protección Civil y Administración de Desastres, como actor clave en la preparación para emergencias. El Clúster de Logística tendrá como meta el establecimiento de líneas de trabajo conjunto con las autoridades locales, a través de la coordinación y la complementariedad de la capacidad de respuesta de los socios del Clúster, y con al apoyo de los Centros de Coordinación en el Terreno. El Clúster de Logística continuará facilitando el intercambio de información dentro de la comunidad humanitaria sobre vías de comunicación para llegar a zonas de difícil acceso y la promoverá el intercambio de recursos logísticos en zonas remotas, como en los estados Amazonas, Bolívar y Delta Amacuro.
Si las necesidades son identificadas y existe el financiamiento necesario, el Clúster de Logística podrá establecer un servicio de transporte y/o almacenamiento.
El Clúster de Logística se propone fomentar las capacitaciones de los socios humanitarios, promoviendo a su vez el intercambio de conocimiento entre ellos. Si se requiere, se apoyarán los esfuerzos de fortalecimiento de las capacidades de las autoridades y de las organizaciones no gubernamentales. Estas actividades no pretenden reemplazar las capacitaciones logísticas de cada organización, sino responder a brechas o necesidades específicamente identificadas.
El Clúster de Logística contribuirá a desarrollar mensajes clave y propuestas técnicas como aporte al ejercicio de incidencia llevada a cabo por el Coordinador Humanitario y otros actores.

project_name: Preparación y respuesta a choques para la seguridad alimentaria

El mismo tiene el objetivo de fortalecer la preparación local de respuesta ante estas situaciones, contribuyendo a la capacidad operativa de socios locales; proveer acceso a asistencia alimentaria inmediata y necesidades esenciales de las personas más vulnerables; así como apoyar estrategias de afrontamiento de medios de vida de personas afectadas. project_name: Mitigate the worst effects of water scarcity through access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services to vulnerable communities in acute crises in South Sudan.
project_objective: The worsening situation in Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Unity can be mainly attributed to the protracted conflict in the country and the unfavorable rainfall patterns attributed to climate change. Panyijar County was affected by heavy flooding. The Humanitarian Needs overview released in February 2022 states that the  cumulative impact of recurrent flooding contributed to the destruction and damage to water facilities, leaving vulnerable people in urgent need of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, and intensified existing vulnerabilities of affected people. The proposed project seeks to provide water and sanitation services to affected households in Panyijar. The intervention will target host communities of the area, returnees and IDPs. The projects will expand on existing WASH infrastructure and services to facilitate access to safe drinking water and sanitation facilities. Water inventories will be conducted in consultation with the respective district administrations to determine where drinking water points, public latrines and handwashing stations, for instance in schools, health centers public spaces within the communities, need to be constructed, rehabilitated, and/or expanded. In collaboration with the local private sector, such critically needed WASH infrastructure will be constructed, rehabilitated, and/or expanded, and trainings for their operation and maintenance will be conducted with the involved communities. For the latter, mobilization of community engagement will be achieved through the establishment of water user and sanitation committees. Moreover, elderly and disabled people will be assisted in building their latrines and menstrual and/or general hygiene kits will be distributed to the affect population (in particular women and girls). To prevent the spread of (water borne) diseases and increase hygiene awareness, of hygiene promotion and Covid-19 campaigns will be conducted, including the provision of relevant IEC and PPE material where relevant.

project_objective: La fragilité de l'environnement sahélien, alliée à la récurrence des chocs et défis (naturels ou d'origine humaine) rencontrés par les populations de Tillabéry ,  Tahoua et de Diffa, conduisent à des situations cycliques d'insécurité alimentaire aggravée pour les plus vulnérables. Les ménages vulnérables peu ou pas aptes au travail dans le besoin, et qui n'ont pas de bras valides dans leurs ménages, WHH mettra en œuvre des actions de distribution de cash inconditionnel dans le strict respect de la dignité humaine sans aucune distinction sociale, raciale, réligieuse ou genre.

project_name: Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan
project_objective:
Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_name: Mental Health Psychosocial Support and Functional Rehabilitation for Persons with disabilities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will address the immediate and long-term health needs with focus on mental health and psychosocial support, physical rehabilitation and disability inclusion needs of the most vulnerable persons that are the center of humanitarian response to cope with recurrent shock and build resilience. 
The project will target returnees, IDPs and host population with specific focus on persons at risk of exclusion specifically people with disabilities, people with injuries and chronic diseases, people experiencing mental health and psychosocial problems, children, older persons; who are often invisible to mainstream humanitarian organizations. The project activities will target an estimate of 14,970 (5,988 Male, 8,982 Female among them will be 2,994 persons with disabilities, 1,780 elderly persons, 200 children and 12,990 adults ) Vulnerable IDPS, returnees and host population. The focus will be on newly and protracted displaced households with a key attention to support positive coping mechanisms and resilience strengthening. HI will have static presence in the target project locations ;  with support from local community structures, local organizations of persons with disabilities, health and protection partners; HI will identify the most vulnerable to MHPSS and physical rehabilitation needs and provide direct services. HI will critically focus on mainstreaming protection, gender and disability Inclusion issues at all stages of the intervention, identifying and giving priority to vulnerable female headed households and persons with disabilities. HI has one (01) MEAL manager and two (02) MEAL officers who will independently conduct all post distribution monitoring and share the outcomes with the team and cluster partners at state and national level.
The activities will be implemented by HI static team based in the Juba ,Pibor, Rubkona, and Aweil Center, with a  mobile response to Morobo and Lainya from Yei where HI has a static base.

project_name: QC's SNFI Response in NWS 2022

The project goal is to support the IDPs to cope with the severe conditions the area is going through from the beginning of the conflict through improving their shelter conditions and access to NFIs. The project includes multi-activity response to ensure full coverage of people’s needs and access to basic services. The project will be targeting both IDPs and host communities to alleviate the pressure on community resources. alongside different gender and age needs including women children elderly and people with special needs will be taken into consideration while designing the project.
The intervention for 2022 and 2023 will be done through in-kind and cash modalities preferably bought from the local market ensuring support to the local economy. Allocation of items in areas will be done through multi-sectoral needs and technical assessments to capture all aspects of IDPs’ and their hosts’ conditions, to ensure appropriate intervention.
