project_name: Sustain the lives of 40,440 persons requiring emergency food assistance across Banadir region with particular focus on IDPs and people with disability.
project_objective:
The proposed project is emergency in nature and is going to deliver immediate humanitarian food assistance to address the food insecurity gap of the severely drought affected IDP populations living across Benadir region. The project will address the acute food insecurity among the targeted households with particular focus on recently displaced families who are at the borderline and have no means of survival, people with disability and vulnerable groups including women who are unable to engage livelihood means for earning and will support 6,740 H.H under IPC#4 phase living in Benadir IDP camps for a period of 4 months with unconditional food assistant through voucher system. The interventions are expected to enhance the vulnerable household’s food consumption score and improve nutrition status among children and also reduce the negative coping mechanism they apply when such nature of crisis strike. 
The project will give an early relief to the crisis affected people enabling them to quickly access food and improve food consumption score among children, women and elderly people living in the IDP camps. At the end, food security status of 6,740 vulnerable H.H living in Benadir will be improved through monthly food voucher assistants thus contributing to the overall cluster strategy of minimizing the number of people in crises (IPC4 and above). QC in collaboration with the target recipient groups, QC will identify food vendors/suppliers in the target zone with particular attention given to the protection concerns in the process of food collection. People will be given the chance to demonstrate their willingness and choice regarding vendor selection process.  Once vendor suppliers identified, Beneficiaries will be given voucher to enable visit the vendor and collect the food ration on monthly basis. QC MEAL staff will conduct continues monitoring exercise on the process of distribution and they will be present at the distribution points to ensure process are smooth and people are receiving their entitlement accordingly. In addition to this, food quality will be inspected before and during distribution exercise to ensure food quality. 
Community based targeting will be used for beneficiary selection process. Gender will be given special role as project will work to improve gender equity and participation in all project planning and implementation processes. Local authorities and camp relief committees will be engaged during the selection process. Community will take the process ownership and identify beneficiary based on vulnerability criteria set. Camp relief committees will be trained on selection process especially vulnerability criteria. Post selection verification will be conducted by QC team to verify the lists with the participation of the whole community. The final and verified list will be jointly approved by the camp relief committee, local authorities and QC.  
Project will engage broader stakeholders in the ground including government officials, local authorities, members from local community and other humanitarian partners for coordination and collaboration reasons. Further on this, QC will work to build exist strategy through linking the supported beneficiaries with other resilience programs going on in the areas. This will be achieved through continued networking and engagement with all including federal ministries officials, local authorities and partners that work resilience programming.

project_name: Gender-based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Population in South Sudan
project_objective: The GBV prevention and response program of International Medical Corps (IMC) in South Sudan aims to empower communities and build resilience through promoting social and behavioral change to address the root causes of GBV in the country. The project targets key population to create a sustainable change in attitude and practices through male engagement, working with community leaders and building capacity of local stakeholders. Leveraging on the vast experiences, gains, and successes of IMC in implementing GBV prevention and response interventions through the FCDO-HARISS program, this project will be continued to implement in the states of Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau IDP Camp and County), Upper Nile and Malakal PoC and County), Unity (Nyal County), and in Canal/Pigi County. It will directly benefit about 27495 vulnerable women and girls across the target locations. One of the project’s key priorities is to further strengthen core services to survivors of GBV and other vulnerable women and girls in the aforesaid intervention sites. These services include quality case management using a survivor-centered approach, along with psychosocial support to enhance healing and recovery. IMC UK works to ensure that survivors’ holistic needs are met by providing multi-sectoral services, referring to health centers for clinical management of rape, to legal justice services and to other kinds of support based on the needs of survivors. In addition to individual PSS for survivors, IMC UK will continue with PSS group activities for all vulnerable women and girls in the women girls’ safe spaces (WGSS). To ensure sustainability of the project and ownership by the community, especially of the WGSSs, in Wau, Nyal and Malakal, IMC already established, leadership committee comprise of 8 members from the community selected by their fellow women with the responsibility to give support, information, feedback, and suggestions that will foster empowerment and ownership of the space and the overall wellbeing of their members. The women committee members will be further empowered with knowledge and skills through hands-on management of the spaces and co-leading with them on the daily functioning of the WGSS. The women committee will be continuously mentored and trained on GBV basic concepts, safe referral, and referral pathways, and on leadership and conflict management and facilitation techniques and on various psychosocial support activities using IMC’s and IRC’s global WGSS toolkit. IMC UK will implement holistic community engagement strategies on the promotion of long-term positive change in the targeted communities. IMC will use the GBV community mobilization tool called SASA! - Phase-based strategy to help communities rethink about “power” and the positive use of power. “Preventing Violence against Women and Girls: Engaging Men in Accountable Practice (EMAP)” is also another tool that will be used to ensure men engagement with accountability to prevent GBV in the targeted community in Nyal, Wau and Malakal. In addition, IMC trains and collaborates with GBV Taskforce members in Wau, Malakal and Nyal. These will be supported by staff IMC UK staff to do awareness raising, and safe confidential referral of any survivors who disclose to them. IMC UK will provide emergency cash assistance for case management to the vulnerable women and girls. Cash assistance is one of the interagency minimum standards in GBV programming in emergency (Standard 11: Dignity Kits, Cash Assistance). In addition to this, IMC UK opts to implement cash assistance based on lesson learnt and feedback from women and girls on importance of cash assistance as lifesaving; for example, it can help a survivor meet the costs associated with fleeing an abusive relationship (e.g., rent, temporary shelter, transportation, food, clothing, etc).

project_name: Provision of integrated, safe, equitable, dignified and disaster-resistant WASH services to IDPs, host communities, and returnees living in extreme and catastrophic WASH vulnerability
project_objective:
The project aims to provide integrated, safe, equitable, dignified and disaster-resistant access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services to IDPs, host communities, and returnees living in extreme and catastrophic WASH vulnerability.

To that end, IOM’s interventions will focus on locations identified by the WASH Cluster as key priorities: priority 1 counties (Tonj East, Malakal, Rubkona, Leer and Guit), priority 2 counties (Tonj North and Koch), priority 3 counties (Aweil East) and priority 4 counties (Twic and Tonj South). Through its Rapid Response Team, IOM will also intervene in any other Priority 4 and/or 5 locations, or any other location identified through WASH Cluster allocation. Although not included in the WASH Cluster Targeting Guidance (2022), IOM's HRP proposal also prioritizes Wau, as IOM will remain the main water service provider in Wau’s Naivasha IDP Camp during 2022. 

IOM’s HRP project contributes to the 4 WASH Cluster Strategic Objectives, focusing on integrating WASH programming with Nutrition, providing access to basic WASH services in emergencies, whilst mitigating WASH GBV and reducing community’s exposure to environmental hazards. In total, IOM plans to reach 550,000 individuals (132,819 women, 127,049 men, 141,594 girls, 148,538 boys) by deploying a range of activity packages that combine hardware and software interventions, adapted to the context at play and to the needs of the most affected population. To support nutrition gains, IOM will rehabilitate/install WASH infrastructure within nutrition sites and/or at community level, while in locations where WASH services need to be rapidly restored due to sudden emergencies, IOM will rehabilitate/drill new boreholes, rehabilitate/set up/operate surface water treatment systems (SWATs). IOM will also ensure the sustainability of WASH infrastructure through the formation and training of community-based operation and maintenance groups. These hardware interventions will be complemented with hygiene promotion, as well as distribution and demonstration on usage of WASH NFIs and/or Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) to help communities sustain the learnt practices. All activities will contribute towards mitigating GBV risks and to improve accessibility to people with special needs, as demonstrated by IOM’s commitment to allocate 2.9 % of the project budget to GBV risk mitigation mainstreaming Where needed, activities will be adjusted to be climate resilient and/or to build the capacity of communities to respond quicker to natural disasters. Where possible, IOM will also prioritise market-based programming approaches, using local markets to support WASH responses. As the largest direct WASH service provider in camp settings, IOM will also continue servicing conflict-affected populations in Malakal Protection of Civilians (PoCs), Bentiu and Wau’s Naivasha Internal Displacement Camp (IDP), and Bentiu’s IDP sites (A, B and C). IOM will provide WASH services through the operation and maintenance of safe and accessible water supply systems, care and maintenance of accessible and secure sanitation and handwashing facilities, as well as management of solid and liquid waste. IOM will also continue investing in cost-effective and climate-resilient means of ensuring adequate service provision within these settings by setting up, maintaining, and scaling up water supply solar systems and biogas schemes. IOM will support the transition process at these sites working to transfer WASH service provision towards community-based ownership where possible, through a participatory approach, with a focus on women’s empowerment. Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and COVID-19 prevention measures will also be mainstreamed throughout the project cycle.

project_name: Food and livelihood assistance to the most vulnerable and crisis affected population in South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed project aims to provide food assistance, livelihood and resilience support to 1,105,380 vulnerable populations in Upper Nile, Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria and Greater Bahr el Ghazal. The project will implement activities that will prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies of target beneficiaries in IPC 5, 4 and 3. The project will also seek to enhance emergency food production and contribute to the reduction of dependency to food and agricultural inputs. World Vision will adopt a mix of intervention approaches including but not limited to unconditional and General Food Distribution, cash transfers, complementary livelihood support, capacity building (e.g., modern agronomic practices, Integrated Pest Management, Natural Resource Management, etc.), and resilience building at the household level. The proposed project will also be implemented in synergy with other sectors implemented by World Vision in the targeted locations such as health, nutrition, WASH, gender and protection related programming while maintaining coordinating and complementarity with the efforts of other humanitarian actors and line ministries. In order to reach the target beneficiaries with prioritized cluster objectives, World Vision South Sudan proposed a total of $4,512,952 US project budget for 2022.

project_name: Emergency Shelter, NFI and Protection Assistance to Vulnerable Households in Afar and Amhara
project_objective:
IOM as Shelter and NFI (S-NFI) Cluster Lead Agency (CLA), plans to reach up to 439,021 vulnerable individuals (79,822 households) whose capacity to anticipate, cope with and recover from conflict stresses have been eroded. To respond to the lifesaving humanitarian needs faced by an estimated 8.9 million persons across the country where as SNFI cluster plans to targets around 5 million persons (1.3 million in Afar and Amhara region (360,260 in Afar and 955,230 in Amhara region). These most vulnerable individuals are the one who are unable to support themselves with lifesaving shelter and non-food items. The targeted communities include newly displaced persons, IDPs in protracted displacement in camps and collective centers, IDPs living with host communities, and affected non-displaced host communities.  The proposed activities are designed in line with HRP strategic objectives 2022, as well as the S-NFI Cluster objectives and key activities.
Output: Improve access to life saving shelter and life sustaining non-food items and enhance resilience of most vulnerable population through area-based programming. (HRP CO1 and CO2; S- NFI Cluster Objectives).
IOM has extensive experience in Shelter and NFI responses in both emergency and post-crisis environments. IOM has static presence across Afar and Amhara and currently responds to humanitarian needs. IOM is the ES/NFI Cluster lead agency which conducts assessments and training for local authorities and Cluster Partners on ES, NFI, cash assistance. IOM supports SNFI Cluster partners through the provision of in-kind ES and NFI kits as well as supportive supervision. 
IOM provides integrated programing alongside health, CCCM, MHPSS, Protection and WASH responses. Delivering Shelter assistance, Housing, Land and Property (HLP) support including ES/NFI assistance to vulnerable communities maximizes the impact of the project in these locations. 
•	Improve access to ES and lifesaving NFIs through in-kind and Cash-Based Interventions. IOM response will provide SNFI assistance to new IDPs, protracted IDPs in camps and collective canters, returnees, PWSN (including Disability and Inclusion (DI) kits) and host community member requiring assistance.
•	Support SNFI Cluster partners through provision of in-kind ES and NFI kits (including DI ES and NFI kits), funding for their response, focus on SNFI Cluster partner capacity building and focus on support to NNGO partners.
•	Upgrade/rehabilitation/maintenance of shelter, in camps and CCs, through both in-kind and CBI;
•	Strengthen evidence-based programming through improved monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning. 
•	Mainstream gender, protection/GBV, HLP, environment and AAP in all activities. The specific needs of women will be taken into consideration in the provision of SNFI supplies to populations, IDP in camps, returnees and host communities. IOM will prioritize households headed by women for in-kind and CBI SNFI support. 
•	Strengthen the capacity of SNFI Staff on emergency and settlement programming, CBI, gender, data quality assessment, AAP and Protection; 
•	Undertake market assessment and multi-sectoral risk and needs assessment
•	Provision of in-kind life-saving ES and NFIs based on need assessment and verification
•	Provision of cash for rent and cash for emergency NFIs 
•	Undertake Monitoring and evaluation through baseline, post distribution monitoring and end-line assessment
•	Undertake Safety Audits and Protection Mainstreaming awareness raising
IOM will target 10 percent of vulnerable host communities in need of support with essential ES/NFI. Including vulnerable host community members within caseload as part of needs-based targeting to improving social cohesion. Considering the COVID-19 pandemic, the proposed project will take into account public health advice to limit beneficiary exposure.

project_name: Increase access to safe, inclusive and quality education for school-age children in in Cabo Delgado
project_objective: The project aim at: (i) improving access to education for boys, girls and CWD 5-18 affected by the crisis and deprived from the right of education due to conflict; (ii) supporting teachers and members of schools communities affected by the crisis to detect risky situations for students, increasing their skills in communicating with children to reduce the effects and consequences of trauma and/or stressful events.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods of Vulnerable Agropastoralists Communities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria States, South Sudan
project_objective:
Climatic extremes, which have in the recent past been characterized by unprecedented flooding, coupled with increasing waves of inter and intra communal violence, bureaucratic impediments including instances of youth aggression towards humanitarian actors, and economic implications of the COVID 19 pandemic that have continued to negatively impact vulnerable boys, girls, men and women, including people with disabilities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria among other States in the country. These have had consequent implications on increased livestock disease outbreaks and mortalities in addition to submerging of agricultural land contributing to unprecedented food insecurity levels, projected to further increase in 2022 with at least 8.3 million people projected to face severe food insecurity by May –July 2022 (Flood Situation Reports 2021; Humanitarian Needs Overview, 2022).

Many vulnerable host, returnee and displaced families, especially women, widowed women, child headed households, the elderly, boys and girls including people with disabilities (who have impaired access to livelihoods); solely depend on livestock, fishing, vegetable and crop farming among other coping strategies. VSF Suisse 26 years of experience in the targeted states, presence on the ground and proven capacity will deliver high quality programming by leveraging on strong grass root networks, local knowledge, understanding of seasonal and location specific contexts. 

Proposed actions will target 187,000 beneficiaries (30000 men, 30000 women, 63500 girls, 63500 boys) who shall include elderly and people living with disabilities. The action will be aimed at ensuring cost efficiency through complementarities by linkages with FAO pipeline for livestock vaccines prepositioning and agricultural livelihood kits - crops, vegetables and fishing kits in order to promote preparedness, household resilience and self-reliance through protection of livelihood opportunities.
 
Proposed actions are in line and correspond with the FSL Cluster 2022 HRP Cluster Objectives Supporting SO1: Life Saving - CO2: Emergency livelihood (crop, vegetable and fishing kits) and livestock support (vaccination and treatment); and Supporting SO3: Resilience & Coping mechanisms CO3: Building self-reliance: by supporting capacity building, asset, market support and value addition. By supporting famine clusters in the catchment areas of health and nutrition facilities and in communities with or without functional boreholes; in addition to the establishment of demonstration sites for vegetable gardening support at nutrition facilities coupled with agronomic training and on-going extension advice and guidance at both main Season farming Response and Dry Season Response that shall include conduct nutrition sensitive feeding and cooking practices. 

The project will ensure a multi-sectoral approach through inter-cluster synergies, quality programming, cost efficiency in addition to mainstreaming cross-cutting programmatic approaches that include application of Accountability to Affected Populations principles, protection including Gender Based Violence mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conflict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention, environmental conservation and sustainability.

project_objective:
To protect livelihoods of vulnerable rural and urban populations and improve food
security through the provision of livelihood support during the main planting and dry
season (crop and vegetable seeds, tools, 􀂦shing kits, livestock vaccines and drugs),

project_name: Creating a Safe Environment for and Providing Life-Saving GBV Response Services as well as integrating child protection components to the Crisis-Affected Women, Girls and Children in South Sudan
project_objective:
In line with the identified needs and gaps, CARE International in South Sudan aims to provide a comprehensive package of GBV response services, which will be complemented with the prevention activities that address the root causes of the GBV in Juba, Magwi, Ikotos, Torit, Kapoeta North, Budi, Wau, Jur River, Koch, Rubkona, Pariang, Bor South, Pibor, Twic East, Duk and Akobo.  The interventions will be provided through static centers and through mobile and outreach teams. Static Women Girls Safe Spaces (WGFS) will be used as entry points to reach out to the communities, while outreach sessions by mobile teams will also be used as means of engaging with communities. The WGFSs will serve as the centers where women and girls can come together and socialize while also improving their psychosocial wellbeing. In order to do that CARE will provide structured and unstructured PSS activities. The unstructured activities will take the form of recreational activities which will be determined in consultation with the women and girls, i.e.. knitting, baking, sewing, painting or handicrafts. The structured activities on the other hand will aim to promote overall life skills of women and girls. Similarly, CARE will train women and girls on usage and set up of Fuel Efficient Stoves as part of GBV risk mitigation measures. These efforts will be supported with experience sharing sessions among women on cooking or sharing recipes to promote cohesion and communication among women groups. CARE will also offer income generation activities to the women and girls who fit into the activity criteria, which will include vulnerable individuals, survivors, female-headed households and so on.

Through the WGFSs, CARE will provide GBV case management services to the survivors, while ensuring updating (or creating referral pathways) referral pathways and service mappings for these locations to provide safe referrals to the services. As part of the individual case management plans, CARE will also provide one-time cash assistance to support the GBV survivors, when deemed necessary according to the developed SOPs. Community members who need legal advice and/or need to attend legal information sessions will also be provided with legal support at the WGFSs. Women and girls of reproductive age, who fit into vulnerability criteria set up in line with UNFPA's guidance will also be provided with dignity kits to ensure they can maintain their dignity and mobility in a crisis context.

CARE will also additionally provide awareness raising sessions to raise awareness on key gender and protection topics, as well as gender equality through mobile teams and at the WGFSs. This will help to engage men and boys in the discussions. Similarly, CARE will lead on the primary prevention activities by engaging men and boys through structured curriculums such as EMAP and Program RA.

In order to ensure that the staff are well equipped to provide support to the communities, all frontline staff and community mobilizers will be trained in various topics including case management, PSS, GBV risk mitigation and GBV core concepts. CARE's previous and existing presence in the aforementioned locations, as well as GBV programming experience in these locations will help to ensure community buy-in and prevent backlash from the communities. 

CARE will partner with UNIDOR to implement CP activities to provide case management, PSS, referrals to support child GBV survivors.

project_name: ''VAINCR'' Venir en Aide aux Communautés à Risque et Survivant.e.s de VBG.
project_objective:
Ce projet s’articule autour d’une réponse multidimensionnelle qui intègre un renforcement des acteurs de première ligne et des structures de santé, un renforcement de la résilience des survivant.e.s  et des populations à risque de violence liées au genre (filles et garçons, hommes et femmes, dont celles.ceux handicapé.e.s), une participation accrue et inclusive de ces dernières à toutes les étapes de leur prise en charge, et le renforcement d’un environnement protecteur. Le renforcement des capacités des intervenants et l’amélioration de la capacité d’accueil des centres de santé permettront une prise en charge accrue et de qualité des survivant.e.s. L'amélioration de l’articulation des différentes interventions (via un appui au mécanismes de référencement des cas de VBG) conduira à une meilleure synergie d’action entre les acteurs intervenant sur le terrain :  acteurs de la société civiles, structures sociales dépendant du Ministère de la santé et du développement sociale et sanitaire, y compris ceux dans les « One Stop Center » soutenus par le FNUAP (Bamako, Mopti, Kolikoro). L’appui aux besoins de base, les sensibilisations et suivi des femmes et filles renforceront leur résilience et favoriseront une meilleure participation sociale de ces femmes à la vie communautaire. aussi, la participation des femmes et des filles à l’ensemble du processus de lutte contre les VBG permettra d’améliorer la pertinence, la qualité et l’efficacité de la réponse apportée dans la lutte contre les VBG . Ce projet a pour objectif de contribuer aux actions de prévalence contre les VBG et renforcer la résilience et l'inclusion des femmes, filles et personnes handicapées.
Les groupes cibles sont: les survivant.e.s de VBG; les populations à risque de VBG; les prestataires de soins; les élus et leaders communautaires, volontaires communautaires et groupement de femmes.

project_name: Saha wa Tarbia
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à améliorer la résilience des communautés des provinces du Lac, du Kanem et du Bahr El Gazel grâce à l’accès accru des populations, notamment des filles, des adolescentes et des femmes, à l’éducation et à la santé, et la capacité des acteurs communautaires à réduire les inégalités et à prévenir et gérer les conflits et les violences de façon inclusive. Le projet est structuré autour de trois volets :
-le renforcement de l'accès pour tous à une éducation inclusive de qualité dans un environnement sûr, protecteur et soutenant
-l'amélioration de l’accès équitable à des services et soins de santé de qualité, notamment en matière de DSSR et VBG pour les enfants, les adolescents, les femmes, y compris celles et ceux avec un handicap
-La promotion de l’inclusion des personnes vulnérables, l’égalité hommes-femmes et l’autonomisation des femmes, des adolescentes et des filles

Les groupes cibles sont le personnel éducatif et sanitaire (350 personnes, dont au moins 10% de femmes), les membres des structures de gestion APE/AME, COSAN et COGES (690 personnes, 30% de femmes), les fonctionnaires des services déconcentrés (140 personnes), les leaders, personnes ressources et OSC locales (475 personnes, dont 15% de femmes et 10% de personnes handicapées), les parents d’enfants/adolescents sensibilisés aux droits à l’éducation et SSR (50 000 personnes, dont 50% de femmes).

Les bénéficiaires directs sont 92 575 femmes en âge de procréer, 84 768 enfants de moins de 5 ans et  210 062 adolescents, jeunes et adultes (15 ans et plus) ayant accès aux services de SSR ; 12 000 enfants et adolescents (dont 50% de filles, et au moins 5% en situation de handicap) bénéficiant d’espaces d’apprentissage ; 97 170 enfants et adolescents (dont 50% de filles, et au moins 2% en situation de handicap) de 25 IPEP bénéficiant du renforcement de la qualité de l’enseignement pédagogique ; 500 adolescentes et femmes bénéficiant des dispositifs communautaires. Les bénéficiaires indirects représentent la totalité de la population de la zone d’intervention, soit  635 570 personnes (52% de femmes).

project_name: Improving access to  quality education services to IDPs, host communities, returnee children and adolescents affected by conflict and flood in Awerial, Pibor, Yei, Lainya and Kajokeji counties of Jonglei, Lakes and Central Equatoria states.
project_objective:
This is a twelve-month project to be implemented in Pibor, Awerial, Kajokeji, Lainya and Yei counties and designed to provide quality education to children especially adolescents girls and young women including those with disabilities, affected by flood, food insecurity and conflict. The intervention targets 14170 as direct beneficiaries (555F, 615M and 7000G, 6000B). Adult men and women targeted by this project are within the age range of 18-60 years while the school age going learners targeted are those between 3-17 years and out of this target, at least 15% of adults, youth and children will be People Living With Disabilities (based on the cluster recommendation), Young mothers, pregnant girls, orphaned children etc. 

The intervention will mainly focus on ECD, Primary and Alternative Education Program levels of learning in all targeted locations. In addition, the project is designed to create access of learners to schools, safe quality and inclusive learning centres while ensuring that barriers like poor access to schools, lack of scholastic materials, school retention for girls, WASH facilities etc. to children's education are addressed through community mobilization and sensitization as well as Back to learning campaigns. Also, the project will plan to improve the quality of education by building the capacity of teachers through continuous professional development tailored to improve their teaching skills. The project will further strengthen the capacity of local education authorities such as County and Payam Education Supervisors and Inspectors by training them on better skills of school supervision, report writings and how to develop strategic plans. This will improve the already ravaged systems in the counties and Payams to deliver quality education services to schools. Also the project shall distribute teaching and age-appropriate learning materials to both teachers and learners targeted since a lack of school supplies have been identified as one of the factors causing poor attendance and learning outcomes in schools. Moreover the project will create better learning environments in schools through construction of inclusive classes to cater for all learners including CWDs. Yet the program plans to renovate those schools that have been destroyed by conflict and floods to enable learners access education in targeted locations and also ensure that gender  segregated latrines and WASH facilities are established in schools lacking such facilities to address issues of girls hygiene while attending classes. But also this project will plan to equip targeted schools with C19 materials to prevent further spread of the pandemic among school going age children in addition to distribution of sanitary materials to adolescent girls alongside training them on MHM and SRHR issues to increase their school attendance. And finally, the project will form Roll Models in the community who shall engage community members on importance of education of children especially the girl child. This will be done in close coordination with the PTAs/SMC who will be trained on school development as well as community outreach activities with parents and guardians of school children and youth

project_name: Enhancing the Protection of Civilians and Resilience of Communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to enhance the protection of civilians and resilience of communities in South Sudan. Civilians throughout the country have been severely affected by the existing humanitarian crisis resulting from recurrent violence, insecurity, and natural disasters. To alleviate suffering and increase the protection and security of affected and vulnerable communities, NP will directly implement activities utilizing a participatory model that seeks to further build on local protection capacities, social cohesion, and resilience as well as prevent and respond to pertinent protection concerns. All project activities will be designed to best respond to the immediate security needs of beneficiaries and support the resilience, adaptive capacity, and recovery of communities from violent conflict, insecurity, and environment shocks utilizing NP’s Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) methodology. The project’s three programming components which will center upon: 1) General Protection 2) GBV and 3) Child protection.

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) will utilize a participatory approach in order to prevent and respond to protection needs, including gender-based violence (GBV) and Child Protection (CP) concerns. All project activities will be designed based on NP’s methodology of Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) to respond to the immediate protection needs of affected populations as well as support the resilience, adaptive capacity and recovery of communities from violent conflict and insecurity.

Project activities are implemented in both static locations, as well as through mobile response missions. NP also recognises the specific and unique needs of women, men, boys, girls, elderly and Persons with Disability (PwD). As such, NP has made use of the community feedback/information in the design of the proposed project. During project implementation, concerns of all community members will be captured and disaggregated by age, sex and PwD, and will be constantly reviewed to adapt the project.

project_name: Multisectoral humanitarian intervention for IDPs and vulnerable Host Communities in North Darfur and East Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to provide multi-sectorial emergency assistance in Eastern Sudan (Kassala/Gedaref/Red Sea) and North Darfur, through provision of WASH, FSL, Protection and Shelter/NFIs services. This project
also mainstreaming Covid-19 in all locations and protection activities focus on sensitization and awareness raising of key protection issues. This project mainly targets IDPs and vulnerable host communities members. In North Darfur and in Kassala the project interlinks with a BMZ project to operationalize the Triple NEXUS, while in Red Sea the project interlinks with SIDA resilience project. For FSL component targets group focused on Host Communities and IDPs in the Eastern Sudan and North Darfur. Small holder pastroralist and agropastoralist farmers will be targeted, using different criteria including vulnerabilities level. Women and youth will be prioritized for activities such as skills development training.

project_name: Projet d’amélioration de l’accès sécurisé à la sécurité alimentaire, à l’eau, assainissement et hygiènes et en protection des populations les plus vulnérables affectées par le déplacement dans la région de Mopti
project_objective: Le projet contribuera à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des ménages vulnérables affectés par le conflit dans la Région de Mopti à travers une réponse visant la sécurité alimentaire, l’eau, hygiène et assainissement et la protection. La présente action s'inscrit dans la continuité des activités déjà initiées par Oxfam dans la zone et en synergie avec les acteurs humanitaires. Cette action capitalisera sur ces résultats pour assurer une meilleure couverture de la réponse aux besoins des plus vulnérables. L'approche de la réponse adoptée vise non seulement à orienter les actions vers les besoins les plus cruciaux, mais aussi compléter d’autres projets en cours de mise en œuvre en visant 21 800 personnes, en particulier les ménages très pauvres et pauvres affectés par la crise, notamment déplacés internes, et les communautés hôtes. L'intervention permettra de renforcer la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages ciblés à travers des transferts monétaires inconditionnels pour contribuer au maintien d’une alimentation diversifiée en quantité suffisante au sein des ménages très pauvres abritant des individus à risque de malnutrition (enfants de -5 ans /FEFA). Face au contexte actuel au Mali - où il existe un risque que les besoins humanitaires actuels des communautés soient aggravés par la propagation de COVID-19 et d’autres épidémies comme le choléra, cette intervention visera à délivrer une réponse de santé publique, à travers le renforcement de l’accès continu, sécurisé et équitable à l’eau, assainissement et à la promotion de l’hygiène publique. Il s’agira aussi de mitiger les menaces de protection des personnes vulnérables réparties sur la zone d'intervention, en renforçant les capacités des communautés à identifier et adopter des mesures de protection, surtout les femmes et les filles, en contribuant ainsi à la lutte contre les Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG) et à la construction d’un environnement protecteur, à travers des efforts de plaidoyer.

project_name: Lifesaving and sustaining protection response services for vulnerable individuals in Khartoum, Gedaref, and Blue Nile
project_objective:
Specialized Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE) prevention and response services will be delivered to support women and girls at risk, such as elderly women, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, women and girls with disabilities, and female headed households (HHs) with minors in charge and without resources. The project will support the integration of reproductive health and WPE services so that gender-based violence (GBV) survivors can access safe and timely clinical care for the harmful health consequences - both physical and emotional. WPE staff integrated into health facilities will provide lifesaving GBV response services, including GBV case management and non-focused psycho-social support (PSS) to at-risk women and girls. At the same time, focused PSS sessions, recreational activities, and awareness-raising will be delivered through a Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS). The IRC will also bolster protection services by providing general and specialized GBV training sessions to internal and external actors, including GBV core concepts, referral pathways, disclosure and safe referrals and other and GBV trainings required to provide services for women and girls. 

The project will also deliver Child Protection (CP) services through the implementation of CP activities. The IRC will ensure that children are safe in their homes when they experience harm. This will be achieved by supporting children facing protection concerns to have access to quality services and a robust Child Protection response inclusive of case management and a Safe Healing and Learning Spaces (SHLS) where the IRC's Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) curriculum will be implemented. The IRC will also engage community members  to further mitigate potential risks for children and adolescents. At the core of the SHLS model is the SEL intervention, which follows a curriculum designed to strengthen five SEL competencies through lessons and games. The SHLS also serves as an entry point to identify children at risk and to refer them for specialized services, as well as supporting children receiving case management services. Case management services will be central to the child protection services provided. Through child-, family- and community focused strategies and coordinated case management service delivery mechanisms, the IRC will identify children at-risk of harm or who have experienced harm and will provide immediate support, ensuring the individual needs of children are assessed and addressed. Targeted children for case management include boys and girls who show signs of psychological distress, children who have experienced abuse and exploitation, unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) and children engaged in the worst forms of child labour.
