project_objective:
L’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en abris, articles ménagers essentiels pour couvrir les besoins immédiats mais aussi pour soutenir la mise en oeuvre de solutions durables au déplacement à travers la distribution de 4,500  kits d’Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME) complets, la distribution et la construction de 2,500 abris d’urgence et transitionnels, à travers une approche communautaire. L'OIM soutiendra égalemment un accès sûr et digne à un logement durable en briques, fabriquées à base de matières premières locales, pour 1,000 ménages des provinces du Lac et du Moyen Chari.       
                                                        
Toutes ces activités seront menées en étroite collaboration avec le Cluster. Des mécanismes de plainte seront mis en place pour accompagner toutes les activités de distribution et un suivi post-distribution sera mené afin de recueillir les feedbacks des bénéficiaires, notamment les personnes les plus vulnérables. Les résultats de ce suivi pourront être transmis au Cluster afin de tirer des leçons apprises.

L’OIM est un membre actif du Cluster abris et AME depuis ses débuts et est engagée dans toutes les discussions stratégiques récentes.

En 2021, l’OIM a pu assister à travers ses interventions en kits AME et abris plus de 23,000 individus dans les provinces du Lac, du Moyen Chari, de la Tandjilé et du Borkou.

project_name: WASH assistance and flood mitigation for vulnerable families and schools across Area C and the H2 area of Hebron, West Bank
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger (AAH) and the Rural Center for Sustainable Development (RCSD)’s proposed project in 2022 will target the most vulnerable families in Area C (including Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho, Jerusalem, Ramallah, and Tubas governorates) and in Hebron’s H2 area. These groups suffer from no, or limited, access to water and sanitation services due to Israeli restrictions on construction and development in the area, as well as the massive demolition and confiscation of WASH structures that took place during 2021 (51 structures according to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), 2022). This makes them particularly vulnerable to the threat of forced displacement. Further, the COVID-19 outbreak and its associated impacts, have added additional challenges to these communities to meet hygiene standards.

The 53 target communities, the majority of which are farming and herding families dependent on livestock and agricultural activities to maintain their livelihoods, heavily rely on water availability, quality, and affordability.
The lack of water has forced families to adopt negative coping mechanisms such as reducing their daily water consumption as stated in the WASH Vulnerability Map 2021, depending on unsafe water resources, or reducing their expenditure on basic needs such as health and education to afford the high cost of water.

In line with Strategic Objectives 1, 2 and 3, the project aims to:

1. Decrease target communities’ vulnerability and dependence on trucked water or unsafe sources of water by constructing and rehabilitating water networks, and household cisterns.
2. Improve communities’ access to sanitation facilities through the construction and provision of household WASH facilities such as latrines. Families often disregard these facilities and prioritize other basic needs such as food and water. This negative coping mechanism has left many households in poor health, hygiene, privacy, and dignity conditions, which are contributing to household members’ vulnerability to face hygiene related diseases.
3. Mitigate the risk of flooding during winter through the supply and installation of storm water systems for areas in serious needs. This will prevent target communities to experience further assets losses, displacement, and disrupted access to livelihoods services.
4. Increase hygiene awareness through trainings and workshops on subjects ranging from hygiene promotion to water saving techniques and cistern management, at both household and community levels.

All these activities will mitigate the effects of the Israeli occupation on water access and thus improve the target communities’ livelihood prospects. The project will reduce the exposure to forced displacement of an estimated 158,308 people (39,047men, 37,585 women, 41,657 boys, 40,019 girls, and 2,253 PWD) and provide them with the means to show resilience in the face of the aforementioned challenges.

The proposed project is guided by AAH Gender and Protection policy and AAH staff endeavor to consider safety and dignity in the design and implementation of all humanitarian interventions. Accountability and participation will be ensured through a detailed Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) framework specifically developed to ensure that beneficiary selection is conducted in a transparent and accountable manner and through applying AAH’s thorough Feedback and Complaint Mechanism to guarantee the inclusion of communities’ suggestions into the project. AAH seeks to achieve equal and impartial access to vulnerable populations, aiming for all community members to be involved and consulted as much as possible including through community consultations and focus groups to further achieve beneficiaries’ empowerment and sustainability beyond the project’s lifetime.

project_name: Prevention of the forcible transfer of Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem through humanitarian assistance and evidence-based advocacy
project_objective:
This multi-sector Project will support the West Bank Protection Consortium (the Consortium) to deliver assistance to 32,007 Palestinians at risk of forcible transfer in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem due to recurrent violations of international law. Building on previous risks and vulnerability analyzes, the Action addresses the protection needs of persons and communities of concern through a multi-sectoral approach that reduces vulnerabilities, builds capacities and responds to threats. 
Specifically, the Project aims at: (1) preventing and responding to protection incidents  (demolitions, settler-related, military operations) with emergency assistance (cash and in-kind) and protective measures (RESPONSIVE ACTIVITIES); (2) mitigating protection risks for highly vulnerable communities (150) through synergizing community-based protection, the provision of basic and social infrastructure, legal aid and stakeholder mobilization, including mitigating the risk of Covid-19 through the delivery of WASH and health infrastructure, and hygiene and RCCE awareness materials (REMEDIAL ACTIVITIES); and (3) promoting increased respect for IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations through coalition advocacy undertaken with Third States, International Organizations, Palestinian authorities and media outlets (ENVIRONMENT-BUILDING ACTIVITIES).
Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Policy Framework and facilitates coordination with other actors addressing the humanitarian and protection needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers for demolitions and settler-related incidents. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSL, legal aid and emergency responses and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs.  Consequently, the Project is envisaged to contribute to the realization of the following HRP objectives: 1. Increased respect for International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL) and accountability for violations; 2. Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence.
Implementing partners will also submit projects as individual agencies, which will include some of the same activities (including legal aid services; shelter upgrades, WASH and other projects). Some of these projects will complement this Project’s assistance, but will respond to a logic of ‘contiguity’ rather than ‘continuity’, since they are informed by different rationales and approaches. For this reason, financial resources will be kept separated. Our planning, monitoring and reporting systems prevent any duplication.

project_name: Support vulnerable population to improve access to basic WASH services in Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
The proposed Action Against Hunger (AAH) response to be implemented in 2022 across the Gaza Strip are aligned with HRP 2022 Strategic Objectives 2 and 3 as well as the WASH Cluster Objectives 2 and 3.
AAH interventions aim to support vulnerable families (including women, men, girls and boys, elderly and people with disability and specific needs) to have safe access to WASH facilities in public facilities (health care facilities (HCF) and schools) as well as the unconnected communities depending on cesspits to discharge their wastewater, and families prone to stormwater floods in three communities of the North Gaza. 
Through connecting households of the Maan, Alstar and Jawrat Alluwt communities to an adequate wastewater drainage system, and other three communities of North Gaza (Jabalia and Biet Lahia) through stormwater drainage systems, all women, men, girls and boys will be protected from being in contact with flooded stormwater or wastewater during the winter season due to the accumulation of stormwater in the cesspits flooding in the streets, in hospitals and schools. This will further help prevent the risk of infections and diseases from flooded wastewater and other health-related issues. 
By improving access to sanitation facilities in public places and communities alongside the hygiene awareness campaign developed with the communities, AAH hopes to improve the communities’ hygiene practices, provide a safe environment and reduce public health risks for all of the community members, women and girls in particular.
The public awareness campaign will target the vulnerable communities and spread messages on the proper use of the WASH facilities at households, schools, hospitals and HCF, in addition to safe water handling and improving the capacity of families in targeted areas to address hygiene practice issues at household level. This awareness campaign will be developed using the communication with communities methodology and will include information on COVID-19 mitigation measures, to contribute to the efforts in limiting the spread of the pandemic in the Gaza Strip. Orientation sessions, initiatives and IEC materials will be conducted by AAH staff to the targeted women, men, boys, girls, elderly and people with disabilities.
A communication plan with communities will be developed at the beginning of the project to ensure proper community engagement at all stages of project implementation. The plan will take into account different groups within the targeted communities, women, men, boys and girls and PWDs. AAH aims to enhance community ownership and active participation from the community, in addition to improving communities’ access and trust to AAH’s Feedback and Complaint Mechanism channels. 
The proposed intervention is guided by the AAH Gender and Protection policy and AAH staff endeavor to streamline safety and dignity in all humanitarian interventions. Accountability and participation will be ensured through interviews and focus group discussions and through applying AAH’s thorough Feedback and Complaint Mechanism.

project_name: Improving WASH Services in to Vulnerable Communities in Gaza
project_objective:
“ Improving Wash Services in Vulnerable Communities in Gaza” is a 12-month project designed to address the WASH needs of vulnerable communities in several areas in Deir Al-Balah and Khan Younis, and respond to the objectives of the WASH cluster, specifically Objective 2: Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians, and Objective 3: Strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacity to the most vulnerable Palestinians to reduce threats and cope with emergencies and shocks.
Vulnerable communities in targeted areas suffer from 1. Inadequate wastewater and HH connections in Khan Younis, 2. Undersized and deteriorated water networks in Deit Al-Balah, 3. Flooding risks at the Shaat Lagoon in Khan Younis, and 4. The lack of hygiene awareness. All these issue represent a physical, environmental, and health risks to the community, including pollution, the spread of diseases and bacterial infections, limitations to movement and conducting daily activities such as work and education, all which add to the enormous challenges faced in these targeted communities that already suffer from poverty and deteriorated living conditions.
The needs of the project were identified in coordination with the Coastal Municipal Water Utility (CMWU), and are planned to improve the lives of over 109,500 beneficiaries, including women, men, boys, girls, people with disabilities, and elders.
Anera will implement this project in coordination with its partner, Bayader for Environment and Development Association (Bayader), to ensure safe and sustainable access to water and sanitation and the reduced risk of flooding and contamination in vulnerable communities in Gaza by improving community-level infrastructure and promoting hygiene practices. The response will be delivered through the following activities:
1. Installation/extension/rehabilitation of sewer collection network and HH connections: Construction of wastewater networks and HH connections at different areas in Khanyounis City to prevent contamination of domestic water and decrease waterborne illnesses by mitigating sewage flooding. 
2. Installation/ rehabilitation of water transmission pipelines, networks and HH connections: Rehabilitation and expansion of water networks at different locations in Dair Al Balah to decrease the loss of domestic water and increase the overall efficiency of the water network leading to less degradation of the system and loss of household water over time, whcih will improve access to safe drinking and domestic water to more than 30,000 beneficiaries.
3. Installation of household flood mitigation measures: Rehabilitation of Shaat lagoon including constructing boreholes in Khan Younis to enhance flood mitigation measures and increase the efficiency of the lagoon, to protect more than 35,000 people from flooding risks.
4. Hygiene promotion awareness campaigns: community-level hygiene awareness workshops to create a sustainable positive impact on community health and encourage hygiene practices on the household level to prevent diseases and infections. 
The project ensures the inclusion of all community members in targeted area, including all age and gender groups and PWDs, and focuses on enhancing the living conditions, safety and access to WASH services to all groups at the community and household levels. The project, specifically through the hygiene awareness campaigns, will include all household members with focus on women, which will increase the role of household members in supporting women in applying hygiene practices at home. It will also increase the awareness of children, and enhance their safety from water borne diseases or flooding risks.

project_name: Comprehensive WASH and protection support to vulnerable households, underserved public health care facilities, schools and solid waste service providers in Gaza
project_objective:
The action, based on the WC vulnerability map, the WC comprehensive assessment in HCFs that involved CESVI and ACTED, consultations carried out with key stakeholders (WC, PWA, MoE, North Gaza JSC), targets the HRP2022 WASH specific objective 2 “Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians” and focuses on:
-WASH and Protection support in HHs
The project targets 800 vulnerable HHs (4,600 individuals) in North Gaza, Deir Al Balah, Khan Younis, Rafah Governorates.
Thanks to the consolidated experience from recent projects, ACTED and CESVI in collaboration with YEC and Beit Lahiya Development Association are proposing to scale up activities for vulnerable HHs and enlarge the access to water, by ensuring increased water storage capacity and improving sanitation facilities. Improving access to safe water for drinking and hygienic use prevents further deterioration of HHs’ living and health conditions, enhances protection against inadequate WASH facilities and exposure to nutrition risks, limits negative coping mechanisms (e.g. water purchase from unreliable vendors, using open spaces as toilets). CESVI has developed strong expertise in WASH (previous/ongoing projects in Hebron and Gaza in partnership with ACTED for adequate access to water). YEC has proven experience in implementing WASH programs (access to services for fragile families, human and protection assistance, hygiene kits distribution, awareness raising). The project design has been coordinated with relevant stakeholders (WC, PWA, MoSD) and simultaneously addresses urgent needs of vulnerable populations while endowing them with proper WASH systems.
-WASH support in public institutions (HCFs and schools)
CESVI and ACTED have direct knowledge about WASH-related risks and needs affecting these institutions and thanks to previous projects in Hebron in partnership with UNICEF, gained relevant experience in improving WASH facilities in HCFs and schools.
The project proposes rehabilitation interventions of WASH facilities in 11 schools (in Gaza, Deir Al Balah and Khan Younis Governorates) and 3 HCFs (in Deir Al Balah and Rafah Governorates).
This component is deemed extremely important in view of the worsened impact due to lack of improved WASH facilities and related health risks in the frame of the Covid19 pandemic. Public places like HCFs and schools are strongly exposed to the risk of contamination, due to the high turnover of users and visitors, if not equipped with proper WASH and sanitation facilities, also in consideration that they serve brackets of population already vulnerable per se (sick people, children).
The activity is implemented directly by CESVI and ACTED with the approach adopted for interventions at HH level. The specific expertise combined with close relationships with relevant authorities (MoE and MoH), results in assessments pre-identifying necessary and specific interventions in each facility.
-Support for Waste service providers
The project supports service providers in 8 Municipalities in North Gaza Governorate, supplying 200 containers to improve the capacity and the environmental situation of existing collection points, and 300 kits with PPE and working tools for the workers to improve working conditions.The project is supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA)      with specific focus on the most vulnerable groups, including women, girls, boys, the disabled and the elderly. Gender principles are mainstreamed throughout the entire action and CBPCs are trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases such as GBV with a particular focus on women and children. Finally, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) is core to the proposed Action.

project_name: Improving access to adequate WASH services for most vulnerable schools and health clinics in Area C from the Jericho and Jerusalem Governorates of the West Bank
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims to contribute to reduction of WASH vulnerability in marginalized communities through improving access to equitable, sustainable, and safely managed WASH services in institutions with a particular focus on Schools and Health clinics in the governorates of Jericho and East Jerusalem. 
The intervention components respond to the 2022 HRP SO2, in addition the WASH cluster Objective 2 through its tailored approach to enhancing WASH infrastructure and resources in institutions and target group responsive promotion of hygiene awareness and promotion with particular relevance to the ongoing COVID pandemic. Further, the intervention  is also in line with SDG 6 “Ensure access to water and sanitation for all”

The intervention will achieve the aforementioned through two main components that respond directly to the identified WASH Cluster priority ” improve access to WASH Services in institutions”  ensuring equitable and dignified access for most vulnerable community groups with a particular focus on PWDs, children and females across 33 vulnerable communities located in the governorates of Jericho ( Jordan Valley) and East Jerusalem 
In particular, MA’AN and WeWorld-GVC are  proposing to  improve WASH facilities and capacities in 62 WASH vulnerable  institutions benefiting in total 247,604 direct beneficiaries (40,578 boys, 38,360  girls, 86,068 men, 82,598 women, of which 3,060 PWDs and 6,323 elderly ) in 33  communities the Governorates of Jerusalem and Jericho, mainly in Area C (72%), and Area A/B (28%).  through:

i)Rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools (handwashing, latrines, sewer system) in coordination with and accordance to MoE standards, targeting 31 schools  (9 Jericho Governorate, 22  East Jerusalem) located in 16 communities of the West Bank in the Governorates of Jerusalem and Jericho.

ii)Conduct hygiene awareness campaigns in targeted schools in partnership with MoE health units to promote hygiene and sanitation practices with gender and protection mainstreaming. 

 iii) Tailored Rehabilitation of  WASH facilities in health clinics/HCFs (handwashing, latrines, sewer system), targeting 31 highly vulnerable Health care facilities (5 Jericho Governorate, 26 East Jerusalem) located in 29 communities of the West Bank in the Governorates of Jerusalem and Jericho.

iv) The provision of environmental and personal cleaning kits for the 31 targeted HCFs 
v)conduct trainings for clinics staff on promotion of hygiene practices to patients and protection guidelines including PSEA.
All proposed activities will ensure protection principles on safety and dignity, meaningful access, accountability, participation, empowerment and claiming of rights.

The intervention has been proposed based on coordinated efforts to complement current WASH aid actors proposed and ongoing interventions to ensure comprehensive contribution to reduction in overall WASH vulnerability amongst marginalized and prioritized communities. and  complements another initiative submitted by UNICEF for the purposes of the HRP 2022 integrated intervention of WASH in school and WASH in Health . Further, the intervention has been coordinated and endorsed by the MoH, MoE and the WASH Cluster. The project is in line with the MOH Strategic Plan (2021-25), The proposed activities were selected upon the WASH Cluster eligible interventions for HRP 2022, based on WASH 2021 community and institutions vulnerability assessments. 

MA’AN and WW-GVC ensure that all the proposed interventions will trigger a positive effect on the reduction of the WASH vulnerability, increasing the protection and the  resilience of the communities and institutions under threat of forcible transfer in Area C including PSEA promotion and messaging. Moreover, the intervention  would enhance the protection of the communities and institutions, supporting preparedness and response on combating COVID-19 outbreak direct and indirect effects.

project_name: Improve access to WASH services for the West Bank vulnerable and under-served Communities
project_objective:
This proposal is in line with the objectives and the framework of the OPTI country 2022 HRP strategy under objective 1: The rights of Palestinians living under occupation, including those living under the blockade and other restrictions, are protected, respected and promoted in accordance with International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL), while duty-bearers are increasingly held to account and objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL. Furthermore, this project is aligned to the WASH cluster HRP Objective 1: In accordance with international humanitarian law (IHL) and international human rights law (IHRL), Palestinians living under occupation access safe and adequate WASH services with dignity and objective 2: Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinian.
 The overall objective is to contribute to strengthening the capacity of essential WASH services for the vulnerable population threatened by the ongoing Covid-19 crisis in the West Bank, while the specific objective of the project is to provide an appropriate, integrated WASH response for Deir al 'Asal al Fauqa vulnerable village located in area C of Dura community in the West Bank to mitigate the insufficient access to WASH services that impacted women, children, girls and boys. The objectives are in line with the needs identified in the humanitarian need overview (HNO) and Oxfam's recent assessments.

project_name: Improving Governance and Access to WASH services in West Bank
project_objective:
The project aims at securing sufficient and safe drinking water quantities for 1,655 households (7,628 individuals) of the targeted communities and families living in Area “B” and “C” of the West Bank for household purposes, including 3,748 women and girls in two locations namely in Jammala and Rujeib in Ramallah and Nablus Governorates respectively, in addition it aims at improving WASH conditions in 10 public schools in Nablus Governorate serving 3,087 students (1,753 males and 1,334 females). The project also aims to improve WASH governance in cooperation with the Water Sector Regulatory Council (WSRC) in collecting specific WASH data from 270 WASH service providers in the West Bank. This data will provide updates for preidentified vulnerability indicators such as water consumption, water price, water quality, wastewater management…etc. Such indicators will allow the humanitarian and development actors to develop their WASH programs to respond to critical WASH vulnerabilities. In total, this project directly serves more than 10,715 inhabitants (5,633 males and 5,082 females) 188 persons out of them are with disabilities, on other hand, more than 2,980,808 persons will be indirectly benefited as a result of conducting early warning indicators assessment in the West Bank.
The initiative responds to needs highlighted in the WASH 2021 HNO and it is also fully in line with the oPt. Response plan, contributing to the WASH Cluster Objective 2: Ensure equitable, affordable, and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians communities as well as contributing to WASH Cluster Objective 3: Strengthen WASH preparedness and response capacity to the most vulnerable Palestinians to reduce threats and cope with emergencies and shocks. Access to safe WASH service is a main concern in the West Bank, where according to WSRC more than 500,000 Palestinians in the West Bank are receiving less than 50 l/c/d through the piped water service and according to PCBS more than 60% of the households in the West Bank are not connected to sewer services.
Proposed interventions and priorities were coordinated with WASH cluster coordination team, area focal points, technical focal points and governmental counterpart focal points, the initiatives have been endorsed by PWA, WSRC and MoE, it is in line with the PWA Strategic Plan (2017-22) and in compliance with the Water Master Plan for Area C. The action is in line with the Sustainable Development Goals, specifically contributing with “Goal 6: Ensure access to water and sanitation for all”.
Further, the initiative allows to reduce and more effectively address the core vulnerabilities of communities and educational institutions in need, improving WASH services for unconnected and underserved communities in area “C” and “B” of the West Bank, precisely in Jammala in Ramallah Governorate, Rujeib and 10 public schools in Nablus Governorate as well as improving WASH sector governance in West Bank communities.

project_name: Provision of WASH response for vulnerable households and communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
As a result of the lack of effective maintenance and the aging WASH infrastructure due to the prolonged closure and repeated escalation of hostilities, the Gaza Strip has seen a significant deterioration in WASH services. Although the coverage of water supply and sanitation services exceeds 90% overall, significant disparities exist, and the service itself is both irregular and below standards. This often leads to vulnerable households seeking alternatives, particularly for drinking water that is often expensive and of quality below the WHO standards. Access to sanitation services, especially outside the urban areas, remains a major challenge in terms of coverage and quality of service, especially for women and girls and people with disabilities. 

UNICEF and its partners will undertake actions to address the urgent needs of the population of the Gaza Strip as outlined in the humanitarian needs overview for 2022. UNICEF and partners will focus on increasing access to WASH services among the most vulnerable communities and institutions by restoring, sustaining, and expanding coverage to reach the most vulnerable populations with a clear multisectoral approach and build on the humanitarian-development nexus. This project will ensure that the most vulnerable women, children, and men have sufficient domestic and drinking water storage capacity whenever it becomes available and have better access to safe water and sanitation facilities and services. UNICEF and the partners will also address the systemic gaps in humanitarian needs, especially targeting female-headed households, including widows. UNICEF also discussed with its partners the importance of having the voice of the participating communities heard and receiving their feedback. UNICEF is strengthening Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) in programmes by systematizing commitments in agreements with all implementing partners, including complaint mechanisms. The proposed activities will take into consideration the special needs of women and girls – for example:  design of sanitation facilities with specific attention paid to location, safety and protection, and those families and children targeted through e-vouchers and the Child Sensitive Cash Support in Gaza implemented by UNICEF, focusing on the most vulnerable families. Furthermore, this proposal aims to strengthen the WASH partners' capacity to better prepare and respond to potential seasonal flooding, which is expected to be the worse in 2022 due to the impact of the May 2021 escalation of hostilities. As part of the UNICEF framework on Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and for the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), the office had designated two complaints handlers.

Therefore, this project aims to improve access to basic life-saving WASH services for 238,000 people, especially among vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip. The project will address the negative coping strategies employed by vulnerable, such as reducing the frequency and duration of handwashing, sharing sanitation facilities, and overcrowding at public water points, due to limited or lack of access to water supply and sanitation facilities, engaged in resulting from the lack of access to WASH services. These coping strategies undermine infection prevention and lead to increased COVID-19 community transmission and other public health and social, economic consequences, coordinated with other key areas such as child protection, health, and education. Additionally, the project will cover advocacy tasks for the limited technical and financial capacities of the WASH service providers.

project_name: Improving WASH and health services in health facilities at Al-Nasser Medical Compound in Gaza governorate and at household level in Deir Al Balah governorate contributing to combat COVID-19
project_objective: Strengthening the WASH and health services and preparedness of Health Care Facilities (HCFs) and improving under-served communities' access to adequate water and sanitation services, are considered extremely urgent needs in Gaza Strip, supporting resilience building and facing the protracted threats and chronic vulnerability. This project is aligned with the HRP Strategic Objectives 1 and 2, complementing WASH cluster objectives 1 and 2, and Health Cluster objective 2, as well as contributing to the achievement of SDG 6. The project also responds to UNICEF strategy 2016-2030, for which “every HCF should have safely managed reliable water, sanitation, hygiene facilities, and practices that meet staff and patient needs by 2030”. The project is in line with the PWA Strategic Plan (2017-22) and MOH (2021-25), implementing the National WASH standards for health facilities (UNICEF/WWGVC 2021). Improved WASH services in HCFs are considered as necessary inputs to be prioritized for achieving all global and national health goals, especially those linked to Universal Health Coverage (SDG 3), and the specific target 3.9 “to reduce the burden of disease from unsafe water, sanitation, and lack of hygiene” and 3.1 and 3.2 “call for reducing maternal mortality and under-five and neonatal mortality”. Effective sanitation, hygiene, and infection prevention and control (IPC) measures are one of the five objectives of the WHO Global Action Plan on antimicrobial resistance.  WeWorld-GVC (WW-GVC), in partnership with Qatar Red Crescent Society (QRCS), aims to enhance the resilience, protection, and dignity of the most vulnerable people in GS. The general objective of the project is to increase the efficiency, predictability, and availability, and accessibility of WASH and health services in health institutions and communities, contributing to mitigating the impact of COVID-19 and other infectious diseases. The needs and interventions were coordinated with and endorsed by the Ministry of Health (MoH), WASH and Health Cluster, Coastal Municipalities Water Utility (CMWU), and the Palestinian Water Authority (PWA). The first specific objective of the proposed intervention is to enhance the access to WASH and Health quality services for Al Nasser medical compound in Gaza City, implementing sustainable improvement in the WASH infrastructure (construction/ rehabilitation of WASH facilities in HCFs - handwashing, latrines, sewer system) and in the quality of health services (hygiene material, medical and protective equipment supply, monitoring tools) for three HCFs: 1) Al Nasser pediatric hospital (NPH), 2) Rantissi specialized hospital (RSH) 3) Ophthalmic hospital (OH), benefitting an average 280,000 people served by the three hospitals annually (data: health cluster HeRAMS Dashboard), specifically  53,000 girls, 55,000 boys, 85,000 women, and 87,000 men including 12320 elders, including 2800 PWD, as well as contributing to improving the public health conditions of more than 652,597 living in the target area.  Therefore, the second specific objective of the proposed intervention is to ensure access to adequate water and sanitation services at HouseHold (HHs) level in Middle Area Governorate, particularly targeting 322 unconnected households (HHs) of two unserved communities, Al’Ansar (Al Musaddarc locality) and Block 8 (Al Buriej locality), through the installation/ rehabilitation of water transmission pipelines, networks, and HH connections, and the installation/extension/rehabilitation of sewer collection network and HH connections, connecting 1,535 vulnerable individuals (392 boys, 374 girls, 359 men, 362 women, 21 elders men, and 27 elders women, including 15 PWD).

project_name: Improving access to WASH services in schools located in area C
project_objective:
The main objective of this proposed project is improving WASH services in 50 schools located in area C in Hebron, Bethlehem, Salfeet, Nablus, Tubas, Jericho, and Jenin governorates. The project's contributed to SO#2 and corresponds with WASH cluster Objective # 2; Ensure equitable, affordable, and sustainable safely managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians. This project is designed to be implemented by World Vision and in partnership with the Palestinian Hydrological Group (PHG). It’s composed of two main components; First, improving WASH services of 50 schools through decreasing the gap between available facilities based on MoE standards, while accommodating the needs of the Children with Disability (CWD). This will be achieved by rehabilitating and increasing
the number of available latrines and drinking fountains to cover the number and be sufficient to both genders and various age groups and CWD (especially for schools accommodating primary and secondary age students).  Meeting the needs of the Children with Disability (CWD) is an integral part of the project, taking into consideration their gender needs, where activities will be intentionally designed to accommodate their needs to increase their access to services and information and participation including infrastructural work (sanitary units and water fountains), awareness on WASH practices (hygiene practices) and the rest of the activities.

Secondly, in parallel with the infrastructural works, capacity building and awareness sessions for all target school students (the 12800 girls and 16192 boys students) as well as teachers in charge of school health committees will take place in a creative and tailored manner so that to uplift the current hygienic practices so that to ensure that children and schools are protected through the improved hygienic situation in their daily lives. Protection measures will be integrated into the capacity building programs by considering the basic needs of girls, young boys, and people with disabilities to have safe access to the WASH services in their respective schools The overall project will be monitored at different levels, at the national level, the Ministry of Education-School Health department will be updated on a quarterly basis about the project implementation and its impact. At Governorates levels, Directorates of Education will be kept in constant communications
by the respective implementation staff. Locally, the village committee in each locality (as explored below) and Child Health Committee at schools will monitor and lead the implementation of activities so that to guarantee, relevance, compatibility, and impact realized

project_name: Emergency interventions to improve access to basic WASH services for the most vulnerable unserved communities in the West Bank
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve access to safe water and sanitation services for the most vulnerable communities and families, including children, in Area C in the West Bank. The interventions will contribute to reducing the targeted communities WASH vulnerability with a focus on children and persons with disabilities (PWD), especially females, as they are considered the most vulnerable and more in need of these critical services. Also, the interventions will target unserved and underserved communities with essential WASH servicers protecting the most vulnerable families under threat of forcible transfer. The interventions will focus on improving the communities’ access to 1) adequate and safely managed water services; 2) sanitation and sewer services and 3) WASH facilities in schools and health facilities; 4) safe and adequate water in underserved communities, including schools and health facilities; 5)  increase the storage capacity of the unconnected households. All interventions will be implemented in parallel with the provision of hygiene materials and hygiene awareness sessions in schools, health centres and communities.

 The project interventions were developed based on WASH cluster eligible actions for HRP 2022 and targeting the most vulnerable communities according to WASH 2020/2021 vulnerability mapping. 
UNICEF and its partners will adopt several implementation methodologies that consider the targeted communities’ locations, proposed response technical standards, and UNICEF’s accessibility and partners to these communities. Therefore, UNICEF and the partners will adopt and consider beneficiary/community implementation mechanisms for household interventions such as construction/rehabilitation of household WASH facilities and cisterns. Implementation through suppliers/contractors will be adopted for WASH facilities in schools , health care centers and water community water infrastructures activity. 

Moreover, the proposed interventions will consider the targeted groups’ socioeconomic, protection and COVID-19-related  vulnerabilities. UNICEF will target the communities under the risk of demolition and forcible transfer in Area C, the families under the poverty line, and the communities highly affected by the COVID-19 outbreak. The proposed interventions will improve the targeted groups’ capacities and resilience to deal with the aforementioned challenges. 

UNICEF and its partners will carefully consider the special and persistent needs of women, children, elders and PWD. Thus, these vulnerable groups will be consulted during the planning, design, and implementation of the interventions. Also proposing sufficient response of these groups that consider the different social and traditional characteristics in the targeted communities.  UNICEF and its partners have developed a complain system and tools.   UNICEF is strengthening Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) in program by systematizing commitments in agreements with all implementing partners. UNICEF supports the partner in strengthening and mainstreaming systems for  Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and AAP in their strategies. It provides training on PSEA and AAP approaches, particularly on community engagement, complaints system, and feedback mechanisms. UNICEF has also initiated a new project to digitalize AAP-PSEA mechanisms in the country office. As part of the UNICEF framework on AAP &PSEA the office had designated two complaints handlers. The complaint email address, in addition to the Interagency Hotline (managed by WFP), will be promoted as community feedback channels to reflect the views of marginalized populations, including stakeholders and partners throughout the program design cycle to feed the information received from beneficiaries back into programme and ultimately encourage community engagement .

project_name: Provision of WASH Services to at-risk Communities in various areas in Gaza and Deir Al Balah Governorates
project_objective:
This proposed project aims to improve access of 34,000 persons, comprised of 9,588 men, 9,418 women, 7,718 boys, 7,276 girls, 1,147 senior citizens and 952 persons with disability, to WASH services in underdeveloped communities which lack WASH services and have been affected by the May 2021 escalations, specifically in eastern Buraij area, Deir Al Balah Governorate, and south of Gaza, Gaza Governorate. The project comes as a direct response to the humanitarian needs of those two regions as the escalations hasn’t only damaged the water and wastewater infrastructure there, but also added further shocks to those areas which require not only the rehabilitating of the escalation-damaged networks, but also expand the works to accommodate to the actual needs of those communities; according to the joint needs assessment conducted with the CMWU, 31,000 and 1,500 people do not have basic access to safe wastewater disposal services at southern Gaza and Al Buraij respectively, knowing that some of those areas has been suffering from the lack of reliable wastewater disposal services for over 15 years. Moreover, around 3,000 persons have no access to safe potable water supply due to the deterioration and damages sustained by the domestic water networks, knowing that the water networks at Al Buraij area are still made of steel and need to be replaces with UPVC pipes. Additionally, 2,000 persons suffer every year from floods caused by improper storm water collection and disposal/injection infrastructure. 
The project will not only rehabilitate damaged WASH infrastructure in the aforementioned areas, but will provide safe access to reliable and efficient WASH services to 34,000 persons in the aforementioned regions. The interventions planned for the aforementioned areas will provide:
1-	Supplying and installing 1,400 and 4,700-meter, PVC wastewater communal carrier lines in Al Buraij and Gaza respectively with diameters of 160, 200, 250 and 300 mm. the works will include the vacuuming of existing septic tanks/cesspits and filling it with sand to avoid the formation of sinkholes which would damage people and property in addition to installing manholes and household connections for around 1600 households.
2-	Supplying and installing UPVC potable water networks at Al Buraij serving around 550 households while replacing the 25-year-old damaged steel carrier lines in addition to installing new household connections under the direct supervision of the CMWU.
3-	Establishing a storm water collection and evacuation infrastructure to protect 2,000 persons from winter floods. The implementation will include gutters, manholes and 350-m long PVC carrier line.
Furthermore, the interventions in those areas will also include WASH awareness campaigns to:
i-	Introduce the project and its importance/impact on the target areas.
ii-	Provide awareness regarding water conservation and sound hygiene practices (including best practices and alerting to negative practices such as flushing diapers and napkins down the toilet).
iii-	Increase awareness towards COVID-19 related hygiene practices in line with SOP’s published internationally via the WHO and adopted by governmental and UNRWA institutions. 
iv-	Distribution of hygiene kits designed to accommodate the needs of all family members based on gender, age, and ability/disability conditions. The kits will also include COVID-19 protective kits, including face masks, latex gloves and 70% rubbing alcohol per WHO and MOH guidelines.
Once completed, the expected impact of the planed interventions will include:
1-	Replacing and rehabilitating WASH infrastructure damaged during the May 2021 military escalations.
2-	Reducing aquifer/groundwater contamination as a result to damaged wastewater infrastructure and the use of septic tanks/cesspits.
3-	Promoting safe hygiene practices, water conservation and containing the spread of COVID-19 among 1600 households located at Eastern Al Buraij and Southern Gaza.

project_name: Food Assistance for Training in Libya
project_objective:
Libya’s economy has been decimated by conflict and instability over the past decade, with many years witnessing a contraction of the economy. While there was positive growth between 2017 and 2019, the impact of COVID-19 and the 11-month blockade of oil facilities resulted in negative growth of -31.3 per cent in 2020 to US$ 37.8 billion.  The annual growth rate of GDP employed person also declined from 24 per cent in 2017 to -20.7 per cent in 2019. Poor economic performance has also had negative consequences for employment opportunities. Total labour force participation (ages 15—64) has been steadily increasing over the past decades, reaching 52.8 per cent in 2019, although the rate of increase has slowed in recent years.  However, the participation rate for women stood at just 36.5 per cent in 2019 compared to 68.8 per cent for men. 

With Libya in a state of protracted conflict and in a fragile context, WFP aims to expand the life-changing programmes that would support the resilience of vulnerable communities across Libya, while addressing the immediate humanitarian needs with the life-saving assistance. 

The reduction in available migrant labour, both skilled and unskilled, combined with the instability of Government salaries and the impact of COVID-19 pandemics, has left many Libyan households reliant on coping mechanisms in order to meet their basic food needs. In this context, WFP Libya will continuously scale up the Food Assistance for Training projects, matching people in need with livelihoods and business skills and eventually decent works in the local job markets. 

Conditional food assistance will be provided to the project participants and their household members as long as minimum attendance requirements are met, giving an immediate boost to food security. After the training, if successful, food security levels should be improved, with less reliance on coping strategies. Household resilience to future shocks should also be improved due to an improved asset base through greater skills, tools, and savings.

project_name: FOURNIR ET AMELIORER L’ASSISTANCE HUMANITAIRE EN SANTE ET LE BIEN-ETRE ECONOMIQUE AUX POPULATIONS TOUCHEES PAR LES URGENCES DANS LA PROVINCE DU LAC TCHAD
project_objective:
Conformément aux priorités du HRP 2021, le programme ciblera les personnes les plus vulnérables affectées par le conflit et le déplacement au sein des communautés de déplacés internes, de réfugiés et d'hôtes, avec une inclusion spécifique des enfants, des femmes et des adolescentes les plus à risque, dans les zones difficiles à atteindre telles que celles proches des rives du lac qui sont en première ligne des attaques du NSAG, en particulier dans les départements de Fouli et de Kaya. Ce programme, aligné sur le SAP de l'IRC au Tchad (qui doit être finalisé d'ici novembre 2021), se concentrera sur trois des principaux domaines de résultats de l'IRC : la sécurité, la santé et le bien-être économique. La flexibilité de la PBA permettra à l'IRC de répondre aux futures lacunes de financement anticipées dans certains sites de la province du Lac, en minimisant les lacunes et en maintenant le soutien aux populations les plus vulnérables. IRC adoptera une approche centrée sur les survivants afin d'accroître l'accès à des services complets de lutte contre la VBG, qui seront intégrés aux services de santé pour des références de qualité, et aux activités de bien-être économique par la distribution du cash pour soutenir le démarrage d'une activité génératrice de revenus (AGR) pour les survivants et les femmes à risque. Les activités amélioreront l'accès à des soins de santé primaires de qualité en mettant l'accent sur la santé infantile et l'accès aux services de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) ; elles intensifieront le programme de nutrition existant en fournissant des services de prévention de la malnutrition aiguë au niveau communautaire et le traitement de la malnutrition dans les centres et postes de santé. L'IRC continuera à se concentrer sur le rétablissement des moyens de subsistance par le biais de la double approche du porte-monnaie électronique afin d'aider les ménages les plus vulnérables à satisfaire leurs besoins fondamentaux. Les principaux résultats comprendront également la création de groupes VSLA et la production de légumes écologiques dans le but de permettre aux femmes de retrouver leurs moyens de production, en les reliant également au développement de la petite enfance (DPE). Les activités de jardinage aideront les femmes à atténuer les effets du changement climatique en utilisant des systèmes d'arrosage solaires et des engrais organiques, et contribueront à fournir de la nourriture aux enfants dans les centres de développement de la petite enfance.
Les activités prévues sur ce projet sont : la distribution du cash a doublé a wallet au profit de 700 personnes (IDPs et populations autochtones)  vivants avec des maladies chroniques. Ils recevront le cash d'un montant de 30,000 pour la ration alimentaire et 10,000XAF pour le cash soin pour la prise en charge médicale pendant 09 tours de distribution. Les activités des AVECs/VSLA (Associations Villageoises de Crédit et d'Epargne au profit de 400 membres, ces dernières (anciennes bénéficiaires du cash Grant) recevront un appui en formation et l'appui en kit pour le démarrage de l’activité proprement dite. Activités de distribution du cash Grant au profit de 350 femmes et filles victimes de VBG. Chaque recevra un montant de 120,000 XAF. Elles sont formées au préalable sur les notions de gestions et de création d'une entreprise florissante.
En ce qui concerne l'appui à la production maraîchères : Construction des ouvrages maraîchers d'une superficie de 0,5ha dans trois (03) sites des IDPs: Clôture grillagée, aménagement système californien, plus installation de système de panneau solaire. 180 productrices recevront la formation sur les techniques maraîchères, bénéficieront de l'appui en semences maraîchers et des outils aratoires. 
Pour la mise en place des activités de développement de la petite enfance. Au total 100 enfant de 0-5 seront identifiés dans 04 sites des IDPs.

project_name: Supporting crisis-affected populations in North-West, South-West, Littoral, and West regions through the provision of multi-sectoral assistance in Cameroon
project_objective:
In the North-West, South-West regions, IOM plans interventions for 2022 to respond to the most urgent needs of displaced populations through a multisectoral approach. The last Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA) exercise conducted in West and Littoral regions that the North-West (NW)-South-West (SW) crisis-related displacements and related needs are spilling over to these neighbouring regions, IOM plans to expand its programmes accordingly.

IOM Cameroon will also mainstream protection and recovery through the development of local capacities, in all its proposed activities to support displaced populations in preparing and achieving durable solutions.
IOM’s multisectoral response in the NW and SW regions will be composed of the following activities:

Coordination Sector

IOM plans to rely on its existing network of enumerators and capacity to:

-	Conduct regular MNSAs in NW, SW, Littoral and West regions in close coordination with humanitarian clusters and OCHA to collect information on the key sectoral needs.
-	Produce and distribute regular sudden displacements alerts through its emergency tracking tool (ETT) dashboards, that present reliable and up-to-date information on the size, trends and triggers of displacements, needs and living conditions, to be shared with humanitarian actors including the RRM and OCHA.  
-	Collect information on livelihoods and stability, through the roll out of a tailored conflict tracker index for the NW and SW regions in order to help facilitate geographic targeting and strategic planning for HDPN interventions.

Shelter/ Non-Food Item (NFI) sector

IOM plans to work closely with the shelter/NFI cluster and coordinate its interventions with the RRM to provide a range of different shelter solutions. Kits will be designed in line with cluster guidelines, and undergo periodic review using beneficiary feedback and complain mechanisms, including:

-	Distribution of 1,000 emergency shelter kits to populations who have been recently displaced and are in need of quick assistance to meet their basic needs. 
-	Distribution of 500 transitional shelter kits to displaced populations that have settled in camp-like informal settings, notably in rural areas, as well as technical assistance to community members for their construction. 
-	Cash-based modalities to respond to the needs of displaced populations (1,000 households) who are based in urban and peri-urban areas that are renting shelters with a financial service provider based on the findings of a rental market baseline assessment and market assessment, in coordination with the Cash working group. 
-	Distribution of 1,500 NFI kits including basic household and cooking items, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) items including soap, sanitary towels, and water purification tablets. 

Health Cluster

Through Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services, IOM aims to bolster the well-being of crisis-affected populations using people-centred and culturally sensitive approaches, in coordination with the MHPSS working group for NWSW. Actions will be tailored to the age and gender of beneficiaries, in line with the IOM Manual on Community-based MHPSS and IASC Guidelines, including:

-	Needs assessment to understand the key challenges, needs and opportunities for MHPSS services in crisis affected areas. 
-	Capacity building for existing MHPSS structures, including local authorities, civil society and NGOs, traditional leaders and women and youth groups, including on Psychological First Aid (PFA), communication skills, stress management skills, or (lay) counselling. 
-	The strengthening or establishing of safe spaces, local structures and committees by promoting communities’ ownership and active participation. 
-	Provide direct MHPSS interventions through the deployment of psychosocial mobile teams (PMT), providing counselling and sensitization to vulnerable groups facing protection concerns such as GBV.

project_name: Multi-sector Emergency response for vulnerable communities in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, White Nile and Blue Nile
project_objective:
Nutrition Sector data for HNO HRP 2021 for the two localities (Guli and Ad Diwaim) in White Nile being proposed for this intervention is as follows (on a scale of 1-5 with 5 being worst): For U5 GAM rate, Ad Diwaim ranks 5 and Guli 4; Both localities rank 5 for stunting rate, rank 4/5 for overall nutrition sector severity, are at IPC level 3 and above for food security needs. Majority of the population are practicing open defecation due to inadequate WASH facilities, being exacerbated by recurrent floods affecting White Nile (being on banks of river Nile) and people's deteriorating purchasing power due to collapsing economy and rising inflation rate. The impact of COVID 19 in 2020 has wreaked havoc on basic needs of vulnerable populations in White Nile.
AAH is present in Sudan since 2018, with operational bases in Khartoum, White Nile, Central Darfur and South Kordofan states. AAH is currently implementing two emergency interventions in White Nile State as part of the COVID-19 response (funded by GFFO) and flood response (funded by SIDA).
Overall objective of proposed intervention is Reduce severe undernutrition on children & PLWs of emergency-affected & highly vulnerable households through multi sectoral life-protecting interventions. Project targets already vulnerable (in terms of nutrition, health and WASH indicators)14 communities in 2 localities, comprising of around 190,209 people, recovering from shocks in 2020 (i.e. floods emergency and COVID 19 and its cascading impact on economy and livelihoods) while these communities were not fully recovered from prior shocks (for instance, 2019 floods emergency). Assistance will be in form of nutrition (support to essential primary health care and nutrition public services, as well as integrated community case management), WASH at health facility and community levels (improving access to basic water services, adequate (basic or limited) protected, and gender-sensitive sanitation services and hygiene promotion services), and mental health care practices gender protection (IYCF, sensitisation on gender discriminatory harmful traditional practices such as FGM and early marriage). Community participation will be fostered via capacity building, mobilization and follow-up of community volunteers that will engage in sensitization activities (related to nutrition, health, hygiene, sanitation, gender). Some volunteers will also be supported to identify and manage cases of undernutrition and common childhood illnesses in the community. Select volunteers will be provided training to be able to facilitate participatory vulnerability capacity assessments (PVCA) at their community levels. Community volunteers will conduct screening and referral of malnourished children and PLW; they will identify, treat and refer children with common childhood illness, do rapid IYCF assessment at HH level and refer PLWs with IYCF problem, conduct home visit, defaulter tracing and community sensitization. AAH and their local partner in White Nile, CAFA, will co implement this project together, as per AAH localization strategy in Sudan. The proposed intervention will encompass emergency preparedness activities for sustainability of this intervention and as exit strategy - AAH and CAFA will establish Water Sanitation User Committees (WSUC), Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Committees at community levels, in addition to Mother-to-Mother support groups, and provide extensive trainings to community volunteers on several essential topics. All volunteers will be trained on needs assessment and AAH complaint response mechanism.
Target population is based on HNO 2021 data and White Nile MoH data, with vulnerability selection criteria focusing on very poor and vulnerable households. Key beneficiaries are 14 OTPs and 56 staff (4 per center); 150 community volunteers; Mass Screening: 32,336 (16,491 girls & 15,845 boys) ; 4300 HH receiving hygiene & dignity kits; soft activities to target all 14 village population

project_name: Acces aux services de protection dans la Region de Tillaberi et de Diffa
project_objective:
La création et formation des filles et femmes et survivantes de la violence fondée sur le genre à l'AGR dans les 24 Communautés ciblés par le projet. Ces femmes seront formées à l'entreprenariat et orientées vers les divers groupes d'AGR.
-	 La mise en place d'un système d'orientation fonctionnel pour les cas de violence fondée sur le genre.
-	Le renforcement des capacités des femmes, des comités et des responsables d'associations sur les questions de genre et autres questions liées à la violence fondée sur le genre.
-	 Organiser des sessions de sensibilisation pour les Communautés et les associations de femmes afin de lutter contre les cas de violence fondée sur le sexe et pour la prévention des cas principaux.
 Ce projet devrait contribuer à un environnement plus protecteur pour 69522 personnes dont 24332 déplacés internes et 45190 membres des  communautés hôtes dont 14683 d'hommes, 15907 de femmes, 20245 filles, 18687 garçons, 3% de personnes âgées soit 2085 et 4% de personnes vivant avec Handicap soit 2780  touchés par le conflit grâce à une approche socio-écologique consistant à travailler avec différents acteurs de l'environnement des enfants : les enfants eux-mêmes et leur famille, la communauté et la société au sens large, y compris le gouvernement et d'autres prestataires de services. 
Le projet intègrera a tous les étapes la réduction des risques de catastrophes, droits de l’homme, égalité des sexes, impact environnemental, et d’autres questions transversales qui font écho de l’engagement de Plan International tels que : Les droits de l’enfant, L’égalité des genres, L’inclusion, La résilience.
 Les autres aspects à prendre en considération en matière de protection de l'enfance sont les aspects liés au sexe, à l’âge, à l'ethnie et à la religion, afin de garantir l'inclusion et l'égalité entre les bénéficiaires et au sein des communautés d'accueil. Cela se fera en étroite collaboration avec les chefs de communauté et les structures de dialogue qui sont basées dans la communauté, et qui seront formées pour soutenir la sensibilisation et la mobilisation de la communauté et soutenues pour la prévention de toutes sortes d'abus auxquels les enfants sont exposés dans les Communautés d'accueil. Les partenaires gouvernementaux, les partenaires de la société civile, le partenaire de mise en œuvre et le personnel de Plan International Niger seront également formés aux VSBGs et au soutien psychosocial pour la gestion des cas de maltraitance d'enfants signalés. Les enfants vulnérables (enfants handicapés, enfants séparés ou non accompagnés, enfants associées aux forces et groupes armées, les filles comme les garçons âgés de moins de 18 ans, mais aussi les jeunes âgés de 18 à 24 ans) recevront un soutien spécial grâce à la contribution des communautés, du gouvernement et des partenaires. Il sera mis en place une stratégie pour se rassurer que les filles et les garçons vivant avec  handicap aient accès aux services disponibles dans le cadre de ce programme, cette sera élaborée sur la base l'évaluation de leur besoins individuelles. Dans le cadre de ce plan de soutien, le partenaire de mis en œuvre du projet fera des référencements avec l’appui de Plan International et le sous cluster Protection d’enfant à travers le circuit de référencement qui sera mis à jour dans le cadre de ce projet, produit en une forme familière aux enfants et sensible aux illettrées et vulgarisé dans la zone de mis en œuvre du projet. Les enfants participeront également à la mise en œuvre d'activités visant à renforcer les mécanismes communautaires de lutte contre les Violences basées sur le genre et les autres abus et violences ; cela se fera par le biais des plans d'action des clubs d'enfants, des membres du Comité de protection, ainsi que par l'implication des animateurs et des responsables communautaires. Afin de renforcer la résilience des parents, renforcer leurs capacités sur le développement et le bien-être des enfants.

project_name: Monitoring de protection et assistance aux populations affectées par la crise
project_objective:
Le HCR met en œuvre le système de monitoring de protection, en partenariat avec AMSS, dont l'objectif principal est d’améliorer l'environnement de protection des populations civiles dans les régions du Mali les plus touchées par le conflit, en renforçant la collecte, l'analyse et la diffusion d'informations, ainsi que son utilisation par les acteurs humanitaires et de développement. Le projet comprend 4 piliers, à savoir : 1) la prévention et le renforcement de la résilience communautaire ; 2) la collecte et le partage d’information sur les violations de droits humains et les risques de protection ; 3) le référencement pour la prise en charge des victimes ; 4) le plaidoyer pour le respect des droits.  

Le système de monitoring de protection couvre les régions de Gao, Kayes, Kidal, Koulikoro, Ménaka, Mopti, Ségou, Sikasso et Tombouctou. Il repose sur 80 moniteurs, 200 points focaux communautaires, et 168 membres de 42 comités locaux de protection communautaire. Le monitoring de protection est désormais un outil inter-agence au service de la centralité de la protection. Il offre une fenêtre unique de collaboration et de partenariat permettant de déterminer les violations de droits humains, mais également d’orienter la réponse et le plaidoyer de l’ensemble du Cluster Protection. Le lien essentiel entre le monitoring, la prévention et la réponse doit être assuré.  

Ainsi, le HCR renforcera sa réponse aux besoins de protection des personnes déplacées internes. Cette réponse s’articulera autour de plusieurs axes à savoir notamment la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre, le soutien aux personnes ayant des besoins spécifiques, et les activités génératrices des revenues. En outre, le HCR contribue à la coordination et à la gestion des sites de déplacement en collaboration avec les autorités maliennes, et soutien la DNDS dans ce rôle à travers l’appui financier et l’appui technique y compris des formations des agents de protection de la DNDS.  

Le HCR œuvre également pour renforcer le cadre légal de protection des PDIs au Mali à travers des activités de plaidoyer et un soutien auprès du gouvernement pour l’adoption de l’avant-projet de loi portant protection et assistance aux personnes déplacées internes en République du Mali.

project_name: Improving children’s access and learning in the most vulnerable schools in Gaza
project_objective:
The proposed project is in line with the education cluster HNO strategic objectives 1, 2, and 3, and is aligned with the MoE Strategy and Plan in adopting the blended learning modality in education, as response to the COVID- 19 crises. The project aims to ensure that boys and girls have equitable safe access to inclusive and quality educational services in vulnerable MoE schools in the Gaza Strip (East Khanyounis, Rafah, Gaza, and North Gaza). The project fits under a multi-year NRC education intervention applying, of providing protection of education and psychosocial support and co-leading the EiE Strategic Advisory Group in Gaza. The project- is intended to focus on the following approaches: i) Implementation of the Psycho-Educational “Better Learning Program” (BLP), reinforcing the system through training new cohort BLP Master Trainers at General Directors, subject supervisors; Capacity building of teaching and non-teaching staff in MoE schools; provision of emergency kits to the schools; awareness sessions for parents; and provision of a “Supporting the Supporter” package for teaching and Non-teaching staff in need; ii) Strengthen the best practices in education contingency and response plans at school level; establish emergency team in each target school; linkage target schools with emergency actors in Gaza; capacity building of emergency team on best practices during, within and before the emergency; revise and update the emergency plan in target schools in line with the specificity of each target school. iii) Carry out remedial/catch up classes for children not active in virtual classes and who are stuck in disrupted academic functioning; improving access of children to distance learning platforms through providing tablets to specific group of children; printing self- learning materials; rehab. schools’ ICT infrastructure. iv) Provision of technical support to education sub-cluster in Gaza through the continuation of co-leading the EiE Strategic Advisory Group to steer the EiE priorities. v) conduct situational analysis on OOSC needs, gaps and priorities, as well as contributing in enhancing their access to quality basic education. vi) Conduct a situational analysis on adolescent/youth needs and priorities, in addition to contributing in enhancing vulnerable youths’ empowerment and skills, capacity and resilience development.  

 

The action is also contributing in improving both skills and knowledge of teaching and non-teaching staff on PSEA principles, and reporting mechanisms on any violation against the main principles. Teaching and non-teaching staff will be benefited from a tailored training on PSEA principles, and received a well-prepared leaflets and printed materials linked to the principles.

project_name: Humanitarian response to the most vulnerable population affected by extreme poverty, humanitarian crisis, and violations of IHL/IHRL in the Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
This project will support 600 most vulnerable households in the Gaza Strip (3600 individuals), based on their protection vulnerabilities, providing multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA), multi-disciplinary rehabilitation and assistive devices, community-based psychosocial support and information, counselling and legal aid. The project will also train a further 50 humanitarian staff and organizations in protection mainstreaming and disability inclusion. Specifically, the project aims at: (1) providing six MPCA instalments to vulnerable households to cover their basic needs including (but not limited to) any newly incurred debts, repairs and maintenance, food and water and education-related costs as well as health, non-food items, communication and transportation costs. (2) provision of multidisciplinary rehabilitation (MDR) center-based services including: physiotherapy, psychosocial support services, occupational therapy, nursing, distribution of wound dressing kits, and provision of Assistive Devices (ADs); (3) provide community mobilization activities with a focus on protection and prevention of violence and abuse, thorough group-based awareness raising sessions and psychosocial support sessions. NRC Legal and Protection Team will work in close synergy with the partner, to guarantee a continuum of care between legal aid, protection identification and referral and community mobilization.  
The project preserves the physical and normative space for a two-state solution, mitigates the impact of occupation by providing cash assistance as well as protection services to vulnerable Palestinian individuals and communities. The project supports strengthening of resilience among the poorest and most vulnerable strata of the Gaza population, improves access to services and restores more dignified living conditions. It protects the most vulnerable Palestinians through a protection-oriented, multi-sectoral approach that encompasses emergency relief, community-based protection, and legal aid. Finally, the projects complements the efforts of the Palestinian National Cash Transfer Program (PNCTP), run by Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) and co-financed by the European Union, to support households living in deep poverty.

project_name: Enhancing IDP Protection Services in South Sudan to facilitate and scale up protection monitoring, targeted  Protection Assistance (including GBV and CP), as well as HLP support to the most vulnerable IDPs and Returnees
project_objective:
The projects seek to ensure that the most vulnerable people in need and Persons with Specific Needs (PSNs) including IDPs, retunes and the host community will benefit from scaled up protection services with a focus on critical lifesaving and resilience targeted assistance through comprehensive structured protection monitoring, allowing to improve efficient targeting for overall protection, , as well as GBV, CP and HLP. The activities will be implemented in Juba, Wau, Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Yei, Yambio and Torit and prioritized respective counties   

The project will facilitate the use of the Protection Monitoring tool piloted in 2021 and used at household H/H level. This will offer standardized methodology of collecting data, which will be used by protection actors across the country for informed planning in  support to vulnerable men, women, boys and girls of all ages and diversity components. Protection concerns identified will be dealt both on individual protection services/case management basis and through community-based approaches (by ensuring referrals to the respective actor or through provision of various types of direct assistance by UNHCR. Community based protection will involve quick impact projects to address infrastructure and livelihood challenges faced by communities. 

Protection challenges will be addressed through awareness raising protection risk, targeting communities and their leaders. Support will be provided through child friendly spaces, outreach to reduce incidence of teenage pregnancy and child labor; support for psychosocial support affecting children.
SGBV issues will be addressed through outreach to ensure communities understand the benefits of reporting of incidence, addressing taboos linked to SGBV enhancing psychosocial support,  case management (including cash-based interventions), legal assistance, renovation and construction of safe houses. 

The project will address House Land and Policy issues by ensuring displaced populations benefit from outreach, legal aid/representation, counselling, support to replacement of ownership documentation through working with the Nationality, Civil Registry, Passports and Immigration. 

Overall the project will seek to empower communities affected by displacement through supporting gaps, outreach and awareness, material and cash assistance to support their resilience and ensure sustainability of assistance provided.
