project_name: Protection of Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh and Promotion of Community Self-Reliance and Cohesion
project_objective:
UNHCR will work with the Government to give Rohingya refugees a legal identity through registration and documentation, which will serve as the foundation for protection, program delivery and solutions, while pursuing community-based protection responses and providing essential services. UNHCR will continue to facilitate access to effective justice mechanisms through its legal partners working in all 34 camps, including through legal counselling, representation in court, alternative dispute resolution mechanisms in non-criminal cases and targeted interventions for the release of refugees held for administrative violations.
UNHCR will remain a central player within interagency disaster preparedness efforts for the monsoon and cyclone seasons and to address remaining COVID-19 challenges. UNHCR will bolster inclusion with host communities to promote peaceful coexistence and social cohesion. Reinforcing accountable government leadership of the response will be an important component of inclusion, and UNHCR will continue to support capacity development across the different levels of engagement with government authorities from the camp level up to the RRRC’s office. 
UNHCR will empower Rohingya refugees by building community capacities for leadership, self-management and engagement with the Government and the humanitarian community in 31 camps, including through the refugee representatives’ system in 4 camps. UNHCR will continue to involve refugees from all parts of the community in a range of community-based protection programs which builds their resilience while supporting the community and thus reducing dependency on aid. This will include refugee volunteer networks such as the Community Outreach Members (COMs), community groups, and religious engagement networks of imams and female religious teachers. Within the current framework, UNHCR will advocate for greater access to education and economic inclusion, so that young refugees retain hope and become a constructive force in the community. While promoting conditions needed for voluntary, safe, dignified and sustainable return in Myanmar, UNHCR will work to improve protection conditions and quality of life for refugees in Bangladesh pending solutions, building upon the framework for responsibility sharing provided by the Global Compact on Refugees.
UNHCR will ensure the centrality of protection through protection and gender mainstreaming, inclusive coordination, and leadership of the humanitarian response as the UN agency leading the protection sector within the ISCG. The Protection Sector will ensure strategic, policy and advocacy coordination of the response for effective delivery of quality protection services and results. Accountability to Affected Populations remains central to UNHCR’s work. UNHCR will support the expansion of the common feedback mechanism, and work with partners within the Protection Sector to further integrate an approach centred on age, gender and diversity across all areas of work to ensure that the specific needs of all individuals are taken into consideration in the response and in service provision. UNHCR mainstreams participation and engagement of refugees across programming and the operations management cycle, as well as through the protection focal points and their protection mainstreaming activities at camp level. 
With a zero-tolerance policy on SEA, UNHCR deploys a variety of actions to ensure appropriate reporting, response and prevention activities are undertaken which target staff, partners, authorities, and refugees. This includes the application of SOPs on SEA complaint referral developed by the CXB PSEA network. There are multiple complaint mechanisms for refugees, such as face-to-face engagement, a hotline, awareness-raising posters, individual case follow-up and regular focus group discussions allowing for the safe reporting of cases of SEA. UNHCR ensures that PSEA is also addressed in all partnership agreements.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Protection and Site Management Services to Internally displaced people, Returnees, Host Community  and Other Persons With Specific Needs in Ethiopia
project_objective:
UNHCR’s 2022 protection programme builds on the scale up of 2021 response and will be implemented in nine regions. The programme, builds on evidence gathered from ongoing protection monitoring using the revamped Ethiopia Protection Monitoring Tool (E-PMT) in the operational areas to ensure the ongoing identification of protection and specific needs and changes in the protection landscape for IDPs, IDP returnees, host communities and other persons with specific needs requiring protection services. 
As the Protection Cluster-lead agency, UNHCR ensures the coordination of its activities, implemented directly or through partnerships, through the Protection Cluster at national and sub-national level as appropriate.
Based on the protection monitoring, UNHCR will implement an integrated set of protection services and interventions tailored to the needs and priorities of the affected, which include:
•	the provision of information, counselling, identification of protection and specific needs, referrals to services/assistance, 
•	direct provision of services and assistance to persons at risk or with specific needs; 
•	GBV awareness, prevention and response activities;
•	child protection awareness raising and case management;
•	strengthening of MHPSS, 
•	emergency EORE as required by the Mine Action AOR,
•	provision of legal awareness and legal aid for GBV case management, HLP, legal identity and civil document restoration, 
•	and strengthen social cohesion and community-based peacebuilding.

project_objective:

project_name: Strenghtening Provision of Humanitarian Services and Disaster Risk Reduction through Camp Coordination, Site Development and Monitoring of Minimum Standards in Rohingya Refugee Camps
project_objective:
The project aims to continue strengthening the provision of humanitarian assistance through supporting the coordination of service providers, enabling community participation and feedback to humanitarian programming, reducing risks from safety and natural hazards, and  increasing the degree of access to key services in refugee camps and host community of Ukhiya and Teknaf upazilas. In collaboration with implementing partners and other stakeholders, IOM intends to target Rohingya refugees and host communities that will benefit from improved service provision, site improvements, site planning interventions and disaster risk reduction which contribute to ensuring equitable access to assistance, protection, and services that improve quality of life and dignity during displacement.

Site Management Support (SMS) activities in 18 camps of IOM’s Area of Responsibility will continue to support the Camp-in-Charge officials (CiC), ensuring services are monitored, coordinated, and appropriately targeted, including through community engagement activities that enable effective avenues for two-way communication with the affected population, while also ensuring that risk mitigation, inclusion and GBV considerations are mainstreamed and implemented across all activities within the camps. Providing humanitarian and development actors with data and information on needs that support informed decision making, the project ensures targeted and appropriate humanitarian service provision within the camps as well as the host community. 

Site Development (SD) works implemented through IOM and partners, and involvement in the Site Maintenance & Engineering Project (SMEP), will contribute to a safer, more dignified, and more accessible living environment for the camp population, working to ensure further community involvement in the identification of priority works. IOM will work towards inclusion of age-gender-disability groups in various community-based structures wherever possible. Mobilization of cash-for-work labour will be key to deliver the site development/improvement results as most of the works are implemented using this modality, which in turn becomes a main income-generating source for refugee households.

Needs and Population Monitoring NPM will continue supporting the SMSD sector through the establishment of a facility monitoring tool. The tool can be used by a variety of stakeholders, both for site planning and development purposes, as well site management operational activities on the ground. It will grant humanitarian partners a better understanding of service provision in camps, thus promoting adequate coverage.

Through Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) interventions, both refugee and host communities will benefit from improved disaster preparedness and response activities and strengthened community resilience. DRR activities will also be streamlined into SMS and SD programming, with a focus on community-based preparedness and response and referral mechanisms, camp and host community contingency planning and mitigation measures. Learning centre and school-based disaster management will improve the access and safety measures of vulnerable people using emergency shelters during seasonal floods, cyclones or other hazards.

Finally, IOM will continue to lead the Site Management and Site Development (SMSD) sector, with coordination and information management capacity and supporting resources, to enable inter-sectoral coordination, including SMEP and other site development and improvement actors. The SMSD sector will continue to work closely with the Inter-Sector Coordination Group (ISCG) secretariat, NPM and other sector and working group coordinators to enable tools that will support centralized data collection of service monitoring and incident tracking to better inform them about the quality of services and gaps across camps, incidence of events due to natural hazards, results of safety audits and other assessments.

project_name: Provision of air services to the humanitarian workers implementing projects
project_objective:
The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), managed by the World Food Programme (WFP), offers safe, reliable, cost-efficient and effective passenger and light cargo transport for the wider humanitarian community to and from areas of crisis and intervention. It is the only humanitarian air service that gives access to all humanitarian entities. UNHAS responds to the need for access to the South Sudan’s most remote and challenging locations, often under precarious security conditions, where no safe surface transport or viable commercial aviation options are available.
In 2022, UNHAS is targeting to provide air transport services to 65,000 passengers and 2000 metric tons (MT) light humanitarian cargo from 313 registered humanitarian organizations to approximately 54 regularly scheduled locations in South Sudan. 
The main objective of UNHAS is to continue supporting Humanitarian community with a safe, effective, cost-efficient and reliable air services. In addition to serving destinations on the fixed regular schedule, UNHAS will support 100 percent of non-scheduled location booking requests for emergencies response (security relocations, medical evacuations and Inter-Cluster Working Group Rapid Response Missions).
UNHAS requires $51,400,000 to sustain its operations across the year and continue supporting the entire humanitarian community.

project_name: Logistics Common Service Provision for North Mozambique crises response
project_objective:
The Northern provinces of Mozambique continue to be confronted with insecurity leading to continued displacements of men, women and children. Logistical access within Cabo Delgado, the epicenter of the insecurity is expected to remain in year 2022 as a consequence. The advent of the rainy season will exacerbate the tenuous situation in some of the more remote locations. Logistical support also requires to be expended toother provinces of displacement including Niassa and Nampula provinces in northern Mozambique to where of the displacement has taken place.
Since 2017, an armed conflict in Cabo Delgado province in northern Mozambique has continued to escalate, affecting more than 1.3 million people including over 700,000displaced people. 950,000 people are facing high levels of food insecurity in the northern provinces of Cabo Delgado, Niassa, Nampula and Zambezia. The conflict exacerbates and compounds existent vulnerabilities experienced in Cabo Delgado province, which despite having significant economic potential in terms of natural resources (including ruby reserves, graphite, gas and oil) and tourism, is the poorest province in terms of multidimensional poverty. Other vulnerabilities including socio economic impacts ofCOVID-19 pandemic and climatic shocks have been reported to affect over 1, 414 persons who are currently food insecure and also in need of other basic needs.
The humanitarian and development actors are fully engaged in responding to support the displaced men, women and children in Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa Provinces. One of the main challenges to ensure success of this support is assured and sustained access from undeveloped tertiary road networks, insecurity, adequate transport service providers for sea transport and the potential for further infrastructure deterioration during the rainy season.
Common services under the logistics cluster would aim to address the above challenges by offering a platform for logistical solutions in warehousing and surface transport. Additionally access via air under the WFP mandated air services (UNHAS) to the humanitarian community for both passenger and cargo air transport will be implemented.

Provision of quality lifesaving essential health services, and enhanced capacity for early detection and response to public health emergencies in South Sudan.
project_objective:
This project aims to contribute to the reduction of excess morbidity and mortality resulting from health emergencies and common communicable and non-communicable diseases in South Sudan. The common emergencies that are likely to impact the vulnerable populations in 2022 include epidemic disease outbreaks, flooding, conflicts, and acute food insecurity. The project objectives will be achieved through the provision of time-critical, life-saving frontline quality health services, ensuring the availability of quality essential medicines and supplies, and well-trained healthcare workers in the health facilities and clinics. 
In addition to procurement and prepositioning of essential emergency health kits in project locations, WHO will capacitate the implementing partners and counties to provide quality health services through training of frontline health workers and provision of guidelines and SoPs on case management of common communicable and non-communicable diseases, and provision of safe maternal and child services, mental and psychosocial care. Furthermore, WHO will deploy a multidisciplinary team; the emergency Mobile Medical Teams (eMMT), to provide integrated health services in deep field locations through mobile outreaches to bridge service delivery gaps in areas with serious unmet health needs.
The country’s capacities to prevent, prepare for, detect and respond to emergencies will be improved at both national and state levels. The public health surveillance, IDSR/EWARN, will be strengthened through continued investment in the system and expansion of reporting sites to enable timely detection, investigation, and response to public health events. The routine surveillance system will be enhanced through the deployment of mobile phone-based EWARS reporting by the static and mobile clinics, and provision of technical support to the implementing partners and counties. This will enhance weekly reporting by facilities to ensure early detection of and response to disease outbreaks. Besides, the national and state RRTs, as well as WHO Mobile Medical Teams (eMMT), will be deployed to conduct risk assessments, alert and outbreak investigation, and to provide initial public health response during emergencies to reduce excess morbidity and mortality. Moreover, WHO will support the deployment of the eMMTs and RRTs to conduct rapid needs assessments to identify the unmet health needs in project locations to inform appropriate responses by health actors and other relevant sectors. As part of outbreak prevention and response, WHO will lead the implementation of preventive and reactive vaccination campaigns for vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles and cholera.
Further, WHO will be conducting IPC/WASH assessments in health facilities and implementing IPC measures as a component of risk identification and mitigation efforts to healthcare-related infections. Lastly, the project will contribute to enhancing the capacities for diagnosis and management of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and associated medical complications with a view of reducing avoidable mortality in collaboration with the Nutrition Cluster. 
Finally, WHO will address Disability and MHPSS needs in the country by ensuring mainstreaming the needs into ongoing programming, it will also make efforts to work with the health TWGs and organizations of persons living with disability to assess and address the needs.

Overall the above strategy and interventions will contribute to the three health cluster objectives of (1) Improving equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment for common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to crisis-affected populations 2) Reducing excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic-prone diseases, and 3) Enhancing resilience and promoting humanitarian-development linkages

project_name: Supporting Outbreak Response and Access to Essential Health Services for the Most Vulnerable Population in the oPt
project_objective:
The already challenged healthcare system in the oPt experiences added strain from the COVID-19 outbreak since 2020, combined with the recurring conflict. The reallocation of scarce resources has undermined people’s access to health. Direct mortality from the virus and indirect mortality from preventable diseases continue to be a major concern for 2022.
The Health Cluster estimates that more than 1.5 million people, including refugees, across the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) will need humanitarian health interventions in 2022, two-thirds of them are in Gaza and one third in the West Bank. Of those in need, around 47% are female and children constitute almost half (47%) of the total.

Through this project, WHO will support the Palestinian Ministry of Health COVID-19 response, and management of other outbreak-related communicable diseases. At least 400K suspected cases will have access to COVID-19 testing; 500 healthcare workers will benefit from capacity building activities on laboratory testing, case management, infection prevention and control, and surveillance. Approx. 1M people will also benefit from risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) messaging. Around 10K will benefit from procurement of essentially needed items.

Planned Trauma and emergency activities will include all levels of trauma care, starting from standardizing national triage guidelines; upgrading the emergency departments and surgical wards of 7 hospitals in Gaza; upgrading emergency departments in 2 West Bank hospitals, and one hospital in East Jerusalem; in addition to supporting the Limb Reconstruction Center. More than 100K patients are expected to benefit from the proposed activities.

With contribution from 12 partner agencies, WHO will continue to document and monitor barriers to healthcare services access, including for patients, companions and health workers requiring permits to reach essential healthcare services, as a basis for evidence-based advocacy. Additionally, around 100 partners will benefit from the implementation of the Health Resources and Services Availability Monitoring System (HeRAMS).

WHO's project has been coordinated at various levels with all counterparts involved in the activities:
(1) COVID-19 response with the MoH and through the Humanitarian Response Plan,
(2) Trauma activities - with the MoH and Health cluster Trauma WG,
(3) Right to Health - with the MoH, counterparts, and partners of the Advocacy WG.

project_name: Provision of emergency public health services to mitigate the negative impacts of COVID-19 for the populations in need
project_objective:
Multiple hazards including, drought, floods, cyclones and conflict have contributed to weakening Somalia's health system for the past three decades, exacerbated further by the COVID-19 pandemic since Somalia’s first reported case on 16 March 2020. To date, WHO has supported the Federal MOH to respond to COVID-19 by: providing coordination/technical support; distributing Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) to frontline health workers, medicines, and medical equipment; establishing level 2 biosafety laboratories ; and collecting and analyzing epidemiological data to facilitate evidence-based decision making. As of 02 November 2021, A total of 22,369 confirmed COVID-19 cases in Somalia, including 1,238 reported deaths, with the majority of cases reported in Banadir, Somaliland and Puntland affecting different population groups with varying levels of severity. Modelling studies conducted by WHO have demonstrated that COVID-19 has severely strained the provision of essential health services especially maternal and child health. Indeed, child mortality increased by 13%, while vaccination coverage for measles amongst children aged below five years reduced by 20% since the COVID-19 epidemic.   The number of cases of epidemic prone diseases reported from districts affected by drought and floods in Early Warning Alert and Response Network (EWARN) attributed to climatic shocks have increased since June 2021: cholera cases by 20% from 2933 to 3551; acute diarrhoeal cases by 15% from 51,760 to 59,786; and malaria cases by 38% from 1837 to 2536. The number of cases of these diseases are expected to increase as a result of further floods and drought expected in 2022 that will negatively affect access to safe water and proper sanitation amongst displaced communities. Similarly, due to the reduction of the number of children vaccinated against measles, cases reported during the same period increased by 24% from 2090 to 2585. Moreover, there has been a 33% increase in the number of trauma cases from 5033 in September 2020 to 6693 in September 2021. The capacity to manage the trauma cases in Somalia is very limited. It is in this regard that improved community-based management of targeted diseases could bridge the critical gap in the availability of essential health services at the health facility level. 

In addition to the above, there is an urgent need for improving trauma care, medical waste management, access to medical oxygen and access to mental health services. For trauma care, a primary assessment conducted by WHO in 2020 across 21 hospitals concluded that trauma imposes a heavy burden on the Somali health system, with approximately 50% of all civilian trauma cases resulting from conflict. WHO has thus identified the urgent need for developing a more robust trauma care system. In the absence of a national policy on medical waste management, handful of hospitals and health facilities in the major cities outsource the services through private contractors, and a little information is available on their current practices. Considering the significant negative environmental impact, a joint systemic assessment is under planning, after which a the national medical waste management policy will be developed,  followed by the infrastructures development to ensure the appropriate management of the biohazard materials. Medical oxygen remains in critical shortage across Somalia. To urgently address this vital life-saving gap, WHO is seeking to leverage on cost-effective medical innovations such as the instalment of solar powered oxygen concentrators at the peripheral health facilities and hospitals, which provide an environmentally friendly and uninterrupted supply of medical oxygen for all types of patients. Finally, mental health remains a major burden across Somalia, with almost no services available and approximately one in three Somalis suffering from some form of mental health illness.

project_name: Improve the quality and coverage of inpatient care for Severe Acute malnutrition under five children in Stabilization Centers all over Sudan in 2022
project_objective: WHO project aims to decrease avoidable under five mortality and morbidity related to Severe acute malnutrition through improved access and quality of inpatient care for the Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications in 154 stabilization centers currently Operating in health facilities. The project includes curative, preventive and promotive measures in the same time. The activities will address the clinical life-saving interventions in Stabilization centers targeting the patients/children with SAM and the mothers/caretakers through IYCF counseling and young children nutrition awareness to lower relapse and prevent SAM cases in the same households. The project activities and costing factored in 38 SCs are supported by NGOs. The SCs Supported by NGOs will require only Medical kits (1st and 2nd line medicines) and technical support. Main activities: Training of the health and nutrition staff of 117 SCs (all except the ones Supported NGOs) to include IPD SAM initial training (7 days) and refresher Training (3 days), provision of guidelines, Job Aids and IEC materials to all participants from the 117 SCs. WHO will procure and distribute to 155 SCs; medicines (SAM inpatient Kits – first and secondary level care), , medical equipment and other supplies based on the needs identified together with MOH. To improve the quality of care and cure rate in SCs, WHO nutrition and public health officers present in all targeted states will conduct jointly with SMOH regular supportive supervisions in all targeted 155 SCs conducting on the job training, coaching, and adherence to the national treatment protocols. Routine nutrition surveillance at HF level/SCs, essential for trends and gap identification and effective planning of activities will be enhanced through training, provision of recording and reporting tools for the SCs in 18 targeted states, and better integration into HFs reporting mechanism to promote sustainability. WHO nutrition team will provide technical and operational support to the MOH at federal and state levels to regularly analysis the data of SAM inpatient care services (using the agreed performance indicators) to identify the trends, and challenges disaggregated by sex and age. The information will be disseminated to all relevant stakeholders through nutrition cluster bulletins, and bring during nutrition sector meetings led by MOH and UNICEF. Effective coordination of WHO with all partners (Nutrition, Health, food security) will promote an improved referral system between the SCs, TSFP, OTP, and community. Linkages with communities will be strengthened through raising awareness and social mobilization conducted by trained community mobilizers/CHW and MSG in coordination with other UN. The modalities and subjects for these activities will be guided by the community members suggestions collected through exit interview and focus group discussions during supervisions. The project activities also includes small repairs of 10 SCs in order to ensure better environment for work and improved hygiene in the SCs

project_name: Strengthening the healthcare system capacity to efficiently respond to COVID-19 outbreak and implement action plans
project_objective:
COVID-19 pandemic is a global public health emergency and specially to Syria, which is facing this emergency in addition to the complex emergency with a significant impact on health and economic development. In 2020; Syria declared its first COVID-19 case on 22 March 2020. The transmission of COVID-19 is classified as community transmission. As of 15 January 2022, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases reported by MoH was 50,674, only 145,491 NAATs (PCR tests) were performed at public health laboratories, the average weekly testing rate was 1,580 for total population, far below WHO recommendation for the testing to be at the level of 1 per 1000 people in the context of comprehensive surveillance (21,000 tests per week) . Moreover, the positivity rate across the country was 34%, higher in some governorates, eg; Swieda, Deir Ez-zor, and Homs above 70%. Considering the limited number of tests being performed the actual number of cases and deaths likely far exceed official figures. Official statistics show an increase in cases, but the high positivity rate and death reports suggest that the true scale of the epidemic is largely underestimated. 
In NWS  the current health system is fragmented and has very limited capacity in terms of COVID-19 surveillance, laboratory testing, contact tracing, human resources for health, case management and measures at points of entry (PoEs). In addition, implementing partners have insufficient capacity to detect, test, isolate, quarantine and treat COVID-19 confirmed and suspected cases. Access to primary health care and hospital care is very limited. Intensive care unit capacity is inadequate. Infection prevention and control (IPC) capacity is very low, due to lack of adequate material and supplies. Access to medicines and medical supplies is also very limited. The COVID-19 Task Force has been formed in early March 2020 to carry out activities under identified pillars in collaboration with implementing partners. The COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan for Northwest Syria (CPRP2020) has been published in 2020

The overall aim of the project is to reduce morbidity and mortality resulting from COVID-19 among the population of Syria by scaling up the country’s preparedness and response operations.    It also aims to stop transmission of COVID-19 in Syria and protect all persons within Syria from the disease, and to strengthen health systems to attain resilience and respond to emerging and re-emerging public health threats.  The response strategy aligns with that of the Health sector strategy as well as the WHO global strategy.    It thus adopted the 11 pillars approach.    The main objectives are as follows: 
•	Strengthen existing national multisectoral coordination mechanism to deliver timely and integrated response and to contain the pandemic, by actively engaging Directorates of Health, line-ministries, UN agencies, INGOs and NNGOs.
•	To ensure people’s understanding of the situation and their compliance to social and public health measures
•	Strengthen surveillance for early detection and response of COVID-19 infections to reduce person-to-person transmission.
•	Early detection and timely isolation of suspected COVID-19 cases among travellers at PoE
•	Strengthen central and directorate-level public health laboratories for virologic testing of COVID-19 samples
•	Strengthen the public health laboratory network central and directorate-level public health laboratories for virologic testing of COVID-19 samples and sequencing of SARS-CoV-2

•	Strengthen and sustain infection prevention and control (IPC) measures to ensure safety of patients, healthcare workers and the caregiving environment.
•	Establish and maintain designated isolation facilities across the country.
•	Maintain stockpile of supplies required for the response, 
•	The continuity of essential health services as to avoid substantial disruptions is secured.
•	Update and maintain vaccination strategy and microplans.

project_name: Improving access to basic services for South Sudan and Ethiopian Refugees including host community in WK, BN, Gadaref and South Kordofan through multi-sector interventions covering WASH, FSL, Education   and Health mainstreamed by Protection activities across sectors
project_objective:
Through this intervention, Islamic relief will contribute to improve basic services for South Sudan and Ethiopian refugees in WK, Gadaref, South Kordofan and Blue Nile by delivering integrated durable and sustainable solutions across all sectors to refugees and host community. The strategy is to deliver multi sectorial services for refugees in all their locations to ensure satisfaction of services. This integrated approach will enable Islamic Relief to work on filling the gaps and need at once in all sectors, and assure that both South Sudan and Ethiopian refugees rights and dignity are fulfilled at all levels.
In West Kordofan, the project will target SSR through multi interventions in Protection, Education, FSL and WASH targeting the in and out of camp refugees in Kailak, El Mairam, Lagawa, El Nuhud. In regard to protection, the intended project will raise awareness on general protection topics to reach around 8,506 refugees in targeted localities of Kailak, Lagawa, El Mairam and El Nuhud, manage to establish eight Community-Based Structures for CPBNs, community reconciliation committees, and youth networks and build the capacity of 160 service providers on general protection topics as well as cash under MPCA at full to around 2,000 refugees. In Education the project will target both SSR and Ethiopian refugees in WK, SK, BN and Gadaref to support both primary and Secondary Education through comprehensive package of activities include; increase learning space for refugees by construction of 16 units of primary school classrooms and rehabilitate 12 units of classrooms. WASH in schools will be improved by construction of units of 8 hand washing stations in targeted schools. Gender sensitive and segregated latrines will be constructed at target school and all schools will be supported with furniture and seating. 7,312 students in target school will be provided with uniform, school supplies and learning materials. 120 teachers will be trained on COVID 19 prevention and control, and will be supported with primary kits and furniture. 120 teachers in targeted schools will be supported with monthly incentives to encourage them for delivery of quality teaching services to refugees.

The project will provide and distribute personal hygiene materials especially for women, provision of soap to HHs, and solid waste and disposal systems, in addition to building the refugees capacities on different WASH related trainings.
In regard to FSL, the project will support SSR and Ethiopian refugees in El Nuhud and Basundah through delivering FSL activities including; provision of agricultural and livestock support, vocational trainings, and provide cash based interventions as well as support the activities for youth issues

project_name: Preparedness and response to Epidemic-Prone Diseases through enhancement of disease surveillance and prevention measures in Syria.
project_objective:
Infectious diseases are major causes of high morbidity and mortality in humanitarian crises. In 2021, Syria experienced several major outbreaks from emerging and re-emerging diseases, including COVID-19, acute diarrhea, and Leishmaniasis. Also, the current outbreak of COVID-19, which reported 50,674 cases and 2,944 deaths (a high case fatality rate (CFR) of 5.8%) as of 15 January 2022, remains active and has been threatening the country.
The principal risk factors contributing to the emergence and rapid spread of epidemic diseases in Syria include acute and protracted humanitarian emergencies resulting in fragile health systems, increased population mobility, climate change and draught, environmental deterioration, weak surveillance and limited laboratory diagnostic capacity, and decline in affordable health services.

These epidemic threats, compounded by protracted complex emergencies, remain potentially devastating to development in Syria, through decline the economic situation, increase poverty, increase avoidable medical costs, loss of manpower due to immigration, and difficulties in access to health services. The need to prevent, quickly detect and respond to any infectious disease outbreaks that pose persistent threats to global health security remains a national priority and requires proper preparedness and effective surveillance system in order to deliver effective and systematic response to health emergencies.

The Early Warning and Response System was established in response to the Syrian Crisis, and EWARN in NWS,  with the objective of addressing the increased potential for communicable disease outbreaks.  Although EWARS has become well established in the country and had largely replaced the main national routine surveillance system, however, new concerns about the spread of infectious diseases, especially emerging diseases such as COVID-19 or pandemic influenza, have emphasis the importance of enhancing the early warning and rapid response surveillance system in addition to the existing routine surveillance system and build integrated surveillance system.  
This project’s aim is to reduce morbidity and mortality due to preventable infectious diseases among general and vulnerable populations (IDPs, refugees and host communities) by enhancing emergency preparedness and response capacities in Syria. 
Specific objectives:
1.	Enhance surveillance system for timely detection and responses to outbreaks and improve the availability of descriptive disease epidemiology data, outbreak early detection and response, provide data required for assessment of disease prevention and control interventions, in addition to improve the information system of surveillance by using a web-based interface with integration of other vertical surveillance systems to detect unusual events that might signal an outbreak.  
2.	Enhance the country’s capacities for timely laboratory confirmation, as outlined in the international health regulations (2005), and to facilitate the transfer of safe and appropriate diagnostic technologies, practices and training to laboratories in the zones of emergence of these diseases. 
3.	Support prevention and control of epidemic prone diseases through the provision of lifesaving medicines and vaccines for effective case management especially for children and women
4.	Strengthening multisectoral health emergencies and outbreak response coordination and community engagement in the surveillance and response to disease outbreaks. 

The project will be implemented through close coordination and consultation with MoH, health directorates at the governorates and district levels, as well as other health partners and NGOs. the project will also contribute to strengthen the capacity of health partners through capacity building and technical support activities for surveillance and lab officers. and will ensure the availability of reliable disease surveillance data, and secure treatment and case management of Infectious disease

project_name: Accroître l'accès à une éducation de qualité, inclusive et sensible au genre pour les garçons et les filles touchés par la crise sécuritaire et sanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le secteur de l'éducation au Burkina Faso est durement touché par les attaques terroristes et le Covid-19. Les attaques contre les écoles, les élèves et les enseignants ont entraîné la fermeture de 2 512 écoles (13,20% des écoles à l'échelle nationale) et privé d'accès à l'éducation plus de 349 909 élèves et 11 219 enseignants au 21 septembre 2020. À la fin de l'année 2020, 100 écoles ont été attaquées et brûlées. Cette situation a été exacerbée par Covid-19 qui a imposé la fermeture de toutes les écoles de mars à mai 2020 et l'adoption de mesures restrictives et préventives pour l'année scolaire 2020 – 2021. Les besoins prioritaires dans ce secteur de l'éducation sont : le renforcement du bien-être physique et mental, de la résilience et des capacités d'adaptation des acteurs de l'éducation et des élèves (approche de l'école sûre et RRC, PSS et SEL pour les élèves et les enseignants) ; l'augmentation de la capacité d'accueil des écoles d'accueil, le développement d'opportunités d'apprentissage communautaires en lien avec les services de protection et de santé, la promotion d'écoles sûres et d'espaces d'apprentissage sûrs accessibles pour assurer la protection des plus vulnérables (filles, enfants vivant avec un handicap, etc.), la promotion des droits des enfants, en particulier ceux vivant avec un handicap), les partenariats communautaires (par exemple avec les associations de parents/mères et d'enseignants pour promouvoir la scolarisation des jeunes filles, les organisations de personnes handicapées, etc. ), la promotion des droits des enfants, en particulier ceux qui vivent avec un handicap), les partenariats communautaires (par exemple avec les associations de parents/mères et d'enseignants pour promouvoir la scolarisation des jeunes filles, les organisations de personnes handicapées, etc.), le développement de nouvelles approches programmatiques (Cash, enseignement à distance via la radio/le domicile, Edu Track, etc.) En outre, il est nécessaire de ramener les enfants non scolarisés dans le système éducatif et de mettre en place des programmes d'autonomisation économique pour les jeunes.   En mars 2020, avant la fermeture des écoles due au COVID-19, l'insécurité affectait gravement le système éducatif et les acteurs dénombraient 2 512 écoles fermées, affectant 349 909 élèves et 11 219 enseignants. Au début de l'année scolaire 2020-2021, il y avait encore 2 398 écoles fermées en raison de l'insécurité, affectant environ 350 000 élèves. Selon l'UNOCHA HN0 2021, 2,1% des personnes déplacées vivent avec un handicap, et 34% des enfants sont exposés au risque de recrutement par des groupes armés, au travail forcé ou à d'autres phénomènes. Un enfant sur quatre est affecté par au moins une forme de violence, et les violences sexuelles touchent 3,1% des enfants âgés de 12 à 17 ans au Burkina Faso.  Selon le MENAPLN, en 2018, le nombre de jeunes filles enceintes était de 1504 en 2017 et de 1639 en 2018. 
Le projet sera mis en œuvre dans les régions du Burkina Faso touchées par la crise et se concentrera sur l'amélioration de la qualité et de la pertinence de l'éducation pour tous les enfants, en particulier les filles et les enfants en situation de vulnérabilité dans les zones touchées par l'insécurité et d'autres facteurs de risque. Le deuxième domaine d'intérêt est d'améliorer la coordination et le pilotage de l'ensemble du secteur éducatif en travaillant avec les autorités et les communautés éducatives. Le dernier domaine d'intérêt vise à accroître les compétences de résilience et à mieux préparer les parents/soignants - hommes et femmes - à s'adapter et à continuer à fournir des soins et un soutien aux jeunes enfants touchés par une catastrophe, un conflit ou un déplacement.

project_name: Protection and Integrated Assistance for Ethiopian and South Sudanese Refugees and Vulnerable Host Communities in Khartoum, Gedaref, South Kordofan, and White Nile.
project_objective:
The country refugee response plan for 2022 integrates multiple programmatic sectors. The LFS response will provide life-saving multipurpose cash and support livelihoods to foster household self-reliance. NRC will engage with the private sector to provide opportunities to improve market-based approaches for both safety nets and livelihoods activities. Communities will be consulted on the most suitable livelihood activities to be supported by the project. Efforts towards an integrated approach by targeting the same communities with food security, livelihoods and interventions from other sectors will be done to strengthen the holistic approach.

The legal protection action will aim to address the limited access to legal identity including civil documentation for the most vulnerable refugees and support the Ethiopian emergency response by facilitating access to essential services and promoting social cohesion through collaborative dispute resolution. The project will provide information, counselling and legal assistance, integrated capacity building and collaborative dispute resolution to achieve this. The project will also work to strengthen capacities of civil registries and local authorities.

The WASH response will ensure that the most vulnerable refugees have access to safe drinking water and sanitation through household level interventions, support water safety plans from the distribution points up to the point of use and provide family shared emergency latrines and vector control interventions. The response will further upgrade/ expand small-scale water infrastructures for both host community and refugees, increase the water supply, improve the water quality which will consequently reduce conflicts over scarce natural resources. Market-based approach will be utilised to effectively meet people’s WASH needs.

The shelter action will undertake the provision of adequate shelters and NFI for refugees, rehabilitation/repairs of existing shelters to ensure minimum protection against the elements, and replenish and/or issue essential NFI kits for the most vulnerable groups. The response will additional support the establishment of communal infrastructures to facilitate social cohesion and integration with host communities. 

The EiE intervention and support will focus on enabling refugee and vulnerable host community boys and girls of school age to gain access to timely, safe and quality education through addressing multiple barriers preventing their education. Structural upgrades, rehabilitation of schools, WASH facilities and distribution of essential hygiene supplies and teaching and learning materials will be a key component.

The action will continue to develop a Digital Community Hub (DCH) which will serve as a two-way communication platform with people of concern. Information distributed through the platform will include life-saving and life improving awareness-raising messages as well as information on how to access services. Similarly, people of concern will be able to ask questions, raise emergency alerts, communicate their needs and obtain referrals for services, and voice complaints or feedback via the hub.

The project will assist the most vulnerable refugee households to meet their basic needs through multi-purpose cash assistance. A market assessment will be undertaken before the proposed cash intervention.

NRC will also undertake advocacy interventions for refugees right and protection issues.

The response will target the most vulnerable refugees living in camps, camp-like, out-of-camp and urban settings in White Nile and Gedaref and those in formal or informal settlements in South Kordofan and Khartoum (i.e. the open areas). Beneficiary targeting, within refugee communities and their nearby hosting communities, will be done by applying socio-economic vulnerability criteria.

project_name: Improving access to safe and nutritious food and enhancing the livelihoods opportunities for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in Sudan
project_objective:
The NRC's Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) core competence will aim at provide an holistic response for displacement affected population including IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities, utilizing a people cantered approach paired with an evidence-based decision making process ensuring adequate response analysis in the different Area offices. NRC currently has LFS outreach in 3 different States in Sudan (i.e. Khartoum, Gadaref and South Kordofan).
The LFS core competency, towards 2022, will implement activities to ensure emergency access to food in areas with IPC level 3 and above, will support rural and agricultural systems through activities focused to enhance: small food production, smallholders' access to markets and improve natural resources management. Moreover, the core competence will support access to income generating activities and employment fostering, in particular, youth entrepreneurship and youth's labour market penetration. 
In delivering its response the NRC's LFS core competency will implement its activities through a market-based approach ensuring sound response analysis and decision making; foundation of the LFS response will also be inclusive and safe programming ensuring safe participation of beneficiaries and adequate protection concepts mainstreaming.

project_name: Supporting access to Housing, Land and Property rights and Legal identity including Civil documentation for displacement affected communities
project_objective:
With the looming economic crisis, uncertain political environment coupled by recent waves of conflict and displacement in North and West Darfur, the context in Sudan remains very fragile. IDP's in the 3 States, North Darfur, West Darfur and South Kordofan continue to face significant challenges to access documentation and enforce their rights to housing, land and property. At the same time recent developments such as the Juba Peace Agreement and the National Protection of civilians plans provide opportunities that could potentially crystallise to support displacement affected communities to attain durable solutions. Conflict over land and natural resources in Darfur and South Kordofan regions remain prevalent and have resulted in massive destruction of property and displacement. Rampant secondary occupation and ongoing disputes over land and natural resources have been identified as a major cause of conflict and hindrance to attaining durable solution in the return context. Inability to access legal identity and civil documents additionally gives rise to various protection concerns including; limited access to essential services, livelihood and employment opportunities.
This project will aim to support displacement affected communities to claim their rights through;
1) Promoting the exercise and enjoyment of housing, land and property rights - The project will create awareness on housing, land and property rights in displacement and contribute towards conflict prevention and non-escalation through peaceful resolution of disputes over land and natural resources. The HLP response will focus on supporting IDP’s and displacement affected communities to attain adequate housing, security of tenure, eviction monitoring and strengthening dispute resolution processes and structures.
2) Facilitating increased access to legal identity and civil documentation. The project will aim to contribute towards the ability to exercise and enjoy rights as a result of increased access and use of legal identity and civil documentation (LCD). Access to legal identity and civil documents is expected to result in increased access and enjoyment of basic services such as education, health, financial inclusion as well as increased access and enjoyment of protection, freedom of movement, security and due process.  for displacement affected communities as well as the 
To achieve these objectives the project will  1) ensure that displacement affected communities are better informed about their HLP and legal identity rights through information sessions, information education and communication (IEC) materials, mobile counselling, individualized legal assistance and collaborative dispute resolution 2) enhance understanding amongst authorities, community leaders, and humanitarian actors on HLP rights and the importance of legal identity and civil documentation through integrated capacity building and 3) promote HLP mainstreaming through adoption of due diligence approach before humanitarian interventions which have an implications on land use and ownership.
The project will target vulnerable displacement affected populations including; IDP’s, returnees, host community and conflict affected communities in Darfur and South Kordofan. Access to HLP rights and legal identity documents are gendered issues with regularly recurring instances of gender inequality regarding ownership of housing, land and property and access to legal documentation. This project will target 60% of female beneficiaries to address this gendered gap.

project_name: Improving access to safe, inclusive quality education for displacement-affected children in Sudan
project_objective: Through collaboration and coordination with key education stakeholders, the project will identify and address leading barriers to accessing education for children and communities affected by displacement; IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities to enable enrolment and retention.

project_name: Mejorando el acceso a servicios WASH en centros escolares y comunidades en Honduras
project_objective:
En el último año NRC ha proporcionado soluciones completas de acceso al agua, saneamiento y promoción de la higiene en once centros educativos ubicados en cinco municipios y alcanzando 6221 NNAJ.
NRC ha entregado 6356 kits de higiene personal diferenciados por género y edad en entornos escolares y comunidades, acompañando las distribuciones de sesiones de promoción de la higiene con enfoque COVID-19.
Durante la emergencia por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, NRC intervino 21 albergues ubicados en 3 municipios brindando soluciones de mejora de sistemas de agua, cabinas de aseo personal diferenciadas por género, reservorios de agua y 4500 kits de higiene diferenciados.
El enfoque integral que caracteriza las intervenciones del NRC ha permitido que estos centros educativos cuenten al día de hoy además de servicios WASH básicos, con estructuras dignas, seguras e inclusivas que reducen el ausentismo en las aulas de clase.
El equipo técnico de NRC diseña proyectos de agua y saneamiento en conjunto con las comunidades de modo de proveer soluciones que se adapten al contexto, usuarios, ecoamigables, duraderas y sostenibles.
Aunado a las intervenciones en infraestructura NRC trabaja fuertemente con estudiantes, docentes, personal administrativo, padres o cuidadores y comunidades vulnerables en procesos de cambio de comportamiento en temas de higiene actualizando con la periodicidad que se requiere los mensajes claves acorde con los cambios en el entorno.

project_name: Apoyando el desarrollo equitativo y el empoderamiento de las zonas rurales incrementando la resiliencia para limitar el desplazamiento en Honduras
project_objective: A través de este proyecto NRC pretende enfocarse en dos áreas: la primera apoyará el desarrollo equitativo por medio de cadenas de valor justas y la segunda empoderará a las zonas rurales marginadas por medio de sistemas de alerta temprana para la acción anticipada. De esta manera se incrementará la resiliencia y se limitará el desplazamiento forzado.

project_name: Construyendo Espacios Protectores y Amigables para la Niñez y Adolescencia que se encuentran en riesgo de desplazamiento por causa de la violencia en Honduras
project_objective:
NRC Honduras desde el año 2016 está proporcionando una respuesta de protección sectorial y focalizada, frente a las necesidades más críticas derivadas de la violencia estructural y de género; el enfoque de implementación se centra en la prevención de todas las formas de violencia y la respuesta de protección, promoviendo el acceso a información, orientación y asistencia legal. Esto refleja una brecha en la respuesta humanitaria actual, en la cual las necesidades y vulnerabilidades más sentidas de las mujeres, niñez, adolescencia, padres, madres y cuidadores de familia no han sido atendidas; de igual manera se identifica la debilidad en el sistema de protección nacional y sus instituciones. Las intervenciones de protección buscan prevenir, mitigar y responder contra el abuso, la explotación y el daño que se puede generar en las poblaciones que han sido afectadas significativamente por los desastres naturales acaecidos recientemente; agravándolas condiciones de pobreza, desigualdades, inseguridad, la violencia y la afectación generada por la pandemia del COVID 19.
El proyecto fortalecerá las capacidades del personal de atención de instituciones gubernamentales vinculados a la promoción y protección de derechos y responsables de la atención de casos derivados.
Asimismo, implementará una estrategia de respuesta a través de la construcción de espacios protectores a la niñez y adolescencia, acompañada de recursos y materiales que permitirá el desarrollo de actividades recreativas y de aprendizaje de saberes que contribuirán en el fortalecimiento de capacidades de autoprotección, educación socioemocional y resiliencia.

project_name: Garantizando una mejora de la situación de protección, seguridad y dignidad de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento forzado en Honduras
project_objective:
NRC ha estado presente en Centro América a partir del año 2015, lo que ha permitido a la organización desarrollar herramientas técnicas adaptadas al contexto de la región. La metodología desarrollada tiene como objetivo fortalecer las instituciones estatales y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil (OSC), establecer mecanismos para proporcionar una respuesta integral a las personas de interés y promover el acceso a la protección y los derechos básicos de las personas.

Los altos niveles de delincuencia y violencia en Honduras, han afectado gravemente el ejercicio y goce efectivo de los derechos humanos y al acceso a los servicios básicos en el país. Las personas huyen de la explotación, la extorsión, el reclutamiento forzado y la violencia sexual, y buscan protección en otros lugares.

La asistencia humanitaria durante 2020 y lo que va de 2021 ha tenido retos extraordinarios para su implementación, las crisis causadas por la pandemia por COVID-19 y los huracanes ETA e IOTA, han tenido un impacto fuerte en las familias desplazadas, quienes tienen dificultades para acceder a la vivienda, trabajos estables y formales, educación, alimentación, salud y protección.

Por lo antes mencionado este proyecto busca que personas con necesidad de protección, reciban asistencia humanitaria, acceden a derechos y servicios especializados y que fortalezcan sus capacidades de autoprotección, para que puedan denunciar el abuso o la mala conducta por parte de personas trabajadoras humanitarias. Se busca implementar acciones de protección comunitaria y vincular entidades estatales con estas actividades, lo permitirá fortalecer el tejido comunitario y brindar más posibilidades de prevención de la violencia en las comunidades y de responder a emergencias con mayor prontitud.
