project_name: Niger Country Strategic Plan
project_objective:
La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_name: Renforcer la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigue chez les IDP et les communautés hôtes du département de Ouallam - région de Tillabery
project_objective:
GOAL soutiendra les activités de nutrition curative (CRENAS/CRENI) au niveau des centres de santé ainsi celles de la prévention de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire (relais, PB mères etc.) tout en renforçant la coordination des acteurs. L’objectif principal est de contribuer à réduire la mortalité et la morbidité chez les enfants de moins de cinq en facilitant le dépistage et la prise en charge précoce de cas.  GOAL entend à travers cette intervention consolider les acquis du projet issu du financement de fond régional pour l’Afrique de ouest et du centre à travers OCHA. Il s’agira pour GOAL d’élargir sa couverture mais aussi de renforcer la qualité de la prise en charge dans tout le DS de Ouallam. Le DS de Ouallam à une population estimée en 2022 à 469.183 personnes dont 108.078 des enfants de moins de 5 ans soit 23,03%(source INS 2021).
L’appui concernera 31 CSI, l’unité de stabilisation (CRENI) du DS de Ouallam et ciblera 6744 enfants 6-59 mois souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère. Le taux de la malnutrition aigue sévère à Tillabery étant de 2,4 %selon l'enquête SMART nutrition de 2021 et tenant compte de l’incidence de la malnutrition de 2,6 . Aussi 548 enfants avec malnutrition sévère avec complications médicales sont attendus au CRENI (source INS 2021). 
Les mères accompagnantes de enfants au CRENI bénéficieront également un appui en aliments et auront une formation sur le dépistage au MUAC en plus de sensibilisations sur les PFE et ANJE. 
Les actions se focaliseront également sur le renforcement de capacité des acteurs communautaires et des agents de santé à travers la mise en œuvre et ou le suivi de l'approche CMAM surge pour renforcer la résilience du système de santé. Les activités qui seront appuyées comprennent le dépistage de la malnutrition et le référencement des cas, la vaccination, mise en place des dispositifs de lavage des mains, Approche PB mères, les sensibilisations ANJE/PFE contre la COVID-19

project_name: Assistance en abris et biens non alimentaires pour 1 000 ménages des déplacés internes du département de Ouallam, région de Tillabéry
project_objective:
Nonobstant le contexte sécuritaire volatile, GOAL Niger vise à travers le présent projet, l'appui humanitaire pour un millier de ménages en termes en biens non alimentaires, dans les communes rurales de Ouallam et Tondikiwindi, qui concentrent l'essentiel des déplacés. Pour les abris, GOAL envisage des kits d'abris standards pour les nouveaux arrivants et également des abris en matériaux semi-définitifs pour les ménages les plus vulnérables et exposés.
Fort de sa présence opérationnelle sur les 4 sites d'accueil de Ouallam et Tondikiwindi, GOAL Niger, à travers ce projet, vise à apporter une assistance à 1 000 ménages vulnérables soit environ 7,000 personnes déplacées  dans le département de Ouallam.  Cette assistance concernera 2 axes majeurs à savoir:
- pour les ménages nouvellement déplacés, 500 kits abri standard en bâche et matériaux locaux respectueux de l'environnement. GOAL envisage également la réalisation de 100 batiments de 2 pièces en matériaux semi-définitifs (avec toit en zinc) pour les plus vulnérables, compte tenu de la persistance de la crise et du niveau de dégradation des anciens kits placés par nombres d'acteurs. Il est à noter le fort impact lié à l'investissement local dans la cadre de la construction des abris semi-définitifs à travers l'acquissition des matériaux locaux et de la main d'oeuvre. Ce qui contribue une source importante de revenus pour les déplacés et les populations hotes. 
- un kit de NFI composé également de 2 nattes plastiques de 2 places, 2 moustiquaires MILDA, 2 couvertures, 3 serviettes hygieniques, 3 slips pour femme, 1 lampe torche,1  bouilloire, 1 bassine de 100 litres, 2 tasses plastiques, 2 bols plastiques, 1 seau de 15 litres,  15 morceaux de savons et 2 marmites.
Des masques relavables seront également distribués dans le cadre de la lutte contre la Covid-19, pour accompagner la campagne de sensibilisation Covid-16 sur la base de l'aproche community Lead action (CLA), qui a déjà été expérimentée par GOAL dans la région de Zinder et la commune de Ouallam.
Le ciblage par rapport à cette assistance accordera la priorité aux ménages des personnes vivant avec handicap,  les ménages dirigées par les femmes, ceux dirigés par des enfants ou acueillant des enfants non accompagnés  et les ménages avec les personnes agées.
le ciblage sera effectué sur la base d'une enquête HEA, completée par la mise à jour des listings tenus par les gestionnaires des sites. Par ailleurs, les bénéficiaires désigneront des délégués qui seront assosociés dans la conduite de l'identification avec la pleine implication des chefs traditionnels locaux (chefs de villages).
Pour ce projet les localités ont été choisis conjointement avec les membres du groupe de travail abris et biens non alimentaires (GTABNA) pour éviter les doublons dans les interventions. Nous pouvons être plusieurs partenaires dans les mêmes départements ou communes, mais nous intervenons généralement dans des localités différentes.

project_name: Emergency  support for IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Blue Nile state
project_objective: The proposed project is an integrated emergency project that will cover thematic areas of FSL, Education and WASH for 22,190 person (7056 women, 6258men, 4615 girl and 4260 boy) from Damazine, Kurmuk, Rosaries, Wad Almahi and Geissan localities in Blue Nile state. The project is aimed at providing the affected vulnerable communities  with sustainable basic services to ensure well-being, improved food security at the HH level, improved enrolment and retention of school going children, provide gender for  and culturally sensitive WASH and protection services while ensuring sustainable environmental practices. The proposed project will complement and linked to existing IRW projects in the proposed project sites and will include of construction and rehabilitation of WASH facilities, construction and rehabilitating school facilities and infrastructure including hygiene and sanitation facilities, providing small holder farmers with seeds and tools, capacity building of community members and healthcare staff on hygiene and sanitation while incorporating Covid-19 awareness and prevention. The proposed will thus contribute to improved and increased access to basic services by the affected vulnerable men, women, boys and girls while creating resilience and sustainability. IRW will coordinate the project activities with other partners and respective government departments in the project sites including UN agencies such as UNICEF, WFP, UNOCHA, WHO and UNHCR. Implementation strategy will be direct implementation strategy while IRW will also involve its implementation partners in community mobilization and engagement.

project_name: Appui à la restauration et la protection des moyens d'existence pour l'amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages affectés par la crise du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
La crise dans la Province du Lac a débuté fin 2014 à la suite des premières attaques de groupes armés non étatiques qui ont entrainé des mouvements de populations et bousculé les échanges et équilibres socio-économiques dans cette région, déjà en proie aux effets du réchauffement climatique qui y aggravent notamment l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle.
La dégradation des conditions sécuritaires en raison de l’intensification des attaques des Groupes Armés Non Etatiques (GANE) et des opérations de l’armée est la cause principale de la détérioration de la situation humanitaire.
Depuis 2020, le nombre total de déplacés dans la province du Lac a plus que doublé passant de                         272 000 personnes à 457 948 individus en Aout et Septembre 2021 (round 16 DTM Octobre 2021). Suivant le plan opérationnel du Lac, plus de 549 000 personnes sont estimées être dans le besoin d’une aide humanitaire. En plus, suivant les résultats de l'analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2021, 198587 personnes sont signalées être en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle. 
Outres les conflits, les principales causes qui ont conduit plusieurs milliers de personnes à ne pouvoir s’assurer une alimentation et une vie socio-économique décente, sont généralement liées aux conditions de naissance (mères très jeunes et naissances fréquentes), manque de diversification de la diète, manque de connaissance, les changements climatiques et le manque d’éducation ainsi que la pauvreté et les conditions et pratiques sanitaires. Les femmes, les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que les jeunes filles sont les principales victimes du non-respects des droits humains. Au Lac, la situation liée à la protection des femmes et des filles demeure préoccupante et pour des raisons culturelles, cette catégorie de population n'a pas le même niveau d’accès à l’éducation, aux ressources naturelles, aux services de base et paradoxalement, ces femmes et filles représentent la principale source de changement tant attendu dans les ménages.
En effet, la FAO se propose d'exécuter les actions de renforcement des moyens d'existence pour améliorer la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle des personnes pauvres et très pauvres.

project_name: Safe learning environments and improved access to quality education for the most vulnerable children in Aleppo, Dar’a, Hama, Idleb, Quneitra and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
•	All the targeted sub-districts fall under severity scores 3-5 based on the HNO Education PiN severity shared by the sector.
•	The cost per beneficiary is $240 as the activities include rehabilitation of schools.
•	Beneficiaries with disabilities is estimated at 5%.
•	Total funding that ZOA received in 2021 was $4,732,378  of which $1,200,000 was SHF funding.
•	Total secured funding for ZOA for the year 2022 is $2,122,655.
•	The total number of beneficiaries that ZOA reached for all sectors in 2021 was 110,000. In 2021 ZOA implemented a pilot education project. 
•	ZOA has secured funding from institutional fundraising and private donors for an education project in Aleppo for 2022.

11 years of conflict have led to the fracturing and under-resourcing of the education system, consequently limiting the ability of children to access education. COVID-19 has added another layer of complexity, further acerbating education constraints. This project is aimed at increasing access to quality education for the most vulnerable children affected by conflict in target locations and build the capacity of the education personnel. Proposed activities are rehabilitation of schools/classrooms to increase access to protected, safe and friendly learning spaces and to ease overcrowding and encourage smooth return to
schools; improvement and rehabilitation of gender-sensitive WASH facilities, provision of education supplies for both students and teachers; provision of school furniture, school bags and teaching/learning materials; teacher training and capacity building; and PSS activities together with the provision of COVID-19 PPE. Proposed target locations are underserved areas in the governorates of Aleppo, Dar’a, Hama, Idleb, Quneitra and Rural Damascus.

Through the project during 2022-23 ZOA is going to target 10,000 beneficiaries (without double counting), taking the special needs of the PWDs into consideration in its activities. In the event of limited funding, ZOA will prioritize areas falling under higher severity scales. The project targets 11 different schools in 6 different governorates over 2 years.

The core beneficiaries of the project are 3-17 years school age children as well as teachers, who will benefit from the main project activities, while parents will benefit from awareness sessions. Apart, a Parent Teacher Association will be established per school and 1 parent engagement initiative will be supported per school/community.

The project is in line with the Education Sector’s objectives since it is focusing on the Sector Objective 1 “Availability & Access - Increased safe and equitable availability and access to in-person and home-based formal and non-formal education for crisis-affected children and youth”, and Objective 2 “Quality -Enhanced quality of formal and non-formal education for children and youth”. Also, the project aims at responding to HRP 2022 Strategic Objective 3.1: “Improved access to basic services, electricity, water, education and health.”

Also, ZOA is aiming to provide humanitarian services with a holistic approach. Therefore ZOA is either present already in the targeted locations providing different services, or the locations are part of ZOA’s 2022-23 plans to have intervention in various sectors, so that resilience of beneficiaries is built. ZOA will choose hybrid modality of implementation, some of the activities will be implemented through partners and some self-implementation. ZOA will choose the best positioned partner from its local implementing partners pool to carry out the activities.

project_name: Increased food security through sustainable activities for most vulnerable households in Aleppo, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Hama, Idlib, Quneitra and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
In 2021 ZOA implemented projects in multiple sectors including FSA, reaching a total of 118,130 beneficiaries. In 2021 ZOA was able to secure $4.7M in funding, of which $1.2M was SHF funding. ZOA was able to allocate $1.7M for activities under FSA, reaching out to 38,000 beneficiaries, thus exceeding its 2021 budget as well as beneficiary target. In 2022 ZOA has to date secured $2.1M with around $1M allocated for FSA. 

Through its 2022-23 proposal ZOA is proposing an expansion of its interventions to reach communities most in need of food security in underserved, conflict affected areas in Aleppo, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Hama, Idlib, Quneitra & Rural Damascus. Based on community based needs assessments & sector guidance, ZOA will target the most insecure households (HHs) with an emphasis on those in areas with high severity of needs. Activities are aimed at improving the food security status of assessed food insecure HHs through life sustaining food assistance. According to needs, market assessments, Ministry of Agriculture & Agrarian Reform (MoAAR) as well as sector guidance and beneficiary preference, appropriate modalities that include vouchers, cash assistance, grants & other support to small-medium farmers will be used. Assistance will be prioritized to the most vulnerable groups that include female-headed HHs, persons with disabilities & elderly. The other activities are building of an irrigation tank, rehabilitation of irrigation wells, provision of solar power & rehabilitation of animal vaccination centers as well as bakeries.

ZOA prioritizes communities with high severity needs, & selects vulnerability & selection criteria in line with sector standards. ZOA’s vulnerability criteria also incorporates protection concerns including PWDs. Issues or concerns highlighted during assessments feed into project & implementation planning to ensure a mainstreaming approach & impactful support to HHs. Project committees will be set up to oversee the project implementation & take ownership of the project activities after project end. Voucher & cash values will be based on Cash Working Group (CWG) as well as Sector recommendations. During 2022-23 at least 21,300 HHs are targeted & the cost per beneficiary is estimated to be $50.

The proposed interventions are in line with the specific objective 2 and 3 of the Sector. The HNO FSA sector chapter is encouraging to move from emergency intervention into more sustainable activities changing the humanitarian work dimensions into early recovery and resilience (HNO 2022-23 FSA Chapter). All targeted sub-districts have 3-4 severity score according to the FSA HNO PiN 2022. Before launching any activity a verification of the needs will be done with local communities as well as authorities, & activities will be altered accordingly.

ZOA has taken into consideration the FSA sector recommendation & is aware of the HRP 2021 related document “Recommendations for Response Packages for Specific Objectives 2 & 3.” We will also take into consideration the CWG recommendations. Therefore all Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance will be 225,000 SYP on average per family. As we do not have the financial capacity to do these distributions over 8 months, all MPCA distributions are planned for 3 months. ZOA will inform its plans through the FSA 4Ws so that duplication of activities are avoided. As for the agricultural input the cap per farmer will be $400 for the whole agricultural season. We are targeting farmers with small to medium capacity, in order to support their livelihood.

ZOA actively participates in the monthly meetings of the FSA sector as well as the Cash Working Group, which is valuable in case any updates are shared by the Sector &/or the Group. Through its flexible programming ZOA will be able to adapt the changes based on the new recommendations. Also, during the past year ZOA closely coordinated its activities with the Ministry of Agriculture, thus establishing a cooperation with the Ministry.

project_name: Rehabilitation of schools, wash in schools, and vocational institutes.
project_objective:
Education services remain highly prioritized and are a critical bridge between relief and early recovery. Supporting education services under a protracted crisis necessitates simultaneously addressing immediate needs and fostering coherent service delivery especially for the most vulnerable people. Under SO1: Availably & Access according to ""Sub-district Severity, Aleppo –Jabal Saman severity score/4/ and Dayr Hafir& Rasm Harma Al –Imam and Eastren Kwairse severity score/3/.
ONG Rescate as part of its responsibility towards the community, submits this proposal to rehabilitate and provide supplies, remedial classes in cooperation with ST, in addition to teachers capacity building: plan in 2022 to rehabilitate and equip
- One Girls vocational school in Aleppo,
- This intervention is a response to NLG the data reveals that 18% are out of school and half of the children who are not in school never enrolled. children face potential risks when traveling to school which may limit access to education services. Over a 1/4 households with school aged children indicated that their children are not in school because there is no school to send their child to.  
Hence two elementary schools in Rural Aleppo, (Yousef al Azmah and Um Al Mara) to facilitate attendance for dropout students due to unsafe road especially for children, and overcrowded classrooms.
Rescate will support 11 schools in (Dayr Hafir-Rasm Harma Al-Imam-Eastren Kwairse). The project focus is students who are attending in the near over-crowded schools 80-90 students/classroom, without functional wash facilities. So, students’ dropout from schooling.
Rescate intervention is an area based approach as Rescate just opened a public Market in Dayr Hafir and the schools rehabilitation is in response to student's families request, the schools are in the surrounding of this facility.
On another urgent need based on this situation analysis Youth and adolescents (10 to 24 years old), representing over 30 per cent of the entire population, struggled to access learning opportunities, vocations or to have meaningful engagement in their communities. Many adolescents had no access to schooling during the height of the crisis and are now unable to return to school due to over age and are in desperate need of alternative pathways. Vocations Institutions are the solution for them since they abandoned school to work, therefore; vocation institutes will support their livelihood.
• In some situations, girls and boys, including recruits and those with disabilities, were also at risk of
additional and multiple forms of violence due to their economic vulnerability. Life Skills and Citizenship Education (LSCE) will be provided to these young people (52% girls) to enhance critical thinking, communication, collaboration and creativity skills to propose solutions to local social challenges.
Rescate plan to rehabilitate and include renewable energy at two community centers in cooperation with the Syria Trust for Development (ST) subject to fund availability to conduct vocational trainings at the centers for students who are out of schooling since years and they are between 14-24 years. Curricula will include remedial classes in addition to vocational trainings mainly on 8 vocations which are needed for rehabilitation of houses, souks, and schools. including furniture production and historical sites restoration handicrafts. Vocational trainings will cover Stone work, Masonry, Carpentry, Smith work, WASH, Electrical works, Glass Paint and Wood works. Tool start up kits will be distributed. 
These will be vocational institutes in community centers to fill the gap for youth boys and girls to be self reliant, productive professional persons who will cover the gap of handicrafts workers. This is for 2023 plans in coordination with the education sector, MoE and ST. entrepreneurship plans will be arranged in coordination with the chambers of industry and trade, and with private sector.

project_name: Rehabilitation of damaged houses for returnees in Deir Ez Zour
project_objective:
This project is proposed in response to the Shelter Sector Objective 2: Strengthen the resilience and cohesion of vulnerable communities by improving housing and related community or public infrastructure. Hence; this project is designed to meet the dire need of returnees’ population in based on HNO 2022, DEZ population 279440, Pin 197584, acute PiN 169920, at risk PiN 27664, and severity score is 4.  Rescate had finished Water and sanitation rehabilitation in 2021 in Al Omal and Air Port neighborhoods. Noting that the area is eventually underserved, there are ~500 houses, yet interventions were limited to rehabilitation of ADRA 89 houses with 52 solar street lights.
The objective of the project is to rehabilitate damaged houses for vulnerable returnees, there are to date around 265 HHs returned to Al Omal and 150 HHs returned to the Old Airport district. Rescate designed a response to rehabilitate damaged houses in the two areas as a 2022 intervention for 175 damaged houses where some houses are used by three families at the same time due to acute vulnerability.  However, Rescate is planning to add 100 houses in 2023. At this stage; Rescate is submitting the proposal to rehabilitate 175 houses in Al Omal and the Old Airport areas. Focus on the Old Airport area with 100 houses because most inhabitants are fresh vulnerable returnees who are in dire need for this intervention. However, the Omal area residents returned since 2018 the reason Rescate is targeting only 75 damaged houses in Al Omal for the most vulnerable who were unable to rehabilitate their homes. Rescate conducted field assessment and detailed BOQs including market studies with updated estimation based on the SWG average costs and works to be conducted. In coordination with the municipality, a desk will be set at the Mayor office to review beneficiaries’ HLP dox. Rescate will submit the intact files for MOLAE especially Rescate has MoU so the approvals are facilitated. Shelter sector standards and buildings’ common areas will be applied to the works, with prioritization to the vulnerability score (FHHs, CHHs, elderly, families with PWDs) in addition to those who lost their jobs to COVID-19.
Due to current unstable currency and market prices, Rescate will encourage contractors to submit proposals by giving the awarded contractors a down-payment of 30% to purchase materials in mitigation to market prices changes.

project_name: Radio Ergo: Informing and Communicating with Somali Communities
project_objective: The project provides critical humanitarian information to the Somali population, especially vulnerable groups, and ensures ongoing communication between communities and responders. It is based on information needs assessed through an audience survey conducted in 2019, supported by smaller local studies of audience views conducted in 2021 and 2021. As there is no national broadcaster and the local FM radios are largely centred on urban areas, significant geographical areas are uncovered by media leaving many rural, pastoralist, farming, displaced, and poor communities without adequate access to information. The local media provides a surfeit of political and current affairs news but far less consistent, reliable issue-based programming that informs and amplifies community voices. As well as the pastoralist and farming groups named above, in particular women, youth and children, IDPs, and the disabled, lack coverage and involvement in media content. Radio Ergo’s broadcast strategy is to reach as many people as possible, using shortwave and FM combined. The purpose of this project is,1. to provide critical information through daily radio broadcasts on lifesaving and life-enhancing issues to Somalis across the country, to enable them to make better informed decisions; and 2. to amplify the voices of local communities, including the most marginalized and excluded, through a trusted feedback platform to enable them to participate in humanitarian planning and response. The original content will be produced by Radio Ergo, a dedicated humanitarian radio with an established reputation among listeners and partners for quality and professionalism. Radio Ergo’s mission is to provide relevant humanitarian and public interest information for listeners (men, women, boys and girls) across all areas, and to facilitate a participatory communication cycle between the listeners and the humanitarian community and local/national governmental authorities. The broadcasts contain original content based on a number of complementary sources. First, Radio Ergo’s unique network of around 25 locally based Somali reporters gathering interviews, reports, features and information from their areas. The local reportage will reflect needs, views, and developments from different genders, age groups, social backgrounds and livelihoods. Second, practical humanitarian and developmental information and advice, aligned with cluster key messaging and advocacy, is incorporated into the radio programming in various formats including interviews with experts, discussions, question and answer, dramas, and advisories. The topics covered includes health, COVID19, agriculture, livestock, protection, displacement, etc. Secondly, Radio Ergo runs an feedback platform which is the only independent voice-based channel open continually to callers free of charge across all regions. The platform has become a popular way for people living in rural and remote areas to voice their concerns on the key issues affecting their lives, hoping to connect with the wider world including responders. Many callers are pastoralists, farmers, displaced, returnee refugees, among others. Radio Ergo compiles weekly feedback analysis reports to share with the humanitarian clusters and others as information for action. Some calls are followed up journalistically by reporters, and others are included in radio segments such as Radio Doctor, farming and livestock programmes. Relevant calls are referred to clusters and/or agencies for response. The feedback forms part of collective efforts in Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA). The project aims to harness the power of radio as the most popular means of mass communication in Somalia to save lives, raise awareness and enable informed decision-making; and to ensure the inclusion of voices that would not otherwise be heard in forums for service planning and provision.

project_name: Multi-sectoral emergency response for populations affected by the crisis in the Lake Chad basin in Cameroun
project_objective:
This project started in January 2021. As part of this intervention, AAH provides technical and organizational support to the health centers of the two health districts regularly affected by shocks in order to better equip them to respond to health / nutrition emergencies and to address psychological distress.  Health workers and community volunteers participated in trainings on health / nutrition / mental health and care practices so they can better address the different needs and facilitate referral to activities provided by AAH and other actors in the region. AAH sets up mobile clinics to provide emergency assistance in nutrition / health / mental health for affected and isolated vulnerable populations in the Mayo Sava & Mayo Tsanaga divisions). The package of services and care is delivered free of charge. It targets children under five, pregnant and lactating women, but also disabled people and the elderly among the newly displaced. With regard to the MHCP (mental health and care practices) component, the activities targets children over six and adults with a specific focus on pregnant and lactating women to ensure they follow appropriate care practices and to limit the impact of traumatic stress on pregnancies and infants.

project_name: Programme d'appui d'urgence en santé primaire et santé mentale aux populations vulnérables affectées par la crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad dans le département de Logone & Chari
project_objective:
A travers 2 cliniques mobiles, ACF propose de poursuivre l’offre directe des soins et services de Santé/Nutrition/santé mentale aux communautés frontalières vulnérabilisés par la crise du Lac Tchad (y compris les déplacés). Dans le même temps ACF maintiendra un appui technique et matériel minimal aux aires santé qui abritent les déplacés et les populations d’accès difficile afin de renforcer leurs capacités de réponses aux urgences. ACF intégrera aussi dans son intervention une composante santé mentale et soutien psychosocial, un mécanisme de référence et de contre-référence d’urgence, un système de surveillance épidémiologique et des déplacements de populations et l’approche de PB/Œdèmes par les mères.
L’objectif de l’intervention étant d’améliorer la couverture et l'accès aux soins en nutrition/santé/santé mentale des populations affectées par des chocs récurrents. Ceci ne sera rendue possible que grâce à une intervention d'urgence et en parallèle, au renforcement des capacités techniques des centres de santé accueillant régulièrement les personnes déplacées (IDPS et refugiés) pour une pérennité de l’action.  
Les cibles de l'intervention sont les populations vivant dans les communautés du département du Logone et Chari frontalières du Nigéria et vulnérabilisées par les chocs récurrents liés aux incidents sécuritaires ou affectés par la crise climatique. Les communautés qui accueillent les déplacés suite à ces incidents, seront également ciblées afin de répondre aux besoins urgents en santé/nutrition/santé mentale aussi bien pour les déplacés internes/réfugiés que les populations hôtes. Les centres de santé ciblés pour la préparation et la réponse aux urgences sont ceux qui accueillent le plus de déplacés (IDPs, Refugiés, retournés) en cas de chocs.
Au sein de ces populations déplacées et hôtes, les cibles prioritaires sont d'une part les enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi que les femmes enceintes et allaitantes. Une attention particulière sera également accordée aux hommes, femmes et enfants (y compris 6-18 ans) souffrant de traumatismes psychologiques suite aux différents chocs subis ou consécutifs à une violence basée sur le genre. Ainsi les bénéficiaires du projet pour les soins de santé se distinguent comme suit:
•	Les enfants de 0-59 moins pour les consultations curatives et les consultations préventives de l'enfant
•	Les enfants de 6-59 mois répondant à l'un des critères suivants : PB<115 mm, P/T< -3 Z score, œdèmes bilatéraux
•	Les mères d'enfants de moins 5 ans sensibilisées et formées au dépistage de la malnutrition
•	Les femmes enceintes et les femmes allaitantes 
•	Les hommes adultes déplacés en besoin d’assistance en santé/nutrition/SMPS 
•	Les personnels des centres de santé ciblés, les relais et leaders communautaires et les acteurs humanitaires (comités de protection).

project_name: Fourniture de services aériens humanitaires au Mali
project_objective:
1. Le Service aérien humanitaire des Nations Unies (UNHAS) est opérationnel au Mali depuis 2013, suite au déclenchement du conflit entre le nord et Bamako en 2012, qui a nécessité une réponse humanitaire à grande échelle dans les régions du nord et du centre du pays. Avec la détérioration continue et l'évolution du conflit au Mali au cours de la dernière décennie, UNHAS est resté un service essentiel à la communauté humanitaire dans le pays en fournissant des services de transport aérien sûrs, fiables et rentables pour les travailleurs humanitaires vers des sites éloignés, et assurer l'accès aux populations vulnérables.
2. Avec l'évolution du contexte sécuritaire, les besoins ne sont plus uniquement liés à la saisonnalité climatique, et nécessitent un soutien continu aux populations vulnérables tout au long de l'année, notamment celles touchées par les conflits et l'insécurité. Cependant, l'accès reste l'un des plus grands défis pour les partenaires humanitaires au Mali, en particulier pour la chaîne d'approvisionnement et la fourniture de services vitaux et d'assistance aux communautés touchées par le conflit ou déplacées dans le centre et le nord du pays. Tout au long de 2020 et jusqu'en 2021, la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à travers le Mali a limité et pratiquement supprimé le transport sécurisé par route. En ce sens, et depuis la levée des restrictions liées au COVID-19, UNHAS a observé une augmentation de la demande et du trafic, en ligne avec les tendances pré-COVID-19, tant pour les passagers que pour le fret léger.
2 • Fournir aux ONG, aux agences des Nations unies, aux bailleurs de fonds et aux missions diplomatiques au Mali un accès sûr, efficace et efficient vers les bénéficiaires et vers les sites de mise en oeuvre des projets.
• Transporter des marchandises légères telles que des fournitures médicales, des aliments à haute teneur énergétique et du matériel de technologies de l'information et de la communication (TIC).
• Fournir une capacité adéquate pour les évacuations médicales et sécuritaires du personnel humanitaire.
3. En effet, la demande croissante de services UNHAS avait déjà conduit à l'acquisition d'un avion supplémentaire en avril 2020, portant la flotte à trois avions. Au-delà de ses 3 avions, UNHAS gère la flotte d'ECHO Flight composée d'un avion supplémentaire depuis mai 2020, grâce auquel la communauté humanitaire est en mesure d'atteindre les sites supplémentaires de Duentza, Goundam et Nianfouke. En 2022, l'augmentation de la demande se traduira par l'exploitation supplémentaire d'un hélicoptère MI8 pour accéder aux villages et communautés les plus reculés. Cette reconfiguration de la flotte permettra à UNHAS de continuer à desservir 5 destinations régulières à travers le Mali (Mopti, Tombouctou, Gao, Bamako et Menaka) et les pistes d'atterrissage secondaires à la demande de Kayes, Ansongo, Goundam, Niafounke et Bourem, ainsi que de nouvelles des destinations telles que Kidal, Niono (Ségou), Koro et Bankass (région de Mopti) et Gourma-Rharous (Tombouctou) conformément aux demandes de l'UNCT et de la communauté humanitaire.

project_name: Provision of essential non-food items and shelter assistance to the most vulnerable families in northwest Syria and emergency response through the RRM
project_objective:
This project aims to support the SNFI response to the immediate needs of the most vulnerable displaced populations in northwest Syria through the (1) distribution of essential non–food items (NFIs) and (2) improving the basic infrastructure and shelter conditions in and out of camps. 

The distribution of NFI activities include:

I.	Provision of essential NFIs to 51,000 households - 510,000 individuals (estimated 255,000 in 2022, 255,000 in 2023) in northwest Syria through IOM’s Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) in coordination with the SNFI and CCCM clusters (activity 1.1.1.1) through both in-kind and cash modalities.
II.	Provision of tents to 48,000 households - 240,000 individuals (120,000 in 2022, 120,000 in 2023) in northwest Syria through IOM’s RRM in coordination with the SNFI and CCCM clusters (activity 1.2.1.2).
III.	Provision of procurement, storage and logistics support to humanitarian partners in Syria under the Single Source Procurement (SSP) pipeline, reaching 1,100,000 individuals (550,000 in 2022, 550,000 in 2023) with 110,000 kits per year (activity 1.1.1.1).
IV.	Provision of 80,000 winter cash payments for seasonal NFIs, reaching 400,000 individuals (200,000 in 2022, and 200,000 in 2023) (activity 1.1.1.2).

The basic infrastructure and shelter activities include:

I.	Installation and/ or construction of 7,000 temporary transitional shelters reaching 45,000 individuals (5000 shelters in 2022 reaching 25,000 individuals, 2,000 in 2023 reaching 10,000 individuals). (Activity 1.2.2.1)
II.	Implementation of site-level improvements/ infrastructure (Infrastructure in IDP sites) targeting 100 informal sites and reaching a total of 200,000 individuals (50 sites in 2022 reaching 100,000 individuals, 50 sites in 2023 reaching 100,000 individuals). (Activity 1.2.3.2)
III.	Rehabilitation of 1,800 damaged or unfinished housing, reaching 9000 individuals (800 units in 2022 reaching 4,000 individuals, 1000 units in 2023 reaching 5,000 individuals) (Activity 2.1.1.1)

Overall, the project intends to reach 1,254,000 individuals in 2022 and an estimated 1,240,000  individuals in 2023 targeting vulnerable men, women, boys and girls according to SNFI Cluster vulnerability criteria, and prioritizing those areas with high uncovered needs, as well as emergencies.

project_name: Community Revitalization & Resilience in northwest Syria
project_objective:
IOM will contribute to community revitalization and resilience through supporting local economic recovery, improving access to basic/social services, and promoting community engagement and social cohesion. The project will strengthen access to livelihoods by creating income-generating opportunities and improving access to production and market infrastructure to foster local economic recovery. This comes in line with both Early Recovery and Livelihood Sector 2021 objectives.

IOM will improve access to basic services by rehabilitating essential infrastructures identified by the communities, through a process of community engagement and consultation, as being most needed. IOM will also provide vocational training and business development support (BDS), including training and financial or in-kind support, to vulnerable IDPs for them to establish or expand their own business. Prior to implementation, IOM will identify the local market gaps in coordination with the communities. 

Furthermore, IOM will provide income-generating activity through Cash for Work (CfW) programmes to enable vulnerable beneficiaries to cover their households’ most urgent needs. CfW wages will be based on local average wages so as not to distort the local labour market, and activities will be identified in consultation with local community representatives and business owners. CfW activities will be implemented in line with the CWG’s minimum recommended actions. For all cash assistance, IOM will coordinate with the ER Cluster and the Cash Working Group to harmonize transfer values and avoid overlap.

Lastly, IOM will improve the livelihood opportunities and community engagement for IDPs and vulnerable communities through the continuation of the Community Enhancement Center (CEC) and establishment of Community Engagement Teams (CETs) in Afrin, Aleppo, A’zaz, Harim, and Idleb sub-districts.

project_name: Enhancing the protective environment for crisis affected populations in NW Syria through the provision of quality and comprehensive protection services
Whole of Syria PSEA Program
project_objective:
Since its initiation by the Syria Strategic Steering Group in 2017, the Whole of Syria (WoS) Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Program has supported the interagency humanitarian response in the joint implementation of international PSEA commitments. The WoS PSEA program is a multi-donor, comprehensive response, designed to address the risks of SEA posed by the complex and protracted humanitarian emergency in Syria. The PSEA program is designed to cover diverse contexts.through an established, robust interagency PSEA Network consisting of more than 300 focal points from senior staff in UN agencies, INGOs and NGOs, the program strives to decrease the risk of crisis‐affected communities experiencing incidents of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) by humanitarian workers and provide technical and operational support to humanitarian actors to prevent and respond to SEA cases. 

The WoS PSEA Network operates an inter-agency complaint hotline in NWS which offers humanitarian staff, beneficiaries and communities a way to make complaints related to SEA and other misconduct by aid providers. The PSEA Network receives and in a timely, confidential way coordinates the referral of the complaint to the relevant organization or agency for follow-up. In cases where there is access to the survivor, survivor assistance is always offered and if consented by the survivor, referred to GBV coordination, with outcomes closely monitored and followed up in coordination with the PSEA Network and GBV sub-cluster. The PSEA Network also offers technical advice to organizations in this process of following up on and investigating the complaint.

Through its more than 300 focal points, the PSEA Network also produces resources such as operational checklists to be used by staff during humanitarian activities to prevent SEA, codes of conduct for humanitarian staff, organizational guides to ensure accountability/reporting mechanisms exist within an organization, as well as providing mandatory PSEA Training-of-Trainers, and refreshers to all focal points, to ensure that all organizations can ensure that 100% of staff are trained on PSEA. The development of these tools, training, resources and free sharing of them, enable significant preventative measures to be in place among all actors engaged in the provision of humanitarian assistance.

The PSEA Network also directly strengthens PSEA interventions through the implementation of IP Projects focused on conducting awareness-raising sessions with both staff and beneficiaries, as well as contributing to PSEA capacity-building materials that are made accessible to other humanitarian actors. The greater community engagement with PSEA Network IPs and partner organizations also results in improved feedback provision from the community related to PSEA programming needs and preferences. Network organizations internally carry out surveys in their areas of operation and with the communities, they are working with to better understand their level of awareness on PSEA and knowledge and access about complaint mechanisms, which allows them to identify and fill gaps and results in PSEA related activities resulting from community input and consultation. In 2020, through its IPs, the PSEA network directly supported the distribution of more than 40,000 awareness-raising materials, to widely disseminate knowledge of the interagency PSEA hotline across NWS.

Finally, the PSEA Network intends to further strengthen evidence-based programming through regular sharing on PSEA related trends and findings obtained through internal data statistics of the PSEA Network NWS inter-agency hotline, and support of an annual household survey on PSEA throughout Syria. These data-backed approaches allow the Network to identify challenges and barriers that require greater levels of advocacy and focus.

project_name: WaSH Joint National Emergency Response (JoiNER)
project_objective:
JoiNER is a common appeal by 13 WaSH NGOs, constituting the majority of non-UN active sector partners. Modalities are adapted from crisis-sensitive components of the HawkaMaa-EU development project consortium. Coordination at the sector level was led/facilitated by the coordination team, which encouraged collective action, and which is also invited to support the implementation of the JoiNER.
The ERP acknowledges that public services are “overstretched and underdeveloped due to years of under- investment” and adopts a “system approach” to maximise reach and cost effectiveness while minimizing inter/intra-communitytensions and adverse effects of parallel services on public utilities. JoiNER reinforces this approach by tackling the two main components of water service provision, production and distribution, across three categories of localities/communities; those served by Water Establishments (WE), others by municipalities, and those unserved by public systems. It assumes that UNICEF and/or WFP, as sector leads (Water and Logistics respectively), will provide the necessary consumables and maintenance required for continued operation of priority pumping stations.
Recognizing that water production does not guarantee its effective and equitable delivery, JoiNER will primarily tackle distribution problems to ensure the minimum standard of safe water (35 l/c/d) is received by the most vulnerable communities and key outbreak-prone institutions. This entails addressing urgent maintenance requirements of WE and municipal networks. Unserved communities/households will be served through temporary water trucking or private pumping systems. It is notable that under the Lebanon Humanitarian Fund First Standard, $1.4 million has been allocated to the WASH sector to respond to the emergency needs through implementing activities (water points & renewable energy) to ensure the minimum standard of safe water is received by the most vulnerable. 
Against referrals from the Health and Food Security sectors, JoiNER will implement a rolling Hygiene Kit distribution activity. Also, it’s relevant to mention that in line with the LHF strategy, ACF, GVC and DPNA provided  5722 WASH kits to mitigate hygiene risks in Akkar, South, and Bekaa.    These activities are made more urgent by the recent Viral Hepatitis A outbreak.

Participation will be subject to partners’ proven access, capacity, and readiness to implement timely interventions. This will be enhanced by inviting them to replicate or jointly tender framework contracts with infrastructure contractors and suppliers based on HawkaMaa-EU’s experience, with guidance from WW-GVC. Similarly, LebRelief will lead a joint national tender for hygiene items, as well as use Hawkamaa-EU (which has dedicated funding) to provide (with ACTED and LEWAP) capacity building for local NGOs.
National coverage will be ensured through a geo-split akin to that employed within the refugee (IS) response, adopting a wider unit of WE branch/section jurisdiction, except for Hygiene Kit distribution which is divided by District/Caza. JoiNER will coordinate nationally to (re)allocate funding dynamically as the understanding of vulnerability evolves with incoming analysis.
 Off-grid renewable energy for pumping stations will be exceptionally considered where feasible to help break WEs’ perpetual ‘energy crisis mode’. JoiNER will prioritize service recovery/improvement in collaboration with public entities by providing the necessary resources while maintaining direct oversight, reinforcing community trust in the public sector. This is critical to support the wider drive to reinforce public institutions, but JoiNER will stop short of providing them with direct support, conscious that the “ERP is strictly of humanitarian nature”. This has become more pressing with the protracted energy crisis and delays in unlocking the World Bank energy loan, which promises to install some USD 30m of solar generators for water facilities.

project_name: Contribuer à améliorer l’accès à une éducation inclusive et de qualité dans un environnement d’apprentissage sûr et protecteur pour les filles et les garçons des populations hotes et deplacees affectés par le conflit dans la region de Tahoua
project_objective:
""Le projet vient en complémentarité au financement de Education Can not Wait (ECW) en cours d’exécution par Plan International Niger dans la région de Tahoua. Le présent projet vise à favoriser le maintien des enfants et le retour des enfants hors école à travers la mise en place d’un mécanisme de réouverture des écoles fermées, le renforcement des structures communautaires de soutien aux écoles et la mise en place du dispositif de l’Education accélérée (SSAP). Ceci impliquera aussi l’amélioration des environnements d’apprentissage sécurisés pour environ 5,532 garçons et 5,968 filles affectés par les conflits et les crises dans 40 écoles de Tahoua (Tassara et Tillia). Le projet vise également à augmenter la capacité des communautés, des écoles et des enfants à protéger leurs écoles et de contribuer à l'éducation, tout en utilisant des outils et des méthodes participatives pour impliquer les parents et les enfants même les plus vulnérables.
Le projet mènera plusieurs actions essentiellement sur la mise en place d’un dispositif régional pour la réouverture des écoles fermées en collaboration avec le groupe de travail Education de Tahoua, la mobilisation sociale permettant de créer une dynamique de cohésion sociale, la construction des nouvelles classes et la réhabilitation de celles endommagées, la dotation des écoles, des élèves et des enseignants, les formations des acteurs sur les questions d’urgences et d’appui psychosocial, le deploiement du programme d'Education alternative (PEA), la mise en place des mécanismes communautaires de protection et de plaintes. Pour les soutenir l’apprentissage des enfants a faible niveau, la stratégie du paquet minimum sur la qualité (PMAQ) sera développée dans les écoles cibles.
Pour réaliser cela, le projet travaillera étroitement avec les services techniques du Ministère de l'Education Nationale (MEN), le cluster éducation, le groupe de travail ainsi que les structures communautaires de l’école. Les stratégies de mobilisation communautaire seront basées sur les mécanismes communaux existants. Le projet travaillera en cohérence avec le cluster éducation et tous les autres partenaires intervenant dans les zones cibles. L´ensemble des activités seront menées dans le respect des mesures de prévention au covid-19.""

project_name: Shelter and Settlements Response in North East Nigeria
project_objective: NRC’s shelter project objective is to adopt a participatory-based approach to improve the living conditions, dignity, and physical protection of the most vulnerable people affected by conflict in targeted areas of Northeast of Nigeria. In response to the protracted nature of the crisis, NRC will increasingly work in an integrated manner, bringing in Shelter and any other relevant competencies to collaborate on providing more durable and holistic solutions to displacement and return. Considering the complexities of displacement and return in both urban and rural areas, NRC will adopt a flexible approach to target specifc needs with adaptable shelter options and incorporate safe programming principles in order to mitigate and respond to any potential adverse effects, which might result from the proposed shelter solution. The following include the overall area for the focus of the project: 1. Emergency Response: Responding to the urgent shelter/NFI needs of IDP and returnee population occurring due to unforeseen reasons such as security incidents, communal clashes, natural disasters (flooding, fire, etc) or premature return or resettlement; 2. Protracted Displacement Response: Improving the shelter conditions in camps and camp-like sites by decongestion of camps and improving the emergency/transitional shelters habitability conditions; 3. Return Context Response: Contribution and facilitating safe and dignified return of IDPs by provision of adequate shelter conditions and exploration of diverse shelter modalities in host communities and areas of return. Based on its mandate, NRC will target the people directly impacted by the conflict, especially the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host-communities living in inadequate dwellings. Based on humanitarian analysis and internal assessment results, NRC in collaboration with the shelter sector will select areas of intervention using defined specific selection criteria, which will consider physical access and security in addition to the presence of IDPs in the area, and the areas offering opportunity for safe and voluntary return. NRC will target and select beneficiaries using a community-based approach, to promote the commitment of leaders and involvement of the host community and target groups.

project_name: Survey and Clearance of  Hazardous Areas and the Provision of EORE Tailored for Specific Needs to Safeguard Vulnerable Populations Within South Sudan Against Landmines and Explosive Ordnance
project_objective: In alignment with the 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan and the United Nations Strategy on Mine Action 2019-2023, UNMAS will conduct the following activities: survey and clearance of confirmed hazardous areas (calculated in square meters (sqm)), safely dispose of explosive ordnance (EO), as well as conduct explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) by deploying one multi-tasking team (MTT) with embedded Community Liaison Officers (CLOs). UNMAS intends to survey and clear 150,000 sqm of land consisting of confrontational areas and cluster munition strike sites. The clearance team within the MTT will be mobile in six counties assessed as having catastrophic needs, to respond to urgent and priority tasks. Concurrently, CLOs within the MTT will provide EORE sessions to 7,500 beneficiaries including Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, refugees, and persons with disabilities, disaggregated as follows 1,910 boys, 1,910 girls, 1,910 women, and 1,770 men. During the EORE sessions, further information will be gathered on suspected hazards, and this in turn will be shared with the clearance teams for surveying, marking and clearance.

project_name: ASISTENCIA Y PROTECCIÓN HUMANITARIA A FAMILIAS AFECTADAS POR LOS IMPACTOS DE LA CRISIS PROLONGADA DE VENEZUELA
project_objective:
El programa está dirigido a las poblaciones las más vulnerables en Venezuela, es decir, que se seleccionaron las parroquias de intervención de acuerdo con los siguientes criterios de vulnerabilidad, operatividad y estrategia de inclusión política y social:
•	Altos niveles de pobreza
•	Altos niveles de desnutrición crónica y alta prevalencia de enfermedades infecciosas.
•	Estados fronterizos que han manejado regularmente la presión adicional del intercambio con poblaciones muy pobres y desplazados del territorio colombiano.
•	Exposición a amenazas naturales
•	Alto nivel de conflictividad y violencia social en los últimos meses, debido a la escasez.
•	Capacidad organizativa comunitaria y capacidad operativa de Cáritas consolidadas.
Los beneficiarios serán involucrados en la identificación de las necesidades para ciertas actividades, como es el caso de la selección de medicamentos a dispensar, el contenido de las bolsas complementarias de alimentos para las familias con niños/as desnutridos y la compra de filtros artesanales de agua. En otras actividades, como la detección de la desnutrición, los niños/niñas son sujetos pasivos, beneficiarios de una acción para diagnosticar y tratar la desnutrición detectada durante la primera fase del proyecto, motivada por la escasez de alimentos en el país a causa de la crisis económica. Durante la ejecución del proyecto, los beneficiarios serán implicados a través de los promotores comunitarios, quienes serán el enlace con el resto de los actores del proyecto. 
El presente proyecto se centrará en cuatro (4) resultados entre sí, que al tiempo que contribuyen a mejorar las condiciones de vida, refuerzan la resiliencia de las poblaciones más afectadas por la crisis. Ellos son: 1) Monitoreo de la situación nutricional y las condiciones de vida en las comunidades en riesgo de desnutrición en niños y mujeres embarazadas. 2) Suplementación nutricional de las comunidades vulnerables asociada a la desnutrición, con entrega de insumos terapéuticos, de insumos alimenticios y de transferencias en efectivo; 3) Atención a la salud y saneamiento, fundamentalmente a la familia de los niños menores de 5 años en situación de riesgo nutricional y de las mujeres embarazadas atendidas. Este enfoque ejecuta dos actividades que brindan respuesta a dos necesidades apremiantes, la salud y la higiene; 4) Fortalecimiento de capacidades de la Red de Cáritas de Venezuela que le permita poder adherirse a los protocolos de Cáritas Internacionalis (CI) y alcanzar un Plan de mejoras que permita incrementar la eficacia en la operatividad de los proyectos

project_name: Emergency WASH response and Building Resilience to crisis more than 1 million affected men, women, boys and girls in Syria
project_objective:
Building on experience of project interventions in Syria since 2013,Oxfam continues to work with local authorities in responding to the vulnerable populations’ WASH needs in districts/subdistricts of Aleppo, Hama, Idlib,Rural Damascus,Dar’a &Deir Ezzor, based on assessments, severity of needs and in response to further emerging needs in NES and NWS.The subdistricts that will be targeted by this project have all been heavily affected by conflict and require WASH support.OXFAM conducted integrated WASH&EFSVL assessments from January 2022 to date covering up to 50 communities through group discussions and key informant in three governorates.This includes consultations with LNGOs, INGOs, secondary data and the Humanitarian Needs Overview 2022.The project will focus during the years 2022&2023 on life-saving WASH interventions and support the resilience of existing WASH systems (water supply &sewer networks, wastewater treatment, solid waste management)&WASH in institutions, such as schools and healthcare facilities, ensuring coordinated and cohesive response strongly aligned to the WASH Sector. It is gender mainstreamed, with a response strategy overarched by a community engagement approach suitable to access and security challenges; implementation engages trusted community structures carefully screened private contractors, community-based volunteers and identified local partners, and strong collaboration with other actors.  
The total estimated population, as per UN-OCHA datasets in these sub-districts, is over 3M people.OXFAM targets the timely response to emerging rapid onset emergency needs in hot spots& potential flashpoints, new returns,new displacements,affected by C-19, economic issues, and the current returned areas with persisting WASH needs. The target locations proposed are according to severity of humanitarian needs and number of populations in need which will be adapted to the evolving ground context, access and people's movement. Although Hama considered under severity scale 1, majority of AlKousor neighborhood suffers from water shortage& still rely on water trucking.Accordingly,Oxfam considered WASH needs there. The project aims to support lifesaving WASH interventions that are resilience-focused, sustainable, durable &cost-effective WASH systems using community engagement approach and mainstreaming C-19 mitigation measures and response throughout all regular WASH activities:  The objectives of the project are;1):support to water,sanitation/sewage&solid waste management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria; 2):deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services,&improve hygienic behavior and practices of most vulnerable people; 3) WASH coordination structures facilitated and enhanced;4) improve WASH facilities and services in institutions to minimize sub-standard WASH conditions of the most vulnerable people in Syria.The type of interventions strongly aligns with: SO1,SO2,SO3&SO4 which captures the sector efforts to respond and assist local water establishments in restoring WASH services to basic functionality for communities, schools&community health facilities.Oxfam will target all age groups for water and sanitation interventions.  Hygiene interventions will target careers women,adolescent girls&school children. Accurate disaggregation of population data will be collected from relevant ministries and actors to ensure coordinated and relevant data and appropriate interventions during WASH assessments and interventions.  Oxfam has unique MOUs with several ministries gaining trust,strong relations,&approval of interventions. Bi-monthly meetings at the MoWR allow insight and agreement for selection of prioritized possible activities and discussion of operational challenges.This project’s close alignment with the HRP in terms of outcomes, activities&methodology reflects Oxfam’s close engagement with the Sector,particularly through strategic discussions&information sharing throughout 2019&2022.

project_name: Apoyo a familias vulnerables para su recuperación y resiliencia frente a choques
project_objective:
El impacto humano y económico asociado a las tormentas ETA e IOTA ocurridos en noviembre de 2020 se sumaron a los impactos, ya de por si graves, de la crisis generada por la pandemia del COVID-19 y a vulnerabilidades preexistentes, como las relacionadas con las sequías, especialmente en el Corredor Seco. El impacto de las recientes crisis han afectado especialmente actividades productivas de la que dependen hogares vulnerables como pequeños productores agropecuarios, trabajadores de pequeños comercios y de actividades turísticas y especialmente a los hogares de jefatura femenina, del ámbito rural y sin vivienda.

El Proyecto está dirigido a recuperar rápidamente a los hogares de las crisis mediante la provisión de apoyo técnico y financiero a población más vulnerable para mejorar sus medios de vida, a través del desarrollo de capacidades organizativas y productivas, la transferencia de efectivo, y la entrega de insumos y bienes. Para la recuperación de medios de vida también se generarán oportunidades laborales con acciones de recuperación de viviendas e infraestructura comunitaria esencial y con enfoque de adaptación climática.

La resiliencia de los hogares a choques, se realizará mediante el fortalecimiento de capacidades de los hogares vulnerables en la gestión de riesgos de desastres, la vigilancia de los derechos humanos, la prevención de la violencia basada en género y la violencia sexual, el embarazo adolescente, las medidas de bioseguridad para la prevención del covid-19, la seguridad alimentaria y el acceso al agua segura como una fuente vital de sobrevivencia.

El proyecto se alinea con los objetivos del clùster de Recuperación Temprana y el Response Plan en la medida que ofrece apoyo técnico y financiero a población más vulnerable para mejorar sus medios de vida (OC1) y con el incremento de ingresos económicos y empleo temporal con actividades relacionadas a la reconstrucción de viviendas y vías (OC2) y el fortalecimiento de las capacidades locales (nivel municipal, local y familias) para incrementar los niveles de resiliencia (OC3).

El proyecto tiene los mecanismos para garantizar los enfoques edad, género, diversidad, protección mediante la focalización y priorización de hogares con jefatura femenina y con NNA, en el diseño de los contenidos formativos para el desarrollo de capacidades enfocándose en roles diferenciados por género frente a desastres. Se propone un abordaje integral de recuperación desde el individuo, hogar y comunidad para promover la recuperación socio ambiental y económica de la población afectada y vulnerable post Eta e Iota para mejorar resiliencia ante choques.

El proyecto se desarrollará en alianza con socios estratégicos con presencia en territorios afectado y experiencia reconocida en los ejes temáticos del proyecto, incluidos Plan Internacional Honduras para promueva el abordaje de género, incluidos los derechos de la niñez y la igualdad de las niñas a lo largo de sus vidas, violencia basada en género y la violencia sexual. La organización internacional, Global Emergency Relief Recovery & Reconstruction (Socorro de Emergencia Mundial Recuperación y Reconstrucción), que tiene experiencia en procesos de reconstrucción de viviendas, remoción de escombros, limpieza y mantenimiento de entorno geográfico. PNUD, mediante resolución 52 / 12A (1997) de la Asamblea General, el PNUD recibió el mandato de liderar la recuperación post crisis/desastre y será el líder de la implementación del proyecto, y establecerá alianzas institucionales y territoriales adicionales para garantizar la implementación efectiva del proyecto. Estas tienen presencia en Cortés y Santa Barbara, Yoro, Intibucá, Lempira, Copán, La Paz y Comayagua (8/ 10 departamentos priorizados por el proyecto, que tambien incluye Atlántida y Colón (para transferencias). Se haran alianzas estratégicas con Secretaria Desarrollo e Inclusión Social, Oficina NU Reducción Riesgo de Desastres y Asociación Hondureña de Municipios Honduras.

project_name: Improved Treatment of severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and improvement of Maternal Infant Young Child (MIYCN) through Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) in Yirol East County, Lakes State.
project_objective: The effects of conflict in South Sudan continues to affect the humanitarian response as the effects of widespread violence and the deteriorating economic situation and will be aligned to Nutrition Cluster specific objectives, namely 1. To increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific services for children, adolescents and women in prioritized locations by the end of 2022.  2 To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW affected by acute malnutrition in prioritized locations by the end of 2022. 3 To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information by the end of 2022.  4 To increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and integrated programming targeting vulnerable groups in prioritized locations by the end of 2022. The project will complement the ongoing intervention in selected priority Counties, narrowing the nutrition care provision gaps in the most remote sites and for the most neglected groups for what concerns MAM/SAM treatment but also prevention and timely detection of acute malnutrition. Nutrition services and related activities will be informed by the most recently updated guidelines, considering COVID19 prevention and containment measures. Different services delivery modalities will be considered, from static to mobile/community based, as a proactive and articulated strategy to overcome the accessibility issues affecting current nutrition care coverage and to reach both hosts and displaced population. The proactive involvement of local communities and health authorities will facilitate the selection of the most responsive, feasible and acceptable option, while orientating the intervention on the most serious and urgent gaps, promoting better outcomes and ensuring the due accountability to beneficiaries. Nutrition services will be provided at the Health Facility level or through mobile team and community-based initiatives in their catchment area and under their supervision and guide, resulting in highly comprehensive, as addressing both health and nutrition conditions and the interrelated complications. In this way, the project will contribute to enhancing the institutionalization of management of acute malnutrition into the health system as suggested by the Cluster. The cornerstone of the proposed nutrition intervention will be its integration with other sectors as well. WASH & FSL will be given high attention, with the result of the applied strategy to be wide enough to tackle some of the key acute malnutrition drivers, as poor hygiene and access to clean water, limited food availability, low knowledge. Being aware of the higher exposure to malnutrition of certain population groups, whose peculiar conditions (disabilities, mental health disorders, exposure to SGBV) makes them particularly vulnerable and their access to services more challenging, besides requiring specific response routine interventions are not used to provide, the project will guarantee adequate integration with the Protection sector, through the opening and sustain of reciprocal referral channels for people to be offered both nutrition and clinical/psychosocial support. In general, a people/right centred approach will be adopted and mainstreamed to guarantee sector-wide responsiveness and acceptability. The quality of provided care will be strengthened through technical assistance and supportive supervision and monitored through an enhanced data collection and analysis, functional to the informed decision-making process to improve the current situation. In an area where GAM above 15% emergency threshold and more than 50% of the population are in IPC Phase 3.

project_name: Increasing Access to essential and integrated Nutrition Interventions to vulnerable children Under five years and PLWs in Kapoeta South, Ibba, Bor South, and Duk counties, South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of this proposed nutrition response plan is to increase access and scale-up to lifesaving essential and integrated nutrition interventions by establishing 10 OTP/TSFP mobile or static sites in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Duk and Ibba counties to benefit about 97,534 beneficiaries (i.e. 12,865 under five years children and 8,232 PLWs. A total of 4,204 children (2,134 girls and 2,070 boys) with SAM, 8,661 children (4,733 girls and 3,928 boys) with moderate acute malnutrition and 8,232 pregnant and lactating women will be reached by CRSF in the three project locations. 
Additionally CRSF will provide nutrition prevention services to reach 23,128 with MIYCN services, 50,140 with VAS and 14,221 BSFP services for under five children and 8,232 BSFP for PLWs in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Ibba and Duk counties.
3 OTP/TSFP mobile sites will be establish at Lonyangat Machi I,  Pwata and Longeleya payams in Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatoria state. The 4 other mobile OTP/TSFPs will provide an avenue to reach children under 5 years in hard-to-reach locations in Anyidi, Makuach, and Baidi payams respectively in Bor south County, Jonglei State while 3 OTP/TSFP mobile sites will be established in Payuel, Padiet and dongchak payams in Duk county.
The activities will aim at linking nutrition Interventions with the existing FSL, WASH, and Health and protection activities by coordinating with other partners in the three locations. CRSF is proposing 2022 HRP activities which will be aligned to the nutrition cluster’s objectives, indicators and activities for the HRP 2022. 
CRSF will coordinate with the existing Nutrition Partners in the four locations to avoid duplications. These partners includes MaCDA & SCI in Kapoeta South, SCI in Bor South, and AFSS in Ibba. We will work in close collaboration with static nutrition partners operating in the project locations for effective referrals and to avoid duplication of nutrition Interventions. CRSF will engage and coordinate with UNICEF and WFP for core supply pipeline support for RUTF, RUSF, CSB++and other routine medications and therapeutic rations for the beneficiaries in both SAM and MAM programs.
CRSF will strengthen the management of SAM and MAM in Health facilities by linking with health partners in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Ibba and Duk counties. All Nutrition staff will be trained on non-specialized protection package to identify and refer children with protection concerns for specialized care.
The project will ensure recruitment of 20 Nutrition Assistants who will be charged with management and treatment of children and PLWs discovered with acute malnutrition in line with the SS CMAM guideline.
Through the established mother to mother support groups, CRSF will ensure that women and youth are engaged in the project design, planning and implementation as well as ensuring that complaints and feedback mechanisms are incorporated into this project. Further, CRSF will ensure that vulnerable caretakers are trained on nutrition sensitive agriculture for production of varieties of vegetables, establish 10 demonstration gardens at 10 mobiles OTP/TSFP sites or health facilities. CRSF will ensure that the response targets children (boys and girls) under five living disabilities. 
To ensure improved coverage of nutrition services in hard-to-reach areas, CRSF will coordinate with other nutrition partners to plan a scale up nutrition response through establishment of 4 mobile OTP/TSFP nutrition outreach services integrated into routine Health outreach activities, Food Security, WASH, services while a close coordination with other partners will be maintained to ensure that Nutrition staffs are trained on Protection and GBV referral mechanisms in the four project locations.

project_name: Provision of Emergency FSL response, Recovery and Resilience Building for vulnerable population in need in Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North, Bor South, and Ibba, and Nzara Counties
project_objective:
Multiple shocks resulting from many years of wars and intercommunal conflicts, coupled with three successive years of heavy floods has resulted into constant loss of livelihoods and key household assets including severe impact on building resilience on sustainable food production and thus leading to a gradual increase in food and livelihood insecurity situation in South Sudan. 
Child Relief and Support Fund (CRSF), an active women-led national organization has been implementing a resilient food and livelihood security programme in three counties (Kapoeta South, Bor South and Ibba counties) since Jan 2020 to date. CRSF is designing this FSL project plan to meet the needs of vulnerable populations previously affected by war, inter communal conflicts, and floods who are located in hard to reach counties (Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North, Bor South, Ibba and Nzara counties) with high food and livelihood insecurity, high morbidity due to preventable diseases, high Malnutrition/GAM rates, depleted community assets and poor WASH infrastructure.
In this proposed project, CRSF has targeted the following counties; Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North (EES), Bor South (Jonglei state), Ibba and Nzara counties (WES) which are in IPC 4 and 2 (IPC, Dec 2020) respectively 
CRSF is designing a 12 months project to effectively contribute to the protection and rehabilitation of livelihoods of the most vulnerable and food insecure population in EES, Jonglei and WES and support them to transit from food shocks through recovery and resilience building through enhancing their food production capacities and livelihood support services.
In line with strategic cluster objectives 2: CLO2 Enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop seeds and fishing and livestock support and objective 3, SO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks, CRSF intends to reach out to the target population with the following activities; 1) Mapping and validating the vulnerable households for their eligibility under the agreed criteria
2) Systematic distribution of on-farm inputs (fast maturing crops and vegetable seeds and associated agro-implements) to enhance access to food production technologies.
3) Systematic distribution of off-farm inputs/kits (fisheries’ hooks and fishing nets) to enhance access to off-farm food production inputs.
4) Link the beneficiaries to already HAA supported health facilities and referral pathway for effective case management and above all Basic water treatment for HH consumption
(WASH)
CRSF is targeting to reach 12,050 households (Kapoeta Sout-2,500 HHs, Bor South-3,500 HHs, Kapoeta East-2,300, Kapoeta North 2,100 HHs, Ibba-700 HHs, and Nzara-950 HHs.
CRSF will ensure that targeting of vulnerable household will be done in consideration of gender and people living with disabilities while ensuring protection and incorporation of Accountability to affected population practices. With support from CRSF technical FSL team, a total of 1,000 households will be trained on modern agronomic practices and 100 Community Animal Health Workers (CAWHs) will be recruited and trained for the livestock support aspect of the Project. Under CRSF supported farmers groups on seed multiplication project in Ibba County, CRSF will further use vouchers to support farmers in other locations during seed fair to access quality seed inputs for sustainable agriculture on food production. CRSF will further ensure that FSL program implementation conforms to the Do No Harm principle is transparency and accountability to the affected population principles as a right for every beneficiary targeting. CRSF derives its strength in its physical and operational presence in the three states particularly in Kapoeta South, Bor South and Ibba counties where there ongoing integrated FSL interventions.
