project_name: Provision of Health services for Conflict Affected Population in North West Syria
project_objective:
Shafak Organization aims to contribute to the provision of access to life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian health services for 233,065 people in need and conflict-affected populations in northern Syria in 2022. The proposed intervention will prioritize internally displaced people and other vulnerable populations especially (women, children, and people with disabilities) in the targeted areas. The intervention will be implemented through:

1. Continue supporting a comprehensive package of health services including Primary Health Care, and Mental Health in eight of the existing health facilities in northwest Syria. The motivation of this project is to continue providing health services in the already established and equipped centers to the population in western and southern rural Aleppo and rural Idlib with outreach and referral activities to the higher level of health services. The project will comprise two convergent components: primary health and mental health care, and their activities will be provided through the following eight health centers:
1)- Al-Jeineh Comprehensive PHC Center with basic obstetric and neonatal care (HF-Code: B0200004). Aleppo, Jebel Saman, Atareb, Jienieh.
2)- Harbanoush PHC center (HF-Code: G0700005): Idleb, Maaret Tamsrin, Harbanush.
3)- Akhtarin PHC Center (HF-Code :B0204077): Aleppo, A'zaz, Aghtrin.
4)- Ziadiyah PHC Center (HF-Code :B0204066): Aleppo, A'zaz, Aghtrin, Ziadiyah.
5)- Arshaf PHC Center (HF-Code :B0204027): Aleppo, A'zaz, Aghtrin, Arshaf.
6)- Kafr Ghan PHC Center (HF-Code: B0204071). Aleppo, A'zaz, Suran, Kafr Ghan,
7)- Ayidoun Kadimoon PHC (HF-Code: G0703006). Idleb-Harim-Salqin-Salqin
8)- Darkoush PHC (HF-Code: G0704016). Idleb-Jisr-Ash-shugur-Darkoush-Darkoush

In average the expected beneficiaries for all proposed PHC centers is: 168,000 for the whole year (33,000 Men, 45,000 women, 50,000 girls, 40,000 boys).

2. The provision of Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC) services and management of SRH-related diseases in addition to the pediatric health care through supporting the specialized hospital for women and children which provides maternal and child health services to most vulnerable people in the rural of Idlib, Marret Tamsrin and through outreach teams:
a) Shafak Specialized Hopsital for Women and Children (HF-Code: G0700073). Idleb, Maaret Tamsrin. 

In average the expected beneficiaries for the proposed hospital : 30,000 for the whole year (20,000 women, 6000 girls, 4000 boys).

3. Continue Supporting 2 dialysis centers in Idlib (35 patients per month) and Atareb (30 patients per month) with running costs and dialysis kits. In addition to conduct capacity building and training for the medical staff of the two centers:
a)- Al-Atareb Dialysis center (HF-Code: B0200181): Aleppo, Jebel Saman, Atareb.
b)- Shafak Dialysis center-Idleb: (HF-Code: G0700074): Idleb, Idleb, Idleb.

4. Continue Provision of Secondary Health Care and operations services through supporting an existing health facility in rural Idleb: 
a) Ariha Surgical Unit (HF-Code: G0705061): Idleb, Ariha, Ariha.

In average the expected beneficiaries for surgical unit : 15,000 for the whole year (5500 Men, 4000 women 3500 girls, 2000 boys).

5. Continue to support only BEmONC services in Armanaz and Sarmada PHC centers in the rural Idleb, which are supported by other NGOs, while Shafak covers only RH and nutrition services in both centers.  

In average the expected beneficiaries for all BeMONC PHC centers: 20,000 for the whole year (15,000 women 3000 girls, 2000 boys). 

By achieving the above components, Shafak will ensure the continuation of essential and life-saving health interventions in addition to maintaining essential health services to contribute in decreasing mortality and morbidity percentage in NWS.  

In 2023, according to Shafak strategy and budget availability, it is expected to reach the same target through supporting the same health services and facilities.

project_name: Assistance inconditionnelle en cash et kits AGRs pour renforcer la résilience des ménages PDIs et communautés hôtes du département de Ouallam, région de Tillabery
project_objective: L'objectif dudit projet vise à améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et renforcer la résilience des ménages vulnérables à travers le cash reçu et les Kits AGRs de protection sociale. Les activités de ce projet seront mises en œuvre au niveau des communes de Ouallam et de Tondikiwindi (Mangaizé, Tondikiwindi et Diney) au profit des ménages vulnérables PDIs et communautés hôtes. Au total, 1 600 ménages seront identifiés à travers l'enquête d'Analyse de l'Economie des Ménages/Household Economic Analysis (HEA).  Cette identification tiendra compte du genre (chefs de ménages hommes et chefs de ménages femmes), de l'inclusion sociale : personnes vivant avec handicap, vieilles personnes, ménage avec enfant non accompagné, femmes enceintes ou allaitantes, etc…). Le présent projet touchera 11 200 personnes (soient 4,72% de la cible présentée dans le document « PIN & Cibles SECAL 2022"") pendant six (6) mois allant de Mars 2022 à Aout 2022 afin de satisfaire leurs besoins alimentaires au cours des périodes de pré-soudure et soudure surtout qu’il y’a risque d’épuisement précoce des stocks céréaliers cette année (décembre/janvier) et des disponibilités fourragères aggravées par l’inaccessibilité dans les zones de conflits et les pertes dues aux feux de brousse. Chaque ménage bénéficiaire recevra une somme de 32 500 F CFA par mois pour lui permettre de se procurer de vivres pour le besoin du ménage. Le paiement des bénéficiaires sera facilité par une Institution de Microfinance. En plus, ces ménages recevront de kits AGRs de protection sociale (les femmes des 1 600 ménages bénéficiaires seront organisés en groupe de 20 femmes, ce qui donne 80 groupes de femmes et chaque groupe recevra un kit AGRs), des séances de sensibilisation communautaire sur les Engins Explosifs Improvisées (EEI) seront conduites par les agents de GOAL et des actions de plaidoyer à l’échelle locale et communautaire seront menées afin d’avoir un meilleur impact national. Le projet sera mis en œuvre avec la participation de tous les acteurs concernés (les autorités : administratives, Communales, Coutumières ; les services techniques et les communautés concernés).

project_name: Les populations affectées par la crise au Niger bénéficient d'une assistance adaptée à leurs besoins en matière de documentation civile dans les régions de Tillaberi.
project_objective:
Dans le souci de promouvoir les droits à la documentation civile et d''identité juridique des PDI, des communautés d'accueil touchées par le déplacement et des autres groupes vulnérables dans les régions de Maradi et Tillabery, NRC à travers son programme d'information, de conseil et d'assistance juridique (ICLA), entreprendra des activités facilitant l'accès à la documentation civile et d'identité juridique et garantissant la protection des droits fondamentaux. 
Les solutions proposées s’alignent à la fois aux objectifs stratégiques du secteur protection. ICLA organisera des campagnes de sensibilisations sur l'importance de la déclaration civile et d'identité juridique ;  fournira des conseils juridiques aux PDI en vue de les aider à surmonter les obstacles les empêchant d’exercer leur droit à la documentation civile et d'identité juridique, apportera une assistance juridique pour l'obtention des actes de naissance et cartes nationales d'identité, et renforcera les mécanismes communautaires et les services techniques en charge de l'établissement des actes de naissance. De même, le programme ICLA apportera son assistance sur sollicitation d’autres acteurs humanitaires intervenant dans la même région et suivant l’analyse de la situation sécuritaire par NRC. ICLA portera une attention particulière aux femmes et filles dont le taux d'enregistrement reste faible dans ces zones précitées. ICLA favorisera l'approche inclusive et participative pour les communautés cibles en facilitant les dialogues communautaires contribuant à identifier les obstacles à l'exercice de ces droits. En outre, les acteurs humanitaires et les décideurs seront ciblés pour le renforcement du plaidoyer autour de ces questions. 
L’action ICLA ciblera au total 21990 sur 2,1 millions de personnes identifier selon par le Plan de réponse humanitaire (PRH) de 2022 à recevoir une aide humanitaire urgente et la protection, soit 57 % des personnes estimées dans le besoin. 
Le projet contribuera de manière significative à la protection des personnes déplacées internes, refugiés et communautés hôtes vulnérables à travers la promotion et la facilitation de l'accès à la documentation civile. Ceci se fera également à travers les actions d'information, conseil et assistance juridique. Un accent sera mis sur le renforcement des capacités des acteurs de l'état civil et  l'appui matériel afin de faciliter la délivrance des services aux usagers. Ce projet ciblera parmis ces 21990 bénéficiaires directs, 11215 femmes et 10775 hommes, tout en assurant de prendre en compte 3% de personnes handicapés.

project_name: GBViE Response, Prevention and Risk mitigations among women, girls and boys in camps and affected host community in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
In 2022 UNICEF and partners aim  to reach 87,196 girls, boys, women, and men, including persons with disabilities and other gender orientations with GBV response, risk mitigations and prevention interventions in camps and host community (80 percent will be  in camps and 20 percent in host). 
UNICEF will continue to work with government institutions and Department of Social Services (DSS) to strengthen child protection systems, through capacity development of the social workforce, and technical support to  police probation officers and social workers to improve children's access to child-friendly services. UNICEF will also work with ORG for system strengthening on birth registration. 
UNICEF will strengthen GBV prevention and risk mitigation, improve responses and ensure preparedness and response for emergencies including supporting human resources in PERU and prepositioning 10,000  Dignity kits and ensure  that women and girls receiving dignity kits, are oriented on proper disposal of the non-reusable materials to address environmental issues. 
UNICEF will actively empower adolescents and youth through Peer Education as one of the key strategies to prevent  Gender-based Violence such as Intermate Partner Violence, child marriage and hence create a social environment free from violence crucial for the adolescents and youth in Cox’s Bazar. Community engagement will be prioritized towards building the protective environment in a durable and sustainable way. 
UNICEF will focus on; i) enhancing the capacities of 900 case workers, social workers, and case managers through trainings, mentorship and coaching, ii) strengthen institutional systems to provide Multi-sectoral services including specialized services for children and adolescent survivors,  iii) maintaining 23 safe spaces for women and girls in camps and host community to provide response services (Case management, Psychosocial support, referral for medical, legal and safety)  in a confidential space, while adhering to COVID 19 safety measures,  iv) engage the community and empower adolescents to address and challenge negative social norms and harmful practices, v) Mitigate GBV risks through safety audits and collaborate with sectors (Health, WASH, CP, Nutrition, Education) on mitigating risk in respective sector programs, vi)  strengthening Child and adolescent survivors initiative and vi) advocacy for equitable access to justice and social services, vii) engage 4,000 women and girls including PWD in structured skills activities, awareness sessions on GBV, nutrition, hygiene, orienting adolescent girls on Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health information using “Girl Shine” curriculum. Also, empowering adolescents in Preventing Gender-based Violence through Peer Education, will be explored. UNICEF supported SSWG in co-location areas will be utilized to implement joint activities enhancing social cohesion among refugees and host population.
Community outreach mobilizers, volunteers and community groups will play a crucial role in reaching religious leaders, Mahjis and other stakeholders with messages on GBV prevention and risk mitigation, creating protective environment for children, women and adolescents while 12,000 individuals will be trained and engaged using evidence proven strategies to address negative social norms. Including Engaging Men in Accountable Practices (EMAP) which aims at engaging men in transformative individual behaviors change and male engagement in a way that improves, rather than endangering, the lives of women.
UNICEF will strengthen Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) by facilitating complaints and feedback mechanisms, and monitoring to ensure that feedback improves programming and UNICEF as a Co-chair of the PSEA Network, will bolster UNICEF and partners’ PSEA and child safeguarding mechanisms, through training of UNICEF and partners on PSEA, conduct partners’ PSEA assessment and implementation of institutional PSEA mechanisms.

project_name: Provision of life-saving nutrition Interventions for Rohingya children, women, and vulnerable host population in Bangladesh and systems-based programming to ensure life-cycle based continuum of care
project_objective:
Rohingya camp: UNICEF will continue implementing components of community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) through its 26 integrated nutrition facilities (INFs) in the 19 camps. The project will combine facility, community and household-based approaches to facilitate improved access for the most at-risk groups. At the INF level, UNICEF and partners will target to admit 7,000 children with SAM for treatment. All nutrition centers will be equipped with disability friendly facilities including access during monsoon. Caregivers of children under 2 will be screened to identify needs for breastfeeding support and will be provided IYCF counselling. The project will strive to achieve optimal IYCF practices by involving men and other family members taking an active role in infant feeding and family activities and influence women on decision making. All staff and volunteer will be trained on prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and PSEA awareness messages will be displayed in the nutrition facilities. Furthermore, a comprehensive complaint and feedback handling mechanism will be established, and a service referral linkage will be established to the protection agency. Monthly Growth Monitoring and Promotion sessions will be conducted focusing on 0-23 months children along with WFP implemented preventive Blanket Supplementary Feeding Programme where children 24-59 months are being targetted for GMP. Considering the COVID-19 situation, all activities will be adapted ensuring protection of beneficiaries and service providers from COVID-19. All community mobilization activities will be conducted through community nutrition volunteers. These volunteers will do follow up visits with an emphasis on absentees, defaulters and non-responders from treatment. Strategies for behaviour change communication will include mother-to-mother support groups, peer groups for adolescent girls as well as courtyard sessions targeting community leaders, male caregivers and other stakeholders. Pregnant and lactating women and adolescents will be given iron folic acid to prevent anaemia. Early childhood development services will be mainstreamed as part of essential basic services of health and nutrition since early childhood development is seen as a holistic approach including protection, stimulation, health and nutrition. In addition to that, attitude of parents, male caregivers, service providers and community people on nurturing care will be promoted as well. Existing contingency plan will be revised according to the need, and partners will be trained to tackle any unanticipated weather incidents including fire outbreak.

Host Community: To ensure quality nutrition services at facility-level, upazilla nutrition supervisors and nutrition counsellors will be deployed in the union health and family welfare centres, and upazilla health complexes. Frontline health and nutrition service providers will be trained on a comprehensive package of nutrition and essential nutrition supplies will be procured and distributed to the targeted facilities. The services in the host community will involve community engagement and mobilization by the multipurpose health volunteers (MHVs). MHVs will be trained on comprehensive package of nutrition who will mobilize Community Groups and Community Support group members to strengthened community level nutrition services. The community engagement activities will mainly focus on practical demonstrations for mothers and caregivers on improving the quality of complementary foods through cooking demonstrations and mukhe bhaat ceremonies. Furthermore, UNICEF will collaborate with department of agricultural extension and the department of livestock services and local NGOs to build the capacities of beneficiary households on sustainable homestead gardening and backyard poultry rearing to improve household level food security.

project_name: « NDAKOMEZA », Appui à la continuité de l'apprentissage inclusif et de qualité pour les enfants affectés par les situations d'urgence
project_objective:
Le projet vise à contribuer pour la continuité de l’apprentissage pour les enfants affectés par les situations d’urgence au Burundi. Le HNO 2022 a fait état de 177 392 enfants dans le besoin de services adaptés leur permettant d’accéder à un enseignement inclusif et de qualité. Le secteur de l’éducation a été secoué par des catastrophes naturelles qui ont endommagé plusieurs centaines de salles de classes ainsi que du matériel d’apprentissage et d’enseignement, conduisant à la perturbation des activités scolaires dans plusieurs localités du pays. En plus d’autres événements qui mettent la pression sur le système éducatif comme notamment le rapatriement des réfugiés burundais qui a suivi une courbe ascendante en 2021 et qui continue, la pandémie COVID 19 est venue s’ajouter aux autres problèmes qui constituent une entrave à l’éducation sûre est de qualité. Il demeure nécessaire de renforcer la prévention de cette pandémie dans les écoles, notamment à travers l’amélioration des conditions d’hygiène. En 2022, la réponse humanitaire dans le domaine de l’éducation se focalisera sur deux objectifs clés : - 176 411 enfants affectés par un choc récent – mouvements de population, désastres naturels et épidémies auront un accès équitable à une éducation inclusive de qualité et adaptée à leurs besoins socio-émotionnels. - 3 306 enseignants des zones affectées par un choc récent – mouvements de population, désastres naturels, épidémies – sont renforcés dans la gestion de l’éducation dans les situations d’urgence.
La réponse proposée par l’UNICEF s’est référée aux planifications d’autres acteurs du secteur de l’éducation et se focalise sur les besoins qui ne sont pas couverts par ces planifications. Elle privilégiera la coordination de la réponse avec les autres secteurs humanitaires, notamment les secteurs WASH et celui de la Protection (Protection de l’enfant). Elle consistera essentiellement à l’appui de la réhabilitation d’infrastructures scolaires endommagées, à l’aménagement de salles de classe temporaires dans des localités affectées par les situations d’urgence en attendant la construction de salles durables, à la fourniture de matériels d’apprentissage pour les enfants les plus affectés par les situations d’urgence, ainsi qu’au renforcement des mécanismes de référencement pour faciliter l’accès des élèves affectés aux services de prise en charge psychosociales et de protection adaptés à leurs besoins. Dans tous les sites qui seront construits ou réhabilités, le programme Education de l’UNICEF collaborera avec le secteur WASH pour y installer des dispositifs de lavage des mains qui se durables et d’autres kits d’hygiène. Le programme Education de l’UNICEF collaborera également avec le secteur Protection pour assurer que les besoins de protection des élèves sont pris en compte. Notamment, dans les activités de construction/réhabilitation et d’aménagement des dispositifs hygiéniques, une attention particulière sera mise sur la prise en compte des besoins spécifiques des enfants vivant avec handicap et des filles. La réponse proposée couvrira les provinces priorisées par le HRP 2022, à savoir Bujumbura, Bujumbura Marie, Cankuzo, Cibitoke, Kirundo, Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana, et Ruyigi et mettra un focus particulier sur les enfants rapatriés, déplacés internes, vivant avec handicap, et les enfants marginalisés en général, sans oublier la question d’égalité des chances entre filles et garçons.

project_name: Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis
project_objective:
Syrian children are now affected by a triple crisis: conflict, economic shock and COVID-19. An estimated 2 million children  are out-of-school and face elevated protection risks related to, among others, child marriage and child labour. Ninety per cent of Syrians live poverty. In many governorates poverty is now the biggest reason for children dropping out of school. In addition, the pandemic has had an impact on the continuity of education in classrooms. 

Only 54 per cent of the 17,958 pre-crisis schools were functional as of February 2020,  causing overcrowding. Some schools operate in double/triple shifts to accommodate displaced children. In 2021, there were 25 reported attacks on schools  (mostly in NWS), further contributing to the deterioration of access to education. 

Many students are behind in their learning, finding it difficult to return to school or at risk of dropping out. Younger children, adolescents and children with disabilities face further challenges accessing learning services due to limited availability of ECE centres, secondary education services and vocational training opportunities or inclusive education for the estimated 15 per cent of children with disabilities. Key reasons children are not in school include schools not being in their area, schooling not being affordable and children working to support the household, the use of schools for non-educational purposes and other safety concerns—particularly in NWS. 

UNICEF proposes to provide education services for preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills in schools that are safe and welcoming, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience.

UNICEF will contribute to: 
A.	Access to inclusive learning
B.	Quality learning in safe and inclusive schools
C.	Resilient Systems

Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, school textbooks and school supplies, support for national exams, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and the provision of temporary classrooms. Schools will be furnished, equipped with gender-sensitive WASH facilities, and established in particularly vulnerable areas (Severity Scale 3-5). Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. UNICEF will ensure “safe access” through the clearing of UXO and COVID-19 free physical access will be guaranteed through sanitization of school buildings.

To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. Corporal punishment and violence in school will be tackled. Nonformal education will give adolescents the chance to find employment or re-integrate into public schools. 

UNICEF will strengthen the resilience of grassroots education systems, facilitating bridges between schools and communities through the establishment of Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and by training education staff in monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning.

A continued failure to invest in education infrastructure, services and quality will result in squandered opportunities to help children learn and thrive. A substantial number of children will stay out of school, and abandon intentions to ever return.

project_name: Renforcement de la préparation, de l'alerte et de la réponse en cas de chocs multirisques dans les zones fragiles afin d’assurer une réponse locale la plus rapide possible, au Niger
project_objective:
""Le Niger est marqué par multiples facteurs de stress chroniques et faiblesse structurelle, auxquels s'ajoute une insécurité croissante, dû à la présence des GANE dans la zone Mali/Burkina Faso et le banditisme à Maradi que provoque des déplacements massifs et soudains des populations. Les populations déplacées s’installent dans des territoires plus surs, de façon anarchique en entrant en conflit avec la population locale et les autorités, pour l’accès aux ressources come l’eau, la santé, l’éducation, les moyens de subsistance déjà insuffisantes. COOPI propose une intervention, en consortium avec MC, DP multirisques de 24 mois, dans 4 communes, avec un focus spécifique sur la protection, en renforcent les capacités des réponses immédiates des communes pour l’accueil des déplacés, en appuyant aussi la population locale, de façon organisée. 
L’action prévoie: a)renforcement des capacités de réponse locale immédiate face aux chocs multirisques; b)transfert de compétences techniques et moyens logistiques aux communes; c)appui aux services de base locaux, visant le nexus urgence-développement. Cette intervention a une approche intercommunale, vu que les risques n’ont pas des limites administratives, et que les actions de préparation/réponse doivent être réalisées en coordination/collaboration entre les communes voisines. 
La redevabilité et le nexus humanitaire–développement seront au cœur aussi de l’intervention : le renforcement de la capacité d’absorption des services de base pour alléger les pressions, et l’accompagnement de la coexistence, en parallèle d’une réponse multisectorielle urgente. 
Ce projet vise aussi le renforcement de la décentralisation a niveau des communes et profite de l'expérience de COOPI et de Mercy Corps en DRR, leur statut d’organisations de nexus urgence/développement et leur présence de longue date dans les communes proposées.""
Pour ce projet les localités ont été choisis conjointement avec les membres du groupe de travail abris et biens non alimentaires (GTABNA) pour éviter les doublons dans les interventions. Nous pouvons être plusieurs partenaires dans les mêmes départements ou communes, mais nous intervenons généralement dans des localités différentes.

project_name: Mobility Tracking and Multi-Sectoral Location Assessment
project_objective:
According to the Government of Kenya (GoK) and the UN, the country is facing its worst drought in 40 years. More than four million people are ""food insecure,"" and 3.3 million cannot get enough water to drink. Prior to that 2016/2017 the Horn of Africa was affected by severe drought and by famine in 2011. It is estimated that over 4.3 million people are in need across 13 counties in Northeastern Kenya. 
While there is a regular monitoring of a number of indicators linked to drought across the Kenyan Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASAL) region through the Long Rains Food Security Assessments and the Short Rains Assessments, such assessments are not mandated to understand the mobility dynamics and vulnerabilities associated with the movement of people and needs, specific to those dynamics.
The Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)-Mobility Tracking and Multi-Sectoral Assessment activities identified 4 types of mobile populations that moved as a result of the drought: (i) absentees are people that left the location and have not yet returned, (ii) arrivals are people who came to the location of study from other places in Kenya, (iii) returnees are people that left the location but came back, and, (iv) foreign-nationals are non-Kenyans who live at the assessment location.
Key activities shall include:
1.	Pre-DTM roll-out workshop with government stakeholders in Turkana
2.	Identify settlements within the ward with drought induced mobility
3.	Train and deploy local team leaders and enumerators on data collectionConduct validation workshops with government officials (CCs, DCCs, NDMA and county government representatives)
4.	Publication of DTM reports.

project_name: Projet de préparation et de réponse à l'urgence en santé, nutrition et protection pour les populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions de l’Est et du Sahel
project_objective:
Afin de répondre à la situation sécuritaire volatile et à l’augmentation des chocs, PUI propose de coupler une réponse institutionnelle (volet Résilience) avec différentes modalités de déploiement en urgence (volet Humanitaire) en s’appuyant sur une forte composante preparedness, indispensable à une réponse rapide et qualitative dans le contexte. En effet, un stock central de contingence à Ouagadougou et 2 autres prépositionnés à Dori et à Fada disposeront de médicaments essentiels, de matériel médico technique et d’intrants nutritionnels. Le stock central alimentera en intrants les 2 autres stocks afin d’éviter toute rupture et ainsi assurer la rapidité de la réponse. Un vivier RH composé de personnel médical et para médical (médecins, infirmiers, sages-femmes, agents psychosociaux …) opérationnel sera identifié sur toute la zone du projet, et permettra de déployer des réponses d’urgence en 15 jours maximum à partir de la date d’alerte/choc en toute situation.
Ces réponses aux urgences seront déployées en lien avec le GCORR (Groupe de Coordination Opérationnelle de la réponse d’urgence), les clusters santé, nutrition et protection, les ONG partenaires, les autorités sanitaires ainsi que les autorités en charge de l’action humanitaire. 
Selon la situation, PUI prévoit 3 modalités d’actions à savoir : 1/ la mise en place de Cliniques Mobiles pour 4 semaines maximum et gérée directement par l’ONG en coordination avec les DS, 2/ la mise en place de Postes de Santé Avancés qui prennent la suite des Cliniques Mobiles pour maximum 3 mois, géré par le District Sanitaire de la zone d’intervention et appuyé/encadré par PUI, 3/ un appui RH, en intrants nutritionnels et médicaux en remote en cas d’impossibilité d’accès sur zone, géré en coordination avec le DS et selon les besoins. Les zones d’intervention concernent l’ensemble de la région de l’Est et les provinces du Yagha et du Séno dans le Sahel.

En complément du déploiement en urgence, PUI apportera un soutien institutionnel à 15 CSPS, 3 CMA et 1 CHR des 4 DS visés dans les régions Est (Fada, Gayéri, Diapaga) et Sahel (Sebba). Ces établissements, sélectionnés après une évaluation des besoins réalisées en octobre 2021, bénéficieront  de formations de leur personnel, de soutien à la supervision, de fournitures de médicaments et de matériel … 

Une équipe d’urgence basée à Dori et Fada sera également recrutée en vue d’assurer un déploiement rapide et simultané de la réponse en lien avec le pool d’urgence (vivier des RH pré-identifiées sur le terrain).

project_name: Emergency response for access to WASH in health services for people affected by the security and humanitarian crisis in the Regions of Boucle du Mouhoun and Sahel, Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Le présent projet prévoit de contribuer à réduire la mortalité et la morbidité des populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire et humanitaire dans les régions du Sahel et de la Boucle du Mouhoun au Burkina Faso en améliorant les conditions de prise en charge dans les formations sanitaires au travers de l'amélioration de l'accès à l'eau, l'hygiène et l'assainissement.
Les formations sanitaires ciblées dans la Boucle du Mouhoun et le Sahel  seront dotées du paquet minimum WASH selon les données recueillies par l'évaluation des besoins. 
L'objectif du projet est d'assurer pour chaque formations sanitaires appuyées:
- Disponibilisation de l'eau en qualité et quantité suffisante selon les normes (stockage de capacité minimum de 1000 L.)                                                                                                                                                                                         
- Mise en place de structure de gestion ; 
- Disponibilisation de dispositifs de lavage des mains avec du savon                                                                                                    
- Mise en place d'un système de gestion des déchets (vidoirs, brûleurs ou fosse à incinération, poubelles pour la collecte des déchets...)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
- Dotation en kit minimum d'hygiène (Pour les questions environnementales, hygiène des mains, nettoyage du milieu, stockage et traitement de l’eau…)                                                                             
- Réalisation/réhabilitation de blocs de latrines/douches séparés H/F/Agents de santé                                                                                                                                                                                                              
- Promotion de l'hygiène (sensibilisations, affiches, prospectus,)

project_name: Mitigation of Threats of Explosive Ordnance in North-east Nigeria
project_objective:
1.27 million individuals are exposed to the risk of explosive remnants of war (ERW),
landmines of an improvised nature, and other improvised explosive devices (IEDs) in Borno,
Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) states. Over a decade of the ongoing conflict between the Nigerian army and non-state armed groups (NSAGs) in north-east Nigeria has resulted in the widespread contamination of the area by explosive ordnance (EO).
UNMAS Nigeria leads the mine action response in north-east Nigeria to mitigate the threats of EO for civilians and humanitarian actors, as well as to develop capacity for national and state authorities and civil society actors to manage humanitarian mine action activities, based on an accurate understanding of the scale and scope of EO contamination. 
UNMAS conducts explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) for IDPs, returnees, refugees and host communities, and implements data collection, mapping of services to establish referral mechanisms for the victims of EO incidents, persons with disabilities and persons with similar needs to facilitate access to immediate and longer term medical and psychological support.
UNMAS also conducts capacity building of national and state authorities as well as local non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) with Training of Trainers (ToT) courses for EORE and non-technical survey (NTS).

project_name: HLP Rights for conflict-affected populations in the North West and South West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
The project aims to mitigate the impact of the armed conflict and COVID-19 on the populations of the North West and South West regions of Cameroon. Specifically, the project seeks to improve access to housing, land and property for conflict affected populations in Fako, Meme, Ndian and Manyu division in the SW region, and Mezam, Donga Mantung, Bui and Boyo divisions in the NW region. Returnees and host populations will have their capacities enhanced to prevent and address HLP disputes and tensions amongst the displacement affected populations.
This will be achieved through an integrated, multi-sector approach comprising Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS), and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) interventions. Through the ICLA Program, NRC will promote the respect of Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights to enhance social cohesion among displaced and host communities, train local and regional authorities, traditional leaders and humanitarian actors to address HLP-related disputes through Collaborative Dispute Resolution (CDR). 
NRC will reinforce its response and provide support to displaced populations and vulnerable host communities to access their HLP rights. NRC will deliver information and awareness sessions to IDPs, returnees, refugees, and host communities on HLP issues.  
NRC mobile teams will also provide counselling to the above target population in displacement and return areas, including IDP sites and refugee camps. These populations will be informed and assisted in accessing and securing customary and formal rights over HLP assets.
Additionally, NRC will provide legal assistance to conflict-affected population (IDPs, refugees) in need of securing their HLP rights. NRC will assist vulnerable individuals to obtain signed agreements from local authorities and traditional leaders (chief of villages) for beneficiaries at risk of forced eviction. Priority will be given to female heads of household, widows, displaced persons, and vulnerable or affected host community members. This process will contribute to the prevention of forced evictions. 
Furthermore, NRC will build the capacity of local and traditional authorities on HLP issues, including through the provision of training and coaching on HLP rights and CDR (Collaborative Dispute Resolution), to strengthen their HLP response. NRC will also train humanitarian actors operating in sectors such as shelter, WASH, education, and food security. This will help ensure that these sectors prioritize land tenure agreements instead of the direct and customary land transfer in their interventions and prevent or solve land-related conflicts. For due diligence approach, NRC will work with beneficiaries of Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS), Shelter, Wash and Education programmes to secure access to land. In order to avoid or reduce forced evictions, NRC will assist Shelter, Wash, LFS beneficiaries to access land with increased security of tenure. 
In order to strengthen the coordination and give further visibility to the needs of affected populations with regard to access to land, housing and property, NRC will lead the HLP Area of Responsibility. This will also contribute to an integrated and multi-sectoral response to HLP from national and local authorities, as well as humanitarian actors.  
NRC will advocate for the HLP rights of conflict-affected populations through events and round tables with relevant government officials and humanitarian actors at national and regional levels. Similarly, actions plans will be developed to follow-up on the challenges and recommendations identified by NRC’s studies.

project_name: Enhance access to inclusive and quality education for children (girls, and boys) affected by displacement in the Far North region including host communities, IDPs and returnees
project_objective: The project aims to improve access to safe and quality education for crisis-affected children, with a particular focus on girls. The action will facilitate access to education for out of school children and adolescents to enable them to obtain the basis for integration into the formal education system. It is urgent to re-engage out-of-school children with the education system since, as these children grow up, their chance and ability to resume school decreases. The project will address gendered barriers to education and sensitization on gender-based violence, through teacher training, awareness campaigns and the promotion of equal and safe education for girls and boys, regardless of their status (IDPs, returnees or host communities.) To achieve this, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the decentralized services of basic education in Cameroon, and will ensure a conflict-sensitive approach while ensuring respect for Do No Harm principles. The project result will be achieved through activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of education actors at the community level and ensuring the protection of children and adolescents. To ensure a consistent and comprehensive response, the project will be developed through the lenses of gender and conflict mitigation, which are two concomitant perspectives to the dissemination of the principles of protection in the project. At the end of the action 30 000 persons including IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community’s children will benefit the above package of education assistance in order to scale up their access to qualities education opportunities.

project_name: Enhancing Coordination of Humanitarian International NGOs (CHINGO)
project_objective:
Please provide a short summary of the intervention, describing its purpose and target (4000 words)/ Veuillez fournir un bref résumé de l'intervention, décrivant son objectif et sa cible
The INGOs forum in Cameroon (CHINGO) was established in June 2019 with the objective to enhance collaboration and coordination between INGOs and between INGOs and external stakeholders (line ministries, UN agencies, donors, civil society organizations) engaged in the humanitarian response to populations affected by the three on-going crises in Cameroon.
Under the strategic guidance of its Steering Committee and the leadership of its coordinator, the INGO forum aims at enhancing information-sharing between INGOs, notably to support coordination of operations and build common positions, improving representation of INGOs and joint advocacy and contributing to the overall humanitarian coordination architecture. The project includes various services to INGOs, including trainings for INGOs and partners’ staff, sharing of experience and lessons learnt, and facilitation and support on issues of common interest. CHINGO also engages with external stakeholders and provides a collective voice for INGOs as well as an entry point for requests to INGOs. Advocacy and communication activities aim to support better understanding of the assistance provided by INGOs in Cameroon, identify and propose solutions to challenges faced by INGOs in humanitarian operations and increase the visibility of the crises in Cameroon with the overall objective to better respond to humanitarian needs of populations affected by displacement.

project_name: Responding to Humanitarian Needs of GBV survivors in East Jerusalem
project_objective:
With the existing health worldwide crisis of COVID19 and its long-term impacts, the number of women in need of GBV services is increasing. In Palestine, the heightened political situation is exacerbating the situation mainly in areas like East Jerusalem, the Jordan valley, and the northern district of the West Bank; coupled with the constant threat of annexation and its impact on Government services. Based on the needs identified through the HNO process, and several analyses of the humanitarian situation specifically in the abovementioned areas; the project and its interventions will aim to strengthen and empower women and girls in Jerusalem mainly the vulnerable and girls and women with disabilities who are exposed to GBV and enable them to live in dignity and peace within their families and communities. Additionally, the interventions will ensure women have access to services being offered through the multi-sectoral approach used by several service providers. The project will also enhance the approach of remote service provision through hotlines and other means in case the current situation of COVID 19 persists but at the same time, readiness to switch back to face-to-face services will also be maintained upon any changes in COVID-19 regulations.. Since the onset of COVID-19, UNFPA has conducted a series of online capacity-building workshops on providing services using hotlines. Those workshops targeted a number of GBV services providers including governmental partners; this experience will be assessed to further develop the virtual service delivery modality. 
The project will build on the current one by providing different kinds of support. mechanisms and tools will be promoted through Through this project starting with awareness, building life skills taking into consideration the left-behind women and WWD, and ending up with having GBV survivors treated and equipped with tools and income generation small projects. creating their own income generation small projects, thus empowering them to lead their lives and future. On the other hand, the project will target the GBV survivors as well the providers to match the scaling up of emergency GBV services with building the capacity of government and noncivil society -government actors to provide quality survivor-centered GBV services. Through the enhancement of new approaches, technologies, and platforms used throughout COVID 19 crises, the project will continue to use the multi-sectoral approach in providing the GBV services and build on past UNFPA achievements.
The project will target GBV survivor women and young girls at risk in Jerusalem (old city and Isawyeh,Abu Deess, Anata and Sufat, Al TurTuor, Silwan and Kufr Aqab suburbs surrounding Jerusalem). 
Currently, UNFPA in cooperation with it’s partner PFPPA and in through coordination with Hemaya Network in Jerusalem are developing a clear and concise referral pathway between Hemaya members to facilitate and ensure GBV survivors and/ or women that seek protection in Jerusalem can obtain multi sectoral services available securely, confidentially and without discrimination or stigmatization. The Pathway includes a comprehensive mapping of services available to deal with the diversity of cases that can be expected to be received by the members and define the referral system. Training is planned to build the capacity of Hemay network on the referral pathway and developed SoP to better understand the pathway and to address the GBV needs in accordance to the referral.
Furthermore, PESA training also is planning for service provider at the safe spaces and for Hemaya network members and relevant CBOs in the areas of project implemented.

project_name: Provision of life-saving and sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene  services for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in sites and host communities along Northern Mozambique
project_objective: IOM’s will ensure the provision of comprehensive WASH services in sites and sites-like settings for IDPs in Cabo Delgado and Nampula building upon its multisectoral expertise and are-based approach. Solutions will aim for a holistic approach including safe access to water, sustainable sanitation and hygiene promotion.

project_name: Plan de prevención y control de enfermedades inmunoprevenibles República Bolivariana de Venezuela, 2022-2023
project_objective:
Al igual que en el resto de las Américas, en Venezuela las actividades de inmunizaciones están orientadas por el Plan de acción regional sobre inmunización (RIAP por sus siglas en inglés): 
Si bien se mantienen logros como la eliminación de la poliomielitis (1989)  y la rubéola (2007),  la prolongada crisis socio económica del país y las presiones impuestas al sistema de salud han afectado el funcionamiento del mismo y su capacidad para responder a situaciones de emergencia, reapareciendo problemas de salud pública como la difteria (2016-2020), el sarampión (2017-2019), y la fiebre amarilla (2019 y 2021).  Las coberturas de vacunación del último quinquenio se ubican consistentemente por debajo del nivel óptimo (≥95%), y más del 50% de los municipios no alcanzan la cobertura mínima requerida para evitar brotes de EPV (80%), generando acumulo de susceptibles que justifican actividades complementarias, como campañas de seguimiento o de puesta al día, para mitigar el elevado riesgo de brotes por EPV. 
SComo agravante, se suma la pandemia por la enfermedad por el coronavirus del 2019 (COVID-19), no sólo por los riesgos asociados a la propia transmisión del SARS-CoV2, sino por la afectación de la normal operatividad de los servicios esenciales de salud como el de inmunización, el descenso de las coberturas de vacunación y el riesgo consecuente de propagación de EPV, máxime con la presencia de brotes activos de estas enfermedades en países de la región y en otras partes del mundo. 
se han priorizado tres líneas estratégicas de acción que buscan recuperar la operatividad de los servicios de salud para impactar en la prestación de actividades de vacunación y vigilancia de EPV, tanto institucionales como comunitarias (extramurales), en el marco de los compromisos nacionales e internacionales de prevención, control y eliminación de EPV: 
1.	Fortalecimiento del programa de inmunizaciones para garantizar el acceso a la vacunación segura.
2.	Consolidación de los planes de eliminación de sarampión-rubéola y polio.
3.	Implementación de planes de control y prevención de nuevos brotes.
El proyecto se enfocará también en la prevención y control de la FA mediante: 1. las personas susceptibles que necesitan ser vacunadas, 2. las comunidades que van a participar de las estrategias de comunicación de riesgo, estrategias de búsqueda activa comunitaria de casos humanos, vigilancia centinela no convencional comunitaria en la vigilancia de epizootias y en las actividades de control vectorial, y 3. los trabajadores de salud que van a ser capacitados en vigilancia epidemiológica de FA, en manejo clínico de FA y en control vectorial.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire pour les populations victimes de la crise sécuritaire et l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle dans les régions de l’Est, du Centre Est, Sahel, Centre Nord et du Nord.
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire s'est progressivement dégradée au Burkina Faso depuis 2015, surtout dans les zones frontalières avec le Mali et le Niger avec les multiples attaques des groupes armées non identités et les confits intercommunautaires. Les attaques contre les civils, les forces de défense et les assassinats ciblés dans les régions ont augmenté depuis juin 2018, entraînant une détérioration de la situation humanitaire et des mouvements massifs de population dans tout le pays. L’insécurité exacerbe une situation de vulnérabilité structurelle déjà très fragile. 
Cette situation accentue une situation de vulnérabilité structurelle déjà très fragile caractérisée par la pauvreté et la récurrence des chocs et risques de catastrophes. Les perspectives de retour immédiat des PDI vers leurs localités d’origine sont très faibles au regard du contexte sécuritaire instable qui pourrait engendrer de nouveaux mouvements des populations. 
La situation sécuritaire continue d’affecter gravement la capacité de ces personnes à subvenir à leurs besoins de base. L’action proposée par ACF vise à apporter une réponse d'urgence aux besoins de base des ménages affectés par la crise sécuritaire afin de leur permettre de satisfaire leurs besoins alimentaires sans avoir recours aux stratégies d'adaptation négatives, par le biais d'une assistance alimentaire d’urgence aux nouveaux ménages et une assistance alimentaire aux PDI et hôtes vulnérables en situation d’insécurités alimentaire aigue. Les activités d’assistance alimentaire seront optimisées avec la distribution de farine infantile pour les enfants de 6-23 mois des ménages ciblés par la réponse soudure afin de maximiser l’impact positif du projet sur la situation nutritionnelle des ménages bénéficiaires. 
Action contre la faim à travers ses interventions, favorisera également une transition vers le relèvement précoce et le renforcement de la résilience à moyen terme pour les nouveaux ménages de déplacés internes et/ou les ménages vulnérables de déplacés internes et d'hôtes, par le soutien d'activités génératrices de revenus (AGR). Il s’agira d’apporter un appui au développement d'activités génératrices de revenus visant à restaurer la capacité de production des ménages vulnérables afin d'améliorer leur accès à l’alimentation, limiter la détérioration additionnelle des actifs de production existant et renforcer leurs résiliences. La modalité de l’assistance alimentaire est le transfert monétaire et non restrictif via un système e-cash. Par ailleurs l’assistance nutritionnelle sera assurée par une distribution en nature via une distribution d’intrants nutritionnels se fera en nature après acquisition auprès des fournisseurs agrées. Par ailleurs, les appuis en AGR seront fournis soit en espèces ou en coupon afin d’offrir la flexibilité ménages bénéficiaires un choix maximal des types d'actifs productifs qu’ils souhaiteraient acquérir.  
Cette action est en cohérence avec les priorités du Cluster SAME et Plan de Réponse Humanitaire 2022 pour le Burkina Faso. Les interventions proposées s’inscrivent dans le but d’assurer une réponse rapide multisectorielle et adaptée aux besoins des populations affectées.

project_name: Assistance en eau Assainissement et hygiène pour les populations affectées par l’insécurité dans les Régions de l’Est, du Centre-Est, du Sahel au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Depuis 2015 le Burkina Faso traverse une crise sécuritaire, alors que le pays faisait déjà face à d’autres chocs liés à sa position géographique dans la bande Sahélienne de l’Afrique et aux effets du changement climatique. Cette crise se caractérise par une recrudescence des violences intercommunautaires et, entre les forces armées burkinabés et les groupes d’opposition armées (GOA) qui touche actuellement la quasi-totalité du pays. L’escalade de la violence qui cible de plus en plus des civiles, a conduit à la dégradation de la situation humanitaire et à des mouvements massifs de population sans précédent au Burkina. Selon le CONASURE, le nombre de personnes déplacées internes du fait de l’insécurité est de 1 407 685personnes en septembre 2021. La majorité de ces personnes sont des femmes (dont celles en âge de procréer =35,14%) et des enfants (dont ceux ayant moins de 5ns représentent 27,20%). La situation de l’approvisionnement en eau potable et assainissement dans les principales régions concernées était déjà précaire malgré les efforts fournis par le gouvernement. L’arrivée des populations déplacées a contribué à augmenter les pressions sur les ressources naturelles, au niveau de points d’eau on observe de longues file d’attente avec des temps d’attente de plus d’une heure (rapport MSA Fada, décembre 2019). En réponse à cette situation Action Contre la Faim propose une stratégie qui vise à répondre aux besoins humanitaires des populations dans le besoin (populations déplacées et populations hôtes) dans le secteur de l’eau de l’assainissement et de l’hygiène. Elle intègre également l’amélioration de l’environnement sanitaire et la prévention et contrôle des infections dans les centres de santé afin d’améliorer la qualité de la prise en charge du traitement de malnutrition et de réduire les maladies nosocomiales.
La stratégie cible principalement les Régions de l’Est, du Centre-Est, elle sera mise en coordination avec les acteurs présents dans les mêmes zones afin de maximiser l’impacts des interventions. L’équipe RRM (dont le Lead est assuré par Action Contre la Faim) continuera de faire la veille humanitaire dans les autres régions zones cibles et aussi la mise à jour des besoins des populations affectées.

project_name: Respuesta humanitaria para la atención integral a niñez y adolescencia afectada por movilidad humana en el departamento de La Unión
project_objective:
Para MdM la niñez y la adolescencia es un agente esencial para el desarrollo de los
países, sin embargo, para que este rol sea desempeñado es necesario generar
condiciones que favorezcan la protección y disfrute pleno de sus derechos, aun cuando el
sistema les coloque en situaciones de vulnerabilidad. Bajo esta visión MdM busca
mejorar el acceso al derecho a la salud y protección de derechos de la niñez y
adolescencia en El Salvador.
Resultado de este análisis se ha planteado el proyecto “Respuesta humanitaria para
atención integral a Niñez, Adolescencia y familia afectada por la movilidad humana en el
Departamento de La Unión”, cuyas acciones se encontrarán alineadas al Sub clúster de
Protección de Niñez, de tal manera que en las actividades a impulsar se buscará
fortalecer el trabajo institucional con la Red de Atención Compartida y el MINSAL del
Departamento de La Unión, a fin de garantizar la mejora en la atención integral en salud
física y mental a niñas, niños, adolescentes en sus familias afectadas por la migración y
el desplazamiento forzado en cuatro municipios del Departamento de La Unión.
Teniendo como línea trazadora el enfoque de derechos humanos y género, así como la
atención sanitaria y atención psicosocial, por lo que se reforzarán las competencias
técnicas del personal de las instituciones y organizaciones en cuanto a la
implementación de la ruta de atención, derivación y seguimiento de los casos de Niñez y
Adolescencia desplazada por violencia, garantizando la atención física y psicosocial,
dotando kits integrales de bioseguridad, higiene, lúdicos e higiene menstrual por género y
edad. El proyecto tendrá una duración de 17 meses en el cual se ejecutará un monto de
$808,000.00, en 2 fases de implementación: la primera de 5 meses y la segunda de 12
meses, ejecutando $263,688.31 y $544,311.69 respectivamente.

project_name: Coordination of the Child Protection Area of Responsibility in the State of Palestine
project_objective:
This project is in line and contributes to HRP Coordination and support objectives. It seeks to respond to the prolonged humanitarian crisis in the State of Palestine affecting the Palestinian by contributing to the protection of children and their families rights and dignity in accordance with IHL and IHRL, and with a cross-cutting focus with other clusters such as health and education. The project will support the implementation of the HRP and is aligned with the strategic objectives of the Protection Cluster as it:
i) seeks to increase the respect for the IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations as well as 
ii) support protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict-related violence. 

Child Protection is an Area of Responsibility (CP-AOR) under the Protection Cluster, with UNICEF as the designated lead agency. The CP-AOR is an active working group of the Protection Cluster, maintains regular contacts with the Cluster, and contributes to overall needs identification, protection analysis, and coordination processes. The CP-AOR’s role is to ensure the timeliness, quality, and coverage of coordinated child protection humanitarian responses. Currently, the CP-AOR has 16 active members in the West Bank and 23 in Gaza.
This project ensures the effective and efficient coordination of CP humanitarian actors in the West Bank and Gaza, including a common situational awareness and timely, appropriate and effective humanitarian response. It will ensure the regular coordination of CP partners and support a strategic humanitarian response, including strengthening needs analysis, contingency planning, promotion of evidence-based programming, and inclusion of cross-cutting issues. 
Gender considerations are an integral part of the coordination and response provided by partners in the field. The CP AoR will notably coordinate the interventions of Mental Health and Psychosocial service (MHPSS) providers in Gaza and the West Bank and support the provision of quality services and referrals with specialized services. This project will ensure the necessary support to CP actors in integrating CP Minimum Standards, including through training and technical support. This project will ensure Child Protection partners in both Gaza and the West Bank coordinate child protection interventions through a predictable, accountable, harmonized approach and understanding child protection needs. It also supports and ensures that there are functioning referral pathways for cases affecting children, notably in cases of violence (including gender-based violence), detention, injuries, but also demolitions, and settler violence response mechanisms. The final aim of this project is to ensure children affected by the conflict and their caregivers are provided with appropriate and quality services, including case management, MHPSS support, and legal aid. 
The project also supports inter-sectoral collaboration, ensuring the Child Protection sector engages with other clusters so that CP concerns are mainstreamed in other areas of humanitarian intervention. This is notably the case with the Protection, Health, and Education sectors, via the MHPSS Technical Advisory Group (TAG) or similar arrangement, to ensure linkages and common standards between psychosocial and mental health actors providing services at different layers of the MHPSS pyramid. Child Protection will also work closely with the Education Cluster to ensure an integrated approach is provided, notably for cases requiring a multisectoral response and cases of violence affecting both areas. 
UNICEF and the CP-AOR will promote compliance with PSEA principles and procedures. AoR members will be oriented on sexual exploitation and abuse. They will receive information on interagency channels, including SAWA Free toll number, social media platforms, and WhatsApp to report on PSEA.

project_name: Informing the humanitarian response in the occupied Palestinian territories through multi-sector, evidence-based monitoring, assessments, and analysis
project_objective:
Through this proposed action, REACH (a joint initiative of ACTED, IMPACT Initiatives and UNOSAT) will support the coordination and technical implementation of two initiatives: a Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) and a Joint Market Monitoring initiative, to provide evidence on vulnerabilities and market dynamics throughout the West Bank and Gaza. 

The MSNA will consist of a multi-sectoral household survey employed among a representative sample of the affected population in both the West Bank and Gaza. The MSNA will be conducted in partnership with OCHA oPt and within the framework of the wider development and humanitarian architecture. As in 2021, household data for the MSNA will be collected in partnership with the Palestinian Central Bureau for Statistics (PCBS). Central to this collaborative data partnership are strategies and protection measures, including specific channels to ensure accountability to affected populations, the most vital of which is a dedicated strategy and platform to ensure complaint mechanisms are accessible, properly communicated, and relevant to all population groups according to CBCM SOPs.

The proposed MSNA and JMMI will aim to achieve the following objectives:

1. Directly inform joint humanitarian-development response planning based on the nexus approach that the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) has adopted beginning in 2022, through the provision of comprehensive, multi-sectoral household data as well as monitoring and reporting of market prices and availability dynamics. Data from both the MSNA and JMMI will therefore aim to inform the development of both the 2023 HNO/HRP and further support the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework planned for 2023-27;

2. Provide a detailed inter-sectoral analysis of the magnitude and severity of humanitarian needs among crisis-affected populations in oPt, to support the calculation of sectoral and overall People in Need (PiN) and severity calculations.

3. Provide a detailed vulnerability analysis to identify at-risk and ‘furthest left behind’ population groups, as well as geographic areas with the most acute needs and vulnerabilities, to subsequently inform assistance targeting and response planning efforts; 

4. Support inclusive and people-centred assistance provision based on the principles of Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), through the collection of information regarding preferred communication, information sharing, and assistance modalities. 

5. To improve access to timely and accurate regional and nationwide data through the harmonized joint market monitoring framework that will provide evolutions in prices, market functionality/access, and household expenditure to inform cash transfer programming, development programmes and identify contextual factors (both historically and on a monthly basis) that might affect market dynamics to support cash-based interventions for programmatic actors.  

REACH will produce the following key outputs: 
1 clean, anonymized multi-sectoral needs household dataset; 
1 static summary findings dashboard; series of presentations to key stakeholders; 
1 package of six sectoral factsheets; 
1 final analytical report (MSNA Bulletin)
1 Interactive/dynamic Market Monitoring dashboard
2 Static infographics on Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (SMEB)/Cash Transfer Value (CTV) and price indexes
2 Static infographics on market functionality and goods availability.
1 final JMMI report/findings summary

project_name: Promoting the inclusion and access of Children with Disabilities to education in the emergency context of oPt
project_objective: The current context in the oPt has been highly impacted by the pandemic of COVID-19, resulting in additional burden on an already stretched education system. This is translated into schools closure and, at times, additional requirements to turn into online education in a context in which, a large number of students, is unable to follow this approach. According to gender analysis conducted by HI in Gaza and West Bank, 56.4% of the surveyed children with and without disabilities could not follow online classes due to the lack of internet connection and educational technologies or lack of classes / adaptive didactic support from the schools.  The study also shown that girls were more affected (65%) than boys (47%). Whereas the pandemic impacted children and educators' psychosocial aspects and well-being, the escalation during May 2021 on the WB and Gaza further aggravated the situation leaving children and educators in an urgent need for emotional and psychosocial support. Observations from the field showed an urgent need of building the capacities of school counselors in providing Inclusive psychosocial first aid. The Education cluster estimates that children with disabilities are one the most affected by the protracted and acute crisis: they lack basic assistive devices and education technologies that would facilitate their learning following the mixed approach of face to face and online learning, and are in need of psychosocial support (PSS) and remedial education. Since 2014, HI has strived to improve the access of children with disabilities to education both in Gaza and West Bank (mainly in Area C); by building the capacity of 260 educational staff in both areas, implementing schools emergency rehabilitation and adapting 36 schools. HI also has been providing specialized education materials, created 22 resource rooms, and developed technical guidelines on the inclusion of 750 children with disabilities and 341 children with learning difficulties in education, developed inclusive education practical manual to improve the delivery of adapted education services responding to children’s individual needs, and increased the capacities of targeted schools to respond to emergencies. Moreover, HI provided more than 614 psychosocial individual and psychosocial sessions to 705 children, teachers, and parents, including responding to COVID-19 emergency with the provision of 581 PSS kits. Building on this solid experience, the project aims to enhance the access of children with disabilities to inclusive education services in emergencies. The project will respond to the education cluster objectives, namely two and three, by identifying dropped out children with disabilities, enhancing the capacities of self-help groups on the localities level to support the children’s return back to education, strengthening their mobility, providing visual and hearing assistive devices, transportation, school kits, education materials and stationary, school-based structured individual and group psychosocial services. HI will also support the provision of holistic services through referrals to other stakeholders. Furthermore, the project will look at developing an enabling safe educational environment that is adequate to respond to emergencies through the provision of technical support for mainstream and special education service providers. This will include development of inclusive emergency response plans on schools level, accessible emergency schools rehabilitation, and capacity building to educators and children in addition to providing technical support to MoE to intervene on the level of Educational platforms to make it accessible for children with disabilities. The project will operate with two local implementing partners in Gaza and West Bank.

project_name: Safe access to inclusive and quality education for most vulnerable girls and boys and teachers in oPt
project_objective:
The project tackles the three objectives; in terms of advocacy and enhancing documentation of education violations, in addition to enhancing safe and equitable access to inclusive and quality services, and lastly supporting preparedness and resilience during emergencies.  In 2021, the Education Cluster recorded 62 education-related incidents affecting 3,200 students. These attacks on education took place when most of the country was shut down or the first month of the 2021-2022 school year. The war on Gaza and the continued blockade increased poverty and unemployment rates, lack of resources, protection concerns and disrupted children’s access to safe education. In WB and Jerusalem, the continued threat of demolitions, the increased attacks on schools located in Area C and H2, and the arrests of children at checkpoints continue to impede access to quality and safe education for children. All of these factors put children at huge risk of losing access to safe education with increased possibilities of drop-out and/or at the risk, especially CWDs and children living under poor conditions . Education related incidents have a harmful impact on students’ wellbeing and academic achievements. According to the “Danger is our Reality” report published by SCI in 2020, children identified many incidents that make them feel unsafe at school and deny them their right to access quality and safe education. In this report, children shed new light on how these threats affect their emotional wellbeing, sense of security, ability to learn, relationship with family and teachers, and how they feel about their futures. These boys and girls will need direct interventions, including psychosocial support, to mitigate the impact of attacks, and other interventions / referrals according to the type of attack. Teachers and school staff are also affected and need special skills and knowledge to deal with the situation on the ground. Gender sensitivity is needed by caregivers in order to support without inflicting unintentional harm, due to the cultural and political sensitivities in these areas.

Therefore, SCI will focus on supporting Safe Back to School by addressing barriers, and through supporting 17,000 vulnerable and underserved girls and boys, directly and indirectly, and 400 teachers, counselors and supervisors through supporting their continued access to quality education, psychosocial support, improved emergency and adaptive infrastructure in schools. In addition to extending support  to MoE and UNRWA teachers on remote learning modalities., it will support conflict-affected students with disabilities with assistive devices, educational kits and IT devices to ensure their equal access to inclusive quality learning opportunities. Furthrmore  supporting 400 parents on self-care techniques, stress release, and supporting children in times if emergencies. SC will also support access through facilitating transportation for students in risky areas based on needs communicated by MoE. In addition to supporting incident reporting and documentation of violations, and establishing prepared teams in the communities affected that are equipped with First Aid knowledge and documentation that can escort students to schools to ensure their safety. These will also be coordinated with MoE.
SC intends to focus on 40 schools in risky areas to be identified by MoE, in WB/G including EJ. Focus will also be on schools in EJ. SC will focus on communities surrounding the schools to ensure safe access.

project_name: Shelter, WASH and food security integrated response for the most vulnerable communities negatively affected by occupation policies in Area C
project_objective:
Through this emergency Project, and in compliance with the FSS’s Objective 1, Shelter Cluster’s Objectives (2) and WASH Cluster’s Objective 2, ACTED and ESDC aim to cover emergency WASH, shelter and food security needs of most vulnerable households in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, for a total of 3,185 individuals. Following a multi-sectoral need assessment of the targeted communities, a response plan will be implemented, covering the needs in WASH, shelter and food security through a cash assistance self-repair approach. The needs not covered by the project, will be referred to the relevant stakeholders to ensure a most holistic assistance.

The targeted area covers 3 of the governorates most exposed to demolitions, and the following 15 communities:
- Hebron: Al Ganoub, Edqeqa (Khirbet Tawil ash Shih), Khirbet at Tabban, Hiwara, Khirbet al Majaz, Khirbet al Fakheit, Halaweh

- Jerusalem: Abu George Road Bedouins – Kassara, Abu George Road Bedouins Nkheila, Az Za'ayyem Bedouins, Al Baqa'a

- Ramallah: Wadi as Seeq, Wadi Salman, Al Mu’arrajat Centre, Al Mu’arrajat East

In order to provide the most complementary assistance to these households, ACTED and ESDC will conduct the following activities, in close coordination with the MoA, PWA, local authorities and related clusters and sectorial stakeholders:
1.	Beneficiary selection through socio-economic and technical assessment
2.	Rehabilitation of residential and livelihood shelter, including HH-level WASH facilities for the most vulnerable households, through cash assistance. 
3.	Winterization/summerization assistance and protective measures for most vulnerable HHs
4.	Cash assistance for land rehabilitation and provision of inputs for the most vulnerable farmers
5.	Rehabilitation of water wheeled tanks
6.	Provision of unconditional cash assistance to support the most vulnerable households
7.	Creation and training of 9 Community-based Protection Committees in target areas, to ensure protection mainstreaming within communities, communications with communities, and accountability to affected populations throughout the project duration.  

The project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA), with a specific focus on the most vulnerable groups, including women, girls, boys, the disabled and the elderly. Gender principles will be mainstreamed throughout the entire action and CBPCs will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases such as GBV with a particular focus given to women and children. Finally, AAP will be core to the proposed Action by giving account to, taking account of and being held to account by affected populations.

project_name: Protecting the livelihood and improving the resilience of farmers and herders who are living in area C in north of West Bank and Jordan valley and affected by COVID crisis
project_objective:

productive capacity and enhance the food security of vulnerable farmers and herders who are living in Area C in north of West Bank and in Jordan valley.

vulnerable households are protected, and their livelihoods, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced. 

Food security in Palestine continues to be affected by protracted nature of the crisis, 
repeated shocks and continued restriction of freedom of movement, mainly for the most vulnerable families under the national social safety net (SSN), in term and type of 
frequency assistance. 

The proposed project goes in line with the first impact/ result “Agricultural assets and 
productive capacities of farms and damaged productive assets (wells, irrigation systems, cisterns, greenhouses) restored, and the clusters plans of the ministry of agriculture in Area C in north of West Bank and in Jordan valley especially in the Jenin, Nablus, Tubas and Jericho governorates. Where more than 10,324 living in 41 communities will be
