project_name: Fortaleciendo los servicios de protección y SSR para mujeres y NNA en comunidades de siete estados del país
project_objective:
Venezuela vive una crisis multidimensional que se ha traducido en un aumento generalizado de la VBG y ha significado un debilitamiento progresivo del sistema de protección estatal, del sistema de salud pública y la mengua de opciones dignas y seguras para el acceso a la SSR. Este panorama impacta de manera diferenciada sobre mujeres y NNA, quienes ya constituyen poblaciones con menos opciones en el sistema patriarcal y quienes son especialmente vulnerables a distintas expresiones de VBG. La implementación conjunta de proyectos de protección y SSR en varias de las comunidades incluidas en este proyecto les ha permitido a COOPI y Tinta Violeta desarrollar diversos análisis de necesidades que arrojan lo siguiente:
La capacidad del sistema sanitario en Venezuela es actualmente muy limitada. Las evaluaciones realizadas evidencian que los problemas de SSR son cada vez más urgentes, debido al aumento de embarazos en adolescentes y de mortalidad materna (esto último sin datos oficiales pero observado por personal de salud en múltiples centros de salud a lo largo del país), lo que preocupa a autoridades sanitarias y a organizaciones de la sociedad civil. Las instituciones carecen de recursos y personal para satisfacer las necesidades de servicios de SSR de las mujeres y NNA. Los centros que prestan servicios no siempre tienen clara la ruta de atención en SSR y las vías de derivación y seguimiento de los casos. La falta de formación y capacidad de los profesionales de la salud para la gestión de casos, prestación de servicios con enfoque de derechos y conocimientos técnicos en materia de SSR que reconozcan las necesidades específicas de mujeres, jóvenes y personas en riesgo de protección son también obstáculos para los servicios. El conocimiento sobre SSR también es un problema: la mayoria de las personas en las comunidades que se han abordado hasta ahora con proyectos anteriores desconocen las instituciones y actores que prestan servicios de SSR y no hay información sobre los lugares a los que pueden acudir para recibir asesoramiento sobre SSR. 
En cuanto a VbG, la violencia doméstica e intrafamiliar sigue siendo un problema en el país. Las instituciones encargadas del acompañamiento de las víctimas están ausentes a nivel comunitario o carecen de recursos y capacidad para tratar los casos adecuadamente. Se han llevado a cabo campañas de sensibilización, pero no son suficientes si no se refuerzan las vías de gestión de los casos de violencia para que los actores locales puedan orientar eficazmente.
Esta respuesta se centrará en la mejora del acceso a los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva incluyendo manejo clínico de violencia sexual (SSR y MCVS); la prestación de asistencia integral en materia de protección y la rehabilitación de espacios (centros de salud) en materia de ASH y AEE para apoyar las actividades de protección y SSR en las comunidades abordadas. Los servicios de SSR incluirán actividades de sensibilización, prestación de servicios (orientación, atención ginecológica, colocación de métodos anticonceptivos) y fortalecimiento de la capacidad local. Se mejorará el acceso a la protección mediante la gestión de casos, la orientación sobre los mecanismos y derechos de protección, el apoyo material a personas sobrevivientes de VbG, la mejora de espacios seguros y el aumento de la capacidad de los actores locales. La respuesta también prevee el apoyo a NNA en el acceso a documentos de identidad. En materia de ASH y AEE, se rehabilitarán los sistemas de agua y energía en espacios comunitarios y centros de salud identificados, los cuales también recibirán dotaciones de enseres y ampliaciones (según sea necesario), complementando la acción con el suministro de información sobre higiene y la distribución de kits.

project_name: PlayMatters-Sparking long lasting Learning in Ethiopia.
project_objective: Plan International Ethiopia (PlE) is implementing a five year (2020-2025) project entitled “PlayMatters (PM)” an education initiative funded by LEGO Foundation. The program reimagines childhood for 800,000+ refugee and host-community children across Ethiopia, Tanzania, and Uganda, especially children whose education and social development has been affected by displacement and trauma. Building on a growing evidence base that children demonstrate resilience when supported by Learning through Play (LtP) methodologies, PM cultivates holistic learning for children ages 3-12+. PM led by the International Rescue Committee and includes Plan International, War Child Holland, Innovations for Poverty Action, the Behavioral Insights Team in partnership with the LEGO Foundation. As part of the consortium member PIE is implementing the project in Afar, Benishangul-Gumuz and Gambella region of Ethiopia.

project_name: Joining Forces for Africa (JOFA)- protecting children during the COVID-19 crisis and beyond
project_objective: This project has been designed to respond rapidly to the global COVID-19 pandemic emergency. It seeks to address the most marginalized vulnerable population in the 5 target African countries: Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Senegal and Uganda. As European Union policy makers have recognised, children are the hidden victims, facing threats to their wellbeing and protection as a result of the increased risks of violence and abuse. Infection prevention control measures that national governments have taken to limit the spread of the disease have a direct impact on the lives of children and their increased exposure to violence. In addition, the action recognises that the global pandemic will continue and evolve, both in terms of disease prevalence as well as social and economic impacts. The proposed action seeks to address the immediate protection needs of children and will regularly assess the evolving needs of the target populations and ensure implementation approaches are modified for maximum impact.

project_name: Respuesta multisectorial humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
En Venezuela, DRC busca proporcionar asistencia humanitaria a poblaciones vulnerables y afectadas por la crisis actual como son las consecuencias socioeconómicas de la pandemia del COVID-19, de los flujos migratorios mixtos hacia fuera de Venezuela y de las problemáticas fronterizas relacionados a actividades ilícitas y conflictos de grupos armados que vive la población que reside en Venezuela, tales como desplazamientos y/o confinamientos masivos. Por medio de una intervención multisectorial, DRC brindará asistencia de emergencia con un enfoque de protección tanto para refugiados en Venezuela, venezolanos con la intención de migrar, venezolanos retornados, desplazados internos y a población de acogida afectada, aplicando de manera transversal un enfoque sensible a la edad, el género y la discapacidad para llegar a un total de 21,288 personas vulnerables. Los perfiles priorizados por DRC serán aquellos que presenten altos niveles de vulnerabilidad como lo son las personas con necesidades específicas de protección (NNA, mujeres, LGBTI, ancianos, etc.), personas con discapacidad, sobrevivientes o personas en riesgo de violencia basada en género, víctimas de desplazamiento masivo o confinamiento, grupos indígenas entre otros. Este proyecto será implementado en todas las regiones en las cuales DRC trabaja en Venezuela, que, al mismo tiempo, son zonas de mayor proporción de necesidades humanitarias severas de acuerdo con el HRP 2022/23: Zulia, Sucre y Apure. Esta acción tiene como objetivo ofrecer una intervención de protección integrada que combina la protección y asistencia de emergencia para mejorar las condiciones de las poblaciones vulnerables antes mencionadas. 
La acción propuesta incluye los siguientes sectores/actividades: Coordinación, Protección, Seguridad Alimentaria, Salud, Agua, saneamiento e higiene y Educación. El presente proyecto tendrá como línea de intervención principal, el abordaje de las necesidades de protección encontradas en una evaluación de campo llevada a cabo en noviembre del 2021 en los estados de Sucre (municipios de Arismendi, Cajigal, Mariño y Valdés), Zulia (municipios de Maracaibo, Rosario de Perijá, Machiques de Perijá, Páez) y Apure (municipio Páez) y como líneas complementarias a los sectores de salud, WASH, educación y seguridad alimentaria. Es por ello que DRC plantea una respuesta integral no solo a necesidades de  protección como son, el acceso a información, asistencia legal y acceso a documentación para población vulnerable, incluidas las personas sobrevivientes y en riesgo de VbG,  el acceso a asistencia individualizada y especifica de protección y prevención de trata sino también a cubrir necesidades básicas de seguridad alimentaria;  mediante distribuciones mensuales de kits familiares alimenticios por 10 meses en las zonas de intervención, salud; con la rehabilitación de centros médicos seleccionados y educación; proveyendo suministros escolares y de higiene personal y familiar, a través de una intervención multisectorial y previamente coordinada con autoridades y comunidades locales. Uno de los hallazgos de la evaluación de campo fue la falta de data relacionada a protección para poder producir análisis confiables, es por esto por lo que DRC plantea implementar un análisis de protección basado en evidencia a través de un monitoreo continuo de protección en las localidades de intervención, con la finalidad de tener información a tiempo para poder identificar riesgos y priorizar necesidades.

project_name: WASH emergency response to the most affected Women, men, Boys and Girls in Yobe and Borno state.
project_objective: The proposed project for 2022 will contribute to the WASH sector  strategy.  Project will be achieved by increasing sustainable use of gender sensitive emergency WASH services such as water supply and sanitation and hygiene promotion sessions, and ensuring that conflict affected populations receive immediate assistance and operation and maintainace support. The project will provide WASH assistance at IDP in camps and community level as well as in health facilities and schools. It will enable male, female, boys and girls to have improved access to safe drinking water in secure places, enhance their knowledge on WASH practices, prevent COVID 19, reduce prevalence of diarrhea and ultimately also lead towards improved nutrition security.  This will be achieved through a combination of interventions such as construction/rehabilitation of water points, Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), formation and training of WASH COMs with 40-50% female and building capacity of government authorities to effectively provide lifesaving assistance and have improved capacity to meet the immediate needs of newly displaced or returning populations. Throughout the course of the project, the active participation of women in the design, implementation and sustainability of interventions will be ensured and protection needs of women and girls will be identified and integrated into programming.

project_name: Provision of Emergency integrated Nutrition and Health interventions to vulnerable population in Borno and Yobe states, Nigeria
project_objective:
The overall aim is to reduce mortality, morbidity and undernutrition by providing life-saving nutrition, health and WaSH services in health facilities and communities.
1.	Affected populations have improved access to quality primary healthcare services in the targeted areas for reduction of morbidity and mortality
2.	Affected populations have access to quality nutrition treatment and preventive services through strengthening the capacity of health facilities
The program will be focusing on; health system for provision of primary health care services that includes basic management and prevention of communicable for all age groups from children to adults, antenatal and postnatal care services, support to uncomplicated vaginal delivery services and minor perinatal complications, support to referral services. It will also focus on support to Routine Childhood Immunization in collaboration with SMOH and WHO, support to provision of clinical management of minor physical injury, and prepositioning for Cholera and Measles outbreak in the targeted LGAs and finally provision of nutrition services. Providing medical equipment, supplies and pharmaceuticals and nutritional supplies to the health facilities through the award and in coordination with SMOH and LGA authorities. Reinforcement of technical capacity through sector/sub-sector specific technical trainings for quality service delivery. Building institutional and community capacity for promotion and provision of appropriate IYCF-E integrated with priority health and hygiene practices.
Target:
1.	Children: 0-59 months of age for malnutrition treatment and other children for provision of primary health services. 
2.	Women: key target of the project, both in its direct activities (e.g. Care Groups) and preventive and curative health services, as well as with the women empowerment agenda applied across the project.
3.	Men: men in the targeted communities will be provided with primary health care services for the management of non-communicable diseases (NCD) and communicable diseases.

project_name: Improve Access to Basic WASH Services for the most vulnerable resident population in Al Fao and Al Mafaza areas of Gedaref State.
project_objective:
In line with the prominent sectoral needs described in the section below, ACTED intends to extend and scale-up the humanitarian response for the vulnerable resident families living in Al Fao and Al Mafaza areas of Gedaref State. On this purpose, the Action envisages a comprehensive intervention in WASH sector which aims at improving the access to water and sanitation infrastructures, as well as to hygiene services, while building local capacities through the existing social bodies and WASH Committees and promoting hygiene practices. The Action priorities a conflict-sensitive and a community-based participatory approach in all its phases.
The proposed project is aligned with the three Sudan WASH Cluster objectives in terms of access to water, sanitation hygiene and environmental health by the rehabilitation of water pumps and water yards, and the rehabilitation of emergency shelter latrines. While both activities will be complemented with hygiene promotion and hygiene kits distribution for 2000 HHs 
ACTED will embed anti-COVID-19 measures in all the proposal activities. ACTED teams will receive trainings on COVID-19 preventive measures and a full set of PPE stock to be used during project activities. During activities, ACTED will ensure the beneficiaries and ACTED staff follow social distancing measures. Moreover, ACTED will install handwashing stations and provide soaps at training and distributions sites for beneficiaries.

project_name: Improve access to WASH Basic services for vulnerable residents’ communities in Khartoum State.
project_objective:
The project aims at providing comprehensive WASH response to most vulnerable communities in Sharg An Neel in Khartoum State.
Based on the needs described in the section below, the Action aims covering the major gaps that are currently preventing the access to a safe and cleaner water, adequate sanitation facilities and to basic hygiene practices. A soft component of sensitisation will be integrating the action and favour the adoption of best hygiene and sanitation practices. ACTED will rehabilitate 5 water pumps, and 5 water yards while ACTED will maintain additional 5 water points in terms of water quality assurance and water safety measures and complement the intervention by the distribution of 2000 Hygiene kits.

project_name: 2022 Humanitarian life-saving response in CP and GBV in North Darfur, South Kordofan, Kassala, Khartoum and White Nile states
project_objective:
This project is aimed to provide humanitarian life-saving child protection assistance for children and adolescents along with GBV response during 2022.  The project targets five states including North Darfur (Melit, Tawilla, Daresalam, Kutum, Kabkabya, Saraf Omra localities); South Kordofan (Kadogli, Talodi and Abojubbha localities); Kassala (Reifi Shamal Ad Delta and Reifi Hamashkureib); White Nile (El Salam, Guli, Al Jabalain, AD Diwaim and localities) and in Khartoum in (Khartoum (Mayo) and Um Bada localities). The child protection response target 10,442 people out of which (2350 girls, 2350 boys, 2872 women, and 2870 men), and will focus on prevention and response to risks affecting girls and boys among IDPs, refugees, returnees and vulnerable affected people and enhance their access to life-saving services and systems in targeted areas. Interventions will include community education/ awareness raising, service provision e.g. case management and family tracing, and community group activities. These will be delivered in line with Minimum Standards of Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPMS).  Linkages will be made between formal and informal systems and structures to enhance coordinated response and operationalize community feedback and response mechanisms and accountabilities among actors. Children with special needs will be given special attention across the activities. Resilience building will be a key component during the interventions beside promotion of life skills, peace building conflict transformation. Ultimately, the response will be in close coordination with service providers and child protection actors, as well as with child protection subsector mechanisms.
The Gender Based Violence (GBV) response is planned in same localities, and is working to prevent and respond sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) that affect girls and boys within IDPs, refugees, returnees and vulnerable affected host communities, targeting 4,41 people 4(807 girls, 807 boys, 1555 women, and 1245 men), and enhance their access to life-saving GBV response services and systems including clinical management of Rape (CMR) in targeted areas. Activities will include supporting running costs e.g. for women’s centre), trainings to strengthen capacity, empower children, and particularly young women with life skills and recreation activities, and empower groups of girls and women with income generating activities and vocational skills. This will be delivered based on survival centered approach, and the minimum standards for GBV in emergency programing. Plan will work to enhance linkages among GBV actors improve coordination, collaboration, and systems strengthening. The same CFRM will be used report and respond SEA issues and ensuring accountability to affected population through different and workable means based on areas of intervention. The intervention will promote gender equality and inclusion to challenge discriminations against women then reduce exploitation and violence among women and girls and support them to voice out their issue and call for their rights, this will be aligned with life skills and vocational training and peace building conflict transformation programing to maximize the impact and ensure developmental nexus to the intervention.

project_name: Integrated Approach to Treatment and Prevention of Acute Malnutrition for Affected Communities, Especially Girls and Boys Under Five and Pregnant and Lactating Women, in Pibor and Fangak in Jonglei, Tonj East and Gograil West in Warrap and Aweil South and Aweil Center in NBeG.
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger strategy is designed to address the main causes of malnutrition through an integrated approach linking nutrition interventions with health, WASH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities' resilience and prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Under this project, the proposed activities include prevention, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition in children U5 and PLW using the national guidelines through static and outreach sites; provision of basic health services at our Stabilization Centers (SC) and community-based healthcare using ICCM approach through the outreach clinics; provision of minimum WASH services to beneficiaries at nutrition sites and at community level in Pibor and Fangak (Jonglei), Tonj East and Gograil West (Warrap) and Aweil South and Aweil Centre (NBeG). Additionally, Action Against Hunger will implement preventive services through early screening at the community level using the Family MUAC approach, timely referrals, increasing access to MIYCN services, deworming and Vitamin A supplementation as well as improving the access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH and FSL services. Disaster Risk Reduction is a key element of the proposed project given the locations and both natural and man-made disasters experienced frequently in these areas. South Sudan continues to face extremely high prevalence of Gender-Based Violence (GBV). Hence, it is imperative that humanitarian interventions are gender sensitive. Action Against Hunger proposes to: a) continue its efforts to mainstream GBV and gender considerations in its Nutrition, WASH and health programs, and b) support the humanitarian community in South Sudan to remain accountable for GBV and gender-sensitivity. The project will target a total of 115,287 beneficiaries. Action Against Hunger will strengthen nutrition surveillance mechanisms through accurate and timely reporting, conducting SMART surveys and monitoring and analysis of data for early and objective decision-making.
The nutrition interventions are in line with HRP strategy and all the four cluster objectives for the 2022 HRP.
Primary/Direct beneficiaries: will include children under 5 with SAM and MAM, PLW with MAM, children under 5 and PLW screened, caregivers of children under 5
Secondary/Indirect beneficiaries: will include family members of beneficiaries and other community members.   In Duk Pagaak, the project will be implemented at the community level using revised guidance on COVID 19 at 3 outreach locations: Chol Tin, Pajimar and Polgour. Chol Tin is located in Tindir Boma in Pagaak payam. Pajimar is located in Uror payam while Polgour is in Ayod payam. However, since both these locations are over 10 hours walking distance from their payam headquarters and closer to Pagaak payam (about 2-3 hours on foot), the community prefers to go to Pagaak to access the services. As per information on ground, there is an internal arrangement between the payam administrators so that these communities can avail the services in Pagaak. In Pibor, ACF will be operating in Kiziongora Payam and there will be no overlap. 
Integrated nutrition, health, and WASH outreach clinics will be organized twice a month at the identified worst affected and hard to reach villages. CU5 both malnourished and non-malnourished, children at risk, PLWs, and other community members suffering from common illnesses will be treated/referred to the nearest health facility.

project_name: CP and PSS on Wheels: A PSS and CP Mobile Unit
project_objective:
Our creative solution to the consequences of the humanitarian crises on children and communities in out-of-reach areas in Lebanon, is PSS on Wheels. Buses serving as mobile units, are equipped to facilitate access to hard-to-reach communities and complement War Child’s ongoing integrated programming of Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Child Protection (CP). 
War Child interventions range from lower-intensity interventions that aim to promote well-being and prevent problems, to higher-intensity interventions targeting only children experiencing significant and enduring distress. The integrated approach embraces a socio-ecological approach, with services targeted at different ecological levels, which recognizes that children’s development is inextricably linked to the families, communities, economic situation, social values and cultural influences that surround them and provide for their basic needs and protection.
The mobile unit will facilitate access to all groups, especially the most vulnerable and girls and women. In addition, and in case of any rising humanitarian emergency, the mobile unit will be able to respond efficiently and in time, delivering vital services such as Psychological First Aid (PFA) and referrals to specialized services through case management.
Key objectives and activities 
1.	Boys and girls, men and women at risk, residing in hard-to-reach communities, have safe and equal access to an integrated package of PSS and CP services, leading to improved mental health and well-being of children.
2.	Vital protection and psychosocial support services are delivered efficiently and in time by the mobile unit. 
An inclusion specialist will be on board to ensure safety of and accessibility for  children with disabilities, to support in adapting/adjusting the activities and provide needed guidance when it comes to identification and referrals to a specific specialized service.
The PSS on wheels will provide the following services on board and in the outside setting: 
	Community-based PSS activities through TeamUp intervention that offers structured movement-based activities for children age 6 up to 17 to learn how to deal with their emotions. The skills they gain from the activities are linked to social-emotional themes and can be of use in their daily life. The intervention includes a Disability Inclusion Guide that will enable facilitators to engage children with disabilities and ensure their full and active participation.
	Puppets, theater and music are integrated in the community-based PSS sessions.  
	CP awareness sessions for children and caregivers, in addition to internal referrals that will take place from the activities to War Child services and/or external referrals to existing external service providers.
	The Caregiver Support Intervention that will enhance caregivers well-being through enabling them to have a better understanding of their emotions and providing them with techniques to cope with the difficult ones , and effective parenting techniques to improve the interaction with their children.
	Provision of focused psychosocial support (FPSS - Level 3 of the IASC MHPSS pyramid) for  children and families whose coping capacity is overwhelmed. These might include children in acute distress due to recent exposure to serious stressors or children who are not growing and learning according to their age and developmental phase.

project_name: Access to Education in The North and Akkar
project_objective:
Due to the unprecedented culmination of crises that Lebanon is facing, and in-line with the ERP objectives, this project aims to provide direct support to the most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant school-aged children and their families. These objectives will be achieved through community support, improving access to formal education services and contributing to the capacity of schools to absorb the growing demand of families in enrolling their children into the public school system. This will be done by provisioning basic education materials for children, capacity and competency building for teachers and increasing engagement for parents and caregivers in their ongoing support of their children’s education.  Thereby, contributing to strengthening the public education system.
The project is aligned with the ERP specific objectives 1. Direct Community Support Measures to most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant children and 2. Improving Formal Education of most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant children through schools.
Project will cover 4 unions and municipalities in Akkar and 3 municipalities in the North. 
The program will directly reach 14,850 Lebanese and migrant public schools’ students and their caregivers, 125 teachers and school staff, 20 public schools in Akkar and 60 public schools in The North. Moreover, the project will have a much wider impact in the target communities as it will develop the competency of teachers and caregivers: it is estimated that another 50,000 children and adults will be reached as indirect beneficiaries. Lastly, the project will contribute to improved equitable access to education and a reduction in barriers to education. 
Lebanese and migrant school-aged children will be provided with catch-up and learning support classes. In addition, children will be provided with quality learning materials together with access to remote learning through devices and internet connectivity. Special devices pertaining to inclusion will be provided to children with special needs and disabilities when required. Children will have access to safe learning environments through protection and psychosocial support sessions adhering to the minimum standards for Education in Emergencies (EiE).
Parents/Caregivers will be given the knowledge, skills and tools to effectively support their children in their learning.  Parents/Caregiver groups will be formed to support children’s learning and increase their engagement with the schools; guidance and continuous follow up by Outreach Workers will be provided to these groups. 
Taking into consideration the current context, families face dire conditions and barriers in meeting their basic needs. To address this and access to education, households of children will be provided with cash so that parents/caregivers can pay school-fees and other education-related costs. Food assistance will contribute to children having the basic nutritional status necessary for effective learning. These activities and direct support to families will enable enrolment of children into formal education, and ensure regular attendance throughout the academic year.
In addition to children and families, the activities under this project aim to ensure public schools have the basic conditions required for effective teaching and learning. Public school teachers will be remunerated for their additional, supplementary responsibilities to children entering the public school system for the first time. Public schools will be provided with funds to cover and support some operational costs in order to increase their enrollment capacity to cater for the current and emerging demands  of quality education while adhering to national and international standards on Education in Emergencies and Child Protection.

project_name: Enhanced Access and Utilization of Quality Health Services in South Sudan (Kapoeta South, Rumbek East, Aweil East, Aweil South, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijar and Rubkona Counties)
project_objective:
Health systems in South Sudan have been impacted by prolonged conflict, natural hazards, epidemics including COVID-19 pandemic. Reliance on humanitarian assistance due to inadequate health financing by the government (<1.9% allocation of the 2021 national budget allocation), inequitable distribution of functional health facility, human resources for health gaps and access constraints due to unprecedented flooding, frequent subnational conflict and runaway inflation contribute to challenges in meeting the health needs of underserved populations in Kapoeta South (Eastern Equatoria State), Rumbek East (Lakes State), Aweil East & Aweil South (Northern Bahr El Ghazal State), Koch, Mayendit, Panyijar & Rubkona Counties (Unity State).
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) proposes to respond to the immediate lifesaving health care needs of 340,728 people in need (71,579 Men, 79,095 Women, 93,220 Boys and 96,833 Girls with the inclusion of the elderly and persons living with disability. This project will provide essential outpatient care (communicable and non-communicable diseases), child health care, safe motherhood, Sexual and reproductive health, mental health care, gender-based violence response and emergency preparedness and response. The project will provide support to 12 static health facilities (2 PHCCs each in Aweil East, Rubkona, Panyijar, Koch; 1 PHCC each in Kapoeta South, Aweil South, Rumbek East, & Mayendit), 10 Rapid Response mobile (RRM) outreach posts (2 RRMs each in Panyijar, Mayendit, Koch, and Kapoeta South; 1 RRM each in Aweil South & Aweil East) and strengthen community health services by deploying 80 Boma Health Workers each in the 8 targeted Counties (39% of the BHI gap coverage).
Support to static health facilities will engage communities and County Health Departments (CHD) to map out underserved populations through assessments of intersectoral needs and prioritization of displaced populations without access to health services. The project will support the rehabilitation of structures, qualified staffing, pharmaceuticals supplies and commodities, health management information systems and reporting. Integration of services will be a priority of the project through multi-sector collaboration with food security and livelihoods, nutrition and protection mainstreaming. Providers will have capacity strengthening on provision of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services, Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) and Infection prevention and control (IPC) measures. The flexible approach deployed by the RRMs including a rapid deployment approach ensures that these teams can provide immediate response within the first 72 hours of an emergency. The IRC will staff, resource, and facilitate early deployment of the RRM teams to locations pre-identified by the community and CHDs factoring the health priorities of affected populations.
Coordination through engagement with local duty bearers and partners, engagement with national and subnational coordination mechanisms will be an integral component of the response. The project will consider the perspective of the affected people through IRC’s Client Responsiveness Measurement Framework using evidence generated during implementation to amplify the voices of the affected people on services provision and decision making. Disability inclusive client responsiveness will be prioritized through engagement of organizations of persons with disability where these already exist and by direct data collection at health service points using the Washington Short Set of questions on disability. Joint support supervision will be an integral part of the intervention to provide mentorship and coaching to health staff. The project will mainstream COVID-19 risk mitigation measures across all service delivery channels to protect clients and the service providers.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition Response to mitigate the impact of malnutrition among the most vulnerable under five children and PLW living in Awe east, Aweil south, Panyjar , Rumbek east , Rumbek North and Yirol west counties of South Sudan.
project_objective:
Humanitarian needs have continued to increase in South Sudan due to decades of civil unrest, recurrent climatic shocks, ongoing public health challenges, and COVID-19.The nutrition situation in South Sudan remain alarming about 2 million children under five years are in need of nutrition assistance . The burned of Acute malnutrition among U5 children is significantly increased in 2022 compared to 2021 from nearly 1.4 to 2 million. Of the six counties IRC is implementing Aweil south and Panyijar counties the recvecnt SMART survey reveals that the nutritional status in both counties were at Critical level with GAM of 23.1 % and 15.7% respectively. According to FSNMS round 27 Aweil east and Yirol west counties have serious nutrition status with proxy GAM rate of 13.1%and 9.2% respectively and the remaining two counties have poor nutritional status with Proxy GAM rate 7.8% and 6.5% in Rumbek north and Rumbek eat respectively. Despite the low GAM rate in four of the counties Multidimensional cases that aggravate the situation is observed that includes, flooding sever food insecurity, sub optimal practice of Maternal infant and young child feeding, and high rate of under-five mortality and morbidity that attributes worsening of the nutrition situation in the counties in the coming seasons
The proposed intervention aims to increase coverage and access to the most vulnerable community through provision of equitable and accessible nutrition prevention treatment services. The nutrition services will delivered through scale up the emergency nutrition responses through 87 static OTP/TSFP (17 in Aweil east, 10 in Aweilsouth,18 in Panyijar, 23 in Rumbek east 7 Rumbek North, and 12 in Yirol west ), 6 Stabilization center(two in Pnayjar, one in Aweil south, 1 in Rumbek eats, 1 in Rumbek north, and 1 in Yirol west) and through 6 RRM mobile tam (2 in Aweil east ,2 in Aweil south, 2 in Panyjar,). The IRC will implement integrated CMAM and MIYCN in all sites. Promotion of optimal nutrition and prevention malnutrition among young children (0-23 months through implementation of MIYCN to ensure vulnerable children have optimal growth and protected from irreversible malnutrition. Strengthening community participation and use of community structure through active engagements of the affected community through strengthening of MtMSG, increase engagement and role of CNV in prevention activities and regular community sensitization sessions. Scaling up of the existing Nutrition response to ensure timely service availability at all times. Scale up family MUAC to ensure early detection of acute malnutrition that contributes to early detection. An estimated of 20,031 SAM children,62,277 under five and 49,716 PLW MAM will be reached through this action across all implementation area in OTP and TSFP, respectively. Continue with the capacity building of CHD, and Primary health care service providers including IRC nutrition staffs. Train health and nutrition staffs on CMAM and MIYCN to ensure the nutrition serveis is provided timely. Rapid response team will be deployed to hard-to-reach area to ensure nutrition services is accessible and vulnerable groups have got timely treatment subsequently mortality and morbidity associated with malnutrition will be reduced, Integration of nutrition activities with other sectors will be also implemented that includes Integration of health and nutrition education messages at triage conduct Malaria Test and treatment , promotion of hygiene and sanitation provision of training on GBV and CP for nutrition staffs and conduct kitchen garden and cooking demonstration to ensure dietary diversification of children 6-234 months are optimized .

project_name: Lifesaving WASH interventions for vulnerable and undeserved populations in Bentiu/Rubkona and  Pariang
project_objective:
There has been decrease in Armed conflict in South Sudan since the parties to the civil war signed a peace agreement in September 2018; although few locations with reported cases of armed conflicts exacerbated by the  2021 flooding with a fragile political situation still exist in the country. The humanitarian situation in South Sudan continue to deteriorate due to the increase of vulnerability drivers including inter communal violence, climatic shock, severe flood leading to population displacement, commodity price fluctuations, and pre-existing vulnerabilities such as malnutrition. The above mentioned triggers has worsen and limited WASH access to the vulnerable populations in South Sudan therein increasing WASH related diseases such as Hep-E posing more protection risks to the vulnerable people. The 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) indicated that about 6.1 million  people’s living standards and their wellbeing will be impacted in 2022 as a result of inadequate or lack of access to safe water and improved sanitation. This intervention targets underserved and vulnerable population in Bentiu/Rubkona and Pariang County which is at catastrophic level according to the WASH cluster 2022 severity map and stressed severity stage in humanitarian conditions shown in 2022 HNO. 

Through this proposed intervention, the IRC seeks to improve access to safe water supply and sanitation for vulnerable communities across Bentiu/Rubkona as well as Pariang, and 2 static primary health care centers (PHCC) and 2 primary schools through the rehabilitation and maintenance of non-functional community water systems, provide safe access to household and or communal sanitation facilities and hand washing stations at strategic locations, provide hygiene promotion activities targeting diseases outbreak hotspots, and provide trainings to WASH committees.

The intervention will work closely with the County WASH department structure, community leadership, and WASH actors present in the targeted location for coordinated response as the custodian of water and sanitation services at the County level to foster coordination and collaboration with key actors in WASH and health in the targeted County. This will also support county led services mapping to ensure complementarity of interventions proposed by this project with other ongoing WASH services delivery partners.
The intervention will mainstream COVID-19 risk reduction measures across all service delivery channels to ensure reduction in transmission.

project_name: Livelihood Emergency Responses to conflict and flood affected food insecure communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
Save the Children proposes this livelihood based emergency project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in eight counties, which are known for track records of severe food insecurity and malnutrition in three States in South Sudan. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, therefore, improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks. The project targets primarily conflict affected children and their families in the internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and host communities.
In response to the ongoing food insecurity crisis, Save the Children proposes a livelihood based emergency project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in eleven counties, in four States of South Sudan. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, therefore improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks mainly intercommunal violence and flooding. 

The project targets primarily conflict and flood affected children and their families in the internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and host communities. The key interventions proposed through this action are food assistances, cash and voucher based assistances as part of rapid responses; and agricultural and fishing inputs provisions and productions with training packages on improved agronomic practices including improved kitchen gardening; and livestock vaccinations and treatment services against diseases greatest economic importance. 

The design of the proposed project is informed by findings of the multi-partner and multi-sectoral assessments, security and risk analysis and recommendations which have been conducted and released in the last six months. 

The proposed emergency response is designed in line with Cluster Objectives (CO1, CO2 and CO3) of FSL Cluster and to contribute to the HRP 2022 Strategic Objectives (SO1, SO2 and SO3). The Action aims at reaching out to 348,000 people (at least 60% female), which fall under IPC 5, 4 and 3 in four States of South Sudan, more specifically Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil East), Jonglei (Akobo, Nyirol, Bor South), and Eastern Equatoria (Lafon, Budi, Torit, Kapoeta North, Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Magwi) and Warrap (Tonj East).

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving Shelter and NFI Responses for the Most Vulnerable Households and Enhancement of Protection & Cohesion of Local Communities in NW Syria
project_objective:
Over 2022, this project aims to enhance the living conditions of vulnerable groups thorough providing a comprehensive lifesaving SNFI and Reinforcement and enabling of protection environment and community cohesion for 29,000 HHs (145,000 individuals) of vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities through the following:

- Distribution of 8,000 new arrival kits/NFIs for 8,000 IDPs households (40,000 individuals disaggregated by gender: 7,920 men 10,080 women, 12,320 girls, and 9,680 boys) in Afrin, Jandaris, Raju, Albab, A'zaz, Jarablus, Ghandoura, Suran, Aghtarin, Armanaz - Idlib - Sarmin - Bennesh - Maaret Tamsrin sub-districts.
- Distribution of 7600 winterization kits/vouchers to 7600 HHs (60% IDPs, 20% returnees and 20% host)/ 38,000 individuals disaggregated by gender (7,524 men, 9,576 women, 11,704 girls and 9,196 boys) in Afrin, Jandaris, Raju, Albab, A'zaz, Jarablus, Ghandoura, Suran, Aghtarin, Armanaz - Idlib - Sarmin - Bennesh - Maaret Tamsirin sub-districts.
- Rehabilitation of emergency shelter spaces in collective centers, unfinished buildings, and damaged houses reaching 750 households, where 550 unfinished houses will be upgraded (medium and light) disaggregated by gender (743 men, 945 women, 1155 girls and 908 boys) in Dana, Maret Tamsrin, A'zaz, Albab, Aghtarin, Bennsh,Idleb and Harim sub district and 200 HHs living in 5 collective centers in Albab, Jarablus, Suran, Aghtarin and Maret Tamsrin, Dana and Jisr Ash-shogor sub-districts in addition to conudcting cash for shelter activity  for 70 HHs disaggregated by gender (69 men, 88 women, 108 girls and 85 boys) in Idleb, A’zaz and Albab sub-districts. .
