project_name: Life saving and life sustaining assistance to the host populations in Gedaref State
project_objective:
All indicators show that Gedaref state suffers from many critical challenges in providing health services to both the local community and the refugees. The intervention aims to fill the gaps in curative health care and preventive aspects. Preventive and curative actions will include supporting the health system to provide quality health services, mobilizing the community to raise awareness of preventable health problems, and promoting healthy behavior. 
Improving environmental conditions, such as water, to minimize the spread of certain environment-related diseases is another key action that will be implemented. The fact that this particular geographic area is at high risk for natural and man-made disasters makes preparedness planning a priority action in order to respond in a timely manner when such a situation occurs. This action must be supported by appropriate data collection and analysis in order to make evidence-based decisions without delay. This could go a long way toward minimizing the impact of delayed actions, for example, in responding to epidemics. 
Availability of some specialized heath services on in few centers make it almost impossible for majority of the people to pay for transportation to go to those centers for such services. Some of these cases are life threatening emergencies such as obstructed labor or bleedings associated with pregnancy and child birth. This intervention will ensure the timely transportation of such patients to the centers providing such services through the support of referral system.
Protection is another issue which needs to be considered as one of the key interventions for vulnerable groups. These services are intended for survivors of GBV cases, children and some groups among the general population with some forms of disabilities.
The area being one of those areas identified as having high burden of malnutrition makes it critical to support the nutrition interventions in different forms. This includes proper screening of children aged under five years and PLW using MUAC and referring them on time to treatment centers. The treatment centers for malnutrition cases will be supported to ensure quality services and proper follow up of children admitted to the programs. Logistic support for transportation of supplies such as RUTF and RUSF will be given to each treatment center to avoid stock rapture of these supplies. Nutrition team will also be trained on different topics to build their capacity in handling of cases, reporting and follow up of children admitted to the center.      
Community volunteers will be identified among the communities under the catchment areas of the health facilities and receive trainings on communication skills, different topics related to health promotion and on how to do MUAC screening properly for children and PLW.

project_name: Integrated Response to Basic Needs and Sustainable Revival of Basic Services in Conflict Affected areas of South Kordofan
project_objective:
The humanitarian situation in Sudan is not showing improvements as access to some of the basic services are becoming more and more challenging for the population. The humanitarian crisis driven by the annual cycles of floods, disease outbreaks, civil unrest, border conflicts, and ongoing economic crisis is manifested by some of the key indicators. According to the health cluster October 2021 update,  availability of emergency medicines has reached 43% and the Pentavalent vaccine drop out this year is 8%. The available health work force is enough to cover only 17% of Sudan population and the price of medicine has increased by 1000%. .Although the signature of a Peace Agreement by some armed groups on October 3rd 2020 is encouraging, the situation remains fragile and volatile. 
Specifically, South Kordofan is highly vulnerable and weakened by several years of war that have aggravated structural development problems that were previously present. The crisis has led to a breakdown in the administrative system and the deterioration or collapse of public services in the region. Many health facilities were destroyed and are still not functioning.

The presence of PUI through medico-nutritional assistance interventions makes it possible to follow the evolution of the needs of the most vulnerable populations. Through the monitoring of activities by its teams at the field and coordination level, the work in collaboration with the health and administrative authorities, and the different NGOs , PUI reaffirms the fact that it is essential to continue supporting the most vulnerable populations through the improvement of access to free and quality medico-nutritional care in the South Kordofan, in particular children and women by extending its coverage through the reinforcement of the mobile strategy.
Taking in to account the humanitarian need in the region, PUI will expand its geographical coverage and intensify its integrated response to the humanitarian needs of the conflict affected population in South Kordofan in 2022. Nutrition is among the most needed interventions and the organization will provide supports for more OTP/TSFP centers in Elabassia, Rashad and El Tadamon localities of the state targeting up to 10 centers. Additionally, awareness raising on nutrition topics will be intensified by use of community volunteers in targeted villages and by IYCF approach. The community volunteers will ensure proper screening of the under five children and PLW for malnutrition. Referral support will be given to those children who have SAM with medical complications to go to stabilization centers for treatment.  
By doing this, the organization will contribute to reducing the morbidity and mortality in the affected population in the region.

project_name: Enhancing access to SRH services to vulnerable Lebanese and migrant women and adolescent girls across Lebanon
project_objective:
UNFPA & its partners will focus on quality life-saving SRH interventions targeting 250,000 vulnerable, marginalized Lebanese & migrant women, men, boys & adolescent girls. They will receive support in SRH information & services including for medical consultations, RH drugs & contraceptives. Migrants will be reached through UNFPA implementing partners Amel, Caritas including in the shelter of the latest. Hidden women and those subject to GBV, Persons with disabilities will be reached including through mobile teams. An estimated 3000 health care-providers & front line/ outreach workers will receive capacity development on SRH & GBV in addition to COVID19 in pregnancy. Interventions are endorsed by MOPH & partners. UNFPA proposed interventions are as follows:
A-Promoting SRH service delivery by
-Enhancing quality of maternal care through a series of training sessions to 1250 health care providers at the primary health care level on the revised RH services delivery guidelines namely for the ANC/PNC package.  
-Procurement of RH drugs and commodities to 120,000 men, women, boys and adolescent girls accessing MOPH PHC network & dispensaries located in remote & poor areas in order to avail RH commodities to the increasing number of vulnerable Lebanese and migrants accessing these heath facilities. Based on data by the MOPH PHC Dept,. the no. of beneficiaries accessing health services at the PHC is constantly increasing, namely, female beneficiaries. 
-Community mobilization and awareness raising on health care with focus on SRH through engagement of 80 midwives & outreach workers who will promote health seeking behavior among 80,000 women and adolescent girls. The outreach workers will receive series of training on health topics. The outreach workers will ensure referral of beneficiaries to the PHCs for further care as needed. Also adolescent girls and PLW identified at risk of poor nutrition will be referred for nutritional counseling and support. A media campaign about promotion of health care & availability of health services including for SRH will be conducted. Migrants will be reached through peer to peer approach, shelters and services run by UNFPA partners Amel and Caritas who have experience with this target population.
-Provision of SRH Services including medical consultation, midwifery care and subsidized tests for the most vulnerable women including women with high risk pregnancies, GBV survivors, etc.
 
B-Enhancing COVID19 response especially for PLWs by
-Establishing a team of specialist trained on the protocol for case management of severe COVID19 pregnant cases who would provide 1) on-site support for COVID19 infected pregnant women; 2) remote support for the management of COVID19 infected pregnant women; 3) facilitate referral to facilities providing specialized care/ intensive care for COVID19 infected pregnant women.
-Engaging midwives to ensure 1) awareness raising about COVID19 and pregnancy including for IPC and Vaccination 2) identification and support to COVID19 infected pregnant women including home care visits & referral to further care as needed 3) linkages with the specialist response team to ensure early response as needed, support transfer/ transportation of cases to health care facilities as needed
-Conducting capacity development for 500 health care providers on updates on COVID19.
-Training of 50 health care providers on management of COVID19 case management as per developed national protocols.

C-Mainstreaming protection for the most vulnerable women and adolescent girls through
-Capacity development on GBV safe identification and referral to 1250 health care providers from the MOPH PHC network to ensure their understanding of GBV and promote referral to further care as needed.
- Integration of GBV services in SRH through referral or within the same site.
-Provision of Dignity kits to 25,000 women and girls combined with the awareness raising on SRH and GBV.

project_name: Access to safe schools and quality education to crisis affected children in Northern Bahr El Ghazal State in South Sudan
project_objective:
While every child has a right to education, access to safe schools and provision of quality education in government schools have been a standing challenge to most South Sudanese children. This has been influenced by different factors including cost of school fees and registration as well as education supplies, access to safe water and latrines with changing rooms has affected girls’ attendance in schools’ low incentive for teachers and limited number of in-service trainings for teachers largely impact the access and provision of quality education. According to the HNO 2022 an estimated 3.6 million people are in need of education services in South Sudan.
The proposed activities aim to ensure girls and boys can be enrolled to school and access safe and quality education while responding to strategic goal 2 and 3 and Education cluster goal 1,2 and 3 in Aweil East and Aweil South of the Northern Bahr el Ghazal as highlighted as second priority by education cluster. The project will reach a total of 5600 (3055G, 1874B, 312F and 359M). The project will ensure all groups are reached including girls, boys, men, and women as well as children with special needs.
To improve access and inclusion students will be provided with scholastic materials and recreational materials which will support retention of adolescent and pedagogical and protection trainings will be provided to teachers to improve their teaching practices and creating safe spaced for the students.  Improvement of WASH practices in school through latrines construction with safe water points and provision of hygiene material which not only will respond to hygiene practices in schools but also the prevention against COVID-19. The education administrator, school management committee and Parents teachers’ associations will be capacitated in school leadership and management and psychosocial social support as well as coaching technique training to school inspectors which will support in supervision and guidance for both educators and learners. During this HRP period, IRC will continue implementing the 15 months existing education project funded by LEGO Foundation ($1.4M), which is aims to contribute to improving children’s wellbeing and resilience  through Learning through Play (LtP) approaches in Aweil East and Aweil South.

project_name: Respuesta multisectorial a las necesidades más urgentes de las poblaciones en alto riesgo en Venezuela
project_objective:
Actualmente, WV tiene su Oficina Central en Caracas y operaciones de campo en los estados Distrito Capital, Miranda, Lara, Aragua, Falcón, Barinas, Bolívar, Zulia y Táchira. Es a través de esta operación extendida que ha logrado trabajar de manera cercana con distintas comunidades y socios locales, para llevar asistencia a los individuos y hogares con mayores necesidades, especialmente niños menores de cinco años, mujeres gestantes y lactantes, personas mayores, personas con discapacidades y familias en alto riesgo, llegando a más de 60.000 personas desde 2019. 
 
Durante Noviembre y Diciembre 2021, WV condujo una Evaluación Rápida de Necesidades con 232 hogares, a través de la cual se encontró que: 1. 70% de los hogares experimentan hambre moderada a severa, 2. Cerca del 30% de niños y niñas menores de cinco años sufren malnutrición crónica, 3. La falta de acceso a agua potable genera la prevalencia de enfermedades causadas por el consumo de agua contaminada, poniendo en grave riesgo la salud especialmente de los niños menores de cinco años, y contribuye a la desnutrición, 4. En Protección, existen vacíos importantes frente a la prestación de servicios especializados, además la protección de las NNA se encuentra en riesgo, ya que muchos han sido dejados atrás por sus padres que han migrado, quedando al cuidado principalmente de abuelos, familiares o incluso vecinos o conocidos en algunos casos. 
 
El proyecto propuesto por WV, en línea con los objetivos propuestos a nivel sectorial para el HRP 2022, contribuye a reducir la vulnerabilidad de la población venezolana afectada por la crisis política, económica y humanitaria, con el objetivo específico de mejorar el acceso a la seguridad alimentaria, los servicios de nutrición, WASH de calidad y un entorno de protección efectivo. A través del cual se alcanzará a cerca de 39,000 personas más vulnerables en los Estados Barinas, Bolívar, Falcón, Miranda, Táchira y Zulia. Para lograr este objetivo WV trabaja en colaboración con organizaciones locales OBFs. 
 
La respuesta incluye detección nutricional, provisión de suplementos nutricionales y canastas de alimentos para hogares con NN-5, MEL, y otras personas altamente vulnerables o con desnutrición, creación de rincones de lactancia y canales de referenciación, estaciones de detección a nivel comunitario; y desarrollo de capacidades para MEL, hogares y profesionales locales. En Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida se apoyarán iniciativas agropecuarias con insumos y asistencia técnica, como una alternativa para fortalecer la resiliencia de familias y comunidades, promover ingesta de alimentos nutritivos que complementen la alimentación de grupos más vulnerables y posiblemente propicie el aumento de sus ingresos en el largo plazo. En ASH se proporcionarán insumos y formación a hogares y centros comunitarios para la promoción de la ingesta de agua segura, así como prácticas adecuadas de higiene y disposición de residuos sólidos. Así mismo se seleccionarán centros comunitarios en los que se realizarán rehabilitación, acondicionamiento y dotación de insumos para espacios de lavado de manos, sanitarios y cocinas; bajo el criterio de garantizar un servicio básico de WASH. Finalmente, en Protección se fortalecerán las capacidades comunitarias para la provisión de atención psicosocial, y a nivel de los hogares e individuos se trabajará en sensibilización para la prevención de violencias contra NNA.

project_name: Salvar Vidas desde la respuesta humanitaria,  mediante el mejoramiento de los servicios integrales de salud de las poblaciones mas vulnerables afectadas por emergencias (flujos migratorios mixtos, desastres naturales, COVID-19 y otras epidemias) y situaciones de violencia que permitan la disminución de los índices de morbilidad y mortalidad.
project_objective:
Se sumarán esfuerzos con comunidades, organizaciones sociales y autoridades territoriales de salud, para el incremento de capacidades y conocimientos del sector salud, incluida la comunidad en la identificación, alerta y respuesta oportuna a riesgos para la salud. Se apoyará técnica y operativamente la disponibilidad y funcionamiento apropiado de los servicios esenciales e integrales de salud en el marco de las emergencias, así como el refuerzo de las acciones de salud pública ante emergencias o desastres.

El proyecto tiene cuatro ejes fundamentales:

1.	Atención indirecta para la respuesta a situaciones de emergencias súbitas y prolongadas principalmente en territorios rurales y con poco o nulo acceso a instituciones de salud mediante el fortalecimiento de capacidades locales, para complementar la atención en salud de los grupos más vulnerables, especialmente en i) atención primaria en salud; ii) salud sexual y reproductiva (SSR); iii) atención a enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles (ENT); iv) salud mental; v) apoyo a la vacunación en esquema general y la COVID-19; y vii) la atención de la VBG.  El fortalecimiento incluye: a. acompañamiento técnico, b. dotación de insumos, elementos, medicamentos, c. apoyo con talento humano y d. consolidación de rutas para la respuesta en el marco de las emergencias.

2.	Apoyo a las autoridades de salud locales para las acciones colectivas de salud pública, incluida la vigilancia epidemiológica, y el refuerzo de las capacidades comunitarias en salud preventiva y detección temprana de eventos importantes de salud pública. Teniendo en cuenta los enfoques interculturales y haciendo participes de esta atención indirecta a sabedores ancestrales, parteras tradicionales y agentes comunitarios.

3.	Acciones de WASH para la prestación de servicios de salud que permitan mejorar el acceso a agua, saneamiento e hygiene, especialmente en los centros de salud; y la medicion de calidad de agua en las comunidades con mayor afectación a causa de las emergencias.

4. Apoyo en la preparación, respuesta y recuperación ante las emergencias desde el fortalecimiento de las capacidades para la coordinación, articulación y concertación de la respuesta en salud desde las mesas de salud y el clúster de Salud.

project_name: Ensuring holistic support in the prevention and response to public health risks of NCDs and GBV
project_objective:
The project will contribute to the improvement of the public health situation in the Rohingya camps and host community by addressing gaps in the access to quality service and the awareness on non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and gender-based violence (GBV). The intervention will entail an extensive health education and awareness programme targeting women and men at risk of NCDs, ensuring that appropriate care and support is provided by their families and clinics. It will enhance community support mechanisms, linking health, protection or social services. Selected existing community health posts and clinics will be supported to assist populations at risk to adopt conducive behaviours for primary and secondary prevention of NCDs, including Covid-19.
Furthermore, the project will acknowledge the role of primary health care facilities for reaching GBV survivors. The intervention will raise awareness and address  shortcomings at selected health posts in the provision of professional, survivor-centered GBV services, to ensure enforcement of their mandate on the Minimum Package of Essential Services (MISP) as per binding policies of the Health sector and GBV sub sector. The project will also strengthen professional medical skills, basic MHPSS and communication to ensure standardized service quality.
MdM will establish 4 community resource centers and provide technical support to the IPs who oversee operations. The CrCs, close to heath facilities, will enhance community-based support mechanisms through GBV outreach and critical health issues including NCDs. The CrCs will increase GBV prevention and holistic assistance to survivors, and reinforce comprehensive referral pathways.
Training on Gender, GBV principles and referrals for all staff and outreach including what is conducted by partner organizations will ensure engagement of staffing and communities in support of GBV survivors. The network and referral coordination mechanism will reinforce a comprehensive GBV response by linking community-based resources, outreach and sensitization, and existing community centres with the available medical facilities of proximity in camps and host communities.

project_name: Provisión de asistencia alimentaria y reactivación inmediata de medios de vida para personas afectadas por la prolongada pandemia del COVID-19 y las tormentas tropicales Amanda, Cristóbal, Eta y IOTA.
project_objective:
La intervención busca complementar la respuesta humanitaria del gobierno para ayudar a las familias más vulnerables cuya seguridad alimentaria y nutricional se ha deteriorado. El proyecto cuenta con dos componentes que permitirán a las familias mejorar su acceso equitativo a alimentos nutritivos y seguros y fomentar la reactivación inmediata de activos que contribuya a la recuperación socioeconómica.
El primer componente tiene como meta brindar asistencia alimentaria de emergencia durante tres meses aproximadamente a 300,000 personas. Según proyecciones de la CIF,1.04 millones de personas estarían en inseguridad alimentaria (fase de crisis y/o emergencia) para el periodo de junio a agosto de 2021, lo cual es indicador de que es necesaria asistencia alimentaria de manera inmediata para evitar que la situación de familias vulnerables se deteriore aún más. En esta actividad, a través de transferencias de base monetaria, se proporcionará acceso directo a alimentos sanos e inocuos de manera inmediata y oportuna a familias afectadas por el COVID-19 y por fenómenos climáticos .Para contribuir a la selección, adquisición y consumo de alimentos adecuados, se realizarán acciones de educación alimentaria y nutricional que motiven a las familias a la adopción y práctica de hábitos alimentarios adecuados y a la correcta manipulación de los mismos, contribuyendo al cuidado de la salud de los mismos y a la reducción de desperdicios de alimentos por su manipulación y conservación inadecuada.
El segundo componente consiste en la implementación de acciones para la reactivación inmediata de medios de vida, teniendo como meta alcanzar a 35,000 personas. El hecho de que 1.04 millones de personas se encuentren en fase de crisis alimentaria o peor, según la proyección de la CIF, indica que algunas familias están usando o han utilizado estrategias de afrontamiento peligrosas, como la venta de activos productivos, lo cual esclaro reflejo del proceso de transformación que las comunidades atraviesan luego de un impacto (shock), como la pandemia y los choques climáticos que afectaron a El Salvador en 2020. Por ello, bajo este componente, se restaurarán bienes naturales, se iniciará la producción de alimentos nutritivos a nivel comunitario (distribución de semillas, herramientas y otros bienes productivos), y se restablecerán los ambientes necesarios para la reconstrucción de medios de vida. Este proceso productivo, se desarrollará con un enfoque sensible a la nutrición, acompañando a las familias con procesos de educación que contribuyan a optimizar la producción de alimentos para diversificar la alimentación y aplicar buenas prácticas de gestión del agua para la producción y consumo, aumentando así la resiliencia física y comunitaria antes las crisis.

project_name: Building resilience and self-reliance of Rohingya refugee women and adolescent girls and livelihoods opportunities for host community women and adolecent girls
project_objective:
This project aims at building resilience of Rohingya and Host Community women and adolescent girls through increased livelihood skills, access to livelihoods opportunities including start-up support and establishing market linkages. 
UN Women has five Multi-Purpose Women’s Centers (MPWCs) in Camps 3, 4, 4 extensions, 5, and 18 and three in Host Community in. In these Centers psycho-social services, 1st aid medical services and counseling and referral services for GBV cases, are provided to Rohingya women, livelihood activities have been carried out. Three new MPWCs is running in the Host Community.  in Ukhiya, Teknaf and Cox’s Bazar Sadar.  6 months livelihood trainings will continue to be provided in the MPWCs to both Rohingya and Host Community women. The trainings will focus on handicrafts, fishery, beauty parlor, tailoring, production of masks, and ecofriendly jute product;  production of re-usable sanitary napkins as part of a joint initiative with IOM and UNFPA. After receiving training beneficiaries will receive in kind grant including sewing machine and other start up kits. Besides training on home stead gardening will be provided. Participants to home stead garden, will receive  seed and gardening tools. . In addition, ways to engage women in bulk production and linkage women’s market will be explored. Specific attention will be given to include most marginalized women and girls in the activities, including the female headed households and women with disabilities.  

UN Women has established a Women’s Market at camp 5, which started operation in January 2021. . Under this project, Women’s Market will be more functional to ensure market linkages for women producers, not only for trained women from MPWCs; but also, for other women producers supported by other partners such as WFP, FAO, UNDP, AAB, BRAC, HSI, PRANTIC, SNKSS and United Purpose. As the women vendors will be both Rohingya and Host Community, the Market is also expected to contribute social cohesion. Basic entrepreneurship skill development trainings will be delivered for the women who have shops in the Market. In addition, there are 3 café and display corner with MPWC in camp 4, 4 ext. and women’s market in camp 5.

project_name: Provide life-saving GBV services and increase risk mitigation efforts within affected communities
project_objective:
It is estimated that around 5,000 women and adolescent girls will be reached with a
comprehensive package of GBV response services (including case management, focused PSS and
legal assistance and better access to shelter, emergency and recurrent cash assistance) . 25000
will benefit of community outreach initiatives, non-focused PSS activities, including life
skills sessions and dignity kits.
UNFPA will focus on the following interventions: 
- GBV Service Delivery 
1) Support access to survivor centered multi-sectoral services for women and girls at risk and survivors of GBV through Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS). UNFPA will continue to support the operations of existing women and girls’ safe spaces and support GBV service provision integrated into primary health care centers  . The key objectives of a safe space are to provide an area where women and girls can: socialize and re-build their social networks; receive social support; acquire contextually relevant skills; access safe and non-stigmatizing multi-sectorial GBV response services (psychosocial, legal, medical); receive information on issues relating to women’s rights, health, and services). UNFPA has a cost effective model of GBV and SRH integration and will support partners in ensuring comprehensive provision of GBV services out of PHCs; 
2) Provide psychosocial support to survivors of GBV and individuals at risk including psychological counselling, case management, focused and non-focused group psychosocial support 
3) Provide legal counselling and representation for survivors of GBV (including survivors of domestic violence and survivor of sexual harassment and exploitation) 
4) Provide technical support to existing target safe shelters to meet minimum standards for optimal care of survivors in needs of safe shelter options. Shelters for survivors of violence are an essential component of a comprehensive and coordinated response and 

are globally recognized as a useful option for women escaping violence. This is because shelters provide survivors with the opportunity to distance themselves from abusive relationships and consider their choices for a life free from violence 
5) Provide emergency protection Cash Assistance to survivors of GBV and individuals at risk of violence and imminent harm. GBV Emergency Cash Assistance (ECA) aims at addressing a situation that exposes an individual to immediate serious GBV harm /risk and/or addressed its consequences. The GBV Emergency cash assistance’s goal is to address the consequence of GBV (such as treatment for injuries) and/or to mitigate the risk of gender-based the violence to occur (e.g. to flee an abusive situation). It can be used to access services that are not provided free of charge. The provision of ECA is a one-time intervention intended to address the critical needs of a GBV survivors. The Recurrent Cash Assistance (RCA) aims at ceasing or mitigating risk of gender-based violence, including to sexual harassment, exploitation, or abuse on the longer term. It might include support to pay for safe accommodations for survivors leaving abusive situations. 
- Outreach and GBV Risk mitigation: 
1) Engage community members in safety audits exercises to identify GBV risks and mitigation measures and disseminate the GBV referral pathways. Promote the peer-to-peer approach 
2) Organize non-focused psychosocial support activities tailored to the different needs of vulnerable and marginalized groups including empowerment  life skills activities with a focus on adolescent girls
3) Engage community in outreach activities to raise awareness on GBV services and risks as well as on menstrual hygiene management addressing period poverty through distribution of dignity kits and other commodities

project_name: Emergency Health and MHPSS in Gaza
project_objective:
The global outbreak of COVID-19 and recurrent escalations including the May hostilities are putting further pressure to the already overstretched health system in the Gaza Strip. UNRWA continues to provide essential primary health care services to 1.4 million Palestine refugees in Gaza, adjusting its approach to integrate COVID-19 risk mitigation measures. The public health system is already overstretched responding to COVID-19 emergency, and expanding the capacity of the UNRWA health services to absorb increasing needs is necessary to ensure access of vulnerable population to health services. UNRWA’s ability to respond to emergency health needs in Gaza is greatly constrained by the tight funding situation as well as the increasing needs, and ensuring the availability of this intervention is crucial. 
In light of these conditions, this proposed intervention aims to support the provision of critical healthcare needs for Palestine refugees in the Gaza Strip, while alleviating the pressure on public health system, through: (1) ensuring access to secondary and tertiary health services for poor refugees in response to MoH’s long-waiting list,  (2) providing life-saving medicines especially for NCD patients, (3) hiring emergency surge staff to cope with increasing needs and new interventions designed in response of COVID-19, (4) providing healthcare services adjusting COVID-19 emerged needs including telemedicine, the triage system in all health centers and enhanced measures including strict use of PPE, (5) providing necessary assistive tools to children with special needs, and (6) providing mental health and psychosocial support especially to women, vulnerable groups and people affected by the hostilities and COVID-19 emergency.

project_name: Emergency Food Assistance to the Crisis-Affected Families through the Appropriate Modality.
project_objective:
Through the proposed project Oxfam plans to enable the most vulnerable families in the targeted subdistricts through two-year programming / project duration to have access to the essential food items. Depending on local market functionality, people preferences, and availability of appropriate FSPs, distribution modality will be through cash, noting that Oxfam had performed market assessment in several communities in the proposed subdistrict and found that cash modality is preferable and feasible. Oxfam will provide up-to 6 rounds of cash transfers to 14,000 HHs, at least 30% of which will be headed by females. This will benefit a total of 70,000 individuals in acute need through the project period. The monthly distribution value will be equal to 65% of the MEB covering food needs for 5 family members “58.4” USD using the Central Bank preferential rate at the time of distribution. The transfer value might be changed based on the discussions within the CWG. Oxfam will coordinate with other humanitarian actors to avoid overlapping in and ensure complementarity in geographical targeting, their coordination will be done through FSA Sector, CWG and even through bilateral meetings. Oxfam will make sure to engage the communities in the selection of the most vulnerable families. Therefore, Oxfam will form a community committee where at least 50% of participants will be women. The committees will be responsible of identifying the most vulnerable families. Oxfam will follow the internal procedures of verification process for the beneficiary list in coordination with the local community committee. The aid delivery process, impact and market prices will be monitored regularly.

Assessments conducted by Oxfam staff show that cash-based assistance would be feasible for cash grants in the targeted subdistricts. Cash modality is aligned with the targeted household preference and the majority of households already reported using markets as their main source for purchasing food and non-food items.

project_name: Community Outreach Mobilization and Empowerment in Misrata and Tripoli (COMEMT)
project_objective:
HLBY21-PRO-173395-1

The IRC’s proposed project, Community Outreach Mobilization Empowerment (COME- MT), aims to provide community-based protection response to vulnerable people with specific protection needs and to strengthen the protection environment for these people with information dissemination and awareness raising with broader communities. The IRC will add an individual protection assistant (in-kind) component to complement the immediate material needs of the most vulnerable to support their socio-economic well-being and to prevent them from adapting a harmful mechanism to cope with their specific needs. COME will target the people not based on the status but on their needs and protection risks. The specific prioritization and the focus will be given on the people in need of mental health and psycho-social support, missing documentation, people with disabilities, and elderly among the communities targeted with this action.
The IRC has successfully utilized the community volunteer system for implementing the community-based protection interventions in Libya to address the protection and health needs of the targeted communities (IDPs, returnees, non-displaced, migrants and refugees) since 2018. For the proposed action, IRC will leverage its community outreach volunteers in Tripoli and Misrata (including, medina, Bani Walid and Tawerga) to identify the people in need of protection assistance, information and access to the required services. The COVs will be trained on psychological first aid, identifying the MHPSS and protection needs, and administering the safe service referrals to the specialized services. The IRC will ensure that the COVs are selected among their respective communities and representative for different age and gender groups. 
To strengthen the protection environment and for its sustainability, the IRC will provide capacity building trainings on Protection and Humanitarian Principles, Protection Mainstreaming, and International Legal Framework and Refugee Protection for the local humanitarian and civil society organizations, local authorities (Ministry of Health, Ministry of Social Affairs, and relevant Municipality staff) (75), and community committee leaders and members (80). 
The IRC has supported the establishment of five migrant and refugee community committees in Tripoli and will target to add five more with this action. The IRC aims improving the function and participation of the committees in responding the needs of their respective communities by supporting them with guidance to create and implement their community based protection action plans and with small funds for the identified urgent action plans (in-kind support). (10)
The action will be complementing the IRC’s ongoing protection, health and governance programs in the target areas, which will help for the timely and safe referrals between health, mental health, and protection (IPA, GBV, and CP) support services provided by the IRC. This will also help the IRC to leverage the exiting CBP capacity and the already established relations with and the ongoing support to the local CSOs and stakeholders.

project_name: Enhancing access to safe water and basic sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable conflict-affected populations in and out of camp across Northern Syria
project_objective: The proposed project aims at enhancing access to water, sanitation, and hygiene services for conflict-affected populations across Northern Syria, with emergency, life-saving WASH assistance mostly provided in camp settings, and longer-term, resilience focused assistance mostly provided off camp. ACTED will provide a variety of assistance modalities toward this aim. In-camp, ACTED will provide life-saving water supply (through a mix of trucking and pumping), sanitation services including wastewater and latrine management, and solid waste management services, to several camp clusters in Northwest Syria (NWS), as well as Washokani and Areesheh camps and multiple informal settlements in Northeast Syria (NES). Complementary to this assistance, ACTED will provide hygiene promotion and awareness sessions to all targeted camp residents, and distribute WASH NFIs to highly vulnerable displaced persons. Off-camp, ACTED will rehabilitate, through contractors and in coordination with all relevant stakeholders (including WASH Cluster, WASH Working Group, and local councils and technical departments), numerous assets, including water pumping stations, water treatment stations, boreholes, etc. ACTED will also install new assets and/or facilities to fit existing assets, in areas where the need for water is highest. ACTED will look to hand over these assets to relevant local stakeholders while providing operation and maintenance support, and capacity-building trainings, in order for WASH-related basic services to remain operational through these assets after the completion of the intervention. In Northwest Syria, ACTED will conduct repairs and rehabilitation of WASH facilities in health centers. Lastly, ACTED will also provide emergency water trucking out-of-camp in Northeast Syria based on needs identified by the Working Group. In total, ACTED expects its activities to reach 1,619,144 individuals under the WASH sector in 2022. ACTED will seek synergies with its response in other sectors, primarily Early Recovery activities, notably through activities falling under indicators from both WASH and ERL sectors, such as WASH asset rehabilitation activities. Specifically, ACTED will seek to rehabilitate key water supply assets and systems off-camp in 2022, particularly in NES, in a effort to restore and sustain communities' access to this service, and to hand it over to local stakeholder where possible. This approach is geared for increased sustainability of the WASH response and is expected to increase cost-efficiency in the upcoming years (2023 and beyond) by reducing the need for live-saving assistance off-camp, particularly water trucking. With regards to in-camp interventions, ACTED will work through targeted communities in camp, notably through community-based structures, to build the sustainability of the WASH activities conducted. In NES, this include involving Water Committees from the resident population to participate in water quality monitoring, whilst informing camp residents on how to raise maintenance and water supply issues. In NWS, ACTED is also evaluating the prospects of cost recovery mechanisms. The approach considers social and economic dimensions, including the enabling environment, willingness to pay, and financial considerations such as fixed and variable costs. Active participation in the Cost Recovery in WASH Infrastructure Technical Working Group at the WASH Cluster will further promote informed decisions are taken. Where conditions allows mall-scale pilots will be considered. Such pilots can range from building capacity of water user committees and station management to fill the vacuum of no regulator  to installing off-grid energy systems. The latter will reduce the marginal cost, by off-setting capital expenditure to be recovered both in terms of initial investment made and reducing operational expenditure by limiting the hours of running diesel-powered generators.

project_name: Protection services for women and adolescent girls in NWS.
project_objective:
The WPE program focus is to ensure women and adolescent girls are supported emotionally, psychologically, and physically while provided further knowledge on GBV, GBV forms, risks and prevention. As the IRC – WPE acknowledges the significant protection concerns women and adolescent girls in Syria face, WPE rounds its functionality in order to directly and indirectly adhere to the prevention and intervention measures required to ensure the increased safety measures are deliberated to women and adolescent girls. The IRC works closely with GBV sub-cluster working groups in Turkey as one of the major protection actors in the humanitarian field. Under the IRC, as a member of the GBV sub-cluster , the program supports sub-cluster raised protection capacity needs, protection knowledge and protection management training material. IRC is an active member on the GBV sub cluster and accordingly, All activities will be implemented with close coordination with the GBV Sub-Cluster and will follow the GBV Sub-Cluster guidelines ,SOPs and tools, with focus on the GBV case management guidelines and GBV M&E tool kit, GBV awareness tool kits, cash for protection ,Individual Protection Assistant (IPA) and case fund GBV criteria.

Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team, supported by the WPE team will conduct GBV need assessment to assess the needs in the community and design the activities to be in line with the assessment result. project_name: Mejoras del acceso a los servicios de salud y seguridad nutricional en instituciones publicas y comunidades vulnerables en la región central y centro occidental de Venezuela

project_objective: Conflict and displacement continue to affect North East Syria (NES), while needs are heightened due to the COVID-19outbreak, impacting healthcare service provision, especially in underserved areas and IDPs/refugees camps in Hassakeh,Deir-ez Zor, Raqqa and Aleppo Gov.Through this Action, in continuation with previous ECHO-funded phases (Jun.’17-Apr.'22), UPP and health and protection local IPs , aim to ameliorate living conditions and save lives of war-affected persons in NES by improving access to emergency&primaryhealth care, life-saving obstetric and reproductive health (RH) services, COVID-19 preparedness&response, and to protection and prevention services. Continued support will be provided toPHCCs in Raqqa city and Areesha, Al Hol, Abu Khashab, Mahmoudli camps, in addition to new support to Serekanyecamp PHCC; to essential RH services at secondary care level in Maternity Deps. in Tabqa and Manbij and in RaqqaMaternity and Pediatric Hospital, and to the COVID-19 Treatment Facility in Manbij. Continued support will also beensured to the Emergency Management and Coordination Center (EMCC) for both emergency and COVID-19 referrals.The protection intervention (described and budgeted in module entry  HSYR22-HEA-188482-1) will ensure continuity of critical CP and GBV life-saving services for women, girls (WGs), and boys, as well as caregivers, in Safe spaces in Raqqa. project_objective:

The WASH component aims at consolidating and where needed establishing the safe system of healthcare waste management in several healthcare facilities in the Governorates of Deir ez-Zor, ar-Raqqah, Aleppo and al-Hasakeh. This will allow to strengthen the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) activities carried out in all targeted health facilities and it is part of the Covid-19 response in NES. project_name: Inclusive access to education and skills development opportunities for crisis affected Rohingya and host community children, adolescents and youth in Cox's Bazar District
project_objective:
UNICEF will support access to inclusive early childhood development, learning and skills development opportunities for 245,994 children (50% girls) refugee crisis affected children, adolescents and youth aged 3-24 years, including 222,026 in the camps and 23,968 in Teknaf and Ukhyia upazilas of Cox’s Bazar District. UNICEF will work with partners to improve enrolment, retention and inclusive learning environment for girls, boys, and children with disability. 

In the camps, over 2,800 learning centres will be supported by UNICEF to provide access to progressive learning in safe and protective environment. The capacity of teachers, technical officers and programme officers will be built to enable them effectively support the delivery of improved learning for 222,026 (50% girls) children aged 3-18 years using the Learning Competency Framework and Approach (LCFA) as well as the Myanmar curriculum for students in Grades 6 to 9 and Grades 1 and 2.  These include, 28,316 (14,237 girls) refugee adolescents and youth (15-24) will be supported with secondary education (10,000) based on the Myanmar curriculum and vocational skills development (18,18,316) programmes.  UNICEF also support capacity building of partners on inclusive education, learning outcomes assessment and the use of education technology solutions to enhance the delivery of education services as part of the COVID-19 response and recovery. The trainings for teachers will also include Code of Conduct, PSEA, Child Safeguarding so as to promote a protective learning environment.

In the host communities in Teknaf and Ukhyia, UNICEF will support 23,968 children, adolescents, and youth to access improved quality preprimary and primary education. The support to host community will include focus on out of schools chidlren and adolescents with access to vocational skills training and non-formal education. Schools will be supported to provide continuity of learning with appropriate safety measures in place as well disaster risk reduction. UNICEF will provide grants to schools to support implementation of school improvement plans in collaboration with school management committees. Through thesse interventions which support HC, the response will promote social cohesion as a conflict sensitive programming approach will be used that encourage participation of the host community.

Strong focus on girls' education will be ensured through a) awareness raising and sensitization of parents and traditional leaders, b) the scale-up of girls-only sessions, c) gender-segregated water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities, d) recruiting and training more female Rohingya teachers and e) developing and sharing gender-sensitive teaching and learning materials with caregivers, teachers and students. A focus on including three per cent children with disabilities will be mainstreamed across interventions such as teacher trainings including across materials developed to support these actions.

project_name: Provision of quality education services for children and adolescents in Syria
project_objective:
The response is primarily focused on supporting children who have lost learning and on those who have no access to safe, quality education due to their displacement. This will be achieved by providing boys and girls with early childhood care and education (ECCE), and basic non-formal education (NFE) services with other integrated MHPSS, CP, WASH and cash components to mitigate the effects of the multiple barriers and vulnerabilities that boys and girls face as they attempt to access education. 
To ensure access to early learning and child development opportunities, non-formal early childhood development (ECCE) services will be provided. 
Wellbeing needs of children is therefore a key part of our response where social emotional learning support is provided for children, along with wellbeing support for teachers. The data indicates children who do not attend school seem to be more likely to come from a household with reported psychological distress with under 18-year olds than children who attend school.
Supporting children’s safe access to quality education does imply the importance of working with teachers and improving their capacity to provide education that is child centered and responsive to the different needs of boys and girls. The project will be supporting the teachers knowledge and skills, through different approaches, so that they are better positioned to showcase positive teaching practices inside the classroom and outside the classroom, specifically when they interact with parents and communities.    Learning spaces infrastructure will be upgraded to support the children’s right to safe and quality education. WASH facilities will be upgraded so children have access to clean drinking water, latrines are segregated and functional and connected to wastewater collection systems that are safe.  
              
The project will be targeting such locations that has no or limited education services in the camp/community, high number of out of school children Internal Displaced children in school age, children in risk for child labor, early marriage and other CP risks. Clear vulnerability criteria will be established to select the most vulnerable beneficiaries, and especially for the CVA support.
The project will be supporting objective number 1: This will be through the ECE, NFE support, BTL campaigns, upgrading classrooms, provision of education materials, winterization and heating support for children and for facilities, winter support/clothes, cash for protection.
As for objective 2: The project will be supporting Teacher and education personnel with professional development opportunities in accordance to INEE standards, PSS support for children and school staff, education materials and supplies and life skills support.
As for objective 3: PTAs will be either established or strengthened and on supporting partners inside Syria to develop strategic thinking on advocacy uses for data on attacks on education: monitoring, reporting.

Children will transition from one non formal education level to another, and same for ECCE. Teachers capacity will be enhance by various Teachers professional development opportunities and the teachers learning centers,. The community structures will be strengthened in the second year based on the learnings from the first years.
The project will work on building the capacity of the trusted and responsible adults in children’s lives – their caregivers, teachers, other community members and service providers. It will strengthen their ability to communicate with children, and better support their learning and development needs. This will be achieved through the establishment of PTA’s. At the wider community level, positive parenting messages and gender equality will continue through the constant dialogue with community structures, Parent/Teacher Associations (PTAs). Out of the 37930 targeted children, 21% are assessed to be in Severity 4, and 79% in severity 3.

project_name: Multi-sector humanitarian assistance to crisis affected populations in Northwest and Southwest Cameroon
project_objective:
The NWSW regions of Cameroon continue to have hundreds of thousands of individuals affected by crisis and in need of humanitarian assistance. DRC is proposing a multi-sector humanitarian response to meet the most urgent needs of affected populations, including a response to protection, shelter, NFI and food security needs.
Through emergency shelter and NFI support, vulnerabilities will be mitigated in the immediate term for those permanently or chronically displaced by conflict in highly vulnerable, hard to reach areas. The proposed action aims to address some of the most critical gaps in assistance through the provision of cluster standard shelter and NFI assistance to 6,500 households.
The crisis is threatening to produce a lost generation of children who have been highly exposed to violence and conflict, without any form of education, and are caught in an environment where community and family structure degradation is pervasive, leading to high needs for psychosocial support. DRC will expand on the demonstrated success of its current child protection programming to continue to meet the social and emotional needs of children affected by conflict through community-based child protection programming, and individual child protection assistance. This will produce an improved protection environment for over 10,000 children in the immediate and medium term.
The crisis in the South West has created diverse and widespread protection needs that are in critical need of being chronicled and addressed. DRC has had dedicated protection monitoring and response capacity in the South West since January 2019. The proposed action will allow DRC to expand coverage of monitoring and response, building the capacity for evidence-based advocacy, and improving the protection environment for individuals and communities in the longer term. Protection needs will be addressed through psychosocial support including psychological first aid, with immediate protection cases being supported through individual protection assistance, as well as community-based protection assistance through Community Based Protection Committees and community protection assistance. Protection monitoring and reporting will allow DRC to continue to gather important information on the protection environment in highly vulnerable communities informing both advocacy and response.
To respond to the urgent food security needs in the NWSW regions, DRC will provide food security assistance through e-vouchers to the 3,000 most vulnerable households. DRC will distribute e-vouchers to these households as well as organize food fairs where they will be able to use these vouchers to buy food items. Suppliers from these food fairs will be selected though DRC logistics. A list of products that have to be supplied will be given to suppliers in advance in order to make sure that all food needs are covered during the food distribution (organized as a fair where beneficiaries can pay with vouchers).
As a result of the proposed intervention, crisis affected households will have better capacity to meet their basic needs, and the protection environment for both children and adults will be improved in the longer term.

Child and Youth Education Pathways for vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
NRC project will contribute to Education sector HRP objectives 1, 2 and 3. NRC will deliver this project through a combination of direct, partner-led and hybrid modalities.

The Education intervention forms part of NRC’s safe, integrated and inclusive response in Syria. NRC’s Education team will continue working in close collaboration with NRC’s ICLA/Capacity Building, Shelter, WASH, and Livelihoods and Food Security (LFS) programmes to enable conflict and displacement affected populations to meet their basic needs, enjoy their rights, and benefit from pathways to durable solutions. NRC will deliver pathways back to learning, integration into formal education, acknowledgement of previous learning through supportive policies (accreditation, certification, examinations, and documentation) and expansion of skills for employment. NRC will respond to the diverse problems and needs faced by vulnerable children and youth across Syria through the delivery of its Child Education Pathways (CEP) and Youth Education Pathways (YEP) programmes. Each response modality (Emergency, Transition, and Recovery) is designed to ensure that conflict and displacement-affected children and youth are provided with age and context-specific educational pathways. All three modalities have been designed to provide equal access to and to welcome all out of school children and youth, prioritizing those that have been displaced by the conflict and are returning home from both inside and outside Syria. All three modalities include capacity development opportunities for teachers, trainers, facilitators and coaches and will be implemented in cooperation with NRC’s ICLA/Capacity Building, Shelter, WASH and LFS programmes and partners. The teacher training package has been adapted from the INEE Teachers in Crisis Context and includes NRC’s Better Learning Programme (an evidence-based Psychosocial Support intervention developed by NRC and the University of Tromso). A particular focus is given to a safe return to school after periods of COVID-related lockdowns: teachers circles will integrate the guidance included in UNICEF “Ready to go back: Teacher preparedness Training Package”.

The target group of NRC’s Education Programme in Syria is defined as conflict and displacement-affected children and youth , including Syrian IDPs, IDP and refugee returnees, host community members, Third Country Nationals and Iraqi refugees. Exact target group definitions will vary for the different response options:
•	Emergency Response activities will target newly displaced and returnee children and youth;
•	Transitional Response will target out of school children and youth in contexts of long­ term displacement and prolonged absence from school with activities tailored on their specific context (see more below); 
•	Recovery activities will target vulnerable populations living in post-conflict and/or stabilized camp and non-camp settings (see more below).

Teachers, facilitators and trainers working in NRC programmes in formal and non-formal education settings, as well as vocational trainers will also be targeted across the 3 response options.  Whilst equal access will be provided to both male and female educators, considering the current scarcity of male educators, those present will be actively encouraged to participate, in an effort to provide positive male role models in all activities.
For all NRC Education activities, civil documentation will not be a pre-requisite to receive assistance. Parents engagement is fostered through awareness raising campaigns and the set-up of Parents and Teachers Associations.

project_name: Provision of WASH assistance to vulnerable populations	affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
The purpose of NRC’s WASH intervention is to deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services to most vulnerable people, and provide support to water, sanitation and sewage systems to ensure continuous services for affected people in Syria. NRC will respond to the diverse WASH needs faced by vulnerable populations throughout Syria through the delivery of a multi-faceted WASH response. The different components of NRC’s WASH project for 2022/23 are intended to contribute to the following HRP WASH Sector Objectives 1, 2, and 4.

NRC will deliver this project through a direct implementation modality: geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable conflict and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities and refugee/IDP returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the conflict. All interventions will seek to prioritize the most vulnerable households. Where appropriate, multi-sectoral vulnerability scoring techniques will be used that integrate vulnerability indicators. The needs of the different genders, elderly and persons with disabilities (PWDs) will be considered; during design, implementation and monitoring processes. 

This project includes:
•	Emergency response through the provision of one-off support as part of an integrated, multi-sector response in accordance with the Emergency Preparedness and Response Plans (EPRPs). Comprises of following Result Areas: Temporary WASH services, household assets (Hygiene NFIs), support to Education in Emergencies (WASH Services for Temporary Learning Spaces), hygiene promotion activities
•	The provision of medium-term WASH support at household and settlement-level to populations living in and out-of-camps. Comprises of two result areas: Provision of WASH infrastructure, services and hygiene items in camps and communal shelters.
•	The provision of  support    for long term improvements in  access to water, hygiene and sanitation services at the settlement and household level. Comprises the following result areas: rehabilitation of community WASH infrastructure (boreholes including solar energy systems, water and sewage networks, solid waste management); rehabilitation of WASH facilities in institutions (WASH facilities in schools as a part of joint interventions with Education, WASH in medical centers, etc.); rehabilitation of household WASH facilities (see NRC’s Shelter/NFI project submission). 

Project will include consultation with community through FGDs, HHQs and KIIs as well as with relevant authorities. Special attention will be given to ensuring that interventions are accessible by all and that there are functional complaint and feedback mechanisms (CFM) set in place.
NRC will invest in more sustainable, longer-term and cost-efficient WASH service provision in IDP camps or rehabilitation of WASH infrastructure in in-camp settings, i.e. rehabilitation and construction of water networks and sewer networks, thus this will reduce the WASH needs and cost in 2023 in the targeted locations. NRC will also invest in more sustainable, long term and cost effective provision of WASH services by rehabilitation of the infrastructure and WASH facilities in shelter and community infrastructure. This will minimize need for short term emergency solutions and enable NRC to reduce the needs in the covered locations as well as to focus on other locations that remain in need.

project_name: Improving access to essential health services among vulnerable migrants and host communities in Lebanon
project_objective: This project aims to support vulnerable individuals overcome barriers to accessing healthcare in Lebanon, while supporting Lebanon’s ailing health system against deteriorating economic conditions and against the continued challenges posed by COVID-19 (C19). The project will provide essential health services across the continuum of care either through an implementing partner or in close coordination with partners already providing the services. These include primary healthcare (PHC), advanced diagnostics, secondary and tertiary healthcare. All interventions will be closely coordinated with Ministry of Public Health (MoPH), WHO, health sector and partners. The selection of supported facilities is based on the geographical distribution of migrants and is done in close collaboration with MOPH's PHC department which facilitates support provided to the MoPH, to strengthen PHC facilities. PHC centres providing a range of specialized services will be prioritized. The modalities follow the MoPH's existing support schemes, by providing subsidized consultation fees for healthcare packages. Focus will also be given to providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) as well as reproductive health services to the most vulnerable migrants. Finally, the project will continue supporting the C19 response in complementarity with existing support.  Under the C19 section, IOM will cover the mandatory PCR tests required by various institutions for admission, e.g. in case of surgeries, or admission to mental health facilities, or shelters. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) trainings for all front liners are planned and supported under the C19 response of the Middle East Response (MER) which IOM is the primary recipient of funds. A network of community mobilizers will be engaged in accordance with the sector guidance and equipped with the necessary trainings and materials to deliver quality, integrated health messaging including C19 prevention and vaccination. Communication will be done following different channels and in the different migrant languages. Upon the request of multiple partners and noting that many partners are new to migrant programming; IOM aims to provide a cultural adaptation training. The main objective is to render the services migrant friendly and accessible to this vulnerable group. Building on IOM’s work to assess Points Of Entries’ (POEs) C19 preventive measures, IOM aims to strengthen the C19 preventive measures at 5 POEs: Masnaa, Qaa, Aaboudieh, Aarida, Bokayaa. To be done by strengthening MoPH capacity at POEs with deployment of Port Health Officers, and development and implementation of standard operating procedures and training of trainers for non-health actors.
