project_name: Provision of Emergency Shelter and Non-food Items through integration with Child protection and WASH Interventions to new displacement (conflcits and flooding), Protracted Displacement and Resilience for IDPs, Returnees, vulnerable Host Community and Persons with Disabilities in Fangak, Ayod, Pigi/Canal, Nyirol Counties of Jonglei State and Nasir County of Upper Nile State of South Sudan.
project_objective:
ADA plans to implement a multi-sector intervention, integrating Shelter and Non-Food Items responses with child protection and WASH activities in Ayod, Nyirol, Pigi/Canal and Fangak Counties of Jonglei State, Mayendit county of Unity state and Nasir county of Upper Nile State.

According to the (Humanitarian Needs Overview -HNO, Feb 2022), a deterioration of people’s physical and mental well-being, living standards and coping mechanisms is expected in 2022. Findings from the various data review processes indicate that 8.9 million people are estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance in 2022, compared to 8.3 million in 2021. This increase is largely driven by compounded shocks triggered by continued conflict, widespread flooding, deepening food insecurity, inflation, high food prices, and lack of access to basic services greatly contributed to the increase of needs. Those in need of help are 24% women, 53% children and fifteen percent persons with disability.

2.4 million people are in need of SNFI assistance and services countrywide (HNO 2022 Report). Of this, the SNFI sector target is 1.4 million people. Hence, the most in need are women 24%, girls 26%, boys 27%, men 23% and persons with disabilities 15% people will be targeted by ADA through this plan (HNO 2022 report) to receive the assistance.  According to the inter-sectoral severity of needs analysis, humanitarian needs 
are most concerning in Fangak, Ayod, Pigi/Canal, Nyirol of Jonglei State and Nasir county of upper Nile State. A continuation and increase in sub-national violence and other forms of crises including floods reported in the HNO 2022 will likely continue to disrupt livelihoods and trade and contribute to an increase in humanitarian needs in 2022. Unprecedented continuous flooding impacted children and their caregivers` physical well-being, living standard, and coping mechanisms are expected to further deteriorate in 2022, as a result households’ populations have increased to more than 6 people, creating congestion and overcrowding, exacerbating the spread of COVID-19 among the affected population. Most affected Households lack basic household kits including plastic sheets, rubber robe, mosquito nets, blankets and kitchen sets. 

ADA through this plan, will target to reach 37,500 individuals’ beneficiaries with in-kind SNFI assistance- 32000 individuals new displacement (conflict and flooding-85%); 5500 individuals Protracted Displacement-15%; SNFI target per location: Ayod – 11,250 individuals; Fangak – 13,125 individuals; Nyirol – 3,750 individuals; Pigi/Canal -3,750 individuals; Nasir -5,625 individuals.

The proposed interventions will be integrated with child protection and WASH responses in Fangak, Ayod, Pigi/canal, Nyirol and Nasir counties. Housing, Land and Property (HLP) mainstreaming. The project will target elderly persons 5% (1,875 individuals) living in crowded communal shelters to de-congest them through the distribution of plastic sheets, rubber rope, blanket and mosquito nets to reduce transmission of Covid-19. In line with SNFI cluster best practices, ADA will mainstream its responses through implementing AAP (Accountability to Affected Populations), HLP assessments, and safety audits activities during the four (stages) of SNFI response methodology, i.e. Needs assessment, Registration and verification of needs; Distribution of supplies and post distribution monitoring. In Ayod, Pigi, Fangak, Nyirol and Nasir contexts, unexploded ordinance (UXOS) and landmines issues or presences will be highlighted through awareness sessions especially during community sensitization and mobilizations meetings. An inter-sectoral referral system will be established to strengthen the SNFI synergies with others sectors like WASH, Child Protection.

project_name: Provision of food assistance to conflict affected IDPs and Host Communities in Fangak, Ayod, Pigi and  Nasir Counties
project_objective: This project targets 43,000 vulnerable beneficiaries in four counties identified to have been severely affected by lack of food that was worsened by natural disasters and human conflicts. The livelihood activities were interrupted by flood which destroyed crops and vegetables,  resulting into death of animals, spread of waterborne diseases and has left many people especially women, children, elderly persons and people with disabilities more vulnerable. Cultivation of crops and vegetables have failed due to the massive floods, as arable land was claimed by water. Lack of fishing gears denied the people from getting food from the nearby rivers and swamps. Relief food from WFP remains inadequate to meet their humanitarian needs. As the result, the harvest was insufficient and far lower to meet the consumption and dietary needs of the people. Inter-communal conflicts also exposed the people to protection risks and varying levels of vulnerability. IDPs, host communities and returnees are in dire need of food assistance and protection. The purpose of this project is four-fold: (a) to provide food assistance through provision of cash transfers and vouchers to 2,150 vulnerable households, (b) to provide agricultural inputs to 8,600 households, (c) to enhance the capacity of 1,000 farmers , (d) establishment of eight (8) nutrition gardens and (e) to provide vaccination and treatment services to 8,000 livestock. . In response to climate change, the project will incorporate climate smart agriculture techniques so that an environmental protection is factored in it. Safety and gender based violence will be mainstreamed in the implementation of of the project. The intervention will require USD 675,000 for one year

project_name: Provision of immediate emergency life-saving WASH response through linkages with GVB/Protection, Nutrition, Health and  to vulnerable IDPs, host communities, returnees, people with disabilities, women, girls, boys and men affected by natural disasters and human conflicts in Ayod,  Fangak, Pigi/Canal and Nyirol (of Jonglei State), Nasir (of Unity State) and Nasir (of Upper Nile State, South Sudan.
project_objective:
The latest South Sudan Humanitarian Need Overview (February 2022 UNOCHA report) revealed that more than 8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance, while WASH Cluster estimates 6.1 million to be in need of  immediate life-saving WASH interventions.  The situation is further worsened by continued violence, climatic shocks, coupled with the effect of COVID 19 and menacing floods resulting in worsening of community WASH infrastructure, nutrition, health and protection/SGBV concerns amongst women and girls.

Africa Development Aid anticipates that, if supported, it will ensure 34540 vulnerable population experiencing multi-sectoral severity levels 3 and 4 targeted by this response will have reduced mobility and mortality through integrated WASH, Nutrition, Health and Shelter/NFI essential services to meet their needs.  It is expected to cost $750,000 in one year. The six counties (Ayod,  Fangak, Pigi/Canal and Nyirol (of Jonglei State), Nasir (of Unity State) and Nasir (of Upper Nile State) have remained consistently with low level of WASH coverage, leaving vulnerable communities without resilience to withstand the chronic and acute crisis that has engulfed the county.  Access to safe drinking-water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services is a fundamental element of healthy communities and has an important positive impact on nutrition. This proposed intervention will provide an overview of the evidence of nutrition and health gains that can be achieved with integrated nutrition, health and SGBV a description of key WASH practices, and practical knowledge.

Poor access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), whilst not the root cause of violence, can exacerbate the vulnerability of women and girls to violence. Men and boys, people of other gender or sexual identities or other marginalized groups can also sometimes be at risk. Vulnerability to violence can have a significant impact on people’s access to adequate water and sanitation and hygiene.

The proposed intervention will be to reduce morbidity and mortality among children through integration with nutrition, protection/GBV and health by providing access to safe water, rehabilitation of water points  and water treatment at nutrition facilities as well as communities and promote hygiene promotion /campaigns.
Nutrition facilities will be provided with WASH/NFI kits/minimum WASH packages to care takers of children admitted and screened with SAM/MAM at functional OTP and training on the use of the items/kits.

The continued conflicts has resulted in devastation of WASH infrastructure largely contributing not only to disease outbreak, but also to increased malnutrition, public health risks and increased gender-based violence among women and girls and other vulnerable groups.
WASH,-Nutrition, health and GBV integrated programming will aim at areas of high level of malnutrition, by targeting of SAM children and their families. These areas will further converge with other Health-related priorities, acknowledging that poor WASH services are a key driver to poor health
These proposed counties already experienced high food insecurity and malnutrition (GAM rates have also heightened WASH needs. Women and girls are the primary direct users of WASH services and GBV risks have significant implications for the success of WASH interventions.  ADA will ensure GBV risk mitigation is a priority area of focus.

ADA WASH will ensure delivery of specific activities such as gender segregated latrines that meet the needs of women, children and people with disabilities.  Consultations by conducting safety audit will be conducted at site level to identify Gender based violence concerns and implement measures. ADA will focus on emergency hygiene promotion targeting community level.  Emphasize will be made on disease prevention such COVID 19 and WASH related illnesses and hand washing with soap.

project_name: Provision of quality Protection services to disasters affected children and their parents facing trauma in Ayod, Pigi, Fangak, Nyirol and Maiwut Counties of Upper Nile and Jonglei States.
project_objective:
Africa Development Aid intends to provide quality protection services to crisis-affected children and their caregivers in Ayod, Pigi, Nyirol and Fangak Counties of Jonglei State, Maiwut county of Upper Nile State. This project will seek to provide an immediate lifesaving response to the vulnerable crisis and flood-affected children from returnees, IDPs, and host communities through strengthened comprehensive case management including family tracing & reunification; referral for services; provision of critical age and gender appropriate psycho social support services including parental skills sessions in a timely, holistic and child-friendly manner as well as to the traumatized adult caregivers whose children are also facing trauma, coordination monitoring and assessments of child protection related risk. The projects will also conduct awareness-raising activities on prevention of family separation, COVID-19 prevention, and response while putting into practice the COVID-19 preventive measures. ADA is having active Child protection activities in  Canal/Pigi, Ayod and Fangak Counties. However, under this project ADA will provide static and mobile critical age and gender appropriate psycho social support services in individual and group sessions including Psycho social support to caregivers of children who are traumatized and undergoing PSS activities, identification, registration, interim care, family tracing & reunification to unaccompanied and separated children, advocate for GBV related risk prevention including early marriage, Sexual abuse, exploitation and violence, referral to other services such as health, education, nutrition, shelter and NFIs among others to those at risk and other vulnerable children including those facing other forms of violence, orphans as well as Justice for children (J4C) in a timely, holistic and child-friendly manner and also promote resilience to the traumatized ones.
The project will also seek to enhance the protection environment of vulnerable crisis-affected girls, boys, and youths to enable durable solutions through the establishment of community-based child protection networks, foster family groups, youth/adolescent clubs, Child-Friendly Spaces, child rights clubs, and recreational centres while observing COVID-19 guidelines. This will create enabling conditions for the realization of solutions and prevention of further displacement which leads to family separations; identification of risks, dangers, and impediments; advocacy and mitigation measures, psycho social support, peaceful co-existence initiatives, and resilience.
In Ayod County, the project will cover the following payams, e.g.,Pajiek, Wau Menime, Haat and Kuach-deng payams, Ayod, Pagil, Paguong and Mogok, ADA will also target Atar, Kurwai, Wulieth, kaldak and Khorfulus payams of Pigi County . In Fangak County, the project will concentrate in Mareang, Keew, Paguir, Toch and Manajang (Juaibor), Barboi, New Fangak and Old Fangak Payams. Meanwhile, since there was no Funded Partner for Child protection activities in Nyirol County in 2021, Identified gaps have been noted in Lankien, Tut, Pultruk, Waat, Nyanbor, Chuil, Pading and Keeth payams. ADA will also response in Mawuit County targeting all its payams namely; Jotoma, Kigila, Mawuit, Jekow and Olang.
A total of 25,000 people (12,500 Males and 12,500 females) will benefit from this project. Out of this, 15,000 will be children (7,500 girls; 7,500 boys) and 10,000 will be adults – 5,000 males and 5,000 females. However, out of the total beneficiaries 30% will be from the host community while 10% will be from Returnees and 60% from IDPs.

project_name: Provision of inclusive education to affected children of IDPs, Returnees and Host communities in Nasir and Maiwut Counties of Upper Nile state and Fangak and Ayod Counties of Jonglei state.
project_objective:
The project is in line with HRP 2022 objective 1 and 2 and also with cluster/sector specific objectives 1, 2 & 3, Besides, it aligns with the cluster strategy to ‘Ensure safe, equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services to enable populations meet their basic needs in locations of severity level 4 and 5’ have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral essential services to meet their needs.
This project will improve access to safe, quality and inclusive protective education services to 5, 284 emergency affected IDPs, returnees, spontaneous refugees, and host communities’ children in Fangak, Ayod, Maiwut and Nasir Counties by 2022. The integrated education project by ADA in hard-to-reach areas aims to ensure that children (boys and girls) have access to quality and inclusive education and those already in schools are retained in Maiwut and Nasir Counties (Upper Nile State), Fangak and Ayod Counties (Jonglei State). The following interventions are envisaged: establishing safe learning and recreational facilities in 12 locations – 3 in each County; teacher training to enhance the teaching/learning function supported in schools; providing monthly stipends to 84 volunteer teachers - 21 teachers per County; campaign for education, encouraging children, especially girls and people with disability to return to school; and provision of school feeding programs to enhance attendance and retention of children at schools. Response priorities will include gender-segregated WASH facilities with much concentration in COVID-19 prevention measures, inclusion of GBV counselling rooms in the schools, provision of learning, teaching and WASH materials, capacity building of School Management Committees (SMCs) and Parents Teachers Associations (PTAs), life-skills and recreational opportunities to support the recovery of children and to promote their overall well-being. Equal access to inclusive education will be prioritized regardless of gender, disability or ethnic background. Through introduction of school gender-sensitive WASH programme, this project will have established strong WASH facilities in schools. The project will seek to support prevention of COVID-19 through rehabilitation/construction of hand-washing facilities and latrines, provision of soap, face masks, sensitizers and maintenance of social distancing. Carry out messaging on coronavirus signs and symptoms, modes of transmission and prevention to children and their parents.
The project will seek to address one of the top causes of school drop-outs (School feeding) that will help increase and maintain school enrolment and attendance, and reduce risks of death, disease and cognitive underdevelopment. School feeding will also improve protection of- in-school and out of school children by keeping them away from potential recruitment into armed groups, child labor, early marriage, exploitation, sexual violence and abduction while on their way to schools and back home. This will help to reduce morbidity and absenteeism, support retention in schools and children to help sensitize their communities. Crisis-affected children will be engaged in basic education and recreational activities in order to create an enabling environment for their critical development and positive engagement with the community. Youths will catch up on primary education through accelerated learning programmes (ALP) to improve their literacy and numeracy, technical and vocational training, and life skills. The project will seek to include physically and mentally challenged children; girls and boys vulnerable to recruitment into armed groups, and child labour; youths; adolescent heads of households; young mothers; and children from different ethnic groups. Teachers, SMCs and PTAs will be trained on life skills and referral pathways to enhance the protective aspect of education in emergency (EiE) intervention.

project_name: Provision of essential primary health care services to affected population in Fangak, Canal/Pigi, in Jonglei state and Leer, Rubkona and Guit Counties of Unity state. Targetting 100,000 vulnerable population.
project_objective: This project will support flood & food insecure affected 100,000 beneficiaries (Men 15,000, Women 25,000, Boys 27,000 and Girls 33,000) in Jonglei state counties (Fangak, Canal/Pigi) and Unity state Counties (Leer, Rubkona and Guit) with improved essential healthcare services. HFO will under take responsibility to implement PHC services activities to achieve health cluster and Ministry of health sectoral objectives. The response will focus on providing basic essential health services in line with national and international humanitarian standards and is based on the epidemiological evidence of disease outbreaks, disease burden seasonality and trauma-related emergency issues. Prevention, preparedness, response readiness and mitigation activities will be supported with special attention given to providing vulnerable groups including women, children and person with disabilities. HFO in collaboration with the Cluster at the national, state Ministry of Health, County health departments and other implementing partners will support different intervention modalities suited to the needs of affected people, including the COVID-19 appropriate interventions. HFO and its health staff will continue prevention, preparedness and response readiness activities addressing Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Bentiu. HFO will link static with mobile health facilities and community-based healthcare systems (Boma health initiatives) to serve communities who do not have access to health care facilities (>5KM) as part humanitarian development Nexus (HND) during e,mergency that can wider coverage in Fangak County. HFO plans to further strengthen health technical staff, capacity and field coordination support to CHD, Boma health workers. HFO as a developmental partners will collaborating with development partners HPF and UNICEF partners who are providing regular health services through static health facilities in crisis affected areas by identifying communities that are still not reachable and providing services through 2 MTs in each county as well as strengthening 2 PHCUs/county and 1 PHCC in Fangak with improved access to essential health services will contribute to the overall reduction of the high maternal mortality rates and under-five mortality rates in women and children and mitigate the transmission of vaccine-preventable and other infectious diseases. HFO will involve affected communities and regular national, state and county health promotion, prevention, and control programs led by county health system in the planning and organizing of emergency health services. Our coordination mechanism at the national, state and County levels will be utilized to coordinate, collaborate, liaise with partners and authorities to implement, monitor and review the response activities. Mnanagement of SGBV as part of CMR and Referral pathways for mental health and SGBV survivors for psychosocial support. Maternal Neonatal and child health emergencies will be streamlined and strengthened. Referral pathways will link the community and facility-based health care system to provide continuity of care such as BHIs lingkage and engagement. HFO will encourage and support infection prevention and control (IPC) and WASH in health facilities including COVID-19 appropriate preventive measures. COVID-19 is expected to continue impact health services in the country for the foreseeable future. Frontline partners coordination mechanism at all levels will work towards comprehensive integration and collaboration with  FSL, Nutrition, Protection and WASH partners on grounds. HFO targeted populations is informed by the intersectoral prioritization information analyzed, the health sectoral severity analysis and a review of disease infection risk by county. We will monitor and evaluate all these actvities through IDSR, 5Ws and DHIS2 to CHD, Cluster, WHO and MoH. HFO gets IEHK from WHO, MoH, CHD and PPE from IOM and WFP to support the response.

project_name: Réponse d’urgence en Eau, Hygiène et d’Assainissement tout en assurant une transition vers des solutions plus durables dans les communes d’accueil des déplacés des régions du Nord, du centre-nord et de l’Est
project_objective:
Le présent projet est un ensemble des projets planifiés et projets acquis pour 2022. Il a pour objectif global la promotion d’un accès équitable et durable aux services d’Eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement des populations rurales, en respectant les normes humanitaires au Burkina Faso et en tachant de combler les lacunes au niveau des communautés d’accueil des personnes déplacées internes dans les régions du Nord et du Centre Nord et de l’est. En soutenant une transition vers des solutions plus durables, le projet s’orientera sur trois axes principaux à savoir :  i) l’accès à l’eau potable, à l’hygiène et l’assainissement, ii) le renforcement de la gouvernance et la cohésion sociale et iii) la création d’emplois et de revenus de la filière hygiène et assainissement.
Le projet se focalisera dans les zones hôtes, où la concurrence autour de l’accès aux services sociaux de base est aggravée par de fortes concentrations de population, mettant souvent en péril l’organisation sociale, la cohésion, les services de base et la durabilité des infrastructures.
Pour sa mise en œuvre, trois approches sont préconisées : i) les approches ATPC au niveau communautaire pour l’auto construction des latrines familiales, ii) WASH FIT dans les établissements de santé et iii) ECOLE BLEUE dans les établissements scolaires.

Depuis son implantation au Burkina en 2019, ACTED a fait des secteurs de l’EHA et Abri sa spécialité dans les régions du Nord, du centre nord et dans la région de l’est depuis 2020. Le présent projet vise un accès à l’Eau, à l’assainissement, à la promotion des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène, mais aussi, l’appropriation des actions du projet par les communautés elles-mêmes. La promotion de l’égalité de genre sera commune à toutes les activités mises en œuvre par le projet. Les zones ciblées étant particulièrement vulnérables au changement climatique, l’ensemble des interventions envisagées prendront en considération leur impact environnemental et l’adaptation des populations aux nouvelles conditions climatiques (transitions vers des solutions plus durables). Ceci inclura notamment : la prise en compte de l’impact environnemental de toute construction envisagée (utilisation de matériaux locaux comme le sable, le gravier, les moellons nécessitant peu d’énergies, adaptés aux conditions climatiques, etc.), l’intégration d’une section sur le changement climatique dans toutes les formations et sensibilisations qui seront menées, que ce soit au niveau communautaire ou institutionnel.
La planification détaillée des interventions et le suivi du projet se fera en coordination avec les autorités locales (DREA, action sociale, mairies) et les services déconcentrés en assainissement et santé. 

Ces activités sont par ailleurs complémentaires des autres projets d'ACTED dans les domaines de la gestion des sites d'accueil temporaires, de la sécurité alimentaire et des abris/AME qui apportent une assistance aux personnes déplacées internes et aux communautés hôtes

project_name: Protection et soins améliorés pour les garçons et les filles déplacés de moins de 18 ans dans les régions du Nord et du Sahel au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Depuis 2015, le Burkina Faso est confronté à un climat d’insécurité, traduit par des pertes en vies humaines, de déplacements internes, les attaques et affrontements armés répétés dans certaines régions du Burkina Faso ont conduit une partie non négligeable de la population à fuir leur localité. Alors que 38 000 burkinabè ont été contraints de se réfugier dans les pays voisins, selon les données statistique CONASUR au 30 septembre 2021, 1 407 685 est le nombre de personnes déplacées internes (PDI) dans le pays dont 618 301 enfants de 5ans et plus.  Sur le nombre total de déplacés en septembre 2021 les deux régions concernées ont accueillies 621 870 déplacés dont 493 708 au Sahel et 128 162 au Nord.  264 521 de 621 870 sont des enfants de 5ans et plus.  À la suite des incidents sécuritaires, ces PDIs cherchent majoritairement à trouver refuge dans les centres urbains les plus proches. Leurs conditions de vie, déjà précaires, dégradent d’autant plus aux sentiments de discriminations auxquelles elles font face de la part des populations hôtes.
IRC à travers ce projet va apporter une réponse intégrée pour la protection des enfants dans les régions du Nord et du Sahel.  Les réponses seront apportées aux besoins identifiés à travers l’interaction de l’IRC avec les communautés dans les zones d’intervention en général et il s’inspire aussi et surtout des différentes évaluations rapides conduites par les autres acteurs humanitaires et les données du CONASUR sur les déplacées internes.   Tout au long de ce projet l’IRC conduira des évaluations sur une base régulière pour informer d’une manière continuelle la réponse et s’assurer que les services fournis répondent aux besoins réels des populations affectes. Ainsi, la réponse offrira la protection aux enfants affectés par le conflit en leur apportant une assistance psychosociale et en les réintégrant dans la vie socioéconomique et scolaire. L’IRC assurera que tout enfant victime d’abus ou exploitations puisse accéder aux services de qualité. Un accent sera mis sur la coordination pour s’assurer que des mécanismes de référencement sont fonctionnels entre les acteurs, et dans le respect des principes directeurs. Vu les risques élevés, l’IRC va également renforcer les efforts de réduction des risques à travers le renforcement des mécanismes communautaire de prévention des cas d’abus sont protégés contre la violence à la maison et dans la communauté.

project_name: Réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité liées à la malnutrition dans les régions du Sahel et du Nord du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Les régions du Sahel et du Nord connaissent depuis 2016 des violences armées avec des exactions sur la population. Cette spirale de violence s’est exacerbée depuis 2018. Ce qui a entrainé des déplacements massifs sans cesse croissants des populations dans le pays. Le CONASUR  estime à 1481701 le nombre de PDIs à travers le pays en Octobre 2021. Les régions les plus touchées sont celles du Sahel, Nord, Centre Nord, Est et Boucle du Mouhoun mais depuis quelques mois, les PDIs sont enregistrés dans l’ensemble du territoire national. La région du Sahel enregistre 510279 PDIs soit environ 34% des PDIs du pays, suivi de celle du Centre Nord (510110 PDIs). Dans ces régions, les mouvements des populations compliquent l’accès des populations aux soins de santé, aux ressources clés telles que l’eau et les denrées alimentaires. Cette crise touche de plein fouet le système de santé avec des centres de santé fermés ou fonctionnant à minima, rendant difficile l’accès des populations aux soins de santé et le dépistage et prise en charge de la malnutrition. En Novembre 2021, 48 formations sanitaires étaient fermées dans la région du Sahel sur 89 structures fermées dans le pays. Dans la région du Nord, 7 FS étaient fermées et majoritairement dans le DS de Titao. La situation sécuritaire et humanitaire s’est dégradée à Titao à la suite d’une vague de violence enregistrée entre au cours du dernier trimestre de 2021. L’enquête SMART de 2020 a révélé des prévalences MAG de 15,1% (IC : 11,7% - 19,3%) dans la région du Sahel et 8,2% (IC : 6,1% - 10,4%) dans la région du Nord. Les prévisions du cadre harmonisé placent la plupart des provinces du Sahel et du Nord en phase 3 et plus. 
Le Burkina Faso a enregistré en Mars 2020 ses premiers cas de COVID 19. La pandémie a touché à la date du 25 Novembre plus de 15000 personnes causant la mort de plus de 280 personnes.
Plusieurs ONG apportent une assistance humanitaire dans ces régions notamment la Croix Rouge Belge et Médecins du Monde France dans le DS de Djibo ainsi que MSF France à Titao pour une réponse nutritionnelle. Cependant en raison de l’inaccessibilité de certaines zones, il existe des poches où les besoins ne sont pas couverts.
IRC qui intervient déjà dans ces zones avec des activités de santé communautaires est à la recherche de fonds pour compléter son action et offrir des soins holistiques aux enfants de moins de 5 ans et aux femmes enceintes et allaitantes.
IRC propose cette intervention pour i) renforcer la prévention de la sous nutrition parmi les populations cibles ii) renforcer le dépistage et la surveillance nutritionnelle dans les zones en insécurité, iii) garantir l’accès aux soins nutritionnels pour les enfants de moins de 5 ans et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes y compris par l’approche simplifiée et communautaire.

project_name: Assistance sanitaire aux personnes vulnérables dans les zones en situation d’urgence au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise humanitaire que traverse le Burkina Faso depuis 2016 a connu une intensification progressive depuis 2019. Face à cette insécurité croissante, 6 régions ont été classées en urgence : l’Est, le Sahel, la Boucle du Mouhoun, le Nord, le Centre Nord et le Centre-Est. A la date du 31 Octobre 2021, le CONASUR estimait à 1 481701 le nombre de personnes déplacées internes dans le pays dont 333,244 femmes et 255,139 sont des enfants de moins de 5 ans. Les zones de concentration de ces déplacées sont principalement le Sahel et le Centre Nord. La commune de Djibo est celle qui rassemble le plus grand nombre de PDI (262,637 individus). Cette crise est caractérisée par une atteinte significative des moyens d’existence pour les populations sinistrées avec une exacerbation de la pauvreté et une limitation de l’accès aux services sociaux de base notamment la santé et l’éducation. Dans ces régions, le niveau de couverture de ces services était déjà problématique avant la crise. En octobre 2021, le cluster santé estimait à 86 le nombre de formations sanitaires fermées dans les régions en urgence et 306 fonctionnant à minima. Les districts les plus affectés par les fermetures des centres de santé restent Djibo (28 FS fermées), Gorom-Gorom (09 FS fermées) et Titao (07 FS fermées). Les fermetures des FS dans le pays affectent l’accès aux soins pour plus de 2 millions d’individus selon le cluster Santé. La plupart des évaluations conduites dans le cadre du RRM auprès des personnes affectées précisent les problèmes de santé en termes de faible accès aux soins de santé primaires, faible accès aux soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive, une atteinte psychologique des proches des victimes, une persistance de la malnutrition avec un faible accès à la prise en charge nutritionnelle. La crise humanitaire a été aggravée à partir de mars 2020 avec l’apparition des premiers cas de COVID 19. Cette pandémie a éprouvé le système de santé dans son ensemble avec une atteinte à sa capacité d’offre de soins. En 2021, malgré la disponibilité du vaccin, les rumeurs et réticences entravent l’adhésion des populations. ET même si la pandémie cause moins de psychose au sein des populations, le taux de létalité dans le pays atteint un niveau de plus en plus alarmant. 
Dans la plupart des zones en urgence, plusieurs organisations humanitaires apportent une assistance, mais les besoins sont loin d’être couverts. IRC intervient dans plusieurs de ces localités dont Djibo dans la région du Sahel, Nouna dans la Boucle du Mouhoun et dans les DS de Yako, Gourcy, Titao et Ouahigouya dans la région du Nord. Les activités mises en œuvre couvrent les soins de santé primaires, le renforcement de la santé communautaire, l’amélioration de la qualité des soins en SR et la prévention de la COVID 19.
IRC compte poursuivre ses interventions dans ces zones et les renforcer au cours des prochains mois. Le programme proposé ici vise plusieurs résultats afin d’apporter une assistance de qualité aux populations déplacées et hôtes de ces zones en urgence à savoir i) le renforcement de la qualité des soins de santé au niveau communautaire, ii) le renforcement de l’accès et de la qualité des soins préventifs, curatifs et promotionnels en santé de reproduction, iii) le renforcement de l’accès des populations sinistrées à la santé mentale et iv) le renforcement de la prévention de la pandémie de la COVID 19.
Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ces activités, IRC se mettra en partenariat avec des ONG et associations nationales en vue d’accroitre l’accès aux zones difficiles et de renforcer les capacités du partenaire local. IRC dispose d’ne liste de potentiels partenaires de mise en œuvre. La sélection finale interviendra au moment de la programmation et cela prendra en compte la zone d’intervention de ces partenaires, leurs capacités et ressources disponibles

project_name: Apporter une réponse d’urgence aux besoins en eau, assainissement et hygiène aux personnes déplacées interne et les populations hôtes affectés par les crises dans les régions du Sahel, Nord et Est.
project_objective:
Le projet proposé vise à fournir une réponse d'urgence WASH aux besoins des personnes déplacées résidant dans les communes de Dori, Gorom-Gorom, Gorgadji, Deou, Titao, Banh, Seguenega, Ouindigui, Bilanga, Coalla, Bogande et Piela ainsi que les populations hôtes de ces communes. Le nombre de bénéficiaires de ce projet est estimé à 100 382 personnes dont 75 287 PDI (75%) et 25 095 hôtes (25%). 

La mise en œuvre du projet prendra en compte les aspects de genre et redevabilité de manière à assurer un accès équitable et sécurisé des infrastructures d’eau et d’assainissement au profit des bénéficiaires. Il faut noter que ce projet prendra également en compte l'approche cash transfert ou de l’approche coupons (selon le contexte). 

Sur le terrain, un suivi de contrôle de la qualité des ouvrages à construire ou réhabiliter sera assuré conjointement avec les services directions régionales ou provinciales de l’eau et l’assainissement. Les activités de ciblage des bénéficiaires des kits WASH se feront en collaboration avec les directions régionales ou provinciales de l’action sociale et les différentes structures communautaires qui seront mise en place à cet effet. Les activités de sensibilisation sur les bonnes pratiques de l’hygiène se feront avec l’appui des relais communautaires qui seront formés et équipés pour conduire ces activités. Une enquête PDM sera faite au moins deux semaines après la distribution de kits d’hygiène et un mois après la distribution de kits de dignité.
En vue d'assurer la durabilité/pérennisation des infrastructures WASH, IRC se propose d'impliquer fortement les communes dans la gestion des AEPS et PEA et les Associations d’Usagers d’Eau (AUE) pour les PMH. IRC prévoit également des mises en place/ renforcement de capacité / recyclage des AUE (pour l'accès durable aux infrastructures) en accord avec la DPEA et les communes concernées.

Le projet reflète la planification des interventions WASH de IRC, pour tous projets confondus, comprenant les projets en quête de financement pour 2022.

project_name: Réponse intégrée en eau, hygiène, assainissement, santé et nutrition (Wash In Nut et Wash Mouvements de population) aux populations touchées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad.
project_objective:
Le présent projet va contribuer à améliorer l’accès équitable aux services essentiels en eau-hygiène-assainissement, l’appui aux structures sanitaires dans le cadre de la prise en charge de la malnutrition et accompagnées avec les actions de protection transversale pour 57 317 000 (21 825 femmes, 19165 hommes, 8883 filles et 7444 garçons) déplacées et hôtes en situation vulnérable dans les départements de Fouli et Kaya de la province du Lac Tchad.
Oxfam applique une approche d’intégration transversale du genre et de la protection dans ses stratégies d'intervention, comme établi dans ses Normes minimales en matière de Genre en contexte d’urgence  et dans la stratégie globale du programme au Tchad. Son approche de programmation sûre (safe programming) est intégrée dans toutes ses activités, avec une analyse des risques préalable à toute mise en œuvre et les moyens de les atténuer (par ex. la sensibilisation sur le partage des ressources au sein du ménage). De plus, les principes d’Oxfam en matière de prévention des inconduites sexuelles (safeguarding)  sont pris en compte dans tous les projets et programmes, avec des formations périodiques du personnel ainsi que la transmission de messages et d‘information sur les mécanismes de plainte aux participants et communautés.
L’implication des communautés affectées est un élément central de la stratégie d'Oxfam pour assurer la réussite et la pérennité de l’intervention. Ainsi, durant la phase de conception de l’intervention, les bénéficiaires sont consultés au moyen de groupes focalisés et d’entretiens avec des informateurs clés (représentants de villages et des PDI, autorités locales, femmes, personnes à besoins spécifiques, etc.). 
Durant l'exécution de l'action, les communautés seront impliquées et responsabilisées en plusieurs occasions: 
•	Participation à l'établissement des listes de bénéficiaires en fonction de critères de vulnérabilité acceptés de tous; 
•	Implication dans le choix des emplacements et de l’architecture des installations d’eau et d’assainissement (surtout des femmes & filles, pour tenir compte de leurs besoins spécifiques et assurer leur dignité et sécurité);
•	Groupes communautaires (comités mixtes de ciblage, de plaintes, de gestion des points d’eau, de protection) mis en place, renforcés et impliqués dans les activités du projet; idem pour les artisans réparateurs, formés et équipés pour répondre aux besoins de maintenance; 
•	Accompagnement et renforcement de capacité des structures communautaires (Clubs mamans) pour la prévention de la malnutrition. 
La participation spécifique des femmes dans le projet fera l’objet d’une attention particulière et permettra de soutenir leur agentivité. Par leur participation dans des consultations en groupe, elles joueront un rôle important dans l´adaptation des activités à leurs contraintes et besoins spécifiques (distributions de trousses d’hygiène féminine et “kits bébés”, sensibilisation à l´hygiène, construction des latrines familiales, salles de soins 100% féminines, etc.). Les activités dans le volet de Protection viseront le renforcement des capacités et habilités en leadership des femmes pour assurer une participation égalitaire dans les prises de décision, surtout dans le domaine de la santé (spécialement la santé sexuelle et reproductive). Meetings and raising awareness sessions on reproduction and family planning will be organized for various target groups with special focus on male and female adolescents, men and women. ; Thirdly, Communication; Accountability and Advocacy using broadcast/ social media platforms;

project_name: Improving the shelters conditions of the most vulnerable population in IDP sites, damaged/unfinished buildings in addition to providing NFI assistance in Idleb and Aleppo governorates
project_objective:
This project is to responds to the need for humanitarian life-saving shelter and NFI assistance to IDPs and host community HHs in sub-districts in Aleppo and Idleb governorates targeting 22,000 HHs (110,000 individuals)
Through:
*Rehabilitation for 250 unfinished buildings (4 rooms in each, for 4 HHs) with value 3000$ (750$ for each room), totaling, they will be hosted by 1000 IDP HHs (5000 individuals).
*Provide NFI assistance (Winter Labelled CASH) with the value of 150$, in one go in Dec, as SNFI Cluster Guidance to 8000HHs (40000 individuals).
*Flood Response (activities include tents winterization, insulation, leveling, graveling pathways, and culverts construction) (over 150 camps), targeting 10000HHs (50000 Individuals) to ensure safety, flood protection, and dignified living conditions
*Provide shelter repair valued at the average of $600 for 3000 HHs (15000 individuals)
Assistance is determined as technical assessment of each house/unfinished building, and camp needs, and BINAA will follow SNFI Cluster Guidance to ensure the scope of work that ensures the standards, dignity, privacy, and protection
The project will be in Idlib and Aleppo covering sub-districts where most vulnerable persons are sheltered in damaged/unfished buildings, IDP sites, and individual houses.
The project is 24 months, from Jan-22 to Dec-23
Shelter repair beneficiaries will be IDP and HC HHs living in an inadequate shelter that does not meet minimum SPHERE minimum standards for square meters of covered living space per person and has inadequate privacy or protection from the elements, settlement planning, and WASH facilities. Targeting houses that have light to medium damage but remain structurally sound. Works include doors and windows repair or replacement, partition installation, sealing cracks and holes in walls, and WASH facilities repairs. The works will ensure increased privacy between males and females, host and hosted families that enhance gender-sensitive response.
Furthermore, for HHs with PwDs, BINAA will follow Washington Tool, additional works will be included to respond to PwDs' needs including disability-friendly entrance and toilet facilities (e.g., a ramp with a handrail for using wheelchairs at the building entrance and seating provisions for toilets)
The rehabilitation varies as the number of rooms in each unfinished building, installation of masonry partitions, repair of WASH facilities within the building. To enhance gender-sensitive response, necessary adaptations that particularly affect women and girls will include appropriate lighting, separate toilets and showers for men and women, accessible facilities for people with disabilities (disability friendly entrance and toilet facilities), areas for bathing, washing of clothing, and partitions to create spaces for different households and additional partitions within households to create privacy for men and women
The minimum standards are derived from Sphere Project standards and indicators, agreed by operational Shelter Actors specifically for the programmatic context in NW Syria so that beneficiaries live in safety with dignity. Using these standards will enable BINAA to achieve the agreed project objective consistently, accountable, and equitably and help to avoid diversion and duplication of aid
BINAA will follow the Cluster guidelines on Shelter repair and rehabilitation
BINAA staff have strong communication skills and a clear understanding of the humanitarian principles to enable a dialogue with communities and avoid potential tension and conflict and will work on the beneficiary selection. BINAA will ensure that these staff had received PSEA training and work closely with the Protection team to identify possible protection concerns
BINAA team is well experienced in delivering both shelter rehabilitation and cash assistance with solid program management. The experience is gained, and lessons are learned to improve the implementation of future programs.

project_name: Strengthening resilience of vulnerable households and communities through agricultural and livestock related income generating activities in Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to strengthen the resilience and coping capacities of vulnerable mobile populations, including Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees and their host community to address food insecurity and enhance livelihood security. This will be achieved through delivering agricultural and livestock related income generating activities with special attention to small-scale farmers, IDPs, returnees and other vulnerable groups such as youths and women. IOM will apply a community centered approach to promote community initiatives to assist durable solutions and ensure that planned interventions are met, based on needs and the rights of the vulnerable migrants and community, to access improved economic opportunities. 

The project will focus on 14 localities: Wad Al Mahi locality (Blue Nile), Yassin locality (East Darfur), Al Fao and Galabat Ash-Shargiah localities (Gedaref), Reifi Khashm Elgirba (Kassala), El fasher and Tawilla localities (North Darfur), Buram, Rehaid Albirdi, Tulus and Um Dafoug localities (South Darfur), Delami locality (South Kordogan), Jebel Moon and Sirba localities (West Darfur). Returnees, IDPs and local communities in these localities are vulnerable to food insecurity and limited livelihood opportunities due to limited purchasing power resulting from inflation and high staple food prices. According to HNO data in 2021, the selected localities have been suffering from the high prevalence in Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) phase 3 (Crisis) and/or phase 4 (Emergency) further highlighting the need for timely and adequate livelihood interventions to address food insecurity, strengthen community resilience to protect lives, and move towards economic self-sufficiency.

Under the HRP 2022, The response plans under the project are in line with FSL Cluster Objective 2: Support self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives; and objective 3: Improve communities' capacity to sustain households’ livelihoods through the rehabilitation and building of productive infrastructure as well as supporting services. The planned interventions will include: (1) provision of agricultural support to the most vulnerable farmers with capacity training for local production cooperatives and inputs on agriculture employing climate adaptation techniques; (2) support sustainable livestock husbandry practice and veterinary services to assist household asset building; (3) small business support for youth and women on agriculture and other livelihood skills such as food processing, brick making, welding activities to enhance community resilience and reinvigorate local economies through the creation of small businesses. 

IOM has already established a good access to most of target localities, and seeks to continue implementing community stabilization and durable solution initiative activities under UNDAF outcomes. 
The planned interventions will be delivered in a way to complement past and on-going activities implemented, thereby strengthening links between the HRP Outcomes and UNDAF Outcomes.

project_name: Providing Critical Multisector Support Services to Refugees and Hosting Communities
project_objective:
This project aims to provide humanitarian assistance to refugees and hosting communities under all three Strategic Objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2022: Objective 1: Provide timely multi-sectoral life-saving assistance to crisis affected people to reduce mortality and morbidity. Objective 2: Contribute to building resilience to recurrent shocks and improving vulnerable people’s access to basic services. Objective 3: Enhance the prevention and mitigation of protection risks, and respond to protection needs through quality and principled humanitarian action. 

IOM will provide multi-sectorial interventions including Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Emergency Shelters (ES)/ and Non Food Items (NFIs), Durable Shelters, and Health based activities to respond to the urgent needs of refugees and hosting communities. IOM will focus on providing the multi-sectoral assistance in several states including South Darfur, North Darfur, Central Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Khartoum, Blue Nile, Kassala and Gedaref. Numerous instances of displacement and increases in the number of refugees influxes have been reported in 2020 and 2021 or are expected in 2022 in these states. The proposed WASH activities will increase access to safe drinking water, adequate quality sanitation facilities and improve personal and public hygiene practices. The proposed ESNFI and durable shelter interventions will be used to improve living conditions for vulnerable refugees and host communities that receive high rates of displacement and offer protection to vulnerable people from the harsh elements. The proposed health activities will focus on delivering a basic package of primary health services (BPPHS) to improve access to services and reduce risks associated with morbidity and mortality and support more favorable protection outcomes. During these intervention IOM will follow national guidelines on COVID-19 preventive measures, such as physical distancing, use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and avoid large gatherings. IOM's project will focus on targeting both refugees and hosting communities in an effort to mitigate the risks of tensions over scarce resources, increase the capacity of hosting communities to absorb population influxes. However, lifesaving assistance will be prioritized for new arrivals and vulnerable groups including women, children, the elderly and people with disabilities or other specific needs to ensure that the most urgent humanitarian and protection needs are addressed.

Emergency Food Security and Livelihood assistance to vulnerable and conflict affected households in north east Nigeria
project_objective:
The ongoing conflict has led to high levels of displacement and continues to severely disrupt food production systems and supply chains in North East Nigeria, thereby contributing to extensive human and socioeconomic losses and negatively affecting production systems leading to reduced crop yields ,livestock productivity and exposure to protection risks for women and girls across the region. The volatile security situation is gradually eroding the gains choked over the years and further intensifying the need. 

In 2022, FAO will continue to support IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities to rebuild their agricultural based livelihoods that has been decimated by the conflict. This includes plans to support 12400 households with improved seeds and other agri-inputs. Households for whom livestock was the primary source of income will be supported with restocking interventions aimed at restoring their traditional livelihoods. 
The oncoming season will be very crucial in terms of the anticipated looming catastrophic food insecurity situation within the northeast of Nigeria. This has led to strong advocacy by all actors within the Food Security Sector including FAO on the need to scale up support on agricultural based livelihoods for the upcoming year, 2022.
Further, the increased displacement in recent months in some Local Governments Areas (LGA) in Borno states (Bama, Banki and Dikwa) due to continued attacks by the arm groups requires urgent actions by FAO to meet the urgent needs of the displaced persons. Over 5000 persons including women and children have been displaced in the month of August 2021 alone in these two LGAs and the numbers are expected to increase in the coming months.  
As a result, FAO is responding by scaling up its emergency intervention programme in the north east Nigeria in 2022 to reach more vulnerable communities and households with various forms of agricultural support including quality seeds and fertilizer, livestock & poultry restocking, aquaculture production, Safe Access to Fuel and Energy and critical agriculture based value chain development to increase food production and household food availability.

project_name: Delivering critical life-saving GBV prevention and response Services for Crisis -affected women and girls in South Sudan.
project_objective:
According to the 2022 HNO, more than two-thirds of South Sudan's population, 8.9 million people, are in need of humanitarian assistance, an increase of 600,000 since 2021. An estimated 2.6 million people risk facing gender-based  violence in 2022, which represents a 25 per cent increase compared to 2021 estimates.  

UNFPA aims to reach 156,342 Beneficiaries  ( women 96,106, Men 7817,  Boys 15,634, Girls 34,395, PWD 2.390) with GBV services and information particularly through  implementing community engagement  and awareness-raising activities focusing on risk factors to GBV, available GBV response services, and timely seeking of GBV response services immediately after the GBV incident ( with in 72 hours). UNFPA  will also support primary GBV prevention programs such as EMAP and SASA. The GBV risk mitigation measures include advocating and supporting integration of GBV and survivor support across different clusters, dignity kit programming, conducting safety audits and providing livelihood and economic support.
The GBV  response interventions include providing psychosocial support, GBV case management services, in UNFPA established One-Stop Centers (OSC), other  GBV service provision centres and Health facilities in the project areas.

As the Core Pipe Line Manager for Dignity Kits, UNFPA will procure and distribute Dignity Kits (DK) to women and girls of reproductive age to enhance their Dignity and hygiene as well as use DK programming as an entry point to provide women and girls with information on GBV prevention, and GBV service availability including information and services on Sexual Reproductive Health.

The livelihood and economic support in the  Women and Girls Friendly Space will also act as  an entry point for women and girls to receive more psychosocial support and other empowerment activities. Cram activities, such as knitting, beadwork, crocheting and embroidering bed sheets, and tea discussions, will be introduced as the women often enjoy these activities,  so they are a good way to bring them together encourage conversation and relationship- building with each other. On the other hand, some of these activities will be introduced as income-generating activities to allow women and girls to earn some income to meet their basic needs and referrals for livelihood support with other programmes supporting women and girls.

It is important to note that as a result of the degradation of community protection systems and the inadequate GBV lifesaving services, women and girls have increased exposure to various forms of violence, including rape, sexual assault, psychological abuse, physical violence, child and forced marriage, denial of opportunities, resources and services where some basic services exist. Also, livelihood options are increasingly limited due to the ongoing conflict, exacerbated with COVID 19, disproportionately affecting adolescent girls and young women, resorting to harmful coping mechanisms that include child marriage, survival sex and sexual exploitation and abuse.
Survivors urgently need to access specialized services, including case management and psychosocial support services. A clear referral pathway needs to be established to facilitate the survivors' access to critical life-saving services.

project_name: Protection of rights and durable solution: ability to exercise and enjoy legal identity for population affected by displacement in South West and North West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
NRC will assist beneficiaries to access civil and legal documentation, through the provision of information, counselling and legal assistance. NRC will use mobile teams to ensure that beneficiaries in hard-to-reach areas can have access to these services. Where it is possible, especially in some localities of  the North west and South west, sensitization sessions will be improved through combination of mass media, and community-based approaches to deliver culturally adapted messages related to legal and civil documentation.
One of the main targets groups for these services will be children along with their parents who need birth certificates to sit public exams as well as people affected by displacement who face obstacles to access civil and identity documents to enjoy freedom of movement and access to other rights and services.
In addition to addressing the lack of awareness of the procedures to access documentation and providing legal assistance to deal with the judicial and administrative process of late registration of births, ICLA will address financial barriers impeding vulnerable populations from accessing civil and identity documentation. ICLA will advocate to reduce the cost of judicial late registration of births and facilitate free of charge access to the medical certificate required for late registration . After successfully advocating for the operationalisation of the administrative reconstitution procedure in the crisis-affected areas in Far North, NRC will continue with the support of BUNEC to advocate for the implementation of this procedure in North West and South West regions. ICLA will also contribute to the ongoing national exercise of revising laws and procedures related to identity and civil documentation. Most of the advocacy initiatives will be undertaken through the National Platform on civil documentation that NRC co-leads, as well as intends to initiate those types of platforms in the North West and South West regions. LI Interventions in the Northwest and Southwest regions will be carried out gradually with keen observation in areas where there is reasonable acceptance based on its sensitivity, and continues monitoring of the context to increase coverage accordingly.
NRC will strengthen the capacity of institutions, local authorities, as well as humanitarian actors (e.g., civil registration centres, courts, traditional leaders, etc.) by providing trainings and capacity building on LI, as well as by organising workshops to highlight challenges in accessing civil and identity documentation and to suggest practical solutions through an integrated plan of action. In order to follow up the actions (trainings, recommendation of workshop), joint supervision mission of officials in charge of LI will be made by BUNEC, MINDELVEL and NRC.
Together with relevant authorities and bodies, NRC will explore how to use technology and other innovative approaches to boost birth registration and other civil status aspects. 
Access to civil documentation will increase the protection of vulnerable populations and their right to move freely, and the access and enjoyment of basic services, including but not limited to education.
The ICLA programme will benefit the following primary target groups are duty bearers: IDPs, refugees, returnees, vulnerable host communities, and other vulnerable populations facing difficulties in exercising their LI rights in displacement and return areas. Priority will be given to women, including widows, and displaced boys and girls in school without documents, as well as to people with disabilities and special needs, and persons facing challenges in realizing to obtain/recover civil or identity documents due to the conflict/crisis. The secondary target group will consist of duty bearers at national and sub-national levels including local and traditional authorities, mayors, civil registration officers, government technical and administrative services, and the court.

project_name: Supporting Disease Surveillance, Outbreak and Response with Provision of Life saving Essential health services and Health system Strengthening  to fragile, conflict affected and vulnerable population in North East Nigeria.
project_objective:
This project aims to maintain and strengthen essential health services and systems for crisis affected populations particularly at the Ward level and rapidly respond to health emergencies by leveraging national capacities while progressively enabling local leadership and ownership. The goal is to gradually shift towards a more resilient approach in strengthening capacity of the health system while at the same time responding to acute health emergencies. This plans to achieve a sustainable transition away from the current substitutionary response and to strengthening systems and local ownership is consistent with the national health strategy which highlights the revitalization and strengthening of the disrupted health system as critical elements for access to better health care service delivery. In order to achieve the overall goal of maintaining essential health services and systems,WHO actions will contribute largely into three core areas:
1.	Maintain access to essential health services via the one PHC per Ward government initiative
2.	Establish a functional health information management system with the integration of platforms such as DHIS, EWARS/SORMAS, Health resource and partners mapping.
3.	Facilitate local ownership by strengthening government leadership, coordination and accountability. Through this, the project will focus on maintaining and improving access and quality of health service delivery and strengthen health systems, strengthen health information management, including surveillance, prevention, and alert, strengthen national and partner capacity to promptly respond to and contain outbreaks and other health emergencies and ensuring effective local leadership, partner coordination and operations support in the States of Borno Yobe and Adamawa. It will focus on re-establishing functional, staffed and equipped health facilities to deliver health services to vulnerable people including host communities and returnees at ward level through a novel approach of “health services under one roof’’. WHO aims to support the availability of health workers, the establishment of a health financing mechanism and strengthening the HDN initiative with the overall objective to restore health systems and enable optimal delivery of health services across the BAY states. While making investments in strengthening the health system, WHO will also position as the provider of last resort in delivering life-saving essential health services in the event of new displacements and acute health emergencies. This will improve the quality of health data and foster peer-to-peer learning through effective monitoring & evaluation. State and partners technical and operational capacity for effective coordination and delivery of health services will be strengthened. The provision of essential health services target people in need (in IDP camps and host communities) is a core area of WHO’s support in health emergency response in NEN. This area essentially covers all service provision and support for outbreak response; In 2022, WHO will expand HTR package of services to include FP and NCD/mental health services, align reporting of health data with national HMIS platform with define indicators for MHPSS, GBV, and HTS. Advocate for utilization of strategic documents to guide service delivery. Community participation in planning and response to Public health emergencies will be supported and strengthened, support PHC services and advocate for implementation of rural incentive & minimum service package in line with governments policy to curb high attrition rate of health staff. Priority will be given to establish and strengthen health workforce and service delivery in current MHT (Mobile Health Teams) areas while strengthening local ownership and accountability through joint monitoring and supportive supervision.

project_name: Réponse d’urgence intégrée pour l’accès aux services de santé de base et de protection au profit des personnes affectées par la crise dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun et du Nord
WASH Response to Drought and conflict - Affected Population in Mudug, Nugaal, Sanaag, Bari, Galgaduud and Hiraan regions in Somalia
project_objective: In Somalia, Only 52% of the  population has access to basic water supply, with limited regulation of private water supplies frequently resulting in high prices, forcing families to fetch water from distant and unsafe open wells. In conflict-affected areas and camps for displaced people, access to safe water is frequently hampered due to damaged water infrastructure, which increases the risk of disease and malnutrition among people living in overcrowded conditions. In March 2021 alone, over 70 boreholes were reported to have broken in Puntland and Galmudug regional states due to over-use, weak management, and high operation and maintenance costs, forcing IDPs and host communities to buy water at prohibitive costs. According to a UNICEF report published in 2020, sanitation and hygiene coverage in Somalia is low, with only 38% of the population having access to basic sanitation facilities and services, posing a high rate of open defecation that leads to contamination of water sources and increases the risk of disease outbreaks. Hand washing with soap at critical moments is practiced by only one-third of the population due to a lack of soap and access to a functional handwashing point Coupled by poor knowledge of good hygiene and sanitation practices. WASH in health care institutions has been a source of concern for many years. A significant proportion of Somalia's health facilities lack on-site water connections and rely on water trucks from long distances. This severely jeopardizes service delivery and undermines safe WASH practices, which are critical in controlling and preventing disease outbreaks. This proposed project will increase access to safe and clean water, promote sanitation and hygiene conditions, and contribute to a reduction in infant and under-5 mortality rates as well as WASH-related diseases in general. The project will address the needs of 28,000 vulnerable population in Somalia's Mudug, Nugaal, Sanaag, Galmudug, and Hiraan regions. This will be done through the rehabilitation of boreholes with solar installations, extension of pipelines and water tank construction for communities and health facilities to improve access and storage, provision of water vouchers, rehabilitation of shallow wells, and training of community structures (committees) to increase their capacity to manage and maintain rehabilitated water systems. In addition, the IRC will construct/rehabilitate sanitation facilities (latrines and solid waste management infrastructure) with a focus on IDPs, as well as ensure access to essential WASH services in health facilities to improve health and nutritional outcomes. In addition, IRC will promote hygiene and sanitation and distribute basic hygiene kits to households, including materials for menstrual management. (Applying market –based programming approach where feasible as a complement to in-kind distribution).  The IRC will target communities in hard-to-reach areas with limited access to WASH services, as well as those in cholera/AWD hotspots and crowded IDP settlements, with particular focus on the COVID-19 situation, risk management, and infection prevention and control measures. The proposed response will be delivered through a strong protection lens, which will include efforts to ensure that latrines are gender separated, have lockable doors, adequate lighting, and that the distance to water points is kept within the agreed-upon standards. The IRC will adopt a universal design to ensure water and sanitation facilities are accessible to all, including persons with disabilities.  The project will also consider the impact of conflict on women and children in terms of access to WASH services, as well as the unique needs of menstruating women and girls. The proposed actions will address and prevent gender-based violence risks, thereby improving and contributing to greater gender equality.

project_name: Essential Primary health services to vulnerable conflict affected populations in Idleb and Aleppo
project_objective:
In line with HRP SO2, DDD’s project for 2022-2023 aims to strengthen access to lifesaving and life-sustaining essential primary health services, protection referrals and COVID-19 response for the most vulnerable people with high-severity needs and limited access to regular services in underserved urban settings and camps in Aleppo and Idleb. They will receive comprehensive Essential Health Service Package: PHC, SRH, and MHPSS through 14 fixed clinics, in addition to COVID-19 testing at 2 dedicated PCR laboratories. There will be increasing focus on outreach services, including health promotion activities and home-based specialized medical care focused on people with chronic conditions, people living with disabilities (PwD), and at-risk pregnancies. In-demand MHPSS services will be expanded, with improved MHPSS consultations, dedicated safe spaces for women and children, and strengthened referrals to third-parties through dedicated referral staff. The services will be complemented by the medical waste management for DDD facilities and other providers in Idleb. A total of 274,798 individuals are expected to directly benefit in 2022 and 288,541 in 2023. An estimated 392,247 catchment population will indirectly benefit from the intervention.
The program will support 14 PHCCs:
- 3 PHCCs in Afrin (Afrin PHC 9!B0203070; DDD Jalma comprehensive PHC!B0203087; Jandairis PHC 3!B0203069)
- 9 DDD PHCCs in Idleb (Qah village clinic/ Qah village!G0703049; Morek Alaez camp PHCC/ Morek Alaez Camp!G0703051; Dier Hassan camp PHCC/ Dier Hassan Camp!G0703088; Alsalam camp PHCC/ Alsalam Camp!G0703101; Aljolan camp PHCC/ Aljolan Camp!G0703048; Aldoaa camp PHCC/ Aldoaa Camp!G0703047; Aldana PHCC/ Aldana village!G0703087; DDD Kelly PHC! G0700164; DDD Sarmada PHC! G0703184)
- 2 PHCCs of Idlib Health Directorate (Al Thawrah PHC/ Dental clinic 10!G0700049; Hay Al Jam3a PHC!G0700036).
The project has been developed to respond to needs identified by the community itself through DDD’s engagement mechanisms and strong links with local communities, as well as its MSNA in 2021. DDD's MEAL framework, based on Medecins du Monde (MdM) Network standards, will continue to ensure results-oriented implementation, measure impact and adjust activities for improved quality. The MEAL plan includes direct supervision and monitoring at field level through 2 offices in Qah and Afrin; monthly monitoring visits by coordination staff based in Antakya; constant tracking of consumptions of drugs and consumables; monthly reporting of situation, workload, morbidities, beneficiaries reach, and indicators progress; and data disaggregation by gender, age, host/IDP and disability. Annual program evaluations are also conducted to assess impact and any changing needs. 
DDD’s close coordination with relevant structures and actors in the region has also informed the project design, to ensure that services are well-integrated and relevant. In the 2022-2023 period, the established coordination is planned to continue with Health, CCCM, Protection, Logistics and Nutrition Clusters, as well as COVID-19 Taskforce, MHPSS WG, NCD WG, the Access WG, the NGO Forum, AFAD meetings, SRH Technical WG, and Afrin and Harim PHC networks. In addition, activities will continue to be supported by cooperation with other partners, including Mentor Initiative Organization for leishmania diagnosis and treatment, Shafak Organization for nutrition services, SRD for referrals, UOSSM for MH-GAP, Horan Foundation for ambulance services, Syrian Immunization Group for COVID-19 vaccination, and GIZ for MHPSS supervision.  
DDD, as part of the MdM network, is one of the largest providers of health care services and one of the few NGOs providing PCR testing in NWS. MdM has been responding to the health needs of IDPs and host communities in Dana sub-district since 2012 and in Afrin since 2018. Support for these 14 facilities in 2022-2023 is essential to maintain availability of services to these populations in need.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination, de la gestion de l'information et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso continue de se développer rapidement, étendant sa portée à de nouvelles zones et aggravant ses impacts sur les populations touchées. En Octobre 2021, le nombre de personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays en raison du conflit, de l'insécurité et du manque d'accès aux services de base a connu une augmentation substantielle pour atteindre 1,5millions de personnes, plus des trois quarts vivant dans des conditions précaires sans accès à un abri adéquat ou à l'eau et à l'assainissement. L'insécurité et les déplacements sont des facteurs clés qui entraînent une forte augmentation du nombre de personnes ayant besoin d'aide, exacerbant l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle chronique. La présence de la COVID-19 est aussi autre facteur d’augmentation des besoins. Au milieu de l'année, le nombre de personnes ayant besoin d'aide humanitaire (PiN - Population in Need) était passé à 2,9 millions dans les cinq régions ciblées par la communauté humanitaire dans le cadre du Plan de Réponse Humanitaire 2020 (HRP). Pour 2021, le pays aura à soutenir 3,5 millions de personnes dans un besoin humanitaire dans 6 régions.
Le bureau de pays du Burkina Faso va appuyer le la mise en oeuvre des activités
prioritaires dans les cinq domaines d'intervention de OCHA, notamment
• Renforcer la coordination humanitaire au niveau stratégique et aux niveaux
opérationnels et assurer un leadership dans de la coordination
humanitaire, y compris la coordination civilo-militaire (UN-CMCoord) ; le suivi et le
plaidoyer en matière d’accès humanitaire ; l'engagement communautaire et la redevabilité
envers les personnes affectées ;
• Renforcer le plaidoyer humanitaire, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées
internes et les personnes non déplacées ;
• Soutenir l'application pratique de la politique humanitaire et les bonnes pratiques, y
compris la promotion de la collaboration entre l'humanitaire, le développement et les
acteurs de la consolidation de la paix tout en respectant la distinction et l'intégrité de
l'action humanitaire ;
• Faciliter une mobilisation cohérente et coordonnée du financement humanitaire ;
• Fournir une gestion de l'information de haute qualité et pour soutenir le leadership
humanitaire et la prise de décision.

project_objective:
El proyecto del UNFPA está dirigido a mujeres y niñas en edad reproductiva, mujeres
embarazadas y sobrevivientes de violencia de género. El proyecto ayudará principalmente
a mujeres y niñas indígenas y afrodescendientes con necesidades humanitarias críticas
como consecuencia del conicto armado que incrementó los niveles de violencia de
género (VBG), en particular la violencia sexual, la violencia de pareja íntima (VPI) y la
pandemia COVID-19 en zonas remotas y semiurbanas sin una respuesta estatal ecaz,
con escasa, nula presencia o baja capacidad de establecimientos de salud y servicios
multisectoriales de VG.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo garantizar servicios integrados de SSR / VG,
particularmente 1) Fortalecer la respuesta multisectorial que salve vidas; 2) Reducir la
violencia de género y los riesgos de SSR; 3) Reducir la mortalidad materna y 4). Reducir
los embarazos no planeados y otros daños a la salud sexual y reproductiva. Esto se
logrará mediante cuatro productos que, en conjunto, forman un enfoque holístico e
integrado de la protección y la salud, en VBG, se espera que i) Las sobrevivientes de VG
tengan acceso a una respuesta integral a las necesidades y a servicios multisectoriales
que salvan vidas (salud, apoyo psicosocial, protección) a través de la gestión de casos de
VG y que iv) Las mujeres y las niñas hayan fortalecido los mecanismos de protección y
mitigación de riesgos contra la VG.
Los servicios y suministros de SSR y VG se proporcionarán principalmente a través de
equipos móviles en áreas rurales y espacios seguros en zonas urbanas. Con respecto a la
respuesta a la violencia de género, seguirá el Marco de rendición de cuentas de la
violencia de género y los estándares mínimos de la violencia de género con un enfoque
centrado en las sobrevivientes que responda a la necesidad de fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta directa multisectorial a la violencia de género, incluidos los establecimientos de
salud (Gestión Clínica de la Violación), otras instituciones de protección y autoridades
indígenas. Con equipos de protección se brindará Manejo de Casos de VBG y Apoyo
Psicosocial, incluida la distribución de efectivo incondicional de emergencia para
sobrevivientes de VG y kits de dignidad contextualizados a las necesidades locales
especícas adaptadas a la pandemia de COVID-19 y sensibles para la población
indígena.
Además, se establecerán espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas para promover la
protección y el empoderamiento de las mujeres enfocándose en la mitigación del riesgo
de VG a través de la distribución de información que salve vidas para grupos de mujeres /
comunidades en las áreas más vulnerables.
