project_name: Respuesta en salud para el acceso de servicios de atención a poblaciones vulnerables de seis departamentos del país.
project_objective:
En noviembre de 2020, la República de Honduras fue impactada directamente por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, que ocasionaron daños de diversa magnitud e importancia en 16 de los 18 departamentos del país, afectando alrededor de 4 700 000 de personas, obligando a la evacuación de 363 762 personas, y el alojamiento en albergues de 172 798 personas, con un recuento final de 99 personas fallecidas. El Valle de Sula, en el departamento de Cortés, localizado al norte del país, fue la zona del país más afectada, junto con los departamentos de Atlántida, Colón, Gracias a Dios, El Paraíso, Santa Bárbara y Yoro. De forma simultánea, el país también ha sido afectada por la pandemia de la COVID-19 y por la epidemia de dengue. De acuerdo con el análisis de daños y necesidades del sector salud posterior al impacto de las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, del total de personas afectadas, 500 000 personas, aproximadamente, tenían acceso limitado o carecían de servicios de salud, debido a los daños a la infraestructura de la red de servicios de salud. Más de 393 establecimientos de salud fueron afectados y al menos 10 reportaron pérdidas totales en el equipamiento de la cadena de frío, equipamientos, insumos y vacunas.
En 2021, persisten personas con necesidades en salud, en particular en regiones postergadas e impactadas por las tormentas tropicales.
En este sentido, el proyecto pretende fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta del sector salud mediante acciones de rehabilitación de los servicios afectados por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota y además reforzar la respuesta ante la epidemia de dengue y COVID-19 en el país, para beneficiar a 100 000 personas con necesidades en salud, incidiendo en la reducción de indicadores de morbilidad y mortalidad, así como en las brechas de género, edad, discapacidad y etnicidad en la atención.

project_name: Prevención, Respuesta y Provisión de Servicios Urgentes de Protección Especializados a Niñas, Niños y Adolescentes y sus Familias Víctimas de Violencia en Contexto de Emergencias
project_objective:
UNICEF proporcionará asistencia urgente para la protección de la infancia a 30.000 niñas, niños, mujeres y hombres en 15 municipios priorizado por el Panorama de Necesidades Humanitarias de Honduras, proporcionando servicios de protección de la infancia y acciones de reducción de la violencia/violencia de género, incluyendo información sobre los servicios de protección de la infancia y cómo buscar ayuda.
UNICEF trabajará con gobiernos locales y la Dirección de Niñez Adolescencia y Familia, DINAF, el Instituto Nacional para Atención de Menores Infractores, y con organizaciones internacionales con presencia a nivel nacional y con Organizaciones No Gubernamentales, para desarrollar sus principales estrategias durante las emergencias.
Las estrategias diseñadas por UNICEF pretenden alcanzar los siguientes resultados:
CP1: Establecimiento de Espacios Seguros para que las niñas, los niños y los adolescentes tengan acceso a Servicios de Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial de emergencia sensibles al género, apropiados para su edad y culturalmente aceptables, y a servicios protección para atender sus necesidades urgentes.
CP2: Construcción de estrategias a nivel comunitario que previenen la violencia de género durante la emergencia inmediata y el fortalecimiento de los mecanismos sociales para reducir los riesgos para las niñas, los niños.
CP3: Las niñas, niños y adolescentes sobrevivientes de la violencia, incluida la violencia sexual y de género (VSG), tienen acceso a servicios de respuesta oportunos, de calidad y multisectoriales a través de la gestión de casos y el fortalecimiento de las capacidades nacionales y locales para interrumpir y reducir la violencia.
CP4: (Transversal): Los niños, niñas y adolescentes y sus familias estarán protegidos de la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA) por parte de los trabajadores humanitarios mediante el apoyo/monitoreo continuo de los trabajadores de primera línea, y la socialización de los protocolos y las líneas de ayuda confidenciales para denunciar el abuso o buscar ayuda.
En Honduras, los principales perpetradores de la violencia y el abuso sexual contra los niños son miembros de la familia (el caso del 47% de las niñas que son víctimas de abuso sexual), o miembros de la comunidad con vínculos con el niño. Por lo tanto, a través de estos las estrategias implementadas, UNICEF y sus aliados desarrollarán actividades con las niñas y los niños para ayudar a desarrollar sus capacidades para identificar los riesgos de violencia y abuso y saber cómo buscar ayuda inmediata.
También trabajaremos directamente con los padres, cuidadores y miembros de la comunidad para aumentar el nivel de concienciación hacia la violencia contra los niños y la violencia sexual y de género, y promoveremos el liderazgo dentro de las comunidades para identificar y denunciar posibles casos a los servicios de protección de la infancia.
La gestión de los casos se agilizará entre los líderes de la comunidad las autoridades municipales de protección de la infancia y la DINAF a través de los procedimientos operativos estándar (POE) preexistentes desarrollados conjuntamente por UNICEF, la DINAF y los gobiernos municipales bajo el marco legal del Sistema Nacional de Protección de la Infancia (SIGADENAH).
Centraremos nuestro trabajo en las comunidades marginadas más afectadas por la violencia, la violencia de género y la migración forzada, así como en las comunidades predominantemente garífunas y afrohondureñas, que también son las más desatendidas por los servicios estatales de respuesta a emergencias.
Las actividades de respuesta están diseñadas para proporcionar servicios inmediatos que salvan vidas a las comunidades más afectadas por las múltiples emergencias que atacan al país (COVID-19, las inundaciones producto de ETA/IOTA, los altos niveles de violencia en comunidades que generan migración forzada y desplazamiento interno). Tendrán una duración de 18 meses.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire et nutritionnelle aux populations déplacées internes et hôtes dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord et du Sahel au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
L’insécurité grandissante au Burkina Faso est à l’origine de déplacements massifs de populations. En effet, le pays connaît une grande crise insécuritaire à l’image de ses voisins (Mali, Niger). Sur 1,5 millions de personnes déplacées internes du fait des conflits et des violences dans la sous-région, 69% (1,03 million) se situent au Burkina Faso. La dégradation de la situation sécuritaire poussent à un nombre croissant de déplacements qui viennent saturer les ressources et bousculent les communautés hôtes dans leur vie quotidienne. Au 31 octobre 2021, le Conseil National de Secours d’Urgence (CONASUR) compte 1 481 701 PDIs. Les régions les plus touchées sont le Sahel avec 510 279 (34,4%), le Centre-Nord avec 510 110 (34,4%), et le Nord avec 142 107 PDIs (9,6%). A la même date, 356 formations sanitaires sont affectées par l’insécurité au niveau des 6 régions (Sahel, Centre-Nord, Est, Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun et Centre-Est), parmi lesquelles 83 (soit 23%) sont complètement fermées et les 273 qui fonctionnent à minima.
 
Le retrait progressif des services sociaux de base du Ministère de la Santé a créé une situation d’urgence humanitaire dans plusieurs régions du Burkina Faso, avec une forte affluence dans les formations sanitaires fonctionnelles dans les zones à forte concentration de populations vulnérables et qui impacte négativement la qualité des soins de santé. Face à l’augmentation des besoins médico–nutritionnels des populations hôtes et déplacées, le consortium ALIMA/Keoogo/SOS Médecins BF prévoit de renforcer sa réponse aux urgences dans la région du Sahel (DS de Dori, DS de Gorom-Gorom), du Nord (DS de Thiou, DS de Ouahigouya), du Centre-Nord (DS de Barsalogho, DS de Tougouri, DS de Kaya) et des Cascades (DS de Mangodara, DS de Banfora) pour l’année 2022.
 
Le projet vise le renforcement de la qualité de l’offre de soins de santé primaire et secondaire voire tertiaire (CHU et CHR) au niveau des aires de santé affectées par la fermeture et le fonctionnement à minima. Cela passera par l’installation de PSA, et de cliniques mobiles /interventions au niveau des sites hébergeant les PDI. Des activités telles que la PCIMA, la CPN, la CPoN, l’identification et référencement des grossesses à risque,  les urgences pédiatriques,  la prise en charge psychosociale et de santé mentale aussi bien des PDIs que des populations hôtes y sont menées. Les cas compliqués seront orientés vers les structures sanitaires pour une prise en charge adéquate. Le consortium appuiera après des populations vulnérables avec un forfait dans le transport et l’hospitalisation. Un appui sera dans données aux cas de MAS avec complications reçus dans les CRENI appuyés par le consortium, avec la psychostimulation et la donations de kits de bienvenus à l’admission et des kits WASH à la décharge, y compris d’un forfait de transport.
 
Un appui en RH est également effectif avec des renforcements de capacité du personnel étatique et l’équipe du consortium en étroite collaboration avec les différentes Direction régionales de la santé et Équipe cadre de District dans nos zones d’intervention. En transversal à ces activités, des activités WASH sont également prévues à savoir le renforcement des dispositifs de lavage des mains, des campagnes de sensibilisation sur l’hygiène corporel, des lieux par les hygiénistes, la distribution de kits Wash et d’hygiène, l’installation de poubelles, la construction de toilettes et d’incinérateur (zone à déchets).
Le volet communautaire connaît une amélioration à travers le renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux et leur prise en main des activités de santé, nutrition et santé mentale. Les ASBC et les promoteurs de santé auront en charge les dépistages actifs, prise en charge de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire et la référence le plus précocement des cas de malnutrition avec complications. Il y aura également la sensibilisation et l’orientation sur les CPN.

project_name: Réponse d’urgence aux besoins de santé des populations affectées par la crise humanitaire et sécuritaire dans les régions du Centre-Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le projet proposé est déjà mis en œuvre dans le district sanitaire (DS) de Kongoussi et une mission d’évaluation a été menée dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun pour une extension dans ladite région. La détérioration croissante de la situation humanitaire dans le pays en particulier dans ces 2 régions justifie l’intervention. En effet, elles font partie des 6 régions prioritaires du pays dans le cadre du plan de réponse aux urgences défini par les autorités nationales en lien avec le plan de réponse humanitaire (HRP) 2022. Ainsi, afin de soutenir le système de santé, le projet couvrira 2DS : le DS de Boromo dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun et le DS de Kongoussi dans la région du Centre-Nord. Le choix des formations sanitaires (FS) est fait sur la base des critères suivants : i) aires de santé où les besoins sont accrus (forte présence de PDI) et les populations sont exclues du système de santé par la fermeture de structures sanitaires ; ii) les faibles capacités de réponse des structures face à un accroissement de population, avec un impact négatif sur la disponibilité et la qualité des services fournis ; iii) l’accessibilité en termes de sécurité. Médecins du Monde-France (MdM-F) entend contribuer significativement à la réduction de la morbidité et mortalité des populations déplacées et communautés hôtes dans ces régions durement affectées par la crise humanitaire et sécuritaire. L’intervention vise à renforcer et à améliorer l’accès à des services de soins de santé primaires (SSP) complets, notamment des services de nutrition, de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) avec un accent sur l’approvisionnement en intrants et médicaments en santé de la reproduction/planification familiale y compris les kits de dispositifs minimum d’urgence pour la prise en charge des survivant.e.s de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et la santé mentale et le soutien psychosocial (SMSP).
L’appui de MdM-F aux formations sanitaires ciblées sera global et permettra de stimuler l’offre gratuite et la demande de services de santé de qualité aux populations affectées par la crise dans les 2 districts sanitaires. L’intervention sera menée en stratégie fixe et mobile et mettra l’accent sur l’offre du continuum de SSPavec un focus sur les droits à la SSR en contexte de crise. Dans une logique de participation des communautés, le projet entend développer une approche communautaire à travers le renforcement et l’appui des agents de santé à base communautaire.
Afin de compenser la gratuité ciblée pour les enfants et les femmes allaitantes en postpartum et la gratuité complète pour les cas d’urgences vitales et de VBG, l’appui de MdM-F se fera sous forme d’approvisionnement en médicaments, intrants, consommables et équipements médicaux, ainsi que la mise à disposition de personnels soignants et le renforcement des capacités du personnel médical des structures appuyées pour une offre de soins de qualité. Pour les urgences vitales, l’appui se fera à travers le remboursement des frais de transport, des frais liés aux médicaments et soins médicaux et à la restauration pendant l’hospitalisation.
Enfin, dans le cadre de la réponse aux urgences, MdM-F mettra en place des activités de renforcement des capacités de réponses en situation d’urgences épidémiques (COVID-19, choléra, méningite etc.) et de déplacements massifs de population, de dotation en intrants et d’amélioration de la coordination des acteurs afin de favoriser la résilience du système et parvenir à une réponse efficace et efficiente.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action to Reduce Explosive Risk Faced by Civilians in Palestine
project_objective:
UNMAS aligns with its Country Programme Strategy in contributing to two outcomes 1.The United Nations, and its humanitarian partners in Gaza, maintain critical functions, uninhibited by explosive hazards. UNMAS is the only provider of specialized explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) capacity that is permitted to operate in Gaza by the Gazan and Israeli authorities. UNMAS continued presence has been requested by the Palestinian and Israeli authorities, the UN RC/HC, OCHA, UNRWA and UNDP. UNMAS continues to provide ERW mitigation measures to UN and humanitarian partner sites to ensure that vulnerable communities are protected and prepared against the threat of explosive hazards from past, present and future escalations in conflict. UNMAS maintains an emergency EOD presence in Gaza to remove and destroy ERW posing a threat to Gaza communities. This allows UNMAS to be ready for a rapid response during potential conflict and to maintain an Emergency Response Preparedness Plan (ERPP) to ensure access for the Humanitarian response in any future Gaza conflict.
Outcome 2: Conflict affected people know how to mitigate the risk of explosive ordnance. An individual’s risk of exposure varies on factors that include where they live and work and the information they have at hand. ERW risk awareness is critical to mitigating the threat posed to civilians. UNMAS has identified two types of educational activities that are required in the specific context of Gaza. After several years of community engagement with beneficiary stakeholders and local partners they have developed targeted curricula which consider the needs of different gender and age groups as well as persons with disabilities: (i) risk education provides information for civilians to protect themselves from existing ERW threats, (ii) Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP) is a novel form of risk education providing resilience training to prepare for future escalations, and is critical to avoid civilian casualties. To address COVID-19 restrictions, remote delivery methodologies have been developed as well as dual messaging addressing ERW and pandemic mitigation. Informal street sessions with social distancing measures have also been utilised.In the West Bank, UNMAS works with the National Mine Action Authority, Palestinian Mine Action Centre (PMAC), to enhance their capacity to provide risk education to vulnerable communities in the West Bank and to address the needs of victims of ERW accidents. There are 16 minefields and over 46 identified areas with recorded ERW contamination that pose a risk to shepherds, farmers, women and children. Lack of resources has impacted PMAC ability to coordinate EORE in the West Bank and provide age, gender and disability appropriate risk education where needed. Victim Assistance (VA), is the pillar of mine action that meets the short, medium and long-term needs of women, girls, boys and men who have been injured by explosive ordnance and addresses affected families and communities. UNMAS works to support PMAC in developing their capacity in addressing this requirement. UNMAS has consulted, via a number of workshops, from 2019 to 2021, to develop a project that will assist PMAC to develop and implement an EORE strategy in the West Bank, that is inclusive of the varied needs of women, men and persons with disabilities; and training of trainers to women volunteers for EORE, with a special focus on children in the West Bank.
In this project, UNMAS will ensure for the partner to utilize a complaint channel, and announce the confidential contact lines established by UNMAS and SAWA, a free toll number, social media platforms and WhatsApp contact. The channels will be adapted to the main target of this project that are women, men and boys and girls. In the selection process of an implementing partner for delivery of risk education, the partner that has a complaint channel and meets PSEA requirements was selected.

project_name: Information Management Support to Humanitarian Responders in Ethiopia
project_objective:
Since May 2017, iMMAP has been providing IM support to humanitarian responders in Ethiopia, with the support of the United States Agency for International Development, Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance (USAID/BHA). Therefore, iMMAP is prepared and well positioned to support the humanitarian ecosystem nationwide, including the response in the Northern regions.
iMMAP proposes to support the humanitarian ecosystem in Ethiopia with a 12-month project divided into two geographical areas: a Northern intervention focusing on Tigray/Afar/Amhara and an intervention covering the rest of Ethiopia.
All interventions will aim at enhancing the coordination capacities and the understanding of the humanitarian needs through three main outcomes:
1. Maintaining and scaling up the IM support to humanitarian coordination bodies to meet the increased needs for accurate information management.
2. Providing bi-monthly thematic reports to enhance the understanding and monitor trends of the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Northern Ethiopia through timely and accurate information on a wide range of operational, sectoral and programmatic topics.
3. Training and mentoring of existing INGO/NGO Information Management Officers involved in Inter-Sectoral coordination in Ethiopia.
In line with the principle of localization of the humanitarian response, iMMAP will rely both on International IM officers to palliate the recruitment/movement difficulties in Northern Ethiopia and to face the surge of humanitarian needs. Ethiopian national staff will receive capacity building to ensure that this support is sustainable. These IMOs will lead the data collection, analysis, visualization, and dissemination efforts. They will also support the Humanitarian Needs Overview and Humanitarian Response Plan (HNO / HRP) processes.

project_objective: The project aims at effectively contributing to building the resilience of the community and enhancing equitable access of most vulnerable to basic health services through providing community based health services and reaching out to PoCs by community health workers, building the capacity and mobilizing the community in addressing health risks, and through assisting in the revitalization of the health system by contributing to light rehabilitation of health infrastructure  while building the capacity of NGOs in health.  Contribution to the sector efforts to respond to COVID-19 pandemic will be integrated through supporting risk communication and community engagement related to COVID-19 prevention and vaccine rolling out, coordinated support to case management, surveillance and continuity of care through the provision of  medical equipment and supplies, and assisting in enhancing preparedness and response capacity through supporting the establishment of 8 points of entry jointly with WHO. In 2022-2023  the project will target nearly 750,000  vulnerable returnees, IDPs and affected communities in geographic areas of moderate to high needs and priority, in urban, rural, camps and camps like settlements, with special focus on health vulnerabilities in children, women at reproductive age, older persons and persons with disability including mental disability. Community and right based approaches will be adopted in addition to networking and collaboration with health actors and interlink with WASH, nutrition, protection and shelter sectors influencing the determinants of health.

project_name: Assistance en eau, Hygiène et Assainissement
project_objective:
L'objectif principal du projet est d'améliorer leur accès à l'eau potable, à l'assainissement et à l'hygiène, ainsi que de prévenir les maladies hydriques. 
Les activités du projet se déclinent comme suit dans les différents résultats : 
Résultat 1 : Les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons dans le besoin (déplacées internes, populations hôtes) ont un accès sécurisé, adéquat et équitable à de l’eau salubre et en quantité suffisante 
•	Réalisation de Water truking pour l’accès à l’eau potable de 54 000 personnes (femmes, hommes, filles, garçon) affectés 
•	Réhabilitation de 360 points d’eau, Construction de 256 nouveaux points d’eau et Installation de 170 système solaire pour l’alimentation en eau des populations affectées (femmes, hommes, filles, garçon) y compris pour les écoles et centres de santé, Cash pour l’accès à l'eau des PDI
•	Renforcement des capacités des différents acteur pour la gestion durables des ouvrages hydrauliques
Résultat 2 : Les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons dans le besoin (déplacées internes, populations hôtes) ont un accès sécurisé aux infrastructures d’assainissements
•	Réhabilitation/Vidange ou construction d'infrastructures d'assainissement (22 500 latrines) basée sur la consultation des femmes, hommes, filles, garçons, personnes âgées et personnes en situation de handicap incluant les approches telles que l'ATPC en situation d'urgence
•	Réalisation de 585 latrines institutionnelles pour les et centres de santé dans zones affectées
•	Distribution de kits d’assainissement pour la gestion des déchets dans les zones affectées
Résultat 3 : Les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons dans le besoin (déplacées internes, populations hôtes) améliorent leurs pratiques d'hygiène.
•	Activités de promotion à l'hygiène et de mobilisation communautaire avec les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons à l’endroit de 720 000 personnes affectées.
•	Distribution de kits WASH pour 216 000 personnes et de kits de dignité pour 92 572 femmes et adolescentes
•	Distribution de 4 500 kits d’hygiène aux couples mère enfants malnutris dans les centres de prise en charge nutritionnelle
Résultat 4 : Les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et les mesures de prévention et de contrôle des infections sont renforcées dans les établissements de santé, les espaces publics et les communautés vulnérables afin de réduire l’exposition et la transmission du COVID-19.
•	Activités de promotion à l'hygiène avec les femmes, hommes, filles et garçons pour contribuer à la prévention 
•	Distribution de kits COVID-19 et/ou de dispositif de lave-mains aux ménages
•	Appui à la prévention du COVID-19 et/ou distribution de kits COVID-19 aux centres de santés
•	Appui à la prévention du COVID-19 et/ou distribution de kits COVID-19 aux écoles

project_name: AMELIORATION DE L'ACCES A L'EAU, L'ASSAINISSEMENT ET L'HYGIENE POUR LES POPULATIONS VULNERABLES EXPOSEES ET TOUCHEES PAR LES CRISES HUMANITAIRES Y COMPRIS LA COVID 19 AU MALI.
project_objective:
Ce projet avise à améliorer les conditions d’accès aux services WASH aux populations les plus vulnérables comme décrit ci-après par le secteur. 
1.	Apporter une assistance EHA d’urgence et de PCI (COVID 19, choléra, etc.) aux populations vulnérables, dans les zones ciblées tant au niveau communautaire, au niveau des structures sanitaires et au niveau des écoles, ceci de façon coordonnée, intégrée et adaptée à leur vulnérabilité d'ici fin 2022 
2.	Contribuer aux réponses d'urgence aux crises nutritionnelles à travers des interventions EHA  
3.	Améliorer l’accès des populations, y compris les déplacés, rapatriés et retournés, aux infrastructures et services EHA de façon durable dans les zones vulnérables ciblées tant au niveau communautaire, des structures sanitaires et des écoles d’ici fin de 2022 
4.	Assurer la prise en compte des risques des protection et l’implication des bénéficiaires ainsi que leur satisfaction dans la réalisation des activités EHA                                                                                                                       
5.	Renforcer les capacités de réponse aux chocs des acteurs locaux et leur gestion pérenne des services et infrastructures EHA

Pour s’inscrire dans cet objectif, UNICEF mettra en œuvre l’approche ATPC dans 100 communautés et écoles pour un changement de comportement, le paquet WASH dans 50 centres de santé, l’accès à l’eau durable à 80,000 personnes par la réalisation de 50 mini adduction d’eau et 50 PMH, la distribution des kits d’urgence et kits COVID-19 pour 390,000 personnes et la prévention contre les infections dans 20 régions du Mali.

project_name: Las poblaciones afectadas por crisis enGuatemala pueden satisfacer susnecesidades esenciales durante unacrisis y forman parte integrante durantetodo el año de sistemas alimentarios sostenibles y resilientes ante el clima, en los que se tienen en cuenta la nutrición y las cuestiones de género.
project_objective:
Durante el período de hambre estacional, de mayo a agosto de 2021, cerca de 3.5millones de personas se encuentran en Crisis o Emergencia (Fase 3 de la CIF o peor), y requieren acciones urgentes. Esta cifra se proyecta que disminuirá a 2.5 millones, durante el período de menor inseguridad alimentaria entre septiembre 2021 y enero de 2022.
Hasta agosto de 2021, 16 departamentos son clasificados en Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF):Alta Verapaz, Baja Verapaz, Chimaltenango, Chiquimula, El Progreso, Huehuetenango, Izabal, Jalapa, Quetzaltenango, Quiché, San Marcos, Santa Rosa, Sololá, Suchitepéquez, Totonicapán y Zacapa.
Mientras que, de septiembre 2021 a enero de 2022, se proyecta que 5 departamentos continúen en crisis (Fase 3): Alta Verapaz, Chiquimula, Huehuetenango, Quiché y Totonicapán; y 11 mejoran a una situación de inseguridad alimentaria Acentuada (Fase 2de la CIF).
La población más vulnerable y priorizados en este proyecto son hogares agrícolas deinfra y subsistencia con pérdidas de ingresos por daños provocados por las tormentas ETA y IOTA durante el mes de noviembre 2020., pequeños comerciantes informales, jornaleros agrícolas afectados por las limitaciones derivadas de la Pandemia del COVID-19. Estos hogares se ven obligados a utilizar estrategias de afrontamiento de crisis y emergencia para solventar sus brechas alimentarias, como venta de activos y uso de sus ahorros.
Este plan contempla la atención de 260 mil personas a través de las siguientes actividades
-Actividad 1: Prestar asistencia directa, teniendo en cuenta la nutrición y el género, a las poblaciones afectadas por crisis: El PMA prestará asistencia oportuna a las poblaciones afectadas por acontecimientos repentinos o de lenta evolución a fi n de salvar vidas, proteger los medios de vida y facilitar la recuperación. La asistencia consistirá principalmente en transferencias de base monetaria no condicionadas a los hogares que padecen inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional, aunque se podrá recurrir a la asistencia alimentaria en especie en el caso de que se vean perturbados los mercados o el acceso físico a los alimentos se vea limitado. Para la selección de los beneficiarios, el PMA pondrá especial cuidado en incluir a los hogares con niñas y mujeres embarazadas y lactantes y niños y niñas menores de 5 años.
-Actividad 2: Proporcionar capacitación, equipo, transferencias de base monetaria y asistencia técnica a los pequeños agricultores vulnerables, las comunidades, las cooperativas y las instituciones locales: Esta actividad prestará apoyo a personas, hogares y organizaciones para fortalecer la capacidad de resiliencia a la inseguridad alimentaria y las perturbaciones de origen climático, aplicando un enfoque integral basado en medidas atentas a la nutrición, equitativas y transformadoras de las relaciones de género y resilientes al clima, que se adapten a las necesidades y condiciones específicas de las comunidades destinatarias, así como tendiendo puentes entre intervenciones que aborden las necesidades inmediatas e iniciativas sostenibles de fomento de la resiliencia. La actividad fortalecerá la capacidad de supervivencia, adaptación y transformación de los beneficiarios seleccionados. Se seleccionarán hogares vulnerables con miras a garantizar la participación y la adopción de decisiones en condiciones de igualdad entre mujeres y hombres, que recibirán TBM condicionadas a cambio de crear activos acordados para la conservación del medio ambiente y la contribución a otras inversiones productivas. El PMA utilizará un enfoque de planificación comunitaria participativa y un análisis integrado del contexto. Los activos contribuirán ala gestión sostenible de los recursos naturales, a las prácticas respetuosas con el medioambiente y a la conservación y restablecimiento de la biodiversidad natural, en particular del suelo, los bosques y las cuencas hidrográficas, para proteger a las comunidades vulnerables de los efectos de la degradación de los ecosistemas.

project_name: Rehabilitación de servicios de salud para garantizar el acceso a servicios esenciales a la niñez y sus familias en Alta Verapaz
project_objective:
Se propone la rehabilitación y equipamiento de 10 Centros Comunitarios Salud afectados por las tormentas tropicales ETA & IOTA en Alta Verapaz, los cuales sufrieron daños en su infraestructura de forma parcial o total, aunado a las diferentes multiamenazas características del sector. El personal técnico del área de salud verificó el estado de los establecimientos de salud para llevar a cabo un catastro de la identificación de la problemática y clasificación de daños, los cuales no han sido atendidos aún, por lo que carecen de las condiciones adecuadas y seguras para su funcionamiento. Los establecimientos están ubicados en los municipios de Cobán, Chamelco, San Cristóbal Verapaz y San Pedro Carchá.
Dentro de las actividades principales se plantea la verificación del estado de los servicios de salud, elaboración de planos y especificaciones técnicas, contratación de servicios y adquisición de materiales, ejecución de las obras, supervisiones de seguimiento y fortalecimiento de capacidades para el cuidado de la infraestructura. Se establecerán planes de mantenimiento y operación para cada centro, según las normativas del área de salud y el Índice de Seguridad de Establecimientos de Salud de acuerdo a los parámetros de la OMS y MSPAS, para establecimientos de mediana complejidad. Para asegurar el funcionamiento, se equipará a los 10 centros comunitarios con mobiliario y equipo básico. Para asegurar la ejecución exitosa se coordinará con el MSPAS, municipalidades y liderazgo comunitario desde el proceso de planificación de las obras hasta la entrega delos centros rehabilitados y funcionales, de acuerdo a especificaciones técnicas y planos constructivos, estableciendo procesos de rendición de cuentas a los donantes, entes rectores y población beneficiada.
Con lo anterior se busca re establecer la capacidad funcional y de infraestructura de los10 centros comunitarios de salud contribuyendo al acceso a la salud de la población guatemalteca en el departamento de Alta Verapaz.

project_name: Treatment and Prevention of Malnutrition among Children (6-59 Months) , Pregnant and Lactating Women
project_objective:
Adequate and quality nutrition is a child’s basic human right, with well-nourished children having a better chance of survival and longer-term growth, development, health and productivity. WFP Sudan aims to prevent and treat malnutrition by providing specialized nutritious foods to children under five as well as pregnant and lactating women and girls (PLWG) among refugee, IDP and vulnerable host communities. Geographical targeting of WFP’s treatment program as part of comprehensive Community Based Management of Acute Malnutrition programming is informed by a comprehensive analysis of national nutrition survey results (such as S3M II) and Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) results with a special focus on vulnerable, shock-affected populations.
The proposed response from WFP is in line with the Nutrition Sector Strategy and with the Multi-Year Humanitarian Response Strategy of Sudan. Through this project, WFP will be responding to the nutritional needs of targeted beneficiaries under Outcomes identified by nutrition sector with particular focus on Do No Harm and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) principles, WFP Sudan strives to enhance protection mainstreaming.

project_name: Improving Access to WASH Services for Disaster Affected Populations in Upper Nile, Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Warrap and Western and Central Equatoria in South Sudan
project_objective:
In South Sudan, only 36 per cent of households reported having access to an improved water source in under 30 minutes without facing any protection concerns. The remaining 64 per cent of people across the country rely on unimproved or surface water sources (41 per cent), either take more than 30 minutes to reach an improved water source (19 per cent), or are able to reach an improved source in less than 30 minutes but face protection concerns while accessing the water (4 per cent). The highest proportion of households relying on surface water were found in Upper Nile, with 66 per cent, followed by Jonglei with 43 per cent and Central Equatoria with 41 per cent. The quantity of water available per day is also below standards in many locations, with 17 per cent of people unable to collect enough water for drinking, and 39 per cent of people reporting insufficient access to water for hand washing.
Access to sanitation remained low, with only 17 per cent of households reporting owning a latrine in their compound, 4 per cent have access to a shared latrine, and 2 per cent have access to a communal/institutional latrine. This means that 77 per cent of people do not have access to a latrine. In 34 counties, zero to 10 per cent of households reported using latrines. At the country level, open defecation is practiced by 73 per cent of the population.
Regional access to sanitation varied greatly, from 75 per cent in Western Bahr el Ghazal to 8 per cent in Warrap, 9 per cent in Northern Bahr el Ghazal and 10 per cent in Jonglei; 
Poor access to WASH services combined with high levels of food insecurity continue to have a detrimental impact on the health of children, as seen through the high prevalence of malnutrition and water-borne diseases. Counties reporting high GAM rates have also high WASH needs. Mothers and care takers of malnourished children lack basic hygiene knowledge and access to safe water at domicile jeopardizing the benefits again.in nutrition programs, WVISS intends to reach the IPDs and Host community with an integrated WASH intervention which will target the population of Upper Nile (Melut, Renk, Malakal, Kodok, Baliet, Panikang counties), Western Equatoria (Yambio, Nzara, Ezo, Nagero, Tambura), Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil North and East) Warrap ( Twic, Tonj North, Gogrial West and Gogrial East), and Central Equatoria (Juba) states. The proposed project by WVISS is aiming to achieve the following specific objectives: Vulnerable people who experience multi-sectoral severity levels of 4 and 5 have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral essential services to meet their needs.  Vulnerable people are exposed to fewer protection threats and incidents, and those who are exposed have access to tailored, timely, appropriate services through integrated and inclusive humanitarian action. Vulnerable people withstand and recover from shocks, have their resilience to shocks and stresses built, and seek solutions that respect their rights.
To realize the WASH cluster objectives, WVISS will provide lifesaving WASH emergency interventions in the targeted Counties in  (Melut, Renk, Malakal, Kodok, Baliet, Panikang counties), Western Equatoria (Yambio, Nzara, Ezo, Nagero, Tambura), Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil North and East) Warrap ( Twic, Tonj North, Gogrial West and Gogrial East), and Central Equatoria (Juba) states.  The WASH emergency interventions will improve access to safe water, secured and gender appropriate sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion, which will be integrated in other sectors, among them health, nutrition, Food security and livelihood, and child protection/ GBV.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Advocacy in Ethiopia
project_objective:
OCHA’s direct beneficiaries are the members of the humanitarian community operating in Ethiopia: UN Agencies, international and national NGOs, government institutions and donor representatives present in Ethiopia and member states through local embassies and consulates.
The humanitarian community in Ethiopia continues to rely heavily on OCHA’s coordination and support function, especially around operational coordination and humanitarian access at national and sub-national levels across the country. OCHA’s work is critical to unlock operational and access challenges, including the regularization of the movement of goods and services. Humanitarian response across Ethiopia has been hampered by the challenging and significant access constraints particularly affecting the Northern Ethiopia response (Tigray, Afar and Amhara), but also in many other parts of the country, including Benishangul Gumuz, Oromia, and Somali regions. 
For 2022 and beyond, in addition to conflict dynamics, it is anticipated that disease outbreaks, including a continuation of the COVID-19 pandemic and/or its aftermath, floods, desert locusts infestations, and climatic shocks along with food insecurity and acute malnutrition will continue to affect lives and livelihoods and wear down development gains, further escalating humanitarian needs. The food insecurity and malnutrition situation in the country is also worsening significantly. Disruption of farming activities, below-normal harvests from previous seasons, devaluation of the Ethiopian Birr, and increase in market demands have also caused market prices of basic commodities to soar.
In 2022, OCHA will continue to scale-up its work in all regions of Ethiopia. This will include a focus on ensuring that coordination needs across the country are addressed by strengthening and harmonizing linkages between national and sub-national coordination structures to enable robust humanitarian response and expansion of coordination mechanisms in Northern Ethiopia and across the rest of the country. OCHA will also support improved and consistent communication on the work carried out by humanitarian partners, based on the principles of accountability and transparency and on a robust evidence-based monitoring of the response. OCHA will support collective advocacy around the protection of all affected communities and principled humanitarian response, which also includes resource mobilization strategies that are based on needs and common priorities. OCHA’s pooled funds (EHF and CERF) will be particularly important in providing financing capacity to enable partners to deliver timely, coordinated and principled assistance. Special attention will be paid to ensuring meaningful participation of local actors in funding opportunities. Finally, through its mandate and comparative advantage in the areas of Access and Civil-Military Coordination, OCHA will facilitate and coordinate humanitarian actors’ efforts to establish and maintain humanitarian access and overcome increased access constraints caused by rising insecurity, rhetoric and misperception around aid workers. 
- Intervention 1 (Coordination),
- Intervention 2 (Information Management),
- Intervention 3 (Humanitarian Financing),
- Intervention 4 (Advocacy/Access)

project_name: Strengthen the collective humanitarian response through effective, agile and efficient coordination, based on humanitarian principles in Far North
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to strengthen the coordination of the humanitarian response in Cameroon to save lives, protect the most vulnerable and improve the resilience of populations. Since the worsening of the crisis in the North-West and South-West regions, Cameroon faces three complex humanitarian crises affecting eight of Cameroon's ten regions. The impact of these three crises on the living conditions of the affected populations is reinforced by pre-existing structural vulnerabilities that hamper their recovery, particularly in the Far North. The security situation in the Far North further deteriorated in 2021, due to the widespread insecurity in the Lake Chad region, with an increase in attacks by NSAGs, including suicide attacks and attacks using improvised explosive devices (IEDs). In terms of the wider Lake Chad Basin region, 2021 has recorded the highest monthly numbers of security incidents attributed to NSAGs since 2018. Between 1 January and 30 October 2021, the total of security incidents in the Lake Chad Basin attributed to NSAGs increased compared to the same period in 2020. Additionally, In the Far North, particularly in the Lake Chad Basin area, the economic context is marked by poverty, the lack of natural and financial resources and market opportunities, and a drastic reduction in agriculture, livestock production and tourist activities due to prevalent insecurity. Agricultural activity has come to a standstill in areas prone to repeated incursions by non-State armed groups (NSAGs). Meanwhile, the agro-pastoral economy is negatively impacted by the increasing depopulation of herders who transit livestock out of risk areas and the disruption of seasonal transhumance, as main border transit points with Nigeria are closed.
The complexity and the scope of these crises therefore require more effective coordination, adapted to the different intervention areas and based on humanitarian principles. OCHA Cameroon's coordination project will thus make it possible to achieve a humanitarian response that is better funded, more strategic and that centralizes human rights and the protection of people in the Far North. It will also enable a better complementarity between emergency actions and development programs, in order to fight together the humanitarian needs and their underlying causes. To this end, OCHA will provide the essential services of disseminating key information products, coordinating the Humanitarian Programming Cycle and facilitating joint multisectoral needs assessments. Its presence in Yaoundé, Maroua and Kousseri will enable it to provide decisive support to coordination mechanisms and promote coherence between operational issues in the field and strategic decision-making bodies. This key position will also enable it to advance the overriding considerations of the Centrality of Protection and Cross-cutting Protection, Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and nexus humanitarian development and peace. From its sub-offices in the Far North, OCHA will also support the scaling up of the response in these regions, including through the management of CMCoord and humanitarian access responsibilities, as well as capacity building of local responders.

project_name: Provide Child Protection Services to IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in Sudan
project_objective: Despite the signature of JPA, armed clashes have continued to be observed across Sudan, the severe economic crisis continued to negatively impact on the life of the people in Sudan. These situations have been exacerbated by the COVID 19 pandemic. The overall protection needs of the children have grown up considerably. According to the HNO/HRP 2022 figures a total population of 2,447,351 children are need across the different states, including 1,221,786 IDPs, 152,249 South Sudanese refugees, 465,488 returnees and 617,828 vulnerable children among the host communities. International support towards the transitional government has not yet translated into substantive financial and policy support to contribute to a progressive reversal of the situation. As a result, humanitarian needs continued to grow, driven by underlying factors including the economic crisis, food insecurity, flooding, disease outbreaks and intercommunal violence. All these factors have resulted in prolonged displacement in addition to recent fighting in Jebal Marra between different factions of armed groups and intercommunal conflict exacerbated by the deteriorating economic conditions and other political factors. Sudan has and is still receiving additional numbers of refugees from South Sudan, Congo, CAR, Eritrea and recently more than 60000 Newly displaced Ethiopian refugees. The country has also continued to experience rains and floods emergencies in 2021, affecting people across the 18 states of the country. Moreover, endemic diseases such as Malaria, cholera, dengue fever and chikungunya, other novel diseases are also emerging including some which have not been reported in over 10 years. The people in need in Sudan will be the highest over the past decade. Protection of children from violence, exploitation, abuse, and neglect within such complex emergencies is challenged by many factors that child protection partners are working to address. Children affected by conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and other emergencies are more prone to all types of violations to their rights including their rights to basic services. Many have been separated from their families due to sudden displacement and become vulnerable to further violations including recruitment and association with armed forces/groups. Others who witnessed violence and atrocities during conflict are psychologically affected and need psychosocial support services to avoid further deterioration to trauma and mental health problems that needs specialized services which is not available in almost all conflict affected areas. Displaced children and adolescents specially adolescents’ girls are subject to GBV because of the breakdown of the protective family and community environment during displacement and conflict. Many children in the states affected by armed conflict are victims of UXOs and some of them lost their lives especially in the newly accessible areas in Blue Nile, south Kordofan and Jabal Marra area in Darfur. The six grave violations against children by armed forces/groups is widespread in the conflict affected areas. Together with UNITAMS, the UN Wide MRM-CAAC is being strengthened across the country to continue the monitoring and reporting on grave violations including community-based approaches to response to these grave violations against children are needed basically strengthening formal and informal child protection mechanisms and ensure that they complement each other. Under the strategic objective one of HRP, child protection emergency response to newly displaced people due to intercommunal conflict, flooding, and pockets of violence in Jebel Marra areas as well as in the newly accessible areas in South Darfur, Blue Nile and South Kordofan states will be provision of lifesaving child protection services such as provision of PSS, FTR services, prevention and response to GBV against children and adolescents, UXO risk education, monitoring reporting and responding to grave child.

project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des populations déplacées, des retournées et hôtes vulnérables dans la région de l’Extrême-Nord Cameroun
project_objective:
La région de l’Extrême-Nord du Cameroun fait face à des contraintes structurelles et sociales qui la classent d’une grande fragilité du fait de son exposition aux aléas climatiques et environnementaux. Les actions de la secte boko Haram sont venues amplifier cette situation de fragilité. Les jeunes sont majoritaires (60%) et sont sous employés (86%) par conséquent sont en proie à la secte Boko-Haram. Les personnes vivant avec handicap généralement exclues des activités de développement constituent 10% de la population. La récente analyse cadre harmonisée (octobre, 2020) dénombre 901 042 personnes en besoin, situées en phase 3 et plus. Alors que l’ensemble des acteurs humanitaires cibleront 325 214 personnes en situation d’insécurité alimentaire, la FAO, à travers ce projet, déroulera une réponse ciblant 78 051 personnes.  
Le présent projet de renforcement de la résilience des populations déplacées retournées et hôtes vulnérables vise à améliorer la capacité d’adaptation des populations vulnérables face à l’insécurité alimentaire. Il sera mis en place dans trois départements à savoir Logone et Chari, Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga.  Le projet se propose d’appuyer 8000 ménages, 3000 jeunes et femmes et 100 groupements, soit moyenne 60 000 personnes. La réponse se déclinera suivant 2 axes d’intervention. L’axe de production céréalière avec un support en cash inconditionnel pour assurer les besoins alimentaires et non alimentaires tout en préservant l’actif productif et un second axe centré sur l’élevage et le maraîchage de contre saison en vue de développer des revenus supplémentaires.

 Le projet se propose, pour ce faire, une approche holistique à travers des activités d’éducation en situation et répond non-seulement aux besoins immédiats de la population cible mais vise également à assurer la durabilité de l'intervention en proposant une approche partenariale   de collaboration   avec toutes les parties prenantes dont   les acteurs étatiques, les Organisations humanitaires   et ceux de la société civile. 
 Save the Children, voudrait à travers ce projet fournir une réponse intégrée en matière d'éducation et de protection aux filles, aux garçons et aux enseignants touchés par les conflits dans la région. Les interventions éducatives seront axées   sur les résultats ci-dessous :

Bien plus, au-delà des formations pédagogiques sus énumérées, le projet prévoit de distribuer les kits pédagogiques aux enseignants, directeurs e animateurs communautaires ainsi que les kits scolaires  aux enfants.
3.	Le système éducatif est résilient et prêt à mettre en œuvre des stratégies cohérentes en situation d’urgence : Le projet prévoit d'appuyer la mise en place, la dynamisation des  CGS , AME, APE , Gouvernements des enfants et les commissions éducatives des Mairies et leur  renforcement des capacités sur  les thématiques pertinentes de la protection, l’Education en urgence , les attaques contre les  écoles et , l élaboration et la mise en oeuvre  des plans  de réduction des risques, catastrophes  et de résilience   ainsi que  les mécanismes de  redevabilité et gestion des plaintes . Dans le contexte de  cette crise qui affecte les enfants , il est envisagé également la formation de enseignants sur la santé mentale et soutien psycho social .

project_name: Provision of GBV Services to Affected Populations of Aleppo and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
Protracted Syrian conflict, economic deterioration, ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, coupled with predated gender inequality rooted in harmful traditional norms and patriarchal culture, significantly exacerbate GBV risks throughout the country.  Evidence show that women and girls are disproportionately affected by GBV, with certain groups being particularly exposed to risks of GBV, e.g. adolescent or separated and unaccompanied girls, women and girls with disability, divorced or widowed women, displaced women and girls. Various forms of GBV were mapped as prevailing, from sexual violence, IPV and family violence, physical and emotional violence, denial to resources, opportunities, and services, early and forced marriage, SEA, and many others. Covid 19 pandemic poses additional challenges: both with gender roles in care provision, further isolation of girls and women, increasing the rates of IPV and family violence, inaccessibility of GBV services, but also increase of reported online violence  , particularly among younger generations.
As demand for GBV related services grows,  the existing GBV services are insufficient to respond to all of the people in need. Aside of their availability, their accessibility for particular groups of vulnerable people can be challenging, while applying intersectional lenses when providing GBV services is often not practiced, resulting in lack of appropriate tailored made, case-by-case, and adapted services. Among the services mapped, where increased number of interventions is needed, are woman and girls safe spaces (WGSS) in various modalities, including quality GBV case management, CVA for protection outcomes, PSS activities, adapted programming for adolescent girls, etc.
Within such context, NCA will implement the project, building on its institutional knowledge on GBV programming (extended to GBV mainstreaming and mitigation as well). In order to respond to the mapped needs, and in alignment with 2022-2023 WoS GBV Framework, the project proposes a series of interventions aiming at improving access to quality life-saving GBV response services to GBV survivors, and women and girls at risk, and putting measures to prevent and mitigate GBV. 
Under Activity 1, Provision of quality and life-saving GBV response services, the project will provide quality GBV case management and referrals, Age-sensitive PSS activities (for adolescent girls and adult women), CVA within GBV case management, and Capacity building of GBV actors to respond to GBV. Under Activity 2, Enhancing strategies to empower women and girls, the project will include Awareness raising activities to address GBV and harmful social norms , available services, and COVID-19, and Distribution of dignity kits. Finally, Activity 3, Promotion of GBV risk mitigation into all aspects of the humanitarian response, will focus on engaging and training non-GBV (WASH) practitioners on reducing GBV risks and referring GBV survivors or women and girls at risk to specialized services. The project will implement all activities through static WGSS, and complimentary mobile teams to extend the outreach and include remote locations.
The selection of locations for the 2022 is informed by (1) HNO severity scale of GBV PiN, targeting Rural Damascus (with in Babella and Hajar Aswad with index 5) and Aleppo (with Jebel Saman, and As Safira with index 3), and (2) NCA’s institutional knowledge and experience in working with these governates through its partners, as well as presence of its WASH projects where GBV mainstreaming activities can be directed. Expansion towards Idleb in the districts with severity scale 4 in the 2023 is considered (Sanjar, Abul Thohur, Khan Shaykun).

project_name: Education in Emergencies Response for Crises Affected Children in Bay region of Somalia
project_objective:
Conflict and environmental shocks have been the primary drivers of humanitarian needs in Somalia, leaving girls and boys out of school. According to the Protection Return Monitoring Network (PRMN), 593,000 people were displaced in Somalia between January and September 2021, of which 420,000 were displaced due to conflict and 98,000 due to drought1. Of the people displaced this year, an estimated 237,200 (40%) are school-aged children. In total, there is about 2.9 million displaced people in Somalia and an estimated 1 million of these are school-aged children.

FCA rapid needs assessment (10/21) highlighted the challenges faced by the assessed schools in baidoa and Dinsoor  which include  lack of accessible and gender friendly structures such as chairs,  desks, classrooms, latrines and handwashing facilities, accompanied by shortage of learning and teaching materials such as books, pens and chalks. Lack of qualified and inadequate number of teachers, especially female teachers as well as teachers who are trained in special education needs to handle children with CWDs and negative cultural norms have contributed to the low enrolment, attendance and retention of girls and CwD in schools. The barriers faced by CwD are not limited to those faced by girls, but their enrolment, retention and movement to education are hindered by additional stigma, discrimination and misconceptions. Lack of adequate fencing of the school compound to promote protection and safety and long distances to school cause safety concerns particularly for girls. EiE actors require capacity to provide quality education to CwD. Caregivers also faced with challenges in covering school fees, uniforms and scholastic materials. Strengthening the involvement of community in school management activities and mainstreaming child protection and child safeguarding mechanisms into education will improve access to education for girls and CwD.
Aligning with the 2022 Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan, the proposed initiative aims to restore and maintain access to and retention of crisis-affected school children to safe, protective, inclusive and continuous learning opportunities in Bay region of South West State of Somalia. The project will put a strong emphasis on an integrated approach to education focusing on access, quality of education, protection, child safeguarding, gender equality, conflict sensitivity, and disaster risk reduction (DRR) in the design, approach and activities. 
The proposed project will benefit 7100, crisis-affected children (4,400 children in Baidoa and 2,700 children in Dinsor) with at least 45% of girls. The vulnerable poor host community children (40%) will also be targeted since they are also affected by the crisis and have limited access to quality education. Protection and psychosocial well-being of the affected boys and girls as well as teachers is central to the project. FCA will closely work with Somalia Institute for Special Education Needs and Disability (SISEND), the only disability NGO in Somalia that specializes in special education needs, to provide capacity building to teachers, MoE and other education personnel. 
FCA has excellent capacity to scale up, applying best practices and lessons learned from its EiE experiences in other districts of South West State (Baidoa, El-berde and Hudur) to Dinsoor.. Utilizing FCA integrated and innovative approach based on well-known Finnish education system, FCA will take into account the potential impact of Covid-19 pandemic and develop innovative solutions to ensure uninterrupted access to education by the target children.

The proposed project will be implemented in Baidoa and Dinsoor where there are high number of IDP and are in IPC 3. The implementation will be done in close partnership with GREDO; a local NGO that is currently partnering with FCA on the ECHO funded EiE Projects. The project will also be implemented in close collaboration with MoE of Southwest State.

project_name: Improving Access to Lifesaving Integrated Emergency Primary Healthcare Services to IDPs and Host Communities in the States of Warrap, Upper Nile and Western Equatoria, in South Sudan
project_objective: Through the 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan, World Vision International (WVI) South Sudan will provide emergency lifesaving health interventions which will be integrated with nutrition, WASH, protection and FSL activities. The approaches shall revolve around mobile clinics in hard-to-reach areas primary healthcare and secondary healthcare at the static sites and emergency health intervention which will include sexual gender-based violence (SGBV), clinical management of rape (CMR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). Owing to the high mortality rate of under 5 children (90.7/1000), maternal mortality rate (789 deaths/100,000 live births) in South Sudan, World Vision will provide also maternal and child health interventions, mainly skilled birth attendance, prevention of post -partum hemorrhage, ante natal care, post-natal care, basic and comprehensive emergency neonatal and obstetrical care (EMNOC), Sexual and Reproductive Health/ family planning service and Expanded Programme Immunization (EPI) and quality management of Severe Acute Malnutrition with medical complication and community health care through the Boma Health Initiative. The Boma Health Workers (BHWs) shall be trained to provide health promotion, treatment of CU5 for the three common causes of morbity and mortality (malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoea) and identification and referral of severe cases to the nearest health facility for treatment. Additionally, World Vision will ensure that there is continuum of care for under 5 with SAM and MAM so that they have access to OTP and TSFP facilities run by nutrition partners, including World Vision who is a provider of Community Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) and Maternal Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) practice. World Vision will ensure that people with disabilities and mental disorders have priority access to emergency health services and are included as vulnerable groups owing to their high-risk during emergencies. The response plan will be prioritized based on epidemiological status and disease outbreaks, cholera hot spot locations, measles outbreaks, malaria seasonality. The emergency lifesaving response will be done in line with the recommended health cluster emergency clinical services package for primary healthcare units, primary healthcare centers, county hospital, mobile medical team, and Boma Health Initiative. These interventions will be in line with the South Sudan Ministry of Health’s policies and guidelines, named as the basic package of health and nutrition services, Boma Health Initiative, sexual and reproductive health, immunization guidelines and health policy of the Republic of South Sudan. This project plans to reach a total population of 100,000 (51,000females, 49,000males), 21,000 (10,290mles, 10710females) children aged below 5years and 1000 ( 490males, 510males) persons with disabilities  with a budget of approximately USD 3,000,000 over a period of one year.

project_name: HOMELESS MIGRANTS TRANSITIONAL SHELTER IN BEIRUT
project_objective:
This project is a continuation of activities already underway since December 2020. 
Concern works in collaboration with Al Makan, a Lebanese Civil Society Organisation based in Beirut, to jointly manage a transitional shelter for homeless and destitute migrants in Beirut. It was initially opened to address the increase in migrant homelessness in the wake of the Beirut Blast. 
Homelessness continues to occur due to the economic crisis, which makes it increasingly difficult for sponsors to afford domestic workers, as well as there being an increase in abusive practices, leading to an increase in both evictions and escapes. Given the complicated legal status of many residents, the location of the shelter is kept confidential. 
Homeless and destitute migrants are provided with safe shelter while they are waiting to either be repatriated or re-engage with another sponsor and re-enter into the workplace in Lebanon. The shelter has a maximum capacity of 30 people at any one time, in order to avoid overcrowding due to COVID-19 or overwhelming PSS and protection staff. As the shelter is not a ‘closed shelter’ (ie the residents are free to come and go) the shelter is not appropriate for complicated cases such as for people suffering from moderate or severe mental health issues – these cases need specialized care which this shelter does not provide.
Based on experience, residents in the shelter stay between one and three months before they can move on –depending on how complicated each individual case is, and how much assistance they get from their embassies or consulates.
While in the shelter, residents receive multi-purpose cash assistance which covers their food and communications costs. Water, electricity and wifi is also provided. All residents receive Psycho-Social Support (PSS) and demand-driven vocational training opportunities. All protection or health concerns that are identified are referred to relevant migrant-focused partners (e.g. Amel, Kafa, LAW, Caritas, This is Lebanon etc). Repatriations are case managed by referring them to embassies and consulates for issuing travel permits and clearing each individual with General Security, and referrals to relevant organisations (e.g. OUR and Amel) for covering flight and PCR costs.
The shelter residents are identified through individual or organizational referrals, handled by Al Makan. Hotline calls that are not eligible for shelter are referred either through assisted referrals or self-referrals, and Al Makan maintains an up to date service map for this purpose. 
The shelter is staffed by a Protection and PSS Officer and two volunteers who share the daily management of the shelters, conduct PSS sessions, organize trainings, and assist with the hotline for receiving referrals. Al Makan takes on the daily management (operation and maintenance) of the apartments and receives/assesses referrals. Concern takes on the daily management of the residents from a protection and PSS perspective, provides MPCA and case manages protection concerns that may arise.
Al Makan has been fundraising with an aim to take over the long term running of the shelter, but their fundraising is proving difficult and slow to mature. An additional 12 months of funding are required to buy Al Makan time to raise the funds required to be able to take the shelter without ongoing support from Concern, creating a sustainable shelter solution for homelessness among the migrant communities.

project_name: Improving access to and utilization of integrated essential health care services by all people in need including the vulnerable and crisis affected in Nyirol and Uror Counties.
project_objective:
The main aim of this project is to address the challenges associated with access to and utilization of essential lifesaving emergency healthcare services by all people in need and endeavour to improve the same in Nyirol and Uror Counties. This is in line with the Health Sector Response plan 2022 for South Sudan which emphasizes three objectives i.e. to improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations, reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases, enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms. The design of this project is emphatic on provision of basic essential health services in line with the established protocols and guided by the epidemiological profile of disease outbreaks, seasonality and trauma related emergency requirements. Prevention, preparedness, response and mitigation activities responding to people in need, with attention to access for vulnerable groups like women, children and person with disabilities is paramount in the delivery of this project. Therefore, the emergency that this project will address is in respect of the high rate of mortality from the highly prevalent epidemic diseases. In the volatile context of Jonglei, the project will target Returnees, IDPs recently displaced by conflict and flooding, and host communities in areas with limited access to health services. Whereas the 2022 HC PIN is 62,246 and 105,919 in Nyirol and Uror respectively, this project targets 80,000 beneficiaries out of the HC target of 115,859 consisting of Host Community, IDPs and Returnees and disaggregated by County, age, gender and disability i.e. U5 =M7,689-F7,758, 6-17 yrs=M17,049-F13,798, 18-60yrs.=M14,267-F15,039, >60yrs=M1,601-F2,799. Of these, the project targets a total of 550 who are PWD (U5-M8-F12, 6-17=M20-F40, 18-60=M175-F245, Over 60=M19-F31). 

The flooding, limited food and income sources all have food insecurity and health implications. In order to achieve the expected results, the project has prioritized PHCC, PHCU and mobile team clinical packages with various strategies namely recruitment and placement of adequate staff in key cadres to provide key services such as provision of OPD consultations, BeMONC and CeMONC services in key health facilities, Initiating and sustaining IPC measures in health facilities, establishment and deployment of mobile response units and medical teams, renovation and equipping of health facilities, Conducting monthly supportive supervision of health facilities jointly with the CHD, Provision of MHPSS and CMR including training of staff on the same based on standard treatment protocols as well as rehabilitation services for disabled, referral of the survivors to safe houses and lastly, establishment and maintenance of feedback mechanism at health facilities. It is envisaged that a successful implementation of these activities through scaling-up access to integrated quality essential health services would significantly result in the overall decrease in morbidity and mortality arising from the epidemic prone diseases. It will further increase access to services for SGBV survivors, disabled individuals and people with mental health disorders. Besides improving resilience among vulnerable populations, the activities are further expected to benefit from an integrated response involving key sectors such as health, WASH, nutrition, FSL and protection. In order to ensure AAP, a mechanism will be provided for affected populations to receive the information needed to make informed decisions on accessing health services, provide feedback on the interventions, share concerns and submit complaints by involving all stakeholders.

project_name: Life-saving and resilience WASH assistance to affected people in Syria
project_objective: WVSR plans to continue provide life-saving comprehensive WASH package for IDPs living in displacement sites across NWS/NES. Water trucking, solid waste management and hygiene supplies/cash/voucher distribution will be provided in the subdistricts of Azaz, Daret Azza, and Atareb (8 IDP locations), Harim (3 Ikhaa Hamaa, Al Khan & Al Kurah camps), Maaret Tamsrin (Rabee Masrounah & Harbanoush), Ras Al Ain (Tal Halaf village), Tell Abıad (Amin village)and future sites. In some of these locations such as Harim, Dana and Azaz there are plans for new water networks in the settlements and towns through connection to existing and new water points/elevated storage tanks to allow for the phasing out of water trucking to a more sustained and durable solution, 8 water treatment stations will be supported in subdistrict in Azaz(4), Janudiyeh(2), and Tell Abıad(2), through the operation (staffing, chlorine and fuel supply), maintenance of generators and submersible pumps and electricity. Some of these sites have potential to provide a solarized alternative of energy to support using hibernate system decreasing the electricity costs of running the systems. In addition to O&M support, there will also be capacity building and feedback consultative meetings arranged to serve as a knowledge sharing with local council, water station management and community focal points on various topics such as cost recovery, maintenance and reporting. Desludging activities are proposed in IDP sites in Azaz (Al-Ryan, Talil & Al), and Atma village, Dana subdistrict. Sewer network rehabilitation and expansions are proposed in the subdistricts of Azaz (8 IDP locations), Dana, and Ras Al Ain. In 2018, WV notably piloted the construction of a wastewater treatment plant (first of its kind) in Sejjo camp with private funds where treated water it acceptable for agricultural purposes. From learnings and ongoing O&M WV also plans to repeat this piloted approach in 2 new locations in NWS this time powered through renewables. On the institutional setting, WV plans to rehabilitate and construct WASH facilities in 32 schools: Ras Al Ain and Tell Abiad (8), Ariha & Jisr-ash-shugur (24) in particular gaps identified for persons with disability. There will be 18 Healthcare facilities in Idleb with proposed improved WASH and IPC support along with HCF waste management for hygiene Promotion, WV will support various hygiene and climate smart promotion interventions and RCCE sessions in various formats (from school messaging, posters in streets, on water tanks, Solid Waste vehicles, social media) with tailored messaging to the appropriate setting and age groups. WV is focusing more on ‘nudges and cues’ such as painted steps to hand washing stations at the school setting to social distancing markers at communal water point to serve as reminders for healthy behaviors. For children, WV will use its existing partnership with Sesame Workshop, in 10 informal learning centers in IDP camps in Azaz, Ras Al Ain, Tell Abıad Sub-districts, with plans to expand to the formal school setting. The Sesame Workshop program educates and empowers children to healthy lives, through promotion of behavioral changes in sanitation and hygiene through children play-based learning materials, and multimedia content program developed through Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. There are also social-emotional objectives, including coping with big feelings, building resilience, fostering hope, developing conflict resolution skills, and practicing kindness and mutual respect, along with climate adaptive water conservation messaging. In summary all of these interventions will improve access to essential WASH services, reduce harmful coping strategies; that have adverse cascading effects on individuals and communities in terms of public health, environment, inequality, poverty and provide a foundation for infection, protection and control of C19 and reduce transmission of water-bourn illnesses and ultimately save lives

project_name: Provision of improved equitable inclusive quality education in emergency to 11,376 affected IDPs and host communities’ children including children with disabilities, and youth (girls and boys) by 2022 in counties under IPC 4 & 5.
project_objective:
Education is not only a powerful driver of development, and one of the strongest instruments for reducing poverty and improving peace and stability, but it can also be a key to ending conflicts. Rebuilding education systems during and after crisis envisaged by the project is crucial in conflict and fragile situations because it will help provide security, facilitate peacebuilding, and foster resilience.
Oxfam’s active presence in Lakes State (Rumbek Centre, Rumbek East, Yirol East, Yiror West, Awerial), Jonglei State (Akobo, GPAA-Pibor), Eastern Equatoria (Kapoeta East and Kapoeta North) has enabled to establish relationship with local authorities, School management committees, and  PTA’s  therefore making the task of responding to the needs of pre-primary, primary schools, ALP/FAL centers effective. 

OXFAM has had extensive history of responding to pressing educational needs and has been an active HRP partner in South Sudan for several years. The need for education in Lakes, Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria states is particularly urgent with an estimated 16,500 children and youths and 210 teachers in need of support. Oxfam will target 12,500 children to improve school enrolment and retention, this outcome will be reached through training teachers, PTAs, SMCs, community leaders, local education officials , and MoGEI staff in quality education delivery, improve school WASH infrastructure and practices, organize COVID-19 awareness campaigns as well as an introduction and integration of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). The proposed response plan will be implemented in the timeframe of 12 Months.

project_name: Enhancing access to  lifesaving WASH services for  vulnerable host and IDP communities in Somalia
project_objective: The proposed project aims to cover the WASH needs of the vulnerable host and IDPs community, the high humanitarian needs in Somalia are driven by seasonal floods, severe drought conditions, acute water diarrhea/ cholera outbreaks and protracted crises, exacerbated by COVID-19 outbreak. In May 2021, 50 of the 74 districts in Somalia faced severe water shortages and water prices increased and this is expected to crossover to 2022 with an already delayed Deyr(October-November) rains, Drought remains the main driver of WASH needs in Somalia leading to displacement and communal conflict over water points and the project intends to cover the needs & offer both emergency and long term sustainable solution to avert the potential risk of losing life’s   through the multiple shocks, The WASH response will contribute to increased access to water and sanitation facilities for the vulnerable communities  and prevention of a further increase in AWD/Cholera which is endemic in Somalia , as well as raise awareness to prevent the spread of COVID-19 through risk communication and community engagement, and support compliance to recommended measures through hygiene promotion, hygiene kits distribution and increased access to water and soap.
