project_name: Strengthening and provision of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for conflict-affected populations in Syria
project_objective:
UNFPA will continue to reduce maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality, support IPC during COVID-19, provide family planning (FP) commodities, and provide medical assistance and care to GBV survivors, including CMR. This will be achieved by (1) ensuring the availability of, access to, and utilization of integrated quality SRH services and information for women, men, girls, and boys; (2) building the capacity of health workers and CHWs; (3) reactivating and activating services in areas where no SRH services exist; (4) ensuring availability of essential medical, PPE, and supplies while mitigating COVID-19 and other infection risks; (5) ensuring delivery of complementary comprehensive services, including for MHPSS and non-communicable diseases; and (6) strengthening referral mechanisms and improving national and subnational SRH coordination.
UNFPA will continue to follow the Whole of Syria approach, with implementation from Damascus and cross-border from Turkey, targeting all 14 Syrian governorates. Vulnerable population groups targeted include women and girls of reproductive age, IDPs, host communities, returnees, adolescents, and PwDs.
Key objectives include:
Increasing access to lifesaving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable health services for the most vulnerable and in need persons.
Increasing access to primary healthcare by providing essential primary health services to cover the reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health needs of vulnerable populations and repairing facilities. Improving access to secondary and tertiary healthcare for high risk pregnancy, malnourished pregnant and lactating women (PLW), EmONC cases, and acute cases which cannot access treatment in their area, particularly rural areas.
Supporting access in areas with service gaps through integrated mobile teams and the midwifery network in Aleppo and Deir-ez-Zor.
Building the capacity of health workers and CHWs on health and GBV principles, COVID-19 IPC and treatment, and to address any technical gaps.
Supporting essential infrastructure maintenance and equipment repair and supply to health facilities, in particular for areas of most acute need (directly or through referrals).
Strengthening and consolidating medical supply chains, ensuring availability of safe and quality medicines for essential primary healthcare, IPC supplies and PPE, obstetric care, infectious diseases including HIV to prevent mother-to-child transmission, and FP methods.
Pre-positioning emergency supply stocks of RH kits, medicines, and supplies in line with contingency scenarios for reduced access and increased hostilities.
Strengthening health sector coordination and HIS, emphasizing enhancing protection, increasing access to health services, and continuing coordination within and across hubs, including thorough joint contingency and preparedness planning.
Engaging in activities that support continuity of care, strengthen community resilience, respond to IDP movements and shifts in control, and beneficiaries’ participation in programming.
Supporting resilience through the midwifery schools in NWS and Deir-ez-Zor, and empowering and supporting the full implementation of DHIS2 in NWS and later at the national level.
Adapting, updating, and adopting the national curriculum for non-physician clinicians, including nurses and midwives, with the MoH, and developing training packages for academic and practical training, which can be subject for potential accreditation.
Continuous monitoring of implementation based on the five AAP principles and UNFPA’s global results-based monitoring framework. UNFPA staff or third party monitors and IPs will jointly conduct monthly supervision visits, subject to access and approvals. Standardized tools including the supported services and supervision checklist are used to assess service availability/quality. Clinic registration data will be collated monthly. Beneficiary feedback (complaints box, FGDs, exit interviews) will be collected.

project_name: Enhancing food security and livelihoods of vulnerable people acutely affected by protracted crises in Gaza
project_objective: The action contributes to the third strategic objective of the HRP 2022 as well as the Strategic outcome 1 National plan of the Ministry of Social Development ""MoSD"", by enhancing food security for highly vulnerable population affected by protracted crisis through improving access to diversified, sufficient and nutritious food. The overall objective is to contribute to reduced social and economic risks and vulnerabilities among crises-affected populations of all gender, age and abilities in the Gaza Strip. It will strongly participate to address the huge humanitarian needs in general and food insecurity levels, specifically under two main interventions with strong links between the Humanitarian Assistance and Social Protection. The main outcomes of the action are: (i) Crisis-affected persons of all gender, ages and abilities in the Gaza Strip have equitable and safe access to multi sectorial needs through Multi-Purpose Cash “MPC” and Cash for Work “CfW” modalities.; and (ii) Enhanced social protection for target population through effective coordination and activation of internal / external referral amongst actors in the Gaza Strip. This component will enhance the social protection of the target communities and individuals when having HHs profiles and protection/empowerment plans prepared and implemented. The projects components are: (i) Cash for Work ""CfW"" opportunities for 350 men and women who are members of the most vulnerable HHs directly benefiting (1,925 individuals including 514 women, 517 men, 435 girls and 459 boys, among them 48 PWDs 50%female and 50%male) for 6 months creating a total of 46200 paid working days. The project will target 50 graduates and 300 laborers (65% Men and 35% Women) who will be placed at CSOs, private sector companies and small-scale farms and food manufacturing factories. The participants will be paid average daily wages of 50 ILS (45 for laborers and 55 for graduates) for 22 working days according to the minimum monthly wages of the approved values within the CfW task force (Graduates 1127 ils and laborers 939 ils). (ii) Multi-Purpose cash assistance to 300 HHs directly benefitting (1,650 individuals including 441 women, 445 men, 372 girls and 392 boys, among them 41 PWDs 50% female and 50% male) for a period of 6 months that will improve their food intake and dietary diversity. The cash provided will be adjusted to the family size and based on the approved transfer value of the Cash Working Group “CWG” (1046 ILS/month). The HHs of the worst scores of socioeconomic vulnerabilities with high food insecurity levels and eroded coping capacities, will be selected and higher priority will be given to FHHs, HHs with protection concerns and HHs with members who are older people, chronically ill, or PWDs. Females will be encouraged to enroll to increase the women participation and engagement rates in the labor market. IRW adheres to protection principles and good practices as guided by the humanitarian standards with special focus on accountability to beneficiaries, applying complaint systems, access to assistance with dignity and gender equality. Also, IRW adheres to PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) among its staff, partners’  and hosting institutions through orientation before the start of the project implementation

project_name: Emergency Health Response for the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), Returnees and Host Communities at Wau, Tonj North and Kapoeta East Counties in South Sudan
project_objective: The effects of prolonged violent conflict and limited investment in the country’s infrastructure have taken a heavy toll on availability of, and access to, basic services. The COVID-19 pandemic and climatic conditions exacerbate poverty and general living standards for many South Sudanese. The country’s health system and infrastructure are among the poorest in the world. Health facilities are poorly equipped and staffed. There is a severe shortage of trained health professionals in all categories. Thus, people rely on inadequately trained or low skilled health workers to provide their healthcare. A quarter of internally displaced and returnees reside in settlements further than 5km from a functional health facility (South Sudan HNO 2022). Approximately more than half of the country’s 2,300 health facilities are non-functional. Nearly 60 per cent of the functioning health facilities are supported by humanitarian and development organizations but many of them are close to displacement sites and returnee settlements and may not be easily accessible by established communities. Health facilities in some locations were reported to be closed due to violence and flooding, for example in Tonj North. The response design focuses on providing lifesaving essential health services in line with national and international humanitarian standards, and is based on the epidemiological profile of disease outbreaks, disease burden seasonality, and trauma-related emergency requirements. Prevention, preparedness, response readiness, response, and mitigation activities will be undertaken with special attention given to providing vulnerable groups including women, children and persons with disabilities. IRW in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and partners will support different intervention modalities suited to the needs of affected people, including COVID-19 control and prevention interventions. Islamic Relief will continue prevention, preparedness, and response readiness activities addressing COVID 19 IRWSS will further support static and mobile health facilities, and community-based healthcare systems to serve communities who do not have access to health care facilities and are affected by emergencies. Additionally, IRWSS plans to further strengthen health cluster technical, operational and field coordination support to partners and authorities. IRWSS will continue to collaborate with development partners who are providing regular health services through static health facilities in crisis-affected areas by identifying communities that are still not reachable and providing services through mobile outreach as well as strengthening support to static health facilities. Improved access to essential health services will contribute to the overall reduction of the high maternal mortality rates and under-five mortality rates and mitigate the transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases and other infectious diseases. IRWSS will involve affected communities and county health system (implementing national health promotion, prevention, and control programs) in planning and organizing emergency health services. The cluster coordination mechanism at the national and state level will be utilized to coordinate, collaborate, liaise with partners and authorities to implement, monitor, and review the response activities. Referral pathways for mental health and psychosocial support, GBV survivors, and for maternal and child health emergencies will be streamlined and strengthened. Referral pathways will link the community and facility-based health care system to provide continuity of care. To protect both the patient and health staff, IRWSS will encourage and support infection prevention and control (IPC) and WASH measures including COVID-19 appropriate prevention and management activities. The Inter-cluster coordination mechanism at all levels will work towards comprehensive integration and collaboration with other clusters, including FSL, WASH etc.

project_name: Réponses aux Crises conçues, gérées et mises en oeuvre par les Survivants et les Communautés au Centre du Mali (SCLR-Pilote)
project_objective:
Basé sur la reconnaissance du fait que les communautés affectées par les crises sont toujours les ""premiers répondants"", le projet proposé pilotera la méthoodologie de l'initiative ""Local to Global"" (du local vers le global, ou ""L2GP"") qui se nomme ""réponses aux crises menées par les survivants et les communautés"" (survivor and community-led crisis response, ou ""SCLR""). Il soutiendra les communautés ciblées de Bankass dans la définition, la planification et l'implémentation de leurs prores réponses à des crises, spontanées ou récurrentes, à petite ou grande échelle. 

La méthodologie SCLR est, par nature, très flexible et adaptable compte tenu de sa nature participative qui vise à autonomiser les communautés dans l'évaluation et la priorisation des risques auxquels ils font face et de leurs besoins, tout en leur fournissant des ressources et le soutien nécessaire pour qu'ils puissent implémenter des réponses dans l'intérêt général de leurs communautés. L'approche se concentre sur le transfert de pouvoir et de possibilité d'action des bailleurs internationaux et des organisations humanitaires envers les individus, groupes et communautés affectés par les crises, afin qu'ils obtiennent des réponses efficientes, rapides et adaptées à leurs besoins. Le processus SCLR est structuré autour de 16 étapes clés pour atteindre cet objectif. 

Dans le cadre de ce projet, DCA mènera les ateliers de formation, et AAPPOR facilitera les étapes SCLR auprès des groupes communautaires. AAPPOR est un partenaire de longue date de DCA depuis 2016 est spécialisé dans la protection, les moyens de subsistance et l'adaptation au changement climatique, notamment dans la région de Mopti et du cercle de Bankass. En tant qu'organisation facilitatrice, AAPPOR servira de point focal pour les groupes communautaires de Bankass tout au long du processus. DCA et AAPPOR fourniront des formations techniques aux comités communautaires sur la gestion de subventions, le rapportage narratif et financier. Les comités seront appuyés pour développer des propositions de projet, en lien avec les besoins recensés et priorisés, qu'ils soumettront afin d'obtenir des subventions. Les propositions de projet seront sélectionnées par le biais d'un processus communautaire et seront subventionnés par des ""micro-fonds"" déboursés par AAPPOR et suivis tout au long de leur implémentation.

Le projet permettra ainsi d'autonomiser les communautés dans la gestion de crises, et les appuiera à la mise en lien avec les acteurs de financement humanitaires et de développement. Il visera dans un premier temps 10 localités de Bankass dans sa première année, avant de démultiplier l'approche et l'étendre sur d'autres localités dans sa seconde année d'implémentation.

project_name: Protective presence and documentation of IHL & IHRL violations
project_objective:
The project’s aims are i) to offer protective presence to vulnerable communities in Palestine living under the occupation, ii) to monitor and report on human rights violations, iii) to support Palestinian and Israeli peace groups, and iv) to advocate for policy change to end the military occupation of Palestine. The Protective Presence that The Ecumenical Accompaniment Programme in Palestine and Israel (EAPPI) is providing contributes to creating a safer environment for women and men to address their own needs, to solve their own conflicts and to protect vulnerable individuals (women, men, and children) and communities. The project´s aim is to ensure a continuation of the Ecumenical Accompaniers (EAs) presence in the most vulnerable areas of the West Bank to deter violence, document violations of international laws and regulations, and gather information for international advocacy work to raise awareness amongst the international community and duty bearers with regards to the current situation in Palestine and the violations of IHL and IHRL, pursuing the vision of a just peace with freedom, equal rights, dignity, and security based on international law.
If EAs are unable to be present on the ground due to restriction of movements, the Jerusalem Office staff will be in close contact with the communities through the local contacts by phone calls to document the IHL & IHRL violations and share the incidents with UN agencies and other local partners. In addition, the EAPPI on an HQ level will conduct advocacy campaigns related to violations of human rights.

project_name: Projet d’assistance alimentaire d’urgence et protection des moyens d’existence des ménages affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions du Centre Nord et du Sahel.
project_objective:
Depuis Avril 2015 le contexte sécuritaire au Burkina se dégrade de plus en plus et cela, du fait des multiples attaques et menaces perpétrées par des groupes armés non étatique (GANE). Selon ACLED, les incidents sécuritaires sont passés de 86 en 2015 à 1547 en septembre 2021 soit une augmentation de plus 1000%. Cette situation a créé une crise humanitaire sans précédent avec des perspectives assez pessimistes au regard de l’évolution du contexte marqué par les principaux facteurs à savoir :
 (I) l’insécurité et la prolifération de plus en plus inquiétante des GANE principalement dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, de l’Est et de la Boucle du Mouhoun qui entrainent des morts d’hommes, des déplacements massifs de population civile ; 
(ii) une crise alimentaire devenue chronique sur fond d’une situation de pauvreté structurelle pour laquelle le gouvernement Burkinabè a du mal à trouver une réponse structurante. Les moyens de subsistance des populations déplacées subissent une forte pression, ce qui impacte leur mode de vie et entraine le développement de stratégies d’adaptation compromettantes pour ces ressources. Du fait de l’insécurité, les populations vivant dans les zones affectées par la crise souffrent des restrictions d’accès à la terre pour la conduite des activités agro-sylvo-pastorales , 
En outre, on assiste à un déficit d’approvisionnement ainsi qu’une augmentation significative des prix des denrées dans plusieurs localités des régions du Sahel et du Centre Nord qui affecte les capacités d’accès à la nourriture aux ménages vulnérables.
Le cadre harmonisé (CH) de Novembre 2021 estime la population ayant besoin d’une assistance immédiate (Phase 3 à 5) à 1 645 939 personnes en situation courante. Ces populations qui représentent 12% de la population totale analysée sont concentrées dans les régions du Centre-Nord (25%), du Sahel (21%), de l’Est (19%), du Nord (14%) et de la Boucle du Mouhoun (5%). Elles sont constituées en partie de populations déplacées à cause de l’insécurité civile qui les a contraints à abandonner leurs terres de culture, leurs bétails et autres moyens d’existence.

project_name: Management of S-NFI Pipeline to Strengthen S-NFI Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe and Appropriate Shelter and NFI Solutions
project_objective:
Conflict, sub-national violence and heavy seasonal flooding continues to cause internal displacement in South Sudan leaving 2.4 million of its population impacted through destruction of housing and loss of essential household goods. The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving supplies continues to be the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2011, IOM has been successfully managing the shelter and non-food items (S-NFI) Core Pipeline, which is an essential support to the S-NFI Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2022, IOM will maintain its commitment to support the S-NFI Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key shelter and NFI supplies to benefit a total of 886,254 people in need in South Sudan. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Rumbek, and Wau to ensure response efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks.

project_name: Management of WASH Pipeline to Strengthen WASH Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe Water; Sanitation and Hygiene Supplies
project_objective:
According to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, about 6.6 million people has inadequate or lack of access to safe water, and sanitation in South Sudan. Insecurity, displacement, natural disasters such as heavy flooding for the last three years have compounded the impact of low access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services in the country. The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving WASH supplies continues to be one of the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2014, IOM has been successfully managing a portion of the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Core Pipeline, which is an essential support to the WASH Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2022, IOM will maintain its commitment support the WASH Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key WASH supplies to benefit a total of 1.2 million people in need. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Rumbek, and Wau to ensure efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, malnutrition, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks.

project_name: Targeted support to persons with specific needs with lifesaving non-food items and emergency shelter to displaced population in hard-to-reach areas and IDP returnee families
project_objective:
In 2022, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) continue to face multi-faceted crises which are worsened by conflict, floods, impacts of COVID – 19 pandemic, and protracted displacement from locations of their habitual residence. Displaced families often have inadequate shelter and household goods which expose them to heightened protection risks. Increased mobility, continued insecurity and protracted displacement has over the years eroded household coping mechanisms and livelihood options especially considering the poor nature of local markets without stocks for household goods and shelter materials. 

UNHCR’s project will focus on responding to the humanitarian needs of IDPs and IDP and refugee returnees with targeted and protection focused core relief items (emergency shelter and non-food items – S/NFIs) prioritizing the most vulnerable households and persons with specific needs especially women and girls.

The project will contribute to the following sectoral objectives:
SO 1 – percentage of the targeted population that is able to access shelter material and non-food items in situations of emergency and transition.
The project will identify the most vulnerable IDPs and returnees through protection monitoring and assessments including through IRNAs and RRMs. The assessments and inter cluster discussions will inform the decisions regarding the specific response modalities between in kind and cash assistance. Unique contextual factors including market conditions will be considered. 

SO 2 - Enhance community dignity and engagement in the provision of S/NFI services.
The project will deliver timely lifesaving activities while streamlining protection-oriented initiatives including COVID – 19 preventive measures. The project will strengthen community-based protection through the involvement of community based structures for self-management in response delivery, ensuring that their capacities to cope, recover, contribute to and achieve solutions are enhanced.

SO 3 - Community members’ exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures.
In 2022, UNHCR will increase its active participation in humanitarian coordination forums including the ES/NFI cluster both at national level and in the field, strongly advocating for protection mainstreaming and joint vulnerability assessments, the results of which will be very useful in the optimization of the limited resources. UNHCR will endeavor to provide timely response to the most critical identified needs of vulnerable IDPs and returnees, among other affected populations. Protection risks remain high among women, girls, boys and persons with specific protection needs which may include transitional shelters and other material assistance.

project_name: Appui d’urgence à la production agro-pastorale et Protection des moyens d’existence des personnes vulnérables affectées par la crise sécuritaire et les chocs climatiques au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso continue toujours de faire face à trois crises complexes d’ordres sécuritaire, climatique et sanitaire. Depuis 2015, le pays est en proie à une insécurité grandissante, suite aux attaques récurrentes perpétrées par des groupes armés non-étatiques qui profitent de la vulnérabilité des populations rurales pour les terroriser et piller leurs biens. Ces groupes armés non identifiés enrôlent ainsi les jeunes en leur promettant une meilleure qualité de vie et des revenus générés par les trafics illicites. A cause de ces nouvelles tensions, des conflits intercommunautaires ont aussi explosé dus entre autres à la compétition pour l’accès aux ressources naturelles déjà sous forte pression, mais aussi à la stigmatisation de certains groupes communautaires qui sont assimilés ou accusés d’être de connivence avec les groupes armés non-étatiques. Cette situation se caractérise de nos jours par une aggravation de la crise sécuritaire et des déplacements massifs de populations qui ont engendré à nouveau d’immenses besoins humanitaires et des défis substantiels pour le pays. En effet, le nombre de Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDIs), selon le Gouvernement est passé de 486 360 à la date du 6 octobre 2019 à 978 744 au 9 juillet 2020 puis à 1 481 000 personnes en Décembre 2021 soit une augmentation respective de 201,23% et 300% au cours des mêmes périodes. Toutes ces populations, plus particulièrement les femmes et les jeunes qui souffraient déjà d’un manque d’opportunités pour protéger et diversifier leurs moyens d’existence constatent impuissamment la détérioration fulgurante de leurs moyens d’existence. Par ailleurs, l’analyse du Cadre Harmonisé (version 2.0) en Novembre 2021 indique en phase projetée environ 2,6 millions de personnes en insécurité alimentaire, dont plus de 500 000 personnes en urgence alimentaire. En plus des déplacements massifs et continus de populations dus à l'insécurité, le Burkina Faso n’échappe pas aux effets de la pandémie de coronavirus (COVID-19) depuis le 09 mars 2020 avec plus de 15 514 personnes touchées et 265 décès selon le Gouvernement à la date du 14 novembre 2021 et dont les mesures de protection ont également fortement affecté l’économie. 
La stratégie de la FAO en réponse à cette crise est de répondre rapidement aux besoins humanitaires des populations vulnérables directement touchées par l’insécurité avec deux types d’interventions spécifiques : 
1) Réponse rapide des personnes touchées par le déplacement en leur fournissant une aide financière polyvalente pour leur permettre de couvrir leurs besoins humanitaires urgents et 2) renforcer les activités de protection et de réhabilitation des moyens de subsistance.
Face à cette problématique de sécurité alimentaire, la stratégie de la FAO face à a pour objectif de répondre de manière rapide aux besoins humanitaires des populations vulnérables, directement affectées par l’insécurité à travers d’une part des activités d’assistance rapide, de protection et réhabilitation des moyens d’existence et d’autre part la mise en place de mécanisme de collecte et d’analyse des données agro-sylvo pastoraux et d’alerte précoce afin de mieux coordonnées les Interventions. 
Ainsi, le projet devra permettre d’atteindre le résultat ci-après : - Protéger et renforcer les moyens de subsistance des populations vulnérables par l’appui et la distribution d’intrants agricoles pour la production agricole, le déstockage des troupeaux dans les zones à risque de surpâturage et soutien à la santé animale et pastorale.
Le projet sera mis en œuvre dans les Régions du Sahel du Nord, de l’Est et du Centre-Nord, Cascades et du Centre-Nord le ciblage prendra en compte l’aspect genre dans les activités avec plus de 40% pour les femmes et 60% homme pour toutes les activités de production agro-pastorales.

project_name: Renforcer les interventions de prévention, d’atténuation des risques et de réponse à la violence basée sur le genre et l’accès des personnes survivantes, des femmes et des filles à risque de VBG.
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer les services qui sauvent les vies des survivantes, des femmes et des filles à risques de VBG par l’adaptation et le renforcement de la disponibilité et de la qualité des services, de prévention, de mitigation des risques. Les survivantes de violence basée sur le genre auront accès à des soins de santé adaptés, y compris des services de santé pour les survivantes de violences sexuelles et conjugales et d’autres formes de VBG. Des services d’orientation pour prévenir et/ou réduire les effets de la violence seront fournis par les prestataires de santé étant donné qu’ils sont souvent les premiers et parfois le seul point de contact avec les survivantes. Cela se fera à travers une bonne coordination et un soutien à la continuité de l’offre des services de santé de prise en charge des violences sexuelles et les autres formes de VBG. A cet effet, en collaboration avec les districts sanitaires des Régions ciblés par le projet, un paquet d’activité sera déroulé afin de fournir une prise en charge de qualité aux survivantes de VBG. Des kits post viol seront mis à la disposition des districts sanitaires des localités cibles du projet pour répartition dans les Centres de Santé de Promotion Sociale (CSPS) et des cliniques mobiles afin de garantir l’accès aux kits à toutes les survivantes. Les prestataires de santé seront formés sur la gestion clinique des cas de viol y compris la prise en charge médicale des enfants survivant-e-s de viol et le soutien de première ligne.
 Le soutien psychosocial étant une étape primordiale dans la prise en charge des cas de VBG, ce service sera intégré à l’offre de service médical par la mise à disposition des centres de santé des travailleurs sociaux, préalablement formés sur le soutien psychosocial y compris la gestion des cas de VBG. Ces travailleurs sociaux bénéficieront de matériels permettant la mise en œuvre de la gestion des cas de VBG à distance (téléphone, smartphone, crédit de communication…). Ainsi, les survivantes auront accès à des services de gestion de cas appropriés et de qualité. L’accompagnement des survivantes par les travailleurs sociaux sera essentiellement basé sur l’approche axée sur les survivantes et ces principes directeurs. 
Le projet préconise et soutient l’intégration de l’atténuation des risques de violence basée sur le genre. Le numéro vert de dénonciation des cas de VBG et d’orientation des survivantes vers les services de prise en charge sera renforcé. Les agents de la ligne verte seront formés sur la prise en charge des cas d’abus et d’exploitation sexuels. La ligne verte permettra aux femmes et aux filles de briser le silence face aux actes d’abus et d’exploitation sexuels. Des stratégies communautaires seront développées pour surveiller en toute sécurité et combattre les risques liés à la VBG et inscrire une tolérance zéro à l’exploitation et aux abus sexuels et leur dénonciation dans les messages communautaires de sensibilisation. A cet effet, des messages clés sur la prévention et la mitigation des risques de VBG y compris la Prévention contre l’Exploitation et l’Abus Sexuels seront conçus avec l’implication et la participation des bénéficiaires et diffusés régulièrement au sein de la communauté. Un plaidoyer encourageant l’élaboration, l’adoption et l’application de codes de conduite interdisant toutes les formes d’exploitation et d’abus sexuels sera mené auprès des partenaires de mise en œuvre ainsi que les acteurs des différents secteurs humanitaires. 
Pour permettre aux femmes et aux filles de préserver leur dignité, des lampes et kits de dignité leur seront distribués dans les zones d’intervention du projet.
Des espaces sûrs à l’usage des femmes et des filles seront installés dans les sites d’accueil temporaire et au sein de la population hôte, afin que les survivantes de VBG, les femmes et les filles à risque puissent accéder en toute sécurité à l’information et à l’orientation vers les services de prise en charge.

project_name: Respuesta nutricional para prevención y tratamiento de Desnutrición Aguda en población materno-infantil en departamentos de la zona Norte de Honduras
project_objective:
Acción contra el Hambre (ACH) cuenta con experiencia en la implementación de proyectos en diversas áreas rurales en el ámbito de acceso al agua potable, el saneamiento y la higiene; nutrición, seguridad alimentaria, gestión de riesgos y atención y respuesta a emergencias. Acción contra el Hambre centra su trabajo en mejorar las condiciones de vida de familias vulnerables afectadas por la situación de crisis humanitaria como consecuencia de los diferentes fenómenos climáticos (sequía, el impacto de los huracanes, inundaciones asociadas), la situación de violencia generalizada, entre múltiples amenazas y en consecuencia el hambre.
La propuesta de proyecto “Respuesta nutricional para prevención y tratamiento de Desnutrición Aguda en población materno-infantil en departamentos de la zona Norte de Honduras” se enfoca en el manejo ambulatorio, la prevención, tratamiento y atención de la desnutrición aguda en niñas y niños menores de cinco años, mujeres embarazadas y en período de lactancia, mediante la mejora de la vigilancia y el tratamiento nutricional, fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal institucional de salud por medio de formaciones sobre el uso de los protocolos nacionales simplificados de manejo de la desnutrición aguda (utilización de cintas MUAC y estándares de crecimiento, específicamente peso para la talla) y entrega de equipamiento e insumos para los establecimientos de salud (equipo médico, antropométrico, micronutrientes y alimentos terapéuticos listos para consumo); así mismo, propone el fortalecimiento de capacidades de voluntarios comunitarios (agentes de cambio) para la identificación temprana y oportuna de niños y niñas con desnutrición aguda, sensibilización a familias sobre prácticas adecuadas de alimentación, nutrición e higiene infantil, promover la utilización de la metodología Family MUAC y dar soporte nutricional a través de la metodología de Escuelas de Campo de Seguridad Alimentaria Nutricional (ECASAN) incluyendo el enfoque de desviación positiva, en estos espacios se promueven prácticas de alimentación y cuidado infantil e higiene para la mejora de prácticas de cuidado del niño y niña pequeños, a través de la metodología aprender haciendo. También se propone brindar soporte con alimento complementario a niños y niñas menores de 5 años, mujeres embarazadas y/o en período de lactancia que se encuentren en riesgo de padecer desnutrición , para mejorar su estado nutricional.
Estas intervenciones se planifican llevar a cabo en tres departamentos de Honduras: Cortés, Yoro y Atlántida.

project_name: Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela.
project_objective: Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

project_name: Improving Food Security and Livelihoods and Building Resilience of Vulnerable IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable Hosting and Resident communities, in Sudan
project_objective:
The project will provide emergency agriculture and livestock-based livelihoods interventions and resilience building support for vulnerable farmers, agro- pastoral and pastoral IDPs, returnees, hosting and resident communities in Sudan.
The vulnerability the target populations stems from the protracted crisis, the ongoing economic hardships at the macro and micro-levels, long dry spells and foods. The situation was aggravated with the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic; the lockdown measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19 significantly decreased commodity movement, market function and cross-border trade, and compromised livelihoods and daily labor opportunities. This situation has led to high rates of acute and chronic food insecurity and malnutrition. FAO prioritized in a participatory manner 81 localities in the 14 states based on the high degree of vulnerability to food insecurity and malnutrition (Phase 3 and above).
FAO project targets 2,000,000 people among the most vulnerable communities including 800,000 IDPs, 600,000 returnees and hosting communities and 600,000 vulnerable residents. The interventions benefit 620,000 women, 400,000 girls (less than 18 year of age), 580,000 men and 400,000 boys (less than 18 year of age). The selection of the proposed interventions based on the basic and specific needs of the beneficiaries taking into account the factors of age and gender. The project will target about 180,000 elderly people among the adult population including persons with disabilities.
The project interventions include as a top priority, Supporting food insecure people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance through agricultural assistance including crop, livestock and veterinary inputs and extension services targeting 2,000,000 people. This will include as well, building the capacity of local communities, governmental institutions and sector partners to improve preparedness and response for new emergencies. The second priority is provide assistance for building self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating to cope with current and future shocks and stresses. Agricultural production will be improved through provision of climate-smart crop production, livestock and veterinary inputs and support to services. Similarly, small-scale farmers will be targeted for reducing food losses and strengthened post-harvest techniques through improved food and crop storage and processing facilities. On and off farm livelihood assistance will be diversified, managed, and coordinated to respond to food chain threats including animal and plant pests specially locust; In addition, communities will be involved in building, restoring and maintaining productive assets through multipurpose cash support. About 300,000 people will be targeted for multipurpose cash transfer support in collaboration with Cash Working Group (CWG). The response will consider prevailing market conditions, availability of financial services and agricultural and livestock inputs prices in the markets; the preferences of the affected population; cultural and gender dynamics; accessibility, safety and security of beneficiaries. Accountability to affected populations and environmental concerns will be mainstreamed into the proposed activities, also risk to GBV will be taken into consideration and application of the PSEA measures in will be applied in collaboration with sister UN agencies.

project_name: Emergency WASH response for drought affected communities at Borena Zone, Oromia Region, Ethiopia
project_objective:
As a result of the failure of the last two consecutive rainy seasons in Borena Zone, critical water shortage occurred and hampered the live and livelihood of the pastoralist communities. 
To alleviate this problem, ANE will work to increase access to safe water supply by performing major activities like rehabilitation of non-functional water schemes and provide water through trucking. Construction of communal latrines will be done to increase access to improved sanitation facilities and basic WASH NFIs will be provided for the most vulnerable HHs so that they will improve their HH level hygienic practices and coupling with the intensive hygiene promotion activities that basically planned to improve knowledge and practice of improved behavior. 
In general, the proposed set of sectoral WASH activities will ease water, sanitation and hygiene related problems among the targeted drought affected pastoralist communities in Borena Zone; so that the mortality and morbidity rate associated with WASH related diseases and risks will be reduced.

project_name: Agricultural Seed Activity Project (ASAP) II
project_objective:
Over the past three years, intercommunal conflict and extreme climate variability and shocks have displaced tens of millions of people in Ethiopia. In the Oromia, Somali and Southern Nations, Nationalities and People’s (SNNP) Regions there are over 1.1 million people in need . As the conflict subsides, the government continues to force IDP’s to return to their former homes, but in the haste of this operation, most return to their communities with few belongings and no productive assets. The provision of seed vouchers alongside basic agricultural advice, for major staple crops (e.g., wheat, tef, OPV maize, sorghum), pulses (e.g., haricot beans) and cash for nutritious vegetable seeds and/or other needed agricultural inputs are essential for the IDP returnees to provide a rapid restart to food production, diversify production for improved consumption and strengthen livelihoods for income generation. 

To support both vulnerable farmers and IDP returnees  Catholic Relief Services (CRS) and our local partners built on the effective response of the first phase of this project funded by USAID/BHA, the Agricultural Seed Activity Project (ASAP) in Oromia Somali, and SNNP by scaling up the cash and voucher-based seed response to benefit farming households who are vulnerable to acute seed insecurity caused by conflict and acute environmental shocks. The purpose of the project is to improve agricultural production through the provision of agricultural inputs (seeds), training in good agricultural practices and links to input suppliers by reaching out to 97,392 beneficiary households.

project_name: Agricultural recovery for drought and conflict affected multiregional community in Ethiopia
project_objective:
The different assessment findings and situational updates of different regions in Ethiopia indicated that the food insecurity situation severely affected. The crop production and productivity become deteriorated and the livestock and crop sectors as well lack of animal health service and feed shortage. Almost in all targeted woredas of the regions the veterinary services are out of function due to lack of veterinary drugs and equipment’s.  
Drought and conflict impacted the community through the depletion of assets such as disruption of crop harvesting season, looting and destruction of household properties. Farmers lost their animals, lost matured crop in the field, living houses destructed, and alternative livelihood assets destroyed due to the conflict. In addition to the private properties, service providing government offices such as veterinary clinics were destroyed during the conflict. Reports showed malnutrition rates remained critically high in all regions in February and March 2022. Further deterioration is expected as the delayed Belg rain disrupts the planting season.
Though this humanitarian assistance is essential to save life and to protect the livelihood of the crises affected communities. For smallholder farmers who rely on subsistence farming, timely assistance will allow them to continue to grow their own food, secure income, take advantage of local economic opportunities and make them rely on less humanitarian and government assistance. GOAL sees that the recovery intervention of agriculture is indisputable in which the effect such activities will improve food and nutrition security of HHs and at the production phase it will boost the local market as well as increases income and employment opportunity.
Therefore, unless urgent recovery actions taken the HHs will face chronic food insecurity and remain waiting external food aid. This is unachievable and undesirable. Thus, the restoration of affected populations agriculture and other off farm livelihoods is unquestionable. Therefore, the recovery of livestock resource would have a multiple effect such as improved nutrition, income, employment, and boost the crop production. GOAL Ethiopia has geographical presence in regions of the target woredas where Nutrition, WASH, Health, and protection sector projects actively implemented with integration to complement each other. GOAL has strong and good partnership with the local communities and with the existing governance system.
The affected community will be supported by crop seeds including vegetables, pulses, cereals, MPC labeled for agricultural inputs, and livestock services to ensure adequate animal fodder and veterinary services. Cash will be used as the preferred modality to provide this agricultural support to help farmers/pastoralist/agropastoral to purchase agricultural/livestock inputs like livestock feed and water based on the functionality of local markets.
GOAL has operations established across the targeted woredas in other thematic interventions, and office and logistical capacity already established. By leveraging existing presence and staff we can ensure a cost-effective response. GOAL has strong targeting, verification, and accountability mechanisms institutionalized across all our responses. We have been a key partner with various donors, including EHF on agriculture interventions. We have long been working with vulnerable groups all over the country and have extensive experience with cash, seed, and agriculture interventions. Proposed interventions under this project are in line with the EHF allocation strategy and priority as well as they are need based and the selected interventions under this project are responsive to the prioritized activities of the agriculture sectoral plans.
GOAL will consider environment and climate changes in its intervention so that natural resources will be protected from any unintended consequences.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition Response for Drought affected and Displaced Communities in Oromia and Somali Regions
project_objective:
The drought emergency in Somalia and Oromia regions has intensified. About 572,700 people have been displaced internally by drought  between October 2021  and  February 2022, more than double the 259,500   people displaced during the same period in 2016/17.

The project will respond to the Nutrition needs among vulnerable communities which have been exacerbated due to drought and displacement.  
A Nutrition response consisting of Community based management of acute malnutrition (Outpatient therapeutic feeding, Stabilization center, Management of Moderate Acute malnutrition, and Community mobilization), support to strengthening and establishment of OTP and SC at Health facilities, provision of logistical and technical support in conflict affected Woredas with high levels of IDPs and returnees without access to free nutrition care. The project activities will reduce malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable groups through timely capacity building, functioning of OTP and SC at health facilities and strengthening management of acute malnutrition systems by delivering Nutrition and medical supplies and materials for the targeted Conflict affected Woredas in Oromia and Somali Regions.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Nonfood Items responses to Drought affected households in Oromia and Somali Regions
project_objective:
As of February 2022, a total of 4.51 million IDPs have been identified thus far across the country. Of the total displaced population, the main causes of displacement were conflict which displaced 3.63 million IDPs (81%), drought which displaced 420,887 IDPs (9%), social tension which displaced 171,727 IDPs (4%), seasonal floods which displaced 122,901 IDPs (3%) and flash floods which displaced 119,807 IDPs (3%). Through Site Assessment round 28 (Dec 2021-Jan 2022), 2.06 million IDPs were identified in 1,440 IDP sites across 9 regions in Ethiopia. Notably, there was a +37% increase in the number of droughts IDPs this round due to the intensifying drought, especially in Afder, Dawa, Dollo and Liban zones in Somali region and West Guji zone in Oromia region. 
In terms of people affected by the drought, the Somali region is the most affected with more than 3.5 million people, followed by Oromia (more than 3.4 million), SNNP (more than 1,1 million), Southwest (more than 200,000 people) regions. Overall, at least 286,000 people have been displaced by drought between October 2021 and March 2022 across the drought-affected areas (183,000+ in Somali, 103.000 in Oromia). 
According to the ESNFI cluster, peoples in need in the proposed locations such as Arero Woreda (1,469), Guchi Woreda (4,261), Kumbi Woreda (2,531), Moyale (OR) Woreda (3,539), Siraro Woreda (1,660) and Moyale (SM) Woreda (10,785) are residing in extremely poor conditions who need urgent emergency shelter and NFI assistance. IDPs are living across all woredas except Arero woreda whereas returnees are found in Arero and Moyale (SM) woredas.
GE assumes the project activities addresses the strategic objectives with significant positive impact on the identified needs of the respective clusters. The project activities are all a priority to the respective sectors. GE aims an in-kind or cash for non-food items assistance for IDPs and shelter repair kit assistance for returnees. To maximize the impact on the intervention, GOAL proposed this ESNFI standalone applications whereby the other GOAL Ethiopia projects are implemented with the same sectors with BHA, ECHO, UNICEF, and IA funding sources and/or proposed for standalone allocation with other sector applications in this EHF/HPC. During implementation phase GOAL easily will do rapid assessments to determine the actual needs in the proposed locations. 
The ESNFI proposed interventions for this HPC will be.
	Emergency shelter repair kits distribution for 1,100 HHs returnees (1,000 Arero woreda and 100 Moyale (SM) woreda).
	Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V2 Lowlands- Drought Response) distribution for 10,510 HHs IDPs (3,622 Guchi, 3,008 Moyale (OR) & 3,880 Moyale (SM)).
	Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V2 Disable Lowlands- Drought Response) distribution for 1,753 HHs IDPs (639 Guchi, 531 Moyale (OR) & 583 Moyale (SM)).
	Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V2 Highland - Drought Response) distribution for 3,562 HHs IDPs (2,151 Guchi & 1,411 Siraro).
	Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V2 Disable Highlands- Drought Response) distribution for 629   HHs IDPs (380 Kumbi & 249 Siraro).
	Conduct independent beneficiary identification and verification process based on revised SOPs considering national/regional cluster standards.
	Information sessions, establishment and roll-out of community response & feedback mechanisms.
	Conduct HLP assessment.
	Conduct regular joint and independent monitoring. 
	Conduct post distribution monitoring.

project_name: ESNFI and shelter repair kit response for Conflict-affected HHs in Legambo, Harbu town and Harbu/Jara, South and North Wello, Amhara
project_objective:
(Proposed project)
In the second half of 2021, armed conflict significantly increased the number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the Amhara region with high displacement figures especially in South Wello and North Wello.  The IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix published on 31 December 2021 indicates that displacement in Amhara region reached 1.4 million IDPs in early December 2021. Per the regional cluster assessment, large scale return movements starting in mid-December 2021 on wards have resulted in the return of an estimated 480,401 IDPs in South Wello and North Shewa zones. According to the preliminary assessment conducted by ESNFI sub cluster members and CRS emergency in the mid-week of March 2022, new IDPs are arriving in the Amhara region's border areas as a result of the ongoing conflict, and the Ethiopian government has relocated more than 10,000 IDPs to the Jara site as of March 22, 2022. Over 58,000 IDPs are expected to be  relocated to the same place by the government as per the Amhara sub-national cluster.  

In response CRS is proposing to address needs of of conflict-affected HHs through ESNFI and repair kit at Legambo and Harbu town in South Wollo and and Harbu/Jara in North Wello, Amhara Region. Legambo and Habru/Jara will be targeted for IDP/returnee responses and Harbu town will be targeted for IDP responses only. For returnee CRS will consider cash for labor while distributing shelter repair kits based on findings of a market assessment. 

CRS is targeting a total of 35,440 individuals (7,876 HH) across the three woredas with the following support: 
- 19,318 IDP individual (4,293HHs) will receive ESNFI V2 kits budgeted at $140. 
- 5,316 non-displaced individuals (1,181HHs) will receive ESNFI V2 kits budgeted at $140. 
- 5,316 disabled individuals (1,181 HHs) will receive ESNFI V2-Disable kits budgeted at $182. 
- 5,490 returnee individuals (1,220 HHs) will receive shelter repair kits.

project_name: Improving analysis and needs assessments capacities in crisis affected areas of Ethiopia
project_objective:
Ethiopia is grappling with multiple ongoing crises in a year of unprecedented emergencies and humanitarian needs. The country has experienced chronic internal displacement due to drought and flooding, and has also seen a steep rise in inter-communal conflict-related internal displacement since 2018, against a backdrop of significant political change. The military conflict in the Tigray region, which began in November 2020, has caused additional forced displacement and led to social tensions in other parts of the country. 
There is a prevailing need for accurate and up to date information that allows humanitarian actors to tailor their planning to the beneficiaries' needs. Indeed, the complex and dynamic nature of the crisis has been requiring a strong and effective humanitarian coordination supported by accurate information management services. Additionally, since the HRP review and the new  crisis in Tigray and Metekel zone (among others), the scale of the humanitarian needs has increased, requiring sustained information management services to the humanitarian coordination bodies and actors specifically regarding needs assessments efforts. 
This project aims at providing the humanitarian ecosystem with IM support to coordinated and joint assessments as well as at providing them with Humanitarian Situation Analysis Reports focusing on each crisis-affected area in Ethiopia. In addition, this project will strengthen the coordination capacity related to the protection cluster through dedicated IM support. Through this project and these activities, the analysis, needs assessments and coordination capacities will be strengthened in order to enhance the response capacity of the humanitarian actors.

project_name: Emergency Shelter, NFI and Protection Assistance to Vulnerable Households in Tigray
Provide food assistance to vulnerable migrants in urban settings in Libya
project_objective:
Due to a lack of access, transparency, the difficulties to monitor, and given that, according to international law, individuals under detention in a country must be provided with the means to live with dignity by the government of this country, WFP, along with the partners of the Food Security Sector, took the decision not to intervene in detention in order not to legitimize detention and provide assistance blindly where access and monitoring is impossible.

Consequently, alternative forms of assistance to vulnerable migrants have been developed and this project, targeting food insecure migrants outside detention centers, has been designed to support the food security and nutrition status of migrants while preserving them from any form of exposure, stigmatization and discriminations, ensuring their protection and promoting their inclusion within the local communities.

WFP and IOM have built their functioning partnership since November 2019 to provide food assistance to vulnerable migrants in Libya based on analyzed data. The most food insecure non-detained migrants were identified in close partnership with IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Unit and Migrant Resource and Response Mechanism (MRRM) Unit. Based on the built success, under the 2022 HRP - Food Security Sector, WFP is looking to continuously work with IOM to maximise the impacts, outputs and outcomes of the food assistance project for vulnerable non-detained migrant individuals in urban settings.

COVID-19 precautionary measures such as masks, disinfection, social distancing, temperature checks will be systematically applied to the distribution. 

To enhance the quality and the impact of the assistance, building on the successful collaboration between IOM and WFP, including WFP-IOM joint-publication on Migrant Food Security in Libya, WFP looks to strengthen the collaboration with IOM in a joint analysis of IOM's face-to-face flow monitoring surveys on food security WFP’s web-based Migration Pulse surveys.  Over half of migrants reported having been worried about not having enough food to eat. Results from face-to-face interviews showed that a third of migrants were found to have poor and borderline food consumption, compared to 12 per cent of Libyan citizens. Similarly, web-based surveys found that 33 per cent of migrants and 12 per cent of citizens reported having to compromise their food consumption by eating only one meal. Food coping strategies were adopted by 57 per cent of migrants due to lack of food or means to buy food. Most concerningly, one in four migrants reported having gone a whole day without eating in the past month.

project_name: Food assistance to vulnerable refugees in urban settings in Libya
project_objective:
Libya still faces multiple challenges, including low cash liquidity and fuel shortages, further compounded by restrictions due to COVID-19. The Libya Food Security Sector based on the 2021 Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment and other secondary data analyzed that 26% of refugees in Libya are in need for food assistance. The proportion is the highest among all population groups: 25% for IDPs, 19% for Migrants, 4% for Non-dispaced persons, and 10% for Returnees. 

Due to a lack of access, transparency, the impossibility to monitor, and given that, according to international law, individuals under detention in a country must be provided with the means to live with dignity by the government of this country, WFP, along with the partners of the Food Security Sector took the decision not to intervene in detention in order not to legitimize detention and provide assistance blindly where access and monitoring are impossible.

Consequently, alternative forms of assistance to vulnerable refugees have been developed and this project, targeting food insecure migrants outside detention centres, has been designed to support the food security and nutrition status of refugees and asylum-seekers while preserving them from any form of exposure, stigmatization and discriminations, ensuring their protection and promoting their inclusion within the local communities or other sustainable solutions.

WFP and UNHCR have built their functioning partnership since June 2020 to provide food assistance to vulnerable refugees and asylum-seekers in Libya based on analyzed data. The most food-insecure non-detained refugees and asylum-seekers will be identified in close partnership with UNHCR. WFP will mobilize its full capacities to procure and distribute its ready-to-eat food assistance to vulnerable refugees and asylum-seekers in urban settings. For every distribution, COVID-19 precautionary measures such as masks, disinfection, social distancing, temperature checks will be systematically applied.

project_objective: DRC’s proposed protection activities for 2022, will build on the existing response in Borno, Adamawa  and Yobe states established since 2015. DRC aims to respond to and mitigate critical protection needs of vulnerable populations through community based protection approach, by building on its gains of its established community protection structures to response to needs of These include people living  in formal/informal camps, host and returnee communities. DRC’s strong presence across 31 LGAs in NE Nigeria strengthened by its diverse programming and ability to aptly respond to emergencies over the years will provide an adequate backing for this proposed protection response. Protection programming will target extremely vulnerable persons and persons with protection concerns through a combination of protection related programming responses including; provision of immediate psychosocial support (PSS)services, psychological first aid (PFA) and community based counselling, individual and household level case management to address protection concerns, individualized protection assistance (IPA) to alleviate vulnerabilities, address environmental and remedial risks which expose individuals/ communities to protection risks through protection assessments, advocacy and coordination. DRC will continue to provide ,life-saving information to communities on services offered within their communities, give communities access to services through establishment or strengthening of referral pathways, provide protection related services through IPA, increase duty bearers capacity for a protection capacity for all. DRC coordination and collaboration efforts with key stakeholders will aim to strengthen service provision to beneficiaries whilst ensuring persons of concerns have access to their entitlements and rights while engaging institutions and actors to enhance their duty bearer commitments. Protection centres/ mobile desks will ensure communities feel safe by embracing protection by presence which will ensure protection services are available to communities throughout the year. The centres will provide access to crucial protection related services for communities situated within accessible distances. Which include referral services for gender-based violence (GBV), child protection (CP), housing, land and property (HLP), and general protection services (documentation, other human rights violations). DRC will carryout protection monitoring assessments which will identify protection risks and feed this information back into programming throughout the implementation period to strengthen the response. However crucial advocacy initiatives will be derived from this information to influence duty bearers so that they improve the protective environment of IDPs, returnees and host communities as DRC addresses protection concerns and mitigation of risks.. project_name: Projet multisectoriel de prévention de l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle en faveur des ménages vulnérables dans les régions de Tombouctou et de Taoudéni
Appui égalitaire en abris, biens non alimentaires et d'accès à l'eau potable
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à apporter un soutien holistique et intégré aux déplacés forcés et victimes des conflits et chocs climatiques en situation d'urgence puis accorde une importance capitale aux solutions durables.  Il vise à apporter dans un premier temps, des solutions coordonnées en abris d'urgences, transitionnels et biens non alimentaires aux groupes vulnérables ; et dans la deuxième phase de relèvement, des logements durables à base des briques hydraformes et l'extension en services sociaux de base de façon coordonnée avec les agences et organisations assurant le lead des secteurs où l'unhcr apporte son appui pour combler aux gaps, notamment en eau potable. En prélude à l'implantation du projet, l'unhcr à travers les services communautaires, l'unité protection et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre veilleront à l'implication à tous les niveaux des bénéficiaires à travers les focus groupes et mécanismes de plaintes, pour intégrer les besoins réels des communautés en élargissant les discussions aux filles, garçons, hommes, femmes, les personnes âgées, les handicapées physiques et mentales. Ces consultations permettront d'identifier les besoins réels des communautés, l'expression de leur attente en matière de la typologie de réponse, la modalité de réponse qu'elle soit en nature ou en cash, la protection contre l'exploitation et les abus sexuels, l'égalité entre les sexes, la prévention des violences basées sur le genre et la mitigation des risques des abus et exploitation du personnel et partenaires de mise en œuvre par le respect et la conformité aux exigences et directives sur engagements minimums, le genre, la fraude et les abus. Ces démarches serviront à répondre de manière appropriée et à éviter des réponses nuisibles à l'environnement, la coexistence pacifique entre les communautés hôtes et les groupes vulnérables ; à réduire la dépendance à l'aide et à assurer une protection.
La synergie entre les agences, les organisations, les services techniques de l'Etat et les partenaires au développement vont faciliter à synchroniser les réponses aussi bien dans les situations des urgences humanitaires et le développement afin de réduire les phénomènes des déplacements pendulaires inhérents au facteur socioéconomique et à la non-couverture des gaps dans les réponses multisectorielles.
L'unhcr s'impliquera davantage en 2022 de façon que ses partenaires de mise en œuvre rapportent régulièrement leurs réalisations en répondant aux outils de reporting développés et mis en oeuvre par les Clusters et à assister régulièrement dans leurs réunions de coordination régionale et nationale. En revanche, lorsqu'un parmi ses partenaires de mise en œuvre ne respecte pas ses engagements, l'unhcr informera les services techniques et les Clusters pour que le concerné se conforme aux exigences.
L'unhcr mettra en œuvre à travers le système de profilage de sites et infrastructures avec l'appui des Cluster Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires et Protection sous les directives du Comité de Pilotage de Gestion des Sites, le Comité Régional de Coordination Humanitaire à renforcer le processus de transition vers les solutions durables. Le projet pilote de village d'espoir du site de 10 hectares à Gao qui a permis réunir les agences des nations unies, les partenaires humanitaires et au développement à s'engager à aménager et construire des abris durables et services de base, va être élargi à Menaka, Segou, Mopti et Tombouctou. Il vise à répondre à la crise spontanée des groupes vulnérables vivants sur les sites collectifs et dans des conditions de vies précaires (abris de fortune, manque d'accès à l'eau potable, à l’hygiène et assainissement). L’unhcr renforcera également ses bureaux de terrain en prédisposant des stocks de contingence, destinés aux réponses d’urgence et transitionnelle en abris et articles ménages essentiels. Les DRH vont être impliquées dans les études de prospection et le suivi d’implantation des ouvrages hydrauliques.

project_name: Emergency GBV Protection Support for Women Survivors
project_objective:
The goal of this project is to strengthen protection for women survivors of violence during the complex humanitarian crisis in Lebanon. Under the Emergency Response Plan (ERP), this project responds to critical protection gaps in GBV prevention and response by targeting underserved Lebanese women, migrant women, and Palestinian refugee (PRL) women in Lebanon. UN Women oversee and monitor the overall project implementation, providing technical assistance. Services will be provided directly by KAFA, with support from the Lebanese Union for People with Disabilities (LUPD). 

The GBV prevention component will respond to the objective 1.1: measures are in place to prevent and mitigate the risks of GBV among the most marginalized communities. It will include:
i)	Outreach campaign with messaging on GBV, including services available
ii)	Awareness sessions raising for GBV interventions, with a focus on women with disabilities 

The outreach campaign will seek to increase women-at-risk and men with access to information about how to prevent and stop gender-based violence, as well as the services available to them. The campaign will have a two-prong approach, utilizing both multi-media platform, and traditional communication materials, including fliers and leaflets in high traffic areas such as health centers. Given the fuel and electricity crisis, expanding outreach interventions to women who are not online or have access to internet and mobile phones, is essential. The awareness sessions will focus on two target groups – women-at-risk of experiencing violence, and men who might become perpetrators. 

The protection service component will respond to objective 4.1: Survivors and individuals at risk have access to quality specialized GBV services. It will include:
i)	KAFA’s emergency helpline (03 018 019) 
ii)	Holistic and comprehensive case management services for women survivors 
iii)	Emergency safe housing
iv)	Specific case management for women survivors with disabilities 

KAFA’s emergency helpline is a well-established service, operating since 2016 and has been inundated with a high case load, since the beginning of the pandemic. It is available for women survivors of violence 24- hours/7 days a week and will be capacitated to expand its reach. Women will receive counseling and referrals to case management and other services. The case management is led by highly experienced and trained case workers and will take place in women safe spaces in Beirut, Bekaa, and Saida, safe housing/shelters, and in case of emergencies, remotely. Specific staff and interventions will be offered to women with disabilities, including ensuring that physical centers are accessible, and staff are equipped with information and tools to best support their needs. To operate effectively in the dual emergency context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and fuel crisis, support will be provided to ensure the continuity of remote services and access for women survivors, including internet packages, mobile applications, and alternative means of power sourcing.

project_name: Emergency Holistic Protection Services for Migrant Women facing Exploitation, Trauma and Abuse
project_objective:
Women migrant domestic workers (WMDWs) – an already marginalized group, continue to be disproportionately impacted by Lebanon’s manifold humanitarian crisis. Due to the Kafala system, WMDWs live with almost no legal and social protection, facing high levels of exploitation and different types of abuse while facing huge obstacles to access justice. They rarely resort to the authorities to seek redress, often due to isolation in their place of work, fear from the authorities, lack of awareness about legal procedures and their rights, the absence of financial means, and language barriers.
In light of this situation, UN Women in partnership with Kafa (enough) Violence & Exploitation and GIZ are partnering to address the emergency protection needs of WMDWs in Lebanon. This project works towards the achievement of the ERP Objective 3: to enhance timely, unhindered, and equitable access to protection assistance for migrants. Under this project, migrant women will have access to a 24/7 helpline, increased access to legal and protection services, better access to quality MHPSS services, and basic and humanitarian return assistance. Socioeconomically marginalized migrant women will be targeted across all regions in Lebanon. UN Women will oversee and monitor the overall project implementation. Services will be provided directly by KAFA, with support on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) technical assistance provided by GIZ. 

Under 1.1, UN Women and Kafa will conduct mass awareness raising of legal information as a first step to increase their access to protection and obtainment of their legal rights. The campaign will utilize both social media platforms and traditional communication materials, including fliers and leaflets in high traffic areas. Given the fuel and electricity crisis, expanding outreach interventions to migrant women who are not online or have access to internet and mobile phones, is essential. All materials will be translated in the languages of migrant workers. Legal aid will also be provided via individual and group legal counseling, and legal representation for specific cases. 

Under 2.1, Kafa will continue the operation of an established 24/7 helpline dedicated to MDWs. The helpline provides information counseling and provide referrals to specialized legal actors and service providers. Victims of physical and sexual abuse, they will be provided with immediate socio-legal protection information and/or measures. MHPSS will be implemented through different modalities. Social workers operating the helpline will provide immediate psycho-social counseling for WMDWs in psychological distress and make specialized refers. KAFA will also provide direct PSS interventions, including targeting the mental health of migrant community leaders in order to help them manage stress and prevent burnout. GIZ has been a key actor in the MHPSS response for migrants in Lebanon, and will provide quality assurance, and advise on technical referrals to specialized services, as well as coordination with the MHPSS task-force for migrant domestic workers.  
Under 3.1, While protection data will be collected and monitored across all project activity implementation, UN Women will specifically collect and analyze data on female migrant population in North Lebanon (Tripoli and Akkar), with a focus on gender and protection in order to respond to data gaps in that region and improve it service provision outreach. 
Under 6.1, UN Women and Kafa will provide multi-purpose cash assistance to address urgent needs of WMDWs. The cash assistance will be provided to the most vulnerable WMDWs to cover rent, and other basic needs. 
Under 7.1, UN Women and Kafa will facilitate voluntary humanitarian return assistance for WMDWs facing high-risk protection issues. A specific focus will be given to scaling up voluntary return support to migrant women who are in detention, and arbitrary detention – a violation of human rights.
