Intervention d'urgence pour lutter contre les épidémies de méningite, de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune, de rougeole , d'Ebola et de la Pandémie de la COVID19 au Tchad
project_objective:
Objectif du projet est de réduire les taux de morbidité et de mortalité dus aux épidémies de méningite, de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune et de rougeole et autres épidémiesLe Tchad reste un pays qui fait face aux épidémies récurrentes et aux catastrophes naturelles tels que les inondations. En 2019 le pays a enregistré plus de 20000 sinistrés dont plus d’une dizaine de morts et disparus suites aux inondations. Le taux de morbidité et mortalité reste élevé. Le taux de mortalité élevé observé lors des épidémies est dû à la faiblesse du système de surveillance, au manque de stratégies de santé appropriées, au manque d’accès des patients aux services de santé et à la mauvaise qualité des services de santé existants.
Méningite : chaque année, le pays est confronté à une vague d'épidémie de méningite dans le sud et l'ouest du pays. En 2012, la vaccination avec le nouveau vaccin MenAfriVac, qui couvrait l’ensemble du pays, a réduit le risque de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype A). Cependant, le risque d'épidémie de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype W135) persiste. En 2019 les districts sanitaires de Goundi et Bedjondo dans la province sanitaire du Mandoul, ont connu une épidémie de méningite à méningocoque (sérotype W135) avec plus 500 cas suspects dont 52 décès. Depuis le début de l'année 2021 plus de 544 cas suspects dont 48 décès ont été notifiés.
La couverture vaccinale contre la rougeole est faible (37%), ce qui a entrainé une épidémie de rougeole. Il s'agit d'une menace sérieuse pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans dans un contexte de forte prévalence de malnutrition chronique. 252550 cas avec 294 décès ont été notifiés.
Choléra : Le choléra apparaît pendant la saison des pluies dans les régions entourant le lac Tchad. En 2011, 17 000 cas de choléra ont été notifiés par 37 districts de santé touchés sur 62. En 2014, 172 cas de choléra ont été notifiés dans les régions de Lac, Mayo Kebbi et N’Djamena. En 2017 plus de 1000 cas ont été notifiés dans le Sila et Salamat. En 2019 les provinces sanitaires du Mayo Kebbi Est et Ouest ont connu une épidémie de choléra avec au total 96 cas notifié. Compte tenu des faibles niveaux d'accès à une source d'eau durable améliorée (52%) et à un assainissement amélioré (12%), il est probable que cela continue d'être un problème chronique.
En 2013, le Tchad a connu une épidémie de fièvre jaune. Plus de 900 000 personnes ont été vaccinées. En 2016, 334 cas suspects ont été notifiés, dont un confirmé et en 2018 426 cas suspects ont été notifiés. Dès le début de l’année,2021, plus de 500 suspects avec 20 décès. Une épidémie a été déclarée dans le Mandoul en Novembre 2021 avec plus 70 cas suspect avec 13 cas confirmés au laboratoire
En outre, le pays connait des flambées de cas de paludisme notamment chez les enfants et les femmes. En 2019, plus de 1 000 000 de cas ont été notifiés
L’épidémie d’Ebola en Afrique de l’Ouest et centrale, et la proximité du Tchad avec cette région de l’Afrique nécessitent des mesures de surveillance adéquates ainsi que des actions de prévention et de préparation.
Afin de contrôler ces épidémies et de réduire les taux de morbidité et de mortalité dus aux épidémies de choléra, de paludisme, de fièvre jaune, de rougeole et de méningite, ce projet vise à prendre en charge de nouvelles épidémies en réalisant une campagne de vaccination de masse de l'ensemble de la population vulnérable( hommes et femmes vulnérables , enfants, garçons et filles , handicapés) sans distinction d’âge en mettant un accès sur les femmes, les enfants de moins de 5 ans

project_name: Maintien des services essentiels de santé pour les populations les plus vulnérables dans les situations d’urgence humanitaire dans 8 provinces sanitaires du Burundi.
project_objective:
La santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et de l’adolescent(e)s a connu des progrès significatifs au Burundi au cours de ces deux dernières décennies. Cependant, la mortalité dans ce groupe vulnérable reste toujours élevée par rapport aux cibles des Objectifs de Développement Durable.
 En effet, selon la dernière Enquête de Santé et Démographique (EDS-III), le Ratio de Mortalité Maternelle et Néonatale sont passés respectivement de 500 à 334 décès maternels pour 100.000 naissances vivantes et 31 à 23 décès néonatals pour 1000 naissances vivantes entre 2010 et 2016. Le même rapport montre qu’au cours de ces cinq dernières années, un enfant sur 20 meurt avant son premier anniversaire et un enfant sur treize meurt avant d’atteindre son cinquième anniversaire soit un quotient de mortalité infanto-juvénile estimé à 78‰ avec un risque plus élevé en milieu rural qu’en milieu urbain. Au Burundi environs six enfants sur dix sont atteints de malnutrition chronique (56%). Sur ce fond de malnutrition chronique trop élevée, la morbidité chez l’enfant de moins de 5 ans est principalement dominée par les trois maladies courantes de l’enfant: le paludisme, la pneumonie ainsi que les maladies diarrhéiques. A cela, il faut ajouter l’infection à VIH sida et les anémies. etc... ce qui rend d’avantages la vulnérabilité des enfants pendant les situations d’urgence.

Si les besoins des femmes, des enfants et des filles ne sont pas intégrés dans la réponse de santé publique en situation d’urgence y compris lors de cette pandémie de la COVID 19, et une priorisation proportionnée des ressources pour la santé sexuelle et reproductive, la santé maternelle, néonatale, infantile et des jeunes et des adolescent(e)s(e)s cela pourrait entraîner des augmentations substantielles de la mortalité évitable.  

Parallèlement à ce profil sanitaire particulier, le Burundi subit des catastrophes d’origine humaine (conflits), naturelle (inondations, sécheresse) et des épidémies (choléra et paludisme). Il doit faire face à des déplacements de populations et à la réintégration de populations rapatriées. Les épidémies passées ont démontré que le manque d’accès aux services de santé essentiels en raison de la fermeture des services non liés à la lutte contre l’épidémie, peut donner lieu à plus de décès que ceux qui sont causés par l’épidémie elle-même. 

L’OMS va capitaliser son rôle normatif et de coordination en matière de santé et son expérience dans l’appui à la mise en œuvre des interventions intégrées de gestion intégrée des cas dans la communauté ou « Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) » sans oublier la réponse aux épidémies de paludisme afin d’accompagner les interventions proposées dans ce projet pour contribuer à l’accès et au maintien des services de santé essentiels de qualité de la mère, du nouveau-né, de l’enfant et de l’adolescent(e)s et au renforcement du système de santé. La réponse sera focalisée sur : (i) l’accès et l’utilisation des services essentiels de santé de qualité (ii) la disponibilité des intrants (iii) la décentralisation du traitement du paludisme à travers l’iCCM (iv) le renforcement du partenariat (v) le suivi et évaluation ainsi que (vi) la gestion et la coordination de la réponse à l’urgence. Ces activités seront mises en oeuvre dans 8 provinces sanitaires du pays à savoir Cankuzo, Rutana, Karusi, Muyinga, Kirundo, Rumonge, Cibitoke et Makamba.

Même si le projet cible en particulier les femmes en âge de procréer-les nouveaux nés-les enfants et les adolescents, tous les groupes de populations vulnérables (y compris les personnes à besoins spécifiques) seront pris en compte dans la mise en oeuvre du projet.

project_objective:
Islamic Relief Ethiopia(IRE)  aims to provide emergency lifesaving Nutrition support to drought-affected vulnerable IDPs and host communities of Bare, Godgod, and Kohile districts in the Afder zone of the Somali   Region, with a primary focus on the full components of Community Based Management of Acute Malnutrition(CMAM). The project will target vulnerable children under children, pregnant and breastfeeding women—both displaced and in host communities, addressing immediate nutrition needs by providing nutrition services and promoting optimal feeding practices to meet nutrition requirements as well as the adoption of best practices on IYCF  and its integration with CMAM response.  In the targeted three woredas, the project will cover all kebeles by enhancing the local health system including OTP and SC sites to deliver quality CMAM and IYCF service to host communities and IDPs. Nutrition services and related activities will be informed by the most recently updated guidelines, considering COVID19 prevention and containment measures. Different services delivery modalities will be considered, from static to mobile/community-based, as a proactive and articulated strategy to overcome the accessibility issues affecting current nutrition care coverage and to reach both hosts and displaced populations.

Further, the project will also strengthen the local health system and build the capacity of health workers and health extension workers to respond to already folded primary health care and nutrition services in all targeted intervention woredas. Besides, IRE will work with district health offices in promoting and strengthening  Family MUAC, best practices of IYCF including Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPS) throughout the implementation period of this project. Further, Nutrition technical staff will be deployed in all of the targeted woredas for the provision of technical and logistic support

project_name: Améliorer la santé des populations affectées par un choc ou une épidémie et contribuer à la réduction de la mortalité infanto-juvénile dans les régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua et Maradi.
project_objective:
L’objectif principal du projet est d’améliorer l’état de santé des populations affectées par un choc, un conflit armé, un mouvement de population, une épidémie ou une catastrophe naturelle; et contribuer à la réduction de la mortalité infanto-juvénile liées à la MAS et aux principales pathologies pédiatriques dans les districts sanitaires de Abala, Ayérou, Banibangou, Tassara, et Guidam Roumdji. L’accès aux soins et la prise en charge médicale de qualité des populations hôtes, réfugiées et déplacées sera assurée via un appui aux CSI et aux HD, et par le déploiement de cliniques mobiles dans les zones à faible accès. Les capacités des structures de santé et des communautés locales dans la préparation et à la réponse aux urgences seront également renforcées. Une évaluation et une réponse d’urgence immédiate en cas de crise sanitaire et humanitaire soudaine sera également assurée dans des zones non couvertes par le projet en collaboration avec les partenaires RRM Santé et Multisectoriel.
Le projet assurera d’abord le mécanisme RRM via une veille humanitaire et sanitaire à Abala, Banibangou, Ayorou, Guidam Roumdji et Tassara à travers la surveillance des MDO et les alertes reçues du réseau ALIMA/BEFEN dans le cadre de la surveillance des événements. ALIMA/BEFEN analyseront les alertes reçues et proposeront une réponse d’urgence en cas d’alertes confirmées. Les réponses se feront via une stratégie mobile. Le déploiement des cliniques mobiles dans chaque DS permettra d’atteindre les populations éloignées/déplacées et réfugiées afin de proposer gratuitement des consultations primaires curatives. La préparation aux urgences passe notamment par le renforcement des capacités des communautés (formations des relais/lanceurs d’alertes). Les zones non couvertes par le projet pourront faire l’objet d’une intervention RRM en fonction des moyens disponibles.
Dans les zones fragilisées par les conflits armées couvertes par l’action, le projet travaillera au renforcement des capacités du système et structures de santé décentralisées (CSI, CS, HD) et des acteurs communautaires pour renforcer la préparation des réponses aux crises nutritionnelles et sanitaires via un appui fixe et le déploiement des cliniques mobiles. L'accès aux soins de santé communautaires sera garanti à travers la mise en œuvre de la PCIME CO et la stratégie matrone sera renforcés au niveau des DS de Abala et Ayorou. Les agents de santé seront formés sur la prise en charge des cas de VBB et VVS et pourront apporter un soutien et une prise en charge médicale aux victimes.

project_name: DROUGHT RESPONSE
project_objective: People affected by drought in Turkana and Tana River counties have access to adequate and safe water supply; meet their basic needs; are protected from harm and that infants, children, pregnant and lactating women receive timely and quality treatment and prevention services for acute malnutrition.

project_name: Strengthening protection and resilience of vulnerable groups in COVID-19 emergency
PEERS: Protection Enabling Environment and Resilience Services
Providing quality and comprehensive GBV Prevention and Response Services in Misrata and Benghazi
Organised Local Response Program - Protection and WASH
project_objective: The program seeks to respond to the prolonged humanitarian crisis affecting the Palestinian population under occupation, exacerbated by the COVID-19 crisis, by contributing to the protection of their rights and dignity in accordance with IHL and IHRL, and with a cross-cutting focus on gender equity and community participation. The program is to be implemented by the Action Group for Organised Local Response (Action Group) and other partners of the protection cluster: a group of civil society organisations that seeks to promote the localisation of humanitarian response and to respond to the multiple needs and demands of Palestinian communities in an organised manner, by working on their respective sectoral and geographical areas of expertise. The program as a whole is multi-sectoral and includes actions linked to protection, with a special emphasis in gender-based violence, WASH, livelihoods, education, mental health and advocacy, which also targets populations affected by the impact of COVID-19 in areas throughout the West Bank. While the program is multi-sectoral, it has been divided in sectoral projects to facilitate the management of such a comprehensive program. In this sense, the present project includes protection and WASH-related activities and the whole program is in line with the strategic objectives (SOs) of both the Protection and WASH Clusters. It includes 1 ) Increased respect for IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations; 2) Putting in place protection response mechanisms such as Community Protection Committees or the provision of protection services, in order to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict-related violence, like settler violence, property damage and confiscation, restrictions, violations against children and gender-based violence; 3) Meeting the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation by providing them with quality basic services and improving their access to resources, such as water and sanitation facilities; and 4) Promoting the capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, like waste pollution. The population targeted under the program is highly vulnerable to IHL/IHRL violations due to the presence of their communities in Area C and East Jerusalem and to their proximity to settlements, military bases and Israeli military checkpoints. The program pays special attention to the different vulnerabilities, needs and capacities of women, men, girls and boys. Specific target groups include children affected by the conflict, women affected by GBV, people with disabilities and others vulnerable to conflict related violence, such as agricultural workers and youth.

project_name: Improving WASH conditions at community & HH levels in Gaza and Middle area Governorates
project_objective:
In line with the WASH cluster objective #2 and country strategic objective #2, the action aims to ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians. through ensuring basic WASH services for conflict-affected, un- or under-served and vulnerable populations and institutions in the Gaza Strip. The proposed intervention responds to the SDG #6. SDG6 aims to ‘ensure available and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all’ and includes targets for universal access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene for all by 2030.
The project aims at reducing the public health and environmental pollution risks that may occur as a result of wastewater percolation from existing cesspits in the target locations in Gaza Governorate. It will benefit nearly 14850 people of which 49% are women in four locations namely in El-Zaytoun South of Gaza, Aldaraj w Alsabra middle of Gaza, Shejaiya in East of Gaza area and Juhor ad Dik south of Gaza City. Total number of beneficiaries in each location can be listed as follows: El-Zaytoun 11000, Aldaraj w Alsabra 550, Shejaiya 2750 and Juhor ad Dik 550. Moreover, the project will indirectly benefiting all people in the target four locations through direct pollution prevention of their areas and also prevent groundwater pollution.
According to the information obtained from CMWU and PWA during the coordination meetings organized with them on 27 September 2021, these information were coordinated again on 29 September 2021 WASH cluster coordination team, area focal points, technical focal points and governmental counterpart focal points and they identified the four locations listed above which are in need of sewer system to connect more HHs in order to avoid flooding of wastewater to neighborhoods and to coastal aquifer. Accordingly, the project will contribute by supplying and installing 4100 m of UPVC sewer lines, 140 concrete manholes and 300 house connection. The project will contribute also in closing down all the cesspits in the target locations to stop further pollution of aquifer and prevent public health risks, hence, reducing ensuring no harm principle.
Also, the project aims at improving the WASH facilities at 500 war affected households in 11 locations in Gaza and Deir Al-Balah governorates to make sure that the access of nearly 3000 inhabitants of which 1481 are women to essential wash services is improved. The number of beneficiaries in each location can be summarized as follows: Shejaiya- 300, El-Zaytoun 300, تل الهوا - 300, الرمال الشمالي-300, الرمال الجنوبي-300, الشيخ عجلين- 300, block 1 - 300. block 3 block 4 -240, block 1 block 2 block 5 -240, block C السوق وكلبوش -300 and block L block f -120.
Following to the termination of Israeli military assault on Gaza on 25th May 2021 PHG has mobilized its entire team in Gaza and conducted rapid assessment to the damage in line with WASH damage assessment and according to the information obtained from the Ministry of Public Works and Housing (MOPWH), these information were coordinated on 29 September 2021 WASH cluster coordination team, area focal points, technical focal points and governmental counterpart focal points and they identified the 11 locations listed above which are in need of urgent rehabilitation of damaged WASH facilities. Accordingly, the project will contribute by rehabilitating 500 WASH facilities for the benefit of 500 households including internal WASH connections, sinks, water mixers, toilets, laundries and PE roof tanks. 
In general, this intervention aims to improve WASH conditions for more than 17,850 people (3,200 families) in 13 locations in Gaza and Middle area Governorates, through the installation of 4.1Km of sewage networks and the rehabilitation of WASH facilities for 500 homes that were damaged during the last war in 2021.

project_name: Emergency Response to improve access to basic WASH needs for the most vulnerable female-headed households in Rafah governorate
project_objective: The cumulative effects of years of prolonged conflict, the COVID-19 Pandemic, chronic vulnerabilities and weak essential services have left over 1.35 million Palestinians across the oPt being affected by public health risks associated with insufficient access to WASH services and in immediate need of humanitarian assistance in 2022 as they are as per (2022 WASH HNO draft). In the Gaza Strip, the ability of the service providers to ensure satisfactory operation of over 500 WASH facilities has been undermined by funding gaps, also, more than 290 WASH infrastructure were affected during May escalations, constraining access to water and sanitation services for more than 1.2 million Palestinians. This situation has reduced households access to adequate water and sanitation services, weakening Gaza households’ capacity to maintain their health, livelihoods, social and hygiene status, of particular concern in light of the ongoing pandemic. Women, children, elders and Persons with Disabilities (PWD) are the most affected by this shortage in WASH services. Women in particular are affected disproportionally, leaving them in a struggle to maintain minimum hygiene and ensure the availability of drinking water. In line with the WASH cluster objective #2: “Ensure equitable, affordable and sustainable safely-managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians”, this project is proposed with the overall objective to enhance the protection of the most vulnerable female-headed households at higher risk of protection concerns and exposure to COVID-19, due to having substandard and inadequate WASH conditions. The project will provide emergency WASH assistance and capacity building support to FHHs, prioritizing households with PWDs, elderlies and people with chronic diseases. Specifically, the project intends to respond by providing an appropriate, integrated WASH response for the most vulnerable FHHs which are affected by the loss of sole breadwinners and the protracted humanitarian and pandemic crises, including women, children, elderly and people with disabilities in order preserve the dignity of vulnerable beneficiaries through improving access to water for drinking and domestic use, sustaining access to protected, and gender-sensitive sanitation facilities and promoting personal and environmental hygiene among the targeted Households. The intervention will complement the cash assistance, which these FHHs receive from IRW’s sponsorship programme, contributing to achieving better outcomes for their families’ members. The project will target 50 of the FHHs in Rafah governorate in the Gaza Strip (75 women, 55 men, 60 boys, 60 girls), that are critically underserved in relation to WASH services as revealed in the Rapid Needs Assessment carried by IRW and its partners in June 2021 and found a need for urgent WASH intervention to improve safety and privacy and to address the protection concerns of women, girls and boys members of the most vulnerable female headed households. Based on the findings of the rapid needs assessments, IRW and partner have identified the following locations for 2022 interventions: Rafah Camp, Alshabwra, al'iidarii, Tal Sultan and Rafah Algharbi. IRW is the WASH cluster focal point in Rafah, and it has the staff, experience and practical presence in the area, thus creating a conducive environment for successful operations. Throughout the project life cycle, IRW will coordinate with WASH cluster and partners, the local authorities and other stakeholders including affected community, and will depend on a local partner on ground for implementing the activities ensure maximum utilization of resources. Throughout the proposed intervention, IRW will monitor any protection concerns (GBV, SEA, child protection issues) by building the capacity of project team and partner and raising awareness of beneficiaries and through referral and Complaint and feedback mechanisms.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security, Self-Reliance and Livelihoods (Phase-2)
project_objective: This project presents an innovative approach aimed at increasing the resilience of host communities and refugees, which 1) in-creases the adaptive capacity of host communities and refugees by supporting the adoption of climate resilient livelihood solutions and the by strengthening local market systems, 2) enhances the absorptive capacity of host communities and refuges by providing cash support and in-creasing awareness of the target groups and 3) fosters the transformative capacity of the target groups through community restoration and awareness raising activities. The objective of the project is to increase resilience of the host communities and Rohingya refugees, in Cox’s Bazar, by improving food security, reducing disaster vulnerability and increasing social cohesion.

project_name: Provision and Management of WASH Core Pipeline Supplies for Emergency Preparedness and Response in South Sudan
project_objective: UNICEF WASH core pipeline supplies project will reach 1,400,000 beneficiaries through provision to people (IDPs and communities affected by other emergencies) with immediate WASH needs through planning, procurement, prepositioning, distribution, and management of critical WASH supplies. The project will contribute to Cluster objectives 1, 2 and 3 through provision water treatment chemicals, spare parts for hand pump rehabilitation/repair, latrine slabs (squatting pans), plastic tarpaulins for latrine construction, latrine digging kits, hygiene kits (jerry-cans, buckets, soap, menstrual hygiene health materials, and dignity items). UNICEF will procure the WASH supplies and in coordination with the WASH Cluster pre-position them in strategic locations throughout South Sudan. Supplies will be released to partners through the approval of the WASH Cluster, and the receiving partner will be responsible for distribution of the supplies. The WASH supplies will be accessible to all WASH partners currently operational in South Sudan through WASH Cluster structures at national and state levels. The project will distribute WASH supplies as per Sphere and South Sudan WASH Cluster standards and in coordination with other clusters (Health, and Nutrition). Through this project UNICEF will focus on delivering rapid assistance in all counties and population affected by a sudden or rapid-onset disaster and targeting at county level will be done through WASH Cluster updates or using various assessment findings (IRNAs, NAWG recommendations, WASH severity classification). Follow-up monitoring and capacity building of partners will be conducted  throughout the project period to ensure proper management of supplies at various warehouses. UNICEF in coordination with beneficiary partners will conduct end user monitoring of the supplies to ensure that supplies distributed are reaching the vulnerable communities and are being used properly.

project_name: Assistance nutritionnelle et sanitaire d'urgence en faveur des personnes les plus vulnérables affectées par les conflits dans les régions du Sahel et du Centre-Nord au Burkina-Faso.
project_objective:
Le projet vise à améliorer l’accès aux services sociaux de base, et notamment les services de santé nutritionnelle et les soins de santé primaire, pour les personnes les plus vulnérables affectées par les conflits dans les zones ciblées, en apportant une réponse multisectorielle appropriée à leurs besoins. 
Dans les régions du Sahel et du Centre Nord, l'assistance multisectorielle sera constituée de l'assistance nutritionnelle et sanitaire visant les IDPs, les populations hôtes et locales affectées par la dégradation de la situation sécuritaire. 
Plus spécifiquement, le projet appuie la prévention et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigüe des enfants de moins de 5 ans à travers l’approche PCIMA/ Protocole simplifié et renforce les capacités des acteurs de santé dans les districts sanitaires, permettant d’améliorer l’efficacité des programmes nutritionnels et renforcer la résilience du système de santé grâce à une détection plus rapide et efficace de la malnutrition en impliquant davantage la communauté. 
Le résultat principal à atteindre est que les formations sanitaires des districts sanitaires de Djibo et Dori (Sahel), et Kaya et Tougouri (Centre-Nord) offrent une prise en charge sanitaire et nutritionnelle de qualité aux enfants de moins de 5 ans malnutris et aux personnes vulnérables affectées par les conflits.
Le programme est mis en œuvre dans un contexte sécuritaire très volatile par MDME. Le projet s'inscrit dans la complémentarité et continuité des actions de MdME et ses partenaires dans la zone depuis 2016.

project_name: Amélioration durable de la santé maternelle, infantile et juvénile dans la région Centre-Est, Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La situation sanitaire et nutritionnelle reste préoccupante dans la région du centre-Est du Burkina-Faso et particulièrement à Ouargaye ou l’afflux des personnes fuyant les conflits exerce une pression supplémentaire sur le système de santé. L’action propose une approche concentrée sur deux principaux piliers afin de 1) renforcer le système de santé au niveau décentralisé à travers l’amélioration de la qualité de la Prise en charge et 2) d’accroitre la pratique des comportements sains en matière de nutrition au niveau communautaire. 
Pilier 1 : L'action proposée renforcera les systèmes de santé dans 10 Aires de Santé en appuyant les Centres de Santé et de Protection Sociale (CSPS) correspondants ainsi que les activités de proximité qu'ils mettent en œuvre. Plus précisément, 5 Aires de Santé ciblées par les projets précédents de Concern bénéficieront d'un soutien continu, tandis que 5 Aires de Santé supplémentaires recevront un paquet complet d'assistance. 
Il s’agit notamment de mettre un accent sur les principales maladies infectieuses qui accentuent les carences nutritionnelles chez les enfants. L’action renforcera les capacités des services de santé de base au travers des formations spécifiques des agents de santé sur les 7 modules de base définis par le ministère de la Santé burkinabé. L’accent sera mis sur la Prise en Charge Intégrée des Maladies de l’Enfant (PCIME),. 80 professionnels de la santé des zones ciblées bénéficieront de ces formations. Dans chaque Aire de Santé, au moins 15 agents professionnels de santé bénéficieront de formations sur les 5 CSPS ciblés pour un appui complet. De plus, 5 professionnels de santé de l'Hôpital de district seront formés.
Le deuxième volet de ce pilier est la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie « WASH in Nut » dans les mêmes airs de santé ciblés et pour lesquels les besoins en EAH ne sont pas encore couverts. 
En effet, l’approche « Wash in Nut » renforcera l’impact de l’action sur la sous-nutrition en ciblant les mêmes bénéficiaires des 10 aires de santé, a raison de 10.000 individus par aire de santé. Des actions spécifiques seront réalisées comme la fourniture de kit de traitement de l’eau, la réhabilitation de forages, de latrines et de lave-mains ; la formation à l’utilisation de kit de traitement de l’eau dans les centres de santé et la formation de 10 comités de points d’eau. Toute la population vivant dans les périmètres de ces centres de santé bénéficiera ainsi d'un accès accru à des services de santé et de nutrition améliorés, et à des conditions WASH plus sûres au sein du CSPS. 

Pilier 2 : Dans le but d’accroitre la prévention de la malnutrition, l’action mettra 3,000 femmes enceintes et allaitantes au centre de l’approche car elles constituent un groupe particulièrement vulnérable dans ce contexte ou le système de santé est affaibli. Le but visé est d’amener les mères à connaître les bonnes pratiques de nutrition et à les appliquer pour maintenir leurs enfants et elles-mêmes en bon état nutritionnel. Un bon état nutritionnel constant est primordial pour maintenir un bon état de santé général. 10 groupes de pairs féminins (Groupe d'Apprentissage et de Suivi des Pratiques d'Alimentation - GASPA) par Aire de Santé seront soutenus par la formation par un suivi régulier. Chaque GASPA regroupe en moyenne 30 femmes enceintes ou allaitantes. Dans le même cadre, les femmes seront activement sensibilisées à la fréquentation des centres de santé offrant des services de nutrition et à la prise en charge des effets de la malnutrition. 
Cette composante sera mise en œuvre par un partenaire local (ASMAD) de Concern, expérimenté dans la communication et l’information des communautés en faveur de la nutrition. 
Enfin, les deux (2) piliers seront renforcés par un axe transversal réservé à la coordination, l’apprentissage et la diffusion des résultats.

project_name: Integrated WASH-GBV response to humanitarian needs in Gaza
project_objective:
DanChurchAid/Norwegian Church Aid (DCA/NCA) and its partners, MAAN Development Centre (MAAN) and Women Affairs Centre (WAC), propose an integrated multisectoral WASH-GBV project in the North Governorate of Gaza strip- Farata (Beit Hanoun) and North American School (Beit Lahia). 

Project objective: The project aims at improving the access to safe and equitable WASH services and appropriate GBV response mechanisms in accordance with the dignity of the underserved and most vulnerable communities.

The project will focus hardship cases, female headed households, GBV survivors, and people with disabilities. The intervention is designed considering a comprehensive assessment that addresses people’s access to equitable, safe, and sufficient water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services and examined the related risks of Gender Based Violence (GBV). An study (conducted in 2020 by DCA/NCA partners, WAC and MAAN) revealed that Poor access to adequate and safe water, hygiene and sanitation services plays a significant role in promoting gender-based violence against women. Upon the study, 53.8 % of the women reported that the bathroom in their homes lack safety and security standards. 
The objective of this action is consistent with the assigned objectives of the OCHA HRP 2022 as such:
•	For WASH component: The intervention is in line with HRP STRATEGIC OBJECTIVE 2: “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL” In addition, it meets WASH Cluster Specific Objectives 2. ""Ensure equitable, affordable, and sustainable safely managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians "".
•	For GBV component:  The intervention is in line with the HRP Protection Cluster STRATEGIC OBJECTIVE 2: Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence.
The WASH partner (MAAN) will identify the most vulnerable families with deteriorated WASH conditions (based on socioeconomic and technical assessments) to improve access to WASH services. This will be followed by the GBV response (by WAC) to address one of the consequences of the deteriorated WASH situation manifested in high rates of GBV. Maan will prioritize the families that include PWD’s to address their specific needs (i.e., rehabilitate the bathroom to be suitable for the use of PWD’s, adding ramps, hygiene kits content to consider PWD’s needs, etc.). This is applied for GBV response as well, where PWD’s will be prioritized for GBV services. Project activities will consider the COVID-19 related risks, needs, restrictions, etc. (i.e. virtual platforms for GBV services, Hygiene promotion and hygiene material support to consider COVID-19 needs, etc).
The intervention will mainly address both WASH and GBV themes, aiming at: 
WASH (implemented by MAAN): Improving equitable and adequate access to WASH services in accordance with dignity (i.e. distribution of water storage tanks, installation/rehabilitation of sewer lines, rehabilitation of sanitation facilities inside homes, hygiene promotion (HP) and hygine material support. 
GBV (implemented by WAC): Preventing and responding to GBV activities will include referral and case management, psychosocial support (PSS), protection and GBV related awareness, legal counselling, cash for protection, multipurpose cash assistance and dignity kits.

Complementarity and harmony will be ensured between the two components, where proper coordination will take place for this purpose. DCA/NCA are active members in the UN clusters, DCA/NCA and its partners, MAAN and WAC, will be engaged effectively in all the processes and activities including joining meetings, coordinating the response and provision of information needed for the 4 W’s systems and COVID-19 response reporting.

project_name: Sector Coordination - UNICEF Supported Sectors
Provision of basic health services for population in need in humanitarian context in Sudan 2022
project_objective:
This project aims at increase access to life-saving and life sustaining basic health services for those most in need population during humanitarian situations in Sudan, 2022.
The project is targeting Khartoum, Sennar, Blue Nile, North Darfur, West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Kordofan, West Kordofan, South Kordofan, and Red Sea. 
This project will strengthen health sector capacity to prevent, prepare for and deliver timely response to population affected by conflict, natural emergencies, and disease outbreaks. This will include a) procurement, prepositioning and rational use of essential medicines, equipment and medical and laboratory supplies including PPE and strengthen capacity on rational use of drugs and supply chain management; b) building the capacity of healthcare providers and community health workers on provision of maternal, neonatal and child healthcare services, communicable and non- communicable diseases healthcare services and COVID19 prevention and vaccination services; c) expanding and maintaining disease surveillance system with early warning component for communicable and notifiable diseases and strengthening related response and information system; d) strengthening the rapid response to emergencies including setting-up emergency health teams, supporting RRTs and treatment capacity; e) improving health facility set-up to provide an acceptable quality of health services including the supply of water and power and basic needs of quality of care; f) support system for early referral of complicated cases; g) supporting community mobilization, health education and preventive messages including for COVID19.
The project implementation plan will be detailed, implemented and monitored jointly with targeted communities and ministries of health at national and state levels and local health authorities. The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $ 13,437,576

project_name: Transferts monétaires multisectoriels pour amortir les chocs multidimensionnels auxquels les ménages font face au Mali
project_objective:
Face a la crise de la COVID-19 et ses conséquences socio-économiques connues à ce jour, les preuves foisonnent à travers des expériences de plusieurs pays que les transferts monétaires sont un outil privilégié des décideurs politiques pour aider les populations vulnérables à rebondir face aux chocs. C'est également un mécanisme courant dans l'action humanitaire, utilisé pour répondre avec plus de dignité aux besoins divers des populations. Ces transferts stimulent les activités génératrices de revenus, contribuent à renforcer les moyens de subsistance et fournissent des soins de santé en cas de maladie. Ainsi, les programmes de transferts monétaires pendant les pandémies peuvent apporter une contribution importante à la protection sociale et avoir des effets bénéfiques significatifs sur la santé. Ils permettent aux bénéficiaires d'améliorer leurs choix en matière de soins de santé. En tant que tels, on peut dire qu'ils constituent un indicateur pour faire face aux chocs sanitaires, tant pour les bénéficiaires que pour les non-bénéficiaires. 
Au Mali, le gouvernement a décidé de faire des transferts aux ménages les plus vulnérables pour faire face aux chocs de la COVID-19 mais après presque deux ans moins de 300,000 ménages ont effectivement reçu ces transferts au mois de Novembre sur un total ciblé d’un million de ménages.  Quelques résultats de missions ont pourtant démontré que les récipiendaires de ces transferts ont permis aux ménages d’agir à différents niveaux, allant de l'augmentation du pouvoir d'achat des ménages, à la protection des actifs productifs, en passant par l'amélioration du niveau de vie des ménages. 
Ce projet vise à élargir la couverture des transferts monétaires d’urgence à un plus grand nombre de ménages dans des situations humanitaires. En particulier 70,000 ménages devraient bénéficier de transferts monétaires à usage multiples dans le cadre d’une programmation multisectorielle comprenant une réponse inclusive : continuité des services sociaux de base pour garantir un accès continu à l'éducation, à la sécurité alimentaire, à l’eau et à l’assainissement et à l’hygiène, la continuité des services de santé y compris pour les femmes enceintes et les services de vaccination, les activités génératrices de revenus, en particulier pour les jeunes, en veillant à ce que personne ne soit laissé pour compte, en mettant l'accent sur les femmes, les personnes vivant avec le VIH, les personnes âgées et les personnes handicapées.

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash: Basic Needs Support Programme for vulnerable families in Al-Hassakeh, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Homs and Hama
project_objective:
The economic collapse and the significant reduction in Government’s social spending have plunged additional segments of the population into humanitarian need, most notably in areas historically less affected by hostilities and displacement. Assessment data from August 2021 (MSNA) indicate that the income gap has continued to widen, with average household expenditure now exceeding income by 50%, compared to 20% in August 2020. Only 10% of households have an income above the cost of Syria’s Minimum Expenditure Basket. 

Needs are particularly acute in urban and peri-urban slums where families, especially families headed by women, families with orphan children and IDP families are disproportionately affected, leaving them unable to provide for the basic needs of children. Needs are even more acute for these families at specific times during the year when they face growing expenses (e.g., during wintertime or prior to the school year). Post-Distribution Monitoring survey conducted in 2021 among beneficiaries of UNICEF multi-purpose cash interventions indicates much higher socio-economic vulnerability among female-headed households (FHH) than among male headed-households (MHH): over 40% of FHH were relying on charity, remittances or borrowing, compared to only 4% among MHH. The average monthly expenditure among FHH was 40% lower than among MHH. 

To respond to this situation, UNICEF is implementing a Basic Needs Support Programme, which main objective is to support highly vulnerable families in urban and peri-urban areas respond to the essential needs of their children and help them cope with the growing socio-economic hardship at critical times during the year to reduce their negative coping mechanisms.  

The programme has two components: (i) three-rounds of cash transfer to vulnerable families with children (0- 17 years old); and (ii) referral mechanism where the most vulnerable children and their families are accompanied and referred to social services in the communities. This referral component is critical to help families better respond to the needs of their children, beyond the cash transfer intervention, thus contributing to strengthen their resilience.

In 2021, UNICEF Post-distribution monitoring survey indicated that the top-ranked categories of expenditures with the cash transfer were as follows: 42% reported that the top category of expenditure was food, followed by 29% for clothing, 7% for medical expense, 6% for rent, 5% for debt repayment, and 5% for heating fuel.

In 2022 and 2023, the project aims to reach 30,000 families (over 150,000 people, including over 80,000 children) each year with cash assistance and referral services in urban and peri-urban slums in 5 Governorates.  

Building on the partnerships established in 2020 with a large network of national NGOs, UNICEF will identify vulnerable families through three targeting methods: (i) geographical targeting, focusing on areas with high severity of needs; (ii) categorical targeting (families with children); (iii) vulnerability targeting (families with greater socio-economic vulnerability such as FHH and families with orphan children)

The programme strategy is in line with the Multi-Purpose Cash interventions falling under the Food Security and Agriculture; Shelter/ NFIs and WASH sectors result framework 2022. UNICEF closely coordinates with the CWG at national & sub-national levels

Accountability to beneficiaries’ is ensured through three main channels: (i) redress and grievance mechanisms; (ii) Post Distribution Monitoring Surveys (PDMS); (iii) on-site monitoring activities.

The project targets 30,000 families each year disaggregated as follows: (i) 31% IDPs, 30% host communities, 39% returnees; (ii) 52% females, 48% males; (iii) 5% persons with disabilities. In 2022, the average severity scale in the sub-districts where the programme will be implemented is 3.5.

project_name: Provision of Child Protection Services to boys and girls affected by the conflict in Somalia.
project_objective:
Conflict, natural disasters, and COVID19 deterred Somalia from making significant development strides to benefit the most vulnerable population. The humanitarian context remains dire. Displacement, conflict, drought and famine have triggered family separation and exposed children to abuse, violence and exploitation as families resort to harmful coping mechanisms. Boys and girls endure multiple protection risks such as sexual and gender-based violence (GBV), child recruitment, mental and psychosocial distress. A trend analysis by the Country Task Force on Monitoring and Reporting covering 2016 to 2021 shows an alarming trend on grave violations, with 21,560 violations verified against 18,079 children (3,291 girls, 14,788 boys). 

In 2021, the protection cluster reported a 25 per cent increase in people in need of protection compared to the previous year, with children’s needs increasing exponentially. At least 607,546 children are in extreme need (26 per cent), 1,449,144 in severe need (61 per cent) and 302,440 in distress (13 per cent), and require humanitarian child protection assistance. Adolescents between 12 and 18 years are exposed to extreme violence, including recruitment and use by parties to the conflict, killing and maiming, child marriage and FGM. In 2021 alone, 631 children (97 per cent boys aged 11-17) were recruited and used, representing a 15 per cent increase compared to the same period in 2020. Preliminary findings of a UNICEF study on drivers of child recruitment show that Al-Shabaab explicitly targets children through forced recruitment and abduction. Rape and sexual violence remain a threat to children’s survival. At least 1 in 3 people in Somalia have mental health-related issues. In 2021 at least 40 per cent of child protection incidents reported to caseworkers were related to mental illness, physical abuse, and neglect. 
COVID19 precautionary measures such as closing schools and social services worsened the situation, exposing children to further risk. During the same period, the CTFMR recorded a 14 per cent increase in rape and sexual violence, with the Southern part of Somalia (Bay, Bakool, Gedo and Middle Juba) recording the highest number of cases. IDPs and minorities, including children with disabilities, remain particularly vulnerable. Integrated community-based responses addressing the multiple protection needs of children remain a priority in Somalia.

project_name: Delivering Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services and Information for Crisis -affected population in South Sudan.
project_objective:
As reported by the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) for South Sudan 2022, it is estimated that 5,467,710 people in South Sudan will require humanitarian healthcare services in 2022. Despite the huge humanitarian health needs, the health cluster will target 3,424,096 people with various health care services in different parts of the country.
The health cluster and its partners intend to reach this target population using two main sectoral objectives among others:
1)	Improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations.
2)	Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms.
UNFPA will partner with health cluster partners and other SRH partners to identify SRH needs, planning response and providing MISP services for the population in need. The SRH services will be delivered by procurement and distribution of IARH Kits through SRH partners in the prioritized counties. UNFPA will work with partners to ensure that beneficiaries have access to quality SRH services and information in the facilities where the IARH Kits are distributed. UNFPA will help partners in providing capacity building. 
UNFPA’s output on Crisis affected populations, particularly women and adolescent girls, have increased access to information and services for maternal health, family planning, gender- based violence and HIV prevention in emergency and fragile contexts and promoting humanitarian-development nexus will fit into the health cluster objectives.
Safe motherhood services including ANC visits and skilled delivery remain low with only 17% of pregnant women attending up to 4th visits and limited access to EmONC services and other factors explains why South Sudan has some of the worst health outcome indicators globally. The unmet need for family planning remains high at 24%. The needs for clinical management of rape and psychosocial services for survivors of sexual violence remains high. 
UNFPA will serve 821,783 women of reproductive age (WRA) group (15-49 years) of whom we expect 119,162 deliveries (17,876 deliveries out of the 119,162 will take place in health facilities), 89,371 women are currently pregnant, 58,347 WRA will attempt to use modern contraceptives, 49,134 people seeking care for STI syndromes, 17,879 women who will experience complications and about 16,436 cases of sexual violence who will seek care. UNFPA will also seek to reach 787,542 girls (476,300) and boys (311,242) with HIV prevention services and information, adolescent sexual and reproductive health services and information. Overall, UNFPA seeks to reach 1,609,325 affected people with various forms of SRH services and information through a well-coordinated mechanism for SRH at the national, sub national and county levels by the SRH technical working groups. Overall, 1,080 maternal deaths will be averted.
The main interventions to achieve the project purpose include, among others:
a) Ensuring availability of skilled staff and quality infrastructure for the provision of integrated SRH/GBV, including emergency obstetric care services at static health facilities and through outreaches.
b) Conducting community dialogues and health education for women, men, families and the community to increase awareness on service availability, benefits of safe sex, HIV prevention, family planning, ANC, PNC and delivery in a health facility by skilled birth attendants.
c) Procuring, prepositioning, and distributing a full range of IARH Kits and Non-Kit RH/maternal medicines and sundries essential for delivering SRH services at the community and health facilities, including RH equipment for EmONC (delivery beds, examination couches, lighting, and others).
d)Training service providers in SRH and GBV related topics.

project_name: Provision of Life-Saving Health and MHPSS Assistance to displaced populations, returnees and host communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The protracted conflict in South Sudan coupled with the 3 year unprecedented flooding and intercommunal violence has left left 8.9 million South Sudanese in need of Humanitarian assistance in 2022 (Draft HNO 2022). Additional shocks levied by the COVID-19 pandemic and on-going epidemic disease outbreaks including measles and Hepatitis E have further stretched existing coping mechanisms and increased vulnerabilities. Inspite of the many challenges, IOM's DTM have reported a mixed population flow reflecting increasing returns of IDPs and refugees in some of the counties including Raja, Morobo and Kajokeji counties.  Health service delivery for vulnerable populations remains heavily reliant on humanitarian assistance. In locations such as Unity, Jonglei and Upper Nile where the International Organization for Migration, IOM has been providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach locations across South  Sudan, populations remain displaced in IDP camps or to far off hard to reach locations due to flooding. IOM's life-saving health and MHPSS support to vulnerable IDPs and host community in Wau, Rubkhona and Malakal counties and through deployment of 9 Rapid Response Missions to crisis affected and IPC4 and IPC5 locations of Kajokeji, Nagero,Akobo, Ayod, Fangak, Mayendit, Panyijar, Twic East and Bor South reached a total of over1,205,302 beneficiaries including 652,055 outpatient consultations, 49238 measles, BCG and DTP3 does and 2542 assisted facility based deliveries in 2021. Through its Rapid Response Teams, IOM conducted 2 rounds of Oral cholera vaccination campaigns in Pibor and a pre-emptive measles vaccination campign in Yambio and Nzara counties to reach a total of 128,323 (62768 males, 65555 females) and 45,404 (22883males,22521 females) respectively. In 2022, IOM will target 865,998 beneficiaries including 130,000 persons with disabilities so as to continue to provide integrated emergency life-saving primary health care, including outpatient consultations, routine immunization, nutrition screening for children under five years, sexual reproductive health services, clinical case management of sGBV survivors including psychosocial support while increasing surveillance and response to disease outbreaks to underserved and conflict-affected IDPs, returnees, migrants/travelers, and host communities. 

IOM will provide health services through  10 static and 20 mobile clinics, while maintaining its comparative advantage in rapidly deploying rapid response teams to address emerging health needs through out the country. MHPSS services will be provided through existing recreational and counselling centers, and will deploy rapid response teams (RRT) to any areas across South Sudan facing acute man-made or natural disasters with unmet health needs. 
IOM will focus on leveraging existing community systems for sustainable solutions and strengthening both community based health initiatives and mental health and psychosocial support. Therefore, IOM will provide direct service delivery in partnership with the respective county health departments, while MHPSS will utilize static and mobile service in coordination with key humanitarian and developmental partners so as to avoid overlaps and ensure accountability to affected populations.

project_name: CCCM Assistance to conflict and disaster-induced displaced persons in South Sudan
project_objective:
According to Round 11 of IOM DTM’s monitoring of displacement and return movement, 2,017,236 people remain displaced in South Sudan, 78% of which are sheltering with already crisis-affected host communities. In a number of displacement sites and collective centers, including current and former PoCs, more than 440,000 individuals continue to live in situations of protracted displacement. Displacement figures have continued to increase despite the signing of the R-ARCSS in 2018 due to an increase of displacement-inducing incidents such as sub-national conflict and unprecedented climate-related disasters.

IOM CCCM aims to target 523,000 people of the total 1.4 million people targeted under the CCCM Cluster Response Plan. IOM will continue to provide displaced communities with basic and emergency camp management services, ensuring that the provision of protection and cross-sectoral humanitarian assistance is equitable, coordinated, monitored and adhering to standards. Of critical relevance to the current displacement environment in the country, IOM CCCM’s interventions will also integrate a robust, community-led disaster-mitigation lens in all care & maintenance interventions and capacity building exercises to enhance protective environments to increase resilience of infrastructure and communities to climate shocks. Further, fully committed to ensuring that AAP is streamlined in any and all activities, IOM will continue to develop and improve AAP mechanisms to ensure that the organization is accountable to the people that it serves and that programmes are informed by the voices of the displaced communities.

IOM intends to contribute to the sectoral objectives through the following interventions:

1)	Continued and adapted provision of critical CCCM activities to IDPs living in Bentiu, Naivasha and Hai Masna IDP Sites as well as critical care & maintenance activities in Malakal PoC.
2)	Deployment of emergency CCCM teams to deliver sustainable mobile responses promoting self-governance, community ownership and resilience in hard-to-reach locations following triggers at the ICCG-level.
3)	Co-lead the CCCM Cluster at national level and continue acting as SFP in WBeG, Jonglei and Upper Nile States in order to support national and state-level partner agencies in accountable CCCM responses and systems.
4)	Continue chairing the CCEWG in order to provide technical CCE support to partner organizations and to operationalize outputs under the 2021 South Sudan AAP Framework.

project_objective:

In water domain, rehabilitation of boreholes and construction of small water supply network powered with solar energy will be prioritized. On hygiene and sanitation issues, communities approached for total sanitation will be implemented at municipality level. Construction of community latrines and showers will be limited to IDP sites. Hygiene promotion with distribution of minimum WASH kits will be implemented in target communities. The area targeted cover the division of Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari. With these interventions, this project targets 60,000 people for access to safe water, 50,000 people for acces to adequate basic sanitation and 150,000 people reached with critical WASH supply (including hygiene items) and services. 
This project will also include a component relative to capacity building of WASH actor at regional level on key issues such as design, installation and maintenance of solar system for water supply, cholera response, flood response, protection and gender mainstreaming in WASH sector.

project_name: Contribution à la fourniture de service de prévention et de protection des enfants affectés par les situations d’urgence et la COVID 19 dans la région du Nord, du Centre-Est et des Cascades au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso est confronté à une crise humanitaire sans précédent liée à une augmentation soudaine de violences et la présence de divers groupes armés. Les effets de cette crise créent une situation d'urgence humanitaire qui touche toutes les couches sociales, femmes, jeunes, enfants, personnes âgées. 
Selon les données du CONASUR au 31 septembre 2021, 1 407 685 de personnes déplacées internes ont été enregistrées dont 860 481 enfants soit 61,13%.  Au niveau des régions, on enregistre 128 162 PDI au Nord, 32 352 PDI dans le Centre-Est et 15 596 PDI dans les Cascades.

Cette situation préoccupante exige une réponse d’urgence rapide d’où la proposition du présent projet.
Le projet vise à améliorer les conditions de vie de 43 000 enfants affectés par les situations d'urgence et le covid-19 dans la région du Nord, du Centre-Est et des Cascades. Pour ce faire, le projet sera mis en œuvre avec une approche communautaire et holistique qui mettra les enfants, leurs communautés et les services techniques de l’Etat au centre de l’intervention.

project_name: Cash Assistance to Vulnerable Community Groups in Gaza Strip to Cover Their Essential Needs, and Restore Their Livelihood Assets.
project_objective:
This proposed action aims to urgently respond to the current rising critical needs among severely impacted households (HHs) to enhance their access to food and other basic needs and restore their livelihood capacities. 


This project will build upon Mercy Corps’ current Cash Programme under the umbrella of Gaza Protection Consortium (GPC), which responds to continually increasing needs amongst targeted vulnerable groups, including those whose situation has been severely exacerbated by COVID-19 and recent hostilities.


Through unconditional cash assistance, this project will identify and select the most vulnerable households (HHs) in two groups of acutely vulnerable HHs from Gaza, Middle Area, Khan Younis, and Rafah governorates: i) vulnerable farmers and breeders in close coordination with Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) and ii) vulnerable HHs from the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) unserved or underserved waiting lists of Social Safety Net (SSN) with focus on Female-Headed Households (FHHs).

Through this project, Mercy Corps and its local NGO partners – Gaza Culture and Development Group and Al Foukhary Association for Country Development – will target 1,125 vulnerable HHs (6,188 individuals), broken down as follows: 

1)	300 eligible vulnerable Farmer and Breeder HHs identified through combined HH vulnerability assessment and livelihood technical assessment. Each selected Farmer and Breeder HH will receive an average amount of $1,500 in three installments. Each installment comprises $500 (~ ILS 1,600) restricted cash for livelihood assets restoration. 
2)	825 Highly vulnerable and crises affected HHs will receive a total amount of $1,300 over a period of four months (ILS 1,046 monthly installments in line with the Cash Working Group (CWG) endorsed MEB 2.0 Transfer Value).

This critical cash support will allow vulnerable HHs to have flexible, reliable, and timely financial support to address their urgent needs, restore their livelihoods, build resilience, and restore agriculture production capacity. Cash installments will be distributed through Electronic Debit Cards (e-cards) or via Cash over Counter through Bank of Palestine, which has extensive geographic coverage and is highly accessible through ATMs and Branches in North Gaza and Gaza. 

By utilizing cash as a modality for direct assistance, beneficiaries have greater power to determine how to meet their own urgent needs, empower them, and maintain their dignity while reducing their vulnerability and contributing to the restoration of their food security. Additionally, in the Gaza Strip, local markets are functional, and vendors continue to have adequate stock available; therefore, cash assistance is an appropriate humanitarian response modality to meet critical basic needs.

Through well-established evidence-based vulnerability and technical targeting, the project will use the Proxy Means Test Formula (PMTF), and Technical Vulnerability Assessment Tool (TVAT) to identify, assess and verify selected vulnerable HHs to receive cash assistance, monitor activities, and ensure full coordination and engagement with the community and primary stakeholders. Mercy Corps will be the focal point of coordination with MoSD, and local partners will coordinate closely with MoA to cross-check names of affected households and affected Farmers and Breeders.

Additionally, Mercy Corps will promote community ownership, accountability, and participation throughout the project through baseline assessments, orientation sessions, Post Distribution Monitoring, and its Community Accountability and Reporting Mechanism (CARM), while also mobilizing key stakeholders to more deeply engage with identified vulnerable HHs.
