project_name: Protection of civilians against explosive weapons in Syria
project_objective:
Throughout 2021 Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA) established a humanitarian Mine Action and Disarmament (MAD) programme in Syria. NPA’s newly established programme will operate in territories currently under the control of the Government of Syria (GoS) with the primary objectives of protecting civilians from the impact of explosive ordnance (EO) and ensure safe access to livelihood opportunities and basic infrastructures for Syrian civilian population.
In 2022, NPA plans to start its operational phase which will focus primarily on recruitment and training national teams who will conduct survey and clearance of EO contaminated areas as identified under the Syrian Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and in coordination with the UN Mine Action Area of Responsibility (AoR) and UNMAS for the 2022 implementation period.
Currently 70% of all people in need of mine action and EO intervention, are living within Government controlled areas, according to the recent 2021 Mine Action analysis of need. More than a decade of civil conflict in Syria has left the country heavily contaminated. Improvised landmines, Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), cluster munitions and wide variation of other EO affect all 14 governorates of the country. The contamination is particularly dense in areas previously held by the Islamic State, with both rural and urban areas impacted. Reports from Aleppo, Hama and Homs indicate a significant amount of contamination left by all sides of the conflict, as do reports from Daraa in the southern parts of the country, as well as from Rural Damascus. Moreover, these extremely high needs are not matched with the presence on the ground of qualified, professional humanitarian mine action actors that can address the problem in an efficient and timely manner. NPA's intervention aims at responding to these needs by ensuring the mapping, marking and safety removal of landmines, IEDs and other EO in full compliance with international standards and best practices.
Throughout the entire project period (2022-23) NPA will deploy, a total of twenty Multi-tasks Teams (MTTs) in conflict affected areas in order to protect the Syrian civilian population from the threats posed by landmines, cluster munitions (CM), improvised explosive devices (IEDs), and other explosive ordnances (EO). During the first year NPA will recruit, train and deploy ten MTTs teams to be deployed in Damascus and Rural Damascus governorates and according to the needs and priorities identified during the assessment phase (Jan-April). The second year of the project period NPA, in coordination with relevant UN agencies and local authorities, envisages of expanding its area of operations and recruit ten additional MTTs teams to be deployed in Homs governorate.
Each NPA MTTs teams will consists of eight team members and will be capable of performing non-technical survey, technical survey, mine clearance, battle area clearance, high risk search, Explosives Ordinance Disposal and Improvised Explosives Device Disposal. The work of the MTTs teams' will be guided by strict prioritizations criteria in order to target those people most in need of mine action and EOD/IEDD interventions. In line with these principles, NPA will primarily allocate its limited financial and operational resources in communities reporting explosive contamination in severity scales 3, 4
and 5.
Since the beginning of the programme NPA established a sound quality management system to ensure high quality and safety of clearance operations on the ground. In addition, NPA's work in Syria is guided by a robust conflict sensitive and “do no harm” approach which takes into account relevant risks and identifies corresponding mitigating measures. Finally, NPA Syria ensures a diverse work environment with staff of different gender, ethnic and religious backgrounds from a wide range of age groups.

project_name: Gender sensitive Water and Sanitation (WASH) services for conflict and flood affected population in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will contributes to WASH cluster strategy with main objective to improve access to gender sensitive WASH services to reduce water and sanitation related morbidity and mortality as well as to reduce protection risks for women and girls. The project will be integrated within Concern on-going multi-sector emergency response in Aweil South, Aweil West and Aweil North Counties in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG); Rubkona and Guit counties in Unity; and Kajo-Keji County in Central Equatoria State. 

Concern will continue to support routine operations and maintenance (O&M) of an existing borehole in Sector-5 of Bentiu IDP camp (hosting 27,000 people), continued support in waste management and repair & maintenance of sanitation facilities in IDP camp  with continued efforts in implementation of WASH cluster transition strategy for IDP camp. Under Current SSHF funded Grant, Concern is hiring a consultant to formulate strategy on community based sanitation management in sector-5 of IDP camp.  Concern will engage with the community as per WASH cluster transition strategy to ensure that the management and ownership of sanitation facilities is transferred to the community with formation of sanitation committee and explore potential for user fee structure for regular maintenance. 

In Rubkona and Bentiu, Concern will continue the provision of safe water through operation of water treatment plant in Bentiu and the surface water treatment system in Rubkona with continued efforts to transfer water management responsibility to state authorities. Concern will also continue water and sanitation services in newly flood displaced camp in Bentiu/Rubkona in collaboration with WASH cluster and other partners. In Guit County, Concern will support repair of boreholes including enhancing resilience of hand pumps to recurrent flooding. In NBeG, Concern will engage with existing trained water management committee (WMC) to repair dysfunctional hand pumps in Aweil North, Aweil West and Aweil South Counties. Concern will continue to implement Community Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) in Aweil North and Aweil Counties. Given the influx of returnees in Kajo-Keji, Concern will repair dysfunctional hand pumps in the catchment areas of health facilities supported by Concern. 

Context specific hygiene promotion based on best practices from international Behavior Change Communication (BCC) standards will be integrated with all sector level interventions to sensitize household on hygiene practices and COVID-19 awareness and prevention. The hygiene promotion will be integrated within nutrition and health interventions where the nutrition staff, CNVs, mother/fathers groups and health staff will be trained to promote hygiene awareness across all target locations. Similarly, the water and sanitation system in health and nutrition centers will be improved in Concern supported health and nutrition centers across all target locations.

project_name: Enhancing capacities of women, men, girls, and boys in IPC 3, 4 and 5 in South Sudan to withstand and recover from food insecurity
project_objective:
Project Summary The proposed HRP 2022 interventions will target locations with IPC 4 and 5 with emergency food security and livelihoods assistance to the most vulnerable populations affected by shocks including floods, conflicts which has contributed to the elevation of food insecurity outcomes with 31 counties of extreme or severe concern and 36 very high or high concern. The convergence of shocks such as floods, conflicts, hyperinflation of prices for basic commodities and now compounded with social and economic impact of Covid 19 at glance have made the population vulnerable deepening the humanitarian situation. The proposed interventions are aligned to the HRP 2022 cluster objectives; CO1: Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations, CO2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support and CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks. The project is planned to be implemented in Kajo Keji, Yirol east, Akobo, Pibor, Uror, Nyirol, Rumbek centre, Pochalla.
This HRP project will complement Oxfam ongoing resilient programming to provide immediate quick impact activities while protecting the gains of resilience programming. Protection and Gender will be mainstreamed throughout the project lifetime, a Do No Harm approach as enshrined in Oxfam safe programming approach will be mainstreamed by ensuring participation and accountability to affected population. This project will be implemented by Oxfam and its local partners.

project_name: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management in Somalia through Improved Climate Data Analysis
project_objective:
FAO Somalia will support the humanitarian efforts in Somalia through Enabling Programs to address the impact of flood and drought on vulnerable communities through the use of technology and communication. This project will contribute to the Enabling Programs Cluster’s strategic objectives 2 and 3 by producing humanitarian products including reports and updated data available for public use to inform near-real time, effective programming.  

The proposed project objective is to reduce drought and flood impacts through the use of FAO Early Warning information. Currently, Somalia is facing the third consecutive poor rainfall season after two poor rainy seasons in Deyr 2020 and Gu 2021. This is followed by two significant flood events earlier in 2020. With the climate change projections calling for an increase in wet and drier than normal seasons in the country, this pattern of alternating droughts and floods is highly likely to continue taking place in Somalia. Such sequential events have had hazardous impacts, eroding resilience, economic reserves, livestock herd size, and health.  

With this in mind, this project proposes to improve the technical capacity for forecasting climate hazards in Somalia.  Also, it aims to scale up the use of modernized early warning systems and climate information to save lives and enhance livelihoods in vulnerable communities through expansion of hydro-meteorological monitoring network that will generate data which will be used in turn in the production of early warning information for early action. To sustain this, FAO will develop standard operating procedures (SOPs) together with the disaster management agencies (DMAs) and improve contingency planning based on improved forecasts and warnings. Further SWALIM will develop feedback mechanisms for improving products/services, processes and SOPs. 

In Somalia climate change related hazards impacts disproportionately affect poor and vulnerable communities and are compounded by contributing factors such as population increase, unmanaged migration, land-use change, reduced soil health, accelerated groundwater extraction, widespread ecological degradation and biodiversity loss. In 2019, SWALIM established two Information Management Centers (IMCs) in Puntland and Somaliland to support the authorities and communities to adapt to climate change and variability impacts through sustainable watershed management approaches. This project is seeking to support the established IMCs in Puntland and Somaliland in collecting, analyzing and dissemination of land and water resources information.  This support will also be extended to the Somali National Bureau of Statistics (SNBS) institution which has been mandated to take over FAO SWALIM activities in the near future.

project_name: Supporting evidence-based humanitarian assistance in Libya
Provision of primary health care services for vulnerable children and women in Syria
project_objective:
After 11-year crisis of in Syria, there is an increased risk of disease outbreaks due to population movement and the erosion of public services and infrastructure. The COVID-19 pandemic and the worsening economic situation are further stretching and disrupting the already fragile health system in Syria, thus affecting the availability and quality of health services, as well as the physical and mental wellbeing of the population. 
There are 12.23 million people in need of health services in 2022, including 4.4 million displaced persons, 1.33 million CU5 years – including an estimated 503,000 live births expected. Youth and young persons, which comprise 1.98 million of the Health Sector people in need are reporting increasing stress and mental health concerns. Under-funding of response agencies has also left the 438k Palestine refugees living in Syria in acute need. The economic crisis also added to the vulnerability of Syrian children and women who are not able to pay for the essential health and nutrition services. (reference: FINAL DRAFT 2022 HNO Sector Template Health Sector 23 November)
This proposal from UNICEF aims to support the provision of basic lifesaving curative, preventive and promotional health services and practices, while enhancing early recovery and resilience of the sector by contributing to:
1. strengthening service delivery to vulnerable population who can not afford paying for health services, specifically children, 
2. supporting community health delivery platforms, including volunteers and trying to include and integrate them within the health facilities to ensure sustainability of those voluntary services
3. supporting health services and interventions for best delivery, including information, supply and monitoring & evaluation. this will help in improving the quality of services for the most vulnerable
The safety of the health workers who are providing maternal and child health services (including newborn care) is also considered through activities which ensure that all health workers are empowered with knowledge on diseases prevention and health promotion. It is also conceived with a view to promoting the complementarity of the contributions of other sections and multi-sectoral integration within UNICEF & other key sector partners.
The project will provide health services to boys, girls and women with disabilities on an equal basis.
UNICEF will be working through local NGOs who run 36 fixed health centres and 47 mobile teams across all the 14 governorates, including in NES and NWS and will focus to support the implementation of the immunization programme for children under the age of 1 year, and supplementary immunization activities (national immunization days and catch-up campaigns) for the CU 5 years
More than five million women and children will directly benefit from the package of services, focusing on the highest severity districts as defined by the Health Cluster/Sector and in integration with UNICEF prioritized high severity sub-districts across its seven sectors. Programme effectiveness shall be enhanced by applying a conflict and risk informed lens to planned interventions, and the promotion of the participation of affected populations. The accountability towards affected population is integrated throughout the programme cycle, UNICEF started to collect information from the affected population on the quality of the services through hotlines, SMS and complaint boxes in fixed clinics of NGOs.
UNICEF will work in 258 sub districts, including 170 with a severity scale of 3 or higher and 88 in a lower severity scale but which are hosting IDPs who need to be supported.
UNICEF will monitor the project through programme monitoring visits and financial spot checks by UNICEF staff, in addition to the third-party monitors and facilitators who will do regular field visits. UNICEF established hot lines to receive feedback from beneficiaries to improve the quality of services and to follow-up on violations.

project_name: Enhance the WOS Nutrition Sector Coordination mechanism for effective, integrated and harmonized nutrition response at scale.
project_objective:
The deteriorating nutrition situation in the Whole of Syria (WOS) calls for a robust coordination mechanism that will enhance provision of an equitable, inclusive and high-quality response at scale. The nutrition sector estimates that 5.5 million vulnerable children and women, including 0.8 million with disabilities will require life-saving nutrition services in 2022. The Nutrition sector through this project, and in line with the six core functions of cluster coordination as outlined by the Inter-Agency Steering Committee (IASC) will provide leadership to Nutrition Sector through the below strategy.

Coordination and Information management: UNICEF as the Nutrition Sector lead agency will coordinate the response planning process in the three hubs of north-west Syria (NWS), Damascus and WOS to clearly articulate the needs analysis, response gaps, and development and harmonization of technical and operational strategies for the response. In collaboration with other sector leads, the nutrition sector lead agency will advocate for availability of required human and financial resources as well as other strategic issues that will provide an enabling environment for a quality response at scale. The sector coordination team will strengthen the reporting systems among Ministry of Health (MOH) and partners through use of nutrition information systems and 4Ws that will enable generation of information products for an evidence driven response. To the best extent possible, this project will support the decentralization of coordination mechanisms to lower levels to ensure a harmonized, coordinated, and inclusive response. The coordination from Damascus Hub will be undertaken at national and sub-national levels through 5 sub-national sector coordinators covering Government of Syria (GOS) controlled areas.

Strengthening nutrition resilience: From a vantage point of leading the WASH and Education Sectors, UNICEF-the nutrition sector lead agency will provide the required inter-sector  support to partners in coordination with Ministry of Health to develop and adopt evidence-based strategies to address malnutrition from a multi-sectorial approach. Through collaboration and coordination with the Food Security and Health sectors, the sector lead will coordinate the development and harmonization of strategies to sustainably address determinants of ill health and sub-optimal consumption of quality diets among vulnerable women and children , both of which are major drivers of malnutrition in Syria.

Implementation of the localization agenda: In line with humanitarian principles and ‘Do No Harm’ approach, the sector lead will strengthen the technical and operational capacities of local actors to coordinate, plan and implement a high quality integrated nutrition response strengthening facilities and services as guided by the nutrition sector response plan to build the resilience of children, families and communities. The sector lead will also advocate for improved funding channels directly to local organizations, including women lead community-based organizations.

Capacity building and technical support: Through a robust capacity mapping exercise, the sector lead will work in coordination with the Ministry of Health  and sector partners to address response capacity and coverage gaps in order to deliver high quality response. 
		
Contingency planning: In collaboration with other sectors, the nutrition sector will conduct risk mapping and analysis and develop scenario based contingency plan to strengthen the collective sector’s preparedness capacity. The plan will be updated with on-gong nutrition sensitive surveillance system.

Accountability to affected population (AAP) and considerations of gender and specific groups/children with disability: The sector lead will support and coordinate the mainstreaming of AAP in the nutrition response through ensuring inclusive consultation and engagement of the affected population in the entire project cycle.

project_name: Education Coordination for a predictable, holistic and well-coordinated response in Syria
Responding to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene  needs of  Women, Girls, men and boys  in South Sudan.
project_objective:
As stated in the Humanitarian Needs Overview of 2022, more than two-thirds of South Sudan's population, 8.9 million people, need humanitarian assistance, an increase of 600,000 since 2021.Findings from the 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview showed a sustained deterioration of people’s physical and  mental wellbeing. In the 2022 HRP, ALIGHT proposes to undertake life-saving interventions to affected populations targeting IDPs and returnees living in IDP like situations while engaging the host community and more settled returnees in activities geared towards resilience building. Resilience building and preparing the community for takeover will be realized through capacity building and building water structures that serve both short-term response to emergency situations while building water and sanitation structures that last beyond the emergency phase. These will include boreholes that are solar powered with minimal operation and maintenance costs. In sanitation, ALIGHT has a positive experience working with communities in Kajo-Keji and Budi through CLTS to build household latrines that are of a more permanent nature. WASH needs will be identified through data collection and analysis in the course of implementation of the ongoing intervention and periodic assessments conducted jointly by UNOCHA and other partners. Over a period of four years, Alight has been implementing an integrated intervention among its sectors of WASH, GBV and Nutrition and will continue and strengthen this approach. This proposal targets geographical locations where Alight is implementing both GBV and Nutrition or either of the two. This makes it easier for implementation and integration of the three sectors (WASH, GBV and Nutrition) critical in addressing humanitarian situations resulting from drought, flooding, or displacements due to conflicts. ALIGHT promotes technical/ infrastructure solutions with the people from the communities, employing human-centered and interactive approaches in hygiene and sanitation promotion such as the PHAST, Wash’em and Super Momas; and gender balanced-community lead operation and maintenance practices. Involving the community at the   design stage builds confidence, transparency and an atmosphere of trust and is a statement of Accountability to Affected Persons. In this HRP plan, ALIGHT Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) sector will provide services to men, women, boys, and girls IDPs, returnees and host communities in Kajo-Keji in Central Equatorial State, Budi and Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatorial State and Aweil West in Northern Bar Ghazal. Besides ALIGHT having presence in the selected areas, Kajo-Keji county where ALIGHT has its major humanitarian response is reported to receive the highest number of returnees in the past six (6) months as per UNHCR/RRC spontaneous return monthly bulletins of October 2021. ALIGHT, as the deep field focal point for UNOCHA in Kajo-Keji has funding support from BHA/USAID, UNHCR, WFP and UNICEF for GBV, WASH, general protection, and Nutrition. Services targeting IDPs, returnees and host community. Similar responses are on-going in selected counties of Budi and Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatoria for GBV and WASH. In Northern Bar Ghazal, ALIGHT is operating ten nutrition centers in Aweil West and one women center in Aweil Center with extensive outreach activities in the outlying villages. WASH has strengthened integration by working with women and adolescent girls on operation and maintenance of WASH facilities and promoting hygiene at the centers.
The WASH sector is responsible for the development, operation, and maintenance of WASH facilities in these centers. Covid 19 pandemic has brought challenges including limited community interactions. ALIGHT has been able to work with the community to introduce and encourage practices that limit the possibility of Covid- 19 spread. These include regular hand washing and social distancing. Use of masks during training has been enforced.

project_name: Provision of Comprehensive and Integrated Primary and secondary Health Services to Conflict-affected, Displaced and Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan.
project_objective: IMCs provide comprehensive, integrated primary and secondary health care services through static health facilities complemented by regular mobile outreach to increase and expand fair coverage and access, especially for displaced or hard-to-reach populations with intermittent periods of stability and weather-constrained access. Aligned with the 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for South Sudan, IMC's health care interventions are designed to (1) Improve equitable access to lifesaving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to crisis-affected populations to approximately 550,000  conflict-affected, displaced and vulnerable host population in Juba, Malakal, and Wau displacement camps, as well as in Canal/Pigi, Akoka, Balliet and Panyikang Counties (2) Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by improving the capacity of the country's health system for early detection preparedness and response with COVID-pandemic and other disease outbreaks, (3) Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms. IMC will continue to provide Primary and Secondary  health care services integrated with Nutrition, SGBV and MHPSS across its 26 supported health facilities in the states of Central Equatoria (Juba IDP Camps, Khor Williang PHCC), Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau IDP camp), Jonglei (Canal/Pigi County), and Upper Nile (Malakal PoC and County, and Akoka, Balliet and Panyikang Counties). These services will include Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI), outpatient consultation for communicable and non-communicable diseases, endemic diseases, trauma, injuries, community-based education at the facility and in the community. Provide the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) at static health facilities and outreach; Provision of Sexual and Reproductive health services across Juba (IDP and Khor Williang health facilities), Malakal (PoC and Malakal Teaching Hospital), , Wau IDP, canal PIGI   sites for vulnerable populations, especially women of reproductive age (15-49 years). IMC will focus on health facilities, Mobile outreach teams, and community-based intervention to ensure access, availability, and utilization of appropriate reproductive health services. Access to treatment and care of chronic disease for patients as well as trauma and injury related services will be provided in all  IMC project proposed sites. Provision of  comprehensive integrated mental health and psychosocial support services, including psychiatric emergency services for in- and outpatients will be done all static health facilities through skilled MHPSS Workers with the guidance of MHPSS Specialist. The facilities will also be supported with  essential psychotropic  drug supplies. IMC will provide Community health education and social-behavioral Change communication helps for disease prevention and health promotion activities,facilitate referrals of pregnant women to a health facility for antenatal, delivery and postnatal services.IMC currently provides advanced emergency obstetric and newborn care, trauma care, trauma surgery, and rehabilitation for major injuries and basic surgical care at the Operating Theatres. These OTs will serve as final referral points for general surgery and obstetric emergencies in the displacement camps and beyond, including the nearby counties/states. All of IMC's interventions will have a particular focus on vulnerable persons, such as women of reproductive age, pregnant and lactating women, children under 5, and people with particular needs and vulnerabilities, adolescents, people living with disabilities, survivors of sexual abuses, minorities, and marginalized groups and Adults, displaced people, and host communities.

project_name: Integrated emergency lifesaving primary health care services to the vulnerable communities of Upper Nile, South Sudan.
project_objective:
This intervention aims at improving equitable access to and utilization of health services through five fixed primary health care facilities including Rirnyang Primary Health Care Unit (PHCU) in Ulang County, Kiechkuon Primary Health Care Centre (PHCC) , Makak PHCU, and Wandeng PHCU in Nasir and Jekow PHCU in Maiwut. To scale-up health care services in Nasir, Longechuk, Maiwut, and Ulang Counties, RI will establish eight Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) and implement Integrated Community Case Management (ICCM) activities to serve the hard-to-reach population. The project will target 53,052 (10,113 women, 16,954 girls, 14,798 boys, 10,447 men, 740 PWDs) , vulnerable individuals. RI will recruit and deploy qualified health workers including clinical officers, nurses, midwives, community health workers, and vaccinators to all supported fixed facilities and mobile medical units. Boma health workers will be selected at the community level to implement Boma health initiative and ICCM activities across the 4 counties. 
The intervention will further focus on continuous screening and treatment of communicable and non-communicable diseases through patient consultations. The intervention will also provide the management of injuries, antenatal care, skilled deliveries, postnatal care, and clinical management of rape (CMR) services in the health facilities and mobile medical units. The intervention will also integrate and strengthen mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and services for people with disabilities. 
The project will continue streamlining and strengthening the referral pathways for MHPSS, sexual and gender-based violence survivors and, maternal and child health emergencies. RI’s health team, through this response, will conduct routine and outreach immunization services to children under 59 months of age. Throughout the provision of health services, RI will ensure Covid-19 prevention and appropriate response activities are integrated while continuing to provide essential lifesaving health services. All fixed health facilities, MMUs and ICCM will be equipped with Infection Prevention and Control, Water, sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) materials, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials on Covid-19 to further strengthen the prevention. Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention, surveillance, and response readiness will be continued as part of disease outbreak, prevention and response. The health activities will be coordinated closely with the RI WASH and nutrition teams to ensure integration of interventions for more effective community mobilization and sensitization on health-related messaging including COVID-19 prevention, availability of immunization services, ANC, skilled deliveries, CMR services, and MHPSS. This project will engage all communities in the targeted counties throughout the implementation stages to enable the sustainability of the program. Patient Exit Interviews will be conducted at fixed facilities and MMUs. RI will also implement community feedback mechanisms such as regular community consultative meetings, feedback boxes and Accountability to Affected Persons (AAP) groups to continue providing feedback and complaints. For the successful implementation of this project, RI will engage the communities during the selection of Mobile medical unit (MMUs) sites and also seek for community support to provide storage spaces for the essential drugs and MMU equipment. The selected MMUs and health facilities will be equipped with essential medical equipment, drugs and test kits. All healthcare staff ( RI will aim to have at least 50% female staffing) will be trained in the core protection principles, including 'Do No Harm'.”

project_name: Emergency Health Support to Vulnerable Communities in Koch and Rubkona Counties in Unity State and Fangak and Canal Pigi Counties in Jonglei State.
project_objective: A total of 422,594 (Male: 210,581,Female: 212,013) people are in need of health services in Fangak, canal pigi, Koch, and Rubkona counties out of which 69,377(Male 30,045,Female 39,332) are children under five years of age. A third consecutive year of flooding has negatively impacted the health status of the populations living in these counties as many of the social facilities; health and nutrition facilities, boreholes, latrines have been destroyed. Many families have been displaced to higher dry areas and are living without access to safe drinking water and sanitation facilities. They are being exposed to waterborne and vector-borne diseases. Increased snake bites due to an increase in swampy environment. Lack of essential medicines and medical supplies are the many challenges facing the flood affected populations. Recent incidences of inter-communal fights and cattle raiding in Koch have worsened the humanitarian situation causing displacements and subsequent loss of livelihood and properties, an estimated 12,198 individuals in (2.033HHs) are said to be in critical need of humanitarian assistance according to the December 2021 IRNA report. Bentiu IDP Camp is currently surrounded by floodwaters and a large scale Malaria outbreak among this population is imminent. HEV transmission continue to persist within the IDP Camp with a surge in the number of cases since the beginning of 2021. In responding to the immediate health needs, this project will ensure the scaling of life-saving essential quality health care services to the population in Fangak, Canal Pigi, Koch, and Rubkona counties through the creation of mobile health outreach units in areas of flood-displaced persons in Fangak and Koch counties. Creation of two PHCUs in Canal Pigi County. Upgrading of Petpet PHCU into a PHCC in Koch county. Likewise health services in Phom will be re-stated and its PHCU will be upgraded  to a PHCC in Fangak County. Activities will also include post-flooding rehabilitation of water damaged facilities, formation of dykes around health facilities in Koch and Fangak counties and the  continued provision of healthcare services through static health facilities. One malaria point will be established in the Bentiu IDP Camp to serve cases during the peak of malaria season to decongest the large numbers of malaria patients going into the health facilities. This will help to enhance social distancing of patients, a pre-requisite to COVID-19 prevention. The project will target a total of 100,000 (Male:50,155, Female:49,845) people as direct beneficiaries, particularly women, children U5(17,000-7000 M, 10,000 F)  and people with disabilities( 15,000) . Primary services at WRSS-run health facilities will particularly focus on addressing the top three morbidities of malaria, acute watery diarrhea (AWD), and acute respiratory infection (ARI), as well as prevention and control of epidemic-prone diseases like Cholera, measles, EVD, HEV, and other outbreaks. MCH services, EPI, disease surveillance, and infection prevention and control. The response will strengthen local capacity to prevent, detect and respond timely to outbreaks; It will Finally integrate activities with WASH, Nutrition, FSL and Protection sectors to provide timely and promptly lifesaving interventions to vulnerable population in the prioritized locations. Referral mechanisms will be established or enhanced towards the care of vulnerable people with specific needs like SGBV survivors and SAM children with medical complications. The project will deliver health response to meet health cluster objectives of improving equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment of common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to crisis-affected populations; Activities will be monitored through well-coordinated supervision strategies together with the CHD, MOH and UN agencies.

project_name: Reduced excess morbidity and mortality among affected populations of the North West region and South West region of Cameroon
project_objective: The North West region and South West region of Cameroon are affected by a complex humanitarian crisis that has resulted in system wide breakdown of infrastructure and services especially in the health sector. This crisis has resulted in the displacement of over 1.1 Million people, especially women and children1.  Data from the MSNA conducted in February 2021, revealed that 199 (22%) out of 893 health centers were no longer functional2.  Attacks on healthcare is a common feature of this crisis and remains a major threat to the availability of healthcare in the North West region and the South West region.  There are limited specialized services to take care of victims of physical and mental trauma in these regions as the number of cases have been on the rise because of the crisis. This situation has been worsened by the COVID-19 Pandemic which has increased the burden on a health system that has already been fragilized by the humanitarian crisis. Three health districts (Ekondo Titi, Mbongue, Bakassi) have had cholera epidemics this year with case fatality rates sometimes reaching 40%. In the most of affected areas, health services are not available while less affected areas have health services of poor quality. This project aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality of internal displaced populations (IDP) and affected host communities in the North West and South West regions of Cameroon affected by the humanitarian crisis by ensuring a timely and equitable access to health care services. The project will target 373,069 IDPs persons (51% of this target are women, 16% are children under 5, and 11% are people over 60 years old). The areas of intervention will be Fako, Meme, Lebialem, Ndian and Kupe - Muanenguba divisions in the South-West region and Mezam, Momo, Bui, Ngo-ketunjia, Mechum and Boyo in the North-West region. The project will emphasize on timely access to equitable health care through mobile clinics in areas with no functional health facilities and the use of vouchers in areas where health facilities are operational.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan
project_objective:
UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards
in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation
and hygiene promotion services for con􀂧ict affected people, vulnerable host communities
and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including
protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to
cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project
will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline
emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination
including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving
support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster
standards.
The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host
communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related
GBV.
The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs
and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term
capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors
such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including
disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_name: Safe access to education and well-being for children and adolescents in Area C, Hebron, East Jerusalem and Gaza Strip
project_objective:
This project aims to respond to the education needs and well-being of the vulnerable school-aged children and adolescents in Area C, Hebron, East Jerusalem, and Gaza Strip to enable them to access education. 
The main drivers of education-related vulnerabilities include attacks on schools, movement restrictions, poor and/or inadequate classrooms, and WASH facilities, and poverty. These factors undermine the quality of education, generate protection concerns, and contribute to the early school dropout. 
This project will contribute to the 2022 HRP Education Objective 2: “Increase equitable safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children” and Education Objective 3: “Children and school staff in vulnerable schools are supported in preparing and responding to emergencies.

Several assessments show that the realization of the right to education remains severely compromised in these locations. The Education Cluster recorded 119 education-related incidents in 2020, affecting 7,757 students and 615 teachers and school staff. The lack of safe access has significant negative consequences for students’ schooling. It results in a decrease of school hours, increased dropout rate of children, discouraging teaching staff, and displacement or separation of families as they seek solutions in getting their children in schools elsewhere.
The need for MHPSS has been exacerbated by the COVID 19, the recent escalation in Gaza Strip, and the chronic protection challenges the children experience going to and from school as they cross Israeli military checkpoints and closed military zones or pass by settlements where they may experience harassment and violence as reported by the education cluster.
Furthermore, the outbreak of COVID-19 significantly compounded children’s vulnerabilities due to intermittent closures of schools as part of the measures adopted to contain the pandemic. As of the end of August 2020, 1.3 million children had lost at least three months of schooling. The move to online education also negatively impacted children from remote, disadvantaged areas of the West Bank and Gaza. Many students lack internet access, devices, and adequate digital literacy to effectively utilize the online learning opportunities. 

The project will ensure safe access to school for 31,000 students aged 6-16 and their teachers in H2, South Hebron Hills, Bethlehem, South Nablus, East Jerusalem, and other selected areas in the West Bank. They will be supported with a holistic package of interventions, including training school counselors, volunteers, and school teachers on child safeguarding, safe identification and referral, and Psychosocial Support interventions.

In partnership with local NGOs, UNICEF will support 30,000 vulnerable children and adolescents (40% females, 1% CWD) with Mental Health and Psychosocial (MHPSS) school-based activities. The MHPSS interventions will be implemented after school and during the summer vacation with support from the Ministry of Education and local implementing partners.
5,000 children (50 % girls) will be provided with remedial education interventions to mitigate the learning loss and improve their numeracy and literacy skills. 

The project will support over 60,000 poorest students in West Bank and Gaza aged 6-17 (50% girls), who may be at risk of dropout due to poverty, to continue in their education by providing basic, urgent school supplies, including stationery kits. These children, if not supported, are at risk of dropping out of school.

UNICEF, in partnership with local NGOs will support 300 schools to operationalize safe schools protocols to prevent infections, including COVID 19 and ensure safe learning environments for children. 1,500 schools will be provided with school hygiene kits to support them operationalize the COVID 19 protocols.

project_name: Integrated psychosocial support and child protection services for the most affected boys and girls in Gaza Strip
project_objective:
This project will support the delivery of quality, integrated child protection and psychosocial support (PSS) services to the most vulnerable boys and girls aged 4-18 in Gaza Strip, especially those affected by the May 2021 escalation, as well as COVID-19. The escalation has affected all aspects of life in the Gaza Strip, including child protection needs and services. 

The project will ensure that 12 family centres and 30 outreach sites in Gaza are fully operational, responding to the pressing mental health and psychosocial and child protection needs of 23,440 children (55% girls) and 5,480 caregivers (77% women).
Service delivery will be directed to the most affected locations and the most vulnerable children through a coordinated continuum of services in Gaza. Each family centre will be connected to a community-based child protection committee that informs the family centre of community child protection needs and acts as a focal point for identifying vulnerable children for referral. Family centres will operate through established Community-Based Organisations (CBOs) and outreach sites and will assess/screen and refer children for further services through:
1) a case management approach for the worst affected;
2) referral of complex child protection cases to child protection services (relevant stakeholders and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs); and 
3) referral of children with further psychosocial support needs to more specialized psychological support services. 

Services will also strengthen outreach capacities to detect and link up children in need with service providers while providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through the family centres. A total of 23,440 children (55% girls) and 5,480 caregivers (77% women) will be reached through the project.
This project aligns with and contributes to the Protection Cluster Objective Two, which calls for putting in place protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate occupation and conflict-related violence.

Ensuring compliance with PSEA principles and procedures, project beneficiaries will be oriented on sexual exploitation and abuse. They will receive information on UNICEF email and other interagency channels, including SAWA Free toll number, social media platforms, and WhatsApp to report on PSEA.

At least 70% of the project budget will be split equally between the two project implementing partners to ensure timely services are provided to children with the protection and MHPSS needs. The money will be transferred in line with UNICEF Harmonised Approach to Cash Transfer (HACT), which ensures close follow-up on expenditures, where only project-related activities are covered by the fund. Partners are normally micro-assessed and spot checks are regularly conducted to ensure compliance with the agreement.

project_name: Renforcement des capacités de reintégration des retournés et personnes deplacées internes du Burundi à travers l'accès au logement, terre et propriété et à la documentation civile
project_objective: L’accès à la terre au Burundi est une problématique majeure à la base de nombreux conflits, notamment intrafamiliaux. Ces problèmes se posent avec plus d’acuité dans un contexte de déplacement. Les ménages forcés de fuir leurs lieux de résidence habituels à la suite de catastrophes naturelles doivent trouver un logement adéquat.Pour l’année 2022, le sous-groupe Logement, Terres et Propriétés (LTP) cible 10 661 personnes pour recevoir une assistance. Parmi elles, 5 723 sont des femmes (représentant 54% de la cible) et 827 sont des personnes âgées (représentant 8% de la cible). 15% (1 599) de cette cible sont des personnes en situation d’handicap. La proportion des personnes déplacées internes est de 39% soit 4 173 personnes et les rapatriés/retournés représentent 61% (6 488 personnes). Afin de contribuer à l’atteinte de l’objectif sectoriel susmentionné, la stratégie de réponse du sous-groupe s’articulera principalement autour i) des activités de sensibilisation afin de renforcer les connaissances des populations cibles sur les thématiques LTP notamment, le droit foncier, le processus d’enregistrement des parcelles, les VBG associées à l’accès à la terre, ii) des actions de plaidoyers auprès des autorités locales et en charge des questions foncières dans les zones cibles pour faciliter l’accès à la terre et a des titres de propriété aux populations vulnérables et, iii) des appuis directs aux ménages les plus vulnérables dans le processus d’obtention de certificat foncier.  Aussi, la coordination sera renforcée avec le secteur abris et articles non alimentaires afin de s’assurer que, les ménages rencontrant des difficultés pour l’accès au logement soient appuyés à travers des appuis au loyer afin de leur garantir une sécurité foncière minimale et leur assurer des conditions de vie dignes et décentes. De plus, la facilitation de l’obtention de certificat de propriété aux populations cibles améliorera leur sécurité foncière et par conséquent, les mettra dans les meilleures dispositions pour un accès à des solutions durables notamment en ce qui concerne le logement. Etant donné le paquet d’activités à déployer pour la réponse au sein du sous-groupe LTP, l’assistance se fera via la modalité in-kind. Les populations affectées seront mises à contribution à toutes les étapes du processus conduisant à la réponse

project_name: Mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) aux mouvements de population au Mali
project_objective:
La présente action vise à répondre aux besoins immédiats et prioritaires des populations du centre, nord et sud du Mali affectées par les déplacements ou une restriction d’accès aux services sociaux de base à la suite de conflits ou de catastrophes naturelles soudaines, à travers le renforcement de la veille humanitaire en zones rurales comme en milieux urbains. Cela se traduira par le maintien et le renforcement d’un système efficace de veille et d’alerte sur les mouvements de population et des évaluations multisectorielles rapides des besoins incluant la protection, l’apport d’une  réponse multisectorielle rapide et coordonnée sous forme de transfert monétaire ou de distribution en nature dans les domaines de Biens Non Alimentaire (BNA), de Sécurité Alimentaire et de l’Eau, l’Hygiène l’Assainissement ainsi  que le monitoring de la qualité des interventions, et la coordination technique et opérationnelle du mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) aussi bien au niveau national que régional.
L’action assistera 72 000 personnes (12 000 ménages) dont 66 000 personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et 6 000 personnes affectées par des catastrophes naturelles soudaines. Ces personnes ciblées par cette action seront constituées de 55% des femmes dont 64% de filles et 45% d’hommes dont 64% de garçons. 
Les bénéficiaires de cette action seront sélectionnés selon l’approche de vulnérabilité individuelle (ménage) mixte (matérielle et sociale). Les familles d’accueil des PDI seront pris en compte selon leur vulnérabilité. Chaque assistance sera précédée d’une analyse de risque protection, et suivi d’un monitoring post distribution 21 jours après intervention par une équipe indépendante à celle de la mise en œuvre. Le cadre de redevabilité et l’approche Genre seront placés au cœur de la mise en œuvre de ce projet s’inspirant de la dernière action. 
La coordination avec les autres acteurs humanitaires est une partie intégrante de ce projet. NRC maintiendra ses efforts de coordination avec l’ensemble des acteurs pour renforcer l’efficacité et la cohérence de la réponse via une participation active aux clusters Sécurité Alimentaire, Abris/BNA, EHA, Education et Protection ainsi qu’aux groupes de travail CWG, Genre et Redevabilité.
NRC à travers ce projet, a développé plusieurs approches et outils pour améliorer la qualité de la réponse mais également pour renforcer la coordination sur terrain. NRC continuera de mettre en place la forte dynamique qu’il a poursuivi en 2021 afin d’aboutir à une harmonisation des approches et outils avec les différentes partenaires RRM et les Clusters. 
La réponse alimentaire sera constituée d’une ration complète pour un mois et cela pour tous les ménages ciblés proportionnellement à la taille de chaque ménage selon la ou les modalités issues de l’analyse des besoins et des risques. NRC pourra couvrir le deuxième et troisième cycle s’il n’y a pas d’autres acteurs du Cluster SA pour couvrir ces cycles et cela dépendra des résultats du PDM.
Pour le transfert monétaire et le coupon, le montant ou la valeur de coupon à donner aux ménages sera calculé sur base du panier de la ménagère de chaque zone en plus des frais de transfert (8% du montant à distribuer) ou du transport (5 000 CFA si l’assistance alimentaire seulement et 2500 CFA si l’aide est couplée avec les NFI) pour le coupon. Pour la distribution en nature, le kit alimentaire sera constitué des céréales, de légumineuses, de l’huile et du sel selon le standard du PAM et du Cluster lead auxquelles se réfère les lignes directrices du RRM. Pour répondre dans le délai, NRC a signé des accords-cadres avec les fournisseurs et cela au niveau de chaque site de déplacés. Cette assistance permettra de réduire la vulnérabilité des ménages déplacés en améliorant leur score de consommation alimentaire. Un kit de lavage des mains, composé d’un bouloir, de 6 gobelets et du savon sera systématiquement ajouté à ce paquet dans le cadre de la prévention de la Covid-19.

project_name: Provision of shelter and NFI support to communities affected by displacement and environmental shocks in Somalia and Somaliland.
project_objective:
As conflicts and recurrent environmental shocks continue to drive people out of their places of origin, resulting in unpredictable and sudden displacements, requiring a quick response from humanitarian actors to deliver essential relief.  According to the CCCM cluster, 2,241,328 people will need humanitarian assistance in 2022 due to the lack of durable solutions, continued conflicts, and recurrent shocks. 
As such, shelter and non-food item needs remain significant across displacement-affected communities in Somalia, with recurrent displacement trends underpinning protracted needs for shelter and NFI assistance in the proposed locations. Therefore, the proposed action will target locations in Kismayo, Hargeysa, Ceel Afweyn, Laasqoray and Baidoa districts. The project will benefit 16,446 individuals (2,741 HHs without double counting). Under this, ACTED proposes an in-kind distribution methodology instead of a voucher system to allow for prepositioning and rapid emergency response when the need arises. The storage and transportation of the materials to the distribution points and related costs are managed by the selected competent and qualified suppliers, a requirement in the contract signed between ACTED and the suppliers.  In parallel with the provision of emergency shelter and NFI support, and in line with the primary objective of working towards facilitating recovery and access to durable solutions, ACTED will provide transitional shelters to IDP households living on land protected by land tenure agreements in IDP sites that have stable land tenure agreements. Significant rates of eviction render durable shelter solutions appropriate only in cases where land tenure agreements exist and provide a critical foundation for persons facing protracted displacement in the assertion of pathways to recovery. 
In order to assess the efficiency of the assistance provided, level of satisfaction of the beneficiaries with the items received and the overall impact, ACTED will conduct post distribution monitoring 6 weeks after the distribution of ESK/NFI and post construction monitoring 3 months after the handover of transitional shelters to analyze the impact and draw lessons learnt for future programming.

project_name: Integrated access to quality basic education in a protective and inclusive environment for crisis affected children and youth
project_objective:
According to the 2021 Humanitarian needs overview report, it is estimated that 3 million school aged children need sustained equitable access to quality education in a protective learning environment. Out of these children, 2,419,059 are from non-displaced families and 667,891 are from displaced families. Despite the low caseload of IDPs, children living in IDP camps are particularly vulnerable to protection risks due to limited provision of services and poor living conditions. REACH 2021 site assessment shows low education service provision in IDP camps. This is the result of a lack of government support, and inadequate and short-term funding to support affected IDP school-aged children. 

It is estimated that 463,042 of the 3 million children in need of education are school aged children living with disabilities. Children with disabilities are significantly affected and face challenges to access an inclusive learning environment. Recent school screening identified prevalent negative attitudes towards children with disabilities by teachers and parents, and structural challenges that hinder these children to access an inclusive learning environment. According to rapid assessment conducted by Ministry of Education in Somaliland in September 2021 in drought affected areas shows 42 schools were closed due to drought. Findings from the assessment reveals 80% of the schools closed are in the rural areas (Sool, Sanag and Togdheer regions are among the regions where most of the schools closed are located). The findings from the assessment highlights that the main reasons for the school closure is due to the movement of the families as a result of the prevailing drought and lack of or inadequate number of school teachers. The HRP project will target areas with most marginalized and deprived communities (displaced and extremely poor host communities) in Southern states, Puntland and Somaliland. 

The project will provide safe and protective learning environments and access to life-saving services for children through an integrated approach targeting 95,600 children in the worst emergency affected areas and drought displaced children in South Central Somalia (47,800 (50% girls) Puntland (18,032; 50% girls) and Somaliland (29,636; 50% girls) 1,000 schools per area will be targeted in South Central Somalia, Puntland and Somaliland respectively (40:25:35).

SC will ensure school going children are retained in their current schools while those dropped out are re-enrolled. Children will be provided with access to safe drinking water, emergency school feeding, hygiene promotion and provision of teaching and learning materials. This is expected to mitigate and prevent children from dropping out from school as a result of the drought. The response will provide a protective learning environment through the construction of temporary learning spaces, distribution of teaching and learning materials, and support to teachers with emergency teacher incentives. 
The project will target 95,600 (50% girls) learners who are either dropped out or at risk of dropping out from school due to the impact of the drought. Psychosocial support services (PSS) will be provided for teachers, Community Education Committees (CECs), Child Welfare Committee (CWC), education officials in terms of case management, referral services for learners, especially in response to the drought impact and enhance their wellbeing. Community-led back-to-school campaigns will also be conducted to ensure that progress made on access to education is not lost.  SC will work with MoE to promote alternative education pathways for children who lost time out of school and will provided catch up and remedial classes to cope with their classmate. Emphasis will be given to IDP children, poor host community children, including children with disabilities and those marginalized children to ensure they are also reached with education services.

project_name: Projet d'assistance multisectorielle aux ménages affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions du Sahel, des Cascades et du Centre-Est du Burkina Faso
project_objective: L’objectif de l’action est de fournir une assistance alimentaire d’urgence de trois mois à 3.000 ménages déplacés qui sont sur les communes de Markoye et  Gorom-Gorom (région Sahel), de Sidéradougou (Cascades) et de Ouargaye (Centre-Est) là où des gaps d’aide humanitaire ont été identifiés. L’action ciblera aussi 1500 ménages hôtes hébergeant directement des ménages PDIs en leur sein. Les femmes enceinte/allaitantes et les enfants de 6-23 mois auront une assistance alimentaire améliorée et adaptée à leur condition. La période de soudure (juin-août) vient s’ajouter à cette situation, met en risque les moyens de subsistance et augmente le risque de conflits au sein des communautés. Cette action fournira aussi une assistance alimentaire ponctuelle à 2000 ménages locaux résidents qui ne peuvent pas répondre à leurs besoins alimentaires de base pendant cette période. La réhabilitation de 50 forages d’eau potable dans les zones à haute concentration de PDI fait aussi partie de l’action pour réduire la pression sur les ressources et pour garantir l’accès à l’eau. Afin de garantir l’accès à des infrastructures d’assainissement et appropriées, l’action visera également la réhabilitation de 5 blocs de latrines dans les formations sanitaires des zones ciblées.  Des activités de promotion de l’hygiène et de distribution de 3000 kits WaSh au profit des ménages déplacés s’ajoutera pour réduire les risques de propagation de maladies hydriques. L’action vise aussi à garantir la fonctionnalité, la continuité et la qualité de l'accès aux soins de santé, nutrition comprise, et aux services formels et informels de protection dans les régions ciblées en occurrence celle du sahel et le district de Gorom-Gorom où 50% des formations sanitaires sont fermées ou fonctionnent à minima.

project_name: Assurer la continuité de l'éducation des enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la région de Tillaberi au Niger
project_objective:
L’escalade de l’insécurité dans les zones frontalières durant continue d’impacter tous les secteurs, mais encore plus durablement le secteur de l’Education.  En effet, selon les résultats de l’analyse de l’impact de l’insécurité sur l’éducation, 579 écoles sont fermées dans la région de Tillaberi avec une situation très critique dans les départements frontaliers, tels que Torodi avec plus 50% d’écoles fermées, Téra, 45% et Ayorou avec 37%. Cette fermeture a affecté plus de 53 562 enfants dont 48% de filles. Les efforts de l’Etat et ses partenaires, ont permis le retour à l’école et l’inscription de certains enfants, soit 18% des enfants (19% chez les filles) issus des écoles fermées (DREN Tillaberi, Novembre 2021). Au cours de l’année académique 2021/2022, plus de 82% des élèves issus des écoles fermées, sans compter les enfants qui devraient s’inscrire cette année en cours d’initiation (CI) sont en dehors de l’école. Selon qu’on soit dans les zones de conflits ou dans les zones d’accueil des populations déplacés, les problèmatiques en matière d’éducation ne sont pas les mêmes.
Il est plus que nécessaire de développer des alternatives éducatives adaptées au contexte sécuritaire de chaque zone (zone de conflit et zone d’accueil) pour favoriser le retour à l’école des enfants affectés par cette crise sécuritaire. C’est ainsi qu’un consortium composé de la Fundacion Education Y Cooperacion ( Educo) et l’ Association Nigérienne pour le Traitement de la Délinquance et la prévention du crime (ANTD) ont initié ce projet dont l’objectif global est de contribuer à la réinsertion et à la continuité de l’accès à une éducation inclusive, sure et de qualité des filles et garçons affectés par les crises humanitaires dans la région de Tillaberi au Niger. De manière spécifique, cette initiative vise à réduire les obstacles à l’éducation des filles et des garçons de 6 à 17 ans hors du système éducatif affectés par la crise sécuritaire et sanitaire dans les départements de Tera, Bankilaré et Ouallam, de la région de Tillaberi. Pour concrétiser ces objectifs, le projet prévoit les strategies éducatives suivante : 1)   le transfert de 734 élèves de 12 à 17 ans en particulier les filles et porteurs de handicap, issus des zones de conflits, vers les écoles des zones les plus sécurisées , 2) la mise en place d’Espaces communautaire d’apprentissage ouvert au profit de 1101 enfants de 6 à 12 ans dans les zones à conflits modéré, 3) la promotion de l’éducation à distance (radio) au profit de 1468 enfants de 9 à 12ans dans les zones à conflits modéré, 4) la réinsertion scolaire par la Stratégie de scolarisation accélérée/passerelle (SSAP) au profit de 734 enfants de 9 à 14 ans en dehors de l’écoles dans les zones d’accueil des PDI et des Réfugiés, 5) l’inscription, réinscription de 2568 enfants de 6 à 17 ans en dehors de l’écoles dans les zones d’accueil des PDI et des Réfugiés et 6) le maintien scolaire de 734 enfants non accompagnés de 13 à 17 ans issus des zones de conflits réinscrit dans les écoles sécurisé. Le projet touchera un total de 7338 enfants, y compris les enfants porteurs d’handicap de 6 à 17 ans dont 60% de filles.

project_name: Integrated emergency response in Nutrition, Health, MHPSS with a specific attention to sexual and reproductive health for the populations affected by the crisis in the southwest region
project_objective:
Since April 2020, AAH delivers health, nutrition and MHPSS activities through mobile clinics in Meme Division. This new project will complete what is currently delivered and aims at answering urgent health needs in the increasingly unstable southwest region of Cameroon, through the provision of emergency primary health care, sexual and reproductive health activities  integrating MHPSS to populations affected by the crisis and particularly children under five and pregnant and lactating women.
The proposed project aims to fill critical gaps, providing lifesaving support to the most affected populations by integrating mental health and care practices in a gender-responsive health and nutrition intervention. The project will provide communities with health sensitization and active detection of acute malnutrition and the most common diseases (malaria, respiratory infections, diarrhea…), as well as  a comprehensive package of primary health care services (including OTP) and psychosocial support through a mobile clinic and 2 private health facilities that will be provided with technical and financial support. The mobile clinic and private health facilities will refer complicated cases to secondary health care facilities, particularly a supported stabilisation center for complicated cases of SAM in children U5.
MHPSS activities will be conducted through the mobile clinic and health staff in supported HFs will be trained on MHPSS care practices. The project will provide psychosocial support and healthcare services to SGBV survivors and will refer survivors according to the pathway elaborated by the GBV AoR led by UNFPA in the region.

AAH aims to consolidate the achievements of previous projects by taking into account experiences to adapt the approach. A mobile clinic will be deployed in Meme's division providing primary health care to beneficiaries, with a focus on children under 5, PLW, but is also delivering services to adults for most common pathologies. AAH integrates into its intervention support for functional private structures and the implementation of a community approach through identification and training of CHWs and thus hope to perpetuate the activities of the project. The interventions will contribute to increase the availability of SRHR services through an initial technical training of the supported health facility staff on SRHR. AAH will support the creation or rehabilitation of a dedicated space for SRHR services within the identified health facility and will ensure the provision of reproductive health equipment and supplies based on available data. Counselling on HIV testing and screening, while ensuring the application of standard precautions by medical team, as well as family planning awareness will be provided to all women and girls. A specific MHPSS protocol will be developed to support adolescents (girls and boys) throughout this particular period in a context where they are particularly exposed to adversities.

project_name: Agua, saneamiento e higiene para la Recuperación, Desarrollo y Resiliencia de comunidades rurales de Guatemala con abordaje participativo e incluyente.
project_objective:
La respuesta se enfocará en 10 municipios de 6 departamentos donde los sistemas de agua están afectados y atenderá a personas vulnerables en áreas rurales. Se coordinará y complementará esfuerzos y actividades en tres niveles: nacional, departamental y municipal.
Se implementará con los socios CARE y Mercy Corps que coordinarán y fortalecerán a las
municipalidades, con el enfoque y abordaje del triple nexo, para que mejoren sus capacidades de respuesta a emergencia y vincularse al desarrollo con modelo de gestión municipal de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene, el cual se orienta a la universalización y sostenibilidad de los servicios.
Realizará sistemas de agua y saneamiento sostenibles y resilientes, vinculado con actividades de cambio de comportamiento de manera inclusiva y participativa. Se orienta a personas con mayor vulnerabilidad: rural, mujeres, niñas y personas con discapacidad.
Coordinará con los clústeres de nutrición, salud, educación y protección para una respuesta cohesiva, integral y generar sinergia con las otras acciones que se integran al proyecto como:
- Fortalecimiento del MSPAS para rectoría del sector WASH.
- Fortalecer sistemas de información para manejo de datos.
- Fortalecimiento de capacidades para sostenibilidad de los sistemas a funcionarios
municipales de WASH, responsables de AOM de sistemas comunitarios y unifamiliares.
- Rehabilitación, mejora y construcción de sistemas de agua familiares y comunitarios.
- Mejorar la calidad de agua en: hogar, comunidad, escuelas y establecimientos de salud.
- Promoción y vinculación del triple nexo en acciones WASH relacionados con captación
de agua lluvia, recursos hídricos, tratamiento de aguas para consumo y residuales.
- Promoción de saneamiento e higiene con actividades disparadoras del cambio de
comportamiento.
- WASH en escuelas y establecimientos de salud abordando necesidades de higiene
menstrual.
- Campañas de comunicación y promoción de hábitos de higiene, desinfección, uso y manipulación del agua en el hogar y escuela.
- Mantenimiento y limpieza de pozos.
- Entregas de kit de higiene y herramientas.
- Atender a población migrante con WASH.

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene para población vulnerable a los efectos adversos del cambio climático.
project_objective:
• Hacia Mayo 2021 y tras el paso de ETA / IOTA, de 3426 comunidades reportando daños en sistemas de agua potable y saneamiento (APS) al Clúster de WASH bajo la coordinación de UNICEF, solo 1459 habían recibido asistencia humanitaria; y de 535 sistemas registrados con daños según el gobierno, con un costo de $14millones, solo 8 habían sido priorizados para financiamiento por $4millones. La fase de primera respuesta continúa siendo una necesidad para comunidades que requieren obras APS de infraestructura mayor. Las reparaciones realizadas a sistemas APS por la comunidades y municipalidades, son en su mayoría temporales, no aplican criterios de resiliencia climática, y no garantizan los criterios mínimos para calidad del agua. Solo un 8% de los centros educativos reportados han sido atendidos con mejoras de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (ASH), sumado a la carencia preexistente de 5963 centros educativos sin acceso a servicios de ASH, lo que representa un reto critico en el contexto de COVID.
• El proyecto se enfocará en proporcionar asistencia humanitaria ASH con enfoque en la niñez para comunidades afectadas cuyos sistemas APS continúan colapsados, según brechas de atención identificadas a través del Clúster de ASH, y en fortalecer la resiliencia climática de los sistemas que han sido temporalmente restaurados, así como el acceso seguro a servicios de ASH en centros educativos, integrando un enfoque de género a través del manejo de higiene menstrual, en coordinación con actores relevantes.
• El proyecto se alinea con los objetivos del Cluster a través del acceso sostenible a servicios de ASH, integrando enfoques de género y edad para la población más vulnerable en situación de primera respuesta ante sistemas colapsados de APS, y en situación de acceso precario ante sistemas APS sin criterios de resiliencia climática.

project_name: Livelihoods based emergency response for conflict and drought affected households in Tigray Amhara, Afar, Oromia and Somali regional States of Ethiopia
project_objective:
The prolonged drought in southeastern and southern Ethiopia is the result of three consecutive failed rainy seasons since late 2020. The impact of the drought is deepening and according to April 2022, UNOCHA update at least 81 million people in Oromia, Somali, SNNP and Southwest regions are affected.  Livestock are suffering from lack of pasture and water. Estimates from regional Governments indicated more than 1.46 million livestock deaths (67 % in Somali, 31 % in Oromia, and 7 % in Southwest and SNNP regions). Surviving animals have a significantly deteriorated body condition which has decreased their market value which has led to decrease of the purchasing power of households. According to the most recent seasonal forecast by ICPAC, a below average belg season is expected. The situation seems not expected to improve rapidly.Thus, the affected pastoral communities require continuous support. According to the humanitarian response plan, Humanitarian partners are targeting 12.8 million people for food assistance (out of which 8.0 million people also receive other types of assistance). To response to the situation CARE proposed three major intervention that include Livestock feed provisions, Animal health provision and restocking with shoat to Liben of Somali region and Borena of Oromia region.
East Hararge DRM office Early warning department report showed the rain delayed by 48days this show in FY22 no longer expect of belg crop (short season) planting and delays may happen on Meher crop planting.  Zonal Agriculture office noted to partners the need to support the farmers on provision of short season maturing seed. Similarly, the shortage of seeds noted in West Hararge Zone.  In response to this CARE proposed the provision of agriculture inputs such as improved seeds and /or vegetables to both Eastern and Western Hararge zones.
The political dynamics have changed dramatically in Ethiopia's Tigray Region following the unilateral ceasefire declaration by the Ethiopian Government on 28 June 2021.  However, the breakdown of essential services such as the blackout of electricity, telecommunications, and internet throughout Tigray region will only exacerbate the already dire humanitarian situation.  According to the UNOCHA the shortages of cash and fuel in the region can compromise the duty of care of aid workers on the ground. Despite the dynamic and uncertain situation, it has been reported the security situation in Tigray has been generally calm over the past few days, with limited humanitarian activities being implemented around Mekelle and Shire.  If the situation improves there will be a possibility of accessing the affected woreda.  
According to UNOCHA recent updates, in Amhara region areas bordering Tigray, namely in Wag Hamra, North Wollo and North Gondar zones, situations remained unpredictable but relatively calm during the reporting period. Several locations remained hard to reach for partners’ humanitarian operations due to security concerns, including Abergele and Tsagibji kebeles, parts of Zequala kebeles in Wag Hamra Zone, large sections of Kobo in North Wello Zone, and in Addi Arekay in the North Gondar Zone. However, the livelihoods of the people in the above zones are highly affected by the conflict that leaves many affected people for need of agriculture input support. CARE proposes the agriculture input provisions which includes improved seeds and /or vegetables, provision of hand tools, and the provision of Draught power for the Amhara and Tigray region affected woredas. The recent UNOCHA updates shows in Afar, the humanitarian situation continued to be dire with a high number of IDPs in need of support while the response is still insufficient to compare with needs in the region. Because of the conflict the main livelihood and income source from livestock highly affected. To respond the situation CARE proposed Animal feed provision, animal health and restocking interventions
