project_name: Integrated lifesaving treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among children U5 and PLW in Somalia
project_objective:
Malnutrition remains persistently high in Somalia. According to FSNAU SMART survey in July 2021, the overall median GAM rate in Somalia was Serious (11.1% weight-for-height z-score) in 2021. The drivers of acute malnutrition include high morbidity, low immunization, low vitamin-A supplementation, reduced access to milk, and food insecurity. Urgent treatment and nutrition support is required for approximately 1.2 million children under the age of five years (total acute malnutrition burden), who will likely face acute malnutrition between August 2021 and July 2022, including 213,400 who are likely to be severely malnourished. Integrated interventions are needed to support recovery and prevent deterioration of the nutrition situation.
This proposed project will provide lifesaving integrated Management Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) Programme to vulnerable communities in Awdal, Bay, Bakool, Lower Shabelle, Banadir, Bari, Galgadud, Hiiran, Lower Juba, Mudug, Nugaal, Sanaag, Sool, Togdheer, Waqooyi Galbed. The project is aiming to reach 594,592 IDPs and host communities affected by drought, conflict displacement and climate change hazards in the targeted locations. 
In addition to the CMAM service and Infant and young child feeding, (IYCF-E) services will be integrated with the CMAM. Trained IYCF-E counsellors will provide support to PLWs and care givers of young children with difficulties in adopting the optimal infant and young child feeding practices recommended by WHO/UNICEF. To reach the population in need in target regions with lifesaving integrated nutrition Programme delivery, the project will operate fixed and mobile nutrition facilities. 
Save the Children proposes a multi-sectoral, integrated health and nutrition response to respond to vulnerable, IDPs, and marginalized communities in Somalia. We will work with MOH to improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services in static health and outreach sites to deliver an integrated package of promotive, preventive, and curative maternal, nutrition services. SC will build the local capacity by providing training and technical support to local government, health facility staff, the Community Nutrition volunteers, representatives of local communities to raise awareness, promote nutrition, and strengthen linkages between the community and health facilities. 
In addition to that Save the Children will increase awareness in the community about the rights of people with disabilities. Children with disabilities are generally hidden from public view including during the active case finding sessions in the community. SC will involve CWDs, providing and affording children the space and opportunity to initiate activities and advocate for themselves. 
To sustain efforts to reduce acute mortality and morbidity related to acute malnutrition we will reach and support the following number of beneficiaries (including 5% Persons with Disabilities).
Total: 594,592 (Boys:  139,192, Girls: 148,955, Women: 200,000 & Men:106,445) IDPs: 112,972 & Host communities: 481,620

project_name: Increased and Sustained access to lifesaving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) support including COVID-19 related BCCE to communities affected by protracted drought and conflict in Lower Juba region of Somalia.
project_objective:
According to latest reports and as indicated in the HNO estimated 6.4 million people representing 40 per cent of the Somali population need emergency life-saving WASH assistance of which 3.5 million will need safe drinking water, 5.1 million sanitation services, and 6.4 million hygiene supplies. 16 per cent of these are females, 64% children and 4% elderly. Additionally, approximately 1,619,415 IDPs and 4,818,944 vulnerable host communities need WASH assistance through 2022 of which 6,058,603 people are categorized as severe condition. They lack access to safe water and proper sanitation services and are highly vulnerable to AWD and cholera. Further, the Cluster estimates, 379,757 people are in extreme condition as they access water directly from rivers and surface bonds, practice open defecation and lack access to soap and other essential hygiene materials and are susceptible to communicable diseases
Water is the greatest need in the community and has remained a serious challenge in both Afmadow and Badhadhe district. Water is mainly supplied by the private individuals, who currently lack the capacity to meet the ever-increasing demand due to booming population with the daily influx of people. IDPs are mostly affected by the water problem and the assessed IDPs cannot also afford the water since they don’t have an income to sustain this. The sanitation situation in Afmadow district is 1 latrine per 300 persons. People living with disabilities remain the most affected and are unable to access any water consumption points. 
Recent assessment conducted by SFH on the existing water supplies including existing boreholes and shallow wells in Lower juba and particularly Afmadow and Dobley tows shows, 3 boreholes requires urgent and significant rehabilitation due to the overuse and lack of sustainable power supply. In this proposed intervention SFH will select 1boreholes and establish into complete water system. This will entail installation of solar system “solar submersible pump, solar panels and a battery”.  Construction of 50M3 elevated concrete water tank, pipeline distribution network and construction of 3 tap stands with 6 facet and benefit 250 persons per tab. Distribution pipelines will be connected to the water tank which will supply water to the tap stands through gravity flow. Each of the pipe line distribution networks will cover approximately 500m length and will benefit approximately 1,500 beneficiaries thus reaching total of 4500 beneficiaries (Boys, girls, men and women-including person living with disability) for 3 pipe line distribution systems. The construction process will include Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) including raised plinths to withstand the structure against flash flood or any other natural disasters. The distance of fetching water will be reduced and water access especially for women will be prioritized through participation on the sites for the pipeline systems, Women will be consulted with in the decision process to identify the locations of the water points to ensure safety and reduce chances of protection risks such as GBV.
Water quality testing will be conducted on the existing shallow wells and the borehole. Automatic chlorine dozing pumps will be provided to disinfect water and decrease the chances of water borne diseases. Water quality tests will also ensure that water is free from fecal coliforms and is fit for human consumption. Community Hygiene Promoters will train the Water management committees on how to maintain the automatic chlorine dozing pumps. This will enrich the community knowledge on water hygiene and will significantly reduce the cases of AWD outbreak in areas of intervention.
SFH will construct 200 Communal Latrines with lockable doors and hand washing stations to eliminate open defecation. Hygiene promotion activities will be conducted through the community hygiene promoters who will be trained and also double to conduct hygiene kits distribution.

project_name: Improved, sustained access and utilization of integrated, essential and quality nutrition services in Lower Juba region of Somalia aimed to reach 24000<5 children, pregnant and Lactating women.
project_objective:
According to the latest FSNAU findings the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) at the national level has remained at a serious level of 11.1% weight-for-height z-score. The nutrition cluster estimates that in 2022 around 1.2 million children, under the age of 5 years, will be at risk of acute malnutrition and will therefore need emergency nutrition services urgently. 295,515 children under the age of 5 are likely to be severely malnourished and an estimated 986,000 children will be moderately acute malnourished (MAM). Further, an estimated 245,909 PLWs will be at risk of acute malnutrition.
Malnutrition in Jubaland is driven by low immunization, low Vit A Supplementation, food insecurity, sub-optimal IYCF practices, poor hygiene and sanitation services. This has adverse consequence on child survival and well being of pregnant and Lactating mothers.
SFH will Strengthen Community component of IMAM and community care practices in lower juba through regular community education; screening of children under five; including referrals and follow-up; promotion of appropriate IYCF practices; and dissemination of key health and hygiene messages. Community mobilization will enhance access to and coverage of nutrition services, contributing to reducing mortality by early detection of acute malnutrition. Key strategies include capacity-building of Community health workers and regular education sessions to equip the target communities with key skills and knowledge on the prevention and promotion of child and maternal health and nutrition practices. This intervention will specifically target 24000 gender disaggregated beneficiaries (Boys, girls, men and women) under the age of 6-59 months and Women of Child-Bearing Age including persons living with disability. Due to the complex operational environment in Somalia and the level of humanitarian crisis in the areas of operation, the primary focus of this intervention is responding to the immediate nutrition needs thus helping to prevent further morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition. Nevertheless, it is designed to also build local capacities, enabling communities to better respond to future crisis, which also serves to improve the sustainability of this action.
Additionally, the proposed action aimed to provide prevention and management of Acute Malnutrition, provide Vitamin A supplementation, immunization, and de-worming treatment for all <5 children admitted in the programme, including health promotion; promote and support optimal IYCF practices at both facility- and community-level; train health workers in delivering IMAM, IYCF and the Baby-Friendly Initiative; and conduct regular monitoring and surveillance. 
OTP distributions will take place on a daily basis. Education sessions for all care takers will include OTP feeding methods and other key messages concerning health and hygiene (including that of water, sanitation and hygiene). Upon admission and following every subsequent distribution, all children included in the programme will undergo a medical check by a nurse, receive routine treatment (e.g. antibiotics, mebendazole, vitamin A, anti-malaria, and measles and other EPI vaccinations) and any additional treatment as necessary (e.g. Resomal to treat mild dehydration).
The immunization status of all children admitted to the nutrition programme will be checked and referrals will be done as necessary to the immunization programme run at the MCH clinics. Micronutrient supplementation and de-worming treatment will be provided to all eligible beneficiaries admitted in the IMAM programme. Severely malnourished children with medical complications will be referred to the nearest Stabilization Centre at Dobley Hospital.
Further, awareness creation interventions will focus on supporting, promoting and protecting breastfeeding practices at the facility level to encourage the majority of caregivers to practice optimum feeding of their infants and young children.

project_name: Improve CCCM to support vulnerable IDP settlements in Kahda and Daynile districts of Banadir Region.
project_objective:
Conflict, drought, COVID-19, and flooding are some of the main shocks that drive displacement and largely affect at least 2.9 million internally displaced persons in Somalia. The majority of displaced people have self-settled in over 2,400 sub-standard and unplanned IDP sites in urban, semi-urban and rural areas across the country as reported humanitarian Programme Cycle 2022 issued October 2021. Over 56 per cent of all evictions occurred within the Kahda and Daynile districts in Banadir which accommodate some 1,808 IDP sites or 848,760 IDPs.290 Furthermore, 11 per cent of households in IDP settlements (17 per cent of Banadir IDPs) believe that they are currently at risk of being evicted from their shelters.291 Inaccessibility to land tenure security continues to function as a primary obstacle preventing IDPs from establishing permanent settlements. This project will establish capacity of the community focal points and understanding of the basic principles of CCCM and support conflict management, risk mitigations, site management, and de-congestion. a 3 days' training will be organized for 60 ( 30 Daynile, 30 Kaxda) participants from the IDP camps in Kahda and Daynile districts of the Banadir region. SCC will work closely with the camp management committees to improve the quality of life, safety, and dignity of displaced people through coordination activities. At the site level, coordination mechanisms will be developed/strengthened involving local authorities, active partners, CMCs in the project sites. SCC will conduct 4 quarterly coordination meetings that each will attend for 30 participants from the camp management committee, local authority, and active implementing partners in Kada. 

The total participants for the coordination meetings will be 120 persons. In the meetings, the participants will discuss and identify humanitarian gaps, mobilize resources, respond and minimize overlaps if there is any.  SCC will implement CCCM project for 24 IDP sites in Kahda and Daynile districts of Banadir region with over 30,000HHs as per the latest detailed site assessment (DSA), targeting a largely undeserved area. Approximately 36000 IDPs (6000 households) will benefit from this proposed intervention, in addition to the community working in these sites including local authorities, clusters, and other NGOs. These numbers might vary due to external factors, which might attract more IDPs, excessive flooding, or conflict with the landowners or the authorities, which may cause IDPs to flee to other areas. Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys, and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age, and diversity dis-segregated data. SCC will implement this intervention in the Kahda district of Banadir region targeting 6000 HHS. Kaxda District is one of the IDP major hubs in Mogadishu that hosts the largest number of IDPs. Throughout the project, the needs of women, girls, men, and boys of all ages will be addressed throughout the planning, implementation and monitoring, and evaluation of the activities. Through regular site monitoring, needs and gaps will be reported and shared with partners and all stakeholders. Particular attention regarding needs will be paid to women and girls who also have to contend with GBV and protection concerns within camp settings. Through this project, SCC will also address the current and newly identified needs by setting up camp coordination structures at the national and, where necessary, regional or district levels, facilitating and supporting the establishment of effective coordination and management in IDP sites while respecting national context and authorities. Currently, SCC is implementing CCCM program with SHF Somalia in Kaxda targeting 16000 (60% women) providing CCCM services.

project_name: Improve access to WASH services for vulnerable crisis affected IDPs and host communities in Kahda, Daynile, Jowhar and Mahaday districts of Banadir and Middle Shabelle regions.
project_objective:
According to JMCNA 2021 findings indicate that 11 per cent of female respondents report that it takes them more than 31 minutes to fetch water and return: 14 per cent and 16 per cent respectively experience drinking and cooking water shortages while 25 per cent report shortage of water for personal hygiene. The population in need of WASH services in Somalia in 2022 is approximately 1,619,415 IDPs and 4,818,944 vulnerable host communities. Estimated that 6,058,603 people (38 per cent) in the severe category” lack access to safe water and proper sanitation services and are highly vulnerable to AWD and According to SCC WASH assessment in Banadir hot sport districts conducted in July 2021, SCC assessed more than 190 IDP sites in Mogadishu. The assessment found out that 70% of IDP the families have not access to affordable water. They go to other camps about 1000 to 1500 meter away for fetching water.  The majority of affected people take more than 30 minutes to reach the nearest water sources which are overcrowded creating access barriers.  The assessment noted that most of the latrines are either damaged by recent floods or overflowing that is harmful to the congested IDPs. According to the Joint Multi-cluster needs assessment carried out by joint partners in Middle Shebelle on 11th -16th May 2021 that SCC participated found out that river flash floods as a result of overflow and breakage of weak river points compounded by heavy downpours has led to massive flooding in both the assessed districts, Mahaday and Jowhar in Middle Shebelle region. This has displaced a total of 11000 households in 27 villages, destroyed over 40,000 hectors of farms and disrupted learning sessions in 11 schools. The floods have also destroyed 82% of all WASH infrastructures in the assessed villages where over 62 shallow wells were damaged, 1646 latrines destroyed and displaced over 92% of all affected villages. In total 66000 individuals have been totally displaced from their dwellings out of which 30% are women, 28% children,7% are people living with disability, 12% are elderly while 23% are men.

The project intervention will address the dire WASH humanitarian needs by floods, droughts and conflict affected communities in Kahda, Daynile, Jowhar  and Mahaday districts of Banadir and Middle shabelle regions through access to safe water, emergency hygiene kits/education and sanitation facilities. The project will address WASH gaps and risks of AWD/cholera outbreaks, morbidity and mortality among emergency affected communities and IDPs. This project will target 18500 people (6475 Women, 5550 men, 3330 girls, 1850 boys and 370 PwDs) including disabled persons and 1280 are elderly persons. Disadvantaged families, elderly persons and disabilities in emergencies will have to be provided access to adequate safe water, sanitation facilities, and hygiene promotion services. WASH services of good hygiene and sanitation practices will be promoted to the target communities through construction of 500 emergency latrines (100 in Jowhar, 100 Mahaday, 100 in Kahda and 200 in Daynile districts) with hand washing facilities, lockable doors and with access for disability persons. The project will provide safe and clean  water to 6000 vulnerable crisis affected  households through construction of 15 shallow wells with hand pump installation ( 5 in Mahaday and 10 in Jowhar), and rehabilitation of 30 nonfunctional shallow wells with disability access  ( 20 in Jowhar and 10 in Mahaday). The project will provide emergency safe drinking water through cash voucher assistance (CVA to 3000 households in the IDPs. Each family will have 40 liters of safe  water per day for a per day for a period of 90 days.

project_name: Provision of emergency and sustainable safe water, sanitation and hygiene to drought/AWD and flood affected communities in Gedo and Lower Juba region Somalia
project_objective:
Unreliable access to a temporary water source and/or unprotected water is still an important feature of the WASH humanitarian landscape in Somalia. Nationwide, access to an improved water source remains below 40%, with large variations from one region to another, however, lower Juba and Gedo region remains to below 25% each. In most urban and sub-urban hubs and IDP settlements, access to an adequate quantity of water is often granted but water is unsafe and often microbiologically contaminated due to cross-contamination by poorly design water supply and sanitation systems. More than half of the population lack access to adequate sanitation. The situation is particularly critical in lower Juba region is below 35% and in IDP settlements in Gedo region, Hand washing with soap at critical moment is practiced by only a third of the population as access to soap and availability to a functional hand washing point is limited. This percentage drops to below 25% in Jubaland regional state, despite that these two region were badly affected by AWD/Cholera COVID-19 pandemic as well as severe drought. Because of the ﬂoods and the chronical lack of investment in WASH infrastructure, Somalia continued to suffer from AWD/Cholera in 2021 and risk factors for an outbreak persist in several hotspots Gedo and Lower Juba region included. SORDES will continue to focus activities affecting most vulnerable populations in hard to reach locations; IDPs, people at risk of AWD /cholera, acutely malnourished and people in drought-affected areas in Gedo and Lower Juba region. Water is the greatest need in the community and has remained a serious challenge during this period where the communities are experiencing the triple effect of the COVID-19, Locust infestation, conflicts and drought. IDPs are mostly affected by the water problem and as per the SORDES assessed IDPs it indicated that IDPs cannot also afford to buy water since they don’t have an income to sustain this. The sanitation situation in the area is 1 latrine per 500 persons. Many people are living with disabilities inflicted from conflict and are unable to access any water consumption points. Protection concerns among women and PLWD are also at an alarming rate where GBV cases are reported daily during SORDES rapid assessment.
SORDES therefore proposed intervention will provide immediate access to safe drinking water to 14,000 vulnerable population boys, girls, women and men affected by the drought and other natural disaster, while ensuring 15% PLWD, SORDES intends to rehabilitates 10 shallow wells beneﬁting 5000 men, women and children to enable enhanced the community access to safe drinking water. The project will also provide the target beneﬁciaries with hygiene kits as well as provide hygiene promotion to ensure community is aware of the water born risk as well as sanitation and other vector born disease. Through this SORDES will ensure to establish 80 water management committee at IDPs and rehabilitate 10 water sources to enable ease the water related protection risk among boys, girls, women, men and these with disability

project_name: Improving the Health and Nutrition status of children under 5 years and mothers of  IDP’s and vulnerable Host Community in Middle, lower Shabelle and Banadir Regions
project_objective:
Acute malnutrition is a major public health problem in Somalia and disproportionately affects children under the age of 5, as well as Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs). Malnutrition is the result of years of conflict and violence, disease outbreaks, drought, locust infestation, recurrent flooding and population displacements. In addition, other factors such as high morbidity, low immunization, low vitamin-A supplementation, reduced access to milk, food insecurity, low access to health services, poor access to water and sanitation, poor maternal nutrition, and high disease burden contribute to malnutrition rates. Poor feeding practices for infants and young children are also strongly linked with undernutrition.
According to the latest findings of 2021 post Gu results of FSNAU, the median prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) at the national level has remained at a serious level of 11.1 per cent weight-for-height z-score. Based on this analysis and the latest population figures, the cluster estimates that in 2022 around 1.2 million children, under the age of 5 year will be at risk of acute malnutrition and will therefore ned emergency nutrition services urgently. Out of this, 295,515 children under the age of 5 are likely to be severely malnourished and around 986,000 children will be moderately acute malnourished (MAM)
To respond  and address the critical nutrition needs of the extremely 34,650 vulnerable children and women in three target districts in Bandir, lower and middle shabelle regions,  SOS CV Somalia proposes to provide a sustained holistic urgent support to recovery and prevention of deteriorations in the nutrition situations in particular for children under the age of five and pregnant and lactating women who will likely face acute malnutrition in Heliwa, Daynile, afgoi corridor, and Kahda, Balcad and Jowhar  districts through  existing  SOS Managed health/nutrition facilities in the proposed districts.
The propose emergency nutrition interventions   will provide integrated lifesaving treatment for acute malnutrition in the targeted districts  through facility and community- based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) targeting children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). The proposed project aims to increase coverage and access to the management of both moderate and severe acute malnutrition (MAM/SAM), vitamin A supplementation and deworming as well as promotion of optimal infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices. SOS will adopt an expansive IYCF in Emergencies (IYCF-E) strategy aimed at increasing reach beyond mothers raising infants but also fathers, grandfathers, community leaders, religious leaders, teachers, etc.
All the proposed nutrition interventions will improve early identification and prevention of malnutrition and therefore reduce excess morbidity and mortality in the target districts.

project_name: Provision of life Saving primary Health care Interventions to vulnerable people in hard to reach area in Banadir, Bay and Middle Shabelle Regions
project_objective:
As per the HNO 2022 report, over 3.9 million people in Somalia need urgent action to maintain their right to health and wellbeing, and to assure their equitable and dignified access to health care. The health sector is overburdened, remaining fragmented, under-resourced and ill-equipped to provide life-saving and preventive services. The COVID-19 pandemic places the population at increased risk and stresses the capacity of the healthcare system. Displaced and marginalized groups inequitably face barriers to healthcare and higher exposure to disease.
In light of these, SOS CV propose to addresses barriers access to health and factors that increase risks of poor  health and diseases including COVID-19 and provision of health services  support to person living with disabilities. SOS will provide basic life-saving primary health care services to 242,500 highly vulnerable IDP, host-community and hard-to-reach populations in Banadir, Afgoye Corridor, Lafole Baidoa,  Jowhar Diinsoor, Balcad with a strong focus towards women and children. SOS will facilitate access to target populations in identified catchment areas safely access comprehensive primary healthcare at no cost, including health and social behavior change messaging and community outreach through CHWs, designed to reduce the spread of communicable diseases. Disease outbreak surveillance, reporting, response and prevention to reduce morbidity and mortality from common diseases. 
Integration of MHPSS in to the primary health care to improve the physical and mental wellbeing of communities. Clinical management of rape services to SGBV survivors to reduce rape consequences. Outpatient consultations will primarily focus on clinical diagnosis and treatment for communicable diseases, treatment of common ailments, Antenatal and Post-natal care visits (ANC/PNC), immunizations, skilled birth attendants specialized obstetric and newborn care and ambulance referral service.

The proposed project will support people with disabilities who will be provided with Health emergency response which is designed to improve the health and protection of the target groups through provision of Health services and mental health support.

project_name: Protection Response services to displaced children and women affected by conflict from Guriceel and Hobyo in Galgadud, Galmudug state
project_objective:
The project is aimed at providing comprehensive protection services to conflict displaced children and women affected by the conflict between the government forces and non-state armed actors in Guriceel and Hobyo districts. It targets families, children and women displaced from Guriceel and Baadweyne who have settle in IDP settlements and host communities in Hobyo, Guriceel and outside villages within the two districts in Galgadud regions. 
Following the conflict, a joint interagency assessment found that at least 100,000 people (16,740 households) have left and sought shelter in 28 nearby villages from the Guriceel conflict while other 7,656 people from the Baadweyne. The displaced include about 1,000 unaccompanied minors and 2,000 PLWDs and health related complications. About 18,440 of the affected people were IDPs living in Guri Ceel before the situation escalated. Three new IDP settlements are accommodating about 44,000 people (7,300 families) with the rest living with relatives in overcrowded shelters or have remained within Guri Ceel area due to lack of capacity to move or no clan ties in rural villages. In Hobyo IDPs who have been forced out of their homes due to armed conflict, drought and other causes are predominantly residing within the host communities and the host communities have been burdened with hosting the IDPs, food, water basic services availability is strained. In addition, families displaced by the recent Baadweyne conflict have settled in Hobyo where they lack protection services. 
TUOS proposes to provide protection services to the displaced children and women in Guriceel and Hobyo. The services will not only be provided within the two towns but also accessible villages in the outskirts where the displaced have settled. Of the displaced more than 1000 were unaccompanied and separated children, women, children and the elderly. In provision of the services TUOS targets to train a core group of women and men as community based child protection committee who will assist in referral of survivors to TUOS and other service providers. The organisation will train 120 community members as CBCP.  The project targets to provide GBV services to affected women and girls from the community and the displaced families. Apart from the services trainings will be conducted to capacitate the community in developing home base solutions in the prevention of GBV/CP, provision of solar lamps and dignity kits. The project will work with all members in the community to enhance protection mechanisms. TUOS proposes to establish 4 child friendly spaces, establishment of 6 mobile protection services which will include CFS providing services to the nearby villages. 10 CFS facilitators will be engaged to coordinate and provide basic PSS services, numerical and literacy skills at the 4 CFS, providing a safe environment for the children among other services. 6 child help desks will be established which will be vital in the collection of information on IDTR, UASC and protection incidences. The proposed project plans to conduct training to 10 social workers who will be providing protection services, referral and overseeing the provision of comprehensive medical services to survivors, and working with 300 foster families for UASC children before reunification. Furthermore 2,009 PLWDs and health related conditions to provide a gender sensitive structured mental health and PSS as well as case management. Capacity building activities will also encompass issues of PLWD, minority groups, women, men, boys and girls Human rights issues, children’s rights, risk mitigation, service provision among other topics to improve on the safety environment of all vulnerable groups in the community.  In addition, TUOS will also conduct trainings to health workers on clinical case management to enhance and provide timely medical services to survivors in the 2 target areas.

project_name: Enhancing food access and protection of livelihood for vulnerable house holds of Puntland and Somaliland.
project_objective:
FSNAU, Sept., 2021, indicates that about 7.2 million people; 3.5 million people in Crisis (IPC Phase 3)1 or worse outcomes, of whom 640,730 people are in IPC4,facing large food consumption gaps and 3.7 million people expected to be stressed (IPC2),facing  depletion of livelihood assets through the end of the year, in the absence of humanitarian assistance. Humanitarian assistance must be sustained through December 2021 to prevent Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) outcomes for 3.5 million people. Livelihoods support is also required for people that are Stressed (IPC Phase 2) or worse. Among them, 1.2 million children under the age of five are facing acutely malnutrition, with 213,400 of them likely to face severe malnutrition despite humanitarian food assistance and government support since January 2021.This situation is driven by combined effects of poor and erratic rainfall distribution, resulting in 60% and 63% harvest below the 1995-2020 average, in Southern and Northwest, respectively; flooding, conflict and multiple declines in food and income sources in rural areas.. 
The poor rains led to below-average Gu poor crop production and harvest in agro pastoral livelihood zones Southern and Northwest Somalia, respectively. In pastoral livelihood zones, poor households are facing large food consumption gaps due to below-average or poor milk availability, a limited number of saleable animals, and increased expenditures on food and water. In agro pastoral livelihood zones, poor households experience large food consumption gaps due to crop losses and low income from agricultural employment. Of those people facing crisis, 2.9million are Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) with limited livelihood assets, few income-earning opportunities, low communal support and high reliance on external humanitarian assistance. As a result, a significant proportion of IDPs (in both rural and urban settlements) facing large food consumption gaps.
Forecasted increased likelihood of below-average rainfall during the 2021 Dyer (October-December) season, will adversely affect food security and nutrition outcomes. From October to December 2021, food insecurity is expected to further deteriorate among poor rural, urban, and displaced populations due to the impacts of anticipated, below-average 2021 Dyer (October-December) season rainfall, continued insecurity and other food security related risk factors, including rising food prices and cost of living, declining availability of milk for both consumption and sale, and a likely reduction in agricultural employment opportunities during the forthcoming Dyer season. Desert Locust continues to pose a serious risk to both pasture availability and crop production across Somalia.

The project targets 5,500 households  in Togdhere Region, Somaliland in IPC 3&4( including IDPs) with; i)Unconditional cash transfer for immediate food access(1,000 hh); ii)cash for work for 1500hh   (iii) Protection of productive livelihood assets for those in IPC 2  -provision of supplementary livestock feed -3000hh,  1500 for animal health services.

project_name: Shelter and NFIs Assistance for Conflict and Drought-Affected Populations in Banadir, Lower Shabelle, Bay, and Hiiraan Regions - Somalia
project_objective:
According to 2022 HNO, an estimated 3.6 million people are in need of shelter and NFIs assistance resulted by recurrent conflict, drought, flooding, evictions and cyclones as key drivers of humanitarian issues and caused vulnerability and migration from rural to urban and peri-urban centers resulted in inadequate shelter conditions, overcrowding, economic hardship, and lack of security of tenure. Those in need of shelter and NFI assistance include displaced and non-displaced populations. A total of 30,800 refugee and asylum seekers and 90,583 refugee returnees need shelter and NFIs assistance in 2022 as they do not have sufficient access to basic and domestic items and shelter assistance as well as financial capacity to build adequate shelters. As per UNHCR post return monitoring data, there is a high proportion of returnees live in housing they do not own and have no documentation as this leads to protection concerns, including housing insecurity and risk of eviction. On 2022 HNO, a total of 593,058 IDPs are to settle in informal and largely unplanned settlements facing unsafe living conditions, they do not have financial capacity to build adequate shelters. They usually do not own the land they occupy and also are not allowed to build any permanent structure. Due to lack of tenure agreements and housing options, minority and marginalized groups including women headed households as the main income earner have no alternative residence options. 
Importantly, Women and girls living in sub-standard and overcrowded shelters are particularly vulnerable. They tend not to feel safe in makeshift shelters which do not offer privacy and sufficient protection from weather elements and increase the risk of gender based violence. Over a quarter, 27%, of IDPs reported that their bathing facilities are not safe as their main shelter concern. In addition, marginalized groups and people with special needs also require additional support and should be prioritized as resources are limited.
As a result, this project is to address shelter and NFIs needs of IDP families and refugee (90%), while  poor host communities  (10%) will receive NFIs only in Kaxda  and Daynile districts of Banadir region, Afgoye and Marka districts of Lower Shabelle region, Baidoa district of Bay region, and Beletweyne of Hiiraan region in South and Central Somalia including women-headed household families, extended families, families with disabled and elderly persons who are most in need of humanitarian assistance to mitigate risk and its consequences on crisis-affected populations at the target areas. The main objective is to improve the living conditions and safe access to services of IDP families including refugee returnees and poor host communities in the targeted locations. HINNA aims at providing 5000 ESKs and NFI kits to 5000 HHs (30,000 beneficiaries/Individuals) while 3000 (10%) people of them will be poor host communities through in-kind distribution to improve the living conditions of the target beneficiaries who faced inadequate shelter/NFIs conditions. The reason we can't use cash transfer programming for this project is that we have had several meetings with the communities in some of the project target areas and most of them have told us that cash transfer program can cause insecurity, family violence that can lead to family breakdown and other things including missing kits or rising market prices.
Disaggregation of gender will be promoted in full consideration with protection mainstreaming. The total beneficiaries of the project (30,000 people) of the drought, floods, and conflict-affected populations including (4,800 women, 4,800 men, 9,600 boys, and 9,600 girls) including 1200 elderly people (4%) in the project target locations will directly be receiving any benefits of the project through selection criteria set by the shelter cluster.

project_name: Nutrition Status of Children in South West, Jubaland, Puntland and Somaliland States Improved
project_objective:
The integrated Somalia nutrition response aims to save lives and mitigate further suffering among children, pregnant and lactating women and their families through accelerated nutrition recovery and sustained rehabilitation of 196,787 beneficiaries affected by malnutrition. The interventions will be adopt a preventive and curative approach. Preventive nutrition intervention aims at promoting good nutrition among, pregnant and lactating women, children under five and the community at large. These interventions will include micronutrient deficiency control (vitamin A, Iron and folate supplementation), promotion of optimal IYCF practices, nutrition and hygiene promotion and linkage with WASH,   livelihood and health interventions aimed at sustaining the rehabilitation. The interventions will also provide high impact health and nutrition interventions aimed at mitigating malnutrition and its consequences among vulnerable groups. Actions will include deworming, and home fortification of foods including distribution of micronutrient powders). 
The curative approach will be aimed at providing treatment to malnourished children under the age of 5, pregnant and lactating women. Timely treatment will be initiated for the malnourished children through active case finding done through nutrition screening of most at risk groups, promote and strengthen family participation in nutrition surveillance. Through Family-led MUAC, Household members will be trained and supported to carry out MUAC screening at the household level and facilitate self-referrals for treatment.  Moderately malnourished children pregnant and lactating women identified through active and passive screening will be referred for nutrition rehabilitation through outpatient treatment of moderately malnourished beneficiaries. Case management of moderate acute malnutrition will be integrated and linked to targeted supplementary feeding program facilities with support from WFP and partners in the respective locations .These services will be provided at 61  fixed and 7 outreach sites located in 17  districts across 7 regions in Puntland, Somaliland and Southern Somalia. At 54 of the targeted 61 fixed sites (Health centers) WVI in collaboration with WFP supports bother TSFP and MCHN activities which provide both MAM case management and preventive maternal and child nutrition interventions, these will facilitate holistic nutrition care to SAM beneficiaries admitted at these health facilities for SAM care, enabling easy beneficiary transition from one phase of nutrition treatment to another.
Severely malnourished children without medical complications will be provided with therapeutic nutrition treatment at outpatient therapeutic feeding program (OTP) sites. Severely malnourished children with medical complications will be admitted for specialized care support at 3 stabilization care centers that will be managed by this project and integrated with the health interventions. 
Households with children on malnutrition treatment will be linked to the food security and livelihood interventions aimed at improving household access to basic food. IYCF knowledge, support and practice will be promoted through campaigns, mother to mother and father to father support groups. These nutrition interventions will further be promoted through timed and targeted counselling (ttC) that focuses on 10 key messages during scheduled CHW home visits with the emphasis message informed by the beneficiary physiological stage. WVI through collaboration with UNICEF and MOH will also support accelerated country wide micronutrient supplementation and deworming campaign in support to the MOH deworming strategy.

project_name: Increased life-saving and sustainable access to water, sanitation and hygiene for disaster Affected Communities in Somaliland
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to contribute towards the improvement of living conditions of Drought, Covid-19, and locust-affected communities in target areas of Sool and Sanaag regions in Somaliland through the supply of clean and safe water, appropriate sanitation, and knowledge of protection mechanisms against water-borne diseases. The WASH intervention of HAVOYOCO will contribute to the life-saving of most vulnerable communities and it will improve the condition and good practice of hygiene through the provision of clean water and in extensive hygiene awareness campaigns. In response to the current crisis. the project will provide much-needed humanitarian assistance to vulnerable people in targeted areas of Lasanod and Erigavo districts. About 13,220 numbers of beneficiaries will benefit from the project intervention. The proposed actions will include, water trucking/water voucher rehabilitation of Berkads, construction of new Berkads, rehabilitation and equipping of boreholes, construction of gender-sensitive Latrines, and hygiene and sanitation promotion activities. Moreover, a total of 9 water and sanitation committees will be identified and trained on safe water handling, hygiene promotion, and water source management. The proposed project will ensure community involvement and participation at all stages. This will promote ownership and in turn ensure the sustainability of the projects. Training and capacity building of water committees selected by the community and the use of Hygiene volunteers from the target villages will ensure continuity of the program beyond the project lifetime.
According to the HAVOYOCO rapid assessment 17-21 September 2021, about 70 percent of the population in the assessed area are in need of urgent water trucking due to acute water shortage, similarly,40 % of existing water points are broken and non-functional. There is huge shortage of water in all the assessed areas and people are susceptible to acute watery diarrhea. Women, girls, the elderly, lactating, and pregnant mothers are most affected. Increased distance to water sources further affects women and girls who are traditionally tasked with water collection. There are no permanent functional water sources except two Boreholes and one semi-borehole in Shululux, Waxari-kaciday and Yeyle which are in need of rehabilitation, maintenance and equipment while the assessed areas in Sanaag are mostly experiencing challenges related to access of safe and sufficient water for both human and livestock consumption. The majority of the community never treat their drinking water, open defecation is widespread with very few washing their hands with soap. These coupled with poor hygiene knowledge & practices and inadequate access to healthcare services exposes women & children to be more susceptible to increased risk of diseases and high mortality rate. Poor and erratic rains cause severe depletion of pasture and water triggering food insecurity. When competition for water and pasture sets in, inter-community hostilities and conflicts, including population displacements occur. In response to these crises, HAVOYOCO proposes in response to the expected crises to provide humanitarian assistance and response to 13,220 vulnerable targeted people in Erigavo and Lasanod, districts. The proposed Intervention include access to water voucher, rehabilitation of Berkads and Shallow wells, hygiene, and sanitation promotion activities including hygiene campaigns, distribution of sanitary kits and construction of gender-sensitive latrines and capacity building of the WASH committee

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods among Vulnerable Communities
project_objective:
In Somalia, nearly 3.5 million people are expected to face food consumption gaps or depletion of livelihood assets indicative of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes through the end of the year 2021, in the absence of humanitarian assistance (FSNAU/ FEWSNET, Sept. 2021). Furthermore, approximately 1.2 million children under the age of five are likely to be malnourished. 

From October to December 2021, food insecurity is expected to further deteriorate among poor and displaced populations due to the impacts of anticipated, below-average 2021 Deyr (October-December) season rainfall, continued insecurity and other food security related risk factors, including rising food prices and declining availability of milk, and a likely reduction in agricultural employment opportunities. Without sustained humanitarian food assistance, 3.5 million people across Somalia are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse outcomes between October and December 2021 and probably into the following year 2022. Out the 3.5 million people in need of urgent food assistance, 640,000 people face significant food consumption gaps and engaging in negative coping strategies to meet their food and non-food needs. 

According to FSNAU (October – December 2021) projections, out of a total population of 464,487 in Sool, 119,340 will be in IPC 2, 81,690 in IPC 3 and 22,260 in IPC 4. In Sanaag, out of 362,723 people, 84,270 will be in IPC 2, 94,640 in IPC 3 and 22,570 in IPC 4. Candlelight assessments and consultations from other cluster partners further confirm the severity of food insecurity in the 2 proposed target districts of LaasCanod and Laasqoray. These require interventions aimed at reducing food consumption gaps, eradicating acute malnutrition, saving lives, and protecting and saving livelihoods. 

Response 
In respect of the above, the proposed project seeks to contribute to Food Security Cluster Objectives 1 and 2; which focus on improving immediate access to food and protecting livelihoods and related food sources respectively. The project will have positive impacts on food security, agricultural productivity, household incomes and resilience of smallholders particularly women in Sool and Sanag. The above will be achieved through 3 components highlighted hereafter.  

Component 1: Cash transfers: Vulnerable families will receive and utilize unconditional and conditional cash transfers to improve their access to food and to stabilize their family’s food security. 200 households (HH) will receive UCTs, while 247 households will receive conditional cash. 

Component 2: Support to small holder pastoral and agro pastoral households’: This will support the rehabilitation of communal infrastructure to ensure pastoral and agro pastoral households have access to water resources, pasture and other livelihood assets and earn income. Also, the project will support timely provision of seasonal agricultural inputs and trainings to help 60 farmers re-engage in their livelihoods and revitalize their value chains. 

Component 3: Cross cutting Monitoring Evaluation Accountability and Learning (MEAL): This will support to track project progress against set indicators and ensure accountability to the beneficiaries. 

Target communities and beneficiaries 
The project targets vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Laasqoray district of Sanag and Laas Caanood district of Sool regions. Specifically, the project will directly target and support approximately 3,549 people (55% female and 45% male). The vulnerable households will be identified in consultation with the communities using a mutually agreed upon criteria. The categories will mainly include IDPs, women or child headed households, elderly (65 years above), PwDs, chronically sick and severely food insecure families among the host community. The project will address the needs of these vulnerable groups who are at high risk or even mostly affected.

project_name: Implementación de planes de prevención de violencia basada en género - (Fase II) FC.0164
project_objective: Este proyecto le da continuidad a la Estrategia de Formadores/as y Promotoras/es para la Prevención de la Violencia Basada en Género (VBG), adelantada en 2017-2018. Esta segunda fase se enfoca en la creación, fortalecimiento e implementación de planes de prevención de violencia basada en género liderados por los grupos, comités o mesas de género de las regiones priorizadas y promotoras y promotores para la prevención de la VBG. El objetivo es aportar desde este enfoque de prevención de VBG a la autonomía política, social y económica, individual y colectiva de mujeres de las FARC en tránsito a la vida civil.

project_name: PREVENCIÓN DEL RECLUTAMIENTO, USO Y UTILIZACIÓN DE NIÑOS, NIÑAS Y ADOLESCENTES EN EL DEPARTAMENTO DEL CASANARE (CS.0393)
project_objective: Teniendo en cuenta la experiencia de la OIM en el diseño e implementación de estrategias orientadas al fortalecimiento de entornos protectores  para la prevención de las vulneraciones contra la niñez, la adolescencia y la juventud, esta propuesta se dirige a contribuir a la prevención del reclutamiento, uso y utilización de niños, niñas, adolescentes y jóvenes (NNAJ) a través de la promoción de acciones que aporten al fortalecimiento de las capacidades individuales y comunitarias para la protección  integral de los NNAJ y la prevención de sus vulneraciones en los municipios de Tauramena y Monterrey en Casanare.

project_name: Hilando Vidas y Esperanza WLH (CS.1128)
project_objective:
Tiene como objetivo asociarse con el Gobierno de Colombia, las comunidades afectados por conflictos y los sobrevivientes de conflictos para promover la inclusión de mecanismos de apoyo psicosocial en las intervenciones comunitarias, mejorando el acceso a los servicios de salud mental y psicosociales; mitigar los riesgos asociados con el trauma psicosocial; y permitir que los sobrevivientes  del conflicto vivan una vida productiva y pacífica. Además, WLH apoyará a las organizaciones de la sociedad civil en áreas como liderazgo, generación de ingresos, resolución de conflictos y comunicación, para desarrollar capacidades locales, promover la resiliencia y fomentar transformaciones sociales para la convivencia pacífica. 

WLH implementará sus acciones en 15 municipios que forman parte de los municipios PDET. Los municipios de intervención de WLH se agrupan en 3 regiones de cinco municipios cada una I. Bajo Cauca y Noreste de Antioquia, 2. Pacífico Medio, Alto Patía y Norte del Cauca y 3. Montes de María.

project_name: Soutien à l’accès inclusif, sain et protecteur à l’éducation formelle (préscolaire, primaire, post-primaire  et secondaire), non formelle et informelle  de qualité pour les 227 380 enfants et adolescents (dont  136 428 filles/60%  et 90 952 garçons/40%) affectés  par les crises sécuritaire et sanitaire (COVID-19).
project_objective:
Le projet vise à : 
-	Soutenir l’accès inclusif, sain et protecteur à l’éducation et la formation formelle (préscolaire, primaire, post-primaire, secondaire et formation aux métiers), non formelle et informelle de qualité pour les 227 380 enfants et adolescents (dont136 428 filles/60% et 90 952 garçons/40%) affectés par les crises sécuritaire et sanitaire (COVID-19). 
-	Renforcer les capacités de 4548 enseignants (2 729 femmes et1819 hommes) sur l’Approche Safe School (développement des plans scolaires de préparation/réponse aux urgences et protocole sanitaire COVID-19), l’assistance psychosociale et l'apprentissage socio-émotionnel.
Parmi les enfants ciblés, 120 511 sont affectés par les mouvements des populations (IDP et refugiés) soit 53% ; 22 738 sont des enfants en situation de handicap (ESH) soit 10% ; 34 107 sont du secondaire (soit 15%) et 45 476 sont des enfants du préscolaire (soit 20%).
 
Tous les bénéficiaires vivent dans les 13 régions du pays dont les six (6) particulièrement affectées par les urgences sécuritaires en plus de la COVID-19. Il s’agit de : La Boucle du Mouhoun, le Centre-Nord, l’Est, le Centre-Est, le Nord et le Sahel. 
Le paquet d’activités proposé leur apportera une éducation et une formation formelle et non formelle dans un environnement sûr, inclusif et de qualité. Cela correspond à la vision de la SSZDS et du HRP 2022 du Burkina Faso.

project_name: Contribution UNICEF à la reponse aux urgences sanitaires au Burundi
project_objective:
La situation des enfants au Burundi est caractérisée par une forte mortalité infanto juvénile estimée à 78‰ naissances vivantes (EDS 2016-2017) avec prédominance de causes évitables ou traitables. La mortalité maternelle reste élevée à 334 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes, (EDS 2016) et demeure extrêmement préoccupante malgré une baisse par rapport à l’EDS 2010 (500 pour 100 000 Naissances Vivantes). Les Burundais de tout le pays, en particulier les femmes et les enfants, restent vulnérables aux crises humanitaires due à des niveaux élevés de pauvreté, et cette situation précaire est aussi aggravée par les catastrophes naturelles (comme inondations, glissements de terrain et déficits pluviométriques), les épidémies, comme le choléra, les pics de paludisme, la rougeole, les plaies ulcéreuses, le risque qu’Ebola se propage dans le pays et plus récemment la pandémie à la Covid19. La survenue des désastres naturels, les impacts socio-économiques de la Covid-19 sur les plus vulnérables et les retours des réfugiés burundais en provenance des pays limitrophes ont contribué à une augmentation des besoins humanitaires en 2021 et en 2020 comparait à l’année 2019. A cet effet, pour les projections pour 2022, les désastres naturels (désormais réguliers) et une intensification du processus de rapatriement sont attendus tandis que des maladies comme le choléra et le paludisme demeurent des risques importants en raison de leur caractère endémique. L'impact de la Covid-19 devrait également se faire sentir pendant l'année 2022. Prenant en compte ces besoins et risques, le nombre de personnes en besoin d’assistance humanitaire est passé de 1,74 million à 2,3 millions (donc 1,06 millions ciblés par les acteurs humanitaires) de personnes, entre 2020 et 2021, représentant ainsi une augmentation de 35 pour cent par rapport à l’année dernière.
Sur le plan épidémiologique, certaines maladies à fort potentiel épidémique restent répandues dans tout le pays, notamment le paludisme, la rougeole et le COVID-19. Le système de santé et les installations au niveau communautaire restent fragiles et un cinquième de la population n'a pas accès aux soins de santé primaires. Il y a eu une augmentation de 14% des cas de paludisme par rapport à la même période l'année dernière. Notons qu’en 2021, 490 cas de rougeole ont été enregistrés dans 31 des 47 districts sanitaires. La pandémie de COVID-19 devrait continuer à interrompre une reprise économique encore fragile, exacerbant les besoins humanitaires. Au 15 décembre 2021, 21 422 personnes au total avaient été testées positives pour 936 339 tests réalisés. La situation s'est détériorée avec une augmentation exponentielle depuis fin juin, bien que la plupart des cas signalés soient asymptomatiques, avec un taux de mortalité signalé inférieur à 1% jusqu'à présent.
Lors de l’atelier d’élaboration du HNO, l’analyse de la situation a conduit le secteur de la santé à identifier les populations affectées comme étant celles de 16 des 18 provinces du pays (Bubanza, Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cankuzo, Cibitoke, Kirundo, Makamba, Muramvya, Mwaro, Rumonge, Rutana, Gitega, Karusi, Ngozi Makamba, Muyinga, Rumonge, Rutana et Ruyigi). Ces provinces sont priorisés du fait de la récurrence des désastres naturels et leurs conséquences sur les déplacements internes, les maladies à potentiel épidémique, les impacts socioéconomiques de la Covid-19 et l’insécurité alimentaire qui contribuent à la sévérité des besoins intersectoriels dans ces localités. Le plateau technique des services de santé maternelle et néonatale est insuffisant et le pays dispose de capacités limitées d’offre de soins obstétricaux d’urgence de base complet. Les ratios de décès maternels et taux de décès néonataux sont excessifs selon les données de la surveillance intégrée de la maladie et la riposte, soit 343 décès maternels et 2,390 décès périnatals notifiés jusqu’à la semaine fin novembre 2021.

project_name: Multi-sectoral humanitarian response for refugees in Sudan
project_objective:
Medair aims to address the emergency humanitarian needs of the refugees through a multi-sectoral approach which will include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) and Emergency Shelter & Non-Food Items.  The project targets the refugees in Gedaref, Kassala, White Nile, and the population targeted include the refugees arriving from Ethiopia due to the Northern Ethiopian crisis started since one year ago and other refugees in the country. The goal of the project is to contribute to the reduction of excess mortality and mobidity among the refugees in Sudan, and to restore dignity of them through improving their living conditions including hygiene and sanitation. 
Since March 2021, Medair has been providing to the refugee population in the two refugee camps in Gedaef multi-sectoral assistance in the areas of Shelter/NFI, site improvements, and WASH. In Tunaydbah, Medair has enrolled over 360 lead mothers and 2,000 female participants in its community-based Care Groups for Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) programming covering topics of hygiene, nutrition and health. Medair has completed almost 30 km of micro drainage throughout Tunaydbah in full coordination with UNHCR for technical design and linkage to their macro drainage schemes for flood prevention, and constructed 108 permanent latrines and bathing shelters. Medair has been selected as a UNHCR Shelter partner for a transitional shelter project in Tunaydbah. In Um Rakuba, Medair runs a Rapid Response Team for cholera prevention (and response in the event of cases/outbreak), with full support of UNHCR WASH technical guidance.

project_name: Increased Access to and Quality of Lifesaving Preventative and Curative Primary Healthcare and Integrated Nutrition, Including Integrated Services for People with Physical Disabilities and Essential GBV Protection Services for Vulnerable Conflict-affected Populations
project_objective:
This project aims to reach 430,682 target beneficiaries (excluding overlap), while building on the experience, expertise and relationships from its previous project cycles. The goal is to reach the most vulnerable with protection mainstreaming and sustainability at the core of its programme. Medair will focus on rehabilitating and/or re-equipping primary healthcare facilities in areas with high needs, prioritizing hard to reach and newly accessible areas, as well as rehabilitating a maternity ward. 

 

Firstly, Medair will engage in infrastructure rehabilitation and/or re-equipment, then a 12-month programme of capacity building for staff will follow. The community health programme (CHP) will target key health, hygiene and nutrition behaviours through messaging at household level in the clinic catchment population. For the PHCCs rehabilitated and/or re-equipped by Medair in 2021, the supervision, training and CHP will continue into 2022. Medair plans to rehabilitate and/or re-equip up to 6 PHCCs during 2022, 6 PHCCs in 2023, and 4 maternity centers in 2022-2023. Additionally, 3 hospitals will be provided with equipment for COVID-19, including training, PPE for visitors, and equipment to support ICU beds. Healthcare for people with disabilities and initial assistance to GBV will be cohesively integrated. Nutrition screening and treatment will also be integrated – submitted separately as per HRP guidance. 

 

Medair Health officers will conduct field visits and training and existing public sector health staff will provide the services as a sustainability measure. To ensure sustained access to healthcare, Medair will exit the locations at the end of the support period, 12 months after rehabilitation by handover to regional health authorities. 615 health workers and 430 CHWs will be trained in 2022. The training package for both is extensive, and delivered over a 12 month period by Medair staff, qualified MOH staff, and external trainers. Medair provides transport/accommodation costs for trainers if needed. Health worker training comprises 28 days per governorate, covering key gaps (RH (ANC, PNC, FP),mhGAP, PFA, Disability inclusion, NCDs, and IMCI) and COVID-19. CHWs receive 8 days of initial training then 6 refresher days, delivered by clinic. Supervisors also attend M+E days. Topics include ANC/PNC, nutrition, MHPSS awareness, PFA, hygiene, communicable diseases, NCDs, GBV awareness, and disability awareness. CHWs will also identify up to 800 PLWMIs in order to support them with Assistive Devices. Consultation target is calculated based on catchment population, a clinic utilization rate of 1 and number of months.

project_name: Soutien à la préparation et la prise en charge initiale des Urgences Sanitaire dans 8 provinces sanitaires cibles au Burundi
project_objective:
Le Burundi est périodiquement frappé par diverses épidémies dont les flambées les plus importantes sont le choléra, le paludisme, la rougeole, les méningites à méningocoque, et les zoonoses telles que la rage, avec le plus souvent, une mortalité et une morbidité élevées. A titre d'exemple, en 2019, le Burundi a été touché une importante épidémie de Choléra dans une dizaine de districts sanitaires du pays (en particulier les district sanitaires situés le long du Lac Tanganyika, répartis sur 6 provinces parmi les 18 que comptent le pays) qui ont fait 1258 cas avec une létalité estimée à 1%. Lors de cette épidémie de choléra de 2019, la tranche d'âge la plus touchée est de 19 à 50 ans avec un sexe ratio égale à 1. Ce phénomène de récurrence des épidémies au Burundi ne concerne pas seulement les maladies hydriques comme le choléra. En effet toujours en 2019, le pays a été touché une épidémie de paludisme avec 8 892 300 épisodes de paludisme enregistrés parmi la population burundaise et 3 294 décès liés à cette pathologie. En 2021, c'est 5 690 045 épisodes de paludismes qui ont été enregistré dans le pays avec 1519 décès.
Le contexte favorable à la survenue des épidémies, se justifie par de nombreux facteurs, en particulier, une succession de crises complexes, qui ont contribué à annihiler les efforts de l’état dans le secteur de la santé et à installer une bonne partie de la population dans un état de précarité chronique les exposants aux maladies transmissibles à fort potentiel épidémique. Parallèlement à ce contexte socio-politique particulier, le Burundi, tout comme les autres pays de la Région des Grands Lacs est en proie à plusieurs Urgences Humanitaires (rapatriement, déplacement des populations par suite de catastrophes naturelles comme; les inondations, glissements de terrain…) qui exposent les victimes de ces aléas et les communautés hôtes à l’émergence ou la ré-émergence de plusieurs maladies à fort potentiel épidémique (voir même pandémiqur). Si on prenait que l'année 2020, une succession de catastrophes naturelle ont touché la province de Bujumbura et ses environs, occasionnant beaucoup de dégâts dont près de 50 000 personnes affectés (avec des déplacements des populations), un délabrement de 6 formations sanitaires et une douzaine d'écoles inondées, plus particulièrement dans la localité de Gatumba (province de Bujumbura).   
   
Afin d’identifier les principaux défis en termes de préparation et de réponse aux différentes Urgence Sanitaires, plusieurs évaluations ont été menées et ont montré que malgré les avancées notables en termes de préparation du pays à la prévention, la détection et la réponse rapide, un décalage important demeure entre le niveau central et le niveau périphérique (niveau district et province sanitaire).

L'objectif de ce projet est de renforcer les capacités du Burundi dans la préparation et réponse initiale à la prise en charge des urgences de santé publique y compris des épidémies, avec un accent particulier au niveau périphérique. Cette préparation va être concentrée essentiellement dans 8 provinces sanitaires qui sont à l'Est du pays le long du lac Tanganyika (Bujumbura Mairie, Bujumbura Rural, Cibitoke, Bubanza et Rumonge) et ceux du Nord (Muyinga, Makamba et Ruyigi) qui reçoivent un nombre conséquent de retournés, de réfugiés et de déplacés interne. 

Même si le projet cible un nombre de total de bénéficieras de 201 436 personnes (suivant la population ciblée comme dans le besoin dans le plan de réponse humanitaire de 2021), les activités du projet auront un impact direct sur le reste de la communauté hôte des provinces cibles (faisant ainsi un parfait lien entre l'humanitaire et le développement). Cette population est estimée à 5 880 430 personnes, dont 2 924 485 femmes et 2 955 945 hommes.

project_name: Assistance nutritionnelle aux principaux groupes les plus vulnérables des régions les plus impactées par l'insécurité
project_objective:
Malgré les efforts notables réalisés au Burkina Faso dans le domaine de la nutrition,  la malnutrition demeure un problème majeur de santé publique. Le pays connait une situation sécuritaire qui continue de se détériorer de façon significative sur l'ensemble du territoire avec pour corollaire un déplacement massif continue de populations, mais aussi un accès limité aux soins de santé primaires qui a été exacerbé par l'impact indirect de la pandémie à la COVID-19 qui n'a pas épargnée le Burkina Faso depuis Mars 2020. Les résultats de l'enquête rapid SMART
de Juillet et Octobre 2020 dans les communautés et sites d'accueil de grand effectif de personnes déplacées internes a révélé une situation nutritionnelle critique des enfants de 6 à 59 mois ainsi que des femmes enceintes et femmes allaitantes (FEFA) chez les PDls mais aussi chez les ménages hôtes,. La prévalence de la malnutrition aigüe globale dépasse le« seuil d'alerte» OMS de 10% dans un grand nombre de communes avec des facteurs aggravants ou surpasse le seuil d'urgence/critique de l'OMS de 15% dans certaines communes des régions du Sahel et du Centre Nord.
La dernière analyse IPC réalisée en Novembre 2021 confirme que la situation du Burkina Faso reste très préoccupante, et ne laisse pas présager de grosses améliorations pour 2022, Bien évidemment, les prévisions de la communauté humanitaire pourraient s’assombrir.
Au regard de ce contexte, et de la  couverture de la prise en charge globale de la malnutrition aigüe toujours insuffisante, le PAM fournira une assistance nutritionnelle d'urgence, avec une approche multisectorielle ( nutrition-sécurité alimentaire, nutrition-santé), sous forme d'un package d'interventions complémentaires et synergiques comprenant l'extension des activités de prévention de la malnutrition , le traitement de la malnutrition aiguë modérée y compris au niveau communautaire, le renforcement de capacité des agents de santé communautaires y compris dans le traitement au niveau communautaire et la Communication pour le Changement Social et Comportemental (CCSC).
Le PAM fournira un appui nutritionnel préventif sous forme de « rations de protection» nutritives et enrichies à  68040 enfants âgés de 6 à 23 mois (IDPs et Pop Hôtes).L’appui aux femmes enceintes et allaitantes rentrera dans le cadre d’un projet de sécurité alimentaire . Cela permettra de réduire les risques de malnutrition ou réduire e les risques d'aggraver davantage la situation nutritionnelle.Cette intervention spécifique, tout en permettant de réaliser des dépistages actifs de la malnutrition aigüe puis en orientant précocement les sujets diagnostiqués malnutris vers les structures de prises en charge appropriées, est une opportunité pour renforcer les connaissances des participants sur les bonnes pratiques alimentaire, d'hygiène, assainissement en vue de leur adoption .
Durant 12 mois, le PAM appuiera également la prise en charge curative « intégrée» au niveau des structures de soins mais aussi au niveau communautaire des enfants de 6-59 mois et des femmes enceintes ou allaitantes présentant une malnutrition aigüe modérée. Les structures de prise en charge étatiques seront approvisionnées en intrants nutritionnels adaptés, pour assister 86852 enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois et 41173 FEFA pendant trois mois. Pour contribuer et  renforcer la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigüe sévère dans les centres de récupération et d'éducation nutrition, le PAM prévoit apporter une assistance alimentaire à 16600 mères d'enfants MAS hospitalisés. 
Le présent projet qui adressera les besoins des populations déplacées, hôtes et vulnérables, vise à contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité infantile et maternelle, à travers une amélioration de la couverture de prise en charge préventive et curative de la malnutrition et à la promotion cohabitation pacifique entre ces populations, tout en assurant une approche multisectorielle, avec respect du genre et protection sociale.

project_name: Prevención y atención humanitaria a niñas, niños y adolescentes víctimas de violencia en el corredor seco.
project_objective:
La niñez y adolescencia en Guatemala constituye un sector de la población altamente vulnerable a sufrir violencia, específicamente violencia sexual. En 2019 el Ministerio Público, recibió 111 denuncias al día por diversos delitos contra la niñez, cifra que durante la pandemia se redujo casi en un 50%, reportándose 70 casos al día, lo que evidenció la dificultad de acceso a los servicios de protección durante la emergencia, y no una disminución real de la violencia hacia ellos.
El panorama anterior se agudiza en los 88 municipios del corredor seco, en los cuales además de la situación alimentaria y nutricional que enfrentan, se suma la alta vulnerabilidad a la violencia en todas sus manifestaciones. El 36% de los delitos cometidos hacia la niñez y adolescencia proviene de los municipios del corredor seco. Los delitos más frecuentes son el maltrato infantil (30%) y violencia sexual (20%).
En la sociedad guatemalteca predominan patrones culturales/normas sociales de género, que reproducen prejuicios y estereotipos que generan violencia de género hacia las niñas, adolescentes y mujeres en todos los ciclos de vida; la brecha es aún mayor para las niñas y adolescentes indígenas, ya que a la discriminación por género se le agrega la discriminación étnica y lingüística.
Ante ese contexto, el proyecto tiene como propósito prevenir la violencia hacia la niñez y brindar atención humanitaria a niñez víctima de violencia, para lo cual se enfocará en las siguientes acciones: a) generar acciones de prevención de la violencia hacia la niñez y adolescencia en los 88 municipios del corredor seco; b) impulsar la puesta en marcha de sistemas municipales y comunitarios de protección a la niñez y adolescencia, en 40 delos 88 municipios del corredor seco, para lo cual se promoverá desde el modelo socio ecológico, la transformación de conocimientos, actitudes y prácticas que generan violencia hacia la niñez y la adolescencia; c) brindar atención humanitaria individual y grupal a niñez víctima de delitos, en los principales departamentos del corredor seco que presentan mayor número de víctimas detectadas, coordinando y trasladando capacidades metodológicas al Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social; d)fortalecer las acciones de monitoreo y supervisión a cargo de la Procuraduría de los
Derechos Humanos.
Beneficiarios:
150,000 niñas, niños y adolescentes beneficiados con las acciones de prevención y 500niñas, niños y adolescentes víctimas de violencia que recibirán atención psicosocial individual y grupal.

project_name: Provide immediate access to water services
project_objective:
In light of the current economic and fuel crises, the intended intervention will aim to support existing infrastructure for water supply system through procurement and supply of chlorine  and other consumables, emergency repair for pumping stations with provision of fuel to maintain minimum operational level and providing the most vulnerable communities with water supply. This approach is deemed to take the most cost-effective pathway to reach a high number of people in need in a short time period. The only way to avoid the complete shutdown of all or part of the water systems in Lebanon is through this intervention and support to pumping stations.  
To identify the communities most affected by the current economic crisis, the water sector is conducting a country wide vulnerability mapping exercise based on two criteria: (1) current access to water, measured in l/c/d; (2) energy source for the water supply system (fuel based, gravity fed, EdL, or PV).
The highly critical communities have been classified as the ones with energy sources relying on fuel exclusively, and currently receiving less than 35 L/c/day based on the Water Sector LCRP minimal standard for water supply in Informal settlements.]
