project_name: Réponse aux effets de la crise sécuritaire dans les écoles des régions de Tahoua et Tillabéri par le programme d'alimentation scolaire
Projet de renforcement par la radio de l'engagement communautaire et de la redevabilité dans la réponse humanitaire auprès des personnes vulnérables.
project_objective:
Depuis 2015, le Burkina Faso traverse une crise sécuritaire faisant de nombreuses victimes et obligeant les populations à fuir leurs foyers. Le nombre de personnes déplacées internes (PDIs) au Burkina Faso est passé de 560.033 en décembre 2019 à 1.074.993 individus en décembre 2020, soit une augmentation de 92%, d’après le Conseil national de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (Conasur) qui pointe du doigt la dégradation continue de la situation sécuritaire. 
Au 2e semestre 2021, au regard de l’aggravation rapide de la vulnérabilité et du nombre de déplacement de population ;
•	Le nombre de PDI reste croissant du fait de la recrudescence des violences ; le pays comptait maintenant 1 428 378 Personnes Déplacées Internes au 31 Août 2021.
•	3,5 millions de personnes en tout ont besoin d'assistance humanitaire au Burkina Faso selon OCHA.
•	Selon le cadre harmonisé de Mars 2021 (période projetée de juin à août 2021), 2,86 millions de personnes sont en insécurité alimentaire aigüe. 
•	892 952 Personnes sont affectées par la fermeture de 85 formations sanitaires et des 271 autres qui fonctionnent à minima. 
Fort est de constater que les acteurs humanitaires présents dans les zones recueillant le plus les personnes déplacées font de leur mieux pour apporter des réponses aux préoccupations des personnes affectées. Cependant nombreux sont encore ceux et celles qui ne savent pas vraiment où se tourner pour des besoins spécifiques. 
D’où l’intérêt de ce projet qui va permettre de faciliter le dialogue entre les personnes affectées et les acteurs humanitaires à travers les médias. Ce projet contribuera à renforcer la redevabilité collective dans la réponse humanitaire du Burkina Faso en assurant la collecte, l'agrégation et l'analyses des préoccupations et plaintes des personnes affectées. En partenariat avec le groupe de travail sur l'engament et communautaire et la redevabilité (CEAWG), la Fondation Hirondelle à travers le Studio Yafa travaillera à reverser les préoccupations et plaintes des populations affectées aux différents clusters.  Le projet permettra aussi de ferme la fermer la boucle de communication avec les communautés en élaborant des messages informatifs pour les personnes affectées.
Le projet contribuera ainsi à améliorer la qualité de l’assistance humanitaire pour sauver les vies et restaurer la dignité des communautés touchées – en particulier leurs membres les plus vulnérables – au Burkina Faso dans le cadre du triple nexus.
Facteur aggravant : La cohabitation entre les PDIs et les familles d'accueil peut également conduire à des tensions sur le partage des ressources, notamment alimentaires, qui deviennent de plus en plus rares, aggravant ainsi les problèmes sociaux.
Valeur ajoutée d'une ONG de médias comme la Fondation Hirondelle
En tant qu'intervenant humanitaire :
Toutes les parties prenantes (y compris le Secrétaire Général du Conseil National de Secours d'Urgence et de Réhabilitation (CONASUR)) sont convaincues de la valeur ajoutée de la Fondation Hirondelle, car elles identifient de nombreuses lacunes dans la collecte d'informations vers les communautés affectées et aussi des communautés hôtes vers les acteurs humanitaires.
C’est en cela que la Fondation Hirondelle a rejoint le Community Engagement – Accountability Working Group (CEAWG) où est louée sa capacité à renforcer le lien entre les communautés dans le besoin humanitaire et l'action humanitaire à travers les médias et sa capacité à jouer un rôle d'interface pour le retour   d’informations des acteurs de l'assistance humanitaire et les communautés bénéficiaires (communication à double sens).

project_name: Scale up access to quality Gender Based Violence Prevention and Response services in North East Nigeria
project_objective:
The project seeks to innovatively scale up and improve access to quality integrated GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response services adapted to both the changing context of protracted crisis in the midst of government camp closures, resettlements/secondary displacement and lingering Covid-19 pandemic across the BAY states of northeast Nigeria.

The targeted interventions will includ provision of lifesaving multi-sectorial and multi-level services that will address the medical, psychosocial, legal and safety needs of GBV survivors in IDP camps, host communities and communities of return as well strengthening inclusive community protection and dispute resolution mechanisms to mitigate and prevent GBV both as the sub-sector lead and as the provider of last resort.

The project will not only focus on expanding and maintain services in safe spaces/shelters and one stop-centres (OSC), but improving referrals to medical and other services while ensuring enhanced capacity for quality delivery of clinical management of rape (CMR), case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), legal and protection services, procurement and distribution of menstrual/dignity kits, cultural appropriate clothing, field coordination including referral pathways and ethical data management. The intervention will also seek to engage men and boys as allies and agent of change through the introduction of evidence based interventions like EMAP to address the root causes and harmful gender norms.
  
Other complementary activities will look at strengthening community resilience and promoting GBV/SEA risk mitigation mechanism in humanitarian setting. Our target is to reach 55% (750,000) of the sectors people in need (1,362,447) in the BAY States. Special emphasis will be put on strengthening joint inter-agency coordination, M&E, capacity building, assessment and partnership that will translate to better outcome.

project_name: Renforcer l'accès aux services de soins obstétricaux et néonatals d’urgence dans les régions humanitaires du Mali
project_objective:
Depuis plusieurs mois les régions du nord et plus particulièrement celles du centre sont le théâtre d’affrontements intercommunautaires qui ont fortement fragilisés la situation des femmes et des filles. Cette situation d’insécurité contribue également de détérioration des soins maternelles obstétricaux déjà très fragile, l’accès aux soins et de services de protection des populations 
Les indicateurs de la santé maternelle et néonatale restent très alarmants, bien que nous n’avons pas d’études comparatives. En effet, la mortalité maternelle est de 368 décès pour 100 000 naissances vivantes, soit environ 3 360 décès de femmes suite à l'accouchement chaque année et le taux de mortalité chez les nouveaux nés est de 34 pour 1000 (EDSV). Ces indicateurs se sont détériorés dans les zones de Gao, Tombouctou, Mopti et Ségou où les attaques récurrentes ont provoqué le départ des agents de santé et la destruction des structures sanitaires ., On note une insuffisance  de services sociaux de base dans les endroits où les populations se deplacent , il y a de CSOM non fonctionnels par manque de prestataires  qualifié à cause de l’insecurité  et les femmes  et jeunes filles font de longues distances pour acceder aux services de SR, les strategies mobiles  pourront faciliter l’acces aux services de ces femmes et jeunes filles deplacées . Il existe une l’insuffisance de personnels formés  sur  les DMU/gestion clinique de violences sexuelles du fait de la grande mobilité de prestataires, En plus de barrieres socio culturelles liés à l’acceptabilité et à l’accessibilité , la presence de groupes radicaux dans certaines zones  demotivent les femmes à recourir  à l’utilisation de services de  Planification familiale .
Les accouchements à domicile , l’absence de suivi  de la grossesse  pendant les  CPN et CPON   demeurent  très frequents  dans les communautés   et cela pouvant contribuer à la morbidité et mortalité maternelle 
L’objectif général du projet vise à contribuer à la  réduction de la mortalité et de la morbidité maternelles à travers une meilleure disponibilité et accès aux services de soins obstétricaux et néonataux d'urgence et aux services de santé sexuelle et reproductive dans les régions de Gao, Tombouctou, Mopti, Ségou et Bamako, dans les cercles prioritaires ci-après  :  Baraoueli ,Segou ,Bla, San, Niono, Macina ,Mopti ,Bandiagara, Bankass, Djenné, Douentza, Koro, Tenenkou, Tombouctou ,Dire ,Goundam, Gourma-rharous ,Gao, Ansongo, Bourem, Kidal, Tin-essako, Abeibara ,Tessalit ,Menaka ,Anderamboukane, Inekar ,Tidermene ;Les interventions viennent en complémentarité pour soutenir les actions déjà entreprises par UNFPA dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie pour répondre aux besoins des femmes et filles en termes d’accès aux soins en santé reproductive et sexuelle mais également aux services de protection dans un contexte fragile marqué par l’amenuisement des services sociaux de base, les conflits intercommunautaires, les mouvements de populations et des violations graves de droits humains telles que les violences sexuelles, l’exploitation et l’abus sexuels, les mariages forcés et celui des enfants.

project_name: Addressing site management needs and enhance assistance for safe and dignified living conditions in refugee camps and sites
project_objective:
The project aims to continue strengthening and improving a wide range of Site Management components including: enhancing the capacity of site management actors through targeted modular training, maintaining and improving site management facilities, ensuring continuous access to services, promoting community participation, promoting adherence to Site Management standards and practices,  enhancing site development including improvement of settlements’ infrastructure, site planning that address vulnerability to natural hazards and natural resource management.  

In partnership with the RRRC, CiCs, IOM and Site Management partners, UNHCR will work towards strengthening coordination structures, site management and development at the camp level.  UNHCR will continue supporting the Government in strengthening and promoting community representation structures and civilian administration of the camps, while its partnership with MoDMR and RRRC will remain key to UNHCR’s engagement in the camps.  

UNHCR expects the gradual transition of Site Management functions to the Government to proceed in 2022, and accordingly through the Capacity Sharing Initiative will continue to prioritize training of the RRRC, CiC and partner staff to enhance understanding and application of Site Management standards. UNHCR’s response will focus on engaging more closely with refugees to ensure interventions respond better to their needs; capacity building and support to the Government; enhancing decision-making structures based on inclusive refugee representation structures and strengthening linkages between refugee preferences and available assistance; and promote the sustainability of interventions in collaboration with partners while continually searching for comprehensive solutions.  

UNHCR will aim to build on the lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic by strengthening remote Site Management through refugee volunteer networks and remote management tools. In order to improve participation and ownership of critical infrastructure and other community assets, UNHCR will continue working with refugees and the Site Management and Site Development Sector to implement community-led projects. 

Community and protection assessments have shown that refugees, specifically women and girls continue to face various protection risks and challenges such as poor lighting at night and increasing threats targeting female volunteers have also added to the sense of insecurity in the camps. UNHCR will strengthen initiatives to reduce tensions and promote peaceful co-existence between the refugee and host communities and will design programs based on community consultations and feedback received from refugees and host communities including through the rollout of the Common Feedback Mechanism. 

As Bangladesh is particularly vulnerable to climate change, UNHCR will continue to enhance the resilience of both refugees and host communities against seasonal natural disasters such as monsoon and cyclones as well as man-made risks such as fire hazards, and to strengthen preparedness and ensure timely activation and deployment of personnel, partners and volunteers, as well continue supporting them with adequate gears equipment and relevant DRM trainings, drills and simulations, while continuing the prepositioning of essential relief items ahead of disasters.  

UNHCR will work to ensure implementation of the Climate Action Plan to further the greening of the camps and plans to invest in bamboo plantations to mitigate the impact of excessive bamboo use for shelter and infrastructure construction. An LPG assessment conducted by UNHCR’s partner found 80 percent reduction in deforestation as a direct impact of the sustainable use of LPG. At the same time, UNHCR will improve community safety through continuous functioning of solar streetlights, mini-grids, and other camp infrastructure.

project_name: Population has optimal access to education
project_objective:
UNHCR will strive to ensure that Rohingya refugee children aged 3-24 have access to equitable quality education opportunities through the continuation of existing programs by maintaining existing learning facilities, recruiting, training and deployment of teachers, procurement of teaching and learning materials and expansion of learning facilities by construction and maintenance of existing and additional single-story classrooms with sex segregated latrines and WASH facilities. Looking at implementation beyond the Myanmar Curriculum pilot, UNHCR supported the Education Sector with the development of a comprehensive scale up roadmap guiding Education Sector partners in MC scaleup approach. Furthermore, considering COVID-19 and its implications, UNHCR and its partners will implement EdTech solutions. UNHCR will continue ensuring community engagement in the overall project cycle ensuring Age Gender and Diversity (AGD) mainstreaming. 
In addition, the transitioning of LCFA level I-II students to Myanmar curriculum (MC) will be a critical undertaking for the second half of the year. As a step forward to ensure the provision of quality education and with the introduction of MC, language and teacher professional development training is required to ensure educators and learners have the required language competencies and expected teaching qualifications, hence teacher professional development incorporating both in-service and ongoing teacher professional development activities, continuation and expansion of language acquisition program for Myanmar and English language as well as scaling up certified mentorship trainings for the education partners’ staff  in collaboration with BARD college and BRAC University will be undertaken. Additionally, certified mentorship training for around 2,500 teachers will be executed to equip them with pedagogical knowledge and skills to deliver MC.
UNHCR will continue its host community support through maintaining and operationalizing the Community Technology Access (CTA) and the satellite teachers training facility, constructing, or renovating classrooms and WASH facilities and provide classroom furniture and supplies. UNHCR further will work with sector and partners to ensure a synchronized student data collection system using proGres data base to avoid duplication and ensure reliable education data and analysis.  Activities will also enhance school community governance and participation mechanisms, including risk reduction activities; integrate school community-based participatory planning and community awareness, with an emphasis on targeted training on child rights and child safeguarding principles, the role of parents in school enrolment, participation and retention, activities promoting peaceful co-existence and social cohesion such as co-curricular activities and community events. 
UNHCR engages with the refugees’ community on a regular basis through the Age-Gender-Diversity-Mainstreaming (AGDM) exercise. UNHCR also collects feedbacks through post distribution surveys and protection profiling exercises.  
In addition, UNHCR has the following mechanisms in place to received feed-back from the refugees:  
•Rohingya refugees are provided a helpline (+88 017 359 3300) to speak directly with a UNHCR protection staff on various thematic issues. The issues raised were channelled to various sections within UNHCR to seek appropriate solutions.  
•Suggestion box are in place in each of learning centre where the parents and community members can share their complain and suggestion for further improvement.
•The community are being consulted periodically through FGDs and KIIs to identify their opening on the services provided as well as identify the area of improvement.
•UNHCR monitors and evaluates its intervention through Multi-functional team visit in which the parents/ LCMC members play a vital role as an important member of the team.

project_objective:
WFP will provide early recovery and resilience to shocks will be promoted through asset creation and preservation and, increased livelihoods  Joint multi-sectoral assessments and Emergency Food Security Analysis will be conducted regularly to monitor the nutrition, food security, and markets situation in crisis-affected states.
A gender-transformative approach that reflects the needs of women, men, girls, and boys will be adopted. WFP will mainstream protection throughout its work, supported by a solid understanding of the operational context and protection analysis. Training and capacity building of staff and partners in the protection and humanitarian principles will include on-the-job coaching. WFP will ensure that affected populations (women and men) will be consulted throughout the programme cycle; beneficiary feedback mechanisms will be tailored to their preferred means of communication. Beneficiaries will continue to be empowered with knowledge on their food assistance entitlements and their rights, including WFP’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). WFP will continue the collection of key information on beneficiaries and assistance provided as part of its M&E activities. Monthly monitoring will include distribution and activity site management; beneficiary and entitlement verification; and ensuring adequate protection and gender measures. Lessons will be regularly drawn from monthly process and biannual outcome monitoring and reporting, and periodic reviews and evaluation to inform strategic and operational decisions.
WFP will further consolidate partnerships to enhance national and state-level emergency preparedness and response systems, including food security and nutrition assessment and monitoring, early warning, protection, gender analysis, targeting, and registration processes, safety nets, cash-based transfer capacities, and supply chain.
Where security and access to land allow, WFP plans to increase livelihood activities to support access to productive assets, income-generating activities, and self-reliance in the long term. Assistance will be coordinated with the local government, to ensure food assistance is complementary and fills gaps.

project_name: The Access Coordination Unit - Facilitating Access of Humanitarian and Recovery Actors in the oPt
project_objective: Access challenges differ greatly across the oPt, primarily due to the range of political and administrative measures implemented by Israeli and Palestinian authorities. Access and movement restrictions are severe, widespread, costly and difficult to overcome. They increase the impoverishment and vulnerability of Palestinian women, girls, boys, and men within the oPt, and directly impede humanitarian/development operations. They make reaching vulnerable communities difficult and compromise the quality of programming and impact the effectiveness of humanitarian and development interventions. These restrictions which have profound gender and protection impacts on different vulnerable groups, have been accentuated by the measures imposed by relevant authorities since March 2020 to contain the spread of C19. The Access Coordination Unit (ACU) provides a more systematic approach to these challenges and improves access of humanitarian personnel and goods in Israel, Gaza and the WB. Overall, 56% of ACU's UN staff beneficiaries are female (3350 from 6000). Working over all access points, the ACU provides direct engagement and advocacy with relevant authorities as well as direct and timely support, information and advice to international organizations and their personnel. The ACU also facilitates the movement of Palestinian staff serving at duty stations around the world, supporting family reunification and career development of humanitarian personnel. The ACU formulates common policies with a coordinated approach to alleviate constraints to access and to negotiate changes to access policies and procedures with the relevant authorities including Israel, the PA, Gaza authorities, Egypt and Jordan. The ACU currently supports the work of 24 UN agencies, over 200 NGOs, and 65 diplomatic missions whose access to populations in need is impeded by a series of political, physical and bureaucratic restrictions on access and movement imposed by authorities. In addition, an estimated 2.1 M Palestinians in need of assistance throughout the WB and Gaza will indirectly benefit through the more efficient and timely  delivery of humanitarian assistance. One of the primary services of the ACU is a 24/7 access hotline where staff can call the ACU to conduct real-time interventions with relevant authorities to resolve access incidents at checkpoints and crossings for both personnel and goods. The ACU also manages the ACULive mobile app which has 312 active users from 95 organizations, and which enables humanitarian and development personnel and agencies in the oPt to obtain timely and effective access information, guidance and support. The ACU also provides information and advice on procedures for obtaining visas, permits, project approvals and materials coordination as well as conditions and accessibility at checkpoints and crossings via the hotline and beneficiary-specific mailing list which includes 644 individuals working in UN, NGOs, and Diplomatic delegations. During emergencies and contingency situations, the ACU deploys to key field and coordination centres to conduct access and civil-military coordination with the relevant authorities. During the July-August 2014 escalation, the ACU facilitated evacuation of over 1,300 foreign and dual nationals from Gaza to Jordan as well as coordinating other humanitarian activities. ACU coordinated the exit of dual nationals from Gaza during the C19 restrictions, as well as the entry and exit of humanitarian personnel. The humanitarian locations notification system developed by the ACU was launched in 2019 and contains over 900 locations that are regularly shared with the Israeli authorities. During the May 2021 Gaza Escalation the ACU provided support to 1,185 UN, INGO, and diplomatic missions. Finally, information, analysis and messaging on restrictions to humanitarian space are made publicly available to support advocacy efforts undertaken by the humanitarian community and other stakeholders on access.

project_name: Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihood (EFSVL) Rohingya Response Programme in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
""The Emergency Food Security and Vulnerable Livelihood (EFSVL) Rohingya Response Programme aims to respond to the compounded risks of Covid-19 and pre-existing vulnerabilities of women and girls, men and boys and at-risk individuals among them in Rohingya and host communities. This project proposes to continue providing food security and livelihood support to vulnerable women, men, boys and girls of Rohingya & Host Community (HC) people for the lifesaving interventions to improve access to adequate diversified food access and livelihood opportunity. Intervention activities include COVID-19 livelihood support services like Unconditional Cash Grants (UCG); Cloth masks & cloth Sanitary Napkin products, complimentary food support to host community farmer’s market initiatives; enhancing DRR resilience linkages to food security; self-reliance and sustainable livelihood opportunity etc. In addition, the EFSVL project will work on Homestead Garden & Pit Composting, rural infrastructure through Cash for Work (CfW) approach, entrepreneurship and small trade business through Income Generating Activities (IGAs) and Vocational Training (VT) for the host communities through a market-based livelihood opportunity. As a result of the COVID-19 Pandemic context, the specific needs of food security & livelihood support, and Government policy restrictions on direct cash injection in the Rohingya camps, Oxfam prefers to do self-reliance activities (e.g. skill-based development training and input supports) for the Rohingya participants at the camps and COVID-19 livelihood activities (e.g. cloth masks and sanitary napkins production etc.) for the most vulnerable. Oxfam will do necessary coordination and cohesion between two communities (Rohingya and Host) by integrating EFSVL work with Oxfam’s Gender and Protection departments. The proposed interventions (e.g. IGAs such as Handicraft’s exhibition from both communities; Market based voucher initiatives; etc.) will contribute to strengthening the relationship and social cohesion within and between Rohingya and host communities. Assisting participants to live with good health, dignity and better safety.
Oxfam’s has a global commitment to build the capacity of local organizations through a partnership approach. Oxfam’s EFSVL sector will continue to work with local partners as part of its programme strategy. Oxfam will review the EFSVL strategy to cope with the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and Rohingya crises in 2022. ""

project_name: Assisting FDMN and Host communities in Cox's Bazar suffering from huge influx
project_objective:
Based on the findings from J-MSNA 2021 published by ISCG, this project will address the needs in WASH sector for both targeted blocks and host communities. The timeframe of this project is proposed one year and that will enable Tearfund and its partners to contribute on achieving the objectives set by ISCG WASH sector through addressing the needs of the targeted FDMN and Host population in Cox’s Bazar. Tearfund will engage local and national NGOs for implementing the project. As primary local partner COAST Foundation, CCDB & World Concern will implement this project funded by Tearfund and respective donors. Tearfund believes and promote in localization and capacity of local and national partners at the beginning of response. This project will support the implementation of localization agenda in Rohingya response. One of the Tearfund’s top focus on WASH will be implemented by three partners in several blocks under Camp 1E, 1W, 04, and Raja Palong, Ukhiya. As a result of its ongoing WASH interventions, one of the partners (CCDB) has been assigned as WASH Focal Organizations by UNHCR in Camp 1E, block- D and Camp 1W, block-G.
The project has been consulted with communities especially during designing phase through different need assessments. All interventions will follow ISCG-WASH sector and working groups’ guidelines. Beneficiary data has been disaggregated by age, gender and disability for informed decisions and decrease barriers to accessing services. To address most vulnerable people WASH needs the project will target women, children, elderly and persons with disabilities. The project also focusses on regular, sufficient and dignified access to WASH facilities for all age and gender groups through its planned interventions.
The project’s major activities includes; repair Tube well/water points, Installation of community water points in host community, repair latrines and bathing place, Latrine installation, Regular de-sludge Latrine pit, repair & maintenance of Faecal Sludge Management point, strengthen WASH management committee, Collect waste regularly from the targeted blocks, Drain repair, Maintenance of secondary waste dumping places, HHs and community waste bin distribution, Construction of waste dumping points, Family Hygiene Kit Distribution and Hygiene promotion session and Disinfection materials including safety materials for community people.
Tearfund and its partners are already active in coordination meeting at WASH sector in Coxsbazar and Camps. This project will keep coordination with WASH sector on regular basis while implementing. Meanwhile, 4Ws, Sitrep and other required reports will be shared for better coordination.
Tearfund will ensure the Accountability to the Affected Population (AAP) conducting community consultation meeting, involve them in project design and monitoring and influence on project activities. Tearfund and its partners will organize workshops at community level. This activity has been proposed to inform and engage affected populations and stakeholders in decision making process of the project. Besides, Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) will be carried out by hiring enumerators after distributions. This activity will help the project to know the community perception, feedback, further recommendations and impact of the distribution in the community. At the initial stage of the project, a baseline survey will be conducted to know the status of community people and how the project will support the most effective ways. Later end line surveys will be conducted to compare the change made due to project intervention and what is the status of targeted outcomes.

project_name: Enhancing smallholder farmers’ livelihood through market linkage and watershed management with social cohesion approach in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
The project will provide support to the targeted population which is identified by addressing the needs of the Rohingya and host communities through a recent study of FAO (FAO, 2021)  as:
1.	Develop portable skills for Rohingya refugees and improve farm productivity for host communities 
The project will provide technical support to refugees in developing portable skills on homestead gardening that will capacitate and equip them with relevant transferable technological competencies for sustainable integration into the economy upon their return to Myanmar. The project will also provide inputs support to the host communities in practicing climate-smart homestead vegetable gardening production methods for year-round households’ consumption and improved nutrition. 
In addition, the Digital Village initiative will be introduced to connect the farming families to agricultural information, ICT-based extension services, and financial inclusion. This will also promote a decentralized digital knowledge-sharing platform among rural farmers.
2.	Strengthening market linkage and social cohesion
Livelihood activities in the host community will mainly focus on marketing system approaches to ensure sustainability and adaptation of methodologies of the smallholders. In this regard, the project will provide technical support to improve the operational capacities of six Aggregation Centers (ACs) to establish vertical integration of the smallholder farmers with the traders and retailers in accessing the WFP led camp market/outlets. The farmers will be linked with the WFP’s ongoing activities including Fresh Food Corners in Rohingya camps to localize the supply of agricultural goods. This will support the income resilience of local farmers and enhance the social cohesion activity between the Rohingya and host communities.
FAO will work to strengthen functioning of the aggregation centers and provide transports, tools and other infrastructural facilities to them in improving efficacy.
The project will also conduct an assessment in identifying barriers to social cohesion and mapping the dynamics including driving factors within and between host communities and Rohingya people. 
3.	   Watershed and natural resource management
The intervention related to natural resource management will be implemented through a number of activities, such as land stabilization and reforestation which will contribute to the strengthen resilience capacities of communities by reducing climate-related risks, such as floods and landslides. The assessment under this output will provide guidance to project implementation and pave the way for future planning of interventions. 
The project will also contribute to applying climate-smart agricultural practices and diversified income-generating activities for the local farmers and forest-dependent vulnerable communities. This intervention will help the project stakeholders in the adaptive planning and decision-making process for sustainable natural resource management, while simultaneously contributing to the conservation of biodiversity and better functionality of the ecosystem.
Gender, age, and disability Inclusion: Project interventions will be identified considering the needs of men and women with an account of concerns, choice, and extra workload of women. The identified trades will also ensure equal access to men and women based on intersectionality analysis including SADDD (Sex, Age, and Disability Disaggregated Data).

project_name: Services multisectoriels et inclusifs d’urgence immédiate aux PDIs
project_objective:
Le principal objectif du HCR au Burundi en 2022 sera de favoriser la protection à tous les niveaux de la réponse humanitaire, y compris par le renforcement dans la direction et coordination du groupe sectoriel de la protection dans le cadre d’inter institutions aussi par la fourniture d'une formation adéquate au personnel et par l'élaboration d'un plan d'action de protection efficace pour l'équipe humanitaire de pays (Équipe Humanitaire Pays, EHP) au Burundi.  La DTM (Septembre 2021) a identifié 113 408 personnes déplacées internes (PDI) réparties dans 25 390 ménages déplacés, 83% des déplacements étaient dus à des catastrophes naturelles et 17% à d'autres raisons. Entre mars et mai 2021, les provinces de Bujumbura, Bujumbura Mairie, Rumonge et Makamba ont été fortement
touchées par des inondations dues à la montée des eaux du Lac Tanganyika qui ont affecté environ 52,000 personnes dont 22 000 déplacées. Dans la province de Bujumbura, certaines personnes déplacées ont été installées dans les sites de Sobel et Kinyinya II qui hébergeaient déjà des personnes déplacées par les inondations de 2020.  Les catastrophes liées aux risques naturels, y compris les
les effets néfastes du changement climatique, sont déplacements contemporains. Entre 2008 et 2015, 203,4 millions de personnes ont été déplacées par des catastrophes, et la probabilité d'être déplacé à la suite d'une catastrophe a a doublé depuis les années 1970 (IDMC 2015). Le changement climatique est également un multiplicateur de menaces, et peut exacerber les conflits pour l'épuisement des ressources. En ce qui concerne l'avenir, les scientifiques les scientifiques s'accordent largement à dire que les que les effets du changement climatique, combinés à d’autres facteurs, augmenteront les déplacements de population (IPCC, 2014). Les personnes déjà déplacées pour d'autres raisons- y compris les réfugiés, les apatrides et les personnes déjà déplacées pour d'autres raisons, y compris les réfugiés, les peuvent être exposées à des déplacements secondaires liés aux catastrophes et aux effets du changement climatique. Leur capacité leur capacité de retour peut être limitée si leur région d'origine est également touchées.

UNHCR Conformément à ces orientations stratégiques, les travaux du HCR sur le changement climatique et les déplacements en cas de catastrophe s'inscrivent dans les domaines suivants sur le changement climatique et les déplacements dus aux catastrophes quatre domaines (voir le diagramme ci-dessous) :
1.	Opérations sur le terrain pour éviter, réduire au minimum et traiter les déplacements internes et transfrontaliers en cas de catastrophe.
2.	Conseil juridique, orientation et développement normatif aux niveaux national, régional et international pour soutenir une meilleure protection des droits des personnes déplacées dans le cadre de catastrophes et du changement climatique.
3.	Cohérence des politiques pour garantir que les questions de catastrophes soient effectivement intégrées dans les autres domaines d'action pertinents.
4.	Recherche et production de connaissances pour combler les lacunes qui sous-tendent ce travail opérationnel et politique
La politique relative aux déplacés internes réaffirme l'engagement du HCR à s'engager de manière décisive et prévisible dans les situations de déplacement interne. Cet engagement fait partie intégrante de nos opérations dans le monde entier et de notre rôle de leader en matière de protection dans les crises humanitaires. La politique exige que les opérations nationales, régionales et mondiales mobilisent et déploient leurs ressources et leurs capacités pour soutenir l'engagement de longue date du HCR à travailler en partenariat avec d'autres pour renforcer la protection et trouver des solutions sûres pour les personnes déplacées à l'intérieur de leur propre pays.

project_name: Renforcement de capacités et réduction des risques des VBG pour les réfugiés hors camp, les PDI et les communautés hôtes de la province du Lac
project_objective:
Depuis 2014, le Lac continue à faire face à des défis sécuritaires importants émaillés de la présence des groupes armés notamment entre les frontières de 4 pays (Tchad, Cameroun, Niger et le Nigeria et qui y occasionnent des déplacements des populations. Cette situation a des conséquences sur le bien-être physique et mental, les conditions de vie et, de manière transversale, à la protection de la population.
Le Lac compte au 30 novembre 2021, 455 252 personnes relevant de la compétence du HCR soit 19 416 Réfugiés, 406 573 personnes déplacés internes et 29 263 retournés tchadiens En décembre 2021, l’Etat Tchadien a adopté la loi d’asile qui traite de l’asile dans sa globalité depuis la réception des réfugiés jusqu’aux solutions durables.
La situation de protection continue de se dégrader dans la province du Lac en raison de l´augmentation des incidents de sécurité liés aux conflits armés (1438 incidents de protection entre janvier et Novembre 2021 et 465 cas de violences basées sur le genre notifiés entre janvier et Aout 2021).
La faiblesse du développement et des investissements dans plusieurs secteurs et les changements climatiques expliquent en partie la persistance des crises humanitaires affectant les conditions de vie des populations.
Dans ce contexte de conflits armés, d’insuffisance d’infrastructures sociales et de dysfonctionnement des structures sanitaires, les violences basées sur le genre y compris les violences sexuelles affectent de manière plus sévère les personnes en situation de déplacement et communauté hôte.
En effet, l´activisme de ces groupes armés et les mesures de sécurité mises en place par le gouvernement tchadien pour lutter contre la violence extrémiste restreignent d´avantage la liberté de mouvement de la population vers des zones d’opportunités. Ceci entraîne l'insécurité alimentaire et par conséquence les cas d´exploitation et d´abus sexuel, la prostitution forcée, les mariages forcés, ainsi que le recours aux moyens de survie néfastes comme le ´´sexe pour survie´´. La rareté des ressources domestiques notamment les bois de chauffe exposent les femmes et les filles à des risques de SGBV qui parcourent des kilomètres pour s’en procurer.
Le projet de renforcement de capacités et réduction des risques des VBG pour les réfugiés hors camp, les PDI et les communautés hôtes de la provinciale du Lac portera sur la prévention, l’atténuation et la réponse aux violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre. Ceci est en droite ligne avec la stratégie du cluster protection donc l’une de six stratégies intégrées du HRP 2022 et conformément à la politique du Comité Permanent Inter-institutions (CPI) sur la protection de l’action humanitaire. 
Le projet, dans sa composante de renforcement de capacités, portera sur les activités de formation, mobilisation communautaire, le renforcement du système communautaire de prévention des VBG et la formation des acteurs étatiques (autorités administratives et judiciaires, l’autorité sécuritaire et le personnel éducatif).

Le projet porte sur l’aspect de l’atténuation des risques d’exposition aux VBG. En effet, il comporte les aspects qui représente les vulnérabilités identifiées. Il s’agit de l’amélioration de l’accès durable aux sources d’énergies vertes, l’autonomisation des femmes et filles, la mise en place de cadres sûrs pour leur permettre d’acquérir des compétences de vie et une autosuffisance conformément à la Politique National Genre.

Lors de la mise en œuvre du projet, le HCR travaillera dans une approche inter-agence et en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires investis dans la lutte contre les VBG (Par ex : CARE international, IRC, InterSOS, etc) en tenant compte des besoins identifiés, de la répartition géographique et des fonds mobilisés. Ainsi, le HCR a besoin des ressources financières pour exercer son mandat de protection international en vue de renforcer ses interventions en matière de lutte contre les VBG.

project_name: Promotion d’espace civique pour les jeunes engagés dans la prévention des conflits et la construction d’une société inclusive et apaisée dans la province du lac Tchad.
project_objective:
Depuis 2015, plusieurs états d’urgence ont été déclarés dans la Province du Lac qui ont menés à la suspension du commerce transfrontalier, qui occupait la majorité des jeunes de la province du Lac. Les communautés locales, et en particulier les jeunes souffrent de l’impact économique des mesures de sécurité, notamment la fermeture des marchés soupçonnés d’être des lieux de commerce des groupes armés, et la fermeture de la frontière nigériane, principal marché économique du Tchad. 
La déscolarisation, le manque d’opportunité, l’absence de structures d’encadrement et d’orientation des jeune déscolarisés et non scolarises couplées du manque de formation qualifiante, l’oisiveté, l’insécurité, l’incapacité d’accès aux ressources augmentent l’exclusion des jeunes. Ces derniers sont en effet dans une situation d’extrême vulnérabilité et une incapacité de répondre aux besoins de base, ce qui les exposent à l’adhésion a ‘idéologie de l’extrémisme voire l’enlèvement par Boko Haram. 
Les jeunes femmes subissent toutes formes de violences dont les violences basées sur le genre et l’enlèvement. La précarité de leurs conditions de vies et l’inégalité de genre encrée dans la culture et les coutumes les rend encore plus vulnérables à l’exploitation et aux abus sexuels. 
De manière générale, le contexte de sous-développement chronique perdure la situation humanitaire et affaibli les capacités de résilience notamment des femmes et des jeunes. Selon le rapport DTM 16 de IOM, 43,5836 personnes (406,573 PDI et 29,263 retournées) sont contraintes au déplacement interne dans la province du Lac au 31 octobre 2021. A ce chiffre s’ajout 19, 416 refugiés (source HCR Baga Sola, 30 novembre 2021). 
Le projet contribuera à la mise en application de la Résolution 2250, qui recommande l’implication des jeunes dans la prévention et la gestion des conflits. Il renforcera la politique du gouvernement tchadien, les lignes directrices de la transition au Tchad et le plan d’action provincial du Lac qui mettent les jeunes du centre du développement communautaire, intimement lié à la paix. Ainsi, il renforcera des capacités de participation des jeunes à la gestion communautaire, le relèvement social économiques, la sensibilisation des communautés sur les questions de protections des droits humains ainsi que la protection et la lutte contre les différentes formes de violences, surtout celles qui affectes le genre féminin et les jeunes personnes ayant de besoins spécifiques comme les handicapes. 
Afin, le projet permettra de créer des conditions de consolidation de la paix, propice à la protection et la recherche de solutions au problème de déplacement forces de populations, avec une analyse des facteurs associés à la radicalisation, la pauvreté et l’oisiveté. 

Le HCR compte apporter son expertise en ressources humaines et logistiques pour la mise en œuvre de son projet et travaillera en partenariat avec l'autorité administrative, sécuritaire et coutumière, la société civile dont les associations des jeunes ainsi que Croix Rouge Tchadienne pour sa réalisation.

project_name: Respuesta a necesidades inmediatas de alojamiento y apoyo a la autosuficiencia y medios de vida de personas desplazadas, en riesgo de desplazamiento y con necesidades de protección internacional en Honduras
project_objective:
Honduras está caracterizada por una situación prolongada de desplazamiento interno a causa de la violencia. Las necesidades persistentes de protección dentro de las comunidades de alto riesgo y la débil gobernanza constituyen retos para brindar una respuesta adecuada a las violaciones de derechos humanos y violencia generalizada,particularmente en entornos urbanos. Sumado al impacto de la violencia, las grandes brechas de inequidad y pobreza, acompañadas de la fragilidad institucional, dificultan abordar los factores de expulsión. Los cambios en políticas migratorias, la inestabilidad en la región, conllevan mayores flujos mixtos y retornados ingresando al territorio.
El impacto de COVID-19 y los huracanes agravaron aún más un ambiente de protección ya precario. La mayoría de las comunidades afectadas coinciden con zonas de alto riesgo de desplazamiento donde ACNUR tiene presencia. La vulnerabilidad y riesgos de las personas de interés ha incrementado, los factores de expulsión siguen generando necesidad de alojamiento temporal, en tanto los medios de vida de las personas afectadas o en riesgo de desplazamiento han sido negativamente impactados o inexistentes por el desplazamiento.
En un contexto de violencia y constantes amenazas contra la integridad y la vida, la asistencia para alojamiento individual es la mejor alternativa para las personas en alto riesgo, a pesar de los altos costos que conlleva. La capacidad de recepción en zonas de frontera es limitada para las necesidades crecientes.
El impacto de COVID-19 y los huracanes sobre la seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida y activos, incrementa los mecanismos de afrontamiento negativo. En el contexto de desplazamiento, ante la ausencia de medios de vida, las condiciones de vulnerabilidad incrementan, así como los riesgos, incluido aquellos asociados con estrategias negativas de supervivencia.
Este proyecto se enmarca en una respuesta integral de protección por parte del ACNUR en Honduras, y responde a las necesidades de las comunidades y población afectada en la etapa inicial de desplazamiento, o al ingreso al territorio, facilitando su acceso a alojamientos temporales seguros y dignos. La dotación de artículos de socorro inmediato en zonas priorizadas busca cubrir necesidades básicas. A su vez, reconociendo que las alternativas de autosuficiencia y medios de vida son una herramienta para mitigar los riesgos enfrentados por la población, el proyecto busca contribuir a la recuperación,fortaleciendo las capacidades comunitarias e individuales, facilitando el acceso a formación y activos con el objetivo de incrementar las oportunidades de acceso a medios de vida seguros, dignos y sostenibles.
Para esto, se ampliarán las capacidades de identificación y respuesta a personas en riesgo con necesidades de alojamiento – enfocándose en aquellas forzadas a desplazarse por motivos de violencia o en flujos mixtos en zonas de frontera -,proporcionando alojamiento de corto plazo. A la vez, se dotará a albergues ubicados en zonas fronterizas para incrementar la capacidad de recepción. Se distribuirán artículos de auxilio inmediato a familias en situación de vulnerabilidad afectadas por eventos naturales en zonas priorizadas, y se entregará kits de protección personal y artículos de higiene a personas de interés.
Se identificarán y fortalecerán las capacidades comunitarias existentes para mejorar la promoción de medios de vida seguros, dignos y sostenibles. Se fortalecerá la oferta de servicios provistos por entidades del gobierno y sociedad civil para que sean más inclusivos. Se realizarán estudios de mercado y consultas a la población afectada. Se identificará y seleccionará hogares de interés para participar en los procesos de formación vocacional, apoyo a emprendimiento o empleabilidad. Para ellos, se elaborarán planes de formación, para el desarrollo de emprendimientos y vinculación al empleo, seguido de monitoreo y acompañamiento durante este proceso.

project_name: Cargo Airlift through the Logistics Cluster, Addis Ababa to Tigray
project_objective:
In November 2020, the outbreak of the Tigray conflict resulted in a dire shortage of vital supplies, leading to a dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in an intense conflict setting. Preliminary humanitarian assessments and consultations with the Government of Ethiopia and relevant humanitarian stakeholders highlighted the limits on accessibility for logistical services. Despite vigorous efforts to overcome these operational constraints, the challenges faced with in-land transport persist and have hindered the delivery of much-needed humanitarian assistance. As of 18 March 2022, no humanitarian convoys have entered Tigray since 14 December 2021 due to significant access constraints along the Semera-Mekelle humanitarian corridor, the last remaining inland corridor to Tigray. While discussions and negotiations for the resumption of convoy movement through the Semera-Mekelle corridor are ongoing, the humanitarian community requires an immediate solution for the delivery of lifesaving cargo given the dire humanitarian situation. 

 

In response to these ongoing challenges and in the face of uncertainties with regards to when the inland access constraints will be eased, the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) and the Logistics Cluster have been supporting the humanitarian community in facilitating airlifts of  life-saving prioritized cargo from Addis Ababa to Tigray. Since January 2022, the Logistics Cluster has facilitated airlifts of approximately 200 metric tons of lifesaving prioritized medical and nutrition cargo on behalf of twelve partners.  

 

As part of this effort, both UNHAS and the Logistics Cluster would like to propose a temporary increase in air transport of life-saving and critical humanitarian cargos for a limited number of rotations from Addis Ababa to Tigray. This will ensure that life-saving cargos reach Tigray as an exceptional measure in an extraordinary circumstance marked by the lack of access into the region. At the time of writing, UNHAS remains one of the only ways to access some remote locations safely in the country, operating in isolated areas where humanitarian assistance is critically needed.

project_name: Joint Emergency Operation (JEOP)
project_objective:
The Joint Emergency Operation (JEOP) is an emergency food assistance program funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA). JEOP targets transitory or acute food insecure households through a participant targeting process led by the Government of Ethiopia’s (GoE) National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC). JEOP complements emergency needs outlined in the GoE’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP). Over the last decade, JEOP has served as a food pipeline for up to 33% of the emergency-affected woredas in five regions and one city administration, flexing to meet evolving need.

Currently targeting over seven million people nationwide, JEOP is one of the largest food operators in Ethiopia, working with the GoE alongside the World Food Program (WFP). JEOP’s principal objective is to ensure that targeted communities in need of emergency food assistance have access to sufficient, appropriate, food in a timely manner. This is done primarily through round-based distributions of commodities to targeted project participants (15kg. wheat, 1.5kg pulses and 0.45kg oil).  Since 2018, JEOP expanded its modalities to include cash transfers in two forms; a) cash in lieu of wheat in line with seasonal availability of grains on local markets, and b) transfers to offset cost of transportation for families living far from final distribution points. Modality decisions are based on market and cash feasibility assessments looking at market conditions, access, preference, risk analysis, cost efficiency and effectiveness, with attention to intra-household and community conflict dynamics.
Led by Catholic Relief Services (CRS), the JEOP consortium includes CARE, Food for the Hungry Ethiopia (FHE), Organization for Rehabilitation and Development in Amhara (ORDA), Relief Society of Tigray (REST), and World Vision Ethiopia (WV). CRS implements through its local Catholic Church partners, the Hararghe Catholic Secretariat (HCS) and Meki Catholic Secretariat (MCS). CRS is responsible for overall consortium management.

In August 2012, USAID/Food for Peace (FFP), now the Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA), approved a two-year award through Cooperative Agreement No. AID-FFP-A-12-00009, initially effective from August 1, 2012 through July 31, 2014. Subsequent modifications extended JEOP through July 2022, the current end date of the program. Meanwhile, CRS is the Apparent Successful Applicant (ASA) for follow on funding for JEOP under another 5-year award and has applied for additional funding under another BHA Emergency mechanism to cover 18 months of the current caseload in Northern Ethiopia Response (implemented in Tigray and Amhara).

As such, from mid-2022, JEOP’s current geographic coverage area will be served by two funding sources: 1) JEOP, operating in Dire Dawa, Oromia, Sidama, and SNNPR (JEOP 2.0) and 2) JEOP-Northern Response (JEOP-NR), operating in Tigray and Amhara. It is anticipated that within two years of the start of the JEOP rebid, the caseload in Amhara and Tigray will have normalized, and these two regions will be enveloped into the multi-year award as before. While each introduces novel interventions and approaches, the foundation of the programs remains largely unchanged. Both will continue to provide in-kind food assistance to vulnerable populations across Ethiopia.

project_name: Emergency Cash Assistance for the Most Vulnerable Palestine Refugees in Gaza
project_objective:
An already impoverished Palestine refugee population in Gaza faces increased vulnerabilities due to on-going blockade with lengthy closures of the border crossings at Erez and Rafah as well as unpredictable commercial crossing at Kerem Shalom and access to the sea. It is further compounded with the loss of income and increase in prices due to the global COVID-19 pandemic with the further economic restrictions that followed, and the recurrent escalation of hostilities. UNRWA continues to provide in-kind food assistance to more than 1 million Palestine refugees in the Gaza Strip, covering a part of daily caloric needs, yet the stagnated economy continues to be a burden for the majority of the refugees. The population has already been facing years of humanitarian crisis, and many people are relying on daily labour and casual work to secure their minimum requirements when and if available. The families with high dependency ratios, including those with children, older persons and headed by females or persons with disability, are particularly at risk, as they are more likely than others to suffer from poverty or other forms of deprivation. Through this project, UNRWA will provide one-off multi-purpose cash assistance of US$40 per individual to more than 180,000 vulnerable and cash-strapped Palestine refugees identified through multi-dimensional vulnerability criteria including female-headed households, households headed by older person or an adolescent, and persons with disability.

The project is directly addressing the HRP Strategic Outcome 3: the ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued.

project_name: Recuperación de los medios de vida agrícolas, la capacidad productiva  y fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de familias vulnerables afectadas por las  Tormentas Tropicales ETA, IOTA e inseguridad alimentaria en 12 municipios de los departamentos de Alta Verapaz e Izabal
project_objective:
Se trabajará en forma conjunta con los otros clústeres,  de esta manera se adopta un enfoque de triple nexo humanitario, complementando acciones de otros sectores. 

Se trabajará  con el 14% de las familias  la metodología de “Estipendio por Acciones”, la cual consiste en  otorgar un estipendio de Q 1,00.00 (US$ 129.00) a cada familia como incentivo por el aporte  mano de obra en el restablecimiento de su unidad productiva. 

El estipendio permite a las familias priorizar sus necesidades y decidir cómo y cuándo gastar el dinero en efectivo.  Proporciona un mejor vínculo entre la respuesta humanitaria y el desarrollo a largo plazo, así como al sistema nacional de protección existente, aumenta el gasto de los hogares en alimentos y  la inversión en insumos y activos;  además  promueve la adopción de mejores prácticas agropecuarias.
Los equipos técnicos del   MAGA y del   proyecto  capacitarán y asistirán técnicamente a las familias.  

Se implementarán prácticas adaptadas al clima para restaurar la capacidad productiva de las familias en su finca (milpa) y en el hogar (traspatio), lo cual les permitirá en corto tiempo disponer de alimentos de origen animal y vegetal para el consumo familiar y venta de pequeños excedentes,  modelos para la cosecha de agua de lluvia y  acciones para la restauración del suelo.

Se rehabilitará la infraestructura productiva protegida (macro túneles, invernaderos, casas malla),  sistemas de riego por goteo y estanques piscícolas, con el objetivo de reactivar y recuperar la producción de hortalizas para el autoconsumo y venta de excedentes.  Se realizarán acciones  para la gestión del conocimiento de las promotorías comunitarias y  equipos de las organizaciones e instituciones socias. 

Se llevará a cabo la incorporación en igualdad de condiciones de las mujeres, en los procesos de recuperación de medios de vida, por medio de capacitaciones para mejorar sus oportunidades de crecimiento y mejora,  fortalecimiento de la autonomía social y económica mediante la implementación de proyectos productivos agrícolas y no agrícolas liderados por mujeres. 

La implementación de las acciones tiene una secuencia o combinación para atender a la misma familia, por ejemplo, una combinación puede ser: recuperación de suelo, sistema de micro riego, cosechador de agua de lluvia; huertos y  gallinas ponedoras. Las combinaciones dependerán de las condiciones de las familias y de la disponibilidad de área en sus parcelas y traspatios.

project_name: Ensuring uninterrupted access to quality Sexual Reproductive Health & Rights (SRHR) for displaced and vulnerable women, girls, youth & adolescents in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: To mitigate the impact of COVID 19 on the health care of Women, Girls, Adolescents, and Youth: This project will increase access to lifesaving basic Sexual & Reproductive Health (SRH) services for vulnerable IDPs, returnees, and host communities in the Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) States. Comprehensive SRHR services including family planning will be provided to women of reproductive age including pregnant women, adolescents’ girls, young people, and men in communities and health facilities observing strict COVID 19 Infection Prevention Protocols (IPC), using appropriate Information Education & Communication (IEC) as well as Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) strategies. The survivors of obstetric fistula complications will also benefit from supported referral and specialized services. Medical equipment, supplies, Reproductive Health (RH) Kits, dignity kits, and other items essential for SRH services will be procured and prepositioned to ensure uninterrupted service amidst COVID 19 restrictions to access and attendant utilization of essential Human Resources for Health. To ensure smooth coordination, advocacy, and leadership of the Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) working group under the health sector is to be strengthened, work with other health partners to channel support to the maternal health program and other specific SRH response; advocate at the health sector level to ensure uninterrupted access to maternal health, and non-diversion of healthcare resources at the expense of pregnant, lactating women and adolescent in dire need of SRH services. The humanitarian crisis in Northeast Nigeria has been ongoing for 12 years has led to the need for essential SRH services. The project aims to ensure the continuation and strengthening of essential SRH services across the BAY States.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de los instrumentos de respuesta a emergencias que afectan los medios de vida de comunidades rurales vulnerables con el enfoque de acciones anticipatorias y el vinculo con sistemas de protección social.
project_objective:

project_name: Ensuring equitable quality curative and preventive nutrition services while addressing root causes of malnutrition in Ikotos, Torit, Magwi and Lopa Lafon Counties in EES as well as selected counties of Lakes State
project_objective:
The main goals of the project are: to increase equitable and dignified access to quality malnutrition-specific curative services for children and women, while enhancing integrated sustainable preventive measures to halt prevalence of acute malnutrition among children and women in Ikotos Count. 
The specific objectives will be; To increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific service delivery for children, adolescents and women in Ikotos county by the end of 2022; To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW affected by acute malnutrition in Ikotos county by the end of 2022; To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information by the end of 2022 and to increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and joint programming targeting vulnerable groups in prior.
 Nutrition service delivery will prioritize provision of comprehensive and timely community management of acute malnutrition at both Nutrition centres at Boma levels and in hard to reach locations without static centres to access service. The project will as well emphasize on promoting breast feeding and optimal feeding practices among children and women through scaling up of MIYCN counselling services. Nutrition for farmers will focus on raising awareness on the importance of producing and consuming specific food items: households will be sensitized and trained on the use of new vegetables and crops that will be selected together with the communities in a participatory process; focus groups discussions will be held with the farmer groups in order to discuss the importance of diversifying the cultivation for nutrition purposes. With the lessons learnt from compounding effect of COVID-19 pandemic to already existing challenges, several revised/new guidelines, and approaches such as family MUAC shall be adhered and implemented in 2022 to ensure continuity of equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services in the context of COVID -19. Given the multi causative contributing factors to malnutrition, the project will ensure existent of operational linkages and joint programming with other relevant sectors such as WASH, health, protection and food security through effectives coordination mechanism that will stimulate integrated approach and dignified access to multi-sectoral basic service which will further reduce prevalence of acute malnutrition and eventually reduce morbidity and mortality among the vulnerable groups (children and women). 
Accountability to affected population (AAP) will be mainstreamed by ensuring that programming of nutrition services approach is community/people centered in such a way that those in needs are fully engaged throughout the program implementation to ensure that the intervention is responsive enough to the arrays of the changing needs. Consideration gender and age variation of the vulnerable groups will be prioritized as well for efficiency of the response more so safety audit will be conducted at every nutrition center to ensure.

project_name: Enhancing food security and livelihoods in Borno and Yobe States, Nigeria
project_objective: The project intends to support vulnerable households with an unconditional cash transfer to help the households meet their immediate basic needs, provision of training on best agronomic practices, and provision of agricultural inputs aimed to support households to improve production. The provision of conditional cash through cash for work initiatives has a dual objective of supporting vulnerable households to generate income to meet immediate basic needs while undertaking activities that aim to rehabilitate, rebuild and restore community assets. Activities that support the conservation of the environment will be promoted through the cash for work. The village savings and loan association and income-generating activities will support households to build resilience, move toward economic recovery, and gradually become self-resilient.

project_name: Protection assistance for conflict affected population in the North West and South West of Cameroon
project_objective: The humanitarian crisis in the Southwest region of Cameroon has exposed the local population to large scale protection risks and human rights violations and impacted vulnerable households’ capacity to meet their emergency food needs. Through this Action, the IRC seeks to improve the protection status of vulnerable people affected by the crisis in North West and South West Cameroon, assisting the most vulnerable people to stay safe, access assistance, recover from violence and claim their rights. The IRC will do this through an integrated program of Protection prevention and response activities to mitigate further protection risks resulting from the use of negative coping mechanisms.
