project_name: Fortalecimiento del acceso a los servicios de salud con calidad y eficiencia en los establecimientos de salud de la población vulnerable en los estados Bolívar, Miranda, Sucre, Táchira y Zulia.
project_objective:
El Estado desde el inicio de la pandemia COVID-19, ha generado estrategias para atender las necesidades de salud de la población, sin embargo, la capacidad de respuesta en materia de salud por parte del Estado ha sido sobrepasada, incluso antes de la pandemia, haciendo que buena parte la acción humanitaria, se enfoque a fortalecer los servicios de salud existentes, con la finalidad de brindar apoyo a grupos vulnerables: mujeres; niñas y niños; personas con discapacidad; personas LGBTIQ+; población indígena; personas en movilidad (afectadas por la falta de acceso a servicios públicos esenciales, falta de medios de vida, la dignidad y la vida), otros que se desplazan entre estados; y, personas retornadas de otros países, motivado a la situación pandemia y/o xenofobia. 
En materia de salud la atención a los derechos sexuales y reproductivos, desde el año 2019, a través del informe presentado por Amnistía Internacional “Mujeres al límite. Derechos Humanos de las mujeres de cara al agravamiento de la emergencia humanitaria compleja en Venezuela” ya se venía alertando sobre la situación y la ausencia de políticas públicas eficaces y eficientes, que garantizaran los derechos sexuales y reproductivos de la población venezolana. A lo dicho, se suma la crisis generalizada por el debilitamiento del sistema de salud público, debido a la falta de inversión y recursos económicos por parte del Estado. Una gran cantidad de centros (centros de diagnóstico integrales, hospitales y ambulatorios), se encuentran en abandono a nivel de infraestructura, no cuentan con insumos y equipos médicos necesarios para brindar atención médica. Es importante sumar la perdida de profesionales de la salud que están migrando, aparejando una notable perdida de capacidades y recursos humanos, por la pandemia. 
Por consiguiente, con la finalidad de fortalecer el acceso a los servicios básicos de la salud, en particular en lo referido a derechos sexuales y reproductivos, a través del presente proyecto abordaran los siguientes ejes de trabajo: 
1.	Fortalecer las capacidades de Profesionales de Salud (PS) y Voluntarios Comunitarios de Salud (VCS) en comunidades focalizadas en:
•	Atención materno infantil, signos de alarma en embarazo y recién nacido.
•	Sensibilización en salud sexual y reproductiva, violencia obstétrica y violencia basada en género, según protocolo ONU-SIDA y UNFPA.
•	Manejo del neonato expuesto a enfermedades de transmisión sexual, VIH/SIDA.
•	Apoyo en Prevención y manejo clínico del COVID-19.
•	Identificación de signos de alarma en la comunidad que puedan ser predictivo de COVID-19 prevención de contagio comunitario
•	Sensibilización e información sobre la identificación, prevención y respuesta a la violencia basada en género con énfasis en signos y señales de alarma, como rutas de atención para la remisión y derivación de casos. Desarrollo de materiales informativos con mensajes claves de prevención de la violencia contra las mujeres por razones de género, con énfasis en la violencia sexual, capacitación de LSS/SUMA de OPS/OMS
2.	Fortalecimiento de la respuesta en salud
•	Identificar casos que ameriten cirugías de baja complejidad o ambulatorias, para derivarlas a los establecimientos de salud donde se pueda solucionar su problema médico quirúrgico.
•	Gestionar la compra de kits para los pacientes que acuden a los establecimientos de salud por parto, cesárea, cirugías de baja complejidad, para evitar demoras por la falta de insumos bajo la modalidad de resguardo en farmacia de hospital o cercana a la institución con jornada de 24 horas de trabajo
3.	Estrategia de respuesta a Derechos Sexuales y reproductivos y VBG
•	Establecer puntos focales con los Voluntarios Comunitarios de Salud, para orientación de la ruta de protección de casos de VBG con énfasis en violencia obstétrica y sexual
•	Identificar casos VBG y remisión a gestoría de casos, para la atención integral
•	Creación de espacios seguros para la atención de sobreviviente de violencia sexual

project_name: Strengthening social cohesion in Syria
project_objective: The program’s overall objective is to strengthen social cohesion amongst conflict affected communities in North Syria and contribute to long-term peace and stability of Syria. Strengthening cohesive communities is vital to supporting the stability that is finally emerging in North Syria, and reinforcing post-conflict economic recovery. The combination of improving inter-communal relationships and reducing resource-based tensions will serve to prevent the escalation of some economic-based disputes into violence – for example between host and IDP communities over livelihood opportunities or social service provision – and reduce the ability of political actors to manipulate ethno-religious divisions and mobilise violence. To this end, and in close collaboration with local and neighborhood councils, Mercy Corps will implement community service projects to support local economic development and address resource-based tensions. Mercy Corps social cohesion approach is grounded on a sound context, conflict and conflict sensitivity analysis that supports the identification of viable entry points for strengthening social cohesion within and between communities on different sides of the conflict divide. Mercy Corps supports community members with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to analyze opportunities and impediments to strengthening social cohesion; and to formulate and implement options for strengthening social cohesion at the community level. Through participatory methodology including community mobilization, dialogue, interest based negotiation and the use of sports and creative arts; Mercy Corps will encourage positive interactions between and among community members from across the conflict divide. Mercy Corps will also support conflicting communities to address drivers of conflict through the joint implementation of projects that address resource based conflict drivers. Mercy Corps community mobilization methodology multi-pronged approach to social cohesion Conflict sensitivity is at the heart of all social cohesion activities. The project will develop a conflict sensitivity strategy, guided by various conflict sensitivity analysis tools including the do no harm matrix and stakeholder analysis matrix, building off the findings of context and conflict analysis in the areas of implementation. Mercy Corps social cohesion project will ensure the meaningful participation of all sections of the community with an emphasis on women and youth (male and female).

project_name: Enhance protection environment through provision of specialized protection and gender-based violence (GBV) response services to internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Ethiopia
project_objective:
Ongoing armed conflict, intercommunal violence and climate change (drought and flood) continue to be the key driver of humanitarian needs in Ethiopia and increased displacements across the country. Specifically, humanitarian situation in Northern Ethiopia remains challenging due to the conflict in regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. In Tigray, 5.2 million people are reported to need urgent humanitarian assistance according to the OCHA Tigray region Humanitarian Update from early September 2021. IOM’s draft Site Assessment (SA) Round 28 identified a total of 4,509,081 internally displaced people (IDPs) displaced across different sites in the country. From this, 2,452,077 are found in Tigray, Amhara and Afar regions. 

Affected populations face longer term protection concerns arising from shocks such as conflict, climate change, and disasters. Systemic, long-standing protection concerns such as gender-based violence (GBV) – including harmful practices, lack of access to specialized services, as well as other basic needs are exacerbated due to conflict or climatic shocks. 

Often in emergencies, women and children with and without disabilities, constitute majority of affected population with heightened risk to different rights abuse including GBV. With limited access to services such as health and MHPSS, food, WASH, shelter, psychosocial support, education and livelihoods coupled with weak social support system, IDPs are living under undignified and distressed conditions. These factors entail increased vulnerability to engage in negative coping mechanisms such as forced marriages, child labour abuse and transactional sex.   Additionally, lack of awareness of the right to assistance and limited coverage of response services, complicated by deep-rooted social norms related to gender make accessing services ever more challenging.
Despite the high number of IDPs, there has been inconsistent humanitarian assistance to the affected population due to limited resource and ongoing security concerns in the regions. Poorly coordinated relocations and returns which fall short of meeting standards also negatively affected the service delivery rendering affected population to secondary displacement and ending up living in collective centres or within host community. 
With the goal of contributing to enhancing protection environment of affected populations through prevention, risk mitigation and response efforts.  Following the Protection Cluster priorities, IOM will target primarily IDPs and returnees affected by conflict and drought through general protection and GBV prevention and response integrating Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) interventions in Amhara, Tigray, Somali, SNNP, Diredawa, Afar and Oromia regions. 
The response and activities will be in line with the three overarching protection objectives in the HRP. 

1.	Mitigate and respond to violence, abuse or neglect and restore capacities: through protection monitoring, individual protection assistance (IPA), including multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) and/or in-kind assistance and community based Mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). 
2.	GBV response and prevention services: including case management, Psychosocial assistance, set-up of women and girls friendly spaces (WGFS) providing safe entry points for women and girls to access GBV services, and skill-building and awareness and knowledge on GBV and Protection issues. 
3.	Strengthening capacities of government counterparts, partners, and IOM staff on Protection and GBV service provision

project_name: Responding to the critical child protection and GBV needs of emergency affected children in crisis (conflict/drought) affected IDP and Host community areas in Metekel and Assosa Zones in BGRS and Guji Zone in Oromia
project_objective:
This project intends to provide comprehensive case management and other psychosocial support services for crisis affected children in Guji Zone of Oromia Region and Metekel and Assosa Zones of BGRS. Liben and Goro Dolla from Guji Zone are the target Woredas selected from Oromia Region. Whereas, PIE targets Dibate, Bulen, Dangur and Mandura from Metekel and Sherkole from Assosa Zones in BGRS respectively. Selection of targeted Woredas was made based on needs on the ground and PIE’s field presence in those areas. 
Through this project PIE aims to reach 15,000 children with essential child protection services such as psychosocial support, awareness raising and case management including alternative care for UASC and family tracing and reunification services. On the other hand, PIE plans to reach 25,000 women, girls, boys and men through the GBV interventions planned as part of this project. In line with the 2021 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and the EHF 2021 second round standard allocation strategy, the project aims to provide psychosocial support and case management services including direct support services such as NFIs for most vulnerable children and dignity kits for adolescent girls as well as referrals for specialized services. Where and when possible, PIE will use cash as a modality to help adolescent girls meet their NFI needs. PIE will draw from its vast experience in using cash as an assistance modality in many project previously. 
PIE will employ close working collaboration with local government partners as a key strategy to materialize project activities and thereby ensuring safe exit and sustainability. Through this project Plan International also aims to engage communities and children as drivers of change and as an essential means to build capacities of these actors. 
This project is designed in consultation with the CP/GBV Sub-clusters at the national level and respective Woreda government offices at local levels. PIE has used the various assessments and field mission reports to inform program design. Additionally, PIE carried out consultations with the respective government partners in each of the locations to identify needs and secure government support.

project_name: Respuesta alimentaria y nutricional a necesidades urgentes de familias vulnerables afectadas por eventos climáticos en el norte de Honduras
project_objective:
Este proyecto tiene como objetivo articular una respuesta humanitaria que contribuya a mejorar las condiciones de seguridad alimentaria y el estado nutricional de 5,640 familias afectadas por los huracanes Eta e Iota, que causaron daños significativos en Honduras en los últimos meses de 2020. Esto se perseguirá a través de tres estrategias principales, a saber: 1) transferencias monetarias multipropósito y no condicionadas: se realizarán transferencias de efectivo, siguiendo criterios de necesidad, y observando estricto respeto de las elecciones y la dignidad de las familias en situación de vulnerabilidad, promoviendo sus capacidades y autonomía para que sean agentes de cambio en su propia recuperación, y apoyando con ello la restauración y sostenibilidad de los medios de vida bajo los enfoques de género, edad y diversidad.; 2) capacitaciones sobre temas nutricionales: se proveerá información y entrenamiento a las familias en condiciones vulnerables para promover cambios de comportamiento y decisiones adecuadas en materia de nutrición y manejo de recursos alimenticios; 3) actividades de fortalecimiento de la gobernanza local: se dinamizarán los sistemas de retroalimentación comunitario, promoviendo la rendición de cuentas a las comunidades afectadas e integrando participantes del gobierno local, cooperantes y población de la comunidad bajo un enfoque de género, edad y diversidad, y apoyando a los grupos comunitarios y gobiernos locales en la adopción, uso efectivo y mantenimiento de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana (SAT).

El proyecto intervendrá en un área sectorial de alta relevancia y urgencia para el país. Como resultado del análisis de Clasificación Integrada de la Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional en Fases (CIF) para Honduras, se ha logrado identificar que el 36% de la población (un aproximado de 3.3 millones de personas) se encuentra en crisis o en emergencia alimentaria, siendo Yoro y Cortés los Departamentos los más afectados.

project_name: Promoción de la resiliencia inclusiva y climáticamente inteligente y la restauración de medios de vida de familias de productores y pescadores afectados por desastres naturales en el norte de Honduras
project_objective:
Este proyecto tiene como propósito promover la resiliencia y seguridad alimentaria de al menos 20 mil productores y pescadores artesanales en los departamentos de Gracias a Dios, Colón, Yoro, Atlántida y Cortes, a través de: i) entrega de paquetes tecnológicos y establecimiento de redes de productores para restablecimiento de parcelas agrícolas climáticamente inteligentes; ii) entrenamiento de productores en agricultura inteligente, manejo y post cosecha de cultivos tradicionales (frijol, maíz, arroz, musáceas y yuca) y no tradicionales (rambután, aguacate, críticos, pimienta, cacao); iii) fortalecimiento económico a cajas rurales y empresas de pescadores constituidas, con el propósito de colocar pequeños financiamientos para la reactivación de actividades productivas.

Estas estrategias incluyen, entre otras actividades, el empoderamiento de las redes de productores y pescadores para generar acuerdos de comercialización; gestión de mejores condiciones en la cadena de suministros; entrenamiento en Sistemas de Alerta Temprana (SAT); rendición de cuentas y habilidades gerenciales; y promoción de la sostenibilidad de los medios de vida con la participación de los gobiernos locales y las estructuras de gobernanza locales.

Se espera con esto contribuir a mitigar los altos niveles de inseguridad alimentaria que afectan al país. Cabe mencionar que, según el Análisis de Clasificación Integrada de la Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional en Fases (CIF) para Honduras, se proyecta que el 31% de la población (aproximadamente 3,3 millones de personas), se encuentran en crisis o en emergencia alimentaria a causa del paso de los fenómenos naturales ETA e IOTA en noviembre de 2020, (siendo la zona norte la más afectada), y la disminución de actividades productivas y comerciales producto de la pandemia del COVID-19. Por otro lado, el Análisis de Necesidades Humanitarias (HNO) estima que las personas con necesidades de seguridad alimentaria y nutricional en Honduras asciende a 3.25 millones. Asimismo, según el plan de respuesta humanitaria (2021), 4 de cada 10 personas viven en pobreza. Las tormentas por sí solas dejaron al menos a 2,8 millones de personas con necesidades urgentes en varios sectores. La proyección de daños al sector pesquero artesanal por el impacto de los huracanes ETA e IOTA fue de al menos 15 millones de lempiras en infraestructura y equipamiento dañado y pérdidas en la producción (GOAL, 2020).

project_name: Prevention, Risk mitigation and integrated Response to Gender based Violence including Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
In line with the UNHCR GBV policy, the Inter-Agency minimum standards for GBV in emergency, the IASC guidelines, the GBV strategic objectives of the HRP  as well as the “Call to Action” road map 2021-2025, the project is designed with the three areas of Prevention, Risk Mitigation and Response to address gender-based violence (GBV). The project aims at strengthening protection of women, men, boys and girls internally displaced and returnees including those with specific needs against exposure to risks of GBV and ensuring that all survivors have adequate and timely access to quality services in Borno and Adamawa states. 
Additionally, the project will address specific issues related to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) involving humanitarian workers, Security actors and community leaders in the camps and host communities.  

In prevention, the project will work to engage all women, men, boys and girls IDPs and returnees to address root causes of GBV such as gender inequality and unequal power dynamics in the community applying community-based approach which entails active participation of community-based structures and innovative approach such as the zero-tolerance village alliance (ZTVA). It is for the purpose to nurture ownership of communities and achieve sustainable localized solutions. Meaningful engagement of men and boys is emphasized throughout, acknowledging their positive power as agent of change toward GBV. Various capacity building will target IDPs and returnees leaders (religious and traditional), peer to peer groups, community volunteers. Raising awareness through mass sensitization campaigns will be conducted in and out of camps on GBV, effective behavior and social changes, sexual exploitation and abuse. 
Risk mitigation is a key component to reduce GBV risks of women, men, boys and girls and promote their safety. The project will promote economic empowerment of women through life skills acquisition as a way to reduce vulnerability and mitigate risks of GBV and Sexual Exploitation and Abuse. Targeted assistance of dignity kits and alternative energy sources (efficient stoves, briquette) will be supported as recommended by the joint NE SAFE assessment. UNHCR priorities the most vulnerable including GBV survivors identified through protection vulnerability screening, protection monitoring and GBV intervention.

For the integrated Response, the project will ensure maintaining quality case management and referral pathways to ensure GBV survivors have safe and meaningful access to safe, timely, confidential and adequate services to immediately address survivors’ needs such as physical safety, health, psychosocial support, legal assistance, material support and economic empowerment in line with the survivor-centred approach. UNHCR manages Women Girls Safe Spaces where women and girls feel physically and emotionally safe, comfortable and able to express themselves and discuss sensitive issues and opportunities for social networking, solidarity-building, confidence-nurturing among fellow community members. The project pays a special attention to women and girls in detention facilities and women and girls previously used or associated with armed group as well as those released or those that have escaped from NSAG abduction. This project will be complemented by the UNHCR “access to justice” project which fight impunity by facilitating survivors’ access to justice for via legal representation, counseling and awareness.

project_name: Respuesta Humanitaria a Grupos Vulnerables Afectados por el Deterioro de sus medios de Vida y la Desnutrición Aguda en Honduras
project_objective:
El proyecto es una respuesta inmediata a las brechas generadas por la convergencia de las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, la sequía experimentada en el primer semestre del 2021, y la pandemia del Covid19 en municipios del sur del corredor seco y del norte de Honduras. Para ello integra de manera complementaria actividades agropecuarias de restauración de medios de vida, y de prevención y promoción de buenas prácticas de alimentación y detección de la malnutrición aguda en grupos vulnerables, especialmente personas discapacitadas, mujeres, niños y niñas.

Las diferentes y concurrentes emergencias humanitarias suscitadas recientemente en Honduras afectaron los medios de vida, la capacidad de recuperación temprana, y la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de muchas familias. Esta afectación se visibilizó de manera aguda en los municipios del corredor seco y del norte de este país. Dentro de estos municipios, grupos especialmente vulnerables como las mujeres y niñas, personas con discapacidad, jóvenes y personas de la tercera edad, en áreas urbanas y rurales enfrentan mayor pobreza, desempleo, carga de trabajo de cuidados no remunerados, y mayor riesgo de tener niveles de desnutrición aguda.

El proyecto tiene como objetivo contribuir a restablecer los medios de vida de las familias afectadas por la secuencia de fenómenos climáticos adversos y el Covid19, además de asegurar la vigilancia, detección temprana, referencia y prevención del deterioro nutricional de grupos vulnerables. Esto, con un enfoque de equidad de género e inclusión de mujeres, jóvenes, personas de la tercera edad, personas con discapacidad, niños y niñas.

Las actividades propuestas por el proyecto están alineadas con el objetivo sectorial 2 del clúster de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional, y con el objetivo sectorial 1 y 2 del clúster de Nutrición.

project_name: Provision of life saving shelter and Non - food items assistance to IDPs, returnees and non- displaced population in Amhara and Afar Region.
project_objective:
The spread of the conflict in Tigray into neighboring regions of Afar and Amhara during 2021, has left millions of people, displaced and non-displaced, in need of assistance and protection in these two regions of Northern Ethiopia. In response to this, UNHCR harmonizes its IDP response with the Cluster system, the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), the Sustainable Development Goals, the Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement (1999) and the Kampala Convention (2009) to support PoCs.
Recognizing that contexts across the region is volatile with unique needs per location, UNHCR Shelter and Non- food item response is planned to address the needs of people in all phases of displacement, with a focus on the emergency phase, care, and maintenance of shelter for people in protracted displacements and supporting sustainable returns and recovery where the context allows. The planned interventions include consideration of shelter preparedness, response, and shelter recovery support to account for both returns and secondary displacement and will be conducted in close coordination with multi-sectoral stakeholders to ensure that approaches are integrated, and that broader needs are addressed. Holding the protection of affected populations at its core: Do no harm incl. accountability, participation and empowerment of affected people, enhancing resilience, coordination, and context-driven responses, principles will be mainstreamed throughout our responses as per the ESNFI cluster strategy.  Through this interventions, including provision of in-kind assistance and cash when feasible, UNHCR planes to reach 80,533 HH (402,664 Individuals) across the Amhara and Afar regions through the below responses.
Emergency Shelters (Communal, family shelters or Emergency Shelter kits) provision Non Food Items and ESNFI provision. For the displaced who have returned to their original homes, support such as Shelter Repair kits either through Cash or In-kind with technical guidance on building better and addressing Housing Land and Property (HLP) will be the focus. Shelter Repair is also planned for displaced populations who are unable to return to their place of origin due to protracted displacement, where government allow to settle in a secondary location. Capacity building of staff, authorities, affected populations and advocacy for those with shelter and household needs is also considered. All the ES/NFIs component will be undertaken in consultation with the IDPs and host communities to ensure it meets their most urgent needs. The IDP hosting communities will also benefit from the responses. As per the cluster guideline 10-15% of the vulnerable host communities hosting IDPs will be targeted. Acknowledging any responses that exclude groups and individuals, increase violence and SGBV risks and increase risk of exploitation, UNHCR will undertake essential actions to reduce risks and mitigate Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) associated with shelter and NFI responses. Awareness-raising sessions will be delivered to ensure that the communities are made aware of the protection risks in shelter and NFI response and how best to mitigate them. UNHCR will continue to use IASC GBV guidelines & related tools for SEA risk assessment and mitigation, including its newly developed GBV policy guidelines, National action plan and Victim centered approach for addressing sexual misconduct to make programmes safe and accessible to all women, girls and other at risk group. Most often persons with disabilities are disproportionately affected by disasters and conflict and they face multi-layered barriers to accessing humanitarian services. As an effort to enhance inclusive humanitarian action principles, UNHCR will provide awareness-raising and training of those at the forefront of service delivery and from the overall target reserving a minimum of 15% of kits (tailor made for disables).

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria en Seguridad alimentaria y Nutrición
project_objective:
El proyecto pretende contribuir a aliviar el sufrimiento humano y dignificar la vida de las personas que han sido afectadas por fenómenos naturales o crisis humanitarias. El objetivo del proyecto es ofrecer asistencia humanitaria en seguridad alimentaria y nutrición a los más vulnerables en los departamentos de Yoro, Cortés, Copán, Intibucá, Francisco Morazán, Santa Bárbara y El Paraíso. En estos siete departamentos, se asistirán 24 Municipios a través transferencia multipropósito, distribución de kits agrícolas para la reactivación de medios de vida, asistencia humanitaria en nutrición en coordinación con la Secretaría de Salud y fortaleciendo las estructuras comunitarias para la vigilancia nutricional y referencia de las niñas y niños en desnutrición aguda y moderada a los centros de salud para su recuperación oportuna. A través del proyecto se capacitarán grupos de cuidadores y cuidadores en preparación de alimentos para mejora nutricional de las familias. Adicionalmente se fortalecerán 41 unidades de salud dotando con equipo y formando a su personal, consultores pediatras apoyarán con su formación y con el manejo de desnutrición. El proyecto es inclusivo y promueve la equidad de género, 69% de la población de los municipios de Intibucá pertenecen al grupo ético lenca. Entre las metas del proyecto figuran:
*Transferencia multipropósito a 20,700 personas
*Distribución de kits agrícolas y asistencia nutricional a 40,000 personas vulnerables,
*24,100 niños y niñas menores de 5 años y 6,300 mujeres embarazadas y lactantes
* 29,700 cuidadores y cuidadoras recibirán formación en preparación de alimentos para diversificar su alimentación y mejorar la nutrición de la familia.
* 82 unidades de salud fortalecidas
*2,460 voluntarios de salud capacitados
En conclusión el proyecto pretende beneficiar a más de 100,000 personas en acciones relacionadas a la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional. Entre los beneficiarios el 52% son mujeres, en el departamento de Intibucá y Yoro se incluirán grupos indígenas, estimando un 69% de lencas en Intibucá y un 4% de varias etnias en Morazán, Yoro. Se estima que un 5% de la población beneficiaria son mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, 2.5% tienen algún tipo de discapacidad, 2% de las niñas y niños tienen desnutrición aguda.

project_name: Strengthening mechanisms that prevent violence against women, men, girls and boys and provide protection services to survivors of gender-based violence, while ensuring specialised GBV services are accessible and vulnerability to GBV is reduced
Fortalecimiento de la SAN y la resiliencia de las comunidades vulnerables, a través de un modelo de Alimentación Escolar saludable proveniente de la Agricultura Familiar local.
project_objective:
La persistencia de la crisis económica y política en Venezuela durante los últimos años ha colocado a una parte importante de su población en situación de extrema precariedad. Las interrupciones de las actividades educativas y la cadena de suministro de alimentos locales debido a la pandemia COVID-19, ha afectado profundamente la oportunidad de la población vulnerable, incluidos niños en edad escolar y familias productoras, de acceder a alimentos esenciales y a insumos productivos que fortalezcan su SAN, respectivamente. 
En este sentido, durante el periodo 2020-2021, la cobertura del Programa de Alimentación Escolar (PAE) ha tenido deficiencia en frecuencia, ingesta nutricional y dieta equilibrada para no menos de 4.5 millones de niños y se estima que alrededor de 1.1 millones corren el riego de abandonar la Escuela. Al mismo tiempo, la disminución continua de la producción local de alimentos se agrava por el limitado acceso a insumos agrícolas esenciales -como semillas con calidad- por parte de los pequeños productores, agravando la inseguridad alimentaria y financiera preexistente en las comunidades.
Por lo anterior expuesto, la presente acción tiene como propósito principal el de mejorar la SAN de niños y niñas en edad escolar, además de los hogares rurales en situación de vulnerabilidad, esto, mediante el desarrollo de modelos de Alimentación Escolar basados en la producción local que FAO y UNICEF han pilotado y validad en cuatro estados del país. Complementariamente, la acción promoverá esquemas comunitarios de producción variada de semillas de forma artesanal, adaptadas climáticamente y que respetan la cultura y saberes locales productivos. 
Bajo este objetivo, se propone el desarrollo de los siguientes componentes:
PRODUCTO 1: Fortalecido el modelo de Alimentación Escolar basado en la producción local de la Agricultura Familiar (AF): A través de rehabilitar y/o mejorar las capacidades productivas de las Escuelas Técnicas Agrícolas (ETA) y Asociación Local de Productores (ALP) incrementando su productividad aplicando prácticas agroecológicas para producción de alimentos, huevos y semillas, además desarrollando acciones de asistencia técnica. Se espera que, con la disponibilidad de una producción local de huevos, hortalizas y frutas, se logre fomentar modelos alimentarios de circuito corto, saludables y sostenibles, en donde los niños y niñas de edad escolar en situación de vulnerabilidad - y de manera indirecta el de familias vulnerables de agricultores de pequeña escala - mejoran el consumo de alimentos diversificados, frescos y nutritivos.
PRODUCTO 2: Mejorado el acceso a semillas con calidad, por parte de los pequeños productores familiares locales; a través de una implementación de un modelo de producción de semillas comunitario, sostenibles y resilientes. En este modelo, las ETA jugarán un rol de motor de producción y difusión de conocimiento y los productores a través de las ALP, serán el factor de escalamiento de la capacidad de producción y accesibilidad de la semillas para los demás productores
Para la implementación del proyecto se han priorizado estados con población indígena y, cuando sea posible, se dará la prioridad de participación a agricultoras y agricultores indígenas y a mujeres líderes de hogar, en los estados Amazonas, Sucre, Monagas, Falcon, Zulia, Delta Amacuro, Bolívar y Apure. La acción espera dar cobertura a alrededor de 13 750 hogares de pequeños productores y productoras, aglutinando alrededor de 450 grupos productivos y/o Bancos de Semillas Comunitarios, que contribuyan a la protección y acumulación de sus medios de vida productivos esenciales y en conjunto con 50 ETAs y 25 escuelas de educación básica y primaria, puedan abastecer complementos alimentarios frescos y sanos para alrededor 27 000 niños y niñas en edad escolar.

project_name: Comprehensive technical support for, and direct delivery of, community engagement and accountability services in Health, Nutrition and Livelihood, and Protection services for Rohingya Refugees and vulnerable host communities in Cox's Bazar.
project_objective:
""The consortium led by IRC with members Concern Worldwide and BBC Media Action (the common service) will deliver an integrated program model to respond to the health, nutrition and protection. IRC will implement health and protection part of the project. It will directly implement protection mainstreaming, GBV response and health activities implemented by IRC partners. 
The program will leverage the expertise of the existing Common Service, led by BBC Media Action, on communication and community engagement support and tools provided to each of the key focus areas of the program. The project will be focusing on providing technical support to the sector/WGs and humanitarian agencies to mainstreaming community engagement and accountability to affected populations (AAP) by build their capacities through training and mentoring as well as producing community facing information product including audio PSA, podcasts, video and graphics contents. 
BBC Media Action will support the establishment and running of listening groups, information desks or other community-facing communication facilities and services by consortium partners. The services will also be available to the government organizations and the wider humanitarian community.  The training and mentoring support will also cover range of diverse aspects with the humanitarian agencies, sector and working groups work on multi-hazards, gender, age and disability components. IRC and Concern Worldwide will form listening group within their existing community groups and mother care groups and facilitate discussion using the podcast that BBC Media Action will produce. Also, CWW will operate their existing information hubs and continue collecting, collating the community feedback data and share with BBC Media Action to produce “What Matters” – the humanitarian feedback bulletin. 
BBC Media Action and CS partners will undertake research and develop knowledge products that help inform project partners about perceptions, concerns and priorities of residents in the camps and host communities. Based on this research, BBC Media Action will produce a wide range of communication tools, specifically developed for Rohingya and host community audiences, in the right language and about literacy limitations - BBC Media Action will also provide in-depth, targeted communication and community engagement activity in specific areas where attitudinal and social norm shifts are crucial to success. Especially in social cohesion and peaceful existence between Rohingya and Host communities, SGBV, MHPSS, there are strong attitudinal barriers to overcome. Addressing these areas will take more than simple, informational ‘messaging’ –long-term, in-depth engagement will be required, using audio or video drama combined with facilitated community discussion and dialogue. project_name: Assistance WASH aux populations affectées par la crise au Burkina Faso régions du Sahel, Centre-Nord, et Nord
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso fait face à une crise sécuritaire sans précédent depuis 2014. Au 30 septembre 2021, les déplacements étaient estimés à 1 407 685 selon les chiffres de la CONASUR. Les régions du Sahel, du Centre-Nord sont les plus touchées (68% du total des déplacés), suivi des régions du Nord et de l’Est. Les mouvements de populations que cette crise entraine génèrent d’importants besoins humanitaires et transforment la dynamique socio-économiques du pays. A cela s’ajoute les aléa inondations et les mesures de protection à prendre contre Covid-19 qui accentuent ces besoins. En WASH, les chiffres provisoires annoncent qu’environ 2 500 000 personnes seront dans le besoin. Ces personnes se retrouvent essentiellement au sein de la communauté, généralement dans des quartiers non lotis où les services sont défaillants. Une partie (17%) se retrouve dans des sites de déplacés temporaires où les services WASH sont encore plus précaires. Le projet a donc pour objectif de répondre aux besoins urgents WASH des populations affectées dans les communautés, les sites, les structures de santé et les écoles, afin de combler les besoins vitaux et limiter leur exposition aux maladies liées à la WASH. De façon spécifique, le projet vise à:
	- Contribuer à l’amélioration de l’accès sécurisé et digne à l’eau potable des populations affectés par la crise
	- Fournir les facilités d’assainissement aux populations à risque sanitaire élevé
	- Promouvoir un changement de comportement en faveur de meilleures pratiques d’hygiène au sein des communautés et des écoles
	- Renforcer les mesures de prévention et de contrôle des infections dans les structures de santé
Le projet sera mis en œuvre avec une forte implication communautaire pour leur participation active aux différents processus et pour la prise en compte de leurs feedbacks qui seront captés à travers un mécanisme dédié mis en place. De même, le projet prendra en compte les piliers de la protection transversale qu’il ressort dans le descriptif des activités à mettre en œuvre.

COVID 19 Vaccination Roll out (70% of the population).
project_objective:
Syria is one of the 92 AMC (Advanced Market Commitment) countries to be supported under the COVAX Facility with COVID-19 vaccines. 
The aim of this project is to provide financial and technical support to cover 70% of the population (14,391,409 population) during 2022 with 2 doses of COVID 19 vaccines. 
The targeted population is over 18 years old with more emphasize on priority categories, The health workforce (including frontline social workers and teachers), older  adults (>55 years) and people with comorbidities as identified in the National Deployment Vacciantion Plan (NDVP are based on the CTAG’s recommendations, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) values framework as well as the COVAX facility fair allocation prioritization roadmap). 
This project will support the operational cost of vaccine roll out in 14 Syrian governorates, including Northeast Syria and part of Northwest Syria GOS controlled areas. Under the current project, 92 hospitals will be used as service delivery points to provide vaccinations, along with 979 primary health care facilities all over the country. In rural areas and camps, 341 mobile teams will be deployed to cover that targeted population.  
Services will be provided by trained hospital teams and routine immunization personnel in mobile teams. This number of facilities and associated teams is preliminary and subject to change based on ongoing microplanning. In total more that 5000 vaccinators will participate in covid vaccination activities during the year. 
Implementation across Northeast Syria will follow the current experiences of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) microplanning through 109 fixed facilities (hospitals and primary healthcare centers) and 94 mobile teams. Formal and informal settlements will be targeted in the same way. Microplanning is covering camps across Northeast Syria. 

For North West Syria NWS, In the absence of the ministry of health, the WHO in partnership with the Syrian immunization group (SIG) and implementing partner supports the COVID-19 vaccination services in NWS. The project will expand vaccination sites and fully support the human resources, operation costs including logistics, transportation and maintaining technical support, supervision, training at the governorate, district, and vaccination site level. Under the guidance of WHO, immunization technical committee will be responsible for the technical aspect of the implementation of COVID-19 vaccination ensuring proper micro-planning, smooth deployment, implementation, and monitoring of COVID-19 vaccination in accordance with national deployment vaccination plan (NDVP) updated strategy. This project will support and sustain the operation cost of 200 COVID-19 vaccination sites.  Each vaccination site consists of four team members including two vaccinators, one data registry, one social mobilizer. During the implementation, different approaches will be applied, such as fixed, outreach, and mobile vaccination sites to reach the most vulnerable populations residing in host communities, camps, and hard-to-reach communities. In addition, the WHO through implementing partner will conduct independent qualitative and quantitative assessment and monitoring of performance, coverage, and quality of campaign-related activities for all targeted communities. This project through trained staff and using of standardized checklist/ questionnaire, will assess COVID-19 pre, intra and post-vaccination campaign including vaccination team, social mobilization performance and beneficiaries’ satisfaction surveys at community level to evaluate the vaccination status during the campaign and identify gaps and areas for improvement.

project_name: Emergency response to urgent WASH needs and flood mitigation prevention for the most vulnerable communities and institutions in the West Bank
project_objective: Ensuring access to improved, safe, equitable, and sustainable WASH services, as well as enhancing preparedness capacity to mitigate and prevent floods, are considered urgent priorities to guarantee the protection, dignity, and resilience of the most vulnerable communities and institutions of the West Bank. The proposed intervention is in line with HRP 2022 Strategic objectives 1, 2, and 3, and it is therefore complementing WASH cluster objectives 1, 2, and 3. The proposed activities were built upon the WASH Cluster eligible interventions for HRP 2022, targeting the most vulnerable communities and institutions according to the WASH 2022 vulnerability mapping and to the Protection Response Plan, an output of WeWorld-GVC Community Protection Approach. The intervention has been coordinated and endorsed by the Palestinian Water Authority. It is in line with the PWA Strategic Plan and compliance with the Water Master Plan for Area C. The intervention complements and another initiative submitted by the West Bank Protection Consortium for the purposes of the HRP 2022. The intervention is also in line with SDG 6 “Ensure access to water and sanitation for all”. WW-GVC, in partnership with MA’AN aims to targets the core vulnerabilities of people in need by: (1) increasing access, availability, quantity, and quality of water at HH and community level, providing safe water by trucking to 34 communities in Area C (4,806 beneficiaries) for all the dry season; connecting 9 communities in Area C (5,927 beneficiaries) trough installation/rehabilitation of water networks, transmission pipelines, and HHs connection; increasing water storage capacity for 37 communities in Area C (4,974 beneficiaries) trough cisterns construction/rehabilitation of cistern at HHs level and through the installation of 1 PE water tank for each HHs benefitting from the water distribution by trucking (595 HHs/tanks) ensuring the quality of the delivered water;  Providing adequate operation and maintenance tools for 1 community in Area C - (2)guarantying a safe and adequate level of sanitation and hygiene services at the household level, through the installation of mobile latrines and construction of HHs sanitation facilities in 5 communities in Area C. (317 beneficiaries) (3) enhancing access to WASH services in institutions, through the provision of safe water by trucking to 6 schools in Area C, for 90 days. Additionally, the schools will be served with adequate and safe PE storage tanks (two for each school) to ensure the quality of the delivered drinking water. (750 beneficiaries),(4) promoting floods mitigation and prevention, by the construction/rehabilitation of stormwater networks and drainage systems in 5 communities in WB (5,770 beneficiaries) (5) Developing awareness products on access restrictions to WASH, to advocate for the right of the most vulnerable Palestinian to receive adequate WASH services. (10 awareness products). The intervention will benefit in total 17,737 direct beneficiaries (4,465 boys, 4,303 girls, 4,266 men, 4,085 women, 276 elders male, 343 elders women, of which 311 PWDs) in 53 communities in the Governorates of Hebron, Bethlehem, Ramallah, Nablus, Qalqilya, Tubas, Jericho, Jenin, mainly in Area C (94%), and Area A/B (6%). Moreover, it is estimated that the awareness products have a capacity of reaching about 2.000.000 viewers/recipients in a year. The intervention will be delivered through different response modalities, primarily cash transfer, when feasible, through WW-GVC Community Implementation methodology, or by services delivery through contracting, and finally in-kind modality. WW-GVC and MA’AN ensure that the proposed interventions will trigger a positive effect on the reduction of the WASH vulnerability, increasing the resilience of the community under threat of forcible transfer in Area C, enhancing the protection, supporting preparedness and response on combating COVID-19 effects.

project_name: Advocating Palestinian WASH rights internationally
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to advocate for Palestinian WASH rights through organizing an advocacy campaign targeting the international community and the main international actors such as the UN, EU parliament, and different embassies/representative offices in Palestine. Through this project, PENGON will work on assessment report about Palestinians limited access to their water resources in the West Bank, and another report for Gaza, these 2 reports will be prepared and discussed within the WASH cluster through different round table discussions in West Bank and Gaza. The report will be submitted to the  Special Rapporteur on the human rights to safe drinking water and sanitation in the UNHRC, and other related human right rapporteurs. in addition to that based on the report PENGON will target the EU parliaments with online negotiations in order to highlight the violations of the WASH rights in West Bank and Gaza, in order to come up with Parliamentary questions that addressed by Members of the European Parliament to other European Union Institutions and bodies in order to take formal actions and declarations.
PENGON will work on advocacy and awareness materials about Israeli measures against WASH sector in Area C including the demolition and confiscation of WASH structures. these materials include Fact sheets, infographics and video infographic. 
  As a continuity of  an advocacy  campaign "" Make Noise for Gaza"" that was launched as Gaza has entered the 15th year of illegal blockade,  PENGON has worked in 2021 in cooperation with the active environmental, legal and human right organizations in Gaza, and other international networks like Friends of Earth International, La via Campensena , so through this project PENGON will advocate and mobilize local, regional and international allies about Israeli restrictions against the flow of WASH material to Gaza.  Different  meeting will also be held among different national and international stakeholders with the aim of bringing the issue of flow of WASH material to Gaza and human rights abuses to the spotlight, to spark discussion and open networking channels among environmental human rights defenders and local and international activists.
  Another part of this project will be developing the capacities of Palestinian institutions in WASH sector in West Bank and Gaza. The capacity building will be  trainings and community engagement for accountability mechanisms and tools that Palestinian institutions in the WASH sector needs to develop this sector and raise their demands and needs.  the  environmental human right defenders to better enable them to defend Palestinian environmental rights through activities and actions at both the national and international levels.

project_name: Reducing Drinking Water Vulnerability In Jordan Valley Communities
project_objective:
As known, the communities of Jordan Valley are subjected to different Environmental and political harsh circumstances. These circumstances vary from the harsh weather including: droughts and high temperatures in summer, floods and freezing in winter, sensitive hot zones in the annexation plan on the political side.

As WASH cluster focal point in the Jordan Valley, PARC has implemented a full need assessment (Sep 2020) in different socioeconomic aspects throughout the Jordan Valley including WASH vulnerability. In Sep2021, PARC conducted a validation for the previous findings and found that the need is still there.

This Project includes a variety of activities and targeted communities aims to reduce the WASH vulnerability related to drinking water in Jordan Valley. These activities including but not limited to: rehabilitation of a 1000m3 drinking water reservoir, construction of two 250m3 drinking water reservoirs, construction of about 6m water carrier pipelines, distribution of 140 PE water tanks of size 5m3 and many other awareness and capacity building activities related to drinking water.

The project is designed to improve the accessibility for the local residents to the WASH facilities through connecting them directly to safe drinking water sources by constructing new water reservoirs, rehabilitating existing reservoirs and constructing new water carrier lines to make the filling points closer and safer. Moreover it is designed to improve their storage capability through providing them with water storage tanks of 5m3 size, these tanks will improve their resilient in resisting the harsh weather and especially in summer season when the water becomes rare and expensive.

The project will target 13 community in the middle area of Jordan Valley, these communities include: Ibziq, Khirbet Yerza, Hammamat Al Maleh, Marj Na'jeh Herders, Al Jiftlik, Isteih, Al Mashrou' Bedouins, Al Nuwei'ma Al Foqa Bedouins, An Nabi Musa, Deir Hajla and Deir al Qilt.

The project will focus on increasing the ability for 140 HHs to store water by providing them with water tanks of 5m3 capacity, these tanks can be used to store extra amount of drinking water and water for the house use during the droughts and the harsh hot weather especially in summer season. These tanks will be built in a heavy duty way with concrete base to ensure the sustainability and the long term use.

The project will also focus on providing more than 200 HHs of Bedouins in different areas with access to safe, sufficient and affordable water source through the construction of 2 drinking water reservoirs and connecting them to safe source of water. In addition, pipelines will be constructed between the water source and the constructed tanks and between the constructed tanks and the near communities to ensure the availability of water. Moreover, pipelines will be constructed close to other communities providing a safe and close filling points reducing the time and cost for transferring water by tanks.

These activities will be followed and implemented along with sessions and workshops increasing the people's awareness regarding saving water and the best practices in consuming, storage, transfer and many activities related to using water on the HH level.

The project is designed in a participatory and flexible way that ensures taking into consideration the points of view of the beneficiaries not only in the need assessment process but also in the implementation of different activities and in closing the project.

With local Residents of more than 12,000, these communities and especially the Bedouins suffer from irregular and expensive water supply. In most cases and especially in summer, they turn to unsafe and expensive water trucking to satisfy their minimum need of water for drinking and house use. These circumstances resulted in using less than 45 liters per capita which is far less than the water vulnerability line set by the WASH cluster which is 70 liters per capita.

project_name: Child Protection response for the most vulnerable and at-risk children and their caregivers in South Sudan
project_objective:
The IRC Child Protection program will continue to provide comprehensive protection response services and create a safe and protective environment for children who are at risk of or have experienced abuse, exploitation, neglect, and violence as a result of recurrent crisis and conflict, assisting them in healing, recovering, and feeling safe again while collaborating with their caregivers and the local government and community-level prevention mechanisms in accordance with the Minimum Standards for CP and national level SOPs, guidelines, and protocols. The IRC CP program will reach 66,201(32,3232M, 33869F) people through an integrated response of static and mobile response approaches in the CP AOR priority locations (severity 3 and 4) of Panyijiar, Mayendit, and Koch Counties in Unity State; Aweil East and Aweil South in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, and Juba IDPs in Rajaf Counties in Central Equatoria State.
The proposed child protection responses are linked with the strategic objectives of the cluster and three domains of the CP AOR for HRP 2022. Case management services will be provided to children who have concerns about their safety. FTR services, alternative care arrangements for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), and protection cash aid will also be provided to meet the basic needs of the children. The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) service will be provided for children and caregivers with psychological distress using a combination of approaches such as Safe Healing and Learning Space (SHLS) and schools for Social and Emotional Learning, Families Make the Difference Curriculum for parenting skills of caregivers, Supporting Adolescents and their Families in Emergencies Curriculum (SAFE) for life skills of adolescents, and IRC’s Brighter Futures Model for malnourished under five years children with protection concerns. Finally, the community-based child protection (CBCP) structures will be established/strengthened to the lower structure of the community, community outreach on CP awareness and COVID-19 prevention messages, and capacity building of the frontline staff and community volunteers.
The CP response will be complementary to the existing IRC’s GBV, general protection, nutrition, health, and livelihood programs to ensure comprehensive care. The existing health and nutrition facilities will serve as screening and awareness-raising spots and IRC will establish CP help desks. IRC’s GBV centers will also serve as a point of referral for rape survivor girls, and the livelihood section will support the cash-based intervention. In addition, the CP team will be part of the integrated mobile team in all locations where IRC is operating.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Support to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will utilize the humanitarian pipe line for crops, vegetables and fisheries kits from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). Where markets are functional market based interventions such as direct purchases and or seed and tool fairs will be sought as informed by respective market assessments. These activities will be complimented by capacity building/training modules in the specific livelihoods so as to improve the targeted farmer production, productivity capacities and improve yields and returns. The fisheries training will enable target beneficiaries utilize their kits in the proper way and also improve their knowledge and skills in fish processing, preservation and marketing. The crops and vegetable production training will be based on the crop production seasonal calendar which includes land preparation, planting weeding, pest and disease management, harvesting, post-harvest management and marketing. Using the training of trainers (ToT) approach, the project will target 7,500 crop/vegetable farmers and 4,500 fisher folk for assorted livelihoods inputs support as well as training and engaging community based extension workers to provide the technical support to these farmers while they replicate the training to the other beneficiaries. The proposed interventions will also train targeted households with trainings on approved agronomic practices, pests and disease control, post-harvest handling and value addition and linkages to markets and other value chain actors In addition, 1,500 HHs will be supported through unconditional/conditional cash transfer programming especially in flood and conflicted affected areas. The action will also target 1250 HHs with small ruminant (goat/sheep) or poultry restocking through livestock voucher modality, 750 women, youth and men will be engaged in VSLAs/IGAs while 450 HHs will be engaged in natural resource management and climate adaptation activities.
To ensure integration the intervention will target nutrition & health centers, schools and mother garden’s locations conveniently with/without of access and proximity of a water source. Additional community gardens will be promoted at locations such as schools, health facilities where they will be jointly tended by students and community volunteers. The FSL interventions will be designed taking into consideration and incorporating mainstreaming of protection, safety, GBV prevention, Prevention of Sexual Abuse & Exploitation and conflict sensitivity analysis.  The project teams will work closely with local authorities to identify persons with disabilities both men and women so that they are supported. This number is not expected to exceed 5% of the 10,500 HH targeted. This ensures participants are selected based on needs alone, a rigorous community-based targeting process with participation and inclusion of vulnerable groups such as female and child headed households, disabled and the elderly.  The proposed project will also take into consideration cross-cutting issues like environmental protection, HIV/AIDS, community-based participatory planning, gender, nutrition will be considered during project implementation.
All agricultural and fisheries activities will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Agriculture in order to ensure that government extension workers benefit from and also contribute to the technical components that will be offered by the project by so doing building capacities that will continue to be utilized after project closure. Community based extension workers such as lead farmers will be trained to continue supporting other farmers during and after project closure.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency Health and Nutrition Services for Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities in the North West Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
Since October 2016, the political conflict and security crisis in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon has led to the displacement of more than 705,000 people internally and over 61,000 people to Nigeria. Conflict related displacement and violence have led to the deterioration of basic services in the North West Region coupled with rising protection, health and nutrition needs among the affected population. In response to this crisis, International Medical Corps proposes to support the Ministry of Health (MoH) in providing integrated health (including mental health) and nutrition services for IDPs as well as host communities affected by conflict in the Mbengwi and Njikwa Health districts. 

Targeted beneficiaries will receive free primary health care, nutrition and mental health services through 4 supported health facilities and at the community level with the support of Ministry of Health (MoH) staff as well as IMC staff to be recruited under the project. Under the health sector, IMC will support the delivery of curative consultations; reproductive health services; the provision of pharmaceuticals, medical supplies, and commodities; training and supervision of health staff and community health workers; community outreach services which include community-based disease surveillance and the integrated community case management of common diseases such as malaria, respiratory tract infections and diarrhea; the strengthening of the referral system between primary and secondary care; and mental health and psychosocial support services. A referral and counter referral system will be set up which will involve the payment of bills for beneficiaries referred for secondary and tertiary care. Under the nutrition sector, IMC will support both the treatment and prevention and malnutrition through support of outpatient treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) in the 4 health facilities; screening in communities and in health facilities; training of health staff and CHWs; and actions focused on improving IYCF practices through social behavior change, including mother support groups and cooking demonstrations. 

The intervention will not create a parallel system but will rather support the existing system which has been weakened as a result of the protracted crisis. The implementation strategy is designed based on findings of a needs assessment conducted by International Medical Corps in seven health districts in the North West and South West regions. The selection of the four health districts in the North West has been motivated by the number of displaced persons, the absence of other partners, as well as other health and nutrition indicators and logistical and security considerations.  
Program Goal: 
To contribute to the improvement of the health and nutrition status of displaced persons and vulnerable communities affected by conflict in the North West region of Cameroon.

Purpose(s):
To contribute to the improvement of the health and nutrition status of displaced persons and vulnerable communities affected by conflict in the North West region of Cameroon through the provision of quality health care and nutrition services including mental health and community-based surveillance of priority diseases.

project_name: Assistance en abris et biens non alimentaire pour les populations vulnérables affectées par la crise au centre du Mali
project_objective:
Reconnaissant le besoin critique d’améliorer l’accès aux abris pour les personnes déplacées, les retournées et les communautés d’accueil, l’Organisation Internationale pour les Migrations (OIM) cherche à garantir l’accès à différents types d’abris pour les populations déplacées à travers le pré-positionnement et la construction d’abris d’urgence conformément aux normes du Cluster Abris/BNA et du manuel de Sphère qui seront adaptés aux besoins et au contexte local pour les populations vulnérables dans les zones à forte concentration de personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et de retournées. L'OIM fournira une assistance en abris d’urgence (500), transitoires (800) et biens non alimentaires (1300) aux déplacés les plus vulnérables, retournées et aux communautés d'accueil, tout en atténuant les risques de protection pour la population locale. L'OIM assurera l'accès aux solutions d'abris d'urgence en nature en achetant 500 tentes pour les populations déplacées affectées identifiées comme prioritaires à la suite des évaluations. Le projet fournira les abris de transition par le biais d'un soutien mixte (en espèces et en nature par la fourniture de matériaux de construction et d'outils) pour la réhabilitation/construction de logements semi-durables des régions de Ségou et Mopti. Le projet cible 7 800 bénéficiaires dans les régions de Ségou et Mopti. L’OIM s’assurera que chaque bénéficiaire d’une assistance en abri puisse également recevoir en même temps un kit BNA.  
En outre, l’OIM assurera l'accès à des Bien Non Alimentaires par la distribution de 1300 kits BNA composés d'articles ménagers (kits de cuisine, kits d'hygiène menstruelle composé de serviettes hygiéniques, sous-vêtements et savon) et de kits covid (200). Grâce à une surveillance continue des déplacements et à une analyse des besoins des populations vulnérables pour informer la communauté humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre permettront que soit fournie une assistance ciblée aux PDI en fonction des besoins identifiés. En outre, les données collectées permettront au Gouvernement du Mali de développer des politiques publiques mieux informées et ciblées pour les populations affectées par le conflit. Les efforts de collecte de données DTM de l'OIM en 2022 iront au-delà de la collecte et de la mise à jour continues des données sur les déplacements pour inclure la mise en œuvre de l'indice de stabilité dans certaines communes de régions ciblées afin de permettre la programmation de solutions durables dans les zones de retour grâce à des informations détaillées et désagrégées. 4 rounds de collecte d’informations sur l’indice de stabilité seront menées. 
Les activités seront alignées sur celles définies dans le Plan de Réponse Humanitaire ainsi que sur les directives des Cluster Abri et BNA et protection en assurant la continuité des interventions en cours pour une meilleure couverture des besoins immédiats et vitaux. Les critères de sélection des bénéficiaires qui tiendront compte des vulnérabilités seront déterminés de manière active avec les communautés et les autorités locales et communiqués de manière transparente aux communautés et aux autres acteurs humanitaires opérant dans la même zone. Toutes ces activités seront menées en étroite collaboration avec la DNDS au niveau régional et avec l'inclusion des communautés afin de renforcer la responsabilité envers la population affectée et de promouvoir l'inclusion des plus vulnérables. L’OIM mettra un accent particulier sur la protection des personnes vulnérables qui sont particulièrement exposées à des risques mettant en péril leur santé et leur sécurité. Ainsi, afin d’éviter tout incident de protection, l’information sur le contenu des kits, la gratuité de l’aide et les critères de sélection sera diffusée à l’ensemble de la communauté. Des mécanismes de gestion des plaintes et de suivi et évaluation seront assurés. Les messages clés seront adaptés à toute la population y compris aux personnes illettrées.
