project_name: Improving Access to WASH Facilities and Services to Rohignya Refugees and Host Community
project_objective:
The project is designed to contribute to a reduction in WASH-related public health risk through improved access for refugees and affected host communities in the area of Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Promotion.  
In 2022, UNHCR will ensure  the operation and  maintainance of 54 water networks in UNHCR-managed camps covering 345,000 refugees. UNHCR and partners will continue maintaining, operating, and upgrading the existing stock of water infrastructure and the development of a large-scale, unified urban-based water system for UNHCR camps along with Teknaf and its host community and will further provide technical support to the sector and DPHE, particularly for the water supply monitoring programme.

UNHCR and partners will continue to support urban scale sustainable sanitation infrastructure, looking to cover all 14 UNHCR camps by end of 2022. Develop and get approval for integrated household latrines and bathing areas to be adopted as the standard in all new transitional shelter designs covering 3,500 households. Increase shared household latrine coverage and bathing area, especially for women and children, and bring coverage rates to UNHCR standards with iron frame bathing areas. Faecal sludge treatment will be increased with a mix of large off-site units and increased use of small-bore sewerage and appropriate cost-effective on-site disposal. UNHCR will ensure a more effective solid waste management systems and infrastructure and further enhance hygiene promotion activities with community engagement and reduce partner support in favour of refugee ownership.

Infrastructure construction and service delivery would mainstream community engagement within the Age, Gender, Diversity (AGD)/ Protection lens for better project outcomes and sustainability ensuring equal access for Rohingya refugee women, men, boys and girls living in camps, and affected host communities to adequate safe drinking water and for domestic purposes as well sanitation and hygiene facilities.

project_name: Assistance d’urgence EAH aux personnes déplacées internes (PDIs) et population affectée par les problématiques et conséquences humanitaires au Niger
project_objective:
Ce projet cible 450 352 personnes dont 216,169 hommes et 234,183 femmes affectées par des crises humanitaires de type mouvements de populations relatifs aux conflits, aux épidémies (COVID-19, choléra, hépatite E, etc.) et aux inondations, à travers la fourniture d’un paquet d'interventions d'urgence en EHA sur les sites d'installation de déplacés, au sein des communautés locales ainsi que dans les écoles, structures de santé et autres lieux publics. Les activités prévues incluent :
•	L’approvisionnement en eau par des mesures d'urgences (water trucking, traitement de l'eau à domicile) et durables dont la réhabilitation/construction des points d'eau l’extension/renforcement de systèmes d'alimentation en eau potable.
•	La fourniture d’infrastructures d’assainissement, notamment la construction de latrines et douches y compris à travers l’approche ATPC en situation d’urgence
•	La promotion de l’hygiène y compris la prévention /riposte contre le choléra et COVID-19 et la distribution de kits d’hygiène y compris du savon, des récipients de collecte, transport et stockage d’eau.   
•	Une meilleure préparation en amont à travers la mise en place de plans de contingences multirisques (inondation, épidémie, mouvement de population, etc) y compris le pré positionnement d’intrants, la signature de partenariats de standby avec des ONG nationales et internationales afin de pouvoir répondre de façon rapide et efficace sur l’ensemble du territoire. 
•	L'implication des services de l'Etat pour l'appui technique qu’ils offrent sera aussi considérée dans la réalisation des activités en vue de l’atteinte des résultats.

project_name: Promouvoir la Formation Professionnelle, l'Accompagnement, la Mise en Réseau et l'Autonomisation Economique des Jeunes Femmes et Hommes au Centre du Mali (DJANTÔ)
project_objective:
Pour répondre au manque d'opportunités et d'intégration des jeunes dans la vie active, le désoeuvrement et le recours à des moyens de survie négatifs, et pour contribuer à la stabilisation et le développement économique et social au Centre du Mali,  le projet vise à promouvoir la formation professionnelle, l'accompagnement, la mise en réseau et l'autonomisation économique des jeunes (femmes et hommes) en milieux urbain et rural au Centre du Mali (régions de Mopti et Ségou).

En ce sens, le projet mettra en oeuvre les activités suivantes:
- Réaliser une étude de marché participative avec les jeunes ciblés afin d'identifier les opportunités économiques et filières porteuses pour l'engagement professionnel des jeunes selon des critères d'offre et de demande, de rentabilité et de durabilité. Cette analyse sera également complétée par une analyse participative sensible au genre, aux conflits et à l'environnement. Ce dernier aspect aura vocation d'amener des réflexions et des discussions sur les effets du changement climatique sur les aspirations professionnelles des jeunes, et les mesures de mitigation pouvant être mises en place et par rapport auxquelles des formations pourront être dispensées dans le cadre du projet sur la base des besoins et des groupes de métiers principaux identifiés.
- Former les jeunes en compétences de base de la vie courante et en techniques de recherche d'emplois (ateliers candidature, sensibilisation aux différentes plateformes d'offres d'emploi, au démarchage etc.)
- Financer la formation professionnelle des jeunes au sein d'entreprises existantes sur des métiers clés, ainsi qu'au sein de centres/instituts de formation professionnelle technique établis
- Faciliter l'accompagnement des jeunes entrepreneurs par le biais d'incubateurs d'entreprises (formations en gestion financière, gestion d'entreprise, marketing, droits et devoirs de l'entrepreneur, législiation et enregistrement des entreprises)
- Fournir un appui financier conditionnel aux jeunes pour la mise en place de leurs projets professionnels
- Mise en réseau des jeunes entre eux pour promouvoir les initiatives de coopératives professionnelles par métier ou inter-métiers, ainsi que le partage de connaissances, d'expériences

Le projet permettra de faciliter l'intégration des jeunes dans la vie active par la mise en place de leurs entreprises ou accéder à des emplois stables, avec un accent particulier sur l'inclusion des jeunes femmes.

project_name: Deme Sira, les chemins de l’aide
project_objective:
Au regard de la rapide détérioration du contexte sécuritaire, de l’augmentation de l’insécurité alimentaire et la dégradation des moyens d’existence, il est apparu nécessaire de faire évoluer les interventions afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des ménages les plus vulnérables. Ainsi, ce projet a été conçu pour répondre aux besoins d’assistance alimentaire des ménages très pauvres vulnérables à l’insécurité alimentaire pendant la période de soudure agricole dans le cercle de Gao et adresser leur vulnérabilité nutritionnelle tout en leur donnant des opportunités de diversifier leur alimentation autour d’activités agricoles à fort potentiel nutritionnel. Le projet intègre une assistance alimentaire saisonnière pour couvrir les besoins de base durant la période de soudure 2021 entre juillet et septembre pour les ménages les plus en insécurité alimentaire. 

L’insécurité sur la zone ne permettant pas de garantir la sécurité des bénéficiaires, des distributions de liquidité pourraient les exposer à des vols, attaques, ou agressions. Les transferts monétaires inconditionnels et restreints ont été identifiés comme le type de réponse le plus approprié pour plusieurs raisons, notamment la liberté pour les bénéficiaires de pouvoir choisir et acheter les denrées en priorisant eux-mêmes leurs besoins. En effet, la responsabilisation des ménages bénéficiaires en faisant leurs propres choix est également un vecteur d’autonomisation dans un processus de graduation vers la sortie de la pauvreté. De plus, les transferts monétaires dans cette zone où, selon le cluster sécurité alimentaire, les marchés sont fonctionnels et approvisionnés permettent également de contribuer à la relance de l’économie locale qui continue de souffrir du conflit. L’injection de liquidité permet de maintenir une offre diversifiée en denrées alimentaires pour les bénéficiaires mais aussi indirectement pour les communautés toutes entières. 
Le coupon électronique est également fait pour limiter les risques auxquels s’exposent les bénéficiaires lorsqu’ils transportent des sommes d’argent importantes et que cela est su dans la zone. De plus, la transition vers un système de coupons électroniques depuis 2019 permet à DRC un déploiement rapide et une efficacité dans la mise en œuvre de l’action à travers ce mécanisme de distribution. 
L’exposition de cette zone à la malnutrition nécessite une action renforcée autour des changements de pratiques nutritionnelles. La diversité alimentaire sera un enjeu majeur de ce projet. Les expériences précédentes ont montré un certain impact des sensibilisations sur les pratiques et donc l’état nutritionnel des personnes à risque de malnutrition pendant la période de soudure. Cependant cet impact s’avère insuffisant faute d’accès pour les ménages à des aliments hautement nutritifs. 
Ainsi, les sensibilisations sur les PFE (Pratiques familiales essentielles), l’Alimentation du Nourrisson et Jeune Enfant (ANJE) incluant l’allaitement maternel exclusif (AME), l’importance de la diversification alimentaire, l’hygiène et qualité de l’eau, etc. seront accompagnées par le renforcement des Groupes de Sécurité Alimentaire et Nutritionnelle (GSAN), travaillant en collaboration avec les groupements de femmes en place. Les GSAN et les groupements de femme seront formés pour sensibiliser les populations à une diversité alimentaire maximale au travers de démonstrations culinaires et de diffusion de messages, sur la base des aliments hautement nutritifs disponibles sur les marchés dans ces zones et les productions des champs écoles. DRC mettra l’accent sur la variété, la qualité et la disponibilité des aliments riches en nutriments lors du choix des commerçants sélectionnés pour les échanges de coupons. En effet, ce projet propose la mise en place des champs-écoles pour permettre aux ménages de maitriser les meilleures pratiques agricoles adaptées aux jardins de case et donc d’avoir accès à des aliments nutritifs et d’être formés à leur production.

project_name: Education support to IDPs and returnees
project_objective:
The Syrian crisis has weakened intensely the capacity of the education system to address basic education needs. According to the Ministry of Education (MoE) over 120,000 teachers required capacity development, an estimated 180,000 educational personnel have left the education system and around 5,722 schools are either damaged or destroyed which has caused an acute need for additional safe learning spaces across the country affecting 2.45 million out of school. The continues spread of COVID-19 has widened the pre-existing education needs and created new gaps. School attendance was interrupted in Syria during 2019/2020 and 2020/2021 academic year, leading to children drop out and a setback in learning.  
The project aims to enhance equitably and quality access to education to crisis affected IDPs, returnees and vulnerable children aged between 5-17 years. UNHCR education intervention includes the rehabilitation of damaged schools in a gender and disability sensitive modes and the provision of non-formal education in community centres. School rehabilitation will focus on areas hosting large number of returnees, as well as priority locations identified by Education Sector. The rehabilitation activities will target moderately damaged classrooms and WASH facilities with gender sensitive and disability friendly approach to safeguard the protection of boys and girls and ensure adequate access to the school premises and WASH facilities. UNHCR pays specific attention to the future adolescents and youth populations that can contribute to resilience and social cohesion in their communities through facilitating their access to education. In line to AGD, AAP and rights-based approach, UNHCR will reach out to children and their parents during project monitoring activities and through focus group discussion seeking feedback including receipt of complaints regarding the project. Resources permit, UNHCR plans to rehabilitate 32 schools, and some 89,000 students will benefit from non-formal education activities in addition to the provision of capacity building training to 3,000 MoE personnel.

project_name: Accelerating Non-Formal Vocational Education for Disadvantaged Youth in Rohingya Refugee and Host Community in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh (Providing Alternative Learning Pathways)
project_objective:
UNESCO has been providing support to the influx of refugees in Cox’s Bazar since 2018. 
As part of the JRP 2022, UNESCO proposes to accelerate non-formal vocational education of youth (aged 19-24) from the camp and the host community in Cox’s Bazar, providing them with alternative learning pathways. Proposed interventions will create educational, social and economic opportunities for marginalized youth and their family members, with a specific focus on women and youth with disabilities, allowing them to respond to economic, cultural, and social challenges which have increased due to the COVID-19 pandemic and recent natural disasters.
Specifically, UNESCO proposes to educate 3,000 youth (50 per cent female) aged 19-24 from the camp and host community through non-formal vocational education in local market demanded areas that enables them to contribute to their self-dependency, support their family members, reduces their vulnerability to risks and increases protection, helps them identify their career path, and contributes to the sustainable development of their communities. 
Specifically, UNESCO proposes to provide 1,500 marginalized youth (50 per cent female) from the camp community of camp 1E, 1W, 2E, 2W, 5, 8E, 8W, 20, 20-extension, 21, 22, 24 in the Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazila (managed by UNICEF and UNHCR) with non-formal vocational educational classes on repairing solar power, plumbing, tailoring/sewing, and English language training through a comprehensive programme (40 hours) will be delivered in Burmese and English in the Rohingya camps and Bangla and English in host community. Career guidance will be provided during and following vocational educational classes which will help learners to find suitable internship, apprenticeship, and job opportunities, identify a career path, and enable them to access guidance regarding their rights and remuneration. 
For the host community, UNESCO proposes non-formal vocational education classes (40 hours) for 1,500 learners (50 per cent female) on food processing, hotel hospitality including English-language training, housekeeping, and mobile phone repairing which will be delivered in Bangla. 

The learning materials (online and offline) for non-formal vocational education will be developed/contextualized in consultation with the Skills Working Group, Youth Working Group, and the Gender Hub in Cox’s Bazar. 
Existing learning facilities operated by UNICEF, UNHCR, and other agencies will be leveraged to carry out in-person classes and training of trainers as appropriate. As part of the non-formal vocational education, each learner will be provided with a certificate and subject-based toolbox that enables her/him to practice their acquired vocational education.
Responding to the significant levels of stress and trauma experienced by marginalized youth from the camp and host community caused by poverty and distress that youth live in, UNESCO proposes to include elements of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) training in its non-formal vocational education classes to provide learners with the help that they need and deserve. 
A showcasing event, organized in Q3/2022, will bring together the different education stakeholders and private sector entities, showcasing good practices and results of the non-formal vocational education programme and acquired skills by learners. In parallel, a career fair will be organized which provides graduates with internship, apprenticeship, and job opportunities in the local labour market. 
In coordination with the District Bureau of Non-formal Education as well as camp authorities, UNESCO proposes to carry out training through blended approaches (in-person and online) leveraging a training of trainer approach that engages local NGOs (e.g. SKUS, MUKTI, PRANTIK, ACLAB, BRAC). Relevant and updated education materials will be developed, contextualized, translated, made accessible and digitalized (online/offline) for each course.

project_name: Protection Safety Nets for People of Concern in the North East
project_objective:
As part of its mandate to provide protection and solutions, UNHCR through the Protection Safety Nets Project will initiate measures through livelihoods programming activities that will provide opportunities for returnees, IDPs and affected populations to recover their livelihoods and, acquire skills and capacities that enable them to engage in profitable income generating activities.  Vulnerable households and individuals are provided a pathway to economic empowerment, recovery and durable solutions. The project aims to ensure that all persons of concern are able to make a safe and sustainable living that meets their basic needs, contributes to their dignity, and provides for the full enjoyment of their rights. The project will promote their resilience, limit negative coping behaviours that heightens protection risk exposures, as well protect the affected population from exploitation and abuse. 
UNHCR will implement activities in support of this project in the following locations:
•	Borno (Ngala, Maiduguri, Jere and Bama)
•	Adamawa (Yola North, Yola South, Mubi North, Mubi South, Michika and Madagali)
•	Yobe (Damaturu and Gujba)
The Project will provide opportunities for Women and Men, Girls and Boys – using the Age Gender and Diversity approach. UNHCR will ensure the achievement of this objective through the following means
I: Enable Access to Agricultural / Livestock / Fisheries Production: Build capacities of vulnerable IDPs, Returnees, and affected populations - through training and support for activities in sustainable agriculture/livestock/fishery production to support economic self-reliance and reintegration. 
II: Facilitate Access to Self-Employment / Businesses: Promote business-oriented community-based cooperative units. Beneficiaries in such cooperatives will be provided necessary training – vocational skills, business management, financial literacy as well as business startup kits to undertake collective production and marketing of the produce. 

The Protection Safety-net measures implemented through livelihoods programming will reduce needs, vulnerabilities, and heightened protection risk exposures - including sexual and gender-based violence risk exposures. It will also contribute to conducive conditions for durable solutions for IDPs and returnees, enhance community resilience and boost the provision of (or access to) sustainable livelihoods.  These actions align with the Strategic Objectives of the 2019 – 2021 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Strategy, the HCT Centrality of Protection Strategy (Nigeria, 2017), and the Strategy on Protection, Return and Recovery for Northeast Nigeria (2017).

project_name: Assistance aux refugiés de la région de Diffa à travers le renforcement de leurs moyens d'existence et leur insertion socioéconomique.
project_objective:
Le projet a pour but d’apporter une assistance pour l’autonomisation économique des réfugiés Nigérians installés dans la région de Diffa et leur intégration dans les organisations de base des communautés d’accueil. Cette assistance se fera à travers:  
 -  Appui aux activités génératrices de revenus des femmes et jeunes : Il est prévu un CASH de 80 000 par personne, en deux tranches (démarrage et renforcement) pour soit initié une activité économique ou développé sa propre activité économique, pour 2000 personnes vulnérables (Femmes et jeunes individuels).  
- Appui à la reconstitution du Cheptel : Distribution des petits ruminants aux ménages des réfugiés (prioritairement pasteurs) qui ont perdu leur cheptel du faite de la crise sécuritaire. L’objectif est de distribuer 4000 petits ruminants au profit de 1000 bénéficiaires à raison d'un kit de 3 femelles et 1 mâle de petits ruminants. Selon les études passées  la majorité des ménages refugiés disposait d’un capital bétail qui joue un rôle important dans l’économie et aussi renforce la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages. Les bénéficiaires seront identifiés parmi les ménages qui ont reçu les intrants agricoles. Des foires aux petits ruminants seront organisées pour permettre aux bénéficiaires de choisir les animaux en présentant leurs coupons PR aux commerçants exposants. 
- Appui en moyens de production à 2000 ménages réfugiés et autochtones qui sont à côté des sites maraichers ou jardins communautaires des commuanautés hôtes. Il s’agit d’une distribution des matériels, semences et engrais pour booster la production agricole en irriguée. Du fait que l’activité touche les deux communautés, l’intégration et l’accès des réfugiés à la terre sera plus facile.  Le Kit comprend pour le maraichage : Matériels agricole (Arrosoirs, une GMP, binette, houe), semences (1 sachet par spéculation et 5 Kg de Maïs), engrais (compost et 1 sac NPK). La vente des produits récoltés leur permettre d’augmenter leur pouvoir d’achat et améliorer la qualité nutritive de leur alimentation.                                                                                                                                                                             - Distribution des semences pluviales aux ménages réfugiés et hôtes des sites d'acueil, 2000 ménages des sites d'accueil seront bénéficiaires dont 60% des réfugiés et 40% des autochtones à raison de 10 Kg de céréales (mil, sorgho) et 5 kg de légumineuse (niébé, arachide). En effet, avec la crise qui perdure, beaucuop de réfugié ont pu avoir accès aux terres de cultures sous forme de prêt aussi bien au niveau du camp de réfugié de Sayam qu'au niveau des sites hors camp.                                                                    - appui en kits de pêches à 300 jeunes réfugiés et en kit de transformation du poisson à 500 femmes et jeunes hommes au bénéfice des pêcheurs issus des réfugiés, IDP et population hôtes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      - 9 champs écoles pastoraux seront animées 3 en culture pluviales, 3 en cultures irriguées et 3 sur les élevages des kits caprins.

project_name: Provision of camp coordination and camp management  support for IDPs in  Baidoa south west Somalia
project_objective:
Given the lack of options for durable solutions and continued conflict in the country which limits the ability to return, it is foreseen that populations will continue to need CCCM services beyond 2022. It is anticipated that increased conflict, frequent climatic shocks and the continuation of the triple threat will lead to further displacements which will strain existing sites and lead to the formation of new sites.

The organization  will implement CCCM project in 42  IDP sites in Baidao districts of  Sout west region of somalia. Approximately 42,000 IDPs (7000 households) will benefit from this proposed intervention, in addition to the community working in these sites including local authorities, clusters, and other NGOs. These numbers might vary due to external factors, which might attract more IDPs, excessive flooding, or conflict with the landowners or the authorities, which may cause IDPs to flee to other areas. 
Gender will be mainstreamed into the project through the specific consideration of the different needs of women, men, boys, and girls during the design of activities. The project will ensure that all participants have equal access to resources and training. Monitoring and evaluation will be based on gender, age, and diversity dis-segregated data. IRS will implement this intervention in  Baidao district of south west somalia targeting 7000 HHS. Baidoa District is one of the IDP major hubs in Bay region that hosts the largest number of IDPs. Throughout the project, the needs of women, girls, men, and boys of all ages will be addressed throughout the planning, implementation and monitoring, and evaluation of the activities. Through regular site monitoring, needs and gaps will be reported and shared with partners and all stakeholders. Particular attention regarding needs will be paid to women and girls who also have to contend with GBV and protection concerns within camp settings. Through this project, IRS will also address the current and newly identified needs by setting up camp coordination structures at the national and, where necessary, regional or district levels, facilitating and supporting the establishment of effective coordination and management in IDP sites while respecting national context and authorities. Conflict, drought, COVID-19, and flooding are some of the main shocks that drive displacement and largely effecting the IDPs

Similarly, to improve the quality of health service delivery, nursing and medical staff will be trained on malaria and other VBD differential diagnosis and case management. project_name: Critical CP and GBV prevention and support services in Bekaa and North Lebanon
project_objective:
The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is appealing for support to implement CP and GBV prevention and response programming targeting vulnerable Lebanese households (HHs) in the Bekaa and North Lebanon. The rapid and devastating deterioration of the Lebanese economy since 2020 has both impacted the value of the Lebanese currency and the already struggling labour market. More than ever before the host community struggled to meet their basic needs. With a lack of access to employment and income generation activities, vulnerable Lebanese HHs have become increasingly been becoming more reliant on humanitarian assistance, at levels previously unwitnessed by DRC during the response. The inability of HHs to meet their daily needs has also had a devastating impact on child labour, with more children and younger children engaging in daily work, a negative coping mechanism that had previously been most witnessed more with refugees is now becoming more evident within the Lebanese community. The threat of eviction with more HHs living under an eviction order, and families further relying on debt to avoid eviction. During implementation of case management in 2021 DRC witnessed rates of Lebanese children requiring and intervention double compared to the previous year, indicating that an increase in specialised attention to child protection prevention and response must be delivered in a tailored fashion to these communities to ensure that Lebanese children have the right to grow in safety.
The current events in Lebanon have also had a devastating effect on rates of GBV for women and girls. An impact survey into the effects of COVID-19 and GBV rates and perceptions on refugee women and girls found that an overall decrease in reporting, down 8%, indicating during periods of lockdown it was difficult for survivors to access support. At the same time incidents of domestic violence and intimate partner violence have been on the rise since COVID-19 and the implementation of lockdown measures. Data collected through the GBVIMS highlights this trend, with 78% of incidents perpetrated by an intimate partner.
DRC will provide urgent protection services in governorates where the greatest numbers of vulnerable Lebanese reside. This will be achieved through the implementation of an integrated package of protection activities. DRC will target individuals at risk or survivors of GBV, with a focus on women at risk of violence and abuse, and adolescent girls at risk of early marriage as the most prevalent protection concerns observed, and for whom individual capacity to overcome without intervention is extremely limited, and high risk. Adolescents survivors will also be identified through FPSS. For emotional support groups (ESG), survivors engaging in case management will be automatically advised about the sessions. Other women in the communities will also be considered eligible depending on dynamics and risk factors within the communities. DRC will target children at risk or victims of abuse, neglect, exploitation or violence with a specific focus on children engaged in WFCL and exposed to violence in the home. Children will be identified through internal and external direct referrals through geographic coordination with other CP actors, through FPSS sessions targeting children and adolescents and CBPSS targeting children and caregiver more broadly, with a particular focus on reducing child labor and addressing harmful gender norms. Legal assistance will be embedded within the CP and GBV process.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response to Conflict Affected People in Somali Region
project_objective:
Somali Region continues to host one of the largest IDP populations in the country, with many who have faced multiple waves of displacement or remain in protracted displacement. Throughout 2021, conflict reignited along the Somali-Afar and the Somali-Oromia regional borders, resulting in new waves of displacement, largely along ethnic lines. According to DTM round 27, there are an estimated 871,176 IDPs (142,671 households) identified in the Somali region across 427 sites, where conflict is the main reason for displacement with an estimated number of 506,089 IDPs (58.1%). Round 27 saw an increase of 36,453 IDPs from round 26.  Despite the emergency response efforts in the target region, there exists an increased need to continue with a sizeable WASH to ensure that minimum lifesaving humanitarian standards are maintained for the affected population.

Ensuring enhanced and safe WASH services to the affected population remains one of the main priorities for the WASH  Cluster strategy as well as  HRP 2022. The locations and activities considered for this WASH intervention are identified in the HRP 2022 prioritization list to address the immediate and life-saving needs of conflict-affected communities in line with the WASH cluster’s priority activities. The action will be WASH services and carried out in line with cluster objectives CLWSH/CO1 (Deliver conflict-sensitive essential life-saving WASH services to affected people), and CLWSH/CO3 (To enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Ethiopia through early recovery and resilience interventions).

This project is submitted to address the immediate and life-saving needs of crisis-affected communities in line with the cluster's priority activities. The project aims to enhance the protection, health, and well-being of the conflict and conflict-induced IDPs and affected host communities and will be focusing on increasing their ability to access safe water supply, improved hygiene and sanitation practices in a right based manner through context-specific approaches that take into consideration the limited access for WASH services.

This project will improve the WASH situations of conflict IDPs in the Somali region. This project will directly reach 43,765 IDPs and non-displaced people aiming at increasing the accessibility of the WASH services for IDPs in general and the most vulnerable, including women, girls, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities in particular. DRC is targeting affected areas where the highest needs for WASH exist and where the risk of disease outbreaks is likely to be significant due to lack of basic services. Through the proposed lifesaving and durable WASH activities, DRC will contribute to the risk mitigation of disease outbreaks due to critical water shortage, limited sanitation, hygiene facilities, lack of essential WASH NFIs as well as physical safety and GBV.

The project will ensure the active participation of the targeted beneficiaries and stakeholders throughout the project cycle. Implementation of WASH activities will be coordinated together with the beneficiaries particularly women participating in decision making and the intervention will increase access to women., children, and other vulnerable groups in particular. Protection and safety concerns will be given priority and considered providing safe and easy access to the facilities by women and children as well as disabled people.

The project strategy considers the needs and concerns of all vulnerable groups by preventing and mitigating protection risks. Protection concerns will be reflected in the assessment, design, implementation, and monitoring, of WASH programs. As a result, DRC will take measures to ensure that WASH approaches will promote and respect the rights and dignity of women, boys, and girls.

project_name: Upscaling Child Protection in Emergencies interventions in Eastern Equatoria and Jonglei States in South Sudan
project_objective:
Following the Humanitarian Needs Assessments and joint other crisis and location specific assessments conducted in the 2021/2022, 2.7 million people in South Sudan are still in need of humanitarian assistance with Kapoeta South, Akobo and Bor South rating with severe and high-risk child protection concerns; child labor, forced early marriage, unaccompanied and separated children, and distress are some of the issues that have also been exacerbated by the multiple crises of floods and protracted displacement that comes with it, food insecurity and inter-communal violence/conflict which put children at risks of abuse, violence and exploitation; the HNO emphasizes the growing child protection concerns with current services not able to cover the gap. In Kapoeta South for instance, there is less coverage of child protection agencies with a high levels of child marriage and child labor attributed to their cattle-keeping lifestyle and passion for livestock. Scenarios in Akobo which is complex after the floods in 2021 and inter-communal conflict, cattle-raiding, abductions and protracted forced displacements causing distress among children and their families.
A comprehensive Child-focused, community-based Child Protection project targeting these three less-served counties; Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatoria and Akobo (East and West) and Bor South in Jonglei states is quite imperative. 
The project will reach 35,000 individuals including persons with disabilities, with standard child protection interventions implemented through needs and evidence-based strategies of non-focused and focused level - 1 MHPSS activities for children and their families in a structured program; The Healing and Education through the Arts (HEART) program, is an arts-based approach to providing psychosocial support for children using expressive arts to help children – in schools, child friendly spaces, youth centers and other structured settings, individual support to extremely vulnerable children and children survivors of abuse, neglect and exploitation through comprehensive child protection case management to, strengthening community-based and community-led child protection systems by establishing and strengthening CBCPNs (Community-Based Child Protection Networks), mass awareness-raising on pertinent child protection concerns and services, community dialogues and establishment of child help desks for monitoring and reporting key child protection concerns as well as information-sharing, as prevention interventions against abuse, neglect and exploitation of crises-affected or extremely vulnerable children and their families in the target locations.  The project will also strive at improving quality of child protection services through capacity building of front-line staff from both child protection on CPIE concepts comprehensive case management, Alternative care for UASC, CPIMS+, roll-out of minimum standards for child protection in humanitarian action (CPMS 2019), centrality of protection and MHPSS/PFA as well as other other sector staff to enhance their participation and in child protection creating opportunities for integration for a more holistic response to children and their families affected by multi-faceted crises
Cognizant of coordination which is the first standard of minimum standards of child protection in humanitarian contexts, the project will support the gaps of child protection coordination at the state level through strengthening effectiveness for activities of the child protection working groups and CPAoR-specific action plans. The project will support advocacy initiatives through the members of CMTF, CPWG and UASC WG. Learning will be incorporated through a case management satisfactory survey to inform our case management system in South Sudan and re-contextualize the standard operation procedures. An advocacy initiative to trigger government accountability will be implemented.

project_name: Provision of PHC services and support to the public health system
project_objective:
IMC propose to continue implementing a mixed approach of direct service provision through its static (currently 3) and mobile facilities (currently 6), providing PHC services in various areas of Damascus, Rural Damascus and Dara’a governorates. Core funding for these facilities is secured until the end of the first and the second quarter of 2022 and IMC will aim at renewing existing funds for at least additional 12 months. The facilities provide comprehensive PHC package with preventive and curative services including reproductive and child health care, management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, health education and awareness individual and group sessions (including on topics related to COVID 19). All children under 5 and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) are screened for malnutrition and referred to the closest public facility for treatment. Medications are provided free of charge based on doctors prescriptions and IMC EML (Essential Medicines List). IMC doctors are trained on mhGAP and work closely to case managers who are also embedded in the health facilities. IMC also support referrals to higher level of care (consultations, surgeries, specialized diagnostic services) through private service providers, including specialists and hospitals, for patients identified as in need of further examination and/or surgeries, to reduce risk of deterioration of their health status as well as mortality and disability. Always through referrals, IMC supports provision of hearing aids and speech therapy as needed, mostly to children with hearing impairments. In addition to the above, two static clinics in Damascus and Jaramana, provide ENT and ophthalmology services, as well as basic laboratory tests. Furthermore, through these clinics IMC distribute mobility/disability consumables (diapers, catheters, colostomy bags) and items such as wheelchairs, crutches, walkers, air mattresses and toilet seats. All facilities are screening patients for COVID 19 symptoms and refer them to the closest designated facility based on the established protocol. 
Although statistics vary among locations, the majority of the beneficiaries seeking services at IMC facilities are women (approximately 60-70%) while for age categories below 18 years the sex disaggregation is more balanced. This can be attributed to the availability of services addressed to women (gynecology) as well as cultural and contextual considerations. Furthermore, approximately 30% of IMC patients are over 50 years old and 2 to 3% are PWD. As such and although this percentage varies across the locations as above mentioned, IMC facilities provide services to all categories of the population, including the most vulnerable categories such as older persons, women, children and PLW. 
In parallel with direct service provision, IMC will continue work towards increased resilience and strengthening of the public health system through enhanced collaboration and support to the PHC facilities managed by the Ministry of Health (MoH). IMC is currently targeting various locations in Hama governorate, however based on gaps, needs and capacities, might be expanding to other governorates as well. Support includes provision of supplies, equipment, furniture and capacity building, aimed at increasing both quality and type of healthcare services provided by the targeted facilities. Monitoring activities are conducted both by health technical staff, to ensure adherence to standards and protocols, and IMC MEAL team. MEAL related monitoring include, among others, visits to the facilities, patient satisfaction surveys, PDM and surveys for beneficiaries supported with referrals, shipment verifications.

project_name: Appui au gouvernement du Burkina Faso pour répondre aux besoins en abris et articles ménagers essentiels des personnes déplacées et hôtes dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord et de l’Est
project_objective:
Ce projet vient en appui au gouvernement du Burkina Faso pour répondre aux besoins en abris et AME des personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et hôtes dans les régions du Nord, Centre-Nord et de l’Est. 
Le présent projet vise non seulement un accès à un logement sécurisé, un accompagnement des bénéficiaires à la formalisation de la sécurité foncière auprès des autorités, mais aussi, l’appropriation des actions du projet par les communautés elles-mêmes. La promotion de l’égalité de genre sera commune à toutes les activités mises en œuvre par le projet. Les zones ciblées étant particulièrement vulnérables au changement climatique, l’ensemble des interventions envisagées sera adapté au contexte local pour les ménages affectés par la crise et prendra en considération leur impact sur l’environnement (utilisation de matériaux locaux, adaptation des constructions aux conditions climatiques, etc.). 
Ce projet cible des personnes affectées par le déplacement ainsi que des nouveaux déplacés qui surviendront pendant la période de couverture., les PDI sans abris adéquats sont les cibles prioritaires mais les plus vulnérables au sein de la communauté hôte seront également touchés en vue de renforcer les liens communautaires. ACTED travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe de protection pour appuyer le ciblage pour la distribution des abris et consultera également les personnes affectées dont les représentants des PDI ainsi que les communautés locales, les structures de prise de décision dont les mairies et la CODESUR des communes et les différents acteurs d'influence dans le but d’harmoniser les critères de sélection des bénéficiaires direct de ce projet.
Le ciblage des bénéficiaires se fera en fonction des critères de vulnérabilité socio-économiques et des conditions de logement des ménages selon les recommandations du Cluster Abris. Pour les bénéficiaires ciblés dans les centres urbains ou péri-urbain disposant des parcelles, ACTED les accompagnera dans la construction de leurs abris. Dans le cas où les bénéficiaires ne disposent pas de parcelles, un contrat d’engagement tripartite sera signé avec le ménage hôte pour avoir toutes les autorisations nécessaires pour construire dans la parcelle du propriétaire; Un délai de non expulsion du bénéficiaire sera spécifié dans le contrat pour la protection du bénéficiaire. ACTED dans sa stratégie abris, adopte les types d’abris semi-durables de 24.5m² et de 18m² correspondant respectivement à des ménages de 7 et de 5 personnes. Ces abris seront construits avec la modalité mixte (modalité combinant le transfert de cash conditionnel et la distribution en nature de certains matériaux de construction non disponible localement) et la construction de l’abri répondra au standard technique et de protection quant à l’accès au Logements, Terres et Biens. Cette méthode doit permettre de maximiser les chances que l’entièreté de l’argent et/ou les matériaux distribués aux ménages bénéficiaires soit dédié à la construction de l’abri.

Les modèles d’abris proposés sont respectueux de l’environnement. En effet, issue du sol, la brique en banco est non polluante, imputrescible et se recycle indéfiniment. Une maison en terre s’adapte ainsi parfaitement à son environnement naturel et crée un micro climat à l’intérieur pour ses occupants. Pour limiter l’impact du projet sur l’environnement, ACTED veillera à ce que les sites de d’extraction des briques ne soient pas à proximité des habitations pour non seulement éviter les accidents mais aussi éviter la stagnation des eaux de pluies, vecteur de maladies.
La planification détaillée des interventions et le suivi du projet se fera en coordination avec les autorités locales (action sociale, mairies). Dès au départ, une présentation du projet sera faite aux autorités locales et services déconcentrés, incluant les cibles, les objectifs et les approches qui seront utilisées.

project_name: WASH resilience oriented interventions improving access to water, and enhancing awareness on hygiene for the most vulnerable population.
project_objective:
WWGVC plans to intervene in Aleppo, Deir-Ez-Zor, and Ar-Raqqa governorates restoring community
services in newly accessible and underserved areas. In line with the WASH sector's objectives, the interventions identified focus on resuming the supply of sufficient and safe water to 85,689 people in need in 2022 and 45,500 in 2023, reducing the impacts of the financial burden of purchasing trucked water, and the health concerns associated with unmonitored water sources for domestic use. WWGVC will coordinate closely with the local water authority of each governorate to assess the infrastructure damage and the possibility of rehabilitation and resuming operations with the funds to be secured. Detailed assessments will also be conducted prior to the prioritization and selection of locations. The assessment will develop a baseline regarding the status of WASH infrastructure and services, the severity of its impact, and the presence of vulnerable individuals that will inform the prioritization decision at the community level.
Water systems in the targeted areas are either out of service or partially functioning with a limited capacity of regular maintenance. The improvement in service provision is achieved by the light rehabilitation of pumping stations, provision and repair of electromechanical equipment for pumping stations, rehabilitation of boreholes, and decentralized water networks rehabilitation and small-scale extensions to ensure water delivery to the affected population. These activities will ensure water systems are operational in all the targeted communities of the project, delivering sufficient water to the households connected to the water networks. In parallel, WWGVC will work closely with the Water Boards of each governorate to build their capacity on water systems management and water safety planning, including training of technical staff and pumping stations operators, along with the provision of equipment, tools, and consumables for an improved and more efficient maintenance of water systems and monitoring of water quality. The above hard component activities will be integrated with awareness campaigns on hygiene promotion (HP) and Covid-19 preparedness and prevention, and distribution of WASH NFIs for the most vulnerable communities. In 2023, in addition to the regular programming mentioned above, WWGVC will also direct focus on solar water pumping and rehabilitation of wastewater networks infrastructure.
The project activities are targeting needs that are similar across all the subdistricts targetted in all three governorates. These include, but not limited to: 1. Damaged pumping stations and catchment areas of water sources prohibiting collection and delivery of water through the networks. 2. Damaged water networks reducing the water system's efficiency in delivering the needed amount of water collected. 3. Low efficiency of water systems management by the water authorities. 4. Inability to afford hygiene items to the most vulnerable populations increasing threat to C-19 and water-born diseases. 5. Reduced awareness and care towards proper hygiene practices caused by the worsening living conditions.

project_name: Ensuring Access to Quality and Inclusive Education and Protection Services to Vulnerable Students
project_objective:
The education sector in Palestine has been facing challenges and obstacles as a result of prolonged education-related violations and vulnerabilities, including attacks on schools, movement restrictions, insufficient and/or inadequate, safe school infrastructure, and poverty. Covid-19 and the escalation on Gaza have only exacerbated the suffering of the education system in Palestine. According to Education Humanitarian Needs Overview, 31% in Gaza and 14% in the WB of the HHs interviewed as part of the MSNA reported having trouble meeting essential education needs.

In this context, this proposal aims to improve students’ academic performance and remediate their learning loss caused by the political instability and implications of COVID-19. This goal shall be achieved through the provision of ToT training for 120 Educational Supervisors and equip them with skills to mitigate learning loss. Following the ToT training, the Educational Supervisor shall provide training for 3000 teachers from 75 schools on the same topic (this is based on the result of an assessment on learning loss done by MoE) with the support of UNESCO and the implementing partner. In addition, this project aims at building the capacity of 500 teachers (males and females) on distance learning with a focus on digital skills including virtual classes. Also, 500 teachers will be provided with specific equipment like microphones and mobile sticks to enhance the quality of online teaching. Moreover, 150 laptops will be distributed among schools based on the needs to support the most vulnerable schools, teachers, and students. These laptops will also be used to support teachers when conducting online classes during crisis times. Most vulnerable schools have a lack of ICT equipment which is considered as one of the main challenges and obstacles hindering the provision of quality online education. 
Moreover, considering the psychological impact of COVID-19 and the political instability on teachers, students, and their parents, the project will provide psychosocial support through the implementation of recreational activities including theatre, storytelling, dance, and music.  These recreational activities shall be conducted through the implementation of teachers' and students’ initiatives to improve the overall psychosocial wellbeing and learning loss of students. 
To support educational counselors during the crisis, 50 of them will receive training on digital and transversal to enable them to provide psychosocial services to teachers, students, and parents during the crisis in 50 schools. This training will provide them with technology skills so they can cope with the modern culture and enhance the service provided for students. Educational counsellors are also in need of educational and counseling materials, in addition to laptops so they can provide the essential psychosocial services for students during the crisis and other times. Psychosocial services target also parents as they were badly affected by the prolonged closure of schools and the crisis in Gaza.
The most affected students during schools' closures and other crises are vulnerable students. Therefore, the project shall focus on providing around 460 students with specific learning needs with tablets and providing 100 students with disabilities with assistive devices. To improve distance learning through this project, 40 resource room teachers will be equipped with skills in the development of adapted learning materials for online classes. Other activities shall be implemented to raise awareness on the right to inclusive and quality education for students with disabilities and students with specific learning needs. 
Within the protection context, all beneficiaries will be educated on PSEA and their right to report any abuse. Complaint mechanisms should be accessible to everyone and data will be confidential.

project_name: Rehabilitation of housing of non-refugees affected by May 2021 Gaza Crisis
project_objective:
The Project’s main objective is to improve the living conditions of the families affected by the hostilities on the Gaza Strip during the May 2021 crisis. This project will support 510 non-refugee families whose houses have been damaged by providing support to rehabilitate their housing. The housing rehabilitation intervention, delivered through self-help modality, will allow for 3000 people including Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) and women-headed households to enable them to restore some degree of normality to their lives. 

The beneficiary selection process will be informed by UNDP’s infrastructure damage assessment and conducted in coordination with UNRWA, Shelter Cluster and with the Ministry of Public Works and Housing, in order to ensure transparency and complementarity of efforts to reach those most in need and  to leave no one behind. The vulnerability of families will be taken into consideration while setting priorities, where priority will be given to women-headed households and families with disabled persons and crowded houses to mitigate COVID19 risk. 

The intervention is also urgently needed in light of the dire socio-economic situation in the Gaza Strip, particularly as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. The people living in the Gaza Strip have become more vulnerable to shocks and unable to meet their essential needs, and many have had to cope with the displacement. 

Building on the experience of previous conflicts, UNDP successfully developed Standard Operating Procedures, which include implementation through self-help modality and fund disbursement to beneficiaries utilizing local banks.

project_name: Gender Responsive and multi-sectoral services for conflict affected women and girls in the oPt
project_objective:
The overall goal of the project is to improve vulnerable women’s access to quality multi sectoral services including multisectoral SGBV services, cash enablement, and sexual and reproductive health services and foster women-led humanitarian response (including in response to COVID-19) in oPt. The project responds to HRP Strategic Objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

This would be achieved throughout three results: 1) To Improve vulnerable women's and girls' access to quality multi sectoral health and protection services 2) To improve the quality of SGBV services provided to vulnerable women and girls 3) Advocate for equitable access to healthcare and protection services, especially for the most vulnerable population to both SGBV and COVID-19 pandemic,  through meaningful women’s and girls´ participation.

UN Women will capitalize on the achievements and lessons learnt of the last years interventions in addressing SGBV needs, supporting partners to improve quality, accessibility and responsiveness of the services to the needs of those who are most vulnerable, including to COVID-19 and to conflict-related consequences. UN Women proposes to implement this 12-month project  to improve most vulnerable women’s and girls´ accessibility to multi-sectoral healthcare and protection services, cash based initiatives, decision-making, awareness-raising and accurate information on COVID-19, on SGBV, and on service availability.

UN Women’s interventions will be carefully tailored to address women’s and girls’ needs following rights-based and survivor-centred approaches. Interventions are designed to address the needs of the most vulnerable women and girls i.e. women with physical and intellectual disabilities, elderly women and those with non-communicable diseases, women at risk of forcible transfer, women heads of households, women SGBV survivors, etc.

Through its local partners in the oPt, UN Women will work to couple SGBV services with cash assistance and cash for work programming to ensure a maximized benefit for women most affected by conflict and COVID-19. Capacity building, case identification, management and referral will be also strengthened with a special focus on community protection mechanisms to deliver healthcare and protection services. At the same time UN Women will support access to comprehensive, accurate and updated information to partners on COVID-19 and its gendered implications. This information will be disability-adapted and produced in several cultural and age friendly formats and disseminated to the population through the CSOs, and the media.

To change social norms and behaviors around SGBV and women’s protection, men and boys will also be engaged through positive masculinity trainings and specialized  trainings on GBV and GBV services.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving integrated Gender Based Violence and Sexual Reproductive Health prevention and response services for IDPs, returnees, and Host Communities in the Ethiopia
project_objective:
UNFPA will continue promoting, coordinating and providing lifesaving integrated GBV services following the survivor-centered approach to address GBV in line with IASC (Interagency Minimum Standard) for emergency  programming including all guidelines  and measurement for COVID response and prevention. The Women and Girls’ Friendly Spaces (WGFS), selected One Stop Centers (OSC), and government service entry points will be offering integrated SRH-GBV services that includes GBV case management, mental health and psychosocial support and services, clinical management of rape, family planning services and counseling, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and emergency referrals to GBV survivors and vulnerable women and girls. GBV risk mitigation and prevention activities will be ensured by engaging community based approach where men and boys will be heavily engaged in line with IASC principles and guidelines. Life skill programmes will be in place and through an interagency partnership  and referral mechanism context based livelihood  and self-reliance programmes will be onboard. Social cohesion and community mobilization will be supported through a number of approach.  As women and girls continue to face protection risks, advocacy and communication for change will be implemented to guarantee their dignity and safety. Accountability towards community will be prioritized to safeguarding of beneficiaries and as co-chair of the PSEA Network at national level UNFPA will continue to lead the PSEA Network, and work with PSEA Network in the regions, to ensure a robust implementation of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse reporting and response mechanisms at all levels in the project sides.  
Under the leadership of UNFPA, the GBV AOR will enhance engagement with other sectors, national and regional government for integration of GBV prevention, mitigation and response programming for quality services of GBV survivors using IASC guidelines.  The AoR will expand comprehensive GBV prevention and response programmes for women, and girls, focusing on case management and multi-sectoral referral systems. Capacities will be enhanced on the GBV minimum standard, GBV handbook, IASC GBV Guidelines to sector leads, government stakeholders, and implementing partners fostering effective coordination in planning, implementing and monitoring essential GBV risk mitigation actions in all humanitarian response and services. This will be supported with regular community based GBV risk monitoring and joint safety audits. The AOR will deliberately target disability inclusion in GBViE response.

project_objective:

Improved accessibility, availability, and quality of GBV services for 4000 women, girls, men, and boys, with focus on women and Girls with Disabilities, Elderly women and GBV Survivors in the affected communities in Gaza Strip and West Bank.

The project is built based on the affected community needs and feedbacks, considering the vulnerable groups and women and girls at risk, in addition to UNFPA partners' experiences and updates from the field, safe spaces, and home visits. The project will reflect UNFPA experience and focal points' capacities in PSEA to spread the knowledge and reporting mechanisms, and the awareness within all target groups.

project_name: Supporting continuation of life-saving sexual and reproductive health services, by MOH and major NGOs in Gaza Strip, through enhancing response, preparedness and resilience of the community and health system to crises including COVID-19.
project_objective:
The need to sustain sexual and reproductive health “SRH” in Gaza, remains very high, considering the impact of the protracted crises, the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, and the latest May escalation, with associated redirection of resources (human, medical and logistics) from the provision of SRH to COVID-19 and casualties etc. As evidenced in the 2022 HNO, more than 150,000 women and girls were identified as high vulnerability of high-risk pregnancy, anemic mothers, female adolescents, and women with unmet need for family planning etc.  
This project is aligned with HNO 2022 Health Cluster Objectives 1 & 2 linked to Strategic Objectives 2 & 3 respectively. The project contributes to preventing excessive maternal morbidity and mortality, which have markedly deteriorated this year. The project will increase access to SRH care and nutrition services and information amid COVID-19, including family planning, gynecological disorders, and ensure that safe delivery, and emergency obstetric and newborn care services are available with specific needs of people with disabilities “PwD” and protection/GBV needs are mainstreamed. 
The project will complement previous and ongoing UNFPA programs/interventions; HPF 2021, third reserve allocation and other projects; by expanding the coverage of health system capacity to ensure continuation of essential SRH and maternal care services at primary and secondary health care levels and community.
The project will: -
- Ensure continuation of SRH services, enhance access to quality SRH care and strengthen SRH management and counselling, including the operationalization of relevant COVID-19 guidelines and protocols.
- Build the capacity of health providers in lifesaving SRH issues with focus on anemic pregnant and lactating women, high-risk pregnancy, detection and management of gynecological and pre-menopausal disorders and continuation of SRH services amid COVID-19, etc. 
- Strengthen the preparedness and response of the health facilities, fill gaps and replenish lifesaving SRH equipment, drugs, commodities, and supplies including contraceptives and PPE.
- Actively engage communities, support coping mechanisms, sensitization, awareness raising and outreach including midwifery led home visits model. 
- Support linking and informing communities on available services, including protection from GBV and psychosocial support, subsidies, and cash vouchers etc.
with special focus on marginalized communities and vulnerable groups including people with disabilities (PwD), young girls, the poor and elderly etc.
- Improve SRH services coordination among various stakeholders/providers, including mainstreaming disability, adolescents need, protection and GBV in SRH service provision and community outreach.
While this project is meant to address immediate response to urgent and critical needs of Gazan’s women, and young girls, especially those in marginalized areas, it will also support men and other vulnerable adolescents and strengthen the preparedness and resilience of both the community and the health system for absorbing shocks, saving lives and recovering from crises. UNFPA will work with MOH, Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) and other NGOs as needed to implement this project. 

UNFPA has been approached by Union of Health Works Committees (UHWC), who is applying for a project to support SRH services targeting women in their centers’ catchment areas in Gaza, to ensure coordination. UHWC has been encouraged to apply, and to continue coordination and sharing experience and information on localities and target groups upon project implementation to avoid duplication and ensure synergism with UNFPA and other projects. Similar coordination took place between UNFPA, CARE/PMRS and MAP-UK to ensure complementarity.

project_name: Strengthen health services including PHC and STHC services in NWS
project_objective:

Increase access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable humanitarian health services for those most vulnerable and in need 
Strengthen health sector capacity to prepare for, detect and deliver a timely response to disease outbreaks
Strengthen health system capacity to support continuity of care, strengthen community resilience, and respond to IDP movements and changes in context

project_name: Improving access to education and employment opportunities through the restoration of key education infrastructure and services
project_objective:
Solidarités International (SI) and its implementing partner Concern Worldwide (CWW) will build on the experience and results accomplished during Phase I  and create safe learning environments for school children, and at the same time, increase the employment opportunities of vulnerable youth. During Phase I which ended November 30th, 2021, fourteen schools were rehabilitated and provide now a safe learning environment for students in Raqqa and Hasakeh, and 358 boys and girls were enrolled in non-formal education services. SI and Concern conducted assessments to fine-tune the response strategy, and developed productive relationships with relevant education departments. The Partners can now determine the needs for Phase II phase together with local authorities, and particularly with the Education Committee and the Education Working Group in Northeast Syria.
In Phase II, SI and Concern will continue to increase access to education in a safe learning environment for Syrian children affected by conflict in Raqqa, Hasakeh, Aleppo and Deir ez-Zor governorates, according to a list of schools prioritized by the local education authorities in consultation with the NES Education Working Group and in addition to technical assessments. The project will prioritise schools with the highest number of out of school children.

project_name: Provision of WASH Assistance Among Vulnerable Settlements and Communities in Somalia
project_objective:
The proposed project will provide adequate safe water, sanitation facilities and hygiene education in targeted villages in Gedo, Banadir and Baidoa Regions of Somalia. The proposed project will provide adequate safe water, sanitation facilities and hygiene education in targeted villages in Gedo, Banadir and Baidoa Regions of Somalia. The project aims to reach 4,500 households comprising 2,070 (46%) children, 1,755 comprising 2,070 (46%) children, 1,755 (39%) adults, 225 (5%) elderly and 450 (10%) people with disabilities giving a total of 27, 000 (13,250 (49%) men and 13,770 (51%) women).
The project proposes to tackle the individual identified priority needs for each area. The project will focus on the construction, upgrading and rehabilitation of existing water supply systems, focusing on simple and familiar technology options – berkads, boreholes and pipeline extensions, as well as water trucking in Gedo, the extension of water pipelines to strategic IDP areas in Banadir and the construction of latrines and sanitation facilities in Baidoa, in full compliance to cluster guidelines. 
Concern will also work with the private sector (local water companies) working in Mogadishu (Banadir) and Gedo Region and Baidoa to supply water to the IDP camps identified. All installed water points at the IDP and community water collection points will be metered. Payments will based on agreed tariffs between the users and the Water Management Committees and the Private Service providers (where applicable), based on the meter readings.
Throughout the project Concern will conduct hygiene and sanitation educational training and outreach at the community level. The project will capitalize on already existing WASH committees and structures, and Community Hygiene Promoters to ensure the sustainability and maintenance of WASH infrastructure inputs. The project’s goals and plan shall be conducted in conjunction with the governmental authorities and local structures, most particularly the Ministry of Water and the Ministry of Planning, Ministry of Health (Public Health Department) and Ministry responsible for Social Services. Local Implementing Partner organizations will also participate in the implementation of the WASH Facilities.
Concern’s WASH Interventions will include cross‐cutting themes, and shall be mainstreamed in the programming, including implementing activities that enhance ways to identify and address differential forms of exclusion, including those based on societal discrimination, protection, power-structures, vulnerability, age, and gender; GBV, PSEA, DRR, disability and is in line with Accountability to Affected Populations commitments. Additionally, Concern will aim at strengthening inclusion of and ensuring accountability by community-based and other non-traditional humanitarian responders, for more effective protection to affected populations.
Concern Worldwide will work proactively in promote synergy with other Clusters and WASH partners, as WASH is mostly cross-cutting in various sectors,  to ensure adequate coordination of the Project activities through regular coordination with Health, Education, Shelter/NFIs, Protection (Including CP and GBV AoR), Nutrition, CWG and FSL Clusters to add value to the overall response through integrated response. 
During the project implementation period, Concern will be well aware of the need to adequately prepare the beneficiaries, local authorities and the line government departments for the Exit/Hand over of the installed systems and services. The strategy is such that the projects are designed keeping in view adequate handover arrangements with clear links to development actors and the relevant Government departments leading to durable solutions and resilience. This will be achieved through training and capacity building initiatives with the local authorities after a thorough capacity assessment including alignment with government plans.

project_name: Providing Access to Emergency WASH Services in Gedo, Somalia
project_objective:
The project proposes to improve access to safe water, sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices in an effort to improve the health conditions of 16,000 ( 8,759F, 6,600M and 640 elderly) drought affected individuals including internally displaced, marginalized riverine and vulnerable host women, men, boys and girls in Belet Xawa, Ceel Waaq, Dollow, Garbaharey and Luuq districts in Gedo region. Among the target beneficiaries will be 2,400 persons with disabilities.				 
The recurrent drought in Gedo has largely contributed to inadequate population access to potable water and resulted in frequent disease outbreaks, mainly AWD/cholera. WASH conditions are particularly poor (inadequate access to water to meet basic needs, lack of access to latrines, reliance on poor quality water sources). An assessment by REACH in June 2020 shows 93% of the households in Gedo have a WASH Living Standards Gap (LSG), with access to improved water sources below 41%. The region is served by small, seasonal, open water sources which are rapidly depleted with the recurrent droughts, leaving communities vulnerable to new outbreaks as they lack access to water for consumption and personal hygiene. Further, the assessment shows that 36% of the households have no access to a functional and improved sanitation facility. Serious protection concerns, and rights violations persist, where persons with disabilities, children and women are among the most affected social groups due to compounded vulnerabilities. The REACH DSA in March 2021 further shows that people with disabilities (100%), children (50%) and women (50%) are the top 3 groups reportedly facing impediments in accessing latrines. 
As part of the WASH cluster’s efforts to address the critical WASH needs in priority populations, this intervention will respond to the WASH gaps in the five target districts through the construction of two (2) solar powered water systems with piping to communities, rehabilitation of two existing shallow wells and training of 4 five-member water management committee. In addition, 8 existing high volume water points will be provided with fuel subsidies for three months during the hot and dry Jilaal season while water trucking will be done for 2,000 persons in rural villages for three months. The project will also construct150 universally design emergency latrines  with handwashing stations and distribute 150 latrine cleaning kits as well as 3,000 hygiene kits through Cash Vouchers. Hygiene promotion messaging will also be conducted in all the five districts. 
Trócaire will collaborate with Somali Humanitarian Relief Action (SHRA) and Active in Development Aid (ADA), national NGOs with strong experience in implementing WASH projects in Gedo, in the implementation of this project in the five target districts.

project_name: Improving access to life-saving and quality health services in Somalia for the most vulnerable.
project_objective:
The emergency health response aims to save lives, contribute towards improved physical and mental wellbeing of 389,988 individuals and their families. This will be realized through provision of sustainable access to quality and comprehensive health care services .The interventions will support 71 Mother and Child Clinics, 44 Primary health units/Health posts and 3 mobile teams located in 21 districts spread across 8 regions in Somalia. The interventions are aimed at contributing towards a reduction in morbidity and mortality vulnerable Somali communities, especially among the most vulnerable groups such as children under 5, pregnant and lactating women (PLW) and people living with with mental and physical disabilities. The project will increased access and quality of basic health services, prioritizing hard-to-reach areas. 
Planned measures will include both  disease prevention and management. 
Prevention measures include vaccination services and community awareness raising, WV will improve child health outcome through Timed and targeted counselling (ttC) which aimed at enhancing demand and health seeking behaviour will be adopted across the target project locations.
On disease management, the proposed project will support clinical diagnosis and management of common illnesses disease outbreak surveillance, reporting, investigation and response. Health facilities will be supported with health care worker capacity building, medical supplies and equipment provision to provide communicable disease management, comprehensive basic reproductive health care services in alignment of Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP). Except for covering essential maternal and child health, the capacity building will also include medical supply chain management, case referral, COVID-19 case detection, diagnosis and management, Gender Based Violence and protection incident management as well as psychological First aid. 
WV will enable PLWDs access health care services through the disability friendly health facility set up including latrines provisions .The project will utilize Community Health Workers (CHWs) who will do home visits ,beneficiary follow up and defaulter tracing with particular attention to PLWD and COVID affected HHs, facilitate their referrals and movement to the health facility to seek health care services. Special emphasis on health promotion and home follows up will be done targeting pregnant women and HHs with children living with disabilities. 
Moreover, WV through continuous engagement with community leaders, disability associations and the protection unit will sensitize communities to raise awareness on health rights of PLWDs to mitigate stigma. In each community engagement, WV will ensure and facilitate representation with 15 % of participants being PLWD during all community engagement forums. Boys and girls, men and women living with disabilities attended to will be closely followed up to ensure continuity in care thus transforming their health and well-being.
