project_name: Strengthening the protection of children and young people at homes and their communities among Rohingya refugees and host communties at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh.
project_objective: The IRC child protection program support children and adolescents in Rohingy and host communities to be safe at homes and in their communities and receive support when they experience any harm. Thus, the project will anchor on support to children and adolescents aged between 0-18 years with comprehensive case management, psychosocial services, life skills and business skills development to meet their safety needs and wellbeing. The project will be implemented in the following camps- 1E, 1W, 5, 8E, 14, 15, 18, 22, 23, 25 and Tecknaf, Sadar, Holidiapalang and Ratnapalong Upzilas in Ukhia host communities. IRC's Staff are highly trained with enormous experience to support diverse needs of the children and facilities regardless of the differences. IRC prevention program is largely local partner led, where IRC provides technical and handholding support to partners to implement IRC’s flagship program on Safe Healing and Learning Spaces (SHLS). Children aged 6-11 years are provided with age specific structured PSS through Social and Emotional Learning (SEL), SEL is nine months curriculum delivered in SHLS through trained facilitator (separate sessions for boys and girls) to help children cope with and heal from trauma; and participate in recreational activities to return to normalcy. Supporting Adolescents and their Families in Emergencies (SAFE) for adolescents aged 12 to 19 years with separate sessions for caregivers on building their resilience and parenting skills, Alternative care arrangement to have safe and supportive mentors to be more resilient to threats to survival and development (Training of caregivers and working with DSS to ensure placement of separated and or unaccompanied children), comprehensive case management services to children aged 0 to 18 years. Adolescents aged 15 to 19 are supported with ""Learn to Lead"" structured curriculum that support building resilience and civic engagement, particularly on issues related to leadership, social cohesion, advocacy, conflict resolution and peace building. They are also engaged in ""Learn to Earn"" sessions to equip them with transferable business and life skills. Adolescents who complete the sessions receive a start-up support in the form of tools/kits such as sewing machines, electrical repair took kits etc. to start their self-employment initiatives in camp and host communities. In addition, linkage support to government extension services is provided to the adolescents in the host communities. Community outreach designed based on the child protection needs identified through CPIMS, and regular child protection situation monitoring in each camp and host communities. Outreach session includes natural disaster and cyclone risk and preparedness issues on a regular discussion using IEC materials. IRC and local partner support establishing inclusive community structures, build their capacity and support in action planning so that they identify children at risk or those harmed, handle minor cases, and conduct timely referral to available service points, and ensure participation of women and adolescent, people with disabilities in the planning and decision-making process.  IRC ensures that the local partners including volunteers/incentive workers are trained on the Safeguarding and PSEA, community and child friendly accountability mechanism is in place, clients are empowered through regular sessions to report. The project is designed in consultation with the clients and Interventions are designed to address age, gender, and disability specific needs of children. Community will be also part of the monitoring and result harvesting process over the year. IRC will continue close collaboration and coordination with CPSS to ensure the program delivered are in accordance with sector objective. Regular on ground coordination with relevant government mechanism will be a key approach to deliver program in camp and host communities.

project_name: Improving Access to Quality and Inclusive Education in NWS
project_objective:
Unicef stated that the crisis in Syria has taken a devastating toll on education; leaving over 7,000 schools damaged or destroyed and about 2 million children out of school. Many of these children are the most vulnerable, including those recently displaced by insecurity. According to HNO, an estimated 6.9 million people (97 per cent children) need humanitarian education assistance. The intervention aims to fill the gaps in education in northwest Syria. School-age children dropping out of schools, as 28% of school-age children have never entered schools due to lack of schools, educational equipment, and the inability of displaced people and vulnerable families to bear Education costs, girls, women and children are at risk due to the lack of protection means in school buildings, as well as children with disabilities suffer from access to education services, as most schools are not equipped with tools and aids for people with disabilities (such as bathrooms, toilets, etc.), and there are no incentives for teachers, as around 5,165 teachers work on a voluntary basis in 565 schools in Idlib Governorate.
The formal system is unable to absorb and retain all school-age children. Many students continue to learn in unfavorable and/or unsafe learning environments. There is one practical classroom for every 178 school-age children in Idlib, and more than a third of schools work in shifts with triple and quadruple shifts in Idlib to address overcrowding and distance.
The purpose of the project is to increase school enrollment rates, maintain the retention of children in schools, provide them with the means to ensure the continuity of their education, improve the quality of education, and strengthen the educational system through the implementation of the following activities:

project_name: Conducting registration and veriﬁcation exercises for affected populations in Sudan
project_objective:
In response to the need for accurate information on displacement and the identification of beneficiaries for the delivery of humanitarian aid, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) began its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) program in 2004 to support the Government of Sudan (GoS) and its humanitarian partners in establishing an accurate data collection system and providing data on displacement in areas most affected by conflict and natural disasters. IOM has been working in close collaboration with the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC) and partners on the field to establish a unified and systematic method to collect individual data on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees in seven states. Since 2004, DTM Sudan has provided rapid emergency registrations with a priority of meeting immediate information needs for guiding direct assistance to vulnerable people. In 2010, DTM expanded to include biometric registrations and data verifications – implemented in response to government or humanitarian partner requests. 
Registration activities were used to collect data according to selected characteristics of displaced individuals and their family members. The information gathered was to build a list of all individuals present in one location at a point in time (updated beneficiary lists) and provide details of their characteristics including demographics information, vulnerabilities, and identify their needs for food, shelter, livelihoods, education, etc. Population groups covered in the past were IDPs and returning IDPs, but the exercises can
be expanded, and the methodology adapted to include other target groups such as Sudanese returnees from abroad and third-country nationals.
Registration data is captured by DTM field teams through direct individual interviews in the target locations, usually with the heads of households. All enumerators are trained on conducting interviews and engaging with female headed households. Additionally, throughout all activities, DTM team secures gender-responsive data collection by establishing gender mixed field teams, collecting sex-disaggregated data, and capturing other forms of social difference (wealth status, age, ethnicity, etc.). Registration data is shared with partners by means of data sharing agreements and used for beneficiary selection, vulnerability targeting and programming.

project_name: Réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité liée à la malnutrition dans les régions de l’Est, Nord, Centre Nord et Sahel
project_objective:
Une crise humanitaire d'une ampleur sans précédent s'est installée au Burkina Faso, se détériorant notamment en 2020 dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord, du Sahel, et de l’Est. En raison de la présence de groupes armés non étatiques perpétrant des violences dans les communautés, les populations touchées sont poussées au déplacement interne, ce qui a des conséquences dévastatrices sur des personnes déjà vulnérables. 
Action contre la Faim (ACF), le Comité international de secours (IRC), Seach for Common Ground , l’association Tin Tua, Terre des hommes et l’association Wupa-Kuwé s'engagent à répondre aux besoins cruciaux des personnes touchées, en particulier les enfants et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes (FEFA), par une approche intégrée qui s'attaque aux principaux facteurs de risques sanitaires dans les situations d'urgence. Le programme vise à améliorer l'accès à des services de santé, de nutrition et de protection de qualité dans les régions susmentionnées. Dans cette perspective, les organisations en consortium contribueront principalement à renforcer les systèmes de santé et à fournir un soutien clinique, réduisant ainsi le taux de mortalité maternelle et infantile parmi les personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays (PDI) et leurs communautés d'accueil dans les régions ciblées.
Action contre la Faim et ses partenaires prévoient de fournir une assistance en santé et Nutrition pour les populations affectées par la crise humanitaire dans les régions de l'Est, Nord, Centre Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun , Sahel et l’Est, à travers:
Des soins de santé primaires: l’assistance sera focalisée sur les pathologies essentielles aussi bien pour les enfants que les adultes
La santé reproductive maternelle et infantile: ces soins concerneront les volets préventifs, curatifs et promotionnels. Le projet appuiera les centres de santé fonctionnels pour fournir des services de qualité lors des CPN. Les femmes seront préparées pour leur accouchement et recevront des kits d’accouchement hygiénique. Ce qui leur permettra d’accoucher dans des conditions acceptables même en situation de mouvement. Un accès sera mis sur la prévention du paludisme chez les femmes enceintes. 
La prise en charge psychologique: des psychologues seront recrutés pour la mise en œuvre du premier secours psychologique dans les communautés et dans les centres de santé. Ces professionnels formeront les personnels de santé et les agents de santé communautaires pour le soutien aux personnes ayant subi des traumatismes psychologiques.
Le renforcement du système de santé: des équipes d’évaluation seront mises en place pour la surveillance du contexte sanitaire et la réalisation d’évaluations rapides en cas de choc.
La prévention: il s'agira de la promotion des pratiques de l'ANJE selon l'approche GASPA (groupe d'apprentissage et de soutien à la pratique de l'ANJE) centrée sur les femmes enceintes et allaitantes dans les communautés et dans les centres de santé. 
Le dépistage: Action contre la Faim s'appuiera sur le réseau des agents de santé communautaires mis en place par le ministère de la santé. Ces acteurs seront formés sur les techniques de dépistage et de référencement des cas de malnutrition. 
La prise en charge des cas de malnutrition aiguë sévère dans les CSPS: Action contre la faim formera les agents de santé des CSPS sur le protocole de prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère sans complication médicale.
L'appui à la PEC des cas MAS avec des complications médicales: Action contre la Faim prévoit d'accompagner l'ensemble des CREN des 5 régions en état d'urgence à travers la formation et l'accompagnement technique continue pour garantir la qualité de la PEC des cas compliqués et réduire les taux de décès intra-hospitalier lié à la malnutrition.

project_name: Projet d’amélioration de l’accès des populations aux soins de santé de qualité dans les régions affectées par la crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
La présente intervention vise à contribuer à l’amélioration de l’accès des populations aux soins de santé de qualité dans les régions de l'Est et du Centre-Est du Burkina, affectées par la crise humanitaire. La stratégie adoptée suit une approche intégrée de la sous-nutrition.  Le projet s’inscrit dans la stratégie du Cluster nutrition au Burkina Faso en 2021. De plus, cette réponse s’aligne avec les objectifs stratégiques du Plan de réponse humanitaire (HRP) 2021: 
Objectif stratégique 1 : Fournir une assistance d’urgence intégrée nécessaire pour adresser les problèmes critiques liés au bien-être physique et mental des populations affectées, notamment : les personnes dans le besoin à la suite d’un choc violent, et les personnes vulnérables qui les accueillent reçoivent une assistance d’urgence multisectorielle par au minimum trois secteurs dans les 30 jours suivants le choc ; les personnes dans le besoin lié aux problèmes critiques ont un accès sécurisé et équitable aux soins et aux services d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement, nécessaire pour garantir leur survie physique ; les filles, garçons et enfants de 0 à 5 ans et les femmes allaitantes, reçoivent une prise en charge intégrée contre la malnutrition, incluant l’accès à une prise en charge de qualité, de l’eau potable et de la nourriture.
Objectif stratégique 2 : Améliorer les conditions de vie des populations affectées à travers une assistance adaptée à leurs besoins, fournie à temps et dans un environnement de protection.
Objectif stratégique 3 : Contribuer au respect des droits fondamentaux et à la protection des populations touchées par les crises.
Ce projet s’aligne également avec l’aperçu des Besoins Humanitaires (HNO).
Action contre la Faim propose de renforcer sa présence dans la région de l’Est et du Centre- Est en étendant et renforçant ses activités d’urgence afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des populations affectées par la crise humanitaire, notamment les femmes et les filles, statistiquement plus vulnérables.  
Les régions de l’Est et du Centre-Est sont confrontées à une crise sécuritaire avec la présence des groupes d’opposition armées radicaux (GOA), rendant l’accès des populations aux services de base, mais aussi l’accès humanitaire difficile. En intégrant dans son programme des activités liées aux pratiques de soins, le programme d’Action contre la Faim vise à atténuer l’impact de la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS) sur les enfants et leurs accompagnants, à prévenir une détérioration des conditions de vie des cas de MAS, à prévenir l’apparition de nouveaux cas de MAS et à améliorer le bien-être des mères et donneurs de soins. Une attention particulière sera portée aux femmes car la plupart des accompagnants d’enfants MAS dans les structures sanitaires sont des femmes. 
Avec un accent sur les femmes et les filles, les résultats de l’action proposée comprendront trois composantes clés: 
1)	Un paquet nutrition/santé au niveau des centres de santé et au niveau communautaire par le biais de cliniques mobiles, caractérisé par la prévention et le traitement de la MAS et la gestion des maladies communes à l’enfance chez les filles et garçons de moins de 5 ans, ainsi que la santé maternelle et reproductive chez les femmes enceintes et allaitantes ; 
2)	Des espaces « mères-bébés » pour les enfants de moins 5 ans (avec priorisation des enfants de moins de 2 ans). Ces espaces viseront à améliorer les pratiques de soins infantiles et apporter un soutien psychosocial aux mères et donneurs de soins afin d’améliorer le traitement mais également de prévenir les risques de rechute des enfants MAS. Ces interventions intégrées à la nutrition permettent de limiter les conséquences négatives de la MAS sur le développement infantile, notamment par des actions de stimulation psychomotrice et de renforcement des pratiques de soins dans les centres de santé et dans les cliniques mobiles.

project_name: Assistance Alimentaire et en moyen d’existence aux populations vulnérables dans les régions du Nord, Centre-Nord et Est.
project_objective: L’alimentation est l’un des besoins de premières nécessités, cette situation est encore plus préoccupante pour les populations affectées par les mouvements de populations. Selon le cadre harmonisé projeté près de 2 632 503 millions de personnes auront besoin d’une assistance alimentaire (insécurité alimentaire phase 3 à 4). Le cluster s’est fixé pour objectif d’assister 2,3 millions de personnes en s’assurant que toutes les personnes en insécurité alimentaire alimentaire chronique phase 4 soient prisent en compte. Dans la même logique, ACTED propose ce présent projet pour répondre aux différents besoins immédiats de prise en charge alimentaire, de relèvement et d’adaptation professionnelle en zone urbaine des populations vulnérables des régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord et l’Est. Le cadre harmonisé estime que 40% de ces personnes seront concentrées au Centre-Nord, 30% à l’Est et 23% au Nord. Ce projet comprendra 4 volets : réponse rapide en assistance alimentaire suite à un déplacement de population (1), assistance alimentaire aux populations vulnérables (2) réhabilitation des moyens de subsistance (élevage) par l’appui au petit élevage (foire commerciale et distribution d'aliments pour bétail pendant la période de soudure...) des ménages vulnérables (3) Appui aux activités génératrices de revenu (AGR) des ménages vulnérables (4). Les volets 1 et 2 pourront utiliser des modalités diverses (cash, inkind, coupons et foires) en fonction du contexte, des préférences de la population et de la capacité des marchés locaux. Les volets 3 et 4 cibleront en priorité les femmes et les jeunes. Au total le projet ciblera 79 820 ménages.

project_name: Humanitarian health assistance to vulnerable population affected by the armed conflict and the Venezuelan migratory crisis in Colombia
project_objective:
This is a multiple-affectation project. It seeks to serve two types of populations: migrants in Colombia and victims of the armed conflict. It is for this reason that priority has been given to Atrato Medio region (Quibdó, Bojayá, Murindó and Vigía del Fuerte) and the Southern migration route (Tunja, Bogotá, Cali and Ipiales), to implement actions in health that contribute to alleviating the suffering of rural communities and migrants in transit, especially walkers in these areas.

The project will contribute to improve access to health services and local capacities through the rehabilitation of health infrastructure, the provision of primary health care services, raising-awareness sessions on key health issues and comprehensive training to target population affected by the conflict.

Facilitate access to primary health care services to migrant population in transit through the implementation of mobile health clinics, referrals for specialized care and raising-awareness sessions on key health issues.

project_name: Assistance en Articles Ménagers Essentiels et en Abris pour les déplacés et les communautés hôtes affectés par le conflit dans 3 régions du Burkina Faso (Sahel, Nord, Centre-Nord).
project_objective:
L’aggravation de la crise sécuritaire au Burkina Faso depuis 2015 et la multiplication des incidents dans 5 régions depuis juin 2018 dues au conflit qui oppose les groupes d’opposition armés et les forces armées burkinabé d’une part et au conflit communautaire d’autre part, a occasionné des mouvements de population sans précédents au Burkina Faso (principalement dans le Sahel, le Centre-Nord, le Nord, l’Est, la Boucle du Mouhoun et plus récemment dans le Centre-Est) et a contribué à la dégradation de la situation humanitaire. Selon les derniers chiffres publiés par OCHA, le nombre de déplacés internes aurait atteint 1 407 685 personnes en Septembre 2021. Depuis le début de la crise, on a pu observer que les populations affectées ont tendance à se déplacer vers les centres urbains où ils sont pour la plupart accueillis par la communauté hôte. Dans la fuite, elles n’ont souvent pas eu le temps d’emporter leurs Articles Ménagers Essentiels ; ce qui occasionne une forte pression sur les communautés hôtes. De même, la plupart de ces populations déplacées trouvent refuge dans les quartiers non lotis et dorment souvent à la belle étoile par manque de place. 
SI est présente au Burkina Faso depuis Octobre 2018 et a déjà distribué près de 13500 kits AME, 3000 kits minimaux d’abris d’urgence, installé 300 abris d’urgence de type tentes sahélienne, construit 260 abris semi-durables et délivré une assistance en CASH pour la location à 410 ménages dans le Nord, le Centre-Nord et le Sahel.
Fort de cette expérience et d’une connaissance approfondie du contexte, SI propose de répondre aux besoins de 17500 personnes affectées à travers la distribution de kits AME, l’installation de tentes sahéliennes, l’appui à la location avec la modalité CASH accompagné d’un appui dans le domaine des Activités Génératrices de Revenu et la construction/réhabilitation d’abris semi-durables dans les régions du Centre-Nord, Nord, Sahel.

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving SRHR services for most vulnerable and in-need population, Sudan, 2022
project_objective:
The provision of Sexual and Reproductive Health services is essential in humanitarian setting, it is an effective approach for preventing deaths, diseases, and disabilities associated and resulted from unintended pregnancy, obstetric complications, sexual and other forms of gender-based violence, HIV infection, and a range of reproductive disorders. UNFPA jointly with partners, will ensure the provision of comprehensive SRH services in humanitarian settings.

The intervention primarily targets women, girls in reproductive age, youth and adolescents, and men and boys. Sudan HNO 2021 indicates total people in need at 8.1 million, health sector target is 5.7 million. UNFPA will target 1.6 million with more than 80% are women and girls in reproductive age. The geographical coverage follows the HNO identified locations with severity ranking three and above.

All SRHR intervention will be implemented simultaneously through coordinated actions with all relevant partners. The planned interventions prioritize and aim reducing SRH mortalities and morbidities through: timely provision of Emergency Obstetric care and save delivery services, timely referral to lifesaving services, support the availability of Family Planning services, improving Clinical management of rape for survivors of SGBV, availing HIV and STIs prevention and response, improving Antenatal and postnatal care, Post abortion care, and other SRH services. These will be achieved through strengthening the capacity of SRH care providers with emphases of midwifery services, timely availability of lifesaving SRHR supplies, timely deployment of temporary clinics and mobile clinics, supporting the referral system, and demand creation through awareness raising and educational activities. Maternal Morbidities such as Obstetric fistula will be given especial attention by UNFPA.

The implementation of activities will be conducted through NGOs and Government partners with the strong technical support from UNFPA, including maintaining the field presence.

project_name: Strengthen GBV prevention mechanism and provision of comprehensive lifesaving interventions for populations in need in Sudan
project_objective:
Across Sudan, GBV continues to be a life-threatening concern, exacerbated by a variety of factors including armed conflict, tribal clashes, forced displacement, and recurring disasters such as floods.  It is estimated that there are 2,940,705 people in need in 2022 for GBV prevention, mitigation and response, including mainly women and girls from localities that are prone to conflict and tribal clashes, hosting refugees as well as disasters, with a high percentage of households engaged in negative coping mechanisms. This also includes 209,366 refugees without access to core GBV services. The severity of protection needs is very critical in 94 localities across 12 states in Sudan. UNFPA intends to target 80% the GBV subsector target of the PiN in severity ranking 5, 60% in severity ranking 4 and approximately 30% of PiN of the GBV SS target in severity ranking 3.

The project pursues the following 3 objectives:
To provide life-saving specialized quality GBV services including CMR, case management and psychosocial support and reinforce referral pathways 
To enhance strategies for community resilience through empowerment of women and girls and strengthened community based interventions
To promote GBV risk mitigation into all aspects of the humanitarian response
To strengthen GBV Coordination mechanism at national and sub-national level and strengthen data collection and information management

project_name: Improved access to safe water and vector control activities for the crisis affected and underserved population in Sudan
project_objective: The situation in Sudan remains fragile with and associated deterioration of the health system in general and preventative programs specifically. This leads to a increase of oro- faecal route transmitted and vector borne diseases occurrence and continuing Covid-19 community transmissionhe public health threat of arboviruses is rapidly growing worldwide. The newly emergeing vector Anopheles stephensi  has been confirmed in 8 states of Sudan and require a rapid scale up of vector control operations to prevent urban and semi urban outbreaks. Vector borne diseases and water borne disease outbreaks like cholera/AWD, are mostly triggered by the yearly heavy rains and related floods, which affected in 2021 more than 41, 000  families in 63 localities.  By October 2021, outbreaks of Dengue fever  were confirmed in 6 states. Malaria,  the leading cause of morbidity in Sudan has crossed the epidemic threshold in sixteen states. The vector borne disease map has changed due to climate change (flooding), poverty, population movement, unplanned urbanization, vector resistance to insecticides and more areas are at considered at risk.  WHO is the main contributor to vector control projects targeting vulnerable populations in Sudan.  In 2021, WHO spent 3.4 M  USD for vector control to protect the most vulnerable populations out of which 29% were covered by SHFand CERF and 71 % from other humanitarian funds. Water and sanitation indicator remain poor with only 37.42 %  of the population having access to improved sanitation, widespread open defecation and about 85 % of the population not using basic hand washing facilities. In 2021,  91% of 2,410 analyzed did not meet the required standards. WASH in heath care facilities remains a major challenge with a lack of basic water services, sufficient numbers of functioning latrines and functional hand hygiene facility at the point of heath care. WHO as technical agency leading the overall coordination and implementation of vector control will continue it is technical support to other partners and advocate for engaging more partners to ensure the protection of crisis affected population from  exposure to vector borne diseases through managing all risk factors by supporting entomological surveillance, multiple Integrated Vector Management Interventions, and community mobilization to apply effective measures for their own protection. Vigilant entomological surveillance will be done including 1. adult mosquito surveillance through different adult collection methods2. aquatic stages surveillance targeting open outdoor mosquito breeding sites and 3.  indoor aedes mosquito breeding sites. Vector control measures will be applied including environmental management, chemical control of aquatic and adult vectors, training of the environmental health officers, CHW workers from MOH and partners on the integrated vector management and other WASH components. WHO will work closely with Health, WASH sectors to improve water quality at all levels.WHO will support water quality surveillance system in prioritized high-risk locations, operational cost for water quality surveillance and water quality monitoring equipment and supplies, and support existing water quality testing laboratories. Awareness raising sessions on best WASH practices and vector borne diseases prevention will be carried out in cholera hot spots and Aedes vector borne diseases high risk areas at household and community level. WHO will continue to support WASH &IPC services at Heath care facilities and COVID 19 isolation centers, assess WASH and IPC services at HCF, provide  operational cost to improve environmental cleaning at HCF (including COVID-19 isolation centers, Cholera Treatment Centers, mobile clinic and fixed clinics for vulnerable populations including refugee, IDP and host communities). WHO will provide printing materials to promote best behavior for the staff and communities and fill the gap by supporting community based waste management.

project_name: Supporting shelter repair and rehabilitation of vulnerable households in Middle Area, Rafah and Khan Yunis governorates in the Gaza Strip to minimize exposure to harsh weather and protection concerns
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims to support 400 households (HH) living in severely or partially damaged/substandard/overcrowded shelters and HH at risk of exposure to harsh weather, the spread of COVID-19 and protection concerns in the Middle Area, Rafah and Khan Yunis governorates in the Gaza Strip in order to meet their basic needs and enhance their coping capacity. It aims at alleviating the impact of the May-2021 escalation, as well as of COVID-19, and the overall protracted conflict affecting the Shelter sector in the Gaza strip. Through conditional restricted cash assistance and technical assistance/monitoring, ACTED and its implementing partner UFA will support the self-repair and rehabilitation of these shelters as well as the purchasing of NFIs (bedding set, kitchen set and dignity kits), to ensure compliance with SPHERE and Shelter Cluster minimum standards and to alleviate unmet needs that expose these 400 HH to protection risks.
The project is heavily informed by assessments ACTED undertook under other projects in 2021, MSNA 2021 findings, extensive consultations with key stakeholders, and recommendations from the MoSD and the MoPWH, the Shelter & NFI Cluster and Cash Working Group (CWG) in Gaza.
The proposed intervention is fully aligned with the 2022 HNO and supports the achievement of 2022 HRP for the Shelter Cluster, most notably by contributing to the Shelter Clusters efforts to address the priority humanitarian needs, namely: “Vulnerable households living in substandard shelter exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns are supported to meet basic needs and enhance their coping capacity (winterization, summarization, shelters upgrade and rehabilitation, damaged shelters repair, COVID-19 shelter related interventions)”. Specifically, ACTED and its local implementing partner UFA will implement a multi-pronged approach to increase access of vulnerable HH to safe and secure shelters through the following means:
-Conducting assessments and verifications of HH nominated as vulnerable by MoPHW and MoSD and on ACTED CRM’s referred lists and waiting lists, defined based on the same criteria, in the targeted governorates to select the 400 most vulnerable HH as final beneficiaries. 
-Facilitating shelter repair and/or adaptation works through a self-repair approach through conditional restricted cash assistance and technical assistance/monitoring to ensure compliance with SPHERE and Shelter Cluster minimum standards and to alleviate unmet needs that expose 400 HH in severely or partially damaged/sub-standard shelters to protection risks.
-Strengthening existing Community-Based Protection Committees (CBPCs) through the provision of trainings (refresher training and new topics) to mainstream protection principles within their communities and ensure community engagement.
Targeted communities will indirectly benefit from the intervention through the enhanced protection delivered by the CBPCs. More specifically, the intervention will directly benefit 400 beneficiary HH (comprised of 2200 individuals) through the cash assistance to support shelter self-repair/ rehabilitation works and purchase of needed NFIs. In addition, 3 CBPCs (18 members in total) will benefit from trainings (refresher training and new topics) to support their communities and ensure mainstreaming of protection principles including key PSEA messages. As such, there will be 2218 direct beneficiaries in total.
The project will be supported by the mainstreaming of an Integrated Protection Approach (IPA), with a specific focus on the most vulnerable groups, including women, girls, boys, the disabled and the elderly. Gender principles will be mainstreamed throughout the entire action and CBPCs will be trained on referral mechanisms of protection cases such as GBV with a particular focus given to women and children. Finally, AAP will be core to the proposed Action by giving account to, taking account of and being held to account by affected populations.

project_name: Soutien médico-nutritionnel de qualité aux populations vulnérables et renforcement du système de santé primaire dans les zones affectées par les crises au nord et au centre du Mali
project_objective:
PUI souhaite continuer à assurer l’accès aux services vitaux et essentiels pour les populations vulnérables, en particulier les FEFA et les enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi qu’aux victimes de VBG, impactées par la crise au Mali. Cette assistance inclura le soutien à la provision du PMA : les soins curatifs préventifs de santé primaire, le PEV, la PCIMA, le soutien psychosocial et l’accès aux intrants médicaux essentiels ainsi que le renforcement du système de référencement vers le niveau secondaire. PUI renforcera également le système de veille et d’alerte épidémiologique avec la mise en place d’un système de riposte efficace à travers son approche Elongo et effectuera le lien avec le RRM. 
Les efforts fournis en 1ère phase permettent à PUI de renforcer et pérenniser l’appui au fonctionnement du système de santé en proposant une aide modulée suivant l’évaluation de performance des CSCom, le renforcement des capacités des agents de santé, des ASACO ainsi que du réseau communautaire. Les activités engageant la communauté notamment la sensibilisation et la communication pour le changement de comportement, resteront des activités phares.
Dans un contexte d’insécurité, PUI supportera de manière plus spécifique la prévention, la mitigation et la prise en charge des VBG, dans le respect des recommandations du dispositif minimum d’urgence.
Ainsi, l’objectif de ce projet est double : il vise à appuyer les activités en soins de santé primaire dans 15 aires de santé dans le cercle d’Ansongo tout en renforçant les capacités des acteurs du système de santé en vue d’un transfert progressif des compétences de gestion, de suivi, de supervision et de formation, quand les prérequis seront présents. Dans le cercle de Bandiagara un appui à la stratégie mobile sera conservé afin d’assurer un accès minimum aux soins de santé primaire pour les populations les plus éloignées et vulnérables.

project_name: Meeting immediate humanitarian needs through provision of emergency food assistance and livelihoods activities
project_objective: This project encompasses food assistance through emergency kits to populations that lack access to standard food distributions, including the newly displaced, returnees, vulnerable host community members. Seasonally appropriate livelihoods activities will support vulnerable households to engage in income-generating or food producing activities.

project_name: Enhanced Access to Household Basic Needs and Strengthened Livelihood Opportunities of Vulnerable Communities in Eastern Equatoria and Upper Nile States, South Sudan
project_objective: The intervention will address urgent food insecurity (IPC 3, 4 & 5) through multi-purpose, unconditional cash assistance and market support; livelihoods support aims to contribute to food security and improve dietary diversity and reduce the use of negative coping strategies for vulnerable host, IDP and returnee populations (Cluster Objective 1); it will enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support (Cluster Objective 2) and reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks (Cluster Objective 3). The project will also ensure protection (Gender-based Violence (GBV) AoR & Mine Action AoR) and age, gender and diversity inclusion principles are mainstreamed throughout all activities.

project_name: Mejor acceso a los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva para la población vulnerable afectada por la crisis socioeconómica venezolana y la recesión económica relacionada con el COVID-19
project_objective: En el contexto complejo de crisis económica y pandemia de Covid19, PUI tiene como objetivo mejorar la situación de atención en salud sexual y reproductiva y apoyo psicosocial específicamente en el ambulatorio Jesús Maestre del Barrio José Félix Rivas zona 10 de Petare, estado Miranda. En este ambulatorio acude una población de estrato socio económico muy bajo y sus principales problemas de salud son las enfermedades de transmisión sexual, complicaciones que genera un embarazo no controlado sobre todo en adolescentes, violencia urbana  que genera ansiedad  e interrupción de las actividades cotidiana que influye en la calidad de vida aunado a esto el deterioro  de  los servicios de salud mental disponibles a nivel público, el déficit de  transporte en la zona ocasiona que las mujeres no tengan acceso a otros centros de salud más lejanos. Por consiguiente,  PUI incluirá ayuda en planificación familiar con la implementación de métodos anticonceptivos, consulta prenatal y psicológica, capacitaciones al personal de salud y sensibilizaciones a la comunidad sobre temas de autocuidado, empoderamiento de la mujer . La población meta será de 3504 su desagregación para adquirir beneficios es de 1440 población femenina en edad fértil para métodos anticonceptivos y 2064  mujeres y hombres   que se le dará beneficio incluyendo tratamiento para enfermedades de transmisión sexual, kit de parto, consulta prenatal  y orientación sobre aspectos de salud mental.

project_name: Enhance safe and equitable access to quality non formal education for children and youth dropping out of schools and those at risk of dropping out.
project_objective:
This project aims to enhance the accessibility of conflict-affected children in NES in Kisreh sub-district, and in NWS in Afrin sub-district to quality, safe, and equitable non-formal education. The project will target children (7-17 years) who have dropped out or at risk of dropping out of schools with NFE programs and children (3-7 years) with Early childhood Education (ECE).
The planned approach of implementation is face-to-face, and in case of imposing curfew by the authorities in the area/s of implementation due to covid-19 outbreak, the modality will be shifted to remote learning.
The project has 3 objectives, that are aligned with the HRP Education sector objectives, which are: 
1-	Increase safe and equitable availability and access to in-person non-formal education for crisis-affected children and youth.
2-	Enhanced quality of non-formal education for children and youth.
3-	Education system is better able to support the education response.
The activities that will be implemented in both NES/ Kisreh and NWS/Afrin are similar including the following:
1-	Establishing and running 2 TLSs, 1 in each of Afrin and Kisreh communities, where the NFE, ECE, and parenting programs/PTAs meeting will be implemented.
2-	Undertaking light rehabilitation to 10 educational facilities where NFE and PTAs will be implemented. These 10 facilities include 2 TLSs and 8 schools. 7 of these educational facilities out of 10 will be in Kisreh sub-district, and 3 will be in Afrin sub-district, i.e.:
-	 In Kisreh: there will be 1 TLS and 6 schools
-	In Afrin: there will be 1 TLS and 2 schools 
3-	Support the 10 educational facilities with operational cost, IT equipment, solar system for lighting, sterilizers, and PPE for educational staff and beneficiaries.
4-	Conducting 10-days Back to Learning (BTL) Campaigns in each of Afrin and Kisreh in order to introduce the project activities and invite the children’s caregivers to register their children to the NFE and ECE programs, note that the BTL campaign will include conducting diagnostic tests for children registered in order to be able to select the most in need children for NFE programs.
5-	Implementing ALP and remedial NFE programs for children dropped out of schools and these children will undertake pre and post-tests to measure the impact of the ALP and remedial program implemented and assess their educational improvement.
In average, 11 classrooms will be utilized in each of the 8 schools (6 in Kisreh and 2 in Afrin), 10 for the implementation of NFE programs, and 1 classroom for admin; therefore, 10 teachers (1 teacher per classroom) will be providing NFE in each of the 8 schools during the afternoon shift. 
While in the 2 TLSs, the space is smaller, so 4 rooms in each TLS will be used to implement the NFE programs but during the morning and afternoon shift, so 8 teachers will be recruited for each of the TLSs, 4 for the morning shift and 4 for the afternoon shift.
6-	Implementing ECE for children (3-7 years) using 2 approaches: static-based in the 2, and through community-based outreach approach in order to reach a wider scope of beneficiaries geographically (those living in distant locations from the TLSs) and physically (EX: people with disabilities facing barriers to come to the TLSs).

7-	Providing transportation for children with disabilities (CwD) from and to the educational facilities in order to attend the NFE (ALP & remedial) and other activities in the schools and TLSs.

8-	Establishing 2 PTAs, 1 in each of Afrin and Kisreh communities, and conducting regular meetings with these PTAs in order to enhance communication between educational personnel and caregivers and get their feedback to improve the services provided.

9-	Distributing monthly incentives and building the capacity of 104 Educational personnel on EIE and INEE, school and classroom management, SEL, PSS, and PFA.
10-	Providing the children attending the NFE programs with school bags, stationery, and curriculums.

project_name: Wash assistance to refugees in Gedaref State
project_objective:
Internal conflict in Ethiopia’s Tigray region in November 2020 led to a sudden mass displacement of more than 69,000 Ethiopians to Sudan’s Kassala, Blue Nile and Gedaref States. Thanks to the support of the Sudanese authorities, UNHCR/COR coordination, new permanent settlements have been identified to accommodate the new wave of displacement from Ethiopia. 
Gedaref State is hosting the majority of the refugees (62,383) in Um Rakuba (20,572) and Tunaydbah (20,604). additionnlay recent new influx from Qemant tribes are as well in GEdaref State, in Basunda locality,  in a very dire situation. 

The activities proposed by SI, based on field evidence needs, assessment and secondary data, are: : 
- Emergency Water trucking in context without any other alternatives access to water
- rehabilitation and maintenance of wash facilities (latrines and shower places)
- construction of wash facilities in new camps (Babikri, possible new open camps)
- waste management
- hygiene  promotion
- Rapid Response team to address the risk of outbreak

project_name: Provision of Safe, inclusive, and quality education for conflict affected IDP and Host community children in Axum, Adwa, Adigrat, Wukro, Kua and Mekelle,
project_objective:
This project will enhance access to equitable, safe, and inclusive education for 16,667 (50% girls, 4% CWDs) emergency-affected school aged boys’ and girls’ in Axum, Adwa, Adigrat, Wukro, Mekelle, and Kuha town of Tigray region. The project will be implemented by three organization in a consortium approach with Imagine 1day, Plan International, and World Vision. These organizations have ample years of experience implementing education and other emergency programs in Ethiopia. In line with the draft 2021 Ethiopia Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), the project mainly aimed to increases access to equitable, safe, inclusive and quality education through non-formal learning opportunities using accelerated learning programs. It will also support education service delivery systems and partners by strengthening their institutional and technical capacities and building resilience of children. communities, parents, and existing education structures through capacity building, coordination and information management support.

To meet these objectives and ensure that children can exercise their right to education and are protected from risks, the consortium members prioritized the provision of safe and protective learning spaces for children affected by the conflict to helping children continue learning and enhance the resilience of communities by supporting learning during this crisis in Tigray region. The consortium partners will capitalize on their collective best experiences in their effort to deliver effective and sustainable program for IDP and host communities in targeted areas. The consortium partners agreed on the geographic share based on their operational area. Imagine1 day will implement the project in Axum and Adwa. Plan International will implement in Mekelle, Kuha, and Wukro. World Vision will implement in Adigrat Plan International is the lead applicant. Imagine1 day will reach 6,667 age 5-14 children and World Psion and Plan International will each impact 5,000 children.

project_name: Improving living conditions of the crisis-affected population in Monguno, Borno state, Nigeria
project_objective: Contribute to improving living conditions of the crisis-affected population in Monguno, Borno State, Nigeria. The proposed intervention targets 53,873 direct beneficiaries to reach through health (38,440 persons), protection (11,556 p.), nutrition, and livelihoods (3,877 p.), while the number of indirect beneficiaries is 95,486 individuals

project_name: Humanitarian Comprehensive Primary Health care response for conflict affected Population in 5 Woredas of Afar Region -GA 20016/SOF -82605289
project_objective: Due to the internal conflict, in Afar Zone 4 Woredas, more than 70,000 populations has been displaced leading to wider ranges of infectious disease and malnutrition. Most of Health facilities in the affected Woredas are not providing services making access to health service a big challenge for the community. In initial program ,Save the children  has targeted   5  woredas of Afar  highly affected by  conflict  (Yallo, Chifra, Awra, Ewa & Golina ) , however  due recent access challenge related with active conflict in those targeted woredas SCI is reprograming this response to other 5 woredas of Afar ( Berhle ,Elidea’r,Mille,Adear and Abala) those  affected by  conflict and /or  hosted high number of IDP displaced from active war area and recently accessible    in consultation with local government and clusters coordination.   The response proposed to implement a comprehensive primary health care service incorporating access to life saving emergency health care through outreach mobile health and nutrition services and concurrently build the local system through technical trainings. The project also include support to the rehabilitation of the local health system through provision of medical supplies and essential equipment which can contribute to resume the routine health service provision. project_name: Access to lifesaving mental health services in Lebanon
project_objective:
Suicide is a pressing health concern worldwide, with over 800,000 people dying by suicide yearly. Since the Covid-19 pandemic, related uncertainties, fears, and health measures led to increase in suicide and associated mental disorders. In 2020, 150 people died by suicide in Lebanon, a low- to middle- income country facing social, political, and economic collapse since October 2019. Despite the impact of mental health activities launched via non- profits such as Embrace, a local non- profit that promotes mental health and suicide prevention, resources remain restricted while community needs exponentiate. Today, people in Lebanon are experiencing severe livelihood risks and absence of basic life necessities including medication, gasoline, and food. These burdens, in addition to the stressors of the pandemic, come as a detriment to citizens’ mental health and are especially magnified for those with predisposition or pre-existing mental illnesses. Additionally, hundreds of people are still grappling with the mental, emotional, and financial consequences of the Beirut explosion which continues to manifesting through trauma symptoms and loss of hope. 

From this project Embrace expects to increase the capacity of both the National Lifeline and the Mental Health Clinic. The current national situation exacerbates the risk factors individuals live on a daily basis further increasing their risk of mental health symptoms and problems, which in return necessitates the need to strengthen community prevention services. The project intends to support the growth of the National Lifeline as a service that has been very well adopted by the community and is under high demand to become a 24 hour service as it currently operates for 21 hours. This service is operated by specialized volunteers trained on active listening and collaborative problem solving for intervention in suicide crises. The current situation has deteriorated the progress and/or treatment of individuals with mental illnesses. Mental health services are no longer affordable, resulting in an increased demand for funded mental health services, usually provided through non- profits, with long waiting lists and limited resources. Additionally, the purchasing power of individuals has dropped dramatically and rapidly, causing them to view mental health as a luxury while prioritizing basic living supplies and bills. The project intends to increase the mental health clinical capacity to respond to the growing community need and respectively sustain a strong impact, while playing a crucial role in the economic recovery of Lebanon, given the link between mental health and one’s ability to function productively in their community and society. Following Embrace’s mandate, this project intends to increase its inclusivity of communities with disabilities and their access to mental health services. The budget lines that are presented as full costs needed for the time frame of the project and to complete the activities presented. Shared costs are those of human resources that complete tasks relevant to the project activity but also tasks in other programs out of the scope of this project and accordingly not billed here.

project_name: Providing Adequate Water Supply (Quantity, Quality, Access) and Improved Community Sanitation to Vulnerable Communities in Specific Locations
project_objective:
The infrastructure in Syria requires substantial repair and operational support, including training for O&M (Operations and Maintenance) of rehabilitation sites and on-grid electricity supply in areas of high need. The proposed intervention will provide life-saving WASH interventions at both the community and HH levels to increase water supply that is in most cases below the Sphere Standard. Furthermore, Medair’s activities will continue to address community sanitation through appropriate waste management, both of sewage and solid waste. The proposed response will reach vulnerable communities for the next 2 years, an approximate 100,000 beneficiaries, with life-saving interventions through the following interventions. 

 

1. Water Network Rehabilitation 

WASH systems suffered additional damages due to years of functioning at high capacity, lack of maintenance, displacement of technical staff, climate change and poor water resource management. Medair will rehabilitate up to 9 community level water systems. Activities will include: upgrade/installation of water pumping equipment; (re)equipment of wells; generator replacement; repair of water distribution lines; and development of water purification stations. Alongside these activities, Medair will promote water conservation awareness, and teach proper operation and maintenance (O&M) techniques to Water Economic Unit (WEU), the water system operators responsible for systems after they are rehabilitated. Medair will further promote environmental sustainability by identifying water stations that have the capacity and/or need to have solar panels installed. 

  

2. Sewage Network Rehabilitation 

A large portion of sewage is presently discharged untreated and many of the necessary sewage systems are completely non-functional, in disrepair, or nonexistent. In order to address life threatening health risks posed by open sewage, Medair will rehabilitate two sewage networks. The intervention will ensure that waste can be safely transported away from the HH and public spaces and that the systems will continue to be monitored sustainably. This will be done through pipe networks free from both leaks and blockages with the goal of connectivity to the main sewage line. This will prevent further discharge of raw sewage and eliminate associated health risks. 

  

3. Solid Waste Solutions 

Local councils remain ill equipped to appropriately manage solid waste throughout communities in Syria. Due to the lack of waste receptables, solid waste is left in the streets, burnt or buried. Furthermore, the available spaces for dumping are unsuited to the volume and frequently poorly managed which in turn increases vector breeding hazards among other health risks. Medair will provide community-sized solid waste bins for communities where poor solid waste management is identified. 

 

Medair’s proposed intervention will target vulnerable households and communities in Government Controlled areas within Homs, Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor, Idlib, Quneitra or Rural Damascus, Hama, and Ar-Raqqa. At present, Medair has a presence within these areas, subject to approvals and identified needs.

In terms of resilience, Medair will insure the sustainability of all interventions. Also, Medair conducts Operations and Maintenance trainings for operators at the project locations and conducts community awareness for safe water and water conservation. Medair‘s staff meet with the community and local authorities, asking about their highest perceived needs and involving them in the design. Additionally, to enhance resilience, sustainability and to reduce the impact on the environment, each rehabilitated water system will be fitted with solar power as a renewable energy operating modality. Water systems are generally connected to a city power source; however, for situations where this is not the case, a generator will be provided in addition. This combination of power sources should power the water point at all hours.

project_name: Assistance WASH au profit des populations vulnérables du cercle de Douentza
project_objective:
Le cercle de Douentza à l’instar d’autres cercles de la région de Mopti est depuis 2018 en proie à des conflits communautaires avec en corollaire des mouvements de populations. 
Avec un taux d’accès à l’eau potable de 51 %, le cercle de Douentza abrite à son sein 6036  personnes déplacées (3269 femmes et 2767 hommes) et 25 896  personnes retournées (14242 femmes et 11654 hommes). 
Cet afflux de population affecte négativement la vie des ménages car d’une part, il plonge les personnes déplacées et retournées dans une situation de vulnérabilité accrue à travers la limitation de l’accès aux services sociaux de base tels que les vivres, la santé, le WASH, et d’autre part contribue à accroître la vulnérabilité des communautés hôtes du fait l’amenuisement des ressources dû à l’augmentation des besoins.  
La pression sur les infrastructures WASH insuffisantes au regard du taux d’accès à l’eau potable du cercle, contribue également a baissé le taux de fonctionnalité de ces infrastructures qui était de 62% en janvier 2016, affectant davantage l’accès à l’eau potable pour ces populations vulnérables. 
La pratique de la défécation à l’air libre est très répandue au regard du taux d’accès national à l’assainissement en milieu rural qui était de 16 % en 2015. 
La situation nutritionnelle à l‘échelle régionale n’est guère meilleure car avec une prévalence de 8.9% pour la Malnutrition Aiguë Globale (MAG) et 7.3% pour la Malnutrition Aigüe Modérée (MAM), elle est jugée précaire selon le rapport d’enquête SMART 2018 
Au regard de cette situation, le besoin d’une réponse dans le secteur eau, hygiène assainissement pour ces populations est réel car elle permettrait d’améliorer l’accès à la WASH ces populations vulnérables exposées à des risques élevés de maladies liés à l’eau et aux mauvaises pratiques d’hygiène. Le lien entre la malnutrition et les mauvaises conditions d’accès à l’eau potable, d’hygiène et d’assainissement n’étant plus à démontrer, dans un contexte de vulnérabilité accrue, l’intégration WASH et nutrition améliorerait davantage les conditions de vie des populations en particulier des enfants de moins de 5 ans. 
Afin d’avoir plus d’impact, cette réponse ciblera aussi bien la communauté, que les centres de santé et les écoles du cercle de Douentza et visera la réalisation de trois (3) résultats : 
•	L’accès à l’eau et l’assainissement est amélioré dans les communautés, les écoles et les centres de santé.
•	Les connaissances et les pratiques d’hygiène dans les écoles, les centre de santé et dans les communautés sont améliorées.
•	Les capacités des structures de gestion dans la communauté, les écoles et centres de santé et des autorités communales sont renforcées
