project_name: Food security and livelihood support and building resilience capacity of vulnerable households to multifaceted shocks in Jonglei and Upper Nile States
project_objective:
This project proposal aims at improving food security and livelihood options  and building resilience to IPC3+ households in Nyirol, Uror, Ayod, Fangak, Duk, Bor in Jonglei state and Renk, Ulang in Upper Nile state. This will be achieved through FSL cluster objectives CO1: Food assistance, CO2: Emergency food production; and CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs with mainstreaming of COVID-19 prevention protocols, gender, protection, persons with disabilities and climate. The targeted beneficiaries are 13,390 households (80,350 individuals; 24% women, 16% men, 36% girls and 24% boys) consisting of  5,356 hosts communities, 2,009 returnees, 1,071 refugees and 4,954 IDPs. Beneficiary by type will be determined through baseline surveys.
  
Food assistance will be conditional through Food for Assets in Ulang county targeting 3,613 households impacting the lives of  21,680 individuals. 

Food will be enhanced through; 
i) in-kind distribution of crop, vegetable and fishing kits to 9673 households (Ayod 1200, Duk 680, Fangak 640, Nyirol 2433, Uror 2160 and Renk 2560 
ii) Restocking poultry and shoats in Ayod and Duk counties to 500 and 680 households respectively
iii) Livestock support; treatment and vaccination campaigns to 5773 HHs in Ayod (500), Duk (680) Uror(2160) and Nyirol (2433) counties targeting an estimate of 200,000 livestock heads through 120 trained Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) (40 per county)

Resilience building and reducing dependency on food and agricultural inputs aids (CO3) will be realized through 
i) Support to seed fairs using locally sourced seed; seed security & multiplication strengthening/ Support market functionality e.g. assist traders to re-supply markets/ local procurement for FAO ITFs & aggregation of produce for WFP assistance in Renk county targeting 560 seed producer farmers
ii) Support value chain addition to fishery groups and fishery values chain actors in Bor South county targeting 630 
iii) Training & capacity building through farmer/agro-pastoral field schools, demonstration plots vocational training cutting across all the project locations targeting 15% of the total targeted households translating to 2,009 house holds. The trainings will cover good and climate-smart agronomic practices, natural resource management, countering post-harvest losses, sustainable income generation activities, value addition with special emphasis on minimising spread of COVID-19.
iv) Conflict related meetings to strengthen local peace structures also done across the all the targeted project location to promote peace thereby allowing the project participants to fully engage in agricultural activities in safe public spaces without fear of displacement and loosing their produce/harvest through conflict related effects.

Community based participatory approach will be adopted  through Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) committees (consisting of RRC representatives, Boma chiefs, Women leaders, Youth Leaders, County Agricultural Department Representative) and through Project management committees.  Indicators like household status (host, IDP, returnees and refugees), gender markers (targeted male and female) and special/minority groups like Child-headed, Elderly and Female-headed households under IPC 3+ will be screened before approval of the beneficiary list. 

Continuous monitoring will be done throughout the project cycles to ensure quality project outcomes are realised within the allocated timeframe. Community representative committees (AAPs and PMCs) and donors  will take part in the monitoring process and also act as a platform for complaint-feedback mechanisms. These feedback will be included in the implementation and project designs where applicable.

Sustainability of the project will be realised through active involvement of the community stakeholders through out the project cycle making them adopt and propagate the knowledge acquired.

project_name: Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Ayod, Uror, Duk, Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States.
project_objective:
This CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2022 seeks to provide inclusive, protective and effective education services to accelerate learning recovery and make schools more equitable, efficient and resilient for 7, 339 (3, 302 girls) school-aged children, 250 (50 female) teachers, 275 (82 female) PTA members and 60 (10 female) local education officials in 6 Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States by building on investments made during the Pandemic and previous years of EiE programming in South Sudan.

The expected results are equalised participation and improved learning outcomes across gender and disability for 7, 339 (45% female) children and youth through provision of essential school facilities and supplies, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics in 25 target schools (5 ECD centers, 15 primary schools, and 5 secondary schools) in Ayod, Uror & Duk Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State respectively. These 7, 339 children (5-17) and 250 teachers will be provided with teaching and learning materials in the form of 10 ECD learner kits, 250 learner kits for primary and 10 learner kits for secondary schools. 250 recreational kits will be provided to enhance learning and play and psychosocial wellbeing during schooling.

For their protective and safe school environment, 30 temporary learning spaces will be established in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019; and 30 gender segregated latrines and 30 water points in line with INEE and sphere standards. (unit of measurement: 1:60 for boys, 1:30 for girls). CMD will distribute 95 (500-litre) plastic water tanks with taps, 95 (50-litre) hand-washing tanks with taps and on their metal stands; 285 (1-litre) liquid sanitisers, 190 cartons of toilet soap, 95 bags (20 kgs) of detergent/powder soap, 95, 000 face masks, and 375 pairs of gumboots to provide sanitation and PPE for students and teachers. 2, 000 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits and undergo MHM sessions to better enhance their self-esteem and school attendance.

The plan targets 2, 339 (935 girls & 1, 404 boys) children in Ayod; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Uror; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Duk; 1, 000(400 girls & 600 boys) in Ulang; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Nasir; and 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Longechuk. 50 (10 female) teachers in Ayod; 40 (10 female) in Uror; 40 (10 female) in Duk; 40 (10 female) in Ulang; 40 (5 female) in Nasir; and 40 (5 female) in Longechuk will benefit from active EiE pedagogy that is centered on children and adolescents and their full development, and that responds to school needs and favours the equitable achievement of learning goals. These teachers will Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Equally important, 75 (27 female) PTA members in Ayod; 40 (11 female) in Uror; 40 (11 female) in Duk; 40(11female) in Ulang; 40(11 female) in Nasir; and 40 (11 female) in Longechuk and 10 (1 female) education officials in Ayod, 10 (1) in Uror; 10 (1) in Duk; 10(1) in Ulang; 10(1) in Nassir; and 10 (1 female) in Longechuk will be trained in School Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction in Education (DRR).

CMD will also conduct 12 Back to Learning (BTL) campaigns through public information campaigns intended for the entire affected population and/or awareness raising activities aimed at specific segments of the out-of-schoolchildren (OOSC) as well as current learners identified as most at-risk.

project_name: Provision of emergency and integrated nutrition services to vulnerable communities in Ayod, Akobo West, and Bor South counties .
project_objective:
This project proposes provision of timely and quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition through a full CMAM package of services for the most vulnerable children Under 5, pregnant and lactating women. 

The project will to reduce morbidity and mortality rate for the IPC 3 and 4 populations in line with CMAM Protocol through detection and treatment of children under 5 reaching at least 2,329 children with SAM, 11,962 with moderate acute malnutrition and 10,290 malnourished PLW. 

CMD will establish 6 nutrition sites to including at 4 outreach island locations through outpatient Therapeutic Program(OTP) for SAM children as well as Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program(TSFP) for MAM children and PLW. SAM Children with medical complication will be referred to existing stabilisation centres (SCs). At the community level, Community Nutrition Volunteers will conduct active case finding to strengthen early detection and timely referral of malnourished children and PLW,Both through routine community screening and family MUAC Approach.All children(6-59M) with SAM without medical complications who are enrolled in OTP program will be tested for malaria as per the national CMAM guidelines and those tested positive will be treated.The nutrition staff at the outreach will  be trained on national CMAM guidelines.
2. Prevention of malnutrition in children under 5 and PLW through promotion of MIYCN,Health,WASH and appropriate feeding and care practices through sensitisation sessions at the nutrition sites and as well community  sensitisation. All mothers/caregivers will be counselled.The staff at the outreach sites as well as CNV's will be trained on the national MIYCN guidelines.
Mother to Mother Support Groups(MtMSGs) will be formed and trained.To meet immediate food security needs,MTMSGs will also conduct sensitive cooking demonstrations as well as kitchen gardening activities.Led by male staff, men Group Discussions will be formed and initiate a dialogue around crucial nutrition specific and nutrition sensitive topics and gender issues(esp.MIYCN,GBV), enable women's  access to services, and safety promote gender equality through encouraging mutual support between gender groups.Safety audits will be conducted at all nutrition sites and outreach sites at least once during the project period using the tool endorsed by the nutrition cluster.A standard Feedback  and Complaints Mechanism(FCM) will be conducted across the sites to understand the concerns of the beneficiaries and collect information on how continue improving the program activities.The community activities will be carried out using other funding source.
CMD will work closely with Nutrition cluster and other partners/actors on ground implementing other interventions such as WASH,Health,NFI's and Food Security and Livelihood to address the emergency nutrition needs of the targeted population.

project_name: Improve access to essential health care services for women, men, girls, boys including persons with disabilities of the host communities and IDPs in Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria states through static health facilities, mobile outreaches and community based case management approaches
project_objective: Two years after formation of Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity, humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains dire. Weak health system, recurrent inter-communal violence, devastating floods and global effect of COVID-19 continuously hamper timely access to equitable and affordable health care services. Such situation continues to increase vulnerability, hence high risk of disease outbreaks, low immunization coverage, poor hygiene and sanitation practices in crowding settlements, and therefore a likelihood of humanitarian catastrophe in 2022. In UNICEF`s humanitarian situation report No. 164, 2021, 1.4 million children faced life-threatening acute malnutrition, whilst approximately 7.2 million people were at risk of hunger largely driven by the impact of floods and displacement in 2021. Malnutrition rate extremely high with GAM rate of over 15%, of emergency threshold and Jonglei state reported the highest admission of SAM admission of 24%. According to health cluster`s response plan 2022, only 8% of the health facilities in the country provide full package of BPHNS and 53% moderately functional. Maternal mortality is one of the highest in the world, with 789 per 100,000 live births. 39% women have access to recommended Four Antenatal Care Services during pregnancy, institutionalized delivery as well as skilled birth attendance low at 12.3% and 14.7% respectively. According to health cluster`s response plan 2022, Ayod is among the counties at health severity level5, with over 20K population at Catastrophic phase. For the past 15 years, CMD has been implementing multi-sectoral humanitarian interventions in Upper Nile Region specially Jongeli and Upper Nile states & GPAA. Capitalizing on its vast knowledge of local context and collaborative partnership with local authorities, community and other humanitarian actors, CMD aims to implement this project in Ayod, and Kapoeta North counties. The project will directly target 20,000 host communities & IDPs of which 9,600 will be males and 10,400 will be females including 4,000 boys and girls of under5 year old and 800 pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Among the target groups will be 1,440 male and 1,560 female Persons With Disabilities (PWD). The model of implementation shall be through thirteen static sites, five mobile clinics and the support to community-based case management using an estimated cost of $600K in 2022. Activities include essential life-saving health services, disease prevention, detection, surveillance & reporting, strengthening RI & NIDs, disease outbreaks & NTDs. For quality of care, BEmONCs/CEmONCs with institutionalized Skilled Birth Attendance 80% live births. 800 pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) receive the recommended FOUR ANC visits & 100% SGBV survivors who report to health facilities receive CMR and basic psychosocial support services. Deploy qualified health cadres to maintain and continuously improve quality of care to mothers of childbearing age, children & persons with disabilities. Construction and rehabilitation of health facilities. Beneficiaries` involvement and capacity building of CHDs. Inter-sectoral synergies with WASH, Protection/GBV, FSL and Nutrition. Use EWARS and weekly IDSR system of reporting to monitor trends of morbidities and outbreaks. Utilize HMIS and other internally improvised reporting tools to ensure data quality and consistency. Obtain beneficiaries` feedback through existing community networks; organize FGDs and installing suggestion boxes in health facilities and CMD offices sub-nationally.

project_name: Emergency WASH support to vulnerable communities in Jonglei and  Upper Nile states.
project_objective:
Chronic WASH needs continue to emerge in parts of Greater Upper Nile States, which are likely to be exacerbated by unprecedented flood waters, COVID 19 restrictions, food insecurity as well as logistical challenges. Provision of adequate WASH services is key to achieving sustainable solutions to communities in emergency. CMD, a national NGO working in the locations of Jonglei and Upper Nile state envisages a targeted response aimed at reaching internally displaced persons, returnees and vulnerable host communities with water, sanitation and hygiene services, integrated with nutrition and protection/ GBV programming. Spanning a period of 12 months, the project targets the locations of Ayod, Duk, Fangak,
Bor South, Nyirol, Twic East and Pibor (Jonglei), Ulang (Upper Nile) with WASH temporary and sustainable services, to address the vital needs, public health and protection/GBV issues. 
The response aims at reducing levels of chronic malnutrition especially amongst children, pregnant and lactating women, mitigating WASH related GBV by providing gender appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities and tackling issues surrounding gender, safety and WASH. Persistence of food insecurity, signalled by high GAM rates, with <5s and PLW mainly affected will be mitigated by the provision of WASH in Nutrition services, through targeted WASH minimum packages at OTP/SC mainly for mother/caretaker – malnourished children. 
Water related disease outbreaks have been traced to health facilities and community infrastructures/settings without adequate WASH facilities.

project_name: Réponse intégrée en urgence en Santé Nutrition Wash et protection en faveur des populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions de l’Est et du Sahel, Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le présent projet apporte son appui à la continuité de la provision des services essentiels et vitaux en santé ainsi qu’au continuum de soins dans les districts sanitaires Fada, Gayeri, Bogandé, Manni dans la région de l’Est, de Dori et de Sebba dans la région du sahel au Burkina Faso.

- Supporter le rétablissement de l’offre du Paquet Minimum d’Activité de qualité en santé primaire et nutrition : 
Dans le but de soutenir ces CSPS sous pression, PUI appuiera en médicaments essentiels génériques (MEG) pour pallier aux ruptures et en matériels essentiels pour assurer leur fonctionnement. Cela contribuera aussi au maintien de la gratuité pour les populations cibles selon la politique nationale (enfants de moins de 5 ans, femmes enceintes et allaitantes). 
En plus de cet appui, PUI renforcera les capacités du personnel de santé, personnel ASBC, AV et membres des COGES sur les thématiques en santé-nutrition et protection.

- Rétablir un accès significatif aux services de santé  et psychosociaux essentiels et vitaux pour les populations déplacées : 
PUI  déploiera une Clinique Mobile (CM) permettant de restaurer l’accès physique et financier des populations non desservies. 
La CM sera une modalité de réponse à l’urgence afin de répondre aux chocs soudains selon la procédure opérationnelle standard développée par PUI pour la santé : 
-	Déploiement de la clinique mobile pour une durée de 4 semaines au maximum ;
-	Mise en place d’une poste de soins avancé au-delà de 4 semaines et pour un maximum de 3 mois ;
-	Renfort des CSPS non accessibles ou surchargés, en ressources humaines et intrants ou support.

- Appuyer le système de référencement des urgences vitales depuis les CSPS vers le niveau secondaire:
PUI soutiendra la prise en charge des urgences vitales dans les niveaux de référence. Les frais de transport et hospitalisation ainsi que des examens des malades référencés seront pris en charge par PUI pour les cas d’urgences vitales maternelles, infantiles et autres personnes vulnérables à travers des modalités remboursement des frais par transfert et ou payement direct. 

- L’accent mis en matière de protection :
La présente action se focalisera sur la PEC médicale des cas de VBG mais aussi l’accompagnement psychosocial selon les besoins spécifiques du bénéficiaire. 
A tous les niveaux de la pyramide sanitaire, les agents seront formés à l’identification, au soutien et à l’orientation des victimes de VGB et autres cas de protection. 

- Redynamisation et implication des acteurs communautaires dans la mise en œuvre de l’action :
PUI prévoit une forte implication des acteurs communautaires dans le développement de ce projet à travers:
	Le support à la provision du paquet de soins essentiels communautaire (SEC) par le renforcement de capacité, l’accompagnement, l’équipement en matériel et médicaments ainsi que des primes mensuels des ASBC et des AV exerçant dans les zones de couverture des DS soutenus. 
	Le renforcement de capacité et des ressources des comités de gestion communautaire des CSPS (COGES), 
Les activités a haut impact seront spécifiquement ciblées : prise en charge intégrée des maladie de l’enfant (PCIME-C), prise en charge intégrée de la malnutrition aigues (PCIMA-C hors traitement) et promotion des bonne pratique de l’alimentation de la mère et de l’enfant (ANJE et démonstration culinaire), prévention de la mortalité materno infantile (soins essentiels lors de l’accouchement et accouchement propre).

- Renforcement du système de santé à répondre aux pics épidémiques :
En collaboration avec l’équipe des DS appuyés, PUI appuiera les FOSA dans l’objectif d’augmenter la capacité du système de soins à répondre aux alertes épidémiques et sanitaires. Les personnels de première ligne seront formés ou recyclés sur la surveillance intégrée de la maladie et la riposte (SIMR/RSI), et les plans de contingences au niveau du district et des formations sanitaires seront redynamisés, en particulier le système d’alerte et de réponse

project_name: Amélioration de l'accès aux services WASH pour les IDPs, Retournés et populations hôtes vulnérables dans le département du Logone et Chari, Extrême-Nord Cameroun
project_objective:
Le présent projet vise à améliorer l’accès aux services WASH pour les IDPs et les populations hôtes du Département du Logone et Chari en répondant aux besoins exprimés par les bénéficiaires.
Pour répondre à ces besoins, le projet va :
- Améliorer l'accès à l'eau potable;
- Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques WASH.
A l’issue de la construction des ouvrages, et de la réhabilitation des points d'eau, un comité composé d’hommes et de femmes sera mis en place afin d’assurer la bonne gestion de chaque ouvrage.
Les activités de promotion de bonnes pratiques WASH seront conduites dans les communautés par des Relais Communautaires.
Les membres de la communauté vont identifier des hommes et des femmes volontaires qui seront formés et équipés en qualité de Relais Communautaires.
Sous l’accompagnement des Facilitateurs du projet, les Relais Communautaires ainsi formés vont conduire les séances de sensibilisation, démonstrations pratiques, ... afin que chaque ménage parvienne à construire une latrine familiale selon la méthode ATPC ou PHAST, et que les hommes, les femmes, les garçons et les filles adoptent les bonnes pratiques WASH telle que le lavage correct des mains, l’utilisation et l'entretien des latrines ou la potabilisation de l'eau à domicile.
En raison des difficultés particulières que rencontrent les femmes chefs de ménages à disposer des revenus, un appui matériel et technique leur sera fourni pour la construction des latrines.
La conduite des activités identifiées va globalement améliorer la santé, les conditions de vie et l’épanouissement des hommes, des femmes, des jeunes filles, et des jeunes garçons.
Les risques d’agressions sexuelles et autres violences basées sur le genre pour les jeunes filles et les femmes seront réduits. 
Les contraintes liées au puisage de l’eau et les maladies hydriques récurrentes seront réduites, ce qui permettra aux jeunes filles et jeunes garçons en âge scolaire de jouir de leur droit à l’éducation sans entrave.
Le présent projet sera réalisé par un consortium de 02 organisations Nationales (ASOL, et AAEDC)
Les activités du projets seront supervisées et coordonnées par les délégués régionaux du Ministère de la Santé et du Ministère de l’Eau et de l’Énergie. Elles s’intégreront dans le plan de développement des Communes du Logone et Chari et contribueront à la mise en œuvre du PND 2030 et à l’atteinte des ODD.
Les Relais Communautaires seront également chargé de:
- La collecte et de la transmission des données statistiques;
- L'enregistrement et la transmission des plaintes ou de la satisfaction des bénéficiaires.

project_name: Anglophone Crisis Emergency Response (ACER) II
project_objective:
CRS and its partner, the Archdiocese of Bamenda, is implementing a 12-month project to meet immediate humanitarian needs and improve food insecurity resulting from the Anglophone Crisis in the Northwest (NW) Region in Cameroon. The Anglophone Crisis Emergency Response II (ACER II) will provide food rations and non-food items (NFIs) through electronic vouchers (e-vouchers) on CRS’ Cash and Asset Transfer (CAT) Platform to vulnerable displaced and host community households in Mezam and Momo Divisions. 

ACER II will reach 18,900 individuals in 2,700 HH from April 2021 through March 2022 by providing e-vouchers for food and NFIs. Providing e-vouchers for food under the Food Assistance Sector will directly address people’s barriers to accessing and consuming sufficient, diverse diets to improve food security.

The project will reach vulnerable displaced and host community households living in existing urban and peri-urban communities as well as informal settlements in the intervention area.

Community and vulnerable groups' representatives will actively participate in all activities, including targeting and sensitization exercises. Community input and feedback will be central in gauging the appropriateness of the program strategy; feedback will be used for programmatic decisions, such as changing the frequency or timing of transfers, setting price ceilings and changing the food and NFI baskets. Community participation will be ensured through the Feedback and response mechanism and regular analysis of incoming data, community and individual consultations including focus group discussions, phone interviews, or through M&E activities including Onsite and post distribution monitoring.

project_name: Supporting crisis-affected populations in Far-North region through the provision of multi-sectoral assistance in Cameroon
project_objective:
Following the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach that IOM strongly supports and actively promotes in Cameroon, and building on the programmes and activities implemented in the recent years, IOM plans interventions for 2022 along two main axis; humanitarian emergency response and promotion of peace and development. Humanitarian emergency response will focus on coordination, protection, shelter and health interventions, while HDPN focus will be strengthened through early recovery  interventions. IOM Cameroon will mainstream protection in all its proposed programmes.
IOM’s multisectoral response in the Far-North will be composed of the following activities:

Coordination Sector
Contributing to the overall highest level of humanitarian coordination in the Far-North by sharing timely and accurate information on displacement figures and trends, IOM plans to:
-	Conduct regular Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNAs) in coordination with humanitarian sectors and OCHA.
-	Conduct mobility tracking rounds to track the trends of displaced populations within crisis areas. 
-	Produce and distribute regular IOM emergency tracking tool (ETT) dashboards, that present reliable and up-to-date information on the sudden displacements events, triggers, trends, needs with the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) and other humanitarian actors.  
-	Collect information on multi-sectoral indicators of stability within crisis areas in order to help facilitate geographic targeting and strategic planning for transition and recovery programming.  
-	Collect information on the return intentions for displaced populations in crisis areas. 
-	Support local humanitarian actors’ coordination platform (CHOI) for the conduct and supervision of an MSNA in the Center region. 

Shelter/Non-Food Item (NFI) Sector 
IOM plans to work closely with the Shelter/NFI Cluster in the Far-North to provide a range of different shelter solutions to displaced populations, with specific interventions including:
-	Distribution of 2,000 emergency shelter kits to populations who have been recently displaced and are in need of quick assistance to meet their basic needs, with technical support to a proportion of beneficiaries for their construction.  
-	Distribution of 500 transitional shelters to protractedly displaced populations that are expected to be in need of a shelter solution for more than six months, with technical support to a proportion of beneficiaries for their construction including through the development of information, education and communication (IEC) materials.
-	Usage of cash-based modalities to respond to the needs of displaced populations (200 households) who are based in urban and peri-urban areas that are renting shelters. 
-	Distribution of 2,500 NFI kits including basic household and cooking items, but also emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene items. 

Health sector
IOM aims to bolster the well-being of crisis-affected populations through the implementation of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) activities. Actions will be tailored to the age and gender of beneficiaries and will include:
-	Further needs assessment to understand the key challenges, psychosocial needs of different groups and opportunities to MHPSS services in crisis affected areas. 
-	Capacity building for existing MHPSS structures on topics such as Psychological First Aid (PFA), basic MHPSS, knowledge of referral pathways. 
-	The strengthening or establishing of safe spaces for women, children and youth.
-	Provide direct MHPSS interventions such as socio-relational activities (e.g., sport and play activities, creative and art-based activities, non-formal education) through the deployment of a multidisciplinary psychosocial mobile team (PMT.
-	Continue co-leading the MHPSS working group in Far-North with the holding of monthly meetings.

Early recovery sector
-	Ensure targeted displaced communities have increased opportunities for inclusive and participatory dialogue.

project_name: Response in support of essential public health needs during the emergency caused by the impact of Hurricane Ian in the provinces of Pinar del Río and Artemisa.
project_objective:
Protecting public health and facilitating access to health services:
• Restore operation of affected health services.
• Ensure access to and adequate care for patients in health services and surveillance of 
infectious diseases transmitted by water, food and vectors, among others. 
• Facilitate education, information and communication for health promotion and disease 
prevention, as well as psychological and psychosocial support actions.

project_name: Restoration of basic habitation/shelter
project_objective:
Restoration of basic habitation/shelter for affected families, prioritizing people with vulnerabilities
whose homes were affected, in the 7 most affected municipalities of the Pinar del Río province.

project_name: Integrated Assistance to Vulnerable Populations in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The proposal is aligned with the overall Food Security, Nutrition, and WASH sectors strategies as defined in the Humanitarian Response Plan 2021. The action is designed to run for 12 months
To deliver on the food security component of this muli-sectoral proposed interventions, Caritas Nigeira will provide wet-feeding to newly arrived refugee returnees and IDPs across border communities/camps in Banki, Bama and Gwoza; and provide energy energy for cooking to vulnerable households not yet reached across Banki, Bama, Gwoza and Konduga LGAs of Borno State. 
The nutrition component will contribute to a reduction of morbidity and mortality caused by malnutrition amongst children under 5 years of age through treatment of SAM with medical complications at stabilisation centers in Hong and Gombi LGAs of Adamawa State: and the prevention of acute malnutrition through screening, identification, referral to the OTP centers, and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP) across Kaga, Konduga, Bama LGAs in Borno State and Mubi North, Gombi and Hong LGAs in Adamawa State. It will also ensure promotion of infant and young child feeding practices amongst pregnant and lactating women (PLW) to prevent malnutrition in the target LGAs. We will form support groups (MTMSG and FTFSG) where they do not exist and strengthen already formed ones where they are weak. Caregivers will be reached with health talk and IYCF Counselling in addition to food demonstration sessions. The programme will also support caregivers of children with SAM who have medical complications to receive a one-off cash transfer for immediate food needs. We will ensure enhanced needs analysis of the nutrition situation and enhanced monitoring and coordination of response. The nutrition programme will also focus on capacity building for staff in government health facilities through on-the-job training, as well as through participation in formal training and courses. Our primary focus is to provide training on Integrated Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition, which promotes the identification and treatment of SAM in line with the Government of Nigeria ministry of health (MoH) guidelines and SPHERE standards.
The WASH component will target host communities, IDP camps, schools, and health facilities, in order to reach the most vulnerable populations in need of WASH across Mubi North, Mubi South, Girei LGAs in Adamawa State and Kaga, Konduga,and Gwoza LGAs in Borno State; through the provision of solar boreholes powered by climate smart energy sources, construction of new ventilated improved pit (VIP) latrine and renovation of damaged ones, construction of new bath showers, distribution of menstrual hygiene management (MHM) and Dignity kits that are reusable to young girls and women of reproductive age, regular Hygiene promotion messaging, distribution of water treatment tablets (Aquatabs), distribution of Cholera Preparedness Kits, procurement of hand wash stations to be placed in strategic public places, including VIP latrines, and training of the beneficiaries on solid waste management. The intervention will complement other ongoing emergency/recovery programmes in the target locations using the SPHERE standards. 
For sustainability, various groups within target communities will be trained on the use locally available food items to prepare nutritious meals as well as on nutrition sensitive agriculture (home gardening). These will help to stem future malnutrition among infants, young children; WASHCOMMS will be formed, trained and strengthened to handle minor repairs and linked to Local Area Mechanics (LAMs) and technicians of solar panels and boreholes. This will help them to know where to go to in case of breakdown that the WASHCOMM cannot handle.

project_name: Mine Action in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The HALO Trust will continue to deliver an integrated Mine Action approach in northwest Syria involving Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD), Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Victim Assistance (VA), delivered both directly and through implementing partners.

HALO and its implementing partners will provide EORE to men, women, boys and girls, with a focus on community members most at risk of accidents (including children, teenagers, IDPs, agricultural workers and rubble removal workers). HALO will also continue delivering ‘Training of Trainer’ (ToT) workshops to NGO workers and Community Focal Points to improve the relevance, integration and reach of EORE messaging across all communities and relevant humanitarian sectors. Incorporation of COVID-19 messaging to EORE sessions will continue and COVID hygiene measures will be observed.

Following the completion in 2020 of HALO's contamination impact survey work in all accessible communities in NW Syria, capturing the scope of explosive ordnance (EO) contamination in the region, in 2022 HALO is conducting detailed non-technical survey to define precisely the types of hazards and technical requirements for disposal. This will enable the training, equipping and deployment of a clearance and disposal capacity to reduce the presence and impact of EO in highly vulnerable communities in a part of the country where HALO is the only INGO able to provide these highly specialised services supported by a sector-leading global EOD advisory team. NTS also provides local authorities, humanitarian actors, the Gaziantep cluster network, and the donor community with a greater understanding of EO threats, including specific locations.

Through its Turkish implementing partner, iMFAD (Turkey's only humanitarian demining NGO)  HALO will also conduct Mine Action activities as and where authorised in accessible districts of Turkish-administered northern Aleppo, including Afrin.

The support to survivors of EO accidents will continue through a Victim Assistance (VA) component implemented by HALO and its partners. This will include the provision of prosthetics and orthotics, physiotherapy, nursing, psychosocial services and multi-purpose assistance delivered by rehabilitation centres. HALO and its partners will also provide victim assistance case management services, providing referrals to specialised services for survivors of EO accidents.

HALO acknowledges the requirement to avoid activity duplication within the MASC as well as addressing gaps in providing EORE (to children, adults, CFPs, and NGO Focal Points), NTS and EOD. This will be achieved through ongoing and regular coordination with other members of the MASC, as well as engagement with local authorities, communities, and other NGOs throughout the implementation of the project. Both HALO and its implementing partners are active members of the MASC (of which HALO is co-chair) and regularly submit 4Ws to the cluster.

project_name: Addressing Critical Nutrition life saving needs of Displaced Populations and their host communities in 10 prioritized and targeted woredas of Tigray, Afar and Oromia Regions.
project_objective:
This project proposed in response to the increasing humanitarian needs among IDPs and their host
community in Tigray, Afar and Oromia regions, the project aims to decrease morbidity and mortality
among conflict and drought affected and displaced girls, boys, women and men in 10 targeted woredas
of Tigray, Afar and Oromia Regions. It will do so through immediate and short-term emergency Nutrition
assistance. The Child Protection and key WASH component is mainstreamed throughout the various
outcomes of the project.
This project primarily focuses on providing life-saving treatment, care and support to affected and
displaced girls, boys, women and men in general as well as for 0-59 months age girls and boys
suffering from communicable diseases such as Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) or Moderate Acute
Malnutrition (MAM), Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) as well as Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW)
suffering from MAM. The project will also strengthen further the local health system and build the
capacity of health workers (HWs) and health extension workers (HEWs) to respond for already doubled
primary health care and nutrition services in all targeted intervention woredas. Besides, the project
strongly work with district health offices in maximizing best practices of IYCF including positive
parenting and Mental Health and Psychosocial Supports (MHPS) throughout the implementation period
of this project. Also, survivals of Gender Base Violence (SGBV) and person with disability specifically
targeted to get appropriate and adequate health and care support from this project. In addition
protection concerns considered to be addressed through mainstream approach in each of planned
activities of the project.
Furthermore, to prevent disease outbreaks and deter underlying factors for the anticipated increased
Acute Malnutrition admission trend, PIE will increases awareness of targeted girls, boys, women and
men on key recommended hygiene practices tailored with COVID-19 prevention measures.
Beneficiary feedback and compliant will be also addressed through establishing and functioning strong
feedback mechanism at each kebeles of targeted intervention woredas. Beneficiary participation will be
further strengthened through ensuring participation of beneficiaries during project start-up workshop,
beneficiary selection, distribution of project input, project review meeting and Focus Group Discussions

project_name: LEARN III & IV - Reduce WASH related morbidity, mortality and public health risk  for conflict-affected populations.
project_objective:
The goal of the proposed intervention is to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve the 
living conditions, resilience and dignity of affected populations in North-East Syria (NES).
This aligns with BHA’s mission by providing multi-sectoral emergency and early recovery 
support to vulnerable people affected by the complex and protracted crisis in NES. The 
integrated approach taken by LEARN in Phase III utilizes and builds on local assets and 
capacities, mitigating the impact of current and potential future shocks. As well as contributing
to immediate lifesaving outcomes, this intervention lays the foundation for recovery at household 
and community levels. 
LEARN III also contributes to the three key objectives of the 2020 UN Humanitarian Response 
Plan (the most recent validated version at the time of writing): 
1. Save lives and alleviate the suffering of the most vulnerable people
2. Enhance the prevention, mitigation and response to protection needs
3. Increase resilience, livelihoods and access to basic services 
These objectives are interlinked and interdependent, meeting acute humanitarian needs while 
also building capacity and resilience in target communities; this holistic approach is reflected in 
the design of LEARN Phase III. 
Theory of Change
If the interlinked economic, health, shelter and WASH needs of conflict-affected populations are 
safely met, then beneficiaries will experience improvements in physical, social and mental health 
and wellbeing, will be better protected, and will be more able to increase their resilience, develop 
positive coping strategies and thrive.
Purposes
As this intervention takes a holistic approach, all sectors are interlinked. For the sake of 
simplicity and transparency, one multi-sectoral purpose is given here, and others are shown in 
their respective sectors.
WASH: Reduce WASH related morbidity, mortality and public health risk for 110,514 people 
(47,747 IDPs) from conflict-affected populations.

LEARN will:
Support solid waste management in conjunction with local authorities and communities.
Rehabilitate water and sanitation infrastructure, while also building the capacity of water 
departments and communities for ongoing maintenance.
Provide appropriate toileting and bathing facilities in collective centers and informal 
settlements (this will also be part of private shelter repairs in the Shelter section), considering 
gender, age and disability.
Provide community-level WASH messaging, including solid waste management, hygiene 
practices (including handwashing, menstrual hygiene management and COVID-19 prevention), 
latrine usage and cleaning, and safe water storage and use.
Distribute essential hygiene materials, again appropriate for age, gender and disability.

project_objective:
Over 85 percent of people in Ethiopia rely on agriculture and livestock for their livelihoods and are consequently heavily dependent on seasonal rainfalls, recurrent droughts are critical drivers of food insecurity and related protection risks for millions of people. The food security situation in Borena zones of Oromia Region continues to deteriorate following the poor performance of 2021 Genna  rains , resulting in severe harvest losses, poor livestock performance, and livestock death, household famine, an alarmingly increasing rate of malnutrition, and limited feed and water availability, resulting in reduced milk and meat, low livestock prices, which have contributed to rising food insecurity and malnutrition rates among livestock dependent households .  Furthermore, on October 5, 2021, OCHA flash update report revealed that, 71 percent of harvest loss has been reported in Borena  Zone and resulting in over 30 percent of the total population need of emergency food assistance. Most of the water sources in the zone have all dried up. In the last three months, malnutrition cases in the zone are showing an upward trend and according to the MUAC readings, children under five years and pregnant and lactating women are at risk. This can be attributed to a lack of consumption of milk and an imbalanced diet. Household milk availability has significantly decreased. The household food security situation has been significantly compromised and pastoralists who have very limited purchasing power are relying on market purchases to get food. 
ACF in coordination with the Borena Zone Pastoral Development Office (PDO) and Disaster Risk Management Office will respond to drought-affected areas. Based on The Livestock Emergency Guidelines and Standards (LEGS), ACF will closely work with pastoralists to target inputs for livestock protection based on existing local strategies.

Emergency medication preventing diseases in livestock populations during emergencies and rainy season, which will cover infectious diseases such as anthrax, clostridial diseases, pasteurellosis, deworming tablets, Newcastle diseases, and other treatments as needed will be conducted. This activity will be handled in collaboration with Zonal and Woreda Animal Production and Veterinary Office. Animal Health Technicians and Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWS) will provide the treatment for the livestock and  faclitate Animal feed  disturbution .

project_name: Integrated Multi-AoR protection services for high at risk groups in Jebel Saman, Aleppo
project_objective:
The intervention is part of a project aiming at securing the basic needs and providing integrated community-based protection activities in Karm Jazmati, Seken Shebebi, Karm al Tarrab, and Dahret Awwad. The project is held by Caritas Germany (CG), back-funded by the German Federal Foreign Ministry (GFO) and implemented from 01.04.2019 -31.12.2022 by Caritas Syria (CS). 
The protection activities carried out under this project have been regularly aligned to the protection sector strategy. In the 2019 established community center in Karm al Jazmati, integrated community-based protection services are offered to residents in Jazmati, Seken Shebebi, Karm al Tarrab, and Dahret Awwad. 
The center follows an open-door policy, ensuring the active engagement of the community, allowing real-time evaluations and timely adjustments of activities as per beneficiaries’ feedback. In response to the feedback collected from beneficiaries, i.e. via PDMs, satisfaction surveys, and FGDs, and following the strategy of the protection sector, the activities are regularly adjusted to the actual needs, or new activities are included.
In 2022, women are provided with courses aiming to prevent GBV, such as literacy. Boys and girls in school age are provided PSS and interactive learning courses accompanying them throughout the school year. Women, men, and children receive a consecutive and tailored package of protection-related awareness sessions. Boys and girls 14-17 years old will participate in community initiatives. Further, socially isolated elderly are visited in their homes by the trained CS elderly team at least once a month, following up on their psychosocial needs as well as aiming to re(establish) relationships in the community. Women are invited to participate in PSS group sessions. In case mothers of young children are participating, the CS team has established a CFS in the center to take care of the children while the mothers are attending courses. In addition, capacity strengthening activities for the CS team will be offered to further increase the responding capacity of CS.
The target groups are selected interconnectedly, aiming for greater impact within the families and, in turns, the entire community: For example, the husbands or adult sons of women participating in the awareness, PSS or GBV prevention sessions, are invited to FDGs to assess their interest and needs in men’s awareness sessions. The parents of children coming to the center are actively addressed and invited either to participate in one of the protection services or for regular follow-up regarding their children. With a newly established safe referral policy, CS aims to enhance their assistance to cases that need other or more specialized support. 
Following a participatory approach, the needs have been regularly assessed, i.e., via PDMs applying a proportional piling method, and FDGs. Furthermore, a robust FCM has contributed to ensure the engagement and thus self-identification of the needs in the community. Hence, throughout the project lifetime, the engagement of all community members has been promoted, establishing a two-way communication with the community. This has ensured a timely incorporation of community feedback.
The regular coordination with the Aleppo-based sub-sectors Protection, CP, GBV, and FSL, CS ensures alignment of its protection activities while avoiding duplication of efforts. The community center in Jazmati has been well received by the residents of Jazmati since its opening in 2019 and continues to be the central point for the provision of integrated community-based protection services, to women, adolescent girls, children, men and elderly.

project_name: Unconditional in-kind and cash food assistance to 115,000 vulnerable Refugees and Internally Displaced People in the Far North Region
project_objective:
Through the project WFP will provided unconditional food support to 115,000 Nigerian refugees, IDPs in the Far North region including 5,000 contingency caseloads. In line with WFP Cameroon Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2022-2026), life-saving assistance will be provided Nigerian refugees in Minawao camp and IDPs that are located in Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari Divisions. Food assistance through in-kind and cash-based transfers will be provided to 73,000 Nigerian refugees, and 27,000 IDPs. The displaced that moved from their villages located Nigeria that were established in Minawao camp for the refugees IDPs that fled from the border villages with Nigeria and that sought safer places within Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga and Logone and Chari Divisions. A 10-month food assistance to the beneficiaries will be delivered through monthly unconditional in-kind food transfer to 100,000 beneficiaries. The full ration of the in-kind distributions will provide 2,100 kcal energy per day per person for the beneficiaries who entirely rely on humanitarian food assistance. Daily in-kind ration are 370g for cereals. 120g for pulses, 40g for vegetable oil and 5 g for iodized salt. 
Cash transfers will be provided to 15,000 IDPs with a monthly ration of 8,500 XAF per beneficiary to support them to access adequate and nutritious food. A 10-month full ration assistance will contribute to prevent the IDPs from adopting negative coping strategies during the farming period.
For the conception of projects, beneficiaries’ opinions have been considered through focus group discussions, gender and protection evaluation field missions, monitoring exercises. These gave beneficiaries opportunities to state their preferences and transfer modalities and opinions on targeting criteria. The preparatory activities are inclusive, WFP ensures that women, men, girls and boys are involved in various stages such as vulnerability targeting process, for in-kind and cash transfers and monitoring. WFP in collaboration with local authorities and partners, conduct assessments to identify IDPs to be considered for assistance based on WFP vulnerability criteria. These criteria included among others household size, presence of under-5 children, the elderly and handicapped, women-headed households, assets.
After distributions monitoring will be conducted through Cooperating Partners and attention will placed on the role played by men, women, girls and boys including decision-making on food consumption and food security in the household.
Through the established complaints and feedback mechanisms, beneficiary IDPs will freely express their views and concerns on the project implementation. Their views will be considered for project adjustment. Through sensitization, WFP will promote women and men equal participation in decision-making and social cohesion between host and displaced communities.

project_name: Asset creation project to support Early recovery and Resilience for 40,000 people through livelihood activities in crisis-affected areas in the Far-North region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The project aims to improve access to food and contribute to improving social cohesion and supporting early recovery and building resilience of vulnerable and food-insecure communities affected by the Boko Haram crisis and violence in the Far North region.   This project will address the immediate food needs of 40,000 vulnerable people, including refugees, internally displaced persons, returnees, and local populations who are severely affected by the 03 crises mentioned above, disrupting economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in these regions. The 40,000 beneficiaries will be distributed as follows: 30,000 people to be assisted under the FFA for early recovery and 10,000 people by the FFA for Resilience. The implementation of livelihood activities, community participatory planning (CBPP) sessions are conducted in collaboration with local community members (women and men) to identify the real needs and priorities of local communities that will help affected populations develop their own response strategies and build resilience. This people-centred approach ensures the provision of effective solutions with beneficiaries and reduces reliance on relief. 
Assistance through for FFA, will be implemented using cash modality and in-kind Food for three months under the FFA-early recovery, and six months for the FFA-Resilience. Therefore, the cash transfer value is aligned with the in-kind food ration. It considers beneficiaries' food preferences for the commodities and prices on the local market. The transfer value is calculated based on the identified food gap and is designed to assist beneficiaries to reach the recommended minimum calories intake of 2,100 Kcal per person per day. The use of cash-based transfers is expected to improve the cost-effectiveness of WFP's operations, while seizing the economic opportunities of local markets, with particular consideration for the beneficiaries’ choice and dignity.
WFP will collaborate closely with Government technical ministries, cooperating partners and communities to ensure project implementation and sustainability. Nutrition, Gender and protection issues are taken into consideration at all the stages of the project elaboration, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Gender and protection risk analysis will be carried out and the most vulnerable will be targeted, including female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities.
Project sites will be in secure areas and at convenient distance from the homes of the beneficiaries.
To support smooth project implementation and ensure sustainability, capacity strengthening sessions will be organized for all stakeholders on gender and protection policy, project management, monitoring and nutrition.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Response for Refugees in Sudan 2022
project_objective:
As of August 2021, Sudan hosts an estimated 1,111,329  refugees and asylum-seekers from the Central African Republic, Chad, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, Syria, Yemen, among others. The main refugee-hosting states are Khartoum, White Nile, Kassala, South and East Darfur, as well as West and South Kordofan. South Sudanese refugees are the largest refugee population, with a recorded number of 786,524(70.8%) refugees living across all states. Most of the current overall refugee population (70%) are living outside of official camps. Out-of-camp settlements include large collective self-settlements, communities that are integrated with the host community, and urban areas. Many out-of-camp settlements are in remote and underdeveloped areas where resources, infrastructure, and basic services are extremely limited. In the camps, the assistance provided is modest and, in some cases, does not meet minimum living standards. 
Basic Vulnerability Index (BVI) analysis conducted by UNHCR show that at least one-third of refugees had high levels of overall vulnerability in all states, except for Sennar Most refugees in Sudan have moderate to high levels of overall vulnerability, with at least one third in every state experiencing high levels of overall vulnerability.  In Kassala, White Nile, East Darfur, and West Kordofan, the majority of both refugees and host communities experience high overall vulnerability. Meanwhile, in Blue Nile, North Darfur, South Darfur, and North Kordofan refugees are more likely to experience higher overall vulnerability. • Overall, refugees in-camp/camp-like situations experience higher levels of overall vulnerability compared to those settled out-of-camp. The highest proportion of refugees in camp/camp-like situations with high to severe levels of vulnerability are identified in Blue Nile, Khartoum, North Darfur, South Darfur, and North Kordofan.. Based on BVI analysis, WASH, Shelter & Energy, and protection vulnerability is higher while Health and Nutrition, Education, and Food security are moderate however, still support is required. Across all assessed states, West Kordofan and East Darfur had the highest level of vulnerability for both refugees and the host community. This means that the overall population in these states had high levels of vulnerability across the assessed sectors and sub-indicators. Refuges are highly vulnerable and need multi sectoral interventions to address their vulnerabilities, and to maintain and fulfil their rights. They are mostly coming to Sudan with poor health conditions with little to no personnel belongings with them and who are in urgent need of protection, WASH, nutrition, shelter & health support.
 The majority of the affected & target population are women & children. 53% of the overall refuges are women & children who are arriving in poor health conditions after walking days to cross in to Sudan and have little to no personnel belongings with them. Refuges are in urgent need of protection, WASH, nutrition, shelter & health support.
The project will seek to provide live saving interventions & sustain services of WASH, Health & Nutrition through safe, clean water & adequate sanitation facilities, quality primary health care, preventive & curative nutritional intervention . The services will be provided in a holistic & collective manner to enhance peaceful coexistence between refuges & host community & improving the peoples’ wellbeing. Gender, protection & accountability will be mainstreamed throughout the implementation. CIS with national partners will work in coordinated manner to provide the needed support, staff will participate & attend coordination meetings at different levels to provide assistance in coordinated & collaborative manner
