project_name: Food security and livelihoods for IDPs , Host community in Sudan
project_objective:
ADRA Sudan will continue to Provide life-saving integrated interventions in Sudan to address the prolonged food security, livelihood challenges  and Protection conditions faced by the population and alleviate the underlying food security issues by restoring livelihoods and agriculture cultivation. A total of 200,000 will be reached by the proposed initiative. The project activities are grounded in this development hypothesis and are focused squarely on the following five parallel “If” statements: IF Project  trains smallholder farmers on best practices aim to increase yield, provide agriculture inputs, in addition to strengthening their production capacity through farmer field schools; THEN, the program participants will be able to decrease their crop yield losses and enhance household level food security and income.
•	If Project  provides access to cash assistance for small businesses interrupted by conflict; THEN, vulnerable households will be able to increase their income resulting in improving their food security. Following nonproductive agricultural methods that lead to land degradation and environmental damage. Decrease in agricultural yields leading to food insecurity as communities are dependent on agricultural production to meet their food needs. Lack of access to improved inputs especially for female farmers and female led households. Project proposed intervention will enhance farming productivity of farmers by introducing improved agricultural methods and organising farmers to farmer field schools. Provision of improved tools and seeds to meet food needs. Especially female farmers.Restarting small business to help in restoring income generation activities for conflict affected households and especially women. ADRA will take steps to ensure that IDPs, women, and youth are given priority during beneficiary targeting to participate in Farm Field Schools (FFS), where demo plots will be used to give beneficiaries hands-on learning opportunities and produce coming from those demo plots goes to beneficiaries. During the implementation of agricultural programs, ADRA will hold meetings with the community leadership to ensure that the land will be set aside for the FFS demo plots. ADRA will continue to promote access to land for those most vulnerable in communities by creating formal agreements with those communities’ leaders, arranging for a percentage of the beneficiaries’ crops to be returned to landowners as compensation after the program has finished. This will be based on the assumption that beneficiaries are willing to work within the framework of the program in agriculture activities,Excessive rainfall will not cause targeted localities to be inaccessible and will allow program activities to proceed without significant delay, Program staff are able to access the program area regularly to work in implementing the components and follow up with installations and progress. Beneficiaries for the FFS will be selected through a participatory approach with the communities in the area. ADRA will work with its national partner on compiling the list of smallholder farmers to be enrolled within the project, especially for those farmers involved in the first trainings who will be doing subsequent cascade trainings. Working with community committees and local stakeholders, ADRA and its local partner will identify small-scale farmers—mainly displaced and returnee HHs—with limited access to seeds and tools for agricultural production. Farmers must also have demonstrated access to land for agriculture (average of 2–5 feddan [.84–2.1 hectares]). Access to land does not necessarily need to be ownership; many farmers farm on a seasonal basis on rented land (share cropping).The FFS group will form the entry point around which ADRA will introduce various awareness messages, especially regarding food security and nutrition.Using a Training of Trainers (ToT) model, ADRA will identify and train 2500 lead farmers .

project_name: Comprehensive Protection Services in Bekaa, Aley, Batroun, and greater Beirut
project_objective:
This project will provide protection services for the most critically vulnerable Lebanese population, including women, men, girls, and boys, working both to prevent protection violations as well as respond to needs. It will address GBV needs through provision of services including psychosocial support and case management. It will also address child protection needs through protection case management, focused and non-focused psychosocial support, and recreational activities. The project will address legal needs for GBV and CP cases through provision of legal services, including legal counselling and payment of legal fees, for individuals both in and out of detention through partner organization, MSD. 

The project will operate through Tabitha-run community centers in Batroun, North Gov.; Aley, Mount Lebanon (3 centers in Aley city, Choueifat and Bayssour) in addition Chouf through the intervention in the SDC of Chehime; Achrafieh, Beirut ; and through the mobile unit in the Bekaa Valley in addition to greater Beirut area (Metn and Baabda) that Tabitha is planning to target through the proposal submitted to OCHA lately. These centers and mobile unit contain Tabitha’s community outreach workers, a psychologist, and social workers who maintain a presence within targeted communities. Cases taken up by these social workers may come from multiple sources- referrals from other NGOs and CSOs, cases identified by community outreach workers, cases identified through individuals or family members already participating in Tabitha’s community center protection services, etc. Tabitha also partners with another Lebanese NGO, Migration Services and Development (MSD), that specializes in legal services and has access to individuals in detention facilities. MSD lawyers also maintain designated offices within Tabitha community centers. 
Tabitha will also coordinate its work with the stakeholders of each area, for Achrafieh and Greater Beirut, Tabitha will coordinate with Makhzoumi & TDH Lausanne following the recommendation of the sector.
Case Management will be implemented through the use of the social work methodology including individual vulnerability/needs assessments (through interviews and home visits when possible), a network of outreach workers (selected and trained among vulnerable refugees/host communities) to facilitate trust and access to isolated groups on a timely and safe manner. Tabitha follows the national protection working groups, all the team is trained on the usage of the national SOP for GBV and CP, using the recognized referrals pathways to ensure cases that require specialized follow-up are referred to be assessed, specialized service providers. MHPSS services will be made available for those attending programs at the community centers in all the locations- this includes the elderly, children, and those who have experienced severe trauma and abuse. A licensed psychologist is present in all locations and animators/facilitators are trained to facilitate group PSS sessions, especially for children. The legal assistance program operates using a holistic approach, whereas both lawyers & social workers provide services to those in need of assistance. Beneficiaries are referred to or approach Tabitha community centers for issues related to civil documentation or access to justice. Services provided include: support with employer or family issues such as divorce; child registration and birth registration; marriage certificates; documentation for the continuity of education; renewal of documentation to stay in Lebanon; or organization of documentation to return to Syria. As the beneficiaries for the legal program are vulnerable conflict affected households, often cases of GBV and CP, cases are referred from social workers either within Tabitha, or from the referral pathway system established in country.  With homelessness rising, legal support is also needed for rental and eviction, another service of MSD.

project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle aux populations vulnérables affectées par les crises dans les DS de Makary, Fotokol et de Mada impactés par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Le Cameroun est aujourd'hui traversé par plusieurs crises, notamment dans la région la plus septentrionale du pays. Ces crises entraînent d'importants mouvements de population et des pertes de biens et de moyens existence qui ont un fort impact sur les conditions de vie des populations hôtes et déplacées. Cette situation conduit par ailleurs à accentuer la pression qui pèse sur les services sociaux de base tels que la santé. 

Face à cette situation préoccupante, le projet ALIMA vient en appui à 9 CSI et à l'Hôpital de Makary, localisés dans trois districts sanitaires (Makary, Fotokol, Mada) de la région de l'Extrême-Nord. ALIMA fournit une assistance médico-nutritionnelle pour les enfants de moins de 5 ans, un accès aux soins de la santé de la reproduction aux femmes enceintes et allaitantes et à la santé mentale pour ces deux catégories de bénéficiaires ciblés par son intervention. Dans le cadre de son action, ALIMA a mis en œuvre une stratégie à la fois fixe (au sein des structures de santé) et mobile (cliniques mobiles). L'intervention d'ALIMA comprend par ailleurs un volet d'activités communautaires qui visent à promouvoir les bonnes pratiques en matière d'hygiène et de santé, d'alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant, l'approche Pb-mères, entre autres thématiques. 

Dans l'Extrême-Nord, le projet a pour objectif de réduire la morbi-mortalité des populations vulnérables réfugiées, déplacées et hôtes en garantissant un accès aux soins et une prise en charge médicale gratuite de qualité. 

De manière transversale, le projet apporte un appui au système de santé national dans la sensibilisation, la PCI, la formation et la protection des staffs ainsi que dans la gestion des cas Covid-19. 

Par ailleurs, le projet assure sur l'ensemble des zones d'intervention d'ALIMA une réponse rapide et adaptée aux besoins médicaux en cas de chocs humanitaires (crisis modifier).  

Au total, ce sont 106 639 personnes qui sont visés par ce projet dont 51 918 femmes et  54 721 hommes.

project_name: Reducing Risk and Meeting Basic Needs of Crisis-Affected Communities in the Far North Region, Cameroon
project_objective: The ongoing conflict between armed opposition groups continues to have widespread impact on communities in the Far North, particularly on their livelihoods and food security, limiting communities’ ability to meet their basic needs and exposing them to various protection risks. The proposed intervention is built on the lessons learned and achievements of activities implemented by IRC through OFDA support over the past three years. It aims to provide direct support to beneficiaries to meet their basic needs across multiple services areas. These include provision of drinking water, promotion of hygiene and sanitation, the restoration of livelihoods, and actions to promote community-based protection and prevent gender-based violence (GBV). the IRC will continue to position itself to respond swiftly to spontaneous movements with mobile services that enable access to hard-to-reach areas in persistent and precarious environments. To support sustainability beyond the project period, the IRC will also continue to reinforce local capacities to ensure a smooth exit strategy.

project_name: Sécurité alimentaire et autonomisation des populations vulnérables de la région de l’Extrême-Nord victimes des exactions des bandes armées et des inondations
project_objective:
Le présent projet se propose de renforcer les moyens de subsistance de 2 000 ménages vulnérables (60 femmes et 40% hommes)  de la population cible des départements du Mayo Sava (Arrondissement de Kolofata, Mora), du Mayo Danay (Arrondissement de Vellé), du Mayo Tsanaga (Arrondissements de Mokolo et Mozogo) et du Logone-et-Chari (Arrondissements de Makary, Goulfey et Logone birni) de la région de l’Extrême-Nord du Cameroun à travers la distribution des intrants agricoles pour les cultures maraîchères et vivrières et leur capacitation pour le développement des AGR sur la période Avril-Décembre 2022, ceci afin de les permettre d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et de renforcer leur résilience aux chocs divers. 
Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira :
De contribuer à la formation sur des thématiques diverses de 2 000 ménages vulnérables, cible du projet. Il sera question de former les bénéficiaires sur les meilleures techniques de culture maraîchères, vulgariser les bonnes pratiques de récoltes, de conservation et de transformations des produits locaux.
D’inciter à la création des activités génératrices de revenus (AGR) afin de réduire la pression sur les moyens d’existence en période de soudure.
Les activités principales suivantes sont envisagées :
Ciblage de 2 000 ménages (14 000 individus, une taille moyenne de 7 personnes)
Le ciblage des 2 000 ménages soit en moyenne 14 000 personnes bénéficiaires intégrera l’ensemble des parties prenantes y compris l’autorité administrative et celle traditionnelle. Les critères prendront leur source des 14 critères généralement reconnus dans la sphère. Un exercice de priorisation sera organisé avec les représentants des cibles et les autorités des sites arrêtés. Le projet ciblera les populations déplacées (40%), les retournées (20%) et les communautés hôtes vulnérables (40%). Un ratio de 60% de femmes cheffe de ménage contre 40% d’hommes sera respecté. Les femmes étant celles victimes de pratiques indécentes des hommes et culturellement, plus actives dans les activités agricoles. Par ailleurs, elles sont celles qui veillent sur la santé alimentaire et sécuritaire de la famille.
Formation des bénéficiaires sur les thématiques diverses liées à la production agropastorale, la récolte, la conservation et la transformation des produits locaux
2 000 ménages recevront des formations théoriques et pratiques au cours de 02 séances sur les itinéraires techniques agropastorales, les meilleures techniques de récoltes, conservation et transformation des produits locaux, la production des biopesticides et des engrais organiques. Un conseil agricole sera offert aux bénéficiaires pendant la durée du projet. Les orientations et cadrages seront assurés par les techniciens du terrain en collaboration avec l’administration camerounaise en charge des questions agricoles et élevages (le MINADER et le MINEPIA) pour une meilleure appropriation et de durabilité des acquis. 
Développement des activités génératrices de revenu (AGR)
L’ensemble des ménages recevront des conseils pratiques sur le développement et la gestion des AGR en donnant une valeur ajoutée aux produits récoltés de la session vivrière notamment à travers la conservation et la transformation des produits locaux.
Les résultats attendus sont les suivants :
R1 : Les ménages bénéficiaires des départements du Mayo Sava, du Mayo Danay, du Mayo Tsanaga et Logone-Et-Chari, ont accès aux meilleures pratiques de production et à des intrants et équipements agricoles afin d’améliorer leur résilience durant la période de soudure et de moins agresser les moyens de subsistance. 
R2 : Les bénéficiaires ayant reçus les connaissances techniques sont à même de créer des activités génératrices de revenus pérennes et de contribuer au développement de l’économie locale.
Les bénéficiaires du projet seront sélectionnés de manière participative parmi les populations déplacées, réfugiées,  retournées et communautés hôtes vulnérables des localités ciblées.

project_name: Community-based Protection response to conflict affected communities in North West and South West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
INTERSOS proposes to promote a protective environment for conflict-affected people, in particular IDPs with a focus on Child Protection and GBV. Four main elements will be addressed: 1) Prevention of child abuse, neglect, and exploitation; 2) Prevention by addressing the risks of sexual and gender-based violence and responding to the immediate needs of survivors of GBV, 3) Material support for the most vulnerable IDPs with NFI; and 4) identifying and strengthening existing positive community protection mechanism.
Outputs to prevent and respond to Child Protection needs and GBV: Creation of 175 Child Friendly Spaces (Fako, Meme, Manyu, Kupe, Mezam, Momo, Boyo) where children and caregivers would be able to improve their protection environment and theirs capacities through the active participation in the existing Protection structures that INTERSOS supported during the year 2021, Integrated GBV Case management for boys girls and their caregivers, share INTERSOS’ Hotline, provision of psychological first aid (PFA), referral and accompaniment to specialized services, individual follow up, Psychosocial Support (PSS) inside and outside CFS facilities though individual & group counselling, community based recreational and PSS activities, basic skills acquisition and informal education, MH support for children and caregivers through individual case management and referrals to specialized services, Targeted material assistance for identified protection needs: Auto-referral for dignity kits to vulnerable women and girls including PwSN of reproductive age; Auto-referral for Mama kits for vulnerable pregnant and lactating women and girls, Auto-referral for cash for protection: Community capacity building on Child Protection and GBV principles & personal/relational accountability, Material support for the most vulnerable IDP household through the distribution of contextualized NFI case by case.
The overall objective of the project is to improve the protection environment of children and caregivers affected by the crisis and foster a community-based approach for the protection of the most vulnerable IDPs by contributing to the reduction of child abuse and gender-based violence (GBV) through promoting socio-cultural norms that respect age/gender equality, through holistic care of children and caregivers affected by the crisis, and GBV survivors by promoting their recovery and resilience. Also, the empowerment of community members and groups in identifying, referring and responding to protection concerns. 
The project aims at initiating key changes in behaviors and socio-cultural norms in order to sustainably reduce child abuse and GBV.
Through awareness-raising campaigns, capacity building of caregivers and the active involvement of community leaders, communities are called upon to adopt attitudes that are protective for children and respectful of gender equality.
CFS are key avenues to providing confidential medium for disclosure of psychosocial distress and GBV without the fear of stigmatization, they also provide caregivers and survivors an opportunity to build support networks through peer-to-peer activities and build on their recovery and resilience through activities that foster social interactions.
Though this project, INTERSOS will integrate the CP response to his spectrum of protection activities in a systematic approach, based on the Community based strategy that INTERSOS is implementing and the Protection monitoring mechanisms already in place covering 10 divisions of NWSW, INTERSOS will be able to early identify cases of child abuse and to promptly address the protection needs of children affected by the crisis. The complementarity of this project with the ongoing protection program, and the recognition that INTERSOS gained in NWSW regions which greatly facilitate humanitarian access in hard-to-reach areas, are valuable assets that will impact the quality and the promptness of the assistance

project_name: Provision of basic nutrition interventions to conflict affected populations in selected sites in Blue Nile, White Nile and South Kordofan in 2022 (Nutrition)
project_objective:
This project will be implemented in three target states (Blue Nile, White Nile, and South Kordofan). The overall aim of the project is to contribute to reduction of mortality and morbidity among the affected persons (internally displaced persons, returnees, and host community members) through provision of integrated Nutrition, Health, and WASH emergency and recovery interventions to vulnerable men, women, boys, and girls in the selected states during the year 2022. The total population targeted by the project is
estimated at 74,732 individuals including children under five years of age, pregnant and lactating women. The nutrition proposed interventions aim at improving the nutrition status of the target population and reducing the nutrition-related mortality and morbidity rates among the most vulnerable groups of the population, especially children under five years of age, pregnant and lactating women (PLW) at the selected geographical areas (Blue Nile, White Nile and South Kordofan) through provision of timely and comprehensive preventive and curative nutritional services. The main activities of this project include: 1.
Supporting nutrition screening for children under five and PLW, 2. Supporting management of MAM cases in the TSFP, 3. Supporting referral of malnourished children from the community to the TSFP, 4. Following up the MAM cases and defaulters tracing. 5. Providing micro-nutrients supplementation to the children in need. 6. Supporting nutrition counseling on infant and young child feeding. 7. Supporting capacity development of the care providers, community-based and civil society organization staffs. 
The total budget required to implement this project is estimated at 267,500 USD.

project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle aux populations vulnérables affectées par la crise anglophone dans les DS de Batibo, Bali et Santa
project_objective:
L'intervention d'ALIMA dans la région du Nord-Ouest s'inscrit dans la continuité des activités menées depuis octobre 2020 par ALIMA et son partenaire DEMTOU Humanitaire, une ONG camerounaise. Elle est déployée dans 10 centres de santé intégrés, répartis dans les trois districts de santé de Bali, Batibo et de Santa ainsi que dans le centre médical d'arrondissement de Widikum. 

Ce projet vise à garantir l'accès gratuit aux soins de santé et de nutrition ainsi qu'une prise en charge médicale gratuite et de qualité à travers la fourniture de soins médicaux via une stratégie à la fois fixe et mobile (basée sur le déploiement de cliniques mobiles). L'intervention dispose également d'un volet d'activités à l'échelon communautaire, notamment des activités de sensibilisation et l'approche PB-mères permettant le dépistage précoce de l'état nutritionnel des enfants par leurs mamans et accompagnants. 

Ce projet comprend par ailleurs le renforcement de la préparation aux réponses aux urgences et la fourniture d'une réponse d'urgence en cas de chocs dans la région du Nord-Ouest à travers l'intégration d'un crisis modifier. 

Cette intervention a pour objectif transversal d'apporter un appui au système de santé national dans la sensibilisation, la mise en place de mesures de PCI, la formation et protection du personnel de santé des structures appuyées. 

Au total, ce sont 24 200 femmes et 26 216 hommes qui sont visés par cette intervention. Les enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi que les femmes enceintes et allaitantes constituent la cible prioritaire de ce projet puisqu'ils représentent la couche la plus vulnérable de la population. Le personnel de santé, les relais communautaires et les chefs communautaires sont également bénéficiaires de cette intervention.

project_name: Appui au renforcement des moyens d'existence des populations affectées par les perturbations climatiques et la récurrence de la crise centrafricaine pour une meilleure cohabitation dans les provinces du sud du Tchad
project_objective:
Le Tchad à l’instar des autres pays du monde touché par la pandémie du COVID-19 a pris des mesures pour protéger sa population contre la propagation de la pandémie COVID-19. Malheureusement certaines de ces mesures ont entraîné un dysfonctionnement dans les chaînes d’approvisionnement en denrées alimentaires et intrants agricoles, des hausses de prix de certaines denrées qui continuent jusqu’en 2021. 
C’est dans ce contexte que le Tchad s’est fixé comme objectif de produire cette année environ 3 132 642 tonnes de céréales pour couvrir les besoins céréaliers de la population. Il est également prévu de produire 1 881 546 tonnes pour d’autres produits vivriers (arachide, sésame, manioc, taro, igname, etc.). Malheureusement, la production céréalière prévisionnelle de la campagne agricole 2020/2021 est estimée à 2 901 683 tonnes, ce qui est de loin inférieur à l’objectif du Ministère en charge de l’agriculture. 
Par ailleurs, la situation nutritionnelle des enfants de moins de 5 ans n’est guère encourageante et reste toujours préoccupante vu les tendances globales des admissions au niveau national. La situation générale est particulièrement alarmante compte tenu de la diminution de la production agricole dans la région soudanaise. Elle est exacerbée par une campagne agricole 2021-2022 qui reste dominée par les pluies supérieures comparée à la moyenne des 30 dernières années ayant entrainé des inondations sur les cultures et les animaux dans certaines localités au sud du pays. Pour mesurer l’ampleur des dégâts causés par les inondations, des évaluations ont été faites par différents acteurs (FAO-ANADER, les mouvements de la Croix Rouge, Comité provincial de Gestion des Catastrophes et World vision) dans les provinces du Moyen Chari, Le Mandoul, le Mayo Kebbi Est et la Tandjilé. En effet, les inondations ont affecté près de 28735 ménages soit 172405 personnes, 69482 hectares détruits toute espèce confondue dont les plus affectées sont les cultures de céréales, les oléagineux et protéagineux.  Il ressort aussi des résultats de cette évaluation que plus 4114 cheptels sont noyés et plus de 757 arbres toute espèce confondues déracinées. Ces dommages sont plus accentués dans les sous-prefecture de Ndam, Lai rural, Deressia, Dafra, Kolon , Bologo, Banda CST, Danamadje, Maro, Moussafoyo, Kyabé rural, Moissala rural, Koumra rural, Goundi et Sarh rural. Ces différentes évaluations sont réalisées en vue de mieux apprécier les dommages causés par les inondations pluviales et de mieux dimensionner la réponse d’urgence sur la base des besoins réels des communautés et des gaps à combler sur le terrain.
Les premiers résultats de l’enquête agricole permanente fait ressortir que les productions prévisionnelles céréalières (Riz, Maïs, Mil, sorgho, Berbéré et Blé) 2021-2022 sont estimées à 2 701 376 tonnes soit une Baisse de 6,28% par rapport à la production totale définitive de la campagne agricole 2020-2021 et de 6,33% par rapport à la moyenne des 5 dernière années. Ces niveaux de productions cachent des disparités entre les provinces. En ce qui concerne les spéculations, le maïs a régressé de 12,8%, le mil de 8,2%, et le riz de 8,2% par rapport à la moyenne des cinq dernières années.  
Pour la production des tubercules, la prévision de production 2021-2022 est estimée à 515 118 tonnes soit une baisse attendue de 2,1% par rapport à la campagne agricole passée et de 8,9% par rapport à la moyenne des 5 dernière années. Concernant les oléagineux, la production est estimée à 1 017 288 tonnes soit une baisse attendue de 2,4% par rapport à production de l’année dernière et de 3,2% par rapport à la moyenne des 5 dernière années. Compte tenu du contexte politico-sécuritaire actuel dans le pays, il est à craindre une dégradation de la situation alimentaire. Il faut aussi signaler l'afflux des Refugiés et Retournés centrafricains au sud du pays qui vient dans une situation alimentaire préoccupante et nécessite un appui pour améliorer leur résilience.

project_name: Provision of critical life-saving assistance through nutrition interventions to most acutely vulnerable groups affected by the expanding severe drought in Dhas, Dire, Elwaye, and Miyo woredas of Borena Zone, Oromia Region with a special attention given to children under-five 5, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), people with disability (PWD) and old people
project_objective:
According to the 2021 Mid-Year Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), 14.8 million are targeted for humanitarian assistance. About 3.2 million of them are targeted to receive basic lifesaving health services, the majority (55%) being children. Likewise, an estimated 2.91 million people are targeted for humanitarian nutrition response, with children under the age of five accounting for 72% of the targeted beneficiaries. This EHF-funded emergency Nutrition response aim to contribute to the reduction of nutrition related morbidity and mortality among children under five years of age (U5), Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW), and women of child-bearing age in six drought-affected and prioritized woredas of Borena zone, Oromia region.
The nutrition response will contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality among children under five years of age (U5), PLW, and women of childbearing age in the intervention woredas. Key nutrition intervention focus areas include both preventive and recuperative services. The recuperative services include strengthening the local health system capacity to detect, refer, and treatment mainly acutely malnutrition children under five years of age and PLW in TFP and TSFP. While the preventive nutrition intervention focuses on the protection, promotion, and support of adequate Infant and Young Children Feeding (IYCF) program in the context of emergency by applying effective and proven methods and mechanisms. In addition, strengthening local health system capacity on early warning, nutrition situation surveillance, and nutrition emergency preparedness and response planning will be given due emphasis. Logistically and technical support will be delivered to nutrition service delivery sites. Procurement and provision of gap-filling routine medications, supplies, and equipment will be done to ensure the quality of SAM and MAM management in intervention areas. Provision of standard nutrition training such as IMAM/CMAM, IYCF will be provided to frontline health workers based on needs and gaps and in line with the national guidelines. Post-training follow-up, mentoring, and coaching of health workers will continue to be key attributes of the AAH’s nutrition intervention approach in proposed woredas. 
AAH endeavors to achieve results stipulated in this EHF project through the active engagement, collaboration, and coordination between local health authorities, WHO, UNICEF and WFP as well as targeted communities. Moreover, cross-cutting issues such as PSEA, AAP, and Gender will be mainstreamed across all proposed activities.

project_name: Provision of GBV response for survivors and implementation of GBV risk mitigation measures.
project_objective:
The activities proposed under this program will provide SGBV Prevention and Response support to approximately 45,340 of the most vulnerable people in West Wollega, East Wollega and Kellem Wollega in Oromia, and Kamashi in Benishangul Gumuz. Action Against Hunger will address the acute protection needs by providing a holistic response on SGBV through support to health and social services, and through community engagement and women empowerment in conflict-affected communities including IDPs, returnees and host communities. 

Specifically, this project aims to support vulnerable groups whose needs have become priorities in areas affected by violence, unrest and security issues, frequent displacement or secondary displacement, limited basic services, poor reintegration and worsening by the prevalence of COVID-19 and its restrictions and the impact of the war. Action Against Hunger will build on its presence and integration with government agencies to prevent and address SGBV cases, improve psychosocial wellbeing and protect the most vulnerable groups – particularly pregnant and lactating women, women, older men with disabilities, adolescents and young girls, and SGBV survivors – while encouraging participation by the wider community including men, older adults and community leaders. In addition, the project will focus on strengthening systems and improving capacities of government service providers, particularly in health care facilities. 

This complex humanitarian emergency manifested by on-going fighting in these areas, secondary displacement, lack of strong reintegration processes and poor co-existence of IDPs are exacerbating the population's negative coping strategies, including unsafe coping behaviours and practices, resulting in higher rates of mortality and morbidity especially among the most vulnerable. Through this project, Action Against Hunger will address these urgent protection needs and build capacity of local government, national and local stakeholders to raise awareness, encourage readiness in provide basic lifesaving services and build community resilience. Action Against Hunger has been working well in this complex region and established strong relationships with local government, mindful of the need to balance a multi-sectoral response that considers the needs of IDPs and the host community – an important aspect in promoting peacebuilding and equality between the communities.

Under this project, Action Against Hunger's overall goal is to reduce SGBV and improve the quality of response by supporting active community and local institutions engagement on SGBV prevention and response activities. This will be achieved through: 1) Provision of Basic training on SGBV and PSS which will be provided for Persons of Concern (including those key influencers selected from community of concern), 2) Provision of Capacity building training to health care staff working in two zones Hospitals and Health Centers on Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) as per WHO Guidelines, 3) Establish and maintain Case Management and safe referral systems among health and other service providers, BoWCYA, Justice/legal, etc., 4) Organize and conduct awareness raising sessions SGBV, Mental Health, PSEA at nutrition sites, health facilities, community gatherings, etc., 5) Conduct Protection Monitoring, 6) Work with local health-care providers to strengthening and support One-Stop Centres to ensure SGBV survivor women and adolescent girls and boys have immediate and appropriate Essential medical service (CMR, etc.), 7) Support and strengthen economic empowerment of women, adolescent girls and Person with disability through IGA activity or Cash Assistance, 8) Establish and strengthen existing safe spaces for women and girls to provide Psychosocial support activities, 9) Targeted support for most vulnerable women, girls, boys and men with disabilities and 10) Dignity Kits for SGBV survivors, vulnerable individuals and women and adolescent girls of rep

project_name: Protection services for most vulnerable residing in NES
project_objective:
Protection is an integral component of CARE’s multiple sectoral interventions linking beneficiaries to essential, needs based protection services and providing stand-alone services as needed and permitted by the context. CARE will integrate a menu of critical protection services, including structured and unstructured PSS, monitored regularly to measure change in people’s ability to cope with stress. The focus will be on ensuring vulnerable men, women and children are reached with protection related information, are linked to available services, have space to voice protection concerns, share information, and build trust. Consideration is being given to providing specialized services particularly GBV prevention and mitigation where gaps exist and community sensitivities allow.  GBV components will account for up to 40% of the budget, with the remainder for Gender Protection interventions. Key services will include:
1. General Awareness raising, information sharing sessions, conducting roleplays and facilitating community-based discussions covering sensitive protection issues including GBV as a prevention approach for all the community members (no GBV Survivors to be included) and other related topics based on the consultation with the community also sharing info about the available service after updating the service mapping and after CARE MSNA is completed. For non GBV sessions, the awareness raising session are intended to enhance beneficiaries access to critical protection information including information about the available services and how to access them.   This information is updated regularly through a service mapping exercise and also continuous consultation with the community members. COVID-19 is also part of the non-GBV awareness raising.
2.	Community volunteers, community members and other service providers will be trained on diverse protection related themes that will enable them to detect, identify and mitigate protection related risks including GBV.
3.	Gender sensitive mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services offering non-specialized sessions to enhance beneficiaries’ psychosocial wellbeing using a “light approach”. Focused psychosocial (PSS) sessions will target vulnerable women and children.
4.	Provision of “safe spaces” activities including recreational activities and community events to enhance the beneficiaries psychological coping mechanism. 
5.	Establishing multipurpose community centers providing a safe space for conducting awareness sessions, psychosocial support and training with a particular focus on GBV.
6.	Provision of holistic case management (as described under Outcome #1).
7.	Provision of psycho-social support (PSS), possibly in tandem with VT.
8.	Information and/or referrals for marginalized individuals on/to needed services (where they exist) to increase safety within the home and community (i.e. GBV, physical rehabilitation, PSS, prosthetic services, etc.).
9.	Training, awareness raising, and /or the dissemination of information on accessing legal identity and civil documentation. 
10.	Distributing female dignity kits to vulnerable women and girls.
Our activities will focus on men and women, children and adolescents’ girls and boys. We will also work inside the camps, in host communities and those who have returned.

project_name: Supporting most vulnerable Lebanese children to access and continue learning through quality and inclusive education programing
project_objective: The purposed intervention takes a holistic approach responding to the economic crisis affecting the learning of children all over Lebanon. Plan will collaborate with LOST to address the educational needs of children by targeting the most vulnerable Leb children in North Beqaa with a focus on out of school, children that dropped out or shifted to public schools to access or remain in formal education. The intervention will be adapted in line with covid-19 measures to ensure children are safe and protected. Caregivers will be supported by addressing both their financial and emotional burden. Also Plan and LOST will be working on supporting the formal education system, to ensure that students are provided with an inclusive and quality education while ensuring schools have the needed basic conditions and resources to adhere to the influx of students transitioning from private education. The project two main objectives are: Obj 1: Direct community support to support the most vulnerable children to ensure continued learning. Plan’s programs are based on a needs bases with a strong emphasis on learning component to ensure that the most vulnerable children educational needs are met.  Plan will coordinate with all educational stakeholders in the area to fully map out the most vulnerable areas in North Beqaa. Plan and LOST will be working on addressing both financial and social emotional burden. Plan has already a strong cash component under its programming and has all the developed guidelines and SOPs established to support families in need. Also, awareness sessions will be provided for caregivers to increase their soft skills while also focusing on decreasing their social emotional burdens using an internally developed curriculum “Parenting skills for protection”. In addition to that, Plan and LOST will support in addressing other educational challenges through a strong referral pathway internally and externally to other service providers such as Basic Assistance and FSS, Protection, WaSH and Health. The Second Obj 2: Improving Formal Education of most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant children through schools. This objective will be focusing on schools and ensuring that all aspects such human and operational resources are fully functional to ensure a protective and inclusive environment for all children. Plan under the Beirut blast response was able to distribute close to 1000 education kits and 735 Laptops to children affected by the Beirut blast. Under this project, Plan will distribute 16700 education kit and 37 school kits in September 2021 to the identified schools and student in BML in coordination with the Beirut District. Finally, schools that have seen major influx from private to public schools are in need of cash assistance to support the transition, PLAN and LOST will coordinate with both MEHE, UNICEF and the Education regions in the areas on the number of schools that are in need of cash assistance. The project target group: 1)Leb and migrant students at risk of dropping out of school 2)Students with high level of learning loss in the last 2 years due to inequitable access to remote learning opportunities 3)OOS children and adolescents and at risk of negative coping mechanism 4)Students transitioning from private to public schools. 5)Schools with the least capacity to support transferring students from private schools based on the total number of existing students and teacher to student ratio. 6)Teachers living and working in identified most vulnerable area. 7)Teachers working in public schools receiving significant numbers of students transferring from private schools.

project_name: Protegiendo a la Niñez y Adolescencia en El Salvador
project_objective:
Este proyecto fue diseñado para un periodo de 12 meses, iniciando en enero 2022 y terminando en diciembre 2022. El presupuesto requerido para este periodo es de USD $223,949. A través del proyecto, se llegará a un total de 2,124 niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA). 

Entre el 2012 y 2019, las Juntas de Protección de Niñez del CONNA recibieron 98,054 reportes de vulneraciones en el ámbito de violencia, abuso y explotación . Los casos registrados por las Juntas de Protección de NNA suelen ser una subrepresentación del número real de vulneraciones, por las limitaciones de acceso al sistema de protección. Del 2016 al 2020, fueron deportados desde México y USA 21,384 NNA  que fueron detenidos en su intento de huir de El Salvador.

Ante la emergencia humanitaria que vive la niñez y sus familias en El Salvador, el IRC ha diseñado el proyecto Protegiendo a Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes en El Salvador. En el periodo de noviembre 2020 a noviembre 2021, el IRC ha gestionado de manera exitosa 157 casos de NNA desplazados, afectados por la violencia, el maltrato, la violencia de género, y ha establecido coordinaciones con actores locales. Sin embargo, la capacidad actual es insuficiente para atender la demanda requerida.

Por medio de la gestión de casos, el IRC identificará y brindará atención psicosocial directa y remisión a servicios especializados y asistencia humanitaria a NNA y sus familias en riesgo con el apoyo de un equipo multidisciplinario y coordinación con actores locales. Para este objetivo, llevará a cabo intervenciones comunitarias para la identificación de casos y sensibilización a nivel territorial. Adicionalmente reforzará dos espacios seguros en los municipios priorizados, fortaleciendo su capacidad existente y capacitando actores locales en temas relevantes basados en metodologías ampliamente probadas por IRC a nivel global para proveer herramientas para la identificación y atención de NNA en riesgo. 

Este proyecto prioriza a la población objetivo del Subsector de Niñez y contribuye al objetivo específico identificado por el Subsector en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria. También responde directamente a las actividades priorizadas en el plan y a los indicadores del subsector.

project_name: Prevención y respuesta a la violencia basada en género en El Salvador
project_objective:
Este proyecto fue diseñado para un periodo de 12 meses, iniciando en enero 2022 y terminando en diciembre 2022. El presupuesto requerido es de USD $280,500 y se espera alcanzar a un total de 1,994 personas. 
El Salvador tiene una de las tasas de feminicidio más altas del mundo y una cultura de discriminación de género que perpetúa patrones de violencia contra las mujeres y poblaciones LGBTQ+. Al menos el 67% de las mujeres han sufrido violencia en su vida y el 34% ha experimentado violencia basada en género (VbG) en el último año. De estas, el 60% tiene entre 12 y 17 años. Distintas organizaciones afirman que la VbG se ha exacerbado por los efectos de la COVID-19. 

En respuesta a este contexto, el IRC se encuentra implementando actividades que se enfocan en la prevención y respuesta de VbG. A través de este proyecto, el IRC pretende ampliar el alcance de sus acciones para mejorar el acceso de mujeres y niñas (incluidas las que tienen discapacidades) sobrevivientes y/o en riesgo de VBG a servicios de respuesta de calidad, centrados en las personas sobrevivientes, seguros, oportunos, confidenciales y coordinados. Adicionalmente, el IRC pretende expandir modelos de prevención de la VbG que promueven la transformación positiva de las normas sociales y que aseguren que las mujeres en riesgo de y/o sobrevivientes de VBG tengan acceso a los recursos que necesiten. 
Las acciones del proyecto generaran cambios positivos en distintos ámbitos, incluyendo el ámbito individual, comunitario e institucional. Por un lado, las actividades del proyecto se centran en brindar servicios de gestión de casos y concientizar a la población de interés sobre la VbG. Por otro lado, a través de este proyecto, se fortalecerán las capacidades técnicas de proveedores de servicios para replicar modelos de atención basados en evidencia y mejores prácticas de la industria.  Las actividades propuestas, se alinean con los objetivos del Subsector de VbG, ya que responden directamente a los servicios y actividades priorizados en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria así como a los indicadores y metas del subsector.

project_name: Emergency WASH and ESNFI Response to Conflict Affected People in Tigray Region
project_objective:
As of February 2022, a total of 4.51 million IDPs have been identified thus far across the country. Of the total displaced population, the main causes of displacement were conflict which displaced 3.63 million IDPs (81%). Tigray has remained to be the priority region and continues to have significant IDPs and affected host population that remains vulnerable under the current circumstances- conflict. According to the Emergency Site Assessment (ESA) round 8, 386,741 households comprising 1,814,284 IDPs were identified in 581 accessible sites in Tigray region due to the Northern Ethiopia Crisis. 
Humanitarian needs remain significantly high as the current response is not meeting the increasing needs of those in need as the resources available are not matching the requirements to ensure that minimum lifesaving humanitarian standards are maintained for the targeted population. According to the northern Ethiopia humanitarian update shared (OCHA, 14 April 2022), between 1 January and 4 April 2022, only 42.11% of the targeted people were reached with ESNFI response in Tigray region. Critical needs prioritized include, provision of adequate shelters and NFIs for IDPs living in highly congested and substandard living conditions, provision of shelter and NFI assistance to IDPs willing to return to their areas of origin, and to IDPs currently living within host communities, and rental assistance schemes or other arrangements for IDPs living in host communities. 
Inadequate provision of WASH services poses a risk of disease outbreaks at IDP sites. About 9,300 water points or more than 54 per cent of the 17,080 water points in Tigray are not functional affecting the access of more than 3.5 million people to safe drinking water. About 418,000 IDPs in 131 sites require 295 trips of water trucking every day which requires 1,990 liters of fuel daily. Construction of more than 17,000 latrines at IDP sites are required to mitigate the risks of disease transmission. Low stock of key WASH NFIs, including water treatment chemical, water containers and hygiene supplies have also been reported in Tigray. Priority WASH needs include, emergency water trucking, rehabilitation of  water schemes, rehabilitation of sanitation facilities, distribution of WASH NFIs, and hygiene promotion activities.
The locations and activities considered for the WASH and ES/NFI interventions under this project plan are identified in the HRP 2022 prioritization list to address the immediate and life-saving needs of crisis-affected communities in line with the respective clusters' priority activities. The actions will be WASH and ESNFI services and carried out in line with cluster objectives CLWSH/CO1 (Deliver conflict-sensitive essential life-saving WASH services to affected people), CLWSH/CO3 (To enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Ethiopia through early recovery and resilience interventions), and CLSHL/CO1, (Ensure contextualized access to lifesaving shelter and NFIs for displacement affected population with a focus on the most vulnerable and at-risk population group to safeguard their health security, privacy, and dignity  )and CLSHL/CO2 (Contribute to improving protection outcomes by ensuring the conflict/displacement affected people have adequate safety, dignity, well-being, and equitable access to shelter solutions).
The projects aim to enhance the protection, health, and well-being of the conflict affected IDPs and host communities, and will directly reach 43,765 people through WASH and 40,055 people through ES/NFI prioritizing the most vulnerable, including women, girls, children, elderly, and people with disabilities in particular.
The project will ensure the active participation of the targeted beneficiaries and stakeholders throughout the project cycle. Protection and safety concerns will be given priority and DRC will ensure providing safe, easy, and dignified access to the facilities by the most vulnerable.

project_name: Livelihood Response to Conflict and Drought induced Emergencies (LRCDE) in Afar region
project_objective: In the Afar region, the humanitarian situation deteriorated by multifaceted natural and man-made hazards such as erratic rainfall patterns and dry spells, ethnic conflict as well as Tigray war which spills over to Afar , degradation of rangeland (due to invasive species of Prosopis juliflora, outbreaks of human (including COVID-19 pandemic) and livestock diseases, invasion by various pests (Fall Armyworm and Desert Locusts) which all contributed towards to poor crop harvests and loss of plant and pastures, which then lead to low crop and livestock production as well as livelihood losses. VSF G collected and analyzed at ground level information with beneficiary communities and then the prioritization of these locations also informed by the currently IPC 3 & 4 priority locations based on the January IPC projections, IDP numbers, experienced droughts and areas with emergency needs as the lean season deepens. To contribute to the achievements of agriculture cluster objective one “protect and sustain core-agricultural livelihoods of climate and conflict affected households in Ethiopia through humanitarian interventions in 2022” and to enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Ethiopia through early recovery and resilience interventions”, VSF Germany designed this project with key activities which includes: provision of veterinary services (voucher based treatment and vaccination); provision of supplementary animal feed to milking goats and provision of emergency seed pack (cereals, legumes, vegetables) and fodder seeds including farm tools. Moreover, this project has proposed restocking of assets for those lost their asset due to drought and multipurpose cash assistance to improve household income through unconditional cash transfer. Different Capacity building training to communities and government experts including awareness creation on COVID-19 control and prevention measures and mainstreaming of accountability to affected population and GBV. The project will give emphasis to beneficiaries such as female-headed households, people with disabilities, child-headed households, as well as IDPs. As indicated above the identified and proposed activities by the cluster and planned by VSF G are in line with the draft 2022 HRP which aims to address the needs of the most at risk and vulnerable populations by focusing on priority needs. The proposed action will ensure synergies/integration with ongoing project or resources being implemented internally and with other partners’ projects in the target woredas. In order to augment the impact of the projects, VSF-Germany links the proposed activities with nutrition, WASH and other livelihood interventions specifically during the targeting of beneficiary HHs. The integration/synergies will have positive impact on the quick recovery of HHs from the shock specifically HHs with cases of malnutrition and other related shocks.  The project will contribute to protection of the environmental by training VSF G staffs, CAHWs, government and community where proper collection and disposal of all packing materials of drugs such as bottles, feeds and seeds after use. This action will be implemented for a period of nine months starting in Mid-April to May in the five woredas (Aba’ala, Erebeti, Berhale, Dalol and Kuneba of zone 2 (Kilbati rasu) of Afar region.

project_name: Plan de respuesta humanitaria ante las necesidades básicas de las personas desplazadas de sus hogares en Honduras
project_objective:
Entre el 01 y el 16 de noviembre del 2020, Honduras se vio afectada por dos fenómenos naturales, el primero la depresión tropical ETA y días más tarde el huracán IOTA, que impactó como Tormenta Tropical. Ambos generaron fuertes impactos en diversas áreas del país, como consecuencia más de 400,000 personas fueron desplazadas a un albergue temporal, llegando a habilitarse más de 1,000 a nivel nacional. La zona norte y Atlántico del país reportaron los mayores daños. El Valle de Sula
(localizado en el noroccidente del país) compuesto por 18 municipalidades fue gravemente afectado, alrededor de 2 millones de personas viviendo en la zona sufrieron fuertes inundaciones y la mayoría de ellos se abocaron a un albergue.
En este contexto, el proyecto se centrará en dos actividades principales a) brindar apoyo a las personas desplazadas que vivieron o que siguen habitando en albergues oficiales y no oficiales, asentamientos espontáneos o similares. Esto con el fin de procurar un servicio de protección y asistencia humanitaria de forma digna, asegurando los enfoques de género, edad y diversidad. b) Incentivar a las familias afectadas por medio de transferencias de efectivo multipropósito considerando la gran necesidad existente en insumos básicos, materiales para el hogar o costo de renta de un hogar temporal. Esta segunda actividad tiene como objetivo promover la elección y la dignidad en los beneficiarios, utilizando las capacidades y la autonomía de las familias afectadas para que sean agentes de cambio en su propia recuperación. Se pretende que mediante la participación de los beneficiarios en la identificación y mejoramiento básico de las infraestructuras comunitarias que sirven de albergues, se logre crear resiliencia en ellos y prepararlos para enfrentar la temporada de emergencia, considerando las diferentes necesidades de género, edad, discapacidad y pertenencia étnica de las personas. El proyecto pondrá gran énfasis en la premisa que estas poblaciones afectadas están en el centro de su propia recuperación.

project_name: Respuesta a necesidades de acceso vital a los servicios básicos ASH de familias en situación de vulnerabilidad en Honduras
project_objective:
Este proyecto tiene como propósito asegurar el acceso a (a) agua potable, (b) saneamiento adecuado, y (c) servicios de higiene personal básica, a familias en condiciones vulnerables cuyos medios de vida fueron severamente impactados por los Huracanes Eta e Iota, en el año 2020, en 12 municipios distribuidos en los Departamentos de Cortés, Atlántida, Yoro, y Gracias a Dios, tanto para quienes permanecen en sus
comunidades como las que habitan albergues. Para ello, se proponen tres áreas de intervención: 1) mejoramiento de los sistemas de agua y saneamiento, incluyendo acciones para garantizar el almacenamiento, la purificación, y el flujo del recurso; 2) facilitación de los servicios de agua, incluyendo rehabilitación de instalaciones, provisión de insumos de higiene, y promoción de buenas prácticas; y 3) fortalecimiento de la infraestructura de agua en centros comunales (centros de salud, mercados, etc.),
mediante rehabilitación de sistemas, medidas organizaciones, y apoyo a los gobiernos locales. Con esto, se beneficiará a más de 28,000 personas, incluyendo mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes, y también a comunidades indígenas, adultos mayores, personas con discapacidad y con enfermedades crónicas graves, mujeres embarazadas y madres solteras.

project_name: Criando y protegiendo con ternura en contextos frágiles
project_objective:
Honduras sigue sufriendo el impacto de la pandemia del COVID-19 y los efectos de las restricciones de movilidad para contener la propagación del virus. A esto se suma los altos índices de violencia e inseguridad de nuestro contexto, y las pérdidas que dejaron los huracanes de ETA y IOTA. Todos estos eventos han dejado a miles de familias más vulnerables; poniendo en riesgo las vidas de personas con necesidades de protección específicas y con mayor exposición a diferentes formas de violencia: física, psicológica, VBG, sexual, reclutamiento forzado, entre otros. La saturación del Sistema de salud y los efectos del cambio climático han puesto en evidencia la fragilidad institucional para poder responder de manera oportuna y eficaz a toda está población. Ante lo antes mencionado, se encuentran poblaciones mucho más vulnerables como niñas, niños y adolescentes, cuyas voces y necesidades son minimizados bajo enfoques adulto centristas, y agendas políticas con intereses creados.
Este proyecto fortalecerá las acciones que se han venido realizando para el bienestar de la niñez. Asegurar los derechos esenciales de niños y niñas a través de la implementación de espacios amigables comunitario donde además de ser espacio de recreación será también para poder socializar dichos derechos e identificar incidentes de vulneración de derechos tanto a los niños como a sus familias. Los niños y niñas en movilidad son de suma importancia y prioridad para WVH tanto por causas de mejora de condiciones de vida como para salvaguardarla; para ello la implementación de herramienta de monitoreo de migración y del Sistema de Alerta Temprana – Migración (SAT – M), será vital para prevenir las causas que fomentan la migración forzada y realizar acciones tempranas, oportunas y pertinentes. Esto también unido al fortalecimiento y coordinación del SIGADENAH a través de los Consejos de Garantías de Derechos municipales y departamentales, así como implementar la metodología de Crianza Con Ternura que permitirá disminución de violencia doméstica, la violencia física y psicológica hacia los niños y niñas.
WVH establecerá Espacios Amigable de la Niñez (EAN) en comunidades de contexto frágil que se recuperan luego de los desastres naturales u otro de tipo de violencia con el objetivo de continuar brindando un entorno seguro para NNA y sus familias y contribuir a garantizar su bienestar psicosocial. Se facilitarán juegos, cuidado y las actividades de apoyo social apropiadas a nivel local, como la educación de madres, padres o cuidadores, el cuidado infantil compartido y los grupos de juego comunitarios. Además, EAN brindará a NNA la oportunidad de aprender sobre sus derechos, problemas de salud relacionados con COVID 19 y otros temas. Las actividades se ejecutarán con diferentes enfoques por edad y género, y llegarán tanto a niñas, niños pequeños como a adolescentes.
Un enfoque clave, será brindar apoyo psicosocial a NNA y sus familias. WVH proporcionará primeros auxilios psicológicos. Los NNA que hayan sufrido abuso serán referidos a los canales adecuados para recibir apoyo. WVH pondrá en marcha acciones de seguimiento adecuadas. WVH trabajará dentro de las redes humanitarias y el gobierno para ayudar a coordinar este apoyo. Estas acciones serán coordinadas con UNICEF, la Dirección Nacional de la Familia (DINAF)y los consejos municipales y departamentales nacionales de protección para garantizar la seguridad y los derechos de los niños afectados por desastres y la violencia.
Este proyecto está directamente ligado y por ende contribuirá a los objetivos uno y dos de del clúster de protección infantil, donde el acceso y atención de servicios integrales, fortalecimiento de los sistemas de protección y repuesta temprana y oportuna están siendo priorizados en las diferentes acciones.
Población meta: niñas: 2,550; niños: 2450; mujeres: 510; hombres: 490

project_name: Proyecto WASH de respuesta a la emergencia por Eta e Iota, en poblaciones vulnerables con enfoque de género e inclusión social. World Vision.
project_objective:
Honduras fue duramente azotada por dos fenómenos naturales: El 01 de noviembre 2020, por la Depresión Tropical Eta y luego el 16 de noviembre 2020 por el Huracán Iota. Según el Plan de respuesta de País Honduras elaborado por la Oficina de la Coordinadora Residente y la Oficina para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA), en colaboración con el equipo de respuesta humanitaria, a la fecha, la población con necesidades humanitarias en Honduras se ha duplicado en relación con el año 2020 (1.3
M), alcanzando 2.8 M de personas (51% mujeres y 49% hombres) con necesidades humanitarias previstas para 2021.
En tal sentido, World Vision Honduras como miembro activo del EHR, ha priorizado realizar el presente proyecto WASH realizando acciones para el acceso universal y sostenible al agua segura, facilidades de saneamiento básico e higiene para el bienestar de las mujeres y niñas, hombres y niños, personas con discapacidades y otros grupos vulnerables aplicando el enfoque de igualdad de género e inclusión social, promoviendo el acceso a estructuras inclusivas, que les permitan un mayor bienestar. Con esa finalidad,
se sensibilizará y capacitará a diferentes grupos metas para promover el cambio de comportamiento, se construirá/rehabilitará sistemas de agua básico para consumo y otros usos, se rehabilitará/reconstruirá sistemas de alcantarillado, se construirán letrinas, puntos de agua, módulos sanitarios con facilidades de manejo de higiene menstrual, facilidades de lavado de manos en los hogares, escuelas, centro de salud, con movilidad limitada ( según sea el caso), así como la construcción/rehabilitación de baños con agua
para mujeres en área de atención postnatal y la entrega de kits de limpieza y de reconstrucción.
Teniendo como finalidad el acceso, participación, toma de decisiones, y bienestar de las personas con enfoque a los grupos más vulnerables, contribuyendo a su vez, a los objetivos del plan de respuesta del país.

project_name: Strengthening the resilience of households with vulnerable pregnant/lactating women through a comprehensive and integrated life saving intervention
project_objective:
Throughout this project, PUI will support vulnerable individuals through health tailored activities designed to strengthen the resilience of households with vulnerable pregnant/lactating women. This project was designed based on PUI’s technical expertise and long-term presence and acceptance in the area of intervention.

Monitoring activities will be carried out throughout the life of the project in order to guarantee the compliance of the activities with agreed objectives and targets. A detailed monitoring and evaluation plan (M&E) will be developed at the beginning of the project by PUI’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) unit together with the technical teams and programme staff, in line with the proposed indicators defined in the intervention logical framework. Tools and monitoring activities detailed in the M&E plan will provide regular feedback on the progress towards the proposed results and allow for swift adjustment if needed. A dedicated MEAL Activities Schedule will also be prepared and followed up by the MEAL Manager.
Data collection and storage tools will grant the highest level of data protection and confidentiality, allowing a systematic disaggregation per sex, age and disability and providing automatic reporting features. While PUI MEAL team will ensure the design, development and maintenance of internal Indicator Tracking Tables and Databases, a wider integration with the MoPH Health Information System (Phenix) will also be pursued, allowing an additional layer of data triangulation between different sources and thus enhancing the overall data quality and accuracy.
 
Programme monitoring will combine different methodologies, based on qualitative and quantitative approaches, including field visits and surveys occurring on a regular basis. Their roll out will be ensured under the supervision of the MEAL Manger, which will be in charge of the design of the tools, the management of the MEAL Officers in the bases, and of the data analysis and report writing and dissemination. In particular:
Patient Satisfaction and Post Intervention Surveys will be conducted at least twice during the project implementation period in order to gather feedback from pregnant women on their perceptions about the quality and the outcomes of the services received, their feeling about topics such safety and accessibility as well as the patient centred approach supported by PUI. While based on a quantitative approach, these surveys might also include qualitative data collection methodologies such as Focus Groups Discussion and in-depth interviews, depending on the context.
Post Distribution Monitoring exercises will be regularly carried out in order to monitor cash and NFIs distribution, focusing on outcome and process related research questions, including direct feedback from beneficiaries about the items distributed and, potentially, complaints to be addressed.
In specific circumstances preventing direct access to the project areas, such as COVID 19 related movements restrictions decided by the GOL or civil unrest, measures will be taken to shift these activities to remote modalities (phone calls, reduced sample sizes, online FGDs, etc.)
 
Dedicated capitalisation activities, to be conducted at least every six months, will include Lessons Learnt workshops and/or project reviews, to be facilitated by the MEAL unit and involving technical and field teams. Such activities will be carried out against specific ToRs and will focus on detailed learning agendas and evaluation questions; best practices, implementation challenges and ways forward will be identified and discussed; capitalisation reports will be issued and disseminated to all relevant stakeholders.

project_name: Provision of integrated and comprehensive primary healthcare services for vulnerable populations in Lebanon
project_objective:
The proposed project aims at improving access to quality, affordable and comprehensive primary health services for vulnerable populations in Lebanon. Given the current deteriorating economic situation in Lebanon – vulnerable populations have become more at risk of being unable to access healthcare in Lebanon. These populations include Lebanese, Palestinian refugees residing in Lebanon, and migrants that are becoming increasingly unable to afford or access healthcare in Lebanon. This compounded with a potential fourth wave of the COVID-19 on the horizon – immediate intervention is required in order to ease the health impact on beneficiaries as well as ensure continuity of operations for Primary Healthcare Centers (PHCCs).

For health activities, IMC will work with 4 PHCCs: Al Moasat PHCC (South), Al Amir Medical Center (Akkar), Nahda Bedawi (Tripoli) and Bar Elias PHCC (Bekaa). These centers have been selected due to the high density of vulnerable Lebanese as well as a considerable size of migrant populations in the areas. Our data has shown a 9% increase in demand for IMC services by vulnerable Lebanese in July 2021 in comparison to the same month the previous year. The support to these 4 PHCCs will include: increasing the hours of operations for PHCCs by 4 hours a day 5 days a week by providing salary support for physicians, nurses, data entry clerks, and other personnel and running costs, secondly, donating essential acute medications as per the Ministry of Public health (MoPH) essential medication list, lastly, IMC will be providing PPE’s for the healthcare providers at the PHCCs in order to be able to provide high-quality services in a safe manner for both the health staff and the beneficiary. IMC will be recruiting and training Lebanese HOVs from the target population in order to disseminate and provide health awareness on IMC services to vulnerable Lebanese communities and migrants - as well as identify cases requiring primary healthcare and referring them back to the PHCC.

IMC Mental Health and Psycho-Social Support (MHPSS) team currently support 20 Case Management (CM) teams based in 20 PHCCs across Lebanon aiming to strengthen the integration of MH into PHCCs. CM teams consist of full-time case managers, part-time psychotherapists and psychiatrists. MH services including PSS with case managers and consultations with psychotherapists and psychiatrists are provided to beneficiaries free of charge to beneficiaries from all nationalities and age groups. Cases that require hospitalization are referred to MH psychiatric wards. Under this project, IMC is proposing to complement MHPSS provided at the 20 centers by procuring additional psychotropic medications to be provided as part of MH case management services to the MH beneficiaries from the target population group including Lebanese and migrants as well as assisting coverage of inpatient care when needed. No additional budget is needed for either specialized services or running costs and these medications will be used to complement the services provided for free. Case managers will be able to conduct closed group awareness raising sessions for the target community (which will also target PwDs) to decrease stigma and promote accessibility to MHPSS services.

IMC is planning to procure acute and psychotropic medication which will be donated to the PHCCs. IMC will coordinate with MoPH to complement quantities and try to plug gaps in the MOPH supply chain. IMC patients (14,400) will also benefit from MoPH medications. IMC will run a detailed assessment, quantities will be shared with MoPH for coordination of numbers and specifying the number of PHCCs to be covered as well as the duration of coverage and timeframe. At the PHCC level, medications will be dispensed free of charge and only upon medical prescriptions. IMC has partnered up with agencies that can help with international procurement and will be actively using this chain of supply rather than rely on local markets.

project_name: Emergency Shelter, NFI and Protection Assistance to Vulnerable Households in Benishagul Gumuz, Oromia, SNNP, and Somali regions
project_objective:
IOM as Shelter and NFI (S-NFI) Cluster Lead Agency (CLA), plans to reach up to 495,993 vulnerable individuals (90,181 households) whose capacity to anticipate, cope with and recover from conflict stresses have been eroded. To respond to the lifesaving humanitarian needs faced by an estimated 8.9 million persons across the country where as SNFI cluster plans to targets around 5 million persons (1.3 million in Afar and Amhara region (360,260 in Afar and 955,230 in Amhara region). These most vulnerable individuals are the one who are unable to support themselves with lifesaving shelter and non-food items. The targeted communities include newly displaced persons, IDPs in protracted displacement in camps and collective centers, IDPs living with host communities, and affected non-displaced host communities.  The proposed activities are designed in line with HRP strategic objectives 2022, as well as the S-NFI Cluster objectives and key activities.
IOM has extensive experience in Shelter and NFI responses in both emergency and post-crisis environments. IOM has static presence across Afar and Amhara and currently responds to humanitarian needs. IOM is the ES/NFI Cluster lead agency which conducts assessments and training for local authorities and Cluster Partners on ES, NFI, cash assistance. IOM supports SNFI Cluster partners through the provision of in-kind ES and NFI kits as well as supportive supervision. 
IOM provides integrated programing alongside health, CCCM, MHPSS, Protection and WASH responses. Delivering Shelter assistance, Housing, Land and Property (HLP) support including ES/NFI assistance to vulnerable communities maximizes the impact of the project in these locations. 
•	Improve access to ES and lifesaving NFIs through in-kind and Cash-Based Interventions. IOM response will provide SNFI assistance to new IDPs, protracted IDPs in camps and collective canters, returnees, PWSN (including Disability and Inclusion (DI) kits) and host community member requiring assistance.
•	Support SNFI Cluster partners through provision of in-kind ES and NFI kits (including DI ES and NFI kits), funding for their response, focus on SNFI Cluster partner capacity building and focus on support to NNGO partners.
•	Upgrade/rehabilitation/maintenance of shelter, in camps and CCs, through both in-kind and CBI;
•	Strengthen evidence-based programming through improved monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning. 
•	Mainstream gender, protection/GBV, HLP, environment and AAP in all activities. The specific needs of women will be taken into consideration in the provision of SNFI supplies to populations, IDP in camps, returnees and host communities. IOM will prioritize households headed by women for in-kind and CBI SNFI support. 
•	Strengthen the capacity of SNFI Staff on emergency and settlement programming, CBI, gender, data quality assessment, AAP and Protection; 
•	Undertake market assessment and multi-sectoral risk and needs assessment
•	Provision of in-kind life-saving ES and NFIs based on need assessment and verification
•	Provision of cash for rent and cash for emergency NFIs 
•	Undertake Monitoring and evaluation through baseline, post distribution monitoring and end-line assessment
•	Undertake Safety Audits and Protection Mainstreaming awareness raising
IOM will target 10 percent of vulnerable host communities in need of support with essential ES/NFI. Including vulnerable host community members within caseload as part of needs-based targeting to improving social cohesion. Considering the COVID-19 pandemic, the proposed project will take into account public health advice to limit beneficiary exposure.

project_name: Protection Response for Vulnerable Lebanese and Other Resident Populations
project_objective:
According to the LCRP (2017-2020), child mothers, early married girls, unaccompanied and separated boys and girls, women and girls with disabilities, older women, and female heads of households continue to be the most at risk. The most commonly reported type of GBV as reported in the GBVIMS and IMC data from its work across Lebanon involves physical violence, mainly linked to violence within the family, sexual violence (rape and sexual assault), as well as forced and early marriage. Protection risks for all targeted populations remains high, with women and girls facing significant risks of multiple forms of GBV. The economic insecurity combined with different levels of crisis affecting the country as well as risks related to legal status, add to these vulnerabilities.

GBV is a pervasive public health and human rights issue, affecting the physical and psychological health of survivors, as well as the health and well-being of families and communities. Throughout the health and economic crisis that Lebanon is going through, the frequency, severity and risk of GBV, especially affecting young women and girls is increasing. Preventing, mitigating, and responding to GBV in emergencies is a lifesaving priority and an essential component of humanitarian action, especially in a country with extreme structural gender inequalities. Lebanon ranks 145 out of 153 countries in the World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Report.

The below proposed activities focus on survivor-centered care with case management teams working with local actors in order to meet the immediate, lifesaving needs of women and girls while laying the groundwork for survivors of GBV, their families and their communities to recover. Under Indicator 1.1, the project will be providing non-focused PSS for 375 participants, dignity kits to 3000 beneficiaries and awareness sessions to 1725 non-unique beneficiaries. There will be an overlap of beneficiaries for this activity where beneficiaries that attend non-focused PSS activities will also be attending awareness sessions (this also applies for the recipients of the dignity kits).  Under Indicator 4.1, IMC will be providing case management and focused PSS for 260 beneficiaries. As part of GBV case management, emergency cash assistance will also be offered. IMC will provide the services in four safe spaces, 2 in Akkar, 1 in Beirut and 1 in the South. GBV department is well established in these areas with well-trained Case managers and Social workers.

Based on IMC’s safety audits previously conducted, focus group discussions implemented in the area and PDM reports, the objectives of the ERP directly address the needs of the communities especially vulnerable women and girls. IMC will organize empowerment activities for women and adolescent girls and will also reach men and boys in awareness raising activities. IMC will coordinate with local actors, authorities, and other sectors to strengthen GBV prevention and response and will continue working with communities to shift social norms that contribute to GBV and threaten the protection and wellbeing of women, girls and individuals at risk.
