project_name: Emergency Nutrition Response for people affected with drought and conflict in Borena zone, Oromia- Ethiopia
project_objective:
CARE has planned to respond to Nutrition need of communities in Borena zone of Oromia region who are affected by food insecurity and under nutrition that happened due to climate change induced drought, desert locust infestation (DLI) and human conflict. Drought, shortage of clean water and occurrence of other emergencies in the proposed woredas has led to the emergence of multiple public health concerns such as undernutrition, and other health problems. Multiagency rapid assessment conducted Nov. 2021 in Borena zone indicated that the last “Gena” rain able to support only 30% of the expected production. The assessment also noted that “Hageya” rain which was supposed to rain b/n mid sept. to Nov. was totally failed in most of the woredas including those proposed for this response. Due to shortage of enough rain fall during the last rain season (Hagaya) dreadful pasture condition was observed in all the visited woredas. Particularly enormous land degradation and the resultant pasture depletion is common in most woredas due to the prevailing drought. In addition, DLS is also reported in 7 woredas, including those proposed for this response, and fueling the scarcity of pasture. Communicative effect of drouth and DLI, that hampered availability of water and pasture, resulted in emaciation and death of livestock mainly cuttle, which are livelihood back bone of the community in Borena. The assessment indicated that over 69,008 livestock died, and 114,264 are emaciated with high likelihood of dying. Of the total livestock death, 5622, 4231, 19469 and 7055 are in Guchi, Wachile, Dillo and Dubluk respectively where this project planned to support. Subsequent effects of the drought and the death/deterioration of livestock has led to serious food insecurity and under nutrition. This situation has been raising the need for humanitarian intervention primarily Nutrition and Health among others. The government of Ethiopia in coordination with UN agencies and INGOs has been providing support. Yet, the support is far less than the need and the strain of health service provision including nutrition continue to exist because of increasing cases of acute malnutrition and in adequate local capacities. Therefore, CARE proposes Emergency Nutrition support to communities affected by acute under nutrition, children, and women in particular, in Guchi, Wachile, Dillo and Dubluk woredas.
The project will also mainstream protection to the nutrition response by integrating PSAE, and protection of GBV. Basic PSAE/GBV training will be provided to HWs and community volunteers, Individual and group counseling on PSAE will also be provided to target community by the trained HWs and volunteers. The project will also establish and support network of reporting to law enforcement body of any SAE and GBV incidents in the project operation area.
This is secured 6 month project funded by OCHA which started in 15 March 2022  with end date 14 September 2022. CARE is implmenting this project in four woredas Guchi, Wachile, Dillo and Dubluk) of  Borena zone.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Health and Protection response for communities affected with Drought and conflict in Chinakson district, East Hararghe, Ethiopia
project_objective:
Ethnic conflict between Jarso/Oromo and Geri/Somali has been ongoing for many years but was historically resource-based with minimal civilian displacements. Since 2015 the nature of the conflict has changed. Destruction of property, mass displacements, and occupation of land have become more common. The security situation along the border of Chinaksen woreda, Oromia Region and Tuliguled Woreda, Somali Region has been volatile since 2017. Large civilian displacements began in 2017 because of the worsening conflicts. A series of peace-building efforts in July 2019, involving traditional leaders and government authorities, resulted in the return of over 25,000 Jarso people to Tuliguled and around 42,000 Geri people to Chinaksen5. Since then, minor clashes have been reported along the regional border, occasionally causing injuries and casualties. The continued movement of people across the regional border, ongoing tensions between ethnic groups, and the increasing severity of clashes is leading to growing concerns for the safety of host communities and IDPs.
Immediate resource mobilization is required to address the urgent needs of the affected populations. Emergency food relief, protection, and emergency health responses are top priorities for the affected populations. Some IDPs are still living in makeshift shelters, exposing them to the elements and increasing their risk for communicable diseases. Damages to critical infrastructure, such as health facilities and water systems, remain critical challenges for IDPs and host communities. Furthermore, there is a need to encourage peacebuilding activities to address the underlying issues causing tensions in the area. Strategies for the eventual return of IDPs also need to be developed to encourage voluntary return.
CARE has proposed multi-sectoral emergency response to address the priority health and protection needs of IDPs and host community. Mothers and children not getting proper health services at the woreda, due to lack of equipment and trained health professionals and some of the health facilities are damaged due the conflict. As the IDPs and returnees are in dire situation, there might be protections and GBV risks around the collection sites. 
This project is secured project which implementation already started in March. The project funded by OCHA and a 7 month project to be implemented in East Hararghe zone Chinalsen woreda.

project_name: Emergency WASH and ERD assistance for host and IDP.
project_objective:
East Bale is one of the Zones found in Oromia Region that newly established a year ago.  Out of seven Rural woredas five woredas   are in lowland, desert, semi-desert weather conditions. In these woredas More than 80% of population are pastoralist that depends on livestock as main economic source and livelihoods. East Bale Zone experiences two rainy seasons, Gena   and Arfasa. Gena lasts from fourth week of August to November while the Arfasa season extends from March to May. Dawe Sarar and Lagahidha are some of the lowland Woredas extremely hard hit by the drought. Following the extreme drought in the Zone, IRC has approached a donor and secured fund from Ireland Government to intervene this drought through deploying relevant and experienced staff. The expected output of this project is Reduced mortality and morbidity and increased recovery and resilience of drought affected people in Dawe Serer and Lagahidha Woreda of East Bale Zone, This will be achieved through provision of multi-sectoral humanitarian response, such as disbursement of unconditional and unrestricted cash transfer which enables the community to purchase basic need as per their choose and provision of safe water supply to targeted drought affected community in order that reduce school dropout rate cased due to drought. The IRC will implement the proposed intervention through close coordination with government and non-government partners in the region to effectively implement the lifesaving interventions across the Two targeted woredas where drought highly affect the community.
The duration of the project is for six months (March 01, 2022, to Aug 31, 2022) and 28140 (Male 13849& Female 14291) individuals will be benefited.

project_name: Emergency WASH and ERD assistance for host and IDP.
project_objective:
According to the Assessment report by IRC’s Addis Ababa Emergency Response   Technical Team in collaboration with the East Bale Zone Drought Impact Task Force in Dawe Serer, Legahidha and Sewena Woreda, in January,2022, a total of 114,788 people and 720,200 livestock are in extreme need of emergency assistance. The zone has seven woredas and one town with a total population of 717,929 people of which five of the Seven woredas are pastoralist woredas and known for their food insecurity and WASH challenges. With support from Sida under HFA V Year 1 RRM funding, IRC Ethiopia’s Adama Field Office has implemented an integrated lifesaving WASH and economic recovery intervention reaching 40,000 affected clients through water trucking, water scheme rehabilitation, hygiene promotion, water line connections with health and school facilities, and provision of unconditional multipurpose cash response for the critically affected people by drought in Legahidha and Sewena of East Bale and Shalla and Siraro of West Arsi. The project was designed based on the rainy season bringing rain. This intervention has phased out to end on March 9th, 2022, but with the continuation of the drought, the humanitarian needs are still acute and are getting worse, putting a greater number of people in need of assistance.
IRC proposed a project with the continuation of the recently ended SIDA project aiming that People affected by climate shocks are protected from Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) related diseases.  And  meet their basic needs and avoid negative coping strategies, The IRC will achieve this aim by increase access to safe drinking water to a high number of people through water trucking, minor maintenance of two water schemes (hand pumps), Expansion of two pipeline, intensive hygiene promotion activities and the provision of essential hygiene kits to 800 households (HHs) including child-headed households, women-headed households and other vulnerable households like people living with disabilities, elderly and those living with HIV/AIDS. Simultaneously, the project will provide unconditional multipurpose cash assistance either through bank account or the cash in envelope modality (administered by the Financial Service Providers (FDPs)) for the most affected 1980 HHs, to support them to access their basic needs which includes but not is limited to food, health care services, scholastic materials for their children, milling costs among others. The modality will be decided based upon FSPs’ availability to deliver cash and the preference of the beneficiaries.by doing the proposed activity a total of 6,071 HH or 30,355 individuals without double counting will be Benefited with in the coming Six Months( 15th March to 15th of Septemper,2022)

project_name: Ethiopia Joint Response 2022 / 2023 (in partnership with INGO_IRC at Fedis woreda in WASH sector)
project_objective:
Historical resource-based conflicts - over water and grazing land - have been prevalent between communities across boundary areas between Oromia and Somali regions. Since 2017, ongoing inter-communal conflicts between Jarso/Oromo and Geri/Somali peoples along the Oromia/Somali regional border have aggravated the situation leading to recurrent and massive displacements and populations from both groups fled boundary areas into their respective regions. The conflicts in 2017 severely damaged critical infrastructure (water, health, education)  and  there  have  been  few rehabilitation  efforts since. A  series  of  peace-building  efforts  in  July  2019, involving  traditional  leaders  and  government  authorities,  resulted  in  the  return  of  over  25,000  Jarso  people  to Tuliguled/Somali and around 42,000 Geri people to Chinaksen/Oromia. Since then, some improvements were observed but conflict restarted in July 2021 with over 8,370 new displacements (OCHA, flash update east and west hararge zones Oromia, as of 9 september 2021).

According to Multi agency WASH Assessment conducted between Feb.27- March 04/2021 in Oromia region including East Harrarghe zone, the number of IDPs in the region is increasing due to ongoing displacement due to security. Exiting and new IDPs and returnees are in need of WASH services. Moreover, over 2 million people including IDPs and returnees in Bale, East Bale, Borena and East Hararghe are facing critical water shortage due to extended drought.
East  Haraghe  zone  wash  cluster  in  collaboration  with  partners  working  in  the  zone conducted joint WASH need assessment  from 8-13 June 2021, to know the depth of the impact in order to advise an evidence-based  lifesaving  humanitarian  response. In  all  the  visited  woredas (Fedis, Kumbi, Gola Oda, Meyu, Chinaksen, Gursum, Deder , Goro Gutu, Midhega Tola, and Jarso), coverage  for  potable  water  is  very  low,  below  50%  at  all  level while coverage goes down to 35% in some woredas. Huge number of non-functional schemes is aggravating lack of access to water. Women and girls are forced to travel 6-8 hrs to fetch water and being exposed attacking by dangerous animals are reported. 
According to the available need assessments, the proposed location is Fedis Woreda, Fedis is one of the woreda in the Oromia region of Ethiopia. Part of the East Hararghe Zone, Fedis is bordering on the southeast by the Erer River which separates it from the Somali Region.
Fedis district consist 19 kebeles including  one  kebele  of  Boko  town. The woreda population is estimated nearly 133,382.  
The project goal is to provide dignified support and save the lives of conflict affected communities in Fedis woreda through water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion and WASH NFIs interventions. The major outcome of the project will be to improve WASH needs of the target people through access to improved and standard WASH services. To achieve the expected project outcomes, ANE will  closely coordinate with IRC and consult with the donor, target communities, local and regional authorities, WASH Cluster, UNOCHA,  and all other concerned stakeholders during the  project life cycles starting from project planning, implementing, supervision and monitoring phase.

project_name: Life Saving emergency WASH and basic needs   for drought affected community in East Bale Zone
project_objective:
IRC assessment identified a significant number of livestock deaths, highly weakening livestock, and mass migration in search of water and fodder.  As of January 2022, the number of reported livestock death was: 37,722 in Dawe Sarar, 368 in Lagahidha, and 847 in Dawe Kachen,. According to the July 2021 hot-spot classification done by the National Disaster Risk Management Commission, a total of 126 woredas in Oromia including targeted woredas, and 71% of the districts in the East Bale Zone are classified as hotspot priority 1and in need of urgent response.

The IRC proposed intervention will be implemented to support drought affected communities in three woredas (districts) namely Dawe Serer, Legehidha and Sewena woredas of East Bale Zone, oromoiya region, Ethiopia. The IRC has prioritized and select these woredas for project intervention after analysis the avialabe data and in consultation with the main partners - regional government bureaus. Some of the main rationales considered for geographical targeting includes complement and synergy with ongoing IRC projects for better impact, scale and magnitude of the drought and its impact, multifaceted crisis (drought, conflict induced IDPs and returnees), limited number of active partners and responses, etc.  
The project aims People affected by drought have increased access to safe drinking water and improved their awareness on sanitation and hygiene and have improved access to food and meet other basic needs and minimize negative coping strategies through provision of unconditional multipurpose cash response in Dawe Serer, Legehidha and Sewena woredas of East Bale Zone. the project will be implemented in the coming Six months and 20901 individuals will be benefited.

project_name: Emergency WaSH Response to drought & conflict Affected communities in Amhara, Afar, Tigray, Oromia & Somali Regions
project_objective: Save the children, International (SCI) plans to provide emergency response in 40 Woredas in Amhara, Afar, Tigray, Somali & Afar regions. SCI in line with the cluster recommended response strategy would propose a full package WaSH response that ensures that the conflict-affected communities will access supports of essential WASH services. This will address the identified needs & gaps of short term emergency water trucking, rehabilitation of water facilities (shallow/hand-dug wells, springs & pipelines), replacement of damaged/non-functional electro-mechanical items, provision of water treatment & testing supplies, training of water management committees & provision of a maintenance kit. SCI will provide gender-sensitive sanitation facilities including emergency pit latrines with hand washing to IDP settlement & semi-permanent latrines in selected priority HCFs with cleaning products. SCI will also train CHVs on key good hygiene practices and cascade awareness raising through hygiene promotion to the IDP & host community through house-to-house visits, health education at HCFs, and mass campaigns. Selected most vulnerable households will be provided with basic WaSH-NFI supplies including Jeri cans, soaps, buckets & water treatment chemicals.

project_name: Emergency nutrition response in  drought  and conflict affected woredas of   Afar ,Amhara,Oromia,Somali, SNNPR,Sidama and Tigray,Ethiopia .
project_objective: The overall objective of this response plan is to increase access to quality nutrition services in targeted woredas both for IDP and host communities. The Nutrition response will support health centers and health posts to improve access to and quality of IMAM services (TSFP, OTP and SC) and  provide quality emergency nutrition services for the most affected and marginalized groups, regardless of their status (returnees or IDPs and host communities). To improve access to quality therapeutic feeding center, SCI planned to establish /strengthen OTP and  SC in existing health facilities in targeted areas. To ensure access to community in hard to reach area, the project support mass nutrition screening campaign on monthly with logistic, finance and technical support. To enhance referral of identified SAM cases, the project support referral mechanism with provision of fuel for ambulance and with covering perdiem for ambulance driver. The nutrition action will promote optimal IYCF-E practices for U5 children and PLW with a focus on exclusive breastfeeding, appropriate complementary feeding and promotion of micronutrient supplementation both at facility and community level through strengthening individual counseling, establishment of M2MSG and mass awareness creation.

project_name: Emergency response for drought-affected households in Somali region
project_objective:
The purpose of this project is to protect and sustain core-agricultural livelihoods and enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Somali region . A total of 15,000HHs across selected Woredas of Somali region will be benefited from this project. A total of 8 woredas are selected.  These woredas are prioritized for this project due to the magnitude of draught impact on livelihoods, SCI interventions areas on other  projects  and less interventions on other organizations . The purpose of the project will be achieved by implementing the following  major activity:
Provision of multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) to the most vulnerable pastoral households. 
MPCA in unconditional direct cash support that gives more flexibility to the HH on how to spend on basic needs. It respects their decision power and dignity. Multipurpose Cash Transfer estimated at $40 per household. The amount of the unconditional MPCA will be calculated to cover the minimum costs to purchase food(50% of the HH food basket), basic WASH items and other HH items and transport to support a family of five.  MPCA transfer values be will be calculated based on the Somali region multi-sector MEB developed by the CWG Group.
Beneficiary targeting will be carried out closely with local authorities and communities. Awareness creation will be done with families to avoid diversion of the money on items that may not benefit the family and concentrate on food and non-food items which can contribute for nutritional and HH livelihood improvement. Cash distribution sites will be selected with active community participation at nearby or short walking distances. Elders, PLWs, and PwDs will get priority services and special support will be provided by CVs. SC will work with the bank which have corporate agreement for cash transfer program to improve services and facilitate for the beneficiaries to access cash from nearby points/cashiers.  Market assessment will be done before the project implementation. 
PDM assessment will be conducted jointly with local government to understand how the process went and address issues. A complaint and feedback mechanism will be established by SC in the target villages, through beneficiaries can confidentially share their concerns and complaints related to the program as well as report on the behavior of our staff. The proposed intervention  is environmentally friendly intervention. SC will teach the community not to harm the environment during the program implementation. MPCA do not have any negative impact on the environment rather it will have positive impact to protect the natural resources. If the affected HHs received money for their basic needs, the vulnerable HHs will not damage the natural resources  to secure their basic needs,

project_name: WASH and agriculture support to communities affected by displacement in Somali Region
Life saving emergency nutrition response
project_objective:
World Vision designed this nutrition response to respond to the emergency needs of the people in the prioritized hot spot districts of East and West Hararghe Zones of Oromia region. The selection of the districts is based on hotspot priority for nutrition responses and the current SAM caseloads in the woreda. Given the current COVID-19 pandemic, needs across health and nutrition are expected to increase as movement is restricted, livelihood opportunities decrease, and prices of food and basic necessities inflate. Effective emergency response requires the implementation of nutrition response program at both the facility and community levels in order to maximize the desired impact.
The health systems will be supported to identify and treat malnourished children, and the intervention will support children in need of Infant and Young Child Feeding practices and malnourished pregnant and lactating women. 
The overall objectives of initiating this response is to provide timely access to live-saving quality treatment of acute malnutrition for children under 5 (CU5) and pregnant and lactating women. In addition, the response will strengthen the capacity of Woreda Health Offices (WHOs) to improve systems for malnutrition response.
The response will intensify MUAC screening among affected households and population for early case detection and treatments. The response will strengthen referral of malnourished cases to health facilities from the IDP sites/camps and host communities. An intensified community sensitization on key IYCF practices, hygiene promotion, and health seeking behaviors will be promoted. The response will support in repositioning of nutrition supplies and drugs for the treatment of malnourished children and PLW. Nutrition services are also strengthened in outreach and IDP sites in collaboration with the woreda health offices.
In all the targeted woredas, WASH services like creating access to water supplies in health facilities, clean and safe sanitation in health facilities, hand hygiene facilities at points of care and at toilets; and appropriate waste disposal systems are implemented. WV has also Integrated livelihood and Nutrition Security (ILaNS) nutrition response in Melka Belo through Private Non-Sponsor (PNS) Canada support. World Vision’s livelihood strategies focuses on equipping and empowering families to overcome uncertainties in practical and sustainable ways; It also equip smallholder farmers to develop productive and resilient livelihoods and in managing the natural resources around them.
Hence, World Vision Ethiopia is proposing emergency nutrition response in the three woredas to implement the minimum package of nutrition interventions. (July-2021 to June 2022) intends to provide nutrition interventions to treat malnourished children, children in need of Infant and Young Child Feeding practices support, and malnourished pregnant and lactating women in order to build their immune response to disease, including COVID-19.

project_name: Integrated Multisctoral response for Conflict and Drought affected communities in Gedeo Guji, Bale and Sidama areas
project_objective: Through this modification, World Vision intends to provide life-saving multi-sectoral response to alleviate the impact of recurrent drought on the affected communities in five woredas; Melka Soda, Dugda Dawa, and Suro Berguda in West Guiji Zone and Goro and Seweyna woredas in Bale Zone, as well as ask for an extension of the phase I activities until December 31st, 2022. Access to safe water supply through water system rehabilitation and household water treatment, construction/rehabilitation of household and institution of latrines and handwashing sites, training community leaders on positive hygiene and sanitation practices, and providing urgently needed essential WASH items will help drought affected people in West Guji and Bale.

project_name: Lifesaving Emergency Health Response for Conflict Affected Communities of East and West Wollega Zones
project_objective:
In alignment with EHF 2021 2nd round strategic allocation document, WVE designed this project to respond to the emergency needs of the people in Oromia region of East Wollega zone (Kiramu , Gida Ayana and Gutu Gida Woredas ) and West Wollega zone (Guliso, Mana Sibu and Kiltu kara Woredas).

WVE will deploy six Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT), one per each Woreda in the two zones.. One MHNT will consist of five health workers and will include: one Health Officer, one Outpatient Therapeutic Patient/Stabilization Center (OTP/SC) Nurse, one Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) Officer, one Midwife, and one GVB, Psycho social and Mental Health Officer. MHNT is expected to act as temporary and /or outreach clinic for OPD consultation like ANC, PNC, labor and delivery, screening of GBV survivable, child and neonatal illness, communicable and non-communicable infectious diseases, referral linkage and other common lines under their respective Woreda or catchment area. The project will support the transportation and distribution of Emergency Drug Kit (EDKs), cholera kits, reproductive health kits, trauma kits, and other medical supplies from SWAN /WHO/UNICEF/UNFPA warehouses to 36 targeted health facilities. 

WV will work in collaboration with district health authorities and communities to support the populations that have suffered from the conflict have access to mentally/psychologically services through enhancing the referral system. Given the especially high levels of health and protection concerns for women in in West and East Wollega of Oromia region, WV expects the needs to be high over the project period. The project will work towards creating referral linkages to an estimated 180 GBV survivors out of these 72 need referral for further investigation, diagnosis and management at referral center .The GBV officer (from protection team) within each of the MHNTs will ensure a response to the health needs of survivors of gender-based violence. The officer will help the women in a way that is supportive, helps to meet her needs, and prioritizes her continued safety without intruding on her privacy. The GBV officer will immediately refer survivors with life-threatening or severe conditions for emergency treatment, otherwise, the GBV officer will screen, diagnose, and provide PSS for less critical cases on site. All survivors will be referred for further clinical care to the nearest health facilities with referral slips. WV will provide PFA and GBV basic principles training for health workers and front line workers. Additionally, WV will advocate for service availability at referral sites through protection cluster for strengthening humanitarian assistance in the area and establishment of referral pathways for protection cases.
WV will support health facilities that are highly affected by the conflict and need support to resume operations. WV will also provide capacity building training to 48 health workers on Psychological First Aid (PFA and train 48 Public Health Emergency Management Task Force and health workers on outbreak control, management, and response. Additionally, 120 health extension workers (HEWs) will be trained on active surveillance, screening, contact tracing and referrals.

In response to high instances of disease outbreaks in East and West Wollega zones\, like measles and cholera, the project will work with the local health authorities. Finally, WV will strengthen Ethiopia Public Health Emergency Management’s (PHEM) response capacity on supervision and monitoring. More than 147, 962 IDPs and host communities who directly affected from conflicts will benefit from the project.

project_name: Drought Response in Borana Zone (Oromia Region), Dawa and Liben Zones (Somali Region) and South Omo Zone (SNNPR)
project_objective:
Communities in Southern Ethiopia are facing the worst drought in decades. The failure of two consecutive rainy seasons has pushed pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities towards severe food and livelihood insecurity. Loss of crops and livestock means that an estimated 1.8 million people are in urgent need of humanitarian support.
The drought has adversely affected livestock production and productivity resulting in occurrence of livestock diseases, poor livestock body condition and death of animals. Viable pastures within local rangelands are highly depleted, leading to a sharp decline in animal productivity. Cattle with poor body condition cannot be sold in the local markets, severely affecting income opportunities and purchasing power of local communities. Household cash availability levels have been negatively affected by declining livestock prices and extremely low agricultural production.
18,000 households (117,000 individuals) will directly benefit from the drought response project. The response aims to enhance the resilience-building capacity and support the livelihood restoration efforts of drought-affected pastoral communities. The project will last for six months and will benefit 3,000 drought affected Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) households and 15,000 host community households. The beneficiary breakdown is as follows: 750 IDP households and 5,250 host community households in Dawa, 750 IDP households and 5,250 host community households in Liben, 750 IDP households and 2,250 host community households in Borana and 750 IDP households and 2,250 host community households in South Omo.
The project will focus on access to supplementary animal feed and cash transfer assistance. The activities are informed and aligned with the Agriculture Cluster objectives and framework priorities, including protection of core productive assets and access to livelihoods of crises affected households, and the Ethiopian Cash Working Group (ECWG) guide on cash transfer programming.
The project is planned to be implemented in four zones of three Regions in Southern Ethiopia. The reasons for the geographic focus are: 1) severity of the drought and needs of the target population; 2) HEKS’s presence on the ground – where the organization has logistics set-up, staff that know the context and culture, institutional relationships – and capacity to respond to the drought; 3) regular engagement of HEKS in local coordination platforms; and 4) sound relationship with the local government. The project will promote localization by working together with local partner Agri-Service Ethiopia building on previous joint interventions and thus developing the capacity of the local partner to deliver emergency responses. The project will also work with Dorcas building on existing partnerships and expertise.
The project will be implemented in locations that do not increase vulnerabilities, do not facilitate forced return, and will be implemented with careful planning to ensure that all targeted groups are consulted, engaged and involved for assistance. The project will ensure the engagement of women, people with disabilities, elderly people and other vulnerable groups in the planning, implementation and monitoring of the projects inputs, outputs and results.

project_name: Emergency WASH response Borana and Guji Zone, Oromiya Region
project_objective:
The project will be implemented in Dilo, Miyo and Moyale woreda, Borana Zone and Liben Woreda Guji Zone, Oromiya Region, where due to conflict 35,311 persons are displaced and in urgent need of humanitarian assistance, especially in the area of access to water, sanitation and hygiene services. The project will last for six months and will benefit all the 29,228 internally displaced persons (IDPs) in the target area and 18,033 host community members. The project activities will focus, construction of 10 semi-permanent latrines benefitting 2,000 IDPs, hygiene promotion and delivery of 500 essential WASH Non-Food Item (NFI) packages, including provision of 1,000 Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) kits for adolescent girls, benefitting 3,250 people, rehabilitation and maintenance of 4 water schemes (motorized scheme) and training of WASHCOs, providing access to safe water to 23,000 people. The proposed project will also promote the practice of adequate hand washing and environmental sanitation to mitigate potential outbreaks of water-borne diseases, including cholera, and curb the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.
To further promote equity, the project will ensure regular consultation of women, PWD (17.6% of the total beneficiaries), elderly people and other vulnerable groups. Staff will follow the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action framework to uphold the rights of children. Project events on WASH will include sessions on gender, children rights, and equity to create long-lasting awareness. The project will promote equitable access to humanitarian assistance regardless of beneficiaries’ sex for example through accessibility of project sites to pregnant women, elders and people with disabilities. The project will also identify potential negative effect on different gender and age groups and put preventive measures in place. As a standard, HEKS follows strict Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) rules when interacting with beneficiaries. Participation of women was key during pre-project consultations and project design and will continue playing a central role during implementation and evaluation. HEKS has been implementing in the target areas for several years in different thematic areas like WASH, Cash transfer, Market system Development, Agriculture and climate and environmental projects both emergency and development programs which have an office in Yabelo. Mixed humanitarian teams including male and female members will carry out activities following a gender-sensitive approach.
The project will be implemented from the HEKS Office in Yabelo town in Borena Zone of Oromiya region. HEKS has qualified staff at field level and equipped facilities to carry out the intervention. HEKS is participating in the local Government-NGO Forum and has been very active in other forums and platforms, including the humanitarian coordination platform since late 2019, and the WASH Cluster SAG. The organization is closely engaged with other key humanitarian actors in the zone including implementing partners GPDI. The zonal and woreda offices, the DRR office and WASH Cluster have been providing information, data and advice in the process of developing this project for coordinated efforts. HEKS will further engage with locally active stakeholders to avoid duplication of effort and maximize efficiency. HEKS will work with relevant government offices/agencies and community leaders that have roles and responsibilities in humanitarian crisis preparedness and response. Coordination will occur through regular information sharing at both local (woreda, zonal and regional) level and at national level for example through 5W reports to different clusters as well as through participation in inter-agency reviews of needs and priorities.

project_name: Improving food availability and supporting resilience for Somali households affected by crisis
project_objective:
ACTED is acutely aware of the ongoing food insecurity situation facing households in many parts of Somalia. In late 2021, this serious situation has been exacerbated by conflict, forced evictions of IDPs, and ongoing drought. ACTED will save lives and improve the ability of Somali households to meet their basic needs through conditional and unconditional cash transfers to affected households. Through this project, ACTED will address food insecurity through providing unconditional cash transfers based on values from the Somalia Cash Working Group and through providing temporary employment opportunities (cash-for-work) for residents of IDP settlements. Cash-for-work provides an excellent opportunity for efficiently using funds, as funds will provide cash support to families suffering food insecurity while also funding basic improvements to local infrastructure (feeder roads, paths, local market infrastructure, fencing of water points). ACTED’s involvement in this project aims at supporting vulnerable households in Baidoa IDP sites of Bay region, El-Afweyn and Erigavo districts of Sanaag region, through unconditional cash transfers through six months of mobile money transfers. The Consortium will target the most vulnerable households with life-saving multi-purpose unconditional cash transfers. The project will specifically target populations in IPC 3, 4 and 5, especially newly displaced and worst-affected pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities. In addition, this Action seeks to provide life-saving assistance to food insecure communities in the target locations while implementing recovery and resilience activities to restore livelihoods and respond to the needs of IDPs and rural communities in Baidoa, El-Afwayne, Badhan, Diinsoor and Buurhakaba districts. 

Gender and intersecting issues (e.g, disability, pregnancy, age) are key determining factors in how displacement in Somalia is impacting populations across multiple domains. Gender norms relating to men’s and women’s societal roles and responsibilities have resulted in women and girls being disproportionately affected by displacement – and in men representing the majority of victims of intercommunal violence.  Gender is also a key factor in determining IDP’s needs and priorities, and this is particularly notable with regard to SGBV concerns highlighted earlier in this concept note and SHRH and menstrual hygiene concerns. A common challenge that IDP girls and women face is managing menstruation safely and with dignity, and a present lack of access to basic materials such as sanitary pads and underwear can lead to stigmatization (stemming from societal beliefs regarding menstruation) and further associated challenges. Insufficient resources for management of menstrual hygiene can also entail more frequent visits to public sanitation/WASH facilities, increasing risk of SGBV and disease. With regard to institutions and governance, informal governance in Somali IDP sites tends to be male-dominated unless CCCM initiatives have explicitly undertaken gender-mainstreaming interventions to improve community-led site management. In a context such as Somali IDP sites, where gender-based threats and challenges are ever-present, humanitarian programming needs to be gender-responsive – not only through targeting gender-based needs, but by ensuring that programming is thoughtfully and consultatively designed to be maximally accessible to all genders and persons.

project_name: Life-Saving Emergency WASH Assistance Conflict-Affected IDPs
project_objective:
The overall objective of these proposed interventions is to increase access to safe drinking water and provide adequate water to conflict-affected communities and promote safe hygiene and sanitation practices in Guto Gida and Sasiga woredas of the East Wollega zone, Oromia region, and Debate of Benishangul Gumuz Region of Ethiopia. 

The assessment findings indicated a critical shortage of water and the community depended mainly on seasonal water sources like rivers, hand-dug wells, shallow wells, and springs. The team visited five hand-dug wells and seven springs that are not functional. In Sasiga, Guto Gida and Debate towns, the host community is getting water from improved water sources through pipelines but due to shortages of water and access problems, the IDPs in the surrounding town have to travel to a nearby river or unprotected spring to fetch water. The assessed non- functional spring water schemes are silted up, totally damaged, or/and cannot retain water due to cracks, while the hand-dug wells had faulty hand pumps. The water bureau estimated that households survive with 1 jerry can of water per day, which means 1.5 – 2 liters per person, which is far below the minimum standard of SPHERE. The limited water resource has led to tensions between IDPs and host communities, resulted in protection concerns as girls are traveling 2-3 km to fetch water, increased the prices of water and there is an anticipated Cholera outbreak.

As an immediate response, distribution of water treatment chemicals, promotion on HH water treatment and safe water handling, provision of hygiene kits (soap, bucket, washing basin, water container, women dignity kits) to support community hygiene promotion, sanitation including the construction of emergency semi-permanent latrines at crowded villages in the three Woredas where HH who lost their shelter are temporarily living in a host community & rehabilitation of water schemes are recommended as an immediate solution. As per the information from both woredas water offices and cluster update, there is no active WASH partner in both proposed woredas. After accounting for all the acute needs, the targeted areas are still in need of access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene promotion. FIDO will work with UNICEF focal, partner, and the relevant government offices to ensure that there is no overlap and coordinate for effective resources utilization.

The project proposes to reach 45,922 beneficiaries with a total budget of 369160.14 USD. FIDO’s interventions are in line with the WASH cluster’s suggestion in terms of prioritized location, intervention types, and budget allocation. FIDO will assure close collaboration with the WASH cluster, concerned government bodies, and beneficiaries in implementing and involving them in the decision-making process of the proposed project.
Start Date: January 2022
End Date: December 2022

project_name: Emergency Protection Response in Moyale Woreda of Borena Zone and Sasiga Woreda of East Wollega zone of Oromia region, Ethiopia.
project_objective:
The proposed project is an Emergency protection response project for IDPs in Sasiga woreda, East Wollega zone and in Moyale woreda, Borena Zone, Oromia region, Ethiopia to address the critical protection needs of those displaced vulnerable individuals through prospective funding opportunities.

The Multi-sectoral Desk Review of Humanitarian Situation report for Wollega and Kamashi zones by December 2021 showed that there are greater than 200k IDPs in Wollegas , of which around 150 k is in East Wollega and more than 100k IDPs in Kamashi who require critical humanitarian assistance. These displacements are due to the intercommunal conflict in the regions which results in fear and protection issues such as family separation, GBV, freedom of movement, HLP-lack of access to agricultural land, lack of access to basic services: food, water, and sanitation, health, and nutrition, shelter, non-food items. The high prevalence of CP/GBV cases is the main protection concern in these areas as most of these survivors are not able to access services due to accessibility issues coupled with the limited presence of CP-GBV partners.

According to the Meher/Hagaya non-food assessment report from November 2021. During the rain condition in Borena zone of Oromia region in the last 2021 Belg was less in amount, erratic in distributions, sever long dry spell and early withdrawal. Meher season rain was also completely absent. Altogether loss of rain in both seasons has led to the widespread loss of livestock, pasture, and vegetables. Therefore, since these people rely on their livestock for survival including economic and social benefit the starvation of this livestock have significantly affected the livelihood of the general community. From the general community, the women, children and those with disabilities are highly burdened. Women and young girls are forced to travel a long distance to fetch water which is exposing them to gender-based violence. A significant number of young children are participating in child labor to win their daily bread for themselves and their families. According to the need, assessment are more than 13,980 children in need of various supports out of which 150 are street children who are moving from rural areas to urban to search for food. In the Borena zone and the number is increasing day today since there is a flow of children from rural to urban for searching food.  

As part of the protection response, FIDO is working towards creating community awareness on CP/GBV, conducting awareness creation on positive coping mechanisms to enhance IDPS physical and mental health, improving child protection case management systems including family tracing and reunification. Access will also be created to MHPSS and preventive intervention and protection response to improve resilience to gender-based violence (GBV). The project will also facilitate capacity building of woreda WoCYA, Social and Labor Affairs, and other responsible stakeholders and IDPs to identify, prevent and respond to CP/GBV cases. FIDO is also creating a transparent platform to address crosscutting issues such as accountability to the affected population (AAP).COVID-19 awareness creation is integrated with the project activities to prevent infection and the spread of the virus and increase vaccine awareness.

project_objective:

To mitigate site-level protection risks and improve site safety, ACTED will implement site maintenance activities, administer safety audits, install street solar lights, and will work in coordination with active protection actors on ground in order to reduce the risk of GBV. project_name: Immediate and lifesaving nutrition emergency response for host communities, affected and internally displacement peoples (IDPs) in Endafelasi and Edega Arbi districts of central zone of Tigray region and,Sekota, Aberegele and Tsegbeji woreda of Waghimera zone of Amhara region Ethiopia.
project_objective:
This EHF response aims to address the critical and emergency nutrition needs of 89,665 (Male: 23,011, Female: 66,654) most vulnerable, conflict affected and internally displaced peoples (IDPs) in Waghimera zone (Abergele, Sekota and Tsegbeji districts) and Central Tigray zone (Endafelasi and Edega Arbi districts). (TSFP), Promotion, protection and support of adequate Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF-E) practices at times of emergencies and Blanket Supplementary Feeding (BSFP).

Besides, to maximize impact and ensure continuum of care across the health system, an integrated Nutrition, WASH and Protection services will be implemented through this EHF reserve allocation on top of the existing complementary projects. project_name: Integrated Multisector Education and Protection response for Crisis affected communitieis in Tigray Amhara and Afar.
project_objective:
Although Tigray education Bureau has decided to resume formal schooling after the two and more years’ interruption due to the COVID 19 and the crisis in Tigray, the majority of the schools have different difficulties to resume the schooling. According to the school damage assessment reports, many schools at southern east Tigray have the following problems. The majority of the schools has lost their facilities/ supplies like; black board, Desks, Books, Chalk, Science kits, teaching aids, etc. They also run out of WASH facilities and they have poor access to clean water and even some of them have lost their classrooms either fully or partially which needs renovation. In addition to this, the teachers and the students are highly traumatized where they are in a high need of PSS and SEL trainings. As the teachers were away from reading, they need to be capacitated with different trainings like; pedagogical trainings, Conflict sensitive education, teaching methodologies, and so on. In this regard, the unreleased school damage assessment report also shows that 83% of schools are either damaged or looted (Education Bureau, 2022). Besides, more than 1,000 schools were damaged or looted in Tigray affecting an estimated 160,000 students. 79 Schools in Tigray, are still occupied by IDPs limiting access to education for 40,518 children, including 20,120 girls. (OCHA 2022). According to the Southeast Zone, 96,687 children (48,134 girls) were planned to attend at the six Woredas that WV has intervening on grades 0-6. Whereas the number of children who are now attending in school are 17,013 (8,662 girls) which is only 17.6%. This shows that, 79,674 (39,472), i.e. 82.4% of the children are still left out of school. The reason behand the children’s low attendances is lack of scholastic materials and lack of food which can be mitigated by scholastic material support and cash injection as motivation for attendance of school feeding if possible. In this regard, WV has best experience to accomplish this for the reason that, World Vision aspires “educated for life” for all girls and boys with strategies; Enhanced Early Readiness of Children, Enhanced Literacy Environment and Conducive School Atmosphere. To realize those expected results, WVE has been employed various appropriate working models to each result. The models include Learning Root (LR), which goes with Early Childhood Development (ECD); Unlock Literacy (UL) it goes with reading, & Basic Education Programme - Safe school and Life skills (BEP) which is for conducive schools. Those models are selected, for each model is directly associated to each immediate outcomes of the Technical Program. In turn, each model has its own well-structured pillars, which indicate how to reach to their results in a synergic manner. P
Protection interventions are also highly needed in Tigray Amhara and Afar. The severity of these conditions was confirmed by the Multi-sector need assessment (MSNA) conducted by WV in the three regions in December 2021. Across the three regions, the top three reported risks affecting boys and girls were, in order, being killed or maimed, mental health/psychosocial problems, and sexual violence. Nearly 95% of respondents in all three regions stated that there is either partial or no access to the following services: safe spaces (56%), case management (47%), and medical care for SGBV survivors (43%), and MPHSS (54%). When asked why, nearly all HHs responded that they have either no awareness/knowledge about the service or that current service providers do not prioritize these services because they are providing for more immediate needs. These facts and field realities require a critical need for protection, SGBV services, mental and psycho-social support for the affected people in general and for children and women who suffered traumatic experiences in particular. In addition, there is critical need to other basic humanitarian assistance.

project_name: Emergency Shelter& NFI response for IDPs and host communities living in Kiremu Woreda, East Wolega zone, Oromia Region. (Funded by UNOCHA/WVE)
project_objective:
The existing humanitarian crises related to the persistent displacement of people in to West and East Wellega Zone of Oromia region has resulted recurrent displacements, which leads to insecurity, access constraints, and socio-economic downturns in West and East Wellega Zone. Currently, 20,809 HH or 127,787 individuals in both East and West Wellega remain displaced in different Woredas, towns and kebeles dispersed in the host community hosting with the relatives, renting houses or living in temporary substandard local material built shelters with the support of the host community. According to Inter agency multi sectoral assessment conducted in West and East Wollega as well as Kamashi zone in August 2021, Shelter and NFI was one of the priorities reported among both the secondary and the new crisis-driven displaced persons, IDPs are living in a congested situation with 4 to 6 HH in one shelter. Rental houses are not affordable for many of them since they do not have means of income. Moreover, the impact of COVID-19 has become an additional burden for families in their struggle for survival.

This project proposal is developed with an objective of providing life-saving emergency shelter services to the conflict affected peoples in Kiremu Woreda of East wollega zone through provision of timely and appropriate cash for rent assistance and ensure that conflict affected peoples have adequate protection, safety, dignity, well-being and equitable access to the shelter solution. Hence, World Vision Ethiopia (WVE) in partnership with Action for the Needy in Ethiopia (ANE) will respond to the emergency shelter and NFI need of the IDP in Kiremu Woreda of East wollega Zone.

Accordingly, the proposed emergency shelter and NFI intervention is aimed at addressing conflict-induced displaced community in Kiremu Woreda of East wollega Zone. The project will be implemented for 6 month with a total budget of $ 280,000.

project_name: Addressing Critical Child Protection Needs of Displaced Populations
project_objective: Plan International (Plan) proposes an eighteen-month project to address critical child protection needs of displaced populations and host communities affected by the ongoing crisis in Northern Ethiopia. The proposed activity will directly benefit an estimated 17,868 children and adults in Tigray and 15,000 children and adults in Amhara through provision of psycho-social support (PSS), case management, family tracing and reunification, positive parenting programming, awareness raising, community-level child protection, and risk and service mapping. The project will contribute to increased resilience among vulnerable children, families, and communities in Northern Ethiopia impacted by displacement and the ongoing conflict

project_name: Responding to immediate life-saving nutritional needs among IDPs and their host communities in five woredas of Tigray and Amhara Region. (ETH-21/DDA-3379/RA2/N/INGO/20039)
project_objective:
This project was proposed in response to the increasing humanitarian needs among IDPs and their host
community in Tigray and Amhara regions, the project aims to decrease morbidity and mortality among
conflict and drought-affected and displaced girls, boys, women, and men in five targeted woredas of the
two Regions. It will do so through immediate and short-term emergency Nutrition assistance through the
CMAM implementation modality. The Child Protection, Gender, and key WASH component such as
Hygiene promotion, COVID-19 prevention measures including IPC at health facilities are mainstreamed
throughout the various activities of the project.
This project primarily focuses on providing life-saving Acute Malnutrition treatment, care, and support to
affected and displaced under-five age girls and boys, and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) who
are suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM). The
project will also strengthen further the local health system and build the capacity of health workers
(HWs) and health extension workers (HEWs) to respond for already doubled primary health care and
nutrition services in all targeted intervention woredas. Besides, the project strongly works with district
health offices in maximizing Family MUAC, best practices of IYCF including positive parenting, and
Mental Health and Psychosocial Supports (MHPS) throughout the implementation period of this project.
Also, survivors of Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) and a person with a disability are specifically
targeted to get appropriate and adequate health and Nutrition care and support from this project. In
addition, protection concerns are considered to be addressed through a mainstream approach in each
of the planned activities of the project such as including topics of protection and gender during the
provision of basic and in-service pieces of training for Health Workers (HWs) and Health Extension
Workers (HEWs).
Furthermore, to prevent disease outbreaks and deter underlying factors for the anticipated increased
Acute Malnutrition admission trend, PIE will increases awareness of targeted girls, boys, women, and
men on key recommended hygiene practices tailored with COVID-19 prevention measures. For
effective awareness creation Plan Int`l Ethiopia will train and use Community Social Workers (CSWs)
who will be closely working with HEWs at the grass-root level.
Furthermore, beneficiary feedback and compliance will be also addressed through establishing and
functioning a strong feedback mechanism at each kebeles of targeted intervention woredas. Beneficiary
participation will be further strengthened through ensuring participation of beneficiaries during project
start-up workshop, beneficiary selection, distribution of project input, project review meeting, and Focus
Group Discussions (FGD).

project_name: Responding to immediate life saving and critical primary health care including SRHR needs among IDPs and their host communities in 4 woredas of Afar Region. (ETH-21/DDA-3379/RA2/H/INGO/20040)
project_objective:
This project was proposed in response to the increasing humanitarian needs among IDPs and their host
community in Tigray and Amhara regions, the project aims to decrease morbidity and mortality among
conflict and drought-affected and displaced girls, boys, women, and men in four targeted woredas of the
two Regions. It will do so through immediate and short-term emergency health and Nutrition assistance
through the MHNT implementation modality. The Child Protection, Gender, and key WASH component
such as Hygiene promotion, COVID-19 prevention measures including IPC at health facilities are
mainstreamed throughout the various activities of the project.
This project primarily focuses on providing technical and logistic supports to health centers, health
posts, and Therapeutic Feeding Programmes (TFP) through Mobile Health and Nutrition Team (MHNT)
implementation modality to identify, refer and treat Severely and Moderately Malnourished children
under 5 and PLWs. Health Centers will be provided with technical and logistical support, including
transport of essential Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) supplies and
routine drugs, to successfully treat children and provide necessary follow-up. Health Workers and
Health Extension Workers will receive training on gender-aware Acute Malnutrition (AM) management
national guideline. Also, the primary health care system will be further strengthened for quality care and
support service deliveries through the provision of logistic and technical supports, emergency drugs, the
establishment of Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) corners. Disease outbreak prevention including
IYCF, COVID-19 prevention measures, and hygiene and sanitation promotion will be tailored with other
ongoing efforts by the local government and other actors. Besides, through logistic and technical
supports the project will maximize access to skilled birth attendance, SRH, and contraceptive for
childbearing-aged girls and women. In addition, specific activities are planned to provide Psychosocial,
health care, and support for SGBV and person with a disability.
Also, there will be joint supportive supervisions to provide on-the-job coaching to the Health Workers
and Health Extension Workers for strengthening their ability to implement the skills learned and provide
enhanced services to boys and girls of under-five age children and PLWs. Mothers, fathers, and
caregivers will further be given orientation on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and positive
parenting to increase their knowledge and ability to follow best feeding practices using the opportunities
of supplementary food distribution programs and Out-Patient Therapeutic Feeding Programmes (OTP)
days.
Furthermore, beneficiary feedback and compliance will be also addressed through establishing and
functioning a strong feedback mechanism at each kebeles of targeted intervention woredas. Beneficiary
participation will be further strengthened through ensuring participation of beneficiaries during project
start-up workshop, beneficiary selection, distribution of project input, project review meeting, and Focus
Group Discussions (FGD).

project_name: Integrated Emergency Shelter and NFI, WASH and Agriculture Support for conflict-affected populations in Eastern Zone of Tigray Regions
project_objective:
In 2021, conflict was the primary cause of displacement in the country. Particularly, the conflict that started in December 2020 in Tigray region with a spillover effect in the neighboring regions of Afar and Amhara in mid-2021 caused strife, limited access to basic services and displacement of a total of 2.11 million IDPs with 1.8 million in Tigray according to DTM Overview 2021. Following the conflict, despite the tremendous efforts by humanitarian partners to assist the most affected population limited humanitarian access, cash deficient, lack of electricity and telecommunications, inflation, hike of price of basic goods and services, inadequate fuel access, and movement and entry restriction to Tigray exacerbated the crisis. 
At the moment, there are 259,000 displacement affected populations in Tigray regions Eastern Zone. To fill the gaps identified in Eastern Zone, through this intervention, ZOA will address the immediate shelter and NFI needs of 8,721 IDP and Returnee households or 47,963 individuals (with the assumption of 5.5 household size) throughout the intervention Woredas selected in the Zone. Overall, a total of 2,616 (14,389) men, 3488 (19,185) women, 1221 (6,715) boys and 1,395 (7,674) girls will be reached. In Freweyni town 1,309 households (HHs) beneficiaries will receive NFI V1 kits and 145 households will receive NFI V1 disable kits for highland. In Gulo Mekeda, 3,223 HHs beneficiaries will receive NFI V1 kits, 50 households will receive Repair Kit for Returnees and 364 households will receive NFI V1 disable kits for highland.  In Saesie, 1,145 households will receive NFI V1 kits and 127 will receive NFI V1 disable kits for highland. In Erob, 2,071 HHs will receive NFI V1 kits, 50 HHs will benefit from Repair kits for Returnees and 236 HHs will receive NFI V1 disable kits for highland. 

This intervention is in line with the shelter cluster’s strategic objective of provision of safe, appropriate, and critical lifesaving Emergency Shelter and non-food items to displacement affected; improving the living conditions, physical protection, and safety of the displaced population and provision of safe, appropriate lifesaving Emergency Shelter Repair Kits to returnees. The proposed intervention will address cross-cutting themes through activities such as awareness raising on protection and gender mainstreaming and the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) in collaboration with organizations to reinforce referral systems in the project sites. Moreover, through the establishment of strong Complaint and feedback mechanisms beneficiaries will concerns and issues will be addressed in time and in a safe manner. Our beneficiary targeting approach will encourage the active participation of women, girls and other marginalized groups. 

Furthermore, this intervention will be complemented with WASH and Food security and livelihoods activities to address the most urgent needs of the conflict-affected returnee and IDP communities in Tigray region. The intervention also includes a capacity strengthening element in both the WASH and Food Security and Livelihoods sectors. ZOA will provide some resources, as well as training to relevant government stakeholders, to capacitate them to fulfill their roles as duty bearers and service providers towards their constituencies.

project_name: Gambella WASH Project
project_objective: Samaritan's Purse (SP) has reflected upon lessons learned from a current three-year water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) program nearing completion in Lare woreda, Gambella region, to develop a strategy to increase access to potable water and sustainable WASH facilities. Samaritan's Purse will seek to achieve this through the construction, rehabilitation and installation of hand and solar water pumps, water points, water pipe networks, reservoirs and communal latrines; the training of water mechanics and water user committees; the implementation of mass health, hygiene and sanitation campaigns and awareness trainings; and training people in biblical leadership and discipleship through local churches across the target areas. •	The project will reach 47,147 individuals (23,102 male and 24,044 female) across the Lare and Abobo woredas of Gambella region. All beneficiaries will be impacted by improved, clean water schemes; the same beneficiaries will receive supplemental sanitation and hygiene trainings and resources.

project_name: Life - saving GBV intervention support to women and girls in crisis, conflict, drought and shock effected regions of Amhara, Tigray and Somali region
project_objective:
The proposed intervention is envisioned to improve GBV through provision of immediate and comprehensive lifesaving services to survivors, and GBV risk mitigation for vulnerable women and girls through the following interventions: Clinical management of Rape (CMR), case management (CM); psychosocial support services (PSS) including psychosocial counselling, psychosocial first aid (PFA), social networking and access to information on available GBV services, through women and girls friendly spaces/safe spaces, and establishment and strengthening of GBV referral pathways (to enable access to comprehensive GBV services including legal, medical and livelihood services) to most vulnerable and displaced female headed and people living with disability special need in the target communities, including IDP and Host communities in the target locations of Amhara, Tigray and Somali. Alight will also strengthen GBV risk reduction through strengthening and engaging community protection groups, distribution of dignity kits, whistles to vulnerable women, girls and mobility reaching Aids and Grabbers for PLWD, provide capacity building and trainings to community volunteers/workers and GBV service providers to enhance service provision and risk reduction for women and girls, and conduct safety audits for GBV risk assessments to inform the project implementation and decisions, among other interventions. The proposed project will therefore increase accessibility, quality and coordination of GBV, and Disability services for conflict and drought affected communities in Amhara, Tigray and Somali Woradas. Alight will work with various stakeholders to ensure women and girls are protected from GBV and receive support when they experience harm. Some of the stakeholders include line ministries at state government level, the local administration, the police, and women leadership at community level, community and religious leaders and will establish protection networks for women and girls. Community action plans and protection mechanisms will be developed and implemented to reduce protection risks for women and girls including those in IDP settings. 
The project will assist in capacity building local authorities, IDP committees etc. on IDP rights/obligations. In addition, the project will also aim to mainstream protection across sectors through advice on effective implementation of protection-sensitive and rights - based approach into the relief assistance for other humanitarian actors/ clusters – PWG/All sectors, training and sensitizing duty bearers and other key stakeholder on protection concerns including GBV, and freedom and safety of movement.
