project_name: Emergency Shelter and Nonfood Items responses to conflict affected households in Tigray Region
project_objective:
Recent armed conflict in the Tigray region of Ethiopia between federal forces and regional security forces has led to extreme humanitarian need, with refugees fleeing to Sudan and widespread displacement throughout northern Ethiopia. In the first quarter of 2022, new displacements continue to take place from multiple corners of Tigray region and bordering woredas due to conflict, as well as from bordering Regions. IDPs from Western Zone, Amhara and Afar are currently living across all accessible zones in Tigray. Congestion is still an issue in the IDP collective sites, resulting in increasing cases of scabies with over 8,000 cases reported in Northwestern Zone sites only since the beginning of the year, that calls for NFI distribution and replenishment. Relocation sites are being prepared in Shire and Sheraro for IDPs from Western Zone, but progress has been slow due to material and cash scarcity. Efforts are ongoing from Cluster partners to airlift ES/NFI stock from Addis Ababa to Mekelle as well as use road transportation.
According to April report of ES/NFI Cluster, partners continued providing life-saving emergency shelter and NFI assistance to IDPs, returnees, and affected non-displaced population with 47K beneficiaries receiving NFI kits, 0.5K ES/NFI kits, 34K ES kits, 4K constructed emergency shelters, 7K shelter repair kits, to the displacement affected people in Tigray. Overall, the Cluster has been able to reach 79K individuals with completed activities which amounts to 9% of the targeted 1.3M people targeted. According to recent assessments from partners in the region, Shelter and NFI is a critical need next to food and health in the IDPs. 
UNOCHA’s displacement scenario stated that there will be as many as 1.8 million IDPs because of ongoing conflict. IDPs are currently sheltering in collective centers, open areas, damaged shelters & with host communities and most of the displaced population are women, girls, and youth. Many IDPs are living in overcrowded settlement sites and collective centers, there are protection concerns for the most vulnerable, including for women and girls at risk of gender-based violence (GBV). According to the ESNFI cluster, peoples in need in the proposed locations such as Adet woreda (1,665 HH), Enticho town (3,290 HH) and Mekelle (7,735 HH) are residing in extremely poor conditions who need urgent emergency shelter and NFI assistance. All the three woredas have IDPs whereas Mekele includes returnees.
GE assumes the project activities addresses the strategic objectives with significant positive impact on the identified needs of the respective clusters. The project activities are all a priority to the respective sectors. GE aims an in-kind or cash for non-food items assistance for IDPs and shelter repair kit assistance for returnees. To maximize the impact on the intervention, GOAL proposed this ESNFI standalone applications whereby the other GOAL Ethiopia projects are implemented with the same sectors with BHA, ECHO, UNICEF, and IA funding sources and/or proposed for standalone allocation with other sector applications in this EHF/HPC. 
The ESNFI proposed interventions for this HPC will be:
- Emergency shelter repair kits distribution for 90 HHs returnees in Mekele town.
- Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V1 highland) distribution for 8,125 HHs (1,415 in Adet, 2,650 in Enticho town and 4,060 in Mekele) IDPs.
- Emergency Non-Food Items Kits (NFI V1 disable highland) distribution for 1,259 HHs (250 in Adet, 400 in Enticho town and 609 in Mekele) IDPs.
- Conduct independent beneficiary identification and verification process based on revised SOPs considering national/regional cluster standards.
- Information sessions, establishment and roll-out of community response & feedback mechanisms.
- Conduct HLP assessment.
- Conduct regular joint and independent monitoring. 
- Conduct post distribution monitoring

project_name: Community based integrated child protection and gender-based violence assistance for the Crisis-affected communities in Afar and Amhara Regions
project_objective:
This integrated child protection and GBV response project targets three woredas in Afar region (Afambo, Asayita and Dubti woredas) two woredas in North Wello (Habru and Gubalafto woredas) in Amhara region, responding to the child protection and gender-based violence concerns exacerbated due to displacement attached with the conflict and systemic traditional practices.  The project will be implemented in partnership with Mother and Children Multisectoral Organization (MCMDO). GOAL will be responsible for the three woredas in Afar region (Afambo, Assyita and Dubti woredas) and MCMDO will intervene in two woreda in Amhara Region (Habru and Gubalafto woredas)
The project aims to make a significant contribution to the mitigation of and response to gender-based violence and child protection problems in the targeted woredas by assisting survivors to become more confident and comfortable in accessing support and strengthening the existing referral pathways. 
Both five woredas are affected by the war and received displaced persons from other conflict affected woredas. In both proposed interventions GOAL has adapted its approach and established a system to mitigate any GBV and Child protection problems and respond any possible to GBV incidences. GOAL has been implemented integrated community-based child protection and GBV response project by BHA fund we received through IRC in Asayita, Afambo, and Dubti woredas from 1 April 2021 –31 March 2022. For the last one-year GOAL Ethiopia (GE) and MCMDO have been supported GBV survivors, orphans, and vulnerable children, established Safe Spaces, and provided psychosocial support and awareness for the affected community in the three woredas in the region. GOAL was conducted baseline and endline survey to understand the protection needs and gaps in those woredas and identified that denial of resources, FGM, sexual, physical, and emotional abuses were the commonly recognized GBV type. Child marriage is also a commonly known child abuse in the area and were affecting more girls than boys. GOAL and MCMDO proposed a joint child protection and GBV intervention based on the experience we had in the field.  
The integration will be reflected in awareness-raising events planning, shared prevention messages preparations, and strategizing response activities. Besides, we will explore existing referral pathways and strengthened relationships with local service providers to improve coordination between local protection actors.
Through the provision of case management services, psychosocial supports, capacity building activities, referrals, community awareness sessions, dignity kits provision and strengthening the coordination and local capacity of the community, GOAL and MCMDO will address GBV and child protection problems in all intervention woredas and contribute to the achievement of cluster objectives. The project will reach 93,049, beneficiaries(Dubti 20471, Assayita 20471, Afambo 16749, Gubalafto 20471, Habru 14888) through this integrated child protection and GBV response project all intervention woredas.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition Response for conflict affected and Displaced Communities in Tigray Region
project_objective:
The project will respond to the Nutrition needs among vulnerable communities which have been exacerbated because conflict-induced and displacement. 
A Nutrition response consisting of Community based management of acute malnutrition (Outpatient therapeutic feeding, Stabilization center, Management of Moderate Acute malnutrition, and Community mobilization), support to strengthening and establishment of OTP and SC at Health facilities, provision of logistical and technical support in conflict affected Woredas of high levels of IDPs and returnees without access to free nutrition care. The project activities will reduce malnutrition-related morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable groups through timely capacity building, functioning of OTP and SC at health facilities and strengthening management of acute malnutrition systems by delivering Nutrition and medical supplies and materials for the targeted conflict affected Woredas in Tigray Region.

project_name: Emergency shelter and NFI support for conflict affected IDPs in Amahar and Afar Region
project_objective:
The northern conflict started in November 2020, and the tension spilled over to Amhara and Afar regions. As a result, hundreds of thousands of people are displaced and lose their assets. The situation in these regions remains volatile and unpredictable despite reported limited improvements in the security situation in some areas where fighting has recently erupted in the border areas between Afar and Amhara regions. According to the UNOCHA report, on March 31, 2022, in Amhara, the situation along areas bordering Tigray, namely in Wag Hamra, North Wollo, and North Gondar zones, remains volatile. Several locations remain hard to reach for humanitarian operations including Abergele, Tsagibji kebeles as well as some parts of Zequala kebeles in Wag Hamra Zone, large parts of Kobo in North Wollo Zone, and Addi Arkay in North Gondar. In Amhara, the regional Government authorities continued with the relocation of IDPs.Since the 14th of March 2022, it has relocated at least 12,000 people out of an estimated 58,000 registered IDPs planned for relocation from Kobo in North Wollo Zone to Jara, near Woldiya, the zonal capital. While regional authorities and a few humanitarian partners are constructing basic facilities at the relocation sites and providing essential assistance including food, there is still a huge need and setting-up proper camp structures mainly emergency shelter, water, sanitation and hygiene, health and nutrition services, and non-food items. Meanwhile, in Afar, a needs assessment was conducted in Afdera and Silsa Guyha IDP sites, where there are currently six sites managed by humanitarian partners in the two woredas, with a total of more than 34,000 people. While limited shelters and non-food items (NFIs) are provided to the IDPs, a huge gap persists with the provision of food, shelter, drinking water, sanitation and hygiene services, education service, primary health care, and NFIs, including dignity kits for women and girls, are urgently required. 
CARE has a longstanding presence in Afar and the Amhara region with different programs. Since the emergency happened, CARE has provided emergency shelter and NFI assistance for the conflict-affected peoples in South wollo, North wollo, South Gondar, and North Gondar zones.  
Hence, CARE proposed an emergency in-kind or cash for shelter and NFI and shelter repairing response for the conflict-affected peoples in Amhara and Afar regions. The objectives of the project are to improve the protection risks by ensuring the conflict-affected people have adequate safety, dignity, well-being, and equitable access to shelter solutions; and to strengthen access to appropriate live-saving Emergency Shelter and Non-food Items (NFI) to safeguard the health and protection of the displacement affected population. Through this project, 49,471 people will be targeted in Afar, and Amhara, and assisted with Emergency shelter, ESNFI and NFI and Shelter repairing kits.

project_name: Gender and Protection Response to Conflict  Affected Community in Ethiopia
project_objective:
According to the humanitarian needs overview, there are 5.8 million people in dire need of GBV prevention, mitigation and response activities majority of them women and girls. Half of the affected population is women and girls, and 6% of those are female heads of households. Women and girls continue to suffer disproportionately from GBV and violations of basic rights due to conflict, insecurity, overcrowding in IDP sites, forced relocations and returns, lack of livelihood opportunities, lack of community awareness on women’s rights as well as lack of access to response services. They are also exposed to survival sex and SEA risks due to lack of access to aid and resources.  
CARE is proposing an intervention to provide immediate and urgent SGBV priority services to conflict affected IDPs, IDP returnees and host communities within North Gondar Zone, Addi Arkay Woreda; North Wollo Zone, Kobo Raya, Meket, Habru Woredas and Woldiya town; South Wollo Zone, Dessie town and Dessie Zuria Woreda; Afar region, Zone one Chifra and Zone 4 Gulina Woreda. These woredas have been classified as ‘priority one’ for emergency response by the national GBV cluster AoR. Meanwhile, the woredas have also been in loss of lives, incidences of SGBV and displacement of households.
In addition, CARE is proposing to intervein in drought affected areas of East Harargeh Zone Chinaksen Woreda; and Borena Zone Wachile, Dilo and Dubluk Woredas

project_name: Addressing the needs of Limb reconstruction patients in Gaza
project_objective:
This project aims to address the urgent needs of Limb Reconstruction patients in Gaza, especially those who suffered from complex LR injuries as a result of the May 2021 assault on Gaza, but also those who are still under ongoing treatment at the LR unit at Naser hospital.
This project is in rhythm with Strategic Objective #2 and Health Cluster Objective #1. 
The complex limb injuries has placed high demands of the Ministry of Health to deal with, as these cases require years of treatment and are financially overwhelming. Plus, the skills' set available in Gaza are only able to meet a tiny proportion of these numbers and complexity of injuries. 
This project will aim to reduce the suffering of the LR patients via bringing medical missions from the UK (with flexibility in time related to COVID-19 restrictions), tele-medicine support, HIS support, and also via the supporting the local teams in Naser with the needed supplies to perform the LR interventions locally. The intervention is coordinated with other key stakeholders serving LR in Gaza such as MoH, WHO, MSF-F, MSF-B, MDM Spain and others.

project_name: Life-saving care of newborns in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The project meets strategic and cluster objectives:

Strategic objective 02: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

HEALTH AND NUTRITION CLUSTER OBJECTIVE 1: Ensure the availability of acceptable and quality essential healthcare services to vulnerable communities in oPt.

In general, this project will contribute to addressing the lifesaving needs for high risk babies at neonatal units in the Gaza and improving neonatal care management in order to contribute to reducing mortality, morbidity and long-term disability among newborns.

The project’s main two objectives are:

1- Saving neonatal lives by ensuring the availability of life saving items and essential infection control supplies at the neonatal units. MAP aims to achieve the project’s objectives in coordination with the Ministry of Health, UNICEF, WHO, UNFPA and other stakeholders.
2- Improving the skills and competencies of staff at the neonatal units on neonatal life support, neonatal safe transport, and infection control.

project_name: Provision of life saving drugs and disposables for trauma and NCD related illnesses to enhance the preparedness and response of health system in Gaza
project_objective:
MAP is planning to purchase a list of essential drugs and disposables to be delivered to the Central Drug Store and also to be prepositioned at MAP’s stores in order to ensure the access of trauma and NCDs patients to the treatment and medical care they need as and when needed. The lists will cover emergency and ICU items as well cardiac, oncology, and hemodialysis patients. This approach will ensure that all vulnerable people have access to essential health services without neglection or fear of diversion of funds. The project is aiming to help mitigate avoidable mortality and morbidity among the trauma and non-trauma patients. Moreover, the project will be contributing to the current emergency response projects that MAP is implementing in coordination with the health cluster and stakeholders and will be in line with the strategic objective 2 and strategic objective 3; and health cluster strategic objective #1 and #2. 
MAP will make sure that all the items are provided to all patients attending MOH facilities without any discrimination. Also, MAP is going to ensure proper safeguarding and PSEA through all of its projects. More details in the following sections.

project_name: Responding to the urgent health needs as a result of COVID-19 in West Bank and Jerusalem
project_objective:
The project aims to address the MoH and East Jerusalem Hospital Network (EJHN) needs in responding to COVID-19. MAP is continuously coordinating with MoH and EJHN regarding their needs during emergencies including the clashes that started in April 2021 in West Bank and Jerusalem as well as the COVID19 pandemic.
Through this project, MAP will procure and deliver medical supplies and consumables according to MoH and EJHN needs focusing on the needs of the groups most affected by COVID-19.

project_name: Enhancing access to essential health care services for vulnerable population in Syria
project_objective: INTERSOS Health program follows an integrated approach which is aimed at providing life-saving and life-sustaining community and primary healthcare assistance. Moreover, INTERSOS, in cooperation with the Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC) and Ministry of Health, is committed to build resilience and capacities of communities affected by the crisis in Syria. INTERSOS will implement multi sectoral actions where health will be integrated with components of Protection (including child protection and GBV) and Education. Health projects aim to achieve the following main results: strengthening skills and capacities of health personnel on PHC and diseases outbreaks (including COVID-19 related topics - IPC, Triage), enhancing access to essential health services in remote areas, raising awareness on good health behavior and practices in the Governorates of Hama, Rural Damascus, Idleb, Dar’a. The action applies a combined mobile (mainly the 2022) and static (in 2023) approach whereby static health facilities are enhanced and equipped alongside with the deployment of mobile health teams in hard-to-reach areas with no health clinic available. As a final result, access to quality PHC services for vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas will be increased and expanded. The mobile units will provide primary health care (including ANC/PNC and pediatric consultations), nutrition-integrated services (screening and IYCF), support to immunization, risk communication and active prevention awareness (for communicable and non-communicable diseases) A comprehensive capacity building program will contribute to strengthen Health Workers and first-line responders’ skills to decrease health risks, protect and assist vulnerable individuals with high-severity needs. Specific, tailored, technical trainings and capacity building sessions will be provided to SARC Health staff and volunteers as well INTERSOS community mobilizers on relevant COVID 19, health topics, PHC, common childhood illnesses, basic emergency obstetric and new-born care and health education and promotion. INTERSOS will facilitate and monitor the delivery of health services to beneficiaries through SARC health workers and INTERSOS medical staff to ensure continuity and availability of PHC services through diagnosis and treatment of common illnesses among children, PLW, adolescents, PwDs, elderly, adults according to the national protocols.

project_name: Enhancing the Protection Environment of Crisis Affected Populations Across Syria
project_objective:
INTERSOS Action tackles identified problems/unmet needs, through an integrated protection response (GP, CP, GBV, MA) targeting most vulnerable population in areas with high severity conditions (3-4 as per Protection Sector Severity & PIN_HRP 2022) in Hama, Southern Idleb, Rural Damascus and Dara. This Action aims to enhance the prevention/mitigation of protection risks and respond to protection needs through supporting the protective environment in Syria (HRP Strategic Objective 2). In 2022, INTERSOS will reach a total of 45,289 beneficiaries (G 12,454; B 10,190; W 12,454; M 10,190) across Hama, Southern Idleb, Rural Damascus and Dara. A similar projection of targeted beneficiaries is foreseen for 2023. Over 2 years, the Action aims at contributing to improving psycho-social wellbeing and self-reliance capacities of conflict-affected populations through stand-alone and integrated protection interventions. Protection activities will be implemented through a static-mobile approach and include: a) targeted protection at individual-group level for the most vulnerable children and adults: case management (CP, PWSN), in kind assistance (medical assistive devices, dignity/education/winter kits, transportation to access services) safe identification/referrals; structured and unstructured PSS activities for children and adults b) work at community level to build on pre-existing strengths and self-protection mechanisms: establishment/support of community groups, community-led initiatives, prevention/empowerment activities for women/girls; awareness raising, MRE, training and capacity building on key protection topics.  
Integrated actions include Child Protection in Education: activities are conducted directly in schools to enhance the protective environment for children through training of education personnel & PTAs; school-based structured and unstructured PSS and case management; referral to specialized services; reduction of barriers to access education and school-dropouts’ rates in addition to targeted intervention for OOSC. Protection and gender considerations are mainstreamed throughout sectoral interventions (Health/NFIs) aiming at avoiding causing harm, ensuring meaningful access, accountability, equal participation/empowerment of all affected individuals.  INTERSOS is currently working under the umbrella of the MoU with SARC jointly implementing protection activities and under the framework of MoUs with relevant Line Ministries. The MoU with MoE was signed in June 2021 and the MoU with MoSAL is at final negotiation stages as of Jan 2022. With the upcoming signature of MoU with MoSAL, INTERSOS aims at strengthening direct implementation of a full range of protection activities targeting most vulnerable groups (with a specific focus towards disability inclusion).

project_name: Integrated livelihood restoration and economic empowerment in Syria
project_objective: Considering the scale and continued rise of needs, in alignment with HRP 2022-2023 objectives, the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor (MoSAL) national strategy as well as the ERL sectors priorities, the Action aims at supporting community recovery and livelihoods and to preserve social cohesion ensuring equitable access to services and mitigating protection risks linked to low income families. For 2022-2023 planning INTERSOS aims at fully integrating livelihood into protection, health and education response, preventing and mitigating negative coping mechanisms such as school drop out, child labor, early marriage and GBV as a consequence of dire economic conditions faced by Syrian families. The Action will be implemented in the Governorates of Hama, Rural Damascus and Southern Idleb targeting newly accessible- hard to reach-rural areas. Clear criteria for BNFs selection are developed based on the vulnerability level of the individuals prioritising Female Headed Households, families with People with Disabilities and IDPs but also HHs that are unable to cover the cost of minimum expenditure resorting to negative coping mechanisms. BNFs are chosen through ongoing Education, Protection and Health intervention promoting integration and population resilience. Based on in-country experience and lessons learnt the intervention builds upon Labor Market Assessments (LMA) carried out in the targeted locations in order to fully link Vocational Training provided to to the characteristics of the labor market in order to support productive sectors and provide employable skills. INTERSOS aims at conducting a specific context analysis of the communities served through the engagement of different layers of society. This will be carried out through KIIs and FGDs involving local entrepreneurs, local authorities’ representatives and vulnerable individuals from the same targeted community (identified through INTERSOS protection-education intervention). The analysis will investigate key barriers in accessing the labor market and livelihood in specific targeted areas, the main services available and referral pathways in place, the soft skills and practical capacities needed by the beneficiaries. The context analysis will investigate the main protection risks faced by individual at risk and Persons with Specific Needs. Such analysis will be linked to the evaluation of the demand of the labor market defining possible pathways for dignified and capacitated access to it. To ensure gender balance and empowerment of girls and women entering into the labor market consultations with communities and focus groups discussion will be carried out enhancing women active participation in the choice of the training topics.  Hence, the action encompasses the following key components: 1. LMA directed at the analysis of demand and supply sides of the local labor market 2. provision of technical and vocational training to build and strengthen beneficiaries’ skills 3. delivery of business and marketing skills workshops to transfer critical skills in communication and marketing to better connect with customers, promote local products and boost business activities, 4. provision of start-up kits to trainees to foster self-employment and broaden income generating activities 5. support to micro and small enterprises in the agri-business sector by provision of assets which are necessary to increase production. As part of the action, INTERSOS is will conduct rehabilitation works in Protection Community Centers (MoSAL)aimed at enhancing accessibility for PwDs. INTERSOS staff and SARC volunteers are provided with briefing sessions on core concepts and policies related to humanitarian principles, Child Protection and PSEA. Awareness-raising sessions are delivered on hazards, risks, preventive and mitigation measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic. INTERSOS regularly coordinates at National and local level with INGOs ERL partner ensuring coordination and avoid overlapping.

project_name: Scaling up, of quality emergency healthcare services to 10,000 IDPs, returnees and host communities in Ayod County.
project_objective:
The project aims to address the problems of high morbidity and mortality rate and common diseases: Malaria, Diarrhea, Pneumonia, Measles and cholera, a situation brought about by limited number of functional health facilities, scarcity of supplies and flooding seasons, not only that, it will also reduce excessive morbidity mortality by timely detection and coordinate response to epidemic prone diseases as well as improve equitable to life-saving essential,  provision of quality comprehensive package of basic healthcare

The beneficiaries will be provided with essential primary healthcare services in static, outreaches and mobile health facilities using qualified, Clinical officers, Midwives, Nurses and other health care providers. They will also be provided with mosquito nets, blankets and water chlorination tabs that will increase drinking safe and clean water which is favorable for human use

This project will take into account the humanitarian – coordination and referral pathway linkages to strengthen SGBV services provision resilient and coping mechanism.
It will also take into consideration issues of gender disparity and try to improve accessibility to services for the most disadvantaged groups in the communities such mental health and people living with disabilities. Stakeholders are to be sufficiently sensitized and kept engaged throughout the lifespan of the project with support from WHO, Health cluster, MoH and County health department (CHD) and community leaders, this project shall target a population of 10,000 people which be assisted in Ayod county as disaggregated as follows; men 1500, women 2500, boys 2700 and girls 3300, people living with disabilities 15% and elderly people age 60 years above 5%) all with be provided with healthcare services.
The project will have supplies from Core pipe lines WHO UNFPA and MoH respectively.
This project will positively contribute to health cluster objectives 1. Improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations

2. Provide access to life-saving essential healthcare, including mental health to women, men, girls and boys, including ability challenged persons

3. Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms

EDA will monitor and evaluate the project and will report to health cluster, CHD and state MoH through 5Ws, EDSR and DHIS2. This report will be collected and analyze by our M & E focal person and data will be shared in weekly and monthly basis. EDA will coordinate with state health cluster and involve in health needs assessment. We will coordinate with other partners from different clusters (nutrition, FSL,WASH protection so that there will be strong effort and synergy to improve the livelihood of affected population in Ayod. EDA will coordinate and maintain AAP strategy to keep local community and beneficiaries in the implementation process.

project_name: Alleviating barriers and challenges to accessing quality and protective education opportunities for boys, girls and youth in the North West.
project_objective:
WV and IP will offer a multifaced project in continuation of the existing and expand in Idleb and Aleppo supporting the most vulnerable as requested by authorities and informed by needs, including CWD from HC and IDP camps between the ages of 5-17, by providing equitable access to quality and protective learning prospects to girls and boys in both formal education-Curriculum B-and in nonformal education through Accelerated Learning Programmes, remedial, catch-up, literacy and numeracy classes and Self Learning Programme. 7 areas with the highest severity rate (5) as per HNO 2022 will be targeted: Maaret Tamsrin, Dana, Bennsh, Armanaz, Salqin, Harim, Atareb, covering 37 (27 new locations). In IDP camps, nonformal education provided to 1540 females and 1470 males including 27 CwDs. In 15 formal schools, we’ll support 3428 female and 3286 male students including 20 CwDs. 355 teachers, 6084 male & 4555 female students will benefit from SPHERE alliant and CWD-considerate rehab and construction including heating fuel in 22 schools that were identified through a comprehensive WV needs assessment. 
We’ll continue to work with and recruit local communities to ensure apt education services are due at a level that meets the cluster and authorities’ standards, which include local outreach, quality and inclusive education in formal and non-formal settings with lifelong learning chances with special focus on CwD. 8300 of parents (F 5300 M 3000) targeted in awareness sessions on the importance of education and CP. In compliance with INEE minimum standards and safe-programming principles, achieving improved learning outcomes through conducting BTL campaigns to encourage children to return and be retained in education while parents prioritise education. The sessions will be complemented in distributing learning supplies. We’ll also provide training to teachers and facilitators on F2F and distant ed, programmatic support throughout the project cycle. OOSC will be bridged back to formal education based on the term’s scores. Holistically, structured and semi-structured PSS sessions using WV’s models and expertise will be offered by training education staff (TICC- PSS- SEL- EiE- CSG) in the established/rehabilitated CFSs at formal and non-formal settings in all of the targeted locations, to enhance the resilience, coping mechanism and life skills of children, in addition to mine risk awareness sessions, hygiene promotion education, case identification and referrals for most vulnerable cases in need of services through the protection team and external pathways.
Ensuring the continuity of learning, adapting plan B for distance learning due to COVID or escalation in the security situation, where we’ll be contingent on sufficient pre-existing equipment (independent contribution) from pervious education project (tablets,cameras,laptops,internet equipment,teaching tools-valued at $80000). The project will provide heating materials (gas heaters in tents, fuel and heaters for block building schools). All projects will provide drinking and washing water, support to operational costs, cleaning materials, sanitisers and solar power systems as an electricity source in the rehabilitation works. Security equipment for education settings (first aid kits and fire extinguishers) given after training staff on first aid and emergency preparedness. 
PTAs established to consult, inform of updates along with teachers support circles as experience sharing and care. Project will offer incentives to teachers, facilitators, guards, cleaners and admin staff as an important factor in securing stable education process and retention of teachers while securing jobs and income for about 348 families. WV and IP will facilitate experience exchange workshops with Aleppo and Idleb Education Directorate education personnel (30 Aleppo/70 Idleb) to improve the level of coordination and help build cooperation and partnership with the local councils and camp management.

project_name: Apoyo en manejo de información a la ONIC
project_objective: En proyecto esta centrado en dar apoyo en manejo de información en situaciones de emergencia para el Equipo Humanitario País y comunidades indígenas en Colombia. En la actualidad, siguiendo los hallazgos presentados en informes publicados por instituciones nacionales e internacionales (i.e. la Corte Constitucional, la Comisión de la Verdad , la Organización de las Naciones Unidas, el Centro por la Justicia y el Derecho Internacional , entre otras), un número importante de Pueblos Indígenas asentados en Colombia se encuentran en riesgo de extinción física y cultural, producto de las dinámicas territoriales e institucionales que están alterando su modus vivendi, sus territorios y su corporeidad, lo cual es evidenciable con mayor fuerza en el escenario actual de post acuerdo con la reconfiguración de espacios y actores (Defensoría del Pueblo, 2018).  En tal sentido, la presente iniciativa está orientada a fortalecer la capacidad instalada y las competencias de los pueblos indígenas, adscritos a la Organización Nacional Indígena de Colombia -ONIC- y a otras organizaciones indígenas del orden nacional, frente a la captura, procesamiento, automatización, visualización y usabilidad de la información y al EHP sobre situaciones de emergencia y de desastre de carácter humanitario y acaecidas en los territorios ancestrales y en comunidades altamente vulnerables de la población colombiana.

project_name: Displaced children and their families have improved access to safe and affordable drinking water as well as improved access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene in Syria
project_objective:
This project will seek to improve access to lifesaving WASH services to conflict affected children and adults in Syria. Aligned with Objectives 1, 2 and 4 of the Humanitarian Response Plan, this project will address WASH needs in a comprehensive and integrated manner by providing a range of services along-side Child Protection, Education and/or Nutrition activities. The purpose is to provide assistance to vulnerable individuals that are impacted by more than a decade of conflict, COVID-19, and climate change, with the goal of reducing the risk of communicable and water-borne diseases, and improving learning environments for children.  

Implementation will take place in North East Syria and North West Syria, and will in large part be a continuation of existing programming. Community acceptance will be prioritised, and a conflict sensitive approach will be taken to reduce the risk of unintended consequences. Activities will be informed through action plans developed together with the community, and may include rehabilitation of communal infrastructure, including at institutional levels, distribution of hygiene items, hygiene promotion, and basic service provision of WASH services such as water trucking, solid waste management, desludging and operations and maintenance of WASH facilities in camps / settlements.  

The sustainability of the project will be ensured through systems strengthening of the technical departments, or where conditions allow, WASH committees. Children youth, women and people living with disabilities will play important roles in the need identification and design stages.

project_name: Improving access to safe and gender-sensitive WASH services for IDPs, host communities, and schools in northwest Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to provide broad support to WASH activities and lifesaving response aimed at increasing access to inclusive, accessible, conflict sensitive and gender sensitive WASH services for at least 344,053 people affected by the crisis. The project will contribute to the following objectives of the WASH cluster: Sector Objective 1: Support to water, sanitation/sewage, and solid waste management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria, Sector Objective 2: Deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services, and improve hygienic behaviors and practices of most vulnerable people, Sector Objective 3: WASH coordination structures facilitated and enhanced and Sector Objective 4: Improve WASH facilities and services in institutions to minimize sub-standard WASH conditions of the most vulnerable people in Syria.
Under 1st objective: Islamic Relief plan a number of activities including repair and rehabilitation of water systems, support to water quality assurance, operation and maintenance of water supply systems, repair, rehabilitation and operational support to sanitation/sewage and solid waste management systems. Under the 2nd  objective, IR plan to distribute essential WASH NFIs, hygiene promotion, and messaging on COVID-19. Under the 3rd objective, IR plan to strengthen prevention and mitigation of WASH-related protection risks, while under the 4th objective four, plan to support WASH facilities and services in schools and child-friendly spaces in close coordination with Education and Protection Clusters. 
The action will target the groups identified in Islamic Relief needs assessment as most in need, including IDPs (displaced, in camps, and in communities), host communities, and particularly women and girls and persons with disabilities). Islamic Relief will work with gender-balanced local community volunteers which will include representatives from each community group, community leaders, and local councils as entry points for community consultation, mobilization, and as key implementation actors. The proposed response aims to meet critical, unmet needs as identified in the previous sections and the gender-based analysis around the lack of safe and accessible WASH services, compromising health and dignity. The proposed actions are developed on the basis of primary need assessment conducted by the IR team. The actions aim at reduced suffering, increasing and maintaining human dignity, and saved lives of conflict-affected IDP and Host communities, women, men, girls, and boys in NW Syria (Aleppo and Idlib Governorates), Syria.

project_name: Child protection services provided and  Strengthened in refugee camps and host communities
project_objective:
With established child protection agencies working in compliance with CPSS strategy and CPMS, the project will address multiple protection risks faced by refugee children through a comprehensive package of activities for preventive and remedial actions in the best interests of children.

Specialised AGD-sensitive case management services considering 'Do No Harm' principle will be provided to children at risk, with provision of appropriate alternative family or community-based care for UASC and tailored service and referrals to competent service for survivors of Gender-Based Violence and children with disabilities.

Strengthened information management through inter-agency collaboration and CPIMS+ reports for trends analysis will support the response monitoring and evidence-based data for evaluation. UNHCR and partners will engage with parents, girls and boys and key community representatives at multi-layered levels to promote meaningful participation in project design and implementation and strengthen the community-based child protection mechanism/ structures, including women and girls’ organisations to ensure effective risk-mitigation for children and sustainability. This will be coupled with family strengthening activities to build up their resilience and reduce potential risks for children. 

Multipurpose Children and Adolescent Hubs will enable children and adolescents to engage in age-appropriate recreational and psycho-social activities in safe and dignified spaces with close involvement of Community-based Child Protection Committees while serious cases of trauma or psychological distress are referred to specialized services.

Effective integration with other sectors, including Community-based protection, education, GBV, Nutrition, MHPSS, Legal protection to enable the provision of services such as menstrual hygiene kits in adolescents’ hubs, Sexual Reproductive Health, support for children in contact with the law and various forms of support to caregivers. 

Capacity of partners’ staff and community volunteers will be strengthened through training, mentoring, coaching considering CPMS, CPSS and IASC guidelines and UNHCR Framework. Child protection tailored trainings will be provided to Government staff including CiCs and law enforcement. Awareness raising sessions targeting the Community will be organized on various topics, including on gender equality/risk, prevention of child labor, child marriage in addition to mainstreaming child protection across sectors.
Child friendly communication on DRR and COVID-19 prevention will be mainstreamed into regular activities. Strengthened community structures will work to prevent temporary separations in case of emergencies. Funds will be dedicated for upgrade and repairs of CP structures affected by natural disasters. 
Partners will complement the communities’ response during disasters by participating in the PERUs and ERTs. The greening projects where children at the multipurpose hubs plant and care for vegetation will continue as efforts to protect the environment.

The project will ensure social cohesion between host and refugee communities, opening activities to children from the host community with particular focus on peace-building activities and appropriate child friendly feedback mechanisms in line with AAP principles and mechanisms such as consultations, FGDs and surveys. UNHCR prioritizes SEA prevention and response activities with internal SOPs and office focal points. PSEA and child safeguarding are embedded trainings provided to partners. The Code of Conduct is displayed in facilities and includes a referral mechanism for complaints and protection hotline.

In the 34 camps, UNHCR will support through assessment and recommendations and registration of child-related challenging cases such as new-borns without documentation.

The project will be implemented in close collaboration with the government structures and stakeholders involved in child protection.

project_name: Responding to the Urgent Needs of IDPs, Host Communities and Returnees in Hard-to-Reach Areas in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
IOM will continue to strengthenits Mental Health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) programme in a more systematic and comprehensive approach with engagement of community volunteers and health promoters. Access to quality reproductive health care services remains a challenge, including the gaps in sexual and reproductive health services including family planning, HIV, clinical care for GBV survivors and linkages with MHPSS. IOM intends to enhance quality access to comprehensive services through the integration of MHPSS with Primary Health Care (PHC). IOM will also continue working with the health partners in outbreak prevention and response efforts, capacity building of health and mental health professionals, health information management, and emergency referral and support system. As part of the health promotional and preventive activities, IOM will partner with local NGOs to implement health outreach through Health Promoters and community volunteers. Under this action, IOM will also strengthen its collaboration with the State Primary Health Care Development Agency (SPHCDA) and will continue to support the State Ministries of Health.

IOM partnered with the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH) in setting-up and operating a 24-bed and 2- bed ICU (intensive car eunit) Health center which includes an isolation center for humanitarian aid workers in north-east Nigeria and a COVID-19 rt- PCR laboratory that addresses the PCR (polymerise chain reaction) testing of humanitarian workers and the hospital community both for case management, surveillance and travel purposes. IOM aims to continue the partnership with UMTH in sustaining essential emergency health services, operating the isolation center and COVID- 19 laboratory for humanitarian aid workers and COVID-19 testing to at ‘risk community’ in north-east Nigeria.
In coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Federal Ministry of Health and related departments, World Health Organization and the UN Medical Services; IOM will continue to leverage its health clinic infrastructure and capacity to contribute to the government’s effort to respond to COVID-19. IOM will continue to support the provision of COVID-19 testing services in Borno, FCT (Abuja) and Lagos. Activities include sample collection and testing for the UN staff, staff of International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs), diplomatic community and migrants using existing UMTH facilities and the communities at risk

project_name: Strengthening Protection & Emergency Response, and Promotion of Sustainable Durable Solutions in NE Nigeria through CCCM in Selected Locations in Adamawa and Borno States.
project_objective:
The project seeks to strengthen protection and emergency intervention and promote durable solutions through a coordinated multi-sectoral response by reinforcing CCCM activities delivery, taking into consideration new developments within the operation. The intervention will be multi-sectoral, focusing on the Out of Camp Area Based Approach (ABA) ,and within prioritized camps/camp-like settings in Borno and Adamawa states, while also maintaining the conventional approach in camps with CCCM needs.  The proposed CCCM approaches have been successfully implemented in NE Nigeria, with ABA recently piloted by UNHCR and partners in Borno, and currently rolled out to Adamawa. Given the prevailing circumstances in NE, it is not practical to abruptly discontinue the implementation of conventional CCCM approaches in camps and camp-like structures, knowing that several camps will still be in existence for better part of 2022. Inclusion of the host communities and returnees, and the population that have relocated or those attempting to integrate in the community is a sure way to promote durable solutions and community cohesion through equitable targeting. The project will cover 4 LGAs in Borno (Ngala, Monguno, Banki (Bama) and Damasak (Mobbar)), 5 LGAs in Adamawa (Yola South, Yola North, Mubi, Madagali and Michika) and 2 LGAs in Yobe state (Damaturu and Gujba). The breakdown of the target for this CCCM project is 97,298 individuals (19,460HH) for IDPs and 22,702 individuals (4,540 HH) for returnees, distributed as follows: 46% (male), 54% (female), 60% (children), 36% (adult) and 4% (elders). 

Overall, the response will focus on enhancing multi-sectoral coordination of humanitarian response, monitoring of protection and assistance, promotion of participatory approach, site facilitation, community organizing, capacity building for government authorities, partners and the community, strengthening information sharing, communication and coordination, promoting, and strengthening of accountability to the affected population, ensuring infrastructureal improvement and to mainstream protection, Child Protection, GBV, Prevention from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and other cross-cutting issues like COVID 19 into CCCM for improved living conditions, and to promote sustainable durable solutions. Variations in gender, ethnic origin, diversity, and age that may be wrongly applied to eliminate specific persons from accessing services and lead to vulnerability and risky coping strategies will be considered during every stage of the project life cycle.
ABA is a steppingstone to early recovery/stabilization, hence CCCM response will attempt to link areas under ABA with public service activities such as education, food security, infrastructure development/rehabilitation, health, and public works among others. The community leaders will be oriented to sensitize the community on peaceful coexistence and how they can benefit from public services, development work within the geographical locations, including how they can get employment, access markets and conduct business, including available livelihood opportunities as contributing factors to sustainable durable solutions.

project_name: Strengthen Provision of Secondary and Tertiary Health Care Across Syria.
project_objective: Strengthening and sustaining delivery of standardized secondary and specialized healthcare services addressing obstetric care, Neonatal Resuscitation services and referral services across the country. The main objectives are to Improving sustainable and quality life-saving secondary health care, Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CemOC),Neonatal Resuscitation services and referral services across the country men, women, boys and girls requiring life-saving surgical interventions and secondary health care, in addition to women of reproductive age requiring emergency obstetric care; and to improving access to essential medicines and strengthening the capacity of secondary care at hospitals’ level to cope with the emerging demands is important. Proposed HRP project is focusing on improving the quality of care for trauma, secondary and tertiary healthcare services in Syria through the provision of continued education and training, endorsement of standardized clinical guidelines, treatment protocol, and standard operation procedure of different subdivision of secondary healthcare services including trauma, emergency, and critical care services and Comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care (CEmONC). Furthermore, the project aims to infection prevention and control activities through delivery of Basic IPC training, provision of technical support. Furthermore, the project aims to infection prevention and control activities through delivery of Basic IPC training, provision of technical support, field monitoring, and measure the quality of healthcare in terms of inputs, the material, resources needed to provide IPC standard measures, and outcomes of the activities based on IPC assessment framework (IPCAF) for health facility. In addition, as last resort funding, the WHO will focus on supporting critical gaps of secondary and tertiary health care, based on a need’s assessment and in coordination with Health Cluster to ensure the vulnerable population has access to emergency care services.

project_name: Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality through WASH integrated programming with Health and Nutrition in Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Pibor and Tonj East counties of Jonglei and Warrap states.
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs.AAH strategy is to addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WaSH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently Action Against Hunger is implementing a WASH program under SIDA, GFFO, GAC, and ECHO activities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Warrap, and Jonglei states with established field offices in Malualkon, Alek, Old Fangak, and Paguir Payam. In 2022, WaSH projects will be implemented to ensure that host communities, IDPs and returnees have safe access to clean water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behavior. The proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5 and pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WaSH and Nutrition response aimed at breaking diarrhea – malnutrition vicious cycle. This SSHF project will ensure the effectiveness of addressing malnutrition in the proposed target area by reducing disease burden in communities as well as availing safe, potable water for use in appetite tests at nutrition sites including monthly Water quality tests which will be carried out by our WASH team in both locations using our established laboratories. To achieve the overall project objective and objectives of the HRP-2022, we will provide critical services to 41,320 individuals with gender segregation of 21,478  males, 19, 842 females. among them 16,471 under 5 children at the both Nutrition/Health facilities and   at the village level with 4 main activities which include: 1) Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition
. 2) Integrate Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties). 3) Community member’s exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures and infrastructure 4) Increasing knowledge of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WaSH-related diseases. ACF will implement the above in the catchment areas of its nutrition facilities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states. Baseline KAP surveys will be conducted in all target areas to identify the WaSH-related knowledge, attitude, and practices of the communities. Detailed needs assessments will be conducted to assess community access to safe water sources and sanitation facilities. The implementation strategy will align with the needs identified in assessments and KAP surveys at the project start. Additionally, the ACF multisector emergency response throughout the country will include a WaSH component to complement its nutrition work. The proposed program strategy takes into account specific gender-related needs during surveys and activity implementation to ensure the equitable participation of all gender and age groups in the locations mentioned above.

project_name: “Reduction of emergency coping mechanisms through the provision of livelihood services.”
project_objective: Provision of livelihoods and economic inclusion services, to impulse economic recovery and address food needs through the delivery of in-kind inputs, CVA, trainings, IGAs such as new livelihood development and cash for work to provide opportunities and reduce the use of emergency coping mechanisms.

project_name: Strengthen Accountability for Gender-Based Violence and Enhancing Gender mainstreaming in multi-sector programs in Jonglie and Warrap States of South Sudan
project_objective:
South Sudan remains to be among the countries with a high prevalence of gender-based violence where half of the girls marry below the age of 18. The rigidly patriarchal system and historic marginalization of women are the root causes of the GBV in the country. This is further exacerbated by recurrent natural disasters mainly flooding and the ongoing conflicts in the different places. Therefore, is imperative that humanitarian interventions are sensitive to this reality, given that they may both cause and exacerbate the incidence of GBV cases. Action Against Hunger proposes to: a) continue its efforts to mainstream GBV and gender considerations in its Nutrition, Health, WASH, and FSL integrated programs and b) Support the generation of evidence and learning for a better understanding of GBV prevention and r risk mitigation humanitarian community in South Sudan providing an evidence base for GBV prevention and risk mitigation.

The purpose of this project is to prevent gender-based violence and mitigate the protection risks for women for affected women, men, boys, and girls in affected communities by monitoring and addressing the gender dynamics on the ground.  It will also put in place measures that will enhance safe and dignified access to available services for survivors and vulnerable women and girls in those communities.  The project will be implemented from Jan. 1, 2022, to Dec. 31, 2022, and shall benefit the target groups in IDPs, host communities and returnees in Pibor, Fangak, Tonj East, Tonj North and Gogrial East Counties of South Sudan. 
In 2022, Action against hunger will conduct gender analysis, its program implementation areas by using the Rapid Gender Analysis tools to generate evidence to support a gender-sensitive and gender transformative program implementation. It will also strengthen its partnership with gender-focused and like-minded organizations for sharing lessons and best practices. 

This project will mainly focus on awareness-raising and information dissemination on GBV prevention and risk mitigation aspects and available services, through sensitization of men and boys and engagement of men caregivers on a dialogue on protection in Men Group Discussions, the project to tackle the root causes of gender inequality and stereotypes. The MtMSG group and the CNVs will also be the gears in dissemination of the information to men, women, boys and girls in the communities as well as on the Nutrition Sites using tailored IEC materials. ACF will conduct mapping of available services in those locations, train the staff on PFA, and safe and confidential referral of survivors. ACF will pilot innovative and environment-friendly IGA options engaging vulnerable women and girls, in particular.

project_name: Integrated Response for Mozambique Affected Populations (IRAMP)
project_objective: FHI 360’s response to the emergency in Cabo Delgado through integrated approach (WASH, Health and Protection) in Ancuabe and Metuge district. FHI 360’s goal for the proposed program is to improve the wellbeing of conflict-affected and displaced populations through an integrated, multi-sectoral response. FHI 360 will collaborate 4 essentials elements of protection principles into its operational and all program cycle management. All IRAMP staffs including volunteers in the target area will get the protection mainstreaming training and produce the action plan of protection mainstreaming. There are huge need and gap of MHPSS amongs effected population due to the crisis in Cabo Delgado. FHI 360 therefore embedded MHPSS activities into our activities. Staffs will be equipped with psychosocial support (PSS) and psychological first aid (PFA) skills. Affected population in the FHI 360 target area will be benefited with PSS and PFA services and safe ad ethical referral services to specialized MHPSS.
