project_name: Strengthening the Protection Environment for Displaced Women & Girls in Mueda
project_objective:
This project proposes to reach 20,000 people in Mueda with GBV programming, in a safe and inclusive manner. 
CARE will prevent and respond to protection risks by establishing WGFSs in sites and within them, conduct MHPSS and empowerment activities and dialogues, strengthen the capacity of case workers and support survivors.

project_name: Emergency response and improved access to essential primary health care across South Sudan
project_objective:
Purpose and overall goal: 
To reduce morbidity and mortality by responding to public health emergencies and providing access to quality essential primary healthcare, including reproductive health, services to survivors of SGBV and mental health services, to girls, boys, men and women in emergency situations, with specific focus on accessibility for persons living with disability and the elderly. To build the resilience of communities and the MoH to prevent, detect and respond to disease outbreaks.

Methodology and target: 
Medair's project focuses on provision of primary health care in areas of high need and where existing services are inadequate, including Leer, Pibor and Renk. Activities include provision of curative consultations in primary health facilities; community-based treatment of common illness in children under five; routine vaccination; reproductive and sexual health including provision of ANC, safe delivery, PNC and clinical management of SGBV; management of at-risk infants through MAMI; and mental health treatment. Medair conducts ongoing training and supportive supervision for capacity building staff of Medair, CHD and other partners in order to improve the quality of service provision. Medair primarily targets children under five, women, and people with disability and mental health conditions, due to their unique vulnerability, though not exclusively.
Through the Emergency Response Team, Medair can respond in any area of South Sudan in response to disease outbreaks, acute displacement, reports of increased morbidity and mortality, nutritional emergencies, flooding and other natural disasters. Medair ERT aims to reduce morbidity and mortality of vulnerable populations through outbreak response such as vaccination campaigns or case management, and provision of primary health care services where these are inadequate. Through training and community engagement, Medair aims to increase the capacity of long-term health partners and the local community to be prepared for future shocks. 

All of Medair's health activities are integrated with WASH, Nutrition, Emergency Shelter/NFI and Protection activities to enhance the effectiveness and address underlying causes of morbidity and mortality.

project_name: Improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable populations in Renk, Leer, Pibor and any other emergency location across South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed WASH project will be implemented in Leer, Pibor, Renk, as well as other emergency and IPC 4 and 5 locations. According to the WASH Cluster's county prioritization for 2022, Leer and Pibor are Priority 1 counties, while Renk is Priority 2. The project is designed based on Core Humanitarian and Sphere Minimum Standards to ensure that affected beneficiaries receive timely, coordinated, adequate, resilient, and impartial basic water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Medair engages the affected beneficiaries in all stages of the project cycle and ensures that the 'Do no harm' principle is followed by not exposing affected beneficiaries to any risk as a result of project implementation. Furthermore, the proposed WASH project will adhere to the WASH Cluster technical guidelines and WHO drinking water quality standards. Medair will continue to integrate WASH and nutrition internally, as well as collaborate with other nutrition and protection partners, to maximize the impact of the proposed WASH project. WASH activities will also be integrated into health activities in the context of disease prevention and response. It aims at breaking the transmission cycle of water related diseases including diarrhoeal, cholera, vector borne diseases and COVID-19. This is intended to be achieved through multiple integrated approaches. Overall, the project is targeted to reach 148,835 people through improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services by the end of 2022.

project_name: Provision of actionable information on population movement and evolving needs to inform evidence-based humanitarian and early recovery programming
project_objective:
The complex and dynamic humanitarian context in South Sudan requires accurate, triangulated, timely and readily accessible information. This project aims to provide the humanitarian community with well analysed and actionable data to fill existing and anticipated information gaps on displacement, returns, and general population movement across South Sudan and inform a fair and evidence-based humanitarian response delivery and early recovery programming. The main deliverables will include:
- A regularly updated IDPs and returnees baseline at location and area level. Information will include population presence, movement reason and needs of IDPs and returnees.
- Providing regular information on sudden displacement and return movements requiring humanitarian assistance through DTM’s event tracking mechanism.
- Biometric data management for accountable, effective and targeted delivery of humanitarian assistance.
- Representative multi-sectoral needs assessment on household level to provide information on needs, vulnerabilities and intentions to feed into South Sudan’s Humanitarian Response Planning (HRP) and Humanitarian needs Overview (HNO).
- Regular updates on population mobility at border points and key internal transit hubs, including displacement sites, through DTM’s flow monitoring mechanism.

project_name: Common Transport Services for Humanitarian Partners in South Sudan
project_objective:
The Common Transport Services (CTS) is a free-for-user service that transports key humanitarian supplies on behalf of humanitarian actors. CTS serves as a critical link in the supply chain, enabling products and materials that arrive from regional and international suppliers to move onwards to partners located deep in the field rapidly. IOM has been managing the CTS on behalf of the Logistics Cluster since 2011. During this time, the project has significantly grown from delivering 2,000 MT of humanitarian cargo in 2011 to a total of 17000 MT by the end of 2021, making a yearly average of 25000 MT since the beginning, highlighting the increase in the use of road transport as the most cost-efficient mode of transportation as access improves. IOM has continued to maintain flexibility and adaptability to the operating environment in South Sudan. Through CTS, IOM works with more than 100 unique agencies in key operational locations in Jonglei, Unity, and Greater Upper Nile Region, in Humanitarian Logistics Hubs (Malakal, Bentiu), and Rumbek, Bor, Juba, and Wau. IOM will maintain heavy vehicles and transport cargo from the main ports of dispatch via air, road, and river including LC beyond responses and will continue support for common warehouse management in key operational locations. 

Through the effective management of the CTS, IOM aims to support organizations' preparedness measures to mitigate risks associated with increased insecurity, looting/theft of humanitarian supplies, critical access impediments to vulnerable people, and reduce expensive air and road transport costs, which ultimately supports the timely response to the needs of the affected populations. With this funding, IOM will directly work with 100 plus humanitarian organizations located in different areas, enabling them to deliver critical life-saving humanitarian services and assistance items.

project_name: Provision of GBV services to communities affected by Conflict and Flooding in South Sudan
project_objective:
According to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, the post independent South Sudan remains in serious humanitarian conditions even after signing of the revitalized peace agreement to resolve conflict among the warring parties. As reported by HNO, ""their situation is worsened by endemic [sub-]national violence, conflict, access constraints and operational interference, public health challenges such as direct and indirect effects of COVID-19 and climatic shocks resulting in the dual phenomena of extraordinary flooding and localized drought, which have a severe impact on people’s livelihoods, hampers access to education and water, sanitation and hygiene and health services. Protection concerns remain high, with people impacted by violence having limited access to justice and the rule of law. In 2022, the humanitarian community in South Sudan estimates that more than two-thirds of South Sudan's population, 8.9 million people, are in need of humanitarian assistance, an increase of 600,000 since 2021. Continued conflict and instability in the country combined with flooding have resulted in large-scale internal and cross-border displacement. At the same time, limited improvements in some areas have prompted some people to spontaneously return. In addition, the government, with the support of some humanitarian agencies - has facilitated returns to certain areas. Due to compounding shocks, both in areas of displacement and return, populations have been forced to keep displacing time and again. At least 90,000 returnees from abroad remained displaced within the country, unable to reach their homes. In 2021, there were 2 million IDPs in the country (55 per cent of whom are women and girls), as compared to 1.7 million in 2020. An additional 2.3 million South Sudanese remain refugees hosted in neighbouring countries.""
Alight has operational presence; in Aweil West, Aweil Centre, Kajo Keji, Ulang, and Kapoeta South and Budi Counties, South Sudan. Alight runs GBV response and prevention interventions in all but one proposed locations. It is only in Aweil West County where we currently don't have active GBV services but have on-going nutrition interventions. HRP funds will be used to complement ongoing BHA/USAID support in; Kapoeta South, Budi, Kajo Keji and Ulang and integrate GBV into our nutrition activities in Aweil West. In Aweil Centre, GBV activities are funded by UNICEF which will end in September 2022. 
To ensure that Alight and other partners do not duplicate services, Alight will undertake GBV service mapping on ‘’who is doing what and where’’ in all the locations targted. This will allow Alight to only target areas not served by humanitarian interventions. 
Through our GBV programming in the aforementioned locations, gaps are emerging in nearby payams of the counties we are operating and these new vulnerabilities to GBV are being identified due to evolving context as a result of floods and related displacements of IDPs, returnees and host communities against a background of limited funding for GBV. The cumulative effects of these emerging gaps therefore calls for scaling up GBV service provisions to locations and populations that have not been benefiting from our current GBV programs. In Aweil West, GBV services have been non-existent as identified by our nutrition staff providing Nutrition services in Aweil West. 
To ensure inclusivity of interventions especially for persons with disability, Alight has a culture of conducting assessment prior to launch of project to ensure that disability information are captured for planning purposes. This information usually help Alight to put in place deliberate measures such as; procurement of white cane for the blind, placing ramps to all constructions and employing skilled disabled persons to form part of our staffing structure. Alight also structures home visits for both GBV messaging and services provision to cater for the interest of the disabled persons.

project_name: Nutrition Response for Children Under Five Years, Pregnant and Lactating Women in Aweil West and Kajo Keji Counties in South Sudan.
project_objective:
American Refugee Committee (ARC), now known as ALIGHT nutrition response will focus on preventive and curative nutrition interventions in Kajo Keji and Aweil West Counties. The response will primarily target children under five years both boys and girls as well as Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) including those with disabilities among the host community, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees in the above-mentioned locations. ALIGHT is present in Kajo Keji County implementing integrated Nutrition, Protection and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) programmes whereas in Aweil West county, ALIGHT is implementing nutrition programmes.
The proposed interventions include prevention of acute malnutrition through behavior change communication to improve Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) practices in the community; prevention of micronutrient deficiencies through Vitamin A supplementation and deworming campaigns targeting children under five years; Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) through the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP) and community mobilization where the community volunteers will be engaged to identify and support enrollment of children and PLW with acute malnutrition before their condition deteriorates. In addition, ALIGHT will work in coordination with other sectors such as WASH, Protection, Education, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) and Health to strengthen integration and linkages of services with the goal of preventing acute malnutrition and to enhance recovery of beneficiaries undergoing nutrition rehabilitation. The proposed interventions seeks to reduce morbidity and prevent mortality associated with acute malnutrition and subsequently improve maternal and child health.
The proposed interventions are in line with the nutrition cluster objectives which seeks to (a) increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific services for children, adolescents and women; (b) increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW affected by acute malnutrition; (c) Enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information, and (d) Increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and integrated programming targeting vulnerable groups in prioritized locations by the end of 2022.
ALIGHT will continue to operate 10 static nutrition sites in Aweil West County spread across the seven Payams whereas in Kajo Keji operate 9 static and 10 outreach nutrition sites in all the five Payams in the County. The project aims to reach 2,584 children aged 6 to 59 months with severe acute malnutrition without medical complications, 9,284 children aged 6 to 59 months with moderate acute malnutrition, 10,889 PLW with acute malnutrition, 36,136 caregivers/mothers with children under two years through individual MIYCN counselling sessions, 81,305 children aged 6 to 59 months with Vitamin A supplements and deworm 75,282 children aged 12 to 59 months with Albendazole tablets. It is important to point out that ALIGHT will target 50% of the nutrition cluster's 2022 HNO targets in Aweil West due to presence of another nutrition partner in the County. In addition, to prevent duplication of activities, ALIGHT together with other nutrition partners and the County health department in both Kajo Keji and Aweil West Counties will map out areas of operation for each partner. The proposed interventions will be implemented in accordance with the Ministry of Health's CMAM and MIYCN protocols as well as the South Sudan Nutrition Cluster's guidelines for nutrition service delivery in the context of COVID-19.

project_name: Protection and Legal Assistance for Displacement affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
The NRC seeks to improve the overall protective environment in South Sudan by not only responding to people's most immediate material needs during a crisis, but also by promoting their safety and dignity, as well as preventing, reducing, or mitigating the protection risks they face. It is also to address the root causes of displacement and to contribute to the creation of conditions conducive to long-term solutions for displaced people. To achieve the project objective, NRC will focus on three key components i.e. 1) General Protection; Housing, Land and Property; 3) Gender Based Violence. 

NRC proposes a community-based approach to displaced and conflict-affected populations protection, including static, mobile, and emergency responses.  Protection context assessments will be done in all locations, as well as, where possible, community-based protection monitoring, in which community focal points will be trained to report on protection needs and risks. Protection incidents will be documented and analyzed in order to better understand trends and evolution in the protection context, and the findings will be disseminated to communities and relevant stakeholders. 

NRC will provide at-risk populations with both awareness-raising sessions and individualized assistance in obtaining national identity documentation. Foster improved ability to exercise HLP rights for individuals and groups affected by displacement with priority given to the most vulnerable, including female and child headed households, the elderly, individuals with physical and mental disabilities, and those who are extremely poor. NRC will target conflict-affected areas and areas of potential return.

NRC will also carry out GBV prevention and risk mitigation activities in 6 counties located in hard to reach areas. Activities will include awareness raising, referrals to response services, cash assistance to GBV survivors, distribution of dignity kits and training on GBV basic concepts among others.

To achieve the main objective, the will focus on the below key activities
1) Carrying out of information and awareness raising activities; awareness will focus on GBV (GBV risks, available response services, GBV referral pathways, timely reporting), HLP (social cohesion and collaborative dispute resolution mechanisms, land rights issues) and general protection (protection risks, available services)
2) Provision of cash assistance (individual protection assistance) to persons at GBV survivors and other persons at heightened risks including referral of GBV survivors for response services
3) Training frontline workers and community focal points on basic GBV concepts, GBV guiding principles and responses services.
4) Training of state-level authorities, community leaders and representative on HLP, alternative dispute resolution
5) Facilitating peaceful coexistence and inclusive resolutions of local conflict through training and mentoring the local community in collaborative dispute resolution (CDR) mechanisms
6) Distribute dignity kits to women and adolescent girls.
7) Provision of legal aid and counselling

project_name: Emergency Child Protection, GBV & Mine Action: Prevention, Mitigation & Response to assist IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in conflict-affected & high risk areas of Warrap, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria and Central Equatoria States, South Sudan
project_objective:
The already high needs of critical child protection services in South Sudan has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, protracted displacement, and limited access to basic services which continues to significantly affect the physical, mental, and social well-being of children, adolescents and caregivers. This situation has been worsened by the limited availability of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services and the low level of core child protection services, including family tracing and reunification, case management, and reintegration services for children affected by armed forces and groups, leaving many children untreated and unable to access the needed services. Climate shocks, severe drought, massive flooding, and conflicts have contributed to the increase in GBV risks in the country which requires to strengthen GBV case management, psychosocial support, legal service, livelihood, economic support, GBV referral pathways and to integrate GBV into other sectoral responses. The high contamination with landmines and explosive remnants of war (ERW), especially in the Greater Equatoria region, along major supply routes and areas for returnees from Uganda, and the increase in expected returns require to prevent, mitigate and respond to mine risk issues through enhanced preparedness and resilience.
This proposed integrated CP, GBV and EORE project is in line with the Protection Cluster Objectives and will ensure the provision of critical protection-related assistance and specialized services and the prevention and mitigation of Protection risks through enhanced preparedness. The project targets to reach an average of 60,000 (20,000 women, 20,000 men, 10,000 girls, 10,000 men) (CP), 50,000 (20,000 women, 10,000 men, 10,000 girls, 10,000 boys) (GBV) and 20,000 (5000 men, 5000 women, 5000 girls, 5000 boys) (MA) including people with disabilities.
Using the 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), World Vision International South Sudan (WVI-SS) aims to reach the most vulnerable populations in 11 counties in Warrap, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria and Central Equatoria States with improved access to quality lifesaving child protection for vulnerable girls, boys, men and women including children with disabilities who are at risk of mortality and morbidity and protection incidents/threats. Through the provision of specialized / lifesaving child protection and multi sectoral services WVI-SS seeks to reduce the suffering of boys, girls, women and men including children with disabilities who are at risk or experience violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect including GBV.
The proposed project will reduce the suffering of GBV survivors including women, men, girls, boys and people with disabilities by providing multi-sectoral specialized GBV response services. Furthermore, WVI-SS seeks to ensure that vulnerable women, men, girls, boys including people with disabilities have improved access to the provision of GBV prevention and risk mitigation interventions. Through protection monitoring, advocacy, awareness-raising and prevention and response services the project aims to reduce the vulnerability of women, men, girls and boys including people with disabilities at increased risk of mortality and morbidity and protection incidents/threats in priority areas.
In line with the Core Humanitarian Standards, WVI-SS will maintain its commitment to engage with affected communities at all phases of the project cycle, through focus group discussions with women, men, boys and girls. Establishing/strengthening local structures such as Project Management Committee is one example of how WVI-SS engages the community in a sustainable and accountable manner to determine and support appropriate need-based responses. WVI's Quality Assurance framework ensures that each project implemented is carried out effectively and continually reviewed in line with community needs and in line with other humanitarian frameworks.

project_name: Provision of Community Based Management of Acute Malnutrition to Under Five Children and Pregnant and Lactating Women in Upper Nile, Warrap, Western and Central Equatoria states in South Sudan
project_objective:
According to the humanitarians needs overview for 2022, about 8.9 million people are estimated to require humanitarian assistance in 2022, compared to 8.3 million in 2021. This increase is largely driven by compounded shocks triggered by continued conflict, widespread flooding, deepening food insecurity, inflation, high food prices, and lack of access to basic services. The 8.9 million people in need include 8.54 million South Sudanese women, men, girls and boys and 328,000 refugees and asylum seekers. Two million people are internally displaced; of these 1.4 million require urgent support, and 1.8 million are returnees, of these 1.2 million have urgent needs. In addition, there are 6 million vulnerable host community/ non-displaced people, of whom some are older persons or persons with disabilities. According to the intersectoral severity of needs analysis, humanitarian needs are most concerning in Fangak, Duk and Pibor counties in Jonglei and Cueibet and Rumbek East counties in Lakes, which were classified as in catastrophic need. People in 71counties face extreme needs, while two are in severe need. The primary challenge driving needs is food insecurity or lack of food, which weakens people’s health and nutritional status and exposes them to greater protection risks. The other main challenge is lack of access to WASH services which increases the likelihood of water-borne diseases, malnutrition and school dropout.

In 2022, world vision will join the humanitarian community to  address the needs by implementing the nutrition programs which aligns with the Nutrition Cluster objectives which include: Objective 1: To increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific services for children, adolescents and women in prioritized locations by the end of 2022, Objective 2: To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW affected by acute malnutrition in prioritized locations by the end of 2022, Objective 3: To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information by the end of 2022 and Objective 4: To increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and integrated programming targeting vulnerable groups in prioritized locations by the end of 2022
The lifesaving nutrition interventions will be implemented in Warrap, Central Equatoria, Western Equatoria and Upper Nile. The proposed nutrition project will be integrated with health, WASH, protection and FSL activities. World Vision will prioritize life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years of age, PLW, and chronically ill persons as the most vulnerable groups to acute malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs. Prevention activities that address the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition will be enhanced. Additionally, the response will expand on nutrition with other clusters to address key drivers of malnutrition: food insecurity, sub-optional child care and feeding practices, morbidity, and lack of safe water and sanitation. It will prioritise areas within World Vision program areas where high prevalence of acute malnutrition, conflict and displacement co-exist.

project_name: Emergency Nutrition support to vulnerable population in koch, Rubkona Counties in Unity State and Fangak, Canal pigi Counties in Jonglei State, South Sudan
project_objective: The humanitarian nutrition overview for 2022 estimates that 2 million children, pregnant and lactating women (PLW) will require treatment for malnutrition. In the same year, around 1.4 million children under 5 years of age (U5) will need to be provided with nutrition services out of which 302,078 will be admitted for acute malnutrition. 675,578 PLW are expected to be acutely malnourished, which is a significant increment when compared to 2021 needs. The need for humanitarian assistance is increased due to emerging issues related with increased food insecurity, flooding and the continuous impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The severe flooding in Jonglei State has impacted health and nutrition service provision in Fangak and Canal/Pigi counties. IRNA assessment conducted in August 2021 in the area, indicated that various locations in the counties have been completely submerged in water including nutrition and WASH facilities while the rest remains under the big threat of being flooded. Communities continue to be displaced to relatively dry high lands in Fangak and Cana Pigi counties. In Bentiu IDP, while official counts have shown fluctuation in the population counts over the years, the recent influx of displaced community from surrounding areas due to flooding is likely to continue causing much stress on existing humanitarian services in the IDP camp. Rehabilitation of nutrition and WASH infrastructure is needed to continue providing life-saving services in flood affected counties. A recent SMART survey done at Canal/Pigi and Fangak counties reveals, a GAM rate of 19% for each of the counites. Mass MUAC screenings conducted by WR in New Fangak in February 2020 show a proxy GAM rate of 11.6% and a proxy severe acute malnutrition (SAM) rate of 2% for children U5, and a proxy GAM of 8% for PLW. In Koch County, mass MUAC screenings conducted by WR in 2020 revealed a proxy GAM rate of 10.6% for children U5 and a proxy modern acute malnutrition (MAM) of 11% for PLW. SMART survey done in August 2021 in Bentiu IDP, reveled the prevalence of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) is 2.4%, and GAM prevalence is 9.7. To strengthen life-saving nutrition services, WR will scale up qualitative service and coverage for community-based management of malnutrition (CMAM), extending services hard to reach sites with underserved communities. The project will target 26,064 children U5 and PLW as direct beneficiaries who show signs of SAM and MAM. Care givers of children will be reached through Maternal and Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) programs in Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Therapeutic Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) sites. This project will establish four new outreach units in each county to provide outreach nutrition services to communities with limited access to services due to displacement. In Fangak County, WR plans to support 5 new OTP and TSFP sites in Canal/Pigi County. A gender-targeted and nutrition-sensitive service delivery approach will be used and nutrition will be integrated with WASH, health and FSL programming. The aim of the project is to reduce morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable children and women while promoting and engaging in recovery and resilience activities in the community. The project purpose is in line with Nutrition Cluster Objective and sectoral strategies. Project activities will be monitored through supportive supervision done together with the County Health and Nutrition Department, MOH and UN Agencies. Activities will be monitored by nutrition project staff with support from the WR Juba M&E department and other program team. Relevant reports will be shared to nutrition cluster and other reporting partners. Community based compliant mechanisms will be established within the nutrition sites and at community level to ensure accountability.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihood Support to Conflict Prone and Flood Affected Populations in Koch County, Unity State and Pigi/Canal and Fangak Counties in Jonglei State
project_objective:
The Humanitarian Needs  Overview (HNO) of February 2022 as well as Food Security and Nutrition Monitoring System (FSNMS) data as of February 2022  estimates that there will be 8.3 million People (including 2.0M IDPs) will be in need of humanitarian assistance during the 2022 lean season between May and July. The need for support on food security and livelihoods is ranked as a top most need by a majority of the people across the counties. Counties of Koch in Unity State as well as Fangak and Canal/Pigi in Jonglei state have at least 85% of the population in IPC 3+ classification, with some pockets classified as catastrophic within Fangak County. With three consecutive years of flooding experienced in these counties, humanitarian response has never been so dire. Crops were destroyed before harvesting and even in storage after harvest. Livestock have died through drowning and starvation as grazing grounds were flooded. Coupled with flooding, are intensified sub-national violence arising from political instability, cattle raids and revenge killings. Violence causes instability limiting access to land for cultivation but also results in deaths of productive members of the HH. Indirect effects of covid 19 on supply chains as well as protracted micro-economic crisis have continued to limit food supplies and continued to push up food prices. Coping strategies of affected households have been exhausted and household assets eroded. Without timely humanitarian intervention, this situation could worsen and plunge populations into famine situation.
The main objective of this intervention is to support the vulnerable populations in these three counties with livelihood kits and training so as to help these vulnerable communities to restore and sustain their livelihoods. This intervention will contribute to the three collective outcomes, the first being reduction of number of people in IPC 4 by 20% and IPC 5 to zero. This will be achieved mainly through increased food production at household level. The intervention will support the target population with crop, vegetable and fishing kits as well as provide them with training in use of inputs provided to avoid causing any harm but also avoid diverting these resources towards unintended uses. It is expected that through this intervention, target populations will be able to supplement food provided through general food distribution which had proved to be irregular and therefore unreliable but also increases dependency to external support systems. The intervention will also contribute towards reduction in flood related displacements in the target counties. This will be achieved through disaster risk reduction strategies that will build the community capacity on early warning signs and mitigation measures including construction of dykes to control flow of water. The project will also ensure minimum package for prevention, risk mitigation and response to GBV rolled out in 80% of priority locations, focusing on safe, timely access to quality case management, psychosocial services and capacity building.
A total of 211,500 beneficiaries (35,250 HH) comprising of 60% women, elderly, youth, disabled and other vulnerable groups will be targeted for crop and vegetable kits. Out of this number, a total of 3,525HHs will be targeted for training on improved agronomic methods, post-harvest handling and utilization. Similarly, 6,500HHs will be targeted with fishing kits, out of which 1,300HHs will be included in training on appropriate harvesting methods and fish preservation. This intervention will also target 1,000HHs with Food for Asset intervention to help them build community structures that will help them to mitigate effects of flooding. To help improve sustainable access to quality seeds, the project will work with 500HHs to produce high quality seeds and avail them to other farmers for subsequent use.
The intervention will run from January to December of 2022

project_name: Emergency WASH provision to the Vulnerable populations in Fangak and Canal Pigi, Jonglei State and Koch County in Unity State
project_objective: WASH is one of the program sectors most affected by the flooding across South Sudan in 2020 and 2021. The WASH severity classification conducted in May 2021 showed that all three targeted counties, Koch, Fangak and Canal/Pigi are under WASH severity Phase 4. This situation worsened with the 2021 flooding which reached unprecedented levels. The main drivers of WASH severity included; flooding of WASH infrastructure, destruction of roads; population displacement; COVID -19 that put extra pressure on medical facilities; and a resulting economic slowdown. Floods experienced later in 2021 have largely remained intact and are expected to continue well into 2022, likely to worsen this already deteriorating situation. With most of the WASH facilities destroyed including latrines, boreholes and handwashing facilities which is further compromised by limited access to health services, outbreak of water borne disease is imminent. World Relief South Sudan (WRSS) WASH will be implemented alongside other services like health, nutrition, protection, FSL, etc. The main purpose of this WASH intervention is to improve the wellbeing of people affected by disaster or who have been chronically exposed to lack of clean water and basic sanitation services in Koch, Fangak and Canal/Pigi counties. This will be done through reducing water and sanitation related morbidity and mortality; provision of safe, equitable access to clean water and basic sanitation services; mitigating Gender-based violence, supporting recovery and resilience building to achieve durable solutions. This intervention will be done both at community and facility levels (i.e. health & nutrition). Namely, this will be achieved through the rehabilitation of existing water points and drilling of new ones; conducting hygiene promotion campaigns; water quality monitoring; and distribution of WASH NFIs to targeted or blanket populations depending on the context. This WASH assistance will reduce the prevalence of WASH-related diseases and risk of outbreak by transmission contexts upon epidemiological investigations. Secondly, contribute to reduction of high prevalence of malnutrition by providing access to safe water and promoting hygiene in locations with high malnutrition prevalence and high WASH vulnerability. Through this objective, water/hygiene committees will be established and trained, hygiene campaigns will be promoted and WASH NFIs will be distributed to target beneficiaries. Thirdly, this project proposes to increase access to basic sanitation services, through the provision of WASH assistance to communities affected by sudden-onset disaster and/or chronically affected by a lack of access to basic WASH services. New water points and/ or rehabilitation of existing water points will be carried out, routine water quality monitoring will be conducted, hygiene campaigns will be organized and WASH NFIs like Aqua tabs, buckets, jerrycans and filter clothes will be distributed. Fourthly, this project will mitigate gender-based violence (GBV) by carrying out specific activities to mitigate GBV risk for users of WASH facilities and services, especially for women and children. Safety audits will be conducted to identify GBV concerns and implement mitigation measures. The project will construct water points, latrines and other infrastructure considering the needs of the most vulnerable in society including women, girls, elderly, disabled and children under five years. This will be done with utilization of the WASH Cluster’s Protection Mainstreaming tip-sheet. Community structures including water user management committees (WUC) will be trained. They will manage the resources and ensure that no harm is caused by these interventions. Water points will be managed ensuring access to all without causing any conflicts among the intended beneficiaries. Messaging on proper hygiene as well as COVID-19 Infection Prevention and Control measures will be communicated through community structures.

project_name: Provide Access to Inclusive, Quality, and Protective Basic Education to Vulnerable Children, Out of School Children and Youth aged (3-18), in Akobo, Nyirol, and Bor South of Jonglei State; Kapoeta East of Eastern Equitoria, Rumbek East of Lakes, Tonj East of Warrap in South Sudan.
project_objective:
To provide access to inclusive, quality, and protective basic education to vulnerable and marginalised children, Out of School Children and youths aged (3-18) in Akobo, Nyirol, and Bor South of Jonglei State; Kapoeta East of Eastern Equatoria, Rumbek East of Lakes and Tonj East in Warrap. The programme will implement interventions that lead to increased access to education for children. The programme will ensure that access to basic education meets the quality standards as set in the INEE minimum standards of Education in Emergencies. Activities will promote enrolment, retention and transition of children to the next school year while minimizing the possibility of dropouts. The learning infrastructure and the school environment will be disability friendly and gender sensitive to learners. School environments will provide intentional MHPSS activities and have clear referral pathways including to CP to ensure school environments are protective. Teachers will receive CPD and volunteer teachers incentivized. The project will target 49,870 total beneficiaries desegregated into 46,870 children and youths (25,779 B & 21,092 G), 1,602 teachers (875 M, & 721 W), 1,398 PTAs/SMCs (769 M, & 692 W); with 3% comprising of persons with disability, host communities and IDPs. 
The project will aim at improving equitable access to safe and protective education services by enrolling 46,870 (25,779 B & 21,092 G) children in pre-primary, primary and secondary schools and in learning centers. 20 Temporary Learning Spaces will be established, rehabilitation of 25 Temporary Learning Spaces, establishment of 20 gender segregated latrines, water points. Additionally, the project will be rehabilitating 25 gender segregated latrines and water points; and distributing or provide sanitation and hygiene materials to 108 schools (hand washing soap, sanitizers, masks) and PPE for students and teachers. 
The project will improve the quality of education, gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children by providing 4,128 (2,270 B & 1,858 G) emergency-affected children quality education recreational materials; providing teaching and learning materials for 96 schools in ECD, primary and secondary school education. The project will equally be conducting training 522 (304 M & 248 F) teachers on EiE pedagogical skills and child-centered methodologies to improve teaching and learning process for emergency-affected children; update 522 (304 M & 248 F) teachers and learners on PSS, CP, and referral mechanisms including CP/GBV, health and nutrition. Providing life-skills and basic vocational training to 1,000 (550 G & 450 G) youth and adolescents provide of dignity kits to 6,480 girls in schools; provide customized support to 840 young mothers in schools and to conduct 1-disability assessment.  All learning centres will have their referral pathways strengthened or established, with teachers trained on how to identify and refer cases through a child helpdesk. 
In order to strengthen/enhance the education system’s response capacity of the school community and national/local education actors the project will: capacity build 1,398 (769 M & 692 F) SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management, governance, PSS and DRR. The project will support prevention and mitigation of communicable diseases through training school communities by providing appropriate Information and Education and Communication (IEC) materials (i.e. posters, leaflets); conducting 5 back to learning campaigns. SCI will implement directly and with national partners, supporting technical, operational and institutional capacity strengthening of 5 national actors.
The projects will ensure that the following will be considered in the project design and implementation: gender and social inclusion, feedback & accountability mechanisms, crisis modifiers, nexus programming and community-based sustainability measures.

project_name: Provision of quality WASH services for vulnerable communities living in Akobo, Tonj East , Kapoeta East , Kapoeta North and Lafon Counties in South Sudan
project_objective:
In the proposed action Save the Children seeks to implement integrated WASH interventions to reduce the burden of WASH related diseases as aggravating factors for malnutrition locations presenting an extreme WASH vulnerability and high prevalence of malnutrition. Services provided will break the transmission cycle of main communicable diseases (i.e. diarrhea), thus improving food intake of malnourished children and contributing to the sustainability of health and nutrition. The proposed action will also seek to address WASH needs in during emergencies such as response to floods and disease outbreaks. The proposed interventions will target 5 counties (Akobo, Tonj East, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North and Lafon Counties) which have a WASH severity classification of 4 /critical, communities high GAM and in which Save the Children has operational presence.

The proposed WASH activities include; construction/rehabilitation of water points in communities  , water quality monitoring, hygiene promotion, construction of latrines in communities, WASH in Nutrition/health care facilities distribution of WASH kits , soap distribution and mitigation of Gender Based Violence, GBV through training of WASH staff on basic skills to provide survivors with information on where they can obtain support and GBV messages (including where to report risk and how to access care) are incorporated into hygiene promotion and other WASH related community outreach activities using multiple formats to ensure accessibility.

The proposed interventions align well with the South Sudan 
WASH cluster objectives 1; contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition, 2.1. Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties and 2.2. WASH specific activities for GBV (or mitigating WASH GBV)

Save the children targets a total of 64,438 beneficiaries (32,960 Male, 31,478 Females) across the five counties. The estimated cost to deliver the proposed WASH interventions is USD 2,500,000

project_name: 2021-22 Integrated Response for Conflict-Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) FSL
project_objective: The food security and livelihood sub-component of the program is aimed at improving the overall food security and livelihoods of 32,100 affected households including 3,367 IDPs, thus improving resilience. It is expected that by improving HH agriculture production and fishing techniques, HHs will rely less on humanitarian assistance and will be able to sufficiently meet their own food needs. Furthermore, local economies will be strengthened and communities will become more resilient against current and future shocks. This is achieved through layering and sequencing of interventions across the two interlinked and mutually supportive sectors, i.e. agriculture/food security and economic recovery and market strengthening. This integrated approach ensures that beneficiaries not only receive the resources they need to thrive, but also the training and knowledge they need to sustain their own livelihoods.

project_name: Mayendit and Mayom Mobile Health Services
project_objective:
In Mayendit and Mayom Counties, Unity State, Samaritan’s Purse, South Sudan, provide life-saving primary health services using a mobile health approach in eight (8)  separate hard to reach, crisis affected communities who are unable to reach existing health care facilities and who have are impacted by conflict and flooding, with many needing to temporarily relocate as well as host IDP’s from surrounding areas. 
Objectives: 
1.	To provide and improve equitable access to basic, lifesaving primary health care in hard to reach, communities (who lack a health service provision), particularly prioritizing vulnerable community members, including women and children, the elderly, people with disabilities and those in need of MHPSS, survivors of SGBV and trauma in selected communities in Northern Mayendit. 
2.	To reduce morbidity and mortality through the provision of basic primary health care, infection prevention and control measures (IPC), rapid diagnostic testing (RDT), treatment, preventative health care strategies (malaria prophylaxis), routine & reactive immunizations, community health education and disease surveillance and reporting. 
3.	Provide consistent services, awareness and education on health the various services and advantages of preventative health measures to improve health seeking behaviour and positive behaviour change in the outreach communities. 
4.	To promote and enable increased resilience and build the capacity of outreach communities, through strong community engagement, representation of all community members in program development (such as developing shelters for services or fences), site development and engagement of local professionals and community health workers in each target site. 
5.	Improve coordination of humanitarian activities through collaboration with the CHD/MOH and other partners as well as multi/cross sectorial activities to improve overall health in Mayandit County. 
6.	SP will participate in single and multisectoral assessment activities to assess ongoing or developing needs and program impact. 
Mayendit County Mobile Health Services
-	SP Mobile Health Clinicians in Mayendit and Mayom include a Program manager who is Medical Doctor, with Mental Health and Paediatric training and experience, a Clinical Officer, Registered Nurse, Registered Midwife (female), a dispenser (all local professionals), vaccinators and locally engaged Community Health Workers (16F, 16M) provide Primary Health services; general outpatients for communicable, non-communicable diseases as well as initial first aid, screening and referral for SGBV/IPV, MHPSS screening, MHPSS first aid and referral, Reproductive health, antenatal, postnatal and neonatal care, nutrition screening and referral, routine vaccinations and community health awareness and education. On a daily basis the team triage and prioritize the most vulnerable, including women and children, the elderly, people with a disability, the very ill and those who have suffered trauma. The team link in with partners for specialized services such as for SGBV, disability (such as cleft lip & Fistula repair) and MHPSS services. The services are informed from learnings through regular community engagement activities & feedback mechanisms. All data is protected, disaggregated by gender and age and reported weekly to the CHD/MOH, the Health Cluster 5 W’s & WHO/EWARS.

The project seeks to serve 45,000 (22,500 male; 22,500 female) people. Of the targets, an estimated 8,700 are children U5; 16,000 children ages 5 to 18 years; 18,000 adults ages 18 to 59 years; and 3,200 adults over 60 years. Approximately 7,400 beneficiaries are expected to be IDPs.

project_name: Promote lifesaving through malnutrition prevention and improved treatment of acute malnutrition of conflict and flood affected, vulnerable communities in Maiwut, Maban, Nasir, Longechuk counties, Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
RI Nutrition sector primary goal is to promote malnutrition prevention and provision of improved treatment of acute malnutrition to promote good health among conflict affected and vulnerable groups. In 2022, RI’s Nutrition interventions will aim to increase malnutrition prevention activities and provide continuous improved and timely community-based management of acute malnutrition projects in the Greater Upper Nile with Health, WASH, FSL, Protection sectors linkages to address interrelated and under-lying causes of malnutrition, such as food insecurity, suboptimal childcare and feeding practices and lack of safe water and sanitation  

RI’s aim is to support South Sudanese including refugees, internal displaced persons, returnees and vulnerable population including people with disabilities. Our response will prioritize life-saving treatment services targeting children under five years and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs), in compliance with relevant national guidelines. These are the most vulnerable groups to malnutrition due to their increased biological and physiological needs. Geographically, our response will continue to prioritize states in the Upper Nile namely Maiwut, Maban, Nasir, and Longechuk which are characterized by high malnutrition, food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 and 4), conflict and internal displacement. 
The RI nutrition sites will act as hubs for integrated programming. The RI health sector will provide malaria testing and treatment among the severely acute malnourished (SAM) children being treated at the nutrition sites, while the RI WASH sector will provide NFI kits to severely malnourished children’s families and the RI FSL sector will establish kitchen gardens at nutrition sites to demonstrate recommended feeding practices.
Furthermore, the RI nutrition sites will integrate the early childhood development stimulation activities and will be considered as potential entry points for GBV victims looking for assistance, with nutrition staff trained on GBV referral pathways. 
To further localize the RI’s response and to ensure sustainability, RI will strengthen the County Health Department (CHD) responsibilities to oversee the nutrition interventions, to coordinate the response with various stakeholders at the county level and provide stakeholder’s capacity building on the new national guidelines on community based management of malnutrition and maternal, infant, and young child nutrition. 
RI will provide technical support to the CHD to review the county level nutrition intervention’s strategy which includes coming with nutrition county action plan, routine monitoring and supportive supervision of routine nutrition site activities, facilitation of Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM), Maternal, Infant and Young Child Feeding Nutrition (MIYCN) training, VASD campaign, FSNMS surveys, advocacy and focusing Family malnutrition screening for timely cases managements and follow up.
RI will reinforce the nutrition information system and the use of nutrition data at the county and the community level by employing a gender-sensitive approach to mitigate any obstacles compromising women and girls’ ability to receive nutrition support. Women’s participation will be encouraged in programme design and feedback mechanisms. RI will also collaborate with existing and planned development interventions on nutrition, such as those funded by the World Bank in the greater upper Nile. 

RI will pursue four objectives including: 
•	Prevent under-nutrition by increasing access to maternal, infant and young child nutrition interventions and VASD campaign. 
•	Deliver life-saving management of acute malnutrition for the most vulnerable and at-risk U5 children and pregnant and lactating women
•	Enhance nutrition situation monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information for early warning and decision making.
•	Increase access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH, FSL and protection interventions

project_name: WASH project for IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable host population to mitigate and prevent malnutrition and gender-based violence in Maiwut, Ulang and Nasir Counties, Upper Nile State, South Sudan
project_objective:
This intervention aims at contributing to the improved health and hygiene status of women, girls, men, boys, the elderly and persons with disabilities (PWDs) through timely and equitable access to safe, potable and adequate water in targeted communities in Maiwut, Nasir and Ulang counties. 
The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with RI’s health , nutrition , protection and FSL programming. Women and girls are the primary users of WASH services, the intervention is designed to be gender-sensitive and prevent GBV. Activities will include provision of safe water supply; upgrading of existing boreholes to solar powered water supply system, pipe line extension from the existing solar powered water supply system and distribution of water purification chemical (PUR), (for those beneficiaries who are depending on river or surface water) , the rehabilitation of water points (boreholes) with secure location and access within the community and nutrition facilities with a focus on construction of flood resilient boreholes for which the apron and flood protective wall will be raised by at least 1m. The designs of the structures will be considered so that people with disabilities (PWDs-both male and female) as well as older people can easily access and collect water. Further, household latrine construction, WASH NFI distribution, and the training of Water Users Committees (WUCs) and pump mechanics will be carried out. RI will encourage selection and participation of female in the WUCs. Each of the WUCs will consist of at least 50% female membership. These WUCs will be responsible for ensuring that sustainable and viable operation and maintenance of these systems are in place at the community level. RI will ensure the quality of water through water quality testing which will be done before and after rehabilitation/construct on of water points.
For the sanitation component, the project plans the implementation of flood resilient communal and institutional ventilated improved pit latrines which will be equipped with hand washing facilities. The design of the structures will be done considering all the segments of the society especially PWDs and older people and ensure that they can access them easily without any barrier. The latrines will be gender inclusive and will have a lock on the doors for protection purposes. The location will also not be far from the beneficiaries’ home and will therefore be easily accessible by women and girls during day and evening time. The construction of latrines will be complemented by the delivery of hygiene promotion messaging on safe excreta disposal to improve the sanitation practices. RI hygiene promoters and trained home health promoters (HHPs) will conduct weekly monitoring visits to at community, nutrition and household level to assess the usage and cleanliness of the latrines and document any challenges or feedback from the household. The HHPs will disseminate information on the five essential hygiene and sanitation practices (fecal–oral route transmission or the ‘F-diagram’), Safe water handling, Safe excreta disposal, Handwashing and personal hygiene, Environmental hygiene and baby WASH messages. RI will continue using its internal hygiene promotion training module as well as the Care Group Manual to train HHPs for the Healthy Practices, Safe Communities Project.
To improve, the WASH condition of the caretakers of SAM/MAM which contributes reduction of malnutrition, WASH NFI kits will be distributed. The integrated approach will address the high levels of malnutrition by targeting the families of SAM and MAM children for WASH interventions and providing access to drinking water, thereby acknowledging that poor WASH services are a key driver of poor health and malnutrition. The WASH intervention in these three counties will be done carefully without creating any conflict among the beneficiaries.
Data will be disaggregated by sex and age wherever possible.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Lifesaving Nutrition interventions to conflict affected populations (Children 0-59 months, pregnant and lactating women) in Canal Pigi, Panyjar, Malakal and Juba IDP Camps Counties in South Sudan
project_objective:
Through the proposed humanitarian responses, International Medical Corps (IMC UK) will provide integrated lifesaving nutrition service to conflict affected and displaced communities in Juba IDP Camps, Panyijar, Malakal and Canal Pigi Counties. With the aim to reduce suffering, morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable populations, IMC will increase equitable access and utilization of comprehensive treatment and preventive nutrition specific services, which are essential for addressing key drivers of acute malnutrition affecting children and women in the aforesaid project locations. IMC UK will also continue to address prevention of malnutrition in children under two years of age through promotion of appropriate Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition Feeding (MIYCN) practices. The service will be delivered through static and outreach sites for remote and hard to reach areas in the targeted project locations. The proposed response will include all components of Community Management of Acute Malnutrition, including Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP), Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP), Stabilization Center (SC) and community mobilization activities. International Medical Corps UK proposes to operate 22 OTPs, 22 Targeted supplementary feeding programs (TSFPs), and 2 SCs across the project sites. IMC UK will work with the Ministry of Health (MoH), UNICEF and WFP to secure timely provision of nutrition supplies, which are necessary for nutrition service delivery. IMC will reach approximately 105,899 individuals, of which 50,831 are IDPs. All project activities will be implemented in line with adapted guidelines for nutrition services delivery in the context of COVID-19 provided by the Nutrition Cluster. 
IMC UK will monitor the nutrition status of the population and the nutrition response through routine nutrition program data, quarterly MUAC screening campaigns and population-based SMART Surveys. IMC UK, with its already established Nutrition Surveillance Team, will undertake nutrition assessments in its operational locations and support to undertake in nutrition assessments in Priority counties as well to provide robust information on the nutrition situation of a given population, this information will be key in responding effectively to nutrition needs in the project area. 
Additionally, IMC UK will reinforce and promote access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH, protection and FSL services provision in the project target areas through geographical integration, activity integration, and integration through common approaches to reduce the burden of malnutrition. IMC will also closely work with Nutrition partners in the target location to prevent overlap of the services and enhance services availability through referral and integration. This project aims to enhance nutrition-sensitive interventions that will ensure safe, equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services; to further decrease the prevalence of acute malnutrition, and ultimately, to contribute to the prevention and reduction of morbidity and mortality associated to malnutrition in South Sudan. IMC will also support hygiene interventions to improve nutrition outcomes and reduce risks of hygiene-related morbidities. Nutrition services will be considered as potential entry points for GBV survivors seeking assistance, with nutrition staff trained on GBV referral pathways and other key GBV concepts. The project protection focal points will perform safety audits and assessments of nutrition sites. Safety audits are one of the key approaches used to identify potential GBV related risks at the program sites using a tested tool. The project will conduct safety audit assessments bi-annually at the health and nutrition sites.

project_name: Primary Health Care Services to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality
project_objective: Under this project, Concern ensures provision of the Ministry of Health (MoH’s) Basic Package of Health Services (BPHS) to communities that are not covered by Health Pooled Fund (HPF) partners in North Bahr al Ghazal (Aweil South, West and North Counties),  and  Kajo-Keji County in Central Equatoria. Concern will support mobile sites that will provide primary health care for outpatient treatment of common illnesses including malaria, ARTIs and diarrhoea and coordinate with partners to ensure Concern is targeting those locations where there are critical gaps in provision of basic services. Concern will also support the SMoH and CHDs to provide the EPI services in Health facilities not covered under HPF 3 through seconding one EPI Worker in identified health facilities, to reduce the risks of communicable diseases. This project will be integrated with other Concern’s multi-donor funded programme that will make will help in coverage of health services is wide geographic area. Concern’s mobile teams will focus on providing services in hard-to-reach areas. In NBeG, these are generally remote areas that are more than 10km from fixed health facilities, where the mobile team will conduct weekly outreach services to 10 locations (Aweil west: 05, Aweil North:05). A mobile team comprised of Clinical Officers, Nurses, Midwives and EPI worker. In Aweil South County, the project will support 4 static health facilities not under HPF3, Concern will continue to provide monthly incentives to SMoH staff, medical supplies and capacity training to those seconded SMoH staff in Aweil South County. In Kajo-Keji, the approach will be provision of Health services in 5 hard-to-reach locations where limited services are being offered, either by the Ministry of Health or other Health partners, however this team will work within the framework of existing facilities where possible. In Kajo-Keji based on coordination with County Health Department (CHD), Concern will also continue supporting Lire PHCC with paying SMOH staff incentives, provision of medical supplies and staff capacity development.

project_name: Provision of life saving nutrition services
project_objective:
Concern will continue to support preventative and curative nutrition services in Rubkona and Guit county in Unity state, Aweil West and Aweil North in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, in Juba IDP camp and Kajo-Koji in Central Equatoria states following the national Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) and community based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) guidelines. The treatment package include management of severe acute malnutrition through the Outpatient therapeutic programme and stabilization centre  (OTP/SC) and management of moderate acute malnutrition through the targeted supplementary programme (TSFP). Concern will emphasise prevention of acute malnutrition in this response through the focus on behaviour change communication, promotion of home gardening to improve MIYCN practices. In Juba IDP, camp (former PoC) Concern manages two OTP/TSFP sites while SAM with medical complications are referred to stabilisation centre managed by other partners. In Kajo-Keji Concern provides nutrition services in 4 mobile and one static health facilities. In Unity, Concern provides nutrition services in 14 sites, while in Leer county in Unity, Concern supports local partner Nile Hope to provide nutrition services in 5 sites. Similarly, in NBeG Concern provides nutrition services in 50 sites both in Aweil North and Aweil West counties. The Caregivers provide treatment for the majority of children with severe acute malnutrition in the home using nutrition supplies and routine medical care. When necessary, severely malnourished children who have medical complications or lack an appetite are referred to in-patient facilities for more intensive treatment. To ensure community participation and improve access and coverage, Concern will involve community volunteers for community mobilization, screening, follow up cases and dissemination of recommended nutrition behaviours. Concern has developed a mothers and fathers group curriculum to re-inforce the mother and father group sessions in the community.  

The level of acute malnutrition often attributed to severe food insecurity, poor access to health and nutrition services, extremely poor diets and limited access to clean water, poor sanitation and hygiene. Therefore, the nutrition service provision will be integrated with provision of WASH, health and food security assistance where possible and appropriate.

project_name: SNFI assistance to the flood and conflict affected population in Unity State
project_objective: Concern is the State focal point for Shelter NFI (SNFI) cluster in Unity State, manages the SNFI re-enforcement needs in Bentiu IDP camp, Rubkona and Guit Counties. This project will focus on improving the living conditions and protecting dignity of the people through SNFI assistance to protracted IDPs, newly displaced flood affected HHs and returnees. The SNFI materials will be sourced from cluster stock. Concern will collaborate with protection cluster to receive referral for PSNs including PWDs, women headed HH, elderly etc.  In addition to routine repair and maintenance of shelter through cluster stock in Bentiu IDP camp, Concern will work on upgradation of the shelter through locally available materials and promoting community ownership in their shelter repairs and improvements. In close consultation with the Camp High Committee (CHC), Camp management, protection partners and local authorities, the target beneficiaries will be provided with a voucher to redeem for grass mats from locally identified women groups who are engaged in production of grass mats within IDP site. Concern will train and provide technical oversight to the beneficiaries on installation of grass mats to improve existing shelters. The vulnerable groups such PWDs, child headed HH and elderly will be supported the labour for repair of their shelter. The flood affected displaced HH will be supported with emergency SNFI assistance (materials sourced from cluster stock) based on assessed needs using SNFI cluster standard operational procedures. The returnees will be supported with shelter and NFI through voucher depending on market assessment. Given, Housing, Land and Property (HLP) issues and related conflict, Concern will closely work with the local government, protection cluster to ensure do no harm and land right issues will be considered during shelter assistance. Concern in coordination with relevant stakeholders including protection partners will identify legal and/or community-based solutions to resolve HLP disputes.

project_name: Capacity Development support for northwest Syrian response community
project_objective:
IOM aims to contribute to effective coordination and the UN's localization efforts by building the capacity of implementing partners. As the humanitarian situation in northwest Syria remains grave with increasing hostilities, a deteriorating humanitarian situation, and new displacements, the capacity of humanitarian actors in northwest Syria is stretched thin after 10 years of conflict. It is also possible that in  the event of non-renewal of the UNSCR, some UN agencies may be forced to scale down or adapt their cross-border activities. INGOs and NGOs would then be required to significantly scale up their operations in order to continue supporting affected communities. INGOs and NGOs will be expected to maintain the delivery of quality humanitarian response activities and ensure effective coordination. As such, it is paramount to continue building the capacity of INGO and NGO partners across technical and cross-cutting topics.

In 2021, IOM supported the capacity development of its partners and cluster partners through trainings, coaching, mentoring, learning exchange workshops, and improving the partner’s institutional process and procedures through reviewing, and developing guidance documents, SoPs and checklists. Topics varied from project cycle management, finance, procurement, humanitarian access negotiation, and Cash-Based Intervention (CBI). In addition to those training, IOM published COVID-19 AAP videos and COVID-19 vaccination videos to support the information sharing, awareness-raising effort towards COVID-19 by the COVID-19 task force and the Health cluster. 

The need for building the organizational capacity of implementing partners remains critical. This has been reflected in the different joint capacity need assessments IOM regularly conducts with its partners.  IPs consistently highlighted the need for more capacity-building sessions on administrative areas such as Governance, Human Resources, Compliance, Programme Development and Reporting to improve their institutional process and procedures in resource mobilization and management. Furthermore, IOM aims to build the capacity of implementing partners and Cluster partners on sector-specific topics and cross-cutting topics such as community engagement, humanitarian principle, access negotiation and disability inclusion. 

Building on its capacity development activities in 2021, IOM will organize around 64 trainings, consultation and coaching sessions on humanitarian access negotiation, human resource management, governance, compliance, and trainings on WASH-related topics in 2022 and 2023. IOM will facilitate a Training of facilitators (ToF) and Advance Certificate training on humanitarian access negotiation under the auspices of Access Working Group and OCHA for the sake of reaching in a wider group. Based on a clear workplan, the participants from the ToF will conduct peer workshops on humanitarian access and negotiation in northwest Syria reaching field humanitarian staff. In addition to the above trainings, IOM will also support the partners’ development of organizational and operational policy and procedures. All activities will be coordinated with relevant Clusters, Technical Working Groups, and other coordination fora.

project_name: Child Protection Intervention for vulnerable children
project_objective:
In Lebanon, with the deepening economic crisis collapse in services and impact of the pandemic, child rights’ violations including child marriage, child labor, and violence are increasing drastically with a heightened risk of detrimental physical, emotional, and mental health consequences. Along with the increased distress levels of the caregivers, children are now at further risk of exploitation, abuse, neglect, separation and distress at the cost of their wellbeing, education. Residential care is the predominant form of Alternative Care available for girls and boys in Lebanon and it is almost exclusively for Lebanese children. While there is a functional informal system, it relies heavily on placement with extended family which is not always in the best interests of the child.
Aim and strategy of Intervention
Ensure children are protected and have access to mental health and psychosocial support. This includes mental health and psychosocial support, providing safe spaces for girls and boys and case management interventions. We plan to provide female support kits to adolescent girls benefitting from case management services, and Alternative care support for children, non-focused PSS, focused PSS, and provision of child protection kits.
•	Establishing safe spaces and/or use existing community spaces for children receive psychosocial support and provide them with the opportunity to integrate with other children,
•	Conducting case management intervention for children at risk of all protection concerns, including CAAC
•	Providing mental health and psychosocial support for children and youth,
•	Providing child protection kits which will include educational and recreational materials for children identified via CM and CP activities.
Ensure caregivers have access to psychosocial support, support group sessions to promote for their children’s safety and well-being, and increase community members’ awareness on child rights, SGBV concerns, and IYCF support. 
•	Conducting caregiver support group sessions to provide them with the needed support and ensure children at risk are being identified and responded to at the safest way possible, 
•	Providing Alternative Care services for children at high risk

Provide emergency cash assistance to children and households supported through case management. 
Launch child protection events and initiatives to address and mitigate child protection risks in communities. SC, with the support from our Child Rights Governance team, will conduct 3 main campaigns and/or events to be conducted that will focus on the reintegration of various communities while addressing children’s rights and mitigation measures, where children led activities will also take place so children can voice their concerns and advocate for their rights.
Intervention areas, targets, and segregation:
SC and partner will aim to reach 260 children through case management specialized services. A total of 2550 children are expected to be supported via community based child protection activities across all 3 offices, while 208 children will receive Focused and Specialized Psycho-Social Support, as well as 658 caregivers are expected to participate in support group activities promoting safety and wellbeing of children. SC and partner will aim to refer 360 individuals to benefit from emergency cash support that are to be identified via case management services. SC will also aim to lead on 3 initiatives and/or events advocating for children’s rights across all areas of intervention reaching an estimate of 600 individuals. SC will provide Female Support Kits to all girls and adult females participating in our activities and child protection kits to all targeted children. In order to ensure inclusion of children and adults with impairments, SC and partner will aim for at least 15% of total reach to be targeting individuals with impairments.
