project_name: WASH static and emergency response for vulnerable IDPs, host communities and returnees in South Sudan.
project_objective:
NRC’s planned and proposed  Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) intervention for 2022  is designed to address the emergency WASH needs through mobile response and  contribute to improve health,  nutrition and protection  outcomes through NRC static WASH response. The proposed interventions are  to reduce prevalence of malnutrition, contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality, provide access to basic WASH services in underserved locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility and durable access to WASH amongst 200, 000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in in South Sudan.


The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with NRC’s health , nutrition  and protection programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to uplift  people’s lives  and  contributing to South Sudan HRP and WASH Cluster objectives and the 2022 Humanitarian Response. Recognizing WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. NRC’s  integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition in targeted locations.


NRC will consult and engage communities in preliminary assessments and design process to ensure all NRC’s interventions are tailored to local context and to establish appropriated water and sanitation facilities at community, institutions and household level. To enhance and ensure sustainability  and proper usage of the facilities comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) and Health & Nutrition facility staff. Solid waste management training will also be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns. NRC  will also construct incinerators for medical waste disposal at health facilities.


To ensure durable and continues access to safe water ; NRC will establish / rehabilitate small scale solar powered water supply schemes , new boreholes through cost effective manual Borehole drilling. The proposed water supply interventions will increase the safe water access to health, nutrition and protection centers , disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WAH facilities and route to WASH facilities. NRC will construct own driven household / family shared latrines to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. The approach will enhance the ownership and sustainability of the facilities.NRC  will also promote good hygiene practices and  awareness through training of community hygiene promoters who then will be conducting hygiene promotion at their own communities , community hygiene campaigns, hygiene promotion campaigns and sessions at intuitional levels and provision of hygiene kits, WASH-NFIs and soaps to the vulnerable communities specially in hard to reach areas.

project_name: Quality Education for Emergency Affected Children and Youth in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the intervention is to ensure that emergency affected girls and boys as well as youth continually access quality learning opportunities relevant for their psycho-social well-being, physical and cognitive development.  The project targets children and youth aged between 6 - 17  from IDP, returnees and host community families with age appropriate interventions that respond to their education needs. Primary focus for this project is displacement affected out-of-school children and youth affected by conflict and climate emergencies. NRC anticipates to reach 38,873 children (52% girls); 875 adults (400 men ; 475 women [375 teachers & 500 parents/caregivers and other non-teaching professionals) as direct beneficiaries. The project will focus on strengthening and improving quality and delivery of education in four strategic response areas which are 1) First Phase response - through NRC's mobile response operations and targeting newly displaced families, with short term education activities lasting from 6-9 months. 2) Formal education - conducted through NRC's static program operations across the country in prioritized counties where NRC has existing physical presence; 3) Non Formal education through ALP classes for over-aged children who missed years of schooling due to conflict and displacement and 4) Youth Education and training with an emphasis on vocational skills training, peace-building and life-skills training.  In close collaboration with parents, caregivers and local actors, NRC will construct and repair learning spaces/classrooms and gender segregated school WASH facilities; provide school hardware assets (desks/benches), essential learning materials, teacher aids, recreational & hygiene kits; girls dignity kits for MHM; support mgt of schools through teacher selection, recruitment, motivation, training on child centered pedagogical methods, curriculum planning, classroom mgt & conflict sensitive education; support teacher learning cycles (TLCs) for continuous professional dvpt; facilitate community engagement in education through establishment/strengthening of PTAs & SMCs through training in roles and responsibilities, school development planning and awarding school improvement grants; conduct awareness raising community dialogue sessions to mobilize enrollment, promote attendance and support retention especially for girls who face multiple barriers to education including harmful and social practices such as forced early marriages and boys who also face protection risks that include child labour and forced recruitment into armed groups; conduct life skills training & support structured recreational activities for physical and psycho-social development; provide technical and material support non-teaching professionals (county education directors,  supervisors) to effectively conduct their school supervision and support duties; training of teachers, facilitators, on Mental Health and psycho-social support (MHPSS), Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), child protection, child safeguarding and PSEA; provide cash and vouchers assistance to the most vulnerable for examination registration. 
Key approaches that NRC will adopt in this project include integration, partnerships and community based programming.  NRC will collaborate local structures as well as with other clusters including protection, WASH, shelter, LFS, Nutrition and Health to deliver comprehensive package that addresses the holistic needs of targeted population. Furthermore, for durable solutions, NRC will work with local actors, parents and care-givers building their capacity for self reliance and also to increase coverage in hard to reach areas  with periodic access challenges and bureaucratic impediments. For effective and efficient use of resources and for learning purposes, NRC will continue to participate in coordination mechanisms at both the national and sub-national levels to avoid overlaps and duplication with other education players.

project_name: Emergency S/NFIs response to IDPs, Returnees and Host Community affected by disasters in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to provide Survival Kits /Emergency shelter/Non Food items both in-kind and in cash modalities to the most vulnerable persons, newly displaced/host communities and returnees. The project will focus on the life saving shelter/NFIs needs, as identified through assessment to protect the affected displaced people from harsh weather conditions and protection risks targeting all states of South Sudan. The intervention will be implemented through mobile response as well as using its static teams based in Kajo Keji, Juba, Koch, Mayom, Leer, Bor, Duk, Twic East, Akobo, Aweil, Wau and Alek. However the major focus areas will be Jonglei, Unity, Northern Bahrel Ghazal, Central, Western and Eastern Equatoria states. Cash programming will also be considered in areas where markets are fully or semi-functional and shelter/NFI items are available and accessible by the community. When blanket targeting is not applicable, the intervention will target mainly lactating and pregnant women, households with malnourished children, and households with members who have certain health complications. Besides unaccompanied children, unaccompanied elderly and persons with no community linkages will also be targeted.
The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities for 2022 HRP's. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 22 days for full-fledged delivery of NFIs and emergency shelters and other activities per location. The project will also support returnees in settlement as part of the local integration or as they settle into their areas of origin. The project will benefit 120,000 individuals directly.

project_name: Education in Emergencies in Syria
project_objective:
The war in Syria continues to have a profound impact on people across the country and at least half of the people affected by the crisis are children. The humanitarian situation in the country remains severe as the decline of the economic situation exacerbates the effects of the conflict. The education sector is impacted by low availability of education services, few functional schools, shortage of teachers, and especially qualified teachers. The targeted areas are expecting large numbers of returnees to further stretch the education sector’s capacity. The impact of the COVID19, rapid devaluation of the Syrian Pound and the international sanctions are putting additional strain on the population and local administrations. 
There are 133 schools in Hama and Homs, out of which only 62 are currently in service.  Most of the schools that are operational are overcrowded. 47% of the schools totally miss furniture, while 53% have partial availability of furniture. In the event of an increase in the number of returnees to the target areas, it is expected that the schools will not be able to accommodate children unless additional classes are opened. All assessed schools are only partially accessible and most of the toilets are unusable. The recent Needs Assessment suggests that there are currently approximately 104,000 children of school age in Hama and Homs, and it is estimated  that 60% - 70% of them are at risk of dropping out, as the areas have high numbers of returnees.
All of the areas that FCA program is covering area are marked as 3 or above on the severity scale. Most of the target location are newly opened returnees areas with the high demand for education services and often presence of operational schools is a motivating factor for the families to return to the area. 
The project directly contributes to HRP priorities both in terms of geographical prioritization as well as by combining soft (non-formal education, protection etc) and hard components (school rehabilitation, school furniture, students kits etc)  in education focusing on quality education. 
The project will address beneficiaries' need by implementing the following activities: 
Access to education related activities: 
1.1. Rehabilitation or establishing of ECE rooms in schools  
1.2. Provision of Non Formal Education (NFE) through remedial and catch-up classes
1.2. Rehabilitation of the school building including WASH facilities (for boys and girls)
1.3. Distribution of Student's kits and winterization items
1.4. Back to learning campaign
1.5. Setting up prefabricated classes in the locations where schools are damaged and cannot be rehabilitated. 

Protection related activities: 
2.1. Protection events in schools
2.2. Establishing and supporting school based protection committees
2.3. Recreational activities in schools 
2.4. Community led initiatives
2.5. Psychological support for teacher (in and outside the classroom)

Quality of Education related activities 
3.1. Equipping schools with furniture and teaching and learning materials.
3.2 Teachers' training
3.3. Support for children with disabilities
3.4. Setting up and supporting Parents Teachers Associations (PTA)

WASH related activities 
4.1 Rehabilitation of water supply
4.2. Water trucking to schools
4.3. Provision of personal hygiene kits (especially for girls) and school hygiene supplies

M&E Framework is used to ensure that stakeholder opinions are heard. Activities will be directly monitored by FCA field staff under the supervision of the Education Project Manager. 2 M&E staff will be responsible for the monitoring of results, activities and indicators as proposed in the action. The data have been collected during the NA conducted in Oct 21-Jan 22; in the beginning of the project FCA team will collect baseline data for each indicator as per the LF. Different M&E tools have been created: activity report, school attendance sheets, child wellbeing questionnaire, entrance/exit tests, school rehab. checklist.

project_name: RESPONSIVE CONDITIONS & CONTEXT MONITORING (RCCM)
project_objective:
There remains an acute, unmet need for responsive qualitative R&A that directly supports humanitarian partners’ ability to efficiently advocate for, develop, and implement targeted programming in Syria. Under current conditions, effective programing requires critical decisions, and therefore deep understanding, of issues related to emergency aid, early recovery, stabilization, and durable solutions. However, feedback from partners demonstrates they continue to struggle to efficiently navigate the multitude of dynamic challenges. To be able to effectively provide vital assistance to millions of Syrians in need, partners and donors require a responsive mechanism for tasking and receiving high-quality qualitative R&A.
RCCM aims to meet this need by creating timely relevant R&A to support programming that improves immediate conditions for Syrians and is also conducive to supporting future prospects for recovery and durable solutions. Over the past eight years, iMMAP has developed a nuanced understanding of the problems, needs, and risks faced by humanitarian partners operating in a prolonged conflict with an array of complexities.
In contrast to most reporting in the humanitarian sector in Syria, RCCM will rely on qualitative primary and secondary data collection tools. Primary data collection tools, employed by highly experience and knowledgeable core RCCM team members and area and technical expert STTAs, will include KIIs with local and international stakeholders relevant to the report topic and semi-structured reports based on discussions with key stakeholders and STTA knowledge. Secondary data collection tools will include review of open-source data, including local and international media reports, quantitative reporting produced by operational partners in Syria, and social media. Tools will be employed to ensure robust triangulation.
RCCM is designed to respond to a growing gap in qualitative, responsive reporting and analysis for humanitarian actors, one which has been repeatedly communicated to iMMAP by partners during RCM, the previous iteration of this project. RCCM is not meant to duplicate ongoing quantitative data collection and reporting efforts carried out by others, but to compliment them. Quantitative data collection is often limited in the type of subjects, information and analysis. RCCM is designed, from teaming to deliverables, to fill these gaps. iMMAP has conducted several discussions with partner organizations in Syria on how to successfully pursue a complimentary, coordinated approach.
RCM produced a number of detailed thematic reports that were released just prior to significant discussion on the focus topics, including reports on potential Turkish incursion scenarios in late 2021 and social support systems across zones of control in early 2022. RCM also produced area profiles that provided an updated and thorough look at several focus areas, namely Quamishli and Deir-ez-Zor, and a response report on the ISIS attack on the Ghweiran prison. Repeated surveys show that RCM’s audience overwhelmingly use these reports for their improved understanding of the Syrian context. Over 40% says it used the reports for decision making and planning activities. 
Potential report topic examples include: 1) Thematic Reports: Current Conflict Assessment: Overview of Frontlines and Potential Flashpoints Across Syria; GoS-Self Administration Talks: Prospects and Impact of a Bilateral Political Agreement; SSG-SIG/Turkey Relations: Future Governance Scenarios for NWS; Crossline and Cross border Trade in Syria; A Divided Education System: Reviewing Curriculums Across Syria, and 2) Response Report Topics: Expectations and Potential Impacts of the 2022 Wheat Harvest; Status of Kurdish-Kurdish Talks in NES; Responses and Impact to the Mulham Campaign in NWS; Overview and Outlook of GoS Reconciliation Drive in Eastern Syria; Implications of the Revised Social Contract in NES; Status of the Justice System in NES.

project_name: To save lives, reduce the psychological suffering and improved and sustain mental health service and psychosocial well-being across Syria
project_objective:
The WoS population continues to suffer extreme physical and psychological harm facing simultaneous multiple emergencies, ongoing displacement and economic hardship compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic. The major objectives of mental health programs are in alignment with the proposed HRP 2022 strategic objectives and the mhGAP extended action plan 2013-2030, is to strengthen effective leadership and the advocacy for mental health; providing comprehensive, integrated, and responsive mental health services in health facilities and at community-based platforms; develop strategies for promotion and prevention in mental health and strengthen information systems for mental health. potential coverage of mental health service, including accessibility-availability- and service acceptance, and psychosocial support services at the level of functioning PHCs across the country reached up to 35%, wherein, 490 functional public health centers providing the integrated services
as 68,569 consultations by trained and supervised Drs on mhGAP program, and 58,185 basic psychological interventions by health workers,
 At the community level, WHO supported 16 key implementing partners by delivering a total of 180,538 MH consultations/services in community wellbeing centers and mobile teams reaching 268 subdistricts, through community workers trained on different MHPSS programmes in response to the people in need (IDPs, host communities in NWS, Southern Syria (SS) and in NES) on the other hands at public health centers and through 5630  health and community workers to enhance the provision of integrated and appropriate services at health and community levels . WHO also procured and distributed 280,848 treatment courses to more than 50 health partners across the country, including in NES, to support the provision of pharmaceutical therapeutic interventions for persons suffering from mental health conditions, In context of COVID19 response and building on 2020 campaigns achievement and lesson learned, series of community campaigns under RCCE pillar with the focus on MHPSS key messages, coping with stress, awareness raising session targeting children, elder adults, and caregivers, combating stigma,  up to 287,700 unique services delivered in Rural Damascus, Aleppo, Homs, Hama, Deir eZZour through more than 18000 different sessions and activities, including remotely MHPSS consultations
In these challenging circumstances WHO continue to provide support to all 141 existing facilities in NWS with MHPSS services, providing technical support and regular supplies of medication in 69 communities and 29 sub-districts. It is planned as well to continue supporting 2 non-specialized MHPSS facilities that are providing quality non-specialized MHPSS care and are helping to fill- in the gap on MHPSS services, including supporting MHPSS Helplines and the 24/7 Suicide Prevention
Hotline for NWS, while ensuring creation of MHPSS messages to conduct awareness raising sessions focusing on reduction of stigma towards mental health patients.
Two main referral pathways for MHPSS in NWS will be secured.   
1. The online referral in case of a need for upper-level care and support to the helpline caller.
2. The physical referral for the more serious and severe cases to receive further help from the psychiatrist upon need.
Herein, all the teams of PSWs will be provided with a service mapping that includes all of the available MHPSS humanitarian actors operating in the covered areas.

project_name: Providing Community Based and specialized Gender Based Violence and Child Protection Services in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
RI aims to provide prevention, empowerment, and response GBV services as well as CP prevention and response services through a standalone and integrated approach with RI health services in the targeted area. RI will target the most vulnerable women, girls, and boys including people with disability, widowed women and children living in widows camps, women and children headed households, adolescent girls, adolescent boys, and older women.RI will utilize a community-based approach to enhance access to the most vulnerable targeted categories through outreach, community committees. RI will support functioning 3 WGSSs in the following subdistricts: Teftanaz in Idleb, Azaz in Aleppo.RI will strengthen its integrated model of health and protection services to prevent and respond to GBV, building the capacity of all staff composed of GBV caseworkers, PSS workers, and outreach teams through training provided by RI technical team utilizing the materials endorsed by the capacity building initiative for GBV and GBV SC including GBV CM training and following supervision mechanisms to ensure service quality including assessing attitudes, knowledge, and skills and providing staff care through in-person and online supervision and follow up. RI will include GBV team in Abin Samaan Medical Complex in Abin Samaan in Atareb /Aleppo to provide integrated GBV prevention and response services with the reproductive health services. RI will use its supported health facility in Teftanaz AlNour Maternity and Children Hospital as an entry point, link survivors to specialized services will be provided in the WGSS there.RI will coordinate with other actors through the referral pathway developed by GBV SC and complementing the localized service mapping will be conducted regularly by the team in the target areas to ensure safe referral and avoid duplication.
In line with the GBV Minimum Standards in Emergencies, the services provided within RI WGSSs are GBV response including case management, PFA, individual and group counseling, and referral to CMR, MH, and non GBV services based on the needs and informed consent of the survivors and women and girls at risk in addition to prevention services, RI will support the establishment of women’s committees to foster the participation of women in decision-making structures as well as build on community protective mechanisms already in place. RI will work on capacity building the humanitarian workers including the health workers to be aware of GBV concepts and deal with GBV survivors upon disclosure.
On the other hand, RI will provide CP services including outreach activities, awareness-raising on CP concepts, structured PSS for boys and girls including children with disabilities, parenting skills, and providing CP case management for children with and at risk of child protection risks. RI will ensure engagement of the community through establishing and training CP committees from the community to be responsible for raising awareness on CP concerns in the targeted areas as well as identification and referral of children at risk to response services provided at the CFSs.
All activities will be implemented while adhering to strict COVID 19 prevention measures. Hotline service will be used additionally to provide online information sharing, Psychological first aid, and referral.
the GBV services will be monitored, measured, and evaluated with recommendations to improve the services delivered in the targeted areas according to the GBV MEAL toolkits developed by the GBV SC with focusing on the quality of service benefiting from the supervision mechanisms and monitoring tools including the survivor satisfaction survey. while CP services will follow a MEAL approach includes monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning which is supported by technical expertise in gender, age & disability, child protection and consistent and accurate flow of information and data in relation to gender, age, and disability.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action Coordination NES
project_objective:
iMMAP sponsors the NES HMAC that acts as the HMA Sector Lead within the Protection Working Group and NES Forum. Acting as an independent focal point for all Humanitarian Mine Action activities. The HMAC Role is also responsible for the collection, collation and sharing of HMA Data in line with International Mine Action Standards.

The HMAC coordinates with all HMA actors that are active in NES in clearance activities, non-technical surveys (NTS), EO Risk Education (EORE) and Victim Assistance. The HMAC represents the HMA sector with the local authorities and supports both the partners and sector and the newly established NES Mine Action Center (NESMAC) has ambitions to act as the Mine Action authority, which is a crucial role, especially when it comes to tasking and prioritization. The HMAC also provides a bridge and services and HMA Coordination across the Inter Sector Working Group (ISWG) and the Whole of Syria HMA and Protection Working Groups.

The HMAC is supported by the Information Management team that collects data with the aim of ensuring a living archive and creating a transparent picture of EO contamination in NES. This information is publicly available that supports local communities, authorities and humanitarian/stabilization actors  and donors in conducting safe agricultural activities and (re-)construction of infrastructure and developing strategic planning that supports such as activities as the HNO, HRP and Donor decision making.

project_name: Education is a priority: An Integrated Approach to Enhance Access and Quality of Education in vulnerable and Underserved Communities Within Syria.
project_objective:
As part of its education response, PUI is targeting vulnerable and underserved communities with a bundle of activities, with the overall objective of enhancing the access to quality education provided in protective and suitable learning environment for affected children, to ensure that they don’t become a lost generation. Indeed, with the protracted crisis approaching its eleventh year in Syria, an entire generation of children and youth is being subject to persistent lack of opportunities to access quality education. This situation could have long-term negative consequences, affecting children’s mental health and wellbeing and preventing them from developing in good and safe conditions, as well as gaining essential life skills and knowledge.

The proposed project in brief:
- Will target locations where high education needs are documented by Education Sector. 
More than 77% of the locations have a severity score of 3 (Tafas, Eastern Ghariyeh, Al Mayadin, Abu Kamal, Sbeikhan, Khasham, Talbiseh, Suran, Madiq Castle, Oqeirbat, Arjel, Um Tinet Simaan, Dayr Hafir
Darayya, Duma, Sabka and Maadan), while 18 % have a score of 4 (Deir-ez-Zor, Mahin, Ein Terma and 
Khan Shaykun). PUI also will target Dar'a city which has as score of 5 (4.55% percentage from all areas).

- The cost per beneficiary is 36$ for remedial classes, 48$ for Self-Learning Program, 60$ for Early Childhood education, 4$ for awareness sessions, 6$ for back to learning campaigns, 120$ for teachers’ capacity building and 60000$ for the school rehabilitation activity. The cost per beneficiary is around 104.185$ (Calculated by dividing the total budget by the total number of people the project will target.) 

- It is estimated that around 4,762 individuals of targeted beneficiaries may have disabilities.

This project aims at encouraging out of school students and dropped-out students to resume their education through tailored back to learning campaigns and empowering those children with self-learning program conceived as transition programs to enable them to catch-up and reintegrate the formal education system after this transition period.

In addition, PUI will assist children in their education by providing them with kits, education supplies and remedial classes to cover for any gaps and ensure every child’s educational needs are met and to prevent them from dropping out of school. Furthermore, PUI will contribute to enhancing the quality of education by providing capacity building activities to teachers and MoE staff, training them on active learning, PSS, and life skills. PUI will also initiate an awareness campaign for children and their parents as well as teachers on health and hygiene, with a specific focus on COVID-19 protection and Mine risk education. Lastly, in parallel to the above-mentioned activities, PUI will ensure that children have access to safe and protective learning environment where they can access quality education by rehabilitating damaged schools in targeted locations.

PUI is planning to conduct Remedial classes, back to learning campaigns, Self-Learning programs, Awareness sessions, Early Childhood education and capacity building for teachers in all the targeted areas while the school rehabilitation will be conducted in all areas except for Khasham, Talbiseh, Suran and Dayr Hafir areas as there is no need identified since PUI has already conducted school rehabilitation activities in those areas. 
PUI will create Parents & Teachers Association (PTA) in each school, to support an inclusive participation of the community in the designing and monitoring of the activities. The PTAs will consist of teachers working in the targeted schools and parents of school students. The PTA committee will consist of around 10 to 15 members from both genders and diverse age groups. 

PUI will be training 120 young volunteers to participate in the BTL campaign. Those volunteers will be working for two months.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving WASH support for the conflict affected populations in South Idlib, Hama, Rural Damascus and Dar’a in Syria
project_objective:
TGH’s intervention is closely in line with the 2022-2023 WASH HRP Objectives 1, 2 and 4, as TGH aims to contribute to life-saving WASH interventions and support the resilience of existing WASH systems by addressing the needs of people affected by the conflict in Syria, coupled with the deteriorating context due to the COVID-19 pandemic and worsened by hyperinflationary economic crisis. 
According the draft WASH 2022 HNO report that 13.2 million require WASH assistance in Syria with 47% of the population is relying on often unsafe alternatives to piped water with at least 70% of sewage is discharged untreated and at least half of the sewerage systems are not functional, overall 2.4 million children out of schools and over 40% of caretakers in households with children attending school received complaints from children on WASH-related issues.
The intervention will be integrated intervention in covering WASH, Education and Shelter activities with protection, gender, and environmental issues mainstreamed. This intervention will be focused on 4 areas: South Idlib, Hama rural areas (Sub Districts: Eastern Bariy, As-Saan), Rural Damascus and Dar’a rural areas. The targeted areas were selected based on their accessibility, the severity of their needs varying between 3 and 5 as per the draft WaSH 2022 HNO, TGH field assessments during 2021 and consultations with Water authorities, SARC, local authorities and municipalities. 
The proposed intervention has been designed based on TGH 4-year experience in implementing WASH projects (with a specific emphasis on WASH-in-school interventions) in Syria. TGH follows a multi-sectorial programming approach that relies on complimentary multi-donor funding to ensure comprehensive coverage, addressing a broad range of critical humanitarian needs that exist in Syria, including WASH, Shelter and education 
In line with Objective 1, activities 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, TGH will propose intervention will include:   
•	In 2022, TGH will commence rehab 6 boreholes equipped with solar system, rehab 3 water networks, support Water trucking, support Water quality test for targeted water supply systems, distribution of 400 water tanks 1m3 at household’s level, and rehabilitation of 2 Sewage network.
•	In 2023, TGH will commence rehab 8 boreholes equipped with solar system, rehab 3 water networks, support Water quality test for targeted water supply systems, distribution of 500 water tanks 1m3 at household’s level, and rehabilitation of 2 Sewage network.

As part of Objective 2, activity 2.1, 2.2, and Objective 4, activity 4.1, and in line with Education Sector objectives, TGH will  propose intervention will include:   
• In 2022, TGH will commence rehab WASH facilities in 7 schools, and TGH will target 5 schools in 2023 with rehab WASH facilities in order to secure the access to water for drinking and hygiene purposes and ensure excreta evacuation to increase measures against infection, prevention and control both at school and at home in Idlib, Hama, Rural Damascus, and Dar’a . The intervention will be part of an integrated approach with Education HRP.
• In 2022 TGH will target 7 schools to distribute of hygiene kits and soap to students, and in 2023 TGH will target 5 school to distribute of hygiene kits and soap to students.
• Provision of emergency WASH services, including response to COVID19 according to need in 2022 and 2023.
The above the proposed activities will be implement during two years project (2022-2023), and TGH is estimating of 30 % of budget already secured for planned 2022 WASH Activities.
As part of its activities, TGH puts a specific emphasis on abiding by protection principles through providing gender and disabled friendly WASH facilities in schools taking into account menstrual needs, including doors lockable from the inside and lighting. TGH will also ensure to provide WASH facilities accessible for children with disabilities.

project_name: Respuesta multi-sectorial para mejorar el acceso a una educación de calidad y segura para NNA afectados por la situación humanitaria
project_objective: La intervención educativa forma parte de la respuesta integrada de NRC Venezuela. El equipo de Educación continuará trabajando en colaboración con los programas Información, Orientación y Asistencia legal (ICLA), Agua Higiene y Saneamiento (ASH) y Medios de vida y seguridad alimentaria (LFS) para permitir que las poblaciones afectadas por la situación humanitaria y desplazamientos satisfagan sus necesidades básicas, disfruten de sus derechos y se beneficien de los caminos hacia soluciones duraderas. La acción propuesta por el NRC tiene como objetivo garantizar la permanencia y los caminos de regreso al aprendizaje y la integración en la educación formal, particularmente luego del cierre de las escuelas por dos años durante la pandemia COVID-19 y su reciente reapertura. NRC responderá a los diversos problemas y necesidades que enfrentan los niños, niñas y adolescentes vulnerables en cuatro estados en Venezuela (Delta Amacuro, Bolívar, Táchira y Zulia) a través de una estrategia de respuesta basada en el Programa de Educación infantil (CEP), Programa Puente (PP) y Programa de Nivelación, así como una versión contextualizada del Better Learning Program (BLP) de NRC. Todos estos programas están adaptados al contexto venezolano.

project_name: Protección y asistencia humanitaria a personas en movilidad y en riesgo, así como comunidades de acogida vulnerables afectadas por el desplazamiento
project_objective: El objetivo principal de la intervención busca brindar protección legal a personas afectadas con necesidades específicas y vulnerables, la mitigación de riesgos asociados a la movilidad tanto interna como externa y el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de la población venezolana afectada, incluyendo a las comunidades de acogida. Dentro de los objetivos específicos se encuentran promover el empoderamiento de las personas en movilidad o en riesgos de movilidad, así como identificar, derivar y atender a personas con necesidades de alta vulnerabilidad y riesgos de protección.  Las actividades de información y orientación a personas en tránsito y desplazadas, retornados, comunidades de acogida y otras personas de interés se realizarán por medio de la atención personal y confidencial en los puntos de información como el centro comunitario y activación de equipos móviles en las comunidades meta de los estados prioritarios (Bolívar, Delta Amacuro, Táchira, Zulia). Las mesas de información y los equipos móviles brindarán información sobre derechos, riesgos, documentación civil y rutas para la migración segura, y asegurarán una atención inmediata y derivaciones pertinentes a las personas con necesidades específicas. La derivación de los casos se hará en base a las rutas de atención existentes, ya sea para la Red de Espacios Seguros para la atención de supervivientes de violencia sexual o de género y niñez en riesgo, como a miembros de las Redes de Protección. NRC también hará derivaciones a organizaciones prestadoras de servicios de respuesta multisectorial a sobrevivientes de VBG. Temáticas como el acceso a la documentación civil será parte de la asistencia humanitaria con enfoque de derechos a implementar. Además, se priorizarán los servicios de información, asesoría y asistencia legal que puedan necesitar la población retornada por causa de la pandemia COVID-19. De esta forma se asegura un mejor proceso de integración de poblaciones retornadas. Por último, ICLA pondrá en marcha su componente Digital ICLA como parte de sus modalidades de prestación de servicios, a fin de mejorar su capacidad para brindar soporte remoto y llegar a las personas en el área de difícil acceso (H2R). Nuestra población meta recibirá información sobre rutas migratorias seguras. NRC utilizará las alianzas y el apoyo brindado a otras ONG, agencias o autoridades que gestionan puntos de atención y explorarán colaboraciones para ampliar aún más el alcance de Digital ICLA. Se explorará el uso de chatbots u otras herramientas tecnológicas.

project_name: Reducing Protection Risks and Meeting Basic Needs for Conflict-Affected Communities in the South West Region in Cameroon
project_objective: The project aims at ensuring the that women, girls, boys and men are able to meet their basic needs; and are safe in their communities and receive support when they experience harm in the targeted locations in the South West region. The project will provide multipurpose cash assistance, water, sanitation and hygiene, gender-based violence (GBV) and protection programming to beneficiaries to help them meet their basic needs, be safer in their communities, and receive support when they experience harm.

project_name: Improved learning outcomes through ‘Connect my School’ initiative in Littoral and West.
project_objective:
This project aims at building an active social and learning environment that permits children and adolescent to enroll, learn and complete the school cycle in 4 schools in 2 subdivisions. The project also will enable teachers to conduct research and self-training as part of capacity building to improve their performance and enhance the quality of teaching.
UNICEF goal is to connect 02 subdivisions in the Zest and Littoral regions with Internet services precisely Menoua (West region) and Wouri (Littoral). 

Presently the Spanish Natcom for UNICEF is financing the connection for 8 schools in East Region with Internet services. A field visit was conducted to visualize how the children are using the tablets with both online and offline content. The children showed a mastery of the usage and this will go a long way to improve on learning and ICT capacity of the underprivileged children in these schools. The tablets with both online and offline content are improving the learning of children. This project will provide teachers and learners not only with learning ICT, but also learning through ICT, it will also aid actors of the educational supervision chain to ensure a better supervision by relying on tools existing through ICTs. This will contribute in improving the quality of education. It will then be a question of revitalizing the internal and external participatory management structures in the schools so that they can mobilize for children in general and most especially girls and other vulnerable children. Thus, it will consequently improve the school retention in the locality of the project.
ICT (Information and communication technology) tools will be installed, these tools will be used to provide children and teachers with learning platforms that gives opportunity not only to learn ICTs, but also to learn using ICTs and through ICTs as prescribed by the National policy of teaching ICTs in the primary cycle. 
The ICT equipment will also support the implementation of the pedagogical supervision model and monitor the attendance of pupils and teachers thereby making information available to the authorities quicker for a quick decision making. This sustainable and attractive method in making changes in the access and retention of pupil in school will be supported by the entire educational community. From this, the project will focus on activities to strengthen the technical and logistical capacities of the internal participatory Management structures (Parent Teachers Association, Association of Pupils’ mothers, School Councils, Management committees, Children's Government) and external (community-based organizations) at the school for the enrolment, monitoring attendance and retention of children in school, especially girls.
The project will consist of constructing e-containers in the 04 selected schools that will serve as multimedia center for the sites and the communities. These schools will be connected with internet using solar power and connectivity system to provide electricity. Materials such as desktops, tablets will be handed to the selected schools. The school administrators in collaboration with the community will make sure the materials are well kept and managed. The teachers will be trained on the use of ICT in schools, on the usage of the tools to improve learning. They will also be trained on how to manage these materials and on the sustainability side of the project. 
The project will be monitored by UNICEF in collaboration with the Government, computer start-ups and the community. 
At the end of the project, it is expected that in each school: students will demonstrate learning improvements, learning ICT based platforms will be ameliorated, teachers will use ICT to improve their teaching, school enrolment and retention for learners and teachers will be improving.

project_name: Psychosocial Support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse for children affected by the North-West and South-West crisis in Cameroon
project_objective:
Since the crisis escalation in late 2017, the North-West and South-West regions (NWSW)
have experienced a drastic deterioration of living conditions, putting children and women
at high risk of various forms of abuses, exploitation and violence.
Girls and boys are the primary victims of the current crisis. This translates into serious
violations of their fundamental rights and constant insecurity, causing both visible and
invisible trauma in the short and long-term, separation from their families and limited
access to basic social services such as education, for the past three years. Being direct or
indirect witnesses of violence linked to the conflict, their wellbeing, both physical and
psychological, is fundamentally at stake.
As of September 2020, the crisis in the NWSW has caused the displacement of an
estimated 200,000 children within those two regions, and an additional 155,794 children
are estimated to be displaced in West, Adamaoua, Littoral and Centre regions. Adolescent
boys and girls, children with specific needs and unaccompanied and separated children
(UASC) remain the primary categories at risk among all affected groups of IDPs, returnees
and affected host communities, especially in rural areas and hard-to-reach areas. Lack of
access to basic social services including child protection services remains a key risk
factor especially for children in rural areas, hard to reach areas and most remote localities
such as the ones along the Nigerian border where access and insecurity prevent protection
actors from implementing any program.
In order to protect children affected by armed conflict from violence, abuse and
exploitation, as a priority and main intervention, UNICEF will work on the offer of services
and provide psychosocial support to 340,000 children and caregivers. Psychosocial
support will be provided to caregivers as well when necessary and to the extent possible
so that they are better equipped to protect their children.
As a direct corollary, based on previous years trends, an estimated 10,200 unaccompanied

In urban and peri-urban areas, both in NWSW and outside where IDP children and families

UNICEF as lead of the Child Protection Area of Responsibility will continue to consolidate

of interventions in the field of child protection.

project_name: Responding to Top Need (WASH) expressed by population affected by the NWSW Crisis
project_objective:
Based on MSNA conducted by OCHA in August 2021, need relative to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene represent the top need expressed by affected population in assessed villages in North West, South West Littoral and West regions. This project aims to provide an assistance to affected population in the four concerned regions by increasing access to safe drinking water, basic sanitation and hygiene practice mainly among displaced population. The project aims to reach 250 000 people for one year. Main interventions will include construction/rehabilitation of water and sanitation infrastructures, distribution of hygiene items. 
The project will also include a component relative to support the WASH cluster coordination in North West and South West regions.

project_name: Enhance access to sure, protective  and quality primary education for girls and boys affected by the crisis in the North & South West Regions
project_objective:
•	This project aims to promote and improve psychosocial support & well-being for children affected by the conflict through appropriate education services. The component will integrate gender issues and sensitization to gender-based violence, through teacher training, promotion of equal and safe education for girls and boys from IDP and host communities. To achieve this, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the decentralized services of basic education in Cameroon, adopting a conflict-sensitive approach while ensuring respect for Do No Harm principles. The project results will be achieved through activity packages aimed at strengthening the capacity of education actors at the community level and ensuring the protection and development (cognitive, physical, emotional and psychological wellbeing) of children and adolescents, boys and girls. The activity packages include, learning and teaching kits distribution, teacher training on psycho-social support and NRC better learning program, revamping school governance structures, set of recreational, breathing, relaxing and calming exercice activities with children and care givers. Additionally, awareness and sensitization activities will be carry on within targeted communities for protection of education from attacks and safe school declaration per on the South West and North West security context. NRC will also help to meet school infrastructure needs by supporting MoE in construction of clasrooms and rehabilitation of existing structures, ensuring meaningful access and equal participation of people with disabilities and special needs. Theses classrooms will be equipped with classroom furniture (including desks with modesty screens) and blackboards to enable their use. To make these schools safer, sensitive to specific needs and inclusive, there will be a particular focus on wash facilities in school (gender sensitive latrines, access to water…), ensuring access for people with disabilities;

However, At the beginning of the project  a baseline will be set up to have measurable and qualitative data to be analyze at the end of the action. This aim to have a better understanding of the impact of the project within the targeted community.   In addition, NRC M&E  staff  will carry on outcome and output monitoring  field activities according to the project period. They will also set up feedback and complain mechanism in targeted communities to ensure our accountability to donors and beneficiaries as  well and to ensure the  compliance  of our action with NRC program and operation policies.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire d'urgence aux personnes déplacées internes affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la Région du Sahel au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise sécuritaire vient s’ajouter à une crise alimentaire chronique au Burkina Faso. Plus de la moitié de la population IDP est en insécurité alimentaire sévère (61%) et seulement 22% des ménages déplacés ont un score de consommation alimentaire acceptable ; le nombre moyen de jours que peuvent couvrir le peu de ressources en nourritures disponibles au niveau des ménages est de 2 jours. 
Les listes des bénéficiaires seront analysées par l’équipe de WW-GVC qui conduira une évaluation du dégrée de vulnérabilité sur la base des indicateurs de sécurité alimentaire et des indicateurs socio-économiques qui permettront l’identification d’une situation de référence avant-projet (baseline). Les bénéficiaires seront ciblés sur la base des critères suivantes (en ordre de priorité) : femmes cheffes de ménage, présence d’enfants de moins de 5 ans, chef de ménage avec handicap, présence de membre(s) du ménage avec handicap, abris (hébergés ou non dans un famille d’accueil). Puis, si une identification plus fine sera nécessaire, on pourra considérer les principaux indicateurs de sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, tels que le Score de Consommation Alimentaire (Food Consumption Score), le Score de Diversité Alimentaire (Household Dietary Diversity Score), le CSI (Coping Strategy Index), l’Echelle de la Faim (Food Hunger Scale). L’activité de distribution sera basée sur la modalité CBT (Cash Based Transfer) à travers des transferts monétaires sous forme de coupon cash inconditionnels et sans restrictions qui seront données aux personnes bénéficiaires de l’action et qui seront échangeable avec des commerçant partenaires contractés par WW-GVC au début du projet et qui, à leur tour, seront remboursés par WW-GVC à travers de transfert monétaires selon le meilleur système de remboursement qui pourra être mis en place. Pour cette action, les bénéficiaires recevront 6.000 FCFA / personne / mois pour chaque distribution et l’intervention tiendra compte de la taille réelle du ménages en divisant en sous-ménages les ménages avec plus de 10 membres. Le plafond fixé pour chaque sous-ménage sera donc basé sur la taille maximale de 10 membres par sous-ménage, qui corresponde à un montant total de 60.000 FCFA / ménage / mois. Un Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) sera planifié à la fin de chaque distribution et la dernière enquête identifiera l’endline du projet. En plus, pour garantir la redevabilité de l’action, un numéro vert sera mis à disposition des bénéficiaires auquel leurs plaintes pourront être adressées. Les plaintes et feedback des bénéficiaires peuvent concerner : la nature du transfert, la quantité ou qualité de la donation, l’organisation d’une opération de soutien aux populations, l’attitude de l’ONG, la période ou le lieu d’une opération de soutien aux populations, les acteurs impliqués, les types de bénéficiaires retenus. Toutes les plaintes ou satisfaction dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet seront traitées avec tout l’anonymat.
Les besoins spécifiques liés au genre, des personnes âgées et des personnes vivant avec un handicap sont pris en compte dans la mise en œuvre des activités comme catégories priorisées et dans la réponse par des mécanismes de distribution et appui adaptés. En plus, l’implication des différents acteurs pour le développement des activités proposés, la collaboration étroite avec les autorités locales. Au niveau de durabilité, l’impact des activités de prévention de la malnutrition et d’amélioration de l’état nutritionnel des ménages PDI concernera le renforcement de la couverture des interventions ANJE dans les communautés concernées tout en renforçant le marché local à travers l’implication systématique des commerçant de la zone.

project_name: Detección de asentamientos de población desplazada interna en la Costa Pacífica Colombiana
project_objective:
La recolección de información relacionada con población desplazada interna enfrenta diversos retos. En muchos casos, no se dispone de recursos suficientes para elaborar un mapeo comprensivo de donde se encuentran estas personas y cuáles son sus necesidades. De igual forma, el acceso a la ubicación de estas comunidades puede verse restringido por la nula o deficiente infraestructura en estas zonas, condiciones de seguridad, condiciones de salud pública, entre otras (Baal & Ronkainen, 2017). 
Estas dificultades han motivado a acudir a fuentes alternativas de información respaldadas por nuevas tecnologías, como el análisis de métricas de redes sociales e imágenes aéreas o satelitales, para citar algunos ejemplos. De igual forma, estas situaciones han puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de incluir a la participación activa de la población en los procesos de manejo de información, de tal forma que no sólo se utilice esta información para planificar la respuesta a sus necesidades, sino que también pueda serles de utilidad para futuros procesos de formalización de la propiedad o restablecimiento de derechos. 
El desarrollo de este proyecto estará guiado en todo momento por los cuatro principios para la protección de población beneficiada o potencialmente beneficiaria de asistencia humanitaria (Global Protection Cluster, n.d.):
Priorización de la seguridad y la dignidad de las personas (acción sin daño).
Promoción del acceso de las personas a asistencia y servicios.
Rendición de cuentas a población afectada.
Empoderamiento de las comunidades y desarrollo de capacidades de autoprotección.
Este proyecto busca Identificar y caracterizar las necesidades de asentamientos de población desplazada interna colombiana ubicados en la Costa Pacífica haciendo uso de inteligencia artificial y nuevas tecnologías, con el fin de proveer insumos a los actores humanitarios que permitan enfocar y priorizar la respuesta, así como proveer a estas comunidades de información que pueda ser de utilidad para sus procesos de restablecimiento de derechos y formalización de la propiedad.

project_name: Livelihoods, Resilience and Social Protection in Syria, 2022 - 2023
project_objective:
A decade-long crisis in Syria has reversed human development, impoverished the lives and livelihoods of Syrian families, and eroded the resilience of vulnerable communities. Syria has also been experiencing an unprecedented economic downturn since 2019, with soaring inflation and a collapse in the value of the Syrian pound (SYP). 

The Syrian crisis is estimated to have resulted in physical capital destruction, including productive assets, and communal infrastructure. The result has been a near-total collapse of food systems in many rural and urban areas, leading to food insecurity and food assistance dependency. The HNO estimates that more than 13 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.

In response and to reduce the high levels of dependency from food assistance, WFP implements a range of projects designed to create livelihoods, and reconstitute the resilience of households, communities, and food systems. These efforts contribute to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2 (Zero Hunger), in addition to having significant positive multiplier effects towards SDGs 1 (no poverty), 4 (quality education), and 5 (gender equality). 

In line with the HRP Strategic Outcomes 1, 2 and 3 and in coordination with the FSA and ERL sectors, WFP identifies the need of enhancing resilience and early recovery to play a significant role in addressing the protracted crisis and food insecurity situation in Syria. In 2022-23 WFP will be scaling up the activities in SO 02 and 03 of the HRP. In fact, resilience-building is a crucial aspect to help vulnerable smallholder farmers and livestock keepers more self-reliant through the improvement of livelihoods assets, rehabilitation of irrigation systems and other community assets, restoration and enhancement of the national bread value chain.

The WFP Livelihoods Strategy focuses on early recovery interventions as necessary tools to relieve the pressure from emergency food interventions and prevent households and communities currently at risk to fall further into food insecurity. The WFP Strategy has 4 pillars: 1: Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) through, a) Provision of household and group-based productive assets; and b) Rehabilitation of agrarian community assets. 2: Food Assistance for Training (FFT) through human capital development. 3: Market Access Support via Retail Sector Rehabilitation, with a specific focus on the wheat-to-bread value chain. 4: Social Transfer/Basic Income via Financial Inclusion.

WFP plan is to support 530,000 beneficiaries (106,000 households) in 2022, with livelihoods and resilience activities. 80% of the beneficiaries are expected to be the users of the rehabilitated assets, while the remaining caseload will be assisted with households’ level complementary activities, including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA), Food Assistance for Training (FFT), both done through food vouchers and vouchers, as well as other livelihoods and income-generating activities. In 2023, WFP plan to continue expanding the caseload reaching 700,000 people, or 140,000 households.  

The long-term overarching goal is to enhance the food security of Syrian communities and enable planning a progressive reduction of food assistance needs in the country. In the rollout of this approach, WFP will closely coordinate with other UN organizations such as FAO and UNDP, as well as with the FAS and ERL sectors. In particular, despite directly reporting to FAS, WFP will foster complementarities with ERL.

WFP plans its activities using the Three-Pronged Approach (3PA) to define appropriate interventions, accurate targeting, and geographical coherence; the tools are the Integrated Context Analysis (ICA), Seasonal Livelihoods Planning (SLP), and; the Community Based Participatory Programming (CBPP). The tools are also important to minimize exclusion errors and to reduce the risk of exacerbating existing conflicts, by ensuring extensive dialogue with communities and other stakeholders.

project_name: Emergency WASH intervention for IDPs, Returnees and host communities living in conflict and drought affected areas of Ethiopia
project_objective: As September 2021, the Ethiopia National Displacement Report 10, highlighted an increase to 4,239,636 displaced individuals nationwide due to several factors, such as conflict (85%), drought (7%) and seasonal displacement (3%). In 2021, the triggers of humanitarian needs in Ethiopia were armed conflict, inter-communal tensions, climatic shocks, desert locusts and disease outbreaks. In 2022, the humanitarian situation for Ethiopia is still characterized by severe shocks, including the conflict in North of the country, drought conditions and persisting inflation (34.5% in January 2022). The project will target both conflict affected population and those climate shocks to reduce the risk of morbidity and mortality through the provision of integrated WASH services. The project will support the response to the gaps identified in: Afar, region is highly prone to climate shocks and human made disasters: desert locust infestation, floods and droughts have severely impacted the food and nutrition security. Ethnic tensions between Afari/Somali and Afar/Oromo have caused violence and displacement. Since the spillover of the conflict in Tigray in Afar, more than 336,000 IDPs in 11 sites in the region require water trucking every day to fill the minimum standard of 10l/p/day (OCHA). 29 woredas of the region face serious water shortage due to damages, electricity down, unavailability of fuel and non-functionality of water supply and 164 water supply schemes are out of service in the region. Low coverage of sanitation and bathing facilities in IDPs sites represent a huge risk for disease outbreak. COOPI will target the Zones 1, 2, 3 and 4. Amhara: from August 2021 the spillover of the Tigray conflict in the region resulted in a huge displacement of population including North Shewa and Oromia Special Zone, already affected by ethnic conflict. COOPI, based in Ataye Town, conducted an assessment in North Shewa and Oromia Special Zone (February 2022): as result of the conflict, a huge number of water supply systems are damaged, Water Offices looted, health facilities destroyed, sanitation facilities of education facilities used as shelter in need desluging, among others. Further displacement is reported also in Awi Zone, where COOPI is present in Chagni, as result of ethnic tensions. iii. Oromia Region: COOPI will focus on both conflict and drought affected areas in Guji, East Bale and East Hararghe Zones. Both East Hararghe, where COOPI is present in Chinaksen, and Guji where COOPI works since 1995, are affected by clan clashes and the presence of UAG. Tensions between UAG and ENDF have resulted in 190.000 IDPs in Guji. Due to the extremely low precipitations in October to December 2021 (deyr) in southern and southeastern pastoral areas combined with two consecutive failures in the rain season in late 2020 and early 2021. The drought has deepened humanitarian needs both in Guji, East Bale, Bale and Somali Region. Specifically in Somali, currently, 3.4 million people are facing water shortage and need urgent water intervention with around 1848 sites (84 Woredas). In accordance with the WASH cluster's objectives the proposal will contribute to: a) deliver conflict-sensitive essential life-saving WASH services to affected people and b) enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Ethiopia through early recovery and resilience interventions. The project will provide maintenance and repairs of 39 water schemes (10 in Afar, 8 in Ahmara, 4 in Benishangul, 12 in Oromia, 5 in Somali); deliver water trucking in Somali, improve access to sanitation and hygiene with construction of latrines and delivery of WASH NFIs kits, improve capacity of WASHco and restore the functionality of WASH services in HCFs. The project will mainstream protection and gender&age approach as well as PSEA. The project targets in total 453920 individuals (22% male; 23% female; 26%boys; 25% girls; 2% elderly men; 2% elderly female).
