Improving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Services for the Most Vulnerable Populations in Ukhia and Teknaf Upazilas of Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh
project_objective:
This project is designed to ensure access to WASH services for all women, men, girls, boys with special consideration for Persons with Disabilities (PwD) in the Rohingya refugee camps and targeted host communities. The project will intervene in the three following subsectors:   

Improved Water Services: two small-scale solar-powered piped water networks will be installed to provide safe water in the newly developed areas for the relocated. IOM will continue the operations, maintenance and upgrade of the existing deep tube wells in the camps within IOM’s area of responsibility (AoR) and of water networks in Camps 12, 13, 18, 19, 24, and 20 Extension. 
In the newly developed areas, deep tube wells will be installed in camps and host communities to  ensure that the most vulnerable people in need have  improved and sustained access. IOM will design and upgrade  surface water treatment and supply system in Camps 24 and 25 to cover the additional refugee and host community caseload. IOM will procure, replenish and replace the emergency stocks for cyclones, fires, floods, or other potential emergencies. IOM will also conduct a study to map the host community boreholes in Ukhiya and Balukhali areas exposed to groundwater levels reduction. IOM will also support the WASH sector in assessing the existing water network systems in camps to update the water strategy.

Access to Sanitation: To ensure dignified and safe access to latrine facilities, IOM will continue to upgrade the existing latrine facilities with gender-inclusive and disability-friendly features in consultation with the community (users) while considering the field needs. IOM will also construct gender-segregated WASH blocks (septic tank or pit type) in the newly developed valleys to avoid frequent desludging and risk of groundwater contamination in order to meet the sanitation needs of the relocated people. IOM will provide assistive devices (commode chair, commode chair with potty, urinal bottles for males and females) to persons with disabilities to ensure their unique sanitation requirements are met. IOM will continue the durable household latrine construction work to cover sanitation gaps at targeted host community villages in Ukhiya. Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Systems (DEWATS) will be built and the upgrade of lime-based fecal sludge treatment plants to DEWATS conducted to meet the coverage gaps. IOM will continue regular desludging and disinfection activities to ensure  safe use of sanitation facilities. In order to ensure complete chain of Solid Waste Management (SWM), IOM will build Material Recovery Facilities-MRFs (small scale composting and segregation units) and secondary drain waste segregation sites at each camp based on the identified gaps and geographical coverage. The complete chain of SWM monitoring system will be continued and strengthened at all levels.

Hygiene Promotion and Community Engagement: IOM will provide critical supplies of hygiene items (soap, water containers, Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) materials) and ensure the related community education and mobilization activities targeting all age groups, genders, and persons with special WASH needs. IOM will scale up the SCOPE distribution system in all camps within the IOM AoR to better support the people in need with hygiene kits . IOM will also pilot the production of reusable sanitary pads in Camp 9 to ensure appropriate distribution according to the needs of female beneficiaries of reproductive age. The community will be furthermore engaged in operations and maintenance of WASH facilities, waste segregation, and prevention of COVID-19 disease transmission. IOM will continue the implementation of a real-time service monitoring and community feedback mechanisms, which shall be strengthened and systematized to enhance accountability to the affected population (AAP).

project_name: Soutien Psychosocial au déplacés et autochtones dans les régions du Sahel, l’Est et du Nord.
project_objective:
Action contre la Faim prévoit de reconduire son intervention en santé mentale et soutien psychosocial pour les populations affectées (DPI & population hôtes) par la détresse psychologique dû à la crise humanitaire dans les régions de Sahel, de l'Est et de Centre-Est. 
Prise en charge trauma : l’assistance sera focalisée sur les troubles de stress post-traumatiques,     de la dépression et les troubles      anxieux aussi bien pour les enfants que les adultes (les protocoles sont spécifiques selon la cible soit les enfants ou les adultes). Il s’agira notamment d’animer des séances de psychoéducation pour la normalisation des symptômes de stress post traumatique et identifier des personnes en détresse pour leur admission au programme de prise en charge. Ces services seront offerts dans la communauté pour faciliter l’accès aux services et mieux garantir la confidentialité des bénéficiaires. L’intervention sera basée sur le protocoles trauma de ACF et celui de traitement d’épisode traumatique (G-TEP). L’équipe des psychologues et des travailleurs psychosociaux suivront la structuration des protocoles de ACF pour accompagner les bénéficiaires lors des séances thérapeutiques. Des échelles d’évaluation psychométriques permettront le suivi de l’amélioration du      bien-être      des bénéficiaires.  

Sensibilisation communautaire : les sessions de sensibilisations seront animées au sein      de la communauté sur la thématique de la santé mentale pour promouvoir la compréhension sur ce que c’est que le service de la santé mentale et soutien psychosocial et comment avoir accès à ce service. Cette intervention vise à édifier la communauté sur les besoins en santé mentale et atténuer la stigmatisation dont sont victimes les personnes en détresse psychologique.

Psychoéducation : le service de psychoéducation sera offert au niveau communautaire et ouvert à toute la communauté pour partager les symptômes de la détresse psychologique qui se développent suite à un choc émotionnel. En plus de la normalisation de ces symptômes chez les hommes, femmes et enfants, c’est aussi un cadre d’identification des personnes en besoin de soutien psychologique et ou psychosocial spécifique.  

Formation soutien psychosocial : les personnes clés de la communauté seront formés      en compétences de Premiers Secours Psychologiques. Pour renforcer durablement les savoir-être et savoir-faire afin de pouvoir apporter un premier support aux personnes vulnérables, identifier les personnes qui nécessitent une prise en charge spécifique et les référer vers les services de soins adéquats. 
ACF a participé à l’élaboration du manuel de l’OMS « Les Premiers Secours Psychologiques : guide pour les acteurs de terrain » qui est donc le document de référence pour la réalisation de cette activité.

project_name: Improving the livelihoods of affected, vulnerable people in NES through integrated livelihoods and agriculture support
project_objective:
The IRC will support vulnerable host communities improve their livelihoods status through integrated livelihoods support. The project will address the needs of the affected community by providing access to income generating opportunities in Hassakah, Der ez-Zor, Raqqa governorate. 1,270 livelihood households are protected and/or restored income generating through appropriate market skills/inputs/services including vocational training, apprenticeship, SME grants, and business start-up kits, as well 1,020 households with appropriate agriculture inputs (seeds, fertilizer, tractor ploughing hours) and farming tools needed to increase production both for domestic consumption and for commercial to increase household income.
The IRC will conduct a market assessment and engage with farmers to understand inputs needed, availability and market prices to best design appropriate input distribution modalities. In addition, livestock breeders will receive cash assistance for fodder to protect productive assets and improve food consumption at household and community levels. 
In addition, 430 households will be engaged in gainful temporary employment through cash for work involving rehabilitation of prioritized community infrastructure. Cash for work activities are intended to provide households with much needed cash injections to meet their basic needs while rehabilitating community assets and infrastructure that are vital to sustaining and restoring the livelihoods of communities.
The IRC will support the agriculture community through skill-building via improving agriculture and veterinary service activities which play a crucial role in boosting agricultural productivity, increasing food security, improving rural livelihoods, and ensuring that 8,000 farmers and livestock breeders have access to improved technologies. Activities will include assistance in the creation of production groups and deliver information on new technologies and innovations available to agriculture manufacturers. Agriculture extension and veterinary services programs will cover a broad area including improved crop varieties, livestock management, improved water management, modern irrigation methods, and control of weeds, pests, and diseases through  mobile veterinary team, training, visuals posters, and brochures, electronic media (WhatsApp app groups), learning by experimentation, field trips and exchanges, and FFS. 
The IRC will mainstream gender equity and promote gender inclusion, allowing the most vulnerable and disadvantaged women, girls, boys, and men to have equal participation in the program and to realize benefits for their own wellbeing. A participatory beneficiary identification and selection including agreeing on affirmative action to register at least 50% female beneficiaries. 
To facilitate women’s accessibility, and promote their participation in livelihoods activities, the IRC provides safe places at livelihoods centers managed by childminders, for children whose mothers attend the livelihoods activities.

project_name: Providing Lifesaving NFIs and Shelter Support in North of Syria
project_objective:
The program provides life-sustaining shelter and NFI support and contributes towards the resilience and cohesion of communities and households by improving housing and related community/public infrastructure. Targeting both IDPs (70%) and host communities (30%) involves activities; 3,000 standard NFI kits distribution (3,000 HHs) and winterization components such as distributing (500,000 L) heating fuel to 1,667 HHs, and (2,000) stoves to 2,000 HHs and (25,000) winter clothes kits for 25,000 children both gender. As well as providing restricted cash for house rent services (1,000 units) for those IDP vulnerable groups and prioritizing female or child-headed households and elderly people and considering people with disabilities (1,000 HHs; 5,000 individuals).
This program includes 2,500 house rehabilitation activities which will target both IDPs and host communities (2,500 HHs; 12,500 individuals), this activity includes rehabilitating partially damaged units through ceiling repair, walls buildings and holes ﬁxing, doors and windows, infrastructure, electricity network, and solar panels, plastering, plumping and providing the water tank. This component will be guided by the shelter rehabilitation guidance published by the SNFI cluster in 2018 and ensuring that HLP documentations are well carried out in parallel with ﬁeld coordination with the relevant local councils

The program will seek feedback from both male and female beneﬁciaries and fully interact with both genders to ensure equitable access and equal opportunities.

project_objective:
WVSR with its partners will be operating in Idlib (Harim district), Aleppo (Afrin and Azaz districts), Raqqa (Tel Abyad)  and Al Hasakeh (Ras al Ain) 18 locations, supporting 10 PHC and 5 Hospitals.  The current 3 MMU will be transitioned to 2 static clinics and a mobile emergency team.  This will include support with salaries, operating costs (electricity, fuel for generators, water supply, equipment, medical supplies – pharmaceuticals and consumables) and transport.  

WVSR’s health program will align programs to implement the EHSP with partners for primary health services, ensuring local communities receive the best possible care.  This is contingent on adequate funding, staff capacity, supply chain and pipeline continuity, and security that does not result in damage or closure of services.  WVSR and partners will be supported to adapt to changing circumstances to continue to offer services.   WVSR will work with hold regular meetings with donors, local governorate health authorities, partners (on a monthly basis or as needed) and other actors to meet these basic needs in conjunction with the health cluster, of which they will actively participate.  

Essential lifesaving primary health care according to the cluster guidelines, this will include child health, reproductive health SGBV prevention and response.  Treatment of communicable and non-communicable disease including basic mental health services.  All health programming will take into consideration COVID-19 prevention and IPC measures in all health facilities.  WV with partners will support 10 PHC, and 5 hospitals and 3 MMU and 1 Rapid response team with free medical treatment.  Where the health facility is unable to meet the needs of the patient, referrals will be provided with follow up, and in Atmeh  will support an ambulance service for patient transfer and referrals during medical emergencies  All health programs will focus on contributing to responding to the COVID-19 pandemic with provision of PPE, infection prevention and control (IPC) protocols in health facilities and with staff including provision of oxygen concentrators at the PHC.  

Capacity building of health staff and community health workers linked to health facilities' on topics such as prevention and management of communicable disease (CD), non-communicable (NCD) diseases, IPC, reproductive health (RH) including family planning, SGBV, STI management, and Integrated management of childhood illnesses (IMCI), based on capacity needs 

Community health outreach with trained CHW, social workers and SGBV specialists to support home- based care, outbreak prevention, immunization awareness, PSS,  SRHR and SGBV awareness and response. COVID-19 prevention, homebased care and vaccine awareness.  

Extended Program of Immunization (EPI), centers supported with a mobile outreach team to cover remote areas and communities that are unable to attend the EPI centers. These centers will be in civil buildings for ease of access for children and their caregivers.  Each EPI center will have 3 vaccinators and 2 social mobilizers.  Social mobilizers will also be engaged in vaccination campaigns on the importance of vaccination and follow up for children that have not returned for subsequent doses 

Support to EWARNS-Covid-19, covering salaries, transport and operations in the 4 labs that can manage PCR tests within NWS and NCS for all COVID-19 related surveillance and response. This project will have the support of WHO for technical guidance and, a reference lab in Turkey to ensure accuracy of testing protocols.    

Monthly reporting from health facilities on patient services, staffing, medication consumption etc. in conjunction with the technical,  MEAL and accountability teams, assessing outputs, reach and acceptability, with third party monitoring on a 6-monthly basis.  It includes feedback from questionnaires and FII from staff, patients and community/health leaders.

project_name: Assistance nutritionnelle aux principaux groupes les plus vulnérables des régions les plus impactées par l'insécurité
project_objective:
Malgré les efforts notables réalisés au Burkina Faso dans le domaine de la nutrition, la malnutrition demeure un problème majeur de santé publique. Le pays connait une situation sécuritaire qui continue de se détériorer de façon significative sur l'ensemble du territoire avec pour corollaire un déplacement massif continue de populations et un accès réduit aux offres de services de santé. L’espace humanitaire s’en trouve de plus en plus réduit.  Cette situation est combinée à des sécheresses récurrentes qui contribuent à la détérioration progressive des moyens de subsistance rendant ainsi les populations vulnérables. Les résultats du Cadre Harmonisé d’octobre 2022 soulignent une détérioration significative de la situation de la sécurité alimentaire à travers le pays. Pour la période d’octobre à décembre 2022, on estime que plus de 2,6 millions de personnes sont en insécurité alimentaire (phase 3-5 du Cadre intégré de classification de la sécurité alimentaire - IPC) pour atteindre 3,5 millions de personnes dont 572 382 enfants de moins de 5 ans et 566 321 personnes en phases 4 et 5
. Les résultats provisoires de l'enquête SMART National 2022, le nombre de cas de malnutritions estimés pour 2023 dans les six régions humanitaires est de 626 492 enfants malnutris dont 458 174 enfants malnutris modérés, et 168 318 enfants malnutris sévères. 
Au regard de ce contexte, et de la couverture de la prise en charge globale de la malnutrition aigüe toujours insuffisante, le PAM fournira une assistance nutritionnelle d'urgence, avec une approche multisectorielle ( nutrition-sécurité alimentaire, nutrition- santé, genre, protection), sous forme d'un package d'interventions complémentaires et synergiques comprenant l'extension des activités de prévention de la malnutrition , le traitement de la malnutrition aiguë modérée y compris au niveau communautaire qui sera renforcé dans les zones à accès difficile compte tenu de son plan de scale-up interne qui  engendrera une capacité de livraison aérienne, le renforcement de capacité des agents de santé communautaires y compris dans le traitement au niveau communautaire et la Communication pour le Changement Social et Comportemental (CCSC) .
Le PAM fournira un appui nutritionnel préventif sous forme de « rations de protection » nutritives et enrichies à 136 500 enfants âgés de 6 à 23 mois non-malnutris (IDPs et Pop Hôtes). L’appui 
 à 50 000 femmes enceintes et allaitantes non malnutries rentrera dans le cadre d’un projet de sécurité alimentaire . Cela permettra de réduire les risques de malnutrition aggravation de la situation nutritionnelle. Cette intervention spécifique, tout en permettant de réaliser des dépistages actifs de la malnutrition aigüe puis en orientant précocement les sujets diagnostiqués malnutris vers les structures de prises en charge , est une opportunité de renforcement des connaissances des participants sur les bonnes pratiques alimentaire, d'hygiène, assainissement en vue de leur adoption .
Durant 12 mois, le PAM appuiera également la prise en charge curative « intégrée » au niveau des structures de soins mais aussi au niveau communautaire des enfants de 6-59 mois et des femmes enceintes ou allaitantes présentant une malnutrition aigüe modérée. Les structures de prise en charge étatiques seront approvisionnées en intrants nutritionnels adaptés, pour assister 137 252 enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois et  36 231  FEFA pendant trois mois. Pour contribuer et renforcer la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigüe sévère dans les centres de récupération et d'éducation nutrition, le PAM prévoit apporter une assistance alimentaire à 8 000 mères d'enfants MAS hospitalisés.
Le présent projet qui adressera les besoins des populations déplacées, hôtes et vulnérables, vise à contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité infantile et maternelle, à travers une amélioration de la couverture de prise en charge de la malnutrition, à la promotion cohabitation pacifique entre ces population

project_name: Contribuer a la réduction de l'incidence de la malnutrition aiguë et les risques de mortalité associés à la malnutrition aiguë dans les zones confrontées à des situations d'urgence tout en renforçant les système de santé et en développant la résilience au Sahel
project_objective:
L’UNICEF apportera son soutien aux partenaires nationaux, provinciaux et des districts sanitaires afin d'assurer un traitement de qualité pour les enfants souffrant de MAS tant dans les unités ambulatoires (UNA) que dans les unités d'hospitalisation (UNT) tout en améliorant la couverture dans les zones à faible couverture de PCIMAS, en renforçant le système de gestion des intrants nutritionnels à tous les niveaux pour éviter les ruptures de stock ou la mauvaise gestion des RUTF ainsi que celui de la surveillance nutritionnelle et la coordination pour la préparation et la réponse aux urgences dans les provinces prioritaires.  
Pour fournir l’accès et améliorer la couverture de la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë, cette action permettra d’ouvrir quelques unités nutritionnelle dans les zones à faible couverture de PCI MAS, d'encadrer 1,233 agents de santé communautaires, ainsi que les mères et les soignants, pour la détection précoce de la malnutrition aiguë, et 2,936 agents de santé sur le protocole PCIMAS ajusté et les pratiques d'alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant (ANJE) y compris la gestion des stocks d’intrants nutritionnels et la protection transversale et PSEA. Une campagne de masse permettra de dépister au moins 1,417,420 enfants, et 337,981 enfants de moins de cinq ans souffrant de MAS seront ciblés pour bénéficier du traitement.

project_name: Delivering critical life-saving GBV prevention and response Services for Crisis -affected women and girls in South Sudan.
project_objective:
According to the 2022 HNO, more than two-thirds of South Sudan's population, 8.9 million people, are in need of humanitarian assistance, an increase of 600,000 since 2021. An estimated 2.6 million people risk facing gender-based  violence in 2022, which represents a 25 per cent increase compared to 2021 estimates.  

UNFPA aims to reach 156,342 Beneficiaries  ( women 96,106, Men 7817,  Boys 15,634, Girls 34,395, PWD 2.390) with GBV services and information particularly through  implementing community engagement  and awareness-raising activities focusing on risk factors to GBV, available GBV response services, and timely seeking of GBV response services immediately after the GBV incident ( with in 72 hours). UNFPA  will also support primary GBV prevention programs such as EMAP and SASA. The GBV risk mitigation measures include advocating and supporting integration of GBV and survivor support across different clusters, dignity kit programming, conducting safety audits and providing livelihood and economic support.
The GBV  response interventions include providing psychosocial support, GBV case management services, in UNFPA established One-Stop Centers (OSC), other  GBV service provision centres and Health facilities in the project areas.

As the Core Pipe Line Manager for Dignity Kits, UNFPA will procure and distribute Dignity Kits (DK) to women and girls of reproductive age to enhance their Dignity and hygiene as well as use DK programming as an entry point to provide women and girls with information on GBV prevention, and GBV service availability including information and services on Sexual Reproductive Health.

The livelihood and economic support in the  Women and Girls Friendly Space will also act as  an entry point for women and girls to receive more psychosocial support and other empowerment activities. Cram activities, such as knitting, beadwork, crocheting and embroidering bed sheets, and tea discussions, will be introduced as the women often enjoy these activities,  so they are a good way to bring them together encourage conversation and relationship- building with each other. On the other hand, some of these activities will be introduced as income-generating activities to allow women and girls to earn some income to meet their basic needs and referrals for livelihood support with other programmes supporting women and girls.

It is important to note that as a result of the degradation of community protection systems and the inadequate GBV lifesaving services, women and girls have increased exposure to various forms of violence, including rape, sexual assault, psychological abuse, physical violence, child and forced marriage, denial of opportunities, resources and services where some basic services exist. Also, livelihood options are increasingly limited due to the ongoing conflict, exacerbated with COVID 19, disproportionately affecting adolescent girls and young women, resorting to harmful coping mechanisms that include child marriage, survival sex and sexual exploitation and abuse.
Survivors urgently need to access specialized services, including case management and psychosocial support services. A clear referral pathway needs to be established to facilitate the survivors' access to critical life-saving services.

project_name: Health Emergency assistance to IDP and Returnees in Jur River and Wau counties, Western Bahr El Ghazal- South Sudan
project_objective:
Johanniter is proposing an intervention focused on access to primary health care through curative, preventive, & promotional health care in general & maternal & child health in particular.
It will specifically support the following:  
-Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) provision at four health facilities
- Functionality of the four health facilities with the provision of medical & non-medical supplies, (equipment, drugs) & capacity building of the MoH staff on BEmONC (Basic Emergency Obstetric Neonatal care), CMR (Clinical management of rape) & referral pathway, IPC (Infection-Prevention & control), EPI (expended program of Immunization)-cold chain & management of the program, IDSR (Integrated diseases surveillance & response). 
-Provision of free primary health care for all IDPs/returnees & Host communities (specifically to those under five years, Pregnant & lactating women).
- Treatment of medical complications associated with the severe acute malnutrition specifically for those under five years at the Naivasha PoC/Inpatient therapeutic feeding program (& prevention through awareness focusing on Family MUAC screening, nutritious food-Balance diet, exclusive breastfeeding, etc in all the health-supported facilities).
-Health promotion of the EPI activities, & diseases surveillance for the potential outbreaks
- Awareness raising on prevention of GBV (Gender Based violence) & provision 1st aid psychosocial support
-Provision of incentives to the seconded staff from the SMoH & volunteers while ensuring easy access to primary health care & secondary via referral health services
The project targets 56,596 people in areas serviced by 4 health facilities including camps in Wau North and South; Kangi & Kuarjena PHC in Jur River  Counties. 
The action will target children under five years of age, pregnant & lactating women, vulnerable groups such as people living with disabilities, survivors of GBV, & minority groups such as orphans, widows & young mothers. This project will compliment other projects currently being implemented in the same region by Johanniter & other actors.
- Johanniter International Assistance with funding from other sources is currently implementing activities in FSL, WASH, protection, Community Case Management, Nutrition sectors in Jur River & Wau counties. 
Johanniter will collaborate & coordinate with other actors in the health sector such as: 
- IOM in Primary health care support to some health facilities in PoCs.
- Islamic Relief in Primary health care service in Bagari PHCC, Kpaile/Bazia & Beseliya PHCCs.
The project will be implemented in partnership with the State Ministry of Health, the county health department, the Health Centers (CS), & local health committees. 
The expected results in the intermediate & long term will be:
-The health facilities are equipped & functioning with reliable supplies of essential medicines & consumables during the project implementation period. 
-MoH staff with capacity to ensure the provision of the quality health care services.
- Enhanced referral service for the under 5 years & PLW
- Increased early access to health service of the GBV survivors through increased awareness on GBV prevention & referral pathways.
- Earlier detection & response to outbreaks
The proposed action is in line with the guidelines & objectives of the South Sudan Health Cluster on life-saving interventions in areas where emergency thresholds are alarming, so as to reduce morbidity & excess mortality of people affected by the crisis. As well as cover, immediate needs whilst simultaneously embed durable solutions in the design of humanitarian interventions by addressing people's vulnerabilities & building their resilience. 
The response will be conflict-sensitive, & it will consider community feedback & the different protection needs of women, men, girls, & boys & disable people affected by the crisis.

project_name: Enhancing Coordination of Humanitarian International NGOs (CHINGO)
project_objective:
The INGOs forum in Cameroon (CHINGO) was established in June 2019 with the objective to enhance collaboration and coordination between between INGOs and external stakeholders (line ministries, UN agencies, donors, civil society organizations) engaged in the humanitarian response to populations affected by the three on-going crises in Cameroon. 

Under the strategic guidance of its Steering Committee and the leadership of its coordinator, the INGO forum aims at enhancing information-sharing between INGOs, notably to support coordination of operations and build common positions, improving representation of INGOs and joint advocacy and contributing to the overall humanitarian coordination architecture. The project includes various services to INGOs, including trainings for INGOs and partners’ staff, sharing of experience and lessons learnt, and facilitation and support on issues of common interest. CHINGO also engages with external stakeholders and provides a collective voice for INGOs as well as an entry point for requests to INGOs. Advocacy and communication activities aim to support better understanding of the assistance provided by INGOs in Cameroon, identify and propose solutions to challenges faced by INGOs in humanitarian operations and increase the visibility of the crises in Cameroon with the overall objective to better respond to humanitarian needs of populations affected by displacement.

project_name: Resumption of life-saving access to food for people following the recent conflict in Sudan
project_objective:
This is a continuation for the 2023 project putting spotlight on the arrangements to resume critical life-saving activities in Sudan, as and where security allows. When the resumption of operations becomes possible, WFP will engage in three key pillars of work:
A.	Resume life-saving assistance to some or all of WFP’s pre-existing 4.9 million relief caseload. Targeted beneficiaries include food-insecure IDPs, refugees and resident population.
B.	Meet new food security and nutrition needs, where feasible.
C.	Provide critical common services to humanitarian partners (Emergency Telecommunications Cluster, Food Security Cluster, Logistics Cluster, UNHAS).
WFP resumed critical food assistance on 2 May 2023 to a proportion of the existing relief and nutrition caseload, where WFP has assured security, capacity, access, stocks and partners. The focus is: 
Gradual provision of general food assistance (GFA) with the aim to reach 4.9 million food-insecure IDPs, refugees and resident population, over the next 2-3 months. 
Given the highly volatile context, a gradual approach will be applied. As a first relief response, a two-month in-kind food ration covering May and June will be provided to refugees (100% ration) in White Nile, Kassala and Gedaref States.
There is a possibility that food commodities in warehouses may be looted if not distributed urgently. Accordingly, only in-kind food will be distributed in this preliminary response (no CBT at this stage with a particular concern on liquidity). While in-kind food relief is being prioritized for the initial response, CBT preparedness options are being concurrently developed. g and fosters gender equality.

project_name: PROVISION OF ESSENTIAL LIFE -SAVING HEALTH CARE SERVICES FOR RETURNEES, IDPS AND HOST COMMUNITIES IN YEI RIVER  COUNTY.
project_objective:
Yei is one of the counties in central Equatoria states which is much affected by the 2016 conflict between the government armed forces and the opposition armed forces, and this has led to displacement of people from their place of origin. 
The Joint Humanitarian assessment headed by UNOCHA in July 2022 conducted in the payams of Lasu and Tore of Yei County indicates that the health condition of the people living in those payams are in high need for humanitarian assistance most of the identified health gaps includes lack of drugs, lack health staff, vandalized health infrastructures. Yei currently host about15,000 IDPs and 4056 returnee which are settled in the main town of Yei. The county is receiving a continues influx of refugee from Uganda and DRC on daily basis according to the RRC.
The conflict in Yei has disrupted the health system in the county where most of the infrastructures are destroyed and need repair. Due to the conflict health services provision became a main challenge especially in the rural areas. The most affected payams of Yei that need health intervention are Lasu, Tore and Otogo. Hence this project will aim to improve health service delivery through supply of drugs, rehabilitation of the existing health infrastures, immunization of children, Health education awareness and conduct treatment of the most communicable disease. The intervention will target 68,550people both men, women, and children from 3 payams Tore, Lasu and Otogo of Yei County.

project_name: Support to vulnerable community to access the improved agricultural items and organize the farmers into saving group in Wau – Yei and Juba.
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to facilitate the targeted community composed by: returnees, vulnerable host community, IDPs and breeders to have access on improved local seeds specifically drought-tolerant and flood-tolerant. The farmers groups and breeders will be organized into Saving groups after they have received improved agricultural items and have conducted at list 2 harvests according to the agricultural calendar in the project region. 
In the actual context, the population of South Sudan particularly the vulnerable community groups are not getting sufficient food to cover the nutritional body need. 
The project activities will focus on an integrated approach of food nutrition security and saving groups for the communal economic stability.
The local crop seeds production will be promoted via community seeds multiplication plot to guarantee the sustainable of the activities. For the environment protection, solar irrigation pumps will be promoted and trees nurseries, these under organized farmer groups and the school’s management.  
In the process of project launching, Malteser International will conduct vulnerability mapping with the involvement of Payams representatives and local community leaders (Boma Chiefs and villages Chiefs).
The project target beneficiaries 3000 HH: 2400 HH with agricultural vocation and 600 breeders (in: Wau – Yei – Peri urban area of Juba). The beneficiary’s selection will be based on criteria such as: returnees, IDPs and vulnerable host community (widows; disable persons…) and small breeders at household level. Good Agriculture Technics will be provided to the community and to 12 pilots schools where school gardens activities will be implemented.
The project will, finally help local farmers to protect their crops from further damage; Promote SMART agriculture that does not make climate issues worse by using crops that require less water, less space and are more nutritious. It will also contribute in Holistic approaches to farming and health which take into consideration the interlinkages of climate, human health and animal health;

project_name: Amélioration de la réponse multisectorielle en faveur des Réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile et mise en œuvre des solutions durables pour les réfugiés au Cameroun
project_objective:
Le projet a pour objectif l’amélioration de l’environnement de protection, l’accès aux solutions et voies complémentaires pour les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile notamment en ce qui concerne  les activités d’enregistrement , de  la documentation, la protection de l’enfance, la prévention ,  la réponse aux violences sexuelles et sexistes, l’accès aux services sociaux de base (santé, éducation et eau), l’accès à un abri décent et aux biens domestiques essentiels ainsi que du  renforcement de la résilience.
Le projet cible en 2023, un total de 491,113 réfugiés au Cameroun notamment : 355,667 réfugiés RCA, 132,151 NIG, 2,533 des nationalités minoritaires, 9,239 demandeurs d’asile ainsi que 15% des populations autochtones par la présence des réfugiés dans les régions affectées.
Au cours de l’année 2021, en dépit du contexte sanitaire marquée par la survenue de la pandémie de la COVID19 qui a négativement affecté l’environnement socio-économiques des populations, la situation sécuritaire fragile en RCA et l’instabilité dans la région du bassin du Lac Chad, le HCR a initié des projets visant à améliorer l’environnement de protection des réfugiés et assurer l’accès aux solutions aux réfugiés.
Les projets déjà initiés requièrent une continuité dans la mise en œuvre afin renforcer la résilience et l’autonomisation des réfugiés de longue date, assurer leur inclusion effective dans les programmes de développement et donner accès aux solutions mais également apporter la réponse aux nouvelles situations d’urgences.
Au cours de 2023, il sera mis en œuvre par le HCR, les acteurs humanitaires et le gouvernement des activités qui garantissent l’accès équitable et la jouissance des droits humains fondamentaux aux femmes, aux hommes, aux filles et aux garçons de tout âge et ceux ayant diverses vulnérabilités.
L’UNHCR compte à travers ce projet :
-	Apporter la réponse aux besoins critiques de protection en assurant l’accès à l’asile, la documentation, la prévention et la réponse aux VBG, l’accès à l’éducation, l’accès durable aux infrastructures et services WASH, aux moyens d’existence et à l’inclusion socio-économique, ainsi que le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de la coexistence pacifique entre les réfugiés et avec la communauté hôte.
-	Mettre en œuvre les solutions durables en renforçant la résilience des communautés affectées par les différentes crises et les moyens d’existence et explorer des opportunités viables par la mise en œuvre des alternatives aux camps notamment dans la région de l’extrême nord.
-	Le HCR continuera à faciliter le retour volontaire des réfugiés dans leur pays d’origine, à identifier les cas de réinstallation, d’importants besoins existent en termes de réfugiés pouvant potentiellement être considérés pour cette solution durable, cette dernière ne peut se réaliser que si les pays de réinstallations offrent des places. Par ailleurs, cette solution ne concerne qu’un pourcentage infime de la population réfugiée dans son ensemble. Le défi reste néanmoins la nécessité d’étendre le pool d’identification des réfugiés vers leurs zones d’installation mais avec des capacités très limitées et à faire le plaidoyer pour l’accès des réfugiés aux voies complémentaires.
-	Améliorer le bien-être socio-économique et environnemental des refugies par la promotion de l’agriculture, la pêche et l’élevage en milieu rural, par la promotion des programmes d’entrepreneuriat et de résilience à travers l’approche communautaire et par la promotion d’une approche sensible à l’environnement chez tous les acteurs et partenaires de la réponse ;
-	Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire des POCs et des communautés d’accueil à travers le Cash Based Intervention ;
-	Favoriser les partenariats, le partage de l'information et la planification conformément aux plans de développement nationaux et locaux ainsi que la stratégie régionale pour la stabilisation, le rétablissement et le développement des zones impactées par les activités de Boko Haram à l’Extrême

project_name: Protection/solution et assistance multisectorielle en faveur des réfugiés au Niger et des communautés d’accueil
project_objective:
En 2023, l’intervention en faveur des réfugiés présents au Niger s’articule autour des objectifs suivants : 
-	Objectif 1 : Continuer de renforcer l’environnement de protection en ajustant de manière continue les dispositifs pour s’adapter aux dynamiques de mouvements.

L’intervention s’inscrit dans les principes du Pacte Mondial pour les Réfugiés et continue d’être guidée par la politique d’alternative aux camps de réfugiés soutenue avec constance par le Gouvernement du Niger et facilitant l’opérationnalisation du triple nexus Humanitaire-Développement-Paix. project_name: Strengthening Protection & Emergency Response, and Promotion of Sustainable Durable Solutions in NE Nigeria through CCCM in Selected Locations in Adamawa and Borno States.
project_objective:
The project seeks to strengthen protection and emergency intervention and promote durable solutions through a coordinated multi-sectoral response by reinforcing CCCM activities delivery, taking into consideration new developments within the operation. The intervention will be multi-sectoral, focusing on the Out of Camp Area Based Approach (ABA) ,and within prioritized camps/camp-like settings in Borno and Adamawa states, while also maintaining the conventional approach in camps with CCCM needs. The proposed CCCM approaches have been successfully implemented in NE Nigeria, with ABA recently piloted by UNHCR and partners in Borno, and currently rolled out to Adamawa. Given the prevailing circumstances in NE, it is not practical to abruptly discontinue the implementation of conventional CCCM approaches in camps and camp-like structures, knowing that several camps will still be in existence for better part of 2023. Inclusion of the host communities and returnees, and the population that have relocated or those attempting to integrate in the community is a sure way to promote durable solutions and community cohesion through equitable targeting. The project will cover 4 LGAs in Borno (Ngala, Monguno, Banki (Bama) and Damasak (Mobbar)), 5 LGAs in Adamawa (Yola South, Yola North, Mubi, Madagali and Michika) and 2 LGAs in Yobe state (Damaturu and Gujba). The breakdown of the target for this CCCM project is 97,298 individuals (19,460HH) for IDPs and 22,702 individuals (4,540 HH) for returnees, distributed as follows: 46% (male), 54% (female), 60% (children), 36% (adult) and 4% (elders).

Overall, the response will focus on enhancing multi-sectoral coordination of humanitarian response, monitoring of protection and assistance, promotion of participatory approach, site facilitation, community organizing, capacity building for government authorities, partners and the community, strengthening information sharing, communication and coordination, promoting, and strengthening of accountability to the affected population, ensuring infrastructureal improvement and to mainstream protection, Child Protection, GBV, Prevention from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and other cross-cutting issues like COVID 19 into CCCM for improved living conditions, and to promote sustainable durable solutions. Variations in gender, ethnic origin, diversity, and age that may be wrongly applied to eliminate specific persons from accessing services and lead to vulnerability and risky coping strategies will be considered during every stage of the project life cycle.
ABA is a steppingstone to early recovery/stabilization, hence CCCM response will attempt to link areas under ABA with public service activities such as education, food security, infrastructure development/rehabilitation, health, and public works among others. The community leaders will be oriented to sensitize the community on peaceful coexistence and how they can benefit from public services, development work within the geographical locations, including how they can get employment, access markets and conduct business, including available livelihood opportunities as contributing factors to sustainable durable solutions.

project_name: AMELIORATION DES CONDITIONS DE VIE DES PDI, REFUGIES, RETOURNES ET COMMUNAUTES HOTES VULNERABLES DANS LA PROVINCE DU LAC, A TRAVERS UNE REPONSE INTEGREE ET DURABLE.
project_objective:
L’actuelle intervention vise à mettre en place un accompagnement aux personnes déplacées internes, aux réfugiés, retournés et personnes vulnérables de la communauté hôte à travers des services intégrés et durables dans les sites de Ngourtou Koumboua, Yakoua et au camp de réfugiés de Dar-Es-Salam, ainsi qu’une assistance aux réfugiés installés dans les 9 villages d’opportunités et en vue de leur autonomisation. Il s’agit d’unprojet pilote d’une année qui ciblera directement environ 75.000 dans les domaines des abris durables, le WaSH et l'education en collaboration avec l'UNICEF, les moyens d’existence, la protection à base communautaire, l’environnement et l'énergie ; en lien avec le nexus humanitaire, développement, paix et sécurité. Cela permettra d’améliorer l’environnement de protection globale de ces personnes déplacées de force dont les assistances humanitaires offertes jusqu’ici ne parviennent pas à inverser la courbe des besoins, alors que la situation humanitaire ne cesse de se détériorer dans la Province du Lac. Au 31 décembre 2022, le nombre de population déplacées s’élevait à 425,772 personnes, dont 381,289 personnes déplacées internes, 20,581 réfugiés et 23,901 retournés, selon les données publiées par le HCR auxquelles s’ajoutent les inondations d’une ampleur inouïe qui ont touché plus de183, 100 personnes, selon le rapport du comité provinciale de crise publié le 02 décembre2022. Dans le même ordre d’idées, plusieurs évaluations conduites par les acteurs humanitaires, indiquent également que ces personnes restent dans une situation d’extrême vulnérabilité les rendant entièrement dépendant de l’aide humanitaires, alors que la couverture des financements reste très faible par rapport aux besoins, et que les crises ne cessent de se multiplier.
De plus, compte tenu de la nature prolongée de la crise sécuritaire et environnementale, de l'ampleur croissante des besoins de protection des populations déplacées, la faiblesse des services sociaux de base et la précarité des conditions socioéconomiques des population et de l'accélération des effets de la désertification, il est important d'investirdans des solutions à plus long terme pour les personnes déplacées de force, enfin d’améliorer les conditions leurs conditions de vie, vision stratégique du gouvernement dans le cadre du plan national de développement. La paupérisation et le manque d’accèsaux besoins sociaux de base de ces populations déplacées et des communautés d’accueil, risque de menacer la paix et la stabilité dans la région et de poser des difficultés pour parvenir à un relèvement post-crise. La complexité des menaces nécessite une approche bien informée par zone, prenant en compte la protection de l'environnement, la résilience socio-économique durable parmi d'autres solutions d'impact à long terme et l’investissement dans des activités à valeur économiquement rentable pour les ménages. Ce projet se propose ainsi de mener des interventions dans les secteurs sites ci-haut et développera deux sites intégrés avec le minimum de services nécessaires afin d’offrir un cadre de vie plus digne aux personnes victimes des crises multidimensionnelles dans la province du Lac.

project_name: STRENGTHENING HUMANITARIAN COORDINATION, ADVOCACY AND QUALITY OF HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE
project_objective: (i) Provide effective coordination by strengthening linkages between the various coordination and working group levels from ICCG in the capital and intersectoral working groups in the regions to HCT level engagements with the Government; (ii)Promote humanitarian access in a complex operating environment, where the security situation remains volatile; (iii)  Strengthen civil-military coordination at the regions and capital levels to improve response preparedness, rapid and safe delivery of humanitarian assistance, and foster enhanced predictability of civil-military coordination processes and platforms; (iv) support country-led identification of strategic HDP collaboration priorities/collective outcomes, which will inform the multi-year Humanitarian Response Strategy framework (2023-2025) and the humanitarian, development, and peace action based on a shared understanding of the nexus, and be reflected in the UNSDCF and the National Development Plan; (v) advocate for principled humanitarian action by relevant authorities and sharing its coordination expertise based on global best practices.  This will include an enhanced interface and support to the Government of Niger, especially the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and the Prime Minister's Office, capitalizing on their willingness to lead on humanitarian issues; (vi) Enhance partnerships with existing and new humanitarian donors through improved bilateral and multilateral engagement; (vii) Increased accountability of the humanitarian system to meet humanitarian needs.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination, de la gestion de l'information et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise multidimensionnelle au Burkina Faso continue de s’intensifier au vu des mouvements de populations et violations accrues des droits humains, engendrant l’impact le plus dévastateur sur les populations civiles depuis ces quatre dernières années. Les populations du Burkina Faso font face à une grave crise due à une insécurité généralisée et à des violations du droit international humanitaire et des droits de l'homme, en raison de l’instabilité politique, de l’activité accrue des groupes armés et des opérations militaires. 

Au cours de l’année 2022, le Burkina Faso a connu en janvier et en septembre deux coups d'État. La crise ne cesse de croitre année après année du fait de la magnitude et de la gravité des effets induits par cette instabilité et insécurité prononcées dans le pays. 

Il semble fort probable que la situation politique et sécuritaire au Burkina Faso continue de se dégrader.  En effet, plusieurs incidents de sécurité relevés au cours de l’année 2022 ont entrainé de nouveaux déplacements de population. Selon les autorités nationales, environ 1,76 million de personnes se sont déplacées jusqu’en octobre 2022, c’est-à-dire, qu’une personne sur douze s’est déplacée. 

En 2023, environ 4,7 million de personnes les plus vulnérables seront en besoin d’assistance humanitaire dont 3,1 million seront ciblées. Le bureau de pays du Burkina Faso va appuyer le la mise en œuvre des activités prioritaires dans les cinq domaines d'intervention de OCHA, à savoir. 

•	Renforcer la coordination humanitaire au niveau stratégique et aux niveaux
opérationnels et assurer un leadership dans de la coordination humanitaire, y compris la coordination civilo-militaire (UN-CMCoord) ; le suivi et le plaidoyer en matière d’accès humanitaire ; l'engagement communautaire et la redevabilité envers les personnes affectées ;
•	Renforcer le plaidoyer humanitaire, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées
internes et les personnes non déplacées ;
•	Soutenir l'application pratique de la politique humanitaire et les bonnes pratiques, y
compris la promotion de la collaboration entre l'humanitaire, le développement et les
acteurs de la consolidation de la paix tout en respectant la distinction et l'intégrité de
l'action humanitaire ;
•	Faciliter une mobilisation cohérente et coordonnée du financement humanitaire ;
•	Fournir une gestion de l'information de haute qualité et pour soutenir le leadership
humanitaire et la prise de décision.

project_name: WASH Response to Conflict Affected Population in North East Nigeria (Borno and Adamawa)
project_objective: The project aims to address the WASH needs of a targeted total of 117,000 conflict affected populations across Borno and Adamawa States. The overall project objective is to ensure that conflict affected have reduced exposure to WASH related illnesses through improved access to potable drinking water, appropriate/dignified sanitation facilities and strengthened hygiene practices. Prioritization of interventions will be based on the needs identified to and tailored to the needs for the disabled, elderly, different age groups and displacement status. The project will address the needs for the internally displaced persons (newly displaced and protracted crisis), returnees and extremely vulnerable host communities. The targeted communities will contribute to the implementation of the project through further needs assessments, contributing to the design, and participation during project monitoring and giving feedback during the project surveys and post distribution monitoring. The project will also be tailored to address the emerging and re-emerging epidemics, related to provision of adequate water, sanitation and hygiene services. This will include responding to such outbreaks such as cholera, the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and other related epidemics. More specially, the project activities will include the following; Rehabilitation/upgrading and construction water points. This includes optimization, solarisation, replacing pumps to optimize the capacity of the boreholes, improvement of the water collection points, replacement of taps and old pipes. Water treatment and water quality monitoring. This includes introduction of inline water chlorination, monitoring of the free residual chlorine levels both at the point of collection and at the household level. Samples will be collected for bacteriological analysis from households that will have zero free residual chlorine levels. Emergency water distribution/treatment via water trucking (where all other water supply options are not available). This activity shall be limited to a period of not more than 3months. Establishment and capacity building of water management committees. Water committees will be equipped with tool boxes in order to undertake minor works Construction of new latrines and bathing shelters. Priority shall be given to communities who practice open defecation and do not have latrines. Operation and maintenance of latrines, including minor repairs and maintenance, desludging and minor rehabilitations such as replacement of broken doors, handles and some missing part of the super structure. Hygiene Promotion messages will be delivered through community based trained hygiene promoters and the information, education and communication materials will be adopted from the sector approved materials. Distribution of Hygiene Non-Food Items (NFIs), including the installation of hand washing stations. The distribution will be targeted, and will be done through both in kind and the use of vouchers (where markets are functioning). The NFIs will also be adopted from the sector approved kits, which includes family hygiene kits, latrine cleaning kits, cholera kits etc. Trainings and capacity building, this will be done for community based hygiene promoters, WASH committees, adolescent girls and other targeted trainings for water, sanitation and hygiene staff implementing the project.The project will target Monguno, Jere, MMC and Gwoza Local Government Areas (LGA) of Borno State and Yola North, Yola South and Mubi North LGAs.The implementation of this project shall be closely coordinated with the relevant government ministry (ministry of water resources), Rural Water and Sanitation agency(RUWASA), UN agencies (UNICEF, IOM), other WASH implementing partners and local Non-Governmental Organizations.

project_name: Linking Emergency Assistance and Response in Northeast Syria (LEARN) - Phase IV
project_objective:
Since October 2018, LEARN Consortium has supported equitable and safe access to essential basic services, including WASH, Shelter and Health, MPCA and Protection, for the most vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Northeast Syria (NES). LEARN is comprised of Solidarités International (SI), Un Ponte Per (UPP), Relief International (RI) and People in Need (PIN).

The Program Vision is to increase the resilience of vulnerable, conflict-affected populations, through the provision of equitable and safe, integrated, multi-sectoral services and agile emergency response. While the Program Goal is to reduce morbidity and mortality and improve living conditions, resilience and dignity of affected populations in North East Syria, through coordinated, timely emergency Health, Protection, WASH, Shelter, MPCA, HCIMA, and ERMS services, which meet the most acute humanitarian needs.

In Phase IV of the project, LEARN will continue to build on and prioritize integration between partners where it is feasible and desirable. LEARN will continue to respond to the emergency needs of the most vulnerable populations in Northeast Syria (NES) through a needs-based, people centered, and integrated, multi-sectoral approach. These approaches will simultaneously build resilience, reduce dependence on aid and restore livelihoods and markets. 

Objective Health: Reduce morbidity and mortality among vulnerable, conflict-affected populations through improved access to quality health services.
LEARN will continue to provide life-saving health services to the affected population in order to reduce morbidity, mortality and injury through sustained support to health facilities and community outreach.  UPP continues to provide both full and partial support to facilities with an extensive exit strategy for each. 
UPP aims to improve clinical quality of health and strengthen the local health system in all its’ components in accordance UPP’s 2021 Health Strategy towards the development of a comprehensive model of primary health care. This will be achieved by applying a participatory approach, to engage and empower individuals and communities in achieving equal access to health, and through an Area-Based Approach (ABA) which entails a geographic focus to strengthen collaboration among partners and ensure a collaborative multi-sectoral response. UPP will implement a person-centered approach combined with an integrated approach based on medical quality, preventative measures, and community engagement. 

Objective Early Recovery and Market Assessment (ERMS): Support vulnerable households to restore, protect and develop livelihoods.
In Phase IV, LEARN will address the growing and disparate needs in the Livelihoods Restoration and New Livelihoods Development sectors by combining economic empowerment of the most vulnerable with employment opportunities and investment in existing value chains, focused on the thematic areas of women empowerment. This will be achieved through support to women cooperatives to restore their livelihoods affected by the crisis, and through support to vocational training graduates for them to start their own businesses and create new livelihoods. The proposed activities will be designed with a view to maximum integration within the livelihoods sector and complementary to other sectoral areas of programming under the LEARN where possible. A “circular” logic to activities is seen as the most effective way to ensure the largest impact possible.

Protection will be mainstreamed through all activities, and complemented by a robust referral mechanism. 
Through a flexible and timely LEARN RRM, which incorporates learning from previous Phases, LEARN will continue to respond to acute shocks across the whole of NES.

project_name: Provision of Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance to Rohingya and Host Communities to claim / exercise their legal identity and HLP rights
project_objective:
NRC ICLA will be implementing activities across 20 camps and 5 host community unions ensuring protection and gender mainstreaming. ICLA will work with the Camp-in Charge’s, UNHCR and other actors in camps to secure identity and documentation of Rohingya refugees through existing registration and documentation guidelines. NRC will also work with Ukhiya and Teknaf government authorities e.g. UNO office, UP office to host communities. The project is designed to positively increase access to identity/civil documentation (mainly Family Attestation Certificate, Smart Card, birth, death, marriage, and divorce certificates), documents required for accessing essential services, and HLP including tenancy rights in the refugee camps and host communities, whilst also mitigating and addressing tensions between the Rohingya and local communities generated by HLP disputes. This objective will be achieved through the increased capacity of refugees and host communities to exercise/claim their identity and HLP rights and improved access to and use of collaborative dispute resolution mechanisms in communities. NRC will provide legal counselling and assistance based on individual needs to enable target beneficiaries to overcome legal, procedural, and documentation challenges, including referral to specialized case management actors as it may be required; combined with information dissemination and awareness-raising initiatives to empower target beneficiaries to claim their rights and access available justice mechanisms. Improvement of the relationships between refugees and host communities, and within the Rohingya community itself, will be achieved through the local leaders` capacity building in HLP dispute resolution. Key staff, volunteers, and other stakeholders, including target communities whenever possible, will be involved to identify existing and emerging threats to safety, dignity and rights faced by different sex and age groups among the refugee and the host populations. Special attention will be paid to threats and vulnerabilities generated or exacerbated by COVID-19 and the associated containment measures. This information will be analyzed and used for evidence-based advocacy and will also be shared externally with other protection actors and stakeholders.

ICLA will arrange information session, individual support, and counselling assisting refugees in obtaining and updating their civil documentation. These supports contributing to beneficiaries’ access to civil justice and other forms of humanitarian assistance, as well as better exercising of their rights. For both civil documentation and HLP, ICLA’s using general information sessions to raise community awareness of rights and to generate interest and awareness of the need for civil documentation and tenure security. Information sessions typically last 45-60 minutes and are open to all camp residents and are also conducted for vulnerable host community members. To address the widespread issue of refugees paying mahjis and others to complete their written applications, ICLA will supporting by the field staff to review refugee applications, assist beneficiaries in gathering supporting paperwork and witnesses, completing the written application, and submitting the completed package to the CiC office.
