project_name: Promoting Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Wellbeing of the Conflict-Affected Population in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The crisis in Northeast Nigeria continues to exacerbate protection risks and needs for the internally displaced populations (IDPs) and host communities. The unpredictable and volatile security situation continues to threaten the populations’ daily safety and health. By fleeing the insecurity, the population is deprived of basic services and often left without any means of livelihood. The project aims at continuing and strengthening IOM’s protection response in Northeast Nigeria through the implementation of protection activities by interdisciplinary Psychosocial Mobile Teams (PMTs) comprised of social workers, lay counselors and community mobilizers. IOM will prioritize coordination with protection actors working in other local government areas and government partners including National Agency of Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) and State Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) States. The following areas of intervention are to be implemented under this project: 1) Capacity building of key stakeholders, including partners and government officials, on protection mainstreaming, counter-trafficking and community-based mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) approach; 2) Increased protection risk assessments to measure and report on trends related to general protection risks and risks of trafficking in person; 3) Provision of specialized protection services to (potential) victims of trafficking (VoTs), including case management, reintegration support, and psychosocial services, as well as to other vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities and older persons; 4) Increased protection advocacy to the government and other key stakeholders incorporating findings from protection risk assessments, as well as advocacy for increased action on trafficking in persons among protection sector partners; 5) Additional training for IOM Women’s and Men’s Committees on identifying key protection risks and trends and making safe referrals for people in need of specialized protection services; 6) Developing reports and other information products on identified protection risks and trends and sharing these with key stakeholders, including PSNE and; 7) Targeted livelihood support to (potential) victims of trafficking to support with their reintegration.

The implementation of planned services will be guided by Guidance note on how to mainstream protection across IOM crisis response (IN/232 Guidance note on how to mainstream protection across IOM crisis response (or Migration crisis operational framework sector of assistance), the IOM Manual on Community-Based MHPSS in Emergencies and Displacement (IOM Manual on Community-Based Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Emergencies and Displacement | International Organization for Migration), IOM handbook on direct assistance of victims of trafficking (IOM handbook on direct assistance for victims of trafficking, 2007, IOM handbook on direct assistance for victims of trafficking), and Caring for victims of trafficking the guidance note for health providers (Caring for trafficked persons: guidance for health providers, IOM, 2009, Caring for trafficked persons: guidance for health providers).

project_name: Child protection assistance for the most vulnerable, at-risk children in Syria
project_objective:
SC’s child protection intervention is: 1) Children and adolescents have increased resilience and access to violence prevention and response services; 2) Caregivers, community members and other sector staff have strengthened capacity to protect children/adolescents, and support their healthy development and resilience.  SC’s intervention aims to improve the safety and wellbeing of girls and boys through individual case management for the most at-risk, including UASC, children with disabilities, child survivors, as well as children affected by armed conflict and armed groups (CAAFAG).  Case management is the entry point to support the needs of UASC, including Syrian, Iraqis and third county nationals, and FTR is initiated by caseworkers in coordination with relevant protection actors. For children without parental care and in line with interagency SOPs, SC trains foster families, supports existing informal care arrangements, and identifies alternative forms of care when foster families are not available, such as supported independent living or ICCs, as a last resort. Case management is also a vital service for CAAFAG and an area of focus for SC to ensure that released or excluded children access the holistic services and individual support for reintegration. CVA for child protection through case management is being piloted in community settings. Training, coaching and supervision for caseworkers is a key part of delivering quality case management, and the Steps to Protect rollout includes a focus on supervision, as well as on feedback and accountability.  

SC reaches children and adolescents through inclusive age and gender-sensitive group activities to foster psychosocial support, stress processing and resilience. In the absence of safe spaces in both camps and communities, a range of static, mobile and integrated child-friendly spaces (CFSs) offer group activities designed for creative expression, to develop protection knowledge and life skills, as well as strengthen an environment of trust. These spaces provide an entry point for community engagement as a hub for protection-related information and referrals, such as for children involved in child labor. Based on assessed needs and in consultation with children and caregivers, SC + partners will deliver structured PSS curricula. A targeted effort will be made to engage children with disabilities. 

For the trusted and responsible adults in children’s lives–caregivers, teachers, community members and service providers, SC builds their knowledge and skills to communicate with children, identify risks facing and take action to increase children’s safety. SC will continue its rollout of the Parenting without Violence (PwV) Common Approach, with an focus on caregiver self-care and stress management alongside positive parenting practices. SC will offer sessions for mothers of young children and incorporate a focus on early childhood nutrition (delivered in tandem with nutrition colleagues) as well as outreach to caregivers of children with disabilities. PwV encourages promotion of positive parenting messages and gender equality through community structures, such as Child Protection Committees and Parent/Teacher Associations (PTAs). These structures have been supported previously and will be sustained in the proposed period. Community members and other sector staff will be targeted with capacity building on safe identification and referral, basic MHPSS including PFA, GBV and PSEA, as well as CPMS. Efforts will be made to build capacity of SC staff and partners to include children and caregivers with disabilities.  Community members, including children, will identify the risks and develop awareness raising initiatives.  To mitigate the risk of GBV, SC will conduct targeted GBV awareness sessions with adolescents and caregivers using an adapted GBV prevention toolkit to improve knowledge on root causes and consequences of GBV and accessing available GBV response services.

project_name: Provisión de ayuda humanitaria a población vulnerable con múltiple afectación (especial enfasís Conflicto Armado) en Colombia
project_objective:
El presente proyecto busca asegurar la provisión de asistencia humanitaria de calidad para 9.000 mujeres y hombres en situación de vulnerabilidad, afectadas por múltiples eventos (en particular, por el conflicto armado interno) y residentes en comunidades rurales de difícil acceso de municipios del Bajo Cauca del departamento Antioquia y el sur del departamento de Córdoba. La asistencia humanitaria se centrará, por un lado, en la cobertura de necesidades básicas en materia de Salud, Protección, Agua e Higiene y por otro en la mejora de la resiliencia comunitaria con las actividades enfocadas en la Preparación ante desastres, sobre todo a inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra. 

El componente de Salud incluye la mejora del acceso a la atención primaria (medicina, odontología, salud sexual y reproductiva, psicología, acceso a medicamento gratuitos y educación para prevención de enfermedades, en especial la COVID-19, y buenas prácticas en salud) en estrecha coordinación con el Ministerio de Salud colombiano, a través de Unidades Móviles de Salud (UMS) en lugares remotos afectados por el conflicto armado. También se proporcionarán los recursos necesarios a casos de gravedad que requieran acudir a las cabeceras municipales o departamentales para exámenes médicos especializados o atención de segundo nivel. Vinculado con el componente de Salud, se mejorará el acceso a agua segura en cantidad suficiente para uso doméstico de la población en situación de vulnerabilidad de las comunidades beneficiarias, a través de pequeñas intervenciones en los sistemas de distribución y la provisión de kits para el tratamiento y almacenamiento de agua a domicilio. Además, se reforzarán las prácticas de higiene para prevenir enfermedades de origen hídrico y reducir la transmisión del COVID-19.  

El componente de Protección se centrará en la asistencia inmediata de personas en riesgo grave para la integridad, en particular para los casos de abusos hacia Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes (NNA), sobrevivientes de violencia basada en género (VBG), víctimas del conflicto armado y trata de personas, con la orientación sobre derechos y rutas de atención, así como provisión de ayudas monetarias para cubrir necesidades básicas en la primera fase del desplazamiento forzoso.

Finalmente, debido a que las consecuencias del conflicto armado y del fenómeno migratorio acentúan la vulnerabilidad, ya de por si preocupante, de las comunidades expuestas a catástrofes de origen antrópico y natural, se desarrolla un eje de intervención de prevención y preparación ante desastres que prevé fortalecer la capacidad local para hacer frente a futuras crisis a través de actividades de prevención y preparación coordinadas con las autoridades locales y las comunidades beneficiarias.

Cabe mencionar que la acción se desarrollará conjuntamente a un proyecto financiado por la Oficina Humanitaria de la Unión Europea (DG ECHO), completándola y reforzándola en sus componentes. Por lo tanto, los impactos y resultados presentados aquí son los globales conseguidos por las 2 intervenciones conjuntamente, en los 2 departamentos propuestos.

project_name: Programme transfrontalier de promotion des solutions durables aux situations de déplacement au Cameroun et en République Centrafricaine (RCA)
project_objective:
Le consortium DRC-ACF-CARE-NRC propose un programme transfrontalier intégré contribuant directement à apporter des solutions durables, diversifiées et localisées aux situations de déplacements au Cameroun et en République Centrafricaine (RCA). Cette action permettra :
●	De répondre aux besoins de base des réfugiés/retournés et communautés hôtes dans les zones d'accueil et de retour (OS1) ;
●	Le renforcement de l’autonomisation économique des populations en situation de déplacement face aux chocs et au changement climatique (OS2) ;
●	Un plus grand respect des droits des populations affectées par les situations de déplacements entre le Cameroun et la RCA (OS3).
Ces axes contribuent aux objectifs du Pacte mondial sur les réfugiés et du Cadre d’action global pour les réfugiés. L’action propose une approche régionale cohérente avec les engagements pris par les Etats dans la Déclaration de Yaoundé en avril 2022, en contribuant à la mise en œuvre des axes III (soutien au cadre institutionnel), IV (promotion de l’inclusion, la résilience et l’autonomisation économique des réfugiés et populations hôtes), V (soutien aux conditions propices au retour durable) et VI (mise en place d’un mécanisme régional de coordination). Le consortium se propose de participer au suivi de ces engagements aux côtés du HCR dans les mécanismes de coordination régionaux et/ou nationaux qui seront mis en place. 
En cohérence avec les programmations multi-annuelles 2021-2027 entre l’Union européenne (UE) et le Cameroun d’une part, l’UE et la RCA d’autre part , l’action sera basée sur l’amélioration du bien-être socio-économique des populations et sur la protection et la promotion des droits humains, avec un accent particulier sur les victimes de violations de droits, notamment parmi les femmes, les jeunes, les réfugié-e-s, les retourné-e-s et les déplacé-e-s. Leur soutien se fera à travers le renforcement de capacités communautaires et étatiques de prise en charge, le renforcement des opportunités économiques, la sensibilisation sur l’accès aux droits et le plaidoyer aux niveaux local et national/transfrontalier. Le programme renforcera le processus de décentralisation impulsé par l’Etat depuis 2019 à travers un appui aux Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées (CTD) qui sont au premier plan de la réponse aux mouvements de populations. Les acteurs locaux tels que les OSC seront des partenaires privilégiés de l‘action afin de favoriser le transfert de compétences et à terme la localisation de l’assistance et la durabilité des actions initiées. En ligne avec le GAP III de l’UE et la résolution 1325 de l'ONU sur la participation des femmes aux processus de paix, l’égalité des genres, l’autonomisation économique et le leadership des femmes et des filles seront promus à travers des activités ciblées et leur participation dans l’action et dans les processus décisionnels.
Le programme proposé est également en ligne avec le Pacte Vert de l’UE. Du fait de la pression exercée par la démographie croissante sur des ressources naturelles menacées, le programme fera de la protection de l’environnement l’une de ses priorités, à travers la promotion de pratiques agricoles agroécologiques, la définition de plans de développement territoriaux durables, ainsi que l’appui à la gestion durable de l’eau et des espaces agro-sylvopastoraux.

project_name: Appui a une education inclusive de qualite aux garcons et filles (3 - 17 ans) retournes et des communautes hotes affectes par la crise de la RCA
project_objective:
L’objectif principal de ce projet est de donner accès à une education inclusive de qualité aux filles et garçons (âgés de 3 à 17 ans) retournés affectés par les mouvements de population liés aux conflits de la RCA et de fournir un environnement d’apprentissage sûr et protecteur ainsi que les compétences pour renforcer la résilience. Le projet contribuera à améliorer la qualité de l’Education des enfants retournés Tchadiens de la RCA et des communautés hôtes grâce à une offre de services educatifs performants dans les 4 provinces du Sud et dans le Salamat affectés 
Pour ce faire, le renforcement des capacités des enseignants, l'appui en matériels scolaires et fournitures didactiques aux élèves et enseignants, le renforcement des infrastructures scolaires devront se poursuivre. 
Le projet vise à promouvoir la cohesion sociale et la cohabitation pacifique et a faciliter l'intégration es enfants déplacés dans les communautés d'accueil.
La mise en oeuvre sera axée sur la participation communautaire, le transfert des compétences aux acteurs pour contribuer au relèvement rapide des communautés touchées et la pérennité des activités scolaires à la fin du projet.

project_name: Projet d’assistance en soins de santé  aux personnes vulnérables ( refugiés,retounés ainsi que les déplaces interne) au sud du Tchad
project_objective:
Le sud du Tchad reste profondément affecté par l’impact de la crise centrafricaine République qui a entraîné depuis 2014 le déplacement de plus de centaines de milliers personnes vers le Tchad fuyant la violence. Plus de 75% d'entre elles sont des femmes et des enfants. Quelques 77 650 retournés (Novembre 2019) tchadiens de la République Centrafricaine (RCA) ayant fui les violences dans le pays voisin depuis 2013 ainsi que 122 958 réfugiés (31 mai 2022) centrafricains arrivés par vagues successives depuis 2003 à 2021sont toujours au Tchad. Les retournés vivent dans cinq sites temporaires et dans des communautés hôtes, majoritairement dans les régions du sud (Logone Oriental, Logone Occidental, Moyen Chari, Mandoul). Les réfugiés sont répartis dans six camps et 23 villages d’accueil dans les régions du Logone Occidental, du Logone Oriental, du Moyen Chari, du Mandoul et du Salamat. Cet afflux de populations entraine une pression accrue sur les ressources déjà affectées par le changement climatique et les faibles infrastructures de base, détériorant ainsi les conditions de vie et moyens d’existence pour les communautés hôtes déjà vulnérables des provinces précitées.
Notons que cette crise a entraîné des répercussions graves sur la capacité déjà faible du système de santé au Tchad qui était déjà fragile. Les formations sanitaires qui prennent en charge ces personnes manquent d’équipements, de médicaments et personnel qualifié pour fournir des services médicaux suffisants de qualité.
En outre, au Tchad décès maternels, néonatals, infantile et infanto-juvéniles restent élevés (respectivement) 860 pour 100 000 naissances vivantes (EDS-MICS 2014-15), 33, 78 et 122 pour 1 000 naissances vivantes (MICS 2019) .

project_name: Approvisionnement en Eau et services assainissement en urgence pour les populations affectées par les conflits dans les Provinces du Logone Occidental, Logone Oriental, Mandoul et Moyen-Chari au Tchad
project_objective:
Ce projet va contribuer efficacement a améliorer la santé et les conditions de vie des personnes retournées  de la RCA, les personnes deplacées (IDP's) et les communautés hots à travers l'approvisionnement en eau potable, assainissement de base et promotion des bonnes pratiques d'hygiène dans les Provinces affectées par la crise des conflits armés en Republique Centrafricaine et l'inondation.
En 2021 et 2022, le Tchad a continue à connaître des mouvements migratoires observés notamment au niveau des points de suivi des flux installés par l’OIM au Sud (Logone Occidental, Logone Oriental, Mandoul et Moyen-Chari). Selon le Cadre des resultats 2023 publies par le Cluster WASH, 439 511 personnes déplacées seront dans le besoin d’une assistance. Les voyageurs observés viennent pour la plus part de la RCA à cause des conflits armés entre les rebelles centrafricains et les conflits intercommunautaires. Les inondations de cette annee dans les provinces du Sud ont affecte une grande partie de la population du Mayo Kebi Ouest qui se sont retrouvees sans abris.Ces personnes étaient principalement des ressortissants tchadiens et centrafricains. 
Le projet va repondre aux besoins identifiés par le Cluster WASH pour une population cible de 22 662 personnes qui représentent 20% de la cible du cluster en assurant l'accès à un paquet d'interventions WASH pour les nouveaux déplacés, les retournés et les populations hotes dans les 4 Provinces citées ci haut.

project_name: Renforcement des services de protection pour la prise en charge des enfants affectées et leurs familles dans les Provinces du Lac, Ndjamena, Tandjile et Logone occidental
project_objective:
Le présent projet vise le renforcement des services de protection y compris les mécanismes communautaires dans les localités sinistrées, la prise en charge multiforme des enfants affectés par les inondations et le renforcement de la résilience des familles vulnérables.  
Le projet contribuera également au renforcement du système d’alerte précoce et de signalement au niveau communautaire de violences à l’encontre des enfants y compris les violences basées sur le genre /exploitations Abus et des Exploitations Sexuels (PSEA). La mise en œuvre du projet permettra d’atteindre les résultats suivants :  
1) 12.000 enfants et parents affectés vont bénéficier des activités de  soutien psychosocial à travers les activités récréatives, ludiques, culturelles et de cohésion sociale dans les espaces ami des enfants fixes et mobiles, les centres d’écoutes communautaires etc.  
2) 400 enfants vulnérables ; à risque ; séparés ou non accompagné ; survivants de VBG seront identifiés et pris en charge  
3) 50 mécanismes communautaires de protection de l’enfant (MCPE) seront renforcés ; 1 système d’alerte au niveau communautaire renforcé ainsi qu’un mécanisme de référencement opérationnel dans chaque localité du projet   
4)  50 intervenants sociaux seront formés sur la protection de l’enfant en situation d’urgence et 200 leaders communautaires sur l’identification des risques de protection et la mise en place des actions de prévention et réponse au niveau communautaire 
5) 20 centres sociaux, centres d’écoute communautaires et centres d’état civil vont bénéficier d’un appui multiforme 
6) 30,000 membres de la communauté vont être sensibilisés sur les risques de protection et les droits de l’enfant 
7) 2000 parents vulnérables auront leurs compétences parentales renforcés et 400 familles vulnérables vont recevoir un appui en AGR en coordination avec les programmes de moyens de subsistance

project_objective: Given the rapidly declining economic situation and compound crises in Lebanon including Cholera, several thousands of Lebanese children are missing out on education or dropping out of school. project_name: Provision of critical and life saving child protection services and social cash assistance
project_objective:
Lebanon is facing a devastating combination of complex crises that are fuelling a rise in the number of children experiencing abuse, exploitation, and violence, with other children’s rights becoming compromised across the lifecycle of the children. The multiple crises the country has been through since 2019 have deepened the vulnerabilities of all populations residing in Lebanon(Syrian/Palestinian refugees, migrants, Lebanese), affecting a much larger population, including those living outside previously recognized most vulnerable localities. The deepened vulnerabilities and rapid impoverishment of families, combined with a lack of access to essential social services, social safety nets and livelihood opportunities amongst displaced populations and vulnerable Lebanese, contributed altogether to an alarming deterioration of the protection situation of children.
As a general objective, UNICEF, together with its implementing partners, aims at increasing access and quality of CP services by strengthening the community-based protective and supportive environment free of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse.
Based on the above, UNICEF will work in collaboration with line ministries, UN agencies and partners to address the psychosocial needs of more than 22,000 affected girls, boys, adolescents and caregivers, using a multi-layered approach through the provision of an integrated package of services, including community-based and more focused psychosocial support activities, case management and access to specialized services, such as mental health psychosocial support services.
The programme will be linked to broader services that vulnerable households will need, particularly child protection. Extensive community engagement, outreach and communication on the programme, efficient payment channel, and clear grievance and accountability mechanisms will be crucial.
UNICEF will also include timely and consistent AAP mechanisms (Accountability toaffected population) to ensure that the programme responds to girls', boy's and caregivers' needs.

project_name: Soutien à l’accès inclusif, sain et protecteur à l’éducation formelle (préscolaire, primaire, post-primaire  et secondaire), non formelle et informelle  de qualité pour les 382 718 enfants (dont 229 630 filles/60% et 153 088 garçons/40%) affectés  par les crises sécuritaire et sanitaire (COVID-19).
project_objective:
Le projet vise à : 
-	Soutenir l’accès inclusif, sain et protecteur à l’éducation et la formation formelle (préscolaire, primaire, post-primaire, secondaire et formation aux métiers), non formelle et informelle de qualité pour les 382 718 enfants et adolescents (dont 202 840 filles/60% et 153 088 garçons/40%) affectés par les crises sécuritaire et sanitaire (COVID-19). 
-	Renforcer les capacités de 4548 enseignants (2 729 femmes et1819 hommes) sur l’Approche Safe School (développement des plans scolaires de préparation/réponse aux urgences et protocole sanitaire COVID-19), l’assistance psychosociale et l'apprentissage socio-émotionnel.
Parmi les enfants ciblés, 202 840 sont affectés par les mouvements des populations (IDP et refugiés) soit 53% ; 38 272 sont des enfants en situation de handicap (ESH) soit 10% ; 57 408 sont du secondaire (soit 15%) et 76 544 sont des enfants du préscolaire (soit 20%).
 
Tous les bénéficiaires vivent dans les 13 régions du pays dont les six (6) particulièrement affectées par les urgences sécuritaires en plus de la COVID-19. Il s’agit de : La Boucle du Mouhoun, le Centre-Nord, l’Est, le Centre-Est, le Nord et le Sahel. 
Le paquet d’activités proposé leur apportera une éducation et une formation formelle et non formelle dans un environnement sûr, inclusif et de qualité. Cela correspond à la vision de la SSZDS et du HRP 2023 du Burkina Faso.

project_name: Appui à la continuité des soins de santé primaire des populations déplacées et des communautés hotes dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Nord et du Centre-Est
project_objective:
Malgré les différents efforts, consentis par le Burkina Faso dans la réduction de la mortalité (de 1993 à 2021, selon les différentes enquêtes EDS, la mortalité infanto-junénile, la mortalité infantile et la mortalité néonatale sont passées respectivement de 187 à 48 /1000 naissances vivantes, de 94 à 30/ 1000 naissances vivantes, de 43 à 18/1000 naissances vivantes) la survie des enfants de moins de 5 ans est marquée par des privations multiples :
- Un enfant sur onze meurt avant de fêter son 5ème anniversaire,
- 1 décès d’enfant de moins de 5 ans sur 3 est un décès néonatal ;
- 2 enfants sur 5 meurent de 3 principales maladies tueuses : Paludisme (21%), Pneumonie/IRA (12%), Diarrhée (8%) ;
- Plus de 2 décès sur 3 (71%), causés par ces 3 maladies tueuses, surviennent dans la communauté ;
- 1 enfant de moins de 5 ans sur 2 ne dort pas sous la MILDA ;
Le contexte sécuritaires actuel dans les 8 régions du pays marqués par les attaques des groupes armées non identifiées remet en cause les acquis engrangés et accentuent les vulnérabilités à tous les niveaux. 
Les régions du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun connaissent depuis un moment une dégradation significative de leur situation humanitaires dues aux différents attaques sécuritaires, avec plusieurs zones d’accès difficiles ou même enclavées (Titao, Thiou, Tougan, Solenzo...). Cette situation n’est pas sans conséquence sur la continuité de l’offre de services de santé avec à ce jour 118/282 formations sanitaires fermées ou fonctionnant à minima dans la Boucle du Mouhoun et 83/253 dans la région du Nord. Des districts sanitaires comme Titao sont isolés avec d’énormes difficultés pour maintenir l’offre de soins de santé de primaire aux populations vivant un blocus. Les efforts des différents partenaires dont UNICEF pour maintenir l’offre de soins curatifs et préventif à travers l’implication des ASBC restent toujours limité et nécessite d’être renforcé au vue des besoins croissant sur le terrain. Par ailleurs, des districts comme Ouahigouya accueille d’énormes déplacés internes avec plusieurs sites de déplacés, entrainant du coup une forte pression sur le système de santé existants avec d’énormes besoins non couverts. Les récents événements sur les sites de déplacés de Youba avec le déplacement de plus de 10 000 PDIs de ces sites viennent aggraver la situation déjà précaire.

Cette situation a des conséquences énormes sur la disponibilité et l’offre de soins de santé aux populations à la fois déplacées et hôtes.
Le présent projet vise donc à renforcer l’offre de santé aux profits des populations déplacées internes et populations hôtes des régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun (districts sanitaires de Nouna, Tougan, Solenzo) et du Nord (districts sanitaires de Titao, Thiou, Ouahigouya, Séguénéga) à travers une offre de santé intégré au niveau institutionnel et communautaire afin de renforcer le système de santé pour répondre aux différents chocs et de renforcer la résilience au niveau communautaire précaires à travers le renforcement des approches utilisant les interventions à base communautaire afin d’assurer la continuité de l’offre de services de soins au niveau communautaire.
 La population en besoin d’assistance sanitaire pour ses 2 régions se décompose comme suit :
Bénéficiaires directs :
- 102 989 enfants de 0-5 ans (dont  61 968 IDPs)
- 46 435 grossesses attendues (33615 IDPs) 

Bénéficiaires indirects
Certaines interventions telles que le renforcement des interventions à base communautaire, la vaccination de routine, la gratuité des soins seront renforcés à l’échelle du district en utilisant les innovations en matière de vaccination

project_name: Appui à prévention et la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë chez les enfants de 0 à 59 mois et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes au niveau national
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso est l’un des quinze pays touchés par une combinaison de chocs dans lesquels l’UNICEF intensifie ses efforts pour atténuer les dommages à long terme de l’émaciation sévère. Les résultats de l’enquête Nutritionnelle réalisée avec la méthodologie SMART en octobre 2021, ont montré une prévalence de la MAG à 9,7% dans 12 régions sanitaires contre 9,1% en 2020 dans tout le pays. Six régions avaient des taux de malnutrition aiguë globale classés élevés selon le seuil de l’OMS à savoir : le Sahel (15.1%) ; le Centre (12.1%) ; le Nord (11.9%) ; le Plateau Central (11.3%) ; La Boucle du Mouhoun (10.8%) et le Centre Ouest (10.2%). Les résultats de l’enquête nutritionnelle rapide organisée en Juillet 2022 dans les communes et localités plus affectées par l’insécurité ont montré une situation préoccupante avec des taux de malnutrition aiguë globale (MAG) classés très élevés selon les standards OMS (compris entre 15 et 20%) dans les communes de Dori (19.8%) ; de Séguénega (19.1%) ; de Fada (15.2% et à Gorom Gorom (16.3%).  La situation était sérieuse avec des taux élevés de MAG variant entre 10 à 15% dans les communes de Gayéri (12.1%) ; Kaya (12.9%) ; Kongoussi (12.8%) ainsi que les localités de Bani (14.2%), Pissila (10.5%), Gorgadji (12.9%), et de Thiou (13.5%). 
Les principaux facteurs associés à la malnutrition au Burkina Faso sont principalement les maladies, l’apport alimentaire inadéquat, les pratiques inappropriées d’alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant, l’insécurité alimentaire, le faible accès à l’eau potable et les conditions inadéquates d’hygiène. Les facteurs aggravants sont liés aux effets négatifs de la crise sécuritaire ayant entraîné le déplacement interne de 1,882,391 personnes  dont 58.44% d’enfants avec la majorité se trouvant dans la région du Sahel (26.4%) ; du Centre Nord (25.2%) ; du Nord (13.3%) et de l’Est (11%). La fermeture des formations sanitaires affecte 211 formations sanitaires sur 2173 soit une proportion de 10%, privant une population de 2,407,381 de l’accès aux services de santé. Le pays connait une dégradation de l’insécurité alimentaire avec 3 533 000 personnes qui seront en insécurité alimentaire pendant la période de Juin à Août 2023 selon l’analyse du cadre harmonisé de Novembre 2022 soit 16% de la population totale. Les 17 provinces les plus affectées sont les suivantes : 1) douze (12) provinces en phase 3 « Crise » : Komondjari, Tapoa, Kompienga, Gnagna, et Gourma dans la région de l’Est ; Bam, Sanmatenga et Namentenga dans la région du Centre Nord ; le Yatenga au Nord ; Sourou et Kossi dans la Boucle du Mouhoun et Koulpelogo au Centre Est ; 2) Cinq provinces en phase 4 « urgence » : toutes les provinces de la région du Sahel (Soum, Seno, Yagha et Oudalan) et une province de la région du Nord (Loroum). 
L’UNICEF continuera à jouer le rôle de Chef de file en Nutrition en assurant la coordination du cluster aussi bien au niveau national qu’au niveau des six régions les plus affectées par l’insécurité politique. project_name: Maternal, Infant and Child Nutrition Emergency Response in South Sudan.
project_objective:
According to the IPC analysis released on 3rd of November 2022, during the lean projection period (April-July 2023), an estimated 7.76 million people (62.7% of the population) will likely face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, with 43,000 people likely to be in catastrophe (IPC phase 5) acute food insecurity in Akobo, Fangak, and Canal/Pigi counties of Jonglei State and Leer and Mayendit Counties of Unity State.  In the lean-season projection period of April to July 2023, 47 counties will likely be in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity, 29 counties will likely be in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) acute food insecurity, and one county will likely be in Stressed (IPC Phase 2) acute food insecurity. 
The nutrition situation remains a major problem. According to FSNMS survey round 28, Prevalence of wasting among young children in South Sudan remains above the World Health Organization emergency threshold in four State (Jonglei, Upper Nile, Unity and NBeG) of the ten states, while the national average as per the latest FSNMS is estimated at 16% percent, showing no improvement since 2019.
Between July and October 2022, 57% of the counties were classified in crises (IPC phase 3) or worse acute malnutrition. During the second projection period (lean season), the situation is expected to deteriorate further where 71 percent counties are projected to be in crises or worse IPC acute malnutrition (IPC AMN Phase 3 and phase4). This represents the highest number classified in IPC AMN Phase 4 (Critical) for the past 3 similar seasons. 
Key drivers to acute malnutrition include high prevalence of diseases. 62.5% of children reported to have been ill two weeks prior to the assessment. The childhood diseases recorded include Diarrhea, fever, and cough. These diseases are among the most common and fatal diseases among children and cause rapid deterioration in health. Poor sanitation conditions are likely contributing to the high prevalence of illness, with open defecation as high as 50% of households in 56 counties. 

In 2023, an estimated 2.14 million people in South Sudan (SS) will be at risk of acute malnutrition, including 345,893 children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM), 1,057,703 children with moderate acute malnutrition (MAM), and 737,812 pregnant and lactating women with acute malnutrition (AM-PLW). 
In response, UNICEF will collaborate with actors in health and WASH sectors to reinforce preventative activities and treat children under five with severe acute malnutrition. These activities will include securing safe water through: rehabilitation of non-functioning boreholes; distribution of water treatment kits to secure safe water; hygiene promotion through distribution of soap; early childhood development (ECD); counselling on appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices; promotion of kitchen gardens and cooking demonstrations  to ensure adequate physical and cognitive developments; malaria testing and treatment; vaccinations, micronutrient supplementation and deworming to boost immunity; and community engagement to encourage greater utilisation of available services. 
To improve community participation and awareness among caregivers and other community stakeholders, UNICEF will use multiple channels to mobilise communities around key behaviours to prevent undernutrition through network of CNVs (community nutrition volunteers) and MtMSG (mother to mother support groups). 
The cost of delivering this UNICEF nutrition project 345,893 children in South Sudan (SS)at risk of severe acute malnutrition, Vitamin A supplementation for 2.7 million, and MIYCN counselling for 1.7 million PLW. To ensure timely and adequate availability of essential nutrition lifesaving supplies at point of use, the estimated total cost of delivering this UNICEF nutrition project is US$ 76 Million.

project_name: Strengthening Child Protection interventions for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria
project_objective:
In line with the CP Area of Responsibility (AOR) Strategy and the “No Lost Generation” framework, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, including for Survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation as well as children with disabilities, targeting 117 high severity sub-districts (3 to 5) and 38 low severity ones.

UNICEF’s CP Strategy in 2022-2023 includes:
• Addressing behavioural, social, cultural and economic determinants of CP violations as a prevention approach.  
• Improving the reach and quality of specialized CP services
• Capacity development of CP responders
•  Monitoring, evidence generation and advocacy 

UNICEF will support the delivery of integrated programming that will encourage social transformation, prioritizing:
• Structured and sustained CP MHPSS and EORE programmes
• Specialized integrated CP services including case management for survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse (child labour, CAFAAG, child survivors of GBV, child marriages, justice for children, birth registration and unaccompanied or separated children amongst others) 
• Parenting programmes to promote positive child rearing skills and experience for caregivers
• Elimination of violence against children, including GBV prevention and empowerment for girls, boys and women, prevention of violence in schools, homes and communities.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks
• Capacity development of CP responders and social workers

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will embrace new delivery modalities and implement cash transfers aimed at child protection outcomes for vulnerable families. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

CP services will be delivered by partners based on minimum standards and IASC guidelines. 7,200 CP and social workers will be trained on case management, MHPSS, EORE, advocacy, evidence generation and coordination across sectors for a comprehensive CP response.
 
UNICEF will support MHPSS for 364,000 children to benefit from improved mental health and social wellbeing. UNICEF will equip 61,500 parents and caregivers with skills to provide a stimulating and safe environment at home, including reduced violence.  

Violence prevention is a key priority. Family violence prevalence is high for girls 12-17 years (47%), boys 12-17 years (44%), boys below 12 (45%) and girls below 12 (44%) (UNICEF 2018). UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes and communities and providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors. PSEA programming will be implemented with the Protection Sector AORs.

Based on HNO 2021, one in three communities in Syria is reportedly contaminated by explosive ordnance. One in four victims is a child (Joint MA & CP Analysis, 2020). EORE messages will be provided to 1,460,000 children and adults through humanitarian actors and public service providers using static facilities and mobile teams. UNICEF will build the capacity of partners to provide quality EORE that is age, gender and disability appropriate and to provide child victims with assistance.
 
UNICEF will strengthen the justice system to ensure that children in contact with the law victims, offenders or witnesses are protected through child-friendly, gender-sensitive services, that are community-based and family focused.

As Lead Agency for the CP AOR, UNICEF will ensure coordination needs at Hub and WOS levels. Two UN-led and one INGO-led coordination hubs in Damascus, Gaziantep and NES, as well as a WOS overall coordination system, to ensure coherence across the CP response.

project_name: Cash for Winter for vulnerable families in Al-Hassakeh, Aleppo, Rural Damascus, Homs, Hama, Lattakia, Tartous, Deir -ez -Zor, and As- Sweida
project_objective:
The economic collapse and significant reduction in government social spending have plunged additional segments of the population into humanitarian need. MSNA 2022 data indicates that the income gap continues to widen, with average household expenditure now exceeding income by 60%, compared to 49% in 2021. 

The recent record-high level of inflation and energy prices mean that the 2023/2024 winter season will inflict further hardship on families who live in extreme poverty and face social and economic exclusion, such as families caring for children with disabilities (CWD) and female-headed households (FHH). These families will be unable to purchase essential items such as fuel for heating and winter clothes for children. UNICEF PDM surveys show that families caring for CWD fall on average 40% below the MEB. FHH in urban and peri-urban slums live in extreme poverty, with most unable to meet their basic needs; they systematically face greater economic vulnerability than male-headed families. Evidence collected by UNICEF indicate that fuel for heating is a massive burden on families’ budget during winter, representing 10% of families’ monthly expenditure. As a result, most families use negative coping mechanisms. 

To respond to this situation, UNICEF is implementing a Cash for Winter Programme, the main objective of which is to support highly vulnerable families in urban and peri-urban areas respond to the essential needs of their children and help them cope with the growing socio-economic hardship during winter months. The cash assistance will be essential for these families to purchase fuel and gas for heating and cooking, as well as other essential items such as warm clothes.

The programme has two components: (i) three rounds of cash transfers to vulnerable families with children during wintertime (one round every two months between October 2023 and February 2024). Each family receives US$ 60 per round, or a total of US$ 180 during the winter season. The amount is informed by the Cash Working Group recommended value for cash for winter NFIs in 2022 and might be updated in 2023 based on the CWG recommendations; (ii) referral mechanism where the most vulnerable children and their families are accompanied and referred to social services in the communities. This referral component is critical to help families respond to the needs of their children, beyond the cash transfer, thus contributing to strengthen their resilience.

UNICEF 2021-2022 PDM surveys indicated that more than 93% of families reported that food was among the top 3 items they spent cash assistance on, followed by heating fuel (50%), medical expenses and rent (31% each), debt repayment (25%), clothing (19%), education (13%) and toiletries/diapers (10%).
 
In 2023, the project aims to reach 47,000 families (235,000 people, including 117,500 children) with cash assistance and referral services in urban and peri-urban slums in 9 governorates.  

Building on the partnerships established in 2020 with a large network of national NGOs, UNICEF will identify vulnerable families through three targeting methods: (i) geographical targeting, focusing on areas of highest winter severity index (2,3,4) as identified in the NFIs sector winter strategy; (ii) categorical targeting: families with CWD; FHH in urban and peri-urban slums where housing infrastructure has been destroyed and where there is high level of displacement; families with a member with a chronic illness; and families with orphaned children

The programme strategy is in line with the NFI sector result framework 2023. UNICEF closely coordinates with the NFIs sector and the CWG at national and sub-national levels

Accountability to beneficiaries’ is ensured through three main channels: (i) redress and grievance mechanisms; (ii) PDM Surveys; (iii) on-site monitoring.

The project targets 47,000 families in 2023: (i) 17% IDPs, 36% host communities, 47% returnees; (ii) 48% females, 52% males; (iii) 40% of families of CWD

project_name: Lifesaving Wash Emergency Response and restoration of basic WASH services to enhance resilience and to ensure equitable and sustainable access to Water and Sanitation in Syria
project_objective:
The proposed project will help mitigate service degradation due to physical damage to water and sanitation infrastructure in Syria and enhance its climate change resilience. The challenge for the Syrian WASH Sector will be to identify strategic entry points to resume WASH service delivery. If this is not dealt with on time, there will be a ""vicious cycle"" whereby insufficient maintenance services, damage and destruction, and non-delivery of services compound on each other, leading to unrecoverable WASH infrastructure and services. The WASH sector is significantly affected by climate change and environmental degradation, as by the consequences of the current prolonged drought. Each stream of UNICEF’s humanitarian WASH response in Syria presents opportunities to act on climate, energy, and environmental issues to deliver more sustainable results, including addressing the water scarcity crisis. The “vicious cycle” of cumulative impact on all three components (people, hardware, and consumables) during the current protracted armed conflict in Syria may lead to a situation that is too technically difficult or simply too expensive to reverse. UNICEF will therefore repair and rehabilitate critical parts of water supply systems and infrastructure while being guided by the principle of “Minimum reliable services for All – rather than All services for Some”. Several criteria will be used for the project identification and selection, including cost per participant, level of project complexity, neutrality, accessibility, severity scale, number of returnees, quality and quantity of water, and sanitation services currently available.
Most rural and urban areas in Syria are witnessing electricity shortages, which have affected the operation of water systems. Electricity generation has severely declined in 2021 and 2022 and is at its worst levels since the beginning of the crisis. Most wells, water pumping stations, and main water tanks, especially in rural areas depend on diesel generators, which makes them more vulnerable to outages, price gouging, and the inability to Water. Boards to secure the required amounts of fuel to operate wells, water pumping stations, and main water tanks. UNICEF is committed to the longer-term sustainable restoration of water services not only by conducting the rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure but also by using solar power as an alternative solution for the electricity and fuel shortage, where it is possible in affected areas, to ensure the provision of clean water to people in need.
UNICEF will continue providing life-saving WASH interventions, as well as distributing supplies of non-food items related to WASH to the most vulnerable population in Syria. Preparation actions and contingency planning will also be maintained at a high level, together with stocks of necessary materials for responding rapidly to changing needs if access becomes more difficult or mass displacements occur in the northwest and/or northeast Syria. Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA), which is an alternative form of supplying hygiene kits and/or services related to WASH, will be promoted in the northwest. 
The cholera outbreak that started in August 2022 also added to the vulnerability of the Syrian population, especially in the northern governorates.  As part of the Cholera response, UNICEF will ensure appropriate lifesaving WASH prevention and response measures to control the spread of AWD/cholera, with special attention to the at-risk populations and improving IPC interventions at institutions. Also, UNICEF will support awareness raising as an integral part of all projects with a focus on risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) for Cholera prevention. The proposed project aims to reach at least 15,400,000 beneficiaries in 204 subdistricts (72% are high-severity areas) in 2023 which represents 70% of the total population for 2023.

project_name: Provision of Critical Humanitarian Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Services to the conflict affected vulnerable population in Northeast Nigeria (Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe) and other States
project_objective:
UNICEF is both a service provider under the partner presence rationalization in the sector and the provider of last resort (POLR). The largest response is in NE Nigeria (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states) where protracted armed conflict has continued to force displacement of population into camps and camp-like settlements for more than a decade. In other regions, the need for response a rise from sporadic conflicts, natural disasters like floods or risks of outbreaks/spread of infectious diseases such as cholera, which is endemic in Nigeria, and the recent covid-19 or other hazards. Gaps also arise as a results of new population displacements or diminished capacity/departure of other humanitarian WASH partners. As a service provider, UNICEF is optimizing the water production and distribution, increasing attainment of the required minimum standards. UNICEF is rolling out the approach of urban type network water distribution in deep field LGAs with high yielding boreholes and high-density population of displaced persons or returnees and host communities. This approach will support decongestion in camps and expansion of WASH services to schools and health/nutrition facilities. UNICEF will also expand cash in wash programming for hygiene kits and other WASH NFIs. Through this project, UNICEF will have specific target populations in needs in IDP camps and host communities in Borno State, specifically in Maiduguri Metropolitan City and 10 LGAs (Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Jere, Kala Balge, Konduga, Mafa, Mobbar, Monguno, and Ngala), whilst in Adamawa and Yobe, and possibly other states, the target population will be determined by locations where needs will arise. UNICEF will adhere to the SPHERE standards and scaleup the sustenance of the services as needed. 

To meet the demands of the POLR responsibility, UNICEF may need to mobilize additional resources. Through this project UNICEF will provide the initial lifesaving response to fill the gaps, prioritizing areas receiving newly displaced people or under an outbreak of cholera, hepatitis or other WASH-related diseases including covid-19. UNICEF will strive to sustain the basic initial WASH services until further response becomes available from other sector partners. The project is also aimed at sustaining critical humanitarian water, sanitation and hygiene services to displaced population affected by protracted armed conflict in NE Nigeria (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States: target 1,512,786  people) and emergency affected population in three states including other locations.

project_name: Management and Monitoring of Emergency Response, and Enhancing Safety and Security
project_objective:
Management, coordination and monitoring of activities, and deployment of professional staff are essential for UNRWA to deliver timely and effective humanitarian assistance, to ensure efficient coordination with relevant stakeholders and to enhance advocacy on behalf of Palestine refugees.

While the vast majority of posts needed to deliver the mandate of the Agency in Syria will continue to be filled by Palestine refugees and Syrian nationals, UNRWA will maintain some international capacity, particularly specialist staff in the fields of humanitarian response, monitoring and evaluation, and grants management.

UNRWA will continue to conduct safety and security trainings for its staff across Syria, UNRWA has made significant investments in the safety and security of its staff, assets and facilities despite financial challenges. 

Finally, under this project, UNRWA will also sustain the operational needs of support departments, including HR, Administration, Procurement and Logistics. UNRWA has also included a budget for the minor repair and maintenance of UNRWA facilities to ensure safe and functional delivery of services for both beneficiaries and staff.

project_name: Shelter and infrastructure assistance for IDPs, returnees and affected population in Syria
project_objective:

The project is in line with both the priorities of the HRP and 2023 Sector Strategy and the

project_name: Enhancing prevention and response to Protection needs for Palestine refugees
project_objective:
Palestine refugees – already suffering from the humanitarian and socio-economic impacts of a 16-year blockade, and the consequences of recurrent hostilities – were confronted with another round of escalation of violence in August 2022, which left 49 Palestinians dead of whom 17 were children and 360 injured (Source: Ministry of Health).

Repeated exposure to conflict, compounded with the effects of continued restrictions on the movement of persons and goods, has created a mental health crisis in Gaza. According to the MSNA, 40% of households reported having at least one family member suffering from psychosocial distress of trauma. Children are the group mostly affected and a recent MHPSS assessment undertaken by UNRWA identified that 42% of new first grade students show signs of trauma and require intervention. 

The impact of a deteriorating socio-economic situation, including extremely high-unemployment rates and related poverty, has resulted in a rise in cases of GBV including early marriage and domestic violence.

Another consequence of the recurrent hostilities is the presence of explosive remnants of war, which pose significant threat to civilians. According to UNMAS, in 2021 60 people were injured by ERW, and 1 boy killed. Since the beginning of 2022, 12 people, including 7 children have been injured by ERWs. While much of the explosive ordnances from the escalation have been removed, the potential for renewed conflict remains high, giving rise to the need for further Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE). 
To mitigate and respond to the  protection concerns and risk factors arising from the repeated escalation of hostilities , UNRWA will increase protection capacities and response through a series of multifaceted initiatives focusing on MHPSS, Child Protection, GBV and EORE. 
Underpinning the initiatives will be a significant coordination with the Protection cluster and a community-based approach that ensures Palestine refugees are partners in decision making.

project_name: Projet de lutte contre l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle aux populations hôtes, déplacés er retournés de la province du Lac en République du Tchad
project_objective:
Sur le secteur Santé Nutrition, l'action visera l’amélioration de la réduction de taux de sous nutrition à travers des actions spécifiques et sensibles à la nutrition. Les actions essentielles auront pour objectifs l’amélioration de la prévention, le dépistage et l’accès à une prise en charge médico nutritionnelle pour les enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi que le renforcement de la participation communautaire dans la prévention et la prise en charge de la malnutrition pour une pérennisation des interventions.  
Pour le secteur sécurité alimentaire, l’action s’attèlera à apporter une assistance alimentaire d’urgence aux populations par le biais des filets sociaux puis de restaurer les moyens d’existence des personnes déplacées et des population hôtes à travers :
	L’apport d’une assistance alimentaire d’urgence à 1200 ménages (7200 personnes) entre Juin et Août 2023,
	La création d’emploi temporaire à 500 jeunes issus de 500 ménages vulnérables (3000 personnes) via des travaux de Haute intensité en main d’œuvre,
	L’amélioration et la diversification des productions agricoles à 1200 ménages. Cette activité visera aussi bien les déplacés que les populations hôtes. Un travail de plaidoyer sera conduit en amont pour faciliter l’accès à la terre à toutes les personnes ciblées par l’action,
	La protection de l’environnement à travers la création de zones boisées dans tous les villages afin de contribuer la concrétisation du projet de la grande muraille verte en Afrique en général et au Tchad en particulier. Cette activité touchera 1900 personnes au total.
	La reconstitution du cheptel que les familles d’éleveurs avaient perdu pendant la crise. Cet appui va consister à fournir à 400 ménages un kit constitué de 3 têtes de petits ruminants (2 femelles et un mâle), d’aliments bétail (son, tourteaux...). Toutes les têtes d’animaux distribuées seront déparasitées et vaccinées conformément aux normes vétérinaires en vigueur dans le pays. 
	La restauration des moyens d’existence des familles de pêcheurs (déplacés et hôtes) sévèrement impactées par la crise. Cet appui va consister à fournir à 200 ménages (1200 personnes) un kit de pêche selon les standards du cluster sécurité alimentaire et à renforcer les capacités des pêcheurs sur les techniques de transformation et conservation des produits de pêche. 
	L’autonomisation de 2400 femmes et des jeunes à travers des AGR individuelles et collectives et le réseautage des groupements AGR, maraichage et pêcheurs.

project_name: Sustaining Access to Lifesaving Gender Based Violence Prevention and Response Services in BAY States, North East Nigeria
project_objective:
The project seeks to sustain, strengthen and initiate rapid responses in emerging emergencies like flood disasters and secondary displacements due to government IDP camp closures and relocation, to ensure access to quality integrated GBV prevention and response services in the protracted insurgency-affected states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY), Nigeria. This will include the provision of lifesaving multi-sectorial services that will address the medical, psychosocial, legal, livelihood and protection/safety needs of GBV survivors in and out-of-camp IDP, returnees and host communities as well as communities of return to strengthen community protection mechanisms to mitigate and prevent GBV. The project will focus on expanding and maintaining services in safe spaces/shelters and one-stop-centre (OSC)/SARC centres, improving referrals to medical services including clinical management of rape (CMR), strengthening case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) as well as legal and protection services, procurement and distribution of
menstrual, dignity kits, cultural appropriate clothing, and strengthening field coordination, referral pathways and ethical data management. Other complementary activities will focus on strengthening community resilience, tackling harmful practices like child/early/forced marriage and restorative justice through increased engagement of men and boys and addressing GBV in and around schools (SRGBV) as well as promoting GBV/SEA risk mitigation mechanism/AAP in a humanitarian setting. Special emphasis will be put on strengthening joint inter-agency coordination, M&E, capacity building, assessment, monitoring and partnership that will translate to better outcomes.

project_objective:
iMMAP supports the humanitarian actions in Nigeria with quality information management services, which include the complete data management cycle, analysis, capacity strengthening in IM, and other thematic expertise. iMMAP's interventions enable partners to make informed decisions that ultimately provide high-quality targeted assistance to those most in need in Northeast Nigeria.

project_name: Renforcer les services de prévention et de réponse aux filles et garçons les plus vulnérables, en particulier ceux à risque ou affectés par la violence, l’exploitation et les abus ainsi que par la négligence.
project_objective:
L’UNICEF continue de contribuer à la réponse à la crise humanitaire que connait le Burkina Faso. Dans le secteur de la Protection de l’enfant Unicef est à la fois agence lead et acteur de dernier recours, son rôle est important tant dans la réponse que dans la coordination. 

Ce projet permettra aux filles, garçons, jeunes, aux parents, aux professionnels et autres membres des communautés touchées par les violences, d'améliorer les systèmes communautaires de protection de l'enfant et de réduire la violence (y compris les violences basées sur le genre), l'exploitation, la négligence et les abus. 

En outre, ce projet va porter principalement sur la fourniture de services de protection aux enfants et à leurs familles, par à travers la fourniture de services essentiels au niveau communautaire. Ainsi les Cellules Communautaires de Protection de l’Enfant (CCPE), seront rendues fonctionnelles afin de contribuer à la gestion holistique et, de qualité des cas d'abus, de violences, d'exploitation, de négligence et de tous les autres cas de protection qui auront été détectés et documentés via la CPiMS+ et les autres méthodes de collecte de données. Les survivants des VBG et les enfants vulnérables auront accès aux services de réponses de qualité via les prestataires de services qui bénéficieront des formations spécifiques à cet effet. 

Pour répondre aux besoins urgents des enfants, l’UNICEF, à travers ses partenaires de mise en œuvre offrira des services de prévention et de réponse aux besoins des enfants dans les régions du Sahel, de Boucle du Mouhoun, du Nord, de l’Est, du Centre Nord et du Centre Est. En lien avec la stratégie humanitaire de 2023 élargissant la réponse humanitaire sur l’ensemble des 13 régions du Burkina Faso, l’UNICEF, adaptera ses interventions en fonction du choix stratégique des zones affectées. 

Ce projet s’articule autour de trois (03) objectifs à savoir :

1. Le renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection de l’enfant à travers la mise en place des CCPE qui seront impliquées dans les activités communautaires. 
2. La prise en charge holistique de cas VBG, ENA, ES, EAFGA et autres formes de violences à travers un système de gestion de cas efficace et adapté. L’UNICEF et ses partenaires collaboreront avec les acteurs d’autres secteurs humanitaires en vue d’offrir aux enfants vulnérables une réponse holistique basée sur leurs besoins.
3. Le renforcement de l’environnement protecteur, des compétences et des connaissances des adolescents et celles de leurs parents pour diminuer la vulnérabilité.

Inclusive access to education and skills development opportunities for crisis affected Rohingya and host community children, adolescents and youth in Cox's Bazar District
project_objective:
UNICEF education will support access to inclusive early childhood development, pre-primary, primary and secondary education, and skills development opportunities for 244,247 children (51% girls) refugee crisis affected children, and adolescents aged 3-18 years, including 200,067 in the camps and 44,180 in Teknaf and Ukhyia upazilas of Cox’s Bazar District. UNICEF will work with partners to improve enrolment, retention and inclusive learning environment for girls, boys, (with about 2 per cent of the targeted population being children with disabilities). UNICEF in partnership with HI will ensure that inclusion and disability mainstreaming is done across all partners as well as capacitating teachers and communities on how to identify and support children with disabilities and assistive devices provided for. The project will address gender issues by ensuring that girls have better access to learning centers through the girls only sessions, especially from grade 6 onwards where normally girls drop out as they reach puberty.  

In the camps, around 2,800 learning centres will be supported by UNICEF to provide access to progressive learning in safe and protective environment. The capacity of teachers, technical officers and programme officers will be built to enable them to effectively support the delivery of improved learning for 184,320 (50% girls) children aged 3-18 years using the Myanmar curriculum for KG, grades 1,2, 6, 7, 8 and 9. While the Learning Competency Framework and Approach (LCFA) level 3 will end in June 2023 resulting in grade 3, 4 and 5 using the Myanmar curriculum & grade 10. Participation in an accelerated learning programme (ALP) will only be available for children who are significantly too old to be in Myanmar Curriculum grade classes, with the intention of moving children back into different grades within the formal national Myanmar Curriculum as soon as they have made sufficient progress.  ALP will be provided on a needs basis also considering the lack of classroom space and required ALP training for teachers by the curriculum providers. To ensure that children have quality education, UNICEF supports capacity building of partners and teachers/facilitators on inclusive education, basic pedagogy, subject knowledge, assessment, safeguarding & PSEA. This includes rolling out Teacher Professional Development (TPD) programmes to improve the quality of teaching and learning.  To ensure social cohesion and conflict sensitive programming, UNICEF engages & trains teachers from the host community and Rohingya camps as part of the teaching force. The use of education technology solutions will enhance the delivery of education services, including community engagement and administration, as well as contributing to TPD in the camps. UNICEF will also continue to support out-of-school adolescents and youth through cross-sectoral interventions in Multi-Purpose Centres (MPCs) across the camps. Through these interventions, OOS adolescents aged 15 to 18 years will be provided with life & softskills, literacy and numeracy to build their resilience. Youth aged 19-24 also receive TVET training in partnership with the Child Protection team. These skill programmes help to deconstruct gender norms and highlight the values, experience and knowledge of females and males.

In the host communities in Teknaf and Ukhyia, UNICEF will support about 44,180 children, adolescents, and youth, including those with disabilities, to access quality primary education as well as vocational skills. A total of 142 schools with an enrollment of about 44,000 children will benefit from the School Effectiveness grants provided by UNICEF. In addition, support to host community will focus on out-of-school adolescent and youth for vocational skills training and children in non-formal education (ABAL). UNICEF also works closely with the government and ministries at a variety of level, including institutional capacity strengthening in Cox's Bazar district.

project_name: Livelihood income and nutrition improvement (through rural job opportunities, family farming)
project_objective:
Overall, the Food Security Sector (FSS) estimates that 12 million people in Syria are facing acute food insecurity, which is at least 54.4% of Syria population (HNO 2023). While the food insecure figures have slightly declined by at least 4% compared to last year’s record increase, the number of people facing acute food insecurity remains extremely high, pre-Lebanese financial crisis period. Lack of access to livelihood opportunities is a major challenge that most rural households are facing and one of contributing factors that is leading most families to leave their place of residence in search of livelihood opportunities. In this context, FAO has designed a project to assist  68,571 crisis-affected households (equivalent to  411,429 people) in Syria, through support to diversify their livelihoods and income sources and improve their food and nutrition security. This will be achieved through supporting vegetable and poultry production in Syria. 
The overall objective of the proposed action is to improve the food security and nutrition of vulnerable crisis-affected households and the project seeks to deliver the following outputs:
Output 1: Increased household food production (family farming) for 40,000 households.
The output aims to increase vegetable/poultry production of 40,000 vulnerable households (of which 30 % are women-headed) through the provision of full vegetable production packages, which include vegetable seeds/seedlings, and organic fertilizers, or through provision of egg laying hens with feed and vitamins.
Output 2: Increased income generating opportunities through agriculture related livelihood support. The market-driven income generating opportunities include examples such as mushroom production or beekeeping, food processing, etc. for 28,571 households.
This output aims to support  28,571 vulnerable households (of which 30 % are women-headed) to generate income from agriculture related livelihood opportunities  
It is expected that the project support through provision of vegetable and poultry inputs, income generating opportunities and associated training such as business skills and marketing, will diversify the diets of the targeted households and also increase household income and employment creation through the sale of products, for the most vulnerable members of the households, especially for women and youth. It is expected this will lead to improvement of livelihoods, increased local availability of food, increased self-reliance and improved food security and nutrition of crisis-affected households, especially the most vulnerable.

project_name: Improved food security and livelihoods of IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable host communities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of the project is to improve food consumption, food security, dietary diversity and coping strategies and enhance emergency food production of vulnerable populations in the targeted counties. This will be achieved through provision of Cash-Based Transfers (CBT) to address food needs of vulnerable communities during the lean season and provision of timely and appropriate complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits coupled with training in improved agronomic and fishing practices.
In line with the South Sudan FSL cluster HRP objectives and priorities, NPA will support vulnerable populations in IPC 4 and 5 locations as well as some IPC 3 locations. Specifically, NPA will target Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Pochalla and Bor South Counties of Jonglei State, Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre, Cueibet, Yirol East, Yirol West and Awerial Counties of Lakes State, Terekeka County of Central Equatoria State and Kapoeta North County of Eastern Equatoria State.

NPA seeks to support 86,200 HHs (517,200 individuals) through provision of complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits across the target counties. Some of the kits will be provided by FAO (core pipeline) while the rest will be procured and distributed directly by NPA to enhance food production.  NPA will build the capacity of the HHs supported with the kits through training on improved agronomic and fishing practices, marketing and group dynamics. A Training of Trainers (ToT) approach will be utilized whereby lead farmers and fisher folk will be trained by NPA. They will then train/share the knowledge and skills with other farmers and fisher folk in their communities. The kits provided through this project and the knowledge gained from the trainings is expected to improve the agricultural and fishing practices of the target HHs thus enhancing and sustaining food production. CBT interventions will target 1,000 HHs (6,000 individuals ) in Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre and Cuiebet Counties in Lakes State to improve their access to food, diversify and improve their food consumption and dietary diversity scores and promote the adoption of positive coping strategies. The planned interventions are aligned to the FSL cluster objectives 1 and 2 and will provide emergency assistance and livelihoods support to save lives and avert total collapse of livelihoods in the target counties.

NPA will integrate development-oriented and conflict-sensitivity activities in this project to enhance the resilience of  vulnerable HHs in line with the Triple Nexus. Therefore, 1,200 vulnerable HHs will be supported with small-scale cash grants to establish IGAs. The target HHs will be mobilized and sensitized to transition to and establish VSLA’s to ease access to financial services and encourage the spirit of saving among the VSLA group members. The IGAs will contribute to increasing and diversifying income and building the resilience of the target HHs at the same time improving functionality of local markets and boosting the local value chains.

NPA will employ a community-based beneficiary selection approach which will entail establishing Project Management Committees (PMCs) to lead the selection of eligible beneficiaries based on the beneficiary selection criteria. Vulnerable HHs with severe food insecurity including female, child, disabled/chronically ill headed HHs; persons living with or at risk of HIV/AIDS and the elderly will be targeted in this project. 
NPA will ensure meaningful engagement of the target communities throughout the project life-cycle through holding regular meetings with the PMCs and community members and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to get their feedback on the project. NPA will ensure that the feedback is incorporated in the implementation of this project and design of future projects. Further, NPA will use a community-based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide a platform for beneficiaries to voice any issues or concerns.

project_name: Ensuring equitable quality curative and preventive nutrition services while addressing root causes of malnutrition in Ikotos, Torit, Magwi and Lopa Lafon Counties in EES as well as selected counties of Lakes State
project_objective:
The main goals of the project are: to increase equitable and dignified access to quality malnutrition-specific curative services for children and women, while enhancing integrated sustainable preventive measures to halt prevalence of acute malnutrition among children and women in Ikotos Count. 
The specific objectives will be; To increase equitable access and utilization of quality preventative nutrition specific service delivery for children, adolescents and women in Ikotos county by the end of 2023; To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW affected by acute malnutrition in Ikotos county by the end of 2023; To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis and utilization of nutrition information by the end of 2023 and to increase equitable access to nutrition sensitive interventions from health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors through enhanced coordination and joint programming targeting vulnerable groups in prior.
 Nutrition service delivery will prioritize provision of comprehensive and timely community management of acute malnutrition at both Nutrition centres at Boma levels and in hard to reach locations without static centres to access service. The project will as well emphasize on promoting breast feeding and optimal feeding practices among children and women through scaling up of MIYCN counselling services. Nutrition for farmers will focus on raising awareness on the importance of producing and consuming specific food items: households will be sensitized and trained on the use of new vegetables and crops that will be selected together with the communities in a participatory process; focus groups discussions will be held with the farmer groups in order to discuss the importance of diversifying the cultivation for nutrition purposes. With the lessons learnt from compounding effect of COVID-19 pandemic to already existing challenges, several revised/new guidelines, and approaches such as family MUAC shall be adhered and implemented in 203 to ensure continuity of equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services in the context of COVID -19. Given the multi causative contributing factors to malnutrition, the project will ensure existent of operational linkages and joint programming with other relevant sectors such as WASH, health, protection and food security through effectives coordination mechanism that will stimulate integrated approach and dignified access to multi-sectoral basic service which will further reduce prevalence of acute malnutrition and eventually reduce morbidity and mortality among the vulnerable groups (children and women). 
Accountability to affected population (AAP) will be mainstreamed by ensuring that programming of nutrition services approach is community/people centered in such a way that those in needs are fully engaged throughout the program implementation to ensure that the intervention is responsive enough to the arrays of the changing needs. Consideration gender and age variation of the vulnerable groups will be prioritized as well for efficiency of the response more so safety audit will be conducted at every nutrition center to ensure.
