project_name: Integrated response for crisis-affected populations in the Far North Region of Cameroon.
project_objective:
The ongoing conflict between armed opposition groups continues to have widespread impact on communities in the Far North, particularly on their livelihoods and food security, limiting communities’ ability to meet their basic needs and exposing them to various protection risks. The proposed intervention aims to provide direct support to beneficiaries to meet their basic needs across multiple services areas. These include provision of drinking water, promotion of hygiene and sanitation, the restoration of livelihoods, and actions to promote community-based protection and prevent gender-based violence (GBV). This will be done via the following: provide holistic support to survivors of gender-based violence, strengthen the capacity of GBV service providers in case management including MHPSS, strengthen GBV prevention activities at community-level including sensitization of conflict-affected communities, local authorities, traditional leaders, and religious leaders; build the capacity of women led organization (WLO) on GBV response, prevention and coordination in humanitarian context. IRC will also conduct construction of gender-sensitive latrines in IDP sites / host communities, emergency WASH needs assessments, survey, studies and others, promotion of safe hygiene and sanitation practices amongst vulnerable people, capacity-building of WASH actors in WASH relative issues. Furthermore, IRC will be strengthening the process of issuance of civil documentation to conflict-affected people, provide targeted protection assistance to the most vulnerable people (men, women, boys and girls, PWD) and also provide legal assistance to crisis-affected people on the protection of their rights, provision of multipurpose cash as as well as grants for both agricultural and non-agricultural income generating activities. 
The IRC will continue to position itself to respond swiftly to spontaneous movements with mobile services that enable access to hard-to-reach areas in persistent and precarious environments. To support sustainability beyond the project period, the IRC will also continue to reinforce local capacities to ensure a smooth exit strategy.

project_name: Atención básica de salud y nutrición para niños/as y mujeres embarazadas/lactantes en Maracaibo - continuación del proyecto de 2021
project_objective:
Este es un proyecto plurianual ejecutado desde el 01.05.2020 con financiación confirmada hasta el 30.04.2022 y posibilidad de extenderlo hasta mayo del 2024. Todas las cifras presupuestarias, los objetivos y los datos de población meta indicados aquí se aplican únicamente al período de 12 meses del PRH 2022.
Objetivo: Mejorar las capacidades de 3 hospitales y proporcionar atención básica de salud y nutrición a niños/as y mujeres embarazadas/lactantes en Maracaibo.
Contexto y necesidades:
La situación actual de Venezuela es el resultado de una prolongada crisis socioeconómica y política, agravada con la pandemia de COVID-19. Esto ha provocado un colapso de los servicios, el deterioro de las condiciones de vida y desplazamientos masivos. La población es cada vez más pobre y al mismo tiempo la hiperinflación ha provocado un acceso limitado a los alimentos, las medicinas y otros bienes básicos. El resultado es la generalización de las enfermedades, la vulnerabilidad a los brotes epidémicos, la malnutrición y altas tasas de mortalidad.
En Maracaibo, las instituciones sanitarias sufren la falta de personal médico para proporcionar servicios. La infraestructura de salud se está deteriorando; la electricidad y el agua se cortan a menudo durante días. Y conseguir combustible, se vuelve cada vez más difícil y costoso, limitando aún más el acceso de la población a los centros de salud.
Las necesidades de salud y nutrición siguen siendo altas en todo el municipio de Maracaibo y sus alrededores. En segundo lugar, la seguridad alimentaria se está convirtiendo en un problema acuciante para las familias afectadas por un largo período de recesión.  A esto se une la necesidad de proporcionar una ayuda complementaria para la alimentación a la que, sin un ingreso o ayuda de terceros, algunas familias tendrían dificultades para acceder.  Por eso se amplía el programa para intervenir también en las actividades de recuperación de alimentos y en pequeñas iniciativas de producir sus propias verduras, que de otro modo no podrían obtener por falta de ingresos.
Grupo objetivo:
Se ha considerado el marcador de género/edad así como los criterios de vulnerabilidad que están alineados con los datos compartidos por OCHA sobre grupos vulnerables y PIN (personas en necesidad).
- Niños/as hasta 14 años con enfoque en niños/as <5. Sobre todo en asistencia de salud y nutrición.
- A menudo son los niños/as mayores o adolescentes los que cuidan de sus hermanos/as mientras los padres trabajan en el extranjero. Por eso la ampliación del proyecto contempla también a este grupo de edad (adolescentes y jóvenes) que además han quedado sin acceso a oportunidades de vida (estudiar, trabajar). Se les apoya con salud mental y apoyo psicosocial.
- Las mujeres lactantes/embarazadas de la zona de captación de ingresos bajos y medios de los
hospitales, entre ellas un alto porcentaje de madres adolescentes que dependen de los servicios médicos que están cerca y son fácilmente accesibles. Apoyo sobre todo en salud.
- Adultos mayores en las comunidades, a menudo a cargo del cuidado de los niños/as. Apoyo mediante distribución de alimentos y asistencia de salud (asistencia básica y salud mental) a través de visitas del equipo médico que se desplaza a las comunidades.
- Entre estos grupos destinatarios se encuentran aproximadamente el 6% de las personas con discapacidad y el 12,7% de las personas que se reconocen como pertenecientes a la población indígena.
- Teniendo en cuenta la actual pandemia de COVID-19, este proyecto también se dirige al personal sanitario que no tiene acceso a los equipos de protección personal ante contagios, siendo el proyecto la única fuente de provisión de estos elementos.
- Este proyecto también se dirige específicamente a las mujeres como responsables de la toma de decisiones, desarrollando la capacidad de la sociedad civil encabezada por mujeres, incluyendo tres hospitales con una fuerte representación femenina en los puestos de dirección.

project_name: Fortalecimiento del acceso a los servicios de salud con calidad y eficiencia en los establecimientos de salud de la población vulnerable en los estados Miranda, Táchira y Zulia.
project_objective:
Venezuela padece una emergencia humanitaria compleja, desde hace algunos años, producto del deterioro estructural en la economía, sociedad, políticas públicas, aunado los efectos de la pandemia y post pandemia del covid-19 específicamente el sector salud, se encuentra muy afectado, evidenciándose por la escasez de profesionales de la salud, calidad del servicio, falta de medicamentos esenciales, insumos médico-descartables, equipos médicos e infraestructuras deterioradas por falta de mantenimiento. Asimismo, para diciembre 2022, según los reportes de OCHA, en los sectores de salud mental y salud sexual y reproductiva, aún existe elevada necesidad. 
Por lo que es necesario, fortalecer y optimizar los servicios en salud primaria y salud de la mujer, bajo una mirada comunitaria con especial incidencia en atención de servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva y salud mental, los cuales en este momento impacta de forma desproporcionada en la salud de las mujeres de todas las edades durante la edad reproductiva, periodos de embarazo y parto y niñas y adolescentes durante sus etapas de desarrollo.  Dadas estas necesidades, la escasez de calidad aunado a los problemas sociales, se genera situación de violencia basada en género y obstétrica que es vital atender. 

Con la finalidad de fortalecer el acceso a los servicios básicos de salud, garantizar la calidad de estos y responder a las necesidades diferenciadas de la población, haciendo énfasis en la promoción atención y prevención de la salud sexual y reproductiva, a través del presente proyecto se abordarán los siguientes ejes de trabajo:

1.	Fortalecimiento de las capacidades del personal de salud, adscritos a los centros de salud a implementar el proyecto: 
•	Capacitación y actualización sobre, ET, ENT, SSR y VBG, asi como promoción de higiene, basadas en protocolos de OMS, OPS, UNFPA, nacionales, dirigido a médicos, especialista y enfermería. 
•	Capacitación y actualización sobre SMAPS, asi como de primera ayuda psicológica, dirigida a profesionales de la salud especializados o no, basándose en protocolos de la OMS/OPS.
•	Capacitación sobre sistema de vigilancia y registros epidemiológicos, dirigida a personal de salud, basado en protocolos nacionales dictados por el MPPS.
•	Capacitación a personal de farmacia del centro de salud en el manejo de cadena de suministros con esquema estandarizado de LSS/SUMA de OPS/OMS
2.	Fortalecimiento de la prevención y promoción comunitaria en comunidades priorizadas:
•	Capacitación de personas claves de la comunidad, y sensibilizaciones comunitarias sobre ENT y estilos de vida saludables, ET y promoción de higiene, SSR, violencia obstétrica, violencia basada en género, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial. 
•	Sensibilizaciones comunitarias adaptadas para población vulnerable (NNAs, población indígena, comunidad LGBTIQ+, personas con discapacidad). 
3.	Fortalecimiento de la respuesta asistencial de los centros de salud a implementar el proyecto:
•	Dotación de medicamentos esenciales, equipos médicos, insumos médico-descartables, asi como dotar de kits para la atención de parto, cesárea, cirugías menores.
•	Dotación de métodos anticonceptivos. papelería para servicios de epidemiologia y estadística, farmacia y productos de higiene.
•	Rehabilitación y/ reparación de baños situados en áreas priorizadas para el proyecto y sala situacional. 
•	Fortalecer rutas de derivación, así como alianzas para pacientes que ameriten atención más especializada y atención específica de población vulnerable. 
4.	Fortalecimiento de la respuesta a Derechos Sexuales y reproductivos y VBG con enfoque comunitario.
•	Fortalecimiento de vías de atención y remisión de casos de VBG.
•	Actividades de sensibilización comunitaria en torno a derechos Sexuales, derechos reproductivos y VBG, dirigido con énfasis a población vulnerable.  
Se implementarán en 4 centros de salud y 8 comunidades de los estados Miranda, Zulia y Táchira, beneficiando a 23132 personas.

project_name: Strengthening social cohesion in Syria
project_objective: The program’s overall objective is to strengthen social cohesion amongst conflict affected communities in North Syria and contribute to long-term peace and stability of Syria. Strengthening cohesive communities is vital to supporting the stability that is finally emerging in North Syria, and reinforcing post-conflict economic recovery. The combination of improving inter-communal relationships and reducing resource-based tensions will serve to prevent the escalation of some economic-based disputes into violence – for example between host and IDP communities over livelihood opportunities or social service provision – and reduce the ability of political actors to manipulate ethno-religious divisions and mobilise violence. To this end, and in close collaboration with local and neighborhood councils, Mercy Corps will implement community service projects to support local economic development and address resource-based tensions. Mercy Corps social cohesion approach is grounded on a sound context, conflict and conflict sensitivity analysis that supports the identification of viable entry points for strengthening social cohesion within and between communities on different sides of the conflict divide. Mercy Corps supports community members with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to analyze opportunities and impediments to strengthening social cohesion; and to formulate and implement options for strengthening social cohesion at the community level. Through participatory methodology including community mobilization, dialogue, interest based negotiation and the use of sports and creative arts; Mercy Corps will encourage positive interactions between and among community members from across the conflict divide. Mercy Corps will also support conflicting communities to address drivers of conflict through the joint implementation of projects that address resource based conflict drivers. Mercy Corps community mobilization methodology multi-pronged approach to social cohesion Conflict sensitivity is at the heart of all social cohesion activities. The project will develop a conflict sensitivity strategy, guided by various conflict sensitivity analysis tools including the do no harm matrix and stakeholder analysis matrix, building off the findings of context and conflict analysis in the areas of implementation. Mercy Corps social cohesion project will ensure the meaningful participation of all sections of the community with an emphasis on women and youth (male and female).

project_name: Support to WASH services and systems through rehabilitation and capacity building in Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, As-Sweida, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Idlib, Hama, Quneitra and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
In 2022 ZOA implemented projects in multiple sectors including WASH, reaching a total of 185,027 beneficiaries. In 2022 ZOA was able to secure $ 4,185,282 in funding, of which $ 1,313,293 was SHF funding. ZOA was able to allocate $ 2,332,774 for activities under the WASH sector, reaching out to 154,150 beneficiaries. For 2023 ZOA has to date secured $ 2,085,141 with around $ 1.5 million secured for WASH interventions. 

Through the proposed project for 2023 ZOA is estimating to target 244,475 beneficiaries, the cost per beneficiary is estimated to be about $12.  Through this proposal ZOA is aiming at expanding its interventions to reach communities most in need of WASH in underserved conflict affected areas in Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, As-Sweida, Dar’a, Deir-ez-Zor, Idlib, Hama, Quneitra and Rural Damascus. All selected sub-districts fall under scores 3-5 on the severity scale, according to the WASH PiN assessment document shared by the sector, also taking into consideration the activity needs in the selected sub-districts. ZOA’s activities focus on the maintenance and/or light rehabilitation of existing WASH systems, specifically prioritizing activities supporting existing water and sanitation systems, including water quality assurance and rehabilitation of infrastructure. Interventions also include solid waste management activities. The overall objective is to provide support to water and sanitation/sewage systems to ensure regular services for vulnerable households in areas with high severity of needs. With the outbreak of Cholera, ZOA will include Cholera awareness as well as Cholera kits distribution.

ZOA is proposing the following broad activities:
Support to water systems and services: Rehabilitation of water wells will ensure sufficient quantity and quality water for target beneficiaries. Since electricity is a major hurdle ZOA has taken into consideration the provision of solar energy systems wherever possible. The rehabilitation of Bab Al Nayrab sand filtration system in Aleppo (ZOA is preparing the tender documents and implementation will start in 2023).

Support to sanitation/sewage networks: Rehabilitation of damaged sewage pipes to prevent groundwater infiltration as well as sewage leaks which can contaminate the environment.

HH water tanks distribution & installation.

Cholera awareness and Cholera kits distribution.

Solid waste management activities are especially important in light of the COVID-19 pandemic as breathing difficulties can arise from the fungi that develop from garbage that has not been safely disposed of. Solid Waste Management helps to prevent the transmission of bacterial infections at a community level. Here are ZOA's activities to solid waste management systems:

- Community debris and garbage clean-up in target communities
- Provision of communal garbage bins so target communities can safely dispose of their household waste.
- Capacity building of municipalities for operation and maintenance of infrastructure.

The project activities are aligned with the WASH sector: Objective 1: Support water, sanitation / sewerage, and solid waste management systems to ensure regular service for affected people in Syria.

The selected activities are either based on the needs that ZOA team came across during the (evaluation of) activities implemented during 2022, or recommendations by local population, WASH sector and authorities, which ZOA all takes very seriously. Therefore, before the final design of any project ZOA will consult the concerned ministry, local authorities, WASH sector and organizes FGDs with different age groups of the community, so that the activities really serve their needs. During 2022 ZOA has signed MoU with the Ministry of Water Resources, which facilitate and speed up approvals.
 
During 2023 ZOA aims at targeting 371,925 beneficiaries - IDPs 78,925, HC 242,100 & Returnees 50,900; male 164,805, female 207,120; CU5 50,225, children 5-17 82,500, adults18-59 171,900 & Older 59+ 67,300.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire d'urgence pour les populations deplacées internes
project_objective:
Situé entre l’Afrique de l’Ouest et l’Afrique centrale, le bassin du lac Tchad couvre le Tchad, le Cameroun, le Niger et le Nigeria. Important bassin de production agro-pastorale et halieutique, le bassin du lac-Tchad repose sur un écosystème fragile mais avec une production variée et connaissant une démographie croissante. On estime ainsi à 2 million le nombre d’habitants vivant directement des ressources du bord du Lac. 

La Province du Lac est l’une des zones les plus vulnérables au Tchad car difficile d’accès, insuffisamment desservie par les services sociaux de base et sujette de façon récurrente aux effets du changement climatiques caractérisés par les sécheresses et les inondations qui sont parmi les aléas les plus importants. Les conséquences de catastrophes qu’elles engendrent pèsent lourdement sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages. 

La crise dans la Province du Lac a débuté fin 2014 à la suite des premières attaques de groupes armés non étatiques qui ont entrainé des mouvements de populations et bousculé les échanges et équilibres socio-économiques dans cette province, déjà en proie aux effets du réchauffement climatique qui y aggravent notamment l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle. Cette crise qui perdure a causée des pertes en vies humaines, des déplacements forcés des populations, des pertes des actifs productifs, des pressions sur les ressources naturelles et une des articulations de l’économie engendrant ainsi des conséquences sur l’emploi en particulier pour les jeunes.

La dégradation des conditions sécuritaires en raison de l’intensification des attaques des Groupes Armés Non étatiques (GANE) et des opérations de l’armée comme l’attaque de Boma, est la cause principale de la détérioration de la situation humanitaire au Lac, particulièrement dans les départements de Kaya et Fouli qui accueillent les sites les plus importants de populations déplacées. 

Le nombre de personnes déplacées dans la province du Lac est de plus de 239 000 individus en 2022 localisés dans 240 localités dont 186 sites et 54 communautés hôtes (round 18 DTM OIM) avec respectivement 93 291 personnes déplacées dans le département de Fouli, 99 062 personnes déplacées dans le département de Kaya et 47 223 personnes déplacées dans le département du Mamdi. 

Ces événements ont, entre autres, entravé l’accès des populations aux productions vivrières et rentières et affectés les moyens de subsistance de ces populations vulnérables. La situation de cette zone reste préoccupante en matière de sécurité dans les zones insulaires, car le contexte continue d’être volatile et précaire. Suite aux récentes inondations, le nombre de personnes déplacées continue d’augmenter. 

Le PAM planifie appuyer 260 000 personnes déplacées internes avec une assistance alimentaire d’urgence inconditionnelle. Cette assistance alimentaire d’urgence sera adaptée sur la vulnérabilité des ménages déplacés vivant dans les départements de Fouli, Kaya et Mamdi. De plus, cette assistance sera combinée à des activités de prévention de la malnutrition, comprenant un paquet de services intégrés incluant la distribution d’intrants nutritionnels.

project_name: Assistance to IDPs and floods affected population in Chad
project_objective:
Chad faces a combination of rapid-onset and protracted humanitarian crises that have been exacerbated by the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Some 6.1 million people, including 3 million children,2 will require humanitarian assistance in 2023. Armed conflict and intercommunal violence have led to increased population displacements, primarily of women and children, both within the country and from neighboring countries. Chad remains highly vulnerable to epidemics and climatic events, including floods and droughts. It also faces a protracted food and nutritional crisis. Access to essential services remains limited.
UNICEF will provide a timely, coordinated, lifesaving multisectoral humanitarian response in provinces facing recurrent population displacement and other crises.
This project aims at ensuring adequate response for 125,600 floods affected and internally displaced persons (15,933 household NFI kit and 5,000 household through HCT) . The project will be implemented in the most affected zones across the country.  
The necessary budget to carry out the activities is $5,273,100 Without sufficient and timely funding, UNICEF will not be unable to support the national response to the country’s continuing crises.

project_name: Enhanced resilience and protection measures among women and girls at risk of GBV including survivors with disabilities through high-quality multi-sectoral services and community involvements in Gaza Strip and West Bank.
project_objective:
This project aims at supporting women and girls survivors of GBV or those at high risk including women and girls with disabilities through the provision of quality, accessible and acceptable GBV multi-sectoral services in six safe spaces, two women Hubs, and 14 community Women-Led organizations across Gaza Strip and West Bank governorates. Also, the project focuses on promoting the role of grassroots community organizations by supporting their solidarity and community outreach in combating GBV issues, women's rights, and PSEA. The project has three main outcomes:

1- Improved accessibility, availability, and quality of GBV services for 5000 women, girls, men, and boys, with a focus on women and Girls with disabilities, Elderly women, and GBV Survivors in the affected communities in the Gaza Strip and West Bank.

2- Enhanced capacity of 300 GBV governmental and non-governmental specialized and non-specialized service providers on GBV case management, GBV detection and referral, CVA in case management, and PSEA.

3- Increased awareness for 10,000 local communities' members about GBV available services, human rights, cyber-crimes and violence, and the developed standard operating procedures of PESA.


The project is built based on the affected community needs and feedback, considering the vulnerable groups and women and girls at risk, in addition to UNFPA partners' experiences and updates from the field, the established safe spaces, and home visits. Moreover, this project builds on the robust experience and evidence of the importance of CVA in case management as part of the GBV multi-sectoral services to guarantee the protection of women and girls GBV survivors and at risk, and enhance the role of integration, consistency, and coordination between the service providers in the referral pathways. Additionally, the project will meet and cover the needs and requests from other clusters for capacity building about GBV safe referral, PSEA, and CVA for protection, and from the GBV Sub-cluster for advanced and technical services’ capacity building.
Moreover, the project will reflect UNFPA experience and focal points' capacities in PSEA to spread the knowledge and reporting mechanisms, and awareness within all target groups through WLOs and CBOs IPs.

This will be achieved through the following main activities: 
- Build the capacity of MOH emergency staff at emergency centers and also at nearby secondary health care services to be able to deal with emergency early pregnancies, obstetric conditions, and imminent birth, and provide the basic life support techniques in a highly qualified manner.
- Provide an integrated package of SRHR and GBV services within three targeted centers in Area C  including services for women, young girls, and adolescents including people with disabilities.
- Enhance Community outreach on essential SRH service packages e.g. danger signs in pregnancy, family planning, etc. Information on when and how to reach services will also be provided.
- Support three centers (2 in Hebron, One in Ramallah district) with needed equipment and supplies to be able to provide emergency obstetric care per quality standards.

project_name: Addressing GBV in Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to ensure the provision of quality GBV response services to GBV survivors and
women and girls at risk throughout Syria as well as ensuring measures are put in place to
prevent and mitigate the risks of GBV.
Through the WoS approach, UNFPA works with local IPs to support the delivery of GBV services. UNFPA is committed to working with local IPs to contribute to sustainability and to its commitment to localization as part of its adherence to the Grand Bargain. UNFPA will build on its achievements, best and promising practices and lessons learned to continue GBV service provision. UNFPA also aims to enhance the COVID-19 response by adapting and contextualizing modalities for continuity of service provision for women, girls, men, and boys seeking care, based on lessons learned from the past two years. Such service adaptation will include scaling up online platforms to provide GBV prevention and response services and capacity development to service providers. Institutionalized coordination mechanisms in GBV will be leveraged to maximize the impact and quality of service delivery on the ground.

UNFPA’s interventions aim to reach the following objectives throughout Syria:
Service Delivery: Increase the availability of and access to specialized GBV services, including through the provision of CVA, especially for women, girls, and persons with disabilities. UNFPA will continue providing essential lifesaving GBV services and will provide CVA to ensure that women and girls, including persons with disabilities, can access the care they need in some of the most vulnerable areas in Syria. Integrating CVA within GBV programming has been shown to contribute to women’s feelings of safety and self-reliance, their access to health, GBV risk mitigation and response, and their urgent lifesaving needs. The integration of cash assistance within GBV case management has proven to have a positive impact both on mitigating further risk of GBV and on supporting access to a comprehensive package of GBV services aimed at improving resilience and wellbeing of survivors and individuals at risk.

Capacity Building: Improve capacity of service providers and implementing partners to provide high-quality, inclusive, and comprehensive GBV services. UNFPA Syria and Turkey XB will continue to build the capacity of UNFPA partners and, through the GBV AoR, of other GBV actors, in an effort to enhance the quality of GBV services provided and to ensure humanitarian actors are well trained, to reach a wide geographical coverage, and to raise women’s and girls’ concerns, needs, and capacities through advocacy - with special attention on Syrian grass-root organizations.

GBV Prevention and Social Norms: Challenge negative social norms that prevent the empowerment of women and girls and develop accountable models of engagement of men and boys. Through the Turkey XB hub, UNFPA will continue implementing the full scope of the GBV SC prevention program based on the awareness raising toolkit. UNFPA’s IPs will also carry out the full scope of activities under the “Adolescent Mothers Against All Odds” (AMAL) initiative, which has been designed to meet the immediate needs of adolescents girls who are pregnant or first-time mothers, while simultaneously addressing community awareness and engagement. UNFPA Syria’s four-year social norms pilot project in Aleppo will continue.

Coordination: Strengthen leadership and coordination of the GBV response through leadership of coordination mechanisms, building capacity, providing technical support, and enhancing monitoring mechanisms. UNFPA effectively leads the Whole of Syria GBV coordination structure (WoS GBV Area of Responsibility (AoR), supporting the GBV coordinators in Syria and Turkey XB hubs, as well as the NGO lead of the NES GBV sub-working group. UNFPA Syria will continue to coordinate the GBV sub-sector, while UNFPA Turkey XB will continue to lead the GBV SC.

project_name: Enhancing access to SRH services to vulnerable Lebanese, Palestinian refugees, and migrant women and adolescent girls across Lebanon
project_objective:
UNFPA & its partners will focus on quality life-saving SRH interventions targeting 250,000 vulnerable, Lebanese, Palestinians & migrant women, men, boys & adolescent girls. Migrants and people with disabilities will be targeted in all interventions. Most vulnerable women will be reached through mobile teams well versed and engaged at community level. UNFPA will ensure technical support, guidance and monitoring of the following proposed interventions 

A-Promoting SRH service delivery by:
-Enhancing quality of maternal care through a series of training sessions to 1500 health
care providers on SRH topics including emergency obstetric care & high risk pregnancies. This is essential considering the recent migration of health workforce
-Procurement of RH drugs & commodities to 130,000 men, women and adolescent girls accessing MOPH PHC network & dispensaries located in remote & poor areas in order to avail RH commodities to the increasing number of vulnerable Lebanese, Palestinians,and migrants accessing these heath facilities. Based on MOPH PHC data for 2022 there has been an increase of 24% in SRH services with a total number of around 350,000 beneficiaries. MSNA findings also expose the shift of patients from private to public sector with more than 50% of surveyed people reported not being able to pay the cost of medication
-Community mobilization and awareness raising on health integrated messages with focus on SRH through engagement of 80 midwives & outreach workers who will promote health seeking behavior among 80,000 women and adolescent girls with referral to care as needed. 25000 dignity kits will be distributed during awareness sessions. The MSNA findings reveal that one quarter of surveyed pregnant women/ mothers did not receive appropriate ANC; and MOPH PHC data shows that only around 10% of new mothers receive Post natal care. The limited access to RH cancer preventive services is alarming and requires prompt action to mitigate the risk of increased incidence
-Provision of SRH Services namely 1) midwifery care for vulnerable women with high risk pregnancies. Data collected about midwifery home care conducted in 2022 shows that 50% of women in need for support presents in their third trimester and the most encountered cases are hypertension, pre-eclampsia, threat of premature birth, diabetes and anemia. Prompt support to these cases would avert maternal and neonatal mortalities and morbidities. 2) Medical consultation through Tele-health with referral to additional services as needed. The increased transportation costs hinder access to care hence availing medical consultation via tele-health present an opportunity for enhanced access to care for the most vulnerable groups. 3) Coverage of advanced diagnostics to high risk pregnancies which will guide the care plan and help reducing maternal morbidities 
B-Enhancing rapid response for PLWs through:
-Engaging a medical team of OBGYN trained specialists to ensure 1) technical support for the community midwives and primary care level health care providers as needed; 2) facilitation and support referral for hospitalization/ emergency OBGYN care for vulnerable women under various projects; 3) Provision of medical consultations through tele-health to vulnerable women and critical cases
-Engaging midwives to ensure 1) awareness raising on SRH including ANC/PNC, Family planning, covid19 vaccination etc; 2) identification and support to high risk pregnancies including home care visits & referral to further care as needed 3) linkages with the OBGYN specialists response team to ensure early response as needed, support transfer of cases to health care facilities as needed
C-Mainstreaming protection for the most vulnerable women and adolescent girls through:
-Capacity development on GBV safe identification and referral to health care providers, sensitization training on clinical management of rape for health &GBV actors and training on GBV/SRH integration to care providers.

project_name: Safe Enabling Learning Environments: A Shared Responsibility
project_objective:
•	Deterioration of Families’ Economic Conditions
The economic, financial, political, and pandemic crises in Lebanon, have affected every aspect of children’s lives, including education, nutrition, and mental health. According to the assessment “Children’s future on the line” conducted by UNICEF on June 2021, nine per cent of families sent their children to work, 15 per cent stopped their education, and 60 per cent had to buy their food on credit or borrow money.
The outlook of the future is grim. The World Bank says the economy looks likely to contract by a further 9.5 per cent in 2021 and has warned that there is “no clear turning point in the horizon” (Lebanon Economic Monitor, Spring 2021). The longer children in Lebanon are out of school, the higher the possibility that they will experience violence and exploitation, including child labor and child marriage. The increasing socio-economic pressure on families in Lebanon during the economic and COVID-19 crisis, increases this possibility. The increased pressure on children to support their families may lead to an increase in psychosocial distress and negative coping mechanisms.
•	Migration from Private to Public Schools
In the scholastic year 2020-2021, around 54,000 students transitioned from private to the public schools. MEHE estimates that another 50,000-60,000 Lebanese students will transfer from private to public schools during the SY 2021/2022, resulting in 100,00- 120,000 Lebanese students migrating to public schools. This will pause additional challenges to an already stressed system. A hiring freeze of teachers in public schools has been in place for around 2 years. With the rapid increase in number of students in public schools, human resources are required to match the demand. However, due to the unprecedented diminishing value of the LBP, teacher salaries in the public system are now valued at less than 1 USD per hour, which is pausing yet another serious risk of teachers leaving the schools or be on strike more often.
The purpose of this project would be to provide direct community support measures to most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant children to retain them in education and to ensure that students affected by the economic crisis are provided relevant, inclusive and quality education adhering to national and international standards on education in emergencies and child protection by ensuring that schools have maintained their basic educational resources, including adequate human resources. Ana Aqra is suggesting the “Safe Enabling Learning Environments: a Shared Responsibility” project as part of the Lebanon emergency response plan.
Aqra strives to make learning accessible to all children and works to support the education sector and the public school to respond to the specific needs of all children as well as empowering partnerships to partake in the responsibility for the safe and enabling learning of girls and boys.

Targeting criteria, intervention and mechanism:
This project will support 10,000 girls and boys and 75 public schools, including those receiving learners transferred from the private sector. The project activities will include provision of funds to ensure that students affected by the economic crisis are provided relevant, inclusive and quality education adhering to national and international standards on education in emergencies and child protection. The project will also ensure that schools will receive necessary stationery, books, and funds to cover operational costs and adequate human resources. It will also ensure school retention of most vulnerable girls and boys by providing them and their caregivers with direct community support program, including remote awareness sessions, remote PSS/SEL activities, responsive caregiving and remote basic and digital literacy to parents /caregivers, assistive technologies for children with disabilities, cash for education support and food parcels during the academic year 2022-2023.

project_name: Protection et Assistance multi sectorielle pour les réfugiés au Tchad
project_objective:
Au 31 décembre 2022, le Tchad accueille 1,1M personnes déplacées de force, dont : 597,728 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile principalement du Soudan (68%), de la République Centrafricaine (22%), du Cameroun (7%) et du Nigeria (4%) ainsi que ainsi que 381,289 PDI et 101,551 retournés dans la Province du Lac et RCA au Sud. Toutes ces personnes forcées au déplacement sont installées dans les camps, sites, villages et certaines villes. Le HCR opère dans un contexte géographique empreint a une conflictualité grandissante provoquant des déplacements internes, des mouvements des refugies vers le Tchad à la recherche de la protection internationale, des mouvements mixtes et secondaires avec des risques de violations du caractère civil et humanitaire de l’asile et des sites et. A titre illustratif de janvier à juillet 2022, plus de 1200 refugies initialement enregistres au Tchad ont été identifiés dans des mouvements secondaires irréguliers dans la région de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre et en dehors de la région. Cette tendance est du fait de la détérioration de la situation humanitaire, de la fragmentation des mécanismes de protection et de la crise de sécurité alimentaire. Malgré ces défis, le Tchad a continué à démontrer une hospitalité en faveur des refugies et travailler dans le sens de la mise en œuvre des engagements pris en marge de la Déclaration de New York et lors du Forum Mondial sur les Refugies qui visent à assurer une inclusion des refugies dans les programmes de développement de l’Etat, l’intégration des refugies dans le système éducatif national ainsi que la reconnaissance des écoles et centres de santé dans le système national en vue de l’autonomisation des refugies et des communautés hôtes. Dans le but de créer un environnement favorable et de rendre effective l’inclusion et l’autonomisation, le Tchad a adopté en décembre 2020 une loi sur l’asile qui consacre la jouissance par les réfugiés des droits civils ainsi que les droits économiques, sociaux et culturels y compris le droit à l’emploi. Même si la situation de transition politique a quelque peu ralenti les efforts déjà entrepris à cause d’une re-priorisation des interventions, il devient urgent de renforcer les projets de développement en accord avec le Gouvernement du Tchad et les partenaires techniques et financiers et de continuer à fournir l’assistance et la protection en vue de la résilience des refugies et de leurs communautés d’accueil. C’est dans cette veine que le présent projet vise à fournir un environnement favorable de protection et d’assistance d’une part et à rechercher de solutions d’autre part au profit des réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile, déplacés internes et les communauté hôte au Tchad avec comme fondement des projets visant la résilience et l’autonomisation. Pour y parvenir une approche a phases interdépendantes sera adoptée :
•	La stabilisation de la situation des réfugiés nouvellement arrivés dans une localité à travers le déploiement d’un paquet minimum de protection et d’assistance, la définition des activités visant leur résilience conformément a la loi d’asile au Tchad, d’autres instruments juridiques pertinents et aux standards internationaux
•	L’inclusion des refugies dans les programmes de développement de l’Etat et dans les filets sociaux de l’Etat et d’autres partenaires en vue de leur autonomisation, gage d’une villagisation effective et réussie
•	La recherche et la mise en œuvre des solutions durables dont le rapatriement librement consenti
Ces priorités seront mises en œuvre par le biais des instruments comme  le nexus humanitaire-développement, le partenariat diversifié, la centralité de la protection dans un environnement caractérisé par l’existence de processus de coordination intergouvernementale notamment, le Processus de Bamako, la Plateforme de soutien pour la recherche de solutions aux déplacements forcés issus de la crise centrafricaine consacrée par la Déclaration de Yaoundé, la Déclaration d’Abuja.

project_name: Access to lifesaving mental health services in Lebanon
project_objective:
Lebanon has been facing hardship on the social, political and economic levels since October 2019, which has led to a severe deteriorxation of living circumstances. The situation continues to decline to date and in a recent report published by the World Bank in May 2021, Lebanon was described as going through a “deliberate depression” that is expected to impact the wellbeing of residents directly and severely, and therefore raised the alarm on the importance of delivering essential public services (Lebanon Economic Monitor, 2021). Today, there are no recent studies measuring prevalence of mental illness in Lebanon, however the increasingly stressful living conditions are expected to translate in the disruption of wellbeing, increase in the rates of depression and anxiety, and decrease in the ability to access mental health services, leading to longer delays in treatment and therefore increased morbidity. The rate of death by suicide in Lebanon continues to average one person every 2.1 days and suicide attempt rates are estimated at once every 6 hours (Bizri et al., 2021). The availability and usage of mental health services in Lebanon faces numerous challenges, including stigma, absent government funding, reliance on restricted national and international funding, sky rocketing costs of mental health services without third party coverage, limited psychiatric units in public and private hospitals, and a critical shortage of mental health professionals. Living conditions and access to mental health services is particularly more difficult to  vulnerable Lebanese, migrants and PRLs. 

Under its mandate to provide quality mental health services, and aligned with the sector objective to ensure access to life- saving and life- sustaining health services for the most vulnerable, Embrace proposes strengthening and sustaining the operations of its two major programs the National Lifeline and the Embrace Community Mental Health Center EMHC that work to serve all individuals and are particularly crucial to the quality of life of vulnerable Lebanese, migrants and PRLs. 
The National Lifeline (1564), launched in collaboration with the National Mental Health Program NMHP provides over the phone support 24/7 to any individual experiencing emotional distress or suicidal ideation. Using a volunteer-based model, the Lifeline trained operators provide callers with emotional support, suicide risk assessment, de- escalation, collaborative problem solving, safety and action planning and orientation to mental health and livelihood related services as needed. The Lifeline has been sign-posted in national psychological response action plans, adapting its operations to the diverse distresses faced nationally. Additionally, the Lifeline plays a role in providing integrated and accessible mental health messaging tackling the barriers preventing individuals from seeking mental health services which include social stigma, negative attitudes, and lack of knowledge of available resources through national campaigns and outreach efforts with front-liners and communities. To complement the life- saving services the National Lifeline offers, Embrace in collaboration with the NMHP launched the National Mental Health Emergency Response Mechanism NMHERM. This unit is a field operation dispatching a psychiatrist and psychiatric nurse to respond to mental health crises and/or suicide attempts with medication administration and hospital admission as needed. The Embrace Mental Health Clinic, launched in 2020, offers fully funded psychiatric and psychological consultations and financial support for relevant medical costs including psychotropic drugs and inpatient administration. Simultaneously, the clinic hosts a graduate psychology training program for students completing their final year of education to build their capacity in practical skills. In this way, the students are offered affordable training sites and are part of cost- effective mental health interventions.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving nutrition information and services to address malnutrition for vulnerable children under 5 years, under 2 years, and PLW among IDPs, returnees, and host communities in Khartoum, South Darfur, East Darfur, South Kordofan, Kassala, Al-Gezira, Gedaref states
project_objective:
This project is designed to improve lifesaving and equitable access to nutrition information and services to address malnutrition for vulnerable children under 5 years, under 2 years, and PLW among IPDs, returnees, and host communities and build resilience among girl, boys and PLWs through multi sectoral preventive response. The total target beneficiaries are 240,000 individuals (47039 men, 48960 women, 73441 girls, 70560 boys). To reduce catastrophic levels of acute malnutrition, CARE will operationalize Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Supplementary Therapeutic Programs (STP) centers, mobile nutrition sites, and Stabilization Centers to offer improved lifesaving preventative and curative nutrition services to malnourished and acutely malnourished children. Through an improved and effective referral pathway, Children under 5 and children under 2 with acute malnutrition, and malnourished children with medical complications will be further referred and admitted receiving quality inpatient care in the stabilization centers. To strengthen the link between target communities and the integrated health and nutrition facilities, community outreach will be in engaged in delivery of this programme. Mother support groups (MSGs) and community nutrition volunteers (CNVs) will be trained to improve Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and provide consoling to caregivers addressing the rout causes of malnutrition and improving children and PLW nutritional status. Also, these groups will raise community awareness through home visits for screening and active case finding and deliver integrated health and nutrition social behavior change (SBCC) approach. Also, nutrition workers and community nutrition volunteers will be trained on (CMAM), PSEA, sensitization protocols and GBV risk mitigation through screening, referral, and treatment. Nutrition services will be coordinated with WFP, UNICEF, and SMOH to ensure provision of adequate food supplies, RUTF, RUSF, and MNP to prevent, treat and improve access to nutrition services especially during time of critical food insecurity all over the state. 
Under current crisis, CARE will provide Nutrition services to additional 75, 259 individuals (14,470 Men, 15,373 women, 23,060 girls, 22,156 boys) through to provide nutrition lifesaving services to under 5 years children and PLW among IDPs, refugees, returnees and host communities in the impacted States by the conflicts in South Darfur, East Darfur, South Kordofan, Kassala, Gedaref states, Khartoum State and Al Jazirah State through nutrition services.

project_name: Protection Response for Vulnerable Lebanese and Other Resident Populations
project_objective:
According to OCHA, approximately 393,000 people across 26 districts are in need of GBV services in 2022, a significant increase from 67,000 people in need in the 2021 ERP. Around a quarter of Lebanese households reported having safety and security concerns for women in their community (OCHA, 2022). The GBVIMS shows that in the last quarter of 2022, the most common types of GBV incidents were physical assault and emotional abuse mostly happening in the context of intimate partner violence, followed by forced marriage. Protection risks for all targeted populations remains high, with women and girls facing significant risks of multiple forms of GBV. The economic insecurity combined with different levels of crisis affecting the country as well as risks related to legal status, add to these vulnerabilities. Shortage in electricity and increased transportation and telecom prices all act as contributing factors to different forms of GBV in all locations. Sexual harassment through online platform and cyber abuse is an emerging GBV trend. Another alarming trend is the increased rates of sexual exploitation by landlords and employers especially affecting female heads of households with financial vulnerability.  Preventing, mitigating, and responding to GBV in emergencies is a lifesaving priority and an essential component of humanitarian action, especially in a country with extreme structural gender inequalities. 

The below proposed activities focus on survivor-centered care with case management teams working to meet the immediate, lifesaving needs of women and girls while laying the groundwork for survivors of GBV, their families and their communities to recover. Under the GBV prevention component, the project will be providing dignity kits to 3000 beneficiaries and awareness raising sessions to 2500 non-unique beneficiaries. There will be an overlap of beneficiaries attending awareness sessions and receiving dignity kits. Also, 120 men will receive men engagement activities (Cycle of Violence), and those are already counted under the awareness sessions target. The COV is composed of three sessions including: Life and daily stressors, Violence and How to deal with stressors. 
Aim of the sessions:
 During the dire economic situation in the country, the team will look at the effects of the family on this period, and its goal is the ability to mitigate its effects on both, society and family. 
 In the three sessions, the team will discuss together with the men about the stress and frustrations of the situation as well its effects on the family members and their reactions towards it in a positive or negative way.
Under the GBV response component, IMC will be providing focused PSS groups for 300 beneficiaries as well as GBV case management (including emergency cash assistance). IMC will also provide non-focused PSS for 500 unique beneficiaries (which overlap with the focused PSS activities as well as the dignity kits beneficiaries). IMC will provide the services in three safe spaces in Akkar, Beirut and South. GBV department is well established in these areas with well-trained case workers and social workers.

Based on IMC’s presence in the different areas proposed under this project, the objectives of the ERP directly address the needs of the communities especially vulnerable women and girls. IMC will organize empowerment activities for women and girls and will engage with men as allies to prevent GBV. IMC will coordinate with local actors, authorities, and other sectors to strengthen GBV prevention and response and will continue working with communities to shift social norms that contribute to GBV and threaten the protection and wellbeing of women and children.

project_objective:

Este apoyo se brindará en el marco del subgrupo de evaluaciones y en los demás que sea pertinente, en aras de armonizar las evaluaciones rápidas y en profundidad y presentar resultados, realizar seguimiento de la respuesta humanitaria con atención al aporte de capital humano en el apoyo a las evaluaciones en el marco del B2B. La gestión de la información es un componente clave de la coordinación eficaz. 
La arquitectura humanitaria en Colombia, incluyendo el EHP y el GIFMM, cuenta con tres o incluso más instrumentos multisectoriales para la identificación rápida de necesidades. Esto hace que la coordinación en el territorio sea más compleja en cuanto a qué tipo de instrumento debe aplicarse. A nivel de coordinación y análisis, la comparabilidad de las metodologías, los indicadores y los resultados se hace difícil. 
La coordinación y la gestión de la información son esenciales para que la asistencia humanitaria se preste de forma cohesionada y con éxito. Una acción humanitaria eficaz requiere información oportuna y fiable sobre la situación, el número de personas (potencialmente) afectadas, la exposición a los riesgos y amenazas de las catástrofes naturales, etc., todo lo cual es importante para la aplicación eficiente y eficaz de los recursos disponibles.

project_name: Education in Emergencies in Syria
project_objective:
The war in Syria continues to have a profound impact on people across the country and at least half of the people affected by the crisis are children. The humanitarian situation in the country remains severe as the decline of the economic situation exacerbates the effects of the conflict. The education sector is impacted by low availability of education services, few functional schools, shortage of teachers, extremely low teachers' salaries. The targeted areas are expecting large numbers of returnees to further stretch the education sector’s capacity. The impact of the COVID19, Cholera, rapid devaluation of the Syrian Pound and the international sanctions are putting additional strain on the population and local administrations. 
According to the HNO 2023, at national level average, self-reported attendance of the children between 6-17 for the 2021-2022 academic year was 88% with 12% reported to be non-attending, while in Idleb it reaches 15%, in Raqqa – 25%, in Aleppo – 16%. Attendance starts to decline from 11 years old at steeper rate for boys through their teenage years. The main reasons why they do not send their children to any form of learning 48% of households cited those economic related issues were the most prominent reason why children were not in school, 27% of households reported that schools were not able to accommodate the child/ren’s.
Thus, FCA projects are focusing on the pockets of low attendance to schools and offers tailor made solution specific per area.
All of the areas that FCA program is covering area are marked as 4 or above on the severity scale. Most of the target location are newly opened returnees areas with the high demand for education services and often presence of operational schools is a motivating factor for the families to return to the area. 
The project directly contributes to HRP priorities both in terms of geographical prioritization and by combining soft (non-formal education, protection etc) and hard components (school rehabilitation, school furniture, students kits etc)  in education focusing on quality education. 

Access to education related activities: 
1.1.	Rehabilitation of schools including ECE rooms (inc. solar power), prefab classes in the locations where schools are damaged and can't be rehabilitated.
1.2. Provision of NFE through remedial and catch-up classes
1.3. Distribution of Student's kits and winterization items
1.4. Back to learning campaign
1.6. Piloting Homegrown School Feeding program
1.7. Transport support for TVET students

WASH related activities 
2.1 Rehabilitation of water supply
2.2. Rehabilitation of the WASH facilities for boys and girls -latrines  
2.3. Water trucking to schools when necessary as an emergency support mode
2.4. Provision of personal hygiene kits (especially for girls) and school hygiene supplies
2.5. Responding to cholera outbreak, provide access to clean water in school and hygiene education. 

Protection related activities: 
3.1. Protection events in schools
3.2. Establishing and supporting school based protection committees and PTA and mobilizing communities through the Community Led initiative methodology
3.3. Recreational activities in schools
3.4. Psychological support for teacher

Quality of Education related activities 
4.1. Equipping schools with furniture and teaching and learning materials.
4.2 Teachers' training
4.3. Support for children with disabilities through aids and teacher training.

Efforts will be made to link parents of OOSC to the livelihood program of FCA or other partners in the area.

M&E Framework is used to ensure that stakeholder opinions are heard. Activities will be directly monitored by FCA field staff under the supervision of the Education PM. 2 M&E staff will be responsible for the monitoring of results, activities, and indicators. The data have been collected during the NA conducted in June-Nov 2022; in the beginning of the project FCA team will collect baseline data for each indicator as per the LF.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving WASH support for the conflict affected populations in South Idlib, Hama, Rural Damascus and Dar’a in Syria
project_objective:
TGH’s intervention is closely in line with the 2022-2023 WASH HRP Objectives 1, 2 and 4, as TGH aims to contribute to life-saving WASH interventions and support the resilience of existing WASH systems by addressing the needs of people affected by the conflict in Syria, coupled with the deteriorating context due to the COVID-19 pandemic and worsened by hyperinflationary economic crisis, including the new rise of AWD/Cholera outbreak in Syria.
According the draft WASH 2023 HNO report that 13.55 million require WASH assistance in Syria with 52% of the population is relying on often unsafe alternatives to piped water with at least 70% of sewage is discharged untreated and at least half of the sewerage systems are not functional, overall WASH in School needs are growing to 56% of students complained to their parents about WASH-related issues - with poor hygiene conditions affecting overall enrollment and especially girls’ attendance.
The intervention will be integrated intervention in covering WASH, Education and Shelter activities with protection, gender, and environmental issues mainstreamed. This intervention will be focused on 4 areas: South Idlib, Hama rural areas (Sub Districts: Eastern Bariy, As-Saan), Rural Damascus and Dar’a rural areas. The targeted areas were selected based on their accessibility, the severity of their needs varying between 3 and 5 as per the draft WaSH 2022 HNO, TGH field assessments during 2021 and consultations with Water authorities, SARC, local authorities and municipalities.
The proposed intervention has been designed based on TGH 4-year experience in implementing WASH projects (with a specific emphasis on WASH-in-school interventions) in Syria. TGH follows a multi-sectorial programming approach that relies on complimentary multi-donor funding to ensure comprehensive coverage, addressing a broad range of critical humanitarian needs that exist in Syria, including WASH, Shelter and education. The intervention will target 260,984 individuals (129,044 female and 131,940 male, 101,784 aged 0-17, 146,151 aged 18-64, 13,049 aged +65). 20% of the budget is already secured for the planned WASH activities in 2023.
In line with Objective 1, activities 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, TGH will propose intervention that will include:
• In 2023, TGH will commence rehab 8 boreholes equipped with solar system, rehab 3 water networks, support Water quality test for targeted water supply systems, capacity of building to water authorities technical staff, distribution of 500 water tanks 1m3 at household’s level, and rehabilitation of 3 Sewage network.
As part of Objective 2, activity 2.1, 2.2, and Objective 4, activity 4.1, and in line with Education Sector objectives, TGH will propose intervention will include:
• In 2023, TGH will commence rehab WASH facilities in 7 schools in order to secure the access to water for drinking and hygiene purposes and ensure excreta evacuation to increase measures against infection, prevention and control both at school and at home in Idlib, Hama, Rural Damascus, and Dar’a . The intervention will be part of an integrated approach with Education HRP.
• In 2023 TGH will target 7 schools to distribute of hygiene kits and soap to students.
• Provision of emergency WASH services, including response to COVID19 and Cholera outbreak according to need in 2023.
As part of its activities, TGH puts a specific emphasis on abiding by protection principles through providing gender and disabled friendly WASH facilities in schools taking into account menstrual needs, including doors lockable from the inside and lighting. TGH will also ensure to provide WASH facilities accessible for children with disabilities.

project_name: Improving children’s access and learning in the most vulnerable schools in Gaza
project_objective: The proposed project is in line with the education cluster HNO strategic objectives 1, 2, and 3, and is aligned with the MoE Education Strategy Plan. The project aims to ensure that boys and girls have equitable safe access to inclusive and quality educational services in vulnerable MoE schools in Gaza Strip (East Khanyounis, Rafah, Gaza, and North Gaza). This project fits under a multi-year NRC strategy to ensure that children will be bridged with formal education, have safe access to education and contribute to create safe learning environments mainstreaming psychosocial support throughout the whole intervention. NRC will regularly coordinate with education partners and be part of the Strategic Advisory Group in Gaza. The intervention will focus on: i) Psychosocial support to help strengthen protective factors for children. The psychosocial intervention is delivered through NRC’s flagship Better Learning Programme (BLP) curriculum, providing support to the Ministry of Education on creating an additional capacity with a cohort of BLP Master Trainers; provision of capacity building of teaching and non-teaching staff in MoE schools; provision of emergency kits to schools; awareness sessions for parents on the importance of mental wellbeing; and provision of a “Supporting the Supporter” package for teaching and non-teaching staff. ii) Strengthen first phase responses supporting MoE and schools on the development and adoption of contingency plans; creation of NRC emergency team to be able to respond to emergency situations. iii) No-formal education interventions (remedial classes an catch-up classes) to bridge out of school children with formal education or support children who have experienced prolonged learning loss and tackle drop-out in formal schools. In the event of no access, NRC will adopt blended modality through digital platforms to keep children engaged and provide continuous learning.  iv) Provision of technical support to education sub-cluster in Gaza through as co-lead in the Strategic Advisory Group. v) Conduct situational analysis on OOSC needs, gaps and priorities, as well as contributing in enhancing their access to quality basic education. vi) Conduct a situational analysis on adolescent/youth needs and priorities, in addition to contributing in enhancing vulnerable youths’ empowerment and skills, capacity and resilience development. The action is also contributing in improving both skills and knowledge of teaching and non-teaching staff on PSEA principles.  During the intervention, gender inclusion will be mainstreamed throughout the project providing information sessions to parents on the importance of education for boys and girls, promoting gender balance in the activities, tackling gender barriers in coordination with parent and teacher associations, teachers and school principals. NRC will work towards an inclusive education programme with attention to children with disabilities coordinating with specialised partners such as Humanity and Inclusion to conduct regular assessments on how to improve access to education for children with disabilities, trainings for teachers and sessions for parents' engagement.

project_name: Child Sensitive Emergency Multi-Purpose Cash-Plus and Shock Responsive Social Protection Strengthening Programme in the State of Palestine
project_objective:
UNICEF will implement 3 main activities: 1) Emergency MPCA to highly vulnerable households within one month after the crisis to address critical and essential needs to save lives;  2) provide at least 3 months of MPCA to highly vulnerable families affected by the crisis to meet their multiple basic needs to enhance safety nets and protect assets; and  3) facilitate referrals (Cash plus), that is vulnerable households with specific needs are referred to Cluster sector specific cash intervention. A fourth activity that this project contributes to is  systems strengthening for the National Cash Transfer Programme drawing upon lessons learnt. 
 
UNICEF will provide graduated cash payments to targeted households to build lessons to feed the capacity building of the national social protection system. Targeted households will receive graduate payments based on the number of children in the household. The payment value for the households will be aligned to the Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (NIS 754) for activity 1 and Minimum Expenditure Basket (NIS 1,080) for activity 2 as defined by the Cash Working Group. UNICEF will also have a referral or cash plus component that will refer beneficiary households with children in need of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support to Child Protection partners for support and follow up. Beneficiary households in need of services available through the Gaza Protection Consortium (Disability Rehabilitation, MHPSS) will be referred to them and other service providers, if there is sufficient capacity, using existing cluster-based Protocols and Guidelines. UNICEF and GPC have a programmatic mutual working relationship given that they currently have received funds from the same donor where indicators between the agencies have been harmonized and they are currently working together to strengthen referrals across UNICEF and the GPC agencies hence UNICEF will capitalize on this existing relationship further to strengthen synergies

The UNICEF cash programme uses a two-pronged approach for addressing both immediate and mid-term needs of children living in poor and vulnerable households. The referral or ‘cash-plus’ approach provides immediate support to children living in poor and vulnerable households  to meet their basic needs (based on gender and age requirements) as well as connecting them to a package of essential services, while the systems strengthening of the national social protection system offers a pathway to protect vulnerable households with children in the medium-to-long term but at the same time strengthening the national system to be shock responsive and adaptive. UNICEF will also make efforts to refer households with potential to available economic empowerment and livelihoods activities to ensure self-reliance by the targeted groups, which is one of the sustainable exit pathways.

The main eligibility criteria for the programme are that a household should be living below the poverty line and have children between 0 – 17 years, and should be shock or crisis impacted. The prioritization criteria will include:  
o	Households affected by an acute shock
o	Households with children with disabilities (CwD)
o	Female and Child-Headed Households
o	Households with PwD which have children 
o	Households with chronically ill member(s) which have children 
o	Households with children of school going age (in and out of school)
o	Households with children who are at risk of falling/sliding back into the negative side of the  CSI, rCSI, FCS scales
o	Households with malnourished children, lactating and pregnant mothers, at risk of malnutrition and children with nutritional deficiencies (stunted, wasted & anemic cases) located in areas with multiple deprivations.
o	Households with children with protection needs, including those subjected to violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation, in particular children involved in child labor, those prone to child marriage and children with severe psychological distress.

project_name: Safe and protected access to education in Areas C and B in the West Bank
project_objective:

project_name: Respuesta multi-sectorial para mejorar el acceso a una educación de calidad y segura para NNA afectados por la situación humanitaria
project_objective: La intervención educativa forma parte de la respuesta integrada de NRC Venezuela. El equipo de Educación continuará trabajando en colaboración con los programas Información, Orientación y Asistencia legal (ICLA), Agua Higiene y Saneamiento (ASH) y Medios de vida y seguridad alimentaria (LFS) para permitir que las poblaciones afectadas por la situación humanitaria y desplazamientos satisfagan sus necesidades básicas, disfruten de sus derechos y se beneficien de los caminos hacia soluciones duraderas. La acción propuesta por el NRC tiene como objetivo garantizar la permanencia y los caminos de regreso al aprendizaje y la integración en la educación formal, particularmente luego del cierre de las escuelas por dos años durante la pandemia COVID-19 y su reciente reapertura. NRC responderá a los diversos problemas y necesidades que enfrentan los niños, niñas y adolescentes vulnerables en cuatro estados en Venezuela (Delta Amacuro, Bolívar, Táchira y Zulia) a través de una estrategia de respuesta basada en el Programa de Educación infantil (CEP), Programa Puente (PP) y Programa de Nivelación, así como una versión contextualizada del Better Learning Program (BLP) de NRC. Todos estos programas están adaptados al contexto venezolano.

project_name: Amélioration de l’accès à des biens et services de base EHA, de manière durable et inclusive pour les populations vulnérables de l'Extrême Nord
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à améliorer l’accès à des biens et services de base EHA, de manière durable et inclusive pour les populations vulnérables et à réduire la pression autour des services Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement accentuée par l’arrivée de réfugiés et déplacés internes. Il entre dans le cadre de la programmation 2022-2026 du HCR et sera mis en œuvre de façon intégrée avec un projet de renforcement de l’autonomie, l’inclusion économique et les moyens d’existence afin d’apporter une réponse holistique aux besoins des populations affectées et à terme d’améliorer la résilience individuelle et communautaire dans les zones d’accueil de l’Extrême Nord du Cameroun, tout en contribuant à la cohésion sociale.
Pour l'année 2023, il vise environ 7 585 personnes qui pourront bénéficier d'activités de réhabilitation/construction de points d'eau et latrines et de sensibilisation aux pratiques d'hygiène.

project_name: Provide access to quality education in a protective learning environment by combining formal and non formal education response in emergency for Out of school children in Far north Region
project_objective: The project aims to improve access to safe and quality education for crisis-affected children, with a particular focus on girls. The action will facilitate access to education for out of school children and adolescents to enable them to obtain the basis for integration into the formal education system. It is urgent to re-engage out-of-school children with the education system since, as these children grow up, their chance and ability to resume school decreases. The project will address gendered barriers to education and sensitization on gender-based violence, through teacher training, awareness campaigns and the promotion of equal and safe education for girls and boys, regardless of their status (IDPs, returnees or host communities.) To achieve this, NRC will ensure close collaboration with the decentralized services of basic education in Cameroon, and will ensure a conflict-sensitive approach while ensuring respect for Do No Harm principles. The project result will be achieved through activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of education actors at the community level and ensuring the protection of children and adolescents. To ensure a consistent and comprehensive response, the project will be developed through the lenses of gender and conflict mitigation, which are two concomitant perspectives to the dissemination of the principles of protection in the project. At the end of the action 30 000 persons including IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host community’s children will benefit the above package of education assistance in order to scale up their access to qualities education opportunities.
