project_name: Strengthening the protection of children in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
UNICEF will reach  167,123 beneficiaries (10% PwD) with child protection services, among which are 116,484  children and adolescents, and 50,639 adults. Women and girls will constitute 60% of beneficiaries. 70% of the project target will be in Rohingya refugee camps and 30% in host communities. UNICEF will reach the above mentioned target through 16 camps in align with rationalization following one partner one camp with maximum  50% coverage of each camp. 
UNICEF will adopt a public health approach to preventing abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect of children, within a social-ecological framework and according to fundamental Protection principles including Do No Harm and the Best Interests of the Child. 

UNICEF will work with government institutions to strengthen child protection systems. We will maintain partnership with the Department of Social Services (DSS) to build capacity of the social service workforce, and provide technical support to justice sector stakeholders including judges, police, probation officers and social workers to improve children's access to child-friendly justice, while promoting juvenile justice principles such as diversion and alternative measures to detention. UNICEF will provide human resources and technical input to the Office of Deputy Commissioner to accelerate Birth Registration through upgraded systems and financing. 

UNICEF will ensure that survivors of abuse, exploitation, violence and neglect - including Unaccompanied and Separated Children and other vulnerable children - have access to case management, care plans and referrals. Family-based alternative care will be promoted. UNICEF will ensure that adolescent girls and boys have access to Life Skills-based learning and are engaged as agents of positive change in their communities through access to information, social mobilization and participation. UNICEF will provide access to structured and unstructured Mental Health and Psychosocial Support for children and adolescents to build resilience and their coping skills, and give Positive Parenting guidance to caregivers including awarness and community sensitization in prevention and respond to any violence against children and women. Covid19 mitigation measures embedded within regular programming.

UNICEF will establish and make functional Community-Based Child Protection Committees through trainings, technical guidance and logistical support and ensure community led awareness raising and sensitization in camps and host community. 

UNICEF will embrace its role as a lead agency in the Child Protection Sub-Sector Strategic Advisory Group, Protection Working Group, Case Management Technical Working Group, Anti-Trafficking Task Force and other coordination forums, ensuring close collaboration with Government, NGOs, Civil Society and the private sector. UNICEF will also provide technical guidnace and organizational development support to implementing partners and government counterparts. 

Child Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be mainstreamed. UNICEF will lead the training of implementing partners and ensure mechanisms are in place in line with the humanitarian code of conduct.

UNICEF will mainstream Emergency Preparedness and Response through DRR capacity building for service providers and communities, and through pre-positioning supplies.

This project will give priority to the inclusion of Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ensuring equal access to services in dignity. 

UNICEF will promote social cohesion and peaceful existence within and between communities through promoting free flow of accurate information, dialogue, coordination, joint activities, sport and recreation.

UNICEF will strengthen Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) by facilitating complaint and feedback mechanisms, and monitoring to ensure that feedback improves programming. Children, adolescents and caregivers - including those with disabilities - will be consulted.

project_name: Strengthening Explosive Ordnance Threat-Mitigation Capacities of Nigerian Authorities in the North-East
project_objective:
This project overall contributes to Conflict Sensitivity of the list of priorities in the GFFO Strategy. While strictly adhering to humanitarian ‘Do No Harm’ principles, under the Protection Sector, and alongside the other Areas of Responsibilities including Gender-Based Violence, Child Protection and Housing Land and Property, UNMAS will ensure that all interventions are fully integrated within the humanitarian response, to ultimately protect and serve affected populations. Through the proposed action driven from Maiduguri, UNMAS will support the national authorities to reduce the impact of armed violence, contributing to a better understanding of the EO related aspect of conflict dynamics in northeast Nigeria. Essentially, UNMAS’ intervention strategy integrates capacity building of national authorities for an enhanced coordination, in accordance with broader frameworks such as the APMBC.

UNMAS Nigeria had received funding from Germany for the 2020-2021 and 2021-2022 projects, both entitled “Strengthening EO threat-mitigation capacities of Security Service Providers in north-east Nigeria'', which helped enhance the capacity of Nigerian authorities. In addition, “Gender Baseline Assessment in Strengthening EO Threat-Mitigation Capacities of Security Service Providers in North-East Nigeria” and “Assessment of the Impact of EO on Groups of Populations in Borno State, Nigeria” have increased the understanding of the situation, challenges and opportunities as well as provided valuable information to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of future activities. This proposed project will further build on the achievements and lessons learnt, as well as the results of assessments from the two projects to further enhance the capacity of the national authorities to protect civilians from explosive threats, with a focus on support to the establishment of an NMAC and capacity building for the NMAC and NPF personnel.
 
For this project, UNMAS proposes to support establishment of an NMAC and capacity development for its personnel in line with GFFO strategy’s priority Embedded to National Strategies. The project will, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, support the development of key documents for the NMAC which are essential for a fully functional NMAC, including Terms of Reference (ToR), a National Strategy, a National Workplan, and National Mine Action Standards. It will also focus on enhancing capacity of NMAC staff to conduct IM activities to collect, map and analyze the information and data on EO incidents, coverage by mine action activities and others, as well as conduct QA to ensure the quality of mine action activities which have been and will be carried out by Nigeria Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Borno State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), and the NPF trained through the past and this German-funded projects, as well as international and national NGOs and other mine action operators. 
In realization of Gender Sensitivity in the GFFO Strategy, UNMAS will train NMAC staff on gender and diversity guidelines. In consideration of the recommendations outlined in the gender baseline assessment, there is a need to create gender parity and inclusion of women in explosive ordnance response. The gender training will be based on the UN gender guidelines for mine action programmes published in 2019. 

Furthermore, the project will develop the capacity to establish and manage VA referral mechanisms for NMAC staff and support them in assisting victims of EO incidents in order to enable access to medical, psychological and other assistance for the victims of EO incidents and persons with disabilities.

UNMAS target: 10 direct beneficiaries for the establishment of the National Mine
Action Center and 200 direct beneficiaries during the training of NPF EOD personnel.
Indirect Beneficiaries: Conflict-affected IDPs, host communities, resettling IDPs under Borno State Resettlement Plan, humanitarian and development workers.

project_name: Multi-sectoral response in Humanitarian Coordination & Information Management, Emergency Camp Coordination and Camp Management to Internally Displaced People (IDPs) in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe States in Nigeria
project_objective: ACTED's proposed intervention will aim to strengthen humanitarian coordination, information management and assessment support will be provided to the humanitarian community by IMPACT Initiatives, through its initiative REACH. Within the proposed Action, the goal of REACH is to improve the quality of strategic decision making within the humanitarian coordination structure, and enhance decisions made by individual organisations by providing an improved evidence base. Through a Humanitarian Situation Monitoring (HSM) in hard-to-reach (H2R) areas and area-based assessments in areas of returns, REACH will improve the overall efficacy of the response, ensuring the correct prioritisation choices are made and strategies deployed. It will also increase the capability of all NGOs and other partners in their everyday decision making by providing up to date, and easily digestible multi-sector analysis on the situation.

project_name: Ensuring improved living conditions and increased resilience of vulnerable families, including IDPs living in informal settlements
project_objective: The objective of the project is to address the basic needs of most vulnerable communities through the provision of shelter rehabilitation, distribution of tents in informal settlements and seasonal cash distributions. The shelter rehabilitation (targeting 2,400 individuals) will be implemented either through a cash modality (conditional shelter grants) or by contractors. The combination of these 2 modalities ensures the coverage of both owners, renters and free-hosted households, with a focus on reinforcing the HLP rights to avoid forced evictions which is a factor to consider, especially in Ar-Raqqa city. The tents will be delivered to households (targeting 3,600 individuals) in informal settlements, selecting manufacturers in the country to stimulate the local economy. Finally, the seasonal cash distributions (targeting 5,000 households) will ensure a quick and flexible emergency assistance response for IDP households (primarily in informal Settlements) and vulnerable host community households. DCA will prioritize beneficiary/ households who are recently displaced, households with disability family members, single-parent-headed households, and households without livelihoods.

project_name: Providing support to persons at risk and vulnerable communities through rebuilding and/or enhancing resilience, support networks, access to services, and ability to lay claim to fundamental rights.
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to support at risk and vulnerable communities with Protection and Child Protection services, through addressing root causes of protection risks and threats and supporting development of positive coping mechanisms. Through provision of structured and sustained group psychosocial support activities, aimed at rebuilding and/or enhancing resilience, the psychosocial wellbeing of children and women in particular will be improved. This includes support groups to rebuild or enhance support networks specifically for women (at risk) and older persons without support networks. Through awareness raising, based on community-identified priorities and needs, DCA works to enhance knowledge and understanding of rights, and aims to reduce prevalence of protection risks by addressing behavioural, social, and cultural practices. Targeted support to respond to individual needs and exposure to risks/threats will be provided through case management, including referral to enhance access to services as well as specialized support (GBV, MHPSS, HLP, and cross-sectoral). DCA will maintain its static facilities and employ mobile approaches to enhance coverage to informal settlements, and communities out of reach of DCA’s Community Safe Spaces in Menbij, Kobane, and Ar-Raqqa. DCA will continue to include persons with disabilities (PWD), including children, in its activities provided in said spaces. DCA used spaces have floor level access to facilitate attendance by persons using mobility devices. Extensive training of staff conducted throughout DCA’s operational presence, on a variety of mental health disorders allows dedicated support to individuals with cognitive disabilities. Where possible, individuals with visual or hearing impairments will be included with adjusted communication methodologies used, and DCA will attempt to support in providing required assistive devices where possible through coordination with other actors or as part of individual support interventions. 
All interventions implemented by DCA are monitored by an independent MEAL team, using a variety of tools. Group activities make use of attendance record-keeping, as well as pre-post surveys (such as wellbeing for PSS, or knowledge-assessment questionnaires for information dissemination sessions). Further, every DCA activity participant is provided the voluntary opportunity to partake in a so-called Satisfaction Survey conducted by MEAL team staff. These surveys aim to further understand value-add of activities, perceived sustainability of gained information/services as relevant to the specific intervention methodology, as well as staff conduct, service accessibility, exclusion, and safety. DCA adheres to data protection protocols, as stipulated in its dedicated SOP. Individual assistance modalities, such as case management, are guided by senior Protection staff with various levels of approvals required. The system also makes use of systematic record keeping, ad hoc visits by mid-level (supervisory) staff where case specifications allow and based on consent provided participation in specific surveys conducted by MEAL team staff.

project_name: Support Acute Mental Health Inpatient and Two Mobile Units in North of Syria
project_objective:
UOSSM seeks to contribute to achieving the following objectives:
Increase access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable humanitarian health services for those most vulnerable and in need.
The proposed project is to keep running the acute mental health unit in Sarmada/Idleb with the two mental health mobile units. The main goal of the project is to promote specialized mental health services to address more severe mental health disorders. 
Upon the need of the affected people for specialized MH services which are not sufficiently available in the area, UOSSM contributed to the response by establishing an acute MH inpatient and outpatient unit where services are provided for the most urgent presentations of severe mental health disorders, like schizophrenia (acute psychotic episodes), bipolar disorder (manic episode), severe depression, suicidal risk, severe substance misuse disorder and severe behavioral disorder related to mental health problems which cannot be managed and addressed in the community, in addition to providing multidisciplinary mental health service in the community (outpatient psychiatric units, psychiatric supervision, follow up and case management, individual, couple and group psychotherapy, and the mental health supervision), and receiving referrals of more severe and complicated psychiatric beneficiaries from other agencies and health providers.
Also, to cover as many areas as possible, the acute MH unit is linked with two MH mobile clinics, where MH interventions are provided by doctors trained in MHGAP program for beneficiaries of children and adults with signs and symptoms of mild and moderate mental health disorders, in addition to psychosocial support activities for children, which are: self-recovery techniques, coping skills with different situation skills, emotional expression techniques, PFA and PFA for children. Also, to facilitate awareness campaigns on mental health and protection concerns, such as (the detection of signs and symptoms of mental disorders, early marriage, GBV prevention. etc.). Not only the detection and referral of the serious and severe beneficiaries to the acute MH unit in Sarmada, but also the referral of beneficiaries or families to community resources to help in recovery from mental or physical illnesses, and to facilitate access to services provided by other humanitarian actors.
 Objectives of the Project:
•To respond to the most urgent acute and serious mental health problems of the affected populations in the area
•To facilitate access of the affected populations to long-term specialized MH services 
•To enhance and promote the affected communities’ healthy coping mechanisms for both locals and IDPs
•To facilitate access for the affected populations to the available services in the area through an active referral pathway.

project_name: Assistance médico nutritionnelle et psychosociale aux populations déplacées internes et hôtes affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord et du Sahel au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
L’insécurité grandissante au Burkina Faso est à l’origine de déplacements massifs de populations. En effet, le pays connaît une grande crise insécuritaire à l’image de ses voisins (Mali, Niger). La dégradation de la situation sécuritaire poussent à un nombre croissant de déplacements qui viennent saturer les ressources et bousculent les communautés hôtes dans leur vie quotidienne. Au 31 octobre 2022, le Conseil National de Secours d’Urgence (CONASUR) compte 1 761 915 PDIs. Les régions les plus touchées sont le Sahel avec 496 804 PDI, le Centre-Nord avec 468 482 PDIs et le Nord avec 249 564 PDIs. A la même date,, au niveau des 8 régions humanitaires (Sahel, Centre-Nord, Est, Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun, Cascades, Sud-Ouest et Centre-Est), 196 formations sanitaires sur 1448 (13,5%) sont complètement fermées et 410 fonctionnent à minima (28,3%), le manque d’accès aux soins de santé prive près de 1 919 889 personnes.
 
Le retrait progressif des services sociaux de base du Ministère de la Santé a créé une situation d’urgence humanitaire dans plusieurs régions du Burkina Faso, avec une forte affluence dans les formations sanitaires fonctionnelles dans les zones à forte concentration de populations vulnérables et qui impacte négativement la qualité des soins de santé. Face à l’augmentation des besoins médico–nutritionnels des populations hôtes et déplacées, le consortium ALIMA/Keoogo/SOS Médecins BF prévoit de renforcer sa réponse aux urgences dans la région du Sahel (DS de Dori), du Nord (DS de Thiou, DS de Ouahigouya, DS de Titao), du Centre-Nord (DS de Barsalogho, DS de Tougouri, DS de Kaya) pour l’année 2023.
 
Le projet vise le renforcement de la qualité de l’offre de soins de santé primaire et secondaire au niveau des aires de santé affectées par la fermeture et le fonctionnement à minima. Cela passera par l’installation de postes de santé avancés, et de cliniques mobiles dans les sites hébergeant les PDI et la réouverture des formations sanitaires fermées dans les zones les plus compliquées d'accès. Des activités médicales telles que la PCIMA (prise en charge intégrée de la malnutrition aiguë, la CPN (consultations pré natales), la CPoN (consultations post natales), l’identification et le référencement des grossesses à risque, les urgences pédiatriques, la chirurgie, la prise en charge psychosociale et de santé mentale aussi bien des PDIs que des populations hôtes y seront menées. Les cas compliqués seront orientés vers les structures sanitaires pour une prise en charge adéquate. Le consortium appuiera après des populations vulnérables avec un forfait dans le transport et l’hospitalisation. Un appui sera dans données aux cas de MAS avec complications reçus dans les CRENI appuyés par le consortium, avec la psychostimulation et la donations de kits de bienvenus à l’admission et des kits WASH à la décharge. 
 
Un appui en RH sera fait avec le renforcement de capacités du personnel étatique et humanitaire en collaboration avec les différentes Directions régionales de la santé et Équipes cadre de District. En transversal, des activités WASH seront également prévues avec le renforcement des dispositifs de lavage des mains, des campagnes de sensibilisation sur l’hygiène corporelle,  la distribution de kits WASH et d’hygiène, l’installation de poubelles, la construction de toilettes et d’incinérateur (zones à déchets). A travers le déploiement de son plan d'action environnemental, ALIMA luttera pour l'autonomisation énergétique des centres de santé avec l'installation de kits solaires.
Le volet communautaire sera aussi renforcé à travers la formation/coaching des acteurs locaux et leur prise en main des activités de santé, nutrition et santé mentale. Les ASBC, AV et les promoteurs de santé auront en charge les dépistages actifs, prise en charge de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire et la référence précoce des cas de malnutrition avec complications, l'identification des grossesses à risques.

project_name: Assurer l'accès à une éducation inclusive et de qualité aux garçons et filles affectés par la crise dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, de la Cascade et de l'Est, au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Le présent projet initié par Save the Children s’inscrit dans une logique de continuité éducative des élèves affectés par la crise sécuritaire et vise à améliorer l’accès inclusif et la qualité des enseignements et apprentissages de 30 000 élèves dans un environnement protecteur (dont 60% de filles , et 1% d’enfant en situation d’handicap). La zone d’intervention couvre la région du Sahel province du Seno et Oudallan ; la région du Nord , province du Yatenga ; la région de l’Est  province du gourma ; la région de la boucle du Mouhoun , province de la kossi et du Sourou ; la région des cascades , province de la Comoé .  
La réponse proposée s’articule autour de trois résultats i) le renforcement de l’accès à une éducation inclusive, ii) l’amélioration de la qualité des enseignements et apprentissages iii) l’amélioration d’un environnement protecteur pour le bien être des élèves. 
L'approche proposée va permettre d’assurer une éducation inclusive de qualité et d’améliorer le bien être des élèves affectés par la crise sécuritaire. En outre l’approche impliquera de multiples groupes de parties prenantes dans les différentes régions afin d'assurer une appropriation locale aux niveaux scolaire, communautaire et institutionnel, alignée sur les meilleures pratiques en matière de programmation de la résilience dans les contextes nexus
 Pour amplifier l’impact de l’intervention, un focus sera mis sur la promotion du genre en milieu scolaire.  Pour ce faire il sera à priori nécessaire de renforcer les capacités des acteurs éducatifs sur le concept genre en situation d’urgence. Des actions de sensibilisations, d’identification et d’orientation des filles déscolarisées ou fille mère seront menées (par les organisations des mères éducatives) pour leur réinscription à travers les alternatives éducatives adaptées à leur âge ou besoin (les stratégies de scolarisation accélérées ou des formations aux métiers). Des mesures incitatives de financement des études des filles (bourses scolaire, kit scolaire, kit GHM …)  seront proposées pour faciliter la réinscription et le maintien des filles à l’école. Enfin toutes les activités proposées prendront en compte les femmes/filles à 60% et les hommes/garçons à 40%. 
Aussi l’engagement communautaire et la redevabilité seront promus à travers les comités de veille safe School , les comités de redevabilités au niveau communautaire, les lignes vertes et les boites à suggestion dans les écoles. La prévention contre les violences et abus sexuel sera renforcée par des sensibilisations. Les enfants et femmes victimes d’exploitation et d'abus sexuels, de discrimination et de négligence seront pris en charge à travers l’accès aux services adaptés, y compris le soutien mental et psychosocial ou le référencement vers des services spécialisés.

project_name: Renforcer la réponse rapide et intégrée en matière de protection et de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial aux besoins des populations touchées par la crise sécuritaire, en particulier les enfants dans les zones d'urgence.
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire au Burkina Faso est plus préoccupante que jamais. L'augmentation continue des besoins a été exacerbée au cours de l'année 2022. La violence quasi quotidienne est généralisée dans 77% du pays (10 régions sur 13), affectant principalement la population civile, notamment les femmes et les enfants. La crise actuelle au Burkina Faso a un impact direct sur plus de 4,9 millions de personnes, dont 3,5 millions ont un besoin humanitaire aigu.     La fermeture des centres de santé, des écoles et des marchés, l'abandon des mairies, les violences contre les civils et la raréfaction des ressources en eau dans plusieurs localités ont un impact sur la vie de la population, notamment des plus vulnérables. L'exercice et la jouissance des droits de l'homme sont ainsi sérieusement affectés, notamment le droit d'accès et de bonne administration de la justice.
Au 31 mars 2022, selon la situation actualisée après la révision de la liste des personnes déplacées, le Burkina Faso comptait plus de 1,7M de déplacés internes. Les enfants représentent plus de 59,13% des déplacés internes et les femmes 23,28% des déplacés internes.
Cette situation de déplacement forcé expose les enfants à de sérieux risques de protection. En effet, les enfants sont exposés au risque de recrutement par les groupes armés. Pendant leur déplacement forcé, les enfants courent le risque d'être séparés de leurs parents. En raison de ce placement, les enfants sont également exposés au risque d'engins explosifs improvisés et de blessures graves. En raison également de la charge des ménages et de leur incapacité à subvenir à leurs besoins, les enfants sont exposés à toutes sortes de violences et d'abus, et pire encore, les ménages adoptent des stratégies d'adaptation négatives en donnant les filles en mariage.
La protection et le soutien psychosocial restent des besoins critiques pour les communautés touchées par l'insécurité dans tout le pays et dans les six régions d'urgence où les attaques violentes et l'utilisation d'engins explosifs improvisés contre les civils ont augmenté. Avec la fermeture des écoles et des crises alimentaires de plus en plus préoccupantes, les garçons et les filles sont confrontés à un risque accru de recrutement dans les groupes armés, d'exploitation, d'abus, de violences sexuelles, de viols et de mariages d'enfants. Le contexte d'urgence a encore exacerbé les inégalités et les vulnérabilités existantes, en particulier pour les filles et les femmes. De manière générale, la crise a considérablement aggravé la situation des enfants, les exposant plus que jamais aux six violations graves dont sont victimes les enfants dans les conflits. En conséquence, le SCI va rationaliser l'intervention de protection dans toutes les thématiques que nous mettons en œuvre tout en ayant une intervention de protection autonome pour 100000 enfants.

project_name: Sustainable Food and Livelihood Security in GPAA through Conflict and Climate Change Resilience and Adaptation
project_objective:
Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA) is one of the most food insecure, conflict and flood-prone areas in South Sudan. An alarming 80% of its population will be in IPC3+ towards the peak of the lean season in 2023, with 45% in IPC4; currently 23,000 people are arleady in IPC5. The resilience and ability of communities to absorb & adapt to shocks is significantly compromised following years of conflict and four consecutive years of atypical flooding. Subnational and localized conflict, coupled with severe flooding, led to loss of harvests, livelihoods and productive assets. A large part of the population resorted to emergency coping mechanisms (ZOA Dorcas, 2022). IDPs, returnees and host communities are all affected, while women, girls, youth, people with disabilities (PWD) and elderly are uniquely impacted by the shocks. Marrying of young girls is a coping mechanism in time of crisis – considering the current food security situation, this is a major protection concern. Women and girls face high levels of (S)GBV when carrying out daily duties; further exacerbated by conflict and flood-related displacement. With few opportunities to engage in productive livelihoods, PWD and elderly face higher levels of food insecurity, while youth have little prospect for alternative livelihood opportunities.
To build resilience and adaptive capacities of communities in GPAA to the adverse effects of conflict and climate and reduce their dependency on food and agricultural inputs, ZOA Dorcas proposes the ‘Sustainable Food and Livelihood Security in GPAA through Conflict and Climate Change Resilience and Adaptation’ Project; an integrated humanitarian-development-peace nexus response. The project targets Pibor, Lekuangole and Gumuruk, and strengthens resilience of 4,597 most affected households (2,303 female, 2,294 male)/27,582 beneficiaries (F:13,818, M:13,764) to absorb and adapt to shocks experienced. Building on a proven and long-standing track record, through the proposed project, ZOA Dorcas will strengthen community capacity to produce sufficient food, mitigate conflicts and build resilience to mitigate and adapt to the effects of climate change. 
The overall objective of the proposed project is: To reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs in order to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb & adapt to shocks and contextual changes (CO3) (while also contributing to CO2). Specific objectives (SO) include: SO1) Women, men, youth and children including those with disabilities have improved food, nutrition and livelihood security; SO2) Communities in Pibor have strengthened local capacity and resilience to mitigate the impacts of climate change and natural disasters; SO3) Communities in Pibor have increased local capacity to address conflicts peacefully and promote social cohesion. The proposed intervention will create a longer-lasting impact along the HDP-nexus and activities are conflict-sensitive. At minimum, 50% of target beneficiaries are women, and age and disability are considered. The proposed project is based on various internal and external needs analyses and input from the community and authorities. 
ZOA Dorcas has over 10 years of experience in GPAA in the areas of FSL, WASH and Peacebuilding and is known as a trusted, reliable partner by the community and authorities. Most of ZOA Dorcas staff originates from the area, which significantly enhances contextual understanding and trust. The proposed intervention builds on ZOA Dorcas’ existing track record in FSL and peacebuilding and projects in emergency food assistance and FSL resilience. As for peacebuilding, ZOA Dorcas has worked with youth, peace committees (LPC), promoters (PP) and various other stakeholders, and has in place a contextualized peacebuilding manual developed with the LPCs, PP and youth which will be mainstreamed across the response. Coupled with DRR experience, this makes ZOA Dorcas uniquely positioned to execute the proposed project.

project_name: Protection assistance for vulnerable children and communities in WoS in 2023
project_objective: The overall goal of the War Child programme is to increase the resilience and wellbeing among vulnerable children and youth in North East and North West Syria. Under this action, War Child would respond to urgent Child Protection needs in Idleb and Aleppo, and expand the service provision for highly vulnerable children in Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor through CFS, structured PSS, awareness raising, and developing specialized service capacity within local partner organizations, so that they can deliver a quality case management service. This will target 8,750 in NW hub, and 8,750 in NE hub over the one-year period. The budget is $1,125,000 for NW and $1,125,000 for NE. This prevention and response approach will address immediate and urgent identified child protection risks while contributing to long-term change. The project aims to reach parents and caregivers as well as local leaders and communities to build a more protective environment for vulnerable children affected by conflict. The project will contribute to multi-sector initiatives (specifically in Education) to support the mainstreaming of Protection outcomes. It will also focus on local organisations to build sustainable technical CP capacity and enhance the quality of the overall response.

project_name: Food and livelihood assistance to the most vulnerable and crisis affected population in South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed project aims to provide food assistance, livelihood and resilience support to 1,105,380 vulnerable populations in Upper Nile, Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria and Greater Bahr el Ghazal. The project will implement activities that will prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies of target beneficiaries in IPC 5, 4 and 3. The project will also seek to enhance emergency food production and contribute to the reduction of dependency to food and agricultural inputs. World Vision will adopt a mix of intervention approaches including but not limited to unconditional and General Food Distribution, cash transfers, complementary livelihood support, capacity building (e.g., modern agronomic practices, Integrated Pest Management, Natural Resource Management, etc.), and resilience building at the household level. The proposed project will also be implemented in synergy with other sectors implemented by World Vision in the targeted locations such as health, nutrition, WASH, gender and protection related programming while maintaining coordinating and complementarity with the efforts of other humanitarian actors and line ministries. In order to reach the target beneficiaries with prioritized cluster objectives, World Vision South Sudan proposed a total of $4,512,952 US project budget for 2023.

project_name: WoS Education assistance for vulnerable and out-of-school children and youth in 2023
project_objective:
For 2023, War Child Holland (WCH) and its consortium of seven Syrian partner organisations will provide an education response to 11,000 (5,750 boys and 5,250 girls) highly vulnerable children in North West and North East Syria across a 12-month action. All targeted sub-districts are severity 3, 4 and 5.  

In Idleb, WCH and its partners will operate in Dana, Harim, Maaret Tamsrin, Qorqeena, Idleb, Ariha & Badama sub-districts. In Aleppo, operations will be in, but not limited to, Al Bab, Afrin, Atareb & Daret Azza sub-districts. In NES operations are planned, and not limited to, sub-districts of Raqqa, Kisreh, Hajin & Susa.  

Recognising the interconnection between protection and education, the action will increase access to non-formal education and strengthen the protection of vulnerable girls and boys who are out of school or at risk of dropping out, to build their resilience and provide a pathway back into a safe and protective environment in school. The action will include non-formal education interventions including Accelerated Learning Program (ALP) for out-of-school children of the ages 5-17 who have missed more than two years of school. The action will also include guided self-learning for informal settlements with no access to learning spaces to keep children connected to learning, and for youth mainly boys who joined the working force to support their households and girls who are not sent to school and run the risk of early marriage. For schooled children with learning gaps, remedial and homework support will be offered to limit the risk of dropping out.  

An effective teacher professional development through a coaching system based on INEE’s TICC and WCH’s Core program to ensure teachers’ and children’s wellbeing, will have coaches build the capacities of 200 teachers receiving incentives under the action. The coaches will be trained and supported by WCH education officer based on INEE’s TICC trainings, to help teachers obtain skills and methodologies for the creation of a safe and quality learning environment for children. For the guided self-learning modality, teachers will be trained to support caregivers with guidance and tips to support their children’s learning and provide them with a safe learning environment at home. The action will adopt an integrated approach through developing the capacity of teachers on child protection and enhancing the accessibility and safety of the school environment. Teachers will be trained on safe identification and referral for CP concerns. This prevention and response approach will address immediate and urgent identified risks to access to education while contributing to long-term change. 

WCH will pilot social emotional learning as an integrated approach that complements WCH’s evidence-based Deals PSS programs. Teachers will be trained to identify, and work with children to develop their life skill and learning competencies in the safe learning environment of the classroom. 

To support in the removal of barriers to education, WCH through its partners will provide transportation to 125 CWD and other vulnerable children such as girls at risk of early marriage, provide cash for education to children who are out of school for economic difficulties based on vulnerability selection criteria, establish temporary learning spaces where none exists to provide a safe travel distance for children. To ensure a safe and quality learning environment, this action will include school rehabilitation with WASH facilities, light repairs, and school kits and stationery. 

WCH will be conducting a needs assessment in NWS and NES in 2023 to ensure its response is appropriate to the needs of communities. An inclusion checklist will be applied to assess accessibility, meaningful participation, inclusive development, engagement of marginalised groups, representation in monitoring and evaluation activities.

project_name: Safe Water Access, Sanitation & Improved Hygiene Practices Among The Communities of Tonji North County
project_objective: This project is designed to address the development problems in Tonji North county of Warrap state associated to lack of clean water access and low level awareness of the people on improved methods of sanitation and hygiene practices. It will specifically targets communities in the payams of Aliek, Marial-Lou ,Rualbet ,Pagol, Akob and Alabek. The total number of population inhabited in this county is 81,240 (County RRC, 2022). The 2021 IPC nationwide report classified the county at the level of five as a result of communal conflict and the devastating impact of seasonal flood. Similarly, the 2022 IPC report (Nov. 2022) depicts that the county is at the level of IPC Phase 4 which requires emergency intervention. The situation in 2021 resulted in displacement of people from six payams and also various infrastructures were damaged including boreholes, houses, roads and institutions. The people displaced were hosted by neighboring communities which  had a significant impact on the livelihood and various types of infrastructures. The coming year (2023) IPC project also shows that the county will remain in the same level and addressing the people that require assistance will be a priority. Hence, this project is aimed at mitigating the challenges related to safe water access in the selected six payams of the county. Besides, it will endeavor to enhance knowledge and technical skills of the target households on improved practices of sanitation and hygiene. A total of 28,200 people will be reached with various types of WASH interventions along with the FSL activities that ZOA Dorcas and its partners are implementing in the area. This sector includes crop production, horticulture, income generation, animal husbandry, disaster risk reduction and humanitarian aid. Furthermore, to improve nutrition status of the target community the project will work with World Vision in building water sources in nutrition facilities, conducting distribution of standard kits to SAM children and PLW, sanitation facilities and enhancing the knowledge of the communities on hygienic practices. The integration of different sectors is expected to bring tangible and sustainable outcome among the target households. Major undertakings of the project will be new drilling of boreholes, Rehabilitation and repairs of boreholes, hygiene and sanitation promotion campaigns, training of water management committee (WMCs), training of Community hygiene promoters (CHVs), training of hand pump mechanics, supply of bicycle for hand pump mechanics, provision of repairs tool kits for boreholes, provision of dignity kits for adolescent girls, conduct water testing for chemical and bacteriological tests, and setting up of hand washing stations in public markets. Furthermore, the project will increase the awareness of the community on sanitation through the application of CLTS approach which will be triggered in each village. ZOA Dorcas has applying this method in Wau and Jur River counties and successful results were achieved by teaching and encouraging people to construct latrines at household level using locally available materials. In addition, in collaboration with nutrition partners provision of standard kit for hygiene promotion will be done to SAM children/caretakers and PLW in the selected locations. Besides, along with hygiene awareness soap will be distributed to the needy households. Following the need at nutrition facilities various activities that will improve access to safe water will be undertaken giving high priority.

project_name: Integrated Drought Emergency Response among the Drought Affected Communities in Kenya.
project_objective: Increase access to essential and life-saving health and nutrition interventions among the crisis affected population across all diversities in Mandera, Isiolo, Baringo and West Pokot counties.

project_name: Provision of Emergency integrated Nutrition and Health interventions to vulnerable population in Borno and Yobe states, Nigeria
project_objective:
The overall aim is to reduce mortality, morbidity and undernutrition by providing life-saving nutrition and health services in health facilities and communities.
1.	Affected populations have improved access to quality primary healthcare services in the targeted areas for reduction of morbidity and mortality
2.	Affected populations have access to quality nutrition treatment and preventive services through strengthening the capacity of health facilities
The program will be focusing on; 
-	Provision of quality primary health care services that includes basic management and prevention of communicable diseases for all age groups from children to adults, 
-	Providing medical equipment, supplies and pharmaceuticals and nutritional supplies to the health facilities through the award and in coordination with SMOH and LGA authorities.
-	Sexual and Reproductive health services; antenatal and postnatal care services, support to uncomplicated vaginal delivery services and minor perinatal complications, 
-	Support to referral services for specialized care.
-	 Support to Routine Childhood Immunization in collaboration with SMOH and WHO.
-	 Support to provision of clinical management of minor physical injury
-	 Prepositioning of treatment kits and supplies for Cholera and Measles outbreak in the targeted LGAs 
-	Provision of nutrition services through CMAM approach in targeted communities.
-	Supplementary feeding program through Cash based intervention for PLW (Porridge MOM)
-	Reinforcement of technical capacity through sector/sub-sector specific technical trainings for quality service delivery. 
-	Building institutional and community capacity for promotion and provision of appropriate IYCF-E integrated with priority health and hygiene practices.
Target:
1.	Children 0-59 months of age for malnutrition treatment and other children for provision of primary health services. 
2.	Women: key target of the project, both in its direct activities (e.g. Care Groups) and preventive and curative health services, as well as with the women empowerment agenda applied across the project.
3.	Men: men in the targeted communities will be provided with primary health care services for the management of non-communicable diseases (NCD) and communicable diseases. 
4. Health workers and community-based structures e.g CHIPS, CV etc

project_name: Mejorando el acceso a viviendas y fortalecimiento de la resiliencia en comunidades vulnerables de Honduras
project_objective:
NRC mediante su programa de protección y en conjunto con la competencia de Alojamiento e Infraestructura ha brindado soluciones de alojamiento temporales y de transición a desplazados internos, personas con necesidad de protección internacional y personas en alto riesgo. NRC prioriza la seguridad, confort, costumbres y necesidades especiales en cada caso que atiende. 

Asimismo, durante las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota NRC brindó apoyo a través de transferencias monetarias para reparación de viviendas afectadas a 320 personas en dos municipios, acción que fue replicada posteriormente alcanzando 110 beneficiarios adicionales.  

Las acciones suponen tres tipos de intervenciones: reparaciones parciales, reparaciones totales y construcción de viviendas transicionales.  

Durante estas transferencias NRC ha reconocido la exposición a la violencia que corren las personas beneficiadas debido a las altas tasas de inseguridad que se presentan en sus comunidades, priorizando transferencias electrónicas y estableciendo mecanismos de seguridad para minimizar el riesgo.  

Para asegurar el éxito del programa se brindaron talleres de “Build Back Better” y “PASSA” en esas mismas comunidades. 

 NRC ha rehabilitado la infraestructura de 28 centros escolares que fueron severamente afectados por fenómenos meteorológicos o en zonas de difícil acceso.  

NRC ha contribuido con la resiliencia comunitaria mediante cinco proyectos de infraestructura en dos municipios que mejoran la calidad de vida y seguridad de sus pobladores. 

Mediante este proyecto NRC pretende seguir con la mejora de vivienda sub estándar en comunidades vulnerables y para ello se ha creado un mecanismo de identificación de beneficiarios que permite el seguimiento y buen término de las obras. 

En las actividades de reconstrucción y provisión de viviendas temporales mediante transferencia monetaria a los beneficiarios, permitirá crear fuentes de empleo a personal calificado, así como la dinamización de los mercados. 
Continuar con la provisión de alojamientos temporales que cumplan con criterios apegados a las normativas, las costumbres de los beneficiarios y la aceptación social.

project_name: Projet de renforcement des soins médico-nutritionnels dans le département de Say affecté par le conflit et l'état d'urgence.
project_objective:
L'intervention du projet proposée s'inscrit dans la continuité de l'assistance humanitaire d'urgence à travers afin d'apporter une amélioration des conditions sanitaires et nutritionnelles des populations affectées dans les localités les plus touchées par la crise humanitaire et sécuritaire du département de Say. Ce projet à pour cible 32616 personnes . L’objectif principal de l’action est de contribuer
à améliorer l’état de santé des populations affectées par un choc (conflit armé, mouvement des populations, épidémies ou
catastrophes naturelles) dans le District sanitaire de Say. Help se propose des
interventions rapides et ponctuelles à travers le déploiement de la clinique mobile et l’accompagnement aux structures sanitaires
existantes. L’action visera à garantir également un accès aux soins gratuits de qualité et une prise en charge médicale de qualité par la mise en
place d’un mécanisme de réponse rapide. Elle visera aussi, le renforcement des capacités des structures de santé et des
communautés locales dans la préparation et la réponse aux urgences dans les zones impactées par les conflits. Un accent particulier
sera mis sur le renforcement de l’approche CMAM & Health Surge afin d’assurer une capacité de réponse locale.
L’appui aux CRENAS se basera uniquement sur le dépassement de capacité des autorités sanitaires et aussi des mécanismes
communautaires mis en place. Au niveau du CRENI, l’appui sera plus focalisé en période de PIC. Help va consolider et renforcer
son action RRM dans le district sanitaire précité en collaboration avec les autres acteurs du RRM multisectoriel. En terme d'indicateur à suivre le nombre des enfants de moins de 5 ans  pris en charge en soins Medico-nutritionnels désagrégés par âge et sexe ;  le nombre des personnes vulnérables  de plus de 5ans.

project_name: Amélioration de la condition de vie des PDIs et communautés hôtes vulnérables dans la province du Lac, à travers la réponse d’abris et établissements dignes et durables
project_objective: Les analyses et évaluations des sous-clusters CCCM et Abris/AME indiquaient en 2021, que 93% des personnes déplacées dans la province du Lac vivent actuellement dans des abris de fortune qui menacent leur sécurité et leur dignité et ce chiffre semble n’avoir pas changer en 2022, où seulement 15% de personnes déplacées ont on put bénéficier d’assistance en abris. De plus, les 15% d’abris construits restent des abris d’urgence qui pour certains ont déjà fait plus de 2 ans et sont en majorité détériorés par l’usure du temps, les intempéries et les incendies récurrents. Par ailleurs, la multiplicité des sites de déplacés (253 sites selon de DTM 17) ne favorise pas une meilleure planification des réponses et un meilleur suivis des infrastructures. L’ensemble de ces facteurs expose d’avantage les populations déplacés à divers risques de protection y compris les VBG et les problèmes de santé primaire et exacerbent leurs conditions de vie de manière générale

project_name: MNCAH Support to most vulnerable communities in Lebanon
project_objective:
Lebanon is facing multiple, unprecedented crises. The COVID-19 global pandemic, in addition to a crippling year-long economic downturn and the acute impacts of the August 2020 explosions in Beirut, has compounded challenges in an already weak public health sector. The cumulative impact has meant that the most vulnerable populations – women and children face even greater hardships and UNICEF’s effort to increase access to quality health services is more critical than ever.  Through this project, UNICEF will seek to minimize the risk of further spread of COVID-19 and communicable diseases among vulnerable Lebanese and migrant populations through strengthening the COVID and communicable diseases intervention at the 5 Border Center Points and increasing the capacities and knowledge of staff working at the all Point of Entry.  This will also enable UNICEF to reach mothers and children from the most vulnerable communities among the Lebanese and migrant workers and aim to enhance their health seeking behaviors and knowledge on MNCAH including immunization.

Thereby, the project will target the 3 layers of enabling environment, demand and supply to support and enhance maternal and child access to qualitative services through:
-	Capacity building of health care providers including community midwives on updated ANC/PNC guidelines
-	Enhancing community health behaviors and preventive practices among vulnerable Lebanese and migrants through capacity building and dispatch of 100 frontline workers who will be providing integrated maternal and child health messaging.

project_name: Emergency Response Towards Resilient Agriculture-based Livelihoods in northern Mozambique.
project_objective: The project will ensure vulnerable populations facing, or at risk of acute food insecurity are provided with urgent agriculture livelihood and nutrition assistance, adopting a humanitarian-development nexus and its contribution to peace to ensure the populations are equipped with appropriate capacities to better withstand and manage future shocks and risks.

project_name: Projet de Relèvement et protection des réfugiés et leur enfant à Niamey (PREN)
project_objective: Installés depuis 2012, les réfugiés urbains de Niamey vivent actuellement dans une situation de précarité absolue au regard de la faiblesse de leur pouvoir d’achat et privent les enfants de leurs droits. La présente initiative vise contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie de ces populations en œuvrant à réduire la vulnérabilité des enfants/adolescents refugiés, demandeurs d’asile et communauté hôte exposés aux risque/victimes d'abus, de violences, d’exploitation par le travail, de la non scolarisation/déscolarisation. Porté par un consortium composé de Educo et de ANTD, elle consistera à apporter une prise en charge de 606 enfants vulnérables en collaboration avec les services communaux de protection de l’enfants, les acteurs du Guiche Unique des réfugiés à Niamey et le ministère en charge de l’action humanitaire. Afin d’améliorer l’environnement de vie de ces enfants, 192 ménages bénéficieront d’un appui pour créer ou renforcer au moins une Activité Génératrice de Revenu (AGR), leur permettant de renforcer leur capacité économique et d’améliorer leur stratégie de survie. Pour garantir la durabilité socioéconomique des AGR, les femmes issues des ménages ciblés seront organisées en Comité d’Epargne, de Crédit et de Protection de l’Enfant (CECI/PE) ou groupe VSLA

project_name: Projet d’accès à une éducation sûre de qualité au profit des enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire et la Covid19 au Niger- Phase 2
project_objective:
L’initiative constitue la phase 2 du projet AECID et contribuera à répondre aux besoins humanitaires en fournissant des offres éducatives de qualité et des services de protection pour renforcer la capacité de résilience des enfants et adolescents affectés par la crise sécuritaire et la pandémie à COVID-19 dans la région de Tillabéri au Niger.   En lien avec les objectifs du HRP 2021, le Plan de réponse COVID-19 du Niger,les orientations du cluster Education,les normes INEE et SHERE, le projet améliorera l’accès équitable et inclusif de 8.966 enfants (1.695 réfugiés, 3.375 déplacés et 3.896 issus des communautés hôtes) dont 4.562 filles dans les départements de Ouallam et Ayorou.Le projet permettra aux enfants d’avoir : (R1) accès à une éducation sûre et inclusive ;(R2) des offres éducatives de qualité ;(R3) des opportunités de protection et d’épanouissement. Ainsi, le projet permettra de réduire les impacts négatifs de la crise et de favoriser un cadre d’épanouissement protecteur pour les enfants.
La présente initiative est une continuité du projet 2020/ACHU/000363. La nécessité de mener une phase 2 est justifiée par le besoin :1) d’optimiser la couverture géographique de la Phase 1 en intégrant de nouvelles écoles et en supprimant une commune de Tillaberi afin de se focaliser sur les écoles prioritaires pour répondre aux besoins éducatifs les plus urgents ; 2) de prendre en compte des centres de regroupements mis en place par l’Etat  pour favoriser le retour à l’école des enfants issus des  écoles fermées ; 3)  d’assurer la continuité des services éducatifs en prenant en compte les leçons apprises de la phase 1 et le besoin de flexibilité lié au contexte qui demeure volatile : renforcement des ressources humaines en logistique, coordination entre ONEN et Educo pour la mobilisation communautaire, révision des contenus pédagogiques par groupe cible ; adoption de l’approche « ardoise géante » 4) de répondre à de nouveaux besoins identifiés comme le soutien aux cantines scolaires ou encore l’autoprotection pour les NNA.

project_name: Assistance en abris et articles ménagers essentiels des personnes déplacées, retournées, migrantes et les communautés hôtes dans la province du Lac et Hadjer Lamis et N'Djamena
project_objective:
L’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en abris, articles ménagers essentiels pour couvrir les besoins immédiats mais aussi pour soutenir la mise en oeuvre de solutions durables au déplacement à travers la distribution de 2,500 kits d’Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME) complets, la distribution et la construction de 3,500 abris d’urgence et transitionnels, à travers une approche communautaire. L'OIM soutiendra égalemment un accès sur le cash pour supporter l'autosufficcient de la population pour 300 menages (cash pour AME).

Toutes ces activités seront menées en étroite collaboration avec le Cluster. Des mécanismes de plainte seront mis en place pour accompagner toutes les activités de distribution et un suivi post-distribution sera mené afin de recueillir les feedbacks des bénéficiaires, notamment les personnes les plus vulnérables. Les résultats de ce suivi pourront être transmis au Cluster afin de tirer des leçons apprises.

L’OIM est un membre actif du Cluster abris et AME depuis ses débuts et est engagée dans toutes les discussions stratégiques récentes.

project_name: Appui á la fourniture de services essentiels pour une réponse aux VBG pour les personnes vulnérables spécifiquement les femmes et filles de la province du Lac - Tchad
project_objective:
- Offrir un accès aux services de prise en charge multisectoriels pour les survivant(es) de VBG
- améliorer l’accès au travers de systèmes d’orientation pour une prise en charge holistique des cas de VBG. 
- Fournir et distribuer des kits de dignité pour répondre aux besoins des femmes et des filles
- assurer qu’un système d’orientation est fonctionnelle pour la prise en charge des cas de VBG

project_name: Emergency Food Security and Livelihood assistance to vulnerable and conflict affected households in north east Nigeria
project_objective:
Food insecurity and malnutrition remain prevalent across Nigeria, mainly driven by the ongoing protracted conflict in the Northeast, mass displacement and the resultant IDP return process, adverse climate change and variability, such as drought, long dry spells, and flood, land degradation increasing insecurity and banditry, natural resource-based conflicts and an unfavorable macroeconomic situation manifested in rising food price inflation, etc. Further, the disruption of food and agricultural input supply chains by the Russia-Ukrainian war has led to severe availability and access constraints especially for poor farming households because of high food and agricultural input prices, especially fertilizer.
Despite the efforts of humanitarian communities in addressing the manifestations of the emergency in the country, the situation of food security continues to be a challenge. According to the latest Cadre Harmonise (CH) analysis, an estimated 19.45 million people, nearly 63 percent of them in Northeast and Northwest Nigeria are projected to be at risk of severe food insecurity during the peak of the 2022 lean season. In addition, the latest IPC acute malnutrition analysis report released in June 2022 estimates that 1.4 million children and, nearly 152,000 pregnant and lactating women are likely to suffer acute malnutrition during this period. Therefore, the urgent need for an expanded humanitarian food security response cannot be overstated. While the humanitarian interventions have been playing vital and critical role in addressing the needs of affected populations, it is obvious more has to be done to support the resilience of the livelihoods and the households. Given that the majority of those in need are involved in agriculture related activities, it has become necessary and urgent to promote agriculture-based livelihoods to famers whose majority are smallholders.  
In 2021 FAO reached over 1 million people and is planning to scale up and reach 2 million people (approximately 285,715 households) in need of agricultural-based livelihoods assistance in Nigeria in 2023/2024 with a stronger focus on Northeast and Northwest Nigeria due to the high level of vulnerability in the two regions. Due to restrictions on target numbers submitted in the HRP and its limited coverage (only targeting the Northeast), 1.7 million people will be targeted through the HRP while the remaining 0.3 million will be planned outside the HRP framework. To achieve this target FAO Nigeria is requiring a total of USD 86 million. Notably, funding for agriculture livelihood had declined significantly, for example, in 2022 the livelihood and agriculture funding stand at 6%, while food assistance is 95% covered. This requires a strong coordinated advocacy strategy to shift the paradigm.  An estimated 1.7 million people will be targeted for emergency agricultural livelihoods assistance while 0.3 million will be targeted for resilience interventions including in agribusiness, skills development for the creation of decent employment and income such as stoves production, aquaculture, livestock, etc. that increase the resilience of the beneficiaries.  
The scale-up plan will target the most vulnerable groups including IDPs, returnees, and host communities, especially women, and girls.    FAO Nigeria provides various agricultural livelihood assistance packages based on the livelihoods of the targeted household and the related activity. This is including agricultural rainy and dry season inputs, livestock restocking goats and poultry, urban and peri-urban homestead gardening, aquaculture, agribusiness enterprise support, nutritional support, and SAFE kits. This intervention will be delivered through a combination of in-kind, cash, and cash+ assistance. The scale-up plan is aligned to the FAO Corporate Global strategy framework of achieving Better Production, Better Nutrition, Better environment and Better life.

project_name: Improved emergency nutrition response and mitigation of the impact of wasting among children in the Arid and Semi-Arid & Urban counties of Kenya and refugees
project_objective: Increase access to life-saving treatment for wasting, improve emergency nutrition response and mitigate the impact of wasting among children in the Arid and Semi-Arid counties, refugee camps and urban informal settlements of Kenya.

project_name: Strengthening resilience of high at risk groups through Multi-AoR protection services in Jebel Saman, Aleppo
project_objective:
The project contributes to increasing the resilience of the local community (46%), returnees (40%) and IDPs (14%) in the four neighbourhoods: Karm Jazmati, Seken Shebebi, Karm al Tarrab, and Dahret Awwad. The project will be held by Caritas Germany (CG), planned to be back-funded by the German Federal Foreign Ministry (GFFO) and implemented from 01.04.2023 -31.03.2025 by Caritas Syria (CS). The preparation of the proposal is still in process, therefore all of the numbers are only estimates.
The Outcome 1 aims in 2023 at meeting the basic needs of 10.000 individuals of 4 conflict-affected neighbourhoods, and they are empowered to better protect themselves. 1.1: Hybrid Food Package Distribution (Oil and Sugar; blanket approach); percentage of most vulnerable will receive additional items depending on family size; 1.2.: Hybrid Hygiene Basket Distributions (Shampoo and washing powder; blanket approach); percentage of most vulnerable will receive additional items depending on family size; 1.3: Distribution of winterization items (carpets, blankets, heaters, clothes). Output 2 aims in 2023 at the reduction of protection risks of 2.000 vulnerable families as well as 100 CS staff. The activities are implemented at the community center in Karm al Jazmati. 2.1.: Awareness Sessions for women, men, children and adolescent girls and boys. 2.2.: Training on and implementation of community initiatives for youth, men and women. 2.3.: Psychosocial Support Sessions for elderly, children, women and men. 2.4.: Literacy and life skill courses for women and adolescent girls; 2.5.: Tutoring sessions for schoolchildren and offering a summer club during school holidays. 2.6.: Capacity building and Protection Activities for the Project Staff; 2.7 Case management and referrals for protection cases
The NFI and Food Kits distribution will be coordinated with the respective sectors and alligned with their strategies. The exact modalities that make sense in this context are still being assessed. The protection activities are alligned to the protection sector strategy. The regular coordination with the Aleppo-based sub-sectors Protection, CP, GBV, and FSL, CS ensures avoiding duplication of efforts. The community center in Jazmati has been well received by the residents since its opening in 2019 and continues to be the central point for the provision of integrated community-based protection services, to women, adolescent girls and boys, children, men and elderly.
The Community center follows an open-door policy, ensuring the active engagement of the community, allowing real-time evaluations and timely adjustments of activities. Following a participatory approach, the needs will be regularly assessed, i.e., via PDMs applying a proportional piling method, and FDGs. Furthermore, a robust FCM will contribute to ensure the engagement and thus self-identification of the needs in the community. Hence, throughout the project lifetime, the engagement of all community members will be promoted, establishing a two-way communication with the community. This will ensure a timely incorporation of community feedback.
In response to the feedback collected from beneficiaries, i.e. via PDMs, satisfaction surveys, and FGDs, and following the strategy of the protection sector, the activities are regularly adjusted to the actual needs, or new activities are included.
The target groups are selected interconnectedly, aiming for greater impact within the families and, in turns, the entire community. With a newly established safe referral policy, CS aims to enhance their assistance to cases that need other or more specialized support.

project_objective:
Building on experience of project interventions in Syria since 2013,Oxfam continues to work with local authorities in responding to the vulnerable populations’ WASH needs in districts/subdistricts of Aleppo, Hama, Idlib,Rural Damascus,Dar’a &Deir Ezzor, based on assessments, severity of needs and in response to further emerging needs in NES and NWS.The subdistricts that will be targeted by this project have all been heavily affected by conflict and require WASH support.OXFAM conducted integrated WASH&EFSVL assessments from January 2022 to date covering up to 50 communities through group discussions and key informant in three governorates.This includes consultations with LNGOs, INGOs, secondary data and the Humanitarian Needs Overview 2022.The project will focus during the years 2022&2023 on life-saving WASH interventions and support the resilience of existing WASH systems (water supply &sewer networks, wastewater treatment, solid waste management)&WASH in institutions, such as schools and healthcare facilities, ensuring coordinated and cohesive response strongly aligned to the WASH Sector. It is gender mainstreamed, with a response strategy overarched by a community engagement approach suitable to access and security challenges; implementation engages trusted community structures carefully screened private contractors, community-based volunteers and identified local partners, and strong collaboration with other actors.  
The total estimated population, as per UN-OCHA datasets in these sub-districts, is over 3M people.OXFAM targets the timely response to emerging rapid onset emergency needs in hot spots& potential flashpoints, new returns,new displacements,affected by AWD, economic issues, and the current returned areas with persisting WASH needs. The target locations proposed are according to severity of humanitarian needs and number of populations in need which will be adapted to the evolving ground context, access and people's movement. Although Hama considered under severity scale 1, majority of AlKousor neighborhood suffers from water shortage& still rely on water trucking.Accordingly,Oxfam considered WASH needs there. The project aims to support lifesaving WASH interventions that are resilience-focused, sustainable, durable &cost-effective WASH systems using community engagement approach and mainstreamingCholeramitigation measures and response throughout all regular WASH activities:  The objectives of the project are;1):support to water,sanitation/sewage&solid waste management systems to ensure regular services for affected people in Syria; 2):deliver humanitarian WASH supplies and services,&improve hygienic behavior and practices of most vulnerable people; 3) WASH coordination structures facilitated and enhanced;4) improve WASH facilities and services in institutions to minimize sub-standard WASH conditions of the most vulnerable people in Syria.The type of interventions strongly aligns with: SO1,SO2,SO3&SO4 which captures the sector efforts to respond and assist local water establishments in restoring WASH services to basic functionality for communities, schools&community health facilities.Oxfam will target all age groups for water and sanitation interventions.  Hygiene interventions will target careers women,adolescent girls&school children. Accurate disaggregation of population data will be collected from relevant ministries and actors to ensure coordinated and relevant data and appropriate interventions during WASH assessments and interventions.  Oxfam has unique MOUs with several ministries gaining trust,strong relations,&approval of interventions. Bi-monthly meetings at the MoWR allow insight and agreement for selection of prioritized possible activities and discussion of operational challenges.This project’s close alignment with the HRP in terms of outcomes, activities&methodology reflects Oxfam’s close engagement with the Sector,particularly through strategic discussions&information sharing throughout 2019&2022.

project_name: Health & Nutrition Project in South Kordofan & North Darfur in 2023
project_objective:
GOAL will support the provision of comprenhensive health & nutrition services in 17 Primary health facilities across South Kordofan (Habila, Abukarshola, Rashad, and Talodi localities including support for Stabilization Center in Talodi and Habila) and 17 clinics in North Darfur (Kutum and Al Waha localities), in areas with high numbers of confict-affected households (including newly displaced persons, long-term IDPs, vulnerable host communities, and some returnees. GOAL will conitnue support to rural and hard-to-reach facilities in these Localities.
Services include Reproductive Health, EPI, early warning and outbreak response, support and training for health staff, clinic running costs, provision of drugs, medical supplies and equipment, and support for the Locality Health Department, including the Health Information System. GOAL also provides community health through Care Groups, community health promotion, defaulter tracing for RH and OTP services, and
the Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP) approach to prevent and treat Moderate Acute malnutrition. GOAL will ensure comprehensive care in supported facilities, and GOAL will continue to
closely coordinate through the Ministry of Health and the Health and Nutrition Sectors in El Fashir, Kadugli and Khartoum, and will also engage in ongoing coordination with other partners in each locality to ensure no overlap. GOAL provides a package of lifesaving primary healthcare services in all supported facilities. PHC services include curative consultation, provision and dispensing of essential drugs, managing injuries, EPI to increase the immunization rates in children and pregnant mothers, nutrition screening for children under 5, OTP for management of SAM, reproductive health services, disease surveillance, outbreak response, and health education. Our ongoing programme in Sudan has taught us that an integrated programme works best, with linkages between health, RH, GBV, community health, and nutrition activities, especially at the community level and in defaulter tracing. Midwives play an especially critical role, both distributing Clean Delivery Kits which encourage skilled deliveries, and also playing a critical role in identifying and referring SGBV cases through GOAL’s existing RH referral pathway, which allows for anonymity and protection of survivors. GOAL’s extensive network of nutrition workers, volunteers and NIPP circle members will also support to identify protection and GBV cases and do appropriate referrals. GOAL also supports referral of complicated SAM and RH cases and ensures provision of medicines and support for staff in rural areas where SMoH has not deployed health workers. On-the-job capacity building, mentoring and formal training for SMoH seconded staff is provided as part of the facility-level support, where needs are identified.

project_name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the vulnerable and food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to:

• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity; and
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations.
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity.

WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded through national surveys, and supporting vulnerable families in vulnerable communities with livelihood activities. By prioritizing assistance poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions. These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food.

The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s objectives, the social development sector strategy 2021-2023 as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians. Additionally, the project contributes to the operationalization of Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus by facilitating programmatic interventions that reduce people’s needs, risk, and vulnerability and strengthens peoples’ resilience with the intent to achieve long-term economic development. In coordination with other actors and based on each and everyone’s respective comparative advantage, the project and related interventions minimizes risks leading to the empowerment of some of the most vulnerable population groups.
