project_name: Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela
project_objective:
Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Super Cereal Plus).

project_name: Prestación de Servicios de Prevención, Respuesta y Apoyo que salvan vidas en Salud Sexual y Reproductiva y Violencia Basada en Género para las mujeres y adolescentes más vulnerables en 10 estados priorizados de Venezuela.
project_objective:
El proyecto plantea proteger y garantizar el acceso  a los Derechos de Salud Sexual y reproductiva y al derecho a vivir una vida libre de violencia de las mujeres y adolescentes más vulnerables, incluidas embarazadas afectadas por la crisis, a través de una estrategia intersectorial para la prestación de servicios esenciales de SSR y prevención y respuesta a la VBG que salvan vidas y promueven el bienestar, en 10 estados priorizados  de Venezuela (Anzoátegui, Apure, Bolívar,Delta Amacuro, Distrito Capital, Miranda, Sucre, Táchira y Zulia) alcanzando a un total de  544.633 personas.  El proyecto está alineado con los objetivos sectoriales OE1.1 y OE 1.2 del Clúster de salud y O.E 1 y E.O.3 del Clúster de Protección. 

Está acorde a la estrategia  concertada del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud para la  disminución de muertes maternas. Dando continuidad a  acciones realizadas desde 2019, para el fortalecimiento del Sistema Público Nacional de Salud,  mejorando  el acceso a los servicios de SSR a  oportunos y de calidad a 350.800 mujeres , para la prevención de morbimortalidad materna, embarazo no deseado, infecciones de transmisión sexual (ITS),disminución de la  Sífilis congénita , transmisión vertical del VIH, y violencia sexual. Se pretende dejar capacidades instaladas en  27 hospitales y 81  centros de la red de Atención Primaria en Salud promoviendo los servicios y suministros, a través de reforzar capacidades del   talento humano a  3520 personal de salud,  provisión de anticonceptivos,  equipos, insumos, medicamentos, pruebas diagnósticas rápidas , EPP y ejecución de  las rehabilitaciones necesarias para disponibilidad de agua y luz en la atención de emergencias obstétricas. Se incluyen acciones para la respuesta intersectorial a la VBG en el MCVS  con el  acondicionamiento  de los espacios ,dotación de insumos, medicamentos, PEP Kit  y capacitación al personal que brinda la atención.

Se pretende facilitar el acceso a estos  servicios integrales de respuesta multisectorial a la VBG desde un enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, con énfasis en la violencia sexual, mientras se reducen y mitigan los riesgos de VBG. 
Se beneficiará directamente a 68.962 personas [46731 mujeres], [10.210 niñas] y adolescentes], [46.731 hombres] y [4480 son jóvenes], a través de 5 objetivos estratégicos: 
1)Proporcionar asistencia y servicios de protección especializados, incluyendo gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial y orientación jurídica a 3290 sobrevivientes. 
2) Fortalecer los mecanismos y capacidades de prevención de la VBG en comunidades y el cambio comportamental de 49.862 personas a través de estrategias de prevención de la VBG. Asimismo, se estima cubrir las necesidades esenciales de higiene y salud reproductiva de mujeres y adolescentes mediante la distribución de 15.000 KD y empoderar a las comunidades en materia de SSR mediante sensibilizaciones en DSSR. 
3) Contribuir a la restauración de los medios de vida y mejorar la resiliencia de 150 mujeres a través del establecimiento de 13 ESMN.
 4)Fortalecer las capacidades de 660 personal humanitario y de instituciones públicas, en enfoque centrado en las sobrevivientes y la entrega de asistencia material a 130 instituciones públicas para la respuesta a la VBG. 
5) Fortalecer los mecanismos de coordinación de las intervenciones de GBV, la actualización regular de las rutas de remisiones y POEs, creación de grupos temáticos de trabajo y armonización de la data de VBG a través del roll out del sistema GBVIMS en Venezuela. 
 
Asimismo,  se fomentará la resiliencia comunitaria a través de acciones que permitan mayores niveles de información y participación, con sensibilización e información en temas de promoción de la SSR, signos de alarma durante el embarazo, prevención de Covid 19, integrando los enfoques de género, edad y diversidad.

project_name: assistance alimentaire aux personnes vulnérables dans les zones du Nord Est et Ouest plus affectées par d’importants chocs, pour la couverture de leurs besoins alimentaires et nutritionnels vitaux
project_objective:
Dans un contexte général du Burundi marqué par une forte vulnérabilité (dont la pauvreté  et la malnutrition chronique ) et  une faible résilience, les différents chocs  ( aléas climatiques depuis fin 2022, impact crise russo-ukrainienne, inflation persistante, etc.) particulièrement dans les zones du Nord et Nord Est et Ouest qui par ailleurs subissent une forte pression des personnes déplacées, le secteur SAME a prévu de concentrer sa réponse humanitaire pour l'année 2023 aux personnes vulnérables de ces régions.
En conséquence, le projet du PAM vise à contribuer substatiellement  au 1er objectif strategique du secteur  de ""Fournir une assistance alimentaire à 991 000 personnes affectées par d’importants chocs, pour la couverture de leurs besoins alimentaires et nutritionnels vitaux"".
Le projet apportera sa réponse à 600 personnes dans les provinces (Kirundo, Muyinga, Ngozi, Kayanza, Cankuzo, Ruyigi, Makamba, Rutana, Rumonge, Cibitoke, Bubanza, Bujumbura et Bujumbura mairie) sous la modalité mixte de TM et de vivres en nature surtout durant les périodes de déficits alimentaires (période de soudure).

project_name: Management of S-NFI Pipeline to Strengthen S-NFI Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe and Appropriate Shelter and NFI Solutions
project_objective:
The HNO 2023, estimates that a total of 9.4 million people are estimated to need humanitarian assistance, including 1.9 million IDPs, 1.4 million returnees and 5.8 million host community/non-displaced people. Every county of the country is in need of humanitarian assistance, along with the Abyei Administrative Area that is in extreme need. Of the 9.4 million PIN, an estimated 56,325 people experience catastrophic need in Panyikang county. There are 7.6 million people experiencing extreme need in 66 out of 78 counties and 1.7 million people in severe need in 10 out of 78 counties. (draft HNO 2023). The most significant risks for 2023 are identified as floods, drought, disease outbreaks, economic  deterioration, violence and conflict.

The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving supplies continues to be the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2011, IOM has been successfully managing the shelter and non-food items (S-NFI) Core Pipeline, which is an essential support to the S-NFI Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2023, IOM will maintain its commitment to support the S-NFI Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key shelter and NFI supplies to benefit a total of 886,254 people in need in South Sudan. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Rumbek, and Wau to ensure response efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks.

project_name: Provision of quality lifesaving essential health services, and enhanced capacity for early detection and response to public health emergencies in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The WHO’s HRP project aims to contribute to the reduction of excess morbidity and mortality resulting from health emergencies and common communicable and non-communicable diseases in South Sudan. The common emergencies that are likely to impact the vulnerable populations in 2022, and 2023 include epidemic disease outbreaks, flooding, conflicts, and acute food insecurity. The project objectives will be achieved through the provision of time-critical, life-saving frontline quality health services, ensuring the availability of uninterrupted quality health services, quality essential medicines and supplies, and well-trained healthcare workers in the health facilities and clinics.
In addition to the above, WHO will capacitate the implementing partners and counties to provide quality health services through training of frontline health workers and provision of guidelines and SoPs on case management of common communicable and non-communicable diseases, and provision of safe maternal and child services, mental and psychosocial care. Furthermore, WHO will deploy a multidisciplinary team; the emergency Mobile Medical Teams (eMMTs), to provide integrated health services in deep field locations through mobile outreaches to bridge service delivery gaps in areas with critical unmet health needs.
The country’s capacities to prevent, prepare for, detect, and respond to emergencies will be improved at all levels. The public health surveillance, IDSR/EWARN, will be strengthened through continued investment in the system and expansion of reporting sites to enable timely detection, investigation, and response to public health events. The routine surveillance system will be enhanced through the deployment of mobile phone based EWARS reporting by the static and mobile clinics, and provision of technical support to the implementing partners and counties. This will enhance weekly reporting by facilities to ensure early detection of and response to disease outbreaks. Besides, the national and state Rapid Response Teams (RRTs), as well as WHO Mobile Medical Teams (eMMT), will be deployed to conduct risk assessments, alert, and outbreak investigation, and to provide initial public health response during emergencies to reduce excess morbidity and mortality. Moreover, WHO will support the deployment of the eMMTs and RRTs to conduct rapid needs assessments to identify the unmet health needs in project locations to inform appropriate responses by health actors and other relevant sectors. As part of outbreak prevention and response, WHO will lead the implementation of preventive and reactive vaccination campaigns for vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles and cholera.
Further, WHO will be conducting regular water quality testing and surveillance, IPC/WASH assessments in health facilities and implementing IPC measures as a component of risk identification and mitigation efforts to healthcare-related infections. Lastly, the project will contribute to enhancing the capacities for diagnosis and management of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and associated medical complications with a view of reducing avoidable mortality in collaboration with the Nutrition Cluster.
Finally, WHO will address SGBV and MHPSS needs in the country by mainstreaming the needs of affected people into ongoing programming, and work with organizations of persons living with disability to assess and address their needs.
Overall the above strategy and interventions will contribute to the three health cluster objectives of (1) Improving equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment for common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to crisis-affected populations 2) Reducing excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic-prone diseases, and 3) Enhancing resilience and promoting humanitarian-development linkages.

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving SRHR services for most vulnerable and in-need population, Sudan, 2023
project_objective:
On 15 April 2023, clashes erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, with devastating consequences for civilians. Due to violence and attacks on health, disruptions in the supply chain, and poor access by the populace to facilities that can provide needed services, health service provision across the nation and particularly in the country's capital Khartoum has been severely impacted. Several maternity clinics are out of service, including Omdurman maternity hospital. Power supply interruptions and blackouts continue to impact hospitals and blood banks, posing a serious impact on lifesaving interventions, including blood transfusion and critical care. 
Furthermore, all nationwide supplies are managed and controlled in Khartoum with is significantly  impacted. Access to lifesaving medicines and consumables as well as infection prevention and control for hospitals and community midwives is nearly absent, pushing several facilities out of services, and increasing the risks for infection and sepsis. 
The total number of people in need of humanitarian assistance in Sudan rose by 57% to 24.7 million. 11 
 million people are in urgent need of health assistance, including 2.4 million women and girls of reproductive age among whom 262,880 are pregnant, and over 60,000 are expecting to give birth in the next three months. All of them are in need of access to essential and lifesaving reproductive health services.
During humanitarian crises including during conflict as the situation in Sudan, sexual and reproductive health services are disrupted, and social support systems are broken down, leading to an increased risk of unintended pregnancies, rape, STIs including HIV, and complications which often imply mortality and/or long-term serious health problems from pregnancy and childbirth for millions of women and girls. UNFPA will consider set of priority SRH activities to be implemented at the onset of an emergency as well as during protracted crises using the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for SRH, hereafter referred to as the MISP. MISP aims at reducing maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity, prevention and response to sexual violence, prevention of HIV transmission, reduction of HIV morbidity and prevention of unintended pregnancies, and sets the platform for comprehensive SRH services integrated into primary health as soon as possible. All intervention of the MISP will be implemented simultaneously through coordinated actions with all relevant partners.
The intervention primarily targets women, girls in reproductive age, youth and adolescents, and men and boys. UNFPA will target 1.8 MILLION individuals. 
All SRHR intervention will be implemented simultaneously through coordinated actions with all relevant partners. The planned interventions prioritize and aim reducing SRH mortalities and morbidities through: timely provision of Emergency Obstetric care and save delivery services, timely referral to lifesaving services, support the availability of Family Planning services, improving Clinical management of rape for survivors of SGBV, availing HIV and STIs prevention and response, improving Antenatal and postnatal care, Post abortion care, and other SRH services. These will be achieved through strengthening the capacity of SRH care providers with emphases of midwifery services, timely availability of lifesaving SRHR supplies, timely deployment of temporary clinics and mobile clinics, supporting the referral system, and demand creation through awareness raising and educational activities. Maternal Morbidities such as Obstetric fistula will begiven especial attention by UNFPA.
The implementation of activities will be conducted through NGOs and Government partners with the strong technical support from UNFPA, including maintaining the field presence.

project_name: Prevención y atención humanitaria a niñas, niños y adolescentes víctimas de violencia en el corredor seco.
project_objective:
La niñez y adolescencia en Guatemala constituye un sector de la población altamente vulnerable a sufrir violencia, específicamente violencia sexual. En 2021 el Ministerio Publico recibió 7,176 denuncias de violencia sexual contra niñas, niños y adolescentes (6,554 de mujeres y 616 de hombres).  Esto se traduce en un  promedio de 20 denuncias de agresión y violencia sexual contra niñez y adolescencia. 

En cuanto al resto de delitos de violencia contra la niñez se contabilizan 17,030 denuncias en el Ministerio Público durante el 2021, (8363 hombres y 8,647 mujeres). 

El panorama anterior se agudiza en los 88 municipios del corredor seco, en los cuales además de la situación alimentaria y nutricional que enfrentan, se suma la alta vulnerabilidad a la violencia en todas sus manifestaciones. El 36% de los delitos cometidos hacia la niñez y adolescencia proviene de los municipios del corredor seco. Los delitos más frecuentes son el maltrato infantil (30%) y violencia sexual (20%).

En la sociedad guatemalteca predominan patrones culturales/normas sociales de género, que reproducen prejuicios y estereotipos que generan violencia de género hacia las niñas, adolescentes y mujeres en todos los ciclos de vida; la brecha es aún mayor para las niñas y adolescentes indígenas, ya que a la discriminación por género se le agrega la discriminación étnica y lingüística.

project_objective:
Solidarites International is responding since 10 years to the relevant needs of the population in Lebanon with close collaboration with the water sector, the leading ministries, the local authorities, water establishment and off course the affected population. 
The recent development in the county context, following the economic crisis and devaluation of the local currency pushed SI to review its country strategy and adapt to respond to the emerging needs related to access to basic services including water, sanitation, and health. 
SI, and through generous funding from OCHA, was able to tackle the drastic decrease in water supply in the most vulnerable areas in Lebanon (i.e Baalbek and Akkar) by sustaining the water source through emergency repairs and solarization, and given its active presence in the field in Akkar, in partnership with UNICEF, was able to actively respond to the Cholera Crisis that outbroke in October 2022 and channel additional funding form OCHA and the French Government to enhance the preparedness of the water and health functions in the high risk areas (Hospitals, PHCs, Water Stations, etc). 
SI, and in close coordination with the sector, will tackle the emerging needs in sustaining water supply to all affected populations within its area of coverage, by coverage the already assessed needs through the sector vulnerability mapping and any additional emerging needs in the upcoming months, aiming to meet at least the minimum standards in terms of water quantity (i.e. 30lpcd) with cautious attention to the quality. 
SI, will implement health-based approach in responding to cases of water borne diseases (Cholera and Diarrheal Diseases, Hepatitis) or vector borne diseases, through the implementation of wide awareness campaigns and distribution of Hygiene and Disinfection Kits to the communities in concern, and in collaboration with active Health organizations. 
SI, through its expertise in the field of sanitation, will work to reduce relying on wastewater trucking, through the installation of decentralized wastewater units in locations that lack access to sewage network and treatment. SI will base this intervention on the agreed design and implementation modality as the ongoing Sanitation Action Plan of the Sector and its contribution to the WWT component of EU-HawKaMaa consortium. 
Si, will ensure that do-no-harm approach is applied throughout the project, and the integration of protection, gender and disabilities consideration in all its field activities. SI will give special attention to the gender inclusion throughout the project cycle management and will grant all beneficiaries a safe and easy access to feedback and complaint mechanisms.

project_name: Humanitarian response to the most vulnerable population affected by extreme poverty, humanitarian crisis, and violations of IHL/IHRL in the Gaza Strip.
project_objective:
The Gaza Protection Consortium (GPC) integrates cash assistance delivered by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) and Mercy Corps, protection assistance delivered by NRC and Médecins du Monde France (MdM) and heath assistance delivered by MdM and Humanity & Inclusion (HI) across Gaza, in collaboration with local partners. The Consortium delivers humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable population affected by the humanitarian crisis and violations of their basic rights. Between October 2020 and March 2022, the GPC provided a lifeline to 8,689 of the most vulnerable households in Gaza affected by deep poverty and/or emergencies.

The GPC follows a ‘cash plus’ approach, whereby protection and health beneficiaries are identified from the cash caseload to provide integrated and comprehensive support to households and better safeguard protection outcomes. This beneficiary identification pathway is distinct from the pathways used for standalone NRC, MdM and HI projects outside of the Consortium, meaning that, while activities are similar, there is no overlap in the support provided. The GPC aims to contribute to learning and evidence regarding how an integrated ‘cash plus’ approach, after the identification of needs through a unified household level baseline assessment, can result in stronger protection outcomes compared to cash alone.

This project will support approximately 12,000 of the most vulnerable individuals across Gaza by providing multi-purpose cash assistance, protection case management, multi-disciplinary rehabilitation and assistive devices, and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS). The project will train 60 humanitarian staff in protection mainstreaming, 342 emergency volunteers training in emergency rehabilitation and 114 healthcare providers in MHPSS, including mhGAP and GBV.

Specifically, the project aims to:
(1) Enhance the ability of households to meet their critical basic needs by providing five rounds of MPCA, with protection mainstreamed throughout and aligned with Cash Working Group (CWG) standards.
(2) Provide shock-affected households with emergency MPCA within 72 hours to restore access to urgent needs during an escalation or weather-related emergency through a Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM).
(3) Increase the ability of vulnerable individuals, with particular attention to women and girls facing violence, to address the protection risks they face by providing general protection case management and community protection mobilization activities with a focus on protection and prevention of violence and abuse.
(4) Improve the availability, accessibility, and quality of MHPSS services at the community and secondary healthcare level.
(5) Improve the independence of women, men, girls and boys with disabilities through the provision of multidisciplinary rehabilitation (MDR) services and assistive devices.
 
The project supports vulnerable households in Gaza living under blockade to meet their basic needs and protects their rights. The project supports strengthening of resilience among the poorest and most vulnerable strata of the Gaza population, improves access to services and restores more dignified living conditions. It protects the most vulnerable Palestinians through a protection-oriented, multi-sectoral approach that encompasses emergency relief, community-based protection, and MHPSS. Finally, the project complements the efforts of the Palestinian National Cash Transfer Program (PNCTP), run by Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) and co-financed by the European Union, to support households living in deep poverty.

project_name: WASH cholera prevention and response activities in high cholera risk areas in Baalbeck-Hermel and South of Lebanon
project_objective:
ACF Started the project in October 2022,  by rolling out a lifesaving cholera response to reduce transmission of the disease in affected areas and minimize the risk of introduction of the outbreak in other high-risk areas. ACF provides assistance to all populations regardless of status and intervenes in all types of settings (urban areas, ITS, CS, or rural areas) to tailor its response based on WASH needs. ACF covers the following geographical areas:  
- Baalbeck (including Aarsal, Qaa, Deir el Ahmar and Labwe clusters),  
- Hermel, and  
- Saida (Clusters 6, 7, and 8).  

Specifically, ACF implements:  
1) Case-area targeted intervention approach (CATI) or case-cluster targeted intervention approach (CATI), to provide affected populations with enough water, sanitation services, and hygiene items for a minimum period of 2 weeks to face a cholera outbreak. 
2) Preventive measures to ensure water safety in high-risk areas through different modalities, ACF works closely with public institutions to ensure water delivered through the public network is chlorinated and safe to drink.
 
As a result of the recently amended (26th April 2023) and extended (Until November 2023) cholera response under this grant and as part of preventive measures, ACF will :  

1. Conduct cholera awareness sessions at community level. 

ACF will work to raise awareness in high-risk areas in Baalbek-Hermel by providing door-to-door sessions to the community, and group awareness sessions on cholera prevention and treatment in: schools, health centers, and crowded areas (ATMs, supermarkets, restaurants, etc.) ACF will recruit community mobilizers (CMs) and focal points (FPs) in host communities and rely on existing volunteering networks in ISs in Baalbek-Hermel to raise awareness about cholera. Importantly, community mobilizers will support in improving referral system through the identification of symptomatic cases during the awareness sessions. 

2. Support targeted schools through rehabilitation of WASH assets and / or distribution of hygiene kits.  

ACF will expand its support to 15 additional schools based on a priority assessment conducted by its team. This assessment has prioritized schools based on several factors, including the availability of water, water filters, and the extent of dependency on water trucking. Additionally, ACF will also focus on the minor works in 31 schools by repairing handwashing points, wash basins, and soap dispensers. This will help to promote proper hygiene and sanitation practices among students, which is crucial for their health and well-being. 

3. Support water establishments with spare parts, chlorination, and / or filter maintenance to mitigate water shortages. 

ACF will provide water establishments with spare parts to improve the capacity of the establishment in maintaining the pumping stations, chlorination stations, and water networks. The list of spare parts is based on a request from the establishment considering the most frequently used accessories that are almost out of stock. 

4: Solarize key water assets to ensure constant water supply to mitigate the spread of cholera 

ACF will improve access to water in two villages in Baalbek-Hermel (Bajjaje and Zabboud) that are at 0.33 and 0.22 risk with respect to the cholera risk map. Zabboud and Bajjaje are connected to the same public borehole that is the only source of water for the community. The borehole is fully equipped and functional, while it relies on EDL (Electricité Du Liban) as the only source of power which is not available most of the time. Action Against Hunger is looking to solarize the main public water source that supplies Zabboud and Bajjaje cadasters with an initial approval from the Municipalities and the water establishment.

project_name: Protecting Civilians through Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in Syria has been exacerbated by the widespread use of explosive ordnance (EO), posing significant risks and requiring different mitigation strategies to reduce its impact on the civilian population and the humanitarian sector delivering aid to those in need. While the full scale of contamination is not known, preliminary findings for the 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview estimate that around 10.2 million, that is to say, 1 in 2 people is at risk from EO, and a third of communities are potentially contaminated. EO contamination in essential civilian infrastructure, agricultural land, roads, and private property is a lethal barrier to a safe movement which deprives civilians of accessing essential basic services, hampers delivery of humanitarian assistance, endangers those seeking refuge from violence or returning to their areas, and precludes resumption of livelihood activities, thus amplifying the social and economic crisis aggravated by the COVID-19 pandemic. A comprehensive humanitarian mine action response is a humanitarian necessity and vital precursor for delivering humanitarian aid and early recovery.
Mine action is a key humanitarian priority and enabler for the wider humanitarian response and is  critical enablers for safe delivery of humanitarian assistance, The overall aim of UNMAS project is to reduce the impact of EO on the civilian population and humanitarian workers through effective sector coordination and implementation of humanitarian mine action activities, in line with humanitarian priorities as identified in the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), and within the framework of agreements between the Syrian State and UN agencies, funds and programs, as well as Security Council resolution 2585 (S/RES/2585, 2021). Under this project, in accordance with the HRP, UNMAS will lead, manage and coordinate humanitarian mine action activities as defined by International Mine Action Standards (IMAS). All components of humanitarian mine action (risk education, victim assistance, survey and clearance) remain critical, but in 2022-2023, UNMAS will focus on expanding survey and clearance, as the only way to permanently remove the threat posed by EO and subject to access and funding. UNMAS will also continue the  delivery of EO Risk Education (EORE), tailored to age, gender, localized threats, and activity patterns of different at-risk groups,  a critical, life-saving activity for raising the awareness of civilians and humanitarian personnel about the dangers of EO, thus directly contributing to HRP strategic objective 1: “Save Lives'' and strategic objective 2: “Enhance Protection.”  As the Syrian crisis has been characterized by large-scale conflict and displacement, survey, data collection, and mapping of EO are critical to informing humanitarian programming, needs-based prioritization, and the expansion of clearance to remove the contamination threats, particularly in high-humanitarian priority areas. UNMAS will support the expansion of victim assistance also and the provision of specialized services for persons with disabilities, including survivors of EO and their families, thus contributing to strategic objective 3: “Increase Resilience and Access to Services”

project_name: Asistencia multisectorial directa para venezolanos vulnerables y fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales locales y comunitarias
project_objective:
La intervención propuesta tiene como objetivo apoyar a la población vulnerable en Venezuela que requiere asistencia humanitaria. La acción se articulará en los sectores prioritarios: Protección, Alojamiento, Enseres y Energía (AEE), Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (ASH), seguridad alimentaria, salud y coordinación, en línea con los principios humanitarios que contribuirá a una respuesta eficaz y eficiente para salvar las vidas de las personas en movilidad. 

El proyecto tiene como objetivo general contribuir a mejorar las condiciones de vida de los venezolanos vulnerables, y a su vez que incrementar su resiliencia. El objetivo específico del proyecto es la provisión de asistencia humanitaria y acceso a servicios para la población vulnerable y fortalecimiento institucional para la asistencia a personas en movilidad, migrantes potenciales y comunidades de acogida. 

Con este proyecto, la OIM brindará asistencia multi-sectorial a personas en movilidad a través de 25 puntos de asistencia móviles instalados en las rutas migratorias y 15 centros de alojamiento temporal administrados por el socio implementador. Los beneficiarios de este proyecto recibirán información que busca reducir el riesgo de trata de personas. También se prevé la recopilación y el análisis de datos para aumentar el conocimiento de las necesidades y vulnerabilidades de las personas en tránsito que se desplazan por todo el país.

Además, la OIM apoyará a los socios para que desarrollen sus capacidades y amplíen los servicios disponibles para las comunidades seleccionadas, incluyendo las comunidades indígenas. El proyecto busca también fortalecer las capacidades de entidades de salud para la prestación de servicios médicos que atienden población vulnerable. Las autoridades nacionales y locales  pertinentes participarán en actividades de capacitación sobre el protocolo para la atención a las Víctimas de Trata (VdT) y actividades de prevención en VbG. 

La acción también está en línea con los objetivos establecidos en el Plan de Respuesta para Migrantes 2022, que tiene como componente integral y transversal la Protección contra la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS).

project_name: General Food Assistance
project_objective: As highlighted in the FSA 2023 HNO, the food security crisis in Syria remains characterized by very complex drivers and contributing factors, from economic worsening and weakened local currency, the impacts from the war in Ukraine, to drought-like conditions and severe agro-climatic fluctuations, water scarcity, limited energy supply, and population movements. Moreover, the food security situation of Syrian families continues deteriorating with recent HNO figures showing that the extremely vulnerable food insecure population has worsened by 39%, (between 2021 and 2022) and therefore, lead to increase in number of food-insecure households in 2023. The Food Security and Agriculture sector has identified the PIN for 2023 – food insecure people and those at risk of food insecurity – to be estimated at 15 million, with 12.1 million facing acute food insecurity and 2.9 million at risk of sliding into food insecurity. 2 million people living in camps are deemed to be 100% food insecure. WFP’s GFA covers critical food needs of Syrian families across 14 governorates. Subject to availability of funds, WFP’s GFA will ensure that food needs are being met through a food basket planned to have a minimum basic caloric value, across modalities from 2,100 kcal per person per day for the most food-insecure, like the IDP in camps in Northeast Syria (NES), 1,700 kcal per person per day for beneficiaries assessed as severely food insecure or living in camps in Northwest Syria (NWS), to 1,300 kcal per person per day for beneficiaries assessed as moderately food-insecure. In total, WFP Interim Country Strategic Plan aims to target 7.75 million food-insecure people each month in 2023, including 1.3 million severely food-insecure; 4.7 million moderately food-insecure; and 1.7 million need based IDPs living in camps/informal settlements across the NWS and NES governorates. This plan is costed at US$1,048,100,440. WFP has completed the nationwide Vulnerability Needs Review (VNR) exercise, to allow effective prioritization of assistance to households identified as most vulnerable. In 2023, the VNR results will replace the currently used ""Beneficiary Selection Tool"" by applying indicators that more accurately capture vulnerability status compared to relying on demographic characteristics. The operational context in Syria continues to present a complex risk climate. WFP applies the organization's enterprise risk management policy and internal control framework that enables WFP to address and monitor risk and opportunities proactively. Some examples of risks that WFP continues to address cover deteriorating economic and security conditions, inconsistent access to affected population, increasing number of people in need of assistance. To address these challenges, WFP continuously reviews its internal and external operating environment, update its risk register, and actively identifies solutions to address current and emerging risks to enable the programme to deliver on its objectives.

project_name: Shelter and NFI support to vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Cabo Delgado and Nampula Provinces.
project_objective:
UNHCR will continue to ensure the centrality and mainstreaming of protection across the shelter and NFI response, supporting the prompt delivery of immediate lifesaving shelter and NFI assistance to newly displaced people; alongside carefully targeted support for improved shelter solutions for protracted populations residing within temporary, and relocation sites or returning to places of origin as well as maintaining shelters which were implemented and provided to IDPs over the years.
UNHCR's response will focus on enabling vulnerable IDPs and host community have access to essential core relief items, in building emergency and sustainable shelters using local construction materials and practices, thereby promoting dignified living conditions, enabling privacy, security, emotional support, and protection from the weather elements and protection risks. The project aims to address needs induced by 1) new displacements requiring emergency shelter/CRI assistance 2) protracted displacements requiring shelters 3) returns to place of origin or integration within host community requiring more sustainable shelter solutions.
The project aims to support vulnerable households with adequate shelter materials that will allow a household to build a shelter and contribute in part or in whole to a more sustainable solution. Similar to other UNHCR programmes, the project will adopt a community-based participatory approach, integrating the centrality of protection, age, gender and diversity approaches. The project is centered on the need to assist IDPs and communities to construct shelters that are safe and meet established technical requirements and centered on the persons of concern as informed decision-makers. The project is defined by four fundamental principles: promoting access to sustainable solutions; building safer environments; sharing safe construction techniques; participatory decision-making. The intervention will consider potential challenges on access to local materials, their effects on the environment and safeguard support from local authorities. Together with shelter support, vulnerable households will receive the standard NFI kit.

project_name: Asistencia alimentaria de emergencia para personas afectadas por la inseguridad alimentaria severa en Honduras.
project_objective: El proyecto tiene como objetivo apoyar los esfuerzos del Gobierno de Honduras en el proceso de restaurar el estado de seguridad alimentaria de los territorios más afectados por eventos climáticos y disrupciones en general Mediante la ayuda alimentaria, el PMA busca promover acciones inmediatas para preservar la vida de 96,800 familias (aproximadamente 484,000 personas de 275 municipios). Son familias que ya han agotado sus reservas de alimentos y se han involucrado en mecanismos de afrontamiento negativos que representan una gran amenaza para sus vidas. Se propone una intervención integral a través de la atención complementaria de asistencia alimentaria en los municipios donde las agencias socias del clúster de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional han priorizado acciones para la reactivación de medios de vida. Esto se ha logrado gracias a la coordinación del equipo humanitario de país. Las intervenciones planteadas consisten en la asistencia alimentaria a través de transferencias de efectivo en las distintas modalidades, según la capacidad de cada territorio. Así mismo se emprenderán acciones de fortalecimiento de las capacidades y de la igualdad de género para la prevención-preparación y respuesta a las emergencias. Los hogares se seleccionarán de acuerdo a los siguientes criterios: a) hogares que han perdido sus bienes, su principal fuente de ingresos, carecen de ahorros, acceso al crédito ya empleo, haciendo uso negativo de estrategias de sobrevivencia; b) hogares a cargo de mujeres o con un solo sostén familiar; c) hogares con poca o ninguna experiencia en autogestión y con una estructura organizativa deteriorada o limitada y la focalización de mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, hogares con presencia de niños menores de 2 años, ancianos y personas con condiciones de salud preexistentes y comunidades indígenas y afrodescendientes. La focalización la realizarán conjuntamente WFP, la ONG asociada para la implementación, los Comités de Emergencia Municipales (CODEM) y representantes de las comunidades.

project_name: Improving Displacement Management and Camp Coordination and Camp Management in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
IOM aims to facilitate the immediate, adequate and equitable delivery of services to the displaced population in camp and camp-like settings through camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) services, information management mechanisms, and sector coordination of partners and stakeholders.

CCCM activities will continue to provide site facilitation support and site-level coordination in formal and informal camps in the following Borno locations: MMC, Bama (including Banki), Dikwa, Gwoza (including Pulka,) Ngala, Monguno, Mafa, Jere, Kala Balge (Rann), and Damboa; and in the following Adamawa locations: Yola North, Yola South, Girie and Song.

As Sector Co-Lead, IOM, with UNHCR, is accountable for the overall CCCM, Shelter and non-food items (NFI) responses in Northeast Nigeria. The sector will continue to ensure access to multi-sectoral assistance in camps and camp-like settings, advocating and identifying durable solutions for displaced families and affected communities and building national capacity through CCCM trainings for national authorities and local partners

project_name: Improving livelihood assistance for enhanced recovery and increased resilience of conflict affected communities in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: The Conflict in Northeast Nigeria stemming from the insurgency of non-state armed groups (NSAG) continues apace. Violent attacks by NSAG have led to the displacement of millions of people, destroying agricultural activities, other livelihoods and disrupting essential services.  The flooding seen in 2022 has further aggravated the plight of the affected population in Northeast states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) with over 513,000 individuals affected. Floods often lead to an outbreak of waterborne diseases. As of 30 September 2022, 7,700, cases of Cholera were recorded, including 324 deaths reported across these three states. The current context has left several displaced individuals in acute need of lifesaving assistance and livelihood opportunities. Although the need for essential life-saving assistance is still widespread, IOM recognizes the urgent need for early recovery interventions, including restoring livelihoods and access to essential services, including access to justice, to strengthen the self-reliance of affected populations, especially girls, youth, women, and the elderly, against future vulnerabilities and shocks. These elements are also crucial for creating conditions for durable solutions for IDPs and restoring social cohesion. Without those pre-conditions, an untimely return of displaced populations may lead to secondary displacement, intensify IDPs’ vulnerability, and exacerbate tension and social polarization between IDPs, host communities and returnees. IOM considers insufficient capacity in areas of return to be a direct risk of the overall progressive resolution of displacement in the Northeast. This project seeks to contribute to the recovery and resilience building of conflict and flood affected populations in Northeast Nigeria through restoring infrastructure, promote early recovery, including through economic and livelihoods restoration, and facilitating a robust resilience building process. Livelihood interventions under this project will include Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), and Cash for Work (CFW). Cash-based interventions are a more dignified way of assisting affected populations, as they empower people to determine their own needs and the best way of meeting them.

project_name: Provision of Shelter and non-food items (NFI) assistance in Northeast Nigeria
Provision of improved, safe, and dignified WASH services to the conflict-affected populations and host communities in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Extraordinary rainfall events related to the climate crisis have increased water-related diseases, especially cholera and acute diarrhea. Floods coupled with the population dynamics in IDPs camps, such as the high density of the population and the increase of returnees to their places of origin, have resulted in problems for the operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructure, and for the proper management of fecal and solid waste, with a high environmental and public health impact. This is in a context of an increase in the number of people needing WASH assistance, whose figure has risen from around 3 million to 5 million, most concentrated in the northeastern part of the country. In response to the needs, IOM will scale up WASH services targeting internally displaced people and returnees in camp, camp-like settings, and host communities in the BAY States.
For this purpose, IOM will (A) Ensure safe access to water facilities and services through the drilling, installation, maintenance, rehabilitation, and water quality monitoring of boreholes; (B) Ensure safe and equitable access to sanitation facilities (latrines, showers, including laundry spaces), handwashing stations) through the operation/maintenance of existing facilities and construction of additional gender-segregated facilities and wastewater treatment systems; (C) Promote improved water and sanitation outcomes in targeted settings through the systematic promotion of personal and environmental hygiene messages (following national guidelines on water-borne diseases) and including COVID-19 preventative measures; and the support for increased capacity of established gender-balanced WASH committees; (D) Ensure environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in operation area through the establishment of WASH Committees including- male and female community members, procurement and distribution of tools/equipment; (E) Distribute WASH NFI following the national/ cluster standards, and contribute to reinforcing the WASH sector core pipeline strategy to facilitate WASH NFI's access to humanitarian actors implementing actions;  (F) Contribute to the strengthening of capacity building activities of local authorities, stakeholders and key partners through the integration of specialists in innovation and research in the areas of management of water, sanitation services and environmental risk mitigation. The project will be implemented in two states: Borno (5 LGAs) and Adamawa (4 LGAs) targeting an estimated 300,000 individuals. 
IOM will ensure that the age, gender, as well as disability-specific needs of the project beneficiaries are considered during implementation and specifically addresses women and girls’ needs, such as Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM). 
Regarding assessments, monitoring, and evaluation of gender, age, and disability-specific needs and the impact of activities, IOM will engage with community structures in these locations during missions and set up communication channels where possible. Using the IOM WASH Monitoring and Evaluation Framework and the Gender Inclusion and gender-based violence (GBV) Risk Mitigation Toolkit for WASH Programming, IOM will ensure that “Do No Harm” principles are adhered to throughout the WASH interventions, particularly in latrine and water point locations, through the use of various mechanisms, such as consultations with vulnerable groups.
IOM will analyze the potential risks due to context-specific environmental degradation and will prioritize actions that mitigate environmental risks. In that regard, IOM will favour the use of solar-powered water supply where possible to reduce the number of fossil fuels generated by diesel pumping. IOM will ensure that groundwater drilling is linked to monitoring initiatives to ensure adequate aquifer recharge. Latrines will be rehabilitated using materials that do not deplete local natural resources, while hygiene items will be of high recycled content

project_name: Displacement Tracking in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: IOM through its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) aims to provide an overall picture of displacement context though timely tracking and monitoring of displacement and population mobility. DTM will continue to provide mobility tracking in the six conflict-affected states in Northeast Nigeria (Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe) with the weekly mobility trends tool deployed mainly in Adamawa, Borno, and when necessary, in Yobe due to fluidity of population movement. Biometric Registration will remain a priority in selected camps and areas of return to assist partners for verification (e.g. WFP) and support other organizations and their assistance distribution. Finally, detailed assessment surveys for return locations will continue in selected areas. DTM will also strive to strengthen existing collaborations (internal and external) with emerging needs.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving GBV interventions for the crisis affected populations in Mayendit, Rubkona, Koch and Panyijiar Counties
project_objective: IRC through the Women Protection and Empowerment program will provide specialized GBV response services and prevention interventions targeting the crisis affected populations in Mayendit, Rubkona, Koch and Panyijiar counties.  This will be through the provision of life saving GBV case management services guided by the survivor centered approach.  IRC will ensure the service provision is in coordination with other service providers for a multisectoral approach which comprise of medical, legal, safety and psychosocial support services. A total of 472(325W, 123G, 12M, 12B) will be targeted for case management services across the proposed locations. IRC will continuously engage women and girls and the community at large to identify barriers in accessing the GBV services and collaboratively work together to address them through the existing community-based protection structures. In addition, quarterly reviews and updating of the referral pathways as well as continuous feedback sessions will be held to ensure that the pathways are functional across the proposed locations. The women and girls’ safe spaces (2 Rubkona, 2 Koch, 2 Panyijiar and 2 Mayendit) will serve as avenues of empowerment for women and girls with a major focus on provision of contextualized psychosocial support interventions which seek to support in the healing, recovery and building resilience of women and girls. The Women and Girls Safe Space toolkit will be instrumental in providing guidance on the operationalization of the safe spaces especially in ensuring accountability as well as encouraging the women-girls led processes and ownership. Tailored curriculums for the engagement of women and girls such as Girl Shine for the adolescent girls and their care givers as well as Women Rise a psychosocial support tool kits for the women will ensure each age group has appropriate and contextualized PSS intervention. 4,500(3,180W, 1,320G) will be targeted for the WGSS activities. On GBV prevention IRC will engage communities through SASA! Together and EMAP as the primary GBV prevention approaches. The two approaches seek to provoke discussions on power imbalance as the root cause of violence while analyzing negative social norms, beliefs, behavior, and practices that contribute to violence against women and girls. Additionally, IRC seeks to build the capacity of communities to respond and prevent GBV through training and community led dialogues which will equip them with knowledge and skills. For GBV risk mitigation measures, IRC will work closely with women and community led structures to carry out GBV safety audits where action points to address the identified risks and concerns will be tasked to the relevant actors. Findings from the safety audits will inform other interventions such as training on Fuel Efficient Stoves for the women as well as production of reusable sanitary materials with the locally available raw materials. In coordination with the GBV SC, IRC will distribute dignity kits to the women and girls of reproductive age at risk of GBV. The proposed interventions aim to target 54,715 (27,904 Women, 19,150 Girls, 4,924 Men and 2737 Boys) where 78% IDP will be targeted, 18% host communities and 4% returnees. Out of the total target, 10% will be people living with disabilities.  IRC currently has presence in Koch, Rubkona (Bentiu IPD camp and in host communities) Panyijiar( Nyal and Ganyiel) and Mayendit. In all these locations, IRC is providing GBV response services, GBV community engagement activities including EMAP, SASA! and awareness raising activities, psychosocial support activities including skills building activities and capacity building activities to community leadership structures and partners and community members.

project_name: Protección, asistencia humanitaria, Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres (RRD) y Preparación para Desastres (DP) para las víctimas del conflicto colombiano, la violencia armada y desastres naturales o provocados por el hombre en Chocó, Antioquia y Córdoba
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivo fortalecer las capacidades de autoprotección, gestión de riesgo de desastres y preparación para desastres y, dar respuesta adecuada a las necesidades humanitarias de las comunidades afectadas por el conflicto colombiano, la violencia armada y los desastres naturales provocados por el hombre en Chocó, Antioquia y Córdoba.  

Lo anterior a través de la atención y acompañamiento en los siguientes sectores:

Seguridad alimentaria: restablecer medios de vida, fortalecer las capacidades técnicas de las comunidades, sensibilizar en hábitos saludables de dieta balanceada y nutrición; tener la capacidad de respuesta rápida ante un escenario de emergencia humanitaria que requiera suplir las necesidades básicas en términos de seguridad alimentaria. Resultado: Al final de la acción se espera haber aumentado la seguridad alimentaria de las personas afectadas por restricciones a la movilidad, confinadas y/o recientemente desplazadas en los departamentos de Chocó, Antioquia y Córdoba.
 
Agua e Higiene: facilitar el acceso a fuentes de agua segura, el tratamiento para asegurar el consumo, el manejo de los residuos sólidos y el control de vectores. Tener la capacidad de respuesta ante un escenario de emergencia humanitaria que requiera suplir las necesidades básicas en agua e higiene. Resultado: Al final de la acción se espera haber mejorado el acceso a agua segura y educación en higiene para familias recientemente desplazadas afectadas por restricciones de movilidad y confinamiento en los departamentos de Chocó, Antioquia y Córdoba.
 
Albergue: Con la atención mediante apoyo de materiales para familias que retornaron sin garantías o que sus viviendas están en condiciones que representan riesgos. Subsidios de alquiler en situación de desplazamiento individual-familiar y el mejoramiento de centros comunitarios de acogida para población desplazada. Resultado: Al final de la acción se espera que las condiciones de refugio para familias recientemente desplazadas o afectadas por restricciones de movilidad y/o confinamiento se hayan mejorado en términos de seguridad y dignidad.
 
Protección: En materia de protección -como enfoque transversalizado a lo largo de la acción- tanto en el componente de asistencia humanitaria como en el componente mismo de las acciones protectoras, se requiere que el equipo de implementación del proyecto identifique y fortalezca las capacidades propias de las comunidades, la agencia, autogestión y autoprotección para contribuir al tránsito de la asistencia en crisis al aporte en construcción de proyecto de vida y futuro deseado. Resultado: al final de la acción las personas o comunidades en riesgo o afectadas por el conflicto y la violencia armada, perciben una mejora en su seguridad y capacidad de resiliencia a través de la implementación de medidas de prevención, protección e incidencia.
 
Se contempla, adicionalmente, un resultado específico de preparación y reducción del riesgo de desastres, afectaciones ocasionadas por las situaciones de emergencia asociadas a desastres naturales y/o antrópicos. Resultado 6 (prevención, sensibilización, formación y fortalecimiento de capacidades de gestión de riesgos de desastres) y Resultado 7 (respuesta ante situaciones de crisis humanitarias asociadas a desastres naturales y/o antrópicos) de la propuesta. 

El proyecto se implementará por parte del Secretariado Nacional de Pastoral Social-Cáritas Colombiana (SNPS-CC) y Jurisdicciones eclesiásticas, con apoyo de Cáritas Alemania, Cáritas Española, con fondos del Departamento para la Ayuda Humanitaria de la Comunidad Europea-ECHO.

project_name: Emergency humanitarian aid for the people affected by the conflict in north-western Syria through cross-sectoral measures
project_objective: The aim of the project is to ensure the survival of the most vulnerable people affected by the conflict through multi-sectoral emergency aid and to make them more resilient to further external shocks.  The project area includes the remaining areas outside the control of the Syrian regime in the north-west of the country (Idlib, Aleppo), where around 1 million people were recently displaced or again internally displaced. The target group of the project are internally displaced persons as well as residents of the host communities. In order to achieve the goal, we use a mix of different measures and dosage forms. For newly internally displaced people, WHH will provide emergency assistance in the food security, WASH and shelter/NFI sectors, both in-kind and in the form of vouchers, to alleviate the first most urgent needs. WASH activities will include: i) to supply and install water tanks for latrines, distribute cleaning materials and perform removal of digesters ii) supply water trucking to the camps and iii) hygiene sensitization and training of the population in camps by the Hygiene Promotion Team. Under FSL, food e-vouchers and bread will be distributed in several locations and people who have already arrived or are residents of host communities will receive agricultural vouchers to make them less dependent on acute emergency aid and thus reduce negative coping strategies. Particular attention will also be paid to the area of humanitarian protection. Under SNFI, the construction work/light rehabilitation of shared/single accommodations will take place and winterization assistance will be provided to beneficiaries in the form of winterization cash. The protection component of the program will be further broadened in 2023, adopting a community approach and increasing the availability of specialized services. Under ERL, a clothes production workshop will be set up. 20 women will be provided with a training on sewing and later produce different sizes of pajamas for 6 months, during which they will receive 1$ per day (for max. 5 hrs/day and average monthly income of 100$). These clothes will be distributed the ones in need to be defined at a later stage. As per the last component, nutrition activities will be implemented by a local partner, PAC, specializing on this field. PAC’s intervention will focus more on awareness raising, prevention and counselling, coupled with the delivery of nutrition cash vouchers (for PLW and caregivers of infants) in the Idleb region, It will focus on most vulnerable women of reproductive age and children who are under the risk of malnutrition and have a lack of access to the food diversity in North-West Syria (NWS). Accordingly, it aims to enhance Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW)’s access to Nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) Services and Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) Supportive Services in Idleb Governorate and Jebal Saman district of Aleppo Governorate. This will be achieved through providing IYCF counselling to the caregivers and PLWs through either OTP center or RRTs. PLWs and caregivers will be also supported with 3 months of food voucher which will provide them with fresh foods to mitigate their malnutrition risks.

project_name: Livelihoods and Economic inclusion for IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in East (Red Sea, Kassala and Gedaref) and West Sudan (North Darfur).
project_objective:
The project aims to provide assistance in Eastern and Western Sudan (Kassala/Gedaref; North Darfur) through provision of WASH, FSL, Protection and Shelter/NFIs, Energy and Environment services for IDPs and vulnerable host community.
Moreover, the project will mainstream protection services to the target population through service mapping and referrals. This project mainly targets IDPs and vulnerable host community members. In North Darfur and in Kassala the project interlinks with a BMZ project to operationalize the Triple NEXUS, strengthening resilience and peaceful co-existence among refugees, IDPs and host communities and while in Red Sea the project interlinks with a SIDA funded project on resilience project. All resilience programming is cross cutting, therefore in most instances actively contribution to life-saving activities e.g., hafir construction.  For FSL component targets group focuses on Host Communities and IDPs in the Eastern Sudan and North Darfur. 
In total approx. 21,000 beneficiaries will be reached under the FSL component  translating to about 11,100 male and 9,900 female beneficiaries. 
Small holder pastoralists and agropastoral farmers will be targeted, using different criteria considering vulnerabilities level. Women and youth will be prioritized for activities such as skills development training for access to employment opportunities and micro-finance ventures.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de la capacidad de respuesta institucional y comunitaria para abordar las enfermedades no transmisibles y la salud mental en poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad
project_objective: El presente proyecto tiene como finalidad desarrollar una serie de estrategias que permitan fortalecer las capacidades institucionales y comunitarias para el abordaje de las Enfermedades no Transmisibles y la Salud Mental, como respuesta a la emergencia, y procurando generar resiliencia en poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, mediante el fortalecimiento de la capacidad de preparación, respuesta y recuperación; capacitación de talento humano; dotación de equipamiento, insumos y medicamentos esenciales; y consolidación de los sistemas de información. La población objeto será de 3.800.000 personas en los estados: Amazonas, Anzoátegui, Apure, Aragua, Bolívar, Carabobo, Delta Amacuro, Distrito Capital, Lara, Mérida, Miranda, Nueva Esparta, Sucre, Táchira, Trujillo, Yaracuy, Zulia, tanto a nivel institucional -Hospitales del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS) 3 Instituto Venezolano de los Seguros Sociales (IVSS) y centros de salud de las Organizaciones no Gubernamentales (ONG) como a nivel comunitario (centros de salud del MPPS y de las ONG y servicios comunitarios de las ONG). En Venezuela, tres de cada cuatro personas fallecen por las Enfermedades no Transmisibles, principalmente enfermedades cardiovasculares, cáncer, enfermedades respiratorias crónicas y Diabetes Mellitus. Más de un tercio de ellas son defunciones prematuras antes de los 70 años y la mayoría son prevenibles si se adoptan medidas para disminuir la exposición a los factores de riesgo, aumentar los factores protectores y asegurar las capacidades de respuesta institucional y comunitaria. Esta situación se ve empeorada debido a la compleja situación del país, con un limitado acceso a medicamentos e insumos, el deficiente cumplimiento de normas o protocolos para su abordaje, y la ausencia de mecanismos de protección de la población general para crear resiliencia frente a ellas. Por lo que la ejecución de este proyecto redundaría considerablemente en el impacto que las ENT y la salud mental tienen sobre la salud de la población.

project_name: Coordinación logística - Clúster de Logística
project_objective:
El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (WFP), liderando el Clúster de Logística, apoyará y complementará las acciones de los socios humanitarios con la coordinación de servicios de logística con el objetivo de contribuir a una respuesta efectiva y oportuna en beneficio de la población más afectada.
La continuidad en las actividades de coordinación y gestión de la información, proporcionando una plataforma de intercambio de información logística relevante y actualizada entre las organizaciones, es una de las prioridades del Clúster de Logística para 2023. A fecha son 45 las organizaciones que forman parte del Clúster de Logística. 
El Clúster busca en establecer relaciones de trabajos con actores claves. En 2023, el enfoque continuará en involucrar a más organizaciones humanitarias nacionales; así como también involucrar al sector privado en sus actividades.

El Clúster de Logística buscará dar el impulso a grupos de trabajo relacionados al sector logístico (transporte fluvial, importaciones, acceso físico), como también crear y fortalecer relaciones de trabajo regulares con actores locales. Será importante reevaluar el interés de los contrapartes nacionales e internacionales en relacionarse en actividades de preparación para emergencias en el sector logístico y promover ante las organizaciones socias la integración de la preparación ante emergencias en su estrategia. Sigue necesario un acercamiento con la Dirección Nacional de Protección Civil y Administración de Desastres, como actor clave en la preparación para emergencias. El Clúster de Logística tendrá como meta el establecimiento de líneas de trabajo conjunto con las autoridades locales Esas actividades se enmarcan bajo el segundo objetivo estratégico.
Si las necesidades son identificadas y existe el financiamiento necesario, el Clúster de Logística podrá establecer un servicio de transporte y/o almacenamiento.

El Clúster de Logística se propone fomentar las capacitaciones de los socios humanitarios, promoviendo a su vez el intercambio de conocimiento entre ellos. Si se requiere, se apoyarán los esfuerzos de fortalecimiento de las capacidades de las autoridades y de las organizaciones no gubernamentales. Estas actividades no pretenden reemplazar las capacitaciones logísticas de cada organización, sino responder a brechas o necesidades específicamente identificadas.

Se pondrá también atención en dar a conocer las principales preocupaciones del sector en notas de incidencia dirigida a los actores pertinentes.

project_name: Provision of primary health care services for vulnerable children and women in Syria
project_objective:
After 11-year crisis of in Syria, there is an increased risk of disease outbreaks due to population movement and the erosion of public services and infrastructure. The COVID-19 pandemic and the worsening economic situation are further stretching and disrupting the already fragile health system in Syria, thus affecting the availability and quality of health services, as well as the physical and mental wellbeing of the population. 
More than 15.3 million people in Syria are estimated to be in dire need of life-saving health assistance in 2023, an increase of 3.2 million from 2022. This includes 6.8 displaced persons, 2.2 million children under 5 years – including expected live births –, 4.2 million women of reproductive age (15-49 years), and more than 700,000 elderly people who will demand integrated and lifesaving health services in Syria. Under-funding of response agencies has also left the 438k Palestine refugees living in Syria in acute need. The economic crisis also added to the vulnerability of Syrian children and women who are not able to pay for the essential health and nutrition services. (Reference: FINAL DRAFT 2022 HNO Sector Template Health Sector 23 November). A cholera outbreak that started in August 2022 has also added to the vulnerability of the Syrian population especially in the northern governorates.   
This proposal from UNICEF aims to support the provision of basic lifesaving curative, preventive and promotional health services and health seeking and care practices, while enhancing early recovery and resilience of the sector by contributing to: 
strengthening service delivery to vulnerable population who cannot afford paying for health services, specifically children, 
supporting community health delivery platforms, with major focus on community engagement through  volunteers  to include and integrate them within the health facilities and be part of the community health system to ensure sustainability of those voluntary services for best delivery, including information, supply and monitoring & evaluation. this will help in improving the quality of services for the most vulnerable. The safety of the health workers who are providing maternal and child health services (including newborn care) is also considered through activities which ensure that all health workers are empowered with knowledge on diseases prevention and health promotion. It is also conceived with a view to promoting the complementarity of the contributions of other sections and multi-sectoral integration within UNICEF & other key sector partners. The project will provide health services to boys, girls and women with disabilities on an equal basis. 
UNICEF will be working through local NGOs who run 36 fixed health centers and 47 mobile teams across all the 14 governorates, including in NES and NWS and will focus to support the implementation of the immunization programme for children under the age of 1 year, and supplementary immunization activities (national immunization days and catch-up campaigns) for the CU 5 years. More than five million women and children will directly benefit from the package of services, focusing on the highest severity districts as defined by the Health Cluster/Sector and in integration with UNICEF prioritized high severity sub-districts across its seven sectors. Programme effectiveness shall be enhanced by applying a conflict and risk informed lens to planned interventions, and the promotion of the participation of affected populations. The accountability towards affected population is integrated throughout the programme cycle, UNICEF started to collect information from the affected population on the quality of the services through hotlines, SMS and complaint boxes in fixed clinics of NGOs. 
UNICEF will work in 258 sub districts, including 170 with a severity scale of 3 or higher. 
NICEF will monitor the project through programme monitoring visits & financial spot checks by UNICEF staff, and by third-party monitors

project_name: Expanding Skills Building for Conﬂict-Affected Adolescents and Youth in the Syrian Arab Republic
project_objective:
In support of the Education Sector, UNICEF, through this project, in 2023, will further support its Generation Unlimited Initiative and the No Lost Generation Agenda by empowering vulnerable adolescents and youth (10-24 years), female and male including those with disabilities, to have access to age and gender sensitive, learning and skills building opportunities for improved learning, empowerment, and employability. 
UNICEF will support access for young girls and boys to multi-sectoral services and opportunities, including technical vocational and education training (TVET), employability skills and life skills and citizenship education, leadership and literacy and numeracy. UNICEF will promote the efficiency and effectiveness in TVET education services nationwide through (i) expanded access and service delivery; (ii) enhanced quality and relevance of TVET provision; and (iii) improved TVET systems including strengthen the capacity of service providers and evidence generation.
The project will strengthen the access of 200, 000 young people (10-24 years) to skills development programming and meaningful engagement opportunities including the development of foundational, transferrable, technical and vocational, and entrepreneurship programming to prepare adolescents better for their future, and to unleash their potential and increase their learning, leadership, and employability opportunities as well as support their smooth transition from learning to earning and decent jobs in particular for young girls. UNICEF will continue its strategic partnerships with national and sub-national stakeholders, local and civic NGOs including youth led origination and youth network to achieve the desired results. The project will target the most marginalized adolescents and youth groups in particular those who are out of school, the poor, those from child- or female-headed households, returnees, IDPs, youth in the camps, adolescents with disabilities, girls headed family and young people affected by the crisis. The project plans to reach a total of 200,000 young people in  the high severity areas such as Dara’a, Rural Damascus, Northern Homs, Southern Hama, East and Northeast of Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor and Idleb. UNICEF will expand its support to young people in NES, focusing on returnees and displaced people in Raqqa, Deer EZour and Hasakah, including those in camps, collective shelters and urban settings. UNICEF will focus on the most deprived areas in rural and urban areas. These will include camps (Hol, Roj, Newroz, Areesha, Mahmoudli) in Al-Hasakeh and Raqqa, the collective shelters in Al-Hasakeh city, and the rural areas in Qamishli, Malikia, Yaroubia, and Raqqa Governorate. The project will implement the activities for the young people affected by the crisis to acquire the right skills, become empowered and resilient community members.
