project_name: Strengthen the collective humanitarian response through effective, agile and efficient coordination, based on humanitarian principles in Far North, North-West and South-West regions
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to strengthen the coordination of the humanitarian response in Cameroon to save lives, protect the most vulnerable and improve the resilience of populations. Since the worsening of the crisis in the North-West and South-West regions, Cameroon faces three complex humanitarian crises affecting eight of Cameroon's ten regions. The impact of these three crises on the living conditions of the affected populations is reinforced by pre-existing structural vulnerabilities that hamper their recovery, in the three affected regions: Far North, North-West and South-West. Widespread insecurity in the Lake Chad basin and border area with Nigeria continued to affect the Far North region in 2022. Attacks against civilians, State security forces (SSF), including army, gendarmerie, police, and their bases, continued and non-State armed groups (NSAGs) and armed criminals continued to carry out lootings in crisis affected areas. NSAGs continue to use improvised explosive devices (IEDs) in the Far North, North-West, and South-West regions, primarily targeting military convoys. In the Far North region, particularly in the Lake Chad basin area, the economic context is marked by poverty, the lack of access to and sustainable management of natural resources, limited income-generating and market opportunities, as well as a drastic reduction in agriculture, livestock production and touristic activities due to prevalent insecurity. 
In the North-West and South-West regions, high levels of insecurity continued. The presence of SSF is concentrated along the main roads and cities, leaving most rural areas under the influence of NSAGs, and civilians exposed to the risks of collateral damage because of regular clashes between SSF and NSAGs and armed clashes among rival armed groups. High levels of criminality and impunity lead to a climate of insecurity whereby civilians and humanitarian workers face risks of kidnapping for ransom, abduction, assault, unlawful detention, carjacking, and threats of violence. The line between targeted, politically motivated acts of violence and criminal activities is increasingly blurred. In 2022, the West region witnessed several NSAG attacks on SSF posts as well as on local markets in small towns. Violence, regular lockdowns and closure of roads continue to have a major impact on the local economies.
The complexity and the scope of these crises therefore require more effective coordination, adapted to the different intervention areas and based on humanitarian principles. OCHA Cameroon's coordination project will thus make it possible to achieve a humanitarian response that is better funded, more strategic and that centralizes human rights and the protection of people in the Far North. It will also enable a better complementarity between emergency actions and development programs, in order to fight together the humanitarian needs and their underlying causes. To this end, OCHA will provide the essential services of disseminating key information products, coordinating the Humanitarian Programming Cycle and facilitating joint multisectoral needs assessments. Its presence in Yaoundé, Maroua, Kousseri, Bamenda and Buea will enable it to provide decisive support to coordination mechanisms and promote coherence between operational issues in the field and strategic decision-making bodies. This key position will also enable it to advance the overriding considerations of the Centrality of Protection and Cross-cutting Protection, Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and nexus humanitarian development and peace. From its sub-offices in the Far North, North-West and South-West, OCHA will also support the scaling up of the response in these regions, including through the management of CMCoord and humanitarian access responsibilities, as well as capacity building of local responders.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de la coordinación y abogacía humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
En 2023, OCHA en Venezuela continuará reforzando las estructuras de coordinación (Equipo Humanitario de País –EHP-, Grupo Inter cluster, cuatro centros de coordinación de terreno y grupos de trabajo temáticos, incluyendo gestión de la información –GTMI-, Comunicación Humanitaria, rendición de cuentas ante las poblaciones afectadas –AAP- y la Red de analistas de acceso humanitario). Para la implementación del Ciclo de Programa Humanitario 2022-2023 (HPC), OCHA apoyará las evaluaciones y el monitoreo de las necesidades en el terreno; facilitará la identificación conjunta de las prioridades intersectoriales de respuesta y el monitoreo regular de la respuesta; y contribuirá a mejorar la comunicación conjunta sobre la situación general, incluyendo avances y retos en la respuesta humanitaria. OCHA planea expandir aún más su abogacía para facilitar el acceso a las áreas más vulnerables y movilizar más fondos para la respuesta, incluyendo mediante el Fondo Humanitario de Venezuela (VHF).

Para apoyar las capacidades operativas de los diferentes actores humanitarios y promover el respeto por los principios humanitarios, OCHA con el apoyo de otras organizaciones, ofrecerá formaciones e iniciativas de desarrollo de capacidades sobre los principios humanitarios, la coordinación humanitaria, la coordinación civil-militar, herramientas de gestión de la información, metodologías para la evaluación de necesidades, el HPC y temas transversales como AAP, PEAS y género.

Las prioridades dentro de la estrategia de OCHA Venezuela para 2023 son:
1. Mejorar la comprensión de la situación, incluyendo el análisis de las necesidades humanitarias, el fortalecimiento del monitoreo, y la publicación regular de productos de información. 
2. Fortalecer los mecanismos de coordinación a nivel nacional y subnacional en términos de toma de decisiones estratégicas y operativas que contribuyan a una respuesta humanitaria oportuna, eficaz y basada en principios. 
3. Mejorar la respuesta en varias temáticas transversales, con un enfoque prioritario en género, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas, inclusión de personas con discapacidad y protección contra la explotación y los abusos sexuales (PEAS). 
4. Promover una mayor comprensión y aceptación de la acción humanitaria mediante el fortalecimiento de los esfuerzos de abogacía y comunicación, incluido para el acceso humanitario.
5. Aumentar la movilización de recursos para la respuesta humanitaria, incluso para las ONG a través del Fondo Humanitario de Venezuela.

project_name: Emergency Response For Rohingya and Host Community, Cox's Bazar (Friendship)
project_objective:
The project aims to improve the well-being and health through integrated healthcare support to the Rohingya community living in the camps and to host communities in Ukhiya in Cox’s Bazar as continuation of previous project phases. The project includes operation of 1 Primary Healthcare Centre (PHC) and the general consultation, dental, eye and limited surgery section of Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU, a secondary Healthcare center).  One primary Healthcare Centre (PHC) in camp 7 will provide services in affiliation with Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). For the Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU), the maternity part (CEMoNC) is funded by IOM, the GBV services are funded by DanChurchAid, the family planning services are supported by IPAS and rest of the services including general consultation services, eye and dental units are funded by the Friendship Luxemburg and provide us the required flexibility to strengthen and consolidate services across the facilities.  The Maternity part (CEMoNC) of the Friendship Hospital Ukhiya (FHU) is identified by the health sector as a referral point to provide higher level maternal healthcare services including Caesarean sections for both host communities and Rohingya. The project focuses on protection against illness and equitable access to (Health Sector Indicator 2) health services without any discrimination and specially targeting the most vulnerable groups (women, children, pregnant/lactating women, people with disabilities, the elderly, GBV and conflict-affected survivors). The project also planning to collaboration with the Ukhia Specialized Hospital (UNHCR) by sharing the expertise, accepting as referral point, receiving maternal patient from USH until the maternity part is started there. Friendship will conduct following activities following the MESP: 
- Provide essential health services to both host and Rohingya community through 1 primary healthcare center in camp 7 and one 24/7 Secondary level health care services named as Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU).
- Strengthen the facility level preparedness for combating COVID-19 infection among the service providers and beneficiaries at Friendship health facilities (FHU and Primary Health Centres).
- Provide SRH services including safe deliveries (assisting Normal Vaginal Delivery ) and providing basic neonatal care, Ante Natal Care (ANC) and Post Natal Care (PNC) services to both host and Rohingya community. 
- Conduct normal vaginal delivery through the PHC and C-section through FHU to ensure safe institutional delivery. 
- Provide Family Planning, Menstrual Regulation, management of STIs and Post abortive care services.
-  Screen and refer Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Medium Acute Malnutrition (MAM) children (6 to 59 months) to Outpatient Therapeutic feeding Program (OTPs).
- Provide Mental Health and Psychosocial Support and Gender Based Violence services including Clinical Management of Rape services and clinical management of Gender Based Violence cases.
- Support Expanded Program on Immunization services in alignment with national program.
- Provide laboratory investigation facility services for the beneficiaries at the health facility level.
- Provide essential medicine and supplements including Vitamin C and Zinc tablet to increase immunity of the beneficiaries 
- Coordinate with District and Upazila level COVID-19 Task Force, Health and Family Planning Department, and other stakeholders.
- Conduct awareness-raising sessions including IPC at facility.
- Strengthen feedback mechanism by developing and implementing action plan based on feedback received from camp level health coordination and health committee meeting.
- Community Health Volunteers are identified, trained, and supervised to identify community members in need of referral for PHC services, EPI, and SRH including ANC/PNC with special attention to term mothers for skilled birth attendant deliveries with the support of outreach Midwives.

Mental Health Psychosocial Support and Functional Rehabilitation for Persons with disabilities in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will address the immediate and long-term health needs with focus on mental health and psychosocial support, physical rehabilitation and disability inclusion needs of the most vulnerable persons that are the center of humanitarian response to cope with recurrent shock and build resilience. 
The project will target returnees, IDPs and host population with specific focus on persons at risk of exclusion specifically people with disabilities, people with injuries and chronic diseases, people experiencing mental health and psychosocial problems, children, older persons; who are often invisible to mainstream humanitarian organizations. The project activities will target an estimate of 85,930 (25,779, Male, 60,151 Female among them will be 12,890 persons with disabilities, 1,780 elderly persons, 2000 children and 83,930 adults ) Vulnerable IDPS, returnees and host population. The focus will be on newly and protracted displaced households with a key attention to support positive coping mechanisms and resilience strengthening. HI will have static presence in the target project locations ;  with support from local community structures, local organizations of persons with disabilities, health and protection partners; HI will identify the most vulnerable to MHPSS and physical rehabilitation needs and provide direct services. HI will critically focus on mainstreaming protection, gender and disability Inclusion issues at all stages of the intervention, identifying and giving priority to vulnerable female headed households and persons with disabilities. HI has one (01) MEAL manager and two (02) MEAL officers who will independently conduct all post distribution monitoring and share the outcomes with the team and cluster partners at state and national level.
The activities will be implemented by HI static team based in Pibor and Panyijiar with a  mobile response to surrounding counties .

project_name: Gender-based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Population in South Sudan
project_objective: The GBV prevention and response program of International Medical Corps (IMC) in South Sudan aims to empower communities and build resilience through promoting social and behavioral change to address the root causes of GBV in the country. The project targets key population to create a sustainable change in attitude and practices through male engagement, working with community leaders and building capacity of local stakeholders. Leveraging on the vast experiences, gains, and successes of IMC in implementing GBV prevention and response interventions through the FCDO-HARISS program, ECHO, SSHF and UNFPA . This project will be continued to implement in the states of Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau IDP Camp and County), Upper Nile and Malakal PoC and County), Unity (Nyal County), and in Canal/Pigi County. This project  will directly benefit about 27495 vulnerable women and girls across the target locations. One of the project’s key priorities is to further strengthen core services to survivors of GBV and other vulnerable women and girls in the aforesaid intervention sites. These services include quality case management using a survivor-centered approach, along with psychosocial support to enhance healing and recovery. IMC UK works to ensure that survivors’ holistic needs are met by providing multi-sectoral services, referring to health centers for clinical management of rape, to legal justice services and to other kinds of support based on the needs of survivors. In addition to individual Psychososcia support (PSS ) for survivors, IMC UK will continue with PSS group activities for all vulnerable women and girls in the women girls’ safe spaces (WGSS). To ensure sustainability of the project and ownership by the community, especially of the WGSSs, in Wau, Nyal Malakal, and Canal Pigi . IMC already established, leadership committee comprise of 8 members from the community selected by their fellow women with the responsibility to give support, information, feedback, and suggestions that will foster empowerment and ownership of the space and the overall wellbeing of their members. The women committee members will be further empowered with knowledge and skills through hands-on management of the spaces and co-leading with them on the daily functioning of the WGSS. The women committee will be continuously mentored and trained on GBV basic concepts, safe referral, and referral pathways, and on leadership and conflict management and facilitation techniques and on various psychosocial support activities using IMC’s and IRC’s global WGSS toolkit. IMC UK will implement holistic community engagement strategies on the promotion of long-term positive change in the targeted communities. IMC will use the GBV community mobilization tool called SASA! - Phase-based strategy to help communities rethink about “power” and the positive use of power. “Preventing Violence against Women and Girls: Engaging Men in Accountable Practice (EMAP)” is also another tool that will be used to ensure men engagement with accountability to prevent GBV in the targeted community in Nyal, Wau and Malakal. In addition, IMC trains and collaborates with GBV Taskforce members in Wau, Malakal and Nyal. These will be supported by staff IMC UK staff to do awareness raising, and safe confidential referral of any survivors who disclose to them. IMC UK will provide emergency cash assistance for case management to the vulnerable women and girls. Cash assistance is one of the interagency minimum standards in GBV programming in emergency. Additionally, IMC UK opts to implement cash assistance based on lesson learnt and feedback from women and girls on importance of cash assistance as lifesaving. IMC will procure and distribute dignity for the conflict-affected women and girls. The dignity kits will include sanitary items, as well as other items explicitly tailored towards the local needs of women and girls of reproductive age affected by the conflict.

project_name: Provision of integrated, safe, equitable, dignified and disaster-resistant WASH services to IDPs, host communities, and returnees living in extreme and catastrophic WASH vulnerability
project_objective:
The project aims to provide integrated, safe, equitable, dignified and disaster-resistant access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services to IDPs, host communities, and returnees living in extreme and catastrophic WASH vulnerability.

To that end, IOM’s interventions will focus on locations identified by the WASH Cluster as key priorities: priority 2 counties (Raja, Aweil East), priority 3 counties (Gogrial East, Gogrial West, Wau, ) and priority 4 counties (Malakal, Jur River, Twic). Through its Rapid Response Team, IOM will also intervene in any other Priority 4 and/or 5 locations, or any other location identified through WASH Cluster allocation. Although not included in the WASH Cluster Targeting Guidance (2022), IOM's HRP proposal also prioritizes Wau, as IOM will remain the main water service provider in Wau’s Naivasha IDP Camp during 2022. 

IOM’s HRP project contributes to the 4 WASH Cluster Strategic Objectives, focusing on integrating WASH programming with Nutrition, providing access to basic WASH services in emergencies, whilst mitigating WASH GBV and reducing community’s exposure to environmental hazards. In total, IOM plans to reach 550,000 individuals (132,819 women, 127,049 men, 141,594 girls, 148,538 boys) by deploying a range of activity packages that combine hardware and software interventions, adapted to the context at play and to the needs of the most affected population. To support nutrition gains, IOM will rehabilitate/install WASH infrastructure within nutrition sites and/or at community level, while in locations where WASH services need to be rapidly restored due to sudden emergencies, IOM will rehabilitate/drill new boreholes, rehabilitate/set up/operate surface water treatment systems (SWATs). IOM will also ensure the sustainability of WASH infrastructure through the formation and training of community-based operation and maintenance groups. These hardware interventions will be complemented with hygiene promotion, as well as distribution and demonstration on usage of WASH NFIs and/or Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) to help communities sustain the learnt practices. All activities will contribute towards mitigating GBV risks and to improve accessibility to people with special needs, as demonstrated by IOM’s commitment to allocate 2.9 % of the project budget to GBV risk mitigation mainstreaming Where needed, activities will be adjusted to be climate resilient and/or to build the capacity of communities to respond quicker to natural disasters. Where possible, IOM will also prioritise market-based programming approaches, using local markets to support WASH responses. As the largest direct WASH service provider in camp settings, IOM will also continue servicing conflict-affected populations in Malakal Protection of Civilians (PoCs), Bentiu and Wau’s Naivasha Internal Displacement Camp (IDP), and Bentiu’s IDP sites (A, B and C). IOM will provide WASH services through the operation and maintenance of safe and accessible water supply systems, care and maintenance of accessible and secure sanitation and handwashing facilities, as well as management of solid and liquid waste. IOM will also continue investing in cost-effective and climate-resilient means of ensuring adequate service provision within these settings by setting up, maintaining, and scaling up water supply solar systems and biogas schemes. IOM will support the transition process at these sites working to transfer WASH service provision towards community-based ownership where possible, through a participatory approach, with a focus on women’s empowerment. Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and COVID-19 prevention measures will also be mainstreamed throughout the project cycle.

project_name: Improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for vulnerable populations in Leer, Pibor and any other emergency location across South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed WASH project will be implemented in Leer & Pibor, as well as other emergency and IPC 4 and 5 locations. According to the WASH Cluster's county prioritization for 2022, Leer and Pibor are Priority 1 counties, while Renk is Priority 2. The project is designed based on Core Humanitarian and Sphere Minimum Standards to ensure that affected beneficiaries receive timely, coordinated, adequate, resilient, and impartial basic water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Medair engages the affected beneficiaries in all stages of the project cycle and ensures that the 'Do no harm' principle is followed by not exposing affected beneficiaries to any risk as a result of project implementation. Furthermore, the proposed WASH project will adhere to the WASH Cluster technical guidelines and WHO drinking water quality standards. Medair will continue to integrate WASH and nutrition internally, as well as collaborate with other nutrition and protection partners, to maximize the impact of the proposed WASH project. WASH activities will also be integrated into health activities in the context of disease prevention and response. It aims at breaking the transmission cycle of water related diseases including diarrhoeal, cholera, vector borne diseases and COVID-19. This is intended to be achieved through multiple integrated approaches. Overall, the project is targeted to reach 148,835 people through improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services by the end of 2022.

project_name: Comprehensive WASH response to affected children and displaced families in the South West and Littoral Regions of Cameroon
project_objective: The socio-political crisis in the NW and SW regions of Cameroon, now in its sixth year, characterized by continued fighting between State security forces (SSF) and non-State armed groups (NSAG, targeted attacks, destruction of property, arbitrary arrest, kidnappings for ransom, extortion of money and continued use of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) (OCHA, 2022), has left more than 1.08 million people from NW, SW, LIT and West region in need of humanitarian assistance (HNO, 2022). More especially, the insufficient investment of Cameroon Government in basic social services, poverty and limited response provided by Humanitarian actor in the Northwest and South west regions continue to exacerbate the water and sanitation need of affected population including neighboring regions (Littoral and West regions). The crisis has had serious negative effects on water, hygiene and sanitation with mostly children, women and girls highly affected, as they are the ones who often access WASH facilities. The situation further compounded with the public health crisis of COVID 19, cholera outbreak and monkey pox which have hit the already crisis affected communities. In September 2022 SitRep, Out of 12 517 cases and 254 deaths reported at national level, the South-West region represent 48% of cases (6017) and 36% (93) of deaths, marking 2022 as the second most affected year by cholera for the past 25 years with more than 13,000 cases and 284 deaths of cholera reported (HNO, 2023). The risk factors are still much evident in these affected regions such as lack safe of access to safe water, sanitation facilities (latrines) and poor hygiene practices that poses a thread to the lives of these vulnerable children and displaced families. It is therefore the responsibility of humanitarian actors and service providers to scale up humanitarian response and delivery of life saving humanitarian needs and services to the affected persons in most insecure and inaccessible locations. It is within this framework that this project in its response will prioritize the safety and dignity of the targeted children, women and girls, as well as affected host population and will reduce the risk and exposure to gender-based violence and other violence related to accessing WASH facilities. Our project will provide WASH humanitarian assistance through all modalities with specificity to 6500 individuals directly utilizing improve water supply service with systematic control of water quality at household level, 1750 households will directly utilize improve sanitation facilities through the support and construction of Eco-friendly boifil latrines, and the provision of latrine kits to displaced families and vulnerable host communities. 15,625 Individuals reached with community sensitization messaging on critical handwashing and good hygiene practices through information and communication materials, door-to-door and cholera tools to efficiently address cholera risk factors and other possible outbreaks associated to poor hygiene practices. 18750 individuals will benefits complete WASH kits through all modalities, 1875 vulnerable adolescent girls and women within reproductive age will be reached with menstrual hygiene kits. 600 beneficiaries will be trained on how to access humanitarian assistance as well as capacitated on how to provide feedback and complains to humanitarian actors. The adoption of community based approached will be the central response strategy through consultation and engagements of all relevant stakeholders and community groups for an impactful, dignify and sustainable WASH service delivery to the vulnerable affected population. For a more responsible intervention that respect the dignity of beneficiaries, the project will mainstream accountability to affected population (AAP) within the response from project inception to the exit strategy and ensure humanitarian principle are respected at all stage of the intervention.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods of Vulnerable Agropastoralists Communities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria States, South Sudan
project_objective:
Climatic extremes, which have in the recent past been characterized by unprecedented flooding, coupled with increasing waves of inter and intra communal violence, bureaucratic impediments including instances of youth aggression towards humanitarian actors, and economic implications of the COVID 19 pandemic that have continued to negatively impact vulnerable boys, girls, men and women, including people with disabilities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria among other States in the country. These have had consequent implications on increased livestock disease outbreaks and mortalities in addition to submerging of agricultural land contributing to unprecedented food insecurity levels, projected to further increase in 2023 with at least 7.76 million people projected to face severe food insecurity by April –July 2023 (IPC November 2022).

Many vulnerable host, returnee and displaced families, especially women, widowed women, child headed households, the elderly, boys and girls including people with disabilities (who have impaired access to livelihoods); solely depend on livestock, fishing, vegetable and crop farming among other coping strategies. VSF Suisse 27 years of experience in the targeted states, presence on the ground and proven capacity will deliver high quality programming by leveraging on strong grass root networks, local knowledge, understanding of seasonal and location specific contexts. 

Proposed actions will target 187,000 beneficiaries (30000 men, 30000 women, 63500 girls, 63500 boys) who shall include elderly and people living with disabilities. The action will be aimed at ensuring cost efficiency through complementarities by linkages with FAO pipeline for livestock vaccines prepositioning and agricultural livelihood kits - crops, vegetables and fishing kits in order to promote preparedness, household resilience and self-reliance through protection of livelihood opportunities.
 
Proposed actions are in line and correspond with the FSL Cluster 2023 HRP Cluster Objectives Supporting CO2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock; and Supporting CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb & adapt to shocks & contextual changes. Proposed actions will establish a nexus between humanitarian response, peace building (conflict sensitivity) and resilience programming. By supporting famine clusters in the catchment areas of health and nutrition facilities and in communities with or without functional boreholes; in addition to the establishment of demonstration sites for vegetable gardening support at nutrition facilities coupled with agronomic training and on-going extension advice and guidance at both main Season farming Response and Dry Season Response that shall include conduct nutrition sensitive feeding and cooking practices. 

The project will ensure a multi-sectoral approach through inter-cluster synergies, quality programming, cost efficiency in addition to mainstreaming cross-cutting programmatic approaches that include application of Accountability to Affected Populations principles, protection including Gender Based Violence mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conflict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention, environmental conservation and sustainability.

project_name: Promotion de l'accès à une éducation de qualité, protectrice et inclusive pour les enfants les plus vulnérables des régions de Mopti et Gao à travers l’alimentation scolaire
project_objective:
Plan International travaille pour un monde juste qui fait progresser les droits des enfants et l'égalité pour les filles. En tant qu'organisation humanitaire et de développement indépendante, Plan International travaille aux côtés des enfants, des jeunes, en particulier des filles et des jeunes femmes, nos défenseurs et partenaires, pour s'attaquer aux causes profondes des défis auxquels sont confrontées les filles, les jeunes femmes et tous les enfants et jeunes vulnérables. Plan s'engage à trouver des solutions fondées sur des données probantes pour les interventions d'urgence afin de sauver des vies et de maintenir la dignité humaine dans les situations d'urgence.
Cette situation de crise est susceptible de dégrader les conditions de vie de la population et d'augmenter le flux des populations déplacées vers les zones plus calmes. L'arrivée de populations déplacées exerce une pression sur les ressources locales. Plan International Mali couvre toutes les zones de crise au Mali comme Ségou, Mopti, Tombouctou et Gao. Le pays fait face à une urgence humanitaire complexe depuis 2012. Cette situation de crise risque d'aggraver les conditions de vie des populations et les élèves ne sont pas épargnés.
Selon une évaluation conjointe des besoins en matière d’éducation – Avril 2022 menée par REACH, seulement 10% des écoles disposent d’un programme d’alimentation scolaire fonctionnel au cours de l’année scolaire 2020 – 2021 au niveau national. Bien les régions du Nord soient plus fournies en cantines scolaires, il y a toujours un gap à combler de 41% des écoles.
Selon une évaluation menée par Plan International Mali en Décembre 2023, il ressort que 81% écoles enquêtées à Mopti et à Gao ne disposent de cantines scolaires fonctionnelles et 91% des écoles enquêtées dont 90% Mopti et 92% à Gao ne disposent pas des jardins scolaires fonctionnels ;
L'intervention vise à améliorer les conditions de vie de 5123 élèves dans la zone de mise en œuvre grâce à une assistance a au moins 11 écoles partenaires en termes de repas, de formation des acteurs, de soutien au jardin. 
Les activités s’inscrivent dans la continuité de l’appui qui a commencé en février 2023 pour une durée de 6 mois. Les écoles partenaires ( Bagoundie I et II, Magnandoue,Ansongo, Bara ans la region de Gao et Bas Fond,Perimpe, Takouti , Ogotena, Joseph Yaro C 2eme Cycle, Kani Kombole 2e cycle dans la région de Mopti) ont déjà les ustensiles et d’autres accessoires comme les kits de lavage de mains, les extincteurs, des fourneaux et un appui financier pour la fourniture des repas chauds aux élèves.

project_name: Renforcement de l’accès des survivant (es) de VBG y compris les victimes d'EAS aux services multisectoriels et réduction des risques d’exposition aux VBG des populations affectées par la crise
project_objective: Le Burkina Faso traverse à l’instar d’autres pays du Sahel, à une crise complexe sans précédent avec pour conséquence, des déplacements massifs de populations entrainant une situation humanitaire très difficile surtout pour les populations déplacées. Selon les nouveaux calculs PiN_Cible_2023 - Cluster Protection VBG, 1 123 183 de personnes au Burkina Faso, sont dans un besoin de protection contre les Violences Basées sur le Genre en raison principalement de la situation sécuritaire très dégradée avec pour corollaire la fermeture des services sociaux de base. Par ailleurs, l’aggravation de la crise, la déscolarisation massive des enfants, en particulier des filles, la perte des moyens de subsistance des ménages les contraignant à l’adoption de stratégies d’adaptation négative sont autant de facteurs qui contribuent à une augmentation de la violence domestique, l’exploitation, les abus sexuels, le mariage et le trafic d’enfants. Cette situation a également fragilisé la situation économique des femmes et des filles, pourvoyeuses des familles et entraine ainsi une limitation de l’accès des populations aux services essentiels tels que la protection, les services liés aux droits et à la santé sexuels et reproductifs (DSSR), et la justice. Dans chaque situation d’urgence humanitaire, ce sont les femmes et les filles qui sont les plus exposées aux risques de violence, y compris les violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre (VSBG), la négligence, l’exploitation et les abus. En effet, la promiscuité des abris, le manque de latrines séparées ou de lumière dans les latrines, les chemins non protégés dans des lieux inconnus pour se rendre au marché/puits, etc. les exposent au harcèlement et a des abus sexuels qui sont en grande majorité non rapportes, faute de mécanisme de référencement clairs et à la culture du silence. Ce projet vise donc, à contribuer au renforcement de la prévention des risques d’exposition aux VBG des populations affectées par la crise et de l’assistance rapide et adaptée pour les survivants (es) de VBG y compris EAS dans un contexte de crise aiguë dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de l’Est du Burkina Faso. L’action présentée est alignée avec la stratégie du sous-cluster VBG, le Plan de réponse humanitaire et la stratégie de réponse globale et nationale de Plan au Burkina Faso. Elle se fonde sur une analyse du contexte prenant en compte les besoins spécifiques des filles et des femmes, des garçons et des hommes et sur l’expérience de Plan Burkina Faso en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des cas de VBG.

project_name: Appui pour une Education inclusive et de qualité pour les enfants déplacés, les réfugiés et la communauté d'accueil  touchés par les crises humanitaires dans ls regions de Tahoua et Tillaberi
project_objective:
""Ce projet vise à lever les obstacles et barrières qui empêchent aux jeunes enfants, déplacés internes, retournés et issus des communautés hôtes des régions de Tahoua et Tillabéry d’accéder à leur droit à une éducation inclusive et de qualité dans un environnement sûr et protecteur grâce à la mise en œuvre d’un programme d'éducation d'urgence dans le système formel et non formel. Le projet s’appuiera sur les structures communautaires et les services techniques de l’État. Environs 15.223 enfants dont 6.530 filles.
Les enfants visés par cet objectif sont:
- Les enfants déjà inscrits à l’école primaire formelle ou ceux ayant l’âge scolaire non encore inscrits. Il s’agit des enfants vulnérables, filles et garçons, de 7 à 12 ans sans discrimination pour l’éducation formelle primaire. 
- Les enfants précocement exclus de l’école ou n’ayant jamais fréquenté l’école. Il s’agit des enfants vulnérables, filles et garçons, de 9 à 17 ans sans discrimination. Cette cible est estimée à environ 400 enfants dont 200 filles.""

project_objective:
In line with the UNICEF Humanitarian Action Appeal and the Health Cluster Humanitarian Response Plan For The 2023 Humanitarian Program, the project is aimed at achieving equitable health outcomes for the vulnerable, most-in-need and hardest-to-reach children. This will be achieved through addressing humanitarian health needs while building the resilience of local communities against health emergencies and linking with development interventions. UNICEF will respond to emerging health emergencies in accordance to the

The nutrition response in 2023 will focus on implementing lifesaving nutrition activities, namely inpatient and outpatient treatment for acute malnutrition, and improving complementary feeding through Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition in Emergencies (MIYCN-E) and the provision of micronutrient supplementation for home fortification. The 2023 HPC is expected to cover the BAY states targeting all the LGAs as much as possible, focusing more on those with the highest burden of children under five suffering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM). Most of these 29 LGAs are also projected to be in the serious and critical phases of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) during the lean season, harvest, and post-harvest periods. High-risk and hard-to-reach locations (such as Gubio, Guzamala, Magumeri, Marte and Rann LGAs) with many Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnee populations will be prioritized for nutrition assistance.

In 2023, UNICEF will primarily target infants and young children with SAM and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) who are vulnerable and nutritionally at risk. The nutrition response will also target all children under five and PLWs with preventive nutrition services such as micronutrient supplementation, to ensure levels of acute malnutrition are not above average thresholds and to reduce morbidity and mortality. The response will prioritize households with persons with disabilities, who face barriers in accessing health, nutrition and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, and who are disproportionately food insecure due to high levels of exclusion. 

The nutrition status of the targeted population in the BAY states significantly deteriorates every year between May and August, which is both the lean season and coincides with the rainy season. This period is characterized by very high rates of acute malnutrition, medical complications due to poor food access, and a high prevalence of diarrhoea, malaria and measles. project_name: UNICEF: Lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative interventions targeting most vulnerable population across Sudan.
project_objective:
The malnutrition situation in Sudan remains dire with an estimated increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition due to the deteriorating nutrition situation following the catastrophic humanitarian crisis. The nutrition sector estimates that 4.6 million children under five, pregnant women, mothers, and caregivers of children under-two will need humanitarian assistance to meet their nutritional needs in 2023.

UNICEF is the sector lead for nutrition, with a mandate to uphold children’s right to nutrition and end child malnutrition in all its forms. UNICEF has been working for children in Sudan over the past 70 years, building and maintaining strong relationships with the Ministry of Health, civil society organisations (CSOs), the private sector, community health and nutrition workers, and other nutrition stakeholders at national and subnational levels, utilising its technical expertise and partnerships to implement effective nutrition programming in the country. 

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and protection minimum package services targeting the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among children under two years, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among children under-five years. UNICEF will prioritize new hotspots and IDP areas while scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services for those already in need.

Over 1.6 million pregnant women, mothers, and caregivers of children under-two, and 5.9 million girls and boys under-five will be reached with a package of essential nutrition interventions for the prevention, early detection, and treatment of child wasting with an estimated cost of USD 346,245,840. However, the total budget for this project is USD 234,700,848 as the estimated target and funding requirement is for seven months from June to December 2023, and not an annual target and funding requirements.

The package of preventive nutrition interventions will be focused on improving diets, services, and practices that protect, promote, and support good nutrition among the most vulnerable children and women, with a specific focus on children under-two. This essential package will ensure that pregnant women have access to good antenatal nutrition, including iron-folic acid; infants benefit from timely and exclusive breastfeeding from birth to six months; and young children receive adequate age-appropriate complementary foods and micronutrients while breastfeeding continues. To facilitate access to nutritious diets and nutrition services, UNICEF will also support the provision of cash transfers targeting 380,000 of the poorest pregnant women/caregivers of children under-two.

UNICEF will strengthen and scale-up early detection and referral of children suffering from wasting using different strategies. To improve access to lifesaving treatment services, UNICEF will scale-up the provision of nutrition curative interventions through the outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP) and strengthen the quality of services. UNICEF will target around 621,600 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition and will procure 808,080 cartons of ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) (including 30 per cent buffer stock).
To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale-up, UNICEF will build on existing nutrition services at the health facility and community level to deliver maternal and child centered integrated nutrition services. As a provider of last resort, UNICEF will scale up the adoption of a ‘simplified approach’ to treat SAM cases until fully cured in all OTPs.

project_name: Provision of WASH Supplies to Strengthen delivery of WASH Services to the conflict affected population in  Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
UNICEF as the provider of last resort, has the accountability for covering critical needs/gaps remaining as a results of new population displacements or diminished capacity/departure of other humanitarian WASH partners in any state throughout Nigeria.
The project is aimed at addressing life-saving WASH assistance to the most vulnerable people affected, displacement (new or continued), flood and mitigate the effects of the current cholera outbreak in the BAY States. This action will also provide complimentary and crucial pipeline support to WaSH partners to better respond to emerging crises and reach an estimated individuals with critical supplies, improve sector coordination within the WaSH to ensure quality and timely assessments and analyses, improve coverage and reduce duplication of services.
Over 516,108 people will be provided with sustained access to safe water through regular water point chlorination (shock chlorination and bucket chlorination) and campaign at community level. Water quality control and emergency water treatment of both clear and turbid water for 50,000 households will be emphasized in communities without communal water sources or relying on rivers and streams as their sources of water. 535,000  people will be provided with hygiene supplies.
The objective of the project is to facilitate the provision of safe water and practice of personal hygiene through sustained chlorination of water points, safe water chain including use of clean containers for water storage and the use of Aqutabs for household water treatment and provision of replenishment hygiene kits and other WASH NFIs.
The envisaged outcome is prevention of disease outbreaks such as cholera, diarrhoea and hepatitis. UNICEF through the common supply will procure water treatment chemicals (Calcium Hypochlorite 65-70% - HTH, Aluminum sulphate, PUR sachet and Aqutabs), inline chlorine dosers and hygiene supplies. These WASH supplies will be prepositioned and used to provide lifesaving WASH services in the hot spot locations affected by displacement (new or continued), cholera and flood. Procured supplies will be distributed to WASH sector partners by UNICEF in line with the WASH sector's needs/gaps analysis and prioritization in response to emergency needs, at the request of the WASH sector coordinator using the sector supply pipeline procedure to access the stock. 
This will be based on satisfactory needs assessment and justification coupled with other compounding factors such as availability of stocks, ensuring no overlapping with other responses, strategy and soundness of the planned response, as well as the sector priority.
The annual requirement of  WaSH supply pipeline for 2023 is estimated  at $23,000,000 This estimate was  done collaboration with WaSH sector partners and based on the humanitarian response plan (HRP).
To meet the demands of the provider of last resort (POLR) responsibility, UNICEF may need to mobilize 50% of the funding requirement i.e ($11,500,000) to provide the initial lifesaving response to the gaps, prioritizing areas receiving newly displaced people, disease outbreak such as cholera, hepatitis or other WASH-related diseases including covid-19.
UNICEF will work together with the sector coordinator and through UNICEF Facilitators to monitor the use of the supplies. These supplies will supplement routine supplies distributed in these locations, and they will target the lifesaving needs of IDP and newly arrivals and host population. project_name: Humanitarian Coordination Assistance for the Syria Response Plan
project_objective:
The 2023 Syria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) sets out the framework within which the humanitarian community will respond to large-scale humanitarian and protection needs in Syria, flexibly leveraging the various response modalities.
Capturing these capacities and efforts under a single strategic framework, the plan aims to increase the effectiveness of the response by improving the identification of needs and gaps, reducing overlap and duplication, and monitoring context changes and progress against collective agreed response results. The Humanitarian Coordinator for Syria and the Regional Humanitarian Coordinator for the Syria Crisis lead and coordinate humanitarian action inside Syria. OCHA, in line with its global mandate, supports the humanitarian leadership in effectively coordinating the response inside Syria. To do so, OCHA maintains country offices in Syria and Turkey, and a regional office in Amman.  OCHA Turkey coordinates cross-border humanitarian assistance delivered from Turkey to Syria as mandated by the UN Security Council resolutions 2642 under the leadership of the Deputy Regional Humanitarian Coordinator (DRHC).
OCHA requires sustained levels of funding to be able to maintain and strengthen effective humanitarian response coordination from these various offices, facilitate strategic and operational coordination platforms, provide information management services, manage pooled funds, support humanitarian access analysis and negotiation, ensure civil-military coordination, and provide public information and advocacy on the
humanitarian situation. Funding requirements for this project reflect the needs of OCHA's three offices directly involved in the Syria response.

project_name: Provision of Life saving Essential health services through  Health System Strengthening, outbreak response and essential PHC services to fragile, conflict affected and vulnerable population in North East Nigeria.
project_objective:
Basic Info
	Project Name	Start Date End Date
Supporting Disease Surveillance, Outbreak and Response with 01/01/2023- 31/12/2023 Provision of Life saving Essential health services and Health system Strengthening to fragile, conflict affected and vulnerable population in North East Nigeria.
Project Summary
1.	This project seeks to strengthen and sustain essential health services and systems for crisis-affected populations, particularly at the Ward level, as well as to respond quickly to health emergencies by leveraging national capacities while gradually enabling local leadership and ownership. The goal is to gradually shift toward a more resilient approach to strengthening the health system's capacity while also responding to acute health emergencies. This plan is in line with the national health strategy, which emphasizes the revitalization and strengthening of the disrupted health system as critical elements for access to better health care service delivery. This plan seeks to achieve a sustainable transition away from the current substitutionary response and toward strengthening systems and local ownership. WHO initiatives will primarily help in three key areas to meet the overall aim of maintaining vital health services and systems:
1. Maintain access to essential health services through the government initiative of one PHC per ward.
2. Create a functional health information management system by integrating platforms such as DHIS, EWARS/SORMAS, and health resource and partner mapping.
3. Promote local ownership by improving government leadership, coordination, and accountability. The project will focus on ensuring effective local leadership, partner coordination, and operations support in the states of Borno, Yobe, and Adamawa, as well as maintaining and improving access and quality of health service delivery. 
Through an innovative strategy of ""health services under one roof,"" it will concentrate on re-establishing operational, staffed, and equipped health facilities to provide health care to vulnerable people, including host communities and returnees, at the ward level. With the overarching goal of restoring health systems and enabling the best possible delivery of health services throughout the BAY states, WHO aims to support the availability of health workers, the formation of a health financing structure, and strengthening the HDN initiative. The WHO will position itself as the last-resort provider of life-saving vital health services in the event of new displacements and acute health emergencies while investing in the improvement of the health system. This will improve the quality of health data and foster peer-topeer learning through effective monitoring & evaluation. State and partners technical and operational capacity for effective coordination and delivery of health services will be strengthened. The provision of essential health services target people in need (in IDP camps and host communities) is a core area of WHO’s support in health emergency response in NEN. This area essentially covers all service provision and support for outbreak response; In 2022, WHO will expand HTR package of services to include FP and NCD/mental health services, align reporting of health data with national HMIS platform with de ne indicators for MHPSS, GBV, and HTS. Advocate for utilization of strategic documents to guide service delivery. Community participation in planning and response to Public health emergencies will be supported and strengthened, support PHC services and advocate for implementation of rural incentive & minimum service package in line with governments policy to curb high attrition rate of health staff. Priority will be given to establish and strengthen health workforce and service delivery in current MHT (Mobile Health Teams) areas while strengthening local ownership and accountability through joint monitoring and supportive supervision.

project_name: Projet d'assistance alimentaire et de soutien aux moyens d'existence de 2 600 ménages déplacés, retournés et hôtes dans les régions du Centre Nord, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective:
Le projet d’assistance alimentaire et de soutien aux moyens d’existence des PDI et ménages hôtes les régions du Nord, du Centre Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun s’inscrit en phase avec le plan de réponse humanitaire 2023 du Burkina Faso et vise à contribuer d’une part à i) sauver des vies face à l’insécurité alimentaire aigüe par la mise en œuvre d’une assistance alimentaire d’urgence visant à répondre aux besoins alimentaires et nutritionnels des personnes les plus vulnérables et d’autre part ii) protéger et reconstituer les moyens d’existence essentiels des populations affectées par les crises alimentaires et soutenir l’amélioration des productions végétales et animales des ménages vulnérables pour prévenir le recours à des stratégies d'adaptation négatives. 
Planifié pour une durée prévisionnelle de 11 mois et un budget total de 1 379 744 USD le projet avec une cible de 11 820 bénéficiaires dont 7 092 PDI, 6 410 Femmes, 350 personnes âgées et personnes vivant avec handicap, le projet sera mis en œuvre dans 11 communes présentant des fortes contraintes en matière de sécurité alimentaire dû à la forte concentration de PDI, le déficit de production durant la campagne agricole et aux difficultés d’accès au marché.  Tenant compte des orientations stratégiques et dans la mesure de la faisabilité, la modalité de cash transfert sera utilisée dans la perspective de faciliter la mise en œuvre du projet et de soutenir le fonctionnement des marchés. Le projet sera développé dans des zones de concentration de Help et cela permettra de créer une synergie entre les interventions et de renforcer les acquis des projets cours. 
La centralité de la protection y compris les la PSEA/VBG (Ne pas nuire ; Accès significatif ; Participation ; et responsabilité envers la population affectée) sera effective dans l’intervention avec la formation et l’information des acteurs de mise en œuvre et des populations bénéficiaires afin de garantir la sureté et la dignité des bénéficiaires et réduire les risques de violations des droits fondamentaux. Des outils de suivi et de référencement seront déployés à cet effet, et le dispositif de redevabilité envers les bénéficiaires hommes et femmes, personnes âgées et personnes vivant avec handicap sera renforcer. Un mécanisme de suivi-évaluation qui va consister à la consultation régulière des bénéficiaires à travers une collecte de données pour renseigner les indicateurs de base et une endline, des enquêtes périodiques, des PDM, des bilan et planification mensuelles, permettra d’assurer la mesure régulière des progrès et de la qualité de l’intervention en tenant compte des spécificités de genre, d’inclusion et de vulnérabilité.
Pour la gestion des plaintes, Help va utiliser et œuvrer à renforcer les mécanismes déjà existants dans chaque zone d’intervention. Ces mécanismes feront l’objet d’une communication adaptée lors des différentes réunions et rencontres avec les bénéficiaires et autres parties prenantes. Help s’engage à donner une suite à chaque plainte de manière individuelle ou collective lorsque les plaintes sont déposées de manière anonyme et cela intègre l’utilisation du numéro vert du PAM qui sera diffusé. Un mécanisme sera en place avec le PAM pour recevoir les données collectées au titre du projet pour les analyses. Le responsable de redevabilité/protection s’assurera de venir en appui aux équipes projets dans la vérification des ouvrages et des processus de distribution pour s’accorder sur la prise en compte de la centralité de la protection.
L’appui sera apporté dans 11 communes qui sont Kaya, Barsalogho, Korsimoro, Pissila et Kaya (province du Sanmatenga), Tougouri et Boulsa (province du Namentenga), Oula, Ouahigouya (province du Yatenga), Gourcy (province du Zondoma) et Tougan (province du Sourou).

project_name: Quality of integrated and equitable health service delivery and effective coverage  to support the health and well-being of children under 5 years and their mothers, including those infected and affected by HIV through strengthening the district and upazila health systems, in Rohingya Refugee Camps and Host Communities affected by the Rohingya Crisis
project_objective: UNICEF will provide support to ensure equitable quality and gender sensitive maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health and immunization services as well as provision of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services including counselling and referral for GBV and support to pregnant and lactating women (inclusive of children with HIV) with inclusion of people with disabilities. The project will focus and ensure adherence with the Minimum Package of Essential Health services for primary health care in PHCs and HPs, and the advance newborn care services in the Field Hospital in the Rohingya refugee camps. UNICEF work with other partners both in health sectors and other sectors to ensure integrated health services are provided. The project will target 424,831 direct beneficiaries (284,446 refugees and 140,385 host communities). The project will be implemented in 13 health facilities in the camps (5 PHCs and 8 health posts) and strengthen advance newborn care and child health services in Hope Field hospital in camp 4, and 1 Diarhoea Treatment Centres (DTCs) as well as strengthening government health system and the health facilities in adjacent host communities in Ukhiya and Teknaf (2 union sub centres and 16 community clinics). Following the 2022 Rationalization exercise in the health sector, UNICEF will observe, explore, and consult regarding the possibility of relocation or closing of HPs in the camps with the transition period at least 6 months to provide sufficient time in consulting with the CiC and awareness of the communities, and upgrade the HP at Camp 16 to be a PHC by midyear as per gap analysis. A special focus will continue to support well functional Newborn Stabilization Unit (NSU) with Kangaroo Mother care, across all the Upazila health complexes and 65 bed Special Newborn Care unit (SCANU) at the district hospital with crucial human resources, maintenance of the equipment, capacity building of the health workers, regular review and follow up, including following up the discharged patients. UNICEF will lead the role in newborn care in the camps and working with other agencies/organization to improve newborn and child health. In addition, we will support the MPDSR to reduce maternal and perinatal (stillbirth and newborn) deaths. UNICEF will continue to play her leading role in supporting vaccine logistic and supply and ensure vaccine availability in all service provision sites in all the camps and host communities in Cox's bazar district. UNICEF will continue to provide technical support, supply and transportation of vaccines and logistic and enhance cold chain capacity, advocacy and social mobilization for strengthening immunization services across all the camps. UNICEF will continue to strengthen the Health Management Information System (HMIS/DHIS2) through deployment of technical staff to the office of the Civil Surgeon and build the capacity of service providers on DHIS2 and support the government in rolling out the e-trackers for improve data collection and monitoring on immunization and maternal health services. Review meeting and constructive feedback will be conducted regularly (monthly and quarterly). UNICEF has developed emergency response plan to ensure better preparedness and response to emergency and disasters including strengthening Infection Prevention and control measures in all the supported health facilities and support the scale up of COVID-19 vaccination program in the camps and host communities.

project_name: Contribuer à la cohésion sociale par une intervention holistique de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre dans les communes de Gisuru et Kinyinya de la Province Ruyigi.
project_objective: IRC propose de mettre en œuvre le projet dans les communes de Gisuru et Kinyinya de la Province Ruyigi afin de contribuer à la cohésion sociale par une intervention holistique de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre (VBGs) dans ces communes, marquées par un accueil très important de rapatriés. Il vise l’amélioration des conditions de vie des personnes vulnérables à travers une assistance digne et adaptée à leurs besoins fournie à temps et dans un environnement de protection afin de réduire leur vulnérabilité aux normes et pratiques néfastes. La pandémie du Covid-19 ainsi que les aléas climatiques ont accentué les problèmes d’inaccessibilité aux services sociaux de protection de base contre les violences, la maltraitance, la négligence et les abus. Ces communes connaissent depuis des décennies des déplacements internes et externes et accueillent des rapatriés burundais venant de l’exil. Ces communautés sont exposées à des risques de protection qui s’accompagnent du développement des mécanismes d’adaptation négatives notamment l’exploitation sexuelle des filles et le sexe de survie. A cela s’ajoute les normes culturelles et sociales négatives qui les exposent à de multiples formes de violence avec une fréquence alarmante au sein de ménages. Différents besoins mentionnés dans les évaluations menées par les acteurs en VBG et du plan de réponse humanitaire 2022, sont entre autres les femmes en âge de procréer en besoin de kit dignité et d’équipement pour des espaces dédiés au soutien psychosocial, le besoin de renforcer les sensibilisations et orientation des bénéficiaires vers les services disponibles et la nécessité de renforcer les services de gestion de cas et les mécanismes communautaires de cohésion sociale. A cela s’ajoute les risques accrus pour les filles au mariage précoce et à l’exploitation sexuelle, le déni des ressources, d'opportunités ou de services ainsi que les cas de violences conjugales. Les femmes évoluent dans un système patriarcal qui est contrôlé par les hommes. Il est important d’identifier et de changer les attitudes et les croyances sous-jacentes qui accordent le pouvoir et l’autorité aux hommes aux dépens des femmes et qui cautionnent la violence envers les femmes et les filles. C’est sur base de ces besoins listées en haut que IRC va contribuer à la cohésion sociale par une intervention holistique de lutte contre les VBGs. Il assurera la gestion de cas centrée sur les survivants et des référencements vers des services appropriés. Pour améliorer la qualité de la gestion de cas de VBG, le renforcement de capacités et le coaching des travailleurs sociaux et des points focaux communautaires seront organisés. Des canaux de référencement seront développés pour faciliter l'accès aux services aux bénéficiaires. Pour contribuer à la réduction des risques, des kits de dignité seront distribués aux survivantes et autres femmes et filles à risque. L’IRC organisera des activités de renforcement des compétences et des activités psychosociales de groupe pour faciliter le rétablissement et la réintégration des survivants de violences et abus. Il travaillera avec les filles via l'approche Girl Shine conçue pour aider à améliorer le bien-être des filles adolescentes en leur fournissant des compétences et des connaissances nécessaires pour identifier les types de VBG et les services de soutien en cas de besoin. Pour renforcer la prévention, les membres de la communauté seront conscientisés sur la sensibilité genre. L’approche EMAP axée sur le changement de comportement individuel menée avec les hommes et guidé par les contributions et voix des femmes sera développée. IRC appuiera les organisations à base communautaire et les ONG locales par des subventions et un renforcement continu des capacités afin de contribuer à l'autonomisation économique des femmes et d'améliorer la qualité des prestations de services.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle aux besoins urgents des populations affectées par les crises sécuritaire et climatique dans la région du Sahel, au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
L’action proposée par le consortium Oxfam-CA vise à répondre aux besoins urgents et prioritaires des populations affectées par les crises sécuritaire et climatique dans la région du Sahel au Burkina Faso, où l’accès aux services sociaux de base est réduit ou interrompu. L’objectif du projet est d’améliorer l’accès des hommes, femmes, filles, garçons et personnes à besoins spécifiques à la nourriture et aux services d'eau-hygiène et assainissement, dans un environnement sûr et protecteur.
Sur une durée de 12 mois, l’action ciblera 32510 personnes déplacées internes et hôtes dans les communes d’accès difficile ou limité et où les besoins ne sont pas couverts : Dori, Déou, Gorgadji, Seytenga, Arbinda et Gorom-Gorom. Le consortium mettra en œuvre un paquet d’activités intégrant une assistance alimentaire et nutritionnelle, un volet eau-hygiène-assainissement et le renforcement de la protection. Sur le plan de la securité alimentaire, l'action vise à fournir une Assistance alimentaire (AA) d’urgence à 11092 nouvelles PDI, une Assistance alimentaire (AA) Post RRM d'une partie de ceux assistés en urgence à savoir 6442 personnes et 12368 personnes issues des ménages TP pendant la periode de soudure. 1603 enfants de 6 à 23 mois de ces ménages beneficieront de la farine infantile pendant au moins 3 mois. l'activité sera accompagné de depistage et de sensibilisation sur l'ANJE. Sur le plan de la WASH, les actions consisteront en des constructions de forages productifs (8), des transformations de PMH en PEA (8), la réhabilitation partielle de 13 PMH, la formation d'artisans réparateurs et le vidange de 100 fosses des latrines et puisards de douches dans les sites d’accueil des PDI et au niveau des familles hôtes. A cela s'associera des activités de sensibilisation à l'hygiène via l'engagement communautaire. sur le plan de la Protection, l'action consitera en des Monitoring de protection (référencement et plaidoyer), la conduite de l'analyse des risques de protection et de genre, la mise en place/redynamisation de comités de protection communautaire (CPC) et Forum des Femmes (FdF) et formations sur les notions essentielles de protection, l'appui aux personnes à besoins spécifiques de protection, l'appui en kits de protection, l'installation des lampadaires solaires pour réduire les risques de protection, la sensibilisations sur les risques de protection (VBG) et promotion de la cohésion sociale.

AGED et SERACOM assureront la mobilisation des beneficiaires, les activités de distribution de vivres sur le terrain. En lien avec les principes et normes humanitaires (CHS, SPHERE, Oxfam inclura  la protection transversale via des analyses continues des risques potentiels liés aux activités :  harcèlement, l’exploitation et abus sexuels (PEAS),  maltraitance des enfants. La Matrice de gestion des risques d’Oxfam sera utilisée pour le suivi et la gestion des risques de protection au cours du projet. De plus, des analyses des risques spécifiques seront menées sur certaines activités comme le cash, la distribution des kits de protection, l’installation des lampadaires solaires et  la construction des forages. project_name: Protección integral a personas en situación de movilidad humana (incluyendo Guatemaltecos en riesgo) en Guatemala.
project_objective:
La violencia se constituye como el riesgo principal que enfrenta la población guatemalteca, solicitantes de la condición de refugiado, así como las personas en movilidad en el país, quienes experimentan regularmente situaciones que ponen en riesgo su vida, seguridad e integridad. Por el alcance, control y violencia ejercida por grupos de delincuencia organizada en la region, las poblaciones están expuestas a delitos violentos, extorsión, reclutamiento forzado y actividades relacionadas con el tráfico de drogas.  Esos afectan especialmente a mujeres, niños, niñas y adolescentes, así como a grupos especialmente marginalizados como la población LGBTIQ+, indígena, en movilidad humana y en condición de discapacidad.
Hasta diciembre de 2023, con este proyecto, ACNUR espera cubrir las necesidades de al menos 280,000 personas. 
ACNUR Guatemala continuará trabajando con el gobierno, la sociedad civil y las comunidades para fortalecer el espacio de protección para refugiados, solicitantes de la condición de refugiado, personas en movimientos mixtos y guatemaltecos en riesgo, mediante la consolidación de iniciativas emprendidas en años anteriores. Para lograr los objetivos de una manera más eficiente, se contemplan intervenciones priorizadas en comunidades con alta presencia de personas a las que servimos, en todas las áreas de responsabilidad. 
En el marco de cuatro orientaciones estratégicas, el ACNUR dará prioridad a las siguientes intervenciones: 
•	PROTEGER: Proporcionar apoyo técnico y operativo a las instituciones estatales para: a) fortalecer el sistema de reconocimiento del estatuto de refugiado y la gestión de fronteras para garantizar el acceso al territorio y al asilo y prevenir la devolución; b) facilitar el disfrute de los derechos y el acceso a los servicios mediante la mejora de las políticas y leyes nacionales, la documentación y los servicios jurídicos. 
•	RESPONDER: a) Facilitar el acceso a las necesidades básicas a través de transferencias monetarias; b) mejorar los servicios del sistema de protección internacional mejorando su infraestructura, capacidad y respuesta de protección; c) reforzar el sistema nacional de protección de la infancia para responder mejor a las necesidades de los niños en movilidad humana, en particular los no acompañados y separados.
•	EMPODERAR: Lograr la inclusión de las personas a las que servimos, mejorar sus capacidades de liderazgo y prevenir la discriminación y la xenofobia a través de intervenciones de CBP en comunidades priorizadas y fortaleciendo la iniciativa Ciudades Solidarias.
•	RESOLVER: a) Responder a los mayores riesgos de protección de los guatemaltecos y refugiados identificando, asistiendo y procesando casos de reasentamiento; b) promover oportunidades de medios de vida mediante el fortalecimiento de las capacidades de las personas a las que servimos, así como de los actores estatales y privados para la inclusión laboral y el espíritu empresarial.
