project_name: Enhancing Community Resilience through Integrated Service Delivery in West and Central Jabal Marra, Central Darfur, Sudan (ECR-ISD Project)
project_objective: Considering the current context in Sudan in particular Central Darfur the project will be implemented in West Jabal Marra (Health and Nutrition) and Zalingei town (Health, Nutrition and WASH). The proposed project will be complimented by other IRS ongoing projects in the target areas. Due to the humanitarian context, (protracted armed conflict and new conflicts that have led to large numbers of IDPs, deaths and destruction of properties) coupled with hyperinflation and civil and political unrest that have caused adverse trickling effects in the target areas, high cost of living, poor harvest due to failed rains and poor agricultural practices, poor health seeking behavior, the area is estimated to be a high priority in the HRP/HNO 2023. The proposed 6-month project will lead to reduced suffering, increased, and maintained human dignity, and lives saved for 154,550 conflict affected people (men 50,847; women 66,920; boys 17,310; girls 19,473) out of which 77,274 will be IDPs, 38,638 Returnees and the remaining 38,638 host community members. The overall project goal is to address the immediate needs of conflict-affected people through integrated health, nutrition and WASH, as identified during IR Sudan’s Needs Assessment and analysis leading up to HRP/HNO 2023. The project will employ a 3 level implementation strategy whereby IRSIRS will do direct implementation of interventions, work with local partner and line ministries and departments and last one being through working with the affected people to achieve project goal. The interventions will be lifesaving, preventive services, improving the quality of services and improving the living conditions, wellbeing and safety of the affected people. Insecurity and threat to life of both affected people and staff and loss of property and displacement still remains a great risk for the project and IRS will work with relevant authorities to reduce the risks involved by strictly adhering to security advisories, full implementing the do no harm policy, conducting security and conflict sensitivity assessments and updating the Conflict Register on a regular basis. IRS has three sub offices in Central Darfur at the State Level in Zalingei, West (Nertiti) and Central (Golo) Jebel Marra where the project will be implemented. The main office is located in Khartoum with over 200 members of staff, 85 (45% Female) of whom are based in Central Darfur. The project staff are based in the West and Central Jebel Marra and Zalingei localities and are able to interact daily with relevant stakeholders including other humanitarian actors, government departments and ministries to facilitate project activities and ensure continued access. Although IRS implements all activities, the team prioritizes collaboration with local actors throughout the project cycle. IRS’ ability to implement quality SRHR and protection programming in such a sensitive context, access to hard-to-reach and conflict-affected areas, and the large amount of institutional donor funding illustrates IRS is highly qualified and accepted as a leading agency in Sudan. In addition, IRS has well-established community relations through well-functioning community structures that will support the project implementation. Members of IRSIRS staff are from the community and speak local languages which supports IR’s continued access and community-based approach, for example the ability to access the IDP camps and IDP informal settlements in Jebel Marra. IRS is uniquely posited as a faith-based organization, enabling IRS to address deeply held beliefs around inclusivity, gender relations, culture, and religion; thus, opening opportunities to contribute to structural and sustainable change.

project_name: Provision of integrated WASH, Education, Health and Nutrition services mainstreamed by protection interventions for war affected IDPs and resident vulnerable host communities in West Kordofan
project_objective:
Islamic Relief Worldwide planning to contribute in provision basic services to communities in El Nuhud and El Khoway Localities of West Kordofan, those impacted by the current crises started on April 15th as a result of ongoing war between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in the country. The intervention targets El Nuhud and El Khoway, located on the highway road linking Darfur and Kordofan States to Khartoum which is the main route for the rebels entering the country. The proposed services align with the revised (HRP) 2023, strategic objectives 1 & 2. This intervention aims to contribute in improving access to Education, WASH, Health and Nutrition and protection services. It is designed to address basic needs of 52,041 individuals, (20,816 women, 18,214 men, 7,806 girls and 5,204 boys), classified as 15,612 IDPs (6,245 male, 9,367 female), 2,602 returnees (1,040 male, 1,562 female), 1,561 refugees (624 male, 937 female) and 32,266 resident vulnerable communities (12,906 male, 19360 female).
In Education, the project targets 7,348 students (4,408 girls and 2,939 boys) focusing on increasing the learning spaces to accommodate the displaced students from North Kordofan and Khartoum, as well as contribute in maintaining attractive schools environment, to both resident students and students fleeing from war areas in El Obeid and Khartoum. The proposed activities aims to increase enrolment of children in child-friendly learning spaces, provide recreational (kits), hygiene kits and establish hand washing stations, provision safe drinking water, rehabilitate latrines, rehabilitate learning spaces and deliver psychosocial support activities. Islamic Relief will implement the project in close coordination with Ministry of Education at State level through direct implementation approach.
In WASH, the project target 18,370 persons (7,348 women, 6,429 men, 2,755 girls and 1,837 boys), including displaced families from war areas to improve their access to WASH services including sanitation and hygiene promotion. WASH activities contain rehabilitation of existing water points to ensure delivery of sustainable water supply. Comprehensive awareness raising campaigns on hygiene and sanitation will be delivered to communities to improve village environment will provide the community with cleaning and waste management tools.
In Health, the project target 15,309 individuals (6,123 women, 5,350 m3n, 2,296 girls and 1,530 boys) to increase access to improved primary healthcare services, by rehabilitating health facilities, strengthening the capacity of health care providers and community health care workers to provide essential health services as well as deliver antenatal care services.
In nutrition, the project target 7,500 individuals, comprised of malnourished girls, boys and pregnant and lactating women focusing on increasing access to improved nutrition services for communities, through management of moderate acute malnutrition for children 6-59 months, deliver Infant and Young Child feeding (IYCF) counselling programming, conduct home-based food fortification with micronutrient supplements to U5 children. The project focus include conduct counselling of pregnant women and caregivers of children 0-23 months as well as early detection of malnutrition among under 5 through MUAC mass screenings/ referral and regular at household level per locality.
For protection, the project targets 6,123 beneficiaries to improve protection conditions and provide support to access basic services with dignity and advocate for their rights to receive quality specialized protection services. The project will consider protection issues, particularly unaccompanied children fleeing from war areas and deliver psychological support to displaced families and focus on issues affecting women and girls in particular.

project_name: Projet d’assistance en soins de santé  aux personne vulnérables affecte par la crise du bassin du lac Tchad ( refugiés,retounés ainsi que les déplaces interne)
project_objective:
Depuis 2009, l’insécurité liée à l’insurrection du groupe Boko Haram et à sa répression s’est diffusée depuis le cœur du Borno nigérian vers tout le nord-est du pays puis vers les zones frontalières des pays voisins, Cameroun, Niger et Tchad. La crise a affecté progressivement toute la région du lac Tchad, un des grands espaces transfrontaliers de l’Afrique sahélienne, à la charnière de l’Afrique des savanes et du désert, de l’Afrique de l’Ouest et de l’Afrique centrale et orientale.
Selon OCHA ,a  la date du 08 Décembre 2022, environ 5,6 millions de personnes sont en situation d'insécurité alimentaire grave, le chiffre le plus élevé depuis quatre ans, et 300 000 enfants souffrent de malnutrition sévère. 2,9 millions de personnes sont déplacées à l'intérieur du pays, dont 2 millions rien qu'au Nigeria, et 624 000 sont des réfugiés. Ces populations se réfugient souvent dans des camps de fortune, ou trouvent refuge auprès de villages d’accueil, plus de 120 villages ou sites ont accueilli des personnes déplacées. Les besoins humanitaires de ces populations restent considérables, tandis que les populations locales, déjà très vulnérables, subissent une pression supplémentaire du fait de leur arrivée.
Cela a des graves conséquences dans la région du Lac au Tchad où la conjonction de ce conflit armé associé à une crise écologique ont poussé au bord de la famine près de 8 millions de personnes.
Cette situation a aggravé les indicateurs d’un système de santé qui étaient déjà faible. Les centres de santé manquent d’équipement, de médicaments et personnel qualifié pour fournir des services médicaux suffisants de qualité.

project_name: Integrated assistance for vulnerable and conflict-affected people in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
Syria ranks among the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, and life-saving assistance is particularly critical as it confronts widespread hunger and disease within the context of a conflict. The need for humanitarian aid is overwhelming: UN-OCHA estimates that 15.3 million Syrians are in need of humanitarian aid in 2023.

This project builds on the ongoing initiatives being implemented by CARE Syria along the emergency, food security, livelihoods, WASH and protection sectors in Northeast Syria. The aim is to continue, expand and scale-up the current programs in order to cover the increasing needs and gaps, and reach more people-in-need, particularly in the host communities and displacement camps of Al-Hassakeh, Deir-ez-Zor and Ar-Raqqa governorates. This integrated, multi-sectoral assistance targets 291,629 vulnerable and conflict-affected people in the governorates of Areesha, Al Hol and Al-Hasakeh sub-districts (Al-Hassakeh governorate);  Kisreh and Sur sub-districts (DRZ governorate), and Ein Issa sub-district (Ar-Raqqa).

CARE Syria’s ‘Impact Hypothesis’ for this project is in line with the HRP Strategic Objectives of ‘saving lives’ (SO1), ‘enhanced protection’ (SO2) and ‘increased resilience and access to services’ (SO3). “If the targeted households have immediate access to emergency NFI kits [emergency/NFI]; If they have improved access to cash assistance, livelihood inputs and capacity strengthening activities [FSL]; If they have increased access to safe and adequate water, sanitation, and hygiene services and improved hygiene practices [WASH]; and If protection risks to affected persons is mitigated and women and girls’ vulnerability to gender-based violence is reduced [Protection]; THEN vulnerable households and communities in NES can be able to increase their long-term resilience, reduce their vulnerability to future shocks and disasters, and improve their overall wellbeing.” 

This project traverses the continuum between the provision of humanitarian aid, early recovery approaches and resilience building, with the ultimate goal of seeking sustainable and longer-term solutions to Syria’s most immediate and pressing needs. Specifically, this project is grounded in several elements including:

Building on a nexus approach to incorporate life-saving assistance while laying the groundwork for early recovery and resilience: All four sectors are focused on providing life-saving assistance given the gravity of the humanitarian crisis in NES as well as in line with HRP’s priorities, but also laying the groundwork for early recovery and resilience through: income-generating activities; skills development and entrepreneurial initiatives; agricultural/livestock inputs and trainings; market linkages; upgrades to critical livelihoods and water infrastructure and more reliable sources of water supply; and, enhanced skills for women and girls to have more control over their lives/ability to make informed choices.

Applying a combined focus on IDPs and host communities: This project will serve both communities in an effort to reduce tensions between the two groups and recognize the host communities’ vulnerabilities so they remain resilient and able to continue to host IDPs. 
 
Integration between sectors and humanitarian actors: CARE Syria has deepened its integration approach across all its programs so that the activities in the sectors are mutually reinforcing and have an amplified effect on the outcomes of the other sectors. For example, WASH, health and nutrition awareness will support one another to promote uptake of behaviors which will have a combined improvement on the overall well-being of the beneficiaries. FSL and protection are linked whereby women who seek livelihoods assistance but also require GBV response will be supported through survivor-centered approaches to enable access to life-saving services and strengthened referral systems for additional support.

project_name: Light infrastructure rehabilitation and efficient use of water (irrigation canals, wells and irrigation systems).
project_objective:
Overall, the Food Security Sector (FSS) estimates that 12 million people in Syria are facing acute food insecurity, which is at least 54.4% of Syria population. While the food insecure figures have slightly declined by at least 4% compared to last year’s record increase, the number of people facing acute food insecurity remains extremely high.,. Drought-like conditions water scarcity and very low availability of energy supplies in Syria are affecting agriculture production capacity, thus affecting farmer’s livelihoods and local food production.  In this context, FAO has designed a programme to assist 92,903 small-scale farming households (equivalent to 557,419 people) in Syria, with the objective of protecting and enhancing the livelihoods of vulnerable farmers and IDPs through the restoration of critical irrigation infrastructures and improve water use efficiency to increase household food production and food security. 
. The project outputs include:
•	Output 1: Critical small-scale irrigation infrastructures in the targeted governorates are assessed and light rehabilitation undertaken. 
•	Output 2: Capacity of technical staff and relevant stakeholders including farmers strengthened to increase water use efficiency and establishment of Water Users Associations (WUAs)
A training programme on enhancing irrigation management, water use efficiency in small-scale irrigation, agricultural land management will be based on FAO standards and approaches. It is expected that stakeholders and farmers will participate in the proposed trainings. 
This programme is expected to contribute to increasing access to irrigation water for crisis-affected farmers and their families in the targeted areas through the light rehabilitation of critical small scale irrigation infrastructure. Crop cultivation and other agricultural practices, including livestock and animal feed production, will consequently benefit from the improved water supply plans as an emergency response to the prevailing crisis and drought-like conditions. The proposed intervention will strengthen household food production capacities, skills and knowledge and address immediate food security and nutrition needs, through increasing local availability and supply of food. This may in turn promote flourishing of agricultural based livelihoods in the targeted rural communities, which would contribute to social cohesion, peace and stability. The programme seeks to utilize intensive labour in order to maximize community participation and inject cash into the local community.

project_name: Fortalecimiento y rehabilitación de los medios de vida de las poblaciones afectadas en la temporada de postrera por la fuerte temporada de lluvias y tormenta tropical Julia, en Honduras.
project_objective:
Honduras es uno de los países de más alto riesgo de desastres del mundo y de los más afectados por eventos climáticos extremos, como inundaciones, huracanes y sequías. Estos choques recurrentes son cada vez más intensos y se vinculan con la migración.

Los pronósticos para la siembra del ciclo de primera 2022 fueron favorables, sin embargo, este se vio limitado a causa de los altos costos de los insumos agrícolas. Los fertilizantes alcanzaron un incremento y superaron el 100%, sumado a la recurrencia de pérdidas por cosecha y faltas de financiamiento, provocando que se decida no sembrar o una reducción en las áreas de cultivo. 

La situación de inseguridad alimentaria agudizada en 2022. Se calcula que por lo menos 2.6 millones de personas (28% de la población clasificada; 51% mujeres, 49% hombres) se encuentra en condiciones de inseguridad alimentaria aguda en fases de Crisis o Emergencia (Fase 3 o 4 de la Clasificación Integrada de la Seguridad Alimentaria en Fases (CIF)) y requieren acciones urgentes. De los 18 departamentos del país, 17 se clasificaron en Fase 3, excepto Islas de la Bahía (Fase 2).  Los departamentos con la mayor severidad de inseguridad alimentaria aguda en Fase 3 o 4 de la CIF son Gracias a Dios (45%), Santa Bárbara, Lempira y La Paz (37%%), de los cuales los dos últimos son productores de granos básicos de subsistencia y cultivo de café (CIF, 2022). 

Según el resumen preliminar de Evaluación de Daños y Perdidas (por sus siglas en inglés (DaLA, 2022), el impacto más severo lo recibió el sector agrícola. Las múltiples crisis en 2020-2022 y los pronósticos climáticos indican que la probabilidad que El Niño se mantiene baja hasta abril-junio de 2023 (49% de probabilidad), y se convierte en la categoría dominante a partir de entonces con probabilidades en el rango del 60-66%, situación que ponen en alerta el ciclo productivo de 2023, más el alta persistente de los insumos agrícolas se podría observar una siembra en extensión menor, uso menor de fertilizantes o no utilizarlos, lo que repercutirá en el volumen de la cosecha, limitando las reservas alimentarias. La expectativa de rendimientos menores al promedio significará una reducción en la disponibilidad de granos básicos para el autoconsumo y una mayor dependencia en la compra en el mercado, sin embargo, la inflación alimentaria continúa por arriba de los valores reportados el año anterior, con variaciones del 12.1, 17.3 y 13.1 por ciento , comprometiendo el poder adquisitivo de los próximos meses, lo que a su vez tiene repercusiones en el acceso a los alimentos. 

Ante dichos pronósticos, es urgente las acciones humanitarias de los hogares en fase 3 y 4 de la CIF  a fin de fortalecer los medios de vida agrícolas para una mejora de la situación de seguridad alimentaria y nutricional. La próxima “temporada agrícola de primavera”, que puedan aprovechar las precipitaciones en el ciclo de primera que comienza en mayo a agosto, es una verdadera oportunidad para apoyar a los agricultores afectados permitiendo una disponibilidad de alimentos de granos básicos y hortalizas en las zonas rurales proporcionándoles semillas de ciclo corto e insumos productivos, establecimiento de áreas de pastos de corte para producción de forraje y alimentación para la alimentación animal, así como los sistemas de riesgo, bloques nutricionales y concentrados caseros para apoyar el nutricional animal en temporada seca, así como  combinar el control zoosanitario para atender enfermedades especialmente en aves como; Newcastle, gripe aviar, gumboro en vacas carbón sintomático, edema maligno y pasterurellosis  las cuales se pueden desarrollar en la próxima estación de verano. 

Más específicamente, este proyecto brindará asistencia agrícola, pecuaria y pesca 16500 hogares vulnerables en 9 departamentos Santa Barbara, Copán, Lempira, Intibucá, Ocotepeque, Choluteca, Francisco Morazan, Valle, El Paraiso en 55 municipios.

project_name: Provision of NFIs and seasonal items to IDPs, returnees, and host communities
project_objective:
UNHCR as a lead agency coordinating the NFI responses in Syria and from Gaziantep (Turkey), will provide through this project the lifesaving and life sustaining NFI support, through two distribution activities of in kind NFIs 1) Core relief items 2) seasonal supplementary items targeting the most vulnerable returnees, IDPs (Internal Displaced Persons), and affected host communities. 70% of our intervention is directed to the returnees, 30% to the IDPs and affected host communities of which 80% for the IDPs and 20% for the affected host communities.
The project is in line with both the priorities of the HRP and Sector Strategy and the project will be completed in line with Sector guidance. UNHCR’s NFI programme recognizes the different needs and vulnerabilities of boys, girls, men, and women of different ages and strives to address the specific needs of each group through a range of NFI interventions. Emergency NFI response will be provided through inter-agency convoy deliveries to hard-to-reach locations, NW Syria, NE Syria situations and camp context and through distribution of seasonal and complementary items. UNHCR planning to allocate almost 20,000 kits as contingency planning for emergency response in 2023
This project aims to assist some 2.2 million individuals with emergency NFIs kits and seasonal NFI kits (winter/summer items). The response will be implemented from Turkey with targeting 35,000 HH (20,000 HH CRIs and 15,000 HH CRI winter kits) and from inside Syria with 2,177,500 (956,125 HH CRIs and 1,221,375 HH CRI winter kits). The overall project targets for two types of assistance package, however a portion of beneficiaries will receive both types of kits, depending on their needs and the season in which assistance is provided. NFI kits will be provided to IDPs, returnee families and host communities, in line with vulnerability criteria. A standard winter kit will be provided as one-time distribution in addition to the NFIs.  UNHCR planning to provide cash for NFI in various locations based on the outcome of the initial pilot project being implemented. The Cash for NFI project is one-off NFI assistance to PoCs in various locations and as it will be expanded based on the pilot project outcome and it will take for the planning year up to 10% of the total budget allocated for NFI provision.

project_name: Protect endangered livelihoods of vulnerable female and male farmers and herders in the West Bank and Gaza Strip through securing time-critical indispensable inputs and services
project_objective:
The overarching objective is to provide time-critical and quick-impact support to the vulnerable farming and herding households affected by man-made and natural shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the global supply shocks induced by local and global crises such as the Russia-Ukraine war. Special focus will be placed on women and youth, and the integration of women in the decision-making process throughout the project. The project aims at ensuring the resilience and protection of the targeted communities and reviving their livelihoods, affected by the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic, the May 2022 Gaza escalations and the food security impacts of the local and global supply shocks. This project falls under HRP 2023 Strategic Objective 3 and the Food Security Sector SO 1: “The resilience of vulnerable households are protected, and their livelihoods, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced"" of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2022, as it improves the coping abilities and reduces shocks and environmental hazards of farmers and herders, with special focus on women and youth in those communities.
This project ensures accessibility and inclusion of all stakeholders regardless of their background, geographical location, or social status. A clear Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) confidential reporting process will be distributed and explained to all stakeholders, including beneficiaries and partners.

project_name: Multisector WASH and GBV response in Gaza
project_objective:
DanChurchAid/Norwegian Church Aid (DCA/NCA) and its partners, MAAN Development Centre (MAAN) and Women Affairs Centre (WAC), propose a multisectoral WASH-GBV project in the North Governorate of Gaza strip - Al Siafa area (Al Amrekyia) in Beit Lahia and Al Masreyeen area (Al Farata) in Beit Hanoun
The WASH component (through MAAN) will address the HNO needs indicators related to the limited access of people to 1) improved functional and safe sanitation facilities at HH level, 2) sanitation services at community level and 3) enough water for drinking and domestic purposes. 

The GBV component (through WAC) will address the HNO needs indicators related to1) Improving GBV response, 2) Improving GBV case management, 3) Increasing focus on GBV prevention and risk mitigation

WASH objective: The project aims at improving the access of underserved people to safe and equitable WASH services. 

SO1: Women, girls, men, and boys are enabled to improve hygiene practices and have access to hygiene items to protect against WASH related health risks
SO2: Women, girls, men and boys’ access safe, appropriate, and hygienic sanitation services and facilities. 
SO3: Women, girls, men, and boys’ access safe, equitable and sustainable quantity of water for drinking, cooking, and personal hygiene

The WASH component contributes to HRP Strategic Objective 2: The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL, and the WASH Cluster Objective 2: Ensure equitable, affordable, and sustainable safely managed access to sufficient WASH services for the most vulnerable Palestinians.

GBV Objective: 
SO1 SGBV survivors safely access quality, survivor-centered mental health and psychosocial support focused on healing, empowerment, and recovery.
SO2 GBV survivors access appropriate, quality case management services including coordinated care and support to navigate available services.
SO3 SGBV programming addresses harmful social norms and systemic gender inequality and informs communities about available services.

The GBV component (through WAC) is in line with the HRP Protection Cluster Strategic OBJECTIVE 2: Protection response mechanisms are in place to prevent and mitigate the effects of the occupation and conflict related violence.
The WASH partner (MAAN) will identify the most vulnerable families with deteriorated WASH conditions (based on socioeconomic and technical assessments) to improve access to WASH services. This will be followed by the GBV response (by WAC). 

WASH component will include the rehabilitation of in-house WASH facilities, installation of sewer lines, distribution of water storage tanks, rehabilitation of desalination plant, hygiene promotion (HP) and hygiene material support via e-voucher system. GBV component will include referral and case management, psychosocial support (PSS), protection and GBV related awareness, legal counselling, and cash for case management services. 
Complementarity and harmony will be ensured between the two components, where proper coordination will take place for this purpose. DCA/NCA and its partners are active members in the UN clusters and will be engaged effectively in all the processes and activities including joining meetings, coordinating the response and provision of information needed for the 4 W’s systems.
WASH stakeholders include the WASH cluster focal point in Gaza North (Save the Children), CMWU and the Municipalities in the tarted locations. DCA/NCA and MAAN have already coordinated the planned intervention with CMWU, PWA and WASH cluster focal point in the Gaza north. 
GBV stakeholder include Protection cluster in Gaza and GBV SWG Coordinator and members, and GBV specialized actors of case management services, DCA/NCA and WAC have already coordinated the planned intervention with Protection cluster focal point in the Gaza.

project_name: Emergency WASH in Nutrition Support to needy Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
This emergency WASH response is to support conflict affected and food insecure populations in 4 counties 3 of which are part of the 15 counties of the South Sudan WASH Severity Classification 4 (WSC 4) for 2022. The project aims to provide support for basic WASH services to households, healthcare centres and nutrition therapeutic centres, including COVID 19 prevention and mitigation support. This is a 9-month project that will have a strong component to support and mainstream GBV, AAP and disability inclusion into the project. The project is focused on supporting communities that have been affected by floods, intercommunal violence including displaced and host communities whose access to safe water has been constrained resulting in the high prevalence for poor WASH related diseases and high rates of malnutrition which is compounded by poor WASH services.

The project will mostly focus on the improvement of access to safe water through (1) rehabilitation of existing hand pumped boreholes (2) surface water treatment  (3) household water treatment and provision of water handling and storage containers (4) construction of flood proof institutional latrine construction (5) hygiene promotion including the mainstreaming COVID 19 preparedness and prevention initiatives (6) distribution of hygiene kits. 

The project will work to achieve its objectives through WASH Cluster Sectoral objective 1, to achieve the HRP Strategic Objective 1. The project will reach a total of 355,969 people with a budget of 713, 320 USDs. NCA will be directly responsible for the implement this project working in partnership with two national partners this approach will ensure the localisation of aid as well as capacity building of local entities. 

NCA being an international ecumenical actor has commitments under the grand bargain to support local partners to deliver humanitarian assistance to a high quality and degree and this project will also ensure resilience of local communities and CBOs in WASH service provision by having components that will promote resilience through training water committees, supporting local government actors and line ministries in WASH service provision. NCA has a static presence in Budi, Kapoeta South, Gogrial East, Tonj North and Gumuruk in Pibor. NCA is also implementing activities in Kapoeta East, Tonj East and Aweil South counties.

project_name: Satisfactory services of shelter life-saving provided in-camp and off-camp settings achieving social cohesion, through improving the shelter conditions for the most vulnerable populations suffering from undignified shelters, accompanied by providing NFI assistance in Idleb and Aleppo governorates
project_objective:
This project is to respond to the need for life-saving shelter and NFI assistance in Aleppo and Idleb, targeting IDP sites and host communities to increase social cohesion and provide equal access to humanitarian aid.
The project has four components as follows:

* In communities/villages:
1)- Individual Shelter Rehabilitation” (HH level). (Target: 1,500 HHs / 7,500 individuals / 800$ per shelter unit/HH house) – to “rehabilitation of collective centers”.
2)- Individual Shelter Rehabilitation” Light repair for partially-damaged individual houses, valued at (600-1,000 USD, average of 800 USD) for 1,500 HHs (7,500 ind).
* Assistance is determined as a technical assessment of each house/unfinished building, and BINAA will follow SNFI Cluster Guidance to ensure the scope of work matches the standards, dignity, privacy, and protection.
Shelter repair beneficiaries will be IDP and HC HHs living in an inadequate shelter that does not meet minimum SPHERE minimum standards for square meters of covered living space per person and has inadequate privacy or protection, by targeting houses that have light to average damage but remain structurally sound, the works include doors and windows repair or replacement, partition installation, sealing cracks and holes in walls, and WASH facilities repairs to increase privacy and enhance gender-sensitive response.
Furthermore, for HHs with PwDs, BINAA will follow Washington Tool and do additional work to respond to PwDs' needs, including disability-friendly entrances and toilet facilities, a ramp with a handrail for using wheelchairs, and seating provisions for toilets.

* In Camps/IDP Sites:
3)- Targeting 800 HHs (4,000 ind) by replacing 800 un-secured, un-protected, non-privacy, and un-dignified tents with 800 dignified shelter units.
The shelter design is classified as dignified, more sustainable, and made of sandwich panels for walls and roofs, PVC internal doors, and windows. Each unit is equipped with a toilet, bathroom, and kitchen, in addition to the final flooring layer through the CFW program.
Moreover, BINAA circulated individual discussions using Consultation Forms, surveyed 16 IDP sites, and introduced 11 shelter solutions ""as per SNFI-Dignified Shelter Guideline"".
That 97% of residents had stated acceptance to such the module for:
- Local availability of skills and materials
- 25 m2 Inter-area
- 5 m2 Covered living space per person (match SPHERE)
- Low-cost design using shared-walls partitions without any effect on privacy
- Min 10-year lifespan
- High protection against weather, fire, dust, wind, rain, snow, and insects
- High privacy and security
- Easy removal and re-use units by local skills
The interlinked SNFI, WASH, and ERL activities are developed with the Clusters to ensure the best integration.
SNFI:
1. Replacing 800 tents with Dignified Shelters solution
2. Constructing 1bath, 1WC, and 1kitchen for each unit
3. Constructing special facilities for PwDs
4. Road graveling in camp
5. Camp lighting
6. Constructing a rain drainage system, 7. Paving people's pathways with stones, and 8. Paving special ramps and entrances for PwDs, all are integrated with the ERL CFW Program.
WASH:
1- Extending and maintaining the Sewage and Water Networks to connect the Units' WASH facilities
2- Installing a 500-liter tank for each unit
3- Construct a high water tank, 80 m3 in the camp
4- Equipping the existing borewell
5- Providing 200 Trash containers (100-liter)
6- Supporting operation costs and WASH services (septic tank desludging and waste removal) for 3-months
7- Hygiene awareness
ERL:
Integrate 250 CFW workers in:
1. Flooring works for the units
2. Paving the rain drainage system with stones
3. Paving the pathways with stones
4. Paving special ramps and pathways for PwDs

* In camps and communities:
4)- Provide to the accommodated 6,800 households (34,000 ind), an NFI assistance (Winter-Labelled CASH) valued at 150 USD, in one go, in Dec, as per the SNFI Cluster Guide.

project_name: Improve safe and adequate access for the IDP’s and Host Community to the WASH services in north Syria
project_objective: The project will target the IDP’s and Host Community in the targeted locations in order to improve the safe, adequate, and sustainable access for these services along with the improvement for the public health and environment to avoid any outbreaks caused by contamination of the drinking water and lack in the SWM which might cause an outbreak in leishmaniasis either cholera. In this project the rehabilitation for water system, sanitation system, and restoration for the SWM system. Moreover, rehabilitation for water system will target increasing the efficiency of the water station and network by conducting the needed maintenance, replacement, and extension for the existing infrastructure and water station as well along with establishment for water ow meters in order to re-activate the tariff system. Rehabilitation for the sanitation system will target maintenance for the sewage network to repair the leakage points to avoid the mixture between drinking water and wastewater along with conduct needed extension for the network in order to ensure that all shelters and settlements are connected to the sewerage network to ensure the best practice for wastewater disposal along with install for rain drainage in the targeted communities and collective centers to avoid ods which caused by heavy rain. The Solid Waste Management restoration will cover distribution for the containers in the targeted areas along with providing the needed equipment, trucks, and tools to the local council/ authorities to collect and transfer the solid waste to the related landll which will also be rehabilitated. Distribution for Hygiene kits (WASH NFI supplies) will be considered for the IDP’s in Camps and communities one-two times during the project duration the in 2022 and 2023 (104,142 beneciaries) will receive a hygiene kit (WASH NFI's) based on the need along with consideration for age and gender in each family along with hygiene promotion session for each family, where the main topic will be COVID 19 pre-cautionary measures. project_name: Protection assistance for displacement affected communities in Sudan
project_objective:
Humanitarian and protection needs, and risks have been widened, expanded and deepened by the 15 April war in Sudan. Affected populations in Khartoum, Gederaf, Al Jazirah, North Darfur, West Darfur and South Kordofan continue to face significant challenges to access safety, dignified life, freedom, and essential documentation and enforce their rights to housing, land, and property. The 15 April 2023 war has heightened pre-existing risks facing civilian population on the move, in camps, gathering sites, hibernating or transit points. 
This protection project will aim to support displacement affected communities and individuals on the move, in camps, gathering sites, in hot spots and in at-risk locations - to claim their rights and access humanitarian and protection services through an integrated NRC protection intervention of Information and Legal Counselling Assistance (ICLA), Site Management, and Protection from Violence. Under ICLA, this will be by; 1) promoting the exercise and enjoyment of housing, land and property rights through creating awareness on HLP rights and contributing towards conflict prevention and non-escalation through promoting the peaceful resolution of disputes over land and natural resources. 2) Improving access to legal identity and civil documentation which will in turn result in the enjoyment of basic services such as education, health, and financial inclusion. Furthermore, the project will 3) work to improve living conditions and access to services in site and site like settings through Site Management through increased participation of women, youth, elderly and people living with disabilities in site governance, refer complaints and feedback to humanitarian service providers at site/camp level.  
 The HLP component will 1) ensure that displacement affected communities are better informed about their HLP and legal identity rights through information sessions, information education and communication (IEC) materials, mobile counselling, individualized legal assistance and support for collaborative dispute resolution 2) enhance understanding amongst authorities, community leaders, and humanitarian actors on HLP rights and the importance of legal identity and civil documentation through integrated capacity building and 3) promote HLP mainstreaming through adoption of due diligence approach before humanitarian interventions which have an implications on land use and ownership. 
For Site Management, the project will work with committees for women, youth, elderly, and people living with disability (PDW) to ensure participation in site management. Build the capacity and awareness of local actors such as community representatives, government officials and local NGOs on Site Management and integrated protection elements. Provision of space for all actors for inclusive engagement. A Complaint, Feedback and Referral Mechanism (CFRM) will run throughout the project in both mobile and static modality. 
Protection from Violence (PfV) will focus on protection monitoring, protection risk mapping and assessment, and protection advocacy, community-based protection towards mitigating protection risks and violence, providing individual protection assistance, and capacity building of different actors (staff, partners, local authorities, community leaders) towards improving safe and inclusive humanitarian and protection response, safe access to basic and protection services, respect of rights and protection of civilians, among others, and information dissemination and awareness raising on rights, entitlements, available services, and CFRMs. 
The project will reach target unique beneficiaries of 55 910 (60% female and 40% male) vulnerable displacement affected individuals with a budget of USD$ 7 136,640.  This updated project contributes to SO1 livesaving and SO2 Protection of the HRP. Gederaf and Al Jazirah state were added as an adjustment too.

project_name: Improved food security for people affected by displacement in Gedaref and White Nile States
project_objective:
The project will contribute to the Sudan humanitarian response plan and specifically the food security and livelihoods (FSL) sector as it focuses on addressing life threatening, life protection and life-sustaining needs through timely provision of life saving cash/vouchers assistance for the purchase of agricultural inputs and garden tools to reduce mortality and morbidity of the affected people while supporting and protecting livelihoods activities. The project will support a target of 18,000 individuals (10,800 females and 7,200 males) comprised of 10,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (6,000 Females, 4,000 Males), and 8,000 non-displaced vulnerable people (4,800 Females, 3,200 Males) in Gedaref and White Nile States prioritizing new displacements due to the ongoing armed conflict. 
NRC focuses on needs-based approach to reach the most in need locations and groups while promoting the Do No Harm principle and protecting target beneficiaries, staff and other stakeholders from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).  The project will make use of NRC’s community engagement toolkit to communicate and engage with the target communities in deciding on the beneficiary selection criteria and the implementation of the activities.  Socio-economic vulnerabilities based on age, gender, disability, and nutrition status will be considered in the beneficiary selection criteria for the life-saving interventions.  Children under the age of five, pregnant and lactating women, all gender types, the youth, women, girls, people with disabilities, the elderly and chronically ill people make up a special target group for NRC’s food security projects.  
Analysis of the situation in terms of gaps, capacities and market functionality will precede response to inform the project on the most suitable modality for project interventions.   Nutrition awareness messaging with special focus on food hygiene and diet diversity will be developed and shared with the target groups.  The project will also include market support interventions through the provision of cash grants to identified small scale traders to enhance their capacity to stock food commodities in their shops and to sustain their businesses while increasing food commodities on the local markets for displaced people.
To ensure accountability to affected populations (AAP) the project will use NRC’s locally tested complaints and feedback handling mechanism (CFM) that has multiple channels that the affected people can use to register their complaints and feedback. The system allows for recording and follow-up of sexual exploitation and abuse cases related to the project implementation.  The monitoring and evaluation activities capture achievements on project objectives and target beneficiaries’ satisfaction of their engagement and treatment during project implementation.

project_name: Provisión de servicios especializados de protección, el fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de autoprotección civil y la respuesta de protección nacional en El Salvador
project_objective:
En El Salvador, las personas desplazadas oscilan entre 114.000 (ACNUR) y 175.000 (IDMC); según datos de gestión de casos, la amenaza de muerte (26,7%) es la primera causa de desplazamiento perpetrada por maras (39,6%) y pandillas (20,5%). A fines de 2021, había 153,249 personas solicitantes de asilo de El Salvador a nivel mundial y 52,041 personas refugiadas salvadoreñas en todo el mundo. En 2021, casi 9,200 personas salvadoreñas fueron retornadas principalmente desde Estados Unidos de América y México. En el mes de agosto de 2022 la autoridad salvadoreña de asilo reportó 160 personas refugiadas reconocidas y 43 solicitudes de asilo en el país se propone asistir las víctimas de desplazamiento forzado (IDPs, solicitantes de asilo y deportados) a través el manejo de casos de protección, que permite a través de un proceso estructurado y especializado, acompañar las personas de interés en la mitigación de sus riesgos de protección debido a la violación de derechos con el fin de garantizar, y en última instancia, reclamar sus derechos, lo que conduce a un incremento de la seguridad, dignidad y a un fortalecimiento de la resiliencia. 

Las comunidades son las que mejor conocen el contexto y el entorno en el que viven, y desarrollan capacidades y estrategias de autoprotección frente a daños adversos. Por ende, este proyecto pone las comunidades y los individuos al centro del programa de protección, con el objetivo de prevenir y mitigar la violencia que afecta la sociedad salvadoreña.  

En el marco de los servicios especializados de protección, se propone implementar asimismo intervenciones de información, orientación y asistencia legal con el fin de facilitar acceso a mecanismos de protección internacional (e.g. condición de refugiado) y reconocimiento de estatuto o estancia legal (e.g. protección subsidiaria, regularización migratoria, residencia, naturalización), así como a los derechos de identidad legal (obtención de documento nacional de identidad, carnet de minoridad, acta de nacimiento, matrimonio, defunción, antecedentes penales, solvencias policiales) y de vivienda, tierra y propiedad (por ejemplo, confirmación de derechos de propiedad/uso, resolución colaborativa de disputas, legalización de herencia). Esto se verá acompañado de acciones de incidencia a favor de la adaptación de prácticas que mejoran la respuesta a las necesidades de los beneficiarios en materia de protección internacional y reconocimiento de estatuto o estancia legal, identidad legal y derechos de vivienda, tierra y propiedad; y de iniciativas de  fortalecimiento del tejido institucional, humanitario y comunitario que buscan la creación de capacidades de funcionarios de instituciones públicas y mecanismos comunitarios para que estén mejor equipados para asumir sus responsabilidades en cuanto al respeto y protección de derechos, así como de actores humanitarios y organizaciones de sociedad civil para llevar a cabo de manera efectiva acciones de incidencia y/o protección de estos mismos derechos. 
 
Con la finalidad de proteger a la niñez y adolescencia en desplazamiento, en riesgo de desplazamiento, deportado y/o afectado por las situaciones de violencia del contexto (OSV), se implementarán espacios a nivel comunitario para que puedan participar y mejorar el aprendizaje, motivación y autoprotección de sus derechos para responder y estar preparados en estos contextos. 
  
NRC considera vital el fortalecimiento de capacidades de protección entre las instituciones gubernamentales para prevenir y responder al desplazamiento, mitigar sus consecuencias, fortalecer los mecanismos de protección nacional, fomentar la protección de los derechos para las personas desplazadas. Por esta razón, el NRC organizará una intervención de fortalecimiento de capacidades destinada a mejorar la respuesta de protección, promover la correcta gestión de la información de protección (PIM), mejorar la coordinación, promover la complementariedad y evitar la duplicación con el objetivo.

project_name: Displacement affected children and youth have access to inclusive quality education in a safe and protective learning environment
project_objective:
The proposed action seeks to address acute education needs for newly displaced children and youth in Sudan. According to the revised 2023 Sudan Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), approximately 8.6 million children require humanitarian support to continue or resume their formal education. Approximately 6.9 million school-aged children (6-18 years of age) were out of school during the 2021-2022 academic year. The project will therefore focus on both formal and non-formal education with alternative learning programmes such as accelerated learning and catch-up to accommodate the needs of both in-school and out of school children (OOSC).
NRC will support a total of 141 026 leaners (50 % female and 5% children with disabilities) with access to inclusive quality education in a safe and protective learning environment. First priority locations in line with Education Sector priority one are White Nile, Gedaref and South Kordofan. Second priority locations North Darfur, West Darfur, and Khartoum will only be supported when the security situation allows for safe access and continued programming.
The action will focus on life saving psychosocial support activities under the NRC Better Learning Programme (BLP), a non-specialized, classroom-based psychosocial support program that aims at equipping the children with strategies to cope with stress and promote their psycho-social well-being. It includes a targeted capacity building for teaching staff and community volunteers to ensure sustainability and promote the psychosocial well-being of learners. Through BLP, teachers and learners are equipped with recreational strategies to cope with stress using practical and adaptable exercises that are integrated into classroom activities and includes a targeted capacity building to teaching staff to ensure sustainability and promote psychosocial well-being to students. Schools will be provided with appropriate recreational materials for both boys and girls, and different ages to facilitate play and entertainment to relieve stress. NRC will strengthen school level child protection initiatives and referral pathways, thereby contributing to resilience building and improved child protection.
The action will also incorporate teacher support and capacity enhancement to improve teacher capacity and contribute to improved teaching and learning. The project will support 1410 (705 male/705 female) teaching personnel (teachers and volunteers). Parent and Teachers Associations (PTAs) and Mother Groups will be targeted to participate in school level decision making and promote displaced girls’ access to education.
Project response components will also include provision of education supplies in the form of teaching and learning materials. The project will also focus on improving the learning environment through rehabilitation of WASH facilities, that is, through construction and rehabilitation of latrines and handwashing facilities. Increased access to safe water will be supported. Gender responsive programming will be promoted through awareness campaigns and community engagement, and 50% of project beneficiaries will be female. Adolescent female learners’ menstrual health and hygiene will be supported through provision of sanitary kits to promote their access to education and retention. School level hygiene awareness campaigns will be implemented to contribute to Personal Health and Hygiene Education (PHHE) and schools will be supported with hygiene kits. NRC will mainstream disability to promote access to education by Children with Disabilities (CWDs). This will be through ensuring awareness campaigns equally target children with disabilities and promoting disability friendly learning environments through ensuring provision of disability sensitive latrines, and training of teachers on inclusive education.

project_name: Construyendo Espacios Protectores y Amigables para la Niñez y Adolescencia que se encuentran en riesgo por causa de la violencia.
project_objective: El NRC en El Salvador desde el año 2016 está proporcionando una respuesta de protección sectorial y focalizada, frente a las necesidades más críticas derivadas de la violencia estructural y de género; el enfoque de implementación se centra en la prevención de todas las formas de violencia y la respuesta de protección, promoviendo el acceso a información, orientación y asistencia legal. Esto refleja una brecha en la respuesta humanitaria actual, en la cual las necesidades y vulnerabilidades más sentidas de las mujeres, niñez, adolescencia, padres, madres y cuidadores de familia no han sido atendidas; de igual manera se identifica la debilidad en el sistema de protección nacional y sus instituciones. Las intervenciones de protección buscan prevenir, mitigar y responder contra el abuso, la explotación y el daño que se puede generar en las poblaciones que han sido afectadas significativamente por las emergencias, incluidas las ocasionadas por la violencia; agravando las condiciones de pobreza, desigualdades, inseguridad. El proyecto fortalecerá las capacidades del personal comunitario o de instituciones gubernamentales vinculados a la promoción y protección de derechos y responsables de la atención de casos derivados. Asimismo, implementará una estrategia de respuesta a través de la construcción de espacios protectores a la niñez y adolescencia, acompañada de recursos y materiales que permitirá el desarrollo de actividades recreativas y de aprendizaje de saberes que contribuirán en el fortalecimiento de capacidades de autoprotección, educación socioemocional y resiliencia.

project_name: Comunidades Educativas y Protectoras para la niñez, adolescencia y juventud en contextos de emergencia.
project_objective:
NRC considera que la educación es una herramienta estratégica para la protección de la niñez, adolescencia, juventud, familias y comunidades en contextos de emergencia. El proyecto tiene como objetivo fundamental promover el acceso y la permanencia escolar en espacios seguros de aprendizaje para la población afectada o en riesgo por lo que se ha denominado Otras Situaciones de Violencia (OSV), migración, desplazamiento en situaciones de emergencia.
El NRC tiene una estrategia de intervención para asegurar la efectividad de la escolarización de los NNAJ, se plantea iniciar con la identificación de la población fuera del sistema escolar o en riesgo de abandono escolar; posterior se incorporan a círculos para la motivación escolar y la educación socioemocional, los NNAJ serán matriculados en el caso que no estén en el sistema de educación formal y finalmente se atiende en el programa permanencia en el cual se realiza acompañamiento pedagógico tanto a NNAJ y docentes para que la población estudiantil permanezca en la escuela para contribuir a su aprobación del año escolar. 
Durante el desarrollo de las acciones de los círculos socioemocionales y permanencia se realizará la entrega de kit educativo para brindarle herramientas para su incorporación y facilitar.
Se contempla la implementación de un enfoque de trabajo integral que fortalezca las capacidades de diversos actores; se capacitará a docentes y funcionarios del MINEDUCYT a nivel central y departamental en temas vinculados a Educación Socioemocional y Educación en Emergencia; a padres, madres, cuidadores o encargados de familia en temas vinculados a la protección, derechos de la niñez y educación socioemocional, así como de la importancia de la construcción de espacios protectores que contribuya al desarrollo integral de la población estudiantil. 
De igual manera se sensibilizará sobre la importancia de enfrentar problemas de abandono escolar para realizar acciones en conjunto para incidir en la reducción de los índices de deserción escolar.
Las acciones del proyecto contemplan la atención de personas con discapacidad si fuera el caso, al identificarse población con discapacidad con sobreedad se apoyará el proceso de matricula para la prueba de suficiencia o modalidad flexible que se adapte a las necesidades de esta población.

project_name: Promoviendo la recuperación de la población víctima de desplazamiento forzado a través establecimiento o restauración de microemprendimientos manejados por las mujeres jefas de familias desplazadas
project_objective:
A través de este proyecto, el Consejo Noruego para Refugiados (NRC), en alianza con el Centro de Desarrollo Empresarial (CDE) -una plataforma público-privado que persigue el desarrollo integral de los emprendedores-, aumentará la resiliencia de 165 pequeñas empresas dirigidas por mujeres jefas de familias desplazadas en Honduras, con el fin de garantizar la continuidad de sus negocios, ayudarles a construir redes de confianza y ganar confianza en el uso de la tecnología para gestionar los riesgos. Esta iniciativa mejorará el restablecimiento de los medios de subsistencia, garantizando unos ingresos estables a las familias desplazadas encabezadas por mujeres. Estos ingresos facilitarán su seguridad alimentaria, el bienestar familiar y la acumulación de capital. 

Para lograr este objetivo, las mujeres participantes recibirán conocimientos especializados sobre riesgos empresariales y formas de mitigarlos. También recibirán apoyo a través de aplicaciones para teléfonos inteligentes que les ayudarán a evaluar sus riesgos y desarrollar planes de acción para mitigarlos. Asimismo, en el ámbito colectivo, las empresarias formarán agrupaciones locales para fomentar redes empresariales y alianzas para la mitigación de riesgos. Además, el proyecto compartirá conocimientos y herramientas basados en pruebas con organizaciones que apoyan la iniciativa empresarial femenina en Honduras para potenciar la ampliación de las innovaciones. La tasa de supervivencia y la estabilidad de los ingresos de las empresas participantes indicarán el éxito del proyecto y la validación de las innovaciones.

project_name: SIRIYO 2 : Promouvoir la protection et la dignité des femmes et des enfants déplacés de Diffa.
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à promouvoir la protection et le droit de vivre dans la dignité des femmes et des enfants de trois sites d’IDP de la région de Diffa. Cherchant une synergie entre les interventions liées à la santé et à la nutrition et les actions axées sur l'atténuation et la prévention de toutes les formes de violence à l'égard des femmes et des enfants. Avec une approche communautaire et de genre, comme éléments structurants, ce projet développera divers programmes de prise en charge (nutrition, prévention des VBG, autonomisation des femmes, protection de l’enfance) dédiés aux enfants et aux femmes en situation de vulnérabilité dans 3 sites de déplacés dans les communes de Diffa et de Chétimari. Le projet consolidera le travail commencé en 2021, proposant une continuité des actions mises en œuvre ainsi que l'élargissement des différents services offerts, tout en renforçant le leadership des acteurs locaux dans une perspective de localisation de l'aide humanitaire et en améliorant la capacité de prise de décision et de participation des femmes dans l’Action Humanitaire dans une perspective de redevabilité.  Les principales activités du projet seront :
1. distribution de Kit alimentaires, 
2. distribution de kits dignité, 
3. formation de para-juristes et relais pour l’assistance psychosociale, 
4. création de groupements féminins, 
5. AGR pour les survivantes de VBG et les femmes les plus vulnérables et à risque, 
6. alphabétisation, 
7. mise en place d'un système intègre de participation et redevabilité, 
8. création et animation d’EAE, 
9. gestion de cas de PE et 
10. distribution de Kits layette, 
11. sensibilisation et plaidoyer en matière de PE et VBG.
