project_objective:
In 2023, building on years of expertise and lessons learned COOPI aims to continue and expand its response to growing Food Insecurity and early recovery of the agricultural sector in Aleppo, Dar’a, Hama, Homs, Idleb, Raqqa and Rural Damascus.
The proposed project is a continuation of the project approved in HRP HSYR22-FSC-188341-1 and aims to respond to SO1 “To Scale-up and sustain minimum food consumption needs through life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance” and SO3 ""To improve communities' resilience and capacity to sustain households’ livelihoods by improving linkages with value chain through the light rehabilitation of productive and economic infrastructure of the Food and Agricultural Sector"".
Projects will target most vulnerable HH’s- especially women HHs, HHs with elderly, PwD, vulnerable returnees/IDP, families with high number of children, HHs with pregnant/lactating women, unaccompanied children in areas with high needs (Severity scale 3 and above). 
Vulnerable IDPs, refugees and/or Host Community members who are moderately or severely Food Insecure and who are lacking the economic means or assets to fulfill their immediate food needs will be provided with CVA- that, in line with FAS sector recommendations, through a minimum of 8 distributions-covering 70% of the food SMEB price to meet the minimum the daily kcal intake per day per person. Value will be based on the recommendation of FAS for 2022/2023.
COOPI will provide agricultural kits for those with no stable income and lacking of reproductive assets, but with access to land and irrigation means The kits will be distributed in accordance with sector recommendations and will include tools for irrigation and combined with training on post-harvest loss reduction techniques, use of compost and fertilizer and improved farming.
Finally, infrastructure for agricultural means (irrigation canals, roads) will be rehabilitated through CFW targeting families that have abled members to work, but lack sustainable and long-term jobs. 
The beneficiaries’ participation will be promoted throughout the project implementation, during the market assessment, trader surveys, focus groups discussion, monthly redemption activities and feedback mechanisms. In order to ensure high quality of the project implementation and beneficiaries’ feedback mechanisms, COOPI staff and volunteers will be trained on PSEA, MEAL tools and Vouchers Assistance (VA) processes.
Programmatic monitoring will be done through regular field visits, PDMs and focus group discussions. COOPI field staff and MEAL will attend all distributions and redemptions. Three rounds of PDM, including FCS and CSI surveys at each location will be conducted (baseline,mid-project and endline). Traders monitoring and price survey will be conducted before every distribution of CVA to ensure that prices are aligned with prices in community (compared to WFP price bulletin).
In order to facilitate the relationship with the several stakeholders and  promote a synergic and multi-sector  approach to challenges at all different levels, COOPI will ensure the coordination with local authorities, as well as Food Security Agriculture Sector (FSA), ERL Sector, Cash Working Group and international and national actors active in the same target areas. With the aim to adopt an integrated area-based strategy, COOPI FSL project will be implemented in areas where COOPI is implementing Protection and Education activities, while strong coordination will be ensured in order to refer and advocate for needs in other areas identified throughout the implementation.  Through it's area-based approach COOPI will continue to collaborate with local authorities, as well as active coordination and participation with sectors at sub and national level, and will refer identified needs and gaps found during the implementation that cant be addressed within COOPIs implementation.

project_name: Anglophone Crisis Emergency Response III (ACER III)
project_objective:
In response to the immense needs resulting from the conflict in the Northwest (NW) and Southwest (SW) regions in Cameroon, CRS is implementing twelve-month third phase to its current Anglophone Crisis Emergency Response (ACER III). ACER III is building on the success and learning of the previous phases of the response. Changes and adaptations are based on community consultations and input, needs assessments, coordination and harmonization with other humanitarian actors, and changes in the security context and accessibility.
The goal of the ACER III project is to improve food security and alleviate suffering of displaced and host households in the Northwest Region of Cameroon. The project seek to achieve this goal through two purposes: (1) vulnerable displaced and host households in the Northwest meet their basic food and NFI needs, and (2) vulnerable displaced and host households in the Northwest improve poultry production. In partnership with the Archdiocese of Bamenda, CRS is delivering an integrated package of assistance, providing vulnerable displaced and host households with poultry production training and support, as well as emergency food and NFIs. The project is using market-based approaches to support 10,800 people in 1,800 households over twelve months.
The project’s theory of change is: If households have improved access to sufficient quantity, quality, and diversity of food; and if they replace essential NFIs; and if they raise poultry to improve their livelihoods and generate income; and assuming that markets remain accessible and functional; then they will improve their food security and experience reduced suffering; because the first two phases of the ACER project have demonstrated that market access to food reduces household hunger scores, broader humanitarian evidence shows that food assistance leads to improved food security, and poultry interventions in Cameroon and Nigeria have demonstrated the potential to improve income and facilitate more sustainable access to food.
ACER III responds directly to the normative and felt needs of the affected population. In the International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s multisector needs assessment (MSNA) conducted in August 2021, food and non-food items (NFIs) continue to be priority needs. In the NW, nearly one million people are food insecure and cannot meet basic household needs.  In response, ACER III will provide food assistance and NFIs using an e-voucher modality that leverages local markets and stimulates the local economy. In CRS community consultations, affected populations have expressed interest in receiving support to restart their livelihoods and generate income so that they do not continue relying on humanitarian assistance. Poultry production was among the most cited and viable livelihoods options considering the context – difficult access to agricultural land and a tradition of a booming livestock sector including egg production. In ACER III, CRS will pilot an intervention to support poultry production among a small subset of the food assistance participants. The poultry pilot intervention includes training, input distribution and creating linkages with the Ministry of Livestock, Fisheries and Animal Industries (MINEPIA) and Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs).
ACER III will continue to focus on two divisions in the NW – Mezam and Momo. ACER III will expand its geographic focus within those divisions where there is demonstrated need and major gaps in humanitarian assistance. ACER III will continue to work in Bamenda I, II and III, Santa, Bafut and Batibo sub-divisions, and will explore the possibility of expanding to Bali and Tubah in Mezam and to Mbengwi in Momo.

project_name: Integrated emergency response in Nutrition, Health, MHPSS for the populations affected by the crisis in the southwest region, Cameroon (Mobile clinics Sites and St. John Fiango (SHC)- Paediatric)
project_objective:
Since April 2020, AAH delivers health, nutrition and MHPSS activities through mobile clinics in Meme Division. This current project aims to meet the urgent health needs in the increasingly unstable southwest region of Cameroon, through the provision of emergency primary health care (PHC) services integrating MHPSS to populations affected by the crisis and particularly children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW)
Through this project, AAH aims to consolidate the achievements of previous projects by taking into account experiences to adapt the approach. 2 mobiles clinics will be deployed in Meme's division providing primary health care to beneficiaries, with a focus on children under 5, PLW, but is also delivering services to adults for most common pathologies. AAH integrates into its intervention support for 3 functional private structures and the implementation of a community approach through identification and training of CHWs and thus hope to perpetuate the activities of the project.
At the MC site (Banga Bakundu, Bombe Bakumndu, Kake 1, kake2, Small Ekombe, Mambanda, Ejumpindi, Boloweme, Kurume, Ndoi,  Wone, Kombe and Kombone Bafaw), all children aged 0 to 5 years, PLW and adults will be offered free medical services. All beneficiaries will benefit from medical and preventive consultations by qualified medical staff. The staff will provide treatment for common childhood illnesses using national guidelines / and standardized IMCI protocols. The immunization status, especially of children requiring measles vaccination, will be assessed.
Additionally, as preventive consultations, children will be growth monitored, screened for malnutrition using MUAC (6-59 months), weight, size and oedemia, dewormed (12-59 months) and provided with vitamin A supplementation (6-59 months). Children (0-23 months of age) will also benefit from IYCF counselling provided to their mothers and caregivers.
The curative consultations component for children over 5 years old and adults will be added at the MC level. These consultations will be linked to the management of the most common diseases (malaria, respiratory infection, skin diseases), including malaria treatment according to the national protocol for adults.
The targeted communities and this age group will be informed to the fact that all chronic diseases will not be managed but if potential sick patients visit AAH MC, they will be referred to the appropriate structures (St. John Fiango (SHC) -  Paediatric). The medicines used will also be essential medicines according to national pharmaceutical guidelines for the level of care as a mobile clinic at the community level.
In regards to people leaving with disabilities (PLWD), AAH will offer the same package of services. General support will be provided with sensorial impairments and other disabilities, as well as orientation to specialized services, but no specific treatments will be provided. The mobile clinic will also be an opportunity to provide sensitization about various topics (common hygiene and nutritious messages, SGBV awareness, COVID preventive measures...). 
At last, a systematic referral will be implemented for mental health identified patients at the mobile clinic level.
The package of care will also include medical and MHPSS care for GBV victims (including rape clinical case management), especially women and children, and referral to appropriate facilities for those whose post-rape condition requires further in-depth care, including, for example, social reintegration.
This project will target all people affected by the crisis: men, women, PLWs, children aged 0-5 and above, adolescents, IDPs, host populations, people living with a disability, the elderly, health staff from targeted private health centers and community actors.

project_name: Provision of quality WASH services for vulnerable communities living in Akobo, Tonj South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North , Budi and Abyei
project_objective:
In the proposed action Save the Children seeks to implement integrated WASH interventions to reduce the burden of WASH related diseases as aggravating factors for malnutrition locations presenting an extreme WASH vulnerability and high prevalence of malnutrition. Services provided will break the transmission cycle of main communicable diseases (i.e. diarrhea), thus improving food intake of malnourished children and contributing to the sustainability of health and nutrition. The proposed action will also seek to address WASH needs in during emergencies such as response to floods and disease outbreaks. The proposed interventions will target Akobo, Tonj South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North , Budi counties and Abyei  which have a WASH severity classification of 3 and 4, communities high GAM and in which Save the Children has operational presence.

The proposed WASH activities include; construction/rehabilitation of water points in communities  , water quality monitoring, hygiene promotion, construction of latrines in communities, WASH in Nutrition/health care facilities distribution of WASH kits , soap distribution and mitigation of Gender Based Violence, GBV through training of WASH staff on basic skills to provide survivors with information on where they can obtain support and GBV messages (including where to report risk and how to access care) are incorporated into hygiene promotion and other WASH related community outreach activities using multiple formats to ensure accessibility.
Due to the conflict and flood situation in Abyei , the proposed action will also target to improve WASH services for 20,000 people ( 10,082, female , 9,918 male ) in Abyei . Main activities will be rehabilitation of existing non operational water points , construction of emergency latrines , WASH in health and nutrition facilities , WASH NFIs distribution coupled with hygiene messaging.

The proposed interventions align well with the South Sudan 
WASH cluster objectives 1; contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition, 2.1. Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties and 2.2. WASH specific activities for GBV (or mitigating WASH GBV)

Save the children targets a total of 84,438 beneficiaries (32,960 Male, 31,478 Females) across the five counties. The estimated cost to deliver the proposed WASH interventions is USD 2,500,000

project_name: Provide Access to Inclusive, Quality, and Protective Basic Education to Vulnerable Children, Out of School Children and Youth aged (3-18), in Akobo, Nyirol, and Bor South of Jonglei State; Kapoeta East of Eastern Equitoria, Rumbek East of Lakes, Tonj East of Warrap in South Sudan.
project_objective:
To provide access to inclusive, quality, and protective basic education to vulnerable and marginalised children, Out of School Children and youths aged (3-18) in Akobo, Nyirol, and Bor South of Jonglei State; Kapoeta East of Eastern Equatoria, Rumbek East of Lakes and Tonj East in Warrap. The programme will implement interventions that lead to increased access to education for children. The programme will ensure that access to basic education meets the quality standards as set in the INEE minimum standards of Education in Emergencies. Activities will promote enrolment, retention and transition of children to the next school year while minimizing the possibility of dropouts. The learning infrastructure and the school environment will be disability friendly and gender sensitive to learners. School environments will provide intentional MHPSS activities and have clear referral pathways including to CP to ensure school environments are protective. Teachers will receive CPD and volunteer teachers incentivized. The project will target 49,870 total beneficiaries desegregated into 48,000 children and youths (26,790 B & 21,210 G), 1,122 teachers (617 M, & 505 W), 748 PTAs/SMCs (411 M, & 337 W); with 3% comprising of persons with disability, host communities and IDPs. 
The project will aim at improving equitable access to safe and protective education services by enrolling 48,000 children and youths (26,790 B & 21,210 G) in pre-primary, primary and secondary schools and in learning centers. 30 Temporary Learning Spaces will be established, rehabilitation of 40 Temporary Learning Spaces, establishment of 20 gender segregated latrines, water points. Additionally, the project will be rehabilitating 25 gender segregated latrines and water points; and distributing or provide sanitation and hygiene materials to 108 schools (hand washing soap, sanitizers, masks) and PPE for students and teachers. 
The project will improve the quality of education, gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children by providing 4,128 (2,270 B & 1,858 G) emergency-affected children quality education recreational materials; providing teaching and learning materials for 96 schools in ECD, primary and secondary school education. The project will equally be conducting training 522 (304 M & 248 F) teachers on EiE pedagogical skills and child-centered methodologies to improve teaching and learning process for emergency-affected children; update 522 (304 M & 248 F) teachers and learners on PSS, CP, and referral mechanisms including CP/GBV, health and nutrition. Providing life-skills and basic vocational training to 1,000 (550 G & 450 G) youth and adolescents provide of dignity kits to 6,480 girls in schools; provide customized support to 840 young mothers in schools and to conduct 1-disability assessment.  All learning centres will have their referral pathways strengthened or established, with teachers trained on how to identify and refer cases through a child helpdesk. 
In order to strengthen/enhance the education system’s response capacity of the school community and national/local education actors the project will: capacity build 1,104 (607 M, & 497 W) SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management, governance, PSS and DRR. The project will support prevention and mitigation of communicable diseases through training school communities by providing appropriate Information and Education and Communication (IEC) materials (i.e. posters, leaflets); conducting 5 back to learning campaigns. SCI will implement directly and with national partners, supporting technical, operational and institutional capacity strengthening of 5 national actors.
The projects will ensure that the following will be considered in the project design and implementation: gender and social inclusion, feedback & accountability mechanisms, crisis modifiers, nexus programming and community-based sustainability measures.

project_name: Strengthen Equitable Provision of Humanitarian Services and Disaster Risk Reduction through Camp Coordination, Site Development and Monitoring of Minimum Standards in Rohingya Refugee Camps
project_objective:
""The Site Management and Site Development (SMSD) project aims to continue the current efforts of IOM to strengthen equitable provision of humanitarian assistance through coordination of service providers, enabling community participation and feedback to humanitarian programming, reducing risks from natural hazards, and increasing the degree of access to key services in refugee camps and host community of Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazilas. In collaboration with implementing partners (IPs) and key stakeholders, IOM intends to target Rohingya refugees and host communities that will benefit from coordination of service provision, site planning support and interventions for disaster risk reduction (DRR) which contribute to ensuring equitable and safe access to assistance, protection, and services for improved and dignified living conditions. The project follows an integrated approach to improve coordination between (i) the Site Management Support (SMS) and administration functions supporting the Camp in Charges (CiCs) (ii) SMS and the sectoral partners (iii) Site Development (SD) and DRR partners including engineering project vis-a-via Site Maintenance and Engineering Program (SMEP) to ensure services for refugee population has geographic coverage between the blocks and camps under IOM Area of Responsibilities (AoR). The Capacity Sharing Initiative (CSI) will continue to work closely with the Office of the Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner (RRRC) to enhance the cooperation between humanitarian sectors and actors and the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) in the management of camps. 

The SMS agencies will ensure that service providers consider the specific needs, safety and dignity of people of different age, gender and diversity. The components of the project include SMS coordination function, information management, advocacy to maintain minimum standards, the Common Feedback Platform (CFP) and referral mechanism, representation, and engagement of Refugee population with their significant role as an entry point for accountability. The project will focus on increased information-sharing through Communication with Communities (CwC) programs to ensure that camp residents understand their entitlements in terms of minimum services or relief provided. Community participation and empowerment will be enhanced through camp committees and groups. Their capacity enhancement will be through training, resources, and establishment of platforms for meaningful dialogue with camp stakeholders and reinforce community capacity and ownership to maintain camp infrastructures.To mitigate multi-hazard risks, IOM with SMEP and Site Planning support will continuously implement cash-based SD and DRR interventions which include the construction, repair and maintenance of slope stabilization, drainage, access (including pathways, stairs, bridges, vehicular roads, etc.), plantation and environmental restoration and solar streetlights. The scope of work will include assessment, prioritization, and design the solutions to address immediate needs linking with existing planning frameworks and mainstreaming environment to achieve nature-based solutions where possible. The project will continue to strengthen community-based disaster response volunteer capacity, camp level contingency plans and Disaster Management Committee, and effective life-saving rapid emergency coordination and assistance delivery systems.

Need and Population Movement (NPM) will continue to support for informed humanitarian and development decision-making through identification of needs, conditions and service provision for the refugee and host communities, enabling strong evidence-based response planning by administering thematic assessments, joint multi-sectoral needs assessment, assisting the inter sectoral coordination group (ISCG) on the post-disaster and preparedness through daily incident reporting, shelter addressing system, facility mapping and joint needs assessment framework. ""

project_name: Every Life Counts (Provision of lifesaving Child Protection and Gender Based Violence interventions for most vulnerable children in North, Central, and West Darfur; North and South Kordofan, Blue Nile, Red Sea, Khartoum, Al Jazirah and River Nile states)
project_objective:
The Child Protection component will target 11 states which prioritize vulnerable boys and girls on the move, with a particular focus on unaccompanied and separated children as well as those at risk of various forms of violence and exploitation, including sexual and gender-based violence, recruitment, child labor, abduction, and other forms of abuse through provision of life saving support through individual case management services based on a best interest assessment. 
In addition to children, the intervention will also aim to support foster parents, women, and men in the affected communities who have been displaced or forced to migrate, including internally displaced persons, refugees, returnees, asylum seekers, and immigrants. 
Furthermore, the response will be built around MHPSS through Children’s regular and consistent engagement of children in group activities that will positively impact their well-being, enhance their resilience, reduce their stress and provide a sense of normalcy in a difficult context through CFS/GFS. Save the Children and its partners will facilitate structured play and recreational activities through GFS/CFS which will provide children opportunities to come together in a predictable and stimulating environment to be safe, to learn, to express themselves, to make connections and to feel supported. This will not only promote protection but allow the project identify children who are vulnerable or who are experiencing abuse, neglect, exploitation or violence and supporting appropriate referrals.

The response is framed around the centrality of protection, involving conflict sensitivity analysis, CP mainstreaming and integration across sectors, with a focus on identification and response to grave and other serious child rights violations including recruitment, and private advocacy on establishing accountability mechanisms for child rights violations.
To strengthen protection of children, community-based child protection structures will be established/ strengthened to enhance and elevate the community-level protection and outreach activities and support the parents and caregivers to provide a safe atmosphere for their children and monitor the hazard and risks in the community such as UXOs.

project_name: Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents
project_objective:
The humanitarian nutritional needs in Sudan are expected to remain at high levels or worsen further in 2023, making Sudan one of the countries in the World with highest estimated acute malnutrition caseload.  While the overall Global acute malnutrition (GAM) remains at 13.6%, the prevalence of GAM varies significantly across the localities with very high situation (GAM above 15% and above as per WHO classification) reported in 64 localities. The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality life-saving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile and Red Sea states in which 29 localities will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 362,874 beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (87,131 boys, 90,680 girls, 184,383 women, 680 men). Save the children will implement lifesaving, preventative interventions, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), referral of SAM children with medical complications and minor rehabilitation to nutrition sites. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities, mobile and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash-based interventions to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied.

project_name: Enhancing Food security and Resilient livelihood to Conflict and Drought affected Population of South Sudan (EFARLCADAP)
project_objective:
South Sudan remains one of the most food insecure countries in the world. Its acute food insecurity situation is caused by multiple and interconnected factors such as prolonged conflict, natural disasters (successive years of flooding and localized droughts), high food prices, dry spells affecting crop and pasture, Covid-19 consequences and displacements among others. According to the IPC report released in November (2022), 6.31M people (51.0% of the population) will be facing severe acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+) during the post-harvest period of December 2022 to March 2023 and are in need of urgent action. This is expected to increase to during the lean season projection period of April to July 2023 to 7.76M people (62.7% of the population) will be facing severe acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+) and are in need of urgent action. The targeted areas of this project are some of the worst affected in terms of food insecurity. Currently, people facing severe acute food insecurity in the project target areas: in Tonj North (145,000), in Wau (112,000), in Yei (106,000), in Kajokeji (94,000), in Kapoeta East (93,000), and in Kapoeta North (79,000). It is estimated that all current crisis IPC levels will deteriorate significantly if emergency assistance is not provided. In the lean season projection period of April to July 2023 the food security situation will significantly deteriorate/worsen.  in 2023. In Tonj North (171,000), in Wau (144,000), in Kajokeji (140,000), in Yei (136,000), in Kapoeta East (118,000), and in Kapoeta North (94,000).

The Project Enhancing Food Security and Resilient livelihood to Conflict and Drought affected Population in Warrap, Eastern Equatoria, Central Equatoria and Western Bahr el Ghazal States aims at saving life and building resilient livelihood of 48,180 vulnerable Population (6,263 Boys, 12,045 Girls, 13,009 men, and 16,863 women) at Warrap state (Tonj North), Eastern Equatoria (Kaoeta East and Kapoeta North), Central Equatoria (Yei and Kajokeji) and Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau). The project will among others provide food parcels; agricultural inputs, training on farming, crop disease prevention, harvest and storage; livestock disease prevention and animal husbandry training and provision of start-up vet-kits. These interventions will contribute to improving agricultural/livestock production thereby improving food security 

The project shall contribute to providing food assistance and emergency food production to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations by employing Accountability to the affected population (AAP) approach and making sure that activities are implemented in line with core humanitarian standards (CHS). All the responds shall be integrated with strategies that bridges gender in equality gaps and addresses issues of GBV that happens to be a major contributing factor for food insecurity and compromise livelihood of men, women and girls. The respond shall aim at addressing risk factors of covid-19 transmission and employ risk mitigation measures during activities implementation. As part of Monitoring Evaluation and learning. IRSS shall conduct Project progress and Midterm review workshop to serve both learning and accountability purpose and will seek to identify any problems and constraints encountered by the project to date and formulate appropriate recommendations for corrective actions for effective implementation of the remaining period of the project implementation. Also ensure the project indicators that are monitored are on track and lesson learnt are drawn for future improvement. The workshop shall involve key stake holders of the projects especially representatives of women, people living with disability, youth, government line ministries, representatives of implementing partners, FSL cluster members, etc.

project_name: Emergency Child Protection and MHPSS responses for girls, boys and families most affected by the escalation of violence in Gaza and West Bank, including Eastern Jerusalem
project_objective:
2022 has been the deadliest year since 2006, on a monthly average, for Palestinians residing in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem. At least 105 Palestinians, including 26 children, have been killed by Israeli forces.

Child protection concerns are on the increase in both the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. Children living near settlements or Israeli military checkpoints are at constant risk of military and settler violence and intimidation. Save the Children (SC) is proposing an emergency integrated protection and MHPSS response to mitigate the impact of conflict, trauma, and child rights violations including, Gender Based Violence (GBV), on boys’, girls’ and caregivers’ mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, through ensuring access to a continuum of MHPSS and protection services. In partnership with Ma’an Development Centre in Gaza and the Young Men Christian Association (YMCA) in the West Bank, the project will provide holistic support to 5,000 individuals, of which 4,000 are children protracted conflict and violence in Gaza, demolitions and forced evictions in Massafer Yatta, and military detention in the West Bank. 
An estimated 5% of targeted beneficiaries are people and children with disabilities, and 50% are women and girls. 

SC and its partners will deliver age sensitive , and gender responsive, inclusive  services to address the complex vulnerabilities of the impacted communities. These services include comprehensive GBV prevention and risk mitigation , child protection case management and individualized intervention plans, management and individual and group counselling. The services will also include, depending on the needs of the boys, girls, men and women, other structured MHPSS support, recreational activities, referral to specialized mental health and protection services, cash for protection, individual and group counselling for caregivers, including positive parenting activities.

Specifically,  iIn Gaza, immediate protection and psychological assistance will be delivered through the Governorate Protection Focal Points (GPFP), the tried-and-tested child protection and psycho-social emergency response system established in Gaza. We SC will use Child Friendly Space/CFSs as an entry-point for MHPSS interventions, including identification and referral of unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) children with protection concern and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). In addition, the project will provide child protection case management and PSS support to children affected by violence and their caregivers, including cash for protection. In the West Bank, the project will provide child protection and MHPSS interventions, including cash for protection to eligible households, to children and their caregivers affected by occupation violence. Through these interventions, the project aims to enhance the wellbeing, resilience, and recovery of girls and boys in the West Bank and Gaza, as well as  their caregivers, who have experienced occupation violence, displacement and rights violations. The project will draw on SC’s evidenced based approaches and expertise including structured home-based MHPSS intervention for children affected by conflict, group MHPSS programmes, positive parenting sessions and SC’s child resilience programme. The project will strengthen parental care and support and build upon the capacity of local organizations with extensive experience delivering protection services in the target communities.

project_name: Provision of in-kind food assistance to Vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
UNRWA estimates that 420,000 Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance in 2023. In a context of rising inflation and additional economic hardship caused by COVID-19, Palestine refugees are more and more affected by food insecurity and therefore increasingly depend on UNRWA assistance to meet their minimum food needs. The Agency will continue to monitor the availability of food on the markets and will retain operational flexibility to adjust to a changing context as appropriate. The composition of the food basket was developed based on WFP guidelines and in view of meeting 50% of daily nutritional needs for 4 months.
UNRWA's original plan is to distribute 3 rounds of in-kind food assistance, each round covering a period of 4 months. However, this depends on the availability of funds. Until January 2023, UNRWA received or confirmed pledges are only sufficient to cover part of the first round of 2023. The Agency will continue to mobilize resources to ensure funding for the food rounds are secured. In 2023, the number of people estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance including for food needs is 420,000 Palestine refugees to strengthen their resilience and prevent further deterioration into acute food insecurity. As per its emergency planning, UNRWA aims to provide food assistance as well as multipurpose cash assistance, and protection interventions at both household and community levels, as well as the coordination of these activities across the different Sectors framework. The in-kind food assistance program remains one of the most important forms of UNRWA emergency support to stabilize the food security status for Palestine refugees in Syria with the MPC based on complementarity approach considering that MPC transfer value will not cover the full needs of the beneficiaries and the potential unavailability of fund. , as it helps them meet part of their basic nutritional and survival requirements (~50% of kcal/person/day) which will increase resilience, and reduce humanitarian needs and the spiraling food insecurity levels.

For beneficiaries living in camps, blanket selection will be applied. project_name: Provision of food and livelihood emergency responses to conflict and flood affected food insecure communities in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Save the Children proposes the livelihood based emergency project interventions in response to the ongoing conflicts, inter communal violence, climate change including flooding and its associated impacts in exacerbating acute food insecurity. The targeted states include; Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Eastern Equatoria, Warrap and Jonglei have known track records of severe food insecurity and malnutrition and continue to face worst food security outcomes. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, therefore, improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks. The project targets primarily conflict and flood affected children and their families in the internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and host communities.

In response to the ongoing food insecurity crisis, Save the Children proposes a livelihood based emergency project in response to the ongoing conflict and its associated impacts in eleven counties, in four States of South Sudan. The proposed action aims at saving lives, addressing the immediate and medium-term needs and improving access to improved agricultures and livestock services, therefore improving the food and nutrition security of the conflict affected communities and increasing their resilience to famine and disaster risks and shocks mainly intercommunal violence and flooding. 

The project targets primarily conflict and flood affected children and their families in the internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and host communities. The key interventions proposed through this action are food assistances, cash and voucher based assistances as part of rapid responses; and agricultural and fishing inputs provisions and productions with training packages on improved agronomic practices including improved kitchen gardening; and livestock vaccinations and treatment services against diseases greatest economic importance. 

The design of the proposed project is informed by findings of the multi-partner and multi-sectoral assessments, IPC analysis, security and risk analysis and recommendations which have been conducted and released in the last six months. 

The proposed emergency response is designed in line with Cluster Objectives (CO1, CO2 and CO3) of FSL Cluster and to contribute to the HRP 2023 Strategic Objectives (SO1, SO2 and SO3). The Action aims at reaching out to 348,000 people (at least 60% female), which fall under IPC 5, 4 and 3 in four States of South Sudan, more specifically Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil East), Jonglei (Akobo, Nyirol, Bor South), and Eastern Equatoria (Lafon, Budi, Torit, Kapoeta North, Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Magwi) and Warrap (Tonj East).

project_objective: The IRC will implement WASH activities at supported Health Facilities (HFs) to support refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host community across Gedaref, Khartoum, Blue Nile, and South Kordofan states. The IRC will increase the availability, quality, accessibility, and reliability of potable water sources by strengthening the maintenance and operations of drinking water sources. The IRC will also promote the uptake of positive hygiene behaviors and practices of households, especially regarding safe water chain activities (from collection to consumption of potable water). The IRC will determine and administer project interventions in Blue Nile’s Wad al Mahi locality and South Kordofan’s Dilling and Habila localities which have the highest level of unmet needs.  The IRC will also administer WASH activities in other areas that can be safely accessed by project staff. To further complement the impact of water supply infrastructure activities, the IRC will primarily utilize local methods and materials to promote post-project sustainability. Water User Committees (WUCs) will be formed by the IRC to support projects and will include members selected based on coordination with community leaders. Each WUC will consist of approximately 5 or 6 members, with the selection criteria including: individuals from the targeted community; those over 18 years of age; if possible, persons with an ability to read and write in Arabic with preference given to a literate person(s) for record keeping and written communications roles; an active participant of community work and those with technical skills or a trusted human resource such as masons, teachers, community health volunteers (CHVs), and religious/customary leaders. Women are specifically targeted to be trained and selected to take on leadership and management roles within the WUCs, and the IRC will advocate to ensure women make up at least 50% of the WUC members. Additionally, WASH volunteers will operate within the project’s three target locations and the IRC anticipates having at least two CHVs (segregated by gender) for every 1,000 individuals within the target communities. Women in particular will be empowered and trained to take on the role of CHVs to serve as agents for change within their respective communities. As well as the IRC response to the emergency situation to support the affected people from the ongoing conflict in Khartoum and the IDPs in Jazera state by providing WASH services for the health facilities and communities.

project_name: Gender sensitive and life saving integrated WASH response for multi-shocks affected vulnerable communities in Syria
project_objective: A leader in the fight against malnutrition, AAH implements gender-sensitive life-saving WASH interventions and provide communities with access to safe water and sanitation as sustainable mitigation for hunger causes. After more than eleven years of conflict, the recent economic downturn and water/climate crisis, all compounded by disease outbreak, basic services and infrastructure in the country are facing unprecedented stress and deterioration, as confirmed by AAH needs assessments. Women, children, IDPs, elderly and disabled people are often those most vulnerable and in need. AAH’s mandate consists of supporting functional authorities in responding to crises and rebuilding resilience and preparedness capacities. Within this framework, AAH prioritizes sustainable WASH projects, while continuing to provide life-saving WASH services when lack of access to basic WASH needs becomes severe or critical. AAH operates through three offices in Damascus, Aleppo and Hassakeh, and provides a wide range of WASH services in Aleppo, Al-Hassakeh, Hama, and Idleb. AAH has MoUs with the Ministries of Water Resources, Local Administration and Environment, Education and Health. AAH actively engages with the WASH, Health, Nutrition, Food Security and Agriculture Sectors and other sub-sectors and technical working groups. AAH keeps in close coordination with SARC, as well as with Governorates and local administrations. In NES, AAH coordinates with UNICEF and NES WWG for its interventions in Hassakeh. AAH interventions focus on locations with WASH severity 3 and higher as per the HNO, and the identification of potential projects is done through integrated (WASH, Health, Nutrition, FSA, mainstreaming Gender, Protection and Environmental Sustainability) and WASH-specific technical needs to support AAH’s multi-sectoral programming approach. Gender roles and the specific needs of women, girls, men and boys, age-groups, PwD and IDPs are analysed and addressed. The identification of WASH interventions in public health facilities will be based on the severity scores of the Health Sector. All interventions will aim at meeting SPHERE standards, and address community identified priorities. Emergency WASH services include life-saving water trucking, water tank distribution and water quality tests. The rehabilitation of water systems carried out by AAH includes both the rehabilitation of networks and water stations. Environmentally sustainable solutions for power supply such as solar panels installations are prioritized, along with connections to public electrical grids, while generators are used as a last resort. AAH also rehabilitates sewage networks, including the drainage systems and the installation of septic tanks, with a significant positive environmental and public health impact, avoiding the pollution of lands and eventually of aquifers. The solid waste management system is supported through improving waste collection at different levels. All water and sanitation system rehabilitation is followed up with support to ongoing operation and maintenance capacity, to ensure a sustained service provision after handing over to authorities. Public health risk communication and community engagement activities tailored according to age and gender target the most at-risk groups, such as children and PLW. Protection and Gender will be mainstreamed in all activities. AAH’s Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism will receive community feedback and inform monitoring and learning processes. This project will reach 312,043  people (157,802 female, 154,241 male, 63,740 CU5, 109,221 children 5-17, 119,387 17-59, and 19,695 over 59 years) . All activities will be monitored to assess the impact and take corrective actions if needed. Feedback mechanisms are also in place to ensure accountability to affected populations. Approximately 70% of the funding required is already secured.

project_name: Projet d’assistance d’urgence multisectorielle au profit des populations (hôtes, déplacées, retournées, agricoles et pastorales) affectées par les chocs climatiques, sécuritaires et sanitaires dans la région de Diffa
project_objective:
L’action a pour objectif de contribuer à la réduction des impacts négatifs des chocs sécuritaires, climatiques et sanitaires sur les conditions de vie des populations vulnérables hôtes et déplacées au Niger dans la région de Diffa (Diffa, Maine-Soroa,  N’guigmi et Bosso)  à travers une approche multisectorielle adaptée aux pics de vulnérabilités. Afin de réduire d'une manière drastique et holistique ces impacts, Action contre la faim (ci-après ACF) propose un projet qui vise l'amélioration de l'accessibilité aux services de santé par la mise en oeuvre d'un mécanisme de réponse rapide (ci-après RRM santé) du paquet santé et nutrition et l'appui aux structures de santé fragilisées par les conflits, le renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle notamment en période de soudure pour les populations vulnérables ycompris les populations pastorales, l'amélioration de l'accès à l'eau potable et des conditions d'assainissement et des bonnes
pratiques d'hygiène et de changement de comportement au niveau communautaire en prévention des épidémies dans ces zones sensibles.
ACF agira en synergie avec les acteurs humanitaires dans les deux zones en complémentarité à la mise en oeuvre du mécanisme de RRM santé. Ce projet sera renforcé en garantissant l’environnement protecteur des communautés à travers une réponse à leurs besoins et une coordination efficace pour un accès libre et durable aux services sociaux de base dans le respect des principes humanitaires. Action Contre la Faim propose donc une approche fondée sur un mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) pour assurer l'accès aux services de santé et de nutrition auprès des populations affectées par la crise du bassin du Lac Tchad dans la région de Diffa au Niger. Cette réponse viendra compléter et intégrer les interventions actuelles des autres mécanismes de RRM en cours par d’autres acteurs RRM dans la région. Le mécanisme proposé sera basé sur un système de surveillance et d'alerte construit sur des réseaux communautaires et les informations régulières recueillies directement auprès des centres de santé. Les structures sanitaires ciblées seront appuyées pour intégrer une surveillance de qualité des maladies à potentiel épidémique. Cet aspect sera assuré par l’amélioration des bases de données et métadonnées et de la promptitude de remontée des données épidémiques au Ministère de la Santé Publique, de la population et affaires sociales. Selon la nature de l'alerte, une évaluation rapide sera réalisée pour identifier la nature des obstacles à l'accès local aux services de santé et une réponse appropriée. Les évaluations rapides se feront selon les modalités d’évaluation mises en œuvre dans le RRM Santé et seront couplées dans la mesure du possible à celle d’autres secteurs dans les Zones affectées. Lors de l’évaluation, Action Contre la Faim fournira déjà dans la mesure du possible une première réponse en santé et nutrition avant la réponse multisectorielle conduite après l’analyse des besoins. 
Le paquet minimum d’activités Santé nutrition du RRM Santé reposera sur deux principales modalités de réponse (flexibles) : 
- L’implantation des Cliniques mobiles : des équipes mobiles capables de fournir le soutien nécessaire aux structures de santé affectées et / ou si nécessaire directement aux communautés par le biais de services mobiles équipes. La stratégie mobile sera composée de soins curatifs gratuits pour toute la population (soins de santé primaires, santé de la reproduction, prise en charge de la MAS), des soins préventifs (vaccination, CPN). L’appui psychosocial à base communautaire et une détection précoce des cas de protection des enfants et des femmes (composante GBV) suivi d’un référencement vers les autres acteurs pour une prise en charge plus globale. ACF accordera aussi , une attention particulière aux groupes spécifiques vulnérables et à besoin spécifiques pour les personnes âgées , les handicapées et tous  les influenceurs de soins de santé dans les communautés.

project_name: Provision of Humanitarian Air Service in Cameroon
project_objective:
his project aims to support the overall humanitarian response by enabling and enhancing access to beneficiaries and project implementation sites through a provision of air service.

Its main objectives are:
• To provide NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations and diplomatic missions in Cameroon with safe, effective and efficient air service;
• To transport light cargo, such as medical supplies, information and communication technology (ICT) equipment;
• To provide adequate capacity for medical and security evacuations of humanitarian staff.

UNHAS was established in Cameroon in November 2015 to provide air transport services to the entire humanitarian community and their implementing partners principally NGOs, UN agencies, red cross/crescent movement, donor organizations and diplomatic missions. Ever since, UNHAS has offered safe humanitarian flights on a regular weekly basis to Adamaoua (N’gaoundere), the North (Garoua) and the Far North (Maroua), as well as to Tchad (N’Djamena). As the conflict worsened in the Northwest and Southwest regions, and following a request from the Steering Committee, UNHAS extended its operations in September 2019 to serve the locations of Bamenda, Mamfe and Tiko.
As the continued insecurity, vast distances and poor road conditions remain the main constraints to the provision of assistance by aid organizations, but also the prevailing Covid-19 pandemic worldwide and in Cameroon in particular, the continuation of UNHAS in 2021 will be vital in enabling humanitarian organizations to access the populations in need and project implementation sites

project_name: To reduce the excess morbidity and mortality of displaced Rohingya children and families through quality primary health care including MHPSS, Nutriton, Rehabilitation and WASH services in inclusive manner
project_objective:
""Save the Children will deliver an inclusive, gender responsive & comprehensive healthcare services through 7 HP and 1 PHCC over the JRP period in 8 camps of Ukhiya and Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar to ensure equitable access to essential healthcare services for diverse Rohingya refugees and host communities including special-need populations (LGBTQI). Project will ensure gender responsive health facilities through sex segregated areas/rooms and presence of sufficient female staff. Those Health facilities will deliver primary health care service with special focus on 24/7 emergency care, sexual, reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health (SRMNCAH); mental health and psychosocial support; physical rehabilitation including assistive device provision and noncommunicable diseases in line with the minimum package of essential Health services (MPEHS). Along with regular health consultation, PHCC will offer IPD service, laboratory; PMTCT; BEmONC service with 5 bedded maternity unit & SGBV services (CMR, IPV and Domestic Violence). All this health facility will offer integrated services with Nutrition (IYCF-E & C-MAMI), Rehabilitation, WASH, Early childhood development (ECD) and Child Protection by ensuring coordination and referral in between, ensuring a child friendly corner considering “Do no harm policy”. To ensure IPC measure, safe disposal practice and to avoid chance of infection, a dedicated IPC focal will work closely with facility level IPC committee and provide necessary guidance aligned with IPC WG and MoH. The recently closed SARI-ITC structure will remain standby to support as a multifunctional outbreak center where other communicable diseases (Dengue, AWD, Measles, Diphtheriae, etc.) will be managed along with the COVID-19 if there is any surge. Clinical services will be complemented with health promotion and community engagement activities through a robust community health worker (CHWs) to encourage timely access to healthcare and address existing challenges in the community level and community-based surveillance will be continued to identify and COVID-19 patients in the communities. Engagement of women, community, and religious leaders to raise awareness of health and identify gender-responsive operations at health facility and arrange the necessary intervention to address those. All staff and volunteers will be trained on gender, GBV, Protection, PSEAH, CP, child safeguarding in health responses. To enhance clinical excellence, team will be trained on identified needs. There will be 2 Mobile Medical team (MMT) aligned with Emergency Preparedness Response Working Group (EPRWG) will be providing services in any emergency health response following any natural or manmade disaster. All the health facilities will be accessible and environment friendly for all age group and for PWD by ensuring ramp, disable friendly latrine, triage area, signage, lighting, and skilled workforce to prioritize and manage geriatric population and PWD. 
SCI Bangladesh has a robust MEAL system and according to the Program’s Logical Framework, develop a MEAL plan including Monitoring Plan that specifies indicators, data disaggregated by sex, age and disability etc. MEAL team will apply IPTT, Quality Benchmark (QB) and SCI Global Medical Team recommended Clinical Standard scorecard in all the health facility to monitor the quality of the key activities as part of monitoring. Multiple channels are using for receiving complaints and feedback from beneficiaries such as the toll-free hotline, help desks, Phone Based PDM and Online feedback response mechanism (FRM). SCI gender focal person will ensure Implementation of gender action plan and monitoring of activities in health indicators. S/he will maintain coordination with GiHA and all the health partners to share update on gender responsive health developments, including needs, gaps, challenges which helps to Identify good gender-sensitive practices regarding the health response.""

project_name: Fourniture d'un ensemble de services de soins de santé de base, en travaillant avec des agents de santé communautaires, en mettant l'accent sur la santé infantile, la santé sexuelle et reproductive, avec des systèmes d'orientation solides pour les soins préventifs (par exemple, les vaccinations) et curatifs.
project_objective:
La situation sanitaire s'est détériorée en raison de la crise sécuritaire du pays. En 2021, le sous-groupe SSR a estimé que 2 427 305 personnes seront affectées par la fermeture ou le fonctionnement minimal des établissements de santé. Les conséquences du manque d'accès et de la discontinuité des services de SSR et les déplacements qui en découlent sont sources d'excès de morbidité et de mortalité maternelle et périnatale. En 2021, le pays a enregistré 1 823 décès maternels contre 1 111 décès en 2020 pour un âge moyen de 17 ans des victimes. La situation humanitaire limite la capacité des adolescents et des jeunes à accéder aux services qui contribuent à réduire la transmission du VIH et à prévenir les grossesses précoces/non désirées et les avortements clandestins. 
Le SCI alignera sa réponse humanitaire sur celle du pays en renforçant le système de santé pour fournir des soins de santé primaires, promotionnels, préventifs et curatifs aux populations affectées, en particulier aux enfants, ainsi que la référence de ceux qui ont des besoins plus spécifiques. La réponse 2023 consistera à renforcer, à équiper et à motiver les agents de santé communautaires et les volontaires communautaires recrutés par les districts sanitaires pour prendre en charge les enfants, y compris les adolescentes, et les femmes enceintes et allaitantes, à proximité de leur domicile et pour promouvoir leurs droits en matière de santé sexuelle et reproductive. Les accoucheuses traditionnelles seront responsabilisées, selon les besoins, par le biais de l'approche de délégation de tâches, afin de garantir la fourniture de soins de SSR. Un système de feedback communautaire sera mis en place pour soutenir les interventions.
Le SCI aidera 100 000 personnes dans les six régions humanitaires du Burkina Faso.

project_name: Expansión y fortalecimiento de atención institucional-comunitaria multi-sectorial para niños, niñas, adolescentes y sus familias en Venezuela.
project_objective:
SC y socios proponen una intervención multidisciplinar en los estados de Anzoategui, Zulia, Miranda, Distrito Capital, Delta Amacuro y Sucre, para atender a las necesitades de NNA de manera holística. 

La implementación tomará en cuenta los hallazgos de análisis de género y de necesidades previamente desarrollados por la organización, así como un plan de acción que permita adaptar la respuesta a las necesidades diferenciadas y evidenciadas por edad, sexo y discapacidades. 

 

El proyecto se enfoca en los sectores de protección, educación, nutrición y salud, y seguridad alimentaria.  

Las acciones inmediatas buscaran fortalecer el sistema de protección comunitario e institucional, generando mayor atención psicosocial en las comunidades, consolidando los mecanismos de derivación y fortalecer las capacidades de los CPNNA para que presten servicios con mayor capacidad y calidad. Se facilita la gestión de casos a NNA con riesgos de abuso infantil y en coordinación con el sistema de protección se dará respuesta a sus necesidades. Se facilitará apoyo psicosocial individual a los casos que lo requieran. SC conformará comités comunitarios de protección, dedicados a la promoción y defensa de los derechos de la niñez y adolescencia, igualdad de género y prevención de VBG, así como la identificación y derivación oportuna de casos. Finalmente se fortalecerán las capacidades técnicas de los CPNNA y fiscalías adscritas a la Dir. General para la Protección de la Familia y la Mujer para el mejoramiento de la prestación del servicio a sobrevivientes, tomando en cuenta sus necesidades diferenciadas. Se ofrecerán servicios de gestión de casos con riesgos de protección identificados (incluida la violencia sexual y de género), con referenciación a otros servicios e instancias del Sistema de Protección infantil. 

En educación, se fortalecerán capacidades técnicas en los docentes comunitarios y de educación formal de inicial, primaria y bachillerato, así como al equipo directivo, en INNE, Educación en Emergencia, Participación Infantil y Juvenil, Escuela Segura, educación inclusiva, aprendizaje acelerado y significativo, didáctica de la lengua y la matemática, a fin de contribuir en la formación de líderes proactivos, resilientes y comprometidos en desarrollar estrategias curriculares que respondan a necesidades diferenciadas de grupos vulnerables en contextos de emergencia. Asimismo, se fortalecerán capacidades a 7 Centros Alternativos de Aprendizaje, a fin de garantizar una atención segura y de calidad. 

En Nutrición, entendiendo que la desnutrición aguda es una de las principales causas de mortalidad para los niños menores de 5 años (U5), y los efectos en su desarrollo son a larga plazo, y que la mujeres/adolescentes en gestación o lactancia son una población en riesgo, las intervenciones de SC y socios se enfocan en disminuir la vulnerabilidad y a fortalecer las capacidades de recuperación a través de incrementación del acceso a los servicios de nutrición en la comunidad para evaluación, prevención y tratamiento; en el mejoramiento del conocimiento y las prácticas de alimentación a Lactante y Niño Pequeño y Lactante en Emergencias (ALNP-E). 

En salud, las actividades estaran destinadas a apoyo de centros de salud primaria mediante el aprovisionamiento de insumos, incluido material de EPP; consultas de APS, SSR y SM, con un enfoque principal en salud materno infantil; capacitaciones al personal de salud sobre IPC, COVID-19, Cuidados de primaria infancia, SSR, VBG y fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitaria con la formación de voluntarios comunitarios en salud y promoción de salud. 

En SA se apoyarán a los hogares con casos de desnutrición y presencia de PLW, derivados del componente de nutrición, con asistencia alimentaria como complemento a su recuperación y/o fortalecimiento. Se estima la entrega mensual de kits de alimentos básicos durante 5 meses en paralelo a las actividades a las actividades de nutrición, de forma incondicional.

project_name: Ensuring continuity of learning for adolescents and youth in safe environment.
project_objective:
The proposed project of NRC aims to ensure that the displacement affected adolescents and youths from the Rohingya and host communities can proclaim their rights to ongoing learning and education in a supportive environment. The sectoral operational plan will continue to guide the implementation process, with a coordinated process which will focus on utilizing Myanmar curriculum for learning. Specialised services will be designed, implemented, and monitored to ensure the access to inclusive education for female students, students with disabilities and youth at protection risks including LGBTI community. Process will be started with education need assessment to identify adolescent and youth (age group with 13 to 24 years) needs where special attention will be given to the learners with disabilities. Based on the findings on the need assessment NRC will seek to provide access to the targeted group for relevant and high-quality learning which will increasing their educational and market driven livelihood opportunities. A customized life skills program including PSS, professional skills training, pre-vocational and vocational training will also be developed and provided. Functional literacy, numeracy, and digital literacy related basic skills will be included with the linkage with skill development programme. Moroever, education in emergency also be imbedded as a part of DRR and risk mitigation which has been clarified in the cross-cutting section of this proposal. Rohingya students will have access to the use of current Myanmer curriculum resources through ALP. Services will include involvement of both rohingya and host in community activities and sports which will ensure social cohesion. Emphasis will be given on female learners with disabilities and LGBTI community for the inclusion of gender and diversity. NRC will work jointly with UNO and other stakeholders to support the host community students reducing engorged learning gap that will also improve the involvement of the government. Remedial classes, conditional monetary assistance, asset or repairing provisions, are few measures that can be taken to mitigate the gaps. A safe space, mostly with CBLF modality to ensuring cost effectiveness for learners to learn, engage, and experiences sharing opportunity will be given through inclusive programming. This space will be renovated or built with temporary community-based learning facilities, gender-specific WASH facilities and water sources, solar power for ventilation and lighting, boundaries etc. NRC will also provide appropriate services for learners with disabilities with structured and documented referral pathways. Besides physical modification offline learning for learners/ children with disabilities will also be incorporated in the programme. To reduce gender participation gap, teacher and facilitator training will be offered by using a framework for professional development of teachers. 
Building capacity on inclusive and gender-responsive educational practices, crisis-sensitive planning, management, and coordination for quality provision will be ensured in collaboration with other actors as well as the government. Throughout the project, curricula and guidelines will be produced and provided to the partners and government. Community education groups will be formed including facilitators, community members, and guardians/ parents of the students. These stakeholders will serve as important discussion forums for the learning process, feedback, raising awareness of initiatives for inclusive education. Better Learning Programme (BLP), psychosocial support, supporting sports activities, and short-term learning programs will alos be included in the services, along with spreading life-saving information and engaging with the local community. The distribution of necessary resources and dignity kits will be included as well.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Support to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will utilize the humanitarian pipeline for crops, vegetables and fisheries kits from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). Where markets are functional, market-based interventions such as direct purchases and or local seed and tool fairs will be sought as informed by respective market assessments. These activities will be complimented by capacity building/training modules in the specific livelihoods so as to improve the targeted farmer production, productivity capacities and improve yields and returns. The fisheries training will enable target beneficiaries utilize their kits in the proper way and also improve their knowledge and skills in fish processing, preservation and marketing. The crops and vegetable production training will be based on the crop production seasonal calendar which includes land preparation, planting weeding, pest and disease management, harvesting, post-harvest management and marketing. Using the Training of Trainers (ToT) approach, the project will target 7,500 crop/vegetable farmers and 4,500 fisher folks with assorted livelihoods inputs support as well as training and engaging community-based extension workers to provide the technical support to these farmers while they replicate the training to the other beneficiaries. The proposed interventions will also train targeted households with trainings on approved agronomic practices, pests and disease control, post-harvest handling and value addition and linkages to markets and other value chain actors in addition, 1,500 HHs will be supported through unconditional/conditional cash transfer programming especially in flood and conflicted affected areas. The action will also target 1,250 HHs with small ruminant (goat/sheep) or poultry restocking through livestock voucher modality, 750 women, youth and men will be engaged in VSLAs/IGAs while 450 HHs will be engaged in natural resource management and climate adaptation activities. The project will support develop youth employable skills through TVET training for 1,000 youths in trades such as welding, bakery, tailoring brick laying and masonry and carpentry, motor mechanics among others for self-sustenance.
To ensure integration, the intervention will target nutrition & health centers, schools and mother garden’s locations conveniently with/without access and proximity of a water source. Additional community gardens will be promoted at locations such as schools, health facilities where they will be jointly tended by students and community volunteers. The FSL interventions will be designed taking into consideration and incorporating mainstreaming of protection, safety, GBV prevention, Prevention of Sexual Abuse & Exploitation and conflict sensitivity analysis.  The project teams will work closely with local authorities to identify persons with disabilities both men and women so that they are supported. This number is not expected to exceed 5% of the 10,500 HH targeted. This ensures participants are selected based on needs alone, a rigorous community-based targeting process with participation and inclusion of vulnerable groups such as female and child headed households, disabled and the elderly.  The proposed project will also take into consideration cross-cutting issues like environmental protection, HIV/AIDS, community-based participatory planning, gender, nutrition will be considered during project implementation.
All agricultural and fisheries activities will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Agriculture in order to ensure that government extension workers benefit from and also contribute to the technical components that will be offered by the project by so doing building capacities that will continue to be utilized after project closure. Community based extension workers such as lead farmers will be trained to continue supporting other farmers during and after project closure. Skilling component will be done in liaison with the vocational training institutions.

project_name: Seguridad alimentaria y medios de vida para la población afectada por la situación humanitaria en Venezuela
project_objective:
El proyecto está conformado por cuatro ejes principales, basado en las necesidades identificadas, población vulnerable y la experiencia de intervenciones actualmente implementándose. NRC tiene la capacidad de adaptar y ampliar sus proyectos, aportando y proponiendo: 

A) Proveer de insumos, herramientas y asistencia técnica que ayude a mejorar la producción y construcción de capacidades en centros educativos que tienen componente técnico agropecuario, con niños, niñas y adolescentes, así como las comunidades aledañas. Esto conlleva el fortalecimiento del modelo productivo orgánico, auto-suficiente y sostenible que sirva de modelo para replicar a nivel de pequeños productores. Entre otras cosas se contempla la entrega de ganado vacuno, ovino, porcino, pollos y gallinas, sistemas de producción de queso; ordeños mecánicos; restauración y rehabilitación de espacios para pasto, siembra, gallineros, jardines, semilleros, viveros, dotación de semillas, tanques de agua y sistemas de riego; alimentos para ganado y animales de granja. Así como todo tipo de apoyo en el área técnica agropecuaria, emprendimiento y capacidad técnica para jóvenes, en sinergia y de forma complementaria con otros proyectos sectoriales ASH, educación, protección, bajo el modelo integral de intervención de NRC. 

B) Concienciación en hábitos de vida saludables y apoyo técnico a hogares en riesgo de inseguridad alimentaria (réplica de modelos productivos exitosos, construyendo capacidades, sostenibilidad y auto-producción ecológica). Se promueve un cambio cultural respecto a hábitos saludables a través de una intervención integral y complementaria, para ayudar en la toma de conciencia sobre la importancia de una buena alimentación, preparación y cocinado, huertos familiares y comunitarios, comedores y ollas comunitarias para personas en tránsito, personas de la tercera edad y/o niños, entrega de semillas, mejora de riego, cultivos y métodos alternativos. 

C) Apoyo a las escuelas y familias de los alumnos: niños y adolescentes. Trabajo conjunto y complementario con proyectos de educación (comedores escolares) en la que se alcanza la mejora de la asistencia escolar, unido a la mejora en las condiciones de seguridad alimentaria de las familias y comunidad. Integral y articulado con proyectos de protección y ASH. 

D) Distribuciones de bolsas de alimentos. Dirigidas a grupos más vulnerables identificados, NRC distribuye una canasta de alimento para atender los gastos calóricos necesarios para 2 o 3 meses de una familia con 4 personas en promedio. Particularmente, las modalidades de asistencia se adaptarán según las necesidades de la población y respetando cualquier riesgo sanitario que pueda afectar a los beneficiarios.
