project_name: Projet post- inondation pour l'amélioration des moyens de subsistance et des services écosystémiques.
project_objective:
Le Tchad est un vaste pays enclavé avec une population de 16,8 millions d'habitants. C'est l'un des pays les plus pauvres du monde, classé 187e sur 189 dans l'indice de développement humain, et 113e sur 116 dans l'indice de la faim. Plus d'une personne sur trois (6,1 millions) avait besoin d'une aide humanitaire dans le pays (PRH 2022). Le pays accueille la plus grande population de réfugiés du Sahel, avec 555 787 réfugiés Soudanais, centrafricains, Nigérians et Camerounais. La situation des conflits au Tchad et dans les pays voisins, les facteurs de stress climatiques, les hausses des prix des denrées alimentaires et la pandémie de COVID-19 ont été les principaux moteurs de l'insécurité alimentaire dans la région.
En plus de la concurrence accrue sur les terres arables et les ressources, ces dernières années, le Tchad a connu une augmentation de la fréquence, de l'intensité et de la variabilité des chocs météorologiques tels que les inondations et les périodes de sécheresse. Le changement climatique et la dégradation de l'environnement entraînent une détérioration de la qualité des sols, une pénurie d'eau, de graves sécheresses et des inondations qui ont toutes un effet disproportionné sur les communautés vulnérables, notamment sur les femmes et les filles, et une augmentation des conflits pour le contrôle des ressources naturelles limitées. Cela génère une vulnérabilité croissante liée à la pression démographique, aux risques technologiques, sanitaires, hydrométéorologiques et socio-économiques, à l'urbanisation incontrôlée, à la dégradation de l'environnement ainsi qu'à l'incidence des épidémies. 
Le Tchad connaît actuellement des inondations sans précédent, les pires depuis 30 ans, en raison des pluies torrentielles qui ont provoqué la rupture des berges des fleuves Logone et Chari. Ces inondations font suite à une vague de pluies intenses observées entre juillet et septembre 2022. Jusqu'à présent, les inondations ont directement affecté plus d'un million de personnes à N'Djamena et dans 18 provinces du pays, dévastant 465 030 hectares de terres cultivées, emportant plus de 19 000 têtes de bétail et provoquant des dommages importants aux habitations et aux infrastructures clés (routes et ponts). 
Le secteur de l'éducation n'a pas été épargné par la crise des inondations que traverse le pays. Le Cluster Sécurité Alimentaire dénombre actuellement 1 143 écoles affectées pour un total de 430 133 élèves (dont 46% de filles) dans 12 provinces. Outre les familles dont les moyens de subsistance ont été affectés par les intempéries et qui sont par conséquent exposées à des risques élevés d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, les inondations auront un impact sur les enfants d'âge scolaire qui risquent d'être privés d'accès à l'éducation. Pour les adolescentes, l'abandon scolaire peut marquer une fin définitive de la scolarité si elles sont données en mariage ou engagées dans les tâches ménagères.
Cette crise environnementale et humanitaire a incité le gouvernement à déclarer l'état d'urgence le 19 octobre. 
Le PAM a été en première ligne de cette crise et joue un rôle actif dans les différents mécanismes de coordination mis en place par le gouvernement et les acteurs humanitaires pour assurer une réponse rapide, cohérente et complémentaire avec les autres secteurs. 49 559 personnes touchées par les inondations ont déjà reçu du PAM 178,5 millions de tonnes de nourriture, dont 12,6 millions de biscuits à haute teneur énergétique (HEB), 20 300 repas chauds et 209 230 USD distribués en espèces au 25 octobre 2022. Globalement, le PAM vise à aider directement 300 000 personnes vulnérables touchées par les inondations à travers le pays, en se concentrant sur les provinces les plus touchées et N'Djamena.
Bien que les inondations soient souvent présentées comme nuisibles et destructrices, elles ont également de nombreux impacts positifs et procurent des avantages aux populations et à la nature grâce aux techniques de collecte de l'eau.

project_name: Livestock asset protection and restoration (animal health, feed distribution/production, distribution of animals)
project_objective:
The overall estimated Sector PIN for 2023 – of food insecure and those at risk of food insecurity – is estimated at 13.9 million, with 12 million facing acute food insecurity and 1.9 million people at risk of sliding into food insecurity (HNO 2023). The acute food insecure figure includes 1.9 million people living in camps and deemed to be 100 percent food insecure. Livestock production is vital in Syria to sustain food availability, food diversity/nutrition and income generation among vulnerable women and men affected by the drought-like conditions and prevailing economic hardships. Livestocksector is facing many challenges that are forcing small-scale vulnerable households to adopt negative copying strategies which includes distress selling-off of their assets, subsequently losing a considerable source of income.
In this context, FAO has designed a project to assist  90,667 vulnerable crisis-affected food insecure farming households (equivalent to  544,000 people) in Syria through protecting and restoring their main production assets (livestock).
The objective of the proposed action is to protect the livestock assets of targeted vulnerable herders through the provision of vaccinations and treatment as well as supporting the provision of feed for the herds of the most vulnerable. The expected project outputs are:
Output 1: Livestock productivity for  80,000 vulnerable crisis-affected breeders is maintained and improved. 
This output aims at improving the availability of animal feed for the purpose of asset protection for 25,000 vulnerable households (300 kg of feed per household, in line with sector recommendations) as well as boosting milk availability through enhanced livestock production. Output 1 also seeks to provide veterinary services (vaccines and/or treatment) for 55,000 herders throughout the country.
Output 2. Improving animal reproduction for about 10,667 beneficiaries through artificial insemination and capacity building, contributing to increased livestock production. This output aims at restoring livestock production through distribution of animals to small scale vulnerable households who lost their animals due to the drought-like conditions and prevailing economic crisis. 
All outputs would include capacity building to enhance the technical skills of herders and technicians and to enable them to resume production in a viable, efficient and productive way and better cope with the challenging conditions.

project_name: Improving living conditions of displaced populations in Lac province through data, Shelter and NFI distribution
project_objective: Since 2014, the crisis unfolding in Lac Province has been characterized by numerous challenging factors, such as insecurity, flooding, large-scale and continuous population movements (Internally Displaced Persons, returnees) as  well  as  community  clashes  and  socioeconomic-related  tensions.  Currently,  there  are  more  than  240,000  Internally Displaced Persons ( IDPs) within Lac Province (DTM Round 18), mainly due to the deterioration of security conditions: 99% of IDPs, 100% of returnees from abroad and 77% of former IDP retrunees indicated lack of security conditions as the reason for their displacement. These persons were forced to flee their homes suddenly, leaving behind assets, food and other belongings. In addition, as the majority of these displaced persons are mostly women and children, serious concerns have been raised about the risk of Gender Based Violence (GBV)  and  of  violence  directed  specifically  against  children  such  as  forced  marriage,  exploitation,  and  child  labor  in  the  crisis  areas. Thus to reach these vulnerable groups IOM will:  1. Strengthen the availability of displacement data and trends in Lac province and 2. Improve living conditions of vulnerable displaced households in Lac Province through data-informed, Shelter and NFI activities.

project_name: Improve access to basic WASH services for Gaza population in vulnerable communities and public facilities
project_objective:
The proposed Action Against Hunger (AAH) response to be implemented in 2023 across the Gaza Strip are aligned with Strategic Objectives 2 and 3 as well as the WASH Cluster Objectives 2 and 3.
AAH’s intervention aim to support around 586,179 individuals representing 143499 boys, 137871 girls, 143949 male adults, 137869 female adults, 11021 male elders and 12425 female elders including people with disabilities and specific needs) to gain safe access to the rehabilitated WASH facilities in public facilities (3 health care facilities (HCF) and 9 schools). The intervention will also target unconnected communities (Alawdah and Tal Hawa in Gaza city, Alsatar in Khan Yunis city and Alzanah in Bani Suhila) that rely on cesspits to discharge their wastewater, and will connect them to adequate wastewater drainage system. Furthermore, AAH will construct stormwater drainage systems in Beit Lahia and Gaza to protect vulnerable women, men, girls and boys from being in contact with flooded stormwater or wastewater during the winter season due to the accumulation of stormwater in the cesspits flooding in the streets and in hospitals and schools. In addition, the intervention will support WASH service providers to carry out electro-mechanical repair works for 5 wastewater pump stations and 6 water wells to ensure the continuous operation of these facilities 
The interventions will be complemented with public hygiene promotion and awareness campaigns including but not limited to community orientation sessions and initiatives, hardcopies and digitalized IEC materials to disseminate key messages about proper use of the WASH facilities to enhance the hygiene good knowledge and practices, distribution of personal and dignified hygiene kit in female schools, and peer to peer activities within the targeted schools.
By improving access to sanitation facilities in public places and communication with communities through the hygiene awareness campaign, AAH aims to to improve the communities’ hygiene practices, provide a safe environment and reduce public health risks, and enhance the ownership and active participation of communities, in addition to improving communities access and trust to use AAH FCM channels for feedback and complaints. 
The proposed intervention is guided by AAH Gender and Protection policy and AAH staff endeavor to streamline safety and dignity in all humanitarian interventions. Accountability and participation will be ensured through interviews and focus group discussions and through applying AAH’s thorough Feedback and Complaint Mechanism.

project_name: Protection of Palestine Refugees Affected by Armed Conflict and Forced Displacement in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem)
project_objective:
The daily lives of Palestine refugees living in the West Bank, incl. East Jerusalem, continue to be heavily impacted by the military occupation that has been in place for over 50 years. The resulting protection threats are wide-ranging and severe. Freedom of movement, economic opportunity, security and political rights are heavily curtailed due to the occupation, the pervasive operations and constant presence of Israeli armed forces.

This action is based on UNRWA's protection mandate for more than 890,000 Palestine refugees in the West Bank. Focus is given to the needs of Palestine refugees living in 19 refugee camps who are particularly impacted by the occupation and military incursions. So far in 2022 (by 18 October), the Israeli Security Forces (ISF) has conduct 7739 military operations in the West Bank, which is more than any other year in UNRWA's records, even with more than two months left of the year. 598 of these operations took place in the refugee camps. The action seeks to address the acute needs of the Palestine refugees exposed to conflict-related violence and the risk of displacement and/or forcible transfer.

The project has three key aims: 
(1) to enhance the protective environment for Palestine refugees exposed to protection threats. Based on monitoring and documentation of protection incidents, UNRWA will advocate for the protection of Palestine refugees in accordance with International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL) – including persuasion, mobilisation and denunciation – targeting duty bearers as well as international and national interlocutors. 
(2) to respond to protection threats linked to the risk of displacement and/or forcible transfer, in addition to military operations and settler violence. UNRWA will mitigate the consequences, improving emergency preparedness, and reinforcing the resilience of affected persons. This is achieved through a combination of shelter support to refugees who have been displaced and/or who have had their homes damaged, and through the provision of Psychological First Aid (PFA) and short-term case management services by dedicated protection social workers. In addition, community-wide initiatives are carried out in affected communities. Shelter support is provided in the form of cash transfers that address immediate needs linked to protection threats. Whilst PFA and case management services provide those affected with the mental health support they need to deal with the trauma, improve access to other UNRWA services and specialised partners, and reinforce the resilience of affected persons. At the same time, community-wide initiatives help improve the emergency preparedness of communities under constant protection threats, and/or coordinate comprehensive response after medium to large-scale events.
(3) to improve the safety and accessibility of complaints, including complaints of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). The project has multiple channels to receive and respond to complaints - including a free hotline - and SOPs are in place to receive and respond to SEA complaints in accordance with the oPt PSEA SOPs on Inter Agency Referrals. Complaints of SEA will be handled by PSEA focal points who will ensure a survivor centered approach in how the complaint is handled and support is offered to the survivor. UNRWA WBFO works closely with the PSEA Network and will raise issues requiring technical support and/or external referral through this forum.

project_name: Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to protect the rights of Palestinians in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem)
project_objective: Provision of information, counselling and legal assistance to Palestinians in Area C and East Jerusalem affected by violations of their rights, including housing, land and property rights, residency rights, access to basic services and freedom of movement.

project_name: Protection programming to make people safer and reduce risks from conflict and violence in Gaza
project_objective: The goal of is to respond to urgent protection needs of persons affected by conflict and violence in Gaza, and strengthen the protective environment for conflict-affected communities. NRC will provide frontline protection services in Gaza, particularly comprehensive protection case management and community-based interventions, including civilian self-protection, to improve resilience and community self-protective capacity and overcome barriers to access services.The project aims to reach 12421 persons in need (unique beneficiaries) and offer training and capacity building to 160 persons (members of Gaza Protection Cluster).NRC will target Palestinians in Gaza affected by the protracted protection crisis and conflict, emphasizing services to the most marginalised. Protection case management will target people at risk of violence, coercion, and deliberate deprivation, and will consider compounding vulnerabilities such as age, disability,chronic illness,and acute poverty in prioritization efforts.General protection Case Management is provided in recognition that protection risks are not limited to those addressed by the Child Protection and GBV AORs, and will instead seek to prevent and mitigate risks such as arbitrary arrest and detention,restrictions on FoM, and conflict-related violence. However, NRC will also support strengthening of the interagency referral pathway, ensuring that all cases requiring child protection and GBV support will be promptly referred to specialized agencies according to existing SOPs.According to case plans created with clients, some might receive cash or in-kind assistance to support protective outcomes. This assistance would be in addition and unrelated to cash or material assistance received from other humanitarian or social protection programmes. Cash might be used to support a client to access a service necessary to resolve a protection risk, or recover from an experience of violence. Cash assistance under protection cash management will not be used to supplement basic needs shortfalls.Community-based interventions will include two pillars.1)NRC will work with Ma’an to offer structured PSS to Palestinians affected by conflict, displacements, and human rights violations. Moreover, NRC would like to grow its protection services at the community level, both alone (civilian self-protection) and through partnership (Ma’an community-based protection). project_objective:
Bengoa y Proyecto Nodriza implementan proyectos de asistencia alimentaria para NN y MEL en 6 comedores comunitarios distribuidos en Sucre, Yaracuy y Miranda. Allí a través de jornadas de tamizaje, han verificado trimestralmente durante el último año que los beneficiarios requieren asistencia, bien para prevenir o para tratar (1) el bajo peso y deficiencia de micronutrientes en MEL y (2) la desnutrición y bajo peso en neonatos y NN hasta 12 años, con énfasis en la población >5. Dirigido a: (i) educar en buenas prácticas de nutrición, alimentación e higiene a la comunidad y a las MEL; (ii) tratar la malnutrición en NN >5 y el bajo peso en NNA y MEL; (iii) dotar de una fuente de agua segura para la higiene y alimentación en el hogar de MEL, a través de la entrega de filtros de agua (TANDAS); y (iv) educar en técnicas de purificación de agua y baby wash. 

NUT:

project_name: Strengthening child protection services, mine risk education, prevention and response to GBV concerns in Syria.
project_objective:
World Vision Syria Response through this project aims to provide child protection services, mine action and GBV prevention and response services in northwest Aleppo, north-west Syria, Tal Abyad and Ras Alin to ensure improving the quality of community- based services through a holistic approach and expand the reach and facilitate the access of widows and their children to CP and GBV services, in addition of strengthening the capacities of local actors in the child protection and gender domains. WV is currently not operating in NES but with the intention to expand operations in possible locations and initiate close coordination with the cluster/AoR in the northeast region. The proposed project will include community centers, CFSs and WGSSs and will cover urban areas and camps specially widow camps. To ensure the access for the hard-to-reach areas the project also will include mobile teams. The main objective of the project is to enhance the prevention and response of child protection and GBV concerns and ensure the mitigation of related risks with adopting a holistic approach: through the provision of quality child protection services which will include general and specialized CP services (case management) including children with disabilities, the provision of GBV prevention and response services which includes (case management). The project will include establishing effective and community-based service mapping, PFA, PSS for children and adults and PM+ for adults, in addition of supporting the most vulnerable children and women with CVAs and Cash for protection. Risk education and awareness will be provided in supporting the implementing partners to provide quality, gender and age-appropriate messages including child friendly material. When relevant, the project will integrate mine risk education into CP and GBV awareness and advocacy activities. Actions will implement strategies that empower women and girls and prevent GBV, with a particular focus on adolescent girls and to reduce the impact of violence and physical harm. The project aims to strengthen the capacity of humanitarian actors and stakeholders at the national and community levels to assess, analyze and address protection risks and needs and to respond to child protection concerns in Syria and build the capacity of GBV specialist and non-specialist to respond, prevent and mitigate GBV.

When appropriate and needed, World Vision and partners will offer legal counselling and assistance, referrals and information sharing where a legal advisor will be presented to discuss with individuals who may have challenges in documentation, marriage and/or custody disputes. This activity will be part of the services provided under individual case management. 

As part of accountability to affected populations and taking into consideration that WMGB are the primary stakeholders WV will ensure the needs of different age and gender groups are addressed and considered throughout the project through regular MSNAs and other needs assessment processes at the local and national levels.

All above activities will be taken into consideration the Safeguarding and PSEA minimum standards and best practices specially after the COVID pandemic and the increased risks after the online modalities and the stressors that raised due to the socio-economic pressure and shortage of services.

Monitoring and evaluation activities will be carried out for all the above-mentioned activities taking into account the sensitivity of some activities (such as case management), All monitoring and evaluation activities will be in accordance with the guidelines shared by the coordination teams (Protection cluster; CP, GBV and MA AoRs), in addition to the periodic reporting mechanisms (4Ws, CM reporting tool), and other reporting mechanisms.

project_name: Improving Access to General Protection Services and Building the Capacity of Vulnerable Rohingya Refugees and Host Communities in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
DRC aims to prevent and respond to the various protection threats identified in the camps 6, 10, 11,12 and in the host communities of Palong Khali and Rajapalong. DRC will provide General Protection services ( case management, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness raising, capacity building and community engagement in camp 6, 10, 11 and 12  aiming to avoid the overlaps in services. This will be done through the project by focusing on bolstering synergies and integrating with other protection and non-protection actors, direct case management services will be made available (wherever possible and appropriate). DRC plans to build on its success by increasing its funding for community-based safety and security initiatives. DRC will provide community-led awareness and sensitization, case management, follow-up and referrals, protection monitoring, and community-led peacebuilding and conflict resolution initiatives are just some ways in which existing community groups will be bolstered to detect better, prevent, and respond better to protection risks.

DRC will conduct disaggregated age, gender, and diversity analysis to inform its programming response (AGD). Alongside, DRC will increase its protection monitoring initiatives to better inform its protection monitoring and advocacy efforts. In order to ensure that data is systematically collected on specific vulnerabilities like PwDs, single-headed households, and sexual minorities, DRC will improve the sampling methodology and expand the staff and volunteer base's capacity to collect data on a wide variety of risks, including protection risks. Further, more women will be included in the community's volunteer force. In order to prevent unnecessary duplication of effort, DRC caseworkers will maintain close communication with the existing complaint and feedback procedures. This involves collaborating and interacting with the CFM and CFP on behalf of each case management client to ascertain that he or she is not already receiving assistance and forwarding any appropriate non-protection situations to the CFM and CFP. Besides, DRC will target beneficiaries who previously has very limited access to protection services and will also conduct outreach sessions in this area.

DRC will be providing PSEA training to its whole employees and volunteers will frequently gives the network SEA data. Additionally, DRC will participate actively in the PWG and its related sub-sectors. Going forward, DRC plans to increase the frequency with which protection monitoring data is shared with the PWG and sub-sectors in the form of summarized overviews of risks observed in the camps while also continuing to comply with routine reporting requirements by the sector and ad hoc requests on information that may arise. To ensure that refugees have access to assistance, that humanitarian aid and protection activities do not cause harm, DRC will also continue providing protection mainstreaming training to non-protection actors in accordance with the resources and guidance provided by the sector.

In the end, DRC will keep working with RRRC and CiCs to coordinate efforts to ensure timely access is prioritized, and resource gaps and duplications are avoided through coordination. Briefings on DRC's operations in the camps and efforts to increase awareness about the significance of protective measures are shared routinely in advocacy briefings with the CiCs to ensure alignment and continuing the project interventions with sustainable strategies together with other actors and partners in an integrated approach.

project_name: Monitoring de protection et monitoring régional harmonise (P21) dans la province du Lac au Tchad
project_objective:
L’actuelle intervention vise à fournir l’assistance d’urgence en Protection, Abris/AME et à renforcer le secteur CCCM dans le cadre de la réponse HCR au Chad. Ces secteurs sont classés parmi les quatre clusters ayant reçu le moins de financements ces deux dernières années alors que le nombre de population augmente, et les besoins d’assistance humanitaire sont de plus en plus croissant. La région du Lac, l’une des régions les plus affectées par la crise, compte à ce jour 381,289 personnes déplacées internes, selon le DTM 18, parmi lesquels environ 362,063 personnes restent dans une situation d’extrême précarité selon les données de base pour le risque de sévérité (HPC 2023). Les besoins en matière de protection y sont critiques et le manque d’abris pour plusieurs ménages dans les sites des PDI, qui expose ces derniers à divers risques, y compris sanitaires. Durant l’année 2022, le monitoring de protection a répertorié 1,785 incidents de protection contre 1,544 en 2021. Une hausse d’incidents de 16%, dont 51% se sont déroulés au domicile des personnes déplacées. Les nombreuses victimes de graves violations des droits humains et les survivants ont un accès limité à la justice et manquent de documents d’identité (65% de PDI en 2022 ne possède pas de documents d’identité selon le monitoring P21). De même, les tensions inter et intracommunautaires constituent également des facteurs aggravant la crise. A cela s’ajoutent les inondations fluviales et pluviales dont la réponse est mitigée en raison de la faible capacité des partenaires de la protection et du CCCM, et Abri/AME.
Ce projet a pour objectif d’améliorer l'environnement de protection des personnes affectées dans la province du Lac au travers du renforcement du cadre légal, du monitoring de protection et de l’amélioration de la réponse. 
D’abord, le renforcement du cadre légal consiste à soutenir les efforts du gouvernement dans le processus de domestication de la convention de Kampala. En effet, le processus d’adoption du projet de loi nécessite des activités avant et après adoption pour une réelle appropriation, vulgarisation. Concernant le renforcement du monitoring, il s’agira de renforcer le système existant, créer des synergies et actions complémentaires avec ce qui existe pour une meilleure répartition pour une bonne couverture des zones. Pour mémoire, la stratégie du cluster protection comporte les activités relevant de la responsabilité de la coordination du cluster, notamment de (i) fournir des analyses de protection à la communauté humanitaire et de développement permettant de déclencher des réponses appropriées ainsi que (ii) promouvoir la centralité de la protection dans tous les secteurs. A travers donc le monitoring des incidents et le monitoring régional dit P21, des données pourront être fournies au cluster afin de fournir lesdites analyses. 
Pour une collecte efficace des informations et des données de protection y compris les incidents liés aux VBG et à la protection de l’enfance, une harmonisation des outils de collecte de données se fera sous le lead des coordinatrices des clusters protection, sous clusters VBG et Protection de l’Enfance. 
L’intervention de la protection sera basée sur cinq axes prioritaires à savoir:
-Le monitoring de protection et la réponse multisectorielle (pour assurer la veille humanitaire et un meilleur encrage communautaire) 
-La coexistence pacifique (pour le renforcement des capacités des structures communautaires et les activités génératrices de revenus (AGR)) 
-La protection légale et le renforcement de l’accès à la justice (pour assurer le plaidoyer envers les autorités et l’accès aux services de justice) 
-La documentation civile des Personnes à Besoins Spécifiques (PBS) et victimes de violations des droits humains (pour renforcer leur accès aux droits et minimiser les risques d’apatridie)
-Le soutien psychosocial et matériel aux survivants des incidents de protection, à travers le counseling, les appuis matériels et en AGR

project_name: Soutien alimentaire d’urgence et restauration des moyens d’existences des personnes affectées par la crise alimentaire et sécuritaire dans les Régions du Centre Nord, du Nord, du Sahel, de l'Est et de la Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective:
La dernière analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de novembre 20221 indique une détérioration de la situation de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle au Burkina Faso dans les zones à défis sécuritaire plus particulièrement dans les zones sous blocus. Les besoins en sécurité alimentaire devraient atteindre plus de 9,1 millions de de personnes pendant la période de soudure 2023 (juin-août), dont plus de 3,5 millions en phase 3+. Les besoins urgents se concentrent principalement dans les régions de l'Est (19%), du Centre Nord (17,5%), du Sahel (17,3%), de la Boucle du Mouhoun (10%) et le Nord (9%).  Selon les résultats de l’atelier bilan de la soudure 2022 tenu en novembre 2022, 81% des besoins planifiés ont été couverts par la réponse soudure. Des efforts supplementaires sont donc necessaires pour améliorer le taux de couverure en 2023.01.

En ce qui concerne les moyens d'existence, le volet est sous financé, ce qui réduit la relance économique, l’insertion des ménages PDI dans un circuit productif, la restauration progressive de leurs moyens de subsistance dans une perspective de durabilité.  En effet les resultats de l’atelier bilan de soudure 2022, indique que moins de 43% des besoins des ménages n’ont pas été couvert dans ce secteur. 

D'autres facteurs jouent également un rôle important dans l'insécurité alimentaire au Burkina Faso. Il s'agit notamment de la dégradation de l'environnement qui nuit à la performance des services écosystémiques avec des implications sérieuses pour les populations qui sont fortement dépendantes des ressources naturelles pour leurs moyens de subsistance et le manque de capacité et de moyens pour mener des activités génératrices de revenus.

L’objectif global de l’action est de contribuer à la satisfaction des besoins alimentaires, nutritionnels et à la restauration des moyens d’existence des populations affectées par les conflits et la mauvaise production agricole dans les régions de l’Est, Centre Nord, Sahel, Nord et la Boucle du Mouhoun.

project_name: Fourniture d’une solution d’abri adapté et AME aux populations affectées par les déplacements au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à améliorer la protection physique, la sécurité et la dignité de 18 900   personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et familles d'accueil vulnérables touchées par le déplacement et vivant dans des conditions inadéquates dans les communes de Kaya, Kongoussi, Tougouri, Dori et Sebba. Cette assistance concerne la fourniture de 2 400 abris d'urgence, 600 abris semi durables, ainsi que 2 700 kits d'articles ménagers essentiels (AME). Les modalités inkinds et cash seront utilisées dépendamment du contexte. Pour atteindre l'objectif du projet, NRC fournira aux personnes déplacées internes les plus vulnérables qui n’ont pas de solution d’hébergement adéquate un appui en abris d'urgence pour leur installation dans les communautés d’accueil et les espaces d’accueil temporaires. Pour les ménages ayant une longue durée de déplacement, souhaitant s’installer durablement vivant dans un logement précaire et ayant un accès à la terre, NRC prévoit un appui en « Cash for Shelter » ou une construction directe dépendamment du contexte. Les familles d’accueil les plus vulnérables constitueront 20% de cette cible dans l’idéal.
Les bénéficiaires seront fortement impliqués dans la mise en œuvre du projet et leur feedbacks, collectés, analysés et pris en compte. Les organisations locales seront aussi renforcées dans une perspective de contribuer à la localisation.

project_name: Assistance en EHA inclusive aux personnes déplacées et aux communautés d’accueils affectées par la crise du Burkina Faso dans les régions du Sahel, Centre-Nord, et Nord
project_objective:
La crise complexe et volatile du Burkina Faso continue de détériorer le contexte sécuritaire du pays depuis 2014. Les premiers mois de l’année 2022 sont marqués par une augmentation massive des personnes déplacées internes (PDI), une augmentation des attaques des points d’eaux et la détérioration significative des conditions de vie de la population en matière d’accès aux services sociaux de base et de la dynamique socio-économiques du pays en général et les régions du Sahel et du Centre Nord en particulier.
Le Sahel et le Centre-Nord sont les plus touchées (68% du total des déplacés), suivi des régions du Nord et de l’Est. La crise a entrainé des mouvements de populations avec une persistance importante des besoins d’assistances humanitaires.
Selon les chiffres provisoires du cluster, sur le plan de réponse humanitaire 2023 environ 3,223,774 de personnes seront dans le besoin d’assistance WASH. 
Le bulletin d’informations du Cluster au mois de Novembre 2022 a rapporté l’intensification des attaques aux points d’eau et les tensions autour des points d’eau à la fois dans la région de Sahel et du Centre Nord. la plupart de ces attaques ont visé des gros systèmes d’adduction d’eau ayant des impacts significatifs en termes de personnes touchées.
Au Sahel
Dans la ville de Djibo, en date du 02 Juin 2022, une attaque dans a engendré plusieurs dégâts qui a touché le réseau d’eau de l'ONEA ,des Postes d’eaux Autonomes (Secteur 5) ,des installations temporaires de Watertrucking.)
A Dori, précisément au niveau du barrage de Yacouta, la station de pompage du réseau urbain qui approvisionne la ville de Dori, a été vandalisée. Ceci a crée un grand dommage sur le système, entrainant un arrêt total de la desserte par l’ONEA de la ville de Dori, soit environ 80 000 personnes impactés par cette attaque. Malgré la mise en service du réseau il faut noter une baisse de 30-45% de la production. 
A Seytenga, l’attaque a provoqué un déplacement massif de PDI vers la ville de Dori (plus de 10 000 personnes) ce qui n’a fait qu’augmenter significativement les besoins en eau et l’assainissement au niveau de la ville.
Les récents attaque de Sebba a occasionné la destruction du groupe électrogène qui faisait fonctionner le réseau de l’ONEA a engendré une diminution du taux de desserte qui était déjà faible car un forage de 7m3/h sur les 4 que compte le système fonctionnait 16h par jour, soit 112m3/j, soit environ 7500 personnes qui ont été impactés par cette attaque.
Au Centre Nord
Suite à l’attaque de Tougouri au mois de Juin 2022, la ligne électrique qui alimentait le système de l’AEPS a été détruit occasionnant ainsi le manque d'eau. Par la suite, le groupe électrogène qui a été mise en place pour pallier ce problème d’approvisionnement en eau tombe souvent en panne suite aux panne récurrente. 
Le 13 juin 2022 à Barsalogho, une PHM et un tank du PEA situé sur le site peulh ont fait l’objet d’attaque. Ces points d’eau étaient d’une grande utilité pour les communautés hôtes et PDI du fait de leur grande capacité. et du fait qu’elles ne tarissaient pas pendant la période chaude, contrairement à la majorité des PMH de Barsalogho.
Au mois de septembre, la station de pompage de l’ONEA (armoires électriques endommagés) au niveau du Lac Dem (15 km nord-ouest de Kaya, route de Kongoussi), ont été vandalisés.  Cela a occasionné la réduction de la production d’eau de plus 70% (3800m3/jour) au niveau de la station. Environ 96 681 personnes sont impactées par cette attaque.
Ce projet a pour objectif de :
- Contribuer à l’amélioration de l’accès sécurisé et digne à l’eau potable des populations affectés par la crise ;
- Faciliter l’accès à des infrastructures d’assainissement sures et inclusives aux populations à risque sanitaire élevé ;
- Améliorer les pratiques d'hygiène de façon inclusive et participative des communautés hôtes et PDIs ;
- Renforcer les mécanismes communautaires en vue de l’autonomisation de la gestion des ouvrages d’eau et assainissement.

project_name: Reducing Protection Risks and Meeting Basic Needs of Conflict-Affected Communities Far North, North West and South West Regions, Cameroon
project_objective:
In the scope of this project, IRC will ensure that affected populations have safe and reliable access to water and sanitation infrastructure, access to basic items and that they can meet their basic needs whilst protecting their livelihoods. 
IRC will provide a range of intervention to support access to WASH infrastructure (rehabilitation/construction of water points, work with Water Management Committees, support to construction of emergency or household’s latrines, distribution of NFI wash related items, development of hygiene promotion focusing on prevention of waterborne diseases such as cholera) and food security (distribution of food voucher or cash to vulnerable households, Train clients on financial management and Facilitate gender discussions among client couples in the community). 
IRC will continue to use data from protection monitoring activities and safety audits to strengthen its response to life-threatening protection risks and psychosocial issues, with a focus on women and children at risk and victims of human rights violations, providing a tailored individual and community response; this response will be PSS, case management, distribution of IPA, referral to other services… depending on the needs of the person. 
IRC will strengthen linkages with community-based organizations (CBOs) and health facilities to ensure an extensive and multi-level capacity response to survivors of GBV, protection risks and violations against children. IRC will train, revitalize these structures and give them monthly support to ensure they can support their community members. IRC will also implement girls shine approach whenever possible.
Finally, IRC will support community-based protection approaches through its paralegal approach in the FN to provide holistic and community-based legal awareness, counselling and assistance to the most vulnerable by strengthening the community paralegal approach. Equally, IRC will support equitable access to justice through justice system strengthening as well as provision of legal awareness, legal counseling and legal assistance to those most at risk, including access to civil status documentation and  housing, land and property rights

project_name: Livelihoods and resilience support to vulnerable and conflict-affected populations throughout Syria to reduce protection risks, negative coping strategies, and improve purchasing power and self-sustainability
project_objective:
Over 11 years into the conflict, Syria remains one of the largest and most complex humanitarian emergencies. Long-term consequences including widespread destruction and the largest number of internally displaced people in the world. In addition to protection threats, the accelerating economic deterioration and impacts of climate change have become additional key drivers of needs, compounding vulnerabilities even further. In 2022, 14.6 million people need humanitarian assistance, an increase of 1.2 million from 2021. In 2021, climate and human-caused shocks affecting natural resources, particularly water, intensified. Erratic rainfall in combination with historically low water levels in the Euphrates River reduced access to water for drinking and domestic use for over five million people and triggered substantial harvest and income losses, decreased hydroelectricity generation, and an increase in water-borne diseases. In the mid to long-term, these developments are expected to have serious and cumulative impacts on health, food insecurity, malnutrition rates, as well as the protection environment.

Long-standing needs of an estimated 6.9 million IDPs remain, particularly for over two million people in 1,760 informal settlements and planned camps, often hosted in inadequate shelters and with limited access to basic services. Overstretched host communities and those who have returned to their – often destroyed – places of origin frequently face inadequate living standards. As the economic situation deteriorates further, the vulnerabilities of people that have not been directly affected by hostilities are also compounded. By population group, it is the vulnerable residents - those that have not been displaced, that show the greatest increase in severity of need - resulting in an increase from 6.4 million to 9.2 million – suggesting that economic deterioration is now a major driver of needs in areas historically less directly affected by hostilities and displacement

The IRC will support 4330 beneficiaries in NES, who are experiencing financial shocks and depend mainly on negative coping strategies to meet their basic needs. This will be in line with the Cash Working Group’s strategy to cover IDPs in host communities according to the overall gap in NES. Through a multipurpose cash modality, affected households will be able to meet their basic needs at the end of a one-month transfer period as their situation stabilizes. To address cases where households are unable to meet their basic needs, the number of transfers will range between one, three, or six rounds. This will provide access to households facing extreme levels of vulnerability with a predictable source of multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA), enabling them to develop positive coping mechanisms that support their resilience to future shocks they may encounter.

Beneficiaries will also receive financial literacy training, which includes a variety of taught skills including identifying differences between needs and wants, living costs, and key start-up business skills. Following three rounds of MPCA, the IRC will integrate project participants into its livelihood-based programs. The IRC implements various projects designed to put participants on the path to early recovery, including vocational training, apprenticeship, small-to-medium enterprise support, and financial management training. In addition, beneficiaries are also trained on how to set up village savings and loans (VSLA) to enable communities to set up projects that serve their communities, build social cohesion and promote joint resource management.

In NWS, IRC will provide support for livelihoods through market-driven skills development and self-employment training to beneficiaries, targeting economically vulnerable households and prioritizing women and youth. Services will be provided via cash for work, MSME, VSLA, vocational training, support to farmers, MPCA, and cash for winter.

project_name: Provision of Shelter and NFI Assistance to Vulnerable Populations Affected by Conflict and Displacement in Syria
project_objective:
The purpose of the Shelter/NFI intervention is to provide lifesaving and life-sustaining shelter and NFI support, and contribute towards the resilience and cohesion of communities and households by improving housing and related community/public infrastructure in Syria. The different components of NRC's Shelter/NFI project are intended to contribute to HRP Shelter & NFI Sector’s Objectives 1 and 2. 
Geographic areas will be targeted based on the severity and scale of needs, inter-agency coordination at hub-level, and access. NRC will provide assistance to vulnerable conflict- and displacement-affected populations, including IDPs, refugees, members of host communities, IDP and refugee returnees, and non-displaced households suffering the effects of the conflict. Where appropriate, multi-sectoral vulnerability scoring techniques will be used that integrate vulnerability indicators. The needs of the different genders, elderly and PWDs will be considered during design, implementation and monitoring processes.  
Based on the needs in Syria for 2022 and 2023 and in line with NRC’s Syria Strategy, this Shelter/NFI project will include emergency, transitional, and recovery response options. These options are not intended to be ""standalone"", and may be delivered in conjunction with one another.  
In NES and NWS (camp- and informal-site settings), activities will be implemented through cross-border operations. NRC will be predominantly focused on the provision of essential winterization assistance (using multi-purpose cash or in-kind assistance, where appropriate) under Activity (1) and rehabilitation of community infrastructure (i.e., roads), as well as providing in-camp transitional shelter and cash for shelter rehabilitation under Activity (2). Shelter and NFI activities will be delivered as a fully integrated, joint programme, where relevant. The implementing modality will be defined based on access constraints and NRC’s capacity, and will include cross-border emergency (unconditional cash, in-kind winterization assistance), transitional (rehabilitation and construction of roads, lighting, and other camp infrastructure), and recovery, where relevant. 
In Government of Syria-controlled areas, NRC will provide core NFIs (in-kind and CVA modalities) to the newly displaced, and support with the rehabilitation and maintenance of collective shelters, as well as with shelter kits. Seasonal NFIs will be provided to households using in-kind or CVA modalities. Rehabilitation of damaged houses will be done using a holistic approach incorporating WASH (rehabilitation of common areas and community infrastructure by ensuring sufficient water storage, connection to water and sewer networks, etc.). Whenever possible, rehabilitation of buildings will include training on shelter repairs, rather than using contractors. In 2023, NRC will explore possibilities on linking housing and infrastructure with solar energy, and further pilot these types of projects in 2023/2024. Other community infrastructure such as markets, schools, and medical centers, will also be rehabilitated in coordination with relevant sectors. Shelter/NFI and WASH activities will be delivered as a fully- integrated joint programme where relevant. The implementing modality will be defined based on access constraints and NRC capacity, and transitional (roads, lighting and other settlement infrastructure) and recovery (housing rehabilitation) needs where relevant.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle d'urgence aux populations affectées par le conflit au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
L'activité proposée vise à fournir une aide d'urgence multisectorielle aux populations vulnérables touchées par le conflit, principalement les personnes déplacées et les communautés d'accueil, au Burkina Faso. Elle visera à offrir une réponse intégrée dans les secteurs de l'assistance alimentaire, de la WASH, des abris et de la protection. Dans le cadre de ce projet, DRC entend soutenir les personnes dans le besoin dans la région du Sahel (Soum, Seno, Oudalan), tout en maintenant les capacités de déployer des équipes mobiles dans d'autres régions du Burkina Faso (province de Yagha au Sahel, Nord, Centre-Nord, Est et Boucle du Mouhoun).

Ainsi, DRC souhaite maintenir son focus en matière d'assistance alimentaire et de nutrition au Sahel, notamment dans les provinces de Seno et d'Oudalan, en plus d'étendre l'action à la province du Soum. De plus, au vu de l'extension de la crise, DRC propose une approche géographiquement flexible dans les secteurs WASH, Shelter & Settlements, et Protection, qui permettrait d'intervenir en cas de nouveaux déplacements dans les provinces affectées du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, de l'Est et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. En WASH, l’intervention vise à assurer que les personnes affectées par le conflit aient accès à l'eau potable et à l'assainissement selon les standards nationaux internationaux ; Augmenter le taux d’accès à l’eau et à un assainissement de base dans les communautés, les écoles et les centres de santé ; Améliorer les conditions sanitaires des femmes, hommes et enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire à travers l’accès à l’Eau, l’Hygiène et l’Assainissement
En abris/AME, l’intervention vise à Fournir dans l’immédiat une assistance d'urgence en abris et articles ménagers essentiels (AME) aux populations affectées par les déplacements internes ; Assurer sur le moyen et long terme, l’accès à des conditions de vie dignes pour les personnes affectées par les déplacements (personnes déplacées internes, familles d’accueil et le cas échéant retournés), en facilitant l’accès à un abri sécurisé et à des AME appropriés.
En protection, l’intervention vise à apporter une réponse immédiate de protection pour répondre aux risques ou incidents de protection identifiée mais aussi de renforcer les communautés affectées sur le plan psychosocial avec des activités à l’échelle de la communauté. Enfin, dans une perspective de mieux appréhender le contexte et les besoins de protection, DRC souhaite renforcer sa prestation de services dans le domaine des VBG notamment via de la prise en charge psychologique et psychosociale ainsi que des référencements dans les situations de déplacements/d’urgence mais aussi apporter une approche gestion de cas en étroite collaboration avec l’Action Sociale notamment dans des zones plus fixes du projet.
Dans une approche de renforcement de la localisation, ce projet travaillera en étroite collaboration avec un autre projet en cours chez DRC, le FLASH, qui est un RRM mis en œuvre par des ONG locales, à savoir A2N et ASMADE. Ce projet contribuera au renforcement de capacités des partenaires OSC locales.

project_name: Provision of Emergency shelter and NFI assistance to the Persons Of Concerns
project_objective: UNHCR will provide life-saving shelter and NFI assistance to the persons affected by conflict and natural disasters such as flooding across Sudan and the population affected by the fire incidents. Newly displaced population especially those affected by recent conflict and population affected by flooding and fire incidents will be prioritized. Where feasible, cash modality will be implemented especially for emergency shelter assistance. Through this project, UNHCR plans to respond to shelter and NFI needs of 1.66 million people through implementing partners. The total financial requirement of this project is $61.3 million. In Shelter/NFI cluster lead capacity, UNHCR will maintain a stock to respond mainly to the displacements in timely manner. UNHCR and implementing partners will inform and consult affected population at each stage of the project and will establish complaint and feedback mechanism.

project_name: Protection Assistance for to IDPs and IDP Returnees in Sudan
project_objective:
Overall, there are 6,596,342 persons in need of protection support across the country. This
includes 3,036,593 IDPs, 969397 returnees, 1,098,272 refugees and 1,492,080 vulnerable
Sudanese. New and protracted displacement, lack of basic services and the deteriorating
economic situation, have all had profound consequences on conflict-affected persons’
immediate physical and mental well-being, living standards, and their long-term resilience.
Rule of law, access to justice and government social protection remains weak in conflictaffected areas of Darfur, South Kordofan and Blue Nile including the two areas controlled
by nonstate actors. The natural disasters, including disease outbreak and scarcity of
resources have further impacted public service delivery and heightened the socioeconomic vulnerability of displaced families.
General protection needs are most severe in the hotspot localities, where inter-communal
conflict and factional fighting have been reported throughout 2021 and people remained
deprive of access to government services in the two areas. Such chaotic situation is
exacerbated by the proliferation of firearms, competition over land and water resources,
unregulated migratory routes, and weak systems for land administration. As a result of
reported incidents: hundreds of civilians were killed or wounded; HLP damaged, looted,
destroyed or occupied; thousands of families displaced; and public facilities destroyed
occupied. Furthermore, UNAMID withdrawal at the end of 2020 created a gap in the
civilian protection framework in Darfur. This left humanitarian protection mechanisms
and services, and durable solutions programming by protection and peacebuilding actors,
as the mainstay across Sudan.
Vulnerable groups - such as women, children, elderly, persons with disabilities and chronic
illnesses - face a range of challenges unique to their individual circumstances,
compounded by their displacement where familial/community support networks not
functioning or are overstretched. These and other groups of people suffer
disproportionately from various protection risks, including violence, sexual and other
forms of exploitation and abuse, and human-rights violations. For women and girls, risks
of GBV remain significant, particularly when they are on the move, working in fields,
collecting water or firewood. Boys and men remain especially at risk of physical violence,
injury and death and arbitrary arrests, as they are often suspected of supporting armed
opposition groups. Child marriage and child labor are on the rise. Access to birth
