project_name: Protection et recherche de solutions durables pour les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile vivant dans les Régions du Sahel, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective:
En 2023, il est estimé que près de 30 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile seront installés dans les Régions du Sahel, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. 90% de ces réfugiés sont installés au Sahel principalement dans les villes de Dori et Djibo où ils vivent dans les mêmes zones d’installation que les PDI. Une telle situation nécessite le maintien d’un dispositif de protection et d’assistance adaptée afin de répondre aux besoins spécifiques mais également de réduire les problèmes liées à la pression sur les ressources des localités d’accueil. 

Le présent projet vise donc à fournir une protection et une assistance d’une part et à rechercher des solutions durables d’autre part au profit des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile maliens vivant au Burkina Faso. Passée la phase d’installation d’urgence des réfugiés à Dori mais également des réfugiés dans le centre-ville de Djibo en 2022 et l’adaptation du dispositif de protection au contexte urbain, les efforts vont se poursuivre pour le renforcement de leur inclusion dans les mécanismes nationaux afin de parvenir à l’objectif de fourniture d’une assistance basée sur la vulnérabilité et non le statut. Malgré le contexte difficile, le partenariat avec les autorités locales sera renforcé afin de permettre également de consolider l’installation des réfugiés dans la ville de Djibo où ils se sont déplacés et vivent dans une situation précaire. Pour les réfugiés installés à Ouahigouya, Yako et Oula, dans la Région du Nord, l'accent sera mis sur le renforcement des structures locales communautaires pour leur intégration dans le tissu socio-économique et sur l’assistance aux plus vulnérables.

project_name: Protection  des populations affectées par la double crise sécuritaire et humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective: Le Burkina Faso traverse une crise sécuritaire sans précédent à la suite d’attaques de groupes armés (GA) qui s’étendent notamment sur les régions du Sahel, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, du Centre Est, des Hauts-Bassins, des Cascades et de l’Est. L’activisme des GANI continuent àprovoquer   des déplacements massifs de population dans presque toutes les régions du pays. Au 31 Décembre, le Burkina Faso comptait 1.882.391 personnes déplacées internes (PDI) enregistrées sur une base individuelle par le CONASUR. 94% de ces PDI se concentrent dans les régions du Sahel, Centre Nord, , Nord, Est, Boucle du Mouhoun et Centre Est. Le Burkina Faso traverse ainsi une crise de protection du fait du nombre de PDI; de multiples déplacements que subissent les ménages; de l’inaccessibilité à certaines populations; de certaines fragilités préexistantes à la crise notamment des conflits intercommunautaires souvent autour de la bonne gouvernance et des questions  foncière particulièrement; des tensions inter communautaires accentuées par des suspicions d’affiliation de certaines communautés aux GANI ou aux milices armées ; de la présence dans ces régions de PDI, retournés Burkinabè, réfugiés, et communautés hôtes très vulnérables ayant tous des besoins de protection et vivant dans des zones avec un faible accès aux moyens de subsistance . Les PDI et leurs communautés d’accueil font face à l’insécurité, l’inaccessibilité ou la faible accessibilité aux vivres, à l’eau, à l’éducation, à la santé, au bien être psychosocial et aux moyens de subsistance dans des communes déjà fragilisées par l’impact du changement climatique. Dans sa stratégie Pluriannuelle 2021-2025 et dans sa stratégie régionale pour le Sahel central, le HCR a réaffirmé son accompagnement aux gouvernements dans leur gestion des populations affectées par la crise avec des activités de Protection, Education, Abris/Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME), Energie et Environnement. Ces priorités définies par le HCR sont en lien avec  le nouveau programme national de développement économique et social (PNDES). Fort de cette analyse de la crise de protection au Burkina Faso, de l’existence des cadres d’action du HCR et du gouvernement du Burkina Faso, et de sa volonté d’accompagner le cluster protection dans la réalisation de ses objectifs sectoriels dans le cadre du HRP 2023, le HCR propose ce projet de protection des populations affectées par le conflit dans les  régions prioritaires autour de: L’enregistrement des PDI en soutien au CONASUR afin d’assurer que ces PDI puissent bénéficier d’une protection et d’une assistance humanitaire optimale ; La documentation des PDI, retournées et autres communautés vulnérables pour leur faciliter l’accès aux droits fondamentaux et leur éviter des violations de droits et libertés ; Le monitoring de protection qui complète l’analyse issue de l’enregistrement et qui tient compte de la mobilité des PDI ; L’engagement communautaire et la redevabilité qui sera renforcée dans tous les domaines d’intervention pour garantir la participation, l’inclusion, la communication avec les communautés, l’éducation à la paix, la Protection contre l’exploitation et les abus sexuelset la redevabilité; La protection contre les violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et la protection de l’enfant (PE) avec des activités de prévention, de mitigation des risques, de réponse multi sectoriels aux VBG et à la PE y compris l’assistance juridique et judiciaire ; La facilitation de l’accès consensuel et sécurisé des PDI à la terre au niveau individuel et collectif pour leur protection et pour une cohabitation pacifique.

project_name: Perfectionnement et amélioration de la gestion des sites d’accueil temporaires et des zones d’accueil de personnes déplacées internes
Apoyo al manejo de la desnutrición aguda global y protección del estado nutricional de niños, niñas y mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia en contexto de emergencia
project_objective:
El objetivo principal del proyecto es reducir la morbilidad y la mortalidad debida a la desnutrición aguda y las carencias en micronutrientes en los grupos más vulnerables que son los niños, niñas y mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (MELs).

Desde el grupo técnico de nutrición (GTN) de Honduras se estima que 48.000 niños y niñas menores de 5 años podrían sufrirán de desnutrición aguda durante el año 2022-2023. De este grupo el 20% cursarán con desnutrición aguda, por lo que tendrán 12 veces más riesgo de muerte comparado a un niño o una niña con un estado nutricional normal. Solamente el 51.4% reciben lactancia materna en la primera hora de vida El 30.2% de niños y niñas de 0 a 5 meses reciben lactancia materna exclusiva. 18.5% a nivel urbano y 38.3% a nivel rural. Por otro lado  hoy en día a nivel nacional, 50% de los niños/as de 6 a 8 meses tienen anemia con consecuencias físicas y fisiológicas negativas, impactando a largo plazo sus capacidades de aprendizaje y desarrollo si una respuesta a gran escala no se implementada para contrarrestar esta tendencia.

El proyecto implementará con la colaboración de socios (ONG nacionales, internacionales y Secretaria de Salud) actividades de  prevención, detección y de manejo de todas las formas de malnutrición que conviven en Honduras (desnutrición aguda, carencias en micronutrientes, desnutrición crónica, desnutrición global, sobrepeso y obesidad) a través del sistema nacional de salud.
 Las actividades en detalle serán: 
1.	Actualización de protocolos de detección y manejo de la desnutrición aguda
2.	Capacitación del personal del sistema de salud y de los socios implementadores en Nutrición y disponibilidad de insumos apropiados
3.	Establecimiento de centro de estabilización nutricional.
4.	Iniciación del MUAC Familiar en zonas prioritarias
5.	Cambio de comportamiento y educación nutricional
6.	Equipos móviles para aumentar alcance y responder a nuevas emergencias
7.	Monitoreo de la información en Nutrición y evaluaciones

El proyecto prevé alcanzar 163,000 NNs menores de 5 años (aproximadamente 83,000 niñas y 80,000 niños), y 47,000 mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia, así como 19,000 hombres con las actividades de prevención, atención y promoción de las buenas prácticas de alimentación del lactante, del niño/a pequeño/a y de las mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia. Aunque el número de hombres cuidadores no se refleja en la meta general del proyecto, si se refleja en la población meta de uno de los indicadores como parte de las intervenciones.

project_name: Securing protection and solutions in communities affected by the Lake Chad Basin Crisis, Far North Region in Cameroon
project_objective:
The Boko Haram insurgency that started in Nigeria spread quickly in the Far-North Region of Cameroun early in 2014, with abduction and killing of civilians, destruction of villages, attacks on military positions, and massive violation of human rights. This led to an relentless movement of populations, both internally and externally, including the arrival of refugees from Nigeria. The protection situation in Far-North Region is a mixed situation, complex and marked by violence inflicted upon the most vulnerable civilians. Besides the armed conflict, the region is still recovering from the recent intercommunal conflict which caused mass displacement and tensions between different communities. Both conflicts have as consequence severe human rights violations include increased gender-based violence, attacks on property, illegal or arbitrary arrests, thefts, lootings of properties and limitation of the freedom of movement due to the loss of civil documentation. All these conflicts are added by flooding which affected around 238,000 people in the last months.

The continued insecurity has resulted in multiple population multiple displacements in Far-North of Cameroon. In its Round 23 Report on displacement conducted in the Far-North Region in June 2022, IOM indicated that more than 377, 800 persons are internally displaced in the Far-North Region due to armed conflict and intercommunal conflict. According to HNO analysis, more than 85% of these displaced persons need protection response. There are over 120,000 Nigerian refugees are living in the Region, both in Minawao camp and communities in the region.   

To contribute to the protection response and fully play its role as the provider of last resort as well as the one of Protection Cluster co-lead lead, UNHCR identified 4 key priorities in 2023: 1) strengthening the centrality of protection, 2) coordination of lead sectors 3) emergency preparedness and response and 4) securing solutions. 

Through a community-based approach, UNHCR intends to secure protection and provide solutions through a comprehensive response. This includes reinforced and expanded protection monitoring and strengthening communities’ ability to contribute to their protection, to respond to protection incidents as well as to participate in the search for solutions. The interventions will focus on community empowerment initiatives, responding to critical GBV and child protection incidents, legal assistance, and support for civil documentation as well as psychosocial services.  In-kind support, Cash-Based interventions, and referrals to available services in the identified communities will be an integral part of the response.  
The use of an area-based approach will consist of selecting specific areas in the 04 districts most affected by the displacement and working with all stakeholders in the priority locations including displaced, host community, returnees and refugees, local authorities, civil society, agencies working in the areas. The approach will ultimately contribute to build sustainability of key services and consequently prevent displacement as well as guarantee greater accountability to affected populations (AAP).

project_name: PERFECTIONNEMENT ET AMELIORATION DE LA GESTION ET LA COORDINATION DES SITES D’ACCUEIL TEMPORAIRES DES PERSONNES DEPLACES INTERNES DANS LA REGION DU SAHEL AU BURKINA FASO
project_objective:
NRC intervient au Burkina Faso dans le cadre de la crise des déplacés que connaît le pays depuis 2019. L’organisation apporte une assistance humanitaire au Centre Nord, au Nord et au Sahel. 
Ses activités au Sahel ont débuté en avril 2021 avec la prise en compte du volet Gestion des sites d’accueil Temporaire. En effet, depuis cette période, NRC a accompagné le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso à la Gestion des Sites d’Accueil Temporaires dans les communes de Djibo, Gorom-Gorom, Bani et Dori en 2021. En 2022, NRC est intervenu dans les localités de Dori, Bani et de Gorom-Gorom dans la Gestion des Sites. Les interventions dans la GSAT concernent aussi bien les personnes déplacées internes vivant dans les sites et en dehors des sites. 
Le projet « perfectionnement et amélioration de la gestion et la coordination des sites des personnes déplacées internes dans la région du Sahel au Burkina Faso » va perfectionner et améliorer les acquis des deux (2) dernières années par un suivi rapproché des activités menées dans les sites et en hors sites.
En concertation avec les communautés dans les sites et avec la collaboration des services de l’action humanitaire, le projet va contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs spécifiques suivants :
* Renforcer l’accès sûr, égal et coordonné des PDI dans les sites d’accueil temporaires, les zones d’accueil de déplacés et les établissements similaires aux services multisectoriels 
* Identifier et permettre un meilleur environnement de protection et d’assistance aux personnes déplacées ;
* Renforcer la résilience individuelle et communautaire par l'autonomisation des personnes déplacées, la participation aux décisions qui affectent leur vie, la communication bilatérale et la cohésion sociale entre les personnes déplacées vivant dans des sites et des environnements similaires et les communautés environnantes

project_name: Quality Education for Emergency Affected Children and Youth in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the intervention is to ensure that emergency affected girls and boys as well as youth continually access quality learning opportunities relevant for their psycho-social well-being, physical and cognitive development.  The project targets children and youth aged between 6 - 17  from IDP, returnees and host community families with age appropriate interventions that respond to their education needs. Primary focus for this project is displacement affected out-of-school children and youth affected by conflict and climate emergencies. NRC anticipates to reach 38,873 children (52% girls); 875 adults (400 men ; 475 women [375 teachers & 500 parents/caregivers and other non-teaching professionals) as direct beneficiaries. The project will focus on strengthening and improving quality and delivery of education in four strategic response areas which are 1) First Phase response - through NRC's mobile response operations and targeting newly displaced families, with short term education activities lasting from 6-9 months. 2) Formal education - conducted through NRC's static program operations across the country in prioritized counties where NRC has existing physical presence; 3) Non Formal education through ALP classes for over-aged children who missed years of schooling due to conflict and displacement and 4) Youth Education and training with an emphasis on vocational skills training, peace-building and life-skills training.  In close collaboration with parents, caregivers and local actors, NRC will construct and repair learning spaces/classrooms and gender segregated school WASH facilities; provide school hardware assets (desks/benches), essential learning materials, teacher aids, recreational & hygiene kits; girls dignity kits for MHM; support mgt of schools through teacher selection, recruitment, motivation, training on child centered pedagogical methods, curriculum planning, classroom mgt & conflict sensitive education; support teacher learning cycles (TLCs) for continuous professional dvpt; facilitate community engagement in education through establishment/strengthening of PTAs & SMCs through training in roles and responsibilities, school development planning and awarding school improvement grants; conduct awareness raising community dialogue sessions to mobilize enrollment, promote attendance and support retention especially for girls who face multiple barriers to education including harmful and social practices such as forced early marriages and boys who also face protection risks that include child labour and forced recruitment into armed groups; conduct life skills training & support structured recreational activities for physical and psycho-social development; provide technical and material support non-teaching professionals (county education directors,  supervisors) to effectively conduct their school supervision and support duties; training of teachers, facilitators, on Mental Health and psycho-social support (MHPSS), Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), child protection, child safeguarding and PSEA; provide cash and vouchers assistance to the most vulnerable for examination registration. 
Key approaches that NRC will adopt in this project include integration, partnerships and community based programming.  NRC will collaborate local structures as well as with other clusters including protection, WASH, shelter, LFS, Nutrition and Health to deliver comprehensive package that addresses the holistic needs of targeted population. Furthermore, for durable solutions, NRC will work with local actors, parents and care-givers building their capacity for self reliance and also to increase coverage in hard to reach areas  with periodic access challenges and bureaucratic impediments. For effective and efficient use of resources and for learning purposes, NRC will continue to participate in coordination mechanisms at both the national and sub-national levels to avoid overlaps and duplication with other education players.

project_name: Protection et renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection des PDI au Niger.
Assistance en Abris et BNA pour les PDI dans la region du Niger.
project_objective:
Le Niger est entouré de pays touchés par des conflits qui ce sont propagés dans les région frontalières. L'insécurité croissante, due principalement aux attaques armées, au crime organisé et aux tensions ethniques, continue de poser le plus grand défi dans les zone frontalières  aux pays limitrophe tel que Mali et du Burkina Faso et le Nigeria.
Une augmentation de la présence militaire internationale est notable avec plusieurs opérations simultanées (Barkane, G5 Sahel et opérations militaires nigériennes) en cours, pour lutter contre le terrorisme et les attaques armées . Depuis fin 2017, l'insécurité dans les régions de Tillabery, Tahoua ,  Maradi et Diffa  entraîné pour la première fois des déplacements internes de population. Aujourd'hui, ces régions sont confrontées à des déplacements internes massifs avec plus de138 229 personnes contraintes de fuir, soit une augmentation globale de 50 % en 2020 dans cette région. Plus, de 40 000 personnes déplacées ont été signalées dans des zones proches de la frontière malienne. Compte tenu de la situation mixte à laquelle la région est actuellement confrontée, accueillant plus de x déplacés internes et y réfugiés et pour assurer l'équité dans l'assistance et renforcer la cohésion sociale et la coexistence pacifique dans les zones affectées par les conflits divers, ce projet vise à assister les personnes déplacées internes dans les régions de Tillabery, Tahoua, Maradi, Diffa, en leur fournissant une assistance en Abris et BNA. Ce projet touche environ 14 826 ménages et a pour objectif l'amélioration des conditions de vie des femmes, des hommes, des filles et des garçons déplacés dans les communautés touchées/affectées et assurer l'équité dans l'assistance ainsi que le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de la coexistence pacifique en vue de la situation mitigée à laquelle la région est confrontée . Pour la réponse hors camp pour les déplacés internes, le HCR assure le leadership de la réponse globale de protection.

project_objective: Suite aux effets du changement climatique , le Niger fait face de manière accentué à des irrégularités tant dans la pluviométrie que la crue des cours d'eau. Ce projet touche  environ 1603 menages et a pour  objectif  l'ameliorartion de conditions de vies des sinistrées .

project_name: Prevention, risk mitigation and multi-sectoral response to Gender Based Violence including Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: In line with the UNHCR GBV policy, the Inter-Agency minimum standards for GBV in emergency, the IASC guidelines, the GBV strategic objectives of the HRP as well as the “Call to Action” road map 2021-2025, the project is designed with the three areas of Prevention, Risk Mitigation and Response to address gender-based violence (GBV). The project aims at strengthening protection of women, men, boys and girls internally displaced and returnees including those with specific needs against exposure to risks of GBV and ensuring that all survivors have adequate and timely access to quality life savings services in Borno and Adamawa states. Importantly, through capacity building and sensitization, the project will address specific issues related to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) involving humanitarian workers, security actors and community leaders in camps and host communities. In its GBV programming, UNHCR is guided by the human rights based, survivor-centered, Age Gender and Diversity (AGD), child friendly, and community based approaches. As such, UNHCR ensures that affected communities, in particular women and girls from all ages, backgrounds and abilities, who are most affected by GBV and the best sources of information about risk factors, are consulted in programming. Year-round focus group discussions, key informant interviews, safety audits, participatory assessments, and reporting/feedback mechanisms are key means through which UNHCR ensures consultative and adapted GBV programming.

project_name: Protection Assistance to People of Concern in North East Nigeria Through the Provision of Shelters and NFI Assistance.
project_objective:
The Shelter and NFI assistance project will target IDPs and returnees in three BAY states; Borno, Adamawa and Yobe with provision of new emergency and transitional shelters, emergency shelter repairs, shelter kits and Non-food Items (NFIs) to contribute to the physical well-being and dignity of PoCs and as protection assistance aligned with Shelter/ NFI/ CCCM Sector strategic objectives for the HRP 2023. The project will also ensure holistic durable solutions approach led by the Government, mainly to enable local integration of IDPs in  Adamawa and Borno State, reintegration of refugee returnees and support to the host community in building resilience and ease the pressure on them.
Therefore in 2023, UNHCR shall build upon progress being made in 2022 in providing shelter and NFI support to respond to unmet needs in Adamawa (Fufore  Mubi South, Madagali, Michika, Yola South and Yola north); Borno (Bama, Banki, Damasak, Damboa, Dikwa, Jere, konduga, Gwoza, Pulka, Maiduguri, Mobbar, Monguno, Rann and Ngala) and Yobe State (Damaturu and Gujba,) through provision of; (1) 10,000 emergency shelters (2) 550 Durable/Transitional, (3) 4,000 shelter kits materials (4 ) 25,000 NFIs kits and (5) 15,000 emergency shelter repairs targeting IDPs and Returnees households both in formal and informal settlements, suffering from protracted displacement, natural disaster and those returning home. To assess and ascertain the level of beneficiary satisfaction with regards to Shelter and NFI support, UNHR plans to carry out 4 post construction/distribution monitoring.

project_name: Strengthening and provision of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services for conflict-affected populations in Syria
project_objective:
UNFPA will continue to reduce maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality; support the EPHS during the crisis, pandemics, and early recovery; provide FP commodities, and provide medical assistance and care to GBV survivors including CMR. In Syria, SRH service gaps remain; access to EmONC services are limited despite increased health needs, including among WRA. This will be achieved by 1) ensuring the availability of and access to integrated quality SRH services and information; 2) building health worker and CHW capacity; 3) increasing access to services in areas where no SRH services exist; 4) ensuring availability of essential medical, PPE, and supplies; 5) ensuring delivery of complementary comprehensive services, including for MHPSS and non-communicable diseases; and 6) strengthening referral mechanisms and improving national/subnational SRH coordination.

UNFPA will follow the Whole of Syria approach, implementing in all Syrian governorates from Damascus and cross-border from Türkiye. Vulnerable populations prioritized include women and girls of reproductive age, IDPs, host communities, returnees, adolescents, and PwDs. Through October 2022, UNFPA reached 845,845 people with SRH services through 97 PHCs, 19 EmONCs, and 99 mobile clinics in government-controlled areas and 118,418 people through 10 EmONC facilities in NWS.

Key 2023 objectives include:
Increasing access to lifesaving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable health services for the most vulnerable and in need persons.
Increasing access to primary healthcare by providing essential primary health services to cover reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health needs of vulnerable populations and repairing facilities. Improving access to secondary and tertiary healthcare for high risk pregnancy, malnourished PLW, EmONC cases, and complex cases which cannot access treatment in their area.
Supporting access in areas with service gaps through mobile teams and the community midwifery network in the most vulnerable rural areas.
Building the capacity of health workers and CHWs on SRH and GBV principles, outbreak IPC and treatment, referrals, and any technical gaps.
Supporting essential infrastructure maintenance, equipment repair and supply to health facilities, in particular for areas in acute need.
Strengthening and consolidating medical supply chains, ensuring availability of safe and quality medicines for essential primary and obstetric care, IPC supplies and PPE, infectious diseases including HIV to prevent mother-to-child transmission, and FP methods.
Pre-positioning emergency stocks of RH kits, medicines, and supplies in line with contingency scenarios for reduced access and increased hostilities.
Strengthening health sector coordination and HIS, emphasizing enhancing protection, increasing access to health services, and continuing coordination within and across hubs, including through joint contingency and preparedness planning.
Supporting continuity of care, strengthening community resilience, responding to IDP movements and shifts in control, and beneficiaries’ participation in programming.
Supporting resilience and early recovery through 2 midwifery schools in NWS and 2 in GOS/NES, and supporting the full implementation of DHIS2 in NWS and later at the national level.
Adapting, updating, and adopting national RH guidelines, including on CMR and Health and Nutrition of PLW in 2023, with the MoH, and developing training packages, subject for potential accreditation.
Continuous monitoring of implementation based on the five AAP principles and UNFPA’s global results-based monitoring framework. UNFPA or third party staff and IPs will conduct joint monthly supervision visits, subject to access/approval.
Standardized tools including the supported services and supervision checklist are used to assess service availability/quality. Clinic registration data will be collated monthly. Beneficiary feedback (complaints box, FGDs, exit interviews) will be collected.

project_name: Camp Coordination and Camp Management Support to IDPs in Northern Mozambique
project_objective: UNHCR will work through a Community-Based and Right-Based approach in Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) targeting 145,121 (52% women and 48% men) IDPs living in camps and camp-like settings. The project has four main components i.e. (i) Enhancing community participation, site level coordination and information management, (ii) Support site planning and site development, (iii) Capacity-development and (iv) Quick impact Projects (QiPs). UNHCR aims to build on the gains made in 2022 in fostering localization through partnership with the relevant local government departments, national NGOs and civil society to enhance meaningful community ownership and self-management of the IDP sites in the targeted districts. The CCCM projects will complement UNHCR’s Protection, Shelter and NFI programmes to provide a holistic intervention in the targeted locations. CCCM services will integrate centrality of protection, age, gender equality and diversity in programme planning and implementation through regular consultation (FGDs) with all community groups i.e., women, men, youth, PWDs and other most at-risk groups and involve the IDPs and host community in the project implementation.  UNHCR CCCM will target IDP sites that the local administration considers villages (also referred to as Aldaires or Relocation sites).  The Aldaires or Relocation sites are considered part of the local municipality plan and provides an opportunity for a local integration solution to IDPs.

project_name: MUPPETS - Multi-Purpose Emergency Transfers in Syria
project_objective:
15.3 million people in Syria are in need of humanitarian assistance (HNO 2023). This constitutes the highest number of people in need since the onset of hostilities in 2011 and is expected to even further increase. In a context of high inflation and rapidly increasing food, fuel and basic goods prices, HHs' income gaps and thus debt loads are increasing. As a response, the project aims to enhance the ability of vulnerable HHs affected by the crisis in government-held Syria to protect and sustain their lives. The action will provide assistance to 983 HHs across the governorates of Aleppo (Jabal Badro) and Rural Damascus (Jdidet Artouz, and Sahnaya). The targeted areas were identified based on the severity scale from the HNO 2023 and the need assessment conducted in December 2022. Furthermore, the accessibility of the implementing partner to the targeted areas was considered in order to monitor the activities during the project implementation. Basic Needs (BN) Assistance will be provided to cover the HHs' BN via Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) on a monthly basis over a period of 6 months. MPCA transfer values (440,00 SYP per month for a period of 6 month, totaling 2,640,000 SYP) are based on the recommendations of the Syria Cash Working Group (CWG). The amounts are considered preliminary and are based on updated price assessments and harmonization efforts of the CWG (last updated in Nov 2022). Prices for basic commodities have soared and the currency continues to lose value, while at the same time salaries have remained stagnant. Unconditional cash assistance is an effective modality that ensures beneficiaries can meet their BN and thus decrease engaging in negative coping mechanisms. Furthermore, a primary needs assessment conducted by Caritas Switzerland (CACH), and its partners indicated a strong preference for cash assistance. The assumption is as follows: (IF) unconditional, unrestricted cash assistance is provided to vulnerable communities (host, IDP, returnee) in Syria, (THEN) beneficiaries can meet their basic needs with dignity and freedom of choice, and thus avoid having to resort to negative coping strategies. 
The field teams continuously register HHs through outreach activities and home visits in the communities. Beneficiaries will also be registered through internal referrals from national partners (Caritas Syria, GOPA, JRS, etc) and external referrals from NGOs and UN agencies present in the areas of intervention. The implementing partner team will assess the vulnerability of registered beneficiaries through a BN scoring system which was developed by CACH and Caritas Syria in December 2017 and refined in 2019 and 2022 to reflect the changing context. Meanwhile, CACH and CS will ensure to avoid any duplication of assistance by other agencies by coordinating and cooperation with the humanitarian agencies working in the targeted areas.
All beneficiaries selected to receive BN assistance will also benefit from Winterization Assistance (WA) from other funded programming. This approach will ensure that the full package of assistance (BN +WA) is provided to the identified most vulnerable population. CACH will also work closely with other actors on the ground to ensure the standardization, harmonization, and coordination of the cash response in Syria. 
The implementation and its impact will be continuously monitored across the life cycle of the project. CACH and CS MEAL teams will conduct PDMs, Outcome Monitoring, FGDs, and market monitoring to ensure that the project is reaching its objective without any negative effects on the market. CACH and CS will ensure full abidance with the FCRM policies in place. This will allow beneficiaries to submit any feedback they deem necessary. This process also allows the partners to take in any lessons learned and readjust during the implementing period. All findings will be shared anonymously with the CWG to further support the humanitarian actors.

project_name: Integrated CP, GBV, PSS intervention to enhance resilience and improve access to services and rights with dignity
project_objective:
IMC will continue its current intervention at its community center in Jaramana and mobile team deployed in Yalda, Rural Damascus, WGSS in Beit Sahem and medical mobile teams in Damascus and Rural Damascus. IMC is planning to establish another community center in Beit Sahem. At its community centers and protection mobile team, IMC will provide the following CP-related activities: case management, non-formal education, skills development, social and recreational activities; inclusion program targeting children with disabilities and their parents; Speech therapy services will also be provided based on the specific needs of each child; parenting skills programs and peer to peer support groups; Youth Empowerment Program (YEP) for youth and adolescents;  IMC also plans to establish community-based committees to facilitate the identification of children at risks and/or survivors, raise awareness and discuss main CP concerns and solutions. Regarding GBV prevention and response programming, IMC will provide case management, psychosocial and referral services, and structured and non-structured activities to enhance awareness, prevention, and response to GBV concerns. Women and girls and the community overall are consulted to better understand the main risks and the existing community support systems. IMC WGSS offers the following activities, aimed at building resilience and fostering social interaction, reducing protection, and more specifically GBV risks and thus improving beneficiaries’ safety and well-being: PSS activities and basic life skills programs; Conflict resolution education, a new program targeting girls and focusing on understanding rights and identify solutions, applying different techniques. Health services are provided at the WGSS  to ensure access to safe and comprehensive services for GBV survivors, in line with a survivor-centered approach. Dignity kits will also be provided based on needs. Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) will be available for beneficiaries to address the immediate consequences of GBV incidents and protection risks. GBV Case managers will provide assistance through assessments of each specific case and established criteria. Additionally, IMC will provide Information and awareness sessions on CP and GBV-related topics, and capacity-building activities to community members and volunteers.
IMC protection intervention will also be linked with health and livelihoods activities, specifically: 1) GBV and CP case management services are provided in static and mobile health facilities; When dealing with CP cases, the case managers will focus on the needs of the child and his/her family, in consideration of the best interests of the child and building upon the child and his/her family resilience and ensuring the child’s meaningful participation and family empowerment throughout the process. 2) Vocational training courses and related start-up kits will be provided to selected beneficiaries, at risk or survivors of CP and GBV, with the aim of reducing protection risks and increasing wellbeing. project_objective: The specific objective is to provide inclusive, safe, and dignified access to immediate food, WASH, and protection assistance and to strengthen community resilience in at least 20 communities in hard-to-reach areas of Kaga and Magumeri LGAs in Borno state. The intervention will focus on providing direct access to integrated multi-sectoral, context-adapted assistance, which will cover the most urgent humanitarian needs of the most vulnerable people and communities. The action will include humanitarian protection, food assistance through cash, access to water for domestic use, improved sanitation and hygiene, protection monitoring, community-based protection activities, as well as referrals. The villages to be covered have been selected in coordination with local authorities and humanitarian clusters to ensure reaching into areas with high needs that have largely been deprived of humanitarian assistance.

project_name: Provision of vital common communication services in North-East Nigeria
project_objective: The ETS will provide humanitarians across Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states with reliable communications services to enable an eﬃcient and safer response, ultimately saving more lives. ETS services allow humanitarians to implement eﬃciently their activities and carry out their jobs safely in areas where services from local services providers are unstable or non-operational. In addition, the ETS will continue to build the capacity of local partners, will map the communication needs of the affected population in North-East Nigeria and evaluate the possibility of implementing a pilot project to address identified needs for communities.

project_name: Livelihoods support in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
WFP will provide early recovery and resilience to shocks will be promoted through asset creation and preservation and, increased livelihoods  Joint multi-sectoral assessments and Emergency Food Security Analysis will be conducted regularly to monitor the nutrition, food security, and market situation in crisis-affected states.
A gender-transformative approach that reflects the needs of women, men, girls, and boys will be adopted. WFP will mainstream protection throughout its work, supported by a solid understanding of the operational context and protection analysis. Training and capacity building of staff and partners in the protection and humanitarian principles will include on-the-job coaching. WFP will ensure that affected populations (women and men) will be consulted throughout the programme cycle. Beneficiary feedback mechanisms will be tailored to their preferred means of communication. Beneficiaries will continue to be empowered with knowledge on their food assistance entitlements and their rights, including WFP’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be embedded in M&E tools, complaint feedback mechanisms, and training of partners and staff.
WFP will continue the collection of key information on beneficiaries and assistance provided as part of its M&E activities. Monthly monitoring will include distribution and activity site management; beneficiary and entitlement verification; and ensuring adequate protection and gender measures. Lessons will be regularly drawn from monthly process and biannual outcome monitoring and reporting, and periodic reviews and evaluation to inform strategic and operational decisions.
WFP will further consolidate partnerships to enhance national and state-level emergency preparedness and response systems, including food security and nutrition assessment and monitoring, early warning, protection, gender analysis, targeting, and registration processes, safety nets, cash-based transfer capacities, and supply chain.
Where security and access to land allow, WFP plans to increase livelihood activities to support access to productive assets, income-generating activities, and self-reliance in the long term. Assistance will be coordinated with the local government, to ensure food assistance is complementary and fills gaps.

project_name: Integrated Emergency, Recovery and Resilience Response for Crisis-affected Persons in MMC and Jere
project_objective: The aim of this intervention is: conflict-affected communities in MMC and Jere LGAs are sustainably protected from, and treated for, the main causes of morbidity and mortality; supported to meet immediate and long-term Shelter and Settlement, WASH and Protection needs, while being protected and provided with the legal assistance they need. To achieve this, the proposed project will be implemented by a consortium led by the International Rescue Committee (IRC), in partnership with the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). The consortium will leverage the expertise of each partner to deliver a multi-sectoral, area-based response, providing integrated services across the following sectors: Health, WASH, Nutrition, Food Assistance, Multi-purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), Nutrition, Economic Recovery and Market Systems (ERMS), Protection and Shelter and Settlements. The consortium aims to meet the most immediate and life-saving needs of IDPs, host communities and returnees in MMC and Jere, which will translate into reduced mortality and improved living conditions. The consortium will also address the ongoing, protracted needs, and supporting early recovery through capacity-building, the strengthening of existing health systems and community-based structures, and increasing the ownership of life-saving, life-sustaining, and life-building services by local authorities, service providers, and local communities to ensure sustainability. In order to build the resilience of individuals and communities, the unique humanitarian and development challenges in MMC and Jere LGAs (presence of service delivery actors against an ongoing flux of IDPs in and out of camps and host communities throughout the city) must be addressed simultaneously by increasing access to quality, sustainable basic services, building sustainable livelihoods, and strengthening local systems and structures.

project_name: Integrated Emergency Response for Crisis-Affected Persons in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: The protracted insurgency-fueled humanitarian situation in the Northeast region of Nigeria remains grim, unpredictable, and underserved. The ongoing conflict is now entering its thirteenth year, and the increase in violent attacks witnessed over the past year has resulted in further deterioration of the security situation, mass displacement of people and a deepening of humanitarian needs. 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) estimated a total of 8.4 million people in need of humanitarian assistance and protection . Out of the 2,171,652 persons displaced across the three North-Eastern BAY states, Borno state, with a population of 4.2 million people is considered the epicenter of the crisis with around 1.6 million Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) . The results of the IOM Round 41 of Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments showed a total of 2,197,824 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) were identified in 452,219 households in BAY states, a 1% increase (26,172 individuals) compared to Round 40 when 2,171,652 IDPs were recorded in March 2022 . With the closure of most IDP camps in Maiduguri, Borno state capital, the decrease of IDPs in M.M.C. was reflected in increasing IDP numbers in the Mongonu, Gwoza, Jere, Ngala, Konduga and other LGAs, further straining limited resources. For instance, DTM 41 showed Mongonu hosts 152,485 IDPs, which is a 2% increase (2,301 individuals) compared to 114,595 IDPs in Round 40 DTM. Acute malnutrition is widespread across Borno sate, and the surrounding areas. Within Borno state, the LGAs in IPC Acute Malnutrition Classification Phase 4 (Critical), include Bama, Dikwa, Gubio, Guzamala, Gwoza, Killable, Kaga, Magumeri, Monguno, Ngala and Nganzai, while LGAs in IPC Phase 3 (Serious) include Maiduguri, Jere, Marte, Mafa, Konduga, Damboa, Mobbar and Bayo. The main contributing factors to acute malnutrition include poor food consumption (quantity and quality) and poor health seeking behaviors. Additionally, poor health services, feeding practices, access to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services and facilities, and food insecurity play a role. According to the Nutrition and Food Security Surveillance (NFSS) round 12 SMART survey prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) was high in Borno (12.3%) while the prevalence of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) was 1.9% in Borno. By domain, prevalence of GAM was highest in Northern Borno (16.5%), followed by East Borno (15.2%). Prevalence was higher among boys than girls in all domains. Prevalence of GAM is highest among children in the younger age cohorts 6-17 and 18-29 months. Through Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition in Emergencies strategy and Management of Acute Malnutrition, IRC will deliver an integrated package of community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) services at 65 Nutrition sites across BAY states, as well as 7 stabilization centers. The selected communities have been impacted by the recent IDPs resettlement and camps closure which saw large populations settle in these areas. This resulted in high malnutrition rates in the region, especially with new arrivals from liberalized areas who are accommodated in transit camps. Services provided in these locations will include outpatient therapeutic program services (OTP), targeted supplementary feeding program (TSFP) services, Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) Corners, provision of micro-nutrient powder (MNP), and sensitization, counselling, nutrition best practices messaging, and follow-up provided by mother-to-mother support groups (MtMSGs) and Men-to-men committees (MtMCs). Children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications will be referred for inpatient care at the nearest stabilization centers, with emergency ambulance services readily available. IRC will also strengthen services at government facilities by building capacity of staff supporting the program and supporting with essential supplies including nutrition commodities

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency Health and Nutrition Services for Internally Displaced Persons and Host Communities in the Northwest Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
Since October 2016, the political conflict and security crisis in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon has led to the displacement of more than 705,000 people internally and over 61,000 people to Nigeria. Conflict related displacement and violence have led to the deterioration of basic services in the North West Region coupled with rising protection, health and nutrition needs among the affected population. In response to this crisis, International Medical Corps proposes to support the Ministry of Health (MoH) in providing integrated health (including mental health) and nutrition services for IDPs as well as host communities affected by conflict in the Mbengwi and Njikwa Health districts.  
In response to the ongoing crisis in Cameroon since 2016, International Medical Corps through Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance (BHA) funding, has been supporting the Ministry of Health (MoH) to provide integrated health including mental health and nutrition services for IDPs as well as host communities affected by conflict in the Mbengwi and Njikwa health districts. This has permitted the provision of health and nutrition services to over 30,000 IDPs and host population members, relieving suffering and preventing maternal and neonatal deaths.  
IMC’s intervention has supported the collapsed health system to meet the needs of IDPs and host populations in Mbengwi and Njikwa since 2021. IMC proposes to continue providing health and nutrition services where there is a growing need for assistance and increasing concerns surrounding the health and nutritional status of both IDPs and host communities. Building on its existing program, IMC proposes to assist an additional 38,328 beneficiaries, expanding into two additional districts of Fudong and Akoh in the health areas of Konene and Akwaja. These areas host a large number of the IDPs in the region, with 8,437 and 5,000 respectively. IMC will also continue to support the four health facilities covered under the current award including Oshie Medicalized health center, the Konda integrated health center (IHC), the Njah-Etu IHC and the Bome IHC.

project_name: Strengthening maternal and infant and young child nutrition in thr refugee camp of Minawao in the Far North Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The project aims to educate the population in best practices related to maternal and child nutrition, birth registrations, routine vaccination of pregnant women and children less than 5 years, and ideal WASH practices. From which it will address the problems of maternal malnutrition by providing iron and folic acid and deworming services and awareness raising in exclusive breastfeeding, complementary feeding practices and WASH will be addressed to reduce malnutrition in Minowa camp. 
Through antenatal consultations (ANCs) and community interactions, pregnant women will be screened for malnutrition and nutrition counselling provided to those in need. Micronutrient powders (MNPs) will be provided for children to diversify their food diet.  Screening of children 6-59 months old will aid in detecting the deterioration of children’s nutritional status where bespoke interventions will be provided to reduce severe malnourishment and limit the possibilities of medical complications. The malnutrition preventive activities will be carried out at both the supported Integrated health facilities (HF) and the community level at the Minowa camp. 
At the health facilities, antenatal consultations will be delivered to screen pregnant women for malnutrition using MUAC tapes and identifying oedema. Follow-up of acutely malnutrition women via counselling will help to optimise their nutrition and better their WASH practices. Iron and folic acid tablets will be provided to all women attending ANCs and pregnant women will be dewormed. During post-natal consultations there will be continuous provision of iron and folic acid up to 6 months after childbirth to prevent nutrient deficiencies in infants and children. During ANC/PNC women will receive education on maternal, infant and child nutrition, optimum IYCF practices, WASH, procedures of birth registration, importance of vaccination and nutritional demonstrations. CHWs will be present at the HF to train on key messages from the health personnel. 
At community level malnutrition prevention interventions will be carried out by CHWs, health promoters, key community actors like IYCF support groups, husband school members who are model husband working towards the amelioration of maternal and child health by educating other men. This network of community actors will provide social, and behaviour change communications for the adoption of health habits concerning maternal, infant and child nutrition as well as basic WASH practices. Nutritional demonstrations including cooking demonstrations will be led by health promoters and CHWs to teach the population on how to complement young children and equally how to adjust diets of pregnant and lactating women.  Trained CHWs will distribute MNPs bimonthly via household of each eligible child 6-23 months and provide key messages on the use of MNPs. Home visits will be organised for the follow-up of children receiving the MNPs. Routine monthly screenings for malnutrition in children aged 6-59 months will be carried out for a close follow-up of the nutritional status of beneficiaries. 
In close collaboration with Health promoters and CHWs IMC UK will work to implement activities such as: nutrition screening, active case finding of defaulters and absentees in the community, referrals to the appropriate nutrition programs at the health centres and informing the community about malnutrition. 
Children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications will be referred to the stabilization centres (SCs) at the district hospital or a CMA (Medical centre of the municipality).

project_name: Protection assistance for conflict affected population in the North West and South West of Cameroon
project_objective: The humanitarian crisis in the Southwest region of Cameroon has exposed the local population to large scale protection risks and human rights violations and impacted vulnerable households’ capacity to meet their emergency food needs. Through this Action, the IRC seeks to improve the protection status of vulnerable people affected by the crisis in North West and South West Cameroon, assisting the most vulnerable people to stay safe, access assistance, recover from violence and claim their rights. The IRC will do this through an integrated program of Protection prevention and response activities to mitigate further protection risks resulting from the use of negative coping mechanisms.

project_name: Protective and adaptive Education Approaches for Children in Emergencies (PEACE)
project_objective:
In recognition that conflict-affected primary school-aged children in Nigeria, Niger, and Cameroon face major challenges to accessing quality education and protection services, IRC Deutschland proposes to partner with ECHO under the Pilot Programmatic Partnership to deliver the 3-year PEACE project. PEACE takes an integrated and adaptive approach to education and child protection, to support 171,065 school-aged boys and girls, their carers and educators, most affected by crisis across target countries to access and learn in safe educational environments. The PEACE evidence-based approach towards improving educational access, quality, and safety builds on previous IRC programming and includes: 
1.	Four core models to expand access to formal and non-formal education that is conflict-sensitive and designed to support children who are most in need;
2.	Support to caregivers and communities so that they may more fully ensure girls’ and boys’ safety, access, and learning; and 
3.	Capacity building of teachers and facilitators in order to improve the quality of instruction and provide safe learning environments for children. 
Child protection measures are integrated throughout PEACE, from individual case management support to individual and group psycho-social support activities for caregivers and children. 
In light of the COVID 19 pandemic, PEACE will adapt programming to ensure the continuity of child protection and learning support in safe environments, as well as COVID-19-specific messaging related to health and or WASH.

project_name: Amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages affectés par la crise humanitaire dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoum et du Sahel au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
En lien avec son positionnement urgentiste dans le secteur EHA et sa participation aux mécanismes RRM de réponse rapide aux mouvements de population, Solidarités International souhaite proposer une réponse en Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d’Existence pour les communautés affectées par le conflit et intègre aussi une assistance alimentaire saisonnière pour couvrir les besoins de base à la période de soudure 2020. Ces activités d'urgence sont complétées par des appuis dans le cadre du relèvement précoce au travers l'appui à l'agriculture, l'élevage et le développement d'AGR. L’objectif de ce projet est de réduire l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle en : 
-	Assurant une réponse en terme d’assistance alimentaire (RRM et Soudure) auprès des populations les plus vulnérables et déplacées affectées par la crise
- Assurant une complémentation nutritionnelle avec des distributions de farines nutritionnelles en faveur des enfants de 6-23 mois et des FEFA;
-	Développant des activités d'appui au moyens d'existence dans le cadre du relèvement précoce. 
Le projet vise à terme de toucher 13 966 ménages (très pauvres des communautés hôtes et ménages déplacés), soit  97 762 individus.

project_name: Réponse d'urgence intégrée en Santé, Nutrition, EHA et Protection en faveur des populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans les régions du Sahel, de l’Est et de la Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à apporter une réponse en santé intégrée pour les personnes déplacées et populations hôtes vulnérables dans les régions de l’Est, du Sahel et de la Boucle du Mouhoun, et a pour objectif spécifique d’améliorer l’accès de qualité aux soins de santé (primaire et secondaire), à la sécurité nutritionnelle, à l’eau et aux conditions d’hygiène et contribuer à la réduction de l’impact psychosocial des personnes vulnérables touchées par la crise. 

A travers ce projet, PUI continuera l’approche initiée par PUI depuis le début de ses activités dans le domaine de la santé avec : 
- Un volet de renforcement et d’appui au système de santé tant au niveau primaire que secondaire de manière à maintenir un continuum des soins dans les structures appuyées. 
- Un volet de réponse d’urgence pour faire face aux chocs de plus en plus nombreux en lien avec la dégradation continue de la situation. 

Du point de vue du positionnement géographique, PUI souhaite maintenir ses activités dans les localités sous blocus de Sebba et Solhan, en lien avec la pertinence du soutien au système de santé face à dégradation de la situation nutritionnelle, et maintenir une capacité de réponse rapide dans les provinces du Yagha et du Seno. 

Dans la région de l’Est, PUI souhaite maintenir un appui aux structures dans le DS Bogandé et de Gayéri, que ce soit au niveau CSPS que CMA/CREN afin de répondre aux besoins d’accès des populations aux soins de santé et appuyer ces deux districts dans la réponse face à la dégradation de la situation nutritionnelle, tout en maintenant une capacité de réponse rapide sur l’ensemble de la région de l’Est. 

Enfin, faisant suite à la dégradation de la situation dans la Boucle du Mouhoun, et suite aux évaluations menées au début du mois de novembre 2022, PUI souhaite développer un soutien aux DS de Boromo un des 2 DS le plus affecté par la problématique de déplacement des populations, avec une augmentation de 61% du nombres PDI enregistrés la province du Balé (données issues des rapports sur la situation des PDI au 31 décembre 2021 et d’octobre 2022 par le CONASUR) 
L’évaluation fait ressortir des besoins en terme de personnels qualifiés, de couverture des soins et d’accès aux services de santé de manière générale, avec une absence de partenaires dans le domaine de la Santé. Ce positionnement permettra également d’anticiper une dégradation de la situation dans cette zone tout en repositionnant des capacités de réponses rapide en cas de besoin.

A noter que cette approche s’intègre dans une réponse régionale PUI incluant le Niger avec une stratégie commune déclinée en fonction des spécificités de chaque contexte.

Lors de la mise en place du projet, PUI se coordonnera avec les différents acteurs présents, afin de permettre un ciblage plus précis des zones, d'éviter les doublons et de rester le plus efficient possible. 
A noter que PUI met au cœur de ses projets la lutte contre les EAS, la prise en compte du genre, la protection transversale. PUI s’inscrit également dans un processus d’amélioration continu de la qualité de ses actions via une meilleure prise en compte des parties prenantes dans le cycle de projet. A ce titre, le système de Suivi-Evaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (SERA) existant sera renforcé dans le cadre de cette intervention. La prise en compte des questions de redevabilité s’appuiera sur trois principaux piliers dont l’information, la participation et la consolidation du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes et retours d’informations.

project_name: Réponse intégrée en santé et nutrition dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun
project_objective:
Faisant suite à la dégradation de la situation dans la Boucle du Mouhoun, et suite aux évaluations menées au début du mois de novembre 2022, PUI souhaite développer un soutien aux DS de Boromo un des 2 DS le plus affecté par la problématique de déplacement des populations, avec une augmentation de 61% du nombres PDI enregistrés la province du Balé (données issues des rapports sur la situation des PDI au 31 décembre 2021 et d’octobre 2022 par le CONASUR) 
L’évaluation fait ressortir des besoins en terme de personnels qualifiés, de couverture des soins et d’accès aux services de santé de manière générale, avec une absence de partenaires dans le domaine de la Santé. Ce positionnement permettra également d’anticiper une dégradation de la situation dans cette zone tout en repositionnant des capacités de réponses rapide en cas de besoin.

Au cours de ce projet, PUI contribuera à améliorer l'accès effectif aux services essentiels et vitaux de santé, de nutrition et de protection dans les situations d'urgence pour les populations touchées par les crises sécuritaires et humanitaires dans le domaine de la santé dans les situations d'urgence pour les populations touchées par la crise sécuritaire et humanitaire dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun

Lors de la mise en place du projet, PUI se coordonnera avec les différents acteurs présents, afin de permettre un ciblage plus précis des zones, d'éviter les doublons et de rester le plus efficient possible. 
A noter que PUI met au cœur de ses projets la lutte contre les EAS, la prise en compte du genre, la protection transversale. 
PUI s’inscrit dans un processus d’amélioration continu de la qualité de ses actions via une meilleure prise en compte des parties prenantes dans le cycle de projet. A ce titre, le système de Suivi-Evaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (SERA) existant sera renforcé dans le cadre de cette intervention. La prise en compte des questions de redevabilité s’appuiera sur trois principaux piliers dont l’information, la participation et la consolidation du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes et retours d’informations.

Il est à noter que le transfert monétaire n'est pas prévu sur ce projet de par la nature des activités en santé, nutrition, wash in nut / wash in health

project_name: Projet d’assistance en santé, nutrition, EHA et Sécurité alimentaire aux populations issues des zones isolées de système des soins dans un contexte d’insécurité dans les régions de l’Est et du Sahel.
project_objective:
Le projet aura lieu dans les régions de l’Est et du Sahel. Il sera mise en œuvre par les ONGI Première Urgence Internationale (à l’Est et au Sahel) et Solidarités Internationale (au Sahel)
Il contribuera au rétablissement et au renforcement de l'accès de qualité à des services de base en santé, nutrition, EHA et à la sécurité alimentaire des personnes vulnérables touchées par la crise dans les régions de l'Est et du Sahel (provinces du Seno et du Yagha).
Le projet ciblera essentiellement les groupes des populations en situation de vulnérabilité extrême. Notamment ;
-	les personnes affectées par des chocs (mouvements de populations, conflits, crises sanitaires et/ou nutritionnelles) 
-	les populations vivant dans les zones enclavées coupées de tout accès au système de soins (aires de santé où les formations sanitaires sont fermées),
-	les personnes en phase IPC 4 et IPC 5 vivant dans des zones enclavées

La stratégie du projet comprend deux principaux axes d’intervention ;
·	Une réponse intégrée aux besoins sanitaires, nutritionnels, alimentaires et en EHA en faveur des populations vivant dans des zones enclavées, essentiellement des zones avec formations sanitaires fermées.
·	Une réponse d’urgence, dans les zones couvertes par l’action et au-delà, aux besoins humanitaires apparaissant suite à de nouveaux chocs, tels que des déplacements de population (PUI) mais également des chocs non couverts par le RRM, en particulier les situations de crise sanitaire et/ou nutritionnelle et/ou alimentaire (PUI et SI), si ces besoins ne sont pas couverts par d’autres acteurs de la réponse d’urgence

Lors de la mise en place du projet, PUI se coordonnera avec les différents acteurs présents, afin de permettre un ciblage plus précis des zones, d'éviter les doublons et de rester le plus efficient possible. 
A noter que PUI met au cœur de ses projets la lutte contre les EAS, la prise en compte du genre, la protection transversale. 
PUI s’inscrit dans un processus d’amélioration continu de la qualité de ses actions via une meilleure prise en compte des parties prenantes dans le cycle de projet. A ce titre, le système de Suivi-Evaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (SERA) existant sera renforcé dans le cadre de cette intervention. project_name: Improving Access to Quality Education for affected Children in the Northern Mozambique
project_objective: The project will contribute to providing access to quality inclusive education in Chiure and Montepuez districts, Cabo Delgado province, for displaced girls and boys, targeting 15,000 IDPs, through activities involving parents and guardians, school coincils, teachers and the community.

project_name: Safe access to the emergency WASH services to the affected  female, male, girls and boys  in Yobe and Borno state
project_objective: The proposed WASH project for 2023 will contribute to the achievement of HRP 2023 objectives through triple nexus approach.  The Project will be achieved by increasing access and sustainable use of gender sensitive and safe emergency WASH services such as water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion sessions, ensuring that conflict affected populations receive immediate and sufficient assistance according to their needs. The project will respond to WASH needs in IDP camps and communities as well as in health facilities and schools. It will ensure free and equitable access to safe drinking water and latrine in secure places, enhance their knowledge on WASH practices, prevent the spread of COVID 19, reduce prevalence of diarrhea and ultimately also lead towards improved nutrition security. This will be achieved through a combination of interventions such as construction/rehabilitation of WASH facilities, Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), Social behavioral change (SBC), formation and training of gender balance WASHCOMs with 40-50% female and building capacity of government authorities to effectively provide lifesaving assistance and have improved capacity to meet the immediate needs of newly displaced or returning populations. Throughout the course of the project, the active participation of the stakeholders and affected persons including women and marginalize group in the design and implementation to ensure the sustainability of the interventions while protection needs of women and girls will be identified and integrated into programming.

project_name: Humanitarian Support to the Vulnerable Communities of Ngala and Gwoza in Mitigating Explosive Ordnance Threat Through Risk Education and Non-Technical Survey
project_objective:
The purpose of the project is to contribute to protection of civilians from the threat of explosive ordnance in Ngala and Gwoza LGAs of Borno State in northeast Nigeria. 
In line with UNMAS Nigeria’s Programme Strategy, the project contributes to a vision of national authorities protecting civilians from the threat of EO in north-east Nigeria and the programme’s mission is to support national capacities active within the Mine Action sector, including the security sector and civil society. The implementation of this project advances two key outcomes: (1) relevant national and local entities mitigate the explosive threat in north-east Nigeria, based on an accurate understanding of the scale and scope of EO contamination, and (2) the immediate threat posed by explosive ordnance to civilians and humanitarian and development actors is mitigated.
To advance the above-stated outcomes, UNMAS will deploy specialist staff to Gwoza and Ngala LGAs to train and equip select members of the Community Stabilization Committee and the Community Security Group, community groups established by UNDP/ Grassroot Initiative For Strengthening Community Resilience (GISCOR) as explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) facilitators. If appropriate, additional community members who have already established trust with, and have access to people affected by the presence of EO will be trained and equipped. 
Following training, UNMAS will provide mentoring, further supporting the newly trained EORE facilitators. As experienced EORE facilitators themselves, UNMAS staff will provide hands-on guidance and advice during the first EORE sessions carried out by the newly trained facilitators. As such, they will fulfill quality assurance (QA) through real-time feedback post-EORE sessions, which will foster an environment of continuous learning and improvement, as well as enabling monitoring and evaluation of the impact and effectiveness.
UNMAS Nigeria will also work with LGA-based National Security and Civil Defense Corps (NSCDC) staff that were previously trained by UNMAS in Non-Technical Survey to establish a community-endorsed reporting chain. The approach is intended to encourage civilians to report on EO and suspected hazardous areas (SHA) and is aligned with the Information Management System for Mine Action (IMSMA), allowing for accurate data collection on EO or SHA reported by the population, following EORE sessions. The IMSMA reports will then be made available to, and coordinated with the UNMAS-trained Nigerian Police Force Explosive Ordnance Disposal (NPFEOD) teams stationed in the LGA, or when they deploy to the LGA to clear the explosive hazard.

To advance the above-stated outcomes, UNMAS will deploy specialist staff to Gwoza and Ngala LGAs to train and equip select members of the Community Stabilization Committee and the Community Security Group, community groups established by UNDP/ Grassroot Initiative For Strengthening Community Resilience (GISCOR) as explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) facilitators. If appropriate, additional community members who have already established trust with, and have access to people affected by the presence of EO will be trained and equipped. UNMAS will provide mentoring for the newly trained EORE facilitators. 
Project target is 3,060 beneficiaries.

project_name: Protection of rights and durable solution: ability to exercise and enjoy legal identity for population affected by displacement in Far North region of Cameroon
project_objective:
This project is aimed at improving access to Legal Identity rights for crisis-affected populations (returnees, displaced persons, refugees and host communities) in Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga and Logone-et-Chari divisions in the Far North region of Cameroon. 
NRC will assist beneficiaries to access civil and legal documentation through the provision of information, counselling and legal assistance. NRC will use mobile teams to ensure that beneficiaries in hard-to-reach areas can have access to LI services. Sensitization sessions will be organized and enhanced through a combination of mass media, and community-based approaches to deliver culturally adapted messages on legal and civil documentation to affected populations.
One of the main target groups for these services will be children along with their parents who need birth certificates to sit for public exams, as well as people affected by displacement who face obstacles to access civil and identity documents to enjoy freedom of movement and access to other rights and services.
In addition to improving awareness on LI and especially on the procedures for accessing documentation, NRC’s ICLA teams will provide legal assistance to beneficiaries regarding the judicial and administrative processes of late registration of births. NRC will also address financial barriers impeding vulnerable populations from accessing civil and identity documentation by covering the cost of the establishment of birth certificates through indirect registration. Moreover, ICLA will advocate for a reduction in the fee imposed by judicial authorities for late registration of births as well as for the medical certificate required for late registration. NRC will join forces with other humanitarian actors within the regional and national civil documentation platforms to advocate for the revision of national laws and procedures on legal identify and registration of civil status events. 
In order to improve the quality of services including the issuance of documentation void of errors, NRC will strengthen the capacities of civil status structures (courts, civil status centres, health personnel, etc.), local authorities and humanitarian actors on the legal framework and procedures for the registration of civil status events. NRC and BUNEC will facilitate the workshops and together with officials from MINDEVEL, the team will carry- out joint supervision to civil status centres to ensure proper use of knowledge and provision of quality and timely services to beneficiaries.
The project will therefore increase access to civil documentation and protection for vulnerable populations including freedom of movement, and access to basic services, including but not limited to education.

project_name: Rapid Response Mechanism 2023
project_objective:
La crise du bassin du Lac Tchad, les aléas climatiques ainsi que les épidémies continuent à provoquer des conséquences désastreuses pour les populations résidentes.
Pour permettre aux acteurs humanitaires de répondre efficacement aux besoins immédiats des populations déplacées au Cameroun, le consortium PUI/ACF propose de continuer ses efforts de veille humanitaire (en zones rurales comme en zones urbaines), évaluation et coordination avec les acteurs humanitaires et de réponse multisectorielle à travers le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM).
En se basant sur les résultats de l’évaluation externe conduite en octobre 2022 et du compte rendu de l’Atelier Externe de décembre 2022, il s’agira d’:
Améliorer la qualité des données collectées au niveau des Evaluations Multi-Sectorielles (EMS) à travers une collaboration renforcée avec les sectoriels, ainsi qu’un appui au reporting interne par l’ONG IMPACT
Maintenir et renforcer le système de veille et d’alerte sur les mouvements de populations grâce à une collaboration renforcée avec l’IOM et les autres acteurs présents sur ce créneau
Faire systématiquement un dépistage de la malnutrition aigüe des enfants de moins de 5 ans dès les EMS avec référencement immédiat des cas de MAS détectés. 
Apporter une réponse de premier recours en Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME), Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), inclus articles pour l’Hygiène Intime, et Sécurité Alimentaire tout en s’appuyant sur les capacités des autres acteurs humanitaires hors RRM à travers un mapping actualisé 
Recourir à la modalité Transfert Monétaire (TM)
 pour les réponses SECAL, AME et kit d’hygiène intime lorsque les conditions d’accès / disponibilité/ accessibilité des marchés et de sécurité le permettront.
Développer le Principe du Ne pas Nuire et les actions de Protection transversale à travers la signature et le suivi des MoU signés avec les partenaires
Améliorer le mécanisme de remontée des avis et plaintes
Poursuivre le   renforcement des capacités et l’appui structurant à une OSC (CADEPI) sur les aspects clés du Mécanisme et identifier de nouvelles OSC, particulièrement dans le Logone Chari.
Poursuivre les efforts visant à une coordination de la réponse performante (matrice de suivi des recommandations des EMS, interface géoportail amélioré grâce à un appui régulier de l’ONG IMMAP.
ASSISTANCE
En ce qui concerne l'assistance, notons que l'accent est mis sur le respect des standard minimum émis par les différents secteurs.

POLITIQUE PEAS.
L’exploitation et l’abus sexuels constituent un échec catastrophique pour ce qui est de la protection. Ils sont préjudiciables à ceux que les organisations humanitaires et leurs partenaires ont le mandat de protéger et compromettent la réputation de ces organisations. Ils violent également les normes et standards juridiques internationaux universellement reconnus. Des allégations d’exploitation et d’abus sexuels généralisés concernant les femmes et enfants réfugiés et déplacés par les travailleurs humanitaires et leurs partenaires ont poussé les organisations humanitaires à mettre sur pied des politiques strictes en matière de PEAS. Celle de PUI  qui date de plus de 12 ans condamne fermement toute violation  de cette politique par l’un de ses staffs, prestataire, partenaire ou fournisseur. Cette politique conforte la bonne  tenue et le bon suivi  du système de collecte et  remontée de plaintes. Cette politique est une des politiques pour laquelle PUI mettra  des mesures coercitives en cas de son non respect.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire pour les populations déplacées, réfugiées et hôtes affectées par la crise sécuritaire et les chocs climatiques dans l'Extrême Nord
project_objective: En tant qu’acteur humanitaire de première ligne dans le Nord du Logone-et-Chari et les communes frontalières du Mayo Tsanaga, qui restent parmi les zones les moins couvertes par les acteurs humanitaires, Solidarités International entend continuer à couvrir les besoins alimentaires des populations vulnérables (en ligne avec le phasage du Cadre Harmonisé) pendant la période de soudure 2023.
