project_name: Respuesta en salud para el acceso de servicios de atención a poblaciones vulnerables de seis departamentos del país.
project_objective:
En noviembre de 2020, la República de Honduras fue impactada directamente por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, que ocasionaron daños de diversa magnitud e importancia en 16 de los 18 departamentos del país, afectando alrededor de 4 700 000 de personas, obligando a la evacuación de 363 762 personas, y el alojamiento en albergues de 172 798 personas, con un recuento final de 99 personas fallecidas. El Valle de Sula, en el departamento de Cortés, localizado al norte del país, fue la zona del país más afectada, junto con los departamentos de Atlántida, Colón, Gracias a Dios, El Paraíso, Santa Bárbara y Yoro. De forma simultánea, el país también ha sido afectado por la pandemia de la COVID-19 y por la epidemia de dengue. De acuerdo con el análisis de daños y necesidades del sector salud posterior al impacto de las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota, del total de personas afectadas, 500 000 personas, aproximadamente, tenían acceso limitado o carecían de servicios de salud, debido a los daños a la infraestructura de la red de servicios de salud. Más de 393 establecimientos de salud fueron afectados y al menos 10 reportaron pérdidas totales en el equipamiento de la cadena de frío, equipamientos, insumos y vacunas.
En 2021, persistieron las personas con necesidades en salud, en particular en regiones postergadas e impactadas por las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota. En 2022, la Secretaría de Estado en los Despachos de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales (COPECO), emitió reiteradas alertas de distinto alcance, por el ingreso de ondas tropicales y sistemas de baja presión que afectaron los 18 departamentos del país, en particular, los más vulnerables a inundaciones por las crecidas de los ríos Chamelecón y Ulúa, localizados en el Norte del país, como son: Atlántida, Cortés, Santa Bárbara y Yoro. Estos fenómenos meteorológicos recurrentes ocasionaron incremento de la humedad del suelo, con saturaciones superiores al 90 % en algunos sectores del país, inundaciones urbanas y crecida de los niveles de los ríos con desbordamientos en las partes bajas de las cuencas y zonas aledañas, deslizamientos, dejando poblaciones afectadas, junto con daños a viviendas, calles, carreteras, puentes, postes de energía, infraestructura pública, sistemas de agua y saneamiento, además de pérdidas de cultivos. Al 3 de octubre de 2022, el Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN) de COPECO reportó 80 249 personas afectadas, 16 369 evacuadas, 1975 incomunicadas, 746 comunidades afectadas, 153 albergues habilitados, 9418 personas albergadas, 15 heridos, 15 fallecidos, por las ondas tropicales y sistemas de baja presión registrados en el país desde el 17 de agosto de 2022. En 2022, el país también fue afectado por la tormenta tropical Julia. De acuerdo con datos de COPECO, al 12 de octubre de 2022, se reportaron 148 157 personas afectadas, 4046 evacuadas, 217 comunidades afectadas, 300 viviendas destruidas, 76 carreteras dañadas, además 7 puentes dañados, Asimismo, se habilitaron 140 albergues en 10 departamentos, 2992 familias fueron albergadas (11 546 personas). También, se reportó daños en la infraestructura de salud, entre ellos, el establecimiento de salud de Estero de Indio, ubicado en el municipio de El Negrito, Yoro, que sufrió daños por inundación. En 2022, el país también experimentó un aumento significativo en el flujo de movimientos mixtos en tránsito por el país, así como el aumento en la exigencia en la provisión de servicios de salud, en particular, en los departamentos de El Paraíso y Choluteca.  

En este sentido, el proyecto pretende contribuir a fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta del sector salud para la atención oportuna de las poblaciones vulnerables afectadas por fenómenos naturales y migraciones por flujos mixtos y beneficiar a 290 956 personas con necesidades en salud, incidiendo en la reducción de indicadores de morbilidad y mortalidad, así como en las brechas de género, edad, discapacidad y etnicidad en la atención.

project_name: Espacios de seguridad y servicios de respuesta a la violencia de género paralas mujeres y las niñas
project_objective:
Como respuesta al análisis de necesidades a nivel nacional que ha identificado los graves riesgos y situación crítica de violencia basada en género que sufren las mujeres y niñas en Honduras, UNFPA propone brindar respuesta con una mirada de emergencia a esas necesidades identificadas a través de garantizar los servicios de atención a las sobrevivientes de VBG, enfocándose en las poblaciones que históricamente han enfrentado mayores barreras, y brechas más profundas para acceder a servicios de calidad y recibir una respuesta integral a sus necesidades, enfocada en sus derechos y en el respeto a sus diversidades. Esto representa que el proyecto está diseñado para ser implementado en los municipios con una alta incidencia de comunidades afrodescendientes (La Ceiba y Tela), y de población de origen indígena tolupán (Yoro). Ala vez que toma en cuenta los enormes desafíos que enfrentan las mujeres que deciden migrar o desplazarse internamente por razones de violencia, siendo San Pedro Sula y Choluteca, dos municipios priorizados por los altos índices de violencia contra mujeres y niñas y su ubicación geográfica de relevancia asociada a la migración y al desplazamiento forzado, tanto por ser municipios expulsores como receptores de personas y puntos de paso migratorio.
Para el proyecto actual, es imprescindible considerar la respuesta basada en el enfoque centrado en las sobrevivientes y sus derechos, garantizando que esta respuesta incluya los enfoques de género, edad y de atención diferenciada, incluyendo la diversidad de cultura, identidad de género y orientación sexual como un pilar en el análisis e implementación de las actividades. Estas actividades están centradas en los servicios de apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal, salud mental, espacios seguros y gestión de casos para garantizar que las mujeres, adolescentes y niñas que también se ven de manera diferenciada y particular afectadas directamente por las emergencias actuales en el país tengan acceso a servicios básicos para sus necesidades inmediatas a través de las actividades descritas y del acompañamiento cercano en las remisiones oportunas que respondan a las necesidades y elecciones libres de las sobrevivientes.
Por otra parte, el proyecto destaca la relevancia de fortalecer a las instituciones del estado y a las organizaciones de base comunitaria para que puedan hacer una prevención efectiva a la vez que se instalan las capacidades para responder a la VBG, y prepararse para esta respuesta en las próximas emergencias, mitigando así los riesgos para las mujeres y niñas de las comunidades más afectadas.

project_name: Assistance en eau , assainissement et hygiène pour les populations affectées par l’insécurité dans les régions de l’Est, du Centre-Est, du Sahel, du Nord, des cascades et des Hauts-Bassins au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Depuis 2015, le Burkina Faso traverse une crise sécuritaire, alors que le pays faisait déjà face à d’autres chocs liés à sa position géographique dans la bande Sahélienne de l’Afrique et aux effets du changement climatique. Cette crise se caractérise par une recrudescence des violences intercommunautaires, entre les forces armées Burkinabé et les groupes d’opposition armées (GOA) qui touche actuellement la quasi-totalité du pays. L’escalade de la violence qui cible de plus en plus des civiles, a conduit à la dégradation de la situation humanitaire et à des mouvements massifs de population sans précédent au Burkina Faso. Selon le Conseil National de Secours d’Urgence et de Réhabilitation (CONASUR), le nombre de personnes déplacées internes du fait de l’insécurité s’élevait à 1 761 915 personnes au 31 Octobre 2022. La majorité de ces personnes sont des femmes (53%) et des enfants (dont ceux ayant moins de 5 ans représentent 13,68%). La situation de l’approvisionnement en eau potable et assainissement dans les principales régions concernées était déjà précaire malgré les efforts fournis par le gouvernement. L’arrivée des populations déplacées a contribué à augmenter les pressions sur les ressources naturelles. Au niveau des points d’eau, les populations sont confrontées à de longues file d’attente avec des temps d’attente de plus d’une heure dans certaines zones. En réponse à cette situation, Action contre la Faim propose une stratégie qui vise à répondre aux besoins humanitaires des populations dans le besoin (populations déplacées et populations hôtes) dans le secteur de l’eau, de l’assainissement et de l’hygiène. Elle intègre également l’amélioration de l’environnement sanitaire et la prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI) dans les centres de santé afin d’améliorer la qualité de la prise en charge, du traitement de la malnutrition et de réduire les maladies nosocomiales.
Le projet cible principalement les régions de l’Est, du Centre-Est, du Nord, des Cascades et des Hauts-Bassins. Il sera mis en œuvre en coordination avec les acteurs présents dans les zones susmentionnées afin de maximiser l’impact des interventions. L’équipe du mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM-Frontline), dont le Lead est assuré par Action Contre la Faim, continuera d’assurer la veille humanitaire dans les autres régions cibles et la mise à jour des besoins des populations affectées.

project_name: Réponse alimentaire et nutritionnelle aux populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire et alimentaire dans les régions de l’Est, du Nord, des Cascades et des Hauts Bassins.
project_objective: L’intervention a pour objectif de réduire l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations déplacées et résidentes affectées par la crise sécuritaire et alimentaire dans un contexte humanitaire dégradé. En effet, le contexte humanitaire du Burkina Faso connait une forte dégradation depuis la fin de l’année 2021 notamment avec l’apparition de nouvelles zones de conflit, l’augmentation des zones à accès difficile et la multiplication des attaques des Groupes d’Opposition Armés (GOA). Cette aggravation de la violence armée a entrainé une hausse de 41% du nombre de personnes déplacées entre septembre 2021 et septembre 2022 (Groupe de coordination opérationnel de la réponse rapide, octobre 2022). Cette situation a accentué la vulnérabilité structurelle des ménages déjà très fragiles, caractérisée par la pauvreté et la récurrence des chocs et risques de catastrophes. Cette vulnérabilité des populations a été aggravée par la crise russo-ukrainienne qui a entrainé une augmentation des prix de céréales ainsi que des intrants agricoles essentiels. Cela renforce la hausse des prix liée à la déstabilisation des marchés et à la baisse de la production agricole aboutissant à une inflation sans précédent.  Le prix moyen des céréales de base a connu une importante hausse comparativement aux années précédentes (+51% par rapport à l’année passée et +73% par rapport à la moyenne quinquennale). Le prix des produits importés (blé, sucre, huile, riz) a connu aussi une hausse importante allant de 18 à 70 comparativement à l’année précédente (Programme Alimentaire Mondial – Société Nationale de Gestion des Stocks de Sécurité Alimentaire du Burkina Faso, octobre 2022). Tous ces facteurs affectent la capacité des personnes à répondre à leurs besoins de base surtout alimentaire qui est identifié comme un besoin prioritaire par la majorité des ménages lors des déplacements ou pendant la période de soudure agricole. Ce projet vise à (i) atténuer les effets immédiats de l’insécurité alimentaire aiguë au sein des ménages les plus vulnérables des régions du Nord, de l’Est, des Hauts-Bassins et des Cascades à travers une assistance alimentaire, et (ii) reconstituer ou renforcer les moyens de subsistance des personnes affectées par le développement d’activité génératrice de revenus pour leur permettre un relèvement précoce et renforcer leur résilience à moyen et long terme. En parallèle, cette assistance sera optimisée avec la distribution de farine infantile aux enfants de 6-23 mois et de compléments alimentaires aux femmes enceintes et femmes allaitantes (FEFA) afin de maximiser l’impact positif du projet sur la situation nutritionnelle des ménages bénéficiaires.  La modalité de l’assistance alimentaire privilégiée est le transfert monétaire et non restrictif via un système e-cash. L’assistance nutritionnelle sera assurée par une distribution en nature d’intrants nutritionnels qui seront acquis auprès de fournisseurs locaux. Par ailleurs, les appuis à la mise en œuvre d'activités génératrices de revenu (AGR) seront fournis soit en espèces ou en coupons afin d’offrir la flexibilité aux ménages bénéficiaires de faire un choix optimal des types d'actifs productifs qu’ils souhaiteraient acquérir.

project_name: Improving access to sanitation and mitigating stormwater risks for vulnerable people and localities in Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve WASH conditions of the vulnerable areas in Gaza Strip and ensuring better access to safe water and sanitation facilities. This is going to be accomplished through the construction and upgrading of existing storm water and wastewater infrastructure. The intervention will in turn will help protect vulnerable individuals in Al Salam and Abu Hamad areas in Khan Younis governorate from the risk of percolation of wastewater from existing cesspits and from flood during the winter season. It will also help protect people in Alkaram in area surrounding al-Sawari School and Almanayaa areas (in Jabalia) from floods during the winter season. 

The project is in line with the strategic objectives 2 and 3 and is also aligned with WASH cluster objectives 2 and 3. The proposed intervention responds to SDG # 6 which aims to ensure available and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all, and includes targets for universal access to drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene for all by 2030.

The project will target 16,861 people in need who depend on only cesspits to discharge their wastewater (3801 women, 3957 men, 3800 girls and 3955 boys, 505 elderly and 843 people with disabilities).

The project will be implemented in cooperation with Youth Empowerment Center (YEC) and includes the following components:
1. Installation of sewer collection network and HH connections: Construction of 6-kilometer-long wastewater networks including 310 HHs connections and 900 m storm water pipe collection in Bani Suhaila in khan Younis governorate
2. Installation of 650 m storm water system through establishing collection network with all fittings in Al Karama area in Jabalia.
Details: 
In south Governorate 1:
Activity 1.1) Installation of 6,000 meters of sewer collection network at Al-Salam & Abu Hamed areas. The Target: 310 households (1,860 individuals, 948 males, 912 females).
Activity 1.2) Constructing of 900 meters storm water system through establishing collection network at the targeted area suffering from recurrent flooding including all required fittings (e.g., manholes, gullies, …etc.) at Al-Salam & Abu Hamed areas in Bani Suhaila in khan Younis Governorate.

In North governorate 2: 
Activity 2.1: Constructing of 650 meters storm water system through establishing collection network including all fittings (e.g., manholes, gullies, …etc.) at Al Karama area 
-2.1.1: AL-Manayaa area: Installation of concrete rain pipes of 100 cm diameter, with a total length of 250 meters, and manholes with a diameter of 150 cm.
- 2.1.2: Surrounding of al-Sawari school: Installation of concrete rain pipes of 100 cm diameter, with a total length of 400 meters, and manholes with a diameter of 150 cm and Square manhole 2x2m.
The activities will be implemented in full coordination with the municipalities of Bani Suhaila and Jabalia, CMWU, and PWA.

project_name: Protection des personnes déplacées, retournées et migrantes au Lac et Nord du Tchad.
project_objective:
En sus de l'insécurité et les déplacements massifs de population dans la province du Lac, environ 400,000 personnes depuis 2021, l'Etat Tchadien doit faire face à l'augmentation des cas de traite des personnes dans le pays. Les besoins des personnes affectées par ces différents phénomènes, notamment les femmes, enfants et personnes vulnérables continuent d’augmenter non seulement en raison des facteurs susmentionnés mais aussi en raison de la crise sanitaire liée à la COVID-19.

Les besoins urgent en protection selon le Cluster Protection ont augmentees notemment dans 2022. Ainsi, l’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en protection pour les personnes déplacées, retournées et migrantes à travers différentes activités de protection ciblées et transversales.

En complément des programmes d’urgence de l’OIM déjà existants principalement centrée sur la distribution de kits d’abris et d’articles ménagers essentiels (AME) et le CCCM, la réponse de l'OIM dans le secteur de la protection en 2023 sera axée sur les services et activités de soutien psychosocial (SPS), la lutte contre la traite d’êtres humains en situation d'urgences, l’atténuation des risques, la réponse et la prévention des violences basées sur le genre (VBG).

Toutes les activités proposées par l’OIM sont alignées sur les objectifs sectoriels 1 et 3 du Cluster Protection de « Renforcer l’environnement de protection en vue d’un meilleur respect de droits fondamentaux et la promotion des solutions durables"" et "" Prévenir les risques liés aux violences basées sur le genre et améliorer l’accès et la qualité des services multisectoriels pour les survivants"" pour l'année 2023.

project_name: RENFORCER LA REPONSE EN MESURES D'ASSAINISSEMENT ET D'HYGIENE DANS La PROVINCE DU LAC
project_objective:
L’OIM prévoit de fournir une réponse en eau, hygiène et assainissement à travers la construction de 150 points d'eau propre afin de renforcer l'accès des populations affectées par des crises à l'eau salubre, en lien avec l'objectif 1 du Cluster WASH dans le HRP 2023. L'OIM prévoit égalemment de renforcer l'accès des populations affectées à des installations sanitaires améliorées, en ligne avec l'objectif 2 de la stratégie de réponse du Cluster WASH pour 2023, en fournissant 1,000 latrines d'urgence, suivant le design validé par le Cluster. Enfin, en tenant compte du contexte sanitaire, l'OIM prévoit la distribution de 500 stations de lavage de main et de 1,000 kits d'hygiene, incluant des articles de gestion de l'hygiene menstruelle. Ces activités seront accompagnées de sessions basiques sur la promotion de l'hygiène, afin de garantir la pleine efficacité des interventions susmentionnées, par le biais, par exemple, de matériels d'information, d'éducation et de communication sur le lavage des mains et d'autres actions visant à prévenir la transmission du COVID-19 et d'autres maladies.
Toutes ces activités seront menées en étroite collaboration avec le Cluster. Des mécanismes de plainte seront mis en place pour accompagner toutes les activités de distribution et un suivi post-distribution sera mené afin de recuillir les feedbacks des bénéficiaires notamment des personnes les plus vulnérables. Les résultats de ce suivi pourront être transmis au Cluster afin de tirer des leçons apprises

project_name: Increasing safe, equitable and dignified access to essential basic protection services reducing exposure of affected vulnerable populations to protection risks, including GBV in Pibor (IPC 5), Nyirol (IPC 4) and Akobo (IPC 4) in Jonglei State
project_objective: The proposed HRP 2022 interventions will be implemented in Pibor, Nyirol and Akobo West which have been classified as IPC 4 and 5 facing deteriorating humanitarian conditions, worsened by endemic violence, conflict, access constraints and operational interference, public health challenges such as direct and indirect effects of COVID-19 and climatic shocks resulting in the dual phenomena of extraordinary flooding and localized drought, which have a severe impact on people’s livelihoods, hampers access to education and water, sanitation and hygiene and health services. Protection concerns remain high, with people impacted by violence having limited access to justice and the rule of law. The proposed intervention will contribute to the HRP 2022 Protection Cluster, General Protection Objectives: Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience; Enhance protection assessment and monitoring to inform protection and overall humanitarian response; and Ensure the provision of critical protection related assistance and specialized services through an integrated approach to address the priority needs of targeted people among vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas. The main objective of the proposed intervention is to increase safe, equitable and dignified access to essential basic protection services reducing exposure of affected vulnerable populations to protection risks, including GBV in Pibor, Nyirol and Akobo in Jonglei State. To achieve this, the proposed intervention has the following specific objectives: SO1 To undertake effective and timely protection assessments in targeted areas for timely and robust humanitarian and protection decisions, influence and actions; SO2 To strengthen community-based protection mechanisms for risk reduction and promotion of local peace and security for women and youths; SO3 To provide Individual Protection Assistance to address priority protection needs for vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in targeted areas; SO4 To support ‘safe programming’ (protection mainstreaming) including safeguarding in all interventions in all the targeted locations. Targeted population are Host Communities, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Returnees consisting of women, girls, boys and men. The intervention will be contributing to the Protection Cluster target of 105,320 women, men, girls and boys provided with individual, group, specialized PSS and other related general protection services. This project will be implemented by Oxfam and its local partners. The expected number of people reached through Oxfam intervention is 6,600 (across all locations 60% women, 20% girls, 10% boys, 10% men): Pibor HC-1000, IDPs-800, Returnees-400; Akobo HC-1000, IDPs-800, Returnees-400 and Nyirol HC-1000, IDPs-800, Returnees-400.

project_name: Promoting the inclusion and access of Children with Disabilities to education in the emergency context of oPt
project_objective:
The proposed project is designed in-line with the education cluster framework to respond to the specific needs of girls and boys with disabilities who are dropout from schools (those children with disabilities who never attended education or dropped from schools) or at risk of dropout. Under the cluster objective one “Strengthen advocacy and reporting on education-related violations across oPt and ensure that school staff and students affected by the education-related violations and pandemic benefit from protective environment” the project plans to develop a mechanism to connect the school with its children to map and identify the hotspots to allow them to take preventive measure to avoid threats at these areas. In line with the IASC guideline on MHPSS in emergency, in particular under the third layer of the MHPSS pyramid of interventions, the trained and supervised school counsellors and PSS volunteers will conduct school based inclusive psychosocial support, collectively and individually targeting children with and without disabilities. In addition, the PSS volunteers will contribute implementing outreach support visits to parents of children to provide psychoeducation sessions enhancing knowledge of parents on how to respond to the needs of their children when they are in a psychosocial distress. Emotional support, structure collective support sessions, psychoeducation, counseling, and PFA will be provided. Moreover, the project will provide school-based inclusive PSS services for those girls and boys who are affected by the education-related violations, while under the education cluster objective two “Increase equitable safe access to inclusive, quality educational services for vulnerable children”, the project will provide its support at two levels, for affected children and affected schools, where after the identification of girls and boys who are out of school or at risk of dropout, children will be supported by personalized support based on the results of social assessment and plan; support will include, provision of assistive devices, educational kits, provision of safe and accessible transportation, referral to other basic services; at the school level, the project will be supporting the development of safe and accessible school environment to welcome all children, capacity-building of teachers to respond to the individual educational needs of learners including those with disabilities, support to parents clubs to develop and lead initiative on the right to education, provision of furniture and equipment to resource rooms to support the learning of students, organization of remedial and catch-up classes and implementation of inclusive recreational activities to support inclusion and diversity and reduce bullying. Under cluster objective three “Children and school staff in vulnerable schools are supported in preparing and responding to emergencies”, the project will support the provision of prepositioned educational materials and stationaries to be used by the school and children in case of emergency. 
The project aims to target 675 girls and 825 boys with disabilities, and will be implemented through a partnership with local organization with substantial experience in the education sector “Teacher Creativity Center”. The project will target 20 schools, 10 in Gaza (across the five governorate) and 10 in West Bank (South Tubas, South Nablus)). The project will also collaborate with technical partners as the Ministry of Education and Organizations of Persons with Disabilities.

project_name: Reducing child labour and school drop-out in the Gaza Strip through multi-sectoral protection services.
project_objective:
The ongoing Israeli blockade and escalations have had devastating consequences on the Gaza Strip: 1.32 million people (63% of residents) are in need of multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance (MSNA 2022). Of these, 988,282 people (of which 148,242 are persons with disabilities (PWD)) are assessed as needing protection services (Protection Cluster, Protection Analysis Update, September 2022). With a poor economic growth rate (3.5% in 2022 vs 7% in 2021) (World Bank, 2022), 60% of households in Gaza have members seeking employment (MSNA 2022). Coping mechanisms adopted by families in response to poverty and vulnerability have negative consequences for children’s rights and ability to access education and protection services, manifested in an increase in school drop-out and child labour (Tdh, 2020; Tdh, 2021). In 2021-22 school year, 6% of school age children (281 children) dropped out of school; and 14% of girls and 68% of boys did so due to child labour (MSNA 2022). By 2022, 7% of households with school-aged children reported that their children were not attending school, of which 36% cannot afford to pay school expenses while 9% have children who are working (MSNA 2022). Additionally, 9% of households are planning not to send children to school, out of which 8% report that they need the child to support the family and 15% cannot afford school expenses. 

This project will provide multisectoral interventions aligned with the HRP Strategic Objectives and those of the Protection and Education Clusters, in order to decrease the prevalence of child labour in the Gaza Strip while increasing children's access to the formal education system and other vocational training opportunities. Interventions include child protection services, mental health and psychosocial services, educational reintegration, family support, and increased community mobilization on issues of child labour and school drop-out. The project will target 11,750 beneficiaries, including 1,000 working children, children who have dropped out, or who are at risk of dropping out (300 working children, 250 out of schools and 450 at risk of drop out).

Proposed activities at the level of the child include provision of individual case management and MHPSS services to children engaged in child labour, out-of-school children, and children at high risk of dropout; as well referral to specialized services as needed; re-integration of out-of-school children (100 boys, 50 girls) in official education and vocational education, provision of school stationery, uniforms, assistive devices, printed self-learning material, and provision of catch-up and remedial classes to out-of-school children. To support vulnerable families with children at risk of drop-out or child labour, cash assistance of 1050 ILS per family will be provided to cover basic food and non-food needs and restore coping capacities. Activities targeting service providers include training sessions for school staff, focusing on issues such as dealing with children with low academic achievement and positive discipline. 
In total, 150 families with children benefitting from case management will also receive cash assistance (840 persons will benefit from this component, each family receiving 1050 ILS). 120 school staff will benefit from training sessions on PSEA, child safeguarding policy, and protection mainstreaming, and 6,000 community members (male and female) will benefit from training on the importance of eliminating child labour. The project team will provide services to the identified cases through the child protection centres which are distributed across the Gaza Strip, one in each governorate. 
Tdh will coordinate with relevant ministries and clusters, including Education and Protection will be utilized in this project. Tdh will report its intervention to the Education and Protection Clusters, UNRWA, CP AoR Working Group. Tdh will be actively involved in the cash-programming working group, relevant ministries/actors.

project_name: Enhancing protection of vulnerable children and their families in the Gaza Strip through provision of integrated services
project_objective:
The ongoing Israeli blockade and escalations since 2008 have had devastating consequences on all aspects of life in the Gaza Strip. It is estimated that 1.32 million people (63% of Gaza residents) are in need of multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance (MSNA, 2022). Of these, 988,282 people (of which 148,242 are persons with disabilities) are assessed as needing protection services (Protection Cluster, Protection Analysis Update, September 2022). World Bank projections (2020) had indicated that 64% of Gaza's population would live in poverty by 2021, and it has one of the highest unemployment rates in the world. By 2022, the economy had not returned to pre-Covid levels, with a growth rate of only 3.5% in 2022 (versus 7.1% in 2021) (World Bank, 2022), due to factors such as the escalation in August 2022, the crisis in Ukraine, and movement restrictions.  
The toll on the well-being of residents of Gaza is high, with 40% of households reporting that at least one member of their household experiences signs of psychosocial distress or trauma (MSNA 2022). In a context characterized by prolonged strain, economic isolation and developmental decline, vulnerable families, including those with many children, female-headed households, and families with people with disabilities, have adopted different coping mechanisms to deal with the high level of poverty and vulnerability. The deteriorating socio-economic condition in Gaza has had a particularly negative impact on the realisation of children’s rights and the risk of protection violations notably gender-based violence.
Nearly 1 million (953,884) children in the oPt are in need of protection and MHPSS services, of which 499,187 are children in Gaza, and 79,936 children and 27,534 caregivers in the Gaza Strip are in need of structured protection and psychosocial support (Protection Cluster Protection Analysis, August 2022).  According to preliminary findings of a UNICEF-supported MHPSS Assessment conducted by Tdh in Gaza from July -September 2022, the need for MHPSS services is very high, particularly for children who have protection concerns (Tdh, 2022). 

The Protection Cluster has identiﬁed the provision of MHPSS services and case management as key interventions needed in the Gaza Strip. This Action is a response to such needs and is consistent with HRP's Second Objective. Activities will include age and gender-appropriate, inclusive child protection services, including specialized case management for GBV survivors, structured MHPSS services, awareness-raising to reduce the prevalence of GBV, and family support to assist in responding to distressed children. Overall, 12,550 persons will benefit from the project (2,500 girls, 2,500 boys, 3,775 women, and 3,775 men).

Of the targeted children, 1,000 will benefit from MHPSS services, 400 children will benefit from case management, and of them, 100 will benefit from MHPSS and case management provided to child survivors of GBV. Community and family members and caregivers will receive awareness and skills strengthening, including on CP, GBV and how to deal with distressed children (7000 persons) and CP workers will benefit from training and coaching sessions. Quality, timely protection services will be tailored according to age, gender disability and the best interest of boys and girls. As part of the case management interventions, cash support to meet urgent needs will be provided to 200 vulnerable families also benefiting from protection services. 
During implementation, beneﬁciaries will be closely involved in designing and monitoring the project activities and a Project Monitoring and Evaluation Plan will be developed at the start of the Action with the participation of the five partner organizations, including indicators, assessments, and means of veriﬁcation tools deﬁned in the logical framework. The Project team will coordinate with the relevant authorities, child protection actors, the Protection Cluster, SGBV-sub-cluster, and CP-AoR.

project_name: Safe and dignified multi-sectoral protection and prevention services for acutely vulnerable women and girls GBV  survivors across Gaza Strip
project_objective: The project addresses main problem ""rise in GBV, discrimination & harmful practices against vulnerable women 18-59 and>59years/ girls 14-17years including with disabilities & cancer patients affected by blockade, conflict-related violence, violence in HHs, protracted crisis in Gaza & their limited access to safe/dignified multi-sectoral GBV services."" It addresses protection/GBV risks, access barriers and needs of women/girls identified in needs assessment (NA)/ gender analysis/GBV risk analysis conducted on 11-16/10/2022. Findings of NA included exposure of women/girls to physical, psychological, social, economic & sexual violence, early marriage; patriarchal culture and gender-biased attitudes; legal illiteracy; women’s reproductive role in HHs; lack of livelihoods/ income; deprived access to basic needs; exclusion of WWDs/GWDs and cancer patients; lack of women’s awareness on their rights, GBV services and PSEA; and their limited access to safe GBV services. Its objective is ""Acutely vulnerable women>18-59 and >59 years/ girls 14-17 years including with disabilities GBV survivors, have meaningful access to safe, dignified, gender responsive& inclusive multi-sectoral services based on GBV Minimum Standards” and outcomes are: 1. Acutely vulnerable women/girls GBV survivors manifested psychological well-being, good health, met basic needs, safety/dignity, knowledge, changed attitudes/behaviors toward reporting GBV, resilience & positive coping; 2. Front-line staff of GBV actors are better able to detect, refer/provide safe/ dignified multi-sectoral services; and 3. Local/national duty bearers sensitized and act to protect acutely vulnerable women/girls GBV survivors via community engagement & advocacy. The project targets directly 9810 beneficiaries (5790 women, 640 men, 3220 girls, 160 boys, out of them 489 PwDs) identified based on vulnerability criteria: with disabilities, cancer, elderly, IDPs, refugees, pregnant women, FHHs, GBV survivors & poverty according to their location, status, protection risks & needs severity. Beneficiaries are selected from Jabalya (Tal Za'tar/Twam) and Beit Lahya (A'tatra/Salatin) by ACHA; Gaza City (Shijaia, Sh-Radwan) & Nuseirat camp by WAC; Kh-Younis-Mawasi& Qarara; Rafah-Mawasi by CFTA & ARAs coordinated with GBV SWG. The project links to MSNA/HNO 2022, HRP SO1, PC obj 3 eligible activities/indicators. Partners consolidate their experience in geographical& thematic areas and coordinate with CBOs to address women/girls GBV survivors needs. They implement activities: A) Provide PSS counseling via partners’ helplines to 2700 women/660 girls & individual PSS to 780 women/180 girls & group PSS to 180 women/45 girls; therapy to 150 couples; specialized MH to 48 women/12 girls; recreational days to 420 women/180 girls; legal counseling to 150 women/30 girls; dignity kits to 360 women; legal representation to 60 women/15 girls; unconditional protection cash assistance to 300 women/30 girls as a complimentary measure to holistic GBV services tailored on specific needs of each women/girl to produce a protection outcome by preventing, reducing or mitigating  their exposure to  protection risks, reducing vulnerabilities& enhancing capacities; economic enablement to 39 women; case management (MHPSS, legal aid, health care to pregnant women/ cancer patients/WWDs, economic support, referral to shelter) to 81 women/9 girls; 1 GBV service directory; PSEA awareness sessions to 160 women/60 girls/160 men/60 boys; B) self-care & PSEA training for 54 partners staff & 120 frontline staff of specialized/non-specialized GBV actors & community members; C) community engagement& advocacy: 1 radio ad, 6 press releases, 9 community meetings, pamphlet on PSEA, 1 fact sheet, 3 position papers, PSEA complaints integrated into overall FCM, integrate PSEA into contracting; advocacy initiative. Partners ensure right-based & survivor-centered approaches, GBV Minimum Standards, SADDD, GBV risk mitigation to uphold do no harm

project_name: Providing multi-sectoral protection services for women and girls survivors or at risk of GBV in Rafah & KhanYounis governorates
project_objective:
The project aims to provide multisectoral protection services to women and girls survivors or at risk of GBV, including PWDs, in the Southern governorates of the Gaza Strip through Al Awda Community Centre- Rafah and Al Awda Community Center- Khanyounis - Bani Suhila.

To provide the project services with the required quality and maximum protection for the target women and girls, the project staff of 10 persons of both sexes, (8 females and 2 males) will be involved in training courses to provide them with the necessary knowledge and skills, where 3 training courses will be carried out on: (i) Disability Inclusion (ii) GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response (iii) AWDA policies related to PSEA, Safeguarding and Code of Conduct.

Through the project, multisectoral services will be provided including: (i) structured psychosocial support services (collective and individual) (ii) legal consultations (iii) case management and referral to more specialized services such as health, Mental Health and court representation, this besides providing emergency needs for each individual case such as medicine, clothes, non-food items, assistive devices..etc. (iv) within the framework of protecting GBV cases cash assistance will be provided (v) to empower GBV cases, they will received grants to enable them to set up small projects after receiving vocational and management trainings that can guarantee a permanent income that contributes to provide their needs and those of their families with dignity. (vi) This in addition to distributing dignity kits to GBV cases upon specific criteria. 

At the community level and to promote the concept of prevention, mitigating risk and response among men, women, girls and boys, including PWDs, awareness sessions will be carried out where 2 sessions will be allocated to include PWDs of both sexes, provided that a sign language interpreter service will be provided during the implementation of these sessions to ensure that persons with hearing disabilities benefit from the sessions information. This in addition to the publication of a motion graphic with a sign language interpretation, which will include awareness messages about PSEA. 

The project will also build the capacity of a group of non-specialized GBV service providers from AWDA and CBOs staff on prevention, risk mitigation and response.

On the other hand, and in order to improve the staff's psychological status, self-care days will be organized to provide psychological rest and alleviate the psychological pressures they are exposed to.

To enhance Accountability to Affected Population (AAP), the project target group will be involved at all the stages of the project. And in order for them to access information about the project's activities and locations, adding to AWDA Feedback, Complaint and Response Mechanisms (FCRM), Facebook advertisement and Radio Spot will be published. 

Noting that the project's services will be provided to the target groups, taking into account the gender needs, where the majority of the staff will be females. Furthermore, impartiality and independently will be taken into account during the provision of the project services with preserving the beneficiaries’ dignity and without any discrimination on the basis of sex, color, religion or political affiliation.

It is worth mentioning that the idea of the project was presented to the GBV Sub-Working Group Coordinator, who in turns supported the idea and confirmed its importance.  Moreover, and in order to avoid duplication of service provision, coordination has been made with the Wefaq in Rafah and CFTA in KhanYonis.

project_name: Providing Protection & PSS Services for Children in Rafah and Gaza
project_objective:
The idea of the project is based on providing protection & PSS services for children aged 6-17 years old affected by conflict related violence & violence in households (from both sexes including PWDs), the activities will be provided through AWDA’s Community Centers in Gaza & Rafah, and for the successful implementation of the project, the local community will be communicated with information about the project’s activities & locations through: (i) Radio spot (ii) Facebook ads (iii) Meetings with the local committees affiliated to AWDA.

In order to ensure the maximum protection for the children who will benefit from the project services, the capacity of the project staff (M&F) will be built through conducting 3 training courses as follows:
• 1st training course in disability inclusion aiming at strengthening protection mainstreaming throughout the humanitarian response.
• 2nd training course in the guidelines on mental health and psychosocial support and child protection standards/tools.
• 3rd training course in AWDA’s safeguarding policy, PSEA policy and Code of Conduct to guarantee the highest protection of the beneficiaries during receiving the services
To relieve the psychological pressure on the project staff, 3 days of self-care will be implemented with them. From the other side, capacity building will be implemented for non-child protection professionals (whether from AWDA’s workers or CBOs) in child protection detection & referral (children who are affected by conflict related violence and household violence and who subjected to protection threats) aiming to mainstream CP in other humanitarian action.
The project staff will provide the following services for the targeted children & their caregivers:
(i) Structured PSS sessions (ii) Collective & individual PSS services (iii) Case management & referral services, while special needs will be provided to some children, such as medicines, clothes & shoes. (iv) PSS caregivers’ sessions in positive parenting, stress management & cyber violence protection. It is worth to mention that these services will be provided by using IDEAL, WE DEAL and PARENTS DEAL manuals

The project will include community-based activities as follows:
(i) Publishing radio spot & Facebook ads with the aim of expanding awareness of the community in the field of child protection (ii) Publishing motion graphic videos (interpreted to sign language to reach PWDs) with awareness messages related to PSEA (iii) Conducting awareness sessions with different groups of the community members, including women, men, boys & girls (PWDs), with the aim of raising their awareness about child protection PSEA in order to encourage them to detect cases & refer them to specialized centers.

In order to achieve the principle of AAP, the beneficiaries will participate in all the project cycle phases & will be informed about AWDA’s Feedback, Complain and Response Mechanism (FCRM). Noting that simulation on submitting feedback & complaints will be carried out with the children in order to encourage them to submit feedback & complaints that will help us to improve the services.

Within the framework of coordination & complementary work & to avoid duplication in the provision of services, coordination was made with the Protection Cluster Coordinator, the Child Protection Coordinator and the Ministry of Social Development who in turns supported the idea and confirmed its importance.
For complementarity in the implementation of services and to avoid duplication in service provision, coordination has been made with GCMHP and WEFAQ association.

project_name: Providing elective surgeries to patients registered on the MoH waiting lists in Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip continues to deteriorate as a result of the accumulation of the humanitarian crises that affecting all aspects of life, including the decline in the quantity and quality of the health services provided to patients in need. As the 2023 HNO indicated that 5,300 patients are in need for surgical interventions and scheduled on the MoH waiting lists. Noting that the No. of those patients usually ranges between 9,000 to 16,000 patients, which means an increase in patients' suffering and a high incidence of life-threatening complications.

To respond to these needs and to bridge the gap in providing surgical services to patients registered on the MoH waiting lists, AWDA through this project will conduct elective surgeries targeting 1,000 patients (women, men, girls, boys including PWDs) at its following health facilities:
1.	Al Awda Hospital- Jabalia
2.	Al Awda Hospital- Al Nuseirat 
3.	The Daily Surgery Unit at Al Awda Health Centre- Rafah 

The spread of AWDA’s facilities in the 3 governorates of the Gaza Strip (North – Middle and South) will facilitate the beneficiaries' access to the project services.

project_name: Prepositioning and provision of life saving drugs and disposables for trauma and NCD related illnesses to enhance the preparedness and response of health system in Gaza
project_objective:

project_name: Upscaling and Improving Trauma and Community Emergency Response and Preparedness Across the West Bank
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to upscale and improve the emergency preparedness and response within the West Bank. 
Community wise, the project intends to support and empower men and women living in the harsh situation, politically, economically, and socially, by building a well-structured emergency response plan, integrating First Aid training, emergency response training, leadership and communication training and creating emergency teams in the targeted locations. 
This activity intends to support community members living within the communities to obtain knowledge on communication and leadership, first aid, emergency training including evacuation, simulation training and Disaster Preparedness. By teaching First Aid and basic life support, we try to mitigate the sudden death related to cardiovascular disease, the primary cause of mortality according to the Palestinian Health Annual Report. In parallel, we foresee that the trainees will be capacitated to respond to any sudden onset disaster, and play major role, within their communities. Along with this training, we intend to provide to the trainees a First Aid Kit, giving them all the means to respond to emergencies as bystanders.
Hebron: Enab al Kabeer, Birein, Shweika, Arab Freijat, Wadi al Reem, Sensana, Deir al Asal, Beit al Roosh, Santana and Zanuta.
Jordan Valley and East Jerusalem: Mihtawish, Trefat, Kurshan, Mlaihat, Tabaneh, Buran, Abu Faisal, Abu Husein, Mikhmas, and Dawaheek1.
Out of the selected trainees, 50% will be trained on disaster management, allowing them to become a part of a bigger network of trained volunteers hence contribution to increase preparedness and response capacity of the target communities.
This project is built on the mobile clinics of PMRS supported by MAP, where PMRS and MAP built a decent trust and connection with the communities, and provide a comprehensive service, in addition to the quality health and mental health services provided by the mobile clinic teams, this comes to further empower the communities and increase their resilience. 
On the other hand, the project will also enhance the Palestinian Health system’s emergency response and preparedness through building the capacity of health workers (nurses, doctors, & paramedics) at the Ministry of health (MoH) both non-governmental, governmental hospitals and emergency services providers (EMS) in the West Bank on trauma care and emergency lifesaving response and enhancing the preparedness further through providing medical equipment to be ready for immediate response during emergencies to ensure the sustainability of the essential health services during an emergency. MAP will target at least 200 health care workers (nurses, doctors, and paramedics) from MoH, NGOs, hospitals and EMS in all governorates in West Bank who will attend several trauma courses. The Training is certified by the American College of Surgeons and will be conducted in cooperation with the International Medical Education Trust (IMET 2000) at their accredited training center in Ramallah. 
 7 courses will be conducted over 2 training days/ course, with participation of 30 participants/course. 
The training is dedicated to preventing death and disability from trauma through education and emergency trauma care. The training will provide health providers with the knowledge and hands-on skills to take better care of trauma patients, including rapid assessment, appropriate intervention and identification of immediate life threats. The course combines classroom learning, hands-on skills stations, and assessment stations that put learning to work in simulated trauma scenarios.

project_name: Health under protection (HUP): Emergency health and nutrition assistance to people living in communities whose rights are inadequately protected in the West bank (WB).
project_objective:
CARE in partnership with Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS)/Local Health NGO will respond to this situation with a comprehensive intervention that combines elements of direct health service delivery to the identified vulnerable communities in Area C, East Jerusalem and H2, with a special focus on women, children, elderly, adolescents and people with disabilities (PWD), those in need of reporting and referral of S/GBV, PSEA cases, and the injured as a result of the Israeli settler and military force violence, and it also responds to the ongoing COVID-19 Pandemic through increased community awareness and full coordination with Ministry of Health offices (MoH) in order to support their vaccination process as well as the logistics processes, if and when needed. CARE will continue working with trained community representatives (focal points) and project staff to report/refer these violations using the agreed upon mechanism.
The proposed intervention will be targeting 50 vulnerable communities in Area C, East Jerusalem, H2 and North Jordan valley in the West Bank (Jenin, East Jerusalem and north Jordan valley, Hebron, and south Hebron hills, Masafer Yatta) that were identified by CARE/Partners/ MoH/ and the HNC during the recently conducted HRP 2023 workshops and via mobile clinics working group. All identified locations have serious access issues and lack of any type of health services. The identified locations will be targeted through 4 mobile health clinics 9 health teams that will visiting these communities regularly to provide the needed health services as per the agreed upon program/plan with the Health and Nutrition Cluster (HNC) and MoH.
The 50 locations are distributed as follows: 16 locations in Hebron Area mainly in Masafer Yatta, 13 locations in Jenin areas mainly inside the wall as Barta’a enclave., and 9 locations outside the wall area C, 12 Bedouin communities in East Jerusalem and middle Jordan valley area.
CARE/partners, in close coordination with MoH centrally and at the governorates’ level, 
will provide life-saving services in targeted communities in the WB using mobile clinics/teams that offer basic curative and preventive Primary Health Care services (PHC), including women’s healthcare/ SRH (ante and post-natal care, obstetric care, adolescent health, elderly, and post-menopausal syndromes. Midwives added to health teams to enhance health awareness activities and quality of services and referral mechanisms, etc.), general practice care (GP), health awareness with focus on communities’ needs and priorities, including COVID-19 control, prevention and referrals, basic lab tests, home visits, children health and psychosocial support. The team will also be provided with emergency kits that will enable them to respond to emergency incidents in these communities while working in the clinics to ensure best case management and lifesaving before transferring to the hospitals. Additionally, the teams will train selected community focal points (mainly females) on First Aid and provide them with First Aid kits to better respond to emergencies in their vulnerable and isolated communities. The package of services was designed jointly with UNFPA, HNC, the communities and MOH to synergize and unify the services all while building on the long operational and programmatic experience in working with the targeted locations.
The project is designed fully in coordination with other actors, mainly MoH, with which CARE/partners conducted several coordination meetings during August and September 2022 at MoH offices around the West Bank, and along with other INGOs (UNRWA, UNFPA, MAP), community leaders, focal points, beneficiaries, and community representatives, and women groups to capture women and girls’ special needs including PWD.
CARE/partners ensured that the existing data are updated, as well as indicators, that the stakeholders’ feedback is reflected in the proposal, activities that meet community needs and no overlapping.

project_name: Enhancing the resilience and protecting the livelihood of farmers and herders live in area C in north of West Bank and Jordan valley
project_objective:
The overall objective of this project is to protect the livelihoods, improve the resilience,
productive capacity and enhance the food security of vulnerable farmers and herders who
are living in Area C in north of West Bank and in Jordan valley. 
The objective is drawn from the FSS country Strategic Objective: SO1 The resilience of
vulnerable households are protected, and their livelihoods, food security and productive
capacity restored/enhanced. 
Food security in Palestine continues to be affected by protracted nature of the crisis, 
repeated shocks and continued restriction of freedom of movement, mainly for the most
vulnerable families under the national social safety net (SSN), in term and type of
frequency assistance. 
The proposed project goes in line with the first impact/ result “Agricultural assets and
productive capacities of farms and damaged productive assets (wells, irrigation systems,
cisterns, greenhouses) restored, and the clusters plans of the ministry of agriculture in
Area C in north of West Bank and in Jordan valley especially in the Jenin, Nablus, Tubas
and Jericho governorates. Where more than 11,100 living in 49 communities will be
directly supported through the project’ activities. 
The main activities will focus on rehabilitation and provision of productive assets and
inputs, for farmers and herders including promotion of technical capacities and small
scale production units, and using the BBB (Build-Back Better) approach for increased
resilience.
To strengthen its accountability toward beneficiaries and partners, CARE applies and has
an easily accessible, community-based Feedback and Accountability Mechanism (FAM),
which also attends to more sensitive, SEA-related complaints. CARE has a global policy on 
Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and Child Protection explicitly
outlining unacceptable behavior, and investigation processes, and follow up, as well as
the Safeguarding Code of Conduct. All project’s team will receive an orientation on the
PSEA related issues.
The proposed activities will focus to improve the access to the essential resources (water,
lands,… etc) through well planned rehabilitation and provide inputs to increase the
production capacities of the targeted farmers and herders in the selected areas. As part of
CARE strategy; and given the nature of the protracted crisis. 
CARE work closely with and through AIDA toward coordinated advocacy, for accountability for IHL violations in Area C. The project targeted communities are located in most vulnerable areas in Area C in north of West Bank and in Jordan valley who most of them were under threat of displacement, ISF. or /and settler’s violence and/or land confiscation and demolitions of assets, high increase in agriculture inputs prices due to Ukraine crisis  and who are affected by the continuing restrictions specifically after September 2022 due to closure of Nablus and Jenin.

project_objective:

project_name: Enhancing Gazan Farmers’ Ability to Recover Livelihoods Through Cash Assistance
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to support vulnerable and crisis-affected Farmers and Breeders in the Gaza Strip to sustain their livelihood assets, recover their production capacity, meet their food security needs, and reduce the use of negative coping strategies. The project is designed to align with and achieve the outcomes of the following Strategic and Cluster specific objectives: (Strategic Objective 03): The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. More specifically, it will contribute to the Food Security Sector Objective 01: The resilience of vulnerable households is protected, and their livelihoods, food security, and productive capacity restored/enhanced.

Through unconditional and restricted cash assistance, Mercy Corps and its local partner – Al Foukhary Association for Country Development (Al Foukhary) – will identify, select, and support 500 of the most vulnerable farmers and breeders from Khan Younis and Rafah governorates (2,800 individuals).

The project will focus on highly vulnerable and crises-affected male and female farmers and breeders in four groups, who will be selected from Khan Younis and Rafah through combined household vulnerability assessment and livelihood technical assessment.:
1)	Agricultural Open-Land: 136 Farmers (70 from Khan Younis and 66 from Rafah): Each selected small farmer will receive an average of $ 900 to rehabilitate 2.0 dunums of open land (ILS 1,500 per open land dunum).
2)	Greenhouse Rehabilitation: 90 Farmers (40 from Khan Younis and 50 from Rafah): Each selected small farmer will receive an average of $ 900 (ILS 3,000) to rehabilitate one Greenhouse.
3)	Poultry Farms Rehabilitation: 149 Farmers (70 from Khan Younis and 79 from Rafah): each poultry farmer will receive an average of $ 1,200 to rehabilitate their farms. Out of these, 12 farmers will receive photovoltaic (PV) systems with an average cost of $ 2,300 per PV system. 
4)	Livestock Farm Rehabilitation: 125 Breeders (65 from Khan Younis and 60 from Rafah): each livestock farmer will receive an average of $ 1,200 to rehabilitate their farms. Out of these, 5 farmers will receive PV systems with an average cost of $ 2,300.

By utilizing cash as a modality for direct assistance through Electronic Debit Cards (eWallet), participants have greater power to determine how to meet their urgent needs, empower them, and maintain their dignity while reducing their vulnerability and contributing to restoring their food security. The project will help farmers and breeders to improve their physical and economic conditions and enhance their resiliency in an effective and efficient way. Additionally, local markets are functional in the Gaza Strip, and vendors continue to have adequate stock available; therefore, cash assistance is an appropriate humanitarian response modality to meet critical basic needs.

Through well-established evidence-based vulnerability and technical targeting, the project will use the Proxy Means Test Formula (PMTF) and Technical Vulnerability Assessment Tool (TVAT) to identify, assess and verify selected vulnerable HHs to receive cash assistance, monitor activities, and ensure full coordination and engagement with the community and primary stakeholders. Mercy Corps will be the focal point of coordination with the main actors, and Al Foukhary will coordinate closely with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) to cross-check the names of vulnerable Farmers and Breeders.

Additionally, Mercy Corps will promote community ownership, accountability, and participation throughout the project through baseline assessments, orientation sessions, Post Distribution Monitoring, and its Community Accountability and Reporting Mechanism (CARM), while also mobilizing key stakeholders to more deeply engage with identified vulnerable farmers.

project_name: Supporting Vulnerable Female and Male Farmers in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:

The project's objectives match the HRP 2023 oPt, Strategic Objective country #(3): The capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. The project will improve the resilience of households and communities to cope with and mitigate shocks and environmental hazards. The three project’s activities are expected to increase support to communities’ livelihoods which in turns will improve the general food security situation and will have a positive effect on their overall nutrition and health status. 

Furthermore, the project is specifically in line with the Food Security Sector (FSS) objective#(1) The resilience of vulnerable households are protected, and their livelihoods, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced. The project will be based on the BBB approach to increase resilience and reduce vulnerability.
The project activities will be implemented throughout the Gaza strip (the five governates). NDC will partner with a locally registered cluster NGO, Palestinian Al Nakheel Association for Progress and Development, who has extensive agricultural experience which makes it to be the most capable one to assist NDC in implementing the project.
NDC will be responsible for the overall management of the project activities, procurement, financial disbursement, monitoring & evaluation, and reporting. In addition, NDC will be responsible for implementing the project activities on the ground in the Gaza and the northern governates. NDC will be also responsible for the formation of the fie local committees, finalizing the beneficiary list in coordination with MoA and the rehabilitation activities. In implementing the project activities, NDC will coordinate with the MoA, FAO, FSS, & INGOs.
