project_name: Projet de renforcement de l'accès aux services EHA dans les zones de déplacement de populations dans la province du Logone Oriental au Tchad
project_objective:
Pour répondre aux besoins identifiés suite à l'évaluation menée dans les deux départements et à l’analyse des données secondaires existantes, SI propose une réponse EHA adaptée au contexte des deux départements et en cohérence avec les actions antérieures conduites. Le projet a pour objectif général de “Contribuer à améliorer l’accès à des infrastructures d’approvisionnement en eau fonctionnelles et durables, tout en participant à la mise en application des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène dans les zones ciblées”. La stratégie de SI se base sur une approche participative et inclusive, à la fois à l’échelle communautaire et à celle des ménages, afin de garantir la pertinence et l'efficience des activités proposées et de contribuer à renforcer la cohésion sociale. La réponse s’articule autour de 3 axes :
I) Améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable au niveau communautaire dans les zones frontalières avec la RCA et le Cameroun
A travers le premier objectif, SI prévoit des interventions communautaires qui contribueront à améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable aux populations par la construction et la réhabilitation de points d’eau. En amont du projet, SI conduira, en coordination avec la Délégation de l’Hydraulique, une cartographie des points d’eau dans les cantons cibles du projet, suivie d’une évaluation technique des besoins en termes de réparation et de construction au niveau des villages cibles. Suite à cette collecte de données, les villages prioritaires seront ciblés pour la construction de Systèmes Villageois d’Adduction d’Eau Potable (SVAEP) ou de pompes à motricité humaine (PMH). Cette action permettra d'améliorer durablement l'accès à l'eau potable pour les communautés, atténuant ainsi les risques de stress hydrique, la flambée des maladies hydriques et de tensions entre communautés qui peuvent être exacerbées par les difficultés d’accès à l'eau.
II) Améliorer durablement les systèmes de gestion des infrastructures en eau
La mise en oeuvre d'une réponse durable implique de promouvoir un processus de gestion communautaire de l'eau, et de s'engager avec les acteurs locaux dans des discussions continues et un partage d'informations sur les questions relatives à la gestion des ressources en eau. SI renforcera ainsi les capacités des comités de gestion des points d'eau (CGPE) et des artisans réparateurs. Ces acteurs seront ensuite dotés en matériel et équipement de gestion et de maintenance des points d’eau pour assurer la durabilité des infrastructures construites/réhabilitées.
III) Améliorer les pratiques d’hygiène des ménages bénéficiaires, en particulier tout au long de la chaine de l'eau
Le troisième objectif du projet est d’améliorer les pratiques d’hygiène des bénéficiaires tout au long de la chaîne de l’eau afin de limiter les risques de contamination et de maladies hydriques. Cet axe sera mis en oeuvre à travers le renforcement de l’accès à des dispositifs d’hygiène et d’assainissement, le suivi de la qualité de l’eau et la sensibilisation des populations aux pratiques d'hygiène. Les messages et modalités de sensibilisation seront identifiés à travers une approche participative, avec pour objectif l’identification des barrières ainsi que les leviers à la mise en oeuvre des pratiques. Ils s’aligneront aux recommandations internationales et nationales. SI s’appuiera également sur les résultats de l’enquête Connaissance, Attitude et Pratique (CAP), qui sera réalisée en début et fin de projet pour évaluer l’évolution des connaissances et pratiques des personnes bénéficiaires et les facteurs motivant l’adoption des pratiques d’hygiène observées. SI mobilisera l’appui de relais communautaires. SI assurera également le suivi de la qualité de l'eau au niveau de tous les points d'eau réhabilités et nouvellement construits ainsi qu'auprès des ménages bénéficiaires. Afin de sécuriser la chaîne de l’eau et de permettre le transport et le stockage de l’eau dans des conditions d’hygiène adéquates, SI distribuera des kits d’articles EHA.

project_name: Amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et de la résilience des populations vulnérables (déplacées, des retournées et hôtes) dans la région de l’Extrême-Nord
project_objective:
Depuis 2014, la région de l’Extrême-Nord fait face à plusieurs crises et choc dont les attaques des Boko-Haram avec des conséquences négatives sur le plan économique, Alimentaire, social et la crise intercommunautaire du Logone Birni occasionnant des dégâts énormes et affectant d’autres départements dont le Mayo-Danay, le Diamaré et le Mayo-Sava. De ce qui précède, s’ajoute le contexte assez particulier des inondations cette année qui a impacté négativement les moyens d’existences des ménages de l’Extrême Nord.
Selon les résultats de l’analyse du Cadre harmonisé d’octobre 2022, en période courante, 786 488 personnes sont en situation d’insécurité alimentaire aigue. En vue d’atténuer cette situation, le secteur sécurité alimentaire se propose de toucher pour l’année 2023, globalement 258 095 personnes. Dans le cadre du présent projet, l’objectif recherché par la FAO est d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et le renforcement de la résilience de 33 864 personnes, représentant environ 4 900 ménages.

project_name: Assistance aux refugiés des régions de Diffa, Maradi, Tahoua  et  Tillabéri à travers le renforcement de leurs moyens d'existence et leur insertion socioéconomique.
project_objective:
Le projet a pour but d’apporter une assistance pour l’autonomisation économique des réfugiés  dans les régions de Diffa, Maradi, Tahoua et Tillabéri. Cette assistance se fera à travers:
- Appui aux activités génératrices de revenus de 4 000  bénéficiaires , principalement  des femmes  (au moins 70%) et des jeunes (au moins 40%) pour l'appui à 4 000 ménages de réfugiés.  : Il est prévu un transfert monétaire (Cash) de 80 000 F CFA par bénéficiaire, pour développer une activité génératrice de revenu (transformation, embouche, pisciculture). Les bénéficiaires seront accompagnés aussi techniquement.  
- Appui à la reconstitution du cheptel : distribution des petits ruminants aux ménages des réfugiés  qui ont perdu leur cheptel ou leur moyen d'existence du fait de la crise sécuritaire. L’objectif est de distribuer des kits de petits ruminants (3 femelles et 1 mâle), incluant un appui initial en aliment bétail et des soins vétérinaires   au profit de 2500 bénéficiaires.  Ce capital bétail joue un rôle important dans l’économie et aussi renforce la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages de réfugiés, qui ont accès limité à la terre.  Les femmes cheffes de ménages seront priorisées ainsi que les ménages ayant des personnes handicapées à leur charge.
- Appui en moyens de production à 3522 ménages réfugiés, disposant d'accès à la terre principalement pour les cultures à cycle court  de contre-saison.  Il s’agit d’une distribution d'outils, semences et accompagnement pour la production agricole en irrigué.

project_name: Ensuring access to skills development and livelihoods opportunities for adolescents and youth in safe environment.
project_objective:
NRC aims to increase socio-economic access of both Rohingya and the host community youth and adolescents by emphasizing on creating self-resilience and livelihood opportunities using training as a key tool. Two modules of market driven training packages will be provided to the beneficiary which will help them to acquire updated skills that aligns with current market needs. The training modules will be continuously upgraded and reviewed through using secondary research thus modules will always be aligned with current market. The first module will focus largely on theoretical and conceptual learning and the second module will focus on practical skills acquisition of the learners. Subject matters such as literacy, numeracy, life skills and business skills will be incorporated along with the 2 modules. Key focus will be on female learners and people of diverse gender groups. NRC will focus on 10 camps. 3% of the overall beneficiaries will be targeted for including persons with disabilities who then will be served as project beneficiaries through referral system. 
There will be trainings for the volunteers and staff specifically focused on inclusion to conduct outreach and referral pathways for persons with disabilities. The referrals will be documented and forwarded to appropriate service providers. On the other way, to materialise the efforts on inclusion and mainstreaming, identified learners with disabilities will be provided customized and appropriate learning pathways based on their needs where physical access also includes. Apart from these, NRC will also include awareness building and sensitization sessions for the inclusion of diverse age group and person with disabilities through including relevant topics in teacher trainings modules and community sessions. NRC will also provide business and employment skills through trainings for all beneficiaries keeping to the needs of the market. Content for this will be cater to the learners in consultation with partners. After the training the semi-skills learners will be put through a re-tooling process where they will get the opportunity to practice and further sharpen these skills and re-learn previously mistaken purposes.  
Participants will also have the access to input in the Youth Working Group advisory meetings promoting youth empowerment through engagement. Youth led community clubs will be created to support this process and will also be promoted DRR activities when needs rise. Moreover, preparedness will also be a core regular part of this activity. Building social cohesion through learning and employment activates for both communities and advocacy initiatives will be integrated with overall education programming that will integrate education programme with NRC’s other core competencies. Education programme will also focus on self and collaborative welling exercise opportunities through community projects that ensure meaningful engagement within peers and community people. 
NRC will implement the proposed activities with the coordination of other humanitarian actors and government as well. NRC will coordinate specifically with local and national government throughout the project cycle by taking feedback, supporting in different emergency situation through preparedness and preventive measures taken by government and involving them in the projects through meetings and field visits.

project_name: Creating a Protective Environment for the People of South Sudan through Safeguarding and Promoting Human Rights and Finding Solutions
project_objective:
In response to identified priority needs of and protection service provision, DRC will deliver this integrated protection (General Protection, HLP, GBV, and Child Protection) project with solutions mainstreamed for conflict and displacement affected communities. The aim is to creating a protective environment for women, men, girls and boys of South through safeguarding, respecting rights and finding solutions. DRC will implement protection activities including in hard to reach locations through both static, outreach and mobile modalities. In doing so DRC aims to contribute to the overarching intersectoral strategic objectives for the 2023 HRP through contributing to the protection cluster strategic objectives too.
The proposed sub-sectors and activities will ensure provision of critical protection related assistance through an integrated approach to address priority needs of targeted communities, women, men, girls and boys in hard-to-reach and priority geographical areas. The project will mainstream durable solutions whilst enhanced protection assessments and monitoring will inform protection and overall humanitarian response. 
DRC also currently has 2 Mobile Protection Teams that respond to emergencies in hard to reach locations where there are limited services and high needs thus under GP. These mobile teams will also provide General Protection services. The target locations are country wide, hard-to-reach and recommended by the Protection Cluster for short response or semi-static response – in coordination with the Cluster. GBV prevention and response activities will be implemented through static and outreach in Unity and Upper Nile State. Child Protection activities by DRC will be implemented through partners focusing but focusing in Jonglei State and Greater Pibor Administrative Area. Proposed activities in this integrated protection project are as follows: 
1.	Protection monitoring, assessments and analysis. This with include safety audits, conflict analysis, and rapid gender and inclusion analysis for the project.  
2.Information Dissemination and Awareness raising on rights, entitlements, assistance opportunities GBV issues, Child protection issues, HLP rights, available services, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA), Peacebuilding issues, etc. 
4.	Strengthening community-based protection structures like women committees, Community Protection Committees, community-based protection networks, Community based child protection structures and networks. 
5.	Comprehensive Case Management (GBV) and (CP) and provision of psychosocial support
6.	Integrated GBV prevention and response with GBV risk mitigation 
7.	Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) in-kind of material or cash.
8.	 Comprehensive Case Management for GBV survivors and Child Survivors. 
9.	Supporting community co-existence, facilitating peacebuilding dialogues, 
10.	Capacity building of staff, partners, and local authorities and leaders on GBV core messages, CPiE, Peacebuilding, ADR, HLP, according to available IASC standards, PSEA Cluster SOPs, DRC tools, among others.
Evidence-based programming and advocacy across the response in will be supported through regular protection monitoring and protection assessments based on pre-identified triggers, with mechanisms to ensure inclusion of persons with specific needs such as persons living with disabilities, older people, young men at risk, adolescent girls at risk, and female headed households.

project_name: Contribution à la réinsertion scolaire des enfants déplacés et des enfants des familles hôtes vulnérables affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la province du Soum
project_objective:
L’intervention proposée vise à adresser à la fois les problèmes d’accès à l’éducation et les problèmes de protection rencontrés dans les écoles. 

L’objectif principal du projet est le suivant : contribuer à renforcer l'accès à l'éducation dans un environnement protecteur pour les enfants affectés par le conflit dans le Soum et plus spécifiquement apporter une réponse intégrée favorisant l'accès à l'éducation dans un cadre protecteur renforcé aux enfants affectés par les déplacements internes et aux enfants à risque de protection des communautés d'accueil dans les communes de Djibo et dans la province du Soum.

L’intervention visera à appuyer directement les élèves par rapport à leurs besoins en matériel scolaire, alternatives éducatives (notamment les cours de rattrapage) mais aussi avec des activités de protection notamment socio-récréatives visant à renforcer le bien-être psychologique des enfants tout en renforçant les liens et le vivre-ensemble. En parallèle, l’intervention renforcera aussi les enseignants et les infrastructures scolaires via de l’appui matériel (table-bancs, classe semi-temporaire, etc.) et du renforcement de capacité en lien avec l’éducation en situation d’urgence mais aussi la protection. En parallèle, l’intervention de DRC contribuera à la coordination et pérennité des activités étant donné qu’un travail rapproché de collaboration sera réalisé en premier lieu avec les partenaires étatiques (ST-ESU, DR et DP de l’éducation sur le terrain) notamment dans le cadre de réflexion stratégique mais aussi dans l’accompagnement des partenaires. De plus, DRC s’appuiera sur les normes d’éducation en situation d’urgence développées par le ST-ESU et le Cluster éducation pour réaliser ses interventions.

Aussi, l’approche proposée par DRC est intégrée combinant des activités de protection, d’éducation et d’eau hygiène et assainissement (appui en kits GHM) favorisant toutes les conditions demandées par le Cluster éducation afin de fournir un accès à l’éducation inclusif, sain et protecteur à l’éducation formelle.

Lors des différentes formations au cours du projet, DRC assurera la présentation d’un module sur le PSEA et les différents mécanismes de remontée d’information à destination des enseignants.

Dans la mise en œuvre des activités, la dimension genre est prise en compte, les cibles sont à chaque fois désagrégées et une équité est fixée entre les filles et les garçons. Pour ce qui est du feedback, deux cadres de concertations sont organisés permettant de recueillir les recommandations des participants/bénéficiaires. Un mécanisme de remontée des plaintes est mis en place par DRC et un rappel sur ce mécanisme est fait aux communautés à chaque rencontre. Elles sont invitées à faire remonter à chaque fois les plaintes et les feedbacks sans aucun risque

9000 enfants des communes d’Arbinda et Djibo bénéficient d’un appui à l’éducation dans les écoles primaires mais aussi post-primaires et secondaires.

Etant donné le contexte actuel, DRC envisage de renforcer l’offre du système informel à Djibo à travers des CBN qui constituent des alternatives éducatives qui permettent aux enfants de continuer à bénéficier de l’éducation si la situation de l’accès aux vivres se stabilise. Le contexte très volatile du Soum, et l’absence de certains leaders communautaires et services publics ne permettent pas mettre en œuvre des activités dans une perspective stratégique de Nexus. Néanmoins, DRC continuera à suivre l’évolution de la situation pour adapter sa stratégie le cas échéant.

En effet, actuellement, pour la mise en œuvre des alternatives éducatives, DRC compte lier un partenariat stratégique avec Tin-tua qui dispose d’énormes expertises sur les CBN.  Tin-tua va dérouler les aspects techniques et opérationnelles liés aux renforcements de capacités des animateurs, des superviseurs ainsi que le suivi.

project_name: Provision of integrated, equitable, and timely WASH services to emergency affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
Protracted crises in South Sudan, including climactic shocks and continued conflict, have resulted in 8.9 million people projected to be in need of humanitarian assistance in 2022. As a result of the shocks, such as flooding, inter-communal violence (ICV) and ongoing armed clashes, the majority of the population are facing increased food insecurity, lack of access to basic services, and protection risks. As per the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in South Sudan will negatively impact an estimated 6.1 million people in 2022. 

Since 2006, Solidarites International has become a key WASH actor in South Sudan, implementing emergency lifesaving responses across the country and providing integrated WASH services to crisis-affected populations in areas of static presence in Upper Nile, Jonglei, and Western Bahr el Ghazal. Since 2012 SI has played a key role in the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) strategy in South Sudan, implementing multi-sectoral assessments and delivering emergency responses to crisis-affected populations all over the country. 

In 2022, SI will continue to provide emergency live-saving  WASH responses across the South Sudan to restore basic access to safe water, hygiene, and sanitation while ensuring equitable access, safety, and accountability to supported populations. Through its roving Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) team, SI will deploy to emergency-affected locations to provide first phase and second phase responses including distribution of household water treatment items and soap, emergency provision of safe water, and rapid repair of emergency-affected infrastructure.

At the same time, SI will expand its presence in Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei to provide basic integrated WASH services that target the most vulnerable, including those suffering malnutrition, food insecurity and protection threats (including GBV survivors). Static programs will focus on providing community-based solutions for sustainable WASH services that ensure that improvements in access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene are durable and can be maintained independently by communities. Engagement and joint programming with Protection and Nutrition actors will ensure that WASH services can be accessed by the most vulnerable and will have a tangible impact on reducing overall priority humanitarian needs. The increased integration of protection, inclusion, and conflict sensitivity analysis in all programming will ensure that WASH services and resources can be safely accessed by all in the community. Greater engagement of communities and local markets will support the design of long term and flood resistant WASH infrastructure and supply chains to ensure that interventions produce durable results for communities.

project_name: Strengthening Food security and Livelihoods for IDPs, Host community in Sudan
project_objective:
West Darfour, White Nile and Blue Nile States depend largely on agricultural production for household food security and livelihoods. Low farmer capacity, poorly functioning market systems, increased climate related shocks and stresses, and decades of insecurity, continue to stunt agricultural production and drive households to face food insecurity. Limited access to climate-smart improved inputs, financial services and technical skills training, further undermine potential agricultural production for the target areas. Medium to large-sized farms are beginning to benefit from growing irrigation schemes, government and private sector financial services, and access to improved inputs, however smallholder farmers remain marginalised. This market marginalisation, coupled with a high dependence on agriculture, increases farmers’ vulnerability to social, economic, and environmental shocks and stressors, directly impacting household livelihoods and food security. 

ADRA, seek to tackle this dynamic, with a goal to improve food security for 323,550 male and female smallholder farmer households through enhanced gender equitable market access and agricultural production. The Project, will strengthen the capacities of key market actors, contributing to improved resilience capacities to shocks and stresses. The Project is guided by a Market Systems Development (MSD) approach, in addition to ADRA’s resilience approach, to sustain food security gains despite the complex risk environment in which smallholder farmers are exposed to. The Project is centred around four key objectives:

Objective 1: Male and female smallholder farmers have increased and more climate resilient yields: Agricultural production yields and a household’s food security are closely linked for smallholder farmers. With limited alternative livelihood opportunities, smallholder farmers face a cycle of poor inputs, variable yields and low profit margins, all greatly influenced by environmental, economic, and political shocks and stresses. The Project will disrupt this cycle through knowledge building, access to climate-smart inputs and market oriented investments contributing to increased yields among 197514 male and female smallholder farmer households. 

Objective 2: Male and female smallholder farmers increase sustainable natural resource management practices: Poor agricultural practices, coupled with increased climate related shocks and stresses (droughts, flooding, wind), have stripped soil nutrients, increased soil erosion, and contributed to poor agricultural yields. Household and communal level natural resource management plans are greatly needed for smallholder farmers to navigate this dynamic. Through the introduction of Community Action Plans, alongside strategic investments in resilient building infrastructure, the Project will empower communities to actively manage individual and communal natural resources, helping to mitigate environmental shocks and stresses. 

Objective 3: Male and female smallholder farmers have improved market linkages: Poorly functioning markets are detrimental to a community’s income generation potential. Market actors, including financial service providers, input agents, transporters, and end buyers, reflect a market dynamic that supports investment and long-term economic growth. The Project will focus on increasing market linkages across key agricultural value chains, increasing access to key goods and services and end markets, subsequently increasing investments to help drive production yields. 

Objective 4: Increased equality between men, women, boys and girls and increased empowerment of women and girls in smallholder agricultural market systems: Gender dynamics play a critical role in resource allocation, decision making and the long-term economic well-being of a household. the Project will tackle this through proven approaches, helping to drive increased gender equity and empowerment within households and the larger communities

project_name: Fournir une réponse d’urgence intégrés aux besoins en sécurité alimentaire, Abris/AME et Wash des populations déplacées et hôtes de la province du Lac au Tchad
project_objective:
Le Tchad compte 2022 environ 17,1 millions d’habitants avec 50,7% femmes et 49,3% hommes. Le Tchad est le deuxième pays au monde le plus touché par l’insécurité alimentaire (il est classé 118ème sur 119 pays dans l'indice de la faim dans le monde). Le Tchad est classé à la 186ème place sur 189 sur l'Indice de Développement Humain de 2018, présentant un niveau de pauvreté élevé (46,7%) avec environ 2,4 millions de Tchadiens (soit 15,5%) dans l’extrême pauvreté (ECOSIT4). 
Selon le HRP 2022, le Tchad est confronté à des problématiques humanitaires persistantes liées à l’insécurité croissante, ainsi qu’aux défis socio-économiques, sanitaires et climatiques dans un contexte de transition politique. L’exposition aux effets du changement climatique, l’ampleur des violences perpétrées par des groupes armés dans la région du bassin du lac Tchad, la fragilité de la situation sécuritaire dans les pays limitrophes et les conflits intercommunautaires dans un contexte de sous-développement pérennisent la situation humanitaire au Tchad. Plus d’un million de personnes sont en situation de déplacement, dont 524 417 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile, 406 573 personnes déplacées internes, 119 121 retournés tchadiens et 26 937 retournés anciens déplacés. Ces personnes sont réparties dans les provinces du Lac, de l’Est, du Nord et du Sud du pays. La province du Lac compte un déplacement cumulatif de 457 948 personnes dont 406 573 Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI), 22 112 personnes qui étaient PDI sont retournées dans leurs localités d’origine. L’insécurité alimentaire affectera plus de 5,3 millions de personnes (51% de femmes) parmi lesquelles 1,8 personnes souffrent d’insécurité alimentaire sévères (phase 3 et plus du Cadre harmonisé de novembre 2021) et 3,6 personnes sont dans la phase sous pression (phase 2). Cette situation résulte de la baisse de production agricole dont la production céréalière de 1,5% accentuée dans la zone soudanienne (3,3%), le tarissement des eaux de surfaces dans la partie sahélienne et une faible disponibilité dans la partie soudanienne affectant le pâturage. La hausse de prix des céréales et la détérioration des termes de l’échange bétail/céréales et cultures de rente/céréales affectent également la consommation alimentaire, l’état nutritionnel et l’évolution des moyens d’existence. La malnutrition reste préoccupante au Tchad avec une prévalence de 10,9% de malnutrition aigüe globale et 2% de malnutrition aigüe sévère. 
Parallèlement, l'accès à l'eau potable au Tchad est faible et inégalement réparti sur le territoire avec une moyenne de 61,8% (HNO, 2022) et 52% dans la province du Lac où 108 907 personnes se trouvent actuellement dans le besoin. Les femmes et les enfants sont particulièrement touchés par le manque d’accès à l’eau potable mettant souvent leur santé en danger, causant en moyenne des milliers de décès chez les enfants. Selon le plan cadre de nation unies d’assistance au développement, UNDAF, Tchad 2017-2021, près de 19 000 personnes décèdent chaque année de maladies liées au manque d´accès à l´eau potable et aux mauvaises conditions d´hygiène et d´assainissement. Pour répondre à ces besoins, le Plan de réponse humanitaire cible 3,9 millions de personnes parmi les 6,1 millions de personnes ayant besoin d'aide humanitaire d'urgence pour un financement requis de 510,9 millions de dollars US.

Face à ces situations, Help-Tchad propose des actions orientées vers trois (03) secteurs primordiaux dont la sécurité alimentaire, l’Abris/AME et le Wash intégrant les activités préventives au COVID 19. Ces actions visent à répondre aux besoins urgents alimentaires, non alimentaires et en Wash des personnes affectées par les mouvements des populations dans les Départements de Fouli, Kaya, Mamdi et Wayi.
Il est en accord avec l’objectif Stratégique 1.1 de HRP 2022 « Fournir une assistance rapide, intégrée et coordonnée aux personnes vulnérables en situation d’urgence, nécessaire à leur survie et adaptée à leurs besoins.

project_name: Emergency Child Protection Services Provision Among Conflict and Floods Affected Vulnerable Girls and Boys in Aweil East, Pibor, Rubkona, Mayendit, Leer, Panyijiar and Koch Counties
project_objective:
The 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview indicated at least 4.6 million children (0-17 years) (girls and boys), are at risk of violence, exploitation, abuse, and neglect and in acute need of immediate child protection. Protracted conflict compounded by prevalent cyclical waves of intercommunal violence, revenge killings, children and women abduction including forceful recruitments and cattle related fighting in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar, Rubkona, Aweil East and Pibor, continue to negatively impact vulnerable populations, particularly among girls and boys who have witnessed various atrocities and at risk of post-traumatic stress disorder, depression and anxiety disorders. This has been coupled with loss of friends and family members further affecting mental health and emotional development of children, further exacerbated by the COVID-19 outbreak with only 2 percent of south Sudan’s having been fully vaccinated (Humanitarian Needs Overview, 2022).


These have been further exacerbated by recurrent yearly flooding extremes (2018, 2019, 2022 and 2022) that have affected at least 1 million people as at November 2022 (Flooding Situation Updates, 2022); with worse affected counties including Unity state and Northern Bahr el Ghazal. This coupled with unprecedented food insecurity levels; with children (boys and girls), men and women with disabilities facing greater challenges to access services. COVID 19 related economic pressures have further contributed to negative coping strategies including child labour and early and forced marriages (UNICEF, 2022; IPC November 2022) in addition to increasing cases of both forceful and voluntary recruitment of children, with recent reports in Unity (UNMISS, 2022). 

Most vulnerable and displaced populations’ needs are further worsened by protection concerns including GBV and sexual exploitation and abuse, predominantly among girls and women with an uptick in cases of GBV cases in 2021; which are often under-reported due to stigma and lack of legal assistance. Women and girls continue to face increased risks of harassment, assault and sexual violence, early marriages with estimated that 52% of girls are married between the age of 15 and 18 (Child Rights Coalition, 2016), poor rule of law which continues to prevent perpetrators from being held accountable for violations.

Proposed project which will target 20,000 beneficiaries comprised of 2000 men, 2000 women, 8000 boys and 8000 girls including people with special needs/ disabilities. Proposed initiatives, which in line key Child Protection Sub Cluster objectives: Vulnerable and at risk girls,  boys, men and women  including  children with disabilities have improved access to quality lifesaving  child protection; and Reduce the suffering of boys , girls , women and men including children with disabilities who are at risk or experience violence , abuse ,exploitation and neglect  including GBV through provision of  specialized/lifesaving child protection and multi sectoral  services.

Proposed action will respond to the critical child protection needs via child rights and child protection awareness, including strengthened psychosocial support, case management and strengthening community based child protection networks including families to prevent and respond to violence against children and other protection concerns including recruitment and use of children in armed forces and groups, family tracing and re-unification, child protection response monitoring, support and referrals among others. These initiatives will ensure COVID 19 mitigation measures in line with the ministry of health/ WHO guidelines including advocacy for COVID vaccine uptake. The project will ensure quality programming, inter-cluster synergies, Accountability to Affected Populations, regular context analysis and advocacy on environmental conservation, ensuring conflict sensitive programming by upholding Do No Harm ethos.

project_name: Access to safe, condential and timely life-saving services for survivors of Gender Based Violence (GBV) in vulnerable, ethnic populations in conict affected departments, during COVID-19 pandemic / Access to life-saving sexual and reproductive health services for women in reproductive age
project_objective:
El proyecto del UNFPA está dirigido a mujeres y niñas en edad reproductiva, mujeres embarazadas y sobrevivientes de violencia de género. El proyecto ayudará principalmente a mujeres y niñas indígenas y afrodescendientes con necesidades humanitarias críticas como consecuencia del conflicto armado que incrementó los niveles de violencia de género (VBG), en particular la violencia sexual, la violencia de pareja íntima (VPI) y la pandemia COVID-19 en zonas remotas y semiurbanas sin una respuesta estatal eficaz, con escasa, nula presencia o baja capacidad de establecimientos de salud y servicios multisectoriales de VG.

El proyecto tiene como objetivo garantizar servicios integrados de SSR/VG, particularmente 
1) Fortalecer la respuesta multisectorial que salve vidas; 
2) Reducir la
violencia de género y los riesgos de SSR; 
3) Reducir la mortalidad materna y 4). Reducir
los embarazos no planeados y otros daños a la salud sexual y reproductiva. 

Esto se logrará mediante cuatro productos que, en conjunto, forman un enfoque holístico e integrado de la protección y la salud, en VBG, se espera que i) Las sobrevivientes de VG tengan acceso a una respuesta integral a las necesidades y a servicios multisectoriales que salvan vidas (salud, apoyo psicosocial, protección) a través de la gestión de casos de VG y que iv) Las mujeres y las niñas hayan fortalecido los mecanismos de protección y mitigación de riesgos contra la VG.

Los servicios y suministros de SSR y VG se proporcionarán principalmente a través de equipos móviles en áreas rurales y espacios seguros en zonas urbanas. Con respecto a la respuesta a la violencia de género, seguirá el Marco de rendición de cuentas de la violencia de género y los estándares mínimos de la violencia de género con un enfoque centrado en las sobrevivientes que responda a la necesidad de fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta directa multisectorial a la violencia de género, incluidos los establecimientos de salud (Gestión Clínica de la Violación), otras instituciones de protección y autoridades indígenas. Con equipos de protección se brindará Manejo de Casos de VBG y Apoyo Psicosocial, incluida la distribución de efectivo incondicional de emergencia para sobrevivientes de VG y kits de dignidad contextualizados a las necesidades locales
específicas adaptadas a la pandemia de COVID-19 y sensibles para la población indígena.

Además, se establecerán espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas para promover la protección y el empoderamiento de las mujeres enfocándose en la mitigación del riesgo de VG a través de la distribución de información que salve vidas para grupos de mujeres / comunidades en las áreas más vulnerables.

project_name: Recuperación rápida de alimentos y medios de vida esenciales para la subsistencia de comunidades afectadas por conflicto, desastres asociados al clima, crisis sociales y eventos de salud pública.
project_objective:
El proyecto busca favorecer la producción rápida de alimentos y de cultivos de ciclo corto y la resiliencia frente a múltiples amenazas (conflicto armado, desastres) de las comunidades rurales vulnerables, instituciones locales de 10 departamentos Chocó,  Putumayo, Nariño, Cesar, Sucre, Córdoba, La Guajira, San Andrés, Antioquia y  Cauca e instituciones del Gobierno (MADR, UARIV, DPS, ADR y UNGRD) como aporte a los esfuerzos previstos en planes de respuesta a emergencias, crisis y desastres relacionadas con diversos riesgos:

-Implementar sistemas de producción rápida de alimentos con comunidades vulnerables y en coordinación con las instituciones locales, como medida específica para favorecer la recuperación e incrementar el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia frente a múltiples amenazas. La producción de alimentos se plantea como una salvaguarda que incrementa la capacidad de las poblaciones afectadas para afrontar las crisis y contribuye a la protección física de personas y comunidades afectadas, reduciendo las medidas negativas de afrontamiento y mejorando la resiliencia.

project_name: Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)-Rohingiya Community
project_objective:
To strengthen resilience of the Rohingya /FDMN population, WFP will be supporting most vulnerable peoples through engaging participatory DRR activities which are able to meet basic food support and part of emergency preparedness. Through this project WFP will  cover 33 camps including 02 Register camps targetting around 79,537 beneficiaries. 
WFP cash for work activities will engage at least 25% women and 5% PwD within safeguards and a do no harm approach. The proposed projects will consider Structural interventions (Access, drainage, slope stabilization etc),  Reforestation/Plantation, Waste Management/Drain Cleaning, Emergency Response/Cash for Workers/Porters.

project_name: Contribuir a las acciones de construcción de paz y respuesta a emergencias derivadas del conflicto armado desde Salud como eje articulador de derecho.
project_objective:
La estrategia de respuesta se encuentra enmarcada en el HRP 2023 que se está construyendo en conjunto con otros actors y sectores, respondiendo principalmente a dos objetivos que se han establecido para Colombia: Contribuir a la disminución de los indíces de morbilidad y mortalidad evitables a traves del acceso efectivo a servicios esenciales de salud por parte de las poblaciónes afectadas por emergencias y situaciones de violencia y a reforzar las capacidades comunitarias para promover la atención primaria en salud, la primera respuesta, la vigilancia epidemiologica y la participación activa en la toma de decisiones referente a los temas de salud.

En este sentido la estrategia está orientada en proteger y salvar vidas apoyando y ampliando las capacidades locales de coordinación, preparación, respuesta y monitoreo en salud para atender las necesidades urgentes e insatisfechas de la población vulnerable impactada por situaciones de emergencias súbitas y prolongadas, con énfasis en los territorios rurales y con poco o nulo acceso a las instituciones de salud que fueron consideradas en mayor necesidad (Choco, Arauca, Antioquia, Norte de Santander, Guainía, Vichada, Amazonas, Guajira, Nariño, Putumayo, Cauca y Casanare)  Considerando la multiplicidad de emergencias humanitarias en Colombia y la diversidad de las dinámicas regionales, es clave promover la entrega de asistencia humanitaria en salud integral en las áreas geográficas priorizadas y a las poblaciones priorizadas. Los esfuerzos deben dirigirse a apoyar la preparación, coordinación y prestación de servicios de salud a las comunidades más vulnerables de forma complementaria a los servicios ofrecidos por las instituciones estatales para garantizar una atención integral, incluyendo i ) La atención primaria de salud; ii) la salud sexual y reproductiva (SSR); iii) la atención a las enfermedades crónicas no transmisibles (ENT); iv) la salud mental; v) el apoyo a la vacunación general y a la COVID-19; y vii) la atención a la violencia de género.

Así mismo es importante asistir a las autoridades sanitarias locales para las acciones colectivas de salud pública, incluyendo la vigilancia epidemiológica, y el fortalecimiento de las capacidades comunitarias en materia de salud preventiva y detección temprana de eventos importantes de salud pública. Considerando la diversidad cultural del país y el impacto desproporcionado de las emergencias humanitarias en los grupos étnicos, son claves los enfoques diferenciales e interculturales que involucren a los expertos ancestrales, a las parteras tradicionales y a los agentes comunitarios en la provisión de atención indirecta. Reconociendo y valorando la responsabilidad del Estado de garantizar la protección de las personas, como primer respondiente en una emergencia, la OMS también continuará fortaleciendo mecanismos efectivos que permitan una mejor articulación y la coordinación eficiente de los múltiples actores humanitarios de salud en el país.

project_name: Apoyo  a la Coordinación Humanitaria en las regiones más afectadas por minas antipersonal (MAP), Municiones sin Explosionar (MSE) y otros artefactos explosivos improvisados (AEI)  en Colombia (15 departamentos)
project_objective:
UNMAS continuará brindando asistencia y coordinación al sector de la acción integral contra minas (AICMA) en Colombia, a través de su participación activa en el Clúster de Protección como líder del Área de Responsabilidad de Acción contra Minas (AdR), con resultados que contribuirán a los objetivos estratégicos del Clúster de Protección y aquellos identificados en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria (HRP) 2023 para Colombia. Como miembro de foros de coordinación clave a nivel nacional y local, como el Equipo País de las Naciones Unidas (UNCT), el Equipo Humanitario País (HCT), el Grupo Inter-Cluster, el Grupo Temático de Gestión de Información, el Grupo de Acceso Humanitario, los Grupos Temáticos de Protección y Equipos Locales de Coordinación, a través de este proyecto, UNMAS continuará promoviendo la AICMA como facilitadora en el triple nexo (acción humanitaria, desarrollo, paz) y facilitará la coordinación entre la AICMA, las actores humanitarias, de consolidación de la paz y de desarrollo a nivel nacional y local. 

Este proyecto permitirá a UNMAS continuar implementando estas actividades, con un énfasis especial en la coordinación humanitaria y la protección por presencia. El proyecto enfocará sus intervenciones de coordinación AICMA en los 15 departamentos mas afectados por artefactos explosivos (Antioquia, Arauca, Caquetá, Cauca, Chocó, Córdoba, Guaviare, Huila, Meta, Nariño, Norte de Santander, Putumayo, Santander, Tolima y Valle del Cauca), donde se reportaron el 100% del total de víctimas registradas en 2021 y 2022, y donde reside el 89% de las personas con necesidad (PiN) de asistencia humanitaria de AICMA, identificadas en el HNO 2023 por el AdR AcM.

A través del despliegue de coordinadores humanitarios regionales en el territorio y el liderazgo del coordinador de AdR AcM, UNMAS coordinará la AICMA con el sistema humanitario nacional y local, y nutrirá el ciclo de programación humanitaria, asegurando que el impacto negativo que tiene la presencia de artefactos explosivos en las comunidades este plasmado adecuadamente en el HNO y el HRP. UNMAS también promoverá la protección de los derechos humanos a través de la promoción y la coordinación de la respuesta humanitaria de AICMA, identificando y manteniendo registros de los riesgos, vulnerabilidades y causas de la protección. UNMAS colaborará y abogará con actores involucrados y donantes para maximizar el impacto con los recursos financieros disponibles. UNMAS también coordinará la respuesta a las emergencias y trabajará con otros actores humanitarios y de desarrollo para identificar y llevar soluciones sostenibles a las comunidades más afectadas.

Con la asistencia de emergencia de Educación en el Riesgo de Minas (ERM), proporcionada por un socio implementador, UNMAS tendrá como objetivo proteger a las comunidades más afectadas por la presencia de artefactos explosivos en situaciones de emergencia. El proyecto propuesto brindará una respuesta humanitaria en emergencias repentinas a través de orientación a los sobrevivientes, sus familias y las comunidades afectadas sobre cómo acceder a la ruta estatal de atención a víctimas. Además, se proporcionarán sesiones de ERM a las comunidades afectadas en situaciones de emergencia, y a los grupos de trabajo de la arquitectura humanitaria nacionales y locales, a las autoridades locales y otros actores para aumentar su conciencia y conocimiento en AICMA, lo que les permitirá responder de manera efectiva y segura a las emergencias y necesidades derivadas de la contaminación por artefactos explosivos en el país. 
Además, el proyecto apoyará el fortalecimiento de la articulación de la AICMA con otras políticas públicas como los Planes de Desarrollo con Enfoque Territorial (PDET) -objetivo del Acuerdo de Paz de 2016, el Programa Nacional de Sustitución de Cultivos de Uso Ilícito, la Política de Víctimas y Restitución de Tierras y la Política de Formalización de la Propiedad Rural.

project_name: Provision of emergency nutrition services and support optimum early childhood development to crisis affected pregnant and lactating women and children aged below 5 years among vulnerable Lebanese and migrants in Lebanon.
project_objective:
With Growing triple burden of malnutrition (undernutrition, both stunting and wasting; deficiencies in vitamins and other micronutrients; and overweight and obesity) among women, children and adolescents which affects health, growth and development. 
70% of young children are not exclusively breastfed; 90% of children aged 6-23 months lack dietary diversity and meal frequency; over 40% of all women and children, including Lebanese, are affected by anaemia. In October 2021, 53% of children skipped a meal due to insufficient food in the house, up from 37% just 6 months before. 453,000 Lebanese women and children need urgent nutritional support.
Nutrition and child development should be prioritized as part of the emergency response plan, hence UNICEF will be working under the ERP appeal through a multi-system approach from food, health, social protection, education and water and sanitation systems to protect and promote adequate diets, practices and services to prevent all forms of malnutrition among children and women and support optimum early childhood development. In 2021, the percentage of childcare service providers encountering families with payment difficulties has doubled, reaching 41%.  Additionally, due to the local currency devaluation and the significant increase in fuel prices, the monthly fees per child are no longer sufficient to cover the operational expenses of childcare providers. Therefore, to remain affordable, childcare providers are often constrained to compromise on quality which can negatively affect the healthy development of children, while children in rural areas, camps or informal settlements have little access to ECD.
Building on this momentum of a strengthened enabling environment for nutrition and child development, UNICEF will work with the government and partners to reach the most vulnerable children and women with an essential service package for prevention, early detection, referral, and management of all forms of malnutrition and development delays. Maternal and child nutrition during the first 1,000 days coupled with a nurturing care framework – from conception to age 2 years – remains core to the response.
This will be done by strengthening national capacity across multiple sectors and systems through better evidence, policies, and facility and community-based solutions and programmes.

project_name: Provision of actionable information on population movement and evolving needs to inform evidence-based humanitarian and early recovery programming
project_objective:
The complex and dynamic humanitarian context in South Sudan requires accurate, triangulated, timely and readily accessible information. This project aims to provide the humanitarian community with well analysed and actionable data to fill existing and anticipated information gaps on displacement, returns, and general population movement across South Sudan and inform a fair and evidence-based humanitarian response delivery and early recovery programming. The main deliverables will include:
- A regularly updated IDPs and returnees baseline at location and area level. Information will include population presence, movement reasons, and needs of IDPs and returnees.
- Providing regular information on sudden displacement and return movements requiring humanitarian assistance through IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) event tracking mechanism.
- Biometric data management for accountable, effective, and targeted delivery of humanitarian assistance.
- Representative Inter-Sectoral Needs Assessment (ISNA) on the household level to provide information on needs, vulnerabilities, and intentions to feed into South Sudan’s Humanitarian Response Planning (HRP) and Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO).
- Regular updates on population mobility at border points and key internal transit hubs, including displacement sites, through DTM’s flow monitoring mechanism.

project_name: Common Transport Services for Humanitarian Partners in South Sudan
project_objective:
The Common Transport Services (CTS) is a free-for-user service that transports key
humanitarian supplies on behalf of humanitarian actors. CTS serves as a critical link in
the supply chain, enabling products and materials that arrive from regional and
international suppliers to move onwards to partners located deep in the field rapidly. IOM
has been managing the CTS on behalf of the Logistics Cluster since 2011. During this
time, the project has significantly grown from delivering 2,000 MT of humanitarian cargo
in 2011 to a total of 17000 MT by the end of 2021, making a yearly average of 25000 MT
since the beginning, highlighting the increase in the use of road transport as the most
cost-efficient mode of transportation as access improves. IOM has continued to maintain
flexibility and adaptability to the operating environment in South Sudan. Through CTS,
IOM works with more than 100 unique agencies in key operational locations in Jonglei,
Unity, and Greater Upper Nile Region, in Humanitarian Logistics Hubs (Malakal, Bentiu),
and Rumbek, Bor, Juba, and Wau. IOM will maintain heavy vehicles and transport cargo
from the main ports of dispatch via air, road, and river including LC beyond responses and
will continue support for common warehouse management in key operational locations.
Through the effective management of the CTS, IOM aims to support organizations'
preparedness measures to mitigate risks associated with increased insecurity,
looting/theft of humanitarian supplies, critical access impediments to vulnerable people,
and reduce expensive air and road transport costs, which ultimately supports the timely
response to the needs of the affected populations. With this funding, IOM will directly
work with 100 plus humanitarian organizations located in different areas, enabling them
to deliver critical life-saving humanitarian services and assistance items.

project_name: Livelihood support to vulnerable rural households across the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger in partnership with UAWC (Union of Agricultural Work Committees), 
will combine their technical experience and well-established presence in local 
communities to provide livelihood support to vulnerable households across 3 
governorates of the Gaza Strip (North Gaza, Gaza and Middle Area). 
The intervention aims to support rural and vulnerable households, enabling them to cope 
with the severe effects of the protracted conflict, including the most recent economic 
impact brought by the pandemic and Ukraine crisis, by strengthening and protecting their 
livelihoods and improving their food security levels. This intervention was developed to 
contribute to the achievement of HRP Strategic Objective 3 (SO3) “The capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”; and in alignment with two of the HRP 2023 Food Security Sector (FSS) objectives: (O1) Livelihoods of vulnerable households are protected, and their resilience, food security and productive capacity restored/enhanced; (O2) Households suffering from limited of access to food and to income opportunities can meet their basic food needs; and is aligned to the strategic priorities of the Ministry of Agriculture. 

AAH and UAWC intend to support and restore the rural livelihoods of 952vulnerable 
individuals whose income relies on agricultural and breeding activities. These individuals 
and their livelihoods are threatened by the rapidly degrading economic context in Gaza 
Strip which has compromised their capacity to access, repair and maintain their key 
productive assets. Furthermore, the project proposes the rehabilitation of key 
infrastructures to guarantee access to water for farmers, such as wells and ponds, and 
equip them with solar systems to reduce the costs of energy and avoid disruption in the 
irrigation processes. In addition, the action will support 560 individuals, characterized by 
high socioeconomic vulnerabilities and lack of access to economic resources, by enrolling 
them in a cash for work program that will allow them to meet the basic needs. The target criteria in the different activities will seek to prioritize female headed HH, women involved in the production processes and youths as much as possible to empower them in fulfilling their critical role in rural livelihoods.

The intervention foresees a combined approach of cash and in-kind support, to guarantee 
both self-reliance of the recipients and quality of the implementation. In-kind modality will 
be adopted for the rehabilitation of assets, such as water wells, ponds, animals’ shelters; 
while conditional cash will be provided to access production inputs and equipment. 
 
The proposed intervention ensures protection mainstreaming as it is guided by protection principles and considers safety and dignity; meaningful access; accountability to affected population (AAP) as well as participation and empowerment.

project_name: Project Title: 	Projet de réponse d’urgence multisectorielle et de relèvement des populations déplacées, réfugiées et hôtes dans le bassin du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Le consortium présent prévoit fournir une assistance multisectorielle d’urgence auprès de 39 311 bénéficiaires ciblés affectées par les crises au Tchad, principalement les femmes, les jeunes et les personnes porteuses de handicap dans le Bassin du Lac Tchad qui sont souvent exposés aux risques de protection et peu pris en considération dans les instances de décisions de leurs communautés et les accompagnera dans leur transition vers le relèvement en prenant en compte leurs besoins spécifiques. Les bénéficiaires seront les déplacés, réfugiés, retournés issus de mouvement de populations appuyés par le RRM ainsi que les communautés hôtes vulnérables et l’intervention sera inclusive et permettra une analyse détaillée des lacunes en matière d’accès aux services et infrastructures en fonction du sexe, âge, statut, vulnérabilité des bénéficiaires de l’assistance. Le projet bénéficiera à la communauté tout entière et on peut néanmoins envisager à plus de 300 000 personnes selon les zones choisies, les besoins identifiés et la population locale.
Les secteurs couverts par l’intervention sont : la sécurité alimentaire, la nutrition et la protection pour permettre aux bénéficiaires ciblés de sortir de l’extrême vulnérabilité pour ensuite s’orienter vers des activités de résilience. Le consortium axe l’entièreté de sa réponse dans le respect de l’environnement et en prenant en compte le changement climatique auquel est fortement confronté la zone ciblée. L’approche est centrée sur le respect des droits fondamentaux des populations afin de répondre à la crise dans le bassin du lac Tchad qui est le résultat d’une combinaison complexe de multiples facteurs, y compris les conflits armés, le niveau extrême de pauvreté, un sous-développement qui persiste et des bouleversements climatiques. Ainsi, ACTED et son partenaire APSELPA, travailleront avec les communautés de déplacés pour fournir une assistance complémentaire et dans le sillage de la réponse RRM pendant 6 à 9 mois qui visera à (i) compléter/apporter une réponse Post-RRM, (ii) augmenter les capacités individuelles et locales de protection, (iii) renforcer l’autonomie des ménages les plus vulnérables (indépendamment de leur statut) et de contribuer à leur offrir des moyens de subsistance durables.
Une analyse environnementale interne sera réalisée quant aux activités prévues afin d’identifier les éléments de mitigation à apporter pour limiter l’impact environnemental de l’action, tout en optant pour des solutions durables par exemple dans la mise en place d’infrastructures durables, avec énergie solaire notamment. Cette approche se veut mobile et flexible pour suivre les interventions du RRM dont ACTED est membre au Tchad et ainsi opérationnaliser le triple nexus en (i) accompagnant sur une durée plus longue certains des ménages les plus vulnérables du RRM tout en (ii) favorisant la cohésion sociale et (iii) en renforçant les capacités locales de réponse aux chocs.
Le principal objectif de ce projet sera de fournir une assistance multisectorielle d’urgence auprès des personnes affectées par les crises dans le Bassin du Lac Tchad et accompagner leur transition vers le relèvement du Tchad. 
Les objectifs spécifiques seront les suivantes :
OS1 – Renforcer la réponse alimentaire d’urgence auprès des déplacés et favoriser l’accès aux moyens d’existence sur le long terme pour les personnes vulnérables des zones ciblées ;
OS2 – Renforcer la situation nutritionnelle via l’amélioration de l’accès aux services de base des populations vulnérables ;
OS3 - Permettre aux populations ciblées de vivre dans un environnement protecteur ;
OS4 – Renforcement de capacité de l'ONG nationale partenaire ;
OS5- Crisis modifier.

Durée du projet : 12 mois
Février 2023 à janvier 2024
Budget 3 841 464 de livres sterling

Le projet prévoit de cibler un total de 39 311  bénéficiaires.

project_name: Improving access to essential health services among vulnerable migrants and host communities in Lebanon
project_objective: This project aims to support vulnerable individuals overcome barriers to accessing healthcare in Lebanon, while also supporting Lebanon’s ailing health system against pressures linked to deteriorating economic conditions and against the continued challenges by different health outbreaks. The project will provide essential health services across the continuum of care. This will include secondary health care and advanced diagnostics, building the capacity of health care workers, community health support through community-based interventions, and support to POEs in response to health emergencies. All interventions will be closely coordinated with MOPH, WHO, the Health and Migrant sectors, and active partners. The project will support migrants’ safe and equitable access to secondary healthcare based on lifesaving, and limb saving criteria, by contracting two hospitals in migrant dense areas, where IOM will be fully covering the hospitalization bill of migrants. This activity will be done through an implementing partner, building on previous cooperation with SAMs, and will involve other local NGOs active in secondary healthcare support. Advanced diagnostic for migrants and vulnerable communities will be supported through the selection of PHCs providing these services and based on migrant dense areas. A network of community mobilizers selected from the catchment area of the PHCs, will be engaged in accordance with the sector guidance and equipped with the necessary trainings and materials to deliver quality, integrated health messaging and link beneficiaries to the available health services. IOM will work in close cooperation with a network of Migrant community leaders and engage them in trainings and awareness raising activities, in addition to, the translation of awareness materials to different migrant languages. Translation will help overcome language barriers to knowledge and accessibility of health services. Under the response to outbreak section, Building on IOM’s active work with the national international health regulation “IHR” focal point to assess the POE’s in regard to health emergency prevention and response measures and the gaps identified, IOM will support 5 key POEs: Masnaa, Qaa, Aboudiyeh, Aarida, Bokayaa. IOM will strengthen MoPH capacity at the said POEs through deployment of health staff where needed, in addition to the development and implementation of relevant emergency response plans and a training of trainers for non-health actors. IPC trainings for all frontliners are planned and supported under the C19RM successful application, that will be channeled through the Middle East Response funded by Global Fund which IOM is the primary recipient. Building on IOM’s successful experience and the request of multiple partners and noting that many partners are new to migrant programming, IOM aims to provide a cultural sensitization training to health care workers. The main objective is to render the services migrant friendly and accessible to this vulnerable group.

project_name: Enhancing community support and ensuring access to specialized services and protection for migrant GBV survivors in Lebanon
project_objective: This project aims to enhance protection for Lebanese and migrants' survivors of Gender-Based Violence in need of protection. The project will expand outreach to survivors of Gender-Based Violence by adapting a ground-up approach to recruitment and build a pool of appropriately placed community volunteers, who will help to improve identification of target beneficiaries, and enable safe and sensitive referral to available services. During this project, IOM will work with one or multiple partners to boost the capacity of local service providers, well positioned to provide the protection services needed. To identify suitable and interested partners, a call for proposal will be launched and partners will be selected through a competitive and transparent process. These include case management, medical care, psychosocial support, safe shelters for survivors of GBV, financial and legal support. Onward referral to multisector assistance will be mainstreamed across the project.

project_name: Ensuring specialized services and protection for migrant children in vulnerable situations in Lebanon.
project_objective: Responding to the need for specialized child case management (including MHPSS) with this culturally sensitive approach, IOM seeks to enhance protection assistance for migrant and Lebanese children in need of protection, including victims of child labour, child marriage, and human trafficking. The project will aim to boost the capacity of local service providers, well positioned to provide the protection services needed. These include case management support, emergency cash assistance, psychosocial support, legal assistance for unaccompanied and/or undocumented children in line with their best interests and community-based child protection activities. Onward referral to multisector assistance such as food, education or health support will be mainstreamed across the project.

project_name: Strengthening Gender Based Violence (GBV) Prevention, risk mitigation and multi-sectoral Response Services for People at risk and Survivors of GBV within affected communities
project_objective:
It is estimated that around 7,500 women and adolescent girls will be reached with a comprehensive package of GBV response services (including case management, focused PSS and legal assistance and better access to shelter, emergency, and recurrent cash assistance). 38,000 will benefit of community outreach initiatives, non-focused PSS activities, including life skills sessions, vocational training, and dignity kits distribution.
UNFPA will focus on the following interventions:
- GBV Service Delivery
1) Support access to survivor centered multi-sectoral services for women and girls at risk and survivors of GBV through Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS). UNFPA will continue to support the operations of existing women and girls’ safe spaces and support GBV service provision integrated into primary health care centers. UNFPA has a cost-effective model of GBV and SRH integration and will support partners in ensuring comprehensive provision of GBV services out of PHCs
2) Provide psychosocial support to survivors of GBV and individuals at risk including
psychological counselling, case management, focused and non-focused group psychosocial support.
3) Provide legal counselling and representation for survivors of GBV (including survivors of domestic violence and survivor of sexual harassment and exploitation)
4) Provide operational (rent, furniture) and technical support to existing safe shelters (NABAA, ABAAD) and/or establish new ones that meet minimum standards for optimal care of survivors in need of safe shelters. Shelters for survivors are an essential component of a comprehensive and coordinated GBV response. They provide survivors with the opportunity to distance themselves from abusive relationships and consider their choices for a life free from violence. The budget required to support the shelter is 130,000 USD (80,000 USD operational and 50,000 USD technical)
5) Provide emergency protection Cash Assistance to survivors of GBV and individuals at risk of violence and imminent harm. GBV Emergency Cash Assistance aims at addressing a situation that exposes an individual to immediate serious GBV harm /risk and/or addressed its consequences. It can be used to access services that are not provided free of charge. The provision of ECA is a one-time intervention intended to address the critical needs of a GBV survivor. The Recurrent Cash Assistance aims at ceasing or mitigating risk of gender-based violence, including to sexual harassment, exploitation, or abuse on the longer term. 
6) Administer Client Feedback surveys for individuals receiving case management interventions. The client feedback surveys are a keyway for us to know how survivors experienced the case management service. This can help us understand what is being done well, what needs to be improved and what the challenges are. Although specifically designed for case management, if needed, the tool can be slightly adapted and administered with beneficiaries receiving counseling services as well. Client feedback surveys are usually implemented at the end of a session or at the closing of a case.
- Outreach and GBV prevention and risk mitigation:
1) Engage community members in safety audits exercises to identify GBV risks and mitigation measures and disseminate the GBV referral pathways. 
2) Organize activities tailored to the different needs of vulnerable and marginalized groups including empowerment life skills activities and vocational training with a focus on adolescent girls.
3) Engage community in outreach activities and information sessions to raise awareness on GBV services, risks, women’s rights, gender related legal frameworks as well as on menstrual hygiene management addressing period poverty through distribution of dignity kits.
- Capacity development:
1) Train GBV service providers staff on GBV prevention and response along with mentoring sessions, Train non –specialized GBV staff on GBV risk mitigation.
