project_name: Alojamientos  Temporales Colectivos (ATC) Seguros a personas en situación de movilidad humana (incluyendo Guatemaltecos en riesgo  ) en Guatemala.
project_objective:
Dadas las dinámicas de movilidad humana en Guatemala, como país de origen, tránsito, destino y retorno de personas obligadas a huir de sus hogares y con necesidades de protección internacional, la capacidad de alojamiento temporal en los albergues, en muchos casos, es sobrepasada y se requiere una mayor y mejor infraestructura para enfrentar estos desafíos. Regularmente, los espacios habilitados actualmente suelen ser edificaciones públicas esto plantea un desafío al momento de alcanzar los estándares mínimos de habitabilidad.  
Así como la limitada disponibilidad física de sitios adecuados para la instalación de un alojamiento temporal, también la provisión de servicios dentro de los albergues es un desafío, como la atención psicosocial, la atención prehospitalaria y educación, entre otros, son limitados.

Este poyecto tiene como ojetivo, fortalecer la red de Albergues Temporales Colectivos que atienden a las personas que sirve el ACNUR y sus socios, en lo particular de este proyecto, la población priorizada son las personas de flujos mixtos en situación de movilidad humana, con diferentes necesidades y situaciones de vulnerabilidad o necesidad de protección internacional y reasentamiento. Especialmente grupos como unidades familiares, NNA, NNA no acompañados. 

La adecuada gestión y coordinación de los alojamientos temporales es fundamental para crear condiciones de entorno seguro, que facilite el ejercicio pleno de los derechos fundamentales y protección frente a riesgos como la violencia basada en género y todos los tipos de violencia.   
Este mismo principio fomenta la estrecha coordinación con los Socios Implementadores e Instituciones gubernamentales para fomentar una respuesta complementaria y articulada. 
Las principales actividades en el marco de este proyecto son: 
	Adecuación, mejoramiento y equipamiento de alojamientos temporales que buscan garantizar los estándares mínimos humanitarios. 
	Implementar soluciones de alojamientos individuales para flujos mixtos masivos, garantizando estándares mínimos humanitarios. 
	Entrega de kits de higiene. 
	Entrega de artículos básicos de socorro (Core Relief Items)

project_name: Resolver para consolidar un ambiente favorable para la protección de las personas desplazadas, en movimientos mixtos, retornadas, refugiadas y solicitantes de asilo
project_objective:
Honduras está caracterizada por una situación prolongada de desplazamiento interno a causa de la violencia al cual se suma el desplazamiento por cambio climático. Las necesidades persistentes de protección dentro de las comunidades de alto riesgo y la débil gobernanza constituyen retos para brindar una respuesta adecuada a las violaciones de derechos humanos y violencia generalizada, particularmente en entornos urbanos. Sumado al impacto de la violencia, las grandes brechas de inequidad y pobreza, acompañadas de la fragilidad institucional, dificultan abordar los factores de expulsión. Los cambios en políticas migratorias en la región y los continuos flujos de población en tránsito conllevan mayores flujos mixtos y retornados ingresando al territorio.

El desplazamiento forzado tiene un impacto negativo sobre la capacidad de generar ingresos para satisfacer las necesidades básicas, aún más cuando más el 70% del empleo es representado por empleo informal, un sector más expuesto al riesgo de extorsión. Basado en los datos del Estudio de Caracterización del Desplazamiento Interno por Violencia en Honduras, una de cada tres personas desplazadas perdió o tuvo que abandonar su trabajo a causa del desplazamiento.

El proyecto, a través de intervenciones focalizadas en zonas de expulsión, de recepción de población desplazada y en comunidades de alto riesgo de desplazamiento afectadas por la violencia, buscará garantizar que todas las personas de interés (población desplazada internamente por violencia y en riesgo de serlo, población retornada con necesidades de protección, población refugiada y solicitante de asilo) puedan tener una vida segura y sostenible que satisfaga sus necesidades básicas, contribuya a su dignidad y garantice el pleno disfrute de los derechos humanos, educiendo la vulnerabilidad socioeconómica para lograr la autosuficiencia.

Las intervenciones tendrán como prioridad la protección como mecanismo integral de respuesta al desplazamiento, respetando siempre el enfoque de Edad, Género y diversidad y perseguirán los siguientes objetivos:

- Fomentar el autoempleo con el apoyo de programas de capital semilla y capacitaciones para el desarrollo de iniciativas productivas
- Facilitar el acceso al empleo y la inserción laboral a través del apoyo e implementación de programas de empleo orientados al mercado.
- Promover la inclusión socioeconómica de las personas de interés vulnerables, pero económicamente activos.
- Facilitar el acceso a la formación en habilidades competitivas.
- Construir alianzas entre sector privado, academia, actores de desarrollo y el sector público para promover la inclusión económica, el acceso a los derechos y la eventual ampliación de las intervenciones de medios de vida.
- Fortalecer el entorno favorable para la inclusión económica y desarrollar la capacidad de las instituciones estatales para encontrar soluciones duraderas para las personas de interés.

Las intervenciones de ACNUR estarán alineadas a la estrategia de medios de vida e inclusión económico-financiera 2022-2026 de ACNUR en Honduras, así como a los siguientes objetivos del cluster:

- Contribuir a la restauración de los medios de vida de las familias a través de la oferta de bienes y servicios de acceso a activos productivos y/o infraestructuras, tecnologías básicas, asistencia técnica, financiera y emprendimientos que apoyen la recuperación económica sostenible, resiliente e inclusiva; 
- Fortalecer las capacidades de instituciones de coordinación nacional, regional y actores claves, bajo el fortalecimiento de medios de vida con enfoque de género, a fin de generar y gestionar acciones concertadas inclusivas ante el impacto de un desastre inminente; y 
- Mejorar las capacidades de las poblaciones en condición de vulnerabilidad protegiendo sus medios de vida y la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional mediante la aplicación de acciones anticipatorias que permitan aminorar el impacto de las crisis que afectan a Honduras.

project_name: Shelter and NFI support for Displaced Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
The objective of the intervention is that vulnerable internally displaced households receive timely humanitarian assistance to meet their needs through the provision of shelter and non-food items (NFIs). Through this project NRC targets 10,000 households i.e., 50,000 individuals through the provision of emergency shelter kits, family tents and non- food items. 
The intervention geographical coverage in Sudan will be in the following states – Gedaref, Al Jazirah, White Nile, West Darfur, and South Kordofan States. These 5 states have been prioritized because they have been increasingly affected by current Sudan armed conflict coupled with inter-communal violence in recent months and suffer from critical gaps in humanitarian response. 
The proposed intervention will provide humanitarian assistance to individuals negatively impacted by conflict and displacement dynamics, a rapid onset natural disaster, within the first 14 days after the shock as part of the first line response. The target population will undergo Rapid Needs and Household level assessments that will further determine whether they meet the set vulnerability criteria and are selected. The main target populations will include: 
•	Individuals that have been directly affected by a conflict, either displaced or unable to flee. 
•	Individuals that have been directly impacted by rapid onset natural disasters. 
•	Vulnerable host populations (in displacement contexts).  
Inclusion of vulnerable groups such as women, people with disabilities, and the elderly will be considered during the response to ensure they have access to services.

project_name: Targeted people and their communities are protected from public health risks through improved access to and knowledge of water, sanitation and positive hygiene behaviours
project_objective:
WASH Interventions will aim at ensuring that populations affected by displacement have reduced risk of exposure to water and sanitation related diseases. NRC will provide access to safe water and sanitation as well as promotion of better hygiene practices that lead to behaviour change.
Primarily target areas are White Nile State, Area East in Gedaref and South Kordofan States through stand-alone WASH interventions, whilst there will be complementary emergency WASH interventions in Al-Jazeera, Gedaref, West and North Darfur states through Education (WASH in Schools), Shelter, MBA, ICLA and Camp Management integrated programming. 
•	WASH interventions in the South Kordofan Area Office are stronger and more durable in nature. Pastoralists and herders frequently pass through these areas (sometimes causing rifts between clans) but very much in sync with ancient seasonal migration patterns. In the South, the focus of WASH activities will be in the harvesting and better utilisation of rain through construction of dams with improved offtake structures and facilities i.e. infiltration gallery, (slow sand filter where feasible), solar pumping, elevated tank and distribution network – as part of an Integrated Water Resource Management Plan for different villages. Capacity building will be an integral part of the project for the village development committee, local NGO and local government technical workers and groundwater sources with excess yields being used for irrigation.
•	The While Nile state area office will prioritise on protracted South Sudanese refugees living in temporary settlement (widely referred to as Open Areas). These refugees suffer lack of tenure on property and land, as such WASH infrastructure is poorly built, inadequately maintained, and prone to destruction and failure. Water supplies are minimal and often contaminated. In White Nile State, current WASH interventions are nested under the umbrella of Education under WASH in schools and NRC is gradually looking into a more stand-alone WASH interventions in the wider community, especially in terms of basic WASH provisions starting with drinking water supplies and sanitation infrastructures.
•	The East Area Office was established primarily to serve an influx of Tigrayan refugees fleeing the recent conflict in Ethiopia. Their needs will be continuously assessed and planned to be met through the provision of integrated, basic WASH services which in turn are currently integrated with shelter provision as well as WASH in schools. Standalone WASH projects are not prioritised in the upcoming year due to other humanitarian actors in the area with similar capacity to serve the currently 50,000+ Ethiopian refugees in Um Rakuba and Tunayadbah camps while supporting other WASH actors like CARE international.
The West Area Office continues to service the needs of internally displaced Sudanese settled into ‘gathering sites’ in Ag Geneina town, West Darfur. NRC also recently opened up an office in El Fasher, North Darfur. Once again a euphemism has been used to describe undocumented settlement in small areas where people have no rights and are being discouraged to stay. Services to these groups are minimal and temporary in nature. NRC WASH services will be limited to support interventions in schools.

project_name: Protection Safety Nets for People of Concern in the North East
project_objective:
As part of its mandate to provide protection and solutions, UNHCR through the Protection Safety Nets Project will initiate measures through livelihoods programming activities that will provide opportunities for returnees, IDPs and affected populations to recover their livelihoods and, acquire skills and capacities that enable them to engage in profitable income generating activities. Vulnerable households and individuals are provided a pathway to economic empowerment, recovery and durable solutions. The project aims to ensure that all persons of concern are able to make a safe and sustainable living that meets their basic needs, contributes to their dignity, and provides for the full enjoyment of their rights. The project will promote their resilience, limit negative coping behaviours that heightens protection risk exposures, as well protect the affected population from exploitation and abuse.
UNHCR will implement activities in support of this project in the following locations:
• Borno (Ngala, Maiduguri, Jere and Bama)
• Adamawa (Yola North, Yola South, Mubi North, Mubi South, Michika and Madagali)
• Yobe (Damaturu and Gujba)
The Project will provide opportunities for Women and Men, Girls and Boys – using the Age Gender and Diversity approach. UNHCR will ensure the achievement of this objective through the following means
I: Enable Access to Agricultural / Livestock / Fisheries Production: Build capacities of vulnerable IDPs, Returnees, and affected populations - through training and support for activities in sustainable agriculture/livestock/fishery production to support economic self-reliance and reintegration.
II: Facilitate Access to Self-Employment / Businesses: Promote business-oriented community-based cooperative units. Beneficiaries in such cooperatives will be provided necessary training – vocational skills, business management, financial literacy as well as business startup kits to undertake collective production and marketing of the produce.

The Protection Safety-net measures implemented through livelihoods programming will reduce needs, vulnerabilities, and heightened protection risk exposures - including sexual and gender-based violence risk exposures. It will also contribute to conducive conditions for durable solutions for IDPs and returnees, enhance community resilience and boost the provision of (or access to) sustainable livelihoods. These actions align with the Strategic Objectives of the 2019 – 2021 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Strategy, the HCT Centrality of Protection Strategy (Nigeria, 2017), and the Strategy on Protection, Return and Recovery for Northeast Nigeria (2017).

project_name: Increasing the protection of displacement affected children with heightened protection needs in Borno and Adamawa states.
project_objective:
Aims of this project include Iidentification and assistance of unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) and other children at risk carried out through protection monitoring, community-based child protection mechanisms, and broad-level awareness raising within communities. Vulnerable children such as unaccompanied and separated minors, children with disabilities, trafficked children/former CAAGs and others will be provided with case management services (including best interest assessments, as required), psychosocial support (PSS) and material assistance at child friendly spaces (CFS) and through outreach towards urban IDP children. Family tracing/reunification services by ICRC and other actors will be leveraged, and through coordination and data sharing, UNHCR will advocate for the expansion of such services in the BAY States. Returning children (former CAAG) will be supported in the reintegration process through the above noted areas of intervention.
Alternative care arrangements and community-based child protection committees comprising of willing foster parents/caregivers (both men and women) will be established and/or maintained in all project locations. Both the community-based child protection committees and the alternative care arrangements will be regularly capacitated on children’s rights and protection. Capacity building and awareness raising on children’s rights and protection will be directed towards communities and duty bearers. Kids clubs will provide sports/games, art and creativity, human rights, debate, music, dance, and drama for children, mitigating child protection risks. UNHCR will continue enhancing the child protection legal framework, interagency coordination of humanitarian assistance, reporting, and information sharing through its active participation in the Child Protection Sub-Sector and the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking of Persons (NAPTIP) at the state level.

project_name: Las mujeres y las niñas que han sufrido/están sufriendo la VBG o que corren el riesgo de sufrirla se benefician de la prestación de servicios de calidad y del acceso a los mismos, y están capacitadas para participar cada vez más en la toma de decisiones y en el liderazgo de la respuesta, la mitigación y la prevención de VBG.
project_objective:
El objetivo de este programa multinacional de ONU Mujeres es proporcionar a las supervivientes de la violencia de género y a las personas que corren el riesgo de sufrirla medios de subsistencia y agencia para facilitar su acceso a los servicios humanitarios que salvan vidas y facilitar su voz para promover la responsabilidad de la violencia de género en contextos humanitarios. El impacto del programa será mitigar, prevenir y responder más eficazmente a la violencia de género entre las comunidades afectadas por la crisis. Las intervenciones de ONU Mujeres se centran en tres resultados, dos de los cuales se lograrán conjuntamente con el UNFPA.

Los tres resultados clave del programa se describen a continuación y abarcan aspectos de la programación de las normas sociales que contribuirán a la protección y el empoderamiento de las mujeres y las niñas afectadas por las crisis en los países prioritarios; la ampliación de las asociaciones con las organizaciones de trabajadores locales y las organizaciones de derechos humanos y el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para participar en la toma de decisiones humanitarias; el aumento del acceso y la mejora de la calidad de los servicios prestados a las mujeres y las niñas afectadas por las crisis (refugiadas, desplazadas internas y en las comunidades de acogida), tanto en relación con la protección como con los medios de vida y la generación de ingresos (incluido el dinero en efectivo para las mujeres). El programa también contribuirá a la protección y abordará las necesidades y prioridades de los grupos en riesgo y marginados, incluyendo las poblaciones LGBTIQ+, las mujeres y las niñas con discapacidad. Los dos primeros resultados se obtendrán en estrecha colaboración con el UNFPA en los 6 países priorizados (resultados comunes: resultados 1 y 2).
Resultado común 1: Las personas destinatarias, a través de las intervenciones del programa, informan de cambios en las percepciones y actitudes hacia las normas y prácticas sociales que perpetúan la violencia de género y las desigualdades de género.
Resultado común 2: Las organizaciones de mujeres y las organizaciones de derechos humanos están capacitadas para participar cada vez más en la toma de decisiones y en el liderazgo de la respuesta, la mitigación y la prevención de la violencia de género.
Resultado 3 (específico de la agencia): Las mujeres y las niñas que han sufrido/están sufriendo la violencia de género o corren el riesgo de sufrirla se benefician de la prestación de servicios multisectoriales de calidad y del acceso a los mismos, incluida la asistencia jurídica.
Resultado 4 (específico de la agencia): Reducción del riesgo de violencia de género a través de la provisión de oportunidades de subsistencia, transferencias de efectivo, incluyendo dinero por trabajo.
El proyecto también invertirá en los organizaciones de mujeres locales para reforzar los conocimientos y las habilidades necesarias para la continuidad de los logros alcanzados en el proyecto. Todas las iniciativas de desarrollo de capacidades se diseñarán con un fuerte enfoque en la impartición de nuevos conocimientos que conduzcan a un cambio positivo en las actitudes y prácticas que promuevan normas de género positivas. Se espera que la programación de las normas sociales y la participación de las mujeres, los miembros de la comunidad y los líderes aumenten la apropiación y la sostenibilidad y mantengan los logros alcanzados. Por último, teniendo en cuenta que los medios de vida y los recursos financieros de las mujeres son una clave y una condición previa para la sostenibilidad, el proyecto tiene un fuerte componente de creación de medios de vida y resiliencia que permitirá a las mujeres, tanto en el entorno de los refugiados como en el de las comunidades de acogida, participar en los procesos de toma de decisiones y en los mecanismos de protección a largo plazo.

project_name: Logistics Cluster activities to support the humanitarian response in South Sudan
project_objective: The Logistics Cluster is a service-based cluster and acts, through WFP, as a provider of last resort for common logistics services. The Logistics Cluster aims to augment the capacities of humanitarian organizations and facilitate the timely delivery of humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations through logistics coordination, information management, preparedness and facilitation of common services to the entire humanitarian community in South Sudan.

project_name: Provision of air services to the humanitarian workers implementing projects
project_objective:
The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), managed by the World Food Programme (WFP), offers safe, reliable, cost-efficient and effective passenger and light cargo transport for the wider humanitarian community to and from areas of crisis and intervention. It is the only humanitarian air service that gives access to all humanitarian entities. UNHAS responds to the need for access to the South Sudan’s most remote and challenging locations, often under precarious security conditions, where no safe surface transport or viable commercial aviation options are available.
In 2023, UNHAS is targeting to provide air transport services to 70,000 passengers and 2000 metric tons (MT) light humanitarian cargo from 234 registered humanitarian organizations to approximately 54 regularly scheduled locations in South Sudan. 
The main objective of UNHAS is to continue supporting Humanitarian community with a safe, effective, cost-efficient and reliable air services. In addition to serving destinations on the fixed regular schedule, UNHAS will support 100 percent of non-scheduled location booking requests for emergencies response (security relocations, medical evacuations and Inter-Cluster Working Group Rapid Response Missions).
UNHAS requires $54,617,428 to sustain its operations across the year and continue supporting the entire humanitarian community.

project_name: Delivering Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services and Information for Crisis -affected population in South Sudan.
project_objective:
As reported by the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) for South Sudan 2022, it is estimated that 6.1 million people in South Sudan will require humanitarian healthcare services in 2023. Despite the huge humanitarian health needs, the health cluster will target 3.4 million people with various health care services in different parts of the country.
The health cluster and its partners intend to reach this target population using two main sectoral objectives among others:
1)	Improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations.
2)	Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms.
UNFPA will partner with health cluster partners and other SRH partners to identify SRH needs, planning response and providing MISP services for the population in need. The SRH services will be delivered by procurement and distribution of IARH Kits through SRH partners in the prioritized counties. UNFPA will work with partners to ensure that beneficiaries have access to quality SRH services and information in the facilities where the IARH Kits are distributed. UNFPA will help partners in providing capacity building. 
UNFPA’s output on Crisis affected populations, particularly women and adolescent girls, have increased access to information and services for maternal health, family planning, gender- based violence and HIV prevention in emergency and fragile contexts and promoting humanitarian-development nexus will fit into the health cluster objectives.
Safe motherhood services including ANC visits and skilled delivery remain low with only 17% of pregnant women attending up to 4th visits and limited access to EmONC services and other factors explains why South Sudan has some of the worst health outcome indicators globally. The unmet need for family planning remains high at 24%. The needs for clinical management of rape and psychosocial services for survivors of sexual violence remains high. 
UNFPA will serve 816,000 women of reproductive age (WRA) group (15-49 years) of whom we expect 118,323 deliveries (17,748 deliveries out of the 118,323 will take place in health facilities), 88,743 women are currently pregnant, 57,936 WRA will attempt to use modern contraceptives, 88,706 people seeking care for STI syndromes, 17,748 women who will experience complications and about 16,320 cases of sexual violence who will seek care. UNFPA will also seek to reach 374,000 adolescent girls and 408,000 adolescent boys age 10-19 with HIV prevention services and information, adolescent sexual and reproductive health services and information. Overall, UNFPA seeks to reach 1,598,000 affected people with various forms of SRH services and information through a well-coordinated mechanism for SRH at the national, sub national and county levels by the SRH technical working groups. Overall, 480 maternal deaths will be averted.
The main interventions to achieve the project purpose include, among others:
a) Ensuring availability of skilled staff and quality infrastructure for the provision of integrated SRH/GBV, including emergency obstetric care services at static health facilities and through outreaches.
b) Conducting community dialogues and health education for women, men, families and the community to increase awareness on service availability, benefits of safe sex, HIV prevention, family planning, ANC, PNC and delivery in a health facility by skilled birth attendants.
c) Procuring, prepositioning, and distributing a full range of IARH Kits and Non-Kit RH/maternal medicines and sundries essential for delivering SRH services at the community and health facilities, including RH equipment for EmONC (delivery beds, examination couches, lighting, and others).
d)Training service providers in SRH and GBV related

project_name: Provision of Shelter and NFI assistance for enhanced resilience in South Sudan
project_objective:
Approximately 2.4 million people in South Sudan continue to struggle with shelters as they experience the destruction of their housing and essential household goods brought about by the compounded effect of the complex protracted humanitarian crisis; intermittent sub-national, endemic violence; displacement; and recurrent long and heavy seasonal rains (Humanitarian Needs Overview, 2022). IOM aims to reach 350,000 people across the country through frontline and static teams in Juba, Wau, Bor, Malakal, and Bentiu.  Based on IOM's extensive experience in implementing Cash and Voucher Assistance, IOM seeks to reach 126,309 individuals with CVA in locations with functional markets like Wau, Raja, Bor, Kajo-Keji, Bentiu, Nasir, and other locations. In addition. In 2022 IOM assisted over 120,000 people through MPCA, restricted vouchers, Cash for Work, and sector-specific cash.  The settlement program in Wau, Bor South, Raja, and other locations will support the long-term shelter needs of the returnees and host communities through innovative shelter construction and environmentally friendly practices, and the use of local materials. IOM aims to implement a durable solution project in Wau, targeting 2,059 households residing in the Naivasha IDP camp. The Housing, Land, and Property team supports mainstreaming HLP in all shelter and community infrastructure projects while ensuring conflict sensitivity and assessment in contested areas. As SFP for the Naivasha IDP camp, IOM will provide SNFI assistance and shelter upgrade to people living in IDP sites. project_name: Building Resilience and Mitigating Protection Risks in Conflict-Affected Areas of South Sudan
project_objective:
This IOM Protection project aims to contribute towards the achievement of the Protection Cluster Objectives 2.4 and 2.5.
The project seeks to build resilience among the most vulnerable i.e. women, children, persons with disabilities and the elderly among others. Building the resilience of the most vulnerable against the surrounding crisis including subnational violence and climatic shocks will help to reduce their vulnerabilities. The building of the resilience will be done through mitigating the risks and addressing the violations experienced by the vulnerable members of the community. The project will focus on providing cash assistance or individual protection assistance (IPA) to those facing protection risks or those who have survived protection violations. The cash assistance will target the vulnerable in areas affected by subnational violence and climatic shock hotspots such as Warrap, Jonglei, Central and Eastern Equatoria.  The counties to be targeted include Twic, Tonj North and South, Wau, Jur River, Rubkona and Mayom. The project will also continue raising awareness on protection and conducting protection monitoring in hot spots of conflict and climatic shocks.
IOM will contribute to strengthening the humanitarian response to GBV  through building national capacities to implement GBV prevention and response programming based on the Interagency GBV minimum standards. 
The HLP Rights component seeks to continue addressing the contextual situational analysis, legal environment and judicial system as the potential tools to better lives of persons faced with HLP related challenges and or issues. It’s evident that the law and legal institutions are charged with the mandate of protecting the dignity of Property Holders and in doing so, fortify those most vulnerable to HLP issues.
The target group consists of IDPs, Host Communities, Returnees and Vulnerable groups in various categories like widows, PWDs, paralegals, elders, regulatory and supportive institutions staff who can help escalate and advocate for the upholding of the dignity of the right holders especially the vulnerable groups and PWDs as the most affected by the impact of continued discrimination in society and violations of their HLP rights as entitled to.
IOM also intends to particularly target Regulatory and Supportive Institutions so that they can represent cases of HLP rights violations among the most affected and vulnerable groups.

project_name: Provide life saving WASH services to mitigate Protection risks among vulnerable communities in Juba IDP camp sites, Pibor and Akobo Counties
project_objective:
The 2022 South Sudan HNO shows that the ongoing protracted crises has left 8.9 million people in dire need of humanitarian assistance which is an increase from 8.3 million people reported in 2021. Despite the signature of the Revitalized peace agreement, the Country continues to face different shocks that contribute to inadequate access to basic services. Access to basic WASH services remains very low with the living standards and well-being of 6.1 million people expected to be impacted due to inadequate access to WASH. This project will provide WASH integrated programming with Nutrition and emergency basic WASH services to the most vulnerable population affected by floods and inter-communal violence (ICV) that leads to massive destruction of facilities, IPC food insecurity and disease outbreaks. This is in line with the 2022 HRP prioritization of communities in locations with the utmost WASH Severity and the Strategic Objectives that contributes to reducing WASH related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition to ensure that vulnerable people who experience multi sectoral severity levels 4 and 5 have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross sectoral essential services and meet their needs. Further, the project is also focused on providing access to basic WASH services and mitigate WASH GBV in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties. 

Both temporary and (semi-)permanent solutions will be considered to ensure that most vulnerable communities are reached with timely and equitable basic WASH services. The project will deliver rapid assistance to affected communities affected by a sudden or rapid onset of disasters mainly with temporary services. This will involve distribution of WASH minimum package to promote access to safe water, access to basic and dignified gender sensitive sanitation and hygiene promotion. Emergency WASH services for 3 months (i.e. EPR/RRT) and more sustained assistance that include rehabilitation of water points and sanitation in crowded settings will be considered. Repairs and maintenance of water facilities including contamination protection through flood-proofing and disinfection and refresher trainings of WASH community structures will be done to ensure continuity and proper management of water sources. Vulnerable HHs will be provided with water containers and minimum package for water treatment products to enable safe and hygienic water access. Communities will be trained on hygiene and sanitation around water sources, maintenance of water containers and hygiene behaviour and practices to reduce disease, prevent malnutrition and improve general well-being. Hygiene promotion will focus on safe excreta management, handwashing, and safe water chain among other WASH domains. WASH NFIs will be distributed to enhance hygiene standards of vulnerable households. At Juba IDP camp sites 1 & 3, the project will provide WaSH services in line with the WaSH transition strategy that is focused on family shared facilities, on-site waste management and participatory hygiene promotion. Oxfam will directly implement the project but in close coordination with the National and Sub-National WASH Cluster coordination, EPR/ERRT task force, Protection Cluster, relevant TWGs groups, The State line Ministries of Physical Infrastructure and Health and the local authorities. This will ensure that there is complementarity among all actors devoid of duplication of services. Important key cross cutting issues will be mainstreamed during the entire project cycle including Protection, Gender, Disability Inclusion, Accountability to Affected Population and Conflict Sensitivity.

project_name: Integrated nutrition project to address malnutrition among Rohingya Refugees living in new settlements in Ukhiya and Teknaf, Kutupalong and Nayapara registered camps in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
UNHCR’s strategic vision is to provide services following the public health approach through the integration of health nutrition services to foster access and a continuum of care for beneficiaries as per UNHCR’s public health strategy and nutrition sector strategy. The project  will ensure  implementation comprehensive nutrition programmes in 19 integrated nutrition centers across 14 camps and two stabilization centers in partnership with health and nutrition partners. UNHCR will implement comprehensive nutrition programmes following the CMAM approach for community outreach programmes and treatment of acute malnutrition in the Outpatient therapeutic  feeding programme and targeted supplementary feeding  programme, blanket supplementary feeding programmes, infant and young child feeding programmes and community engagement. UNHCR will lead the implementation of the annual nutrition surveys following the Standard Expanded Nutrition Survey (SENS) methodology and support other nutrition sector assessments. 
Programmes to improve the nutrition situation among children under five years will be strengthened by the partners and more collaboration with other sectors health, WASH, food security and livelihoods and education to address the high levels of malnutrition. In terms of health addressing child hood diseases, sexual reproductive health services (ANC/PNC)  immunization and early detection and treatment of anaemia will be strengthened. Collaboration with WASH will focus improving the hygiene and sanitation through messaging and community-based hygiene promotion with focus on households with malnourished children. New collaboration with education to promote community awareness on the causes and effects of malnutrition, general nutritional and dietary requirements, including balanced diets at the household level by engaging school-going children as agents for positive change. 
Since 2022 UNHCR started the health and nutrition integration in UNHCR managed camps to foster more support and access to health care and nutrition services with to partners providing both health and nutrition and where there are nutrition partners referrals and screening of children and PLWs was initiated and is being monitored. In 2023 UNHCR will strengthen this programmes and where feasible expand to other camps. 
The nutritional needs of older adults and other vulnerable categories, such as children above five years, medical cases and other specific needs, will be considered and supported per the sector guidelines. Continued capacity building of the nutrition staff will be strengthened to ensure implementation of the nutrition services as per the protocols to ensure good quality of care and overall outcomes and the overall nutrition well-being of the beneficiaries. In 2023 UNHCR and its partners will strengthen programme monitoring and make relevant adjustments to ensure the implementation of good quality programmes and accountability to the affected population. More focus on the implementation of nutrition-sensitive programmes, disability inclusion, and AGDM approach in all the nutrition centers m, community engagement and scaling up of the mother lead MUAC concept to ensure its sustainability will be done in collaboration with other relevant sectors. 

UNHCR continues to support the GOB in strengthening its localization strategy through the engagement of two national NGOs and is working towards building its capacity to implement comprehensive nutrition programmes and increase their coverage in the future. The camps in Cox’s Bazar are regularly affected by the monsoon rains and cyclone threats and to ensure uninterrupted provision of life saving nutrition services, UNHCR will coordinate with the nutrition sector, and partner on emergency response plans, ensure adequate supplies and training of nutrition mobile teams and funding for partners to carry out emergency nutrition activities.

project_name: Improving Food Security of Conflict-affected Population of Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: DRC will provide food security assistance to IDPs, returnees and host community members of the conflict affected communities in the Northeast Nigeria. This will be achieved through provision of cash and voucher assistance. DRC proposes a cash assistance programme to improve household food security, reduce vulnerability, and reduce negative coping strategies. Unconditional cash distributions in this case are suited to meeting the food security objectives of the proposed response, especially when it comes to diversification of diet and beneficiary needs. Cash transfers allow beneficiaries to make their own choices, with experience demonstrating that extremely food insecure households typically spend a significant proportion of the cash on food with high nutritional value. DRC will also facilitate farming communities with improved agricultural inputs and small ruminants. In coordination with the Government Agriculture Development Program (ADP), DRC will also train farmers on improved and climate resilient crop and livestock production practices. DRC will target 48,590 individuals with Food Assistance and fuel, 1,000 individuals with inputs and training. This project will be implemented in Borno State.

project_name: RÉPONSE MULTISECTORIELLE D'URGENCE AUX POPULATIONS AFFECTÉES PAR L'INSÉCURITÉ ALIMENTAIRE ET LE CONFLIT DANS LES RÉGIONS DE TILLABÉRI ET DIFFA ET APPUI AUX SERVICES D'INFORMATION HUMANITAIRE AU NIGER
project_objective:
Ce projet de 24 mois vise à appuyer les personnes déplacées, réfugiées et communautés hôtes des régions de Diffa et Tillabéri au Niger. project_name: Réponse d'urgence multisectorielle aux populations affectées par l'insécurité alimentaire et le conflit dans les régions de Tillabéri et diffa, et soutien aux services d'information humanitaire au Niger
project_objective:
L'intervention se concentrera sur les zones difficiles d'accès, souffrant d'une très faible couverture humanitaire, notamment le nord de Tillabéri et le nord-est de Diffa. Compte tenu de la continuité de la crise et de l'augmentation des besoins, le programme propose une approche intersectorielle à travers une réponse à 4 niveaux. 
Une assistance alimentaire d'urgence flexible, répondant aux besoins immédiats des communautés touchées par le déplacement et l'insécurité alimentaire, dans les zones difficiles à atteindre. Le programme adaptera l'aide au contexte et aux besoins, en combinant des actions soudaines et des actions en période de soudure. Une approche à deux piliers sera mise en œuvre chaque année en fournissant une assistance alimentaire d'urgence pendant la période de soudure pendant 3 mois et 3 autres mois pendant la période ordinaire. 
Complété par des activités multisectorielles, renforçant la capacité de production alimentaire, les moyens de subsistance et la cohésion sociale, par une intervention dans deux secteurs. Pour soutenir les capacités agricoles et les mécanismes d'adaptation, dans les zones où l'assistance alimentaire sera fournie, le programme soutiendra la production agricole et alimentaire au niveau des ménages, en intégrant les ménages les plus vulnérables dans les systèmes de résilience communautaires. En outre, la diversification des ressources économiques au-delà de l'agriculture est essentielle pour assurer un accès inclusif, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées et les femmes (non-agriculteurs), aux activités économiques et couvrir la sécurité alimentaire et les besoins nutritionnels. Les personnes vulnérables supplémentaires bénéficieront d'un soutien aux AGR et au bétail par le biais i) d'un soutien aux éleveurs, ii) de la vaccination du bétail et des moyens de subsistance, et iii) des AGR.  
Et en tenant compte de la nécessité de mesures de protection au niveau communautaire, en particulier en raison de la crise accrue de la protection et du déplacement ; pour améliorer la qualité, la responsabilité et l'efficacité de la réponse tout en assurant l'accès à la protection de base et aux services WASH pour les personnes les plus vulnérables touchées par le déplacement. A travers des activités de type CCCM en dehors du camp  , la troisième ligne de réponse vise à prendre en compte le lien intersectoriel entre le déplacement et la sécurité alimentaire et à fournir un cadre de protection amélioré pour la population affectée par le déplacement et les communautés d'accueil. 
Soutenir les acteurs humanitaires par la production de produits d'information pertinents et adaptés au contexte (multisectoriel, thématique et sectoriel, cartographie) et la mise en œuvre d'activités de renforcement des capacités techniques afin d'informer la réponse humanitaire : En tant que partenaires mondiaux, IMPACT et ACTED mettent en œuvre l'initiative conjointe REACH et coordonnent la mise en œuvre sur le terrain.  d'accueil). Les bénéficiaires directs de ce projet seront également les acteurs humanitaires ayant besoin de renforcer leurs capacités en matière de gestion de l'information (80 ONG).

project_name: Unconditional food assistance to 320,000 Internally Displaced People (IDPs), local population in the North-West and South-West Regions
project_objective:
The Project aims to provide immediate unconditional 12-month in kind and in Cash food assistance to the most vulnerable IDPs and local populations affected by crisis in the North-West and South-West regions. Access to some hard-to-reach communities is still challenging and risky, however, WFP has been able to penetrate some of these communities through its implementing partners to ensure that the vulnerable persons are identified and assisted. Beneficiary targeting is done through the WFP formal targeting process using the Household Economic Analysis which places the  affected population, communities and their lived realities  at the center of the  decision-making at every stage of the programme cycle. The approach allows for better targeting of beneficiaries according to their degree of vulnerability and helps to provide precise information about the beneficiaries of actions undertaken, in terms of who benefits from what and when, and what effects the activities have had on the lives of households. Community leaders and/or members representing all different groups in the community together will actively be involved in identifying those eligible for assistance
 In line with the results of the Comprehensive Emergency Food  Security Assessment, and the Cadre Harmonise. WFP will provide food support to 320,000 targeted people affected by the crisis in the South West and North West regions. To save lives and protect the food security and nutrition status of these vulnerable people, WFP will provide immediate humanitarian food assistance to the targeted 320,000 IDPs and local vulnerable host populations (210,000 in the NW and 110,000 in the SW) in their various locations in urban, semi urban and rural communities. The modalities of assistance will be in-kind general food distributions and Multipurpose cash (MPC). Special attention will be paid to beneﬁciaries located in rural areas and diﬃcult to access settlements. The food basket and the daily ration are rations of 370 g rice, 120 g pulse, 40 g vegetable oil, 100 g super cereal and 5 g salt per person. project_name: Unconditional food assistance to 40,000 IDPs, in the Far North through Cash and In-kind.
project_objective:
In accordance with WFP's National Strategic Plan for Cameroon (CSP 2022-2026), life-saving assistance will be provided to 40,000 people displaced from their villages along the border with Nigeria and settled in safer locations in the Far North region. Food aid to beneficiaries will be provided monthly through cash and in-kind transfers.  
WFP will use cash transfers in areas where markets are functional and accessible to provide assistance to 15,000 IDPs; the ration is XAF 7,500 per beneficiary to help them access adequate and nutritious food; the ration provided to beneficiaries is equivalent to the food deficit defined in the Far North SEM. In addition, 25,000 IDPs will be supported through in-kind distributions that will provide 1,050 kcal of energy per day per person to beneficiaries who are entirely dependent on humanitarian food aid. Food rations include 185g of cereals, 60g of legumes, 20g of vegetable oil and 2.5g of salt.
For the conception of projects, beneficiaries’ opinions have been considered through focus group discussions, gender and protection evaluation field missions, monitoring exercises. These gave beneficiaries opportunities to state their preferences and transfer modalities and opinions on targeting criteria. The preparatory activities are inclusive, WFP ensures that women, men, girls and boys are involved in various stages such as targeting process, cash transfers and monitoring. WFP together with local authorities and partners, conduct assessments to identify IDPs to be considered for assistance based on WFP vulnerability criteria. These criteria include household size, presence of under-5 children, the elderly and handicapped, women-headed households, assets.
After distributions monitoring will be conducted through Cooperating Partners and attention will placed on the role played by men, women, girls and boys including decision-making on food consumption and food security in the household.
Through the established complaints and feedback mechanisms, beneficiary IDPs will freely express their views and concerns on the project implementation. Their views will be considered for project adjustment. Through sensitization, WFP will promote women and men equal participation in decision-making and social cohesion between host and displaced communities.
This assistance will be coupled to the nutrition prevention and treatment activities, WFP will provide support for children aged 6–59 months, this will include blanket supplementary feeding, counselling and support for moderate acute malnutrition treatment and improvement in adherence to treatment; mother and child health and nutrition programmes; and gender and nutrition- informed social and behaviour change communication as part of an integrated nutrition package. The daily ration for the specialized nutritious foods per assisted child will be 100 g.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Emergency WASH Services for IDPS,  returnees and Most Vulnerable Host community in Uror, Ayod counties of Jonglei, Panyijiar and Mayom counties of Unity and Juba Mangateen IDP Camp of Central Equatoria States.
project_objective:
Panyijiar and Mayom Counties are two of the Nine Counties in Unity State currently grouped in WASH Severity Classification 3&4. while Uror and Ayod Counties of Jonglei state are classified under IPC4.The four counties have been beset by conflict and instability since the  2013 civil strife in South Sudan; characterized by localized violence, inadequate infrastructure development, and the situation even compounded by incessant floods for the last three years (HNO 2022). This has aggravated the WASH needs in the aforementioned Counties thus recording poor WASH indices; low access to clean water per person per day, the average distance to the nearest clean water source exceeding the standard 500m, and access to safe sanitation facilities are inadequate. In Uror, Ayod, Mayom and panyijiar Counties like the rest of South Sudan, 18 percent of households reported feeling unsafe while collecting water, of those, 12 percent of women and girls reported avoiding water points due to GBV concerns (FSNMS, 2021). Humane Aid for Community Organization (HACO), therefore, proposes to support most vulnerable communities in Uror, Ayod, Mayom and Panyijiar Counties; returnees, IDPs, and host with emergency WASH services;  Distribution of WASH kits to unit “caretaker/SAM child”, WASH in nutrition facilities; with focus on water supply and hygiene) in Communities with high GAM and WASH vulnerability, Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies including COVID-19 and EBOLA messages adopted from WASH Cluster and WHO, conduct WASH specific activities for mitigating WASH GBV-During Waterpoint rehabilitation, Construction or rehabilitation of Sanitation facilities and distribution of WASH NFIs,  Construction of disaster-resistant structures and infrastructure, Build/rehabilitate water points with flood-resilient designs, Build/rehabilitate toilets with flood-resilient designs and carrying out safety audits before conducting WASH activities. HACO intends to reach 24,000 Individuals in Uror, Ayod, Panyijiar and Mayom. The response targets 51% IDPs, 35% Vulnerable host, and 13% Returnees in Mayom County. 

Lower WASH standards in WASH Parameters has been recorded in the most recent WASH Severity mapping gains in service provision over the years have been eroded by adverse weather effects resulting in prolonged flooding, leading to the destruction of WASH infrastructure, displacement of communities, deprivation of markets, and access to most parts of the states in focus. Flooding has further increased WASH-related mortality and morbidity affecting mainly under 5s, pregnant and lactating women, persons with special needs as well as persons living with HIV/TB. Lack of adequate WASH services directly affects the well-being of persons and communities, contributing to health, nutrition, food security, education, and protection indicators within the affected communities. 

Humane Aid for Community Organization in Jonglie and Unity states of South Sudan  plan a robust WASH response aimed at improving community well-being while integrating and working closely with other thematic areas.
The project will focus on fostering community-driven WASH responses to triggers. The project will further seek to enhance the reduction of WASH-related morbidities and mortality, through the provision of adequate, safe, and clean water for both domestic and livelihoods purposes, mitigating WASH-related GBV, and prevention of livelihood deprivation associated with inadequate WASH standards. HACO further will roll out an integrated response modality, seeking to implement jointly WASH, Health, Nutrition, FSL, Education, and Protection projects in the aforementioned counties 60% target will be female and 40% are children and 20% male.

project_name: Emergency food security and livelihoods surpport to IDPs, returnees and most vulnerable Host Communities in Mayom, Koch and Panyijiar Counties
project_objective:
South Sudan is likely to experience severe food insecurity at peak of the lean season 2023 (May-July), an estimated 8.2 Million people; comprising the refugees, and Abyei (HNO 2023) this is comparable with the situation in food security, and livelihood sectorial Analysis (December 2021), IPC Analysis (March 2022) where the food security needs continue to be large and severe. The food insecurity in Unity State (75%) of the population is likely to face severe acute food insecurity, with the highest levels of severe acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 and worse) at the peak of the lean season 2023. The main drivers to face unprecedented levels of food insecurity. covariate climatic, conflict, and economic shocks (such as floods and dry spells, inflation and rising food prices, and the continued disruption of livelihoods due to conflict and insecurity); and household-level idiosyncratic stressors (such as the death of a breadwinner, gender-based violence, morbidity and mortality due to poor hygiene, and lack of access to essential basic services) which are greatly amplified by the compounded effect of shocks. Food insecurity is greatest when these shocks and stressors are compounded by the persistently high levels of vulnerability and poverty associated with the protracted crisis that has existed since December 2021 and progressively worsened over time reaching peaks in 2022 and it is continuing now in 2023.

This situation will be further exacerbated by the progressive reductions in funding against increasing humanitarian needs in recent years which has forced humanitarian agencies to reduce entitlements and prioritize the most vulnerable households. Given the high levels of severe acute food insecurity in the state, there is a need for an immediate scale-up of multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to save lives and prevent the total collapse of livelihoods in the affected counties (Mayom, Koch, and Panyijar).  Based on the IPC findings, at least three-quarters of the population in the Mayom, Koch, and Panyijar counties are classified in IPC Phase 3 and above. The severe food insecurity situation pressed for calls for livelihood and food security support through the provision and distribution of Agriculture inputs of (crops seed, vegetable seeds, fishing kits, and agriculture hand tools. The intervention has to be supplemented by support training to target households in agriculture good agronomic practices, good fishing practices, i.e. seedbed and nursery preparation, all best agricultural practices, fishing, and fish postharvest handling, preservation, nutrition, and preservation techniques.  

Furthermore, there should be vaccination of livestock, and training in climate change adaptation. Humane Aid for Community Organization intends to target to support 13,033 Households (78,200 individuals) in Mayom, Koch, and Panyijar Counties/Unity State.

project_name: Co-creando paz: participación de mujeres jóvenes diversas en el espacio cívico urbano-rural e indígena en Nariño y Cauca
project_objective:
Este proyecto busca promover la participación inclusiva de las mujeres jóvenes de Nariño y Cauca en el cuidado de los espacios cívicos como contribución a la resolución del estallido social, transformación de conflictos y el sostenimiento de la paz mediante estrategias innovadoras co-diseñadas con mujeres jóvenes, especialmente campesinas e indígenas. 
Igualmente, el proyecto tiene como finalidad aumentar la participación y liderazgo, de las mujeres beneficiarias, en los espacios cívicos y en la toma de decisiones, mejorando la coordinación de sus organizaciones con los entes de gobierno y fortaleciendo la capacidad de diálogo y reconocimiento de las beneficiarias como constructoras de  paz, de modo que disminuya la estigmatización y se consoliden como una experiencia catalítica de participación juvenil que contribuya a la igualdad de género y el  empoderamiento de las mujeres en los espacios cívicos.

project_name: Hilando Vidas y Esperanza WLH (CS.1128)
project_objective:
Tiene como objetivo asociarse con el Gobierno de Colombia, las comunidades afectados por conflictos y los sobrevivientes de conflictos para promover la inclusión de mecanismos de apoyo psicosocial en las intervenciones comunitarias, mejorando el acceso a los servicios de salud mental y psicosociales; mitigar los riesgos asociados con el trauma psicosocial; y permitir que los sobrevivientes  del conflicto vivan una vida productiva y pacífica. Además, WLH apoyará a las organizaciones de la sociedad civil en áreas como liderazgo, generación de ingresos, resolución de conflictos y comunicación, para desarrollar capacidades locales, promover la resiliencia y fomentar transformaciones sociales para la convivencia pacífica. 

WLH implementará sus acciones en 15 municipios que forman parte de los municipios PDET. Los municipios de intervención de WLH se agrupan en 3 regiones de cinco municipios cada una I. Bajo Cauca y Noreste de Antioquia, 2. Pacífico Medio, Alto Patía y Norte del Cauca y 3. Montes de María.

project_name: Essential Primary health services to vulnerable conflict affected populations in Idleb and Aleppo
project_objective:
In line with HRP SO2, DDD’s project for 2022-2023 aims to strengthen access to lifesaving and life-sustaining essential primary health services, protection referrals and COVID-19 response for the most vulnerable people with high-severity needs and limited access to regular services in underserved urban settings and camps in Aleppo and Idleb. They will receive comprehensive Essential Health Service Package: PHC, SRH, and MHPSS through 10 fixed clinics. There will be increasing focus on outreach services, including health promotion activities and home-based specialized medical care focused on people with chronic conditions, people living with disabilities (PwD), and at-risk pregnancies. In-demand MHPSS services will be expanded, with improved MHPSS consultations, dedicated safe spaces for women and children, and strengthened referrals to third-parties through dedicated referral staff. The services will be complemented by the medical waste management for DDD facilities and other providers in Idleb. A total of 274,798 individuals are expected to directly benefit in 2022 and 288,541 in 2023. An estimated 392,247 catchment population will indirectly benefit from the intervention.
The program will support 10 PHCCs:
- 3 PHCCs in Afrin (Afrin PHC 9!B0203070; DDD Jalma comprehensive PHC!B0203087; Jandairis PHC 3!B0203069)
- 9 DDD PHCCs in Idleb (Qah village clinic/ Qah village!G0703049; Morek Alaez camp PHCC/ Morek Alaez Camp!G0703051; Dier Hassan camp PHCC/ Dier Hassan Camp!G0703088; Alsalam camp PHCC/ Alsalam Camp!G0703101; Aldoaa camp PHCC/ Aldoaa Camp!G0703047;  DDD Kelly PHC! G0700164; DDD Sarmada PHC! G0703184)
The project has been developed to respond to needs identified by the community itself through DDD’s engagement mechanisms and strong links with local communities, as well as its MSNA in 2021. DDD's MEAL framework, based on Medecins du Monde (MdM) Network standards, will continue to ensure results-oriented implementation, measure impact and adjust activities for improved quality. The MEAL plan includes direct supervision and monitoring at field level through 2 offices in Qah and Afrin; monthly monitoring visits by coordination staff based in Antakya; constant tracking of consumptions of drugs and consumables; monthly reporting of situation, workload, morbidities, beneficiaries reach, and indicators progress; and data disaggregation by gender, age, host/IDP and disability. Annual program evaluations are also conducted to assess impact and any changing needs. 
DDD’s close coordination with relevant structures and actors in the region has also informed the project design, to ensure that services are well-integrated and relevant. In the 2022-2023 period, the established coordination is planned to continue with Health, CCCM, Protection, Logistics and Nutrition Clusters, as well as COVID-19 Taskforce, MHPSS WG, NCD WG, the Access WG, the NGO Forum, AFAD meetings, SRH Technical WG, and Afrin and Harim PHC networks. In addition, activities will continue to be supported by cooperation with other partners, including Mentor Initiative Organization for leishmania diagnosis and treatment, Shafak Organization for nutrition services, SRD for referrals, UOSSM for MH-GAP, Horan Foundation for ambulance services, Syrian Immunization Group for COVID-19 vaccination, and GIZ for MHPSS supervision.  
DDD, as part of the MdM network, is one of the largest providers of health care services and one of the few NGOs providing PCR testing in NWS. MdM has been responding to the health needs of IDPs and host communities in Dana sub-district since 2012 and in Afrin since 2018. Support for these 10 facilities in 2023 is essential to maintain availability of services to these populations in need.

project_name: Provision of life saving nutrition services
project_objective: Concern will provide life-saving curative and preventative nutrition services in Aweil North County in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG); Guit County in Unity, and Juba IDP camp and Kajo-Keji County in Central Equatoria State. In NBeG, Concern will provide nutrition services across 28 sites in Aweil North, 15 in Guit and 2 in Juba IDP camp, while the OTP services are integrated in primary health care services provided by Concern in Kajo-Keji County. Concern will use the Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) approach and the guidelines approved by the national Nutrition Cluster and State Ministry of Health (SMoH) for treatment of malnutrition in Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP), Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) and Stabilization Center (SC). Concern will continue to prevent malnutrition through a combination of interventions including Social Behavior Change (SBC) through group sessions and individual counselling, promotion of home gardening, cooking demonstrations and promotion of good hygiene practices. To ensure community participation and improve access and coverage, Concern will involve community volunteers for community mobilization, screening, follow up cases and dissemination of recommended nutrition behaviors. Concern will continue its success with pre-emptively reducing risks of malnutrition through supporting mother and father groups in improving Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN). The SBC curriculum mother/fathers groups promotes gender equality and male involvement in child caring and feeding practices. The nutrition service provision will be integrated with WASH, health and FSL interventions to realize broader outcomes including improved access to safe water, sanitation, adequate diet and health care services.

project_name: Appui à la restauration et la protection des moyens d'existence pour l'amelioration de la disponibilité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des ménages affectés par la crise du Lac Tchad
project_objective:
Depuis 2015, le Tchad fait l’objet d’attaques perpétrées par des groupes armés non-étatiques présents dans le bassin du Lac Tchad engendrant des déplacements massifs de populations, aussi bien internes que transfrontaliers. Ces attaques de groupes armés non étatiques ont entrainé des mouvements de populations et bousculé les échanges et équilibres socio-économiques dans cette région, déjà en proie aux effets du réchauffement climatique qui y aggravent notamment l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle.
Selon le Round 17 collecté par OIM, le Lac compte plus de 381 289 personnes deplacées internes, 23 901 retournés venus de l'etranger et 20 674 retournés anciens deplacés. 
. En plus, suivant les résultats de l'analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2022, plus de 165 111 personnes seraient en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle dans la periode projetée de Juin à Aout 2023. 
L‘insécurité au Lac, la baisse attendue de production liée aux inondations, et les prix atypiquement au-dessus de la moyenne continue de perturber les sources typiques de nourriture et revenus de ménages pauvres dans le pays. Malgré les récoltes en cours, l’insécurité alimentaire de Stress (Phase 2 de l’IPC) sera répandue dans la plupart de zones sahariennes et sahéliennes. Au Lac, l’assistance alimentaire en cours permet aux ménages d’avoir une consommation adéquate, mais ils ne peuvent assumer certaines dépenses non-alimentaires qui sont en Stress ! (Phase 2 ! de l’IPC). Compte tenu de la persistance de l’insécurité, les ménages du Lac continueraient d’éprouver des difficultés de consommation alimentaire à la suite des baisses de production et des perturbations de leurs moyens d’existence. L’épuisement précoce de leurs stocks céréaliers va accentuer la sévérité de leurs situation alimentaire à partir de mars 2023 et ces ménages resteraient en Crise (Phase 3 de l’IPC), en l’absence d’assistance.
Outres les conflits, les principales causes qui ont conduit plusieurs milliers de personnes à ne pouvoir s’assurer une alimentation et une vie socio-économique décente, sont généralement liées aux conditions de naissance (mères très jeunes et naissances fréquentes), manque de diversification de la diète, manque de connaissance, les changements climatiques et le manque d’éducation ainsi que la pauvreté et les conditions et pratiques sanitaires. Les femmes, les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que les jeunes filles sont les principales victimes du non-respects des droits humains. Au Lac, la situation liée à la protection des femmes et des filles demeure préoccupante et pour des raisons culturelles, cette catégorie de population n'a pas le même niveau d’accès à l’éducation, aux ressources naturelles, aux services de base et paradoxalement, ces femmes et filles représentent la principale source de changement tant attendu dans les ménages.
En effet, la FAO se propose d'exécuter les actions de renforcement des moyens d'existence pour améliorer la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle des personnes pauvres et très pauvres.

project_name: Proyecto de Mecanismos de Información, Respuesta Rápida y Recuperación a la crisis en contextos de multiafectación en Colombia
project_objective: El devenir de la crisis por COVID en 2020 trajo a la región latinoamericana, y en especial a Colombia una agravación generalizada de la situación humanitaria, impactando en los sistemas de salud, seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida y protección social. Además, la situación de seguridad se ha deteriorado recientemente con el re acomodamiento de los grupos armados y las disputas por las rutas del narcotráfico y el control territorial. En relación a la situación de los desastres naturales, se calcula que estos han afectaron hasta 2021 al menos a 500.000 personas y la proyección para 2022 para el fenómeno de la Niña es a que esta tendencia continúe. Todo ello justifica la importancia de una respuesta humanitaria sólida que incluya la generación de alertas tempranas, preparación y alistamiento, además de los procesos de atención y respuesta rápida postcrisis.  De esta manera, se requiere trabajar en la continuación del Proyecto de OCHA con PNUD, en asocio con el Departamento Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (UNGRD) y la Unidad Nacional de Víctimas (UARIV) para fortalecer los esfuerzos nacionales de preparación, respuesta y recuperación ante emergencias, particularmente a nivel territorial en las zonas más afectadas por la violencia y los desastres naturales. El Proyecto busca fortalecer la capacidad instalada de la institucionalidad colombiana encargada de la gestión del riesgo, fortaleciendo los procesos de emisión de alertas tempranas, preparación de emergencias, rehabilitación post-crisis, reporte y mitigación de daño, con un fuerte enfoque comunitario para la acción. La idea es que se creen efectos multiplicadores con la capacitación que se ha venido brindando a los actores territoriales en sus esfuerzos de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias y la descentralización del sistema humanitario, brindándole un mayor enfoque de recuperación temprana.

project_name: Assistance humanitaire aux ménages vulnérables hotes pour faire face à la crise alimentaire de 2023
project_objective: L'intervention a pour but de préserver les moyens d'existence des populations deplacées et hotes dans les régions de Tillaberi, Maradi et Diffa. L'objectif visé est l'accès de 7835 ménages vulnérables de ces trois régions à des ressources leur permettant de couvrir leurs besoins alimentaires durant la période de soudure. Les 7 8835 ménages bénéficiaires sont des vulnérables autochtones déclarées déficitaires à l'issue du Cadre Harmonisé de novembre 202 dans les régions de Diffa (départements de Mainé Soroa, Bosso), de Maradi (Départements d'Aguié, Tessaoua, Guidan Roumdji) et de Tillaberi ( départements de Tillaberi, Ayorou). L'implication de ces bénénficiaires se fera dès au ciblage auquel ils seront associés, tout comme les autorités locales, les communautés et les services techniques déconcentrés, dans la définition des critères de sélection des bénéficiaires mais aussi dans le choix des modalités de l'intervention. Save the Children utilisera à cet effet l'outil Household Economic Analysis (HEA). Des comités villageois seront mis en place pour le retour d'informations (rédevabilité) dans la mise en oeuvre du projet. L'impact attendu du projet est que 25% des ménages déficitaires de ces trois régions (enfants, jeunes, femmes) ont des conditions de vie améiorées et sont résilients à l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle à travers les distributions de cash et d'actifs productifs.

project_name: Emergency Health and MHPSS response for conflict affected populations in Cabo Delgado and Nampula, Mozambique
project_objective: Ensure access to and continuity of essential primary health and MHPSS services, including capacity building, procurement of equipment and medicines, service delivery, emergency referrals and outbreak response and surveillance operations for vulnerable displaced people and host communities. This will be implemented through an integrated community-based approach in Cabo Delgado and Nampula provinces and through the deployment of mobile clinics, mobile brigades and fixed health posts.

project_name: Improving access to civil documentation and enhance HLP normative and institutional frameworks to influence policy in Cabo Delgado
project_objective: Displaced households in Cabo Delgado often lack legal documentation, including civil and property documents. This can have far-reaching implications on their ability to fully enjoy freedom of movement, access basic services or secure land tenure rights. NRC will address this through a 2-prong approach. Firstly, the ICLA programme will support displacement affected households in obtaining legal identity documentation through the establishment of mobile legal clinics and access points providing information, counselling, and referral to relevant Government authorities. Secondly, through the co-chairing of the HLP Area of Responsibility (AoR) Working Group, NRC will provide leadership, technical support, and capacity building to the humanitarian community, to mainstream HLP into assessment tools used in localities where HLP issues of highest prevalence and concern are reported. NRC will carry out joint HLP field assessments with the HLP AOR co-chair, Protection Cluster, and other humanitarian actors focusing on sensitization and information sharing regarding HLP legal frameworks.

project_name: Réponse d'urgence (RRM) aux besoins en soins de santé, nutrition et soutien psychosocial des populations les plus vulnérables, déplacées et d’accueil, dans les régions touchées par les conflits, au Niger

project_name: Projet d’Appui à la lutte Contre la malnutrition aigüe dans les districts sanitaires de Tillia, Bouza et Madaoua ( Région de Tahoua), les districts sanitaires de Madarounfa,  Nguidam-Roudji et Mayahi (Région de Maradi) et les districs sanitaires  de Diffa, Mainé Soroa (Région  de Diffa) au Niger.
project_objective:

Il s’agira d’assurer le suivi du paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé pour l’amélioration du traitement de la Malnutrition AÏgue sévère (MAS) et aussi de renforcer les capacités des acteurs de la santé et des communautés en matière de prévention de la malnutrition. Les couples mères enfants répondant aux critères d’admission CRENI seront ciblés prioritairement par les actions WASH.
