project_name: Provision of shelter assistance to the crisis-impacted population in the BAY states
project_objective: Due to the high insecurity in the BAY states, we observe a lot of displacement, which creates a great need for shelters and NFI. Moreover, the climatic conditions (wind, rain, etc.) often washes away the shelters and basic items of the population living in the camps and host communities. To meet these needs, SI plans to distribute shelter repair kits, construct, with the help of skilled carpenters, BAMA shelters. SI also wishes to have a longer-term impact by repairing transitional shelters. Finally, every household that will receive shelter assistance will also be given a NFI kit. These actions will benefit 8,360 individuals.

project_name: Increase Equitable Access to Comprehensive Health and Emergency Services in Syria
project_objective: Improving and sustaining essential, equitable, quality health services at primary and community levels are pivotal for effective response to the needs of the affected population. The protracted crisis in Syria has left only 54% of primary health care centers (PHCs) fully functional. The Cholera outbreak that was declared in September 2022, is further draining health resources. Overall, there is a lack of available, qualified, and trained staff, with limited financial means to support service provision, supervision, and referral services. Findings from AAH assessments reveal that communities face a range of challenges, including rampant poverty, poor employment, limited access to healthcare resources, stigma, transportation challenges and proliferation of illicit substances, all impacting communities’ ability to engage in healthcare, as well as women’s health seeking behavior and decision-making. Access difficulties constitute a distinctive barrier to health care in areas with high severity scores. AAH proposes an integrated approach to meet the priority needs in the 2023 HRP, focusing on activating community structures for the sustainable use and provision of public services and prevention of undernutrition and epidemic diseases, and restoring essential health systems and capacity within targeted communities to ensure local capacity meets the different needs of women, men, girls, and boys. Targeting criteria are based on needs severity and assessment, vulnerability (including prioritization of PLW, WRA, CU5, IDPs, returnees, populations hosting displaced persons, and people with socioeconomic hardships), contextual volatility and strategic operational presence of AAH. The project will intervene at multiple levels within the targeted health districts, including primary static and mobile healthcare facilities. Readiness of health facilities to foster resilience and effective management of outbreaks will be promoted through the provision of medical supplies and support for health information systems. Medicine shortages in the supported facilities will also be addressed. AAH will increase availability of MHPSS services by supporting points for MH counselling in NES. Competency-based capacity building and leadership/governance empowerment for community and health/nutrition workforce will be included.  PHC staff will be trained on integrating primary health care services (including MHPSS and nutrition) with activated supervisory visits to ensure adequacy of implementation. Midwives will be targeted by tailored capacity building programs aiming at empowering them with the skills, knowledge and tools needed for quality provision of SRH services integrated with nutrition and MHPSS. Community Health Workers will also be trained to integrate and deliver MHPSS, nutrition and RMNCAH prevention at the PHC, community, and household levels within the selected health districts. Optimal menstrual hygiene practices will be promoted at community level with linkages to PHCs, targeting female adolescents. A comprehensive MEAL plan is designated to support collection and tracking of sex, age and disability disaggregated data in line with proposed health interventions and is undertaken directly by MEAL in collaboration with AAH’s Health and Nutrition department. Monitoring methodologies include needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and activity monitoring. Systematic collection of information on risk environment, gender roles and responsibilities, gender relations and decision-making dynamics, access to and control of resources, and social norms, will be done with a conflict sensitivity approach. Qualitative interviews and satisfaction surveys will complement monitoring activities to examine the project’s effect on social dynamics in communities and pathways of change. Focus group discussions and key informant interviews with stakeholders, such as health facility workers and beneficiaries, at key points and midway through program cycle.

project_name: Emergency Health Response in Northeast Syria
project_objective:
After eleven years of conflict, extensive and multifaceted humanitarian needs across Syria remain. The conflict has grave direct and indirect health implications for civilians, including women and children. The collapse of public services, health systems, and social networks places a disproportionate burden on women and children's health, which can be further exacerbated when they are forcibly displaced from their homes and communities. Building on its experience providing lifesaving health services for the past several years, RI proposes comprehensive health, institutional WASH and protection intervention in NES. The services are designed to provide an integrated health, institutional WASH, and protection monitoring package. The intervention will target all affected populations, focusing on the inclusion of vulnerable groups.
Using health as an entry point, RI will support essential lifesaving health services provision in Syria along with the integrated WASH in Health Facilities and protection services. RI will provide primary and secondary healthcare services through integrated health and protection activities at the community level by providing information and education to minimize the risk of diseases along with GBV and RI will conduct protection monitoring activities in NES. RI will utilize evidence-based information based on protection monitoring in implementing health and protection activities to inform advocacy efforts to address critical needs.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de capacidades de respuesta comunitaria e institucional ante la ocurrencia de desastres asociados a eventos naturales  y de origen antrópico en los estados Trujillo y Mérida
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene por objeto disminuir la vulnerabilidad y fortalecer las capacidades de recuperación y la resiliencia de las personas afectadas por grupo de edad, género y diversidad en comunidades vulnerables ante eventos adversos de origen natural y antrópico en los estados Trujillo (municipio Urdaneta) y  Mérida (municipios Tovar y Pinto Salinas). 
Las zonas objeto de intervención son frecuentemente impactadas con inundaciones, crecidas torrenciales y  movimientos en masa producto de las características topográficas de la región, la inestabilidad geológica,  las frecuentes  lluvias y el impacto del cambio climático en la zona, el periodo de retorno de eventos con importantes consecuencias parece reducirse según investigaciones recientes de la Universidad de Los Andes y análisis hechos por los organismos de seguridad del estado, como protección civil. 
El último evento ocurrió en octubre y noviembre de 2022, dejando secuelas importantes sobre la vialidad en la zona y medios de vida de las familias afectadas.
Tomando en cuenta el nexo entre actividades humanitarias y de desarrollo, dadas las características de las zonas de intervención y sus  antecedentes, en función de mitigar el impacto en vidas humanas  y contribuir a  mejorar el restablecimiento de medios de vida, mantenimiento y protección de los hogares,  se prevé la capacitación para la gestión del riesgo y el fortalecimiento de la capacidad de respuesta de los habitantes de  5 comunidades vulnerables de los referidos municipios, así como la transversalización  del conocimiento de la gestión del riesgo mediante la formación  a docentes en tres escuelas. 
Asimismo, se hará  la identificación del riesgo y preparación para la respuesta en emergencia de los hospitales de Tovar y  Santa Cruz de Mora y el ambulatorio de Quebrada de Cueva en el municipio Urdaneta de Trujillo, con la capacitación del talento humano y la instalación de sistemas fotovoltaicos que  garanticen la atención en áreas vitales de estos centros de salud en momentos de emergencia.
El relacionamiento con las autoridades de salud estatales  se hará de manera directa,  toda vez que los centros de salud priorizados son gerenciados  por personal dependiente de las Corporaciones de Salud, quienes han aportado información para la elaboración de esta propuesta. En el caso del estado Mérida las autoridades de salud conocen el trabajo que  CISP ha efectuado  en otras implementaciones en centros de salud dependientes de la Gobernación del estado Mérida.
Se prioriza también la necesidad de atender debilidades en cuanto a la preparación de respuesta por parte de las instituciones del Estado y la creación de planes de gestión de la emergencia.
La iniciativa comprende actividades de sensibilización y formación para fortalecer las capacidades comunitarias, institucionales y de organizaciones de la sociedad civil para identificar el riesgo,  adaptarse, prevenir, mitigar y responder a eventos adversos.
Este fortalecimiento de capacidades pasa por acciones educativas y de comunicación; la identificación y evaluación de zonas vulnerables, la zonificación de susceptibilidad y escenarios de amenazas hidrogeomorfológicas por parte de las propias comunidades, la conformación de brigadas de emergencia comunitarias y la implementación de medidas adaptativas (sistemas de alerta temprana) que ayuden a la gestión preventiva y  correctiva del riesgo de desastres; actividades orientadas a brindar atención diferenciada para personas con discapacidad en medio de la emergencia,  así como la preparación para la gestión del agua en situaciones de emergencia y el fortalecimiento y capacitación de los organismos de primera respuesta.
Se trata de un proyecto con acciones replicables en otras zonas del país con características similares. Al término de la implementación contaremos con comunidades conscientes del riesgo y preparadas para gestionar de forma efectiva la emergencia.

project_name: Apoyo a la atención primaria de salud, salud sexual y reproductiva y salud mental para poblaciones en ruta migratoria o afectadas por la crisis migratoria en los estados Táchira y Apure
project_objective: A través del proyecto propuesto, MdM proporcionará servicios de salud a 27.000 beneficiarios en la ruta migratoria  o afectadas por la crisis migratoria, principalmente  niños, mujeres,  incluidas las mujeres embarazadas.   El proyecto prevé proporcionar apoyo material y técnico a 10 centros de salud en los estados de Táchira y Apure y proporcionar servicios de calidad  de APS, SSR y MHPSS de forma directa y gratuita. La respuesta será guiada teniendo en cuenta los procedimientos del MPPS y los lineamientos establecidos por la Organización Panamericana de la Salud (OPS). Los 10 centros de salud recibirán apoyo de dos maneras: 1) mediante  apoyo material con el suministro de equipo médico, medicamentos e insumos médicos esenciales y 2) proporcionando servicios de atención primaria de salud, salud sexual y reproductiva y salud sexual y reproductiva directa a través de sus equipos a comunidades normalmente atendidas por estos centros pero que viven en zonas remotas mediante el despliegue de clínicas móviles. También se invitará a los trabajadores de la salud a asistir a sesiones de capacitación en atención primaria de salud, SSR y SMPSP para garantizar la calidad de la atención y una mejor gestión de los insumos. El personal será apoyado técnicamente por MdM a través del apoyo posterior a la capacitación, con miras a la sostenibilidad.

project_name: Operation and Maintenance of Humanitarian Hubs in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective: Since April 2018, IOM has operated and managed a total of nine Humanitarian Hubs composed of a base camp in Maiduguri (Red Roof) and eight field hubs located in Gwoza, Bama, Ngala, Dikwa, Monguno, Banki (with two hubs) and Damasak. The Humanitarian Hubs provide humanitarian actors the ability to work in safe and secure accommodations, office space, and meeting/training facilities, in order to access generally insecure locations and deliver interventions necessary to improve and save the lives of hundreds of thousands of conflicts affected populations. The hubs also host the internet connectivity service of the Emergency Telecommunication Sector (ETS). With the ongoing security risks faced by humanitarian responders, especially in locations outside Maiduguri, the continued operation of the nine humanitarian hubs will contribute significantly to ensuring the presence and operational capacities of responders in hard-to-reach locations, which will result in delivering life-saving assistance to people in need where they need it the most. It is estimated that 1.3 million internally displaced persons (lDPs) reside where the Humanitarian Hubs are located.

project_name: Improving uninterrupted access to quality live-saving  Sexual and Reproductive Health Services for the displaced and vulnerable women, girls and adolescents from IDP camps and returnees in the Northeast States of Nigeria
project_objective: The project will focus to improve the access to life-saving sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care services to the IDPs and vulnerable women and adolescent girls including the returnees and those from the host community in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe States (BAY States). The minimum initial service, and comprehensive SRH services covering but not limited to antenatal care, postnatal care, supporting for delivery services, clinical management of rape and family planning services to the women and girls in needs will be strengthened through the supported health facilities and local partners. The survivors of sexual violence and women with obstetric emergencies who need the tertiary level care will also benefit from specialized referral support services of the project. UNFPA will also procure inter-agency emergency reproductive health kits including clinical management of rape kits, and other essential medical items to support un-interrupted SRH service delivery, as well as for the prepositioning. The unpredictable situations of COVID-19, and cholera will also be taken into account, such as ensuring uninterrupted protection supplies, provision of essential drugs, continuation of key SRH services guided by the preparedness activities. The efforts of advocacy and leadership of the SRH sub-working group under the health sector will be strengthened to maximize the momentum of SRH response, including the preparedness for any emergency across BAY States. In addition, the clinical management of rape task force (CMR TF) will be activated and strengthened the integration of SRH and GBV, to ensure the GBV survivors received appropriate timely health care services and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS). The ultimate aim of the project is to ensure the continuation and strengthening of SRH services through the provision of reproductive health supplies, capacity building and strengthening of coordination across the BAY States.

project_name: Strengthening the protective environment of refugees and host populations by prioritizing women and adolescent girls access to protection services and socio-economic assistance to mitigate risk of GBV in the commune of Kette, Batouri, Garoua-Boulai and Kentzou
project_objective:
The project aims to address the mentioned issue through a community-based approach and strong partnership with local governments at the municipal level and other relevant humanitarian partners. IMC will engage with communities in the target municipalities through members of community-based organizations (CBOs), traditional and religious leaders, etc… IMC will also put in place community structures that will support different interventions for child protection and GBV. It should be noted that these structures will be made up of both nationals and refugees. In addition, IMC will work in close collaboration with the municipality, social centers (MINAS), schools as well as with the Ministry in charge of the Promotion of Women and the Family (MINPROFF).  

Key interventions include trainings of project staff, community volunteers/animators, relevant humanitarian partners, community and religious leaders, women's advocates, leaders of community organizations and members of established community mechanisms on the issues related to GBV, child protection, promotion of girls' rights, inclusive education, ... Awareness-raising activities will also be carried out at the community level on various subjects, including reporting of Protection cases, the rights of children and adolescents to be protected from violence, the harmful effects of early marriage and other cultural practices and behaviors affecting children and adolescents, the importance of education inclusive. Additionally, IMC UK will provide material support to vulnerable children and those at heightened risk of violence, abuse and exploitation and to foster families of unaccompanied and separated children. 

 IMC will adopt the's innovative approach will be the ""Girl Shine"" model for the development of life skills for adolescent girls at the community level to improve their protection against all forms of violence and promote their rights.

project_name: Strengthening National and community capacity for women's empowerment, prevention and response to GBV, harmful social and gender norms and practices particularly FGM and child marriage, including in humanitarian settings and public health emergencies
project_objective:
According to recent data on the population of Cameroon population1, it is estimated in millions, at about 27.9 inhabitants in 2022 with an average annual rate of change in the population, in percentage, 2020-2025 estimated at 2.5. The population aged 0-14 is approximately 42%, those aged 10-24 is 33%, and between the ages of 15-64, the estimation is 56%. 
Each year around the world, 12 million of girls are married before the age of 182. Child marriage disproportionately affects girls and deprives them of their basic rights to health, safety and education. Girls married before the age of 18 are more likely to experience violence from their intimate partner, as well as sexual abuse, physical abuse, psychological pressure and emotional abuse from their in-laws.
The project's goal is to strengthened national capacity for women’s empowerment, prevention and response to GBV, harmful social and gender norms and practices particularly FGM and child marriage, including in humanitarian settings and public health emergencies through; the reinforcement of the capacities of youth-led and women-led organizations to initiate and implement GBV prevention and risk mitigation actions in their communities and improve delivery and access to quality multi-sectoral responses services to vulnerable women and girls including survivors of GBV. 
To meet the objectives of this project, IMC aims to; identify and train youth and women led organizations on GBV core concepts, Gender (this will include women’s rights including SRHR, promoting gender equality, women’s empowerment, leadership and participation in decision making), Advocacy and, community mobilization techniques for the elimination of GBV; train law enforcement agencies (FMO) and legal authorities on GBV core concept and their implication in the referral pathway and support local organizations to initiate and lead community engagement for promotion of women’s rights, gender quality and elimination of GBV.
Rehabilitate/construct and equip women and girl’s safe spaces (WGSSs); facilitate group psychosocial support and empowerment activities in WGSS to support the implementation of information sessions, socio recreational activities and skill building activities; support the set-up of VSLA as part of women’s economic empowerment to improve the implication of women in decision making and management of resources; provide case management services for GBV survivors and support GBV coordination meetings for a better coordination of GBV interventions between partners under the lead of MINPROFF/UNFPA.

project_name: Improving the nutritional status and the livelihoods of affected populations through the strengthening of agri-food chains and local processors, social and behavior change communication and education on optimal IYCF practices in the Adamawa and East regions
project_objective:
UNHCR figures from the December 2021 factsheet of CAR refugees in the Adamawa and East regions reveal that there are 281,898 refugees from CAR, of which 79,583 live in the camp of Borgop, Gado, Lolo, Mbile, Ngam, Ngarisingo and Timangolo with 12,499 children under 5 years of age living in these refugees camps. The large presence of refugees in these communities have aggravated the prevalent food insecurity situation among host communities where opportunities for income-generating activities, such as subsistence farming, livestock and small businesses are limited.
The project aims to Improve the nutritional status of affected populations through the strengthening of agri-food chains and local processors, communication for social and behavioral change (SBCC) in the Adamawa and East regions by Strengthening social and behavior change communication (SBCC) of beneficiary populations on appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF), maternal nutrition and other family practices to prevent all forms of malnutrition, promoting sustainable livelihoods by supporting farming and income generating activities groups in favor of the most vulnerable families to strengthen their self-reliance and support early recovery and Build local capacities for sustained implementation of complementary nutrition activities.
During the implementation period, the project will focus on the development of mechanisms allowing access to safe, adequate and nutritious food to crisis-affected populations that include refugees and the host population in East and Adamawa regions during and after crisis with an interest in prevention of the risks of GBV and on livelihood activities with the aim to strengthen their self-reliance and support early recovery. This will lead to building capacity of households in agricultural and livestock techniques, including setting up small businesses, which will enable them to meet their basic needs to achieve food self-sufficiency to contribute to the empowerment of these households and to reduce malnutrition at the community level. 
Community health workers (CHWs) will mobilize the community for any nutrition education sessions so all members of the community, have the opportunity to participate, including community leaders, men, women, and adolescents (girls and boys). Furthermore, nutrition education will also be provided to PLWs who are visiting the health facilities either for treatment or for ANC or postnatal care. These education sessions will be organized for groups and individuals. IYCF counseling and skilled support for those with difficulties with breastfeeding and/or complementary feeding will be provided through the health facilities. Cooking demonstration will be conducted at community level based on local foods, tools and materials will be provided by the community.
IMC UK will facilitate the establishment and support of Community-Based Organizations (CBO). These CBOs including CHWs will be trained and involved in information dissemination, identification and addressing of malnutrition in the community. Through the Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) and “Economic and Social Empowerment” (EA$E) curriculum, IMC UK will continue to build the capacity of women and girls in order to allow them to implement small-scale projects and to address food security among communities. These VSLA members will be train on the VSLA and EA$E approaches with the support of MINPROFF, MINADER and MINEPIA in order to help them to have the appropriate techniques.  
Priority assistance will be given to households with children under 5 years and women living with disabilities.  
Mass screenings will be conducted on a quarterly basis for all children aged 6-59 months and all children who are detected with severe acute malnutrition will be referred to the nearest CMAM program

project_name: Renforcement de la prise en charge et la prévention de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants âgés de 0 à 59 mois
project_objective:
Les interventions de l’UNICEF dans le cadre de la réponse Humanitaire 2023 vont cibler les objectifs suivants :  1) le renforcement de la coordination au niveau central et décentralisé ; 2) le renforcement des capacités des acteurs à tous les niveaux pour la préparation et la réponse aux urgences, la dépistage précoce, le référencement et la prise en charge des enfants souffrant de la malnutrition aiguë sévère (y compris les approches simplifiées, les cliniques mobiles et l’approche Surge) et la promotion de l’ANJE dans le contexte d’urgence; 3) le renforcement de de la chaine d'approvisionnement en intrants nutritionnels (aliments thérapeutiques prêts à l'emploi (ATPE), laits thérapeutiques),  les médicaments pour le traitement systématique et spécifique, les équipements et le matériels anthropométriques ; 4) L’appui au fonctionnement du système d’information sanitaire (DHIS 2) ainsi que le suivi et la supervision de la mise en œuvre des interventions.
L’UNICEF dans le cadre de la multisectorialité travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les autres secteurs notamment la Santé, la Sécurité Alimentaire/Moyens d’Existence, la Protection, l’Eau/ L’Hygiène/l’Assainissement pour une meilleure synergie des interventions et un plus grand impact sur les bénéficiaires.  Cette synergie avec les autres secteurs visera à réduire la survenue des cas de malnutrition aiguë sévère dans les communautés avec un focus sur la prévention et une prise en charge adéquate des cas de malnutrition aiguë sévère.
L’engagement Communautaire sera la clé de voûte de la stratégie de prévention a travers l’implication de la communauté dans la préparation, la mise en œuvre et le suivi des interventions dans la communauté.
Les ménages seront impliqués dans la détection précoce des enfants malnutris à travers l’approche PB/Famille et seront sensibilisés pour la conduite à tenir en cas d’identification d’enfants malnutris aiguë. Les Agents de Sante communautaire seront egalement impliques dans la mises en oeuvre des activites de prevention pour le changement de comportement dans les communautés.

project_name: Education in Emergencies: Improve access and learning for children in the most vulnerable schools of the West Bank including and East Jerusalem.
project_objective: The proposed project is in line with the EIEWG  framework objectives 1 and 2,and HRP SO 1 and 2, with the MOE protection and recovery plan 2020, the cluster objectives related to “increase equitable safe access to inclusive ,quality educational services for the most vulnerable children”, and the protection objective related to provision of school based PSS to school staff and students affected by the education related to violation and C-19 and legal aid in WB. The project aims to provide protection of vulnerable children affected by conflict and other situations of violence, particularly those at risk of denied access to educational services and individual and mass forcible transfer in the WB. NRC will work with the MoE and partners to identify new methodologies to reach the most vulnerable children and promote more inclusive education practices, in-person and the blended approach and distance education programs. NRC will promote the identification and coordinate inclusive education activities with CBOs in Area C and EJ. NRC will promote parental engagement in education, but also include a legal and counselling component at the school level and with teachers and non-teaching staff. The project targets 70 most vulnerable MoE and MoEHE schools supporting children access to a protective and safe learning environment for a total of 17,710 (9,342M and 8,268F):1) 17,710 (9,342 M and 8,268 F)students will be provided with PSS through training of teachers on how to manage a classroom with children who have gone through stressful and traumatic events, how to better support under-achievers and training of counsellors to support students with chronic nightmares that severely affect their school functioning thought the NRC flagship BLP; 2) 17,710 (9,342 M and 8,268 F) will benefit from emergency school kits to support crisis-disaster risk reduction in tandem with capacity building; 3) 17,710 (9,342 M and 8,268 F) will benefit from delivery of legal information sessions through awareness raising for students, school staff and parents about legal rights as well as response to incidents/violations through documentation; 4) advocacy pursuing enhanced protection from violations of the right to education. 5) 800 (400 M and 400 F) children will be involved in remedial education and catch-up classes to contribute to mitigation to the learning loss and children drop out of school due to C-19 restrictions. 6) 800 (400 M and 400 F) children support distance learning by providing tablets to most vulnerable children; printing self-learning materials; rehabilitate ICT infrastructure in schools, and trainings on digital literacy. Throughout the intervention a gender-responsive approach will be adopted to ensure girls and boys participation and needs assessment conducted to identify gender barriers that could affect access to education.Informative sessions will be conducted with parents and teachers on the importance of education for both boys and girls, reducing risks to access learning opportunities, with provision of psychosocial support in order to ensure children’s ability to freely express themselves in a protected environment. During the project, NRC will partner with Humanity and Inclusion to address challenges and barberries in accessing education for children with disabilities, promoting recommendations for schools on adapting or adding facilities for children with disabilities and promoting schooling for those children. Moreover, NRC will adopt Washington Group questions to ensure a disaggregation of identified disabilities. PYALARA, NRC’s local partner, is mainly devoted to transforming the role of education in Palestine to become a socially responsible education. Their objectives are to alleviate the suffering of adolescents and build the capacity of teachers and counsellors .

project_name: Lifesaving and Life-sustaining WASH assistance to IDPs, Returnees, Vulnerable Residents, and at-Risk People in Sudan
project_objective: This project aligns with cluster objectives that aim provision of timely life-saving WASH assistance, to ensure crisis-affected populations access basic water services, adequate (basic or limited), protected and gender-sensitive sanitation services, and hygiene promotion and other environmental health interventions to reduce mortality and morbidity. Furthermore, it contributes to building resilience to recurrent shocks and improving vulnerable people’s access to basic WASH services, by enhancing the prevention and mitigation of protection risks and responding to protection needs, strengthening community resilience, and enhance risk mitigation measures. The project will target 255159 (58789 boys, 63,688 girls, 67,668 women, and 65,014 men) individuals in need living in 32 localities within 8 states including Blue Nile, North Darfur, North Kordofan, South Kordofan, Central Darfur, West Darfur, Sennar, Al Gazira, Khartoum, Gedaref and Red Sea states. The project will be focusing on provision of water supply at IDPs gathering points/camps, community and institutional level including water trucking in areas supply is disrupted , provision of essential WASH supplies & NFI (Soap, jeri-cans, aqua tabs and water purifications), establishment/ construction of  emergency sanitation and handwashing facilities in the current hotspot locations construction, light rehabilitation and improvement for water sources, in addition to connection of water to schools, health facilities, and child friendly spaces. The project will contribute towards the elimination of open defecation within our operational areas through enhancing the capacity of local communities and mobilizing targeted communities to construct their own latrines. This in line with the construction of emergency latrines during emergencies for people affected by crises. The project will also contribute to solid and medical management efforts through provision of garbage and collection tools, support to the disposal of solid waste, construction of medical incinerators at health facilities to facilitate safe disposal of medical wastes. The project will focus on improving the hygiene situation and status within the targeted communities to mitigate and reduce the risk of diseases outbreaks as a result of poor WASH services through general hygiene campaigns, awareness sessions, home visits as well as strengthening the capacity of local community committees such as hygiene promotors, conduct training and establishing hygiene clubs at schools and child friendly spaces, this will be accompanied with provision of hygiene items such as soap to promote hand washing practices as mitigation measures to prevent disease outbreaks  as well as supporting female with basic menstrual hygiene items to facilitate safe and dignified menstrual management for female at menstrual age. Moreover, the project will support families who have malnourished children with hygiene items including soap, jerry-cans and aqua tabs to address underlying causes of malnutrition. The project will create synergies, complement, and integrate with Health, Nutrition, NFIs, Shelter and Food security interventions within the targeted areas and worked with other sectors to address root causes of malnutrition and factors contributing to diseases outbreaks. The project will focus and enhance gender, protection, disability mainstreaming and management of environmental risks. Furthermore, the way that services are provided will seek not only to meet immediate life-saving and life-sustaining needs, but to build community resilience, contribute towards durable solutions, and strengthen the capacity of local and national actors, including the appropriate government authorities, to lead future service delivery. The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $ 10,710,000

project_name: Provision of Shelter solutions and NFI for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable communities
project_objective: This project is aligning with cluster objectives that aiming to support newly displaced individuals in open spaces, public buildings, and camps, as well as those residing with friends/relatives, including populations in transit at border points or within the country with emergency shelter and basic NFIs, mitigate the negative impact of hazards, and ensure preparedness to people affected by crisis, ensure people affected by crisis receives timely shelter solutions and NFI assistance to reduce mortality and morbidity, mitigate health threats, and improve living conditions, and to improve access to shelter solutions for volunerable people in order to support the transition to recovery.  The project will target 114,132 (30268 girls, 29081 boys, 28487 women, and 26296 men) individuals including 1911 elderly and 490 people with disabilities in need living in 37 localities within 13 Save the Children priority states including North Kordofan, North Darfur, South Kordofan, Centeral Darfur, West Darfur, Khartoum, Gazira, Red Sea, Gedaref, River Nile, White Nile, Sennar, Blue Nile, and West Kordofan. The project will be focusing in mitigating the negative impact of hazards through community sensitization, capacity building and training for affected communities to reduce the impact of hazards,  provision of timely Shelter solutions and NFI assistance for new and protracted displacement people  to reduce mortality and morbidity, mitigate health threats, and improve living conditions through construction of shelter accompanied with essential NFI items, or distribution of life-saving emergency shelter items and materials in addition to life-saving non-food items, shelter repairs, as well as provision of cash/voucher for NFIs, and Shelter, in addition to cash for rent. The project will also focus on supporting transition, recovery and reintegration of returnees, volunerable and protracted households, and protracted IDPs through provision of transitional shelter items, cash for shelter, cash for non-food items, more over the project will be supporting prepositioning of NFIs and shelter items and materials to support timely response for anticipated and potential hazards. The project will work to ensure cross cutting issues have been addressed through ensuring households have sufficient living space, in addition to ensure as part of accountability to affected populations; complains and feedback mechanisms are in place. The project will be implemented in 12 months with estimated budget at $10,524,351.

project_name: Enhancing Emergency Health Preparedness and Response Capacity for Vulnerable Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to (1) strengthen the capacity of health facilities and public health interventions in the hard-to-reach communities; (2) enhance emergency preparedness and response; and 3) address urgent and protracted essential health needs at and around Points of Entry (PoEs) and in the mobility corridors. The proposed action will strive to protect the most vulnerable, including women of reproductive age, pregnant lactating women (PLW), children under five (U5), elderly, people with disabilities, people living with HIV, and ethnic and religious minorities, internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, and people affected by natural hazards or conflict especially the military conflict between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Response Forces (RSF) that commenced on 15 April 2023. 
Against this backdrop, IOM will support the health facilities in affected areas to address the urgent need for provision of lifesaving basic package of primary healthcare services (BPPHS), and to improve emergency preparedness and response capacity. IOM will also support the local health system to improve their coordination with state and/or federal level Ministry of Health (MoH) and WHO, by strengthening public health interventions at PoEs and supporting community-based surveillance of infectious diseases. IOM will also promote the continuity and sustainability of BPPHS to (1) ensure the quality of essential, timely, and lifesaving preventative healthcare; (2) enhance risk mitigation efforts and close monitoring of disease outbreak trends; and (3) improve overall community health services targeting approximately 390,000 people including IDPs, returnees, and host communities.
The project’s objectives will be achieved by strengthening capacity of healthcare service providers, including community healthcare workers (CHWs) and community midwives (CMs). Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) activities will also be implemented through the community health structure that IOM supports, to empower the community to prevent, detect early, and minimize the impact of public health emergencies, such as disease outbreaks. This activity is in line with the Strategic Objectives of the HRP and promotes resilience of the community to multi-hazard risks. The planned activities will be extended to support the state MoH and border authorities to enhance disease prevention and response measures at prioritized PoEs. Some of the targeted localities are located on the intersection of diverse human mobility patterns, including returnees, asylum seekers, and irregular migrants especially with the intra/interstate and cross-border movements due to the conflict and new displacements. IOM will therefore enhance public health interventions at the identified PoEs to mitigate the risk of transmission of communicable diseases including COVID-19. This will be achieved through building capacity of key stakeholders such as the state MoH, border officials, and frontline services workers including health service providers.

project_name: Improving Access to Lifesaving Nutrition Services for Crisis affected and Internally Displaced Persons in Sudan
project_objective:
The aim of the project is to improve access to quality and lifesaving nutrition services including screening, treatment, referral and preventative measures of acute malnutrition among IDPs and vulnerable crisis-affected communities. The intervention will also aim to reduce mortality and morbidity among children under two (U2), who face the highest risk of malnutrition, mortality, and morbidity, exacerbated by the current military conflict between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Response Forces (RSF) that commenced on 15 April 2023. The conflict has had a significant impact on humanitarian needs, with 19.9 million people classified as food insecure, 11 million people in need of health services and 4.6 million in need of nutrition services. The project is in line with the Nutrition Cluster’s Objective 1: Life-saving preventive and protection intervention focusing among under-two and Objective 2: Treatment of Severe and moderate among under-fives and PLWs. The project will provide a minimum package of nutrition services through the health facility in Daba Naira Camp, Ag Geneina, Al Fao, Al Galabat Al Gharbyah- Kassab and Port Sudan as well as other locations affected by the ongoing conflict. The multi-sectoral approach with Health, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Food Security and Livelihood (FSL) elements will maximize the impact of prevention of malnutrition, by providing basic and life-saving assistance to the vulnerable target population. The project covers basic and minimum package of nutrition including community outreach; outpatient treatment of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) without medical complications under community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) protocol; referral of SAM and MAM cases to higher level of care at Stabilization Centers (SC) or hospitals. The project also provides counselling and health education at the community and facility level, such as optimal infant and young child feeding in emergency (IYCF/E) message dissemination, promotion of exclusive breastfeeding and continued breastfeeding, close monitoring and reporting of BMS code violations and critical early detection of malnutrition. 
IOM has the technical and operational capacity to provide quality nutrition service in the support of, and in coordination with, UNICEF, WHO, SMoH and other sector partners. IOM will coordinate with local authorities, field office, UNDSS, to obtain timely information and mitigation measures to ensure the continuity of service provision if security risks arise and humanitarian access to target locations are hampered.

project_name: Projet d’amélioration de l’accès des populations aux soins de santé de qualité dans les régions affectées par la crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso
Réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité liée à la malnutrition dans les régions de l’Est, du Nord, du Centre Nord et du Sahel
project_objective:
La présente intervention vise à contribuer à l’amélioration de l’accès des populations aux soins de santé de qualité dans les régions du Sahel, de l'Est et du Centre-Est du Burkina Faso, affectées par la crise humanitaire. La stratégie adoptée suit une approche intégrée de la sous-nutrition. Le projet s’inscrit dans la stratégie 2022 du Cluster nutrition au Burkina Faso. De plus, cette réponse s’aligne avec les objectifs stratégiques du Plan de réponse humanitaire (HRP) 2022 :
Objectif stratégique 1 : Fournir une assistance d’urgence intégrée nécessaire pour adresser les problèmes critiques liés au bien-être physique et mental des populations affectées,notamment les personnes dans le besoin à la suite d’un choc violent, et les personnes vulnérables qui les accueillent. 
Ces personnnes recevront une assistance d’urgence multisectorielle dans les 30 jours suivants le choc. Elles auront également un accès sécurisé et équitable aux soins et aux services d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement, nécessaires pour garantir leur survie; Les  filles, garçons et enfants de 0 à 5 ans et les femmes allaitantes, recevront une prise en charge intégrée contre la malnutrition, incluant l’accès à une prise en charge de qualité, de l’eau potable et de la nourriture.
Objectif stratégique 2 : Améliorer les conditions de vie des populations affectées à travers une assistance adaptée à leurs besoins, fournie à temps et dans un environnement de protection.
Objectif stratégique 3 : Contribuer au respect des droits fondamentaux et à la protection des populations touchées par les crises. Action contre la Faim propose de renforcer sa présence dans la région du Sahel, du Centre-Nord, de l’Est et du Centre-Est en étendant et renforçant ses activités d’urgence afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des populations affectées par la crise humanitaire, notamment les femmes et les filles, statistiquement plus vulnérables. Les régions du Sahel, du Centre-Nord, de l’Est et du Centre-Est sont confrontées à une crise sécuritaire avec la présence des groupes d’opposition armés (GOA), rendant difficile l’accès des populations aux services de base, mais aussi l’accès humanitaire difficile. En intégrant dans son programme des activités liées aux pratiques de soins, le programme d’Action contre la Faim vise à atténuer l’impact de la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS) sur les enfants et leurs accompagnants, à prévenir une détérioration des conditions de vie des cas de MAS, à prévenir l’apparition de nouveaux cas de MAS et à améliorer le bien-être des mères et donneurs de soins. Une attention particulière sera portée aux femmes car la plupart des accompagnants d’enfants MAS dans les structures sanitaires sont des femmes. Avec un accent sur les femmes et les filles, les résultats de l’action proposée comprendront trois composantes clés: 
(i) Un paquet nutrition/santé au niveau des centres de santé et au niveau communautaire par le biais de cliniques mobiles, caractérisé par la prévention et le traitement de la MAS et la gestion des maladies communes à l’enfance chez les filles et garçons de moins de 5 ans, ainsi que la santé maternelle et reproductive chez les femmes enceintes et allaitantes; 
(ii) Des espaces « mères-bébés » pour les enfants de moins 5 ans (avec priorisation des enfants de moins de 2 ans). Ces espaces viseront à améliorer les pratiques de soins infantiles et apporter un soutien psychosocial aux mères et donneurs de soins afin d’améliorer le traitement mais également de prévenir les risques de rechute des enfants MAS. Ces interventions intégrées à la nutrition permettront de limiter les conséquences négatives de la MAS sur le développement infantile, notamment par des actions de stimulation psychomotrice et de renforcement des pratiques de soins dans les centres de santé et dans les cliniques mobiles.

project_name: Psycho-trauma : Soutien psychologique et psychosocial des Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) et hôtes dans les régions de l’Est, du Sahel et du Nord
project_objective:
Action contre la Faim (ACF) prévoit de reconduire son intervention de prise en charge du psycho-traumatisme pour les populations affectées (personnes déplacées internes et populations hôtes) par la détresse psychologique due à la crise humanitaire dans les régions du Sahel, de l'Est et du Nord. L’intervention proposée consistera en :
- une prise en charge psycho-trauma : l’assistance sera focalisée sur les troubles de stress post-traumatique, de la dépression et les troubles anxieux aussi bien pour les enfants ( âgés entre 6 et 17 ans) et les adultes. Il s’agira notamment d’animer des séances de psychoéducation pour la normalisation des symptômes de stress post traumatique et identifier des personnes en détresse pour leur admission au programme de prise en charge. Ces services seront offerts dans la communauté pour faciliter l’accès aux services et mieux garantir la confidentialité des bénéficiaires. L’intervention sera basée sur le protocole trauma d’Action contre la Faim et celui du traitement d’épisode traumatique (G-TEP). L’équipe des psychologues et des travailleurs psychosociaux suivront la structuration des protocoles ACF pour accompagner les bénéficiaires lors des séances thérapeutiques. Des échelles d’évaluation psychométriques permettront le suivi de l’amélioration du bien-être des bénéficiaires.  
- des sensibilisations communautaires : les sessions de sensibilisations seront animées au sein de la communauté sur la thématique de la santé mentale pour promouvoir la compréhension sur ce que c’est que le service de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial et comment avoir accès à ce service. Cette intervention vise à édifier la communauté sur les besoins en santé mentale et atténuer la stigmatisation dont sont victimes les personnes en détresse psychologique.
- la psychoéducation : le service de psychoéducation sera offert au niveau communautaire et ouvert à toute la communauté pour partager les symptômes de la détresse psychologique qui se développent suite à un choc émotionnel. En plus de la normalisation de ces symptômes chez les hommes, femmes, garçons et filles y compris les personnes handicapées, c’est aussi un cadre d’identification des personnes en besoin de soutien psychologique et ou psychosocial spécifique.  
- une formation en soutien psychosocial : les personnes clés de la communauté seront formés aux Premiers Secours Psychologiques (PSP) afin de renforcer durablement leur compétences à apporter un premier support aux personnes vulnérables, identifier les personnes qui nécessitent une prise en charge spécifique et les référer vers les services de soins adéquats. ACF a participé à l’élaboration du manuel de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé intitulée:  « Les Premiers Secours Psychologiques : guide pour les acteurs de terrain » qui servira de document de référence pour la réalisation de cette activité.

project_name: People affected by displacement benefit from improved access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and strengthened hygiene practices
project_objective:
To contribute to the overall WASH objective and ensure populations affected by displacement have reduced risk of exposure to WASH related diseases, NRC will strengthen populations’ capacity to engage in safe practices to promote better hygiene behaviours to limit health risks associated with poor WASH practices. NRC will use a range of technical approaches to provide the hardware required for access to safe water, improved hygiene and safe sanitation.

Target group
NRC will target the most vulnerable individuals and communities affected by crisis including IDPs and vulnerable host communities, in both urban, peri urban hard to reach areas including bushes and rural areas. NRC WASH interventions in the North West and South West regions aims to reach 77,000 persons (39,269 females and 37,731 males) in 12,834 Households Specifically, the following beneficiaries will be targeted:
1.	Internally Displaced Persons: NRC seeks to address the needs of vulnerable persons who have been displaced as a result of the different crises in the North West and South West Regions. These include: a) persons affected by primary, secondary or by multiple displacements situation with limited access to WASH services; b) protracted displacements, host communities, and IDPs living in collective buildings with limited access to WASH services c) those who are unable to return for security reasons to their area of origin or who have not consented to reintegration in displacement areas for one reason or another.  
2.	Returnees (includes refugee returnees): These include IDPs returning back to their original locations of displacement.
3.	Vulnerable Host Communities: These include vulnerable families living within communities hosting at least 50% IDPs as compared to the host population. Competition over limited resources over time can result to tensions which may cause further harm 
4.	People living in areas currently not accessible: These are groups of people who in one way or another did not move and have been blocked from access to services due to the ongoing conflict. These can only be reached should the security situation and access improve. 
5.	Persons living with disabilities and those with special needs:  These group include the disabled, persons with special needs and the elderly. By bringing water points and sanitation facilities closer to populations, NRC considers that beneficiaries will be less exposed to protection risks and will have more time to engage in income generating activities for women and school attendance for children.

project_name: Provision of Emergency FSL response, Recovery and Resilience Building for vulnerable population in need in Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North, Bor South, and Ibba, and Nzara Counties
project_objective:
Multiple shocks resulting from many years of wars and intercommunal conflicts, coupled with successive years of heavy floods has resulted into constant loss of livelihoods and key household assets including severe impact on building resilience for sustainable food production and thus leading to a gradual increase in food and livelihood insecurity situation in South Sudan. 
Child Relief and Support Fund (CRSF), an active women-led national organization has been implementing a resilient food and livelihood security programme in three counties (Kapoeta South, Bor South and Ibba counties) since Jan 2020 to date. CRSF is designing this FSL project to meet the needs of vulnerable populations previously affected by war, inter communal conflicts, and floods, and are in hard to reach counties (Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North, Bor South, Ibba and Nzara counties) with high food and livelihood insecurity, high morbidity due to preventable diseases, high GAM rates, depleted community assets.
In this proposed project, CRSF has targeted; Kapoeta South, Kapoeta East, Kapoeta North (EES), Bor South (Jonglei state), Ibba and Nzara counties (WES) currently in IPC 4, 3 and 2 (IPC, Feb 2022) respectively 
The FSL project will effectively contribute to the protection and rehabilitation of livelihoods of the most vulnerable and food insecure population in EES, Jonglei and WES and support them transit from food shocks through recovery and resilience building by enhancing their food production capacities and livelihood support services.
In line with 2023 FSL cluster objectives 2: CO2 Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock and objective 3, CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb & adapt to shocks & contextual changes, CRSF intends to reach out to the target population with the following activities; 1) Validating vulnerable households for their eligibility under the agreed criteria through FSNMS
2) Emergency food production: main season agriculture seeds & tool distribution; fishing, vegetable & crop kits; Emergency food production: main season agriculture seeds & tool distribution; fishing, vegetable & crop to enhance access to food production technologies.
3) Emergency food & livelihood support:  fishing kits/ vegetable kits; rapid response kits (fish kit/ cow pea and varieties of fast maturing vegetables
4) Livestock treatment and vaccination; livestock disease surveillance, Community Animal Health Workers Training and inputs support, cold chain establishment and maintenance.
CRSF is targeting to reach 12,050 households (Kapoeta Sout-2,500 HHs, Bor South-3,500 HHs, Kapoeta East-2,300, Kapoeta North 2,100 HHs, Ibba-700 HHs, and Nzara-950 HHs.
CRSF will target vulnerable household in consideration of gender and people living with disabilities while ensuring protection and Accountability to affected population practices. With support from CRSF technical FSL team, a total of 1,000 households will be trained on modern agronomic practices and 100 Community Animal Health Workers (CAWHs) will be recruited and trained for the livestock support. Under CRSF supported farmers groups on seed multiplication project in Ibba County, CRSF will  use vouchers to support farmers in other locations during seed fair to access quality seed inputs for sustainable agriculture on food production. CRSF will further ensure that FSL program implementation conforms to the Do No Harm principle and transparency and accountability to the affected population principles is adhered to as a right for every targeted beneficiary. CRSF derives its strength in its physical and operational presence in the three states particularly in Kapoeta South, Bor South and Ibba counties where the current ongoing integrated FSL interventions is being supported funds from Care Plus Foundation International.

project_name: Increasing Access to essential and integrated Nutrition Interventions to vulnerable children Under five years and PLWs in Kapoeta South, Ibba, Bor South, and Duk counties, South Sudan
project_objective:
The purpose of this proposed nutrition response plan is to increase access and scale-up to lifesaving essential and integrated nutrition interventions by establishing 10 OTP/TSFP mobile or static sites in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Duk and Ibba counties to benefit about 97,534 beneficiaries (i.e. 12,865 under five years children and 8,232 PLWs. A total of 4,204 children (2,134 girls and 2,070 boys) with SAM, 8,661 children (4,733 girls and 3,928 boys) with moderate acute malnutrition and 8,232 pregnant and lactating women will be reached by CRSF in the three project locations. 
Additionally CRSF plans to reach 23,128 with MIYCN services, 50,140 with VAS and 14,221 BSFP services for under five children and 8,232 BSFP for PLWs in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Ibba and Duk counties.
3 OTP/TSFP mobile sites will be establish at Lonyangat Machi I,  Pwata and Longeleya payams in Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatoria state. The 4 other mobile OTP/TSFPs will provide an avenue to reach children under 5 years in hard-to-reach locations in Anyidi, Makuach, and Baidit payams respectively in Bor south County, Jonglei State while 3 OTP/TSFP mobile sites will be established in Payuel, Padiet and dongchak payams in Duk county.
The activities will aim at linking nutrition Interventions with the existing FSL, WASH, and Health and protection activities by coordinating with other partners in the three locations. CRSF is proposing 2023 HRP activities which is aligned to the nutrition cluster’s objectives, indicators and activities for the HRP 2023. 
CRSF will coordinate with the existing Nutrition Partners in four locations to avoid duplication of interventions and to ensure effective referrals . These partners includes MaCDA & SCI in Kapoeta South, SCI in Bor South, and AFSS in Ibba. CRSF will engage and coordinate with UNICEF and WFP for core supply pipeline support for RUTF, RUSF, CSB++and other routine medications and therapeutic rations for the beneficiaries in both SAM and MAM programs.
CRSF will strengthen the management of SAM and MAM in Health facilities by linking with health partners in Kapoeta South, Bor South, Ibba and Duk counties. All Nutrition staff will be trained on  protection package to identify and refer children with protection concerns for specialized care.
The project will ensure recruitment of 20 Nutrition Assistants who will be charged with management and treatment of children and PLWs discovered with acute malnutrition in line with the SS CMAM guideline.
Through the established mother to mother support groups, CRSF will ensure that women and youth are engaged in the project design, planning and implementation as well as ensuring that complaints and feedback mechanisms are incorporated into this project. Further, CRSF will ensure that vulnerable caretakers are trained on nutrition sensitive agriculture for production of varieties of vegetables, establish 10 demonstration gardens at 10 mobiles OTP/TSFP sites or health facilities. CRSF will ensure that the response targets children (boys and girls) under five living with disabilities. 
To ensure improved coverage of nutrition services in hard-to-reach areas, CRSF will coordinate with other nutrition partners to plan a scale up nutrition response through establishment of 4 mobile OTP/TSFP nutrition outreach services integrated into routine Health outreach activities, Food Security, WASH, services while a close coordination with other partners will be maintained to ensure that Nutrition staffs are trained on Protection and GBV referral mechanisms in the four project locations. Currently, CRSF secured funds from Care Plus Foundation International (CPFI) to support integrated nutrition sensitive interventions in Bor South and Kapoeta South Counties. The activities support women and adolescent girls with skills on cooking demonstrations and setting up kitchen gardens for dietary diversity as well as training them on family MUAC. CRSF has gained sufficient experience and strong presence.

project_name: Emergency WASH assistance in Gedaref, Sennar, North Kordofan, White Nile, Blue Nile and Al Jazeera States
project_objective:
Since the eruption of armed violence mid-April, WASH assistance was highlighted as a priority need in particular in states that have received significant IDPs and other affected populations that have settled in informal sites and in camps. This also includes populations of local host communities, where water supply, sanitation systems and the general hygiene environment are at risk of collapse due to the onset of the rainy season, ongoing conflict, and the increased burden placed on WASH systems by the newly arrived IDPs. Acted's RNA findings are in line with IOM-DTM's situation reports, highlighting that displaced households are currently seeking shelter with relatives, temporary shelter or in IDP gathering sites prepared by the local government in Al Jazirah, Gedaref, Sennar Blue Nile and White Nile.

The present project aims at scaling up Acted's pre-conflict, multisectoral operations to respond to the new emergency WASH related needs of conflict-affected populations including IDPs, refugees, and local host communities in White Nile, Blue Nile, Al Jazirah, Sennar, Gedaref and North Kordofan.

project_name: Child Protection and GBV humanitarian Response in Kassala, North Darfur, North Kordofan, South Kordofan, White Nile and Aj Jazirah
project_objective:
The project aims at ensuring vulnerable children, especially girls, live in resilient communities and have free and safe access to life-saving services during and after natural disasters and conflict crisis, this will be achieved through provision of Child Protection and gender based violence humanitarian response services and activities  targeting 400,000 people (94,080 men, 101,920 women, 97,920 boys and 106,080 girls) including IDPs, returnees &host communities in Khartoum,South Kordofan, White Nile, Aj Jazirah, Kassala and North Kordofan. 
 Awareness will be provided to girls and boys on child rights. Children with special needs will be prioritized. Children and parents will be oriented on how to access information on child protection referrals, provision of inclusive complaints and response facilities. Child Protection will be incorporated across all sector interventions to promote meaningful access, safety and dignity. The approach will be based on Protection Principles as per the Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards of Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPMS) including avoiding causing harm by preventing and minimizing any unintended negative effects. Child Friendly spaces will be provided 2 in each of the 3 targeted localities. Some 2000 (1000 boys and 1000 girls) adolescent boys and girls will be trained on life skills and supported to form social clubs.
Gender based violence interventions will provide among others provision of mental health Provision of mental health and Psychosocial support services including provision of Psychological first aid, clinical counselling and recreational, social and life skills interventions for GBV survivors targeting 2000 SGBV survivors. Dignity kits will also be provided to 2000 GBV survivors in addition to cash/voucher assistance will also be provided targeting 2000 SGBV survivors among other services.

project_objective:

The rigidly patriarchal system and historic marginalization of women are the root causes of the GBV in the country. This is further exacerbated by recurrent natural South Sudan remains to be among the countries with a high prevalence of gender-based violence where half of the girls marry below the age of 18. Sector de asistencia alimentaria: Contribuir a reducir la niveles críticos de inseguridad alimentaria de las personas afectadas, al tener las familias recién desplazadas un acceso limitado a la comida en su lugar de llegada después de huir; Sector WASH: garantizar el acceso oportuno a WASH-NFI de calidad para las familias recién desplazadas en cumplimiento de los estándares Esfera en los primeros 30 días después de presentar una declaración; Sector alojamiento: intervenciones centradas en apoyo de arriendo durante seis meses para garantizar el acceso a un alojamiento seguro y adecuado donde las familias puedan reanudar sus actividades sociales y económicas; y Sector protección: intervenciones con metodologías, que se basan y mejoran la capacidades y estrategias de afrontamiento de las víctimas y comunidades desplazadas para su bienestar psicosocial, en complemento a la respuesta del Gobierno. Meta número total de personas únicas (individuos): 14.062. En los municipios de Cali (Valle del Cauca); Santander de Quilichao y Toribío (Cauca); Florencia, Puerto Rico y San José del Fragua (Caquetá); Montería y San José de Uré (Córdoba); y Caucasia (Antioquia). La definición de estos lugares obedece a acuerdos conjuntos de priorización con la Unidad para las Víctimas en el marco de demanda de asistencia humanitaria inmediata, complemento a actividades de rehabilitación comunitaria en el marco de PIRC o comunidades retornadas, y considerando la severidad final (entre 4 y 5) en función de los municipios priorizados desde el Clúster de Protección 2023

project_name: Mejorando el Acceso a los Servicios Multisectoriales: Resiliencia, Estabilización y Protección en Colombia/Improving Access to Multi-Sectoral Services: Resiliencia, Estabilización y Protección en Colombia (Más Resiliencia IV)
project_objective: HAI pretende hacer realidad esta Teoría del Cambio y el Objetivo del Proyecto a través de cinco Propósitos interrelacionados directamente alineados con los sectores y subsectores de la BHA: Propósito 1: Los supervivientes de conflictos y las comunidades vulnerables experimentan una mayor sensación de seguridad y protección; Propósito 2: Los supervivientes de conflictos y las comunidades vulnerables en situaciones de emergencia humanitaria experimentan un riesgo mínimo de problemas crónicos de salud mental, y gestionan mejor su salud menstrual y sexual; Propósito 3: Los supervivientes de los conflictos y las comunidades vulnerables en riesgo de ser víctimas reducen sus necesidades alimentarias durante las emergencias humanitarias; Propósito 4: Los supervivientes de los conflictos y las comunidades vulnerables en riesgo de ser víctimas tienen cubiertas sus necesidades de alojamiento temporal durante las emergencias humanitarias; y Propósito 5: Los supervivientes de los conflictos y las comunidades en riesgo tienen mejores prácticas de higiene. HAI estima que el proyecto llegará a 27.883 beneficiarios directos únicos y a 75.900 beneficiarios indirectos.  La Ley de Víctimas de Colombia establece que el GOC debe proporcionar asistencia alimentaria inmediatamente después de una emergencia humanitaria durante un período de tres meses. Sin embargo, el creciente número de emergencias humanitarias en Colombia ha limitado la capacidad del GOC para movilizar una asistencia alimentaria inmediata y efectiva a las personas afectadas por la violencia y los desastres. El problema de las emergencias humanitarias y los desplazamientos forzados supera de forma desproporcionada la capacidad de respuesta de los gobiernos locales, especialmente en los municipios de bajos ingresos con poco acceso a los recursos públicos. En estos casos, HAI establece acuerdos de cooperación para complementar la respuesta de los gobiernos locales en coordinación con otros actores humanitarios. En respuesta, HAI reforzará la capacidad de los gobiernos locales para responder a las emergencias agudas con la distribución de asistencia alimentaria en especie o vales a 4.000 hogares. Los paquetes de alimentos en especie se diseñan cuidadosamente de acuerdo con la Carta Humanitaria del Manual Esfera y las Normas Mínimas de Respuesta Humanitaria y responden a las necesidades nutricionales de las familias solas durante un mes. Para las familias numerosas, se considerará la distribución de más de un paquete de alimentos de emergencia. Para la distribución de los vales de alimentos, HAI trabaja con los proveedores de servicios locales en las comunidades seleccionadas para garantizar que los participantes puedan reclamar sus vales en lugares convenientes. HAI se coordinará estrechamente con el GOC local y los equipos humanitarios y, como parte de la respuesta integral a las comunidades recientemente desplazadas o afectadas por el confinamiento, identificará conjuntamente a las familias afectadas que necesiten asistencia alimentaria de emergencia. HAI consultará con el CAAC para garantizar que la atención especial al género, la discapacidad, la edad y otras consideraciones especiales guíen las provisiones y que la asistencia alimentaria cumpla con los principios de No Hacer Daño.

project_name: Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality through WASH integrated programming with Health and Nutrition in Fangak, Pibor, Duk, Aweil center, Aweil East, Gogrial West and Twic counties of Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Warrap states.
project_objective:
Action Against Hunger has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs. AAH strategy is to addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WASH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently Action Against Hunger is implementing a WASH program under SIDA, GFFO, GAC, and ECHO activities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Warrap, and Jonglei states with established field offices in Malual-kon, Alek, Old Fangak, and Paguir Payam. In 2023, WASH projects will be implemented to ensure that host communities, IDPs and returnees have safe access to clean water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behavior. The proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5 and pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WASH and Nutrition response aimed at breaking diarrhea – malnutrition vicious cycle. This proposed project will ensure the effectiveness of addressing malnutrition in the proposed target area by reducing disease burden in communities as well as availing safe, potable water for use in appetite tests at nutrition sites including monthly Water quality tests which will be carried out by our WASH team in both locations using our established laboratories. 
To achieve the overall project objective and objectives of the HRP-2022/3, we will provide critical services to 41,320 individuals with gender segregation of 21,478 males, 19, 842 females. among them 16,471 under 5 children at both Nutrition/Health facilities and   at the village level with 4 main activities which include: 
1) Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition.
2) Integrate Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties).
3) Community member’s exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures and infrastructure.
4) Increasing knowledge of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. ACF will implement the above in the catchment areas of its nutrition facilities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states. Baseline KAP surveys will be conducted in all target areas to identify the WASH-related knowledge, attitude, and practices of the communities. 
Detailed needs assessments will be conducted to assess community access to safe water sources and sanitation facilities. The implementation strategy will align with the needs identified in assessments and KAP surveys at the project start. Additionally, the ACF multi-sector emergency response throughout the country will include a WASH component to complement its nutrition work. 
The proposed program strategy takes into account specific gender-related needs during surveys and activity implementation to ensure the equitable participation of all gender and age groups in the locations mentioned above.

project_name: Provide lifesaving gender sensitive WASH intervention to sustain and expand service level and reduce morbidity and mortality among IDPs, returnees, and host communities in Khartoum, South Darfur, East Darfur, Kassala, Gedaref, Al-Gezira and South Kordofan.
project_objective:
This WASH intervention by CARE is designed to deliver a comprehensive WASH package to IDPs, returnees and host communities in South Darfur, East Darfur, Kassala, Gedaref, and South Kordofan. The overall objective of this intervention states “Decreased WASH related morbidity and mortality through provision of improved and sustained access to water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion services among IDPs, returnees and host communities”. project_name: CP and PSS on Wheels: A PSS and CP Mobile Unit
project_objective:
Our creative solution to the consequences of the humanitarian crises on children and communities in out-of-reach areas in Lebanon, is PSS on Wheels. Buses serving as mobile units, are equipped to facilitate access to hard-to-reach communities and complement War Child’s ongoing integrated programming of Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Child Protection (CP). 
War Child interventions range from lower-intensity interventions that aim to promote well-being and prevent problems, to higher-intensity interventions targeting only children experiencing significant and enduring distress. The integrated approach embraces a socio-ecological approach, with services targeted at different ecological levels, which recognizes that children’s development is inextricably linked to the families, communities, economic situation, social values and cultural influences that surround them and provide for their basic needs and protection.
The mobile unit will facilitate access to all groups, especially the most vulnerable and girls and women. In addition, and in case of any rising humanitarian emergency, the mobile unit will be able to respond efficiently and in time, delivering vital services such as Psychological First Aid (PFA) and referrals to specialized services through case management.
Key objectives and activities 
1.	Boys and girls, men and women at risk, residing in hard-to-reach communities, have safe and equal access to an integrated package of PSS and CP services, leading to improved mental health and well-being of children.
2.	Vital protection and psychosocial support services are delivered efficiently and in time by the mobile unit. 
An inclusion specialist will be on board to ensure safety of and accessibility for  children with disabilities, to support in adapting/adjusting the activities and provide needed guidance when it comes to identification and referrals to a specific specialized service.
The PSS on wheels will provide the following services on board and in the outside setting: 
	Community-based PSS activities through TeamUp intervention that offers structured movement-based activities for children age 6 up to 17 to learn how to deal with their emotions. The skills they gain from the activities are linked to social-emotional themes and can be of use in their daily life. The intervention includes a Disability Inclusion Guide that will enable facilitators to engage children with disabilities and ensure their full and active participation.
	Puppets, theater and music are integrated in the community-based PSS sessions.  
	CP awareness sessions for children and caregivers, in addition to internal referrals that will take place from the activities to War Child services and/or external referrals to existing external service providers.
	The Caregiver Support Intervention that will enhance caregivers well-being through enabling them to have a better understanding of their emotions and providing them with techniques to cope with the difficult ones , and effective parenting techniques to improve the interaction with their children.
	Provision of focused psychosocial support (FPSS - Level 3 of the IASC MHPSS pyramid) for  children and families whose coping capacity is overwhelmed. These might include children in acute distress due to recent exposure to serious stressors or children who are not growing and learning according to their age and developmental phase.
