project_name: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items Response to Assist IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities affected by conflict or natural disaster in Western Equatoria, Upper Nile, and Warrap States, South Sudan.
project_objective: The 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) indicates that ‘’approximately 2.4 million people in South Sudan continue to be impacted by the destruction of housing and loss of essential goods caused by ongoing flooding and conflict. In addition, nearly 329,000 refugees and asylum seekers also require shelter and non-food item (NFI) support. At the end of 2021, nearly 1.9 million men, women, boys, girls, and older people live in inadequate shelter, while a total of 2.3 million require NFIs. The number of people in need increased in 2022 due to the increased displacement of approximately 300,000 people in 2021 and the returns of nearly 270,000 from neighboring countries. The top three shelter/NFI-related needs are access to emergency shelter, NFIs and housing, land and property (HLP) rights to ensure security of tenure’’. With the budget of $700,000, this project will enable World Vision International South Sudan to serve 55,000 (17,500 men, 17,500 women; 10,000 boys, 10,000 girls) IDPs, returnees and host communities with in-kind emergency shelter and non-food items in the counties of Tambura, Nagero and Yambio in Western Equatoria State, Tonj North, Tonj East, Tonj South, Gogrial East, Gogriel West and Aweil South counties in Warrap State, Laukpiny/Nasir, Ulang Melut and Baliet counties of Upper Nile State. In areas with existing functional markets, 18 % of the targeted beneficiaries will be supported through unconditional but restricted modality of cash-based interventions. Beneficiaries for both in-kind SNFI and cash interventions will be identified during needs assessments, where methodologies like Focused Group Discussions (FGD), Key informants (KI), Observation will be deployed to collect data for decision making and before beneficiary registration and distribution missions. Post distribution missions would also be effected to get feedback from affected population. In the course of the project, WVISS team will continuously conduct community awareness meetings and workshops on issues like climate change, AAP, Covid-19 etc. The project would contribute to the two Cluster objectives; (1). Percentage of the targeted population are able to access shelter material and non-food items in situations of emergency and transition, (2). Enhance the community’s dignity by increasing their ability to respond to new shocks and building on existing skills. World Vision International South Sudan will implement the project in adherence with the SNFI cluster standards where the cluster coordination team is closely consulted on operations at national and sub-national levels. The organization will also collaborate with men, women, boys, girls, persons with special needs, government authorities and partners like UNHAS, UNOCHA, IOM/pipeline, local and international organizations to realize durable solutions for emergency shelter and non-food items. The affected populations will be encouraged to actively participate in the project through the mainstreaming of AAP (accountability to affected populations) approach into project activities. Existing local community structures would be strengthened to support the project and where they are non-existent, WVISS will facilitate the formation to enhance full participation of affected populations in area. The CFM, (Complaint Feedback Mechanism) will be introduced in each project site and community members would be sensitized on how to use it throughout the project period. The awareness creation sessions will be tailored to complement efforts for conflict mitigation, long-term solutions for floods, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, Housing, Land & Property, and COVID-19 pandemic. WVISS will continue to respond through the mobile response mechanism by deploying teams in hard to access locations or where there is urgent need of intervention across the country based on SNFI request.

project_name: Provision of emergency lifesaving and nutrition services to improve and prevent the deterioration of the nutrition status of nutritionally vulnerable Syrian women, girls and boys
project_objective:
The Nutrition project aims to address urgent and life-saving nutrition needs of mothers and children in Syria, located in high severity areas across the entire country, as depicted by the 2023 HNO. 
5.9 million people including 3.75 million children (2.2 million girls and 1.55 million boys) and 2.1 million women are in need of nutritional assistance in Syria, amongst which 0.5 million children are stunted and around 363,556 children below five years of age suffer from acute malnutrition. Mimicking  the elevated levels of stunting, disparities in prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) in children was recorded across the entire country, with GAM rates in the North-West of Syria and Damascus approached the 5% threshold, while the north-east recorded a high of 12% ( classified as critical as per the nutrition severity ranking scale) resulting in 287,830 children with MAM. Simultaneously, maternal malnutrition remains an impeding concern, with prevalence of Acute Malnutrition (AM) ranging from 11% in the North-west to 25% in the North-East, resulting in  544,752 PLWs suffering from AM,  including 460,124 suffering from anemia. Similarly, an approximate 25 % (721,388) children under five years suffer from anemia.
 In line with the nutrition sector priorities, the project aims to provide preventative and curative nutrition services to the most vulnerable groups (namely; children U5 and PLWs) amongst all affected populations, including IDPs, host communities and returnees identified with high severity food insecurity and nutrition indicators. The project will, therefore, focus on:
- Improve access to equitable and quality curative nutrition services through the most appropriate modalities to include early identification, referral, and treatment of moderate and severe wasting among children under five and PLWs in collaboration with the WASH, health and food security sectors to address the drivers of malnutrition. The targets for MAM treatment are: (35,193 CH, PLW:32,586 )in NES  and (41,494 CH, PLW: 80,511) in NWS and (109,525 CH, PLW: 231,903) in inside Syria. 
− Scale-up Blanket Supplementary Feeding Program (BSFP) to  prevent Acute Malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in children 6-23 months
− Improve access  and utilization  to nutrition services, nutritious and age appropriate  diets and  feeding practices for CU2 and PLWs. Vulnerable PLWs  will receive cash assistance of a maximum  value of  25$ in NWS and 36$ in the rest of the country for a max of 15 cycles. 
WFP aims to target boys and girls aged 6- 23months and PLWs, including those with disability, through its programmes. , the project will adopt a context and severity-based approach to prioritize sub-districts identified with high nutritional and food insecurity severity, mainly those with severity level 3,4 &5. In case of lower funding, priority will be given to locations were severity of food security and nutrition of is more than 4 and to newly accessible areas.
WFP monitors will carry out regular monitoring visits to oversee implementation and collect quantitative and qualitative data through on-site monitoring, Focus group discussions and  post-distribution surveys. 
To ensure proper and effective implementation of the Nutrition activities, WFP will start the obligation of reporting children and PLWG’s with disability in their prevention and treatment programs if applicable. This will be done through the already established reporting channels (4W’s Considering the high needs and limited resources , 10% of each allocation(that was given by HRP committee) was applied to calculate disability, this might change during the implementation of the programs . WFP will maintain regular coordination with MOH and other nutrition actors through the nutrition sector, and various thematic group.

project_name: LOGISTICS AUGMENTATION AND COORDINATION TO SUPPORT HUMANITARIAN OPERATIONS IN SYRIA
project_objective:
The Logistics Sector will continue supporting cross-border activities from Türkiye into the northwest of the country by facilitating access to free-to-user transshipment services to the humanitarian community at Bab al-Hawa border crossing, pending extension of the current UN Security Council Resolution 2462. The Logistics Sector will continue to facilitate inter-agency convoys from Aleppo availing partners to free-to-user transport and handling services for dispatches into NWS. Explore humanitarian needs for augmented storage capacity, in Qamishli and other locations if required, where access is more challenging while working closely with partners to identify alternative solutions to meet long-term logistics needs in the region. Priority will be given to make use of local available logistics capacity and advocate for the pooling of resources among partners when and where possible. The Logistics Sector will preposition extra storage capacity in key locations across the country as a preparedness measure and make them available for loan when and where needed. Coordination and information management activities will continue to support sharing of up to date relevant information, best practices, efficient supply chain planning, addressing logistics bottlenecks, common advocacy etc.
UNHAS will continue to provide passenger and light cargo air services for the humanitarian community to hard-to-reach destinations inside Syria.

project_name: Integrated Protection Services for the Conflict-Affected Population in Northwest Syria
project_objective: The program will strengthen the overall protective environment and resilience of the most vulnerable internally displaced people and host community members in Northwest Syria. Our organization will provide integrated protection services, including specialized gender-based violence and child protection case management, advanced and focused, and/or those who are survivors or at risk of gender-based violence and abuse – especially women and children. The program will target at least 26,025 beneficiaries. Attention will be given to appropriate entry points such as existing women’s groups and support networks. Areas of operation are selected in coordination with Clusters and health directorates. Case management services will be tailored to beneficiaries’ individual needs, taking into consideration family and caregivers. Psychosocial support will help beneficiaries to improve their coping mechanisms, manage stress and find solutions to their challenges. Group work will provide space for beneficiaries with similar issues, problems or circumstances to come together for mutual support. Outreach services will spread information on positive mental health and protection risks, as well as assist in reaching the most vulnerable in communities and making appropriate referrals to services. Training will target both community members and front-line service providers to increase their capacity to help and support others. Awareness-raising activities aim to decrease stigma around accessing services through encouraging people to be more aware of protection risks faced. Protection services will be integrated with health and physical rehabilitation services under other programs in order to improve access, ensure strong referral mechanisms and identify those most at-risk. Activities will be accessible by all and include: psychosocial support, community-outreach, group work, awareness-raising activities, training for service providers, community members on mental health and protection topics, and integrated mental health services for the most vulnerable people, including people with disabilities, people facing mental conditions, psychological distress and trauma. Activities will also target children and women assessed to be at high risk of abuse, exploitation, neglect or violence, children found to be associated with armed forces and armed groups, unaccompanied or separated children, persons with mental disorders or psychological distress, the elderly, chronically ill, and people with disabilities. All activities will be based upon the principles of the IASC Guidelines on MHPSS in Emergency Settings, Minimum Standards for Child Protection, and Guidelines for Integrating Gender-Based Violence Interventions in Humanitarian Action. Our organization will work to improve the availability of holistic response for the most vulnerable by conducting training targeting a range of humanitarian actors in order to strengthen response with a survivor-centered approach.

project_name: Emergency Food Security in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
SO1. In a response to the continued deterioration of the food and nutrition situation and the increased reliance and adoption of negative coping strategies that impacted the resilience of households as many as 77 per cent of households reported buying less expensive and less preferred foods resulting in poorer diets, this project aims to contribute to increased food security for vulnerable displaced and host community households in Idleb and Aleppo Governorates. It has 2 main components Household Food Security and Bakery Support. Within the Household Food Security component, NGO X targets an average of 65,000 HH/ 325,000 food-insecure individuals per month with food kits, cash for food, or value vouchers. The regular food assistance is to the value of 70% of the food SMEB (Survival minimum expenditure basket) or 70% of the Sphere minimum standards of 2100 kcal/p/day.
The Bakery Support component provides subsidized bread to individuals living in supported bakeries ’catchment areas with bread at a reduced and stabilized price. This is achieved through subsidizing up to 40% input (flour and yeast) of bread production thus supporting local bakeries to produce a stable quantity of bread that meets local needs. This support is conditional upon the selling of this bread in the local markets at a reduced and stabilized price agreed with and monitored by NGO X’s Cash and Markets, and Monitoring Teams. Approximately 33 bakeries are targeted to benefit from this assistance.
SO3. Also, NGO X will be conducting a rehabilitation activity for 5 bakeries in both of Idleb and Aleppo, the component will be used as an emergency response to the contracted bakeries under the clustering objective of SO3.
NGOX will implement the proposed project in partnership with 3 NGOs. Please note that these 3 NGOs will input into the OCHA HPC separately under this project. This decision was agreed between all parties and submissions have been coordinated to ensure there is no duplication with regards to either budget or beneficiary targets.
No funding is yet secured for 2023, but with high likelihood of doing so. NGO X has permission to operate in all proposed locations.

project_name: Provide Lifesaving WASH Assistance to Vulnerable Populations in North West Syria
project_objective:
NGO X proposes to provide lifesaving safe water to approximately 518,999 vulnerable individuals in Idleb Governorate and North Aleppo, Northwest Syria. This will be implemented via the provision of essential support to 37 Water Stations (WSs) that are currently functioning and 4 Water Units (WUs).
NGO X has extensive experience delivering water supply programming in Idleb since 2014. In 2022 NGO X provided clean safe water to the homes of over 800,000 people in Idleb via 51 WS and 12,190 people in North Aleppo via 2 water stations. 
The proposed project builds upon the experience of having successfully delivered several similar projects funded by OCHA, FCDO, ECHO and BHA. The aim of the action is to ensure access to reliable, safe, and clean drinking water to vulnerable conflict-affected communities and IDP sites including host and displaced populations in high priority northern sub-districts of Idleb Governorate and North Aleppo. 
Core activities under water supply sector will include procurement of electricity and/or fuel, minor infrastructure rehabilitation, training the water station operators, coaching of WUs and water quality monitoring. The proposed action will enable people living in the targeted areas to get enough clean and safe drinking water. Improving the access to safe water will reduce the time spent on collecting water, reduce protection risks and prevent the spread of waterborne diseases, often affecting children. Following WASH cluster standards, between 30 - 40 liters/person/day (LPD) will be piped directly to households (HH) to ensure equitable access for all community members. It should be noted that due to funding constraints and limited water network capacity, it may not be possible to go over 35 LPD. 
Under sanitation sub sector: the activities will include the rehabilitation of sewage infrastructure in 4 locations including IDP sites, through converting the open sewer system to closed sewer system in order to reduce the impact of open sewage system and to ensure the sustainability in the sanitation services.    
In addition to that NGO X proposes to implement infrastructure rehabilitation or improvement in targeted sites including roads / shelter rehabilitation to ensure complementarity, sustainability, and access to WASH facilities.
In target areas, to complement WASH activities, HHs—including school children, WU staff and vulnerable individuals benefiting from NGO X food or cash distributions will be reached with essential hygiene promotion sessions adapted to COVID-19 and cholera best working practices as outlined by the WASH cluster. Themes covered will include water safety, water conservation, COVID-19, cholera prevention and safe hygiene practices.
