project_name: Displacement Tracking Matrix: Mobility Tracking of IDPs, Returnees, and Other Mobile Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
Following the crises that has affected Sudan since February 2003 and, in response to the need for accurate information on displacement and the identification of beneficiaries for the delivery of humanitarian aid, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) began its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) program in 2004 to support the Government of Sudan (GoS) and its humanitarian partners in establishing an accurate data collection system and providing data on displacement in areas most affected by the conflict and natural disaster. DTM is a system to track and monitor displacement and population mobility. It is designed to regularly and systematically capture, process and disseminate information to provide a better understanding of the movements and evolving needs of displaced populations, whether on site or en route.
Data collection strategies and tools are based on the DTM global methodology but have been adapted to reflect context and population movements specific to Sudan. IOM has been working in close collaboration with the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC) and partners in the field to establish a unified and systematic method to collect individual data on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees in seven states. Up until 2018, the DTM program in Sudan focused on registration, including biometric registration (since 2010), of IDPs and returnees. Registration was mostly carried out in response to requests from the government and humanitarian partners for the identification of beneficiaries and the delivery of humanitarian assistance (i.e., food vouchers by WFP), positioning DTM Sudan as the reference source of displacement data in the country. There remains a strong need to restructure the program and tailor the operation to better suit the current protracted displacement and return scenario, to in turn inform evidence-based programming by IOM and the wider humanitarian community in Sudan. Specifically, there is the need to further update displacement figures more frequently, comprehensively, systematically, and in regular intervals to ensure that data is continually collected, provides a meaningful resource, and is available through IOM’s DTM system. Since 15 April 2023, military conflict has erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) across Sudan. The fighting has been centralised in Khartoum, and has also broken out across the Darfur region (including cities such as Ag Geneina, El Fasher, and Nyala), as well as in the North (Merowe) and Kordofan (El Obeid). The conflict has led to rapidly increasing civilian vulnerability, significant losses and casualties across Sudan, the destruction of key infrastructure in affected areas (such as hospitals, warehouses, and markets), and the immediate suspension of humanitarian activities, widespread looting of UN facilities, and the evacuation of international staff and foreign nationals. Despite the notable limitations to DTM's logistical operations (given the deteriorating security and economic environments) and the connectivity and telecommunication challenges, DTM has been able to maintain key data collection operations, and has provided the UN community with preliminary estimates of displacement and return. These preliminary estimations have expanded from providing initial information on incidences and mobility (locations of origin to displacement), to capturing information on shelter typology, return intentions, and priority needs. In this way, data collection activities have adapted to the current context, establishing an operational framework for the resumption of Mobility Tracking Rounds. Given the pressing emergency context presented by this military conflict, DTM is best placed to provide essential and evidence-based information about the humanitarian context. DTM forms a core component of IOM’s ongoing response to the unfolding humanitarian crisis, among IOM’s other PC1 programming, in Sudan.

Provide access to life-saving essential healthcare, including mental health to women, men, girls and boys, including ability challenged persons

Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms	
								
The project will work closely with the County Health department and other partners to support health service delivery through supply of essential medicines and technologies, capacity building, technical support, Human resources support, documentation & reporting as well as demand creation for essential health and nutrition services. The project will be implemented in a duration of 8 months in Kajo-Keji County.

project_name: Assistance humanitaire en abri et en Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) pour les sinistrés d'inondation au Niger
project_objective: Dans le cadre de HRP 2023 au travers de ce projet, l'OIM vise à apporter un appui au gouvernement du Niger dans le cadre de la réponse d'urgence aux personnes sinistrées des inondations. Ce projet propose de répondre aux besoins des ménages sinistrés à travers les requêtes qui seront exprimées par le Gouvernement au travers du Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes (MAH/GC). Cette réponse s’adressera uniquement aux ménages vulnérables victimes d’inondations dont les abris ou cases auront été effondrées et/ou ceux dont les Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) auront été emportés par les eaux. Le présent projet poursuit comme objectif d’atteindre 10 000 ménages soit 70 000 personnes à travers tout le Niger prioritairement dans les régions de Zinder, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua. En coordination avec le MAH/GC et la Direction Générale de la Protection Civile (DGPC), l’OIM mettra à disposition 10 000 kits abris et 10 000 kits Biens non-alimentaires qui seront distribués aux ménages sinistrés. En plus des kits, l’OIM couvrira les coûts liés à la logistique et à la distribution des kits. Ce projet ne couvrira pas une zone ou région donnée mais permettra d’intervenir là où les besoins se présentent et aussi de pouvoir compléter les activités des autres acteurs en cas de besoin en tant que prestataire de dernier recours pour la réponse humanitaire en abri d'urgence et BNA. L’OIM en tant que Co-Lead du Groupe de Travail Abri et Bien non-alimentaire (GTABNA) avec le MAH/GC s'assurera que les activités sont menées en étroite coordination avec les autres partenaires humanitaires membres du GTABNA pour la réponse en abri et Biens non-alimentaires pour les ménages sinistrés des inondations au Niger. Conformément à la logique de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et en fonction de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transferts monétaires conditionnels. Cela réduirait considérablement les coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes mais aussi et permettrait aussi de résoudre en partie le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui souvent retarde les interventions. Enfin, la mise en œuvre du présent projet fera l’objet d’un suivi régulier de la qualité des interventions réalisées mais aussi de l’implication des bénéficiaires et autorités locales. Pour cela, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que ses actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires. A cet effet la phase d'évaluation de besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, les sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées à l'attention de communauté bénéficiaires, le mecanisme de ciblage de bénéficiaires sera réalisé en étroite collabation avec les autorités au niveau local (do no harm). Une collaboration étroite faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de près de toutes questions de protection et de LTB. Le cout total du projet sera de 6.090.000 USD.

project_name: Shelter and Non Food Items kits assistance to IDPs, returnees and host communities in high return and natural-hazard affected areas in Burundi
project_objective:
This project aims to address some of the current gaps identified by the SNFI sector in 2023 in 42 priority communes identified in the HNO in Burundi through the provision of comprehensive Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFI) assistance. IOM proposed response will include:  
a) Rapid assessments following natural disasters and other displacement events to assess life-saving needs (including shelter and NFI) of affected individuals.
b) Distribution of Shelter assistance that will include emergency shelters, semi-permanent shelters, repair kits and rental support to returnees, IDPs and host communities based on needs assessments and context, including resettlement assistance for IDPs in protracted displacement situations.
c) Distribution of NFI kits to returnees, IDPs and host communities based on needs assessments and context.
d) Establishment of AAP mechanisms to targeted individuals through the provision of a toll-free hotline hosted in the premises of the Burundian Red Cross. This hotline will be in charge of processing the feedbacks and complaints to whomever it concerns and to call back beneficiaries to provide them with a response when needed.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
The majority of humanitarian needs for Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) in Burundi are caused by recurrent disasters related to torrential rains, strong winds, floods and landslides. These affect thousands of households and cause massive displacement of persons every year, resulting in significant human and material damage, particularly in rural areas.  According to the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM, October 2022), 89 % of the 75,300 displaced persons in Burundi are displaced due to climate related hazards. Between September 2022 and January 2023 only, more than 90,000 individuals were affected dur to climate events, including more than 10,000 IDPs. Additionally, the situation of displacement is prolonged for more than 40% of the 75,300 IDPs who have been displaced for more than one year. On top of the needs of internally displaced persons, in 2023, UNHCR estimates that 75,000 Burundian refugees with high humanitarian needs will return to Burundi, including support on shelter and NFI as they often come back to find their houses destroyed or their land occupied.

In 2023, 218, 438 individuals have Shelter and NFI needs. 

IOM's proposed response is in line with the sector's 2023 strategy and will aim to address objectives 1,2 and 3.

In order to meet objective 1 of the sector strategy, IOM plans to, following a thorough rapid needs assessment, distribute 900 emergency shelter kits, provide rental support to 3,200 households and 8,300 NFI kits to natural hazard affected populations. 

In order to meet objective 2, IOM plans to distribute 2,250 repair kits, 1,000 semi-permanent shelters and 5,500 complete NFI kits to individuals in protracted displacement situation, returnees and host communities.

Finally, in line with Objective 3 of the sector strategy, IOM will strengthen the accountability to affected populations mechanisms through the funding of a hotline dedicated to receive feedback and complaints for SNFI interventions. Feedback and complaints received through the hotline will be directly oriented toward IOM will be used to improve IOM interventions in line with accountability toward affected population. 

Post-distribution monitoring will systematically be conducted to collect feedback on the assistance provided. The results of these monitoring visits will be shared with the sector to share beneficiaries' impressions and lessons learned.

project_name: Amélioration des conditions de vie des populations autochtones et déplacées dans la province du Lac via une assistance d'urgence pour un meilleur accès à l’eau, l’hygiène, l’assainissement et à la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle
project_objective:
Le Tchad est confronté à plusieurs situations critiques. La province du Lac est l’une des zones les plus affectées : insécurité liée aux conflits armés et intercommunautaires, pauvreté et chocs climatiques s'y cumulent. Les incidents de protection contre les populations civiles les contraignent à se déplacer. L’insécurité alimentaire, la malnutrition croissante, les urgences sanitaires potentialisent également le besoin de se déplacer. D’après le DTM #18 de l’OIM (11/2022), on compte actuellement plus de 239 000 personnes déplacées dans la province du Lac. Ces mouvements obligent les populations à abandonner leurs moyens d'existence, ce qui compromet davantage leur sécurité économique et alimentaire. Les données du Cadre harmonisé (décembre 2022) révèlent que la situation alimentaire dans la région va se détériorer de façon dramatique en 2023. En effet, le taux de personnes en phase d’IPC 3+ évoluerait de 8 à 30% dans le département du Fouli et de 10 à 25% dans le département de Kaya, entre la période actuelle et la période projetée de juin-août 2023. Contribuer à la restauration des moyens d’existence des populations apparaît donc essentiel, voire indispensable.  

Les déplacements engendrent également des besoins urgents et prioritaires en termes d’accès aux services d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement (EHA). Le diagnostic mené par Solidarités International (SI) en novembre 2022 révèle que les populations déplacées ont accès, en moyenne, à 7,25L d’eau par jour, soit la moitié des 15L recommandés par les standards Sphère.  

Au regard de ces constatations, le projet présenté ici propose une assistance d’urgence en EHA et en moyens d’existence à, respectivement, 13 560 personnes et 400 ménages vulnérables déplacés à la suite d’un choc. Cette action viendra ainsi en complément et/ou en continuité des réponses apportées par le mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM).

project_name: Multi-sectoral life-saving assistance, including life-saving GBV prevention and response services, to conflict-affected population in Pulka, Monguno and Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria
project_objective:
This project’s objective is to contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity of the most vulnerable, IDPs and host community, including children under 5, pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, the elderly, and people with disabilities, in the hard-to-reach areas of Pulka and Monguno (respectively Gwoza and Monguno LGA), and in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC). To meet the most vulnerable populations’ urgent and complex needs, and ensure a long-lasting impact, integrated multi-sectoral activities in health, nutrition, protection, psychosocial support (PSS), food security, and livelihoods, will be implemented. The response will also be based on a robust community-based approach, with community activities planned for all sectors to ensure beneficiaries' and communities' ownership of the project. This comprehensive approach and the proposed activities align with all the sectors’ and HRP's priorities, including targeting hard-to-reach areas in Northeast Nigeria’s Borno State, the state most affected by the large-scale humanitarian crisis.
Premiere Urgence Internationale will continue to provide free quality life-saving healthcare services to IDPs and host community in the 9 facilities the organization already supports in Maiduguri MC, Monguno, and Pulka. These services include free outpatient consultations to all age groups and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRH) services. SRH activities comprise ante/postnatal care, 24 hours skilled birth delivery services, including Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmONC), and Gender-based Violence (GBV) treatment with CMR (Clinical Management of Rape). 
PUI will continue to provide life-saving treatment to children under 5 suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) by supporting 4 OTPS across all three locations (one in Maiduguri’s Bollori II, two in Monguno, and one in Pulka), for treatment of SAM without medical complications, and three Stabilization Centres (SCs), one in every three locations, to provide treatment to SAM with medical complications. In case further emergencies arise, PUI plans to increase its SCs' bed capacities in Monguno and Pulka, and to establish three more OTPs. The nutrition response will include systemic identification and referrals of children suffering from SAM to PUI-supported OTPs and SCs, and awareness-raising sessions and sensitization implemented at community level.
PUI will continue to implement a range of activities to contribute to strengthening targeted protection services to address the needs and vulnerability of persons at heightened risks of violence and exploitation, with tailored responses for GBV survivors, through internal/external referrals whenever needed (i.e legal assistance). To prevent GBV and violence, awareness sessions for women and girls on their rights, as well as for community members, boys, men will be conducted. Community knowledge on protection will be strengthened, with key community stakeholders receiving training on protection issues, including GBV, mental health, PSS, to in turn support identification of cases and concerns, and ensure referrals. PUI will continue to ensure protection monitoring in the intervention areas, to ensure risk identification, referrals, concerted and tailored interventions, as well as advocacies with partners at all levels.
To promote the targeted beneficiaries' self-reliance, and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance, PUI will provide food assistance to 5,390 vulnerable individual beneficiaries on a monthly basis for 12 months, as food e-vouchers or e-cash. PUI will identify 700 individuals among beneficiaries of PUI Nutrition services and survivors of GBV or persons exposed to Protection risks due to their economic vulnerability. These persons will receive a training on the management of small business, and a start capital to launch an Income Generating Activity (IGA) of their choice.

project_name: Provision of timely life-saving WASH response to the most vulnerable communities affected by conflict, floods, disease outbreak and malnutrition through integrated response in Panyikang, Wau,  Raga, Duk, uror, Bor South, GPAA, Kapoeta North, Ayod and Fangak counties.
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to grapple with challenges of limited access to WASH infrastructure which has been attributed to continuous years of massive flooding that has been exacerbated by continued inter-communal conflicts among various communities which has caused enormous destruction and vandalizing of the already limited existing WASH infrastructures.
Relief Corps Organization seeks to execute WASH actions that will contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality attributable to the consumption and use of unsafe water, the lack of or inadequate sanitation facilities during emergency situations and inadequate hygiene practices. 
Further, RCO aims at responding to the prevailing WASH gaps affecting the vulnerable populations in most complicated emergency zones – using its past experiences in emergency. RCO will to target 5,000 households (30,000 beneﬁciaries amongst the most vulnerable emergency affected IDPs, returnees and host communities directly affected by the floods & conﬂict with a WASH/GBV, WASH/NUT & WASH/Health integrated response in line with 2022/23 HRP WASH cluster strategic objectives through addressing and provision of acute WASH needs among beneﬁciaries at risk of gender and sexual based violence, those at risk of health-related WASH $ malnutrition.
The project will equally address malnutrition and health related cases by providing WASH services at OTP/SC centers and PHCC/PHCU health facilities as well as addressing the root causes of active of WASH related diseases and protection especially among IDPs, women and girls who face GBV, a key protection concern while they trekking for long distances in search for water among others.
To ensure this succeeds, the project (with strict adherence to COVID-19 guidelines) will train WASH/Nutrition/Health hygiene promoters on core WASH’Nut, WASH’Health and WASH’GBV competencies including referrals and case reporting and they will in turn train others and conduct Mass hygiene promotion campaigns. 
Boreholes and hand dug wells will be rehabilitated and drilled by the trained pump mechanics and Water Management Committees who will be flushing out to ensure they (bore holes & hand dug well) are well cleaned and removed turbidity by air compressors and treated with chlorine for disinfection and improve water quality as well as replacing the worn-out parts. RCO will address the sanitation situation both at the communal level and institutions like OTP/SC, schools and PHCC/PHCU health centers through rehabilitations of gender/disability segregated latrines with doors and locks as well as installation of a hand washing facilities at each latrine.
Finally the project will synergize multi sector response by coordinating with counterpart agencies on ground to ensure effectiveness and referrals of other cluster objectives in addition to mainstreaming cross-cutting programmatic approaches like COVID-19, AAP/AQA principles, protection including GBV/ Sexual exploitation mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conﬂict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention and sustainability.

project_name: Prevention and Treatment of Malnutrition among Children (6- 59 Months) , Pregnant and Lactating Women
project_objective:
Adequate and quality nutrition is a child’s basic human right, with well-nourished children having a better chance of survival and longer-term growth, development, health and productivity. WFP Sudan aims to prevent and treat malnutrition by providing specialized nutritious foods to children from 6-59 months as well as Pregnant and Breastfeeding Women (PBW) among refugee, IDP and vulnerable and conflict-affected population. Geographical targeting of WFP’s treatment program as part of comprehensive Community Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) which informed by a comprehensive analysis of national nutrition survey results (such as S3M II) and Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC).  
The proposed response from WFP is in line with the Nutrition Sector Strategy and with the Multi-Year Humanitarian Response Strategy of Sudan. Through this project, WFP will be responding to the nutritional needs of targeted beneficiaries under outcomes identified by nutrition sector with particular focus on DO NOT HARM and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) principles. 
During April, fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has caused tremendous human suffering and exacerbated significant pre-existing humanitarian needs amongst the civilian population in Sudan coupled with mas displacement of households which has resulted in an increase of vulnerability to malnutrition that attributed to inflations, reduced access to 
food, lack of water and poor hygiene situation as well as increased risk of infections. 
1. The deterioration of the nutrition situation has led to an estimated 30% increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition in hotspot areas,15% increase in IDP hosting states and 10% increase in other localities. 
2. Interruption of nutrition monitoring and reporting impacting on the understanding of the evolving 
nutrition situation in most parts of the country particularly in the hotpot areas.
3. The estimated target and funding requirement is for seven month from June to December 2023.

project_name: Traitement de la malnutrition aigue moderée et prevention dans les camps de réfugiés au Tchad
project_objective:
Le Tchad du fait de sa frontière avec beaucoup de pays instables enregistrent des vagues de populations cherchant refuge au niveau du territoire Tchadien depuis une période de plus de 10 ans. Il s’agit principalement des :
-	Réfugiés Soudanais implantés à l’EST dans les sites de Iriba, Farchana, Gozbeida et Ambdjarass
-	Refugiés Centrafricains implantés au Sud du Tchad au niveau des sites de Doholo, Gondje, Amboko, Dosseye, Belom et Moyo
-	Réfugiés du Nigéria se trouvant au niveau du site de Dar El Salam dans la province du Lac
-              Refugiés Camerounais se trouvant à la périphérie de la ville de Ndjamena
Au total c’est 592,769 réfugiés, 200,031 IDPs et 100,249 retournés qui ont été recensés au niveau du territoire Tchadien en 2022 (UNHCR 2022) avec une population constituée majoritairement de femmes et d’enfants. Les différentes évaluations qui ont été conduites au sein de la population de réfugiés mettent en évidence plusieurs problématiques en lien avec les défis liés aux conditions de vie, à l’insertion et à l’intégration, la faible autonomisation des populations de réfugiés, les difficultés d’accès aux services sociaux de base notamment la santé, l’éducation, l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement. 
Sur le plan de la nutrition, la dernière enquête SENS qui a été réalisé par le UNHCR et le PAM a montré que les prévalences de malnutrition aiguë et chronique ont atteint des proportions inquiétantes dans la plupart des sites enquêtés. Six sur les vingt sites de réfugiés notamment Ourecassoni, Iridimi, Amnaback Touloum, Milé et Kounougou ont enregistré des prévalences de MAG supérieur à 10%. Quatre des 20 sites ont enregistré une prévalence de MAG qui dépasse le seuil d’urgence de 15% fixé par l’OMS.

project_name: Projet d’assistance nutritionnelle aux enfants 6-23 mois et femmes enceintes et allaitantes pendant la période de soudure au Sahel
project_objective:
La malnutrition aiguë demeure un problème de santé publique majeur au Tchad avec une prévalence de la Malnutrition Aiguë Globale au niveau national estimée à 8,6 % (SMART 2022) ; ce qui représente une situation moyenne d’après la nouvelle classification de l’OMS. Mais cette prévalence au niveau national masque des disparités au niveau des provinces où on note une dégradation au niveau des provinces de la zone sahélo-saharienne.  La prévalence de la MAG atteint ou dépasse le seuil préoccupant (10%) au niveau de 15/23 provinces (Wadi Fira (17,7%), Borkou (16,2%), Ennedi Est (15,7%), Ennedi Ouest (14,4%), Salamat (14,3%), Batha (13,8%], Bahr El Gazal (12,9%), Kanem (12,2%), Ouaddaï (12,1%), Tibesti (11,6%), Sila (11,1%), Lac (11,0%), N’Djamena (10,7%), Guéra (10,6%) et Hadjer Lamis (10,5%)). Elles constituent comme telles les provinces prioritaires d’intervention car considérant seule la zone sahelo-saharienne on observe la MAG à 12,2% contre 5,2% pour la zone soudanienne.
Cette situation nutritionnelle préoccupante qui dure depuis des années est exacerbée par de multiples crises récurrentes notamment les conflits armés avec d’important mouvements de population dans le Sud (crise RCA), à l’Est (crise du Darfour et de la RCA), dans le Chari Baguirmi, Ndjamena (Crise Cameroun) et dans la zone du Lac (attaque des GANE dont Boko Haram), avec les populations insulaires qui sont les plus affectées et les moins accessibles par l’aide humanitaire pour des raisons sécuritaires.
On note aussi que le taux de mortalité des enfants de moins de 5 ans qui est également un facteur de gravité a dépassé le seuil critique de 2 personnes/10 000 habitants/ jour dans une province (Sila) (SMART 2022).
Face à cette situation nutritionnelle caractérisée par des crises multiformes et d’autres facteurs qui peuvent accentuer la dégradation de la situation nutritionnelle au Tchad, le PAM propose la mise en œuvre d’un programme de prévention de la malnutrition chez les enfants de moins de 2 ans et les femmes enceintes/allaitantes pour atténuer la degradation de la situation nutritionnelle dans cette population vulnerable.

project_name: Projet de resilience pour la population vulnerable
project_objective:
Le Tchad est un pays d'Afrique subsaharien enclavé à faible revenu, classé parmi les pays les plus pauvres par les Nations unies. L’agriculture et l’élevage constituent les moyens d’existence de la grande partie de la population essentiellement rurale. La majeure partie de son territoire est située dans la ceinture sahélienne, le Tchad est sujet à des chocs climatiques saisonniers qui entraînent des crises alimentaires régulières affectant la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations. L'insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition restent récurrentes et à des niveaux très élevés. L'indice mondial de la faim pour 2022 place le Tchad au 117 place sur 121 pays avec un score de 37,2. Cet indice présente une légère baisse par rapport aux autres années (2000 : 50,7 ; 2007 : 49,0 ; 2014 : 40,7 mais reste toujours classé dans les niveaux de faim alarmants. Sur le plan mondial, le score GHI 2022 est considéré comme modéré (18,2). 
La situation pourrait se détériorer au regard des crises mondiales actuelles qui se superposent ainsi que leurs conséquences qui sont entre autres les effets du changement avec les inondations qu’a connu la grande partie du pays cette année ; la flambée des prix des denrées alimentaires à cause de la guerre en Ukraine ainsi que les effets de la pandémie du COVID 19. En plus de ces crises s’ajoutent les facteurs sous-jacents qui sont la pauvreté, les inégalités, la mauvaise gouvernance, le mauvais état des infrastructures, une faible productivité agricole, qui dans leur ensemble, contribuent à la faim chronique et à la vulnérabilité.
L’analyse de la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle au Tchad (cadre harmonisé, novembre 2022) fait ressortir que sur les soixante-sept (67) départements analysés, cinq (5) connaîtront des déficits de survie (Mangalmé, Batha Est, Dagana, La Nya et Loug Chari) et vingt-sept (27) autres des déficits de protection de moyens d’existence. Le bilan céréalier prévisionnel dégage un déficit net de -270 163 tonnes avec une disponibilité apparente de 144 kg/pers/an, soit un déficit de 15 kg/pers/an. 
La situation nutritionnelle demeure préoccupante dans la plupart des provinces des zones sahéliennes et sahariennes. Sur le plan national, la prévalence de la Malnutrition Aiguë Globale (MAG) est de 11% dont et celle de la malnutrition sévère (MAS) est de 2,1% (MAS) (cf. enquête SMART de septembre/octobre 2021). 
Les résultats de l’analyse de la situation de l’insécurité alimentaire aiguë actuelle révèlent que 809 237 personnes se retrouvent dans la phase crise pour la période courante (Octobre - Décembre 2022) et pour la phase projetée près de 1 480 287 personnes seraient en « phase crise » et 32 483 personnes seraient dans la « phase d’urgence ». 
A travers ce projet, nous comptons entreprendre des actions de résilience en faveur des populations en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle et aussi pour les populations en phase sous pression pour protéger leurs moyens d’existence dans les cinq départements qui sont susceptibles de connaitre les déficits de survie à savoir Mangalmé, Batha Est, Dagana, La Nya et Loug Chari. La zone soudanienne enregistre des baisses de production céréalière prévisionnelle de 2,3 % par rapport à l’année 2021 et de 2,4% par rapport à la moyenne des cinq (5) dernières. Pour cette raison nous envisageons également d'entreprendre des activités de resilience dans les départements tels que la Nya pende ; la pende, le département de Kou Est et Ouest; la grande Sido et le lac Iro pour booster la production. Ces actions s’alignent étroitement avec les objectifs fixés par la coordination humanitaire dans la définition stratégique : (i) Sauver des vies ; (ii) Renforcer la résilience.
Le présent projet trouve sa valeur ajoutée dans l’appui et le renforcement de la résilience des ménages vulnérables vivant dans ces zones travers une assistance alimentaire conditionnelle. Il concernera 280,000 personnes ce qui représentent 16% du caselot .

project_name: School Feeding for Refugees and Host Communities in Chad
project_objective:
The results of the Joint Assessment Mission (JAM) conducted in 2021 by WFP and UNHCR reveals that most refugees’ camps in Chad identified the lack of regular school meals programme as one of the main reasons for children not attending school, after the limited number of classrooms and lack of school equipment. One of the main demands made by refugees and their host communities to help tackle the current malnutrition crisis and school dropout rates for both refugee and host community children is the introduction of a programme of regular school meals in the 213 schools in the camps and host villages.. Equal access to a school feeding package will enable refugee children to learn, thrive and develop their potential, build individual and collective resilience, and contribute to peaceful coexistence and civil society.
Under Strategic Outcome 1 in the WFP Country Strategic Plan (2019-2023), , WFP aims to support crisis-affected people in targeted areas to be able to meet their basic food and nutrition needs during and in the aftermath of crises. Under this outcome, WFP will implement school meals for crisis-affected populations and host communities in crisis-affected areas. The WFP school meals programme objectives are in support of the implementation of the Government of Chad’s National Policy of School Feeding since 2017. 
In line with the strategy of the Ministry of National Education of Chad, schools in refugee camps are integrated into the Chadian education system. WFP plans to distribute nutritious and diversified hot meals procured from the local community where possible, through the promotion of local farmers to supply schools according to the basket and the quantities established. The school menus will be enriched with fresh products from vegetable gardens according to seasonality. Food procurement from local sources close to the project area will increase the income of smallholders, leading to an increase of their productivity and investment. In addition, better access to economic opportunities will contribute to the economic growth of the household.
In addition, WFP also links with its resilience activities inside refugee camps in Ouaddaï, Lac and Sila, which focus, in particular, on local purchase of food or joint planning for a friendly school feeding environment (kitchen, storage space, water and sanitation) inside schools.
To promote social cohesion between refugee and indigenous communities, meals will be distributed to refugee as well as host community students attending schools in refugee camps without any distinction of origin. In addition, during the implementation of activities, WFP will ensure that the canteen management committees will be made up of both local and refugee populations at the level of all decision-making and participation bodies.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire et nutritionnelle d'urgence aux populations les plus vulnérables en insécurité alimentaire severe pendant la période de soudure
project_objective:
L’analyse du Cadre Harmonisé de novembre 2022 prévoit pour la saison de soudure que 1,512,770 personnes seront en insécurité alimentaire sévère pour la phase projetée de juin à aout 2022.  En 2022, la situation alimentaire s’est légèrement améliorée dans le sahel en raison d’une campagne moyenne avec une production céréalière en hausse de 9,9 % par rapport à l’année dernière et de 1,7 % par rapport à la moyenne des 5 dernière année. Cette hausse est imputable dans la zone sahélienne qui enregistre globalement une hausse de 14% par rapport à l’année dernière et de 4% par rapport à la moyenne quinquennale.  Par contre la zone soudanienne a enregistré une baisse de 2,3% et 2,4% respectivement par rapport à 2021 et à la moyenne. Le bilan céréalier prévisionnel dégage un déficit net de – 270 163 tonnes. 

Le prix des denrées alimentaires de base en octobre 2022 sont globalement en hausse par rapport a ceux de l’année dernière et de la moyenne des cinq dernières années. Cette hausse est essentiellement due aux perturbations des approvisionnements en produits importés à cause des conflits, baisse de l’euro par rapport au dollar et les fortes demandes des céréales et d’autres produits agricoles de Soudanais. 

L’analyse de consommation alimentaire indique que 5.6% et 18.7% des ménages du Tchad ont respectivement une consommation alimentaire pauvre et limite. Les départements de la zone saharienne sont principalement touchés par cette détérioration. 

L’analyse des résultats HEA ressort que sur les 67 départements analyses, cinq connaitrons des déficits de survie (Mangalme, Batha Est, Dagana, La Nya et Lou Chari) et 27 départements rencontreront des déficits de protection de moyen d’existence. 

Toutes fois une mauvaise répartition des pluies dans le temps et dans l’espace ont été constatées dans la bande sahélienne et une détérioration dans la zone soudanienne due en partie aux inondations ayant affecté la production agricole et d’autres moyens d’existence. Une détérioration globale de la situation est possible en raison d’une production certes en hausse mais limitée au sahel et d’énormes tensions sur les marchés, La hausse de prix des céréales et la détérioration des termes de l’échange bétail/céréales et cultures de rente/céréales affectent également la consommation alimentaire, l’état nutritionnel et l’évolution des moyens d’existence. Cette situation affectera plus de 3,8 millions de personnes qui sont actuellement dans la phase sous pression et font face à la dégradation de moyens de subsistance pour avoir un accès minimum aux services sociaux de base et risquent de basculer en phase crise.

Les résultats du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2022 font ressortir 9 départements seront en « phase 3 – crise » pour la période projetée de juin à aout avec 1 480 287 personnes en phase de crise et 32 483 personnes en « phase 4 - urgence ». Tandis que 3 824 287 personnes sont sous pression (Phase 2).

La situation nutritionnelle est aussi très préoccupante au Tchad bien que la prévalence soit de 8.6 % pour la malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG) et de 1.5% pour la malnutrition aigüe sévère (MAS). Selon les résultats de la SMART 2023, au total, 13 provinces sur 23 sont en situation préoccupante avec une prévalence de la malnutrition aigüe et un taux de mortalité élevé supérieur aux seuils sévères ou critiques. Elles constituent les provinces prioritaires d’intervention. Parmi elles, 3 provinces sont en situation d’urgence car elles présentent des taux supérieurs aux seuils critique de l’OMS pour la malnutrition aigüe globale (MAG ≥ 15 %). La zone saharo-sahélienne a enregistrée une prévalence de la MAG de 12.2% contre 5.2% pour la zone soudanienne. 

Le PAM planifie appuyer 1,000,000 personnes avec une assistance alimentaire inconditionnelle pour trois mois (juin à aout) avec rations complètes. Cette assistance alimentaire sera combinée à une assistance nutritionnelle afin d’assister 75,000 enfants de 6 à 23 mois ainsi que 50,000 femmes enceintes.

project_name: Provision of sustainable primary health care services to Rohingya community living in refugee camp-24  in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
""MedGlobal will provide essential primary healthcare services at the Health Post operated by MedGlobal in Camp 24 as per Minimum Essential Service package (Health Post level) following clinical guidelines of Bangladesh and Sphere Standards. Besides, prevention and treatment of communicable and non-communicable disease will be prioritized. Special health camps and telemedicine service sessions will be organized for catering special health needs. MedGlobal will also engage CHWs in raising community level awareness, promotion and increasing preparedness on health issues and emergency response. They will be equipped with an electronic health system as developed by MedGlobal to strengthen community to facility referral systems.
From the MedGlobal Health Post in Camp 24, Leda, Teknaf -minimum essential primary healthcare services required as per health sector guideline will be provided that includes outpatient curative care, maternal and child health, adolescent health, family planning, gender-based violence, diseases, mental health and psychosocial services, capacity building for local health care professionals, and community health worker such as case-follow up and public health education keeping gender, disability and diversity inclusion considerations in programming. The activities and outputs will be monitored using KOBO toolbox and internal clinic census, and reports will be made available to the Health Sector. The project also intends to provide crucial medical supplies and equipment to other camp facilities. All activities will be prepared in accordance with strategies of the Health Sector to ensure that they are consistent with the Health Sector's priorities and strategies in Camp 24. MedGlobal will prioritize global advocacy through showcasing outcomes and lessons learned from the activities. To ensure accountability to affected population the following steps will be taken:
(1) A continuing logic model planning process based on needs assessments and baseline surveys with the goal of involving the community.
(2) Rigorous audits and budgets to ensure financial transparency; and
(3) Program monitoring and evaluation to assure program quality management.
(4) Protection, Age, Gender, and Diversity (AGD), disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations, PSEA, disaster risk management, and environment and ecosystem rehabilitation for addressing the impacts of climate change to be mainstreamed in the MedGlobal 2022 sustainable operation strategy. At the health post, MedGlobal's work concentrates on 51 percent women and includes maternity care for young mothers, as well as family planning. Gender, sex, disability, diversity, and age are reported in the statistics. MedGlobal is already performing needs/baseline evaluations for 2022, with women, girls, disability, diversity, and other age groups in mind, and we will aim to incorporate the results into our next logical framework model and project management cycle. We already conducted multiple COVID 19 capacity projects in 2020 and 2021 including supporting to Bangladesh government health facility e.g., the Upazila Health Complex with Central Oxygen Systems and other medical equipment and supplies to health facilities in the FDMN camps, and we spent roughly $505,000 on the projects. MedGlobal is committed to building the capacity of the health sector partners. In this JRP MedGlobal with collaborate with health sector and SRH working group in building local capacity for reducing maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity. ""

project_name: Kalyana: Ensure Access to life-saving integrated and sustainable services to the Rohingya population & host communities in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh.
project_objective:
Tdh will continue to ensure access to quality health services at two PHCs in camp 26 and 27, with a focus on infants, children, adolescents, and their mothers. Across both PHCs, the PRM funded program will ensure 150,000 OPD consultations each year. Given the PHC is one of the first entry points with an established service delivery infrastructure in the community, Tdh will continue to support capacity building of health care service providers in both PHCs, enabling them to adequately identify and refer vulnerable children and caregivers to child protection services. All health services will continue to be delivered with utmost adherence to the COVID-19 Standard Operating Procedures. An Electronic Medical Record ( EMR) system will continue to be used, with the aim of enhancing data capture, validation, analysis, timely reporting, and informed decision making. Tdh will continue providing the full Essential Package of Health Services at the two PHCs, including services for Mental Health, Basic Emergency Obstetric and New-born Care (BEmONC), Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI), Non-Communicable Diseases and nutrition. MHPSS support will be done by Psychologist. This will ensure a continuum of quality care by improving patient diagnosis and treatment, reducing redundancy in diagnostic testing, and supporting more efficient and effective decision-making and care. Both PHCs have a dedicated pharmacy with an automated logistics management system and an adequate level of diagnostic facilities to address primary health care services with a provision of immunization services. Tdh PHCs will continue to support COVID-19 testing and vaccination as well as maintain triage and infection prevention protocol. Integrated community outreach activities will continue by a multi-skilled community outreach team reaching an estimated 15,000 beneficiaries. Sessions will focus on disseminating information on health, child protection and hygiene awareness in the camps, and host communities. To reduce home delivery, Traditional Birthing Attendants (TBAs) will be engaged to promote facility-based births. The project will further increase the capacity of maternity services to ensure deliveries under a high-quality standards framework, and that antenatal and postnatal care processes and results are in place. This includes strengthening Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services such as 24/7 BEmoNC, ANC, PNC, and family planning within both  PHCs. Tdh will follow key protocols such as Helping Babies Survive, Helping Mothers Survive, Helping Babies Breathe, and will provide training to physicians on new-born treatment protocols. Tdh will continue sharing its expert knowledge to other organizations, especially NNGOs, of Simulation of Essential Skills in Obstetrical and Neonatal care (SIMESON), which trains midwives and healthcare workers through the use of Laerdal mannequins. 

Through the strengthening of counselling activities to mothers in the Breastfeeding corner equipped with an IYCF Counsellor, and through outreach activities, Tdh will continue increasing number of children under 6 months who are exclusively breastfeed. Due to availability of a SAM/MAM) centre adjacent to the PHC, Tdh will focus on identifying the children suffering from malnutrition, referring them, and following up after they received nutritional services.
Through nutrition screening and outreach team support, Tdh will be able to ensure 100% referral, engage Traditional Birth Attendant to improve referral for facility delivery, support drop out for EPI vaccination and promote  family planning services. Through multi skill community volunteer support with PNGO work for integration of health, WASH and protection activities. Tdh will roll out EMR system and improve capacity building of other actors. Tdh will increase coordination with local actors for transitioning two PHCs through a detailed handover plan, selecting a local partner with capacity development.

project_name: Kalyana: Ensure Access to life-saving integrated and sustainable services to the Rohingya population & host communities in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh.
project_objective:
In 2023, Tdh will scale up its WASH response through gender-responsive, rights-based, adolescent and youth-friendly inclusive services in camp 26, camp 27 and the surrounding host communities. WASH activities will offer knowledge and awareness on how to maintain personal hygiene and WASH facilities in appropriate ways. Tdh will also address adequate and equitable access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene, which Tdh continuously advocates for. All activities will ensure the do-no harm principle by prioritizing the safety and dignity of women and girls. Tdh will continue its sensitization regarding safety measures before and during natural disasters, including disaster risk reduction, AWD/dengue outbreak, COVID issues etc. WASH operations and maintenance committee and key stakeholders were included throughout the project development and community feedback mechanism and response will be maintained during the implementation period.  
Tdh WASH activities will focus on Rohingya refugees residing in camps as well as the surrounding host communities, according to the gaps and needs at different community levels, being inclusive to age (05-17 years boy and girls, 18-59 years men and women, and 60 years plus elderly men and women), gender and diversity (If there are any transgender families living there, the project will also support them). Tdh will continue to operate and maintain the Feacal Sludge Management plant (desludging, treatment, and disposal) that is already built (including an incinerator) in camp 27 as well as waste management activities (collection, transportation, segregation, and disposal) including organic composting. Tdh-operated FSM and waste management services will continue to receive, sludge, treat and dispose (dry sludge and waste) from the camps 26 and 27, the two Primary Health Care Centers run by Tdh and the host communities, as well as the Tdh Multi-Purpose Community Centres. The two PHCs run by Tdh have an incinerator but given the PHC’s current production of large quantities of contaminated waste which cannot be treated at the PHC that’s why an autoclave will also be installed in one PHC to sterilize plastic parts of infectious waste then all waste will be managed at waste management plant, where crusher machine, pits (ash and sharp) and incinerator is already built-in accordance with proper standards. Tdh will continue to operate and maintain the WASH facilities in the PHCs, Camps and surrounding host community as well as construct/rehabilitate/decommission WASH facilities (latrine, bathing cubicle, garbage bin, and environmental cleaning area) in the Camps based upon their condition and needs. Additionally plastic recycling plant will be installed in camp 27 (to make toys, ring, slab, alphabet cube, and bricks/tiles). Due to the scarcity of water in Teknaf, 03 water recycling hand washing station will be installed in camp 26 and 27 (02 at PHC and 01 in camp), to ensure access to hand washing. Tdh will conduct continued management and improvements of all facilities to ensure adequate Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)/disinfection.
Awareness raising activities will be delivered to both refugees and host communities through household sessions/meeting, campaigns, day celebrations and the development and distribution of IEC/BCC materials. These activities will cover the topics of waste management, sanitation, handwashing, COVID-19/AWD/Dengue, and Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) among adolescent and women. This will be complimented by the distribution of NFI/WASH kits (during emergency Tdh will distribute NFI items as contingency plan, as like; handwashing device, WASH kit, MHM kits at HH’s level) to ensure beneficiaries’ adequate WASH support.

project_name: Strengthening child protection services for the well-being of children and adolescents of Rohingya and host community
project_objective:
Tdh will continue child protection services for the well-being of children and adolescents of Rohingya and host community with the objective is to strengthening protective factors and reducing risk factors. Tdh will operate an Integrated and Holistic Child protection program in camp 27 at every level of the socio-ecological framework. Besides this, Tdh Child Protection (CP) sector has been implementing child protection interventions since 2017 in refugee camps and host communities across Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazilas of Cox’s Bazar.
Tdh's Child Protection Sector wants to strengthen services and systems for protecting children throughout the camps and host communities by 2023. The program will maintain sectoral coordination with a priority on integrated services for children with disabilities while ensuring the continuation of existing services such as, unstructured psychosocial support (PSS), structured PSS, case management services, adolescent engagement, and community-based child protection mechanisms, such as the Community-based child protection committee (CBCPC). Children with disabilities will get the services listed above in every area of the Child Protection program. To provide prompt assistance, referral support for kids and teens, especially kids with impairments will be boosted. The program will take the effort to make sure that every facility is secure from calamity. For better understanding on the part of the emergency response team, PSS programming will be tailored to the specific needs of girls and boys with a particular focus on adolescents and with the objective of increasing resilience and well-being From the MPCC/home-based one and one session and Child Play Area (CPA), children from both refugee and host communities will be received support. Tdh will complement these one-off, low-impact structured play activities at the CPA with more holistic, longer-term structured PSS in the Multi-Purpose Community Centre (MPCC) at camp 27. The objective will be to strengthen children’s resilience and well-being through weekly sessions for two months, targeting core competencies outlined in Tdh’s MHPSS Framework.
By attending the meetings, workshops and offering technical help as needed, Tdh will continue to maintain excellent collaboration with the Child Protection Sub-Sector (CPSS), Case Management Technical Working Group (CMTWG), and CPSS localization working group. Through active participation and contribution, Tdh CP activities will be carried out in coordination with  protection working group (PWG), the mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) working group, the age and disability working group,  and the youth working group. The status report, the 5W report, and the need-based report would all get sectoral contributions from Tdh.
Child protection data will be gender-, age- and disability- disaggregated. In line with the IASC Guidelines on Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Action, the Washington Group Short Set of Questions will be used to ensure Tdh identifies the risks, barriers and needs faced by persons with disabilities.

project_name: Protegiendo vidas y fortaleciendo soluciones sostenibles en la respuesta en Albergues y población albergada en Honduras
project_objective:
Durante las tormentas Eta e Iota y los fenómenos meteorológicos que han afectado el territorio hondureño desde 2020, NRC ha trabajado con población con doble afectación: Por fenómenos climatológicos y OSV. 
Es en este sentido que NRC ha detectado las necesidades que el sector de coordinación de alojamientos aún presenta. 
NRC mediante este proyecto pretende rehabilitar la infraestructura y servicios de las edificaciones comunitarias que han funcionado o pueden llegar a funcionar como albergues temporales. NRC asegurará el cumplimiento de estándares mínimos para el alojamiento en estas edificaciones. NRC incorporará los requerimientos que las
poblaciones vulnerables presentan (género, movilidad universal, edad).
Asimismo, NRC tomará en consideración las características ambientales propias de la localidad como ser temperatura,
clima y costumbres locales.
NRC proveerá atención personalizada y de calidad, siguiendo un enfoque de protección a
todas sus actividades, priorizando la identificación de casos y refiriéndolos al mecanismo
que la organización cuenta para su atención y seguimiento.
NRC pretende dar al proyecto un enfoque sistémico fortaleciendo las capacidades
institucionales de los diferentes entes involucrados en el sector de gestión de albergues
mediante talleres de formación enfocados en esta temática adicionando módulos de
protección y temas transversales.
NRC asegurará mediante evaluaciones periódicas y con la coordinación del clúster de
CCCM la situación y la pertinencia de los servicios en los centros de albergue temporal y
espontáneo. De este modo podrá proveer asistencia adecuada y coordinar esfuerzos con
otros instituciones gubernamentales y actores humanitarios dedicados al sector.

project_name: Mejora de la gestión de alojamiento y estructuras comunitarias para personas migrantes o en riesgo de desplazamiento en El Salvador.
project_objective:
Desde el año 2019 el Consejo Noruego para Refugiados (NRC) trabaja desde su componente de Alojamiento e Infraestructura en Honduras y El Salvador, mejorando las condiciones de infraestructura en 11 centros educativos en ES, además de 2 proyectos de vivienda en Honduras y un fuerte despliegue en 21 Albergues colectivos durante Eta e Iota.  Asimismo, el NRC ha ejecutado proyectos de mejora de infraestructura en las instalaciones de la “Gerencia de Atención al Migrante GAMI”. 

Mediante el proyecto “Mejora de servicios de alojamiento y estructuras comunitarias para personas migrantes o en riesgo de desplazamiento en El Salvador. El NRC reestablecerá a condiciones dignas y equipará establecimientos de albergue colectivos, casas de migrantes o centros de recepción de migrantes retornados.
