project_name: Improving access of vulnerable families to multisectoral needs through MPCA in Gaza
project_objective:
DanChurchAid/Norwegian Church Aid (DCA/NCA) and its partner, MAAN Development Centre (MAAN) propose a project that aims at supporting 300 crisis-affected families whose children were exposed to child protection threats, enabling them to meet their basic needs through multipurpose cash assistance. 
The pool of beneficiaries will be the families whose children were targeted previously by the child protection response through MAAN development center, where they received psychological first aid and referral services. However, based on the available data, the majority of previously targeted children and their families are socioeconomically vulnerable and are with poor access the basic services.  
The 300 families will be targeted based on socioeconomic and vulnerability criteria. The targeted localities are Gaza north (Beit Hanoun, Beit Lahiya, Jabalia, Jabalia camp, AL Qarya Al Badawiya), Der Al Balah (Burij, Maghazi, Nusirat, Zawaida, Der Al Balah), Khanyounis (Mawasi, Qarara, Bani Suhaila, Khanyounis Camp, Qa' Al Quren) and Rafah (Al Bayuk, Rafah, Rafah camp, Shokat Al Sofi, Tal Al Soltan). 
The targeted families will be selected based on their socioeconomic vulnerabilities making use of the UVAT. Criteria will include the families with monthly income below the poverty line, unemployed head of household and vulnerable female headed households. DCA/NCA and MAAN will ensure that beneficiaries have not received other assistance from other organizations and/or the governmental social protection schemes through coordination with relevant actors. The proposed intervention has been coordinated with the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) and food security sector. 
The project will provide the target families with multipurpose cash assistance for four months with a value of 1081 NIS per family per month. 
The project contributes to HRP strategic objective #2: “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under International Humanitarian Law”, and to the CWG MPCA objective: “Vulnerable HHs in oPt affected by shocks and stresses due to conflict and natural disaster supported with MPCA are able to meet their immediate essential needs and access to lifesaving services, decreases the incidence of negative coping strategies”.

project_name: Emergency WASH response to cholera outbreak in West Bekaa, Zahle, Beirut, Chouf, El Meten, Keserwan, Aley, Baabda, and Palestinian Camps/Gatherings Naameh 001, Gaza Buidling Beirut, Said Ghawash Beirut, Daouk Beirut 001, and Burj el Barajneh camp
project_objective:
Through this allocation, Save the Children (SC) aims to contribute to the interagency Health, WASH and RCCE operational plan to combat the spread of the cholera in Lebanon affecting vulnerable and marginalized communities. 

The proposed WASH project will seek to eliminate cholera transmission through the implementation of: a) case-area targeted intervention approach (CATI) or case-cluster targeted intervention approach (CCTI) to be deployed after 48 hours after a cholera case has been identified; and b) preventive measures to ensure water safety in high-risk areas. 

SC will implement the proposed intervention in areas of Beirut, Mount Lebanon, Central Beqaa, and SC partner SAWA Group will implement in West Beqaa. Supported communities will be Syrian, Lebanese, Palestinians living in 5 Palestinian Refugee camps and gatherings (Naameh 001 – Gaza Buidling Beirut 001 – Said Ghawash Beirut 003 – Daouk Beirut 001 – Burj el Barajneh camp)as well as Informal tented settlements and residential households. 

All of the previously mentioned localities are part of the 3Ws of the WASH working group and WASH in Schools task force and assigned under SC geographical area of coverage. An expected total of 300,000 individuals will be supported through this project. 

Based on the Health sector guidance and the number reflected in the allocation paper, SC expects a 1% attack rate for a total population of 300,000 individuals with a total of 3,000 cases to be responded for as part of the CATI/CCTI approach. The attack rate is calculated based on MOPH and WHO projection in the Cholera National response plan. The two key epidemiologic indicators used during a cholera outbreak are the attack rate and the case fatality ratio or rate. These indicators are standard measures of epidemic intensity and impact. They allow for comparisons between different locations and previous outbreaks. The attack rate (AR) is the cumulative incidence of cholera since the start of the outbreak. 

SC and SAWA Group are going to follow the sector area-based targeting response through the implementation of the Case Area Targeted Interventions (CATI) with minor contextual adaptations. SC and SAWA Group will receive referrals from the RDMS platform, within a period of 24 to 48hrs, Rapid Response Teams will visit the suspected cases and provide the proper cholera kits, awareness and conduct the right intervention from water cleaning and chlorination. Following this, SC will close the case to reflect an accurate number of active cases that still require support. 

SC and SAWA will also implement preventative measures to ensure safe water at communal level through the support of Water Establishments, municipalities and public schools in monitoring quality by providing pool tester, tool usage training session and chlorine for water establishment, communal/municipal water sources and public schools, in addition to provision of Fuel for Pumping stations, water & wastewater treatment plants. Furthermore, SC will implement decentralized water treatment solution such as UV sterilizers, dozing pumps that will be identified based on a needs/solution assessment.

project_name: Promoting WASH Services  IDPs and Host communities in WD , WN & BN - Sudan
project_objective:
ADRA has been working in Sudan for over four decades, working in providing both direct relief and development projects. Currently, ADRA Sudan is present in 5 out of the 18 states in Sudan; Khartoum, White Nile, Blue Nile, West Darfur, and Central Darfur. ADRA In WDS, had implemented about 10 WASH projects through DANIDA fund Targeting 60,000 beneficiaries in Geneina , Kreneik , and Jabal Localities, in WDS. ADRA had rehabilitated 12 Hafirs and drilled and rehabilitated more than 120 HPs, benefiting and serving about 150,000 IDP and host communities. In BNS ADRA was one of the first responders when the civil conflict broke out in 2010. Through its work with communities, ADRA was successful in reaching remote and war-torn villages in BNS and providing lifesaving assistance.
For the submitted project PWS, ADRA Sudan targets 310,600 affected populations whether from conflicts or from natural disasters such as floods. The IDPs, returnees and host communities in the four targeted states are West Darfur State, Central Darfur State, White Nile State, and Blue Nile Region. The project will target to fulfill the needs and gaps in WASH services for the IDPs and Returnees. The Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) situation has deteriorated due to a worsening economic crisis, non-functional or aging WASH infrastructure, and decreased/insufficient revenue collections. For Water supply needs, the project will carry on the rehabilitation of 60 non-working Hand pumps.12 water yards are going to be rehabilitated, operating them through solar systems instead of using diesel which is not eco-friendly, besides its high operation cost which could be affordable to the communities which are vulnerable. Therefore, the solar systems are going to ensure the sustainability of fetching water by the targeted affected people. 6 wells will be rehabilitated in three locations (WD, BN and CD).
For Sanitation, PWS will enhance the sanitation condition for the targeted groups by coordinating with the local partners and the Government line ministries and targeted groups themselves in conducting the interventions. PWS will construct 15 institutional latrines in all targeted states to cover schools, health centers and public markets. 300 will be constructed and another 300 will be rehabilitated in the targeted states.
For Hygiene, the project will target the youth groups male and female to train a team of hygiene promoters, to enhance good hygiene practices through hygiene promotion for IDPs and returnees’ people. Hygiene kits are going to be distributed. Menstrual Hygiene Materials will be provided in addition to Soaps, jerry cans , Buckets and Ibrigs and all these activities will cover the four states(WN,CD,WD and BN).   
Aguatabs and Purs are going to be distributed to ensure that people there would not be exposed to water contamination dieases and PWR will be focus on capacity building through training of the different groups of target communities which will cover the all WASH topics.

project_name: Food, Livelihood and Agriculture for Syrian Households (FLASH)
project_objective:
The FLASH project has been designed to offer a package of integrated services to provide life-saving assistance at household (targeting the most vulnerable including female headed households, people with disabilities as well as young boys and girls) and community levels. Potential areas have been selected based FAS severity scales, gap analysis and presence of highly vulnerable populations (such as FHH, IDPs and limited economic opportunities). The most vulnerable households within these communities will be selected to receive food assistance while those who had previous businesses in food or agricultural related businesses will be eligible for livelihood assistance. ADRA will use the modality of in-kind grants for livelihood activities and food vouchers (physical or electronic). At the community level, ADRA will repair / rehabilitate existing agricultural or associated infrastructure including irrigation canals, pumping stations etc. The irrigation infrastructure to be rehabilitated is a cement canal 1.5 kilometer long.
ADRA will target the areas for food security and livelihoods where other complimentary activities are being implemented, such as WASH, shelter and education.

project_name: Improved equitable access to safe and protective quality education services for emergency affected population in Upper Nile, Warrap, Eastern Equatoria, Western Equatoria and Central Equatoria states.
project_objective:
The proposed project will target 26,600 people (school children, teachers, PTAs and education officials and  improve equitable access to safe and protective quality education services for 26,111 (boys=14,361 girls=11,750, boys with disabilities=1320, girls with disabilities=971)  emergency affected IDPs, returnees, spontaneous refugees, and host community children including children with disabilities and youth (girls and boys) in 87 schools (including primary, ALP and ECD) in Upper Nile (Ulang, Maiwut and Longechuk), Warrap (Tonj South), Eastern Equatoria (Budi), Western Equatoria (Yambio) and Central Equatoria (Terekeka) states through the implementation of the following activities. 
Establish 28 disability inclusive Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS) in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019, rehabilitate 14 disability inclusive TLS/schools , establish 84 stances (42 blocks) of gender sensitive and disability inclusive latrines according to INEE and sphere standards, rehabilitate 28 blocks (56 stances) of gender sensitive and disability inclusive latrines according to INEE and sphere standards, provide dignity and Menstrual Hygiene Management  kits to 5828 adolescent girls, provide learning materials to 4700 learners, teaching kits to 300 teachers, provide Early Childhood Development kits to 2068 children  and recreational materials to 4700 learners. The project will train 300 teachers for 5 days on Education in Emergency, basic pedagogical skills, classroom management, Psychosocial Social Support, Child Protection and referral mechanisms. It will further train 154 PTAs/SMCs and 35 education officials on Psychosocial Social Support  and Disaster Risk Reduction in education, provide Information  Education and Communication materials with prevention and mitigation messages on Child Protection, disaster risk reduction  in education to 189 PTAs/SMCs and education officials. The project will also facilitate 14 (2 per county) back to learning campaigns (BTL) to encourage out of school children to return to schools.
ADRA has presence in all the targeted locations and identified critical education gaps that this intervention will respond to. The intervention is designed to build synergy with other existing ADRA interventions in Food Security, Education and emergency response. For instance  some of the targeted schools benefit from school feeding  and school gardening programs that ADRA implement in partnership with WFP., and will therefore  benefit from complementary  activities in the proposed interventions. In most of the counties targeted, ADRA implement in-service teacher training and continuous professional development for teachers, construct/ rehabilitate  permanent classrooms and TLS, for which the proposed intervention will  address gaps( additional TLS rehabilitation etc.)  ADRA is the state anchor for GESS in Warrap and Eastern Equatoria and also implements (in partnership with UNICEF) teacher continuous professional development in Warrap, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria states. We also implement NORAD funded education projects in Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria, work with WFP in food distribution, school feeding and food for Asset in Warrap, Eastern Equatoria and Central Equatoria. ADRA also implements SSHF projects in Western Equatoria and Upper Nile states. In designing this intervention, ADRA has taken into consideration gender, age, disability and diversity mainstreaming to carter for the needs of the diverse community groups targeted. ADRA has ensured that the proposed project will be phased out into existing and planned ADRA interventions in the targeted locations.

project_name: Promoting Gender Equality and Inclusion by ending Sexual and Gender Based Violence in South Sudan
project_objective:
Gender inequality gaps in South Sudan continue to widen as Gender Based Violence cases increase. According to Protection Analysis Update, Jan-Mar 2022, It notes that the situation of women and girls in South Sudan is daunting: conflict-related sexual violence is widespread and systematic and it is seen as a form to disrupt the fabric of communities, lack of accountability is exacerbated by conflict with poor socio-economic conditions of women and girls contributing to harmful social and gender norms practices.
This project will work to tackle the unequal power relations and harmful social and gender norms that contribute to GBV using Plan's gender transformative approach.
These will be done  through our gender transformative programming and influencing and Community engagement approach that addresses the root cause of power imbalance. Plan mainstreams GBV, safeguarding and PSEA in all its programs by mitigating risk to the people that we work with and ensuring that they feel safe while working with us. Interventions shall be tailored to have the involvement and participation of men, women, girls and boys in diversity including persons with disabilities.

The project will involve key actors in GBV response and prevention through taking leadership of the Protection Cluster or GBV sub Cluster at the state and county level. Currently, Plan International leads the protection Cluster in Nimule and Co-chair the protection Cluster in Yei. Also, in the rest of the states Plan International has been an active member in the cluster meetings and activities as a member. Plan will build on this to support the initiative of the cluster in coordinating GBV prevention and response interventions. 

Plan International will create, engage and maintain linkages/ relationships with  the key stakeholders and partners, such as Government including Ministry of Gender, police, judiciary including the ABC Court (A- the grassroots traditional court system at the Boma level headed by the Boma Chief;  B- middle traditional court headed by the Payam Head chief; and C- Last Traditional Court system headed by the Paramount chief at County level), religious institutions, cultural and community leaders, etc.

While building on the projects like Action Research on Violence against Women and Girls; Youth Voices in Eastern Equatoria, Integrated response to conflict-affected at-risk boys, girls, women and men in Central Equatoria State, South Sudan, Improving the quality and access in provision of life-saving integrated Health, Protection, Education and Nutrition services for vulnerable children and targeted communities in Pibor county, Jonglei State and Humanitarian protection measure for children and young people affected by South Sudan Crisis(GFFO) in Lakes state, among other Protection/ GBV projects that Plan International implements.

The project will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Gender, GBV cluster/partners, community leaders and women and youth groups at different levels. Plan International will ensure that these life-saving interventions eg PSS and referrals are provided to critically needed GBV survivors including vulnerable groups and other special cases such as Persons with disabilities. Cases with compounding medical conditions will be supported through CVA and referred for clinical management.
The project will mobilize communities to form drama groups that will will be trained and supported to conduct awareness raising on GBV in communities through radio, community mobilization and sensitization, participating in advocacy events such as 16 days of activism, etc. Youth will be mobilized into groups/ clubs as Champions of Change(CoC) plays a pivotal role in peer to peer mobilization of young people to challenge negative and discriminatory social norms that contribute to GBV. 
COVID-19 mitigation measures will especially those affecting public gatherings will be strengthened with COVID SOPs and items to effect COVID.

project_name: Protection and assistance for Refugees in Burundi
project_objective:
La protection internationale des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile est au coeur du mandat duHCR (Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies pour les Réfugiés - UNHCR), qui , en appuyantle Gouvernement du Burundi à travers l’Office National pour la Protection des Réfugiés etApatrides (ONPRA) , s’assure que les activités d’identification des demandeurs d’asile aux frontières et leurs accès à la procédure de détermination du statut de réfugié, en particulierdans les centres de transit (CT) de Cishemere et de Rumonge ainsi que dans les camps de réfugiés et en milieu urbain, soient de qualité, afin de préserver le caractère civil et humanitaire de l’asile et de garantir la prise en charge des personnes vulnérables y compris les enfants non accompagnés et séparés, et les survivants des VBG.
Jusqu’au 31 Décembre 2022, la population totale des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile (DA)enregistrés au Burundi est de 88 599 personnes (50,5% femmes et filles ; 49,5% hommes et garçons). La plupart d’entre eux a fui les violences dans les provinces du Sud et NordKivu en RDC. 35% de cette population vit en milieu urbain et 65 % sont reparties dans cinq camps : Kavumu, Bwagiriza, Kinama, Musasa et Nyankanda. Avec environ 400 nouveaux demandeur d'asile qui arrivent par mois, ainsi que, considérant les récents développements en RDC, lenombre des réfugiés au Burundi pourrait atteindre à environ 115 000 avec 5 000 Demandeurs d’asile en 2023. L’installation des réfugiés sur les sites tiendra compte de laprotection de l’environnement, aussi dans le souci de préserver un équilibre harmonieuxavec les populations hôtes.
Le HCR Burundi continuera à travailler avec l'Office Nationale de Protection des Réfugiéset Apatrides (ONPRA) afin - d’améliorer les procédures d'asile et de détermination de statutdes demandeurs d'asile et des réfugiés. En termes de protection, le HCR continuera àplaider pour que l'ONPRA garantisse une totale liberté de mouvement ainsi que d'autresdroits et libertés fondamentaux aux réfugiés qui résident légalement sur son territoire, etqu'ils mettent fi n aux arrestations et détentions arbitraires ; - et de réaliser le potentiel d'autonomisation des réfugiés tout en continuant le plaidoyer pour un cadre plus favorable à leur intégration locale qui restera une priorité. Un effort sera fait pour une meilleure autonomisation des réfugies orientée vers leur coexistence pacifique avec la population d’accueil. Le projet « Turikumwe » de la Banque Mondiale, avalisé par le HCR apour objectif premier la promotion de projet communautaire des Refugies avec desBurundais. Dans le même ordre d’idée, le HCR Burundi, inclut dans ses projets d’intégration, la prise en charge de 20% de la population vulnérable local. Cette autonomisation se fera par le biais de projets novateurs conformes aux Objectifs deDéveloppement Durable (ODD) et par un soutien ciblé aux initiatives en faveur des
réfugiés dans les camps et en zone urbaine, incluant également les populations d'accueil,y compris les rapatriés et les personnes déplacées. L'opération du HCR au Burundicontinuera à fournir des formations et à mener des campagnes de sensibilisation pour atténuer les attitudes négatives du public à l'égard des réfugiés, et pour augmenter les espaces de coexistence pacifique entre les communautés. L'enregistrement continu mettra à jour les données disponibles sur les réfugiés et les demandeurs d'asile au Burundi. Lesdonnées recueillies permettront d'affi ner les recommandations de protection et de concevoir des solutions plus durables pour les bénéfi ciaires. Les femmes, pour des raisons sociales, sont souvent exclues de la possibilité d'exercer des activités génératrices de revenus. En réponse à cette situation, le HCR Burundi et ses partenaires poursuivront leurs efforts de plaidoyer près du GoB pour l’amélioration du climat juridique nécessaire à la promotion du Genre et de l’enfance ; notamment l’accès à l’Education et la prise encharge des survivant de GBV.

project_name: Enhancing equitable access to safe, Inclusive and gender transformative Quality Learning Opportunities,Community engagement and system strengthening to address the education needs and barriers of Rohingya Refugee and Crisis-Affected Host Community Girls, Boys and Youth in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
In 2023, PIB will extend its support to enhance access to quality, gender-transformative equitable and inclusive learning opportunities in a safe and protective environment for Rohingya refugees and host community children, adolescents and youth (aged 3 to 24 years). PIB will continue education interventions in camps and host communities through direct implementation and local implementing partners. PIB will sustain its community-based learning facilities (CBLF) modality and establish and refurbish new integrated ECD, Myanmar Curriculum, Adolescent and Youth learning facilities. Project beneficiaries will be benefitted from improved WASH facilities through setting up hand washing stations, distribution of basic hygienic, MHM kits and COVID 19 preventing materials.  Facilitators and learners for the project LF will be jointly identified with community members and financially supported through 2023. This project includes an evident disability inclusion focus, aiming to identify and assess disability status of learners attending learning facilities. In 2023, PIB will assure the quality of the project’s learning opportunities through updating and upgrading teaching and learning modules for our various education levels, ensuring inclusion, gender sensitiveness and SEL is mainstreamed across our learning facilities.The project aims to count the number of learners, facilitators, youth, and CEM/PTA  who are involved in carrying out the endeavor (both male and female). It also focuses on community engagement to reduce gender inequality in to ensure quality education. 
PIB will build the capacities of teachers/facilitators of SBK, MC ,Functional Literacy Numeracy which will includes pre-vocational skill training especially life skill and  host primary and secondary school teachers and sector education partners on Integrated Sbk, gender responsive pedagogy, inclusive education, safeguarding and PSEA theme-based training, crisis sensitive education and planning  to become better teachers and improve learning outcomes of refugee and host communities’ learners. PIB will also identify and build the capacities of Rohingya women to become Myanmar Curriculum teachers and create a pool of female facilitators. In 2023, PIB is planning to incorporate technology-based teaching and learning approaches teachers training approaches in a sample of learning facilities across the various educational levels to assess its impact and benefits on students' learning outcomesto maximize the best outcome of training. To ensure students learning progress is assessed and tracked, PIB will conduct regular learning assessment and an individualizes progress tracking system put in place. In this JRP 2023, PIB will continue to support the community engagement and capacity strengthening of Education Sector partners (ECDWG), parents and affected communities to enhance their participation in the education of children, adolescents and youth. Key community stakeholders, parents and members of the learning facilities committees will be trained on gender, girls education, disability inclusion, child protection and safeguarding. PIB will also work on capacity strengthening of Parents support group and community members on DRR to jointly design emergency preparedness and response plans to equip Learning facilities and communities with required skills to respond to potential emergencies. Furthermore, through different capacity building training on gender responsive pedagogy, SEL, inclusive education and crisis sensitive education planning and management etc. PIB education partners will also be benefitted on planning and implementation of education project throughout the project period. This project will work with both host community and camp through supporting key community leaders, including members of education support groups, to undertake community consultations, advocacy initiatives, dialogue and strengthen their capacity to promote social cohesion and co-existence.

project_name: PRACTICE (Prevention and Response of CP concern through Timely Initiative with Children Engagement)
project_objective:
In 2023 PLAN International will focus on implementing integrated CP program in camp 17,20E, 21,24,25 and host community of Ukhiya and Teknaf for prevention, mitigation and response to Abuse, neglect, violence and exploitation to Children in Rohingya camp and host communities of Cox’s Bazar. The proposed project will include Awareness raising, CP Systems strengthening and Capacity building, Case management, Community-based child protection, Structured and unstructured PSS and Support activities for adolescents through life skill education. These interventions will ensure inclusion of Children/persons with disability, other children with specific needs. Special attention will be paid to child survivors of sexual abuse and GBV, early/forced/child marriage, child labor, trafficking as well as unaccompanied and separated children. 
The project will reach 46350 people (Female-23186, Male-23164), It will closely involve the children and their caregivers from both Rohingya and host communities, they will be consulted throughout the project cycle from designing to Evaluation stage. The parents and caregivers will be receiving positive parenting sessions for strengthening their parenting skill through this project for addressing harmful practices and attitudes to children.
Project will establish/refurbish structure for providing CP services to the children and their caregivers including community members.
CBCP activities will be structured through feedback from community consultation and participation to ensure inclusion and ownership by both the host and the refugee community. Community-level interventions will include promoting social cohesion and strengthening self-protection of children. Workshop with duty bearers (government officials and local authorities), community leaders, parents, teachers and religious leaders within both community groups on developing a basic understanding of everyday peace, social cohesion, social trust and public accountability will also take place.  PLAN will ensure that child friendly feedback mechanisms are in place with strong emphasis on PSEA and Child Safeguarding.  
For strengthening the CP system, this project will coordinate with other sectors and government officials to enrich their capacity to protect and deliver quality services in a child friendly way, train the volunteers and other local and INGO CP staff. This proposed project will also train non-CP actors on age- and gender-sensitive child protection principles, approaches, child safeguarding PSEA. ECCD intervention will also be carried out in Teknaf area with the support from Education sector of PLAN International. 
The project will offer gender responsive comprehensive case management services including referral, integrated Menstrual Hygiene management (MHM) services, MHPSS that covers structured, on-structured PSS and specialized services. LGBTI will be kept in special consideration.
Plan will establish adolescent groups / clubs (disaggregated by age, gender and disability). It will consider 10% person with disability in targeting beneficiaries.
PIan International is committed to coordinating the response through active participation in sectors such as Protection, Education, GBV and Child Protection Sub-Sector and other working groups like Strategic Working Group (SAG), CMTWG to ensure meaningful access, prioritization of safety and integration of services.  The services offered will be in line with CPMS, interagency tools and SOPs, CPSS strategy and will be ensured through structured training enhancing competencies in providing quality gender-responsive and timely services. This project will also include a contingency plan for natural disaster and will do best for keeping the environmental impact of the project will be minimal.
As the project will be implemented through national NGO, Plan will undertake various capacity strengthening initiatives for PNGO and community volunteer as well at every stage of the project.

project_name: Livelihood and Skills development of the youth from host communities and Rohingya Camps in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
Plan International conducted a job market scan at Teknaf to identify market-relevant skill development training for girls, boys and young women. The target people for the skills development will be selected from the extremely poor households in the host community and from the Rohingya Camps. The age of the target people is from 18 to 24 years. For the host community, Plan Internation will use the curriculum and books from the Bangladesh Technical Education Board (BTEB) which is equivalent to the grade 1 of the NTVQF competency standard. The training will be for 360 hours based on the nature of the trade course. The major areas of skills development found in the market scan are driving, mobile phone servicing, industrial sewing operator, para-vet, computer literacy & hardware, beauty parlour, hospitality & tourism, food and beverage etc.  
To implement the skills development training in the host community, Plan International will follow 3 strategies because there is no Technical Training Center of BMET in Teknaf nor Cox’sbzar. Firstly, Plan will establish a temporary training centre for a few of the courses like driving and industrial sewing operators, computer literacy and hardware, and freelancing. Already Plan International successfully implemented this type of training in Teknaf.  Secondly, the target people will be admitted to the training centres in Cox’s Bazar. Plan International’s partner UCEP Bangladesh has established a training centre in Cox’sbazar recently where Plan will expand its partnership with UCEP for arranging training in Cox's Bazar. The major courses would be electrical and electronics, plumbing, hospitality etc. Plan International will also establish a partnership with the renowned Tomy Mia’s training centre for food and beverage course. The courses will follow the curriculum and books of BTEB including certification. The project will also explore, the opportunity for skills training locally at the department of youth development and women, women & children affairs and the ICT division of the Government (there is 2 popular government TVET programme SIEP and learning & earning). Thirdly, Plan International will follow a mentor-mentee approach for the target people who are unable to join the training courses outside of the union based on their family situation. However, Plan International will ensure the curriculum of BTEB to the mentors. After successful completion of the training, the target people will be placed in a paid job or enterprise. As 85% economy of the country is informal, therefore, the project will follow the approach of job and enterprise development. For the improvement of their livelihood, the young entrepreneurs will be linked with MFIs for further capital to expand their businesses. 

To implement the skills development training in the camps, the project will arrange temporary training sessions inside the camps in the selected courses. The trade courses would be electric maintenance, knitting, tailoring, handicrafts, etc. However, the project will ensure a competency-based curriculum and books of BTEB for the quality of the training. After training, there will be an assessment. The youth in the camps will be supported to start a small business inside the camps.    
For the coordination with the Government, the project will follow the curriculam and books of the Bangladesh technical Education Board. Already Plan International has a working relations with BTEB which will be further explored.

project_name: Addressing critical protection gaps through GBV prevention, response, and capacity building, with a focus on women migrants and women with disabilities.
project_objective:
The goal of this project is to strengthen protection for women survivors of violence during the complex humanitarian crisis in Lebanon. The project targets underserved Lebanese women, migrant women, and PRL by addressing critical protection gaps in GBV prevention, response and through capacity building. The project will be directly implemented by KAFA, with support from (LUPD), and overseen and monitored by UN Women, providing technical assistance to ensure effective project implementation.

 This project will aim to address the following areas:
1.1 GBV Prevention: target women, girls, men and boys who participate in targeted gender equality and empowerment activities in safe spaces or at community level as part of GBV prevention programs.  
2.1	Provide specialized GBV services: case management, psychosocial support, legal assistance, and shelter to GBV survivors and those at risk of GBV.
3.1	Assess the satisfaction of GBV survivors who received case management services.
5.1 Increase the capacity of institutions and civil society actors to respond to GBV cases by providing training to improve their knowledge of GBV.

Under prevention, activity 1.1 – the project aims to implement sensitization activities, including education and awareness sessions on GBV, menstrual hygiene management, women's rights, gender existing legal framework related to GBV/gender, and the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). Additionally, the project will provide information sessions, conduct safety audits at the community level, distribute dignity kits to those in need, and encourage participation in community-based committees on GBV to increase community involvement and promote local ownership of the prevention efforts.  [KAFA, LUPD]

Under specialized services, activity 2.1, the main outreach mechanism for survivors receiving these services will be through KAFA’s helplines, services are available for women survivors of violence and human trafficking for labor exploitation. Women will receive holistic case management, led by highly experienced and trained case workers and will take place in women safe spaces in Beirut, Bekaa, and Saida, safe housing/shelters, and in case of emergencies, remotely. The case management services, provided inside or outside the safe shelters, include social care services, psychological and psychosocial interventions, health services, legal assistance as well as safe referrals to other multi-sectoral services.  For women migrant domestic workers, case management could include assistance with safe voluntary return by ensuring administrative follow up for travel procedures and/or travel tickets to country of origin. In partnership with LUPD, specific staff and interventions will be offered to women with disabilities, including ensuring that physical centers are accessible, and staff are equipped with information and tools to best support their needs.  [KAFA, LUPD]

Under satisfaction follow-up, activity 3.1, the project will use various feedback methods to evaluate the satisfaction levels of GBV survivors who received case management services. To ensure that survivors receive adequate case management services, the project will adopt a survivor-centered approach, provide case managers with training and mentorship, create feedback mechanisms for survivors, analyze feedback to improve services, and regularly monitor and evaluate case management services. [UN Women, KAFA]

Under capacity building, activity 5.1, the project will provide training to institutions and civil society actors to increase their knowledge and capacity to effectively respond to gender-based violence (GBV) cases, with a focus on women and girls with disabilities. Target actors will include MOSA and UN Women’s livelihoods partners in order to increase GBV and livelihoods linkages.  [UN Women, KAFA, LUPD]

The implementation of the activities will be done by KAFA and LUPD. UNW will oversee the project and support in the Capacity building and M&E.

project_name: Addressing urgent protection and psychosocial needs of children and adolescents through mobile response in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Plan International’s mobile programming has been effectively used in its German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) funded project in 6 LGAs of Borno State. Plan proposes using the mobile unit approach in the four targeted LGAs of Borno. The mobile response ensures the deployment of the mobile team within 72 hours of a specific request, or of a report from relevant humanitarian clusters groups of acute needs. In cases of first response, the mobile unit will be deployed for a period of 6 and up to 12 weeks to provide urgent lifesaving assistance including provision of cash transfer. The mobile team currently is based in Maiduguri and serves LGAs within Borno state. They are being deployed in Kaga, Damboa, Bama, and four different locations of Maiduguri Metropolitan City-Jere, Madinatu, Bolori and Teachers village camp. The team can also be stationed in other field locations like Mubi, Dikwa, Pulka or Gwoza and be deployed from there. The mobile protection team will conduct a participatory rapid needs assessment, engaging the affected population to identify immediate needs. The outcome of the rapid assessment will be used to determine the line of response and also to identify existing community based services. Based on the findings of the assessment a rapid referral pathway will be developed to guide the provision of protection services to the children and adolescents. The referral pathway will be disseminated among stakeholders and will be used to coordinate actors providing services on the ground especially during the first line of response which will include provision of direct case management services. 
In addition, the mobile team will set up rapid complaints and feedback response mechanism to address issues of protection of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) as well as advocate for services that are needed and not available. Communities will be engaged to identify the most suitable and safe mechanisms to raise complaints and provide feedback on both services and operations of the mobile team and other available community services. The mobile team will provide targeted response for high-risk children including children with no suitable caregivers, children at risk of abuse in their current care arrangements, and UASC

project_name: Strengthening Health Sector Coordination Towards Improving Access to Health Care Services and Promoting Ealy Recovery Across BAY States
project_objective:
As the crisis in northeast Nigeria continues to persist, the operational environment remains complex. Despite significant counter-terrorism efforts by the Nigerian military and its partners, access to affected areas remains challenging due to insecurity. The humanitarian community continues to struggle to respond to urgent humanitarian needs with the already overstretched available capacity. The response capacity to a crisis of this scale is not commensurate to the needs of the affected population especially the new influx, forced displacement of communities, and state returning IDPs back to their LGAs of origin. Overcrowding in camps continues to be prevalent with over 40 percent of camps in Borno State remaining over-congested and some closed. As military operations are expected to intensify in the coming months across Borno State, further evacuation and displacements of civilians are expected. This situation will likely worsen the overcrowding situation and have a direct impact on the health situation of the population, especially in light of the ongoing measles and cholera outbreaks in the region. The onset of the rainy season coupled with a weak sanitation infrastructure further increases the risk of a cholera outbreak further exacerbating the situation, especially in IDP camps. The Aftermath of the flooding in the year 2022 will tell a lot in the coming months which has its effects on food security. In addition, Lack of shelter and food has a direct impact on people’s health especially children, pregnant women, the elderly, and other vulnerable groups exposed to harsh weather conditions.
The Health sector, in collaboration with development partners including the State MoHs and Ministries/Committees of Reconstruction, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (MoRRR), will support a comprehensive recovery strategy for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of health facilities with the overall objective of health system restoration and with the underlying principle of “building back better”. Moving away from geographically and thematically fragmented interventions. The program is designed with the flexibility to respond and adjust to situation changes and to address the health needs of each community. The provision of well-measured training and incentive packages to health professionals, to offer essential uninterrupted healthcare services in the communities is an additional priority of the health sector. Training of state M&E and partners to improve data collection and inform better decisions also needs to be prioritized.

project_name: FORTALECIMIENTO DE LA RUTA MATERNA A NIVEL DE LA RED DE ATENCIÓN PRIMARIA EN SALUD/ ÁREAS DE SALUD INTEGRAL COMUNITARIAS EN LOS ESTADOS MIRANDA Y ZULIA
project_objective:
Este Proyecto está orientado a la inclusión de grupos poblacionales constituidos por mujeres gestantes, puérperas, niños, niñas y adolescentes, en las que barreras geográficas, institucionales y culturales les impide tener acceso a servicios de salud, en este caso a salud sexual y reproductiva.
La Asociación Civil Redes Integrales de salud desde 2018 ha mantenido un trabajo permanente en los estados: Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, Lara, La Guaira, Mérida, Miranda, Táchira, Trujillo, Zulia y el Distrito Capital, a través del monitoreo de indicadores, que dan cuenta de la implementación de la Ruta Materna, en cuanto a: número de referencias oportunas de las gestantes de control prenatal para la atención del parto en hospitales de referencia, número de partos, prevención de la transmisión vertical de sífilis y VIH, seguimiento nutricional de las gestantes y enfermedades prevalentes de la infancia, particularmente diarreicas y respiratorias agudas,  control postnatal e inmunizaciones; los cuales evidencian la situación de la salud materno/infantil en centros de salud priorizados en los estados mencionados y, sirve de base para el conocimiento de las necesidades de poblaciones que son responsabilidad de esos  centros de salud.
La propuesta de fortalecer la Ruta Materna, como una ruta que permite articular en cada territorio social acciones institucionales a través de una unidad básica territorial denominada Área de Salud Integral Comunitaria (ASIC), orientada a garantizar respuestas bajo un modelo de atención con enfoque familiar y comunitario en los cuales se encuentran ubicados  los Ambulatorios que fueron priorizados en los Planes de Salud Estadales bajo los criterios de  presencia de equipos básicos de salud, comunidad organizada y alta frecuencia  de embarazos no controlados y, que para el caso de esta propuesta fueron seleccionados en el estado Miranda son, según sus Ejes Territoriales: Mirandinos: Puerta Morocha, Montaña Alta, Francisco de Miranda y Camatagua. Metropolitano: Araguaney, Bloque 1, Medicentro, La Urbina, San Miguel Arcángel, Los Dos Caminos, La Suiza y Joaquín Blanco. Guarenas-Guatire: Care 1, Casa Amiga de la Salud, Bellard, El Mirador, Menca de Leoni y en el estado Zulia: Encontrados (Mcpio. Catatumbo), La Laguna (Mcpio. Guajira), Campo Lara (Mcpio. Lagunillas) Cuatro Bocas y Santa Cruz (Mcpio. Mara), El Tokuko, Toromo y Las Piedras (Mcpio. Machiques de Perijá), Cuatricentenario, San Jacinto, Cujicito, Los Claveles, Centro de Atención al Indígena y La Victoria (Mcpio. Maracaibo) y EL Silencio, Sierra Maestra y San Felipe (Mcpio San Francisco). Cuya finalidad es dotarlos de equipos médicos (tensiómetro. estetoscopio, infantometro, balanza, tallímetro, equipos de otorrino, cinta métrica, gestometro, doppler fetal)  y no médicos (escritorio, sillas) y formación a los equipos básicos de salud y comunidades, para el desarrollo de capacidades en: factores protectores de la vida, control prenatal, prevención y control de la transmisión vertical de sífilis y VIH,  gestantes de bajo peso, inmunizaciones, implementación de formato de la tarjeta de vacunación, referencia oportuna de gestantes, identificación de los síntomas y signos de alarma en la emergencia obstétrica y violencia obstétrica. project_name: Programa Nutrifamilias FUNDANA
project_objective:
FUNDANA desde hace 30 años, a través de su entidad de atención, ha brindado un hogar protector a más de 32.000 niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA) víctimas de maltrato, abuso o negligencia. Producto de la crisis social y económica, en nuestra organización hemos evidenciado un aumento significativo de niños y niñas con desnutrición infantil, motivado a una situación económica precaria, impactando negativamente en su alimentación y salud.

En respuesta a esta problemática en 2017 se decide inaugurar el Programa de Atención y Recuperación Nutricional ¨Nutrifamilias¨, que tiene como objetivo promover la recuperación nutricional de los niños, niñas con riesgo o desnutrición aguda sin complicaciones, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (MEL), que además se encuentren en situación de vulnerabilidad social, facilitando su rehabilitación y posterior reinserción a la comunidad.

Para el 2023 el Programa espera atender 6.200 NN menores de 5 años y 2054 Mujeres embarazadas y lactantes a través de tamizaje nutricional, 7500 NNA de 2 a 14 años desparasitados, 375 NN y 375 NN de 6 a 59 meses reciben tratamiento para la desnutrición aguda y suplementos para la vulnerabilidad nutricional respectivamente. Asimismo, 8.254 personas reciben consejería en prácticas claves en temas de Nutrición, WASH y Protección NNA. También, 1.875 personas acceden a productos de higiene y tienen acceso a agua segura. Además, 50 profesionales de salud de la red ambulatoria aliada se ven fortalecidos a través de la capacitación en temas de nutrición y WASH. Finalmente, 120 familias donde uno de sus miembros cursa con desnutrición aguda y tiene una alta vulnerabilidad psicosocial reciben acompañamiento por promotores de convivencia familiar. 

Por otra parte, el Programa contempla la conformación de grupos estables de padres y cuidadora para sensibilizaciones en temas relacionados a la alimentación del lactante y niño pequeño ALNP-E, a fin de fomentar el desarrollo de capacidades y promover estrategias EDC. 
El programa Nutrifamilias se ejecuta en 6 Centros de Protección ubicados en los estados Miranda; municipio Sucre y Baruta  y Distrito Capital; municipio Libertador. Asimismo, se establecerán alianzas con 5 Centros de Salud en comunidades periféricas a los Centros de Protección de FUNDANA a fin de acortar las brechas de acceso a los servicios de nutrición, WASH y Protección. 

Adicionalmente, la estrategia intersectorial de Nutrición, WASH y Protección es una respuesta integral que busca centrar los servicios en el individuo, por medio de una visión integradora y respaldada que responda a sus distintas necesidades y enfocada en la sostenibilidad y la resiliencia.

Finalmente, la participación de los beneficiarios durante todas las fases del proyecto permite medir necesidades sentidas, tener retroalimentación de las acciones y mejorar los servicios constantemente. Para ello, todos los datos estarán desagregados por género, edad, discapacidad y  diversidad, a fin de tener in enfoque inclusivo y adaptado al contexto.

project_name: Prevención de la VBG en Mujeres y Niñas con Discapacidad, madres y/o cuidadoras de PcD, municipios Plaza y Zamora, Miranda.
project_objective:
La evaluación de necesidades realizada por FundAFID a través de cuatro grupos focales y 120 encuestas telefónicas, indica que el 78% de las personas encuestadas (en su mayoría mujeres) manifestó requerir apoyo psicosocial. Desde el inicio de la pandemia la crisis económica las ha impactado con mayor fuerza y ha incrementado la violencia intrafamiliar. Muchas han perdido su empleo o no tienen permisos para cuidar a la persona con discapacidad y refieren dificultad de acceso a servicios públicos para ejercer sus derechos.
FundAFID atenderá y empoderará a esta población con un enfoque multiseccional (Mujer-Discapacidad), para prevenir la VbG, en mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, así como en madres y/o cuidadoras de personas con discapacidad.
Se brindará apoyo psicosocial a mujeres afectadas por la pandemia, la crisis socioeconómica y aquellas en riesgo o sobrevivientes de la VbG.  Se proveerá sensibilizaciones y capacitaciones en DDHH de la mujer y de las PcD, derechos sexuales y reproductivos, prevención y mitigación de la VbG, masculinidad y crianza positiva, así como, fortalecimiento de la resiliencia, toma de decisiones y autoestima, en los municipios Plaza y Zamora del estado Miranda. Estas actividades serán extensivas a la comunidad. La accesibilidad está garantizada tomando en cuenta las discapacidades presentes entre las beneficiarias.
 Se tiene previsto capacitar al personal de la alcaldía del municipio Zamora en temas de discapacidad, protección y DDHH, mitigación, prevención y respuesta a la VbG.
 Las actividades del proyecto se articularán con los programas y servicios del sistema de protección de las alcaldías (Consejo de Protección de NNA, Consejo Municipal de Derecho de NNA y Dirección de Personas con Discapacidad y Adulto Mayor, entre otros).
Con el fin de garantizar la dignidad de la población meta, que enfrenta inseguridad alimentaria, se distribuirán mensualmente (por 3 meses) canastas de alimentos, a un total de 600 hogares de las mujeres beneficiarias, estimándose un costo aproximado de $89.85 canastas medias (familias hasta 4 miembros) y de $173.03 canastas full (familias de 5 o más miembros), que contribuirá a mantener a las beneficiarias en la ruta de atención y asegurar la eficacia de la protección. Las canastas alimentarias estarán diseñadas según las directrices del Clúster de Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida y serán distribuidas durante el proceso de empoderamiento (atención psicosocial, capacitación). Adicionalmente, se entregará Kit de Higiene, el cual será diseñado juntamente con las participantes del proyecto, tomando en cuenta sus necesidades. 
Buscando un impacto transformador, de empoderamiento económico y crecimiento personal, se estima para el año 2023, continuar con el proyecto, desarrollando iniciativas de actividades generadoras de ingreso en las mujeres participantes en la primera fase.

project_name: Proyecto un Hábitat Sano para San Blas: Mejorando espacios de protección, de grupos vulnerables del Municipio Sucre del estado Miranda.
project_objective:
La situación de espacios de protección y el acceso a servicios, específicamente de energía, agua y saneamiento, son un grave problema en el estado Miranda, siendo el municipio Sucre, una de las zonas más afectadas. Esta situación es más grave en grupos vulnerables con necesidades específicas, que requieren mayor atención para disminuir sus riesgos.
Según la información sistematizada de la experiencia del Monitor Comunitario y de aportes del Grupo de Trabajo de Información (GTMI), en el estado Miranda, evidenciamos fallas en agua, energía y saneamiento: En el sector salud, siguen existiendo debilidades en el acceso al servicio de agua y persisten fallas en la infraestructura; Existe escasez y fallas en calidad del servicio de agua en varios sectores, las personas se ven en la necesidad de comprar agua, obtenerla de fuentes cercanas o recolectar agua de lluvia; En el sector educación hay deficiencia en la infraestructura y dificultades de agua e iluminación en algunos planteles; El servicio de recolección de basura en algunas zonas del estado funciona de forma regular o deficiente, sobre todo en barriadas/sectores populares. Las personas queman la basura o la acumulan en lugares no adecuados; En varios sectores del estado existen fallas con el alumbrado público, lo que aumenta el riesgo de inseguridad para los habitantes. 
Estas situaciones hacen que el acceso a espacios de protección, especialmente en salud, educación y centros comunitarios, o son inexistentes o tienen condiciones precarias para un buen funcionamiento y la posibilidad de brindar una adecuada atención a grupos vulnerables, principalmente a mujeres, NNA y adultos mayores, entre otros
Así, el proyecto busca disminuir factores de riesgo asociados a construcciones de mala calidad y deficiente acceso a servicios (energía y agua), en espacios de salud, educación y comunitarios, y alojamientos individuales, brindando protección a la comunidad y disminuyendo los factores de riesgo de PNE, especialmente de mujeres, madres cabeza de hogar, personas con discapacidad, adultos mayores y NNA; Igualmente, disminuir problemas de salud y ambientales, por manejo inadecuado del agua, su almacenamiento y disposición y capacitar en temas claves a PNE y líderes comunitarios.
Se propone atender problemas previstos en la respuesta humanitaria 2022-2023: Salud (a través de espacios dignos para la prestación de la asistencia); servicios (con la atención de problemas de agua y saneamiento); educación (mejorando las condiciones de las instalaciones escolares) y riesgos de protección (atendiendo a grupos vulnerables, mejorando el acceso a servicios de protección). En definitiva, contar con espacios de protección para mejorar la atención a NNA, adultos mayores, mujeres, personas con discapacidad y Personas LGBTI. Igualmente, se espera atender alojamientos individuales, según diagnósticos realizados de PNE. En ambos casos, se deben considerar los espacios de producción de alimentos (comedores comunitarios/cocinas).
La intervención se realizará en una zona conformada por 11 barrios, conocida como el Gran San Blas y un Centro Educativo de José Félix Rivas, en Petare, Municipio Sucre, estado Miranda. Esto, por el conocimiento que se tiene de las zonas y la verificación de necesidades humanitarias.
El proyecto se enmarca dentro de los objetivos y actividades previstas en los Clúster de Agua Saneamiento e Higiene; Alojamiento, Energía y Enseres; y Protección. Tenemos así, desde el enfoque de AEE y ASH, intervenir el funcionamiento de espacios de salud, educativos y comunitarios (especialmente, su adecuación o mejoramiento y dotación de enseres; el acceso al agua y el saneamiento, mediante buenas prácticas) y desde Protección, la prestación de servicios especializados a PNE, mejorando su cobertura y atención (haciendo énfasis en enfoque de edad, género y diversidad, de personas adultos mayores y VbG), con apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal según el caso.

project_name: Protección de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes en riesgo, y fortalecimiento de las capacidades de cuidado de sus familias
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivo promover la protección integral y el ejercicio de derechos de los Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes (NNA) con riesgos de protección y en mayor vulnerabilidad, así como, atender a sus familias para la sostenibilidad de la protección y el alcance del bienestar. Incorpora un componente de desarrollo de medios de vida de las familias de las que hacen parte los NNA, así como, del fortalecimiento de su capacidad de crianza positiva, cuidado adecuado a la edad de los NNA y de la prevención de violencia y otros importantes que pueden impactar a las familias, particularmente a los NNA. 

El proyecto está dirigido principal y prioritariamente a NNA en movilidad, NNA separados de sus progenitores y al cuidado de familiares o terceros, NNA de comunidades indígenas y afrodescendientes, NNA de madres adolescentes y adultas jóvenes, NNA víctimas o en riesgo de violencia, reclutamiento a actividades delictivas, violentas o de explotación, NNA en riesgo de protección y que no ejercen o acceden a sus derechos por no poseer documentos de identidad (acta de nacimiento, cédula, otros), al estar fuera de la escuela, no acceder a la nutrición/alimentación adecuada, no recibir la asistencia en salud que requiere, entre otros, que los exponen a riesgos y deterioran el adecuado desarrollo. 
Desde un enfoque de protección integral, se identificarán los NNA con riesgos de protección en y con las comunidades, se evaluará su situación y necesidades, se proveerán servicios psicosociales, en protección legal y social, así como serán refridos y acompañados para acceder a serviciso complementarios brindados por el sistema de protección público y por otros actores no gubernamentales.  Se establecerán las vías de derivación seguras a través del trabajo articulado con organismos competentes como el CPNNA, CMDNNA, Ministerio Público, DdP entre otras.
 Adicionalmente, la intervención incluye procesos de prevención, formación psicosociales y vinculación con los NNA en las comunidades, que incluirá el entrenamiento en habilidades para la vida, sociales, importancia de la diversidad, la protección personal,  y primeros auxilios psicológicos y cooperación, para que aprendan a identificar situaciones en sí mismos y cuándo un amigo o compañero experimenta estrés, angustia o sentimientos de tristeza, cómo expresar sus emocionas y cómo brindar apoyo. Estos procesos apuntan a fortalecer la experiencia colectiva propiedad de la edad de los NNA, a fortalecer capacidades afectivas, cognitiva y sociales personales que le permitan mitigar y retardar el acercamiento a riesgos del contexto, y a estar en mejores condiciones para enfrentarlos. 

El componente de desarrollo de los medios de vida y fortalecimiento de la capacidad de cuidado y protección de los NNA de las familias se llevará a cabo: 
(i)Actividades de información, orientación y psicoeducación de las personas cuidadoras de los NNA: madres, abuelos u otras familias en condición de vulnerabilidad cabezas de hogar, hombres solos cabeza de hogar y con NNA de los perfiles descritos antes. Las actividades coadyuvarán a su resiliencia, estabilidad emocional y fortalecimiento de capacidades de crianza positiva y para la protección y cuidado de los NNA ante un contexto retador de violencia, separación, movilidad, entre otras. Esto se desplegará mediante la aplicación de metodologías escalables.
(ii)Formación, orientación, acompañamiento y entrega de asistencia en especie y mediante servicios para el desarrollo o fortalecimiento de medios de vida o de generación de ingreso que le permitan a las familias mitigar la difícil situación económica que atraviesan y responder a necesidades básicas, de modo que puedan facilitarse acciones de protección y cuidados de los NNA que las integran.  
El proyecto plantea una mirada multisectorial y promueve el nexo entre lo humanitario con respuesta a necesidades y el desarrollo, trabajando en fortalecimiento de las familias y la protección de NNA en las comunidades

project_name: Food security and livelihood support and building resilience capacity of vulnerable households to multifaceted shocks in Jonglei and Upper Nile States
project_objective:
This project proposal aims at improving food security and livelihood options  and building resilience to IPC3+ households in Nyirol, Uror, Ayod, Fangak, Duk, Bor in Jonglei state and Renk, Ulang in Upper Nile state. This will be achieved through FSL cluster objectives CO1: Food assistance, CO2: Emergency food production; and CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs with mainstreaming of COVID-19 prevention protocols, gender, protection, persons with disabilities and climate. The targeted beneficiaries are 13,390 households (80,350 individuals; 24% women, 16% men, 36% girls and 24% boys) consisting of  5,356 hosts communities, 2,009 returnees, 1,071 refugees and 4,954 IDPs. Beneficiary by type will be determined through baseline surveys.
  
Food assistance will be conditional through Food for Assets in Ulang county targeting 3,613 households impacting the lives of  21,680 individuals. 

Food security will be enhanced through; 
i) in-kind distribution of crop, vegetable and fishing kits to 9673 households (Ayod 1200, Duk 680, Fangak 640, Nyirol 2433, Uror 2160 and Renk 2560 
ii) Restocking poultry and shoats in Ayod and Duk counties to 500 and 680 households respectively
iii) Livestock support; treatment and vaccination campaigns to 5773 HHs in Ayod (500), Duk (680) Uror(2160) and Nyirol (2433) counties targeting an estimate of 200,000 livestock heads through 120 trained Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) (40 per county)

Resilience building and reducing dependency on food and agricultural inputs aids (CO3) will be realized through 
i) Support to seed fairs using locally sourced seed; seed security & multiplication strengthening/ Support market functionality e.g. assist traders to re-supply markets/ local procurement for FAO ITFs & aggregation of produce for WFP assistance in Renk county targeting 560 seed producer farmers
ii) Support value chain addition to fishery groups and fishery values chain actors in Bor South county targeting 630 
iii) Training & capacity building through farmer/agro-pastoral field schools, demonstration plots vocational training cutting across all the project locations targeting 15% of the total targeted households translating to 2,009 house holds. The trainings will cover good and climate-smart agronomic practices, natural resource management, countering post-harvest losses, sustainable income generation activities, value addition with special emphasis on minimising spread of COVID-19.
iv) Conflict related meetings to strengthen local peace structures also done across the all the targeted project location to promote peace thereby allowing the project participants to fully engage in agricultural activities in safe public spaces without fear of displacement and loosing their produce/harvest through conflict related effects.

Community based participatory approach will be adopted  through Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) committees (consisting of RRC representatives, Boma chiefs, Women leaders, Youth Leaders, County Agricultural Department Representative) and through Project management committees.  Indicators like household status (host, IDP, returnees and refugees), gender markers (targeted male and female) and special/minority groups like Child-headed, Elderly and Female-headed households under IPC 3+ will be screened before approval of the beneficiary list. 

Continuous monitoring will be done throughout the project cycles to ensure quality project outcomes are realised within the allocated timeframe. Community representative committees (AAPs and PMCs) and donors  will take part in the monitoring process and also act as a platform for complaint-feedback mechanisms. These feedback will be included in the implementation and project designs where applicable.

Sustainability of the project will be realised through active involvement of the community stakeholders through out the project cycle making them adopt and propagate the knowledge acquired.

project_name: Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Jonglei & Upper Nile States.
project_objective:
This CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2022 seeks to provide inclusive, protective and effective education services to accelerate learning recovery and make schools more equitable, efficient and resilient for 7, 339 (3, 302 girls) school-aged children, 250 (50 female) teachers, 275 (82 female) PTA members and 60 (10 female) local education officials in 6 Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States by building on investments made during the Pandemic and previous years of EiE programming in South Sudan.

The expected results are equalised participation and improved learning outcomes across gender and disability for 7, 339 (45% female) children and youth through provision of essential school facilities and supplies, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics in 25 target schools (5 ECD centers, 15 primary schools, and 5 secondary schools) in Ayod, Uror & Duk Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State respectively. These 7, 339 children (5-17) and 250 teachers will be provided with teaching and learning materials in the form of 10 ECD learner kits, 250 learner kits for primary and 10 learner kits for secondary schools. 250 recreational kits will be provided to enhance learning and play and psychosocial wellbeing during schooling.

For their protective and safe school environment, 30 temporary learning spaces will be established in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019; and 30 gender segregated latrines and 30 water points in line with INEE and sphere standards. (unit of measurement: 1:60 for boys, 1:30 for girls). CMD will distribute 95 (500-litre) plastic water tanks with taps, 95 (50-litre) hand-washing tanks with taps and on their metal stands; 285 (1-litre) liquid sanitisers, 190 cartons of toilet soap, 95 bags (20 kgs) of detergent/powder soap, 95, 000 face masks, and 375 pairs of gumboots to provide sanitation and PPE for students and teachers. 2, 000 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits and undergo MHM sessions to better enhance their self-esteem and school attendance.

The plan targets 2, 339 (935 girls & 1, 404 boys) children in Ayod; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Uror; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Duk; 1, 000(400 girls & 600 boys) in Ulang; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Nasir; and 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Longechuk. 50 (10 female) teachers in Ayod; 40 (10 female) in Uror; 40 (10 female) in Duk; 40 (10 female) in Ulang; 40 (5 female) in Nasir; and 40 (5 female) in Longechuk will benefit from active EiE pedagogy that is centered on children and adolescents and their full development, and that responds to school needs and favours the equitable achievement of learning goals. These teachers will Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Equally important, 75 (27 female) PTA members in Ayod; 40 (11 female) in Uror; 40 (11 female) in Duk; 40(11female) in Ulang; 40(11 female) in Nasir; and 40 (11 female) in Longechuk and 10 (1 female) education officials in Ayod, 10 (1) in Uror; 10 (1) in Duk; 10(1) in Ulang; 10(1) in Nassir; and 10 (1 female) in Longechuk will be trained in School Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction in Education (DRR).

CMD will also conduct 12 Back to Learning (BTL) campaigns through public information campaigns intended for the entire affected population and/or awareness raising activities aimed at specific segments of the out-of-schoolchildren (OOSC) as well as current learners identified as most at-risk.

project_name: Provision of emergency and integrated nutrition services to IDP's and Vulnerable communities (Children Under 5 and Pregnant and lactating women) in Ayod, Akobo West, and Bor South counties.
project_objective:
This project proposes provision of timely and quality lifesaving management of acute malnutrition through a full CMAM package of services for the most vulnerable children Under 5, pregnant and lactating women. 

The project will to reduce morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable population with who have fall into  alarming status (IPC 4) in the 3 Counties. CMD will increase equitable access and utilization of comprehensive  treatment  and preventive nutrition specific services which are essential for addressing the key drivers of acute malnutrition among children and women.In line with CMAM Protocol, through detection and treatment of children under 5 reaching at least 10,656 children with SAM, 40,125 with moderate acute malnutrition(MAM) and 21,521 malnourished PLW. 
CMD will establish 6 nutrition sites to including at 4 outreach/outreach static sites for remote and hard to reach areas at island locations through outpatient Therapeutic Program(OTP) for SAM children as well as Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program(TSFP) for MAM children and PLW. SAM Children with medical complication will be referred to existing stabilisation centres (SCs). At the community level, Community Nutrition Volunteers will conduct active case finding to strengthen early detection and timely referral of malnourished children and PLW,Both through routine community screening and family MUAC Approach.All children(6-59M) with SAM without medical complications who are enrolled in OTP program will be tested for malaria as per the national CMAM guidelines and those tested positive will be treated.The nutrition staff at the outreach will  be trained on national CMAM guidelines.
2. Prevention of malnutrition in children under 5 and PLW through promotion of MIYCN,Health,WASH and appropriate feeding and care practices through sensitisation sessions at the nutrition sites and as well community  sensitisation. All mothers/caregivers will be counselled.The staff at the outreach sites as well as CNV's will be trained on the national MIYCN guidelines.
Mother to Mother Support Groups(MtMSGs) will be formed and trained.To meet immediate food security needs,MTMSGs will also conduct sensitive cooking demonstrations as well as kitchen gardening activities.Led by male staff, men Group Discussions will be formed and initiate a dialogue around crucial nutrition specific and nutrition sensitive topics and gender issues(esp.MIYCN,GBV), enable women's  access to services, and safety promote gender equality through encouraging mutual support between gender groups.Safety audits will be conducted at all nutrition sites and outreach sites at least once during the project period using the tool endorsed by the nutrition cluster.A standard Feedback  and Complaints Mechanism(FCM) will be conducted across the sites to understand the concerns of the beneficiaries and collect information on how continue improving the program activities.The community activities will be carried out using other funding source.
CMD will work closely with Nutrition cluster,MoH,UNICEF and WFP to secure timely provision of Nutrition supplies which are necessary for nutrition services. CMD will also work with other partners/actors on ground implementing other interventions such as WASH,Health,NFI's and Food Security and Livelihood to address the emergency nutrition needs of the targeted population.

project_name: Emergency WASH support to vulnerable communities in Jonglei and  Upper Nile states.
project_objective:
Chronic WASH needs continue to emerge in parts of Greater Upper Nile States, which are likely to be exacerbated by unprecedented flood waters, COVID 19 restrictions, food insecurity as well as logistical challenges. Provision of adequate WASH services is key to achieving sustainable solutions to communities in emergency. CMD, a national NGO working in the locations of Jonglei and Upper Nile state envisages a targeted response aimed at reaching internally displaced persons, returnees and vulnerable host communities with water, sanitation and hygiene services, integrated with nutrition and protection/ GBV programming. Spanning a period of 12 months, the project targets the locations of Ayod, Duk, Fangak,
Bor South, Nyirol, Twic East and Pibor (Jonglei), Ulang (Upper Nile) with WASH temporary and sustainable services, to address the vital needs, public health and protection/GBV issues. 
The response aims at reducing levels of chronic malnutrition especially amongst children, pregnant and lactating women, mitigating WASH related GBV by providing gender appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities and tackling issues surrounding gender, safety and WASH. Persistence of food insecurity, signalled by high GAM rates, with <5s and PLW mainly affected will be mitigated by the provision of WASH in Nutrition services, through targeted WASH minimum packages at OTP/SC mainly for mother/caretaker – malnourished children. 
Water related disease outbreaks have been traced to health facilities and community infrastructures/settings without adequate WASH facilities.

project_name: Host community’s economic enhancement and socio-ecological restoration along with nutrition improvement of the Rohingya people in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
The goal of the project is to improve food security, nutrition and resilience of vulnerable people, especially women, youth and persons with disabilities (PWDs) from the refugees and host communities. This is intended to achieve with a landscape perspective, acknowledging that community based natural resource management and long-term socio-ecological system restoration, creates the foundation for socio-economic development of the vulnerable communities. 
The project aims to provide the Rohingya refugees with portable skills and knowledge on homestead gardening and accessibility to nutritious diversified food. FAO will provide technical assistance and input support to the 4,000 Rohingya households (i.e. 19,340 individuals) in achieving the desired goal that will capacitate and equip them with relevant transferable technological competencies for sustainable integration into the economy upon their return to Myanmar. 
 The programme will use conflict sensitive approaches to build capacity with consensus on sustainable use and management of natural resources with communities while safeguarding the ecosystem. This will be achieved through interventions such as forest restoration and watershed management, which are interlinked with agricultural farming practices for sustainable socio-economic improvement. . FAO will also promote disaster risk preparedness and reduction, through scaling-up piloted early warning system for landslides and conducting land stabilization and reforestation activities. Cash for work modality will be applied to implement these reforestation and forest restoration activities.
The host community people will have increased availability, and accessibility to nutritious foods; adopt climate-smart agricultural practices and improved and sustainable household income and resilience to shocks. FAO will provide input support to the host communities in practicing climate-smart homestead vegetable gardening production for year-round households’ consumption and improved nutrition.
FAO will further focus on marketing system approaches to ensure sustainability and adaptation of methodologies for the targeted beneficiaries. To ensure market linkages, income generation and increased productivity, FAO will support 4,000 farming households comprised of 200 farmer groups in practicing collective actions through ten aggregation centers in Cox’s Bazar. 
FAO will provide technical support to improve the operational capacities of the aggregation centers to establish vertical integration of the smallholder farmers with the traders and retailers in accessing local market. 
To assist smallholder farmers in increasing their farm productivity, a digital financial solution model called A-Card (‘A’ stands for Agriculture) will be piloted to solve the demand-supply gap in the capital market by offering a win-win partnership. FAO will also pilot an area-specific crop insurance programme for smallholder farmers that will include a method for yield measurement by using crop cutting; homogeneous and rain-fed or irrigated cropping system; similar varieties; and adopting improved farming practices through FAO Farmer Field School (FFS) approach. This will include GIS-based mapping tools for area zoning and Agricultural Hazard Vulnerability Analysis Mapping (AHVAM) land use planning for the selection of crop varieties, cropping season, and potential risks of different hazards.  
This project will support the school feeding programme implemented by WFP and the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE) with value chain interventions, for ensuring the supply of nutritious vegetables. 
FAO will pilot efficient and environment friendly irrigation systems i.e. “Solar charging station with battery operated portable water pump irrigation system”. The proposed innovative technology is new in the region and the solar power charging station will be installed at the FAO-supported Aggregation Center’s premises for charging the batteries.

project_name: Provision of comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response interventions to the floods and conflict affected communities in Ayod, Duk, Fangak and Malakal Counties in Jonglei  and Upper Nile states.
project_objective:
SAADO's proposed project will provide comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response interventions to the floods and conflict affected communities in Ayod, Duk, Fangak and Malakal Counties in Jonglei and Upper Nile states respectively.
