The proposal will target 4,000 beneficiaries (1000 boys;1000 men;1000 women;1000 girls) in Malakal County and 10,672 beneficiaries (1974 boys, 2436 girls,2852 men and 3410 women) in Ayod, Duk and Fangak Counties of Jonglei state. SAADO proposes to implement comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response activities by providing quality and timely, age appropriate, case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors. 
The proposed project seeks to implement GBV prevention, response and risk mitigation activities by providing quality and timely, age appropriate, case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors. Further, the proposed project will provide cash assistance to the most vulnerable women and girls visiting WGFSs who are facing financial challenges to facilitate them in accessing multi-sectoral GBV services. Priority will be given to survivors who require clinical management of rape (CMR) and survivors of Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) so that they can continue to visit health facilities, access for legal aid and they can also access the nearest available centers and safe spaces that provide PSS. 
This proposed project is designed to improve responses to cases of GBV and enhance the ability of survivors to recover from GBV incidences. SAADO will provide individual psychosocial support for women and girls in established women and girls' safe spaces in the targeted locations. The project's proposed activities will also include Strengthening Psychosocial Support services and collaboration with MHPSS working group, GBV awareness and risk mitigation measures, Strengthening the implementation of primary GBV preventions  interventions, Strengthening coverage of dignity kit distribution and programming as part of risk mitigation, GBV preparedness and contingency planning and provision of livelihood support, through the provision of need based capacity building trainings to GBV actors and frontline service providers and strengthening GBV case management and referral pathways. The activities in the established WGFS will be conducted using the guidelines from the ministry of health and World Health Organization (WHO) on COVID-19 prevention and will include maintaining social distance, wearing of masks and washing hands with soap. SAADO also intends to strengthen gender-based violence prevention through EMAP and community care programs to reduce GBV risks on men, women, boys and girls.
The targeted locations have been selected because of the prevalent needs stated in the HNO 2023 and appearing in category 5 and 4 in the severity mapping as well as SAADO's long standing presence  and GBV programming in Duk, Ayod, Fangak and Malakal Counties through implementation of CERF funded GBV Prevention & Response in Ayod including management of two (2) WGFS in Jiech and Mogok payams; GBV violence risk mitigation in Schools in Duk including management of (2) WGFS in Duk Pajut and Duk Pagak and four (4) WGFS established in Duk Poktap and Padiet and implementation of the South Sudan Humanitarian Funded (SSHF) GBV Prevention and Response project in Fangak since August 2022. 
The proposed project will build upon and complement SAADO's currently ongoing GBV prevention and response projects in the targeted locations. SAADO will coordinate this proposed response with the GBV sub cluster to ensure that the proposed activities are not duplicated and there is no overlap of activities and will work with health partners such as HRSS, CARE and John Dau Foundation to refer survivors for Post Rape services.

project_name: 2022-2023 Integrated Response for Conflict-Affected Populations (Inter-CAP) WASH
project_objective: The WASH component of the program is aimed at improving the overall health and wellbeing of 43,500 individuals including 4,787 IDPs. Water supply, Sanitation and hygiene education and promotion activities are designed to complement Nutrition and Livelihoods programs in order to deliver comprehensive health and wellbeing support to the targeted beneficiaries.

project_name: Mayendit and Mayom Mobile Health Services
project_objective:
Samaritan’s Purse SP, South Sudan, propose to provide essential life-saving primary health services to using a mobile health approach to affected peoples and communities in crisis and who are under-served and or unable to access existing health care services.  SP propose to continue Mobile health services in Mayendit and Mayom Counties, Unity State to eight (8) crisis affected communities who are unable to reach existing health care facilities and who are impacted by conflict and flooding, with many needing to temporarily relocate as well as host IDP’s from surrounding areas.
As an extension to the above activities Samaritan’s Purse propose a  Rapid Mobile Health Response to newly crisis affected communities by prepositioning resources and mobilizing a team to respond rapidly to emerging crisis as way to seek to prevent an escalating humanitarian situation for affected communities. This response may be up to three months while other partners ready themselves or the crisis is settled and the community return to their area and regular services. This rapid mobile health team may also be mobilized to respond quickly when there is an outbreak and need for a reactive vaccination campaign.

project_name: Integrated WASH services reinforcing resilience for communities affected by conflict, disasters, disease outbreak, in areas of high WASH severity.
project_objective:
PAH will implement both static and mobile WASH and multi-sectoral responses. As an organization active in 5 sectors - WASH, NFI, Protection, FSL and Education PAH will provide cross sectorial aid for the most vulnerable population of South Sudan. PAH will cooperate with partners in Nutrition and Health to provide the synergy of the actions. PAH will use its strong expertise in WASH to provide access to water and improve sanitation.
PAH will mainly target people facing high level of WASH vulnerability, those in locations if WASH Severity Classification 4 and 3, displaced or returnees and host communities with over-stretched resources. 
PAH is an experienced organization with broad portfolio of successfully implemented projects in various sectors. PAH will use is strongest expertise in WASH to provide assistance to vulnerable communities across the country by providing accessing to water, improving and sanitation both as single approach as well as in multi-sectoral responses PAH always seeks the synergies with other actions, as WASH sector covers the needs crucial for other aspects of life too. 
PAH will mainly target people facing high level of WASH vulnerability, those in severity 4, displaced or returnees and host communities with over-stretched resources. In case of need PAH will respond in mobile modality in other locations, according to the needs.  PAH will focus on rehabilitation and building water sources in institutions and those prioritized by community members. Sanitation will be provided on institutional level. Household level latrines will be promoted and sample ones constructed. PAH provides hygiene promotion, combined with protection, health, nutrition elements. Strong cooperation is implemented especially with the sector of Nutrition, by improving sanitation and water access in nutrition sites and training of the Nutrition personnel. The capacity building is always based on community members chosen to be promoters, water user committees and other engaged people within the community. PAH holds itself accountable to affected population and ensures its ownership of project results.
Recognizing the cross-cutting nature of WASH, PAH combine the described activities with other sectors by pro PAH will focus on rehabilitation and building water sources in institutions and those prioritized by community members. Sanitation will be provided on institutional level, establishment of the latrines at the household will be promoted.  PAH will provide hygiene promotion, combined with protection, health, nutrition elements, with cross-sectoral topics adjusted to the needs of the groups. This capacity building will be always based on community members chosen to be promoters, water user committees and other engaged people within the community. PAH holds itself accountable to affected population and ensures its ownership of project results.
Recognizing the cross-cutting nature of WASH, PAH combine the described activities with other sectors by providing dignity kits and NFIs, PAH works to improve protection status of women and girls. While improving access to water PAH takes care of irrigation needs for farmers and water for livestock, which contributes to improvement of food production and contain elements of diseases prevention. By improving sanitation and water access in nutrition sites, health centers and schools, PAH contributes to work in those sectors. As part of environmental approach PAH plants new trees around the water points, to implement environmental sustainability approach.
PAH, were feasible, will implement flood resilient infrastructure construction, such as elevated platform boreholes, community latrines and will encourage construction of flood resilient household level latrines, with use of local materials. 
Taking into consideration Ebola preparedness plans due to the cases in neighboring Uganda, in case of outbreak in South Sudan PAH  will follow the preparedness plans and procedures of respective authorities.

project_name: Management of WASH Pipeline to Strengthen WASH Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe Water; Sanitation and Hygiene Supplies
project_objective:
According to the 2023 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2023, about 6.3 million people has inadequate or lack of access to safe water, and sanitation in South Sudan. This is a reduction from 2022 where 6.6 million people were in need. The WASH situation has significantly improved in Pibor, Akobo, Bor South, Duk, Aweil South and the Greater Tonj counties, where WASH and nutrition needs were jointly prioritized in 2022. WASH conditions were found to be most severe in the Nile Basin states of Jonglei, Upper Nile, Unity and Northern Bahr el Gazhal. Canal/Pigi and Fangak were identified as the counties with the greatest WASH needs. WASH vulnerability was also found extreme, together with the high prevalence of malnutrition in Budi, Kapoeta East, Leer, Longochuk, Luapkini/Nasir, Maiwut, Manyo, Panyikang and Twic counties. Insecurity, displacement, natural disasters such as heavy flooding for the last three years have compounded the impact of low access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services in the country. The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving WASH supplies continues to be one of the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2014, IOM has been successfully managing a portion of the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Core Pipeline, which is an essential support to the WASH Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2023, IOM will maintain its commitment support the WASH Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key WASH supplies to benefit a total of 1.2 million people in need. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Rumbek, and Wau and newly identified locations to ensure efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, malnutrition, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks.

project_name: Provision of emergency shelter and non-food items and solutions to vulnerable internally displaced persons, returnees and host community in Jonglei, Unity, Central and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective:
South Sudan, generally is still a tough place to live especially for the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host community. The intercommunal violence spread almost across the entire country, common in Jonglei, other areas in Upper Nile and Bar-el-ghazel regions. It is mostly the women and children who are often at most risk plus the youth who are mobilized to fight inappropriate wars.
The impact of COVID-19 and failing economy continue to bite, affecting mostly the locals who lost their casual jobs, businesses. The greatest impact is on land tenure linked with returns. Though there is no data collected to prove this, but as a local NGO, many vulnerable South Sudanese are being evicted from time to time; landlords increase their rents at will or evict their tenants for their returning families. It seems many are returning due to inability to sustain their living standards in the neighbouring countries of Uganda and Kenya for those living in the suburbs. This is also the case with refugees in the camps; unavailability of cultivation land, decreasing food rations, long COVID-19 lock down are some of the reasons fostering returns apart from the struggling and holding peace.
In Jonglei and Unity States, subnational violence that results in child abductions, cattle raids, loss of lives and displacements, destruction of property including shelters razed down, continue to severely affect the two states. Currently Bentiu in Unity is the only County rated by IPC in the HNO 2022 at the catastrophic level in South Sudan. The rest of the counties in Unity and Jonglei are just at level 4 which is still extreme for human conditions.

Floods have also caused displacements, increased animal diseases which is wiping out the livelihoods and exacerbating shelter and non-food items needs among the internally displaced persons.
Floods and chronic insecurity have made these two states inaccessible making it difficult for humanitarian aid to reach. This makes delivery of aid more expensive.
Central and Eastern Equatoria have recently been impacted much by conflicts especially with the cattle keepers from Jonglei who seek pasture for their cattle and often drive cattle to the farms of the host community. These conflicts continue to cause further displacements at a small but well spread scale. The destruction of crops and other livelihoods including the cattle that are finding no pasture due to severe impact of extremities of climate change is having its toll on South Sudanese. 
Ebola virus disease is also a looming threat to lives of the impoverished South Sudanese. WHO and IOM have supported the South Sudan Ministry of Health in early preparations in case of an outbreak.

Central and Eastern Equatoria have high number of anticipated returns as reported by REACH monitoring team. This means huge needs for shelter and non-food items. However in order to build the local economy through the local markets, HDC will respond through cash and voucher assistance since the markets are highly functional in these areas.
CVA is highly recommended by the cluster in the year 2023. HDC has implemented cash programming in the past years and is well positioned to implement the project with experience.
Though all areas in Central and Eastern Equatoria have functional markets, parts of the areas in Jonglei; Twic East, Pibor and Duk have limited functionality in the markets if not functional. In-kind response will be prioritized in these areas.
HDC is capitalizing on its static presence to promote integrated response by responding in target locations through both SNFI and Protection. This will embed the strategic objective 2 of ensuring centrality of protection in all emergency responses. This will ensure dignity and protection of the most vulnerable groups among the internally displaced, host community and returnees
The project will target 40,643 vulnerable individuals; 16,250 women, 8,143 men, 16,250 children, 6,000 older persons and PWDs.

project_name: Assistance en Abris/AMEs et WASH aux populations déplacées internes et communautés hôtes dans les régions du Centre-Nord, du Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoun et du Sahel au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le présent projet s’inscrit dans l'articulation stratégique du plan de réponse humanitaire 2023 en cours de finalisation afin d’augmenter la capacité de réponse des acteurs humanitaires situés en première ligne de réponse à travers la mise en place d’interventions d’urgence. Le projet est axé sur une approche multisectorielle et couvrira les interventions WASH, Abris et AME dans les régions du Centre-Nord, du Nord de la Boucle du Mouhoun et du Sahel. Il s’agira de façon spécifique de fournir un paquet minimum d’activités afin de contribuer à repondre aux besoins les plus critiques et urgents en Abris/AME et en WASH des populations déplacées internes et communautés hôtes dans les communes de Nouna et Tougan (Boucle du Mouhoun), Kongoussi, Tougouri et Kaya (Centre-Nord), Ouahigouya et Séguénéga (Nord), Gorom-Gorom, Dori, Gorgadji et Djibo (Sahel). 
Le projet visera ainsi :
- la construction des abris d’urgence type pignon et la distribution de kits minimum standards d’AME à travers la modalité cash ou nature
- L’assistance des PoC par la mise à disposition de l’eau en qualité et en quantité par la réhabilitation des points d’eaux situés aux alentours des sites des PoCs; 
- L’accompagnement et la pérennisation de la mise à disposition de l’eau et la gestion des points d’eau pour les nouveaux déplacés des communes bénéficiaires avec l’appui en formation des associations des usagers des points.
- La contribution à la lutte contre la défécation à l’air libre et la préservation de la dignité par la construction des latrines et des douches en tenant compte de la question sensible du genre des besoins spécifiques des femmes en matière de protection en séparant les latrines et douches hommes et femmes.
- L’accompagnement de la vulgarisation par les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène, d’eau d’assainissement, de la protection du genre dans le respect des mesures barrières par des actions de sensibilisations.
-La prévention des maladies liées à la chaine de l’eau et aux mauvaises pratiques d’hygiène et d’assainissement par des activités de sensibilisations.
-La protection de l'environnement par la plantation et l'entretient des arbres. 
- La promotion de l'energie par l'installation d'éclairage public dans la communauté et sur les site PDI pour garantir une protection adéquate des femmes et des filles.
Ces activités seront réalisées dans onze communes de quatre régions précitées. Ces localités identifiées enregistrent chacune un grand nombre de déplacés internes suivant les alertes récentes et les données du CONASUR au 31 octobre 2022. Ainsi le projet prévoit toucher une cible de 56 000 bénéficiaires à travers les quatre régions, non compris la cible liée à l'éclairage public. Il y aura une complémentarité indispensable entre les activités Abris/AME et WASH du fait que la construction des abris d’urgence implique la distribution des AME la réalisation des infrastructures d’assainissement pour la préservation de la dignité humaine et la lutte contre la défécation à l’aire libre. De même l'éclairage des sites et espaces public augmente la sécurité et la protection des femmes et des enfants contre les violences basées sur le genre. La mise en œuvre des interventions se fera en partenariat avec des ONG locales afin de faire progresser la localisation en intégrant le renforcement de capacités des ONGs locales et d'améliorer la redevabilité envers les communautés bénéficiaires. Ces organisations loacales auront la charge de mettre en œuvre des activités telles que les sensibilisations, l’identification et la mobilisation des bénéficiaires, la redynamisation des comités, le recensement des points d'eau et latrines, la distribution des kits d'hygiène etc. Ce partenariat permettra de renforcer d’une part la localisation et d’être au plus près des populations et faciliter la mise en œuvre et d’autre part de contribuer à la pérennisation du projet par le renforcement des capacités des acteurs des ONGs locales.

project_name: Assistance humanitaire en WASH à 20 000 PDIs et 12 000 populations hôtes et vulnérables dans 6 communes des régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Centre-Nord et du Nord du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire au Burkina Faso s’est détériorée depuis 2015 entrainant près de 1 719 332 déplacés Internes selon les données du CONASUR du 30 Septembre 2022. La violence quasi quotidienne est généralisée sur 77% du territoire (10 sur 13 régions), affectant principalement les populations civiles, notamment les femmes et les enfants. 
Dans les zones d’accueil, les ressources naturelles déjà limitées sont insuffisantes pour couvrir les besoins des ménages hôtes et des PDIs. Sur les sites de PDIs et au sein des communautés hôtes, les besoins de première nécessité comme l’approvisionnement en eau salubre, l’assainissement et les notions de base en bonnes pratiques sont insuffisants voire inexistants, ce qui engendre et/ou aggrave la situation nutritionnelle des personnes vulnérables en générales et des enfants de moins de cinq ans en particulier.
Selon l’enquête SMART nutritionnelle réalisée en Août 2022 par le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de l’hygiène (avec le concours de l’UNICEF, d’IRC, du PAM et de DAVYCAS International), les regions du Sahel, de l’Est, du Nord, du Centre-Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun sont les plus affectées par la crise nutritionnelle notamment les communes de Nouna, Tougan (dans la boucle du Mouhoun), Barsalogho et Pissila (dans le centre Nord). 
 En tant qu'acteur du Cluster WaSH, avec une présence dans ces communes particulièrement touches ainsi que dans celles de Titao et Ouahigouya où des projets sont déjà en cours, APADE dispose des capacités et de l'acceptance communautaire dans ces zones pour mettre en œuvre une réponse d’urgence WASH dans ces communes en vue de contribuer à l’appui de la prise nutritionnelle dans ces zones vulnérables, APADE en 2023 prévoit d’intégrer la WASH in Nut dans ses projets et d’en faire une priorité. Le paquet minimum Wash pour le couple/mère enfant sera assuré dans différents centre de santé notamment de la région du Nord, ainsi qu’un suivi des bénéficiaires en matière de bonnes pratiques d’hygiène jusque dans les ménages. Les activités de réalisations et/ou réhabilitation de forages, de puits, de construction de latrines et de gestion de déchets solides et de boues de vidange viendront appuyer cet accompagnement et assurer une meilleure pérennité. 
Les populations ciblées seront celles des régions du Nord (Ouahigouya et Titao), du Centre Nord (Tougouri et Pissila) et de la Boucle du Mouhoun (Tougan et Nouna), avec une intégration continue de la PSEA et une attention particulière sur les personnes à besoins spécifiques et sur le renforcement de capacités des partenaires locaux.
APADE mise sur le recrutement de personnel local, le partenariat avec des associations et ONG locales.
Cette stratégie couplée à l'implication des leaders communautaires dans les orientations des interventions ont permis d'assurer une présence opérationnelle dans les zones inaccessibles tel que Titao. A travers UNHAS, le cluster logistique ou encore les convois, APADE assure la livraison des intrants vers les zones difficiles d'accès. 
Dans les localités où le marché local permet l'approvisionnement, APADE procédera à un cash transfer aux bénéficiaires de kits d'hygiène et de dignité.
Conformément à la stratégie de partenariat de APADE, l'ensemble des réalisations seront suivies et réceptionnées par les DREA des régions concernées.

project_name: Assistance en abris et en AME pour les PDI et PHV dans les communes des régions du Centre-Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, de l'Est et du Nord du Burkina-Faso.
project_objective:
Les derniers développements sécuritaires dans la Région du Centre-Nord du Burkina-Faso ont entrainé des déplacements de populations des villages vers plusieurs centres communaux.
Malheureusement, au regard des chiffres IDPs mensuels du CONASUR, les perspectives semblent s’assombrir. Aussi, une augmentation des afflux est prévisisble compte tenu du faible rendement de la campagne agricole. Ces déplacements continuent d'exercer une pression aigue sur les services sociaux et accroissent les besoins humanitaires (LTB, Éducation, Santé, Wash, Protection, Sécurité alimentaire…).
Ce faisant, dans les communes ciblées, malgré les constructions d’abris d’urgence menées en 2022, le besoin reste énorme. Des ménages continuent de dormir à la belle étoile et sous les arbres.
Le projet d’APADE s’aligne sur les types de construction préconisés dans la région du Centre-Nord et dans le Nord par le cluster Shelter/NFI au Burkina-Faso. 
Ainsi, le présent projet a pour objectif de fournir 2800 abris d’urgence destinés à accueillir 19 600 PDI dans 10 communes.
Dans les régions du Centre Nord et du Nord, l’action de APADE viendra compléter celle en cours de NRC et Plan International. APADE interviendra dans les 10 communes urbaines pour réduire le nombre de ménages vulnérables.

Objectifs spécifiques :
- Doter en abris d’urgence ossature à pignon (toiture à double pente), 2 800 ménages en absence complète d’abris et ceux vivant dans des abris précaires ou chez des PHV
- Former au moins 1 membre par ménage à l’entretien de l’abris d’urgence ossature à pignon
- Fournir des kits AME minimums standards aux 2 800 ménages bénéficiaires des abris
- Former les bénéficiaires à la gestion des déchets et les sensibiliser sur l’hygiène et l’assainissement
- Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d’usage de l’eau et de l’assainissement par la promotion de l’hygiène auprès de la population rurale et urbaine.

Aspects transversaux du projet :
Ces constructions seront complétées par celles de latrines du projet WaSH connexe. Celui-ci verra la construction de 840 latrines et de 30 forages avec PMH pour répondre aux normes SPHERE, ainsi que la dotation en kits d’hygiène de 5 600 femmes et/ou filles en âge de menstruation.
Le personnel ainsi que les membres des Comités du projet bénéficieront d’une formation VBG/PSEA.
APADE mise également sur la coordination avec les autres acteurs humanitaires présents dans les communes d’intervention. Cela se traduit, comme dans le passé avec NRC et Plan International, par le croisement des listes de bénéficiaires pour éviter les doublons ou encore la formation commune des menuisiers intervenant dans la construction des abris dans une même localité.
En termes de redevabilité, un Comité de Gestion des Plaintes (CGP) sera mis en place dans chaque commune. Mais aussi, des boites à suggestion seront rendus disponibles auprès des communautés bénéficiaires.

project_name: Aurore de la masculinité positive: Prévention et prise en charge multisectorielles des survivantes des VSBG au Centre Nord, au Nord et au Sahel
project_objective: Il s’agit d’un projet de prévention et de réponse multisectorielle des survivantes de violences sexuelles basées sur le genre (VSBG) dans la région du Centre Nord. L’objectif global est de contribuer à réduire l’incidence des VSBG parmi les femmes et filles des populations hôtes et déplacées et d’apporter une assistance holistique aux survivantes des violences sexuelles basées sur le genre. La zone d’intervention est la région du Centre Nord, Nord et le Sahel plus précisément les communes de Barsalogho; Kaya et Pensa ( Province du Sanmatenga) de Ouahigouya, Titao(Province de Loroum et de Ouahigouya) et de Dori, Gorom-Gorom et Sebba (Provinces de Séno, de l'Oudalan et de Yagha). D’une durée de 12 mois ce projet soulagera 54000 bénéficiaires dont 15000 hommes, 15000 femmes, 12000 garçons et 12000 filles. Les principales activités à mettre en œuvre sont: le renfoncement des capacités de l'équipe projet et des partenaires étatiques; les activités de prévention et de mitigation des risques des VSBG ainsi que la prise en charge des survivantes de VSBG. Ces activités permettront de former 80 agents de santé; 80 agents des services sociaux; 40 volontaires communautaires sur les VSBG; la réalisation de 36 émissions radio; 36 théâtres fora; et des activités récréatives et de sensibilisation au profit de 54000 personnes déplacées internes et de la population hôte; la dotation de kits de dignité a 3600 femmes et filles vulnérables; la dotation de 600 kits gaz a 600 femmes et filles vulnérables ainsi que la mise en place de 9 espaces surs pour les femmes et filles qui permettront la prise en charge de 2250 survivantes de VSBG dans les zones couvertes par le projet.

project_name: Prevention and response to S/GBV through Risk Reduction, Women Empowerment and Enhancement of Access to Services and Opportunities in Jonglei and Unity state
project_objective:
Protection needs remain the one of the most important priorities in South Sudan. In Jonglei and Unity State, protection concerns including GBV continue remain a high risk for vulnerable mainly women and girls. Cultural norms, traditional gender roles, regional conflict, militarized environment, and the frequent cattle raiding, and revenge killings are some of the factors contributing to this plague. There is Urgent needs of Gender based violence prevention, mitigation, and comprehensive response. 
Through this project INTERSOS aims to strengthen the prevention and response to GBV risks in in some of the counties with the GBV catastrophic severity (Ayod, Pibor, Rubkona and Mayendi) and extreme severity (Nyirol). The intervention will seek to address the immediate needs of GBV survivors and women at risk through establishment of women and girl friendly spaces where women can be empowered through life skills acquisition trainings and access to services and opportunities, Case management services and Psychosocial support services. To promote durable solutions and challenging negative social norms a strong component of GBV prevention has also been foreseen in the form of awareness through a community approach.

project_name: Provision of Integrated food and nutrition security services to the vulnerable house holds in Ulang County, Upper Nile state ,South Sudan
project_objective:
This project is a response to critical and lifesaving, Nutrition, and health needs of the IDPs and Host communities in Ulang County Upper Nile state  targeting a  total of 7923 beneficiaries (MAM under 5=3712 and MAM PLW=4211 with the main objective of reducing malnutrition prevalence rates amongst children 6-59 months and pregnant women (PLWs)
This project will be implemented by GOAL in conjunction with local NGO (UNKEA). GOAL will implement TSFP while UNKEA  will implement OTP services.  Food security activities will be integrated as part of the main nutrition program. The proposed response aligns with the HRP 2022 priorities  for food security and livelihoods, nutrition, and health cluster strategies and the  interventions will meet both immediate and lifesaving needs among affected populations while strengthening local capacity to deliver high quality service and contributing to reducing dependencies on food assistance as well as fostering longer term behavior change outcome.
This project will be implemented in all Payams in Ulang County targeting hard to reach areas and key activities will include;  providing  integrated preventive and curative nutrition services targeting the most vulnerable groups including responding to severe and moderate acute malnutrition and improve maternal infant and young child feeding practices comprehensive

project_name: WASH:  Emergency WASH support to Vulnerable households in Maiwut County of Upper Nile State, Pigi/Canal, Fangak and Ayod Counties of Jonglei State.
project_objective:
The counties of Ayod, Pigi, Fangak, Maiwut, and Nasir in Jonglei and Upper Nile respectively display some of the lowest standards in WASH parameters according to the most recent WASH cluster severity mapping. 
Gains in service provision over the years have been eroded by adverse weather effects resulting in prolonged flooding, leading to the destruction of WASH infrastructure, displacement of communities, deprivation of markets, and access to most parts of the states in focus. Flooding has further increased WASH-related mortality and morbidity affecting mainly under 5s, pregnant and lactating women, persons with special needs as well as persons living with HIV/TB. Lack of adequate WASH services directly affects the well-being of persons and communities, contributing to health, nutrition, food security, education, and protection indicators within affected communities. 
Community Action Organization (CAO) works in Jonglei and Upper Nile States in South Sudan and plans a robust WASH response aimed at improving community well-being while integrating and working closely with other thematic areas. 
The project will focus on fostering community-driven WASH responses to triggers. The project will further seek to enhance the reduction of WASH-related morbidities and mortality, through the provision of adequate, safe, and clean water for both domestic and livelihood purposes, mitigating WASH-related GBV and preventing livelihood deprivation associated with inadequate WASH standards. 
The project will reach a total of 63,000 persons in the counties of Ayod, Pigi, Fangak, Maiwut, and Nasir in Jonglei and Upper Nile respectively, 60% of these females, and 5% persons with special needs. 
CAO further will roll out an integrated response modality, seeking to implement jointly WASH, Health, Nutrition, FSL, Education, and Protection projects in the aforementioned counties.

project_name: FSL: Enhance provision of emergency FSL interventions and build Resilience for vulnerable population in need in Ayod, Fangak, and Canal/Pigi Counties, 2023
project_objective:
This project will contribute to the overall strategic objectives of the 2023 HRP and the three sectoral FSL cluster sector objectives through support provided by CAO’s donors and Food security and livelihood partners in order to improve food security and livelihoods situations during an emergency and resilience building of 71,400 (11,900HH) vulnerable women, men, boys, and girls by providing improved access to livelihood inputs for food production, consumption, and dietary diversity. 
The outcome of this project is anticipated to increase agricultural food production, protect and build productive assets and restore livelihoods for the vulnerable individuals that are affected by floods, inter communal conflicts, and physical access among vulnerable populations in high food insecure counties of Ayod, Fangak and Canal/Pigi counties whose populations are currently in IPC phase 5 4, and Phase 3 and has high disease comorbidity due to preventable diseases, high GAM rates of Malnutrition
Community Action Organization (CAO) is proposing a 12-month FSL project targeting 11,900 HH (71,400 vulnerable individuals; 10,400 IDPs, 17,600 returnees, 43,900 host community members; of whom 28,859 Women, 24,887 Men, 7,810 boys and 10,344 girls). CAO is an active FSL national partners having implemented emergency food security and livelihoods under 2021 SSHF SA1 in Ayod county and Fangak. 
In line with the FSL cluster and 2023 HRP strategic objectives, CAO will scale up response in the target locations by distributing main season and dry season response kits (crop and vegetable seeds, and fishing kits), train and develop the capacity of child protection workers, WASH staff, CNVs, and health workers on the establishment of Kitchen gardens and modern agronomic practices, livestock vaccination, training of CAHWs, assets creation, and business (VSLA) creation at the community level. 
The overall objectives of CAO’s planned FSL project are to; 1: Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations in line with the HRP SOs and FSL cluster objective 2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock. This will help to reduce vulnerabilities and risks associated with the current severe food insecurity, poor economic conditions, climatic shocks or floods, and reduced market access due to the poor road conditions among the affected population in Ayod, Fangak, and Canal/Pigi counties.
In this proposed project, CAO has targeted the following counties; Ayod, Fangak, and Canal/Pigi (Jonglei state) currently in IPC phase 4 & 5 (IPC, Feb 2022). The project will contribute to protection and recovery of livelihoods of the vulnerable population in Jonglei state.
In line with strategic cluster objectives 2: CLO2 Enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop seeds and fishing and livestock support and
objective 3, SO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb & adapt to shocks, CAO intends to reach out to the target population with the following activities; 1) Identification and validating the vulnerable households for their eligibility using a standard criteria, 2) Distribution of on-farm inputs crops and vegetable seeds and to enhance access to food production technologies, 3) Distribution of off-farm inputs/kits (fisheries’ hooks and fishing nets) to enhance access to off-farm food production inputs and 4) Link the beneficiaries to already available health facilities and referral pathway for effective case management to ensure effective integration.
CAO will target vulnerable households in consideration of gender and people living with disabilities, and ensure protection and Accountability to the affected population. CAO has a technical FSL specialist, is implementing FSL and protection with Oxfam GB in Ayod.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene services to flood and Conflicted Affected populations
project_objective:
The Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) situation in South Sudan remains dire. (All counties including Administrative area of Ruweng) Central Equatoria (Juba, Terekaka, Keji Keji, Yei, Upper Nile State (Longechuk, Maiwut, Ulang,Nasir,Malakal,Baliet and Manyo), Jonglei ( Fangak, Pibor, Pocholla, Twic East, Ayod,Akobo, Uror, Bor), Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil West, Aweil East, Aweil Centre and Aweil North), Warrap ( Tonj North, Tonj East and Tonj South) and Lakes State (Yirol, Rumbek North, Rumbek East, Rumbek Center and Wulu).. The specific states and counties targeted for this project remain worst hit by lack of WASH services as a result of floods and a number of other factors including general insecurity, poor socio-economic conditions where there are no markets or if available, functionalities are at minimum. Women and children are among the most affected population and hence increased deaths among U5. According to OCHA Humanitarian Needs Overview Report, it is estimated that 6 million people’s living standards and their wellbeing will continue being impacted in 2023 due to inadequate access to safe water and improved sanitation facilities. This number is higher than the 5.6 million people in need reported in 2021 and this is attributable to protracted conflicts, COVID-19 and perennial floods which have constantly devastated the entire Country for the past 3 years. 

The situation is worse in Fangak and Canal Pigi (severity level 5), Abyei, Budi, Kapoeta East, Ayod, Pibor, Twic East, Uror, Awerial, Cueibet, Aweil (Center, East, North), Guit, Leer, Mayom, Rubkona, Fashoda, Longochuk, Luapkini/Nasir, Maiwut, Malakal, Manyo, Melut, Panyikang, Renk, Twic, Jur River and Tambura (Severity level 4). Sanitation facilities across the entire Country are uncommon with 80% of households lacking access. Using of latrines has been considered a taboo in many parts of the country especially in states with a larger rural and/or pastoral population. Constructed latrines are hardly used in certain areas due to societal pressure with some people preferring walking long distances to practice OD even at night. 
Floods have damaged already constructed latrines and the situation coupled with conflicts that displaced households from time to time have resulted into households’ fatigue and discouragement to invest in, reconstruct, or repair sanitation facilities. 
This project is therefore in line with WASH cluster specific objectives in the HRP (2022)-2023 which are to;
1.	Contribute to reducing prevalence of malnutrition
2.	Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality
3.	Provide access to basic WASH services in underserved locations affected by disaster
4.	Mitigate WASH-related GBV and disability inclusion
5.	Provide sustainable access to services in long-term IDP sites and communities chronically affected by disaster
Coalition for Humanity will address these gaps by
1.	Rehabilitation of water points, distribution of WASH core pipeline items like aqua tabs, water storage facilities and hand washing facilities.
2.	Construction and rehabilitation of flood resilient latrines within nutrition facilities and public institutions in the community where IDPs seek temporary shelter during floods.
3.	Identification of vulnerable girls and women of child bearing age and provide them with MHM kits.
4.	Conducting Protection monitoring and GBV risks analysis at water points to ensure safety of women and girls
5.	Training hygiene promoters to create awareness and sensitize communities on the importance of good nutrition, importance of latrine construction and water treatment
6.	Establishment and training of water resource management committees that will take over the maintenance of the rehabilitated water points beyond the project funding.
This project will target 20,000 HH (120,000 Individuals) in  Central Equatoria (Juba, Terekaka, Keji Keji, Yei) Unity (All counties including Administrative area of Ruweng), Upper Nile (Longechuk, Maiwut, Ulang, Nasir, Malakal, Baliet and Manyo), Jonglei (Fangak, Pibor, Pocholla, Twic East, Ayod, Akobo, Uror, Bor), Northern Bahr el Ghazal (Aweil West, Aweil East, Aweil Centre and Aweil North), Warrap ( Tonj North, Tonj East and Tonj South) and Lakes State (Yirol, Rumbek North, Rumbek East, Rumbek Center and Wulu). The beneficiaries will be segregated by gender as follows;
Men = 25,000
Women = 45,000
Gils = 25,000
Boys = 25,000

project_name: Strengthening the provision of emergency and integrated lifesaving primary health care services for the vulnerable communities of Mayendit and Guit Counties of Unity State and Manyo County, Upper Nile State
project_objective:
Malaria, acute watery diarrhea, acute respiratory tract infections, pneumonia and snake bites are common causes of morbidity in Guit and Mayendit Counties of Unity and Manyo County of Upper Nile State. 
Therefore the project is designed to support over 40,000 OPD (5,500 boys, 4,900 girls, 19,000 women and 10,600 men including 850 persons with disabilities) consultations in static facilities and mobile health facilities, facilitate 1,900 normal deliveries attended by skilled birth attendants, and facilitate the immunization 8,500 children (Girls 3,825 and Boys 4,675) with 3 doses of PENTA-3 vaccine. It will also provide quality maternal healthcare services to 4,650 women of child bearing age of IDPs, returnees and host community including FP, ANC, PNC, IPT 1 and 2, de-worming and TT immunization and further provide child healthcare services (routine immunization, Vit A supplementation and child growth monitoring) to 7,815 girls and 8,919 boys, including accelerated mass measles and polio campaigns. 
In addition the project is designed to provide psychiatric treatment and psychosocial support to 75 (45 male and 30 females) mentally ill persons and provide community-based level 2 and level 3 (non-specialized) MHPSS to 700 persons living with disabilities (PLwD's), including referrals for specialized services from other partners. The project will support screening 6,700 pregnant women, lactating mother and children under 5s for malnutrition and refer them to for treatment/management.
In the management of common illnesses, the project will facilitate the management of 7,400 uncomplicated diarrhea cases with ORS and Zinc, management of 11,200 uncomplicated malaria cases with ACT, management of 7,400 uncomplicated respiratory infections (pneumonia) treated with Amoxicillin. 
In collaboration with community health workers, health promoters and Boma Health Workers, About 40,000 people (5,500 boys, 4,900 girls, 19,000 women and 10,600 men including 850 persons with disabilities) will be reached with health education and promotion to prevent disease outbreaks. In addition, 27,500 (Females 16,500 and Males 11,000) will be reached with awareness through community engagements strategy on GBV prevention, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, drug abuse, peace building and peaceful coexistence.
In each target County, CASS will conduct 12 community meetings in each Payams of the targeted Counties to provide accountability to the communities (AAP strategy). Monthly joint supportive supervision visits to increase quality of services will be facilitated to all health facilities and field mobile teams and linkages with Boma Health Initiatives (Boma Health Workers) for community-based disease surveillance and referral will be strengthen. 
Finally, the project will provide care to physical injuries and CMR including level 2 and level 3 non-specialized MHPSS to survivors of GBV, support active epidemic disease surveillance, prevention and control diseases including outbreak detection, investigation and responding within 48 hours and support 52 timely and weekly EWARS/IDSR reports from each of the 3 focused Counties, in addition it will support IPC in health facilities through regular assessment using score cards, provision of supplies and protocols and continuous monitoring of WASH in health facilities.

project_name: Nutrition Interventions for Disaster affected populations in Abiemnhom, Koch, Mayom, Pariang, Rubkona and Twic East
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to grapple with devastating conflict that has led to an unprecedented humanitarian crisis. The main drivers of the protracted humanitarian crisis include political and communal violence, climate-induced shocks including floods, disease outbreak and economic hardships. The ongoing flooding remains the worst recorded in the history of the country .  Climatic shocks (flooding, dry spells, and droughts), insecurity (sub-national and localized violence), population displacements, and high burden of diseases and disease outbreaks as well as the economic crisis  are the drivers of the food insecurity. As a result of the high food insecurity, high disease prevalence, poor quality and diversity of food, poor access to health and nutrition services and covid-19 related disruptions, 2, 175,546 are at risk of acute malnutrition in 2023. 

Unity State was disproportionately affected by flooding in 2022, with 80% of its surface area (7 out of the 9 Counties) flooded and 240,000 people displaced  by floods and 120,000 displaced by conflict. The most affected counties of Rubkona, Mayom, Pariang, Abiemnhom and Koch, where CARE runs its largest Emergency Nutrition Programme, have the majority of those displaced. There are also 124,004 Refugees are in Pariang, in addition to Returnees and vulnerable host communities who are particularly hit hard by the crises in the state, given their vulnerability and lack of coping mechanisms. Particularly concerning is that floodwaters have not showed any sign of  receding 10 months later and  the stagnant flood water is now responsible for an upsurge in communicable diseases (Cholera, Acute Watery Diarrhoea and Malaria) in the Counties of Rubkona, Koch, Pariang and Mayom. 10 Nutrition Facilities have been destroyed, leaving 1,650 children at high risk in Rubkona . In addition, WFP has in the recent has a funding cut that resulted in the reduction in the food basket provided to the population. 

CARE international is well known for its high-quality Nutrition Programmes in South Sudan. In 2022, CARE reached over 262,461 children under the age of 5 and Pregnant and lactating women/Girls with Nutrition Services, as well as 330,000 with health services across the 5 counties within the state. CARE is also a member of the Health and Nutrition Clusters, as well as the Strategic Advisory Groups (SAG) for both Clusters. This project will provide Integrated, lifesaving, emergency nutrition interventions for children under the age of 5, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), elderly men and women. Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Returnees will be of special interest to this project because of their high levels of vulnerability. To do this, CARE will implement all the components of CMAM as follows: 
1.	Community mobilisation
2.	Outpatient Therapeutic Programme for management of SAM without medical complications (OTP)
3.	Outpatient Therapeutic Programme for management of MAM (SFP)
4.	In-patient care for management SAM with medical complications (SC/ITP)

project_name: Provision of immediate emergency life-saving WASH response through linkages with GVB/Protection, Nutrition and Health to the vulnerable IDPs, host communities, returnees, people with disabilities, women, girls, boys and men affected by natural disasters and human conflicts
project_objective:
The situation is further worsened by continued violence, climatic shocks, coupled with the effect of   floods resulting in worsening of community WASH infrastructure, nutrition, health and protection/SGBV concerns amongst women and girls. According to Food Security and Nutrition Monitoring System(FSNM  August 2022 report revealed between July 2022 and June 2023, an estimated 1.4 million children under five are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition based on analysis and estimations from the results of the SMART nutrition surveys
Africa Development Aid anticipates that, if supported, it will ensure 34540 vulnerable population experiencing multi-sectoral severity levels 3 , 4  and 5 IPC targeted by this response will have reduced mobility and mortality through integrated WASH, Nutrition, Health and Shelter/NFI essential services to meet their needs.  It is expected to cost $750,000 in one year. The six counties (Ayod,  Fangak, Pigi/Canal and Nyirol (of Jonglei State), Nasir (of Upper Nile State) and Mayendit  (of Unity  State) have remained consistently with low level of WASH coverage, leaving vulnerable communities without resilience to withstand the chronic and acute crisis that has engulfed the county.  Access to safe drinking-water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services is a fundamental element of healthy communities and has an important positive impact on nutrition. This proposed intervention will provide an overview of the evidence of nutrition and health gains that can be achieved with integrated nutrition, health and SGBV a description of key WASH practices, and practical knowledge.

Poor access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), whilst not the root cause of violence, can exacerbate the vulnerability of women and girls to violence. Men and boys, people of other gender or sexual identities or other marginalized groups can also sometimes be at risk. Vulnerability to violence can have a significant impact on people’s access to adequate water and sanitation and hygiene.

The proposed intervention will be to reduce morbidity and mortality among children through integration with nutrition, protection/GBV and health by providing access to safe water, rehabilitation of water points and water treatment at nutrition facilities as well as communities and promote hygiene promotion /campaigns.
Nutrition facilities will be provided with WASH/NFI kits/minimum WASH packages to care takers of children admitted and screened with SAM/MAM at functional OTP and training on the use of the items/kits.

The continued conflicts has resulted in devastation of WASH infrastructure largely contributing not only to disease outbreak, but also to increased malnutrition, public health risks and increased gender-based violence among women and girls and other vulnerable groups.
WASH,-Nutrition, health and GBV integrated programming will aim at areas of high level of malnutrition, by targeting of SAM children and their families. These areas will further converge with other Health-related priorities, acknowledging that poor WASH services are a key driver to poor health
These proposed counties already experienced high food insecurity and malnutrition (GAM rates have also heightened WASH needs. Women and girls are the primary direct users of WASH services and GBV risks have significant implications for the success of WASH interventions.  ADA will ensure GBV risk mitigation is a priority area of focus.

ADA WASH will ensure delivery of specific activities such as gender segregated latrines that meet the needs of women, children and people with disabilities.  Consultations by conducting safety audit will be conducted at site level to identify Gender based violence concerns and implement measures. ADA will focus on emergency hygiene promotion targeting community level.  Emphasize will be made on disease prevention such COVID 19 and WASH related illnesses and hand washing with soap.

project_name: Provision of quality Protection services to disasters affected children and their parents facing trauma in Ayod, Pigi, Fangak, Nyirol and Maiwut Counties of Upper Nile and Jonglei States.
project_objective:
Africa Development Aid intends to provide quality protection services to crisis-affected children and their caregivers in Ayod, Pigi, Nyirol and Fangak Counties of Jonglei State, Maiwut county of Upper Nile State. This project will seek to provide an immediate lifesaving response to the vulnerable crisis and flood-affected children from returnees, IDPs, and host communities through strengthened comprehensive case management including family tracing & reunification; referral for services; provision of critical age and gender appropriate psycho social support services including parental skills sessions in a timely, holistic and child-friendly manner as well as to the traumatized adult caregivers whose children are also facing trauma, coordination monitoring and assessments of child protection related risk. The projects will also conduct awareness-raising activities on prevention of family separation, COVID-19 prevention, and response while putting into practice the COVID-19 preventive measures. ADA is having active Child protection activities in  Canal/Pigi, Ayod and Fangak Counties. However, under this project ADA will provide static and mobile critical age and gender appropriate psycho social support services in individual and group sessions including Psycho social support to caregivers of children who are traumatized and undergoing PSS activities, identification, registration, interim care, family tracing & reunification to unaccompanied and separated children, advocate for GBV related risk prevention including early marriage, Sexual abuse, exploitation and violence, referral to other services such as health, education, nutrition, shelter and NFIs among others to those at risk and other vulnerable children including those facing other forms of violence, orphans as well as Justice for children (J4C) in a timely, holistic and child-friendly manner and also promote resilience to the traumatized ones.
The project will also seek to enhance the protection environment of vulnerable crisis-affected girls, boys, and youths to enable durable solutions through the establishment of community-based child protection networks, foster family groups, youth/adolescent clubs, Child-Friendly Spaces, child rights clubs, and recreational centres while observing COVID-19 guidelines. This will create enabling conditions for the realization of solutions and prevention of further displacement which leads to family separations; identification of risks, dangers, and impediments; advocacy and mitigation measures, psycho social support, peaceful co-existence initiatives, and resilience.
In Ayod County, the project will cover the following payams, e.g.,Pajiek, Wau Menime, Haat and Kuach-deng payams, Ayod, Pagil, Paguong and Mogok, ADA will also target Atar, Kurwai, Wulieth, kaldak and Khorfulus payams of Pigi County . In Fangak County, the project will concentrate in Mareang, Keew, Paguir, Toch and Manajang (Juaibor), Barboi, New Fangak and Old Fangak Payams. Meanwhile, since there was no Funded Partner for Child protection activities in Nyirol County in 2021, Identified gaps have been noted in Lankien, Tut, Pultruk, Waat, Nyanbor, Chuil, Pading and Keeth payams. ADA will also response in Mawuit County targeting all its payams namely; Jotoma, Kigila, Mawuit, Jekow and Olang.
A total of 25,000 people (12,500 Males and 12,500 females) will benefit from this project. Out of this, 15,000 will be children (7,500 girls; 7,500 boys) and 10,000 will be adults – 5,000 males and 5,000 females. However, out of the total beneficiaries 30% will be from the host community while 10% will be from Returnees and 60% from IDPs.

project_name: Improve Food Security and Livelihoods in West Bank, Area C
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve the food security and livelihoods of some of the 
most vulnerable farmers and herding communities in the West Bank through 
the provision of comprehensive support to a total of 160 small-scale farmers (48 female, 112 male) and herding communities, targeting indirectly (226 women and 526 men) from the following communities: 
West Bank: Area C, including Jordan Valley, Masafer Yatta and Badyat al-Quds 
The project will help small-scale farmers and herding communities, including women, in Area C improve access to resources to better cope with emerging crises and sustain their livelihoods. 
This will be achieved through the following activities: 
ACTIVITY #1: Provision of 160 tons of seeds for grazing for 160 livestock farmers 
ACTIVITY #2: Provision of 160 milking machines for dairy production for 160 livestock 
farmers 
ACTIVITY #3: Rehabilitation of 160 livestock sheds 
ACTIVITY #4: Rehabilitation of 2km agricultural roads 
ACTIVITY #5: Increase public awareness of project staff, partner and beneficiaries on 
PSEAH and gender mainstreaming.
The project will target small-scale food-insecure livestock farmers from Area C. Selection of beneficiaries will be in line with the general pre-set vulnerability criteria agreed by the FSS cluster. NPA and the 
implementing partner will narrow down the selection criteria based on technical field 
assessments in coordination with local committees/community representatives. 
The selection criteria will be as the following:
-	women headed households (WHH) 
-	small-scale farmers who are living in poverty 
-	households with over 3 dependent children 
-	households supporting elderly relatives 
-	households supporting people with physical impairment 
-	families who have lost access to livelihoods
-	families forced or who are experiencing lockdowns and isolation. 
-	families whose land is close to Israeli settlements 
-	farmers who have been recently impacted by the ‘Foot and Mouth Disease’ 
Women participation in the project will be ensured throughout the project cycle. Women 
have already participated in the assessment that informed the design of this project and 
will continue to engage in the implementation and monitoring of project activities. NPA /PFU uses the United Nations minimum quota for women’s participation, which is 30% of project beneficiaries. Under this minimum quota, at least 48 of the direct beneficiaries (160 total), must be women. To ensure that the minimum amount of women’s participation is achieved, PFU will use its connections with its governorate-based farmers’ associations and women’s cooperatives to target vulnerable female-led households to benefit from the project activities and assisting them in completing the applications. To ensure that the maximum number of women benefit from the project, as long as all other criteria are met, women who apply to benefit from the project activities in target locations will be accepted as beneficiaries of the project, by being constantly aware of the social barriers that limit women’s participation and mitigate them. Women-headed households will be prioritized to participate in the project as according to HNO they are most vulnerable and under-served. NPA and implementing partner will coordinate closely with all key stakeholders including the Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security Cluster and other humanitarian actors in all project localities. Information about activities and progress, including 4Ws matrix will be shared with the FSS cluster. The proposed activities under this project have already been 
coordinated and agreed with the Ministry of Agriculture, FSS cluster. A monitoring and evaluation framework will be developed to track progress made and ensure relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and impact of the project.

project_name: Conflict Preparedness and Protection Risk Education for At-Risk Communities in the Gaza Strip - CPP
project_objective:
The proposed project will seek to ensure civilians living in high risk conflict-affected communities in the Gaza Strip are better prepared and protected in case of armed conflict and are empowered with the knowledge they need to mitigate risks associated with explosive weapons.
NPA’s CPP approach for 2023 will focus improving civil protection through the following core activities: providing CPP and EORE training for adult beneficiaries living in Gaza via community-based training sessions, implementation of child-friendly CPP and EORE training for children in schools through in-class sessions and school events, public awareness raising of CPP and EORE principles via social media campaigns, psychosocial support to beneficiaries who have experienced trauma resulting from armed conflict, and the development of early emergency warning systems for target schools.

project_name: Burkina Faso Accès à la scolarisation des enfants dans les zones à forts défis sécuritaires « BASE »
project_objective:
Dans un effort de contribution et d’alignement avec la réponse humanitaire au Burkina Faso, Plan International, avec le soutien financier de l’Agence Française de Développement (AFD), apporte une alternative de scolarisation dans les zones à fort defi securitaire à travers le projet BASE (BFA Accès à la scolarisation des enfants dans les zones à fort défi sécuritaire). Financé par l’AFD à hauteur de 3 millions d’euro (1 967 871 000 FCFA), le projet a pour objectif de faciliter l’accès à la scolarisation de 32.050 enfants de 6-15 ans (50% de filles) affectés par la crise dans la région du Centre Nord (6 communes dont Kongoussi et de Bourzanga dans le Bam, Pissila, Kaya et Barsalogho dans le Sanmatenga et Bouroum dans le Namentenga) sur une durée de 30 mois (18 Septembre 2020 au 17 mars 2023).
La mise en œuvre des activités du projet est assurée par deux (02) ONG locales partenaires (ARCOP & FDC) au sein de 70 de écoles primaires et franco-arabes, 15 établissements Post-primaire et trente (30) centres d’éducation accélérée (SSA/P) avec l’implication des services techniques déconcentrés, les autorités locales, les communautés et les organisations d’enfants et de jeunes. Les différentes interventions de ce projet se font dans le respect des mesures sanitaires de prévention contre la COVID-19, et des principes « Do-No-Harm » dans une approche sensible aux inégalités de genre et aux conflits.

project_name: Fourniture de services d’Eau-Hygiène et Assainissement au profit des institutions, des ménages y compris en situation de crise humanitaire dans la région de l’Est
project_objective:
Avec la crise sécuritaire et sociale qui sévit le Burkina-Faso en général et la région de l’Est en particulier, les ressources en Eau potable deviennent de plus en plus insuffisantes dans certaines communes d’accueil des Personnes Déplacées Interne. On note parallèlement un manque criard des infrastructures d’assainissement (latrines, douches avec puisards) et cela entrainent la recrudescence des maladies liées au péril fécal. Le projet consiste donc à mettre en œuvre un paquet d’activités dont l’objectif est de réduire les risques de santé publique dans les zones d’intervention. Les actions conduites se résument à la promotion des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène ; l’approvisionnement en eau salubre et potable ; la fourniture d’équipements d’assainissement appropriés ; la réduction des risques sanitaires liés à l’environnement ; L’amélioration des conditions d’hygiène dans les formations sanitaires et dans les écoles, la garantie de conditions permettant aux personnes de vivre dignement, en bonne santé, dans le confort et la sécurité. 

Les actions s’inscrivent dans une logique globale d’intervention incluant la nutrition, la santé de la mère et de l’enfant et l’hygiène dans les espaces amis d’enfants. Notre projet cible les institutions (écoles, formations sanitaires, centre de formation professionnelle), les ménages y compris les ménages déplacés dans le cadre de l’insécurité. 
Dans nos approches, la participation de la communauté est au centre de toutes les activités WASH. En effet, dans nos projet WASH, la participation de la communauté est un processus dynamique permettant d’établir un lien entre la communauté et les autres parties prenantes, et permettant aux personnes affectées par la crise d’avoir une meilleure maîtrise de l’intervention et de son incidence. Le projet met l’accent sur l’engagement efficace des communautés et les équipes d’intervention afin de maximiser le rôle de la communauté dans la réduction des risques de santé publique, de fournir des services appropriés et accessibles, d’améliorer la qualité du projet et de mettre en œuvre des mécanismes de responsabilité. Nos actions s’appuient sur la capacité et la volonté de la communauté à gérer et à entretenir les systèmes WASH. 
Spécifiquement, notre projet poursuit les objectifs suivants :
- Améliorer l’accès digne, durable et sûr des populations hôtes et déplacées aux infrastructures d’eau, d’hygiène et assainissement dans la région de l’Est d’ici à fin 2023 ;
- Renforcer la gouvernance des infrastructures d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement et la cohésion sociale dans les communes de la région de l’Est d’ici à fin 2023 ;
Contribuer au développement des initiatives de création d’emplois décents portées par les jeunes, les femmes y compris les déplacés et les acteurs de la filière hygiène et assainissement dans la région de l’Est d’ici à fin 2023.
- Encadrer et former les communautés pour un programme WASH résilient au climat.

project_name: Je m'engage pour les enfants déplacés internes
project_objective:
Le Projet je m’engage pour les enfants déplacés interne est une initiative du consortium Children Believe et l’Association M’aNathan dans les régions de l’Est et du Centre Nord. L’objectif global est de contribuer à l’épanouissement et à l’autonomisation des enfants affectés par la crise humanitaire dans les régions ciblées afin qu’ils soient à même de répondre à leurs besoins d’éducation, de protection  et développement  dans un environnement sûr et protecteur. 
Le volet protection de l’enfant du projet contribuera à l’atteinte de la Tolérance Zéro contre les Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG), les Abus et Exploitations Sexuelles (AES) et les violences faites aux enfants sous toutes ses formes. Les questions de VBG d’AES et de SPSS seront adressées aussi bien en milieu scolaire que communautaire en favorisant l’émergence d’un engagement et d’un leadership communautaire fort. 
Différentes approches seront utilisées dont l’approche basée sur les droits humains, L’approche Redevabilité Sensible à l’Enfant (Child Friendly Accountability) qui assure une pleine participation des enfants et des jeunes. Un focus sera mis sur les filles vulnérables à besoin spécifique à travers les renforcements de capacités en vue de faire d’elles des jeunes filles/dames leaders, ambassadrices et modèles engagées pour un changement de mentalité et de paradigme au sein des communautés. Le projet qui sera réalisé en collaboration avec les services déconcentrés de l’Etat et les organisations de la société civile, permettra de briser le silence, les tabous et d’accroitre la redevabilité. Par ailleurs dans le cadre des efforts d’intersectorialité, le projet je m’engage pour les enfants déplacés intègrera également dans ses interventions des questions liées à la nutrition, la santé sexuelle et reproductive et le WASH dans le respect des principes humanitaires

project_name: Santé mentale et dispositif mobile intégré en santé, nutrition et protection pour les personnes affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans l'Oudalan
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer l’accès aux soins de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial en intégrant la prise en charge sanitaire ponctuelle (soins curatifs), des soins préventifs (vaccination) au besoin, le référencement ainsi que la sensibilisation sur les bonnes pratiques d’ANJE et le dépistage systématique de la malnutrition aiguë chez les enfants de 6-59. Il s’agira de mettre en place une équipe mobile pluridisciplinaire pour l'offre de prestations multisectorielles aux populations affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans l'Oudalan. La principale cible sera les personnes affectées par la crise sécuritaire (PDI et hôte) mais également les enfants de 6-59 mois issus des ménages mobilisés pour l’activité. L’activité se fera au travers des sorties conjointes de l’équipe projet (gestionnaire de cas, agent psychosocial, infirmier) avec une équipe santé du district sanitaire (DS) pour l’offre de soins gratuit au compte du projet. Cette équipe mobile sera en cas de chocs déployée pour des réponses d’urgence mais en dehors des urgences sur les sites de personnes de PDI ainsi que les villages affectés par des chocs sécuritaires pour l’offre de ces prestations en particulier l'offre de soins en santé mentale.  Le projet vise à couvrir au moins 30% des FOSA par commune. Cette stratégie mobile intégrée à la santé entend couvrir toutes les personnes affectées sans distinction pour des soins curatives et préventives y compris la PEC des VBG tout en veillant au respect de la gratuité ciblée de l'Etat. Pour cela un stock de contingence de médicaments essentiels sera mis en place pour assurer les différentes sorties d’urgence et au besoin appuyer le DS en cas de rupture.
Afin d’assurer une prise en charge continue et un appui d’urgence en soutien psychosocial au sein des populations, les agents de santé, les ASBC et les AV seront formés en premiers secours psychologiques et sur l’identification et le référencement de cas de VBG.
Le projet couvrira la province de l’Oudalan en cas choc pour les réponses d’urgence mais sera recentré dans la commune de Gorom-Gorom pour les interventions de routine. Outre les prestations de soutien psychosociales offertes par l’équipe mobile, des soins de santé mentale seront disponibles pour les personnes avec des besoins d’accompagnement spécifiques au niveau du CMA. Cette prestation sera assurée par un attaché de santé en santé mentale recruté et mis à la disposition du district sanitaire par COOPI.
Le projet prévoit toucher 8 000 personnes en thérapie de groupe et au moins 500 personnes en individuel durant 10 mois de mise en œuvre opérationnelle sur le volet santé mental et soutien psychosocial avec la gestion d’au moins 100 cas de protection dont la PEC d'au moins 30 cas de VBG. En ce qui concerne le volet santé au moins 1 000 personnes vulnérables/ très pauvres détectées sur les sites et ou référés par les services de l’action humanitaire et autres ONG partenaires seront touchées par la prise en charge sanitaire ainsi que le dépistage et le référencement d’au moins 300 cas de malnutrition aiguë (MAM et MAS) vers les formations sanitaires (PSA/CSPS) fonctionnel de proximité pour leur prise en charge. Un suivi du référencement des enfants dépistés sera également assuré par le projet.
COOPI dispose d’un référent sécu très imprégné de l’évolution du contexte sécuritaire de la province qui assurera la veille humanitaire sur les différents déplacements de l’équipe. COOPI possède également des relais au niveau de la sous-région notamment au Mali et au Niger qui avec lesquels une veille sera également assurée au regard de la proximité de la zone d’intervention avec ces pays limitrophes. 
L’équipe du projet sera formée sur les principes humanitaires et les règles et mesures de sécurité en contexte de crise. Les équipes seront également formées sur la prévention des EAS et les mécanismes d’alerte, des liens seront créés avec les services sociaux existants (réseau de protection et directions provinciales notamment).

project_name: Assistance en Abris d’urgence (abris à pignon)/abris semi-durable et AME au profit des PDI et populations hôtes dans les regions de l'Est, Centre-Nord et Centre-Est du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
La crise sécuritaire continue de provoquer des déplacements massifs des populations au Burkina Faso depuis 2015. A la date du 31 octobre 2022, le nombre des populations déplacées internes est passé à 1 761 915 soit une augmentation d’environ 2,48% par rapport à la date du 30 septembre 2022 (SP/CONASUR, 2022). La crise s’est généralisée dans presque toutes les régions du pays dont le Centre-Nord, le Sahel, l’Est et le Nord et la Boucle du Mouhoun, les Haut-Bassin, le Centre-Est, les Cascades et le Sud-Ouest.
Dans ce contexte de crise, ces populations font face à d’importants défis en termes d’accès aux services sociaux de base. Les conditions de vie des communautés d’accueil se sont dégradées et les capacités d’accueil dans certaines familles se sont retrouvées réduites. Certaines familles se sont déplacées à plusieurs reprises en raison de l’insécurité et les perspectives de retour immédiat sont faibles au regard de la dégradation de leurs moyens de subsistances les rendant plus vulnérables.
Au cours de l’année 2022, cette situation d’insécurité couple avec l’inflation des prix sur le marché a engendré une importante augmentation des besoins des populations déplacées. Prévu initialement a 3,5 M dans le HRP de 2022, les besoins sont passe à 4,9 M de personnes dans le HRP révise en Aout 2022. Le secteur Abris/AME dénombre 2 092 582 personnes dans le besoin, soit une augmentation de 37% lors du HRP 2022 initial. De plus l’urbanisation de la crise et la concentration des PDI dans les centres urbains contribue à amplifier les risques d’exploitation des PDI et d’éviction, désorganise la planification urbaine et réduit l’accès au loyer.
A travers ce projet, DEDI vise à renforcer la sécurité des personnes vulnérables par l’amélioration de l’accès aux abris (urgence et semi-durable) et aux articles ménagers essentiels dans des meilleures conditions. Le projet cible 83 888 personnes soit 1 398 ménages qui recevront des Kits couplés abris d’urgence et articles ménagers essentiels dans 3 régions du Burkina à savoir le centre-Nord, l’Est et le centre Est.
L’approche BBB intègre des mesures de réduction des risques de catastrophe en matière de restauration des infrastructures physiques, des systèmes sociaux et des abris, de revitalisation des moyens de subsistance, des économies et de protection de l’environnement. La participation et l'appropriation communautaires sont aux cœurs de cette approche. Les activités seront dirigées par les propriétaires et la participation de la communauté plutôt que par le prestataire de service. Ce concept donne la priorité aux pratiques de construction et aux matériaux locaux dans la construction d'abris. L'hypothèse est que les communautés locales savent le mieux les matériaux adapte à leur environnement local, la conception d'abri la plus appropriée pour la culture et le contexte climatique, et l’entretien de leur abris. DEDI prendra en compte les questions de protection transversale (VBG-PE, PEAS, Genre).

project_name: Protection des droits fondamentaux des enfants et élèves PDI dans les Régions du Sahel, du Nord e du Centre-Est
project_objective:
Dans le but d'amener les communautés à devenir résilientes et à s'impliquer directement pour l'assistance au public cible des interventions humanitaires, l'action proposée vise les membres communautaires déjà actifs au niveau du RPE des quelques communes dans la Sahel, dans la région du Nord et la région du Centre Est et elle a pour objectif principal de les rendre proactifs en termes de sensibilisation et d'accompagnements des personnes déplacées internes affectées par la crise, particulièrement les femmes et les enfants. En plus, l’action vise à assurer des conditions acceptables d'éducation à travers entre autre l’aménagement des ETA et des EAE, et poursuite de formation a travers des formes d'éducation en situation d'urgence et la formation  et la sensibilisation par radio. Assurer et supporter l'enregistrement de la déclaration de naissance des enfants et surtout l'enregistrement des élèves PDI et la promotion du retour scolaire sera une des interventions prévues. En autre, mettant en place ou renforçant le RPE pour un référencement et une meilleure prise en charge des cas les plus vulnérables, nous voulons soutenir les victimes des VBG, les EAFGA, et des enfants porteurs d’handicap. Le volet protection de droits des enfants touchés/capturés par les actions/opérations de ratissage des forces armées, essaie de garantir la prise en charge des cas, leur réinsertion et acceptation sociale dans la communauté. Ceci prévoit un sous- volet de soutien aux enfants déjà détenus dans des maisons d’arrêt sous accusations de participation/collaboration avec les GANI.
Il s'agit d'abord pour ces réseaux d'être formés sur les principales problématiques objet des sensibilisations, sur leur rôle dans la réponse à la crise notamment par rapport au référencement et l'accompagnement des déplacés internes et sur les méthodes qui peuvent leur permettre d'atteindre les effets désirés. 
Ensuite ils mèneront des activités de sensibilisation (avec l'appui des animateurs des associations partenaires ACD NANGUE, UNIJED, et l'Association Zoodo pour la Promotion de la Femme de Ouahigouya, association Koolesmen) auprès des communautés hôtes sur l'accueil des populations déplacées et des nombreuses thématiques en lien avec la prévention et la réponse à la violation de droits des enfants, des discriminations et VBG, des risques des mines.
Aussi ces réseaux seront des acteurs dans la détection et le référencement des cas de violences sur les femmes et les enfants auprès des services et acteurs compétents pour une prise en charge efficace. Pour la facilitation dans le référencement ils seront en contact direct et permanent avec les animateurs d'associations et les agents terrain, moniteurs et animateurs de TDHI. Ce plan d’intervention est fruit de l’expertise accumulée et conçue en synergie et en coordination avec les autres actions de TDHI prévus dans l’accord de collaboration et un plan d’investissement 2019- 2024 avec le MENAPLN, et l’accord de collaboration avec le Ministère de la Justice et de la promotion des droits humains.
