project_name: Enhancing Access to Comprehensive GBV Prevention and Response Services for the most vulnerable Lebanese and Palestinian Refugees in Lebanon in Akkar, North, Bekaa and Baalbek
project_objective:
DRC and partners will implement comprehensive GBV prevention and response services in the Bekaa, Baalbek, North, and Akkar, targeting the most vulnerable and hard-to-reach Lebanese and Palestinian Refugees in Lebanon (PRL). The compounded socioeconomic crisis in Lebanon has significantly deepened the vulnerability of aforementioned target populations, and resulting limited coping capacities have heightened exposure to GBV, disproportionally affecting vulnerable and marginalized groups, including female-headed households, older women, persons living with disabilities, and increasingly children. Through programming in 2022, DRC has identified significant increase in the adaptation of negative coping mechanisms to meet basic needs, with women and girls particularly being increasingly exposed to exploitation, violence and abuse when trying to meet their needs. Feelings of safety have starkly deteriorated amongst targeted communities, with increasing reports of robberies and harassment in public spaces. Proposed activities under the ERP are designed based on coordination with the GBV sector, and aim to complement services provided under the LCRP to allow for better and increased inclusion of PRL and Lebanese. 
DRC will respond to increased needs for specialized GBV response interventions by providing comprehensive Case Management (CM) services following a survivor-centered approach to support informed decision making about how to address the GBV incident, risk, or violation, and understand which services are available and to facilitate access to these services in a holistic and dignified manner. Protection cash will be integrated into CM services where relevant and appropriate and to support the achievement of protection outcomes, and survivors will have access to individual psychosocial support as part of CM, including PFA, which will be complemented by ensuring access to Emotional Support Groups (ESG) to restore feelings of safety and dignity and to enhance available community support networks. For children, DRC will leverage its own and partners’ CP and GBV CM capacities to ensure a tailored response to child survivors following established GBV and CP guiding principles and approaches. Quality and outcomes of CM services will be monitored through satisfaction surveys, ensuring services can be continuously improved and any challenges addressed in a timely manner. DRC as part of GBV response services will also provide Focused Psychosocial Support services based on the “I Am Here” approach, developed to identify the most marginalized adolescent boys and girls through a door-to-door assessment methodology. Adolescents will participate in the design of participatory curricula whereby adolescents prioritize their own needs in terms of skills, knowledge and attitudes in pre-defined thematic areas related to GBV concerns. The FPSS curricula will also target caregivers and key male household members as decision-makers in adolescent’s life’s, requiring their engagement to empower adolescents and facilitate access to rights and services. 
DRC will implement GBV prevention activities at community-level, including GBV sensitization activities, aiming to contribute to the reduction of violence against women and girls by addressing gender-inequality as root cause of gender-based violence, and to encourage help-seeking behavior of survivors of GBV. Dignity kits will be distributed as part of sensitization activities and to address a critical need for women and girls. Particular attention will be paid to engaging men in prevention activities, amongst others through delivering the Engaging Men in Accountable Practices (EMAP) curriculum aimed at engaging men in the reduction of violence against women and girls. Impact of prevention activities will be measured using tools from the GBV PEF to ensure robust learning. DRC will also build capacities of partners on GBV response and prevention, including on administering satisfaction surveys.

project_name: Localized and more accountable, inclusive and coordinated emergency response for vulnerable migrant populations in Beirut and Mount Lebanon
project_objective:
The Action aims at securing migrants’ access to humanitarian aid and multisectoral assistance (sector overall objective). It will take a two-pronged approach to implementation, both of which will focus on the BML area. Indeed, BML is identified as a priority area for the migrant sector as set out in the 2023 Sector Response Plan due to the high density of migrant communities.

1. Grassroots humanitarian NGOs are often first responders, including to migrants’ urgent needs. However, they are too often left out of the institutional international funding streams and not given the opportunity to develop a more accountable, evidence-based and inclusive response through tailored capacity sharing. ACTED Lebanon has a long track record of CSO support and is a key member of the Localisation Task Force. 84% of our projects were designed & implemented with national CSOs in 2022. With an increasing focus on the emergency response, ACTED has been building the capacity of local frontliners to improve the quality, accountability and impact of emergency aid delivery in the current crisis, with support from LHF. Furthermore, ACTED’s standards for AAP are recognised at global level by the CHS Alliance, with ACTED’s system scoring overall higher than other organizations, and ACTED representatives having presented the mechanism during global learning events. ACTED also has a dedicated MEAL unit, separate from the project implementation team and reporting directly to the Country Director, which further informs project design & implementation according to global standards of quality, accountability, relevance and impact. Through the proposed project, ACTED will further share this capacity with grassroot CSOs.

This part of the Action will take an innovative approach to inclusive localization, benefiting 4 grassroot organizations. To this end, ACTED will partner a well-established national NGO (“the Mentor”) specialized on protection issues as they affect migrants in BML. The Mentor will be selected based on its sector of expertise and will take a “bigger brother approach” to technical coaching on protection for the 4 grassroots organisations. They will receive operational capacity strengthening, informed by ACTED’s Grassroots Organisational Capacity Assesment (GOCA). They will then be provided with subgrants to improve migrants’ access to and knowledge of protection services (as per the Sector Outcome 1), with ACTED guidance on operations and grant management. 

2. In line with Outcome 2 of the Sector Response Plan, vulnerable migrants will have improved access to multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance through the provision of MPCA for 600 migrant households (1,800 individuals) in BML, where ACTED has been implementing projects since 2007 and has high community acceptance.

This will build on ACTED’s experience implementing unconditional cash distribution projects globally, including currently to 325 vulnerable migrant households (975 individuals) in Bourj Hammoud.

To select the vulnerable migrant households, ACTED in collaboration with the 4 grassroots organisations and the Mentor will outreach widely in the targeted location. Eligibility will be assessed and prioritization based on pre-defined criteria developed with the expertise of the MEAL unit (gender of the head of HH, food consumption score, level of income, etc.), and coordinate with relevant partners for de-duplication. 2022 consultations showed there is no existing system for de-duplication of assistance, nor any harmonized guidelines for the targeting of migrants through cash assistance. ACTED will thus continue to coordinate de-duplication efforts directly with actors present in BML, the mentor and Grassroots Orgs and the Sector.

ACTED will provide the selected households with 100 USD per household for 10 months, through the money transfer agency it has a contract with. Recognizing that many migrants do not have proper IDs, so prepaid cards have been issued to the beneficiaries.

project_name: Provision of educational opportunities for Lebanese and Palestinian children affected by the crisis in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Baalbeck/Hermel Governorates.
project_objective:
The multiple crises impacting Lebanon and its institutions have left thousands of children without the basic right to education and are faced with major protection risks threatening their immediate/long-term wellbeing and opportunities. As an emergency response, the proposed project will promote equitable access to inclusive educational opportunities for socio-economically vulnerable Lebanese, Palestinian and Migrant children impacted by the multiple crisis in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Baalbeck/Hermel Governorates. In the light of the current situation, where public schools are being closed for a prolonged period of time (Jan ’23), retention support and catch up programmes become even more relevant and needed.

In Lebanon, children are witnessing one of the major violation to the basic right to education, also considering that children attending public school are usually the most vulnerable of the Lebanese society. This will have a major impact in the long term period with a generation that has lost several years of education, pushing children out of school and feeding the inevitable spiral of poverty

Moreover, recognizing the link between child protection and educational outcomes, the project will fully integrate CP in Education to support children and families severely affected by the crisis cope with the stressors of the situation through protective, safe, and inclusive environments. Building upon TDH IT’s long-lasting experience in preventing and responding to protection threats faced in various communities, this education project will make use of the technical expertise, guidelines and tools developed by TDH IT in collaboration with UNICEF and the CP WG. CP and Inclusion specialists will be part of the implementation of this project, providing training, guidance and tools to be used by Education staff to ensure that children with disabilities are not excluded from education/CP services provided, and are provided equal opportunities to benefit from the project. This approach focuses on enhancing the skills, knowledge and tools available for staff to better assist each child and family, while enhancing families and community awareness of children’s rights and how the crisis is affecting them. 
In response to the limited data available on the educational status and barriers faced by Lebanese children as a result of the crisis, needs assessment will be conducted considering both in-school and out-of school Lebanese children in specific locations where TDH IT has years of experience implementing Formal/NFE/CP programs, as well as strong connections with the communities. 

Community-based retention activities will be implemented, complemented by PSS support, awareness raising sessions and in-kind support (food and educational materials needed for learning). TDH IT’s CP-Education integrated approach will allow the identification of households’ educational gaps and the child protection risks families are exposed to. Engagement of key stakeholders and duty-bearers at community and governance levels will take place to increase their accountability in upholding children’s rights and foster inclusion during this emergency response.

The project will be implemented in line with Sphere Protection Standards and CHS, and National Sectors technical guidelines and SOPs.

project_name: Provision of Financial Hospitalization Coverage for Vulnerable Lebanese and Non-Refugee Migrants
project_objective:
Aligned with ERP Health SO1, SAMS will support in-patient hospital care for at least 720 vulnerable Lebanese citizens, and non-refugee migrants  whose ability to access life-saving treatment has been eroded  due to  the pandemic and Lebanon’s deteriorating socio-economic situation. The decision to include Lebanese and migrant populations stems from the increasing numbers of Lebanese and migrants who can not meet their basic needs and access secondary healthcare.
In 2022, the Health sector was further strained by the pressure of the ongoing financial and economic crisis that has been ranked by the World Bank as one of the most severe globally since the mid-1800’s. The multifaceted crisis started late in 2019 with country-wide protests in response to a deteriorating socio-economic situation. It got coupled in 2020 with the Corona Virus Disease (COVID-19) outbreak, and the devastating Beirut Port explosions. In October 2022, the first cholera outbreak in nearly three decades was declared in Lebanon following the detection of the first laboratory-confirmed case.
Moreover, according to findings shared in health sector coordination meetings held in April 2022, some hospitals have reduced operating capacity by as much as 50 percent due to fuel shortages that lead to electricity cuts.  The availability of hospital beds has also become more limited because of dwindling financial support from the MoPH. In addition, some advanced medical conditions are not approved for financial support by the ministry. For these reasons, SAMS will support life-saving hospital care for the most vulnerable patients on an as-need basis for beneficiaries where insurance scheme doesn't cover them. 
SAMS will provide patients full financial coverage to support hospital admission and treatment for urgent, life-saving care. SAMS will screen referred cases against vulnerability criteria to determine whether or not they qualify for full coverage. This criteria is based on prior coordination with MoPH, MoSA, IOM, ICRC, Caritas and other key stakeholders. Concerning payment modality, there will be no transfer of funds to patients. Rather, a network of around 30 contracted hospitals across the country that SAMS has previously vetted  will submit invoices to SAMS for review and payment of bills of up to $1,800 per Lebanese patient, $1,500 per migrant patient, and $1,300 per psychiatric patient. The cost per patient was determined in coordination with Health Sector leads, IOM, and based on SAMS’ prior experience.  
As an immediate result: 720 patients experiencing severe economic hardship will receive the medical care  they could not afford, while alleviating any protection concerns associated with hospital admissions (such as document confiscation and refusal to admit/detention in hospitals due to a lack of payment). While only an estimate, the anticipated disaggregation is as follows: 450 Lebanese and 270 migrants.
As a long term result: Hospitals will benefit from additional income and patient bills paid.
Having implemented hospital referral programming for refugees, Lebanese, and non-refugee migrants over the past four years, SAMS has built relationships with relevant ministries, UN agencies, and other vital stakeholders, alongside a network of contracted hospitals across the country. SAMS has also developed a robust outreach plan that has involved reaching out to community centers, leaders, and volunteers to increase access to local communities and supplement its work with regular privately funded medical missions.

project_name: Increasing access to child protection mechanisms and psychosocial support services for vulnerable children and families in Lebanese and Palestinian Communities.
project_objective:
The proposed intervention aims to strengthen the provision of Child Protection (CP) services and Child Protection support to the children and families affected by the crisis among the Lebanese and Palestinian communities. 
It will be built up on existing projects, benefiting from the long-lasting experience of TDH IT in preventing and responding to protection threats of the migrants and Lebanese children and from the experience of the organization working with Palestinian communities in Lebanon. 
Targeted beneficiaries will be supported with the provision of full cycle quality CP prevention (Awareness, Community based PSS, Caregivers Program) and response services (Focused PSS and Case Management) in vulnerable localities particularly affected by the crisis in Beirut, Mount Lebanon and Baalbeck-Hermel Governorates, as well as in Palestinian refugee camps across Lebanon. 
In line with sector request to prioritize the enrollment of extremely vulnerable children and those who are the hardest to reach, TDH IT has refined and reinforced its Needs assessment tool with additional criteria which have enabled the staff to identify and enroll children and caregivers facing multiple and complex protection vulnerabilities. The outreach process includes those in our waiting list, household/door-to-door visits, consultation with communities as well as internal/external referrals in coordination with other humanitarian actors based in the areas of intervention. 
Thanks to TDH IT integrated programming, children will be referred from CP to EDU, and vice versa, according to their specific needs. Inclusion of children with disabilities represents one of the main pillars of the intervention and it will be ensured from the assessment and outreaching phases to the provision of services. All TDH and partners' staff will be trained on inclusive methodologies to actively involve children with disabilities, and to spread a culture of inclusion during the implementation of the activities. Children with disabilities will be also screened through the use of the Washington Group Questionnaire, which is already integrated in TDH IT multi-sectoral needs assessment tool. 
The intervention will be implemented both through TDH IT direct implementation and through the involvement of local organizations, benefiting from their technical skills and added values in providing PSS through alternative modalities (e.g.: sports, arts, yoga). Such collaboration has been piloted by TDH IT through previous initiatives with successful achievements in terms of child protection mainstreaming, outreaching new typologies of beneficiaries and addressing related vulnerabilities. 
Among targeted Palestinian camps, the intervention will be fully implemented through local organizations, already collaborating with TDH IT in the provision of NFE services to increase Child Protection in Education integrated approaches and mainstreaming. 
Community engagement initiatives will be organized in all the locations mentioned to raise awareness on the main Child Protection threats (especially child labor, early marriage and violence against children) as well as on safe identification and referral (SIR) mechanisms in order to activate the related prevention and response intervention. 

The modality of implementation will be face-to-face, unless additional issues will require to adapt to the emergency situation in the country and will require the return to remotely or blended modality, through the use of ad hoc tools (interactive sessions, videos and games, arts to be implemented via remote) and the use of online platforms (WhatsApp, Zoom, conference calls). Specific cholera and COVID-19 awareness sessions will be delivered throughout the intervention in line with the MoPH/health sector recommendations.

project_name: Retention Support and Summer Learning with Extracurricular Activities for Lebanese, Migrants and PRL in North and Akkar Governerates
project_objective:
By the proposed Program Al-Fayhaa association (AFA) is willing to apply an Education retention and remedial support program targeting Lebanese, migrants, and PRL in Akkar, Tripoli, El Koura, El-Minnieh-Dinnieh, Zgharta.
At the beginning of the program, AFA will hold an outreach activity to target the most vulnerable children who will participate in the program, on top of that AFA through different community engagement initiatives and awareness sessions will make sure to fill in the vulnerability criteria checklist to be able to refer Out of School Children to Formal education, non-formal education, protection or any other needed services.
Aiming to retain in school children from dropping out, AFA will implement retention and remedial support program targeting 2400 child. 
In this program AFA aims to cover Akkar, Tripoli, El Koura, El-Minnieh-Dinnieh, Zgharta Areas, in school children from grade 1 to 6 who are at risk of dropping out or due to their poor academic performance and achievement results will get interactive learning support for 6 months in all major subjects of the Lebanese curriculum (Arabic, Foreign language, Math, Science, Social and emotional learning sessions).
The proposed educational program will also support 5% of the target children with disabilities, and 50% of total children with disabilities will receive 16 therapy sessions each. In addition, AFA will procure assistive devices such as hearing aids, wheel chairs, walkers to cases in need in an aim to facilitate their access and retention in education.
The program focuses on girls, boys and women, who reside in marginalized areas in North and Akkar governates.

project_name: Providing Case management, CB-PSS, FPSS to 1550 children and their Caregivers in North and Akkar
project_objective:
The current economic crisis in Lebanon has presented itself on the CP sector through the increase of working children in different facets.
This has been reflected by CP sector dashboard shared by UNICEF during February 2022, which states that CP sector partners reported, through (RTM) survey, Child Labor (52% of responses) was the most predominant risk throughout 2021, Violent Discipline (19%) and Street-Connected Children (18%). 
The UNHCR has shown in its report that there has been 23% increase in children receiving Case Management in 2021, in areas including Tripoli and Akkar. This states the need for a call of act towards protecting these children and preventing the increase of cases.
By the proposed Programme Al-Fayhaa association (AFA) is willing to apply for a Child Protection program targeting Lebanese, migrants, and Palestinian in North and Akkar.
At the beginning of the programme, AFA will hold an outreach activity to target the most vulnerable children who will participate in the program’s different Pathways, on top of that AFA through different community engagement initiatives and awareness sessions will make sure to fill in the vulnerability criteria checklist to be able to refer Out of School Children to Formal education, non-formal education, protection or any other needed services, .

The programme focuses on both girls, boys and women from Lebanese, migrants and Palestinian backgrounds that reside in marginalized areas in North. Moreover, vulnerable Lebanese, migrants and Palestinian children still experience physical violence, abuse and child labor that contributes with the need of case management, Focus Psychosocial Support and community based Psychosocial Support activities.

AFA will implement case management, for 150 cases of children involved in child labor and street connected children in Akkar, Tripoli, Minnieh-Dinnieh, and Zgharta. 

Moreover, AFA will conduct Community Based PsychoSocial Support to low and medium case children at risk of child Labor, early marriage, or any other type of risks, this target will be divided to two age groups, 200 Children aged (6-11) and 200 children aged (12-17), in addition to 400 Medium to high-risk Cases benefiting from Focussed PsychoSocial Support sessions, including Focus actions on meeting the immediate identified needs of the child and the services they are willing to accept and provide information on other services or supports that are available to meet their needs. 
To establish the purpose of the program and to provide a holistic approach to all the family, 600 caregivers will participate in positive parenting and focus psychosocial support sessions to provide children’s caregivers the best methodologies and parenting skills to deal with their children and protect them from any possible risks and harm. 
Moreover, AFA team will implement several community-initiatives related to Qudwa toolbox, which engages the community for the aim of finding solutions and raise awareness on the Violence Against Children, Child Protection, Violence Against Women, Child Labor.
AFA has gained a high reputation in the community where its centres have become safe spaces for many children and their families. AFA has the potential to plan, implement and follow-up CP activities since the organization has successfully completed a CP program in collaboration with DRC under the fund of UNICEF, with the following activities: Case management (child labor), Focussed and community based Psychosocial Support activities. As for Positive Parenting, it was directed to female caregivers to help them learn more about their children’s needs and feelings, as well as equip them with positive parenting tools. AFA has the potential to respond to CP matters with its trained staff on SOP. Other activities have reinforced positive attitudes and social norms among parents through using the Qudwa caregiver’s toolbox.

project_name: Outcome 2: Solarization for two water pumping stations and provision of critical hygiene support for affected communities in Nabatiyeh District (Habboush and Harouf)
project_objective:
Under the Outcome 2 of the national WaSH Sector, AVSI aims to provide access to minimal standards of water and critical hygiene items to vulnerable people in Nabatiyeh district. The project targets six vulnerable cadasters in Nabatiyeh district where 16,400 people live, including 13,285 host community members, 2,952 Syrians, and 164 PRL and PRS. The intervention will meet urgent and unmet WASH needs in the area where 23 schools operate and a total of 9,600 direct and 7,800 indirect beneficiaries will be targeted. The proposed intervention includes two main activities:

1- The installation of a 138.6 KWp and 130.9 KWp PV solar systems in two pumping stations (Habbouch Chreifeh well, Harouf Sekran well) in line with the SOP endorsed by the national WaSH sector and the specifications set by the LWE. The solarization of these two pumps is expected to ensure more consistent power supply and to increase the quantities of water available to households in the two municipalities of intervention, currently under-served. AVSI will carry out the installation of the PV systems through a national contractor being selected through a national tender and continuously monitored by a third party technical consultant. AVSI will also ensure community engagement by creating local committees in each municipality. The local committees will be engaged in the implementation process to exercise ownership over the PV systems after the handover.

2- The provision of Menstrual Higiene Kits containing locally produced reusable sanitary pads to adolescent girls and women in reproductive age in the targeted cadasters. The project also includes interactive awareness activities on the prevention of SGBV, PSEA, hygiene, menstrual health, and the best use of water, which will take place in women safe spaces in collaboration with Primary Health Care centers, schools, NFE, and social community centers. AVSI will also ensure linkages with other NFE centers and child protection actors to improve school readiness and support case management interventions.

project_name: Safe, Protected and Inclusive Environments for a Sustainable Educational Path for Vulnerable Children in the governorate of Mount Lebanon
project_objective: The proposed project seeks to promote human development for vulnerable children and families, with particular reference to education, protection and psycho-social support in the school, family and community spheres in Beirut and Mount Lebanon area. In particular, the project aims to increase the resilience of children affected by trauma enhancing access to services, supporting the intervention capacities of relevant local institutional and civil society actors, and thus fostering the integration of the refugee community with the host community.

project_name: Strengthened GBV response services to vulnerable Lebanese and migrants and reduction of protection risks through preventative community awareness activities
project_objective: The proposed project seeks to address the protection concerns of vulnerable Lebanese and migrants who are at-risk of or survivors of gender-based violence. The intervention adopts a comprehensive approach including both prevention and response activities undertaken by a staff of multi-functional protection practitioners. The target areas are Bekaa, Mount Lebanon and the South. The intervention is structured through a combined approach: individually-tailored specialized GBV response services, including case management, focused PSS, cash for protection and emergency cash assistance, which are provided to medium and high risk survivors and at-risk individuals through, in most cases, already established safe spaces at the Community Development Centres (CDCs);while prevention activities such as non-focused PSS, awareness-raising and information-provision services, are implemented through a community-based approach and are provided through mobile outreach and community mobilization. Outreach for these activities will be conducted by community-based volunteers, trained in inclusive targeting approaches and safe-identification and referrals.

project_name: Protection of Vulnerable Migrant Workers in Response to the Socio-economic Crisis in Lebanon
project_objective:
The overall objective of the proposed project is to address the emergency protection and basic assistance to the most vulnerable Migrant Workers in Lebanon. 

The deteriorating socio-economic situation added to their challenges, making the most basic of services and needs, including shelter and healthcare, unattainable for many. This project aims to reduce the risk of evictions, exploitation, abuse and human trafficking through the provision of NFIs, Voluntary Return, Cash for Rent, access to protection services (case management and socio-legal services), MHPSS and awareness raising on preventive measures by contributing to the Migrant Sector Outcomes under the ERP 2023:

Outcome 1: Vulnerable migrants have improved access and knowledge of protection services, legal assistance and MHPSS assistance. The proposed project’s Objective 1 “Provision of Protection Services” contributes to this goal through:
Act. 1.1: Delivering psycho-social support (PSS) and legal awareness sessions to at least 2080 migrants, including referral to individual therapy where relevant. This includes awareness raising material provided to landlords for prevention of abuse in rent increase.
Act. 1.2: Providing legal counselling and assistance to at least 300 migrants including legal aid, negotiation and access to justice, provided by Amel's specialised in-house legal team focusing on issues such as salary theft, detention, lack of legal residency, employer-employee disputes.
Act. 1.3: Protection services to least 1800 vulnerable migrants with urgent protection case management who face violence incl. GBV, abuse, exploitation, and human trafficking, among other challenges. 
Act. 1.4: Screening and registering all migrants requesting support (though Amel hotlines, and referrals from NGOs, migrant groups, embassies, etc.) (at least 4460) to ensure they meet the vulnerability criteria to be eligible for Amel services.

Outcome 2: Vulnerable migrants have improved access to multi-sectoral, dignified and lifesaving assistance. The proposed project’s Objective 2 “Temporary shelters” contributes to this goal through:
Act. 2.2: Provision of 3040 NFIs including Blankets, hygiene kits, dignity kits, luggage, and baby kits.
Act. 2.3: Providing 1860 at-risk migrants with Cash for Rent (CfR), especially migrants with children to reduce risks of eviction, homelessness, violence and abuse. CfR is a sub-form of MPCA that supports all migrants including undocumented migrants who face the highest vulnerabilities.
Act. 2.2: Provide training and awareness raising on cultural sensitivity and migrant inclusivity to build the capacities of 60 humanitarians and service providers

Outcome 3: Vulnerable migrants have access to Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) assistance to their country of origin. This goal will be contributed to through Objective 3 of the proposed project: “Voluntary Return” through:
Act. 3.1: Facilitating counselling and Voluntary Return (VR) for 300 Migrant workers, including those in detention, back to their home countries managing all necessary processes including waivers of penalties and documentation to travel, in addition to coordination with GS offices, embassies, employers

Outcome 4: Efficient and evidence-based humanitarian programming is enabled across sectors due to coordination, and improved data collection and analysis
Act. 4.1 Conducting a nation-wide assessment on migrants extracted from its database of already supported cases to be agreed upon with the migrant sector
Act. 4.2 Conducting a thematic assessment which findings will be utilized for dissemination to other partners and beneficial for increased support to MWs
Act. 4.3 Amel was voted by the migrant core sector members to co-lead the migrant sector as co-coordinator. Accordingly, Amel sustains its effort for the remaining 9 months of the year by including its technical and 12+ years’ experience in the support of MWs, due to the large amount of work required.

project_name: Ensure Access to Health for the Most Vulnerable and Irregular Migrants in Lebanon
project_objective:
The overall aim of the proposed project is to ensure Access of Health to the most Vulnerable Migrants in Lebanon especially the individuals with Irregular Status (non-ID/ undocumented). 

This project is proposed for a duration of 12 months starting from 1st January 2023 until end of December 2023.

Amel efforts in primary health care date back to its establishment in 1979, with the recent national efforts played a major role in the national response to the pandemic, cholera outbreak including vaccination, surveillance, response, policy involvement among others.

Amel has been working in the support of Migrants since 2011 with established connections and outreach to almost all migrant communities of 28+ nationalities and 80+ migrant leaders through its specialized team. Outreach is conducted by Amel team specialized in the support of migrants’ cultural sensitivity, including migrants all over Lebanon, and related to embassies, GOs and other stakeholders. Migrants reach out to Amel through 30 field centers all over Lebanon, through migrants’ hotlines, community leaders, diplomatic representations and referral by other organizations. Amel is also specialized in identifying victims of trafficking and ensuring their livelihood.

Locations of the project includes AMEL PHCCs all over Lebanon that are part of the MoPH accredited network, and in the process of application or that Amel is managing within national consortiums located in Beirut, Beirut Suburbs, Bekaa and the South. The largest requests for access to health are located in BML and specifically in Amel centers in Ashrafieh, Bourj Hammoud and Burj El Barajneh. 

This includes primary health care support in Amel PHCCs with referral to advanced lab and Diagnosis, when needed, for effective follow up to health counselling. The support is conducted through a comprehensive approach of humanitarian assistance that starts with registration/screening and support to basic assistance of the case through the migrant sector directives and channels of support. Since 2011, Amel succeeded to support thousands of migrants through social support, Voluntary return to their home countries, Cash for Rent Assistance, legal support, empowerment, capacity building, awareness raising, advocacy, access to health, support of basic assistance, food security, NFIs, support of migrants in detention among other activities.

The project aims at ensuring access of health to the vulnerable migrants in Lebanon especially with irregular status through:

Outcome 1 – Ensure Access of Primary Health Care support to Migrants in Lebanon including provision of essential and chronic diseases Medications, and Advanced Diagnosis 

Obj. 1.1: 1200 patients/visits supported with chronic disease medicines in Amel provided in designated Amel PHCCs upon prescription by the doctor consultation 
Obj. 1.2: 2500 Migrants receive health consultation and medication upon prescription in Amel PHCCs through GP and specialized doctors. This includes cases referred through different referral pathways from other Response or Community agencies (NGOs, CSO, INGOs..), GOs, and diplomatic representations of Migrants, among others.
Obj. 1.3: 50 patients supported with advanced secondary care diagnostic (outside ER/Hospital)

Outcome 2 - Enhanced protection environment in humanitarian health response

Obj. 2.1: 100 frontline health workers trained on culturally sensitive approaches to improve health access for migrants
Obj. 2.2: 1300 women and girls receiving dignity kits, including personal hygiene items

Population includes migrants that are female, male, children and older persons. 

The target population includes migrants of African and South-East Asian nationalities, including Sudan, Iraq, Egypt and Afghanistan.

project_name: Provision of a comprehensive and integrated lifesaving intervention and a rapid response to cholera alerts
project_objective: Throughout this project, PUI will support vulnerable Lebanese, PRL, migrants through health-tailored activities designed to strengthen the resilience of households with vulnerable pregnant/lactating women. This project was designed based on PUI’s technical expertise and long-term presence and acceptance in the area of intervention. Furthermore, PUI will also respond to cholera alerts through prevention and response by supporting 2 cholera treatment units (CTU)/cholera treatment centers (CTC)/PHCCs in Cholera hot spot areas in addition to 8 contracted hospitals. Furthermore, PUI will raise awareness at community level while distributing as well oral rehydration salts (ORS). The 2 CTU/CTC/PHCCs will be equipped with medical and nonmedical items to stabilize cases and refer them to the hospital or discharge them home. This project will also support HR, fuel additional costs, waste management, and light rehabilitation works to make the centers’ flow adjustable to this alert. Monitoring activities will be carried out throughout the life of the project in order to guarantee the compliance of the activities with agreed objectives and targets. A detailed monitoring and evaluation plan will be developed at the beginning of the project by PUI’s MEAL unit together with the technical staff. Data collection and storage tools will grant the highest level of data protection and confidentiality, allowing a systematic disaggregation per sex, age, and disability and providing automatic reporting features. Programme monitoring will combine different methodologies, based on qualitative and quantitative approaches, including surveys and regular field visits. Patient Satisfaction and Post Intervention Surveys will be conducted at least twice during the project implementation period in order to gather feedback from pregnant women on their perceptions about the quality and the outcomes of the services received, their feelings about topics such safety and accessibility as well as the patient centered approach supported by PUI. In specific circumstances preventing direct access to the project areas, such as COVID-19 related movements restrictions decided by the GOL or civil unrest, measures will be taken to shift these activities to remote modalities (phone calls, reduced sample sizes, online FGDs, etc.).

project_name: Securing Quality and Inclusive Education for Most Vulnerable Out-of-School and Out-of-Learning children in North Lebanon, Akkar, and Mount Lebanon through a Recovery Program
project_objective:
The education sector is paralyzed and hurtling from crisis to crisis. This position is underpinned by a lack in human, financial, and managerial resources. In 2023, the sector continues towards ultimate collapse, leaving 520,000 children at risk of losing out on quality learning. RMF’s proposed project adopts a rights-based approach to rescue education for all, through securing safe and protective access of children (Lebanese, no-Lebanese, in the first and second shift schools, dropped out / never schooled) to learning opportunities using multiple modalities for maximizing the benefit to children, and ensuring the highest reach at the lowest possible cost. Within the ERP framework, an integrated programming is followed, stressing on the right of schooling seeking: 
-Further involvement of existing entities in referring children to public formal education or Multiple Flexible Pathways. 
-Increased access to an integrated package of quality services that contributes to learning retention of 1,140 OOS and OOL.
-Enhanced capacity of 750 caregivers, 216 teachers in formal education, 12 school principals and 180 educators in non-formal education for supporting children’s education.
-Larger engagement of 200 children with disabilities in educational programs. 
-Use of the SEL and PSS frameworks/ observation tools, and digital tools and resources

To achieve this, RMF will be working throughout both ERP’s outcomes through the following model:

Outcome 1: Activities will be adapted in-line with the mitigating the crises’ impacts, ensuring that children are receiving equitable, safe, and inclusive access to quality learning opportunities considering the Social emotional framework aspects. RMF’s socio-ecological approach focuses on engaging the community, schools, and families, to mitigate the learning losses efficiently and effectively. This will be achieved through:
-Organizing Back-to-Continuous Learning campaigns in the targeted three governorates for advocating and communicating efforts through creating a map identifying all active stakeholders and NGOs to get out-of-school (OOS) and out-of-learning (OOL) children, back to education/learning. RMF, will rely on existing QUDWAs in targeted communities to act as active advocators.  
-Providing an integrated package of services for 1,440 children registered in grades 3, 4, 8, 9, 11 and 12 in both morning and second shift schools, who are struggling to learn including. This includes cash for education, healthy snack pack, and retention support classes. 
-Providing 900 OOLs aged 8-14 with foundational literacy and numeracy classes.  
-Involving 200 children with disability in formal and non-formal education, through the provision of assistive technologies and devices that enable their access to education and working on differentiating approaches and adding tools and adaptive materials. 
-Supporting 12 schools in Akkar, North Lebanon and Mount Lebanon in covering their operational cost for guaranteeing continuous education. 
-Offering low-cost support solutions for 1,440 children to link them with the education support platform established by UNICEF in partnership with Teach for Lebanon, to receive the needed support while studying. 

Outcome 2: Its outputs are cross-cutting with Outcome 1 and they complement each other, especially that RMF will be closely collaborating with CERD for offering 216 school teachers, 12 school principals and 180 educators in non-formal education with several capacity building trainings, focusing mainly on approaches to teaching and learning in crisis time, as well as social and emotional learning. Finally, 1,440 targeted schooled children will be benefiting from extra-curricular activities and SEL/ PSS through establishing and equipping 12 school clubs; whereas 900 OOL children will be participating in community based psycho-social support activities SEL as a means for increasing resilience. Furthermore, RMF will be organizing 12 school-led SEL initiatives.

project_name: World Vision International in Lebanon's Provision of Education Needs in Relation to the Emergency Response Plan
project_objective:
Based on the multidimensional poverty index, it is alarming to note that 1.45 million school-aged children in Lebanon are in dire need of support to access education, with 662,000 of them being Lebanese (52% girls), more than 715,000 being Syrians (51% girls), around 13,300 being migrants (73% girls), and about 56,000 being Palestine refugees (52% girls). This calls for urgent intervention to ensure that these vulnerable children and youth are not left behind.

In response to this dire situation, WVL is committed to targeting the most vulnerable children, youth, Lebanese, Palestinians, and migrants, along with their caregivers under the Emergency Response Programme (ERP). The intervention will be focused on ensuring equitable and inclusive access to, participation in, and completion of safe and protective education for all learners in Lebanon. Specifically, WVL will be working towards two major outcomes, the first of which will ensure access to education for the most vulnerable children and their caregivers. To achieve this, WVL will kick-start a holistic intervention starting with a Back to School Campaign where children will be referred to learning, supported with cash for education to eliminate the economic barrier to education, and provided with retention classes to ensure they acquire the necessary foundational skills that will allow them to stay in education. Moreover, children registered in retention programs will receive snacks, hygiene materials, and health prevention measures and supplies. Caregivers will also be targeted to engage in the education of their children, while learning centers will be supported to continue their operational activities. WVL will also ensure access to learning materials based on our experience in remote learning provision for different age groups. The second outcome aims to improve teaching and learning by focusing on learning outcomes for children and youth through enhanced quality of formal and non-formal education services that are safe, protective, adapted, and inclusive for multi-crisis situations. This will be achieved by training teachers on formal and non-formal education, providing psychosocial support to children, and monitoring the number of children progressing to the next school year.Despite the challenges and difficulties that families and their children are facing, WVL is committed to ensuring that education is not de-prioritized in the face of the curtailing crises in the country. We will leverage our presence in the areas and our long-standing partnerships in the communities, utilizing previously implemented outreach strategies that have proven effective in reaching the most vulnerable children and youth among the targeted population, such as through local partners, door-to-door, media including social media, and phone calls.

project_name: Solarization for WE and WASH assistance
project_objective:
The water systems will be supported through in-kind operation and maintenance assistance to the Water Establishments and municipalities managing the systems. The alternative of providing direct support through water trucking would be costlier, presents higher risks in terms of public health and the environment, and might create inequalities between households and localities and create or exacerbate social tensions, particularly as water trucking or desludging is a very visible support modality. 

Despite the higher initial cost of investment activities supporting WaSH systems are economically justifiable in the mid-term run and are crucial for mitigating public health risks and for enhancing equity and poverty reduction. Given the ongoing energy crisis that heavily impacts water production and distribution, and focusing on reducing the water dependency on fossil fuels, through systems solarization, powering by other renewable energy, and transformation to gravity-fed systems where feasible. 
The systems will be provided with solar systems, and minor repair and rehabilitation will be conducted for the water distribution networks to mitigate the risk of water and environment contamination, targeting cholera high-risk and cholera hot-spot areas to mitigate the risk of water and environment contamination. 
In addition, the containment of the cholera outbreak will continue to be done through CATI response, hygiene kits distribution, and cholera awareness sessions, municipalities will be provided with chlorine, training and monitoring tools in an attempt to chlorinate water supplied by private water trucking vendors. 
the most socio-economically vulnerable households will be targeted in coordination with the Food Security. Given the alarming results of MSNA and VaSyr assessments highlighting that a significant portion of people from all population groups face issues with accessing adequate hygiene materials, ensuring access to critical hygiene items and water treatment consumables for the most vulnerable. 
Women and girls of reproductive age will be provided with menstrual hygiene kits, and awareness sessions including topics related to GBV. People living with disabilities, families with young children and the elderly will be also targeted with hygiene kits and awareness sessions.
The targeting will be executed based on needs estimated by the sector using various data sources available in 2022: MSNA, VaSYR, WaSH Sector Assessment Platform, Water Market Monitoring, and Water and Sanitation Vulnerability Mapping focusing on the feasibility of solarization. Estimated WaSH sector People in Need, estimated area severity, as well as cholera WaSH risk map and cholera hotspots, will be used for prioritization. Interventions will be coordinated with relevant authorities such as Water Establishments, municipalities and concerned ministries.

project_name: Ensure access to life-saving hospitalization and life-sustaining medications to the most vulnerable populations living in Lebanon
project_objective:
Lebanon's complex crisis (protracted Syrian refugee crisis, political instability, severe financial and fiscal crisis, Covid 19 pandemic, and Beirut port explosions) heavily impacted the health sector. 

First, Lebanon’s unprecedented devaluation of the currency forced the Lebanese government to remove subsidies on most medications leaving people unable to access or afford vital and life-saving medication. Moreover, the global shortage and the central bank restrictions lead to further disturbance in the availability of free and low-cost medication at primary healthcare centers which are also facing an increase in demand. Thus WHO hopes to support with ensuring acute and chronic medication to support the most vulnerable. 

Second, catastrophic medication remains subsidized minimally by the government, however with severe shortages of life-saving medicine /cancer medications and very few available. In this domain WHO hopes to support further the MOPH to be able to serve a larger number of patients.

Third, with protracted delays in government payments of its dues to hospitals and the severe shortage of medications and supplies in the Lebanese market, access to health care is threatened including lifesaving care. Hence, the role of WHO is to provide hospitalization in cases of an outbreak and life-saving for the most vulnerable populations living in Lebanon. 

This project comes as a response to the humanitarian need with the aim to promote universal health coverage, equity, and access to health for all vulnerable in Lebanon (Lebanese, Migrants, and Palestinian), in line with the WHO commitment of saving lives and reducing suffering during times of crisis across the response pillars (coordination, communication, case management and continuation of essential health services).

project_name: Mejora del acceso a los servicios integrados de salud, protección y WASH en las comunidades indígenas vulnerables del Estado Amazonas
project_objective:
El proyecto proporcionará servicios integrados de salud de emergencia, protección y ASH para las comunidades indígenas del Municipio Atures (Estado Amazonas), con un enfoque especial en las vulnerabilidades de las mujeres, los niños y las personas con discapacidad. INTERSOS construirá su respuesta basándose sobre las análisis de los datos recogidos (INTERSOS ERN de Amazonas – Noviembre 2022), a través de un equipo multidisciplinario, activo y desplegado en el terreno y con el pleno apoyo y experiencia de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
El paquete de servicios sanitarios está diseñado para apoyar al sistema nacional de sanidad a nivel de atención primaria, y a las autoridades locales en la prestación de servicios sanitarios de emergencia para responder a las necesidades prioritarias relacionadas con la salud, con un enfoque particular en la SSR y el apoyo con equipos médicos específicos para las instalaciones de salud identificadas.
Además, INTERSOS integrará los servicios de protección a través de una gestión completa de los casos, que incluye PFA, PSS, asistencia jurídica, servicios de protección de la infancia y respuesta a los casos de violencia de género (VBG).
También se organizarán sesiones de concientización e información para aumentar los conocimientos sobre temas de protección (violencia de género, trata, tráfico de personas, riesgos de protección y abusos, incluso para los niños, niñas y adolescentes) y difundir información sobre los servicios disponibles. INTERSOS utilizará los servicios de un antropólogo para estudiar la mejor estrategia de sensibilización con respecto a las comunidades indígenas beneficiarias del proyecto.
Por último, un componente de agua, saneamiento e higiene complementará el proyecto mediante la
rehabilitación de las instalaciones de agua y saneamiento (depósito de agua, aseos, lavabos, etc.) en los centros de salud a los que se presta apoyo. Además, las comunidades a las que se dirige el proyecto recibirán apoyo con la distribución de filtros de agua y kits de higiene (con enfoque a mujeres y niñas en edad de reproducción), así como formación sobre el uso, el mantenimiento y las mejores prácticas de higiene personal y doméstica.
El proyecto se implementará en conjunto con la Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV), que llevará a cabo
todas las componentes comunitarias del proyecto.
Finalmente, como parte del proyecto, INTERSOS organizará un plan de capacitación sobre temas de protección por la CRV.
El proyecto se llevar a cabo en el municipio de Atures (eje sur y sur-este) en el estado de Amazonas, con la oficina principal establecida en Puerto Ayacucho.
INTERSOS implementará la respuesta en coordinación con las autoridades sanitarias y sociales, y con los socios locales y los grupos de interés (indígenas y autóctono) para la complementareidad en las áreas de intervención, para lograr la implementación de intervenciones de alto impacto en los lugares seleccionados. Como parte de una estrategia de salida, INTERSOS garantizará la coordinación continua y el desarrollo de capacidades también con los servicios nacionales existentes y los socios.

project_name: FHV - Refuerzo a la reinserción de jóvenes en educación media técnica a través del apoyo al personal docente,la rehabilitación de infraestructuras, las actividades socio-productivas y la formación en escuelas técnicas del estado Apure.
project_objective:
""El proyecto se centra en la reinserción de alumnos vulnerables en o en riesgo de deserción escolar en el contexto actual de acceso limitado a oportunidades económicas, impacto del Covid-19 y cambios en la composición familiar en los municipios Páez, Pedro Camejo y Rómulo Gallegos del Estado Apure. 

El proyecto consta de una intervención integral en centros de educación media técnica, que los actualice para ponerlos en plena capacidad de dar clase. Esto se conseguirá a través de:
     * Rehabilitación de infraestructuras básicas para proveer de agua limpia, baños, sistemas de gestión de residuos, sistemas eléctricos fotovoltaicos, impermeabilización de techos, pintura, etc. en 7 centros
     * Refuerzo a los procesos productivos propios de 4 escuelas técnicas, a través de un proyecto presentado por la propia escuela, para la compra de insumos, reparación de maquinaria o talleres, etc.
     * Prevención de embarazos no deseados en edad temprana, poniendo a los centros educativos en el centro de una estrategia diseñada para retrasar los embarazos y mantener a las alumnas el mayor tiempo posible en el sistema educativo. Asimismo, los centros educativos recuperan su papel como lugares de referencia en la prevención de la violencia basada en género y la explotación y acoso sexual.

Se trata de una estrategia de una efectividad ya probada en el mismo Estado Apure en 2021 y 2022, en escuelas elementales. En este caso, se propone la intervención en 8 centros, todos los cuales son públicos y entran en alguna de las siguientes categorías: Escuela Técnica Industrial (ETI), Liceo Bolivariano (LB), Escuela Técnica Agropecuaria (ETA), Centros de Capacitación Laboral (CECAL) o el Instituto Nacional de Capacitación y Educación Socialista (INCES). 

Se pretende llegar a 1.302 jóvenes y adolescentes de entre 12 y 24 años, 155 maestros y 61 personas que trabajan en los centros en mantenimiento y comedores con un proyecto de 12 meses de duración.

La intervención es realista, con un impacto tangible inmediato, y perfectamente alcanzable en el tiempo asignado de un año.""

project_name: FHV - Respuesta multisectorial integrada a las necesidades de la población en los municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Sucre del estado Sucre.
project_objective:
""La A.C. Grupo Social CESAP organización privada de interés público, comprometida con la acción popular, que durante 48 años ha promovido la construcción de una sociedad incluyente, justa y con equidad, impulsando la participación de los sectores populares como actores y autores de la transformación social y con experiencia en el desarrollo de proyectos sociales desde la gente y con la gente a partir de sus necesidades, se plantea con apoyo regional del Centro de Desarrollo Integral Sucre,  desarrollar el proyecto “Respuesta multisectorial integrada a las necesidades de la población en los municipios Cruz Salmerón Acosta y Sucre del estado Sucre”. 

Con este proyecto, se busca que, en cinco comunidades del municipio Cruz Salmerón Acosta (Punta Araya, Punta Colorada, Chacopata, Caimancito y Guayacán) y tres comunidades del municipio Sucre (Santa Ana, Caigüire (La esperanza), Santísimo Sacramento), seriamente impactadas en sus medios de vida, por las restricciones económicas y productivas que afectan al país, se puedan ofrecer opciones válidas y efectivas para minimizar las carencias nutricionales, alimentarias y fortalecer con asistencia técnica y capacitación el impulso de actividades productivas, además, ofrecer información que incentive la adopción de hábitos y conductas que mejoren las condición de vida y el bienestar de niños, niñas y adolescentes, madres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia, adultos mayores y personas con discapacidad.

Por ello, la propuesta de este proyecto responde a las estrategias planteadas por el plan de respuesta humanitaria, en los sectores Nutrición, Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida, Agua, Saneamiento e higiene con un componente de protección en atención al contexto de las comunidades que serán atendidas, a fin de mitigar diversas situaciones de violencia, abuso, negligencia y explotación de la niñez.""
