project_name: Promoting protection, Resilience and livelihood of conflict affected women and girls in Northeast Nigeria (PPRC Project)
project_objective:
Since 2009, the Boko Haram insurgency has crippled northeastern Nigeria, thousands of people have lost their lives either through gun shots, abduction, bomb blast etc. women and girls are the population that have been particularly most affected AOGs also continue to attack LGAs which led to increase food insecurity and hardship.  
According to the 2022 Humanitarian response Plan (HRP) 8.4 Million people are estimated to be in urgent need of humanitarian assistance with only 5.5m targeted. 22 percent of this population are women, 62% are children while 7 % are persons with disability. Looking at this data women and children are the worst hit by this crisis. 
Between June 1 and August 31 2022, IOM’s DTM programme carried out assessments to ascertain the level of damage sustained in IDP and host community sites due to heavy windstorms, rainfall and flood. Overall, 72 host community locations, 11 camps and nine collective settlements were assessed. The worst-hit of the assessed sites was Banki, a host community location in Buduwa/Bula Chirabe ward of Bama LGA, where heavy rainfall alongside the opening of the dam gates in Cameroon led to the flooding of the community aﬀecting an estimated 7,389 individuals. In total, 4,989 shelters/houses were damaged by the flood, leaving a total of 8,181 households (4,645 in Borno State, 962 in Adamawa State and 2,574 in Yobe State) in immediate need of shelter. Three hundred and thirty-four casualties were reported as a result of rainstorms and floods during the period. A total of 37,475 individuals (16,393 in Borno State, 5,979 in Adamawa State and 15,042 in Yobe State) have been aﬀected by heavy rainfalls that have led to flooding since the inception of the rainy season. Of the total individuals, Borno State accounts for 44%, Yobe State 40% and Adamawa State 16%.  This has led to increase vulnerability of women and girls to various forms of Gender based violence against women and girls and if urgent intervention is not rendered it might lead to loss of lives. 
Violations and sexual abuse against women and children are widespread both in and out of camp settings. According to the 2022 HRP, an estimated 1.3 million people are identified to be in need of GBV prevention and response services across the BAY states. 46% IDPs, 23% returnees and 31% host communities many of whom are heads of households living in crowded, culturally inappropriate conditions. Women and girls are often targeted while performing basic tasks such as travelling to water points, collecting firewood to cook food, accessing farmlands to supplement food rations during the farming season and going to communal latrines. GBV threatens the health of women and girls through injuries, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, unwanted pregnancies, and obstetric fistula caused by sexual violence. Women and girls who experience GBV are also prone to mental health issues resulting from stigmatization, discrimination, isolation, exclusion and other social impacts. 
A substantial and coordinated effort is required to address this needs. FRAD currently operates integrated health, nutrition, protection, gender based violence (GBV), WASH and accountability to affected population and Localization programs in three hard to reach areas in Bono, Adamawa, and Yobe states. In addition, FRAD has integrated GBV, education and early recovery and livelihood activities in Konduga, Mobbar and Monguno. this support will ensure these life-saving programs can scale up and be sustained to meet urgent needs for this crisis-affected population in Northeast Nigeria.

project_name: Integrated Rapid WASH and Nutrition response to conflict affected persons in Vulnerable communities and areas of Return in Borno and Yobe
project_objective:
Since 2009, the Boko haram insurgency forced millions of people to become food insecure with millions of people estimated to need humanitarian assistance in North east Nigeria, according to the 2022 humanitarian Need overview (HNO), 8.4 million people are projected to be in need in the BAY states 58% of which are children, women and girls.
The challenges facing these populations are enormous, millions of which are fighting food insecurity with little or no source of livelihood. The conflict makes the general humanitarian situation complex and it becomes more complex in Borno states with the recent closure of IDP camps by the state government that bringing about movement of population from one place to another.
The recent IOM DTM No 262 shows that 1329 new arrivals with 218 screened for MUAC with 9 identified to be at high risk with Many partners reporting increased cases of malnutrition in children. The 2022 HNO shows that 3.0 million need Nutrition services 50% of which are children. Children and women who are acutely malnourished, have weaker immune systems and are therefore vulnerable to frequent infections that may overburden the health system with an estimation of 320,000 children expected to suffer from SAM and will need highly specialized nutrition services which will require increasing coverage of the OTP program centres in all accessible LGAs and wards to strengthen identification and referral of severely malnourished children.
The ongoing return of people back to their former communities has created the need for continued WASH assistance and already existing WASH facilities are stressed in these selected proposed LGA’s, the continued influx of people back to these LGA’s increases the risk of outbreak with history of frequent outbreak of cholera during raining season, there is need to support these LGAs with safe Water, sanitations infrastructure, hygiene education, WASH NFI and cholera prevention kits to respond effectively to ensure safety and dignity of these population.
With the current challenges at hand, there is need to build a stronger and more efficient Rapid response mechanism that strengthen the spotting of outbreak, identification of SAM cases using mass MUAC screening to ensure a quality response is administered to high risk cases within 72 hours. FRAD propose to implement this project to deliver an integrated robust Rapid response to meet WASH and Nutrition needs of this population through and integrated approach to provide lifesaving activities to address WASH and Nutrition needs of these hard to reach LGA’s.

project_name: Emergency WASH in IDPs camps, host communities, and in institution to reduce communicable disease in Bama, Dikwa, Maiduguri, Monguno, Magumeri and Ngala LGAs Borno State Northeast Nigeria.
project_objective:
This project focuses on addressing the emergency WASH needs of 72,575 IDPs and
returnees in Borno State and to ensure their dignity, welfare and save their lives. The project will be implemented in Bama, Magumeri, Monguno, Dikwa, and Ngala LGAs where INTERSOS is already established and is implementing WASH activities. INTERSOS has continued to provide WASH needs to the people Magumeri, Bama, Dikwa, and Ngala LGAs, through integrated WASH/Health/Nutrition/Protection/Livelihood projects. The needs for WASH in the mentioned LGAs, are still high as there is a perpetual influx of new arrivals and returnees into these locations, from other adjacent locations. Currently, in addition to INTERSOS, there are 5 agencies carrying out WASH activities in these target locations i.e., DRC, FHI 360, IOM, Mercy Corps and UNICEF.  

This proposed project for Magumeri, Monguno, Bama, Dikwa, and Ngala LGAs will lead to reduction of the incidence of water related diseases within locations and general well-being and behaviors change of the targeted 72,575 individual and indirectly to many more people within the target location. The following is a summary of the targets and outputs of the proposal

• Construction/rehabilitation of 50 emergency shower facilities in the IDP camp and focusing on new arrivals and transit center
• Desludging of 320 emergency latrines in the IDP camps in the target locations focusing on new arrivals
• Provision of 350 units of cleaning kits and hand washing stations
• Training for 100 CHV and 30 Chlorinators and 50 community leaders as well as 75 WASH committees’ members to ensure the knowledge is impacted to the key people in the LGAs and contribute to sustainable management of developed WASH facilities.
.Introduction of local content in WASH.(Biofilter).
These proposed activities contribute directly to the sector objectives as described in the WASH sector’s 2022 HRP plan and directly contributes to the global mission of providing humanitarian assistance to over 2.8 million individuals that needs WASH assistance in the North East Nigeria crisis

project_name: Provision of critical lifesaving Protection Prevention, Response and Mitigation services to survivors of GBV, other vulnerable IDPS and members of Host communities and strengthening local engagements and coping capacities in Borno and Adamawa States, NorthEast Nigeria
project_objective:
INTERSOS is a non-profit humanitarian organization that is committed to working at the front-line to bring humanitarian assistance to people in danger, victims of natural disasters and armed conflicts. INTERSOS has been implementing integrated multi-sector lifesaving and protection interventions in the proposed project sites since July 2017.
INTERSOS will continue to strengthen its communication with communities to support the drive for Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), with a strong focus on making service delivery equitable and transparent, through regular community meetings with community representatives and service providers on service provision, site management and site planning in close coordination with local authorities. In addition, INTERSOS will ensure that space is given for AAP mechanisms such as information desks and the operation of a complaints and feedback mechanism.
The protection project is designed to alleviate suffering, save lives and maintain human dignity with the aim to build the resilience of the community and promote local ownership so the benefits of the project are relevant beyond the emergency phase into development phase.  Thus, engaging the community in planning, implementing and monitoring is a fundamental strategy to ensure that the project is guided by the identified needs and capacities. Gender-based violence is considered a public health issue and a human rights violation, which means that mitigation and response to GBV are among immediate life-saving priorities in emergencies and need to be integrated in all sectors of humanitarian response. Since the experience of GBV can be a distressing event, MHPSS will be a component intertwined to GBV response, prevention and risk mitigation and a part of care and support in this project. 
The project will focus on provision of protection  assistance to beneficiaries through capacity building, awareness and sensitization, sexual and gender-based violence related services, psychosocial support and material assistance. The protection interventions aim at providing the targeted population with quality services to respond to current protection needs but also contributing to strengthen their capacity for self-protection reinforcing positive coping mechanisms to stressful events.

project_name: Intensifying WASH Response in the BAY States to save lives and improve living condition of people affected by conflict
project_objective:
Through this project, GOALPrime will improve the life of 100,000 conflict-affected individuals (30% female, 20% male, 30% girls & 20% boys) through intensification of the WASH response to sustained safe and quality water, clean latrines, and sanitation facilities across 14 LGAs in BAY States. 50,000 individuals (60% women/girls & 40% men/boys), including 30,000 household heads will benefit from hygiene promotion via both door-to-door and 100,000 individuals will benefit from the mass motorized speaker campaign for hygiene promotion sensitization approach. 20,000 vulnerable women in camps and adolescent girls in schools and camps will be sensitized on menstrual hygiene management, promotion, and education after which they will receive reusable sanitary pads (RSP) and laundry soap for daily maintenance of the RSP. Key messages will include prevention and control of COVID-19, Cholera, Measles, Lassa fevers and messages on PSEA, gender, and disabled inclusion. GOALPrime will also distribute 20,000 hygiene kits and PPEs from the WASH common pipeline to 30,000 household heads. 5% of the total target will be people living with disabilities.

Handwashing has been established as a component to achieve proper hand hygiene and a range of health and development Objectives. Through this project, GOALPrime will established 200 handwashing facilities which will be positioned across all the latrines provide and in some other strategic locations across the camps and host community, and would be managed maintain by the WASHCOM team. Constant water supply to the handwashing stations with a mild chlorine content at 0.5% chlorine to ensure decontamination of jams and other hands transmitted diseases .

Also, through this project, GOALPrime will rehabilitate 100 boreholes to provide safe and clean water to 150,000 individuals and continue to maintain rehabilitated boreholes via the services of community local artisans which would be trained by the GOALPrime boreholes engineering team who will continue overseeing the O&M activities of the community based local artisan and WASHCOM. This approach is to ensure that there is no disruption of water supply across the target LGAs.

This project will support the Water Point Chlorination (WPC) and free Residual Chlorine (FRC) in line with best practices and standards as recommended by the Water Technical Group (WTG) through an engaged community water point chlorinator. An online chlorination method will be majorly used by using an automated Dosatron on the rehabilitated boreholes, 100 dosatrons would be installed and calibrated according to the sector standard.

Through this project, GOALPrime Water Testing Lab will continue the water quality testing and monitoring of the chemical parameter and bacteriological contamination of water samples from the target LGAs and will also support partners from other LGAs referred by the WASH sector to assure continuous quality and safety of the water accessed by beneficiaries across LGAs of implementation.

project_name: Delivering Life-saving WASH Assistance for the Most Vulnerable in IDP Camps and Host Communities in BAY States, NE Nigeria
project_objective:
Deteriorating public health conditions threatened by annual outbreak of infectious diseases like Cholera, reduced humanitarian footprints due to insecurities and dwindling funding, Increase Protection risks, Government mandated camp closures leading to the influx of IDPs/returnees into camps and host communities along the transit routes, floods, rainstorms, and other adverse weather conditions have further complicated the humanitarian response in the BAY States (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe State), requiring a holistic approach that will appropriately address gaps and advance coordination. 
LPF through this project will reach a total of 98,740 (30% female, 20% male, 30% girls & 20% boys) conflict-affected individuals in Askira Uba, Dikwa, Damboa, Gwoza, Nganzai, Gombi, Mubi North and South  and Fune LGAs of BAY state. 
This project aims to promote personal and public well-being of conflict and flood affected populations through improved access to basic water, sanitation, and Hygiene services that will avert or reduce the incidences of acute watery diarrhea /cholera and other infectious diseases. It also seeks to strengthen livelihood & economic activities in targeted locations.
The project acknowledges that vulnerabilities vary hence particular emphasis will be placed on the most vulnerable groups such as children, adolescents, women, men elderly, and groups with special needs” in targeting beneficiaries. The project is committed to reaching people with disabilities and has put in place deliberate measures to achieve this objective. 
Through this WASH response, LPF will consciously mainstream Protection and support Nutrition, to leverage on knowledge, expertise, reach, and resources, benefiting from combined and varied strengths and shared goal of improving living conditions and building resilience of affected populations in the BAY States.
The response will adopt WASH Sector harmonised facilities designs & approaches in improving and sustaining access to WASH services in the target locations prioritising improved access to safe water through rehabilitation of twelve strategic broken-down water facilities, operation and maintenance of twenty eight water facilities, Construction and rehabilitation of emergency and household sanitation facilities, support health institution and schools with latrine cleaning materials, establish solid waste management systems. Conduct Door-to-door, focus group discussions, mass campaigns, and the use of Information, Education and Communication materials for hygiene promotion activities while increasing access to hygiene items that include menstrual hygiene management items to adolescent girls, Pregnant and lactating women, and survivors of GBV.

project_name: Strengthening of government health facilities on management of  Acute Malnutrition (AM) through the provision of preventive and curative live-saving nutrition services  in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa State.
project_objective:
Plan International Nigeria will implement a 12-month nutrition response focusing on the provision of life-saving emergency nutrition services through the strengthening of the existing government health services in BAY State. The project will strengthen the capacity of the government healthcare providers on the management of Acute malnutrition in the community, OTP,  Stabilization Centers (SCs), TSFP/BSFP and MIYCN to promote the sustainability of these critical services in the government existing health facilities and Communities. The project will treat children with complicated SAM and/or failed appetite tests in established SCs , uncomplicated SAM at OTP, and MAM at TSFP. The project will also provide brain stimulation services such as psychosocial support to the children and caretakers of children with  SAM admitted to the SCs/OTP and behavioral change communication on Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN). 
Furthermore, the project will integrate gender-responsive messaging and child safeguarding in its community engagement processes, share information, encourage discussions and address gender and safeguarding issues that impact on Maternal nutrition, optimal Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and others.  The project will also strengthen  the management of acute malnutrition through supportive supervision and monitoring and   through the provision of logistical and technical support in collaboration with the Ministry of health and nutrition sector. The project will focus on supporting the most vulnerable population groups, specifically children under five years of age, caretakers of SAM children,  PLW, caretakers of SAM children who are living with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. Plan International will integrate management of Acute Malnutrition into existing health services in each general hospital and in the LGA health system using State Primary Health Care and Development Agency (SPHCDA) and hospital staff and activating the LGA  nutrition coordination meeting in all targeted LGAs.
At project inception , Plan International Nigeria will prioritize identifying Acute malnutrition to facilitate access to life-saving services for children under five years of age and to enable management of these SAM cases in collaboration with SPHCDA and Hospital Board Management (HBM) staff. PLAN will strengthen the capacity of the government health service providers as well as parents, guardians and caretakers to prevent malnutrition, respond timely the treatment of SAM and MAM cases and we will work closely with government and nutrition/other partners working in each LGA. The project will strengthen accountability to beneficiaries through the establishment and strengthening of an inclusive and appropriate community and facility -based complaints and feedback mechanism that will allow women, girls, men, and boys to safely report concerns of the emergency nutrition response in their respective Hospital. The project also will ensure gender sensitive monitoring and evaluation is undertaken by dis aggregating all data by sex, age, disability and creating complimentary qualitative and quantitative indicators.

Provision of life-saving response for the most vulnerable population and reduce morbidity and mortality through improved access to curative and preventive nutrition services in Borno and Adamawa State, Nigeria
project_objective:
LABDI is a national and a women led organization that operates across the BAY state and implement activities in areas of nutrition, WASH, Protection …. In this project, LABDI will engage in provision of quality   nutrition preventive and curative activities in Yobe and Borno state. Children and PLWs will be the key targets of the project and the beneficiaries will be admitted in to the nutrition programs and receive treatment according to the national guidelines while preventive nutrition services will be provided to caregivers and beneficiaries to prevent and reduce the incidence of malnutrition. LABDI is implementing nutrition project by strengthening the screening, identification and referral of acute malnutrition among children under five, pregnant and lactating women (PLW); ensuring that malnourished children receive timely treatment & quality nutrition services; and ensuring provision of support for appropriate, safe feeding for children 0-23 months (specific focus on <6m) in Yobe and Borno state. In this project, LABDI will also ensure pregnant and lactating women, children under 5, adolescents and other members of the targeted communities receive quality nutrition services by, providing supplies, supporting the daily provision of curative nutrition services in health facilities and community, and other various interventions to reduce morbidity and mortality. The project will also treat children and PLWs with MAM through the use of ToM Brown.
The project will provide capacity building to government healthcare providers and in prevention and treatment of severe acute malnutrition through promotion of appropriate infant and young children feeding (IYCF), community mobilization, identification and referral of SAM cases and treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) among children less than 5 years in Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and also ensuring those with Medical complications are referred to Stabilization center.

project_name: Improve maternal and child health services of vulnerable Lebanese and Migrants in Bekaa and the South.
project_objective:
This project aims to improve availability, access, quality and demand of maternal and child health services at primary health care level of vulnerable Lebanese and Migrants, especially in Baalbek-Hermel, Bekaa, South and Nabatiyeh. The planned response of Action Against Hunger (AAH) under the Health Sector Response is to improve primary health care services for women and children and complement the nutrition-specific interventions under the Nutrition Sector Response within this health response. 
AAH will build on its multiple years of experience with community mobilization in WASH and nutrition and expand to improve knowledge on routine immunization, health seeking behavior for sexual and reproductive health, maternal and child health, and mental health. In addition to this, AAH plans to incorporate targeted awareness during public health outbreaks, to limit the spread of the outbreak and timely tackle misinformation. Through this community mobilization women and adolescent girls attending awareness sessions will receive a dignity kit to improve access to menstrual hygiene and so minimize menstrual poverty. To complement this community outreach AAH will also hire community midwives to complement the ANC received through primary health care facilities with a community outreach for women with high-risk pregnancies. This could be women that are malnourished or have COVID-19 or other risks. 
To support primary health care facilities to be able to provide lifesaving and life-sustaining health services, AAH will provide costs for primary health care facilities to be able to extend their opening hours for essential primary health care, such as maternal and child health care, to ensure more people are able to access the services. 
To ensure health care staff are equipped to respond to outbreaks; health facilities are able to mainstream protection; and provision of ANC and PNC in line with the new package, health care workers will be provided with specific training to improve quality of services and so able to responds to the needs of vulnerable communities. To respond to outbreaks health facilities will also be provided with basic medical supplies, such as PPE. 
Overall, this project will aim to ensure primary health care, including a community outreach component, is able to respond to the current needs among vulnerable Lebanese, migrants and Palestinian refugees, but will indirectly also support vulnerable Syrians, since AAH will also ensure that the supported primary health care facilities are accessible to all, irrespective of their nationality.  
This project will target 3 primary health care facilities that will reach approximately 15,000 patients during extended hours and 8,000 through community outreach activities.

project_name: Improving the nutrition security of Lebanese and migrant caregivers and young children through provision nutrition services that are both preventive and manage undernutrition
project_objective:
This project aims to address the increasing nutrition insecurity conditions in the country, in particular those affecting the most vulnerable Lebanese and migrant communities. The response of Action Against Hunger (AAH under the Nutrition Sector Response is divided into interventions that cover both prevention and management of malnutrition. In order to ensure that services aiming to prevent and manage malnutrition complement each other, the response entails improving promotion, protect and support for appropriate infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices to pregnant women and caregivers of children 0-2 years of age and improve timely detection of malnutrition and appropriate management of malnutrition, especially wasting, the most dangerous form of malnutrition. AAH will complement this support to the most vulnerable households, based on in-depth assessments, with multi-purpose cash assistance under its Food Security Response, especially households with women who are pregnant and breastfeeding and children under the age of 5 years. AAH will also dedicate efforts to ensure that multi-sectoral needs expressed by targeted communities are actively referred and followed up, especially that impact on nutrition outcomes are amplified when WASH, food security, protection, GBV, health, including mental health, are simultaneously addressed. Interventions under this program will target communities in Beirut, Bekaa, and South governorates, though it is important to note that not all interventions included here below will be implemented in all 3 governorates concomitantly, but depending on the needs, context, as well as AAH's capacity.

Overall, 2885 caregivers and 3875 children aged 0-59m will be targeted, inclusive of LHF activities. As AAH is mainly targeting migrants only in Beirut a maximum of 5% of the targets will be dedicated to support migrant communities.

To address malnutrition AAH implements interventions that it has experience with and are evidence-based, by prioritizing pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) and caregivers of young children with IYCF, health and hygiene promotion and counseling, both one-on-one and in groups, in health facilities and household level, including community mobilization. Another aspect of address malnutrition is timely detection of cases. For this reason, community mobilizers will be trained and supervised to conduct community level screening of wasting of children aged 6-59 months through MUAC (mid-upper arm circumference) screening. Caregivers with children aged 6-59 months will also be trained on the Family MUAC approach, so that they themselves can conduct screening on their own children on a regular basis. Included in this approach caregivers will also be supported to seek timely treatment in the nearest treatment center. Children aged 6-59 months will also receive micronutrient supplements to mitigate the risks associated with inadequate dietary intake. In parallel, AAH staff and stakeholders, including health facilities, will be supported to create and maintain enabling environments that protect, promote and support breastfeeding and optimal feeding practices. This includes training on the evidence based IYCF principles as recommended by WHO, MoPH, nutrition sector, IYCF committee etc. and oriented on the implementation of Law 47/2008 that adopts all the provisions of the International Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes. Health facilities will also be supported to create safe, private spaces to support breastfeeding. 
All interventions prioritized by AAH are in line with the ERP's Nutrition Sector's response.

Additionally, AAH plans to conduct a nutrition survey at governorate level, in line with the SMART methodology to be able to update the specific nutrition needs in AAH areas of interventions, especially in Baalbek-Hermel, where this project is targeted.

project_objective:
WV directly and with IPs will offer a multifaced project in continuation of existing and expanding in NWS to support the most vulnerable in response to needs, including CwD in HC and camps between the ages of 6-17, by providing equitable access to quality and protective learning prospects to girls and boys in both FE and in NFE through ALP, Remedial, Catch-up, BLN classes and SLP. Additionally, nutrition, CVA, protection and WaSH will be integrated. 7 areas with the highest severity rates (4&5) as per HNO 2023 will be targeted: Maaret Tamsrin, Dana, Bennsh, Armanaz, Salqin, Harim, Atareb, covering 50 (13 new locations) as this is where populations & needs are highest.
In IDP camps, NFE provided to 1445 females and 1446 males including 40 CwDs. In 25 formal schools, we’ll support 3000 female and 2550 male students including 100 CwDs. 981 teachers, 29,441 14441 male & 15000 female students will benefit from SPHERE aligning and CWD-considerate rehab, construction and heating for schools in 120 schools that were identified through a comprehensive WV needs assessment. 
We’ll continue to work with and recruit local communities to ensure apt education services are due at a level that meets the cluster and authorities’ standards, which include local outreach, a quality education in formal and non-formal settings with lifelong learning chances with a special focus on CwD. 13100 of parents (F 8100 M 5000) targeted in awareness sessions on the importance of education, nutrition, health, hygiene and CP. In compliance with INEE minimum standards and safe-programming principles, achieving improved learning outcomes through conducting BTL campaigns to encourage children to return and be retained in education while parents prioritise education. The sessions will be complemented by distributing learning supplies. We’ll also provide training to teachers and facilitators on F2F and distant ed, programmatic support throughout the project cycle. OOSC will be bridged back to formal education based on the term’s scores. Holistically, structured and semi-structured PSS sessions using WV’s models and expertise will be offered by training education staff (TiCC- PSS- SEL- EiE- CSG) in the established/rehabilitated CFSs at formal and non-formal settings in all of the targeted locations, to enhance the resilience, coping mechanism and life skills of children, in addition to mine risk awareness sessions, hygiene promotion education, case identification and referrals for most vulnerable cases in need of services through the protection team and external pathways.
Ensuring the continuity of learning, adapting plan B for distance learning due to COVID or escalation in the security situation, where we’ll be contingent on sufficient pre-existing equipment (independent contribution) from previous education projects (tablets, cameras, laptops, internet equipment, teaching tools-valued at $80,000). The project will provide heating materials (gas heaters in tents, fuel and heaters for block building schools). All projects will provide drinking and washing water, support to operational costs, cleaning materials, sanitisers and solar power systems as an electricity source in the rehabilitation works. Security equipment for education settings (first aid kits and fire extinguishers) given after training staff on first aid and emergency preparedness. 
PTAs and SMC established to consult, inform of updates along with teachers' support circles as experience sharing and care. Project will offer incentives to teachers, facilitators, guards, cleaners and admin staff as an important factor in securing stable education process and retention of teachers while securing jobs and income for about 348 families. WV and IPs will facilitate experience exchange workshops with Aleppo and Idlib Education Directorate education personnel (30 Aleppo/70 Idlib) to improve the level of coordination and help build cooperation and partnership with the local councils and camp management.

project_name: Provision of safe access to water, sanitation, and Hygiene promotion (WASH) needs to the flood-affected IDPs, returnees and vulnerable communities in Yirol East and West, Awerial, Twic East and Duk counties of Lakes and Jonglei state.
project_objective: Since December 2020, the WASH gaps identified in Awerial especially in Mingkaman and the surrounding villages of Padaar, Dounygok, Ahuo, Marik, and Kaltok by the WASH partners are numerous as a result of the influx of IDPs from Jonglei that affected the already strained services delivery in WASH, with no funding by the WASH partners to cover the old caseload of IDPs of 68,000 individuals, and the currently verified new influx of IDPs from Jonglei is 52,015 individuals by the WFP.  In September 2022 (IRNA report, 11.10.2022 Awerial County in  Lakes State), the flood overpour from Gel river to the nearest low land settlements in Awerial county forcefully displaced 4,841 HHs with 24,205 individuals in 7 payams which include Dor, Bunagok, Abuyung, Magok, Nile, Alel and Puluk  and 17 Bomas of Awerial County. This increased the needs of humanitarian assistance and require urgent consideration of the affected population for humanitarian’s intervention. The flooding affected schools, food security and livelihood, health & nutrition, shelters and road access.Most of the boreholes in Awerial Center have been submerged by floodwaters and some have collapsed- meaning that water in the boreholes have been contaminated. The displaced populations in Dor and Watnhom drink water from seasonal water ponds, 100% of the displaced persons are practicing open defecations and they have no knowledge of hygiene and sanitation practices. As the result, majority of children are suffering from diarrheal and other waterborne diseases. There are numerous WASH gaps identified during the IRNA assessments report ranges from the shortage of water for drinking and domestic use that requires drilling of new wells in the up/dryland settlement areas far from the water sources, rehabilitation of the non-functional motorized systems, rehabilitation of broken-down wells, and shock chlorination of wells submerged by the floodwater, construction of shared household latrines, de-commissioning of latrines, distribution of latrine construction materials to family/households willing to construct their pits, hygiene awareness sessions and WASH NFI’s distributions. According to the IRNA report (04-06 December 2021), the main triggers and drivers of the situation in the Duk Islands settlements were in two folds: the inter-communal violence due cattle raids and abductions that occurred in July 2020, and this forced the people to relocate from the Duk mainland to the islands for safety and security. The displacement was followed by devastating floods in 2020, 2021 and 2022. According to the estimate, the number of people affected both IDPs and the host are 27,006 individuals confined in deferent islands within Dongchak Payam of Duk County during the visit, the team found that the most affected people are female and children including youths in the islands. The immediate priority needs identified by the assessment team include, WASH for hygiene promotion, noting open defecation in the river is being practiced, the affected community relies on river water for their daily uses without treating or boiling and the available water points are submersed in water. The IRNA report (21.10.2021 Twic East County) indicate that devastating flood from 2020, TwIc East as one of the Jonglei state became one of the most affected regions with thousands of people displaced to different locations. Some people flee to Mingka,man (Awerial County), Mangala (Rajab County) and Bor County Headquarter. IRNA report of 21.10.2021, an estimated 58,069 individuals (20,324 host community, 31,938 IDPs and 5,807 returnees are affected, and the figure by now has increased with the more devastating floods of 2022. Out 249 boreholes in Twic East, over 200 of them have submerged, Approx.65% of HH assessed use surface water for drinking and other household uses, Limited or no latrines on islands and IDPs camps, Poor personal hygiene due to lack of basic hygiene items such as soaps and MHM kits for women and girls.

Once the schools re-open ensuring continued access to education services and retention of both the displaced and non-displaced vulnerable girls and boys, children with disabilities affected by the conflict, poor households, girls, hard to reach areas children  SCI through this project will intervene in Blue Nile (Al Kurmuk- Ar Rusayris –Baw – Geissan) localities, South Kordofan in (Dilling- Kadugli –Rashad –Abujibiha) localities, Sinnar in (East Sinnar –Alsokey-Abuhajar-Aldaly WalMazmom-AlDinar) ,Red Sea in Port Sudan localities ,Aljaziera state in (Wadmadani-Hashish-Om-AlGora-Almanagil-South aljaziera-AlKamleen-Sharg Aljaziera- Rofaa) s targeting a total of 407,372 compromise of 400,000 vulnerable and newly displaced children  (196,000 boys ,204,000 girls) 5% out of them are children with disabilities ,778 teachers (2741 male , 2853 female) and 5594 OOSC(2741 boy ,2853 girl).This action will be executed into two phases, phase one from June to September 2023 through  provision of  services to the most vulnerable children and supports water and sanitation infrastructure in schools with an integrated package of education and protection assistance and integrated interventions in Wash in school and provision of clean water and distribution of hygiene kits and provision of psychosocial support activities which includes access to life-saving information and survival skills, including awareness of hazards, better nutrition, protection from SEA and other forms of GBV, and child protection and well-being awareness. To support the traumatized children and enhance their psychological wellbeing. Phase 2 of this action will be from September until end of December, a mobilization campaigns will be conducted to register and enroll the newly displaced and vulnerable children into the established temporary learning spaces and schools near their gathering points and to facilitate children’s safe return to school in the longer-term, there is an intervention of construction of new   gender sensitive latrines following the universal design in order to accommodate all children including CWDs and construction temporary handwashing facilities, in addition , children will be provided with feeding programs in close coordination with SCI feeding interventions in the targeted localities. .These interventions are combined with specific Education in Emergencies support including providing temporary learning spaces for displaced children, distributing teaching and learning materials, training teachers and facilitators and enhance their professional development and trained on Psychosocial, safe schools, GBV, children’s rights and violence free learning, including child protection. During phase 2, this action will support the innovative alternative learning modalities through ALP classes, which will be established in the newly constructed learning spaces. Mapping of referral pathways will be conducted to identify existing ones to support the most vulnerable children .

project_name: Improving Access to Quality Basic Education among Adolescent Girls and Women from the Rohingya and Host Communities
project_objective:
DCA will implement a basic education programme for 2,000 adolescent girls and young women (aged 15-24)  from the Rohingya and host communities, who are illiterate or pre-literate and therefore would not otherwise be able to benefit from the Myanmar Curriculum Pilot (MCP). DCA will provide literacy and numeracy sessions in English and Bangla or Burmese, using DCA's Non-Formal Curriculum Frameworks for Rohingya and Host Community Youth and Adolescents, as well as the Self-Learning Kit Phases 1-3, a community-based, autonomous learning program that can be implemented as a standalone or a supplement to the Curriculum Framework. Lessons will be delivered in person in Women and Girls Safe Spaces, as well as through community-based approaches like the SLK. DCA will develop Level 2 of its Curriculum Framework for Rohingya Youth and Adolescents, which will build on Level 1 (endorsed by the CXB Education Sector in 2021) and support learners to develop the foundational literacy and numeracy skills they need to engage in further livelihoods and skills development initiatives. Through the provision of education programming aligned with protection and its work in shared spaces with DCA's GBV team, DCA will ensure female learners are able to access a full array of services (education, protection, GBV).

Further, the project will work to mitigate a significant gap in teacher training opportunities for female educators from the refugee and host communities. Throughout the last two years, DCA has developed, implemented and refined a remote Female Teacher Professional Development (FTPD) package for female Rohingya teachers and developed a 23-module training course adapted from its Remote TiCC Training Pack. The modules were adapted and contextualized to meet female Rohingya teachers' latent literacy and numeracy skills and were provided over the course of several months to include repetition, practicums, and scaffolded content. DCA will further refine this training course that can be implemented both in-presence and remotely using a combination of print-based materials, audio/visual tutorials, and interactive audio instruction via MP4 players. This blended approach will also allow DCA to expand its reach among teachers, accounting for the movement restrictions women face in and between the Rohingya camps. As part of the continuous TPD modules, DCA will focus on developing Myanmar language literacy and numeracy tools to support teachers and learners in the acquisition of Myanmar language skills. DCA has developed a strong working relationship with Burmese language experts at Translators Without Borders who have supported the development of DCA’s audio files, workbooks, and Self-Learning Kit.  DCA will support the development of a training on language pedagogy and ways to support teaching Myanmar language, which will provide an opportunity to help teachers upgrade their skills and accelerate learning. DRR will be integrated into the FTPD modules as well as considered an outstanding agenda item during the Alternative Learning Committee meetings.

The project will continue to support community engagement and awareness raising on the importance of ensuring girls can return to learning opportunities through its robust network of Alternative Learning Committees, and equip adolescent girls and young women with the skills and knowledge to support themselves, their families and communities.  The project will continue to provide training on PSS, DRR, PSEA, and inclusive education and will expand its ECD programming as a lack of childcare means that female learners must often bring their children to the learning spaces. Ultimately, the project will support teachers, caregivers, adolescents and youth, contributing durable solutions that aim to generate resilience across the entire community.

project_name: Shelter and NFI Assistance in Whole Syria
project_objective:
This project is designed to improve Syrian families living in poor livelihood conditions, focusing on those living in their damaged apartments facing harsh weather circumstances without any protection and privacy.
The rate of people in need in this sector increased an 8% from 2022- to 2023 and reached 5.5 million people who need shelter assistance. The areas in need are spread all over the country but mostly concentrated in Aleppo, and rural Damascus governorates, where approximately 2.5 million of PiN are living in conditions ranked between severity levels 3-4 (Shelter HNO 2023). In Rural Damascus areas such as Moaadamieh, Modira, Misraba, Zabadin and Arbin, there is a high need to rehabilitate damaged houses. The high apartment rental prices forced people to return to their original damaged apartments or to stay in them illegally. 
In Deir Ezzor governorate, more than 135,000 people are in shelter need (Shelter HNO 2023). In addition, ADRA identifies a high need for the rehabilitation of damaged houses in the neighbourhoods of Al Omal (west and east) and Al Arfi, where there is an increased number of returning families because the directorates, other government bodies and INGOs are working to provide essential services (electricity, water, sanitation…). Most of the buildings are structurally safe.
In Aleppo, as per ADRA’s assessments, the needs in Southern Rural Aleppo areas (such as Al Hajeb and Khanaser) are amongst the highest, and also in Aleppo ( Al Shaara Karm Al Jabal and Al Sakhour) due to the increased number of returnees and lack of presence of humanitarian partners.
ADRA scoop of work will be under the following activities:
Activity 1.1.1.2: Provision of seasonal and supplementary NFIs. (550,000 USD)
Activity 2.1.1.2: Supply and installation of HH-level solar energy systems. (130,000 USD)
Activity 2.1.1.1: Rehabilitation of damaged or unfinished housing. (660,000 USD)

In 2023 ADRA is planning to respond to 12350 individuals including (male, female, boys and girls) from the most vulnerable families (IDPs, Returnees and host communities) through several shelter activities such as the rehabilitation of damaged houses, Shelter kits distribution and Winterization vouchers distribution and supply and installation of HH level solar energy systems in the governorates of Deir Ezzor, Rural Damascus, Aleppo, and Homs. project_name: Junto a ellas: Fortaleciendo mecanismos integrales de respuesta a la VBG para mujeres y niñas
project_objective:
La continua epidemia de COVID19, las tormentas ETA y IOTA en 2020, la tormenta tropical Julia en 2022 fueron situaciones de crisis que demuestran como las situaciones de crisis han impactado significativamente los proyectos de vida de las mujeres y niñas de Honduras, especialmente aquellas que viven en condiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad y  confrontan diversas discriminaciones y violencias interseccionales. Las constantes crisis y emergencias en Honduras han contribuido a profundizar las desigualdades estructurales preexistentes al generar presiones adicionales con pocas ofertas de solución a las vulnerabilidades en los sistemas sociales, políticos y económicos. En todos los ámbitos, desde la salud hasta la economía, desde la seguridad hasta la protección social, los impactos negativos se han exacerbado para las mujeres y niñas simplemente en virtud de su género (ARG Honduras 2022). Análisis recientes en Honduras evidencian los retrocesos significativos en los indicadores o condiciones estructurales relacionadas con la feminización de la pobreza, y los que inciden directamente en los factores de riesgo y aquellos protectores conexos a la VBG, los cuales particularmente se ha agudizado. Esto se debe por un lado, a que las mujeres se vieron obligadas a permanecer en sus hogares con sus agresores en un momento donde las tensiones económicas se incrementaban y en donde el acceso a los canales de denuncia y servicios se han debilitado (Care & ONU mujeres, 2020). Por el otro, los repertorios de violencia de grupos criminales en las zonas más vulnerables contra las mujeres (amenazas, extorsiones, femicidios, violencia sexual) no han disminuido sino por el contrario continúa siendo limitado el acceso a las mujeres a denunciar y ser atendidas. Partimos de reconocer el valor de las mujeres de diferentes edades, etnias, clases sociales que confrontan estas violencias. También y con un rol protagónico, la respuesta se construye con la participación de organizaciones de mujeres, feministas y de sociedad civil situadas en los territorios, quienes pese a un escenario adverso han impulsado importantes logros para la defensa de los derechos de las mujeres. A su vez, las instituciones nacionales y locales responsables de brindar protección y dar respuesta a los derechos de las mujeres son actores clave para el impulso de las estrategias que busquen mejorar las condiciones de las mujeres y su igualdad en términos de derechos.  El proyecto desarrolla acciones de atención inmediata a las mujeres a la vez que impulsa sostenibilidad fortaleciendo e instalando nuevas capacidades en instancias proveedoras de servicios. Las mujeres sobrevivientes de VBG recibirán servicios psicosociales integrales y acompañamiento, fortaleciendo su capacidad para identificar y exigir respuestas efectivas y que respondan a los estándares de calidad del paquete de servicios esenciales. Además, se realizarán acciones para fortalecer los mismos desde OMM y organizaciones locales y sus procesos de comunicación, coordinación intersectorial y atención, gestión de casos, rutas de referencia.
Pondrá en marcha mecanismos de apoyo a sobrevivientes para re activación de sus medios de vida, desde una perspectiva de atención para la transformación mejorando sus capacidades vocacionales y mapeando los servicios que contribuyan a crear y restablecer sus medios de vida para superar situaciones previas de vulnerabilidad. 
Como parte importante de esa transformación para reducir vulnerabilidades previas, se fomentarán escuelas y espacios de reflexión feminista, se impulsarán formaciones para actores comunitarios y una campaña masiva de comunicación y sensibilización orientada a promover cambios concretos en cuanto a la situación de VBG.
Finalmente, también se trabajará con actores/as que contribuyen de manera indirecta o directa en la ocurrencia y persistencia de la VBG: empresas; miembros de las fuerzas de seguridad; iglesias, establecimientos educativos, y la sociedad en general.

project_name: Humanitarian Response in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique (Phase III)
project_objective:
Partners access up-to-date, regular and systematic information to respond to humanitarian, peace and development response

The Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) provides support to the Government of Mozambique and humanitarian partners by establishing a comprehensive system that collects, analyses, and disseminates data on IDPs and returnees to ensure timely and practical assistance to the affected populations. In each round of DTM assessments, IOM works in coordination with a network of district focal points, Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) technicians and community structures to collate data in the field, including displacement baseline data at locality-level. DTM additionally conducts detailed assessments in displacement sites at regular intervals to ensure accurate and up-to-date information- collecting age, sex and vulnerability disaggregated data. 
 
IOM has been implementing its DTM baseline assessments in the districts most affected by insecurity since February 2019 but modified its methodology in July 2021 to adapt the tools to the evolving nature of displacement in northern Mozambique. DTM covers all accessible districts in Cabo Delgado impacted by displacement due to insecurity, as well as the provinces of Inhambane, Nampula, Niassa, Sofala and Zambezia. IOM's DTM team has grown with well-trained and experienced DTM enumerators, a strong information management structure supporting robust data processing and analysis. DTM's field presence is based on dynamic and responsive mechanisms, capable of scaling up activities in a short space of time.

Under the proposed intervention, DTM will continue with mobility tracking assessments to gather and analyse data in order to disseminate critical multi-layered information on displaced and mobile populations' mobility, vulnerabilities, and multi-sectoral needs. As such, IOM enables decision-makers and responders to provide displacement affected populations with better and context-specific assistance. Through technical and operational advantages in the region, DTM will most especially support primary data collection for holistic, inter-sectoral analysis of crisis-affected population needs, vulnerabilities, causes and risks while strengthening the collection of data based on age, gender and disability disaggregation for the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) and Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) 2022.

project_name: Protegiendo a la Niñez y Adolescencia en Honduras
project_objective:
Honduras, se encuentra en una crisis humanitaria compleja, cuyas causas fundamentales se relacionan con la pobreza sistémica, la profunda desigualdad socioeconómica y de género, en un contexto marcado por la violencia generalizada, el desplazamiento forzado, la violencia basada en género, la vulneración de derechos sobre las mujeres, las personas LGTBIQ+, las niñas, los niños y adolescentes (NNA), así como por los impactos generados por los movimientos mixtos de refugiados y migrantes y la limitada capacidad estatal para responder a los desafíos de protección que enfrenta la población. 
De acuerdo con la actualización del Análisis de Protección del Clúster y sus Áreas de Responsabilidad, Honduras enfrenta una violencia generalizada que sigue generando múltiples impactos humanitarios y riesgos de protección.
Se estima que en el país hay más de 1.4M de personas con necesidades de protección, el 40 por ciento son niñas, niños y adolescentes (NNA), el 61 por ciento son mujeres y al menos 70.000 personas LGTBIQ+ enfrentan riesgos diferenciados y desproporcionados. 
Desde el programa de protección de NNA, IRC se encuentra en las zonas de Atlántida, Cortes y Francisco Morazán con fondos financiados por BHA   e interviene en la gestión de casos con herramientas de apoyo psicosocial y responde a los impactos humanitarios generados por las diferentes vulneraciones de derechos en esta población. Además de la gestión de casos, el IRC propone trabajar con la red de Comités Locales de Derechos de Niñez y Adolescencia para fortalecer capacidades a través de la transferencia de metodologías ampliamente probadas, mejoras a los espacios seguros, y capacitaciones para la identificación y atención de NNA en riesgo y para el cuidado de niños sobrevivientes de abuso sexual. También se concienciará a los NNA, madres, padres, y cuidadores sobe la protección de niñez a través de sesiones psicoeducativos. 

El enfoque del IRC hacia la protección de la niñez se basa en tres creencias fundamentales:
•	Las niñas, los niños y adolescentes tienen derecho a crecer en un entorno libre de violencia, que defienda sus derechos y apoye el logro de su máximo potencial;
•	Las niñas, niños y adolescentes tienen derecho a participar activamente en su propia protección y desarrollo;
•	Las familias, las comunidades y los gobiernos juegan un papel fundamental en el cuidado, apoyo y protección de la niñez.
 

El IRC propone a través de la teoría de cambio lo siguiente, “Si los servicios son seguros, dignos, significativamente accesibles e informados por la participación del cliente, entonces las NNA están seguras en sus comunidades y casas y reciben apoyo cuando experimentan daños.”  

De manera que el proyecto propuesto contribuirá a la respuesta del objetivo del sector por medio de las siguientes actividades: 
 
Objetivo  del sector Asegurar el acceso a la atención de servicios de protección integrales, de calidad y específicos para NNA y sus familias, incluidos los grupos de atención prioritaria, en situaciones de crisis humanitarias, por movilidad humana, desplazamientos forzados, cambio climático y contextos de violencia y VBG.

project_name: Assistance aux sinistrés suite aux inondations dans les provinces  du Mayo Kebbi  Est (MKE), Mayo Kebbi Ouest (MKO) et de la Tandjilé
project_objective: Les effets néfastes du changement climatique se manifestent chaque année au Tchad. Cette année des données secondaires publiées par OCHA (Mise à jour situation d’inondations du 05/12/2022) font état de 977 501 personnes affectées; 162 917 ménages affectés à différents niveaux dans 18 des 23 provinces; 465 030 hectares de champs détruits et 19 399 têtes de bétail englouties. La province du Mayo Kebbi Est est la plus touchée par ces inondations avec 228 708 personnes affectées et 38 118 ménages. Une Enquête Multisectorielle Rapide réalisée par la Croix Rouge du 1er au 09 septembre 2022 dans les provinces du Mayo Kebbi Est, de la Tandjilé et Mayo Kebbi Ouest a rapporté environ 375 460 personnes touchées dans les 3 provinces et réparties dans 1975 villages de 39 sous-préfectures et communes.L’intervention proposée par la Croix Rouge Française - dans une logique de complémentarité aux expertises des membres du mouvement Croix Rouge/Croissant-Rouge vise la réduction de la vulnérabilité des populations sinistrées et le renforcement de leur résilience. Elle améliorera l’accès aux services vitaux de base (Santé, Eau , Hygiène , Assainissement, abris/AME) et à la sécurité alimentaire. Elle contribuera à la restauration de leurs moyens d’existence à travers trois résultats : Les ménages ciblés reçoivent une assistance directe en biens non alimentaires, en outils de construction et une assistance technique adaptée (R1 ); Le risque sanitaire de la population affectée est réduit par la prévention des maladies à potentiel épidémique et l'accès aux soins médicaux d’urgence (R2); La vulnérabilité des populations affectées est réduite à travers le renforcement de leur sécurité alimentaire, leurs moyens d'existence (R3). Une réponse d'urgence 500 000 a été financée par ECHO suite aux inondations de 2022.

project_name: Appui aux  communautés et aux institutions publiques dans la mise en place d’actions de préparation et de réponses face aux aléas climatiques dans la province de la Tandjilé
project_objective: Ce projet intitulé vise à améliorer le niveau de préparation et de réponse des communautés, des institutions publiques locales et de la Croix-Rouge du Tchad (CRT) face aux inondations et vents violents. De manière spécifique, à travers ses actions, le projet compte renforcer les connaissances des communautés et les capacités des institutions publiques locales et de la CRT pour qu’elles soient mobilisables en cas d’éventuelles catastrophes. Ainsi, quatre résultats sont attendus: 1) Les capacités de réhabilitation et de construction pérennes et résilientes des communautés sont renforcées; 2) Les capacités des autorités déconcentrées de l'État tchadien (dans la Tandjilé) en matière de surveillance, d'alerte et de réponses sont renforcées; 3) Les capacités de préparation de la Croix Rouge du Tchad sont améliorées pour faire face aux risques d'inondations; et 4) Les communautés ont accès à une réponse rapide en cas de matérialisation de l'aléa inondation. Au total, 26 activités sont définies permettant d’atteindre les résultats du projet. Les différentes actions du projet compte laisser au niveau communautaire une conscience des risques d’origine naturelle et leurs potentiels impacts et comment y faire face avec des compétences significatives dans les bonnes pratiques constructives. Au niveau des acteurs étatiques, le projet vise à renforcer leur capacité sur le suivi des alertes précoces ainsi que l'accueil et le refuge des personnes évacuées. Sur la base d’une collaboration Mouvement et d’une synergie d’action selon les mandats des uns et des autres, le projet compte renforcer les capacités des volontaires et ou cadres de la Croix-Rouge sur divers thématiques de préparation telles que l’approche PASSA et ENAP. Enfin, le projet développera une culture de veille, d’évaluation et de réponse humanitaire au sein du mouvement de la Croix-Rouge, en particulier la CRT nationale/locale et des autorités locales déconcentrées de la Tandjilé.

project_name: Provision of essential healthcare services for women, men, girls, boys within the host communities and IDPs in Jonglei and Eastern Equatoria states
project_objective: Two years after formation of Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity, humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains dire. Weak health system, recurrent inter-communal violence, devastating floods and global effect of COVID-19 continuously hamper timely access to equitable and affordable health care services. Such situation continues to increase vulnerability, hence high risk of disease outbreaks, low immunization coverage, poor hygiene and sanitation practices in crowding settlements, and therefore a likelihood of humanitarian catastrophe in 2022. In UNICEF`s humanitarian situation report No. 164,  1.4 million children faced life-threatening acute malnutrition, whilst approximately 7.2 million people were at risk of hunger largely driven by the impact of floods and displacement in 2022. Malnutrition rate extremely high with GAM rate of over 15%, of emergency threshold and Jonglei state reported the highest admission of SAM admission of 24%. According to health cluster`s response plan 2022, only 8% of the health facilities in the country provide full package of BPHNS and 53% moderately functional. Maternal mortality is one of the highest in the world, with 789 per 100,000 live births. 39% women have access to recommended Four Antenatal Care Services during pregnancy, institutionalized delivery as well as skilled birth attendance low at 12.3% and 14.7% respectively. According to health cluster`s response plan 2022, Ayod is among the counties at health severity level5, with over 20K population at Catastrophic phase. For the past 15 years, CMD has been implementing multi-sectoral humanitarian interventions in Upper Nile Region specially Jongeli and Upper Nile states & GPAA. Capitalizing on its vast knowledge of local context and collaborative partnership with local authorities, community and other humanitarian actors, CMD aims to implement this project in Ayod, and Kapoeta North counties. The project will directly target 20,000 host communities & IDPs of which 9,600 will be males and 10,400 will be females including 4,000 boys and girls of under5 year old and 800 pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Among the target groups will be 1,440 male and 1,560 female Persons With Disabilities (PWD). The model of implementation shall be through thirteen static sites, five mobile clinics and the support to community-based case management using an estimated cost of $600K in 2022. Activities include essential life-saving health services, disease prevention, detection, surveillance & reporting, strengthening RI & NIDs, disease outbreaks & NTDs. For quality of care, BEmONCs/CEmONCs with institutionalized Skilled Birth Attendance 80% live births. 800 pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) receive the recommended FOUR ANC visits & 100% SGBV survivors who report to health facilities receive CMR and basic psychosocial support services. Deploy qualified health cadres to maintain and continuously improve quality of care to mothers of childbearing age, children & persons with disabilities. Construction and rehabilitation of health facilities. Beneficiaries` involvement and capacity building of CHDs. Inter-sectoral synergies with WASH, Protection/GBV, FSL and Nutrition. Use EWARS and weekly IDSR system of reporting to monitor trends of morbidities and outbreaks. Utilize HMIS and other internally improvised reporting tools to ensure data quality and consistency. Obtain beneficiaries` feedback through existing community networks; organize FGDs and installing suggestion boxes in health facilities and CMD offices sub-nationally.

project_name: Improved Access to basic services through Provision of Integrated WASH, Education, FSL, Health and Nutrition services mainstreamed by Protection interventions for Ethiopian, South Sudanese refugees and war affected populations in Gadaref, Blue Nile and West Kordofan
project_objective:
IR-Sudan is planning to implement this integrated project which aims to enhance access to basic services education, food security and livelihood, WASH, Health & Nutrition, and protection for vulnerable communities including IDPs, Refugees, and host communities and war affected populations in three States, West Kordofan in El Nuhud, Wad Banda and Babanousa Localities with a total target group 47,498 South Sudan Refugees, 4,727 IDPs war affected and 13,738 vulnerable host communities, Blue Nile with total target 26,240 IDPs affected by recent inter-communal conflict in Rosaires & Wadelmahi localities (10,496 & 15,477) respectively, in addition to around 3,788 IDPs from recent war and Gadaref State Babikri refugee camp and Basundah locality with a total target of 30,000 Ethiopian Refugees and host-communities, as well as war affected populations displaced from KHT, estimated around 7,410 individuals. In Education sector and in line with strategic objectives 1&2 of revised HRP, the project will focus on improving access to quality education through increasing access and improving the school environment for target groups, to ensure increasing additional learning spaces to accommodate the new war affected IDPs students whom displaced with their parents from war hotspot areas, in addition to the Eritrean and South Sudan refugees and resident host communities. The proposed activities under this sector will include enrolment of children in child-friendly learning spaces, provision of recreational (kits), and hygiene/Dignity kits, hand washing stations, safe drinking water, rehabilitate gender responsive latrines, rehabilitate temporary learning spaces, and provision psychosocial support.
In WASH, the project will support refugees, war affected IDPs and host communities to improve their access to WASH services that will include sanitation and hygiene promotion services aligned with strategic objectives 1&2 of revised HRP 2023. 
Health sector interventions will focus on increasing access to health services by rehabilitating and refurbishing nonfunctioning health facilities, as well as provision of medical equipment, strengthening the capacity of health care providers and community health care workers to provide essential health services in targeted areas.
In FSL and livelihood, the project will aim to enhance the beneficiaries’ resilience and self-reliance through diversifying their livelihoods options, improving access to employment opportunities and income generating activities, especially for those fleeing from war hotspot areas and lost their work opportunities. This will be achieved through provision of simple agricultural tools, provision of seeds, deliver extension trainings to farmers and conduct vocational trainings for youths and support them with income means. The project will support women households in particular with provision of goats restocking to help in promoting their income, and train them on food processing.
The protection interventions will focus on delivering services to acutely vulnerable boys and girls, girls and boys will be provided with specialized child protection response services. Specific sources of threat challenging vulnerabilities of children will be identified and addressed particularly high risk of abuse, neglect, exploitation, or violence. Vulnerable and at-risk children will be provided with gender & age appropriate (structured) psychosocial support and life skills including literacy and numeracy. Communities will be mobilized to support children through activation of child protection networks. Finally the project will enhance and build human resource capacity through targeted groups to respond to child protection concerns at all levels.

project_name: Projet d’appui en eau, hygiène et assainissement au District Sanitaire du Barh El Gazal dans le cadre de la prévention de la Malnutrition.
project_objective:
Oxfam intervient dans les provinces du Bahr el Gazal (Moussoro Ouest) depuis des années, suite à une crise d’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle devenue chronique dans la province. Pour faire face au pic de la malnutrition, Oxfam et son partenaire envisagent mettre en œuvre un projet efficace basée sur le renforcement des capacités des structures locales à mieux faire face à la situation,  de façon pérenne et autonome, pour prévenir la malnutrition voire réhabiliter les enfants malnutris modérés dans les villages du projet mais aussi,  à soutenir les centres de prise en charge nutritionnelle à travers le dépistage et référencement, l’appui en kit minimum Wash, la réhabilitation et construction des ouvrages hydrauliques et d’assainissement.
De services en eau, hygiène et assainissement sera fourni dans 10 des structures de prise en charge de la malnutrition et 10 villages avec les actions à base communautaires (mise en place des clubs mamans/FARN, la mise en place des séances de sensibilisation sur les bonnes pratiques nutritionnelles etc.) avec un objectif de toucher de 3857 personnes dont 2315 MAS et 1542 hommes et femmes. L’intervention sera cordonnée avec les district sanitaires ciblés, et des autres partenaires intervenant dans le secteur Nutrition. 
L´objectif de l´action est de contribuer à la réduction du taux de malnutrition aigüe global par l’accroissement de l’accès à l’eau, à l’hygiène et a l’assainissement au profit des communautés affectées par la crise nutritionnelle dans les communes du Bahr El Gazal Nord et Sud.
Toutes les activités à mettre en place pour atteindre les objectifs et résultats du projet, ont pour corolaires d´améliorer l’autonomisation et la participation des femmes dans les instances de gestion et de développement communautaires (différents comités de gestion des points d'eau, les comités d'assainissement, les clubs mamans/FARN…) et la prise en compte des problématiques de genre, afin de permettre aux femmes et aux jeunes de devenir des moteurs du changement. Nous savons tous que les femmes et les filles sont les premières responsables des questions de l’hygiène, eau et assainissement ainsi que l’alimentation des enfants au niveau de la communauté. 
OXFAM adhère et met en œuvre les 4 principes de protection SPHERE, dont le « Do No Harm » est l’un des principes énoncés. Oxfam effectuera des analyses des risques constants afin d’identifier les différents facteurs pouvant affecter les membres de la communauté pendant le projet ainsi que les possibles conséquences négatives, non souhaitées du projet.
OXFAM travaille toujours en étroite collaboration avec les services techniques étatiques décentralisés, basés dans les zones de mise en œuvre du projet à travers l’identification des besoins, la supervision des travaux, la réception des ouvrages etc.

project_name: WAVE - Winterization Assistance for Vulnerable Households in Emergencies
project_objective:
In 2022, 14.6 million people in Syria are in need of humanitarian assistance. This constitutes the highest number of people in need since the onset of hostilities in 2011 and is expected to even further increase in 2023. In a context of high inflation and rapidly increasing food, fuel and basic goods prices, households' income gaps and thus debt loads are increasing. As a response, the project aims to enhance the ability of 6,537 vulnerable households (HHs) in Al-Hasakeh (Al Masaken), Aleppo (Jabal Badro), Homs (City), Hama (City), Damascus (Dwelaa) and Rural Damascus (Jdeidt Artouz, Sahnaya, and Daraya) affected by the crisis in government-held Syria to protect and sustain their lives. Following the guidance and the needs identified in the HNO 2022 and NFI sector HNO 2023, all selected localities have a severity scale of 3 or above. Winterization Assistance (WA) covering additional costs during the winter months (for 4 months) will be provided as per the SNFI/CWG guidance. This is especially relevant in the context of soaring prices for basic winter commodities and continuous deterioration of the currency, while at the same time salaries have remained stagnant. With winterization needs covered, HHs will be able to prevent the recourse to irreversible negative coping mechanisms and even reduce the ones already in place. Meanwhile, Cash for Winter transfer values (TVs) (146,250 SYP per month for a period of 4 month, totalling 585,000 SYP) are based on the recommendations of the CWG/NFI sector concerning the winter response and represent a monetization of the recommended winter NFIs in addition to 50 litres of subsidized fuel. The amounts are considered preliminary and are based on updated price assessments and harmonization efforts of the NFI WG and the CWG (last updated in November 2022).
The purpose of the project is that vulnerable, crisis-affected communities have improved ability to cover their winterization needs, hence reducing the adoption of harmful coping strategies. The assumption is therefore as follows: (IF) winterization assistance is provided to vulnerable communities (host, IDP, returnee) in Syria, (THEN) beneficiaries can meet their winterization needs with dignity and freedom of choice, and thus avoid having to resort to negative coping strategies.  
The field teams continuously register HHs through outreach activities and home visits in the communities. Beneficiaries will also be registered through internal referrals from national partners and external referrals from NGOs and UN agencies. The implementing partner team will assess the vulnerability of registered beneficiaries through a basic needs scoring system which was developed by Caritas Switzerland (CACH) and Caritas Syria (CS) in December 2017 and refined in 2019 and 2022 to reflect the changing context.
All beneficiaries selected to receive winterization will also benefit from Basic Needs (BN) assistance from other funded programming. This approach will ensure that the full package of assistance (BN +Winter) is provided to the identified most vulnerable population.

project_name: People affected by displacement benefit from improved access to potable drinking water, appropriate sanitation facilities and strengthened hygiene practices
project_objective:
To contribute to the overall WASH objective and ensure populations affected by displacement have reduced risk of exposure to WASH related diseases, NRC will strengthen populations’ capacity to engage in safe practices to promote better hygiene behaviours to limit health risks associated with poor WASH practices. NRC will use a range of technical approaches to provide the hardware required for access to safe water, improved hygiene and safe sanitation.

Target group
NRC targets the most vulnerable individuals and communities affected by crisis including IDPs and vulnerable host communities, in both urban, peri urban hard to reach areas including bushes and rural areas NRC WASH interventions in the Far North region aims to reach 15,000 persons (7,650 females and 7,350 males) in 2143 Households. Specifically, the following beneficiaries are targeted:
1.	Internally Displaced Persons
2.	Returnees (includes refugee returnees)
3.	Vulnerable Host Communities
4.	People living in areas currently not accessible
5.	Persons living with disabilities and those with special needs

          Beneficiary selection:
The identification of beneficiaries is based on the findings of needs assessment conducted by NRC and guided by gaps on the current 5W matrix at cluster level and guided by the Emergency tracking tool updated and shared by IOM every month. The final selection of beneficiaries will be done during focus group discussions with the community in a beneficiary validation process involving NRC’s CFM staff. NRC prioritizes vulnerable households headed by women and children who will benefit from WASH kits and construction of latrines. when households headed by men are identified as part of the most vulnerable, NRC will ensure that women in those male-headed households are the focal points to receive the assistance for the household, while making sure that this respects the principle of do no harm. NRC promotes women’s active participation to ensure community ownership and gender inclusion. NRC WASH interventions in the Far North region aims to reach 15,000 persons (7,650 females and 7,350 males) in 2143 Households.

Community engagement
NRC ensures adequate community engagement throughout the programme to strengthen an integrated, coordinated, gender-responsive water, hygiene and sanitation programme. Engaging with the users/ residents/ refugees/ displaced people helps them be active participants in the response rather than passive beneficiaries. It should make interventions more effective, efficient, and sustainable. The WASH intervention community engagement covers all four areas: i) community participation, ii) community mobilisation including behaviour change interventions, iii) community management and iv) accountability. For the strategic period, it is necessary to focus on strengthening the capacity in community engagement through improving community participations and behaviour changes techniques. A minimum number of staff need to be able to use and analysis participatory and qualitative methods such as observation and focus group discussions whenever relevant.
Gender inclusion in WASH: A particular focus is placed on women-headed households, girl children, persons living with disabilities and the elderly. Within the socio-economic context of Cameroon, women and girl children carry much of the domestic chores and other time-consuming burdens. As such, by bringing water points as well as hygiene and sanitation services closer to populations, NRC considers that beneficiaries, and in particular women and girl children, will be less exposed to protection risks and will be better able to engage time and energy elsewhere, potentially in income generating activities.
