project_name: Provision of Comprehensive Quality Coordination of the Child Protection Area of Responsibility and MHPSS in the West Bank and Gaza
project_objective:
This project is in line and contributes to HRP Coordination and support services. It seeks to respond to the prolonged humanitarian crisis in the occupied Palestinian territories affecting the Palestinian population under occupation, by contributing to the protection of their rights and dignity in accordance with IHL and IHRL, and with a cross-cutting focus with other clusters such as health and education. The project will support the implementation of the HRP 2023 and is aligned with the strategic objectives of the Protection Cluster as it seeks to increase respect for the IHL and IHRL and accountability for violations as well as support protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate the effects of occupation and conflict-related violence. 
Child Protection is an Area of Responsibility and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services under the Protection Cluster, with UNICEF as the designated lead agency. The CP-AOR/MHPSS is an active member of the Protection Cluster, maintains regular contacts with the Cluster and contributes to overall needs identification, protection analysis, and coordination processes. The CP-AOR/MHPSS’s role is to ensure the timeliness, quality and coverage of coordinated child protection/MHPSS humanitarian responses. Currently the CP-AOR/MHPSS has 30 active members in the West Bank and 30 in Gaza.
This project ensures the effective and efficient coordination of CP/MHPSS humanitarian actors in the West Bank and Gaza, including a common situational awareness and timely, appropriate and effective humanitarian response. It will ensure the regular coordination of CP partners and support a strategic humanitarian response, including the strengthening of needs analysis, contingency planning, promotion of evidence-based programming, and inclusion of cross-cutting issues. 
Gender considerations are an integral part of the coordination and response provided by partners in the field. The CP AoR will notably coordinate the interventions of Mental Health and Psychosocial service (MHPSS) providers in Gaza and the West Bank and support the provision of quality services and referrals with specialized services. This project will ensure the required support to CP actors in the integration of CP Minimum Standards, including through training and technical support. This project will ensure Child Protection partners in both Gaza and the West Bank coordinate child protection interventions through a predictable, accountable, harmonized approach and understanding of child protection needs. It also supports and ensures that there are functioning referral pathways for cases affecting children, notably in cases of violence, detention, and injuries, but also the demolitions and settler violence response mechanism. The final aim of this project is to ensure children affected by the conflict and their caregivers are provided with appropriate and quality services including case management, MHPSS support, and legal aid. 
The project also supports inter-sectoral collaboration, ensuring the Child Protection sector engages with other clusters so that CP concerns are mainstreamed in other areas of humanitarian intervention. This is notably the case with the Protection, Health, and Education sectors, via the MHPSS Technical Advisory Group (TAG) or comparable arrangement, aimed at ensuring linkages and common standards between psychosocial and mental health actors providing services at different layers of the MHPSS pyramid. Child Protection will also work closely with the Education Cluster to ensure an integrated approach is provided notably for cases requiring a multisectoral response and cases of violence affecting both areas. 
UNICEF and the CP-AOR will promote compliance with the AAP, PSEA principles and procedures. AoR members will be oriented on sexual exploitation and abuse and will receive information on interagency channels including SAWA Free toll number, social media platforms, and WhatsApp to report on PSEA

project_name: GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response service provision for the Rohingya refugee response
project_objective: The project aims to 1) improve the quality, accessibility, and inclusion of existing response services for GBV survivors, especially linkages between case management, PSS, medical care, self-reliance, educational activities, and legal services for the most vulnerable groups 2) mitigate the risk of GBV and SEA through multi-level and cross-sectoral strategies, including capacity building and community-led  initiatives and 3) prevent GBV by motivating significant changes in social norms undergirding violence, systematic discrimination, and gender and age inequalities through structured and evidence-based programs. Highly vulnerable and underserved populations will be targeted, such as PWD and gender-diverse populations. UNHCR and partners work based on community-based and survivor-centered approaches, engaging refugees as active agents and emerging leaders within their communities and during individual case management. We will increase women and girls’ participation in decision-making and leadership by building their confidence and capacities with skills-building and vocational training sessions, engaging female refugees of all ages in our CBP work, and involving men and boys as allies in promoting gender equality. Key components of the 2023 GBV programming include improving the quality of safe spaces, delivering life, vocational skills, and continuous MHPSS, enhancing community volunteers’ capacities on how to work with people with disabilities and GD population, EMAP, encouraging women-led initiatives, and delivering women’s leadership training to make them empowered and safe to make their own life decisions. UNHCR and partners continue to provide case management and specialized PSS services for survivors of GBV, with particular attention to strengthening the survivor-centered care practices within the multi-sectoral referral network and increasing accessibility for and capacity to serve target populations, gender, and age wide. Also, a more integrated approach to GBV response services is prioritized, including within health centers, legal service centers, learning centers, and drop-in centers for the LGBTIQA+ population and sex workers. This approach will streamline our services and improve free access to key populations. Capacity-building components include caseworkers’ minimum training package on case management, confidential referrals, comprehensive follow-up, supervision, diversity, and safeguarding GBV cases. Training sessions are also prioritized to sensitize health, legal, site management, law enforcement service providers, and community members on how to identify and refer GBV and SEA cases safely. GBV risks will be mitigated through a three-tiered strategy: working with the community; UNHCR multi-functional; and inter-agency levels. Community-level work will include GBV risk mapping and the generation of risk mitigation measures by refugee women and girls, with community GBV risk mitigation actions. UNHCR’s multi-functional work will develop GBV risk mitigation action plans across functional units, using safety audit tools to assess and measure GBV potential risks. Finally, the inter-agency work will be done in collaboration with other agencies to mainstream GBV risk mitigation across all eight sectors in the Rohingya humanitarian response and an initiative for PSEA. UNHCR and its partners will implement structured and evidence-based GBV prevention activities, both those that take a whole-of-society approach (SASA! Together) and those that target specific groups (Girl Shine, EMAP, Male Role Models). The multi-year SASA! program is closely coordinated with UNFPA and its partners to avoid operational overlaps. Promoting the centrality of protection and AGD approach, UNHCR and partners will invest in AAP with community-based complaints and feedback mechanisms, SEA risk mitigation through capacity-building and protection mainstreaming across sectors, and targeting highly vulnerable populations.

project_name: CARE Integrated GBV Response
project_objective:
The project aims to reinforce an effective protection environment and to reduce the risk of GBV for girls, boys, men, and women from Lebanese, PRL, and Migrant communities. The project will build on GBV prevention and response mechanisms currently in place, as it will continue to provide a multi-sectoral response to GBV and upscaled prevention services through improving community engagement. CIL with its local partner will provide a comprehensive package of services for GBV survivors through the implementation of case management, recurrent protection cash assistance, focused and non-focused PSS,
awareness-raising activities, PSEA, and distribution of dignity kits. 

This package will be combined with community outreach, which will involve stronger community engagement and will ensure timely access to services. Beneficiaries with specific needs, survivors of GBV, or women and girls at risk of GBV will be identified to benefit from project services. Identification of beneficiaries will happen through: outreach, external referrals, internal referrals, self-referrals through the helpline, and referrals from partners. A combination of targeting methods will be used in order to improve access and inclusion. Specific vulnerability criteria of targeted beneficiaries with specific protection risks will be put in place in order to ensure the identification of “most at risk” individuals, especially for the selection of beneficiaries under the emergency cash assistance activity, an example of prioritized most at risk or most vulnerable groups: women head of household, women and girls with limited or no access to SRH services, women with medical needs, elderly women, PWSN, etc,. 

The project aims to achieve two main outcomes: 1) To reduce the risk of GBV through prevention services and strengthening community engagement; 2)To mitigate the impact of GBV through improving access to response services and activating referral pathways. The project will also promote accountability through strengthened coordination, community participation, improved access to information about PSEA, and prevention and response through service provision. Project services will be provided through a combined approach of static (in partner(s) community centers) and mobile services in different areas: Beirut, Mount Lebanon, North and Akkar.

project_name: Food Security of the people in the host communities and Rohingya Camps in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective:
The project includes a comprehensive household-based food security approach by increasing the technical skills for climate supported food production and increasing the income so that they meet their food requirement. The project will be implemented both in the host community and in Rohingya camps.  
The household-based approach will analyse current trends of income and agricultural production of each household and will facilitate a development plan for strengthening food security at the household level.  Based on the plan, alternative agro or non-agro-based income-generating activities will be started. The project will include 80% of the female member or young women. The project will contribute to starting additional income sources in each household by engaging female household members. 
The project will adopt two steps income-earning and food security plan.  Firstly, the project will engage the target people for quick income earning and food production from the kitchen garden and rearing of poultry birds. This will ensure quick income and nutritional foods at the household level. Secondly, the project will develop a business plan for each household for long-term income generation activities either in the agricultural sector or in the non-agricultural sector. The project will include a strong contextual analysis for sustainable food security at the household level.    
Each of the target people will receive training in climate-sensitive food production (chicken, duck, goat rearing, and homestead garden). They will also receive training on ‘starting and improving your business (SIYB).  The business capital will be transferred to each household to purchase productive assets for climate-sensitive food production. A community-based purchase committee will be formed to improve the negotiation and bargaining capacity of the target people. As the project will select 80% female members, therefore, this involvement with the purchase committee will improve their access to the market. The project will emphasize the plantation along with kitchen gardening and will coordinate with the EETWG. 
The project will increase the market linkages to purchase inputs and sell the products in a coordinated way. The periodic meeting will be organized between the market actors and the target people to have access of them at the agro-based value chain. A risk mitigation plan will be developed for the security of food production. The target people in the host community will be linked with the MFIs for further capital for a better food security situation and the sustainability of the intervention. The regular meeting will be organized with the Government Extension Department ( Agriculture, Fisheries, Livestock) to improve the relationship between government officials and target people so that the target people receive technical support beyond the project period. The project will conduct a fortnightly session on the rights issues, early warning, and recovery system.

project_name: Lifting Healthy, Empowered and Protected Girls and Women in Cox's Bazar (LEAP)
project_objective:
LEAP is informed by proven, evidence-based approaches, programmatic lessons and
consultations with stakeholders, including girls, boys, women, men, community leaders,
partners and government actors. The project duration is 36-month and projected
budget is $6.8 million for whole project and all working areas (CXB Sadar, Ramu, Ukhiya, Teknaf and 3 Camp- 1W, 3 and 4).But under the provision of JRP, the project
will cover 7 locations- Teknaf- Sabrang & Teknaf Sadar, Ukhiya- Jaliapalong & Holudiapalong, Camp-1W, 3 and 4 of Ukhiya. The project
will employ a rights-based health services , gender-transformative (GT) and three-pronged
strategy to: i) improve the individual and collective agency and resilience of adolescent
girls and young women to exercise their SRH and protection rights (1100); ii) strengthen
health systems to provide sex- and age-responsive quality health and protection services
(1200); and iii) enhance the capacity of local women's rights organizations (WROs),
including girl-led organizations (GLOs), and youth-led organizations (YLOs) on evidencebased advocacy for GARI health and protection services while advocating for long-term
change for evidence-based GARI SRH, SGBV and MHPSS services and programming
(1300). Improved, integrated SRHR outcomes for girls have shown to contribute to better
lifelong outcomes in education, protection, livelihoods and overall wellbeing (Brookings,
2016). LEAP’s multi-sectoral and feminist approach works across health and protection
sectors to strengthen horizontal linkages while integrating women and girl's agency
throughout and engaging WROs/GLOs and YLOs as influencers to improve accountability
for GARI SRH and SGBV services and policies.
Aligned with national and local humanitarian, health, protection and GE policies and
strategies, as well as the SDGs and Canada’s Feminist International Assistance Policy
(FIAP), LEAP will contribute to poverty reduction by targeting marginalized groups in
Rohingya camps and host communities facing multifaceted dimensions of exclusion. In
partnership with four local partners where three implementing partner working in demand side and one key technical partner working on supply side, LEAP will directly reach  97,774 people, where 60,578 female + 37,196 are male including four Unions of
Ukhiya and Teknaf sub-districts, as well as three Rohingya refugee camps (37,529 where 21,462 is in 4 Host Union + 16,067 is in 3 camp).

project_name: Emergency Cash Assistance in Gaza
project_objective:
An already impoverished Palestine refugee population in Gaza faces increased vulnerabilities due to on-going blockade with lengthy closures of the border crossings at Erez and Rafah as well as unpredictable commercial crossing at Karem Shalom and access to the sea. It is further compounded with the increase in prices following the Ukraine Crisis on top of the loss of income due to the aftermath of global COVID-19 pandemic, and the recurrent escalation of hostilities in May 2021 and August 2022. UNRWA continues to provide in-kind food assistance to more than 1 million Palestine refugees in the Gaza Strip, covering a part of daily caloric needs, yet the stagnated economy continues to be a burden for most of the refugees. 
The population has already been facing years of humanitarian crisis, and many people are relying on daily labour and casual work to secure their minimum requirements when and if available. The families with high dependency ratios, including those with children, older persons and persons with disability, and/or families headed by vulnerable groups are particularly at risk, as they are more likely than others to suffer from poverty or other forms of deprivation. Through this project, UNRWA will provide one-off multi-sectorial cash assistance of US$40 per individual to more than 180,000 vulnerable and cash-strapped Palestine refugees identified through multi-dimensional vulnerability criteria including female-headed households, households headed by older person or an adolescent, and persons with disability.
The project is directly addressing the HRP Strategic Outcome 3: The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued, and contributing to the 2023 FSS Strategic Objective 2: Households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs by providing support through cash assistance.

project_name: Projet de protection des personnes déplacées et populations hôtes dans la région de Diffa
project_objective:
Le projet vise à améliorer la protection et le bien-être des femmes, hommes, filles, garçons et enfants vulnérables affectés par la crise insurrectionnelle du Bassin du Lac Tchad
Les résultats suivants permettront d’atteindre cet objectif :
Résultat :1. Les personnes déplacées et populations hôtes savent où et comment accéder aux services de lutte contre les VBG
Résultat :2. Les personnes déplacées et populations hôtes rejettent et s’engagent pleinement pour mettre fin à toutes formes de violences
Résultat :3. Les survivants sont satisfaits des services de gestion des cas de VBG
Résultat :4. Les Enfants à risque de protection bénéficient d’une procédure d’intérêt supérieur
Résultat :5. Les Enfants participent à des programmes communautaires de protection de l’Enfance
Résultat :6. La coexistence pacifique entre les communautés est promue à travers des initiatives fédératrices et d’intérêt collectif
Résultat :7. Les services de protection aux Personnes à Besoins Spécifiques sont assurés
La méthodologie de mise en œuvre du projet sera axée essentiellement sur : (i) la participation communautaire ; (ii) La Centralité de la protection et la protection communautaire ; (iii) la redevabilité collective envers les populations affectées, (iv) l’Inclusion (principe de ne laisser personne derrière), l’innovation et la coordination.
L’approche communautaire sera privilégiée par l’implication des communautés bénéficiaires, avec une participation active et inclusive des personnes vulnérables et à besoins spécifiques en général y compris les enfants Séparés/Enfants Non Accompagnés en particulier. Les Services Techniques Déconcentrés, les municipalités, les chefs coutumiers et les leaders communautaires/religieux seront aussi associés dans toutes les étapes du projet. L’approche communautaire permet d’avoir la confiance des communautés et facilite le leadership, l'engagement et la capacité au niveau local. Des évaluations participatives seront conduites pour :
	Aider à identifier les causes profondes des risques, les besoins, les capacités, les vulnérabilités et les stratégies d'adaptation existantes ;
	Aider à éviter que les interventions n'exacerbent accidentellement les problèmes ou n'en créent de nouveaux.
La centralité de la protection et la protection communautaire seront prises en compte à toutes les étapes d’exécution du projet. Les communautés affectées seront impliquées dans :
	L’Identification des risques/problèmes de protection auxquels elles font face;
	L’analyse des causes et des conséquences;
	L’identification conjointe des stratégies de prévention et de réponse
La redevabilité envers les personnes affectées se traduira par un engagement actif de prendre en compte, de rendre compte à, et d’être tenu pour responsable, par les personnes à qui nous fournissons une assistance. Des mécanismes de retour d’informations accessibles à tous, y compris aux enfants seront identifiés et mis en place. 
L'action sera inclusive, se concentrera sur l'identification et la suppression des obstacles afin que les individus et les groupes les plus exposés aux risques, victimes de discrimination ou d'exclusion puissent participer à la prise de décision et bénéficier de l'action humanitaire. 
La coordination se traduira par des partenariats avec les principales parties prenantes afin de mieux comprendre les contextes locaux, assurer la synergie d’actions, optimiser les ressources et permettre une prise de décisions intersectorielles.
Le système de suivi et supervision qui sera mis en place suit les méthodologies et pratiques de suivi et évaluation en vigueur à CARE. Il reposera sur un plan détaillé de suivi évaluation avec l’établissement d’une base de travail, basée sur une identification participative et transparente des bénéficiaires des interventions, un processus continu d’analyse et de suivi continu ou suivi opérationnel.

project_name: Solidarité avec les Populations Déplacées Internes dans le Centre-Nord (SPDI-CN)
project_objective:
CARE propose de travailler dans la région du Centre-Nord qui accueille à elle seule 34% des personnes déplacées internes sur l’ensemble des 13 régions du pays. Les communes de Rollo, Yalgo et Boulsa sont sélectionnées sur la base de l’évaluation des besoins et de l’analyse genre rapide menées par CARE en septembre 2021 dans ces localités (Rollo et Yalgo) et aussi de l’analyse du cadre harmonisé en situation projetée pour l’année 2022. Les besoins prioritaires identifiés comprenaient l'assistance alimentaire, l'accès à l'eau potable, l'hygiène et l'assainissement et les abris/AME.
Ces données sont confirmées par l’aperçu des besoins humanitaires 2021 révisé publié par OCHA en mai 2021, on note 3,5 millions de personnes dont 52% de femmes, 59% d’enfants et 2,2% de personnes avec un handicap qui ont besoin d’assistance. Selon la même source qui classe la gravité des besoins, 81.000 personnes sont dans un besoin minimal, 2 millions dans une situation de stress, 983.000 dans une situation sévère, 175.000 dans une situation extrême et 284,000 dans une situation catastrophique. Les secteurs prioritaires selon les populations et relatés par OCHA sont la Sécurité alimentaire (2,9 millions de personnes dans le besoin), la Santé (2,5 millions), l’Eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement (2,5 millions), la Protection (1,5 millions), les Abris/AME (1,4 millions), la Nutrition (1,4 millions) et l’Education (805 000).
Les zones les plus touchées par ordre d’importance de besoins sont la région du Sahel du Centre-Nord, de l’Est, de la Boucle du Mouhoun et du Nord.
Pour répondre à ce besoin, la communauté humanitaire a besoin de 607,9 millions USD mais seulement 112,8 millions USD ont été reçus à ce jour soit un gap de 495,1 millions USD d’où l’urgence de l’assistance humanitaire.
Ainsi, l’intervention proposée par CARE porte sur l’assistance alimentaire qui est le premier besoin des populations affectées. Cette intervention ciblera 2730 personnes représentant 390 ménages dont 110 ménages hôtes et 280 ménages déplacés répartis sur l’ensembles des trois (03) communes et vise à améliorer l’alimentation des personnes déplacées et les ménages hôtes ayant accueilli les déplacés en mettant l’accent sur les plus vulnérables.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving maternal, newborn and child health and nutrition interventions for vulnerable women, boys and girls in Gaza
project_objective:
The project aims to provide urgently needed essential maternal, newborn, and child health and nutrition interventions serving vulnerable communities, particularly pregnant and lactating women, neonates, and children under the age of ﬁve, both boys and girls.

The project responds to two of the Health Cluster's strategic objectives:
-	Strategic objective 2: Ensure the availability of acceptable and quality essential healthcare services to vulnerable communities in oPt
-	Strategic Objective 3: Strengthen the healthcare system's capacity to respond to emergencies and build community resilience to cope with the impact of current and future crises

The project will provide an urgent response to immediate health needs by ensuring access to essential health and nutrition services for the most vulnerable in the target population. This will be achieved through the implementation and provision of health and nutrition interventions including:
-	Support the Ministry of Health to maintain the provision of essential maternal, neonatal, child health, and nutrition services for high-risk women and young children through the provision of medical supplies including essential drugs, equipment, and consumables. 
-	Prevention and control of micronutrient deficiencies in children and pregnant lactating women.  Prevention and Management of acute malnutrition in children under five
-	Provision of postnatal home visiting services after delivery to high-risk pregnancies and vulnerable mothers and babies. These services are important for mother in terms of providing postnatal care, including medical checks, assessment of health status, provision of medication and supplements, ultrasound images, health education, and counselling
-	Capacity building of service providers particularly in relation to the implementation of the national Maternal and Child Nutrition Protocol
-	Additionally, the project will provide essential drugs and consumables for prepositioning purposes, which will contribute to the timely and effective response to emergencies.
The project will be implemented in close coordination with Health Cluster partners including WHO, UNFPA, and international and local NGOs to ensure the complementarity of the interventions for the improvement of maternal, newborn, and child healthcare.
The number of women and children benefitting from the project will be 196,155 across the ﬁve Gaza governorates over a twelve-month period. This includes 36,000 high-risk women and caregivers and 60,000 children under the age of ﬁve (30,000 boys and 30,000 girls), 10,000 neonates (5,000 boys and 5,000 girls). 20,000 people (18,000 women and 2,000 men) will benefit from awareness sessions and health education. 155 health professionals will be trained (35 males and 120 females). 60,000 persons (30,000 women, 24,000 children, 6,000 men) will benefit from prepositioned drugs and consumables.

project_name: Improvement of critical WASH services for the most affected communities in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The WASH services in Gaza Strip have deteriorated significantly because of the lack of effective maintenance and overhaul of the ageing WASH infrastructure due to the prolonged blockade and repeated escalation of hostilities. This has caused major interruption in the delivery of WASH services across the strip.  Consequently, some 800,000 people experience major limitation to their access to basic water supply. Furthermore, over 60% of the sewage generated in Gaza was discharged into the sea untreated on partially treated. Overflow of sewage treatment and pumping stations also resulted into the flooding of some communities with sewage, causing contamination of water sources and the environment, with major public health concerns.
In Gaza, more than 93 per cent of households are connected to the domestic water network, but only 3% use it for drinking. And 96.4 per cent of water resources are contaminated in terms of chloride and nitrate content. Households refer to private vendors for the provision of drinking water, while, in the Access Restricted Areas in Gaza, boys and girls fetch water from the closest desalination plant or public and free filling points. Gazans have limited access to adequate WASH facilities severely impacted during the   2021 escalation.   Wastewater treatment plants functioned at a reduced capacity due to lack of fuel. For women and girls, limited access to WASH negatively impacts their health, including menstrual health and hygiene, household chores, and school attendance.
Access to sanitation services especially outside urban areas remains a major challenge both in terms of coverage and quality of service especially for women and girls and people with disabilities. 
UNICEF and its partners is planning to address the urgent needs of the population of the Gaza Strip as outlined in the humanitarian needs overview for 2023. UNICEF and partners will focus on increasing access to WASH services among the most vulnerable communities and institutions through the restoration, sustaining and expansion of coverage to reach the most vulnerable populations with a clear multisectoral approach and build on the humanitarian-development nexus. This project will ensure that the most vulnerable women, boys and girls, and men have sufficient domestic and drinking water storage capacity whenever it becomes available and have better access to safe water and sanitation facilities and services. UNICEF and its partners will also address the  critical gaps in humanitarian needs, especially targeting female headed households, including widows.   UNICEF also discussed with its partners the importance to have the voice of the targeted community heard, including the ability to file a complaintt. For that, UNICEF is strengthening Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) in its programs by systematizing commitments in agreements with all implementing partners. As part of the UNICEF framework on Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and for the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) the office had established  two complaints mechanisms and SOP have been developed to handle the complaints.
This project therefore aims at Improving access to basic lifesaving WASH services for 750,000    boys and girls, men and women especially among vulnerable communities in the Gaza Strip and considering the need of provision of chlorine and chemical to all water facilities in Gaza . The project will address the negative coping strategies employed by vulnerable people, such as reducing the frequency and duration of handwashing, sharing sanitation facilities, and overcrowding at public water points, due to limited or lack of access to water supply and sanitation facilities, engaged in resulting from the lack of access to WASH services . These coping strategies undermine infection prevention and lead to increased public health and social economic consequences coordinated with other key areas such child protection, health and education

project_objective: The project aims to strengthen water, sanitation and hygiene response to affected population in Far North region of Cameroon with a focus on IDP camp, communities hosting IDP and returnees. In water domain, rehabilitation of boreholes and construction of small water supply network powered with solar energy will be prioritized. On hygiene and sanitation issues, communities approached for total sanitation will be implemented at municipality level. Construction of community latrines and showers will be limited to IDP sites. Hygiene promotion with distribution of minimum WASH kits will be implemented in target communities. The area targeted cover four divisions of Far North region: Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga, Mayo Danay and Logone & Chari. With these interventions, this project targets 60,000 people for access to safe water, 50,000 people for access to adequate basic sanitation and 150,000 people reached with critical WASH supply (including hygiene items) and services. project_name: Psychosocial Support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse for children affected by the North-West and South-West crisis in Cameroon
project_objective: The Anglophone Crisis continues to have devastating effects on the people of the North West and South Regions of Cameroon. Girls and boys are the primary victims of the current crisis. This translates into serious violations of their fundamental rights and constant insecurity, causing both visible and invisible trauma in the short and long-term, separation from their families and limited access to basic social services such as education, for the past four years. Being direct or indirect witnesses of violence linked to the conflict, their wellbeing, both physical and psychological, is fundamentally at stake. Through this project, UNICEF and its partners will work to protect children affected by armed conflict from violence, abuse, and exploitation through a series of interventions. These will include mental health and psychosocial support targeting 326,800 children and caregivers; case management for an estimated 42,000 unaccompanied and separated children and other vulnerable children; birth registration for an estimated 2,000 conflict-affected children; sensitization campaigns with the aim to reach out to 157,260 persons, with specific attention to parents to pass on messages on child protection in emergencies, trauma early warning signs for children affected by armed conflict, effects of family separation, GBV in emergencies and other types of violence children are at risk of at the community level so that parents and community members can play an active role in child protection in emergencies.

project_objective:
Ce projet est une partie du Programme Pluriannuel de Resilience (PPR 2022-2023) financé par Education Cannot Wait pour l'année 2023.
Le Programme Pluriannuel de Résilience (PPR) est une intervention multisectorielle qui cible les Communes affectées par les crises dans le but d'améliorer l'accès à une éducation équitable, inclusive et de qualité pour les garçons et les filles en âge scolaire. L’objectif général du plan est de fournir un paquet d’appui intégré et holistique (éducation, WASH, protection, santé mentale et appui psychosocial, genre, nutrition, agriculture) pour promouvoir un accès continue et inclusif a une éducation de qualité, sure et environnement protecteur pour les enfants en âge scolaire, filles et garçons (y compris ceux issus des populations déplacées Internes, les retournés, les réfugiés et les enfants vivant avec handicap), les adolescents, les jeunes. Il vise à mettre en place des modèles réussis pouvant être mis à échelle pour améliorer le capital humain dans les communautés sélectionnées à travers l'éducation et la protection. 
Il vise l'atteinte de 4 resultats ci-dessous:
1. Accès : Les filles et les garçons de 4 à 17 ans affectés par les crises (NORD OUEST/SUD OUEST, CAR, LCB) accèdent davantage à une éducation équitable et inclusive
2. Qualité : Les filles et les garçons de 4 à 17 ans affectés par les crises (NORD OUEST/SUD OUEST, CAR, LCB) améliorent leurs compétences de vie et sur les disciplines fondamentales
3. Protection : Les filles, les garçons et les adolescents, ainsi que le personnel enseignant affectés par les crises se sentent plus en sécurité dans l’environnement scolaire
4. Gouvernance : Le système éducatif a des capacités accrues pour planifier, suivre, coordonner et fournir une réponse éducative inclusive, équitable, de qualité dans les zones affectées par les crises

project_name: Reduced excess morbidity and mortality among affected populations of the North-West region and South-West regions of Cameroon
project_objective:
The North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon are affected by a complex humanitarian crisis that has resulted in a system-wide breakdown of infrastructure and services, especially in the health sector. This crisis has resulted in the displacement of over 1.1 million people, especially women and children1. Data from the MSNA conducted in August 2022, revealed that 202 (18%) out of 1115 health centers were no longer functional. Most of the functional health facilities are not functional to full capacity. Attacks on healthcare are a common feature of this crisis and remain a major threat to the availability of healthcare in the North-West and the South-West regions. There are limited specialized services to take care of victims of physical and mental trauma in these regions as the number of cases has been on the rise because of the crisis. This situation has been worsened by the numerous outbreaks (Cholera, Covid-19, Monkey Pox) that have increased the burden on a health system that has already been fragilized by the humanitarian crisis. At least 10 health districts (Ekondo Titi, Mbonge, Bakassi, Limbe, Tiko, Buea, Muyuka, Kumba North, Kumba South, and Mundemba) reported cases of cholera this year. Mbonge, Tombel and Kumba South health districts reported cases of Monkeypox this year. 
In some of the most affected areas, health services are not available while less affected areas have health services of poor quality. This project aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality of internally displaced populations (IDP) and affected host communities in the North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon affected by the humanitarian crisis by ensuring timely and equitable access to healthcare services. The project will target 373,069 IDPs persons (51% of this target are women, 16% are children under 5, and 11% are people over 60 years old). The areas of intervention will be Fako, Meme, Lebialem, Ndian, Manyu and Kupe - Muanenguba divisions in the South-West region and Mezam, Momo, Bui, Ngo-ketunjia, Mechum, Donga Mantung and Boyo in the North-West region. The project will emphasize on timely access to equitable healthcare through mobile clinics in areas with no functional health facilities and the use of vouchers in areas where health facilities are operational.

project_name: Projet Approvisionnement en Eau et Promotion d’Hygiène/Assainissement dans la région de Diffa
project_objective:
La proposition de CARE vise à apporter une réponse adaptée et coordonnée aux besoins dans le l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA). Elle cherche à contribuer à des solutions adaptées pour atténuer les souffrances des communautés d’accueils, des retournés et des réfugiés dans la région de Diffa. En effet, en dépit des efforts importants de l’État du Niger et de la communauté humanitaire, d’importants gaps sont encore à combler en matière d’eau, hygiène et assainissement particulièrement sur les sites d’accueil des personnes déplacées et dans les villages de retour des populations déplacées internes. Pour répondre aux besoins croissants en matière d’ l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement, CARE procédera à la construction et/ou réhabilitation d’ouvrages d’approvisionnement en eau potable et d’assainissement, la mise en place, formation et équipement de Comités d’Hygiène et Assainissement (CHA), la fourniture de kits EHA (matériel de transport et de stockage de l'eau, des produits de traitement de l'eau et des kits d'hygiène intime pour les femmes), la création de dépotoirs publics et fosses à ordures et la sensibilisation sur le changement de comportement dans la pratique d’hygiène et assainissement. Aussi, là où l’approvisionnement en eau potable est payant, CARE organisera une opération « Voucher eau de consommation » au profit des ménages pauvres. 
Ainsi, le projet contribuera à l’amélioration des conditions de vie de 14000 personnes (dont au moins 60% de femmes) vivant dans les ménages vulnérables des déplacés et familles d’accueil.
CARE travaillera en collaboration avec les (i) les autorités, (ii) les services techniques déconcentrés, (iii) les leaders communautaires à tous les niveaux. Cette implication permettra une appropriation des activités et est gage d’une durabilité des actions. 
Dans la région de Diffa, CARE a conduit plusieurs Analyses Genre Rapides (RGA) jusqu’en 2020 qui ont ressorti les besoins spécifiques des hommes, des femmes, des filles et des garçons dans tous les secteurs, y compris le secteur EHA ; ainsi que la meilleure façon de les impliquer dans la mise en œuvre de la réponse humanitaire. Le présent projet proposé procédera à une mise à jour des analyses genre rapides. Ainsi, la réponse sera bâtie non seulement sur la base des besoins identifiés par les acteurs, mais également en se basent sur les besoins spécifiques ressortis par les l’analyse genre rapide. Dans sa mise en œuvre, le projet se basera sur les recommandations de la RGA pour assurer une pleine implication de toutes les composantes sociales et apporter une réponse de qualité dans le secteur de l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement, prenant en compte les besoins spécifiques des bénéficiaires.

project_name: Provision of integrated WASH services to Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals and Host community people
project_objective:
Caritas employs robust protection and gender mainstreaming strategy and apply age/gender/diversity lenses to all aspects of implementation at all phases of the project cycle, including paying special attention to particularly vulnerable groups in this context. It utilizes the Protection Mainstreaming Framework and is committed to follow the guidance and practical tip-sheets and strategy developed by the WASH Sector by incorporating the principles of Safety and Dignity, Do No Harm, Meaningful Access, Accountability, Participation and Empowerment throughout the response. Under this project, CB will offer full WASH package to the people of concern in the targeted blocks that includes operation & maintenance of facilities, provision of water supply and hygiene promotion etc. 
CB’s national policy for PSEA, is adapted and complaints will be collected through the several entry points and are directly processed by the dedicated PSEA focal point. Trainings on PSEA, Safeguarding and how to report is organize for volunteers and staff. 
CB closely works with Government like- NGOAB, Deputy Commissioner, CiC and sectors for approvals and coordination. Regularly submits 5Ws and Sitrep to sectors and as active member it participates in Education Sector Coordination meetings Cox’s Bazar level and camp level CiC meetings and education sector meetings. CB Intends to participate and work with Water, Sanitation and Solid waste TiWG. 
These challenges are due to a lack of strategic focus on operation and maintenance, quality, and durable solutions of all essential WASH Services, building resilience with a community-engaged approach. Therefore, CB intends to address the above challenges to keep operating Maintenance capacity ensuring facilities remain functional.
In a joint agency gender analysis on the response, children and adolescents also raised concerns about safety when accessing WASH facilities. Girls were prevented from using latrines that were being used by both men and women, due to the lack of segregation and privacy. It was alarming that a good number of HHs with persons with disabilities not reporting having used an improved water source. CB intends to ensure inclusive WASH service too.
The projects aim to mainstream protection for ensuring that beneficiaries safely access their services, without causing harm, and for promoting meaningful access, accountability, and participation of beneficiaries in the provision of WASH assistance and it will maximize the positive impacts of WASH programs on people’s safety and dignity and support affected populations access and enjoy their rights and strengthen participation and empowerment. 
The program includes DRR components integrated into WASH activities that will have special attention for upholding environmental sustainability. CB will integrate site improvement and construction will be implemented for the improvement of the WASH facilities. The community people will be motivated to protect the soil erosion through the roadside plantation. The community people will be motivated not to do open defecation. They will also be made known and motivated not to cut trees indiscriminately and to plant trees at their homesteads. Besides. All DRR activities will employ an Environmental Stewardship tool which is being developed under the DRR Coordination group comprised of CRS, Caritas Australia, CAFOD and Trocaire.
Finally, the project will support social cohesion through the localization process, through developed proactive communication strategies, including challenging negative stereotyping within and between communities. Through community engagement across all WASH components activities, sports events, outings, and welcome events, as part of wider strategies to promote community cohesion and community engagement.

project_name: Provision of life-saving WASH services to the Rohingya refugee population in Ukhiya Upazila, Cox's Bazar District
project_objective:
CARE’s approach responds to identified needs  through own assessments and other agencies approved by WASH sector. The database of the situation in the camps will be the reference point to all infrastructure improvement works. In HOST community people have less access of safe drinking water. Also to collect safe drinking water female are mainly responsible to collect it which is far distance from household level. For people with disability the water points are not accessible and this a challenge of daily life. For more accessible water source water distribution network will be established for HOST community people.CARE will put particular attention to sanitation by providing technical support to the partner staff to engage sub-block level desludging teams for a more decentralized service delivery due to the high population in the targeted camps versus the existing latrines. Mechanized extraction of sludge will promote high public health standards to prevent potential cross contamination as well as ensure environmental safety and protection. Based on need, sludge transfer stations will be used as holding chambers to fasten the desludging process and safer transportation to existing FSM’s. New latrines and bathing cubicles will be constructed and existing ones will be assessed for quality, safety and security. In HOST community safe sanitation is not available which CARE will ensure safe sanitation which will be accessible for all. Also for the lack of bathing facility gender based violence can occur in HOST community, to reduce GBV women friendly space will be constructed. More awareness session will be conducted by CARE to make community learn more.    Gender markers will be assigned to ensure privacy and safety especially for women and girls. CARE will prioritize menstrual hygiene management for women and adolescent girls by upgrading existing facilities and or constructing new facilities with exclusive MHM provisions (I.e enhanced privacy, water supply, washing areas, hanging lines, disposal chambers, etc).
CARE will conduct capacity building to WASH committees (including partner staff and volunteers, etc.) to strengthen their skills and practical knowledge on simple maintenance procedures, water safety and effective management of WASH facilities within the sub-block levels. The training will also consider/involve community leaders (Imams, Manjis, etc.) to be able to convey accurate messages to their respective audiences and contribute in influencing positive behaviour change. CARE proposes a multi-sector response to prevent the spread and respond to the corona virus in the targeted camps 15 and 16, leveraging current networks and programming to ensure effective and timely intervention. The project will put special focus on the inclusion of most vulnerable groups, such as the elderly, unwell, caregivers and people living with disabilities to ensure appropriate messages/services and shared inline/with the approval of the Ministry of health/Civil Surgeon and WASH sector. Approaches will enhance community resilience through capacity building to minimize the spread of Covid-19 within the community, households and individual levels to prevent the re-emergence or spread of the disease including acute watery diarrhea (AWD’s). CARE has a strong emphasis on community engagement and will ensure block/sub-block level sessions are relevant to the WASH sector strategy and are actively coordinated at the sub-block level to sensitize women, girls, men and boys as well as the general community level actors to create awareness across-section of key health exposure risks thus mobilize participatory actions such as mass clean camp campaigns (in coordination with respective CiC’s, other implementing partners), awareness on proper use/maintenance of WASH facilities.

project_name: Developing the resilience, well-being and capicity among the adult women and adolescent girls of forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals in Rohingya Camp(s)
project_objective: The Rohingya community people from Myanmar fled their country of origin, sought as refuge. Some pre-existing social reasons (i.e. discrimination, violence etc.) put the Rohingya community in a vulnerable situation. However, children, adolescent, women, elderly person and person with disabilities from any community are always more vulnerable than others and are at risk of any kind of harm and violence. Caritas Bangladesh will implement this project Rohingya camp 20 (palongkhali, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar). First goal of this project will be to reduce the risk of gender-based violence, intimate partner violence as well and as other form of violence among the FDMNs. Community people will play the key activist to identify community protection risk, mental health needs through door to door visit. 6 Community activist group will be formed with 72 community people, where the participation of different group (Age, gender, person with disabilities) of people will be ensured. Among 8052 people, 5000 (>17 years= 1843, 18-59 years= 3060 and 60+ years= 100) individual including will 92 person with disabilities will have awareness raising session on needs based protection and mental health issues. Community volunteer will conduct the sessions. The next goal of this project will be to improve the quality of response services and to enable the access to the non-communicable community based mental health and psycho-social support services to. Multipurpose Women and girl center (MWGC) will be established in an inclusive and person friendly form where person with disabilities, adolescent girls and victim of any form of violence can get their required services. IASC guidelines of MHPSS pyramid for mental health service, PFA services will be maintained to community people segregated by age, gender and disability to build the resilience and well-being. Case worker will provide the case management service maintaining ISCG and protection guidelines. To provide prevention and response services this project will also focus on the capacity building of community protection activist, community volunteer and project staff. They will have training on facilitation skill, protection mainstreaming and process of community people engagement, advance MHPSS services, GBVIMS and referral. To identify the protection risk, concerns and to get immediate response, the community protection activist will trained up on developing action plan. To integrate with other sector, training on protection mainstreaming, safeguarding, PSEA will be conducted to other sector staff of CB. As part of reaching the vulnerable people proactive engagement in empowerment activities such as life skill or vocational training (i.e. solar repair, tailoring and jute product making) initiative will be taken, where the participants will be the survivors of GBV. To engage the children and adolescents, play therapy will be provided to build early childhood development. Assistive device (Wheel chair & hearing aid) will be provided to support the person with disabilities. Women and male led focus group discussion will be conducted to identify the barriers, needs and way of mitigation to any protection concerns. For addressing the needs of diverse groups (i.e. persons with disabilities, marginalized groups, members of LGBTQ etc.), CB will ensure the coordination among the government stakeholders, developmental organizations, multi-sectors through participating coordination meeting, submitting- 5W & sitRep, incident report to sectors, participating training, Day observations (i.e. World mental health day, 16 days of activism, International Women day etc.) and so on as part of gender mainstreaming and disability inclusion. Feedback and response will be collected through the CFRM mechanism and response safeguarding and committee to improve the quality of the project activity. These activities will have impact of community based protection and helps when the FDMNs will be repatriate to their country of origin.

project_name: Projet d’Assistance Alimentaire aux populations vulnérables des régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Centre Nord, du Nord, l'Est et du Sahel
project_objective:
Le cadre harmonisé de mars 2022 estime que 3,45 millions de personnes seront en situation d'insécurité alimentaire sévère (CH phase 3+) pendant la période de soudure (juin-août) 2022, ce qui représente 16% de la population du pays, dont 630 000 au bord de la famine. Cela représente une augmentation de 40% de la population en phase 3+ par rapport à 2021. La plupart (70%) de ces personnes en insécurité alimentaire sont concentrées dans des régions du pays à forts enjeux sécuritaires. Il s'agit des régions du Sahel (685.729), de l'Est (591.766), du Centre-Nord (575.082) et du Nord (549.085).
 Les facteurs aggravants sont les conflits couplés à une augmentation de 40 à 60 % des prix des aliments de base, exacerbés par l'impact de la guerre en Ukraine et les mauvaises performances de la saison agricole 2021-2022. Les prix des céréales ont augmenté de 60%, le niébé de 62%, l'huile végétale de 56% par rapport aux prix de mars 2021. De plus, l'insécurité empêche les agriculteurs d'accéder à leurs champs (réduction de 412 000 ha depuis le début du conflit). En conséquence, la production agricole devrait baisser de 10% entre 2021 et 2022. La crise affecte négativement l'accès aux acteurs pour apporter des réponses appropriées aux bénéficiaires dans certaines localités. 
La construction de familles résilientes suppose que la communauté humanitaire soit en mesure d'accéder aux zones les plus touchées pour y mener des interventions. Nous devons donc consacrer de l'énergie au plaidoyer humanitaire, avec d'autres organisations humanitaires, pour que la question de l'accès soit traitée et que les actions humanitaires restent possibles. 
Avec un budget total d’environ $2,500,000  , SCI compte appuyer les populations touchées par l’insécurité alimentaire et permettre le renforcement des moyens d’existences en faveur de 92600 bénéficiaires dont 60% enfants dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Sahel ,du Nord et du Centre Nord. Ces populations sont soit touchées par la pauvreté ou l’insécurité surtout dans la partie Nord du pays entrainant des déplacements massifs vers les centres urbains.
L’objectif de cette intervention est de pouvoir fournir l’aide alimentaire d’urgence, permettre le renforcement des moyens d’existences tout en insistant sur l’autonomisation des ménages

project_name: Increase access to equitable quality essential health services for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable population in South Sudan through provision of immunization core pipeline and use of the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM)
project_objective:
In line with our organizational Core Commitment to Children in Emergency, UNICEF will continue to provide the population of South Sudan especially children, pregnant and lactating women, with quality preventive, and curative services as well as outbreak response activities. The IRRM enables UNICEF, through direct implementation as well as in partnership with IPs, to provide high impact lifesaving emergency response in inaccessible and conflict affected areas. UNICEF will ensure availability of core pipe line vaccines and cold chain supplies to respond to vaccine preventable disease outbreaks.
This project aims to increase access to quality equitable essential primary health care interventions through IRRM and provide a core pipeline to increase access to quality equitable immunization services by vulnerable populations living in host communities and IDPs living in Protection of Civilian Sites (POCs), formal IDP camps or host communities in conflict affected areas as well as refugee returnees.
The activities to be implemented are:
• Procurement and distribution of vaccines for emergency response .
• Procurement, distribution and maintenance of cold chain 
• Technical support for improved vaccine and cold chain management
• Conduct 10 IRRM missions
• Procurement and distribution of anti- snake venom 
• Procurement and distribution of LLINs
• Procurement and distribution of Health Emergency Kits, Clean Delivery Kits and items for diarrhea (IEHK2017 basic unit kit and Supl.1-medicines kits, AWD Periphery Kit drugs), malaria and Pneumonia prevention and treatment 
The expected beneficiaries of core pipeline supplies are 650,000 vulnerable children aged 6 months-15years (323,988 Female; 326,590 Male) living in camps, PoCs, formal IDP camps or host communities in conflict affected areas and refugee returnees. The children will benefit from emergency vaccination to sure up their immunity to vaccine preventable diseases. Vaccines against measles, and traditional childhood vaccine. UNICEF will also support repair and maintenance of the damaged cold chain equipment and devices as well as replacement of the non-repairable equipment to ensure the continuity of the vaccination services.
The curative consultations will be provided for an estimated 28,000 children (13,972 female; 14,028 male) during the Rapid Response Missions. These will include children aged 6 months-15 years who will be reached with immunization services and curative consultations and pregnant women who are expected to benefit from ANC services, tetanus toxoid vaccination, curative consultations and the provision of long-lasting insecticide treated nets (LLITN).
Under the IDP response through IRRM, provision of Emergency Maternal and Newborn care will prioritize provision emergency health kits for obstetric emergencies during curative consultations. Also mainstreaming GBV referrals and strengthening the referral pathway for Psychosocial first aid.

project_name: Response integrée RRM et Post RRM de santé, protection et nutrition aux popolations affectée per les conflits dans les régions de Diffa, Tahoua et Tillabery.
project_objective:
Le projet envisage de garantir l'assistance humanitaire à 265.539 (138 421 femmes et 127 118 hommes ; 169 921 PDIs et 26 518 refugiés) personnes entre PDIs, refugiés et population hôtes touchés par la crise; en leur assurant les services de santé, protection, nutrition et une composant EiE à travers l'intervention RRM et Post RRM.
L’intervention RRM couvre la Région de Diffa dont certaines zones, comme Maine Soroa, Goudomarie et Diffa, ne reçoivent pas l’assistance humanitaire. COOPI s’engage à intervenir pour une période de 3 mois afin de répondre rapidement aux besoins spécifiques. Les cliniques mobiles seront déployées en cas d’alerte RRM et pour garantir les services de santé, protection et nutrition dans les villages qui se trouvent au de-là de 15 km du centre de santé ou centre spécialisés.
L’intervention Post RRM couvre les Régions de Tahoua et Tillabery, où COOPI s’engage à intervenir au moment de la sortie des acteurs RRM, qui doivent nécessairement quitter après 3 mois, afin de garantir la continuation  des services et les renforcements des institutions locales dans les secteurs de la santé, la protection et la nutrition à travers l'installation des postes de santé temporaires directement liés aux CSI de référence.
L'action de COOPI dans le secteur de protection se propose de mettre en place le renforcement des capacités du mécanisme de protection communautaire et renforcer les solutions durables pour accroître la résilience de la communauté, fournir aces aux services de protection et de soutien PSS, soutenir le renforcement des capacités des acteurs communautaires sur la PSP.
Pour les autres volets l’intervention facilitera l'accès des femmes et des filles aux opportunités socio-économiques tout en engageant les hommes et les dirigeants de la communauté à discuter de l'égalité des sexes et de l'accès des femmes aux processus décisionnels. Les maris seront impliqués dans les activités d'autonomisation des femmes afin d'éviter les tensions au sein du foyer. Les hommes seront également impliqués dans la sensibilisation et la formation aux soins nutritionnels des enfants afin de promouvoir la responsabilité des hommes en matière de soins et d'éducation des enfants. L'équipe de COOPI recevra une formation spécifique sur la PSEA et la GBV, et du personnel féminin sera recruté dans les trois secteurs d'intervention afin de garantir l'accès aux femmes bénéficiaires.

project_name: Renforcement de la résilience des personnes déplacées à l’interne, des communautés hôtes et des retournés dans la région de Diffa, à travers la fourniture de services WASH et de protection
project_objective: COOPI ciblera 20165 bénéficiaires avec une intervention visant à favoriser un environnement de protection pour les personnes déplacées à l’interne (PDI), les retournés et les communautés hôtes. Par le biais de la fourniture d’une assistance holistique en matière de protection de l’enfance (PE) et des survivant(e)s aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG), le programme renforcera les mécanismes communautaires de protection, les capacités et le niveau de sensibilisation des communautés touchées, s’occupera de la gestion des cas, de la fourniture de soutien psychosocial (SPS) et d’appui à la réintégration socio-économique. Le programme opérera aussi pour : l’amélioration de l’accès à des services durables d’eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène sur le camp de Sayam Forage et hors camp ; la réhabilitation des infrastructures WASH ; la promotion de l’hygiène ; le soutien aux efforts de prévention et réponse à la Covid-19 pour les bénéficiaires des activités et des services de protection et WASH. Les nombreux besoins identifiés et la nature de l’intervention nécessitent un programme pluriannuel soit pour les travaux derealisation des infrastructures et suivi des composantes WASH, soit pour la réalisation d’un changement concret de comportement des communautés ciblées. A cela s’ajoute que les groupes cibles se déplacent continuellement et donc certaines activités, c’est-à-dire les sensibilisations en matière de protection et WASH, devront être répétées plusieurs fois au cours de l’année avec des groupes différents de bénéficiaires. Il faut noter que COOPI utilisera une approche au préalable avant de commencer toutes réalisations des infrastructures EHA qui permettra de connaitre, les habitudes culturelles de la communauté ciblée pour influencer leurs préférences en matière d'infrastructures  EHA et qui pourront facilement entretenir periodiquement sans aucune subvention.  En outre, il convient de rappeler que toutes  les infrastructures d'Assainissement tels que les latrines familiales, les aires de lavage et les points de collecte des déchets solides seront erigés  par les ménages eux memes et nous faciliteront l'application de la Haute Intensité de Main d'Oeuvre qui consiste à former et a employé la main d'oeuvre locale favorisant le transfert de compétence et l'implémentation de l'approche rurale participative. Aussi, toutes les infrastructures EHA realisées dans le cadre de cette intervention seront dotées des equipements qui vont inclure la prise en compte des personnes à besoins spécifiques et à mobilité réduite.

project_name: Provision of integrated life-saving services to vulnerable populations in West of Sudan
project_objective: Through this intervention aims at improving health & nutrition status of crisis-affected populations, including IDPs and host communities in the intervention areas, PUI will focus on 2 localities in West Darfur. PUI aims at targeting 4 locations in Al Kereneik and Geneina in West Darfur. PUI aims at targeting a total of 45997 beneficiaries directly and indirectly. This includes 7,819 children under 5 years and 3,680 pregnant and lactating women. The intervention will target health and nutrition sectors, aiming at supporting and providing lifesaving integrated health services to IDPs and host communities, in addition to improving the nutrition status of vulnerable population with reduced morbidity and mortality associated with acute malnutrition, and finally to involve communities in improvement of their health, nutrition and psychosocial status. Risks could include armed conflict and insecurity with severe deterioration of the security situation, local authorities reduced cooperation with the humanitarian community, significant population movements due to climate hazards or increasing insecurity, epidemic outbreak occurs during the project (COVID19, Monkeypox, Ebola etc.), hampered access to fuel or transportation, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA), fraud/corruption, and finally exchange rate volatility (between SDG and foreign currency).

project_name: Provision of Health and Nutrition services in Village 8 Transit Camp
project_objective:
This project will ensure continuity of health and nutrition services to Ethiopian refugees and host population of Village 8 and its transit refugee camp, in cooperation with the Ministry of Health (MoH), COR and other partners. 
The project aims to support directly the refugees hosted in Village 8 transit site through the provision of health and nutrition services. The number of refugees in Village 8 may vary during the course of the year, but are estimated to 3,137 according to UNHCR figures published the 8th of December 2021.
The health services supported will also be available to the host community of Village 8, estimated to 9,000 Sudanese.
The project also entails the distribution of hot meals to new arrival refugees and people with specific needs in Village 8 transit site. The number of beneficiaries of this assistance is expected to be 164. 
PUI will maintain an essential presence in the Welcoming Center in Village 8, providing triaging for refugees, and basic consultation by two clinical officers, this is also were PSS support is provided by PSS providers. If the patient requires further treatment or observation by a doctor or midwife, they are referred to the PHCC, a few hundred meters away from the Welcoming Center. Children under the age of five years will also be screened for malnutrition and sent to the PHC if they need treatment and follow up. Consultation of patients who do not need observation or further investigation and treatment at the health facility will be treated by the clinical officers at the reception center.    
PUI intervention under this project is well in line with the UNHCR 2022 result framework described as Persons of Concern (PoCs) have access to relevant humanitarian services and their basic needs met through access to multi-sector assistance services. As such, the activities by output are as follow.
PUI will ensure two main outputs, that 1. Primary healthcare services provided and 2. Nutrition services provided. Under output 1, PUI will:
•	Ensure provision of primary health care package and psychosocial care,
•	Support preventive health services 
•	Provide capacity building and financial support for the MOH health staff
•	Strengthen SRH services including ANC/PNC, FP, CMR and delivery
•	Strengthen and maintain prompt and effective referral system to secondary/tertiary health care, including follow up of the patients
•	Strengthen emergency preparedness and response capacity
And under Output 2, PUI will ensure:
•	Screening and referral of malnourished children for treatment
•	Community awareness raising on nutrition
•	Support malnutrition treatment services 
•	Provision of hot meal for new arrivals and people with specific needs at reception center in Village 8
PUI is closely working with different stakeholders, both governmental and non-governmental in achieving its goals to provide aid to populations affected by natural disasters, economic crises and conflicts. As such, the organization is active member of coordination platforms for humanitarian responses to people of concern, including the health, nutrition, logistics clusters and the PSEA network and SRH working group.

project_name: Livliehoods Skills Development through an Integrated Protection and Reproductive Health Approach
project_objective:
Initiated by UNFPA and implemented by national partners in Cox’s Bazar, this programme will contribute to Government of Bangladesh & Inter-agency efforts to actively promote skills and livelihood’s development amongst Rohingyas Refugees and Bangladeshi host community. For UNFPA it is an opportunity to facilitate improved health and protection outcomes through livelihood skills development programs. 

The programme framework is holistic. It captures agency-led technical expertise in Gender Based Violence (GBV/Protection sector), Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH/Health sector), and Youth (A&Y Working Group) and is operationalised through national knowledge, technical expertise and experience. It is a multi year approach anchored in the livelihoods &  skills development sector while achieving cross-sectoral impact. 
Developed in-line with the Government of Bangladesh-United Nations Framework on Skills Development for Rohingya Refugees, as established with the Government of Bangladesh.

A few components that make this livelihoods response programme unique:
- SRH/GBV services provision to livelihood activities centers.
- Leveraging “pre-conditionalities” to accelerate women and  youth-led community engagement/ SBCC.
- Linking Antenatal Care &  nutrition services to livelihoods opportunities/access. 

Outputs: 
- Improved health (SRH) and protection outcomes across service users (i.e. trainees, skilled workers).
- Project level sustainability over space & time (i.e. sustainability). 

The program will consist of project level outputs and will scale according to financial and operational capacities of partners. Project cohort numbers are defined at project level by both curriculum needs and capacity to accommodate participants. Capacity building will be given based on consultations and then using practical methodology for curriculum in handicrafts, batik print, tailoring, weaving workshop, shoe workshop, benne (yarn) making, flormat workshop, fabrication of eco-responsable menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits. Training curriculums will align with Myanmar Curriculum & ASEAN standards to ensure sustainability and credibility to participants receiving the intervention. UNFPA will work to ensure this by engaging in the Livelihoods sector on adherence to this & aligning all training coordination, curriculums, and trainers to the standard from the design phase to close out . 

This programme will have  priority target groups:
- Vulnerable households and/or individuals (i.e. pregnant and lactating women &  girls; caregivers).
- Referred individuals or households (SRH/Nutrition/GBV pathways).
- Youth between 18-24 yrs (men/women) w/potential for “pre-conditionalities' '.
- vulnerable groups of 80+ yrs for men, boys, women and girls, with an emphasis on PWDs, LGTB, and other vulnerable communities.

The application of a “pre-conditionality” is not mandatory. “pre-conditionalities” would include:
- Previous Girl Shine / Champions of Change experience/completion;
- Members of Women’s Support Groups, Community Watch Group & Self-help Group;
- Previous relevant experience and knowledge of volunteering, community engagement; 
- Readiness to learn/support and participate in SBCC SRH/GBV focused skills/activities development/outreach; 

The programs will take place in A&Y Centers  (F/M ages 10-24 + caregivers) and Women Lead Community Center (WLCC) (all ages F/M). Between the two centers, UNFPA facilitates comprehensive case management services, sexual and reproductive health services, emergency referrals, life skills development, and structured psychosocial support activities.
