project_name: Expanding Social, Civic and Economic Engagement and Social Cohesion Interventions for Conﬂict-Affected Adolescents and Youth in the Syrian Arab Republic
project_objective:
In support of the ERL Sector (Strengthened Communities and Participation), UNICEF, through this project in 2023, will further support its Generation Unlimited initiative and No Lost Generation Agenda by empowering vulnerable adolescents and youth (10-24 years), female and male and those with disabilities, to access social, civic and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement (including participation in social cohesion initiatives) with the objective of contributing to enhancing resilience and social cohesion. UNICEF will build on strategic partnerships, integration and at scale programming focusing on the most vulnerable adolescents to strengthen skills development, employability and meaningful engagement through friendly spaces and mobile teams. The proposed project will support young women and men to have better access to civic, social, and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement and to unleash their potentials and increase their learning, leadership, and employability opportunities. 
UNICEF will promote the active and meaningful participation of young people brought together from different ages, genders, abilities and cultural and educational backgrounds to be agents of positive change in their communities. UNICEF will work in the following three pillars and related interventions: (1) Provide access to services and skills-building for adolescents and youth for enhanced employability. (2) Strengthen social, civic and economic engagement of adolescents and youth and foster volunteerism and social cohesion-building. (3) Support young entrepreneurs to start their own project projects through seed funding. UNICEF will continue strengthening the capacity of local partners including services providers, youth workers and young volunteers to improve the quality of provided services and enhance the evidence generation. UNICEF will support the scalable and sustainable approaches with national partners including integrated centers & platforms.
In this project, UNICEF will give priority to adolescents and youth in the high severity areas such as Dara’a, Rural Damascus, Northern Homs, Southern Hama, East and Northeast of Aleppo, Deir-ez-Zor and Idleb. UNICEF will expand its support to young people in NES, focusing on returnees and displaced people in Raqqa and Hasakah, including those in camps, collective shelters and urban settings. UNICEF will focus on the most deprived areas in rural and urban areas. These will include camps (Hol, Roj, Newroz, Areesha, Mahmoudli) in Al-Hasakeh and Raqqa , the collective shelters in Al-Hasakeh city, and the rural areas in Qamishli, Malikia, Yaroubia, and Raqqa Governorate. Projects engaging young people will be essential needs for their effective integration in their communities. In addition, since 2014, many young people have been staying in camps and collective shelters. They do not enjoy the freedom of movement and face other risks, thus offering them activities that will enhance their skills and allow them to catch up to their peers in terms of skills and non-formal education.  The programme will coordinate with and support other UNICEF programmes to ensure interventions are tailored to the particular needs of young people. The programme will implement activities for young people affected by, or at high risk of, emergencies or the socio-economic situation, to acquire the right skills, become empowered and resilient community members who help their communities to cope with emergencies. Life-skills and citizenship education for these adolescents will equip and empower them to act as both participants and catalysts of change in their community as volunteers and peer influencers.

project_name: Enhancing youth resilience, skills and social participation with a special focus on adolescent girls
project_objective:
Through the proposed project, UNFPA will invest in empowering youth, especially young girls aiming to enhance their resilience, by building their personal and social assets that can promote their positive development and enable them to reach their full potential. The Project will also contribute to the wellbeing of the young people’s families and communities, enabling them to have access to livelihood opportunities and social participation by building the capacity of youth to take the lead and the responsibility to identify and prioritize their needs as well as the community needs. Specifically, the Project will focus on supporting youth female headed households for business startups and provision of seed funding to support them in leading entrepreneurship projects.

Two youth friendly spaces will be established in Rural Damascus and Hama. A set of activities will be provided at the center aiming to promote young people’s wellbeing, leadership, participation and economic empowerment. The project will be implemented in Rural Damascus and Hama, the communities selected based on the 2022 severity scale and on the fact that they are priority return destinations and accessible to UNFPA IPs.

The project will follow a gender transformative and gender equality approach, as per existing IASC  guidelines. More so, the interventions in this proposal are in line with the “Compact for Young People in Humanitarian Action” launched at the World Humanitarian Summit (2016). UNFPA promotes efforts to put young people at the center of humanitarian action and does so through key actions as follows: 
1) On services: Promoting and increasing age- and gender-responsive and inclusive programmes that contribute to the protection, health and development of young women, young men, girls and boys within humanitarian settings 
2) On participation: supporting systematic inclusion, engagement and partnership with youth, in all phases of humanitarian action, through sharing information and involvement in decision-making processes.
3) On capacities: Recognizing and strengthening young people’s capacities and capabilities to be effective humanitarian actors by their active participation in the community and livelihood opportunities. 
4) On resources: increasing resources intended to address the needs and priorities of adolescents and youth affected by humanitarian crises and identify ways to more accurately track and report on the resources allocated to young people in humanitarian contexts.

UNFPA is committed to invest in youth and emphasizes the rights of adolescents and the need to increase their potential to contribute to positive social transformation. UNFPA is mandated to address the needs of young people that are considered life saving for their future well-being, and work on projects that will contribute to empower young people and prevent them from participating in harmful practices that affect their decisions, health and future.

project_name: Resumption of lifesaving food assistance to refugees following the recent conflict.
project_objective:
VERSION 2:
This is to highlight the arrangements to resume critical life-saving activities in Sudan, as and where security allows. When the resumption of operations becomes possible, WFP will engage in three key pillars of work:
A.	Resume life-saving assistance to some or all of WFP’s pre-existing 4.9 million relief caseload including 700K Refugees. Targeted beneficiaries include food-insecure IDPs, refugees and resident population.
B.	Meet new food security and nutrition needs, where feasible.
C.	Provide critical common services to humanitarian partners (Emergency Telecommunications Cluster, Food Security Cluster, Logistics Cluster, UNHAS).
WFP resumed critical food assistance on 2 May 2023 to a proportion of the existing relief and nutrition caseload, where WFP has assured security, capacity, access, stocks and partners. The focus is: 
Gradual provision of general food assistance (GFA) with the aim to reach 4.9 million food-insecure IDPs, refugees and resident population, over the next 2-3 months. 
Given the highly volatile context, a gradual approach will be applied. As a first relief response, a two-month in-kind food ration covering May and June will be provided to refugees (100% ration) in White Nile, Kassala and Gedaref States.
There is a possibility that food commodities in warehouses may be looted if not distributed urgently. Accordingly, only in-kind food will be distributed in this preliminary response (no CBT at this stage with a particular concern on liquidity). While in-kind food relief is being prioritized for the initial response, CBT preparedness options are being concurrently developed.

project_name: Protección de niñas, niños y adolescentes migrantes, desplazados forzados, o que han sufrido violencia, abuso y explotación en El Salvador en emergencias
project_objective:
Las niñas, niños y adolescentes en El Salvador sufren altos niveles de violencia en las escuelas, hogares y comunidades. Los niveles de violencia, incluida la violencia de género, se agravan en situaciones de emergencia, principalmente debido al aumento del estrés en las familias y la pérdida de espacios seguros en la comunidad o en las escuelas. 

Además, se ha identificado un aumento en el número de niñas, niños y adolescentes en movimiento. Durante el 2022 se identificaron 13,721 personas deportadas en El Salvador, de las cuales alrededor del 32 % eran niñas, niños y adolescentes (OIM, 2023). Asimismo, en la frontera sur de Estados Unidos de América se identificaron en el año fiscal 2022 97,030 personas salvadoreñas, de las cuales el 16.93% (16,431) era niñez y adolescencia no acompañada y 29.71% (28,824) grupos familiares (US Customs and Border Protection, 2023). 

De acuerdo con datos de OIM relativa a niñez y adolescencia no acompañada retornada a El Salvador, la violencia / inseguridad, reunificación familiar y la mejora de las condiciones de vida son las tres principales razones para migrar. La violencia, el abuso, la explotación, los desplazamientos forzados y la migración tienen importantes consecuencias a nivel emocional, educativo o familiar, entre otros. Lo anterior se ha podido constatar mediante un aumento en la demanda de servicios de salud mental a través de organizaciones de la Sociedad Civil. 

Con el presente proyecto, UNICEF tiene como objetivo brindar una respuesta humanitaria para que niñas, niños y adolescentes migrantes, desplazados forzados o afectados por la violencia, incluyendo población LGTBIQ+ y con discapacidad, accedan a mecanismos de denuncia y servicios especializados e integrales de protección de la infancia. Esto orientado a la restitución de sus derechos y la reintegración en las comunidades como solución duradera. El propósito es fortalecer y ampliar los programas especializados brindados por el Consejo Nacional de la Primera Infancia, Niñez y Adolescencia (CONAPINA), los gobiernos municipales y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, para lo que se promoverá la coordinación y la articulación del sistema de protección de la infancia a nivel nacional y local. 

Las niñas y niños con necesidades de protección beneficiarios recibirán protección a través de albergues o acceso a espacios seguros, apoyo psicosocial, asistencia legal y respuesta a otras necesidades humanitarias; lo anterior, junto con el desarrollo de habilidades para la vida de las personas cuidadoras, apoyo para la empleabilidad y emprendimiento para que fortalezcan su resiliencia y empoderamiento a nivel familiar. Para ello se fortalecerán mecanismos de denuncia, servicios especializados, líneas de ayuda, mecanismos de gestión de casos y espacios amigables de apoyo psicosocial y se promoverán entornos protectores familiares a nivel comunitario. El proyecto será implementado bajo un enfoque inclusivo, de género y de discapacidad y se promoverá la continuidad de los servicios que pueden ser afectados por brotes de COVID-19 u otros virus y/o enfermedades estacionarias. 

El proyecto se implementará en 12 meses, por un monto total de $2,163,000.00.

project_name: Continuidad educativa en espacios seguros y protectores para niñas, niños y adolescentes afectados por emergencias.
project_objective:
Atención educativa como primera respuesta humanitaria, la cual asegura que el retorno a la normalidad sea más rápido, restableciendo espacios de aprendizaje seguros, amigables y equipados, garantizando el derecho a la educación y a la recreación. Las intervenciones están enfocadas en salvar las vidas de las niñas, niños y adolescentes proporcionando mensajes clave para la protección y la salud física y mental. Además, facilitan las condiciones para la recuperación socioemocional y académica para reanudar el curso de sus vidas.   

Con el proyecto, de 12 meses de duración, se pretende apoyar a 58 espacios temporales de aprendizajes y/o centros educativos y equiparlos con materiales lúdicos, educativos y mobiliario, con el fin de brindar los primeros auxilios psicológicos y el fortalecimiento de los aprendizajes básicos de lectoescritura y matemática. 
En estos espacios, al menos 7,470 niñas, niños y adolescentes afectados por la emergencia, reciben atención psicosocial y (atención educativa) fortalecimiento de sus habilidades básicas de aprendizaje. 
El monto total del proyecto es de $ 621,996

project_name: Respuesta integrada de servicios especializados de Protección de NRC que reducen y mitigan el impacto del conflicto armado colombiano sobre personas desplazadas internas y comunidades afectadas por el mismo, permitiéndoles satisfacer necesidades urgentes, acceder a mecanismos de protección, disfrutar de sus derechos básicos y alcanzar soluciones duraderas.
project_objective:
Los proyectos de Protección de NRC involucran el trabajo de dos equipos, por un lado, servicios especializados de protección y, por el otro lado, servicios de asistencia legal. 
Los proyectos de Protección contra violencia de NRC buscan reducir y mitigar el impacto de la violencia y el conflicto sobre individuos y comunidades expuestas al conflicto armado interno colombiano; inclusive riesgos de protección como amenazas, asesinatos, desplazamiento forzado, confinamiento, explotación, extorsión, robo, violencia basada en género, riesgos de minas y reclutamiento, uso y utilizo por grupos armados. 
Las actividades de Protección contra violencia miran a prevenir la violencia antes de que ocurra, mientras se contribuye a la restauración de la seguridad para comunidades e individuos en riesgo. Se logra este resultado asegurando que los individuos sobrevivientes de violencia tengan recursos y capacidades de enfrentamiento mejoradas, aumentando la resiliencia y capacidad de mitigación frente a los riesgos de comunidades expuestas, fortaleciendo políticas públicas que protejan los individuos más vulnerables, y mejorando las capacidades de respuestas de instituciones y autoridades. 
Las actividades incluyen servicios individuales especializados de protección como gestión de casos y asistencia inmediata de protección, acompañamiento protectivo y apoyo psicosocial individual estructurado; acciones de autoprotección civil que incluyen mapeo de los riesgos dirigidos por las comunidades, aumento de capacidad en protección para miembros de comunidades, diseño y fortalecimiento de estrategias de autoprotección civil, asesoría y acompañamiento a las comunidades; actividades de fortalecimiento de entornos, incluyendo monitoreo y análisis de protección, protección por incidencia, y fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de coordinación de protección. Las actividades incluyen también intervención en contextos de emergencias como desplazamientos masivos, confinamientos, desastres naturales e incluyen evaluación rápida de necesidades de protección, asistencias de protección inmediata, entrenamientos en protección para líderes y lideresas, campañas de comunicación y talleres de manejo de estrés durante emergencias. 
En línea con la Estrategia de Protección de NRC, y dentro del contexto de respuesta a las dinámicas del conflicto armado en Colombia , el programa de protección se enfocará en personas afectadas por violencia, coerción y deprivación deliberadas con un énfasis particular en líderes y lideresas comunitarias, sociales y ambientalistas; comunidades expuestas a riesgos de protección como desplazamiento forzado, restricción de movilidad, confinamientos, amenazas, homicidios, violencia física y psicológica; individuos sobrevivientes o en riesgo de violencia, abuso, explotación, deprivación. 
Las intervenciones de protección contra violencia se priorizarán para los grupos más vulnerables como líderes/as sociales y defensores de derechos humanos, miembros de comunidades rurales, comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas, mujeres, comunidad LGBTQI+ y personas refugiadas y migrantes. 
Con respecto a la respuesta por parte de ICLA, las personas desplazadas internas recibirán gestión de casos legales a través de la información, orientación y asistencia legal para acceso al registro de víctimas, acceso a derechos y servicios esenciales como educación y salud, acceso a identidad legal y regularización migratoria en el caso de las personas refugiadas y migrantes afectadas por el conflicto armado, acceso a derechos de vivienda tierra y propiedad y acceso a derechos de empleo. Esto a través de los servicios implementados en territorio a través del Contact Centre, atención en oficinas, espacios protectores, clínicas móviles y actividades de intervención con enfoque comunitario. Adicional, facilitaremos asistencia técnica y capacitación a entidades públicas y otras organizaciones, para el fortalecimiento integral en el territorio.

project_name: Renforcer les interventions de prévention, d’atténuation des risques et de réponse à la violence basée sur le genre dans les six régions humanitaires du Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer les services qui sauvent les vies des survivantes, des femmes et des filles à risques de VBG par l’adaptation et le renforcement de la disponibilité et de la qualité des services, de prévention et      de mitigation des risques. Les survivantes de violence basée sur le genre auront accès à des soins de santé adaptés, y compris des services de santé pour les survivantes de violences sexuelles et conjugales et d’autres formes de VBG. Des services d’orientation pour prévenir et/ou réduire les effets de la violence seront fournis par les prestataires de santé. Cela se fera à travers une bonne coordination et un soutien à la continuité de l’offre des services de santé de prise en charge des violences sexuelles et les autres formes de VBG. A cet effet, en collaboration avec les districts sanitaires des 6 régions ciblées par le projet, un paquet d’activités sera déroulé afin de fournir une prise en charge de qualité aux survivantes de VBG. Des kits post viol seront mis à la disposition des districts sanitaires des localités cibles du projet pour répartition dans les Centres de Santé de Promotion Sociale (CSPS), des centres intégrés de prise en charge (One Stop Center) et des cliniques mobiles afin de garantir l’accès aux kits à toutes les survivantes. Le soutien psychosocial étant une étape primordiale dans la prise en charge des cas de VBG, ce service sera intégré à l’offre de service médical par la mise à disposition des centres de santé des travailleurs sociaux, préalablement formés sur le soutien psychosocial, y compris la gestion des cas de VBG. Ces travailleurs sociaux bénéficieront de matériels permettant la mise en œuvre de la gestion des cas de VBG à distance. Le projet préconise et soutient l’intégration de l’atténuation des risques de violence basée sur le genre. Le numéro vert de dénonciation des cas de VBG (80 00 12 87) et d’orientation des survivantes vers les services de prise en charge sera renforcé. Les agents de la ligne verte seront formés sur la prise en charge des cas d’abus et d’exploitation sexuels.  Des stratégies communautaires seront développées pour surveiller en toute sécurité et combattre les risques liés à la VBG et inscrire une tolérance zéro à l’exploitation et aux abus sexuels et leur dénonciation dans les messages communautaires de sensibilisation. A cet effet, des messages clés sur la prévention et la mitigation des risques de VBG y compris la Prévention contre l’Exploitation et l’Abus Sexuels seront conçus avec l’implication et la participation des bénéficiaires et diffusés régulièrement au sein de la communauté. Pour permettre aux femmes et aux filles de préserver leur dignité, des lampes et kits de dignité leur seront distribués dans les zones d’intervention du projet.
Des espaces sûrs à l’usage des femmes et des filles seront installés dans les sites d’accueil temporaire et au sein de la population hôte, afin que les survivantes de VBG, les femmes et les filles à risque puissent accéder en toute sécurité à l’information et à l’orientation vers les services de prise en charge. Les bénéficiaires de ces espaces bénéficieront également d’activités de soutien psychosocial qui favorisent la solidarité et le soutien communautaire. Des groupes de parole et des activités de promotion de leadership seront organisés régulièrement dans ces espaces, ainsi que des activités d’apprentissage artisanal et récréatives.  Le projet, dans sa mise en œuvre, s’appuie sur la capacité communautaire pour prévenir la VBG. Les groupements de femmes seront formés sur les VBG y compris la protection contre l’exploitation et l’abus sexuels et la Violence Infligée par le Partenaire Intime (VPI). Ces groupements féminins auront pour tâche de sensibiliser la communauté sur les conséquences de la VBG, le mécanisme de référencement et les services disponibles.

project_name: Delivering life skills education that include comprehensive sexuality education elements for Rohingya adolescents and young people in the camps and host communities
project_objective:
Within the framework of the Education sector JRP for 2023, UNFPA will continue provision of Life Skills Education (LSE) programme, including Comprehensive Sexual Education (CSE), among Rohingya and host community adolescents and youth to ensure that they have knowledge and power to make informed choices about their bodies and lives in an environment where harmful social and gender norms such as gender-based violence (GBV) and early and forced child marriage, unwanted pregnancy, uncertainty about future still pose serious risks to their health and well-being. Guided by the International Technical Guidance on CSE, the project aims at delivering scientifically accurate, incremental, age and developmentally appropriate, curriculum-based CSE programmes as part of the Myanmar Curriculum (MC).    

The project is built on the “Gender Equality Movement in Schools (GEMS)” curriculum, which has been one of the successfully implemented flagship programmes of the Ministry of Education and UNFPA in Bangladesh.  The curriculum is contextualized into Burmese and covers all eight key concepts of the International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education focusing first on strengthening and motivating learners to explore values, attitudes, and norms concerning sexuality, before going on to address specific facts, knowledge, and skills. Edutainment technology based approaches such as games, short videos and cartoons on SRHR and gender equality will complement classroom sessions. This project will reach 10,000 Rohigya students (50% male and 50% female) under 18 enrolled in the MC in 250 community learning centers, will distribute MHM kits among the female students, and will build the capacity of the host and rohingya community teachers to deliver the GEMS sessions in learning centers.   
 
To reach adolescents and youth, and to reinforce internalization of knowledge and positive gender norms among adolescents, UNFPA will establish 3 more adolescent and youth centers in three different camps and will continue to provide its two flagship interventions that target adolescent boys and girls from Rohingya and host communities in community and multipurpose spaces, including 7 established adolescent and youth centers. 

Girl targeted education programme - Girls shine- aims at empowering girls, 7,500 in the Rohingya camps and 2,500 in the host community, to acquire skills and knowledge to identify different types of GBV and seek support services if they experience or are at risk of SGBV. Moreover, the Girls Shine programme includes sessions on bodily autonomy, gender equality, MHPSS, SRHR, menstrual health, and promotes positive social and emotional skills, awareness of existing GBV response and case management services. Through this particular intervention as well MHM kits will be distributed among the female students. 

The Champions of Change education programme- Boy specific intervention- aims at creating safe space for adolescent boys and young men, 7,500 in the Rohingya camps and 2,500 in the host community, to reflect on what it means to be a man and encourages them to redefine masculinity and to be more supportive, inclusive, compassionate members of the community. 

Capacity building and awarenss are also important part of this project in which sessions for male and female caregivers, community leaders will be provided to challenge existing harmful gender norms and practices such as SGBV and early and forced child marriage. As such, besides Parents/Caregivers meetings, UNFPA will continue implementing structured, community-level sessions for caregivers, community leaders and community members and volunteers  to complement awareness building activities both in the camps and immediate host communities.  

Coordination and advocacy are important elements of this project by which UNFPA aims at building the capacity of partners of the Youth Working Group to advocate for youth sensitive data and programmes across the Rohingya response.

project_name: Garantizar la supervivencia de niñas y niños con desnutrición aguda a través de identificación y tratamiento oportunos y cuidado nutricional y de salud integral materno infantil en Alta Verapaz y San Marcos, Guatemala
project_objective:
Los desastres naturales recientemente vividos en el área de Alta Verapaz y San Marcos (tormentas e inundaciones) incluyendo secuelas de la pandemia de COVID (aún no resueltos) y de la Guerra de Ucrania (actualmente), se ha visto reflejada en el aumento de la inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional en el área.  A pesar de que el total de niñas y niños con desnutrición aguda reportados ha disminuido en 2022 comparado a 2021 (probablemente por la falta de identificación), el porcentaje de desnutrición aguda severa ha aumentado considerablemente hasta 25% y 29% de los casos de desnutrición en Alta Verapaz y San Marcos, respectivamente.  Esta situación es sumamente preocupante porque aumenta asimismo el riesgo de muerte por esta causa. Se implementarán acciones integrales de atención nutricional y salud a través de “brigadas integrales” que llegan hasta las comunidades más lejanas y rurales, donde la presencia de salud es muy limitada.  La pertinencia de esta Estrategia ha sido validada y ha probado ser efectiva desde 2018 en contexto de emergencias.  La Estrategia ha sido tan efectiva que ha logrado identificar y tratar oportunamente a niñas y niños afectados por desnutrición aguda que no habían sido detectados previamente por salud (hasta un 68%). Es un abordaje estandarizado y monitoreado que ha sido mejorado y complementado hasta que el día de hoy brindan atención integral a la niñez  (evaluación nutricional, tratamiento oportuno, suplementación con micronutrientes múltiples en polvo, zinc y vitamina A, desparasitación, consejería alrededor de los temas de la Ventana de los 1,000 días y vacunación) y a las mujeres en edad fértil incluyendo adolescentes, embarazadas y en período de lactancia (evaluación nutricional, suplementación con hierro y ácido fólico, vacunación y consejería).  Estas brigadas adicionalmente dejan formados “agentes de cambio” (líderes y lideresas formados en aspectos básicos para identificación oportuna de desnutrición aguda, signos de peligro, y alimentación infantil e higiene) para orientar a su comunidad.
El proyecto responde a los siguientes objetivos:

•	Identificar la población afectada por desnutrición aguda y brindar tratamiento inmediato
para salvar sus vidas.
•	Mejorar las competencias del personal de salud y otros actores locales para la atención
nutricional en emergencias
•	Brindar insumos necesarios para el cuidado nutricional
•	Fortalecer capacidades de líderes y lideresas comunitarias en la preparación y respuesta para la atención nutricional en emergencias
•	Activar sistemas de alerta temprana nutricional en la comunidad

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria con abordaje de triple nexo e inclusión para recuperar condiciones de WASH en familias vulnerables afectadas por eventos climáticos en cinco municipios de Alta Verapaz.
project_objective:
UNICEF enfocará la respuesta en 5 municipios de Alta Verapaz en donde los sistemas de agua están afectados por los huracanes Eta e Iota, así como Julia en 2022 y que, por ser un área de alta incidencia de desnutrición aguda, atenderá a 77,289 personas vulnerables en áreas rurales. La información de base del HNO, INFORM (2022) y otras fuentes de información como la línea de base de la Gran Cruzada Nacional por la Nutrición, evidencian la severidad de la situación.  Se coordinará y complementará esfuerzos y actividades a nivel departamental y municipal con diferentes instancias como la Coordinadora Nacional para la Reducción de Desastres (CONRED), Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MSPAS) y otras instancias representadas en Alta Verapaz.
La intervención se implementará en coordinación con las municipalidades y MSPAS, con el enfoque del triple nexo, pues se busca mejorar sus capacidades de respuesta a emergencia y resiliencia para vincularse al desarrollo con sistemas de información pertinentes y oportunos en cuanto a WASH se refiere.

project_name: Sustaining the continuation of essential lifesaving sexual and reproductive health services for women, girls, boys and men in Area C, and H2 area in the West Bank.
project_objective:
This project aims to improve access to Primary Health Care with a specific focus on provision of integrated sexual and reproductive health services (SRH) in area C of the West Bank to ensure lifesaving care for especially women and children in the most vulnerable and remote communities. The selected target locations of this project proposal are the same locations that UNFPA/PMRS currently working on however the current project will be completed by Dec 31st 2022. To anticipate and avoid any gap in the service provision in these locations after Dec 2022 this project aims as well to continue the services in these locations. 
  This will be achieved through the following main activities:
1. Provision of health services that are needed due to the humanitarian crisis by
supporting Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMR) to run primary health care level 2 mobile clinics including provision of SRH services for women, girls, young people including people with disabilities.
2. Strengthening the capacity of SRH providers in the targeted locations on GBV detection and referral, and training on SRH issues including Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) to sustain vital SRH services during emergencies.
3. Enhance accessibility of PHC and SRH services for persons with disabilities.
4. Community outreach on essential SRH i.e. danger signs in pregnancy, family planning, etc. Beside other public health issues, and NCDs with particular focus on breast Cancer BC.

project_name: Empowering women and adolescent girls in the Rohingya refugee camps and host community through livelihoods and skills development support
project_objective:
This project aims to build the resilience of Rohingya and Host Community women, adolescent girls, women with a disability, and transgender (Hijra) through increased livelihood skills and access to livelihood opportunities, including start-up support and support to establishing market linkages. 
UN Women has five Multi-Purpose Women's Centers (MPWCs) in camps 3, 4, 4-Extension, 5, and 18; and three MPWCs in host communities in Ukhia, Teknaf, and Cox's Bazar Sadar. Through these centers, women and girls including gender diverse population can access tailored multi-sectoral services that consider their specific needs and challenges, with a focus on women’s empowerment to build resilience and strengthen women’s role and leadership in their communities. The project has a separate programme for the transgender (hijra) community in the camp.
Activities provided through these centers encompass 1) those that promote the empowerment of women and girls, building their resilience through livelihood and skills development activities; and 2) activities that respond to and mitigate risks of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), inclusive of psychosocial support, case management and referral services for GBV survivors, alongside 1st aid medical assistance, SRH services and awareness-raising sessions on women’s rights issues. The current project is focused on the former (1) activities, with specific attention placed on ensuring the inclusion of the most marginalized women and girls in the project’s activities, including women and girls from female-headed households, women with disabilities, and gender-diverse persons in the MPWCs. 
Through the project, skills development training ranging in length from one to six months will be provided in the MPWCs to Rohingya and host community women. The training will focus on handicrafts, beauty parlors, tailoring, production of masks and reusable sanitary napkins, as well as eco-friendly jute products. At the end of the training, the skills of the participants will be tested. Upon the successful completion of the test, the participants will receive certificates. If the participant is found unsuccessful, they will be provided the opportunity to continue attending the training. UN Women will also be liaising with the sector on the standard training modules and provision of the certificates. 
Following the training, beneficiaries will be supported to continue their own businesses through the provision of in-kind grants comprising specific materials from the training and other start-up kits, and support to set up shop and access the market through the Women's Market in Camp 5 as well as three dedicated women’s café and display corners set up in camp 4, 4-Ext. and in the Women's Market in camp 5, facilitating private sector engagement and contributing to social cohesion, as the women vendors will be from both Rohingya and the host community. UN Women will provide the shopkeepers with a monthly incentive in kind/cash for coming to the market and running their business, alongside which the women can collect orders from the community and do home delivery. Project activities will include basic entrepreneurship skills development training for the women for setting up their businesses. 
In Camp 5, the Women's Market will continue to serve as a hub for women producers supported by also other partners such as AAB, DCA, FAO, HIS, PRANTIC, SNKSS, UNDP, and WFP.
Linkages to the local and national market and private sector will be strengthened by the Women Entrepreneur Association of Bangladesh (WEAB), a Women Peace and Humanitarian Fund grantee. In addition, the implementing partners (Oxfam, ActionAid Bangladesh, and BRAC) will sell the products through their national-level outlets. Also, UN Women will explore opportunities for conducting a market assessment and will engage with the ISCG for the planned market survey.

project_name: Enhancing coordination to support the Early Recovery and Livelihood Response
project_objective:
Opportunities and needs for improved Early Recovery intervention on the ground are growing. This necessitates additional efforts to improve collaboration at the national and sub-national levels by allocating human resources to help the growing membership of the Early Recovery Sector in undertaking comprehensive Early Recovery assessment and planning as well as ensuring successful coordination in sector partners’ collective response. Furthermore, given the wide range of Early Recovery initiatives across many line ministries and the sectors they serve, it is critical to continue advocate for the early recovery approach within the local administrations, at the relevant decision-making and operational levels to ensure continuous knowledge exchange on assessed needs and objectives, as well as to expedite clearances needed for implementation.
The ERL sector has built this sector coordination and interface capacity in the governorates where UN hubs are currently located. Furthermore, coordination for cross-border ERL activities has been established at the Syria-wide level. Coordination at the field level proved critical in bringing the ERL partners under one umbrella to improve context-sensitive early recovery efforts on the ground, prevent duplication and discrepancies, and achieve synergies in interventions.

project_name: Conditional Cash Assistance to Persons with Severe Disabilities
project_objective:
While many components of the Syrian society suffer from the repercussions of the crisis, the category of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and their families is among the most affected. Despite the efforts of multiple governmental and non-governmental organizations to respond to the needs of persons with disabilities, available resources –whether human or financial – are unable to cover the needs during the current time and the near future. In addition to these challenges, there are cases of persons with severe disabilities who severely suffer from lack of access to services – whether basic or medically rehabilitative – not to mention economic and social support services, considered currently a difficult goal to attain under the current situation.
Moreover, the cases of persons with severe disabilities present one of the greatest challenges as they suffer from higher mortality rate and deeply depressed socioeconomic situation.
Within the situation of limited resources and capacities to respond to the needs of persons with severe disabilities, cash-based intervention represents an effective mean to fill the gap and provide important support to persons with severe disabilities and their families.
The suggested project aims to achieve the following main objectives:
1. Improve the protection of persons with severe disabilities through individual targeted protection interventions (conditional cash assistance).
2. Strengthening the resilience of the families of persons with severe disabilities by preserving the financial, material and human assets within the family.
Based on the amount requested, the project could target approximately 500 PWDs.
The criteria for targeting beneficiaries is mainly based on the severity of the disability they live with, in addition to the socioeconomic vulnerability of the household.
UNDP has experienced implementing similar project in the governorate of Aleppo where it targeted 500 persons with severe disabilities namely spinal cord injuries with cash assistance for 6 months in the amount of 155$ per month. The cash assistance was conditioned to following a rehabilitation treatment Programme designed by specialist individually for each beneficiary. The project was also coupled with a graduation model to support one household member to secure job opportunity to further support the resilience of the whole households of the persons the severe disabilities. UNDP has benefitted from this experience and collected lessons learnt that fed in the developed model. This model of the project is able to be replicated in other governorates especially the ones most affected by the war

project_name: Enhancing the Resilience of Syrian Population through Economic Development and Livelihoods Support
project_objective:
The main objective of this project  is to strengthen the interface between humanitarian action and sustainable livelihoods and economic recovery  while building the resilience and self-reliance of vulnerable communities in Syria and delivering sustainable and integrated interventions. The proposed four main areas of interventions will be as follows:
a) Rural Economic Recovery through Rural-based Sustainable Livelihoods; b) Inclusive and sustainable Micro-Small and Medium Enterprises recovery and development; c) Market-driven vocational and skills training and employment services; and finally d) Sustainable job creation for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) provided  with physical support.
Under the first component, UNDP aims to support sustainable and climate smart agricultural livelihoods through supporting community-based sustainable agricultural activities, developing value chains on key commodities, supporting new innovative business ideas for rural areas, and the establishment and management of cooperatives, farmers’ markets and rural development centres targeting a total of 150 men and women. Under the second component, UNDP aims to support both start-up, recovery  and acceleration of new and existing MSMEs, targeting 600 men and women. Support will include entrepreneurship training and start-up support, recovery  support, and acceleration support with advance business training, access to inclusive   finance and access to market. Under the third component, UNDP aims to result in job creation beyond  provision of vocational and skills training through providing employment services such as job matching, targeting 100 men and women through OJT and 70 men and women will be supported to be specialized trainers, coaches and mentors. In addition to provision of soft skill training, career counseling and internship opportunities to 100 youth at higher education and graduates, and provision of support to 35 graduation projects to be start-up microbusinesses. Finally, under the forth component, UNDP aims to continue supporting PWDs with both physical rehabilitation and socioeconomic inclusion of PWDs; moreover, prosthetic services will be provided  through already  established prosthetic workshops for physical rehabilitation of which support will enable PWDs to be ready to access to job opportunities. Activities will include support of existing three workshops for continued and expanded services, in addition to selecting 234 PWDs with lower limb amputation and
support the to provide lower limb prosthetic devices and other rehabilitation treatment to selected beneficiaries, and providing them  with sustainable livelihoods opportunities. Types of livelihoods support will be identified based on the feasibilities of PWDs and also
market and livelihoods conditions in targeted areas.

project_name: Protection risk response, prevention, and mitigation amongst conflict- and displacement-affected communities in Syria
project_objective:
Through community-based and individually targeted protection interventions delivered at the community centres, DRC will seek to address the protection needs and improve the well-being, self-protection, and resilience of vulnerable women, girls, men, and boys.
DRC will target 4500 beneficiaries throughout interventions in the targeted locations. DRC will provide psychosocial support (PSS) to children, youth, and adult caregivers through structured sustained, and unstructured PSS for children, parenting sessions for caregiver activities at the community centres. 
DRC’s PSS programs are tailored to different age and gender-related needs and experiences of beneficiaries and aim for equal participation of girls and boys. DRC will conduct structured PSS following DRC’s Under the Rainbow and Youth Program courses with vulnerable children and adolescents to develop their ability to process emotions and express themselves, increase feelings of self-worth and self-confidence, and positively interact with other children, parents, and wider social networks. DRC’s PSS programs are tailored to different needs and experiences of children (6-12 years) and adolescents (13-18 years) and aim for equal participation of girls and boys. In parallel, PSS sessions will be conducted with adult caregivers on stress management and positive and nurturing parenting. Structured PSS will be complemented by unstructured activities such as recreational activities, workshops, and social events around specific themes which will be chosen based on the needs and feedback expressed by the children, youth, and adults who visit the CC. In addition, young people who are interested and committed to coming together and forming a youth committee will be supported to implement community-based initiatives which will be identified by the youth themselves upon reflection on the protection risks that are most prevalent in their communities. The ultimate goal of the CBI would be to contribute to reducing exposure of children and youth to certain protection risks. Unstructured PSS and CBI will also contribute to enhancing the community's social fabric and social cohesion through interaction and dialogue; these activities will also facilitate community engagement and empower the youth to become active and responsible community members.
 DRC will provide protection case management services, including individual protection assistance and referral to relevant services, to persons with specific needs (including older women and men, and people with disability) in order to address, and RE. Beneficiaries provided with case management support will likely be at high risk of multiple intersecting protection concerns, due to experience of trauma. Case management and structured PSS – provided at community centres are designed to respond to a different but equally urgent set of individual needs.  
DRC will implement Explosive Ordnance Risk Education activities addressing the threat posed by the presence of EO for 7000 individuals, which is a designated priority for Humanitarian Mine Action interventions. DRC RE awareness-raising sessions will be participatory and educational sessions lasting between 40-90 minutes for groups of 5-25 participants, with the help of audio and visual aid to improve recognition of EO identification of risk indicators and factors and safe behaviors. Sessions will be provided to both adults and children, using age and gender-sensitive methodologies. DRC will also provide contractors engaged in construction works with RE sessions to ensure they have the knowledge and tools to recognize an explosive threat and act safely in hazardous situations.

project_name: Protection and Integrated Assistance for Ethiopian and South Sudanese Refugees and Vulnerable Host Communities in White Nile, Al Jazirah, Gedaref, South Kordofan, and Khartoum.
project_objective:
The country refugee response plan for 2023 integrates multiple programmatic sectors. The LFS response will provide cash-based food assistance to both new and protracted displacement situations, specifically targeting households that have no meaningful access to sustainable form of livelihood. Communities will be consulted on the most suitable livelihood activities to be supported by the programme. The Food Security component, whenever possible, will be delivered through a market-based approach, either through cash or vouchers ensuring adequate survey and understanding of the local context, markets, and traders.

The legal protection action will aim to address the limited access to legal identity including civil documentation for the most vulnerable refugees and support Ethiopian refugees in Gedaref by facilitating access to essential services and promoting social cohesion through collaborative dispute resolution. The project will provide information, counselling and legal assistance, integrated capacity building and collaborative dispute resolution to achieve this. NRC will further include employment law and procedures response and a new thematic area - legal stay, residency, and other protection mechanisms response.

The WASH response will ensure that the most vulnerable refugees have access to safe drinking water and sanitation through household level interventions, support water safety plans from the distribution points up to the point of use and provide family shared emergency latrines and vector control interventions. The response will further upgrade/ expand small-scale water infrastructures for both host community and refugees, increase the water supply, and improve the water quality. Market-based approach will be utilised to effectively meet people’s WASH needs.

The shelter action will undertake the provision of adequate shelters and NFI for refugees, rehabilitation/repairs of existing transitional shelters to ensure minimum protection against the elements, and replenish and/or issue essential NFI kits. The response will provide additional support to the establishment of communal infrastructures as well as site settlements across the three Ethiopian refugee camps – Um Rakuba, Tunaydbah, and Babkiri.

The EiE intervention and support will focus on enabling refugee and vulnerable host community boys and girls of school age to gain access to timely, safe, and quality education through addressing multiple barriers preventing their education. Structural upgrades, rehabilitation of schools, WASH facilities and distribution of essential hygiene supplies and teaching and learning materials will be a key component. NRC will also provide a classroom-based psycho-social support and wellbeing programming for children.

NRC will continue to use its Digital Communication Hub (DCH) which serves as a two-way communication platform with people of concern. Information distributed through the platform will include life-saving and life improving awareness-raising messages as well as information on how to access services. Similarly, people of concern will be able to ask questions, communicate their needs and obtain referrals for services, and voice complaints or feedback via the hub.

The project will also assist the most vulnerable refugee households to meet their basic needs through multi-purpose cash assistance. A market assessment and cash feasibility exercise will be undertaken before any proposed cash intervention.

NRC will also undertake advocacy interventions for refugees right and protection issues, particularly around freedom of movement, right to access essential services, registration and non-refoulement. 

The response will target the most vulnerable refugees living in camps, camp-like, out-of-camp and urban settings in White Nile, Gedaref, South Kordofan, Al Jazirah, and Khartoum. Beneficiary targeting will be undertaken by applying socio-economic vulnerability criteria.

project_name: Outreach emergency health units serving Palestine refugees in the West Bank
project_objective:
In light of the deteriorating security conditions in the West Bank with daily ISF operations, lockdowns and closures, this proposed intervention aims to support the provision of critical primary healthcare needs for Palestine refugees in the West Bank while alleviating the pressure on public health system, through: 

1) ensuring access to primary health services for refugees in emergency situations due to closures, lockdowns or natural disasters. 2) providing life-saving medicines especially for NCD patients, 3) hiring and training surge staff to cope with increasing needs, 4) visiting vulnerable patients, 5) enhancing health response capabilities in situations of emergency,  6) providing mental health and psychosocial support especially to women, vulnerable groups, people affected by the hostilities and staff; 7) strengthening the capacity of current staff respond to emergency situations; 8) equipping UNRWA health centers to better respond in emergency situations; 9) RCCE.

project_name: Emergency Cash Assistance for Abject Poor Palestine Refugees in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem
project_objective:
In 2023, UNRWA will seek to provide unconditional and non-restricted cash assistance to 3,198 abject poor Palestine refugee households (approx. 20,509 individuals) in the West Bank through the e-card modality, to support them with covering their basic food needs and restoring their coping capacities. This project contributes to: 
•	Strategic Objective 3 “The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”, as well as to 
•	Food Security Cluster Objective “Households suffering from limited access to food and to income opportunities are able to meet their basic food needs”. 
Distribution will be complemented by consultations with beneficiaries and awareness raising on PSEA and complaint mechanisms.

project_name: Safeguarding Education in Emergencies for vulnerable Palestine refugee children in the West Bank including East Jerusalem
project_objective:
The proposed intervention will safeguard quality, equitable and inclusive basic education for vulnerable, school-aged, Palestine refugee children in the West Bank and East Jerusalem.  Through this project 20,560 students (9,853 boys and 10,707 girls)  will continue to learn and to benefit from having access to quality education in a context of increased violence as a result of the protracted crisis and continued military occupation. This intervention targets 42 UNRWA schools that are affected by frequent military incursions, clashes and settler violence and are located at high-risk areas namely East Jerusalem, Hebron H2, Area C, as well as UNRWA schools that are currently affected by the increased deteriorating situation in Nablus and Jenin.
This intervention will aim to increase safe access and provide psychosocial support for 20,560 vulnerable refugee students and 783 teachers, in addition to other non-teaching staff. Activities aim to support UNRWA school staff and students who are affected by the education-related violations to enjoy a protective environment as well as to assist children and school staff in vulnerable schools in preparing and responding to emergencies. 
UNRWA will work to scaling up the scope of its ongoing core interventions in response to the emergency situation in the West Bank, both in terms of increasing target groups and increasing the frequency of interventions, such as providing recreational activities in camp schools, as well as proposing other new activities to respond more in-depth to this situation, and to the needs of schools identified by the needs assessment under this emergency situation, an example of which is the protective presence - gatekeepers in the school.

Finally, this intervention also aims to improve the confidentiality, safety and accessibility of complaints mechanisms, including complaints of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). The project provides multiple child-friendly channels to receive and respond to complaints which are adapted to the target population. UNRWA has developed ad hoc SoPs on the management of cases of SEA which abide to CBCM SoPs. Complaints of SEA will be handled by PSEA focal points who will ensure a survivor centered approach in how the complaint is handled and support is offered to the survivor. UNRWA West Bank
Field Office works closely with the PSEA Network and will undertake compulsory reporting and external referrals.

project_name: Provision of essential primary health care to remote and vulnerable communities of Palestine refugees in the West Bank (Mobile Health Teams)
project_objective:
The Mobile Health Teams project seeks to improve accessibility to essential primary health services for 
28 remote Palestine refugee communities in Area C who are facing access restrictions to health services 
due to Israel's restrictive planning system.
Through the deployment of three Mobile Heath Teams, UNRWA will provide essential health services while 
taking measures to ensure accessibility for people with disabilities and a strong emphasis on accessibility of SEA complaints mechanisms.

project_name: Mine Action in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
The HALO Trust will continue to deliver an integrated Mine Action approach in northwest Syria involving Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD), mechanical clearance and Victim Assistance (VA).

HALO will provide EORE to men, women, boys and girls, with a focus on community members most at risk of accidents (including children, teenagers, IDPs, agricultural workers and rubble removal workers). HALO will also continue delivering ‘Training of Trainer’ (ToT) workshops to NGO workers and Community Focal Points to improve the relevance, integration and reach of EORE messaging across all communities and relevant humanitarian sectors. 

Following the completion in 2020 of HALO's contamination impact survey work in all accessible communities in NW Syria, capturing the scope of explosive ordnance (EO) contamination in the region, in 2022 HALO started conducting detailed non-technical survey (NTS) to define precisely the types of hazards and technical requirements for disposal. NTS will continue in 2023 and provide local authorities, humanitarian actors, the Gaziantep cluster network, and the donor community with a greater understanding of EO threats, including specific locations.

HALO’s NTS work enabled the training, equipping and deployment of a disposal capacity to reduce the presence and impact of EO in highly vulnerable communities in a part of the country where HALO is the only INGO able to provide these highly specialised services supported by a sector-leading global EOD advisory team. HALO’s two mixed-gender EOD teams are currently destroying one explosive item per day. They are focusing on agricultural areas where the removal of explosive hazards not only contributes to casualty reduction but also boosts economic activity. In addition to the deployment of the EOD capacity, HALO will train and equip a mechanical demining team that will use an armoured excavator in early 2023. This will allow to safely tackle threats that are too dangerous or time-consuming for manual clearance.  

The support to survivors of EO accidents will continue through a Victim Assistance (VA) component. HALO will provide victim assistance case management services, providing referrals and transportation to specialised services for survivors of EO accidents.

HALO acknowledges the requirement to avoid activity duplication within the MASC as well as addressing gaps in providing EORE (to children, adults, CFPs, and NGO Focal Points), NTS and EOD. This will be achieved through ongoing and regular coordination with other members of the MASC to which HALO is co-chair, as well as engagement with local authorities, communities, and other NGOs throughout the implementation of the project.

project_name: Provision of WASH services in Eastern Equatoria, Central Equitoria, Western Equatoria,  Jonglei, Upper Nile States, and hard-to-reach areas
project_objective:
According to the South Sudan HNO 2022, it is estimated that 6.1 million people will be impacted by inadequate or lack of access to safe water and improved sanitation. Presently, only 39% of the total population of South Sudan have reported to meet their water needs – a figure which drops to 34% in rural areas. Statistics which are expected to significantly impact standards of living and wellbeing. 
In line with the exacerbated WASH needs with the COVID-19 pandemic, ACTED will implement a variety of WASH activities in 2022 including WASH infrastructure and rehabilitation, hygiene promotion activities, and supporting communities in prevention against diseases such as COVID-19 and Ebola. The response will be in line with the following cluster objectives:
CO 2: Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties
CO 3: WASH specific activities for GBV mitigation
CO 4: Community members exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures and infrastructure

project_name: Facilitating access to protection and justice services, and information services on protection and HLP for recovery of at-risk displacement and conflict-affected  people in Mayendit, Panyijiar and Juba Rejaf in South Sudan
project_objective: The proposed project in Unity State and Juba is designed to provide protection services through strengthening the protection capacity and resilience of the most vulnerable individuals in targeted communities of Mayendit, Panyijiar and Juba (Rejaf) of South Sudan. The project will have a 60% protection mitigation and response component and a 40% access to justice and HLP rights component. The protection concerns of the communities across South Sudan and specifically in areas where there is little to no permanent protection actors remain high. Communal violence, including cyclical revenge killing, tribal conflict, and cattle-related violence, have continued across the country, fueled by negative coping mechanisms resulting from multi-generational trauma and militarized community response structures. Repeated shocks have weakened individual and household capacity and community-based structures plus consistent services. Government continue to exhibit and perpetuate a weak system that compels the civil society to fill that gap so as to address protection and HLP needs of people in need. In light of that, durable remains a pipe dream for displaced and conflict affected people in Mayendit, Panyijiar and Juba Rejaf. Through an integrated protection and lifesaving support mechanisms (collaborating with IRC WPE, CP, ERD, Health and Nutrition actions coupled with interventions by other actors plus linking with service provider alliances from the government), this action intends to provide protection mitigation and response activities including responsive protection, return/ post return and HLP monitoring, comprehensive protection case management, targetted individual assistance including emergency cash assistance to the most vulnerable groups of people, legal counseling and assistance (coining a fine nexus with HLP support activities and referrals from WPE and CP), two-way communication and information system (linking with and integrating risk communication services), incident profiling and reporting, and provide a platform for discourse on HLP and durable solutions. This activity will be complemented through the strengthening of community-based protection networks plus establishing a community of paralegals that will assist in the identification of vulnerable beneficiaries and the provision of support provided to individuals with protection, legal and HLP concerns in their communities. Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights is becoming one of the most critical issues for IDPs, and returnees in Panyijiar, Mayendit and Juba (including host of displaced communities). As such this action will promote community-based monitoring of HLP issues, establish HLP trends to inform response and advocacy, raise awareness on HLPs and build the capacity of duty bearers at county level and community level on their role and need to prioritize HLP concerns as human rights issues. IRC will deploy a roving legal protection team to support access to justice and HLP programming. In Panyijiar and Juba, IRC will scale up its protection and rule of law activities that empower communities to influence their recovery and protection - placing the centrality of protection across all the activities, and taking into account conflict sensitivity aspects. Protection activities will be conducted through static and mobile teams in Mayendit and Panyijiar. The action will also endeavor to create links between protection actors and peace committees in the target locations to implement peace building activities.

project_name: Upscaling Child Protection in Emergencies interventions in Eastern Equatoria and Jonglei States in South Sudan
project_objective:
Following the Humanitarian Needs Assessments and joint other crisis and location specific assessments conducted in the 2021/2022, 2.7 million people in South Sudan are still in need of humanitarian assistance with Kapoeta South, Akobo and Bor South rating with severe and high-risk child protection concerns; child labor, forced early marriage, unaccompanied and separated children, and distress are some of the issues that have also been exacerbated by the multiple crises of floods and protracted displacement that comes with it, food insecurity and inter-communal violence/conflict which put children at risks of abuse, violence and exploitation; the HNO emphasizes the growing child protection concerns with current services not able to cover the gap. In Kapoeta South for instance, there is less coverage of child protection agencies with a high levels of child marriage and child labor attributed to their cattle-keeping lifestyle and passion for livestock. Scenarios in Akobo which is complex after the floods in 2021 and inter-communal conflict, cattle-raiding, abductions and protracted forced displacements causing distress among children and their families.
A comprehensive Child-focused, community-based Child Protection project targeting these three less-served counties; Kapoeta South in Eastern Equatoria and Akobo (East and West) and Bor South in Jonglei states is quite imperative. 
The project will reach 35,000 individuals including persons with disabilities, with standard child protection interventions implemented through needs and evidence-based strategies of non-focused and focused level - 1 MHPSS activities for children and their families in a structured program; The Healing and Education through the Arts (HEART) program, is an arts-based approach to providing psychosocial support for children using expressive arts to help children – in schools, child friendly spaces, youth centers and other structured settings, individual support to extremely vulnerable children and children survivors of abuse, neglect and exploitation through comprehensive child protection case management to, strengthening community-based and community-led child protection systems by establishing and strengthening CBCPNs (Community-Based Child Protection Networks), mass awareness-raising on pertinent child protection concerns and services, community dialogues and establishment of child help desks for monitoring and reporting key child protection concerns as well as information-sharing, as prevention interventions against abuse, neglect and exploitation of crises-affected or extremely vulnerable children and their families in the target locations.  The project will also strive at improving quality of child protection services through capacity building of front-line staff from both child protection on CPIE concepts comprehensive case management, Alternative care for UASC, CPIMS+, roll-out of minimum standards for child protection in humanitarian action (CPMS 2019), centrality of protection and MHPSS/PFA as well as other other sector staff to enhance their participation and in child protection creating opportunities for integration for a more holistic response to children and their families affected by multi-faceted crises
Cognizant of coordination which is the first standard of minimum standards of child protection in humanitarian contexts, the project will support the gaps of child protection coordination at the state level through strengthening effectiveness for activities of the child protection working groups and CPAoR-specific action plans. The project will support advocacy initiatives through the members of CMTF, CPWG and UASC WG. Learning will be incorporated through a case management satisfactory survey to inform our case management system in South Sudan and re-contextualize the standard operation procedures. An advocacy initiative to trigger government accountability will be implemented.

project_name: Improved Access to WASH Services for Palestine Refugees in Syria
project_objective:
Extensive damage to Syria's water networks and sewerage infrastructure during the conflict has resulted in restricted access to safe water supplies. This has affected domestic and personal hygiene and increased the burden on women (who are usually responsible for the family's household water use and hygiene). 
The lack of safe water increases the risk of water-borne diseases and is a potential public health hazard. Providing adequate environmental health services in Palestine refugee camps to mitigate the risks of disease has become even more critical, as evidenced during the recent cholera outbreak, reportedly affecting all 14 governorates in Syria. Between 25 August and 8 October 2022, 15,823 suspected cases of cholera were reported, including amongst Palestine refugees, resulting in 68 deaths. 
In 2023, SFO will undertake a self-assessment of all its operations to identify actions that could be made more environmentally sustainable. Recommendations will be used as a blueprint for implementing various actions to improve environmental sustainability, including under the EA. The Agency-wide Environmental and Social Management Framework will also be applied/rolled out at the field level with technical support from UNRWA Headquarters (HQ). 
In 2023, UNRWA will continue to provide essential WASH services to the most vulnerable among Palestine refugees including WASH items (Hygiene kits, baby diapers) which will be identified and referred for assistance by the UNRWA Health Programme. Hygiene kits will be distributed to at least 5,190 refugees and will include baby kits/diapers (for 500 infants) and adult incontinence pads (for 3,000 older persons and persons with disabilities). 
Solid waste management and sanitation services will continue to be provided in Palestine refugee camps by UNRWA sanitation workers. The Agency will also conduct minor repairs and maintenance of water and sewerage networks and surface drainage systems in accessible refugee camps. Upgraded equipment, such as garbage compactors and water tankers, will be procured to improve the quality and efficiency of service provision in nine refugee camps. 
As part of its measures to prevent additional health hazards, UNRWA will recruit 27 additional sanitation workers and ensure that all sanitation workers continue to be equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE). UNRWA will continue disinfection campaigns and the sanitization of garbage collection points to support cleaner environments in the refugee camps, helping to prevent the spread of disease.
UNWRA's Emergency Appeal 2023 estimates to cover a total of 149, 769 vulnerable Palestinian refugees (including 71,889 Male  and 77,880 female) with an estimate 2,102,583 USD budget requirement for the planned WASH activities, out of which 100% of the funding needs to be secured.
