project_name: Flexible Mine Action response supporting emergency, recovery and resilience needs in South Sudan
project_objective:
DRC will deploy 2 highly mobile Multi-Task Teams (MTTs), to respond to urgent threats to physical safety, dignity, freedom of movement and access to humanitarian assistance within communities. Additionally, DRC will deploy 5 Teams focused on delivering Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) to conflict-affected communities to further mitigate risks of explosive hazards. The proposed project aims at:

•	Providing immediate lifesaving assistance to address the urgent protection needs of the most vulnerable (including women, children, elderly, disabled and survivors of ERW in conflict) in hard-to-reach areas.
•	Enhancing prevention and preparedness programming to mitigate risks and strengthen resilience
•	Enabling durable solutions for IDPs and other affected populations

Tasks that will support the humanitarian response in the country will be prioritized through the following key activities:

•	Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Technical Survey (TS) – NTS and will be conducted to target and prioritize clearance according to humanitarian need. Surveys will be conducted using a mixture of key informant interviews and household questionnaires held with the local population and authorities. NTS will determine the likely locations and density of ERW contamination in target locations, whilst assessing the impact of these hazards on vulnerable populations in any given location. TS (using detectors) will be used upon discovery of an area with a high concentration of explosive hazards.
•	Manual Mine Clearance (MMC) / Battle Area Clearance (BAC) - the MTTs will be able to act as a MMC / BAC capacity, performing static clearance activities across larger, clearly defined areas (identified through the above data collection activities and technical survey as appropriate).
•	Explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) – once NTS has determined the nature of the threat, technical capacities within the teams will be deployed to remove and destroy identified hazards.
•	Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) – all teams will contain a capacity to deliver risk messaging, toraise awareness about how to recognize dangerous items. as the risk education will emphasize safe practices that should be followed, and high risk behaviour that should be avoided in relation to mines and explosive remnants of war.

project_name: Projet d’insertion socio-économique des populations vulnérables (PISEV) des départements de Fouli et de Kaya dans la province du Lac
project_objective:
Dans le contexte de la grave crise sécuritaire sévissant dans la province du Lac Tchad, ayant conduit au déplacement de milliers de personnes, et afin de faciliter à l’insertion socio-économique des populations vulnérables de 12 sites d’intervention des départements de Kaya et Fouli, HI met en oeuvre, sur 15 mois, le projet PISEV, dont l’objectif général du projet est de contribuer à améliorer la couverture des besoins de base, le renforcement des moyens d’existence des populations déplacées et hôtes vulnérables dans la province du Lac et l’accroissement des opportunités économiques. Le projet articule son action autour de 2 résultats : 
• Résultat 1 : Les ménages déplacés et hôtes retenus ont amélioré leur régime alimentaire et augmenté leurs revenus par le biais des filets sociaux
• Résultat 2 : Les ménages déplacés et hôtes retenus affirment leur indépendance financière via les AGR et garantissent leur sécurité économique

Il s'agira dans ce projet d'assurer les besoins primaires des populations vulnérables à travers les filets sociaux mais aussi de les soutenir à développer des AGR afin qu'elles soient plus résilientes.

Les bénéficiaires du projet seront des ménages extrêmement pauvres et parents d’enfants bénéficiaires du projet PROSCOLAC qui seront sélectionnés selon l’approche Household Economy Approach (*). Au total 460 ménages bénéficiaires directs seront sélectionnés (ménages hôtes et déplacés), soit environ 2760 personnes bénéficiaires sur une estimation de 6 personnes par ménage, comprenant : 
-	10% de Personnes en Situation de Handicap (PSH), soit 276 personnes
-	47% d’hommes, soit 1297 hommes et 53% de femmes, soit 1463 femmes
En supposant que chaque personne qui bénéficiera de l’appui du projet fera profiter des bienfaits du projet à cinq (05) personnes (solidarité), le nombre de bénéficiaires indirects est estimé à 13800 personnes (amis, parents et voisins).

Forte des acquis des interventions passées, ce projet a pour but l'amélioration durable des conditions socio-économiques des populations hôtes et déplacées dans la province du Lac Tchad. Il contribuera à leur offrir de meilleures opportunités socio-économiques à moyen et long terme, et de fait, à améliorer leur régime alimentaire. Cette ambition s’inscrit dans la stratégie opérationnelle de HI au Tchad et s’inscrit dans une cohérence avec le projet d’éducation inclusive et d’urgence dans la province du Lac (PROSCOLAC, financé par ECHO), en permettant de soutenir en priorité les parents et familles les plus pauvres des enfants bénéficiaires de nos actions d’éducation inclusive par une approche communautaire participative, en s’appuyant sur les comités déjà existants (composés principalement des relais communautaires, des points focaux inclusion) et accompagnés par HI.

(*) Note : L’approche Household Economy Approach (HEA) se base sur la catégorisation socioéconomique d’une société dans une démarche participative et communautaire s’appuyant sur des critères et des perception clefs locaux en vue de classifier les ménages en quatre groupes selon leur statut socio-économique au sein du site ou du village (très pauvres, pauvres, moyens et nantis).

project_name: MPCA and Food Vouchers for the most vulnerable HHs in the Gaza Strip
project_objective:
The proposed project aims to improve the access of vulnerable and food-insecure households (HHs) to diversified food and to support their basic needs from further deterioration of living standards, as a result of the protracted crisis and socio-economic conditions. The project aligns with the HRP's second and third Country Strategic Objectives: “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”, and ”The capacity of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with and overcome the protracted crisis, including from environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued”. The project is also aligned with the Food Security Sector's (FSS) Specific Objective 2: ""Households suffering from limited access to food and income opportunities are able to meet their basic needs"", and to the MPCA's Specific Objective: “Vulnerable HHs in oPt affected by shocks and stresses due to conflict and natural disaster supported with MPCA are able to meet their immediate essential needs and access to lifesaving services, decreases the incidence of negative coping strategies”.
The project will target 500 vulnerable HHs (2,800 individuals; 736 Boys, 717 Girls, 683 Men, and 664 Women; among them 87 Elderly, and 56 Disabled) with high levels of food insecurity and those on the Ministry of Social Development's (MoSD) waiting list. Households with cancer patients needing urgent assistance as well as HHs with people with disabilities (PWDs) will be prioritized.
The project aims to reduce the immediate food gap by providing a bundle of food items through an e-voucher system (345 ILS/month) for six months, targeting 350 HHs (1,960 Individuals; 515 Boys, 502 Girls, 478 Men, 465 Women; among them, 55 Elderly, and 39 Disabled) with no or very limited access to food. In addition, the project seeks to support an additional 150 HHs (840 Individuals; 221 Boys, 215 Girls, 205 Men, and 199 Women; among them, 24 Elderly, and 17 Disabled) with unrestricted cash assistance. The target groups will be supported through MPCA (1,080 ILS/month) over the duration of four months to cover their basic needs (food, non-food, health, hygiene needs and other basic needs). The selected HHs will be those with the lowest PMTF scores and those with protection concerns. HHs selected for food vouchers will be those with severe and moderate food insecurity.  
The project, implemented in partnership with WEFAQ Society for Women and Child Care, will target Rafah governorate. Al Wefaq has extensive experience in the targeted localities, efficient capacity in implementing cash assistance interventions, as well as a strong profile in protection which will help achieve project outcomes. Al Wefaq will have a leading role in reaching out to the project beneficiaries and implementing the planned activities, in close cooperation with and support of Oxfam. All project activities will be closely coordinated with relevant stakeholders, including the MoSD and the FSS cluster.

project_name: Reduce shelter protection risk through creating adequate living space for substandard shelters of most vulnerable families including people with disabilities in the Gaza strip
project_objective:
The overall project's objective is to contribute to enhancing the coping capacity and meeting the basic needs of vulnerable HHs with protection concerns due to their substandard housing conditions through shelter rehabilitation/adaptation support.
Specifically, the project aims at supporting substandard shelters of the most vulnerable HHs exposed to harsh weather and with protection concerns to meet basic shelter needs and enhance their coping capacities (winterization, summarization, and shelter upgrade, rehabilitation, and repair).
The targeted groups include women, men, girls, and boys with protection concerns such as persons with disabilities (PWDs) including people with vision impairment, people with down's syndrome and female-headed HHs (FHHs), and those in fragile and critically under-served communities affected by the ongoing crisis in the Gaza Strip.
The objectives aligned with the needs identified in the humanitarian need overview (HNO) and Oxfam's recent assessment conducted in September 2022. This is in line with the objectives and the framework of the OPTI country 2023 HRP strategy specifically objective 2: “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”. It’s also aligned with objective #2 of the shelter and NFI cluster which is about supporting vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns to meet basic needs and enhance their coping capacities.

In partnership with the Youth Empowerment Center (YEC), Oxfam plans to target 230 HHs with substandard shelters (including 70 HHs for PWDs). In addition, 130 (a subset of the targeted 230 HHs) vulnerable HHs at risk of exposure to or affected by natural or manmade hazards (e.g. summer/winter storms, flooding) will receive essential protective shelter NFIs.
A community engagement approach will be adopted during the design and implementation of the intervention for a balanced representation, including the specific needs, views, and feedback of women and PWDs.
Local community committees (with equitable gender and age representation) will be established/activated in coordination with the MoSD to ensure the committees’ direct engagement with targeted communities and beneficiaries. This includes nominating and selecting beneficiaries and collecting their feedback and level of satisfaction during and after implementation, etc.

project_name: Adequate Shelter Solution for vulnerable households living in substandard housing units in Gaza
project_objective:
The project responds to the Shelter/NFIs Cluster’s Objective n. 2: “Vulnerable households exposed to harsh weather and protection concerns are supported to meet basic needs and enhance their coping capacity”. This is linked to HRP 2022 SO.2; “The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of quality basic services, and improved access to resources, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL”. 

The overall project objective is to ensure that 150 most vulnerable HHs (855 individuals) from Gaza, North Gaza, and middle area Governorates are supported with adequate durable shelter solutions that meet their basic needs and enhance their coping capacity.  

The proposed response will be tailored on the HHs’ needs and will be including the provision of: 

1) Rehabilitation and repair of 150 sub-standard housing units up to the minimum shelter standards, and provision of technical support to the most vulnerable households. Based on the Humanitarian Needs Overview for 2022, the Ministry of Public Works and Housing, performed a field assessment of 45,000 housing units in Gaza during the period from June to December 2019. From the total assessed housing units around 21,300 inhabited units across Gaza are classified as substandard since they do not meet the Shelter minimum standards for repairs and upgrades developed by the Shelter Cluster. They lack minimum requirements for adequate living space, weather protection, hygiene facilities and privacy, and require different degrees of rehabilitation. From the already received cases, NRC had assessed and identified 100 cases in urgent need of rehabilitation support. The case load consists of households with socio-economic vulnerability, elderly, FHHs, people living in overcrowded living conditions, marginalized groups living in flood prone areas, with high socio-economic vulnerability, living in substandard housing unit. Additionally, 50 cases were identified as referrals from the NRC protection program (case management) and the Gaza Protection Consortium and include households with severe protection issues in need of extended shelter support as a positive copying mechanism for their wellbeing.  

The provided support for all cases will ensure durable shelter solutions that meet basic needs, enhance coping mechanisms, improve physical protection, mental wellbeing, and reduce Gender Based Violence risks (GBV) through safe and dignified shelters.  

The required support will be provided through restricted cash transfer with active technical support and supervision, or -in exceptional cases- through a contractor approach if the beneficiaries are unable or not willing to manage the required coordination to complete the agreed works. Finally in case of a need for short term relocation of the household members until required rehabilitation works are completed NRC will be supporting into the identification of appropriate rented accommodation and provide short term cash for rent to facilitate the relocation. 2) Provision of case-by-case restricted cash assistance for essential household items. The support will be tailored according to needs and may include items such as bedding items, gas stoves, heaters with gas cylinders and fuel, emergency lighting system with batteries. Following the Do No Harm principles in case of heater provision all necessary safety measures will be applied and required items such as fire extinguisher, fire blanket awareness raising, and training will be provided.3) Provision of hygiene kits and hygiene awareness material for the targeted families throughout the project cycle. This project is designed in consultations and coordination with NRC local partner, the Shelter Cluster, GPC, Protection Cluster and the MoPWH and coordinated with active shelter partners to avoid duplication and ensure fair distribution of the limited humanitarian funds among affected communities across Gaza Strip.

project_name: Life-saving livelihoods assistance to vulnerable households in Sudan
project_objective:
Sudan's ongoing food insecurity endangers people's lives, means of subsistence, and stability. A large portion of Sudan's population is at risk of food insecurity as a result of the protracted conflict, environmental degradation, and other disasters such as drought and floods, in 2023, there would be an estimated 11.7 million individuals in need of FSL assistance in Sudan.
This project is designed to improve the food security and livelihood status of 29,650 (14,825 Female, 14,825 male) vulnerable agro/pastoral individuals directly, as part of the project activities, 11,600 individuals (5,800 males, 5,800 females) will receive agricultural assistance, 3,650 individuals (1,825 males, 1,825 females) will receive livestock assistance, and 14,400 (7,200 males, 7,200 females) will receive cash or vouchers to support their livelihoods, as well as their families indirectly. The action is expected to reach up to 177,900 people including children, youth, adolescent girls, people with disabilities, women-headed households, IDPs, and Returnees in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, North Darfur and Kassala States. The project interventions will allow households to grow their own reliable food for family consumptions while earning some money from the sale of the surplus. This will be conducted through improving farmers and pastoralists awareness on good agricultural practices, provision of improved seeds and essential agricultural hand tools, distribution of milking goats to enhance the availability of milk and meat for home consumption and conducting a livestock vaccination campaign to maintain the households' animal assets in the targeted communities and vouchers for goods or services will be provided directly to affected people to meet one or more of their basic humanitarian needs.

project_name: Child protection services for children at risk in the North, Akkar and BML
project_objective:
This project will target vulnerable children at risk, through the identification and registration of vulnerable children, such as those who have been orphaned, separated from their families, or are at risk of exploitation or abuse. Once identified, vulnerable children will be provided with individualized support, which includes assessments, care plans, referrals, and follow-up under the case management intervention. Case managers will work with children and their families to address the identified needs, such as access to education, healthcare, and withdrawal from child labour, and psychosocial support. Concern will also ensure the creation or upgrade of child-friendly spaces to provide a safe and supportive environment for children to play, learn, and receive psychosocial support, including structured activities and emotional support to children. Concern will also conduct awareness-raising activities in the targeted communities, to raise awareness of child protection issues and to encourage communities to take action to protect children. The topics will include positive parenting, as well as other topics to challenge negative social norms like early marriage and child labour. Through these discussions and sessions, Concern will aim to increase the engagement of the community in identifying and responding to child protection risk. Concern will also work with local partners in the targeted areas, with capacity building plans to enhance their ability to identify and respond to child protection issues in their respective areas of intervention. Concern is currently conducting an identification and assessment exercise to select local partners to work with on protection projects. Until now, the potential partners include Mouvement Social for CP activities and LECORVAW for GBV activities.
In brief, the activities will include child protection case management, focused psychosocial support services targeting children and their caregivers and awareness sessions, campaigns at community level as well as cash assistance such as emergency cash assistance (ECA) to ensure that the targeted populations has the capacity to overcome the faced risks. The project will target 360 children and 540 caregivers in awareness sessions, and 100 children with case management. The targeted population will include vulnerable Lebanese, Syrian and Palestinian refugees, as well as migrant children at risk. For the migrant children, a needs assessment will be conducted to further understand the community needs and the associated risks, to ensure the project responds to them. This would include exploring needs for child friendly spaces, access to education and legal services as well as cash assistance to meet basic needs – including food and non-food relates needs.
Overall, this project, and under the Lebanon ERP priorities, would aim to prevent and respond to child protection risks, promote the well-being of vulnerable children, and ensure that they are able to access essential services and support.

project_name: Contribuer au développement de la résilience des ménages affectés par les chocs à travers des actions d’assistance alimentaire soutenues par la Réduction de Risques de Catastrophes au sein des communautés affectées (Tillia et Tassara)
project_objective:
Concern propose un projet d'un an pour améliorer l'état de la sécurité alimentaire des communautés vulnérables vivant à Tillia et Tassara, dans la région de Tahoua. La réponse ciblera les ménages les plus vulnérables en leur permettant de sauver des vies grâce à l'assistance en espèces et appliquera une approche sensible aux conflits pour améliorer la capacité des ménages les plus vulnérables à satisfaire leurs besoins de base (alimentaires et non alimentaires). 
La réponse identifiera d'abord les ménages et les individus les plus nécessiteux via un ciblage rapide utilisant des critères de vulnérabilité axés sur les femmes et les jeunes enfants. 
Concern fera toujours référence aux lignes directrices élaborées par le Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires(DNPGCA), pour la mise en œuvre du Projet. L’assistance va consister en trois mois d’aide alimentaire pour couvrir au moins 80 % des besoins énergétiques (2 100 Kcal par personne et par jour). En fonction de la crise, Concern évaluera la possibilité d’intensifier l’intervention initiale en termes de durée.   
Les départements de Tillia et Tassara ont été choisis sur bases du niveau de vulnérabilité de leurs communautés.  En effet, selon les données du Cadre Harmonisé de Novembre 2022, ces départements affichent respectivement une situation projetée en rapport avec la population en phase 3, avec un peu près 14,423 (27%) à Tillia en phase 3 et 9 770 (27%) à Tassara. A ceci s’ajoute un contexte sécuritaire assez fragile au niveau de ces zones.   
Concern va privilégier modalité de réponse via transferts monétaires à travers une étroite collaboration avec les agences de transferts et instituts de micro finances locaux, capitalisant les leçons de la mise en œuvre du Projet ERNE financé par la DG/ECHO. Concern estime que les transferts monétaires constituent la modalité de réponse la plus appropriée car elle améliore la sécurité et la dignité des bénéficiaires ciblés en raison de l'élément de prise de décision. En plus, les communautés ont une forte préférence pour recevoir de l'argent car elles l'utilisent déjà pour répondre à la plupart de leurs besoins. 
Un accent particulier sera mis sur l'inclusion des femmes à chaque étape du processus. Ceci pourra être atteint en mettant en place des critères de ciblage qui tiennent compte de la dimension genre, avec implication des femmes dans les équipes de ciblage. 
L'expérience des précédentes distributions via transferts monétaires a montré que les femmes participaient au processus de ciblage en tant que membres des comités de ciblage et que la majorité des bénéficiaires ciblés étaient des ménages dirigés par des femmes. La prévention de la violence sexuelle et sexiste et l'atténuation des risques, y compris l'exposition aux abus sexuels et à la violence conjugale ainsi qu'au mariage précoce, seront intégrées dans les thèmes de sensibilisation avant, pendant et après les interventions de transfert monétaire. 
Les prestataires de services financiers seront appuyés par les équipes de pour identifier les problèmes de protection afin de minimiser les risques éventuels de VBG.

project_name: Responding to humanitarian WASH needs with focus on Resilience in Rural Damascus, Aleppo, Idlib, and Hama Governorates
project_objective:
Syria’s protracted conflict has left 13.55 million people in need of WASH assistance (HNO 2023), undermining the collective objective of public health as a common good, and exacerbating humanitarian needs. In determining projects with the Sector Coordinator, NCA’s principle is to raise awareness and support the equitable distribution of WASH benefits and opportunities, with selected areas as ranked according to severity in the HNO 2023. The main purpose of NCA’s WASH program is to reduce health-related and protection risks among conflict-affected populations by providing sustainable access to safe water, adequate sanitation, and improved hygiene. This will address the need for long term prevention and control measures for maintaining public health, and for promoting socio-economic development among the target communities. The involvement of local stakeholders is important so as humanitarian crises are not used to reduce what needs to be maintained as a public service. The targeting adheres to sector needs and priorities, as identified and reported in the HRP and HNO 2023, this being the best guarantee of a truly good outcome. Activities include the use of renewable energy (solar power) for pumping and distributing water; monitoring and optimising groundwater extraction using remote sensing; operation and maintenance training and tools for pump operators; and the support of vulnerable groups with the distribution of essential hygiene items and awareness that meet family needs and are gender appropriate. In terms of geography, the targeting is informed by the needs as expressed by the severity scale for HNO 2023, with priority given to sub-districts with overall score of 4 or 5. Overall score of 3 is also considered under some conditions, e.g., if corresponding overall score for protection/GBV sectors is high. Relevance with recent, ongoing, and planned projects implemented through NCA directly, and through local partners is also considered. 
The selected governorates and potential locations at the sub-district level are: (i) Rural Damascus (Nashabiyeh, Dhameer, Haran Al'awameed, Kafr Batna), (ii) Aleppo (As-Safira, Banan, Hajeb, Dayr Hafir, Tall Ed-daman), (iii) Hama (As-Saan, Suran, Hamra); and (iv) Idlib (Sanjar, Ma'arrat An Nu'man, Abul Thohur, Tamanaah, Khan Shaykun). 
In summary, the project will address a) Access to safe water (also related to public health and protection risks) b) Access to essential hygiene items to most vulnerable groups (women, girls, disabled, elderly, etc.) c) Resilience of public water systems (O&M and environmental protection). 
NCA has established office in Damascus since 2021 and has a team consisting of program and support staff. Furthermore, NCA has secured core funding for its direct implementation of WASH activities in selected areas in 2023. This will allow NCA to coordinate with all stakeholders and mobilize financial and human resources for conducting detailed needs assessment in the locations included in this submission. This will be done in communication with relevant stakeholders and targeted communities and in close coordination with the WASH Cluster. Activities will be reported in the 4Ws by NCA's program/MEAL team
For this project, NCA will target total of 58,000 people (16,820 W, 15,080 M, 11,600 G, 14,500 B), and has secured approx. 35% of requested budget for 2023 activities

project_name: Supporting the Recovery and Resilience-building of Crisis-affected Rural Communities in Rural Damascus
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to support vulnerable populations to rebuild their longer-term resilience. Mission East aims to facilitate access to improved and sustainable services and inputs in environmentally friendly ways within the governorate of Rural Damascus. Interventions will fall under the Food Security and Agriculture Sector (FSA) and target 27,600 crisis-affected individuals (IDPs, returnees, and host communities alike). From this amount, 26,800 individuals will benefit from the economic infrastructures rehabilitated, while a total of 800 individuals (160 households) will benefit from either agricultural or livestock inputs.

The agricultural and livestock industry, which was previously a cornerstone of the Syrian economy, has been affected greatly during this protracted crisis. Climate and crisis-induced agricultural production losses, economic decline and weakened local currency, price inflation, water scarcity, damaged infrastructure, and protracted hostilities in some areas of the country have led to farmers curtailing, or in some cases abandoning, their enterprises. For this reason, ME aims to provide agricultural or livestock inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, livestock, and animal feed to affected farmers and livestock owners, as well as to help restore agricultural services through the rehabilitation of irrigation systems, solar-powered wells and pumps, and other agricultural community assets. The assumption is as follows: (IF) crisis-affected communities are supported with sustainable agricultural services and inputs, (THEN) beneficiaries can increase their resilience and restore their household food and livelihood security. Ultimately, ME envisions that with the added livelihoods opportunities, households in rural areas will be able to better meet basic needs, thereby increasing their food and nutrition security.

The intervention itself will be designed with a participatory approach, allowing affected community members to highlight their needs and preferences. For the restoration of agricultural services and community assets, projects will be decided in coordination with community stakeholders, as well as relevant technical bodies based on the needs in the community. For agricultural and livestock support, KIIs will be carried out before the intervention kicks off to identify the needs in the community and targeted recipients will be able to select their preferred inputs from a list of context relevant items based on FSA recommendations and the recommendations of specialized veterinarians and agricultural engineers, that have been approved by the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA). For this reason, the specific inputs to be distributed will be identified after the start of the project and based on the information mentioned. This will ensure that recipients are receiving assistance based on their needs, while at the same time ensuring that the inputs provided are native to the area, are of the correct specifications, are standardized and in line with sector recommendations, and will ultimately do no harm to the environment. Inputs will be provided via the in-kind modality.

Activities will work to support small scale farmers (with land size between 5-10 dunums) already working in agriculture and/or livestock rearing. The intervention will prioritize the identification and selection of the most vulnerable and marginalized groups. Targeting criteria will be set that will guide the selection process and consider factors such as vulnerability (for example: women headed HHs or HHs with a large number of dependents, including PWDs), motivation, available skills and land, and commitment to climate and environmentally friendly practices. Rehabilitation of economic infrastructures such as irrigation canals, wells, and water and irrigation systems will aim to target households working in the agriculture and livestock rearing by selecting public works that will, either directly or indirectly, support their livelihoods

project_name: Contribuer à améliorer l'accès à une éducation inclusive et de qualité dans un environnement d'apprentissage sûr et protecteur pour les enfants affectés par les conflits dans la région de Diffa
project_objective:
Le projet vise à améliorer l'accès aux environnements d’apprentissage sécurisés pour environ 18 000 garçons et 19 600 filles affectés par les conflits et les crises dans 80 écoles de Diffa (Diffa, Maine Soroa, Chetimari, Nguigmi, Goudmaria) . Le projet vise également à augmenter la capacité des communautés, des écoleset des enfants à protéger leurs établissements scolaires et de contribuer à l'éducation, tout en utilisant des outils et des méthodes participatives pour impliquer les parents et les enfants, y inclus les plus vulnérables.  
Des réhabilitations, constructions de classes évolutives et de latrines seront effectuées afin de garantir que les espaces d'apprentissage soient adéquats pour accueillir le nombre croissant d'enfants inscrits. Ces activités profiteront à 37600 élèves inscrits dans le système formel. Des formations et un accompagnement pédagogique tout au long de l’action seront proposés à 860 enseignants en lien avec les services techniques pour améliorer la qualité des enseignements. Des dotations de kits scolaires pour les élèves et de ressources pédagogiques pour les enseignants seront effectuées. Le projet travaillera par ailleurs avec les communautés pour les sensibiliser sur l'importance de l'éducation, surtout des filles et des enfants en situation d'handicap et renforcera les structures éducatives communautaires pour qu’elles puissent qu’elles appuient l’élaboration de plans de gestion des risques et la mise en place de code de conduite dans les écoles. Les enseignants recevront également une formation pour mieux répondre à la détresse des enfants - approche « École sûre », identification de la détresse psychologique et gestion du stress, premiers secours psychologiques et appui psycho-social. Des bibliothèques itinérantes seront créés afin d’offrir aux enfants un accès facilité à des ouvrages éducatifs mais aussi ludiques.  Afin de favoriser la réintégration de 3600 enfants précocement exclus ou n’ayant jamais intégré le système scolaire, 120 classes passerelles seront mises en place au sein des écoles formelles appuyées. La collaboration avec des structures communautaires ainsi que les formations d´enseignants accroitront la durabilité de l´intervention par une mobilisation et un ancrage communautaire. L'accent sera mis aussi sur la responsabilisation des structures communautaires et sur la capacité des enseignants en termes d’encadrement des filles afin d’améliorer la rétention ainsi que le niveau des acquis scolaires des filles.        
Pour réaliser cela, le projet travaillera étroitement avec les services techniques du Ministère de l'Enseignement Primaire, de d'Alphabétisation, de la Promotion des Langues Nationales et de l'Éducation Civique (MEP) ainsi que les structures communautaires de l'ecole. On travaillera aussi avec les communes en vue d’assurer leur appropriation de ce problème et une prise en charge future de certaines actions. Le projet travaillera en cohérence avec le cluster éducation et tous les autres partenaires intervenant dans les zones cibles.
Le projet s'étend sur la période du 01/05/2021 au 30/07/2023 (financé), avec une extension souhaitée jusqu'au 30/07/2025 (recherche de financement en cours).

project_name: Una mirada noble al Autismo y sus fronteras
project_objective:
Los padres y los familiares influyen significativamente en el desarrollo social e intelectual de un niño. Dentro de esta relación, es sumamente lógico que los niños influencien a sus respectivas familias y se puede notar como ésta influencia adquiere un carácter mucho más significativo cuando el niño tiene discapacidades y aunque el nivel de dicha influencia se relacione con factores tales como la severidad y la naturaleza del problema, cualquier discapacidad de un miembro de la familia afecta inmediatamente a la misma. La mayoría de padres de niños con autismo, declaran que aunque la situación les causa muchísima angustia, dolor, confusión, llanto, risa, trauma emocional, requieren de una dosis inmensa de paciencia, pero que al mismo tiempo les proporciona recompensas indescriptibles de carácter profundo y espiritual. A través de este proyecto se tiene como objetivo principal brindar técnicas y recursos pedagógicos para lograr el bienestar psicológico de los padres y niños inmersos  en el autismo o cualquier otro trastorno que afecta la salud mental. .

Son muchas las formas en que las condiciones mentales y físicas de los niños pueden verse afectadas, originando dificultades en el desarrollo de la conducta normal, siendo una de ellas el autismo. Estos niños se ven a primera vista distintos, así como de aquellos que padecen las clases más comunes de incapacidad. No obstante, cada uno de los problemas que presentan puede encontrarse en otros niños con desventaja, especialmente en aquellos que tienen ciertas condiciones congénitos que afectan la percepción y el desarrollo del lenguaje. Es así como hemos conformados un gran equipo profesional, de pediatra, psicólogo, psiquiatra, neurólogo y estimuladores, para una primera fase de evaluar y diagnosticar  a niños y niñas que son considerado como población flotante dentro del sistema educativo por no tener un diagnostico claro de sus necesidades intelectuales, psicológica y emocionales. Una segunda fase de intervención que basado en la evaluación y el diagnostico se establecerá un plan de actividades, tareas, estrategias y posible tratamiento médico, para lograr resultados favorables en el bienestar de los niños, niñas, padres y representante. Llegando a la ultima fase de apoyo a la familia y la concientización comunitaria para reforzar los avances logrados en las intervenciones  y descartar la estimatización de las personas por su condición. Al mismo tiempo acondicionar espacio, como centros de salud, centros educativos y comedores, para brindar de igual manera seguridad alimentaria complementando la asistencia integral de los niños y niñas. project_name: Réponse humanitaire en matière de protection et d'éducation pour les enfants affectés par la crise multidimensionnelle à Mopti
project_objective:
Au Mali, l'insécurité, les conflits et les catastrophes naturelles ont empêché plus de 582 600 enfants d'accéder à l'éducation en toute sécurité en 2023. L’aversion des groupes armés luttant contre le modèle d’éducation occidental dans les régions du centre et au nord du Mali reste une constance depuis le déclenchement de la crise en 2012. A cela s’ajoutent les conflits communautaires et les catastrophes naturelles telles que les inondations qui réduisent les opportunités d’accès à l’éducation et la qualité des services de supervision des apprentissages. 
Selon les données collectées par le Cluster Education et le gouvernement du Mali, 1 762 écoles demeurent fermées en février 2023. Cela révèle que, malgré les efforts déployés pour ouvrir des écoles, le nombre d'écoles touches par le conflit continue d'augmenter chaque année. Par exemple, en 2020, le nombre d'écoles fermées était estimé à 1 344, puis à 1 664 en 2021, pour arriver à un pic de 1 776 en 2022. Les régions de Mopti, Tombouctou, Ménaka, Ségou et Gao, sont celles qui comptent avec le plus grand nombre d'écoles non fonctionnelles en raison de l'insécurité.  
De plus, 419 incidents de protection (dont le 16% concerne des enfants) ont été signalés entre depuis le début de 2023 dans la seule région de Mopti (Rapport de Monitoring de Protection, Cluster Protection). Une analyse rapide de besoins d’éducation et protection des enfants dans communes urbaines de Mopti et communes rurales de Fatoma et Bassirou réalisée en février 2023. Sur la base des informations collectées, les enfants sont particulièrement affectés par les violations graves de leurs droits, notamment le recrutement et utilisation des enfants par des groupes armés, les enlèvements, les attaques contre les structures sanitaires et éducatives. La fermeture des écoles constitue davantage un facteur de risque et d’exposition des enfants à la violence et aux abus. De plus des signes de détresse psychologique, inclus un sentiment d’insécurité (Rapport d’évaluation rapide : NRC, SCI, SLDSES de juillet 2022), ont été remarqués. Le besoin de services de soutien psychosocial et de santé mentale se manifeste pour les enfants affectés par le conflit, déplacés et de la communauté hôte, inclus les élèves des écoles fermés et leurs enseignants. Les filles restent particulièrement exposées aux violences basées sur le genre. Selon les données GBIMS du mois de janvier 2023, Mopti reste la région avec un plus haut taux de cas de VBG signalés (376, soit 44% du total mensuel). Pour les 99% de cas il s’agit de femmes, dont 21% de filles de moins de 18 ans, et 1% de garçons de moins de 18 ans (Rapport Situation de la Protection, Janvier 2023, Cluster Protection). 
Pour répondre aux besoins identifiés en matière de protection et d'éducation, SC propose fournir une réponse intégrée et rapide en faveur des enfants déplacés et des communautés qui accueillent les familles déplacées à travers la mise en place d‘espaces temporaires d’apprentissages sûrs et protecteurs dans les communes rurales de Fatoma et de Bassirou de la région de Mopti. Également, SC espère qu'avec le projet proposé les filles et les garçons ont accès à des espaces d'apprentissage sûrs, inclusifs, sensibles au genre et protecteurs, et à des services de protection de l'enfance et de soutien psychosocial. 

Save the Children mettra en œuvre le projet avec le soutien de son partenaire local, Action Mopti. Le projet aura une durée de 12 mois. SC coordonnera la réponse avec les clusters protection et éducation, les autorités locales et nationales, et les acteurs humanitaires travaillant dans la zone d'intervention.

project_name: Improving MIYCN and CMAM service provision in Syria
project_objective:
According the 2023 HNO, the number of people in need of life saving services increased to 5.9 million. 15 million people in Syria - more than half the population – currently face acute food insecurity which may further accelerate all forms of under-nutrition among vulnerable children and women. The rising food insecurity will negatively impact on the nutritional status of an existing 2.1 million mothers who are already consuming a poor maternal diet, with an estimated 544,752 PLW currently in need of treatment for acute malnutrition with 460,124 of them being anemic. The already concerning levels of maternal malnutrition is anticipated to increase among displaced populations. Children with malnutrition are at an elevated risk of mortality and morbidity. 363,556 young children who are currently suffering from acute malnutrition will require appropriate, timely and sustainable treatment interventions, with almost one million of them being in dire need of robust anemia treatment and prevention interventions.

SMART surveys conducted in NES and NWS indicate that there is an increment of malnutrition for both U5 children and women of childbearing age. The stunting levels  show an increasing trend: GAM levels were found as high as 5.5% in NES. The result indicated an alert level of chronic malnutrition (stunting) close to exceeding the 30% critical threshold. The results for malnourished pregnant and lactating women (PLW) based on Mid Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) (<230 mm) reached 20.5%. According to the survey findings, the IMDD is below 50% (45%) and MAD is at an average of 20%. The challenges and the existing situation on the ground needs a great focus and effort to address the problems both in NES and NWS. SC will focus on responding in Idleb, Al-Hassakeh, Aleppo, and Ar-Raqqa governorates.

Over the last 2 years, food prices across Syria have hugely increased and the value of the Syrian Pound plummeted. This has left communities vulnerable to food insecurity amongst many other risks. Food insecurity is directly related with the risk of malnutrition, highest for PLWs and children under 5 year who have an increased nutritional need (SC Nutrition SMART Survey 2021). Caregivers of children under 2 years and pregnant and lactating persons will be provided with MIYCN services in the target areas. CU5 will be screened for acute malnutrition and treatment will be provided at the facility or through referral. SC will follow-up all cases of malnourished children until they complete their treatment and achieve the desired nutritional outcomes. Gender and disability considerations will be integrated into the design of activities.

The nutrition teams will work with the health teams to provide integrated, inclusive services – inclusive of screening, treatment, IYCF awareness, early initiation of breastfeeding, delivering nutrition supplies, and applying CMAM to treat malnutrition cases and referral for complicated cases and acutely malnourished infants below 6 months for inpatient treatment services. All PLWs and caregivers of CU-5 within the intervention population will be linked with MPCA support to enable improved dietary practices; particularly, improved dietary diversity for reduction of micronutrient deficiencies amongst infants and young children and PLW, and improved child growth and development. Mothers requiring PSS and GBV support will be referred to the protection teams for additional assistance.

The target population will include mothers, children (aged 0-23 and 24-59 months) as well as children with disability. The HIMS will be used for collecting and compiling all intervention data both internally and also for 4Ws reporting at the sector level. MEAL teams will enable program beneficiaries to share feedback on quality of services, accessibility and available services. The M&E team and health team will ensure protection of health data and control accessibility to only authorized personnel.

project_name: Protection - Protracted Crisis Response
project_objective:
The project will address the critical need for strengthened child protection (CP) and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) prevention and response services in  Saida, Wadi Khaled and Akkar Governorate. The project will target at-risk Lebanese girls and boys aged 10-17 and young women and men aged 18-24 at risk or survivors of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation (especially those engaged in worst forms of child labour, children without legal status or documentation, and girls at risk or survivors of child marriage); and adult women at risk or exposed to GBV, as well as parents and caregivers, partners,  community leaders and local service providers. 

This project is a consortium Led by Plan Lebanon with IMC and Mouvement social, and its aim is to provide services to address the increasing protection risks amidst the multi-layered crisis in Lebanon. The consortium will utilize psychosocial support (PSS) modules, outreach strategies, community-based initiatives, established networks, trust built with the community, and specialized case management tools to strengthen the protection environment around boys, girls, women and other vulnerable groups

The project will provide a range of services, with each service delivered by a partner. Quality case management will be provided by Mouvement Social (MS), while IMC will handle GBV case management and referral. Both MS and IMC will provide cash assistance, with IMC handling cash for protection. Psychosocial support activities will be conducted by Plan International Lebanon (PIL), in addition to life skills sessions and positive parenting sessions. IMC will handle non-focused PSS activities, cycle of violence sessions, and inter-gender dialogue sessions. Emotional support group sessions will be conducted by IMC, and parenting sessions by PIL. Finally, PIL will conduct trainings to local community leaders on gender equality and inclusion, sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR), GBV, child protection (CP), and safe identification and referrals, in addition trainings to local PWD organizations will be run to support safe identification and referral of CP and GBV survivors and children at risk. By carefully coordinating the delivery of these services, the project aims to provide comprehensive support to those in need, while ensuring efficient and effective implementation.

project_name: Support to access and retention of vulnerable children in education in Beqaa
project_objective:
The Strategic ERP objective adopted by this project is to provide essential humanitarian support to most vulnerable people affected by the economic crisis in Lebanon for them to meet their critical needs.

The project aims at increasing access to and retention in quality and inclusive education for the most vulnerable children (6-17 years) in the area of Beqaa, Baalbeck-Hermel by providing retention support, financial assistance, and protection interventions in schools/community centers responding to the high rate of drop-outs among the Lebanese population and migrant workers after the multifaceted crises targeting 1,000 school-aged children in total over 1-year duration. 
 
Description of activities:

The project activities include three main interventions:

Provide Supportive and Complementary Learning Opportunities through retention and remedial classes in schools/community centers following an integrated approach with child-protection measures.
Provide financial support to HHs to enhance retention through cash for education.
Provide teacher capacity building packages focusing on quality and inclusive education, and protection-related trainings, PSEA, CP, SRHR, SG, and GBV.

project_name: Improving access to safe, equitable, inclusive, competency-based  and age-appropriate learning opportunities for girls and boys in Rohingya camps and host communities
project_objective:
""Save the Children (SC) aims to continue education services for children and adolescents, through access to safe, equitable, inclusive, competency-based, and age-appropriate learning opportunities, within a child-friendly and protective environment inside the camps and host communities, under Ukhiya and Teknaf of Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh.
Activities will focus on maintaining and upgrading Learning Centres (LCs), establishing new Community Based Learning Facilities (CBLF), Peer Education Programs (PEP), Distance Education (DE), and Cross-Sectoral Facilities (known as Girl Friendly Spaces) for early learning and basic education for children and adolescents. SC will implement LCFA, MC, CBLF, ECD, and interventions in Rohingya and host communities covering children and the age group 3-18 . The intervention will be implemented in the Camps and host:  Total LC in RR: 97, Camp 04 (Block: E, G ), Camp 10 (Block: A, C), Camp 13 (Block: A,B, C,E, F,G), Camp 14 (Block: A,E, I,Q), Camp 15 (Block: E, F ), Camp 16 (Block: D), Camp 18 (Block: C), Camp 19 (Block: B), Camp 1E (Block: A, B,C), Camp 25 (Block: D ), Camp 26 (Block: D,F, H), Camp 8W (Block: A)),  CBLF-RR: 154 (Camp 07 (Block: A,B,C,D,E,F,G ), Camp 9 (Block :  A, B, C, D, E,F,G), Camp 13 (Block: A,C, D,E, F,G), Camp 14 (Block: A,B, C, D,E), Camp ,15 (Block: C,D, E,F,G,H), Camp 21 (Block: A,B,C) and Learning centre in host community 3 and all are in Jaliapolong Union under Ukhiya Upazila. 
Interventions also include enhancing the knowledge of parents and caregivers on how to support their children’s learning, development, and social well-being. Besides, activities will aim to improve teaching quality through continuous teachers’ professional development support for all education sector partners. Inclusive aspects of programming include Mental-Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), gender-responsive, child-sensitive, psychosocial support, and disability-friendly as well as integration between sectors, including child protection and health will be mainstreamed in all activities to ensure that different needs of girls and boys are responded to, and they are equitably benefitting from the interventions.
Moreover, special attention will be paid to the capacity building of relevant staff members on key teaching-learning based on the new Myanmar Curriculum (MC) and Accelerated Learning Program (ALP), as well as Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) issues. All the learning facilities will be equipped with gender-segregated WASH points, including Menstrual Health Management (MHM) services. In addition to that physical infrastructure, materials, and facilities will be strengthened to ensure access and equity for children living with disabilities. Being a sector co-lead, SC will continue to play a key role in advocacy, increased quality, and sustainability of education services for the displaced Rohingya and adjacent host communities.
Furthermore, to combat the sudden pandemic and other unprecedented crises, SC plans to continue the caregiver-led education modalities, such as Interactive Radio Instructions and web-based & E-learning resources to accelerate and support remedial learning. Besides, SC will continue to advocate for the continuation of education as an essential service and the permission of technology-based interventions in the camps, so that the technology/remote learning activities can be ensured. Additionally, consulting with the District Primary Education Office and Upazila Office, SC will support the lower-performing government primary schools to ensure quality education among the learners. 
The project and programmatic initiatives are and will be enhancing social cohesion within the host and Rohingya communities. Besides, they are increasing inclusion and mutual understanding, creating a sense of belonging, promoting trust, and offering its members the opportunity for upward social mobility through different day observations, cultural events, awareness sessions, and meetings.

project_name: Assistance en eau, Hygiène et Assainissement pour les populations déplacées et des populations hôtes affectées par la crise sécuritaire dans la région de l’Est du Centre Est du Centre- Nord et du Nord du Sahel du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le projet ambitionne couvrir 5 régions, 27 communes avec un total estimé à 80000 bénéficiaires PDI et communautés hôte. Il contribuera à répondre aux besoins essentiels, renforcer la résilience des PDI et des communautés hôtes touchés par la crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso. L’assistance visera la satisfaction des besoins urgents des PDI et population hôte par la réalisation/ réhabilitation de points d’eau, une assistance en assainissement par la construction de latrines des ménages et des latrines scolaires, la sensibilisation pour la PHA, la distribution de kits d’hygiène, d’assainissement de GHM aussi bien au PDI qu’aux communautés hôtes.
Il adoptera un cadre de triple Nexus « humanitaire - développement - paix » avec une approche intégrée qui améliore l'accès à des moyens de subsistance plus durables et à des services de base de qualité.
Objectif global : Améliorer la résilience, la dignité, et les conditions d’accès à l’AEPHA des
PDI, des populations hôtes femmes, hommes, filles, garçons, personnes vivant avec un
Handicap.
Résultat 1: Les PDI, populations hôtes femmes, hommes, filles, garçons, les personnes vivant avec un handicap, des 5 régions ont un accès équitable à de l’eau potable pour leur de boisson;
Résultat 2 : Les PDI, les populations hôtes, femmes, hommes, filles, garçons, les personnes vivant avec un handicap des 5 régions ont un accès sécurisé aux latrines adaptés prenant en compte la gestion des menstrues
Résultat 3: Les PDI, populations hôtes femmes, hommes, filles, garçons, les personnes vivant avec un handicap des 4 régions améliorent leurs pratiques d'hygiène.
Le projet cherche à renforcer la résilience pour surmonter les stress et les chocs qui entravent la jouissance pleine des droits de l'homme.

Il vise l’amélioration de l’accès à des moyens de subsistance durables et à des services WASH de qualité, engage les principales parties prenantes, au niveau communautaire, et contribue à la cohésion sociale dans les communautés. project_name: Enhancing Access to Comprehensive CP Prevention and Response Services for the most vulnerable Lebanese and Palestinian Refugees in Lebanon in Akkar, North, Bekaa and Baalbek
project_objective:
The Danish Refugee Council (DRC) together with partners is appealing for support to implement comprehensive child protection prevention and response services in the Bekaa, Baalbek, North, and Akkar, targeting the most vulnerable and hard-to-reach Lebanese and Palestinian Refugees in Lebanon (PRL). The compounded socioeconomic crisis in Lebanon has significantly deepened the vulnerability of aforementioned target populations, and has resulted in exacerbated protection concerns for vulnerable children as confirmed by most recent MSNA data. Through programming in 2022, DRC has identified significant increase in exposure of children to violence, exploitation and abuse, severely impacting the well-being and healthy development of children. Vulnerable households are increasingly adopting negative coping mechanisms to meet basic needs, including child labor and child marriage, with severe protection consequences for children. Proposed activities under the ERP are designed in coordination with the Child Protection sector, and aim to complement services provided under the LCRP to allow for better and increased inclusion of PRL and Lebanese into child protection services. 
DRC will respond to increased needs for specialized child protection interventions by providing comprehensive case management services tailored to the needs of children and following a child-friendly approach to support children and where relevant caregivers in informed decision making about how to address child rights violations or incidents, and understand which services are available and to facilitate access to these services in a holistic and dignified manner. Protection cash will be integrated into case management services where relevant and appropriate and to support the achievement of protection outcomes, and children and caregivers will benefit from have access to individual psychosocial support as part of case management, including psychological first aid. For child survivors of sexual abuse, DRC and partners will leverage CP and GBV case management capacities to ensure a tailored response to child survivors following established GBV and CP guiding principles and approaches. Quality and outcomes of case management services will be monitored through satisfaction surveys, ensuring services can be continuously improved and any challenges addressed in a timely manner. DRC as part of child protection response services will also provide Focused Psychosocial Support services based on the “I Am Here” approach, developed to identify the most marginalized adolescent boys and girls through a door-to-door assessment methodology. Adolescents will participate in the design of participatory curricula whereby adolescents prioritize their own needs in terms of skills, knowledge and attitudes in pre-defined thematic areas related to cross-cutting themes of GBV and child protection. The FPSS curricula will also target caregivers and other male household members as decision-makers in adolescent’s life’s, requiring their engagement to empower adolescents and facilitate access to rights and services.
To complement response services, DRC will implement CP prevention activities targeting children and caregivers at community-level through community-based psychosocial support (CBPSS) activities aimed to contribute to enhancing the protection of children. The project will also establish youth committees to strengthen community-based networks with the aim to empower communities and engage them in the protection of children. Youth committees will receive capacity-building and coaching on child rights, protection, gender mainstreaming and inclusion, to be able to develop, plan and implement two youth-led initiatives within their communities aimed at mitigating child protection risks. project_name: Renforcer la réponse rapide et intégrée en matière de protection et de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial aux besoins des populations touchées par la crise sécuritaire, en particulier les enfants dans les zones d'urgence.
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire au Burkina Faso est plus préoccupante que jamais. L'augmentation continue des besoins a été exacerbée au cours de l'année 2022. La violence quasi quotidienne est généralisée dans 77% du pays (10 régions sur 13), affectant principalement la population civile, notamment les femmes et les enfants. La crise actuelle au Burkina Faso a un impact direct sur plus de 4,9 millions de personnes, dont 3,5 millions ont un besoin humanitaire aigu.     La fermeture des centres de santé, des écoles et des marchés, l'abandon des mairies, les violences contre les civils et la raréfaction des ressources en eau dans plusieurs localités ont un impact sur la vie de la population, notamment des plus vulnérables. L'exercice et la jouissance des droits de l'homme sont ainsi sérieusement affectés, notamment le droit d'accès et de bonne administration de la justice.
Au 31 mars 2022, selon la situation actualisée après la révision de la liste des personnes déplacées, le Burkina Faso comptait plus de 1,7M de déplacés internes. Les enfants représentent plus de 59,13% des déplacés internes et les femmes 23,28% des déplacés internes.
Cette situation de déplacement forcé expose les enfants à de sérieux risques de protection. En effet, les enfants sont exposés au risque de recrutement par les groupes armés. Pendant leur déplacement forcé, les enfants courent le risque d'être séparés de leurs parents. En raison de ce placement, les enfants sont également exposés au risque d'engins explosifs improvisés et de blessures graves. En raison également de la charge des ménages et de leur incapacité à subvenir à leurs besoins, les enfants sont exposés à toutes sortes de violences et d'abus, et pire encore, les ménages adoptent des stratégies d'adaptation négatives en donnant les filles en mariage.
La protection et le soutien psychosocial restent des besoins critiques pour les communautés touchées par l'insécurité dans tout le pays et dans les six régions d'urgence où les attaques violentes et l'utilisation d'engins explosifs improvisés contre les civils ont augmenté. Avec la fermeture des écoles et des crises alimentaires de plus en plus préoccupantes, les garçons et les filles sont confrontés à un risque accru de recrutement dans les groupes armés, d'exploitation, d'abus, de violences sexuelles, de viols et de mariages d'enfants. Le contexte d'urgence a encore exacerbé les inégalités et les vulnérabilités existantes, en particulier pour les filles et les femmes. De manière générale, la crise a considérablement aggravé la situation des enfants, les exposant plus que jamais aux six violations graves dont sont victimes les enfants dans les conflits. En conséquence, le SCI va rationaliser l'intervention de protection dans toutes les thématiques que nous mettons en œuvre tout en ayant une intervention de protection autonome pour 100000 enfants.

project_name: Building resilience through supporting basic needs and income-generating capacities to vulnerable households within the Syrian Arab Republic
project_objective:
The project is aligned with the objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) 2022“Enhance access to market-based livelihood opportunities and production”.
DRC will support vulnerable conflict-affected populations toward self-sufficiency. DRC will aim to achieve the below outcome: “To improve the adaptive capacities and socio-economic well-being of people, civic actors and communities” through:
 -Increasing households’ income, assets, and consumption of needed goods and services.
DRC believes that households’ income, assets, and consumption of needed goods (including food) and services will increase if people participate in functioning markets which will be restored if people have appropriate skills for income generation and employment; and if people have safe and equal access to capital, markets, and employment; and if business norms enable people’s equitable economic participation.
- Creating more cohesive, inclusive, and equitable communities in Syria.
For people to achieve cohesive, inclusive, and equitable communities, marginalized groups must be able to exercise social and economic influence equal to those of other dominant groups and participate in decision-making.
A total of 11,000 will be targeted through DRC intervention in Daraa, Homs, Hama, Rural Damascus, and Aleppo. DRC will deliver Early Recovery assistance to persons of concern (PoCs) targeting conflict-affected youth and adults, men and women, including people with disabilities, to develop skills and increase income-generating opportunities with an aim to strengthen their access to livelihoods through microgrants for business development (start-up or scale-up), business development skills training, vocational training, distribution of toolkits in addition to the rehabilitation of community infrastructure restore through rehabilitation of Irrigation water canals and provide the beneficiaries with the needed assets or MGs or improve access to spaces in support of livelihoods. PoCs with protection-related concerns and vulnerabilities will be particularly targeted, and internal and external referrals will be made to ensure that protection services are provided in parallel based on identified needs.
The intervention will be coordinated within the Early Recovery and Livelihoods Sector meetings led by UNDP, and the Protection Sector led by UNHCR, where DRC is an active member to ensure coherence with other livelihoods and protection interventions. DRC will also coordinate closely with SARC, the Chamber of Industry of Aleppo, and The Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (MoSAL) at both field and country levels. Initial needs assessments will be conducted jointly with MoE, MoSAL, and SARC field staff, when applicable.  EcRec team will firstly conduct a Labour Market Assessment (LMA) to identify the employment sectors for both women and men, with more potential to grow, and which creates diversified jobs suitable for rural and urban areas. DRC will develop linkages with the private sector based on the LMA, where DRC will provide opportunities to vulnerable individuals through the internship placement programme. the intervention will target and support vulnerable individuals (at least 35% women) with financial and business development skill trainings. The beneficiaries will be selected based on a standardized vulnerability and suitability assessment of the proposed activities. Selected beneficiaries’ technical experience and eligibility are tested through a supervised technical test. Individuals will be trained on business and financial management, and how to develop and run a business). DRC will invite all participants to submit business proposals based on their skills, capacities, and assets needed. The business grant could be allocated either for start-ups businesses or scale-ups, allowing growth of existing enterprises, or the creation of new scalable ones.

project_name: PROJET DE RENFORCEMENT DE LA SURVEILLANCE A BASE COMMUNAUTAIRE, LA RECHERCHE DES ZERO DOSE ADAPTEE AUX ZONES A SECURITE COMPROMISE
project_objective:
Le Mali a une superficie de 1 241 266 Km2 et une densité de 17 habitants au kilomètre carré. Selon le Département de la sûreté et de la sécurité des Nations Unies (UNDSS), Tout le Mali est en insécurité y compris Bamako (capitale politique du Mali). Le niveau de sécurité varie selon les régions de trois à cinq sur une échelle de six. La situation sécuritaire reste dominée par des attaques terroristes, des enlèvements de personnes et de leurs biens, des braquages le long des routes et des dégâts causés par les mines surtout dans les régions centres et nord du Mali. L’OMS à travers ses médecins d’appui auprès des Directions Régionales de la Santé intervient dans le renforcement du système de santé depuis 2017. Ce projet vise à renforcer surveillance à base communautaire et la recherche des zéro dose dans 18 districts sanitaire a risque.  
Il vise au renforcement de la sensibilité du système national de surveillance à détecter toute circulation du poliovirus et MEV au Mali dans les zones à sécurité compromise.
50 relais communautaires, 10 investigateurs, un point focal par district sanitaire dans 10 aires de santé et un point focal régional seront recrutés et formés la surveillance à base communautaire et la recherche des zéro dose.
L’OMS et le ministère de la santé à travers les Directions régionales de la santé et les Districts sanitaires vont assurer la supervision trimestrielle des activités. Les relais communautaires travailleront avec les autorités locales administrative et sanitaire pour faciliter l’accès des sites PDI. Les données seront collectées intégrées dans le DHIS2.
