project_name: Assistance en Abris d’Urgence et Articles Ménagers Essentiels auprès des Personnes  Déplacées Internes (PDI) et Communautés Hôtes des Provinces de Namatenga, de Bam et Sanmatenga  dans la Région du Centre-Nord du Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Les activités des groupes armés continuent de pousser les populations à fuir les violences et rendent difficile l'accès aux personnes dans le besoin, notamment dans la région du Centre-Nord.
Selon les évaluations menées par la CONASUR a la fin septembre 2022, le nombre de PDIs a atteint 1 719 332 individus soit une augmentation de% par rapport au mois de d’environ 11,59% par rapport à la publication actualisée du 30/04/2022 (1 520 012 PDI).
Selon les mêmes évaluations, la région du centre a enregistré plus de 27% des IDPs enregistres et le besoin en abris était estime à 42,53% soit le deuxième besoin exprime par les PDIs.
L’augmentation significative du nombre des personnes déplacées internes (PDI) augmente les besoins d’abris et d’articles ménagers essentiels (AME). Le secteur dénombre 2 092 582 personnes dans le besoin, soit une augmentation de 37% depuis l’estimation faite lors du HRP 2022 (de 1 524 824 personnes).
L’OIM propose une intervention ciblée dans les communes les plus affectées par le déplacement des deux provinces de Namatenga de Bam et Sanmatenga, qui répondra aux besoins en abris d’urgence pour 2000 ménages (14,000 personnes), et des kits d’articles ménagers essentiels (AME) pour 2000 ménages (14,000 personnes) des communautés hôtes et des PDIs. Les kits seront achetés localement (National ou régional) dans la mesure du possible tout en respectant les procédures d’achats de l’OIM, ils seront acheminés et stockés sur les sites mise en œuvre, les constructions des abris seront faites avec la main d’œuvre locale qui recevra d’emblée une formation des experts Shelter de l’OIM puis élèveront ces abris avec la présence effective des bénéficiaires et délivré directement en faveur des populations hôtes. Ces derniers, tout comme les PDIs seront sélectionnés de façon transparente avec la présence des représentants de deux communautés en tenant compte de l’aspect genre et l’implication des autorités locales et des partenaires humanitaires.
L’OIM a déjà une expertise avérée dans le domaine de la construction des abris et de l’appui psycho sociale, en plus de cette expertise, dans le cadre des fonds GFFO (en cours) dans le Centre -Nord et du CERF 2022 (terminé dans le Centre – est), les activités similaires ont été mis en œuvre sur le terrain avec le staff OIM, des consultants engagés et des partenaires de mis en œuvre (Croix rouge, DEDI, VSF).
Conformément aux procédures d’achats de l’OIM, un appel d’offre sera lancé afin d’avoir les fournisseurs potentiels pour les achats des kits dans le cadre du projet, cet appel offre pourra concerner les localités de mise en œuvre du projet pour minimiser le risque d’incident sécuritaire lors du transport des kits et aussi de revitaliser les marchés locaux.
Sous réserve d’une évaluation préliminaire, l’ONG DEDI (Developpement, Equite, Durabilité et innovation) sera le partenaire local identifié pour la mise en œuvre des activités de construction des abris et de distribution des AME

L’objectif du projet est d’apporter une assistance en abri et articles non alimentaires afin de répondre aux besoins des personnes déplacées internes et des communautés hôtes dans la région centre-nord du Burkina Faso.

L’OIM adaptera ses interventions conformément à la stratégie du cluster abris/AME, aux résultats des évaluations menées par les différents partenaires, les leçons apprises des précédents projets ainsi qu’aux évaluation menées de façon continuelles sur le terrain.  

Les activités suivantes seront mises en œuvre :
-	 Identifier les bénéficiaires les plus vulnérables pour l’allocation de l’assistance en abris.

-	Achat et transport d'abris et de kits d’articles non alimentaires dans les zones de mise en œuvre du programme à travers des compagnie de transport locales.

-	 -	 En coordination avec les autorités locales, fourniture d’abris et de kits d’articles non alimentaires aux bénéficiaires du projet.

-	Mise en œuvre des 4 activités PSEA (directives PSEA)

project_name: Shelter, NFI and winterization assistance for the most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls in NW Syria
project_objective:
The project aims to respond to 11,700 HH with a total of 58,500 individuals disaggregated roughly as(13,000 men, 13,500 women, 15,500 boys, and 16,500 girls) of the most vulnerable conflict-affected IDPs, and host communities in Idleb and Aleppo governorates, and prioritizing households headed by a female, child, disabled, or elderly, then households with severely ill or disabled members, children below 5, elderly, pregnant or lactating women; with particular attention to those recently displaced or living overcrowded.
The project contributes to providing dignified shelter & NFI assistance through the following activities:
1- provide 8,500 HH with seasonal and supplementary NFIs and assistance, including winter clothing, stoves, and fuel in Al-Bab, Afrin, and Azaz subdistricts and camps. Each household will receive cash assistance with a value of 150$ (one-off $150 cash assistance as recommended by cluster and CWG) and prioritize its needs accordingly. Each beneficiary with a cash voucher by which they can obtain the cash from FSP.
2- Provide and installation of dignified shelters in two IDP sites (Dana, Maaret Tamsrin) in the Idleb governorate. Covering the needs of 500 HHs of IDPs. The activities will include installing 500 new dignified fabricated shelter units (of steel structure and sandwich panel) with associated infrastructure in line with the dignified shelter guidance.
3-Conducting site improvement works (Infrastructure in IDP sites) for 2500 HHs in (Dana, Maaret Tamsrin) in Idleb governorate, including construction and maintenance of drainage systems, roads, sewage networks, and installing lighting devices. This project will also contribute towards reinforcing an enabling protection environment and community cohesion by improving housing and related communities through
4- Rehabilitation of 700 of damaged or unfinished housing with an average cost of 750$ per house in (Harim, Salqin, Iskat, Kafr Takharim, Dana) in Idleb governorate, (Azaz, Al-Bab, Suran, Daret Azza) in Aleppo governorate.
In all activities, SDI considers the protection of the beneficiaries, so the distribution centers and the shops will be prepared with functional firefighting equipment, and brochures of safety and security practices will be distributed to beneficiaries. Moreover, a female staff will be recruited and trained to ensure more protection from exploitation and sexual abuse for girls and women and to deal with any GBV cases they may encounter during the project.
Most importantly, SDI pays excellent attention to people with disabilities, elderlies, and people with special needs, and for those, assistance will be delivered to home.
Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) rights of shelter sites, shelter beneficiaries, and house owners will be considered throughout all shelter repair interventions. An agreement will be signed to guarantee the rights of the beneficiaries. Coordination with the SNFI cluster and other active members is essential to ensure geographical separation and avoid overlapping/duplication.
All covid 19 precautions measures were adopted during the project, such as (respecting social distancing, wearing masks, and Sterilizers). Also, banners were fixed at meeting points to raise beneficiaries against covid19, complaints mechanism, PEAS…etc.
M&E staff will monitor the activities implementation and continually give their feedback and comments to the project manager; the surveys will include questions on the teams’ performance, beneficiary satisfaction, and complaints.

project_name: Strengthen resilience and access to market-based livelihood opportunities for vulnerable farmers in NES, through enhancing wheat/bread availability and reinforce better access to income-generating opportunities
project_objective:

Bahar intervention will improve the wheat/bread production capacity of 10 bakeries and one mill in the targeted locations, and purchasing power, where 800 MT of wheat will be purchased from 400 farmers in planting season 2022-2023 and will divide into two parts, the first: 171.2 MT will be sieved into 160 MT of pure wheat (93%) and 11.2 MT impurities (7%). The 160 MT pure wheat quantity will be allocated as wheat seeds and distributed to another 800 farmers for next season 2023-2024. The second part, 628.8 tons will be
milled into 503.04 tons of flour with 80% rate extraction and will be supplied to the rehabilitated bakeries. Consequently, approximately 710,000 bread bundles with a weight of 800 gr will distribute for 29,579 IDPs individuals free of charge for 3 months duration/78 distributing days based on the daily survival needs (250 g
bread/person/day). On the other hand, 1000 new farmers will benefit from 1- 600 wheat farmers from the distribution of wheat inputs (fertilizers, pests control materials), including irrigation and harvesting costs, 2- 400 vegetables farmers from the distribution of vegetables inputs (seeds, fertilizers, pests control materials), including establishment of 50 greenhouses, accompanied with capacity building related to Crops integrated management through How-to-Do approach. Moreover, 250 CFW (200 semi-skilled, 50 un-skilled) will implement activities related to bakeries and mills rehabilitation/maintenance works, bread distribution, berms, earthen barriers, irrigation canals, pumps, gates rehabilitation actions, existed greenhouses maintenance, existed eggs hatcheries maintenance and DRR including fire and vole pest-fighting.

project_name: Scaled-up access to basic food needs in high-needs and underserved areas by providing cash for food, food voucher assistance, and emergency Life-saving (RTERs, Cooked meals, and bread) in Idlib and Aleppo governorates.
project_objective:
The project will target 1500 families with regular (monthly) food assistance through two appropriate modalities:
1- Cash for food: GAN will target 750 most vulnerable families in village and camps with cash for food, the cash intervention is feasible in these camps as they all have access to different main markets in the targeted communities, eight rounds of cash for food will be distributed, each round consists of 20 days for distribution and 10 days for validation and PDM, 60$ will be allocated for each family as recommended by FSL cluster and CWG, the data gained from the FSL cluster indicate these areas as high priority ranking and no partner plan to target the same vulnerable and underserved camps, according to the needs assessment, the first priority is food, the proposed modality is a cash for food, as it is considered one of the most effective modality since the markets are available near camps.
2- E-voucher for Food: GAN will target 750 most vulnerable families in the village with food voucher with the aim of saving lives and ensuring continued and regular access to food for 8 months for most vulnerable groups, beneficiaries could replace the monthly top-up assistance (60$ per family) with the main food items from the markets contracted with GAN and will be able to buy among 40 specified items with restricted amounts that allowed us to fulfill the calories min standard set by the WFP.

The project will target the IDPs with emergency food assistance through four appropriate modalities:
1- Providing cooked meals to 750 families of newly IDPs in the targeted locations 30 times respectively within 30 days, this intervention is considered as a rapid response for affected IDPs suffering from lack of resources, instability, and don’t have cooking facilities, GAN designed the cooked meals based on its experience along past 10 years, and each beneficiary will receive 500g of high-quality cooked food daily for 30 days (this period of this type of assistance is recommended by FSL cluster).

2- Providing RTERs to 750 families of newly IDPs in the targeted locations enough for 5 persons for 7 days, this intervention is considered as a rapid response for affected IDPs suffering from lack of resources, instability and don’t have cooking facilities.

GAN will monitor the distribution, according to the M&E plan

project_name: Support people in Idlib and Aleppo governorates with emergency food and improve the resilience of the most vulnerable populations
project_objective:
The project aims to improve food security and livelihoods for IDPs and vulnerable households in Harim and Salqin camps, Maarrat Misrin, and Azaz in Aleppo and Idleb.
Objectives:
1. Free bread distribution for displaced people.
2. Promote CFW bread-baking and distribution jobs.
3. E-cash for food transfers to help IDPs and vulnerable households get food and other necessities.
4. To provide agricultural supplies, financial assistance, and guidance to local farmers.
5. To improve livelihoods by giving families egg-laying hens and fodder batches.

The project will reach 5841 households (29205 people), including 560 PWDs people. The project will implement free bread distribution, E-cash for food transfers, and agricultural and livestock programs.
Timeline: Contracting with vendors and bakeries, hiring field staff, and renting cars will take the first month of the eight-month project. Bread distribution will last 7 months, cash transfers will occur monthly for 6 rounds, and agricultural and livestock support will occur for 6 months.
Key Deliverables:
1. 6,933 bread packs will be baked and distributed daily in 25 camps.
According to the Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) group, each person should get 200 grams of bread per day. We will distribute 800-gram bread packs to families of various sizes to meet this recommendation. For the entire month, families with 1-4 members will receive 1 pack, 5-8 members will receive 2 packs, and 9+ members will receive 3 packs. Daily 800-gram packs will be distributed for 30 days. This distribution program will ensure that all family members get the recommended daily bread intake. 800 grams of loaves make up the bread pack.
2. IDPs and vulnerable households will receive six rounds of Conditional Unrestricted Vulnerability-based Cash e-vouchers worth $120 per household per round.
500 local farmers will receive agricultural supplies, financial assistance, and guidance.
Mixed-farming will reduce the risk of crop loss from climate change-related diseases and insect invasions.
Parallel lines will divide the half dunum of land. These crops are chosen by need.
The selection of crops is based on a need assessment that considers local farmers' experience, soil suitability, and natural water sources. Peas, beans, and spinach will be grown on the same land unit in polyculture.
4. Support for 500 families with 10 egg-laying hens and fodder for 6 months, including veterinary services. For six months, recipients will give 500 families 10 eggs a week to improve nutrition and social cohesion.
In order to apply voucher schemes for all beneficiaries, especially to ensure that beneficiaries supported by (Poultry kit) will give 10 eggs weekly/free to another family, we will use vouchers mechanism for receiving (Agriculture kit, poultry and fodder)
-500 vouchers for agriculture kit distribution (on-off)
500 in-kind poultry lit (10 hens) and 500 vouchers * 6 months for fodder = 3000 MWL will support 500 families to provide them with 10 Egg-Laying-Hens as one-time with fodder batches for 8 months and veterinary services. The kit composition/response package for SO2 and SO3 matches the poultry flock (10 hens, 1 rooster). Meanwhile, those families supported by poultry kits will give another 500 families under (specific criteria) 10 eggs weekly/free for 6 months to improve social cohesion and nutrition.
Afrin's Field Logistic assistant will ensure accurate procurement and contract documentation and transparent procurement. He or she will research suppliers, tender bids, vet suppliers and contractors, and process procurement approvals.
Expected Results: 1. Improved food security for displaced people through free bread distribution.
2. Improved food and basic needs access for IDPs and vulnerable households.
3. Improved livelihoods from agricultural support.
4. Improved livelihoods by supporting livestock.
5. Support egg-laying hen families to improve community nutrition and social cohesion.

project_name: Food assistance to vulnerable conflict affected populations in Northern Syria
project_objective:
As the Syria crisis moves into its twelfth year its impact continues to blight the present, and the future prospects of its population, with the impacts felt most negatively on the lives of vulnerable civilians across the country. In response to these needs, People in Need's (PIN's) project proposes to contribute towards saving and sustaining lives of targeted conflict-affected communities in Northern Syria through the provision of food assistance (multiple modalities). Responses between immediate needs and resilience- building will be adapted according to continuous assessments and analysis of the local contexts within a flexible and responsive framework.
Activities will be underpinned by emergency preparedness and response plans developed in coordination with relevant clusters, working groups, and partners – to promote timely, efficient and joined-up responses that seek to maximize geographic and sectoral coverage and minimize gaps. PIN will also focus upon assisting vulnerable, conflict-affected to meet basic food needs. Activities will target the most vulnerable households in communities chronically affected by the adverse impacts of the conflict, using common assistance modalities and selection criteria, per the recommendation of the working groups.
PIN will plan to reach beneficiaries with monthly food assistance (food baskets, food vouchers, MPCA), agriculture vouchers, and farmer field schools, and bakery support through reduced-price bread on a community level through providing contracted bakeries with 50% of flour and 50% of yeast to reduce the price of the bread price up to 40% in comparison with the free market bread price, while another activity targets only IDPs in camps free bread distribution where PIN provides 100% of flour and yeast needed and the baking cost to bakeries in order to distribute the bread for free to the targeted camps. Beneficiaries are targeted from both IDPs and host community members, meeting eligibility and vulnerability criteria to avoid creating tensions within and across communities. Selection criteria was elaborated in consultation with the affected communities, as well as based on evidence from previous project monitoring and community feedback obtained through the Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM), and include low-income families from the following groups: Female-headed households (FHH); Child-headed HH; Elderly-headed HH; HH with disabled and chronically ill members; HH with high dependency ratio; Unemployed male and female youth; Poor farming HH. PIN is aware that needs are different amongst gender and age groups, and other vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities. PIN aims to provide the most needed assistance by employing a wide spectrum of different activities to meet the distinct needs, establishing beneficiary selection criteria to prioritise the inclusion of those most vulnerable, and adapting its assistance delivery to promote access for the most vulnerable people. PINs programmes are coordinated with local authorities at various levels – from cross-border to hubs to district and village levels. PIN engages in regular dialogue with authorities to ensure transparency, accountability, and protection mainstreaming; including consultations and briefings on needs, humanitarian principles, PIN procedures, and beneficiary selection at projects' planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation stages.

That he does not have a fixed source of income

project_name: WATAN  2023 - Food Security and livelihood
project_objective:
More than 11 years of crisis have inflicted immense suffering on the civilian population, who have been subject to massive and systematic violations of international humanitarian and human rights law. More recently, the accelerating economic deterioration and impacts of climate change have increasingly become additional key drivers of needs, compounding vulnerabilities even further. The overall estimated Sector PIN for 2022 – of food insecure and those at risk of food insecurity – is estimated at 13.9 million, with 12 million facing acute food insecurity and 1.9 million people at risk of sliding into food insecurity. The acute food insecure figure includes 2 million people living in camps and deemed to be 100 per cent food insecure. FSA sector foresees an increase in the number of food-insecure households in 2023 (HNO 2023). 
The food security situation of Syrian families continues deteriorating which will lead to a possible increase in the number of food-insecure households in 2023. According to WFP RBC’s remote food security monitoring, in 2022, (especially female-headed) reported facing food shortages and engaging in some sort of food coping mechanism to maximize the use of little available resources. 
 Therefore, in order to improve the food security of the resident and displaced population, mitigate the negative coping mechanism, and restore income-generation opportunities to increase the state of food security, their livelihoods, and the population’s participation in economic life, WATAN Foundation designed the following axes taking into consideration the priorities of Food Security & Livelihoods cluster:

A. Food Assistance support
1- Cash and Voucher for food assistance [for 200 households]
2- Food basket distribution [for 200 households]
3- Ready-to-eat rations distribution [for 300 households]
4- Support the bread value chain and bakery rehabilitation support [for 5 bakeries, 1,000 beneficiaries]

B. Agriculture activities support
5- Supporting the wheat value chains [for 500 farmers];
5.1- Distribution of agricultural inputs including irrigation and harvesting costs, provision of technical extension sessions.
5.2- Rehabilitation of bakeries, flour mills, and silos for storage.
5.3-To purchase wheat from farmers and use it either in bread production (through a contract with flour mills and bakeries) or in wheat cultivation for the next season by contracting new farmers.
6- Supporting the olives value chains [for 500 farmers]
6.1- Distribution of agricultural inputs including irrigation and harvesting costs, provision of technical extension sessions.
7- Supporting the vegetable value chains [for 400 farmers];
7.1- Distribution of agricultural inputs including irrigation and harvesting costs, provision of technical extension sessions.
7.2- Supporting food processing and vegetable marketing.
7.3-Rehabilitation of canals, wells, and pumps through cash for work and service providers.
7.4- Support the solar-powered energy resources that support irrigation activities.
8- Supporting the legumes value chains [for 400 farmers];
8.1- Distribution of agricultural inputs including irrigation and harvesting costs, provision of technical extension sessions.
9- Supporting intercropping agricultural systems that include small-medium farming activities and home gardening in specific areas [for 500 farmers]
10- Support small business grants linked to agriculture activities [for 200 beneficiaries]

C. Livestock support
11- Supporting fodder crops cultivation [for 600 livestock breeders]
12- Vaccination campaigns (especially (PPR), LSD, bovine ephemeral fever, sheep pox, FMD), training, and support for local animal health service providers, [for 20,000 livestock breeders, including vaccination of 1200 animals]
13- Support livestock value chains for smallholder dairy [for 400 livestock breeders]

project_name: Integrated Multi-sectoral Response to the IDP and host in A'zaz and Afrin
project_objective:
The project is designed to respond to the needs of most vulnerable households in A’zaz and Afrin districts through meeting their food and WASH needs, response to the severe needs of winter season and strengthen the self-reliance and resilience of the affected communities through integrated 11 months intervention reaching out to 15000 individuals, supporting their priority needs and enabling them to shift to the early recovery stage. 
The intervention targets IDPs camps and host communities in Afrin, Raju, Suran and A’zaz sub-districts as these locations have been classified as one of the highest vulnerability scoring areas. 
The project consists of 3 pillars:

Food and WASH cash assistance worth $100 (In the format of MPC as e cards ): 
1- Distribution of e cards (cash value 65 USD) for 8 regular rounds and improving of food consumption scores for the targeted HHs, integrated with WASH needs (additional 35 USD) and responding to the needs of water trucking and hygiene promotion of the targeted HHs. 
2- Winter response: 
Distribution of Cash for winterization (oneoff 150 USD cash) and support the HHs to meet their urgent needs for heating and winter clothes. 
 3- Livelihoods and Early Recovery:
Improving the access of the targeted HHs to livelihood opportunities and basic services through the integration of ERL, FSL introductory vocational training, mentorship and small enterprises supports (Small business grants). DWHH will target the same markets hosting apprenticeship with market rehabilitation to enhance access and strengthen the market capacities to include higher number of apprenticeship and open the space for new enterprises. Vocational training will be, 240 participants will benefit of vocational training in the sewing, electrical maintenance and vehicles maintenance, beauty care and sewing. Out of 240 trainees, 120 trainees will be selected for mentorship programme which will be 3 months on-job training and 50 will be supported to start their own business. More focus will be given to existing to small business who will be encouraged to join the programme. The Vocational trainees will be selected from the same targeted locations supported by food and WASH cash assistance or locations targeted by winterization.  
4- Protection
WHH will aim to enhance the availability, sustainability and accesibility of quality and integrated protection services. For a total of 3000 individuals, the following activities will be conducted: awareness raising, case management services, capacity-building activities, community based protection committees and monitoring, GBV response, etc.


The project will target PWD, Youth and women specifically and will ensure involvement of the community through formation of community committees per each community and activation of CRM system via many channels of communication.

project_name: Strengthening the Livelihoods of the Vulnerable Population Groups in North-West Syria
project_objective:
According to HNO 2023  report and the primary need assessment that conducted by Women Support Association (WSA) in conjunction in Idleb,  Jarablus sub-districts and Azaz.
this project is developed to:
Firstly: support Wheat Value Chain (WVC) in 1200 hectares, which is expected to benefit 2400 smallholder households (12000 individuals. 3240 B, 3360 G, 3500 W, and 1900 M)   in 2023, 50% of targeted populations are female head households (FHH), and 30% are IDPs, will be supported with nitrogen fertilizers (such as urea 46%), fuel for supplementary irrigation, and harvesting cost support, for the 2023 season.
2- Purchase seeds from farmers the expected amount to be collected is 400 MT for grinding in  the summer of 2023, price per ton 480 $
Secondly, contribute towards addressing critical food insecurity aspects through enhancing access to bread in 2023.
1-WSA will conduct a detailed food security need assessment at the household level to identify 2400 families and 12000 individuals. 3240 B, 3360 G, 3500 W, and 1900 M) (50 % host community and 50% IDPs) with focusing on the most vulnerable segments of the population including( Female-HH caring for children, elderly, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, family with no source of income, as well as families with the largest number of women and girl.
2-Daily free bread distribution for a period of 5 months, targeting 2400 of the most vulnerable household 1 kg/day/HH. This activity will be materialized through supporting one bakery in Idlib and one in Jurablus with 60 MT flour/month and associated materials for bread production (yeast, salt), as well as covering the operational cost (fuel and labor).
the project will adhere to a Do No Harm approach (DNH), and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) to ensure quality livelihood services without causing any harm to the existing social system. WSA proposed program is cost-effective, and leverages existing operations and program resources, to maximize efficiency. As part of an exit strategy, WSA  will inform all relevant stakeholders of the exact project dates including closure from the onset of the project. WSA  M&E department will complete an end-line survey to gauge the outcome and output level results.

project_name: Emergency Food assistance to the IDPs in NW Syria
project_objective:
The food security situation in Syria has drastically deteriorated since last year. In 2023, an estimated 15 million people will need some form of food and agriculture assistance, representing 68 per cent of the total population. At least 12.1 million people are estimated to be food insecure, including all 2 million people living in camps who are deemed to be 100 per cent food insecure, and 2.9 million people are estimated to be at risk of food insecurity, an alarming increase of people at risk who could shift to become food insecure during 2023 if the crisis continues at same worsening levels. (HNO, 2023)
The proposed project will contribute to achieve the SO1:To Scale-up and sustain minimum food consumption needs through lifesaving and life-sustaining food assistance via swiftly addressing food insecurity of 11,000 households (50,600 individuals), where 5,000 households from the IDPs in Idleb and Afrin countryside will be supported via eight rounds of food distribution, After informing details of food distribution 3-7 days prior to the event, 5,000 households will receive food baskets for 8 months through small and multiple distribution points at each camp or village, all of the contents of the food basket will be selected based on the FSL recommendations and beneficiaries feedbacks on similar previous interventions, in addition to distribute a fresh bread on daily basis to 6,000 HHs (27,600 individuals) whom living in the camps in North of Syria for continues 6 months, where each family will receive 1 K.G of bread for 6 days a week for 6 months, 1350 MT flour of the milled wheat will be baked in local bakeries selected after a public tender taking in consideration that the quality of the bread should be inline with the global standards and inline with Syrian bread, the bread will be delivered to each camp on the morning, many distribution points in each camp will be to avoid the crowded lines.
People with disabilities PwDs will be given more attention during the selection and distribution where their rations will be delivered to their residences. 
in the distribution points, HIHFAD will separate tow line one for men and another for women, Also, all the project staff will attend PSEA training.
Ensuring the beneficiaries feedbacks and recommendations to inform the project implementation, a leaflet on feedback mechanism will be circulated during distribution in addition to PSEA leaflets.
Through setting a selection criteria based on vulnerability analysis, the most vulnerable groups among the IDP will be supported and they can reduce their likeliness of engaging negative coping mechanism, and their life-risks related to food shortage to be mitigated which will be verified through post distribution monitoring activities.
the project is considered as a planned.

project_name: Food and Cash Distribution for affected families in the Northwest Syria.
project_objective:
The project aims to increase the resilience of IDP Households who had to leave their houses due to the deterioration of their security status, as well as targeting a percentage of the host communities who match IYD’s selection criteria. The project will provide food rations on monthly basis for 12 months to 47,500 families in camps of Dana Sub-district in Idleb province. The same camps' beneficiaries will benefit from bread distribution every other day as a part of the general food assistance, which covers the minimum need. In addition, the project will distribute bread to beneficiaries in camps every other day as a part of the general food assistance, which covers the minimum need.

Furthermore, multi-round cash distributions of $ 70 will be provided to 4,000 HHs in Aleppo and Idleb divided as follow: Idleb, Idleb District, Maaret Tamsrin sub-district (Kafr Nabi, Kelly, North and South Shekh Bahr, and Maaret Elekhwan). Idleb, Harim District, Dana, Kafr Takharim, and Qourqeena sub-districts (Burdaqly, Kafr Takharim, Koknaya, Mashhad Ruhin, and Selwa).
Additionally, multi-round value voucher cash distributions will be provided to 37, 500 HHs in  Idleb divided as follow, 7,500 vulnerable families in Idlib District, Maaret Tamsrin sub-district will receive $ 80 Per HH per round. 30,000 families in camps of Dana Sub-district in Idleb province will receive $ 60 Per HH per round.  Here we should mention that beneficiaries benefiting from cash in Idleb are not the same targeted with food rations.
Also, IYD will distribute MPCA $100 per month per household for 4000 HHs on a regular basis for at least eight rounds (one round per month) has a significant positive impact on vulnerable household’s ability to meet their basic needs, improve household food security and reduce household usage of negative coping strategies among conflict-affected households (HHs) living in Al Bab, Arima, Dana, and Maaret Tamsrin sub-districts.
In addition to that, the project aims to improve food security for the newly displaced people households and most vulnerable families by providing emergency cash for food of $150 value for a one-off to 5,000 vulnerable households within the project-targeted sub-districts (1,000 HHs in Al-Bab, 1,000 HHs in Jarablus, 1,000 HHs in Harim, 1,000 HHs in Jebel Saman, and 1,000 HHs in Idleb). 

The IDPs are wholly dependent on humanitarian assistance for their daily needs, and the host communities in both provinces Aleppo and Idleb, are agricultural communities with very limited financial and livelihood resources, and the IDPs became a liability to the host communities because of this lack of livelihood, this issue is clearer in the areas where a limited number of NGOs provide humanitarian support. 

IYD's MEAL plan will be done by monitoring the implemented activities and evaluating the objective achievements, to ensure that the project meets the required quality and time frame, tackles challenges faced, and summarize lessons learned. The IYD’s MEAL team will prepare a post-distribution monitoring report, and the data analysis and issue the report with key findings.
IYD will share the 5Ws report with appropriate clusters in order to find the gap if any and coordinate more on the cluster level. Also, IYD will prepare a final narrative and financial report.

IYD will coordinate with the camps' management committee in Idleb only, and with local councils in Aleppo. This coordination will facilitate IYD’s work, especially in terms of data collection and verification, and assist in solving any disputes that might happen during the distribution.


Approximately 80 % of this project fund is secured

project_name: Prevention of Vector-Borne Diseases in Northern Syria
project_objective:
In order to continue to address the burden of vector-borne diseases and the leishmaniasis epidemic across northern Syria in particular, The MENTOR Initiative proposes to continue partnering with stakeholders and communities to ensure that the most vulnerable populations, such as IDPs and those with poor access to healthcare services, receive:
1. Prevention of leishmaniasis and other vector-borne disease transmission within their homes. MENTOR will provide protection to 555,602 households through an Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) campaign northern Syria of Idleb, Aleppo, Al-Hasakeh, Ar-Raqqa and Deir-ez-Zor governorates.
2. Raising awareness of leishmaniasis, other vector-borne and infectious diseases (such as cholera) and their transmission and prevention. MENTOR will run combined Information, Education Communication as well as Behaviour Change Communication (IEC/BCC) campaigns to ensure that households are empowered to prevent disease transmission in their communities. This will be achieved through leveraging the access that the IRS campaign provides and various other channels of communication, such as dedicated IEC workers, focus sessions and training key community representatives. This strategy will maximize the acceptance and uptake of IRS and sustainably increase knowledge and the capacity to self-protect in vulnerable communities, as well as improving healthcare seeking behaviour, which will in turn also improve disease surveillance.

project_name: Support vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities affected by conflict-related crises and climate change year 2023 to 2024 in the sub-prefectures of Liwa and Daboua (Lac province) with identifying and reducing protection vulnerabilities, as well as improving food security and WaSH to achieve safe and fair access
project_objective: La situation sécuritaire dans la Région du Lac due à la menace terroriste a occasionné la réduction de l'accès humanitaire et le rétrécissement de l'espace civique dans cette région, accroissant ainsi la vulnérabilité de la population. Les efforts déployés par le gouvernement ne parviennent pas à enrayer la situation, ce qui met à rude épreuve les actions des acteurs humanitaires. La mise en œuvre du présent projet apportera une réponse multisectorielle en répondant aux besoins en assistance alimentraires et protection des moyens d’existence, la WASH et la protection. Il attenuera la cette situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle précaire qui risque de se détériorer davantage en en période de soudure 2023 en raison des cocktails de crises de la province. Le projet sera mis en œuvre dans la sous-préfecture de Daboua, Liwa et Bagasola en complémentarités avec les autres acteurs humanitaires présents.

project_objective: Asistencia mediante mejoras a la infraestructura (Shelter, Wash, Infraestructura comunitaria) a las familias afectadas en los departamentos de Cortes y Yoro en los municipios de La Lima, Choloma y El Progreso

project_name: Fortalecimiento de las capacidades locales en coordinación y gestión de albergues con énfasis en la asistencia a poblaciones móviles.
project_objective:
En Honduras a raíz de los fenómenos naturales del 2020, más de 494,000 personas fueron desplazadas a albergues temporales, llegando a habilitarse más de 1,000 albergues. Se calcula que 33.541 personas buscaron auto albergues o se concentraron en asentamientos informales, donde su identificación y asistencia son más complicadas.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo fortalecer las capacidades locales de 10 comités de emergencia municipal (CODEM) en la gestión de albergues, comenzando por las instituciones gubernamentales, voluntarios de Cruz Roja Hondureña y creando un efecto multiplicador que pueda extenderse a los niveles comunitarios. Se incluirán protocolos armonizados de manejo de albergues y temas esenciales como los Estándares Mínimos Esfera, Estándares Mínimos para la Gestión de Albergues, Estándares de género y VBG en albergues, mecanismos de referenciación para casos de protección, VBG, PEAS, protección de la niñez, entre otros.
Cruz Roja Hondureña promueve los derechos de las personas migrantes y garantizar que satisfagan sus necesidades básicas; en ese sentido uno de los objetivos en el proyecto es implementar un programa de transferencia monetaria multipropósito (PTM) que permita cubrir las necesidades básicas a personas desplazadas y/o migrantes retornados, la identificación de beneficiarios se hará de acuerdo a criterios de selección enfocados en protección, genero e inclusión.

project_name: Ensuring access to basic primary and Early Childhood Development for out of school and schooling children in Aweil South County.
project_objective: In the proposed project, Save a Life International (SLI) will directly target 3,185 beneficiaries, among them being 2,000 Girls and 1,185 boys within Aweil South County.  Also, 75 new volunteer teachers will be identified, trained, recruited to support ECD and Primary school learning in targeted 47 schools. Further, 94 SMCs and 56 PTAs will have their capacity built to enable them to support Education activities in schools and in their respective communities. To achieve this, SLI will establish 3 new learning spaces and rehabilitate 4 existing ones to reduce congestion and allow for new enrollments. 94 new latrines will be established while 47 latrines will be rehabilitated across the 47 schools. All new and rehabilitated latrines will be equipped with hand washing facilities and will be segregated by gender. To increase enrollment and retention of out of school boys and girls, SLI will conduct back to learning campaigns at the Boma Level in close coordination with teachers, school management committees, parent teachers associations and Ministry of Education officials. The campaigns will be sustained for a period of twelve months to ensure enrollment and retention of boys and girls who are currently out of schools. Further, SLI will provide learning, teaching and recreation materials for pupils and teachers in all the targeted schools. To reduce incidences of school drop outs, SLI will work with community leaders, PTAs, Teachers and SMCs to monitor cases of school dropout, make follow up on cases and ensure readmission and retention in schools. Noting that adolescent girls who have reached the reproductive age miss schooling due to lack of menstrual hygiene training and materials, SLI will ensure girls are provided with reusable sanitary pads and soap. For an integrated response, SLI will work closely with child protection partners to conduct school and community based child protection monitoring, awareness on child protection concerns, making of referrals for specialized services. To reduce SGBV cases in schools, SLI will coordinate with GBV partners for information sharing in schools, GBV awareness and referrals. Prior to establishing new learning spaces and latrines, SLI will conduct in-depth consultation with Camp Coordination Mechanism and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) partners, community leaders and local administrators to address any underlying land issues and ownership before proceeding to establish or rehabilitate the facilities. In the current HRP call, FSL and Nutrition partners are expected to establish farming and nutrition demonstration sites/gardens. As such, SLI will coordinate with FSL and Nutrition partners to encourage pupils and teachers to participate in FSL and Nutrition activities conducted in demonstration gardens located within schools. Aware that the project will be implemented in Covid19 context, SLI will work closely with the Ministry of Health at the State and County level to ensure adherence to Covid19 protocols. Health partners will be engaged in Covid19 messaging in all schools targeted through the project. Wash partners will be engaged in during hygiene promotion in schools and in the community. SLI will participate in Education assessments and activities supported by the Ministry of Education, cluster and partners in Aweil South to ensure education needs that arise during implementation are identified and met as long as available resources allow.

project_name: Increasing equitable access to integrated preventative and lifesaving emergency nutrition services for affected populations in severity levels 4 and 5 in Fangak, Uror and Nyirol counties
project_objective:
The emergency this project will address is the high GAM rate in Fangak, Nyirol and Uror counties for children under 5. All three counties are rated at the severity of need classification 4 for acute malnutrition and food insecurity. GAM rates of U5 children are 19.6% in Nyirol, 22.2% in Fangak and 25.5% in Uror (NC PiN for 2023, 10 Nov 22). Malnutrition prevalence for PLW is 53.3% in Fangak, 71.9 % in Nyirol and 78.2% in Uror. The project will serve the payams of Manajang, Greater Pulita, Mareang and Phom in Fangak with a population of 115,524; the payams of Chuil, Pultruk, Thol, Nyambor, Pading and Waat in Nyirol with a population of 119,041; and the payams of Pathai and Tiam in Uror with a population of 61,840. 

Flooding from past years along with insecurity continue to cause disruption of nutrition service delivery. The project will use a combination of approaches to strengthen sustainable nutrition outcomes, specifically: 1) Increased program of preventative actions that reduce the rate of malnutrition and improve the sustainability of treatments; 2) Community engagement by taking services closer to households, through the roll out of the revised CNV guidelines and Family MAUC screening; 3) Facility-based data analysis and feedback information to improve overall performance of service delivery and timely coordination of response decision making; 4) Intensified integration of nutrition with complementary sectors by gap analysis and coordinating with co-located partners in FSL with NPA, ADA and Oxfam, in Protection with FCA and NP and in WASH with ACF, SI and Oxfam. At all sites, nutrition will be completely integrated with health services with HFO in Fangak and with CMA in Nyirol and Uror.

The project will use a combination of response modalities - RRM/ICRM, static, outreach and mobile approaches with nutrition survival kits to ensure timely response to emergencies. Services will be delivered from 24 static OTP-TSFP sites, and these sites will support mobile outreach services to cover displaced populations in 23 additional sites. The response activities will cover (1) case-finding screening using the Family-MUAC method from static units and mobile outreaches to IDP locations; (2) admission to OTP services for severe acute malnourished U5 children and TSFP services using expanded criteria where needed including malaria testing; (3) provide SC services for SAM children with medical complications; (4) deliver expanded MIYCN services to PLW and care-givers of children under 23 months through counselling PLW, care-providers and MtoM support groups, including vitamin A supplements, de-worming and kitchen gardens.

The critical outputs will be treatment of: 1) U5 SAM children – Fangak 1002, Nyirol 3024, Uror 1107 (Total 5133); 2) U5 MAM children – Fangak 1928, Nyirol 4950, Uror 1625 (Total 8503); 3) MAM for PLW – Fangak 908, Nyirol 3685, Uror 945 (Total 5538).

The project will mainstream protection and disability inclusion and emphasize gender and age considerations. To improve sustainability, this project will strengthen local capacity of CHDs, project staff and CNVs through job-relevant training. To address insecurity risks for PLW and U5 children, CMA will conduct safety audits and collaborate with the targeted communities to implement protection practices to reduce risk of SGBV. 

By applying IASC guidance, specific needs of men, women, boys and girls will be identified and addressed through a gender equity and social inclusion approach. In relation to AAP, the project will provide the information beneficiaries need to make informed decisions on accessing nutrition services, provide feedback on the interventions, share concerns and submit complaints. CMA will work with local authorities, leaders and beneficiaries, to ensure their inclusion in decision-making throughout the program cycle.

project_name: Improving access to and utilization of integrated essential health care services by all people in need including the vulnerable and crisis affected in Nyirol,Fangak and Uror Counties.
project_objective:
The main aim of this project is to address the challenges associated with access to and utilization of essential lifesaving emergency healthcare services by all people in need and endeavour to improve the same in Nyirol, Fangak and Uror Counties. This is in line with the Health Sector Response plan 2023 for South Sudan which emphasizes three objectives i.e. to improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations, reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases, enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms. 
The design of this project is anchored on improving access to essential life-saving health care services including maternal, child, adolescent health provision through static health facilities, medical mobile teams and community health volunteers. Renewed focus on sub-national health delivery systems and quality improvements and timely detection of disease outbreaks, investigation and response to by supporting and strengthening disease outbreak surveillance and response systems in Nyirol, Fangak and Uror Counties. Therefore, the emergency that this project will address is in respect of the high rate of mortality from the highly prevalent epidemic diseases. In the volatile context of Jonglei, the project will target Returnees, IDPs recently displaced by conflict and flooding, and host communities in areas with limited access to health services. Whereas the 2023 HC PIN is 106,887, 83,930 and 136,488 in Nyirol, Fangak and Uror respectively, this project targets 132,385 beneficiaries out of the HC target of 205,324 consisting of Host Community, IDPs and Returnees and disaggregated by County, age, gender and disability i.e. U5 =M11,769-F12,113, 6-17 yrs=M21,569-F27,438, 18-60yrs.=M21,357-F30,974, >60yrs=M2,441-F4,724. 
The flooding, limited food and income sources all have food insecurity and health implications. In order to achieve the expected results, the project will prioritize services through both community and clinical consultations (OPD) for curative, preventive and promotive services. It will focus on MNCH as well as improvement of HF infrastructure, HMIS and capacity building of personnel. Partners will support county M&E to collect data from health facilities and BHWs and enter into DHIS2. Data will be analyzed and used for decision making. Health education will be a key strategy in dealing with prevention and improving health seeking behavior. MNCH Services will include Health education; Immunization, ANC services, skilled delivery, postnatal care, IMNCI, HIV/PMTCT, BEMONC and referral. SGBV and MHPSS services to be provided will include Identification, counselling, GBV/CMR and proper referral for all including rape victims. This project will continue to increase COVID-19 vaccination coverage through HF and outreach-based services. 
It is envisaged that a successful implementation of these activities would significantly result in the overall decrease in morbidity and mortality arising from the epidemic prone diseases. It will further increase access to services for SGBV survivors, disabled individuals and people with mental health disorders. Besides improving resilience among vulnerable populations, the activities are further expected to benefit from an integrated response involving key sectors such as health, WASH, nutrition, FSL and protection. In order to ensure AAP, a mechanism will be provided for affected populations to receive the information needed to make informed decisions on accessing health services, provide feedback on the interventions, share concerns and submit complaints by involving all stakeholders.

project_name: Réponse intégrée de prévention et de protection des communautés affectées par l'insécurité dans les régions de Maradi,  Tillabéry et Tahoua.
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer les  mécanismes de prévention et protection des populations dans les zones d’urgences des régions de Tillaberi, Tahoua et Maradi à travers :
• Le mécanisme de monitoring communautaire basé sur une chaine de collectes et partages d’information sur la situation de protection notamment le suivi et le partage des incidents de protection, le suivi des mouvements des populations, l’identifications et le référencement des personnes à besoins spécifiques et les cas de protection. Pour se faire un réseau de points focaux et personnes ressources sera mis en place au niveau communautaire pour faciliter la collecte systémique des données hautement sensibles en situation d’urgence.
Cette collecte de données concernera aussi le monitoring régional en s’appuyant sur des informateurs clés afin de fournir les données filables et à temps sur toutes les communautés affectées ou vulnérables à la crise sécuritaire au Niger.
• Les évaluations rapides de protection dans les zones d’accueils et/ou lors des nouveaux mouvements de populations permettent d’identifier les problèmes de protection les plus urgents des ménages : les femmes, les hommes, les filles les garçons y compris les personnes à besoins spécifiques particulièrement les personnes vivant avec handicaps. Les résultats de ces évaluations servent à orienter les réponses de protection en identifiant les besoins immédiats.
 • Des comités de préventions et gestion des tensions intercommunautaires seront redynamisés. Ils seront également chargés de la prévention à travers des sensibilisations, médiations et signalement dans leurs zones respectives pour la prévention et l’atténuation des risques éventuels de tensions intercommunautaires et interethniques dans ces zones  
• La promotion de l’implication, l’engagement et la participation de la communauté́ pour une prise en charge efficace des enfants dans un contexte d’urgence, et ce conformément aux standards pour la protection de l’enfant. Les principales interventions au niveau des mécanismes communautaires visent à renforcer les capacités de la communauté́ à :
- Identifier et signaler les enfants et les familles vulnérables aux acteurs sociaux compétents sur le terrain, y compris le signalement d'enfants gravement touchés aux services spécialisés ; 
- Elaborer des systèmes de remontées de plaintes permettant aux enfants et membres de la communauté́ de dénoncer ces abus en-dehors des mécanismes  communautaires pour la protection de l’enfant ;
- Promouvoir une documentation adaptée aux enfants et soutenir les organisations et les initiatives des enfants.
• Des comités de prévention/référencement des VBG, seront mises en place et/ou redynamisés dans les villages d’intervention du projet à Tahoua, Tillabéry et Maradi. Ces structures seront chargées de veiller à la prévention, l’identification, le référencement et le suivi des cas de protection, de VBG et la mobilisation communautaire au tour des problématiques de protection dans un contexte d’urgence. 
• La création d’un environnement protecteur aux personnes déplacées internes à travers des évaluations rapides de leur situation suivi d’assistance en kits.

project_name: Enfrentando los desafíos para responder a las necesidades humanitarias de las personas en movilidad a través de la gestión y coordinación de asistencia, servicios y acciones de protección en albergues
project_objective:
Guatemala enfrenta una variedad de desafíos y necesidades humanitarias resultantes de factores y amenazas estructurales comunes, tales como: alta pobreza, colapsos climáticos recurrentes, violencia crónica, acceso limitado a los servicios, migración y desplazamientos masivos, entre otros. Estos desafíos y amenazas estructurales afectan profundamente a las poblaciones y comunidades, y que están relacionadas con los factores de vulnerabilidad interrelacionadas. 

Guatemala fue severamente afectada por las tormentas tropicales ETA e IOTA en el 2020, principalmente las comunidades rurales o parte de barrios marginales de las ciudades. A finales del año 2022 las tormentas Julia y Lisa también afectaron los diversos territorios de país, principalmente a las comunidades indígenas en condiciones extremadamente vulnerables.  

Los impactos de la pandemia por COVID-19 y la temporada de huracanes más activa registrada en la historia (enfrentada por la NCA en 2020), exacerbaron la complejidad de la crisis humanitaria estructural, mientras que los niveles de resiliencia de la población, necesarios para enfrentar futuras amenazas externas, están en su punto más bajo. La pandemia y las tormentas provocaron un aumento en el número de personas que necesitan asistencia humanitaria en Guatemala y Centro América. 

La urgencia y desesperación sigue empujando y aumentando la movilidad humana. El desplazamiento interno y la migración se están incrementando, particularmente en las personas más afectadas y en condición de vulnerabilidad. 

Por lo anterior, la coordinación y la gestión de albergues adecuada es urgente para asegurar el acceso a servicios básicos frente a los desastres, ya que son eventos cada vez más recurrentes en el territorio. Para que esto sea posible, es necesario mejorar, así como facilitar la disponibilidad y el acceso a espacios de refugio para personas en movilidad humana. 

Esta intervención brindará asistencia vital a familias desplazadas por emergencia, en tránsito y personas retornadas, con herramientas que faciliten el ejercicio de sus derechos fundamentales y la construcción para la resiliencia, tomado en consideración las necesidades individuales y las acciones de protección ante la violencia basada en género.

project_name: Access to Education for Refugees, IDPs and Host Communities in Ruweng (Parieng), South Sudan
project_objective:
Ruweng Administrative Area  currently hosts about 124,000 Sudanese refugees and at least 4,868 internally displaced persons(IDPS) who have moved from Benitu due to the flooding. This has posed increased challenges to the already stretched service delivery point in the area. Available records from the Area Ministry of Education indicates that 83 learning facilities in the Administrative Area are currently not operational due to lack of paid teachers. Additionally safe learning environment remains a huge challenge with over 90%  of all learning centers in the area are temporary structures.. This intervention is geared at providing education for learners in the host communities of the Ruweng Administrative Area (Parieng). Below are the goal and three principal objectives of the proposed intervention:
Goal: Increase access to inclusive quality education for host community children especially girls and children with disabilities

Objective1:
Improve equitable access to safe and protective education services for 4550 emergency affected IDPs, returnees, spontaneous refugees, and host community children including children with disabilities and youth (girls and boys).

Objective 2:
Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Objective 3:
Strengthen/enhance the education system’s response capacity of the school community and national/local education actors to mitigate the impact of existing emergencies on learners, teachers, and communities

Target:
Some of these refugee learners will be hosted by within the existing refugee schools located in the Ajuong Thok and Pamir refugee camps and will therefore together with the refugee learners directly benefit from this intervention 
•	4,264 learners (2,132F, 2,132M) at ECD, primary & secondary levels 
•	76 (20F, 56M) teachers and head teachers 
•	 200(100F,100M) executives and members of PTAs/SMCs/BoGs
•	10 (3F, 7M) Area Education leadership members
