project_name: Provision of basic lifesaving WASH services among Rohingya refugees and Host Communities in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective: BRAC will design projects for the JRP 2023 aiming to enhance the quality and ensure equitable access to WASH services with establishment of susceptible, cost-efficient and sustainable WASH services targeting the gaps of ten camps (1E, 1W, 2E, 2W, 3, 10, 14, 20Ext, 21, 25). BRAC project design includes integration with relevant sectors and special focus on protection, skill development in both the refugee and host communities and entrepreneurship development in the host community. BRAC will also focus community engagement and building ownership for ensuring regular repair and maintenance of WASH facilities by strengthening capacity of the WASH management committee and user groups where women leadership will be ensured. The sector will consider comprehensive and inclusive approaches to tailor the needs for ensuring WASH services through sex-disaggregated data, person with disability data, LGBTQ+ and with key steps in the implementing processes. BRAC will continue to prioritize water quality at household level and at water points. This will include periodical water quality testing, along with operation and maintenance of water sources, treatment, and equitable distribution of water to the target population. BRAC has piloted RWHS in camp and gets very positive learning from the pilot. To reduce the tension of groundwater depletion, BRAC will also install rainwater harvesting systems at both communities based on previous learning, use of surface water treatment and take initiative for ground water recharge. In addition to regular repair and maintenance of WASH facilities BRAC will also upgrade and construct new WASH facilities as per needs focusing the reallocation of Rohingya and in the gap areas in coordination with CIC, RRRC and DPHE offices and address the needs of the special vulnerable groups such as women, children & adolescents, elderly people, person with disability and LGBTQ+. BRAC will allocate 74% and 26% of the proposed funds for refugees and host communities respectively. BRAC will work for the enterprise development and linkages on plastic waste management and environment friendly reusable sanitary napkin production to make a sustainable supply chain of WASH products for both the refugee and host communities. BRAC will be strengthening collaboration and coordination with donor agencies and WASH sector to fill the WASH gaps where needed. BRAC will also be working with the local organization on WASH and will work for the capacity building of the local WASH organization under the pool funding. BRAC has project implementation quality (PIQ) indicators based on which project monitoring plan will be developed in alignment with the JRP monitoring framework and will be monitored periodically by the BRAC MEAL team for the improvement and necessary adjustment of the WASH programme. BRAC will continue with emphasis on preventing high-risk behaviour and thus enabling safe water use, healthy hygiene practice and solid waste containment through the integration with health, nutrition, and education and protection sectors. BRAC will have a contingency plan to address AWD outbreak, Covid-19 aftermath, Scabies, dengue prevention, special incident & monsoon rain, cyclone & and any other natural disaster in host and Rohingya community. BRAC will also develop different knowledge products and conduct research on FSM in collaboration with international University, engage the private sector in FSM  & advocacy on WASH. WASH sector strategies and the guidelines will be followed in all stages of the implementation without any overlapping considering CHS standards and AAP principle. BRAC has a very rich and historical background in managing WASH programs in different approaches such as enterprise development, micro-financing and private sector engagement and those knowledge and  learnings will be capitalized for the improvement of the BRAC WASH response as and where  needed.

project_name: Inclusive specialized (Rehab, PSS, SRHR) services forvulnerable persons including persons with disabilities in Cox'sBazar Rohingya camps and host communities
project_objective:
By addressing immediate acute and chronic health needs of refugees and host communities through multi-sectoral mobile units as well as center-based services, HI is continuing more than 13 years of broad support for refugees and FDMNs. The proposed intervention will be delivered through twin modality:
1. Multisectoral mobile units comprised of qualified nurses, physiotherapists, MHPSS officers, protection officers and social workers will be deployed to identify and provide tailored and individual assistance to those most vulnerable, especially persons with disabilities and their caregivers that might not be able to access services due to mobility or social barriers. In this setting, mobile teams deliver services focused on educating beneficiaries and their caregivers on safe, effective therapeutic exercises and reasonable accommodations.
2. Static points: Multidisciplinary teams support beneficiaries with rehabilitation, MHPSS, basic healthcare through nurses and protection. Training is provided to persons and caregivers on basic home-based rehabilitation and proper use, maintenance and repair of mobility devices. Group & individual sessions on MHPSS and assessment for protection beneficiaries take place.
-In home-based and center-based services, Nurses will support beneficiaries with: wound care, bedsores care, ante and post-natal care. A key focus will be to provide maternal care for women who cannot access health facilities (i.e. women and girls with disabilities), including the prevention and detection of pregnancy- related risks and complications. Nurses refer to the nearest Health Facility and follow up to ensure they receive needed specialized services.
- Support to government hospitals and health facilities both in the host and refugee communities to provide rehabilitation services. HI coordinates at Age & Disability Working Group (ADWG) as co-founder to provide services to unserved camps if disability specific services are required. HI also have modality of outreach rehabilitation team to serve the areas where HI does not serve on regular basis.
- PSEA focals are assigned at each site offices who ensure PSEA principles are mainstreamed through all activities through extensive training of all staff and volunteers using PSEA Network materials and recommendations. Various forms of feedback are regularly collected, including suggestion boxes, hotlines for refugee communities and community discussions. To ensure referral for needed services and survivor advocacy, a dedicated Focal Point is assigned in the Cox's Bazar base to receive complaints.
HI is currently implementing five projects that address the above mentioned health services. HI supports 5 health facilities including Cox's Bazar Sadar hospital, Ukhiya Upazila health complex, Teknaf Upazila health complex, KTP MSF-OCA-331 and IOM Leda-200 with physiotherapists providing rehabilitation services. These facilities serve refugees as well as beneficiaries from the host community.
Beneficiaries' complaints and feedback are welcome as part of the project activities. At present, different complaints and feedback collection modalities exist in both host communities and camps, which are led by the HI MEAL team.
Face-to-face interviews, group discussions, a hotline, and feedback boxes are the methods HI uses to provide prompt solutions to complaints.
Support women, men, boys and girls in the camps with basic nursing and SRHR services (ANC, PNC, FP awareness), with a focus on vulnerable populations (persons with disabilities, pregnant women, older people, chronically ill people and those who are unable to access the facilities).
The total budget targeted for HI in 2023 is $2,464,732. Of that, $1,864,731 has already been secured from different donors ($1,326,973 for refugees and $1,137,759 for host communities) with the remaining $6,000,00 likely to be secured, but not confirmed, but HI is appealing for this amount.

project_name: Répondre aux besoins en soins de santé primaire et mentale des populations touchées par la crise dans les régions de Tillaberi et Tahoua (frontières du Mali et du Burkina Faso) du Niger par un mécanisme de réponse rapide (RRM) et un soutien aux services existants, Phase 3
project_objective: Le projet répond aux besoins des Sante et Protection dans les régions de Tillabery et Tahoua pour le déplacé et la population touche par la crise de ces deux régions. L'intervention sera réalisé avec le biais d'une approche RRM, dans le but global de fournir une assistance sanitaire et des soins MH vitaux aux populations déplacées et hôtes touchées par la crise par le biais de RRM et d'un soutien aux services de santé existants. En particulier pour ce que concerne le secteur de sante l’action vise à améliorer l'accès à des SSP de qualité répondant aux besoins en SSP (santé physique et mentale) des populations déplacées et hôtes affectées par la crise. En revanche  rapportent  au volet de protection l’action contribué à l’amélioration du  bien-être psychosocial des populations déplacées et hôtes affectées par la crise à travers le renforcement : de la stratégie mobile par le déploiement de cliniques mobiles ; de  l'offre de soins au niveau communautaire ; de la capacité des services de santé primaire, de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial ;des soins de santé mentale par le déploiement de psychologues formés pour fournir un soutien en matière de santé mentale aux personnes qui en ont besoin, et par la fourniture d'une formation technique supplémentaire au personnel de santé mentale et de soins de santé ; de la gestion des cas de VBG ; et la formation des équipes médicales du consortium à la prise en charge clinique des survivants de violences sexuelles, y compris les enfants survivants, conformément aux directives internationales actualisées pour la prise en charge clinique des survivants de viols. Les secteurs de la protection et de la santé ne sont pas mis en œuvre comme deux programmes distincts et autonomes, mais comme deux composantes liées d'une même activité. Les questions de protection qui peuvent se poser dans les établissements de santé sont transmises et suivies par les membres de la communauté qui ont été sensibilisés par l'activité. L'action proposée par COOPI facilitera l'accès des femmes et des filles aux processus décisionnels en abordant les obstacles liés au genre afin que toutes les filles et tous les garçons, femmes et hommes puissent bénéficiaires des activité implémentées par le projet. Les communautés et les hommes et garçons seront aussi engagé afin de les sensibiliser sur la question de l'égalité des sexes dans la société.  L'équipe de COOPI recevra une formation spécifique sur la PSEA et la GBV, et du personnel féminin sera recruté dans les secteurs d'intervention afin de garantir l'accès aux femmes bénéficiaires.

project_name: Promoting comprehensive primary, SRH and NCD health services including MHPSS services for Rohingya refugees and host communities in Teknaf and Ukhia sub-districts in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh
project_objective:
The IRC Bangladesh is one of the important health partners of Health Sector in Cox’s Bazar in Rohingya response and will be providing essential health services focusing Maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health (MNCAH), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) including adolescent SRH, Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) including MHPSS and Communicable Diseases (CD) from 04 Primary Health Care Centers (PHC) (camp 6, 11, 22 and 25), 01 BEmONC Center (camp 2E PHC) with Inpatient Department (IPD) services, 13 Referral Hubs, and community health components in different camps especially. A NCD clinic will be established in camp 11 to cover the NCD needs in this camp as well as in the surrounding few camps. 
The 24/7 PHC services from 4 PHCs will be guided by health sector approved Minimum Package of Essential Health Services (MPEHS) for Rohingya people. In camp 6 and 11 PHCs, a coordinate approach will be considered with SRC/BDRCS. In camp 2E PHC, the IRC will work in coordination with BDRCS/SRC to fill the comprehensive SRH services (ANC, PNC, FP, CMR, STI, MR, PAC) including normal vaginal delivery (NVD) services and 24/7 IPD services. All these health facilities will have adequate clinical & support staff (staffing norms stipulated in the MPEHS) and logistic support to ensure free health care services for the targeted beneficiaries and these facilities will be backed up by comprehensive diagnostic laboratories to ensure proper diagnosis to prevent unnecessary referrals to secondary/tertiary level care facilities. An adequate supply of essential medicines and quality of medical commodities will be ensured with temperature-controlled warehouse/storage management for ensuring pharma qualities. Under the guidance of the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR), the IRC will continue to maintain 4 surge Mobile Medical Teams (MMTs) in camp 6, 11 and 25. An additional MMT will be formed in camp 22 based on the gaps and need in this camp. Adequate Emergency Preparedness for health facilities and required capacity building of MMTs will be targeting natural disasters and artificial hazards in Cox’s Bazar (Fire, Monsoon rain, Cyclone, Floods) and epidemic-prone Infectious/communicable disease through training and simulations. Reporting of health services to DHIS2, 4Ws and Early Warning, Alert and Response System (EWARS) will be done regularly and on time. 

The IRC supported Referral Hubs (RH) in 13 camps (4, 4E, 6, 7, 8E, 8W, 12, 13, 19, 20, 20E, 26 and 27) is to ensure referral and transportation support for patients with emergency obstetric conditions and other medical emergencies to access to PHC/BEmONC facilities through community health volunteers and deployed ambulances. These hubs will work closely in coordination with PHCs and BEmONC facilities and CHWs in these respective camps. The IRC will expand community health component in coordination with community health working group (CHWG) within Rohingya camps especially in camp 11 and 25. The aim of this intervention is to enhance the capacity of Rohingya people in terms of increasing knowledge on health seeking behaviors especially on MNCH, SRH, NCD and to work on gender norms to influence this behaviour. Male engagement activities in MNCH, family planning (FP) and SRH will be periodized. Additionally, needs of children, adolescents, youth and old in all their diversity (gender, age, disability, ethnicity) will also be addressed. IRC will focus on Sex, Age and Disability Disaggregated Data (SADDD) for program quality improvement. 
The IRC will coordinate with BBC Media Action to mainstreaming AAP by building capacities of project staff members, producing community facing contents, also assist partner agencies to establish CFRM and analysis of feedback for programme development. The insights from rigorous research are shared among the organization so that aid worker can take necessary measure in effective community engagement and accountability.

project_name: Humanitarian protection including GBV assistance to Rohingya refugees and host community of Cox’s Bazar
project_objective: This project consists of 3 components: 1- GBV Prevention and Risk Mitigation, 2-GBV Response and 3-GBV Coordination and Advocacy which will be implemented in 3 Women and Girl Safe Spaces (WGSS) in camps 5, 18, 25, four PHCC in camps 25, eight nutrition centers in camps 13, 14, 15, 16, 22 and two GBV service points in Ratnapalong and Holiapalong and two WGSS in Nhilla & Jalia Palong. Response activities will be implemented by IRC and prevention activities by 6 local partners 4 of which are women-led. Component 1 GBV Prevention. Result: Social Norms support women and girls’ rights: outcomes are that social norms support women and girls’ rights and condemn GBV. Girl Shine will focus on empowering adolescent girls to acquire skills to identify GBV, access services and assert their rights. Structured PSS for male and female caregivers will help to ensure a protective environment for adolescents. EA$E includes women’s economic empowerment interventions. It will create a pathway for income generation, enhance women’s access to financial resources, foster healthy dynamics within households and build women’s business skills to develop business plans. EMAP will address the root causes of GBV by engaging men and transforming men’s beliefs and attitudes towards gender and violence. SASA! Together will use a community mobilization approach to support communities to create positive and sustainable changes around norms underlying GBV. Community engagement and outreach will be conducted using integrated community outreach module to facilitate diverse women’s and girls’ access, including those with disabilities, to services in the WGSS. IRC will provide dignity kits to women and girls at risk including GBV survivors. Safety audits will be conducted including risk mitigation measures and GBV risk mapping, allowing the community to take the lead in creating a safe environment for women and girls. Component 2 GBV Responses. Result: GBV Services are safe and accessible Outcomes: 1. quality GBV services are accessible, well equipped and provide safe spaces for confidential care. 2. Female service providers have the attitudes, skills, training, and supervision support to provide competent care to GBV survivors; 3. GBV services are effectively planned, managed, resourced and operational. (i) GBV Case Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and activities Through WGSS IRC will ensure availability and access to quality GBV case management, PSS services, and referrals delivered by frontline service providers trained by IRC according to GBV Case Management Guidelines. Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) services will be available in 3 WGSS, including SRH clinics and information sessions delivered by midwives. IRC will develop capacity to provide case management services to male GBV survivors by ensuring Health-GBV integration in primary health centers. IRC will collect, store, and analyze case management data in-line with the information sharing protocol (ISP) using GBVIMS and GBVIMS+. Community volunteers (Community outreach members) will be used to link case management services to the community through information dissemination, training, and referrals. IRC will roll-out Women Rise, a structured PSS group curriculum run by GBV actors. A referral system will be maintained and disseminated within the community. IRC will support beneficiaries to use a complaint and feedback mechanism incorporating safeguarding. Service providers will receive training on GBV case management, basic PSS, and GBV core concepts to improve quality of care. IRC will adapt WGSS in settings responding to natural disasters from the onset of the emergency to relief and recovery phases. Component 3: Advocacy and Coordination IRC will raise funds and influence government policy and legislation. It will provide technical support to capacitate state actors, religious and community leaders to address GBV

project_name: Assistance wash aux déplacés internes, retournées et communautés hotes affectées par la crise humanitaire et aux inondations dans la région de Diffa
project_objective: L'accès aux services d'EHA est un droit fondamental aussi bien en période de stabilité qu’en période de crise, dans des contextes urbains et ruraux. Lorsque les enfants, et particulièrement les jeunes filles, les femmes et les personnes à besoins spécifiques n'ont pas accès à de l'eau potable ou à des activités visant aux changements de comportement sur les bonnes pratiques d'hygiènes dans le but ultime de prévenir les maladies liées à l'eau et à l'assainissement, cela pourrait avoir un impact négatif sur leur santé, leur nutrition, leur éducation, leur sécurité et bien être et tous les autres aspects de leur vie. Cette intervention vise à favoriser un environnement sur et protecteur  pour les femmes, les hommes, les jeunes filles et garçons y compris les personnes à besoins spécifiques et à mobilité réduite, un accès continu et durable à une quantité minimale d’eau potable de 15l/pp/jour, à un endroit de défécation approprié, protégé et adapté aux circonstances, à la promotion des bonnes pratiques de l'hygiène et le soutien aux efforts de prévention et réponse aux maladies tels que le cholera et la Covid-19 au niveau de toutes les couches concernées. Les activités proposées seront implémentées dans la région de Diffa, département  Bosso et N'Guigmi et touchera 21 044 personnes déplacées internes, retournées, communautés hôtes et les sinistrées dont 56,20% sont des jeunes filles et garçons de moins de 18 ans  vivant sur les sites de  Toumour et le site de N'Guigmi.  En effet, lors de la mise en œuvre des activités, les mobilisateurs communautaires wash supervisés par les experts wash vont utiliser des canaux de communication appropriés au contexte du projet pour expliquer à la communauté les messages clés de l'intervention tout en prenant en compte du groupe le plus à risque et/ou le plus impliqué dans la promotion des bonnes pratiques au niveau de l'habitation et de la famille comme les femmes et les enfants.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Aussi, COOPI utilisera une approche considérable en collaboration avec la DRHA/Diffa, le mécanisme qui permettra de connaitre les habitudes culturelles de la communauté ciblée pour influencer leurs préférences en matière d'infrastructures EHA et qui pourront facilement entretenir périodiquement sans aucune subvention externe tout en prenant en compte les aspects liés au genre et et aux personnes à besoins spécifiques.  En outre, il convient de rappeler que toutes les infrastructures d'Assainissement tels que la constructions/réhabilitations des latrines familiales et d'urgences, les dispositifs locaux de lavage des mains seront érigées  par les ménages eux-mêmes à travers des activités cash for work et qui favorise le transfert de compétence et l'implémentation de l'approche rurale participative. L'action proposée par COOPI facilitera l'accès des femmes et des filles aux processus décisionnels en abordant les obstacles liés au genre afin que toutes les filles et tous les garçons, femmes et hommes puissent bénéficiaires des activité implémentées par le projet. Les communautés et les hommes et garçons seront aussi engagé afin de les sensibiliser sur la question de l'égalité des sexes dans la société.  L'équipe de COOPI recevra une formation spécifique sur la PSEA et la GBV, et du personnel féminin sera recruté dans les secteurs d'intervention afin de garantir l'accès aux femmes bénéficiaires.

project_name: Renforcer la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigue chez les IDP et les communautés hôtes du département de Ouallam -région de Tillabery
project_objective:
GOAL soutiendra les activités de nutrition curative (CRENAS/CRENI) au niveau des centres de santé ainsi celles de la prévention de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire (relais,PB mères etc.) tout en renforçant la coordination des acteurs. L’objectif principal est de contribuer à réduire la mortalité et la morbidité chez les enfants de moins de cinq en facilitant le dépistage et la prise en charge précoce de cas. GOAL entend à travers cette intervention consolider les acquis du projet issu du financement de fond régional pour l’Afrique de ouest et du centre à travers OCHA. Il s’agira pour GOAL d’élargir sa couverture mais aussi de renforcer la qualité de la prise en charge dans tout le DS de Ouallam. Le DS de Ouallam à une population estimée en 2022 à 469.186 personnes dont 100.932 des enfants de moins de 5 ans soit 23,03%(source Pop DS Ouallam 2022).L’appui concernera 32 CSI, l’unité de stabilisation (CRENI) du DS de Ouallam et ciblera 6744 enfants 6-59 mois souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère. Le taux de la malnutrition aigue sévère à Tillabery étant de 1,3 %selon l'enquête SMART nutrition de 2022 et tenant compte de l’incidence de la malnutrition de 2,6 . Aussi 548 enfants avec malnutrition sévère avec complications médicales sont attendus au CRENI (source INS 2021). Les mères accompagnantes de enfants au CRENI bénéficieront également un appui en aliments et auront une formation sur le dépistage au MUAC en plus de sensibilisations sur les PFE et ANJE.
Les actions se focaliseront également sur le renforcement de capacité des acteurs communautaires et des agents de santé à travers la mise en œuvre et ou le suivi de l'approche Health  surge pour renforcer la résilience du système de santé. Les activités qui seront appuyées comprennent le dépistage de la malnutrition et le référencement des cas, la vaccination, mise en place des dispositifs de lavage des mains, Approche PB mères, les sensibilisations ANJE/PFE contre la COVID-19

project_name: Assistance aux systemes d'approvisionnement en eau pour un acces equitable des IDPs a l'eau et aux infrastructures sanitaires a Ouallam et Ayorou
project_objective:
Par le présent projet, GOAL Niger vise à apporter une assistance WASH aux personnes déplacés internes ainsi que leur communauté d’accueil sur les sites de deplaces internes d'Ayorou et de Ouallam, region de Tillaberi. Cette assistance concernera l'accès à l'eau potable, la promotion des latrines et la sensibilisation sur l'hygiène et la Covid-19,  tout en garantissant la protection des plus vulnérables.
en rappel, grace au financement acquis aupres de BPRM, GOAL va augmenter la capacites de production de la station de pompage d'Ayorou, faire une extension du reseau vers le site des refugies et deplaces internes, ainsi que la subvention de l'eau a environ quelques centaines de menages tres vulnerables a Ayorou.
Ainsi, notre présente action dans le sous-secteur de l'eau visera à consolider les acquis en
-  étendant la subvention de l'eau a 10500 personnes vulnérables parmi les IDPs et les communautés hôtes de Ayorou et Ouallam conformément aux normes du cluster (minimum 10 litres / jour/personnes) pendant 10 mois. Une enquête HEA sera conduite afin de mener un ciblage qui prendra en compte de manière intentionnelle les besoins des personnes et/ou des groupes les plus vulnérables à savoir les ménages des personnes vivant avec handicap, ceux dirigés par des femmes ou des enfants, ceux accueillant des enfants non accompagnés, les ménages avec les personnes âgées. 
- promouvoir la purification de l'eau dans les 4 localités à travers un appui à la vulgarisation des purifiants par des opérateurs économiques privés. l'objectif étant de disposer d'au moins un revendeur de purifiants d'eau dans chacune des localités.
Pour l'hygiène et assainissement:
pour combattre la défécation a l'aire libre et améliorer les pratiques d'hygiène de base, GOAL se propose 
- d'initier un dialogue communautaire (community conversation) et convenir d’un plan d’action basé sur le renforcement du système en faveur des latrines améliorées au niveau des sites et des communautés hôtes. 
- appuyer les communautés cibles en kits d'hygiène WASH classique (savons, bidons vides, kit de digne pour les femmes et jeunes filles, etc). 
- appuyer le système de marche de l'assainissement en stimulant la demande des latrines améliores (campagne de sensibilisation suivant l'approche Community Lead Action), et incitant une offre attrayante (disponibiliser des équipements adaptes, hygiéniques auprès des acteurs prives locaux, formation des maçons locaux, mesures de subvention desdits équipements, plan de promotion)  
 Pour susciter davantage la demande, des concours inter quartiers d'hygiène et assainissement seront lancés sur chaque sites avec l'adhésion des bénéficiaires. les critères établis par les bénéficiaires, seront évalués par des jurys locaux et les lauréats récompensés par des kits WASH. Nous envisageons de former/recycler une vingtaine de maçons privés, équipés pour la construction des latrines améliorées dans les 4 localités. Ces maçons seront utilisés pour la construction de latrines familiales améliorées principalement à Ayorou et Mangaïsé, mais également sur les autres sites suivant les besoins.
Ainsi 3 000 kits NFI WASH seront  partagés aux bénéficiaires. Environ 60 relais communautaires seront identifies et formés/recycles pour accompagner les champions des secteurs.
- GOAL utilisera également la sensibilisation digitale vocale compte tenu de la bonne pénétration du réseau téléphonique, en collaboration avec son partenaire stratégique VIAMO.
Enfin, une campagne de sensibilisation radiophonique sera entreprise à travers les 3  radios communautaires de Ayorou,  Ouallam et Tondikiwindi, sur les thématiques de l'hygiène assainissement et de la COVID-19.

project_name: Enhancing Community Safety, Peaceful Coexistence and Access to Justice for Refugee and Host communities in Cox Bazar
project_objective: The main objective of the project is to improve protection, safety and security and enhance access to justice and peaceful coexistence between refugees and host communities (HC) in Cox's Bazar. The project will give particular attention to vulnerable groups such as women, elderly and people with specific needs. The project will provide a forum through which refugees and host communities will have improved access to protection services and conflict resolution mechanisms, as well as access to legal assistance and victim support services. The expected results will reinforce the capacities of actors that are currently working on community safety and security, justice and protection in both refugee and host communities, focusing on addressing crime prevention, access to relevant safety and legal services, promoting women and youth empowerment, and responding to any violation of rights. The interventions proposed are based on the findings of a community safety pilot project carried out in camps and HC in 2020 and 2021, which emphasized the need for increased police presence in the camps and capacity building of actors on refugee law, GBV, counter trafficking, protection principles and community outreach and conflict resolution. The project will focus on coordinating with law enforcement agencies and the judiciary to ensure refugees and host communities have access to justice and they are aware about reporting mechanism. The project will contribute towards improving governance of the relevant institutions. In implementing the project, the agencies will ensure that persons with different age-gender and other background can benefit equitably from the activities. The project will be jointly implemented by UNDP, UNHCR and IOM in close collaboration with the RRRC and Camp in Charges, APBn, District Police, local government institutions and Judiciary in Cox’s Bazar. The propsed proposal will have synergy with many projects implemented by the UN agency, INGOs and NGOs to contribute the peaceful-coexistence between and among the host and camp communities.

project_name: Renforcement des mécanismes de prévention et de protection de l'enfance dans les régions de Diffa et de Maradi.
project_objective:
Tout en s’alignant sur les priorités du cadre sectoriel du SCPE pour 2023, le présent projet d’une durée de 6 mois (juillet – décembre 2023) entend assurer la continuité des interventions de IRC (les projets en cours s'acheveront en Juin 2023) dans les régions de Diffa et Maradi en matière de la prévention et réponse aux violences, abus et négligence dont sont exposées et victimes les enfants. Il se propose de contribuer à l’amélioration de l’environnement protecteur des enfants dans les départements Diffa, Bosso, N’guigmi et Mainé Sorao (région de Diffa) et Guidan Roumdji (région de Maradi) à travers la mise en œuvre simultanée des activités de prévention (activités de sensibilisation sur les problématiques de protection de l'enfance, des espaces de bien-être et d’apprentissage) et de prise en charge des cas de protection de l’enfant (fourniture de services de PSS, prise en charge alternatives et gestion de cas des ES/ENA et des autres cas d'enfants à besoins spécifiques). 
Par ailleurs, la mise en place des activités conjointe avec d’autres secteurs notamment des évaluations conjointes Protection de l’enfant – Violences Basées sur le Genre - Education - favorisera l’intersectorialité à travers des interventions ciblées. Le système de référencement des enfants aux fins d’une réponse adaptée aux besoins est un des points d’intersection entre les activités de protection de l’enfant pour renforcer la multisectorialité de la réponse et enfin contribuer aux différents objectifs stratégiques. 
S’alignant sur les objectifs sectoriels du Sous-Cluster Protection de l’Enfance, le projet touchera 6,820 bénéficiaires (3,492 hommes et 3,328 femmes) y compris 2,865 enfants à travers les activités de 1) de réalisation des évaluations de la situation de protection de l’enfant, 2) la fourniture des services de soutien psychosocial via les centres SHLS et l’approche SAFE développée par IRC, 3) l’assistance individualisée/gestion des cas pour les enfants affectés (ENA/ES, EAFGA, Enfants victimes et à risques de protection) avec possible réunification familiale et accès à la documentation civile ; 4) sensibilisation  des communautés pour prévenir les risques de protection, renforcer leurs résiliences aux chocs et faciliter la création d’un environnement protecteur. 
Aussi, pour faire face aux défis d’accès à la réponse psychosociale énorme constaté dans la region de Diffa, IRC prévoit de renforcer les capacités endogènes en plus de développement des interventions mobiles (PSS de groupe à travers l’approche mobile) en particulier dans la commune de Bosso (village de Baroua) ; en plus des interventions et plaidoyers pour lutter contre le mariage des enfants/précoce. La collaboration avec le sous-cluster VBG et autre secteurs (éducation) pour mettre en place une cartographie conjointe des services favorisant l’accès à la réponse pour les garçons/hommes est également utile.  
IRC prévoit de gérer au moins 135  cas d'enfants vulnérables durant les 6 mois d’intervention dans les 5 départements ciblés. La gestion des cas relatifs à la protection de l’enfance se déroulera de préférence au domicile de l’enfant ou dans tout espace jugé sûr et confortable pour l’enfant et pour les adultes aidant l’enfant à se rétablir. 
IRC continuera à soutenir les comités de protection communautaire existants pour renforcer leurs capacités et les aider à identifier activement et à référer les cas de protection de l'enfance à la DRPE ou aux agents de cas de l'IRC. IRC continuera de veiller à ce que les membres de ces comités comprennent les concepts de protection de l’enfant et le développement de l’enfant, afin d’identifier de manière appropriée les problèmes de protection et de prendre en compte les opinions et les préférences de l’enfant, en fonction de son âge et de sa maturité. Les nouveaux membres du comité de protection de l'enfance seront formés à la fourniture de premiers secours psychosociaux (PFA).

project_name: Education Support to IDPs and Returnees
project_objective:
The Syrian crisis has weakened intensely the capacity of the education system to address basic education needs. According to the Ministry of Education (MoE) over 120,000 teachers required capacity development, an estimated 180,000 educational personnel have left the education system and around 5,722 schools are either damaged or destroyed which has caused an acute need for additional safe learning spaces across the country affecting 2.45 million out of school. Education needs and  gaps are also compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic which resulted to children drop out and a setback in learning.  
The project aims to enhance equitably and quality access to education to crisis affected IDPs, returnees and vulnerable children aged between 5-17 years. Several barriers prohibit children from being in school. Schools are destroyed or unsafe, some children feel unsafe on the way to school or while in school due to lack of electricity especially for the second shift students, families have had to displace to areas where schools are no longer available; as a result schools in safe areas are overcrowded and tensions between host community and those who were displaced have increased, lack of documentation prevent children from accessing primary and/or secondary education in which case, children may be exposed to higher risks of child labour, early marriage and social protection. Beyond that, the socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic combined with the currency depreciation has placed additional challenges for children in accessing education imposing children to work to support their families and families’ ability to afford school expenses such as school uniform, stationery, and transportation continue to be a key reason for children are not attending school.
UNHCR education intervention includes the provision of non-formal education in community centres. The non-formal education activities will enhance the school enrolment of out of school children and the retention of children with low school performance. School rehabilitation will be very limited as a last resort and part of a comprehensive intervention in priority return areas. UNHCR pays specific attention to the future adolescents and youth populations that can contribute to resilience and social cohesion in their communities through facilitating their access to education. In line to age gender and diversity, accountability to affected population and rights-based approaches, UNHCR will reach out to children and their parents during project monitoring activities and through focus group discussion seeking feedback including receipt of complaints regarding the project. Resources permit, UNHCR plans to provide non-formal education activities to over 185,000 children and rehabilitation of around 150 classrooms.

project_name: Innovative Socio-Economic Development through providing MSMEs grants and establishment of Vocational Training Centers in Idleb districts
project_objective:
This project is a multi-pronged approach, serving at both individual and community levels in both basic sectors and Livelihood Support for the target beneficiaries and Early Recovery by stimulating the economic growth of the target communities.
The project is going to be implemented within 12 months to achieve:
The Overall Objective is To reform and strengthen the performance of the local economic system and scaling-up the community resilience in NW Syria.
BINAA will work to achieve this objective through four main interventions:
1st: Providing an MSME grant of 1,000 USD to 500 beneficiaries to establish new business projects or repair or resume existing ones that are heavily affected by the war or the current Covid-19 pandemic.
Initial beneficiaries (M/F), women-headed households, PWDs, and other vulnerable segments such as families having child-labour are a priority, to be targeted, where 2-day sessions, be conducted to develop the Business Plans ""BPs"" and apply to the grant, and then, BINAA team be evaluating the submitted proposals, select the best projects to be supported, and identify the final beneficiaries of the grants.
Afterward, providing to the finally selected beneficiaries a 5-day Training Program on Entrepreneurship Skills to build their capacities in managing and sustaining their businesses.
The grant is to be provided in the form of CASH for assets and into several payments to ensure that the beneficiary is committing, achieving good progress, and being businesslike to receive the next payments. Additionally, BINAA, to provide 200 USD to the most successful 50 projects, (representing 10% of BNFs), as additional monetary bonuses, be given based on hard work and noticeable progress.
2nd: Providing Vocational Training (VT) for 300 males and females and PWDs, paid for three months, and then, providing Internship Training within the private sector, also paid for 3 months, to link them to the market.
The appropriate professions and training are according to two groups:
1. The professions do not require any qualifications e.g. Hairdressing and Sewing.
2. The professions require relevant experience e.g. Computer Maintenance and Web Development.
Three months paid internship are to be provided by contracting with business owners in the private sector, who are willing to accommodate the trainees and provide them with the Internship and BINAA will provide allowances to the beneficiaries for three months of VT and three months of Internship, $120 a month (totaling $360), which is empowering the beneficiary to gain the trust of the employer and gain practical experience.

Within the continuous Covid-19 pandemic, BINAA be supporting and ensuring all precautionary measures through disinfecting meeting venues before and after each meeting, distributing masks to attendees, printing guiding instructions and caution signs everywhere, and also, selecting suitable venues that be primarily accessible by women and PwDs and having all comfort facilities for both genders.

project_name: Strengthening resilience and enhancing physical access through the provision of road-infrastructure restoration service and rehabilitation of flood-affected roads and associated flood drainage systems around prioritized IDP camp sites in Idleb
project_objective:
Based on the ERL Cluster, HNAP, HNO, and IMMAP reports, and BINAA Need Assessment (all in 2022), the overall development challenge of the target area is represented in increased poverty, absence of community services, the tension between hosts and IDPs, less access to markets, damaged roads, minimal employment opportunities, and widespread negative coping mechanisms.
Recurrent floods in NW Syria in winter severely impact physical access to IDP sites by rendering roads completely or partially impassable. Heavy rains trigger flooding, primarily affecting self-settled IDP sites, which do not have the appropriate infrastructure to withstand this elemental onslaught and negatively impact the physical access for IDPs as well as the safety and dignity of residents. This further limits access to markets, livelihood opportunities, health, and other critical services.
The project will provide critical improvements to road and associated flood drainage infrastructure through: 
1. Rehabilitating critical flood-affected roads and drainage systems that connect IDP sites to host communities in Harem.
2. Creating short-term work opportunities to involve local community members to directly contribute to and benefit from preventative rehabilitation works. 
3. Training the local communities on Asset Management aspects to improve the sustainability of infrastructure and increase social cohesion.
The interlinked ERL activities have been developed in coordination with the ERL, SNFI, CCCM, and Logistics Clusters, where:
*First, the project will rehabilitate 40 km of roads and 5 km of drainage systems in immediate proximity to 35 IDP sites flood-affected in Idleb.
*Second, the project will engage 400 people in CFW activities, including rehabilitating closed canals of road drainage systems, road paving for road shoulder support, road painting and marking, and installing road signboards.
*Third, the project will train 250 key stakeholders on asset management to ensure that the infrastructure will be maintained beyond the project.
The project aims to provide road infrastructure restoration for flood-affected IDP communities, simultaneously creating short-term livelihood opportunities.
The project will directly benefit 2,000 individuals (400 HHs) under the CFW, and specifically, ERL activities will directly benefit 200,000 individuals in Harem (40,000 HHs) from the rehabilitated community infrastructures and ensured access to 35 IDP sites.
Transfer Modalities going to be used in the project are identified based on Need Assessment and Market Assessment, in addition to secondary data collected from HRP, HNAP, and Clusters Reports.
Designing the CFW component has been done following the Do No Harm approach, where consulting community/local stakeholders at the area level, especially for the daily wage rate, the number of working hours per day, and project duration, in addition, to ensuring the CFW daily wage rates do not distort local labor market and draw workers away from local employment opportunities, not harming local producers, and not arbitrarily introducing non-sustainable practices.
Each beneficiary must be paid the wages for four months, 132 USD for each month, totaling 528 USD, divided into four payments, “one a month” to help the beneficiaries to secure their households’ needs for living.
Payment is according to his/her timesheet, paid money in his/her village by the contracted Hawala agency to ensure protection-mainstreaming and safety, where each worker is provided with the Payment Slip showing the # of working days and due amount.
BINAA has a proven track record in the rehabilitation of roads and drainage systems, as well as in the creation of livelihood opportunities. This will strengthen overall risk management and ensure timely implementation of the project along with the high quality of activities and deliverables. project_name: Garantizar supervivencia de niñas y niños con desnutrición aguda a través de identificación y tratamientos oportunos y cuidado nutricional y de salud integral materno infantil en Escuintla y Suchitepéquez, Guatemala
project_objective:
Los desastres naturales recientemente vividos en el área de Escuintla y Suchitepéquez (tormentas e inundaciones) incluyendo secuelas de la pandemia de COVID (aún no resueltos) y de la Guerra de Ucrania (actualmente por el incremento de precios de combustible y alimentos), se ha visto reflejada en el aumento de la inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional en el área.  A pesar de que el total de niñas y niños con desnutrición aguda reportados ha disminuido en 2022 comparado a 2021 (probablemente por la falta de identificación), el porcentaje de desnutrición aguda severa ha aumentado considerablemente alcanzando hasta 21% y 35% de los casos de desnutrición en los departamentos de Escuintla y Suchitepéquez, respectivamente.  Esta situación es sumamente preocupante porque aumenta asimismo el riesgo de muerte por esta causa. Se implementarán acciones integrales de atención nutricional y salud a través de “brigadas integrales” que llegan hasta las comunidades más lejanas y donde la presencia y acceso a los servicios de salud es muy limitada.  La pertinencia de esta Estrategia ha sido validada y ha probado ser efectiva desde 2018 en contexto de emergencias.  La Estrategia ha sido tan efectiva que ha logrado identificar y tratar oportunamente a niñas y niños afectados por desnutrición aguda que no habían sido detectados previamente por salud (hasta un 68%). Es un abordaje estandarizado y monitoreado que ha sido mejorado y complementado hasta que el día de hoy brindan atención integral a la niñez  (evaluación nutricional, tratamiento oportuno, suplementación con micronutrientes múltiples en polvo, zinc y vitamina A, desparasitación, consejería alrededor de los temas de la Ventana de los 1,000 días, vacunación) y a las mujeres en edad fértil incluyendo adolescentes, embarazadas y en período de lactancia (evaluación nutricional, suplementación con hierro y ácido fólico, vacunación y consejería).  Adicionalmente, para complementar las acciones, estas brigadas dejan formados “agentes de cambio” (líderes y lideresas formados en aspectos básicos para identificación oportuna de desnutrición aguda, signos de peligro, y alimentación infantil e higiene) para orientar a su comunidad.

El proyecto responde a los siguientes objetivos:

•	Identificar la población afectada por desnutrición aguda y brindar tratamiento inmediato
para salvar sus vidas.
•	Mejorar las competencias del personal de salud y otros actores locales para la atención
nutricional en emergencias
•	Brindar insumos necesarios para el cuidado nutricional
•	Fortalecer capacidades de líderes y lideresas comunitarias en la preparación y respuesta para la atención nutricional en emergencias
•	Activar sistemas de alerta temprana nutricional en la comunidad

project_name: Nutrition Sensitive-Agriculture and Livelihood intervention for the FDMN and vulnerable host communities in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh

Food processing, preservation of various types of foods and promotion and small business will improve household income. The project will ensure dissemination of key information on climate smart agriculture, training on livelihoods targeting the most vulnerable population including pregnant and lactating women (PLW), husbands of the PLW, elderly people. 
Activities includes:

ii. Facilitate participatory cooking sessions to develop innovative nutritious recipes
iii. Support small livestock production and increase household income
iv. Capacity building for the small businesses to improved household income

project_name: Green graduation programme
project_objective:
Green Graduation programme as a graduation Programme will include four main pillars: social protection, livelihood promotion, financial inclusion and social empowerment. It will provide a comprehensive and sequenced package of support over a fixed period.  This simultaneously will improve livelihoods and income and provides access to basic services including financial services.  As Green Graduation, the Programme will apply a green lens to every stage of programme cycle and strive to address social and economic inequalities whilst taking a transformative approach to tackling negative environmental practices. It will ensure a Do No Harm approach [to the environment] whilst improving livelihoods and building the resilience of communities. Green graduation programme will provide an integrated support that includes consumption support via regular cash transfers, business training, coaching, increased knowledge on nutrition, asset transfers to help beneficiaries develop their own sustainable income-generating activity (IGA), savings assistance through establishment and running of viable Voluntary/Village Saving and Loan Associations; support environment protection initiatives; and additional trainings including Men Engage (topics on household governance, gender-based violence, working together as partners, making decisions as a team, sexual and reproductive health-HIV, education of children…), Women life skills, livestock rearing, improved farming practices, awareness on environment and other natural resource protection. The programme will be implemented in different phases/cohorts and activities will be the same for each cohort. Due to lack of viable partners in Sila, Concern will use direct implementation strategy. Yet, the organization will explore ways to engage with one active Association that works on social cohesion and pacific cohabitation and provides capacity building training to improve their capabilities; we already have a list of preselected local associations (that worked with DIZA Programme and PIRCS) and that the final selection process will be undertaken at the beginning of the project. The programme will also work closely with government representatives in charge of overseeing the different intervention in the province through MOUs. 

Targets: Total: 7,400 HH / 36 260 individuals
Male: 17 767 individuals
Female: 18 493
Full graduation package beneficiaries (included in the Total):
Total: 2,400 HH/ 11,760 Individuals
Male: 5,762 individuals
Female: 5,998 individuals
Vulnerable group: female-headed households; households with persons with disabilities (PWD), serious illness, elderly; Orphans heading HH; very poor farmers and Sedentary pastoralists

project_name: Improve food security through provision of emergency food and enhance food production of food insecure housholds in Aweil North, Aweil West, Aweil South, NBeG State, South Sudan
project_objective: Given the high level of food insecurity, Concern will continue to provide FSL support to most vulnerable households in Aweil North, Aweil West and Aweil South Counties in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG) state while the nutrition sensitive agriculture support is integrated across all nutrition centres in Juba IDP camp in Central Equatoria and Guit County in Unity State.  Concern will provide access to food, agriculture inputs and improve agriculture production to prevent famine and support vegetable production to improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations. Concern will engage with the County Agriculture Department (CAD), extension workers and lead farmers for training on agriculture extension services and Climate Smart Agriculture practices, informal seeds systems, pest and post-harvest management. Concern will also support vegetable production across all targeted location to increase HHs dietary diversity and contributing to improved complementary feeding practices among children 6-23 months of age. Considering asset depletion, crop losses due to flooding, inflation and limited access to livelihood, hunger is expected to deepen due mainly to depleted food stocks and high food prices therefore Concern in partnership with WFP in NBeG continue to provide emergency food assistance through General Food Distribution, School Feeding Program and Cash/Food for Asset program.

project_name: Promouvoir la protection et la cohésion sociale entre les populations déplacées et les communautés hôtes de Ouallam,Tillabery
project_objective:
GOAL est présente sur les 4 sites des déplacés de Ouallam à savoir Ouallam, Tondikiwindi, Diney et Mangaizé, sur financement de OCHA (FRHAOC) dans les secteurs de la santé (Cliniques mobiles), nutrition, Abris et biens non alimentaires. GOAL vise à travers ce nouveau projet à donner une réponse aux gaps en contribuant aux Objectifs Spécifiques  du cluster protection, en renforçant la cohésion sociale par une sensibilisation sur les thématiques de la protection et de la redevabilité ainsi que des actions d’accompagnement et d'assistance ABNA/CASH pour certains vulnérables, dans les sites IDPs des communes rurales de Tondikiwindi et Ouallam, dudit département. Le projet ciblera intentionnellement parmi les populations déplacées et les communautés hôtes les veuves, les ménages dirigés par les femmes ou les enfants, les personnes vivant avec handicap, les vieillards, les familles accueillant les enfants non accompagnés, les jeunes filles, les élèves déplacés. L’éveil des consciences général et le renforcement de l’autonomisation financière se feront à travers des formations, des sensibilisations sur les thématiques de protections et des remises des kits de protection ou de réhabilitation. Ainsi le projet contribuera en:
 • Formant les personnels sur la sécurité, l'équipe genre et inclusion sociale, les droits des enfants et leurs protections, la protection transversale, la redevabilité, PSEA et le plaidoyer lobbying, Do No Harm.
 • Mettant en place un cadre d'écoute et d'échange favorables aux plus vulnérables notamment les PVH, les femmes. Ainsi, des points focaux genre sensible seront identifiés avec les communautés suivant le zonage existant sur chaque site (ou ajuste au besoin). Ces points focaux et les mobilisateurs communautaires seront formes et accompagnes sur l'équité genre et inclusion sociale, les droits des enfants et leurs protections, la protection transversale, la redevabilité, PSEA et le plaidoyer lobbying) pour mieux prendre en compte les intérêts des plus vulnérables. GN s'appuiera sur l'existant en termes de structuration tout en le renforçant. 
• mettant en relation les points focaux protection avec les autres acteurs clés de la  protection de leurs zones pour le référencement au besoin, renforcer le circuit de référencement et contre référencement dans la zone.
 • collaborant avec les autres partenaires intervenant dans les programmes pour une meilleure prise en compte des plus vulnérables dans leurs ciblages. 
• Organisant des conférences débats sur la cohésion sociale et/ou Organisation d'émissions radios sur la paix et la réconciliation. 
• Créant et diffuser des messages de sensibilisation via la plateforme de service Viamo et les ondes des radios communautaires.
 • Organisant des séances de sensibilisation sur la prévention au COVID-19.
 • Mettant en place un mécanisme d’Ecoute & de Gestion des Plaintes. 
• Renforçant et promouvant les activités génératrices de revenus comme le maraichage, VSLA, la savonnerie, la teinturerie, tricotage etc au profit de vulnérables (veuves, enfant chef de ménage) pour renforcer leur autonomisation. Compte tenu du contexte sécuritaire, toutes les formations se feront à Ouallam. GOAL intervient toujours en collaboration avec les autorités locales, les services techniques déconcentrés, les bénéficiaires, les partenaires présents. Tags PRP Organizations GOAL Implementing Partners ONG GOAL travaillera avec les services techniques déconcentrés concernés, les autorités locales et traditionnelles, les structures gestionnaires des sites, les structures communautaires, les SCAP-RU et le comité départemental de gestion de catastrophe et reponse d'urgence, sous la coordination de OCHA, pour éviter la duplication infructueuse des actions. Comme à son habitude, les roles de chaque structures notamment les services techniques et autorités locales seront précisés dans un protocole de mise en exécution qui sera établi avec les autorités compétentes

project_name: Supporting food insecure and vulnerable households with FSL programming in North Darfur and South Kordofan by GOAL in 2023
project_objective:
In North Darfur, GOAL works closely with the Ministries of Agriculture and Animal Resources in Khartoum and in North Darfur as well as FAO on identifying needs/gaps, coverage and program implementation. In addition, GOAL remains an active participating in the FSL Cluster at both national and state levels where FSL programming is implemented, including North Darfur. GOAL’s FSL programming is closely integrated with
other sectors, especially nutrition, health, and protection through targeting vulnerable households (including affected by malnutrition, people living with disabilities, and women headed households) in catchment areas of supported clinics. GOAL will also incorporate protection and women’s empowerment approaches. GOAL proposes to focus on the IDP populations in Kutum Town as well as Kassab and Fata Borno Camps near Kutum to reach vulnerable host communities in Kutum and Al Waha localities to ensure all relevant communities have their needs addressed. Activities are closely coordinated with other FSL actors in North Darfur to eliminate any duplication of effort. Through the FSL Cluster and Cash Working
Groups. GOAL incorporates and shares lessons learned and harmonized approaches to livelihoods activities in order to maintain high technical standards in its work. In South Kordofan, GOAL will work with Village Development Committee (VDC) in areas where they are already established and functional. If the VDC are not available, GOAL will work community leaders to form a VDC consisting of community leaders, including influential community members (such as teachers, health workers, religious leaders etc.) as selected by
community members. A close effort will be made to ensure that gender representation is observed in the composition of VDC members. GOAL will identify and support existing Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) in the targeted areas to provide training and ongoing monitoring and care for the distributed animals. GOAL will provide refresher training to CAHWs and facilitate their work, in particular by supporting their transportation to rural and IDPs areas, as the lack of vehicles or resources for transport has been identified as a major challenge to effective support for animal welfare services across South Kordofan. GOAL has identified that displaced households in North Darfur and South Kordofan are facing multiple shocks including the looming drought that will severely lead to limited livelihoods, which has come on top of economic erosion, failed harvests that are stretching the lean season, tribal violence in South Kordofan, and displacement. In response, GOAL plans to target 800 households with Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC) transfers in order to meet immediate food security needs and to prevent further deterioration of assets and use of more harmful coping strategies, and to put households in a better position to engage in productive livelihoods in the future.

project_name: Establishing and Supporting Learning Opportunities for Conflict affected Children in the NWSW
project_objective: Since 2016, the North West and South West regions of Cameroon have witnessed a socio-political crisis which has deteriorated overtime with violent clashes between armed forces and Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) which have led to loss of lives and property, internal displacement, attacks on education and a growing climate of fear and incertitude. Much of this violence is targeted at local communities and, in particular, at schools, with teachers frequently facing attacks in the form of kidnapping, harassment, decapitation and killing, while children have been exposed to a number of protection risks such as harassment, exploitation, abuse and recruitment and some have been killed due to the crisis. The NSAG have adopted school boycott/disruption strategy since 2017 to apply pressure on government in the form of Monday ‘ghost-towns’ and other spontaneous calls for ‘lockdowns’, especially on commemorated national days, sometimes lasting for several days and even weeks. The school boycott strategy has had a severe impact on children’s ability to attend school, learn and retain previously learnt content. Calls for a return to normal functioning of schools from different individual, national and humanitarian actors have been challenged by other separatist groups. In addition to the threats and direct acts of violence leading to school disruptions, other factors such as social media misinformation, false alarms and panic have led to the further disruption of school activities. The ongoing violence has left some 700,000 children out of school in the Northwest and Southwest regions and over the last four years, increased attacks on schools have been recorded and over two thirds of the schools are now closed. On its part, the reaction by the international community has not been robust enough in terms of condemnation and action to ensure that the right to education is upheld. The Norwegian Refugee Council has referred to the crisis in Cameroon as one of the most neglected in the world. This research seeks to identify and provide an overview of all the converging factors leading to disruption of school activities, outline a timeline of school attacks, and provide an educational needs assessment for children of school going age in the Anglophone regions. It provides a brief background to what is now known as the Anglophone crisis, a timeline on attacks in schools and other factors including, social media misinformation, false alarms and panic, leading to further disruption of school activities. Around 7 million learners are currently affected by schools’ closure, of these an estimated 15% of children live in the NWSW region. In order to ensure education continuity and mitigate the impact of school closing, the Education Cluster is developing an Education response plan in line with National response strategy that includes measures to mitigate the impact of school closure. These measures include rapidly adapting distance education and community sensitization on COVID- 19. Plan International aligns the HPD strategies with the National response strategy, NWSW COVID 19 Readiness and Response Guidance in the NWSW, Education Cluster, COVID-19 Risk and Mitigation plan, the NWSW Education Cluster Response Annex and Plan Global Education COVID 19 Response considerations. Plan on the ground will coordinate and work closely with the WASH and Protection partners including Plan’s WASH, NFI and CPiE thematic areas, to ensure vulnerable girls and boys affected by the conflict and closure of schools and non-formal learning spaces due to COVID 19, access education and minimize on the lost time for learning.

project_name: Promotion of peace for vulnerable people affected by protracted conflict in South Sudan
project_objective: According to the recent Faith Actors case study (2019-20), the main driver of the current crisis has been the armed conflict (between the Government and opposition forces) from 2015 - 2018 which led to multiple displacements of civilian populations resulting in a total loss of livelihoods. Furthermore, the competition for natural resources is the main cause of violent intra/inter communal conflicts in the some states. Pastoralist communities compete for access to grazing land, water, fishing areas and these drivers are exacerbated by civilians having access to guns, erosion of moral authority of local and traditional leaders, weak states institutions to protect the population and a culture of cattle rustling. The majority of the youths that participate in conflicts have less education, are not employed and have disengaged with the traditional authorities. This makes it easy for the youths to be easy targets for recruitment into the army or local militia groups. Local conflicts and militarization are linked to increasing poverty, sexual and gender based violence (SGBV), psychological abuse, denial of education and economic opportunity, have a profound effect on women and girls. It is currently estimated that 50 % of girls in South Sudan are married off before 18 years and 7% marry below ages of 15. Girls are usually considered as a means for transfer of wealth (dowries). Adolescent birth rates in South Sudan are estimated at 300/1000 females aged 15-19. SGBV is promoted by a culture of silence and stigma, linked to masculine identity tied to cattle raiding, bride price, no access to legal recourse, and customary practices that promote crimes like rape. The ineffective justice system limits access to justice for victims and prosecution of perpetrators of violence. The proposed project will help enable durable solutions for IDPs and other population on peace building and peaceful co-existence. World Vision will conduct awareness raising activities and trainings on conflict resolution and peacebuilding with women, men, girls and boys in the former states of Warrap, Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Western Equatoria. World Vision will work on reducing barriers to engagement in resilience building, food security and income generating activities, especially for women and youth; increasing anticipatory, absorptive, and adaptive capacity with respect to disruptive events including natural disasters and conflict as well as create cohesion among community members in the target counties so that conflicts will be reduced.

project_name: Assistance en Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène pour les déplacés et les communautés hôtes affectés par le conflit dans 4 régions du Burkina Faso (Sahel, Nord, Centre-Nord et Boucle du Mouhoun)
project_objective:
L’aggravation de la crise sécuritaire au Burkina Faso depuis 2015 et la multiplication des incidents dans 6 régions depuis juin 2018 dues au conflit qui oppose les groupes d’opposition armés et les forces armées burkinabé d’une part et au conflit communautaire d’autre part, a occasionné des mouvements de population sans précédents au Burkina Faso (principalement dans le Sahel, le Centre-Nord, le Nord et l’Est) et a contribué à la dégradation de la situation humanitaire. Selon les derniers chiffres publiés par OCHA, le nombre de déplacés internes aurait atteint 1 761 915 personnes en octobre 2022. Depuis le début de la crise, on a pu observer que les populations affectées ont tendance à se déplacer vers les centres urbains où elles sont pour la plupart accueillies par la communauté hôte ; ce qui occasionne une forte pression sur les infrastructures en eau et assainissement et ne favorise pas l’application des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène. A ceci s’ajoute une crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle, et des vandalisassions récurrentes des infrastructures en eau par les groupes armés. 
Selon les récentes évaluations EHA réalisées par SI dans ses zones d’intervention, il apparaît que 14% des ménages (hôtes et PDIs) enquêtés n’ont pas accès à une source d’eau salubre. Et selon l’enquête MSNA réalisée par REACH dans les 20 provinces d’accueil de personnes déplacées, 51% des ménages (hôtes et PDIs) utilisent des latrines non hygiéniques ou défèquent à l’air libre.
SI est présente au Burkina Faso depuis octobre 2018 et a déjà réalisé plus de 300 réhabilitations de points d’eau, près de 4200 latrines d’urgence et communautaires, réhabilité 21 latrines institutionnelles dans les écoles, réhabilité les infrastructures d’assainissement dans 16 centres de santé, distribué plus de 46 000 kits d’hygiène pour les déplacés et 1000 kits d’hygiène pour les enfants malnutris, sensibilisé près de 400 000 personnes aux bonnes pratiques en termes d’EHA.
Fort de cette expérience et d’une connaissance approfondie du contexte, SI propose de répondre aux besoins de    80080 personnes affectées à travers la réalisation d’activités en Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène dans les sites d’accueil des déplacés et dans les communautés hôtes.

project_name: Addressing Adverse Drivers of Human Mobility through Emergency Livelihoods Support in Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims to support vulnerable mobile populations, including internally displaced persons (IDPs) and migrants as well as their host communities to address food insecurity and enhance socioeconomic stability through improving access to livelihood opportunities. This will be achieved through support to agricultural and livestock-related income generating activities for approximately 60,000 individuals (15,288 men, 15,912 women, 14,112 boys and 14,688 girls) and at least 15 per cent of the target group will be persons with disabilities. The target population will also consist of IDPs, vulnerable migrants, and host community members, all targeted based on their needs. IOM will apply a people-centered approach with community based planning to improve conditions in target areas and ensure that interventions are based on needs and the rights of the vulnerable migrants and communities to access food and improved livelihood opportunities.
The project will focus on communities across Blue Nile, Gedaref, Red Sea, Kassala, South Kordofan, and West Kordofan; when possible it will also focus on vulnerable communities in Darfur. IDPs, returnees, migrants, and local communities in these areas were already vulnerable to food insecurity and limited livelihood opportunities prior to the outbreak of fighting in April 2023 between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF), due to limited purchasing power resulting from inflation and high staple food prices. Now, in light of recent events, existing vulnerabilities have been drastically increased and many people have found themselves newly or secondarily displaced, lacking liquidity and without livelihood opportunities. According to HNO data and revised HRP information, the selected localities have been classified as Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) phase 3 'Crisis' and/or phase 4 'Emergency' further highlighting the need for timely and adequate livelihood interventions to address food insecurity, protect lives, and move towards economic self-sufficiency. Under the HRP 2023, the project is in line with FSL Cluster Objectives to support self-reliance of affected households by protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives. 
The planned interventions will include: provision of cash assistance; provision of agricultural support including seeds to vulnerable farmers or other individuals for subsistence; provision of small livestock and veterinary services; and inputs and small business support tailored to IDPs, youth, and women in agriculture and in income generating skills such as food processing, brick making, welding activities. IOM has already established good access to most of the target localities through ongoing projects, and seeks to continue implementing life-sustaining, early recovery, community stabilization initiatives. The planned interventions will be delivered in a way to complement past and ongoing activities.

project_name: Providing Critical Multisector Support Services to Refugees and Hosting Communities in Sudan
project_objective: This project aims to provide humanitarian assistance to refugees and hosting communities under the Strategic Objectives of the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan. IOM will provide multi-sectoral interventions, including Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), Emergency Shelters and Non-Food Items (ES/NFIs), health, and nutrition-based activities to respond to the urgent needs of refugees and hosting communities. The military conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that commenced on 15 April 2023 has caused increased vulnerabilities of the 1.1 million refugees and asylum seekers across Sudan and triggered urban to rural, intra/interstate and cross border population movements. For example in Khartoum it has caused secondary movements of refugees and asylum seekers. There are further concerns that premature returns to countries of origin will place refugees at risk of forced and unsafe returns. The conflict and subsequent displacement in Sudan is causing refugee crises in all the neighbouring countries. IOM will focus on providing the multi-sectoral assistance in Darfur, Kordofan, Khartoum, Blue Nile, Kassala and Gedaref. Numerous instances of internal displacement and increases in the number of refugee and migrant movements have been reported in 2022 and are expected to increase significantly in 2023 in these states due to the crisis. The proposed WASH activities will increase access to safe drinking water, adequate quality sanitation facilities, and improve hygiene practices. The proposed ES/NFI interventions will be used to improve living conditions for vulnerable refugees and host communities that receive high rates of displacement and offer protection to vulnerable people from the harsh elements. The proposed health activities will focus on delivering a basic package of primary health services (BPPHS) and nutrition services integrated to BPPHS, to improve access to services and reduce risks associated with morbidity and mortality and support more favorable protection outcomes. IOM's project will focus on targeting both refugees and hosting communities in an effort to mitigate the risks of tensions over scarce resources and increase the capacity of hosting communities to absorb population influxes. However, lifesaving assistance will be prioritized for new arrivals and vulnerable groups including women, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities or other specific needs to ensure that the most urgent humanitarian and protection needs are addressed.

project_name: Safety Advisory Services and Analyses for Humanitarian Access in Cameroon
project_objective:
INSO in Cameroon through this project will continue to disseminate and aggregate detailed analysis of the contextual developments in its services to the partners.  
INSO Cameroon will provide the following services: 

INSO Alerts - Prior to, or on the occurrence, of an incident carrying an imminent threat to NGOs and requiring an immediate operational response (such as movement restriction) INSO will provide an immediate Alert via the quickest technical medium available (e-mail, SMS text, voice call). The Alert will include the time, place and nature of the incident and a recommended response plan.

INSO Reports - Upon the anticipation or occurrence of a significant incident - including all incidents which directly involve the humanitarian community- but which does not require an immediate operational response from NGOs, INSO will provide a written Report of the incident via email noting the time, place and nature of the event along with a succinct analysis that includes an assessment of the probable impact and - where necessary - an advisory notice.

Bi-Weekly/Monthly Reports - A written bi-weekly/monthly analytical report with individual analysis plus key data and trends for each province as well as a macro level summary for the period. The report is intended to complement the statistical data with observations on security, political, demographic, climactic and cross border issues etc for that period. The report is provided in electronic format only and is distributed regionally and nationally. The report is currently in a biweekly format but will move to a monthly format in 2024.

Quarterly Reports - A quarterly report, providing the highest level of analysis and statistics. The report has a focus on longer term trends and incorporates developments at the national, regional and international levels with summarized data on the humanitarian sector and the various conflict trends. The report is intended to orient NGO in the 'strategic' context, within which all local events are occurring, and so to try and look ahead at the implications of changes in the structure of the conflicts, politics and inter-regional dynamics.
