project_name: FOOD CRISIS RESPONSE FOR PEOPLE AFFECTED BY CONFLICT IN SUDAN
project_objective:
The ongoing conflict has led of widespread displacement, economic crisis and disruption of food production. Approximately 17.7 million people are facing high level of acute food insecurity across Sudan.  Of those, about 4.9 million are in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency), and almost 12.8 million people are in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis). 
WFP’s primary focus is to reach the most food insecure populations (equivalent to IPC phase 4), due to funding constraints. The vast majority of the people in IPC phase 3 will not be assisted, despite being in need of life-saving humanitarian assistance. This will increase the risk of this demographic slipping into  IPC phase 4, particularly with the continuation of the current conflict. 
WFP’s emergency general food assistance will target 3.1 million  out of 5.6 million1) of the acutely food insecure population (Residents, IDPs, and Refugees) in Sudan. This concern is particularly acute as WFP’s unconditional food assistance has comprised almost the full caseload of the cluster response post-conflict. Given the mounting need amid budget constraints, WFP will focus on  geographical and household targeting to ensure available resources reach the most food insecure. 
WFP will undertake cross-border operations for access constrained locations especially for West and Central Darfurs through the Chad-Frachana Corridor, as well as through South Sudan (Reink and Aweil) to reach people  in East Darfur, South Darfur and Kordofans as well as other population group who have been double displaced in Al Jazeera and Kosti.

Activities/Outputs: 
For the project's duration, WFP will support 3.1 million vulnerable people, excluding refugees  with lifesaving general food assistance. 20% of the assistance will be in the form of cash-based transfers (CBT) while 80% will be in the form of in-kind food. WFP is scaling up unconditional CBT in its response, as this modality enables the most vulnerable people to address their multisectoral needs.  The assistancewill be provided in close collaboration with other WFP’s Cooperating Partners,  UN agencies, NGOs, and local partners, by building synergies.  
 WFP’s transfer value for CBT assistance has not been adjusted since August 2022 due to funding constraints. Monthly price monitoring indicates a significant food price increase (above the 15 percent threshold) that warrants a revision of transfer value. Therefore, the transfer value for half ration was adjusted from the SDG 5,000 to SDG 7,000/person/month (USD 11), for all categories of beneficiaries, i.e,  IDP, resident population and refugees. 
WFP Sudan’s targeting approach entails a geographic component, where localities and locations are identified based on a combination of assessed needs, with the IPC being the main reference point; the impact of conflict; level of displacement; and access and security as informed by the Humanitarian Access and Civil Military Coordination mechanism.. Household targeting, in which households are selected for assistance, is executed via three different targeting methodologies adapted to the operating environment on-ground. Blanket targeting is done in access-constrained areas, such as in Khartoum and Geneina, where, in line with WFP’s “no regrets” approach, all households in conflict-affected areas are eligible for assistance. In more accessible areas, status-based targeting is done among the newly internally displaced people living in state-arranged shelters and settlements as well as newly displaced camp-based refugees (e.g. refugee camps in White Nile). Community-based targeting is done in accessible areas to identify newly displaced households living in host communities and the households hosting these IDPs based on their level of vulnerability and food insecurity. Resident households in IPC Phase 4 are also targeted using community-based targeting.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de protección y respuesta humanitaria para la seguridad y bienestar de las comunidades en Antioquia, Córdoba y Chocó
project_objective:
En respuesta a las crisis humanitarias desencadenadas por conflictos, violencia armada y desastres naturales en los departamentos de Antioquia, Córdoba y Chocó, el proyecto tiene como objetivo fundamental de fortalecer los mecanismos de protección y reducción de riesgos. Enfocando las acciones en la integridad física, el bienestar psicológico y la dignidad humana de las comunidades afectadas, guiados por un enfoque basado en derechos.

Para alcanzar este propósito, se delia los objetivos específicos y medibles hacía la reducción de la vulnerabilidad y el fortalecimiento de las capacidades locales en protección, análisis y gestión del riesgo.

Resultados del Proyecto (Resultado 1):

Nuestro primer resultado se centra en la población afectada que, gracias a las herramientas proporcionadas, puede hacer frente a las amenazas de protección y exigibilidad de sus derechos. A través de estrategias, se proyecta alcanzar a 500 personas con respuestas adecuadas, llegando a otras 3,200 mediante medidas de prevención específicas. Además, se realizará asistencia psicosocial y fortaleciendo los conocimientos sobre derechos. Se establecieron iniciativas para prevenir el reclutamiento y planes de autoprotección comunitaria.

Se desarrollarán productos de gestión de información sobre protección que respaldan las acciones basadas en evidencia. 

Acceso Satisfactorio a Asistencia Básica (Resultado 2):

El proyecto tiene destinadas capacidad en los municipios de Quibdó e Istmina para satisfacer necesidades básicas de alimentación y elementos de higiene personal esenciales para la supervivencia y el bienestar en medio de la crisis antrópicas y/o naturales.

Fortalecimiento de Conocimientos en Protección (Resultado 3):

Reconociendo la importancia de fortalecer a los actores clave en la respuesta humanitaria, se capacitarán a los colaboradores en territorio y a nivel nacional en gestión de conflictos y en conocimientos y habilidades en aspectos relacionados con la Protección y sus estándares internacionales para una mayor especialización y calidad en las acciones.
Actividades Clave:

Nuestro enfoque estratégico se traduce en una serie de actividades, desde la gestión de casos y estrategias de autoprotección comunitaria hasta la elaboración de productos de gestión de información sobre protección y la distribución de ayuda humanitaria, que incluye paquetes de alimentos y kits de higiene personal. Además, hemos implementado acciones específicas para la capacitación y fortalecimiento de capacidades, colaborando con la comunidad local y agentes pastorales.

Con el propósito de, no solo busca aliviar las consecuencias inmediatas de las crisis humanitarias, sino que también establece las bases para comunidades más resilientes de las comunidades afectadas en Antioquia, Córdoba y Chocó.

project_name: Strengthening Community Capacity to Reduce Malnutrition in  Rubkona County and Torit , South Sudan.
project_objective:
Between July 2022 and June 2023, an estimated 1.4 million children under five are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition based on analysis and estimations from the results of the SMART nutrition surveys, Food Security and Nutrition Monitoring System (FSNMS) and program admission trends. As for the severity of the situation, during July and October, 30 counties are classified in IPC AMN Phase 4 (Critical), 15 counties in IPC AMN Phase 3 (Serious), 19 counties in IPC AMN Phase 2 (Alert) and 13 in IPC AMN Phase 1 (Acceptable). Approximately 345,893 will need SAM treatment, while another 1,057,703 will need MAM treatment. Acute malnutrition burden will be highly concentrated in the four states, Unity being one of them.
In the case of Eastern Equatoria State as projected from the IPC Acute Food Insecurity And Malnutrition Analysis Report of November 23, 2022, from April to July 2023, the food security situation was projected to remain dire with an estimated 578,000 people (51.3% of the population) likely to be in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, of which 213,000 people are likely to be in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and 365,000 people are likely to be in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) acute food insecurity.
As presented by the FSNMS, the proposed project seeks to address the prevalence of malnutrition in Unity and Eastern Equatoria States, covering Rubkona and Torit Counties respectively by promoting increased access to prevention and treatment services for children under 5 suffering from severe and moderate acute malnutrition and pregnant and lactating women in targeted vulnerable communities through referrals, increased percentage of households with improved food security and nutritional status by 20% in the target community, and enhanced access to functional nutrition services through the renovation of nutrition treatment centres, delivery of equitable WASH services within target locations. Targeting 30,000 children under the age of five, and 20,000 PLWs.

project_name: Emergency Response For Rohingya and Host Community, Cox's Bazar (Friendship)
project_objective:
The project aims to improve well-being and health through integrated healthcare support to the Rohingya community living in the camps and to host communities in Ukhiya in Cox’s Bazar as a continuation of previous project phases. The project includes the operation of 1 Primary Healthcare Centre (PHC) and the general consultation, dental, eye and limited surgery section of Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU, a secondary Healthcare center).  One primary Healthcare Centre (PHC) in Camp 7 will provide services in affiliation with the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). For the Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU), the maternity part (CEmONC) is funded by IOM and UNFPA, the family planning services are supported by IPAS, and the rest of the services including general consultation services, eye and dental units are funded by the Friendship Luxemburg and provide us the required flexibility to strengthen and consolidate services across the facilities.  The Maternity part (CEmONC) of the Friendship Hospital Ukhiya (FHU) is identified by the health sector as a referral point to provide higher-level maternal healthcare services including Caesarean sections for both host communities and Rohingya. The project focuses on protection against illness and equitable access to (Health Sector Indicator 2) health services without any discrimination and especially targeting the most vulnerable groups (women, children, pregnant/lactating women, people with disabilities, the elderly, GBV, and conflict-affected survivors). The project also plans to collaborate with the Ukhia Specialized Hospital (UNHCR) by sharing the expertise, accepting referral points, and receiving maternal patients from USH until the maternity part is started there. Friendship will conduct the following activities following the MESP: 
- Provide essential health services to both the host and Rohingya community through 1 primary healthcare center in camp 7 and one 24/7 Secondary level healthcare service named Friendship Hospital Ukhia (FHU).
- Provide SRH services including safe deliveries (assisting Normal Vaginal Delivery ) and providing basic neonatal care, Ante Natal Care (ANC) and Post Natal Care (PNC) services to both the host and Rohingya communities. 
- Conduct normal vaginal delivery through the PHC and C-section through FHU to ensure safe institutional delivery. 
- Provide Family Planning, Menstrual Regulation, management of STIs, and post-abortive care services.
-  Screen and refer Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Medium Acute Malnutrition (MAM) children (6 to 59 months) to Outpatient Therapeutic feeding Program (OTPs).
- Provide Mental Health and Psychosocial Support and Gender Based Violence services including Clinical Management of Rape services and clinical management of Gender Based Violence cases (in Camp 7 1 MHPSS Officer and 1 GBV case worker).
- Support Expanded Program on Immunization services in alignment with the national program.
- Provide laboratory investigation facility services for the beneficiaries at the health facility level.
- Provide essential medicine and supplements including Vitamin C and Zinc tablets to increase immunity of the beneficiaries 
- Coordinate with District and Upazila level COVID-19 Task Force, Health and Family Planning Department, and other stakeholders.
- Conduct awareness-raising sessions including IPC at facility.
- Strengthen the feedback mechanism by developing and implementing action plan based on feedback received from camp-level health coordination and health committee meetings.
- Community Health Volunteers are identified, trained and supervised to identify community members in need of referral for PHC services, EPI, SRH including ANC/PNC with special attention to term mothers for skilled birth attendant deliveries with the support of outreach Midwives.

project_name: Improving the multisectoral response in favor of refugees and asylum seekers in Cameroon
project_objective:
The project will aim to improve the multisectoral response for the refugees and asylum seekers in Cameroon, and the implementation of sustainable solutions for their benefit.
UNHCR commits to support the Cameroonian Government in implementing the Global Refugee Forum pledges in health, education, protection, employment, and socio-economic opportunities and will work with development actors and the private sector to increase refugee inclusion in national services, development plans and activities. This will enable a transition from humanitarian assistance to more sustainable development, reduce refugees’ dependence on humanitarian assistance, and strengthen their resilience. By becoming self-reliant, refugees will also be able to contribute to the country’s economy.
This will be done through improving the protection environment, access to complementary solutions and pathways for refugees and asylum seekers regarding registration activities, documentation, protection of childhood, prevention, response to sexual and gender-based violence, access to basic social services (health, education, and water), access to decent shelter and goods essential domestic needs as well as building resilience. To achieve this UNHCR Cameroon will have to reinforce Government capacity building and strengthen non-transitional partnerships and inclusion of refugees in the programs of other funded actors, as well as repatriation.
The interventions of UNHCR and its partners will be aligned with the priorities defined by the government (national development strategy 2020-2030). They are also part of its contribution to achieving the SDGs, the UNSDCF and the principle of leaving no one behind. Emphasis will be placed on the continued inclusion of refugees and asylum seekers in government programs, as well as humanitarian and development actors such as the World Bank.
For the year 2024 the project will target 472,806 refugees including 354,078 CAR, of which 187,585 children (<18 years), 153,535 adults (18-59 years), 12,958 older people (>60 years); and   118,728 Nigerians, of which 73,658 children (<18 years), 40,379 adults (18-59 years), 4,691 older people (>60 years); as well as 15% of vulnerable host populations.

project_name: Protection et Assistance multi sectorielle pour les réfugiés au Tchad
project_objective:
Au 31 octobre 2023, le Tchad compte 1 377 146   personnes en situation de déplacement forcé, dont 1.055.122 réfugiés enregistrés et 5.553 demandeurs d'asile, qui sont originaires du Soudan ; de la République Centrafricaine; du Cameroun; du Nigeria et d'autres pays et qui sont pour la plupart (90%) répartis à travers 26 camps et sites de réfugiés, (17 camps et 1 site à l'Est, 6 au Sud, 2 près de N'Djamena et 1 dans la province du Lac Tchad), et plusieurs villages d'accueil notamment au Sud et le long de la frontière avec le Cameroun; 14% dans des villages d'accueil et 2% dans des zones urbaines de N’Djamena et Abéché.
Depuis le mois d’avril 2023, à la faveur du conflit qui a éclaté au Soudan entre les Forces armées soudanaises (FAS) et les Forces paramilitaires de Soutien Rapide (RSF), plus de 450.000 nouveaux réfugiés ont afflué vers le Tchad, exerçant une pression additionnelle sur les ressources déjà maigres de leurs communautés hôtes. Malgré ces défis, le Tchad a continué à démontrer son hospitalité en faveur des réfugiés et travailler dans le sens de la mise en œuvre des engagements pris en marge de la Déclaration de New York et lors du Forum Mondial sur les Réfugiés qui visent à assurer une inclusion des réfugiés dans les programmes de développement de l’Etat, l’intégration des réfugiés dans le système éducatif national ainsi que la reconnaissance des écoles et centres de santé dans le système national en vue de l’autonomisation des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes.
Dans le but de créer un environnement favorable et de rendre effective l’inclusion et l’autonomisation des réfugiés, le Tchad a adopté en décembre 2020 une loi sur l’asile puis en 2023 son décret d’application. Ces textes consacrent la jouissance par les réfugiés des droits civils ainsi que les droits économiques, sociaux et culturels y compris le droit à l’emploi.
Même si la situation de transition politique a quelque peu ralenti les efforts déjà entrepris à cause d’une re-priorisation des interventions, il devient urgent de renforcer les projets de développement en accord avec le Gouvernement du Tchad et les partenaires techniques et financiers et de continuer à fournir l’assistance et la protection en vue de la résilience des réfugiés et de leurs communautés d’accueil.
Le présent projet vise ainsi à fournir un environnement favorable de protection et d’assistance d’une part et à rechercher de solutions d’autre part au profit des réfugiés, demandeurs d’asile, déplacés internes et les communauté hôte au Tchad avec comme fondement des projets visant la résilience et l’autonomisation. Pour y parvenir une approche à phases interdépendantes sera adoptée :
•	La stabilisation de la situation des réfugiés nouvellement arrivés dans une localité à travers le déploiement d’un paquet minimum de protection et d’assistance, la définition des activités visant leur résilience conformément à la loi d’asile au Tchad et son décret d’application ainsi que d’autres instruments juridiques internationaux que la Tchad a ratifiés. 
•	L’inclusion des réfugiés dans les programmes de développement de l’Etat et dans les filets sociaux de l’Etat et d’autres partenaires en vue de leur autonomisation.
•	La recherche et la mise en œuvre des solutions durables dont le rapatriement librement consenti ; la réinstallation et les voies complémentaires ainsi que l’autonomisation des réfugiés. 
Ces priorités seront mises en œuvre par le biais des instruments comme  le nexus humanitaire-développement, le partenariat diversifié, la centralité de la protection dans un environnement caractérisé par l’existence de processus de coordination intergouvernementale notamment, le Processus de Bamako, la Plateforme de soutien pour la recherche de solutions aux déplacements forcés issus de la crise centrafricaine consacrée par la Déclaration de Yaounde, la Déclaration d’Abuja et la Stratégie Régionale de Stabilisation, de redressement et de résilience des zones du Bassin du Lac Tchad affectées par la crise.

project_name: Enhancing Food Security and Livelihoods of Vulnerable Agro-pastoralists Communities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria States, South Sudan
project_objective:
Climatic extremes, which have in the recent past been characterized by unprecedented flooding and prolonged dry spells, coupled with increasing waves of inter and intra communal violence, bureaucratic impediments including escalating Sudan conflict with increasing influx of refugees, returnees and asylum seekers crossing into South Sudan and deteriorating local currency and high food prices have continued to negatively impact vulnerable boys, girls, men and women, including people with disabilities in Unity, Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Central Equatoria among other States/ administrative areas in the country. 

These have had consequent implications on multiple displacements of people, prolonged congregation of livestock in marsh lands with consequent impacts on increased livestock disease outbreaks and mortalities in addition to submerging of agricultural land contributing to unprecedented food insecurity levels, with the lean season projection period of April to July 2024, where food security situation will deteriorate and an estimated 7.1 million people (56.3 percent of the population) will be severely food insecure (IPC Phase 3 or above). 79,000 people are likely to be in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe) while an estimated 2.34 million people are likely to be in Phase 4 (Emergency) (IPC November 2023 Report).

Many vulnerable host, returnee, refugee and displaced families, especially women, widowed women, child headed households, the elderly, boys and girls including people with disabilities; solely depend on livestock, fishing, vegetable and crop farming among other coping strategies. VSF Suisse 28 years of experience in the targeted states, presence on the ground and proven capacity will deliver high quality programming by leveraging on strong grass root networks, local knowledge, understanding of seasonal and location specific contexts. Proposed actions will target 187,000 beneficiaries (30000 men, 30000 women, 63500girls, 63500 boys) who shall include elderly and people living with disabilities. The action will be aimed at ensuring cost efficiency through complementarities by linkages with FAO pipeline for livestock vaccines prepositioning and agricultural livelihood kits - crops, vegetables and fishing kits in order to promote preparedness, household resilience and self-reliance through protection of livelihood opportunities.

Proposed actions are in line and correspond with the FSL Cluster 2024 HRP Cluster Objectives Supporting CO2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock and Cluster Objective 3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb  and adapt to shocks and contextual changes. 

Proposed actions will establish synergies with other sectors to maximize the response impact, to ensure complementarity and integration with other clusters’ interventions, starting with the “Famine prevention clusters” (Health, Nutrition and WASH) and the Protection cluster. This is in addition to promoting a nexus between humanitarian response, peace building (conflict sensitivity) and resilience programming. The project will ensure quality programming, cost efficiency in addition to mainstreaming cross-cutting programmatic approaches that include application of Accountability to Affected Populations principles ,protection including Gender Based Violence mitigation measures, Do No Harm, conflict context analysis, gender equity, HIV/AIDS awareness and prevention, environmental conservation and sustainability.

project_name: Psychosocial Support for women/girls, Orphans and Vulnerable children affected by the sociopolitical crisis in the South-West Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The project, "Psychosocial Support for women/girls, Orphans and Vulnerable children affected by the sociopolitical crisis in the South-West Region of Cameroon," aims to provide comprehensive psychosocial support and protection to individuals affected by the sociopolitical crisis. With a target of 2000 participants distributed across various target beneficiaries, the project intends to address the urgent needs of women, girls, orphans, and vulnerable children by restoring emotional well-being, empowering individuals, and creating a safer and more inclusive environment.
The project will implement a range of activities to address the assessed needs of the target beneficiaries. Trauma counseling and support will be provided to help individuals heal from the emotional trauma caused by violence, displacement, and loss. Safe spaces and support networks will be established to foster empowerment, resilience, and a sense of belonging among women, girls, and children.
To ensure access to quality education and skill development, the project will provide education support through  document catch-up classes, scholarships, and vocational training. Concurrently, awareness programs on child rights, protection, and gender equality will be conducted to promote the well-being and development of vulnerable children.
To ensure that the target enjoyed their citizen right, the project will assist in the establishment of civil document like Birth certificate and ID Card.
To tackle gender-based violence, the project will offer medical and psychological support for survivors, conduct awareness campaigns, and provide legal assistance. Dignity kits containing essential hygiene and personal care items will be distributed to promote the well-being and dignity of survivors. Economic empowerment opportunities, such as microfinance initiatives and vocational training, will be provided to help survivors regain independence and rebuild their lives.
The project will also address housing, land, and property issues by advocating for secure HLP rights, providing legal assistance, and conducting sensitization programs. Efforts will be made to facilitate access to interim land for farming for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and ensure their rights in housing and land tenure.
A participatory and community-based approach will be adopted, engaging key stakeholders, community leaders, and local organizations in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of activities. A robust monitoring and evaluation framework will be established to track progress and assess the effectiveness of interventions. The project's sustainability will be ensured through capacity-building activities, collaboration with government agencies, and income-generating initiatives.
By implementing this project, we aim to make a significant impact on the lives of those affected by the crisis, fostering their recovery, development, and overall well-being. Through psychosocial support, protection measures, and empowerment opportunities, we aspire to create a more resilient and inclusive community in the South-West Region of Cameroon

project_name: Promoting Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Wellbeing of the Conflict-Affected Population in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
The crisis in Northeast Nigeria continues to exacerbate protection risks and needs for internally displaced populations (IDPs) and host communities. While in some locations the situation became more stable, in many locations the unpredictable and volatile security situation continues to threaten the populations’ daily safety and health. By fleeing insecurity, the population is deprived of basic services and often left without any means of livelihood and access to basic protection and MHPSS services. The project aims at continuing and strengthening IOM’s protection response in Northeast Nigeria through the implementation of protection activities by interdisciplinary Psychosocial Mobile Teams (PMTs) comprised of social workers, lay counselors and community mobilizers, and including government staff such as from the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development. IOM will prioritize coordination with protection actors working in other local government areas and government partners including the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) and the State Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) States. 

The following areas of intervention are to be implemented under this project: 1) Capacity building of key stakeholders, including partners and government officials, on protection mainstreaming, counter-trafficking and community-based mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS); 2) Increased protection risk assessments to measure and report on trends related to general protection risks (i.e. a situation where an individual or group are at risk of or suffering from violence, coercion and deprivation) and risks of trafficking in persons; 3) Provision of specialized protection services to (potential) victims of trafficking (VoTs), including case management, reintegration support, and psychosocial services, as well as to other vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities and older persons; 4) Increased protection advocacy to the government and other key stakeholders incorporating findings from protection risk assessments, as well as advocacy for increased action on trafficking in persons among protection sector partners; 5) Additional training for IOM Women’s and Men’s Committees on identifying key protection risks and trends and making safe referrals for people in need of specialized protection services; 6) Developing reports and other information products on identified protection risks and trends and sharing these with key stakeholders, including the Protection Sector in NE Nigeria and; 7) Targeted livelihood support to (potential) victims of trafficking to support their reintegration.

The implementation of planned services will be guided by the Guidance note on how to mainstream protection across IOM crisis response (IN/232 Guidance note on how to mainstream protection across IOM crisis response (or Migration crisis operational framework sector of assistance), the IOM Manual on Community-Based MHPSS in Emergencies and Displacement (IOM Manual on Community-Based Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Emergencies and Displacement International Organization for Migration), the IOM handbook on direct assistance of victims of trafficking (IOM handbook on direct assistance for victims of trafficking, 2007, IOM handbook on direct assistance for victims of trafficking), and the Caring for victims of trafficking guidance note for health providers (Caring for trafficked persons: guidance for health providers, IOM, 2009, Caring for trafficked persons: guidance for health providers).

Cherchant une synergie entre les interventions liées à la santé et à la nutrition et les actions axées sur l'atténuation et la prévention de toutes les formes de violence à l'égard des femmes et des enfants. Avec une approche communautaire et de genre, comme éléments structurants, ce projet développera divers programmes de prise en charge (nutrition, prévention des VBG, autonomisation des femmes, protection de l’enfance) dédiés aux enfants et aux femmes en situation de vulnérabilité dans 3 sites de déplacés dans les communes de Diffa et de Chétimari. Le projet consolidera le travail commencé en 2021, proposant une continuité des actions mises en œuvre tout en renforçant le leadership des acteurs locaux dans une perspective de localisation de l'aide humanitaire et en améliorant la capacité de prise de décision et de participation des femmes dans l’Action Humanitaire dans une perspective de redevabilité. 

Les principales activités du projet seront : distribution de Kit alimentaires, dépistages, campagne de sensibilisation sur la nutrition, distribution de kits dignité, accompagnement de groupements féminins, AGR, sensibilisation et plaidoyer en matière de protection.

project_name: Strengthening humanitarian coordination and advocacy in Mozambique
project_objective: OCHA has been present in Mozambique with a Humanitarian Advisory Team (HAT) since. March 2019, following the landfall of and humanitarian response to cyclones Idai and Kenneth. Subsequently, OCHA HAT supported the coordination and response to a number of crises in the country, including the conflict and displacement in northern Mozambique, climatic shocks (tropical storms and cyclones, floods, etc.), etc. Over the past years, OCHA HAT continued to expand its presence in Mozambique and, effective January 2022 transitioned into a fully-fledged OCHA Mozambique Country Office (CO). In 2024, OCHA will be strengthening its pivotal role in galvanizing, coordinating, and supporting the overall humanitarian action in Mozambique, focusing on OCHA's main functions, i.e. coordination, advocacy, humanitarian financing and information management.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination and Common Services in Sudan
project_objective: After years of protracted crisis, Sudan plunged into a conflict of alarming scale in mid-April 2023 when fighting between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group, broke out initially in the capital Khartoum, and quickly expanded to other areas across the country. The current bout of insecurity has resulted in human casualties, with more than 12,000 fatalities.  Khartoum has been the site of heavy fighting, while severe violent clashes and heavy bombardments have also been reported in the greater Darfur and Kordofan regions. The escalating hostilities have resulted in extensive damage to critical infrastructure and facilities, including water and healthcare, the collapse of banking and financial services, frequent interruptions to electricity supply and telecommunication services and widespread looting. The conflict created massive displacement, with over 6.1 million people forced to leave their homes in search of safety elsewhere. Of this, 1.3 million crossed the border to neighboring countries, while 4.85 million were internally displaced (54 per cent women) – the majority of whom were originally from Khartoum areas and over half were children (under 18 years of age).  In addition to the 3.8 million internally displaced persons (IDPs ) resulting from past internal conflicts, Sudan currently faces the largest internal displacement crisis in the world, and also the most significant child displacement crisis, with 3 million children displaced inside and outside the country.

project_name: Strengthening Humanitarian Coordination, Advocacy and Common Services in South Sudan
project_objective: This project aims at strengthening OCHA's role in the leadership and coordination of humanitarian action in South Sudan based on a people-centered approach. Specifically, the project will bolster OCHA's coordination role (at national and sub-national levels), information management, needs assessment and analysis, leadership on access and cash coordination, humanitarian financing and advocacy. The direct target of this project is the humanitarian community in South Sudan who benefits from OCHA's services while the indirect target is affected people whose needs have to be addressed in a principled and effective manner.

project_name: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad
project_objective:
Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_name: Renforcement des capacités de coordination, de gestion de l'information et de plaidoyer humanitaires au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
•	Le Burkina Faso est en proie à une crise humanitaire sans précédent. Les mouvements de populations et les violations des droits humains s'intensifient, entraînant une détresse sans précédent pour les civils.

•	En 2023, comme lors des années précédentes, le pays a connu un grand nombre de chocs violents. Les mouvements de populations forcés, qui réduisent l’accès de la population aux services sociaux de base et aux moyens de subsistance, contribuant ainsi à l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, sont les principales conséquences. 

•	Il est probable que la situation politique et sécuritaire au Burkina Faso continue de se détériorer. En effet, plusieurs incidents de sécurité ont provoqué de nouveaux déplacements de population en 2023. Des déplacements forcés de plus en plus nombreux et prolongés. 2 062 534 de personnes se sont déplacées à l’intérieur du pays à la date du 31 mars 2023, selon le CONASUR (soit près de 10% de la population totale du pays). 

•	En 2024, plus de 6,3 millions de personnes au Burkina Faso auront besoin d'assistance humanitaire, dont 3,8 millions seront ciblées. Le bureau de pays d'OCHA au Burkina Faso soutiendra la mise en œuvre des activités prioritaires dans les cinq domaines d'intervention suivants : 

•	Améliorer la coordination des efforts humanitaires, à la fois au niveau stratégique et opérationnel. Cela comprend la coordination civilo-militaire, le suivi de l'accès humanitaire, l'engagement des communautés et la redevabilité envers les personnes touchées.

•	Intensifier les efforts de plaidoyer humanitaire, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées internes et les personnes non déplacées.
•	Assurer la mise en œuvre de la politique humanitaire et des bonnes pratiques, notamment la collaboration entre l'humanitaire, le développement et la consolidation de la paix, tout en respectant la distinction et l'intégrité de l'action humanitaire.
•	Faciliter la collecte et la répartition efficaces des fonds humanitaires.

•	Fournir des informations fiables et à jour pour aider les humanitaires à prendre des décisions éclairées.
2. Besoins, activités et résultats attendus : 
•	Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du plan de réponse humanitaire 2024, l’activité centrale de la coordination sera d’améliorer la réponse à la crise par une meilleure coordination de l’assistance humanitaire afin de préserver des vies et protéger les moyens de subsistance.
•	L’appui au Bureau du Coordonnateur Humanitaire dans la mise en place, la révision et le fonctionnement des structures de coordination au niveau national et régional.
•	L’organisation de réunions de coordination aux niveaux national et régional afin de garantir une réponse humanitaire efficace et dans les délais.
•	L’appui au Bureau du Coordonnateur Humanitaire et à l’Equipe humanitaire Pays dans la mise en œuvre des engagements relatifs au Sommet Humanitaire Mondial (WHS), Grand Bargain et du programme nexus humanitaire – développement-Paix.
•	La production et la diffusion de produits d’information de qualité sur les données et le contexte humanitaire.
•	L’appui à la gestion de sites web au profit de la communauté humanitaire et de leurs partenaires.
•	La coordination du groupe de coordination opérationnelle de la réponse rapide (GCORR).
•	La coordination des activités de transferts monétaires en tant que modalité de la réponse humanitaire globale.
•	La coordination du mécanisme d’Accès Humanitaire, de CMCOORD au niveau national et dans les régions touchées par les conflits.
•	Plaidera auprès des autorités compétentes pour garantir un accès humanitaire aux populations dans le besoin d’assistance et de protection.
•	Continuera de soutenir la vulgarisation des principes humanitaire à travers des activités de sensibilisation.
•	Poursuivra ses activités pour la mobilisation des fonds nécessaires à l’assistance et à la réponse humanitaires.
•	Organisera ou soutiendra des réunions de plaidoyer du coordonnateur humanitaire et du Gouvernement avec les donateurs.

project_name: Strengthen the collective humanitarian response through effective, agile and efficient coordination, based on humanitarian principles in Far North, North-West and South-West regions
project_objective:
The objective of the project is to strengthen the coordination of the humanitarian response in Cameroon to save lives, protect the most vulnerable and improve the resilience of populations. Since the worsening of the crisis in the North-West and South-West regions, Cameroon faces three complex humanitarian crises affecting eight of Cameroon's ten regions. The impact of these three crises on the living conditions of the affected populations is reinforced by pre-existing structural vulnerabilities that hamper their recovery, in the three affected regions: Far North, North-West and South-West. Widespread insecurity in the Lake Chad basin and border area with Nigeria continued to affect the Far North region in 2023. Attacks against civilians, State security forces (SSF), including army, gendarmerie, police, and their bases, continued and non-State armed groups (NSAGs) and armed criminals continued to carry out lootings in crisis affected areas. NSAGs continue to use improvised explosive devices (IEDs) in the Far North, North-West, and South-West regions, primarily targeting military convoys. In the Far North region, particularly in the Lake Chad basin area, the economic context is marked by poverty, the lack of access to and sustainable management of natural resources, limited income-generating and market opportunities, as well as a drastic reduction in agriculture, livestock production and touristic activities due to prevalent insecurity. 
In the North-West and South-West regions, high levels of insecurity continued. High levels of criminality and impunity lead to a climate of insecurity whereby civilians and humanitarian workers face risks of kidnapping for ransom, abduction, assault, unlawful detention, carjacking, and threats of violence. The line between targeted, politically motivated acts of violence and criminal activities is increasingly blurred. Violence, regular lockdowns and closure of roads continue to have a major impact on the local economies.

The complexity and the scope of these crises therefore require more effective coordination, adapted to the different intervention areas and based on humanitarian principles. OCHA Cameroon's coordination project will thus make it possible to achieve a humanitarian response that is better funded, more strategic and that centralizes human rights and the protection of people in the Far North. It will also enable a better complementarity between emergency actions and development programs, in order to fight together the humanitarian needs and their underlying causes. To this end, OCHA will provide the essential services of disseminating key information products, coordinating the Humanitarian Programming Cycle and facilitating joint multisectoral needs assessments. Its presence in Yaoundé, Maroua, Kousseri, Bamenda and Buea will enable it to provide decisive support to coordination mechanisms and promote coherence between operational issues in the field and strategic decision-making bodies. This key position will also enable it to advance the overriding considerations of the Centrality of Protection and Cross-cutting Protection, Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and nexus humanitarian development and peace. From its sub-offices in the Far North, North-West and South-West, OCHA will also support the scaling up of the response in these regions, including through the management of CMCoord and humanitarian access responsibilities, as well as capacity building of local responders.

project_name: STRENGTHENING HUMANITARIAN COORDINATION, ADVOCACY AND QUALITY OF HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE
project_objective: (i)	Provide effective coordination by strengthening area based coordination and leadership, reinforcing sub-national effectiveness and linkages between the various coordination and working group levels from ICCG in the capital and intersectoral working groups in the regions to HCT level engagements with the Government; (ii) Promote humanitarian access in a complex operating environment, where the security situation remains volatile; (iii)  Strengthen civil-military coordination at the regions and capital levels to improve response preparedness, rapid and safe delivery of humanitarian assistance, and foster enhanced predictability of civil-military coordination processes and platforms; (iv) foster greater accountability of the humanitarian response, raising awareness of the crisis, promoting best practices and international law, and bringing the voices of affected people to the forefront; (v) support locally-led identification of strategic priorities through the Flagship project, promote  HDP collaboration which will inform the multi-year Humanitarian Response Strategy framework (2023-2025) (vi) advocate for principled humanitarian action by relevant authorities and sharing its coordination expertise based on global best practices. This will include an enhanced interface and support to the Government of Niger, especially the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs; (vii) Enhance partnerships with existing and new humanitarian donors through improved bilateral and multilateral engagement; (viii) Increased accountability of the humanitarian system to meet humanitarian needs.

project_name: Coordination of the Humanitarian Response in Colombia
project_objective:
OCHA plays a crucial role in monitoring and coordinating humanitarian efforts at the local level, providing essential analysis for well-informed decision-making. It operates through 12 Local Coordination Teams (LCTs) and 3 Humanitarian Local Teams (HLTs) in border departments, where OCHA leads six LCTs/HLTs. Additionally, OCHA offers information management support to LCTs in other regions led by different UN agencies. Regular data gathering and analysis contribute to creating products related to ongoing emergencies and response status.

OCHA spearheads inter-cluster coordination group, access efforts, and the Flagship Initiative. It also supports conflict analysis and facilitates coordination. Moreover, OCHA collaborates closely with offices in Venezuela, Peru, and Ecuador to analyze cross-border dynamics and enhance coordination. In 2024, OCHA will maintain its presence with coordination staff in 6 sub-offices and 10 field information managers in the most crisis-affected departments. In addition OCHA will have three Area-based advisors to support the efforts of the flagship initiatie.

project_name: Humanitarian Coordination Assistance for the Syria Response Plan
project_objective:
The 2024-2025 Syria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) sets out the framework within which the humanitarian community will respond to large-scale humanitarian and protection needs in Syria, flexibly leveraging the various response modalities.
Capturing these capacities and efforts under a single strategic framework, the plan aims to increase the effectiveness of the response by improving the identification of needs and gaps, reducing overlap and duplication, and monitoring context changes and progress against collective agreed response results. The Humanitarian Coordinator for Syria and the Regional Humanitarian Coordinator for the Syria Crisis lead and coordinate humanitarian action inside Syria. OCHA, in line with its global mandate, supports the humanitarian leadership in effectively coordinating the response inside Syria. To do so, OCHA maintains country offices in Syria and Türkiye, and a regional office in Amman.
OCHA Türkiye coordinates cross-border humanitarian assistance delivered from Türkiye to Syria as mandated by the UN Security Council resolutions 2642 under the leadership of the Deputy Regional Humanitarian Coordinator (DRHC).
OCHA requires sustained levels of funding to be able to maintain and strengthen effective humanitarian response coordination from these various offices, facilitate strategic and operational coordination platforms, provide information management services, manage pooled funds, support humanitarian access analysis and negotiation, ensure civil-military coordination, and provide public information and advocacy on the humanitarian situation. Funding requirements for this project reflect the needs of OCHA's three offices directly involved in the Syria response.

project_name: Assistance médico-nutritionnelle pour les personnes déplacées et populations hôtes victimes de choc dans les régions de Maradi, Tahoua et Tillabéry
project_objective:
ALIMA-BEFEN propose une intervention médico-nutritionnelle afin d'assister les populations déplacées et hôtes des régions de Tillabéry, Tahoua et Maradi en contribuant à la réduction de leur morbi-mortalité, notamment en garantissant un accès aux soins primaires gratuits et de qualité avec un focus spécifique sur les femmes enceintes et allaitantes et les enfants de moins de 5 ans. La stratégie d'intervention est à la fois fixe au travers du renforcement de la résilience des structures de santé, et mobile au travers du déploiement des cliniques mobiles afin d'atteindre les populations les plus éloignées des CSI. Le projet assurera le renforcement de la prise en charge des soins de santé primaires dans les structures existantes (CSI et HD) tout en assurant le paquet de soins minimum aux populations ciblées dans les zones plus éloignées. 
Les cibles principales du projet sont les populations déplacées et  hôtes des 3 régions. Les enfants de moins de 5 ans constituent la cible prioritaire de l'action puisqu'ils sont la couche la plus vulnérable de la population. Les femmes enceintes, allaitantes et en âge de procréer seront aussi des cibles prioritaires pour l'action du fait de leur vulnérabilité aux attaques et aux violences basées sur le genre, en plus de leur importance dans la détection de la malnutrition et des maladies chez les enfants. Les personnes blessées victimes de violences sont également visées, afin de combler le manque quant à la prise en charge et la gratuité de leurs soins de santé. Grâce à une stratégie communautaire au travers de la formation de nombreux relais communautaires dans chacune des zones d’intervention, les besoins des populations cibles seront identifiés et pris en charge rapidement. Des sensibilisations à la PCIME, au PB-mère, aux pratiques d’hygiène familiale essentielles, à la SSR, seront effectuées grâce à l’implication de ces relais et matrones formés. L’ensemble du personnel d’ALIMA-BEFEN et leurs partenaires au sein des cliniques mobiles et au travers des CSI seront également formés/recyclés à la détection, à la prise en charge et au suivi des victimes de VBG touchant particulièrement les femmes et les enfants. Un appui psychosocial est apporté grâce à la présence de professionnels du domaine en attendant leur référencement vers des structures plus adaptées. ALIMA permet aux populations affectées de jouer un rôle actif tout au long du cycle du projet et veille à ce que les plus marginalisés soient représentés et puissent faire entendre leur voix, à travers les points notamment l’identification des personnes à besoin spécifique lors de la mise en œuvre des activités ; permettre aux femmes, hommes, enfants et personnes âgées de participer et d'influencer la conception du projet, la mise en œuvre du projet et le suivi et l'évaluation ; veiller à ce que les systèmes de représentation communautaire soient justes et représentatifs, et que les plus marginalisés, vulnérables et affectés aient une voix.
Une importance?particulière sera donnée au rendu de compte auprès des populations, notamment par le biais des Comités Locaux, des relais communautaires et des matrones. Une collaboration régulière continuera d’être mise en œuvre avec les communautés bénéficiaires, garante aussi bien de la qualité de la réponse que de la sécurité des équipes d'intervention. Les plaintes et inquiétudes liées au projet et à son déroulement seront canalisées et permettront de réadapter les activités et les améliorer dans une optique permanente de qualité des soins et de redevabilité envers les bénéficiaires. Les projets disposent d'un mécanisme permettant à la population locale de fournir des retours d'information et de signaler les incidents de violences sexistes et sexuelles. Ce mécanisme inclut un point focal désigné sur chaque zone, chargé de garantir la confidentialité de ses interlocuteurs et de remonter les plaintes. L’ensemble des staffs d’ALIMA-BEFEN et partenaires sont régulièrement sensibilisés à PSEA.

project_name: Faciliter l’insertion des enfants et des adolescent(e)s affectés par la crise humanitaire au sein d’un système éducatif sûr et protecteur au Niger
project_objective: COOPI propose une Action d’EiE qui vise à faciliter l’accès et le droit à l'éducation pour les enfants affectés par la crise humanitaire dans la région de Tahoua, notamment dans le département de Tillia et Bagaroua (frontière malienne) et de Madaoua(frontière Nigeria).Plus particulièrement, l'Action a comme objectif de faciliter l'insertion/réintégration des enfants les plus vulnérables (communauté hôte, PDI) dans le système éducatif formel tout en répondant à leurs besoins de protection psychosociale et cognitive. Dans 20 écoles primaires d’accueil, il est prévu la mise en place d’un programme d’éducation accélérée(SSA/P), la réhabilitation des salles des classes et la dotation en intrants scolaires (R1).Une attention particulière sera donnée aux enfants les plus vulnérables issus des déplacements et victimes de traumatismes aigues et aux enfants en situation de handicap. Une approche communautaire à plusieurs niveaux sera employée, afin de favoriser une implication forte des communautés ciblées dans l'implémentation de l'Action. Le projet prendra en compte aussi le renforcement des capacités des acteurs clés gravitant autour du système éducatif au niveau communautaire (enseignants et COGES),régionale (Inspections) et humanitaire (R2 et R3).Dans le but de répondre à la demande grandissante de récupération scolaire des enfants victimes de déplacement forcé, le projet prévoit la mise en place de cours de rattrapage à travers l’activation du mécanisme RRM(R4).L'action proposée s'inscrit dans la continuité avec les actions mises en place par COOPI sous financement ECHO depuis 2016 à Diffa et UNICEF depuis 2019 à Tahoua. De plus, elle vise à contribuer aux priorités EiE énoncées dans l’HIP 2024. Enfin, l'action contribuera aux objectifs du Cluster Éducation et du Sous-cluster PE et s'aligne aux politiques du Gouvernement de Niger en matière de protection et éducation formelle.

project_name: Amélioration des conditions d'accès aux infrastructures WASH et aux centres de récupération nutritionnelle pour les communautés affectées par le mouvement de population dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéri
project_objective:
Le projet « Amélioration des conditions d'accès aux infrastructures WASH et aux centres de récupération nutritionnelle pour les communautés affectées par le mouvement de population des régions de Diffa et Tillabéri » est un projet multi-sectoriel qui a pour objectif général de couvrir les besoins vitaux en eau, hygiène et assainissement des personnes et enfants malnutris affectés par la problématique de mouvement de population, à travers une réponse adaptée et ciblée sur une durée de 12 mois. 
La cible du présent projet, est particulièrement les populations affectées par la crise de mouvement de population au niveau des Départements de Diffa/Région de Diffa, et ceux de Téra, Tillabéri et Torodi, Région de Tillabéri. Ainsi à travers cette approche multisectorielle intégrant les composantes WASH et nutritionnelle, ce projet permettra spécifiquement d’une part aux personnes les plus vulnérables de ces départements aux besoins aigus, à avoir un accès continu aux services sociaux de base de qualité, en matière d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement, et d’autre part, à couvrir les besoins en services promotionnels, préventifs et curatifs de nutritionnels pour les enfants de 0 à 5 ans, et femmes enceintes et allaitantes.
A travers la mise en œuvre de ce projet, les communautés des régions de Diffa et Tillabéri verront leurs conditions d’accès améliorées à l’eau (qualité, quantité, trajet/distance, temps d’attente, …) à l’hygiène (lavage de mains à l’eau et au savon) et assainissement (utilisation de latrine adéquates) améliorées. A cela s’ajoute également l’acquisition de connaissance, pratiques et kits (dans le cas échéant), en matière de collecte, transport et stockage d’eau et de la préservation de la dignité humaine. Enfin ces communautés, notamment les enfants et femmes allaitantes ou enceintes admis aux centres de récupération nutritionnelle bénéficieront en plus de la promotion à l’hygiène, des connaissances sur la malnutrition et l’alimentation du nourrisson et du jeune enfant, des suppléments nutritionnels et kits de collecte, de stockage et traitement de l’eau à domicile.
Afin d’atteindre les différents objectifs assignés à ce projet, cette réponse s’articulera essentiellement à 4 activités ci-dessous : 
1) la mise en place des mesures et installations temporaires et/ou durable d'eau d'urgence aux personnes affectées par le mouvement de population à travers la fourniture d’eau, la distribution des produits de traitement d’eau à domicile et/ou désinfection des points d’eau inondés, le diagnostic suivi de réhabilitation et/ou optimisation des points d'eau existants, le fonçage de nouveau forage, etc. 
2) la promotion des bonnes pratiques d'hygiène et prévention des maladies (COVID-19, Cholera...) y compris l’accès aux kits d’hygiène, les formations /sensibilisations aux personnes affectées par le mouvement de population. 
3) la mise en place des mesures et installations d'assainissement d'urgence temporaires et/ou durable à travers la construction des latrines/douches/salle GHM d’urgence dotées des dispositifs de lavages des mains, la gestion des déchets solides et la réhabilitation des latrines, etc.
4) la mise à disposition du paquet minimum WASH in Nut aux couples enfants malnutris/accompagnant des centres de prise en charge jusqu'à domicile (kits d'hygiène, messages, suivi à domicile, activité de promotion des bonnes pratiques d'hygiène et prévention des maladies, etc.)

project_name: Réponse inclusive et de qualité aux besoins en éducation en urgence des enfants et des jeunes les plus vulnérables de la communauté des retournés au Sila, touchés par la crise à l’est du Tchad liée au conflit Soudanaise

project_name: Food Security and Nutrition sensitive livelihood options to build recovery and resilience to returnees, IDPs and host communities of Nasir and Ulang Counties in Upper Nile State
project_objective:
The war that broke out in Sudan in April 2023, has increased the number of people migrating into South Sudan through the Renk border. Migrants who consist mainly of returnees, are moving from Renk into Malakal and then transported to different location in South Sudan including areas in Upper Nile such as Nasir and Ulang. The populations of incoming migrants are faced with challenges of food insecurity, malnutrition for children under the age of 5 years & pregnant and lactating women, poor water- sanitation & hygiene, limited shelter, disease outbreak, lack of education for children of school going age and natural disaster such as flooding. According to a report by IMC in August 2023, for women and children fleeing Sudan and host communities, conflict, displacement and rising costs are worsening malnutrition rates. Returnees and IDPs have lost their livelihoods due to movement to safer areas, forcing the populations to depend on humanitarian assistance. This is further aggravated by flooding in Nasir and Ulang which began in October 2023. 
The Food Security Outlook report for South Sudan, published in July 2023, states that Emergency (IPC Phase 4) is expected to persist in Upper Nile State counties, with pockets of the population likely in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5) pushing the communities into dire food insecurity situation. However, during the needs assessment conducted by ADRA in Ulang and Nasir, returnees and IDPs stated that all means of production and tools were lost during the flee from violence rendering them not able to produce food unless assisted.  For the host community, access to traditional livelihoods such as livestock rearing and crop cultivation have decreased over recent years due to recurring shocks, including flooding, conflict, and displacement.
The project in Nasir and Ulang will target South Sudanese returnees who have fled from Sudan and Ethiopia to their country of origin due to the war and conflict which broke out in April 2024 in Sudan and sporadic conflicts in Ethiopia- Gambella, IDPs from within Upper Nile State and the Host community residing in the target areas. The main groups to be targeted will be children, women and youth and people with disabilities. According to the 2023 HRP Intersectoral Prioritization, Nasir is under priority 1 and Ulang under priority 2. ADRA has ongoing projects in these two locations and this project will be complementing the already existing activities and a layering approach will be employed. •	The project will target pregnant and lactating mothers, widows and teenage mothers. Pregnant and lactating women are vulnerable due to their increased nutritional needs and susceptibility to the harmful consequences of deficiencies. Pregnant and lactating women have been exposed to stressful conditions during migration and high levels of food insecurity where those interviewed mentioned that they spent days travelling without eating.  This group of women will be targeted for nutrition and livelihoods especially agriculture production. When war broke out in Sudan most women and children fled to South Sudan and men remained and this has increased the vulnerability of women who have become head of household within the returnees. Within the host community and IDPs women head of households will be targeted. Protection issues including GBV will be mainstreamed.
•	Children that will be targeted in this project include; children with disability, unaccompanied minors, orphans and those not attending schools or children with manifesting risk behaviors, children who are neglected by parents. 
•	Youths –youths will be targeted for livelihoods options. Youths will also be involved in peace building activities – (peace dialogues and conferences), peace structures in the communities will include youths who usually are not consulted for during decision making process due to lack of representation.
