project_name: WoS Education assistance for vulnerable and out-of-school children and youth in 2024
project_objective: For 2024, War Child (WC) and its consortium of 12 Syrian partner organizations will provide an education response to 23,932 highly vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities (240) PWD, (11,966 boys and 11,966 girls)in North West and North East Syria (Idleb, Aleppo, Raqqa, Deir-ez-Zor & Al-Hasakeh governorates) across a 12-month action. All targeted sub-districts are severity 3, 4 and 5. Recognizing the interconnection between protection and education, the action will increase access to non-formal education and strengthen the protection of vulnerable girls and boys who are out of school or at risk of dropping out, to build their resilience and provide a pathway back into a safe and protective environment in school. The action will include non-formal education interventions including Accelerated Learning Program (ALP) for out-of-school of vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities of the ages 6-17 who have missed more than two years of school. The action will also include guided self-learning for informal settlements with no access to learning spaces to keep vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities connected to learning, and for youth mainly boys who joined the working force to support their households and girls who are not sent to school and run the risk of early marriage. For schooled vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities  with learning gaps, remedial and homework support will be offered to limit the risk of dropping out. War Child's integrity framework fully incorporates (PSEA) strategy. Throughout the project cycle, we ensure that all our partners' staff receive comprehensive training and awareness sessions on PSEA, emphasizing its critical importance. An effective teacher professional development through a coaching system based on INEE’s TICC and WC’s Core program to ensure teachers’ and vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities wellbeing, will have coaches build the capacities of 200 teachers receiving incentives under the action. The coaches will be trained and supported by WC education coordinator based on teachers’ needs, to help teachers obtain skills and methodologies for the creation of a safe and quality learning environment for vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities. For the guided self-learning modality, teachers will be trained to support caregivers with guidance and tips to support their vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities learning and provide them with a safe learning environment at home. The action will adopt an integrated approach through developing the capacity of teachers on child protection and enhancing the accessibility and safety of the school environment. Teachers will be trained on safe identification and referral for CP concerns. This prevention and response approach will address immediate and urgent identified risks to access to education while contributing to long-term change. WC will be delivering its Core program, which combines scaffolded psychological care with real-time, individualized classroom support to teachers. Teachers’ competence and skills progression is monitored through WC developed follow-up tools.  WC will pilot social emotional learning (SEL) as an integrated approach that complements WC’s evidence-based Deals PSS programs. Teachers will be trained to identify, and work with vulnerable boys and girls including those living with disabilities to develop their life skill and learning competencies in the safe learning environment of the classroom. WC is incorporating the digital learning application Can't Wait to Learn (CWTL) into their System of Care. CWTL supports education, psychosocial support, child protection, and specifically aids vulnerable children, including those with disabilities, in crisis areas.

project_name: Strengthening Resilience and Wellbeing for Vulnerable Children and Youth in Syria
project_objective: The War Child (WC) programme, with a budget of 2,415,300 USD, is dedicated to increasing resilience and wellbeing among vulnerable children and youth in Northeast (NE) and Northwest (NW) Syria Hubs. This one-year project aims to respond to urgent Child Protection needs in Idleb and Aleppo and expand services in Raqqa, Al Hasakeh, and Deir ez-Zor. The project targets 9,939 people in need, focusing on Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC) and Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAAFAG). Under this project, WC will utilize Child-Friendly Spaces (CFS), structured Psychosocial Support (PSS), and awareness-raising activities. A key component is developing specialized service capacity within local partner organizations to deliver quality case management service. This approach addresses immediate child protection risks and contributes to long-term change by supporting parents, caregivers, local leaders, and communities in building a more protective environment for children affected by conflict. The project also involves collaboration with youth aged between 14-17 and their caregivers, focusing on enhancing life skills and strengthening protective factors at individual, family, and community levels. Structured workshops will address cognitive, emotional, and social functioning, supplemented by meetings with parents and caregivers. By aligning with the overarching objectives of the WC program and the North Syria hubs, the project not only tackles immediate needs but also fosters sustainable technical Child Protection capacity within local organizations, thereby enhancing the quality of the overall response and contributing to the mainstreaming of Protection outcomes. The War Child program diligently navigates various protection risks encountered in its operational areas. These include security incidents affecting staff, facilities, and beneficiaries. In response to these challenges, War Child adopts a vigilant and proactive stance. This involves a keen observation of security trends and developing contingency plans. Moreover, the organization is committed to providing thorough training to the management of partner organizations, equipping them with the necessary skills to manage these risks effectively. Furthermore, incidents related to child safeguarding are met with immediate and focused action. This includes the implementation of training initiatives and ongoing support to local organizations. The foundation of this approach lies in establishing clear policies and appointing dedicated focal points for these issues. Additionally, War Child enhances its adherence to humanitarian standards, creating a barrier against increased local authority interference. Efforts to counteract burnout and psychological distress among staff and caregivers are also a key focus. This is achieved through staff care programs and capacity-building initiatives. These measures are integral to War Child's strategy of collaborating with communities and caregivers. Special attention is paid to fostering social cohesion and easing tensions in areas with high concentrations of internally displaced persons (IDPs). The emphasis on these last two points is crucial, as they underline the organization's comprehensive approach to Protection risk analysis and the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, thereby maintaining the consistency and integrity of the program's objectives. To enhance the project's effectiveness and ensure a targeted response to the unique challenges in Northeast and Northwest Syria, WC conducted a comprehensive internal needs assessment. This assessment focused on Child Protection in general with more focus in understanding the specific requirements of Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC) and Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAAFAG).The assessment utilized key insights from the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) for years 2023 &2024, integrating this information to align the project needs

project_name: Réponse d'urgence (RRM) aux besoins en soins de santé, nutrition et soutien psychosocial des populations les plus vulnérables, déplacées et d’accueil, dans les régions touchées par les conflits, au Niger
project_objective:
"COOPI propose la continuation de l'intervention d’urgence (RRM Santé/Nut) sous l’égide de la protection transversale, visant à améliorer l’intégrité psychophysique des populations déplacées et d’accueil, basée sur les volets santé, nutrition et santé mentale .L’action propose une réponse coordonnée avec les acteurs présents dans la zone (acteurs santé étatiques et partenaires du cadre RRM/Santé et RRM/MultiSectoriel), en permettant aux populations déplacées et d'accueil de bénéficier d'une prise en charge spécialisée et holistique, gratuite et de qualité. Les axes principaux d’intervention sont: (i) le renforcement du mécanisme de veille humanitaire et épidémiologique, (ii) l’évaluation conjointe des alertes et la réponse rapide aux alertes confirmées, (iii) la PCIMAS, la prise en charge médicale au niveau de CRENI et l’assistante institutionnelle temporaire (iv)le renforcement de la coordination opérationnelle. Le projet présente un haut degré de flexibilité grâce à la prsence du crisis modifier, qui permet une rapide adaptation à la volatilité du contexte.
Le projet cible  les enfants (filles et garçons) de moins de 5 ans, vulnérables en terme nutritionnelle, les filles adolescents, les femmes et filles adolescentes enceintes, allaitantes et victimes de VBG, vulnérables pour la santé primaires/reproductive/nutritionnelle/mentale et les personnes handicapées. En plus des personnes affectées par la SMSPS sont aussi bénéficiaires, incluant les épileptiques, et la prise en charge sanitaire des personnes avec des handicaps est prévue. Le projet promu l'accès aux services de santé reproductive en recrutant et renforçant les capacités des spécialistes de la santé reproductive, y compris des prestataires féminins, comme les sage-femmes, en fournissant le paquet de services initial (MISP) pour la santé reproductive, en prévenant la transmission du VIH et des IST, en favorisant la promotion des services SR au niveau communautaire, en accompagnant efficacement les femmes enceintes et en fournissant une assistance médicale aux survivantes VBG. La problématique du handicap est prise en compte, les équipes avec les collaborateurs communautaires facilitent l'accès aux services d'assistance VBG et PSS aussi aux personnes vivant avec handicap. Les espaces pour femmes et enfants déplacées sont accessibles à toutes et tous à l'intérieur des sites, grâce à la mise en place des tentes; l'accès aux CSI et autres services pour personnes avec handicap est facilité par les moyens logistiques de l'équipe, à travers l'utilisation des cliniques mobiles.

project_name: Livelihoods and Economic Recovery NWS: Strengthening the resilience for conflict and EQ affected population in NW Syria
project_objective: The economy, severely impacted by the February EQ & conflict on October 23, has seen a major downturn. Data from REACH and ILO note significant declines in economic activity and jobs, with about 170,000 workers losing jobs due to EQ in February 23, impacting 725K Ind. While there is a high percentage of females working in the agriculture sector, 80% of them indicated that there were fewer jobs compared to other years, emphasizing challenges related to operating costs, water scarcity, and a lack of agricultural inputs. In January 2023, before the EQ, over 80% of businesses in Albab and Dana  were interested in expansing, albeit with high costs (cost of business assessment). According to IMMAP’s recent crop monitoring report, farmers reported a decline in production, due to factors such as drought and elevated prices of agricultural inputs such as seeds and fuel. The proposed project aims to support vulnerable populations lacking reliable income by improving access to markets and income-generating opportunities. CARE will establish VSLAs to provide disadvantaged communities with a platform for saving and accessing loans for business startups or acquiring productive assets. Infrastructure rehabilitation and maintenance of electricity stations will ensure equitable access to essential services, livelihood opportunities, and social cohesion.CARE's layered and sequenced activities, including vocational training and support for new and existing businesses, will enhance market resilience. The wheat and livestock VC initiative is pivotal in fostering economic sustainability and food security in NWS. By supporting the wheat-to-bread and its infrastructure, CARE aims to strengthen market systems, enhance sustainable livelihoods, and improve access to productive assets.CARE will provide cash assistance for agriculture support. The cash values are estimated by market assessments and FSL cluster guidance.CARE will collaborate with farmers andstakeholders to train farmers on effective soil enhancement techniques Seed quality are offered to both farmers and seed vendors, emphasizing the use of llocal varieties adapted to the agro-ecology and ensuring seed quality through germination tests. CARE will purchase flour to support bread subsidies, allocating 30% of this support as free bread to camp residents during the winter season.For bread production,high-quality ingredients from trusted suppliers will be provided, Staff will conduct regular inspections and tests throughout the baking process to monitor dough consistency, baking time and temperature, and product appearance, ensuring quality taste, texture, and appearance. CARE's livestock mobile clinics will provide essential veterinary services, while support for animal feed during the cold season and promotion of green fodder cultivation will ensure a sustainable source of fodder. Technical teams will supervise the mixing process of animal feed and ensure the purchase of both medicines and tools from trusted suppliers.- Integration of CARE ensures integration of protection priorities and provides training on the Code of Conduct & Safeguarding Policy to program staff. - Conflict Sensitivity and Risk Assessment: Utilizes tools like Do No Harm to identify potential harmful impacts of activities, prioritizing the safety and dignity of beneficiaries, especially women.- Global Protection Cluster Guidance: Committed to mitigating physical and psychological threats faced by affected populations, providing safety training and equipment, and facilitating access to assistance and services.-GBV Mitigation: Implements mitigation measures in line with IASC Guidelines, considering the risk of increased GBV due to changes in power dynamics resulting from women's. Youth and PWDs will be engaged during the design and implementation through integration with the protection team, inclusive outreach programs, tailored training sessions, and accessible communication channels.

project_name: Increased Access to Inclusive Quality Education in a Safe and Protective Learning Environment
project_objective:
The proposed project by NRC aims to ensure the right to equitable quality education in a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment for the displaced Rohingya refugees and surrounding host communities. The focus will be on providing access to non-formal education through the Myanmar Curriculum Accelerated Learning Programme (ALP) and Offline learning programme for the Rohingya community. Support to formal and non-formal education for the vulnerable host community will also be provided through remedial classes and offline library as well as need based rehabilitation support to WASH facilities in schools. NRC will support a total of 15,400 learners (55% female and 13% learners with disabilities) with access to equitable and inclusive quality education in a safe and protective learning environment. Specialized services will be designed, implemented, and monitored to ensure access to inclusive education, prioritizing female students, students with disabilities, and youth at protection risks, including the LGBTI community. 
The project also incorporates teacher support and capacity enhancement to strengthen teacher capacity to ensure improved teaching and learning support towards the learners. Project response components will include the provision of education supplies in the form of teaching and learning materials. The project will also focus on improving the learning environment through the rehabilitation of gender-segregated WASH facilities, handwashing facilities, and required classroom setup materials. Menstrual health and hygiene of adolescent girls’ learners will be supported through the provision of dignity kits to promote their access to continuous education and retention, and school-level hygiene awareness campaigns will be conducted. NRC will mainstream disability to promote access to education by children with disabilities. This will be through organizing awareness campaigns equally involving children with disabilities, promoting disability-friendly learning environments, and training teachers on inclusive education and gender-responsive educational practices. 
The project will also focus on the holistic development and well-being of the targeted population through psychosocial support activities and the integration of co-curricular activities. The NRC Better Learning Programme (BLP), a non-specialized, classroom-based psychosocial support program aiming at equipping youth with strategies to cope with stress and promote their psychosocial well-being. It also includes targeted capacity building for teaching staff and community volunteers to ensure sustainability and promote the psychosocial well-being of learners. Through the Safe and Inclusive Programming Approach (SIP), NRC will strengthen Community-Based Learning Facilities (CBLFs) protection initiatives and referral pathways, thereby contributing to resilience building and improved child protection mainstreaming. Furthermore, NRC will work jointly with the government and other stakeholders to support host community students in reducing engorged learning gaps that will also expedite/accelerate the involvement of the government.
NRC will work with Rohingya and host communities to promote cohesion and peaceful co-existence. NRC will also use a community engagement approach to promote community participation, ownership, and sustainability. Gender-responsive programming will be promoted through awareness campaigns and community engagement. Thus, community education groups consisting of community members and parents/guardians of learners will be formed and capacitated. Community members will also play a key role in engagement meetings and awareness raising of education activities. Crisis-sensitive planning, management, and coordination for quality provision will be ensured in collaboration with other actors as well as the government.

project_name: Provision of Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance to Rohingya and Host Communities to claim and exercise their legal identity and HLP rights
project_objective:
Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) provides a comprehensive legal aid approach designed to support individuals in navigating complex legal, administrative, and civil issues, every step of the way. It focuses on providing personalized assistance through tailored counselling and legal assistance. NRC will be implementing activities across 25 camps and 8 host community unions ensuring protection and gender mainstreaming. ICLA will work with the CiCs, UNHCR and other actors in camps to secure identity and documentation of Rohingya refugees through existing registration and documentation guidelines. Furthermore, through mobile clinics, ICLA provides its HLP services throughout all the camps. NRC will also work with Ukhiya and Teknaf local government authorities e.g. UNO office, UP office to host communities. 
The project is designed to positively increase access to identity documentation including Family Attestation Certificate, Smart Card, birth, death, marriage, and divorce certificates, required for accessing essential services, and HLP including tenancy rights in the refugee camps and host communities, whilst also mitigating and addressing tensions between the Rohingya and local communities generated by HLP disputes.   ICLA Bangladesh operates across several thematic areas, including access to legal identity documentation (LID) and Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) rights, addressing tenancy rights, rental disputes, evictions, ownership issues, and other HLP-related concerns. The approach involves assessment of each case, developing tailored plans that may include legal representation, advocacy, or mediation, and maintaining records to ensure effectiveness of support. ICLA case management stands out for its emphasis on empowering individuals with the knowledge and resources to address their specific barriers, promoting both immediate resolution and long-term resilience.
This objective will be achieved through the increased capacity of refugees and host communities to exercise their identity and HLP rights and improved access to collaborative dispute resolution mechanisms in communities. NRC will provide legal counselling and assistance based on individual needs to enable target beneficiaries to overcome legal, procedural, and documentation challenges, including referral to specialized case management actors as it may be required; combined with information dissemination and awareness-raising initiatives to empower target beneficiaries to claim their rights and access available justice mechanisms. Improvement of the relationships between refugees and host communities, and within the Rohingya community itself, will be achieved through the local leaders` capacity building in HLP dispute resolution. 
These supports contributing to project participants’ access to civil justice and other forms of humanitarian assistance. For both civil documentation and HLP, ICLA’s using general information sessions to raise community awareness of rights and to generate interest and awareness of the need for civil documentation and tenure security. Information sessions typically last 45-60 minutes and are open to all camp residents and are also conducted for vulnerable host community members. To address the widespread issue of refugees paying mahjis and others to complete their written applications, ICLA will supporting by the field staff to review refugee applications, assist beneficiaries in gathering supporting paperwork and witnesses, completing the written application, and submitting the completed package to the CiC office. ICLA follows a step-by-step approach, extending beyond application submissions to the CiC. This includes information dissemination, counselling, hospital visits for birth registrations, and intricate advocacy for necessary permissions and validations for identity documentation.

project_name: Multisectoral Area-Based Response for Vulnerable people affected by the protracted conflict in Adamawa and Borno states.
project_objective:
The proposed action will improve the living conditions of displacement and conflict individuals in Borno and Adamawa states across Maiduguri, Monguno, Gwoza/Pulka, Madagali through a multi-sectoral area based response. The affected populations in need of assistance will receive through Food Security, WASH, Shelter, Education General Protection and ICLA (Information Counselling and Legal Assistance) services building on NRC’s response under the 2022 HIP and ongoing interventions within the same targeted
localities to maximize the impact. Aligned to the HIP priorities and NRC’s view that the current emergency is protection centred all activities will be focused on reducing protection risks like exploitation, physical risks of movement, and transactional sex, among other risks and negative coping mechanisms caused by the lack of access to basic services. The action will equally focus on the displacement and conflict affected children provide and maintain access to safe, inclusive and quality Education to out of school
children. A comprehensive approach will be adopted to address identified barriers to education which include structural and economic barriers that hindered children access to education. The action will also build on the protection sector efforts towards the centrality of protection to ensure that NRC and other partners are taking a protection-focused lens in the Northeast response. Aligned to the
HIP2023 strategic priority, NRC will seek to address the growing and unexpected needs caused by floods and communal clashes through the use of the “Crisis Modifier”/”Disaster Preparedness” to ensure a timely response with Borno and Adamawa. Lastly, to contribute to better humanitarian access and protection, NRC through in-country, regional and global advocacy teams, will build on advocacy efforts to bring attention to the crisis in Nigeria.

project_name: Enhancing protection environment and well-being of populations affected by conflicts and other disasters in Adamawa (Mubi North and South, Madagali, Michika LGA) and in Borno (Maiduguri, Jere, Gwoza, Ngala, Bama, Monguno, and Konduga)
project_objective:
The project will focus on integrated protection monitoring with several sub-sectors including Mine Action, Trafficking and legal documentation. Following 2024 camps closures/other alarming protection concerns in Borno and Adamawa on top of rapid protection assessment for new areas, DRC will focus on adjusting its responses programmes according to protection concerns identified. IPA will still be provided as a direct response while DRC protection desks/centres will initiate a generalised responses to cases through further individual counselling in some areas as a pilot approach. Protection response services will be delivered at DRC Protection desks/Protection centers and the pilot of case management in cooperation with specialized (CP/GBV) case management services by strategic/operational partners will lead to a network of practictionners in emergency which will collaborate into exchanging good practices. DRC will also reinforce capacities and awareness on general PSS services through specific curricula adapted based on protection monitoring findings. DRC will especially pay attention on survivors of trafficking and SEA to follow proper referrals pathways and provide further support on spotting the signs of risks associated with it. While the project will strengthen the community-based approach and support the community based structures in choosing their favourite forms of community engagement (awareness sessions, drama, songs etc),  DRC within this project will expand its PSS services for the elderly and people with limited mobility opportunity to feel included. 
DRC will train relevant service providers at a community level, such as teachers, health workers and community structures, on MHPSS and work with the CB structures  to reduce stigma around mental health in Borno and Adamawa. 
  

The innovative approach that consists of integrating protection monitoring, trafficking and age concerns into the protection response will particularly materialize through the implementation of structured PSS, support of community based networks in identification of marginalised persons and an age, gender, diversity sensitive protection monitoring tools, and adapted curricula for all PSS age and gender groups.

project_name: Contribuir a mitigar las consecuencias de la crisis humanitaria en las comunidades afectadas para habilitar vías educativas para los niños en Venezuela
project_objective:
La Acción busca aumentar el acceso a vías educativas formales seguras, dignas e inclusivas para los niños y niñas vulnerables, al tiempo que fortalecer los mecanismos de prevención y respuesta a los riesgos de protección a nivel comunitario, garantizando al mismo tiempo una prestación de calidad de servicios de protección en el Estado Amazonas de Venezuela, en los municipios de Ature y Autana. En total, 4.395 personas (2.278 mujeres/niñas y 307 personas con discapacidad) se beneficiarán de este programa que se implementará en 7 escuelas y en las correspondientes comunidades.
Bajo el primer resultado, INTERSOS fortalecerá la capacidad de la comunidad educativa (incluidos maestros, padres y cuidadores, líderes comunitarios) para satisfacer las necesidades de aprendizaje de los niños y niñas, al tiempo que les permite identificar y abordar los principales riesgos de protección que podrían afectar a los NNA. Se mejorarán las instalaciones escolares (rehabilitaciones menores), prestando atención a las necesidades de los grupos con mayor riesgo de sufrir exclusión (niñas y adolescentes, NNA con discapacidad). Los docentes recibirán formación pedagógica específica con el fin de mejorar la calidad de enseñanza, y se les proporcionará material didáctico para fomentar el proceso de aprendizaje de los niños, niñas y adolescentes. Para disuadirlos de abandono de la profesión docente, y para asegurar su compromiso durante la ejecución del proyecto, se establecerán compensaciones distribuidas a los profesores de escuelas seleccionadas en forma de canasta de alimentos. Además, los NNA en edad escolar no escolarizados o en riesgo de sufrir el abandono de los estudios se incluirá en programas de clases de recuperación y se apoyará con material de aprendizaje. Por último, pero no menos importante, tanto los estudiantes como los profesores de las escuelas objetivo se beneficiarán del servicio PSS escolar destinado a mejorar su bienestar psicológico y, por tanto, la calidad de la enseñanza.
En el marco del segundo resultado, los riesgos de protección, cuales la alta tasa de abandono escolar, reclutamiento forzado, embarazo adolescente, violencia intrafamiliar, falta de documentación y por lo tanto invisibilizacièon de los menores e imposibilidad de acceso a los servicios del Estado (particularmente entre los niños , niñas y adolescentes) se abordarán mediante la prestación directa de servicios de protección ofrecidos por INTERSOS (gestoría de casos, asistencia legal y apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal) y formación de líderes comunitarios. Los servicios de proteccièon involucrarán especialmente los NNA y sus cuidadores, así como profesores, líderes comunitarios e instituciones, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a establecer un entorno protector a nivel comunitario/familiar para permitir el acceso de los niños a la educación. 
Las actividades de sensibilización y formación, incluirán sesiones de género, e INTERSOS realizará una gestión diferenciada de casos de VBG en la escuela, tomando en cuenta el género. INTERSOS, entre su personal de coordinación, cuenta con especialistas en protección, quienes guiarán el equipo técnico en las definición de las temáticas y metodologías más adecuadas para la implementación de las actividades y garantizarán una transversalidad de la protección durante toda la ejecución del proyecto, tomando en cuenta el contexto cultural de las comunidades indígenas.
Este proyecto se ha presentado y ha sido aprobado por ECHO.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle d'urgence aux populations affectées par l'insécurité alimentaire et les conflits dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa et Tahoua, et soutien aux services d'information humanitaire au Niger
project_objective:
Ce projet fournira une réponse d'urgence multisectorielle pour les individus les plus vulnérables affectés par la crise de sécurité alimentaire et la crise de protection/conflit. L'intervention se concentrera sur les zones difficiles d'accès dans les régions de Tillabéry, Diffa et Tahoua. 
i) Une aide alimentaire d'urgence flexible, répondant aux besoins immédiats des communautés touchées par les déplacements et l'insécurité alimentaire, dans les zones difficiles d'accès. Le projet adaptera l'assistance au contexte et aux besoins, en combinant des actions soudaines et des actions en période de soudure. Une approche à 2 piliers sera mise en œuvre : i) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant la période de soudure via du cash ; et ii) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant 3 mois aux personnes qui sont tombées plus tôt dans l'insécurité alimentaire en raison d'une très faible production alimentaire avant la période de soudure, en particulier lorsqu'elles sont victimes d'un choc. 
ii) Complété par des activités multisectorielles, renforçant la capacité de production alimentaire, les moyens de subsistance et la cohésion sociale, grâce à une intervention dans deux secteurs. Pour soutenir les capacités agricoles et les mécanismes d'adaptation, dans les zones où l'assistance alimentaire sera fournie, le projet soutiendra la production agricole et alimentaire au niveau des ménages, en intégrant les ménages les plus vulnérables dans des systèmes de résilience communautaires. En tenant compte du calendrier agricole, pendant la période de soudure, les bénéficiaires recevront des intrants agricoles pour les cultures pluviales et les cultures maraîchères. En outre, la diversification des ressources économiques au-delà de l'agriculture est essentielle pour assurer un accès inclusif, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées et les femmes (non-agriculteurs), aux activités économiques et couvrir la sécurité alimentaire et les besoins nutritionnels. D'autres personnes vulnérables bénéficieront d'un soutien aux AGR et à l'élevage par le biais i) d'un soutien aux éleveurs, ii) de la vaccination du bétail et des moyens de subsistance, et iii) des AGR.  
iii) Et en tenant compte de la nécessité de mesures de protection au niveau communautaire, notamment en raison de la crise accrue en matière de protection et de déplacement, afin d'améliorer la qualité, la responsabilité et l'efficacité de la réponse tout en garantissant l'accès à la protection de base et aux services WASH pour les personnes les plus vulnérables touchées par le déplacement. Grâce à des activités de type CCCM en dehors des camps, la troisième ligne d'intervention vise à prendre en compte le lien intersectoriel entre le déplacement et la sécurité alimentaire et à fournir un cadre de protection amélioré pour la population touchée par le déplacement, y compris les communautés d'accueil. Selon le CH, les départements ciblés affectés par les déplacements et les conflits sont en phase IPC3+ ; et l'impact de la crise de la sécurité alimentaire sur la protection des plus vulnérables ne fera que s'aggraver. La qualité et l'impact de la réponse doivent s'améliorer avec i) le renforcement de la coordination des déplacements au niveau de la crise, ii) une meilleure participation des communautés affectées, iii) des mesures de protection communautaires améliorées, iv) et une meilleure responsabilisation de la réponse humanitaire. La coordination et la diffusion de l'information seront renforcées et un mécanisme de protection mis en place pour améliorer la qualité de la réponse apportée aux PDIs. En outre, compte tenu de l'impact évident de la crise des déplacements sur l'accès aux services WASH et le lien avec la sécurité alimentaire et la nutrition, l'accès aux services WASH doit être assuré pour contribuer à renforcer l'environnement protecteur.  Ce niveau de réponse fournira un cadre et une base pour une réponse plus intégrée par zone, à tous les niveaux.

Further, IOM will build government capacity for humanitarian interventions through training of healthcare workers and emergency infrastructure and equipment support, and ensure mainstreaming of SRHR, HIV and GBV interventions in emergency capacity building to ensure no one is left behind.

Ensure access to and continuity of essential primary health and MHPSS services, including capacity building, procurement of equipment and medicines, service delivery, emergency referrals, and outbreak preparedness, response and surveillance operations for vulnerable displaced people and host communities. project_name: Appui EHA à la lutte Contre la malnutrition aigüe dans les départements de Tillia, Bouza et Madaoua ( Région de Tahoua), les départements de Madarounfa,  Nguidam-Roudji et Mayahi (Région de Maradi), les départements de Diffa, Mainé Soroa (Région  de Diffa) et les départements de Bankilaré, Say et Téra (Région de Tillabéri) au Niger.
project_objective:
"L’action s'inscrit dans une logique programmatique d’ACF-E visant le renforcement de l'accessibilité, de la qualité de la prise en charge et de la prévention de la malnutrition aigüe au Niger et en particulier dans les départements de Tillia, Bouza et Madaoua ( Région de Tahoua), de Madarounfa,  Nguidam-Roudji et Mayahi (Région de Maradi) de Diffa, Mainé Soroa et N'Guigmi (Région  de Diffa) et de Bankilaré, Say et Téra (Région de Tillabéry) . L'objectif est de réduire la morbidité et la mortalité due à la mauvaise qualité de l’eau et de l’assainissement, ainsi qu’au manque d’hygiène chez les personnes touchées par la crise et d'atteindre le niveau «de base» des services WASH pour tous, surtout chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans (filles et garçons). Le projet contribue à atteindre ainsi à l'un des objectifs principaux du cluster qui est de ""couvrir les  les besoins en EHA des enfants malnutris par les interventions adaptées et ciblées"". 
Il s’agira d’assurer le suivi du paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé pour l’amélioration du traitement de la Malnutrition Aiguë sévère (MAS) et aussi de renforcer les capacités des acteurs de la santé et des communautés en matière de changement de comportement et de la prévention de la malnutrition. Les couples mères enfants répondant aux critères d’admission CRENI seront ciblés prioritairement par les actions WASH. Par ailleurs, en intervenant dans les zones hotspot au choléra et autres aux maladies liées aux conditions WaSH, ACF-E se propose également d’apporter un appui aux structures de santé des Districts sanitaires ciblés en termes de renforcement de capacités et dotations des kits de désinfection pour accompagner les activités de la prise en charge de la malnutrition aigüe sévère dans les CRENAS et dans le CRENI.  De manière spécifique, l'intervention se fera à travers :                                                                                  
- la facilitation de l’accès à une eau potable dans les ménages MAS et leurs communautés (construction et/ou réhabilitation de points d’eau, mise en place CGPE/AUSPE, Promotion de la bonne gouvernance de l'eau, etc.) en collaboration avec les services techniques et la communauté cible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
- la mise en place d’un paquet minimum WASH dans les structures de santé de la zone d’intervention  ( système de stockage d'eau, maintenance périodiques des infrastructures, Gestion des déchets, Construction/réhabilitation d'ouvrages d'assainissement, dotation des kits WASH, etc.)                                                                                                                                   
- le Renforcement de capacités des centres de santé et du personnel en matière de prévention et contrôle des infections  ( formation sur les méthodes préventives et la désinfection des lieux, dotation en kits de prévention et riposte, etc. )                                                                                                                                                                                  
- la promotion du changement de comportement auprès des communautés cibles (DPI et hôtes) à travers les structures communautaires (Edm, GSANJE, etc.) sur les bonnes pratiques en matière d'hygiène et Assainissement: traitement de l'eau à domicile, Promotion du lavage des mains (WaSH'Em).
- le suivi à domicile des enfants MAS sortis de centres de traitement de la malnutrition (VAD) par approche Baby Wash. "
