project_name: Gender sensitive and life-saving integrated WASH response for multi-shock affected vulnerable communities in Syria
project_objective:
Leading the fight against malnutrition, ACF implements gender-sensitive and life-saving WASH interventions and provides communities with access to safe water and sanitation as sustainable mitigation for the causes of hunger. After 13 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their living conditions worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Türkiye. The erosion of basic service capacity has continued steadily, with water and sanitation systems, and public health services under immense strain, in a context of little development investment.
ACF operates through four offices in Damascus, Aleppo, Hama, and Al-Hassakeh. ACF has MoUs with the Ministries of Water Resources, Local Administration and Environment, Education, and Health. ACF actively engages with the WASH, Health and Nutrition, Food Security and Agriculture, and Early Recovery and Livelihoods, and Protection Sectors, as well as other sub-sectors and technical working groups such as Cash and AAP. ACF maintains close coordination with SARC, as well as with Governors’ offices and local administrations, and Line Ministries with which it has MoUs in place, including MoH, MoE, MoWR, MAAR, and MoSAL. In NES, ACF coordinates with UNICEF and the NES WWG for its interventions in Al-Hassakeh. 
ACF conducts integrated assessments to understand the needs and interlinkages of WASH, FSL, and Health and Nutrition. After conducting assessments in Aleppo, Hama, Latakia, and Al-Hassakeh, it was identified that community members have access to less than 30 l/p/d of water. Al-Hassakeh city relies on humanitarian agencies for water trucking, with no sustainable and complete exit strategy in sight (not least due to the condition of water resources in the governorate, and the lacking political solutions to ensure the permanent functioning of Allouk pumping station), and all targeted governorates need rehabilitation of the water systems, and the water pipelines as well as the sewage systems.
Under Sector Objectives 1 and 4, emergency WASH services provided by ACF include life-saving water trucking, distribution of water tanks, water quality testing and light maintenance of boreholes. ACF also undertakes the rehabilitation of damaged and malfunctioning water systems, which includes repairing boreholes, upgrading to solar energy, connecting water stations to the electric grid, repairing elevated tower tanks, repairing water networks at the community level, and providing equipment for water testing facilities. By providing water through public networks, ACF ensures greater control over quality and quantity, making it an affordable service. ACF also repairs sanitation systems at different levels, including pipelines, manholes and septic tanks, and provides support for solid waste management. This includes providing garbage bins for safe disposal in coordination with municipalities, as well as technical capacity building for technicians, PPE, tools and spare parts provision for sustained service provision after handing over to the local authorities. To improve public health, ACF engages in risk communication and community engagement activities that are tailored according to age and gender. 

Gender sensitive approaches and safeguarding of beneficiaries are integral to ACF programming, with dedicated staff upholding gender minimum standards and mainstreaming safeguarding processes. ACF recognizes the right of everyone to be treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation and abuse. ACF’s policy on PSEA complies with the IASC six principles relating to sexual exploitation and abuse. ACF provides compulsory training to each new staff member and refresher sessions to existing staff on organizational ethical policies. Internal policies relating to fraud, anti-corruption and abuse of power and whistleblowing/reporting mechanisms are followed with employees receiving instruction on these internal policies.

project_name: Enhance Equitable Access to Comprehensive, Integrated and Sustainable Health Services in Syria
project_objective:
Improving and sustaining essential, equitable, quality health services at primary, secondary and community levels are pivotal for effective response to the needs of the affected population. In 2024-2025, both humanitarian and economic indicators continue to deteriorate, with strains from the ongoing fuel crisis, February earthquakes and its aftershocks, and multiple disease outbreaks - such as measles, and cholera, and climate-related shocks exacerbating an already dire situation in Syria. According to the HNO (Health Chapter, 2024), over 14.9 million people in Syria are estimated to need healthcare assistance in 2024. Access and availability of health services are further compromised, especially for the most vulnerable groups, and the National Health System capacity to address the population’s needs is more strained than ever. 45% of public hospitals and 47% of PHCs are either non- or only partially functioning. Post-earthquake, the health system capacity suffered an estimated decrease of 10%  in affected areas. Additionally, a 28% increase in morbidity was reported for common conditions including diarrhea, with concerns for a spike in the ongoing Cholera outbreak and a subsequent exponential increase in rates of severe malnutrition in children. The Mental Health WG has reported an increase in psychological support needs, with cases of adults suffering from PTSD and panic attacks, and children suffering from micturition reflex, hyperactivity, and speech impairment. In NES, Al-Hassakeh continues to suffer from a severe shortage of health services; the ACF-supported Al-Lou'loua PHC is the only public health facility in government-controlled areas that provides in-patient services. The facility is undergoing transformation to a fully operational hospital to address the dire needs for secondary and emergency healthcare in the government-controlled areas of the governorate. ACF conducted a multi-sectoral community study in 2023 with 3,600 households in Aleppo, Al-Hassakeh and Hama, which revealed that health-seeking behaviours appear to be deteriorating in the communities surveyed, indicating poor uptake of healthcare services. Only 6% of surveyed women said they sought sexual and reproductive health services when needed and zero reported seeking mental healthcare. The percentage of home deliveries was high in the three governorates. C-sections were reported to be twice the standard. Most of the surveyed women lack access to trusted sources of information when it comes to their sexual and reproductive health, as well as their mental health. 
In 2024-2025, ACF response strategy will be aligned with Health Sector strategy in enhancing access to life-saving integrated primary and emergency healthcare health services, with a focus on surveillance and early detection of disease outbreak and increasing community and health system preparedness in targeted locations in Aleppo, Hama, Al-Hassakeh and Lattakia. Through its Health programme, ACF aims at improving access to comprehensive health services by enhancing entire health ecosystems through a layered and scalable strategy. This includes renovating targeted PHCs and mobilising medical outreach teams, providing training for quality primary healthcare services, providing medical supplies and providing renewable energy sources to operate effectively and provide safe and dignified health services. Linked secondary care facilities will also receive support with essential items and training to deliver critical life-saving services. A robust and trained community health network will deliver health (and hygiene) messages and facilitate the complete referral process. Moreover, feasibility studies will be conducted on medical procurement and Health Information Systems at PHC level to further strengthen the health ecosystem. In 2024, a particular emphasis will be placed on the mental health of the targeted population.

project_name: Comprehensive Lifesaving Health Intervention, including cash assistance, Idlib and Aleppo, north-west Syria.
project_objective:
In 2024, over 14.9 million people in Syria need life-saving primary and secondary health care, this includes 5.1 million displaced persons, 2.3 million children under five years – including 532,595 live births expected, 4.1 million women of reproductive age (15-49 years), more than 700,000 older persons, and 2.4 million persons with disabilities. Categories 3 and 4 health severity districts have increased from 89 and 113 in 2023 to 122 and 118 in 2024. 152 out of 270 sub-districts, home to 11.76 million people, lack minimum standards for hospital beds, healthcare workers, and functional primary healthcare centres (HNO 2024).
The project aims to address the severe healthcare challenges in North-West Syria, where compounded emergencies and socio-economic decline have resulted in widespread mental distress and significant health system strains. With many health facilities non-operational, the project focuses on improving access to primary and secondary healthcare services, including specialized oncology, for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities. Expected outputs include comprehensive primary healthcare services, impactful secondary healthcare, and improved access to oncology services. Specifically, the project establishes five primary healthcare centers and operates one general hospital, and one maternity. Through these facilities, services ranging from communicable and non-communicable diseases to emergency care, primary and specialized treatments are provided. Moreover, the project ensures equal access to quality healthcare services for all genders and age groups, directly addressing the diverse needs of women, men, boys, girls, and vulnerable individuals.

 Key Project Risks: 
- Natural Phenomenon/Earthquake/Aftershock (Medium):  
Sheltering during earthquakes and avoiding aftershock-prone areas. 
- General Protests & Demonstrations (Medium):  
Avoidance of protest areas and maintaining a neutral stance. 
- Aerial Bombardment/Shelling/Mortar (Medium):  
Various security measures include following SOPs, fortification, and early warning systems. 
- Opposition armed group internal clashes (Medium):  
Provision of situation reports, adherence to security protocols, halting activities if necessary, and SOPs. 
- Lack of Skilled Staff and Resource Access (Medium):  
Recruitment strategies, staff care, training programs, and advocacy. 
- Delay in Procurement of Medical Supplies (Medium):  
Early procurement approval and good planning.  
- Continuous Fluctuation in Exchange Rate (High):  
Advance funding, monthly budget review, and early fund amendment requests. 
- Temporary closure of border crossing between Türkiye and Syria for humanitarian aid (Medium):  
A reserve was allocated for contingency cases and close contacts with local Turkish authorities to ease the border crossing of goods and personnel. 

Protection/gender/GBV strategy
MI prioritizes gender equality across all its programs, mandating the disaggregation of data by gender and age. Compliance with this standard is obligatory for MI's partners. Ensuring equitable access to medical supplies, MI actively fosters fair healthcare delivery.
Field staff undergo comprehensive training on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) principles and utilize gender markers to address healthcare accessibility. The project staunchly advocates for the equitable access to humanitarian services, seamlessly integrating Gender-Based Violence (GBV) policies and PSEA principles through staff, activities, and information dissemination. All MI and partner staff receive orientation on no-harm principles and the protection of beneficiaries' rights. The project seamlessly integrates GBV awareness and PSEA measures, providing confidential complaint mechanisms and hotlines for reporting misconduct. Risk mitigation strategies include comprehensive service mapping, safety audits, and the provision gender and age sensitive facilities and services.

project_name: Respuesta multisectorial a población en situación de movilidad y comunidades vulnerables (incluidos retornados) y fortalecimiento de capacidades locales y comunitarias
project_objective:
Este proyecto brinda asistencia y protección multisectorial, facilitando una perspectiva humana de la movilidad,  a través de una extensa red de respuesta compuesta por 9 Centros de Alojamiento Temporal (CAT), 15 Puntos de Asistencia Móvil y 5 Refugios Temporales para Personas con Necesidades Especiales de Protección. La asistencia se desarrolla operativamente a lo largo de la ruta migratoria, áreas fronterizas terrestres y marítimas, comunidades de tránsito / acogida y comunidades indígenas en los Estados de Táchira Barinas, Apure, Zulia, Bolívar, Amazonas, Falcón y Sucre. En las zonas de frontera con Brasil y Colombia, el proyecto apuesta por una respuesta binacional más solida y coordinada. El foco de la asistencia y la protección está puesto en las personas en movimiento, (con especial atención en este proyecto a los retornados), mujeres, niñas, niños no acompañados (NNA), personas mayores, LGBTQI+, personas que viven con VIH, personas con discapacidad, sobrevivientes de violencia de género y víctimas de trata. Las comunidades remotas y vulnerables en riesgo de desplazamiento en los estados fronterizos, incluidas las comunidades indígenas en zonas mineras en Bolívar y Amazonas, son de especial de interés del proyecto debido a los altos riesgos de protección y desplazamiento interno. 

Además, la asistencia directa y protección incluye una estrategia de estabilización comunitaria para promover el nexus humanitario-recuperación, destinada a abordar las necesidades básicas de la comunidad, iniciativas de recuperación económica y medios de vida a nivel comunitario para una mejor reintegración y el fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de cohesión y participación de las redes comunitarias. El proyecto hace especial énfasis en el desarrollos de iniciativas de medios de vida como estrategia para la prevención/ protección de víctimas de trata y sobrevivientes de violencia de genero y en la preparación comunitaria para los desastres (migración-cambio climático), mejorando la comprensión de los riesgos/amenazas y desarrollar una cultura de adaptación al cambio climático. 

La Matriz de Seguimiento del Desplazamiento  de OIM (DTM) y los productos de gestión de la información (paneles de control, informes temáticos, estadísticas, evaluaciones multisectoriales, encuestas, etc.) es un elemento transversal del proyecto, facilitando  información clave sobre los flujos migratorios, la dinámica y las tendencias de desplazamiento, las necesidades humanitarias y los principales riesgos para los actores humanitarios.

Resultado 1: Las personas en movilidad y las comunidades vulnerables tienen acceso a asistencia humanitaria oportuna y vital en AEE. 
Resultado 2 Las personas en tránsito y comunidades de acogida han mejorado su seguridad alimentaria y medios de vida.
Resultado 3: Las personas en tránsito y comunidades vulnerables de acogida en Venezuela han mejorado sus condiciones de higiene y de acceso al agua segura. 
Resultado 4: Las comunidades vulnerables y la población en movilidad tienen acceso a la Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial (MHPSS) y  a la Atención Primaria en Salud incluyendo en los 9 Centros de Alojamiento Temporal y 15 Puntos Móviles de Asistencia.
Resultado 5: Fortalecimiento de la capacidad de las entidades locales en temas relacionados con la migración y la asistencia en servicios básicos y de protección a los venezolanos en situación de vulnerabilidad (con especial énfasis en sobrevivientes de GBV, VoT, NNA).
Resultado 6: Actores humanitarios tienen acceso a información sobre flujos, tendencias necesidades y vulnerabilidades y análisis temáticos específicos de la población en movilidad a través del DTM

Socios: OIM ha consolidado una cartera de 15 socios  locales, que garantizan el enfoque de localización con altos estándares de implementación y un marco de rendición de cuentas a las comunidades.

project_name: Leo, juego y aprendo
project_objective:
El proyecto busca promover, a través de un modelo de innovación educativa, el desarrollo de habilidades para el presente y el futuro en niños y niñas vulnerables de Venezuela, como lectura y escritura. Se propone (i) ofrecer a docentes/formadores acceso y capacitación en herramientas educativas innovadoras, y (ii) generar productos de investigación, conocimiento y comunicaciones que permitan sensibilizar sobre la importancia de la innovación y  fortalezcan capacidades de organizaciones de la sociedad civil.

El proyecto, desde su modelo de innovación educativa beneficiará a 50.000 niños y niñas vulnerables, 3.300 docentes/formadores en 19 estados del país , se fortalecerán capacidades de 10 organizaciones de la sociedad civil.

El proyecto tiene como objetivo lograr que los niños/as entre preescolar, primero y segundo grado de primaria, adquieran habilidades de lectura y escritura a través de la capacitación y apoyo a docentes y organizaciones de la sociedad civil en el uso de estrategias pedagógicas innovadoras. Este modelo innovador está centrado en: recursos impresos y digitales con el material ATAL (Aprendamos Todos a Leer), tanto para niños/as y personal docente, el cual  suministra estrategias pedagógicas efectivas para el aprendizaje de la lectura y escritura de los niños. También contamos con la capacitación y seguimiento al docente y la evaluación.

project_name: Fortaleciendo la respuesta en VBG para mujeres, adolescentes, niñas y otros grupos vulnerables en contextos de respuesta humanitaria
project_objective:
Honduras es el segundo país con mayor índice de violencia contra las mujeres en Centroamérica, y la vulnerabilidad de las mujeres y niñas aumentó por la pandemia de COVID-19 y el paso en 2020 de las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota (CDM, 2020). Dado este contexto desafiante se propone la prestación de servicios de atención especializada para las mujeres, adolescentes y mujeres sobrevivientes de violencia (MSV). Trócaire ha demostrado que con sus intervenciones las MSV experimentan procesos de cambios reales en sus vidas en términos de su bienestar y calidad de vida. Estos cambios se han dado a partir de su integración a procesos donde se satisfacen sus necesidades específicas, por ejemplo, formación y apoyo integral que las dotan de herramientas para abordar la situación de violencia que experimentan y a plantearse rutas de salida ante esas situaciones. En la práctica, la inclusión del enfoque de género ha revelado como reto el conocer la complejidad del “patriarcado”, y reconocer sus manifestaciones. Es decir, el reto ha sido comprender cómo el patriarcado controla todas las decisiones y normas sociales dentro del ecosistema que opera en los Programas (Trocaire, 2020). Es por ello que se fortalecerán las organizaciones centradas en mujeres para la presentación de servicios especializados para responder a las necesidades específicas de las mujeres y niñas, incluyendo además las necesidades de las mujeres defensoras de derechos humanos (MDDH). Así mismo que las OSC conozcan las rutas de atención para una adecuada referencia a servicios especializados. Se propone tener un mayor enfoque de trabajo con MDDH, ya que los obstáculos para las defensoras son aún mayores en la medida que las violencias dirigidas contra ellas y los mecanismos formales para su protección han estado permeados de las condiciones históricas de discriminación y subordinación hacia la población femenina (altos niveles de VBG y de impunidad, normativas restrictivas, cultura machista, amplias brechas de género para acceso a derechos), (Red Nacional de Defensoras, 2020). 
El enfoque geográfico se centrará en 8 departamentos del país: Choluteca, Francisco Morazán, La Paz, Comayagua, Intibucá, Cortes, Atlántida y Colón. Estos departamentos presentan altos niveles de vulnerabilidades por los desastres naturales, vulneraciones de derechos humanos y el comportamiento de la violencia contra las mujeres, así como la presencia de prácticas sociales e institucionales que refuerzan la discriminación contra las mujeres y las niñas, naturalizando las violencias basadas en género y profundizando las relaciones desiguales de poder.
Se trabajará de manera directa con las mujeres, niñas, las adolescentes mayores, las MSV y las que se encuentran en situación de riesgo, así como las MDDH. Además, se trabajará con Organizaciones de mujeres, redes de mujeres y OSCs mixtas para el fortalecimiento de capacidades. En cuanto a los grupos objetivos secundarios el enfoque del proyecto está dirigido a titulares de deberes vinculados al marco legal e institucional de los derechos de las mujeres.
A nivel micro, se trabajará en el desarrollo de capacidades individuales para mujeres incluyendo MDDH, las adolescentes y las MSV, para que se reconozcan como sujetos de derechos. También se fortalecerán las capacidades de organizaciones y redes para el establecimiento de estrategias y programas centrados en mujeres, y la incorporación de servicios especializados en VBG en emergencias. Además, se implementarán herramientas para la sensibilización en materia de igualdad de género para el cambio de patrones culturales y sociales patriarcales.
A nivel meso, se consolidarán las articulaciones y alianzas en espacios de coordinación local y regional, se desarrollarán investigaciones como base para desarrollar estrategias de incidencia. A nivel macro, las redes, organizaciones y plataformas coordinarán acciones de incidencia a nivel nacional frente a marcos jurídicos, legal y presupuesto.

project_name: Providing health and nutrition life-saving services to the most affected populations in NWS.
project_objective:
Needs: According to HNO 2024 summery an HPC health sector package, over 14.9 million people in Syria are estimated to be in need of life-saving primary and secondary care health assistance in 2024.The already exhausted Health System in NWS cannot cope with this increased number of people in need. 
After earthquake, Out of the total 585 health facilities assessed by the health cluster in NWS, 15% (97) health facilities were reported damaged [23 fully damaged and 71 partially damaged],which affects the access to health services for the population of NWS. Additionally, 4.2 million women of reproductive age in the health sector PIN require health care assistance to access essential reproductive health services, including antenatal care, safe deliveries, postnatal care, family planning, and comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care. Of the 501,783 live births expected163 in 2023, an estimated 75,267 of those women will need assistance to access emergency cesarean sections to save their lives and that of their newborns.
Intervention, Implementation of Activities: CARE will continue to address health and nutrition needs including SRH, general consultations, pediatric consultations, awareness raising on health and nutrition, nutrition services and contributing to strengthening the health systems by operating ambulance networks facilitating transport of high-risk cases. Additionally, the project will focus on integration between SRH and GBV through implementing AMAL initiative and ensuring safe referral in place. To support localization, CARE will implement the proposed activities through local organization and will provide the needed technical and administrative support. The activities are monitored via regular monitoring, and evaluation by implementing partners as well as by CARE's health and protection technical consultants. The locations and facilities will be as following: Amal hospital for maternity and pediatric in Azaz, Amal PHC for primary health care in Azaz, Ambulance centers in Armanaz,DaretEzzah and JisAlshugur.three BEmONC centers in Baba Alsalam,Aghtrin,and Albab, with integration of SRH  within three CARE WGSSs in azaz including RH consultation, FP and SRH awareness raising session ,Kelly and Bennish.Nutrition teams will be integrated in the HFs.They will deliver  nutrition services, including MUAC screening, distribution of micronutrients, IYCF awareness sessions, and referrals to CMAM centers. One RRT will be established in the Aghtrin sub-district.


PRA: CARE aims to address community needs, particularly those of women, boys, and girls, while considering local norms. Facilities will be located for accessibility, including for PWDS. Transportation will be provided as needed, prioritizing women, girls, and boys, to improve access to health services. CHWs, both male and female, will be mobilized to reach the most vulnerable, with a focus on outreach services. Integrating SRH clinics into CARE WGSS will create additional safe spaces for women, girls, and GBV survivors to access essential health support. 

PSEA strategy: CARE Safeguarding Policy applies to all Employees and Related Personnel. CARE conducts programmatic safeguarding risk assessments for each project, conducts GBV and PSEA Field Check List quarterly and mitigates risks accordingly with the risks identified. All feedback and complaints channels are shared with the community members on regular basis. CARE carefully examine allegations and investigate, and take appropriate disciplinary action where needed, considering the rights and interests of the survivor.

Risks, and Mitigating measures: CARE prioritizes security protocols and closely monitors conflict developments. Project activities are directly monitored at various levels. CARE has drafted a contingency plan detailing planning efforts, scenario forecasting, and options to adapt programming. Contingency plans are in place to manage significant outbreaks in NWS while safeguarding field staff.

project_name: Mitigación del impacto de la crisis migratoria en la Selva del Darién (Colombia y Panamá) en la salud de la población vulnerable
project_objective:
El tapón del Darién es un área de selva pantanosa ubicada en el límite de America central (Panama) y América del sur (Colombia). Desde hace más de 20 años la ruta del Darién ha sido una ruta migratoria para las personas que buscan mejores condiciones de vida en el norte del continente, específicamente para quienes intentan llegar a Estados Unidos, sin embargo, en los últimos años el número de personas que emigran por esta ruta ha tenido un incremento exponencial a pesar de ser considerado el punto más peligroso de las rutas migratorias. Tanto en referencia a lo reportado por Migration Mixed Centro, como lo referido por MSF y los diferentes testimonios de personas que han logrado cruzar el Darién, el principal riesgo para la vida de los migrantes es las enfermedades y accidentes agravado por las condiciones físicas de los migrantes. El 91 % de las personas que cruzaron el Darién se vieron expuestos a lesiones o enfermedades durante la travesía, el 77% a situaciones de muerte, el 73% a situaciones de robo, el 46% a violencia física, el 39% a violencia sexual, el 31% a soborno y extorsión, el 28% a violencia no física, el 26 % a secuestro, el 20 % a detención, y el 86 % de los niños estuvieron expuestos a situaciones de riesgo. MdM presente en Darién desde septiembre 2023 apunta que muchos migrantes no están todos en condiciones físicas para realizar este recorrido, y en especial los niños y niñas, y las personas no tienen la información pertinente de lo que les espera. Por este motivo MDM trabaja, desde el ultimo campamento antes de la entrada a la selva, mejorar la probabilidad de preservar la integridad física y moral de los migrantes, y en particular niños, niñas y mujeres que deciden cruzar la selva del Darién, mediante una mejor preparación y prevención de los factores de salud física y moral. Esto a través de:

•	El fortalecimiento de  la capacidad de resiliencia a las enfermedades de la población a punto de cruzar el Darién:  Brindando servicios de consulta en atención primaria en salud , psicológicas y medicamentos (medica, psicología, enfermería)  a mujeres migrantes, especialmente a embarazadas, madres solteras, víctimas de violencia basada en género, niños/niñas y adolescentes no acompañados, personas víctimas  de violencia durante la ruta migratoria, minorías  a quienes se les vulneran sus derechos, (población LGTBIQ,  minorías étnicas, entre otros)  personas con enfermedades crónicas sin acceso a medicamentos y seguimiento de sus patologías. Verificar que no tienen heridas abiertas o infecciones de pieles a se podrían complicar en el ambiente de selva 1.b Proporcionar medicamentos necesarios para restablecer condiciones de salud eventuales; brindar el tratamiento básico para los pacientes crónicos (Hipertensos y diabéticos no insulinodependientes, garantizando 1 mes de tratamiento) y brindar el tratamiento con micronutrientes para las embarazadas. (2000 beneficiarios)

•	Reducir las probabilidades de incidentes accidentes de salud que comprometan el pronóstico vital de los caminantes: equipando debidamente los migrantes para evitar enfermedades en el camino, brindando información sobre situaciones de peligro que se pueden presentar en la ruta y como brindar los primeros auxilios básicos y formando los primeros respondientes en primeros auxilios, con énfasis en las afectaciones de salud que más se presentan en la ruta, así como proporcionando kit de primeros auxilios para el manejo de las afectaciones de salud que más se presentan en la travesía.

project_name: Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions
project_objective:
The project titled ‘‘Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions” aims to empower communities and achieve gender equality by ensuring that People of concern to UNHCR receive proper assistance, including livelihood opportunities, cash-based interventions and inclusion initiatives that will ensure a dignified life and the respect of beneficiary rights. Activities planned to be implemented in 2023 seek to improve the protection and living conditions of 60,450 direct beneficiaries (42,315 refugees and 18,135 Cameroonians) and 181,350 indirect beneficiaries during lifetime of project. The project targets East, Adamawa and northern regions focusing on the most vulnerable groups, with 52.33% representing female (women & girls) and 53.63% of children (girls & boys) respectively. Based on IMC-UK October 2022 statistics, these regions host 327,976 Central African Refugees (CAR) in both developed sites (74,503 refugees) and off-sites (253,473 refugees).2 In addition, among these Central African refugees, 57,726 are people with specific needs, including 12,103 women at risk and 6,474 persons living with physical disability.  
As part of this project, it is necessary to strengthen community anchoring, thus facilitating the exit and sustainability strategy, which are based on the full participation of all stakeholders. Sustainability therefore aims at a transfer of competence to the government and its decentralized structures, including the communities. In other words, it is about preparing them to take charge of the protection of refugees and vulnerable populations. To do this, the proposed project will be implemented through four main strategic axes: 
Capacity building of community-based organizations for self-ownership of all activities carried out for their benefit, in particular protection activities. In doing so, it will be able to identify its problems and provide solutions based on resources that can be mobilized locally. This involves revitalizing all the protection committees (School for Husbands, Women's Committees, Youth Committees, Gender Club, Girl Shine, etc.) within refugee sites, building the capacity of Local Protection Committees (LPC) by providing them with working materials, the strengthening of community mechanisms for the identification, reporting and care at community level of people with specific needs, in particular survivors of GBV, abandoned children or children living alone, the elderly, people living with disabilities, the chronically ill and large families (under the lead of the CLPs). 
Capacity building of decentralized State structures (MINAS, MINPROFF, MINSANTE, MINJUSTICE, MINJEC, FMO, etc.) so that they are better equipped to take care of vulnerable people. The sectors seem to consider community-based protection activities as the competence of humanitarian actors. When they are called upon to be involved, they sometimes make their participation conditional on financial motivation. At both the operational and strategic levels, there is a lack of knowledge of subjects such as GBV by all sectors. This does not facilitate better appropriation of interventions and weakens coordination. 
Safe spaces for women and girls will be converted into centers of wealth production. To do so, the beneficiaries of the services (skills building and informational activities) offered by these centers will be trained and organized in such a way as to ensure proper management of the center and of the products resulting from their work. These structures will be technically supported by the MINPROFF with financial support from the Councill of the locality. 
A multi-sectoral approach that is psychosocial, medical, security and legal assistance will be necessary to ensure the success of our main objective. IMC-UK will focus on the services most crucial to ensure maximum impact on the target populations (refugee and vulnerable host community).

project_name: Emergency response to the nutrition crisis in Chad
project_objective: The priority provinces for 2024 are targeted to strengthen the national capacity to improve access to quality treatment for 382,015 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition in the existing nutrition treatment units, both the outpatient (OTPs) and inpatient units (IPFs), while strengthening preventive nutrition services at community and health facility levels. This will include i) the provision of nutrition therapeutic supplies including RUTF as well as medicine for the timely and quality treatment of children suffering from SAM and medical complications deriving from SAM and ii) Strengthening the capacity of SAM treatment of health structures and an effective nutritional surveillance system and iii) strengthening of nutrition preventive interventions through awareness raising activities using the promotion of optimal infant and young child feeding practices as an entry point. This action will also contribute to the measles response through Vitamin A supplementation for 1,120,000 children.

project_name: Una respuesta integral de protección y salud con enfoque de género e inclusión frente al conflicto armado en Colombia
project_objective:
Humanity and Inclusion (HI) han formado un consorcio para proporcionar protección integral y complementaria y asistencia sanitaria a las poblaciones vulnerables afectadas por la crisis en Colombia. Se llegará a un total de 38.285 Un total de 38.285 personas se beneficiarán de estos servicios en los departamentos de Cauca, Nariño, Norte de Santander, La Guajira, Cundinamarca y Antioquia.
La acción proporcionará la prestación directa de servicios de alta calidad en a) protección; b) rehabilitación física y funcional y estimulación de la primera infancia, c) servicios clínicos de salud mental; y d) atención sanitaria sexual. La capitalización de proyectos anteriores en estas respectivas áreas permitirá desarrollar un enfoque reforzado e integrado de la protección que reforzará los espacios seguros, la formación, la información y la sensibilización, así como la promoción de los intereses. De este modo, se abordarán las barreras estructurales y socioculturales al tiempo que se crea un entorno propicio para satisfacer las necesidades urgentes y específicas, y la participación e inclusión significativas de las personas afectadas en la acción humanitaria.
En Colombia, debido a la intersección entre el conflicto armado interno, la migración mixta transcontinental y los frecuentes desastres, las poblaciones metas serán las personas vulnerables. Se prestará especial atención a las poblaciones más afectadas por la violencia, el conflicto y el desplazamiento. El proyecto abordará las necesidades específicas de las personas con discapacidad y/o problemas de salud mental, las mujeres, los adolescentes, las mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, las comunidades étnicas e indígenas y otros grupos marginados, como las personas LGBTQI+. El diseño de la acción se basa en gran medida en la experiencia adquirida en la ejecución de programas financiados por ECHO y otros programas en años anteriores.

project_name: Supporting crisis-affected populations in Far-North region through the provision of multi-sectoral assistance in Cameroon
project_objective:
Following the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach that IOM strongly supports and actively promotes in Cameroon, and building on the programmes and activities implemented in the recent years, IOM plans comprehensive emergency interventions for 2024 focusing especially on coordination, shelter, mental health support (health), psychosocial support (protection) and WASH interventions. IOM’s multisectoral response aims at contributing to reinforce life-saving assistance and to improve well-being of displaced and the most vulnerable populations affected by the crisis in the Far North region of Cameroon. Critical data on displacement situation, alerts as well as humanitarian needs following our DTM methodology will be provided to the humanitarian community in the frame of the Coordination Sector. IOM will also distribute shelter and NFI kits using cash-modality solutions when possible (bearing in mind that lack of civil documentation poses a huge challenge) and help the construction for most vulnerable people. In the WASH response, IOM will drill and rehabilitate boreholes, construct water points, latrines and other infrastructures and conduct hygiene sensitization and promotion activities. Finally, IOM multisectoral assistance will also include mental health activities including direct MHPSS assistance using PMTs, reinforcing 
referral mechanism and capacity building of health actors (Health sector), while also directly providing psychosocial support to populations impacted by crisis by reinforcing safety and social network as well as strengthening community capacity to provide psychosocial support to victims of GBVs (Protection sector). These interventions are complementary to other programmes IOM implements in the region, focusing on DDR or social cohesion and by creating synergies within such initiatives, aim at achieving the HDP collective outcome set by the National HDPN Taskforce of Cameroon : “the most vulnerable populations in the convergence areas or in other regions affected by the crises recover indiscriminately their fundamental rights and improve their physical well-being and social welfare.”
The project will target various localities in the Far North region considering the level of needs and vulnerabilities observed and consulted with coordination with each sector of planned interventions. When feasible and appropriate, participative targeting workshops involving local community members and Humanitarian, Development and Peacebuilding partners in the localities will also be held.  
IOM respects its procedures to handle complaints on SEA starting with a focal person to receive and handle complaints and the building of knowledge of IOM staff and IPs about IOM’s policy and mechanisms to prevent SEA, including training on the proper conduct to handle SEA disclosures. IOM will also make usage of the Far North GBV referral pathway to refer SEA cases.
Through activities, direct feedback from beneficiaries and community members will be gained via IPs and also directly by IOM staff during field visits and visits of the M&E/AAP independent team in accordance with the wider IOM AAP emergencies workplan. AAP focal points will be assigned in Maroua and Yaounde respectively, with clear SOPs to be in place to capture complaints from beneficiaries and to take any appropriate action. Members of IP will be trained on topics such as the proper handling of disclosures of gender-based violence (GBV) incidents, aspects of confidentiality, and respectful communication in high-stress environments.

project_name: Enhancing Nutrition Access and Multi-Sectoral Services for Maternal and Child Health in South Sudan: Aweil South, Rumbek East, Rumbek North, Panayjair, and Yirol West Counties
project_objective:
Children and women in South Sudan continue to experience the devastating effects of malnutrition. According to the 2023 FSNMS and SMART survey’s findings, the national Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) levels remain above the WHO emergency threshold of 15%, with 2.5 million children and women at risk of acute malnutrition in 2024 and will need urgent treatment. The recent SMART survey 2023 and FSNMS round 29 findings, reveals serious and critical nutrition situations in the 5 counties that IRC operates in.  The SMART Survey 2023 reveals GAM rates of 14.3%, 19.2% in Yirol west and Aweil South counties, respectively. According to the FSNMS round 29, Panyijiar county has alarming proxy GAM rate of 28.2%, Rumbek north and Rumbek East counties have Proxy GAM rates of 12.1% and 11.6% respectively. The key drivers of malnutrition are high morbidity among under five children, high household food insecurity resulting in sub-optimal infant and young child feeding practices, poor water, sanitation and hygiene. This underscores the pressing need for multi-sectoral response and coordination mitigate the impact of malnutrition on children and PLWs. 
The objectives of this action will be: To increase equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services to prevent malnutrition and build resilience among children, adolescents, and women. To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of wasting for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW. To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis, and utilization of nutrition information. To strengthen coordination & integrated programming with health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors for equitable access to services that address key drivers of malnutrition among vulnerable groups in Aweil South, Rumbek East, Rumbek North, Panyijiar and Yirol west by the end of 2024.The proposed intervention aims to increase coverage and access to the most vulnerable community by providing equitable and accessible nutrition prevention treatment services. The nutrition services will deliver by scaling up the emergency nutrition responses through 62 static OTP/TSFP (10 in Aweil south,10 in Panyijar, 23 in Rumbek east, 7 in Rumbek North, and 12 in Yirol west), 5 Stabilization center (1 inPanyijar, 1 Aweil south, 1 in Rumbek east, 1 in Rumbek north, and 1 in Yirol west) and through 4 RRM mobile tam (2 in Aweil south, 2 in Panyjar,). In addition, the IRC will implement integrated CMAM and MIYCN in all sites. Promotion of optimal nutrition and prevention of malnutrition among young children (0-23 months through the implementation of MIYCN to ensure vulnerable children have optimal growth. IRC will strengthen community participation using existing community structures and active engagements of the affected community. IRC will conduct meetings with MtMSG, regular community sensitization sessions and scaling up of the existing Nutrition response to ensure timely service availability. Scale up family MUAC to ensure early detection of acute malnutrition. An estimated 21,223 SAM children, 52,069 MAM, and 37,064 PLW MAM will be reached through this action across all implementation areas in OTP and TSFP, respectively. IRC will continue with the capacity building of CHD, primary health care service providers and nutrition staff on CMAM and MIYCN to ensure timely nutrition services. A rapid response team will be deployed to the hard-to-reach area to provide nutrition services that are accessible and vulnerable groups. Integration of nutrition activities with other sectors will also be implemented, including integration of health and nutrition education messages, Malaria testing and treatment, promotion of hygiene and sanitation, training on GBV and CP for nutrition staff. Similarly, with food security, establish kitchen garden, cash programs and train CNVs on agronomic and fish preservation techniques.

project_name: Enhanced Access and Utilization of Quality Health Services in South Sudan (Aweil East, Aweil South, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijar and Rubkona Counties)
project_objective:
Conflict, natural hazards, epidemics, and the recent Sudan Crisis have severely impacted South Sudan's health systems. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) proposes a project to address the immediate lifesaving healthcare needs of 243703 people in need, including the elderly and persons living with disabilities. The project will provide essential outpatient care, child health care, safe motherhood, sexual and reproductive health, mental health care, gender-based violence response, and emergency preparedness and response in Rumbek East (Lakes State), Aweil East (Northern Bahr El Ghazal State), Koch, Mayendit, Panyijar & Rubkona Counties (Unity State).

The project will support 10 static health facilities, and 10 Rapid Response mobile (RRM) outreach posts and strengthen community health services by deploying 80 Boma Health Workers each in the targeted counties. Communities and County Health Departments will be engaged to map out underserved populations and prioritize displaced populations without access to health services. The project will also support rehabilitating structures, qualified staffing, pharmaceutical supplies, and health management information systems.

The integration of services will be prioritized through multi-sector collaboration with food security, livelihoods, nutrition, and protection mainstreaming. Providers will have capacity strengthening on mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services, Clinical Management of Rape (CMR), and infection prevention and control (IPC) measures. The IRC will staff, resource, and facilitate early deployment of RRM teams to locations pre-identified by the community and CHDs, factoring in the health priorities of affected populations.

Coordination through local duty bearers and partners, as well as national and subnational coordination mechanisms, will be an integral component of the response. The project will consider the perspective of affected people through IRC’s Client Responsiveness Measurement Framework as part of its AAP, and people with disability will be prioritized in its response. A joint support supervision for health staff will be done with CHDs and partners to reinforce capacity building and project quality.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving GBV interventions for the crisis affected populations
project_objective: IRC through its Women Protection and EmpowermenIRC through its Women Protection and Empowerment interventions will support at risk women and girls through provision of quality and timely lifesaving GBV Response and Prevention services in Juba, Aweil, Leer, Mayandit, Rubkona, Maban, Rotriak, Koch, Rumbek, and Panijiyar. At risk women and girls including GBV survivors will receive response services following interagency GBV case management guidelines focusing on survivor centered approach to support the healing process. IRC will provide capacity building trainings and supportive supervision to response team for provision of quality services to at risk women and girls. The interventions will strengthen the coordination among GBV service providers to improve referral mechanism during GBV case management processes. Multisectoral referral pathways will be developed and updated on regular basis. IRC will not only lead the coordination with other service providers during case management but will also ensure that the client is satisfied with the services. Regular case conferences will be conducted with relevant GBV actors involved in case management to improve the quality of the service provision maintaining confidentiality. The data will be managed and protected through GBVIMS and GBVIMS+. IRC will also share the trends and analysis of GBV cases with relevant agencies that will guide the service provision process. IRC will establish women and girls safe spaces for healing, recovery and empowerment of at risk women and girls. The activities at the safe spaces will be guided by WGSS toolkit, tailored curriculums including Women Rise and Girls Shine for PSS and life skill-based education for women and girls. All the interventions at safe spaces will be women and girls centered. The safe spaces will serve as an entry point for GBV survivors to get GBV case management services through trained case workers. To prevent GBV, IRC will engage community through multiple outreach activities including awareness raising campaigns, capacity building of community leaders and women support networks and behavioral change interventions. The behavior change interventions will include implementation of EMAP and SASA! Together curriculums. The prevention interventions will also strengthen the community protection mechanism to ensure safe referrals of GBV cases. For Risk mitigation, IRC will conduct regular safety audits engaging women and girls at the community and safe space levels. IRC will develop an action plan on the basis of safety audit findings to mitigate the identified GBV risks by women and girls including distribution of dignity kits and menstrual hygiene and management sessions. IRC will make conscious efforts to include all marginalized groups including persons with disabilities in prevention and response interventions. Activities will be conducted at an accessible place and suitable time for persons specially women and girls with disabilities. IRC will make information accessible for persons with disabilities through door to door visits and in local easy to understand languages. IRC will also link persons with disabilities with the service providers through referral pathways. Special measures will be taken to make women and girls safe spaces accessible for wheel chair users. Similarly, IRC will also ensure to allocate space for children following CP guidelines so that lactating mothers can also actively participate in the interventions. IRC will also foster an inclusive culture by raising awareness, challenging stereotypes, and promoting positive attitudes towards persons with disabilities within communities and society at large.

project_name: To reduce the excess morbidity and mortality of displaced Rohingya children and their families through integrated quality primary health care including MHPSS, Nutrition, Rehabilitation and WASH services in inclusive manner
project_objective:
"Since influx in 2017, Save the Children has been providing a quality and integrated health service and has become one of the most trusted health partners to the affected beneficiaries. SCI will deliver an inclusive, gender responsive & comprehensive healthcare services through 3 HP and 2 PHCC over the JRP period in 5 camps of Ukhiya and Teknaf to ensure equitable access to essential healthcare services for Rohingya and host communities including persons with disability and gender diverse population (LGBTQI). As per localization strategy, some health intervention will be covered by the local implementing partners PHD, CDD, Bandhu Social Welfare Society and Nari Maitree.  Project will ensure sex segregated areas/rooms and presence of sufficient female staff. Health facilities will deliver primary health care service with special focus on sexual, reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health (SRMNCAH); MHPSS; rehabilitation including need based assistive device provision and noncommunicable diseases in line with the minimum package of essential Health services (MPEHS). project_name: Mejorar el acceso a la documentación para las personas venezolanas afectadas por el desplazamiento y fortalecer la capacidad de las personas con necesidad de protección internacional (PNPI) en Venezuela
project_objective:
La intervención de protección legal (ICLA) busca que las personas afectadas por el desplazamiento en Venezuela tengan mayor capacidad de gozar de su derecho a la identidad legal. Para este objetivo, el programa de protección legal busca, a través de clínicas móviles, informar, orientar y sensibilizar a las comunidades más vulnerables y alejadas de los entes administrativos sobre los diferentes procedimientos y trámites para la obtención de actas de nacimiento y cédulas de identidad, así como sobre sus derechos y como hacer valer su derecho a la identidad legal. 

En particular, ICLA brinda orientación y asistencia legal a: i) NNA y sus representantes legales con los procedimientos de registro tardío de nacimiento; ii) NNA de 9 años o mayores y sus representantes legales para la cedulación por primera vez la cual es el prerrequisito para que puedan obtener el título de bachillerato; iii) Personas adultas que no tienen ningún documento civil o de identidad con los procedimientos de registro tardío de nacimiento/ cedulación por primera vez de persona mayor de 18 años; iv) hijos de venezolanos nacidos en el extranjero sin partida de nacimiento y en riesgo de apatridia, así como a hijos de venezolanos nacidos en el exterior que necesiten apostilla para su partida de nacimiento emitida por el otro país (en la mayoría de los casos Colombia) para poder obtener la nacionalidad venezolana.

Para los venezolanos en movilidad, el programa de protección legal también brinda información sobre migración segura. El alcance de la información y orientación brindada en esta área temática gira en torno a temas de protección legal, a saber: los diversos regímenes migratorios y de visa disponibles para los venezolanos, según su país de destino, así como información actualizada sobre los prerrequisitos y trámites a seguir para tener acceso a los mismos. El objetivo de estos servicios es aumentar el acceso de las personas en movilidad a la estadía legal, una vez que llegan a su lugar de destino previsto y así reducir los riesgos de protección que se derivan de su ausencia, como también aumentar el conocimiento de dichas personas sobre las realidades allí para que puedan tomar decisiones más informadas con respecto al viaje. 

Adicionalmente, el programa de protección legal de NRC busca fortalecer la capacidad de las personas con necesidad de protección internacional (PNPI) en Venezuela de acceder a la estadía legal y de ejercer y gozar de sus derechos: se busca brindar orientación y asistencia legal a personas con necesidad de protección internacional en la obtención de la condición de refugiado en Venezuela, así como el acceso a derechos, tales como el derecho de permanecer en el territorio venezolano, el derecho a la educación y el derecho al trabajo.

project_name: Enhancing safe and equitable access to qualitative Education in Aleppo, Dar'a, Hama, Idleb and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
TGH will directly contribute to Objectives 1, 2 & 3 for Syria through providing safe andequitable access to qualitative non-formal education (NFE) to OOSC and children at-risk of dropping out within public educational institutions (this project will be part of an Education, Protection, WASH and Shelter integrated programming under 2024/2025 HRP).
The response proposed by TGH is based on their 5-year experience in implementing ECHO, SHF and SDC funded education projects in Syria. TGH is intending to carry on its integrated approach and replicate its successes in sub-districts of Rural Damascus, Hama, Idleb, Aleppo and Dar’a. They were selected based on their level of accessibility and the severity of needs as per the 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) with all the localities being rated over 3 (66% of level 4, 34% of level 3), TGH 2023 & 2024 field assessments and coordination with municipalities SARC, DoE & other NGOs. In addition, these areas are all witnessing important returns and/or displacements movements thus increasing the level of needs. Through the proposed intervention, TGH will simultaneously address immediate needs and foster coherent services by providing/enabling rapid and sustainable access to formal and non-formal education (NFE) for the school year 2024. This will benefit 14,755 individuals (5,915 boys, 6,852 girls, 1,476 PwD, 12,009 individuals from host communities, 2,236 IDPs, 510 returnees). TGH will ensure access to education by rehabilitating schools in locations where facilities are partially destroyed. Children will be both encouraged to participate in the activities through BTL campaigns. A specific focus will be made on supporting the reintegration of OOSC, CwD, early married girls and child labour cases into the FE system. TGH will support the most needed youth in education and livelihood opportunities through TVET. In coordination with the Protection sector, TGH will provide PSS to students and teachers, campaign awareness to parents. In coordination with ERL sector and other partners, TGH will explore all the possibilities to support the economic situation of parents through livelihood opportunities in order to sustain the access and retention of children at school. The proposed intervention will include:
-Rehabilitate 13 schools, incl. gender-sensitive and disability-sensitive WASH facilities; and provide prefabricated schools; Provide the rehabilitated schools with solar power system when feasible; Repair damaged classroom furniture; Provide schools with school furniture, including winterization items such as heaters.
-Provide OOSC and children at-risk of dropping out with NFE; Provide students and teachers school based PSS; Conduct BTL campaigns; Provide students with school supplies; Provide students with hygiene items including sanitary pads for girls; along with health and hygiene campaign awareness; Provide students with winters clothes through CVA; Provide maintenance and running costs in schools; Provide cash for education given the priority to children at risk of dropping out; Provide professional development to teaching staff and education personnel; Provide teachers with teaching resources and transportation; Provide children with sup. learning materials; Provide transportation incentives for student in school and youth in TVET; Establish and support parents engagement initiatives.
All M&E activities are gathered in a MEAL workplan, monthly updated and shared to PMs to ensure the activities' completion in time and make sure the team is supported by the necessary tools that are developped with the HQ support.

project_name: Provision of  protection assistance to vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement in Syria
project_objective:
The 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) estimates that over 16.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance across Syria. Syria remains a protection crisis. Children continue to be killed, women and girls continue to fear for their safety and 7.2 million Syrians remain in displacement. The protracted conflict in has severely limited access to civil documentation, leaving a significant portion of the population undocumented or under-documented. Lack of documentation hampers freedom of movement, access to services, and increases the risk of statelessness. Housing, Land, Property (HLP) issues, particularly for women, exacerbate protection concerns. Legal assistance and awareness-raising are critical to address these challenges.
The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)’s comprehensive protection focuses on direct provision of information, counseling, and legal assistance (ICLA) to Persons Affected by the Crisis and Displacement (PACD). NRC aims to enhance knowledge and response capacity among duty-bearers, promoting the integration of ICLA with Shelter, WASH, Livelihoods, Food Security, and Education programs. NRC’s Protection programming aligns with Sector Objectives #1 and #2, aiming to improve the protection of crisis-affected populations, advocate for durable solutions, and strengthen technical capacities at national and community levels to address protection risks and needs.
Direct Assistance to PACD: NRC's direct assistance services target PACD facing legal challenges related to civil documentation, housing, land, property (HLP) rights, and access to essential services. Key priorities include issuance of basic civil documentation, catering to the most vulnerable, and preventing forced evictions. Special attention is given to female-headed households, children without proof of legal identity, and those facing HLP concerns.
Increased Knowledge and Capacity: NRC undertakes legal analysis, research, and technical assistance, providing training modules on legal identity, HLP, and employment law. Community leaders, including formal and traditional authorities, receive capacity-building interventions. Emphasis is placed on resolving HLP, employment, and labor disputes, with a commitment to protecting the rights of women, girls, and persons with disabilities.
Focus on Vulnerability and Inclusion: NRC places a gender, age, and disability inclusion lens on its protection interventions, recognizing the heightened vulnerabilities of specific groups. Advocacy is integral to NRC's activities, emphasizing that civil documentation should not be a prerequisite for receiving assistance. Tailored interventions and capacity-building efforts aim to empower communities and duty-bearers.
Target Group: NRC prioritizes IDPs, returnees, host community members, Iraqi refugees, Palestinian refugees, stateless individuals, and those at risk of statelessness. Protection activities aim to address rights to legal identity, civil documentation, HLP rights, and access to essential services. Vulnerability criteria include gender, age, disability, ethnicity, and religion.
Implementation: NRC implements protection programming directly, emphasizing the importance of house-to-house verification processes and community-supported targeting approaches for beneficiary selection. Thorough cash feasibility studies guide the decision-making process, especially concerning the provision of assistance through cash. NRC implements these interventions directly. In exceptional circumstances, when access to communities is limited, NRC collaborates with partners, respecting anonymity for security reasons.

Monitoring and Evaluation: NRC maintains a robust monitoring and evaluation framework, conducting regular reviews of awareness-raising and training materials. The organization actively contributes to Protection service mapping, ensuring accurate and up-to-date information. Ongoing reviews inform program adjustments, advocacy efforts, and preparedness measures.

project_objective:
The proposed NRC’s Shelter interventions for 2024 is continued to support the people affected by conflict, natural disaster and displacement in emergency context and static as long-term support for the IDPs, returnees and host community to return, resettle and reintegrate with host community. The interventions are designed to address the emergency shelter / NFIs needs through rapid response mechanism (RRT) and emergency response and   contribute to improve people’s protection and durable solutions through NRC static shelter response. 

The proposed shelter interventions are to provide access to basic shelter services in underserved and hard to reach locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GVB and durable access to shelter among 125,000 IDPs, Returnees and host communities in South Sudan. NRC’s Shelter interventions will be integrated and implemented in close coordination with NRC’s other core competencies of WASH, Education, Livelihood and Food security, ICLA and protection programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to uplift people’s lives and contributing to South Sudan 2024 HRP  and Shelter Cluster objectives.

The project aims to provide Survival Kits /Emergency shelter/Non-Food items both in-kind and in cash modalities to the most vulnerable persons, newly displaced/host communities, and returnees. The project will focus on the lifesaving shelter/NFIs needs, as identified through assessment to protect the affected displaced people from harsh weather conditions and protection risks targeting all states of South Sudan. Moreover, the project will provide static as long-term and durable shelter solutions to the IDPs, returnees and host communities who wanted to return, resettle, or reintegrate with communities. The first line intervention will be implemented through mobile response as well as using its static teams based in Kajo Keji, Juba, Koch, Mayom, Leer, Bor, Duk, Twic East, Akobo, Aweil, Wau and Alek. However, the major focus areas will be in Jonglei, Unity, Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Central, Western and Eastern Equatoria states. 

Cash programming will also be considered in areas where markets are fully or semi-functional and shelter/NFI items are available and accessible by the community. When blanket targeting is not applicable, the intervention will target mainly lactating and pregnant women, households with malnourished children, and households with members who have certain health complications. Besides unaccompanied children, unaccompanied elderly and persons with no community linkages will also be targeted.

The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities for 2024 HRP's. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 22 days for full-fledged delivery of NFIs and emergency shelters and other activities per location.

project_name: Provision of quality WASH services for vulnerable communities living in Akobo, Nyirol, and Abyei.

project_name: Cash Assistances for the most Vulnerable in Aleppo, Hama and Latakia
project_objective:
This intervention is in line with Sector Objective 2: Most vulnerable HHs near markets receive repeated MPC and are able to prioritize a variety of basic needs, reducing reliance on negative coping strategies over time. The goal is to empower these households to address various essential needs, thereby reducing their reliance on negative coping mechanisms . The project centers on distributing regular cash assistance to identified most vulnerable households, with key focusing on the percentage of households assisted and the percentage reporting improved living conditions due to this assistance.

Leveraging TDH's prior experience in providing multipurpose cash assistance in these areas, the intervention will be targeting 6,000 HH across Latakia, Aleppo, and Hama (with 2,000 HH in each area) through 8 cycles each cycle is aligned with the transfer value by CWG (1,430,000 SP as per the latest update) for each HH, the project aims to swiftly and effectively assist those facing hardships. This multipurpose cash aid allows households the flexibility to prioritize urgent needs such as food, shelter, healthcare, and other vital services. TDH is regularly attending CWG meetings to update on the values and prioritizations' of the MPCA.

Implementation strategy revolves around a thorough process to identify and reach the most vulnerable households, ensuring that assistance reaches those who need it most, and are situated near vital marketplaces. This careful selection process guarantees impactful and efficient aid distribution.

Furthermore, the project adheres to CWG guidelines, meticulously assessing local market functionality and accessibility in the target areas. This assessment evaluates market infrastructure, supply chains, price stability, and product diversity to ensure that beneficiaries can utilize their cash assistance effectively. 

Protection Risk Analysis:
PR1: Beneficiaries and project staff may face physical safety risks due to conflict, violence, or insecurity in the targeted areas.
M2: TDH have a Security officer who regularly conduct security assessments and implement measures to ensure the safety of beneficiaries and staff, establishing secure distribution points, and coordinating closely with local authorities and security actors. Provide training on personal safety and security protocols./PR2:  Women and girls may be at heightened risk of GBV, including domestic violence, sexual exploitation, and harassment, especially in contexts of displacement and instability/ M2: TDH integrate prevention and response measures into the program activities, such as providing gender-sensitive information sessions, establishing safe spaces for women and girls, and training staff on GBV identification and referral protocols./ PR3: Collecting and storing beneficiary data may pose risks to privacy and confidentiality, including unauthorized access, misuse, or data breaches. M3: TDH always obtain informed consent from beneficiaries before collecting personal data and ensure compliance with relevant data protection laws and regulations, also, TDH ensure data privacy by collecting minimum beneficiaries information during assessments.

project_name: Améliorer la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelles ainsi que l’autonomie alimentaire des ménages les plus vulnérables dans les provinces du Lac, du Logone Oriental, du Ouaddaï et du Sila.
project_objective:
Ce projet souhaite répondre à l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations du Lac, de l’Est et du Logone Oriental. Il est composé de deux axes : les transferts monétaires non restrictifs et le soutien aux Activités Génératrices de Revenus (AGR).  

Au Lac, SI soutiendra les ménages avec de faible score de consommation alimentaire avec des transferts monétaires non restrictifs (3 rounds sur 3 mois). Cela permettra de répondre aux besoins alimentaires immédiats des ménages. Des farines enrichies seront aussi distribuées aux ménages avec un ou des cas de malnutrition. Pour compléter cette action et sortir les ménages de la dépendance à l’assistance alimentaire, SI soutiendra au Lac et dans l’Est des AGR agricoles (activités vivrières, de maraichères, de transformation, petit commerce alimentaire, etc.) et des AGR liées à l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement dans le Logone Oriental, qui seront identifiées selon les préférences des ménages. Ainsi, des groupements seront équipés, conseillés et accompagnés techniquement pour la conduite de leurs activités. Dans le cas des AGR de transformation notamment, les revenus générés permettront aux ménages de s’acheter d’autres biens/vivres essentiels. Dans les camps à l’Est, ces groupements seront articulés avec les Comité de Gestion des Points d’Eau afin de pouvoir pérenniser les infrastructures construites. De plus, des Associations Villageoises d’Epargne et de Crédit seront créées et soutenues, renforçant ainsi les moyens d’existence et l’autonomie des bénéficiaires. Dans la province du Logone Oriental, ces AGR seront liées à la mise en œuvre d’un projet accès sur l’eau et l’assainissement.

project_name: Support self-reliance of affected households ,protecting the productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities.
project_objective:
This program aims to support the resilience of the conflict-affected people in northwest Syria, particularly in Idleb and Aleppo governorates. Shafak's proposed action is designed to contribute to supporting the transition to the early recovery phase, as it helps the targeted communities with long-term assistance activities, programs that focus on building/restoring the communities' infrastructure, local economic empowerment, and initiatives that ensure engagement and participation of the community in recovering from the protracted crisis. This program will achieve its objectives by supporting Men, Women, and PWDs through the following: 
a)	Vocational Training: 400  affected households’ members are supported through Vocational Training activity to improve their employability opportunities and skills building.
b)	 On-job Training: 100 Vulnerable Households who received Vocational training will be enrolled in a 3-month training program at workshops/ trainers. 
c)	Entrepreneurship training: 100 Vulnerable Households who received Vocational training for one month of training program at workshops/ trainers.
d)	Life skills for success Training: 200 Vulnerable Households who received  VT and Entrepreneurship training for a one-month training program.
e)	Basic Literacy and numeracy training: approximately 50 vulnerable individuals among those who attended the above training will be enrolled for two months of training.
f)	Establishing or expanding Small-Micro Enterprises: 500.  Through business grants and Business development skills training (BDS).  The BDS will be for 3-5 Days, and the cash grants will range from 750-1200 USD. The targeted beneficiaries will be from two pathways: those who are not skilled and have passed the different above-mentioned training programs and the other path from those who already have existing businesses that need development or who have skills and need to restart their businesses. 
g)	Temporary Employment: 1200  vulnerable HHs within the targeted communities are supported through temporary income generation opportunities through Cash for Work activities. Cash-for-Work activities will enable the provision of 1200 temporary labor opportunities focusing on the rehabilitation of community-identified projects and referral to market approach for 1-3 Months.  
h)	 Financial Services: Facilitating the Establishment of 20 Village Savings Loaning Associations (VSLAs) to improve access to financial services. An estimated 20 Savings and Loan Groups, each consisting of approximately 10-15 members, will be facilitated to establish. 
i)	Graduation Approach: 100 HHs. Support the self-reliance of vulnerable households from those supported with Cash for food. The Graduation approach will also include market-facing skills, transfer of productive assets, financial services through VSLA, mentoring, and Coaching, and a Referral mechanism.
j)	Rehabilitating the local economic, public, and social infrastructure (20 Projects) through linking with the Cash-for-Work activity or through service providers. Each project cost will be about 25000 USD. The projects include constructing small markets in the IDP camps to enhance access to the market and creating IGAs within the camp.
k)	Supporting local community and social cohesion initiatives: Through forming a community engagement team representing the different segments in the community.

Founded in 1945, CARE works collaboratively through its 14 members to end poverty. CARE has been working in Mozambique since 1984, delivering lifesaving assistance, building resilience and disaster management capacities, and empowering girls and women from vulnerable communities. CARE has offices in Maputo, Pemba, Nacala, and Maxixe, and works across the country through partnerships with civil society organizations. 

Mozambique is Africa’s most vulnerable country to climate change, a country which previously recorded cyclones and other climate shocks over a period of years, changing weather cyclones have seen Mozambique exposed to weather events such as cyclones, tropical storms, floods, and drought on a yearly basis. Between 2019 and the first quarter of 2023, the south-eastern African country has registered 2 tropical storms and 5 cyclones, with the most recent being that of Cyclone Freddy – an exceptionally long-lived, powerful, and deadly storm that traversed the southern Indian Ocean for more than five weeks in February and March 2023. Freddy is both the longest-lasting and highest-ACE-producing tropical cyclone ever recorded worldwide, additionally it is the third-deadliest tropical cyclone in the Southern Hemisphere, only behind 2019’s Cyclone Idai which also hit Mozambique. One of the provinces affected by cyclones and climate shocks in recent years is the northernmost province – Cabo Delgado. In addition to the climate shocks, Cabo Delgado has been the backdrop of armed conflict since 2017, and as a major consequence, more than 1.5 million people have been displaced and a humanitarian crisis erupted.
