project_name: People affected by disasters in Sudan have improved access to safe water, appropriate sanitation facilities and increased durability of targeted positive hygiene behaviours
project_objective:
The project will aim to ensure 130,593 people affected by conflict, flooding, drought, and waterborne diseases have dignified and sustainable, meaningful access to sufficient safe water, appropriate sanitation facilities, and a healthier environment. The same interventions will aim to ensure increased durability of targeted positive hygiene behaviours.
The project interventions will target White Nile, Al-Jazira, Gedaref, South Kordofan, and Sennar states through an integrated approach focusing on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and vulnerable host communities in and out of camp or gathering sites. The project will focus on life-saving interventions in newly displaced populations, closely coordinated with the rapid response mechanism (RRM) to ensure optimal utilisation of resources. Using a strong presence in the target areas, NRC will aim to restore access to basic WASH services, with markets guiding the design of interventions. In water supply, the planned interventions will improve access to equitable, sustainable, and affordable safe water with the aim of at least 15 litres per person per day (lpd) for drinking and domestic purposes. This will be through quick-fix rehabilitation of existing water systems based on a rapid technical assessment. This will be through the repair of damaged water pumping stations and water treatment chemicals like coagulants (for surface water sources) and chlorine. The rehabilitation will also entail the repair of damaged water distribution networks and water points or the replacement of solar panels in systems using renewable energy. In locations served by shallow wells equipped with handpumps like South Kordofan and Gedaref, the NRC WASH team will provide fast-moving spare parts to trained technicians to ensure their continued functionality during the crisis. To ensure water quality, household water treatment and safe storage (HWTSS) will be prioritised by providing water purification and treatment tablets for water systems without centralized chlorination and ensuring adequate water collection and storage containers. Residual chlorine will be monitored in collaboration with the government line ministries to ensure a minimum of 0.2 to 0.5 mg/l at the point of use. Land tenure for water supply infrastructure, in close collaboration with ICLA, will be prioritized to minimise service disruptions and disputes. Gender and protection assessments will inform the locations of water points to mitigate risks associated with water collection and ensure meaningful access for vulnerable or marginalised individuals.
To ensure an environment free of human excreta, which is essential for people’s dignity, safety, health, and well-being,  NRC, in the first phase of an emergency, due to land tenure and space availability, will aim to rehabilitate existing latrines to restore them to functionality; this could be through infrastructure improvement or desludging. Proper disposal and transport of the excreta will be ensured at designated sites. The emergency latrines will be constructed in consultation with the government to ensure compliance and will be equipped with handwashing stations. NRC will use participatory approaches that aim to adopt positive behaviour change by the target population. The focus will include raising awareness about handwashing with soap, sand, or ash at critical times. NRC will undertake mass hygiene campaigns during emergencies like an outbreak of diseases and then focus on behaviour change. Various communication channels will be explored, including social media, to ensure wider reach and coverage. The campaigns will be coupled with the provision of hygiene-related NFIs after thorough market surveys, with the option of market-based programming. Menstrual hygiene management (MHM) will form a key component of the hygiene promotion targeting adolescent girls to address barriers related to hygiene, access, and disposable.

This will be achieved by providing Cash-Based Transfers (CBT) to address the food needs of vulnerable communities during the lean season and providing timely and appropriate complementary vegetable, crop and fishing kits coupled with training on improved climate-resilient agronomic and fishing practices. In line with the South Sudan FSL cluster HRP objectives and priorities, NPA will support vulnerable populations in IPC 4 and 5 locations and some IPC 3 locations. Specifically, NPA will target Canal/Pigi, Fangak and Bor South Counties of Jonglei State; Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre, Cueibet, Yirol East, Yirol West, Wulu and Awerial Counties of Lakes State; Terekeka County of Central Equatoria State and Kapoeta North and Budi Counties of Eastern Equatoria State. 
NPA seeks to support 111,148 HHs (569,866 individuals) by providing timely and appropriate complementary vegetable, crop and fishing kits. Some kits will be provided by FAO (core pipeline) and NPA partnership projects, while others will be procured and distributed directly by NPA to enhance food production. NPA will build the capacity of the HHs supported with the kits through training on group cohesion and group dynamics, improved climate-resilient agronomic and fishing practices, post-harvest processing, value addition and marketing. A Training of Trainers (ToT) approach will be utilized whereby lead farmers and Lead fisher folk will be trained by NPA. Through farmer field schools, they will share their knowledge and skills with other farmers and fisher folk in their communities. The kits provided through this project and the knowledge shared through the training are expected to improve the agricultural and fishing practices of the target households, thereby contributing to food security and enhancing climate-resilient sustainable food production. 
CBT interventions will target 3,000 HHs (18,000 individuals) in Rumbek East, Awerial, Cuiebet, Wulu, Yirol East and Yirol West Counties in Lakes State and 400 HHs (2,400 individuals) in Fangak, Canal / Pigi and Bor South Counties in Jonglei State, to improve access and consumption of diversified food. The planned interventions are aligned with the FSL cluster objectives 1 and 2. They will provide emergency assistance and livelihood support to save lives and avert the total collapse of livelihoods in the target counties. NPA will integrate humanitarian, development-oriented and conflict-sensitivity activities in this project to enhance the resilience of vulnerable populations in line with the Triple Nexus. Therefore, 2,125 vulnerable households will be supported with small-scale cash grants to establish Income Generating Activities. The target HHs will be sensitized to set VSLAs for easy loan access and enhanced saving skills among the VSLA group members. The IGAs will contribute to increasing and diversifying income and livelihood opportunities while building the resilience of the target households and strengthening market functionality. 
NPA will employ a community-based beneficiary selection approach, which will entail establishing Project Management Committees (PMCs) to lead the targeting of eligible beneficiaries based on the beneficiary selection criteria and targeting guidelines. Vulnerable households facing severe food insecurity, including female-headed households, child-headed households, people living with disabilities, chronically ill-headed households and the elderly, will be targeted in this project. NPA will ensure meaningful engagement of the target communities throughout the project life-cycle through holding regular meetings with the PMCs and community members and conducting Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to get their feedback on the project. NPA will ensure that the feedback is incorporated into the implementation of this project and the design of future projects.

project_name: Renforcement des soins de santé primaires et nutritionnels, de santé sexuelle et reproductive et de PEC des survivant.e.s de violences basées sur le genre pour les populations hôtes et déplacées internes affectées par les crises humanitaires persistantes dans la région de Tahoua
project_objective:
Ce projet  vise à réduire les situations de vulnérabilité, augmenter et maintenir la dignité humaine ainsi que sauver les vies dans les communautés touchées par des crises humanitaires à travers la sensibilisation, le dépistage, la Prise En Charge (PEC) et le référencement améliorés des cas de malnutrition et Violences Basées sur le Genre (VBG), ainsi que des besoins en Soins de Santé Primaire (SSP) et Santé et Droits Sexuels et Reproductifs (SDSR) au niveau institutionnel et communautaire dans la région de Tahoua (départements de Konni, Bagaroua, Madaoua). 
Le projet cible 47 515 (Santé: 28218; Nut :281 et Protection:19016) incluant 24290 femmes et 23225 hommes . Une attention particulière sera accordée aux personnes vulnérables notamment les femmes, les adolescent.e.s, les jeunes enfants ainsi que les personnes vivant avec un handicap et les personnes ayant des SOGIESC divers qui représentent 4% du total des bénéficiaires directs. 
Le projet se base sur l’hypothèse que les différentes crises en cours dans la zone d’intervention vont se poursuivre voire empirer dans les prochains mois comme le prévoit le HNO 2023 pour le Niger. L’expérience de MdM BE au Niger depuis 2014 révèle que le manque d’accès physique et économique, les défaillances des systèmes de santé ainsi qu’une faible littératie en santé des populations locales et des acteurs communautaires sont les principales barrières d’accès aux soins pour les populations. 
MdM BE propose de rétablir un accès d’urgence aux SSP d’urgence, à la PEC nutritionnelle, à la SDSR, à la PEC des VBG ainsi que l’appui financier, matériel et technique des institutions de santé fragilisées par la crise. Le projet permettra également aux communautés éloignées d’accéder à des services de santé adaptés selon les besoins différenciés des femmes, adolescent.e.s et des hommes. Cela à travers des cliniques mobiles, des stratégies avancées ainsi que la formation et la sensibilisation des acteur.rice.s communautaires afin d’améliorer la prestation de services de santé offerts. Le manque de personnel qualifié ou sa grande mobilité liée aux conditions sécuritaires ou salariales a une répercussion sur la qualité des soins. Un accent sera donc mis sur la disponibilité d’un personnel qualifié en charge du suivi des urgences vitales et la formation ou recyclage du personnel de santé et agents à base communautaire sur le dépistage, la PEC et le traitement afin d’améliorer la qualité de l’offre de soins. Le projet appuiera également à rendre plus performant le système des références et contre références des cas. Le projet visera également à accroître la capacité des institutions appuyées à fournir des services de SDSR et de PEC des VBG accessibles, confidentiels et centrés sur les patient.e.s notamment les personnes marginalisées. Les services de SDSR seront améliorés et centrés sur la femme grâce au renforcement des capacités du personnel de santé sur les thématiques clés de la SDSR, des soins obstétricaux et néonataux d’urgence, du dispositif minimum d’urgence et de la surveillance de décès maternel et périnatal y compris la riposte (SDMPR). Enfin, un plaidoyer à différents niveaux (local, régional et national) sera effectué pour renforcer l’application des cadres légaux en matière d’avortement et appuyer la vulgarisation du protocole de Maputo et des lois. Par ailleurs, MdM BE veillera à prendre en compte les besoins spécifiques des populations bénéficiaires sans aucune distinction, en mettant l’accent sur les aspects liés au genre et aux vulnérabilités de chaque personne. L'influence du genre sur le domaine de la santé est significative et se manifeste par des disparités de santé entre les sexes, des différences dans l'accès aux soins de santé, des besoins de santé spécifiques liés au genre et des facteurs sociaux et culturels qui jouent un rôle clé dans la santé des individus. MdM BE plaidera pour l’autonomie psychologique, corporelle et sexuelle dans ses actions en promouvant les droits et la SDSR.

project_name: Equitable and Dignified Access to life-saving assistance for Sudan Crisis effected communities in Renk
project_objective:
The proposed intervention will contribute to the HRP 2023 Strategic Objectives:1) Vulnerable crises-affected people have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable, safe, and dignified access to life-saving assistance to meet their needs, 2) Vulnerable crises-affected people’s protection risks are mitigated as humanitarians uphold a commitment to the centrality of protection in humanitarian action informed by communities’ priorities. The main objective of the proposed intervention will contribute to the Protection Cluster's objective, to ensure the mobile or static provision of critical protection assistance and services, including specialized response services, tailored to the specific needs, considering age, gender, and disability.  To achieve this, the proposed intervention has the following specific objectives:1) To undertake effective and regular protection monitoring in targeted areas for timely and robust humanitarian and protection decisions, influence, and actions. 2) To strengthen community-based protection mechanisms for risk reduction and promotion of local peace and security for women and youths;3) To increase access to safe and dignified protection and GVB emergency services for crisis-affected populations, especially the most vulnerable groups including PWDs and GBV survivors. 
This project will support 5110 conflict-affected people from Returnees and Host communities in Renk, Upper Nile State by strengthening community-based protection mechanisms that prevent, mitigate, and respond to protection issues and providing specialized assistance to people with specific protection needs. Oxfam will establish three Information and Protection desks to share protection messages, information about the available services, and guidance and support to Sudan crisis-affected communities in Renk. The three information desks will support the identification and referral process to the most vulnerable protection cases. Each of these will serve as a hub for the local community to provide protection services including services mapping pathway sheets and awareness-raising messages. The project will prioritize community participation and ownership and will strengthen partnerships with other key stakeholders. The project will address the immediate protection needs of highly vulnerable people by identifying community-level protection risks and referring people with needs, including women, children, the elderly, and people living with disabilities. Oxfam will ensure that safe referral mechanisms are in place, including specialized support for survivors or those at risk of gender-based violence. 
The project will include a protection cash assistance component for persons facing urgent protection risks or victims of indiscriminate conflict. Oxfam will closely coordinate with the case management actors, Protection and other key stakeholders to ensure that the entire Cash for Protection process including identifications, referrals, and provisions of operations is safe, accountable, and inclusive.
Furthermore, Community-Based Protection Networks (CBPNs) will be established and strengthened. This effort will consider age, gender, and diversity groups of displaced and conflict-affected communities, to address and mitigate protection concerns, promote referral mechanisms, lead protection initiatives, and enhance community self-protection mechanisms. Furthermore, it will promote the acknowledgement of the need to monitor protection issues and advocate for it. The intervention will address this through conducting regular protection monitoring aiming to assess the pattern of abuse or repeated threats and their impact on vulnerable groups and the findings will be shared externally with the wider humanitarian community considering Safe Programming principles.

project_name: Promotion of access to safe water, improved sanitation and hygiene services to prevent high prevalence of Malnutrition in Awerial , Yirol East, Twic East and Ayod.
project_objective:
From the time of attainment of independence in July 2011, South Sudan has be having a protracted conflict that has put its entire population from extreme to catastrophic need to a minimum essential humanitarian services.  The two targeted states have experienced decades of conflict both as the frontline in the national level conflict between the government and opposition as well as the inter-communal conflict over resources and rivalry amongst ethnic groups. Protracted conflict, corrupted with endemic natural shocks, have triggered a humanitarian crisis that has severely damaged WASH, FSL and Nutrition infrastructure, services and practices. 
According to HNO 2023 (Inter-sectoral analysis), the limited access to WASH infrastructure coverage alone, such as water points and latrines, poses multisectoral impacts. Poor access to WASH services and goods, combined with high levels of food insecurity, has a detrimental impact on the health of the most vulnerable people, as evidenced by the high prevalence of malnutrition in the country. At the national level, the GAM prevalence for children between 0 and 59 months is at 16 per cent, while SAM was at 5.9 per cent according to the preliminary FSNMS and 2022 SMART surveys. The presence of water-borne diseases such as diarrhoea in children under age 5 is also indicative of poor WASH conditions. The WASH situation in certain locations is projected to worsen before the end of 6 months due to heavy flooding, which has caused further disruption to livelihoods, displacement and damage to WASH infrastructure while limiting humanitarian access. Limited sustainability of the WASH response in the IDP sites due to funding shortage will increase the likelihood of waterborne disease and outbreaks, including Hepatitis E, AWD and cholera. 
The project will complement the newly secured 3 years German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) funding for implementation of Integrated WASH, Food Security and Nutrition services to conflict and disaster-affected persons in the selected priority Counties in Lakes and Jonglei States. The strategy of integrating WASH in Nutrition is to tackle some of the key acute malnutrition drivers, as poor hygiene and access to clean water, limited food availability knowledge. 
This project will mainly target SAM/caretakers at nutrition sites, nutrition facilities with poor WASH conditions and communities with high GAM and no access to safe water and all work will be done in line with the WaSH Cluster strategy in close coordination with line ministries, WASH Cluster and international guidelines for implementing WaSH. The project has 5 Main Strategic Objectives (SOs); CLWSH/SO1) Contribute to reducing prevalence of malnutrition; CLWSH/SO2) Contribute to reducing WASH related morbidity and mortality; CLWSH/SO3) Provide access to basic WASH services in underserved locations affected by disaster; CLWSH/SO4) Disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility; CLWSH/SO5) Provide durable access to services in long-term IDP sites and communities chronically affected by disaster. The following activities will be carried; (Re)Construction of flood resilient water points with hand pumps and motorized systems; Water quality analysis, Training of Community hand pump mechanics, Training of Water Management Committees, (Re)construction of flood resilient latrines, Hygiene promotion, Distribution of WASH NFIs distribution, solid and liquid waste management at Health facilities and communities, and incorporation of PSEA and GBV into Protection mainstreaming training.
Target Population = 45,455
Yirol East = 12,724
Awerial = 13,728
Twic East = 3,119
Ayod = 15,884

project_name: Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents
project_objective:
Sudan is among the top four countries globally with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) estimated at 13.6 percent. Following the conflict in May 2023, the acute malnutrition People in Need (PIN) increased by over 13% from 4.0 M in January to over 4.5M in May.  The nutrition situation is projected to continue worsening in 2024 aggravated by the conflict, deterioration in food security, health and WASH services and the continuing displacement. As a result, the 2024 PIN is estimated to increase by between 10% and 30% in non-IDP and frontline localities respectively; with an overall additional 4.1% increase from 2023 PIN levels reaching over 4.7M in 2024, the highest PIN ever estimated in Sudan. 

 About, 76% acutely malnourished under-five children, pregnant and Lactating women in host and IDP settings live in 103 localities (54% of the total localities in Sudan). These localities are most affected, classified with severity scale 3-5 for WASH, Health, and Food Security; above national average acute malnutrition PIN and very high GAM prevalence of 15% and above- the WHO emergency threshold.  Micronutrient malnutrition among children is also very high with 48% of under-five children suffering from anaemia most of which is due to iron deficiency.  Minimum dietary diversity among under-five is one of the lowest trailing at 25% which is projected have deteriorated further following the ongoing massive displacement that has disrupted feeding and caring practices.  
The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality lifesaving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services  that includes; Preventive nutrition interventions focusing on  Maternal and Young child Nutrition (MYCN) & Infant and young child feeding practices, detection, referral and treatment of severe acute malnutrition  with and without medical complications as well as supplementation of moderate acute malnutrition among under-fives, Pregnant and lactating women and girls , Management of Small and Nutritionally at risk infants under-six months and their mothers (MAMI) and Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP).The action will implemented in South Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile, River Nile and Al Gezira states in which 25 localities with severity scale 3-5 will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 323,298beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (71,287boys, 87,129girls, 163,233 women, 1,649 men. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash based interventions in one prioritized location in SK  to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied. Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely delivery of core nutrition supplies.

project_name: Provision of lifesaving GBV prevention and response Services to crisis -affected populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
GBV is the biggest protection concern in South Sudan. Exacerbated by a variety of factors including armed conflict, inter-communal fighting, climate change and forced displacement 2.7 million people will be in people need of GBV interventions in 2024. Of these, 546,000 people will be targeted by GBV prevention, mitigation, and response interventions. The severity of protection needs for 2024 is very critical in 25 localities with severity classification levels 4 across 10 states and 3 administrative areas in South Sudan. Among the targeted people will be IDPs, returnees and host communities. UNFPA will ensure inclusion of gender, disability, and age in the identification of beneficiaries. The people with disability will be part of the planning, implementation, and monitoring. UNFPA will establish a special mechanism for the involvement of people with disabilities in all levels of the project.  
UNFPA and its implementing partner plan to reach 114,051 (women 69571, men 5703, boys 11,405, girls 25,091 and PWD 2,281) vulnerable people including returnees, people with disabilities and poor host communities with lifesaving and specialized GBV services across the country through GBV prevention interventions engaging men and boys through Accountable Practice (EMAP); Start, Awareness, Support, Action (SASA), and Community Cares Program. The planed interventions will also include economic empowerment, livelihood support, and awareness sessions and sensitization on PSEA. GBV risk mitigation activities will include integrating GBV actions into other sectorial response, conducting multisectoral safety audits, distributing fuel-efficient stoves, distribution of dignity kits and delivering cash assistance to vulnerable women and girls.  
Under the GBV response the priority interventions will include GBV case management service, psychosocial support, safety and security services, legal assistance, provision of services in safe houses, and establishing / strengthening Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) and GBV referral pathways. The livelihood and economic support in the Women and Girls Friendly Space will also act as an entry point for women and girls to receive more psychosocial support and other empowerment activities. On the other hand, some of these activities will be introduced as income-generating activities to allow women and girls to earn some income to meet their basic needs and referrals for livelihood support with other program supporting women and girls. 
UNFPA will organize regular coordination meetings among key stakeholders, including government agencies, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and local communities. These meetings can serve as a platform for sharing information, aligning strategies, and fostering collaboration to ensure a more coherent and comprehensive response to health crises. Through the proposed activities UNFPA will ensure continuity of critical services in targeted areas to ensure that GBV programs are maintained considering the current economic crisis and its impact on those who were already in need of humanitarian assistance. The project will also support strengthening capacity building on GBV through training of the GBV partners and non-GBV humanitarian actors ((Linked to the HRP Strategic Objective 2)
UNFPA will procure and distribute Dignity Kits (DK) to women and girls of reproductive age to enhance their Dignity and hygiene as well as use DK programming as an entry point to provide women and girls with information on GBV prevention, and GBV service availability including information and services on Sexual Reproductive Health.

project_name: WASH Integrated Humanitarian Lifesaving Response for armed conflict, epidemics and natural disasters affected population.
project_objective:
UNICEF’s WASH humanitarian response will focus on the provision of and sustaining access to lifesaving gender responsive basic level water supply, adequate & equitable sanitation facilities and promoting personal and environmental hygiene for 5 million most vulnerable people affected by the massive wide scale armed conflicts, WASH related epidemics with focus on cholera response, and natural disasters, mainly floods and drought. The project geographic focus will be Khartoum, North, South, East, West and Central Darfur, South, West and North Kordofan, Blue Nile, White Nile, Sennar, Geziara, Kassala, Gedarif, Red Sea, River Nile and Northern States.
UNICEF’s WASH humanitarian response will focus on:
•	Provision of and sustaining access to lifesaving basic level water supply for 4.5 million affected population.
•	Provision of and sustaining access to adequate emergency sanitation facilities for 270,000 affected population.
•	Promoting personal and environmental hygiene for 4.5 million affected population.
•	Distribution of critical hygiene promotion supplies for 450,000 affected population
•	Providing 75 schools and 75 health/nutrition institutions with adequate basic WASH facilities
•	Building communities' resilience to WASH related recurrent shocks with emphasis on community empowerment of women, girls, young people and people with disability. 

The following indicators will be used to monitor the progress:
• # people accessing a sufficient quantity of safe water for drinking and domestic need (target: 4.5 million)
• # people in humanitarian situations accessing appropriate sanitation facilities and living in environments free of open defecation (target: 270,000).
• # people reached with hand-washing behavior-change programmes (target: 4.5 million).
• # people reached with critical WASH supplies (target: 450,000).
• # health centers with access to basic WASH service (target 75).
• # schools with access to basic WASH service (target: 75)

Main Targeted Interventions: 
Deliver coordinated/integrated gender-responsive lifesaving domestic WASH services for crises and epidemics affected and rural unserved population as follows:
Basic Water Supply:
-Water disinfection, operation and maintenance and water trucking support
-Rehabilitation and constructing of gender responsive basic water facilities
-Promotion of WASH services sustainability through Community management with focus on women/youth engagement.

Basic Sanitation and Hygiene:
-Construction/rehabilitation of gender responsive (separated, locked and nearby) emergency latrines.
-Desludging IDPs settlement/gathering sites communal and shared latrines.
-Conducting effective hygiene promotion interventions with focus on handwashing with soap and cholera prevention
-Distribution of hygiene promotion supplies, mainly soap, jerricans, hygiene kits and MHM supplies.
-Supporting solid waste management interventions.

WASH In Institutions:
-Construction/rehabilitation of gender responsive and disabled friendly WASH basic services for schools, Health/nutrition facilities and child friendly spaces.
-Conducting hygiene promotion interventions with focus on handwashing with soap, cholera prevention and MHM.

WASH Enabling Environment:
-Maintain and support active sectoral/intersectoral humanitarian coordination forums national and state levels
-Strengthening WASH IMS/monitoring systems in terms of HR capacity and input-process-output stages.
-Invest on WASH sector partners capacity building to overcome the staff high turn-over rates.

project_name: Provision of life-saving and sustainable Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) holistic services for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and returnees in sites and host communities along Northern Mozambique, Cabo Delgado
project_objective: IOM’s will ensure the provision of comprehensive WASH services in sites and sites-like settings for IDPs in Cabo Delgado building upon its multi-sectoral expertise approach. Solutions will aim for a holistic approach including safe access to water, sustainable sanitation and hygiene promotion. The total target will be of 54000 persons

project_name: Improving access to Protection/MHPSS services, referrals and direct assistance for displaced, host, and returnee communities, including vulnerable individuals, GBV survivors, people at risk of violence, and child survivors of violence in sites and urban areas
project_objective:
Building on its protection by presence approach, integrated Protection-MHPSS strategy, solid coverage of several worst-affected districts and strong linkages to CCCM, Shelter/NFI, WASH and Health sectors, IOM will work towards improving the provision of and access to services for displaced, host, and returnee communities in sites and urban areas in Cabo Delgado and Nampula. With the modality of direct implementation, IOM will provide protection and MHPSS services to address protection risks and needs. 

Finally, the project will focus on strengthening the protection environment through data and knowledge generation that can inform the advocacy efforts of the cluster. Also, IOM will organize protection mainstreaming activities for non-protection IOM programmes to enhance safe and dignified service provision to the most affected communities. These efforts will cover Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa Provinces.

project_name: DTM Northern Mozambique: A Data-Driven Approach to Addressing Protracted Displacement and Humanitarian Needs
project_objective: This project will complement ongoing efforts by IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support partners with data for Northern Mozambique Humanitarian, Development and Peacebuilding (HDP) approaches aimed at monitoring displacement, reducing overall vulnerabilities, root causes of fragility, strengthen risk management capacities and respond to critical needs.

project_name: Provision of immediate life-saving NFI assistance and shelter solutions for emergency and early-recovery support to population affected by conflict and climate disasters in Northern Mozambique
project_objective: IOM proposes to support migrants, displaced persons and communities affected by conflict and climate disasters in accordance with humanitarian principles through shelter solutions that include the construction, upgrade or retrofit of shelters and the immediate shelter NFI assistance for the most vulnerable families, while using a people-centered approach and increasing local capacity and knowledge in BBB.

project_name: Protección de los niños, niñas y adolescentes en riesgo o afectados por movilidad humana y violencia, brindando orientación y atención individual, familiar y comunitaria.
project_objective:
De acuerdo con el estudio elaborado por ICEFI – Instituto Centroamericano de Estudios Fiscales, indica que, en Guatemala, siete de cada 10 niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA) viven en hogares en situación de pobreza.  Del Observatorio de Derechos de la Niñez, las principales vías por las cuales se ocasiona una muerte violenta a las y los NNA en el país, siguen siendo cinco, arma de fuego, ahorcadura, arma blanca, estrangulamiento y desmembramiento. Durante los primeros siete meses del 2023, 75 Niñas y Adolescentes mujeres habían sido asesinadas y 230 Niños y Adolescentes hombres. La principal causa de muerte violenta en adolescentes hombres es por arma de fuego. La tendencia actual en el país revela que una o un NNA es asesinado cada dos días.
En el informe del Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia de UNICEF, se presentan que el 26% de los niños y niñas en la primera infancia de 24 a 59 meses, edad crucial para el desarrollo afectivo y cognitivo, recibieron atención afectiva de parte de los y las cuidadoras que incluye actividades como jugar, leer cuentos y una gama de actividades sensoriales que fortalece el vínculo afectivo entre cuidadores/as y los niños y niñas. 
Según el Observatorio de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva, entre enero a octubre de 2023, Guatemala y Huehuetenango reporta 6,016 y 6,630 casos de embarazos de niñas de 10 a 19 años, respectivamente. 
El IRC comenzó a brindar respuesta a la creciente crisis humanitaria en Guatemala en el 2018. En los últimos cuatro años, el IRC ha alcanzado a más de 213,370 personas a través de programas de respuesta humanitaria; incluyendo intervenciones de educación basadas en evidencia, servicios de respuesta a violencia basada en género y de protección de niñez, asistencia en efectivo para familias en crisis, asistencia legal y acceso a información confiable. El IRC sirve a personas y familias que han sido desplazadas internamente, solicitantes de asilo, retornados, refugiados, y a sobrevivientes de violencia de género; especialmente mujeres, niñas y adolescentes. Desde el programa de protección de niñez y adolescencia, IRC interviene en la prevención y la respuesta a la explotación, el abuso, la negligencia, las prácticas nocivas y la violencia contra los niños, niñas y adolescentes. Específicamente, IRC interviene en la gestión de casos con herramientas de apoyo psicosocial y conexiones a servicios disponibles en la comunidad y responde a los impactos humanitarios generados por las diferentes vulneraciones de derechos en esta población. Además de la gestión de casos, el IRC propone trabajar con organizaciones de la sociedad civil para fortalecer capacidades a través de la transferencia de metodologías ampliamente probadas en evidencia, mejoras a los espacios seguros y amigables con la niñez a nivel local, y capacitaciones para la identificación y atención de NNA en múltiples riesgos. En cuanto a los espacios seguros, el IRC basa sus actividades en un método integral propio denominado "Safe learning and healing space", en el que los profesionales apoyan a los NNA en desarrollar sus habilidades socioemocionales, así como en el aprendizaje de las matemáticas y la lectura. A través de los espacios seguros y de otras actividades específicas, también se tomará en cuenta la sensibilización a madres, padres, y cuidadores sobre crianza sin violencia, desde el amor y con estrategias de afrontamiento positivas y manejo del estrés, esto responde al modelo socio ecológico de la atención donde se interviene en el contexto inmediato de los niños y niñas para incidir en una mejora de condiciones para su desarrollo integral. Finalmente, para asegurar de la calidad y de la adecuación de nuestro proyecto con las necesidades de nuestros clientes, el IRC cuenta con un sólido sistema en termino de Monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y aprendizaje.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Assistance for people affected by Extreme Weather Hazards
project_objective: Through this HRP, IOM will provide first-line emergency services in the form of rapid needs assessment and community engagement to respond to the emergency needs of affected population. Ability to respond will be based on logistical capacity, funding, and accessibility. project_name: Improving Access to Basic Need for the Most Vulnerable IDPs and Host Communities in NW Syria
project_objective:
The intervention will involve implementing both One-Off and Multi-Round (8 Rounds) MPCA for the crises affected population in NW Syria. One-Off MPCA will be utilized for any Emergency that may occur during the year while the Multi-Round MPCA will cover the needs of the most vulnerable HHs selected based on the harmonized beneficiary selection criteria developed by the Cash Working Group targeting up to 2,000 HHs with One-Off MPCA valued at150$ as per the CWG recommendations.
MPCA Value: Concern will comply with the CWG recommendations for Multi-Round MPCA (100 USD x8) targeting a total of 1,000 HHs, and the transfer currency will be primarily USD to preserve the value of the assistance and protect the purchasing power of recipient HHs, as long as 100 USD bills remain available. An alternative would be TRY if local/current context justifies; and provided decision is consulted with the CWG, Donor, and other NGOs in the same area.
Baseline Survey: As soon as the beneficiary verification is complete, when undertaking beneficiary registration, the baseline survey will be carried out to measure Coping Strategies Index (CSI) and Food Consumption Score (FCS) using sample size calculator software with confidence level at 95% and 5% confidence interval.
Distribution point selection: All distribution sites will be agreed upon with the local authorities for security and coordination purposes. The selected distribution point should be meeting the minimum requirement of safety and security including:
•	Safe for both staff and Beneficiaries, with a minimum of one entrance and one exit
•	Located in a central location from all beneficiaries’ residence
•	Accessible for all beneficiaries including PWDs, and should have enough space for two separate lines
•	Shaded from weather conditions, equipped with a water resource for drink, and separate latrines for males and females
Beneficiary Selection Criteria: Concern and Implementing Partners will rely on the harmonized beneficiary selection criteria which is being developed by the CWG, if the fund was secured prior to receiving the beneficiary selection criteria, the below criteria serve as a guideline to identify and prioritize households in need of assistance during the winter period:
1.	Disability.
2.	Chronic Diseases.
3.	Pregnant/Lactating Women.
4.	Children Attending School.
5.	Household hosting orphaned, unaccompanied children or homeless relatives due to the conflict.
6.	Living in a temporary settlement.
7.	Household with no source of income.
8.	Household headed by a person with a disability.
Beneficiary Invitation: each of the selected beneficiaries will receive a coupon from the local council agent specifying the date, time and location of the distribution. 
Voucher Distribution: The beneficiaries will collect their vouchers from the distribution table in the distribution point after verifying the beneficiary ID against the approved beneficiary list. The program staff responsible for voucher distribution will stamp the voucher “verified” once the verification is completed and collect beneficiary’s signature on the Voucher Distribution Form, then guide the beneficiary to the redemption table.
Voucher Redemption: when arrived to the redemption table, the programme staff responsible for verification will compare the beneficiary ID with the list and stamped voucher, and ask the beneficiary to sign the Cash Redemption Form. Once the signature is completed, the designated staff will take a photo of the voucher and beneficiary ID to be archived as a Mean of Verification. Then stamp the voucher “Paid” before handing it over to the Financial Services Provider who will exchange the voucher for the determined value ($100 per voucher) and keep the voucher for Financial Reconciliation.

project_name: Expansión y fortalecimiento de atención multi-sectorial a nivel institucional y comunitario para niños, niñas, adolescentes y sus familias en Venezuela.
project_objective:
SC y socios proponen intervenir multisectorialmente en Anzoátegui, Bolívar, Distrito Capital, Miranda, Monagas, Sucre y Zulia, atendiendo las necesidades de NNA de manera holística a partir de los hallazgos de análisis de género y necesidades desarrollados por la organización, a través de un plan de acción que se adapte a las necesidades diferenciadas y evidenciadas por edad, sexo, discapacidad y otras diversidades. Los sectores involucrados son Protección, Educación, Nutrición y Salud, ASH, MdV y Seg. Alimentaria.
Desde la Protección de la niñez, buscará prevenir y responder a los diferentes niveles de riesgos y amenazas de violencia y abuso, incluyendo las violencias basadas en genero. La estrategia comprende tanto prevención (fortalecimiento de capacidades de adultos y NNA a través de sesiones sobre crianza sin violencia basadas en la metodología de Familias Seguras de SCI, así como la construcción, sensibilización y socialización de rutas de atención de servicios de protección) como respuesta (ofreciendo servicios de gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial, orientación legal a NNA y sus familias sobre riesgos de protección utilizando el enfoque común de SC "Pasos para Proteger", articulado con el Sistema de Protección infantil, incluida VBG). A nivel institucional se amentará capacidades técnicas de órganos del sistema de protección local tomando en cuenta necesidades diferenciadas de sobrevivientes. En relación a Educación, las actividades estarán orientadas a contribuir al acceso y permanencia de NNA en situación de riesgo, a través de la dotación de materiales educativos de enseñanza, aprendizaje y para centros educativos. Fortalecer capacidades técnicas en docentes y de educación formal de las etapas inicial, primaria, media y general, así como equipo directivo, en programas, las temáticas estarán asociadas a:  Educación en Emergencia, a través de Creando Aula, participación de NNA, SC Escuela Segura y Day1. Para Nutrición, la desnutrición aguda es la principal causa de mortalidad en niños menores de cinco años, y puede causar efectos negativos en su desarrollo cognitivo si no es detectado a tiempo. Las mujeres/adolescentes en gestación con bajo peso están vinculados a mortalidad materna, parto prematuro y bajo peso al nacer, las intervenciones de SC se enfocan en comunidades en diagnóstico, tratamiento y seguimiento de casos de desnutrición aguda en niños menores de 5 años, adolescentes y mujeres embarazadas mediante el apoyo a centros de salud con aprovisionamiento de insumos y formación a personal de salud e intervenciones a nivel comunitario en zonas de difícil acceso, evaluación de la dupla -madre lactante y niños menores de seis 6 meses- para detección de riesgos, y referencia en casos de ser necesario, creación y formación de guardianes de nutrición con lideres comunitarios y grupos de base comunitaria en prevención de desnutrición, lactancia materna y alimentación del Niño Pequeño y Lactante. Para Salud, las actividades se centran en apoyo de centros de salud primaria aprovisionándoles de medicamentos e insumos, incluido material de EPP, para consultas de atención primaria, cuidado de primera infancia, SSR y VbG. En Medios de Vida, formaciones en habilidades para la vida, habilidades técnicas y emprendimiento o empleabilidad (dependiendo de las oportunidades diagnosticadas en dichos mercados), para el empoderamiento social y económico de adolescentes y mujeres jóvenes; se complementará con dotación de kits productivos con acompañamiento para efectiva utilización para generación de ingresos. En Seguridad Alimentaria se brindarán kits de alimentos -con Nutrición (atendiendo necesidades nutricionales de casos en riesgo)- a los hogares con perfiles de vulnerabilidad. Para WASH, fortalecimiento de mesas técnicas de agua, con enfoque de cambio de comportamiento con temas de higiene y saneamiento, actividades de rehabilitaciones mínimas necesarias, kits de higiene y saneamiento para MEL y familias con menores de 5 años.

project_name: Protection des enfants vulnérables affectés par les conflits dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéry
project_objective: Ce projet vise à améliorer l'environnement protecteur des filles et garçons affectés par les conflits par les biais des mésures préventives, de l'accès inclusif aux services de prise en charge adapaté à leur besoins, ainsi que par le renforcement du système formel et informel de la protection de l'enfant dans les régions de Diffa et Tilabéry. A travers cette intervention, SCI va continuer à se concentrer à promouvoir le cadre politique de la centralité de la protection pour atteindre les enfants les plus touchés et leurs communautés afin que les risques de protection auxquels ils sont confrontés soient identifiés, signalés et prise en charge. Nous nous concentrerons également, sur les dommages causés par les violations des droits et leur impact sur les filles différemment des garçons en tenant compte de leur capacité pour une réponse individualisée de la gestion de cas intégrant le soutien psychosocial et la réintégration socioéconomique. Pour renforcer le système de protection, une cartographie des services et un circuit  de référencement harmonisé seront regulièment actualisés pour promouvoir l’accès aux services essentiels assurant un environnement protecteur. En outre, Les acteurs communautaires seront mobilisés et formés aux outils et approches d'information et de sensibilisation adaptés aux enfants, afin d'assurer un changement de comportement positif et l'adoption de mesures préventives contre les risques et les violations des droits dans les contextes humanitaires.  Les interventions seront orientées vers les enfants les plus vulnérables parmi les populations déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes avec un focus sur ceux difficilement accessible ou en mobilité fréquente en raison de la crise à travers l’approche mobile. Les enfants affectés directement par la crise humanitaire, notamment, les enfants non accompagnés /séparés, associés aux forces et groupes armés et les enfants à risque d’autres violations ou de violences physiques et sexuelles, bénéficieront d’un appui psychosociale individuel et de groupe dans les espaces amis d’enfants, qui soutiennent la protection, le bien-être et l'apprentissage des enfants dans les crises par le renforcement du système, de la qualité et des méthodologies des activités de SMSPS, garantissant l'amélioration du bien-être des enfants et de leur résilience. Le système de protection sera renforcé à travers les approches intégrée  du modèle socio-écologique et des approches communes de SCI. Notamment, le renforcement des capacités sur la manière dont l'assistance sous forme de transfert monétaire et de bons sera utilisée pour atténuer les risques pour les enfants et soutenir une réponse à leurs besoins.  Les familles les plus vulnérables et les familles d’accueil seront soutenus par le Cash à l'aide d'un plan d’action individuel « PAI » participatif afin de réduire les vulnérabilités et renforcer la capacité des familles. Pour les enfants touchés par les conflits armés, l'aide comprendra des services destinés aux enfants qui ont besoin d'une aide à la réunification familial, à la réintégration communautaire comme les EAFGA, une aide aux enfants survivants des VBG liées aux conflits, aux victimes d'engins explosifs, ainsi qu'une aide connexe. Afin de renforcer la gestion des cas individualisée pour tous les enfants ayant besoin des multiples services et ayant des risques élevés. Nous allons faire recours à l' approche commune "Steps to Protect" de SCI, pour assurer une réponse multisectorielle. Il sera aussi question de déployer le CPIMS+ pour renforcer  la mise en œuvre d'un système de gestion de l'information inter-agences. De monitoring de la situation de protection seront organisées. La collaboration avec les autre secteurs (éducation, santé…VBG) sera envisagée pour mettre en place une intervention multisectorielle et multi acteurs. ceci répondra aux sévérités liées aux incidents de protections aux quels un grand nombre des enfants IDP sont exposés

project_name: Integrated response to emergency needs in Nutrition, Health and Protection for recently displaced populations and other disaster-affected people in West Darfur
project_objective:
The Darfur states area remains one of the areas worst-affected by the ongoing conflict which erupted in April 2023 between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which is heavily impacting civilians and has triggered in Sudan the world's
largest displacement crisis. The overall objective of this project is to contribute to reducing the morbidity and mortality of vulnerable populations in the targeted localities in West Darfur, by improving access to quality primary healthcare, nutrition, and community-based PSS support, strengthening the health system and other community-based mechanisms.
PUI will provide assistance and basic quality lifesaving health services to recent IDPs and host communities with increasing needs, supporting five health facilities in West Darfur, 3 HFs in Geneina (Alwadi, Aljabbel,
and Shokri PHCs) and 2 HFs in Kereinek (Um Duwain PHC + one HF to be handed over by SMoH), + 2 Mobile Health teams, 1 in each of these two localities:
-provision of essential pharmaceutical commodities following standard purchase quality process, distribution and management, and non-medical equipment and supplies to health facilities + HFs rehabilitation, including necessary WASH rehabilitations, in and around the HFs. PUI will continue to coordinate with UNFPA and WHO for the provision of SRH and IEH kits.
-Provision of free life-saving primary health care services for the population in the targeted localities through support to health facilities and mobile clinics (OPD, SRH services, including ANC, PNC, family planning and deliveries, immunization, nursing care, investigations and drug dispensing, + medical care for SGBV), referrals to higher level of care to facilities supported by partners (MSF in Geneina and Kereinek), + provision of psychosocial support groups sessions. All services will be free of change to the beneficiaries. The second modality is the deployment of mobile health teams to reach locations where security and infrastructure do not allow for the provision of primary health care through fixed facilities)
-Staff training (outbreak preparedness, national/WHO standard protocols and guidelines, SRH.
Nutrition:
-support to community management of acute malnutrition: provision of quality nutrition services to IDPs and host communities in 3 HFs in Geneina, 2 HFs in Kereinek and 2 MHT, one in each location, through support to OTPs for children with SAM without complications and support to TSFPs for MAM children. Services provided will follow PUI’s Simplified Approach, as endorsed by the Federal MoH in case supplies are not available. PUI coordinating with UNICEF for nutrition commodities supplies, but will will purchase contingency stock to ensure access and continuity of the treatment for the newly displaced population or in newly accessible areas. + referrals of SAM with complications in Geneina and Kereinek hospitals, both supported by MSF. 
-establish 5 Mother Support Groups, one per HF's catchment population areas, of 10 women each => provided with IYCF training, cooking demonstrations + Family MUAC. Network of trained community volunteers, in charge of active screening in community and community awareness
The project and activities will be directly implemented by PUI team on the field, and through our office in Geneina, West Darfur. PUI has a sub-base in neighboring city of Adre, Chad, where our central pharmacy is located. PUI is an active member of the Health and Nutrition Sectors, of the Protection Technical Working Group (TWG) and the MHPSS TWG, at the national and sub-national level in West Darfur., and of the Consortium Protection/Safeguarding TWG. 
PUI plans to provide 78,976 OPD consultations, 2,288 deliveries attended by skilled birth attendants, and provide PSS support to 3,840 people; PUI will provide treatment to 1,182 children under 5 suffering from MAM or SAM without complications, and with complications through referrals.

project_name: Bhasan Char Inter Agency Response
project_objective: Bhasan Char was established by the Government of Bangladesh where it is planned to relocate 100,000 members of the Rohingya community from Myanmar on a voluntary basis. Aimed at addressing the overcrowding in Cox’s Bazar and improving living conditions, the project is led by the Government with relevant Ministries and agencies actively involved, as well as national and international NGOs. With the MoU between Government of Bangladesh and UNHCR (on behalf of the UN) in place, UN operations have been developed on the island and as of 31 October 2023, 30,881 refugees has been relocated there.  Humanitarian community will continue to make efforts to supplement and complement the humanitarian activities of the national and international NGOs in support of this national led effort. The project will support refugees on Bhasan Char, who are highly vulnerable and entirely dependent on humanitarian assistance. Women, children, and person with specific needs reported the most significant unmet needs, leaving them vulnerable to negative coping strategies. Bhasan Char is vulnerable to climate risks such as cyclones, storms, frequent lightning and flooding due to monsoon and tidal surges. The Inter-Agency efforts will provide support and assistance to refugees including protection, shelter, food and non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene, health and nutrition, education, livelihoods and skill development. To mitigate disaster risks, emergency, preparedness, and response (EPR) will be part of the inter-agency response.

project_name: Provide lifesaving, comprehensive, multi-sectoral and inclusive Gender-Based Violence services, integrated with Sexual & Reproductive Health services, to Rohingya refugees & host communities in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
Guided by the IASC Minimum Standards, UNFPA will promote, coordinate & provide lifesaving, comprehensive, multi-sectoral & inclusive GBV prevention & response services to Rohingya Refugees & Bangladeshi host communities in Cox’s Bazar, in line with the survivor-centered approach and the principles of value-for-money and accountability of affected populations.

UNFPA will provide integrated & age-responsive GBV/SRH services including case management, MHPSS, clinical management of rape, voluntary family planning, STI testing & treatment, and emergency referrals, in 53 Women Friendly Spaces (WFS) and 15 health facilities. UNFPA will also promote & advance gender equality & women’s empowerment, and foster social behavior change among women, girls, men & boys in 10 Women-Led Community Centers (WLCC) that offer PSS, life skills development, self-reliance activities, GBV prevention & awareness raising and emergency referrals. 

Through WFSs & WLCCs, UNFPA will provide life-skills based empowering programs for adolescents & youth (A&Y) aged 10-24 to prevent violence against adolescent girls & child marriage. The Girl Shine program will equip girls with skills & knowledge on GBV, service availability, bodily autonomy, gender equality, MHPSS, SRH, menstrual health and emotional skills. Alongside, the Champions of Change program will engage boys in safe spaces to identify and challenge harmful social norms that perpetuate inequality and redefine masculinity. 

The project will mobilize communities to challenge gender-biased social norms & harmful practices and prevent GBV through community engagement, awareness raising and enhancement of women & men’s caregiver roles. Key modalities that will be used are the SASA! Together approach, to address social norms that perpetuate gender inequalities; and structured, community-level sessions for A&Y caregivers.

Across UNFPA-supported facilities, Rohingya women, men & young people will benefit from increased volunteer opportunities; skills development training; and a pilot intervention for the provision of Dignity Kits items through voucher modality; to contribute to their self-reliance and livelihood, thus to community wellbeing and social cohesion. Community engagement and social cohesion will also be promoted through Women Support Groups, Community Watch Groups and Self-Help Groups. 
The project will address the needs of vulnerable groups by integrating targeted measures in programming and developing partnership with specialized organizations, including women-led organizations. UNFPA will capacitate partners on intersectional vulnerabilities to enhance GBV programmatic support and case management services for persons with disabilities, gender diverse populations and elderly women.

As both beneficiaries & aid workers are at risk of sexual exploitation and abuse, UNFPA will advocate & provide technical guidance alongside capacity development to IPs in coordination with ISCG PSEA Network to ensure safeguarding for beneficiaries and that PSEA referral, reporting mechanisms & policies are in place. UNFPA will strengthen PSEA Champions to prevent SEA & raise awareness on reporting mechanisms among the Rohingyas.  

Under UNFPA leadership, the GBVSS comprises 67 members managing the inter-agency GBV response in Cox’s Bazar as per IASC Minimum Standards. GBVSS will engage with & enhance the capacities of members, other sectors & government stakeholders for effective, coordinated & integrated GBV prevention, mitigation & response. Focus will be on ensuring the continuity, quality & sustainability of comprehensive GBV services, case management & multi-sectoral referral systems with the rollout of Digital Referral Pathway App (eRPW). Regular community-based GBV risk monitoring & joint safety/service audits will support such efforts. GBVIMS Task Team of GBVSS will continue its transition to GBVIMS+ with features for online GBV case management & incident recording, embracing more advanced technology.

project_name: Continued provision of quality life saving comprehensive and integrated sexual reproductive health and rights services, for Rohingya refugees and host communities targeting women and girls as well as young people and adolescents in Cox's Bazar
project_objective: Despite the improvement in the proportion of facility-based deliveries at 82% and access to four antenatal care visits at 78% , the number of preventable maternal mortalities is still unacceptably high with an average of 7 maternal deaths reported  every month. Of these deaths, 76% occur at health facilities, 44% during pregnancy and labour while over 70% have attended at least 3 antenatal care visits. This project will focus on strengthening strategies and interventions to improve the access to quality maternal health care for women and girls to reduce the number of preventable maternal and perinatal mortality and morbidity occurring in the Rohingya response. UNFPA as the coordinating agency of the sexual reproductive health working group (SRH WG) will strengthen the coordination of over 42 SRH partners to improve the quality of SRH services. The SRH WG will continue to ensure collaborative inter-sectoral coordination with the health sector, Gender based violence (GBV) sub sector, community health workers (CHW) working group, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) working group and Government stakeholders. This project will strengthen the maternal and perinatal surveillance and response (MPMSR) and the SRH information management systems to identify and address the preventable causes of maternal and perinatal deaths and work with the relevant stakeholders to improve the quality of care provided to women and girls during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. UNFPA will guarantee the availability of family planning and other reproductive health commodities and supplies through enhanced supply chain management to satisfy the unmet needs of refugees and surrounding host communities. Operationalization of the family planning (FP) strategy for Cox’s Bazar through support to facility and community-based provision of voluntary family planning methods as well as FP evidence generation will be a major focus. In addition, the continued mentorship and skilling of the midwifery workforce in the management of emergency obstetric and newborn emergencies, improved emergency obstetric and newborn ambulance referrals and access to SRH services, improved quality of antenatal and post-natal services as well as quality facility-based deliveries will be of high priority. UNFPA will focus on provision of and access to SRH services targeting adolescents and youths as well other minority groups like the persons with disabilities. UNFPA will continue to support the provision of basic emergency Obstetric and newborn care (BEmONC) services at 21 health facilities and 1 CEmONC facility across 11 camps and surrounding host communities with support to the Upazilla health complexes as well as Sadar hospital. UNFPA will provide integrated SRH/GBV/MHPSS/ASRH services at health facility and community levels working with CHWs for community engagement, pregnancy mapping, EDD and high-risk pregnant mothers mapping and referral, social mobilization, and other awareness-raising interventions as well as traditional birth attendants (TBAs) as facilitators of improved SRH services uptake. The TBAs will be incentivized to refer and escort pregnant mothers for facility-based deliveries and provide nonclinical labour support as trusted community members to pregnant mothers while at the health facility in the camps with low facility-based deliveries according to the CHW WG data. UNFPA will enhance its preparedness to ensure that during natural disasters and disease outbreaks, the minimum initial services package (MISP) for reproductive health are integrated within the health response plans and emergency response teams, emergency response teams are trained on MISP as well as preposition of emergency reproductive health kits. The capacity of health practitioners, community health workers and other stakeholders providing adolescent health to deliver integrated, client-centered, respectful high-quality services will be enhanced.

project_name: Assurer l'accès à une éducation inclusive et de qualité aux garçons et filles affectés par la crise dans les régions du Sahel, du Nord, du Centre Nord, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, de la Cascade et de l'Est, au Burkina Faso.
project_objective:
Le présent projet initié par Save the Children s’inscrit dans une logique de continuité éducative des élèves affectés par la crise sécuritaire et vise à améliorer l’accès inclusif et la qualité des enseignements et apprentissages de 100 000 élèves dans un environnement protecteur (dont 60% de filles , et 1% d’enfant en situation d’handicap). La zone d’intervention couvre la région du Sahel province du Seno et Oudallan ; la région du Nord , province du Yatenga ; la région de l’Est  province du gourma ; la région de la boucle du Mouhoun , province de la Kossi et du Sourou ; la région des Cascades , province de la Comoé .  
La réponse proposée s’articule autour de quatre résultats 
 1-Les filles et les garçons âgés de 6 à 18 ans ont accès à des possibilités d'apprentissage dans des espaces d'apprentissage sûrs, protecteurs et inclusifs. 
2-Les filles et les garçons âgés de 6 à 18 ans bénéficient de possibilités d'apprentissage de qualité.
3-Les enfants sont capables de réintégrer l'école à leur niveau d'âge lorsque les activités scolaires reprennent.
4-La réponse de l'éducation en situation d'urgence est bien coordonnée, favorise les interventions localisées et répond aux besoins des enfants.
L'approche proposée va permettre d’assurer une éducation inclusive de qualité et d’améliorer le bien être des élèves affectés par la crise sécuritaire. En outre l’approche impliquera de multiples groupes de parties prenantes dans les différentes régions afin d'assurer une appropriation locale aux niveaux scolaire, communautaire et institutionnel, alignée sur les meilleures pratiques en matière de programmation de la résilience dans les contextes nexus
 Pour amplifier l’impact de l’intervention, un focus sera mis sur la promotion du genre en milieu scolaire.  Pour ce faire il sera à priori nécessaire de renforcer les capacités des acteurs éducatifs sur le concept genre en situation d’urgence. Des actions de sensibilisations, d’identification et d’orientation des filles déscolarisées ou fille mère seront menées (par les organisations des mères éducatives) pour leur réinscription à travers les alternatives éducatives adaptées à leur âge ou besoin (les stratégies de scolarisation accélérées ou des formations aux métiers). Des mesures incitatives de financement des études des filles (bourses scolaire, kit scolaire, kit GHM …)  seront proposées pour faciliter la réinscription et le maintien des filles à l’école. Enfin toutes les activités proposées prendront en compte les femmes/filles à 60% et les hommes/garçons à 40%. 
Aussi l’engagement communautaire et la redevabilité seront promus à travers les comités de veille safe School , les comités de redevabilités au niveau communautaire, les lignes vertes et les boites à suggestion dans les écoles. La prévention contre les violences et abus sexuel sera renforcée par des sensibilisations. Les enfants et femmes victimes d’exploitation et d'abus sexuels, de discrimination et de négligence seront pris en charge à travers l’accès aux services adaptés, y compris le soutien mental et psychosocial ou le référencement vers des services spécialisés.

project_name: Fourniture d'un ensemble de services de soins de santé de base, en travaillant avec des agents de santé communautaires, en mettant l'accent sur la santé infantile, la santé sexuelle et reproductive, avec des systèmes d'orientation solides pour les soins préventifs (par exemple, les vaccinations) et curatifs.
project_objective:
La situation sanitaire du pays est préoccupante, avec 375 centres de santé, soit 17,7 % des établissements de santé, fermés en raison de l'insécurité. De plus, 357 autres structures fonctionnent avec une capacité minimale, ce qui signifie que 3 398 560 personnes n'ont pas accès aux services de santé. Cette situation a un impact significatif sur la vie des nouveau-nés qui naissent dans des conditions précaires. Cependant, le groupe santé s'efforce de combler les lacunes laissées par les agents de santé communautaires afin d'aider les femmes à obtenir des soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive d'urgence.
Depuis la 32ème semaine de l'année, le pays a connu une forte augmentation des cas de dengue, affectant principalement les régions du Centre, des Hauts Bassins et du Sahel. Au cours de la 40ème semaine, sur un total de 40361 cas, plus de 166 décès ont été enregistrés. La situation humanitaire limite la capacité des adolescents et des jeunes à accéder aux services qui aident à réduire la transmission du VIH, à prévenir les grossesses précoces ou non désirées et à empêcher les avortements clandestins.
Le SCI alignera sa réponse humanitaire 2024 sur celle du pays en renforçant le système de santé. La réponse vise à fournir des soins de santé primaires, promotionnels, préventifs et curatifs aux populations affectées, en particulier aux enfants, ainsi que des références pour ceux qui ont des besoins plus spécifiques. La réponse de 2024 consistera à renforcer, équiper et motiver les agents de santé communautaires et les volontaires recrutés par les districts sanitaires pour s'occuper des enfants, y compris des adolescentes, des femmes enceintes et des mères allaitantes. L'action visera également à promouvoir leurs droits en matière de santé sexuelle et génésique. Les accoucheuses traditionnelles seront habilitées et déléguées pour fournir des soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive, le cas échéant. Un système de retour d'information communautaire sera mis en place pour soutenir les interventions. Une attention particulière sera accordée à la prévention et à l'endiguement des maladies épidémiques telles que la dengue.
Avec un budget de 3 millions de dollars, le SCI vise à assurer l'accès aux services de santé primaire, y compris la santé sexuelle et reproductive, pour les personnes déplacées et non déplacées dans les zones difficiles d'accès.
Cible : 100 000 personnes, dont 60 % d'enfants.

project_name: Horizontes Unidos
project_objective:
El proyecto se enfocará en una serie de acciones integrales destinadas a abordar las necesidades variadas y complejas de la población beneficiaria. Se implementará un enfoque holístico que garantice la protección, el apoyo y la inclusión de los migrantes vulnerables, refugiados y solicitantes de asilo, especialmente aquellos en situaciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, como niños no acompañados, mujeres embarazadas, familias solas y personas con enfermedades crónicas o discapacidades

Las acciones propuestas incluirán la entrega de 3 transferencias monetarias por un monto de US$140 para 100 familias migrantes que residen en comunidades de acogida, que podrán utilizarse para la regularización de estatus migratorio en el país, o facilitar el acceso a los servicios de educación en emergencia especialmente la inscripción de niños, niñas y adolescentes migrantes al sistema formal de educación.  También, se hará entrega de 500 vouchers a población en tránsito que podrá ser utilizado para cubrir sus necesidades más inmediatas. Además, se propone realizar la entrega de 3000 kits de hidratación para población en tránsito y 3000 kits específicos para Niños, niñas y adolescentes.   Se fomentará la colaboración estrecha con instituciones de gobierno garantes para la protección de la niñez como la Secretaría de Bienestar Social SBS, la Procuraduría General de la Nación PGN, el Ministerio de Salud, de Desarrollo Social, y Educación, líderes comunitarios, organizaciones de protección y familias locales de acogida para garantizar un entorno de apoyo y aceptación.
Finalmente, se desarrollarán iniciativas específicas para abordar las necesidades de supervivientes de violencia de género y personas LGTBQI+, promoviendo entornos seguros y libres de discriminación. Estas acciones se llevarán a cabo con un enfoque centrado en los derechos humanos, la dignidad y la promoción de la igualdad, reconociendo la diversidad y singularidad de cada individuo dentro de la población beneficiaria.

project_name: Assistance humanitaire aux personnes vulnérables réfugiés, déplacées et familles hotes de régions de Diffa, Tahoua et Tillabéri
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire continue à aggraver le besoin humanitaire avec des mouvements massifs de population dans la région de trois frontières et celle du lac Tchad. Au 28 février 2023, le nombre de personnes en situation de déplacement dans la région de Tillabéri était d’environ 139 051 personnes déplacées internes, 41 187 réfugiés et 25 632 demandeurs d’asile qui sont des Burkinabés et des Maliens. La région de Tahoua quant à elle a accueillie environ 72 022 personnes déplacées internes, 20 621 réfugiés et 16 431 demandeurs d’asile. Près de 81% des PDI se sont installées dans les départements de Tillia et Tassara alors que la majorité des réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile se trouvent dans les départements de Tillia et de Madaoua. (Rapport OCHA 25 mars 2023)
Toujours en termes de mouvement de population, selon les derniers chiffres de recensement au 31 janvier 2023, la région de Diffa a enregistré 314 888¹ personnes en situation de déplacement (personnes déplacées internes, réfugiées, retournées et demandeurs d’asile), soit une augmentation de 21% comparativement à la même période en 2022.
En effet, des mouvements de populations complexes (secondaires et pendulaires) ont été observés dans la région au cours des douze derniers mois, en raison de la situation sécuritaire qui reste volatile. Le nombre de personnes déplacées internes (PDI) est quant à lui passé de 81 464 à 140 593 personnes, soit une hausse de 73%.
WHH se propose donc d'assurer la sécurité alimentaire de ces ménages pendant la période critique de la soudure, mais également de renforcer leur sécurité nutritionnelle.
Le projet vise à fournir le plus rapidement possible à 7500 ménages particulièrement vulnérables et qui sont en phase 2 et 3 de l'insécurité alimentaire, un accès aux denrées alimentaires, aux intrants agricoles et maraichères ainsi que les aliments de bétail pour leur cheptel. Les ménages vulnérables peu ou pas aptes au travail dans le besoin, et qui n'ont pas de bras valides dans leurs ménages, WHH mettra en œuvre des actions de distribution de cash inconditionnel dans le strict respect de la dignité humaine. sans aucune distinction sociale, raciale, religieuse ou genre.
