project_name: Prestación de Servicios de Prevención, Respuesta y Apoyo que salvan vidas en Salud Sexual y Reproductiva, Educación Integral de la Sexualidad y Violencia Basada en Género para las mujeres y adolescentes más vulnerables en 11 estados priorizados de Venezuela
project_objective:
El proyecto plantea proteger y garantizar el acceso a los derechos de salud sexual y reproductiva (SSR), a la educación integral de la sexualidad (EIS) y al derecho a vivir una vida libre de violencia de las mujeres y adolescentes más vulnerables, incluyendo a las embarazadas, personas con discapacidad y poblaciones indígenas, a través de una estrategia intersectorial para la prestación de servicios esenciales de SSR, EIS diferenciado para adolescentes, y prevención y respuesta a la VBG que salvan vidas y promueven bienestar, en 11 estados priorizados de Venezuela (Amazonas, Anzoátegui, Apure, Bolívar, DC, Delta Amacuro, Falcón, Miranda, Sucre, Táchira y Zulia) alcanzando a un total de  582.399 personas. El proyecto está alineado con los objetivos sectoriales de los clústeres de salud, protección y educación.
Acorde a la estrategia del MPPS para la disminución de muertes maternas y al Plan Gran Misión Venezuela Mujer para garantizar la protección de la salud de la mujer en todas las etapas. Procura fortalecer el Sistema Público Nacional de Salud, mejorando el acceso a los servicios de SSR oportunos y de calidad a 420,034 mujeres, para la prevención de morbimortalidad materna, embarazo no deseado, infecciones de transmisión sexual (ITS), disminución de la Sífilis congénita, transmisión vertical del VIH, violencia sexual. Deja capacidades instaladas en 34 hospitales y 85 centros de la red de Atención Primaria en Salud, promoviendo los servicios, suministros y fortaleciendo capacidades del talento humano (1576), provisión de anticonceptivos, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, pruebas diagnósticas rápidas y ejecución de las rehabilitaciones necesarias para disponibilidad de agua y luz en la atención de emergencias obstétricas. Se incluyen acciones para la respuesta intersectorial a la VBG en el MCVS con el acondicionamiento de los espacios, dotación de insumos, medicamentos, PEP Kit y capacitación al personal que brinda la atención.
Por parte de EIS, la población estimada a alcanzar es 171.889 de NNA en las comunidades con énfasis en la población indígena. Se pretende, a mediano y largo plazo, reducir la vulnerabilidad y fortalecer la resiliencia de NNA y personas con discapacidad, previniendo embarazos no intencionales a edad temprana y en la adolescencia, VBG, VIH e ITS a través de la Educación Integral de la Sexualidad. Para ello se espera: Proveer servicios de SSR diferenciados y de calidad que salven vidas para NNA, que incluyan la dispensación de anticonceptivos, asesoría, seguimiento y adherencia. Establecer espacios de calidad para la EIS en el medio extraescolar y desarrollar redes comunitarias de apoyo para la prevención de embarazos no deseados, VBG, VIH e ITS. Formar docentes en EIS y personal de salud en anticoncepción para la atención de las CDA y los Espacios de Atención comunitarios. 
Se pretende facilitar el acceso a servicios integrales de respuesta multisectorial a la VBG desde un enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, con énfasis en la violencia sexual, mientras se reducen y mitigan los riesgos de VBG. Se beneficiará directamente a 80,510 personas, 54,438 mujeres, 9,177 niñas y adolescentes, 10,217 hombres y 6,672 jóvenes, a través de 5 objetivos estratégicos: 1)Proporcionar asistencia y servicios de protección especializados de gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial y orientación jurídica a 3,180 sobrevivientes. 2)Fortalecer capacidades de prevención de la VBG en comunidades y el cambio comportamental de 69,231 personas a través de diversas estrategias. 3)Contribuir a la resiliencia de 550 mujeres a través del establecimiento de 14 ESMN. 4)Fortalecer las capacidades de 692 personal humanitario e instituciones, con enfoque centrado en las sobrevivientes y la entrega de asistencia material a instituciones para la respuesta a la VBG, y 5)Fortalecer los mecanismos de coordinación de las intervenciones de GBV, la actualización regular de las rutas de remisiones y POEs, acompañando los grupos temáticos de trabajo.

project_name: Provide Access to Safe, Inclusive, and Quality Basic Education to Vulnerable Children, Out of School Children and Youth aged (3-18) in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The project will seek to provide access to safe, inclusive, and quality basic education to vulnerable children, out of school children and youth aged (3-18) in South Sudan for the year 2024. The project will be implemented in Akobo, Nyirol, Bor South counties of Jonglei State, Maban county of Upper Nile State, Kapoeta East and Magwi counties of Eastern Equitoria State; and Abyei Administrative Area. The education project will target a total of 27, 301beneficiaries (24,360 learners, 3,398 B & 10,962 G; 1,575 Teachers, 866 M & 709 F; 1,365 PTAs/SMCs, 751M & 614 F). The project goal will be achieved through three objectives: 
The first objective:  Emergency-affected children and youth have access to safe, protective, inclusive education services that are appropriate to their age, learning level and need. This objective will be achieved by supporting the enrollments of 24,360 learners (3,398 B & 10,962) in pre-primary, primary and secondary schools/learning centers; establishing & rehabilitating 49 temporary learning structures for the children affected by various emergencies; constructing 49 gender segregated WASH facilities in schools and learning spaces; conducting 7 BTL campaigns to support in enrolling out of school children in 7 counties; mapping teacher/tracking for re-integration into education system to support continuity of education in 7 counties; establishing child help desks in 105 schools; establishing and support CP/GBV community protection committees in 7 project targeted counties; Providing and distributing sanitation and hygiene materials to 105 schools; and providing of dignity kits to 10,500 girls in schools.
The second objective: Children and youth are provided with quality teaching and learning services that support retention and progress through the education cycle. This objective will be achieved by training 1,575 teachers (866 M, & 709 W) on EiE pedagogical skills and child-centered methodologies to improve teaching and learning process for emergency-affected children; providing to 4,128 (2,270 B & 1,858 G) emergency affected children quality education recreational materials; providing 21 education kits to leaners in schools; training 210 (105 M & 105 F) teachers on MHPSS to support mental health healing of learners; and supporting catch-up classes in 105 schools and learning centres affected by various emergencies.
The third objective: Coordination and crisis management capacity is strengthened to promote efficient, accountable, and timely education in emergencies response. This objective will be achieved by training 49 (28 M, & 21 W) SMCs/PTAs and education authorities on school management, governance, psychosocial support and Disaster Risk Reduction.

project_name: Improving Access to HLP Rights and General Protection Services for conflict-affected communities in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
The Norwegian Refugee Council through its Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) and General Protection programming seek to address needs of IDPs, host communities, returnees and other vulnerable individuals by increasing access to protection services, basic essential services, and securing Housing Land and Property (HLP) rights through improved security of tenure to the conflict-affected population in Northeast Nigeria, Nigeria.

NRC being the HLP AoR co-lead will coordinate and strengthen HLP services and structures for the target communities through a series of coordination meetings, community engagement, initiatives, and events. To achieve that, logistical support will be provided to collaborative dispute resolution centers/structures and the land ministry to facilitate their work. The project intends to enhance the capacity of local authorities and community leaders on HLP and collaborative dispute resolution so they can uphold the basic human rights of IDPs, returnees, and host communities. Furthermore, the absence of civil administration in hard-to-reach LGAs poses a challenge in terms of accessibility to basic essential services, especially for the physically disabled and other vulnerable groups. Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) in north-east Nigeria continue intensely across villages, communities, and towns and this has led to more displacement. Ongoing camp closure and return by the Borno State Government has exerted pressure on existing facilities and structures both at return locations as well as areas of integration which has led to reduced access to essential services especially for IDPs and returnees. Cases of evictions have been reported, and the trend will likely continue into 2024, with the most vulnerable households at risk of eviction and other related HLP rights violations.

NRC’s Protection from Violence (PfV) (the general protection component) team aims to contribute to increasing the rights and capacity of the conflict affected populations to prevent protection risks and threats. Specialized protection activities such as protection case management and individual protection assistance will be provided to improve the well-being and strengthen their resilience, protection, and dignity of the conflict-affected population in BAY States. The NRC protection project will target vulnerable individuals from displaced and host communities to benefit from the protection interventions that respond to their needs. This project will contribute to Protection Sector’s response objective to; a) to mitigate and respond to the harm caused to persons who have suffered violence, coercion, exploitation, serious neglect, or discrimination, and to restore their capacity to live safe and dignified lives, and b) to strengthen targeted protection services to address the needs and vulnerability of persons at heightened risks of violence, exploitation, serious neglect, or discrimination; enhance their capacities and reduce the risk of resorting to negative coping mechanisms.

project_name: provision of low-cost, high-impact basic health services in Yei River County.
project_objective: Yei is one of the counties in Central Equatoria State that has been heavily affected by the 2016 conflict between government and opposition forces, resulting in the displacement of people from their places of origin. Yei is currently home to some 61199 IDPs, 22848 returnees and 4056 refugees, who have settled in the main town of Yei. According to the RRC, the county continues to receive a daily influx of returnees from Uganda and the DRC.The conflict in Yei has disrupted the health system in the county, with most of the infrastructure destroyed and in need of repair. As a result of the conflict, the provision of health services has become a major challenge, particularly in rural areas. The most affected payams in Yei that require health interventions are Lasu, Tore, Mugwo, Yei Town and Otogo. This project will therefore aim to improve health services through the provision of drugs, rehabilitation of existing health infrastructure, child immunisation, health education and treatment of the most communicable diseases. The intervention will target 82513 people including men, women and children from the 5 payams of Tore, Mugwo, Yei town, Lasu and Otogo in Yei County.

project_name: Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery Response for the Most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria
project_objective:
The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities. The essence of the project is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited -support to regain control over their basic needs (access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations will be based on a context analysis and needs assessment conducted, prioritizing areas based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to reach areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage) and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services. The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions.

project_name: Integrated response for crisis affected population in Far-North region of Cameroon.
project_objective:
Cameroon is continuing to face a severe and complex humanitarian crisis in its Far North region caused by recurrent shocks, including insecurity with the increasing presence and influence of Non-State Armed
Groups (NSAGs) and armed conflicts, increasing effects of climate change with droughts and floods, and
epidemics, that can occur simultaneously, in an already underserved region with a disrupted local economy. The impact on the most vulnerable populations is severe as it exposes them to important protection risks, while the continuous violence, including recurring incursions by NSAGs in the targeted areas, but also clashes between communities, has continued to lead to conflict-driven displacements. In this context, the IRC is proposing to address humanitarian needs through a two-year intervention aiming at providing an integrated response for crisis-affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon. The IRC has designed the proposed program to combine both lifesaving and early recovery services for affected populations so that communities can increase their resilience and capacities to better face future shocks. The IRC will implement a tailored, beneficiary-centered and gradual and integrated package combining complementary interventions in Protection, Multipurpose Cash, Economic Recovery and WASH. The IRC will involve local actors, authorities, community leaders and the targeted communities in the implementation of the program, to ensure it is addressing their most pressing needs, as well as to foster local ownership of the activities.

project_name: Social protection, Inclusion and Cohesion (SPIC)
project_objective:
The project aims to address the complex challenges faced by Syrians due to prolonged crises and especially persons with disabilities (PWDs) and their families as they are among those most affected. It focuses on the depletion of financial capital, loss of human capital, erosion of social capital, and systemic inequalities. It provides concentrated resources and expertise that offer an integrated, multifaceted modular approach to revitalizing individuals' and communities. It is structured into three interlinked areas of work: Social Protection and Inclusive Socioeconomic Empowerment, Social Inclusion, and Social Cohesion.
The severe stress Syria has been under since 2011 due to several crises, including armed conflict, economic collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, and an earthquake in 2023, have led to vast infrastructure damages, increased poverty, social tension, brain-drain due to youth migration, and an erosion of social capital. Data from 2022 showed an alarming 90 per cent rate of people expected to be living below the poverty line and 85% of households being unable to meet basic needs (HNO 2023). It is estimated that 16% of female-headed households are completely unable to meet basic needs , and more than 60% of persons with disabilities are out-of-work (Human Development Report, 2021).
To address these complex challenges, our approach integrates long-term developmental and peace-building approaches with efforts to fill protection gaps. Implementation includes cash assistance conditional to inducing positive health and education outcomes. Additionally, we aim to implement hybrid intervention consisting of cash for work and skill development schemes to yield positive impact. In parallel, the labour market component will consist of a skill development program. Activities also focus on gender and disability inclusion as blueprints of social inclusion and create learning experience to advocate for additional intersectionality and social structures, with possible expansion to include youth and elderly. The project also proposes the delivery of in-kind assistance with focus on the health and wellbeing aspects of human capital. This includes the provision of assistive products for persons with disabilities to alleviate financial pressure and to contribute to the health and autonomy of beneficiaries. In addition to the inclusion of mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS), to improve cognitive resilience which is essential for social cohesion. As for the PSEA Strategy, UNDP will prepare training and awareness gender materials according to UNDP guideline, then conduct training/orientation/ awareness sessions on promoting gender sensitivity behaviors with targeted communities and institutions of civil society.
The projects faces the following Risks, as follows are the Assumptions and mitigating measures:
1- Capacity of Local Partners: sensitization, awareness-raising and capacity development of our partners will be prioritized.
2- The comparative advantage of vulnerable groups in leading peacebuilding efforts: We will provide tailored training and resources to these groups and the creation of opportunities for representation.
3- Access to electricity and internet: After conducting a needs assessment, If access is found to be limited, we will explore partnerships to facilitate improved access, or adapt alternative solutions.
4- Contact approach efficiency: Ensuring that all facilitated interactions between groups
are under conditions that promote safety, equality and inclusion, common goals, intergroup cooperation, and support by social and institutional authorities.
5- Additional crisis and political and economic instability: The project design should be adaptive and flexible to adjust to changes in the country's situation.
6- Funding Inconsistencies: Enhancing trusted partnerships and keep donors and stakeholders regularly informed about the progress of the project and challenges faced.

project_name: Services vitaux intégrés de santé sexuelle et reproductive pour les populations affectées dans les  régions de L'Extreme-Nord, Nord-ouest et Sud-ouest.
project_objective:
La situation sécuritaire dans la région de l'Extrême-Nord (EN) du Cameroun reste toujours extrêmement préoccupante en raison de l'insurrection de Boko Haram dans le bassin du lac Tchad. Bien que leur fréquence ait diminué, les raids de Boko Haram continuent de pénétrer dans les départements du Logone et du Chari, du Mayo Sava et du MayoTsanaga, entraînant des meurtres, des pillages et des vols de bétail, des enlèvements et des incendies de villages. La crise du NW et du SW ont entrainé des déplacements internes, les destructions des formations sanitaires avec un impact considérable sur le système de santé. Encore, les enlèvements se poursuivent dans les zones frontalières de l'EN, provoquant un traumatisme au sein des familles et des communautés. Au 31 Août 2022 par exemple, OIM à travers le DTM Round 25 a enregistré  573 184 personnes en situation de déplacement dans la région de l’Extrême-Nord. Parmi ces personnes, 385 372 sont des PDIs, 138 152 retournés et 49 660 réfugiés vivant hors du camp de Minawao. Ces personnes sont déplacées par le conflit lié au GANE, au conflit intercommunautaire et aux inondations. Les populations dans ces trois régions en crise ont des besoins de base à satisfaire, mais aussi une pression énorme sur les populations hôtes. Les femmes, en particulier les adolescentes jeunes et les enfants, sont très affectées par les conflits et sont exposées à la violence, aux abus et à l'exploitation, séparation des familles et ont des besoins importants en matière de santé reproductive et besoins psychosociaux.
Dans ces situations d'instabilité, les femmes et les enfants représentent toujours plus de 75 % des personnes enregistrées et sont les plus vulnérables. Les violences sexuelles et sexistes, notamment les viols, les agressions sexuelles, les violences physiques, économiques ou psychologiques, sont fréquemment perpétrées. Le taux de mortalité maternelle qui est à l’échelle nationale de 406 décès maternels pour 100 000 naissances vivantes. A l’Extrême Nord pour ne citer que cette région, 70% d’accouchements se font en communauté, les besoins non satisfaits en planification familiale sont élevés avec un taux de 7% de  prévalence contraceptive moderne. 
Le Dispositif Minimum d’Urgence en SSR est la réponse aux problèmes susmentionnés mais force est de constater que sa disponibilité, son utilisation et accessibilité restent des préoccupations à adresser de façon efficace par le repositionnement du DMU-SR dans les zones humanitaires.

project_name: Provision of holistic GBV services to IDPs, returnees and host communities in the protracted conflict zones of the North west, South west & Far North regions, Cameroon.
project_objective:
Since 2016, the North West and South West regions of Cameroon have been going through fragile security and continued hostilities, targeted attacks and destruction of property and infrastructure, causing human rights violations and massive population movement. As of June 2023, about 638,421 are estimated to be internally displaced people . While many of the affected people in the regions take refuge within the other subdivisions that are seemingly safe, several of them tend to flee to the neighboring centers around Buea and Bamenda within the NW/SW regions, and others flee to the Littoral and West regions. But with these movements of populations, the services in the various parts of those towns and regions are getting constrained, and therefore there is need for support to strengthen social services in these two regions too. The NW/SW crisis has also impacted other regions. The Littoral and West regions, because of proximity to the South West region, and as a cosmopolitan city, is hosting over 194,065 IDPs  in prolonged displacement situations. 

In the Far North region, the security situation remains critical, with attacks by non-state armed groups (NSAGs) on the increase, 90% of which took place in the Logone-et-Chari, Mayo-Sava and Mayo-Tsanaga divisions. Clashes between non-state armed groups and state security forces have also increased. Rural areas remain particularly affected as national security entities are concentrated along the main roads and exercise less control over other locations.  In addition to the increasingly volatile security situation, the Far North region is subject to the consequences of climate change, leading to droughts and floods and rampant food insecurity. In 2022, heavy rainfall led to a flood crisis affecting 313,000 people in the Far North region. The floods destroyed farming and livestock activities, leaving many families in extremely vulnerable situations. The Far North region is prone to recurrent epidemics such as cholera. These crises continue to force millions of people to move around the Far North region. By October 2022, violence had uprooted a total of 662,000 displaced people, returnees and refugees, an increase of 81,000 since October 2021. The mapping of Safe Spaces carried out by UNFPA in April 2023 in the Far North and updated in October 2023, shows that there are few of these facilities in areas of need, and that the majority do not meet minimum standards.

Gender-Based Violence (GBV) is one the most widespread human rights violations in the world. It affects women and girls disproportionally due to the underlying social injustice and power imbalance leading to gender inequality. Between January and October 2023, 1,599 incidents of GBV were reported to the GBVIMS specialist services. Sexual violence was reported in 13% of cases. It includes rape, sexual assault and forced marriages. 77% of IPV cases are also reported within couples, and 5% of child sexual abuse cases. Denial of resources/opportunities is reported by 45%, physical abuse by 23% and psychological violence by 20%.
The main activities will focus on sensitization and awareness raising for communities, emphasizing the participation of men and boys, strengthen referral and legal assistance mechanisms for internally displaced persons and host communities with legal protection needs (detention/documentation, GBV survivors etc.), provide basic vocational training and economic/Empowerment support to women and girls, Provide cash transfer assistance, build the capacity of operational organizations on the holistic response to GBV. UNFPA and partners will continue providing individualized case management and psychosocial support to survivors of GBV and other vulnerable people. Finally, UNFPA, in collaboration with the Ministry of Women Empowerment and the Family (MINPROFF), will also continue to reinforce close collaboration between actors and service providers involved in responding to the needs of women and girls.

project_name: Provision of timely intergrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services to the crisis -affected populations in South Sudan.
project_objective:
South Sudan is grappling with a profound health crisis driven by a combination of factors, encompassing climate change, protracted conflicts, inter-communal fighting, outbreak of infectious diseases and regional conflict. Thousands have been displaced within the country while the number of returnees from Sudan has exceeded 360,000 individuals of whom over 50 percent are women and girls. 
According to the Humanitarian Needs Response Plan (HNRP, 2023), 8.9 million individuals are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance. This assistance is particularly crucial in regions that have been severely affected by these challenges. The health cluster, in collaboration with its partners, has set ambitious goals to reach 3.2 million people with life-saving health services of whom 384,00 are women of reproductive age. This target population includes those internally displaced, refugees from neighbouring nations, and over half a million returnees from Sudan.
UNFPA and its implementing partners intend to reach this target population using two main objectives:
1)	Improve equitable access to comprehensive, quality health care services covering maternal, child, and adolescent health, as well as Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH). 
2)	Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen the recovery of the health system and coping mechanisms.
UNFPA through implementing partners will provide integrated quality services to 320,000 women of reproductive age, with 55,682 expected live births, among which 8,352 are anticipated to occur in health centres. Additionally, UNFPA will target 64,000 adults living with a sexually transmitted infection (STI). The full implementation of MISP and universal access to Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC) services is projected to avert 504 maternal deaths. 
In the course of the implementation, UNFPA will champion the delivery of the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) in acute emergencies and tailoring sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care to the specific needs of protracted crisis situations. The focus of this will revolve around the six key components of the MISP, which include (1) leading the coordination of MISP activities  at both the national/field level in collaboration with the Ministry of Health 2)prevention of sexual violence, and catering to the needs of survivors (3) preventing the transmission of and reduce morbidity and mortality due to HIV and other Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) (4) prevention of excess maternal and newborn morbidity and mortality (5) Prevention of unintended pregnancies and (6) Planning  for comprehensive SRH services.
The main interventions to achieve the project purpose include, among others:
1)	Delivering MISP services, which involve providing clinical management for rape for survivors of sexual violence, case management, psychosocial support (PSS) through individual and group counselling, HIV/STI prevention and treatment services, maternal healthcare services including antenatal, Labor, and postnatal care services, facilitating referrals for obstetric services, and increasing access to reliable contraception. These efforts will also encompass community health education and awareness campaigns.
2)	Procuring and distributing interagency reproductive health kits to ensure access to essential medical supplies.
3)	Enhanced management and coordination between humanitarian and development programs to aid the delivery of comprehensive services.
UNFPA and its implementing partners will also address the cross-cutting issues including inclusion of age and disability; mainstreaming protection and Gender-based Violence (GBV) including Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA); Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MPHSS); localization and community engagement.

project_name: Programa del IRC en Venezuela 2024
project_objective:
En el 2024, el IRC tiene previsto intensificar su respuesta humanitaria para abordar las necesidades críticas de las comunidades marginadas y vulnerables en áreas remotas y de difícil acceso, se atenderán aproximadamente 35,294 clientes. Con la experiencia acumulada desde 2018, en este año nos enfocaremos en reforzar las operaciones en Zulia, Lara, Falcón, Táchira, Apure y el Distrito Capital. En colaboración con ocho organizaciones civiles locales venezolanas involucrando feministas, defensores LGBTQI+ y minorías étnicas marginadas; continuaremos proporcionando servicios esenciales en áreas fronterizas y en la ruta migratoria del país.

 Nuestro enfoque se centra en las necesidades prioritarias y desatendidas de los más vulnerables, y en complementariedad con la oferta de cooperación. El énfasis serán servicios de Salud Primaria, Salud Sexual y Reproductiva, Seguridad Alimentaria, Nutrición, Educación en emergencia, Protección de la Niñez, y Protección y Empoderamiento de la Mujer; con un enfoque transversal de promoción a la diversidad, inclusión, igualdad de género, y Prevención y Protección contra la Explotación y los Abusos Sexuales. 

Particularmente en el Cluster de salud, el IRC gestiona la sensibilización comunitaria a partir de sesiones informativas que van orientadas según los servicios que se preste, tales como la difusión del conocimiento en planificación familiar, la identificación de ETS, las rutas de atención en un marco de 72 horas, la prevención y atención a la salud, y la promoción a lactancia materna. Cada metodología informativa tiene una duración entre 45 minutos a una hora que se adaptan a los marcos normativos internacionales. Así mismo, a través de una estrategia de localización, el IRC se enfoca en fortalecer las capacidades de los socios locales con mayor experticia y alcance en los servicios de salud, quienes tienen un relacionamiento directo con los establecimientos de salud y el personal sanitario. 

Ahora bien, en el Cluster de Protección, vale la pena aclarar que la Organización centrará sus esfuerzos para el 2024 en los servicios de apoyo individual y grupal, orientación comunitaria sobre rutas de protección, capacitaciones para fortalecer conocimientos en materia de derechos, igualdad de género y protección de NNA, y colaboración con la sociedad civil para capacitar en manejo clínico de violencia sexual y ka protección infantil. Se espera que estas acciones mejoren la situación de las personas atendidas al fortalecer su conocimiento sobre protección, prevenir riesgos, mitigar situaciones de violencia y fomentar un entorno más seguro y equitativo para todos los grupos atendidos.

Este año, también estamos dedicando esfuerzos significativos para ampliar la capacidad de respuesta de emergencia a desastres naturales recurrentes, como inundaciones, deslizamientos de tierra y avalanchas. Además, estaremos atentos a cualquier cambio en el contexto político y económico que podrían afectar la entrega de suministros médicos esenciales.

project_name: Upscaling of child protection services to children and their families affected by conflict and climate induced shocks in Renk, Maban and Akobo Counties.
project_objective:
Save the Children International intends to increase protective factors for boys, girls, adolescence, youths and women affected by conflict and climate induced shocks in Renk, Maban and Akobo counties of South Sudan. The proposed intervention will target most vulnerable children and families’ returnees and refugees affected by the Sudan and Ethiopia conflict and climate induced shocks in host communities and refugee camps. 

According to the Humanitarian Needs Overview, around 3.1 million children and adolescents face violence in South Sudan. The situation is currently compromised by the large number of the returnees and refugees coming into South Sudan with some integrated into host communities where there are pre-existing challenges of economic hardship and negative coping mechanisms which increase protection risks. From early 2023, South Sudan has been receiving an influx of returnees and refugees displaced by the ongoing conflict in Sudan and Ethiopia refugee camps. According to the OCHA (0ct, 2023), 341,967 people had been recorded crossing into South Sudan from Sudan since April 2023 due to the ongoing conflict. Of these, half of the arrivals are female and about half are children under age 18 with South Sudanese returnees accounting for 86% of all arrivals. In October, there was significant rise in the number of arrivals per day of up to 3800 individuals which was more than double the number received in previous months putting a resource constrain on the ongoing response.  On the other hand, shrinking response services and conflict between Anyuak and Nuer Ethnic groups in Gambella Region of Ethiopia forced South Sudanese who were once staying in Ethiopian refugee camps to return home. The local authority and RRC in Akobo County reported approximately more than 23, 000 returnees to have arrived in the county during April to August 2023 to the centers and the surrounding villages without any humanitarian assistance. With Maban being the main county supporting refugees, the numbers have been soaring due to the displacements with Save the Children child protection camp programming recording a total of 36, 829 households and 183, 112 individuals across all four refugee camps.

Pre-existing challenges in South Sudan inclusive of intercommunal conflicts and flooding increases child protection issues resulting in high numbers of unaccompanied and separated children caused by displacements and abductions, negative coping strategies such as child marriages, dropping out of school, child labour and joining armed groups among others. The influx of returnees and refugees escalates the situation increasing need for a strengthened protective environment of an already vulnerable population and the new populations. Save the Children  proposes to reach 28,983 beneficiaries (17,440 children (8,690 boys and 8,750 girls) and 11,543 adults (5,806 females and 5,737 males  through child protection in emergencies interventions inclusive of focused and non-specialized mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) using the HEART model to address trauma and distress; provision of case management services including cash based assistance, family tracing and reunification, alternative family care arrangements for unaccompanied and separated children and strengthening of referral pathways;  distribute dignity kits to vulnerable adolescent girls and women;  provision of recreation and PSS services in child friendly spaces, awareness raising sessions on norms and practices that perpetuate and violate violence against women and girls (VAWG), strengthening community-based child protection mechanisms and the social service workforce. SCI interventions aim to provide lifesaving interventions and where possible integrating with other sectors and defining linkages with other actors supporting the strengthening of child protection systems.

project_name: Promoción de los derechos y protección de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento y la movilidad humana
project_objective:
NRC fortalecerá los mecanismos de protección de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento, entendidas para esta propuesta como personas en situación de desplazamiento, solicitantes de asilo y personas con necesidades de protección internacional, deportadas con necesidades de protección y personas en tránsito con necesidades de protección. NRC ofrecerá tres tipos de servicios:  
El primero, centrado en asistencia legal, la gestión de casos y atención humanitaria inmediata. El segundo es enfocado en la instalación de capacidades de las instituciones locales, especialmente en la respuesta al desplazamiento y la seguridad en la tenencia de la vivienda, tierra y propiedad (VTP). También se contempla el monitoreo de protección con la finalidad de expedir documentos situacionales que sean de utilidad a las instituciones, las organizaciones civiles y humanitarias. El tercero centrado en contribuir al enfoque comunitario de autoprotección y resiliencia.
En el proyecto se contemplan las siguientes actividades: 
Manejo de casos: La gestión de casos de protección es un servicio estructurado para una persona en situación de alto riesgo de violencia. Lo presta un gestor de casos formado que trabaja con la persona para evaluar su situación de protección, desarrollar y aplicar conjuntamente un plan de acción completo, suele durar entre 3 y 10 meses, desde la admisión hasta el cierre. La gestión de casos de protección tendrá como objetivo mitigar y responder al daño causado por la OSV a partir del análisis de riesgos de protección. NRC adoptará un enfoque centrado en el cliente en la implementación de la gestión de casos, basado la centralidad de la protección en principios clave de confidencialidad y consentimiento informado, acceso significativo sin discriminación, no hacer daño, participación y empoderamiento, responsabilidad y autodeterminación. 

Asistencia de Protección Individual, IPA: Es una ayuda puntual o limitada en el tiempo, con un seguimiento limitado. Es específica, intencionada y diseñada para lograr un resultado de protección para el participante. La asistencia es tanto una acción de respuesta como de reparación.  Está vinculada a la prevención, reducción o mitigación de la exposición a los riesgos de protección, limitando los efectos de las violaciones en las víctimas. No es una intervención a largo plazo que busque soluciones duraderas, ni está diseñada para ayudar a la vulnerabilidad generalizada y a las necesidades básicas. La IPA abordará un riesgo de protección específico a través de una asistencia puntual con un seguimiento estrictamente limitado y por un período no superior a un mes desde la admisión hasta el cierre. 
 
Servicios legales: NRC, a través de un equipo legal especializado local, brindará información y asistencia legal para acceder a mecanismos de protección internacional, reconocimiento de estatus legal y obtención de documentación, incluida la identidad legal. Para solicitantes de asilo y refugiados, se ofrecerá información sobre el proceso, derechos y deberes, con acompañamiento durante la determinación de la condición de refugiado y obtención de documentación. En casos pertinentes, se proporcionará orientación sobre naturalización. Para personas desplazadas internamente o deportadas con necesidades de protección, NRC ofrecerá información sobre el derecho a la identidad legal, con orientación para obtener documentación civil e identidad. La identificación de casos se realizará mediante remisiones y jornadas en zonas fronterizas, abordando temas de protección internacional y riesgos. NRC cuenta con capacidad para servicios nacionales mediante atención telefónica y jornadas. En cuanto a la presencia en frontera, NRC mantiene relaciones con la Dirección de Migración y Extranjería, promoviendo el fortalecimiento de capacidades desde 2023. Los servicios tendrán alcance nacional, priorizando jornadas en zonas como La Hachadura, El Poy, Las Chinamas, San Cristóbal y El Amatillo.

project_name: Recuperación de la población afectada por desplazamiento forzado a través la provisión de servicios especializados de protección, el fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de autoprotección civil y la respuesta de protección nacional.
project_objective:
El proyecto propone contribuir a la respuesta de la situación de riesgo de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento forzado (IDPs, solicitantes de asilo, deportados y migrantes vulnerables) a través de líneas de trabajo:
1.	Manejo de casos: A través de un proceso estructurado y especializado, NRC compaña a las personas de interés en la mitigación de sus riesgos de protección debido a la violación de derechos con el fin de garantizar, y en última instancia, reclamar sus derechos, lo que conduce a un incremento de la seguridad, dignidad y a un fortalecimiento de la resiliencia. En este acompañamiento identifica necesidades humanitarias, mecanismos e intensidad del apoyo cash; como también la necesidad de acompañamiento legal en acceso a mecanismos de protección internacional (e.g. condición de refugiado) y reconocimiento de estatuto o estancia legal (e.g. protección subsidiaria, regularización migratoria, residencia, naturalización), a derechos de identidad legal (obtención de documento nacional de identidad, carnet de minoridad, acta de nacimiento, matrimonio, defunción, antecedentes penales, solvencias policiales) y a alternativas de seguridad de la tenencia de vivienda, tierra y propiedad (por ejemplo, confirmación de derechos de propiedad/uso, resolución colaborativa de disputas, legalización de herencia). 
2.	Incidencia en política pública: NRC continuará contribuyendo en la reglamentación de la ley de prevención y atención de desplazamiento, con mayor concentración en la respuesta estatal de la protección de los bienes abandonados y despojados.
3.	Autoprotección comunitaria: NRC priorizará comunidades con altos índices de violencia con acceso humanitario para implementar estrategias de autoprotección que disminuyan los riesgos de protección y aumenten la capacidad de resiliencia y tejidos comunitarios. En esta intervención se proponen intervenciones comunitarias mejoradas.

La población total a beneficiar es de 20,452 con 6780 beneficiarios directos.

project_name: Mécanisme de réponse rapide dans la province du lac Tchad - Phase 5
project_objective: Ce projet vise à répondre à la crise de déplacement en cours dans la province du lac Tchad, qui a été déclenchée par l'insécurité croissante depuis 2015 et le début d'un nombre croissant d'attaques par des groupes extrémistes violents. Ce projet vise à répondre aux besoins fondamentaux des communautés déplacées en matière de sécurité alimentaire, d'abris, de NFIs, de WASH et de protection pendant une période allant jusqu'à trois mois après leur déplacement. Le mécanisme de réponse rapide est conçu comme une première réponse aux besoins d'urgence suite aux déplacements dans la province. Il s'agit donc d'une première étape essentielle, non seulement pour répondre aux besoins urgents le cas échéant, mais aussi pour collecter des informations cruciales à des fins de plaidoyer et de coordination. Il s'inscrit dans le cadre plus large de la réponse humanitaire à la crise du lac Tchad et agit en collaboration avec les acteurs humanitaires et les autres parties prenantes concernées pour atténuer les dommages subis par les populations touchées.

project_name: Humanitarian Mine Action response supporting emergency, recovery and protection environment in South Sudan
project_objective:
DRC will deploy 2 highly Mobile Multi-Task Teams (MTTs) to respond to urgent threats to physical safety, dignity, freedom of movement and access to humanitarian assistance. Alongside this, DRC will deploy 6 (Explosive Ordnance Risk Education) EORE teams to provide Explosive Risk Ordnance Education to conflict or displacement affected communities to mitigate risks of explosive hazards and this will include new arrival of some South Sudanese returnees from Sudan. DRC will work with other sector responses, peacebuilding and development actors to ensure maximum socio- economic benefit of cleared land, and to strengthen the protective environment for affected populations. DRC will support both static and emergency responses with EORE, NTS and clearance activities. 

The proposed project aims at: 

• Providing immediate lifesaving assistance to address the urgent protection needs of the most vulnerable (including women, children, elderly, disabled and survivors of ERW in conflict) in hard-to-reach areas. 

• Enhancing prevention and preparedness programming to mitigate risks and strengthen resilience 

• Enabling durable solutions for IDPs and other affected populations  

 

Tasks that will support the humanitarian response in the country will be prioritized through the following key activities: 

Non-Technical Survey (NTS) and Technical Survey (TS) – NTS and will be conducted to target and prioritize clearance according to humanitarian need. Surveys will be conducted using a mixture of key informant interviews and household questionnaires held with the local population and authorities. NTS will determine the likely locations and density of ERW contamination in target locations, whilst assessing the impact of these hazards on vulnerable populations in any given location. TS (using detectors) will be used upon discovery of an area with a high concentration of explosive hazards. 

Manual Mine Clearance (MMC) / Battle Area Clearance (BAC) - the MTTs will be able to act as a MMC / BAC capacity, performing static clearance activities across larger, clearly defined areas (identified through the above data collection activities and technical survey as appropriate) or already recorded open Hazardous Areas in Information Management System for Mine Action (IMSMA) data.  

Explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) – once NTS has determined the nature of the threat, technical capacities within the teams will be deployed to remove and destroy identified hazards. 

Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) – all teams will contain a capacity to deliver risk messaging, to raise awareness about how to recognize dangerous items. The risk education will emphasize safe practices that should be followed, and high-risk behavior that should be avoided. 

Integration: DRC will work with economic recovery, HLP and other relevant responses to support individuals use land for socio- economic purposes. This involves stakeholder mapping, and where DRC has other activities, coordination on the integration of beneficiaries into existing programming.

project_name: Provision of quality WASH services for vulnerable communities living in Akobo, Kapoeta East, Budi, Abyei and Lafon.
project_objective:
In the proposed action, Save the Children aim to implement integrated WASH interventions to reduce the burden of WASH related diseases as aggravating factors for malnutrition locations presenting an extreme WASH vulnerability and high prevalence of malnutrition. Services provided will break the transmission cycle of main communicable diseases (i.e. diarrhea), thus improving food intake of malnourished children and contributing to the sustainability of health and nutrition. The proposed action will also seek to address WASH needs during emergencies such as response to floods, returnees and disease outbreaks. The proposed interventions will target WASH Cluster priority 1 and 2 counties of Akobo, and Kapoeta East, lafon, Abyei and Budi counties in which Save the Children has already established good operational presence.

The proposed WASH activities include; Distribution of Dignity/Hygiene kits among SAM/MAM children and caregiver families, hygiene promotion sessions conducted at Nutrition sites and catchment areas, construction /rehabilitation gender-disaggregated latrine facilities at nutrition site with consideration of People with Special Needs based on based on area analysis and if required, latrines constructed/rehabilitated as per WASH Cluster guidelines with flood resilient designs, construction /rehabilitation of water sources/boreholes at nutrition site and catchment areas with consideration of People with Special Needs based on based on area analysis and if required, water sources/boreholes will be constructed/rehabilitated as per WASH Cluster guidelines with flood resilient designs. water quality monitoring, safety audit for construction of borehole/handpump/water yard drilling/rehabilitation, mobile Sanitation Teams deployed to clear environment from faeces, dissemination of IEC material and using mass media for hygiene promotion, MHM kits distribution to IDPs and returnees distribution of WASH Emergency Kit (buckets, aquatabs, PuR Sachets, filter cloth and soap) during Emergency response Safe water sources developed (rehab/new) as per the WASH Cluster guidelines for flood resilient structures, barrier analysis conducted for disability inclusion, hygiene promotion and construction of latrines in communities using CLTS approach

Save the children targets a total of 33,333 beneficiaries (M: 5,667, F: 6,333, B: 10,666, G: 10,667) across the five counties. The estimated cost to deliver the proposed WASH interventions is USD 1,500,000.

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to vulnerable families in northwest Syria (NWS)
project_objective:
As of December 2023, 4.8 million IDPs reside in NWS, and more than 4.1 milion people in need. Access to essentials like safe water, food, medicine, healthcare, and livelihoods is limited. According to REACH Needs Assessment 2023, food and livelihood were reported as the top unmet needs by internally displaced persons (IDPs) and resident/host community members, with 43 per cent of households lacking income and work opportunities. Households in NWS more often reported that unemployment was a challenge in meeting basic needs.  

Food insecure households are also highly likely to adopt food-related coping strategies, including reducing the number of meals and the size of portions. Additionally, the ever-increasing prices of food and other necessities further compounds the vulnerability of households. The Cash Working Group (CWG) has reported that the price of the food component of the Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (SMEB) had increased by 40 per cent (NWS CWG REACH market monitoring, Feb 2024). 

IOM plans to implement the following activities:
1) Deliver emergency MPC to the most vulnerable to cover their most urgent needs immediately following a shock; and
2) Distribute regular MPC*to the most vulnerable households to meet a variety of basic needs and reduce reliance on negative coping strategies.

Beneficiaries will be selected based on vulnerability criteria from CWG. Based on the CWG’s recommendations, IOM will ensure through third party monitoirng (TPM) that the IPs follow 'No Harm' principles during the distributions. A rapid market capacity check shall be undertaken by the IP prior to each distribution to attest those targeted markets can absorb the demand for goods and replenish supplies. Three to four weeks after the distribution, PDM activities will be coordinated between the partner’s M&E unit and IOM’s TPM. 

IOM will use PTT to first transfer resources from Turkey to PTT offices in NWS, and then utilize a Financial Service Provider (FSP) to transfer the money to the chosen areas. Following CWG recommendations, cash assistance is provided in USD as standard. When USD notes are insufficient in quantity or quality, beneficiaries have the option to select the currency in which the remaining amount can be received.  

The distribution of cash assistance shall be organized in full by IPs with the announcement to beneficiaries, organization of the premises, registration, data control, distribution, accounting, and security staff. The role of the FSP’s transfer agent will be only to hand the money to the selected beneficiaries under supervision of the IP upon verification of identity by the IP.  

All IP staff are required to have undertaken training on PSEA and signed a PSEA Code of Conduct. Details of IOM’s AAP mechanism are communicated to participants, as well as the Interagency PSEA hotline where appropriate. Gender segregated lines and gender-mixed distribution teams are always used by IPs to further mitigate SEA risks. As IOM is the leading agency for PSEA, all programmes are required to follow the network’s recommendations and incorporate them into each project. 

In case of sustained insecurity and inaccessibility, IOM will be in regular communication with IPs to report any security incidents and conduct needs assessments to determine alternative locations. IOM also has a dedicated access unit that monitors and facilitates principled access for partners within Syria, and IOM will continue to participate in OCHA’s access working group. To mitigate the impact of inflation on cash recipients, IOM will conduct strong and constant market monitoring and will distribute USD to prevent currency devaluation. Additionally, there is the risk that beneficiaries will use cash for unintended purposes which IOM will mitigate by tailoring cash to SMEB needs and by raising awareness of the intended use of cash to beneficiaries during distributions.

project_name: Provision of Essential Humanitarian Health Services for People in Need in Sudan 2024
project_objective:
This project aims at increasing access to quality lifesaving and life-sustaining essential health services for vulnerable and needy population during humanitarian situations in Sudan, 2024.
The project is targeting Khartoum, Red Sea, Gedaref, Sennar, Blue Nile, White Nile, Gezira, North Darfur, West Darfur, Central Darfur, River Nile, South Kordofan. Humnaitarian access will be an issue in some conflict active zones. SCI will be jointly assessing the situations prior the implementation. SCI with new innovative mode of service delivery were able to collaborate and coordinate successfully with Community Medical Response Teams in Active conflict zone of Khartoum state. Such teams the have been incentivized by SCI. Indeed, they utilize these incentives to buy medicines and provide mobile services in areas where they live and can access. These CMRTs are well-trained and having medical specialists among them where supervision and monitoring might be of low concern to SCI due to their high commitment towards serving needy and hard-to-reach population. This delivery modalities could be replicated in similar settings where humanitarian access would be an issue. 
This project will strengthen health sector capacity to prevent, prepare for and deliver timely response to population affected by conflict, natural emergencies, disease outbreaks and pandemics. This will include a) procurement, prepositioning and rational use of essential medicines, basic medical equipment, laboratory equipment and supplies, PPE and strengthening capacity on rational use of drugs and supply chain management; b) building the capacity of healthcare providers and community health workers including volunteers on provision of maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health services, communicable and non-communicable diseases, referral healthcare services and vaccination services; c) integrating, expanding and maintaining effective disease surveillance system with early warning component including community-based surveillance for communicable and notifiable diseases while strengthening related response (IDSR) and health information system; d) strengthening the rapid response capacities to emergencies including setting up emergency health teams, supporting and training RRTs and case management capacity; e) improving health facility set-up to provide an acceptable quality of health services including the supply of water and power and basic needs of quality of care; f) supporting system for early referral of complicated cases; g) supporting community mobilization and participation, health education and preventive messages aiming at changing communities towards healthy behaviors. 
SCI will be prioritizing and collaboratively working with other partners such as WHO to respond to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. SCI Health sector in integration with protection sector will be able to provide counseling, awareness raising, and tailored services to victims including identified referral pathways within supported health facilities in addition to community-based services. Supported health facilities will be equipped with trained personnel to serve as focal points for SEAH services with joint supportive supervision to monitor the implementation and assess capacities.   
The project implementation plan will be detailed, implemented and monitored jointly with stakeholders including targeted communities at national and state levels and local health authorities. The project will be implemented over 12 months with estimated budget at$16,234,200.

project_name: Vulnerable school-age children, including CwDs are supported to access safe and equitable education in emergency services in, Aljazeera, Sinner, Central Darfur, Gedaref and river Nile states 2024
project_objective: The escalation of violence in April 2023 had forcibly displaced at least 3 million children and Over 19 million school-aged children are expected to stay out of school in the 2023–2024 academic year because of the displacement. Unpaid teachers, and schools’ infrastructure damage resulting from the conflict. This number includes 6.4 million school-aged children directly affected by the conflict. Children will continue to miss out on urgent psychosocial support, protection from physical threats, social-emotional learning, and recreational services. Lack of education will also increase protection risks for children, exposing them to the risk of early marriage, child labor, trafficking, forced recruitment, and GBV. Teacher shortages were prevalent because of salary instability, inadequate training, and a lack of capacity to cater to all children’s needs. SC through this one-year action purposefully designed in response to the above challenges and needs to contribute to the impact of the conflict in Central Darfur, Gadarief, Sinner, Aljazeera, and River Nile states and provide access to safe, inclusive, and quality education to newly displaced vulnerable, crisis-affected children and new returnees aged 6-18 years, as well as children at risk of dropping out, and ensure retention for girls and boys including (CWDs). The project aligns with the 2024 HRP strategic objectives and priorities by responding to sector objectives (1) and (2) through formal and informal education, this project is designed to target 630,000 school-aged children (50% Girls), of which 15% are CWDs. Activities include the provision of teaching and learning materials, recreational and hygiene kits accompanied with hygiene messages and waste disposal, provision of safe drinking water stations, establishment of temporary hand washing facilities, rehabilitation of damaged classrooms, and WASH facilities following the universal design to accommodate all vulnerable children, including CWDs. Teachers will be capacitated through teachers' training in psychosocial skills and will be aligned with CP subsector guidelines, which focus on the provision of teachers and children's well-being for a positive enabling environment. To ensure the continuation of education services and investment following the crisis, teachers will be incentivized through payments to continue teaching; the incentive payments will consider conflict sensitivity and promote safety, equity, and inclusion to avoid tensions that result from the influx of IDPs to host communities. This action will provide training for PTA members and teachers on safe school, GBV issues, MHPSS, the provision of social-emotional learning to the crisis-affected children, children’s rights, and violence-free learning spaces, the establishment of referral pathways to support the most vulnerable children and will relate to schools with a diversity of PSS services for the children. The selection of targeting states is based on accessibility, severity, and protection situations and aims for 100 percent coverage of the accessible states, 60 percent in partially accessible, and 30 percent in hard-to-reach areas when the security situation allows. This project will ensure inclusivity and equity considering equal access to boys, girls, and (CWDs) gender-appropriate needs of diverse needs of IDPs, host communities, and returnees.SC will follow a complementarity approach by building on the GPE program in Aljazeera, and ECHO in CD. The team will work in close coordination with UNICEF and other INGOs/NGOs during implementation to avoid duplication and create synergy and complementarity. SC will follow the conflict sensitivity approach throughout the project time frame and the selection of beneficiaries will consider the diversity of IPDs, and host communities.SC will partner with the State High Council of People with Disabilities to ensure that CWDs learning and well-being are adequately met.

project_name: Establishing and Supporting Learning Opportunities for Conflict affected Children in the NWSW
project_objective: Since 2016, the North West and South West regions of Cameroon have witnessed a socio-political crisis which has deteriorated overtime with violent clashes between armed forces and Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) which have led to loss of lives and property, internal displacement, attacks on education and a growing climate of fear and incertitude. Much of this violence is targeted at local communities and, in particular, at schools, with teachers frequently facing attacks in the form of kidnapping, harassment, decapitation and killing, while children have been exposed to a number of protection risks such as harassment, exploitation, abuse and recruitment and some have been killed due to the crisis. The NSAG have adopted school boycott/disruption strategy since 2017 to apply pressure on government in the form of Monday ‘ghost-towns’ and other spontaneous calls for ‘lockdowns’, especially on commemorated national days. The school boycott strategy has had a severe impact on children’s ability to attend school, learn and retain previously learnt content. Calls for a return to normal functioning of schools from different individual, national and humanitarian actors have been challenged by other separatist groups. In addition to the threats and direct acts of violence leading to school disruptions, other factors such as social media misinformation, false alarms and panic have led to the further disruption of school activities. The ongoing violence has affected some 1.3 million children and left more than 955,700 out of school in the Northwest and Southwest regions. As of October 2022, an estimated 54% of schools are not operational in both NWSW regions (Government Statistics, October 2022). On its part, the reaction by the international community has not been robust enough in terms of condemnation and action to ensure that the right to education is upheld. The Norwegian Refugee Council has referred to the crisis in Cameroon as one of the most neglected in the world. This research seeks to identify and provide an overview of all the converging factors leading to disruption of school activities, outline a timeline of school attacks, and provide an educational needs assessment for children of school going age in the Anglophone regions. It provides a brief background to what is now known as the Anglophone crisis, a timeline on attacks in schools and other factors including, social media misinformation, false alarms and panic, leading to further disruption of school activities. Around 7 million learners are currently affected by schools’ closure, of these an estimated 15% of children live in the NWSW region. In order to ensure education continuity and mitigate the impact of school closing, the Education Cluster has developed Education response plan in line with National response strategy that includes measures to mitigate the impact of school closure. These measures include adapting provision of e-learning, radio education and other alternative learning and well-being interventions. Plan International aligns the HPD strategies with the National response strategy, Education Cluster, the NWSW Education Cluster Response Annex and Plan Global Education COVID 19 Response considerations. Plan on the ground will coordinate and work closely with the WASH and Protection partners including Plan’s WASH, NFI and CPiE thematic areas, to ensure vulnerable girls and boys affected by the conflict and closure of schools and non-formal learning spaces, access education and minimize on the lost time for learning.

project_name: Providing an integrated protection and education response in the Far-North region of Cameroon
project_objective:
Considering the continuing deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the Far North regions, which
affect access to quality education and protection services, IRC in partner with DG ECHO proposes to
continue to implement an integrated protection approach base on the PEACE project lessons learned,
to Improve the well-being, resilience and learning environment of school-age girls and boys, the most
impacted by humanitarian crises in Cameroon's Far North region context.
. IRC offers an integrated approach to education and child protection, to improve the well-being,
development, safety and learning environment of school-age girls and boys while strengthening local
community-based services and child protection. IRC will work to ensure that the children 18,432 targeted
by this Action are safe in their schools and communities and receive support when they experience harm.
Through the programming of innovative activities initiated in the PEACE project, pupils in Koranic schools
will continue to have access to quality education in a safe and secure environment. IRC will integrate a
holistic localization approach into the Action through the formalization of a partnership with a local
organization with the capacity to reach the children and populations most affected by the crisis, including
providing psychosocial support, case management and community engagement interventions. Finally,
particular emphasis will be placed on coordination with state actors, especially in terms of the
implementation of Accelerated Learning Programme (ALP) activities, but also on supporting educational
actors to develop risk and disaster reduction plans in schools and learning institutions. Based on evidence
and aimed at improving access, quality and safety in education, the project aims to achieve the following
results:
- School-age girls and boys enroll in and attend safe, effective, and appropriate formal and non-
formal education programmes, supported by caregivers, communities, and local partners.
- School-age girls and boys receive support and access to protection services to reduce their
exposure to risk and improve their safety and access to education.

project_name: Client centered humanitarian response: Improving lives of crisis affected people in the North West and South West regions
project_objective: The IRC continues to expand its humanitarian support in the NW and SW regions, where the humanitarian situation will likely persist, if not worsen. The project will implement an integrated, adaptive programme responding to both the risks associated with crisis situations and underlying vulnerabilities, aligned with our SAP and the HRP/HNO. We will continue lifesaving programming centred around crisis-affected population’s protection and basic needs, combining direct service delivery, support to existing services and partners, multi-purpose cash assistance, access to essential services and referrals. IRC will ensure that protection needs of people affected by human rights violations, gender-based violence (GBV) and child protection issues are addressed whilst local capacities are strengthened for a safer and more protective environment. IRC will support the most vulnerable households to meet their economic wellbeing and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) needs, with the cash modality weaved throughout when feasible, in order to avoid harmful coping strategies, and support their capacity to face shocks. IRC will continue to identify the most vulnerable to health challenges and provide health support assistance through referrals as well as building community awareness on SRH issues. The project will continue to target the most vulnerable and hard to reach populations, including internally displaced populations (IDPs), returnees and host communities; in particular the most at-risk including victims of human rights violations, GBV survivors, women and girls, children (girls and boys) at risk of violence, abuse and neglect, persons with disability, elderly and other vulnerable people at particular risk of protection. The flexibility of the funding will enable us to respond to the most urgent needs will support us with increased access and reach through deepening community engagement, capacity building with frontline staff, key stakeholders engaged with programming and scaling up our partnership strategy. IRC will continue build upon operational and programmatic learning from utilising the flexibility of the PBA, which has in the past few years enabled the IRC to quickly respond to outbreaks (such as cholera outbreak in the SW in May 2022), to start crucially needed child protection activities in the SW – which we have now been able to scale up through other funding in the NW. We will continue to support and empower communities to better analyse the risks they face, and to develop their own strategies to reduce exposure to and mitigate the effects of these risks.

project_name: Respuesta Humanitaria a Grupos Vulnerables Afectados por el Deterioro de sus medios de Vida en el Sur de Honduras.
project_objective:
El proyecto es una respuesta inmediata a las brechas generadas por la convergencia de los diferentes efectos provocados por el cambio climático y otras crisis en el Sur del Corredor Seco de Honduras. Para ello integra de manera complementaria actividades de agricultura sostenible, recuperación de medios de vida, y de prevención y promoción de buenas prácticas de alimentación.
Las diferentes y concurrentes emergencias humanitarias suscitadas recientemente en Honduras afectaron los medios de vida, la capacidad de recuperación temprana, y la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de muchas familias. Esta afectación se visibilizó de manera aguda en los municipios del corredor seco y del norte de este país. Dentro de estos municipios, grupos especialmente vulnerables como las mujeres y niñas, personas con discapacidad, jóvenes y personas de la tercera edad, en áreas urbanas y rurales enfrentan mayor pobreza, desempleo, carga de trabajo de cuidados no remunerados, y mayor riesgo de tener niveles de desnutrición aguda.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo contribuir a restablecer los medios de vida de las familias afectadas por la secuencia de fenómenos climáticos adversos. Esto, con un enfoque de equidad de género e inclusión de mujeres, jóvenes, personas de la tercera edad, personas con discapacidad y niños. Las actividades propuestas por el proyecto están alineadas con el objetivo sectorial 1,2 y 4 del clúster de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional.
