project_name: Projet sur la prévention et de la prise en charge intégrée de la violence basée sur le genre dans les districts sanitaires de Makary, Mada et Fotokol dans le département de Logone et chari au Cameroun.
project_objective:
Ce projet vise à réduire la prévalence des violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et à améliorer la prise en charge des victimes dans les districts sanitaires de Makary, Mada et Fotokol, situés dans le département de Logone et Chari au Cameroun. Le projet s’intéresse à quatre éléments ou résultats pour atteindre les objectifs assignés : 
Renforcement de la prise en charge médicale des victimes de VBG : Des formations seront dispensées au personnel médical pour détecter, traiter et documenter les cas de VBG. Des centres de soins spécialisés seront également mis en place, équipés de matériel et de médicaments appropriés. 
 Amélioration de la prise en charge de la santé mentale ou psychosociale des victimes de VBG : Les travailleurs sociaux et les professionnels de la santé mentale seront formés pour fournir un soutien psychosocial aux victimes de VBG. Des centres de soutien psychologique seront mis en place pour offrir des conseils et un soutien adéquat. 
Distribution de kits de dignité aux victimes de VBG : Des kits de dignité contenant des articles d'hygiène personnelle, des vêtements propres et d'autres articles essentiels seront élaborés et distribués aux victimes de VBG identifiées dans les communautés locales. 
Prévention de l'exploitation et des abus sexuels : Des sessions de sensibilisation seront organisées dans les écoles, les communautés et les organisations locales pour informer sur les droits des femmes et des filles, ainsi que sur les dangers de l'exploitation sexuelle. Des mécanismes de signalement et de suivi des cas d'exploitation et d'abus sexuels seront également mis en place. Ce projet mettra en œuvre des stratégies d'intervention telles que la coopération avec les autorités locales, les organisations non gouvernementales et les acteurs de la société civile. Il prévoit également une sensibilisation régulière des communautés, la collaboration avec le système de justice et la coordination avec les services sociaux et les organisations de protection de l'enfance. L'objectif général de ce projet est de contribuer à la réduction des VBG dans les districts sanitaires de Makary, Mada et Fotokol, en garantissant une prise en charge médicale et psychosociale adéquate aux victimes, en soutenant leur dignité et en prévenant l'exploitation et les abus sexuels.La politique de lutte contre les VBG chez ALIMA s'aligne à la stratégie nationale de VBG 2022-2026.

project_name: SNFI support to most vulnerable IDPs in northern Syria
project_objective:
Project Summary:
The project responds to the urgent winter needs of 8086 households in Idlib and Aleppo governorates, prioritizing vulnerable groups. With a total individual target of 40430 persons, It focuses on providing shelter assistance and upgrading sites to mitigate flood damages, particularly for households headed by females, children, persons with disabilities, or the elderly. Special attention is given to recently displaced individuals and those in overcrowded conditions.

Activities include:
1. Winterization assistance: Providing heating materials to 6,068 families, prioritizing vulnerable households, both in and out of camps.
2. Rehabilitation of household-level shelter units: Renovating 99 damaged houses to improve safety and privacy, targeting vulnerable areas.
3. Construction of 818 HH dignified shelters: Building concrete units in targeted districts for IDPs, with infrastructure improvements.
4. Distribution of 1,101 HH core NFIs: Providing essential items in selected villages and camps.

Needs:
After 12 years of conflict and earthquakes, there's increased demand for shelter and NFIs, with 8.6 million in need of shelter support and 2.6 million requiring NFI support. Economic conditions worsen, driving displacement and reliance on humanitarian aid.

Implementation:
Activities will be implemented systematically, including assessments, beneficiary verification, and distribution. Renovations and constructions will adhere to SPHERE standards and vulnerability criteria, ensuring inclusivity and quality. Regular monitoring will ensure effectiveness.

Protection Risk Analysis:
Risks include conflicts among beneficiaries, inclusion errors leading to exploitation, mistreatment of beneficiaries, and safety concerns around infrastructure. Mitigation strategies involve community engagement, staff training, and consultation with vulnerable groups.

PSEA Strategy:
IR Syria field offices adhere to PSEA policy, ensuring staff awareness and establishing mechanisms for feedback and complaints handling. Special attention is given to potential incidents related to gender-based violence and child protection.

Risks, Assumptions, and Mitigating Measures:
Risks include funding shortfall, resource burden, insecurity, political instability, and weather instability. Assumptions include cooperation with local partners and authorities. Mitigation measures involve continuous financial assessment, market monitoring, enhanced security, and strategic implementation in stable areas.

project_name: Contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie, au respect de la dignité des populations vulnérables affectées par les crises humanitaires dans la province du Lac Tchad et au renforcement de leurs capacités à y faire face.
project_objective:
L'AICRL et la CRT répondent aux besoins urgents des populations nouvellement déplacées (2022- 2023) et celles précédemment installées (2021- 2022) suite aux incidents sécuritaires dans la province du Lac. L’action a pour but de couvrir les besoins primaires en abris, eau et assainissement de 2233 ménages déplacés (11 165 personnes) installées à Kalgalawa et Acétchou, proche de Liwa. A court terme, l’action contribuera à la survie et la protection des plus vulnérables sur les sites de Kalgalawa, Wargana, Ngorgoua et Acétchou (2023- 2024)  et sur les sites de Biodou Limboye et Bibi Barrage (2024-2025). A plus long terme, renforcer leurs capacités de relèvement. Le projet vise ainsi à fournir 2233 kits d’abris complétés de kits outils, 224 latrines d'urgence de qualité (1 latrine pour 50 ménages) et 8 forages équipé de PMH et 2 forages à énergie solaire, en un maximum de 24 mois. La participation communautaire, la protection de l’environnement; et la promotion de la cohésion sociale et la paix seront transversales dans notre action de réponse.
Pour s’adapter au fait que les PDIs ont de plus en plus tendance à rester au moyen/long terme sur leurs sites de déplacement, le projet propose une adaptation à l’abri d’urgence classique et évolutif, en y ajoutant une fondation et un soubassement. La composante un abri- deux arbres, le renforcement de capacités des communautés sur la régénération Naturelle Assistée (RNA) et la confection des foyers améliorés traditionnels en 2024-2025 sur les sites de Bodou Limboye et Bibi Barrage.
Concernant le financement, en plus de DG ECHO, AICRL soumettra au MAEE un projet en synergie d’action avec cette proposition et dans les sites de projet.

project_name: Access to essential preventive and curative child health services in humanitarian context
project_objective: UNICEF will implement the HRP 2024 through the Health Cluster approach, through integrated and multisectoral response to address the needs of most vulnerable children, children with disabilities, adolescents, and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). UNICEF will work in close coordination with Health and Nutrition partners to deliver essential health services, supporting lifesaving for populations affected by the conflict, providing essential commodities, strengthening systems and building technical capacity of (CHWs, APEs, ACSs, Activists).

project_name: Humanitarian WASH Response to Northern Conflict Crisis
project_objective:
UNICEF is dedicated to collaborating with government entities, the private sector, international and local non-governmental organizations to deliver a comprehensive package of Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This collaboration aims to provide essential WASH services, items, and facilities to vulnerable displaced populations in camps and host communities as well as returnee zones, prioritizing critical services to prevent disease transmission.
This project includes ensuring access to life-saving WASH services for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) residing both in camps and host communities aiming to mitigate the impact of IDP influx on already strained WASH services in host communities, emphasizing the importance of transitioning from short-term relief to sustainable, resilient solutions that consider present and future climate impacts and support WASH in health care facilities and learning environments. The project also will work towards strengthening local capacities in operation and maintenance of WASH infrastructure.
Assistance to returnees focuses on reconstructing pre-existing water and sanitation infrastructure while promoting appropriate hygiene practices. During disease outbreaks, particularly Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) and Cholera, UNICEF promptly responds by providing life-saving WASH services and supplies, closely coordinating efforts with the health sector.
An integral part of the strategy involves gender mainstreaming, with a special focus on Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and risk mitigation. This emphasis is geared towards ensuring the safety and resilience of girls and women through the provision of inclusive and gender-sensitive water, sanitation, and hygiene services. Inclusion mainstreaming will include provision of access to WASH services for people with disabilities.
As WASH sector lead, UNICEF will support to identifying gaps, advocating effectively, responding promptly to critical needs, establishing robust monitoring and evaluation, and fostering knowledge management processes.

project_name: Prompt detection and response to Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) outbreaks in areas prone to cyclones and tropical storms in Mozambique
project_objective:
The major goal is to protect vulnerable people from disease outbreaks by quickly detecting and responding to Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) outbreaks. This will largely focus on provinces that have previously been hit by climatic disasters such as cyclones and tropical storms, as well as an increase in the number of Acute Watery Diarrhoea and Cholera Outbreaks.
This will be accomplished through working jointly with  SPS/DPS to effectively improve the current weak coordination and leadership for AWD and cholera response, guide in developmental and use of comprehensive multi-sectoral response plans at the provincial level .The project will focus on enhancement of community health surveillance to ensure timely detection and response to outbreaks. 
This project also aims to promote the use of rapid test kits for suspected cholera cases, which are currently underutilized. In addition, work with the departments of Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), health logistics, and Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) to put together rapid response teams from several sectors. This goal will be met by executing a capacity-building for health team aimed primarily at improving disease surveillance and laboratory pillars. Forums will be held to enable for the exchange of information on the most effective methods for enhancing disease surveillance and response, including use of laboratory protocols.

project_name: Respuesta integrada de servicios especializados de Protección de NRC que reducen y mitigan el impacto del conflicto armado colombiano sobre personas desplazadas internas y comunidades afectadas por el mismo, permitiéndoles satisfacer necesidades urgentes, acceder a mecanismos de protección, disfrutar de sus derechos básicos y alcanzar soluciones duraderas.
project_objective:
Los proyectos de Protección de NRC involucran el trabajo de dos equipos, por un lado, servicios especializados de protección y, por el otro lado, servicios de asistencia legal. 

Los proyectos de Protección contra violencia de NRC buscan reducir y mitigar el impacto de la violencia y el conflicto sobre individuos y comunidades expuestas al conflicto armado interno colombiano; inclusive riesgos de protección como amenazas, asesinatos, desplazamiento forzado, confinamiento, explotación, extorsión, robo, violencia basada en género, riesgos de minas y reclutamiento, uso y utilización por grupos armados. 

Las actividades de Protección contra violencia miran a prevenir la violencia antes de que ocurra, mientras se contribuye a la restauración de la seguridad para comunidades e individuos en riesgo. Se logra este resultado asegurando que los individuos sobrevivientes de violencia tengan recursos y capacidades de enfrentamiento mejoradas, aumentando la resiliencia y capacidad de mitigación frente a los riesgos de comunidades expuestas, fortaleciendo políticas públicas que protejan los individuos más vulnerables, y mejorando las capacidades de respuestas de instituciones y autoridades. 

Las actividades incluyen servicios individuales especializados de protección como gestión de casos y asistencia inmediata de protección, acompañamiento protectivo y apoyo psicosocial individual estructurado; acciones de autoprotección civil que incluyen mapeo de los riesgos dirigidos por las comunidades, aumento de capacidad en protección para miembros de comunidades, diseño y fortalecimiento de estrategias de autoprotección civil, asesoría y acompañamiento a las comunidades; actividades de fortalecimiento de entornos, incluyendo monitoreo y análisis de protección, protección por incidencia, y fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de coordinación de protección. Las actividades incluyen también intervención en contextos de emergencias como desplazamientos masivos, confinamientos, desastres naturales e incluyen evaluación rápida de necesidades de protección, asistencias de protección inmediata, entrenamientos en protección para líderes y lideresas, campañas de comunicación y talleres de manejo de estrés durante emergencias. 

En línea con la Estrategia de Protección de NRC, y dentro del contexto de respuesta a las dinámicas del conflicto armado en Colombia , el programa de protección se enfocará en personas afectadas por violencia, coerción y deprivación deliberadas con un énfasis particular en líderes y lideresas comunitarias, sociales y ambientalistas; comunidades expuestas a riesgos de protección como desplazamiento forzado, restricción de movilidad, confinamientos, amenazas, homicidios, violencia física y psicológica; individuos sobrevivientes o en riesgo de violencia, abuso, explotación, deprivación. 

Las intervenciones de protección contra violencia se priorizarán para los grupos más vulnerables como líderes/as sociales y defensores de derechos humanos, miembros de comunidades rurales, comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas, mujeres y comunidad LGBTQI+. 

Con respecto a la respuesta por parte de ICLA, las personas desplazadas internas recibirán gestión de casos legales a través de la información, orientación y asistencia legal para acceso al registro de víctimas, acceso a derechos y servicios esenciales como educación y salud, acceso a identidad legal y regularización migratoria en el caso de las personas refugiadas y migrantes afectadas por el conflicto armado, acceso a derechos de vivienda tierra y propiedad y acceso a derechos de empleo. Esto a través de los servicios implementados en territorio a través del Contact Centre, atención en oficinas, espacios protectores, clínicas móviles y actividades de intervención con enfoque comunitario. Adicional, facilitaremos asistencia técnica y capacitación a entidades públicas y otras organizaciones, para el fortalecimiento integral en el territorio.

project_name: Strengthened Child Protection programme for the children of Rohingya Community and Host Community in Cox's Bazar
project_objective:
UNICEF will prevent and respond to all forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect of children, including GBV. Will reach 182,965 beneficiaries of whom 101,515 children and adolescents, and 81,450 adults. Women and girls will constitute 60 % of beneficiaries and persons with disabilities 11 %. While 70% of the project target will be of Rohingya refugee camps and 30 % host communities. UNICEF will cover 16 camps (4, 4 Ext, 8 E, 8W, 9,11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 20 Ext, 22, 24) following a 50% coverage approach in line with rationalization.  Will engage gender transformative programming to prevent exposure to violence and support children affected by or are at risk of violence. Department of Social Services as lead government department will deliver case management services in 31 camps. DSS presence across the camps is significant towards localizing child protection efforts and fostering greater sustainability across the humanitarian-development nexus. 
UNICEF will follow a public health approach to child protection that prioritizes prevention and ensures interventions are rights-based and value for money. Interventions will Do No Harm and be in the Best Interests of the Child and based on robust needs analysis.  Will strengthen child protection systems as illustrated in the socio-ecological model . Support government to lead and scale-up presence in the Rohingya response. DSS is responsible for implementing overarching social welfare programmes in Bangladesh to enhance the quality of life. DSS is one of the first government agencies present in the camp and providing services for the children. Partnership with DSS contributing to establish community-based child protection mechanisms, strengthen capacities of social workers and deliver case management.  UNICEF will support DSS with more social workers for case management and on government leadership within the Child Protection sub-sector for better coordination in the response . 
UNICEF will invest in multi-sector coordination of judges, police, probation officers,  and community-based structures for a comprehensive continuum of care for children. Continue working with the Office of the Deputy Commissioner to accelerate Birth Registration through BDRIS .
Key elements of this endeavor along with strengthening social service workforce, reinforcing case management, will be provide comprehensive package of services through MPCs with outreach services. Through a blend of approaches along with Child Protection Facilities i.e. 76 Multipurpose centers essential lifesaving child protection services will be continued for children, parents and caregivers in an integrated manner. 
UNICEF will ensure child survivors and those at-risk of violence have access to case management and CPIMS+, care plans and referrals. Family-based alternative care will be promoted. The social service workforce will collaborate with CBCPCs to ensure a robust continuum of care for children. Access to structured and unstructured MHPSS for recovery and resilience will be extended for children. Parents and caregivers will be supported with knowledge and skills emphasizing positive parenting and nurturing environments. Children aged 10-18 will have access to Life Skills sessions and engage as agents of changes in their communities. UNICEF will strengthen the community-based child protection mechanisms through CBCPCs to identify child protection risks and work together to find appropriate solutions in the best interests of the child.  Also, will be empowered through training, mentoring and access to resources.
UNICEF will embrace its role as a lead agency in the Child Protection Sub-Sector Strategic Advisory Group, Protection Working Group, Case Management Technical Working Group, and other coordination forums for close collaboration with Government, NGOs, Civil Society, and private sector. UNICEF will also support organizational development of government counterparts and implementing partners.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Education Services to Palestine Refugee School Children in Syria
project_objective:
In 2024, UNRWA will continue to deliver basic, quality and inclusive education to 51,000 Palestine refugees through 104 schools managed by the Agency across Syria, of which 40 are running a double-shift in buildings on loan from the Ministry of Education (MoE) to compensate for UNRWA schools that have been destroyed or severely damaged by the conflict.
UNRWA, through its Education in Emergencies (EiE) programme helps to ensure that Palestine refugee children can continue to access education, even in times of emergencies, and facilitate linkages between the school and the community through PTA platforms. The UNRWA approach to EiE involves "doing things differently" (delivering education in alternative ways), "doing more of other things" (more PSS to children) and "doing things that had not been the focus before" (safety and security training for students, staff and parents).
In 2024, UNRWA will provide back-to-school kits (including school bags) at the beginning of the next school year (2024/25) to all 51,000 students; stationery will be procured and provided to students at the beginning of the 2024/2025 academic year to alleviate some of the economic burden faced by parents. 
UNRWA will also provide (1) catch-up classes for 17,500 students including including for Grade 9 students to help them prepare for their official end-of-school exams as well as (2) summer recreational programmes for 12,000 UNRWA students where PSS, together with educational activities, will provide them with the opportunity to address learning gaps while sharing experiences and forging friendship with their peers.　UNRWA will also provide transportation (contracted buses) for students from the destructed Ein el Tal camp and Senaya to take them to schools in nearby areas. 
The Agency will continue to provide PSS to address anxiety, stress and trauma caused by years of conflict and deteriorating socioeconomic conditions. Psychosocial counsellors will be deployed in all Agency schools to provide individual and group counselling and support to students and teachers. This is to address the emotional toll associated with: (i) the conflict; (ii) socio-economic crises; (iii) natural disasters, including the 2023 earthquakes; and (iv) the effects of bullying, low self-esteem and other concerns which, if not addressed, may lead to school drop-outs and other societal issues. 
A number of training sessions will be conducted for teachers and school principals on topics such as GBV, child protection and addressing violence against children (AVAC). Similar training sessions will be delivered to parents through the PTAs, which will continue to play a pivotal role in developing a holistic approach to education for Palestine refugees. 
UNRWA will also aim to rehabilitate one school and conduct minor repairs of 74 UNRWA school facilities that require urgent maintenance. 

As an international relief and human development agency and in order to further effective service delivery, UNRWA requires high standards of accountability, transparency and refugee participation, in line with its protection mainstreaming principles. In this regard, the Agency has committed to establish and use feedback and complaint mechanisms as valuable means to: (a) further working partnerships with Palestine refugees, (b) incorporate refugee feedback into programme delivery; and (c) secure early detection and community response to issues of importance to the population served.

Lastly, this action contributes to the achievement of all three strategic objectives under HRP 2024-2025 as all three of Education Sector's objectives (objective 1 - availability & access, objective 2 - quality, and objective 3 - resilient systems).
M&E data on student enrollment, school attendance, students reached with PSS counseling will be recorded in Agency’s online Education Management Information System and in the Agency's Result Based Monitoring System. Data will also be reported externally to the Syria HRP’s 4Ws system.

project_name: Provision of Lifesaving SRHR services for most vulnerable and in-need population, Sudan, 2024
project_objective:
In addition to the ongoing war, the country remains prone to various risks and hazards such as floods, inter communal violence, displacement, climatic shocks, disease outbreaks, food insecurity, malnutrition, protection risks and deteriorating economic status, leading to an increased risk of unintended pregnancies, sexual violence, STIs including HIV, and complications which often imply mortality and/or long-term serious health problems from pregnancy and childbirth for millions of women and girls. In Sudan, girls and women face substantial gender inequalities that increase their vulnerability. The presence of armed actors, economic hardship, resource shortages continue to exacerbate the risk of GBV, sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and negative coping mechanisms, including survival sex. Poor women feel compelled to become sex workers increasing their vulnerability to violence, abuse and poor health outcomes including unsafe abortion and HIV risk. People living with disabilities face additional concerns and challenges in this unstable environment. Maternal Mortality remains a key issue affecting women of reproductive age across Sudan with a high maternal mortality rate (270 per 100,000 live births as per 2020 UN estimates). In reference to Sudan Maternal death surveillance and Response (MDSR) reports, the most prevalent cause was Obstetric hemorrhage, followed by hypertensive disorders then sepsis. The functionality of MDSR was significantly affected after 15 April clashes resulting in staff forced displacement with poor communication network combined with loss of reports and assets. EMONC coverage was already low prior to the conflict, with only 43% of needs covered. This figure is expected to be much lower due to the ongoing conflict and its consequences. Capacities of the community midwives were identified as low and further deteriorated as midwives are operating with limited access to commodities and supplies; while some of them were forced into displacement due to insecurity further impacting the service coverage in conflict affected locations. Responding to the health needs of survivors of SGBV remains challenging due to limited access to (CMR) services with only 23% of the previously identified facilities are still able to deliver, and even where services are available, it can be life-threatening to physically access these services due to ongoing hostilities. Sudan HNO 2024 indicates total of 24.8M will need humanitarian assistance. Health cluster indicated 14.7M in need of health intervention, it is estimated that out of them 3.5M are women at reproductive age in need of humanitarian assistant, including 351,312 pregnant women
UNFPA will target 980K using the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for SRH aiming at reducing SRH mortalities and morbidities through: functioning coordination mechanisms and MDSR system, timely provision of Emergency Obstetric care and save delivery services, timely referral to lifesaving services, support the availability of Family Planning services, improving Clinical management of rape for survivors of SGBV, availing HIV and STIs prevention and response, dissemination of awareness-raising material on positive health seeking behavior including prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and reporting mechanisms, improving Antenatal and postnatal care, Post abortion care, and prevention and response of obstetric fistula. The stock of IARH kits currently available in port Sudan and in the pipeline will boost the continuation of the provision of SRH services covering over 10 M population
The geographical coverage follows the HNO identified locations with severity ranking Four and Five. Intervention will be implemented through government partners and NGOs (CAFA, SRCS, CDF, NIDO, SFPA, NEF, ALIGHT, NCA, HAI, PHF) in close coordination with the relevant partners in the National and state levels SRH working groups to avoid duplication in addition to effectiveness and efficiency.

project_name: Provision of Onward Transport and Cash Assistance to Returnees Affected by Sudan Crisis
project_objective:
The outbreak of fighting in Sudan on April 15, 2023, has triggered a devastating humanitarian crisis in neighboring South Sudan, particularly in the country's northern states. Since the onset of the conflict, a massive influx of people fleeing Sudan has overwhelmed the border points between the two countries, primarily in Upper Nile, Northern, and Western Bahr el Ghazal States. As of November 22, 2023, over 394,006 individuals have crossed the border, with the majority entering through the Wunthow border point in Upper Nile, seeking refuge from the ongoing violence.

 Since the start of the Sudan crisis, IOM has facilitated over 118,000 returnees with Onward Transportation Assistance. In 2024, IOM seeks to assist an additional 150,000 returnees with OTA assistance so that they can reach their final destinations.  Onward transportation assistance is a critical component of the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and will be facilitated by IOM via river, air, and road to ensure that returnees reach their final destinations safely and securely. IOM will also provide protection and basic needs assistance to South Sudanese returnees at transit and reception locations, offering multi-modal transportation options to their final destinations. Additionally, IOM will support local authorities providing transportation to returnees and collaborate closely with them to facilitate the onward movement from border crossing points to transit locations and onwards to final destinations. Cash assistance will be provided to returnees to help cover last-mile transportation costs from state capitals to their final destinations.

IOM will continue to conduct rapid vulnerability screenings in order to identify and register the most vulnerable people at points of entry (PoE) and ascertain their voluntariness to return to their areas of origin or intended destination (if different from area of origin) and thereafter facilitate OTA. Prior to provision of movement assistance, protection safeguards through provision of specialized protection interventions will be undertaken for individuals with heightened protection needs, risks and vulnerabilities including unaccompanied children and victims of violence, exploitation, and abuse.

project_name: Targeted support to persons with specific needs with lifesaving non-food items and emergency shelter to displaced population in hard-to-reach areas, Refugees Returnees (sudan Situation) and IDPs returnee families.
project_objective:
In 2024, the South Sudanese returning home due to Sudan situation are facing serious challenges in terms of shelters, NFIs while at the same time Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) continue to face multi-faceted crises due to conflicts and protracted displacement from locations of their habitual residence.Since 16th April 2023, a total of 326,11 South Sudanese individuals (73,731 HHs) have been returned at several entry points along the border among Sudan and South Sudan.
Reference :UNHCR IOM joint dashboard  ,endorsed by RRC- https://app.powerbi.com/view?r=eyJrIjoiZTMwNTljNWYtYmVhYi00ZGI2LTgwYzAtN2UyNDZmZTRlNjBkIiwidCI6IjE1ODgyNjJkLTIzZmItNDNiNC1iZDZlLWJjZTQ5YzhlNjE4NiIsImMiOjh9&pageName=ReportSection95859b8850a76994e6fb
The project also aim to support the affected refugees coming from Sudan and will address their Shelter and NFIs needs with an overall allocation of USD 1 million.

 Flooding and climate changes impacts is another challenge which aggravating the situation for humanitarian response and the communities.  Displaced and the recent refugees’ returnees from Sudan often have inadequate shelter and household goods which expose them to heightened protection risks. Increased mobility, continued insecurity and protracted displacement has over the years eroded household coping mechanisms and livelihood options especially considering the poor nature of local markets without stocks for household goods and shelter materials.

UNHCR’s project will focus on responding to the humanitarian needs of IDPs and refugee returnees with targeted and protection focused core relief items (emergency shelter and non-food items – S/NFIs) prioritizing the most vulnerable households and persons with specific needs especially women and girls.

The project will contribute to the following sectoral objectives:

SO 1 – percentage of the targeted population that is able to access shelter material and non-food items in situations of emergency and transition.
The project will identify the most vulnerable IDPs and returnees through protection monitoring and assessments including through RMS,IRNAs and RRMs. The assessments and inter cluster discussions will inform the decisions regarding the specific response modalities between in kind and cash assistance. Unique contextual factors including market conditions will be considered.

SO 2 - Enhance community dignity and engagement in the provision of S/NFI services. The project will deliver timely lifesaving activities while streamlining protection-oriented initiatives. The project will strengthen community-based protection through the involvement of community-based structures for self-management in response delivery, ensuring that their capacities to cope, recover, contribute to and achieve solutions are enhanced.

SO 3 - Community members’ exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures.

In 2024, UNHCR will increase its active participation in humanitarian coordination forums, including the ES/NFI cluster, both at national level and in the field, strongly advocating for protection mainstreaming and joint vulnerability assessments, the results of which will be very useful in the optimization of the limited resources. UNHCR will endeavor to provide timely response to the most critical identified needs of vulnerable IDPs and Refugees returnees, among other affected populations. Protection risks remain high among women, girls, boys and persons with specific protection needs which may include transitional shelters and other material assistance.

project_name: Food and cash assistance to meet increasing and critical levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan
project_objective:
The main objective of the project is to meet the lifesaving food requirements of the most vulnerable, food and nutrition insecure people in South Sudan, including IDPs living in Rubkona POC and Malakal ex-POC, recent returnees from the Sudan crisis and protracted and new caseload of refugees (from Sudan crisis). A second objective is to ensure that boys and girls in the most marginalised and acute food insecure areas have access to quality education and receive safe, nutritious school meals to improve school attendance and eventually their education outcomes. Finally, WFP will provide an integrated package of health and nutrition support to malnourished children under 2, pregnant women and girls and new mothers living in these same areas where access to health and nutrition services and education is severely limited.
WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP field offices and implemented by cooperating partners. WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.
Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (light resilience- building activities, peace/conflict resolution training also called GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with FAO and their cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. 
The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from agricultural training, or sensitisation on peaceful resolution of conflicts, nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment.  WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Asset Creation and Livelihoods (ACL) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace through strengthened social cohesion and community structures and collaboration with local authorities and peace actors.

project_name: Provision and Management of WASH Core Pipeline Supplies for Emergency Preparedness and Response in South Sudan
project_objective: UNICEF WASH core pipeline supplies project will reach 800,000 beneficiaries through provision to people (IDPs and communities affected by other emergencies) with immediate WASH needs through planning, procurement, prepositioning, distribution, and management of critical WASH supplies. The project will contribute to Cluster objectives 1, 2 and 3 through provision water treatment chemicals, spare parts for hand pump rehabilitation/repair, latrine slabs (squatting pans), plastic tarpaulins for latrine construction, latrine digging kits, hygiene kits (jerry-cans, buckets, soap, menstrual hygiene health materials, and dignity items). UNICEF will procure the WASH supplies and in coordination with the WASH Cluster pre-position them in strategic locations throughout South Sudan. Supplies will be released to partners through the approval of the WASH Cluster, and the receiving partner will be responsible for the distribution of the supplies. The WASH supplies will be accessible to all WASH partners currently operational in South Sudan through WASH Cluster structures at national and state levels. The project will distribute WASH supplies as per Sphere and South Sudan WASH Cluster standards and in coordination with other clusters (Health, and Nutrition). Through this project UNICEF will focus on delivering rapid assistance in all counties and populations affected by a sudden or rapid-onset disaster and targeting at the county level will be done through WASH Cluster updates or using various assessment findings (IRNAs, NAWG recommendations, WASH severity classification). Follow-up monitoring and capacity building of partners will be conducted throughout the project period to ensure proper management of supplies at various warehouses. UNICEF in coordination with beneficiary partners will conduct end user monitoring of the supplies to ensure that supplies distributed are reaching the vulnerable communities and are being used properly.

project_name: Provision of gender sensitive Water and Sanitation (WASH) services to conflict and flood affected population in South Sudan
project_objective:
This project will provide access to safe water and sanitation in targeted locations in Rubkona and Guit counties in Unity State, Aweil North in NBeG State. In Rubkona and Guit, this project will continue supporting routine operation & maintenance (O&M) of existing water systems/boreholes in Bentiu IDP camp, SWAT in Site E, Site D-2, Mankui and Bentiu Water Treatment Plant, Rubkona SWAT and existing Solar Water Yards in Guit. Concern is currently exploring funding from UNICEF to drill new boreholes in IDPs sites (E, D-2) to transit from continued O&M of SWAT in IDP sties to community managed solar water boreholes. Similarly, Concern has worked on its hand over plan for transfer of Bentiu Water Treatment Plant to State Ministry that will be done toward the end of this project. The plan for linking UNICEF support to reduce O&M cost of water systems and transit to community management of water sources is a new intervention; Similarly, implementation of transition plan for Bentiu Water Treatment plant will be a new initiative under this project.

The project will support routine O&M of communal latrines in Bentiu IDP camp, and Concern proposes few blocks of new latrine design (piloted by Concern in Sector-5) to address the challenges related to frequent repair, desludging and decommissioning of latrines. (The latrine with new design in Bentiu IDP camp will be a new intervention in this project). Based on recent discussion with USAID WASH advisor, Concern will conduct a cost analysis study for old and new latrine design, including various cost and non-cost parameters (life span/sustainability and local adaptability) for learning and sharing with other partners for adoption if validated by the study. Concern will also collaborate with other WASH partners piloting different design of sustainable latrines in Bentiu and through WASH cluster the partners will agree on suitable design for scale up. In flood displaced site (Site E, D2 and Mankui), Concern will support routine O&M of latrines and monitoring the cleaning of family shared latrines which is done by the household and cleaning materials are provided on need basis. 

In Aweil North, the WASH services will be only linked to health/nutrition facilities and catchment population where Concern will conduct supervision and training of existing hand pump mechanics (provided with tools under Irish Aid Program) to conduct repair of any dysfunctional hand pumps in target areas. Similarly, the health and nutrition beneficiaries including mother and father groups will be supported with targeted messages and sensitization on adoption of behaviour/practices to construct their own latrines using local materials. (The WASH approach in Aweil North will only focus on linking to health/nutrition beneficiaries). The restoration of water supply will also be linked to nutrition outcomes including access to water for vegetable production at household level. 
Concern will review the approach of hygiene promotion across all locations to integrate the health, hygiene and nutrition under a single team (Community Health Promoters) where appropriate. In IDP settings, Concern will focus investment on practices like cleaning materials, cleaning campaigns, hand washing, and hygiene, and support the eventual handover of projects to communities.

project_name: Enhancing resilience of EQ affected communities by improving access to livelihood opportunities in NW Syria
project_objective:
Syria continues to be one of the most complex protracted conflict humanitarian crises globally, exposed to high levels of ongoing conflict, and prone to natural disasters and epidemic outbreaks. These factors have forced an increase of 1.4M of people in need (PIN) since 2023, totaling 16.7M (HNO, 2024) people in need in Syria. Given the myriad needs and vulnerabilities, Concern proposed this action across Northwest Syria (NWS). Concern has proposed intervention areas in line with the severity of the needs identified by Humanitarian Needs Overview where there continues to be lack of, or challenges for NGOs to provide assistance in Afrin and Azaz Districts. Concern will work with local partners to comprehensively address gaps in the response, ensuring the inclusion of diverse beneficiaries, including girls, children with disabilities, and marginalized communities. 
The intervention will involve implementing small business grants support for persons with disabilities (individuals who were injured during the earthquake), each of the selected beneficiaries will receive business cash grants of up to an average of $800 to start or rebuild their own business. Based on a labor market assessment conducted by Concern and Implementing Partners, the field team will provide the selected beneficiaries with mentoring and coaching during a two months minimum period (no TVET will be provided before delivering the grant), or once the business is running properly, subject to ongoing monitoring. The beneficiaries will be selected through self-targeting mechanism and will receive the cash grant on three instalments, the cash will be transferred through PTT directly to the beneficiary’s PTT account and with get the support needed for transportation from and to the PTT branch in the targeted area. The small business grant value for Syria is according to the Syria ERL Cluster recommendation, still the estimated value in the budget reflect the average grant value taking into consideration the deferent needs for each single project.
Concern will conduct FGDs with beneficiaries to gather feedback on the current activities and suggest ways in which they could be improved. The insights gathered from these discussions are then used to guide the implementation of future activities, ensuring that they are tailored to the specific needs of the population. Throughout the implementation of these activities, Concern and its partners will be present in the field to offer support and assistance to beneficiaries. This may include providing direct services or referring beneficiaries to other actors who can provide the necessary support. By being present in the field and working closely with beneficiaries, Concern and its partners are better able to understand the challenges faced by the population and ensure that their activities are responsive to their needs. During all project phases, Concern and Implementing Partners will consider the AAP measures, mainstreaming of protection, and PSEA. The project has a risk analysis and mitigation matrix. Along with all activities, monitoring, and evaluation processes will be carried out. At the end of the project, a meeting will be made for the project staff and key stakeholders to evaluate the project results and register the lessons learned and the best practices that have been followed to achieve project results.
So far, Concern was able to secure 50% of the proposed budget covering 100 beneficiaries in Afrin district, and the beneficiaries will be reported to the respected clusters (FSL and ERL) based on their business type. Rural businesses (agriculture, livestock, food processing, and linked livelihoods) will be reported to FSL cluster and the remaining business types will be reported to ERL Cluster.

project_name: Sudan: Integrated Health, Nutrition and WASH services for conflict affected, most vulnerable population in West Darfur, West Kordofan, South Kordofan and Port Sudan states in Sudan.
project_objective:
This intervention links to the strategic objectives outlined in the 2024  HRP by providing a life-saving humanitarian intervention through an integrated health, nutrition and WASH package for conflict affected and vulnerable displaced population, their host communities, returnees and other vulnerable groups in West Darfur, South Kordofan, West Kordofan and Red Sea State. 
The total direct target for this integrated services pack is 385, 000 beneficiaries across all targeted states: West Darfur, South Kordofan, West Kordofan and Red Sea States. 
The project will focus on addressing the most critical, life-saving humanitarian needs for conflict affected, as well as protracted vulnerable population in health, nutrition and institution WASH services  through static and mobile outreach services in the targeted localities,. Concern’s operating  in the target localities   and in 2023  scaled up in Red Sea State in response to displacement  as the result of the current fighting in Sudan. 
The proposed operational and financial plans are based on projections through BHA, EU, Irish Aid,  UN (UNICEF, WFP, SHF, IOM)  and other private Funding. The 2024 programming targets to support 83 facilities across 4 states:  30 facilities in West Darfur, and 59 facilities in Kordofan and 4 health facilities in Red Sea State. 
The intervention will increase access to essential lifesaving primary health care (PHC) , including provision of pharmaceuticals, consumables, and LLINs maternal, reproductive health, and child health and community education for vulnerable populations (pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5) will be provided. In Line with health sector objectives, Concern will focus on key humanitarian interventions  including strengthening existing emergency obstetric and new-born care facilities, provision of Antenatal care, skilled delivery and postnatal, immunization service, curative consultation and support the referral system including covering operational costs, fuel and WASH support in health facilities. In addition, reactivating the disease surveillance system and reporting in both government and partner supported facilities and supplying the static vaccination centres with the needed supplies will be a priority. 
The need for increased access to essential, lifesaving, and quality nutrition services and community sensitization for the management of moderate to severe acute malnutrition of the vulnerable population (pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5) will also be addressed. In line with the nutrition sector objectives, integrated with the  health interventions , Concern will scale up maternal and young child nutrition services. The priority will be the , early detection and treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among under-five children, pregnant and lactating women, preventive nutrition interventions, and micronutrient supplementation among children under age 5 and PLW to prevent further deterioration of nutrition situation. Mother and child nutrition care will focus on improving IYCF practices, and improve dietary practices through community engagement and Mother Support Groups . 
Finally, improvement and maintenance of WASH services within health facilities, and hygiene-related community sensitization for vulnerable population (pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5), including distribution of essential dignity kits, will be guaranteed. In line with the revised HRP and at targeted facility levels, Concern will support provision or rehab of latrines, incinerators, and handwashing points depending on needs assessments; water trucking; distribution of essential WASH supplies and NFI emergency sanitation; and extensive hygiene promotion especially for those reliant on surface/river

project_name: Projet Education aux Risques des Engins Explosifs et Assistance aux Victimes dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéry
project_objective:
Le Niger a le huitième indice de risque le plus élevé au monde et le deuxième du Sahel avec un score de 7,5 en 2023 selon les résultats de l’analyse des risques (modèle INFORM). Depuis près d’une décennie (2015-2023), le pays fait face à l’insécurité et la violence persistante contre les civils et les forces de défense de sécurité par des groupes armés non étatiques (GANES) opérant dans les zones frontalières avec les pays voisins notamment le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Nigeria.
Le contexte politique, sécuritaire et humanitaire du Niger continue d'être martelé par une multitude de chocs liés au changement institutionnelle, à la démographie et aux conflits armés (avec un front à l'est - frontière avec le Nigeria - et un autre dans le Liptako). 
La situation sécuritaire ajoutée à la pauvreté endémique (extrême pauvreté à 41,8% en 2021), la forte pression démographique (3,7% par an en 2021), la porosité de ses frontières, l’absence d’opportunités économiques viables pour les jeunes et celle de protection dans la région de Tillabéry et Diffa  est marquée au cours de l’année 2023 par une présence des éléments de GANE suivi d’attaques récurrentes des villages ayant occasionné des vagues de déplacements forcés, des violences intercommunautaires meurtrières, des assassinats ciblant des leaders communautaires.
En raison de l'insécurité, et du ratissage par les FDS les escortes imposées par les nouvelles autorités ont largement contribué à restreindre l'accès et l'assistance humanitaire aux populations les plus vulnérables. Ce projet vise à contribuer à la couverture des besoins urgents de protection dans les régions de Tillabéry et Diffa au Niger. A travers ce projet, HI compte articuler sa stratégie d'intervention autour de la mobilisation des communauté à adapter un comportement vis à vis des risques liés aux engins explosifs (sensibilisations communautaires, confection et diffusion des outils de communication, la formation des acteurs locaux, étatiques et humanitaires sur la problématique des engins explosif,  la collecte et la remontée des informations liées aux incidents) et l'assistance aux victimes (referencement et le suivi des victimes; prise en charge sanitaire et psycho-sociale, mise à disposition des provision d'aide technique et appui aux AGRs).

project_name: Appui aux enfants vulnérables et enfants survivants de VSBG affectés par les conflits armés dans la region de Diffa, tillaberi, Tahoua et Maradi
project_objective:
"Plan International (PIN) propose á travers ce projet une intervention de Protection  (VBG,Protection de l'enfance , Protection générale) pour 12970 garçons et filles, hommes et femmes affectés par le conflit dans les 4 regions d’urgence du Niger (Diffa, Tahoua, Maradi et Tillabery)
En effet , la violence et les déplacements continus dans ces 4 régions ont eu un impact négatif sur l'environnement protecteur des enfants, laissant des nombreux garçons et filles vulnérables avec des besoins de protection aigus et les exposant à des risques de protection comme le recrutement , l'utilisation par les GANEs, la séparation familiale familles, la déconnexion au système éducatif déjà faible , mais surtout la VSBG
Ainsi,ce projet consolidera les structures de protection departementales, communautaires ou locales, formelles et/ou informelles en leur dotant des ressources et des capacités nécessaires pour atténuer et répondre aux besoins de protection des filles et des garçons vulnérables et de leurs familles dans leurs communautés respectives.
 
Une gestion des cas sensible au genre, un soutien psychosocial, des dispositions alternatives de prise en charge , l’appui á la securité et á la reintegration, y compris un soutien à la réinsertion et/ou réintégration des EAFGA seront assurés pour aider les enfants survivant(e)s ou les enfants á risque d’abus, d'exploitation, de violence ou de négligence de bénéficier d’une prise en charge á temps opportun et selon les standards requis .
Utilisant les approaches fixes et ou mobiles couplée par des activités de prévention et mitigation des risques ,l'intervention de protection consistera à (i) fournir des soins individuels et des services de protection, notamment aux survivants de violences sexuelles, aux ENA/ES et/ou aux enfants libérés des milices ; (ii)  accompagner les adolescentes et jeunes, surtout la jeunes filles vulnérables dans l'accès aux kits( Kits d'hygiène ou de dignité) et/ou soutien soutien socio économique modeste(CASH) pour améliorer leur bien être et pour contribuer  á leur autonomie (Iii) améliorer la capacité des prestataires de services, des autorités locales, des réseaux et structure de VBG et/ou de protection de l’enfance, des acteurs locaux, des parents/tuteurs et des membres de la communauté à prévenir ,répondre,et à atténuer les risques PE, en particulier la VSBG, la séparation familiale et le recrutement d'enfants."  (IV) Améliorer les compétences parentales et familiales dans le support et dans  la prise en charge de leurs enfants , mais surtout dans le développement d’un environnement familial protecteur

project_name: Life-saving food assistance in North-East Nigeria
project_objective:
WFP will provide unconditional food assistance to the most food-insecure, crisis-affected populations. Life-saving general food assistance (in-kind food and cash-based transfers) will be delivered to IDPs, returnees, and host populations in North-East Nigeria (Borno, Yobe, and Adamawa States). Early recovery and resilience to shocks will be promoted through asset creation and preservation and increased livelihood opportunities. Joint multi-sectoral assessments and Emergency Food Security Analyses will be conducted regularly to monitor the food security, and market situation in crisis-affected states. 
A gender-transformative approach that meets the needs of women, men, girls, and boys will be adopted. WFP will mainstream protection throughout its work, supported by a solid understanding of the operational context and protection analysis. Training and capacity building of staff and partners in the protection and humanitarian principles will include on-the-job coaching. WFP will ensure that affected populations (women and men) will be consulted throughout the programme cycle; community feedback mechanisms will be tailored to their preferred means of communication. Beneficiaries will continue to be empowered with knowledge of their food assistance entitlements and their rights, including WFP’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be embedded in M&E tools, community feedback mechanisms, and training of partners and staff.
WFP will continue the collection of key information on beneficiaries and assistance provided as part of its M&E activities. Monthly monitoring will include distribution and activity site management; beneficiary and entitlement verification; and ensuring adequate protection and gender measures. Lessons will be regularly drawn from monthly process and biannual outcome monitoring and reporting, and periodic reviews and evaluation to inform strategic and operational decisions.
WFP will further consolidate partnerships to enhance national and state-level emergency preparedness and response systems, including food security and nutrition assessment and monitoring, early warning, protection, gender analysis, targeting and registration processes, safety nets, cash-based transfer capacities, and supply chain.
Where security and access to land allow, increasing livelihood activities will complement food assistance to support access to productive assets, income-generating activities, and self-reliance in the long term. Assistance will be coordinated with government distributions to ensure food assistance is complimentary with other ongoing assistance from other clusters with no gaps.

project_name: Strengthening food and nutritional security and the resilience of vulnerable populations affected by the crisis and climate change in the North, Adamawa and East regions of Cameroon, through activities to create productive assets to support livelihoods.
project_objective:
The project aims to improve access to food, enhance livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable and food-insecure communities affected by the crisis and climate change in the North, Adamawa and East regions. This project will focus on the deployment of food assistance through the distribution of food and cash transfers conditional on participation in activities, as well as on strengthening the technical capacities of beneficiaries. The project will support 56,000 vulnerable people (60% women), including small farmers, internally displaced people (IDPs), returnees and local populations affected by the crisis and climate change in localities in the North, Adamawa and East regions. To implement the activities, Community-Based Participatory Planning (CBPP) sessions will be carried out in collaboration with local community members (women and men), decentralized technical services of key ministries and partners to identify the real needs and priorities of local communities that will help affected populations develop their own response strategies and strengthen their resilience. This people-centred approach ensures the provision of effective solutions with beneficiaries and reduces reliance on relief.
The project's objective will be achieved through the implementation of two major interventions: food assistance for early recovery (31,000 targeted beneficiaries) and food assistance for resilience (25,000 targeted beneficiaries). Food assistance will be provided using two modalities: cash transfers and in-kind food distribution. The project will provide six (06) months of food assistance to vulnerable households participating in early recovery activities and 10 months to those participating in resilience-building asset creation activities. Early recovery activities will focus on the socio-economic empowerment of beneficiaries. Asset creation activities are grouped around three priorities: climate adaptation and mitigation; infrastructure rehabilitation; and food system resilience.
WFP will work closely with government line ministries, cooperating partners and communities to ensure project implementation and sustainability. Nutrition, gender and protection issues are taken into consideration at all stages of project design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. A gender and protection risk analysis will be carried out, and the most vulnerable will be targeted, including female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, and people with disabilities. Project sites will be located in safe areas and at a convenient distance from beneficiaries' homes. To support successful project implementation and ensure sustainability, capacity-building sessions will be organized for all stakeholders on gender and protection policy, project management, monitoring and nutrition.

project_name: Provision of school means to boys and girls including those with disabilities in formal and non formal education in Syria.
project_objective:
The school meals programme (SMP)  aims to restore and stabilize access to education and enhance the health and nutrition status of children by addressing short-term hunger and improving intake of essential macro and micronutrients. Simultaneously, SMP contributes to protection of children from reverting to negative coping mechanism ( child labour,  early marriage), as a consequence of financial constraints. The programme meets the sector’s 1st objective “ Saves lives: Provide life-saving and life-sustaining humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable .“
SMP targets boys and girls including those living with disabilities:
- In kind  daily distribution of fresh meals or fortified datebars to children in formal education (pre&primary) and to children enrolled in non-formal education (NFE) supported by UNICEF.
- Provision of electronic vouchers to out of school students enrolled in curriculum B or NFE.
SMP is implemented in coordination with MOE,NGOS, INGOS and UN. Considering the elevated needs and limited resources, the project will focus on areas with low food security and education indicators(Severity >=3). 
 SMP supported 839,362 children over 2023,  and is planning to reach 780,000 children monthly in 2024.
Needs 
The education system in Syria faces compounded challenges due to prolonged conflict, economic instability, and the recent earthquake, impacting infrastructure and disrupting learning. WFP's monitoring data from 2023, indicates a consistent level of enrolment and retention rates compared with 2022, while a noticeable decrease in attendance from 97% in 2022 to 87% in 2023 was noted. Concurrently,  anecdotal data gathered from beneficiary interviews indicated a rise in incidences of child labour, with 21% of households withdrawing their children from school in Q1 2023, marking a 5% increase from Q4 2022. A 2022 national assessment, led by MoH, of the nutritional status of school-aged children revealed elevated prevalence of malnutrition. The findings indicated  that 40% of children were skipping breakfast and 80% lacked dietary diversity.  Additionally, one in five children were identified to suffer from iron deficiency anemia, with certain regions facing even higher rates. As addressing these challenges remain vital, noting the long-term repercussions of malnutrition and inadequate education,  school meals play an instrumental role in providing essential nutrients key for learning and development, while also alleviating economic burdens on families.
Implementation process:
1-	Distribution of Fortified Date Bars :
Targets children in schools and NFE in prioritized sub-districts in the 3 WOS hubs. 
•WFP dispatches monthly shipments of fortified date bars to target schools/learning centers.
•Daily distribution of 1 pack (80 gr) of fortified date bars per child  .
2- Distribution of Fresh Meals :
Targets  primary schools children in selected sub-districts in Aleppo, Rural Damascus, and Deir Ez Zour. Targeted locations are  identified based on education and food insecurity vulnerability and feasibility.
•Sandwiches are prepared in kitchens run by WFP partners, with fresh material sourced out from local markets. The project aids in creating employment and enhancing livelihoods of specifically vulnerable women within the community.
•Fresh meals are prepared and distributed daily to children in targeted schools.
3-Electronic Vouchers (Cash Transfer):
targets OoSC, encouraging them to re-enter the educational system either through CB or NFE, providing incentive to children, and families, to pursue their education and to safeguard children from dropping out again.
•the transfers (e-vouchers) are conditional to achieving 80% monthly attendance rate, and are redeemed at designated retailers, allowing beneficiaries to purchase essential food items. 
Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) are conducted by WFP FM utilizing a comprehensive array of data collection tools, post-distribution surveys, and engaging focus group discussions.

project_name: Empowering Rohingya refugees and host community women through leadership, learning and livelihoods
project_objective:
Through the intervention, UN Women will support more Rohingya and host community women to have access to diversified livelihood opportunities and are empowered with increased social and economic security. UN Women, with mandate of gender equality and women’s empowerment, responds not only to immediate protection needs including GBV services but to address the needs of sustainable livelihoods and resilience-building for vulnerable women. In order to assess the specific livelihood challenges and opportunities that women in refugee and host communities experience, UN Women plans to conduct a gender analysis of livelihoods in Cox’s Bazar. Upon assessment, UN Women tailor skills development and vocational training based on the needs and priorities of the targeted women and provide the livelihood services through the Multi-Purpose Women’s Centers (MPWCs).
Since 2018, UN Women had established the MPWCs and the Women’s Market in camps 3, 4, 4ext, 5 and 18 and host communities in Ukhia, and Teknaf. The MPWCs provide women, girls and gender diverse persons with access to tailored multisectoral services that consider their unique needs and difficulties, with an emphasis on empowering women to build resilience and enhancing their leadership and participation in their communities. The MPWCs, already providing livelihood services, will strengthen its efforts on women’s economic empowerment and offer a diversified livelihood opportunities to both refugee and host community women, ensuring the inclusion of the most marginalized women, girls, and gender diverse persons. UN Women plans to relocate one MPWC in the host community. Furthermore, UN Women will further standardize the operations of the MPWCs, and train local women-led organizations with the standards and technical tools so that they can take over the Centres by themselves independently in the future. Beyond the camps with the MPWCs, furthermore, 6 UN Women partners through WPHF provide women with accelerated learning and non-formal vocational training to strengthen socio-economic stability in Ukhiya, and Teknaf and camp 1E, 1W, 2W, 5, 6, 8E, 10, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 22, 24, and 26. UN Women continue to enhance their capacities in service delivery, and monitor their activities and results in the field.
In 2024, UN Women plans to provide three kinds of vocational training courses, sewing machine operation, bakery and pastry, and solar (PV) system installation and maintenance to the vulnerable Rohingya and host community women through its existing MPWCs. In the camps, a total of 2,600 women will benefit from the skills development opportunities (500 with vocational training, and 2,100 with non-formal technical training. Out of the 2,600 women, 1,000 will receive the accelerated learning before training to enhance feminist literacy skills. Upon training, 2,100 women will be provided with in-kind grants for self-employment. In the host community, 1,350 women (150 with vocational and 1,200 with non-formal technical training) in total will benefit from training opportunities and in-kind grants that support them to start business. In addition, 25 women will be provided with computers and access computer literacy training. Through the project, UN Women plans to mobilize 93 unskilled volunteers (55 Rohingya and 38 host community members) to support the training sites within the MPWCs within the camps. In addition, 24 women will receive monthly grants to run the shops in the Women’s Market in the camp 5. Overall, the project plans to refer 100 trainees as semi-skilled and skilled volunteers once they graduate from the vocational training.

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria multisectorial a población vulnerable y retornada en los estados Apure, Táchira y Zulia
project_objective:
La acción busca responder a las necesidades humanitarias complejas que enfrenta la población venezolana altamente vulnerable y los retornados con un abordaje holístico y una respuesta multisectorial con miras a lograr la estabilización biopsicosocial de las personas, con enfoque diferencial y centrado en el ejercicio de sus derechos. Para ello, se tiene previsto, la configuración de equipos multi-tasking y especializados para responder a las necesidades individuales, familiares y comunitarias.
En PROTECCION, se tendrán unidades especializadas brindando servicios de orientación legal, apoyo psicosocial, gestoría de casos y programas de asistencia material para complementar la atención a las múltiples necesidades que pueden tener; se priorizará a las familias de comunidades altamente vulnerables y retornados; se trabajará con aliados locales, que serán fortalecidos, a fin de promover un trabajo en red y acciones sostenibles. También se apoyará el restablecimiento o inicio de actividades de subsistencia para sobrevivientes de la violencia de género, familias retornadas en Venezuela y familias afectadas por el cambio climático (inundaciones).
En Educación en Emergencias se desarrollarán acciones dirigidas a garantizar la permanencia e inclusión de NNA en el sistema escolar y la promoción de espacios seguros y de calidad, a través de la mejora y dotación de comedores escolares, así como la rehabilitación de los sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y saneamiento básico. Asimismo, se trabajará en la identificación de casos de NN que han abandonado la escuela y se les acompañará en su reintegración al sistema escolar; también se apoyará a NNA con elementos esenciales para la educación y se capacitará a docentes en diferentes asignaturas.
En el sector Salud se fortalecerá las capacidades de los servicios de salud materno infantil y la salud sexual y reproductiva, y de prácticas basadas en WASH FIT y de prevención y control de infecciones. A nivel familiar se complementará con acciones de gestoría de salud. Asimismo, desde el componente de Educación, se promoverá la identificación y atención de NNA y sus familiares con afectaciones de salud, especialmente en temas de nutrición y con necesidades de abastecimiento y potabilización de agua. Las acciones de los diferentes sectores están íntimamente relacionadas y son complementarias entre sí con miras a alcanzar un apoyo integral.
En general, los riesgos, afectaciones y necesidades humanitarias identificados por diversas OSC y ONG’s internacionales, coinciden con los identificados por CISP en los estados priorizados para esta propuesta. De acuerdo a resultados del instrumento de caracterización aplicado en 2022-23 a 4.654 familias en Venezuela, se identificó que el 75% de ellas refiere tener afectaciones psicosociales. En promedio, el 19% de los NN de las familias caracterizadas han dejado de asistir a la escuela por diversas causas. En promedio, 26% de las familias refieren tener un miembro con discapacidad, principalmente de movilidad o visual. 
El 46% de las familias reporta enfermedades crónicas, principalmente HTA. 54% de las familias, ha padecido enfermedades agudas y 59% enfermedades de origen hídrico. 68% de ellas consumen el agua sin tratar y 42% no tienen un manejo adecuado de los residuos sólidos. El 48% de familias logran alimentarse solo dos veces al día con una dieta principal de carbohidratos; el consumo de vegetales, frutas y proteínas es casi nulo; en general, 80% de las familias tiene dificultades para cubrir necesidades básicas más urgentes, 76% de ellas ganan un salario mínimo o menos y 61% tienen trabajos ocasionales, mientras que 17% no cuentan actualmente con una fuente de ingresos.
El desabastecimiento de insumos en las emergencias de los hospitales alcanzó 46,8 % durante 2022-2023,  el desabastecimiento de insumos para los quirófanos fue de 71,5 % . La inoperatividad de los servicios de diagnóstico alcanzó 79%, según reporta la Encuesta Nacional de Hospitales.

project_name: Rapid Response Mechanism 2024
project_objective:
La crise du bassin du Lac Tchad, les aléas climatiques ainsi que les épidémies continuent à provoquer des conséquences désastreuses pour les populations résidentes.
Pour permettre aux acteurs humanitaires de répondre efficacement aux besoins immédiats des populations déplacées au Cameroun, le consortium PUI/ACF propose de continuer ses efforts de veille humanitaire (en zones rurales comme en zones urbaines), évaluation et coordination avec les acteurs humanitaires et de réponse multisectorielle à travers le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM).
En se basant sur les résultats de l’évaluation externe conduite en octobre 2022 et du compte rendu de l’Atelier Externe de décembre 2022, il s’agira d’:
Améliorer la qualité des données collectées au niveau des Evaluations Multi-Sectorielles (EMS) à travers une collaboration renforcée avec les sectoriels, ainsi qu’un appui au reporting interne par l’ONG IMPACT
Maintenir et renforcer le système de veille et d’alerte sur les mouvements de populations grâce à une collaboration renforcée avec l’IOM et les autres acteurs présents sur ce créneau
Faire systématiquement un dépistage de la malnutrition aigüe des enfants de moins de 5 ans dès les EMS avec référencement immédiat des cas de MAS détectés. 
Apporter une réponse de premier recours en Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME), Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), inclus articles pour l’Hygiène Intime, et Sécurité Alimentaire tout en s’appuyant sur les capacités des autres acteurs humanitaires hors RRM à travers un mapping actualisé 
Recourir à la modalité Transfert Monétaire (TM)
 pour les réponses SECAL, AME et kit d’hygiène intime lorsque les conditions d’accès / disponibilité/ accessibilité des marchés et de sécurité le permettront.
Développer le Principe du Ne pas Nuire et les actions de Protection transversale à travers la signature et le suivi des MoU signés avec les partenaires
Améliorer le mécanisme de remontée des avis et plaintes
Poursuivre le   renforcement des capacités et l’appui structurant à une OSC (CADEPI) sur les aspects clés du Mécanisme et identifier de nouvelles OSC, particulièrement dans le Logone Chari.
Poursuivre les efforts visant à une coordination de la réponse performante (matrice de suivi des recommandations des EMS, interface géoportail amélioré grâce à un appui régulier de l’ONG IMMAP.
ASSISTANCE
En ce qui concerne l'assistance, notons que l'accent est mis sur le respect des standard minimum émis par les différents secteurs.

POLITIQUE PEAS.
L’exploitation et l’abus sexuels constituent un échec catastrophique pour ce qui est de la protection. Ils sont préjudiciables à ceux que les organisations humanitaires et leurs partenaires ont le mandat de protéger et compromettent la réputation de ces organisations. Ils violent également les normes et standards juridiques internationaux universellement reconnus. Des allégations d’exploitation et d’abus sexuels généralisés concernant les femmes et enfants réfugiés et déplacés par les travailleurs humanitaires et leurs partenaires ont poussé les organisations humanitaires à mettre sur pied des politiques strictes en matière de PEAS. Celle de PUI  qui date de plus de 12 ans condamne fermement toute violation  de cette politique par l’un de ses staffs, prestataire, partenaire ou fournisseur. Cette politique conforte la bonne  tenue et le bon suivi  du système de collecte et  remontée de plaintes. Cette politique est une des politiques pour laquelle PUI mettra  des mesures coercitives en cas de son non respect.
