In 2024, WVB will continue the implementation to address the gaps in education, especially for the children, and adolescents aged between 3 to 18 years living in the Camps and Host Communities in Ukhiya, and Teknaf at Camps 13, and 19 and extend to 27 and Host Communities where the number of targeted beneficiaries will be 1990. WVB will continue the ECD intervention and start the Myanmar Curriculum, Adolescent and Youth Learning, and Skill activities at the same locations.  WVB will sustain its Community-Based Learning Facilities (CBLF) modality and establish, use, or renovate ECD centers in the project locations. WVB concentrates on implementing the Myanmar Curriculum, and Adolescent and Youth learning facilities. Community Support Group/Learning Center Management Committee supports identifying the learners and potential Facilitators in the camps and host communities. This project includes an evident disability inclusion focus, aiming to identify and assess the disability status of learners attending learning facilities and cater individualized support for those most vulnerable to reduce learners dropping out. In 2024, WVB will ensure the quality of learning opportunities following the Education Sector and WVB NO’s guidance and will emphasize updating and upgrading teaching and learning materials ensuring inclusion, and gender sensitivity across the learning facilities. The project focuses on community engagement to reduce gender inequality to ensure quality education in all aspects of the project implementation. 

WVB will build capacities of facilitators of ECD and Myanmar Curriculum including Pre-vocational/Vocational skill training, especially soft skills. WVB will involve and support the development of gender-responsive pedagogy, inclusive education, safeguarding and PSEA theme-based training, crisis-sensitive education, and planning to improve learning outcomes of refugee and host communities’ learners. WVB will identify and build the capacities of Rohingya women to become Myanmar Curriculum teachers and create a pool of female facilitators. The project team and MEAL team of WVB will conduct regular assessments to monitor and track the enrolled learners' progress. The project will invite the Education Sector's colleagues to share learning. 

WVB will continue to emphasize community ownership by engaging them and strengthening their capacity enhancing participation in all the education activities for children, adolescents, and youths. Parents, Parents Support Group, and faith leaders will receive training on gender, girls' education, disability inclusion, child protection, and safeguarding. WVB will support the Community Support Group in preparing emergency response plans related to Learning. By implementing aforesaid interventions, the proposed WVB project will reach a total of 1990 children, categorized into 1140 children aged 36-59 months participating in the ECD program and 850 children aged 5-18 engaged in the Myanmar Curriculum.

project_name: Strengthen community-based protection services through Barefoot counselor approach.
project_objective: The Rohingya community, compelled to flee Myanmar, grapples with heightened vulnerability due to entrenched social issues like discrimination and violence. This susceptibility disproportionately affects children, adolescents, women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. The project's core objective is to bolster community mobilization by disseminating information through established, inclusive community centers. These centers will facilitate the formation of diverse groups, categorized by age, gender, vulnerability, and diversity. FDMNs will receive specialized sessions addressing anti-trafficking, emergency response, gender-based violence prevention, and positive parenting. Persons with disabilities will actively participate in a self-help committee, contributing to the development of action plans. Barefoot counselors, serving as community volunteers, will conduct door-to-door visits to identify protection concerns and support needs. Staff and volunteers will be trained to form a Community-Based Protection Committee (CBPC) and develop action plans to address various forms of violence and mental health condition. Installation of solar streetlights at the block level aims to enhance safety and dignity. Inclusive activities, such as play therapy for children and focus group discussions, address diverse needs. The project establishes a community-based complaint mechanism, ensures transparent referral support, and provides basic primary health care by paramedic support. Tree plantation activities contribute to ecological protection, and a contingency plan with project staff involvement in the PERU team addresses emergencies. Counter-trafficking initiatives involve advocacy, screening, and collaboration with stakeholders, aligning with the project's broader goal of impacting community-based protection and supporting potential repatriation for FDMNs to their country of origin.

project_name: Promoting livestock productivity through intervetions that ehnance livestock health and nutrition, and safeguarding livestock loss.
project_objective: 1. Procure, distribute and undertake control and vaccination activities to combat opportunistic infections, parasites, diseases, and health stress induced impact.                                                                                                                                     2. Distribution of drought tolerant fodder crops to the most vulnerable households in the affected areas to promote livestock nutrition and safeguard deterioration of animal body conditions and eventually promote or sustain good health.                                                                                                                            3. Procure and undertake livestock restocking programmes by distributing disease-free breeding stock to households that lost their livestock (i.e. poultry, goats, and pigs) under pass-on programmes to maintain or increase livestock numbers and eventually achieve food and income security.

project_name: Alojamiento de Emergencia para personas desplazadas y en riesgo de desplazamiento forzado, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, solicitantes de asilo, refugiadas y afectados por desastres naturales en El Salvador
project_objective:
ACNUR como líder del Sector Alojamientos de Emergencia en El Salvador, y como agencia humanitaria, implementará este proyecto para contribuir con el acceso a alojamiento de emergencia y la mejora de resiliencia en situaciones de crisis para personas afectadas por desplazamiento forzado y en riesgo de desplazamiento, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, personas solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas, que hayan sido afectadas por efectos del cambio climático y/o desastres naturales.

El proyecto de ACNUR El Salvador para el HRP 2024 se alinea a los objetivos del Sector Alojamiento de Emergencias en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria, en el cual se proponen acciones para cubrir la necesidad de alojamientos transitorios dignos y seguros. El proyecto también se encuentra alineado con las prioridades nacionales y contribuye al Plan de Acción Nacional del Marco Integral Regional para la Protección y Soluciones (MIRPS). ACNUR brindará orientación y apoyo técnico a instituciones y partes interesadas para la inclusión de personas en situación de desplazamiento. Junto con contrapartes nacionales, ACNUR desarrollará procesos de capacitación y fortalecimiento técnico a instituciones estatales, actores humanitarios y actores comunitarios. 

Para el acceso a alojamiento de familias que no tienen donde pernoctar, se prevén modalidades transitorias como carpas, módulos temporales de vivienda, kits de materiales de construcción y kits de herramientas. En el caso de familias cuyas viviendas han sufrido afectación moderada, el proyecto prevé prestar apoyo bajo la modalidad de subsidios tanto para alquiler como para reparación de vivienda.

A su vez, el proyecto incluye la entrega de insumos no alimenticios de apoyo complementario a través de kits domésticos que pueden incluir colchonetas, lámparas, frazadas, menajes de cocina, mosquiteros, ropa, instrumentos de limpieza, entre otros, con el objeto de mitigar las carencias domésticas de las personas y/o comunidades que hayan sido forzadas a desplazarse a causa de un evento climático o un desastre natural. 

Sabiendo que las afectaciones en materia de alojamiento son diferenciadas según el edad, género y diversidad, la respuesta humanitaria que se implemente a través del proyecto debe considerar dichas necesidades diferenciadas, para tal efecto se mantendrá el enfoque de centralidad de protección y acción sin daño.

En cuanto a cobertura geográfica, el proyecto se implementará en todos los departamentos del país donde exista necesidad por las causas establecidas. Sin embargo, las acciones se enfocarán prioritariamente en los departamentos cuya necesidad de alojamiento fue expuesta como de alta severidad en el análisis del HNO 2023, a saber: Ahuachapán, Chalatenango, Cuscatlán, La Libertad, La Paz, La Unión, Morazán, Sonsonate y Usulután.

project_name: Fortalecimiento de la Coordinación y Gestión de Albergues Temporales con enfoque de Protección
project_objective:
ACNUR dará apoyo técnico al Gobierno de El Salvador en el fortalecimiento de la gestión y coordinación de albergues temporales, a través de la Dirección Nacional de Albergues y la Comisión Técnica Sectorial de Albergues (CTSA).

ACNUR ejercerá el co-liderazgo del Sector de Coordinación y Gestión de Albergues con OIM Temporales del Equipo Humanitario de País. A través del Sector, ACNUR apoyará la coordinación de la respuesta humanitaria en albergues temporales, promoviendo el enlace entre los actores humanitarios y la CTSA. También fomentará el análisis e identificación de las necesidades en el proceso de activación y gestión de albergues, contribuyendo a la resolución de brechas identificadas con los miembros del Sector. 

Para incorporar el enfoque de protección en la gestión de albergues, ACNUR promoverá sesiones de construcción de conocimiento con enlaces departamentales y municipales de albergues. ACNUR acompañará la coordinación y gestión de albergues durante emergencias, como co-líder del Sector y participante en la CTSA, brindando apoyo técnico, orientación y acompañamiento en los albergues activados.

project_name: Protección a comunidades afectadas por desplazamiento forzado y en riesgo de desplazamiento, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, personas solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas en El Salvador
project_objective:
La estrategia de ACNUR aborda las necesidades de protección de las personas desplazadas por la fuerza, apátridas y las personas retornadas con necesidades de protección independientemente de su edad, género y diversidad. Para lograr esto, ACNUR impulsará acciones con otros actores para construir un entorno de protección favorable y abogará por salvaguardar los derechos y la dignidad de las personas y comunidades afectadas. Con un enfoque de área, ACNUR trabajará con sus socios para buscar soluciones al desplazamiento.

El proyecto de ACNUR está alineado con las prioridades nacionales, y contribuye al Plan de Acción Nacional del Marco Integral Regional para la Protección y Soluciones (MIRPS) y a los compromisos del II Foro Mundial sobre los Refugiados asumidos por El Salvador en 2023.

ACNUR brindará orientación y apoyo técnico a instituciones y partes interesadas clave para la inclusión de personas desplazadas internas en programas e iniciativas. Junto con contrapartes nacionales, ACNUR conducirá monitoreos de protección y contribuirá a actualizar la información sobre los perfiles de las personas desplazadas por la fuerza internamente en El Salvador. ACNUR desarrollará procesos de capacitación y fortalecimiento técnico a instituciones estatales y actores humanitarios. 

ACNUR asegurará la gestión de casos con la continuidad de implementación de cuatro Espacios de Apoyo “A tu lado” en Santa Ana, San Salvador, San Vicente y San Miguel en coordinación con socios e instituciones nacionales. Las Unidades Móviles “A tu lado” mejorarán el alcance de ACNUR para difundir información e identificar y remitir casos. ACNUR proporcionará a las personas asistencia en efectivo para cubrir las necesidades básicas de los casos identificados en mayor riesgo. 

En el marco del Equipo Humanitario de País, ACNUR liderará el Sector de Protección, asegurando que el Equipo Humanitario País responda adecuadamente a las necesidades de las personas desplazadas. 
ACNUR de la mano de sus socios fortalecerá 93 comunidades a través de procesos participativos con enfoque de edad, género y diversidad. Las intervenciones de ACNUR fomentarán la inclusión y el compromiso a través de la colaboración con 15 estructuras comunitarias como voluntarios, facilitadores judiciales, comités de jóvenes, líderes comunitarios, grupos de mujeres, comités locales, centros comunitarios CUBOS y los Centros de Integración Comunitaria (CIC) y Espacios de Apoyo. ACNUR fortalecerá iniciativas lideradas por las comunidades con las cuales trabaja y proyectos de coexistencia pacífica. ACNUR fortalecerá aún más los liderazgos de personas jóvenes y LGBTIQ+ en la búsqueda de soluciones. ACNUR garantizará que las mujeres y las niñas participen de manera equitativa y significativa.

ACNUR reforzará las oportunidades de medios de vida para las personas desplazadas internamente o en riesgo de desplazamiento, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo y personas retornadas con necesidades de protección de modo que logren la autosuficiencia y la inclusión económica. ACNUR con sus socios desarrollará programas sobre orientación al mercado e inserción laboral, emprendimiento y capital semilla, educación de formación profesional y educación de adultos. 

A través de un acuerdo directo con el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, ACNUR apoyará la estrategia de desarrollo de capacidades de la Comisión para la Determinación de la Condición de Refugiado (CODER) para aumentar las habilidades y conocimientos de su personal, e impulsará el marco legal y los protocolos internos de la institución. Bajo el liderazgo de CODER, ACNUR contribuirá a difundir el conocimiento y la información disponible sobre los derechos de la población refugiada y solicitante de asilo y el proceso de solicitud de refugio en El Salvador. ACNUR fortalecerá las actividades de monitoreo de fronteras, brigadas y campañas de información, y reforzará el apoyo a la población con necesidades de protección que son parte de movimientos mixtos.

project_name: Atención integral de protección a la niñez en desplazamiento o en riesgo de desplazamiento en El Salvador
project_objective:
ACNUR trabajará en el fortalecimiento del sistema Nacional de Protección de la Primera Infancia, Niñez y Adolescencia de El Salvador. La alianza con la autoridad nacional de protección de la niñez CONAPINA, y las unidades dedicadas de la Procuraduría General de la República (PGR) y la Procuraduría para la Defensa de los Derechos Humanos (PDDH), del Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología (MINEDUCYT), sustentarán y reforzarán acciones para la protección de la niñez desplazada por la fuerza.

ACNUR apoyará a las instituciones con recursos humanos para poder atender a niños, niñas y adolescentes que se encuentran desplazados o en riesgo de desplazamiento, buscando protección como refugiados y retornados con necesidades de protección.  Específicamente, ACNUR apoyará con profesionales de psicología que brindarán atención en los puntos de recepción, aeropuertos y fronteras; además de en comunidades donde había alto riesgo de violencia de pandillas en las que se implementarán espacios amigables para niños, niñas y adolescentes. Además, ACNUR fortalecerá capacidades y apoyará la adecuación de espacios para buscar soluciones para niños, niñas y adolescentes en situación de desplazamiento forzado.

ACNUR cooperará en apoyo a las comunidades históricamente afectadas por la violencia donde el Gobierno impulsará las respuestas a la niñez desplazada o en riesgo que requieren servicios básicos como educación y salud mental. ACNUR dará prioridad al trabajo en cinco comunidades para dar seguimiento a la situación de niñas, niños y adolescentes en mayor riesgo, trabajando con socios y el Gobierno en la identificación de casos y necesidades, y en la provisión de respuestas de protección.

Teniendo en cuenta los avances actuales en el entorno de seguridad, ACNUR impulsará soluciones a través de intervenciones dirigidas a la participación, el retorno a la educación y el bienestar de los niños, niñas y adolescentes. ACNUR adaptará espacios colectivos en cinco comunidades históricamente bajo control de pandillas como espacios amigables de estudio. Estas instalaciones contarán con una persona profesional en psicología y una persona promotora educativa. Trabajando juntos, ayudarán a los niños a recuperar las habilidades sociales y la autoestima afectadas por la violencia y las limitaciones de movilidad causadas por fronteras invisibles. Se guiará a niños, niñas y adolescentes en un proceso de reflexión y resiliencia. La persona promotora brindará apoyo para el retorno al sistema educativo en caso de deserción en coordinación con el Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología.

Dada la numerosa identificación de casos de niños, niñas y adolescentes en mayor riesgo, ACNUR creará un equipo especializado y dedicado a su gestión. La gestión y seguimiento de los casos incluirá el análisis y determinación del interés superior a la luz de sus necesidades de protección y posibles soluciones, incluido el reasentamiento.

project_name: Alojamientos Colectivos (AC) Seguros para personas en situación de movilidad humana (incluyendo guatemaltecos en riesgo) en Guatemala.
project_objective:
Dadas las dinámicas de movilidad humana en Guatemala, como país de origen, tránsito, destino y retorno de personas obligadas a huir de sus hogares y con necesidades de protección internacional, y frente al aumento de personas en movimientos mixtos cruzando Guatemala al final de 2023, la capacidad de alojamiento temporal en los albergues, en muchos casos, es sobrepasada y se requiere una mayor y mejor infraestructura para enfrentar estos desafíos. 

Este proyecto tiene como objetivo, fortalecer la red de Albergues Temporales Colectivos que atienden a las personas que sirve el ACNUR y sus socios, en lo particular de este proyecto, la población priorizada son las personas con necesidades de protección específicas y situaciones de vulnerabilidad, necesidad de protección internacional o reasentamiento, y en general personas en situación de movilidad humana. Especialmente grupos como unidades familiares, NNA, NNA no acompañados o separados.

La adecuada gestión y coordinación de los alojamientos temporales es fundamental para crear condiciones de entorno seguro, que facilite el ejercicio pleno de los derechos fundamentales y protección frente a riesgos como la violencia basada en género y otros tipos de violencia.
Este mismo principio fomenta la estrecha coordinación con los Socios Implementadores e Instituciones gubernamentales para fomentar una respuesta complementaria, articulada y estandarizada.

Las principales actividades en el marco de este proyecto son:
1.	Brindar soluciones alojamiento digno, seguros, que cumplen con estándares mínimos a través de socios implementadores, especializados en brindar este servicios de forma integral y coordinada, buscando alcanzar a 95,000 personas aproximadamente.
2.	Entrega de Insumos no alimentarios como kits de higiene o artículos básicos de socorro a un estimado de 6,600 personas.
3.	Adecuación, mejoramiento y equipamiento de 2 Alojamientos Colectivos para garantizar mínimos estándares humanitarios.
4.	Fortalecimiento de capacidades en gestión y coordinación de alojamientos temporales (CCCM) a 12 instituciones humanitarios.
5.	Implementar con al menos 8 socios y comunidades de acogida, herramientas prácticas, eficientes e innovadoras para la gestión y coordinación de alojamientos colectivos (CCCM).

project_name: Proteccion integral a personas en situacion de movilidad humana en Guatemala
project_objective:
A lo largo de 2022 e inicios de 2023, se ha notado un incremento en los impactos humanitarios y de necesidades de protección que dejan las diferentes crisis que afectan al país. Por un lado, la situación de violencia e inseguridad sigue impactando a miles de personas, evidenciado en el indicador de muertes violentas el cual registró un incremento de 6,7 por ciento con respecto al año anterior, llegando a una tasa de 17.3 por cada 100 mil habitantes, una de las más altas en Centro América. Los principales delitos denunciados son extorsión, hurto, robo, homicidios, lesiones, violencia sexual a NNA y mujeres adultas. A pesar de la mejora en ciertos indicadores de seguridad en el país, el alcance, control y violencia ejercida por grupos de delincuencia organizada continúa planteando serios desafíos a la protección de la población. Las pandillas poseen un amplio control en el país y están vinculadas a delitos violentos, extorsión, reclutamiento forzado y actividades relacionadas con el tráfico de drogas. Adicionalmente, las elecciones presidenciales y una transición política alterada, ha generado que los lideres indígenas se movilicen en protestas, generando varios bloqueos paralizando las principales rutas del país.  
Adicionalmente, las consecuencias del cambio climático en el área del corredor seco están provocando una crisis de inseguridad alimentaria, con cerca de 4.9 millones de personas afectadas, según el análisis del CIF (Clasificación Integrada en Fases) para el periodo junio/septiembre 2022; lo que representa un 25% del total de la población. Estas afectaciones incrementan situaciones de desigualdad, pobreza y de violencia, incluida la violencia basada en género (VBG) y vulneración de los derechos de los niños, niñas y adolescentes, así como a grupos especialmente marginalizados como la población LGBTIQ+, indígena, en condición de discapacidad, generando desplazamiento al interior del país y hacia los países del norte del continente. 

Se estima, por lo tanto, que hay más de 2.9 millones de personas con necesidades de protección en Guatemala. Aproximadamente 41% de las personas con necesidades son mujeres adultas y un 40% NNA. Hasta diciembre de 2024, el clúster de protección proyecta cubrir las necesidades de al menos 810.000 personas. 

A esto se suma, que durante 2023 se generó un aumento del número de personas en movilidad humana (personas solicitantes de la condición de refugiado y refugiados, retornadas, desplazadas y migrantes en tránsito) que atraviesan el país. Según el Servicio Nacional de Migración de Panamá más de 400,000 personas habían cruzado el Darién en septiembre 2023, con la cifra más alta registrada en agosto 2023 de 82,000 personas. Los anuncios y cambios en la política migratoria regional de los EE. UU, han generado incertidumbre frente al futuro inmediato de las personas en Movilidad Humana y reflejan los desafíos institucionales que tiene el país para asegurar una respuesta adecuada y acceso a medidas de protección frente a la agudización de las necesidades humanitarias y recrudecimiento de las condiciones en la ruta (extorsiones, robos, violencia sexual).  

ACNUR Guatemala continuará trabajando con el gobierno, la sociedad civil y las comunidades para fortalecer el espacio de protección para refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, personas en movimientos mixtos y guatemaltecos con necesidades de protección; mediante la consolidación de iniciativas emprendidas en años anteriores. Para lograr nuestros objetivos de una manera más eficiente, nuestro enfoque basado en áreas contempla intervenciones priorizadas en comunidades con alta presencia de personas a las que servimos, en todas las áreas de responsabilidad. 

ACNUR se compromete a fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones estatales (incluyendo a las municipalidades) para proporcionar respuestas de prevención y protección para las personas a las que servimos para garantizar la sostenibilidad de las intervenciones.

project_name: Acceso y disfrute de los derechos básicos y fundamentales, reducción de la exposición a los riesgos de protección y asistencia humanitaria para las personas refugiadas y solicitantes de asilo, retornados, personas en movilidad y comunidades de acogida en Venezuela.
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivos la prevención, mitigación de riesgos y protección de las personas de interés del ACNUR en 71 comunidades priorizadas de Venezuela. Se trata de un proyecto multisectorial que trabajará en función a los derechos, servicios básicos y asistencia humanitaria para responder a problemas identificados tales como: 
1. Falta de acceso a servicios de asistencia y asesoría legal, así como a documentación legal. 
2. Incidentes de violencia de género y protección contra el abuso y explotación sexuales, acceso limitado para sobrevivientes a servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva, legales y de atención psicosocial.
3. Baja calidad constructiva y deficiente mantenimiento de infraestructura social y servicios básicos.
4. Gestión deficiente de espacios de Alojamiento temporal.
5. Deficiencia en el servicio eléctrico y ausencia de energías alternativas.
6. Limitado suministro del agua, así como su inadecuado almacenamiento, manejo y disposición final.
7. Dificultades de las organizaciones comunitarias para enfrentar sus problemas; falta de espacios para llevar a cabo actividades comunitarias.
8. Insuficientes ingresos familiares para cubrir las necesidades básicas; falta de formación y proyectos dedicados a medios de vida; falta de acceso a asistencia material para necesidades específicas y artículos básicos. 
9. Disminución de la calidad de los servicios de índole social por deterioro de la infraestructura.
ACNUR continuará trabajando en un contexto de población mixta donde los refugiados y solicitantes de asilo, así como las personas en movimiento, las personas en riesgo de desplazamiento, las personas en riesgo de apatridia, los retornados espontáneos y sus comunidades de acogida requerirán intervenciones de protección y salvaguardias. 
La protección basada en la comunidad seguirá siendo la base de la estrategia de la Operación para los grupos de población mencionados y ampliará su alcance geográfico a las zonas con una gran concentración de refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, retornados espontáneos, personas en movimiento y personas en riesgo de desplazamiento debido a las mayores necesidades y riesgos de protección.

project_name: Enhancing the delivery of quality protection services by improving the protection environment and supporting Durable Solutions for IDPs, returnees and host communities in Northeast Nigeria.
Protection Safety Nets for People of Concern in the Northeast.
project_objective:
As part of its mandate to provide protection and solutions, UNHCR through the Protection Safety Nets Project will initiate measures through livelihoods programming activities that will provide opportunities for returnees, IDPs and affected populations to recover their livelihoods and, acquire skills and capacities that enable them to engage in profitable income generating activities. Vulnerable households and individuals are provided a pathway to economic empowerment, recovery and durable solutions. The project aims to ensure that all persons of concern are able to make a safe and sustainable living that meets their basic needs, contributes to their dignity, and provides for the full enjoyment of their rights. The project will promote their resilience, limit negative coping behaviours that heightens protection risk exposures, as well protect the affected population from exploitation and abuse.

UNHCR will implement activities in support of this project in the following locations:
	Borno (Ngala, Maiduguri, Jere and Bama)
	Adamawa (Mubi North, Mubi South, Michika and Madagali)
	Yobe (Damaturu and Gujba)

The Project will provide opportunities for Women and Men, Girls and Boys, and PWDs– using the Age Gender and Diversity approach. UNHCR will ensure the achievement of this objective through the following means
I.	Enable Access to Agricultural / Livestock / Fisheries Production: Build capacities of vulnerable IDPs, Returnees, and affected populations - through training and support for activities in sustainable agriculture/livestock/fishery production to support economic self-reliance and reintegration.
II.	Facilitate Access to Self-Employment / Businesses: Promote business-oriented community-based cooperative units. Beneficiaries in such cooperatives will be provided necessary training – vocational skills, business management, financial literacy as well as business startup kits to undertake collective production and marketing of the produce.
The Protection Safety-net measures implemented through livelihoods programming will reduce needs, vulnerabilities, and heightened protection risk exposures - including sexual and gender-based violence risk exposures. It will also contribute to conducive conditions for durable solutions for IDPs and returnees, enhance community resilience and boost the provision of (or access to) sustainable livelihoods. These actions align with the Strategic Objectives of the 2023 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Strategy, the HCT Centrality of Protection Strategy (Nigeria, 2020), and the Strategy on Protection, Return and Recovery for Northeast Nigeria (2020).

project_name: Provision of Non-Food Items (NFIs) and Shelter Assistance to Vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
In 2024, UNRWA estimates that 155,500 of the most vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria will continue to require humanitarian assistance. Many among them struggle to secure basic shelter and NFI need, and will be supported by UNRWA through this project as part of the Humanitarian response Plan, while adhering to the shelter Sector technical guidance. 
The Humanitarian Needs Overview for 2024 underscores the profound impact of enduring political, economic, and humanitarian crises on Palestine refugees. An alarming October 2023 post-distribution monitoring survey revealed distressing trends: 92% borrowing food or seeking help, 64% reducing daily meals due to financial constraints, and 40% adopting emergency livelihood strategies, highlighting the diminishing ability to cope with increasing poverty.
The vulnerability of Palestine refugees was exacerbated by the February 2023 earthquakes. UNRWA records indicate a doubled number accessing Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) from February to June 2023, indicative of elevated trauma levels. The earthquakes displaced 1,511 households, adding to the 40% already in protracted displacement due to the Syrian conflict.
Between January and October 2023, 1,059 Palestine refugees returned to Syria, while others returned to camps, with a significant number returning to Yarmouk and Ein el Tal camps. However, challenges persist due to the high cost of living outside the camps. As of September 2023, around 2,000 families had returned to Yarmouk, 170 to Ein el Tal, and 750 to Deraa camp.
The comprehensive intervention comprises four key components:
a) Winterization: Providing 155,500 of the most vulnerable Palestine refugees with core NFIs for winterization in various locations, including blankets, mattresses, mats, and tarpaulin sheets. The unit cost of the winterization kit is approximately $51.12 per beneficiary.
b) In-kind distribution of NFIs: Targeting 500 families (1,690 beneficiaries) facing special hardship cases, eligibility dependent on assessments conducted by UNRWA social workers. The unit cost is approximately $78.35 per beneficiary, covering blankets, mattresses, kitchen sets, jerry cans, mats, tarpaulin sheets, solar lamps, plastic buckets, and wood stoves. Locations and eligibility depend on assessments to be conducted by UNRWA social workers.
c) Contingency stock of NFIs for 2,000 families (6,765 beneficiaries) for potential shocks. Planning depends on the scale and nature of any potential crisis.
d) Cash assistance for major shelter repairs: Targeting 653 families (corresponding to 2220 refugees considering the average family size  - 3.4 members - retrieved from the UNRWA registration and information system) in Ain Al Tal , Deraa and Yarmouk camps with an average transfer value of 3,500 USD /HH. It is worth mentioning that the actual transfer values that will be disbursed to the beneficiaries will depend on the income level of the agency, market conditions, and needs assessments by the agency and any future revisions of the values by the sector.  Distribution will occur through two financial service providers.

project_name: Provision of Core Relief and Seasonal Items for IDPs, Returnees and Host Community
project_objective:
UNHCR is the leading agency coordinating NFI responses in Syria, NES, and NWS. UNHCR will provide lifesaving and life-sustaining CRI support in cases of large-scale population movements, including refugee flows, IDPs, returnees, and affected host communities. The following situations may trigger such a response:
Natural Disasters: such as earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, tsunamis, droughts, or wildfires
Armed Conflict: Civil unrest, or violence leading to displacement and humanitarian crises
Public Health Crises: Outbreaks of infectious diseases, pandemics, or health emergencies resulting in population movements and significant humanitarian needs.
Sudden-Onset Crises: Sudden displacement due to eviction or building collapses.
Protection Concerns: Human rights abuses, persecution, discrimination, or threats to the safety and security of individuals or communities leading to displacement.
The support provided will encompass the distribution of essential relief alongside seasonal items during winter or summer periods.
The CRI assistance will be administered through inter-agency convoys to remote locations, in addition to the provision of seasonal items.
The project's objective is to assist approximately 475,000 individuals with CRIs and seasonal support when necessary. The assistance will also be extended to 25,000 individuals residing in hard-to-reach areas through Crossline interventions. Assistance will be directed towards vulnerable individuals based on established protection criteria and will be dispensed as a one-off allocation.

Needs
As outlined in the 2024 HNO, the overall NFI PiN has seen a 7 percent increase to 6.1 million. Given the current funding shortages, the limited NFI sector response in 2023 is anticipated to further compound needs as 2024 progresses. Essential core relief items are crucial for individuals, but unfortunately, they remain inaccessible to most due to affordability issues.
The data from 2023 supports this assumption, seeing a rise and expected to continue increasing in 2024, particularly following the destructive earthquake that struck the country in 2023.
UNHCR's CRI response will prioritize addressing significant population movements, in cases of large-scale population movements, including refugee flows, IDPs, returnees, and affected host communities, in addition to beneficiaries residing in camps and informal settlements. Furthermore, UNHCR plans to provide support to the NWS IA crossline, offering nearly 5,000 CRI kits and seasonal or supplementary items in line with identified needs.
UNHCR's initial cash feasibility assessment’s findings show that MPCA would be feasible, and the major market would be able to respond to increased demand as it has a good capacity to absorb the increase in demand. It is planned to be aligned with the targeted preference who already reported using markets as their main source for purchasing basic needs.

Implementation of activities

With available resources, UNHCR is strategically planning to supply CRIs and seasonal to more than 95,000 HHs within Syria. Furthermore, UNHCR intends to deliver CRI packages to serve 5,000 households through a crossline modality. These CRI kits consist of essential items such as blankets, mattresses, plastic sheets, jerry cans, and solar lamps, among others. The distribution plan prioritizes vulnerable groups, including unaccompanied minors, women, elderly individuals, and female-headed households, as well as those with physical or mental challenges.
Beneficiary identification is meticulously carried out by UNHCR Field Offices in collaboration with relevant authorities and sector partners to ensure a comprehensive approach and prevent duplication.

project_name: Education in emergencies response for the school aged children in Aleppo, Raqqa and Latakia
project_objective:
This project integrates a multi-sector approach, linking Education in Emergencies (EiE) with long-term development. It will be implemented in locations rated 4 on the education sector severity scale based on the HNO 2024: Al Thawara-Raqqa, Lattakia city, and Jabal Saman-Aleppo. Identified locations and schools were selected in collaboration with local authorities (Department of Education) and have been confirmed as areas of high need and potential for return. The main activities of the project include school rehabilitation,
provision of furniture to those schools, organizing NFE classes for out-of-school children and children at risk of dropping out, winterization distribution for all children, increasing the quality of education through teacher training, providing teaching and learning
materials to schools, and improving protection and psychosocial well-being of children in and outside the schools. At the same time, building on previous experience and following Education sector suggestions, the project will support graduating students enrolling in
national exams with transport support to reach the exam locations from students’homes. School rehabilitation works will include strong WASH elements by rehabilitating segregated and dignified WASH facilities in the schools, accessible for children with disabilities, as well as rehabilitating/installing water points that will be accessible not only for the students and staff of the schools, but also to the surrounding communities, thus expanding the number of people benefiting from the project. Hygiene materials will be distributed to schools and students, and students will receive COVID-19 awareness sessions. All schools will receive solar panels that will power the water pumps as well as provide lights in the schools that operate in two shifts, especially during the darker winter season. This project will support 4 NFE cycles within a 2-year project duration. In total, 6000 children will be positively affected by this project. The needs assessment for the proposed proposal was conducted in Aleppo, Latakia, and Raqqa governorates through field visits that took place in December 2023. During these visits, FCA's team assessed the situation of education services and facilities, as well as
the needs of students living in the communities targeted by the assessment, Three schools/areas were selected for project interventions after thorough consultation with the DoEs, the Education sector, and coordination with other INGOs:
In Aleppo:
- Rahmo Hattab School in Jabal Saman subdistrict, Jabal Saman district.
In Ar-Raqqa:
- Mesharefet Assab (in Debsi Afnan), Mansura subdistrict, Ath-Thawrah district.
In Latakia:
- Fares Saubaih (Al Jamhoureh street), Latakia subdistrict, Latakia District.
In the areas surveyed in Aleppo, Latakia, and Raqqa, an estimated 5300 children are outof school. The main reasons given by key informants were poverty, earthquakes, child labor, and child early marriage. The number of Out of School Children (OOSC) in the communities surrounding the three schools is 1000.
While Rahmo Hattab School and Meshrefet Essab are functioning, Fares Subaih School in Latakia is not operating due to significant damage caused by the February earthquake. Allthree schools are in dire need of rehabilitation due to their poor condition. The assessed schools present critical gaps not only in basic facilities, such as classrooms and bathrooms, but also in their overall structure. Most of the schools lack doors, windows, electrical cables, pipes, and tiles, making them unsuitable for immediate use. The remaining doors and windows require maintenance work as most are non-functional. One out of three schools are completely empty of furniture, while the other two have partially available furniture - noting that the average class occupancy in the three schools is around 55 students.

project_name: Building Resilient Communities in Aleppo
project_objective:
The project aims to increase resilience and enhance the community's access to basic services and livelihood opportunities in the Qadi Askar area in the Jebel Saman district in Aleppo. The initiative embodies three key outcomes: supporting basic services, increasing livelihood access, and strengthening social cohesion. Through a multifaceted approach, the project endeavors to install street lighting, remove debris, provide livelihood support, and empower communities, thereby fostering sustainability and inclusivity. This intervention will contribute to increasing safety and security in the community, enhancing community vitality, improving health and the environment, and creating opportunities for economic improvement and new job opportunities. It will also empower households in the community to achieve self-sufficiency and promote social cohesion and community participation.

At its core, the project resonates with the essence of recovery and renewal. Strengthening access to basic services includes lighting the streets through the installation of 20 solar-powered lighting panels. Beyond lighting, this initiative increases safety, security, and a renewed sense of community vitality, especially after dusk, while it will promote a safe feeling among the community members who move into the community during the evening. Concurrently, addressing environmental concerns becomes paramount, with plans to remove 5000 cubic meters of debris and 3500 tons of waste, thereby alleviating economic burdens and health hazards that mainly may cause in the dark evening where there is no lights in the streets.

Yet, the project's ambitions extend far beyond infrastructure. Recognizing the intertwined nature of livelihoods and community well-being, it ventures into economic empowerment. For 100 individuals, a lifeline emerges in the form of short-term Cash for Work opportunities, offering not just financial support but a chance to reclaim dignity through meaningful engagement. Moreover, 130 aspiring entrepreneurs receive tailored training and financial grants, heralding a new era of self-sufficiency and enterprise. Through vocational skills training, 70 young beneficiaries will find pathways to employment, underscoring the project's commitment to long-term prosperity.
The project will also equip 30 young volunteers with advocacy skills and community engagement tools to ensure community empowerment and ownership of the project. This will support the volunteers in mobilizing their peers and neighbors around common goals and initiatives, whether organizing community clean-up campaigns, advocating for improved access to services, or facilitating dialogue on pressing issues, the project will support the community to create their ERL plan and led the ERL process in their community.

project_objective: UNHCR, as the protection lead agency of the protection cluster, will continue  implementing core protection activities in northern Mozambique (while adapting them to the changing context), including providing civil documentation; legal assistance; housing, land and property (HLP) assistance; GBV prevention and response; child protection; community-based protection (CBP); protection capacity-building of duty- and rights-bearers; and protection monitoring, while ensuring accountability to affected populations, PSEA safeguards, localization, and age/gender/diversity approach that provides specialized responses for the most vulnerable groups, including women and girls, older people, people with disabilities, and other people with specific needs.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Nutrition Assistance in Greater Pibor Administrative Area.
project_objective:
The occurrence of multiple crises including insecurity, subnational violence, economic crisis (local currency depreciation) challenges compounded by the effects of climate-related shocks (flooding and dry spells), the ongoing effect of Sudan conflict (causing displacement) all adversely impact the food security of South Sudanese families. The country remains one of the most food insecure countries; with low agricultural production, household stocks depletes earlier than usual in many areas and staple food prices are atypically high, exacerbated by disrupted trade flows and increased demand related to the conflict in Sudan and influx of refugees and returnees. According to IPC report (Nov, 2024) 5.83 million people (46 percent of the population) are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity classified as IPC Phase 3 or above (Crisis or worse), with 1.64 million people in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency). Between July 2023 and June 2024, an estimated 1.65 million children between 6-59 months are expected to suffer acute malnutrition (AM) including 480,000 million children expected to suffer Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and 1.16 million expected to suffer Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM).
Pibor County is one of the hard-to-reach areas with frequent cattle raiding, inter- communal conflicts/displacement, age set fighting, negative cultural practice and high level of complex vulnerability. The Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) prevalence in the area is estimated to be 18.8% (3.9% SAM and 14.9% MAM) (Nutrition Cluster PIN data 2023). Under-fives, PLW and adolescent girls remain the worst affected by malnutrition. ForAfrika Positive Deviance Inquiry Study, Pibor County (2022 Report) shows that, among the poor households 53.7% (812 were non-positive deviant and only 40.2% of the population in Pibor utilize form of health care services in an area of high prevalence of diseases. Further, some women practice inappropriate feeding including poor breastfeeding/weaning and poor caring practices to the children whom are also at risks of many form of social and environmental norms including abductions. There is need to address the mentioned underlying causes of malnutrition.
ForAfrika will work with MOH/CHD to improve their capacity the proposed plan is to contribute to increase equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services to prevent malnutrition and build resilience among 19,222 children, 5,592 adolescents, and 21,676 women as Sectoral Objective 1 and in line with Strategic Objective (SO) 1: Vulnerable crises affected people have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to life-saving assistance to meet their needs and SO3 Vulnerable people’s capacity to withstand or cope with the impact of new and protracted crises is increased, and durable solutions to root causes of their vulnerability and shocks are enabled by humanitarian action.39 static nutrition sites (standalone and those embedded within health facilities) and 5 outreaches will be supported through Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) to reach out to 6,772 SAM cases in Outpatient therapeutic program(OTP) and 12,450 under 5 and 21,676 PLW in Targeted supplementary feeding program (TSFP). 163 children with SAM and medical complication will be reached in one Stabilization Centre. To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of wasting for 9804 girls and 9418 boys under five years of age and 12,450 PLW will be reached as a contribution to (SO1 & SO 2). ForAfrika will pilot the PD- Hearth menu and scale up the local nutrient food to combat malnutrition, integrated the response with health, Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihood (FSL), Education and Protection sectors to address key drivers of malnutrition. Stakeholders engagement AAP, protection mainstreaming and monitoring of the protection environment will be supported.

project_name: Enhance Safe and Dignified Living Conditions for the Rohingya refugees through Camp Management Services and Shelter/NFI Assistance
project_objective: The project aligns with the Shelter-CCCM Sector strategy and specific objectives. UNHCR and partners will continue to strengthen and improve a wide range of camp management components including; enhancing the capacity of camp management actors through targeted modular training, maintaining and improving camp facilities, facilitating access to services, advancing community participation, promoting adherence to camp management standards and practices, improvement of settlements infrastructure, combined with site planning to address vulnerability to natural hazards and foster natural resource management. In collaboration with the Office of the Refugee Relief and Repatriation (RRRC), IOM and Shelter-CCCM partners, UNHCR will work towards strengthening coordination structures, promoting good governance and civilian administration of the camps. The Capacity Sharing Initiative (CSI), undertaken with the RRRC, camp-in-charges (CiCs) and partner staff will advance the understanding and application of standards relevant to the sector. To encourage community participation and ownership, UNHCR will continue consulting and working with refugees to implement community-led projects under care and maintenance through cash for work (CfW) and material support. UNHCR will partner with other stakeholders to foster initiatives to promote peaceful co-existence amongst refugee and host communities in the camps. The Common Feedback Platform (CFP) will be harmonised and strengthened to increase access and speedy resolution of cases by respective sectors.. Recognizing Bangladesh's susceptibility to climate change, UNHCR will continue its efforts to enhance the resilience of both refugee and host communities. Results from the J-MSNA show that 96% of the population is satisfied with how humanitarian agencies have responded to natural hazards. UNHCR will also sustain its commitment to strengthening preparedness by ensuring the timely activation and deployment of personnel, providing necessary equipment, conducting relevant disaster risk management (DRM) trainings, drills and simulations and prepositioning essential relief items ahead of potential disasters. Adjustments to the LPG refill cycle, informed by data collection, underscore ongoing efforts to optimize efficiency. Advocacy and promotional activities, including the ongoing promotion of pressure cooker usage across the camps, aim to ensure higher utilisation rates. Recognizing the temporary nature of approved shelter material and the impact of seasonal hazards in Bangladesh, regular maintenance of refugee shelters throughout the year is deemed essential. In coordination with CiCs, UNHCR and its partners actively support refugee households in maintaining their shelters using bamboo, tarpaulin, rope, and wires. Additionally, tie-down kits are being considered for emergency distribution to reinforce shelters in anticipation of strong winds during monsoon and cyclone seasons. UNHCR remains committed to prepositioning contingency stocks and conducting distributions based on needs assessments and validation, drawing insights from the Joint Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (J-MSNA) and UNHCR's post-Distribution Monitoring Reports. Similarly, due to the temporary nature of site infrastructures developed with non-durable materials, UNHCR commits to regular maintenance to ensure the longevity and functionality of these infrastructures, fostering a sustainable and resilient environment in the camps. This includes maintenance of pathways, bridges, drains and slope stabilization works. In addressing environmental concerns, UNHCR seeks technical solutions which are aligned with the natural environment, ensuring safety, supporting good living conditions and promoting climate-friendly practices. Initiatives encompassing rehabilitation, disaster risk reduction, and biodiversity conservation will be sustained.   Refugees will continue to access non-food items (NFIs) and renewable energy solutions, including LPG refills.

project_name: Food and Livelihood Assistance for Resilience in South Sudan
project_objective:
This project is designed in alignment with the Food Security Cluster (FSL) Response Plan for South Sudan for 2024-2026. It seeks to contribute to the three main objectives of the FSL Cluster including (CO1) “provides food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations in IPC4 and IPC5 ”; (CO2) “enhance emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihoods and fishing and livestock supports” and (CO3) “Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks”. 
In 2024, the project plans to extend food and livelihood assistance for people facing severe food insecurity in 9 counties across five states of South Sudan. The project targets a total of 227,776 people expected to face severe food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or worse) specifically 8,134 people in Central Equatoria, 60,000 in Jonglei, 100,828 in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, 15,567 in Unity, and 43,247 people in Warrap State. Of these about 63,600 people will receive livelihood inputs to boost emergency food production. Further, the project will provide a fortified rice food (also known as Mannapack) to support over 3,400 returnees. 
The project will be premised on two major interventions which augment and reinforce each other’s. The pathway to food security starts with the direct delivery of food assistance to affected people which is designed to strengthen food security in the immediate term, in particular, during lean seasons. This will be complemented by interventions targeted at restoring local food production through the provision of key emergency livelihood inputs and resilience building measures. In doing so, the project will stabilize households in the short run by safeguarding livelihoods and remaining assets and lay the foundation for long term recovery.
Building on the consumption stability achieved through food assistance, the project will extend appropriate emergency livelihood inputs and skills as well as support community participation in asset creation actions which will lead to recovery of local food production and the development of durable and productive assets. This will in turn enhance food security, restore livelihoods, and build resilience to ongoing and future shocks and stressors.
Specific interventions include:
a)	General food distribution GFD and Asset Creation and Livelihood (ACL):  These are meant to provide access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food to address ongoing hunger among the most vulnerable people (IPC4 &5). The GFD assistance will be used to engage beneficiaries in value-added activities (GFD+) to facilitate shift in their mindset from ‘free food’ to self-reliance. While the ACL intervention encourages beneficiaries to get engaged in complementary asset creation activities such as restoration of crop lands which will in turn improve farmers’ productivity and resilience to shocks. 
b)	Providing emergency livelihood assistance including the distribution of crop and vegetable seeds, agricultural tools and fishing kits coupled with skill enhancement measures to stimulate local food production. Vegetable demo plots and kitchen gardens will be promoted to showcase best practices for improving production. To strengthen linkage with nutrition measures, kitchen gardens will be promoted as simple interventions that can promote improved nutrition at household level especially for families with malnourished children. The adoption of better farming and fishing methods will improve food self-sufficiency and reduce dependency on external food assistance in the long run.
The project will set up feedback mechanisms through which targeted community members can voice their needs, preferences and demand inclusive processes. It will also ensure conflict sensitive approach so as to safeguard the safety and security of target community and staff.

project_name: Provision of Basic Primary Health Assistance in Greater Pibor Administrative Area
project_objective:
In South Sudan at least more than 8 Million people in the country needs humanitarian assistance including health services. Legacy of conflict, food insecurity, flooding, disease outbreaks, weak economy and poor infrastructural development have resulted in a fragile health system. Moreover, the previous occurrence of COVID-19 Pandemic and the current influx of returnees, refugees and asylum seekers due to the Sudan crisis posed additional constraints to an already weak system. Women, men and children are in need of sufficient health care services whereas South Sudan’s still has poor health indicators including maternal mortality rate of 1,223/ 100,000 live births, child mortality at 81deaths/1,000 live births are at alarming level. Greater Pibor Administrative Area corroborates the national level and in need of humanitarian response. The health system is worsened by frequent population displacement and interruption of services due to sub-national violence and flooding. A substantial number of individuals in hard-to-reach remain without adequate services (only 12 Bomas supported by BHI). Health services is limited, only 17 (69%) of the 27 Health Facilities which are functional. The referral system is weak and worse during the rainy season due to physical access constraints. Health facilities structures are dilapidated and 60% of County health department (CHD) health workforce are not qualified. There is need to address issues of continuous low routine vaccine (50%) coverage which results to building up of cohorts of “Zero Dose” and under-vaccinated children, rendering them susceptible to the outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases (VPD). In reproductive health, while proportion skilled birth attendant is at 44%; women attends antenatal care 1 (ANC+1) at third trimester leading to low (26%) of mothers attending at least 4 ANC visits during pregnancy. The GPAA prevalence of wasting is above WHO emergency threshold i.e Pibor County GAM of 18.8% and Pochalla County increased from 10% to 19% (IPC Nov 2023 report). Menstrual hygiene management and handwashing practice at critical periods remain lacking. Barriers to access to health facilities, particularly for women include lack of female health workers, poor roads, leading to higher protection risks such as sexual abuse and harassment; and Mental Health and Psychosocial challenges.
	
To improve equitable access to life-saving essential comprehensive quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV, ForAfrika formerly (JAM), will work with MOH/ CHD and coordinate with other partners, cluster for integrated response that includes nutrition, protection and WASH. The plan is to support three (3) additional health facilities to meet WHO IPC Minimum Requirements, improve vaccine coverage, engage Community health workers to reach out to 20,000 individuals as well us consultation and treatment. ForAfrika intends to reach to more additional 420 pregnant women with skill birth services, 1383 persons with disability, Mental Health, Psychosocial support and at least 20 SGBV cases; key staff will be trained on case management to ensure eligible cases access basic services are referred accordingly. To respond to SO2, reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases and SO3; ForAfrika will ensure notification of diseases of potential outbreak within 24hrs, last mile deliveries of Interagency Emergency Health kits and at least 20 SGBV survivors receiving CMR services. Leveraging other interventions and platform, behavioral change communication including building capacity of Integrated community mobilization networks and BHI committees and other stakeholder, staff on AAP, lifesaving communication and other actions, consultative meetings shall be undertaken to identify needs, enable participation to reduce health impact.

project_name: Increase access to safe water and improved sanitation (WASH) for communities in need in South Sudan
project_objective:
The project's objective is to improve the health, dignity, and overall well-being of South Sudan communities through the provision of sustainable water and sanitation infrastructure and the promotion of good hygiene practices. The project's approach involves three main components: increasing access to safe and sustainable water for poor and vulnerable communities, reducing the incidence of WASH-related diseases by promoting personal hygiene and environmental practices, and integrating nutrition and health initiatives to foster institutional synergy. By implementing these measures, the project aims to improve the health outcomes of South Sudan communities while promoting sustainable development practices.
This project seeks to improve health, promote dignity and well-being of communities in South Sudan by providing appropriate water and sanitation infrastructure, and educate people on good hygiene practices. ForAfrika will contribute to the success of the WASH cluster in collaboration with the humanitarian response plan with the contribution to the WASH Strategic objectives and approaches ranging from CO1 to CO3 namely; 
1.	Contribution to the reduction of morbidity and mortality focusing on malnutrition through the WASH and Nutrition-integrated programming in targeted counties. 
2.	Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and mainstream protection with a focus on GBV mitigation (safety audits) and disability inclusion.  
3.	Provide durable access to services in long-term displaced sites and communities by building resilience. 

Of the total 5.5 million targeted people, ForAfrika will address the WASH needs of 45,455 people facing crisis in 3 Counties across 3 States of South Sudan. 18,656 people in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, 12,295 people in Jonglei State and 14,595 in Warrap State. 

The focus of this project will provide safe, adequate water, sanitation, and hygiene kits through the development of boreholes (deep wells and hand pumps) and solarization, pipeline expansion and reticulation, rehabilitation of wells, and improved water quality and monitoring. Construction of disability-friendly and gender-segregated sanitation facilities at institutional level and household, establishment of hygiene clubs/education for children and adults to promote hand washing practices. The complexities surrounding social behavior will be addressed through the introduction of social behavior communication change. Introducing cutting-edge innovative designs and technologies, the project seeks to improve access to safe and clean water sources, as well as promote the adoption of effective sanitation practices that reduce the incidence of waterborne diseases and other related health issues.
As part of our initiative for resilience and sustainability, we will provide training to community members on the operation and maintenance of water and sanitation facilities. They will lead various committees that promote ownership, community well-being, and improvements. This approach will foster a sense of ownership among community members while promoting their well-being. Women’s participation in leadership and decision-making will be encouraged ensuring each Water user committee is composed of women.  ForAfrika will lead the innovative provision through the provision of irrigation, water ponds and wells for domestic and farming purposes. To ensure Accountability to the affected population, ForAfrika will conduct community engagements addressing beneficiary entitlements, benefits and roles to play within the project implementation. In each community, ForAfrika will put in place complaint and feedback mechanisms such as Phone lines, suggestion book and utilize the monitoring feedback meeting to get feedback from the community. These summarize our approaches to the cluster objective with WASH integration with health, nutrition education food security and Livelihoods.

project_name: Femmes  au cœur des systèmes pour améliorer les conditions alimentaires et nutritionnelles des communautés vulnérables de la Région de Tillabéri
project_objective:
L'intervention vise à apporter une réponse aux besoins immédiat des personnes vulnérables (phase 3 et plus) dans un contexte d'insécurité alimentaire accentué par une crise alimentaire due à la mauvaise campagne agricole (sècheresse), une forte pression de déplacés internes/réfugiés fuyant l'insécurité et la nécessité de leur intégration sociale dans la paix avec les communautés hôtes. Elle vise l'amélioration des conditions de vie et de résilience des populations vulnérables victimes de la crise humanitaire dans la zone du Liptako Gourma au Niger. L'intervention agira sur la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations les plus vulnérables afin de restaurer et améliorer les capacités de production, augmenter la production de biens alimentaires de base, protéger les ressources naturelles et contribuer à la consolidation de la paix entre communautés. Il s'agira en particulier de développer un approche triple nexus qui puisse, d'un coté, répondre aux besoins plus urgents des populations vulnérables en particulier pendant la période de soudure et, de l'autre coté, soutenir une production agricole locale à travers l'accompagnement de 60 coopératives agricoles membres du partenaire FCMN. 
Le projet cible 300 ménages vulnérables (PDI et Hôte) qui recevront soit de vivres alimentaires soit de kits NFI et, en outre, un accompagnement dans le développement d'AGR. En plus de ses activités, la question de la scolarité sera abordée afin d'apporter une réponse aux enfants PDI abandonnant les écoles pour chercher de quoi survivre et faire des actions d'accompagnement des écoles par l'approvisionnement par les coopératives des fruits et légumes, le développement de jardin scolaire pour rendre plus résilients les futurs génération. En outre la Nutrition sera au centre de toutes les activités en matière de sensibilisation pour prévenir la malnutrition au niveau global.

project_name: Population has optimal access to quality education
project_objective: UNHCR will strive to ensure that Rohingya refugee children aged 3-18 years can access equitable quality education opportunities through existing programmes in the two registered camps in Cox’s Bazar, as well as through the delivery of additional interventions across other camps. This includes maintaining existing learning and WASH facilities, recruiting, training and deploying teachers, and procuring teaching and learning materials. UNHCR will construct additional classrooms with gender-segregated latrines and WASH facilities to accommodate additional learners. In support of the full rollout of the Myanmar Curriculum, a two-month basic pedagogy training will be provided to teachers from a range of education partners, along with refresher training for master trainers participating in the ongoing mentorship program. Considering Government of Bangladesh (GoB) directives on the non-use of the Bangla language, the introduction of the English version of the Bangladeshi curriculum or the use of any other English language curricula - as applicable to the two registered camps only - will represent a critical undertaking for 2024. An English language acquisition program for registered camp schoolteachers and continuous professional development for all teachers will be provided to ensure the required language competencies and teaching skills. Regular training on cross-cutting issues (e.g., child protection, gender and disability inclusion, gender-responsive pedagogy, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and mental health and psychosocial support) will also be provided. The project will recruit Rohingya women, who will be trained and deployed to ensure gender parity. There will also be a focus on disability inclusion through identifying children with disabilities, ensuring accessibility to the learning facilities, and providing individual support for the most vulnerable. In addition to mainstream education for 17,316 refugee children, UNHCR will continue providing Early Childhood Education (ECE) interventions for 1,400 children aged 3-4 years through community-based learning facilities aligning with sector standards. Additionally, UNHCR in collaboration with BARD College will implement a Language, Images, Analytical Thinking (LIT) youth empowerment and upskilling programme to promote the English language and soft skills related to analysis and communication including basic ICT skills development, as r those refugees who possess previous lower secondary level education but who have not previously received education either through the Myanmar Curriculum in the learning centres or registered camp secondary schools. After completing LIT, students will have the opportunity to move to the bridging programme and will be supported. Adolescents, especially girls who have completed the highest available level of education, will be organized into groups where they will participate in activities aimed at not only boosting their life skills and literacy skills, but also keeping them safe. UNHCR will continue ensuring community engagement in the overall project cycle through regular community consultations, monthly parent meetings, and monthly school management committee and Education Support Groups (CESG) meetings while maintaining Age Gender, and Diversity (AGD) principles. It will enhance school community governance and participation mechanisms by including the community in risk reduction activities, as well as integrating school community-based participatory planning and conducting community awareness on key areas as they emerge. UNHCR will continue its host community support by maintaining existing access to technology, renovating classrooms and WASH facilities, and providing classroom furniture and supplies. To ensure social cohesion and peacebuilding, the project will observe different days including 16 days of Activism, literacy days and refugee days, and organize annual cultural events and sports competitions.

project_name: Actions Intégrées EHA,VBG et SSR en faveur des communautés affectées par les conflits armés à répétition dans les régions de la Boucle de Mouhoun et de l’Est au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le Projet d’assistance humanitaire VBG, SSR et WASH dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun et de l’Est vise à renforcer la réponse d’urgence aux besoins immédiats des populations déplacées et communautés hôtes affectées par la crise humanitaire à répétition au Burkina Faso. Il se propose d’apporter un meilleur accès à une réponse holistique à ces populations, spéciquement pour les femmes et les adolescent.e.s dans les régions humanitaires de la Boucle du Mouhoun et de l’Est. Le projet mettra l’accent sur le renforcement des capacités des agents locaux dans ces domaines, y compris les aspects liés à la PSEA à travers la formation et le partenariat avec des associations locales comme SOS Jeunesse, OCADES, URCB et les autorités locales impliquées.
L’objectif général de l’action est de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des 22 000 personnes vivant dans les régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun et de l’Est d’ici décembre 2024 en leur favorisant un accès sûr et sécurisé aux services de base de VBG, SSR et WASH.
De façon spécifique, la satisfaction de cet objectif se fera principalement à travers des interventions qui consisteront dans ces régions au renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux avec une bonne implication des acteurs du Gouvernement pour faciliter l’accès aux services WASH, psychosociaux, sanitaires(SSR&Prise en charge clinique des violences sexuelles et violences entre partenaires intimes), économique et sociale de qualité, mais aussi pour atténuer les risques de VBG pour les femmes et filles, à travers les objectifs specifques ci-après :
GBV
1. -Faciliter l’accès à une prise en charge holistique de qualité aux survivant.es des VBG conformément aux directives inter-agences de gestion des cas de VBG.
2. -Renforcer les capacités techniques et matérielles des acteurs locaux, y compris les organisations féminines à base communautaire pour un accès aux services de qualité aux survivant.es de VBG dans les zones d’intervention.
3. Contribuer à la prévention et la mitigation des risques des violences basées sur le genre pour les femmes et les "lles dans les différentes zones de programmation.
SSR :
1. Renforcer les capacités des structures de soins à fournir des services de SSR de qualité aux femmes et adolescent.e.s touché(e)s par la crise humanitaire ;
2. Renforcer l’intervention communautaire en SSR au pro"t des femmes et adolescent.e.s touché(e)s par la crise humanitaire
3. Améliorer la gestion des données relatives à la couverture des interventions en SSR.
WASH
1. Assurer un accès sur et équitable a l’eau de qualité et en quantité pour la boisson et d’autres besoins aux femmes, hommes, les et garçons dans le besoin dans les zones du projet
2. Assurer un accès sécurisé, adéquat et à tout moment à des infrastructures d'assainissement aux femmes, hommes, filles et garçons dans le besoin 
3. Améliorer les pratiques d'hygiène des femmes, hommes, filles et garçons dans les zones du projet L'implémentation de ce projet sera effectué à travers des partenaires nationaux (ONG) membres de la société civile sélectionnés en tenant compte de leur niveau d'engagement dans les deux régions et leur capacité d'implémentation. Un plan de leur renforcement des capacités sera renforcé et suivi durant toute la durée d'implémentation du projet.
Une coordination sera renforcée avec d'autres ONGs actives dans ces régions et avec les acteurs gouvernementaux engagés dans les mêmes secteurs.
Un cadre de redevabilité local sera renforcé à travers différents leaders communautaires et les membres de la communauté afin d'assurer le suivi du mécanisme mise en place pour recueillir les plaintes et donner des feedbacks. Le renforcement des capacités  du comité de gestion sera fait pour assurer un meilleur traitement des plaintes et la remontée des feedbacks en toute sécurité et confidentialité.
