project_name: Emergency WASH  Support to needy Populations in South Sudan
project_objective:
This emergency WASH response is to support conflict affected and natural disaster affected populations in 4 counties 3 of which are part of the 15 counties of the South Sudan WASH Severity Classification 4 (WSC 4) for 2022. The project aims to provide support for basic WASH services to households, healthcare centres and nutrition therapeutic centres, including COVID 19 prevention and mitigation support. This is a 9-month project that will have a strong component to support and mainstream GBV, AAP and disability inclusion into the project. The project is focused on supporting communities that have been affected by floods, intercommunal violence including displaced and host communities whose access to safe water has been constrained resulting in the high prevalence for poor WASH related diseases and high rates of malnutrition which is compounded by poor WASH services.

The project will mostly focus on the improvement of access to safe water through (1) rehabilitation of existing hand pumped boreholes (2) surface water treatment  (3) household water treatment and provision of water handling and storage containers (4) construction of flood proof institutional latrine construction (5) hygiene promotion  
The project will work to achieve its objectives through WASH Cluster Sectoral objective 1, to achieve the HRP Strategic Objective 1. The project will reach a total of 355,969 people with a budget of  640,000 USDs. NCA will be directly responsible for the implement this project working in partnership with two national partners this approach will ensure the localisation of aid as well as capacity building of local entities. 

NCA being an international ecumenical actor has commitments under the grand bargain to support local partners to deliver humanitarian assistance to a high quality and degree and this project will also ensure resilience of local communities and CBOs in WASH service provision by having components that will promote resilience through training water committees, supporting local government actors and line ministries in WASH service provision. NCA has a static presence in Budi, Kapoeta South, Gogrial East, Tonj North and Gumuruk in Pibor. NCA is also implementing activities in Kapoeta East, Tonj East and Aweil South counties.

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items response for disaster affected communities of  Aweil East, Baliet, Fashoda, Longchuk, Nasir, Maiwut, and Manyo counties  of South Sudan
project_objective: Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) demonstrates unwavering commitment and active engagement in providing vital emergency support, particularly focusing on Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFI) within South Sudan's Aweil East, Baliet, Fashoda, Longchuk, Nasir, Maiwut, and Manyo counties of South Sudan. Our response strategy is founded on our extensive experience in emergency interventions and our ongoing efforts in NFI, Multi-purpose Cash, and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) programs. With this project, NCA's targeted goal is to assist approximately 45,000 individuals, specifically aiming to reach 20,000 males and 25,000 females within these target areas. Our strategic project focuses on cash voucher assistance, the distribution of shelter materials, and household non-food items, integrating these interventions within our broader emergency response initiatives. These efforts are part of NCA's holistic approach, intertwining Gender-Based Violence prevention and WASH programs within South Sudan. By implementing these strategic interventions, our project seeks not only to provide immediate relief but also to instill resilience and contribute to the long-term recovery of communities grappling with these crises. NCA's approach remains guided by the urgency of the situation, ensuring that our interventions are precisely tailored to address the most pressing needs of vulnerable individuals and families. In doing so, we aspire to kindle hope and actively participate in rebuilding lives amid the ongoing crisis in South Sudan.

project_name: Responding to humanitarian WASH needs with focus on Resilience in Damascus, Rural Damascus, Aleppo, Idlib, Hama, Lattakia, Ar Raqqa, As Sweida, Dara’a and Tartous Governorates
project_objective:
In 2024, 16.7 million people (8.4 million female, 8.3 million male) are assessed to need humanitarian assistance across Syria, up from 15.3 million in 2023. Of the 16.7 million people in need, 5.5 million are displaced, including over 2 million who live in last resort sites. After 12 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their situation worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Türkiye on 6 and 20 February 2023. The earthquakes uprooted hundreds of thousands of families, resulted in almost 5,900 deaths and more than 12,800 people injured in Syria, and severely damaged infrastructures already weakened by the conflict. The erosion of basic service capacity has continued, with water and sanitation systems, and public health services under immense strain, in a context of barely any development investment. Recurrent disease outbreaks, waterborne diseases, a prolonged drought and water crisis, vaccine-preventable illnesses, and food insecurity are contributing to rising mortality and morbidity. 
The main purpose of NCA’s WASH program is to reduce health-related and protection risks among conflict-affected populations by providing sustainable access to safe water, adequate sanitation, and improved hygiene. This will address the need for long term prevention and control measures for maintaining public health, and for promoting socio-economic development among the target communities. The involvement of local stakeholders is important so as humanitarian crises are not used to reduce what needs to be maintained as a public service. The targeting adheres to sector needs and priorities, as identified and reported in the HRP and HNO 2024, this being the best guarantee of a truly good outcome. Activities include the use of renewable energy (solar power) for pumping and distributing water; monitoring and optimising groundwater extraction using remote sensing; operation and maintenance training and tools for pump operators; and the support of vulnerable groups with the distribution of essential hygiene items and awareness that meet family needs and are gender appropriate. In terms of geography, the targeting is informed by the needs as expressed by the severity scale for HNO 2024, with priority given to sub-districts with overall score of 4 or 5. Overall score of 3 is also considered under some conditions, e.g., if corresponding overall score for protection/GBV sectors is high. Relevance with recent, ongoing, and planned projects implemented through NCA directly, and through local partners is also considered.
The selected governorates and potential locations at the sub-district level are: 
(i)	Damascus (Damascus)
(ii)	Rural Damascus (Haran Al'awameed, Kafar Batna), 
(iii)	Aleppo (As-Safira, Jabal Saman, Al Khafsa), 
(iv)	Hama (Shat-ha, Oj, Kfar Zeita) 
(v)	Idlib (Khan Shaykun)
(vi)	Lattakia (Lattakia, Al Qardaha)
(vii)	Tartous (Sheikh Bader)
(viii)	As Sweida (As Sweida)
(ix)	Dara’a (Dara’a)
(x)	Homs (Hawash)
(xi)	Ar Raqqa (Ath Thawra)
In summary, the project will address: 
a) Access to safe water (also related to public health and protection risks) 
b) Access to essential hygiene items to most vulnerable groups (women, girls, disabled, elderly, etc.) 
c) Resilience of public water systems (O&M and environmental protection)
d) Access to safe sanitation facilities
NCA has established office in Damascus since 2021 and has a team consisting of program and support staff. Furthermore, NCA has secured core funding for its direct implementation of WASH activities in selected areas in 2024. This will allow NCA to coordinate with all stakeholders and targeted communities and in close coordination with the WASH Cluster. Activities will be reported in the 4Ws by NCA's program/MEAL team
For this project, NCA will target total of 100,510 people (29,148 W, 26,133 M, 20,102 G,25,127 B), and has secured approx. 56% of requested budget for 2024 activities

project_name: Improving the Food Security and livelihood situation of vulnerable Households in Malakal, Fashoda, Panyikang, Pigi canal and Fangak Counties
project_objective:
The effects of Sudan conflict have affected more than 300,000 South Sudanese returnees including Sudanese refugees. Over 500,000 thousand people are expected to cross to South Sudan by the end of December this year (2023). The targeted states are leading in receiving the highest number of affected people include Upper Nile and Jonglei States of South Sudan.
Generally, the food insecurity situation in Jonglei and Upper Nile state has remained poor due to prolonged flood situation, dry spells, existing conflict and insecurity, low agricultural production and the current influx of refugees and returnees from the Sudan conflict. To address the flood & Conflict induced acute food insecurity situation (IPC4) as well as livelihood need of most vulnerable households in the above counties, ADA intends to carry out the following interventions;
a) Food Assistance: Address immediate household food security needs through provision of food ratios to vulnerable household.
b) Climate Smart Agriculture:  Through flood adaptive agriculture practices to promote and increase production among the most vulnerable households.
c) Economic Recovery: Through Livelihood interventions for example the Village Savings and Association (VSLA).
d) Cash Based Programming: For immediate access to basic needs.

project_name: Provision of Protection response to Children and their Caregivers in Renk, Fangak, Panyikang, Pigi/Canal, Ayod and Malakal Counties of Jonglei and Upper Nile States
project_objective: Africa Development Aid intends to provide quality protection services to crisis-affected children and their caregivers in Ayod, Pigi, and Fangak Counties of Jonglei State, Malakal, Renk and Panyikang Counties of Upper Nile State. Emergency Response to 600 Unaccompanied and Separated children through family tracing and reunification services. Emergency response to 21,000 children, adolescents and caregivers through community-based mental health and psychosocial support interventions, conduct parental sessions on child protection issues affecting children in the community. 3750 children with different protection concerns will receive  case management services through cash based initiatives. Conduct 30 awareness raising on child protection issues, formation of community based child protection committees to identify key protection concerns and help in advocacy on how to solve issues affecting children in the communities. Establishment and update of Child Protection referral pathways and training of women and men (community leaders or humanitarian and government staff including ADA staff ) trained on Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE) these are inline with Protection cluster objects on response plan to child protection issues for both returnees and host communities in South Sudan. A total of 30,000 people (15,000 Males and 15,000 females) will benefit from this project. Out of this, 15,000 will be children (7,500 girls; 7,500 boys) and 15,000 will be adults – 5,000 males and 10,000 females. However, out of the total beneficiaries 30% will be from the host community while 30% will be from Returnees and 40% from IDPs.

project_name: Providing physical protection through Shelter and Core Relief Items Support in the Northwest and Southwest

project_objective: UNHCR will continue to ensure the centrality and mainstreaming of protection across the shelter and NFI response, supporting the prompt delivery of immediate lifesaving shelter and NFI assistance to newly displaced people; alongside carefully targeted support for improved shelter solutions for protracted populations residing within temporary, and relocation sites or returning to places of origin.

project_name: Coordination et Gestion des sites pour les personnes déplacées internes et rétournées dans la Région de l’Extrême-Nord
Securing solution and protection for displaced persons and returnees in the Far North of Cameroon
project_objective:
The Boko Haram insurgency that started in Nigeria spread quickly in the Far-North Region of Cameroun early in 2014 and continues to date, primarily impacting the districts in the west along the border with Nigeria (Logon Chari, Mayo Sava, and Mayo Tsanaga).  In 2020 and 2021, intercommunal conflict broke out in the eastern part of the Region, along the border with Chad (Logon Birni and Mayo Danay, with displacement to the Diamare as well). 

The protection situation in the Far North Region is a mixed situation, complex and marked by violence and rights violations against civilians. In addition, the region is recovering from the 2021 intercommunal conflict which resulted in additional displacements and unresolved tensions between pastoralists, farmers, and fishermen. Both conflicts resulted in increased gender-based violence, abductions of civilians, destruction and looting of property, illegal or arbitrary arrests, and limitations on freedom of movement.  Furthermore, seasonal flooding regularly destroys property and livelihoods, reducing the resilience of the already vulnerable populations.  

This led to continual displacement of people to and within the Far North, both internally and externally, including the arrival of over 100,000 refugees from Nigeria.  According to the latest figures, more than 450,000 persons are internally displaced in the Far-North Region due to armed conflict and intercommunal conflict, while another 200,000 have returned to precarious situations in their communities and are at risk of being displaced again. 

According to HNO analysis, nearly 425,000 of these displaced and returned persons need a well-designed and delivered protection response. 

In 2024, through a community-based approach, UNHCR will secure protection and provide solutions through a comprehensive response in 4 key areas during the year: 1) strengthening the centrality of protection and protection monitoring, 2) coordination of the protection sector, long with the respective sub-sectors of GBV, Child Protection and HLP; 3) promoting and securing solutions, and 4) meeting urgent protection needs of the affected communities. 

The project is fully aligned with the objectives and activities of the protection sector, and specific activities include reinforced and expanded protection monitoring, using the Projet21 methodology and joint analysis, building community engagement around solutions, and strengthening communities’ ability to respond to protection incidents. Interventions will focus on responding to critical GBV and child protection needs and support for civil documentation. In-kind support, cash-based interventions, legal assistance, and referrals to available services will be an integral part of the response.

The search for solutions will follow an area-based approach selecting specific areas and sites in the districts most affected by the displacement and working with all stakeholders in the displaced, host community, local authorities, civil society, and agencies working in the areas. The approach will ultimately contribute to building sustainability of key services and consequently prevent displacement, develop conditions favorable to return as well and guarantee greater accountability to affected populations (AAP).

project_name: Increasing equitable access of essential, and quality healthcare service to 74,571 populations in Jonglei, Unity, Upper Nile and Warrap states South Sudan
project_objective:
This project will support flood & food-insecure affected 74,571 beneficiaries (Men 11,186, Women 18,643, Boys 20,134 and Girls 24,608) in Jonglei, Unity, Upper Nile and Warrap States. to improve essential healthcare services. HFO will undertake the responsibility to implement PHC services activities to achieve the health cluster and Ministry of Health sectoral objectives.

 The response will focus on providing basic essential health services in line with national and international humanitarian standards and is based on the epidemiological evidence of disease outbreaks, disease burden seasonality and trauma-related emergency issues. Prevention, preparedness, response readiness and mitigation activities will be supported with special attention given to vulnerable groups including women, children and persons with disabilities.

 HFO in collaboration with the Cluster at the national, state Ministry of Health, County health departments and other implementing partners will support different intervention modalities suited to the needs of affected people.  readiness activities addressing the Hepatitis E Virus in Rubkona and Fangak. HFO will link static facilities with mobile outreach  Teams and community-based healthcare systems (Boma health initiatives) to serve communities who do not have access to health care facilities (>5KM) as part of humanitarian development. 

HFO plans to strengthen the capacity of health staff at the field level to support and coordinate with CHD, Boma health workers. HFO will be collaborating with developmental partners UNICEF and WHO by providing regular health services through static health facilities in crisis-affected 10 states of South Sudan by identifying communities that are still not reachable. 

HFO will provide services through 2 MTs in each county as well as strengthening Mobile outreach Teams, PHCU and PHCCs in targeted Counties with improved access to essential health services will contribute to the overall reduction of the high maternal mortality rates and under-five mortality rates in women and children and mitigate the transmission of vaccine-preventable and other infectious diseases. HFO will coordinate with CHD, other partners in the planning and organizing of emergency health services. Our national, state and county-level coordination mechanism will be utilized to coordinate, collaborate, monitor and review the response activities. Management of SGBV as part of CMR and Referral pathways for mental health and SGBV survivors for psychosocial support. MNCH emergencies will be streamlined and strengthened. 

Referral pathways will link the community and facility-based health care system to provide continuity of care such as BHIs linkages and engagement. HFO will encourage and support IPC and WASH in health facilities including Hepatitis E Measles appropriate preventive measures that are expected to continue improving health services outcomes of affected populations. Health project will ensure to coordinate with partners at all levels to comprehensively integrate and collaborate with Nutrition, WASH and in some extend with FSL. HFO targeted populations is informed by the inter-sectoral prioritization and information analyzed, the health sectoral severity analysis and a review of disease infection risk by county. We will monitor and evaluate all these activities through IDSR, 5Ws and DHIS2 to CHD, Cluster, WHO and MoH. HFO gets IEHK from WHO, MoH, CHD and PPE from IOM and WFP to support the response.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle et intégrée aux besoins urgents des populations les plus affectées dans les Régions du Centre-Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun, Nord
project_objective:
La présente intervention vise à répondre aux besoins multi sectoriels en abris & AME, WASH et Protection nés de la crise humanitaire en cours. La détérioration continue de la situation se traduit par un accroissement des besoins dans plusieurs secteurs au Centre-Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun et du Nord qui demeurent les régions les plus touchées par la crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso. Son objectif global est de contribuer à améliorer la fourniture d'abris d'urgence et l'amélioration des moyens de subsistance des personnes affectées, l’accès à l’eau à l ’hygiène et à l ’assainissement (EHA) ainsi que à la protection des populations.
Sur une durée de 12 mois, l’action sera mise en œuvre par SOLIDEV avec les communautés et les autorités locales. Au total, le projet ciblera 25 000 personnes bénéficiaires (13 000 femmes et 12 000 hommes) y compris les personnes handicapées dans les régions du Centre-Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun et du Nord.
EHA : Le contexte est caractérisé par la persistance des gaps en matière d ’accès aux infrastructures et services EHA résultant des afflux continus de PDI avec une augmentation continue des besoins que les interventions peinent à résoudre.
Abris & AME : Les activités sont axées sur la fourniture d'abris d'urgence et l'amélioration des moyens de subsistance des personnes affectées dans les communes de Nouna et Tougan. 
Protection : La protection reste préoccupante. Des incidents de VBG tiennent la tête des cas rapportés. Les femmes et filles sont sujettes à plusieurs types de VBG avec des cas d’exploitation sexuelle, de violences physiques et psychologiques, de déni des ressources et séparation familiale, etc. L’accent sera mis sur l’organisation des activités de sensibilisation, la formation sur la prévention et l ‘atténuation des risques des VBG.
Changements climatiques : Les actions viseront à promouvoir l’éco-citoyenneté et l’éco-responsabilité, d’une part, et à vulgariser un changement de comportement favorable à la préservation et à la protection de l’environnement d’autre part. 
Il ressort des besoins des communautés que des Gap subsistent et révèlent une insuffisance dans la couverture des besoins, la faible couverture des besoins en eau, hygiène et assainissement (EHA) et le manque criard des abris & AME. De même, on note la forte méconnaissance des risques de protection et les lois y relatives. Toute chose qui constitue un terrain propice à l ’augmentation des cas de VGB
Les impacts attendus du projet sont les suivants :
- La construction des abris d’urgence et la distribution pour des ménages déplacés internes;
- L'Amélioration de l´accès à l´eau, aux services d´EHA des communautés ciblées 
- L'Amélioration de l’environnement protecteur en termes de réduction des cas des Violences basées sur le Genre (VBG) et des cas d’Exploitation et des Abus Sexuels (EAS) ;
- L'Amélioration de la qualité de la réponse via des mécanismes de redevabilité et de programmation sûre ;
Le projet adoptera une approche participative en soutenant la participation significative des femmes, des filles et groupes à risque (personnes en situation de handicap, personnes âgées) à chaque étape de la mise en œuvre. Le respect des principes de protection sera mis en avant afin de promouvoir un accès significatif à l ’aide humanitaire, dans la sécurité et la dignité. Il s ’agira concrètement de veiller à ce que le projet ne crée pas et n ’exacerbe pas des risques existants en organisant des activités de renforcement de capacités sur la programmation sûre. Ces activités aideront à prévenir et atténuer d’EAS y compris les VBG dans les zones cibles sur la base des analyses des risques systématiquement effectuées et actualisées durant la mise en œuvre du projet. 
La mise en œuvre de ce projet se fera en collaboration avec les différentes directions régionales des services techniques concernés de l’Etat.

project_name: PROJET MONITORING DE PROTECTION HARMONISE ET DE FRONTIERES ET ASSISTANCE MULTISECTORIELLE EN FAVEUR DES PERSONNES DEPLACEES INTERNES, DES RETOURNES ET AUTRES POPULATIONS AFFECTEES AU SUD, A L’EST ET A L’OUEST DU TCHAD
project_objective: Le projet « Monitoring de Protection harmonisé dit Projet 21 et de frontières en faveur des personnes déplacées internes, retournées et autres populations affectées et assistance multisectorielle », sera mis en œuvre dans les trois zones du Tchad à savoir le Sud, l’Ouest et l’Est. Ces trois zones sont caractérisées par des déplacements forcés de populations. En effet, le contexte de l’opération du Tchad reste                                                    marqué par une situation sécuritaire fragile aussi bien à l’intérieur du pays que dans les pays frontaliers. Cette fragilité est accentuée par la crise politico-sécuritaire qui sévit actuellement au Soudan et qui a entrainé le déplacement forcé de personnes y compris les retournées à l’Est. Quant à la zone Sud, elle a été affectée par des conflits intra et intercommunautaires, notamment des attaques d’individus armés qui ont provoqué de nombreux déplacements, des pertes de vies humaines et des dégâts matériels alors même que la capacite de retraite est faible.  Par ailleurs, dans la province du Lac à l’ouest, des éléments des groupes armés non étatiques (GANE) continuent par leur activisme d’accentuer la vulnérabilité des populations déplacées de force et des communautés hôtes. L’objectif poursuivi à travers la mise en œuvre des activités de monitoring de protection harmonisé dit P21 à l’Est, au Sud et à l’Ouest est de renforcer l’environnement de protection des personnes déplacées de force y compris les personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et les membres des communautés hôtes (y compris ceux à risques d’apatridie). Pour mémoire, le monitoring de protection harmonise ou encore dit régional ou P21 est le monitoring de protection comportant plusieurs outils harmonisés et interconnectés. Il s’agit de la collecte continue des perceptions des communautés sur l’évolution des risques et de leur environnement de protection auxquelles elles sont confrontées, à l’aide d’outils harmonisés à l’échelle régionale (questionnaires « ménages » et « informateurs clés ») et l’outil de suivi des incidents individuels de protection.

project_name: acces aux services de protection et aux solutions durables pour les commuanautes affetectees  par les crises humanitaires au Niger
project_objective:
En 2024, en partenariat avec le gouvernement du Niger, le HCR prévoit de soutenir les personnes déplacées internes (PDI) dans 5 régions touchées par les mouvements de population (Diffa, Maradi, Niamey, Tahoua et Tillabéry), en mettant l'accent sur la protection et les solutions.
Le HCR assurera son rôle de co-coordonnateur du cluster protection et des groupes de travail protection. En collaboration avec ses partenaires, le HCR accompagnera le Niger dans la mise en œuvre de la stratégie nationale des solutions durables des PDI dans les régions concernées, adoptant une approche zonale, ainsi que la diffusion de la loi de 2018 sur la protection et l'assistance aux PDI. De plus, il étendra ses activités de protection en veillant à ce que les PDI aient un accès non discriminatoire aux services sociaux de base et puissent participer activement aux décisions qui affectent leur vie. Les interventions de protection seront axées sur les activités suivantes.

Dans le domaine des LTB, les activités du projet incluent :

project_name: Protection  des populations affectées par la double crise sécuritaire et humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective: Le Burkina Faso traverse une crise sécuritaire sans précédent à la suite d’attaques de groupes armés (GA) qui s’étendent notamment sur les régions du Sahel, de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Nord, du Centre-Nord, du Centre Est, des Hauts-Bassins, des Cascades et de l’Est. L’activisme des GANI continuent à provoquer  des déplacements massifs de population dans presque toutes les régions du pays. Au 31 mars 2023, le Burkina Faso comptait 2 062 534 personnes déplacées internes (PDI) enregistrées sur une base individuelle par le CONASUR. 81% de ces PDI se concentrent dans les régions du Sahel, Centre Nord, Nord, Est, Boucle du Mouhoun et Centre Est. Le Burkina Faso traverse ainsi une crise de protection du fait du nombre de PDI, des multiples déplacements que subissent les ménages, de l’inaccessibilité à certaines populations, de certaines fragilités préexistantes à la crise notamment des conflits intercommunautaires souvent autour de la bonne gouvernance et des questions  foncière, particulièrement des tensions inter communautaires accentuées par des suspicions d’affiliation de certaines communautés aux GANI ou aux milices armées, de la présence dans ces régions de PDI, retournés burkinabè, réfugiés, et communautés hôtes très vulnérables ayant tous des besoins de protection et vivant dans des zones avec un faible accès aux moyens de subsistance . Les PDI et leurs communautés d’accueil font face à l’insécurité, l’inaccessibilité ou la faible accessibilité aux vivres, à l’eau, à l’éducation, à la santé, au bien être psychosocial et aux moyens de subsistance dans des communes déjà fragilisées par l’impact du changement climatique. Dans sa stratégie Pluriannuelle 2021-2025 et dans sa stratégie régionale pour le Sahel central, le HCR a réaffirmé son accompagnement au Gouvernement dans leur gestion des populations affectées par la crise avec des activités de Protection, Education, Abris/Articles Ménagers Essentiels (AME), Energie et Environnement. Ces priorités définies par le HCR sont en lien avec le nouveau programme national de développement économique et social (PNDES). Fort de cette analyse de la crise de protection au Burkina Faso, de l’existence des cadres d’action du HCR et du gouvernement du Burkina Faso, et de sa volonté d’accompagner le cluster protection dans la réalisation de ses objectifs sectoriels dans le cadre du HRP 2024, le HCR propose ce projet de protection des populations affectées par le conflit dans les  régions prioritaires autour de: l’enregistrement des PDI en soutien au CONASUR afin d’assurer que ces PDI puissent bénéficier d’une protection et d’une assistance humanitaire optimale ; la documentation des PDI, retournées et autres communautés vulnérables pour leur faciliter l’accès aux droits fondamentaux et leur éviter des violations de droits et libertés ; le monitoring de protection qui complète l’analyse issue de l’enregistrement et qui tient compte de la mobilité des PDI ; l’engagement communautaire et la redevabilité qui sera renforcée dans tous les domaines d’intervention pour garantir la participation, l’inclusion, la communication avec les communautés, l’éducation à la paix, la Protection contre l’exploitation et les abus sexuels et la redevabilité; la protection contre les violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et la protection de l’enfant (PE) y compris les activités de prévention, de mitigation des risques, de réponse multi sectoriels aux VBG et à la PE ainsi que l’assistance juridique et judiciaire ; la facilitation de l’accès consensuel et sécurisé des PDI à la terre au niveau individuel et collectif pour leur protection et pour une cohabitation pacifique.

project_name: Improving Skills and Economic Opportunities for the Refugees in Cox’s Bazar
project_objective: The project aims to assist refugees in acquiring transferable and portable skills relevant to the labour market needs in Myanmar and the camp context. This is with the objective of supporting refugees' sustainable return and integration in Myanmar when conditions permit, as well as enabling refugees to maintain hope for the future and lead dignified and productive lives in the camps, including through engagement in multi-sectoral camp-based activities, minor livelihood activities and community works, through the utilisation of acquired competencies. Accordingly, strategies will be geared towards enhancing skills development, economic and social empowerment, and self-reliance of the Rohingya refugees, pending durable solutions. UNHCR will also enhance the engagement of refugee women in productive activities inside the camps, with participants producing female hygiene materials for distribution in the camps. This will be achieved by strengthening the quality of final products, including through improving production processes and upgrading current production centres. The project will develop occupation-based skills with globally recognised competency standards (level 1) for 6,500 refugees aged 18+ years that include all gender groups and persons with disabilities (will be assessed during enrolment by using Washington Group Short Set Questions). An additional 250 refugees who complete occupation-specific skills training will receive industry readiness training to prepare them for immediate sector involvement. The project will implement 10 competency standards-based training for refugees inside the camps. The project will create income generation/self-employment opportunities for the skills-training graduates, covering 4,800 graduates who completed the training both during 2023 and in earlier years. The production of female hygiene materials and jute bags for distribution in the camps will also be facilitated through production activities, which will engage around 800 semi-skilled/skilled volunteers on a payment basis. In 2024, UNHCR will continue implementing pre-vocational education (accelerated adult literacy) for Rohingya adolescents and adults aged 18-24 in the Rohingya refugee camps. As part of the project, UNHCR will provide pre-vocational education to 11,568 youths. The course will cover basic literacy, numeracy, functional English, and life skills knowledge for the learners. To ensure the quality of the adolescent program, UNHCR will provide a basic pre-vocational module for training participants on literacy, numeracy, and soft skills for the adolescent program. In 2024, UNHCR will roll out an International English Language Testing System (IELTS) training. Administered by the British Council and co-owned and franchised by IDP Global, and assessed and validated by Cambridge, the IELTS is a globally recognized standardized test designed to assess the English language proficiency of non-native English speakers. The training will mainly target 150 refugee graduates who intend to apply for the Japan Initiatives for Education Pathways (JIEP) programme.

project_name: Education Support to IDPs and Returnees
project_objective:
The project aims to enhance equitably and quality access to education for crisis-affected IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable children aged between 5-17 years. Schools are destroyed, and some children feel unsafe on the way to school or while in school due to the lack of electricity, especially for the second-shift students. Families have had to be displaced to areas where schools are available; as a result, schools in safe areas are overcrowded, and lack of documentation hinders the children from accessing primary and/or secondary national examinations. 
The earthquake has weakened the capacity of the education system to address basic education needs more than ever. According to the Ministry of Education, 229 schools were damaged in the affected governorates. Additionally, 92 schools were used as collective shelters in February 2023. Thousands of children were not able to go back to school in the affected governorates, leading to dropping out and a setback in learning.
UNHCR plans to provide non-formal education activities to over 169,000 children and rehabilitate around 1,050 classrooms.

Needs assessment.
The protracted crisis in Syria has hindered children from accessing and enjoying their full rights to education. According to the 2023 HNO 7.2 M children/youth are in need of education. Economic factors and currency depreciation, including children working to support households, are key factors for children not attending school. The formal system is unable to absorb and retain all school-age children. Existing services are unable to physically accommodate or meet the different learning needs of IDP returnee children, including those with specific needs. The limited availability of non-formal education services continues to reduce the opportunities for children to return to learning at age-appropriate levels. UNHCR believes that children with access to education are less exposed to harmful negative coping mechanisms such as early marriage, child labor, and other forms of exploitation. The routine and milestones of going through the education process offer children stability and a sense of normalcy. 

Implementation of activities 
Education interventions will be in line with the “No Lost Generation” initiative launched in 2013. With over 2.45 million children and youth out of school. UNHCR will participate in the EWG to coordinate education interventions and will respond to the identified needs with due consideration of security and resource limitations. The following education interventions build on the priorities and the identified needs of the Education Sector. Education interventions will include non-formal education programs such as remedial classes, catch-up classes, and homework cafe activities for all children, including those with disabilities. Activities will take place in UNHCR community centers and education facilities. Interventions will adhere to the MoE and Education Sector guidelines. School rehabilitation will be limited as a last resort and as part of comprehensive intervention in a priority return area. Access to persons with disability will be taken into consideration in school rehabilitation, and UNHCR will coordinate with the WASH and Shelter Sectors and ensure that the re-tabulated schools have WASH facilities in place for both genders and are disability friendly to safeguard the protection of boys and girls. project_name: Provision of safe, inclusive and protective education opportunities for conflict and displacement-affected girls and boys in Sudan.
project_objective:
The ongoing conflict in Sudan had negatively affected the education sector. With school closure and lack of access to education in safe and protected learning environment, children in Sudan have been exposed to life-threatening protection risks such as: child recruitment, child marriage and Gender Based Violence (GBV). In addition, pre-existing challenges related to insufficient learning resources and supplies, the crisis has left learners and teachers displaced and traumatized; damaged learning infrastructure and school spaces, and constrained access to schools. All those reasons had affected the schools re-opening which is being also challenged by two main key factors: lack of finances to support teachers’ salaries and the fact that more than 10% of schools are being used as shelter by displaced people.  
NRC’s response will focus on two pillars; prioritizing improvement of children’s wellbeing, centered around provision of psychosocial support and lifesaving skills through our First Phase Education Response (FPER) activities and; provision of basic appropriate non-formal education pathways.) and ensuring referral mechanisms are in place to address the holistic needs of children. The response will provide equal access to girls and boys in addition to children with disabilities. 
The (FPER) package will support children to remain connected, protected; and learn through NRC’s Child Education Pathways (CEP) emergency curriculum integrated with life–saving education skills and the Better Learning Programme (BLP). The BLP aims to strengthen children’s resilience and wellbeing. Volunteer teachers will be incentivized and trained with the skills to provide BLP and CEP, through child-friendly approaches, including the identification and referral of children in need of specialized service providers. Rehabilitation works will ensure safety and inclusiveness of schools and Temporary Learning Spaces used for education purposes as per INEE standards including WASH facilities and taking into consideration the needs of the children with disabilities.  Investing in schools’ rehabilitation will contribute to reduce challenges facing the MoE to re-open schools in the long term and serve as safe learning spaces.
To ensure continuation of learning and to support children to gain back learning losses due to the schools’ closure since April, structured non-formal education (NFE) pathways will be introduced according to the education background and age of the children as the following: 1). School readiness for children between 6 to 7, 2). Catch-up classes: for children between 8 to 14 years old who previously attended school, 3). Accelerated Learning Programme (ALP), targeting children between 9 to 14 years old who have never been in schools before or missed more than 3 schooling years. 
Quality will be ensured through the delivery of “Teachers in Crisis Context – TiCC" training to all teachers involved in the NFE activities. The TiCC will focus on introducing new pedagogical techniques focused on active learning and child-centred approaches, including child protection and teacher wellbeing principles. In addition to BLP where teachers will be able to provide basic psycho-social support to children. The distribution of the stationery kits to learners and teaching kits to teachers respond to the challenge of poverty and financial constraint. Provision of dignity kits for use in menstrual health management for girls between 12 to 14 years old will result in increased participation of girls in education. Community engagement through social mobilization and working with PTAs will provide a platform to increase awareness on the importance of education and the promotion of schools/learning spaces as protective environments. 
This approach will be carried out throughout the project period as long as formal schools are closed. In the scenario of schools’ re-opening, NRC will support the transition of children attending NFE classes to formal schools.

project_name: Assistance médico nutritionnelle et psychosociale aux populations déplacées internes et hôtes affectées par la crise sécuritaire et alimentaire dans les régions du Nord, du Centre-Nord et du Sahel au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le Burkina Faso connaît depuis 2015 une dégradation croissante de la situation sécuritaire entrainant des déplacements de population qui viennent exacerber les besoins accrus déjà existants et mettre une pression supplémentaire sur les personnes déjà très vulnérables. Au 31 mars 2023, le CONASUR compte 2 062 534 PDIs avec pour le Sahel 501961 PDI, le Centre-Nord 493954 PDIs et le Nord 256060 PDIs. A la même date, au niveau des 10 régions, 397 formations sanitaires sur 1448 (27,4%) sont complètement fermées et 381 fonctionnent à minima (26,3%), le manque d’accès aux soins de santé prive près de 3 656 427 personnes. Un SMART rapide a été conduite en juillet 2023 et les résultats témoignent d'une situation nutritionnelle critique. Dans le DS de Dori, le taux de MAG est de 14,3% et de MAS de 3,3%; à Titao, le taux de MAG est de 9,3% et de MAS de 1,1%; à Ouahigouya, le taux de MAG est de 10,5% et de MAS de 1,9%; dans le DS de Kaya, le taux de MAG est de 11,2% et de MAS de 1,6%.Le retrait progressif des services sociaux de base du Ministère de la Santé a créé une situation d’urgence humanitaire dans plusieurs régions du Burkina Faso, avec une forte affluence dans les FOSA fonctionnelles dans les zones à forte concentration de populations vulnérables et qui impacte négativement la qualité des soins de santé. 

Face à l’augmentation des besoins médico–nutritionnels des populations hôtes et déplacées, le consortium ALIMA/Keoogo/SOS Médecins BF prévoit de renforcer sa réponse aux urgences dans la région du Sahel (DS de Dori), du Nord (DS de Ouahigouya, DS de Titao), du Centre-Nord (DS de Barsalogho, DS de Boulsa, DS de Kaya) pour l’année 2024. Le projet vise le renforcement de la qualité de l’offre de soins de santé primaire et secondaire affectées par la fermeture et le fonctionnement à minima. Cela par l’installation de PSA et de cliniques mobiles dans les sites hébergeant les PDI et la réouverture des formations sanitaires fermées dans les zones les plus compliquées d'accès. Des activités médicales telles que la PCIMA, la CPN, la CPoN, l’identification et le référencement des grossesses à risque, les urgences pédiatriques, la chirurgie, la prise en charge psychosociale et de santé mentale aussi bien des PDIs que des populations hôtes y seront menées. Les cas compliqués seront orientés vers les structures sanitaires pour une prise en charge adéquate. Un appui sera dans données aux cas de MAS avec complications reçus dans les CRENI appuyés par le consortium, avec la psychostimulation et la donation de kits de bienvenus à l’admission et des kits WASH à la décharge. 
Un appui en RH sera fait avec le renforcement de capacités du personnel étatique et humanitaire en collaboration avec les différentes Directions régionales de la santé et Équipes cadre de District. En transversal, des activités WASH seront également prévues avec le renforcement des dispositifs de lavage des mains, des campagnes de sensibilisation sur l’hygiène corporelle, la distribution de kits WASH et d’hygiène, l’installation de poubelles, la construction de toilettes et d’incinérateur (zones à déchets). A travers le déploiement de son plan d'action environnemental, ALIMA luttera pour l'autonomisation énergétique des centres de santé avec l'installation de kits solaires.

Pour le volet communautaire, ALIMA va renforcer les capacités du partenaire KEOOGO pour mener le paquet complet de prévention de la malnutrition aiguë (Dépistage et ANJE-U) dans les localités : Titao, Barsalogho et la Commune de Pissila.s En plus, la formation/coaching des acteurs locaux et leur prise en main des activités de santé, nutrition et santé mentale sera renforcé. Les ASBC, AV et les promoteurs de santé auront en charge les dépistages actifs, prise en charge de la malnutrition au niveau communautaire et la référence précoce des cas de malnutrition avec complications, l'identification des grossesses à risques.

project_name: Renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de préventions et prise en charge des cas de violences basées sur le genre les PDIs et communautés hotes
project_objective:
Le projet a pour objectif général d'assurer une protection coordonnée et intégrée sur la prévention des risques et réponses aux VBG dans les régions de Diffa, Tillaberi et Maradi. A Tillabéri, IRC propose de organiser des activités de prévention et réponse aux VBG. Pour cela, IRC propose de continuer à suivre et accompagner les organisations communautaires de base (OCB) composées par des femmes qui ont été mises en place dans les années précédentes, dans l'identification des risques pesant sur les femmes et les filles dans leur communauté, dans l'organisation de sensibilisations dans les communautés et dans la mise en œuvre des actions de plaidoyer auprès des autorités locales. IRC propose d’accompagner les OCB aussi dans les activités avec les femmes et les filles dans les espaces surs mis en place par IRC, qui représentent une porte d’entrée confidentielle pour les services de réponse aux VBG (surtout le référencement et l'appui psychosocial), et qui fournissent aux survivantes et aux femmes et filles les plus vulnérables des compétences de vie, et des moyens de surmonter la stigmatisation et de se réintégrer dans leurs communautés. En collaboration avec le secteur Nutrition de IRC, ces OCB mèneront aussi des activités de sensibilisation sur l’approche ANJE (Alimentation du Nourrissant et du Jeune Enfant).
A Diffa et à Maradi, IRC mettra en place des activités holistiques de protection pour les personnes ayant subi une violence basée sur le genre. L’action se concentrera sur les services à destination des femmes et filles vulnérables et à risque de violence, en investissant sur la protection à base communautaire et notamment les OCB qui seront mises en œuvre dans les zones avec un fort taux de recrudescence de VBG. IRC souhaite concentrer son soutien sur la structuration et le coaching rapproché et constante de ces groupements et leur mise en réseau avec les autorités publiques décentralisées afin qu’ils puissent faire avancer les enjeux de lutte contre les VBG de leurs communautés. Dans des deux régions, IRC mettra en place des nouveaux espaces surs et organisera des activités Psychosociales (PSS), de group (socio-récréatives) et d’intégration avec les femmes et les filles adolescentes, et des activités de sensibilisation au niveau communautaire.
Deux autres approches de IRC qui visent l'engagement des hommes dans la lutte contre les VBG (EMAP), et le renforcement de la résilience des jeunes filles adolescentes dans les situations d'urgence (Girl Shine), seront aussi continués dans la région de Tillaberi (Abala et Ouallam), dans la région de Diffa et initiés dans la région de Maradi.
En concentrant ses efforts sur la qualité des services pour les survivantes, IRC maintiendra dans toutes les zones du projet, les activités indispensables de gestion des cas, assistance directe et référencements, et visera aussi à la formation et/ou le recyclage du personnel sanitaire dans les soins cliniques pour les survivantes d’agression sexuelle (Diffa, Maradi et Tillaberi).

project_name: Contribuir a mejorar el acceso a la salud de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad, en los estados de Táchira, Apure y Sucre en Venezuela.
project_objective:
La intervención propuesta por Médicos del Mundo (MdM) da continuidad y amplía el alcance de las actividades financiadas en los últimos años en Venezuela. El objetivo es salvar vidas y prestar asistencia humanitaria, contribuyendo a mejorar el acceso a la atención sanitaria de las poblaciones vulnerables de los estados de Táchira, Apure y Sucre. Se prestará especial atención a los niños, las mujeres, las embarazadas, las madres lactantes, los ancianos, las personas con discapacidad y las personas con movilidad reducida. Esta propuesta se constituye en el sector salud. A través de los resultados propuestos, se definen líneas de trabajo y contribuciones en SMAPS, VBG, Nutrición y Malaria. La intervención abordará aspectos de coordinación y complementariedad con diferentes actores de Protección, WASH y SAN en ambulatorios, hospitales y comunidades priorizadas en los 3 estados. MdM proporcionará asistencia humanitaria a través de la provisión de medicamentos y suministros para la Atención Primaria de Salud (APS), Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR), Nutrición y Malaria, permitiendo que las personas tengan acceso a una atención digna y a medicamentos de calidad, mejorando la prestación de los servicios y aumentando su cobertura. MdM proporcionará apoyo técnico al personal sanitario y no sanitario y a las comunidades objetivo, para mejorar y aumentar las capacidades locales, y promover el desarrollo de entornos saludables en las comunidades priorizadas a través de la implementación de actividades educativas a nivel comunitario. Esta propuesta será implementada directamente por MdM, coordinando actividades con otros actores, así como con las autoridades de salud. El objetivo es buscar la complementariedad en las acciones y dar una respuesta integral. Todas las actividades se desarrollarán bajo enfoques de derechos humanos, género e interculturalidad, alineados con las políticas de ECHO, los objetivos de la misión de MdM y los planes de trabajo acordados con las autoridades locales de salud. 
En el componente de nutrición se van a tamizar niños y niñas de 0 a 5 años, de 5 a 17, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, y adultos mayores, mediante centros de salud del sistema público y escuelas. Los casos no complicados de desnutrición moderada o severa serán tratados con alimento terapéutico listo para el consumo; y Los casos complicados de desnutrición serán referidos al listado de hospitales de la red pública con capacidad de respuesta según el clúster de nutrición. Los casos de desnutrición crónica en NNA o bajo peso en adultos mayores serán apoyados con complementos nutricionales (super cereales). En paralelo, vamos a realizar tamizaje y tratamiento de anemias nutricionales en niños de 0 a 59 meses y mujeres embarazadas y lactantes a través de muestras rápidas de hemoglobina que permiten un diagnóstico preciso y tratamiento con suplemento de hierro. Para fortalecer la respuesta en nutrición del sistema de salud vamos a dotar de equipos antropométricos, equipos e insumos de laboratorio, medicamentos y suplementos nutricionales a los centros de salud priorizados. También, vamos a realizar sesiones de capacitación y apoyo técnico al personal de salud trabajando de forma integral con lideres comunitarios.  Por último, todas las actividades serán diferenciales y especificas por cada grupo de edad y sexo; y se tiene previsto identificar personas con discapacidad, indígenas, y personas de grupos vulnerables para trabajar acciones diferenciadas que respondan a sus necesidades específicas en salud, salud sexual y reproductiva, nutrición, salud mental, apoyo psicosocial, prevención de la VBG y WASH. El presupuesto dentro de los recursos humanos contempla un oficial de género encargado de garantizar que todas las actividades incluyan el componente de género, con acciones específicas y diferenciadas para cada necesidad identificada.
Población meta: 131.076 (73.427 mujeres, 58249 hombres) Todos los indicadores están desagregados por edad y sexo.

project_name: Strengthen access to and utilization of quality protection, psychosocial support, legal services, and housing, land and property information and support services for population in displacement and conflict-Affected situations in four selected locations of Panyijiar, Mayendit, Koch, Juba IDP camps, and Rubkona counties in South Sudan.
project_objective: The project seeks to provide comprehensive, responsive protection services for at-risk conflict and displacement affected people, to address protection risks, human rights violations, gaps in available service in relations to IDPs, returnees and the host community in five counties of Rejaf (Juba), Panyijiar, Mayendit, Koch and Rubkona. The project will target the most vulnerable people at risk, including returnees from Sudan and flood affected people. The objective of the project is to strengthen the protection of most vulnerable girls, boys, women, and men affected by conflict, displacement, and climatic shocks by reducing risks and vulnerabilities and increasing community capacities. Key to this action will be a focus on improving capacity, including community protection networks, for immediate response to violations and remedial action as well as strengthening the protective environment in target locations. The project will have a 60% protection mitigation and response component and a 40% access to justice, through legal information services, safe referrals on HLP monitoring and response (including eviction monitoring) and civil service documentation support - reinforcing sustainable community-based protection activities at community level. The project aims to build and strengthen local capacities within the community and support them to establish a protection framework to prevent and respond to violations. It will focus on improving capacity for immediate response to violations and remedial action as well as strengthening the protective environment in target locations. On immediate response, the action will aim to address acute protection needs of women, girls, boys, and men, stemming from violence, displacement, climatic shocks including rights violations, as well as coercion, and abuse. In terms of delivery modalities and outputs, the overarching objectives of the project will be achieved through a combination of complementarily reinforcing set of actions that are framed around the following core pillars; monitor protection trends (legal, HLP and rights violations) in targeted areas, in the framework of the Protection Monitoring System (PROMOS) of the Protection Cluster and informed by IRC's ongoing protection and legal analysis initiatives at target locations; promote inclusive identification and screening through assessment and analysis of persons at risk to receive protection services and basic needs; provision of psychosocial activities plus structured self-help to enable PSNs to manage distress; protection case management targeting persons with special needs to complement GBV and CP case management services; service mapping and review of referral pathways to promote and coordinate safe referral of cases; provide information services designed to assist displaced and conflict-affected people (including returnees and flood victims) to access services, navigate complex procedures, and utilize existing remedies in areas of displacement to enhance their own protection; awareness raising, information services and outreach on rights, access to justice, housing land and property issues (HLP) and civil documentation; provision of targeted individual assistance including cash for protection and NFIs targeting the most vulnerable individuals – that will include civil service documentation support; Legal aid support will include  provision of specialized counselling, legal assistance and information services through fixed centers and mobile clinics. Access to legal aid services will be unrestricted due to the nature of the service. The project takes PWDs as among the most vulnerable in target communities. On advocacy, Action will strengthen coordination of protection services and enhance advocacy on protection with relevant stakeholders in the four locations. Key advocacy activities will include strengthening of referral pathways, mapping of service providers and Protection Monitoring of rights violations

project_name: Renforcement de l’accès aux soins de santé primaires, de santé reproductive et aux services de prise en charge de violences basées sur le genre, en réponse aux besoins vitaux des communautés affectées par la crise humanitaire dans les provinces du Sud

Il vise d’une part, à réduire la surmorbidité et la surmortalité tributaire d’un faible accès aux soins de santé primaires (SSP), santé reproductive (SR) y compris santé mentale, et soins nutritionnels ; et d’autre part, à la prévention et prise en charge des VBG. Les bénéficiaires de cette intervention sont les personnes les plus vulnérables parmi les populations de déplacés, des retournés et des communautés hôtes des six délégations de sante des six provinces du sud sus mentionnés. 
Ce projet a 5 objectifs spécifiques dont 3 dans le volet Santé et 2 dans la Protection/VBG, à savoir :
- 8 798 personnes dont 1709 hommes, 1944 femmes, 2525 garçons, 2619 filles ont accès aux soins de santé primaires et secondaires (6321 dans la prise en charge des affections courantes parmi lesquels 962 cas compliqués, 202 cas de complications médicales de la malnutrition aiguë sévère, 2098 enfants vaccinés et 177 cas de santé mentale) dans les six provinces du sud. 
- 153 prestataires de service (94 hommes et 59 femmes) sont capacités pour l’offre des soins de santé primaires, Santé Sexuelle et Reproductive ainsi que Santé mentale de qualité, dans les six provinces du sud.
- 1 130 personnes (dont entre autres 429 femmes enceintes, 386 Nouveaux nés, 64 cas de complications de grossesses à l'accouchement / césariennes, 210 cas d'IST, 41 cas de VBG, et les femmes visiblement enceintes bénéficiaires de kits d'accouchement individuels) accèdent gratuitement aux soins de santé sexuelles et reproductives de qualité dans les six provinces du sud.

En vue de l’atteinte de ces résultats, des activités seront mises en place en rapport avec le renforcement des capacités techniques des prestataires et capacités institutionnelles des structures ciblées, - l’offre gratuite de services notamment la prise en charge des cas selon leurs spécificités dans une approche avancée (clinique mobile) et fixe (les formations sanitaires) ; - et les activités de prévention et mitigation de risques VBG/EAS entre autres à travers des sensibilisations.

project_name: Management of WASH Pipeline to Strengthen WASH Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe Water; Sanitation and Hygiene Supplies
project_objective:
According to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, about 6.5 million people has inadequate or lack of access to safe water, and sanitation in South Sudan. Insecurity, displacement, natural disasters such as heavy flooding for the last three years have compounded the impact of low access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services in the country. The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving WASH supplies continues to be one of the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2014, IOM has been successfully managing a portion of the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Core Pipeline, which is an essential support to the WASH Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2024, IOM will maintain its commitment support the WASH Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key WASH supplies to benefit a total of 1.2 million people in need. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal, Rumbek, and Wau to ensure efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, malnutrition, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks

project_name: Provision of Integrated Protection Services to the Most Affected Population in NWS
project_objective:
In the years 2024 and 2025, the Shafak Organization proposes a project aimed at mitigating and responding to protection risks faced by conflict-affected individuals in theAfrin, Jarablus, Al-Bab, and Azaz districts of Aleppo governorate, as well as in the Harim, Ariha, Jisr Ash Shugur and Idleb districts of Idleb governorate. The initiative seeks to empower local communities and individuals affected by conflict in Northwest Syria, fostering their role in societal building and determining their future.
The project will provide protection services and emergency assistance to 88,500 internally displaced persons (IDPs) 77895 and members of the host community 10605.  The comprehensive protection services will encompass mitigation and response, as well as specialized and non-specialized protection services. The overall target includes 32500 Male, 56000 Female project target and 5000 Persons with disabilities project target.
The proposed project will offer gender and age-appropriate general protection services, including structured and recreational psychosocial support, recreational and mental health psychosocial support activities, case management, life-saving assistance, referral to specialized services, awareness-raising on protection-related topics, life skills and vocational training, legal assistance, and legal awareness sessions on housing, land, and property rights and child safeguarding. Community committees will be established and trained to enhance protection through CPMS, safe identification, referral, and communication skills.

To ensure inclusivity, Shafak will maintain a gender-balanced team and deliver training on housing, land, and property rights and child safeguarding to legal staff and community actors in Syria and Turkey. The services will prioritize vulnerable groups, such as women-headed households, children-headed households, persons with disabilities, elderly women and men, families with children at risk of child labor, unaccompanied orphans, and newly displaced individuals without financial means.

In emergencies, the project activities will swiftly respond to the urgent protection needs of newly displaced people, offering a protection emergency package, including psychological first aid, referrals, and emergency case fund support. The initiative will uphold principles of equity and non-discrimination, respecting the basic social and human rights of participants while considering the cultural, historical, and social specificities of the targeted populations. All static centers will be rehabilitated and equipped to be disability-friendly spaces.
In 2024, 16.7 million people (8.4 million female, 8.3 million male) are assessed to need humanitarian assistance across Syria, up from 15.3 million in 2023. After 12 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their situation worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Türkiye on 6 and 20 February 2023. The earthquakes uprooted hundreds of thousands of families, resulted in almost 5,900 deaths and more than 12,800 people injured in Syria, and severely damaged infrastructures already weakened by the conflict. Many families lost their main breadwinner due to death or injury, at a time when the economic situation was already dire, increasing the vulnerability of millions of people previously unable to meet their basic needs. (HNO, Summary, 2024). Within the protection sector, numbers indicate an increase in the number of PiN in 2024 to 2,375,850 in Idleb, and 3,566,142 in Aleppo who are in dire need for protection services.

project_objective:

The number of people in need has increased In 2024, 16.7 million people (8.4 million females, 8.3 million male),are assessed to need humanitarian assistance across Syria, up from 15.3 million in 2023. Of the 16.7 million people in need, 5.5 million are displaced, including over 2 million who live in last resort sites.
After 12 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their situation worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Turkey on 6 and 20 February 2023. The earthquakes uprooted thousands of families, resulted in almost 5,900 deaths and more than 12,800 people injured in Syria, and severely damaged infrastructures already weakened by the conflict. Many families lost their main breadwinner due to death or injury, at a time when the economic situation was already dire, increasing the vulnerability of millions of people previously unable to meet their basic needs HNO 2024.
Women and girls in NWS face various forms of Gender-Based Violence (GBV), including forced marriage, forced labor, workplace exploitation, and domestic violence, with vulnerable groups such as female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, and widows being disproportionately affected. Safety audits conducted by the Shafak revealed increase in security concerns specifically affecting women and girls, with a surge in reported cases of rape and sexual violence, often met with extreme measures, perpetuating a distressing cycle of trauma, according to the GBVIMS+ third quarter report of 2023, The analysis shows that the reported incidents decreased by 11.6 % compared to the previous quarter. Reported GBV incidents included; Physical assault, psychological /emotional abuse, denial of resources and opportunities, sexual assault, forced marriage and rape. 0.4% of the reported GBV incidents were male survivors, while female survivors made up 99.6% of the reported incidents, GBVIMS Report.
In 2024-25, Shafak organization plan to respond to the increased GBV concerns of the crises affected women and girls by providing prevention, response, and mitigation GBV activities through 8 WGSS and 16 mobile teams in 7 central Districts. GBV services will be delivered to 32000 individuals from IDPs and host communities, focusing on the most vulnerable, including survivors, adolescent girls, older women, and PWDs.
The proposed project will offer gender and age-appropriate GBV services, including GBV case management (including case fund and cash) by using GBVIMS+ system, recreational and structured PSS activities, Income Generating Activities (IGA) through the provision provide small-grants for, Support women-led organization WLOs, Engaging men and Boys, AMAL initiative includes three components (Young Mothers’ Clubs (YMCs), and provider-cantered components), GBV awareness raising sessions and campaign, life skills, safety audits, as well as GBV risk mitigation training for GBV and non-GBV actors including humanitarian actors (workers in other sectors like WASH, Shelter/NFI, and Education). 
Shafak will provide legal awareness-raising sessions regarding the registration of civil accidents and real estate documents, in addition to Provide legal consultations regarding the registration of civil incidents and issue the necessary supporting documents to complete the registration of civil incidents, in addition to consultations related to real estate documentation and the issuance of real estate documents.
Mitigating measures are in place to address risks such as accessing vulnerable populations, inadequate community engagement, and resource limitations, ensuring the project remains adaptive and responsive while upholding stringent PSEA measures to prevent any form of exploitation or abuse by Conduct awareness sessions, train staff on PSEA, CSG, provide reporting mechanisms, and emphasize confidentiality.

project_name: UNICEF WASH Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions to Natural Disasters in Mozambique
project_objective:
Mozambique is a climate hotspot in sub-Saharan Africa, where powerful effects of climate change affect large populations of poor and vulnerable communities – over half of which are children. The Mozambican population is especially vulnerable to climate shocks due to existing gaps in access to basic essential and social services and underlying poverty and deprivations. This is evidenced in several global climate risk assessments, including the Global Climate Risk Index 2021, which assessed the impacts of extreme weather events (fatalities and economic losses) and ranked Mozambique as the fifth most affected country in the world from 2000 to 2019, and one of three countries most affected by the impacts of extreme weather events in 2019. Given the history, intensity and frequency of occurrence, the likelihood of another cycle of cyclones/ storms and flooding during the upcoming rainfall season is very high. When these occur, there are serious implications to WASH infrastructure, displacements of people and interruption of services, increasing the risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks such as AWD, cholera.

These anticipatory actions will be geographically focused on the North, Central and Southern Regions of Mozambique, targeting the districts that have been identified by the Instituto Nacional de Gestão e Redução do Risco de Desastres be most at highest risk by cyclones, floods and or droughts. The main purpose of this preparatory action is to ensure the readiness of critical WASH-related supplies, including hygiene kits, with a focus on the most vulnerable families in the targeted areas, and pre-positioning of emergency WASH supplies in critical provinces throughout the country. UNICEF has in place long-term agreements with suppliers of WASH goods and services, both in-country and offshore, that enables rapid procurement of essential WASH items for prepositioning and response. UNICEF warehouses are also strategically positioned to service the three regions efficiently, located in Pemba, Beira and Maputo. In preparation for the 2024 rainy season, UNICEF published a country-wide Expression of Interest which seeks to establish standby arrangements with active WASH sector partners for emergency response and preparedness actions.  Additionally, UNICEF will support capacity building initiatives on emergency preparedness, response, and coordination for WASH Cluster partners (in particular local NGO partners) as well as government counterparts. 

This project will target over 300,000 people at risk for catastrophic natural disaster.

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) for conflict affected populations and IDPs in Sudan
project_objective:
Mercy Corps will target newly displaced IDP and vulnerable conflict affected HHs affected by the ongoing conflict in Khartoum, South Darfur, North Kordofan, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Kassala, Central Darfur and Red Sea States that are experiencing an inability to meet their immediate needs for survival due to acute food insecurity and poor access to basic services and practices as a result of the severe crisis. Displacement and conflict results in both the immediate loss of households’ livelihoods and an inability to meet their needs; it also affects their ability to regain their livelihood and access income. Economic decline across the country and high food prices result in conflict affected households having little cash to cover their food and other needs.   

Mercy Corps will provide multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) to IDP and CAP households to improve their abilities to meet immediate basic needs and reduce use of negative coping mechanisms. A Mercy Corps market assessment conducted in January 2024 along with secondary market assessments demonstrate that although local markets are heavily disrupted and face price inflation for specific items, in the target states are still functioning and able to provide basic food commodities and essential items.  

The proposed MPCA transfer value reflects 100% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) approved by the Cash Working Group in recognition of (1) the gap left by the pause in food security activities led by the World Food Programme (WFP) and (2) the inflationary impacts since the start of the crisis. CAPs are either sheltering close to home or have fled the fighting with little or no possessions. MPCA will provide a flexible and dignified approach to enable them to meet basic needs during the immediate months following the start of the crisis. This approach will also bolster continued market functionality through the crisis. Where possible, Mercy Corps will layer the household level MPCA interventions proposed alongside market systems strengthening interventions at the vendor level supported through other donors.

In Sudan, conflict affected households are facing the immediate loss of livelihoods and an inability to meet their needs in both displacement and hosting locations and in locations where households have remained and sheltered. Food security remains a critical concern in the target areas and is exacerbated by the current conflict in the country. Increases in food and other commodity prices, a reduced harvest, and the continued conflict indicate that acute food insecurity in Sudan continues to worsen. Multipurpose cash interventions play a crucial role in addressing immediate food needs by enabling beneficiaries to purchase nutritious food items from local markets. Given challenges with in-kind distributions and the setting up of commodity supply routes - we propose cash and market support as the core modality to address food insecurity and access to basic non-food items.

Moreover, cash transfers can be utilized in different ways to meet the needs of those who are displaced by the current crisis such as using the money to pay for transportation to safer locations, communicating with family members, and reducing the potential use of negative coping strategies. Multipurpose cash interventions provide the necessary flexibility to address the unique circumstances and priorities of households and individuals in these regions. By allowing beneficiaries to decide how best to allocate the cash, this approach recognizes and respects the diverse needs, preferences, and cultural contexts within these communities.

project_name: Addressing food insecurity of conflict-affected communities in Northern Syria
project_objective: In Northeast Syria (NES), the economic downturn, exacerbated by the devaluation of the SYP against the USD, has far-reaching implications for people’s ability to meet their daily needs. The most commonly reported obstacles to meeting basic needs were the gap between wages and rising prices and the over lack of employment opportunities, while access to livelihoods has consistently been highlighted as the first priority need of host communities and IDPs alike.  Production losses in the agricultural sector severely affect the estimated 18% of the employed population working in the agricultural sector across NES. The death rates and/or destocking reduced farmers’ abilities to generate incomes, and therefore have long-term implications for their livelihoods. In Northwest Syria (NWS), the aftermath of the earthquake on the livelihoods and the local economy in the area, compounded an already critical economic and labour market situation by exacerbating the income/expenditure gap caused by the 2022 reductions in subsidies, general price increases, exchange rate volatility, and the global economic outlook affecting remittances and return rates. In fact, prior to the earthquake, Aleppo and Idleb governorates OCHA informants, reported the access to income generation activities and livelihood opportunities as the top-ranked unmet need, a condition which further hindered the households’ ability to cope with the average inflation of 90% and devaluation of the national currency and Turkish Lira throughout 2022 and the related food price increase. The earthquake had a significant impact on agricultural livelihoods and production in Northwest, where 72% of the population rely on crop and livestock production. Additionally, the livestock value chain, source of livelihood for the 64%5 of people, was also significantly affected by the shocks. As such, the support of agricultural and livestock local production is notably among the top priorities identified for the possible restoration of livelihood in NWS. The proposed project aims at improving food security of conflict-affected communities in Northeast and Northwest Syria. This will be achieved through a combination of different complementary interventions at the individual household and community-level. At the household level, emergency responses assistance will be delivered through distribution of Ready-to-Eat Rations, cash and voucher assistance. In addition, Acted will enhance food production at HH level, through kitchen and home garden kit, enhancing individuals' food security. Acted will also target farmers and livestock holders with longer-term support, delivering agricultural inputs to redeem seeds, fertilizers, polytunnels and tools, and training on climate-smart agriculture and best practices. In addition, Acted will rehabilitate communal productive assets such as mills, bakeries, etc and provide flour assistance to one public bakery in Al-Hasakeh governorate, serving the overall targeted community. All project activities will be designed in a way that enables resilience to be built at a local level and that builds the capacity of men, women, boys, and girls to access basic items and meet basic needs themselves. Specifically, at the household and community levels, Acted will support men and women in building their own capacities to meet their basic needs so that they are more resilient and better able to access commodities and services in the future. This project is estimated to benefit 404,730 individuals overall. As part of its PSEAH strategy, Acted has also developed training packages on the matter which are delivered to all its staff members during the first month of employment and through regular refresher trainings. Training sessions will also be delivered to all the contractors under this intervention to ensure beneficiaries’ safety during the delivery of the services.
