project_name: Centrality of Protection in Protracted Crises at Rohingya and Host Community in Coxs Bazar
project_objective:
CARE proposes an integrated approach to gender-based violence, integrated sexual and reproductive health and MHPSS services that will reach 39628 people living in Camps 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and Jaliapalong Host Community in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. The project design is tailored to the findings of the AHP III gender assessment, focusing on program areas and interventions that empower women and girls to live free from violence. CARE’s current rapid gender analysis and operational expertise is adapted to meet the differing needs of men, women, adolescent boys, adolescent girls, person with disabilities, and gender diverse populations. CARE is committed to providing high-quality protection services aimed at preventing and responding to gender-based violence against women and girls, through the enhancement of GBV services.The GBV component (response, prevention, and risk mitigation) of the project will deliver services and information through WGSS, multipurpose center, and outreach activities. GBV activities will begin with the upgrading of the current WGSS to ensure added safety, privacy, and comfort. Women and girls will receive GBV case management, MHPSS services and participate in recreational activities that include resilience building and empowerment programs within the WGSS. Case workers will be trained in the full package of Case Management procedures and proper confidential documentation and adhere to the GBV minimum standard in the program. The MSP service package, as piloted and recommended by the ISCG, will be integrated into the program. This initiative aims to help individuals to manage stress and encourage them to adopt healthy coping strategies, positively impacting their health, well-being, safety, and social relationships and staff well-being. CARE will also implement ‘Girls Shine’, and EMAP an initiative for adolescent girls focusing on life skills and transforming beliefs and attitudes towards gender and violence. Protection activities will use community outreach to improve access to information and service-seeking behavior and will be delivered at the multipurpose community centers to ensure equitable access, with special focus on including people with disabilities. This project will include (MHM) services, which involve education and provision of appropriate menstrual products like sanitary towels/napkins. Additionally, project will offer specialized case management services for survivors of child sexual abuse  (CCS) and will also collaborate with child protection actors to support and promote child-centered good practices.  CARE will offer Women Lead in Emergencies (WLiE) approach focuses on supporting women’s empowerment by identifying barriers to their participation and creating opportunities for them to become leaders and decision-makers. 
CARE plans to offer integrated GBV and SRH services. This strategy will create opportunities for survivors to access comprehensive services, where both GBV and SRH can serve as entry points. Through the multipurpose center, men and gender diverse populations will have access to GBV services including GBV case management. 
Disability Inclusion is critical to this project. CARE’s activities themselves will be tailored to meet the needs of the vulnerable, including people living with disabilities. This project will ensure accessibility of service, reasonable accommodation of self- help/DSC group and assistance device of person with disability people. CARE will ensured to use the Washington Group Set of questions for disability disaggregated data collection for proper identification and needs. 
CARE will maintain robust coordination with key entities like the GBV sub sector (GBV SS), GBV information management system, case management working group, Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) working group, PSEA, Age and disability WG and other relevant teams to ensure harmonized, quality, and collaborative GBV services.

project_name: Improvement the quality of life, empowering communities and ensuring access to decent shelter, settlements, and essential non-food items for both Forcibly displaced myanmar nationals (FDMN) and the host community.
project_objective:
Caritas Bangladesh is proposing a targeted Shelter/NFI program under the JRP 2024 of SCCCM Sector, focusing on specific camps 13 & 19 and the host community under Ratna Palong and Raja Palong union. Our plan aims to assist a total of 15259 households  (76,140 individuals) including Camp 13 (9,231 HHs,),Camp 19 (5,428 HHs,),and 600 Households in the host community (Ratna Palong and Raja Palong union).This initiative has planned based on the identified needs through J-MSNA report,shelter standard assessments report, and internal monitoring/assessment report by Caritas.The Joint Response Plan (JRP-2024) outlines key activities, including emergency NFI support (400HHs),regular NFI support (1,000 HHs),Rapid damage verification (RDV) (2204HHs), emergency materials prepositioning (1000 HHs),Tie down kits (TDK) (14,659 HHs),Household level Shelter Improvement (6,902 HHs),New Mid-Term-Shelter (400 HHs),regular shelter reinforcement(TSA, SUM and/or R&M, MTS R&M etc.) (9,202 HHs), continuation of treated bamboo support from IOM (9,602 HHs),solar lamps distribution/repair (1,000 HHs),tree plantation (5,428 HHs),solar streetlight repair/new installation (100 Nos.) in the camp and research-based pilot on alternative shelter materials solutions including construction materials waste management both for camp & Host community.Moreover, In the host community, we have also considered shelter Repair (200 HHs) and rural road construction/repair under Cash for Work (CFW) intervention (500 HHs). Families who has already received shelter support in the FY23, will receive regular shelter assistance in FY24 again but they will be considered for emergency shelter/NFI support (if needed).Emergency NFI support, RDV related shelter materials, relocation shelter construction, and emergency TDK will be ensured from IOM pipeline and distribute with technical support from caritas.Catchment area/camp focal points will be assigned for emergency support,shelter/protection-related referral services in the targeted camps 13 & 19. Persons with disabilities and extremely vulnerable individuals including elderly aged peoples will receive porter and construction support for the targeted-shelter/NFI-activities. 

Community based approach including integrated approach with maximum community engagement in all phases all through the program cycle (assessment, project design, decision making, implementation and monitoring) for each targeted intervention whether male, female, adolescent girls, boys, elderly aged peoples, person with disabilities will be engaged and specially women & elderly aged people will be engaged as daily labor with lightweight work. Inclusion of women in gender-segregated training, and recruitment of women volunteers will be ensured in FY24. The program aims to create a durable, safe, secure, dignified, and environmentally friendly, more disaster resilient shelter/NFI program ensuring social cohesion. JRP2024 has considered rationalization of SCCCM Sector. The overall program will include policy related to PSEA,child protection,safeguarding,complain/feedback mechanism,enhancing Protection/gender Mainstreaming , Gender sensitive & transformative Shelter/NFI programming. Technical support for design and implementation of specific accessibility and provision of additional materials for access of persons with disability people will be coordinated with ADWG/Protection sector. Caritas will coordinate with Energy & environment network on the climate action strategy particularly for the activities like solar lamps & Solar street lights, tree plantations, research on environment friendly alternative shelter materials. CRS Bangladesh will provide technical support to Caritas throughout the Program cycle in FY24.  Effective coordination with relevant sectors and humanitarian actors including CiC, RRRC, CIMO, DC Office, Site Management, UNO Office, union parishad etc. with effective participation in the meetings, reporting etc. will be maintained.

project_name: Appui adapté aux besoins alimentaires et à la résilience des populations vulnérables, y compris les populations les plus touchées par les conflits et changements climatiques au Burkina Faso.
Prévention et amélioration de l’accès et de la qualité de la prise en charge nutritionnelle adaptée au sein des populations affectées par la crise humanitaire au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
IRC a commencé ses interventions en nutrition et santé depuis 2020. Reconnue comme un des acteurs essentiels pour ces secteurs dans les zones d’accès difficile, IRC se propose de poursuivre et de renforcer sa programmation au profit des personnes affectées au cours de l’année 2024. 
La programmation nutritionnelle d’IRC se décline sur plusieurs composantes à savoir :
La prévention : elle s’inscrit dans l’objectif spécifique N°1 de la politique nationale nutrition. La prévention de la malnutrition chez les enfants de moins de 5 ans y compris dans les périodes de crises passe par la promotion des pratiques optimales de l’ANJE. IRC a développé une approche centrée sur l’écoute et le soutien pour la pratique de l’ANJE en prenant en compte les contraintes individuelles. Cette approche qui est mise en œuvre dans plusieurs pays depuis quelques années sera également déployée dans les zones couvertes par IRC au Burkina, en prenant en compte l’ANJE en situation d’urgence.
Le dépistage : IRC se propose de mettre en place des stratégies probantes pour réaliser des dépistages continus à large échelle notamment le déploiement de l’approche PB à domicile. IRC a innové dans cette approche avec le montage de video qui standardise le message et la démonstration de la prise de mesure et de la recherche des œdèmes. Cette video intègre des composantes de science comportementale afin de permettre aux mères d’être plus disposées à pratiquer le dépistage de la malnutrition chez leurs enfants après les formations. Cette approche complète sera appliquée dans les zones d’intervention d’IRC
La prise en charge des cas de malnutrition : lors des interventions d’IRC, un appui sera assuré aux personnels soignants pour garantir une qualité optimale de prise en charge des cas. Dans les DS concernés par le protocole simplifié, IRC s’alignera et fera en sorte que la prise en charge atteigne les standards de performance.
Les interventions nutritionnelles d’IRC ciblent toutes les populations sans discrimination de race, de sexe ou d’appartenance ethnique ou religieuse. Elles ciblent aussi bien les personnes déplacées internes que les populations hôtes, la seule considération étant l’état nutritionnel qui sera apprécié par le PB, la recherche des œdèmes et le rapport poids-taille pour la prise en charge, l’état de grossesse ou de femme allaitante pour les sensibilisations sur les pratiques de l’ANJE et le fait d’avoir un enfant de moins de 5 ans pour les formations sur l’utilisation du MUAC. Un regard particulier sera mis sur les personnes vivant avec un handicap dans un esprit d’inclusion

A la date du 31 août 2023, le cluster santé indiquait pour ces 4 régions, 244 formations sanitaires fermées et 302 fonctionnant à minima, privant 2 154 282 personnes de soins (Femmes=515089, Hommes=378938, Enfants=1260255). Au cours de l’année 2024, IRC se propose de contribuer à la restauration et à l’amélioration de l’accès aux soins de santé pour ces populations affectées à travers la réalisation des évaluations pour des réponses de renforcement des soins de santé primaires, sexuels/reproductifs, le soutien psychosocial et la santé communautaire adaptés aux besoins des femmes, des filles, des garçons et des hommes.

project_name: Réponse multisectorielle adaptée d'urgence aux populations touchées par la crise au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
Le but du projet est de sauver des vies et renforcer la résilience des personnes touchées par les crises en fournissant une assistance intégrée et multisectorielle dans les domaines de la santé, de la nutrition, de l'eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène, de la protection, de l'aide financière polyvalente, de la reprise économique et des systèmes de marché par le biais d'actions d'urgence et de relèvement rapide dans les régions les plus touchées par le conflit au Burkina Faso suivant les besoins spécifiques des femmes, des filles, des garçons et des hommes.
L'intervention WASH est mise en œuvre uniquement dans le cadre de la phase post-RRM et les localités touchées se trouveront dans la région Nord à la suite des activités lis en œuvre par le RRM Santé, afin de couvrir les besoins en eau et assainissement dans les centres de santé fonctionnels et les villages associés.

project_name: Renforcement de l’environnement protecteur des enfants contre l'abus et l’exploitation
project_objective:
Le Burkina-Faso connait une recrudescence d’actes de violences avec les groupes armés qui dégradent l'accès aux services sociaux de base et l’environnement protecteur des enfants. Ceux-ci sont de plus en plus exposés aux VBG et au recrutement par ces groupes armés. Ainsi, pour contribuer aux charges familiales ils sont exposés à l’exploitation, l’abus et la négligence. La fermeture des écoles contribue à la multiplication des incidents, exposant les enfants aux violences physiques et psychologiques.
IRC va continuer à fournir un soutien aux enfants vulnérables et à risques, y compris les enfants victimes d'abus et d'exploitation. IRC fournira également aux enfants un soutien holistique, y compris la réintégration par le biais d'un soutien à la gestion de cas individuels et fournira un renforcement des capacités des parents et tuteurs des enfants en matière de parentalité positive pour leur permettre d'améliorer la protection de leurs enfants au seins de leurs familles et communautés. Ils seront engagés dans des activités et des discussions pour les aider à adopter des comportements et des pratiques qui minimisent les risques et la vulnérabilité des enfants.
L'IRC renforce les capacités des membres de la communauté et des professionnels qui sont en contact avec les enfants dans leur travail quotidien, notamment en formant des agents de santé, des enseignants et des travailleurs sociaux aux concepts de base de la protection de l'enfance. IRC travaille avec les membres de la communauté (dirigeants communautaires, autorités locales, etc.), qui aident à prévenir les incidents potentiels de protection de l'enfance dans la communauté.

project_name: Cantines scolaires d’urgence pour les personnes déplacées internes
project_objective:
La crise dans la province du Lac a débuté fin 2014 à la suite des attaques de groupes armés non étatiques qui ont entrainé des mouvements de populations et bousculé les échanges et équilibres socio-économiques dans cette région, déjà en proie aux effets du réchauffement climatique qui y aggravent notamment l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle. Selon le dernier rapport de l’OIM (Round 20 – mai 2023), le nombre de personnes déplacées internes dans la province du Lac est de 215 928 personnes réparties dans 250 localités dont 200 sites et 50 villages, avec respectivement 106 624 personnes dans le département de Fouli, 71 448 personnes dans le département de Kaya et 37 856 personnes dans le département du Mamdi.

La dernière évaluation de la vulnérabilité des personnes déplacées internes réalisée en août 2023 par le PAM indique une détérioration de la situation de la sécurité alimentaire par rapport aux années précédentes de 2021 et 2022. Cette détérioration est liée au déplacement continu des ménages en raison de l’insécurité persistante, à la réduction de la production agricole et à l’augmentation des prix des denrées alimentaires. Le pourcentage de ménages déplacés ayant une consommation alimentaire acceptable s’est détérioré, passant de 71 % en 2021 à 61 % en 2022, puis à 35 % en 2023. En ce qui concerne la mauvaise consommation alimentaire, 40 % des personnes déplacées internes ont une mauvaise consommation alimentaire en 2023, contre 10 % en 2021 et 14 % en 2022.

A cette fin, le PAM prévoit de poursuivre ses activités de cantines scolaires d’urgence en faveurs des enfants des déplacés internes dans la province du Lac. Le PAM prévoit de distribuer des repas chauds nutritifs et diversifiés provenant de la communauté locale, dans la mesure du possible, en encourageant les agriculteurs locaux à approvisionner les écoles en fonction du panier et des quantités établis. Les menus scolaires seront enrichis de produits frais provenant de jardins potagers en fonction de la saisonnalité. L'approvisionnement en denrées alimentaires auprès de sources locales proches de la zone du projet augmentera les revenus des petits exploitants, ce qui entraînera une hausse de leur productivité et de leurs investissements. En outre, un meilleur accès aux opportunités économiques contribuera à la croissance économique du ménage.
L'égalité d'accès à un programme d'alimentation scolaire permettra aux enfants des déplacés internes d'apprendre, de s'épanouir et de développer leur potentiel, de renforcer la résilience individuelle et collective et de contribuer à la coexistence pacifique et à la société civile.

project_name: Appui aux  moyens de subsistance des personnes vulnérables
project_objective:
Le Tchad est un pays sous-développé qui est classé avant-dernier en Afrique sur l'indice de développement humain (IDH). Le niveau de pauvreté est passé de 31,2 % de la population en 2018 à 35,4 % en 2023.
L’Indice de la faim dans le monde (GHI) de 2023 place le Tchad au 119 place sur 121 pays avec un score de 34,6 alors qu’en 2022, il était au 117 place avec un score de 37,2 %. Cet indice présente une légère baisse par rapport aux autres années (2000 : 50,7% ; 2008 : 49,9% ; 2015 : 40,1 % ; 2022 : 37,2 % mais reste toujours classé dans les niveaux de faim graves. Sur le plan mondial, le score GHI 2023 est considéré comme modéré avec une légère variation par rapport à celui de 2022 (2022 :18,2 % et 2023 : 18,3 %).
Le Tchad est un pays sujet à des chocs climatiques saisonniers qui entraînent des crises alimentaires régulières affectant la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations. L'insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition sont récurrentes. L’analyse de la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle de mars 2023 du Tchad présente une situation alimentaire très préoccupante. Cette situation donne un nombre de personnes en situation de besoin de 6,9 millions de personnes comparativement à celui de 2022 qui est de 6,1 millions de personnes dans le besoin soit une augmentation de 13,11 %.
Au regard des crises mondiales actuelles qui se superposent ainsi que leurs conséquences qui sont entre autres les effets du changement avec les inondations qu’a connu la grande partie du pays cette année ; la flambée des prix des denrées alimentaires à cause de la guerre en Ukraine ; les effets de la pandémie du COVID 19 ainsi que la crise au soudan avec l’afflux des réfugiés à l’Est du pays. En plus de ces crises s’ajoutent les facteurs sous-jacents qui sont la pauvreté, les inégalités, la mauvaise gouvernance, le mauvais état des infrastructures, une faible productivité agricole, qui dans leur ensemble, contribuent à la faim chronique et à la vulnérabilité.
 
Les résultats de l’analyse de la situation de l’insécurité alimentaire aiguë actuelle révèlent que 1,892,756 personnes se retrouvent dans la phase crise pour la période courante  et pour la phase projetée près de 2,613,151 personnes seraient en « phase crise » et 271,747 personnes seraient dans la « phase d’urgence ».

Pour toutes ces raisons, le PAM compte Entreprendre des actions de résilience en faveur des populations en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle et aussi pour les populations en phase de crise et d’urgence pour protéger leurs moyens d’existence à travers une assistance alimentaire conditionnelle et la création d’actif. Ce projet concernera 432,735 personnes ce qui représentent 15% des personnes de la période projetée de la phase de crise à la phase de famine.

project_name: Humanitarian Programme Based Application
project_objective:
La situation humanitaire au Tchad est caractérisée par quatre crises interconnectées aux effets
humanitaires multiformes dans un contexte de sous-développement, des défis socio-
économiques ainsi qu’à l’insécurité croissante sur certaines parties du territoire et dans les pays
voisins. Les déplacements forcés des populations, l’insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition, les
urgences sanitaires, les effets du changement climatique affectent près de 6,1 millions de
personnes ([1] OCHA, Rapport de situation, 15 juillet 2022,
https://reports.unocha.org/fr/country/chad/) au cours de l’année 2022. D’après des résultats
du Cadre Harmonisé actualisé en mars 2023, pour la période de soudure allant de juin à août
2023, 1 864 299 de personne se retrouveront en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle sévère
(phase 3 et 4) (CH, mars 2023). La situation actualisée en juillet 2023 suite à la crise sociopolitique
au Soudan a fait ressortir 2 132 929 personne en situation d’insécurité alimentaire sévère soit
une augmentation de 14%. Sur les 2 132 929 personnes actuellement en insécurité alimentaire,
279 402 sont en phase sévère et résident dans les départements des provinces du Bahr El Gazal
et du Lac où les bases opérationnelles d’Oxfam sont présente. Cette situation est due
particulièrement aux aléas climatiques qui ont affecté successivement plusieurs campagnes
agricoles d’une part mais également aux conflits communautaires, la crise soudanaise et les
actions des groupes armés non étatiques au Lac.
Depuis le début des affrontements au Soudan, plus de 400 000 personnes ont traversé la
frontière vers le Tchad. L’OIM estime que plus de 62 300 parmi eux sont des retournés tchadiens
et s’attend à ce que ce nombre passe à 80 000 dans les semaines à venir. Afin de répondre à
toutes ces crises prolongées dans ces zones fragiles du Tchad, Oxfam et ses partenaires locaux
(dont HELP-Tchad et SAHKAL) prévoient d'atteindre à travers le PBA ASDI, 50.000 personnes
affectées par an avec une aide vitale dans les zones de conflit dans les secteurs EFSL, WASH,
protection transversale, plaidoyer et genre avec un budget prévisionnel de 455.452.173 SEK pour
la période 2022-2026 En ce qui concerne l’opérationnalisation de la localisation de l’aide
humanitaire, il est ciblé d’allouer entre 15% du budget total aux partenaires stratégiques
d'Oxfam, qui ont un encrage institutionnel et une présence effective dans les zones humanitaires.
Pour réduire l’impact environnemental de nos actions, un partenaire stratégique dans le domaine
sera identifié et évalué.

project_name: Informar el proceso de planificación del HNO/HRP a través de una Evaluación de Necesidades Multisectoriales (MSNA)
project_objective:
Después de más de medio siglo de una crisis socioeconómica y política prolongada, Colombia sigue haciendo frente a olas de violencia fomentadas por grupos armados disputándose el control de economías ilegales, así como el dominio de tierras y recursos naturales. La inseguridad que ha generado el conflicto armado ha afectado comunidades a lo largo y ancho del país y provocando el desplazamiento que a pesar de la firma del proceso de paz en 2016, siguen siendo eventos frecuentes.

En el contexto de estos desafíos, la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas de Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA) y la comunidad humanitaria decidieron llevar a cabo la Evaluación de Necesidades Multisectoriales (MSNA) de Colombia en 2021 y 2022. Estas evaluaciones, liderada por la Iniciativa REACH (REACH), tuvieron por objeto abordar la falta de datos actualizados sobre las condiciones humanitarias para los procesos estratégicos de planificación y adopción de decisiones humanitarias, una deficiencia que afecta especialmente a ciertos grupos de población, y a partes del país que históricamente han visto menor presencia de actores humanitarios. Gracias a estos ejercicios los resultados sectoriales e intersectoriales contribuyeron a fortalecer la programación estratégica del país plasmada en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria 2022 y 2023.

La compleja situación que atraviesa Colombia sigue demandando una comprensión actualizada y exhaustiva de las condiciones de vida de las poblaciones más afectadas por la crisis. Por lo tanto, REACH propone continuar prestando su apoyo a OCHA y a la comunidad humanitaria colombiana para poder abordar de manera conjunta las brechas de información más transcendentales que le permitan delinear e implementar una estrategia de respuesta humanitaria adaptada y eficiente durante los próximos procesos de planificación humanitaria para 2024.

project_name: Provision of emergency life-saving primary health care services to 40,968 host communities, Returnees, and IDPs in Maiwut County
project_objective:
Samaritan’s Purse South Sudan proposes to support Maiwut Primary Health Care Center (PHCC) in 2024 in a bid to enhance access to basic primary health care and nutrition services through treatment of common communicable diseases, promotion of safe motherhood and Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI), and promotion optimal maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN), in order to improve community resilience. 

The project will be implemented in close collaboration and coordination with the State Ministry of Health (SMOH) and County Health Department (CHD). The project will support the PHCC in providing the Basic Package of Health and Nutrition Services (BPHNS), in order to prevent the already fragile health situation from deteriorating. The Project will support the County Health Department in paying incentives for the health workers, providing capacity building trainings and mentorship, stocking of essential medicines and medical supplies to aid the delivery of inpatient and outpatient consultations, maternal and newborn care, and prevention of malnutrition through regular growth monitoring promotion and micronutrient supplementation among the target population.  

This project will also respond to the immediate humanitarian health and nutrition needs of communities in crisis within Samaritan’s Purse areas of operation in Unity and Upper Nile states. In the past years, Samaritan's Purse emergency response projects have mainly focused on distributing non-food items (NFIs) to address emergency shelter needs and provision of limited WaSH items, but the beneficiaries never receive support in managing health conditions as part of humanitarian support in crisis. This year’s Health Rapid Response Team (HRRT) strategy was informed by the SPSS teams’ learnings in running mobile health services, flood responses and mass vaccination campaigns conducted for ‘communities in crisis. The project will deploy a mobile rapid response team to address the immediate, basic humanitarian needs for health and nutrition services due to multiple crisis including extreme flooding, violence, poverty, food insecurity, displacement, and limited access to essential services, existing access constraints, operational interferences, public health challenges such as measles and cholera outbreaks, and climatic shocks resulting in extraordinary flooding and localized drought which are all exacerbated by the Sudan crisis, the humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains dire with only 26% of the Humanitarian Response Plan currently funded. The Country’s Health system cannot cope with, respond to, and provide essential life-saving health services in humanitarian emergencies as it relies heavily on international humanitarian assistance that continue to face constrained funding.  

This project seeks to improve the health status and nutritional wellbeing of 59,106 people (28,492 males and 30,614 females) in Maiwut County (38,492 host community, 1,850 internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 18,760 are returnees), through the delivery of quality and comprehensive primary health care and nutrition services at Maiwut PHCC. The vulnerable population groups that will be reached by this project include children under five years old (U5), pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) and other women of reproductive age, people with disability, returnees and internally displaced persons (IDPs).

project_name: Integrated Nutrition, WASH, and FSL Response in Mayendit County
project_objective:
Samaritan’s Purse (SP) proposes an integrated multisectoral humanitarian assistance with the aim of providing life-saving assistance and improving resilience by increasing access to health and nutrition services, increasing access to safe water supply and storage, and improving household food security through promotion of sustainable farming systems, and creation of alternative livelihoods to provide a comprehensive approach to addressing the underlying causes of food insecurity and malnutrition in Mayendit county. 
Sustainable behavior change requires longer-term engagement but is key to enhancing resilience within beneficiary communities. In the proposed project, SP will work with community nutrition Care Groups (CGs) and key social leaders to create awareness, promote and support positive behavior change on issues of maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN). 
The proposed project is designed to build on SP’s experience in implementing nutrition sensitive projects in Unity state and incorporate lessons learnt into the design and the implementation of this project. The proposed action will capitalize on existing local community and government strengths and targeting weaknesses in health systems. The proposed activities will focus on capacity building and community engagement and education to ensure that inputs are sustainable and there is a clear exit strategy for SP.  Instead of creating inefficient and unsustainable parallel systems of health services provision, project activities will work within and strengthen existing government structures. 
SP will collaborate with the county health department (CHD) and other health and nutrition implementing partners in Mayendit to support 8,324 children under five (U5s) and 2,898 Pregnant and Lactating women (PLW) through direct treatment of malnutrition. With support from WFP, SP will reach 3,525 children under two years and 2,938 PLWs through blanket supplementary feeding program (BSFP). Furthermore, 10,471 PLWs will be targeted for MIYCN activities through the Care Group Model. Additionally, SP will train 16 health care workers and 1,120 Care Group Members in skills essential in strengthening the implementation of high-impact nutrition interventions. 
SP will continue providing community-based malnutrition preventive services to all children less than five years, and pregnant and lactating women, ensuring improved capacity in nutrition information systems and knowledge-generation.
Samaritan’s Purse will employ a phased approach with full project support at start-up and allow the responsibility to shift to local structures towards the end of the project period. Specific activities will be focused on building the community’s ability to maintain project gains. The project will invest in local structures such CGs, WMCS and lead farmers through capacity building, mentorship and input provision to empower them to carry on with the knowledge and skills gained beyond the life of the proposed project, in an effort to sustain the resilience building initiatives. 
SP believes that building synergies with a wide range of partners enable us to achieve the aspired multi-sectoral outcomes with limited resources. In its commitment against food insecurity and malnutrition, SP established healthy working relationships with various partners and MOH at both national and local level coordinating its nutrition programming with the CHD who is in charge of service provision and supervision of health facilities. In the greater Mayendit County, SP will coordinate its activities with all the organizations present supporting health and nutrition, including UNIDO, IRC and CASS.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Lifesaving Nutrition interventions to conflict affected populations (Children 0-59 months, pregnant and lactating women) in Canal/Pigi, Panyjar, Malakal, Fashoda, Manyo, Panyikang and Juba IDP Camps Counties in South Sudan
project_objective:
With the proposed humanitarian responses, International Medical Corps (IMC UK) will provide integrated lifesaving nutrition service to conflict affected host communities and displaced population in Canal/Pigi, Panyjar, Malakal, Fashoda, Manyo, Panyikang and Juba IDP Counties of Jonglie, Unity, Upper Nile and CE states. To address the suffering, morbidity and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable children and women, IMC will continue to increase equitable access and utilization of comprehensive quality preventative, promotive and curative nutrition services for children, adolescents and women in the targeted counties experiencing multiple deprivations, including high acute malnutrition rates above WHO emergency threshold, food insecurity, high morbidities, high GBV concerns and poor WASH conditions. The proposed response will include management of wasting, through the treatment severe acute malnutrition without medical complication at OTP sites, severe acute malnutrition with medical complication at SC sites, and Moderate acute malnutrition treatment for both under five children and PLW at TSFP sites. In addition, the project will support and promote optimal breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices through Maternal-Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) activities focusing on the first 1,000 days of a child's life.  IMC UK propose to deliver a comprehensive package of nutrition services provided through establishing and strengthening 60 OTP/TSFP static and outreach/mobile facilities and 4 SC sites across the project sites.
IMC UK will spearhead the integration of nutrition services in the health system, and promote the simplification of early detection, referral, and treatment of children with acute malnutrition including empowering families and communities by promoting the use of Family-MUAC, mother and father support groups, CNVs/BHW as a main vehicle for delivering multi-sectoral services at community, household, and facilities level. To continue boosting the existing coordination, knowledge and experience transfer and sustainability, IMC will work with SPEDP (Support for Peace and Education Development Program) the local partner active in UNS, Unity, Jonglei and CES to enhance the localization efforts and strengthen the capacities of communities and CHD staff at the county level to support preparedness and transition of provision of nutrition services from Implementing Partners. 
IMC UK will monitor the nutrition status of the population and the nutrition response through routine nutrition program data, quarterly MUAC screening campaigns and population-based SMART Surveys. With its Nutrition Surveillance Team, IMC will undertake nutrition assessments in its operational locations and support to undertake in nutrition assessments in Priority counties as well to provide robust information on the nutrition situation of a given population, this information will be key in responding effectively to nutrition needs in the project areas. 
IMC will employ a people-centered approach that mainstreams Accountability to Affected population (AAP), strengthen the community system and collaborate with FSL, WASH, Health, Education and Protection partners to target and ensure that children and women access a safe, equitable and dignified comprehensive package of essential services through the nutrition sites to prevent malnutrition. IMC is the leading health and GBV partner in Malakal, Panyjar, Pigi/Canal Counties and Juba IDP, this will present a unique opportunity for the integration of health, nutrition and GBV, thus reducing challenges associated with coordination, monitoring, and evaluation. The integration approach will also reduce operational costs by leveraging IMC’s operational presence and the established relationships with the authorities.

project_name: Gender-based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Population in South Sudan
project_objective:
The International Medical Corps (IMC) will continue to implement GBV prevention and response program targeting returnees, IDPs and host community with the aim of empowering. communities and build resilience through promoting social and behavioral change to address the root causes of GBV in the country. IMC will work closely with Hope Restoration South Sudan (HRSS) to ensure that wider communities are reached and that the partners capacity is build. 

GBV prevention efforts will focus on behavior and attitude change interventions through engaging men and boys, working with community structures and local activities as well as women and girls. Response activities will focus on strengthening survivor cantered case management services and psychosocial support. Further IMC and HRSS will strengthen the linkages to ensure that survivors receive necessary information through integrating services with health, nutrition and mental health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS).   

IMC and HRSS will take advantage of its vast experience and success and continue to implement GBV prevention and Response activities  in  Upper Nile (Malakal PoC and Malakal ton Renk, County), Unity (Nyal County),  Panyijar ( Leer and Mayendit) (Canal/Pigi County, Kurwai,  

 Fangak). 

  

The interventions will focus on the provision of individual support in line with the Inter-Agency GBV Case Management Guidelines for at-risk women and girls as well as provision of group psychosocial support activities within Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS.) in line with IMC/IRC WGSS global toolkit (2017).   IMC UK and HRSS community engagement activities will focus on long-term social and behavior changes strategies which aims at addressing the root cause of violence. These strategies will include use of SASA! Community mobilization tool which aims at encouraging the communities to rethink use of power, promote gender equality and ensure balanced and safe societies SASA!IMC and HRSS will work with men and boys through Engaging Men in Accountable Practice (EMAP) which is a primary prevention model, which aims at men’s gender equitable attitudes and reducing violence against women and girls.  In addition, IMC will work closely with community structures including community leaders, Payam administrators and camp leadership. The afore mentioned groups will be trained on GBV key concepts, PSEA, Psychosocial Fist Aid (PFA) and safe referrals. Similar training will be conducted with other stakeholders including the Ministry of Gender Child, and Social Welfare (MOGCSW), Women Association (WA) and Police. Targeted capacity building of the partner HRSS will be done upon capacity gap assessment.   The project aims at reaching 22483 direct beneficiaries with services

project_name: Management of S-NFI Pipeline to Strengthen S-NFI Cluster’s Capacity to Improve the Access of Vulnerable Populations in South Sudan to Safe and Appropriate Shelter and NFI Solutions
project_objective:
Conflict, sub-national violence and heavy seasonal flooding continues to cause internal displacement in South Sudan leaving 2.4 million of its population impacted through destruction of housing and loss of essential household goods. The complex operating environment combined with accessibility challenges indicates that in-kind provision of lifesaving supplies continues to be the most significant modality for emergency responses in the country. 

Since 2011, IOM has been successfully managing the shelter and non-food items NFI (S-NFI) Core Pipeline., which is an essential support to the S-NFI Cluster in providing critical services to Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) partners. 

Under the HRP 2024, IOM will maintain its commitment to support the S-NFI Cluster Pipeline through the provision of key shelter and NFI supplies to benefit a total of 1,390,286 people in need. Procured supplies will be transported for prepositioning in strategic logistic hubs throughout the country, namely Bentiu, Bor, Malakal and Wau from which responding SNFI Cluster partners can access  the supplies for distribution hence ensuring efficiency by contributing to the reduction of response time through moving the supplies closer to final distribution sites. The Pipeline system optimizes economies of scale, reduction of cost, harmonized quality of items, non-duplication and supply chain efficiencies. The distribution will be prioritized to directly benefit vulnerable people affected by displacement, conflict, natural disasters (such as the heavy seasonal rains and flooding), disease outbreak, famine/food insecurity, and GBV risks.

project_name: Provision of Integrated Nutrition services to children under 5 and pregnant lactating women in Longechuk, Melut, Nasir, Ulang, Renk, Maiwut and Maban counties
project_objective:
This project seeks to reduce nutrition related morbidities and mortalities in the 6 counties of upper Nile state through prevention and provision of improved treatment of acute malnutrition. The project will target South Sudanese in upper Nile State living as refugees, internal displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and other vulnerable populations including people with disabilities. Specifically, the project targets children U5 years with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), U5 children with Moderate Acute malnutrition (MAM) and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) with MAM. 
In line with Nutrition Cluster Strategy for 2024, the project has three objectives:
1.	Increase equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services to prevent malnutrition among children, adolescents, and women 6 counties of Upper Nile State by the end of 2024 
2.	To increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of wasting for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW in 6 target counties of Upper Nile State 
3.	To improve nutrition and health-related knowledge and practices that prevent malnutrition of pregnant women and girls and new mothers, caregivers and community members through social and behaviour change communication strategies
4.	To enhance nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis, and utilization of nutrition information by the end of 2024 
RI will provide nutrition-sensitive services through early screening at the community level using the Family MUAC approach and timely referrals, increasing access to MIYCN services, deworming and Vitamin A supplementation as well as improving the access to integrated nutrition, health, WASH and FSL services. Gender sensitive approaches will be utilised in the project to ensure equitable access to nutrition services. Though Nutrition sites integrated services will be provided to prevent and treat malnutrition. RI will link this nutrition project to the health, food security and WASH projects RI is implementing in Maban, Melut, Longechuk, Maiwut, Ulang and Nasir to ensure that children and women access a safe, equitable and dignified comprehensive package of essential services through the nutrition sites and integration of early childhood development as stimulation activities to prevent malnutrition. RI will strengthen nutrition surveillance mechanisms through accurate and timely reporting, participating in SMART surveys, monitoring, and analysis of data for early and objective decision-making. Protection mainstreaming will be integral across the project cycle to ensure that the services are provided in safe spaces and conditions for children and women
In Maban, Melut, Longechuk and Maiwut, RI as the Lead partner will be directly implementing a comprehensive package of nutrition services. In Ulang and Nasir, as part of RI integrated Mobile Medical units, RI will provide mobile nutrition services in hard to reach areas of the counties in collaboration with the Lead Nutrition Partners. In the later, the treatment commodities will be provided through the Lead partners and the data from the outreaches will be shared through the Lead partner in line with the Nutrition cluster strategy. To further localize the RI’s response and to ensure sustainability, RI will strengthen the County Health Department (CHD) responsibilities to oversee the nutrition interventions, to coordinate the response with various stakeholders at the county level and provide stakeholder’s capacity building on the new national guidelines on management of malnutrition and maternal, infant, and young child nutrition.

project_name: Equitable  Access to Integrated Water and Sanitation services in Melut, Baliet and Nasir
project_objective:
The Equitable Access to Integrated Water and Sanitation services project will seek to reduce the Water and Sanitation (WASH) morbidity and mortality through provision of resilient WASH in Melut, Baliet and Nasir. This project seeks to increase equitable access to portable water, appropriate sanitation, and promote safe hygiene practices by IDP populations, returnees, and host community in Melut, Baliet and Nasir counties. The project will contribute to the 3 WASH Cluster sector objectives which are, to Contribute to reducing water and sanitation related morbidity and mortality; Provide safe, equitable access to water and sanitation basic services; and Support recovery and resilience building to achieve durable solutions
The project will achieve the following 3 outcomes:
1.	Increased access to adequate portable water by 27,000 people (14,000 women and13,000) Men, returnees and host community members in Melut, Baliet and Nasir
2.	Increased access to basic sanitation facilities for 16,000 people (Women-8500 and Men-7500)  and 700 Under 5 children and their caretakers, Pregnant and Lactating mothers in Melut, Baliet and Nasir
3.	Improved access to hygiene promotion and Covid-19 awareness for 90,000 community members in Melut, Baliet and Nasir
Relief International will leverage on its long-term contextual understanding and analysis of WASH needs in Melut, Baliet and Nasir in designing and implementing the project activities. To improve equitable access to portable water, RI will facilitate the rehabilitation of 30 non-functional hand pumps in the two counties. 6 of the water points, will be installed with solar pumps to increase availability of drinking water at IDP and returnee sites. Water quality tests will be conducted before and after borehole rehabilitation, with shock chlorination performed based on the water quality test results. To ensure sustainability, pump minders and water point user committees will receive training on the maintenance and management of the water points, respectively.
To improve sanitation outcomes, the project will facilitate the construction of 800 flood resilient latrines at household level (200 in Baliet, 300 in Melut and 300 in Nasir). Community will be encouraged to fix their own handwashing stations for promotion of safe hygiene practices. 10 flood resilient latrines with hand washing facilities will be constructed at nutrition facilities.  Gender and protection measures for children and women will be incorporated in the design, siting and construction of the latrines. 
Similarly, Hygiene sessions will be conducted in both the community and in nutrition facilities. An estimated 6,000 hygiene promotion and Covid-19 awareness sessions targeting 90,000 people will be conducted during the project period. 4,500 most vulnerable households and caretakers of Children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) will receive NFI kits sourced from the WASH cluster to promote hygiene practices in the community.
In this context, RI will specifically consider the impact of activities on gender dynamics, actively ensuring that measures are in place to promote safe and equitable access to WASH services by women and girls. RI will highlight gender mainstreaming and integrate gender-related considerations into all planned activities to ensure that men, women, boys, and girls have equal access to project services. Some specific considerations will include: RI will consider the water points are easily and safely accessible; designs of WASH infrastructure is gender and protection sensitive; ensure security of latrines (with locking mechanisms inside and outside); construct separate latrines for males and females; NFI kits are sensitive to the needs of girls, women, children and other vulnerable groups; and women will be equally represented in water user committees and other project community monitoring structures. Also, to ensure equitable access, the needs of people with disabilities, and older people will be considered.

project_name: Health system strengthening and improved access to integrated emergency lifesaving primary health care services to the vulnerable communities of Upper Nile, South Sudan.
project_objective:
Purpose and overall goal:
In line with health sector objectives, the project will seek to improve equitable access to life-saving essential comprehensive quality healthcare services in 6 counties of Upper Nile state (Longechuk, Maiwut, Renk, Maban, Ulang, and Nasir). This will be achieved through implementing the basic health package that includes maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment of common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to girls, boys, men, and women in emergency situations, with a specific lens on accessibility for persons living with disability (PWD) and the elderly. In partnership with the Ministry of Health and the County Health Departments, the project will support the delivery of the Basic health care package, and support in facilities in refugee camps, transit centers, and host communities.  RI will directly support 14 health facilities in Renk, Maban, and Melut providing primary health care services.  To reach the population in hard-to-reach locations in Nasser, Ulang, Maiwut, and Longechuk counties, RI will continue supporting seven integrated Mobile Medical Units (MMUs).  RI will also support the Boma Health Initiative (BHI) in the 6 target counties.
Methodology and target:
RI’s project focuses on the provision of primary health care in areas of high need and where existing services are inadequate. Activities include the provision of curative consultations in primary health facilities; community-based treatment of common illnesses in children under five; routine vaccination; reproductive and sexual health including the provision of ANC, skilled delivery, PNC, and clinical management of SGBV; and mental health treatment. Medair conducts ongoing training and supportive supervision for capacity-building staff of RI, CHD, and other partners in order to improve the quality of service provision. RI primarily targets children under five, women, and people with disabilities and mental health conditions, due to their unique vulnerability, though not exclusively.
RI aims to increase the capacity of CHD, SMOH, and the local community to be prepared for future shocks.
All of RI's health activities are integrated with WASH, Nutrition, and Protection activities to enhance the effectiveness and address underlying causes of morbidity and mortality. The project will target 203,757 (107,991 Female, 95766 Male) among which, 69,277, 79465and 10,187 are Hosts, IDPs, and people with disabilities respectively.

project_name: "Respuesta basada en asistencia alimentaria a familias afectadas por la múlti-amenaza en El Salvador, incluyendo niñez y adultos con discapacidad".
project_objective:
El proyecto basado en Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición, se llevará a cabo en las tres zonas del país (Occidente, Centro y Oriente). El enfoque principal es promover la seguridad alimentaria en familias priorizadas con miembros (adultos y niñez) con algún tipo de discapacidad. Cabe destacar que, de acuerdo al Consejo Nacional de Inclusión de Personas con Discapacidad (CONAIPD), para el 2015 el porcentaje de discapacidad oscilaba al 6.4 % de la población total del país, siendo este porcentaje, un equivalente a 410,798 personas bajo este grupo vulnerable, teniendo una mayor prevalencia en los sectores urbanos y peri-urbanos. La meta propuesta o alcance poblacional de la propuesta, es llegar un total de 32K personas (8K familias) bajo tres resultados: 
 1) Familias capacitadas en temas que les permita mejorar o recuperar sus medios de vida posterior a la 
     múltiple amenaza.
 2) Familias que reciben apoyo monetario mediante programas de transferencias multipropósito y sin 
     condición con enfoque de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición en Emergencias. 
 3) Familias sensibilizadas mediante la difusión de información clave para la adopción de buenos hábitos 
      y prácticas alimenticias.
Con esto, se busca mejorar las condiciones de Seguridad Alimentaria durante la fase de respuesta y recuperación para las familias específicamente donde uno o más miembros de su núcleo presentan un grado de discapacidad priorizando el tema, sin embargo, podrán ser tomadas también familias que presenten y estén dentro de los rangos de "criterios de selección más adelante especificados para la propuesta en curso".

project_name: Prevención y atención a niñas, niños, adolescentes víctimas de violencia en el corredor seco
project_objective:
La niñez y adolescencia en Guatemala constituye un sector de la población altamente vulnerable a sufrir violencia, específicamente violencia sexual. En el 2023 el Ministerio Público registró 6,541 denuncias de casos de violencia sexual y 7,941 de maltrato infantil. En el mismo año, el Observatorio de Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (OSAR), registró en 52,878 nacimientos de madres que oscilan entre las edades de 10 a 19 años. Reporte que año con año va en aumento.

El panorama anterior se agudiza en los 88 municipios del corredor seco, en los cuales además de la situación alimentaria y nutricional que enfrentan, se suma la alta vulnerabilidad a la violencia en todas sus manifestaciones. El 36% de los delitos cometidos hacia la niñez y adolescencia proviene de los municipios del corredor seco. Los delitos más frecuentes son el maltrato infantil (30%) y violencia sexual (20%).  

En la sociedad guatemalteca predominan patrones culturales/normas sociales de género, que reproducen prejuicios y estereotipos que generan violencia de género hacia las niñas, adolescentes y mujeres en todos los ciclos de vida; la brecha es aún mayor para las niñas y adolescentes indígenas, ya que a la discriminación por género se le agrega la discriminación étnica y lingüística. 

El proyecto se enfocará en generar acciones de prevención de la violencia hacia la niñez y adolescencia en los municipios del corredor seco, así como en impulsar la puesta en marcha de sistemas municipales y comunitarios de protección en el 50% de los municipios del corredor seco, para lo cual se promoverá desde el modelo socio ecológico, la transformación de conocimientos, actitudes y prácticas que generan violencia hacia la niñez y la adolescencia. 

Asimismo, ante la ausencia de atención psicosocial a niñez víctima de violencia, se brindará atención individual y grupal a niñez víctima y su familia de los principales departamentos del corredor seco, que presentan mayor número de víctimas detectadas, coordinando y trasladando capacidades metodológicas a la Secretaría de Bienestar Social, Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social, Secretaría contra la violencia sexual, explotación y trata de personas, y corporaciones municipales priorizadas. Así también, se fortalecerán las acciones de supervisión a cargo de la Procuraduría de los Derechos Humanos.

project_name: Espacios de aprendizaje seguro para NNA en situación de movilidad humana.
project_objective:
Honduras sigue siendo un país de tránsito, donde se ha registrado que entre el 1 de enero y el 8 de julio de 2023, una entrada de Personas con necesidades de protección internacional- PNPI cercana a los 148,489. De ellas, el 38% eran venezolanos, el 14% ecuatorianos, el 12% haitianos y el 8% cubanos y el 69% de las entradas irregulares en este periodo se produjeron en los municipios de Danlí y Trojes, cerca de la frontera con Nicaragua. En el marco del anterior contexto, el proyecto busca fortalecer la respuesta educativa ante el flujo mixto migratorio que transita por Honduras en la ruta migratoria, por medio de una estrategia de atención itinerante centrada en la protección y entrega del servicio educativo a NNA por medio de actividades lúdicas, recreativas y de fortalecimiento de aprendizajes en los municipios de Danlí, El Paraíso y Ocotepeque, Ocotepeque.  

NRC quiere proponer un enfoque de Respuesta educativa de Primera Línea (es decir, a corto plazo y tras una situación de crisis/emergencia), utilizando materiales ya desarrollados en los países donde opera NRC para llegar a niños/niños/adolescentes (NNAs) en tránsito, y proporcionar actividades básicas de aprendizaje (p. pj. Matemáticas, lenguaje, actividades recreativas) al tiempo que proporciona mensajes clave de para salvar la vida/ habilidades para la vida (o de autocuidado/autoprotección) a estos niños/niñas en tránsito y de forma diferenciada por género y edad en el desarrollo de las actividades.     

Esta respuesta se articularia principalmente a partir de 4 rincones de aprendizaje. Estos rincones promoverían un pensamiento crítico en torno al contexto y las posibilidades de ser, saber y hacer. Las experiencias de estos Rincones se basarían en competencias básicas de aprendizaje para proporcionar elementos que le sean propios y adaptables a los niños. Por otro lado, se incluiría un componente de habilidades para la vida (mensajes clave para salvar la vida), orientadas desde una mirada de la educación, a mejorar las condiciones de salud, bienestar para generar oportunidades de aprendizaje sobre mensajes claves.  Para asegurar un espacio que sea lo más seguro y protector posible, NRC Incluirá su programa ‘flagship’ de apoyo psicosocial: BLP (‘Better Learning Programme’, en su sigla en inglés). El Programa para un Mejor Aprendizaje (BLP) se convierte en una oportunidad importante, ya que, al implementar el Aprendizaje Social y Emocional, facilita la adquisición de competencias para que los niños puedan reconocer y gestionar sus emociones, mientras continúan su proceso de aprendizaje. Dentro del desarrollo de actividades también se contempla trabajo con madres, padres y cuidadores, como forma de darle sostenibilidad a la estrategia durante el transito de las familias, así cumpliendo estos un papel de agentes educativos comunitarios.

project_name: Comunidades Educativas y Protectoras para la niñez, adolescencia y juventud en contextos de emergencia.
project_objective:
El proyecto del NRC busca utilizar la educación como una herramienta estratégica para proteger a la niñez, adolescencia y juventud en situaciones de emergencia, especialmente en contextos de violencia, migración y desplazamiento. Se enfoca en promover el acceso y la permanencia escolar en espacios seguros, abordando impactos emocionales causados por detenciones familiares. Mediante "Espacios seguros de aprendizaje", se ofrecen talleres socioemocionales y mensajes de protección, entregando kits recreativos con apoyo psicosocial. El proyecto identifica y apoya a NNAJ fuera del sistema escolar, incorporándolos en círculos de motivación y educación socioemocional, con un programa de permanencia que incluye acompañamiento pedagógico y entrega de Voucher educativos. Se adopta un enfoque integral, capacitando a docentes, funcionarios y familias en temas de educación en situaciones de emergencia, derechos de la niñez y protección socioemocional. La iniciativa busca fortalecer capacidades para lograr el triple nexo: Acción humanitaria-Desarrollo-Paz.


Espacios Temporales Protectores:

Jornadas de educación socioemocional para la recuperación de Niños, Niñas, Adolescentes y Jóvenes (NNAJ) tras emergencias.
Enfoque en comprender reacciones al miedo y estrés, abordando experiencias traumáticas.
Entrega de Insumos Educativos:

Kits recreativos y Voucher Educación para fortalecer vínculos con la educación formal y garantizar permanencia educativa.
Identificación de NNAJ en Riesgo:

CENSO Educativo para identificar NNAJ fuera del sistema por emergencias, con participación comunitaria.
Caracterización de población, considerando riesgos y obstáculos para la reincorporación escolar.
Encuentros Lúdicos y Pedagógicos:

Formación de círculos educativos para NNAJ del censo, enfocándose en educación socioemocional.
Implementación del programa "Para un mejor aprendizaje" para potenciar habilidades y resiliencia.
Refuerzo Escolar para Permanencia:

Acompañamiento a NNAJ para incorporación a la escuela regular, con actividades lúdicas y refuerzo académico.
Dos jornadas semanales durante cuatro meses, adaptándose a necesidades presenciales o virtuales.
Capacitación a Educadores:

Formación para diversificar metodologías pedagógicas en círculos educativos, centrada en educación socioemocional.
Dos jornadas presenciales y virtuales con metodologías innovadoras.
Apoyo de Padres y Cuidadores:

Jornadas de sensibilización sobre la importancia de proteger a NNAJ en emergencias.
Fortalecimiento de habilidades socioemocionales para mejorar la convivencia familiar.
Capacitación a Docentes en Emergencias:

Proceso formativo sobre Educación en Emergencia con énfasis en educación socioemocional.
Proporcionar material educativo para incorporar acciones sociemocionales en la planificación educativa.
Indicadores y Objetivos Sectoriales:

Objetivo 1: Contribuir a la recuperación socioemocional y continuidad educativa de NNAJ en emergencia.
Objetivo 2: Reactivar el sistema educativo para promover el derecho a la educación.
Indicadores incluyen entregas de kits, participación en espacios temporales, formación de educadores, atención psicosocial, y sensibilización familiar.
Metas:

325 Vouchers y 900 Kits entregados.
300 Docentes fortalecidos.
Atención a 4625 NNAJ en refuerzo escolar y salud psicoemocional.
Formación de 1050 responsables familiares en educación socioemocional.
La estrategia aborda la educación socioemocional y la continuidad educativa en situaciones de emergencia, con acciones específicas para diferentes grupos, destacando la participación comunitaria y la adaptabilidad a las necesidades locales.

project_name: Conflict Preparedness and Protection Risk Education for At-Risk Communities in Cabo Delgado
project_objective: Under this project, NPA’s interventions alongside our local partner Fundação Wiwanana in close coordination with INGD at both national and regional level in Cabo Delgado focus on reinforcing local and national preparedness capacity. NPA therefore through this intervention strengthens Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP) at the national and local levels, with focus on developing a national capacity to implement CPP and contribute to the preparedness and protection of people residing in high-risk areas or likely to return to such areas. The action will strengthen national and local conflict and disaster preparedness. At the national level, NPA will partner with both the national and regional  INGD delegations to develop conflict hazard DRR/DP protocols, activities, and mechanisms and utilize its CPP framework to provide training, technical, and material assistance to enhance INGD’s capacity. The aim of this component is to create baseline capacity within INGD to coordinate, monitor, and support CPP activities and enable different actors (local authorities, humanitarian actors, first responders such as the fire brigades, community safety councils, peace clubs, etc.) at various levels to implement and benefit from these actions. At local level, NPA will partner with Fundação Wiwanana for implementation in communities to pilot the approaches developed with INGD. NPA and Wiwanana, in coordination and partnership with INGD, will deliver CPP safety and EORE trainings in target at-risk communities. The overall aim is to develop and pilot CPP activities with INGD and equip civilians with the concrete knowledge, skills, and tools they need to better prepare themselves and their communities for eventual attacks and conflict-associated risks and increase their ability to cope with crisis situations. Training modules (tailored to address the different needs and participation requirements of girls, boys, women, and men) will be designed and delivered for at-risk communities and IDP populations with high return rates as well as community focal points and partner staff. Civil servants and humanitarian staff working in high-risk areas will receive pre-deployment CPP training.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods Programme Cabo Delgado
project_objective: NPA is supporting its implementing partner União Provincial de Camponeses de Cabo-Delgado (UPC CD) in the implementation of Foods Security and Livelihoods Programme in northern province of Cabo-Delgado. The Programme aims to provide life-sustaining emergency livelihood support to crisis affected persons in Metuge district in the Cabo Delgado province, in line with the response priorities in the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan. The programme also aims to restore and strengthen people’s livelihoods to improve their sustainability and thus their resilience. The programme’s main objective is to provide access to quality agricultural inputs (seed and tools) for increased household food productivity, increased access to sufficient food in quantity and quality to meet dietary needs and enable livelihoods access to food through production (agriculture) or income. The agriculture inputs assistance will enable target households to meet their immediate needs in initiating life sustaining food production (6 weeks cycle for horticulture inputs and 3 to 6 months for cereals), diversify and improve their nutrition.

project_name: Protección de niñez y adolescencia vulnerable en situación de movilidad y afectada por la sequía
project_objective:
El Salvador enfrenta grandes retos asociados a la niñez y adolescencia en contexto de movilidad (desplazamiento forzado, flujos de salida del país, retornos, migrantes en tránsito hacia el norte del continente, refugiados y solicitantes de asilo). 
Los factores que subyacen a la movilidad humana en El Salvador son diversos y complejos e incluyen, entre otros: desigualdad social, brechas de acceso a servicios básicos, violencia en sus diversas formas y ámbitos, incluida la violencia basada en género (VBG), limitado acceso a empleo formal y oportunidades económicas, y pretensiones de reunificación familiar. 
Los desastres naturales y de origen humano, exacerbados por el cambio climático, agravan los factores subyacentes a la movilidad. 
La violencia basada en género también motiva a las niñas, adolescentes y mujeres a huir y recurrir al desplazamiento interno y a la migración en condición irregular como medidas de afrontamiento, que ponen en riesgo su vida y seguridad en tránsito y destino. 
Más de 70,000 niños y niñas viven en el país sin uno o ambos padres como resultado de la migración.
La ubicación de El Salvador en la ruta migratoria en el norte de Centroamérica, su economía dolarizada y una percepción de seguridad son factores que inciden en el incremento de personas en movimientos mixtos que atraviesan el país. 
La violencia generalizada que sufren los niños, niñas y adolescentes en sus hogares, comunidades o escuelas, siguen siendo un detonante para el desplazamiento y la migración. La violencia tiene impactos diferenciados; si bien los homicidios disminuyeron en los últimos cinco años, seis de cada diez víctimas son niños y hombres jóvenes (entre 13 y 35 años), y la violencia sexual afecta desproporcionadamente a niñas y mujeres jóvenes.
La Organización Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) declaró en julio de 2023 que se habían dado las condiciones para la aparición del fenómeno de El Niño.  También declaró que los efectos serían más notables a partir del segundo semestre de 2023, con una duración de 9 a 12 meses. Para la región centroamericana, la OMM informa que el fenómeno suele causar sequías severas.  
Se prevé que la sequía tenga graves repercusiones en los medios de subsistencia y la seguridad alimentaria de los hogares de las zonas más afectadas. Estos impactos pueden llevar a las personas a adoptar estrategias negativas para hacer frente a la situación, como el trabajo infantil, la discriminación en el reparto de alimentos dentro de la familia y el matrimonio precoz, entre otras. 
Con el presente proyecto, UNICEF tiene como objetivo brindar una respuesta humanitaria para que niñas, niños y adolescentes en contexto de movilidad o afectados por sequía, que están expuestos a violencia, abuso o explotación, incluyendo a población LGBTIQ+ o con discapacidad, accedan a servicios especializados e integrales de protección de la infancia. Ello orientado al fortalecimiento de su resiliencia, la reintegración en sus comunidades y la plena restitución de sus derechos. 
Las niñas, niños y adolescentes con necesidades de protección beneficiarios recibirán protección a través de albergues o acceso a espacios seguros, apoyo psicosocial y atención a la salud mental, asistencia legal y respuesta a otras necesidades humanitarias (asistencia humanitaria); junto con el desarrollo de habilidades para la vida para ellas y ellos, así como para las madres, padres o personas cuidadoras, fortaleciendo los lazos familiares. Para ello, se apoyarán servicios especializados de protección adecuados a la edad, género y diversidad, líneas de ayuda  mecanismos de denuncia, espacios amigables de apoyo psicosocial, mecanismos de referencia y gestión de casos, promoviendo entornos protectores a nivel familiar y comunitario. El proyecto se implementará bajo un enfoque inclusivo de género y discapacidad, promoviendo la continuidad de los servicios que puedan ser afectados.

project_name: Ayuda humanitaria multisectorial para atender las necesidades urgentes de las personas más vulnerables de Venezuela (2ª Fase) --- Multisectoral humanitarian assistance to address the urgent needs of the most vulnerable people in Venezuela (2nd Phase)
project_objective:
El proyecto tiene como objetivo dar cotinuidad, fortalecer y consolidar el consorcio CONAHVE que actualmente lleva a cabo un proyecto multisectorial, en el que participan 5 organizaciones internacionales y 7 socios implementadores locales. El proyecto busca mejorar el acceso a servicios de protección, brindar servicios de salud primaria y asistencia humanitaria a las personas y comunidades más vulnerables afectadas por la compleja crisis venezolana.  En esta segunda fase, las organizaciones del consorcio centrarán sus acciones en 8 estados de Venezuela: Amazonas, Distrito Capital, Bolivar, Miranda, Sucre, Zulia, Falcón, y Delta Amacuro, brindando una respuesta integral, multisectorial y coordinada. La intervención pretende hacer frente a las consecuencias humanitarias de la crisis, respondiendo a las necesidades más urgentes de las personas vulnerables a través de la prestación de servicios y asistencia en los sectores de: 
Protección: Incluye actividades de prevención y atención a personas en riesgo y sobrevivientes de VBG, víctimas de Trata de personas y protección de NNA. Los servicios facilitados incluyen la gestión de casos,atención psicosocial individual y grupal y orientación legal. Se brindará asistencia material para la atención específica de los casos de acuerdo a niveles de vulnerabilidad, así como espacios de alojamiento temporal para mujeres sobrevivientes de VBG bajo riesgo inminente a la vida y víctimas de Trata de Personas. Se efectuaran sensibilizaciones comunitarias que promuevan la visibilización de las violencias, y se incluiran sesiones sobre nuevas masculinidades; se realizará fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales.Se realizarán dotaciones a instituciones públicas de protección, principalmente asociadas al área de Protección Infantil o de atención VBG. 
Servicios de Salud Primaria: Se facilitaran consultas de APS en centros de salud fijos y clínicas moviles. Se acompañará de actividades de promoción de la salud en escuelas y comunidades. Los servicios y asistencia a través de los puntos moviles serán brindados mensualmente por personal médico especializado.
Salud Sexual Reproductiva: Se brindarán servicios de SSR en línea con el MISP, con enfasis en la atención de mujeres, adolescentes y niñas en edad reproductiva. El Paquete de Servicios de SSR incluye: planificación familiar,colocación de métodos anticonceptivos,anticoncepción de emergencia, consulta ginecológica, tamizaje de ITS y tratamiento médico, examen citológico, servicio básico de  atención prenatal con controles médicos.
Salud Mental: Se efectuaran sesiones de apoyo psicosocial individual y grupal, a través de equipo especializado que contribuirán a la identificación temprana de signos de alerta en salud mental, autocuidado y mecanismos saludables de afrontamiento. Se realizarán actividades de bienestar comunitario y actividades psicocosiales comunitarias centradas en educacion sexual, manejo emocional, crianza positiva y habilidades de afrontamiento saludables. 
Nutrición: Se realizará tamizaje nutricional, entrega de micronutrientes y desparasitación profiláctica a U5 y mujeres embarazadas y lactantes. Todos los casos con dx de desnutrición aguda/crónica serán derivados para la atención necesaria. 
Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene: Rehabilitación de instalaciones WASH en centros de salud, protección y escuelas. Entrega de kits de purificación de agua, higiene y dignidad a personas vulnerables. Se realizarán sensibilizaciones comunitarias en agua segura, lavado de manos, higiene del hogar, higiene menstrual, PCI y gestión de residuos. Capacitaciones a personal de salud en WASH-PCI, con suministros de insumos. En los centros rehabilitados, se promoverá una mejor gestión de residuos y las buenas prácticas para mitigar la proliferación de vectores y fomentar cultyura de eliminación y reciclaje apropiado de desechos.

project_objective:

1. Las comunidades wayúu pueden evaluar su vulnerabilidad y su capacidad de adaptación al cambio climático mediante prácticas ancestrales.

Actividades:
1. Taller de formación sobre buenas prácticas de resiliencia y adaptabilidad frente al cambio climático.
2. Desarrollo de espacios de diálogos inter-generacionales sobre el cambio climático y prácticas ancestrales.
3. Desarrollo de iniciativas sobre cambio climático.
4. Implementación de campañas que sean lideradas por los niños, niñas y adultos sobre la resiliencia en el cambio climático.

project_name: Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Risk Mitigation, Prevention and Survivor-Centered Support for Rohingya and Host Communities
project_objective:
IOM will be enhancing its GBV program, that was established in 2017, with a focus on refugees and host communities. The program centers around three key pillars: survivor-centered support, risk mitigation, and addressing the root causes that perpetuate GBV, all in alignment with IOM's GBV in Crises Institutional Framework targeting people of all genders and ages, including people with diverse sexual orientations, gender identities, gender expressions, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC).
IOM directly oversees case management, providing a comprehensive support package through nine Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) at eight different camps, abd uses appropriate camp facilities to support male and SOGEISC individuals who  need case management.  IOM also supports an emergency safe shelter for survivors of GBV. IOM’s WGSS offers various services, including information dissemination, age-appropriate psychosocial support, awareness and educational activities, life-skills training, and forums for information-sharing and learning. This includes peer-led programs on topics such as GBV, sexual and reproductive health, menstrual hygiene, and disaster preparedness. IOM, with its implementing partner PULSE Bangladesh Society, will roll out MBR (MaBoinor Rosom-Mother’s and Sister’s Way) edition 1 & 2 as well as EMAP and Girl Shine Curriculum in the locations IOM is operating. For sustainability and local involvement, IOM, with it’s partner, will expand capacity-building efforts to include community groups, community advocates, imams, majhis, GBV volunteers, and women's committee members. These activities aim to transition key WGSS awareness and outreach functions into regular meetings, capacity-building sessions, and supervision. This approach enhances community ownership and accountability, addressing the root causes of gender inequality. IOM will collaborate with the Protection Research Unit to develop peer-led, evidence-based curricula, involving men, women, and people with diverse gender identities and sexual orientations, ensuring inclusivity and safe entry points for GBV services.
IOM's program will prioritize GBV risk mitigation, placing a stronger emphasis on the increased participation of women, girls, SOGEISC, and persons with disabilities. IOM will identify GBV risks and vulnerable groups through participatory assessments and data collection, including regular safety audits, involving women and girls in assessing their access to and their safety around provision of services. Menstrual health education, based on IOM's summary report ""Ma Boinor Rosom"" and its related curriculum, will be a focus, along with life skills and male engagement programs. Empowerment and skills development activities for women and girls will be more structured and diversified including the production of reusable sanitary pads through CFW. Graduates from skills-building programs will serve as peer trainers and receive coaching and capacity-building support. IOM will continue to ensure the preposition and distribution of dignity items that specifically address women and girl’s needs. IOM will continue its capacity building effort to train IOM and partner staff and national authorities protection, GBV core concepts, principles, risk identification and mitigation measures, PSEA, AAP and Code of Conduct.
IOM will also support Rohingya women in identifying opportunities for enhanced participation and engagement, replicating its Women's Participation Project as a best practice model for fostering social cohesion and ensuring disability inclusion.
