project_name: Provision of critical support to the health care system in NW Syria
project_objective:
Hyperinflation, worsened by the Ukraine war, has drastically increased staple goods prices in Syria, outpacing wage growth and pushing 90% of the population below the poverty line. The health sector, largely dependent on outside funding, has seen numerous facility closures since late 2021. A cholera outbreak since September 2022 has reported over 71,463 cases and 23 deaths in NWS. Severe and acute malnutrition among children has risen catastrophically from 1% in 2021 to 1.7% in 2022. Acute maternal malnutrition affects 11% of mothers in NWS.
The need for free, quality healthcare is at an all-time high, especially for vulnerable groups like IDPs and PWDs. Primary needs include essential primary healthcare, emergency care, treatment for NCDs, pediatric consultations, dialysis sessions, medicines, and both general and specialized surgical services.
The dramatic increase in medication prices is due to the small pharmaceutical industry in NWS, which relies on expensive imports and medicines from GoS-controlled areas. This has led to a large increase in medicine prices, causing many patients to reduce treatment. This is particularly concerning for young children and the elderly suffering from NCD. The high price of antibiotics has become a significant barrier for most families. The availability of specialized medical items is even lower. Essential pregnancy-related medication and supplements are increasingly inaccessible for women and girls of reproductive age.
Also, supplements like iron, folate, and calcium, are given high anaemia (25% in children under 5) and malnutrition (11%). Stunting affects 25-28% of children under 5. Heart surgery patients face death without intervention, but at $5,000, most can’t afford it. Dialysis patients depend on free sessions and medicine.
Intervention
The project seeks to provide free-of-charge medicine to 23 health facilities including dialysis centers, cardiology centers, PHC centers, General hospitals, and mobile emergency units. Furthermore, the project aims to provide stipends and running costs to 4 MEUs, 3 PHC centers, 1 blood bank, 1 pediatric/neonatal ICU, 2 dialysis centers, 1 cardiology center, and 1 physiotherapy/rehabilitation/prosthetic center. Furthermore, the project will include the support of 10 referral vehicles, training of 150 health staff, rehabilitation of 8 health facilities, and provision of medical equipment to 10 health facilities.
Protection risks and other risks
In response to health facility violence, emergency plans are prepared for high-risk situations, including staff guidance, equipment relocation, and schedule adjustments. Communication with IR’s safety and security department is established for immediate updates on risks or emergencies. For Gender-Based Violence (GBV) during travel to health facilities, IR trains health workers on GBV case management, increasing personnel at target facilities. IR supports a referral system with designated staff and transport for GBV victims, enhancing access to specialized medical services. To protect from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, all IR employees sign a code of conduct outlining proper behavior and disorderly conduct measures. A whistleblowing policy is clarified to all personnel, ensuring serious and confidential handling of sexual exploitation or abuse complaints. Contact details for reporting such incidents are made available to IR partners and communities.
PSEA:A survey of potential beneficiaries is conducted and analyzed to understand and respond to the targeted community. This ensures participation and rights of all genders and ages, adhering to IRW’s Safeguarding policy, including PSEA. Staff and volunteers are educated on PSEA and safeguarding. 3- Project updates are communicated to local councils and advertised in targeted areas. With referral services, IR ensures the participation of vulnerable groups in the project. Outreach workers, trained in PSEA, inform community members about their rights toward IR.

project_name: Improving Access to WASH Services for Conflict-Affected Communities in Ndian, Meme and Kupe-Manenguba Divisions, South West Region, Cameroon
project_objective:
The project aims to improve access to emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services for conflict affected and vulnerable host communities in the South West region of Cameroon. Recurring violence continue to fuel instability in the North West and South West leading to large-scale displacements, aggravating WASH vulnerabilities.
As of February 2023, close to 70,000 persons are estimated to be internally displaced while almost 90,000 have returned to their habitual place of residence, as per the multi-sectoral needs assessment (IOM MSNA, February 2023). The use of unsafe drinking water sources is considered the most likely cause of repeated cholera outbreaks, according to an August 2023 OCHA report. Limited access to clean water and poor sanitation services have accelerated the spread of water-borne diseases like cholera, which remains highly contagious and potentially fatal.
This project will target 35,000 conflict-affected people with sustainable and gender-sensitive WASH services. It will prioritize reestablishing damaged facilities and extending supply systems in IDP/returnee locations and strategic urban areas across Ndian, Meme and Kupe-Manenguba Divisions. Focus will be on providing equitable services to women and girls and persons living with disabilities.
Key activities will include:
	Rehabilitating damaged water points and extending supply systems with new distribution connections to increase availability and access to safe drinking water. This includes in harnessing of springs, rehabilitating water catchments and or extending existing community piped water supply system, such as construction of stand taps in areas with high population density, which provide adequate quantity of portable water. This will help eliminate dependence on contaminated sources and cut disease transmission.
	Distributing critical WASH Kits like soaps, menstrual hygiene supplies, and water purification tablets. These basics supplies improve health and hygiene practices while reducing the risk of poor hygiene-related morbidity and mortality. Provision of Menstrual Hygiene Management ( MHM) Kits to Women and Girls of menstrual age will be imperative in order to prevent them from engaging in negative coping mechanism to provide for their needs.
	Constructing emergency communal latrines and handwashing facilities for displaced groups to largely reduce open defecation. This is crucial to interrupt disease spread and ensure safety and dignity, especially for women and girls in rural areas and clustered urban neigborhoods. 
	Conducting hygiene promotion and capacity building to sustain services beyond the project's lifetime. This aims to spur behavioral change and community ownership for long-term impact.
The recent needs assessment conducted across conflict-affected communities of the South West highlighted alarming gaps in water, sanitation and hygiene services faced by both displaced and host communities. Therefore the project will have an important impact on the safety, health and wellbeing of women and girls in the target communities. Improved access to water and sanitation facilities is vital to ensure dignity, privacy and security for females. The provision of menstrual hygiene items is also key to enabling adolescent girls and women to manage their periods in a healthy way. Overall, enhanced WASH services will cut water-borne disease rates and decrease preventable illnesses and deaths. This will benefit the wider population, spurring productivity and human capital gains.

project_name: Contribuer au renforcement de la prévention et de la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë modérée chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois et chez les femmes enceintes et allaitantes dans le cadre de la réponse à l’urgence soudanaise à l’Est du Tchad
project_objective:
Le 15 avril, des combats ont éclaté à Khartoum, la capitale du Soudan, entre les Forces armées soudanaises (FAS) et les Forces de soutien rapide (FSR). En quelques jours, des affrontements ont éclaté dans tout le pays, notamment au Darfour, région frontalière avec le Tchad. Ces affrontements sont le résultat de tensions politico-militaires, alimentées par de profondes rivalités ethniques, qui divisent le pouvoir en place et, plus largement, le pays tout entier. 

Au 15 juillet, plus de 225 000 soudanais ont traversé la frontière vers le Tchad et selon l’UNHCR, d’ici la fin de l’année, ce serait plus de 300 000 réfugiés soudanais qui pourraient arriver au Tchad. Ces réfugiés se sont principalement installés dans les provinces du Ouaddaï et du Sila. Ainsi, le Ouddai compte actuellement plus de 206 000 réfugiés et le Sila 47 000. Avant l’éclatement de cette crise, le Tchad accueillait déjà plus d'un million de personnes déplacées, dont 407 000 réfugiés soudanais et demandeurs d'asile dans 14 camps situés à l'est dans les provinces d'Ennedi Est, Ouaddaï et Wadi Fira.

Parmi les réfugiés, la majorité est constituée de femmes et d' enfants dont 21% < 5 ans.  93% des retournés sont des femmes et des enfants. On note une prévalence élevée de la malnutrition chez les enfants parfois associée à la rougeole, avec pour conséquence une mortalité élevée. 

Au mois de juin 2023, l'hôpital d’Adré a enregistré une quinzaine de décès d’enfants chez les enfants liés à la malnutrition. Il est donc urgent pour les acteurs intervenant dans le secteur de la santé et de la nutrition de renforcer les efforts tant en matière de prise en charge que sur la prévention de la malnutrition.

ALIMA et son partenaire national Alerte Santé interviennent depuis le 8 mai au Ouaddaï à travers 3 cliniques mobiles (Labandafak, Midjeguilta, Lycée 2 d’Adré) à travers lesquelles 2 048 enfants ont été dépistés pour malnutrition au 16 juillet 2023, dont 376 MAM (18%) et 258 MAS (13%). Par ailleurs, 9 585 personnes ont été sensibilisées sur la prévention de la malnutrition dans cette zone d’intervention. Au camp de Zabout au niveau du Sila où le consortium intervient depuis le 16 juin 2023 à travers un poste de santé, 1 303 enfants ont été dépistés pour malnutrition, dont 426 MAM (33%) et 289 MAS (22%). 19 460 personnes ont été également sensibilisées sur la prévention de la malnutrition.

Dans le cadre de ce projet, ALIMA/AS interviendra dans le camp de Réfugiés de Zabout dans le DS d’Adré, ainsi que dans les sites de cliniques mobiles dans le DS de Goz-Beida.

project_name: Provision of Food Security and Livelihoods Support to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan
project_objective:
The overall objective of the NRC’s proposed project is to ensure vulnerable crises-affected people have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable, safe, and dignified access to life-saving assistance to meet their needs. The overall objective is to be achieved through three main cluster objectives namely; provision of food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations (in IPC 4 and 5), enhancement and sustainability of emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock and reduction of dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb & adapt to shocks & contextual changes. 
This will ensure improved food availability and access to vulnerable households in crisis and emergency phases through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support, capacity building and reduction of dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks and shift to resiliency. NRC will ensure a timely preposition of assorted crop and vegetable seeds as well as tools, complimented by capacity building in the respective livelihoods areas thus providing beneficiaries with the means to reestablish their own production and help them address the threat of hunger. To support the pastoralist households, refresher trainings of Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) and small ruminants restocking will be supported. In addition, the fisher folk will be supported with fishing gear and skills through training on fish hygiene, processing, and preservation. 
NRC will conduct vulnerability mapping during Payam Community Based Participatory Planning (CBPP) consultative meetings at the start of the project, involving key community leaders including women, village headmen, local authorities, key line ministry representatives, religious leaders and sub-chiefs. Households that are extremely food insecure as a result of the severe loss of assets as a result of disasters either natural and man-made including food production inputs and are unable to support themselves will be prioritized for agricultural inputs and livestock support. The projects provided smallholder farmers with both on-farm and off-farm support such as, agricultural value addition, processing and marketing, enterprise development, post-harvest handling, seed multiplication, village saving and loans (VSLAs) as well as cross-cutting issues as gender and GBV, nutrition, HIV/AIDS and group dynamics. In most agro-pastoralists’ communities in South Sudan, women are the main providers of the daily food for their families while men are considered to be providing security and herding livestock. However, women continue to be unequally affected by food insecurity and have less access to land and credit than men, limiting their ability to purchase agricultural tools, seeds, or hire labor that could increase their crop production Reduction in food intake as a coping mechanism has greatly affected the female population. During targeting and implementation, priority will be given to women and people with disabilities and their specific needs will be addressed. The proposed project will be implemented to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Upper Nile, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan where NRC has a long record of implementing food security and livelihoods activities. The project targets a total of 209, 000 through various FSL interventions. The project teams will work closely with local authorities, protection partners, government and key line ministries.

project_name: WASH Emergency and Static as long-term response for vulnerable Host, IDPs, returnees and refugees in South Sudan.
project_objective:
The proposed NRC’s WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) interventions for 2024 is continued to support the people affected by conflict, natural disaster and displacement in emergency context and static as long-term support for the IDPs, host community and people to return, resettle and reintegrate with host community. The interventions are designed to address the emergency WASH needs through rapid response mechanism (RRT) and emergency response and   contribute to improve health, nutrition, education, Livelihood and food security, shelter and protection outcomes and durable solutions through NRC static WASH response. The proposed interventions are to reduce prevalence of malnutrition, contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality, provide access to basic WASH services in underserved and hard to reach locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility and durable access to WASH amongst 250, 000 IDPs, returnees, refuges and vulnerable host communities in in South Sudan. NRC’s WASH interventions will be integrated and implemented in close coordination with NRC’s other core competencies of Shelter, Education, Livelihood and Food security, ICLA and protection programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to uplift people’s lives and contributing to South Sudan HRP 2024 and WASH Cluster objectives and the 2024 Humanitarian Response. 

Recognizing WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. NRC’s integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition in targeted locations. NRC will consult and engage communities in preliminary assessments and design process to ensure all NRC’s interventions are tailored to local context and to establish appropriated water  and sanitation facilities at community, institutions and household level. To enhance and ensure sustainability and proper usage of the facilities comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) , Schools and other institutional staff. Solid waste management training will also be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns.

To ensure durable solution and continues access to safe water; NRC will establish / rehabilitate small scale solar powered water  supply schemes , new boreholes through cost effective manual Borehole  drilling and machine drilling . The proposed water supply interventions will increase the safe water access to schools, health, nutrition and protection centers, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WAH facilities and route to WASH facilities.

NRC will construct owner driven household / family shared latrines to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. The approach will enhance the ownership and sustainability of the facilities.  NRC will also promote good hygiene practices and awareness through training of community hygiene promoters who then will be conducting hygiene promotion at their own communities, community hygiene  campaigns, hygiene  promotion campaigns and sessions at intuitional levels. NRC will also provide hygiene kits, WASH-NFIs and soaps to the vulnerable communities specially in hard-to-reach areas.

project_objective:
Objective: The project aims to improve maternal and child nutrition in Venezuela, with special emphasis on strengthening the early detection and treatment of wasting and other forms of life-threatening acute malnutrition in early childhood and preventing malnutrition, nutritional deficiencies micronutrients and overweight in childhood, adolescence and during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

Project Description: In line with UNICEF's global strategy and commitment to protect and promote diets, services and practices that support optimal nutrition, growth and development for all children, adolescents and women, UNICEF aims to strengthen public health and nutrition services to ensure adequate water, sanitation, basic equipment and treatment supplies for routine maternal and child care of malnutrition and management of complications. The project includes a strong capacity building component for health workers and the community in coordination with universities, academic institutions, the Ministry of Popular Power for Health (MPPH) and the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) for early identification of malnourished and at-risk patients,  timely referral and appropriate case management.

UNICEF will support in providing regular health checks through the national public system and extending services to the community through nutritional assessments carried out by health and nutrition teams from MoH, NIN or implementing partners to identify undernourished individuals and ensure the necessary supplements and dietary plans are provided. Additionally, the project will expand its reach to schools, implementing educational programs on healthy eating habits to encourage a healthy diet in children and adolescents, crucial for their long-term health and well-being.

Strategies and Implementation: 
UNICEF's strategy will be based on five strategic changes to improve maternal and child nutrition:
1. A systemic approach to strengthening maternal and child nutrition services.
2. An explicit focus on addressing child malnutrition in all its forms.
3. A comprehensive life cycle approach to nutrition programming.
4. A deliberate emphasis on improving diets, services and practices.
5. Greater attention to community participation.

The project will focus on community engagement, working with local health and nutrition authorities and developing sustainable nutrition practices. Through close collaboration with local communities, we aim to adapt our interventions to effectively fit cultural dietary practices. Our collaborative efforts prioritize knowledge sharing and resource optimization, both crucial to project success. Additionally, we will achieve sustainability of this initiative by empowering communities and establishing local support networks.

Monitoring and Evaluation: To ensure the effectiveness of the project, we will implement a robust monitoring and evaluation system. This will involve regular monitoring of nutritional and health status, competency assessments of health professionals after training, and feedback from schools on accountability for the impact of nutrition education programs. It will also include monitoring the distribution and use of supplies, as well as evaluating the quality of case management based on standardized treatments.

Prioritized areas: the project will mainly focus the full interventions on 54 municipalities, located in Amazonas, Apure, Bolívar, Delta Amacuro, Distrito Capital, La Guaira, Miranda, Sucre, Táchira, and Zulia states, however this also includes the support to national programs such as deworming program.

project_name: Protección de los niños más vulnerables en 54 municipios prioritarios de Venezuela --- Protection of Most Vulnerable Children in 54 Priority Municipalities in Venezuela
project_objective:
In 2024, UNICEF will increase the convergence and quality of its programme for most affected populations in the most vulnerable regions, addressing underlying risks to vulnerability to reduce humanitarian needs by enhancing access to critical services with an integrated package of health, nutrition, education, child protection and WASH. Improving child protection services remains a priority, and UNICEF's systemic approach include tackle child protection issues: birth registration and identity, case management for at-risk and vulnerable children including victims of violence, human trafficking, and unaccompanied and separated children, and psychosocial support and mental health care for children and caregivers.

In this project, UNICEF's key intervention will be: i) Strengthening the capacity of sub-national child protection system to carry out case management of vulnerable children.3 Ii) Provision of community mental health and psychosocial support services. iii) Access to a safe channel to report sexual exploitation and abuse. iv) Alternative care measures for children and adolescents and family reunification. v) Support community platforms on empowerment, participation, behaviour change actions and social norms linked to the protection of children and adolescents. 

The area of implementation will be in 54 municipalities in District Capital, Amazonas, Apure, Bolivar, Delta Amacuro, Miranda, Sucre, Tachira, Zulia and La Guaira.

project_name: Seguridad alimentaria, agua y saneamiento en la escuela
project_objective:
Seguridad alimentaria, agua y saneamiento es un proyecto que tiene como propósito desarrollar capacidades de la comunidad educativa para garantizar la disponibilidad y acceso de alimentos frescos mediante la implementación de huertos escolares y promover el aprovechamiento biológico a través de la adecuada preparación e ingesta de alimentos escolares. Además, promover el involucramiento de la comunidad educativa para implementar infraestructura básica escolar.
Este proyecto está considerado para ser implementado en 10 escuelas de los municipios de Cunén, Sacapulas y San Pedro Jocopilas del departamento de Quiché, Guatemala.
El proyecto se desarrollará mediante tres fases: 
I.	Desarrollo de capacidades de la comunidad educativa: involucramiento de actores clave para el diseño y planificación de la intervención en el área escolar. 
II.	Seguridad alimentaria: promover la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional mediante la implementación de un huerto escolar que involucre a maestros, estudiantes y padres de familia.  Capacitación en buenas prácticas en la manipulación de alimentos  y nutrición, dirigido a madres de familia que participan en el proceso de preparación de la alimentación escolar.  Capacitación a maestros y estudiantes sobre nutrición balanceada, que les permita introducir la cosecha del huerto escolar a su menú de consumo diario. 
III.	Agua y saneamiento: construcción de infraestructura básica que garantice el agua y saneamiento para los estudiantes.  En esta fase se involucra a padres de familia y actores clave de la comunidad educativa para el diseño y construcción de cosechadores de agua de lluvia, módulos de servicios sanitarios, lavamanos, cocinas básicas con bodega, estufa y filtro para el consumo de agua segura. 
Población meta: 
Beneficiarios directos 4,500 estudiantes. Población indirecta 23,000 personas (incluida la comunidad educativa de 15 establecimientos educativos).

project_name: Generación Verde/ Green Generation
project_objective:
Generación Verde/ Green Generation (GG) es una iniciativa piloto conjunta de Save the Children y el Fondo Mundial para la Naturaleza -WWF- por sus siglas en inglés, diseñada para para reforzar la acción medioambiental en a través de actividades educativas extraescolares mediante la metodología basada en proyectos.
El propósito de este proyecto es concientizar a los niños sobre la importancia del cuidado del medio ambiente y los recursos naturales, así como buscar soluciones para la adaptación basada en ecosistemas y cambio climático. 
La metodología basada en proyectos propone actividades centradas en los niños y dirigidas por ellos, basadas en diversos enfoques de enseñanza y aprendizaje. Las actividades proporcionan la oportunidad de identificar y resolver problemas medioambientales de la vida real de forma crítica. 
El programa GG ofrece oportunidades para que los niños aprendan  temas medioambientales relevantes en la escuela y la comunidad y adquieran experiencias y habilidades que pueden promover la elaboración de un plan de acción a nivel comunitario, que involucre a toda la comunidad educativa. 
El programa está diseñado por unidades. Los temas de las unidades son:
 1. Por qué es importante la naturaleza
 2. Nuestros bosques
 3. Deforestación
 4. Vida salvaje
 5. Consumo y contaminación del agua
 6. Residuos y basura
Todas las unidades están adaptadas al contexto de Guatemala y los recursos didácticos para los maestros están traducidos al idioma K´iche. El aprendizaje basado en proyectos se espera que los estudiantes puedan buscar soluciones e incorporar acciones innovadoras a largo plazo. 
El proyecto se desarrollará mediante tres fases: 
I.	Capacitación docente sobre la metodología basada en proyectos de Generación Verde/ Green Generation. 

II.	Desarrollo del proceso formativo dirigido a estudiantes. 


III.	Agua y saneamiento: construcción de infraestructura básica que garantice el agua y saneamiento para los estudiantes.  En esta fase se involucra a padres de familia y actores clave de la comunidad educativa para el diseño y construcción de cosechadores de agua de lluvia, módulos de servicios sanitarios, lavamanos y filtros para el consumo de agua segura. 
Población meta: 
Este proyecto está considerado para ser implementado en 33 escuelas del municipio de San Pedro Jocopilas del departamento de Quiché, con un alcance de más de 7,000 estudiantes. El impacto se verá reflejado en una población indirecta de más de 25,000 personas incluida la comunidad educativa.

Costos:
El proyecto tiene un valor total de $,1,500,000.00 los cuales serán ejecutados de acuerdo a la programación:  
1.	Contrataciones y gastos generales (personal que acompañará la implementación y será responsable de capacitar al personal docente).
2.	Compra y Reproducción de materiales educativos.
3.	Costos de facilitación del proceso formativo. 
4.	Construcción de infraestructura básica escolar.

project_name: Strengthening food and nutrition security through livelihood asset creation activities to support the early recovery of 20,000 people in crisis-affected areas in the North-West and South-West regions of Cameroon.
project_objective:
The project aims to improve access to food and help improve social cohesion, support early recovery  of vulnerable and food-insecure communities affected by the internal socio-political crisis in the North-West and South-West regions. This project will focus on the rapid deployment of food aid through the distribution of food conditional on participation in activities. And it will address the immediate food needs of vulnerable people (women, men, children), including internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees and local populations severely affected by the crisis and suffering from food insecurity disrupting economic, agricultural, and pastoral activities in these regions. A total 20,000 beneficiaries (60% women) will be covered, i,e. 10,000 per region. Food distributions will be linked to participation in economic empowerment activities. To implement the activities, Community-Based Participatory Planning (CBPP) sessions will be carried out in collaboration with local community members (women and men), decentralized technical services of key ministries and partners to identify the real needs and priorities of local communities that will help affected populations develop their own response strategies and strengthen their resilience. This people-centred approach ensures the provision of effective solutions with beneficiaries and reduces reliance on relief. Assistance through for FFA, will be implemented using in-kind Food for six (06) months under the FFA-early recovery. The transfer value is calculated based on the identified food gap and is designed to assist beneficiaries to reach the recommended minimum calories intake of 2,100 Kcal per person per day. 
WFP will collaborate closely with Government technical ministries, cooperating partners and communities to ensure project implementation and sustainability. Nutrition, Gender and protection issues are taken into consideration at all the stages of the project elaboration, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Gender and protection risk analysis will be carried out and the most vulnerable will be targeted, including female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, people suffering from chronic diseases, etc. Project sites will be in secure areas and at convenient distance from the homes of the beneficiaries. To support smooth project implementation and ensure sustainability, capacity strengthening sessions will be organized for all stakeholders on gender and protection policy, project management, monitoring and nutrition.

project_name: Respuesta nutricional para tratamiento de Desnutrición Aguda en población materno-infantil en condición de Tránsito migratorio en municipios de Frontera Sur-Oriente de Honduras.
project_objective:
A raíz del alto flujo migratorio en el departamento de El Paraíso se ha aumentado la demanda de servicios básicos, en especial de salud y nutrición, que no pueden ser cubiertos por instituciones del Estado, los CDT,S cuentan con las mínimas condiciones en temas de seguridad alimentaria, salud y nutrición, lo que puede originar que el estado nutricional de los niños y niñas, lactantes y embarazadas se agrave. Surge la necesidad de la intervención para contribuir a la reducción, morbilidad y mortalidad de niños y niñas migrantes y en tránsito, que se ven afectados por las pobres condiciones en temas de nutrición.
La propuesta de proyecto “Respuesta nutricional para tratamiento de Desnutrición Aguda en población materno-infantil en condición de Tránsito migratorio en municipios de frontera Sur-Oriente de Honduras.” se enfoca en el manejo ambulatorio, tratamiento y atención de la desnutrición aguda en niñas y niños menores de cinco años, mujeres embarazadas y en período de lactancia, mediante la mejora de la vigilancia y el tratamiento nutricional, fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal institucional de salud por medio de formaciones sobre el uso de los protocolos nacionales simplificados de manejo de la desnutrición aguda (utilización de cintas MUAC y estándares de crecimiento, específicamente peso para la talla); así mismo, propone la sensibilización a familias sobre prácticas adecuadas de alimentación, nutrición e higiene infantil, en los espacios de intervención  se promueven prácticas de alimentación y cuidado infantil e higiene para la mejora de prácticas de cuidado del niño y niña pequeños. También se propone brindar soporte con alimento complementario a niños y niñas menores de 5 años, mujeres embarazadas y/o en período de lactancia que se encuentren en riesgo de padecer desnutrición, para mejorar su estado nutricional.
Estas intervenciones se planifican llevar a cabo en tres municipios: Danlí, El Paraíso, Trojes

project_name: Addressing Food Insecurity Crisis through an integrated approach to Food Security, Health/Nutrition, and WASH in the South-West region of Cameroon
project_objective:
This project is titled: Addressing Cameroon’s Food Insecurity Crisis through an integrated approach to Food Security, Health, Nutrition, and WASH in the South-West region of Cameroon. It will be implemented by a Red Cross with the support of the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC). The estimated budget is 1,00,000 US dollars for a period of 12 months starting from January 2024 to December 2024. This project will be implemented in the Southwest Region specifically in the Fako division.  The project is targeting 10,000 direct beneficiaries and 100,000 indirect beneficiaries. Benefits will be in the areas of Food Security, Health, Nutrition and WASH in all regions. The aim of this initiative is to contribute to addressing food insecurity, health and WASH challenges for internally displaced populations and vulnerable hosts of the Northwest and the Southwest Regions. This project meets the SDG 1 and SDG 2, to eradicate poverty and to end hunger, through the provision of direct livelihoods support to beneficiaries and care for malnourished children under 5. It also promotes SDG 3 to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for the beneficiaries through quality health care for populations affected by displacement (IDPs, refugees and hosts) in the supported area. The project also meets the SDG 5- Gender equality through livelihood support to women making the financially sustainable and the SDG 6 – Clean water and sanitation through WASH training and the construction of boreholes. 


Background: 
Cameroon is facing a complex and unprecedented humanitarian crisis. Over 4.4 million people need humanitarian support and the food security situation in Cameroon is becoming more serious with more than 2.6 million people needing urgent food security interventions. The country has been heavily affected by three complex crises for several years now: the armed conflict between the Non-State Armed Groups (NAG) and the Regular Army that has intensified in the North West and South West regions (NOSO); the NAG insurgency in the Lake Chad Basin causing an influx of refugees from Nigeria, internal displacement in the Far North region, and the influx of Central African Republic (CAR) refugees in the Adamawa and North regions. OCHA estimates that in 2022, 3.9 million people needed humanitarian assistance. Of these people, 2.4 million were estimated to be severely food insecure over the period from June to August 2022 . Between 2020 and 2021, pre-existing vulnerabilities were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. OCHA, in January 2019, declared 440,000 people as internally displaced with 220,000 in the North-West and 200,000 in the South-West region and the number keeps increasing as the crisis continues to go unresolved.



Project Goal/Main Objective:  
This project aims at supporting the Cameroon Red Cross Society (CRC) in responding to the climate and conflict-induced food insecurity crisis by saving lives, protecting livelihoods, and promoting early recovery of the most food-insecure people.

Specific Objectives: 
1.	To contribute to achieving food security as a response to climate and conflict induced food insecurity.
2.	To improve health, Nutrition and WASH services to the displaced population

Target 

This project has as target area is the Fako division Southwest region of Cameroon where we have carried out a number of activities recently and have already trained volunteers and a regional office. It targets 1000 persons for CASH activities, 1000 for farm livelihoods support, 2000 consultation outpatient consultations and 5000 women for nutrition activities. This project also plans to reach 10,000 people with WASH and construct 20 boreholes.

project_name: Fostering enhanced protection amongst conflict-affected communities in the North-West Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The persistence of the ongoing conflict in the North West and South west regions of Cameroon over the years, has continuously deteriorated the security context and protection environment in these regions. The most recurrent protection incidents are property destruction, killings, physical assaults, unlawful arrests and detention, abductions, forced recruitment, and Gender-based Violence (GBV). This breakdown in the socio-economic tissue has created gaps in the mitigation/prevention of GBV cases, families have fled their habitual residents leading to an increase in displaced persons and separated families. An increase in the number of persons without civil documentation either through lose/destruction or inaccessibility to institutions responsible for the establishment of these documents, especially young children (boys and girls). This has led to an increase in unlawful arrest and detention. Due to the destruction of property/livelihood and the persistent lockdowns, families have lost their sources of income and they are unable to afford their basic necessities especially for young children and survivors of GBV (Hygiene and MHM kits). 
This Project is aimed at improving and strengthening the protective environment and support services for children and adolescents (girls and boys) in crisis-affected communities of the North-West (NW) Region of Cameroon. Children and adolescents especially girls will have increased knowledge, skills, wellbeing, positive coping strategies, and psychosocial support through the establishment of Child Friendly Spaces (CFS), strengthening of community-based systems and provision of specialized services to at-risk children and adolescents- including survivors of Sexual Gender-Base. The project will target 25 communities- including hard to reach areas, targeting a total of 2,582 people (1,571 females, 1011 males) direct beneficiaries.

project_name: Strengthening Local Resilience Through Inclusive Livelihoods and Food Security Support for Conflict-Affected Communities in Northwest Syria
project_objective:
FSA 2024 Syria HNO indicates worsening food security, impacting 15.5 million people (65% of the population), based on a country-wide assessment of 42,000 HHs. This marks an increase from the previous year, with 12.9 million needing food assistance & 2.6 million at risk. Concentrated in areas like Idleb (73%), Al-Hasakeh (74%), Quneitra (65%), Hama (59%), Ar-Raqqa (59%), Aleppo (58%), & Deir-ez-Zor (50%), food insecurity is exacerbated by displacement, especially in NWS & NES hubs, with 73.4% of IDPs affected. Recurring disease outbreaks, drought, & economic instability escalate mortality, morbidity, & humanitarian needs. Economic challenges, including currency depreciation, spur displacements. Agricultural constraints, such as climate change & limited inputs, strain vulnerable farmers. In response, IRC's 2024 ERD strategy enhances livelihood opportunities, climate-smart agriculture, & market systems reinforcement. IRC aligns interventions with ERL & FSL objectives. In ERL, IRC enhances and increases access to LVDs & job opportunities in NWS. In FSL, support self-reliance, & enhance resilience through irrigation rehabilitation, food processing & women's agribusiness. Interventions target financially vulnerable beneficiaries to reduce negative coping strategies. Livelihood projects offer vocational training & start-up support, prioritizing economically vulnerable groups. IRC focuses on climate-smart interventions for food security & income generation. Training in climate-smart agriculture is provided, followed by support for input & irrigation systems. CFW initiatives create temporary employment & promote economic inclusion. Agribusiness support empowers women, promoting gender equality, climate adaptation, & agricultural resilience. Gender-specific needs are addressed, SADD information is collected. Community tension due to perceived inequality & discrimination poses risks for staff. Mitigation includes establishing area-based coordination groups, ongoing engagement with community leaders, & communication. Selection criteria based on vulnerabilities & collaboration with protection service providers ensure targeted assistance. Continuous M&E with feedback mechanisms, clear complaint channels, community participation, & staff  training on PSEA are crucial. The medium likelihood & high impact of beneficiary safety risks & exploitation are mitigated through collaborative planning, coordination, & adjusting project plans. Integrating protection priorities, staff adherence to IRC policies, conflict sensitivity, & risk assessment tools ensure safety & accessibility. GBV mitigation measures aligned with international guidelines reduce risks in project locations.
FSL & livelihoods team, supported by the protection team, will promote "Do No Harm" principles & PSEA. Working with community leaders, representatives, & elders, IRC raises stakeholder awareness about rights & responsibilities. Clients are informed of entitlements & support procedures. Stakeholders & staff are sensitized to uphold humanitarian principles. Confidential reporting mechanisms are available to staff & clients, encouraging use of IRC's feedback system. IRC will integrate program activities with the protection sector to assist survivors & ensure referral pathways during beneficiary selection, data sharing, & follow-up. IRC ensures marginalized groups review selection criteria, conducts FGDs, & engages authorities to clarify services & expectations. Pre-project security assessments address conflict risks, & clear FARM mitigate impartiality risks. Protection Risk Analysis identifies tension in the community due to perceived inequality, addressed through robust selection criteria mechanisms & ongoing engagement with community leaders. Medium likelihood risks, like physical safety of clients, taxation, & exploitation/abuse, are mitigated through collaborative implementation plans, amendments to project plans, & awareness of FARM among clients.

project_name: Assistance d'urgence en santé et action humanitaire inclusive pour les populations vulnérables touchées par la crise du Soudan, à l’'Est du Tchad
project_objective:
Suivant la grave crise sécuritaire touchant le Soudan et ayant conduit à des déplacements massifs à l’Est du Tchad, HI met en œuvre pendant 7 mois, un ensemble de services dans la province du Ouaddai, visant à améliorer au plus vite les conditions de santé de 6905 hommes, femmes, filles et garçons, y compris les personnes blessées, impactées par le conflit. Grâce à la capacité de déploiement de son pôle urgence, HI se positionne en tant qu'acteur clé de la réponse à l’Est depuis mai 2023, afin de contribuer à sauver des vies en améliorant l'accès à des services essentiels et inclusifs de qualité pour les personnes vulnérables touchées par la crise, y compris dans les zones les plus isolées, et assurer une meilleure prise en compte des personnes handicapées dans la réponse. Ainsi, son action se décline autour de 2 piliers :
 (i) la mise en place des services de réadaptation et santé mental à travers 2 résultats
• la formation et information des acteurs de l’aide sur l’identification des personnes ayant besoin de réadaptation et sur les notions de premiers secours pyschologiques. 
• l’amélioration de l’indépendance fonctionnelle et capacité de résilience grâce aux services de réadaptation physique et soutien psychosocial des femmes, hommes, filles et garçons touchés par la crise du soudan qui ont un besoin immédiat de réadaptation et secours psychologique (en plus des personnes blessées et/ou handicapées).
(ii) le renforcement des capacités des acteurs de l’aide sur l’action humanitaire inclusive à travers 1 résultat visant l’amélioration de la prise en compte des personnes handicapées et leur accès aux services de base.

project_name: Assistance alimentaire et nutritionnelle d'urgence envers les populations les plus vulnérables en insécurité alimentaire sévère pendant la période de soudure
project_objective:
Le Tchad est un pays d'Afrique subsaharien enclavé à faible revenu, classé parmi les pays les plus pauvres par les Nations unies. L’agriculture et l’élevage constituent les moyens d’existence de la grande partie de la population essentiellement rurale. La majeure partie de son territoire est située dans la ceinture sahélienne, le Tchad est sujet à des chocs climatiques saisonniers qui entraînent des crises alimentaires régulières affectant la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations. 

L’évaluation de la campagne pastorale par les directions techniques du ministère de l’élevage et des productions animales indique une situation préoccupante caractérisée par une production de biomasse inférieure à celle de l'année dernière et à la médiane des cinq dernières années à la même période et un épuisement précoce des eaux d’abreuvement dans les zones pastorales. Cela entrainé une descente précoce des transhumants. Dix provinces de la zone sahélienne sur 15 ont enregistré des déficits fourragers. Les déficits les plus marqués sont enregistrés dans la province du Lac (93%), Hadjer Lamis (80%), Tibesti (79%), le Batha et Ouaddaï (72%), Kanem (58%) et Wadi Fira (56%).

L’analyse de la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle au Tchad selon le Cadre harmonisé de novembre 2023 fait ressortir pour la phase projetée que 29 départements sont déclarés en Phase 3 et plus avec 2 878 501 personnes en insécurité alimentaire. 
Les interventions prévues pour le projet d’assistance saisonnière seront concentrées dans la bande sahélienne et les zones de l’Est et du Sud. L’identification des zones ciblées par le PAM sera effectuée conjointement avec le SISAAP, l’ONASA, le Cluster Sécurité Alimentaire et les acteurs humanitaires afin d’éviter la duplication des efforts. 

Le PAM planifie appuyer 1,000,000 personnes avec une assistance alimentaire inconditionnelle pour trois mois (juin à aout) avec rations complètes. Cette assistance alimentaire sera combinée à une assistance nutritionnelle afin d’assister 75,000 enfants de 6 à 23 mois ainsi que 50,000 femmes enceintes.

project_name: Aide durable aux populations déplacées dans la province des lacs
project_objective:
Depuis le début de l'année 2018, l'OIM Tchad a observé des flux migratoires réguliers et croissants motivés par des raisons économiques à travers le nord du Tchad qui borde la Libye, probablement en raison des opportunités économiques limitées, de la crise de la sécurité alimentaire en cours et des mesures d'austérité imposées. Afin de continuer à fournir des informations cruciales sur les dimensions du déplacement et de la migration, l'intervention de l'OIM se concentrera sur les solutions durables en matière d'abris et de lavage et mettra l'accent sur l'engagement des communautés dans ces interventions sur certains sites. En outre, l'OIM se concentrera également sur la collecte de données par le biais : i) du suivi de la mobilité et de l'indice de stabilité ; ii) du suivi des situations d'urgence ; iii) du suivi des flux.
Ces interventions soutiendront l'objectif à long terme d'une solution durable dans la province du lac.

project_name: Projet d'éducation intégré et de renforcement de la résilience dans la province du Lac auprès des déplacés et des populations vulnérables
project_objective: Acted propose un projet d’éducation intégrée, dans le département du Fouli sur une période de 24 mois. Les populations du Lac font face à des crises récurrentes liées notamment à l’activité des GANE et aux chocs climatiques qui impactent leurs moyens d’existence. Les populations déplacées en situation de crise, perdent leur accès à l’éducation, renforçant leur vulnérabilité et le risque croissant de radicalisation ou d’embrigadement dans les groupes armés de la région. ACTED soutiendra les communautés via un appui en infrastructures EHA, un renforcement de l’accès à l’éducation ainsi que des activités de protection (mis en place par un partenaire local APSELPA) et de résilience (mise en place par le partenaire local SOS Sahel Tchad).

project_name: Projet multisectoriel pour les populations vulnérables du Fouli, Tchad
project_objective: Acted prévoit à participer à la couverture des besoins humanitaires des populations déplacées et vulnérables dans la province du Lac, dans le département du Fouli, sur une période de 18 mois auprès des populations déplacées et populations hôtes. Les populations déplacées en situation de crise, perdent leur accès aux services de base, renforçant leur vulnérabilité et le risque croissant d’embrigadement dans les groupes armés de la région. Acted prévoit d’assurer une réponse multisectorielle via un appui en infrastructures EHA, un renforcement de l’accès à l’éducation, les moyens d’existence de communautés hôtes et déplacés, renforcer la protection de l’enfance dans les écoles et sensibiliser les communautés sur la protection transversale.

project_name: Provision of a comprehensive WASH and protection package to Refugees and asylum seekers in Gadaref and East Darfur
project_objective: This WASH and protection intervention by CARE international is designed to deliver a comprehensive WASH and protection package to refugees and asylum seekers in Gadaref  and East Darfur refugee camps. The overall objective of this project is “Decreased WASH related morbidity and mortality and protection risks through provision of improved and sustained access to water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, and protection services for Ethiopian and south Sudanese Refugees in Gadaref and East Darfur camps and surrounding host communities”. This objective is developed in line with the revised humanitarian response plan of 2024, cluster priorities and strategies in supporting resilience and self-reliance through rehabilitation of facilities, operation and maintenance and capacity building of communities. The total number of individuals targeted by this project is 100,000 Refugees and asylum seekers settled the targeted location and host community members settled around the target refugee camps. The total target doesn't include duplication in targeting beneficiaries in WASH and protection. However, the number of targeted beneficiaries will not exceed 100,000 per sector. The project implementation will focus on gender equity and equality in all activities including hygiene sessions, training, and latrines rehabilitation and beneficiaries’ selection. The project will be focus on women and children as most vulnerable community members particularly in terms of mother and child health.  Women will be consulted by the project team to identify their priorities and be part of decision making within their communities to encourage more equitable solutions. CARE will integrate an inclusive approach, with a strong focus on gender and social habits of the beneficiaries, on addressing the needs of people with disabilities and mitigating against GBV risks.

project_name: Multi-Sectoral Response in Khartoum, West Darfur, White Nile and Blue Nile
project_objective:
Medair aims to deliver multi-sectoral lifesaving basic services in health, nutrition, basic Mental Health and Pychosocial Support Service (MHPSS), and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH), emergency shelter & non-food items (ES/NFIs) along with strengthening local preparedness and response capacities in delivering humanitarian aid, responding to crisis and strengthening resilience.  

In Blue Nile, with underlying conflict for decades, has seen an estimated influx of 118.093 IDPs in the State since April. Medair conducted a mass MUAC screening in target catchment areas in October 2023, with 10.828 CU5 and 2.896 PLW screened. 3,7% of CU5 were identified as having severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and 11,1% with moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) and 14,7% of PLW had a MUAC < 210mm. Sexual and gender/based violence (SGBV) is sensitive to address, and is further complicated by continuous displacement. Suspected measles and chilera cases were also reported in Blue Nile. 

In White Nile, current data estimates 303 active gathering points (GPs) providing refuge to 43,493 IDPs. In Tendalti there are 20 GPs with 230 households and 1000 IDPs integrated in host community. Average clinic utilization rate is 0.4 in assessed areas along with cholera outbreak and poor response measures to contain it.

In West Darfur, approximately, 123,835 IDPs have so far sought refuge. Kereneik locality, identified at severity level 4 (HNO Sudan 2024) and predicted to be at IPC level 4 (IPC Oct 2023 to Feb 2024), has been hardest hit by the most recent fighting. 5 out of the 6 HFs visited have been looted and are temporarily closed for services (Dawr Shari, Ramaliya, Hajr Tama, Mandi and Konjoltori) and 1 has been destroyed (Um Ashwush). Main mortalities of CU5 were reportedly malaria, diarrhoea, and malnutrition. Screening for malnutrition amongst PLW is only available at 20% of the HFs assessed and unavailable for CU5 in any of the HFs. OTP was available at 3 HFs prior to the crisis, but TSFP only available at 1 HF. Together with non-functional HFs, the influx of IDPs have increased the burden of the health services. 

Therefore, this project addresses critical needs in hard-to-reach areas of Khartoum, West Darfur, White Nile, and Blue Nile.In West Darfur, White Nile, Blue Nile, through supporting Primary Health Care Centres/Units and mobilising the Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs), Medair will deliver integrated health and nutrition programming which includes the provision of Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) for children aged under five (CU5); reproductive health (RH) services (antenatal and post-natal care, family planning, safe delivery and sex and gender based violence (SGBV) management); support of outbreak responses; Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) and IYCF; integrated community support through Mother-to-Mother Support Groups (MtMSGs); and MHPSS programming. Basic WASH packages will be provided at supported health facilities to reduce the risk of the spread of communicable diseases. Medair will also conduct distributions of cash assistance and/or non-food items (NFIs) to cover the basic shelter and household needs of the affected populations. Medair has established Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with IOM and so core pipelines will be mobilised to save cost and increase efficiency. 

And in Khartoum, Medair will support primary health services with supporting operational costs through local partners. This will include essential child and maternity health services. 

Protection will be mainstreamed across all activities to ensure safe and equitable access, beneficiary participation, empowerment, and dignity. 

By targeting the most vulnerable (esp. PLW, CU5, the elderly, people living with disabilities), this project will help reduce excess morbidity and mortality and decrease the risk of communicable illnesses among the affected populations.

project_name: Conducting Registration and Verification Exercises for Affected Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
In response to the need for accurate information on displacement and the identification of beneficiaries for the delivery of humanitarian aid, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) began its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) program in 2004. The program aimed to support the Government of Sudan (GoS) and its humanitarian partners in establishing an accurate data collection system and providing data on displacement in areas most affected by conflict and natural disasters. The military conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that began on 15 April 2023, has led to the destruction of key infrastructure in affected areas, significant displacement and increase in morbidity and mortality, and interruption of humanitarian activities across Sudan. Despite the limitations to DTM's logistical operations due to the access and security challenges in conflict-affected states such as Khartoum and Aj Jazirah, and Darfur and Kordofan regions, DTM has been able to maintain key data collection operations and has provided humanitarians with preliminary estimates of displacement and return. Amidst a rapidly changing context, registration requests from humanitarian partners have reduced significantly over the last 5 years due to the emergence of different types of data requests from inter-agency groups and Clusters and a change in the methodology used in Sudan. In response to requests and the current security context, DTM appropriately expanded its Mobility Tracking data collection since 2023 to focus on remote and in-person key informant interviews to provide evidence-based information about the humanitarian context which other organizations rely on for their programming and anticipating beneficiaries' needs. However, DTM Sudan will still continue to routinely assess and anticipate partners' needs for humanitarian information. Should the context, beneficiaries, and humanitarian partners benefit from the information derived from registration activities, DTM Sudan will rapidly deploy registration teams to gather information for inter-agency coordination on future humanitarian interventions and support DTM's partners to identify hotspots of vulnerability and support precise targeting of assistance.
IOM has been working in close collaboration with partners in the field to establish a unified and systematic method to collect individual data on internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees. Registration data is captured by DTM field teams through direct individual interviews in the target locations, usually with the heads of households. All enumerators are trained on conducting interviews, engaging with female headed households, as well as safe and ethical referrals. Additionally, throughout all activities, DTM teams secure gender-responsive data collection by establishing gender mixed field teams, collecting sex and age disaggregated data, and capturing other demographic information (wealth status, ethnicity, vulnerability etc.). When collected, registration data is shared with partners by means of data sharing agreements, in line with data protection principles, and is used for beneficiary selection, vulnerability targeting, and programming.

project_name: Displacement Tracking Matrix: Mobility Tracking of IDPs, Returnees, and Other Mobile Populations in Sudan
project_objective:
Following the multiple crises that affected Sudan since February 2003, and in response to the need for accurate information on displacement and the identification of beneficiaries for the delivery of humanitarian aid, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) began its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) program in 2004 to support the Government of Sudan (GoS) and its humanitarian partners in establishing an accurate data collection system and providing data on displacement in the areas most affected by the conflict and natural disasters. DTM is a system to track and monitor displacement and population mobility. It is designed to regularly and systematically capture, process and disseminate information to provide a better understanding of the movements and evolving needs of displaced populations, whether on site or en route. Data collection strategies and tools are based on DTM global methodology but have been adapted to reflect the context and population movements specific to Sudan. Since the start of the current conflict that erupted in April 2023, between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), there has been an increase in the destruction of key infrastructure in affected areas, significant displacements and increase in morbidity and mortality, and disruption of humanitarian activities across Sudan. Despite the notable limitations to DTM's logistical operations and the connectivity and telecommunication challenges, DTM has been able to maintain key data collection operations, releasing information products in as little as 24 hours after the start of the initial clashes on 15 April 2023.  DTM is operational in 180 of Sudan’s 189 localities across all 18 states (90% of the country) and will continue to provide detailed updates on displacement in Sudan which currently has the largest displacement caseload in the world.
The methodology and modalities for the data collection in 2024 will be flexible to the needs of the context but can include: (1) Mobility Tracking data collection exercise to gather vulnerable population's data baselines; (2) Early Warning Flash Alerts to update the humanitarian community of recent or potential incidents of displacement; (3) Emergency Event Tracking to provide the humanitarian community with datasets relating to sudden incidents of displacement; (4) Weekly Displacement Snapshots to update the humanitarian community with timely information on displacement context post 15 April 2023; (5) Monthly Displacement Overviews to provide the humanitarian community with comprehensive indicators on displaced caseloads. (6) Situation Assessments to provide information on displaced caseloads in non-emergency context, where possible. (7) Integrated Location Assessment to provide the humanitarian community with information on access to services at major sites of displacement. (8) Return Index to be provide critical information on living conditions in IDP locations which support returns of displaced communities, where feasible. DTM will also continue to provide the humanitarian community with routine information on rapid incidents that affect displacement, population mobility, shelter typology, return intentions, and priority needs as well as population baseline estimates and bespoke information products. Given the pressing emergency context, DTM is best placed to provide essential and evidence-based information and forms a core component of IOM’s ongoing response to the unfolding humanitarian crisis.

project_name: Managing a Common Pipeline System for Humanitarian Assistance in Sudan.
project_objective: Under this project, IOM will manage and maintain a common humanitarian pipeline system in order to improve localization, coverage, effectiveness, and efficiency of distribution of relief items in hard-to-reach areas. IOM has established the online portal where partners will continue to access material, technical, logistic, and operational support for the distribution of relief items. The database for the active partners will be available to relevant stakeholders including cluster leads, working groups, and donors for further information, coordination, and funding purposes. In addition, IOM will continue to work in coordination with the government and the clusters in prepositioning, maintaining and managing the common pipeline. IOM plans to supply partners with the following items through the pipeline: (1) 60,000 non-food items (NFI) kits to reach approximately 300,000 individuals; (2) 20,000 emergency shelter kits (ESKs) to reach approximately 100,000 individuals, and (3) 120,000 family hygiene kits (FHKs) to reach approximately 720,000 individuals; as well as logistics and operational support. The support provided through the pipeline will act as a preparedness and response measure for addressing the needs of newly displaced and protracted populations as well as other and vulnerable people with special needs in different states. The distributions will be conducted in close coordination with the cluster leads, partners, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure consistency in provision of assistance and to reduce possible duplication of assistance. This will strengthen the role of local partners in delivering timely and effective emergency response to the affected populations through the system, fostering transparency, accountability, and integrity, and more generally building the promoting the capacity and promoting the role of local partners in responding to humanitarian crises.

project_name: Displacement affected people have access to coordinated and responsive assistance and protection through inclusive community participation and empowerment towards durable solutions.
project_objective:
The project aims to facilitate access to coordinated and responsive services to displacement affected communities, where the IDPs will be inclusively participating in the processes of multi-sectoral assistance. The project will target IDPs living in sites and site like settings in the east, central and western parts of Sudan. 
The project will establish, or actively contribute to site-level coordination mechanisms to support humanitarian response, with strong emphasis on using this forum to raise joint advocacy on protection risk and concerns of the community, reduce duplication of services and improve access to services for displaced community. Site-level coordination will also ensure mainstreaming of protection and strengthening of site management committees to enhance participation, empowerment and accountability to the affected population.   
Improvement of the site environments is an important aspect of this project which will increase the quality of living conditions for site residents and ensure that basic standards are met. Site improvement works will focus on preparedness activities such as digging of drainage systems, sandbag filling, risk mapping, building or reinforcement of communal infrastructures, and support to site safety committees. Site improvement works will be identified and prioritized in consultation with site management committees and community leaders through safety audits, complaint and feedback mechanisms and observations. The project will also focus on mainstreaming protection in care and maintenance activities, ensuring that the site have proper lighting, fencing and demarcation when required. 
NRC will build the capacity of key stakeholders such as community leaders and community volunteers on leadership, self-management, service monitoring, PSEA, humanitarian principles, community participation with emphasis on inclusion of women and other vulnerable groups, information sharing in addition to other identified needs by these stakeholders. 
The project teams will engage and facilitate community volunteers to communicate regularly with communities in the target locations. This will include regular information and awareness sessions about specific topics using IEC materials when required. It will also focus on establishing an information and feedback mechanism to improve communication with the communities, ensuring that IDPs have access to information about services and are able to provide and receive feedback. The project will strengthen safety and site maintenance committees within the IDP sites, which will be trained and supported to conduct regular safety mappings of the sites and preparedness exercises. These committees would be equipped with essential tools and would be deployed to respond to emergencies and hazards, such as fire outbreaks, floods and large influxes in IDP sites.
