project_name: Syrian Children Have Open Opportunities for Learning (SCHOOL)
project_objective:
The project aims to enhance access to safe and fair education for crisis-affected children and youth aged 5-17 while improving its quality within protective settings. Implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and related departments, it prioritizes beneficiary protection with a 'do no harm' approach. ADRA Syria will facilitate access to education for 24471 affected children and teachers, fostering safe learning environments in governorates including Rural Damascus, Homs, Aleppo, Lattakia, and Deir Alzour. Through a holistic approach encompassing psycho-social, familial, and educational support, the project aims to elevate formal and non-formal education for both genders, engaging parents in educational activities. ADRA will collaborate with stakeholders to identify vulnerable children and conduct thorough needs assessments to address out-of-school children and those with priority educational requirements.
Need assessment 
The ongoing crisis in Syria, exacerbated by the earthquake aftermath, continues to detrimentally affect the education system. There's been a 4% rise in People in Need (PiN) compared to the previous year, indicating an urgent requirement for emergency education services to assist approximately 7.1 million school-aged children and teachers, including those with disabilities. PiN includes 6.9 million children aged 5-17 (46% girls, 54% boys) and 230 education personnel (48% female, 52% male), with 10% being children with disabilities, underscoring the necessity for specialized education services. Over 2.45 million Out of School Children (OOSC) (46% girls, 54% boys) exist, with over a million at risk of dropping out, particularly prevalent in governorates like, Rural Damascus (40%), and Aleppo (38%). OOSC face various gendered protection risks, and prolonged absence from school reduces their likelihood of returning. Pre-existing inadequacies in the education infrastructure persist, with around 3,700 schools needing rehabilitation (HNO 2024)
Additionally, inadequate or non-functional WASH facilities pose risks, particularly for girls and Persons with Disabilities (PwD), often resulting in dropouts and absences, hampering education progress. Secondly, the shortage of qualified teachers further hampers quality learning. Thirdly, economic difficulties strain parents, who may struggle to afford school supplies or transportation, leading children to work to support their families (ADRA assessment 2023)
Activities:
The project activities will include rehabilitation damaged classrooms and schools, ensuring equal access for all students, including those with disabilities, through gender-segregated WASH facilities and improved accessibility features. It involves repairing doors, windows, and painting, installing western-style toilets for mobility-impaired individuals, and introducing solar power systems. Additionally, it provides non-formal education programs such as remedial and summer classes for at-risk children, including those out of school. PSS counsellors will be appointed to assist OOSC in adapting to the educational setting and remedial class students to address any challenges in obtaining their educational potential. A Back to Learning campaign targets dropout students to re-enter either formal schooling or non-formal education programs.  School supplies, including bags and stationery, will be distributed to children. Professional development opportunities for teaching staff, focusing on active learning and psychological support, will be available. ADRA Syria, with extensive experience in teacher capacity building, has conducted numerous training sessions benefiting thousands of teachers over the past five years To ensure sustained impact and local ownership of the Education intervention, ADRA will collaborate with parents and teachers to establish Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) where there is community willingness. This initiative is vital for enhancing local capacity and ownership

project_name: Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance for Extremely Vulnerable Households in Aleppo, Hama, Daraa, Deir-ez-Zor, and Rural Damascus
project_objective:
To enable extremely vulnerable households to meet their basic needs based on their own priorities and to mitigate or reduce reliance on harmful coping strategies, DRC will provide unrestricted and unconditional MPCA to extremely vulnerable households in Aleppo, Daraa, Rural Damascus, and Deir-ez-Zor. DRC will leverage different channels to identify potential MPCA recipient households and adopt a multi-step verification process to ensure independent and needs-based targeting. To mitigate risks of exclusion, DRC will collect self-referrals through community outreach and its CFM hotline, while informing the CWG of the planned response and geographical coverage to facilitate inter-agency referrals. With a strengthened focus on integrated response to enhance the effectiveness and impact of sectoral interventions, DRC will prioritize internal referrals of households targeted under other Sectors in close coordination with Shelter, WASH, Protection, and Economic Recovery teams. At the beneficiary registration stage, DRC will carry out a gender-age and protection risk analysis to identify potential risks associated with a cash modality, including intra-household and community power dynamics and safety and accessibility considerations. On a monthly basis, DRC will also conduct joint market monitoring across the target locations to assess market functionality, ensure programming is not causing market distortions due to the sudden influx of cash, and to verify that both the TV and continued use of cash as a response modality remains appropriate.

DRC will utilize the currently agreed MPCA TV with a recommended buffer of 20%, which amounts to a monthly TV to 1.716.000 SYP. Each household will receive MPCA for a period of 6 months, and DRC will also provide transportation costs (50.000 SYP) for each cash cycle to cover beneficiaries’ expenses of travelling to and from the distribution points to remove barriers in accessing assistance and to ensure the MPCA package can be exclusively used to cover basic needs. Given the severity and scale of needs among target households, MPCA will be provided for a period of 6-months via successive distributions, in line with monthly consumption patterns and expenditure cycles, to ensure a minimum period of time to strengthen and stabilize household consumption. However, the number of instalments will remain flexible and adaptable to evolving needs and circumstances of beneficiaries and the broader context, such as new shocks, severe inflation, or displacement. In accordance with sanctions, DRC utilizes a pre-contracted local financial service provider (FSP) for the delivery of cash to beneficiaries, with three-way counting of the cash by DRC, the FSP, and the beneficiary. DRC also has experience negotiating for the opening of temporary branches in close proximity to beneficiaries’ residence (within walking distance) as needed. Continuous, real-time risk assessment and mitigation measures will underpin all distributions, especially mindful of the heightened vulnerability of individuals selected for MPCA. If the protection risk analysis alerts DRC to encashment-related risks, prior to confirming the distribution plan, DRC will verify with beneficiaries that they are able to safely access the distribution point. To the greatest extent possible, MPCA will be sequenced with complementary livelihoods programming that moves towards the longer-term objectives of resilience and self-reliance, and thus provides exit opportunities for humanitarian assistance. 

Note: This project is anticipated to be covered through multi-donor funding, rather than a single, standalone project. (see more information on mitigation and criteria in Extended Summary).

project_name: Saving lives, creating safer communities, facilitating stabilisation & redevelopment efforts in Ar-Raqqa and Deir-er-Zor (DEZ).
project_objective: The intervention aims to 1) Saves lives: Provide lifesaving and life-sustaining EORE through Community Focal Points (CFPs), in areas with a high severity of needs, to women, girls, boys and men, and by safely removing explosive hazards from contaminated communities. 2) Enhance protection: Enhance the prevention and mitigation of protection risks and respond to protection needs through DCA’s systems for internal referrals through CL activity (namely to psychosocial support and Cash for Food) as well as external referrals (for victim assistance, namely prosthetics and assistive device provision). 3) Increase resilience and access to services: By clearing EO from buildings, agricultural land, and key infrastructure, increase the resilience of affected communities by improving access to livelihood opportunities and basic services, especially among the most vulnerable households and communities in areas with a high severity of needs.

project_name: Supporting Vulnerable Populations in Homs to Meet their Basic Needs
project_objective:
The objective of this project is to support vulnerable populations in Homs to meet a variety of basic needs and reduce reliance on negative coping strategies. This will be done through the provision of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to the most vulnerable households for a period of 6 months. Mission East (ME) will adhere to the transfer value and guidance recommended by the Cash Working Group. ME is present at the working group meetings to ensure proper coordination, collaboration, and adherence to recommended guidelines and practices. 2,250 individuals (450 households) will benefit from MPCA through this intervention.

In terms of location, this project will build upon ME’s existing ongoing programming in Homs with LAMSA that works with inclusive and integrated approaches to support sustainable early recovery and to rebuild longer-term resilience. ME has identified the district of Homs to be the target location for this intervention. This area is also targeted by the Cash Working Group, as 43,428 individuals have been highlighted as in need within the district of Homs.

ME and its partner will initially identify vulnerable households through both internal and external referrals. Once a referral is received, an assessment will be done with the household that considers factors such as number of household members, whether a household has a disabled member(s), whether the household is headed by a female or child, as well as other factors. The results of the assessments will guide ME and LAMSA in the selection of the most vulnerable households.

The cash modality is increasingly being used globally due to its numerous advantages such as giving beneficiaries the dignity of choice, as well as economic benefits such as the multiplier effect. In the contexts of Syria, where prices for basic commodities have soared and the currency is continuing to lose value, while at the same time salaries have remained stagnant, unconditional cash assistance is an effective modality that ensures beneficiaries can meet their basic needs and thus decrease engaging in negative coping mechanisms. The disbursement of cash will take place through financial service providers (FSPs). FSPs are commonly used throughout Syria, so targeted populations are familiar with the procedure. Nonetheless, ME, alongside with LAMSA will ensure that selected FSPs adhere to the code of conduct, as well as that beneficiaries are fully aware of their consumer rights vis-à-vis FSP field agents. The response is on best practices related to cash and voucher assistance, such as Sphere companion MISMA and Sphere’s “Delivering Assistance through Markets” and will build on ME’s ongoing CVA programming.

project_name: Contribute to the comprehensive Nutrition project to address under-nutrition among vulnerable populations living in Rohingya & Host communities in Cox's Bazar Bangladesh.
project_objective:
ACF will continue its efforts to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with acute malnutrition in children under 5, primarily by operating Stabilization Centers (SC) in Kutupalong and Balukhali Makeshift Camps. These SCs will provide critical care for severely malnourished children, infants with low birth weight, and those referred from other nutrition facilities. ACF will also work with Integrated Nutrition Facilities (INF) teams to improve timely referrals and follow-up care.
In addition to treating complicated SAM cases following the 10 essential steps, the Stabilization Centers also offer Supplementary Sucking Technique (SST), wet nursing, and relactation for infants under six months of age. This further enhances the centers' capability to address a wide range of nutritional challenges faced by this vulnerable population.
ACF will continue the support CMAM program implemented by the Ministry of Health (MoH) in Upazila health complex following inpatient management of SAM and in Community clinic level IYCF including MNP distribution 6-23 months children as per national guideline, hygiene promotion, and Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services including IFA distribution to Adolescents girl and Pregnant Women focusing women and adolescent girl including gender transformative approach to access quality health and nutrition services. Further more the project will continue to targeting GVB , PSEA sensitization, male engagement including active case identification and referral
Furthermore ACF will implement CMAM research through implementing partner icddr,b in  collaboration with IPHN and WFP. In addition, ACF has plan for contributing Coverage survey at Rhogingya Refugee /FDMN and Host community. The surveys will be discussed and agreed at the Nutrition sector level and with approval from the IPHN/NSS.

project_name: Fostering enhanced protection amongst conflict-affected communities in the North-West Region of Cameroon
project_objective:
The Project is aimed at improving and strengthening the protective environment and support services for children and adolescents (girls and boys) in crisis-affected communities of the North-West (NW) Region of Cameroon. Children and adolescents especially girls will have increased knowledge, skills, wellbeing, positive coping strategies, and psychosocial support through the establishment of Child Friendly Spaces (CFS), strengthening of community-based systems and provision of specialized services to at-risk children and adolescents- including survivors of Sexual Gender-Base
Violence (SGBV)- through Immediate support. The project will target 25 communities- including hard to reach areas, targeting a total of 2,582 people (1,571 females, 1011 males) direct beneficiaries.

project_name: Empoderamiento agrícola a familias indígenas campesinas de la comunidad de Pampatameru, Apoipo y Betania al sur del estado Bolívar en Gran sabana desarrollando actividades educativas y resilientes para el uso y consumo correcto del agua transversalizado en educación primaria mediante la entrega de alimentos a las familias beneficiarias.
project_objective: Ofrecer a las familias herramientas que permitan hacer un mejor uso de sus recursos para los diferentes cultivos en sus bien llamados conucos y tierra conjunta los cuales son la principal fuente de trabajo de las familias beneficiarias, Es imperante educar en el tratamiento y distintos métodos de purificación y potabilización de agua respetando su idiosincrasia y los medios por el cual el vital líquido llega a estas comunidades. La implementación de ciertas innovaciones de WASH (p. ej., cloradores solares, sistemas de recolección de agua de lluvia, etc.) no solo permitirán la adopción de prácticas seguras de agua, saneamiento e higiene, sino que también aumentara la resiliencia de la comunidad y ayudara a responder a los desafíos del cambio climático que viven estas comunidades tales como sequías, inundaciones, etc. En estas comunidades los problemas de salud y nutrición se ven exacerbados por el acceso insuficiente al agua potable y los sistemas de saneamiento inadecuados. La mala calidad y cantidad del agua, combinada con el acceso intermitente a agua segura, particularmente en estas áreas rurales y remotas, hacen que estas acciones a implementar sean extremadamente desafiantes. Sin embargo esto nos lleva a desarrollar distintas sesiones educativas de atención a la edad primaria paralelas a las mujeres jefas de hogar, estas mismas categorizadas en higiene, lavado de manos, el consumo, inocuidad e higiene de alimentos y el correcto desarrollo de estas acciones. Brindando una asistencia a través de dos componentes; 1 Distribución general de alimentos para las familias, mediante cursos de formación técnica y de capacitación en aptitudes para el fortalecimiento de sus medios de vida en el área agrícola impartidas por el equipo de ADRA y asistencia alimentaria condicionada a la participación de los beneficiarios en los cursos de formación. Este componente incluirá acciones específicas dirigidas a empoderar a las mujeres y los grupos más vulnerables, promoviendo su acceso a actividades generadoras de ingresos, Esto con la finalidad de medir el alcance de las actividades impartidas tanto en formaciones agrícolas como en sesiones de formación, teniendo como propósito fomentar los sistemas agrícolas sostenibles, equitativos y resilientes por medio de herramientas y estrategias educativas que le permitan a la población cultivar alimentos para complementar su alimentación diaria, de la misma manera apoyar y fortalecer la participación de las comunidades locales en la mejora de la gestión del agua y el saneamiento, buscando educar a la población meta que estima alcanzar a 1108 personas aproximadamente, es decir 277 familias de las comunidades mencionadas. La manera como se construye el género en las distintas sociedades indígenas está relacionado a la división y complementariedad en el trabajo. Para los pueblos indígenas, sólo a partir de la diferencia y la complementariedad puede darse una buena vida en comunidad y una buena relación de pareja.  Por ello, las relaciones entre hombres y mujeres se expresan en términos de horizontalidad y no de verticalidad. Las tareas de las mujeres son transformadoras: la horticultura, la preparación de alimentos, la alfarería, la cestería y crianza de niños.  Dada esta división y complementariedad dentro de las comunidades indígenas, es posible enumerar una serie de roles tradicionales femeninos trabajando en empoderarlos y reforzarlos, Estos son algunos de ellos: Empoderar a las pequeñas agricultoras, Orientar mediante estrategias educativas el trabajo de cuidados de niños y niñas, Apoyar el liderazgo  y Proteger la salud de las mujeres. Mencionando a las mujeres como cuidadoras principales del hogar el cual es un  trabajo y nos proponemos orientar en la importancia de la maternidad la cual se resalta como motor del proceso de participación y organización protagonizado por las mujeres indígenas Las situaciones de desigualdad de genero y discriminación que enfrentan la mayoría de ellas.

project_name: Mejorar la capacidad de adaptación a las consecuencias del cambio climático y reforzar la preparación ante las catástrofes naturales en Venezuela
project_objective:
El proyecto humanitario propuesto por ACTED/IMPACT, tiene como objetivo abordar los riesgos y vulnerabilidades relacionados con desastres naturales y el cambio climático en Venezuela. El proyecto surge como respuesta a la creciente frecuencia e intensidad de fenómenos meteorológicos extremos y la amenaza potencial de eventos climáticos como El Niño. Se reconoce la importancia de abordar la resiliencia comunitaria como elemento central en la programación humanitaria, considerando de manera integral las diversidades de género, edad y discapacidad. 
La metodología AGORA creado en 2016, adopta un enfoque basado en zonas para la planificación y ejecución de proyectos humanitarios y de desarrollo. Su lema, "Think local, Act global," refleja la importancia de la participación local y el empoderamiento de las comunidades. La metodología se basa en capacitar a actores locales, proporcionar tecnología e información, y utilizar el conocimiento local para planificar y ejecutar acciones que reduzcan la brecha entre ayuda humanitaria y desarrollo. 
Objetivos y Grupo Destinatario:
1.	Promover la toma de decisiones informada mediante la recopilación de datos locales sobre vulnerabilidades y capacidades, considerando las diferencias de género, edad y discapacidad.
2.	Movilizar comunidades marginadas, prestando especial atención a las necesidades específicas de mujeres, niños, niñas, personas mayores y personas con discapacidad, para priorizar acciones de Reducción del Riesgo de Desastres (RRD) y mitigar impactos.
3.	Capacitar a comunidades, asegurando que las estrategias de refuerzo de la resiliencia sean inclusivas y aborden las necesidades particulares de cada grupo, considerando género, edad y discapacidad.
4.	Mejorar el acceso y la calidad de la información sobre impactos climáticos, asegurando que sea accesible y comprensible para todos, independientemente de su género, edad o discapacidad.
5.	Suministrar teledetección y análisis a escala nacional, para desarrollar tendencias a largo plazo y capacidad predictiva inclusiva.
IMPACT llevará a cabo actividades para recopilar datos a nivel nacional, priorizando zonas vulnerables. Se beneficiarán directamente las comunidades locales y la comunidad humanitaria en general, garantizando una planificación basada en pruebas. La acción incluirá la colaboración con organismos de la ONU y la participación en el Protocolo Interagencial para la Preparación y Respuesta ante Emergencias.
El proyecto utilizará teledetección y datos satelitales para obtener una visión general de las tendencias climáticas y riesgos de desastres. Se realizarán evaluaciones trimestrales de riesgos por zonas en áreas identificadas como altamente vulnerables. Se emplearán datos de alta resolución, como el sensor Sentinel-2, para analizar cambios medioambientales a nivel administrativo. La recopilación de datos primarios respaldará el análisis de teledetección, permitiendo la identificación de zonas vulnerables.
ACTED desarrollará una sólida comprensión basada en la zona de las vulnerabilidades, así como de los riesgos externos y las tensiones que amenazan a las comunidades y sus medios de subsistencia; apoyará a las comunidades marginadas a identificar y aplicar soluciones de RRD reforzando la resiliencia de sus medios de subsistencia y fomentando al mismo tiempo sinergias sostenibles entre los agentes locales y el sistema de ayuda para ampliar y reproducir las soluciones identificadas localmente (la intervención incluirá la promoción de prácticas indígenas tradicionales). La metodología sitúa a la población y a los actores locales en el centro, proporcionándoles formación, tecnología e información, utilizando los territorios como base para la planificación y la prestación de asistencia y garantizando que la acción se guíe por los conocimientos locales y apoye las estructuras y capacidades locales.

project_name: Intervención humanitaria de WASH para reducir la desnutrición aguda en Chiquimula.
project_objective:
El proyecto se centra en brindar asistencia humanitaria para abordar las necesidades urgentes de WASH (Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene) en los municipios de Jocotán, Chiquimula, Camotán y San José La Arada del departamento de Chiquimula. Estos municipios se enfrentan a una grave situación de desnutrición aguda en donde la falta y deficiencia de servicios de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene son factores claves que contribuyen a la desnutrición de niños y niñas de la primera infancia. El proyecto atenderá a 62,443 personas pertenecientes a los grupos más vulnerables, incluyendo mujeres, niñas y niños. La información de base del HNO, INFORM (2022) y otras fuentes como la línea de base de la Gran Cruzada Nacional por la Nutrición, se utilizaron para evidenciar la severidad de la situación y tomar estas medidas de urgencia en esta área.  

World Vision y UNICEF enfocarán la respuesta de manera urgente en 4 municipios de Chiquimula en donde las intervenciones estarán enfocadas en: Rehabilitar sistemas de agua, implementar sistemas de tratamiento del agua a nivel comunitario y de hogar, desarrollar procesos de entrenamiento rápido para la práctica de hábitos higiénicos y sistemas de saneamiento para bloquear las rutas de contaminación feco-oral para contribuir en la reducción de casos de desnutrición aguda. 

Además, se rehabilitará los módulos de WASH en establecimientos de salud para facilitar la atención a la población afectada en la región de cobertura. Se coordinará y complementará esfuerzos y actividades a nivel departamental y municipal con diferentes instancias como la Coordinadora Nacional para la Reducción de Desastres (CONRED), Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MSPAS) y otras instancias representadas en Chiquimula y así fortalecer sus capacidades en la respuesta a emergencias.

project_name: Emergency WASH Interventions for Conflict-Affected Internally Displaced People in Cabo Delgado Province
project_objective:
To ensure the most vulnerable conflict-affected households (HHs) in Cabo Delgado can meet their basic household needs through access to adequate water, sanitation and hygiene facilities through the construction of key infrastructure.
People continue to be seriously affected by the ongoing conflict in northern Mozambique. The impact of armed conflict, violence and insecurity in the region, combined with successive climate shocks and disease outbreaks, have led to recurring waves of internal displacement in the province, in search of safety and basic means of survival. According to the International Organization for Migration's (IOM) DTM Mobility Tracking Assessment, the region has a total of 834,304 internally displaced people and 420,200 returnees in 221 locations. The majority of this group is made up of women and children, with 79% of current internally displaced people and 76% of returnees being women and children (under 18). Although many communities have decided to return to their place of origin, the situation remains very uncertain with security risks in many districts, making it difficult to implement long-term interventions in some areas. In this unstable scenario, families are unable to access the most basic services in several sectors and assistance does not reach several districts. Assessments conducted by CARE and partners revealed that WASH interventions are among the most urgent needs, as described below:
WASH: Access to water continues to be one of the biggest challenges in Cabo Delgado. An RNA in Macomia revealed that there are no water points in the internally displaced areas, forcing people to pay or travel long distances to access water. Schools also face a lack of water and adequate sanitation, creating barriers to school attendance, particularly for menstruating girls who often miss school during their cycle. Furthermore, the lack of a latrine was reported in all assessments consulted. Most households and settlement sites do not have latrines or the latrines are damaged and do not function.

Therefore, CARE proposes to focus on WASH interventions in Quissanga and Macomia districts to benefit both IDPs and returnees. Because both districts are hard to reach and underserved, CARE will combine emergency assistance with long-term solutions. This will allow families to benefit from long-lasting interventions.

project_name: Provision of emergency multi-sectoral assistance to conflict-affected populations in Sudan, in Gedaref, and Khartoum
project_objective:
Nine months into the conflict which erupted in April 2023 between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) the total estimate of Internally Displaced People (IDPs) across Sudan has reached 6 million as of January 2024 (IOM DTM). 54% of them are women, and over 50% of them under 18. The majority of IDPs are staying with host communities. Hundreds of thousands of people have arrived in Gedaref and Al Jazirah, along Madani road, fleeing Khartoum. Even though 3.5 million persons fled Khartoum, an even more important number remain in the city, and needs in the capital remains very high, while access to services is very limited. Following intense fighting in December in Al Jazirah state, Sudan's breadbasket, and the fall of Madani to the RSF, more than 509,796 people have been (re)displaced since then, with more than 60% fleeing to neighboring states (Gedaref, Sennar, White Nile, ...), putting an additional burden on IDPs already present settled in these states and host communities. The remaining 40% were displaced or re-displaced within the state. The disruption of harvest threatens national food availability. The cholera outbreak which was declared in Gedaref state in Sept. 2023, has spread to 10 states, with close to 10,000 suspected cholera cases, with 275 associated deaths reported as of January 20th, 2024 (WHO). 
The integrated project's goals are to improve immediate access to free, quality, emergency medical care to internally displaced populations and host communities, to seek to contribute to a reduction in mortality and morbidity by increasing access, coverage, use and quality of Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition, with the support to 1 Health Facilities (HF), 1 in Gedaref and 2 Mobile Health Teams (MHTs), one in Gedaref and one in Khartoum. 
Activities:
1) Health : provide Basic infrastructure, drugs/medical equipment and financial support to health facility, with the provision of essential pharmaceutical commodities following standard quality process for purchase, storage, distribution and management, and nonmedical equipment and supplies to health facilities, their financial support and necessary rehabilitation. PUI will continue to coordinate with UNFPA and WHO for the provision of SRH and IEH kits.
-Training and capacity building for MoH staff
-Provision of medical consultations through MHT and HFs, with preventive and curative services for common communicable and vaccine-preventable diseases, provision of quality Sexual and Reproductive Services (SRH) by implementing Minimum Initial Service Package for Sexual and Reproductive Health (MISP) objectives. PUI will support ante-natal care (ANC) and post-natal care (PNC) deliveries and Family Planning consultations. PUI has been a partner of UNFPA for the last two years and will ensure the distribution of dignity kits, including necessary items for menstrual hygiene kits, through MHT.
-Support referrals to higher level health care services, based on continuous service mapping
-Community based health intervention, with a network of 30 Community Health Volunteers from the targeted communities. CHVs will be trained and provide community awareness sessionson prevention of most common diseases, infection prevention and control, use of SRH services, prevention of outbreak diseases, vaccination, through door-to-door visits, under supervision of PUI’s team. 
2) Nutrition:
-Integrated management of malnutrition at MHT / HF levels, with OTP/TSFPs at HFs and MHT
-Support referrals to higher level health care services for SAM with medical complications to the most accessible Stabilization Centre
-Community based nutrition intervention: the trained CHVs will screen, refer and raise awareness on nutrition issues, at community level, in the HF supported by PUI and in the MHT. CHVs will implement collective IYCF awareness sessions at gathering points (markets, HFs, schools and worship places).
PUI will coordinate with UNICEF, WFP for nut supplies.

project_name: Prevención, Respuesta y Provisión de Servicios Urgentes en Protección Especial a  Niñas, Niños y Adolescentes y sus Familias Víctimas de Violencia en Contexto de Emergencias
project_objective:
UNICEF proporcionará asistencia urgente para la protección de la infancia a 40.000 niñas, niños, mujeres y hombres en 17 municipios priorizados por el Panorama de Necesidades Humanitarias de Honduras, proporcionando servicios de protección de la infancia y acciones de reducción de la violencia/violencia de género, incluyendo información sobre los servicios de protección de la infancia y cómo buscar ayuda.

En Honduras, los principales perpetradores de la violencia y el abuso sexual contra los niños son miembros de la familia (el caso del 47% de las niñas que son víctimas de abuso sexual), o miembros de la comunidad con vínculos con el niño. Por lo tanto, a través de estos las estrategias implementadas, UNICEF y sus aliados desarrollarán actividades con las niñas y los niños para ayudar a desarrollar sus capacidades para identificar los riesgos de violencia y abuso y saber cómo buscar ayuda inmediata.
También trabajaremos directamente con los padres, cuidadores y miembros de la comunidad para aumentar el nivel de concienciación hacia la violencia contra los niños y la violencia sexual y de género, y promoveremos el liderazgo dentro de las comunidades para identificar y denunciar posibles casos a los servicios de protección de la infancia.
La gestión de los casos se agilizará entre los líderes de la comunidad las autoridades municipales de protección de la infancia y la SENAF a través de los procedimientos operativos estándar (POE) preexistentes desarrollados conjuntamente por UNICEF, la SENAF y los gobiernos municipales bajo el marco legal del Sistema Nacional de Protección de la Infancia (SIGADENAH).
Centraremos nuestro trabajo en las comunidades marginadas más afectadas por la violencia, la violencia de género y la migración forzada, así como en las comunidades predominantemente garífunas y afrohondureñas, que también son las más desatendidas por los servicios estatales de respuesta a emergencias.
Las actividades de respuesta están diseñadas para proporcionar servicios inmediatos que salvan vidas a las comunidades más afectadas por las múltiples emergencias. Tendrán una duración de 12 meses.

project_name: Increasing equitable access and utilization of quality preventative and integrated nutrition services and building resilience among vulnerable groups in Fangak and Nyirol Counties
project_objective:
Recurrent Conflicts, floods and macro-economic challenges in South Sudan continue to worsen nutrition emergency. According to the SS 2023 FSNMS and SMART survey findings, the national GAM level remain above the WHO threshold of 15% with 1.65 M U5 children and 870,000 PLW at risk of acute malnutrition in 2024. Fangak and Nyirol Counties are classified as IPC 3 & 4 respectively with the latter having 3000 people classified in IPC Phase 5 (IPC Nov 2023), Similarly, they are among the 18 NC 2024 priority counties with multiple aggravating factors namely nutrition wasting, food insecurity, Poor WASH, Morbidity & GBV-in Emergency concern. This calls for a concerted effort for urgent treatment and prevention interventions and this is the background upon which this project has been designed and proposed.
In order to optimize results, an Integrated Package of interventions using nutrition sites as entry point will be adopted which involves: 1) Working with other sectors for multiple services vulnerable families 2) Collaboration with key sectors such as FSL, WASH, Nutrition, Health and GBV Interventions. In order to strengthen sustainable nutrition outcomes, the project shall adopt preventative actions that reduce the rate of malnutrition and improve the sustainability of treatments; enhance community engagement by taking services closer to households, through the roll out of the revised CNV guidelines and Family MUAC screening; as well as facility-based data analysis and feedback information to improve overall performance of service delivery and timely coordination of response decision making.
In the context conflict and flooding, services will be delivered from targeted static OTP-TSFP sites and mobile outreach services to reach the displaced with nutrition survival kits to ensure timely emergency response. The response activities will cover (1) case-finding screening using the Family-MUAC in all sites including IDP locations; (2) admission to OTP services for SAM U5 children and TSFP services using expanded criteria where needed including treatment of malaria, diarrhea and other high prevalence diseases (3) provide SC services for SAM children with medical complications; (4) deliver expanded MIYCN services to PLW and care-givers of children under 23 months through counselling PLW, care-providers and MtoM support groups, including vitamin A supplements, de-worming and kitchen gardens. To address these multiple drivers of chronic malnutrition, this project will scale up multi-sector solutions by working with co-located partners.
This project will strengthen AAP, by establishing QAAP committees and community complain and feedback mechanism in the nutrition facilities plus initiating community FGDs with community members. Similarly, programme staff will be trained on how to serve best the beneficiaries using the QAAP approach, while sensitization will focus on raising community awareness of systems in place for representation of their different interests and needs. Further there will be focus on raising awareness and providing information to beneficiaries on their rights and entitlement in all the nutrition sites and ensuring that communities are involved in the design, implementation, M and E on the planed nutrition project.
The drivers of GBV remain unchanged from past years. Therefore, this project will mainstream protection and disability inclusion and emphasize gender and age considerations and also conduct safety audits and collaborate with the targeted communities to implement protection practices to reduce risk of SGBV. To improve sustainability, this project will be integrated fully with health and use the BPHNS to guide targeted capacity building of both health and nutrition staff. Strengthening local capacity will target SMoH CHDs, project staff and CNVs as well as other common interest groups such as MtoMSG and local authorities with a focus on job-relevant training including refresher courses.

project_name: Improving access to and utilization of integrated essential health care services by all people in need including the vulnerable and crisis affected in Ayod, Nyirol, Fangak and Uror Counties.
project_objective:
The main aim of this project is to reach 121,428 people out of cluster target of 238,830 with essential lifesaving health services in Ayod, Fangak, Nyirol and Uror Counties of Jonglei State. The targeted population includes; Host community, IDPs, refugees, and recent returnees from Sudan. The project will scale up interventions to prevent and respond to disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies, integrate with nutrition, WASH, protection FSL and also strengthen community health services and engagement to bridge the gaps in accessing health care. This is in line with the 2024 Health Sector Response plan which accentuates three objectives i.e. to improve equitable access to life-saving essential comprehensive quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment of common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations, Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases, Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms.
The design of this project is anchored on improving access to integrated essential life-saving health care services through static, mobile and community health volunteers. The project will strengthen sub-national health delivery systems, quality improvements, timely detection of disease outbreaks, investigation and response in targeted Counties. High mortality rate from prevalent epidemic diseases will be addressed. In the volatile context of Jonglei, the project will target Sudan returnees, IDPs recently displaced by conflict and flooding, and host communities in areas with limited access to health services. Whereas the 2024 HC PIN is 60,241,74,525, 60,650 and 70,326 in Ayod, Fangak, Nyirol and Uror respectively, this project targets 121,428 beneficiaries out of the HC target of 238,830 consisting of Host Community, IDPs and Returnees and disaggregated by County, age, gender and disability i.e. U5 =M10,011-F12,285, 6-17 yrs=M18,902 -F21,898, 18-60yrs.=M23,117-F24,776, >60yrs=M4,520 -F5919. 
The flooding, conflict, IDPs, returnees, disease outbreaks, limited food and income sources all have food insecurity and health implications. In order to achieve the expected results, the project will prioritize services through both community and clinical consultations (OPD) for curative, preventive and promotive services. It will focus on MNCH as well as improvement of HF infrastructure, HMIS and capacity building of personnel. CMA will support county M&E to collect data from health facilities and BHWs and enter into DHIS2,IDSR,EWARS and 5Ws. Data will be analyzed and used for decision making. MNCH Services will include Health education; Immunization, ANC services, skilled delivery, postnatal care, IMNCI, HIV/PMTCT, BEMONC and referral. SGBV and MHPSS services to be provided will include Identification, counselling, GBV/CMR and proper referral for all including rape survivors. 
A successful implementation of these activities would enhance access and quality health care to crisis-affected people, prevent and respond to health threats, and strengthen the health system significantly resulting in the overall decrease in morbidity and mortality arising from the epidemic prone diseases e.g. Measles, HEV, EVD.  It will further increase access to services for SGBV survivors, PWDs and people with mental health disorders. Besides improving resilience among vulnerable populations, the activities are further expected to benefit from an integrated response involving key sectors such as WASH, nutrition, FSL and protection. In order to ensure AAP, a mechanism will be provided for affected populations to receive the information needed to make informed decisions on accessing health services, provide feedback on the interventions, share concerns and submit complaints.

project_name: Lifesaving Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) response services for vulnerable individuals in Khartoum, Gedaref, Blue Nile, White Nile and Jazeera states
project_objective:
The IRC will be implementing Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) activities to support refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and host communities across Gedaref, Khartoum, Blue Nile, White Nile, and Jazeera states. The IRC aims to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, and reliability of clean drinking water sources by strengthening the maintenance and operation of drinking water sources. Additionally, the IRC will promote the adoption of positive hygiene behaviors and practices, especially regarding the safe water chain activities from collection to consumption of clean drinking water.
The IRC will determine and execute project interventions in Blue Nile's Wad al Mahi locality and White Nile's Kosti and Rahad localities with the highest unmet needs. The IRC will also administer WASH activities in other areas that can be safely accessed by project staff. To ensure long-term sustainability, the IRC will primarily utilize local methods and materials to complement the impact of water supply infrastructure activities.
The IRC will form Water Management Committees (WMCs) to support projects. The members will be selected based on coordination with community leaders and will consist of approximately 5 to 6 members. The selection criteria will include individuals from the targeted community, those over 18 years of age who can read and write in Arabic and are active participants in community work. Those with technical skills or trusted human resources such as masons, teachers, community health volunteers (CHVs), and religious/customary leaders will be given preference. Women will be specifically targeted to be trained and selected to take on leadership and management roles within the WMCs, and the IRC will advocate to ensure women make up at least 50% of the WMC members.
Moreover, WASH volunteers will operate within the project's three target locations. The IRC anticipates having at least two CHVs (segregated by gender) for every 1,000 individuals within the target communities. Women, in particular, will be empowered and trained to take on the role of CHVs to serve as agents for change within their respective communities.
Lastly, the IRC will respond to the emergency by supporting the affected people from the ongoing conflict in Khartoum, Jazeera, and the IDPs in Gedaref, Blue Nile, and White Nile states by providing WASH services at the health facilities and community levels.

project_name: Food security support to crisis affected populations in Al Jazira, Gedaref, White Nile, Khartoum and Blue Nile states.
project_objective: IRC intends to target crisis affected communities with livelihoods activities to cushion them, the affected communities in various states needs to recover from the shocks, the crisis and the economic collapse,  The IRC team intends to target men and women in host communities to be able to produce staple foods, and other cash crops to boos economic status of small scale farmers whose value chain has been affected by the ongoing crisis in Sudan. IRC through its interventions intends to improve the agricultural productivity of the affected population. The purpose of the food security support is to take most vulnerable populations from further deteriorating into severe food insecurity, to make sure that the IPC levels of affected communities' is reduced.  To improve the food diversity and dietary diversity by most persons at all the time. The country is facing shortages of food stocks and this has caused many to be in poverty, and worse malnutritional levels. IRC will work with livelihoods partners to improve the seed systems of affected persons so that they can produce. All the targtetd persons who can produce will be trained to do smart agriculture. Conservative farming. IRC believes the target will be food secure in the long and short season, also that the communities will be able to sell surplus and look after their families as before. IRC believes that the communities will recover from the shocks if they are empowered to practice farming and look after their livestock. In some areas some veterinary trainings will be done to preserve the loss of livestock due to diseases or other animal health problems. Sudan is rich in livestock and cropping activities as a result these should be upholded at all costs by livelihoods practitioners. In The FSL interventions IRC intends to partner with local non governmental organisations and other cluster members to carry out assessments to the target group and see what they need most. IRC will also use desktop reviews to come up with a response plan in hard to reach areas especially in contested areas with a target majority of farmers and small scale farmers. The needs being analayzed it will be easy to reach the targets and to scale up the food security support in the chosen areas. The affected communities needs agricultural inputs and equipment so that they produce for domestic consumption and go to markets with surplus. IRC has been in these areas on intervention and because of its presence field teamd have so established good relations with local leadership and other value chain systems. This will enable IRC livelihoods team to effectively implement without any bottlenecks. IRC teams have now institutional memory that will build up the needs of the affected communities and recommend any food security support interventions in the chosen geographical locations. Despite the ongoing crisis, IRC teams will work in these areas and taking caution in security , also the team will feed in other ICCG meetings at state levels and share notes on project interventions and share challenges in any.

project_name: Improving livelihood assistance for enhanced recovery and increased resilience of conflict affected communities in Northeast Nigeria.
project_objective:
The ongoing insurgency in Northeast Nigeria is widely reported as the main driver of displacement. This insurgency has been followed by communal clashes, disasters and, in recent times, inter-communal conflicts. These clashes involve confrontations between ethnic and religious groups, often triggered by land and border issues, and increasing tensions between herder communities and sedentary farmers.
The majority of IDPs displaced by the insurgency are located in Bama, Damboa, Gwoza, Jere, Konduga, Maiduguri M.C., Monguno and Ngala local government areas (LGAs) of Borno state. The populations displaced as a result of communal clashes are concentrated in the north-western part of Adamawa, the southern part of Borno, Taraba, Gombe, and western Bauchi states. According to IOM DTM mobility tracking, while communal clashes accounted for 4 per cent of the displacements before the year 2021, they were cited as the main trigger of displacement by 35 per cent of the IDPs displaced in 2023.  
IOM considers the insufficient capacity of the host communities in areas of return to be a direct risk of the overall progressive resolution of displacement in the Northeast. This project seeks to contribute to the recovery and resilience of conflict and flood-affected populations in Northeast Nigeria by restoring infrastructure, promoting early recovery, including through economic revitalization restoration of livelihoods, strengthening government capacity, promoting social cohesion and peaceful coexistence, and facilitating resilience-building. Early recovery and livelihood interventions under this project will include Cash for Livelihood, Cash for Work (CFW) climate-smart businesses including Individual Livelihood Assistance (ILA) and other income-generating activities (IGA) in the form of vocational skills training, apprenticeships, and business support assistance for start-up or scale up as a means to achieving peaceful reintegration and social cohesion through engagement with various populations on the move. Through the adoption of cash-based interventions, IOM strives to assist affected populations in a more dignified manner, as they empower people to determine their own needs and the best way of meeting them. Government plays a crucial role in developing and establishing stable mechanisms for economic and social development. The level of management capacity is a key element of success; IOM strives to promote cross-sectoral collaboration and systems to strengthen support and localization – the support will be guided by need assessment with the key stakeholders and the targeted government might include the economic recovery ministries, environment, and climate change.

project_name: Provision of improved, safe, and dignified essential water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) supplies to the conflict-affected populations and host communities in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Unprecedented rainfall events, a consequence of the climate crisis, have escalated water-related diseases, notably cholera, and acute diarrhea. Furthermore, extraordinary floods, coupled with the dynamic population shifts within internally displaced persons (IDP) camps, characterized by high population density and an influx of returnees to their places of origin, have posed formidable challenges to the operation and maintenance of water and sanitation infrastructure. Properly managing fecal sludge and solid waste is compromised, leading to a substantial environmental and public health impact.
These challenges unfold within a context marked by a surge in people requiring water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) assistance, predominantly concentrated in the country's northeastern part. According to the Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) conducted by IOM between 2021 and 2022, Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) states experienced a significant increase in the number of people in need of WASH humanitarian assistance, rising from three million to five million individuals. This surge is evident across internally displaced persons (+29%), returnees (+113%), and host communities (+95%).
In response to these identified needs and alignment with the objectives of the Nigerian WASH Sector, IOM is poised to enhance its provision of WASH services. The focus extends to IDPs, returnees in camp and camp-like settings, and hosting communities in BAY states. Additionally, IOM will distribute hygiene kits following national/cluster standards and reinforce the WASH sector's common pipeline strategy to facilitate access to hygiene kits for regional humanitarian actors.
The primary activity will ensure access to standard hygiene kit supplies through IOM's common supply unit. This includes various hygiene kits such as Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM), replenishment, Cholera, and sanitation kits. This comprehensive approach supports rainy season preparedness and response, including critical cholera preparedness and response activities.
The project's implementation targets an estimated 1,193,206 individuals in the BAY states, specifically focusing on hotspot areas identified through previous flash reports and occurrences. Various local government areas (LGAs) have been earmarked, including those in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe states, carefully considering specific geographic and community contexts.
IOM is committed to ensuring that the design and implementation of all WASH activities are inclusive of age, gender, and disability-specific needs, explicitly addressing the unique requirements of women and girls, including MHM. Engaging with community structures on the ground during missions and establishing communication channels where possible is integral to assessing, monitoring, and evaluating gender, age, and disability-specific needs and the impact of activities.
Using the IOM WASH Monitoring and Evaluation Framework and the Gender Inclusion and Gender-based Violence (GBV) Risk Mitigation Toolkit for WASH Programming, IOM will uphold "Do No Harm" principles throughout WASH interventions. This commitment is particularly emphasized in activities involving latrine and water point locations and construction, with mechanisms such as consultations with vulnerable groups playing a pivotal role.
In analyzing potential risks associated with context-specific environmental degradation, IOM will prioritize actions that mitigate ecological risks. This includes a preference for locally made items and local procurements within the BAY states for cost-effectiveness, time efficiency, and support to the local economy. Furthermore, in procurement, IOM will prioritize products with greater durability and high recycled content, contributing to sustainability and environmental responsibility.

project_name: Améliorer l'accès à une éducation de qualité et sûres pour les personnes déplacées et les populations hôtes (y compris les personnes handicapées) au Niger/ Projet Beerey
project_objective:
Beerey est un projet qui vise l'amélioration des services éducatifs et des conditions de vie des communautés dans un contexte d'instabilité socio-politique et économique au Niger. Il s'agira d'offrir une éducation inclusive de qualité et sûres aux personnes en situation d'urgence et d'améliorer les moyens de subsistance. Le projet est orienté vers les femmes, les filles, les garçons, les adolescent.e.s, les personnes handicapées et les chef.f.es de ménages issus de populations déplacées et des communautés hôtes.			
Nous utiliserons une approche communautaire et participative afin de poser les jalons de l'engagement communautaire et les prémices de la durabilité/appropriation de l'action.
Spécifiquement, les enfants retournés, déplacés internes et enfants de la communauté d'accueil âgés de 7 à 17 ans, filles et garçons y compris ceux en situation de handicap qui n’ont pas d'accès à l'éducation en raison des mouvements des populations; les jeunes retournés, déplacés internes et les jeunes de la communauté d'accueil âgés de 15 à 18 ans qui souffrent d'un manque d'opportunités de développement personnel; les enseignants et les autorités éducatives locales qui seront ciblés pour contribuer à renforcer leurs capacités techniques et à fournir un soutien psychologique et logistique/didactique pour la mise en œuvre de leurs responsabilités dans les zones ciblées afin d'assurer une éducation de qualité; les cellules communautaires de base du secteur de l’Education (Associations des Parents d’Elèves, AME, COGES, etc.) seront ciblées dans les écoles pour améliorer la gouvernance scolaire et la pérennité de l'éducation dispensée dans la zone d'intervention.
Au sein de ces groupes cibles, une attention particulière sera portée aux enfants et aux jeunes les plus vulnérables touchés par le conflit tels que les filles mères, les enfants en situation de handicap, les enfants non accompagnés et séparés, les enfants des minorités qui sont soumis à des abus ou à la discrimination. Telles sont les cibles potentielles du projet Beerey.

project_name: Provisión de serviciós de Nutrición para los niños, niñas menores de cinco años y las mujeres como  respuesta de acción anticipatoria en las zonas afectadas por la sequía en Honduras
project_objective:
La iniciativa principal del proyecto se basa en mejorar el acceso de las comunidades más vulnerables del Corredor Seco de Honduras a servicios vitales claves de  nutrición, con el objetivo de prevenir el deterioro del estado nutricional de mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (PLW) y niños de 6 a 59 meses.
El Corredor Seco ha sido afectado por sequías  durante varios años, y hay indicios de que los desastres de origen natural aumentarán en frecuencia, fuerza e imprevisibilidad en los próximos años exacerbados por el cambio climático. En Honduras, más de 1.5 millones de personas han sido afectadas por las más recientes sequías e inundaciones causada por El Niño y los fenómenos asociados

La inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional debida a la sequía afectara principalmente a las familias rurales del sur, centro y occidente de Honduras, en particular las dedicadas a la agricultura de subsistencia, ya que muchas se desarrolla en ecosistemas altamente frágiles, principalmente en zonas de laderas con suelos degradados, susceptibles a deslizamientos y a expensas de las constantes alteraciones climáticas, tal es el caso de la sequías. Los niños, niñas y las mujeres son los grupos mas vulnerables que se veran afectados ante la escases de alimentos, impactando en su  estado nutricional, y en riesgo de presentar desnutrición aguda debido a un desequilibrio de dieta alimenticia y nutrientes esenciales, las tasas de desnutrición aguda grave (emaciación) en niños menores de cinco años van de 3 a 10 %, en Centro America, mientras que el promedio en Honduras es de 1.9%. Las tasas de desnutrición crónica (retraso del crecimiento) en las zonas afectadas van desde 20% hasta 70% 5,6 cuando el promedio de América Central es de 15.4%, esto podría relacionarse a la baja productividad y calidad en sus cultivos, a la dispersión geográfica, falta de acceso a alimentos nutritivos y el limitado acceso a la información de las madres sobre el aprovechamiento de los recursos disponibles en temas de nutrición, ademas de los anterior y no menos importante es la falta de acceso a agua segura, por lo cual, es necesario eficientar la coordinación con los sectores de WASH para garantizar la apropiada preraración de alimentos y evitar riesgos de infecciones intestinales  ya que estas reducen  el apetito de los niños y limitan la absorción de nutrientes, lo que resulta en el deterioro del estado nutricional.

Las actividades previstas incluyen: 
a. El cribado y la vigilancia nutricional de niños y niñas menores de cinco años para identificar y derivar los casos para un tratamiento que salve vidas. 
b. Tratamiento de la malnutrición aguda  moderada y severa 
c. Distribución de suplementos de hierro y ácido fólico a las madres embarazadas y lactantes.
d. Suplementación con micronutrientes en menores de cinco años incluyendo la desparacitación.
F. Suplementos de Zinc terapéutico a niños y niñas menores de cinco años en el manejo de la diarrea
g. Acciones de promoción para  prevención de la deficiencia de yodo, a través del consumo de la  sal yodada.
h. Apoyo en consejería y comunicación para una alimentación complementaria adecuada en cantidad y calidad para niños menores de 2 años asi como la consejería nutricional para promover el consumo adecuado de alimentos y nutrientes y su conservación de manera segura.
i. Promoción del lavado de manos con agua y jabón antes de preparar la comida y comer, y después de ir al baño y de limpiar a los niños.
J. Coordinar con cluster WASH la gestión adecuada de los desechos sólidos en las comunidades intervenidas con el proyecto.

El proyecto prevé alcanzar 16,260 niños & niñas menores de 5 años, 3000 mujeres embarazadas & en periodo de lactancia y 1000 hombres cuidadores en las actividades de prevención, atención y promoción. Aunque el número de hombres cuidadores no se refleja en la meta general del proyecto, si se refleja en la población meta de uno de los indicadores como parte de las intervenciones.

project_name: Protegiendo a Niñas, niños, adolescentes y familias migrantes y refugiadas en tránsito por Honduras.
project_objective: Honduras por su posición geográfica y políticas migratorias ha sido tradicionalmente un país de ingreso y tránsito de personas que integran movimientos mixtos que se dirigen hacia el norte, tanto desde América Latina como desde fuera del continente, en el último año 2023 se registraron las cifras más altas de 545,043 migrantes en tránsito, principalmente de nacionalidades venezolana, cubana, haitiana, ecuatoriana, entre otras. Además, en 2023 la adopción de nuevas políticas migratorias resulto en que población principalmente venezolana se quedaran por periodos largos en Honduras, superando la capacidad de respuesta nacional. La magnitud de la crisis de personas refugiadas y migrantes ingresando por las fronteras sur y oriente se ve exacerbada por las condiciones de vulnerabilidad de los municipios de Danlí, El Paraíso y Trojes que no cuentan con las condiciones mínimas de recepción: alojamiento, apoyo psicosocial,cash transfer; así como los servicios de protección adecuados para la niñez. UNICEF proporcionará asistencia humanitaria urgente para la protección de la infancia a mas de 100,000 niñas, niños, mujeres y hombres que se encuentren en tránsito por Honduras, en zonas fronterizas, municipios priorizados o lugares de alta vulnerabilidad para los migrantes, refugiados y desplazados por la ausencia de servicios o donde los servicios son muy débiles. UNICEF implementará las actividades de protección multisectoriales por medio del CONSORCIO LIFE-HONDURAS que integra socios en protección de niñez, albergue, salud mental y derivando tenciones de agua y saneamiento, nutrición, educación, protección social, salud psicosocial. Actualmente el Consorcio lo integran: Acción contra el Hambre (ACH), la Fundación Alivio del Sufrimiento (FAS), Pure Water for the World, ChildFund y ADRA este modelo de coordinación y asistencia se inició en 2022 y facilito la complementariedad sectorial en la emergencia migratoria y aseguro respuestas rápidas y oportunas para la habilitación de espacios seguros y provisión de asistencia humanitaria adecuada. + − Leaflet | © OpenStreetMap Además, UNICEF se articula con gobiernos locales, Instituto Nacional de Migración, la Secretaria de Niñez, Adolescencia y Familia y otras ONG´s nacionales e internacionales de la Red Humanitaria que responden ante la emergencia migratoria. Mediante esta estrategia se busca el fortalecimiento y ampliación de la capacidad nacional de atención a la migración por medio de Consorcio LIFE, alianzas estratégicas, desarrollando modelos de respuesta rápida bajo los estándares y principios humanitarios. Las actividades de respuesta están diseñadas para proporcionar respuesta humanitaria que salva vidas a migrantes y refugiados en situación de alta vulnerabilidad y se adaptan a los cambios en las dinámicas migratorias con servicios móviles, multilingües y multiculturales, con enfoque de protección de derechos, rendición de cuentas, protección contra PEAS y enfoque de género.

project_name: Rehabilitación de infraestructura de Centros Educativos
project_objective:
Al inicio del año escolar 2023, se estimó que había cerca de un millón deniños y niñas fuera del sistema eductaivo. La pandemia del COVID-19 sumado a las tormentas tropicales Eta e Iota amplió las brechas educativas, lo que ha agravado el problema de la baja cobertura escolar y el bajo rendimiento del aprendizaje. En este contexto, muchos más niños, niñas y adolescentes están fuera de la escuela, y los resultados de aprendizaje en están en proecso de mejora.  Existen cientos de centros educativos dañados,como consecuencia de la sequía, falta de inversión o las repercusiones del cambio climático en las zonas postergadas. A muy corto plazo, se debe rehabilitar las escuelas, garantizando el acceso al agua potable, el saneamiento y la higiene, promoviendo la matrícula a tiempo y proporcionando apoyo a los padres y madres para que lleven a sus hijos e hijas a la escuela. Luego, es necesario diseñar e implementar modalidades flexibles que faciliten la reincorporación y permanencia de más niñas y niños en la escuela, de manera presencial y semipresencial. Será necesario garantizar el acceso a material impreso, además de utilizarlo con algún medio de comunicación (WhatsApp, radio o televisión). El apoyo de las madres y padres en el hogar seguirá siendo clave para apoyar el aprendizaje de los niños. El apoyo educativo, ya sea de refuerzo o de nivelación, debe complementarse con acciones que tengan en cuenta la perspectiva de género y que les permitan un acceso igualitario a las actividades educativas.

Esta propuesta está alineada con el Plan de Respuesta 2024 y las actividades prioritarias expuestas en esta propuesta., respondiendo a los indicadores pririzados las lluvias y las inundaciones han afectado a las infraestructuras escolares, y muchos centros educativos siguen siendo utilizados como albergues, por lo que es necesario repararlos y rehabilitarlos antes de que puedan volver a utilizarse como escuelas.

La propuesta mantendrá la estrategia de clúster educación recientemente desarrollada con un enfoque en la reparación de los centros educativos dañados, la apertura de las escuelas y la recuperación del aprendizaje. La estrategia de clúster se basa en las recientes evaluaciones de los centros educativos dañados. UNICEF, Save the Children y SEDUC  lideran la propuesta y se acordó con la SEDUC y DECOAS que la selección de escuelas incluya centros con daños menores y no estructurales, ya que este tipo de daño puede implicar la reconstrucción parcial o total. Esto ayudará a centrarse en los municipios más afectados y en las especificidades de los daños, lo que ayudó a establecer una secuencia de acciones prioritarias para la recuperación

En algunos casos, la rehabilitación de los centros estará a cargo de los gobiernos locales, mientras que en otros se recurrirá a una entidad ejecutora externa al municipio. Esto dependerá de la capacidad institucional que demuestren los municipios en temas similares. En cualquier caso, UNICEF hará un seguimiento cercano de las intervenciones, estableciendo relaciones estrechas con los gobiernos locales, directores y docentes, y madres y padres de familia de las comunidades.

Además, las actividades de esta propuesta están alineadas con los dos documentos estratégicos de SEDUC, incluyendo: Estrategia para el Retorno Seguro a los Centros Educativos Gubernamentales y No Gubernamentales ante la Crisis de la COVID-19 en Honduras y el Plan de Contingencia de Atención Educativa: Ante Emergencia por Tormenta Tropical Producida por Huracán ETA. 

Todas las actividades han sido discutidas y coordinadas tanto con la Dirección General de Construcciones Escolares y Bienes Inmuebles (DIGECEBI) de la SEDUC y la Dirección Educación, Comunicación, Ambiente y Salud  (DECOAS). La DIGECEBI de la SEDUC se encarga de los planteles escolares

project_name: Support WASH response to affected population in Lac Chad Basin of Cameroon
project_objective: The project aims to strengthen water, sanitation and hygiene response to affected population in Far North region of Cameroon with a focus on IDP camp, communities hosting IDP and returnees. In water domain, rehabilitation of boreholes and construction of small water supply network powered with solar energy will be prioritized. On hygiene and sanitation issues, communities approached for total sanitation will be implemented at municipality level. Construction of community latrines and showers will be limited to IDP sites. Hygiene promotion with distribution of minimum WASH kits will be implemented in target communities. The area targeted cover four divisions of Far North region: Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga, Mayo Danay and Logone & Chari. With these interventions, this project targets 60,000 people for access to safe water, 50,000 people for access to adequate basic sanitation and 150,000 people reached with critical WASH supply (including hygiene items) and services. This project will also include a component relative to capacity building of WASH actor at regional level on key issues such as design, installation and maintenance of solar system for water supply, cholera response, flood response, protection and gender mainstreaming in WASH sector.

project_name: Prevention of all forms of malnutrition and Treatment of life-threatening forms in the context of Lake Chad Basin, Far North region, Cameroon.
project_objective:
Children, adolescents and women have access to diet, services and practices that support the nutritional status in the humanitarian context of Lake Chad Basin, Far North Region:
45,117 children (21,598 boys and 23,010 girls U5 admitted for SAM treatment)
65,892 children (33,604 boys and 32,288 girls) U2 admitted in the Homebased Food fortification programme
95,000 people (M/W) sensitized including 35,000 women trained for SAM detection
(mother MUAC)
106,200 pregnant women receiving weekly iron and folic acid supplements
Activities or outputs
• Caregivers of children aged 0-23 months are supported to adopt recommended infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices, including both breastfeeding and complementary feeding
• Children aged 0-59 months have improved nutritional intake and status through age-appropriate nutrient-rich diets, micronutrient supplementation, home-fortification of foods and deworming prophylaxis.
• Adolescent girls have access to community-based package of interventions that includes at a minimum: iron and folic acid supplementation, deworming prophylaxis, nutrition education, counselling and support.
• Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers - with special attention to pregnant adolescent girls and other nutritionally at‑risk mothers – have access to a package of interventions that includes at a minimum: iron and folic acid/multiple micronutrient supplementation, deworming prophylaxis, weight monitoring, nutrition counselling, and nutrition support.
• All children aged under five years in affected areas are screened regularly for the early detection of severe wasting and other forms of life‑threatening acute malnutrition and are referred as appropriate for treatment services.
• All children aged under five years suffering from severe wasting and other forms of life-threatening acute malnutrition in affected areas benefit from facility and community-based services (Fix or mobile) that provide effective treatment.

project_name: Psychosocial Support, care and protection from violence, exploitation and abuse for children affected by the Lake Chad Basin crisis, including support to children formerly associated with armed groups, in the Far North Region
project_objective:
The year 2023 was marked by numerous protection incidents affecting children in Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava and Mayo Tsanaga in the Far North. In addition, significant flooding has exacerbated pre-existing child protection problems such as GBV. Significant population movements continue to be recorded adding to the pre-existing difficulties of access to basic social services for children as well as the lack of opportunities for adolescents and youth to develop their potential in a region where 64% of the current displaced population are children.

This project will support formal and community-based CP systems, placing particular emphasis on (i) capacity building of adolescent girls and boys as agents of change for conflict and violence prevention, peacebuilding, and the promotion of intergenerational and interreligious dialogue, (ii) capacity building of deconcentrated CP structures in a humanitarian/development Nexus approach focusing on case management, referral, psychosocial support, and family/community reintegration of vulnerable children girls and boys and (iii) increased coordination at all levels, under the leadership of the Regional Delegation of Social Affairs (RDSA).

The key result of the project which is in line with the objectives of the protection sector, is that conflict-affected children and caregivers are protected from violence, abuse and exploitation in armed conflict settings and live in a protective environment in the targeted localities of Logone-et-Chari, Mayo Sava, Mayo Tsanaga, Mayo Kani and Mayo Danay Divisions in the Far-North Region of Cameroon.

The project builds on previously established dynamics and community structures and will provide PSS to children and caregivers. PSS will be provided both through a one-on-one approach (through social workers or other trained child protection actors) and through community-based approaches, such as CFSs, adolescent clubs, and intergenerational dialogue.

Implementing partners will continue to identify unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). Based on previous trends and on partners capacities, the project plans to assist UASC, ensuring and providing those children with psychosocial support, alternative care arrangements, reunification with their families of origin and reinsertion in their communities. All will benefit from close individual follow-up.

To address both social norms but also to ensure smooth community reinsertion, the project will work at strengthening community mobilization and will organize community activities around prevention of GBViE including activities to abandon child marriage, to promote intergenerational dialogue and social cohesion. Based on the projections, a total of 70,000 persons (women, men, girls, boys) are planned to be reached through community mobilization activities. Partnership with religious and traditional leaders, including female stakeholders will be an important channel to display messages and address complex issues. In complement, the work on youth empowerment and participation will enable to merge with the other members of the communities and promote prevention and protection of children from violence and exploitation.

The issue of conflict-affected children without a birth certificate was confirmed to still be a major issue. The project aims at supporting conflict-affected children in obtaining a birth certificate. 60 former CAAFAG are expected to be identified, will receive PSS, and will be supported UNICEF will continue to closely work with civil society implementing partners, providing them with capacity building, supporting the setting up of SOPs for case management and referral. UNICEF will also strengthen the coordination mechanism led by RDSA.

project_name: Renforcement des structures communautaires en faveur des structures des femmes sur la violence basé sur le genre
project_objective:
Depuis le déclenchement du conflit armé dans la Province du Lac et le déplacement massif due à la crise soudanaise dans l'Est du pays, les structures communautaire et spécifiquement les femmes n'ont pas d'accès a des activités de résilience leurs permettant de subvenir a leurs besoins élémentaire afin de leurs permettre d'être autonome au sein de leurs foyer et communauté. Pour réduire cette dépendance non seulement à l’’assistance humanitaire et les risques de protection, ce projet proposera de développer des activités génératrices de revenus en faveurs des structures des femmes fréquentent les espaces amis des filles et des femmes, couche la plus vulnérable parmi les personnes déplacées vivant dans les sites, les camps et en familles hôtes que sont les femmes. C’est un projet qui promeut la capacité des femmes à générer des ressources suffisantes, d’une manière durable, pour qu’elles puissent répondre à leurs besoins et à ceux des personnes à leur charge, assurer leur autonomie et leur épanouissement au sein de leur famille et de la communauté et avoir une capacité d’épargne pour réinvestir dans leurs activités économiques et faire face aux situations d’urgence. 
Le projet sera réalisé dans 12 sites/villages dans la province du Lac (départements de Mamdi, Kaya et Fouli) et dans le provinces de Ouaddai et Sila.
