project_name: Criando y protegiendo con ternura en contextos frágiles
project_objective:
Honduras sigue sufriendo los altos índices de violencia e inseguridad de nuestro contexto, que provoca altas tasas de desplazamiento forzado y migración. Lo anterior ha aumentado la vulnerabilidad de miles de familias que ya lo eran; poniendo en riesgo aún más las vidas de personas con necesidades de protección específicas y con mayor exposición a diferentes formas de violencia: física, psicológica, VBG, sexual, reclutamiento forzado, entre otros. Los altos índices de violencia, el aumento en migración irregular y los efectos del cambio climático han puesto en evidencia la fragilidad institucional para poder responder de manera oportuna y eficaz a toda está población. Dicho lo anterior, se encuentran poblaciones mucho más vulnerables como niñas, niños y adolescentes, cuyas voces y necesidades son minimizados bajo enfoques adulto centristas, y agendas políticas con intereses creados. Por otra parte, WV tiene una presencia y cobertura en casi todos los municipios de Honduras, y por lo que tiene un acceso humanitario importante para implementar acciones rápidas en contexto de las emergencias.

Este proyecto fortalecerá las acciones que se han venido realizando para el bienestar de la niñez. Asegurar los derechos esenciales de niños y niñas a través de la implementación de espacios amigables comunitario donde además de ser espacio de recreación será también para poder socializar dichos derechos e identificar incidentes de vulneración de derechos tanto a los niños como a sus familias. Los niños y niñas en movilidad son de suma importancia y prioridad para WVH tanto por causas de mejora de condiciones de vida como para salvaguardarla; para ello la implementación de herramienta de monitoreo de migración y del Sistema de Alerta Temprana – Migración (SAT – M), será vital para prevenir las causas que fomentan la migración forzada y realizar acciones tempranas, oportunas y pertinentes. Esto también unido al fortalecimiento y coordinación del SIGADENAH a través de los Consejos de Garantías de Derechos municipales y departamentales, así como implementar la metodología de Crianza Con Ternura que permitirá disminución de violencia doméstica, la violencia física y psicológica hacia los niños y niñas. 

WVH establecerá Espacios Amigable de la Niñez (EAN) en comunidades de contexto frágil que se recuperan luego de los desastres naturales u otro de tipo de violencia con el objetivo de continuar brindando un entorno seguro para NNA y sus familias y contribuir a garantizar su bienestar psicosocial. Se facilitarán juegos, cuidado y las actividades de apoyo social apropiadas a nivel local, como la educación de madres, padres o cuidadores, el cuidado infantil compartido y los grupos de juego comunitarios. Además, EAN brindará a NNA la oportunidad de aprender sobre sus derechos, entre otros. Las actividades se ejecutarán con diferentes enfoques por edad y género, y llegarán tanto a niñas, niños pequeños como a adolescentes. 

Un enfoque clave, será brindar apoyo psicosocial a NNA y sus familias. WVH proporcionará primeros auxilios psicológicos. Los NNA que hayan sufrido abuso serán referidos a los canales adecuados para recibir apoyo. WVH pondrá en marcha acciones de seguimiento adecuadas. WVH trabajará dentro de las redes humanitarias y el gobierno para ayudar a coordinar este apoyo. Estas acciones serán coordinadas con UNICEF, la Secretaría de Niñez, Adolescencia y Familia (SENAF) y los consejos municipales y departamentales nacionales de protección para garantizar la seguridad y los derechos de los niños afectados por desastres y la violencia.

Este proyecto está directamente ligado y por ende contribuirá a los objetivos uno y dos del clúster de protección infantil, donde el acceso y atención de servicios integrales, fortalecimiento de los sistemas de protección y repuesta temprana y oportuna están siendo priorizados en las diferentes acciones.

project_name: Asistencia humanitaria en Seguridad alimentaria y Nutrición
project_objective:
El proyecto pretende contribuir a aliviar el sufrimiento humano y dignificar la vida de las personas que han sido afectadas por fenómenos naturales o crisis humanitarias. El objetivo del proyecto es ofrecer asistencia humanitaria en seguridad alimentaria y nutrición a los más vulnerables en los departamentos de Yoro, Cortés, Copán, Intibucá, Francisco Morazán, Santa Bárbara y El Paraíso. En estos siete departamentos, se asistirán 23 Municipios a través transferencia multipropósito, distribución de kits agrícolas para la reactivación de medios de vida, asistencia humanitaria en nutrición en coordinación con la Secretaría de Salud y fortaleciendo las estructuras comunitarias para la vigilancia nutricional y referencia de las niñas y niños en desnutrición aguda y moderada a los centros de salud para su recuperación oportuna. A través del proyecto se capacitarán grupos de cuidadores y cuidadores en preparación de alimentos para mejora nutricional de las familias. Adicionalmente se fortalecerán 82 unidades de salud dotando con equipo y formando a su personal, consultores pediatras apoyarán con su formación y con el manejo de desnutrición. El proyecto es inclusivo y promueve la igualdad de género, 69% de la población de los municipios de Intibucá pertenecen al grupo ético lenca, contempla grupos de edad y discapacidad. Entre las metas del proyecto figuran:
*Transferencia multipropósito a 20,700 personas
*Distribución de kits agrícolas y asistencia nutricional a 40,000 personas vulnerables,
*Distribución de silos metálicos para almacenar granos que sustentarán a las familias en épocas de crisis, se beneficiarán a aprox. 5,000 familias.
*24,100 niños y niñas menores de 5 años y 6,300 mujeres embarazadas y lactantes recibirán micronutrientes y estarán en control de las unidades de salud.
* 29,700 cuidadores y cuidadoras recibirán formación en preparación de alimentos para diversificar su alimentación y mejorar la nutrición de la familia.
* 82 unidades de salud fortalecidas
*2,460 voluntarios de salud capacitados
En conclusión el proyecto pretende beneficiar a más de 120,000 personas en acciones relacionadas a la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional. Entre los beneficiarios; el 52% son mujeres, en el departamento de Intibucá y Yoro se incluirán grupos indígenas, estimando un 69% de lencas en Intibucá y un 4% de varias etnias en Morazán, Yoro. Se estima que un 5% de la población beneficiaria son mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, 2.5% tienen algún tipo de discapacidad, 2% de las niñas y niños tienen desnutrición aguda.

Adicionalmente, WVH es una organización con presencia en los 18 departamentos de Honduras. De presentarse una emergencia o crisis, los equipos priorizan la respuestas a la emergencia.

project_objective: Le projet intervient dans les régions du Sahel, du Centre Nord, du Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun. Il sera mise en œuvre par Solidarités International en coordination avec les ONG AGED, Première Urgence Internationale et le consortium RRM. Il contribuera au rétablissement et au renforcement de l'accès de qualité à des services de base au travers de la prévention nutrition, la sécurité alimentaire et l'appui aux moyens d'existence des personnes vulnérables touchées par la crise dans ces dites régions notamment dans les provinces du Seno et du Yagha pour le Sahel, le Bam pour le Centre-Nord, Yatenga, Loroum et Zandoma dans le Nord, et Sourou et Nayala dans la Boucle du Mouhoun. Le projet ciblera essentiellement les groupes des populations en situation de vulnérabilités liées au calendrier saisonnier, aux déplacements et à l'insécurité. Il s'gira notamment en direction des personnes affectées par des chocs (mouvements de populations, conflits, crises sanitaires et/ou nutritionnelles et alimentaires), des populations vivant dans les zones enclavées coupées de tout accès au système de soins (aires de santé où les formations sanitaires sont fermées), des personnes en phase IPC 4 et IPC 5 vivant dans des zones enclavées.

project_name: La Réponse  à la crise humanitaire dans la région Est du Burkina Faso ''FIIMBA''
project_objective:
Les défis pour les petits exploitants agricoles dont les ressources sont déjà épuisées par des années d'insécurité et de production agricole limitée sont désormais aggravés par les augmentations mondiales des prix des produits de base et des engrais provoquées par la crise ukrainienne. La région de l’Est demeure ainsi confrontée à des enjeux en termes d’accès à la nourriture (l’accroissement des prix, l’épuisement des stocks et la disponibilité très limitée des produits), des déficits de productions agricole, inaccessibilité à des moyens de subsistance (les plus perturbées) ? l’inaccessibilité aux services de santé. Selon une étude interne de LWR en octobre 2023 dans la région de l’Est sur les communes concernées par le projet, 85% de la population connaisse une pénurie alimentaire et 20% ne disposent pas assez de stock alimentaire (moins de 7 jours). Près de 93% n’ont bénéficié d’aucune aide pour maintenir ou continuer leur activité économique. Cette situation expose sans doute les femmes enceinte et les enfants à la malnutrition. LWR mettra en œuvre le projet dans les communes de Fada, Gayéri et Diapangou en collaboration avec l’organisation communautaire l’Union des Associations Diema Tin Tua (UADTT) basée dans la région avec des sous-bureaux dans les différentes communes. Le projet vise à développer des activités de relèvement rapide à travers la production agricole, les activités génératrices de revenus et les liens avec le marché, offrir de l’eau potable et prévenir la malnutrition chez les enfants de 0 à 59 moi et de femmes enceintes et allaitantes. 
Ce projet déploiera une approche incluant les bénéficiaires de l’aide alimentaire immédiate (SO1) des acteurs de la réponse rapide (ACF, ACTED, PAM…). LWR va coordonner avec ces acteurs pour développer des activités de subsistance à court, moyen et long terme (SO2) au profit des bénéficiaires de l’aide alimentaire immédiate, ce qui va leurs permettre de générer des revenus pour réduire la dépendance à l'aide et accroître la résilience aux chocs. Les activités comprennent :
SAME :
•	Améliorer la disponibilité et la diversification alimentaire par le soutien à l'augmentation de la production locale grâce à la réalisation d’un périmètre maraîcher pour soutenir l’accès de 100 femmes (PDI et Hôtes) aux opportunités agricoles. 
•	La promotion de meilleures pratiques agropastorales écologiquement saines et respectueuses de l'environnement : la formation des bénéficiaires sur la production de fumure organique bokashi qui leur permettra de renforcer la fertilité des sols et de limiter l'utilisation d'engrais chimiques.
•	La diversification des sources de revenus des ménages : Le projet soutiendra les coopératives à la diversification des sources de revenus de 700 ménages(4900personnes) en Production-vente de savon solide et liquide, beurre de Karité et de Soumballa. L’organisation des bénéficiaires du projet en coopératives et constitution des Associations Villageoises d'Epargne et de Crédit (AVEC).
WASH :
•	Améliorer l'accès à l'eau potable et promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d'hygiène et d'assainissement dans les communes d'intervention du projet grâce à la réalisation d‘un forage à haut débit (entièrement alimenté en énergie solaire) pour faciliter l’accès en eau pour l'arrosage des légumes et la boisson des ménages environnants du périmètre et des sensibilisations WASH sur les pratiques essentielles dans les domaines de l'hygiène et de l’assainissement (75% des bénéficiaires). 
Nutrition préventive :
•	Diminuer la malnutrition conjoncturelle et structurelle à travers la Promotion des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène, de santé et de nutrition pour 2205 FEFA sur les comportements, attitudes et pratiques de prévention de la malnutrition : Le projet utilisera les groupes AVEC comme plateformes pour promouvoir les meilleures pratiques et le changement de comportement. Le projet profitera de ces rencontres pour mener des séances de sensibilisation et de focus groupe avec un agent de santé.

project_name: Child Protection Response for the Most Vulnerable and Conflict-Affected Children of Returnees, IDPs, and the Host Community in Unity, NBeG, and Central Equatoria States in South Sudan
project_objective:
The IRC Child Protection (CP) program will provide life-saving immediate support to the extremely vulnerable and conflict-affected children of returnees, internally displaced individuals (IDPs), and host communities in Unity, Northern Bahar el Gazhal (NBeG), and Central Equatoria States in South Sudan. The IRC CP program will reach 40,525 individuals (13,275 B, 13,650 G, 6,010 M, & 7,610 W) individuals through an integrated static and mobile response in the priority locations of Rubkona, Guit, Panyijiar, Koch, Aweil East, Juba, and Pariang Counties. The proposed CP responses are linked with two strategic objectives (SO) of the 2024 HRP such as (SO) 1: vulnerable crisis-affected people have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to life-saving assistance to meet their needs and (SO) 3: Vulnerable people’s capacity to withstand the impact of shock is increased, and nexus opportunities are optimized. The IRC will continue responding to Sudan Crisis in Rubkona, Guit, and Aweil East while continuing the humanitarian response in Koch, Panyijiar, Pariang, and Juba (IDP Camps). The IRC will provide comprehensive case management services to children with protection concerns, family tracing and reunification (FTR) services, alternative care arrangements for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), and cash assistance to meet the basic needs of children. The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) service will be provided for children and caregivers with psychological distress using a combination of approaches such as Social and Emotional Learning through Safe Healing and Learning Space (SHLS), Families Make the Difference for parenting skills of caregivers, Supporting Adolescents and their Families in Emergencies (SAFE) for life skills of adolescents, and IRC’s Brighter Futures Model for malnourished children with protection concerns. Finally, the community-based child protection (CBCP) structures at the lower community level will be established and strengthened, a series of community awareness sessions on CP risks and prevention messages will be done, and capacity building of the frontline staff and community volunteers will be done. In addition, child-friendly feedback and complaint reporting mechanisms will be established.
The IRC CP program has ongoing funding from various donors, such as BHA, SIDA, PRM, SSHF, GFFO, UNICEF and GiZ, during the proposed HRP period. The CP response will be complemented by the existing IRC’s programs, including GBV, general protection, education, nutrition, health, and livelihood programs, to ensure comprehensive care.

project_name: Life-saving and life-sustaining integrated intervention to provide dignified living conditions and enhance self-reliance of most vulnerable conflict-affected population in hard to reach and underserved areas of Cabo Delgado.
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to ensuring dignified living conditions and to enhance the self-reliance and resilience of the most vulnerable population affected by the ongoing conflict and natural hazards through the provision of safe, equitable, inclusive, and gender-responsive life-saving and life-sustaining assistance mainstreaming safe programming attuned to the protection risks and needs of the most vulnerable groups such as women and girls. The project has two main components:
1) Life-saving assistance: ACF will focus on providing support for the most vulnerable population to satisfy their basic needs. ACF will be providing first-line survival assistance for basic needs such as food (either in kind or in cash/voucher, with a flexible methodology adapted to the specific context of each community that will take into account the market functionality and capacity, governmental restrictions on cash assistance, and beneficiaries preference among others) with a focus on newly displaced persons and returnees. 
2) Life-sustaining assistance: ACF intends to protect, re-establish, and support the livelihoods including diversification as well as provide access to life-sustaining essential services to the affected population with restoration activities focusing on areas of return and diversification in areas of displacement. ACF will provide emergency livelihood support such as farming/fishing inputs, and complementary training (including life skills) and Income Generating Activities (IGAs) to enhance their self-reliance and resilience through agricultural production, access to income, and diversified livelihoods. Rehabilitation of essential and strategic infrastructures (e.g., markets, roads, schools) through cash for work will be prioritized targeting young adults and other HHs not targeted with the other life-sustaining interventions and creating temporary employment.

project_name: Provision of improved, safe, and dignified WASH services to the conflict-affected populations and host communities in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
Nigeria is still facing a severe humanitarian crisis where armed conflict, insecurity, displacement, food insecurity, malnutrition and disease outbreaks have affected millions of people. Humanitarian needs are expected to remain high in 2024 as the conflict continues and the impact of climate change worsens. 
In addition to the above, with the expansion of a government strategy for locating IDPs and decongesting camps, IOM will continue providing WASH support to displaced populations in need while reinforcing its humanitarian WASH activities with the idea of transition and recovery to support the influx of returnees to their places of origin. In direct response to the identified needs and as a significant contributor to the objectives of the WASH Sector in Nigeria, IOM is poised to expand its provision of WASH services, targeting internally displaced people and returnees in camp and camp-like settings, as well as the hosting communities in BAY (Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe) states.
To this end, IOM commits to continue:
(A)	Safeguarding access to water facilities and services through comprehensive drilling, installation, maintenance, rehabilitation, water quality and groundwater monitoring of boreholes.
(B)	Ensuring safe and equitable access to sanitation facilities (including latrines, showers, and laundry spaces) through the diligent operation and maintenance (O&M) of existing facilities and the construction of additional gender-segregated facilities and wastewater treatment systems.
(C)	Fostering improved water and sanitation outcomes in targeted settings by systematically promoting personal and environmental hygiene messages aligned with national guidelines on water-related diseases. This includes incorporating Cholera preventive measures and supporting increased capacity within established gender-balanced WASH committees.
(D)	Guaranteeing environmental sanitation (solid waste management) in the operational areas through the establishment of WASH Committees comprising both male and female community members. This involves procuring and distributing tools and equipment for effective waste management.
(E)	Distributing WASH non-food items (NFIs) in adherence to national sector standards. IOM is committed to reinforcing the core pipeline strategy within the WASH sector, facilitating access to WASH NFIs for humanitarian actors implementing crucial actions.
(F)	Contributing to bolstering capacity-building activities for local authorities, stakeholders, and key partners. This includes the integration of specialists in innovation and research in the fields of water and sanitation service management and environmental risk mitigation.
IOM is committed to ensuring that the planning and execution of all WASH activities are sensitive to the diverse needs of the project beneficiaries, incorporating considerations for age, gender, and disability. Special attention will be given to addressing the unique requirements of women and girls, including aspects of Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM). IOM will rigorously uphold the "Do No Harm" principles throughout the entirety of WASH interventions. This will be particularly emphasized in the context of WASH infrastructure locations and construction, with mechanisms like consultations with vulnerable groups playing a pivotal role.
A comprehensive analysis of potential risks stemming from context-specific environmental degradation will guide IOM in prioritizing actions that effectively mitigate environmental threats. Notably, continues championing using solar-powered water supply whenever feasible, aiming to curtail reliance on fossil fuels generated by diesel pumping. In groundwater drilling, IOM will ensure a symbiotic link with monitoring initiatives to uphold sufficient aquifer recharge.
In the design of sanitation facilities rehabilitation, a preference will be given to materials that do not deplete local natural resources or contribute to long-term environmental damage.

project_name: Responding to the Urgent Health Needs of IDPs, Persons living with Disabilities, Host Communities, and Returnees in Northeast Nigeria
project_objective:
IOM will expand its Health and Nutritional programme to a more systematic and comprehensive approach with nutrition community mobilization volunteers and utilizing the rapid response mechanism. Access to quality emergency health care and nutritional services remains a challenge, especially for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and migrants at reception centers and arrival camps. IOM intends to enhance quality access to comprehensive services through the integration of emergency mobile health care and nutritional services at the deep field locations with other health services at outposts. IOM will also continue working with health partners in outbreak prevention and response efforts, capacity building of health, nutrition, health information management, and emergency referral and support systems. As part of the health promotional and preventive activities, IOM will partner with UNICEF and local NGOs to implement health outreach through health promoters and community volunteers. Under this action, IOM will also strengthen its collaboration with the State Primary Health Care Development Agency (SPHCDA) and will continue to support the State Ministries of Health.

IOM will partner with the Borno State Ministry of Health and Borno State Primary Health Care Development Agency in providing health needs in the hard-to-reach areas. IOM will work with the agencies to develop a response strategy primarily targeting the populations on the move, persons living with disabilities, and refugees including vaccination against vaccine-preventable diseases among these vulnerable populations.

In coordination with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and related departments, World Health Organization (WHO), and the Health sector in Maiduguri, IOM will leverage on its health capacity to contribute to the government’s effort to respond to epidemics.

project_name: Provision of  Integrated Quality  Life Saving Nutrition Services for Children Under Five with Severe Acute Wasting with Medical Complications
project_objective:
Through the Humanitarian Response Plan Project (HRP) 2024, the World Health Organization aims to increase access to quality lifesaving nutrition services for children with acute wasting and tackle the high prevalence of malnutrition in the country. To achieve this, the WHO strategy will focus on providing integrated nutrition, health and WASH services targeting 10% (39729) of children under five suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition who are likely to develop medical complications, the project will also focus on malnutrition prevention in priority locations with a high burden of acute malnutrition and food insecurity. 

WHO’s HRP project interventions will prioritize provision of PAEDS/SAM kits to nutrition partners supporting Stabilization centers and other treatment centers for management of medical complications, deworming campaigns, capacity building of nutrition partners on inpatient management for severe wasting with medical complications, and stabilization center data management as well as support to early childhood development and rehabilitation of children on admission using psychosocial simulation tools. 

To ensure benefits of integration is realized, the project will also support improvement of water quality for safe preparation of F75 and F100 in the stabilization centers through provision of water candle filters. Finally, the project will facilitate integration of stabilization centers in health facility services delivery. Overall, the project will facilitate Early detection and treatment of girls and boys under 5 years of age and pregnant and lactating women with acute malnutrition contributing towards the NC sector objective 2 that seeks to increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of wasting for girls and boys under five years of age and PLW in prioritized locations by the end of 2024.

project_name: Strengthening capacity for Water quality surveillance and Infection Prevention and Control measures in cholera hotspots and other priority locations facing acute emergencies in South Sudan
project_objective:
In 2024, the World Health Organization South Sudan through this HRP project titled “Strengthening capacity for Water quality surveillance and Infection Prevention and Control measures in cholera hotspots and other priority locations facing acute emergencies in South Sudan” will reduce prevalence of malnutrition as well as contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in line with the WASH Cluster Strategy. To achieve the above objective, the project will prioritize water quality testing, monitoring and provision of real time data to WASH and Health partners for programming decision making. WHO considers safe water to be water that has zero Escherichia coli or thermotolerant coliform bacteria in any 100-millilitre sample of drinking water in accordance with national and WHO water quality guidelines. The project will further build capacity of WASH, Health and Nutrition cluster partners in waste management, and sanitary inspection. In addition, WHO will procure and provide WASH partners with water quality testing kits to expand capacity for testing. 
The project will further address gaps in clean and safe water in Nutrition stabilization centers where children suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition with medical complications are treated by providing candle filters to partners supporting stabilization centers to increase access to safe water. 
Through these activities , WHO will reach 59,937 men ,women ,boys and girls from the following  priority locations which have been identified as hotspots for cholera as well as  other places facing acute emergencies; sample locations selected by the project are Manyo, Fangak, Aweil East, Rubkona, Ayod, Leer, Renk, Kapoeta East, Aweil South, Awerial, Yirol East, Aweil North, Twic, Pibor, Abyei Region, Pariang, Abiemnhom, Twic East, Wulu, Rumbek Center, Yirol East, Juba, Wau Counties which are listed by the cluster under priority 1, 2,3, and 5 respectively.

project_name: WASH assistance to affected population in Adamawa, Borno and Plateau State
project_objective:
The situation in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) States continues to deteriorate as the effects of shrinking humanitarian space and increase in needs because of other natural disasters including flooding, further displacements and disease outbreaks . There are significant and severe humanitarian needs across Nigeria, caused by poverty – further deepened by high rates of inflation – lack of access to basic services, weak rule of law, widespread insecurity and criminality, and the impact of climate change. Four population groups are identified as in need of humanitarian and protection assistance across the Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (BAY) states: (i) internally displaced persons (IDPs) living in camps or camp-like-settings; (ii) out-of-camp IDPs living in host communities; (iii) returnees; and (iv) host communities. The latter also comprises communities affected by conflict that may not necessarily host IDPs or returnees.

Year 2023 had five themes endorsed as the key drivers of the humanitarian crisis: conflict and displacement, food insecurity and malnutrition, disease outbreaks (including cholera), floods, and camp closures and involuntary relocations and resettlement . As part of the 2023 Humanitarian response plan (HRP) for Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states, the funding appeal by United Nations and partners for 2023 is US$ 1.31 billion to respond to the critical needs of 8.3 million people needing life-saving humanitarian assistance   . As at July 2023, only $379.5 million, which represents 28.9 per cent of the total requirement had been received with Food Security and Health sectors being the highest funded sectors. The humanitarian funding overview on WASH as at 31 July 2023 had WASH funded at $18.9m which represents 17% of the total requirement of $18.9 m. The shrinking humanitarian space according to European Commission  is largely due to deteriorating security and restrictions imposed by the government and mistrust towards humanitarian actors. The Covid-19 pandemic has made WASH needs and response more complex because of existing vulnerabilities in BAY States. Self-organized and government-led movement of people, (new displacements and returns) have constrained development of durable WASH solutions as the outlook constantly changes. On the other hand, protracted displacement is straining host communities because of the high pressure on the existing, already-overburdened water points and sanitation facilities.

Access to sanitation is fragile from wear and tear of emergency-type construction, and seasonal flooding. WASH needs in the Yobe and Borno states entail water supply in form of deep boreholes, sanitation and hygiene sensitization. WASH NFIs are also part of the humanitarian needs especially for the population affected and displaced by floods in Yobe states. Low sanitation access raises rates of open defecation and reduced handwashing elevates the risk of a major outbreak within the susceptible community. A critical gap for the sector is sanitation for persons with special needs, women and children to ensure safety and equitable access; solving these issues of proximity and design of the facilities is likely to require additional resources OCHA, 2021. Effects of extreme weather conditions have worsened the situation.

project_name: Integrated response to emergency needs in WASH, Child Protection, FSL and NFI-Shelter Health and Protection for recently displaced populations and other disaster-affected people in Sudan – FSL
project_objective:
This is a complex 6-month intervention that aims to Improve the food security and livelihoods for war-affected populations through various areas in Darfur, Khartoum and Jazeera. 3 months into the conflict, the total estimate of IDPs across Sudan reached 2.6 million. The critical needs of 5,855,848 IDPs and 1,532,350 mixed cross borders movements (Dec 2023, IOM) add onto those of 25M overall identified by OCHA. 
Considering the inconceivable suffering of the Sudanese population, TGH have coordinated its efforts to present cash assistance to support the war-affected population in Darfur, Khartoum and Jazeera, as they are the most affected states since the beginning of the conflict in Sudan.  
Newly displaced and conflict affected households are unable to meet basic needs for survival. Displacement and conflict result in both the immediate loss of households’ livelihoods and an inability to meet basic needs; it also affects individuals’ ability to regain their livelihood and access income. Economic decline across the country and high food prices resulted in conflict affected households having little cash to cover their food and other needs.  
In line with the revised HRP strategic objective 1 (SO1), TGH believes the provision of MPCA is a timely multi-cluster (multi-sectoral) life-saving form of assistance. The use of MPCA as a response modality has been proven across the Horn of Africa to reduce the use of negative coping strategies and contributes to the mitigation of protection risks in support of the revised HRP strategic objective (SO2) on protection.
Multipurpose cash interventions play a crucial role in addressing immediate food needs by enabling beneficiaries to purchase nutritious food items from local markets. Given challenges with in-kind distributions and the setting up of commodity supply routes – partners propose cash and market support as the preferred modality to address food insecurity and access to basic non-food items.  
TGH plans to conduct distribution of unconditional food assistance through Cash Based Transfers to contribute to the reduction in mortality and morbidity for food insecure households through unrestricted cash assistance. Unconditional Food Assistance will be targeted at the most affected populations and meant to cover emergency needs on a short-term basis. Where conditions allow, cash will be the preferred method for the delivery of Unconditional Food Assistance based on the rapid needs and market assessments. The program will provide targeted households (HH) with 100% of the required 2,100 kilocalories per person per HH per month for a period of 3 months. This is equivalent to 68% of the Cash Working Groups’ Minimum Expenditure Basket (Local Food Basket) for food related item. As of September 2023, the amount was set at 20,000 SDG per individual per month. TGH will cover 3 months of LFB value during the lean period (June – August 2024). In the HPC sheet, the unit cost has been revised taking into account recent exchange rate (63,8 USD per capita for 3 months + 9% of transfer fees = 69.5 USD) but will be updated as conditions on the ground change and in line with CWG recommendations. TGH will also rely on CWG methodology for beneficiaries’ identification, selection and verification. At inception, consortium partners will sensitize the targeted community by sharing information about the objective and methodology of the action. TGH will adopt community-based targeting, targeting HH identified by the community as most impacted by the conflict, food insecure and who are not receiving any other assistance. Once the beneficiary list is finalized, it will then be presented to the community for validation. Any individuals not considered to meet the criteria will be discussed and replaced with the participation of the community.TGH will conduct verification of beneficiaries to ensure they meet the target criteria.Targeted beneficiaries will receive 3 rounds of assistance for the peak of the lean period.

project_name: Provision of In-kind food assistance to most vulnerable Palestine refugees in Syria
project_objective:
As Syria enters its thirteenth year of crisis, the 438,000 Palestine refugees face socio-economic challenges, heightening their vulnerability. Addressing their needs is crucial for UNRWA, focusing on food assistance amid the deepening crisis. Of these refugees, 60% have experienced displacement, enduring the impact of broader macro-economic and social conditions, including growing scarcity of food and financial resources.
The 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) underscores the severity of the ongoing political, economic, and humanitarian crises in Syria, placing an additional burden on Palestine refugees, an already vulnerable group. An October 2023 post-distribution monitoring (PDM) survey highlighted distressing trends: 92% of households resorted to borrowing food or seeking help, 64% had to cut daily meals due to financial constraints, and 40% adopted emergency livelihood strategies, including begging (4%) and selling challenging-to-recover assets (36%). These indicators underscore the diminishing ability of refugee households to cope with increasing poverty.
The vulnerability of Palestine refugees deepened in February 2023 with earthquakes compounding their challenges. UNRWA health records revealed a nearly doubled number of patients accessing Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) in earthquake-affected areas from February to June 2023, emphasizing elevated trauma levels. The earthquake displaced an additional 1,511 households, adding to the 40% already in protracted displacement due to the Syrian conflict.
In-kind food assistance remains a crucial intervention to safeguard the resilience of the most vulnerable Palestine refugees. UNRWA's 2024 plan adopts a more targeted approach, focusing on providing in-kind food assistance to 155,500 of the most vulnerable groups. This selection process adheres to the Agency's two-tier targeting approach, prioritizing female-headed households, families led by individuals with disabilities, families led by older persons, and unaccompanied minors or orphans. The food ration for one person includes essential items like flour, rice, pasta, and sardines…etc, procured internationally or locally, depending on price competitiveness and timely availability. UNRWA's distribution strategy ensures efficient delivery through its distribution centers in targeted governorates.
Monitoring and Evaluation are assured through regular field visits, feedback from implementing staff, and the dedicated Area Support Team and SFO-based Programme Support Team. The UNRWA PSO's Monitoring and Evaluation system closely follows up on and provides feedback and donor reports for all projects. The Multipurpose Cash (MPC) component, with a reduced transfer value, complements the in-kind food assistance program, recognizing potential fund unavailability. UNRWA's commitment extends to mobilizing resources for the four planned distribution rounds, one each quarter, contingent on fund availability. The comprehensive approach integrates not only food assistance but also multipurpose cash assistance and protection interventions, ensuring a coordinated effort across different sectors. The in-kind food assistance program stands out as a crucial form of UNRWA's emergency support, stabilizing food security for Palestine refugees in Syria, reducing humanitarian needs, and mitigating escalating levels of food insecurity.

project_name: Renforcer l'accès des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive dans les zones humanitaire du Mali
project_objective:
Le projet vise à réduire la mortalité maternelle, améliorer la santé intégrale de femmes et filles à travers une approche intégrée des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive tout en prévenant et répondant aux violences sexuelles, y compris de santé mentale.
L’objectif global de ce projet est de renforcer l’accès aux services de santé sexuelle et reproductive y compris la prise en charge des violence sexuelles dans les localités les plus touchées par la crise humanitaire. Ce projet cadre parfaitement avec les objectifs globaux du plan de réponse humanitaire 2024 du Mali. Il vient donc en appui pour l’atteinte de deux objectifs stratégiques à savoir :
1. Assurer une offre de soins de qualité à toutes les personnes affectées par la crise.
2. Améliorer l’accès inclusif, opportun et adapté aux services de base de qualité des personnes affectées par les chocs récurrents selon les droits fondamentaux et les standards.
Les principaux axes d'interventions sont les suivants : 
	Accroître l'accès des personnes vulnérables à des services vitaux de SSR et de prise en charges de violence sexuelle y compris la santé mentale ;
	Faciliter la coordination inter-agences en matière de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) dans les zones humanitaires y compris la gestion de l’information sûre et éthique ;
	Promouvoir la mobilisation et l’engagement communautaire pour l’utilisation des services SSR/VBG.

project_name: Amélioration de l'accès et de la continuité des soins et services de Santé Sexuelle et Reproductive et de Violences Basées sur le Genre dans les régions prioritaires de la réponse humanitaire (Centre-Nord, Sahel, Nord, Est, Boucle du Mouhoun et Centre-Est) au Burkina Faso
project_objective:
L'aggravation de la situation sécuritaire affecte profondément l'accès des populations vulnérables, en particulier les femmes et les filles, aux soins obstétricaux et néonatals d'urgence et aux services cliniques de prise en charge des viols. Elle limite également la capacité des personnes affectées (surtout les femmes et les jeunes adolescents qui restent sexuellement actifs) à accéder aux services qui contribuent à réduire la transmission du VIH, à prévenir les grossesses non désirées et les avortements clandestins. Selon le rapport du ministère de la Santé datant du 31 Octobre 2023, 18,8% des formations sanitaires de 10 régions du Burkina Faso sont fermées et 17,99 fonctionnent à minima. Cette situation affecte 3 628 202 personnes qui sont privées de soins et/ou qui ont un problème d’accès continu à l’offre de santé sexuelle et reproductive.
L’analyse de la mortalité maternelle et périnatale de janvier à Novembre 2023 montre que ce sont les régions humanitaires qui payent le plus lourd tribu (en dehors des centres de référence).
La réponse actuelle apportée dans le cadre de la prévention et de la lutte contre la VBG ne couvre pas les besoins en termes de prise en charge multisectorielle. Le système manque de façon criarde de structures adéquates pour une prise en charge holistique des survivantes. En effet, le volet réinsertion socio-économique des personnes survivantes de VBG est insuffisant dans l’ensemble des régions humanitaires. Quant à la prise en charge médicale, elle suscite parfois des frais qui ne sont pas toujours à la portée des personnes survivantes et l’accès précoce aux soins est faible. En effet 58% des personnes survivants sont vues après les s72h et 39% ne bénéficient d’aucune prise en charge médicale (AoR VBG)
Au regard de ce qui précède, les défis majeurs demeurent : (i) l’insuffisance de mesures de prévention des décès maternels évitables ; (ii) les difficultés pour les acteurs d'assister certaines survivant(e)s liées à la réduction de l'espace humanitaire ; (iii) la faible disponibilité des services sociaux de base (santé, éducation) du fait de la situation sécuritaire ; (iv) la faible couverture des six régions humanitaires en services de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG. Pour faire face à ces défis, les interventions du projet seront axées sur une approche globale et intégrée qui tient compte des éléments structurels et des identités sociales qui comprennent et intègrent pleinement le caractère indivisible des droits humains. 
L’objectif général du projet est d’améliorer l’accès des femmes en âge de procréer, des adolescent-e-s et des jeunes aux services de SR/VBG de qualité dans les six (6) régions humanitaires.  De façon spécifique, il s’agit de : (i) Améliorer l’offre de service de SSR dans les six régions prioritaires de la réponse humanitaire ; (ii) Renforcer les capacités des structures pour assurer la prise en charge holistique des personnes survivantes de VBG ; (iii) Renforcer l’engagement communautaire sur les questions de SSR et de VBG  en développant des actions novatrices de plaidoyer impliquant les hommes à travers la stratégie de masculinité positive et (iv) Assurer la coordination et la capitalisation des interventions du projet.

project_name: Protection of Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh and Strengthening of Community Self-Reliance and Cohesion
project_objective: UNHCR delivers comprehensive protection services in Cox’s Bazar and ensures the centrality of protection through protection and gender mainstreaming, inclusive coordination and leadership of the humanitarian response. In 2024, UNHCR will continue to work with the Government to secure identity and documentation for Rohingya refugees through continuous registration, which will serve as the keystone for protection interventions, assistance delivery and solutions planning. UNHCR will also strengthen its community-based protection approach, which provides the foundation for age, gender and diversity responsive services. UNHCR’s response will deliver integrated protection services including registration and documentation, legal protection, and community-based protection. UNHCR will conduct protection monitoring in all 33 camps to identify protection incidents/trends to support advocacy and address protection gaps, identify and assist refugees facing urgent and serious protection concerns and facilitate multisectoral referrals. UNHCR will strengthen access to justice through the capacity building of law enforcement/justice sector actors, strengthening of legal assistance activities (through its partners) in all 33 camps, including outreach and legal awareness to eliminate barriers for all persons of different ages, genders and specific needs, legal counselling, legal assistance and representation, and mediation support. UNHCR will empower Rohingya refugees by strengthening community capacities for leadership, self-management and engagement in 33 camps, including through elected refugee representatives in four camps. UNHCR will support refugee volunteer networks such as Community Outreach Members (COMs), community groups, religious networks (including imams and female religious teachers) and sports for protection clubs. COMs will identify and support persons with specific needs, and will mobilize communities for protection. Male and female community groups, including youth groups, will deliver community initiatives that foster community self-reliance and social change. Communication with communities will be mainstreamed. Community and information centres will also act as essential hubs to disseminate timely, accurate and life-saving information. UNHCR will strengthen disability inclusion in all its protection interventions as well as provide targeted services for persons with disabilities. Within the current Government policy framework, UNHCR will advocate for greater access to age, gender and diversity (AGD) responsive education and economic inclusion, so that young refugees retain hope and become agents for positive change in the community. UNHCR’s solutions strategy takes into account the Government’s policy that voluntary repatriation is the only feasible solution for Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, and promotes the conditions needed for voluntary, safe, dignified and sustainable return in Myanmar. UNHCR will work to improve protection conditions and quality of life for refugees in Bangladesh pending solutions, building upon the framework for responsibility sharing provided by the Global Compact on Refugees (GCR). As reinforcing accountable Government leadership of the response will build a foundation for the inclusion of refugees in the national systems in the future, UNHCR will continue to support the capacity development of both Government and humanitarian actors across its operations.

project_name: GBV prevention, risk mitigation and response service provision for the Rohingya refugee response
project_objective: The project aims to (1) improve the quality, accessibility, and inclusion of response services for GBV survivors, especially linkages between case management, MHPSS, medical care, self-reliance, educational, and legal services for the most vulnerable groups; (2) mitigate the risk of GBV and PSEA through multi-level and cross-sectoral strategies, including capacity building and community-led (especially by women and girls) initiatives and; (3) prevent GBV by motivating significant changes in social norms undergirding violence, systematic discrimination, and gender and age inequalities through structured and evidence-based programs. Highly vulnerable and underserved populations will be targeted, such as people with disabilities and gender-diverse populations. UNHCR and partners work based on community, right-based, and survivor-centered approaches, engaging refugees as active agents and emerging leaders within their communities and during individual case management. We will increase women and girls’ participation in decision-making and leadership by building their confidence and capacities with skills-building and vocational training sessions, engaging female refugees of all ages in our community-based protection work, and involving men and boys as allies in promoting gender equality. Key components of the 2024 GBV programming include improving the quality of safe spaces, delivering life, vocational skills, and continuous MHPSS, enhancing community volunteers’ capacities on how to work with people with disabilities and GDP, engaging men in accountable practices, encouraging women-led initiatives, and delivering women’s leadership training to make them empowered to make their own life decisions. Considering the recent trends and the exponential increase in GBV incidents due to the security situation in the camps and the impact of the cuts on food and NFIs delivered to refugees, UNHCR and IPs will continue to provide case management and specialized MHPSS to survivors with particular attention to strengthening the survivor-centered care practices within the multi-sectoral referral network and increasing accessibility for and capacity to serve target populations, gender, and age-wide. A more integrated approach to GBV response services is prioritized to streamline our services and improve free access. Capacity-building components include caseworkers’ minimum training package on case management and IASC Minimum standards. GBV risks will be mitigated through a three-tiered strategy: (i) working with the community, (ii) UNHCR multi-functional, and (iii) inter-agency levels. Community-level work will include GBV risk mapping and the generation of risk mitigation measures by refugee women/girls, with community GBV risk mitigation actions. UNHCR’s multi-functional work will develop GBV risk mitigation action plans across functional units, using safety audit tools to assess and measure GBV potential risks. Finally, the inter-agency work will be done in collaboration with other agencies to mainstream GBV risk mitigation across all eight sectors in the Rohingya humanitarian response and an initiative for protecting refugees from SEA. UNHCR and its partners will implement structured and evidence-based GBV prevention activities that take a whole-of-society approach (SASA! Together) and those that target specific groups (Girl Shine, EMAP, Male Role Models). Programs promote the centrality of protection and AGD approach. Despite UNHCR mainly focusing on the refugee camps, we are also present in 5 Host Community areas, Thaingkhali, Whykong, Leda, Ukhyia, and Cox's Bazar, implementing and assisting the most vulnerable groups at 5 GBV and health facilities dedicated to LGBTI individuals, sex workers, and extremely vulnerable adolescents (EVA) at risk, as per sector strategy. These facilities are managed by Bandhu as UNHCR IP and work based on an inclusive perspective, delivering unique services to refugees and members of the host community.

project_name: Protection of Rohingya refugee children in Bangladesh
project_objective: The project aims to deliver child protection services and longer-term protection solutions (i.e., durable solutions) to 182,105 Rohingya refugee children (89,063 girls; 93,041 boys) in 16 camps and 30,717 host community children (15,017 girls and 15,700 boys) in six host community sites in Bangladesh, comprising a total of 212,822 children (104,080 girls; 108,741 boys). The programme includes case management, structured and sustained psychosocial support, strengthened community-based child protection structures, child protection recreational activities, life skills for adolescents, positive parenting, system strengthening and capacity building for child protection and non-child protection partners, and the operation of facilities and safe spaces. Activities and facilities are designed and implemented using a community-based approach and considering gender equality, AGD and disability inclusion to ensure that vulnerable children can access services. Community-led initiatives will be supported according to the needs identified by community members. Children, adolescents and youth will be engaged in designing, implementing, monitoring and evaluating child protection prevention and response activities for their community with the aim of strengthening resilience and fostering a spirit of development. A special initiative will be implemented in coordination with the local authorities and community, especially adolescent girls, to support efforts to tackle child labour and child marriage. UNHCR will uphold core guiding principles and protection standards, AAP and PSEA to guide its interventions to ensure adherence to national standards and quality of services. Child protection interventions will consider disaster risk reduction (DRR) measures to prevent recurrent disaster risks occurring due to cyclones, landslides, fires and floods. Child protection case management services will respond to incidents of abuse, neglect, exploitation and violence towards children. Structured and sustained psycho-social support (PSS), including child protection recreational activities, will be provided to children at risk. Evidence-based approaches will be applied to strengthen children’s own knowledge, skills and capacities for self-protection, and those of their parents and families.  In coordination with the Child Protection Sub-Sector (CPSS) and partners, the existing Community-Based Child Protection Mechanism will be provided with technical and material support in identifying solutions to address the protection needs of children. UNHCR will enhance its coordination and partnership with different humanitarian actors to raise awareness amongst community members, volunteers and social workers on child protection prevention, mitigation and response through the provision of capacity building for the purpose of mainstreaming the best interest procedure (BIP) and child safeguarding. In collaboration and coordination with the CPSS, UNHCR will improve the quality of services provided to targeted children, particularly with regard to case management and child protection intervention systems by enhancing the capacity of partners, target communities and Government through trainings. Positive parenting sessions will reinforce the capacity of parents to care for their children. Structured curricula life skills, GBV awareness, adolescent engagement, social cohesion and peaceful co-existence sessions will be delivered to support adolescents and youth. Early Childhood Development (ECD) activities will be initiated and supported, with linkages made with child protection activities to tackle Adverse Childhood Experiences. UNHCR will work closely with the Government, including but limited to the justice systems, Department of Social Services, Office of the RRRC and Ministry of Women and Children Affairs to coordinate interventions such as safety and security, legal protection, case management and protection coordination.

project_name: Enhancing access and efficiency of comprehensive quality healthcare services for Rohingya refugees and surrounding host communities in Cox's Bazar District
project_objective: Based on the “Minimum Package of Essential Health Services for Primary Healthcare Facilities in Refugee/FDMN camps, Cox’s Bazar” and the “Standard Operating Procedure for Patient Referrals to Secondary and Tertiary Healthcare Facilities for Refugees/FDMNs, Cox’s Bazar,” the project will offer primary and secondary healthcare services to refugees and the host communities in the surrounding areas in Cox’s Bazar. The project will be aligned with the 2022–2024 Cox's Bazar Health Sector Strategic Plan. A total of 10 primary healthcare centers (PHC), two health posts and give drop-in centres serving the key and gender-diverse demographics will all provide services as part of the project. One specialized hospital in Ukhiya for service delivery will be incorporated into the project and handed over to the Government. PHCs situated in the camp will include two in-patient mental health facilities to provide care to severe mental health cases. Persons with disabilities (PWDs) and the elderly will be able to access health facilities with accompanied referrals from supported households. PWDs will receive services tailored to meet their needs, including access to appropriate equipment. Primary healthcare facilities will provide and incorporate mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS). New evidence-based psychological counseling methodologies will be implemented at the community level. Care will be more locally accessible through trained para counselors and community psychosocial volunteers from the community. Strengthening integration of MHPSS with WASH, nutrition, protection, GBV and other sectors is planned. The project will cover the cost of referrals of emergency cases from UNHCR’s areas of operations, in addition to ambulances for its partners. A robust community health system will ensure disease surveillance, early detection, and response to health hazards such as diseases with epidemic potential, as well as health promotion which will contribute to community resilience. Through the coordination of the Community Health Working Group (CHWG), partners in the response will ensure harmonized community-based health interventions. The CHWG will also provide toolkits, IEC materials and capacity building for community health workers (CHWs). As part of the project, one infectious disease treatment center (IDTC) will remain on standby at Ukhiya Specialized Hospital to support case management of outbreak prone diseases. Stockpiling of medicines and medical supplies and support to emergency medical teams will be ensured. During monthly facility-based health forums where the community has the opportunity to provide feedback, the project will incorporate refugees in the provision of service delivery. Camp health focal points will continue to collaborate with different camp actors to plan activities at the camp level and offer support supervision to health services offered in the camps and healthcare facilities, which will be achieved through utilizing existing UNHCR and Health Sector monitoring tools. Monitoring of performance through age and gender-disaggregated data collection and analysis systems e.g., the community-based health information system, UNHCR integrated refugee health information system (irHIS), compliance with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s (MOHFW) District Health Information Systems -2 and the health sector’s 4Ws, Early Warning Alert and Response System etc. will be undertaken and data used to generate evidence to guide interventions. The project will coordinate with the Health Sector and all associated working groups such as the working groups for sexual and reproductive health (SRH), epidemiology and MHPSS, as well as the Emergency Preparedness and Response Committee. Integration of services with other sectors will continue, aiming for partners to implement integrated health and nutrition services by the end of 2025. Integration will be fostered with the WASH, protection and GBV sectors.

project_objective: El proyecto de respuesta a emergencias en WASH presentado por UNICEF, atenderá las necesidades inmediatas en municipios afectados por la variabilidad climática; así como el fenómeno de la movilidad humana, ateniendo al menos 10,000 personas en los departamentos de Usulután y San Vicente. La intervención está orientada a brindar servicios de WASH equitativos, protectores y resilientes al clima; asegurar agua para consumo humano, higiene personal, cocina, limpieza y otros usos; apoyar el acceso a servicios sanitarios seguros, protectores y dignos, y opciones para el tratamiento de aguas residuales; promover la instalación de puntos de lavado de  manos con agua segura y jabón; apoyar la provisión de servicios de agua y saneamiento en instituciones que garanticen servicios esenciales de salud, educación, protección; la dotación de Insumos de higiene personal que estén adaptados a los diferentes géneros, edades y condiciones de discapacidad, movilidad, albergue u otros; y a promover la educación para el riesgo y cambio de comportamiento para llevar a cabo buenas prácticas de higiene, manejo del agua, manejo de los desechos sólidos, excretas y otros relacionados con WASH. Con estas acciones se pretender generar resiliencia comuntiaria y reducir el riesgo a contraer enfermedades transmitidas por el agua, vectores e inadecuadas prácticas higiénicas.

project_name: Continuidad educativa en ambientes seguros, protectores e inclusivos para niñas, niños y adolescentes afectados por la emergencia.
project_objective:
UNICEF, a partir de muchas experiencias, sabe que las situaciones de emergencia y crisis humanitarias afectan los sistemas educativos; las redes sociales y los sistemas de apoyo que normalmente protegen a las niñas, niños y adolescentes se ven afectados y muchas veces por tiempos prolongados, dejándolos fuera de los ambientes protectores. Es por esta razón que la respuesta de educación en emergencias debe ser inmediata para tratar de restaurar en lo posible la normalidad en las vidas de las niñas, niños y adolescentes y atender su derecho a la educación y recreación. Las intervenciones están enfocadas en la reapertura de los ambientes de aprendizaje seguros e inclusivos  para la recuperación socioemocional y educativa. 
Con el proyecto, de 7 meses de duración, se pretende instalar 54 ambientes temporales para el aprendizaje y/o centros educativos, al equiparlos con materiales lúdicos, educativos y mobiliario, con el fin de brindar los primeros auxilios psicológicos y el fortalecimiento de los aprendizajes básicos de lectoescritura y matemática.
En estos ambientes, al menos 5600 niñas, niños y adolescentes afectados por la emergencia, reciben atención psicosocial y atención educativa, fortalecimiento de sus habilidades básicas de aprendizaje.
El monto total del proyecto es de $ $532,667

project_name: Intervención humanitaria de WASH para población migrante en tránsito por Guatemala en los departamentos de Izabal y San Marcos.
project_objective:
El proyecto se centra en brindar asistencia humanitaria para abordar las necesidades urgentes de WASH (Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene) en la población migrante en ruta a Norteamérica. Las acciones se realizarán en los municipios de Puerto Barrios y Ayutla de los departamentos de Izabal y San Marcos, respectivamente. Esta población en movilidad en el trayecto de entrada y salida del país requieren el uso de servicios de agua y saneamiento, así también de insumos para satisfacer sus necesidades de higiene. En consecuencia, HELVETAS enfocara la respuesta de manera urgente en estos sitios fronterizos con los grupos de población más vulnerables, que incluyen, niños, niñas, mujeres adolescentes y mujeres adultas, atendiendo a 18,000 personas en total. 
HELVETAS proveerá de insumos y suministros, particularmente de kits de higiene diferenciados por género y edad, agua para consumo y habilitación o mejora de las facilidades que proveen de agua y saneamiento en sitios de acogida de esta población vulnerable. 
Se coordinará y complementará esfuerzos y actividades con diferentes instancias como autoridades municipales y departamentales, la Coordinadora Nacional para la Reducción de Desastres (CONRED), Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MSPAS), agencias de las Naciones Unidas entre otras organizaciones.

project_name: Garantizar la supervivencia de niñas y niños con desnutrición aguda a través de identificación y tratamiento oportuno y del cuidado nutricional y salud integral materno infantil en Huehuetenango, Chiquimula, Alta Verapaz y San Marcos, Guatemala
project_objective:
El aumento de la inseguridad alimentaria y nutricional ha aumentado en las diversas regiones de Guatemala, debido a la sequía que ha reducido las reservas de granos y elevado los precios de la canasta básica alimentaria. Además, las condiciones de El Niño previstas a continuar en el 2024 exacerbarán las brechas preexistentes, lo cual afecta en la nutrición de las niñas, niños y mujeres. Durante el año 2023, se identificó el incremento sostenido de niñas y niños menores de 5 años con desnutrición aguda, el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social reportó para la semana epidemiológica 50 (10 al 16 de diciembre de 2023) un total de 25,237 casos de desnutrición aguda, representando el 26% de incremento respecto al año anterior lo cual, pone en riesgo la vida de miles de niñas y niños menores de 5 años. Los departamentos de Alta Verapaz, Huehuetenango, San Marcos y Chiquimula son afectados por inseguridad alimentaria (Fase 3 y 4 de la CIF) y desnutrición crónica y aguda, donde la proporción de casos de desnutrición aguda severa se encuentra entre el 21 al 26% de los casos totales reportados, incluyendo casos de desnutrición aguda por signos clínicos, la expresión más grave de la desnutrición: Marasmo y Kwashiorkor, lo cual incrementa el riesgo de muerte por esta causa.

Para asegurar la supervivencia de los más vulnerables, se implementará la identificación y tratamiento oportuno de la desnutrición aguda en niñas y niños menores de 5 años, además de acciones integrales de atención nutricional y salud a través de "Brigadas integrales" en las comunidades más lejanas y rurales con acceso de los servicios de salud es limitado. La Estrategia ha sido validada y efectiva como respuesta de nutrición en emergencias desde el 2018, ha logrado identificar y tratar oportunamente a niñas y niños afectados por desnutrición aguda que no habían sido detectados previamente por salud (hasta un 68%). Este abordaje es estandarizado, el cual proporciona atención integral a la niñez (evaluación nutricional, tratamiento oportuno, suplementación con micronutrientes múltiples en polvo, zinc y vitamina A, desparasitación, consejería en temas relacionados a la alimentación del lactante y niño pequeño y vacunación) y a las mujeres en edad fértil, con énfasis en adolescentes, embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (evaluación nutricional, suplementación con hierro y ácido fólico, consejería y vacunación). 

Las Brigadas además, capacitarán a "agentes de cambio" (líderes y lideresas formados en competencias necesarias para la identificación oportuna de desnutrición aguda, signos de peligro y prácticas de alimentación e higiene infantil)  en su comunidad de tal forma que los casos de desnutrición aguda se detecten tempranamente y puedan referir inmediatamente para brindar tratamiento y salvar la vida.  

El proyecto responde a los siguientes objetivos:
- Identificar a la población afectada por bajo peso, desnutrición aguda y otras deficiencias nutricionales para su tratamiento oportuno.
- Brindar atención integral para resguardar la salud de la población afectada
- Brindar competencias al personal de salud y líderes comunitarios para la detección temprana y referencia oportuna de personas afectadas con desnutrición aguda o con complicaciones asociadas al embarazo, parto y post parto para su pronta referencia.

project_name: Espacios de Aprendizaje protectores e innovadores para la infancia en movilidad humana, retorno y desplazamiento por violencia
project_objective:
En lo que va del año 2023 se ha evidenciado el notable aumento del tránsito migratorio por la frontera Su-oriente de Honduras en relación a 2022. Según las cifras oficiales del Gobierno de Honduras, entre el 1 de enero y el 31 de septiembre de 2023, ingresaron más 545,000 personas sin documentación formal al país. Esta situación está teniendo un impacto significativo en todos los países de la región centroamericana, lo que ha implicado la adopción de diferentes medidas por parte de los Gobiernos de la región.  La magnitud de este fenómeno migratorio también se refleja en las cifras del Servicio Nacional de Migración de Panamá, que dan cuenta de cinetos de miles de migrantes habían ingresado en el país a través de la selva del Darién en el años 2023, un promedio de 1,491 personas por día, lo que supone un récord sin precedentes. En este contexto, el 26 de septiembre de 2023 Costa Rica emitió una declaración de emergencia nacional en respuesta al incremento de personas en movimiento a través de su territorio. La mayor prevalencia de nacionalidades reportada en los últimos 6 meses es de Venezuela, Haití, Ecuador, Perú y se está incrementando las nacionalidades asiáticas y africanas. Esta situación ha incidido en el incremento de los flujos migratorios masivos mixtos en la frontera Suroriente aumentando la demanda de servicios desde la perspectiva humanitaria.

Beneficiar a NNA en vulnerabilidad, movilidad humana, desplazados por la violencia y en la frontera sur oriente del país, a través de entrega de kit educativo, a NNA en movilidad humana, en detalle el proceso de educación está compuesta por: i) habilitación de centros de descanso temporal donde se facultan espacios de aprendizaje con acompañamiento de facilitadores educativos en los Municipios de Danlí y Trojes, con actividades de promoción educativa en lógica matemática con hojas de trabajo, incentivar la lectura con las bibliotecas móviles, promoción del arte y la música en espacios amigables como actividades lúdicas de esparcimiento; ii) entrega de textos “Mi cuaderno viajero” elaborados para NNA en flujos migratorios; iii) la preparación de herramientas digitales como el Pasaporte de aprendizaje en respuesta a atención integral para brindar atención educativa durante su estadía en el país.

Para la población de retorno y desplazamiento interno se utilizará la metología de reingreso y nivelación educativa de puentes educativos, que es una estrategia para la prevención de la violencia, la Re-vinculación, nivelación, de los aprendizajes de los NNA migrantes retornados, los que han abandonado el sistema educativo, NNA en rezago escolar(sobreedad), o de aquellos NNA que están en potencial peligro de abandono de la escuela. (sobreedad). La estrategia responde a la reincorporación de las niñas, niños y adolescentes entre los 6 y 17 años que permanecen fuera del sistema educativo, respetando las vivencias a las que han sido expuestos y reconociéndose el derecho a educarse en la diversidad. 

Se conformarán equipos de Educación integrados con los equipos de Protección, siguiendo la guía metodológica de espacios educativos para la niñez en movilidad. En esta fase se continuará con el fortalecimiento de la estrategia de abordaje en Trojes y en Danlí, Francisco Morazán y Ocotepeque centrada en el crear Espacios Educativos Protectores e innovadores que incluye el uso de Pasaporte de Aprendizaje para NNA en movilidad e implementar las nuevas actividades incluidas en LP creadas específicamente para adolescentes. Se promoverán los cursos rápidos ágiles para el desarrollo de capacidades asegurando la conectividad a internet así como la disponibilidad de dispositivos móviles para que NNA tengan fácil acceso al menú de contenidos de Pasaporte de Aprendizaje. De igual manera se trabajará en coordinación con la Secretaría de Educación de Honduras (SEDUC) para garantizar el seguimiento y el cumplimiento de los indicadores establecidos.

project_name: Asistencia Humanitaria en Servicios de Nutricion a niñas, niños menores de cinco años y cuidadores de menores de dos años Inmigrante y en transito, en Honduras
project_objective:
La emergencia migratoria por Centro America se ha vista incrementada en los ultimos años y en Honduras el flujo migratorio  ha venido incrementando desde abril 2021. En marzo y abril 2022 el departamento de Danlí y Trojes fueron declarado en emergencia migratoria por la magnitud de flujo de población en tránsito. Para el año 2023 el Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM) ha reportado el ingreso de 545,043 inmigrantes, en comparación con 188, 858 reportado para  el año 2022. De los cuales alrededor de 47,000 son niños y niñas menores de 10 años y de estos el 30% lo representan los menores de cinco años. A raíz de esto se ha aumentado la demanda de servicios básicos, en especial de salud y nutrición, que no pueden ser cubiertos por instituciones del Estado. Los albergues que en su mayoría son administrados por la sociedad civil e iglesias, cuentan con las mínimas condiciones en temas de seguridad alimentaria, salud y nutrición, lo que puede originar que el estado nutricional de los niños y niñas, lactantes y embarazadas se agrave. Surge la necesidad de la intervención para contribuir a la reducción, morbilidad y mortalidad de niños y niñas inmigrantes y en tránsito, que se ven afectados por las pobres condiciones en temas de nutrición.
El  proyecto tiene como objetivo evitar el deterioro nutricional y la mortalidad  de niños niñas, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes, que durante la ruta migratoria se ven afectados al  no tener acceso a alimentos nutritivos ni a micronutrientes que ayuden a evitar las carencias nutricionales, y por ende contribuyan a debilitar su sistema inmune, la intervención  se enfocara en: 

Manejo ambulatorio, tratamiento y atención de la desnutrición aguda en niñas y niños inmigrantes y en transito, menores de cinco años.

Fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal institucional de salud de las zonas de intervención por medio de formaciones sobre el uso de  un protocolo de recuperación nutricional en contextos de emergencia (utilización de cintas para medición del perimetro braqueal MUAC)

Suplementación con micronutrientes a mujeres embarazadas y lactantes inmigrantes y en transito para prevenir las carencias por micronutrientes.

Proporcionar suplementos a base de lipidos  como ración de protección a todo niño y niña menores de cinco años inmigrantes y en transito, para evitar el riesgo de desnutrición aguda durante la ruta migratoria. Asi como una ración fresca que complemente los requrimientos proteíco caloricos diarios requeridos.

Sensibilización a cuidadores primarios de niños y niñas menores de 2 años,  sobre sobre alimentación del lactante y del niño pequeño.

El proyecto prevé alcanzar 17,500 NNs menores de 5 años (aproximadamente 8,715 niñas y 8,785 niños), y 2,500 mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia inmigrantes y en transito por Honduras, así como 1,000 hombres con las actividades de prevención, atención y promoción de las buenas prácticas de alimentación del lactante, del niño/a pequeño/a y de las mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia. Aunque el número de hombres cuidadores no se refleja en la meta general del proyecto, si se refleja en la población meta de uno de los indicadores como parte de las intervenciones.

project_name: Contribution to Increasing the resilience of affected communities by providing livelihoods and job opportunities
project_objective:
Reports from humanitarian actors indicate that financial insecurity, caused by an increasing unemployment rate and unstable, low wages, has had a detrimental effect on purchasing power. Furthermore, droughts, water scarcity, and limited energy supply have complicated people's ability to meet immediate food needs and sustain their livelihoods. The decline in agricultural production over the past two seasons has made it imperative to prioritize support for the agriculture and agri-food sectors, aiming to enhance food production and improve food security for the population.
Additionally, the situation is exacerbated by climate change, as the country has experienced record-high droughts resulting in a significant decrease in cereals' biomass. Wheat, in particular, has been severely impacted, with estimates suggesting that the drought will leave Syria 1.5-1.7 million tonnes short of its domestic wheat needs in 2022. Certain practices, such as subsidizing irrigation for strategic crops and supporting fuel prices, have also contributed negatively to the water crisis by promoting excessive water pumping and groundwater depletion issues.
The linkage of input subsidies to fixed centralized purchase prices and the energy crisis have also had detrimental effects on crop production, resulting in inefficiencies, reduced returns for farmers, and the emergence of informal market dynamics. The energy crisis has escalated production costs, impacted food storage and transportation, and hindered agricultural productivity.
All of these factors have severely hindered the sustainable functioning of food systems and value chains throughout the country. Producers are unable to restore their full productive capacity as they are compelled to prioritize immediate daily needs, leading to unsustainable practices and the utilization of saline underground water, exacerbating land salinization and agricultural land loss. Sanctions, import restrictions, exchange rates, and high inflation have forced producers to rely on limited availability and high-priced local agriculture inputs of low quality, which often prove unsuitable for the new climate conditions. 
Market functionality is low, and market demand is affected by high food prices, inactive credit institutions, and a heavily regulated environment. In areas with returning populations, the absence of social cohesion and mutual trust makes it difficult to establish local trade networks, share information, or engage in collective action for livelihoods. Employment and income-generating opportunities are limited, and income levels fail to meet expenditure needs. While the number of women working as daily laborers has increased, the gender pay gap persists in both urban and rural contexts.
To address the identified needs based on the recommendations of the early recovery sector, Oxfam has decided to focus on providing livelihoods and job opportunities for the most vulnerable households affected by the crisis. Supporting the resumption of economic activity should involve assisting local shops and businesses by linking them with value chain assessments for different agricultural goods and conducting labor market assessments related to the selected value chains. Furthermore, vocational training, business support, smart grants, and on-the-job opportunities should be provided along the selected value chain to enhance skills and improve economic prospects for the affected population.

Oxfam has skilled staff to implement the project, increase the skills of target beneficiaries, and provide the necessary capacity building for the target group to enable an increase in their income and economic security, based on market and value chain assessments. A risk assessment will be conducted before the start of the project to understand the preferences of the beneficiaries, delivery mechanisms, potential risks, and mitigation measures.
