project_name: Projet de Sécurisation des Ressources des Ménages vulnérables  dans la commune de Chetimarie /Région de Diffa
project_objective:
La Région de Diffa est une zone à vocation agro pastorale par excellence. Elle dispose d’énormes potentialités afin d’assurer sa propre souveraineté alimentaire (terres irrigables, un important capital bétail, ressources en eau, main d’œuvre, etc.). 
 Les communautés ont essentiellement des sources de revenus fondés sur l’agriculture de subsistance. Cependant, depuis la sécheresse de 2012 qui a touché les pays du sahel, les communautés de la zone d’intervention n’ont pas véritablement pu reconstituer leur potentiel de survie. Les campagnes hivernales qui ont suivi n’ont pas apporté de réponses efficaces au problème de retard de croissance des enfants de moins de 5 ans. Les pratiques culturales ne répondent pas convenablement aux attentes des ménages vulnérables. Ces derniers sont en effet obligés de faire le salariat agricole  pendant la période de culture pour pourvoir subvenir aux besoins alimentaires de leurs ménages au lieu de travailler dans leur propre champs. De toutes les façons, cette agriculture de subsistance sur laquelle repose l’espoir de tous les ménages reste le plus souvent confrontés aux caprices et défis du climat. Il faut souligner que les actions que compte impulser le projet  mettent l’accent sur des activités plus résilientes. En effet, les actions du projet tablent également sur la durabilité en faisant la promotion des activités qui renforcent les stratégies d’adaptation des ménages notamment l’introduction du moringa qui est déterminante dans la lutte contre les conséquences de la malnutrition et la lutte contre la paupérisation des ménages. Le choix du groupe cible reste sans doute motivé par le fait que les femmes et les enfants sont les plus touchés par les situations couplées de crises d'insécurités et alimentaires que connaissent les département  presque chaque année. Les attaques des groupes armées et la réduction des moyens d’existence poussent les hommes à partir en exode vers la Libye et l’extrême Est du Nigeria en laissant derrière eux femmes et enfants dans des besoins énormes. Les femmes n’ont pas assez de pouvoirs économiques pour supporter la charge du ménage. Les actions du projet notamment pour les transferts de Cash ,CFW et les AGR visent à apporter un soutien substantiel aux femmes et de facto aux enfants de moins de 5 ans de ces ménages vulnérables. Le soutien en semences de qualité va aider également le ménage dans son ensemble à mieux renforcer sa stratégie d’adaptation. L’introduction de la culture de moringa et les  Jardins Potagers du Ménage touchent directement les femmes car leurs permettant de produire de la feuille de moringa qui a une valeur nutritive démontrée par les scientifiques mais également produire des légumes avec les Key Hole Garden pour soutenir l’alimentation de tout le ménage. le projet  prévoit également la culture de case pour aider les ménages vulnérables à produire du gombo pour renforcer l’économie du ménage.
Au vue de tout ce qui précède que le projet qui concerne 15 000 participants, vise à contribuer à la réduction de l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations les plus vulnérables dans le département de Chétimari, Région de Diffa. Plus spécifiquement, il vise à augmenter la production alimentaire et les revenus des ménages vulnérables et à améliorer leur résilience face aux  changements climatiques.

project_name: Improved access to quality Nutrition - through innovative approaches - for women and children in Damboa and Dikwa LGAs, Borno State.
project_objective:
LABDI is a women led organization, having a strong presence in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states with over 8 years’ experience working with at risk groups, vulnerable persons, community structures, community groups, internally displaced persons, returnees and host communities and government through the implementation of child protection, WASH, Nutrition, Education, GBV programs. LABDI have successfully implemented humanitarian and developmental projects which activities include Explosive ordnance risk education, establishing and strengthening community structures, case management, Advocacy, Campaign and awareness, Nutrition programs, WASH, working with women and caregivers, programs for in school and out of school children, youth sessions, psychosocial support activities for children and parents as well as other community impacted activities. LABDI is a key partner of GBVAOR, Mine Action WG, Education In Emergency WG, WASH, Nutrition (SAG NNGO forum co-chair), and is a leading member with the Borno Women led civil society organizations (Chair), BAY network of women led CSO and CPAOR SAG (coordinator). LABDI implementation works through community-based approach which ensures community active participation in project and enhances ownership and sustainability of project.
Through this project, in Damboa and Dikwa LGAs of Borno State, LABDI proposes to provide holistic care for malnourished pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, and their children in targeted supplementary feeding programs through community-based platforms and using macro and micronutrient-rich foods that will be entirely sourced from the community. LABDI will establish a robust network of Community Care Groups (CCG) which will serve as the primary platform for nutrition service delivery, provision of quality messaging on optimum maternal and child nutrition, in addition to enhance linkage to other sectoral interventions. LABDI will engage and train community health workers (CHW) to provide technical and operational support to these groups. LABDI will also prioritize mothers and caregivers of underweight (low weight-for-age) or wasted (low weight-for-height) 1-5 months old infants as well as mothers and infants with breastfeeding difficulties for intensified, needs based MIYCN support; as thee groups of children, if not catered for, would translate to become part of the caseload of acute malnutrition once they turn 6 months. To achieve significant impact from this MIYCN intervention, LABDI will engage and train ‘’MIYCN Promoters’’ (IYCF-P) whose goal is to ensure needs based MIYCN support is provided to the above stated groups, based on their needs. Another crucial role of the IYCF-Ps would be consistent growth monitoring of these children to closely watch the progress of the children and their caregivers. LABDI will engage and train a team of Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMS) to conduct house-to-house screening of the mid-upper arm circumference of pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls (PBWG), and children 6-59months to identify and enroll those who are malnourished in care groups. The CNMs and health workers will also carry out anthropometric assessment (WFA and WFH) of children 0-5 months to identify undernourished (underweight or wasted) children to enroll their caregivers for intensified and needs-based MIYCN support.  
Thrice during the life cycle of the project, LABDI will conduct mass MUAC screening for PBWG and children 6-59 months old to identify and enroll them into TSFP. In the same vein, LABDI will carry out mass WFH and WFA screening of under-6 children to identify undernourished infants and refer them and their caregiver for intensified feeding support either in stabilization centers or in community care groups.  
It is intended that LABDI will engage beneficiaries in backyard gardening activities and train them in various livelihood-enhancing skills, including gardening.

project_name: Support the delivery of critical lifesaving emergency Nutrition Services to vulnerable population in Twic, Renk, Kaje Koji and Ulang Counties South Sudan
project_objective:
This project is seeking to respond to the critical integrated lifesaving, Nutrition, health and food security needs of the IDPs, returnees and host communities in Renk, Twic and Ulang Counties in Upper Nile  and Warrap States targeting a total of  103,985( Renk= 7,772,  Ulang=  19,659 and Twic = 76,554) 

Beneficiaries. Of these total targets MAM under 5= 48,163 and MAM PLW= 32,745 and SAM under-five 23,078. All three counties have a GAM rate above the WHO 15% percent thresh hold (Renk= 25.1%, Ulang= 26.4% and Twic 25.3%. all three counties are categorized as IPC phase 4.  The main objective is proving critical lifesaving nutrition support to vulnerable populations including women and children with a specific focus on  reducing malnutrition prevalence rates amongst children 6-59 months and pregnant women (PLWs) 

This will be implemented by GOAL as an integrated package of the Nutrition, health, and the Food security and livelihood interventions. This will contribute to the over objective of the nutrition sector, is aligned with the South Sudan ministry of health strategi plan. This project is seeking to create a nexus between emergency, transition, and sustainable nutrition outcomes. 

The proposed response aligns with the HRP 2024 priorities for Nutrition food security and livelihoods, and health cluster. 

Strategies and the interventions will meet both immediate and lifesaving needs among affected populations while strengthening local capacity to deliver high quality service and 

contributing to reducing dependencies on food assistance as well as fostering longer term behavior change outcome. 

 

GOAL currently have nutrition grants in Renk, Ulang and Twic and is seeking to build on those to reach more facilities with an integrated package of interventions that will help to address the root causes of undernutrition. The plan is to integrate our health interventions in the same area. GOAL will undertake formative research to help inform its intervention and improve the impact.  

This project will be implemented in all Payams in the Ulang, Renk, Twic and Kajo keji Counties targeting all the payams. 

 

 GOAL is going to work closely with the County Health Departments in all counties and their respective State Ministry of Health making sure the capacity of these institutions is built as part of the system building resilient and sustainability. Key activities will include providing integrated preventive and curative nutrition services targeting the most vulnerable groups including responding to severe and moderate acute malnutrition and improving maternal infant and young child feeding practices. leverage on support of other sectors to provide a package that is not only cost effective but also high impact.

project_name: Provision of integrated basic life-saving WASH services to disaster affected and at risk communities of Aweil East, Aweil South, Fangak, Uror, Duk and Twic of Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Jonglei and Warrap States respectively.
project_objective: Action Against Hunger in this 2024 project concept proposes to extensively provide contextualized interventions to the targeted Counties within its' 3 operational States. These Counties include; Aweil East, Aweil South, Fangak, Uror, Duk and Twic of Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Jonglei and Warrap States respectively. The interventions are aligned to the WASH cluster strategic plan focusing on the 3 key sectoral cluster objectives as well as inter-sectoral objective of; 1. Well, Being Reduce Morbidity and Mortality, 2. Basic Services Provide safe, equitable and dignified access to services, 3. Build resilience. Action Against hunger intends to carry on with ensuring integration of with its' nutrition sector within the organization especially as a result of the Nutrition cluster rationalization of one county, one partner according to our recently completed mapping of nutrition sites and WASH facilities/service status in the above mentioned and targeted Counties, focus will be to ensure provision of comprehensive WASH services at facility and community level. among the proposed activities are; rehabilitation of non-functional water points of all types, drilling of new deep wells especially in our nutrition sites, carry on with ensuring, disability friendly sanitation facilities within our sites are constructed, supporting women with dignity/menstrual hygiene kits targeting SAM/MAM caregivers, conduct participatory hygiene awareness involving affected communities to ensure best hygiene practices. with the continues influx of returnees, transiting refugees as well as displaced persons due to Sudan crisis, floods and sporadic inter-communal conflict such as in Warrap state, Action Against Hunger will ensure, WASH facilities are provided in consultation with women, girls and the disabled to mitigate GBV linked to access to WASH services/facilities. In some of the location particular Aweil East, Twic, Aweil South and Fangak, Action Against Hunger will use cash modality for provision of WASH non-food items tapping in from the expertise within the organization on the ongoing ECHO CCD supported cash project. Prior to engaging in this activity, market assessment of basic and essential communities will be conducted including financial risks and measures put in place to mitigate.

project_name: Provide an  Integrated  life-saving response   access to safe  drinking water, sanitation and hygiene services with nutrition and GVB  mitigation activities  for IDPs,host and returnees  people affected by conflicts, flood, diseases and malnutrition in  Panyikang,Renk,Ayod,Nyirol,Canal /Pigi,Fangak and Nasir Counties
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to face multiple compounding shocks and stressors. Insecurity, sub-national violence, regional and national macroeconomic challenges – intensified by the global economic downturn, the impact of climate change and the ongoing Sudan conflict – all adversely affect the food security of South Sudanese families.
 As of 16 October, 317,993 people have been recorded crossing into South Sudan from Sudan since the onset of the conflict in April. Overall, half of the arrivals are female and about half are children below the age of 18. South Sudanese returnees account for 88.5 per cent of all arrivals. (Situation Report OCHA No. 16 as of 20 October 2023)
The main purpose of this proposed intervention is to establish basic hygiene standards and provide clean water to the affected populations impacted by emergencies-women, men, girls and boys, especially IDPs, IDPs returning to their place of origin or chosen place of return, returnees and vulnerable persons in areas affected by conflict, natural disasters; alongside nutrition emergency responses or in areas with outbreaks of waterborne diseases.
 The intervention will be achieved by integrating WASH with nutrition and community level through distribution of WASH NFI kits to SAM/caretakers children paired with hygiene promotion, rehabilitation/construction of water sources at nutrition and at community level, rehabilitation/construction of permanent and semi-permanent latrines and conduct safety audit at site level to identify GBV concerns for latrines and water points.
 This intervention WASH proposed will target 60,000 beneficiaries in Fangak, Canal/Pigi.Nasir, Renk,  Nyirol, Nasir  and Ayod is anticipated to cost USD 1,980,000 that include returnees, IDPS and host communities  about 72211 beneficiaries and secured 20%  mainly Fangak County  County  
As of 3rd September according to IOM report more than 253,023 persons   were registered crossing the border into South Sudan since the fighting in Sudan erupted on 15 April. The Sudan conflict prompted an escalation in the cost of commodities, including food, particularly in the counties neighboring Sudan consequently diminishing the purchasing power of the population. In August, according to UNHCR, more than 22,000 South Sudanese refugees² returned spontaneously to South Sudan through eight official entry points from Gambella, Ethiopia, citing the lack of access to basic services, livelihood opportunities and insecurity in the Gambella region as reasons for return.

project_name: Strengthening the provision of integrated lifesaving primary health care services for the vulnerable communities of Mayendit and Guit Counties of Unity State and Manyo and Fashoda Counties, Upper Nile State
project_objective:
CASS will be directly targeting about 108,836 people. Children under 5 years are 18,502 children (9,795 boys and 8,707 girls), children above 5 years to 18 years of age are 40,269 children (18,502 boys and 21,767 girls) and adult 18 years above to 60 years are 37,004 people (17,414 men and 19,590 women) and persons 60 years and above are 13,060 people (3,265 men and 9,735 women). Among them are 2,176 persons with disability (1,175 males and 1001 women).
CASS will conduct 78,867 consultations in static facilities/mobile clinics, facilitate 4,353 normal deliveries attended by skilled birth attendants, submit 52 timely and weekly EWARS/IDSR reports from each of the 4 focus Counties, facilitate 11,500 children (5,920 boys and 5,520 girls) with 3 doses of PENTA-3 vaccine, provide maternal healthcare services to 4,353 women of child bearing age of IDPs, returnees and host community including FP , ANC, PNC, IPT 1 and 2, de-worming and TT immunization, provide child healthcare services (routine immunization, Vit A supplementation and child growth monitoring) to 16,734 children (7,815 girls and 8,919 boys), including accelerated mass measles and polio campaigns and provide psychiatric treatment and psychosocial support to 175 mentally ill persons 
In addition, CASS will provide community-based level 2 and level 3 (non- specialized) MHPSS to 11,200 persons living with disabilities (PLWD's), including referrals for specialized services from other partners, manage 8,300 uncomplicated diarrhea cases with ORS and Zinc, 14,700 uncomplicated malaria cases with ACT and 7,800 uncomplicated respiratory infection (pneumonia) treated with Amoxicillin. About 78,867 people will reached with health education and promotion to prevent disease outbreaks and awareness raising community engagements on GBV prevention, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, drug abuse, peace building and peaceful coexistence.
CASS will conduct 12 monthly community meetings in each target county to provide accountability to the communities (AAP strategy), screen 11,500 pregnant women, lactating mother and children under 5s for malnutrition and refer them to for treatment/management, facilitate 12 monthly joint supportive supervision visits to increase quality of services, strengthen linkages with Boma Health Initiatives (Boma Health Workers) for community-based disease surveillance and referral, provide care to physical injuries and CMR including level 2 and level 3 MHPSS to survivors of GBV, provide active epidemic disease surveillance, prevention and control including outbreak detection, investigation and respond within 48 hours including ensuring IPC in health facilities through regular assessment using score cards, provision of supplies and protocols and continuous monitoring of WASH in 31 target health facilities and capacity building of front-line health workers.

project_name: Provision of Emergency Health Interventions to the vulnerable Population (IDPs, returnees and the host community) in Nasir ,Fashoda and Ulang Counties Upper Nile State South Sudan
project_objective:
Provision of Emergency Health Interventions to the vulnerable Population (IDPs, returnees and the host community) project will focus on the major causes of morbidity and mortality in Nasir, Fashoda and Ulang. It will improve access to integrated basic health care and avert excess morbidity and mortality among 41,913 women, children and men. The project targets the most vulnerable population whose right to access health care services is in jeopardy following the continued inter-communal violence, floods, the Covid 19 pandemic and crisis in Sudan (Khartoum) and Ethiopian, Gambella. Of the targeted 37,022 people; there will be 6,917 host community, 6,253 IDPs, and 23,852 returnees respectively. The breakdown according to gender , age and disability is reflected below. 9.33% of the targeted will be people with disabilities translating to 3,910 individuals.

Children under five years  6,762  ( Males - 3608;  Females - 3,177 )
Children Five to 17 years  14,124 ( Males - 7,065; Females - 7,059 )
Adults  18 to 60 Years       13,715 ( Males - 6,871; Females - 6,845 )
Adults over 60 years          2,421  ( Males - 984;   Females  - 1,438 )

The project will support provision of critical lifesaving interventions aligned to the Humanitarian Response Plan criteria and the South Sudan Basic Package of Health and Nutrition through a network of 26 PHCUs, 12 PHCCs, 2 Hospitals and 8 mobile clinics in hard to reach locations. The project activities will focus on prevention and case management of epidemic-prone diseases such as malaria, pneumonia, acute watery diarrhoea, cholera, and measles through both static and outreach services; provision of essential medicines and medical supplies accessed through the core pipeline; capacity building of staffs through on-job mentorship, disease surveillance including EVD and COVID 19, and routine monitoring of health information through strengthening the EWARS/DHIS2 system.
The clinical package will include; Health education and promotion, curative outpatient and inpatient services, routine immunization including supplementary immunization activities focusing on measles and polio, Maternal New-born and Child Health Services (MNCH), and HIV/TB services including e-MTCT. The project will integrate Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) at PHCCs and Hospital; management of severe cases of malnutrition with medical complication at the stabilisation centres; identification, and referral for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS); and Water Hygiene and Sanitation (WASH) at health facilities.
This project will contribute to addressing the needs of the 148,083 of the estimated 3.2 million women, children and men that will need basic essential health services in South Sudan in the year 2024 and hopefully contribute to a reduction in high maternal mortality rates (789 deaths per 100,000 live births) and under five mortality rates (90.7 deaths per 1,000 live births) in women and children and mitigate the transmission of vaccine preventable and other infectious diseases.

project_name: Emergency WASH Response to conflict and flood affected populations in Unity State
project_objective:
South Sudan's struggle with access to basic water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services stems from a chronic lack of investment in WASH infrastructure, recurring conflicts, and devastating floods that have left facilities in ruins. The WASH cluster estimates that out of the country's 12.44 million inhabitants, 8.5 million will require humanitarian assistance in 2024, with 5.5 million specifically targeted by the WASH cluster. Leer, Mayendit, Koch, and Rubkona in Unity state and Maiwut in Upper Nile state are among the worst-hit counties, facing a multitude of hazards that threaten to cripple their livelihoods. According to HNO 2023 (Inter-sectoral analysis), the limited access to WASH infrastructure coverage alone, such as water points and latrines, poses multisectoral impacts. The dire sanitation and water access conditions in the counties are expected to deteriorate further with the influx of returnee populations from the Sudan Crisis (OCHA Sudan Crisis-SITREP No. 16)

A recent Coalition for Humanity survey revealed that a staggering 73% of households in Leer and Mayendit already lack adequate sanitation facilities and resort to open defecation, a practice attributed to various factors. For instance, reconstruction of latrines is a constant struggle due to soil erosion and flooding, depleting household resources and energy. The market for affordable and durable sanitation facilities is underdeveloped, making it challenging for households to access suitable options. It is also evident that the absence of stable and sustainable livelihoods hinders households' ability to invest in latrine construction and maintenance which affects about 41% of households. Conflicts and acts of criminality have also led to the destruction of sanitation facilities, further exacerbating the sanitation crisis (Coalition for Humanity WASH KAP Survey June 2023)
Furthermore, 24% of households continue to source their drinking water directly from rivers and streams, exposing them to contamination and health risks. This highlights the urgent need for improved water infrastructure and access to clean water sources.
The proposed project will introduce several initiatives to enhance and save the lives of affected populations in the project area. These initiatives include the construction of flood-resistant latrines, the conversion of boreholes into solarized water yards in the community linked to nearby nutrition centers, the provision of life skills training to households, the distribution of WASH minimum kits for SAM and MAM cases, and the implementation of hygiene promotion campaigns across the project locations.
The project aligns seamlessly with the WASH cluster's strategic objectives and the Humanitarian Response Plan for 2024, which aim to
1.	Contribute to reducing prevalence of malnutrition through integration with nutrition at community level and integration with nutrition at facility level
2.	Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality through integration with health at both community and facility level (technical support).
3.	Provide access to basic WASH services in underserved locations affected by disaster-through delivery of services through static partners and mobile emergency response mechanism (EPR). 
4.	Disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility- through mainstreaming protection with a focus on GBV mitigation (safety audits) and disability inclusion. 
5.	Provide durable access to services in long-term IDP sites and communities chronically affected by disaster

project_name: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items Response to Returnees, Conflict-affected, and Flood-affected Populations in the Greater Upper Nile Counties
project_objective:
This project will focus on returnees from the Sudan crisis, IDPs, and resident communities in priority 1 counties (Rubkona and Leer) and priority 2 counties (Mayendit, Koch, Guit, and Panyijiar). As of November 12, 2023, UNHCR and IOM recorded 373,094 people crossing the border from Sudan into South Sudan. In the month of November alone, 19,314 people arrived, with an average of 1,609 people arriving daily (Humanitarian Updates Note, November 15, 2023). This situation is expected to worsen with the continued escalation of Crisis in Sudan. 
A recent assessment conducted by CH in October 2023 in Rotriak further revealed that among the thousands fleeing the conflict in Sudan are South Sudanese nationals returning through Panakuach, Unity state. Most of these returnees have settled in Rotriak because many villages in Unity are still flooded. Other returnees lacked the means for onward movement to other parts of the country, forcing them to settle in Rotriak with more than 90% currently seeking shelter beneath trees, with only a few having been integrated into IDP communities. Many of the makeshift shelters of IDP households are already totally or partially damaged, and some are sleeping in the open. Therefore, returnees settling in Rotriak without shelters have added to the number of people sleeping/living in the open, ultimately increasing the level of vulnerability in the community. Living conditions are continually deteriorating, particularly during this rainy season, when these temporary structures are further damaged. The absence of suitable shelter and essential non-food items, such as mosquito nets, continues to expose residents to diseases associated with harsh weather conditions like malaria. 
Coalition for Humanity (CH) will provide in-kind support for the construction of new shelters and the repair or rehabilitation of damaged shelters for returnees, IDPs, and residents living in camp-like settings. In locations with functioning markets, CH will conduct rapid market assessments and gather information from the Cash Working Group and the joint market monitoring initiatives (JMMI) led by REACH to determine appropriate cash-based modalities for those locations and determining the multi-sector survival minimum expenditure basket (MSSMEB).
CH anticipates a shift in its shelter programming approach and plans to incorporate locally sourced shelter solutions, with a particular consideration on environmental conservation. To mitigate potential housing, land, and property (HLP) cases, CH will conduct thorough due diligence, collaborate with relevant stakeholders, and integrate HLP training for returnees, IDPs, and resident communities in partnership with the appropriate authorities.

project_name: Beyond Zero Maternal and Child Deaths: Provision of Lifesaving Primary Healthcare and Reproductive Health Services to Persons Most in Need in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang Counties Through Primary Health Care Units and Mobile Clinics
project_objective:
According to the Health Cluster Response Plan for 2024, 8.9 million South Sudanese are in need of Humanitarian Aid, with 6.3 million among them requiring essential lifesaving healthcare services. Insecurity, long distances, limited healthcare supplies, inaccessibility of healthcare facilities and inadequate healthcare workers have disproportionately affected access to healthcare, especially among women and children. Unity State counties such as Leer, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijiar and Pariang have been adversely affected by these emergencies and currently lie in severity 4. 

In Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang, an estimated 405,576 persons are in need of emergency life saving healthcare. The rates of immunization are extremely low, malaria cases remain high, while acute watery and acute bloody diarrhea are endemic in multiple counties. Thousands of hepatitis cases have been reported due to a dire WASH situation, while infectious diseases such as COVID-19 continue spreading, with significant portions of the population depending on traditional healers as a coping mechanism.  
The proposed project shall extend primary health care and reproductive health services to vulnerable persons, including IDPs, returnees and host populations in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang. 

This project is in line with the health cluster objectives and the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan which seek to:
1. Improve equitable access to life-saving essential comprehensive quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations.
2. Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases.
3. Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms.
This project is targeting 45,400 beneficiaries and will support them with lifesaving emergency health care and reproductive healthcare services through 12 Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs), 3 Primary Health Care Centers and mobile clinics that CH has been supporting in the targeted counties. CH will work with the State Ministry of Health in Bentiu and the County Health Departments in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang, as well as the nutrition cluster for nutritional supplies to PHCCs, Protection and GBV sub cluster for reproductive health supplies and clinical management of rape, and the WASH cluster for WASH in health facilities. CH is a strong member of these clusters.
The project requires USD 1,100,000 to reach 45,400 vulnerable individuals in Leer, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijiar and Pariang.

project_name: Provision of ES/NFI and Multi-purpose cash assistance for crises affected populations, IDPs, returnees and residents in Renk, Malakal, Meluth, New and Old Fangak, Pigi Canal, Nyirol, Ayod, Rubkona, Mayendit and Mayom counties of Upper Nile, Jonglei and Unity States respectively.
project_objective:
ADA -HRNP 2024 programming seek to address the needs of the highly vulnerable populations affected by the prolonged crises in Unity, Upper Nile and Jongei States. ADA will provide timely life-saving and resilience-strengthening assistance to returnees, protracted and newly displaced IDPs, and residents through multi-sectoral Cash base and emergency shelter and non-food items interventions to holistically restore community dignity. 49% of this response will be channeled to protracted and newly displaced IDPs, 26% returnees and 25% most affected residents. The main focus and the target of this programing shall be women and children, elderly 60+, female headed household, single parents, child headed household and separated children, pregnant or lactating mothers, persons without community links and those who are living with severe sickness. ADA HRNP 2024 programing is anticipating to directly reach a total number of 14,500 HHs, approximately 87,000 individuals in Upper Nile, Jonglei and Unity States. ADA will target 3,000 HHs, 18,000 individuals in Renk for a period of 6 months, 1,500 HHs 9,000 individuals in Malakal and 1,000 HHs 6,000 individuals in Meluth, of Upper Nile State. ADA will also target 2,500 HHs 15,000 individuals in New and Old Fangak, 1,000 HHs 6,000 individuals in Pigi canal, 1,500 HHs 9,000 individuals in Nyirol, 900 HHs 5,400 in Ayod of Jonglei State, 1,500 HHs 9,000 individuals in Rubkona, 900 HHs 5,400 individuals in Mayendit, 700 HHs 4,200 individuals in Mayom of Unity State. The above mentioned counties are expected to be IPC 4 and IPC 5. ADA is already a static partner in the mentioned counties, it will be collaborating with other mobile partners in the same counties. Partners will include IOM on CCM responses, NRC protection, PAH for WASH, and MedAir for multi-sector interventions. In all cases, ADA will endeavor to provide interventions that would contribute to the cluster strategies and programming for the most vulnerable communities. Where a single-sector approach will be used, ADA will ensure integrating it with protection mainstreaming, Do No Harm principle will be the guiding principle in ADA activities, land housing, and property rights. ADA will ensure an inclusive engagement with all key stakeholders in the target areas and in all the programing. ADA will keenly adopt the cluster objective, of ensuring provision of timely and adequate access to safe and dignified emergency shelter and lifesaving NFIs to newly displaced people or populations with new vulnerabilities. Improve the living conditions of highly vulnerable protracted IDPs, returnees, and the host communities who are unable to meet their SNFI needs. Support the most vulnerable returnees, residents and IDPs access adequate durable housing options that will enable them self-recover and build resilience of affected population to recover from shocks. ADA in all her integrated responses will, aim at protection mainstreaming including the establishment of community social networks, conducting protection training to project committees to implement, and conducting mine risk awareness sessions through the committees to ensure the safety of the communities. ADA is having an active Cash base funding from CAFORD that aims to cover the needs of 3,000 individuals in Renk, and this funding will continue up February 2024. That amount to 15% of this HNRP and will contribute to and boost the resilience and improving the living conditions of the 87,000 affected populations through improved housing solutions. ADA, through a mobile and static approaches, will coordinate responses with the Cluster coordinator and SFPs and monitor both the single and multi-sector services through its static and roving teams to deep field locations in all its project areas.
The project will be implemented over a period of 6 and 12 months in all the 10 counties of Upper Nile, Jonglei and Unity States.

project_name: Provision of camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) services to internally displaced and returnee population in displacement and transit sites in Central Equatoria, Western Equatoria, Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Abyei, Unity, Upper Nile and Jonglei States in South Sudan.
project_objective:
Of the total estimated 2.2 million internally displaced people in South Sudan, as of October 2023 there are 897,205 individuals (162,019 HHs) living in 140 formal and informal IDP sites across the country. Self-settled, unplanned IDP sites are the least visible and most underserved, placing this already vulnerable population group at an even higher risk of exclusion from access to basic services. With the inclusion of the Phase 1 Sudan ERP into the 2024 HPC, an additional projected 400,000 people will require CCCM support to access immediate, life-saving services in the transit and reception centers. CCCM cluster estimates that up to 20% of the returnees from Sudan will settle in existing IDP sites across the country. 
The project will focus on assisting IDPs living in the most underserved sites, in locations prioritized by the CCCM Cluster, applying area-based, roving and mobile response approaches to reach informal sites, working through localized response and coordination structures that will allow access to hard-to-reach areas, identification of common needs among sites within a geographic proximity, where possible linking those site populations with existing, available services in the area. Mobile response will remain the emergency, time-bound modality to respond to new displacements. Mobile CCCM teams will work closely with identified local partners on the ground to build their capacity and ensure the sustainability of the response.
A key component of the project will be to support community-based structures to enhance participation in planning and decision-making, in particular seeking empowerment of communities. This will be done with a focus on vulnerable groups, PSNs and PWDs so that their views are received, and acknowledged and service delivery meets the specific needs of all groups. To this end, protection will be mainstreamed into all CCCM activities to respect and promote the rights of the most vulnerable. Site care and maintenance improvement projects will be implemented though community engagement and will be aimed at minimizing risks at site level.
UNHCR will put in place mechanisms to strengthen site/area level coordination and monitoring, improving the wellbeing of displaced populations whilst providing some level of dignity and equitability by promoting AAP. IDPs’ engagement in the delivery of services in an equal and needs-based manner will be possible through regular feedback and dissemination of information for example through community-based networks and complaints and feedback mechanisms. 
In line with the CCCM Cluster Strategy 2023-2025, UNHCR will leverage the pivotal role of CCCM, linking service providers, IDP and host communities, and government authorities, as catalyst for effective and sustainable solutions. In all locations, UNHCR will support the regular roll-out of the Comprehensive Site Profiling Tool, which makes available site-level information highly relevant for solutions programming, for a variety of partners across the HDP nexus. The project will also explore phase-out and transitional strategies for managed sites, advocate for, and support increased responsibility of the government in the management and administration of displacement sites. UNHCR and partners will ensure coordination for solutions for the IDPs in sites – this may include return, safe and dignified camp exit, go and see visits, community engagement and consultations, identification, and implementation of self-reliance activities in IDP sites, etc.
Additionally, UNHCR will continue to ensure static CCCM coverage at the transit and reception sites receiving new arrivals from Sudan. The project includes contingencies for the potential need for establishing a new high-capacity transit center. Minimum CCCM interventions in these locations will include activities corresponding to the HPC 2024 Strategic Objective 1, related to facilitating safe access to life-saving services and protection.

project_name: Improving the livelihoods of disaster affected persons (IDPS, refugees and vulnerable host communities households) through provision of agricultural inputs (vegetable, crop and fishing kits) to enhancing emergency and sustainable food production in priority locations across South Sudan.
project_objective:
According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) projection, in the lean season projection period from April to July 2024, the food security situation will deteriorate and an estimated 7.1 million people (56.3% of the population) will be severely food insecure (IPC Phase 3 or above). 79,000 people are likely to be in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe) while an estimated 2.34 million people are likely  to be in Phase 4 (Emergency). The project aims at addressing the food security and livelihood of the most affected people with chronic vulnerabilities worsened by frequent climate-related shocks (severe flooding and dry spells, the macro-economic crisis, conflict and insecurity. Assistance will help affected people to meet their immediate, medium and long-term food security needs of the target communities of IPC level 3,4 and 5. 

To ensure the target population recover from food insecurity and the disaster which occurred as a result of flood, conflict, insecurities and displacement, PAH will distribute agricultural inputs such as vegetables kits, staple seed kits and tools to the most vulnerable households as well as multi purpose cash assistance. In addition, PAH will conduct trainings and agricultural extension activities focusing on good agronomic practices, Integrated pest management, post-harvest management and market linkages (value-addition).
Extension workers will be trained as trainers for community farmers. This methodology ensures ownership and long-lasting effects, as the capacity of trainers stays within the community. PAH will introduce different irrigation methods including drip irrigation systems together with community training on their adequate and sustainable use to enhance the copying mechanism during the dry season. The extension workers will be trained on production of quality seed, seed testing, packaging, labelling, pricing, preservation of seeds from weather conditions like humidity and pests and proper storage. Special attention will be given to seed quality testing to ensure high quality of the seeds. 
Additionally, to traditional plots, PAH will encourage setting up small-scale vegetable gardens, which can be established at the Nutrition/Education sites. This facilitates planting and irrigation allows higher diet diversity and minimize SAM/MAM cases and support enrolling children to schools. 
Fishing has the potential to immediately address food security needs. It enables people to immediately harvest fish from the rivers and swamps in the areas. 
In the communities with access to functional markets and availability of cash programming, will be considered. The decision will be based on initial market and community assessments, considering cash vouchers/MPCA or cash for work. Food for asset (FFA) will be conducted in the areas where there are needs and local markets can support the project targeting the establishment of community structures and facilities like schools and infrastructures like community road projects and communal farms establishment.
Food for education and school feeding programme will be considered in the project areas where PAH carries food security and livelihood activities with seeds distribution and vegetable and cereal crops production. 
A holistic approach to addressing food security and livelihood, building resilience and long-lasting effects, PAH will integrate interventions with other sectors such as WASH, Nutrition, Education, Protection and S/NFI through combined hygiene and nutrition promotion in addition to screening and referral to nutrition partners on the ground. Education and health will be integrated through training of school hygiene clubs and school gardening and awareness at the schools, nutrition and health centers. Protection will be mainstreamed across all sectors and additional protection team will be supporting the communities.

project_name: Education Quality and Access Support in South Sudan
project_objective:
The current education situation in South Sudan is deeply concerning, with a multitude of challenges that hinder access to quality education. According to the HNO 2023 an estimate of 3.3 million people needs education services in South Sudan. United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) estimates 2.8 million children in South Sudan are currently out of school for the academic year 2023. This situation is exacerbated by the ongoing armed conflict and environmental crisis which has resulted in the overall need for 8.5 million people, the existing educational infrastructure is inadequate, with only 27% of schools having basic facilities, as reported by the World Bank. Additionally, there is a severe shortage of qualified teachers. A comprehensive approach is required to address these challenges. 
The proposed education project seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging innovative teaching methodologies and the power of technology to create inclusive and sustainable educational initiatives. By harnessing the potential of technology, we can bridge the gap in education provision, deliver high-quality instruction, and empower the children and youth of South Sudan to acquire the necessary skills for future success. Through this project, we aim to create a transformative learning environment that not only addresses immediate educational needs but also contributes to long-term resilience and development in South Sudan as well as informed program approaches through the availability of rigorous evidence and information. The project will target a total of 3,821 individuals including 100 (25F ,80M) teachers who will approximately support 3699 (1850F, 1849M) and 22(4F,18M) SMC and PTA members in Central Equatoria from Juba County as a priority severity 3 county by education cluster by and support responding to education cluster goal 1 and 2. The project will ensure all groups are reached including girls, boys, men, and women as well as children with disabilities (CwDs).

project_name: Ensuring safe and equitable provision of life-saving NFIs and appropriate emergency shelter for conflict and disaster affected returnees, refugees, IDPs and vulnerable host communities through resilience strategies and integrated response in South Sudan.
project_objective:
To respond to the needs, PAH will conduct short and long-term interventions across the country, both static and emergency especially in the areas where cross-sectoral needs are dire. Shelter/NFI projects may complement other responses and PAH will always work to ensure synergies with its own projects or other partners’ programs. PAH will use both in-kind (light and standard kits distribution) and CVA modalities to respond to emergency shelter and essential NFI needs for the newly displaced persons and the ones with vulnerability, returnees, and others living in conditions of high vulnerability in coordination with the protection team. PAH will strengthen its CVA interventions in 2024 to approximately 30% of the project. It will be implemented in areas of returns with functional and accessible markets. In-kind responses will be conducted through mobile and static teams in close coordination with cluster partners. PAH will use the established humanitarian hubs for logistic coordination, information centres, and organizing responses to reach remote locations. Where such a modality is not available PAH will use its own procurement and transportation solutions, especially for last-mile transportation. PAH plans to implement both static and mobile responses. Concerning the beneficiaries breakdown, while planning the responses PAH will follow OCHA population aggregation.
PAH is an experienced organization with a broad portfolio of Shelter/NFI projects successfully implemented across the country. In the provision of transitional and essential shelter kits, PAH and protection partners will conduct in-depth HLP rights analysis using the unified cluster tools/questionnaires in the areas of shelter construction.
Land tenure consultation meetings and Community sensitization meetings on HLP rights will be organized throughout the project cycle. Such meetings will result in identification and agreements on land ownership for the shelter construction and provision of essential shelter kits. Through the support of HLP focal point, UNHCR, IOM, and NRC (protection and HLP partners), the beneficiaries will be supported to obtain communal land tenure documents in order to avoid the risk of being forcibly evicted.
PAH will consider the formation of shelter committees in the areas of project implementation. The committee will include representatives from local authorities, traditional chiefs/elders, women, and youth to ensure equal rights and representation to every age and gender group. These committees will work throughout the project cycle to monitor the implementation progress and give complaints/feedback. Before the construction of any transitional shelter, PAH will require the beneficiary to provide proof of land ownership with legal documents with close consultation from local chiefs and the Ministry of Land and Housing especially from urban settlements to avoid escalation of land-related disputes.
In areas/plots of collective centers, PAH will sign agreements (MoUs) with the Ministry of Water and physical Infrastructures, Housing and Land utilization, and Land tenure/local authorities to guarantee a minimum period of land use to avoid eviction of beneficiaries. Wherever possible, PAH will a set follow-up strategy to support in identifying land ownership.
PAH will continue to identify HLP-related issues throughout the project phases among the affected population and do refer them to the HLP focal point and other stakeholders.
As part of flood resilience and sustainability of the project, PAH plans the construction of transitional and flood resilience shelters for both returnees and flood-affected population.
PAH implements multisector responses to ensure covering the diversified needs of affected population targeting 41,667 individuals.

project_name: Emergency Health Interventions for disaster affected populations in Bor South, Twic East, Duk, Pariang, Wau and Pibor Counties
project_objective:
This project will provide Integrated, lifesaving, emergency health interventions for populations affected by conflict, flood, disease outbreak and displacement, targeting a total of 168,057 people (82,348 Males and 85,709 Females). Out of these, 35,292 will be under the age of 5 years (17,293 Males and 17,999 Females) and 132,765 above the age of 5 years (65,055 Males and 67,710 Females). 6,722 will be Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW). 2,689 of those targeted will be people living with disability. 21,087 of those targeted will be IDPs (under-5 – 5,063 and above 5 – 16,024), and 36,581 of those targeted will be Returnees (under-5 – 9,056 and above 5 – 27,525).  The project will focus on women, girls, boys, and men among the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) , Returnees and host populations with limited or no access to health services. The project will ensure improved access to integrated emergency lifesaving healthcare services focusing on the major causes of morbidity and mortality for conflict-affected, flood-affected, and vulnerable IDPs, host community and returnee households in Bor South, Wau, Twic East, Pariang, Pibor, and Duk Counties. In addition, due to its geographical presence and health programming in Wau and Pibor Counties under the Health Pooled Fund funding, MOFA, and ECHO funding, CARE will have the capacity to provide emergency health interventions in the 2 counties (Wau, and Pibor) depending on the need and availability of funding. To address the identified health needs within the 5 counties, CARE will deliver a package of emergency and essential health services in line with the three 2024 Health Cluster Objectives as follows: 
(1)	Vulnerable people who experience multi-sectoral severity levels of 4 and 5 have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services to meet their basic needs.			
(2)	Vulnerable people are exposed to fewer protection threats and incidents, and those who are exposed have access to tailored, timely, appropriate services through integrated and inclusive humanitarian action.
(3)	Vulnerable people withstand and recover from shocks, have their resilience to shocks and stresses built, and seek solutions to displacement with respect to their rights.

project_name: Provision of basic WASH services to underserved communities affected by multiple hazards in Aweil East, Aweil South, Aweil North, and Pibor Counties.
project_objective:
The intervention ensures 31,740 beneficiaries have safe access to basic WASH services. The project intends to provide quality, gender-responsive services including safe water and sanitation facilities. The contribution cluster sectoral objectives will be achieved through the provision of safe water for drinking with climate-resilient structures, conducting water quality analysis, provision of climate-resilient sanitary facilities in emergencies, conducting hygiene/sanitation promotion campaigns, distribution of WASH NFI’s and conducting gender risk analysis (safety audits) to mitigate WASH related GBV. This will contribute to sectoral objective 4, minimizing exposure of vulnerable groups to protection threats and incidents, and those who are exposed have access to safe, tailored, timely, and dignified access to appropriate services through integrated and inclusive humanitarian action. The intervention contributes to WASH Cluster sectoral objective 3, which reduces community members’ exposure to environmental hazards through the construction of climate-resistant WASH infrastructure. This will build resilience and provide sustainable WASH services.
According to the HNO, 2023, an estimated 6.1 million people will need WASH services with only 3% under minimum, 4 % under stress, 56% under severe, 36% under extreme, and 1% under catastrophe. Aweil East, Aweil North and Aweil South Counties are classified under severe with 100,000 to 200,000 people in need of WASH services each County.  Pibor County is categorized under extreme with over 200,000 people, Pariang under Severe with 50,000 to 100,000 people and Aweil West is categorized under minimum stress with 25,000 to 50,000 people in need of WASH services respectively. The vulnerabilities have been exacerbated by high risks from a broad range of hazards: floods, water scarcity, extreme heat, wildfires, a medium earthquake risk, disease outbreaks, and an influx of returnees and refugees from Sudan. These have disrupted socio-economic systems and livelihoods. Recurring multi-faceted socio-economic impacts on people, including severe economic contractions, soaring in prices of basic commodities, and loss of livelihoods particularly in urban areas have increased protection risks and disrupted access to basic services. 
The project targets the host communities, IDPs, and Returnees. The total beneficiary figure is 31,740 people. They are disaggregated as follows 6,253 men, 6,348 women, 9,522 boys, and 9,617 girls. The beneficiary figures are inclusive of the persons with disabilities in the communities.

project_name: Integrated lifesaving nutrition assistance to conflict and flood-affected vulnerable populations in IDP camps and host communities of Koch and Rubkona Counties in South Sudan.
project_objective:
In September 2023, nearly 5.83 million people, 46 percent of the population, experienced high levels of acute food insecurity and classified as IPC Phase 3 or above (Crisis or worse) in South Sudan. Malnutrition continues to affect the well-being of women and children and is driven by flooding, economic crises associated with depreciation and high food prices, recurrent conflict, forced displacement, low agricultural production, and a reduction in humanitarian assistance. In Rubkona and Koch Counties, 116, 000 people are in emergency and 15,000 people are in famine. Among the people in famine, the majority, 14,000 South Sudanese returnees fled from the ongoing conflict in Sudan. As per the nutrition cluster update of September 2023, the number of SAM and MAM admissions has subsequently increased for five years from 608,584 to 758,914 in South Sudan with a 24% increment. 
Protracted shocks including three years of regional flooding have disrupted livelihoods and availability and access to food which has contributed greatly to food security deterioration at the household level. The severe flooding in Unity has impacted health and nutrition service provision in Koch and Rubkona, counties. At the WRSS field observation, various locations in Koch and Rubkona have been completely submerged in water while the rest remain under threat of being flooded, and communities continue to move to relatively dry highlands. Nutrition sites and WASH facilities in Koch and Rubkona counties have been damaged, and the rehabilitation of infrastructure is needed to continue providing life-saving services. 
WRSS will strengthen life-saving nutrition services and scale up the quality and coverage for community-based management of malnutrition (CMAM) by extending services to hard-to-reach areas and underserved communities. The project will target 87,228 children U5 with acute malnutrition as direct beneficiaries. 84,919 children will receive Vitamin A supplements and deworming tablets. 69,943 caregivers of children will be reached through Maternal and Infant Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) programs in outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) sites, as well as during nutrition outreach interventions in Koch and Rubkona counties. This project will establish three new outreach units in these counties to provide outreach nutrition services to communities with limited access to services due to displacement. In Rubkona and Koch Counties, WRSSR will be supporting 33 static nutrition centers, including three stabilization centers in Rubkona Hospital, Sector Two in Bentiu IDP camp, and Koch town. A gender-targeted and nutrition-sensitive service delivery approach will be used, and nutrition services will be integrated with WASH, health, gender and FSL programming through social mobilization on critical handwashing and food safety, prevention of GBV, cooking demonstrations using locally available food produced in the kitchen gardens. In addition, nutrition screening services will be implemented in the health facilities to ensure that all malnourished children are referred to nutrition centers. In the end, the project aims to reduce morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable children and women in these hard-to-access locations, while promoting and engaging in recovery and resilience activities in the community. Project activities will be monitored through supportive supervision done together with the County Health and Nutrition Department, the MOH, and UN Agencies. Activities will be monitored by nutrition project staff with support from the WRSS Juba office program team. Relevant reports will be shared with the nutrition cluster and other reporting partners. Community-based complaint and feedback mechanisms will be established within the nutrition centers and in the community to ensure accountability.

project_name: Strengthening health service provision to vulnerable communities in Fangak and Canal Pigi Counties in Jonglei State and Koch and Rubkona Counties in Unity State.
project_objective: The project aims to provide comprehensive quality health care services to crisis-affected people, prevent and respond to health threats, and strengthen the health system. This goal aligns with the the 2024 HRP’s (Humanitarian Response Plan) objectives of saving lives, reducing health risks, and enhancing coping and recovery. The project will use a multi-faceted approach to address the problems being faced in the health system. The project will address challenges from 3 sides, that is the health service delivery, community, and individual components. Health service delivery: WR will work with the State Ministry of Health (SMOH) to support and capacity build the CHD in project leadership, program implementation, supervision, and monitoring. WR, together with the CHDs, will recruit qualified frontline staff to work in the HFs and they will receive regular supportive supervision, on the job training, and mentorship, including trainings on BEmONC, IMNCI, family planning, clinical management of rape (CMR), EPI, IPC, PMTCT, and drug and laboratory management. Through the UNICEF and WHO supply pipeline also project contingency funds the project will ensure that there is consistent supply of medicines and supplies. The project will create a conducive environment through rehabilitation of existing infrastructure and construction of new semi-permanent and permanent structures. Furthermore, the project will strengthen safe motherhood package by ensuring that ANC, labour and delivery, PNC services are available 24/7 in all PHCCs being provided by competent health workers. EPI services will be provided at both static and outreach sites. The project will implement and strengthen integrated mobile outreaches to ensure that health services are brought to the people and no one is left behind. To ensure effective continued and consistent communication between referral centers, referral pathways will be strengthened through the provision of ambulances and communication means in both counties. PHCCs will be equipped to provide PMTCT/life-long ART services as well as functional gender-based violence (GBV) referral pathways. The project will reach 353 904 U5s with HF and community consultations whilst 707 808 Vitamin A supplementation doses will be provided to U5s. In addition, 22 586 children under 1 (U1) will be reached with DPT3 vaccination and 20,328 U1s with measles vaccination. A total of 88,477 U5s will be screened for malnutrition  and referred to Nutrition Centre. The project will also reach 31,620 pregnant and lactating women (PLW) with maternal, infant, and young child nutrition interventions and 141 159 women with safe family planning counselling. Community: With a focus on social behavior change, the project will intensify community awareness raising activities focusing on health service availability and utilization of health services. Various information dissemination methods will be used (IEC materials, radio channels, community meetings, etc.). Furthermore, the project will use promotional materials for ANC, Penta 3, PNC, and HF deliveries, motivating people to access health services. Promotional materials may include grocery hamper, t-shirt, and pads. The project will also train gender champions selected from the BHI and other community cadres to champion gender equality issues in the community, focusing on ending early child marriages and GBV as well as report GBV cases for timely management. Furthermore, community ownership will be created through engagement with key influential leaders so that they can lead in social behaviour change. Individual: The project will aim to build assertiveness of women and men to seek health services, through one on one engagement with community mentors. The Boma Health Committees will encourage equal gender representation to ensure equity in access of health services. To ensure comprehensiveness of services the project will be working WASH, Protection, Nutrition and FSL partners.

project_name: Provision of life saving nutrition services in Guit and Aweil North
project_objective: Concern will continue providing life-saving curative and preventative nutrition services in Aweil North County in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (NBeG) and Guit County in Unity state. In Aweil North, Concern will provide nutrition services across 22 sites and in Guit; Concern will provide nutrition services across 11 sites. The nutrition services include Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) for severely malnourished children 6-59 months.  The two Inpatient care services (SC) will provide inpatient care services for children 0-59 months, Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programme (TSFP) for children 6-59 months and Pregnant and Lactating women (PLW) and Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) services. Concern will use the national Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) approach and the national guideline. Concern will continue to promote the prevention of malnutrition through a combination of interventions including Social Behavior Change (SBC) through group sessions and individual counselling, promotion of home gardening, cooking demonstration and promotion of good hygiene practices. To ensure community participation and improve access and coverage, Concern will involve community volunteers for community mobilization, screening, follow up cases and dissemination of recommended nutrition behaviors. Concern will continue its success with pre-emptively reducing risks of malnutrition through supporting mother and father groups in improving MIYCN. The SBC curriculum mother/fathers groups promotes gender equality and male involvement in maternal and child nutrition and health. The nutrition service provision will be integrated with WASH, health, FSL and GBV interventions to achieve broader outcomes.  In 2024, in Aweil North County, the management of severe and moderate acute malnutrition will be integrated with the existing health services and CHD staff will be trained to treat acute malnutrition as part of BPHNS package. Concern, CHD and SMoH have signed a strategy on exiting from NGO direct nutrition service delivery to integrated health and nutrition service delivery. Concern will provide technical and logistical support to CHD/SMOH to carry out nutrition activities at the facility and this will support the national strategy of integrating nutrition with the health service delivery and ensure sustainability.

project_name: Emergency Food Security and Livelihoods Support Project for IDP, Returnee and Vulnerable Host Communities in Fashoda County - Upper Nile State.
project_objective: The aim of this project is to enhance and sustain emergency food production through provision of complementary and integrated agricultural crop and vegetable seeds, farming tools, fishing kits and agricultural extension support. The other objective of the project will be to reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks in a way that builds the resilience of households. It seeks to enable vulnerable IDPs and host communities to recover from crises, with a focus on seeking more durable solutions and building the capacity of communities to cope and withstand recurrent shocks and strengthen resilience to future shocks. It will build on interventions that CAFOD and its implementing partners Caritas Diocese of Malakal (CDoM). The communities have endured food insecurity caused by a complex interplay of climate variability induced factors such as cycles of droughts and floods. These have been compounded by intensified inter-ethnic conflict, livestock raiding and worsening economic situation across the country. This project will provide integrated streams of livelihood inputs including crop and vegetable seeds, farming tools including ox-ploughs as well as provision of fishing kits. The project will continue to support seed fairs to support local market where feasible, as informed by assessments that CAFOD and its partners will continue to carry out. This will be accompanied by a comprehensive farmer training package on sustainable agroecological farming practices and climate smart agriculture including soil and water conservation techniques. The project will be implemented through a network of farmer extension services using recruited and well trained and equipped community based extension workers. The project will also strengthen capacity of lead farmers. Seed selection, preservation and storage will also be supported to strengthen seed security. The training will also include improved fishing practices, hygienic handling of fish and fish preservation for fisher folk. The project will reach 12,000 individuals IDP, returnee and host communities) in Dethwok and Lul payams of Upper Nile State. The community will be involved in targeting and a clear vulnerability criteria will be agreed. As part of beneficiary selection CAFOD will also deploy its SADI (Safety, Access, Dignity and Inclusivity) Framework to ensure inclusion of vulnerable and often hard to reach groups such as female headed households, disabled and elderly persons. To realize the inclusion of persons with disability, the project will ensure that at least, 10 percent of the benefiting households have a person/s living with disabilities. The project will collaborate and work with other agencies working on Food Security and Livelihood intervention to achieve synergy and avoid duplication, utilize their expertise, work with health and nutrition actors and Ministry of Health to support households with malnutrition cases with a basket of interventions. This project will build on the previously implemented CTP projects in Fashoda and will address gaps not met on the current programming in Fashoda County

project_name: Provision of Integrated Protection Services for the people in needs in Unity, Upper Nile and Jongelie States.
project_objective:
This project targeting 113,080 people, 30,000 women 21,000 men, 38,950, boys ,and 23130 girls, and  is an integrated GP, GBV, CP and HLP aims at prevention and mitigating various protection risks through  provision of protection services for the conflict-affected population, returnees, and host communities through emergency mobile response to key entries point of Rotriak, Renk and Malakal, as well as protection that will informed MHA response  through static presence in Unity and Jongelei States respectively, and activities will includes; protection monitoring, Housing, land and property(HLP), CP/mine risk education Programming using community based approaches and accountability to the affected population, GBV services including creation of safe referral pathway, PSS in CFs WGFs  in all project locations as elaborated in the activities section.
Mobile Humanitarian Agency (MHA) will use the existing community-based structures as working with CBPNs at the community level throughout our programming proven to be the right approach to better understand various protection needs in the communities, and for the sustainability of the protection activities.
 
MHA will carry out routine protection monitoring to identify the potentials protection concern and will ensure involves the community in the all stages of the project design and implementation phases to have the true need and the priority from the beneficiaries themselves. 
MHA will work with the affected communities of returnees and IDPs in various location and assess their both in village and urban setting to assess their HLP related for immediate attention and response. In urban setting, MHA provide legal awareness session to the affected communities, provide legal assistance and legal aid to ensure IDPs and returnees have access to services including civil registration and are able to recover lost documents and property.

project_name: Increasing equitable access and utilization of quality Preventive Nutrition Service delivery and targeting (193,056) children & women in Jonglei and Unity states of South Sudan
project_objective:
The project will focus on  Increasing the equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services on prevention of acute malnutrition of children 6 -59 months of age and pregnant and lactating women of child bearing age (PLWs) and build resilience among young children, adolescents through behavior change communication  and micro-nutrient supplementation to boys & girls 6-23 months and Prevention of malnutrition through provision of BSFP to boys & girls 6 - 23 Months  including PLWs in Fangak Canal/Pigi, Leer, Rubkona, and Women, Men will  benefit from MIYCN Counseling focusing on social behavior change communication, improving households dietary intake children 6-59 months will be provided  with Vitamin A, (674 children 12-59month will benefit from deworming by the end of 2024

HFO project will contribute to the achievement of Nutrition Cluster strategic objectives for humanitarian response in 2024 by conducting community nutrition screening and  referrals of SAM/MAM cases children 6-59 months, support  children 6-23 months & PLWs during BSFP distribution, The project will coordinate meetings with IPs,CHD SMOH, and focuses on strengthening MIYCN Counseling, vitamin A supplementation and  deworming services and community outreach integrating with health and hygiene promotion, Distribution of WASH Kits, LLINT  during extensive community mobilization

1: To increase equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services to prevent malnutrition and build resilience among children, adolescents and women in prioritized locations by the end of 2024
4: To strengthen coordination & integrated programming with health, WASH, FSL, Education and Protection sectors for equitable access to services that address key drivers of malnutrition among vulnerable groups in prioritized locations by the end of 2024

The recruitment of community Nutrition workers, community nutrition volunteers and Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselors will be conducted in consultations with community members and local authority for their participation in the selection criteria by making sure local stakeholders are involved and gender balance is taken into account of getting workers from both males and females where necessary and including the people with disability. The nutrition response will be designed to ensure that Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) is a part at all stages of the response. HFO staff will continue to use the Nutrition Cluster and Global Nutrition Cluster operational framework on AAP that includes minimum and/or major key activities and indicators focused on participation, establishment of complaints and feedback mechanisms, transparency and communications, planning and implementation of nutrition responses as well as monitoring and reporting. The project response will promote a consultative approach by consulting a wider range of affected communities to ensure communities have simplicity and have their inputs on the objectives of the nutrition response, the activities, the locations, and their titles where the most affected groups are, and will consist of a package of treatment and prevention services delivered through the health facility/nutrition sites and through community outreaches, as per national BHNS with support from MtMSGs, CNVs integrated to EPI. This will be supported through an ongoing capacity building effort at facility and community levels, including community mobilization and engagement for participation. Hard-to-reach areas will be covered through outreaches services and Integrated packages of services with Health, Food Security, WASH, Protection, HFO will continue to report to NIS/5Ws activity-info.

project_name: Emergency Protection for Refugees, Returnees and Host Communities in Rubkona- Rotriak and Renk-North (Unity and Upper Nile) State,
project_objective:
The arms in Sudan has displaced large returnees and refugees to South Sudan. The conflict has brought large number of women, girls and boys and person with disabilities. Child malnutrition, women and girls and person with disabilities are in urgent needs of assistance in Rubkona and Renk counties as these county received large number home newly arriving women and children. DRI currently is  members of Strategic Advisory Group (SAG), with protection Cluster UNHCR, will respond to emerging emergency crises in Rubkona and Renk with assistance to returnees, refugees and host communities to provide timely situation through integrated approach develop harmonized key messaging informed by findings from the protection monitoring analysis such as, screening, provision of shelter, individual  protection assistance. DRI will used it solid protection assistance,  advocacy and lobbying, human rights and peace building strategy to deescalate tension among communities on GP conflict prevention, justices and rule of law, women and youth empowerment. The project is in -line with Cluster Strategic Objectives which emphasis the emergency assistance for Women, men, boys, girls, and other marginalized vulnerable groups such as persons with disabilities and to ensure mobile and static presence to promotes timely provision of critical protection assistance and services, including specialized response services, tailored to the specific needs, age, gender, and disabilities. The project will assist 19,659 beneficiaries disaggregated as (5,000 women, 3000 men, 5000 boys, and 5000 girls and 1659 PWDs) will be reached in Rubkona –Rotriak Payam and Renk county. Sectoral integrated GBV, GP, and CP confident centres for reporting while the project breakdown shall be as follow, GBV 30% GP 40%, CP20%,  and 10% PWDs.The project activities per the Cluster objectives below:
•	Through integrated approach develop harmonized key messaging that is also informed by the findings from the protection monitoring analysis
•	Working with communities of affected population and protection partners, develop key protection awareness raising messages and information on availability of services
•	Working with protection partners, develop and implement static or mobile activities targeted at identification and referral of PSNs, especially in emergency situations.
