•	Strengthening GBV awareness through house-to-house visit, focused group interventions, campaigns, and mass media  
•	Integrating Cash and Integrating Cash and Voucher Assistance into GBV program•	Integrating Cash and Voucher Assistance into GBV programming by working closely with Cash Working Group
•	Strengthening the reach and coverage of dignity kits distribution and programming
•	Strengthening specialized GBV response services ( GBV case management, referrals, legal aid,  safe ho
DRI will conduct interviews and groups discussions with the community members to share their reflections on protection issues, engagement strategy will include the provision of legal assistance to vulnerable groups on legal aid services, an awareness session on channel for resolution of disputed of cases and shall conduct routine follow up with authorities, providing feedback  communities, family and individual affected. DRI has robust protection of refuges, migrants and returnees and legal aid  protection through funding from  (UK-FCDO), USAID,  GP, Child Protection and rights documentation supported by USAID -IRC as lead agencies on Community Managing Conflict-CMC promoting GP, Peace and Human Rights, lands and borders disputes and human trafficking.

project_name: Provision of equitable access to gender and disability inclusive education for IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities children aged 3-18 years in Panyinjiar, Mayendit and Guit Counties of Unity State
project_objective:
The project will be primarily and directly targeting the enrollment of 6,638 children (3,452 boys and 3,186 girls) primary school from IDPs, Returnees and Host Community population. Among the direct beneficiaries are 332 children (173 boys and 159 girls) Children Living with Disabilities (CLwDs). Other secondary beneficiaries are 160 teachers (132 men and 28 women) supported with training and incentives, strengthening the capacity of 190 SMC members (90 men and 100 women). The project will be implemented in coordination with Health, Nutrition and WASH service providers for school-based health, nutrition and hygiene programming. The project will also mainstream protection for PSEA, schools safety audit, distribution of dignity kits and MHM training. The project will also involve FSL partners for school-based vegetable demonstration gardening for skill learning especially for adolescent girls. To increase community participation, the project will support monthly AAP community meetings for feedback responses and collective plans of actions and implementation. 
The project will establish 12 temporary learning spaces and classrooms including establishing 24 gender segregated latrines with water points for hand washing and distribute or provide sanitation and hygiene materials (hand washing soap, sanitizers, masks, etc.) and PPE for students and teachers. The project will support the distribution of recreational materials from the cluster pipeline to the 12 target schools and provide teaching and learning materials for ECD, primary, and secondary school education. Capacity strengthening will be provided by training of 160 teachers (132 men and 28 women) on EiE pedagogical skills and child-centered methodologies to improve teaching and learning process for emergency-affected children and train and update teachers on PSS, CP, and referral mechanisms including CP/GBV, health and nutrition including training of 190 SMCs/PTAs members (90 men and 100 women) on school management, governance, psychosocial support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)/ climate change. Other activities will include provision of life-skills and basic vocational training to youth and adolescents, support prevention and mitigation of communicable diseases through training school communities by providing appropriate Information and Education and Communication (IEC) materials (i.e. posters, leaflets), conduct back to learning campaigns and Post Distribution Monitoring to document how supplies are used.

project_name: Provision of access to safe and inclusive education services, to the most vulnerable, crisis-affected children and youth including those with disabilities in Fangak, Pigi, of Jonglei State and Luakpiny/Nasir and Longochuk Counties in Upper Nile State.
project_objective:
The project is in line with HRP 2023 objective 1 and also with cluster/sector specific objectives 1,2& 3, Besides, it aligns with the cluster strategy to ‘Ensure safe, equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral basic services to enable populations meet their basic needs in locations of severity level 4 and 5’ have reduced morbidity and mortality through equitable and dignified access to critical cross-sectoral essential services to meet their needs.
This project will improve access to safe, quality and inclusive protective education services to 4002 emergency affected IDPs, returnees, spontaneous refugees, and host communities’ children in Fangak, Pigi, and Longochuk and Nasir Counties by 2024. The integrated education project by ADA in hard-to-reach areas aims to ensure that children (boys and girls) have access to quality and inclusive education and those already in schools are retained in Nasir and Longochuk Counties (Upper Nile State), Fangak and Pigi Counties (Jonglei State). The following interventions are envisaged: establishing safe learning and recreational facilities in 12 locations – 3 in each County; teacher training to enhance the teaching/learning function supported in schools; providing monthly stipends to 80 volunteer teachers - 20 teachers per County; campaign for education, encouraging children, especially girls and people with disability to return to school; and provision of school feeding programs to enhance attendance and retention of children at schools. Response priorities will include gender-segregated WASH facilities with much concentration in COVID-19 prevention measures, inclusion of GBV counselling rooms in the schools, provision of learning, teaching and WASH materials, capacity building of 40 School Management Committees (SMCs) and Parents Teachers Associations (PTAs), life-skills and recreational opportunities to support the recovery of children and to promote their overall well-being. Equal access to inclusive education will be prioritized regardless of gender, disability or ethnic background. Through introduction of school gender-sensitive WASH programme, this project will have established strong WASH facilities in schools.The project will seek to address one of the top causes of school dropouts (School feeding) that will help increase and maintain school enrolment and attendance, and reduce risks of death, disease and cognitive underdevelopment. School feeding will also improve protection of- in-school and out of school children by keeping them away from potential recruitment into armed groups, child labor, early marriage, exploitation, sexual violence and abduction while on their way to schools and back home. This will help to reduce morbidity and absenteeism, support retention in schools and children to help sensitize their communities. Crisis-affected children will be engaged in basic education and recreational activities in order to create an enabling environment for their critical development and positive engagement with the community. Youths will catch up on primary education through accelerated learning programmes (ALP) to improve their literacy and numeracy, technical and vocational training, and life skills. The project will seek to include physically and mentally challenged children; girls and boys vulnerable to recruitment into armed groups, and child labour; youths; adolescent heads of households; young mothers; and children from different ethnic groups. Teachers, SMCs and PTAs will be trained on life skills and referral pathways to enhance the protective aspect of education in emergency (EiE) intervention. ADA has a policy on, and extensively uses feedback mechanisms in project implementation. This provides for a complete loop of communication between the field, programs and management. In essence, ADA employs four key steps in providing beneficiary feedbacks: design, implement, collect data and analyses; provide feedback through an agreed feedback loop.

project_name: Access to humanitarian food assistance and emergency livelihood and resilience support to vulnerable populations affected by climate shocks and conflicts in Jonglei (Fangak, Canal/Pigi, Ayod, Bor South) and Lakes (Yirol West, Awerial) states
project_objective:
The high levels of acute food insecurity in South Sudan is worrisome with 7.10 million people expected to experience acute food insecurity in 2024. The most severely acute food insecure populations remain significantly affected by frequent climate-related shocks (flooding and dry spells), the economic crisis (currency depreciation and high food prices), conflict and insecurity – including the spillover effects of the conflict in Sudan – causing forced displacement, low agricultural production and a reduction in humanitarian assistance (South Sudan: IPC Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition Analysis September 2023 - July 2024). 

The prolonged history of food insecurity, due to isolation, inequity, conflicts and climate shocks in Awerial and Yirol West Counties of Lakes State and Bor South County in Jonglei has resulted to severe food shortages. Of the estimated 35,000 people facing catastrophic food insecurity in South Sudan from September 2023 to July 2024 (IPC phase 5), 3,000 people are from Duk and 3,000 people from Nyirol Counties of Jonglei. 

To contribute to FSL CO 1 (humanitarian food assistance): Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations (in IPC 5 and IPC 4), CINA will reach individuals from the most vulnerable food insecure households with unconditional food assistance in IPC4+ locations not reached by WFP (through cash response) and in-kind food assistance (including GFD: blanket/ seasonal/ targeted and GFD plus); More hybrid rations in-kind plus cash component; Cash & voucher-based transfers with food security/ nutrition objectives; Food, fishing & quick maturing vegetable seeds through IRRM; Conditional cash transfers (social skills & safety nets) through investments in assets, training, or communal work groups/ planning committees etc.; and Conditional food assistance through food for assets. 

To contribute to FSL CO 2 and 3 (livelihood and resilience): CINA will enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support; Livestock treatment and vaccination, livestock disease surveillance, Community Animal Health Workers and community-based extension service providers (CBESP); Training and inputs support; Good Agronomic practices; Integrated Pest Management; Fisheries Training; Provision of water pumps; Irrigation training/support; Ox Ploughs & training; PHL Storage granaries; Provision of Canoe, Fishing, Boating materials/tools; Procurement from local traders through seed fairs and Produce/products aggregation; Village Savings/Loans Associations; Processing Equipment for value addition; Training on value addition, Vocational & other enterprise/business related support; Provision of hives for bee-keeping livelihood groups; Install or strengthen community based EWS by providing required equipment; Support downscaling of climate information-flood early warning information through radio programme; Pre-position grain and seed protection kits; Conduct assessment and review existing early action protocol.

CINA has FSL projects running in Lakes into 2024 and will align this project with FSL Cluster HRP 2024 strategy, by following the guidelines on Harmonization of Food Ration, Intervention Modality, Target Complementarities, Conditionality of food assistance and Response Strategy for returnees from Sudan as well as working with HDP actors to ensure sustainability and localization of food aid. The project will be coordinated with other sectors (Nutrition, WASH, Education) to strengthen synergies and will integrate protection dimensions by caring out FSL activities that contribute to safety, dignity, and integrity of at-risk individuals/groups and do not increase the protection risks faced by the crisis-affected populations.

project_name: Provision of protection assistance to crises affected persons of concern, Returnees, IDPs and Host communities in Jonglei (Ayod, Fangak and Canal/Pigi), Upper Upper Nile (Luakpiny/Nasir, Baliet and Renk) and Lakes States (Awerial and Yirol West)
project_objective:
South Sudan is facing complex multifaceted protection crisis with 5.53 million people in need of protection services in 2024 being in severe need. The humanitarian situation is driven by severe climatic shocks, economic meltdown, and frequent conflicts resulting in increased displacement.
With populations remaining displaced, people are unable to access food, safe drinking water, livelihood activities, protection information and assistance. In particular, returnees affected by Sudan Crisis are too far from full recovery and rebuilding of their lives. This situation has resulted to increased reliance on humanitarian assistance.

Similarly, recurrent subnational violence and localized violence among community-based militias or civil defense groups in the proposed areas have displaced civilians, exposing communities, particularly children, women, persons with specific needs, people with disabilities, elderly and other vulnerable community groups to multiple protection risks and vulnerabilities, including grave violations such as killing, injury, family separation, GBV/CRSV, sexual exploitation and abuse, targeting of civilians, revenge attacks and killings, cattle rustlings, burning of house and property, restriction of freedom of movement, forced recruitment, abductions, constraints on safe and equitable access to services, housing, land and property, and other protection risks associated with negative coping mechanisms. This exacerbated the scale and urgency of these needs. Persons with specific needs (PSNs) are particularly affected in such emergencies where they face physical and psychosocial threats, including, risks of drowning, behind left behind during flights, sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and other extreme shocks. The PSNs tend to lack food, shelter/NFIs, medicines, and assistive devices. 

CINA will therefore, reach 16,000 persons of concern (5,600 men, 7,200 women, 2,560 girls, 2,240 boys) including 2,400 persons with disabilities with timely lifesaving protection services including, Protection assessments and monitoring; Psychosocial support services and access to documentation; Protection awareness and prevention messaging; Peacebuilding and peaceful coexistence; Strengthening protection monitoring systems within the community; and Prevent and mitigate protection risks through enhanced preparedness and resilience.

CINA will employ a number of approaches including static programming with field-based roving response in the proposed locations and use of cash assistance for comprehensive case management in line with protection principles. To ensure centrality of protection, protection analysis will be done in collaboration with Protection Cluster, to inform the Do No Harm and protection, conflict sensitive and child-centred approaches to other sectors’ programming and response and inclusion of protection aspects during data collection. Community engagements will be ensured through regular consultations on feedback, complain boxes, hotlines and streamlining of complain and feedback mechanisms, incorporated in the project design and implementation and coordinated with Communication and Community Engagement Working Group. AAP and protection mainstreaming will be upheld, including SEA prevention, survivor assistance, accountability and investigations, with technical support sought from PSEA Task Force.

CINA has a strong static presence and access to the proposed locations, currently implementing child protection, GBV, EORE and education programs and operates field offices, with qualified personnel in Malakal, Renk, Nasir, Awerial and Yirol. CINA owns two new motor speedboats, currently stationed in Malakal and providing access to locations, including their surrounding islands. This project will therefore require 400,000 USD to provide timely and unhindered protection services in the proposed crises affected locations.

project_name: Provision of emergency life-saving primary health care services to 50,224 host communities, Returnees, and IDPs in Akobo and Uror Counties of Jonglei State and Panyijiar County of Unity states.
project_objective:
South Sudan continues to face multiple compounding shocks and stressors. The interrelated hardships continue to adversely impact the weak health care systems. This is evidenced by some of the health-related indicators, Maternal mortality rate (MMR) is still among the highest in the world at 1223 per 100,000 live births with death occurring within 42 days during pregnancy (MMEIG, 2022). Under-five and neonatal mortality rates estimated to be 98 and 40 per 1,000 live births, respectively, reflecting a heavy disease burden for South Sudanese children (UNIGME, 2022), also utilization of maternal-child health services is wanting. 
The country generally has low EPI coverage for the last couple of years as number of zero dose children at national level 7,817 while DPT3 stands at 73% and Measles at 72% below the recommended threshold of 85% by end of December 2022 (WHO Immunization Portal report 2022). Cold chain availability and Limited health facility functionality, capacity, and poor coverage and transmission of infections prevented by immunization like measles remain very high. ISNA 2023, indicates that the main barriers to access and utilization of care services were long distance to health facility and lack of transport (62.2%), long waiting time for services (36%) and insecurity or security concerns (6%) (floods, and high cost of healthcare (mentioned by host communities, IDPs, and returnees). 
The 12- month project proposed by Medicair will align her responses with Health Cluster strategic objectives 1). Improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment of common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services to crisis-affected populations. 2) Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases. 3 Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms to vulnerable population of Akobo, Uror and Panyijiar County.
Medicair will collaborate and work closely with State Ministry of Health and County Health Departments to deploy static and mobile teams to provide health care services in the targeted locations (1 PHCUs and 2 mobile teams in Akobo, 1 PHCU and 2 Mobile teams in Uror and 1 PHCU and 2 mobile teams in Panyijiar County) to improve accessibility of hard-to-reach areas.
The target Population will include 50,224 in total men 10,547 (21%), women 12,556 (25%), boys 13,058 (26%) and girls 14.063 (28%) while persons with disability being 7,534 (15%) M, 1,582. W. 1,884. Boys. 1,959. Girls. 2,110. (52%) 26,116 of the population will be women of the targeted population.
The activities include i) carry out disease surveillance, prevention and control including outbreak detection prevention and response, ii) OPD consultation, iii) case management of common illnesses, iv) immunization against vaccine preventable disease, v)Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEmONC)(ANC,PNC and skilled deliveries), vi) Clinical Management of Rape, vii) Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, viii) Capacity Building, ix) infection prevention and control, x) community health service linkage, mobilization and consultative meetings

project_name: Provision of immediate lifesaving access to basic WASH Services in emergencies for vulnerable IDP’s, Host communities, returnees and Refugees affected by conflict, food insecurity and natural disaster through Rapid Response Mechanism and Static Interventions in Priority 1 and 2 Counties of Jonglei and Upper Nile.
project_objective:
Under this proposed Emergency WASH Interventions for 2024, The Rescue Mission intends to support the people affected by conflict, natural disaster and displacement in emergency context and static as long-term support for the IDPs, host community and people to return, resettle and reintegrate with host community. The interventions are designed to address the emergency WASH needs through rapid response mechanism (RRT) and static interventions which will contribute to improve health, nutrition, education, Livelihood and food security, shelter and protection outcomes and durable solutions. The proposed interventions are to reduce prevalence of malnutrition contributing to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality, provide access to basic WASH services in underserved and hard to reach locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facilities, TERM will respond to the Sudan crisis, flooding and disease outbreak in the priority 2 counties through Rapid Respond Mechanism (RRT) with static interventions in priority 1 counties. The project will seek to enhance supply of sustainable access to safe and clean water (15l/p/d), dignified, inclusive and adequate access to sanitation services and opportunities aimed influencing social behaviour and norms in relation to personal, household, communal and institutional hygiene. 
The proposed intervention will reach a target population of 22,222 vulnerable Individuals (Host 8400, IDP’s 6000, Returnees 7822, People with disabilities 250). The activities will include, Construction of new water points; rehabilitation of water points, Construction and rehabilitation of sanitation facilities at Health/Nutrition facilities, Schools and at the community levels; installation of hand washing facilities to promote hand washing; hygiene promotion education through door to door visits, participatory hygiene sessions in public places for effective behavioural change; distribution of hygiene kit to SAM children WASH NFIs to the most vulnerable.

Menstrual hygiene management (MHM) kits will be provided to adolescent girls and women of reproductive age group accompanied with menstrual hygiene management sessions. TERM will ensure ownership and sustainability of the response through involvement of the targeted community throughout the life cycle of the intervention. All the WASH temporary and sustainable services will address the vital needs, through accountability to affected populations (AAP) , working with all the sex and age groups, people with disabilities (PWD), pregnant and lactating women (PLW) incorporating gender dynamics and specific needs of different groups into needs assessment and response recommendations. WASH structures and infrastructure in the flood prone areas, contributing to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties. 
To enhance and ensure sustainability and proper usage of the facilities, TERM will deliberate on comprehensive training to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs), Schools and other institutional staff. Solid waste management training will also be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns.

project_name: Provision of quality inclusive education services to emergency-affected children and youth in Jonglei State (Fangak, Pigi, Nyirol counties), Lake State(Yirol West , Awerial counties) and Upper Nile State ( Melut, Panyikang and Fashoda counties)
project_objective:
The South Sudan Education cluster prioritisation 2024 (Humanitarian Needs Overview 2023), estimates that about 3.3 million children are in need of urgent educational service provision in 2024 and that 244,233 of these children are located in the 8 Counties from the three states of Lake (Yirol West, Awerial), Upper Nile State( Melut, Panyikang, Fashoda) and Jonglei State (Fangak, Pigi and Nyirol). South Sudan education sector plan objective is to provide equitable and safe access to inclusive, quality education; Improve educational management; and Promote quality non-formal and formal post primary TVET. The realization of this objective is impeded by poor infrastructures, insecurity, impact of climate change that results to many displacements of the communities, influx of refugees and returnees following the conflict in Sudan and communal fighting that displaced many people in western Ethiopia to South Sudan eastern state of Jonglei (Fangak, Pigi and Nyirol,) and Upper Nile state ( Melut, Panyikang and Fashoda) and Lake State( Yirol, Awerial). The most pressing education needs as requested by all schools to operate were: recruitment of additional teachers, provision of WASH facilities, school feeding programme, teachers’ salaries/incentives, teaching and learning supplies, security for schools, rehabilitation of school infrastructures and training of teachers.

To meet the Education Cluster HRP 2024 Objectives of: 1) ensuring ''access to safe, protective and inclusive education services to emergency-affected children and youth, that are appropriate to their age, learning level and needs’’, CINA will establish/rehabilitate 17 learning spaces in line with INEE's Minimum Standards; Establish change rooms for girls; Establish/rehabilitate gender sensitive latrines in line with INEE and sphere standards.  CINA will increase enrolment of ALP children, Functional Literacy children, Life Skills for Children and Youth, Pre-Primary children, Primary children, Secondary children, Skills for Life and TVET. CINA will conduct distribution of dignity kits to adolescent girls; Awareness raising on key issues; Distribution of hygiene kits to school boys and girls and assistive devices to children with disabilities; CINA will establish reporting (toll free lines, suggestion boxes, designated focal-points etc.) mechanisms; Conduct training of teachers and staff on child safeguarding and GBV risk mitigation, referral mechanism; Provision of school meal to children; Establish school gardens at school; Training of teachers on PSS and Provision of PSS to learners.
2)To ensure that ‘’children and youth are provided with quality teaching and learning services that support retention and progress through the education cycle’’, CINA will distribute ECD Kits to school children and Recreation Kits to children; Train teachers on EiE, subject matter, and pedagogical skill and support volunteer teachers with financial incentives. 3) To ensure that ‘’Coordination and crisis management capacity is strengthened to promote efficient, accountable, and timely education in emergencies response’’, CINA will conduct training for SMC/PTA members and education authorities on school management, governance, climate change and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR).

CINA has qualified personnel, governance and organizational structures and is currently implementing GESS besides child protection, MHPSS, GBV, EORE, and FSL programs in Lakes (Yirol West, Yirol East and Awerial), Jonglei (all the counties), GPAA (all counties) and Upper Nile (all counties). CINA will maximize its education capacity to accelerate learning for the crises affected out of school children to increase enrolment and retention while maintaining the quality of education, safeguarding and protection of learners. To ensure success, education services will be coordinated at state and national levels, optimizing nexus efforts with humanitarian-peace-development actors for improved learning outcomes for children.

project_name: Provision of Comprehensive GBV response, prevention and mitigation services  to the most vulnerable women, men, girls and boys in Jonglei (Canal Pigi, Fangak and Nyirol Counties)), Lakes (Yirol West  and Awerial Counties), and Eastern Equatoria (Magwi)
project_objective:
South Sudan is still in protection crisis despite the implementation of Peace Agreement following the 2013 and 2016 national violence. The displaced populations face extreme gender-based violence, in particular. An estimated 2.8 million people will faced GBV risks in 2023 – a 9 per cent increase from the 2022 estimates (HNO 2023). With influx of returnees who are affected by the Sudan Crisis into the country coupled with unsafe protection environment, the prevalence of GBV may rise significantly.  Women and girls are differently affected and their vulnerability is exacerbated by various forms of GBV, including rape, physical assault, forced marriage and SEA. Similarly, men and boys are also exposed to killings, abductions and forced recruitment, especially in conflict settings. 


In line with the inter-sectoral strategic objectives and under the overall Protection Cluster objective and the GBV AoR, CINA aims to ensure the provision of comprehensive GBV Response, prevention and risk mitigation measures, to reduce the suffering of GBV survivors and to strengthen vulnerability assessment and risk analysis to identify risks to various forms of gender-based violence.    The project will also employ a combination of Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) and in-kind support such as dignity kits and provision of frontline GBV services as appropriate.  Primary GBV prevention programme, such as Engaging Men and Boys through Accountable Practice and Community Care Programme, will address harmful social norms and systemic gender inequality as part of the primary GBV prevention intervention approaches. Community engagement and awareness-raising activities will focus on the risk factors for GBV, available response services and timely seeking of services and reporting of GBV incidents within 72 hours. The GBV risk mitigation interventions will prioritize the integration of GBV actions and survivor support across the sectoral interventions of different Clusters and AoRs within the Protection Cluster, along with dignity kit distribution and programming, distribution of fuel-efficient stoves, conducting joint safety audits, ensuring the implementation of the recommendations and providing livelihood and economic support. Similarly, the GBV response interventions will include the provision of psychosocial support, GBV case management, establishment and strengthening of GBV referral systems and implementation of Women and Girls Friendly Space programming.  Other response priorities will include the provision of legal services, livelihoods and economic support, provision of cash-based individual protection assistance and capacity-building of frontline GBV service providers.     

This project aims at response services to strengthen primary GBV prevention, GBV risk mitigation and integration into other sectors, and scaling up GBV response services for 35,000 vulnerable people (21,000 women, 10,500 girls, 1050 boys, 2450 men) including 15% people with disability and elderly from the IDPs, returnees and host community in line with the “do no harm” principle''. The project will ensure accountability to affected population mechanisms through community sensitization, engagement of project management committee, regular feedback mechanisms. This project will build into existing CINA's approaches to Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) through formation of community complaint mechanisms, increasing awareness for service-demand and establishing reporting channels for complains within communities. The project will ensure inclusivity in all aspects. Women, girls and boys living with disability will receive top priority attention. Gender, age and inclusion checklists shall be developed and deployed at project site to be used for all project delivery.

project_name: Life Saving Emergency WASH Assistance, Unity State
project_objective:
Leer and Mayendit counties populations are the most affected by many years of conflict, flood and other natural disasters with majority of the population being food insecure, in IPC 4 in Mayendit and IPC 3 in Leer. The number of people bordering IPC 5 catastrophe and Emergency IPC 4 are continuing to increase in the two counties. The Torrential rains across South Sudan have repeatedly devastated several parts of the country in the year 2020 and in 2021, rainfall continue to cause floods.  OCHA has placed the current affected population at 10,000, from a total projected total Mayendit county population of 66,015 and a total of 26,145 in Leer County. According to Inter-Agency Flood Assessment Report, Mayendit and Leer County, Unity State, 18th – 21st August 2021, 7,971 people have voluntarily moved out of Mayendit South due to the flood.  An estimated population of 15,000 people affected by floods are yet to be evacuated from Mayendit South. As the IDPs integrate in the community, there is pressure on resources in Mayendit North. An estimated total of 24,000 people affected by floods in Mayendit South are expected to move to Mayendit North. According to the IRNA reports, some of the displaced populations moved to Leer County. This is despite the fact that in Leer County a total of 6,944 households and 41,664 individuals have been affected by floods. An estimated 23% of 66,015 people in Mayendit North is already or will be affected by the current flood as the water level keeps rising. Malaria, Diarrhea and injuries were highly recorded in the health facilities. 
The floods have affected WASH facilities in Mayendit County and a total of 13 hand pumps were reported submerged and are not accessible, while 20 hand pumps were reported flooded but accessible by the communities. Besides the submerged boreholes, coalition for humanity has identified more than 50 boreholes that are broken down and need rehabilitation in Leer County while those flooded but functional require raising of the platform to minimize contamination. Due to floods, 43 household and 18 institutional latrines were reported to have collapsed.  People have to wait till late to ease themselves and this put women and girls in danger of rape and sexual abuse.  WASH facilities in schools are also affected, 18 schools (learning spaces) were reported flooded, and children were relocated to highlands. 
Open defecation has become unsafe especially for women living with disability, who have increasingly faced sexual abuse and violence at night. On 12th July one rape case was reported in Pilieny Payam. Cases of rape, sexual harassment and abuse are common during dry season because perpetrators have been reported to take advantage of the women and girls who wake up very early to take their water buckets at the water points so as to avoid longer hours of queueing. Conflicts at water points among women and girls are very common. Intimate partner violence is very common when women delay at water points. It arises as a result of men suspicion that their women could have been with other men at the water points hence their delay to come back home. Women and girls remain vulnerable to SGBV cases. Cases of women fighting at water points over the limited access to water at current IDP settlement in Mayendit North have been reported. Communities’ social institutions like women and child friendly spaces got flooded hence access to justice system whether legal or customary courts to handle GBV related complains are rendered unfunctional. Women report to NGO staff cases of assault, but some don’t due to fear and shame that comes along the ordeal. Personal hygiene is very poor and women of the childbearing age and adolescent girls find it hard to cope during their monthly menstrual cycles leading to increase of women & girls’ health/hygiene risks. There is need to rehabilitate water points close to where women live to reduce congestion at one water points.

project_name: Provision of Basic WASH Services to Vulnerable communities in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Warrap State.
project_objective:
Ayod, Twic, Maiwut, and Luakpiny/Nasir are high-priority counties facing acute vulnerabilities in WASH and malnutrition, compounded by high WASH-related GBV. The WASH, nutrition, and protection-related challenges affect an estimated 2 million people needing humanitarian aid. WASH services are highly required following the declaration from the MoH about an outbreak of HEV disease in Fangak. The WASH severity classification places these counties in phase 4. 

The main findings highlight minimal access to clean drinking water with worse scenarios in Ayod, Fangak, and Nasir. People rely on rivers, swamps, or ponds as their primary source of drinking water, yet open defecation is a norm in the area. Despite all the efforts made by humanitarians, the response remains constrained due to access impediments and insecurity, including the delivery of humanitarian supplies with barge movements.

These counties display the lowest standards in WASH parameters according to the most recent WASH cluster severity mapping, which is likely to be exacerbated by unprecedented flood waters leading to the destruction of WASH infrastructure, food insecurity, logistical challenges, displacement of communities, deprivation of markets, and the increasing number of returnees from Sudan. The flooding has further increased WASH-related mortality and morbidity, affecting mainly under five children, pregnant and lactating women, persons with special needs, and those living with HIV/TB. 

Providing adequate WASH services is critical to achieving sustainable solutions for communities in these targeted areas. Community Action Organization (CAO) is a national NGO working in Jonglei & Upper Nile States in South Sudan & plans a robust WASH response aimed at improving community well-being and improving the worst WASH indicators in the targeted counties.

The plan targets internally displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities with water, sanitation, and hygiene services integrated with nutrition and protection/GBV programming for one year. Following the Cluster response plans, CAO aims to respond to sudden-onset disasters and the needs of WASH Services, maintaining integration with the Health and Nutrition Clusters to prevent WASH-related epidemics. 

The action prioritizes alleviating suffering through minimal hardware interventions, rehabilitation of existing systems, and promoting safe hygiene practices through sustainable services to address the vital needs in public health/nutrition and protection/GBV issues. It also aims to reduce levels of chronic malnutrition amongst children and pregnant and lactating women, mitigate WASH-related GBV by providing gender-appropriate sanitation and hygiene facilities, and tackle gender issues, safety, and WASH. 

Persistent food insecurity, signaled by high GAM rates, with <5s and PLW mainly affected, will be mitigated by the provision of WASH in Nutrition services through targeted WASH minimum packages at OTP/SC, mainly for mother/caretaker and malnourished children. Water-related disease outbreaks have been traced to health facilities and community infrastructures/settings without adequate WASH facilities. 

CAO will ensure that 33,485 individuals have timely and equitable access to WASH services to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. The design of the activities covers access to safe/clean water through digging boreholes, distribution of Water Treatment kits, distribution of WASH kits and MHM materials, and construction of latrines. In addition, adapted messages on hygiene good practices will complement all the other WASH services to provide the population with dignified means of hygiene and sanitation. CAO aims to have a long-lasting impact, even after the end of the project.

project_name: Provision of integrated emergency Food Security and Livelihood (FSL) services to vulnerable and affected populations in Rubkona, Kapoeta North and Abiemnhom Counties, South Sudan
project_objective:
Since the conflict crisis in 2013, and the consequent aggression coupled with drought, locusts, floods and the army warm infestation, the factors of food production for families over the years has been greatly affected to the present state. Household livelihood systems and patterns has been on the shift with many households only counting the cost. The cost of foods prices has remained every year high which has also affected the food production capacity of many households. Furthermore, family household incomes and dietary intakes has been greatly affected and to larger extent deteriorated and very wanting. As the hard economic times continue to press and bite the communities, many households have succumbed to survival mode as their livelihoods has been diminished or destroyed. Many household dietary intakes have significantly deteriorated and many can hardly afford two meals per day.
Conflict in Sudan has also greatly affected the food security situation in South Sudan with over 260000 returnees pushing the already worse food security and livelihood situation to precarious levels. The returnees are currently competing for very limited food staffs in the country that is recovering from its own conflict and three years of flooding that have destroyed farm lands.
The objective of the project is to provide food and livelihood protection to population affected by conflict and flood related displacements, hunger and diseases in Abiemnhom,  Kapoeta North and  Rubkona Counties. In line with FSL Cluster priorities and HRP 2024 strategy, WART will provide complementary and integrated agricultural crop and vegetable seeds, farming tools, fishing kits and agricultural extension support including training on improved agronomy practices and fish handling/preservation techniques to the communities in Abiemnhom,  Kapoeta North and  Rubkona Counties where indicators show a continuously degrading situation. The project will target 13,000HHs most vulnerable IDP, returnee and host populations in in these counties and provide Agricultural to support and increase their Agricultural production and productivity hence strengthening their capacity to produce enough food for household consumption and help them evade future shocks and builds their resilience.
The project will endeavour to support integration of activities through nutrition and protection to offer the vulnerable and affected populations with the best integrated services as well as putting the protection needs on the communities in the implementation of the project.
This project will further ensure protection mainstreaming; acknowledging that women, girls, men and boys with diverse ages, disabilities and backgrounds have very different needs, risk and coping strategies. This will be achieved by paying particular attention to protection and inclusion of vulnerable groups based and on gender and diversity analysis in addition to ensuring prevention of incidences of Gender Based Violence, sexual exploitation and abuse and other protection concerns and ensuring activities adheres to Do No Harm approach, and environmental protection.

project_name: Provision of integrated WASH services to vulnerable and affected populations in Rubkona County.
project_objective:
South Sudan is struggling to cope with different shocks that have affected the WASH infrastructure in the country. This has left a lot of people in the country struggling to meet the basic WASH needs. Integrated WASH service delivery is essential in alleviating the immerse WASH needs of the vulnerable and affected populations in South Sudan that have been affected by conflict and shocks associated with flooding as a result of climate change. 
Rubkona county  is having Immerse WASH needs and are in need of urgent which needs integrated WASH services to alleviate the suffering of the vulnerable populations. Rubkona County is bordering Sudan and in the recent days received influx of returnees 
The county is in IPC phase 4 and therefore require urgent WASH intervention to ensure that the vulnerable and affected populations have access to safe drinking water, sanitation facilities, protection mainstreaming is observed and malnourished children in the counties have access to clean water for consumption.
Women Agency for resilience and Transformation (WART) proposes to cater for WASH needs of the vulnerable population in the three counties by integrating WASH in nutrition by provision of clean and safe water in the nutrition centers and supplying WASH NFIs and WASH kits to Couples with Malnourished children(Caretaker/child). This is because it has been proven that WASH needs aggravate or contribute to malnutrition.
Hygiene promotion is key in supporting behavior change among the communities to avoid hazardous behavior like open defecation that lead to contamination of water points thus increasing the risk of water infections. WART will conduct hygiene promotion in the target counties with focus on open defecation free bomas and proper utilization of sanitation facilities.
WART will also ensure access to sanitation facilities by rehabilitating temporally sanitation facilities to the vulnerable and affected populations in the target counties. Temporary water solutions will be offered by light rehabilitation of the water points and formation of water management committees.
WART will offer integrated WASH and protection services by conducting safe audits during rehabilitation of the water and sanitation facilities as well as distribution of MHM kits and ensure that the sanitation facilities are safe for women and girls by having locks that will ensure their safety during use of the sanitation facilities.
Training health workers and nutrition workers on minimum WASH package activities is key in supporting integration of services, WART will train the health workers and nutrition workers on this key topic to ensure that they are able to implement WASH activities in the health facilities and the nutrition centers. The organization will as well distribute hygiene kits to the children admitted in stabilization centers and nutrition facilities to ensure proper and hygienic practices that will hence improve their recovery.
Project will target 11111 vulnerable and affected populations in the three counties with of which  2500 will be children under five with malnutrition, 5511 women and  4100 men. 1029 will be persons with disabilities and the rehabilitation of water points and the sanitation facilities will also be disability inclusive to ensure that access to all in the project implementation.

project_name: Provision of quality comprehensive GBV and protection services to 26881 Women, Men, Girls and boys of the Returnees, IDPs and Vulnerable host communities affected by conflict in Malakal, Melut, Fangak, Pigi, Pibor and Terekeka counties in Upper Nile state, Jonglei states and Central Equatorial states.
project_objective:
This project intervention is meant to increase access to, and quality of GBV response, Prevention and Risk mitigation targeting 26881; 15053 Women,6451 men, 2756 Girls and 2581 boys of the returnees, IDPs and Vulnerable host communities including people living with disability (PLWD).   Women and girls in South Sudan including the one fleeing conflict in Sudan continue to face high risks of GBV including rape, sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), intimate partner violence and physical violence. Adolescent girls are even more vulnerable with child marriage increasing in many locations across South Sudan. Incidents of conflict-related sexual violence have been documented within the country and Sudan crisis. The impacts of this are compounded by gaps in lifesaving GBV services in the country including clinical management of rape (CMR) and GBV case management and psychosocial support. In addition, due to economic stress, flooding and dry spell that is being experience currently in the country and which is expected to spiral to the year 2024, Cases of gender-based violence is expected to rise due members of the household being more likely to perpetrate violence. Overall, the capacity and coverage of multi-sectoral GBV responses including health, GBV case management and PSS, higher-level mental health and other services remain scarce in the targeted counties of Malakal, Melut, Akobo, Fangak, Pigi, Pibor and Terekeka in Upper Nile, Jonglei and Central equatorial states where SAADO has predominantly presence. 
The increased risk of GBV and gaps in response services in Malakal, Melut, Pigi, Fangak, Pibor and Terekeka counties, coupled with shrinking humanitarian funding, highlight an urgent need for GBV prevention, risk mitigation, scaling up of specialized GBV response services and Prevention of sexual exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) in targeted mention areas where SAADO operates. Specifically, there is a need to strengthen GBV case management, health response to GBV survivors, psychosocial support and GBV referral pathways. Primary GBV prevention interventions such as Community Cares program, integration of GBV actions into other sectoral responses including safety audits, strengthening of GBV coordination, and provision of dignity kits are high priority interventions for the GBV in 2024 South Sudan. 
For accountability to the affected population (AAP) and in order to involve all the beneficiaries in the response, SAADO will create a committee in each county that will compose of 50% women, 20% Men and 30% people living with disability (PLWD) to oversee the project implementation as from its initiation. The beneficiaries will be relying their concerns and feedbacks to the committee after a series of consultation, then the committee will share feedback with the partner to enhance the quality of the project. The involvement of the community will be key in building trust and creating a sense of ownership thus increasing the sustainability of the project in the targeted locations.  SAADO will mainstream protection in this project by contacting risks analysis and continuous monitoring access, Safety and dignity of all targeted beneficiaries.  Through this intervention and response, SAADO estimate the cost of this project to be 940,835. SAADO has prominent presence in this targeted location, implementing GBV project in Malakal, Melut, Pigi and Fangak; FSL and WASH in Northen Bahr-el-gazal and central Equatorial including Terekeka and Livelihood in Pibor. SAADO propose to expand its GBV programming to area that it operates to enhance integration. All the mentioned area, we do have established offices and mean of transport thus reducing it operation budget.  Integration of GBV activities with other sector including Protection, WASH, FSL, Health, Education and Nutrition will be key to enhance synergy in the targeted area.

project_name: Sudan: Lifesaving Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) response to conflict affected, most vulnerable individuals in West Darfur, Kordofan and Red Sea State.
project_objective:
The proposed intervention links and contributes to the Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) Sector strategic objectives for the upcoming 2024 humanitarian cycle by  
1) improving the food security status of  food insecure, conflict affected people through life-saving and life sustaining food assistance; 
2) supporting the self-reliance of conflict affected households through  protecting and building productive assets and restoring or creating income generating opportunities to save and sustain lives; and 
3) improving conflict affected communities’ capacity to sustain households’ livelihoods through the rehabilitation/building of productive infrastructure as well as supporting services. 
The programme in 2024 targets  conflict affected displaced populations, returnees and host communities to meet their basic needs and essential basic services in West Darfur, Red Sea West Kordofan, and South Kordofan States. 
this intervention will also contribute  to the  FSL sector sub-objectives by addressing life threatening and life sustaining needs. 

In 2024, Concern aims at reaching (target: 2000 MPCA, 2000 Food assistance, 18,000 Input kits, 3,500 Livestock Vaccinations and 1,050 livelihoods/Agric trainings shelter kits)  across West Darfur, Red Sea, South and West Kordofan through a integrated,  multi-funded interventions. In-kind food assistance will provide immediate, life-saving support where cash programming is not an option,  , cash, and voucher assistance will be the preferred option in geographic locations where transfer system exists and can be utilized by humanitarian response,  agricultural and livestock interventions for both farmers and pastoralist (including animal vaccination campaigns will be promoted in locations where the conflict did not affect the local agriculture system and both agriculture and livelihoods activities can be implemented.).
Vulnerability targeting will follow selection criteria preferring integrated approaches, and the most vulnerable people, including the newly displaced and protracted displaced, refugees and host communities will be prioritized, with a special focus on women and girls.

Based on Concern's current present in West Darfur, West and South Kordofan and Red Sea states, response will mobilize local networks, available social structures especially in places where IDPs settled with local/host community population to minimize the social, community level conflicts over limited resources.
