project_name: Enhancing Integrated Lifesaving Health and Nutrition Response in West Darfur, Central Darfur, Khartoum, Blue Nile, Jazeera and South Kordofan States of Sudan
project_objective:
The project aims at providing Emergency healthcare and nutrition services to respond to the needs of the conflict affected people in new and existing areas of operations to IDPs, Returnees, pastoralist and most vulnerable communities in 6 states of Sudan, namely: Khartoum, Central Darfur, Blue Nile, South Kordofan and West Darfur where World Relief (WR) has been operating in previous years. In addition, for this ongoing conflict, WR plans to resume operations in the state of Jazeera to provide lifesaving interventions for IDPs and host community. As a result of this project, morbidity and mortality attributable to high malnutrition rate and burden of common diseases in the targeted communities will be reduced significantly. 
The following are the targeted localities:  Azum, Golo, Nertiti, Rokero, Zalingei, Bindisi,  Mukjar & Umdukun (8 localities of Central Darfur State); Geneina, Kerenik, Habila, Beida  and Sirba (5 localities of West Darfur); Bahri, Karari, Khartoum, Omdurman, Sharg En Neel, Um Bada and Jebel Awlia (7 localities of Khartoum); Demazine, Kurmuk, Bau and Rosaries (4 localities of Blue Nile states) and 1 locality of South Kordofan (Kadugli);  Sharg al Jazeera and Medani (2 localities in Jazeera). It is estimated that 560,000 (F:294,737; M:537,480) people; among which 95,238 are children under five years old and 23,330 with disability) will benefit from this project. The beneficiaries are mostly IDPs in the conflict affected states such as Darfur states, South Kordofan and Khartoum while Jazeera, and Blue Nile states, they are most scattered IDPs and refugees who are integrated in the communities and poor families.
 The project will ensure that children under five years, women and especially pregnant or lactating (PLWs) are prioritized as part of people with specific needs and vulnerable to diseases and malnutrition. Thus, the services are in line with the needs of the specific and general population and considering also the services package of the Primary Healthcare (PHC). In addition, the project will focus on the life-saving emergency activities while initiating and reinforcing those strengthening and contributing to resilience of the health systems in targeted localities. 
Under Health program, the activities will range from the promotional, preventive to curative of common diseases. Immunization campaign for ,1 year old children will be organized, IEC on different health topics at PHC and community level, maternal health services, ANC, PNC, delivery and newborn care; strengthening the PHC functionality through running cost and establishment of health committees as part of governance & leadership component of the PHC; supplies of essential medicines as per WHO and FMoH guidelines, early warning system activation for disease outbreak or any relevant emergency; support with incentives for the health cadres especially in hard-to-reach areas; capacity building of health cadres, etc.
 Nutrition programing will focus on lifesaving preventive activities such as, protection and promotion of breastfeeding; Maternal and Young Child Nutrition (MYCN) Counseling; micronutrient supplementation for under-twos and pregnant women; early detection using Mother/family MUAC. Will also support capacity building of community volunteers & Mother support groups (MSGs) and nutrition cadres at the health facilities; curative activities focusing on CMAM; for Outpatient management and TSFPs. Management of at risk mother and infants will also be done WR has been implementing health and nutrition programing since 2005 in Darfur and other states of Sudan using an integrated approach where the center of focus will be the
 patient. The project design is to engage the community in identifying the needs and their participation in the implementation of the project as part of accountability to the beneficiaries. WR will ensure the mitigation plan and other risks.

project_name: Food Security and Livelihoods interventions in Jazeera, Blue Nile, South Kordofan, Khartoum, Central and West Darfur states:
project_objective:
The Majorities of the IDPs, returnees, host communities and pastoralists are suffering from food shortage and malnutrition due to the recorded poor production of crops which is ascribed mainly to the nationwide conflict between RSF & SAF forces, which was also triggered by tribal disputes and displacements in Darfur states. Moreover, the deteriorated economic situation, currency inflation, skyrocketing price of agricultural and industrial food products in the market didn’t favor the poor and vulnerable people to purchase their food items and subsist the life of their family members. The aid agencies (UN agencies and NGOs) which used to provide food aid are barely able to provide assistance to the increasing number of needy people in Darfur, Aljazeera, and Kordofan states. In line with the acute hunger, children are facing severe and moderately acute malnutrition due resulted from the acute food insecurity, lack of timely and appropriate response to save their life. The restricted inter/intra state movement of supplies and the increasing demand for taxations in many checkpoints discouraged traders to transport and sale farm and nonfarm products to customers and in the rural and urban areas. Furthermore, the shortage and alarming price of fuel has direct contribution in increasing the price of essential food and nonfood items in Sudan and in the targeted intervention areas. Likewise, the production and income from the livestock sector is drastically deteriorating due to poor access to livestock feed, veterinary services, market outlets and fear of livestock rustling by armed groups and individuals.
This Food security and livelihoods (FSL) project is designed with the overall objective of saving lives and building resilience of the most vulnerable HHs and reducing acute food insecurity and malnutrition through ensuring availability of nutritious food to  78,347 HHs (391,735 individuals 227,206 female & 164,529 male)  (in 26 localities in the six states including (Ar rashad, Abu jubayhah, Abassiya, Kadugli, and Al buram localities in South Kordfan state), (Altadamon, El Kurmuk, Rosaries, El Damazine, Geissan, Wa almahi and Baw localities of Blue Nile Region), (El Geniena, Jebel Moon, Kulbus and Sirba in West Darfur), (Gharb jabal marrah, Shamal jabal marrah, Zalingei, Azum, Um Dukhun and Wasat jabal marrah of Central Darfur), (Madani Alkobra, AL Hassa hissa and Jonob Al Jazeera in AL Jazeera state) and (Karrari locality in Khartoum state) . 
WRS has planned the following response options in its targeted areas in cooperation with the donor community: Provision of food/cash assistance to selected target beneficiaries 309,946 individuals (179,769 female & 130,177 male) using inclusive, conflict sensitive, gender sensitive approaches through MPCA and food assistance modalities. Support poor 84,728 farmers (49,142 female & 35,586 male) with agricultural inputs (seeds) tools to enable them producing food crops for subsistence and marketing and building the technical and management capacity of farmers on agricultural production, post-harvest management, marketing, etc. Distribution of farm tools to poor farmers. Provision of restocking animals including goat distribution to 1,000 beneficiaries (580 female and 420 male) in planed localities of the six states. Provide emergency veterinary services (vaccination, deworming/treatment, and animal disease surveillance) for the control of zoonotic and trans-boundary animal diseases to 50,000 beneficiaries (29,000 female and 21,000 male) to support pastoralists through improving the veterinary service delivery systems. Facilitate FFA activities to restore the communities’ assets by implementing appropriate activities in collaboration with WFP and participation of 1,000 (460 female and 540male) (FFA participants in North and Central Jebal Marra. Provide deferent skills training sessions to 1,200 beneficiaries (696 female and 504 male) to build their resilience.

project_name: Multi-sectorial Life-saving Intervention to the Conflict-affected Displaced and Vulnerable Households in West Darfur, South Darfur, Greater Kordofan States (West, South and North), Blue Nile, Red Sea and River Nile States
project_objective: The project aims to provide life-saving support to 337,500 people (WASH), 14,700 (Education), 4,250 (G Protection) 3,800 (CP), 4,050 (GBV), 2,750 HH (Shelter & NFIs) and 6,000 (FSL). IAS/LM targets IDPs and host communities (vulnerable women, children, PWDs & elderly, considering gender-sensitive issues) affected by the current conflict between RSF and SAF in SD (Beleil, Nyala Shima & Ganoub and Elsalam), WD (El Geneina, Habila and Sirba), WK (Keilak, Lagawa and Al Meram) SK (Dilling, Abbasiya and Elreef Elshargi), NK (Sheikan and Um Rawaba localities), BN (Damazine, Kurmuk, Gissan, Wad Elmahi and Alruseris), RN (Atbara, Shendi, Ed Damer and Barbar) and RS (Agig, Algonab, Dordeib, Hya, Port Sudan and Sinkat). The project will implement WASH as a lifesaving intervention including new Installation and rehabilitation of HPs, solarized MWY, water distribution points, water trucking, O&M of water points, water points quality monitoring and WMC, rehabilitation of institutional latrines and O&M, disinfection and desludging of the existing latrine, solid waste management, vector control & cleaning tools, multi-purpose soap for individuals, jerrycans and hygiene kits, construction of HWF, hygiene training for community volunteers and campaigns in communal setups. Displacement has overwhelmed host communities, straining their fragile education systems and limited services. 49 Access barriers remain significant, with an additional 6.9 million children out-of-school including children with disabilities, many living in vulnerable communities. The crisis caused significant psychological distress among children, potentially impacting their long-term mental health and education progress if not urgently addressed with the mentioned lack of trained female teachers (HRP 2024). IAS/LM will provide educational recreational materials to 14,700 students, rehabilitate 30 Temporary learning spaces, rehabilitate 30 HW stations, psychosocial support to 3800 students, establish referral pathways between schools and child protection services for 1000 children, teachers & Parent Association members with increased knowledge on MHPSS skill, teaching & learning materials for 5000 children. HRP 2024 reflected that conflict targeted population requiring psychosocial support and individual assistance to respond to rising protection needs. PSN require specialized support amid severe economic hardship and rising inflation. IAS targeting GBV 4,050 (810 boys, 1013 girls, 810 men, and 1417 women), CP target 3,800 (760 boys, 950 girls, 760 men, and 1330 women), and general protection target 4,250 (850 women, 1,063 men 850 boys and 1487 girls), including PSEA awareness in PSS approach and provide PSS services to children with disabilities with a referral mechanism for the affected population. Under the GBV activities 1000 people at risk will be supported, rehabilitate 2 WCs, conduct training in GBV prevention and response for 3347 people and conduct 10 large-scale public community awareness-raising campaigns on GBV. GP includes (IPA)/ Cash Grants, referral to specialized services, psychosocial support, protection training and assessment. Shelter & NFIs target 13,750 beneficiaries (2,750 HHs) with NFI Kits to 500, cash/vouchers for NFIs to 500, Tents to 500, ESKs to 750 and cash/vouchers for shelter to 500 HHs. The FSL component aims to provide life-saving support to 6000 (1200 women, 1500 men 1200 boys and 2100 girls), contribute to the reduction of morbidity associated with malnutrition, prevent livelihood depletion of vulnerable communities through responding to immediate FSL needs of the target people in WD, SD and RN States, through improved access to agricultural inputs and services, provision of livelihoods for conflict-affected HHs and direct provision of agricultural inputs and services, quality assorted crops, legumes & vegetable seeds and tools besides multipurpose cash transfer and half ratio food voucher for 3 months during the lean period.

project_name: Lifesaving WASH services and resilience building for IDPs, returnees and host communities in Khartoum, Al Gedaref, Kassala, Port Sudan, Al Jazeera, East Darfur, South Darfur and West Kordofan states
project_objective:
The WASH condition in Sudan is deteriorating from time to time. Access to WASH services becomes more challenging for communities. Several WASH infrastructures remain in disrepair due to lack of spare parts and lack of maintenance budget and chronic socio-economic and political problems. East Darfur, South Darfur, West Kordofan, Al Gezira, Al Gedaref and Kassala states are amongst the highest affected states with more than 93% localities having WASH severity 4 & 5. In these states, lack of WASH services is exacerbating the health and nutrition problems. Reports showed that severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and WASH-related diseases are still very high among IDPs, returnees, and other vulnerable populations. The condition needs humanitarian intervention and working on long-term sustainability of WASH facilities.
Following the war erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on 15 April 2023, Sudan is facing one of fastest unfolding crises globally, the humanitarian situation in Sudan is dire, with 24.8 million people in need of assistance, including 6 million internally displaced. The main sectors of need are health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and FSL, which are driven by multiple factors, such as conflict, insecurity, social tensions, climate shocks, poor governance, and disease outbreaks. The ongoing conflict has worsened the situation for all families, but especially for the vulnerable groups, such as new and protracted IDPs, refugees, and returnees. These groups live in overcrowded conditions and face overcrowded conditions and face repeated emergencies and displacement. This project aims to contribute to lifesaving of targeted communities in Khartoum,
Aljazeera, Al Gedaref, Kassala, East Darfur, South Darfur and West Kordofan through provision of timely WASH services to cope up current emergencies and respond to future emergencies. Alight will provide inclusive WASH services that respond to the immediate needs of affected people and implement activities that contribute to the long-term sustainability of services. 
The following are main activities:
• Repair, Maintain and Rehabilitation of existing nonfunctioning water supply systems
• Upgrade (solarize) and extend/expand water supply systems.
• Installation of Emergency sanitation services for emergency affected communities
• Establish emergency water supply systems through treatment of surface water or
through distribution of water treatment chemicals.
• Distribution of essential WASH NFIs.
• Support operation and maintenance of the water supply systems, and sanitation facilities.
• Conduct water treatment and ensuring water qualities.
• Increasing awareness and behavioral change on hygiene, sanitation & environmental practices.
• Promoting community participation and improving sense of ownership.
• Support communities and local governments in improving the management of O&M of water supply systems.
 The specific target locations (sub-localities and villages) will be selected through joint need assessments and identification of hotspot areas for emergencies to maximize the impact; the project prioritizes service delivery for IDPs, returnees, and vulnerable populations affected by emergencies (including WASH-related epidemics and water resource-related conflicts) and facing severe acute malnutrition (SAM) & high food insecurity. This project contributes to overall national and state level humanitarian assistance initiatives by implementing the humanitarian WASH response activities responding to their immediate need of emergency affected people and building resilience to future emergencies, i.e. by implementing community & local government empowerment activities. The project aimed to reach 841,645 most in-needed people in the targeted areas. The project facilitates community participation especially women, girls, young people, and marginalized groups and engage throughout the different stage of project assessment and implementation.

project_name: Provision of health and nutrition lifesaving interventions for IDPs and host community and vulenrable residents in South Darfur, East Darfur, Al Jazeera, Khartoum, Kassala and Gedaref states
project_objective:
The project aims at improving equitable access to quality lifesaving curative and preventive services through the provision of primary health care and nutrition interventions. This will contribute at reducing morbidity and mortality including those related to vaccine preventable diseases, maternal complications and malnutrition. The project tends to address the health and nutrition needs mainly targeting people affected by displacements resulting from conflicts that erupted from 15 April 2023, causing displacements, affecting health system which was already weak and resulting in inaccessibility to essential services to IDPs and hosting communities as well as people residing in conflicts affected areas. The targeted states are Kassala, Gedaref, East Darfur, South Darfur, Al Jazirah and Khartoum states which are either conflicts affected areas or hosting many IDPs all in need to access health and nutrition services. 
Under health, the project tends to support 24 static health facilities and 4 mobile clinics that will provide lifesaving health care services including outpatient department for communicable diseases and common non communicable diseases, provide EPI services, provide reproductive health and maternal health services, outbreak prevention and response and mental health and psychosocial support.  
Under nutrition the project will provide nutrition services including (i)screening of malnutrition for early detection and treatment of malnourished children and PLWs; (ii) Outpatient therapeutic feeding, (iii)Targeted supplementary feeding, (iv) Infant and young child nutrition. In addition, Alight plans to conduct one nutrition smart survey in East Darfur, the locality will be determined based on nutrition cluster priority to inform on nutrition situation and required efforts. The target is to support 24 fixed OTP/TSFP sites, 3 stabilization centers and 4 mobile clinics. 
Considering that some facilities have been looted or damaged, a deep analysis will be done, and the project tends to rehabilitate/refurnish health facilities accordingly.  
Alight will collaborate with stakeholders including FMOH, SMOH, HAC, health cluster and nutrition cluster at national and state level to ensure coordinated efforts and interventions based on the most in needs for rationale use of resources. Considering volatile situation in Sudan, Alight will rely on 4 Ws and capacity and gaps mapping from health and nutrition clusters. Where necessary the project will adapt to evolving situation including change of locations or modality to ensure the project responds to emergency health and nutrition to the most in needs. 
Alight will also coordinate with UN agencies such as WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA and WFP either directly or through SMOH to ensure a constant supply chain of essential supplies such as medicines, vaccines, nutrition supplies and transport of supplies to Alight supported facilities will be arranged though this project.
Alight plans to ensure integrated approach is used as much as possible, where other sectors such as WASH, protection are available, referral mechanism will be discussed, and all relevant staff will be oriented. As part of integration, WASH education will be integrated in IEC at facility level, latrines and hand washing facilities rehabilitated/renovated while waste will be collected and disposed in safe manner.  IYCF counseling will be integrated in IMCI, ANC, EPI and post-natal care. While on the other hand, parents attending nutrition services will be targeted with messages on EPI as well as risk communication and community engagements on any outbreak that may occur in targeted locations. 
The project targets 342,056 people (310,000 for health and 32,056 for nutrition) among them 40% are IDPs, 31% are host communities and 27% are non -IDPs but residing in conflicts affected areas. The project target 47% female and 53% male while children cover more than 50% of targeted people. The project includes people with disabilities.

project_name: Emergency Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance in conflict frontlines and IDP-hosting states from North-East to South-West Sudan
project_objective:
Due to the conflict in Sudan since the 15th April, 2023, humanitarian needs have increased dramatically across all sectors. Repercussions of economic collapse, fueled by disrupted supply chains, mass displacement, and the destruction of critical infrastructure have triggered a surge in the prices of food, rent, and basic commodities. The humanitarian landscape has witnessed a 57% increase in the number of people in need (OCHA), with 37% of the population in a state of severe food insecurity (IPC). With 65% of displaced people currently residing in host communities (IOM-DTM), sharp increases in rental costs are a growing concern, as well as the ability for IDPs living in collective gathering sites to meet key non-food item (NFI) and WASH needs. In response to these significant and evolving needs, Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) is a priority modality of assistance. Market assessment findings indicate functioning markets in over 95% of surveyed areas (REACH), MPCA offers a significant advantage in providing greater flexibility for recipients to address their specific and evolving needs and affected populations have themselves identified MPCA as a key priority. The value of the MPCA modality within the Sudanese context is also underscored by the security landscape, as humanitarian access to areas with the highest needs is at best unstable and often fully restricted. As such, remote cash transfers offer strong potential to reach vulnerable populations not directly accessible to humanitarian actors.  

This project aims to continue Acted's efforts to offer timely, impactful, and flexible assistance to conflict-affected populations through MPCA, in complementarity with its multisectoral operations. As such, MPCA will constitute a core element of Acted’s multisectoral mobile CCCM assistance package to displaced individuals and in-need host communities. Where Acted does not have direct programmatic access, such as Al Jazeera and Khartoum, MPCA will be leveraged as a primary modality of remote assistance to conflict-affected communities. This will be implemented in close collaboration with local NGOs and CBOs with on-the-ground access to the targeted communities, to enhance follow-up, beneficiary engagement, local community participation, and activity monitoring. Beneficiary identification will be conducted alongside with local communities, other INGO actors (notably the Cash Consortium of Sudan, of which Acted is a member), and the relevant clusters, to ensure MPCA support reaches the most in-need individuals whilst avoiding duplication of assistance. Acted will prioritise blanket provision of support within specific localities level, as informed by multiple data sources including but not limited to the HNO Severity Ranking and People in Need, as well as internal rapid needs assessments. Blanket targeting thus prioritises conflict sensitivity and a “do no harm” approach, by mitigating tensions within communities that arise due to targeting based on individual status. Acted is partnering with multiple Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to maximise sustained coverage, according to the security situation and viability of different cash transfer modalities across the targeted areas. Modalities of cash transfer vary according to security, access, and the needs of affected individuals within the targeted localities. Where access is possible, direct cash distribution to individual households, in partnership with local stakeholders and community representatives (in particular, representatives of people with specific needs), will be implemented. Prior to the finalization of direct distribution arrangements, a gender and safety assessment will be conducted for each distribution to ensure targeted households have safe and equal access to MPCA support. In all cases, Acted’s MEAL staff will conduct beneficiary verification and post-distribution monitoring to ensure that MPCA sufficiently reaches and meets the needs of the targeted households.

project_name: Emergency Protection assistance in Khartoum, Gedaref, Sennar, White Nile, Blue Nile and Al Jazeera States
project_objective: Since the start of the conflict on April 15th, 2023, protection needs in Sudan have dramatically increased amid continued intense fighting, physical violence, sexual and gender-based violence, and mass displacement. Sudan has been qualified as the worst displacement crisis in the world. Reports of physical violence committed against residents in conflict hotspots and IDPs as well as GBV committed against women and girls have increased since the eruption of the conflict. With schools being turned into emergency shelters for IDPs, 19 million Sudanese children in Sudan have lost access to education since April 2023 (UNICEF). The already fragile social protection system in Sudan has collapsed with the conflict due to the destruction of critical infrastructures. As a result, 19.9 million individuals are in need of general, GBV and CP protection assistance according to the HNRP 2024 for Sudan. The present project aims at continuing Acted's efforts to offer timely and quality General Protection, GBV-related and CP assistance to conflict-affected populations and IDPs. In all locations, Acted and its partners will map out available protection services and conduct safety audits to ensure all protection risks are identified and survivors or at-risk individuals get appropriate reliable information on possible assistance. In Gedaref, Sennar, Blue Nile, White Nile and Al Jazeera, Acted will establish CBPNs, taking into consideration gender, age and disability, as well as Male Agents of Change Groups (MACGs). Acted protection staff will provide capacity-building to the CBPNs, MAGCs and other humanitarian actors on general protection, CP and GBV issues. In non-conflict zones, Acted will train health care workers in Clinical Management of Rape (CMR). In IDP-hosting states, Acted and its partners will conduct awareness-raising sessions on protection issues and referral pathways to mitigate against protection risks in IDP sites. In Khartoum state, Acted will financially and technically support Women’s Groups, assisting displaced women, to provide PSS activities for children and support to GBV survivors. These activities across all locations will contribute to the creation of a more protective environment through community-led interventions to address protection issues. In addition, in all states except Khartoum, Acted will also support IDPs transiting to another location with transportation cost covered though IPA. Acted will also provide case management for adult and children IDPs remaining in their first location of displacement, which will comprise of in-kind assistance and cash for health referral. When feasible, CP services will be provided through PSS and case management to ensure all identified at-risk children receive assistance. For women and girls in reproductive age, Acted will distribute monthly dignity kits. Thus, Acted will be able to provide quality and timely protection assistance to at-risk individuals in hard-to-reach and other areas.

project_name: Continuity of cardiac specialised health care service provision in Khartoum State
project_objective:
The project aims at decreasing the high morbidity and mortality rate across Sudan by providing life-saving access to INR consultations and specialised cardiac consultations and surgeries in response to the effect of the Rheumatic Heart Disease (RHD), to decrease the prevalence of chronic cardiac disease across the Country. EMERGENCY Salam Centre for Cardiac Surgery in Khartoum has remained open since the onset of the conflict in Sudan and the closure of it's services may leave thousand of patients without life-saving therapy and treatment. 3,500 cardiological examinations will be provided and 500 admissions will be granted (including cardiosurgery). In light of the above-described scenario, in Khartoum the situation is becoming increasingly difficult. 
The ongoing fighting, lasting for over 9 months, has severely damaged most of the city's 
infrastructure. As a result, the majority of hospitals are shuttered, due to either physical damage or 
an inability to offer assistance owing to the scarcity of medications and essential supplies. In the dire 
humanitarian context highlighted, it is of utmost importance to ensure the continuity of high-quality 
health services for cardiac patients. 
The rheumatic heart disease, endemic in Sudan, is one of the leading causes of mortality among 
young people in developing countries. This disease inflicts severe damage to the heart valves, 
compromising their proper functioning and leading to the progressive deterioration of the patients' 
quality of life, ultimately resulting in death. This issue significantly affects regions in Africa, Southeast 
Asia, and the Western Pacific. 
Unfortunately, few healthcare facilities have the capacity to provide adequate prevention and 
treatment for this infection, making rheumatic fever the primary cause of cardiovascular diseases in 
children and adolescents, especially in the age group between 5 and 15 years, in Africa. The root 
cause of this critical issue lies predominantly in the limited access to care, especially for children, 
stemming from the absence of free services, inadequate healthcare facilities, and a shortage of 
qualified medical personnel. In this situation, it is crucial to emphasize the significance of the Salam Centre and its uniqueness. 
The Salam Centre for Cardiac Surgery is the only facility in Sudan (and in the Region) that provides 
comprehensive cardiac services completely free of charge. Furthermore, for cardiac patients 
undergoing surgery at the Salam Centre, receiving the necessary medications, therapies, and post-operative examinations is a matter of life or death. It is essential that the Salam Centre can continue 
its operations as planned, as it represents an essential resource in addressing this serious healthcare 
issue

project_name: Provision of lifesaving services and improve protection environment in Jazeera, Blue Nile, South Kordofan, and Central and West Darfur States
project_objective:
The conflict in Sudan, over nine months now, resulted severe deterioration in the protection environment and leaving almost the entire populations in dire humanitarian needs. This project contributes to achieving HRP SO1 ensuring provision of safe, timely, principled and gender-responsive life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable groups to reduce mortality and morbidity in areas with high severity of need or at risk of a further deterioration of critical humanitarian needs; SO2 to directly respond to the conflict-driven protection needs of crisis-affected people through principled and conflict-sensitive assistance and advocacy as well as prevent and mitigate emerging protection risks, according to international norms and standards.
 WR protection interventions are founded on bodies of laws such as human rights, international humanitarian law and refugee law, and actions are guided by humanitarian principles, and international standards in humanitarian actions. WR ensures conflict sensitivity and inclusiveness using age, gender, disability and diversity approach to create and support a peaceful co-existence between IDPS, nondisplaced and host communities and provide case management, lifesaving services to persons with specific protection needs through provision of in kind or cash assistance and MHPSS to adults and timely response to mitigate protection risks, human rights violations and other forms of violence. WR will build relationships with and among affected populations, IDPs, nondisplaced and host communities with the goal of enabling them to identify and respond to their own protection needs through establishment and support of community-based protections mechanisms. With the support of the community-based structures and other key stakeholders, WR will engage in protection monitoring to inform timely response and prevent exposure of women, girls and other vulnerable populations to harm, as well as identify needs and gaps in service provision. WR will collaborate and enhance capacities of partners and authorities to prevent and mitigate risk of evictions of affected population. 
WR will provide life-saving timely and quality GBV and child protection services, including case management of GBV survivors and vulnerable children particularly UASC and with disabilities, psychosocial support, legal assistance and reinforce the referral pathways. WR will support establishment of women centers and rehabilitate existing ones, while also provide running cost. To economically empower GBV survivors, they will be provided with livelihood opportunities and vocational skills. To ensure coordination, collaboration, advocacy and information sharing, WR with actively support state and national level protection, child protection and GBV working groups, conduct awareness among all stakeholders and ensuring participation of men and boys on the prevention and response to GBV risk including safety audits.  WR will establish child friendly spaces where children will receive structured and sustained psychosocial support activities. Caregivers and partners will also receive MHPSS and training on child protection. WR will conduct awareness raising activities and information dissemination on child protection and PSEA to IDPs, host communities and nondisplaced communities.
WR will ensure conscious and intentional efforts to avoid all actions that will further expose the populations from harm and ensuring all staff, volunteers, contractors and workers are equipped with knowledge and adhere to the organizations policy on prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as ensuring confidential and accessible feedback mechanism. WR will closely collaborate with protection clusters and sub-clusters, and partners for effective and impactful response and advocacy to enhance well-being of affected populations.

project_name: Emergency WASH Interventions for IDPs, Returnees and Host Community in Central & West Darfur States, Aljazeera, South Kodufan, Blue Nile, and Khartoum in Sudan.
project_objective:
The purpose of this project is to provide lifesaving WASH services to conflict affected vulnerable populations, including IDPs, Returnees and Host Community in Aljazeera, South Kordofan, Blue Nile, Khartoum, and Central & West Darfur States in Sudan. The project targets 586,300 crisis-affected people (239,211 women, 229,829men, 59,802 girls, 57,458 boys), including 196,800 IDPS, 163500 Host Community, 226,000 Non displaced community in above-mentioned states in Sudan.  
The Sudan 2024 HRNP depicted critically deteriorating WASH coverage that even existed before the ongoing conflict. The conflict led to further destruction of water infrastructures and disruptions in the WASH supply chain, and collapse of the revenue system to the extent that employees of water and sanitation facilities have not been paid since the crisis began. Without government subsidies, critical supply shortages, inflation, and decreasing community incomes, the population increasingly resorts to unsafe water and sanitation practices and adopts unhygienic behaviors. The increasing concentration of newly displaced populations strains the already scarce WASH resources. Due to limited financial means and capacity, neither communities nor the government can sustain existing WASH services or establish new ones to address the growing needs. The ongoing outbreak of cholera has claimed 131 lives, with 4,114 confirmed. The Interagency rapid needs assessment conducted in Central and West Darfur in September 2023 showed that in security in all the states of CD&WD plus some clashes between SAF&RSF is still remains the main cause of displacement for more than 300,000 people and death of more than 2000 innocent civilians in Geneina, Sirba and Kreneik and localities in West Darfur and displacement of many women and children from Nertiti, Zalingei, Mukjar and Azoum areas in Central Darfur state. The displaced persons have lost all their valuables including residences, livestock and crops. The ethnic conflict in North and Western Ethiopia contributed to migration of around 15,500 refugees to Blue Nile. All the vulnerable people have poor access to clean water supply, sanitation and hygiene facilities. The inflation affected the purchasing power of poor families, accelerating the food insecurity and malnutrition levels increase the venerability of the affected people of the society - IDPs, refugees and hosting. 
In response to the first strategic objective (SO1) to provide safe, timely, principled and gender-responsive life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable groups to reduce mortality and morbidity in areas with high severity of need or at risk of a further deterioration of critical humanitarian needs, this project aims to ensuring access to basic water, sanitation and hygiene services for crisis-affected populations. Firstly, interventions ensure drinking water from an improved source with a collection time of not more than 30 minutes roundtrip, including queuing to affected people. People targeted with basic water services will benefit from new installations and maintenance, operations, and rehabilitation of existing handpumps, water yards, protected wells, check-dams, and haffirs where feasible. Secondly, project aims to ensure improved access to adequate, protected, and gender sensitive sanitation services for vulnerable populations. Interventions will ensure the installation, rehabilitation, and use of ventilated improved pit latrines (VIP), pit latrines with slabs. Household latrines (basic), latrines shared between two households (limited), and communal latrines  to reduce open deification, and to have their household latrine for family use. Thirdly, the project will establish information dissemination system at the community level guided by trained community hygiene Promotors, 1 promoter per 50 HHs to ensure effective awareness razing for behavior change. Women and girls who are part of the  displaced population will receive personal dignity kits.

project_name: Response to urgent protection needs (GP, CP, GBV) among IDPs and Host Communities in Sudan
project_objective: Alight will support community-based approaches that enhance protection for all Persons of Concern and strengthen community-based protection structures (CBPNs, Child Protection Committees, Women groups..) which will identify protection concerns, raise awareness on protection-related issues, respond to issues at the community level where appropriate, and refer to relevant partners based on need. Alight will continue to build their capacity and ensure they are operational. This project includes life-saving intervention for the affected population, including case management for PSNs, GBV survivors, UASC and other children at risk, PSS for adults, GBV survivors and children, including children with disabilities, cash or in-kind assistance depending on the case, provision of dignity kits. Alight and its partners will improve monitoring, identification and reporting of protection incidents and analyze trends including grave child rights violations, including through the use of focus groups and specific protection assessments. Alight will support timely and targeted responses to protection incidents, information sharing, and awareness-raising along with other protection measures to mitigate protection risks and respond to actual protection incidents and concerns. Alight intends to establish and support temporary Women Centers and Child Friendly Spaces as entry point for protection activities, identification of cases, awareness raising and PSS and recreational activities. project_name: Protection of girls and boys in conflict and post-conflict areas in Sudan through quality preventative and remedial interventions
project_objective:
Across Sudan, girls and boys and their families face risks associated with conflict, violence and displacement including family separation, Sexual Gender-based Violence (SGBV), mine risk, psychological distress, and child labour, especially during the current Sudan Emergency. According to Sudan Situation Report (OCHA) of January 21th, 2024, about 7.6 million people have been displaced inside and outside Sudan since fighting broke out between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces on 15 April 2023. More than 13,000 people have been killed and another 26,000 injured since April 2023, according to ACLED and Federal Ministry of Health respectively. More than 9,700 suspected cholera cases, including 269 associated deaths, were reported as of 16 January 2024. Health partners provided 2.6 million patients with medicines and 1.8 million out-patient consultations across Sudan between 15 April and 31 December 2023.
Plan International in Sudan (PIS) will ensure the provision of timely and rights-based child protection services to the most deprived and marginalized girls and boys, especially those affected by conflict and displaced from their homes. These services will include case management; prevention and response to the needs of child victims of Sexual and Gender Based violence (SGBV); material support, service provider training, support services, and life skills training for extremely vulnerable children and adolescents affected by conflict; and safe places for play, recreation and the provision of psychosocial support to children displaced or affected by conflict.
To prevent and mitigate child protection risks in communities affected by conflict and displacement, PIS will strengthen the capacity of social workers, teachers, and law-enforcement staff, as well as investing in capacity building of the States Councils for Child Welfare and other humanitarian partners. In order to reinforce the resilience of communities and strengthen capacity of child protection institutions, Plan will support community-based child protection mechanisms and civil society organisations to disseminate information on relevant services and contribute to advocacy and the referral of child protection cases; and to promote safer environments for children, especially girls and those with disability.

project_name: Shelter /NFIs services for emergency affected people in, Khartoum, Al Jazeera, Kassala, Al Gedaref, Port Sudan, East Darfur, and South Darfur states
project_objective:
Timely life-saving Shelter and NFI assistance is essential to prevent physical hazard and ensure safety, security, and dignity of IDPs and vulnerable residents. The purpose of the project is to contribute to improving protection, safety & security, and dignity of new IDPs through provision of life-saving assistance, and extremely vulnerable people as well as PWSNs living in protracted displacement with more sustainable, emergency-recovery type of interventions. The project targets localities in Khartoum, Al Jazeera, East and
South Darfur states that experienced several displacements in 2023 and are still hotspot areas. The project basically targets two groups; first new crises-affected people will be provided with emergency shelter making materials & NFI assistance. Second, people living in protracted displacement will be supported with replenishment of S/NFI and shelter upgrading solutions. Based on the experience, in this project we planned to support 79,765 people (about 15,953 HHs) by ES/NFIs. To achieve the above purposes Alight will monitor situations, preparing hotspot areas and identifying affected & vulnerable communities, and raising awareness of the communities on hazards. We regularly coordinate with HAC and UNHCR to exchange information on existing humanitarian situations. Whenever responses are required (suppose conditions
worsen or new humanitarian conditions emerge such as displacement of people due to conflict or extreme hazard (drought/flood)) then Alight will trigger joint need assessment (with state level stakeholders), conduct joint verification exercises and response plans. Any response prioritization will be done through cluster conventional processes. Activities that are in line with cluster objectives and relevant to the locality culture and traditions are carefully selected and will be implemented to deliver effective responses.
Wherever and whenever possible Cash Base intervention (CBI) (up to 20% of total budget) will be applied to help households fulfill their S/NFI needs. Alight will engage local authorities, COR, HAC, UNHCR and other key partners and jointly monitor and Supervise distributions and conduct Post distribution evaluation and document learnings.
To make this project a success, Alight uses its leverage of cumulated knowledge and experience. During implementation, Alight will work with the communities and local administrations, mobilize its potential suppliers and transporters, which will help to timely responses. Also, in case NFI gaps occur in the market Alight will utilize the Core Pipeline to respond to emergencies. As much as possible uniformity of responses will be respected by applying standardized NFI packages and Standard Operating Procedures
(SOPs) developed by the ES/NFI cluster. Wherever necessary to deliver holistic response,
Alight will combine WASH and protection responses with the S/NFI distribution. As much as possible Alight will respect and take care of the environment, culture, traditions and local businesses. We will use environmentally friendly and culturally appropriate shelter materials, most of the procurements will be locally sourced, which will help to activate local economies. Alight also provides on-the-job training in building techniques of shelters that will be useful for developing self-reliance and resilience. To improve accountability, transparency in programming, and adherence to “Do no harm principles,” Alight will strengthen the capacity of staff (men, women, and youth) and local national NGOs through training in the complete package of PSET for emergency response. Additionally, Alight will implement the project by considering protection and accountability to the community and to the donor. Our MEAL system will gather important data and produce information. Communities will be provided with information about our
complaints and feedback systems and Alight document complaints, refer and take corrective measures.

project_name: Integrated response to nutrition, health and WASH emergencies affecting populations affected by conflict and displacement in Sudan's most severely affected regions.
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in Sudan, exacerbated by fighting that began in April 2023, has led to significant increases in humanitarian needs, particularly for the displaced population. Over 7.4 million people have been displaced, both within and outside Sudan, severely straining the already fragile health system. Many health facilities in conflict areas are non-functional, leaving two-thirds of the population without healthcare access. The prevalence of malnutrition is high and expected to worsen due to the compromised health system, poor Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services, and displacement.

The River Nile and Northern States, hosting significant numbers of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), are struggling with weakened basic services and increased demand from IDPs.In response to the critical situation, MedGlobal, alongside its health-focused partner, the Sudanese American Physicians’ Association (SAPA), is initiating a wide-ranging health, nutrition, and WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) program. This program aims to swiftly address and fulfill the immediate humanitarian needs of the communities in question, fostering rapid improvements in their living conditions. This strategic intervention is consistent with the goals and priorities of the State Ministry of Health, the Humanitarian Aid Commission, and various involved clusters.

The intervention includes the following activities:

**Wadi Halfa**:
- Operational support for Halfa Hospital and a mobile team in Argeen, offering integrated health, nutrition, and WASH services.
- Comprehensive healthcare services, including maternal and child health, newborn and childhood illness management, reproductive health, chronic disease management, and support for non-communicable diseases.
- WASH support with clean water trucking, construction of latrines, distribution of hygiene kits, and promotion activities.
- Mass screening for malnutrition in under-fives and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), with treatment programs for severe and moderate acute malnutrition.
- Community-based activities for malnutrition case finding and referrals, and support for SAM (Severe Acute Malnutrition) cases requiring medical attention.
- Enhancement of IYCF activities.
-1 SC
1-OTP 

**River Nile State**: (In partnership with SAPA)
- Support for two primary healthcare centers (PHCs) in Atbara and two mobile clinics.
- Provision of medicines, medical equipment, staff incentives, and operational support.

- WASH initiatives including water trucking, equipment for water supply improvement, latrine rehabilitation, and hygiene awareness.

This project aims to alleviate the humanitarian crisis in Sudan by providing essential health, nutrition, and WASH services to the affected communities, with a focus on the most vulnerable populations.

project_name: Integrated response to emergency needs in WASH, Child Protection, FSL and NFI-Shelter Health and Protection for recently displaced populations and other disaster-affected people in Sudan – WASH
project_objective:
This a complex +12-month intervention that aims to improve access to emergency services, address urgent needs and provide lifesaving and life sustaining emergency support within WASH to conflict and/or displaced-affected populations and vulnerable host communities through various areas in Darfur, Khartoum and Jazeera. Also, the project aims deploy life-saving WaSH interventions to ensure conflict-affected populations have access to safe drinking water, as well as minimum hygiene standards to mitigate the risk of waterborne diseases and protect people’s dignity. The project design integrates WASH with other sectors in different localities throughout Sudan which corresponds to the most recent crisis to an entrenched regional and national crisis. 3month into the conflict, the total estimate of IDPs across Sudan reached 2.6 million. The critical needs of 5,855,848 IDPs and 1,532,350 mixed cross borders movements (Dec 2023, IOM) add onto those of 25M overall identified by OCHA, and revolve around food, water, hygiene and sanitation, health, nutrition, and emergency shelter. If not addressed, they will lead to crisis into crisis, preventable outbreaks and an increase in the mortality due underlying causes. 
Considering the inconceivable suffering of the Sudanese population, TGH have coordinated it efforts to present a comprehensive WASH package of support to the internally displaced population as well as those hosting them in Darfur, Khartoum and Jazeera, as there are the most affected states since the beginning of the conflict in Sudan.  
TGH aims to support the communities through:
