project_name: Réponse multisectorielle d’urgence auprès des populations affectées par les déplacements dans la région de Diffa
project_objective:
La présente action vise à apporter une réponse multisectorielle d’urgence aux populations affectées par les déplacements dans les communes de Kablewa, Toumour et N’Gourti à travers des interventions en CCCM/Protection, WASH et Moyens d’existence. Elle vise à Améliorer les conditions de vie des ménages les plus vulnérables par le renforcement de l’accès aux services sociaux de base et par un renforcement économique, permettant aux ménages de renforcer leur résilience.
Acted mettra ainsi en œuvre des AGR pour promouvoir la diversification des ressources économiques pour assurer un accès inclusif, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées et les femmes (non-agriculteurs), aux activités économiques. Acted tiendra compte de la nécessité de mesures de protection au niveau communautaire, notamment en raison de la crise accrue en matière de protection et de déplacement, afin d'améliorer la qualité, la responsabilité et l'efficacité de la réponse tout en garantissant l'accès à la protection de base et aux services WASH pour les personnes les plus vulnérables touchées par le déplacement. Grâce à des activités de type CCCM en dehors des camps, la troisième ligne d'intervention vise à prendre en compte le lien intersectoriel entre le déplacement et l’accès aux moyens d’existence et à fournir un cadre de protection amélioré pour la population touchée par le déplacement. La qualité et l'impact de la réponse doivent s'améliorer avec i) le renforcement de la coordination des déplacements au niveau de la crise, ii) une meilleure participation des communautés affectées, iii) des mesures de protection communautaires améliorées, iv) et une meilleure responsabilisation de la réponse humanitaire. La coordination et la diffusion de l'information seront renforcées et un mécanisme de protection mis en place pour améliorer la qualité de la réponse apportée aux PDIs. En outre, compte tenu de l'impact évident de la crise des déplacements sur l'accès aux services WASH et le lien avec la sécurité alimentaire et la nutrition, l'accès aux services WASH doit être assuré pour contribuer à renforcer l'environnement protecteur.  Ce niveau de réponse fournira un cadre et une base pour une réponse plus intégrée par zone, à tous les niveaux.
La région de Diffa est confrontée à une série de crises multiformes à la fois sécuritaire, économique et environnementale qui entrainent d’importants déplacements de populations majoritairement provoqués par les attaques répétées des Groupes Armés Non Etatiques (GANEs) dans la région du Bassin du Lac Tchad. L’état d’urgence dans la région est en vigueur depuis 2015 suite aux attaques simultanées des GANEs sur les villes de Diffa et de Bosso . Ces facteurs d’insécurité sont aggravés par des facteurs tant structurels (faible gouvernance, pauvreté, manque d’opportunités économiques, chômage, faible niveau d’instruction des jeunes, etc.) que conjoncturels (tensions intercommunautaires entre éleveurs et agriculteurs par exemple). En raison de sa position géographique, la région de Diffa, exclusivement ciblée pour ce projet, se trouve particulièrement affectée. Sur les 707 133 personnes en situation de déplacement forcé que comptent le Niger , la région de Diffa en abrite à elle-seule 314 820, dont 137 573 réfugiés, 14 593 PDI, 34 139 nigériens résidant au Nigéria et forcés à fuir vers leur pays d’origine et 2 515 demandeurs d’asile . La région de Diffa étant la première région d’accueil des personnes en situation de déplacement forcé , s’en suit conséquemment une saturation des services de base et des difficultés accrues d’accès aux ressources.   Selon les chiffres publiés par le HNO 2023, 563 849 personnes auraient besoin d’assistance humanitaire dans la région. 
Acted est membre des Clusters SECAL, ABNA, Protection, GT Cash et co-facilitateur du cluster WASH. Cette implication lui permet de développer des synergies, d’harmoniser les pratiques d’intervention et de partager les informations programmatiques lors des réunions.

project_name: Increasing the resilience of most vulnerable IDPs in NWS through integrated SNFI support.
project_objective:
TAS has designed this proposal to provide Shelter and NFI assistance for the most affected people in NWS to improve their living conditions.
The project areas were selected to be within a severity scale of 3 and the highest PIN according to the WoS list.
The project will benefit these high priority areas by strengthening and enhancing the dignified living conditions in both in/ and off-camp locations. TAS will consider Do No harm principles, Cluster guidelines, matching with the context and ensuring the adhering to HLP rights to prevent any harm.
As the beginning of the project coordination communications with the SNFI cluster will be done in order to ensure that no overlapping occurs.
TAS will seek to achieve the following deliverables:
- Provision of Cash for Winter assistance (180 USD per HHs) for provision of seasonal and supplementary NFIs such as of heating fuel, stoves, winter clothing kits and winter NFI kits. This activity will be through voucher modality (target: 25,000 individuals /5,000 HHs - $180 USD per HHs).
- Installation and construction of 520 dignified Shelters/temporary transitional shelters (target: 2,600 individuals/ 520 HHs - 520 Shelter units)
- Improving the Site Infrastructure/ HH level improvements implemented (target: 16,460 individuals /3292 HHs) through land preparation, drainage system, water & Sanitation networks, and lighting poles in addition to all relevant infrastructure needed
- Rehabilitation of minor repairs to damaged and affected houses -600 houses (target: 3000 individuals/ 600 HHs - 600 Shelters).
- Rehabilitation of of damaged or unfinished housing  (Moderate and Severe) -600 houses (target: 3000 individuals/ 600 HHs - 600 Shelters).
The total estimated beneficiaries of the proposed project are as follows:
- Shelter Component: 22,460 individuals / 4492 HHs
- NFI Component: 25,000 individuals / 5,000 HHS.
Following the priorities identified in the Humanitarian Response Plan 2023, TAS has designed this project to enhance dignified living and address acute needs for 9,492 HHs/ 47,460 individuals living in Idleb and Aleppo with different ages and vulnerable cases (23 % men, 25 % women, 26 % Boys, and 27% girls ) taking into consideration Gender and age diversity through integrated Shelter and NFI interventions.
All activities within the proposed project will be according to the Shelter cluster objectives and will be designed according to the SPHERE standards.
In addition, the planned intervention will mainstream protection principles especially “Do no harm” throughout the project cycle by considering the different needs of men, women, boys, and girls. During this project, TAS will consult with the community and individual IDPs taking into account the specific need of each group, TAS also will involve the women and girls through Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) during the community outreach plan.
The main objective of the proposed project is to reach 47,460individuals targeting most vulnerable men, women, boys and girls and prioritize family members with high vulnerabilities according to the beneficiaries selection criteria (female/single/child-headed households, IDP status, no source of income and support, people with disabilities, elderly,...etc.).
TAS will ensure high-level coordination with all parties involved in the project (SNFI cluster, OCHA Clusters, Donors, local authorities, other NGOs, and other related parties) to implement the project in good quality and avoid any duplication.

project_name: Provision of emergency WASH services to vulnerable communities in Jonglei and Upper Nile State
project_objective:
Chronic WASH needs have a significant impact on living standards amongst communities, thereby contributing to several vulnerabilities. Different gender groups are affected uniquely by stressing factors. Low levels of WASH adversely affect coping mechanisms of already vulnerable rural populations. Correlations are evident amongst low WASH and high malnutrition, GBV and food insecurity data sets from the states of Jonglei and Upper Nile. 
Christian Mission for Development (CMD) works in Greater Upper Nile and Equatoria providing much needed support to vulnerable communities. The project will be implemented in the counties of Ayod, Duk, Nyirol, Twic East, Bor South and Fangak (Jonglei) and Renk, Nasir, Maiwut and Longechuk (Upper Nile State). CMD envisages an opportunity to provide much needed WASH services through an integrated approach aimed at reducing mortality and morbidity amongst women, girls, boys, men, the elderly and persons with special needs. The project will seek to enhance supply of sustainable access to safe and clean water (15l/p/d), dignified, inclusive and adequate access to sanitation services and opportunities aimed influencing social behavior and norms in relation to personal, household, communal and institutional hygiene. 
Community led durable solutions in the provision of services will be sought through the establishment and upgrade of flood resilient WASH infrastructure, the roll out of sustainable initiatives to access to water and sanitation. 
A total of 22,222 persons will be reached (58% of these female) in the counties of Ayod, Duk, Nyirol, Twic East, Bor South and Fangak (Jonglei) and Renk, Nasir, Maiwut and Longechuk (Upper Nile State)

project_name: Provision of essential healthcare services to crisis-affected vulnerable communties in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Eastern Equatoria States
project_objective:
The proposed response plan seeks to contribute to provision of quality health care to crisis-affected people, prevent and respond to health threats, and strengthen the health system in need (IPC3+) in Ayod, Uror, Fangak (Jonglei state), Ulang (Upper Nile State) and Kapoeta East, Kapoeta South, Kapoeta North (Eastern Equatoria State) through the implementation of CO1#: Improve equitable access to life-saving essential quality health care services including maternal, child, and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment of common illnesses, disability, MHPSS, and GBV health services; CO#2: Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases, and CO#3: Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms. CMD 2024 HRP aligns with its strategic goal to contribute to reduction of mortality and morbidity rate through quality health care services to communities. This also aligns well with 2024 cluster HRP objectives of saving lives, reducing health risks, and enhancing coping and recovery.

In response to the arising Health needs CMD will focus on the following services including maternal, child, adolescent, sexual and reproductive health, common and chronic diseases, neglected tropical diseases, MHPSS (Mental Health and Psychosocial support) and GBV (Gender Based Violence). The response will also improve sexual reproductive health services of EmONC (emergency newborn and obstetric care), family planning, PMTCT (prevention of mother to child transmission), Clinical Management of Rape and supplies for vulnerable women and girls. The response will use referral mechanism to enhance efficiency, integration, and quality of care. The response will follow Universal Health Coverage principles and prioritize prevention, preparedness, response, and mitigation for vulnerable groups. The response will also continue EVD (Ebola Virus Disease) prevention, preparedness, and readiness activities, as South Sudan faces the threat of EVD and other viral hemorrhagic fevers. The response will support health facilities and community-based systems to serve people in need. The response will also strengthen technical, operational, and field coordination with partners and authorities. 

The response will also support disease surveillance and reporting system and preposition medical supplies and equipment in areas affected by Sudan Humanitarian Crisis, IDPs and floods.
CMD response will be aligned with the National, State and County MOH, CMD HRP plan considers the new Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP) 2023-2027 and specific implementation strategic and plans; the National Health Policy, 2022 Pharmaceutical Policy and Strategy and National Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Strategic Plan 2012.

The project will directly target 22,200 host communities & IDPs of which (60% female) including boys and girls of under 5 year old and pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Among the target groups will be 51 male and female Persons With Disabilities (PWD). The model of implementation shall be through thirteen static sites, seven mobile clinics and the support to community-based case management.

project_name: Provision of Gender-responsive & Disability-inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Crisis-affected Children & Youth in Duk, Akobo, Ulang, Longechuk & Pibor Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States and Greater Pibor Administrative Area
project_objective:
The aim of CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2024 is to provide a gender-responsive and disability-inclusive increased school enrolment and attendance for 7, 256 (3, 265 girls & 3, 991 boys)  children and youth , including 725 (326 girls & 399 boys) children with disabilities (CWDs), in a manner that improves the quality of their education and promotes their protection, mental health and wellbeing in 25 schools (5 ECD, 15 Primary & 5 Secondary) through the facility of 100 (25 female & 100 male) teachers and the support of 150 (50 female & 100 male) PTA members in crisis-induced situations across Duk & Akobo Counties in Jonglei State, Ulang & Longechuk Counties in Upper Nile State and Pibor County in Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA).

Of the total target 7, 506 (3, 340 female & 4166 male), children account for roughly 96.6% or exactly 7, 256 (3, 265 girls & 3, 991 boys), spread in 25 target schools (5 ECD, 15 Primary & 5 Secondary). The total number of children with disabilities (CWDs) stands at 725 (326 girls & 399 boys)), constituting 10% of 7, 256. Children originating from the Host, IDP & Returnee segments of the target population account for 50%, 29%, and 21% of 7, 256 respectively. These translate into 3, 628 (1, 632 girls & 1, 996 boys) from the Host; 2, 104 (946 girls & 1, 158 boys) from IDP; and 1, 524 (685 girls & 839 boys) from Returnee families in the 5 communities of Duk, Akobo, Ulang, Longechuk & Pibor Counties.

100 (25 female & 75 male) teachers and 150 (50 female & 100 male) SMC/PTA members will support the target 25 schools to strengthen the technical, organizational, and institutional capacity of County Education Departments (CEDs) to inject local energy that builds professional and community capital to support children’s learning & achievement in the five Counties. CMD will work in an integrated manner and exploring linkages that exist with WASH, Health, and Nutrition Clusters. By working together, we shall include an integrated component of WASH, Health & Nutrition, specifically addressing critical WASH gaps in the schools through rehabilitating toilets and hand-washing facilities; and promoting hygiene to avert disease outbreak.  Health-wise, we shall also target actions to prevent HIV/AIDS and STIs through raising awareness and reflections on prevention and response, thus, improving the sexual and reproductive health of girls and women, boys, and men.  Furthermore, dignity kits are provided to girls in upper grades (P5-P8) and secondary schools as a preventive measure to assure school attendance and completion in any given academic year.

CMD will focus on reducing risks and strengthening protective factors for SEA victims/survivors and mainstream effective female inclusion in all stages of project design and implementation. Particular attention will be given to tailoring activities that respect cultural norms and traditions for female beneficiaries. The Project will involve women, girls, and other at-risk groups in all aspects of programming while being duly cautious where their inclusion poses a potential security risk or increases their risk of SEA. There are significant risks associated with SEA documentation, in relation to data protection. Failure to ensure information security can expose survivors, in particular, to harm, e.g. reprisal attacks by perpetrators, stigma and ostracism by their families/ communities. This means that SEA documentation must be carried out with great care.

The key strategy is to use primary and secondary schools acting as buffer spaces against acts of sexual, physical, or psychological violence inflicted on children due to stereotypes and roles or norms attributed to or expected of them on the basis of their sex or gendered identity; and promote crisis-affected children’s academic achievement through gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics.

project_name: Emergency and Resilience food security and livelihood response to Food insecure households in Jonglei and Upper Nile states
project_objective:
The proposed response plan seeks to contribute to food security and livelihoods of the persons in need (IPC3+) in Renk, Ulang, Nasir counties of Upper Nile state and Ayod, Bor South, Uror, Twic East, Duk and Nyirol counties in Jonglei state of South Sudan. Achievements will be through CO1: Conditional and conditional food assistance, CO2: Increased food production through in kind support of farming inputs, fishing kits, livestock restock treatment and vaccination, CO3: Capacity Building on Good Agronomic Practices for both trainers and farmers, training of community animal health workers, market support through livestock and seed fairs and strengthening livestock, fishery and farming value chains through investment of post-harvest handling equipment and technologies and anticipatory actions on disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and ecosystem management and restoration through tree planting and agroforestry, dike construction , dissemination of early warning signs among others.  
The targeted beneficiaries are 20,000 households (individuals; 24% women, 16% men, 36% girls and 24% boys) consisting of 10,000 hosts communities, 6,000  returnees, 2,000 refugees and 2,000 IDPs. Beneficiary by type will be determined through baseline surveys.

Community based participatory approach will be adopted through Accountability to Affected Population (AAP) committees (consisting of RRC representatives, Boma chiefs, Women leaders, Youth Leaders, County Agricultural Department Representative) and through Project management committees. Indicators like household status (host, IDP, returnees and refugees), gender markers (targeted male and female) and special/minority groups like Child-headed, Elderly and Female-headed households under IPC 3+ will be screened before approval of the beneficiary list.

Continuous monitoring will be done throughout the project cycles to ensure quality project outcomes are realised within the allocated timeframe. Community representative committees (AAPs and PMCs) and donors will take part in the monitoring process and act as a platform for complaint-feedback mechanisms. This feedback will be included in the implementation and project designs where applicable.

Sustainability of the project will be realised through active involvement of the community stakeholders throughout the project cycle making them adopt and propagate the knowledge acquired.

project_name: Provision of integrated lifesaving nutrition intervention to Vulnerable communities (Children Under 5 and Pregnant and Lactating Mothers) in Ayod and Uror Counties (Jonglei State).
project_objective:
The project is a 2024 intervention to mitigate humanitarian crises in Ayod and Uror Counties (Jongei State). The aim of the project is to ensure provision of needs-based emergency aid to prevent or decrease morbidities, mortality and acute malnutrition especially for vulnerable people in acute humanitarian crises triggered by fight and displacement, droughts, floods and anticipated periods of hunger. This project will contribute to the overall strategic objectives of the 2024 HRP and the 4 sectoral Nutrition cluster objectives to assist vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host community comprising of 5,293 households in Ayod and Uror Counties of Jonglei state by #1; increasing equitable access and utilization of quality nutrition services to prevent malnutrition and build resilience, #2; increasing equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for early detection and treatment of wasting, #3; Enhancing nutrition situation and program monitoring, analysis, and utilization of nutrition information, and #4; Strengthening coordination & integrated programming for equitable access to services that address key drivers of malnutrition among vulnerable children and women. The 2024 IPC report states that climate change continues to impact different sectors, particularly agriculture, which is one of the most climate-sensitive economic sectors. Above normal rainfall for the fourth consecutive year in 2024 led to prolonged floooding, which impacted areas that had not ooded in previous years. Other key drivers for malnutrition include low agriculture production and localized conflicts that continues to disrupt livelihoods and forcing displacement of people in Ayod and Uror counties. 

Due to vastness of Ayod and Uror Counties, CMD will maintain establish OTP/TSFP sites that includes those within MoH structures, standalone and outreach sites/teams including further decentralisation in Ayod,Uror counties (islands, canal and cattle camps). Reduction of morbidity and mortality rate for the IPC 4 populations in line with CMAM Protocol through detection and treatment of children under 5 reaching at least 4,532 children U5 with SAM, 8,085 children U5 with MAM and 7,796 MAM- PLW in Ayod and CH<5 with SAM 7,480,CH<5 with MAM 11,512 and MAM PLW 10,428. SAM Children with medical complication will be referred to existing stabilisation centres. At the community level, Community Nutrition Volunteers will conduct active case finding to strengthen early detection and timely referral of malnourished children and PLW, both through routine community screening and family MUAC Approach. 

The programme will support nutrition specific, and nutrition sensitive sectors as follows:- Apply in-country (MoH) CMAM and MIYCN technical guidelines in the implementation of the program, Strengthening care practices and services for maternal, infant and young child nutrition (MIYCN) by improving management of peer groups (MTMSG, FTFSG); actualizing of Positive Deviance Study (PD) enquiry finding, scaling-up SBCC; promotion of Exclusive breast feed, diet diversity, of Acute Malnutrition in Infants (MAMI) through counselling; implementation of Baby Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI)  in Ayod Hospital and Strengthen Family MUAC, growth monitoring and promotion, VASD for children under 5 years. Project will link with food security activities e.g Promotion Model, IGA, kitchen and increase community vegetable gardens to care givers and peer groups. Continuous improvement on ECD activities in the nutrition sites; promotion of nutrition,supplementations of older children, adolescents through collaboration with PTA, School clubs by ensuring BCC and supplementation for prevention of micronutrient deficiencies, training Youths and school heads on how to take MUAC.CMD will work to improve Nutrition information data quality check, and documentation of lessons that will generate knowledge.

project_name: Adolescents and young people supported with integrated protection programing in North Syria
project_objective: Mercy Corps aims to strengthen our protection interventions using a gender sensitive lens to support the overall protection cluster objectives towards the provision of quality integrated protection services. Mercy Corps will focus the intervention on vulnerable adolescent girls and boys and young women utilizing community-based approaches taking into considerations the existing resources in the communities. Informed through a conducted multi-sector needs assessment in September 2023, Mercy Corps will expand on its commitment to integrating protection outcomes into other sectoral interventions including cash, food security and livelihoods, WASH and social cohesion. Mercy corps will implement projects through 2 different but complementary modalities: direct implementation and though local partners in north east Syria. Mercy Corps projects aim to ensure vulnerable adolescents and young people exposed to acute and/or protracted crises are safe, protected and more resilient and have the capacity to address root causes of inequalities. This will be achieved through 1) Opportunities in livelihood and resources including cash grants or cash assistance; 2) Individuals, couples, and community leaders are supported to unlearn harmful values and social norms and to adopt new values and attitudes and become more committed to equality and diversity 3) Adolescents and young people who are survivors and marginalized understand their rights, exercise self-efficacy 4) Adolescents are supported to to work together and communities on building a peaceful coexistence, through peacebuilding practices and violence risk reduction. These interventions will complement existing sectoral programming where Mercy Corps or its partners are operating in and will not be standalone. Mercy Corps will also continue to ensure protection mainstreaming is embedded across all our activities and programming.  Mercy Corps staff and partners are trained in protection and gender mainstreaming principles and approaches, protection risks analysis and Safeguarding/PSEA; Mercy Corps community accountability feedback and response mechanism are designed in consultation with communities and feedback received are use to track red flags; community awareness sessions to inform the communities of their rights and entitlements, complaints and feedback mechanism and the code of conduct of all individuals providing aid. Budget Breakdown: NES (521,435), NWS (223,472)

project_name: Reducción de las vulnerabilidades enfrentadas por los jóvenes y las mujeres indígenas de Amazonas
project_objective:
La acción propuesta tendrá un enfoque de fortalecimiento de los sistemas de prevención que amenazan la salud y la integridad física y social de las mujeres y los niños indígenas de Amazonas, contribuyendo a reducir la mortalidad materna y concienciando sobre la salud sexual y reproductiva de las mujeres, la prevención de violencias y la concienciación de la comunidad respecto a su participación en acciones de protección. Se han seleccionado estas comunidades por las limitaciones de acceso a la institucionalidad pública debido a procesos de discriminación y exclusión históricos para con las poblaciones indígenas. Además, por su cosmovisión tienen mecanismos de atención de sus realidades internas. En ese sentido, es necesario reconocer esos mecanismos y fortalecerlos para la atención de situaciones que están presentes como la VBG, la Trata y otras violencias relacionadas a las dinámicas de minería (Arco Minero). Asimismo, estas comunidades se ven altamente afectadas por enfermedades de transmisión vectorial así como de transmisión sexual e infecciones por consumo de agua no apta. Debido a limitaciones de acceso, inexistencia de personal médico localmente, falta de insumos y falta de ambulancias fluviales (botes con este propósito), estas comunidades son excluidas de los programas de promoción de la salud en el Estado de Amazonas. Los pocos recursos de los centros de salud se concentran en el eje carretero y la capital Puerto Ayacucho, los cuales están a más de 5 horas de recorrido para las comunidades indígenas más próximas y con altos costos de transporte. Esto afecta en mayor medida a las mujeres y adolescentes ya que no pueden acceder a información ni insumos de salud sexual y reproductiva. En ese sentido la acción incluye la distribución de kits de higiene menstrual adecuados al contexto amazónico, e información y materiales para promover la reducción del embarazo no deseado, en particular el adolescente (se presentan altas tasas en estas comunidades). 
La acción también desarrollará capacidades para contribuir a reducir la mortalidad de niños, mujeres y personas mayores frente a la malaria a través de la distribución de mosquiteros, el uso adecuado para alargar su vida útil ; y las epidemias gastrointestinales mediante la concienciación sobre prácticas de higiene.

project_name: Una respuesta integral con enfoque de edad, género e inclusión frente a la multi-afectación en el Municipio Paez (Estado Apure - Venezuela)
project_objective:
El objetivo del proyecto es proporcionar protección integral y asistencia en salud (con actividades complementarias en seguridad alimentaria y medios de vida) a las poblaciones vulnerables afectadas por la crisis en Venezuela (Emergencia humanitaria compleja, originada por crisis socioeconómica, presencia de grupos armados ilegales y desastres naturales). Se selecciona el municipio Paéz por ser uno de frontera afectado por la presencia y actividad de grupos armados, reclutamiento forzoso. Además, es una ruta de movilidad humana para migrantes y retornados al país, que presenta una alta afectación por inundaciones y presenta serias limitaciones de sus servicios básicos en entorno altamente rural y disperso. En particular las personas con discapacidad no pueden acceder a servicios de salud y de rehabilitacion física y funcional por las altas distancias entre parroquias (desplazamientos promedio de 5 a 6 horas en vías no asfaltadas y afectadas por inundaciones). En este contexto de violencia por presencia de grupos armados, ambién existen pocas oportunidades de empleo para jóvenes lo que promueve una alta tasa de migración. 

La acción proporcionará la prestación directa de servicios de alta calidad en a) Protección integral transversal; b) Rehabilitación física y funcional; c) Servicios comunitarios de salud mental; d) Salud sexual y reproductiva; e) Medios de vida para el autoconsumo y la promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y f) Acciones tempranas de gestión de riesgo que pueden reducir el impacto tanto medioambiental como de violencia armada. La estrategia que se plantea es a través de brigadas itinerantes para poder hacer frente a las limitaciones de transporte y distancia que afectan a las parroquias alejadas de la capital del Municipio (Guasdualito). Así estas brigadas buscarán promover capacidades en las comunidades para la atención entre pares mediante Grupos de Ayuda Mutua y Primeros Auxilios Psicológicos (salud mental), Rehabilitación basada en la Comunidad y la promoción de brigadas comunitarias de preparación y respuesta ante desastres. Para el caso de personas con discapacidad o en riesgo de desarrollar una, se contará con personal especializado en rehabilitación física y funcional para poder dar asistencia remota y presencial según requiera el caso. Asimismo, y de acuerdo a un diagnóstico, se brindarán ayudas técnicas adecuadas al contexto y necesidad de la persona.

De este modo se abordan las barreras estructurales y socioculturales al tiempo que se crea un entorno propicio para satisfacer las necesidades urgentes y específicas, y la participación significativa y la inclusión de las personas más afectadas.

project_name: Respuesta multisectorial para atender las necesidades urgentes de la población con necesidades específicas de protección de los estados fronterizos Amazonas, Falcón y Zulia
project_objective:
Para responder a la crisis migratoria de Venezuela y a sus consecuencias, es necesario atender las causantes de esta, para ello, se debe aumentar el acceso a los derechos fundamentales y servicios esenciales, reducir o mitigar los riesgos de protección, aumentar la autosuficiencia través de la generación de medios de vida sostenible y generar un ambiente de integración y coexistencia pacífica en las diferentes comunidades.
El abordaje de este proyecto es de naturaleza holística y contextualizada. A través de una relación de causa-efecto multisectorial, se abordarán las diversas problemáticas que motivan los desplazamientos de las poblaciones de interés, para ello, se tendrán criterios de flexibilidad técnica en todos los resultados, con el objetivo de adaptarse a las realidades de cada comunidad a través de un enfoque de participación comunitaria que garantice una verdadera atención adaptada al contexto.
Más a detalle, desde una perspectiva sectorial, se plantea una intervención con un objetivo general y transversal de protección, abordado desde los sectores de agua, saneamiento e higiene; energía y medios de vida. De igual manera, se abordarán de manera directa áreas temáticas internas del sector protección, como construcción de Paz y Empoderamiento femenino. Sumado a esto, como enfoques transversales, se trabajará la participación comunitaria en todas las etapas del proyecto y el cuidado del medio ambiente será tomado en cuenta en todos los procesos.
En términos territoriales y de selección de beneficiarios, se trabajará en 2 municipios del estado Amazonas, 4 municipios del estado Falcón y 4 Municipios del estado Zulia, aplicando el total de las actividades y metodología en al menos 2 comunidades por cada municipio atendido, dando un total de 20 comunidades atendidas en este proyecto. Debido a la naturaleza de las actividades planteadas, se asume como beneficiarios al total de la población de cada comunidad, pero simultáneamente se considerara “población de interés” a un grupo de beneficiarios que tendrá mayor participación en las actividades a realizar, este grupo estará conformado por: personas venezolanas afectadas por la situación humanitaria, especialmente personas retornadas, en movilidad, en riesgo de apatridia, que se encuentran en alto riesgo de protección relacionado con el desplazamiento y/o extranjeros con necesidad de protección (incluidos refugiados/solicitantes de asilo).
Lógica de intervención
Resultado 1: Reintegración de las poblaciones de interés a través del fortalecimiento a la infraestructura y los servicios básicos.
Actividad 1. Acondicionamiento de espacios y estructuras comunitarias con enfoques de protección, mejorando el acceso al agua, saneamiento, higiene y energía renovable.
Actividad 2. Talleres de fortalecimiento de capacidades y sensibilizaciones a personas de interés sobre, construcción segura, afrontamiento de desastres naturales, WASH y Energías renovables.  
Resultado 2: Fortalecimiento de la Autosuficiencia, inclusión económica y medios de vida de las poblaciones. 
Actividad 1. Talleres de formación sobre medios de vida: 
Actividad 2. Dotación de insumos de medios de vida para fortalecer las actividades productivas de los beneficiarios 

Resultado 3: Promoción de iniciativas comunitarias que potencien la integración y el empoderamiento de la mujer
Actividad 1. Iniciativas comunitarias son desarrolladas para fortalecer la reintegración de las personas retornadas
Actividad 2. Intervenciones comunitarias de protección con enfoque en empoderamiento femenino 
ACTED, con el apoyo de los grupos de lideresas comunitarias, realizara campañas educativas y de sensibilización en materia de derechos y para la prevención de riesgos de protección, incluido VBG y protección de la infancia, las mismas serán adaptadas al contexto, teniendo como opción la difusión de mensajes claves a través de medios digitales, físicos o incluso, la elaboración de réplicas de las formaciones, acompañadas por ACTED.

project_name: Provision of Primary Health Services for the Conflict and Vulnerable Communities in the states of Aljazeera, Gedaref, Northern Sate, Khartoum, South Kordofan, and the five Darfur Sates
project_objective:
The conflict that erupted in April 2023 in Sudan has decimated the country’s public infrastructure, including the health system. The health care system is suffering from an acute lack of staff, funding and medical supplies in addition to repeated attacks, looting and occupation of medical facilities and hospitals. More than 70% health facilities in conflict-affected regions of Sudan are inoperable or closed. 
The displacement of civilians has placed an additional strain on already overwhelmed health care resources, as well as water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. An outbreak of measles in the second half of 2023 has claimed the lives of more than 1000 children across Sudan. The country is also grappling with a severe cholera outbreak, with the number of suspected cases surpassing 8,500 in December 2023, having increased by 94% over the past month. With high rates of malnutrition, a debilitated health system and low levels of immunization, disease outbreaks will continue to have catastrophic impacts, particularly for children.
The remote areas that affected by the current conflict in Darfur and Kordofan states are inaccessible and suffer much from lack of medical assistance. The difficulty of transporting patients from rural areas to urban centers and from the remote state capitals to Khartoum for advanced diagnosis and medication is now extremely not possible mainly due to security risks along the main roads and because the health system in Khartoum itself and other big cities like Medani have collapsed due to fighting.
All the above mentioned challenges and difficulties place huge responsibilities on the shoulders of the humanitarian agencies to endeavor tom outreach the vulnerable people who need lifesaving health services and need prevention from expected epidemics resulting from fighting, negligence of environmental health, living in crowdedness conditions and lack of enough medical services.
United Peace Organization (UPO) is aiming to contribute in saving lives and alleviate the suffering of the people being affected by conflict and suffer from the magnitude of the epidemics which are driven by the conflict that triple doubled their impacts on the far majority of the communities. The intervention aims to support essential public health assistance with focus on primary health care services (including emergency trauma response). The project will address the needs of vulnerable groups who are disproportionally affected by health emergencies exacerbated by conflict and epidemics. UPO endeavors to access the remote areas that are currently disconnected from health care services due to the conflict, and that will be achieved in close coordination with the governmental departments and local communities.

project_name: Provision of livelihood and agricultural support to the conflict affected populations in Darfur, Eljazeera, Khartoum, Red Sea, Gadaref, South Kordofan, and Northern State
project_objective:
The HRP for 2024 highlight that total food availability in Sudan for the 2023/24 consumption year is expected to be significantly below average due to below-average domestic cereal harvests, i depleted food stocks and bureaucratic and insecurity-related challenges impeding food assistance deliveries.
The Food Security Analysis report in Sudan for the period October to February 2024 shows that about 17.7 million people across Sudan (37%) are suffering high levels of acute food insecurity, being classified in Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Phase 3 or above; among whom 4.9 million (10%) are in IPC Phase 4 (Emergency), and 12.8 million (27%) are in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis). This reflects the magnitude of the food insecurity across the country. Not only that; the situation is expected to further worsen due to the ongoing conflict. 
Currently access to food is counter affected by a number of interacting factors which include (1) wide scale displacement due to conflict, (2) the harvest have been affected by spread of fighting at harvest time, especially in Aljazira and South Kordofan, (3) decline in areas cultivated by food crops during 2023 rainy season due toof poor financing of the production inputs resulted from collapse of banking system, (4) blockage of roads that used to transport commodities from production areas and (5) restricted access to movement of humanitarian assistance that blocked aid agencies to deliver food supplies to some acutely food insecure areas. The IPC3 is higher in Khartoum (38%), Darfur States 38%, 35%, 32%, 30%, 26% in (West, East, Central, South and North Darfur respectively), whereas it is 33% in South Kordofan and 24% in Aljazira. The IPC 4 scale is higher in Khartoum (22%), West and Central Darfur (17% each), South Kordofan (15%), South Darfur (14%), North and East Darfur (12% each) and Aljazira (7%). These threatening figures are expected to increase during the lean period when produced stocks deplete and labor opportunities shrink while the conflict resolution is not seen on the near horizon.
The overall aim of this project is to support the most vulnerable and conflict-affected populations in Darfur, Eljazeera, Khartoum, Red Sea, Gadaref, South Kordofan, and the Northern State. The key objectives of the project are to: 1) Reduce acute food insecurity and save the lives of extremely vulnerable populations affected by conflict and natural disasters by providing emergency agriculture assistance to the underserved populations; and 2) increase access to food security and livelihood diversification for the newly displaced and most extremely vulnerable conflict-affected populations through cash based transfers.  
The UPO proposed project will focus on intervening in the most affected areas and will prioritize assisting the people most at risk and, most vulnerable groups in collaboration and coordination with the FSL cluster. Our interventions include enabling at risk people to access immediate food (e.g. through cash and food assistance) and supporting them to secure future food through agricultural inputs and seeds for women, men, boys, and girls, as well as conducting extension training and vaccinations for livestock. The project will also ensure the provision of emergency livelihood start-up kits, agricultural inputs, and tools for the most vulnerable HHs.  Awareness campaigns will be conducted for the most vulnerable population, both female and male, on environment protection, gender involvement, and equality. In addition, 40% of this program will be cash through distribution of vouchers, cash for work, and cash for business. 
The project will be implemented in close coordination with the relevant actors, ensuring that gender-sensitive programming and investment, including protection, are adhered to during the implementation.  UPO focuses on maintaining an inclusive, sustainable, and accepting implementation environment that results in community collaboration and ownership.

project_name: Provision of Protection Assistance to Vulnerable Populations in Darfur States, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Khartoum, Red Sea, Northern state and Al Jazirah
project_objective:
The overall objective of the project is to provide integrated GBV, child protection, and general protection services to the 70,000 most vulnerable conflict-affected populations, including IDPs, resident communities, and returnees in Darfur, South Kordofan, Jazirah, Red Sea, Gedaref, Northern and Khartoum States. Under GBV sub-sector, UPO aims to reach 30,000 most vulnerable women and young girls affected by conflicts in Al Manaqil, Al Qurashi, Janub Aj Jazirah, Um Algura, Gharb Jabal Marrah, Shamal, Jabal Marrah, Wasat Jabal Marrah, Zalingi, Abu Karinka, Ad Du'ayn, Yassin, Al Galabat Al Gharbyah - Kassab,Al Qureisha, Gala'a Al Nahal, Galabat Ash-Shargiah, Madeinat Al Gedaref, Wasat Al Gedaref, Karrari, Um Durman, Al Fasher, Dar As Salam,Kelemando,Tawila,Ad Dabbah,Dongola,Halfa,Haya,Port Sudan,As Salam - SD,Beliel,Ed Al Fursan,Kas,Kateila,Kubum,Mershi localities with provision of dignity kits, awareness raising, gender sensitive consultation (medical and mental) and capacity building, construction and rehabilitation of women multi use centers to help increase their protection, sharing and participation. The project will also focus on the provision of PSS, GBV community networks and safe channels, livelihood start-up kits for the most vulnerable, training of GBV front-line service providers, and a GBV referral support system. UPO conducts its projects with an inclusive and responsible business model that ensures two-way communication pathways throughout the implementation and exit stages, in addition to providing meaningful access and feedback to all stakeholders. UPO will coordinate all project activities with the GBV across the target states, including regularly sharing the ¾ W. For the child protection sub-sector, UPO aims to reach 20,000 children with CBCPNs PSS, CFS, capacity building, identification of UAC, referral supports, distribution of dignity kits, alternative care, case management, assessment and awareness raising to the public on child protection and development, disaster reduction, and coping mechanisms. 20,000 vulnerable people will be provided with general protection, identification, documentation, and legal aid support. UPO commits to strengthening coordination both at the field and Khartoum across the protection sector and the sub-sectors.
Over ten percent of the activity costs of the project will be implemented through a cash assistance approach for the PSN and extremely affected populations. This CASH will be directly distributed to the target populations. Each family will receive cash support for 12 months, $150 per month, to help support the essential needs of the family. The majority of the activities are designed in a durable, environmentally friendly, and sustainable way for long-term solutions for the IDPs, returnees, and host communities. i.e., women and community centers will be constructed from permanent materials that can last for over 10 years. Community structures, protection committees, and networks should be strengthened and supported to continue taking on their roles beyond the project's lifetime. Women capacity building and training to continue tacking, preventing, and addressing any protection concerns beyond the project duration.  UPO uses and focuses on gender-sensitive programming and modalities by designing all activities through gender role frameworks and gender matrix frameworks to ensure safe and inclusive participation and sustainability of the project outcomes by creating a change theory in the co-gender norms and harmful practices and promoting healthy habits and co-existing spheres.

project_name: Provision of Shelter solutions, and lifesaving NFI to IDPs, integrated IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in Khartoum, Gadaref, Aljazeera, Red Sea, Darfurs, Northern state and South Kordofan
project_objective:
UPO will focus primarily on supporting 12,600 families and ensuring that the most vulnerable women, men, boys, and girls are at the center of the UPO ESNFI response. The ESNFI Needs Assessment will continuously be conducted with support from other partners to understand the gaps and social issues affecting vulnerable communities and triangulate into programs addressing these needs. The communities in the target areas are in desperate need of NFI and shelter materials as a step of support in improving their lives to cope with managing recurrent shocks and building resilience. In order to have an effective and efficient response to the needs, UPO will continue with its ESNFI response in Darfur, Khartoum, Gedaref, Al Jazirah, Red Sea, the Northern State, and South Kordofan. UPO activities in target locations will include coordination of needs assessments, NFIs distribution, mobilization of resources, sensitization of communities, cash for shelter, reception and communal centres, tent  distribution, ESK distribution, gender and environment protection and coordination of responding to the immediate needs of the people.
The project will also focus on promoting peaceful coexistence and community-shared management of the provided services to ensure ownership and sustainability in these harsh times that Sudan is going through.

project_name: Siempre protegidas: niñas, niños y adultos con acceso a protección aún en emergencias.
project_objective:
El Salvador tiene una población de 6,7 millones de personas, es el país más pequeño y densamente poblado de Centroamérica. De acuerdo con el Panorama de Necesidades Humanitarias 2024, se estima que 1,1 millones de personas tienen necesidades humanitarias urgentes como resultado de la combinación de problemas estructurales y coyunturales que tienen impacto humanitario y están poniendo en riesgo la vida, la seguridad y el acceso a derechos y servicios básicos de las poblaciones en situaciones de riesgo. 

Por otra parte, los eventos climáticos extremos agudizan la crisis multidimensional preexistente, tales como las brechas de acceso equitativo a servicios de protección y otros servicios de respuesta a violencia de género (VdG), alimentación, educación, agua segura, salud sexual y reproductiva, y emergencias coexistentes. Las poblaciones víctima de desplazamiento forzado, migración, desempleo entre otros factores que han incrementado las situaciones de riesgo desde la seguridad, las necesidades de protección y el abordaje de problemas de desarrollo, por lo que una respuesta integral y coordinada a estos múltiples escenarios se vuelve esencial. 

La exposición cotidiana a múltiples factores de vulneración de derechos genera impactos a nivel de salud mental y emocional, como consecuencia de la desintegración familiar, la afectación de los medios de vida por extorsión, y riesgos en los entornos escolares y otros que causan la deserción y el abandono escolar. Estas situaciones conducen a que la población en contextos de violencia, desencadenan el desplazamiento forzado y la migración como estrategias de supervivencia.

Save the Children propone el desarrollo de acciones que aseguren la protección de niñas, niños y adolescentes en entornos familiares y comunitarios seguros, con acceso a servicios de atención psicosocial para sí mismos y sus cuidadores basados en una estrategia para el cambio social de comportamiento. El proyecto se ha diseñado para una implementación total de 9 meses, con presupuesto total de $535,000.00

A través de este proyecto se pretende contribuir al logro de los siguientes resultados: 1) Niñez y sus familias afectadas por emergencias con acceso a atención en albergues que cumplen estándares internacionales de protección, salud, alimentación, educación y seguridad, entre otros; 2) Fortalecido el acceso seguro a artículos no alimentarios esenciales para mantener la salud, seguridad y dignidad de las personas afectadas por distintas necesidades de protección, particularmente afectados por la violencia, desastres y efectos de las crisis; 3) Fortalecidos espacios seguros de protección y entornos protectores familiares.

project_name: LIFELINE
project_objective:
Vulnerable families in Northeast Syria are grappling with persistent challenges in securing safe and adequate shelters, a consequence of the decade-long conflict that has severely impacted housing availability and displaced millions. According to REACH November HSOS, over one third of the population resides in substandard, damaged, or inadequate shelters, with 31% of assessed communities reporting occupied shelters with major damage. Finding suitable housing is critical, especially during the winter months, and households renting properties face challenges due to unaffordability. Security incidents in 2023, such as tensions between tribal leaders and authorities or Turkish airstrikes, increase the risk of conflict escalation and further displacement. In Raqqa, 84% of households experienced shelter inadequacies from October 2023 to January 2024, with issues like lack of lighting and a decline in daily electricity hours. Eviction risk, coupled with the prevailing security and economic challenges, has led to increased mobility, particularly in the Al-Hassakeh governorate, where IDPs and host communities face notable disparities in shelter conditions and livelihoods, impacting their living situations.
 
The organization will provide winterization support to vulnerable households in Ar-Raqqa and Al Hassakeh governorates, aiming to reach 5,640 individuals from November 2024 to the end of February 2025. Focusing on informal settlements as a priority, the organization will utilize experience gained from the LEARN consortium and employ a needs-based approach. In Ar-Raqqa, the organization plans blanket distributions in informal settlements based on SNFI WG rankings and will conduct needs assessments considering winterization criteria. In Al Hassakeh, 410 IDP households in neglected villages near collective centers will be targeted with vulnerability-based assistance. the organization aims for flexibility in responding to unforeseen emergencies, conducting market and risk assessments to determine the appropriate modality (vouchers, in-kind, cash, or mixed). Tailored approaches for persons with special needs will be implemented, and distributions will be accompanied by sensitization campaigns. The winterization kits' contents will be adapted based on SNFI WG guidelines and ongoing dialogue with other actors, with an average planned distribution value of 190 USD per household.

In the context of safe programming, field teams, comprising both male and female workers, prioritize gender balance and meaningful access for all groups. Gender-segregated consultations continue through various methods, and data analysis for household selection is done by project managers with IM department support. To mitigate safety and diversion risks in cash distribution, the organization communicates distribution details discreetly and implements protective measures during the process, including separating recipients by gender and prioritizing vulnerable individuals. A secure feedback mechanism and monitoring of cash usage are established. Recognizing evolving gender dynamics exacerbated by the crisis, the organization implements gender-sensitive approaches in cash programming, challenging traditional norms by considering voucher alternatives to empower women. Additionally, addressing the intersection of gender-based violence and shelter concerns, the organization emphasizes strategic shelter design, community engagement, and providing gender-specific spaces. For age and disability considerations, the organization acknowledges the marginalized status of elderly and disabled individuals, emphasizing the importance of transportation services and accessible premises but recognizing persistent challenges and discrimination, particularly for displaced populations.

project_name: Emergency life-saving response to cover the essential WASH needs in northeast Syria.
project_objective:
Needs:
The proposed action aims to address the WASH needs of the people affected by the humanitarian crisis in northern Syria, based on needs assessments and stakeholder consultations. The action also includes longer-term solutions to improve water, sanitation, and hygiene conditions and resilience in the region. The HNO for 2024 shows that most people in northeast Syria need humanitarian and WASH assistance, due to critical water issues, hygiene challenges, and the impact of the 2023 earthquake.
Implementation and intervention activities:
• The organization will provide comprehensive WASH support package for targeted informal settlements and host communities Raqqa and Hasakeh governorates.
•The organization will improve access to safe water to 85,231 individuals. In Raqqa, by installation new Water Treatment Units (4,935 individuals), the rehabilitation of water networks in 4 villages and water trucking rehabilitation support (19,942 individuals), the chlorination of filling points (9,243 individuals) and the continuation of support to 3 water stations (29,700 individuals). In Hasakeh, this will include additional water trucking support during the summer months (increasing the total reach to 13,830 individuals) and the rehabilitation of the Markada water network (6,500 individuals). 
•To support the safe storage of water, the organization will also provide communal and household-level water tanks to vulnerable populations in informal settlements and villages in Raqqa, and household-level tanks in Markada town, benefiting a total of 24,297 individuals. 
•The organization will reach a total of 13,838 individuals through sanitation activities. In informal settlements in Raqqa the organization will increase the number of household latrines provided, install household showers for selected PwSN, and conduct maintenance of sanitation infrastructures. In host communities, the organization will cover sanitation pits and provide desludging in 7 villages in Raqqa District (3,198 individuals). In Markada town.
•The organization will extend hygiene promotion activities to Markada village in Hasakeh, and villages and new informal settlements in Raqqa (34,598 individuals). Soap distributions will be organized in a targeted manner to individuals in households and informal settlements (7,795 individuals), and the organization will distribute menstrual hygiene kits to the 988 households in the informal settlements in Raqqa. 
•As part of its emergency contingency stockpile, the organization will supplement its originally planned cholera kits with 10 emergency kits in Raqqa and 700 emergency WASH kits. 
•The organization will begin solid waste management activities in NES, including support to the municipal waste collection system in Raqqa District, and the organization of an environmental health campaign in Markada town. To support these activities, the organization will distribute communal and household bins across the SWM locations. 
Risk and assumption:
Economy: Price and exchange rate fluctuations; Closure of banks or restrictions from banking system negatively impact the flow of funds inside Syria; Partial or total disruption of the supply chain; Lack of proper controls for distributions resulting in theft/loss; Lack of fuel with impact on project activities; Cash transfer modalities are disrupted or restricted, money transfer agents increase their commissions due to the restrictions of USD liquidity in Iraq and KRI. 
Natural disaster/Epidemics: Natural disasters, catastrophes or epidemics occurred in the project areas: droughts are more frequent and are affecting underground water levels causing dried up boreholes;; risk of cholera outbreak due to water supply constraints.
Environment: The project generates significant greenhouse gas emissions coming from energy production and transport of goods, plastic pollution, and groundwater pollution.
Escalation of conflict affects the project activities in operational areas.

project_name: Protection for IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in Mozambique
project_objective:
The project seeks to provide a holistic protection response to IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in northern Mozambique in response to the insurgency in the region. The project will also provide integrated protection services (including GBV and Child Protection ). The project seeks to provide GBV case management as welll as provision of mental health and psychosocial support services to GBV Survivors, including awareness raising on GBV, PSEA as well as promotion of accountability to affected persons. Capacity building on GBV, referral pathways (local level as well as the hotline), community mobilisation, positive masculinity, as well as in use of various modalities will be used. Women and Girls' Safe Spaces will be established and strengthened to ensure an integrated interactive intervention contributing to social cohesion among internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. The WGSS will provide a comfortable environment for women and girls to express themselves without fear of judgment or harm. Protection Focal Points will be identified and trained to provide first aid MHPSS to GBV Survivors as well as in case identification and referrals. The project will create a comprehensive model for GBV responses, incorporating rapid assessments, simplified referral pathways for hard-to-reach areas, community mapping, and orientation for GBV community volunteers (activists) as well as Protection Focal Points. 

In terms of Child Protection, the project seeks to provide child protection services to unaccompanied and separated children, including identification and provision of foster care for the children, while at the same time providing mental health and psychosocial support services to traumatised children due to natural disasters as well as due to the insurgency in northern mozambique. Family tracing and reconciliation will also be prioritised as most children get lost and/or lose contact with their parents and/or guardians as they flee from man-made as well as natural disasters. Child Friendly Spaces will be set up, including recreational parks for the provision of MHPSS as well as for case identification. Integrated case management including filing and documentation will be prioritised.

project_name: Multi-sectoral assistance to camps and IDP sites in northwest Syria
project_objective:
After 12 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their situation worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Türkiye on 6 and 20 February 2023. The earthquakes uprooted hundreds of thousands of families, resulted in almost 5,900 deaths and more than 12,800 people injured in Syria, and severely damaged infrastructures already weakened by the conflict. 
Over 6.7 million Syrians are internally displaced, with 2.8 million in the northwest region alone, living in dire conditions. Access to essentials like safe water, food, medicine, healthcare, and livelihoods is limited, particularly in northwest Syria. 
Over 2 million IDPs are living in last resort camps, Informal settlements, reception/transit, and collective centers (HNO, December 2023), 90% of the 1,510 IDP active IDP sites in NWS are self-settled and lack organized camp management systems. (CCCM Cluster, Dec 2023). The needs of those who are displaced are increasing rapidly and critical basic services such as health, shelter, food, WASH, and protection persist for hundreds of thousands of men, women, and children. Additionally, economic hardship, insecurity, and the threat of continued displacement leave more than 2 million people in NWS vulnerable and in need of essential, multi-sectoral assistance in formal and informal sites.  

IOM will assess the needs of the most affected communities, engage with multiple and diverse stakeholders, provide small-scale care and maintenance activities, and coordinate the provision of multi-sectoral support in reception centers (RCs) and IDP sites.  
IOM will implement the Area Based Approach to target the most vulnerable and underserved self-settled sites through Monitoring Assessment Team (MAT) to identify, assess, and refer for a sectoral response within Cross-Border.  Furthermore, the project will strengthen emergency preparedness and fire response by establishing and training fire committees, distributing fire points and fire mitigation tools, refilling used fire extinguishers, and providing awareness courses on fire mitigation/prevention for displaced people. In addition, IOM will focus on strengthening community engagement to enable camp populations to participate in the decision-making process as well as to play an active role in camp management, by establishing inclusive camp management committees and delivering capacity-building training to them. 
IOM will conduct community-led integration and skills-building activities in the targeted locations, emphasizing the inclusion of women and youth in the process. As part of these efforts, people in camps will be provided with vocational training, equipping them with the necessary expertise to pursue sustainable livelihood opportunities. Additionally, the initiative will support individuals with start-up grants to rehabilitate, develop, or start social or business entrepreneurship initiatives within the camps. Through these endeavors, IOM aims to empower individuals and foster resilience and self-reliance within the camp communities. These initiatives will be conducted in coordination with the early recovery (ERL) cluster to ensure alignment with broader development goals and maximize impact through collaborative action. 
Finally, through the MAT, IOM will continue identifying and assessing the needs of most vulnerable informal sites and refer them to the IOM Cross-Border Unit for targeted assistance. 
PSEA strategy: IOM recognizes the risk of SEA by IPs and their sub-contractors during the implementation. Key mitigation measures include ensuring that all IPs staff have read and signed their Code of Conduct, have taken part in PSEA training, have a dedicated complaint mechanism in place, and delivering PSEA awareness-raising activities and materials for beneficiaries and local communities. Furthermore, IOM, through its TPM teams, will ensure that activities are carried out in a principled manner.

project_name: Protecting Civilians through Humanitarian Mine Action in Syria
project_objective:
The humanitarian crisis in Syria has been exacerbated by the widespread use of explosive ordnance (EO), posing significant risks and requiring different mitigation strategies to reduce its impact on the civilian population and the humanitarian sector delivering aid to those in need. Although the scale and scope of EO contamination in Syria remains undefined, according to the 2024 Summary HNO, more than 65% of the Syrian population (14.4 million people) are at risk from EO contamination, which represents over 20% increase from 2023 (11.5 million people). According to OCHA access analysis of June 2023, the presence of mines and EO remains a major access impediment to the safe delivery of humanitarian assistance in 146 sub-districts (54 percent of all sub-districts). EO contamination is also acknowledged in the UN Common Risk Register as a high residual and inherent, strategic and operational risk to UN operations.
Mine action is a key humanitarian priority and enabler for the wider humanitarian response and is critical enablers for safe delivery of humanitarian assistance. In the absence of comprehensive technical survey and clearance, continuous hostilities for the last 12 years have been constantly creating new layers of explosive contamination. Based on open-source data (ACLED), from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2023, a total of 71,289 EO incidents were recorded. This is an average of 31 Explosive Ordnance incidents per day. 
Interventions: The overall aim of UNMAS project is to reduce the impact of EO on the civilian population and humanitarian workers through effective sector coordination and implementation of humanitarian mine action activities, in line with the framework of agreements between the Syrian State and UN agencies, funds and programmes, as well as Security Council resolution, S/RES/2672(2023). Under this project, UNMAS will provide advisory support to the national authorities, and technical and operational support to the HMA actors, including through accreditation and quality assurance of HMA activities. UNMAS will also continue coordinating the HMA Area of Responsibility (AoR) at both Whole of Syria (WoS) and Damascus Hub levels, ensuring the integration of the HMA needs into UN strategic plans and advocacy documents, and disseminating relevant EO data and analysis. 
UNMAS will follow an integrated approach in implementing HMA interventions, where it is capable of prioritizing and implementing several activities simultaneously, to ensure a comprehensive response. Furthermore, HMA activities will be planned jointly with the humanitarian and early recovery partners to fulfill their role as integral enablers of their operations.
All components of humanitarian mine action (risk education, victim assistance, survey clearance) are critical, but UNMAS will focus on expanding survey and clearance, as the only way to permanently remove the threat posed by EO.
UNMAS operations will be fulfilled through the deployment of non-technical Survey (NTS), Multi tasking Teams (MTTs) and integrated Explosive Ordnance risk education/ Victim Assistance (EORE/VA)teams. The teams will support ongoing and planned humanitarian and early recovery operations of the UN and the wider humanitarian and early recovery community and establish the extent of contamination in their areas of deployment. 
PSEA:UNMAS contract and grants has standard clauses for implementing partner’s (IP) requirement for Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Sexual Harassment and incorporate UN Supplier Code of Conduct where there is a requirement for the IP to put in place an“Organizational Code of Conduct/Rule.
PRA:Creation of beneficiaries wrong expectations, who could wrongly attribute to RE teams ability of removing EO, this is mitigated by clear explanation of intervention & objectives. Not reaching all vulnerable groups: mitigated by involvement of community focal points & inclusion team in planning,adaptation&delivery of inclusive RE sessions.

project_name: Réponse d'urgence pour l'amélioration de l'accès à l'eau potable, à l'hygiène et l'assainissement  des populations  déplacées et des communautés hôtes de la commune  de Ouallam, département de Ouallam, Région de Tillabéri
project_objective:
La dégradation de la situation sécuritaire dans l'ouest du pays a occasionné le déplacement des populations de certains villages vers les zones plus sûres et sécurisées. Malheureusement ces zones d'accueil ne possèdent pas suffisamment d'infrastructures de base pour répondre aux besoins fondamentaux de survie de ces déplacés et des populations hôtes. C'est au vu de ces constats, qu'une réponse d'urgence s'avère nécessaire pour  la satisfaction des besoins en eau, hygiène et assainissement, ainsi que les moyens d'existence de ces communautés d'environ 4000 personnes (PDI et communautés hôtes). La démarche de mise en œuvre proposée  est fondée sur l’initiative et la responsabilité locale. Chaque activité sera réalisée avec une forte implication des bénéficiaires (populations, communes, chefferie traditionnelle), Les activités identifiées dans ce projet répondent aux besoins des bénéficiaires. Dans un premier temps, des relais communautaires seront identifiés et formés avec le concours des CSI. Ensuite, ces derniers vont mener la sensibilisation de porte en porte dans leur communautés sur l'utilisation des produits de traitement de l'eau, le suivi de la qualité de l'eau de consommation à domicile et la sensibilisation pour changement de comportement en matière d'eau et d'assainissement. Chronologiquement, la réalisation de toute activité du projet suivra les étapes suivantes :

1. Analyse de la situation pour quantifier le besoin
2. Etudes techniques pour les réalisations physiques
3. Contrôle technique des travaux pour s’assurer de leur qualité
3. Suivi et évaluation interne et/ou externe par les communautés avec l'appui des services techniques
4. Réception technique des réalisations

Compte tenu des difficultés d'accès dans certaines zones, le cash transfert sera adopté comme moyen pour le paiement des relais communautaires à travers les agences de transfert monétaire, les bons et les coupons pour faciliter l'accès au savon lors des séances de distribution à travers des opérateurs économiques de la zone. Des missions de suivi sont prévues au cours de la durée du projet. Elles seront menées par la commune elle-même en rapport avec les villages concernés, accompagnés et conseillés par les services techniques régionaux et départementaux.

project_name: Assistance en abris et BNA (biens non alimentaires) aux personnes déplacées vulénarbles dans la région de Tahoua
project_objective:
Le projet proposé par l'ONG Elbourak Charité vise la continuité d’une meilleure coordination pour répondre de façon adéquate aux besoins en abris et en BNA de populations deplacees internes dans la région de Tahoua au Niger surtout avec la periode du grand froid qui s'annonce un tel projet va enormement assister la population cible. L'objectif de cette proposition est de contribuer à l'amélioration des conditions de vies des populations déplacées internes à travers: i) la fourniture d'abris aux ménages vunérables, la distribution de kits BNA.  Il s'agit, de répondre de facon specifique aux beoins crées par les premiers mouvements avec 1500 abris d'urgence et 1500 kits BNA à Tahoua notamment dans les departements de Bagaroua, Tchintabaraden et Tassare pour améliorer les conditions de vie des ménages dont le retour dans les villages d'origine se plonge chaque jour dans l'obscurité du fait de l'insécurité dans cette région. 
La réponse de l'ONG Elbourak sera conforme à ses Principes de Protection et au Cadre GBV en plus, l'ONG Elbourak intégrera des mesures visant à assurer la sécurité, la dignité et le bien-être de la population touchée, y compris en atténuant les risques liés au VGB dans ses interventions abris/BNA. L'ONG Elbourak veillera également à ce que les principes de ne pas nuire, la sécurité et la non-discrimination guident toute activité et soient respectées tout au long de la mise en œuvre du projet.

project_name: Reponse aux mouvement de Population au profit des familles d'accueil, déplacés et rétournés dans la région de Tillabery au Niger
project_objective:
Le Niger est confronté à une crise humanitaire causée par des chocs récurrents et simultanés, dont les conflits armés, sécheresses, épidémies et inondations. La situation sécuritaire est caractérisée par une violence généralisée liée à la présence importante de groupes armés non étatiques (GANE) ; comme dans la région de Tillabéri, où ils opèrent dans les zones frontalières avec le Mali et le Burkina Faso. Les exactions répétées de ces groupes entraînent des déplacements importants. Le Niger compte ainsi 564,000 déplacés,  34,000 retournés et 231,000 réfugiés (HNO 2023). Selon les prévisions du HRP, 3,8 millions de personnes auront un besoin urgent d'aide humanitaire en 2021, soit une augmentation de 31% par rapport à 2022. L’accès aux services de base, particulièrement en milieu rural, est très faible.
Tillabéri est l’une des régions la plus sévèrement affectée par la détérioration des contextes sécuritaires et humanitaires. Selon le HNO, elle fait partie des régions les plus vulnérables du pays, classée à 7.5 lors de la dernière analyse multidimensionnelle INFORM. le niveau de services publics (eau potable, santé, éducation) disponibles ne cesse de diminuer, les déplacements augmentant la pression sur les ressources disponibles déjà limitées.
 Les départements d’Ayerou, Say et Ouallam  sont parmi les plus affectés par l’insécurité et les déplacements. Pour des raisons d’insécurité, l’accès humanitaire y est toujours plus difficile, laissant les populations de plus en plus isolées. Les besoins en EHA sont particulièrement critiques. 
Le projet proposé contribuera directement aux objectifs du HRP, et est aligné avec les priorités géographiques et opérationnelles de l’Allocation. Il est complémentaire aux interventions en cours des organisations Humanitaires, afin d’en renforcer l’impact sur les populations touchées, mais sans aucune duplication.
Ce projet cible 14,479 a pour objectif la mise en place des actions d'eau, Hygiene et Assainissement dans la prévention et la lutte contre les maladies diarrhéique  aux populations impactées par les mouvements de population dans la région de Tillabery (Ayerou, Say et Ouallam)
 EBC assurera l’intégration des principes de protection transversale et le respect du principe de « Ne Pas Nuire » tout au long de la mise en œuvre."

project_name: Assistance d'urgence aux retournees aux frontiers Tchadien-Soudanais
project_objective: Depuis le début des hostilités au Soudan le 15 avril 2023, près de 550 000 personnes déplacées ont fui vers le Tchad. Cela comprend plus de 109 000 Tchadiens rapatriés, un nombre qui devrait atteindre 150 000 d'ici mars 2024. Selon les informations recueillies sur le terrain par l'OIM, de nombreux rapatriés vivaient au Soudan depuis des décennies et n'avaient pas de logement au Tchad. Les rapatriés séjournent actuellement dans des sites de déplacement dans trois provinces situées le long de la frontière avec le Soudan : Ouaddaï, Sila et Wadi Fira. Selon les évaluations de la Matrice de suivi des déplacements (DTM), 52 % des rapatriés sont des femmes et des filles et 67 % ont moins de 18 ans. Bien que les communautés d'accueil aient accueilli les rapatriés, l'afflux important de personnes déplacées et les ressources limitées dans ces provinces signifient que de nombreuses personnes déplacées vivent dans des conditions déplorables. Pour faire respecter le droit des personnes déplacées à des conditions de vie dignes l'OIM prévoit de fournir une assistance d’urgence aux rapatriés sous la forme d’abris et articles non alimentaires, et activités WASH qui bénéficieront 8,000 rapatriés.

project_name: Renforcer le système éducatif inclusif dans les régions de Tombouctou et Gao au Mali.
project_objective: Le projet a pour objectif de promouvoir l'accès à une éducation inclusive de qualité, en mettant particulièrement l'accent sur les enfants handicapés et déplacés dans les régions de Tombouctou et de Gao. Il apportera un soutien aux écoles ordinaires, aux centres SSA/P et aux écoles coraniques rénovées. Ce soutien comprendra : i) l'appui aux Commissions Communales d'éducation inclusive pour faciliter l'intégration scolaire des enfants handicapés/déplacés ; ii) le renforcement des capacités du personnel éducatif et des animateurs pour répondre aux besoins spécifiques des enfants vulnérables ; iii) la fourniture de matériel pédagogique adapté ; iv) la création d'espaces d'apprentissage sûrs (MHPPS, Plan de réduction des risques) ; v) le soutien à des alternatives éducatives telles que les centres SSA/P et les écoles coraniques. En collaboration avec d'autres projets menés par HI et financés par Education Can Not Wait et le Ministère des Affaires Etrangères luxembourgeois, l’action soutiendra également des travaux d'aménagement et l'équipement des écoles et des centres SSA/P et coraniques pour améliorer les conditions d'apprentissage des enfants. En outre, HI travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les services sociaux locaux pour assurer l'accès des enfants handicapés aux services médicaux et de réadaptation.
